This activity is mechanistically rooted in metabolic interference against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), including disruption of ABC transporters and inhibition of the biosynthesis of essential amino acids (valine, leucine, isoleucine) and ribosomes. Concurrently, ZnSi FMPs can promote microenvironment remodeling by modulating inflammatory responses and angiogenesis, evidenced by suppressed inflammation mediated by the complement and coagulation cascades pathway and robust activation of the Areg/HB-EGF-mediated ErbB signaling pathway. Hence, in both S. aureus-infected and diabetic wound models (mice and minipigs), ZnSi FMPs exhibited superior chronic wound healing capacity compared with commercial silver sulfadiazine® (AgSD) and 45S5 bioglass®. This improved healing was achieved through enhanced antibacterial activity, anti-inflammatory effects, and angiogenesis, accompanied by elevated expression of CD163, CD206, CD31 and α-SMA. By synergizing bacterial metabolic interference with microenvironment regulation, ZnSi FMPs effectively facilitate tissue healing and provide a promising candidate for clinical wound treatment.

articles.title: Continuity and Discontinuity in Artefact Distributions from Multi-Period Archaeological Sites.
articles.journal: Journal of archaeological method and theory
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Artefact finds recovered by metal detecting and reported by members of the public are a growing source of archaeological information, with over 1.2 million finds recorded to date by the Portable Antiquities Scheme in England and Wales. Heritage schemes in many other European countries where hobby detecting for archaeology is legal likewise report growing numbers of finds. Using point pattern analysis, this paper presents a worked-out set of computational methods to study diachronic processes within artefact assemblages at field or local (e.g. parish) levels. We present a simulated 'toy' example to illustrate the methodology and test it with two large artefact assemblages from the counties of North Yorkshire and Norfolk that differ in terms of finds record quality and known contextual archaeological landscape information. The proposed approach and example code can be reapplied to other archaeological point patterns. It formalises a spatial statistical workflow that produces an assessment regarding landscape persistence and reuse, and which can be used, for example, to assist fieldwork or planning decisions by identifying areas for further research. The case studies highlight the considerable need for formal analytical workflows in public finds research, which can be easily deployed at different sites and local assemblages. Moreover, while the proposed workflow has been designed with public finds scatters in mind, it is scale-agnostic and can be reapplied to investigate a range of archaeological phenomena from monument distributions across a larger region to investigating artefact scatters within an excavated area.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10816-026-09821-0.

articles.title: Impact of Non-Tobacco Nicotine Products on Postoperative Outcomes in Soft Tissue Hand Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Use of non-tobacco nicotine products (NTNP), including e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches, and oral nicotine devices, has risen sharply, yet their impact on postoperative outcomes across elective soft tissue hand surgeries remains poorly defined. Although nicotine from combustible tobacco impairs wound healing, whether NTNP exposure confers similar risk is unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between preoperative NTNP use and postoperative complication rates following elective soft tissue hand surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network identified adults (≥18 years) undergoing elective soft tissue hand surgery from 2004 to 2024. Patients with non-tobacco-specified nicotine dependence diagnoses documented within 1 year before surgery were compared with patients without any documented nicotine dependence. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on demographics and comorbidities. Postoperative complications at 1, 3, and 6 months included deep, superficial, and unspecified surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism. Odds ratios with 95 percent confidence intervals were calculated, with P < .05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: After matching, 36,811 patients were included per cohort. NTNP use was associated with significantly increased rates of unspecified surgical site infection, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and wound dehiscence at all assessed postoperative time points. Deep and superficial surgical site infection rates did not differ significantly. Effect sizes were consistent across all intervals.

CONCLUSIONS: NTNP use within 1 year is independently associated with higher risks of wound dehiscence, thromboembolic events, and unspecified postoperative infection after soft tissue hand surgery. These findings suggest that nicotine exposure, regardless of delivery method, adversely affects postoperative healing and should be addressed through preoperative screening and cessation counseling.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective cohort study III.

articles.title: Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Gas signaling molecules, including nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide, have recently gained attention in erectile dysfunction treatment research because of their roles in regulating blood vessel function, reducing oxidative stress, and protecting nerves and other cells. This article reviews how nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide are involved in the development of erectile dysfunction and their potential as treatments. The review focuses on how these gases improve blood vessel function, relax smooth muscles, repair nerve function, and reduce tissue scarring. Current research shows that methods of gas delivery, especially those using nanocarriers or prodrugs, greatly increase how well these gases are absorbed and where they act in the body. Early animal studies and initial clinical trials support the effectiveness of these gasotransmitters in treating various causes of erectile dysfunction, including diabetes, aging, and nerve damage. Although challenges remain in controlling the speed of delivery, determining the appropriate dosage, and tailoring treatment to individual patients, there is reason for optimism. The development of responsive delivery systems, combinations of multiple gases, and additional therapies for difficult cases suggests that gas signaling molecules could transform erectile dysfunction treatment.

articles.title: Molecular crosstalk between gas transmitters and catecholamine biosynthesis pathways: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Catecholamines, particularly the hormone and neurotransmitter epinephrine, are important regulators of blood pressure and cardiovascular function. The expression of genes encoding catecholamine biosynthetic enzymes is subject to strict transcriptional regulation through both hormonal and neuronal mechanisms. These genes are also regulated by hypoxia and reactive oxygen species. A class of small gaseous transmitters, known as gas transmitters, serve as potent regulators of blood pressure and hypoxic signaling; however, their roles in catecholamine biosynthesis remain poorly understood. This manuscript reviews the current state of catecholamine and gas transmitter research, particularly their interactions in relation to hypertension. Current evidence shows that the gas transmitters nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide modulate catecholamine biosynthesis and release through both shared and distinct mechanisms. This regulation is highly dependent on concentration, cellular context, and mode of delivery. Additionally, this review explores hypoxic signaling as a link between catecholamines and gas transmitters. Together, these findings highlight a complex and context-dependent regulatory signaling between gas transmitters and catecholamines. Further mechanistic studies investigating endogenous signaling are required to elucidate these interactions and their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

articles.title: Rectal ozone insufflation modulates gut microbiota: improving lung function in mice with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: Ozone rectal insufflation possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects and is used for the treatment and prevention of diseases. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ozone rectal insufflation on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and explore the potential underlying mechanisms from the perspective of gut microbiology. A mouse chronic obstructive pulmonary disease model was established by intratracheal spraying of lipopolysaccharide and elastase. Mice received ozone rectal insufflation intervention following modeling. We found that ozone rectal insufflation improved pulmonary function, alleviated emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis, and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. Additionally, ozone rectal insufflation modulated the pathogenic-to-beneficial gut bacteria ratio in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. The treatment also led to an upregulation of short-chain fatty acids. The fecal microbiota transplantation results further confirmed that the gut microbiota of ozone rectal insufflation-treated mice was sufficient to attenuate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms. In summary, our findings indicate that ozone rectal insufflation enhances lung function and reduces inflammation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice by modulating the gut microbiota and its associated metabolites.

articles.title: Hydrogen-rich water combined with traditional Chinese medicine compound in the treatment of kidney stones: a randomized controlled prospective clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The formation and development of kidney stones are related to abnormal urine metabolism, oxidative stress and inflammation. Hydrogen-rich water has clear efficacy in antioxidant and improving inflammatory status, while Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula is a clinically effective traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation for treating kidney stones. This randomized controlled prospective clinical trial from July 2025 to March 2026 at the Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine examined the effect of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula on kidney stones. The included 100 patients with kidney stones were randomly divided into blank, hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine, and Chinese medicines groups. The patients received drinking hydrogen-rich water and/or Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula daily for 12 weeks. All subjects received basic treatment following the guidelines. Imaging examination, urine metabolism testing, renal function, inflammation and oxidative stress index, blood routine and liver function are used to detect the efficacy and safety of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. Results showed that the total effective rate of kidney stone treatment in blank group, Chinese medicines group, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine group and hydrogen-rich water group was 28%, 76%, 80% and 32%. The Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula can partially alleviate the oxidative stress, uric acid metabolism and urinary magnesium levels of patients with kidney stone and improve the function of renal tubules. The hydrogen-rich water therapy showed only efficacy in improving glutathione reductase but the combination of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula has shown superior efficacy in improving oxidative stress and related metabolic factors of blood uric acid and urine stones, as well as in renal tubular function. The results indicate that the addition of hydrogen-rich water can improve urinary metabolism and oxidative stress status in the treatment of kidney stones with Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. The study was registered at the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No. ITMCTR2025001446).

articles.title: Ambient particulate matter pollution and stroke burden.
articles.abstract: As a major component of air pollution, ambient particulate matter pollution has rarely been studied with respect to its global stroke burden. This study aims to evaluate the global stroke incidence, mortality, and health inequalities related to ambient particulate matter pollution from 1990 to 2021. Utilizing the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, we analyzed global stroke-related mortality, disability-adjusted life years, and their age-standardized rates. The estimated annual percentage change was calculated using a linear regression model. Health inequalities were measured using the concentration index and slope index of inequality. Between 1990 and 2021, global ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke deaths and disability-adjusted life years increased by 107% and 101% respectively, yet age-standardized rates declined. China experienced the largest increases in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, Vietnam had the fastest rise in age-standardized mortality rates, the Russian Federation saw the steepest declines in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, and Estonia had the most rapid drop in age-standardized mortality rate. Middle socio-demographic index locations accounted for 46% of the global stroke burden, with age-standardized mortality rates and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years surpassing those in high socio-demographic index locations. From 1990 to 2021, age-standardized disability-adjusted life years rose in low-middle socio-demographic index locations but fell in high socio-demographic index locations. While the concentration index signaled an improvement in global inequality, the slope index of inequality in 2021 worsened compared with that in 1990. Between 1990 and 2021, the global burden of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke declined. However, substantial disparities persisted across different regions, sexes, and nations. For ongoing and future research efforts, priority should be given to high-risk populations and regions, while also developing innovative interventions to further reduce the incidence of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke and enhance patient outcomes.

articles.title: Microbeamformer-aware layout optimization of a 2D intracardiac echocardiography array for grating-lobe suppression.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) has emerged as a promising imaging modality for interventional cardiology. However, catheter-based 2D ICE probes are subject to strict vascular-access constraints, which limit the transducer aperture and independent channel count, leading to spatial undersampling and pronounced grating-lobe (GL) artifacts. This work investigates microbeamformer-aware array-layout optimization for GL suppression in 2D ICE arrays. Using a hybrid analog-digital microbeamformer architecture, the proposed design maps 768 array elements to 64 system channels while retaining the intended transmit focus. Under manufacturable kerf constraints, simulated annealing is used to optimize the element spacing along the elevational direction. With a minimum kerf width of 0.015 mm, the maximum GL level at a focal distance of 50 mm and a common steering angle of θ=φ=45° is reduced from -16.04 dB to -20.97 dB, with the main-lobe full width at half maximum nearly unchanged. Along the evaluated common-angle steering path, θ=φ=0°-45°, the GL reduction increases from 3.15 to 4.93 dB and is accompanied by a 5.60-6.90 dB increase in the maximum near-focus sidelobe level. Numerical phantom imaging simulations further demonstrate reduced GL-related artifacts, with the artifact-to-background contrast ratio decreased by up to 6.98 dB. As an exploratory, layout-preserving alternative to kerf optimization, nonuniform subaperture grouping reduces the maximum GL by 4.07 dB at θ=φ=45° without changing the physical element positions. These results demonstrate the potential of microbeamformer-aware layout optimization for balancing channel reduction, structured GL suppression, and fabrication constraints in miniaturized 2D ICE arrays.

articles.title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health.
articles.abstract: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.

articles.title: ROS-responsive H2S-releasing quaternized chitosan dental implant coating for improved soft tissue integration, antibacterial and immunomodulatory capacities.
articles.abstract: Early and stable soft tissue integration is a prerequisite for the long-term success of dental implants. Crucially, the formation of this biological seal is closely associated with bacterial invasion and the modulation of the local immune microenvironment. Herein, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogen sulfide (H2S)-releasing quaternized chitosan (QCS) coating on the transmucosal interface of Ti-6Al-4V implants, termed TC4/PQCS/H2S. This coating exhibited favorable biocompatibility, enhancing the adhesion of human gingival epithelial cells (HGECs) and human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs), and improving soft tissue compatibility. Additionally, the TC4/PQCS/H2S possessed potent antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, and oral anaerobic pathogens, with effective suppression of biofilm formation. Furthermore, the TC4/PQCS/H2S enhanced cellular antioxidant defense and activated the Nrf2 pathway. It also promoted macrophage polarization toward the pro-healing M2 phenotype, with the involvement of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. Overall, this study presents an efficient surface modification strategy that integrates cell-adhesive, antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions, demonstrating great potential for soft tissue integration.

articles.title: Synergistic antibacterial and osteogenic properties of micro-arc oxidation GO@Ag/SF composite coatings for the repair of infectious bone defects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration of titanium-based implants remain major clinical challenges. Conventional drug-loaded coatings often fail to simultaneously achieve long-term antibacterial activity and the construction of an osteogenic microenvironment.

METHODS: In this study, a graphene oxide-supported silver nanoparticle/silk fibroin (GO@Ag/SF) composite coating was developed and modified via micro-arc oxidation. By precisely controlling the GO/AgNO3 volume ratio, the antibacterial and osteogenic performances of the coatings were systematically evaluated. A rat model of infectious bone defect was employed to verify the in vivo therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: The optimized GO@Ag-2/SF coating exhibited pH-responsive sustained Ag+ release, with cumulative release increasing from 0.23 μg/mL under physiological conditions to 0.69 μg/mL under acidic conditions over 672 h. Under NIR irradiation, the coating reached 59.8°C within 10 min and achieved potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, with inhibition rates up to 98.3 ± 1.2%. The GO@Ag-2/SF coating also promoted osteogenic differentiation by enhancing ALP activity, collagen secretion, calcium mineralization, and the expression of RUNX-2, ALP, COL-I, and OCN. In vivo, GO@Ag-2/SF reduced inflammatory infiltration and improved peri-implant bone regeneration, with increased BIC, BV/TV, and Tb.Th and reduced Tb.Sp. Moreover, pull-out testing demonstrated the highest bone-implant mechanical fixation in the GO@Ag-2/SF group, confirming enhanced functional osseointegration in the infected bone defect model.

CONCLUSION: Through the synergistic effects of its components, the GO@Ag/SF coating established a dynamic antibacterial-osteogenic balance, offering a promising strategy for the repair of infectious bone defects.

articles.title: Photothermal-magnetic dual-activated Janus dressing for microenvironment purification and wireless electrically triggered healing with reduced scar formation.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic scarring remains a major clinical challenge that impedes functional wound regeneration. Although electrical stimulation (ES) shows great promise in activating endogenous repair pathways and suppressing fibrosis, excessive exudate and bacterial infection in chronic wounds not only exacerbate inflammation but also disrupt interfacial electrical contact, thereby attenuating the efficacy of in situ-generated ES. To address this, we designed an electroactive and antibacterial Janus dressing that integrated active microenvironmental purification with wireless ES, ultimately inhibiting scar formation during wound healing. The dressing featured electroactive cotton gauze with asymmetric wettability, achieved via SiO2 and AgNPs@poly 5-hydroxytryptamine/polyethyleneimine (AgNPs@PHT/PEI) coatings to form a unidirectional fluidic gate. Enhanced by a near-infrared-driven mild photothermal effect, this design enabled rapid exudate pumping and evaporation while achieving > 99% antibacterial efficacy within 15 min. Leveraging electromagnetic induction, it delivered tunable wireless microcurrents (13.44-43.18 μA) that upregulated endogenous fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) secretion, which contributes to the downregulation of TGF-β1-driven myofibroblast activation, as evidenced by reduced α-SMA expression. This strategy achieved 99.37% closure of large infected full-thickness rat wounds, featuring highly ordered collagen remodeling. Collectively, this study presents an innovative platform for rapid healing and scar inhibition in chronic wounds, holding promise for broader applications in mitigating fibrotic disorders.

articles.title: A multifunctional DECM/PLMA hydrogel incorporated with engineered PRP-derived exosomes enabling PHD2 silencing for skin wound repair.
articles.abstract: Skin defect repair remains a formidable clinical challenge, characterized by persistent infection risk, compromised angiogenesis, and dysregulated inflammatory responses. Existing hydrogel-based wound dressings fail to simultaneously address structural integrity, antimicrobial efficacy, and spatiotemporal coordination of tissue regeneration. Here, we report the development of a multifunctional bioactive hydrogel system fabricated by integrating decellularized tendon extracellular matrix (DECM) with Poly-L-lysine Methacryloyl (PLMA), and further functionalized with engineered platelet-rich plasma exosomes (PRP-Exos) loaded with siRNA targeting prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2) via electroporation. The inherent cationic nature of PLMA confers robust, broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, while the sustained release of siRNA-PHD2-laden PRP-Exos achieves efficient PHD2 silencing, thereby stabilizing hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and potentiating downstream pro-angiogenic signaling. Concurrently, bioactive cues released from the DECM-based matrix promote fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation and type I collagen biosynthesis, fostering a regeneration-permissive microenvironment. In both normal and diabetic murine full-thickness skin defect models, DEPL@E-SI significantly accelerated wound closure by promoting angiogenesis, inflammation resolution, and extracellular matrix remodeling. These findings establish DEPL@E-SI as a promising therapeutic platform with translational potential for skin tissue engineering and clinical wound management.

articles.title: Orally activatable membrane fusion-mitochondria hitchhiking on intestinal macrophages for targeted therapy of bacterial meningitis and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Targeting the formidable physiological barriers and neuronal damage refractory to conventional bactericidal agents for bacterial meningitis, we engineered an infection microenvironment-activatable membrane fusion-mitochondrial formulation (Mito@MFL-Glu). This formulation integrates endogenous macrophage hitchhiking, lysosomal exocytosis-driven cargo release, and in situ mitochondrial transplantation. Orally administered, its glucan shell is recognized by microfold cells, enabling macrophage-mediated transport across the blood-brain barrier and chemotactic accumulation at infectious foci. During macrophage uptake, stimulation of the Dectin-1 by the glucan shell sustains intracellular Ca2+ levels. Upon reaching the infectious lesion, the pro-inflammatory microenvironment induces macrophage polarization toward an M1 phenotype, which further elevates intracellular Ca2+ levels. The synergy of these two sequential Ca2+ concentration events cooperatively triggers TFEB-mediated lysosomal exocytosis, resulting in a cargo efflux efficiency of 43.3%. Elevated local reactive oxygen species (ROS) cleave the ROS-responsive linker, detaching the glucan shell and exposing the fusogenic lipid bilayer. This activated layer then directly fuses with damaged neuron and microglial membranes, delivering exogenous mitochondria into the cytosol while bypassing lysosomal degradation and achieving a transplantation efficiency exceeding 36% within 1 h, whereas naked mitochondria show much lower efficiency. Concurrently, the liberated cefotaxime eliminates pathogens, culminating in a synergistic and non-invasive oral closed-loop bactericidal and neuroreparative strategy in a murine meningitis model.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid-cerium nanocatalysts enable oxygenation-enhanced ROS neutralization and PET imaging-guided therapy for acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is driven by a vicious interplay among excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and persistent renal hypoxia, which collectively disrupt redox homeostasis and exacerbate tubular injury. However, current therapeutic strategies primarily provide supportive care and fail to simultaneously modulate these interconnected pathological stressors. Herein, we report a cerium-doped rosmarinic acid nanosystem (RA/Ce NPs) formed via self-polymerization that catalytically eliminates ROS while simultaneously generating oxygen to reprogram the pathological renal microenvironment. The ultrasmall RA/Ce NPs enable efficient chelator-free 89Zr radiolabeling for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Redox-switchable Ce3+/Ce4+ centers confer robust catalytic activity and ROS-responsive biodegradation, ensuring potent antioxidation with safe clearance. RA/Ce NPs suppress intracellular ROS, preserve mitochondrial membrane potential, and protect against oxidative injury in vitro. In rhabdomyolysis-induced AKI mice, PET imaging reveals pronounced renal accumulation, while treatment markedly alleviates tubular damage, oxidative stress and hypoxia, leading to restored renal function with excellent biocompatibility. This work presents a natural-product-derived catalytic nanoplatform integrating antioxidation, oxygenation, imaging and biodegradability, offering a promising strategy for precision therapy of AKI.

articles.title: Retrievable "sea-island" microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel devices: augmented oxygen transport and anti-fibrosis for sustaining islet survival.
articles.abstract: Islet encapsulation is a transformative strategy for type 1 diabetes (T1D) cellular therapy, enabling islet transplantation without lifelong immunosuppression. However, macroscale encapsulation faces prominent challenges: poor surgical retrieval, hypoxia, and foreign body response (FBR)-induced fibrosis, which severely compromise clinical translation. Herein, we develop a sea-island microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel device via copolymerization of siloxane monomer SiGMA, zwitterionic monomer carboxybetaine acrylamide (CBAA), and hydrogen-bonding monomer N-acryloyl glycinamide (NAGA). Notably, NAGA enhances hydrogel structural stability via strong H-bonds, reinforcing network and mechanical integrity to facilitate safe retrieval; importantly, NAGA's hydrogen bonding crosslinks allow the hydrogel device to be heat-sealed, preventing cell leakage and maintaining immunoisolation. The incorporation of SiGMA induces hydrophobic phase separation, generating silicone-rich polymer microdomains that enhance oxygen permeability to alleviate islet hypoxia, while zwitterionic CBAA significantly improves antifouling performance and mitigates fibrotic encapsulation by suppressing the host FBR. After 8 weeks of implantation in mice and beagle dogs, the device exhibits minimal fibrotic encapsulation and can be readily retrieved. Notably, even without pre-vascularization or immunosuppression, the transplanted islets in diabetic mice sustain normoglycemia for up to 400 days. These results demonstrate a robust retrievable encapsulation device that addresses key bottlenecks in islet transplantation, advancing its potential translation for T1D.

articles.title: A hierarchical, pH-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform for synergistic microenvironment reprogramming and attenuation of inflammatory periodontal bone loss.
articles.abstract: Conventional periodontitis therapies are limited by their inability to concurrently address the interconnected challenges of persistent bacterial infection, excessive oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. To overcome this, we developed an injectable, pH-responsive nanocomposite polypeptide hydrogel, PepGel@ZnO-PLP, through rational molecular interface engineering. The system is constructed by integrating poly-L-proline (PLP)-functionalized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-PLP) into a poly-L-glutamate containing polypeptide network (PepGel) via dynamic Zn2+-carboxylate coordination. This critical PLP interface ensures colloidal stability of ZnO nanoparticles and enables the formation of a homogeneous, pH-responsive release network. In the acidic periodontal microenvironment, the hydrogel exhibits potent antibacterial and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging activities. Furthermore, via PLP-enabled interfacial engineering, PepGel@ZnO-PLP reprograms inflammatory macrophage immunometabolism by driving a glycolytic-suppressed metabolic state that establishes metabolic homeostasis toward a reparative M2 phenotype, a process in which the PI3K-Akt pathway may be involved. In a murine periodontitis model, PepGel@ZnO-PLP adheres to periodontal defects, effectively disrupting the infection-inflammation cycle and leading to significant alveolar bone preservation. This work underscores the power of precise molecular-level design for holistically reprogramming the pathological microenvironment and offers a novel nanocomposite hydrogel for ameliorating inflammatory periodontal bone loss.

articles.title: Biomimetic stress granules replenish lysosomal repair to reinstate macrophage immunometabolic antibacterial programs.
articles.abstract: Severe intracellular bacterial infection can progressively compromise lysosomal defence in macrophages, yet the underlying repair bottleneck remains unclear. Here we identify a time-dependent exhaustion of stress granule (SG)-associated lysosomal repair during sustained infection: progressive depletion of core SG components, including G3BP1 and galectin-3 (Gal-3), undermines lysosomal membrane resealing, resulting in lysosomal deacidification and persistent cytosolic acidification. This pH imbalance suppresses glycolytic metabolism and blunts macrophage pro-inflammatory antibacterial programs, thereby enabling intracellular bacterial persistence. Since this exhausted repair module cannot be readily reconstituted by conventional pharmacological or genetic approaches, we engineer biomimetic stress granules (BSGs), Gal-3-functionalized nanodiscs cloaked in acid-responsive fusogen-expressing macrophage membrane vesicles (Gal3-NDs@EF-MNVs), to achieve sequential targeting and cytosolic delivery to damaged lysosomes. BSGs stabilize membrane lesions, suppress lysosomal leakage and restore lysosomal acidification, pH homeostasis and metabolic fitness, thereby recapitulating the 'plugging' behavior of native stress granules at sites of membrane injury. This work establishes biomimetic organelle repair as a general, materials-driven paradigm to restore innate immunity against intracellular infections - without escalating antibiotics or genetic manipulation.

articles.title: Exosomes in brain diseases: Mechanisms, advances, and perspectives.
articles.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a major biological obstacle limiting the effective delivery of therapeutics for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Although conventional drug delivery approaches have achieved continuous advances, their clinical translation is frequently restricted by limited brain penetration, insufficient target specificity, and systemic adverse effects. Exosomes, endogenous extracellular vesicles (EVs) involved in intercellular communication, have emerged as promising candidates for CNS therapeutic delivery owing to their favorable biocompatibility, relatively low immunogenicity, and potential ability to interact with biological barriers. In this review, we first summarize the structural characteristics of the BBB and the mechanisms underlying exosome-BBB interactions and transport. We then discuss current strategies for exosome isolation, characterization, and engineering, highlighting how these approaches influence therapeutic performance and translational feasibility. Subsequently, we analyze recent advances in exosome-based therapies for major CNS disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases, brain tumors, and ischemic stroke, with emphasis on how distinct pathological environments guide the design of exosome cargos, targeting strategies, and functional modifications. Finally, we discuss key challenges associated with clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, pharmacokinetic evaluation, safety assessment, and regulatory considerations. This review provides a pathology-driven and engineering-guided perspective for understanding the rational design and future development of exosome-based therapeutics for CNS disorders.

articles.title: Deep Learning-driven synergistic engineering of PET hydrolase for post-consumer PET depolymerization.
articles.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) offers a promising route to mitigate the increasingly severe problem of plastic pollution. However, the development of highly efficient PET hydrolases capable of processing post-consumer PET remains a critical challenge. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) provide new opportunities to accelerate the enzyme engineering of PET hydrolases. Here, we report a systematic computational redesign of the PET hydrolase NI (ThcCut1-AICCG-H185N/F189I) using the deep-learning framework, EITLEM-Kinetics. By integrating mutation free-energy constraints with kinetic parameter prediction, the framework enables simultaneous optimization of catalytic activity and thermostability. A total of nine beneficial substitution sites were identified and experimentally validated that overcoming the activity-stability trade-off. Combinatorial iteration yielded an optimal variant, NI-E65K/H107Y/A2R/L33F (NI-KYRF), which exhibited an 80% and 90% increase in depolymerization activity toward Gf-PET film and one-step pretreated post-consumer PET (pc-PET powder), respectively, along with a 2.61 °C increase in melting temperature (T m). NI-KYRF displayed a specific activity of 665 μmolTPAeq h-1 mgenzyme -1, representing 2.0- and 1.48-fold improvements over representative high-performance PET hydrolases ICCG and TurboPETase. The depolymerization performance of NI-KYRF towards various post-consumer PET wastes and polyester plastics was significantly improved. At 70 °C, it achieved a 95.5% depolymerization conversion of pc-PET powder within 24 h, and for untreated post-consumer PET film, the conversion reached 80.1%, representing a 2.1-fold improvement in depolymerization efficiency over the parental NI. In addition, enhanced activity toward polyesters plastics, including PBAT and PBT, indicates an expanded substrate scope. Molecular dynamics simulations and structural analysis reveal that these mutations enhance enzyme performance through synergistic mechanisms. Overall, this study establishes a deep learning-guided computational design framework based on EITLEM-Kinetics and demonstrates its effectiveness and broad potential for engineering high-performance PET hydrolases.

articles.title: Global stability analysis of within-host Zika virus-chikungunya virus co-infection with CTL immune responses.
articles.abstract: We formulate and analyse a mathematical model for the within-host co-infection dynamics of Zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), incorporating latently infected cells and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) immune responses. We establish the nonnegativity and boundedness of solutions. Using the next-generation matrix method, we derive the basic reproduction numbers (RZL) and (RCL) for the ZIKV and CHIKV submodels, respectively, and the overall reproduction number (R0L=max{RZL,RCL}). Invasion reproduction numbers, (RZL,inv) and (RCL,inv), are derived to characterise the ability of either virus to invade an established infection. Global stability of the equilibria is established using Lyapunov functions. We investigate three therapeutic protocols: antiviral treatment blocking viral entry, treatment reducing viral production, and IL-2 therapy enhancing CTL responses. Sensitivity analysis of (RZL) and (RCL) is performed, and numerical simulations support the stability results. Simulations indicate that combined antiviral and immune-based interventions suppress co-infection by reducing viral replication and enhancing immune-mediated clearance.

articles.title: A clinical-radiological model for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbation of COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) has emerged as a promising tool for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) phenotyping. However, its prognostic value in acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD) remains insufficiently explored, and existing risk stratification models have limited integration of imaging-derived metrics. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic model that integrates multidimensional clinical variables with QCT-derived metrics, and to compare its predictive performance with traditional clinical scores for in-hospital mortality in AECOPD.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥40 years hospitalized with severe AECOPD were enrolled from September 2010 to October 2024, with collection of demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory indices, and chest CT imaging data. The cohort was randomly split into training and testing sets (7:3). Candidate predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Four classification models were developed and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Discriminative performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and compared with conventional clinical scores.

RESULTS: A total of 465 patients with AECOPD were included, of whom 47 (10.1%) died during hospitalization. Five independent predictors were identified: confusion, lymphocyte count <0.8 × 109/L, chronic heart failure, white blood cell count ≥10 × 109/L, and reduced pulmonary vascular fractal dimension. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI, 0.738-0.965) in the testing set, significantly outperforming other models and established clinical scores.

CONCLUSIONS: A predictive model integrating QCT-derived metrics with clinical features improved AECOPD in-hospital mortality prediction over traditional scores, supporting its utility for individualized risk stratification and management.

articles.title: PmZapA orchestrates zinc homeostasis and pleiotropic stress responses to drive pathogenicity in Talaromyces marneffei.
articles.abstract: Zinc homeostasis is critical for pathogenic microbes during their interactions with hosts. In Aspergillus nidulans, the transcription factor ZapA serves as a key regulator of zinc uptake. However, the function of ZapA in the thermally dimorphic pathogen Talaromyces marneffei remains largely unexplored. In this study, we identified and characterized the ZapA homolog in T. marneffei. Our results demonstrate that PmZapA acts as a master regulator of zinc homeostasis by directly controlling the expression of the zinc transporter encoding genes. Deletion of PmzapA severely impaired growth under Zinc - conditions and reduced pigment production. Notably, in a Galleria mellonella larval infection model, the ΔPmzapA strain exhibited significantly attenuated virulence. However, the reduced pathogenicity was not solely attributable to defective zinc transport, as additional pleiotropic effects were detected. Specifically, the ΔPmzapA strain showed impaired reactive oxygen species (ROS) clearance capability, as well as increased susceptibility to cell wall stress and alkaline pH. Integrated RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analysis revealed that PmZapA governs a broad regulatory network, directly and indirectly modulating pathways involved in redox homeostasis, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, as well as carbon metabolism. Collectively, our work identifies PmZapA as a novel virulence determinant in T. marneffei.

articles.title: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation of the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and interstitial lung diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No instruments exist to assess palliative care knowledge among Portuguese with chronic respiratory diseases.

AIM: To translate and cross-culturally adapt the Palliative Care Knowledge Scale (PaCKS) into European Portuguese and explore its measurement properties in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung diseases (ILD).

METHODS: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedures were followed. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α); test-retest reliability [intraclass correlation coefficient with 95% confidence interval (ICC2,1 [95% CI]), standard error of measurement (SEM/SEM%), minimal detectable change at 95% confidence level (MDC95/MDC%) and Bland-Altman method]; floor/ceiling effects; and, construct validity [convergent/divergent, correlation (Spearman's - rs) with the Bristol COPD Knowledge Questionnaire (BCKQ)/modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea questionnaire/lung function] were evaluated.

RESULTS: Two forward translations/back-translations were conducted. Five experts approved the prefinal version. Cognitive debriefing involved 12 participants. Measurement properties were analysed in 102 people with COPD and 54 with ILD (73.1% male; 67.6 ± 10.0 years). PaCKS score was 11.0 [9.0-12.0] and 10.0 [8.8-11.0] in COPD and ILD, respectively. Internal consistency was acceptable (αCOPD = 0.76; αILD = 0.80). The test-retest reliability was good in COPD (ICC2,1 0.84 [0.77-0.89]) and ranged from good to excellent in ILD (ICC2,1 0.89 [0.78-0.94]). SEM/SEM% and MDC95/MDC% were 1.0/9.6% and 2.8/26.6%, and 1.0/10.1% and 2.7/28.0% in COPD and ILD, respectively. The Bland-Altman method did not suggest systematic bias, with 95% limits of agreement of approximately ±3.0. No floor/ceiling effects were observed, except for a ceiling effect in COPD (20.6%). The PaCKS/BCKQ correlation was significant, positive and moderate (rs = 0.40, p < 0.001) in COPD. Other correlations were non-significant and ranged from negligible to weak.

CONCLUSION: The European Portuguese PaCKS is now available and provides reliable and valid data on palliative care knowledge in COPD and ILD.

articles.title: Gut virome remodeling after fecal microbiota transplantation is associated with virus-bacteria co-variation and metabolic response in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modifies gut bacterial composition and improves metabolic outcomes in subjects with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObT2), but bacterial changes alone do not fully explain the heterogeneity in clinical response. We performed virus-like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing coupled with bulk-DNA metagenomic sequencing on longitudinal fecal samples from a randomized controlled FMT trial in ObT2. Using random forest classification, post-FMT virome changes showed accuracy comparable to bacteriome changes (84.8% vs 81.4%) in distinguishing LDL responders from non-responders. Donor-derived viral contig engraftment was detected in 64.7% (11/17) of recipients receiving FMT alone and 58.8% (10/17) receiving FMT with lifestyle intervention (LSI), versus 5.6% (1/18) in the sham with LSI group. FMT was associated with increased virome diversity, compositional shifts toward the donor virome, and coordinated virus-bacteria associations, with most responsive viral contigs classified as Caudoviricetes. FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

articles.title: High cardiometabolic burden among people with HIV and obesity in Peru.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiometabolic disease has been studied in people with HIV, but evidence focused on people with HIV and obesity remains limited. This study assessed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, metabolic abnormalities, markers of inflammation, and cardiovascular risk scores among people with HIV and obesity.

METHODS: We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study in clinically stable people with HIV aged ≥35 years and BMI >30 kg/m² in Lima-Callao, Peru, in 2024.

RESULTS: Participants enroled were 126; 77.7% were male, mean age was 50.6 years, mean time on antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 12.4 years, mean CD4 count was 759.8 cells/µL, and 97.6% had HIV-RNA <200 copies/µL. Mean BMI was 34.0. Clinical cardiovascular disease history was uncommon (2.4%); however, carotid Doppler ultrasound showed atherosclerotic changes in 34.4% (increased CIMT or carotid plaque), which associated with older age and longer time of ART. Abnormal glucose metabolism was identified in 89.7%, dyslipidemia in 82.5%, metabolic syndrome in 50.8%, elevated inflammatory markers in 28.2%, and low apolipoprotein A1 in 22.6%. Only 8.1% had normal findings across all evaluations. High cardiovascular risk was observed in 19.4% by Framingham, 9.4% by ACC/AHA, and 75.4% by HIV-CARDIO-PREDICT score.

CONCLUSIONS: This population of middle-aged, clinically stable people with HIV and obesity presented substantial burden of subclinical atherosclerosis and metabolic abnormalities despite low reported cardiovascular disease history. Cardiovascular risk estimates varied substantially across scores, with an HIV-specific score identifying a much higher proportion of patients as high risk than general-population scores. Targeted evaluation and timely preventive management may help reduce cardiometabolic complications.

articles.title: Placental mitochondrial impairment in preeclampsia patients.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder characterized by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation, accompanied by end-organ dysfunction with or without proteinuria. Affecting approximately 5-7% of pregnancies worldwide, it remains a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Despite decades of research, the underlying pathophysiology of preeclampsia remains incompletely understood. However, increasing evidence implicates placental mitochondrial oxidative stress in its pathogenesis. In this review, we summarize the current literature pertaining to ultrastructural evidence of mitochondrial damage, defects in oxidative phosphorylation and electron transport chain activity, and alterations in reactive oxygen species production, antioxidant defense, and mitochondrial biogenesis. Finally, we discuss translational considerations and highlight how therapeutic strategies targeted at restoring mitochondrial function may represent a promising approach for managing preeclampsia.

articles.title: Intratumoral Fusobacterium nucleatum promotes ferroptosis resistance and a disulfide-stress-associated vulnerability under glucose restriction.
articles.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) is an intracellular oncogenic bacterium implicated in multiple cancers. Although Fn has been linked to resistance to anticancer therapies, its effects on therapies targeting metabolic cell-death programs remain unclear. Here, we show that intratumoral Fn abundance is positively associated with SLC7A11 expression and that Fn infection attenuates Era- and RSL3-induced ferroptosis in tumor cells. Live-versus-killed, donor-based, and pharmacological evidence suggests that H2S generated during Fn infection contributes to SLC7A11 induction and engagement of the downstream GSH/GPX4 axis. Fn infection also reduces lipid-peroxide and Fe2⁺ accumulation and is accompanied by ACSL4 downregulation and FTH1 upregulation. Fn-infected cells display increased glucose uptake and a heightened dependence on glucose. Under glucose-replete conditions, Fn-infected cells are relatively resistant to ferroptosis, whereas glucose deprivation exposes a conditional vulnerability accompanied by disulfide stress. RSL3 further sensitized Fn-infected cells to glucose restriction, and combined GPX4 inhibition with the GLUT1 inhibitor BAY876 enhanced antitumor activity in Fn-infected solid-tumor models. These findings identify a nutrient-dependent metabolic liability associated with Fn infection and support further evaluation of combined glucose-transport and GPX4 inhibition in appropriately controlled models.

articles.title: High ex vivo recombination rate of African swine fever virus in porcine alveolar macrophages.
articles.abstract: Using fluorescently labeled African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) strains, a high (~0.2) quasi-recombinant frequency (qRF3-4) was detected ex vivo during 3-4 replication cycles in naïve porcine alveolar macrophages (PAM). While co-infection and recombination frequencies remained low in PAM, they increased sharply between the second and fourth viral cycles. Infection multiplicity and synchronicity significantly influenced ASFV recombination frequency, which correlated positively with genetic distance. Crossing the ASFV/Lv17/WB/Rie1 mutants yielded a saturation curve resembling the Haldane mapping function, plateauing at ~20% recombination frequency at 160 kbp. Crossing less homologous strains (ASFV/Lv17/WB/Rie1 × ASFV/NHV/P68) reduced the recombination frequency; however, at large marker distances (140 kbp), it approached values (0.18) observed in homologous strains. A novel mathematical model estimated the average co-infection rate to be 0.47 after three viral cycles. Empirical application of the model revealed that 1 centimorgan translates to ~550-1650 bp, meaning offspring virions from a single cell undergo an average of 1.15-3.45 recombination events. This high recombination rate is consistent with in vivo observations and has critical implications for ASFV prevention and vaccination strategies. Such genomic plasticity can facilitate rapid viral evolution, potentially undermining the efficacy of live-attenuated vaccines globally.

articles.title: D-enantiomeric β-casein 197 disrupts biofilm-associated infection of MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii through superior LPS binding and host cell protection.
articles.abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. L-form antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are rapidly degraded by proteases, whereas D-enantiomeric peptides offer enhanced resistance to proteases. Here, we synthesized L- and D-β-casein 197, a milk-derived AMP, and systematically compared their antibiofilm activities against eight clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii. The D-form reduced biofilm biomass by up to 83% during formation and by up to 88% in preformed biofilms. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the D-form caused more extensive membrane disruption, as demonstrated by flow cytometry and transmission electron microscopy. Isothermal titration calorimetry showed that the D-form bound LPS with higher affinity (KD 0.8 μM vs 3.1 μM), and molecular docking identified additional hydrogen bonds with lipid A. The D-form also more effectively inhibited bacterial motility. Both peptides exhibited low cytotoxicity toward cells (>90% viability at 100 μM), and the D-form reduced bacteria-induced cytotoxicity and bacterial internalization in infected macrophages more effectively than the L-form. In a Galleria mellonella infection model, D-β-casein 197 significantly improved survival against P. aeruginosa no. R1 and A. baumannii no. 13 challenge over 96 h compared to the L-form and untreated infected controls, while larval survival remained comparable to PBS controls, indicating negligible host toxicity. These findings identify D-β-casein 197 as a potent antibiofilm peptide against MDR Gram-negative biofilms, with enhanced activity, and LPS-neutralization assays confirmed that its antimicrobial potency is, at least in part, attributable to its stronger LPS binding affinity.

articles.title: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant: one case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report a case child of Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant in a child and to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment methods, and prognosis of this syndrome based on a literature review.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of a child girl with Pacak-Zhuang syndrome admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital in July 2019. Using the search terms 'Pacak-Zhuang syndrome', 'EPAS1', 'HIF-2α', 'HIF-2A', and 'Polycythemia-paraganglioma syndrome', relevant literature was retrieved from PubMed and Web of Science. The clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, treatment plans, and outcomes of patients with this syndrome were analyzed.

RESULTS: A 4-year-old girl had recurrent hypertension, polycythemia and renal hilar masses. Diagnosis was confirmed by imaging, biochemical detection and paraffin tissue genetic testing. She received three operations for paragangliomas; pathology showed CgA(+), Syn(+), NSE(+) and Ki‑67 ≤5%. Follow-up revealed tumor recurrence, but the condition improved with oral temozolomide. Combined with 10 retrieved articles, 18 patients (4 males,14 females, mean age 25 years) were analyzed. Polycythemia was the cardinal manifestation. All patients received surgery, and 10 suffered uncontrolled tumor recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome is a rare disorder involving the neuroendocrine and hematopoietic systems, often initially presenting with 'polycythemia'. Most cases are sporadic, with no apparent familial inheritance or history of other neuroendocrine tumors. When encountering pediatric patients with unexplained hypertension accompanied by polycythemia symptoms, the possibility of this syndrome should be considered, and further imaging studies and genetic testing are required for definitive diagnosis.

articles.title: Acute liver injury is triggered by dysbiosis and microbial translocation involving gut-liver axis.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition that can progress to chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma, yet therapeutic options remain limited. Here, we investigated how hepatotoxin-induced gut-liver dysbiosis drives hepatic inflammation through microbial crosstalk. Using three murine ALI models, we assessed liver injury, intestinal barrier integrity, microbial composition along the gut-liver axis, and immune activation. Each hepatotoxin recapitulated distinct features of human ALI and induced unique patterns of hepatic and intestinal injury, enabling the progressive translocation of live bacteria from the gut to the liver and bloodstream. ALI was consistently associated with depletion of commensal taxa (Lactobacillaceae, Ruminococcaceae, and Bifidobacteriaceae) and enrichment of opportunistic pathogens (Enterococcaceae, Clostridiaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Burkholderiaceae). Dysbiosis also involved reduced gut bacteriophages and the expansion of viral families, including Retroviridae and Herpesviridae, in the liver and blood. Transplantation of the fecal or liver microbiota from ALI mice into microbiota-depleted recipients reproduced liver injury, immune activation, and intestinal barrier disruption, demonstrating that dysbiotic microbial communities alone are sufficient to trigger hepatic inflammation. These communities activated Th1/Th17 associated pathways (NF-κB, IL-17, TGF-β, and antigen presentation networks) and expanded pro-inflammatory immune populations. A key advance of this study is the direct comparison of fecal- versus liver-derived microbiota, revealing distinct mechanistic roles for each in driving liver pathology. Across all models, hepatotoxin-induced intestinal barrier breakdown drives gut-liver dysbiosis, microbial translocation, and immune-mediated liver injury. These findings uncover a unifying mechanism by which microbial imbalance reprograms hepatic immunity and accelerates ALI progression.

articles.title: Association of serum creatinine-to-albumin ratio with hyperandrogenemia and low sex hormone-binding globulin in women of reproductive age: a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperandrogenemia (HA) and low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) are core features of polycystic ovary syndrome. The creatinine-to-albumin ratio (CAR), a simple renal-nutritional marker linked to female infertility, has not been studied in relation to HA or low SHBG.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the association of CAR with low SHBG and HA, defined by the free androgen index (FAI), in U.S. women of reproductive age.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016, we included 683 women aged 18-49 years. CAR (serum creatinine/albumin) was categorized into tertiles; low SHBG was defined as < 30 nmol/L and HA as FAI ≥ 75th percentile. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used, with multiple imputation (m = 5) as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: In Model 1 (age, race/ethnicity, education, income), the highest CAR tertile was associated with low SHBG (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.49-5.75; P = 0.003; P for trend = 0.004) and FAI-defined HA (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.05-3.34; P = 0.036; P for trend = 0.044). In Model 2 (plus smoking, BMI, low HDL-C), associations attenuated (OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.05-3.64 for low SHBG; 1.24, 95% CI 0.65-2.34 for HA-FAI). HA defined by total testosterone was not associated with CAR.

CONCLUSION: Higher CAR was associated with low SHBG and FAI-defined HA after demographic adjustment, with attenuation after metabolic adjustment, suggesting confounding by shared metabolic factors. As CAR derives from routine laboratory tests, it may be a practical marker of reproductive metabolic risk; the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Sustaining nursing practice in Greenland: insights from a positive deviance study on motivation, resilience, and holistic care in arctic healthcare.
articles.abstract: Health disparities in the Arctic remain substantial, with Inuit populations experiencing shorter life expectancy and higher morbidity than global averages. Nurse shortage exacerbates these challenges, and Greenland continues to rely on nurses from other countries. Despite these constraints, health outcomes have improved over time, including increased life expectancy, enhanced diabetes care, and better child growth indicators. To sustain professional well-being and retention in the Greenlandic nursing workforce, this study explores how nurses deliver high-quality care under constrained conditions, and what motivates them to remain in healthcare using a positive deviance framework. Ethnographic fieldwork was conducted across five Greenland regions, involving participant observations and interviews with nurses and students across professional roles. Across backgrounds and seniority, nurses demonstrated a shared passion for their work, with patient encounters central to practice. Resilient communities, shaped through collaboration and humour, supported creative problem-solving and a strong sense of responsibility, extending from individual patients to healthcare and society. Nurses sustain their practice through patient-centred values, community resilience, improvisational competencies, and commitment to societal well-being. Using a positive deviance perspective, insights from effective nursing practices can inform nursing education and Arctic healthcare, improving patient care, job satisfaction, staff retention, and long-term cost efficiency.

articles.title: Low health literacy among individuals with chronic disease in Kalaallit Nunaat: a cross-sectional study with implications for health literacy responsiveness.
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases are an increasing public health challenge in Greenland (Kalaallit Nunaat), requiring self-management and navigation in healthcare information. Health Literacy (HL) refers to the ability to access, understand, and use health information. Low HL is prevalent in other Indigenous populations, negatively affecting self-care, health outcomes, mortality and contributing to social inequalities. Despite health inequalities in Kalaallit Nunaat, HL has not been quantitatively assessed. The aim was to investigate HL among individuals with chronic diseases in Kalaallit Nunaat and assess the HLS19-Q12 questionnaire in Greenlandic (Kalaallisut). This cross-sectional study (25 February - 2 April 2025) included participants (≥18 years) with diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, obesity, and/or asthma. HL was assessed using the concise HLS19-Q12 questionnaire in Kalaallisut and Danish. Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were evaluated using Cronbach's alpha and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). 230 individuals completed the questionnaire, including 28 retests. HL levels were categorised into four levels: inadequate 32.2%, problematic 50%, sufficient 12.4% and excellent 5.4%. The Kalaallisut HLS19-Q12 demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.78-0.93) and test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.71-0.94). Overall, 82.2% of participants had inadequate or problematic HL, highlighting the need for interventions to strengthen HL responsiveness in Kalaallit Nunaat.

articles.title: Reducing period poverty through interventions, innovations, policies and multilevel barriers and facilitators: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Period poverty is a persistent global inequity that undermines health, dignity, education and socioeconomic participation. Although increasingly recognised, evidence on effective responses remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesised menstrual health interventions, innovations and policies, and examined the multilevel barriers and facilitators across low- and middle-income and high-income countries. Following PRISMA 2020 and the SPIDER framework ProQuest Central, Scopus, MEDLINE and PsycINFO were searched for English-language studies from inception to 15 December 2024, identifying 8385 records. After screening, 49 studies were included, comprising interventions, other initiatives, innovations and policy analyses across school, community, workplace, humanitarian and policy contexts. Given substantial heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was undertaken. Effective responses were multidimensional, combining product provision, menstrual education, stigma reduction and enabling infrastructure. Education improved menstrual literacy and confidence, while product-access strategies reduced absenteeism and social withdrawal in specific studies. Innovations including biodegradable and reusable products and community-managed pantries, expanded access but faced WASH constraints, stigma and cultural concerns about insertable products. Policy measures showed promise, but persistent funding and implementation gaps remained. Sustainable progress requires integrated, context-sensitive action combining education, product choice, infrastructure, stigma reduction and effective policy implementation.

articles.title: Pharmacy students' knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 receptor agonist adverse effects in obesity management: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are important therapeutic options for obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite their increasing use, safety concerns remain, and pharmacy students' knowledge of their adverse effects is unclear. This study evaluated pharmacy students' knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 RA adverse effects in obesity management. A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among undergraduate Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) students (1st-7th year) at Umm Al-Qura University, Saudi Arabia, between November and December 2025. A newly developed questionnaire, reviewed by two experts and pilot-tested among 10 students, assessed 17 knowledge and five attitude items covering indications, mechanisms, adverse effects, and clinical scenarios. Of 1,118 eligible students, 296 completed the survey (response rate: 26.5%). Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses were performed using RStudio (version 2024.9.1.394). Among participants (63.9% male), the mean knowledge score was 7.6 ± 4.0/17. Most agreed that adverse effects significantly impact clinical use (59.4%) and supported further education on less common side effects (61.1%). Nausea was the most frequently recognized adverse effect (59.1%), whereas thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodent studies (25.0%) and diabetic retinopathy complications (36.5%) were less commonly identified. Only 37.2% correctly recognized that hypoglycemia is uncommon with GLP-1 RA monotherapy. Higher knowledge scores were significantly associated with greater confidence in knowledge (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.06-1.17; p < 0.001) and stronger endorsement of further education on less common side effects (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.06-1.18; p < 0.001), whereas gender and academic year were not significant predictors of any attitude item. Pharmacy students demonstrated limited knowledge but generally positive attitudes regarding GLP-1 RA safety. These findings highlight the need to strengthen pharmacovigilance and evidence-based medication safety education within pharmacy curricula to improve clinical preparedness and patient counseling.

articles.title: Electrocardiograms and screening echocardiograms in young adults who acquired HIV perinatally and non-perinatally: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifelong exposure to HIV and antiretroviral therapy (ART) may elevate cardiovascular risk as individuals with perinatally acquired HIV transition into adulthood. We evaluated subclinical electrocardiographic (ECG) and echocardiographic abnormalities in this population.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Thailand between 2022-2023. Young adults who acquired HIV perinatally were enroled, alongside age-matched adults who acquired HIV non-perinatally. Participants underwent standard ECG and screening echocardiography.

RESULTS: A total of 62 participants (31 who acquired HIV perinatally and 31 non-perinatally) were included in the study. Of these, 31 (50.0%) were men, and the median (interquartile range; IQR) age was 25.4 (23.9-27.0) years. The median (IQR) CD4 + count was 595 (453-835) cells/mm3. Yong adults with perinatal HIV had longer HIV/ART exposure and greater historical use of zidovudine, stavudine, and protease inhibitors. Abnormal ECG findings were present in participants with perinatally acquired HIV and non-perinatally acquired HIV, including sinus bradycardia (16.1% vs. 12.9%), low-voltage QRS (12.9% vs. 3.2%), ST-T abnormalities (6.5% vs. 3.2%), and QTc prolongation (3.2% vs. 3.2%). Abnormal echocardiograms were observed, including hyperdynamic left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF > 70%) occurring in 9.7% vs. 0.0% (p = 0.238). In multivariable analysis, incomplete virologic suppression (viral load ≥ 200 copies/mL) was independently associated with low-voltage ECG (odds ratio 8.57; 95% confidence interval 1.16-63.30; p = 0.035).

CONCLUSIONS: Subclinical cardiac abnormalities were infrequent and comparable between young adults with perinatally and non-perinatally acquired HIV. Low-voltage ECG was associated with incomplete virologic suppression. Optimising antiretroviral regimens to maintain a suppressed viral load may help reduce subclinical cardiac abnormalities in young people with HIV.

articles.title: A helminth-microbiota metabolic relay promotes disease tolerance.
articles.abstract: Persistent infection by helminths requires limiting inflammatory damage despite incomplete pathogen clearance, yet how helminths mobilize resident microbiota to establish this state remains unclear. Here we identify a cross-kingdom metabolic relay through which Trichinella spiralis promotes systemic disease tolerance. Infection selectively expanded Ligilactobacillus murinus and redirected microbial tryptophan metabolism toward indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), a direct ligand of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Antibiotic perturbation abrogated ILA production, AhR activation and Treg-Th17 remodeling, whereas transfer of helminth-conditioned fecal preparations or supplementation with L. murinus or ILA restored these responses. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of AhR eliminated the protection conferred by T. spiralis, L. murinus and ILA against endotoxin-induced lung injury. In lethal SARS-CoV-2 infection, oral ILA improved survival and limited pulmonary immunopathology without reducing viral burden, thereby uncoupling host protection from pathogen control. In a human COVID-19 cohort, ILA relative abundance remained inversely associated with IFN-γ after adjustment for available clinical covariates. These findings reveal that helminths can reprogram commensal metabolism to govern systemic immune tolerance and identify microbial ILA production as a tractable postbiotic strategy for limiting inflammatory tissue damage.

articles.title: The impact of prophylactic azithromycin on the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome.
articles.abstract: Early-life antibiotic exposure can profoundly impact the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome, with short- and long-term consequences for health. In a large multi-center (n = 28) study of 693 preterm infants, we investigated the effects of 10 d of prophylactic intravenous azithromycin on the gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The AZithromycin ThErapy for Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity (AZTEC) study was a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of preterm infants (born < 30 weeks of gestation), treated from birth for 10 d with either intravenous azithromycin or placebo, and sampled longitudinally for 21 d or discharge. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and quantitative PCR, we show azithromycin reduced microbial diversity and the relative abundance of health-associated Bifidobacterium and increased relative abundances of pathobionts Staphylococcus and Enterobacter/Klebsiella. This early azithromycin treatment increased the number of macrolide-resistant genes, including the presence of erm (C), which persisted for the duration of the study. Probiotic use (at individual unit discretion) increased alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium relative abundance, but did not fully mitigate the effects of azithromycin receipt. Combined azithromycin and probiotics further increased the enrichment of Enterobacter/Klebsiella and total ARGs, including erm(C). These findings highlight the impacts of antibiotic and probiotic use, both important in balancing infection control issues and microbiome disruption and antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.abstract: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

articles.title: Stability and structure-preserving numerical analysis of a stochastic delayed pine wilt disease model.
articles.abstract: Pine wilt disease is a destructive forest disease involving pine trees, pinewood nematodes, and insect vectors. This study develops deterministic and stochastic delayed host-vector models to examine waiting periods and variability in transmission.
