SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02120-1.

articles.title: Effects of chiglitazar on glycemic, lipid, and hepatic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chiglitazar is a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pan-agonist with potential metabolic benefits. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed its efficacy and safety versus placebo or active comparators in adults with metabolic disorders.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to August 2026 for studies assessing chiglitazar in adults with metabolic disorders. Outcomes were pooled via random-effects meta-analysis with 95% confidence intervals, alongside heterogeneity, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Five studies involving 1,457 participants were included. Chiglitazar reduced fasting glucose at 24 weeks (MD - 0.99 mmol/L, 95% CI - 1.75 to - 0.24). HbA1c decreased at 12 weeks (MD - 0.52% points, 95% CI - 0.68 to - 0.37), but its 24-week reduction was not statistically significant. Fasting insulin decreased at 12 weeks (SMD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.39 to - 0.11), and HOMA-IR decreased at 12 and 24 weeks. Triglyceride levels decreased and HDL-C increased at both time points; total and LDL cholesterol increased at 12 weeks. At 12 weeks, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) decreased (MD - 4.44 U/L, 95% CI - 6.09 to - 2.79; and - 1.23 U/L, 95% CI - 2.28 to - 0.19, respectively). AST decreased at 24 weeks (MD - 3.03 U/L, 95% CI - 5.85 to - 0.21), whereas ALT did not significantly decrease (MD - 4.52 U/L, 95% CI - 9.34 to 0.30). No significant differences in overall or serious adverse events were detected; edema was increased (RR 8.77, 95% CI 1.60-47.97).

CONCLUSION: Chiglitazar may improve short-term glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, selected lipid measures, and aminotransferase levels in adults with metabolic disorders. Increased edema risk, heterogeneity, and limited follow-up warrant cautious interpretation; long-term clinical benefits remain unproven.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02119-8.

articles.title: Trends, patterns, and determinants of dietary supplement use in patients with Type 2 Diabetes Melitus.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study examined 16-year trends in dietary supplement use and its associated sociodemographic and clinical characteristics among adults with type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

METHODS: This study included adults with T2DM participating in the third (2006-2008, n = 1077), fourth (2009-2011, n = 1376), fifth (2012-2014, n = 1520), sixth (2015-2017, n = 1592), and seventh (2018-2022, n = 1554) examinations of the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS). Trends in supplement use and participant characteristics were described across phases, and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of any supplement use in the 2018-2022 examination.

RESULTS: Over 16 years, mean age increased from 57.3 to 62.0 years. Abdominal obesity (38.1% to 47.0%), hypertension (41.9% to 56.5%), and chronic kidney disease (23.1% to 38.2%) remained highly prevalent. Supplement use increased significantly from 8.9% in 2006-2008 to 23.9% in 2018-2022, driving by increases in thiamin (2.0% to 16.0%), folic acid (2.5% to 10.6%), cobalamin (1.6% to 8.5%), vitamin C (1.4% to 8.2%), vitamin E (1.9% to 8.7%), and zinc (0.3% to 3.8%), while calcium supplement use declined from 5.8% to 1.0%. Supplement use was more likely among women (OR = 1.63, 95% CI = 1.28-2.08) and individuals with good glycemic control (OR = 1.28, 95% CI = 1.01-1.62), while late middle-aged (OR = 0.41, 95% CI = 0.18-0.95), elderly adults (OR = 0.43, 95% CI = 0.18-0.97) and housewives (OR = 0.41, 95% CI = 0.23-0.72) had significantly lower odds.

CONCLUSION: These findings indicate a significant increase in dietary supplement use alongside persistent cardiometabolic comorbidities in adults with T2DM, with patterns varying by type of supplement, demographics, and clinical determinants.

articles.title: Association of conventional and non-conventional lipid profile with cognitive impairment among type 2 diabetic patients.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore the connection between atherogenic index of plasma, non-HDL-C, as well as conventional lipid profiles in relation to cognition dysfunction among the diabetic participants aged over 60 years.

METHODS: The data of this cross-sectional research study came from the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program (Phase II) carried on the participants aged 60 and above. The functional status of the participants was assessed using the Functional Assessment Staging tool (FAST) and Category Fluency Test (CFT). After the measurement of lipid parameters, we used multiple logistic regression to analyze their relationship with cognitive impairment (CI) among the participants.

RESULTS: There were 836 participants in this cross-sectional study. Of them, 339 had cognitive decline. The average age of the subjects was 68.6 ± 5.7 years. There was no relationship between lipid parameters and cognition dysfunction with the exception of HDL-C. A higher amount of HDL-C had a protective role. While older age (OR = 1.05, 95% CI = 1.01-1.08, P = 0.002) and higher education (OR = 1.08, 95% CI = 1.04-1.12, P < 0.001) were positively related to cognitive impairment, male gender (OR = 0.41, 95% CI = 0.27-0.62, P < 0.001) was associated with 59% reduced odds of cognition impairment.

CONCLUSION: Among conventional lipid profiles, only the HDL-C levels were related to cognitive dysfunction and no relationship was observed between cognitive impairment and non-conventional lipids.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of Lianhua Qingwen versus oseltamivir in children with influenza: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, positive parallel-controlled study.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: High-quality evidence on Lianhua Qingwen (LHQW) for treating influenza in children remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of LHQW in children aged 3-14 years with influenza, compared with oseltamivir.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, positive parallel-controlled trial, participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either LHQW + oseltamivir placebo or oseltamivir + LHQW placebo. The primary outcome was clinical recovery time. Secondary outcomes included time to defervescence, symptom scores on the Canadian Acute Respiratory Illness and Flu Scale, the incidence of complications and severe/critical influenza, and the improvement rates for individual influenza symptoms. Safety outcomes were assessed based on adverse events.

RESULTS: A total of 520 participants were randomized (260 per group). Baseline characteristics were comparable. Median clinical recovery time was 5 days in both groups, with similar clinical recovery rates (71.5% vs. 71.2%; HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.84-1.29; one-sided p < 0.025). Median time to defervescence was shorter with LHQW (24 h vs. 30 h, p < 0.05). LHQW showed higher improvement rates for cough (56.9% vs. 45.5%) and sore throat (90.9% vs. 74.2%) (both p < 0.05). No severe or critical influenza occurred in the LHQW group. Adverse events incidence was similar between groups (p > 0.05).

DISCUSSION: LHQW may offer a safe and effective alternative to oseltamivir for pediatric influenza, with particular benefits for defervescence, cough, and sore throat.

CONCLUSIONS: LHQW was non-inferior to oseltamivir in clinical recovery time and resulted in faster defervescence and greater improvement in cough and sore throat, with comparable safety.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR1900028390 (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, Dec. 20, 2019).

articles.title: The impact of rising global temperatures on neurological diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change, driven predominantly by anthropogenic actions, represents a defining challenge of the 21st century. While its general health implications are well documented, the specific impact of global warming on neurological diseases has remained underemphasized for decades.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between rising global temperatures and the exacerbation or incidence of various neurological conditions through a systematic review.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE and SciELO databases for studies published between 2011 and 2026. Following strict eligibility criteria, 13 peer-reviewed articles were selected for qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: The evidence reveals that rising temperatures are increasingly linked to the worsening of conditions such as epilepsy, stroke, multiple sclerosis (MS), and neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Specifically, heat exposure is associated with higher hospitalization rates and acute symptom exacerbation, such as Uhthoff's phenomenon in MS and autonomic thermoregulatory failure in Parkinson's. Although some geographic and methodological discrepancies exist, particularly regarding stroke and seizure frequency, the overall trend indicates increased neurological vulnerability to thermal stress.

CONCLUSION: While research is expanding, neurological diseases remain an understudied frontier of the climate crisis. Targeted scientific investigation and robust public health strategies are imperative to mitigate the emerging neurological risks of a warming planet.

articles.title: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of enhanced cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) screening in UK, France, Germany and Australia: a microsimulation-based enhanced CVRM screening analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) conditions, including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, dyslipidemia, obesity, and heart failure, are major drivers of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and Australia. This study evaluated the 20-year clinical, economic, societal, and environmental impact of implementing a comprehensive CVRM screening strategy versus current standard of care (SoC) in these four countries.

METHODS: A discrete-time patient-level microsimulation model projected 20-year health trajectories calibrated to country-specific demographic and epidemiologic profiles. The enhanced screening strategy included broader eligibility, more frequent screening, and assessment of key CVRM indicators relative to SoC. Disease progression across six CVRM conditions was modeled using validated country-specific risk equations capturing multimorbidity and dynamic risk interactions. Analyses were conducted from payer, societal, and environmental perspectives using country-specific costs, wages, and CO2-equivalent emissions factors. Deterministic sensitivity analyses varied key parameters by ±20%.

RESULTS: Enhanced CVRM screening produced consistent benefits across all countries that increased over time. Over 20 years, in populations aged ≥35 years, mortality reductions ranged from 109,863 in Australia to 467,297 in Germany, and corresponding life-years gained ranged from 640,870 to 2,803,783. Most survival gains accrued after the first decade. Under the modeled assumptions, the strategy was projected to be cost saving in all countries, with total savings ranging from $368.9 million in Australia to $46.5 billion in Germany, and dominant across payer and societal perspectives. Additional benefits included fewer hospital bed-days, lower productivity losses, and reduced CO2 emissions.

LIMITATIONS: Results depended on structural and epidemiologic assumptions, including screening uptake, disease progression, and risk equation recalibration. Uncertainty was assessed using deterministic rather than probabilistic sensitivity analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive CVRM screening, when embedded in preventive care pathways and linked to appropriate follow-up, may improve population health while generating substantial economic, societal, and environmental benefits.

articles.title: Bioengineering strategies for next-generation female reproductive organoids: A roadmap to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: The human female reproductive system is characterized by highly dynamic tissue remodeling, cyclical endocrinology, and the precise orchestration of maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Historically, deciphering reproductive pathologies ranging from infertility to obstetric complications and malignancies has been hampered by the fundamental physiological and interspecies disparities inherent in 2D cultures and animal models. While three-dimensional (3D) organoid technology has initiated a paradigm shift, conventional static cultures relying on poorly defined, xenogeneic matrices (e.g., Matrigel) introduce profound immunogenic confounding factors and severe bioengineering bottlenecks. To bridge this gap, this review comprehensively delineates the advanced bioengineering strategies driving the next-generation of female reproductive models. We first outline foundational engineering pillars, highlighting the transition toward intelligent biomaterials, deterministic 3D bioprinting, and microfluidic microenvironments. Subsequently, we critically evaluate state-of-the-art organoid models across the ovary, fallopian tube, the maternal-fetal interface containing endometrium and placenta, cervix, and vagina. We emphasize how multi-lineage "assembloids" and multiorgan microphysiological systems successfully recapitulate transient implantation events and bidirectional endocrine crosstalk. Finally, we propose a strategic roadmap for the field, demonstrating how the integration of materials science, genetics, multi-omics, and engineering methods will overcome current limitations, ultimately accelerating the transition from benchtop in vitro models to standardized clinical diagnostics and reproductive regenerative therapeutics.

articles.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and female sexual function: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to systematically map the available evidence on the association between Mediterranean diet adherence and female sexual health and to explore potential biological and psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship.

METHODS: The review was conducted according to the methodological frameworks of Arksey and O'Malley, Levac et al., and the Joanna Briggs Institute. MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, PsycINFO, and CINAHL were systematically searched, supplemented by manual reference screening. Reporting followed the PRISMA-ScR guideline, and methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT).

RESULTS: Seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall, higher Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with more favorable female sexual health outcomes. Greater adherence was linked to lower rates of female sexual dysfunction and higher Female Sexual Function Index scores among women with type 2 diabetes; reduced deterioration in sexual function in randomized evidence; and improved lubrication, orgasm, and sexual satisfaction among women with severe obesity undergoing bariatric surgery. Favorable associations were also reported in women with inflammatory bowel disease and endometriosis, whereas in chronic liver disease, the initially observed associations were no longer statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. Proposed mechanisms included improved vascular and metabolic health, reduced inflammation and oxidative stress, and enhanced psychological well-being.

CONCLUSION: Higher Mediterranean diet adherence was generally associated with more favorable female sexual function and well-being; however, the predominantly observational and cross-sectional nature of the evidence precludes causal inference. The limited evidence base highlights the need for high-quality longitudinal and interventional studies.

articles.title: Cord blood lipid mediator profiles associated with maternal passive smoking during pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal passive smoking (PS) during pregnancy remains a common environmental exposure associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. However, its effects on fetal lipid mediator profiles have not been fully characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether maternal PS during pregnancy is associated with alterations in umbilical cord blood lipid mediator profiles in term neonates.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed umbilical cord blood samples from 56 term neonates, comprising 17 born to mothers with documented PS exposure and 39 born to mothers without PS exposure. Targeted lipid mediator profiling was performed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis, univariate analyses with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and exploratory multivariable linear regression were performed.

RESULTS: Four lipid mediators showed nominal differences between the groups, with higher levels of 14,15-LTE₄, platelet-activating factor, and 13-HpODE and lower levels of oleoylethanolamide (OEA) in the PS-exposed group. However, none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. OEA was subsequently evaluated in post-hoc exploratory multivariable analysis and remained associated with maternal PS exposure after adjustment for maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and diabetes mellitus.

CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory study identified several candidate cord blood lipid mediator signals related to maternal PS exposure, although none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings are hypothesis-generating but suggest that lipid mediator pathways involved in inflammatory and metabolic signaling may warrant further investigation in relation to prenatal tobacco smoke exposure.

articles.title: Olipudase alfa for acid sphingomyelinase deficiency: Evidence of efficacy from a compassionate use program.
authors: SIMMESN Italian Enzyme Replacement Therapy Study Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the SMPD1 gene, leading to systemic accumulation of sphingomyelin, primarily affecting the liver, spleen, lungs, and central nervous system (CNS). Olipudase alfa represents the first approved enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) targeting the non-neurological manifestations of ASMD. This study evaluates real-world safety and efficacy data of olipudase alfa in a cohort of Italian patients.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical, radiological, and laboratory data from 8 Italian patients (5 pediatric, 3 adult) with chronic visceral or chronic neurovisceral ASMD. All patients received olipudase alfa through a compassionate use program between December 2021 and November 2023. Data was collected at baseline, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 months of treatment.

RESULTS: At baseline, the cohort exhibited hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial lung disease, dyslipidemia, cytopenias, and hypertransaminasemia. Treatment led to significant improvements in hematological parameters, lipid profiles, and liver enzymes. A marked reduction in lyso-sphingomyelin levels was observed, alongside a decrease in spleen and liver volumes. Pulmonary function either improved or remained stable in most patients. While seven patients showed a robust response, one individual exhibited a suboptimal clinical and biochemical clinical outcome. Overall, the therapy was well-tolerated, with a favorable safety profile and few adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, olipudase alfa was safe and effective in improving clinical and biochemical markers of ASMD, consistent with results from pivotal clinical trials. However, the observed variability in individual responses emphasizes the importance of personalized monitoring and tailored management strategies.

articles.title: Exertional heat stroke induces liver injury through the activation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exertional heat stroke (EHS) disrupts the intestinal barrier and facilitates lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocation, thereby activating hepatic inflammatory signaling pathways and contributing to liver injury. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) pathway in EHS-induced liver injury.

METHODS: An EHS Sprague-Dawley rat model was developed through treadmill running, with EHS defined as achieving a core temperature of 42.9°C ± 0.1°C. The model rats were pretreated with either TAK-242 (10.0 mg/kg), a TLR4 inhibitor or saline prior to running. Real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunohistochemistry, and Western blot (WB) analyses were performed to investigate the expression of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway in the liver and the tight junction proteins in the intestine. HepG2 cells under heat stress and LPS exposure were utilized to examine TLR4/NF-κB activation at transcriptional and protein levels.

RESULTS: EHS rats exhibited significantly increased liver inflammation and elevated levels of ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase), AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase), TNF-α (Tumor Necrosis Factor-α), IL-1β (Interleukin-1β), and IL-6 (Interleukin-6) compared to the normal control group (all P < 0.05). There was a reduction in intestinal occludin, Zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), E-cadherin and an increase in serum LPS levels, and upregulation of hepatic TLR4/NF-κB signaling (all P < 0.05). Pretreatment with TAK-242 reduced hepatic TLR4/NF-κB signaling and inflammation both in vivo and in vitro. However, it did not significantly restore occludin, ZO-1, and E-cadherin expression levels in EHS rats.

CONCLUSIONS: EHS leads to liver injury through the activation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway. TAK-242 pretreatment attenuates liver inflammation by downregulating the TLR4/NF-κB signaling, supporting a mechanistic role for this pathway in EHS-induced liver injury.

articles.title: Deletion of a rheumatoid arthritis risk enhancer in mouse disrupts Bim expression and immune homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterise the in vivo function of a murine regulatory region syntenic to the human rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-associated enhancer at the ACOXL locus and its role in immunity.

METHODS: Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated the Bim-eΔ mouse model by excising a 15 kb genomic region syntenic to the human RA-associated locus tagged by rs13401811 from C57BL/6J zygotes. Bim expression was assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Thymocytes and splenocytes were profiled by flow cytometry, and whole-spleen RNA-seq was used to define transcriptional changes. Immune responses were tested using a Trichuris muris infection model and an antigen-induced arthritis (AIA) protocol.

RESULTS: Bim-eΔ mice show reduced Bim expression vs wild-type counterparts. This indicates that Bim is a transcriptional target of this region. Enhancer loss was correlated with differences in T cell proportions across age- and sex-stratified cohorts consistent with altered thymic selection. Splenic T and B cells were altered, and the transcriptome skewed toward inflammation. Bim-eΔ and wild-type mice mounted comparable responses to T. muris, whereas Bim-eΔ mice developed a severe adverse response during the sensitisation phase of the AIA protocol.

CONCLUSIONS: A murine noncoding regulatory region modulates Bim expression and immunity in vivo. Enhancer deletion altered the splenic transcriptional profile and lymphocyte composition while revealing a context-dependent phenotype upon inflammatory in vivo challenge. These findings support a role for RA-associated regulatory architecture in shaping immunity and point to BIM regulation as a potential therapeutic lever for restoring immune balance.

articles.title: CDKN1B undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation and attenuates lipid accumulation and inflammatory response by promoting mitophagy in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The role of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1B (CDKN1B) in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and its underlying mechanism remain unclear. In the present study, NAFLD models were constructed in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice and free fatty acid (FFA)-treated HepG2 cells. The expression of CDKN1B, markers of liver injury, inflammation, and mitophagy (PINK1, Parkin, Beclin1, and the LC3II/I ratio) were assessed. CDKN1B overexpression and knockdown were performed in HepG2 cells to investigate the functional roles of CDKN1B. The phase separation potential of CDKN1B was predicted bioinformatically and validated via in vitro droplet assays, immunofluorescence, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP). To determine whether the protective effects of CDKN1B depend on its phase separation property, the phase separation inhibitor 1,6-hexanediol (1,6-HD) was applied at graded concentrations. The results indicated that CDKN1B was downregulated in both in vivo and in vitro NAFLD models, accompanied by lipid accumulation, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired mitophagy. CDKN1B overexpression effectively reversed these pathologies, whereas CDKN1B knockdown exacerbated them. Moreover, CDKN1B contains an intrinsically disordered region and undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) both in vitro and in HepG2 cells. Critically, 1,6-HD abolished the protective effects of CDKN1B overexpression on mitophagy, mitochondrial integrity, lipid metabolism, and inflammation in a concentration-dependent manner. Collectively, CDKN1B alleviates NAFLD by promoting mitophagy, and this protective function is dependent on its ability to undergo LLPS. This study unveils a novel phase-separation-dependent mechanism of CDKN1B in regulating mitochondrial function and mitophagy, presenting CDKN1B condensates as a potential new target for NAFLD therapy.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01100-w.

articles.title: Effectiveness of theory-based educational interventions on fertility and childbearing intentions: a systematic review and meta-analysis among Iranian populations.
articles.abstract: Declining fertility highlights the need for theory-based educational interventions that shape couples' childbearing intentions. We examined their effectiveness on fertility and childbearing intentions through a systematic review and meta-analysis. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, SID, Magiran and Google Scholar were searched up to 18 August 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, and two reviewers extracted data. Pooled standardised mean differences (SMD) were estimated with random-effects models in Stata; heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran's Q. Twelve studies (1118 participants) were included. Interventions significantly increased fertility and childbearing intentions (SMD 0.79; 95% CI 0.48 to 1.09; I2 = 88.5%). Effects were significant at short-term (SMD 0.52; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.90) and long-term (SMD 0.96; 95% CI 0.53 to 1.39) follow-up. The Theory of Planned Behaviour showed the largest effect (SMD 1.01; 95% CI 0.55 to 1.48), whereas multimedia education without a theoretical foundation showed no significant effect (SMD 0.05). Interventions of three, five, and eight sessions showed significant effects, whereas two and four sessions did not. Theory-based interventions, especially those grounded in the TPB, were associated with higher fertility intentions among Iranian couples. Culturally adapted programmes may inform policy, although most studies were small, quasi-experimental and relied on self-reported intention.

articles.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
articles.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

articles.title: Estimates that cannot fail visibly: a current debate on measuring child mortality as household surveys contract.
articles.abstract: Global health has an argument on its hands that it has not yet had openly. For most of the countries that carry the burden of child deaths, the published under-five mortality rate is not a measurement. It is a model output built largely from birth histories collected in household surveys, because only about a tenth of deaths are registered in the World Health Organization African region. That input stream contracted sharply in 2025, when United States funding ended for the survey programme that had supplied about half of the child mortality data points for sub-Saharan Africa; interim funding now sustains only selected services. Three positions can be discerned in response, two of them largely implicit: that the estimation model will absorb the loss, that the contraction is a reason to accelerate civil registration, and that the survey stream must be restored. I argue that none can be settled on present information, because the evidence behind each estimate is published apart from the estimate and from the products that use it, so the figures look the same whether or not new evidence has arrived. I propose three steps in order of priority: print the age, number and type of the data sources beside every country estimate; direct scarce survey funding first to countries whose evidence is oldest and whose burden is largest; and make sample-based mortality registration a nationally owned and financed function of the state, as the bridge to complete civil registration.

articles.title: Investigation of the relationship between exposure to secondhand smoke and quality of life and life satisfaction among new students at Tehran University of Medical Sciences.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure is associated with numerous adverse health outcomes, posing a substantial public health burden. Despite well-documented physical and psychological harms of SHS, based on our search, no previous research has examined its association with Quality of Life (QoL) and Life Satisfaction (LS) in university students; therefore, this study aimed to investigate these relationships in this vulnerable population.

METHOD: This study utilized baseline data from a prospective cohort of newly enrolled students at Tehran University of Medical Sciences. SHS exposure, QoL, LS, and demographic characteristics were assessed using standardized and validated questionnaires. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to compare groups. Linear regression models were used as the primary analyses to examine associations between SHS exposure and continuous QoL and LS scores, while logistic regression models were conducted as secondary analyses for categorized outcomes: poor/moderate versus good QoL and low versus high LS.

RESULTS: Among the 372 participants included in the analysis, SHS exposure at home or outside was significantly associated with a 1.37-point lower QoL score (95% CI: -2.32, - 0.42; p = 0.005), while exposure in both settings was associated with a 1.80-point lower QoL score (95% CI: -3.08, - 0.52; p = 0.006). For life satisfaction, only exposure in both settings remained significantly associated with lower scores in the adjusted model (adjusted β = -2.12; 95% CI: -3.92, - 0.32; p = 0.021), while exposure at home or outside was not significantly associated with the continuouse LS score (p = 0.305). In adjusted logistic regression models, exposure at home or outside significantly increased the odds of poor/moderate QoL (AOR = 1.87; 95% CI: 1.16 to 3.01; p = 0.010), as did exposure in both settings (AOR = 1.97; 95% CI: 1.18, 3.30; p = 0.009). However, no significant associations were observed between any SHS exposure level and low life satisfaction in the adjusted logistic models.

CONCLUSION: The findings indicated that SHS exposure was associated with lower QoL scores and higher odds of poor/moderate QoL among university students. Exposure in both settings was also associated with lower continuous LS scores; however, no statistically significant association was observed between SHS exposure and low LS in the adjusted logistic regression models.

articles.title: Insights into morbidity and mortality in Gaucher disease: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gaucher disease (GD) is a rare lysosomal disorder classified, on the basis of neurological involvement, into type 1 (GD1, non-neuronopathic) and types 2 (GD2) and 3 (GD3) (neuronopathic). Data on morbidity and mortality in Latin American cohorts remain scarce.

AIMS: To characterise morbidity and mortality patterns in a Brazilian GD cohort.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study at a single GD referral centre in Porto Alegre, Brazil (2003-2023; n = 53; GD1 = 45, GD2 = 4, GD3 = 4). Diagnosis was molecularly confirmed by Sanger and massive parallel sequencing of GBA1. Comorbidities and causes of death were retrieved by chart review; survival was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results: Median follow-up was 15 years. In GD1, comorbidities were predominantly psychiatric (71%), metabolic/endocrinological (69%) and cardiovascular (60%). Nine patients (17%) died: four GD1 patients (median age 65 years; three from malignancy, one from sepsis), all four GD2 patients (median age 5 months; respiratory or hepatic failure, sepsis) and one GD3 patient (Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy at 27 years).

CONCLUSIONS: The phenotype-specific mortality pattern - malignancy as the leading cause of death in GD1, uniform early death in GD2 reflecting the disease's neurological trajectory rather than a failure of enzyme replacement therapy, and neurological death in GD3 - underscores the substantial burden of oncological, cardiovascular, metabolic and neurological comorbidities in this population and supports systematic multidisciplinary surveillance as a routine component of GD care in Brazil, even in resource-limited settings.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Adult patients with Gaucher disease type 1 require close clinical monitoring for oncological, cardiovascular, metabolic and psychiatric comorbidities. Gaucher disease type 2 remains a devastating disease with a poor prognosis under current therapies.

articles.title: Intravenous leiomyomatosis with marked edematous degeneration mimicking IVC thrombus: A case report.
articles.abstract: Intravenous leiomyomatosis (IVL) is a rare variant of leiomyoma characterized by proliferation of smooth muscle cells within uterine veins, with potential extension into the inferior vena cava (IVC), right atrium, or even pulmonary arteries. In advanced stages, IVL can lead to life-threatening complications, underscoring the need for accurate diagnosis and timely intervention. We report the case of a 40-year-old woman in whom an isoechoic structure within the IVC was incidentally detected on transabdominal ultrasonography and initially suspected to represent an IVC thrombus. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated an enlarged posterior uterine wall with heterogeneous internal enhancement. A filling defect with subtle contrast enhancement within the dilated vessels extended continuously from the uterus through the pelvic venous plexus and right ovarian vein into the IVC. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed heterogeneous high-signal-intensity lesions in the uterine myometrium with extension into the pelvic venous plexuses, ovarian veins, and the IVC, findings suggestive of a neoplastic process rather than thrombosis. The patient underwent surgical excision of the intravenous mass in conjunction with hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Histopathological examination confirmed IVL with prominent edematous and degenerative changes. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty of IVL with marked degeneration, which can closely mimic venous thrombosis, and emphasizes that a continuous pelvic-to-IVC extension, an associated uterine mass, and subtle contrast enhancement should strongly prompt the inclusion of IVL in the differential diagnosis.

articles.title: Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess mimicking hepatic malignancy in a non-diabetic patient: A case report from Kazakhstan.
articles.abstract: Pyogenic liver abscess is an infectious condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality, with Klebsiella pneumoniae emerging as a major pathogen. We report a case of Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess in a 76-year-old woman from Kazakhstan, representing one of the first indexed reports from Central Asia. The patient presented with prolonged fever, jaundice, and constitutional symptoms without diabetes mellitus. Initial ultrasound revealed a large heterogeneous hepatic mass with a solid, tumor-like appearance, raising concern for malignancy in the setting of chronic hepatitis B infection. MRI and contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated diffusion restriction, multiloculated architecture, and mild peripheral and septal enhancement without arterial hyperenhancement or venous washout, favoring hepatic abscess over hepatocellular carcinoma. The solid, tumor-like ultrasound appearance, atypical for a pyogenic abscess in its resemblance to hepatic malignancy, posed the primary diagnostic challenge, underscoring the value of multimodal imaging in characterizing hepatic lesions. Additionally, KPLA should be considered in the differential diagnosis even in the absence of classical metabolic risk factors and in regions with limited epidemiological data.

articles.title: Challenges in implementing the 2020 EULAR Points to Consider on nonadherence in RMDs.
authors: EULAR Study Group on Adherence to Therapy in RMDs
articles.abstract: Low or nonadherence to treatment is a widespread challenge in the management of rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs), significantly affecting disease outcomes, quality of life, and healthcare costs. The 2020 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Points to Consider provide a comprehensive framework for the prevention, screening, assessment, and management of nonadherence in RMDs. However, real-world implementation of these recommendations remains limited. The challenge is no longer the lack of recommendations, but their integration into routine rheumatology care. This viewpoint discusses the rationale and evidence supporting implementation of the 2020 EULAR Points to Consider in clinical practice and highlights key priorities for the operationalisation of the recommendations into feasible and sustainable care strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on routine adherence assessment, patient-centred communication, multidisciplinary collaboration, and healthcare professional training as essential components of adherence support in RMD care.

articles.title: Pre-stroke frailty in patients with first-ever acute stroke: Its associations with stroke subtype and impact on activities of daily living.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Few studies have examined frailty in patients with first-ever stroke who were independent in activities of daily living (ADLs) prior to onset. This study aimed to investigate the characteristics of pre-stroke frailty and its impact on ADLs at discharge.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 152 patients aged ≥65 years with first-ever stroke admitted to the stroke unit of a university hospital were enrolled. Pre-frailty/frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Associations between frailty status and clinical characteristics were evaluated. Multivariate regression analysis identified independent predictors of the Barthel Index (BI) at discharge.

RESULTS: Pre-frailty/frailty was present in 35.5% of patients, and was associated with higher rates of atrial fibrillation (p = 0.043) and cardioembolic stroke (p = 0.001). Compared with the robust group, the pre-frailty/frailty group had significantly lower BI scores at both admission and discharge, as well as more extended hospital stays. Both groups, however, demonstrated significant improvement in BI at discharge (p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis revealed that NIH Stroke Scale score (p < 0.001), stroke type (p = 0.010), and CFS score (p = 0.044) independently predicted BI at discharge.

CONCLUSION: Pre-stroke frailty is associated with a higher risk of cardioembolic stroke and poorer functional status during hospitalization. Nevertheless, patients with frailty still achieved significant ADL improvement with rehabilitation, underscoring the importance of active rehabilitation strategies in this population.

articles.title: 'Let's work alongside it': healthcare professionals' perspectives of generative AI in supporting care at home in paediatric rheumatology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly explored in healthcare, yet its potential to support care at home remains largely unexamined. In paediatric rheumatology, where families frequently undertake complex tasks to manage treatment plans between appointments, safe and effective guidance is essential. The aim of the current study was to understand healthcare professionals' (HCPs') views on adopting GenAI tools to help families manage their child's care.

METHODS: Utilising a vignette-based methodology, paediatric rheumatology HCPs were invited to focus groups and presented with 3 hypothetical scenarios: (1) injection administration, (2) flare assessment, and (3) physiotherapy exercises. Following the principles outlined by Braun and Clarke, data were analysed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 37 HCPs from the wider multidisciplinary team from 14 different hospitals participated in this study. Six main themes were identified: (1) opportunities of GenAI to benefit patient care; (2) disadvantages and challenges; (3) risks, safety netting, and evaluation; (4) different approaches of utilising GenAI; (5) role of HCPs in the world of GenAI; and (6) ensuring inclusivity and accessibility.

CONCLUSIONS: HCPs recognised opportunities for how GenAI could support caregivers in managing their child's healthcare or young people's self-management, particularly through guidance support rather than clinical interpretation. However, concerns were raised regarding the accuracy, reliability, privacy, and data governance of currently existing GenAI tools. The perspectives of HCPs are critical to ensuring that the application of GenAI in healthcare aligns with clinical expectations, ethical standards, regulatory processes, and the needs of patients and families.

articles.title: Income-related differences in survival across disease categories in Sweden: a retrospective population-based register study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower income is consistently associated with poorer survival after disease diagnosis, even in countries with universal healthcare such as Sweden. While income-related survival differences have been documented for specific conditions, comparative evidence across a range of disease categories with long-term follow-up is lacking. We quantify income-related differences in survival across 100 disease categories focussing on leading non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

METHODS: All individuals aged 16-95 years registered in Sweden between 2001 and 2023 were followed from first diagnosis until death or the end of 2023. By disease category cohort, individuals were matched to five general population controls (no prior diagnosis of that category) on birth year, sex, and income quartile. Flexible parametric models were used to estimate standardised survival curves for diagnosed individuals and their matched controls.

FINDINGS: For all 100 disease categories, estimated 10-year survival was lower for the lowest income quartile (Q1) than higher quartiles. For 37 conditions, the Q1 vs Q4 10-year survival gap exceeded 10 percentage points; the largest gaps were for other pharynx cancer (10-year survival 34.2% [95% CI 32.5-35.7] in Q1 vs 58.2% [56.3-60.1] in Q4), larynx cancer, mouth cancer, COPD, and endocarditis. Income-related survival disparities accounted for 6.2 million (95% CI 5.9-6.6 million) person-years of survival loss within 10 years of diagnosis across all cohorts compared to a high-income survival counterfactual, with cardiovascular diseases accounting for the largest share for Q1 (1.3 million). Survival loss after diagnosis relative to undiagnosed controls was significantly greater for Q1 compared to Q4 for 73 of 100 conditions.

INTERPRETATION: Substantial income-related disparities in survival persist in Sweden across all the most prevalent NCDs. Policies addressing income inequality alongside targeted disease-specific interventions are likely required to reduce income disparities in survival.

FUNDING: Swedish Research Council for Health, Working Life and Welfare.

articles.title: Impact of direct transfer to critical care on mortality for patients who undergo emergency colorectal cancer resection: a national population-based cohort study in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is recommended that patients receiving emergency surgery and with 'high-risk' of morbidity and mortality should be transferred directly from theatre to critical care. Using a national, population-based cohort study, we estimated the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality after emergency colorectal cancer resection, and the variation amongst English NHS hospitals.

METHODS: Patients who underwent emergency colorectal cancer resection between December 2016 and November 2019 according to Hospital Episodes Statistics, National Bowel Cancer Audit or National Emergency Laparotomy Audit were included. Patients were identified as having a direct transfer to critical care through linkage with the Intensive Care National Audit and Research Centre Case Mix Programme. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score methods were used to measure the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: In total, 10,441 patients underwent an emergency colorectal cancer resection. Unadjusted 90-day mortality was higher in the direct transfer to critical care cohort (10.9%) than in patients without direct transfer to critical care (3.7%) (odds ratio [OR]: 3.16, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.65-3.77). There was no evidence of an association after risk adjustment (adjusted OR: 1.16, 95% CI: 0.94-1.43) or after propensity score analysis (weighted OR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.69-1.27). For patients at high risk with a predicted mortality ≥5%, the proportion of patients with a direct transfer to critical care varied widely amongst hospitals (interquartile range 68%-92%; median 83%).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that apparent higher postoperative mortality in patients having direct transfer to critical care can be mostly explained by characteristics of patients, tumours, physiology and surgery. However, the extent to which direct transfer to critical care is used varies widely amongst hospitals. Further work to understand this variation has the potential to improve patient outcomes after emergency colorectal cancer resection.

articles.title: Balancing safety and efficacy in photodynamic therapy for facial port-wine stains in children aged 2-7 years: a prospective controlled study of light-intensity optimization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoporfin-mediated photodynamic therapy is increasingly used to treat port-wine stains (PWS), but evidence regarding appropriate light intensity for young children remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare safety and efficacy of two light-intensity regimens for hemoporfin-mediated photodynamic therapy in 2- to 7-year-old children with facial PWS.

METHODS: In this open-label prospective controlled study, 40 children were enrolled sequentially to receive photodynamic therapy using light intensities of 60 or 75 mW/cm2 with a hemoporfin dose of 5 mg/kg. The primary outcome was the overall effective rate at 8 weeks after treatment. Clinical outcomes were evaluated at 8 and 24 weeks. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04106258).

RESULTS: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated and achieved similar overall effective rates at 8 and 24 weeks. The higher light-intensity regimen was associated with a higher complete clearance rate at 24 weeks but also a significantly higher incidence of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. No serious adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: Both light-intensity regimens improved facial PWS in children aged 2-7 years. In this exploratory, non-randomized comparison, 75 mW/cm2 was associated with a higher observed complete-clearance rate, but an increased risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Lower light intensity may be considered when minimizing post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation is a clinical priority.

articles.title: HMGN5 promotes renal tubular inflammation and pyroptosis‑associated signaling in chronic kidney disease via the IFNAR2 axis.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a condition that is characterized by persistent tubular injury, inflammation and progressive fibrosis, ultimately leading to an irreversible loss of renal function. Pyroptosis, a notably pro‑inflammatory mode of programmed cell death, contributes to tubular epithelial injury and amplifies renal inflammwation. The present study investigated the role of high mobility group nucleosome‑binding protein 5 (HMGN5) in CKD and its regulatory relationship with interferon (IFN) receptor 2 (IFNAR2) signaling. The present study found that HMGN5 expression was significantly upregulated in renal tissues obtained from patients with CKD and CKD‑model mice; this upregulation was accompanied by enhanced renal injury, fibrosis and inflammatory cytokine production. In vitro, HMGN5 overexpression in HK‑2 cells: i) Promoted the expression of IFNAR2, phosphorylated‑interferon regulatory factor (IRF)3/IRF7 and absent in melanoma 2; ii) enhanced the cleavage of caspase‑1 and gasdermin D; iii) increased IL‑1β, IL‑8 and IFN‑β secretion; and iv) promoted lactate dehydrogenase release. These findings suggested the activation of pyroptosis‑associated cellular responses. Conversely, silencing HMGN5 or blocking IFNAR2 signaling markedly attenuated these effects. In vivo, pharmacological blockade of IFNAR2 ameliorated renal tissue damage, reduced fibrosis, restored renal function, decreased systemic cytokine levels and suppressed pyroptosis‑associated signaling in CKD‑model mice. Collectively, the findings of the present study identified HMGN5 as a novel regulator of IFNAR2‑related pyroptosis‑associated signaling in renal tubular epithelial cells and suggested that the HMGN5‑IFNAR2 axis represents a pathophysiological pathway of interest in CKD that warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Gut‑kidney axis in chronic kidney disease: Dysbiosis, uremic metabolites and therapeutic opportunities (Review).
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) poses a notable global health burden. Beyond traditional pathways, the gut‑kidney axis has emerged as a potential contributor to disease progression. In the present narrative review, current evidence on the role of intestinal dysbiosis, characterized by reduced microbial diversity, depletion of beneficial short‑chain fatty acid producers and expansion of uremic toxin‑generating bacteria, in the accumulation of nephrotoxic metabolites (such as indoxyl sulfate, p‑cresyl sulfate and trimethylamine N‑oxide) is summarized. These toxins promote oxidative stress, inflammation and fibrosis, accelerating renal decline. By contrast, microbially derived short‑chain fatty acids exert protective effects. Although therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiome (including probiotics, prebiotics and adsorbents) and fecal microbiota transplantation (targeting the gut microbiome) exhibit potential in modulating toxin levels, evidence for clinical endpoint benefit remains insufficient. In the present review, mechanistic insights were critically evaluated, clinical intervention studies are systematically summarized in tabulated form and a roadmap for personalized, microbiota‑informed therapeutic strategies is proposed.

articles.title: Research progress in neural regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapy of obesity (Review).
articles.abstract: Obesity is a multifactorial chronic metabolic disease driven by disrupted energy homeostasis and excessive adipose tissue (AT) deposition under genetic, environmental and central neural regulation. Sustained energy surplus triggers AT hypertrophy, endocrine dysfunction and low‑grade inflammation, elevating risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases and multiple cancers while impairing physical‑mental well‑being. Hypothalamic central neural circuits integrate peripheral metabolic signals to govern feeding and systemic energy balance and serve as core pathological drivers of obesity. Conventional interventions including bariatric surgery, calorie restriction and exercise yield only transient weight loss with poor long‑term outcomes, as they fail to reverse obesity‑related neural‑circuit dysfunction and thus produce high weight‑regain rates. Translational obstacles remain for neuromodulatory therapies, including poorly defined cell‑type‑specific neural control and limited blood‑brain barrier penetration of candidate agents. The present review systematically outlined obesity‑associated hierarchical neural networks centered on hypothalamic arcuate nucleus pro‑opiomelanocortin and agouti‑related peptide neurons and the leptin‑melanocortin axis. The present review summarized recent progress in hypothalamic neurons, key neuro‑transmitters and downstream cascades controlling energy metabolism; characterized gut‑microbiota‑vagus‑nerve gut‑brain signaling and dual appetite‑regulatory roles of short‑chain fatty acids; and delineated pathological links between gut dysbiosis and hypothalamic pro‑opiomelanocortin neuronal injury, distinguishing confirmed mechanisms from unvalidated hypotheses. Three neural‑targeted anti‑obesity modalities (GLP‑1R agonists, MC4R agonists and NMU‑R2 small‑molecule candidates) are comparatively assessed, covering preclinical evidence for NMU‑R2, adverse‑effect profiles, target populations and animal‑to‑human translational gaps. The present study further addresses multimodal combined interventions and balanced pros‑and‑cons of neuromodulation techniques. This multi‑system overview provided theoretical support for developing novel precision anti‑obesity strategies.

articles.title: Psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults: a systematic review of formats and delivery approaches.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a prevalent mental health condition that may develop following direct or indirect exposure to traumatic events. Psychoeducation offers a low-cost and accessible entry point to care. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of psychoeducation for PTSD and identify the conditions and delivery formats associated with greater effectiveness.Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating psychoeducational interventions for PTSD in adults. Searches were performed in PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, PTSDpubs, and Cochrane databases, covering 1 January 2000 to 30 April 2024 with an additional targeted search for PTSD Coach trials conducted in July and August 2026. Eligible studies included adult participants and assessed psychoeducation delivered as either a stand-alone or primary component. Findings were synthesized narratively.Results: Twenty-six RCTs with a total of 3,304 participants met the inclusion criteria. Psychoeducational interventions varied substantially in format, duration, and delivery.Discussion: Nine trials demonstrated significant reductions in PTSD symptoms attributable to psychoeducation (one preventive intervention and eight post-diagnosis). All trials showing significant between-group effects used digital delivery, and most included form of human guidance. However, overall treatment effects were inconsistent across studies, and the methodological quality of the evidence was limited, with several positive trials presenting some concerns or a high risk of bias. Several trials also reported improvements in outcomes such as perceived stress, anxiety, stigma, and help-seeking intentions.Conclusion: Psychoeducation alone is insufficient as a stand-alone treatment for PTSD but remains a valuable component of stepped-care approaches. Future research should systematically assess outcomes such as stigma reduction and help-seeking behaviours, which are critical for engagement in intensive therapies. Preventive interventions may also benefit from focusing on high-risk populations identified through established risk factors, thereby enhancing trial design and minimizing the inclusion of individuals likely to remit without intervention.Registration: This review was not prospectively registered.

articles.title: Radiographic union rate and predictors of nonunion after primary surgical implant generation network intramedullary nailing for open tibial shaft fractures at a major trauma center in Ethiopia.
articles.journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Open tibial shaft fractures are a major source of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries, yet outcome data after Surgical Implant Generation Network (SIGN) intramedullary nailing (IMN) remain few. The study aimed to determine the radiographic union rate and identify predictors of nonunion after primary SIGN IMN for Gustilo-Anderson (GA) grade I through IIIA open tibial shaft fractures at a large trauma center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at AaBET Hospital, reviewing records and radiographs of patients treated between July 2016 and July 2022. Radiographic union was assessed at minimum 1 year using the Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures (RUST). Associations between clinical variables and union were analyzed with Fisher exact test, Mann-Whitney U test, and binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 32.9 years; 86.2% male). Road traffic accidents accounted for 78.2% of injuries. The radiographic union rate was 89.7% (78 of 87). On multivariable analysis, GA grade IIIA (odds ratio [OR]: 36.2; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.21-90; P = 0.013), postoperative infection (OR: 20.2; 95% CI: 2.15-189; P = 0.023), and surgical delay beyond 48 hours (OR: 16.5; 95% CI: 1.88-144; P = 0.009) were independently associated with nonunion.

CONCLUSIONS: Primary SIGN IMN yielded a high union rate for GA I to IIIA open tibial shaft fractures in this low- and middle-income countries setting. GA grade, postoperative infection, and delay to surgery were the principal barriers to union. These findings support early surgical intervention and rigorous infection control in resource-limited settings.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level IV.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis in an adolescent with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Youth-onset type 2 diabetes (T2D) is increasing, prompting expanded use of pharmacotherapies previously approved only for adults. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, approved for pediatric use in 2023, improve glycemic control by promoting glucosuria, but they carry a known risk of euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in adults. We describe a unique pediatric case of SGLT2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic DKA in a 12-year-old female with T2D. The patient developed DKA with normal glucose shortly after initiating an SGLT2 inhibitor, leading to diagnostic uncertainty and recognition only after exclusion of more common etiologies. She was successfully treated with intravenous insulin and fluids with resolution of DKA and subsequently transitioned to subcutaneous insulin therapy. This case underscores that euglycemic DKA can occur in youth receiving SGLT2 inhibitors, particularly during puberty when physiologic insulin resistance may heighten risk, and that subtle presentations can complicate early recognition if clinicians rely on hyperglycemia alone. As SGLT2 inhibitors enter broader pediatric use, heightened diagnostic vigilance, guided assessment of ketones and acid-base status in symptomatic patients, and patient and family education are essential to ensure safe use in children and adolescents with T2D.

articles.title: Severe insulin-requiring diabetes in a noradrenergic giant pheochromocytoma: a secretory-metabolic phenotype paradox.
articles.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor associated with hypertension and dysglycemia in 20% to 40% of cases. Insulin-requiring diabetes has been reported in tumors with an adrenergic profile, owing to epinephrine-mediated inhibition of β-cell secretion. A 37-year-old man with a normal body mass index and an 18-year history of insulin-requiring diabetes and hypertension was found to have a right adrenal mass measuring 10.1 × 8.0 × 6.7 cm. Biochemical evaluation showed a noradrenergic profile, with urinary normetanephrine greater than 5000 μg/24 hours (SI: >26 400 nmol/day; reference range, 70-538 μg/24 hours [SI: 370-2841 nmol/day]) and normal urinary metanephrine. Right adrenalectomy and histopathology confirmed an intra-adrenal pheochromocytoma. After surgery, insulin was discontinued, and glycated hemoglobin remained below 6.1% (SI: 41-43 mmol/mol) without therapy. A preoperative insulin requirement of 0.83 units/kg/day, normal C-peptide, and negative glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies supported a mixed and reversible mechanism involving catecholamine-induced insulin resistance and β-cell suppression. Severe postoperative hypoglycemia was attributed to reversal of catecholamine excess. This case challenges the association of severe diabetes with adrenergic pheochromocytomas and suggests that catecholamine burden and exposure duration may be more important determinants of metabolic severity than secretory profile alone, after prolonged exposure to high catecholamine concentrations.

articles.title: Persistent atherogenic lipoprotein changes during lorlatinib therapy.
articles.abstract: Lorlatinib, a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, frequently induces hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia, but longitudinal qualitative lipoprotein changes remain incompletely characterized. We describe a 52-year-old woman with ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer who developed persistent dyslipidemia despite lipid-lowering therapy. Before lorlatinib, total cholesterol was 164 mg/dL (SI [International System of Units]: 4.24 mmol/L) (reference range, 148-248 mg/dL [SI: 3.83-6.41 mmol/L]), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol was 52 mg/dL (SI: 1.34 mmol/L) (reference range, 65-139 mg/dL [SI: 1.68-3.59 mmol/L]), and triglycerides were 54 mg/dL (SI: 0.61 mmol/L) (reference range, 30-117 mg/dL [SI: 0.34-1.32 mmol/L]). Within 3 weeks after lorlatinib initiation, these increased to 340, 245, and 166 mg/dL, respectively. Longitudinal profiling showed persistent apolipoprotein B (ApoB) elevation, increased oxidized LDL, and a prominent pre-β-lipoprotein fraction. Subclinical hypothyroidism was later detected, and pitavastatin was switched to rosuvastatin. This case highlights the potential value of ApoB and qualitative lipid assessment during prolonged lorlatinib therapy.

articles.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea after the Great East Japan Earthquake: A case report.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is frequently accompanied by sleep disturbance, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is an important potential comorbidity. Although PTSD-OSA coexistence has been reported mainly in military veterans, reports after natural disasters remain limited. We describe a patient who developed PTSD after the Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) and was subsequently diagnosed with severe OSA.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old man with hypertension and dyslipidemia, but no prior psychiatric illness, experienced temporary burial under rubble during the GEJE. He subsequently developed persistent trauma-related nightmares, depressed mood, and panic responses to disaster-related cues and was diagnosed with PTSD. Paroxetine and alprazolam improved mood and panic symptoms, whereas nightmares, excessive daytime sleepiness, and impaired concentration persisted. Polysomnography later demonstrated severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index, 41.6 events/h; rapid eye movement (REM) AHI, 47.6 events/h; minimum oxygen saturation, 79%). Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was initiated without changes to psychiatric treatment. Daytime sleepiness improved, and nightmare frequency decreased from almost daily to approximately weekly during the period of CPAP treatment, although adherence was low and symptoms later recurred after treatment interruption.

CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that persistent nightmares, sleepiness, and impaired daytime functioning in a patient with PTSD may coexist with clinically significant OSA. Because longitudinal standardized PTSD measures were unavailable and CPAP adherence was limited, the observed improvement cannot be attributed to CPAP alone. Systematic assessment for sleep disorders, including OSA, should be considered when sleep-related or daytime symptoms persist during psychiatric treatment.

articles.title: Continuous caloric restriction and diet replacement but not alternate-day fasting may enhance susceptibility to glucose intolerance, dyslipidemia and cell stress under renewed high-fat diet.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight regain affects most individuals attempting to treat obesity and its comorbidities, and it is associated with increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. Several strategies have been proposed to induce weight loss, including caloric restriction (CCR), diet replacement (DR) and alternate-day fasting (ADF).

AIM: To compare these approaches in terms of weight maintenance and metabolic, oxidative, and inflammatory outcomes.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats underwent a three-phase protocol. First, animals received a high-fat diet (HFD) for eight weeks to induce obesity. Second, they were divided into four groups: ad lib-HFD (continued HFD), R-HFD (30% reduction of HFD w/w), ADF-HFD (24 h fasting alternating with 24 h ad libitum HFD), and ad lib-LFD (DR via ad libitum access to low-fat chow) for six weeks. Finally, all groups returned to free access to HFD for four weeks.

RESULTS: All interventions delayed weight gain; however, discontinuation led to rapid weight regain. Under renewed HFD ad libitum exposure, CCR and DR induced higher susceptibility to dyslipidemia, as shown by the temporal analysis. These strategies also impaired hepatic and adipose antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses and heightened lymph node stress upon return to unlimited offer of obesogenic diet. In contrast, ADF appeared to confer partial protection against the metabolic complications of weight rebound.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite similar weight-loss efficacy, ADF may better preserve metabolic homeostasis during weight regain.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02112-1.

articles.title: Role of intestinal microbiota in pathogenesis and perspective therapeutics events for diabetes mellitus: A narrative review.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetes mellitus is a widespread metabolic condition characterized by persistent high blood sugar, contributing significantly to global disease burden. Recent studies have turned attention to the intestinal microbiome as a critical factor influencing metabolic health and glucose control. Disruptions in normal microbial ecosystem, referred to as dysbiosis, are now linked to the development and worsening of diabetes. Gut bacteria and their metabolic outputs affect host energy use, immune responses, inflammation, digestive efficiency, and even genetic activity.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using relevant keywords such as "gut microbiota," "dysbiosis," "short-chain fatty acids," "bile acids," "probiotics," and both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with diabetic complications.

RESULTS: Evidence indicates that an increased Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio is commonly observed in T1D patients, underscoring the significance of microbial imbalance. In T2D, positive associations have been reported with genera such as Blautia and Ruminococcus, while genera like Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium, and Roseburia show negative correlations. However, these findings are predominantly derived from cross-sectional studies, and definitive causal relationships remain to be established.

CONCLUSION: Elucidating the relationship between gut microbiota and diabetes not only clarifies the role of dysbiosis in metabolic disease and opens avenues for novel therapeutic strategies. Modulating the microbiome may improve insulin sensitivity and glycemic control. Future research could pave the way for innovative diagnostic tools, clinical assays, and treatment designed to alleviate diabetic symptoms. Nevertheless, translation of these findings into clinical practice requires further rigorous investigation.

articles.title: Effectiveness of outpatient financing reform from health savings accounts to pooling scheme in China: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Outpatient services are fundamental to safeguarding population health and promoting the efficient use of healthcare resources. However, China has long faced limited risk pooling and inadequate financial protection for outpatient services. In 2021, China launched a nationwide outpatient financing reform to address these limitations. This study examines the effectiveness of this reform, which shifted outpatient financing from individual health savings accounts (HSAs) to an outpatient pooling scheme. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) was conducted for studies published between 1998 and December 2025. A total of 21 studies were included in this review. Overall, the reform was generally associated with increased outpatient utilization. Several studies suggested substitution between outpatient and inpatient care, whereas others indicated complementary effects. Findings on medical expenditure and out-of-pocket spending were mixed, while limited evidence suggested increased primary healthcare utilization and improved health-related behaviors. Overall, the effects varied across outcomes and policy settings, highlighting the importance of policy design and local healthcare contexts.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization of a hemorrhagic renal mass in an octogenarian initially unfit for nephrectomy.
articles.abstract: Palliative transarterial embolization is an established option for symptomatic renal tumors in patients who are poor surgical candidates, but conventional particle or coil techniques sacrifice uninvolved parenchyma and permit reflux-related non-target embolization. We report an 89-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who presented with one month of gross hematuria, transfusion-requiring anemia, and acute kidney injury secondary to a 5.8 × 4.6 × 3.4 cm hypervascular right upper-pole renal mass extending into the collecting system. Deemed unfit for nephrectomy during the index admission, he underwent super-selective balloon-occluded embolization with ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer delivered through a balloon-occlusion microcatheter. Hematuria resolved, hemoglobin stabilized without further transfusion, and creatinine returned to near baseline by post-procedure day 2. He remained free of hematuria for approximately 12 weeks despite resumption of apixaban. Recurrent intermittent bleeding from a persistent enhancing collecting-system component prompted readmission; surveillance imaging demonstrated a devascularized cortical tumor bed with an approximately 69% reduction in tumor volume and preserved parenchymal enhancement of the treated kidney. After interval stabilization, he underwent elective robotic nephrectomy with minimal blood loss. Pathology demonstrated clear cell renal cell carcinoma (grade 3, stage pT3a) with 50% tumor necrosis and post-embolization changes; urothelial carcinoma was excluded. Balloon-occluded ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization may provide effective temporizing hemostasis and histologically confirmed tumor devascularization in nonsurgical patients, serving in this case as a bridge to elective nephrectomy.

articles.title: Urologically silent intravesical migration of a copper intrauterine device presenting as chronic pelvic pain: CT features and comparison with reported cases.
articles.abstract: Uterine perforation with migration of an intrauterine device (IUD) into the urinary bladder is a well-documented complication that usually presents with lower urinary tract symptoms, recurrent urinary tract infection, hematuria, or a secondary bladder calculus. We report a 35-year-old woman (G2P2) with a copper IUD inserted 5 years earlier who presented with progressive chronic pelvic pain and no urinary symptoms. Pelvic ultrasound showed an abnormally positioned device, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a T-shaped device of metallic density traversing the anterior uterine wall, with one arm protruding into the bladder dome and coated by a small encrustation. The fixed, non-dependent position of the linear metallic core, its continuity with the myometrium, and its T-shaped morphology distinguished the device from a primary bladder calculus. Cystoscopy confirmed partial intravesical protrusion of the encrusted arm, which was extracted intact with forceps without complication, and the patient was asymptomatic at follow-up. Compared with published intravesical cases, in which urinary complaints or a bladder stone usually prompt investigation, this case shows that bladder involvement may remain silent from a urinary perspective. In IUD users with unexplained pelvic pain, imaging should specifically assess the bladder, and a delayed excretory CT phase is advisable to evaluate bladder-wall integrity before removal.

articles.title: Impact of wildfire smoke waves on the association between long-term exposure to fine particulate matter and cardiovascular hospitalizations among older adults in the United States.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD), even at concentrations below U.S. air quality standards. The frequency and severity of wildfires are increasing, causing episodic PM2.5 spikes. Our study examined whether associations between long-term exposure to PM2.5 and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed in the presence and absence of wildfire smoke waves.

METHODS: We conducted a cohort study of 65.2 million U.S. Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥ 65 years across the contiguous U.S. during 2017-2022. Daily total and wildfire smoke PM2.5 concentrations were estimated at 1 km and 10 km spatial resolutions, respectively, using validated machine learning models that incorporated satellite, meteorological, emission, and land-use data. Exposure estimates were aggregated to beneficiaries' residential ZIP codes by population-weighted averaging. Wildfire smoke waves were defined as ≥ 2 consecutive days with daily smoke PM2.5 > 10 μg/m3. We applied quasi-Poisson regressions to estimate relative risks (RR) of first hospitalizations for overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, and hypertension in ZIP-years with and without smoke waves.

RESULTS: In the full cohort, an increase in two-year average PM2.5 from 5 μg/m3 (WHO annual air quality guideline) to 9 μg/m3 (current U.S. annual PM2.5 standard) was associated with increased risks of overall CVD, cerebrovascular, and hypertension hospitalizations, with stronger associations in ZIP-years without smoke waves than in those with smoke waves (overall CVD: RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.09-1.10 vs. RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.03-1.04; ratio of RR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06). Similar patterns were observed among beneficiaries residing in ZIP codes with annual PM2.5 concentrations below 9 μg/m3 throughout the study period. Smoke wave-related differences in PM2.5-CVD associations were greater among males, urban residents, and residents in the western region compared with their counterparts.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular hospitalizations differed by wildfire smoke wave occurrence. These findings suggest that long-term average PM2.5 may not fully capture episodic high-intensity exposures and may underestimate the cardiovascular morbidity burden in smoke-affected areas, highlighting the need for risk assessments accounting for exposure patterns.

articles.title: Evaluation of carvacrol and quercetin against surgical site infection pathogen Escherichia coli: In silico target identification, anti-biofilm efficacy, and cellular safety.
