Post hoc analyses suggested baseline depression severity moderated the condition effect; participants with moderate and severe comorbid depression responded better to MAST than PCBH TAU. While MAST was not superior to PCBH TAU at post-treatment as hypothesized, it may potentially yield a more enduring impact and work better with comorbid depression; however, these findings require prospective replication. This study advances the literature by comparing brief CBT for anxiety in primary care to a strong active comparison comprising behavioral treatment. MAST may offer implementation advantages due to being manualized and modular. Further research on modular CBT for anxiety is warranted.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of Dimdazenil in primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia: A post-marketing, randomized, open-label, positive-controlled study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the efficacy and safety of Dimdazenil in primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia.

METHODS: In this post-marketing, positive-controlled study, eligible patients were assigned 1:1 to receive either Dimdazenil 2.5 mg or Midazolam 15 mg (minimum 3 doses/week) over 14 days. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in subjective total sleep time (sTST) on Day 14.

RESULTS: 185 patients were included (Dimdazenil, N = 93; Midazolam, N = 92). Dimdazenil significantly increased sTST from baseline (LSM difference, +113.33 min, P < 0.001), with a mean between-group difference of +7.36 min versus Midazolam. A higher proportion of patients in the Dimdazenil group achieved sTST≥390 min (59.49% vs. 48.72%) and sTST≥8 h (34.8% vs. 23.1%). Significant reductions from baseline were also observed in sSL and ISI (both P < 0.001). Daytime functioning was significantly improved with Dimdazenil, as evidenced by marked reductions in ESS, FFS, and TMT-A completion time (all P < 0.001). Moreover, FFS decreased more from baseline with Dimdazenil than Midazolam (-3.86 vs. -2.48). Descriptive improvements in sWASO, sNAW, and FFS scores were observed in patients with depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia. Most TEAEs in the Dimdazenil group were mild (89.66%, 26/29), with no severe TEAE or death reported.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, Dimdazenil was associated with improvements in subjective sleep parameters and daytime functioning in patients with primary insomnia and depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia. Improvements in sleep maintenance outcomes and in patients with depressive episodes/bipolar depressive episode with insomnia warrant further investigation in adequately powered confirmatory studies.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (https://www.chictr.org.cn; registration number: ChiCTR2400085915).

articles.title: The longitudinal relationship between co-rumination and depressive symptoms in adolescents: A systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Co-rumination is associated with depressive symptoms in adolescents, yet the temporal directionality remains unclear because previous meta-analyses have relied largely on cross-sectional evidence. This study examined the longitudinal associations between co-rumination and depressive symptoms and tested moderators using meta-analytic structural equation modeling.

METHODS: Following a preregistered protocol, seven databases were systematically searched for longitudinal studies. Forty-six datasets comprising 18,222 participants were included. One-stage meta-analytic structural equation modeling was used to estimate cross-lagged panel models from pooled correlation matrices. Moderators included age, gender, publication year, individualism, time lag, study quality, co-rumination partner, co-rumination modality, and measurement instruments. Sensitivity analyses examined T1-Tlast associations and modeled co-brooding and co-reflection separately.

RESULTS: T1 co-rumination prospectively predicted T2 depressive symptoms (β = 0.036, p = .020), and T1 depressive symptoms showed a small association with T2 co-rumination (β = 0.031, p = .0495). The forward pathway was consistent across sensitivity analyses, with co-brooding showing the most robust forward association; the reverse pathway was attenuated under T1-Tlast extraction. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, only measurement instruments significantly moderated the cross-lagged paths; publication year showed a suggestive but non-significant omnibus effect. Gender, age, time lag, study quality, individualism, co-rumination partner, and co-rumination modality were not significant moderators.

CONCLUSIONS: Co-rumination is a small but reliable prospective predictor of adolescent depressive symptoms, with co-brooding showing the most consistent forward prediction. The weaker, less robust reverse pathway argues against a strong reciprocal cycle. Future research should examine whether targeting maladaptive, repetitive co-brooding in close peer relationships may benefit prevention efforts.

articles.title: Anxiety and depression associated oral health problems in pediatric populations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Anxiety and depression are common mental disorders and frequently coexist with oral health problems (OHPs) that impair overall well-being and quality of life. While the association of mood disorders and OHPs is well documented in adults, evidence regarding their association in pediatric populations remains unclear.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and reference lists to identify eligible studies. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale. Pooled estimations, including odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences, were calculated with random- or fixed-effects models determined by I2-assessed heterogeneity.

RESULTS: A total of 33 studies were included, 27 of which were eligible for meta-analysis, involving a total of 31,834 participants across 15 countries. The pooled prevalence of anxiety and depression were 57% (95% CI: 41%-73%) and 38% (95% CI: 20%-56%), respectively, among individuals with OHPs, with considerable heterogeneity. The pooled estimations tended to support the hypothesis that anxiety and depression were significantly associated with OHPs, with Odds Ratios (ORs) of 2.67 (95% CI: 1.43-4.97, I2 = 89.2%) and 1.93 (95% CI: 1.22-3.04, I2 = 71.1%). In subgroup analyses, both anxiety and depression appeared to be associated with bruxism and temporomandibular disorders (TMDs).

CONCLUSION: Based on the available evidence, anxiety and depression were associated with OHPs, particularly bruxism and TMDs, in pediatric populations. Given the high heterogeneity and methodological variability across included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Multidisciplinary collaboration is recommended to promote both mental and dental health at an early age.

articles.title: Consensus by design: Conflict of interest and the intravenous ketamine Delphi guidelines.
Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation enhances reward-effort efficiency in severe major depressive disorder.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a highly prevalent psychiatric disorder with changes in motivation to work for rewards being a core symptom. Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has emerged as a promising therapy but its effects on the core features of MDD, such as changes in motivation, remained relatively unexplored. In this randomised, single-blind, cross-over, controlled trial, we used a grip strength effort task to investigate how tVNS impacted choices to exert different levels of physical effort for varying monetary rewards in MDD patients (n = 53) and a non-depressed control group (n = 45). The primary analyses showed no interaction between condition (sham versus tVNS) and group (control versus MDD). However, secondary analyses showed that tVNS effects were dependent on symptom severity. Compared to sham stimulation, tVNS enhanced the efficiency with which participants with severe depressive symptoms allocated physical effort for rewards (reward-effort efficiency). These effects were not seen in healthy participants or MDD patients with less severe symptoms. The effect of tVNS on reward-effort efficiency was driven by reduced unnecessary effort in those with severe MDD symptoms - a reduction in choices to exert additional effort when this was not required to gain a larger reward. This suggests a motivational mechanism by which tVNS exerts its therapeutic effects in severe MDD but these remain secondary findings which should be interpreted with caution. Determining whether the effects of tVNS are linked to broader changes in executive functioning, such as improvements in cognitive flexibility in MDD, should be a key aim for future work.

articles.title: Acupuncture improves depressive symptoms and prefrontal cortical function in mild to moderate depressive disorder: A randomized sham-controlled trial and fNIRS study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive disorder is a common mental illness associated with substantial functional impairment. Although pharmacotherapy is widely used, its effectiveness is often limited by adverse effects and poor adherence. Acupuncture has been increasingly applied as a complementary treatment for depression, and its neurobiological characteristics remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This randomized, sham-controlled trial aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for mild to moderate depressive disorder and to investigate its effects on prefrontal cortical function using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

METHODS: Patients with mild to moderate depressive disorder were randomly assigned to a real acupuncture (RA) group or a sham acupuncture (SA) group and received standardized treatment for 8 weeks. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36), and a traditional Chinese medicine syndrome score. A subset of participants underwent fNIRS assessment during resting-state and task-based conditions to evaluate prefrontal cortical activation and functional connectivity.

RESULTS: Compared with baseline, the RA group showed significant reductions in SDS and SAS scores and significant improvements in SF-36 emotional domains, with effects emerging at Week 4 and persisting up to 12 weeks after treatment. Improvements were greater and more stable in the RA group than in the SA group. fNIRS analyses revealed enhanced activation in dorsolateral and medial prefrontal regions and strengthened prefrontal functional connectivity following acupuncture, whereas neural changes in the SA group were limited.

CONCLUSION: Acupuncture is effective for improving depressive and anxiety symptoms and quality of life in patients with mild to moderate depressive disorder. Modulation of prefrontal cortical activation and connectivity may underlie its antidepressant effects.

articles.title: Aripiprazole once-monthly for patients diagnosed with bipolar I disorder: Number needed to treat, number needed to harm, and likelihood to be helped or harmed.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This post hoc analysis assessed the benefit-risk profile of aripiprazole once-monthly 400 mg (AOM 400) as a long-term maintenance treatment in patients diagnosed with bipolar I disorder (BP-I), using the evidence-based metrics of number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), and the likelihood to be helped or harmed (LHH).

METHODS: Data were derived from a double-blind, randomized withdrawal study that evaluated the efficacy and safety/tolerability of AOM 400 versus placebo over 52 weeks (NCT01567527). The main efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients free from recurrence of any mood episode, while the main safety/tolerability outcome was the incidence of patient discontinuation due to treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

RESULTS: Overall, 73.5% of 132 patients randomized to AOM 400 and 48.9% of 133 patients randomized to placebo were free from recurrence of any mood episode at Week 52 (NNT = 5 [95% CI: 3,8]). NNT (95% CI) values were 5 (4, 9), 4 (3, 7), and-116 (not significant) for patients free from recurrence of a manic mood episode, mixed mood episode, and depressive mood episode, respectively. Discontinuation due to TEAEs was lower with AOM 400 (17.4%) versus placebo (25.6%), resulting in a negative NNH. Using an imputed NNH versus placebo of 1000, LHH was 200 for patients free from recurrence of any mood episode relative to discontinuation due to any TEAE at 52 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Data suggest a favorable benefit-risk profile for AOM 400 versus placebo as a long-term maintenance treatment for BP-I.

articles.title: Single-cell eQTL and Mendelian randomization analyses of shared genetic architecture in major depressive disorder and schizophrenia.
articles.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) and major depressive disorder (MDD) are severe psychiatric disorders with substantial shared genetic liability and frequent clinical co-occurrence, yet their shared cell type-specific genetic mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data from eight major brain cell types with large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for SCZ and MDD. Cell type-specific genetically regulated gene expression was evaluated using Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analyses, followed by validation in independent single-cell RNA sequencing datasets and functional characterization using virtual gene knockout and phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analyses. Integrative analyses prioritized three shared candidate genes, ZSCAN31, BTN3A2, and YLPM1, all showing strong colocalization support (PP·H4 > 0.8). Single-cell transcriptomic validation supported distinct cell type-specific patterns, with ZSCAN31 enriched in astrocytes and endothelial cells, BTN3A2 in microglia, and YLPM1 in oligodendrocytes. Virtual knockout of YLPM1 suggested perturbation of neurodevelopment-related pathways in SCZ and synaptic signaling pathways in MDD. These findings provide a cell type-resolved view of shared genetic architecture between SCZ and MDD and highlight candidate genes for further mechanistic and translational investigation.

articles.title: Measurement stability and differential domain-specific trajectories of the PHQ-9 in late-life depression: Evidence from a collaborative care trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) is routinely used to monitor depressive symptoms. However, whether its empirically derived two-factor structure remains stable across repeated assessments in clinically depressed populations is not well established.

METHODS: Using item-level data from a secondary analysis of the PROACTIVE cluster-randomised controlled trial (N=558; PHQ-9 ≥10 at baseline; aged ≥60 years), we evaluated longitudinal measurement invariance of an empirically derived two-factor PHQ-9 structure across three assessment points using WLSMV structural equation modelling with multiple imputation. We then modelled domain-specific latent growth trajectories by trial arm and examined within-person temporal dynamics using a random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM).

RESULTS: Metric invariance was supported and partial scalar invariance achieved across all three time points, after freeing thresholds for three interpretable items (sleep disturbance, fatigue, and suicidal ideation). The intervention was associated with a steeper improvement in cognitive-affective symptoms but showed no significant effect on somatic symptom trajectories. Within-person somatic deviations at baseline were temporally associated with subsequent cognitive-affective deviations, whereas the reverse was not.

CONCLUSIONS: The two-factor structure of the PHQ-9 is metrically stable through clinical recovery in older adults with moderate-to-severe depression. Domain-specific subscores capture differential treatment response and temporal symptom dynamics that total scores conceal, and can be calculated from existing PHQ-9 items at no additional burden. These findings support the routine use of domain-level monitoring in collaborative care programmes serving older adults in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings.

articles.title: Impact of amyloid-Beta on the functional hierarchies and clinical outcomes in late-life depression.
articles.abstract: Late-life depression (LLD) is characterized by high treatment resistance, particularly in patients with significant cerebral amyloid-beta (Aβ) deposition. However, the underlying mechanisms through which Aβ compromises clinical recovery remain poorly understood. We investigated whether Aβ burden drives treatment resistance by inducing hierarchical rigidity in the brain's macroscale functional organization. We analyzed longitudinal resting-state fMRI and amyloid-PET data from 93 LLD patients (44 Aβ+, 49 Aβ-) around a one-year treatment interval. Functional connectivity (FC) gradients were constructed using diffusion map embedding to characterize the sensory-to-transmodal cortical hierarchy. At baseline, Aβ+ patients exhibited widespread FC gradient aberrations, primarily within the frontoparietal control and default mode networks, despite equivalent depression severity to Aβ- patients. Following treatment, the Aβ+ group showed significantly poorer clinical remission (p < 0.001). Longitudinal analysis revealed a lack of significant group × time interaction, indicating that gradient disorganization in Aβ+ LLD remained unresolved. Cerebral Aβ acts as a physiological constraint on the hierarchical plasticity required for antidepressant response. This "hierarchical rigidity" suggests that Aβ anchors the brain in a dysfunctional, compressed state, precluding the adaptive reorganization necessary for recovery. Baseline functional gradients may serve as a potent prognostic marker for identifying amyloid-associated treatment resistance in LLD.

articles.title: Prospective controlled study of the recombinant zoster vaccine in autoimmune rheumatic disease: robust seroconversion despite intravenous cyclophosphamide.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) prevents shingles in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARD), but intravenous cyclophosphamide (IVCYC) impact on immunogenicity is unknown. Given cell depletion/cytotoxicity, IVCYC is expected to induce profound immunogenicity impairment, we therefore evaluated its impact.

METHODS: This subanalysis of prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial included ARD patients receiving IVCYC (ARD-IVCYC) compared with patients without IVCYC (ARD-no IVCYC) and healthy-controls. RZV was administered in two doses. Humoral response (≥4-fold), geometric mean titers (GMT) and cellular response were assessed after second dose. Disease activity and adverse events (AEs) were recorded.

RESULTS: Forty-one ARD-IVCYC, 164 ARD-no IVCYC, and 164 controls were included. Seroconversion did not differ between ARD-IVCYC and ARD-no IVCYC (91.9% vs. 91.5%) and were lower than controls (99.4%, p = 0.022). Post-vaccination GMTs were comparable between ARD groups (p > 0.999), but lower than controls (p = 0.006). Cellular response and ARDs flares did not differ between groups (p > 0.05), with no severe AEs.

CONCLUSION: RZV elicited >90% humoral response in IVCYC-treated patients, supporting it during IVCYC when warranted (NCT05879419).

articles.title: Ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake among among 55+ year-old Canadians: Exploring the role of racial discrimination, chronic disease comorbidities, and conspiracy beliefs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Canada's COVID-19 vaccination program achieved high overall coverage, yet older racialized and Indigenous people experienced lower uptake and far higher infection and mortality rates. Structural inequities, low health literacy, mistrust, and misinformation contributed to these gaps. Despite early vaccine prioritization, little disaggregated data exist for racialized and Indigenous older adults. This study examines vaccine uptake in these underserved groups to inform more equitable public health strategies and strengthen future pandemic responses.

METHODS: We conducted a Canada-wide cross-sectional online survey of adults aged ≥55 years in March 2025 using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing. Participants completed measures assessing COVID-19 vaccination doses, experiences of major racial discrimination, conspiracy beliefs, health literacy, chronic conditions, and sociodemographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Of the 581participants, 90,3% received at least one dose. Black and Indigenous people were more often unvaccinated (17%), compared to 5.5-6% for Asians and Arabs. Receipt of ≥5 doses was observed in 50% of White, 41.8% of Asian and 13.8% of Black individuals. Older adults (≥65 years) had greater uptake (OR=1.58, 95%CI: 1.07-2.32), as did retirees (OR=2.47) and more highly educated participants (college OR=2.29; Bachelor OR=2.77). Higher conspiracy belief scores were significantly associated with lower odds of receiving higher doses (OR=0.91, 95%CI: 0.89-0.93; p<0.001). Additionally, a greater number of chronic diseases was associated with higher odds of being in a higher vaccine-dose category (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18).

CONCLUSION: Despite pandemic efforts, substantial ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake persisted, with lower coverage in racialized and Indigenous groups. Addressing structural inequities, comorbidities, and misinformation is critical to achieving more equitable, culturally responsive vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Assessment of the Fasciola hepatica saposin-like protein 2 (rFhSAP2) vaccine candidate in sheep: Immunogenicity without protective efficacy.
articles.abstract: Fasciolosis caused by Fasciola hepatica is an economically important parasitic disease of livestock and a major zoonotic disease in humans. Vaccination is a promising strategy to reduce the impact of fasciolosis and dependence on fasciolicides. Saposin-like protein 2 (FhSAP2) has previously shown high immunogenicity and reductions in fluke burden in experimental animal models; however, its efficacy has not been evaluated in sheep. Twenty-one female sheep were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 7): vaccinated, adjuvant control, and infection control. The vaccinated group received 400 μg of rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG, the adjuvant control received Montanide ISA 201 VG alone, and the infection control received saline. Animals received three subcutaneous immunizations at four-week intervals and were subsequently challenged orally with 200 F. hepatica metacercariae. Vaccine efficacy was evaluated based on fluke burden, fecal egg counts, and egg viability. Antigen-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2 antibody responses were assessed by ELISA. Vaccination with rtFhSAP2 resulted in a 16.4% reduction in fluke burden compared with the infection control group (p > 0.05). Reductions in fecal egg counts ranged from 8.9% to 34.5% (p > 0.05). Fecal egg viability remained high, ranging from 88.9% to 91.3% among groups (p > 0.05). Gallbladder-derived egg viability was lower in vaccinated sheep (56.9%) than in the infection control (75.9%) and adjuvant control (73.6%) groups (p > 0.05). Vaccination induced a strong and sustained humoral response. IgG and IgG1 levels were significantly higher in vaccinated sheep than in both control groups from weeks 4-24 and 4-32, respectively. IgG2 levels were also significantly higher from weeks 4-24, although the response was lower than that of IgG1. Overall, rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG was highly immunogenic in sheep, but the humoral response did not translate into significant protection against F. hepatica.

articles.title: A phase III randomized study: Immunogenicity and safety of a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MenACYW-TT is a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine approved for individuals aged ≥6 weeks. This Phase III study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT and MenPS-ACWY in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and in healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.

METHODS: In total, 1,328 participants were randomized by age into three cohorts (Cohort Ia: adults aged 18-55 years, India [N=198]; Cohort Ib: adults aged ≥56 years, India [N=200]; Cohort II: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years, India [N=465] and South Africa [N=465]). The immunogenicity of vaccines was assessed with a serum bactericidal assay using human complement (hSBA). The primary objective was to demonstrate the non-inferiority of immunogenicity of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in terms of hSBA titers in India and South Africa.

RESULTS: The primary objective was met. The non-inferiority of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT was demonstrated on post-vaccination Day 30 in participants aged 2-17 years. The lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the difference in the percentages of the participants achieving seroprotection (hSBA titers ≥1:8) against all four serogroups was greater than -10%. MenACYW-TT demonstrated robust immunogenicity in adults aged 18-55 years and ≥56 years in India. The rates of solicited injection site and systemic reactions were comparable between the participants who received MenACYW-TT versus licensed comparator vaccines. No vaccine-related serious adverse events, study discontinuations, or deaths were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of MenACYW-TT induced non-inferior immune responses and a comparable safety profile versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years. MenACYW-TT was well tolerated and immunogenic in adults, adolescents, and children in India and in adolescents and children in South Africa.

articles.title: Child Neurology: Neonatal Management of Tyrosine Hydroxylase Deficiency: How Early Is Early Enough?
articles.abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency is a rare, treatable, autosomal recessive disorder of monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis that typically presents in infancy or early childhood. Despite potential benefits of presymptomatic treatment with levodopa/carbidopa, prenatal or neonatal diagnosis remains extremely rare. We report 2 preterm neonates from unrelated families, both with known family history of tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency. After early diagnosis, levodopa/carbidopa therapy was initiated during the neonatal period. This proactive approach proved feasible and well tolerated, leading to early normalization of subtle motor abnormalities. These cases highlight the importance of early genetic diagnosis of this rare condition and the feasibility of levodopa/carbidopa treatment in neonates.

articles.title: Recanalization and Recurrent Stroke After Cervical Artery Dissection: Developing Appropriate Clinical Guidance?
Recanalization After Acute Cervical Artery Dissection: A Multicenter International Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rates and factors associated with complete recanalization after cervical artery dissection (CeAD) have not been comprehensively quantified in large cohorts. We sought to determine the 6-month rate of complete recanalization in CeAD, clinical and imaging factors associated with recanalization, and risk of recurrent ischemic stroke based on recanalization status.

METHODS: This was a planned subanalysis of the Antithrombotic Treatment for Stroke Prevention in Cervical Artery Dissection study, a multicenter retrospective cohort including patients with imaging-confirmed CeAD diagnosed between January 2015 and June 2022 at 63 sites worldwide. For this analysis, we included 1,095 patients with single-vessel CeAD causing stenosis at presentation who had available follow-up vascular imaging at 6 months after CeAD. The primary outcome was complete recanalization within 6 months after CeAD. Clinical and imaging variables, as well as recurrent stroke, were compared between patients with and those without complete recanalization. Factors independently associated with complete recanalization were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Time to complete recanalization was analyzed using an accelerated failure time Weibull model.

RESULTS: Among 1,095 included patients (median age 45 years; 46.7% female), 634 (57.9%) achieved complete recanalization by 6 months. In multivariable analysis, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of complete recanalization (odds ratio [OR] 0.97 per year; 95% CI 0.96-0.98; p < 0.001). Diabetes (OR 0.46; 95% CI 0.27-0.81; p = 0.006), active smoking (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50-0.95; p = 0.025), and complete occlusion at presentation (OR 0.44; 95% CI 0.32-0.59; p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of complete recanalization. Complete occlusion at presentation was associated with both longer time to, and lower rates of, complete recanalization. We observed no effect of antithrombotic regimen (antiplatelet therapy vs anticoagulation) on complete recanalization. Incomplete recanalization was associated with a nonsignificant numerically higher proportion of recurrent stroke (5.4% vs 3.5%; p = 0.064).

DISCUSSION: Almost 60% of patients with CeAD achieved complete vessel recanalization by 6 months. Older age, diabetes, smoking, and complete occlusion at presentation were independently associated with incomplete recanalization. Further study is required to determine whether these findings may help guide tailored imaging surveillance and secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Associations of Antibodies Against Several Infections With Alzheimer Disease Neuropathology: A Prospective Cohort Study Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Associations of common infections with Alzheimer disease (AD) risk have been reported. A hypothesized mechanism for these is cerebral β-amyloid (Aβ) aggregation as a defense to infection. We studied whether serologic measures of several infections in the UK population are associated with measures of AD neuropathology.

METHODS: This prospective association study used data from the 1946 British birth cohort. Circulating antibodies against 14 pathogens, measured at age 60-64 years, were modelled as pathogen serostatus (indicating lifetime exposure to an agent), pathogen burden indices (measuring cumulative exposure to 2+ pathogens), and seroreactivity tertiles (indicating recent immunologic activity against pathogens). Associations of these were tested with plasma phosphorylated tau at threonine 217 (p-tau217) (primary outcome) and Aβ status (secondary outcome), measured with PET scans, at ages 69-71 years. Modelling used multivariable quantile and logistic regression. Model 1 adjusted for sex and ages at serology and outcome assessment, and models 2 and 3 additionally adjusted for APOE ε4 carriage and education, respectively. We also tested for interactions in associations by APOE ε4 carriage, education, and sex, and for interactions between herpes simplex virus 1 exposure with cytomegalovirus (CMV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) exposure.

RESULTS: A total of 1,356 and 424 individuals had complete data for p-tau217 and Aβ-PET analyses, respectively. Mean age at p-tau217 was 69.9 years (SD 0.7), and 51.3% of participants were female. Median p-tau217 was 0.30 pg/mL (interquartile range 0.21-0.44). 28.3% had Aβ-positive scans. No notable associations were observed for serology measures with either outcome in main models, except for an unexpected association of herpes simplex virus 2 seropositivity with lower p-tau217 at the 75th quantile (-0.07 pg/mL in seropositive individuals; 95% CI -0.10 to -0.03). Odds of Aβ-PET positivity may have been higher for individuals seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus (odds ratio [OR] 2.84; 95% CI 0.95-8.52) and Toxoplasma gondii (OR 1.69; 95% CI 0.94-3.05). There were also potential interactions in p-tau217 associations by APOE ε4 carriage (for Helicobacter pylori and CMV) and educational attainment (for H pylori).

DISCUSSION: These findings do not imply associations between exposures to many common infections and AD neuropathologies. The possibility of pathogen interactions with APOE ε4 carriage and education in relation to AD neuropathology warrants further study.

articles.title: Infection as a Contributor to Dementia: The Plot Thickens.
Recommendations for the Management of Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension With Spinal Longitudinal Epidural CSF Collection: A Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) results from spinal CSF leakage. Epidural blood patch (EBP) is an important first-line treatment. However, pre-EBP, intra-EBP, and post-EBP practice varies widely owing to limited consensus guidance. We aimed to develop expert consensus statements to support clinical decision-making in SIH management, including peri-EBP practices, focusing on patients with spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection (SLEC) before definitive leak type classification.

METHODS: An international multidisciplinary Delphi process was conducted between January 2024 and July 2025, involving experts in neurology, neurosurgery, radiology, and anesthesiology. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥70% agreement for strong agreement, 60%-69% for partial agreement, and <60% for no consensus, based on a 5-point Likert scale in round 3. Responses were collected anonymously using an online survey platform, with summarized feedback from the previous round provided between rounds.

RESULTS: Fourteen experts were invited, with 10, 9, and 9 participants in rounds 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Before EBP, bed rest was recommended for recent-onset SIH with severe orthostatic headache (88.9%); other conservative methods such as abdominal binder and hydration were considered not mandatory (90%). Semitargeted EBP was recommended as initial management for patients with extradural CSF collections (70%). Dynamic CT myelography was preferred for localization (70%). Post-EBP care was variable, particularly in bed rest duration, with most recommendations (70%) exceeding 12 hours. Definitions of clinical remission (80%) and radiologic remission (90%) were established. Radiologic follow-up after clinical remission was recommended (78%). No consensus was reached on follow-up strategies for persistent symptoms, although "doing nothing" was not recommended. No consensus was reached for persistent extradural CSF despite clinical remission, requiring an individualized approach. Light activity after EBP was recommended within a few days (70%). No consensus was reached on the optimal number of EBPs before invasive leak localization or surgical intervention.

DISCUSSION: This Delphi study outlines expert recommendations and uncertainties for SIH management, including peri-EBP practices. This study incorporated the initial management strategy for patients in whom leak-type classification was incomplete. However, the treatment section primarily focused on the SLEC-positive setting and presumed ventral dural tears; lateral dural tears and CSF-venous fistulas warrant future consensus development.

articles.title: Bibliometrics and Thematic Content of the Papers Published in Neurology Over the Past 75 Years.
Incidence and Post-Stroke Survival in the Normandy Stroke Population-Based Study (2017-2022): Impact of Time-Based Versus Tissue-Based Definitions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The 11th edition of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11) incorporates a tissue-based definition of stroke and may alter estimates of incidence and outcomes. We assessed whether transitioning from a time-based to a tissue-based definition introduces age-dependent changes in stroke incidence and post-stroke survival.

METHODS: The Normandy Stroke Study is a population-based study using multiple overlapping sources to identify stroke cases in Caen-Normandy-Metropole, France. Events occurring between May 15, 2017, and December 31, 2022, were classified using time-based (symptoms ≥24 hours) and tissue-based definitions (symptoms ≥24 hours or <24 hours with neuroimaging evidence of ischemic injury).

RESULTS: Among 3,826 first-ever strokes meeting the tissue-based definition, median (IQR) age was 76 (64-85) years, and 1,932 (50.5%) were female. The age-standardized incidence rate of stroke (95% CI) was 161 (156-166) per 100,000 person-years (ESP2013), including 132 (128-137) for ischemic or undetermined stroke, 22 (20-24) for intracerebral hemorrhage, and 7 (6-8) for subarachnoid hemorrhage. Three-year mortality was 36.4% (95% CI 34.9-38.0). Compared with the time-based definition, the tissue-based definition increased stroke incidence by 6.5% and reduced 3-year mortality by 3.9%. The impact of the tissue-based definition on stroke incidence was greater at younger ages (all strokes: younger than 55 years = +8.5%; 55 years or older = +6.0%; ischemic stroke: younger than 55 years = +12.5%; 55 years or older = +7.3%).

DISCUSSION: Adoption of a tissue-based definition modestly increased stroke incidence and post-stroke survival, with greater impacts at younger ages. Implementation of ICD-11 may introduce age-related differences in temporal trends, highlighting the importance of consistent definitions in stroke surveillance.

articles.title: Intracerebral Hemorrhage Expansion in Late Presenters: Proposed Target Expansion Criteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The benefit of therapies targeting hematoma expansion (HE) in acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is highly time dependent and greatest within the first 2 hours after onset. We aimed to develop imaging-based "target expansion criteria" to identify late presenters (2-12 hours from onset/last seen well) who remain at high risk of HE. To achieve this goal, a practical risk score (target expansion score) was developed.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective cohort study. To mirror a clinical trial population, we excluded patients with brainstem ICH, anticoagulation, and baseline ICH volume >100 mL. The primary outcome was HE (>33%/6 mL). The following imaging predictors of HE were analyzed: high ultra-early hematoma growth (uHG) (baseline volume/onset to imaging time >10 mL/h), hypodensities on noncontrast CT (NCCT), and spot sign on CT angiography (CTA). The study population was randomly divided into development and validation cohorts, and a weighted score was derived from estimates from multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Overall, 492 patients were included: 345 (70.1%) in the development and 147 (29.9%) in the validation cohort. A 4-point score was created, based on independent predictors of HE (high uHG: 1 point, NCCT hypodensities: 1 point, and CTA spot sign: 2 points). The score showed good discrimination in the development and validation cohorts (area under the curve [AUC] 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.83, and AUC 0.79, 95% CI 0.71-0.87, respectively). We observed a nonlinear increase in the frequency of HE and mean absolute hematoma growth with higher scores: 9.8% and 0.9 mL (score 0), 17.1% and 3.9 mL (score 1), 48.3% and 11.5 mL (score 2), 70.8% and 13.0 mL (score 3), and 87.5% and 26.9 mL (score 4). These findings were confirmed in the validation cohort. A dichotomized score greater than or equal to 2 predicted HE with 0.61 sensitivity and 0.85 specificity in the development cohort and 0.64 sensitivity with 0.84 specificity in the validation cohort.

DISCUSSION: Imaging-based target expansion criteria, defined as a target expansion score ≥2, identified late-presenting patients with ICH at high risk of HE. These findings might inform future trials targeting HE and increase the pool of eligible patients.

articles.title: The Rural Hospital Crisis Is a Neurologic Crisis: Advancing Equity in Neurology.
Disease Control in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: Consensus Definition, Evolution, and Patient Characterization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a chronic fluctuating neuromuscular disease. Some patients keep experiencing symptoms or adverse events (AEs) despite tailored therapeutic schemes. The aim of this study was to characterize adequately controlled gMG and describe patients' evolution and outcomes, including estimated direct health costs in a universal health care system.

METHODS: Spanish expert neurologists developed a definition of adequately controlled gMG using Delphi methodology. This was applied to an existing cohort of patients recently diagnosed with gMG during 1998-2020 in a Spanish referral neuromuscular diseases' unit. Control status, clinical outcomes, AEs, and health care resource utilization (HCRU) were described biennially.

RESULTS: We assessed 220 patients diagnosed with gMG (54.5% women; mean age at onset of 58 years; 84% anti-AChR, 6% anti-MuSK, 10% seronegative). Adequately controlled gMG was defined as achieving Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America Post-Intervention Status classification of clinical stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or minimal manifestations stable for a year; having an MG-ADL score ≤2; experiencing no clinical exacerbations during the last year requiring a change in immunosuppressive therapy or rescue therapy; and having no or mild AE to therapies (100% of experts in agreement or total agreement). The proportion adequately controlled (AC) patients increased from 62.0% at 2 years after first visit to 81.9% after 8 years of follow-up. 47.3% of patients remained AC in every observation, and 17.7% remained not adequately controlled (NC) in every observation. No features were significantly associated with adequate control. AE-related drug interruption rates were higher in NC patients (ranging from 50% to 100% during the study). The mean cost per patient/year ranged from 2,718.6€ in the first biennial period to 843.1€ in the last biennial period for AC patients and from 10,190.1€ to 5,827.4€ for NC patients.

DISCUSSION: Based on the new gMG control consensus definition, almost 1 in 5 patients do not reach disease control even after 8 years of evolution. Those patients lacked specific clinical features, underscoring the unpredictability of the gMG course. Burden of AE-related drug interruptions, HCRU, and costs per patients/year were higher among those patients NC. However, our study is unicentric and included patients from a referral unit, with a possible overrepresentation of NC patients.

articles.title: Acute Imbalance Syndrome vs Acute Vestibular Syndrome: Clinical and Topographical Differentiation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Stroke is a major differential diagnosis in patients with acute vertigo/dizziness or imbalance. Current diagnostic algorithms such as head impulse test, gaze-evoked nystagmus, and test of skew are optimized for presentations with spontaneous nystagmus (SPN), traditionally called acute vestibular syndrome (AVS). However, in recent studies, a relevant proportion of patients with stroke-related vertigo/dizziness had no SPN, but rather postural or gait imbalance, a phenotype lately termed acute imbalance syndrome (AIS). We aimed to outline the pathoanatomical differences of stroke-related AIS vs AVS and its clinical implications.

METHODS: Patients with MRI-proven stroke-related acute vertigo/dizziness or imbalance were included in this emergency department (ED) cohort study at LMU Hospital prospectively. Vestibular, ocular motor, and postural signs were documented (including SPN presence/intensity by video oculography, postural imbalance by posturography). Patients were classified as suffering from AIS or AVS based on the presence of SPN. Stroke lesion distribution was depicted in Montreal Neurological Institute space and supplemented by structural disconnectome mapping from the lesion cores. Multivariate lesion symptom-mapping based on support-vector regression and disconnectome mapping was applied for SPN intensity and sway path as surrogate markers for AVS and AIS.

RESULTS: Of 75 patients (age: 65.7 ± 13.3 years, 40% female), 58.7% were diagnosed with AIS, 38.7% with AVS, and 2.7% with central positional vertigo. In AIS, the lesion core was located in the anterior cerebellar lobe and deep cerebellar nuclei (superior cerebellar artery/posterior inferior cerebellar artery territory) connecting to the bilateral pontomesencephalic tegmentum through the superior cerebellar peduncle. AVS stroke lesions were mostly located in the posterior cerebellar/flocculonodular lobe (posterior inferior cerebellar artery/anterior inferior cerebellar artery territory) and connected to the ipsilesional vestibular nucleus (VN) and bilateral medial longitudinal fascicle (MLF) through the inferior cerebellar peduncle. SPN intensity correlated with voxels in the cerebellar lobules VI-IX connecting to VN and MLF. Postural sway was associated with a small local cluster in the cerebellar Crus I.

DISCUSSION: AIS accounts for more than half of patients with stroke-related vertigo/dizziness or imbalance. AIS lesions were located in the anterior cerebellar lobe, disturbing cerebellar-pontomesencephalic networks for posture and gait control. AVS lesions affected the posterior cerebellar/flocculonodular lobe and associated vestibulo-ocular reflex networks. Recognition of both clinical phenotypes is essential to identify all strokes among patients with vertigo/dizziness in the emergency setting.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: DRKS00008992; U1111-1172-8719.

articles.title: Effects of Blood Pressure Lowering by Hematoma Location in Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
authors: as the INTERACT and ATACH-II Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering is now recognized as an effective approach to improve outcome after acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). However, whether the effect varies by hematoma location is uncertain. We aimed to determine the heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome by hematoma location.

METHODS: We conducted a pooled analysis of individual patient-level data (IPD) from all 4 Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction in Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage Trials (INTERACT) and the second Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage (ATACH-II) trial, which were international, randomized, open, blinded end point assessed, controlled trials that investigated the effectiveness of early intensive BP control in acute ICH. ICH location was classified as lobar or deep hemisphere or infratentorial. The primary outcome was death or disability (modified Rankin Scale scores 3-6) at 90 days or 6 months (for INTERACT3). The heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome by ICH location was estimated using generalized linear mixed models with trial as a random effect and adjustment for prespecified clinical covariates and an interaction term of "treatment-by-location."

RESULTS: Among 11,288 patients (mean age 62.5 years [SD 12.7]; 4,056 [35.9%] women), 1,141 (10.1%) had lobar ICH, 9,202 (81.5%) had deep ICH and 945 (8.4%) had infratentorial ICH. Compared with deep or infratentorial ICH, lobar ICH occurred in older patients, was less often associated with intraventricular hemorrhage, and had larger hematoma volumes (all p < 0.001). The effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome of death or disability differed by ICH location (p for interaction = 0.033). A clear benefit was only seen in deep ICH (adjusted odds ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.74-0.89; p < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: Hematoma location modifies the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome after ICH, with the benefit observed only in deep ICH.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: These trials are registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (INTERACT1 NCT00226096; INTERACT2 NCT00716079; INTERACT3 NCT03209258; INTERACT4 NCT03790800; and ATACH-II NCT01176565).

articles.title: Neurology Journal Club: Characteristics and Outcomes of Patients With IDH-Mutant Grade 2 and 3 Gliomas After Deferred or Adjuvant Radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: This journal club article reviews the strengths and limitations of a 2025 study by Lanman et al., investigating outcomes-particularly overall survival-in patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase mutant (IDHmt) WHO grade 2 and 3 gliomas who received either adjuvant postsurgical radiotherapy (aXRT) or deferred radiotherapy (dXRT). Despite unclear evidence of survival benefit, current standardized guidelines recommend aXRT-after surgery but before progression-as first-line treatment for high-risk patients defined by higher grade, older age, and subtotal resection. This study demonstrated that although aXRT delayed tumor progression in this cohort, it was associated with worse overall survival. This retrospective, dual-institution analysis highlights a discrepancy between current guidelines and real-world clinical outcomes, emphasizing the need for prospective studies evaluating dXRT in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas.

articles.title: Contraceptive and Enzyme-Inducing Antiseizure Medication Coprescription Among US Medicaid Beneficiaries With Epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: People with epilepsy of child-bearing potential (PWECP) require access to highly effective contraception, yet many antiseizure medications (ASMs) can reduce the effectiveness of some hormonal methods by inducing hepatic enzymes. In this retrospective cohort study, we aimed to identify the proportion of PWECP prescribed a susceptible hormonal contraceptive method who were concurrently prescribed an interacting ASM and patient characteristics associated with coprescription.

METHODS: We obtained Medicaid claims data from 2016 to 2021 for female beneficiaries and defined a cohort of people with epilepsy on ASMs prescribed at least 1 method of hormonal contraception susceptible to hepatic enzyme induction. Using prescription fill dates and contraceptive procedure dates, we identified periods of inducing ASM and susceptible contraceptive overlap lasting at least 14 days. We used descriptive statistics to calculate the proportion experiencing overlap and median days of overlap. We used logistic regression to identify associated patient characteristics with any 14-day period of overlap and binominal regression to identify characteristics associated with greater proportion of overlap days.

RESULTS: Our cohort included 110,976 PWECP (median age 24 [interquartile range 18-30] years, 54.8% White non-Hispanic). Of those, 21,923 were prescribed a susceptible contraceptive method from 2018 to 2021. In that group, 7,154 (32.6%) had at least a 14-day period of overlap with an enzyme-inducing ASM. The median days of overlap for this group were 218 days (interquartile range 74-511). Patient characteristics associated with both any period of overlap and longer periods of overlap included intellectual disability (any overlap: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.33, 95% CI 2.19-2.48; longer overlap: 2.27, 95% CI 2.05-2.53), drug-resistant epilepsy (any overlap: aOR 1.73, 95% CI 1.62-1.84; longer overlap: 1.27, 95% CI 1.14-1.41), and age older than 35 years compared with 19-34 years (any overlap: 1.45, 95% CI 1.32-1.59; longer overlap: 1.51, 95% CI 1.29-1.75).

DISCUSSION: Drug interactions with ASMs leading to reduced contraceptive effectiveness are common among PWECP prescribed susceptible hormonal contraception. Certain populations, including those with intellectual disability, drug-resistant epilepsy, or age older than 35 years, were more likely to experience these drug interactions. Limitations include that our data set lacks information on adherence, counseling, pregnancy intentions, sexual orientation and activity, and barrier use.

articles.title: "Railroad Track" Brain Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET Sign in Antiphospholipid Syndrome-Related Posterior Cortical Atrophy.
LncRNA 34962 drives pulmonary vascular remodeling in pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease through the miR-3575/cMYC/TERT signaling axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is the most prevalent form of pulmonary hypertension, characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling driven by abnormal proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Although long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate cardiovascular pathophysiology, their role in PH-LHD remains unclear.

METHODS: PH-LHD was established by aortic banding. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) revealed differentially expressed lncRNAs in the pulmonary vasculature. The roles of lncRNA 34962 in PASMC proliferation and migration were assessed through gain- and loss-of-function experiments and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation, Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), and wound-healing assays. The competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanism was examined using dual-luciferase reporter assays and RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analyses. Therapeutic potential was evaluated in vivo by intratracheal delivery of adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated short hairpin RNA.

RESULTS: LncRNA 34962 was upregulated in pulmonary arteries and PASMCs from PH-LHD rats. Its overexpression enhanced PASMC proliferation and migration, whereas its knockdown exerted inhibitory effects. Mechanistically, lncRNA 34962 sequestered miR-3575, thereby relieving miR-3575-mediated repression of cMYC. cMYC upregulation increased telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) expression and telomerase activation, sustaining cell-cycle progression and the proliferative and migratory capacity of PASMCs. In vivo, AAV9-mediated lncRNA 34962 knockdown attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, reduced right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and left atrial pressure (LAP), and alleviated ventricular hypertrophy in PH-LHD rats.

CONCLUSIONS: LncRNA 34962 promotes pulmonary vascular remodeling in PH-LHD through the miR-3575-cMYC-TERT signaling axis, supporting its therapeutic potential in PH-LHD.

articles.title: Gentiopicroside attenuates renal ischemia-reperfusion injury through suppression of JNK/MAPK signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) with significant clinical impact. Gentiopicroside (GPS), a natural secoiridoid glycoside isolated from traditional medicinal plants, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective activities, yet its potential role in renal IRI has not been fully explored.

METHODS: Mice underwent bilateral renal ischemia with oral GPS pretreatment. Renal function, histological injury, apoptosis, and inflammation were evaluated. Primary mouse renal tubular epithelial cells (mRTECs) and BUMPT cells were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R). Network pharmacology, molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were performed to identify potential GPS-associated pathways and targets. JNK signaling was further examined using JNK1-specific siRNA and anisomycin.

RESULTS: GPS improved renal function, reduced tubular injury, apoptosis, and inflammation in IRI mice, and increased viability while reducing apoptosis in OGD/R-treated mRTECs and BUMPT cells. Network pharmacology highlighted MAPK signaling, and docking identified MAPK8 (JNK1) as a candidate GPS target. CETSA showed increased JNK1 thermal stability after GPS treatment. JNK1 silencing phenocopied the anti-apoptotic effects of GPS, with no significant additional reduction in JNK phosphorylation or caspase-3 cleavage after GPS treatment. Conversely, anisomycin partially reversed GPS-mediated protection. GPS also attenuated oxidative stress and modulated ferroptosis- and autophagy-associated molecular changes during OGD/R injury.

CONCLUSION: GPS protects against renal IRI and OGD/R-induced tubular injury, with JNK/MAPK signaling serving as an important, but not exclusive, mediator of its anti-apoptotic effects. These findings support further investigation of oral GPS as a potential therapy for AKI.

articles.title: Selenomethionine regulates macrophage polarization through mitochondrial dynamics via NF-κB signaling to attenuate sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis frequently leads to multiple organ dysfunction, among which sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) is a severe complication associated with high mortality and limited targeted therapies. Selenomethionine (SeMet) possesses potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its role in SIC remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: SIC models were established in C57BL/6J mice by intraperitoneal injection of LPS at 10 mg/kg or by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Mice were pretreated with SeMet (7.5 μg/20 g) by gavage for one week, followed by LPS challenge for 24 h. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography, including left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDd), and left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVEDs). SeMet improved cardiac function in SIC mice, and this protective effect was associated with NF-κB signaling-mediated regulation of macrophage polarization. To further investigate the anti-inflammatory effects of SeMet in vitro, RAW264.7 macrophages were treated with 1 μM SeMet for 24 h and then stimulated with 1 μg/mL LPS for another 24 h. Immunofluorescence staining, Western blotting, and ELISA were performed to evaluate inflammatory responses and the underlying mechanisms. The results showed that SeMet modulated macrophage polarization through the NF-κB signaling pathway and exerted significant anti-inflammatory effects.

CONCLUSIONS: SeMet regulates macrophage polarization by inhibiting activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby alleviating sepsis-induced cardiac dysfunction in SIC mice.

articles.title: In vitro investigation of sitagliptin on HaCaT keratinocyte migration and proteomics analysis for wound healing applications.
articles.abstract: Sitagliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor commonly used to treat diabetes, has been linked to improved wound healing in diabetic patients. However, its direct effects on skin repair are not well understood and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the concentration dependent effects of sitagliptin on HaCaT keratinocytes and primary fibroblasts in vitro and explored the molecular pathways involved. Sitagliptin enhanced keratinocyte migration at 150 μg/mL, without affecting proliferation, while no significant effects were observed on fibroblast proliferation and migration, indicating a cell-type specific response. Sitagliptin treatment induced morphological changes in HaCaT keratinocytes, including elongated actin filaments and increased cell surface area, consistent with cytoskeletal changes that support motility. Proteomic analysis revealed keratin remodeling (Keratin5 (KRT5), Keratin 16 (KRT16), Keratin 17 (KRT17) upregulation and Keratin6A (KRT6A) downregulation), increased Enkurin domain-containing protein 1 (ENKD1), Family with sequence similarity 83 member H (FAM83H) and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and reduced β-catenin (CTNNB1), suggesting cytoskeletal reorganization and reduced intercellular adhesion associated with enhanced keratinocyte migration. Targeted RT-qPCR validation confirmed these transcriptional changes and identified integrin β1 (ITGB1) as an induced network hub in the associated protein-protein interaction network. Overall, sitagliptin enhances keratinocyte migration in association with changes in cytoskeletal and cell-adhesion-related proteins, although a direct causal relationship between these molecular changes and enhanced migration remains to be established. These findings provide preliminary evidence that, beyond glycemic control, sitagliptin may have therapeutic potential for wound healing applications to accelerate skin repair and tissue regeneration.

articles.title: Hierarchical analysis of metabolic phenotype reveals distinct microbiota and circulatory transcriptome in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate how visceral adiposity and insulin resistance, defined respectively by visceral adiposity index (VAI) and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, jointly influence gut microbiota composition and immune transcriptomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and to explore potential mechanistic pathways.

METHODS: We enrolled 169 adults stratified by VAI, controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), TyG index, and physical activity. Gut microbiota and immune transcriptomes were profiled using 16S rRNA and RNA sequencing, respectively. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified across subgroups. Functional annotation and upstream regulatory networks were analyzed using DAVID and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA).

RESULTS: Higher VAI correlated with obesity, inflammation, and steatosis, while the TyG index independently predicted fibrosis risk. Specific taxa, includingTM7x,Acidaminococcus, andDielma, were consistently enriched in adverse metabolic phenotypes. Transcriptomic analysis of circulating immune cells identified 348 TyG-associated DEGs significantly enriched in mitochondrial and cytokine signaling pathways. IPA highlighted IL6, SREBF1, PTGS1 and SNCA as central regulators linking metabolic stress to mitochondrial dysfunction.

CONCLUSIONS: Gut microbiota shifts and immune transcriptome alterations jointly mediate the interplay between insulin resistance and visceral adiposity in MASLD. The identified insulin resistance-associated genes suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction and cytokine dysregulation contribute to obesity-related hepatic pathology, supporting precision strategies targeting VAI and metabolic dysregulation.

articles.title: Click chemistry-driven modular radionuclide labeling of HER2 nanobody: An integrated platform for diagnosis and treatment of precision oncology.
articles.abstract: Current HER2-targeted theranostics lack a unified platform capable of integrating high-resolution PET/SPECT imaging, 177Lu radionuclide therapy, and personalized dosimetry. To address this, we developed a bioorthogonal "click-to-label" platform​ enabling universal radiolabeling of a single anti-HER2 nanobody (HER2VHH) with four clinically relevant isotopes (18F, 68Ga, 99mTc, 177Lu). This trans-cyclooctene (TCO) and tetrazine (Tz)-mediated approach circumvents direct exposure of the fragile nanobody to harsh radiolabeling conditions, thereby preserving its immunoreactivity. Compared to conventional direct labeling, our platform demonstrated significantly enhanced tumor retention and superior imaging contrast, while allowing flexible labeling with various radionuclides. Notably, the 177Lu-labeled HER2VHH effectively inhibited tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner without detectable off-target toxicity. These findings support 18F/68Ga/99mTc/177Lu-TzTCO-HER2VHH as a promising HER2-targeted theranostic platform, combining sensitive PET/SPECT imaging with effective radionuclide therapy, and demonstrating substantial potential for clinical translation in precision oncology.

articles.title: Discovery of novel ROCK inhibitors RX-021 and RX-044 with intraocular pressure-lowering effect for glaucoma treatment.
articles.abstract: Through systematic optimization of lead D25, we identified two novel ROCK inhibitors, RX-021 and RX-044. Maintaining DFG interactions while optimizing linker flexibility was critical for potency. RX-044 showed excellent ROCK1/2 inhibition (IC50 = 10.01 and 9.68 nM), favorable kinase selectivity, and no cytotoxicity in HTM cells. In a mouse ocular hypertension model, RX-021 achieved superior IOP reduction (5.38 ± 1.51 mmHg at 4 h) versus (S)-Netarsudil, with sustained 24 h efficacy and reversible HTM cell effects. Both compounds provided significant retinal neuroprotection, preserving retinal ganglion cell survival, restoring electroretinography responses, and ameliorating histopathological changes. Slit-lamp exams confirmed that initial ocular irritation subsided with extended dosing. These findings establish RX-021 and RX-044 as promising novel ROCK inhibitors with enhanced IOP-lowering efficacy and good retinal protective effects for glaucoma therapy.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of HSP70-mediated HEMTACs as novel androgen receptor degraders.
articles.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as an important therapeutic strategy for addressing challenging protein targets. While Proteolysis-Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs) are the leading TPD approach, their reliance on a limited set of E3 ligases poses challenges, including tissue-specific restrictions and the emergence of drug resistance. To address these limitations, we previously developed the HEMTAC (HEat shock protein-Mediated TArgeting Chimeras) platform, which recruits HSP90 to induce target protein degradation. Building on this concept, the current study expands the HEMTAC framework by integrating HSP70, a key molecular chaperone, to target the androgen receptor (AR). We designed and synthesized a series of novel HSP70-recruiting HEMTACs by linking an HSP70 ligand (a derivative of VER-155008) with an AR-binding ligand. Biological evaluation identified compound 39 as an active degrader that induced substantial AR degradation in LNCaP prostate cancer cells. This work supports the feasibility of recruiting HSP70 for TPD and provides a molecular tool for AR-degradation research, thereby expanding the TPD toolbox for future drug discovery.

articles.title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Intracellular Ca2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K+ channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K+ currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (CaV) channels that provide localized Ca2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+CaV channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β4 (BKβ4), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and CaV channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ4 promotes BK+CaV nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the CaV subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+CaV channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.

articles.title: Septin binding restricts Shigella growth and triggers intracellular tolerance.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Pathogen survival relies on their ability to adapt to changing environments, yet how intracellular bacteria tolerate cell-autonomous immunity remains unclear. Septins assemble into cage-like structures around cytoplasmic Shigella targeted by autophagy, but their antibacterial activity was unknown. Using advanced microscopy and cell-free reconstitution, we show that septins polymerize into circumferentially oriented filaments that inhibit bacterial growth. RNA-sequencing reveals that septin binding to Shigella upregulates type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors and triggers a stress response. Underlying this, septin-bound Shigella possess hyperpolarized membranes, but without lethally damaged cell envelope. We show that exposure to septin binding enhances the impact of the cell envelope-targeting antibiotic polymyxin B. During infection, T3SS effector OspC1 prevents septin recruitment, while stress-response regulator cspC protects against septin-mediated changes to membrane potential. Hence, septin binding is intrinsically antibacterial and is sensed by Shigella as a danger signal to promote mechanisms of intracellular tolerance.

articles.title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body's glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.

articles.title: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log10 at 3 mo postpartum, "controllers") and 12 with more stable levels ("noncontrollers"). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure.

articles.title: Revised estimates of types and duration of long COVID symptoms based on claims records from 245 million US patients.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: COVID-19 has been reported to cause multisystem effects lasting years [Z. Al-Aly, E. Topol, Science 383, 830-832 (2024)]. These findings are primarily based on cohort studies comparing test-positive COVID-19 patients to controls without known COVID-19 infection, tested or untested [M. Cai, Y. Xie, E. J. Topol, Z. Al-Aly, Nat. Med. 30, 1564-1573 (2024)]. However, such comparisons can be biased by the reasons people were tested. Using 14.4 billion insurance claims from 244.7 million US patients, we find that most long-term effects attributed to COVID-19 by unrestricted control designs likely reflect bias due to selective testing of individuals with non-COVID conditions, causing long-term effects of those conditions to be misattributed to COVID-19. We removed this bias by analyzing only tested individuals, comparing test-positive to test-negative patients. Across 614 clinical outcomes followed over 2 y, the test-based design resulted in 83.5% fewer symptoms being attributable to COVID-19 between 30 to 119 d after infection (43 attributable symptoms vs. 262 for the unrestricted control design), a 98.2% reduction at 120 to 359 d (5 vs. 286), and a 100% reduction at 360 to 719 d (0 vs. 369). The unrestricted control design also attributed unrelated outcomes (e.g., firearm injuries) to COVID-19 at a high rate, whereas the testing-based design did not. The test-based control design may modestly underestimate some effects. This study does not indicate that symptoms beyond one year are not genuine but that their attributability to COVID-19 is uncertain.

articles.title: Propagating shocks and transitions across networked food systems: Insights from multiplayer microeconomic modeling.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Accelerating global change is affecting coupled natural ecosystems and human activities in every part of the world. The local and regional expressions of these changes are a product of interacting and networked systems such that a shock, trend or development transition in one region, ecosystem, or sector can propagate impacts to other regions, ecosystems, and sectors. Informed adaptation and development strategies require an understanding of how signals propagate through these coupled systems and regions. Here, we synthesize findings from our work in Ethiopia and Mali, where we developed and applied a modeling system designed to capture cross-sector dynamics of networked food, water, and energy systems at subnational scale. We approach the problem using a multiplayer microeconomic model that accounts for diverse objectives through chains of food production, distribution, and consumption that connect resource regions to market regions. This paper draws lessons from three case studies in Ethiopia and one in Mali that are designed to examine impacts of a subnational climate shock (drought), a centralized national policy decision (export restrictions in response to food shortage), a distributed development strategy (solar-powered groundwater irrigation), and an external intervention (food aid). In each case, we consider how an initial signal propagates through the country via markets, infrastructure, and interactions between economic actors. An understanding of this propagation can inform strategies for food security in a changing climate.

articles.title: circEPSTI1 regulates miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 signaling axis to enhance dengue infection and is suppressed by Tiplaxtinin.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as crucial regulators of gene expression in various diseases. Their role in dengue remains unexplored. In this study, circEPSTI1 induction was observed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma of dengue patients. The induction of circEPSTI1 is interferon-dependent and enhances DENV infection by sponging the expression of miR-942-5p. The antiviral role of miR-942-5p is mediated by bidirectional inhibition through targeting conserved genomic sequences of the DENV genome of different subtypes across NS1, NS3, and NS5 and the host AKT1 signaling pathway. RNA-seq analysis of DENV-infected circEPSTI1 knockdown A549 cells identified SERPINE1 and AKT1 signaling pathways to be dysregulated significantly. circEPSTI1 relieves the inhibition of miR-942-5p over DENV genomic RNA and the host SERPINE1 to activate AKT1 signaling. The activation of AKT1 signaling facilitates cell survival and enhances DENV replication. The expression of SERPINE1 and circEPSTI1 was upregulated in Dengue patients, and pharmaceutical inhibition of SERPINE1 through Tiplaxtinin inhibits the DENV replication by reducing the expression of circEPSTI1. Overall, our result demonstrates the therapeutic potential of Tiplaxtinin by targeting the circEPSTI1-miR-942-5p-SERPINE1-AKT1 axis in dengue treatment.

articles.title: Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft observations.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
