articles.abstract: Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is linked to Mars' extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar wind, this finding bears on solar-wind interactions at comets and other small bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind-planet coupling at unmagnetized worlds.

articles.title: Norovirus outbreaks: maintaining infection prevention standards in community nursing.
articles.abstract: This article explores the evolving evidence surrounding norovirus outbreaks, considers lessons learned since the COVID-19 pandemic and discusses practical implications for community nursing practice in light of current UK guidance and infection prevention standards.

articles.title: Reducing diabetes care costs and district nurse visits through novel insulin regimens.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An increasingly frail and ageing population has resulted in an unsustainable demand on district nurse teams in terms of insulin administration.

AIMS: This quality improvement initiative aimed to reduce district nursing team visits by adjusting the insulin regimens of people with type 2 diabetes from twice to once daily, where possible.

METHODS: The integrated community care team audited all people receiving district nursing visits for insulin administration. Community diabetes specialist nurses provided personalised insulin adjustment guides. HbA1c levels before and after the intervention were assessed over a 3-year follow-up period.

FINDINGS: Twice daily visits were reduced by 77%. Mean HbA1c significantly decreased by 16.3 mmol/mol (1.5%) (from 94.9 [10.8%] to 78.6 [9.3%]) at 12 months. The mortality rate was 30%, and median follow up was 18 months.

CONCLUSIONS: This innovative way of working and change of insulin regimens lessened the burden of insulin administration on district nursing teams, while improving glycaemia and yielding estimated savings of approximately £839 500 annually.

articles.title: Dissecting diastolic stiffness.
articles.abstract: JGP study (Shahid et al. https://doi.org/10.1085/jgp.202614028) reveals sex-based differences in the contributors to diastolic stress in cardiomyocytes from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction model mice.

articles.title: Highly neutralizing anti-IFN-ω autoantibodies underlie severe pediatric adenovirus infection.
articles.abstract: Neutralizing autoantibodies (auto-Abs) against type I IFNs (IFN-α and IFN-ω) have emerged as major acquired risk factors for severe viral infections. Human adenovirus (HAdV) is highly prevalent in children and can cause severe pneumonia, but the host determinants of disease severity remain poorly understood. We describe here a 5-year-old child with life-threatening HAdV-B7 pneumonia requiring intensive care who carried high-titer anti-IFN-ω auto-Abs of the IgG1 and IgG3 subclasses. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells produced normal amounts of IFN-α and IFN-ω ex vivo; however, IFN-ω was undetectable in the plasma during acute illness. Functional assays demonstrated that the patient's plasma strongly neutralized IFN-ω, abolishing its antiviral signaling and protective effects, resulting in high levels of adenovirus replication and virus-induced cytotoxicity. These findings implicate anti-IFN-ω auto-Abs in severe adenoviral infection and support immunological screening of pediatric patients with unexplained severe viral pneumonia, which may guide targeted management.

articles.title: IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency: Clinical features and transplant outcomes.
articles.abstract: IRF4 is a transcription factor within the interferon regulatory factor family that controls key aspects of lymphocyte differentiation and adaptive immunity. The heterozygous IRF4 p.Thr95Arg (p.T95R) variant affecting the DNA-binding domain was recently identified to cause a new inborn error of immunity, but the longitudinal clinical course and therapeutic implications remain incompletely defined. We performed detailed clinical characterization and follow-up of all 10 known patients. Each presented with early-onset combined immunodeficiency characterized by hypo- or agammaglobulinemia and marked susceptibility to opportunistic infections. Pulmonary disease was universal, and gastrointestinal involvement was associated with a more severe clinical course. Four patients underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation; two survived, and two died. Notably, both deaths occurred in patients transplanted in the setting of active infection. These findings define IRF4 p.T95R as a profound combined immunodeficiency with high infectious burden and demonstrate that disease severity and intervention timing may contribute to transplant outcomes, supporting early diagnosis and timely transplantation before uncontrolled infection.

articles.title: Lipid remodeling enables adaptation to chronic hyperosmotic stress.
articles.abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) accumulate in response to diverse cellular stresses. However, their regulation and physiological roles remain poorly understood in most contexts. Here, we show that in budding yeast, chronic hyperosmotic stress induces sustained LD accumulation. Unlike the transient LD response observed during acute osmotic shock, chronic stress triggers prolonged, Dga1-dependent triacylglycerol synthesis. In the absence of triacylglycerol synthesis, cellular fitness is impaired. Lipidomic profiling reveals extensive membrane remodeling during chronic hyperosmotic stress, most notably an increase in phosphatidylcholine (PC) resulting in changes to membrane properties. In LD-deficient cells, the hyperosmotic stress-induced PC increase is blunted, while enhancing PC synthesis improves the fitness of triacylglycerol-deficient cells. Thus, LD accumulation and phospholipid remodeling underlie an adaptive response to chronic hyperosmotic stress.

articles.title: The IKKε-GABPA axis regulates STING transcription to orchestrate antiviral immunity and inflammation.
articles.abstract: The cGAS-STING pathway plays a critical role in antiviral defense and inflammatory homeostasis. While posttranslational regulation of STING is well characterized, the transcriptional networks directly governing Sting1 expression remain unclear. Here, we identify the transcription factor GA-binding protein alpha (GABPA) as a critical regulator of STING-dependent type I IFN (IFN-I) responses in macrophages. Mechanistically, GABPA directly binds to the Sting1 promoter, thereby transcriptionally sustaining basal STING expression. Upon viral infection, activated IκB kinase epsilon (IKKε) phosphorylates GABPA at S447, which further enhances its transcriptional activity and amplifies the STING-IFN-I signaling cascade. Notably, Gabpa deficiency protects mice from DSS-induced colitis, and this protective effect is abolished upon Sting1 deletion. Strikingly, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) exhibit elevated GABPA expression that positively correlates with STING hyperactivation and enhanced inflammatory signatures. Moreover, a GABPA-blocking peptide effectively suppresses aberrant IFN-β production in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from SLE patients, highlighting its therapeutic potential for interferonopathies.

articles.title: State-dependent inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels by DCPIB.
articles.abstract: DCPIB is the prototypical inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat containing protein 8 volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), yet the structural basis and state dependence of inhibition remain unclear. Here, we used chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to define the determinants of DCPIB inhibition and elucidate how drug binding is coupled to channel gating. Effective inhibition required coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 (EL1) and transmembrane domain 2 (TM2), which together form a functional module governing access to and stabilization of DCPIB-bound states. Within TM2, a single hydrophobic residue strongly influenced inhibition, indicating that subtle differences in helix packing shape drug sensitivity. Using the homo-heptameric 8C-8A(IL125) channel as a defined model, we found that DCPIB acts exclusively from the extracellular side, inhibits cooperatively, and enhances voltage-dependent inactivation. Mutational analysis showed that DCPIB interacts permissively with R103 of the outer constriction site (OCS) but does not depend on it for inhibition, suggesting that the inhibitor intercalates between subunits within a hydrophobic cleft to achieve stable pore engagement. Charged substitutions within TM2 provided functional evidence that DCPIB penetrates beyond the OCS. Mutations at positions implicated in lipid interactions markedly altered DCPIB efficacy without affecting volume sensitivity, indicating that productive drug-channel interactions, rather than lipid gating itself, are required for inhibition. Finally, charge neutralization on the conserved N-terminal constriction enhanced DCPIB sensitivity, supporting long-range coupling within the pore. Together, these results establish DCPIB as a state-dependent VRAC inhibitor that stabilizes an inactivated channel conformation and define mechanistic principles for the rational design of more potent and selective VRAC inhibitors.

articles.title: Human inborn errors of the phagocyte respiratory burst: Chronic granulomatous disease and beyond.
articles.abstract: The phagocyte respiratory burst is an effector mechanism of immunity by which granulocytes, monocytes, and other myeloid cells generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). Inborn errors of core phagocyte NADPH oxidase components (gp91phox, p22phox, p47phox, and p67phox) underlie most cases of chronic granulomatous disease, characterized by severe, recurrent bacterial and fungal infections. An expanding spectrum of inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) has been identified that affect molecules that trigger (IFN-γ, TNF, and their signaling pathways) or control NADPH oxidase assembly and activation (EROS, p40phox, PKCδ, RAC2, and DOCK2), thereby impairing ROS production. Studies of these genetic disorders, which include infection, autoinflammation, and autoimmunity, have identified crucial pathways governing the induction, regulation, assembly, priming, activation, and function of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex. We review here the diverse IEIs affecting phagocyte ROS production, highlighting disorders in which ROS generation is absent, reduced, or subset-specific, and the corresponding cellular, immunological, and clinical phenotypes.

articles.title: High prevalence of autoantibodies neutralizing type I IFNs in Japanese patients with hepatitis C.
articles.abstract: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I IFNs (AAN-I-IFNs) are being identified as major, common, and global determinants of a growing range of severe viral diseases. We examined whether persistent hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, with or without IFN-α therapy, could induce AAN-I-IFNs. We tested 2,573 HCV patients aged 1-95 years (1,115 treated with IFN-α, 1,458 untreated) and 1,000 healthy controls. AAN-INF-α2 prevalence was significantly higher in hepatitis C patients (2.7%) than in healthy controls (0.7%) and was higher still in those treated with IFN-α (3.9%) than in untreated patients (1.9%) (P = 0.0053). A longitudinal study of 15 IFN-α-treated patients with AAN-IFN-α2 revealed that only one had AAN-IFN-α2 before IFN-α therapy and that 12 patients developed AAN-IFN-α2 in the year following treatment. However, 80% eventually became AAN-IFN-α2 negative. These findings suggest that chronic HCV infection, perhaps due to the chronic production of endogenous IFN-α, and exogenous IFN-α treatment promote the development of AAN-IFN-α2.

articles.title: Upper respiratory tract CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells protect against viral transmission.
articles.abstract: Intranasal vaccination elicits CD8 tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) throughout the respiratory tract that provide cross-protection against heterosubtypic viral strains and reduce immunopathology. We previously demonstrated that CD8 TRM can reduce the probability of respiratory virus transmission and the magnitude of infection, using a murine model of parainfluenza virus transmission. Here, we show that CD8 TRM-mediated protection occurs independently of circulating leukocytes, B cells, or CD4 T cells. Additionally, we investigate the contributions of CD8 TRM in different respiratory tract compartments and illustrate that CD8 TRM in the upper respiratory tract (URT), but not the lower respiratory tract (LRT), become activated and proliferate in response to transmitted virus. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CD8 TRM in the URT alone provide sufficient immune surveillance to prevent propagation of infection after viral transmission. These findings offer insights into the development of T cell-based respiratory virus vaccines and shed light on the critical role of URT CD8 TRM in the prevention of viral transmission.

articles.title: The proximal N terminus of IRAG is required for potentiation of HCN4 channels.
articles.abstract: The inositol triphosphate-associated, ER transmembrane proteins inositol triphosphate receptor-associated guanylate kinase substrate (IRAG) and lymphoid restricted membrane protein (LRMP) are isoform-specific regulators of the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-sensitive isoform 4 (HCN4) channel. LRMP prevents cAMP-dependent potentiation of HCN4, while IRAG mimics the effect of cAMP on the channel. We previously showed that regulation by LRMP requires both the N terminus of HCN4 as well as a unique set of residues in the cAMP transduction center of HCN4, which is comprised of the N-terminal HCN domain (HCND), the C-linker, and the S4-S5 linker. However, it remains unknown if the homologous IRAG requires similar structural features to mimic cAMP-dependent potentiation, or if the site and mechanism of action are different between the two regulators. Using patch-clamp electrophysiology, we determined that the initial 43 amino acids of IRAG are necessary and sufficient to confer regulation of HCN4. Similar to LRMP, IRAG also requires a portion of the N terminus of HCN4 to confer its regulatory effects. Also like LRMP, two point mutations in the C-linker region, near where the C-linker of one subunit contacts its neighboring subunit, were able to eliminate the effect of IRAG. Taken together, these findings suggest a model whereby IRAG and LRMP make complex interactions with a number of intracellular domains of HCN4. For both proteins, regulation of HCN4 requires a portion of the N terminus and at least some portions of the structural domains required to convert the binding of cAMP to the cyclic nucleotide-binding domain (CNBD) to a change in channel gating.

articles.title: Prevalence of neutralizing autoantibodies against type I interferon in dengue patients.
articles.abstract: The presence of neutralizing autoantibodies (NAbs) against type I IFN (IFN-I) has been associated with severe complications arising from various viral infections. However, the prevalence of IFN-I NAbs in dengue virus (DENV) infection remains unclear. Here, we enrolled 216 hospitalized dengue patients in 2024, including 7 individuals with dengue shock syndrome (DSS) and 42 individuals with dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Utilizing a sensitive luciferase reporter assay, IFN-I NAbs were detected in 7 patients (14.3% of DSS/DHF cases), and their neutralizing ability was further validated in DENV-infected cells. Notably, all NAb-positive patients exhibited plasma leakage tendency and cardiac injury and were significantly older than the overall cohort (75.34 vs. 50.75, P = 0.010). IFN-I NAbs were correlated with clinical parameters of myocardial injury and plasma leakage, with increased odds ratio (OR) for cardiac injury (OR = 22.8, P = 0.003) and hypoproteinemia (OR = 53.5, P = 0.001). These findings suggest that IFN-I NAbs may contribute to severe clinical manifestations of dengue, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Temporal windowing of recurrent sinusitis improves EHR-based immunodeficiency classification.
articles.abstract: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections are a hallmark of common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), yet electronic health records (EHR) struggle to distinguish multiple discrete infections from a single infection comprising multiple clinic visits. Using diagnosis codes and antibiotic prescriptions, we developed a temporal windowing methodology that groups related sinusitis encounters into episodes based on timing and antibiotic escalation patterns. We applied this approach to 79 CVID patients, 224 rituximab-treated patients with hypogammaglobulinemia, and 2,994 matched controls. Immunodeficient patients had more frequent sinusitis episodes and greater episode burden than controls. Windowed episode features, when combined with infection PheCodes, yielded the best-performing Ridge regression classifiers in both the CVID-only (AUC-ROC 0.787) and pooled CVID/RTX (AUC-ROC 0.724) models, outperforming PheCodes combined with simple encounter counts and PheCodes alone. In a held-out cohort of five patients with pre-diagnosis sinusitis data, the classifier correctly flagged 4 of 5 as high-risk. Quantifying recurrence and refractoriness of infections through temporal windowing improves EHR-based phenotyping of immunodeficiency.

articles.title: Ureaplasma parvum septic arthritis in LRBA deficiency: An infectious mimic of autoimmune arthritis.
articles.abstract: We report Ureaplasma parvum septic arthritis in lipopolysaccharide-responsive and beige-like anchor protein deficiency during rituximab-based chemotherapy for relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma. This case highlights culture-negative infection mimicking autoimmune arthritis and supports early 16S ribosomal RNA PCR in immunocompromised patients with a primary immune regulatory disorder.

articles.title: STAT1 gain-of-function variant in a previously healthy patient with disseminated Mycobacterium genavense infection.
articles.abstract: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) defects present with diverse clinical phenotypes. We describe an unusual genotype/phenotype: disseminated mycobacterial infection without chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis in the context of a pathogenic STAT1 gain-of-function variant (p.Lys388Glu). To our knowledge, this is the first report of such a case.

articles.title: Diastolic contributors in cardiomyocytes of a cardiometabolic HFpEF-like mouse model.
articles.abstract: Three main contributors to cardiomyocyte diastolic stiffness are (1) passive sarcomere stiffness, (2) microtubules, and (3) diastolic crossbridges (XBs), the XBs that are present in the diastolic phase. However, the relative contributions of these key determinants in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) conditions are unclear. We quantify the relative contributions of passive sarcomere stress, the microtubule network, and diastolic XB activity to overall diastolic stress in intact cardiomyocytes isolated from two-hit mice, a cardiometabolic HFpEF-like model, in both sexes. The stretch-release protocol was used to obtain the diastolic stress-sarcomere length relation. XB inhibitor and colchicine treatment were used to determine the contributions of diastolic XBs and microtubules, respectively. Passive sarcomere stress was measured in cells treated with both colchicine and the XB inhibitor. Male HFpEF-like cardiomyocytes exhibit increases in both passive sarcomere stress (by 70%) and diastolic XBs (by 52%), whereas female HFpEF-like cardiomyocytes show an increase in passive sarcomere stress alone (by 55%). The microtubule network contributes to diastolic stress by augmenting the extent of diastolic XBs in males. The elevated diastolic XBs in male HFpEF-like mice are accompanied by altered Ca2+ transient, suggesting that remodeled Ca2+ handling accounts, in part, for the enhanced diastolic XB activity in males. These findings imply that, in males, both increased passive sarcomere stiffness and diastolic XB activity represent potential therapeutic targets for reducing cardiomyocyte diastolic stiffness, whereas in females, diastolic stiffness is predominantly driven by elevated passive sarcomere stiffness.

articles.title: A meta-analysis and systematic review of Salmonella prevalence in table eggs from China and the efficacy of inactivation technologies for Salmonella in table eggs.
articles.abstract: Salmonella contamination of table eggs poses a significant public health risk in China. However, systematic assessments of the national prevalence and comparative efficacy of inactivation technologies remain limited. We systematically searched the PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and Wan Fang databases from 1990 to 2025. Studies reporting Salmonella prevalence in Chinese table eggs or log reduction values of inactivation technologies were included. The total of 7472 records were identified. The total of 73 prevalence and 91 inactivation studies were finally analyzed. The risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists, and random-effects models were used to pool estimates, with subgroup analyses and meta-regression to explore heterogeneity. The prevalence of Salmonella in Chinese table eggs varies significantly across production stages. The farm stage showed a high contamination rate (10.03%, 95% CI: 5.87-16.61%), whereas the sale and consumption stage had a lower rate (1.00%, 95% CI: 0.52-1.94%). Eggs from open-style farms had a high rate of 18.92% (95% CI: 5.87-16.61%). Regarding inactivation, pasteurization consistently achieved >5 log CFU/g reduction across all liquid egg products. Electrolyzed water was the most effective on eggshell surfaces (4.71 log CFU/g, 95% CI: 4.54-4.87). Radiofrequency combined with water also achieved strong inactivation on shelled eggs (4.92 log CFU/g, 95% CI: 3.94-5.91). Taken together, these findings highlight priority areas for intervention and provide a quantitative benchmark for technology selection. Control efforts should target farm-stage contamination, particularly in northern regions and on small open farms. While established technologies such as pasteurization and radiofrequency remain reliable for inactivation, emerging methods, including electrolyzed water, offer promising alternatives. Future research should focus on optimizing combined technologies to balance microbial safety with egg quality preservation and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Social and clinical determinants of liver transplant evaluation in hepatocellular carcinoma: A multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation (LT) is curative for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but requires timely referral. Comprehensive data on factors impacting LT referral and outcomes for HCC are limited. We evaluated social, system, and clinical factors associated with listing, LT, mortality, HCC stage at referral, and time from HCC diagnosis to referral.

METHODS: The California Liver Network is a consortium of 6 LT centers comprising >75% of adult LTs in California. Demographic, clinical, psychosocial, and social determinants of health and outcome data were collected for adults referred for LT. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 9987 adults referred, 1573 (15.7%) had HCC. Median age was 63.3 years; 73% males, 40% Hispanic, and 26.1% Medicaid insurance. Median MELD was 12.7 (IQR 8-16), and median time from HCC diagnosis to LT referral was 124 days (IQR 32-410). In all, 10% were T1 and 70.5% were T2 at referral. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (OR 0.99), HCC stage, Medicaid insurance (OR 0.55), LT site, and marital status (OR 1.90) were associated with listing. Transplantation was associated with HCC stage (OR 0.42) and LT site. Mortality was associated with MELD (OR 1.02), hypertension (OR 1.44), dialysis (OR 2.48), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 1.54), and portal vein thrombosis (OR 1.44). Referral at more advanced HCC stage was associated with male sex (OR 1.55), AFP (OR 1.01), Medicaid insurance (OR 1.40), primary language (OR 0.70), and prior HCC treatment type. Longer time to referral was associated with HCV/alcohol liver disease and prior HCC treatment type.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter study of adults with HCC, Medicaid insurance, LT site, HCC treatment history, and psychosocial factors were key determinants of HCC care cascade progression, identifying targets to improve LT access.

articles.title: Adaptive immune plasticity in MASH: Functional states, pathological consequences, and regulatory mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by both metabolic stress and immune dysregulation. A growing body of evidence suggests that adaptive immune cells exhibit significant functional plasticity during the progression and resolution of MASH. CD8+ T cells can assume various states, including pathogenic cytotoxicity, functional exhaustion, and tissue repair; CD4+ T cells exhibit enhanced Th1/Th17 programming, reduced Treg stability, and a functional shift toward Th17/Treg; and B cells undergo remodeling between regulatory, pro-inflammatory, and antibody-effect states. These functional states determine disease outcomes through distinct effector mechanisms. The cytotoxicity and inflammatory factors of pathogenic T cells promote hepatocyte damage, metabolic dysregulation, and hepatocyte stellate cell activation, while B-cell antigen presentation, cytokine, and antibody responses further amplify inflammation and fibrosis; conversely, Tregs, Bregs, and tissue-resident CD8+ T cells with reparative functions can limit inflammation or promote the resolution of fibrosis. Adaptive immune plasticity is, in turn, continuously shaped by the hepatic metabolic environment, in which glycolipid and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming determine the metabolic basis of different functional states, while metabolite-driven epigenetic remodeling stabilizes corresponding transcriptional programs. Microbiome components and metabolic signals originating from the gut-liver axis further regulate the state of T and B cells within the liver. Consequently, the functional states of adaptive immune cells, their pathological effects, and their metabolic regulation collectively constitute a critical immunometabolic network linking metabolic dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and the progression of fibrosis, providing a unified mechanistic framework for understanding the sustained progression of MASH and tissue repair.

articles.title: Rapid assessment of diabetes mellitus and diabetic retinopathy in the rural-tribal population of Tapi district of western India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The present study assessed the prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and diabetic retinopathy (DR) in a rural-tribal population in western India.

METHODS: The standard RAAB (Rapid Assessment of Avoidable Blindness) methodology with DR module was used in this survey. A total of 139 clusters of 60 people each aged ≥50 years were selected by cluster random sampling with probability proportionate to size. The participants were classified as having DM if they were known to have DM or if their random blood glucose (RBG) level was ≥200 mg/dL, detected by the test offered at the doorstep. Dilated retinal examination and Scottish DR grading were performed for all diabetics.

RESULTS: In total, 7835 (93.9%) out of 8344 eligible participants were examined. The prevalence of DM (381/7835) was 4.9% (95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-5.6). Of these, 68.5% (261/381) were known diabetics and 31.5% (120/381) were identified by spot RBG test. Fifty-five per cent (n = 144/261) of known diabetics had RBG ≥200 mg/dL. The prevalence of any DR, any maculopathy, and sight-threatening DR was 16.3% (95% CI: 12.5 to 20.1), 9.2% (95% CI: 6.2 to 12.2), and 2.1% (95% CI: 0.7 to 3.5), respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of DM and DR in the rural tribal population was lower than the national average but is emerging. More than half of the diabetics had uncontrolled DM, which needs improved awareness and accessibility to health care services for this underprivileged population. Further studies are needed to establish predictors and causal relationship between prevalence of DM/DR in the rural-tribal population.

articles.title: Ethnolinguistic differences in diabetic retinopathy within a shared geographic setting in South India: The Gudalur diabetic retinopathy study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence and severity between Tamil- and Malayalam-speaking adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) living within a shared geographic setting and to examine differences in clinical, behavioral, and dietary characteristics.

DESIGN: Community-based cross-sectional screening study.

METHODS: Adults aged ≥40 years with self-reported T2DM, ≥10 years' residence in Gudalur taluk (Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu), and mother tongue Tamil or Malayalam were recruited through 12 outreach eye camps conducted between January and December 2024. Participants underwent dilated fundus examinations by indirect ophthalmoscopy. Sociodemographic and socioeconomic characteristics, anthropometry, diabetes duration, physical activity, knowledge and screening practices, and dietary intake were assessed using standardized instruments. Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate tests, and logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between mother tongue and any DR.

RESULTS: Among 295 participants (Malayalam n = 171; Tamil n = 124), Malayalam speakers were older ( P = 0.008) and had longer diabetes duration ( P < 0.001), while HbA1c was comparable. DR was more prevalent among Malayalam speakers (49.7% vs 30.6%; P = 0.002). Malayalam mother tongue remained associated with any DR after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.88; 95% CI 1.10-3.22; P = 0.021). Awareness and annual eye examination uptake were higher among Malayalam speakers, who also had higher total energy intake and a greater contribution of saturated fat in the dietary subset ( P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Within a shared geographic setting, Malayalam-speaking adults with T2DM had higher DR prevalence and severity than Tamil-speaking adults, after adjustment for age and diabetes duration, alongside differences in awareness and dietary fat patterns.

articles.title: Toward a comparative endocrinology of aging: insights from insects.
articles.abstract: Insulin-like signaling modulates aging and lifespan in insects. Here, we discuss a novel view of this control: insulin hormone in the adult regulates the production of the sesquiterpenoid juvenile hormone (JH) that in turn acts as the systemic regulator of aging and lifespan. Work in Drosophila establishes that insulin signaling is allatotropic - it stimulates the production and secretion of JH from the corpora allata. JH then exerts systemic effects on adult survival through its control of specific proteins, translation and proteostasis. The interdependent functions of insulin and JH allow reproduction and longevity to be coupled in many insects or decoupled in social insects with long-lived queens and in some long-lived genetic mutants of Drosophila. Features of these insulin-regulated life history syndromes are also found in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. Recognizing the systemic role of JH in aging provides grounds to search for analogous systems in mammals that might modulate human lifespan.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The expected clinical and functional trajectory after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with left ventricular dysfunction remains uncertain. Recent trials have highlighted substantial heterogeneity in both clinical outcomes and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement, underscoring the need for improved post-PCI prognostic risk stratification in this high-risk population. This study aimed to develop machine learning models predicting clinical outcomes and LVEF improvement after PCI in patients with reduced LVEF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective single-centre study included adults undergoing PCI between 2004 and 2025 with baseline LVEF <45%. Two CatBoost models were developed using 53 routinely available pre- and intra-procedural predictors. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of death, myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or coronary artery bypass grafting. The secondary endpoint was an absolute LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and enrichment analysis. The dataset included 3336 procedures from 2793 patients (median LVEF 35%). For the primary endpoint (n = 2152; event rate 37.5%), the model achieved an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83) and a PR-AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.63-0.77), with event rates of 83.7% in the highest-risk decile and 9.3% in the lowest-risk decile. For LVEF improvement (n = 2551; 34.7% improved), performance was moderate (AUC 0.73), with enrichment to 76.9% in the highest-probability decile.

CONCLUSION: Machine learning models using routinely available patient and procedural data enabled meaningful prognostic stratification in patients with left ventricular dysfunction undergoing PCI, supporting individualized estimation of clinical and functional trajectories after revascularization.

articles.title: Rapid Progression of Acute Acalculous Cholecystitis to Gangrenous Cholecystitis in an Initially Non-Critically Ill Patient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Acute acalculous cholecystitis (AAC) is not confined to the critically ill and may behave like calculous disease. A 65-year-old hypertensive man with localized, stone-free cholecystitis deteriorated on hospital Day 4 with peritonism, acidosis, and acute kidney injury. Emergency open cholecystectomy confirmed gangrene; deterioration warrants urgent source control.

articles.title: Knowledge of Nipah Virus and Associated Factors Among Rural Population in Bangladesh: Evidence From a Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic threat and posing serious public health risks in Bangladesh due to its high fatality rate, high transmissibility, and the lack of particular licensed vaccinations.

METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out among 415 adult rural respondents. Data were collected using a paper-based structured questionnaire consisting of respondents' sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge-related questions regarding NiV. Participants' sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge level were summarized using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. The statistical significance level was set at p < 0.05, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 37.56 ± 14.63 years, and 66.5% were male. Although 71.1% of participants had heard of the NiV, only 16.4% demonstrated good knowledge (≥ 65% of total score). The mean knowledge score was 7.99 ± 3.86. Knowledge was particularly limited regarding routes of transmission, including person-to-person transmission, clinical manifestations, treatment availability, and the ineffectiveness of antibiotics. In the adjusted analysis, participants aged 25-34 years (AOR = 2.85, 95% CI: 1.13-7.63), females (AOR = 2.73, 95% CI: 1.09-7.09), and those with graduation or higher education (AOR = 10.70, 95% CI: 2.10-67.70) were significantly more likely to have good knowledge. Conversely, participants who consumed fresh date palm sap had significantly lower odds of good knowledge (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.17-0.68).

CONCLUSION: The rural respondents in this study area demonstrated inadequate awareness of the NiV. Participants' understanding of disease symptoms, treatment limitations, disease transmission, and prophylactic measures was remarkably poor. To prevent NiV transmission and outbreaks in Bangladesh, these findings highlight the significance of targeted, culturally appropriate, and community-based health education programs that focus on safe date palm sap consumption, early symptom recognition, and other effective preventive measures.

articles.title: Integration of Aromatherapy and Essential Oils in Asthma Symptom Relief: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Asthma affects 262 million people globally, causing 455,000 preventable deaths, with higher mortality in low-resource areas due to limited diagnosis and treatment. Aromatherapy, using bioactive essential oils (EOs), has emerged as a promising complementary approach for asthma symptom management.

METHODS: This review synthesizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of EOs in alleviating asthma-related inflammation, bronchoconstriction, and immune dysregulation through anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and immunomodulatory mechanisms.

RESULTS: Key oils such as lavender, eucalyptus, and peppermint demonstrate efficacy in reducing airway hyperresponsiveness, oxidative stress, and Th2-mediated inflammation, supported by preclinical and clinical studies. Methods of application, including inhalation, topical use, and environmental diffusion, are evaluated for their physiological and psychological benefits, particularly in stress and sleep modulation, which are critical to asthma control. Safety considerations, such as allergenicity, proper dosing, and potential drug interactions, are emphasized to ensure safe integration with conventional therapies.

CONCLUSION: Despite the promising findings, further large-scale clinical trials are needed to validate the efficacy, optimize protocols, and explore personalized approaches based on genetic and phenotypic variability. This review underscores aromatherapy's role as an adjunctive therapy within a holistic asthma management framework, bridging traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific validation to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: The Moderating Role of Social Support in the Relationship Between Diabetes Distress and Psychological Well-Being Among Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study Protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Type 2 diabetes imposes a considerable psychological burden on older adults, including elevated diabetes distress and diminished psychological well-being. Social support may buffer the harmful mental-health effects of chronic disease-related stress, yet whether it moderates the link between diabetes distress and psychological well-being remains rarely examined among older Iranian adults with type 2 diabetes. This protocol aims to determine the moderating role of social support in that relationship in this population.

METHODS: This descriptive-analytic cross-sectional protocol will recruit 300 adults aged 60 years or above with type 2 diabetes from the Bandar Abbas Diabetes Clinic through simple random sampling from the clinic electronic registry. Trained interviewers will administer a demographic and clinical form, the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, the PAID-5 (diabetes distress), the MSSS-5 (social support), and the WHO-5 Well-Being Index in person or by telephone using identical structured interviews. Hierarchical multiple regression will test the diabetes distress by social support interaction on WHO-5 scores, in an unadjusted model and a model adjusted for a pre-specified demographic and clinical covariate set, with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors, bootstrapped confidence intervals, and simple-slopes and Johnson-Neyman probing. Missing data will be handled with multiple imputation. Analyses will use IBM SPSS Statistics version 28 with two-sided tests at α = 0.05.

RESULTS: As a protocol, no empirical results are reported. The completed study will yield estimates of diabetes distress, social support, and psychological well-being levels, their bivariate associations, and the moderation effect with appropriate uncertainty quantification.

CONCLUSION: The findings are expected to provide a scientific basis for nursing and psychosocial interventions that strengthen social support networks to protect the psychological well-being of older adults with type 2 diabetes. Ethical approval has been obtained (IR.HUMS.REC.1405.013); written or audio-recorded verbal informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infection with Entamoeba histolytica in children can seriously affect individual and public health. Moreover, the prevalence of this disease varies significantly across different regions of the world, and comprehensive and accurate data on its global prevalence among children are lacking. The present study aims to determine the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children.

METHODS: This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing evidence on the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children, conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 statement criteria. The search was conducted using the (AND) and (OR) operators, and the retrieved data were transferred to the EndNote reference management software. The quality assessment of the studies included in the study was conducted based on the STROBE checklist, considering the nature of the cross-sectional studies included in the study. I2 index was used to evaluate heterogeneity. Funnel Plot and Begg and mazumdar correlation test were used to evaluate the publication bias. Data were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis software (Version 2).

RESULTS: A total of 119 studies with a sample size of 70,259 children were included. The I 2 heterogeneity test indicated high heterogeneity (I 2: 97.7%); therefore, a random-effects model was used for data analysis. Based on the meta-analysis, the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children was reported as 8.4% (95% CI: 7.1-10). However, given the results of the publication bias test, the results should be considered with caution, and it is also stated that the geographically heterogeneous distribution of the studies is also a limitation of this study. the pooled prevalence estimate should be interpreted with caution despite the subgroup and meta-regression analyses performed.

CONCLUSION: According to the results of the meta-analysis, the global prevalence of Entamoeba histolytica in children was reported as 8.4%; therefore, although the final prevalence is relatively high, it should be investigated and considered in light of the transmissibility of this disease in children and its impact.

articles.title: Time to Discontinuation and Risk Factors for Outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy in Primary Care: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Survival Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) provided by registered dietitians is effective for managing non-communicable diseases, but patient discontinuation remains common in clinical practice. Studies examining the timing and predictors of MNT discontinuation are limited. This study aimed to identify the timing and patient factors associated with MNT discontinuation in primary care settings.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who initiated outpatient MNT at a primary care clinic between April 2018 and March 2023. Patients aged < 18 years and those with cancer- or malnutrition-related conditions were excluded. Discontinuation was defined as no MNT visit or scheduled appointment within 3 months after the last visit. Patients were followed for up to 24 months through March 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated continuation rates, and multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models identified factors associated with discontinuation. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 470 patients (median age, 63 years; 59.4% women), 241 (51.3%) discontinued MNT during follow-up. Median time to discontinuation was 15 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12-21). Continuation rates were 88.3% at 3 months, 70.4% at 6 months, and 43.5% at 24 months. Obesity, dyslipidemia, and medication use were associated with lower discontinuation risk, whereas complications, living with family, and preparation stage of behavior change were associated with higher risk. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results.

CONCLUSIONS: MNT continuation declined rapidly within 6 months. Multiple patient factors were associated with discontinuation risk, suggesting the need for early risk identification and individualized support strategies.

articles.title: Association of the ADAMTS14 rs4747096 Polymorphism and C-Reactive Protein Levels With Knee Osteoarthritis Severity: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The rs4747096 polymorphism in the ADAMTS14 gene and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels have been associated with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) severity; however, evidence from Vietnam remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of rs4747096 genotypes, assess CRP levels, and examine their associations with KOA severity.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 120 patients with KOA treated at Tien Giang General Hospital from July to December 2025. rs4747096 genotyping and serum CRP measurement were performed, and radiographic severity was graded using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) classification. Severe KOA was defined as KL grade ≥III.

RESULTS: The mean age was 51.98 ± 10.24 years. KL grades II, III, and IV were observed in 66/120 (55.0%), 37/120 (30.8%), and 17/120 (14.2%) patients, respectively. KL grade distribution differed significantly by CRP category (p = 0.008), with grade IV disease more frequent in patients with CRP > 8.0 mg/L than in those with CRP ≤ 8.0 mg/L [12/49 (24.5%) vs. 5/71 (7.0%)]. Genotype frequencies were 41/120 (34.2%) for AA, 52/120 (43.3%) for AG, and 27/120 (22.5%) for GG. In univariable analysis, AG + GG genotypes (OR = 2.32; 95% CI, 1.05-5.13; p = 0.035) and CRP > 8.0 mg/L (OR = 2.67; 95% CI, 1.26-5.64; p = 0.009) were associated with severe KOA. In multivariable analysis, age ≥ 60 years (aOR = 4.59; 95% CI, 1.52-13.90; p = 0.007), overweight or obesity (aOR = 4.86; 95% CI, 1.96-12.06; p < 0.001), dyslipidemia (aOR = 2.81; 95% CI, 1.02-7.76; p = 0.047), and CRP > 8.0 mg/L (aOR = 3.43; 95% CI, 1.24-9.53; p = 0.018) remained independently associated with severe KOA, whereas rs4747096 did not.

CONCLUSION: Elevated CRP was independently associated with severe KOA, whereas the association with rs4747096 was attenuated after adjustment. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the independent role of this polymorphism.

articles.title: Therapeutic Potential of [(AP)2M]: A Rationally Designed Polyherbal Formulation for Antidiabetic and Antihyperlipidemic Effects in Alloxan-Induced Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants are widely used in diabetes management due to their multi-targeted bioactive constituents. Phyllanthus emblica, Piper nigrum, Aegle marmelos, Moringa oleifera, and Azadirachta indica possess well-documented antidiabetic properties, providing a scientific basis for developing a rationally designed polyherbal formulation. This study evaluated the basic phytochemical characterization, antioxidant, antidiabetic, antihyperlipidemic, and preliminary toxicity profiles of a polyherbal formulation (designated as [(AP)2M]) in an alloxan-induced type 1 diabetic mouse model. Polyphenolic (phenolic and flavonoid) contents, antioxidant activity (DPPH & metal-chelating assays), and α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities were determined. Acute oral toxicity was assessed according to OECD Guideline 423, with LD50 estimation to establish the preliminary toxicity profile and effective dosing. Diabetic mice received the formulation [(AP)2M] (30-120 mg/kg) orally for 3 weeks, after which blood glucose, the lipid profile, SGPT, SGOT, and histopathological changes in the liver, kidneys, and pancreas were evaluated. The formulation exhibited substantial phenolic (111.52 ± 0.444 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (211.30 ± 5.129 mg CAE/g) contents together with strong antioxidant and antidiabetic enzyme inhibitory activity. Acute oral toxicity assessment estimated an LD50 of 900 mg/kg (GHS Category 4). At 120 mg/kg, it reduced blood glucose to a level comparable with glibenclamide and significantly improved lipid profile, SGPT, and SGOT levels (p < 0.001). Histopathological examination demonstrated improvement in pancreatic, hepatic, and renal tissues. Since the formulation demonstrated promising antioxidant, antihyperglycemic, and antihyperlipidemic activities in a diabetic mouse model, it could be a potential alternative for further investigation as a complementary therapeutic approach for diabetes management.

articles.title: Baseline Clinical Predictors and Toxicological Drivers of In-Hospital Poisoning Mortality in Resource-Constrained Emergency Care: A Firth Penalized Regression Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding clinical characteristics and determinants of mortality among patients with acute poisoning in agricultural regions of Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate baseline clinical predictors associated with in-hospital mortality among acutely poisoned patients in a low-resource tertiary emergency department.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted among consecutive acute poisoning cases presenting to Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital (October 2022-September 2024). Of 372 screened cases, 7 patients who left against medical advice were excluded, yielding a final analytical cohort of 365 patients. Sociodemographic, toxicological, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was performed to minimize small-sample bias given sparse outcome events (15 deaths). A sensitivity model additionally adjusted for sex and rural residence.

RESULTS: The median age of patients was 22.0 years (IQR: 19.0-27.0); 230 (61.8%) were aged 15-24 years, 199 (53.5%) were female, and 245 (65.9%) were rural residents. Insecticides were the predominant poisoning category (157; 42.2%). Aluminum Phosphide (AlP) exposure occurred in 43 (11.6%) patients, resulting in 12 deaths (case-fatality rate: 27.9%; 95% CI 15.3%-43.7%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (15/365; 95% CI 2.3%-6.6%), with AlP accounting for 80.0% of all cohort deaths. In the primary multivariable Firth model, AlP exposure (aOR 30.48, 95% CI 7.88-117.95) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale < 15 (aOR 19.90, 95% CI 5.09-77.88) were strongly and independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired consciousness at admission (GCS < 15) and Aluminum Phosphide exposure serve as critical baseline indicators for rapid, low-cost risk stratification. While these exploratory parameters highlight high-risk groups, prospective multi-center validation across diverse hospital tiers is required before formal integration into clinical triage algorithms.

articles.title: Sepsis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, and Management.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality despite advances in recognition, antimicrobial therapy, and organ support, reflecting its biological heterogeneity and the absence of broadly effective host-directed treatments. Here, we synthesize recent evidence across the three domains that define contemporary sepsis: epidemiology, pathophysiology, and management. Global and regional data indicate a persistently high but uneven burden, shaped by differences in case definitions, population structure, healthcare resources, and ascertainment. Mechanistically, sepsis is best viewed as an interconnected systems disorder in which hyperinflammation and immunoparalysis coexist with oxidative stress, endothelial and coagulation injury, immunometabolic dysfunction, gut dysbiosis, mitochondrial damage, and dysregulated programmed cell death, collectively driving organ dysfunction. Current management remains centered on timely antimicrobials, source control, individualized fluid and vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, and organ support, while biomarker-guided immunotherapy and other host-directed strategies remain investigational. Recent randomized trials have mainly refined how established treatments are delivered rather than identified a universally effective new therapy. We also evaluate preclinical evidence for natural compounds targeting inflammatory and cell-death networks and highlight persistent methodological, pharmacokinetic, and translational barriers. Integrating rigorous phenotyping, mechanistic biomarkers, and guideline-based care may provide a more realistic path toward precision sepsis therapy.

articles.title: From Framework to Toolkit: Practical Guidance for Using the PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) framework was developed to support systematic evaluation of Context, Fidelity, Dose, Reach, and an integrative assessment of Quality of Delivery (QoD). Its practical use, however, requires explicit guidance on selecting measures, constructing QoD, assessing changing context, and governing prospective use.

METHODS: We undertook a retrospective comparative synthesis of process evaluations embedded in four randomized U.K. critical care trials: Biomarker-guided antibiotic stewardship in suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAPrapid-2), Provision of Psychological Support to People in Intensive Care (POPPI), Sedation AND Weaning In CHildren (SANDWICH), and Alpha-2 agonists for sedation to produce Better outcomes from critical illness (A2B). We selected them because they informed POETIC's development or application and provided sufficiently detailed quantitative and qualitative evidence. We mapped the reports, protocols, and process evaluation findings to the five dimensions; compared recurring and contradictory patterns, quantitative-qualitative agreement, measurement and interpretation problems, and mechanism-specific limitations; and translated our learning into guidance for applying the framework.

RESULTS: The relevance and measurement of POETIC dimensions varied according to how each intervention was expected to work. Contextual influences changed over time and differed between sites. Combined assessments of QoD required explicit decisions about component selection, weighting, thresholds, aggregation, and missing data. VAPrapid-2 showed why a separate Dose measure and a QoD composite were not meaningful for a one-off diagnostic recommendation; POPPI used a weighted site composite; SANDWICH summarized delivery of four intervention components, staff training, and patient Reach; and A2B combined four equally weighted indicators in a 0-12 site score. This cross-trial learning informed practical guidance on selecting measures, assessing context over time, integrating quantitative and qualitative findings, constructing QoD, and governing prospective use.

CONCLUSIONS: POETIC is best used as a mechanism-aligned, mixed-method scaffold rather than a requirement to measure every dimension or calculate a universal composite. Prospective use is feasible when outputs, recipients, review times, permitted actions, and safeguards are prespecified. The framework and accompanying toolkit support reproducible assessment while protecting trial integrity.

articles.title: Pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil versus pars plana vitrectomy alone for postoperative endophthalmitis: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The role of silicone oil (SO) tamponade in pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) for postoperative endophthalmitis remains controversial. This study compared outcomes of PPV with SO versus PPV alone in severe cases, incorporating intraocular cytokine profiling and regression analysis.

METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 40 eyes with post-phacoemulsification postoperative endophthalmitis unresponsive to initial intravitreal antibiotics were randomized to PPV alone (n = 20) or PPV with 1000-cSt SO tamponade (n = 20). The primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included recurrence of infection, retinal detachment (RD), and intraocular cytokine levels (interleukin [IL]-6, IL-8). Correlation and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of final visual outcome.

RESULTS: Final BCVA improved more in the SO group (1.5 ± 0.3 logMAR) compared with the PPV-alone group (1.7 ± 0.4 logMAR), although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.289). Recurrence was observed in two eyes (10%) within the SO cohort compared to eight eyes (40%) in the PPV-alone cohort (P = 0.021). At 8 weeks, intraocular cytokine levels were markedly reduced in the SO group (IL-6: 142 pg/mL vs. 298 pg/mL, P = 0.018; IL-8: 84 pg/mL vs. 176 pg/mL, P = 0.024). In the PPV-alone group, 8-week IL-6 levels strongly correlated with final BCVA (r = 0.712, P = 0.006). Multivariate regression identified recurrence of infection (β = 0.31, P = 0.009) and 8-week IL-6 levels (β = 0.001, P = 0.003) as independent predictors of worse visual outcomes.

CONCLUSION: PPV with SO tamponade significantly reduces recurrent infection and intraocular inflammation in severe postoperative endophthalmitis, leading to trends toward improved visual outcomes. These benefits appear mediated by both anti-infective and anti-inflammatory mechanisms, supporting the use of SO in complex cases.

articles.title: Measuring the impact of migraine: a systematic review of the measurement properties of MIDAS, HIT-6, and MSQoL.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migraine is a leading cause of global disability. Valid, reliable instruments are essential for quantifying its impact. The Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS), Headache Impact Test (HIT-6), and Migraine-Specific Quality-of-Life questionnaire (MSQoL) are widely used, yet their comparative measurement properties across populations remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and compare the measurement properties of MIDAS, HIT-6, and MSQoL following the Consensus-Based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) methodology.

METHODS: This systematic review followed the COSMIN guidelines for systematic reviews of outcome measurement instruments and was reported per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-COSMIN guideline. In total, seven databases were searched from study inception to January 31, 2025, restricted to English-language full-text studies. Methodological quality was appraised with the COSMIN Risk of Bias checklist; results were rated against criteria for good measurement properties, and evidence was graded using a modified Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: Of 2,674 records, 22 studies (20,455 participants) were included. All three instruments showed sufficient internal consistency and construct validity. The HIT-6 showed sufficient ratings across all properties (moderate-to-high quality evidence). Also, the MIDAS showed sufficient core properties but limited responsiveness and inconsistent reliability across cultural versions. Finally, MSQoL showed sufficient structural validity and internal consistency but insufficient test-retest reliability.

CONCLUSION: Both HIT-6 and MIDAS can be recommended for measuring migraine impact (Category A), whereas MSQoL shows potential but requires further reliability and responsiveness research (Category B). A combined approach is recommended for comprehensive migraine burden evaluation.

articles.title: Revisiting the use of adenosine deaminase in cerebrospinal fluid analysis for infectious meningoencephalitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels in the cerebrospinal fluid have neither been validated as a reliable diagnostic marker nor sufficiently studied in patients with tropical diseases and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)ADA levels in different central nervous system (CNS) infections, define a cutoff value, and assess correlations between CSF-ADA and other laboratory parameters.

METHODS: In 206 patients whose CSF-ADA levels were measured, we analyzed data on baseline characteristics, diagnoses, CSF-ADA levels, and additional laboratory parameters. These CSF-ADA levels were compared according to microbiological diagnosis, and correlations with other CSF and blood parameters were analyzed.

RESULTS: Compared with the non-CNS infectious control group (n = 40), 2 subgroups showed significantly higher CSF-ADA levels: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (n = 45, p < 0.0001) and Neisseria meningitidis (n = 11, p = 0.0400). The identified cutoff values were 5.5 and 7.3 IU/L for M. tuberculosis and CNS coinfections, respectively. For M. tuberculosis, sensitivity was 61.2% and specificity was 72.4%, whereas coinfections demonstrated 50% of sensitivity and 82.8% of specificity. The CSF-ADA levels correlated positively with CSF protein (Spearman rank correlation coefficient [rs] = 0.3009, p < 0.0003) and weakly correlated negatively with CSF glucose (rs = -0.1895, p < 0.0254). Patients with M. tuberculosis infection exhibited significantly higher CSF-ADA levels, as reflected by the mean, median, and standard deviation, than those with other infectious etiologies combined (n = 121) and those with bacterial and viral infections analyzed separately (p < 0.05). When stratified according to HIV status, a significant difference in CSF-ADA levels was observed only among patients with varicella-zoster virus infection (p = 0.0428).

CONCLUSION: The CSF-ADA levels were elevated in tuberculous and meningococcal meningitis. Higher cutoff values may occur in CNS coinfections. Therefore, CSF-ADA may serve as a supportive diagnostic tool in cases of suspected TBM, meningococcal meningitis, and CNS coinfections.

articles.title: Biologic therapy: A paradigm shift in asthma management.
Biologic therapy: A paradigm shift in asthma management.
articles.abstract: Biologic medications provide opportunities to improve the health, safety, quality of life, and long-term outcomes of patients with moderate-to-severe uncontrolled asthma. This article provides primary care nurse practitioners with an overview of the pathophysiology of Type 2 inflammation in asthma, the mechanism of action of biologics approved for asthma, monitoring considerations, and practice considerations.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation Burden as an Outcome in Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: AbstractAtrial fibrillation is the most common cardiac arrhythmia in the world. In clinical trials evaluating interventions for atrial fibrillation, outcomes have been traditionally defined using a thirty second arrhythmia end point. In this Clinical Trials Workshop, we evaluate the role of atrial fibrillation burden as a primary outcome for atrial fibrillation intervention trials. In particular, we evaluate key considerations for ascertainment, definition, and analysis of atrial fibrillation burden while further considering regulatory implications of its use as a primary end point.

articles.title: Next-Generation Bed Nets to Control Malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with more than one insecticide have been insufficiently evaluated in West Africa.

METHODS: In this cluster randomized clinical trial, 33 clusters of villages (1-3 villages per cluster) in Côte d'Ivoire were randomly assigned (11 clusters per group) to use pyrethroid-only (py-only; MAGNet) (control), piperonyl butoxide-pyrethroid (PBO-py; Veeralin), or chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid (CFP-py; Interceptor G2) LLINs. One net was distributed for every two people, followed by door-to-door visits to assist with hanging the nets and to promote their use. The primary outcome was the incidence of malaria cases among children aged 6 months to 9 years over the year following net distribution. Incidence rate ratios compared cases per child-year between clusters randomly assigned to use PBO-py versus py-only nets and CFP-py versus py-only nets.

RESULTS: A total of 25,660 LLINs were distributed to 11,283 households (py-only, n=3797; PBO-py, n=3559; and CFP-py, n=3927). The primary outcome analyses included 549, 551, and 549 children in the py-only, PBO-py, and CFP-py groups, respectively. Mean malaria incidence over 12 months was 1.11 cases per child-year in the py-only group (control), 0.84 in the PBO-py group, and 0.65 in the CFP-py group. The incidence rate ratios were as follows: PBO-py versus py-only nets, 0.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.99; P=0.045); and CFP-py versus py-only nets, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.43 to 0.75; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Malaria incidence over 12 months was significantly reduced among children aged 6 months to 9 years residing in clusters of villages in Côte d'Ivoire that were randomly assigned to use CFP-py versus py-only LLINs and PBO-py versus py-only LLINs. (Funded by The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05796193.).

articles.title: E-Cigarettes with and without Behavioral Support for Smoking Cessation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trials that have shown that e-cigarettes are effective in helping people quit smoking typically provided behavioral support in addition to e-cigarettes. Behavioral support is not always available or wanted, but it is not known whether e-cigarettes are effective without it.

METHODS: Participants who smoked and were motivated to quit were randomly assigned to National Health Service SmokeFree automated email messages (supportive messages), an e-cigarette starter pack alone (EC-only), or an e-cigarette starter pack plus multisession telephone-based behavioral support (EC+). The primary outcome was biochemically validated sustained abstinence from smoking at 6 months. Participants who were lost to follow-up or did not provide biochemical validation were assumed to continue to smoke. A significance level of 0.025 was prespecified for each of the two primary comparisons (EC-only vs. supportive messages and EC+ vs. EC-only).

RESULTS: The 6-month abstinence rates were 6.4% in the supportive messages group, 11.3% in the EC-only group (EC-only vs. supportive messages relative risk 1.76; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 1.03 to 3.01; P=0.018), and 21.1% in the EC+ group, (EC+ vs. EC-only relative risk 1.87; 97.5% CI, 1.27 to 2.75; P<0.001). Serious adverse events were reported by 8.1%, 10.8%, and 10.7% of participants in the supportive messages, EC-only, and EC+ groups, respectively. There were four deaths, two in the EC-only group and two in the EC+ group.

CONCLUSIONS: E-cigarettes without further support were more effective than supportive messaging in helping people achieve sustained validated abstinence from smoking at 6 months. E-cigarettes with multisession telephone-based support were more effective than e-cigarettes alone. (Funded by The National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Technology Assessment programme (NIHR129627); ISRCTN number, 61193406.).

articles.title: Real-world implementation of AI-assisted PERT-workflow and its association with care processes and budget impact: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. In intermediate-high and high-risk PE, timely escalation beyond anticoagulation is critical, yet real-world pathways are often delayed. Pulmonary embolism response teams (PERTs) improve decision-making, but activation remains inconsistent. Whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled triage strengthens PERT and improves acute PE care has not been elucidated so far.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively screened 2500 patients presenting to our university hospital with a symptomatic central or segmental PE between 08/2022 and 07/2024. Clinical and economic outcomes were compared during a 1-year timeframe before and after implementation of an AI algorithm that analyses CT scans, flags suspected PE, and supports PERT triage. 424 patients met inclusion criteria. AI-supported triage increased PERT activation from 9.2% to 84.5% (P < 0.001). Time from CT completion to PE diagnosis decreased from 2.1 to 1.3 h (P < 0.01). Time from PE diagnosis to interventional therapy was reduced by 50% (P < 0.05). Hospital/ICU length-of-stay and 30-day mortality showed non-significant reductions. Model-based economic analysis showed lower 1-year per-patient costs and annual savings associated with AI-supported PERT.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of an AI-supported PERT workflow was associated with significant improvements in PE care processes, including higher PERT activation rates and shorter diagnostic and treatment intervals. Numerical reductions in mortality, hospital/ICU length-of-stay did not reach statistical significance. The exploratory budget impact model suggested potential cost savings, mainly driven by trends in reduced resource utilization; however, these findings require prospective validation using adequately powered clinical endpoints.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Perceived Organizational Justice and Workplace Alienation Among Nurses in Northern Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Perceived organizational justice may influence nurses' workplace alienation. This study examined the relationship between perceived organizational justice and workplace alienation among nurses in Northern Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 183 nurses working in government hospitals in the Al-Jouf region, Saudi Arabia. Participants completed the Colquitt Organizational Justice Scale and the Work Alienation Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, group-comparison tests, and simple linear regression.

RESULTS: Mean perceived organizational justice was 4.04 (SD, 0.39) and mean workplace alienation was 2.71 (SD, 0.47), each scored from 1 to 5. Perceived organizational justice was inversely associated with workplace alienation (   r = - 0.455    ,   p < 0. 001    ). Perceived organizational justice explained 20.7% of the variance in workplace alienation (    R 2 = 0.207    ,   p < 0. 001    ).

CONCLUSION: Higher perceived organizational justice was associated with lower workplace alienation among nurses. Longitudinal research is needed to examine temporal and causal relationships.

articles.title: Acute Angina in Anomalous Left Main Coronary Artery With Prepulmonic Course: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Although a prepulmonic left main coronary artery is usually considered a lower-risk AAOCA subtype, it may still be associated with acute ischemic symptoms when significant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is present. Multimodality imaging is essential for defining the coronary anatomy, and coronary artery bypass grafting may be the preferred strategy when severe multivessel disease coexists.

articles.title: The Prescription Pattern, Care-Seeking Behavior and Glycemic Status Among the Diabetic Patients in a Tertiary-Level Hospital of Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prevalence of diabetes mellitus is on the rise globally, presenting a significant challenge to healthcare systems, particularly in developing countries like Bangladesh. However, treatment modalities, care-seeking attitudes and clinical profiles among these patients are not well explored. This descriptive cross-sectional study examines the prescription patterns, care-seeking behavior and glycemic status among the diabetic patients in a tertiary-level hospital in Bangladesh.

METHODS: A total of 231 previously diagnosed type II diabetic patients from outpatient services, comprising 129 males and 102 females, were approached using a well-structured questionnaire. Socio-demographic characteristics, along with physical activity, tobacco smoking, adherence to a diet chart, and consultation with pharmacists, were obtained through participants' recall. 'Patients' biochemical parameters, such as blood pressure and glucose level were also taken into consideration.

RESULTS: The majority of respondents were in the 40-59 age group (55.8%), with a mean age of 50.67 ± 11.9 (SD) years. On average, 4.23 ± 1.23 (mean ± SD) drugs were prescribed for the management of diabetes and its comorbidities. A moderate correlation (r = 0.546, p < 0.01) was found between the average number of drugs and patients mean age. A single antidiabetic drug was prescribed to 121 patients (52.4%), two drugs to 82 (35.5%), and three drugs to 28 patients (12.1%) only. Although antidiabetic medications were prescribed, uncontrolled glycemic control was reported in 186 patients (80.5%). A weak association was found between glycemic status and the types of antidiabetic therapy among the diabetic patients, with a chi-square statistic of 6.10 (p < 0.01). Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and fasting and 2-h postprandial blood glucose levels were significantly higher in aged diabetic patients (p < 0.001). The majority of participants (211, 91.3%) followed the diet chart advised by their physicians, which was associated with better control of diabetes-related complications (χ2 value 3.36, p < 0.1).

CONCLUSION: Given the heavy drug burden and comorbidities, these findings support regular glycemic monitoring, timely review and adjustment of medication, adherence to diet and lifestyle counseling, and closer attention to aged diabetic patients. The insights from this research may provide valuable guidance to healthcare providers and policymakers in devising patient-centered treatment strategies for the diabetic patients in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Microbiological Spectrum and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Tubo-Ovarian Abscesses Managed by Surgery or Drainage at a Tertiary Hospital in Vietnam: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Tubo-ovarian abscess requires empirical antimicrobial therapy before culture results are available, but local antimicrobial resistance data are limited in Vietnam. We described the microbiological spectrum and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of tubo-ovarian abscesses managed by surgery or drainage.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of 66 patients with tubo-ovarian abscess who underwent surgery or drainage and had procedure-obtained abscess material submitted for culture at Nhan Dan Gia Dinh Hospital from January 2021 to May 2025. Antimicrobial susceptibility data were summarized for recovered isolates when available. Descriptive statistics and Wilson 95% confidence intervals were used for key proportions. Antimicrobial susceptibility was summarized using the number of isolates tested for each agent as the denominator.

RESULTS: The analytic sample comprised 66 surgically treated or drained patients. Culture positivity was 43.9% (29/66; 95% CI, 32.6%-55.9%), with 39 bacterial isolates reported. Escherichia coli was the most frequent isolate (19/39, 48.7%), followed by Streptococcus spp. (9/39, 23.1%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (7/39, 17.9%). Among E. coli isolates, 6/19 (31.6%) were extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producers and 1/19 (5.3%) was an AmpC producer. Resistance among tested E. coli isolates was 13/14 (92.9%) to ampicillin, 7/14 (50.0%) to ceftriaxone, and 10/19 (52.6%) to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Antibiotic-specific denominators were small and variable.

CONCLUSION: Tubo-ovarian abscesses managed by surgery or drainage in this Vietnamese case series frequently yielded enteric Gram-negative organisms and streptococci, with substantial E. coli resistance to commonly used agents among tested isolates. These findings support procedure-obtained abscess culture, local antibiograms, clinically indicated anaerobic coverage, and antimicrobial stewardship; they should not be generalized to all patients with tubo-ovarian abscess.

articles.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength.

OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional.

PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728).

EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3).

OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis.

METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated.

RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men.
