Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women.

CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

articles.title: Association of SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) Gene Polymorphisms With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in the Bangladeshi Population: A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has a strong genetic component and variations in specific gene alleles can significantly influence individual susceptibility. Stromal cell-derived factor-1 beta (SDF-1β) plays a crucial role in inflammatory responses, glucose regulation, and the maintenance of pancreatic β-cell function, while TCF7L2, a key regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway, governs insulin secretion and overall glucose homeostasis. The present study evaluated the association of the SDF-1β rs1801157 and TCF7L2 rs12255372 polymorphisms with T2DM development in the Bangladeshi population.

METHODS: In this case-control study, 140 clinically diagnosed T2DM patients and 95 healthy controls, were enrolled after obtaining approval from the institutional ethics committee. Genomic DNA was genotyped for SDF-1β (rs1801157) and TCF7L2 (rs12255372) SNPs using PCR-RFLP, with MspI used for SDF-1β digestion and MluCI for the TCF7L2 fragment. The resulting genotypes were then identified through agarose gel electrophoresis. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was tested in both groups. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared using Fisher's exact test, with crude and adjusted (for age, sex, BMI) odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: All genotype distributions were in the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Using the homozygous dominant genotype (GG) as the reference, a statistically significant association was observed for SDF-1β (rs1801157) with the AA genotype (p < 0.05), whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no significant association. Additionally, the allele frequency distributions for both SDF-1β and TCF7L2 did not differ significantly between cases and controls (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The SDF-1β (rs1801157) AA genotype was significantly less frequent among T2DM patients, suggesting a possible protective association, whereas TCF7L2 (rs12255372) showed no such association. Given the modest sample size and limited statistical power, these findings indicate a possible association rather than a definitive marker of susceptibility and require replication.

articles.title: SLE Complicated With AIHA and Parvovirus B19 Infection Secondary to PRCA: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a woman in her 30s with SLE and AIHA who developed parvovirus B19 infection and secondary PRCA. Hemoglobin did not increase significantly after IVIG treatment; her condition improved significantly following the addition of foscarnet, providing a practical treatment option for secondary PRCA.

articles.title: Suspected Gluteal Epithelioid Sarcoma Complicated by Secondary Infection and Sciatic Neuropathy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Secondary infection can coexist with and obscure an underlying soft-tissue sarcoma. A deep mass that persists or progresses despite drainage and appropriate antibiotics, especially with progressive neurological deficit, warrants image-guided core biopsy and sarcoma-center referral before further surgery.

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Traditional Uvulectomy: A Study Done Among Infants at University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional uvulectomy remains a significant public health concern in Ethiopia. Despite multiple complications associated with this traditional malpractice like bleeding and infection transmission the practice continues. This traditional practice is more commonly performed on infants. This study provides evidence on the prevalence and associated factors of traditional uvulectomy.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of and associated factors for traditional uvulectomy among infants under 12 months of age who visited the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2024/2025.

METHOD: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among infants under 12 months of age who visited the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital from August 2024 to January 2025. A pretested, researcher-administered questionnaire was used to interview caregivers and extract data from medical records. The data were collected using the Kobo Toolbox by two trained general practitioners and analyzed using STATA version 17 software. Binary and multivariable logistic regressions were employed to determine factors associated with traditional uvulectomy and the presence of multicollinearity was checked and no value more than 3 was there. The statistical association between dependent and independent variables was declared at p-value of ≤ 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 426 participants were included in this study, with ages ranging from 3 days to 12 months and a median age of 3 months (interquartile range [IQR] = 0.9-9 months). The prevalence of traditional uvulectomy was 69.7%. Among the participants, poor maternal knowledge and poor attitude were prevalent, accounting for 69.3% and 65.3%, respectively. Identified factors for traditional uvulectomy were: mothers with no postnatal counseling (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 3.08, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.65-5.73), mothers with poor attitude (AOR = 4.41, 95% CI: 1.87-8.96), and mothers with poor knowledge (AOR = 8.30, 95% CI: 3.70-18.61) toward traditional uvulectomy. The model had good performance, with a Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test p-value of 0.236.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of traditional uvulectomy was high. Lack of postnatal counseling about traditional uvulectomy, poor attitude, and poor knowledge were found to be independent contributing factors for traditional uvulectomy. Practicing comprehensive and consistent parental and postnatal health education and counseling about traditional uvulectomy is very important to overcome this malpractice.

articles.title: PAs in Latvia.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: The physician assistant (PA) or associate profession in Latvia has its root in the feldšeris, or feldsher, profession of eastern Europe. Initially trained for military service, Latvian feldshers began receiving education to provide care to civilians in 1954. The profession changed its name to ārsta palīgs ("physician assistant") in the early 2000s. Latvian PAs are trained in a 3-year diploma program consisting of basic sciences, clinical sciences, and clinical placements in core medical disciplines, and have the option to obtain a specialized credential in emergency medicine or outpatient medicine with an additional year of study. Approximately 2600 PAs in Latvia practice in primary and specialty care across the country, and there are twice as many PAs per capita in Latvia as there are in the United States. PAs are an important part of Latvia's health care workforce solution to a significant provider shortage.

articles.title: Increasing use of SGLT-2 inhibitors among patients with heart failure.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this quality improvement project was to identify and address barriers contributing to the underutilization of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors in eligible patients with heart failure across the health system.

METHODS: The heart failure registry was used to identify the prescription percentage of SGLT-2 inhibitors pre- and postintervention. Interventions to increase prescribing included pharmacist education to primary care providers and use of a cost information handout.

RESULTS: Following the intervention, SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription for eligible patients improved from 7.1% (n = 630) to 9.0% (n = 814), representing a relative increase of 26.8% from baseline.

CONCLUSION: A multimodal approach involving pharmacy and primary care effectively increased SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing in patients with heart failure. Physician associates, a key part of the primary care workforce, play an important role initiating guideline-directed medical therapy.

articles.title: Atopic dermatitis.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that commonly begins in childhood and can persist or first appear in adulthood. Its burden reflects pruritus, sleep loss, pain, infection, psychosocial effects, and treatment demands rather than visible extent alone. Diagnosis is clinical and requires recognition of age- and skin tone-specific morphology and exclusion of mimics. AD management begins with moisturization, gentle bathing, topical anti-inflammatory therapy, education, and proactive maintenance. Newer nonsteroidal topical agents and targeted systemic therapies have expanded options, but treatment should be individualized according to age, disease severity and control, comorbidities, safety, access, and patient preference. Routine elimination diets, topical antimicrobials for uninfected disease, antihistamines as primary antipruritic therapy, and systemic corticosteroids are generally not recommended for AD. This review provides physician associates with a practical approach to diagnosis, severity assessment, stepwise treatment, complication recognition, and timely referral.

articles.title: Female infertility in the 21st century.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: More than 12% of reproductive-age women in the United States seek infertility services each year. Infertility is commonly defined as failure to conceive after 12 months of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse. Common gynecologic causes of female infertility include endometriosis; diminished ovarian reserve; ovulatory dysfunction and anovulation; and other cervical, uterine, or tubal factors. Advances in medicine and assisted reproductive technology have expanded treatment options for women and couples experiencing infertility. This article provides an updated review of female infertility to support PAs in delivering informed patient counseling on treatment options, recognizing potential complications, and facilitating timely and appropriate referrals.

articles.title: Correction to: 2026 Guideline for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery: A Guideline From the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association.
Reimagining Stroke Research Infrastructure: Lessons From NIH Center Models to Build Community-Engaged Systems That Enhance Participation and Implementation.
Advances in Pediatric Stroke.
Caseous Mitral Annular Necrosis: A Diagnostic Role for Cardiac CT in Recurrent Embolic Stroke.
Type A Aortic Dissection Presenting as Common TIA.
Cytoprotection for Acute Ischemic Stroke: Critical Appraisal of Recent Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Several phase III clinical trials testing cytoprotective approaches have recently been completed, and many of these studies report a clinical benefit. Reviewing the outcomes of these trials in light of their specific designs reveals intriguing results. Trials designed with shorter treatment time windows (≤24 hours) and featuring high rates of recanalization therapies predominantly show neutral outcomes, that is, no therapeutic benefit. Studies using later time points (>24 hours to 14 days) and often enrolling patients in whom recanalization is not or only infrequently established show clear treatment effects. These results challenge our current understanding of cytoprotective approaches, which are believed to primarily target the penumbra as the key to therapeutic success. The reasons for this are unclear. They may include other, potentially unknown mechanisms of action that improve clinical outcome even when applied within longer time windows rather than exerting acute cytoprotection. Here, we discuss such potential mechanisms, to what extent they could explain the results of recent cytoprotection trials, and review consequences for future translational and clinical research.

articles.title: November 2026 Stroke Highlights.
Modeling Deep Stroke in the Awake Brain: Sleep Oscillations, Thalamocortical Repair, and Auditory Neuromodulation.
Pulsatile Tinnitus Alleviated by Contralateral Stent Implantation.
Different Enough?: Rethinking Trial Generalizability in the Era of Chinese Neurovascular Research.
From Discovery to Confirmation: Building a Replication Pathway for Influential Randomized Controlled Trials.
Stroke Images Hemi- "Vehicle" -Prosopometamorphopsia Associated With Splenial Infarction.
Efficacy and Safety of Lucitanib in Advanced Thymic Carcinoma: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
articles.abstract: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Negative impact of single housing on chronic kidney disease mineral and bone disorder outcomes.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a disorder of acquired disrupted mineral metabolism that affects millions in the United States and has no cure. Due to disturbed mineral homeostasis bones are particularly affected showing substantial bone loss during CKD and intricately linked with morbidity and mortality. Animal models serve as a crucial platform to investigate and elucidate the tissue cross-communication that facilitates pathogenic changes during CKD. One preclinical rodent model gaining in popularity is the adenine-diet induced CKD, which negates the requirement for highly technical surgical interventions and displays several of the CKD disrupted mineral metabolism hallmarks observed in patients. Interestingly, although CKD alone can negatively impact bone, other factors, such as individual housing, can impair normal bone homeostasis. This could be encountered experimentally especially when generating experimental animals in-house, in particular, using males that maintain aggressive territorial actions. We sought to evaluate the impact of reduced cage housing numbers, replicating potentially encountered cage number conditions, on the progression of CKD. We hypothesized that single housing alone would accelerate bone loss and therefore exacerbate CKD mineral dysregulation and related outcomes. To test this, C57BL/6J male mice at 10 wk old were maintained at 5-, 3-, or 1-mice per cage while receiving casein-control or the CKD-inducing adenine diet. We found that within 4 wk of diet administration, individually housed mice had more profound weight loss corresponding with increased circulating urea, hyperphosphatemia, and bone loss compared to mice maintained at 5 per cage. Additionally, 50% of the individually housed CKD animals developed cardiovascular calcifications, a sequelae of impaired mineral excretion. These data demonstrate housing density significantly impacts outcomes related to CKD and an important variable to consider when conducting basic and translational mouse CKD studies.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.

METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.

FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.

INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

FUNDING: Key Clinical Research Initiative Program of Union Hospital, National Key Technology Research and Development Programme of Hubei Province, and Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Potential Association of BRCA Mutation and Lymphocytic Lobulitis.
articles.abstract: Lymphocytic lobulitis (LL) is a rare fibroinflammatory breast lesion historically associated with long-standing Type 1 diabetes mellitus and autoimmune conditions. Recent evidence suggests possible links between LL and hereditary breast cancer syndromes, particularly BRCA mutations. We present the case of a BRCA1 mutation carrier who developed bilateral lymphocytic lobulitis with B-cell predominance, discuss its clinicopathologic features, and review current literature on the intersection of autoimmune, metabolic, and genetic risk pathways.

articles.title: Two Eruptive Calcified Nodules in the Same Artery.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous calcified nodule destabilization may occur in a multifocal manner, analogous to the phenomenon of multiple plaque ruptures, leading to an acute coronary syndrome. Optical coherence tomography can identify multiple eruptive calcified nodules in the same coronary artery and can influence treatment planning.

articles.title: Disparities in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and severe maternal morbidity: Evidence from a statewide birth cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) complicate 15% of pregnancies nationally and are a major contributor to severe maternal morbidity (SMM). We aimed to characterize temporal trends and demographic disparities in HDP incidence and evaluate the association between HDP and SMM in a statewide cohort.

METHODS: This study is a descriptive and regression-based analysis of a retrospective cohort of Wisconsin births from 2017 to 2023. Data were obtained from the Wisconsin Hospital Association (WHA). Subtypes of HDP were identified using ICD-10 codes. Incidence rates of HDP per 10,000 births and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were estimated using Poisson regression and examined across demographic variables. Outcomes measured included SMM incidence, AAPCs, and SMM indicators by HDP.

RESULTS: Among 388,250 pregnancies, the incidence of nearly all HDP subtypes rose from 2017 to 2023. Severe pre-eclampsia had the highest AAPC (11.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6%-13.0%). HDP incidence was highest in urban areas, though the AAPC in preeclampsia was greater in rural areas (8.7%; 95% CI, 7.1%-10.3%; p = 0.004). Black patients experienced higher incidences of HDP, with significant differences in AAPC for HDP overall, chronic hypertension, and severe preeclampsia (p < 0.001). Patients with HDP had higher SMM rates compared to those without, though the AAPC in SMM did not differ by HDP status.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a growing burden of HDP in Wisconsin, with an increase in severe preeclampsia incidence and disparities by geography and race. Targeted interventions in rural areas and for Black patients are needed to improve disparities in HDP incidence and reduce SMM across Wisconsin.

articles.title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
articles.abstract: This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence-informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large-volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine-preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

articles.title: Latest findings on complications following trans- catheter aortic valve replacement: A literature review.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis (As) is the most common valvular heart disease in developed countries, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has expanded across surgical risk groups. However, procedure-related complications remain clinically important, and their reported incidence and management have evolved with newer-generation devices and techniques. This review summarizes major TAVR complications, including their incidence and pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical impact, prevention and management, and outlines remaining knowledge gaps.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for studies published between 2012 and 2026, including randomized trials, registries, cohort studies, and systematic reviews.

RESULTS: Major complications reviewed included Stroke, Delirium, Conduction disturbances (CD) and Arrhythmias, Bleeding/Vascular(access) site injuries/Paravalvular leak (PVL), Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), Structural valve degeneration and thrombosis, Infective Endocarditis (IE) and Coronary Obstruction (CO).

CONCLUSIONS: TAVR complications remain multifactorial, and their incidence and management continue to shift with device evolution and procedural experience. Optimized patient selection, procedural refinement, frailty assessment, and individualized antithrombotic strategies remain important areas for improving outcomes.

articles.title: Renal Transplantation in Recipients With Modified Lower Urinary Tract: A Systematic Review and Implications for Adult Transplant Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with a modified lower urinary tract (MLUT) represent a growing but understudied population in renal transplantation. Concerns regarding long-term graft survival, infection, and urological morbidity persist, yet adult-specific outcome synthesis and clinically useful guidance are lacking.

METHODS: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review of studies reporting posttransplant outcomes in adults with abnormal or surgically MLUT anatomy. Primary outcomes were 1- and 5-y graft and patient survival. Secondary outcomes included urological complications. Given substantial heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies, including 511 MLUT recipients, were identified. Most were retrospective single-center series, and only a minority included comparator cohorts. Several studies included mixed adult-pediatric cohorts where adult-only outcomes could not be separated. Across comparative studies, 1-y graft survival appeared broadly similar between MLUT and control recipients, whereas 5-y graft survival was more often lower in MLUT cohorts. Patient survival was comparable, although long-term comparative data were limited. Urological morbidity was consistently greater in MLUT recipients, particularly recurrent urinary tract infection and the need for further urological intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: Renal transplantation in selected adults with MLUT is achievable with acceptable early outcomes, but the burden of urological morbidity is substantial, and longer-term graft outcomes are less favorable. These findings support careful pretransplant lower urinary tract assessment and highlight the need for pragmatic optimization pathways, although higher-quality prospective data remain necessary.

articles.title: Impact of Elderly Donors on Patient Survival and Postoperative Complications in Liver Transplantation: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation is the gold standard treatment for end-stage liver disease, yet approximately 23% of candidates die or are removed from the waitlist because of organ shortages. To expand the donor pool, elderly donors are increasingly used, but their impact on outcomes and postoperative complications remains controversial. Livers from elderly donors often show reduced regenerative capacity and diminished blood flow, which may increase posttransplant risks.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 950 adult deceased-donor liver transplantations performed at Huashan Hospital between August 1, 2017, and November 30, 2023. Recipients were divided into an elderly donor group (≥60 y; n = 201) and a younger donor group (<60 y; n = 749). The study compared overall survival, disease-free survival for hepatocellular carcinoma, and various complications.

RESULTS: Overall survival (P = 0.681) and hepatocellular carcinoma disease-free survival (P = 0.486) were similar between groups. The elderly donor group had higher incidences of primary nonfunction (PNF; 4.0% versus 0.9%; P = 0.002), acute rejection (AR; 29.4% versus 10.9%; P = 0.001), and splenic artery steal syndrome (SASS; 2.0% versus 0.5%; P = 0.045). Retransplantation was numerically more frequent in the elderly donor group (4.0% versus 1.9%; P = 0.077). After adjustment, elderly donor status remained associated with PNF (odds ratio [OR], 3.199; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.131-4.802), AR (OR, 5.314; 95% CI, 1.720-16.420), and SASS (OR, 5.881; 95% CI, 1.043-33.149), but not overall survival or retransplantation.

CONCLUSIONS: Elderly donor grafts were not associated with inferior long-term recipient survival but were associated with higher risks of PNF, AR, and SASS.

articles.title: Appearance Over Health: A Phenomenological Study of Obese Adolescents With a Family History of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Collectivistic Indonesian Context.
articles.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), and Indonesia ranks fifth in the prevalence of diabetes worldwide, coupled with the increasing rate of youth obesity. This phenomenological study explored adolescent obesity as a high-risk group within Indonesia's collectivistic cultural context to generate qualitative insights that may inform culturally grounded, family- and peer-supported interventions for T2DM prevention. The study does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific intervention.

METHODS: Conducted in Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia (March 2021-April 2022), the study recruited 11 adolescents, 11 parents, and 9 peers from four primary care clinics using purposive sampling until data saturation. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's method.

RESULTS: The majority of adolescents reported being more concerned about their appearance than about their health. The findings also indicated that all groups had limited awareness of T2DM risks. Adolescents perceived intimate relationships as important in shaping healthy lifestyle choices. Peers offered emotional support and encouragement for healthier behaviors, while parents were described as supervising diet and promoting physical exercise.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that health education could potentially address adolescents' appearance-related concerns as an initial entry point to enhance engagement. For Indonesian adolescents to effectively avoid obesity and lower their risk of T2DM, strategies involving peers and parents may be an important consideration; however, these are presented as implications derived from the qualitative findings, rather than as interventions whose effectiveness has been demonstrated. Future research is needed to empirically test such culturally tailored approaches.

articles.title: Leptin Neutralization Attenuates Inflammaging in Endothelial and Immune Cell Models.
articles.abstract: Leptin, a proinflammatory adipokine, contributes to the chronic low-grade inflammation seen in obesity, but its role in age-related inflammation, that is inflammaging, has been poorly studied. We thus tested the effect of blocking leptin receptor (LEP-R) binding in five models of inflammaging, that is replicative senescent endothelial cells, hyperglycemia-treated macrophages or endothelial cells, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-exposed macrophages, and TCR-stimulated CD4+ T cells. In endothelial cells, leptin enhanced senescence, while leptin neutralization suppressed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, two effects mediated in part by the mTOR pathway. In both macrophages and endothelial cells, leptin blockade blunted hyperglycemia-induced inflammation, while in macrophages, it also suppressed the LPS-induced senescent and proinflammatory phenotype. In T cells, leptin neutralization produced divergent effects, attenuating the expression of inflammatory and senescence markers in conventional T cells but not in regulatory T cells. To assess translational relevance, we measured leptin and inflammaging markers in plasma samples from two independent cohorts, one of healthy individuals (n = 121) and another of people with Type 2 diabetes (n = 93). In healthy subjects, leptin levels were higher in people with hs-CRP ≥ 3 mg/dL compared with those below such threshold, also after adjustment for BMI. Leptin levels showed BMI-adjusted positive correlations with IL-6 and hs-CRP in healthy individuals and with hs-CRP and IL-8 in people with diabetes. These findings suggest that leptin might fuel inflammaging and that its neutralization exerts anti-inflammatory effects across multiple, related models.

articles.title: Multi-Omics Insights Into Circulating T-Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and Treg Dysfunction in Moyamoya Disease.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disease linked to immune dysregulation, yet T-cell metabolic reprogramming and regulatory T-cell (Treg) function remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics approaches, including mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and flow cytometry to characterize T-cell metabolic alterations and Treg dysfunction in MMD, uncovering a key metabolic-immune axis. Compared with healthy controls, MMD patients showed chronic immune activation and broad suppression of amino acid, glycolytic, and fatty acid metabolic pathways. Although Tregs were aberrantly expanded, they displayed metabolic inflexibility, together with impaired intercellular communication. Single-cell transcriptomics indicated Treg-to-Th17 conversion, while flow cytometry confirmed increased IL-17A+ cells within the CD4+FOXP3+ compartment. Besides, these dysfunctional Tregs correlated with advanced Suzuki stages, ischemic stroke, and posterior cerebral artery involvement. Bulk transcriptomic and serum metabolomic analyses further confirmed coordinated immune activation and metabolic suppression at the gene, protein, pathway, and metabolite levels. These findings define a metabolic-immune axis in MMD in which metabolically constrained, functionally unstable Tregs may contribute to neuroinflammation and vascular remodeling, suggesting that restoring Treg metabolic fitness could represent a therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Recurrent Fetal Intracranial Hemorrhage and a Maternally Inherited COL4A1 Variant of Uncertain Significance: A Case Report With Maternal Reverse Phenotyping.
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman with two consecutive pregnancies affected by fetal left periventricular germinal matrix hemorrhage (Grade IV) and progressive ventriculomegaly underwent trio whole-exome sequencing. A heterozygous COL4A1 c.4249G>C (p.Gly1417Arg) variant, classified as a variant of uncertain significance, was identified in the fetus of the current pregnancy and found to be maternally inherited; concurrent copy-number analysis incidentally detected a maternal 17p12 microdeletion encompassing PMP22, which was not inherited by the fetus. Systematic reverse phenotyping of the mother revealed right corticospinal tract Wallerian degeneration, persistent microscopic hematuria, a renal cyst, and retinal arteriolar changes-a phenotype compatible with the COL4A1-associated spectrum, although molecular causality remains unproven. Following multidisciplinary review, the pregnancy was terminated at 29 weeks, primarily on the basis of the grave fetal prognosis, with early-onset preeclampsia contributing to the overall maternal risk assessment; the mother's post-termination course was uneventful, with resolution of hypertension and proteinuria. This case illustrates that recurrent anatomically congruent fetal intracranial hemorrhages may prompt maternal reverse phenotyping that identifies maternally inherited COL4A1 variants of uncertain significance, and underscores the need to distinguish phenotypic concordance from proven molecular causality in prenatal counseling.

articles.title: Klebsiella pneumoniae Epidural Abscess Presenting as Tubercular Spondylodiscitis: A Diagnostic Pitfall in a Diabetic Patient From Nepal.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae spinal epidural abscess is rare and can mimic tuberculous spondylodiscitis in endemic regions. We report a diabetic patient with pulmonary tuberculosis presenting with lumbar spondylodiscitis and epidural abscess. CT-guided biopsy identified Klebsiella pneumoniae, with no evidence of tuberculosis. Ceftriaxone led to recovery, highlighting the importance of tissue-based diagnosis.

articles.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers as Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Inflammatory biomarkers have been proposed as prognostic indicators in COVID-19; however, their prognostic associations within critically ill ICU-admitted patients remain of interest. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of selected inflammatory biomarkers with in-hospital mortality and their discriminatory performance among critically ill COVID-19 patients.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 244 adult patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia admitted to the ICU between August 2020 and June 2021 were analyzed. Disease severity was assessed using the ISARIC 4 C Mortality Score. Associations between inflammatory biomarkers and mortality were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminatory performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis.

RESULTS: The in-hospital mortality rate was 90.6%. ESR and LDH levels were significantly higher in non-survivors. In a biomarker-restricted multivariable logistic regression model, ESR (OR 1.023 per 1 mm/h increase; 95% CI 1.004-1.042; p = 0.016) and LDH (OR 1.002 per 1 U/L increase; 95% CI 1.000-1.003; p = 0.009) remained significantly associated with in-hospital mortality after mutual adjustment for the other prespecified inflammatory biomarkers. LDH demonstrated good discriminatory performance (AUC 0.725; 95% CI 0.645-0.805). ESR showed modest discriminatory performance (AUC 0.646; 95% CI 0.559-0.732).

CONCLUSION: ESR and LDH remained significantly associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for the other prespecified inflammatory biomarkers. These findings suggest that ESR and LDH may provide adjunctive prognostic information in critically ill ICU patients; however, they should be interpreted in the context of the biomarker-restricted model and the limited adjustment set. Confirmation in larger prospective studies incorporating established clinical prognostic factors is warranted.

articles.title: Navigating Professional Code of Conduct Among Undergraduate Dental Students in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non-maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts.

AIM: To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences.

METHODS: A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 6 months (November 2020-April 2021) at two dental colleges in Peshawar, Pakistan, one public and one private. Purposive sampling was used to recruit clinically exposed undergraduate dental students. Fifty students were approached and 37 participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Template Analysis. The report follows the COREQ framework and makes the analytic, reflexive, and trustworthiness procedures explicit.

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 20.9 ± 1.96 years (range 17-25); 29 (78.4%) were female and 8 (21.6%) male. Four interconnected themes were identified: unprofessionalism, harassment, poor communication, and discrimination. The accounts included concerns about infection control, empathy, accountability for clinical error, dishonesty, physical/verbal/emotional harassment, inadequate instruction, failures of informed consent, abuse of power, victimization, and targeting.

CONCLUSION: Students' accounts point primarily to breaches of professional conduct and to tensions between formal ethical expectations and the hidden curriculum of clinical learning. Professionalism education should therefore be embedded longitudinally in dental curricula and reinforced through faculty role-modeling, safe reporting pathways, supervised clinical practice, and context-sensitive ethical reasoning that can hold universal duties together with legitimate cultural and religious considerations.

articles.title: The Effects of Poor Self-Care Behaviors on Uncontrolled Hypertension in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hypertension affects nearly one in five adults in Ethiopia. Effective self-care behaviors, including medication adherence, regular physical activity, healthy dietary practices, weight management, moderation of alcohol intake, and avoidance of tobacco, are essential for optimal blood pressure (BP) control. Although individual studies have examined these behaviors, their combined contribution to uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia has not been comprehensively synthesized. This study aimed to evaluate the pooled effects of inadequate self-care behaviors on uncontrolled BP among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Electronic databases and gray literature sources were searched to identify observational studies reporting associations between self-care behaviors and uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia. Eligible studies were screened, and data were extracted using standardized tools. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using STATA version 17.0 to estimate pooled odds ratios (PORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Inadequate self-care behaviors were significantly associated with uncontrolled hypertension. Medication non-adherence (POR: 2.29, 95% CI: 1.90-2.77), poor salt restriction (POR: 3.33, 95% CI: 1.83-6.07), insufficient physical activity (POR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.53-2.77), inadequate weight management (POR: 2.31, 95% CI: 1.85-2.88), alcohol consumption (POR: 2.54, 95% CI: 1.37-4.73), and smoking (POR: 2.73, 95% CI: 1.51-4.94) were associated with higher odds of uncontrolled BP. Moderate to high heterogeneity was observed across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of findings, and no significant publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: Poor self-care practices substantially contribute to uncontrolled hypertension in Ethiopia. Strengthening patient-centered interventions targeting adherence and lifestyle modification is essential to improve BP control and reduce hypertension-related complications.

articles.title: Beyond Pigmentation: Interplay of Metabolic Profile, Carotid Intima-Media Thickness, and Fatty Liver in Vitiligo: An Age- and Sex-Matched Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Vitiligo shares inflammatory and metabolic pathways with cardiovascular and hepatic steatosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) is an established marker of early subclinical atherosclerosis, whereas non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) reflects hepatic involvement in chronic inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation. This study aimed to evaluate subclinical vascular and hepatic changes in patients with vitiligo and to explore their associations with disease characteristics and metabolic parameters.

METHODS: In this age- and sex-matched case-control study, adults with mild vitiligo (Vitiligo Area Severity Index [VASI] < 5%) and no metabolic syndrome were compared with healthy controls. Participants underwent carotid duplex ultrasonography to assess common carotid IMT and atherosclerotic plaques, liver ultrasonography for steatosis grading, and laboratory testing, including lipid profile (total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein [LDL], high-density lipoprotein [HDL], and triglycerides [TG]), fasting blood glucose (FBS), and body mass index (BMI). Disease duration and VASI score were also assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 46 participants (23 patients with vitiligo and 23 healthy controls) completed all assessments. Common carotid IMT measurements and liver ultrasound findings were comparable between groups. However, abnormal HDL levels were more frequent among patients with vitiligo (69.6% vs. 39.1%, p = 0.03). Greater disease severity, measured by VASI score, and higher BMI were independently associated with increased right carotid IMT (p = 0.01, 0.02, respectively). Exploratory interaction analyses demonstrated significant sex-dependent associations of HDL, triglycerides, and fatty liver status with carotid IMT. Post hoc analyses identified higher carotid IMT among male patients with abnormal HDL.

CONCLUSION: Selected subgroups of patients with vitiligo, particularly men with HDL metabolic abnormalities, may exhibit differences in subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Disease severity and BMI may also contribute to the vascular risk. Although exploratory, these findings warrant further investigation of cardiovascular and hepatic risk profiles in selected patients with vitiligo.

articles.title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear.

METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed.

RESULTS: Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01, P = .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70, P < .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (P for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33, P for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

articles.title: Alder-Reilly Anomaly Leading to Incidental Diagnosis of MPS VII in an Asymptomatic Adult.
articles.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type VII (MPS VII; Sly syndrome) is a rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of β-glucuronidase due to pathogenic variants in the GUSB gene. Impaired degradation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) results in multiorgan dysfunction with highly variable clinical presentation, ranging from severe neonatal disease to attenuated adult phenotypes. We report an incidental diagnosis of MPS VII in a 31-year-old woman identified through routine laboratory testing. Review of a peripheral blood smear was prompted by automated hematology analyzer flags and revealed Alder-Reilly anomaly with characteristic aberrant leukocyte granulation. Subsequent biochemical analysis showed elevated urinary dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate, alongside reduced β-glucuronidase activity (~2%-3% of normal). Genetic testing of GUSB identified compound heterozygosity for a likely pathogenic frameshift variant (c.133_134del) and a missense variant (c.454G>A) previously associated with pseudodeficiency. Despite biochemical and genetic findings consistent with MPS VII, the patient exhibited no typical clinical manifestations, and detailed phenotyping showed no organ involvement. This case illustrates an atypical, asymptomatic presentation of MPS VII diagnosed in adulthood, in which Alder-Reilly anomaly served as a critical diagnostic clue. The combination of a null allele with a pseudodeficiency-associated variant resulted in reduced enzyme activity without overt disease. These findings highlight the importance of peripheral blood smear evaluation in identifying lysosomal storage disorders and underscore the complexity of genotype-phenotype correlations in MPS VII.

articles.title: The entorhinal cortex atrophy score for diagnostic distinction between phases of the Alzheimer's disease continuum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type of dementia, causing functional impairment in millions of individuals and accounting for a large amount of healthcare costs. The entorhinal cortex appears to be one of the first brain structures affected by AD in its early stages. The Entorhinal Cortex Atrophy (ERICA) score is a visual atrophy score used by neuroradiologists in clinical practice for the diagnosis of AD.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the effectiveness of the ERICA score for distinguishing between patients with subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD dementia.

METHODS: A systematic review of the literature was conducted on the Science Direct, PubMed, Virtual Health Library, and Cochrane databases, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Of 1,413 studies identified, 6 were ultimately included in the present review, comprising 844 participants: 2 retrospective cohort studies and 4 cross-sectional studies. The methodological quality of the studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. The focus was on the diagnostic performance of the ERICA score in the continuum phases of AD.

RESULTS: The ERICA score had lower sensitivity than the medial temporal lobe atrophy (MTA) score but higher specificity, reinforcing its importance for diagnostic accuracy, especially in contexts of clinical uncertainty. The ERICA score showed reproducibility between examiners similar to or greater than that of the MTA score. There are a few heterogeneous studies in the current literature on the applicability of the ERICA score in clinical practice.

CONCLUSION: Diagnostic accuracy of the ERICA score is satisfactory in differentiating SCD or MCI from AD dementia.

articles.title: Unexpected coagulopathy in thrombolyzed stroke: experience from a single center in Chile.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent, and waiting for coagulation tests (COT) may delay treatment initiation. In several countries, IVT is initiated without waiting COT results; this approach has not been evaluated in South America. In this region, excessive alcohol consumption may increase the prevalence of unrecognized chronic liver disease.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of unsuspected coagulation abnormalities among patients with AIS treated with IVT at a single tertiary care center in Chile.

METHODS: A prospective analysis of all patients treated with IVT at Clínica Alemana between June 2016 and July 2025, assessing the proportion of individuals with unexpected coagulation abnormalities.

RESULTS: A total of 480 patients with AIS received IVT. The COTs were normal in 445 patients (92.7%), abnormal in 9 (1.88%), and incomplete or not performed in 26 (5.42%). No clinical differences were observed among the three groups. Patients with coagulation abnormalities or incomplete/not performed COT were significantly less frequent in the Emergency Room (ER) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (p = 0.001). Among those with abnormal COT results, significant differences were found in international normalized ratio (INR) values (p < 0.000) and platelet count (p = 0.001). The functional outcomes at 3 months, as well as mortality and rate of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, did not differ across groups.

CONCLUSION: Unexpected coagulation disorders are an infrequent finding in patients with AIS treated with IVT at our center in Santiago, Chile. Therefore, blood test results should not be awaited before initiating IVT.

articles.title: Laboratory Diagnostics for Thrombosis and Hemostasis Testing-Part V.
New dyslipidemia guideline makes more than half of U.S. adults eligible for statin therapy.
Efficacy and Safety of Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib in Advanced Endometrial Cancer: Results of a Multi-Cohort, Phase II Study (ETER200).
articles.abstract: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

articles.title: Spontaneous Renal Hemorrhage Secondary to MRSA Renal Abscess Requiring Nephrectomy After Failed Percutaneous Drainage: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spontaneous renal hemorrhage (SRH) caused by renal infection is extremely rare. Furthermore, sepsis caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has a high mortality rate and requires prompt source control.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old man with severe diabetes presented to the emergency department in shock. Computed tomography revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma. Based on his clinical course and history, infection-induced SRH was suspected. Blood and urine cultures yielded MRSA. Although percutaneous drainage was performed after the initial bleeding stabilized, persistent infection was followed by rebleeding, necessitating left nephrectomy. The patient recovered postoperatively. Histopathology confirmed abscess formation and chronic inflammation without malignancy.

CONCLUSION: For inadequately controlled infections following percutaneous drainage, particularly when recurrent hemorrhage is suspected, early nephrectomy may be considered for definitive source control.

articles.title: Hippo signaling-linked circulating microRNA networks are associated with cardiovascular disease in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) markedly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for patient stratification and may provide mechanistic insight into dysregulated pathways in T2D-associated CVD.

OBJECTIVE: This work aimed to identify circulating miRNA signatures in T2D patients with CVD (T2D-CVD) vs T2D patients without CVD using a novel network-based medicine approach.

METHODS: Patients (n = 110) were stratified into T2D and T2D-CVD groups based on the absence or presence of macrovascular complications. Circulating miRNAs, proinflammatory cytokines, and growth factors were profiled in a discovery cohort (n = 80) and confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 30). Differential expression, network-based approaches, and pathway enrichment analyses identified miRNA signatures, coexpression communities, hub miRNAs, and associated signaling pathways.

RESULTS: T2D-CVD patients showed a set of elevated inflammatory cytokines and circulating miRNAs. Particularly, 19 miRNAs were differentially expressed between T2D-CVD and T2D patients. Pathway enrichment of these miRNAs highlighted Hippo signaling together with transforming growth factor-β, mechanistic target of rapamycin, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Network analysis identified a coexpression community of 34 miRNAs, including hub miRNAs let-7a-5p, miR-132-3p, and miR-1306-3p, all linked to Hippo signaling. Key miRNA interactions were validated, and differentially expressed and hub miRNAs both correlated with inflammatory mediators such as PAR-1, CXCL1, and NEMO, which are linked to Hippo pathway regulation.

CONCLUSION: This study identified a network of circulating miRNAs associated with inflammatory cytokines and Hippo signaling pathway in T2D-CVD. These findings reveal novel molecular aspects of the systemic inflammation characterizing T2D-CVD and support the potential of Hippo-related circulating miRNAs as mechanistic biomarkers for cardiovascular risk in T2D.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease.
articles.abstract: Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes in human blood, have multifaceted roles in health and disease. Here we assembled a single-cell atlas of human neutrophils (SCAHN) by integrating transcriptome data from 1 million human neutrophils from 781 samples and 43 independent datasets. Using SCAHN, we identified multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and robust changes in gene expression and subset proportions in infection, cancer, immune suppression and sex differences at single-cell resolution. Cross-species reference mapping of mouse and nonhuman primate neutrophils onto SCAHN revealed both conserved and species-specific features. Using 17,023 bulk blood transcriptome profiles from 40 datasets, we found that neutrophil-specific signatures predicted mortality in acutely ill patients at presentation, were associated with cancer diagnosis and survival, and correlated with metabolic dysfunction and long-term all-cause mortality. Our study highlights how neutrophil biology can improve immune risk stratification and develop effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Moving Beyond the Checklist: A Three-Tier Model for Integrating Geriatrics Expertise into the CMS Age-Friendly Era.
articles.journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
articles.abstract: As the Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement enters a new phase of policy integration, hospitals face a pivotal moment. The U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Age Friendly Hospital Measure has created regulatory conditions necessary for hospital systems to institute high-quality, personalized care for older adults. As the CMS is expected to transition from pay-for-reporting to pay-for-performance for age-friendly care in the coming years, health systems must urgently move beyond reporting compliance toward true care redesign. The authors highlight three interrelated strategic risks and challenges that hospital leaders and executives must navigate in the current environment. First, there is the danger of reducing age-friendly care processes to siloed checklist exercises to satisfy reporting requirements, a risk that hospitals must mitigate by ensuring age-friendly care bundles are implemented as synchronized, outcome-driven approaches that respond to changes in the clinical status of patients and their transitions of care. Second, hospitals must account for older adults who are suffering from complex care needs, or multicomplexity, particularly because these patients disproportionately drive high costs and utilization metrics. Hospitals with constrained resources may also treat the 4Ms (What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility) framework as a substitute for specialized care, shifting investment away from geriatric specialists, palliative care practitioners, and allied interdisciplinary teams. Third, given the profound shortage of geriatric expertise, health systems must accept that they cannot provide specialist-level care to every patient 65 years of age or older. Even well-resourced health systems often struggle with risk-stratification blindness, failing to distinguish between universal age-friendly interventions appropriate for all inpatients and the subset of patients who require more intensive care with interdisciplinary geriatric teams. Without clear risk stratification, implementation efforts may become fragmented, inefficient, and difficult to sustain. To mitigate these risks, the authors propose a risk-stratified, three-tier operational framework that hospital leaders can utilize for age-friendly system redesign. This paradigm treats the 4Ms and other geriatric care processes enshrined in the CMS Age Friendly Hospital Measure as a foundation that should be delivered to all hospitalized older adults 65 years of age or older. It then builds on this foundation to identify strata of higher-risk older adults who require greater resource allocation, ranging from specialized interdisciplinary programs and protocols (such as hip fracture protocols and Geriatric Surgery Verification), which can be delivered primarily by generalists with geriatrician oversight, to higher-intensity models of care (such as acute care for elders units or geriatric-surgical comanagement), which require more intensive involvement from specialist geriatric teams. This operational roadmap will help hospital systems better match limited geriatric workforce resources to patient complexity, reducing inefficient care and improving both clinical and operational outcomes in alignment with the triple aim of health care.

articles.title: Age-Friendly Health System Recognition and Its Association with Improved Clinical Outcome Measures.
articles.journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
articles.abstract: The number of adults 65 years of age and older is rapidly increasing, as is health care utilization by older adults with multiple chronic conditions. The Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement, with a focus on What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility (the 4Ms), was launched in 2017 to improve management of older adults across health care settings. However, evidence of impact on outcomes remains limited. Using a national cohort of 4002 hospitals (388 with AFHS recognition from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement, as of December 31, 2024, and 3614 controls), the authors explore the associations between AFHS recognition and hospital readmission rates, mortality, and patient-reported experiences. Using difference-in-differences analyses, the authors find that level 2 AFHS recognition (i.e., hospitals with at least 3 months of data of older patients who have received 4Ms care) is associated with lower 30-day mortality rates for acute myocardial infarction (-0.41 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.75 to -0.06), pneumonia (-0.71; 95% CI, -1.29 to -0.13), and stroke (-0.56; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.07). Level 1 recognition (i.e., hospitals that have successfully developed plans to implement the 4Ms) is associated with lower readmission rates only for pneumonia (-0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.10). Furthermore, both level 1 and level 2 recognition are associated with modest reductions in Medicare spending per beneficiary. No determinative associations were identified between AFHS recognition and patient-reported experience measures. These findings provide one of the first national studies to suggest that organizations with AFHS recognition could be associated with improvement in certain outcomes and spending.

articles.title: [Sport as an offer in institutions of open child and youth work : Study results on the use of sports facilities in youth centres, especially from the perspective of young people].
articles.abstract: According to Social Code Book VIII § 11, institutions of open child and youth work in Germany are a place of child and youth welfare where the interests of young people are in the foreground. Young people use this place in a self-organized way to practice sports.This article provides an overview of elected findings of the state of research on sport in open child and youth work, beginning with a look at the official child and youth welfare statistics (2021) and the youth centre survey by the German Youth Institute (2018). Based on this, the focus of this article is on the results of a qualitative, subject-oriented interview study conducted in 2023 as part of the "Move for health project" and a quantitative online survey of adolescents. It is shown how sport is practiced by young people in institutions of open child and youth work and what significance it has for them.

articles.title: [Physical activity and mental health in childhood and adolescence: a summary of the evidence from three national studies].
articles.abstract: Young people are increasingly burdened by global crises. Physical activity (PA) is considered a key factor for mental health; however, for Germany, an integrated synthesis of population-based evidence is still lacking. The aim of this narrative overview is therefore to consolidate current findings on the association between PA and mental health.The analysis draws on three population-based studies conducted as module or follow-up studies in cooperation with the KiGGS study: the MoMo study (motor performance/physical activity), the BELLA and COPSY studies (mental health), and the COMO study (interdisciplinary integration). Nationwide representative samples of children and adolescents aged 4 to 23 years were examined using validated instruments to assess PA and mental health. Findings are synthesised narratively and reported by type of activity, age, sex and socioeconomic status.Overall, positive associations between PA and mental health are observed. Higher levels of PA are associated with fewer psychological problems and higher health-related quality of life. There is evidence of protective effects, particularly in relation to leisure-time sport, both within and outside sports clubs. Self-reported PA shows stronger associations with well-being than objectively measured PA. Children from socioeconomically disadvantaged families are less likely to be physically active and experience more mental health problems. Social integration and sense of competence in sport have been identified as further key psychosocial factors. PA can therefore be considered an important resource for promoting mental health. There is a need to promote low-threshold access to physical activity programmes that specifically target disadvantaged groups in order to reduce health inequalities.

articles.title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)].

RESULTS: At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Gaps in awareness of metabolic liver disease among high-risk populations in the United States.
Prospective comparative assessment of liver stiffness and steatosis between iLivTouch and FibroScan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease currently represents the leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. FibroScan and iLivTouch are 2 devices that employ similar principles to estimate liver steatosis and fibrosis, although few studies have directly compared their results.

AIM: To evaluate the concordance of 2 transient elastography devices for the estimation of liver steatosis and fibrosis.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted. Each participant underwent liver elastography with both devices consecutively under standardized conditions. Clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical variables were collected. The diagnostic accuracy of iLivTouch was calculated using FibroScan and noninvasive scores as references.

RESULTS: A total of 1004 patients were enrolled, with a median body mass index of 25.7 kg/m2 [IQR=23.6-28.7]. Median of attenuation values was 250 dB/m [IQR=214-291] with FibroScan, 262 dB/m [IQR=239-310] with iLivTouch. Median liver stiffness measurements were 4.1 kPa [IQR=3.4-4.8] for FibroScan and 6.2 kPa [IQR=5.5-7.1] for iLivTouch. Bland-Altman analysis revealed mean differences of -19.45±49.62 dB/m for steatosis and -2.43±2.51 kPa for stiffness. Using FibroScan (>269 dB/m) as the reference, iLivTouch ≥244 dB/m demonstrated 90% sensitivity for detecting liver steatosis. The correlation between the FAST scores of the 2 devices was very strong (rho=0.90, p≤0.0001).

CONCLUSION: iLivTouch serves as an effective alternative to assess liver fibrosis and steatosis in the general population, including overweight and obese individuals.

articles.title: Effects of the GnRH agonist leuprorelin on liver volume in premenopausal women with severe polycystic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is characterized by multiple liver cysts, sometimes leading to severe liver enlargement, with associated physical and psychosocial complaints. Treatment options are limited. Female gender is a risk factor for PLD; estrogen supplementation increases liver size in women with PLD, whereas the polycystic liver decreases after menopause. Estrogens may therefore be a target for therapy.

METHODS: In this prospective, open-label study, premenopausal women aged 18-45 years with severe PLD were randomized 1:1 to a direct start of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist leuprorelin (n=6) or to standard care with delayed start of leuprorelin 18 months after randomization (n=8). The gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (11.25 mg injections once every 3 mo) leads to a reduction in estrogens and progesterone, and consequently to medically induced menopause. The primary outcome was liver growth rate at 18 months. Secondary outcomes comprised quality of life, menopausal side effects, and adverse events. An interim analysis was performed when all participants had reached month 18, as notable side effects were expressed.

RESULTS: In the group with direct start of leuprorelin, liver volume still increased in half of the participants, with the median liver growth rate not significantly different from the standard care group (4.04 [-4.62 to 6.84] vs. 11.0 [0.70-13.2] %/year, respectively, p=0.15). Importantly, PLD-related quality of life did not improve with treatment, whereas menopausal side effects were severe, leading one participant to stop treatment early. The total number of adverse events in the direct versus standard care group was 38 versus 9, respectively (p<0.001). Because of these results, the study was terminated early.

CONCLUSIONS: leuprorelin treatment did not reverse liver volume, while menopausal side effects and adverse events were substantial.

articles.title: Enhanced liver fibrosis score is associated with cognitive performance during an 11-year follow-up period.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with poorer cognitive performance and greater cognitive decline. However, the liver-brain axis and the role of liver health in cognitive decline are still poorly understood. Thus, using both cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, we aimed to study how liver fibrosis score (ELF), an indicator of liver fibrosis, is associated with cognitive performance.

METHODS: This study was based on the Health 2000 Survey and its follow-up, the Health 2011 survey, which collected data from a nationally representative sample of the Finnish adult population. At baseline, verbal fluency, wordlist learning, delayed wordlist recall, and simple and multiple-choice reaction time tests were conducted. At follow-up, all tests except the reaction time tests were repeated. A global z-score was derived from the individual cognitive domains. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to study the association between ELF and cognitive performance while adjusting for demographic, metabolic, and cardiovascular covariates.

RESULTS: Cross-sectionally (n=5115; mean age 53.2 y; 58.6% women), high ELF was associated with poorer global cognition and slower simple and multiple-choice reaction times compared with low ELF. High ELF was also associated with worse global cognition and performance in the wordlist learning test, both cross-sectionally and longitudinally (n=2490; mean age 48.7 y at baseline; 58.0% women).

DISCUSSION: High ELF, an indicator of liver fibrosis, was associated with poorer global cognition both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. Worse performance was observed in cognitive domains that reflect poorer processing speed and executive function, verbal learning, attention, and working memory.
