These results imply that liver fibrosis could represent an early modifiable marker of cognitive vulnerability.

articles.title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. The studies were categorized into five distinct groups: prediction of disease or mortality, replication of established measures, segmentation of cardiac chambers, classification of chamber views, and assessment of image quality. High heterogeneity that could not be resolved was observed in studies focusing on cardiac chamber segmentation and classification. Model performance was influenced by a variety of different factors, including medical target and input characteristics such as video resolution, number of frames used, and total participants included during training.

CONCLUSION: DL models achieve high performance across various applications in echocardiography. In selected tasks, they may reduce reliance on expert input and support greater automation of echocardiographic workflows. However, further validation, assessment of clinical utility, and evaluation in real-world settings are required before widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Polyomavirus Drives Cerebellar Lesions in AIDS Monkeys With Ataxia.
articles.abstract: Cognitive and motor dysfunction occurs in 30%-50% of people with HIV/AIDS. Within this clinical spectrum, HIV-associated ataxia is an uncommon but debilitating disorder with poorly defined neuropathological mechanisms. This study investigated two rhesus macaques with chronic simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection that developed progressive ataxia, characterized by postural imbalance and nystagmus. Comparative neuropathological profiling of cerebellar tissue from ataxic SIV-infected macaques, non-ataxic SIV-infected macaques, and uninfected controls revealed that ataxia was associated with diffuse cerebellar atrophy, disrupted tissue organization, Purkinje cell degeneration, demyelination, glial nodule formation, and prominent microglial neuroinflammation. Cerebellar infection with simian polyomavirus 40 (SV40), a member of the Polyomaviridae family, was identified as the cause of the lesions, with viral tropism primarily involving cerebellar granule neurons. Mechanistically, SV40 infection induced neuronal pyroptosis and inflammatory cytokine release, promoting microglial recruitment and activation, amplifying local neuroinflammation, and culminating in nodular aggregate formation. Collectively, these findings establish SV40 infection as a direct driver of cerebellar pathology in SIV-associated ataxia and define a pathogenic sequence linking granule neuron pyroptosis, microglial activation, and progressive cerebellar injury-a cascade that may parallel polyomavirus-induced ataxia in people living with HIV-1.

articles.title: The Role of Astrocytes in the Inflammatory Response in Neurodiseases.
articles.abstract: Astrocytes have emerged as central regulators of neuroinflammation, extending far beyond their traditional roles as structural and metabolic support cells. In neurological disorders, astrocytes undergo reactive remodeling that encompasses morphological, transcriptional, metabolic, and functional changes. Rather than fitting into a fixed A1/A2 dichotomy, reactive astrocytes exist along a disease-, region-, and stage-dependent continuum shaped by local pathology and intercellular crosstalk. This review summarizes how astrocytes contribute to neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, central nervous system injury, infection, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder. We highlight convergent mechanisms, including cytokine and chemokine release, complement activation, glutamate and ion homeostasis disruption, oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming, and blood-brain barrier regulation, while emphasizing disease-specific astrocytic programs. We further discuss astrocyte interactions with microglia, neurons, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and peripheral immune cells, as well as key regulatory pathways, epigenetic remodeling, and lipid-dependent metabolic signaling. Finally, we evaluate current and emerging astrocyte-targeted therapeutic strategies, including metabolic modulation, receptor targeting, gene editing, nanodelivery, and gut-brain axis interventions. Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: [Branchial cleft anomalies of the neck : Embryology, clinical presentation, and management].
articles.abstract: Branchial cleft anomalies are the second most common congenital neck lesion. They present as cysts, sinuses, or fistulas arising from remnants of the pharyngeal apparatus; second arch anomalies predominate. The embryologic origin determines their anatomical relationships to nerves, vessels, and the pharynx and guides diagnosis and surgical planning. Typical findings are cervical swelling, cutaneous discharge, or recurrent infection. Third and fourth branchial anomalies may cause recurrent neck abscesses or acute suppurative thyroiditis, particularly in children. Ultrasonography is the primary imaging modality. Complete excision during a non-acute inflammatory interval remains the treatment of choice. Endoscopic treatments have become established as the first-line approach for pyriform sinus tract anomalies due to lower morbidity. Branchio-oto-renal syndrome should be considered in patients with ear malformations, hearing impairment, or renal abnormalities.

articles.title: Functional disability, diabetes and hypertension among adults in the United States, August 2021-August 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe diabetes and hypertension prevalence, diagnosis status and measured-threshold outcomes by functional disability.

METHODS: We analyzed the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted in the United States during August 2021-August 2023. Adults aged 18 years or older were classified using six Washington Group functioning domains. Outcome-specific weights and direct age standardization were used. Disability-minus-no-disability differences and 95% confidence intervals accounted for the complex survey design.

RESULTS: Among 8101 adults with complete functioning data, total diabetes and hypertension were classifiable in 5974 and 6172. Standardized total-disease differences were 9.3 percentage points (5.8, 12.7) for diabetes and 8.3 (3.1, 13.6) for hypertension. Undiagnosed-disease differences among eligible adults were 0.6 (-0.4, 1.7) and -3.4 (-7.2, 0.5), respectively. Among hypertension cases with known diagnosis status, the undiagnosed fraction was lower with disability: -14.1 (-19.9, -8.3). Conditional diabetes estimates were imprecise and sensitive to sparse younger-age cells.

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with functional disability had higher standardized total diabetes and hypertension prevalence. Diagnosis-status and measured-threshold findings depended on the condition and denominator; they do not establish equivalent care or explain the origins of prevalence differences.

articles.title: Caring for a patient with Fournier gangrene.
articles.abstract: Fournier gangrene (FG) is a form of necrotizing fasciitis that affects the genital and perineal tissues. This life-threatening condition is most often caused by a polymicrobial bacterial infection of the tissues. Predisposing factors include obesity, advanced age, chronic alcohol abuse, and immunosuppression. Although rare, FG can be life-threatening and can significantly impact the patient's quality of life. Adept nursing care can improve patient outcomes. This article discusses the pathophysiology and common complications of FG and outlines expected nursing considerations for patients with this type of infection.

articles.title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy Study of Porcine and Rabbit Antithymocyte Globulin in the Treatment of Patients With Severe Aplastic Anemia: A Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized, Open-Label Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a T lymphocyte-mediated bone marrow failure disorder. Only porcine ATG (p-ATG) and rabbit ATG (r-ATG) are available in mainland China, with the optimal first-line regimen undetermined. This study compared their pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Ninety-three SAA patients ineligible for transplantation or lacking a suitable donor (p-ATG, n = 55; r-ATG, n = 38) who were receiving immunosuppressive therapy were prospectively enrolled between 2020 and 2024. The primary endpoint was dynamic changes in lymphocyte subsets. Both ATGs peaked on treatment Day 5; r-ATG cleared significantly faster, with comparable peak active concentrations. The p-ATG group showed a stable early neutrophil increase, whereas the r-ATG group had an initial decline, with comparable recovery at 1 month. The r-ATG group exhibited prolonger lymphopenia, lower CD3+/CD4+ T cells, reduced Treg cells, and higher CD19+ B-cell proportions. IL-10 was significantly elevated on day 2 after ATG administration. At 6 months, the CRR was 18.87% with p-ATG and 18.92% with r-ATG; ORR was 69.81% with p-ATG and 56.76% with r-ATG. Two-year ORR and overall survival were similar, with no significant differences in infection or serum sickness. P-ATG and r-ATG have distinct pharmacokinetic and immunomodulatory but comparable efficacy and safety profiles, supporting interchangeable use in clinical practice.

articles.title: Bulk peripheral-blood transcriptomic analysis identifies a STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid immunosuppressive signature in sepsis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Sepsis involves immune dysregulation with myeloid activation and impaired antigen presentation. This study identified a compact immunosuppressive transcriptional signature associated with signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and arginase 1 (ARG1) using public peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets. GSE28750, including 10 sepsis samples and 20 healthy controls, was used for discovery; GSE65682, including 120 sepsis-related baseline/ICU-admission samples and 40 healthy controls, was used for external validation. Differential expression, enrichment, ssGSEA, and correlation analyses were performed in GSE28750, whereas candidate-gene directionality and composite-signature performance were reproduced in GSE65682. Differential expression analysis identified 482 genes, with 301 upregulated and 181 downregulated. Representative STAT3/ARG1-associated myeloid and immunoregulatory genes were upregulated, whereas HLA-DRA and HLA-DRB1 were downregulated. Enrichment analysis highlighted myeloid activation, IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, arginine metabolism, and impaired antigen processing and presentation. Sepsis samples had higher myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC)-like scores than controls (0.72 ± 0.21 vs. -0.36 ± 0.18, P = 1.1 × 10 - 7). The composite signature showed exploratory diagnostic performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.94 and 0.88 in the discovery and validation cohorts, respectively. This study provides a reproducible bioinformatic framework and candidate transcriptional signature for assessing sepsis-related myeloid immunosuppressive remodeling.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05087-1.

articles.title: Renal Abscess Secondary to Urinary Tract Obstruction Caused by Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Report of Two Cases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic organ prolapse can cause urinary tract obstruction, leading to hydronephrosis, pyelonephritis, and in rare cases, renal abscess.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report two elderly women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse who developed renal abscesses. Both presented with pyelonephritis and acute renal impairment accompanied by bilateral hydronephrosis. Imaging demonstrated poorly enhanced renal lesions consistent with renal abscess. Infection was successfully controlled with antimicrobial therapy, followed by surgical correction. Renal function improved, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Advanced pelvic organ prolapse can cause severe urinary tract obstruction, leading to pyelonephritis and, in rare cases, renal abscess. Early recognition of advanced pelvic organ prolapse and urinary dysfunction, prompt infection control, and timely surgical management are essential to prevent serious complications.

articles.title: Structure-based development of Glypican-3-targeting peptide candidates for hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains highly lethal, and extracellular GPC3 provides a tumor-associated surface target for structure-guided peptide design. This study established an entirely in silico workflow for de novo discovery and prioritization of GPC3-targeting peptide candidates using the human GPC3 structure from Protein Data Bank entry 7ZAW. W260, Y264, and M269 were selected as coordinate-resolved hotspot residues. A single 100 ns apo-GPC3 simulation was performed, and the centroid of the most populated cluster, accounting for 35.6% of the stable trajectory, was used for downstream design. RFdiffusion generated 100 peptide backbones near the hotspot surface, and ProteinMPNN generated a nonredundant peptide sequence library from the retained backbones. PepPAP was used as a sequence-level prediction model to rank candidates by its model output, which was treated as a relative computational prediction value rather than an experimentally measured binding free energy. The top 120 PepPAP-ranked sequences were refined with Rosetta FlexPepDock, generating 600 receptor-peptide poses, of which 565 satisfied the applied geometry/contact criteria. The top 30 docked peptides were evaluated using in silico solubility and toxicity predictors; 21 passed both filters. Integrated ranking identified five final priority candidates with Rosetta interface energies from - 20.459 to -18.255 REU. These peptides are computationally prioritized candidates for future experimental validation.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05092-4.

articles.title: Global and Regional Risk Factors for Vision Impairment in 2020 and Multi-decadal Trends 1990-2020: A Meta-Analysis and Visual Display Based on Prevalence Data From the Global Burden of Disease study and Vision Loss Expert Group.
authors: Vision Loss Expert Group of the Global Burden of Disease Study
articles.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate global and regional risk factors for blindness and vision impairment pertaining to all geographical locations between 1990 and 2020.

METHODS: (1) Twenty-four covariates were selected with a potential link to vision impairment from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) Covariates database as predictive factors. (2) From these, the linear association was investigated, with crude and age-standardised prevalence estimates of blindness and distance and near vision impairment in 2020 by using data for the whole population, sex and 5-year age groups, and by stratifying severity through mild, moderate, severe and total impairment. (3) Analysis investigated whether percentage rates of change in risk factors were associated with rates of change in prevalence in 1990-2020.

RESULTS: For adults (50+ years), for crude and age-standardised vision loss prevalence estimates for the year 2020, a significant negative association of smoking prevalence was found initially for all persons and for each sex, which appears to be due to ecological confounding and became a positive association using more granular regional and age group data. Maternal care and immunisation, sanitation proportion, Health Access and Quality Index and Socio-demographic Index were other significant age-standardised negative associations. Ophthalmologists/million population had a weak but significant protective effect, and positive associations were found for pollution (outdoor and indoor), stronger for greater vision impairment severities. Years in education per capita were weakly, negatively associated with vision loss prevalence, yet zero education proportion had a stronger but positive association for both sexes.

CONCLUSIONS: This study confirmed associations at population level globally, which appear to be stable over decades. In addition, the study quantified the contribution of epidemiologically-based risk factors to vision loss at a GBD super-regional level, which is novel. This opens useful avenues for targeted intervention by policymakers. For example, reduction in sex inequity in blindness rates over 30 years has been positively associated with reducing overall prevalence of blindness.

articles.title: Effects of Single-Session High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (HD-tACS) Combined with Robot-Assisted Hand Exercises on Corticospinal Excitability in Chronic Stroke.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This preliminary study investigated whether a single session of high-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) could improve corticospinal tract (CST) excitability compared with sham stimulation in healthy individuals and individuals with chronic stroke.

DESIGN: Twelve healthy adults and 7 individuals with chronic stroke received active and sham HD-tACS over the primary motor cortex (M1) flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) hotspot, ipsilesional in stroke subjects, for 30 minutes at 2mA and 21 Hz in a randomized crossover design. All subjects performed robot-assisted grasp-and-open hand exercises during active and sham stimulation.

RESULTS: HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in the healthy group (15.3%). In the stroke group, FDS MEP amplitudes were increased by ∼22.3% after HD-tACS, but this change was not statistically significant. When MEP amplitudes were normalized as percentage change, HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in both groups compared with the sham condition. No significant extensor digitorum communis (EDC) modulation was observed in either group.

CONCLUSION: HD-tACS combined with robot-assisted hand exercises may enhance CST excitability compared with robot-assisted hand exercises alone after a single session in both healthy and stroke subjects. However, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Turning down the ammonia dial: Phase 2a evidence for YAQ007 in cirrhosis.
A gentler squeeze: A first signal from OCE-205, a selective V1a mixed agonist-antagonist for hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury.
Key Predictors of Cerebral Vasospasm Following Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening condition often leading to complications such as cerebral vasospasm, which causes delayed cerebral ischemia and increases mortality. In intensive care, early identification of vasospasm risk factors by nurses is essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: We sought to review and synthesize evidence on risk factors associated with cerebral vasospasm after SAH and inform early risk assessment and nursing care strategies in intensive care.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies. A comprehensive search was conducted on August 30 to 31, 2024, across 8 databases. Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist and the Risk of Bias (RoB 2.0) tool.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies were included in the systematic review, of which 27 were included in the meta-analysis, involving 19 033 patients. Clinical severity measures were most strongly associated with cerebral vasospasm, including Modified Fisher grade (odds ratio (OR) = 2.88; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.04-4.07), Fisher grade (OR = 2.27; 95% CI, 1.91-2.69), and hemodynamic status (OR = 2.56; 95% CI, 1.17-5.59). Aneurysm-related factors and comorbid conditions were associated with increased risk of cerebral vasospasm, whereas clinical biomarkers and inflammatory markers showed relatively smaller effect sizes.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical severity scales and hemodynamic status are the strongest predictors of cerebral vasospasm following SAH. These findings support early risk stratification and the implementation of structured monitoring strategies to improve patient outcomes.PROSPERO trial registration number:CRD42024605605 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024605605).

articles.title: Atrial cardiomyopathy: from knowledge gaps to clinical impact : The role of the EmbRACE Network.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is increasingly recognised as an underlying atrial substrate contributing to atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), and cardio-embolic stroke. However, diagnostic criteria, disease thresholds, and targeted treatment strategies remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the rationale, structure, and translational strategy of the EmbRACE (Electro-Molecular Basis and the theRapeutic management of Atrial Cardiomyopathy, fibrillation and associated outcomEs) network, a national consortium established to address key knowledge gaps in AtCM.

METHODS: EmbRACE integrates mechanistic research, computational modelling, clinical trials, and implementation science within seven interconnected work packages. Human atrial tissue biobanking and deep phenotyping (WP1) enable molecular profiling of candidate pathways (WP2), which are validated in experimental models (WP3). Computational modelling and artificial intelligence (WP4) integrate multimodal clinical and biological data to derive composite AtCM phenotypes and severity frameworks. Substrate-targeting clinical trials evaluate AF ablation (RACE X; WP5), weight reduction using GLP‑1 agonists (DUTCH-WAIST; WP6), and optimised rate control using calcium channel antagonists (SMART-VERAPAF; WP6). Implementation science (WP7) focuses on guideline integration, decision-support tools, and governance of AI-based risk models. EmbRACE establishes a translational pipeline from mechanistic discovery to clinical application. By integrating tissue-level insights with multimodal risk modelling and interventional trials, the consortium aims to define clinically meaningful AtCM thresholds, to validate indirect markers, and to determine whether targeted treatment modifies disease progression and clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: EmbRACE provides a multidisciplinary framework to transform AtCM from a theoretical construct into a clinically actionable entity, enabling earlier detection, improved risk stratification, and AtCM-directed therapy in cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy : Statement of endorsement by the NVVC.
articles.journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
articles.abstract: This article contextualises the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for managing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and pregnancy in the Netherlands. The guideline addendum provides additional recommendations for situations where the ESC guidelines may not fully align with Dutch clinical practice. By endorsing the ESC guidelines through this addendum, the Netherlands Society of Cardiology (Nederlandse Vereniging Voor Cardiologie) supports its members in adhering to evidence-based management strategies for CVD and pregnancy.

articles.title: Hepatocyte senescence in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a major global health challenge, with particularly high morbidity and disease burden. Cellular senescence has been identified as one of the core mechanisms driving the onset and progression of MASLD. Hepatocytes, the primary functional cells of the liver, can undergo a senescent state under metabolic stress. These senescent hepatocytes secrete a series of pro-inflammatory and profibrotic factors, directly exacerbating hepatic inflammation and activating hepatic stellate cells, thereby leading to pathological fibrosis. The purpose of this review is to explore the key molecular pathways of hepatocyte senescence and their impact on MASLD progression. Finally, we discuss relevant intervention strategies that can be used for the prevention and treatment of MASLD.

articles.title: Lower circulating angiotensinogen levels across ACLD stages are associated with hepatic dysfunction and mortality.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The liver produces angiotensinogen (AGT), the key upstream precursor of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). We measured AGT levels in patients across distinct advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) stages and investigated the impact of AGT levels on clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We included clinically stable ACLD outpatients undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement between May 2018 and October 2023, as well as healthy controls (HCs) recruited in the prospective Vienna Cirrhosis Study (VICIS; NCT03267615). AGT was assessed by converting it to angiotensin I (Ang I) through incubation with excess recombinant human renin. RAS parameters were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Patients were stratified as compensated (cACLD), single decompensated (sdACLD), or further decompensated ACLD (fdACLD).

RESULTS: Overall, 60 individuals (cACLD: n=16; sdACLD: n=22; fdACLD: n=12; HC: n=10) were included. AGT levels decreased significantly compared with HC and with increasing ACLD severity (HC: 943.2 vs. cACLD: 550.4 vs. sdACLD: 476.9 vs. fdACLD: 439.8 nmol/L; p<0.001). In contrast, plasma concentrations of Ang II (cACLD: 23.1 vs. sdACLD: 156.0 vs. fdACLD: 162.4 pmol/L; p=0.002) and Ang 1-7 (cACLD: 3.0 vs. sdACLD: 3.2 vs. fdACLD: 8.5 pmol/L; p=0.022) increased significantly with ACLD severity. AGT did not correlate with Ang II (ρ=-0.23; p=0.101), but with Ang 1-7 (ρ=0.32; p=0.022) and MELD-Na (ρ=-0.29; p=0.042). Exploratory survival analyses, limited by the small sample size, showed that lower AGT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted for age and MELD-Na: asHR: 1.59; 95% CI: 1.09-2.27; p=0.012/adjusted for age and albumin: asHR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.05-2.21; p=0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: AGT levels decreased in ACLD, correlated with hepatic dysfunction, and were linked to all-cause mortality in exploratory survival analyses. Still, classical and alternative RAS parameters increased in parallel to ACLD severity.

articles.title: Patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes in refractory ascites secondary to cirrhosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory ascites (RA) secondary to advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) results in poor health-related quality of life (HRQL), high symptom burden, and caregiver workload. Patient/caregiver-reported outcomes (PROs) remain uncharacterized in this cohort. This review summarises the available evidence on this topic.

METHODS: MEDLINE/Embase/Cochrane/PsycINFO/Web of Science/CINAHL were searched for articles that included PROs in RA secondary to ACLD. A structured narrative synthesis and a meta-analysis were undertaken.

RESULTS: Sixteen articles were included, comprising 1040 patients and 47 caregivers. Fourteen PRO measures were used, most commonly the Short Form-36 (SF-36) and the Chronic Liver Disease Questionnaire (CLDQ). Domain scores were pooled from 4 SF-36 and 3 CLDQ studies. Pooled domain scores were lower than those reported in stable outpatients with cirrhosis in 3/8 SF-36 domains: Social functioning (mean difference -18.8 [95% CI: -30.2 to -7.3]), Mental health (-17.9 [-33.5 to -2.3]), and Physical functioning (-13.6 [-24.5 to -2.7]); and 4/6 CLDQ domains: Abdominal symptoms (-1.5 [-2.3 to -0.7]), Activity (-0.9 [-1.4 to -0.5]), Worry (-1.2 [-2.1 to -0.3]), and Emotional function (-0.7 [-1.3 to -0.1]). Disease-specific tools had broader domain coverage and were more sensitive at picking up impairments in HRQL compared with generic ones. One symptom tool (the Ascites Questionnaire) had been validated in RA. The Short-Form Liver Disease Quality of Life questionnaire (SFLDQoL), the only HRQL measure validated in decompensated ACLD, was used once. Only 2 studies assessed informal caregivers.

CONCLUSIONS: RA in ACLD detrimentally impacts HRQL across multiple domains. However, the lack of validated tools remains a barrier to assessing PROs and conducting well-designed RCTs in this cohort. This review highlights potential domains for the future development of such tools, which could drive equitable, patient-centered care in ACLD.

articles.title: Clinical and patient-reported predictors of days alive and out of hospital in decompensated cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Days alive and out of hospital (DAOH) is a patient-centered outcome, but has not been studied in decompensated cirrhosis (DCC). We aimed to quantify DAOH and to identify clinical and patient-reported factors associated with DAOH.

METHODS: Using an ongoing prospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with DCC, DAOH was calculated by subtracting days hospitalized, transplanted, or deceased from 90 days post-discharge from index hospitalization. Univariable and multivariable negative binomial hurdle models were used to identify clinical and patient-reported variables associated with DAOH, where DAOH was treated both as a categorical (any readmission, transplant, death vs. all 90-DAOH) and continuous (proportion of event days) outcome.

RESULTS: Among 363 adults (median age 54 y; MELD 3.0 score 23), 40% experienced all 90-DAOH while 90-day readmission, death, and transplant occurred in 49%, 21%, 11%, respectively. Mean DAOH was 68.3 (SD: 29.0). In multivariable models, transplant evaluation status (listed vs. not listed/evaluated: OR 7.55, p=0.004) was associated with experiencing an event within 90 days. In comparison, when considering the number of event days, higher PROMIS Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities scores were independently associated with a lower proportion of event days (rate ratio, RR 0.91 per 3-point increase, p=0.030) in addition to MELD 3.0 >25 (vs. <15, RR 2.75, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DAOH is a holistic, patient-centered outcome for decompensated cirrhosis that integrates readmission, transplantation, and mortality into a single measure of post-discharge burden. By using DAOH and moving beyond readmissions, we show that lower MELD 3.0 and higher patient-reported social well-being were independently associated with more days at home after hospitalization.

articles.title: Impact of body composition on clinical outcomes in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormalities in body composition are common in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, their impact across different treatment modalities remains poorly understood. We systematically reviewed the prognostic value of body composition in patients with HCC, stratified by curative, locoregional, and systemic therapies.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (January 2015-March 2025) for studies reporting associations between CT/MRI or bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-assessed body composition and outcomes in HCC.

RESULTS: Ninety-two studies were included (35 curative, 10 locoregional, 39 systemic, 8 mixed). Sarcopenia prevalence ranged from 6.4% to 62.8% (median study-level prevalence 38%-50% depending on treatment stratum). Sarcopenia independently predicted worse overall survival across all strata: curative (HR 1.52-3.76), locoregional (HR 1.72-2.51), and systemic therapies (HR 1.34-2.20). Sarcopenic obesity conferred the highest risk in the curative setting (HR up to 3.15). In systemic therapy, myosteatosis independently predicted mortality (HR 1.45-2.01), whereas visceral adiposity was protective (HR 0.56-0.66). In a random-effects meta-analysis of 44 studies, sarcopenia was associated with a pooled HR of 1.85 (95% CI 1.75-1.94; I2=0%), with consistent effects across curative (HR 1.86), locoregional (HR 2.10), and systemic strata (HR 1.71). Sarcopenia also predicted recurrence after curative treatment (pooled HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.61-1.82; k=14).

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia predicts mortality in HCC, independently of treatment modality. Visceral adiposity appears detrimental after curative treatment but may be paradoxically protective during systemic therapy. Body composition should be integrated into clinical decision-making in HCC, though a clear consensus on measurement standardization is needed.

articles.title: Shock Synopsis November 2026.
Machine learning-driven discovery of TGFBR1 inhibitors from Mangifera indica for Atorvastatin-based antidiabetic therapy.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mangiferin, a C-glucosyl xanthone from Mangifera indica, has known antidiabetic activity, but the specific protein target underlying this activity, and its compatibility with existing antidiabetic drugs such as Atorvastatin, were not defined. In this work, machine learning, network pharmacology, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation identified and validated TGFBR1 as a novel molecular target of Mangiferin and evaluated a Mangiferin-Atorvastatin combination for diabetes therapy. A curated collection of TGFBR1 inhibitors from BindingDB was used to train several supervised learning models, with the best performance from Random Forest (94.68% accuracy, κ = 0.8981) and robust external validation (79.35%) on 868 unseen compounds. Screening of 545 M. indica phytochemicals with this model identified Mangiferin, Fisetin, Isochinomin, Mangiferolic acid, and Astragalin as high-confidence TGFBR1 inhibitors. Network pharmacology identified TGF-β as the most central protein in the interaction network (cumulative score 350), and molecular docking showed that Mangiferin forms stable hydrogen bonds with SER-287, ILE-211, and GLU-208 at the TGFBR1 binding site, together with hydrophobic contacts. This binding pose remained structurally stable (RMSD 1.50-1.75 Å) over 100 nanoseconds of molecular dynamics simulation, with ligand-residue occupancy > 85%. ADMET profiling showed favorable drug-likeness (Lipinski compliance, low predicted toxicity) with a moderate permeability limitation (TPSA 201.28 Å²), and DFT analysis showed a HOMO-LUMO gap of 2.85937 eV, supporting antioxidant activity. In cultured cells, Atorvastatin combined with Mangiferin increased apoptosis through the mitochondrial pathway (Bcl-xL downregulation, BAK upregulation, cytochrome c release, caspase-7/8 activation) and enhanced insulin sensitivity, shown by increased glucose uptake (2-NBDG assay) and higher GLUT-4 and pIRS-1(Tyr896) expression. In high-fat diet-fed rats, Atorvastatin plus Mangiferin given for 24 weeks significantly improved glucose tolerance and reduced HbA1c, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and random blood sugar relative to untreated high-fat diet controls, with preserved pancreatic architecture and increased muscle GLUT-4 expression. These findings identify TGFBR1 as a plausible molecular target of Mangiferin and provide a mechanistic rationale for the Mangiferin-Atorvastatin combination as a candidate antidiabetic therapy.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05088-0.

articles.title: Moyamoya disease presenting as galactorrhea.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular condition marked by carotid narrowing and collateral vessel formation. Patients are often diagnosed after a stroke, but here we describe a case of galactorrhea as the presenting symptom of MMD. A 30-year-old gravida 1, para 0 woman noted milky, nonbloody discharge leaking from both breasts after manual compression during sexual intercourse. Prolactin was mildly elevated at 29.4 ng/mL (SI [International System of Units]: 29.4 µg/L) (reference range, 3-23.1 ng/mL [SI: 3-23.1 µg/L]). Magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary gland showed no microadenoma but incidentally revealed a tortuous right internal carotid artery compressing the pituitary, raising the possibility of vascular compression contributing to galactorrhea and mild hyperprolactinemia. Magnetic resonance angiography and catheter angiography confirmed MMD. Mild cognitive impairment, persistent headaches, and secondary hypertension eventually necessitated neurosurgical revascularization. After surgery, the patient experienced a significant reduction in symptoms although challenges with memory and headaches have persisted. This case underscores the importance of brain imaging in evaluating hyperprolactinemia and highlights the potential for endocrinologic sequelae when MMD involves vessels in proximity to the pituitary gland.

articles.title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia.
articles.abstract: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m2). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.2 µg/24 hours; <166 nmol/24 hours), and unsuppressed adrenocorticotropic hormone of 19.1 pg/mL (4.2 pmol/L; reference range: 7.3-63.1 pg/mL; 1.6-13.9 pmol/L). The cortisol level after the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test was 23.9 µg/dL (659 nmol/L; reference range: <1.8 µg/dL; <50 nmol/L). Cortisol remained markedly elevated after nasogastric feeding and weight restoration. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 4 mm left anterior pituitary lesion. High-dose dexamethasone suppression, corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation, and inferior petrosal sinus sampling confirmed a pituitary source of adrenocorticotropic hormone. The patient underwent transsphenoidal resection of a corticotroph adenoma. Eleven months later, her hypertension and restrictive eating behaviors had resolved, and her mood significantly improved. Cushing syndrome can coexist with anorexia nervosa, masking typical cushingoid features and presenting with psychiatric manifestations and weight loss. Persistent hypercortisolemia despite nutritional rehabilitation should prompt dynamic endocrine testing and pituitary evaluation to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Aortic coarctation and McArdle disease in histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome: expanding the SLC29A3 spectrum.
articles.abstract: Histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome (HLPS) is a rare inherited disorder caused by SLC29A3 variants. We report 2 Pakistani brothers with HLPS and markedly different clinical features despite identical genotypes. The 15-year-old had severe growth failure, facial dysmorphism, insulin-dependent diabetes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring balloon dilatation. Genetic testing identified SLC29A3 and PYGM variants, indicating concurrent HLPS and McArdle disease. His 20-year-old brother had insulin-dependent diabetes and celiac disease from age 3, later developing hypertension, proteinuria, and characteristic skin changes. This case highlights marked intrafamilial variability in HLPS and identifies CoA as a rare cardiovascular feature. It also supports comprehensive genetic testing in patients with early-onset diabetes and multisystem disease.

articles.title: Mycoplasma genitalium prevalence, bacterial load, and antibiotic resistance in paired vaginal and anal specimens from Chlamydia trachomatis-infected women.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) frequently co-infects women with Chlamydia trachomatis (CT), but the epidemiology and clinical significance of this association remain poorly understood. This study assessed MG positivity, antimicrobial resistance, mgpB genotyping and bacterial load in paired self-collected vaginal and anal swabs from 426 women with urogenital CT infection, and assessed the risk factors for CT/MG coinfection compared with CT monoinfection.

METHODS: MG detection and quantification were carried out using an in-house quantitative PCR targeting the MgPa adhesin gene. Macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance-associated mutations were determined by sequencing the 23S RNA gene and the parC gene, respectively. The mgpB types were determined by sequencing a 281-bp region of the mgpB gene. Clinical, demographic, and behavioural characteristics were compared between women with CT monoinfection and CT/MG coinfection.

RESULTS: MG was detected in 22.8% of women, more frequently in vaginal than anal specimens (18.5% vs 12.9%, p = 0.03). Among MG-positive women, 43.3% had vaginal-only infection, 18.6% anal-only infection, and 38.1% infection at both sites. Macrolide and fluoroquinolone resistance were detected in 16.7% and 9.1% of evaluable cases, respectively. Anal MG was usually asymptomatic and unrelated to reported anal intercourse. MG bacterial load was significantly higher in vaginal than anal samples, and paired specimens shared identical mgpB genotypes, supporting the hypothesis of secondary anal colonization from the vagina. Being born in France was the only factor associated with CT/MG coinfection, compared with CT monoinfection in the multivariate analysis. MG coinfection did not influence the CT bacterial load.

CONCLUSIONS: MG coinfection was common among women with CT infection but was not associated with higher CT bacterial load, more severe clinical manifestations, or distinct behavioural characteristics. Further studies are warranted to clarify the biological interactions between these two pathogens in women.

articles.title: Expanded Longitudinal Validation of Adaptive Learning Stability in AI-Assisted Neurosurgical Residency Training.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and robustness of Adaptive Learning Stability (ALS) within an expanded AI-assisted neurosurgical residency cohort during a 12-month observation cycle.

DESIGN: This was a prospective controlled educational study. Residents completed 4 consecutive quarterly checkpoints integrating cognitive, technical, and decision-making assessments over 12 months. The RCKaS-AI framework incorporated predictive analytics, individualized adaptive remediation, and mentor-validated feedback pathways. Primary analysis evaluated longitudinal entrustment trajectory stability across checkpoints. Secondary analyses included inter-resident variance dynamics, remediation frequency, faculty workload, and predictive agreement between forecasted and observed competency progression.

SETTING: Two accredited neurosurgical residency programs in Kazakhstan, from January 2025 to January 2026.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-four neurosurgical residents randomized into standard RCKaS (n = 32) and AI-enhanced RCKaS-AI (n = 32) cohorts.

RESULTS: Both cohorts demonstrated progressive improvement in entrustment scores across sequential checkpoints. In the RCKaS-AI cohort, mean entrustment scores increased from 59.1 ± 12.8 at CP1 to 94.3 ± 6.9 at CP4, compared with 58.4 ± 13.1 to 85.7 ± 10.4 under standard RCKaS conditions (p = 0.001). Inter-resident variance decreased by 41% in the AI-assisted cohort versus 18% in the standard cohort. Residents within the RCKaS-AI framework achieved entrustment level 4 significantly earlier than controls (38 ± 7 weeks vs 50 ± 9 weeks, p = 0.003). Mean remediation frequency decreased from 3.4 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 0.7 sessions per resident, while faculty workload declined by 34%. Predictive analytics demonstrated strong agreement between forecasted and observed competency trajectories (r = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77-0.89).

CONCLUSIONS: Expanded longitudinal implementation of the RCKaS-AI framework demonstrated reproducible stabilization of competency trajectories during neurosurgical residency training. These findings support the robustness of adaptive AI-assisted feedback systems as a practical mechanism for longitudinal competency regulation within structured surgical education programs. Further multicenter validation is required to evaluate external reproducibility across broader residency environments.

articles.title: Can't Name It, Can't Log Off: Alexithymia and Problematic Internet-Related Behaviors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Alexithymia has been proposed as a ransdiagnostic vulnerability for behavioral addictions, but its role in problematic Internet-related behaviors (PIB) has not been quantified across phenotypes and populations. We conducted a preregistered systematic review and meta-analysis following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses. Major databases were searched in October 2025 for studies reporting quantitative associations between alexithymia and PIB (problematic Internet, smartphone, social media, gaming use, or cyberbullying). Risk of bias was appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects models pooled correlations and standardized regression coefficients; three-level and robust-variance models accounted for multiple effects per study and examined moderators and adjustment for internalizing symptoms. Eighty-three studies met inclusion criteria; 78 independent samples (N = 42,478; 369 effect sizes total, comprising 302 zero-order correlations and 67 standardized regression coefficients) contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled correlation between alexithymia and PIB was r = 0.36 (95% confidence interval 0.34-0.38; I2 = 77.6%). Associations were stronger for addictive-use PIB (r = 0.37) than for cyberbullying (r = 0.29), broadly comparable across world regions, and tended to be larger in adults than adolescents. In multivariable models, coefficients attenuated from about β = 0.37 to β = 0.18 after controlling for depression, anxiety, and other internalizing symptoms, but remained statistically significant. Sensitivity and publication-bias analyses indicated that the association was robust. Alexithymia shows a moderate association with PIB across age groups, partly via shared variance with internalizing psychopathology but also through unique pathways. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies should test whether targeting emotional awareness can help prevent or reduce PIB.

articles.title: Evolving Sero-immunological Profiles of Solid Organ Transplant Candidates in Korea.
Incentivizing Faculty and Promoting Engagement in General Surgery Residency Entrustable Professional Activities Assessments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The American Board of Surgery (ABS) implemented Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) to facilitate transition to competency-based resident assessments in July 2023. To improve faculty engagement, our institution established an intervention with a required target of less than 25% expired faculty EPA assessments for the 2024 to 2025 academic year (AY) to qualify for a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form.

DESIGN: A retrospective review of de-identified institutional EPA data for the AYs 2023 to 2024, preintervention, and 2024 to 2025, postintervention, obtained from the ABS website was conducted. Faculty rater, division, activity name, phase of care, entrustability score, and narrative feedback were analyzed. Descriptive statistics were employed to assess EPA assessment volume, number of faculty raters and evaluations by division, expired assessments, and details by postgraduate training year (PGY). Chi-Square, 2-proportion z-tests, and paired t-tests were employed to compare pre and postintervention EPA assessment completion and qualities.

SETTING: Affiliate hospitals of the Medical College of Wisconsin including Froedtert Hospital, a tertiary referral center in Milwaukee; Clement J. Zablocki Veteran's Affairs Hospital; and 3 community hospitals in the Milwaukee area.

PARTICIPANTS: De-identified data from general surgery residents and faculty who completed any EPA assessment in AYs 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 were included.

RESULTS: A total of 1111 and 1464 EPA assessments were completed for the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 AYs, respectively, yielding a 1.32-fold increase post-intervention. There was a 1.27-fold increase in participating faculty raters (63 vs 80). Meaningful narrative feedback increased from 53.3% to 57.8% (p = 0.02). Of 11 service rotations with participating faculty raters, 5 met the <25% EPA assessment expiration metric in 2023 to 2024, compared to 8 in 2024 to 2025. The overall EPA assessment expiration rate decreased from 40.0% pre-intervention to 13.9% postintervention (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Incentivizing faculty to improve upon expired EPA assessments using a shortened end-of-rotation resident evaluation form increased EPA assessment completion, improved narrative feedback quality, and decreased expired EPA assessments. Initiatives to motivate faculty and residents to engage in timely and high-quality feedback will aid the ongoing transition to competency-based surgical education.

articles.title: Current review of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists and risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Emerging data has identified a potential association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a typically sudden, painless, and irreversible cause of optic nerve-mediated vision loss. This review synthesizes the current clinical, epidemiologic, and potential mechanism linking GLP-1RA-based therapies to NAION risk, informing balanced risk assessment and interdisciplinary clinical decision-making. A structured PubMed search was performed using terms including "GLP-1 receptor agonist," "semaglutide," "liraglutide," "tirzepatide," and "nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy," in addition to NAION risk factors, including disc-at-risk anatomy, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, renal disease, and ischemic heart disease. A small cup-to-disc ratio ("disc-at-risk") was found to be the most robust anatomical predictor of NAION. Systemic microvascular disease (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia) and conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea and end-stage renal disease were also linked to increased susceptibility to optic nerve head ischemia. Although data across electronic health records, national registries, and pharmacovigilance analyses suggest a very low absolute incidence of NAION, the use of GLP-1RAs demonstrates a statistically significant association with NAION development, yielding relative risk estimates between 1.2 and 4.3. At this time, the potential association between GLP-1RA therapy and NAION should be interpreted as a safety signal rather than a contraindication. Screening for disc-at-risk anatomy, consideration of prior NAION history, and patient counseling regarding acute visual symptoms may be warranted prior to initiation of therapy. As evidence evolves, collaboration between endocrinologists and ophthalmologists will be essential to support safe and effective patient care.

articles.title: Standardized postpartum blood pressure protocol and lower rates of hypertension at 6 weeks postpartum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) increase the risk of chronic hypertension (HTN) and cardiovascular (CV) disease later in life. It is unknown how strict blood pressure (BP) monitoring postpartum (PP) may affect rates of HTN at 6 weeks PP.

OBJECTIVE: We evaluate the effect of a PP HTN standardized clinical assessment and management plan (SCAMP) on HTN at 6 weeks PP.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study of patients with PP HTN at a quaternary care center for 6 months after enacting an institution-wide SCAMP. The prospective group was compared with historical controls who delivered prior to initiation of the SCAMP. The SCAMP included (1) initiation or uptitration of medication for any BP ≥150/100 or any 2 BPs ≥140/90 within a 24-h period with a goal of BP <140/90 12 h prior to discharge and (2) enrollment in a remote BP monitoring system upon discharge. Inclusion criteria were an existing diagnosis of chronic HTN or HDP and a documented BP at a 6-week PP visit. The primary outcome was HTN, defined as systolic BP (SBP) ≥140 or diastolic BP (DBP) ≥90, at 6 weeks PP. Secondary outcomes included mean BP values as measured in the outpatient setting at 6 weeks PP and use of anti-HTNs at the time of the 6-week PP visit. For all analyses, p values were two-way, and the level of statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Of 780 PP HTN patients in the prospective cohort study, 627 (80.4%) met inclusion criteria for the secondary analysis, 305 in the SCAMP cohort and 322 historical controls. The SCAMP cohort had lower rates of chronic HTN, more patients on anti-HTNs, and higher rate of nifedipine use. The primary outcome of HTN at 6 weeks PP was significantly lower in the SCAMP group (10.5% vs. 18.3%, p = 0.005). After adjusting for confounding variables, multivariable logistic regression showed that the SCAMP group had 38% reduced odds of HTN at 6 weeks PP compared to controls (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.38-0.996; p = 0.048). Mean SBP at 6 weeks PP was significantly lower in the SCAMP group (120 ± 12 vs. 124 ± 14 mmHg, p < 0.001), as was mean DBP (76 ± 8 vs. 81 ± 8 mmHg, p < 0.001). A subanalysis only including patients with diagnosed HDP and excluding those with only chronic HTN demonstrated similar findings.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of a SCAMP was associated with reduced rates of HTN at 6 weeks PP, with lower mean SBP and DBP. More data are needed to evaluate how these findings mitigate long-term HTN risk.

articles.title: Medical School Performance Evaluations (MSPEs) Lack Objectivity: A Challenge in the Surgery Residency Selection Process.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In the past several years, the methods used to evaluate medical students have undergone significant shifts. The United States Medical Licensing Examination Step 1 grading has become pass/fail, as has clinical grading at many institutions. Residency program directors have lamented the loss of objective data in applications.

OBJECTIVE: To assess and compare current practices of medical school performance evaluations among MD, DO, and Top 40 schools.

DESIGN: A retrospective review was performed of the Medical Student Performance Evaluations. Grading systems, formulas, and distribution for surgery clerkships were measured. Statistics were performed using Chi-square tests.

SETTING: This study was performed at a single general surgery residency program.

PARTICIPANTS: Medical schools associated with applications during the 2024 to 2025 application cycle to the residency program. Medical schools located within the United States, both MD and DO, were included. Medical school rankings were determined using the Blue Ridge Institute's 2024 Schools in Medicine report.

RESULTS: Applications were received from 138 MD schools and 26 DO schools. Seventy-six schools (46.3%) ranked the students, 143 (87.2%) graded clerkships, and 77 (47%) displayed the formula used for grading. Top 40 schools were less likely to use class rank (26.3% vs 52.4%, p < 0.01) or give clerkship grades (71.1% vs 92.1%, p < 0.001). For Top 40 schools, the shelf exam was less likely to constitute more than 40% of the clerkship grade (0% vs 27.1%, p < 0.05). These schools were more generous with grading, with no Top 40 schools bestowing less than 25% of their class honors (0% vs 27.4%, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: There is little available to distinguish academic performance in Medical Student Performance Evaluations and Top 40 medical schools are less discerning in the evaluation of medical students.

articles.title: Demographic and epidemiological patterns of reported malaria cases in Aseer Region, Saudi Arabia: An eight-year surveillance analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and public health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress toward malaria elimination in Saudi Arabia, imported infections continue to threaten re-establishment of transmission, particularly in southwestern regions. Aseer Region, contains diverse ecological settings that may support malaria vectors. This study examined the demographic and epidemiological characteristics of malaria cases reported in Aseer between 2016 and 2023.

METHODS: A retrospective surveillance analysis of malaria surveillance records was conducted using data from the Vector Diseases Control Unit of the Ministry of Health. All laboratory-confirmed malaria cases reported from January 2016 to December 2023 were included. Demographic variables and malaria species were analyzed. Cases were classified as imported, introduced, or local according to World Health Organization definitions. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed using R software, and spatial distribution was mapped using QGIS.

RESULTS: A total of 1254 laboratory-confirmed malaria cases were identified during the study period. Annual case numbers declined from 266 in 2016-63 in 2018 before increasing to 343 cases in 2023. Imported infections accounted for 799 cases (63.7%), followed by local (303, 24.2%) and introduced cases (152, 12.1%). Case classification varied significantly by year (χ²=570.54, df=14, p < 0.001). Males represented 84.4% of cases, and the median age was 26 years, with the highest burden among individuals aged 25-34 years (32.9%) and 15-24 years (31.0%). Non-Saudi nationals accounted for 65.1%, with Ethiopian, Sudanese, and Yemeni. Plasmodium falciparum was the predominant species (75.2%), followed by P. vivax (24.3%). In multivariable analysis, nationality and P. vivax infection were independently associated with importation-related malaria, whereas sex was not.

CONCLUSION: Malaria in Aseer during 2016-2023 was characterized by fluctuating incidence, increasing predominance of importation-related infections. Multivariable analysis identified non-Saudi nationality and P. vivax infection as factors associated with importation-related malaria. Sustained surveillance, targeted interventions for mobile populations, and continued vector control are essential to prevent re-establishment of indigenous malaria transmission and support national elimination goals.

articles.title: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT Detection of Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy in a Pediatric Patient With Neuroblastoma Following Anti-GD2 Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: A 5-year-old boy with high-risk neuroblastoma underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT as part of a clinical trial to assess treatment response after anti-GD2 immunotherapy. The scan showed symmetric increased uptake in bilateral femora and tibiae with periostosis. 18F-MFBG PET/CT revealed no abnormal uptake, and no metastasis was found. The diagnosis was hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. This case demonstrates that hypertrophic osteoarthropathy can occur as a rare complication after anti-GD2 therapy and can be detected by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.

articles.title: Longer sleep duration and the incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep duration has been linked to adverse health outcomes, but its association with diabetic nephropathy remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the association between sleep duration and a composite endpoint of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy.

METHODS: The study participants were 678 Japanese outpatients with type 2 diabetes. Lifestyle habits were assessed at baseline and at years 2 and/or 5. Mean values of lifestyle factors were calculated by averaging measurements from baseline to the date of endpoint onset or the end of follow-up. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used.

RESULTS: During a follow-up of 6.0 ± 2.7 years, 215 participants experienced the endpoint. Among lifestyle factors, mean sleep duration was the only factor associated with the endpoint. Compared with participants sleeping <6 hours, the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for mean sleep duration of 6 to <7, 7 to <8, and ≥8 hours were 1.08 (95% CI, 0.74-1.57), 1.56 (95% CI, 1.05-2.31), and 1.92 (95% CI, 1.15-3.19), respectively (P for trend = .003). This association remained significant after adjustment for key lifestyle and diabetes-related factors. The association was stronger in older participants and those with microalbuminuria or reduced kidney function.

CONCLUSION: Longer, but not shorter, sleep duration is associated with an increased risk of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy.

articles.title: Stage IIIB pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma treated with spatially fractionated radiotherapy combined with antiangiogenic therapy and sequential chemo-immunotherapy: A case report.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is a rare subtype of non-small-cell lung cancer, characterized by high invasiveness and treatment resistance. Patients with PSC often exhibit poor treatment outcomes, short median survival and a dismal prognosis, necessitating novel comprehensive treatment strategies to address this clinical challenge. A 64-year-old man with PSC was initially diagnosed with stage cT4N2M0 IIIB disease and was negative for programmed cell death-ligand 1 expression. Owing to the large tumor size and unfavorable performance status, treatment initially involved an induction regimen that combined tomotherapy-based spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) with recombinant human endostatin injection (Endostar). As the condition of the patient improved, two additional cycles of low-dose albumin-bound paclitaxel were administered as concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Following radiotherapy, the patient received two sequential cycles of systemic therapy with paclitaxel liposome and ivonescimab. This combined regimen demonstrated favorable short-term efficacy with improved performance status. However, the patient developed pneumonia caused by infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii and aspergillus, subsequently succumbing to respiratory failure (with an overall survival of 5.5 months). The present case provides a clinical reference for the selection of treatment strategies in locally advanced, large PSC, highlighting the potential of SFRT combined with antiangiogenic therapy as a promising, novel local treatment option. However, the ultimate survival outcome of this patient should serve as a stark warning that heightened vigilance against opportunistic infections is essential during combination therapy in such patients.

articles.title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
articles.abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

articles.title: MRI-Negative Sarcoid Myelitis Revealed by Spinal 18F-FDG-PET Hypermetabolism.
Astrocytic and Axonal Injury Biomarkers in AQP4 Antibody-Positive NMOSD: Insights From PREVENT and CHAMPION-NMOSD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light chain (NfL) are biomarkers of astrocytic and axonal injury, respectively, in aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4-Ab+ NMOSD). We evaluated serum GFAP and NfL levels during treatment with complement component 5 inhibitors eculizumab or ravulizumab and examined associations between pretreatment biomarker levels, clinical characteristics, and on-trial relapse risk using samples from the PREVENT (eculizumab) and CHAMPION-NMOSD (ravulizumab) phase 3 trials.

METHODS: Serum GFAP and NfL levels were analyzed retrospectively in PREVENT and prospectively in CHAMPION-NMOSD and compared with levels in demographically matched external healthy donors. Associations between baseline clinical characteristics and high biomarker levels (≥2 SDs above the healthy donor mean) were evaluated using logistic regression with a test-and-validate strategy. Changes throughout treatment were assessed relative to pretreatment baseline. Biomarker changes associated with adjudicated on-trial relapses were examined. Associations between baseline biomarker levels and time to first adjudicated on-trial relapse were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses.

RESULTS: Samples were available from 41 PREVENT and 55 CHAMPION-NMOSD patients. Pretreatment baseline GFAP and NfL levels were elevated in patients compared with healthy donors. High baseline GFAP levels were associated with older age at initial presentation, less time since last relapse, and higher baseline Hauser Ambulation Index (HAI) score. High baseline NfL levels were associated with older age and higher baseline HAI score. High baseline GFAP and NfL levels using age-adjusted Z-scores were evaluated and would not have materially changed the conclusions. The median GFAP levels declined rapidly (within 4-6 weeks) and were sustained with both eculizumab and ravulizumab. The median NfL levels declined significantly with ravulizumab but not eculizumab. In PREVENT, adjudicated on-trial relapses were associated with increased GFAP levels in placebo-treated patients, while GFAP increases were attenuated in eculizumab-treated patients.

DISCUSSION: Serum GFAP and NfL levels are elevated in patients with NMOSD and are associated with clinical features of disability. Complement component 5 blockade biologically suppresses astrocytic injury in NMOSD, validating GFAP as a pharmacodynamic biomarker and mechanistic readout of target engagement in randomized phase 3 trials. This aligns with earlier findings across different compounds in separate phase 3 trials.

articles.title: Technical Refinements in Brain-dead Donor Uterus Transplantation: Lessons From the 3 First Cases in France.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uterus procurement from brain-dead donors during multiorgan procurement for uterus transplantation (UTx) presents a technical challenge because the uterus is not a vital organ and also because of the need to harvest uterine and ovarian veins for transplantation. The aim of this article is to describe the technical refinements in uterus procurement from brain-dead donors during multiorgan procurement and evaluate their impact on graft viability in UTx.

METHODS: According to a prospective interventional study within a national multiorgan procurement network, we described uterus procurement during multiorgan retrieval with protocol modifications between the first and second procedures, including bilateral femoral artery cannulation for pelvic perfusion and in situ identification of uterine and pelvic vessels before cold flushing. The main outcomes were the feasibility of procurement, graft viability, surgical parameters (ischemia times, operative duration), and short-term graft outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 8 evaluated recipients, 3 UTx procedures from brain-dead donors were performed. The first transplantation resulted in early graft loss because of bilateral arterial thrombosis requiring graft explantation on postoperative day 1. The second and third transplantations demonstrated sustained graft viability with normal perfusion on Doppler imaging up to 2 and 7 mo, resumption of menstruation, and only 1 episode of mild rejection responsive to corticosteroids. Technical refinements reduced back-table complexity and operative time (5 h 40 min versus 4 h 15 min) and enabled improved venous outflow through additional anastomoses. Bilateral femoral artery cannulation allowed effective pelvic perfusion without interfering with standard multiorgan procurement.

CONCLUSIONS: UTx from brain-dead donors is feasible within a multiorgan procurement setting. Bilateral femoral cannulation combined with in situ vascular identification improves graft preparation and may enhance reproducibility without compromising retrieval of vital organs. These refinements represent important steps toward standardization of deceased donor UTx.

articles.title: Optimizing longitudinal follow-up after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: A quality improvement initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are associated with increased risk for future cardiovascular disease. Guidelines recommend longitudinal follow-up for cardiovascular risk stratification after pregnancy complicated by HDP; however, adherence to this recommendation remains suboptimal. Our aim was to evaluate the impact of the Postpartum Hypertension Program (PHP), a quality improvement initiative designed to address patient, clinician, and system barriers to longitudinal follow-up after HDP.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study evaluating rates of longitudinal follow-up before and after PHP implementation at a level IV maternal care center. Individuals were eligible if they had a diagnosis of HDP and were discharged on antihypertensive medication after delivery. A post-implementation cohort (eligible individuals referred to the PHP with delivery discharge from January 21, 2024 to March 22, 2025) was compared to a pre-implementation cohort (all eligible individuals with delivery discharge from January 1, 2021 to January 20, 2024). The primary outcome was follow-up with a longitudinal clinician (Cardiology, Internal Medicine, or Family Medicine) within 1 year postpartum. Secondary outcomes included rates of longitudinal follow-up at 3 and 6 months postpartum and patient characteristics associated with 1-year follow-up. Program components included: (1) clinician education, (2) patient education, and (3) a streamlined process for transfer-of-care to a longitudinal clinician. Data were abstracted from the medical record. Bivariate analysis compared outcomes between cohorts, and multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for potential confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 227 individuals met inclusion criteria (pre-implementation: n = 145, post-implementation: n = 82). PHP implementation was associated with increased longitudinal follow-up within 1 year postpartum (60.7% vs. 76.8%, p = 0.013). Follow-up rates in the post-implementation cohort were also higher at 3 months (31.7% vs. 62.2%, p < 0.001) and 6 months postpartum (49.0% vs. 72.0%, p = 0.001) compared to the pre-implementation cohort. Individuals who had a longitudinal visit within 1 year were more likely to have medical comorbidities compared to those who were not seen within 1 year. After adjusting for confounders, PHP implementation remained independently associated with increased follow-up within 1 year (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.6; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.3-4.7; p = 0.008).

CONCLUSION: PHP implementation was associated with 2.6-fold increased odds of longitudinal follow-up within 1 year after pregnancy complicated by HDP. With adequate infrastructure and resources, this program can serve as a model for institutions seeking to improve longitudinal care transitions for individuals with HDP. Further study is needed to determine the impact of improved follow-up rates on long-term cardiovascular health.
