Across both sexes and age bands, the most reported fracture sites were "other" (including digits and facial bones), wrist, ankle, arm, leg, spine, and hip, in descending order. In HES-linked data, 43 572 fractures were identified. Incidence patterns mirrored those from self-report: higher early midlife fracture rates in men, followed by a transition to female predominance from approximately age 45. This large-scale, dual-method analysis offers the first clear evidence that female fracture risk begins to increase from age 35, with a marked acceleration from 45 yr onward. These sex-specific trajectories in midlife fracture incidence are not fully captured in current clinical models and indicate that further work is needed to determine whether earlier or tailored approaches to risk assessment could provide cost-effective benefit in reducing the burden of fracture in midlife.

articles.title: Expected change: a new concept for monitoring patients on oral bisphosphonates.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: It is essential to closely monitor the response to oral bisphosphonate therapy for osteoporosis, as many patients are nonadherent. The conventional approach is to monitor whether changes in BMD or bone turnover markers (BTMs) exceed the least significant change. This approach assumed that if a patient were not receiving a treatment, there would be no change in the BMD. We propose an alternative approach, that of expected change. We define this expected change as the change in BMD (at 24 mo) or BTMs (at 3 mo) that is exceeded in 90% of patients who are adherent with oral bisphosphonate therapy. We studied 108 postmenopausal women (age < 85 yr) who were randomized to the licensed dose of alendronate, ibandronate, or risedronate treatment for 2 yr, along with calcium and vitamin D supplementation. We identified the performance of BMD and BTMs in 3 ways. We calculated the signal-to-noise ratio, which was lower for BMD (4.1 and 2.1 for lumbar spine BMD (LSBMD) and total hip BMD (THBMD), respectively) compared to BTMs (9.4 and 10.2 for C-telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX) and procollagen I N-propeptide (PINP), respectively). We estimated the response rate as the percentage of women exceeding the least significant change, which was lower for BMD (47% and 24% for LSBMD and THBMD, respectively) than for BTMs (96% and 94% for CTX and PINP, respectively). We estimated the expected change as the 90th (or 10th) percentile of change in adherent patients. We required the expected change to exceed the least significant change, and this was not observed for LSBMD and THBMD, but it was observed for CTX and PINP (expected changes of 0.233 and 12.1 ng/mL, respectively). Thus, the BTMs CTX and PINP showed the best performance as response markers for monitoring oral bisphosphonate treatment, and the new approach is based on a biological rather than a statistical endpoint when using the expected change approach.

articles.title: Evaluation of the effect of rituximab on fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis using the Chalder Fatigue Scale.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fatigue is a frequent extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), with a reported prevalence ranging from 40% to 90%. It affects physical, emotional, and cognitive aspects of daily life and significantly impairs quality of life. Although biologic therapies may improve fatigue, the specific effect of rituximab on this symptom remains insufficiently documented. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of rituximab on fatigue at baseline (M0), 4 months (M4), and 6 months (M6) using the Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFS).

METHODS: This prospective, observational, single-center study included patients fulfilling the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria for RA and treated with rituximab. Rituximab was administered as two intravenous infusions (500 mg or 1000 mg) on day 0 and day 15. Fatigue was assessed at M0, M4, and M6 using the CFS, with a score ≥4 indicating clinically significant fatigue. Clinical and biological data were collected at each visit. Statistical analyses were performed using Jamovi version 2.4.14.

RESULTS: Ninety-four patients were included (mean age 57±9 years; 88% female). The median CFS score decreased from 4 [2-6] at M0 to 2 [0-4] at M4 (p<0.001) and remained stable thereafter through M6 (p=0.11 for the M4-M6 comparison). Disease activity improved in parallel, with the Disease Activity Score 28 using C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP) decreasing from 4.7±1.1 at M0 to 2.9±0.9 at M4 and remaining stable at M6. Functional status assessed by Health Assessment Questionnaire also improved significantly. In multivariable analysis, higher M0 DAS28-CRP was associated with a greater reduction in fatigue.

CONCLUSIONS: Rituximab therapy was associated with a significant improvement in fatigue in patients with RA, parallel to reductions in disease activity and functional disability.

articles.title: Dissociation between structural reverse remodeling and clinical outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy: a real-world analysis.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) generally exhibit better responses to cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) due to more pronounced reverse remodeling compared to ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) patients. However, the prognostic impact of CRT in ICM patients remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) etiology on reverse remodeling, clinical outcomes, and survival following CRT in a real-world population. We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients who underwent CRT-P (pacing)/CRT-D (defibrillator) implantation. Patients were stratified according to HF etiology (ICM vs. NICM). The primary composite endpoint was the occurrence of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization. Secondary outcomes focused on echocardiographic measures of left ventricular reverse remodeling. Survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models. Of the 95 patients initially screened, 83 were included in the final analysis, of whom 38 (45.8%) had ICM. The mean age was 69.5±10.4 years, and 75.8% were male. Both groups received similar medical therapy. NICM patients demonstrated a significant improvement in reverse remodeling after CRT [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF): 32.3±11.5% to 44.0±13.2%, p=0.001); end-diastolic volume (LVEDV): 189.6±74.3 mL to 143.9±48.9 mL, p=0.010] with post-CRT LVEF being higher than in ICM patients (44.0±13.2% vs. 35.5±13.5%, p=0.003). NICM patients were more likely to be super-responders (58.1% vs. 25.0%, p=0.014). No significant differences were observed between groups in the primary composite endpoint (27.3% vs. 42.1%, p=0.171) or overall survival over a mean follow-up of 35 months (log-rank p=0.733). Although ICM patients showed less pronounced reverse remodeling following CRT, long-term clinical outcomes and survival were comparable to those observed in NICM. These findings reinforce the role of CRT as a disease-modifying therapy that prevents disease progression irrespective of HF etiology and support its systematic use in all eligible patients.

articles.title: Estimand-based design strategies for cardiovascular recurrent event trials of combination therapies.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular trials increasingly evaluate combination therapies in settings where patients may experience recurrent events such as myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, or stroke. Traditional single-event analyses fail to capture the cumulative disease burden and temporal dynamics, motivating the integration of recurrent event methods within an estimand framework. This manuscript reviews estimand strategies for recurrent event analyses in cardiovascular trials of combination therapies, emphasizing alignment between clinical questions, intercurrent events, and causal interpretation. We compare commonly used models, including the Andersen-Gill, Prentice-Williams-Peterson, and Negative Binomial approaches, highlighting their suitability for different estimands. We distinguish each model's conditional or marginal estimand, its identifiability assumptions, and the difference between sensitivity analyses that vary assumptions under the same estimand and supplementary analyses that target alternative estimands with different intercurrent event strategies. The impact of intercurrent events such as treatment discontinuation, rescue therapy, and mortality on estimand interpretation is explored. Novel methodological considerations specific to combination-therapy trials, including component-specific intercurrent events (ICE), drug-drug interaction estimands, mixed intercurrent event (ICE) strategies, and principal-stratum estimands conditional on dual adherence, are formally defined and discussed with work examples. We further discuss how the choice of estimand influences causal inference and model selection. Finally, we provide a regulatory perspective on estimand-based approaches in cardiovascular trials. This manuscript serves as a methodological guide for designing and analyzing cardiovascular trials with recurrent events for combination therapies to ensure clarity of clinical interpretation, robustness of causal conclusions, and regulatory alignment.

articles.title: The low fasting serum C-peptide level was associated with reduced sural nerve action potential amplitudes: A cross-sectional study of Japanese type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: The association between the fasting serum C-peptide levels and diabetic polyneuropathy (DPN) in patients with type 2 diabetes remains controversial. Furthermore, the association with the electrophysiological parameters of nerve conduction studies (NCS) has not been elucidated. Therefore, we investigated whether the fasting serum C-peptide levels are associated with nerve conduction velocity (CV) and action potential amplitude (Amp) in patients with type 2 diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled outpatients with type 2 diabetes who underwent the DPNCheck® at the Higashikurume Ekimae Clinic in Tokyo, Japan, between March 1, 2016, and June 30, 2025. Participants were categorized into tertiles according to their fasting serum C-peptide levels. Abnormal values of CV and Amp were defined as CV <46.5 m/s and Amp <10.5 μV. A logistic regression analysis was used to evaluate whether the fasting serum C-peptide levels were associated with CV and Amp abnormalities.

RESULTS: One-hundred thirty-one participants were included and stratified into tertiles based on fasting serum C-peptide levels: Tertile 1, ≤1.9 ng/mL; Tertile 2, 2.0-2.8 ng/mL; and Tertile 3, ≥2.9 ng/mL. Tertile 1 was independently associated with an abnormal Amp (odds ratio: 5.08, 95% confidence interval: 1.41-18.4), whereas no independent association was observed with an abnormal CV. Tertile 2 was not associated with an abnormal CV or Amp. Additionally, a nonlinear relationship was observed between the fasting serum C-peptide levels and an abnormal Amp.

CONCLUSIONS: Low fasting serum C-peptide levels were independently associated with abnormal Amp in patients with type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6-Sulfo Sialyl Lewisx Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus.
articles.abstract: The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6-sulfo sialyl Lewisx (6-sulfo-SLex) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo-lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N-trifluoroacetyl-glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc-6-O-sulfotransferases 2 (CHST-2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6-sulfo-SLex glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6-sulfo-SLex derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS-CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol-based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS-CoV spike protein N-terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre-organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

articles.title: Sustained Psychosocial Benefits of Telehealth Occupational Therapy for Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Long-Term Follow-Up of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to examine 12-month outcomes of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) intervention for young adults with diabetes.

METHODS: Young adults ages 18 to 30 years with type 1 diabetes ≥1 year and A1C ≥7.5% (≥58 mmol/mol) were randomized 1:1 to REAL-T (6 months of telehealth occupational therapy) or usual care. Continuous glucose monitor metrics, diabetes distress, and diabetes-related quality of life (DQoL) were assessed at baseline, 6, and 12 months, while A1C and hypothesized mediators were assessed quarterly. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal treatment effects.

RESULTS: Of 209 randomized participants, 171 (82%) contributed 12-month data. No significant between-group differences were observed for glycemia. REAL-T participants showed greater improvements in emotional distress and diabetes self-efficacy than control group participants. Per protocol analyses excluding untreated participants yielded stronger effects, with significantly improved DQoL and regimen distress.

CONCLUSIONS: A telehealth occupational therapy intervention produced durable improvements in emotional distress and self-efficacy over 12 months, supporting psychosocial outcomes as central treatment targets in young adults with type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: An Adipocyte MKK3-p38β Axis Preserves Insulin Responsiveness in Mice and Is Reciprocally Altered in Human Obesity.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a major risk factor for insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Adipocyte stress responses can either promote metabolic dysfunction or preserve insulin action, but the contribution of the p38 MAPK activator MKK3 to adipose tissue physiology remains poorly understood. Here, we show that adipose MKK3 expression increases early during high-fat feeding and is also elevated in human obesity. In human visceral adipose tissue, MKK3 expression was positively associated with body mass index and leptin and inversely associated with HbA1c in unadjusted analyses. Using germline, Fabp4-Cre, and Adipo-Cre Mkk3-deficient mice, together with p38β-deficient mice and primary adipocytes, we found that loss of adipocyte MKK3 impairs insulin responsiveness. Adipo-Cre;Mkk3fl/fl (AdipoMkk3) mice displayed reduced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake selectively in subcutaneous white adipose tissue despite unchanged body composition and basal brown adipose tissue activity. Mechanistically, MKK3 or p38β deficiency increased p70S6K activity and inhibitory IRS1 Ser307 phosphorylation, reduced GLUT4 translocation and Akt activation, and these defects were partially rescued by rapamycin or the selective p70S6K inhibitor PF-4708671. Together, these findings identify an adipocyte MKK3-p38β-p70S6K axis that helps preserve insulin signaling during nutritional stress.

articles.title: Stroke-Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning.
articles.abstract: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply-demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time-resolved framework. Eight provisional, non-mutually-exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke-triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre-existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome-specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke-cardiology decision-making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.

articles.title: The agmatinase MrAGM1 is required for Metarhizium robertsii virulence by modulating putrescine-associated appressorium development.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fungal polyamine metabolism plays an integral role in cellular development and host-pathogen interactions. However, the biological functions of agmatinase, a key enzyme that hydrolyzes agmatine to putrescine and urea, remain poorly characterized in entomopathogenic fungi.

RESULTS: In this study, we characterized the agmatinase gene, MrAgm1, in Metarhizium robertsii. Transcriptional analysis showed that MrAgm1 was upregulated during appressorium development. Fusion protein of MrAGM1-GFP was localized to vacuoles and cell membranes. Although the deletion of MrAgm1 did not alter vegetative growth, conidiation, or tolerance to various abiotic stresses, it significantly attenuated fungal virulence against Galleria mellonella larvae via topical inoculation, as evidenced by a 1.94-day delay in the median lethal time. Conversely, intrahemocoel injection bioassays revealed no significant difference in virulence between the WT and ΔMrAgm1 strains, indicating that MrAgm1 is specifically required for host cuticle penetration rather than postinfection colonization. Further phenotypic assays demonstrated that ΔMrAgm1 exhibited compromised conidial adhesion, reduced appressorium formation and impaired penetration through cicada wings. These defects correlated with the significant downregulation of key infection-related genes encoding adhesins (mad1), proteases (pr1A, pr1B, pr1C and pr1F) and a chitinase (chit30). Notably, the addition of exogenous putrescine successfully rescued the appressorium formation defect of the ΔMrAgm1 strain.

CONCLUSION: MrAGM1 regulates conidial adhesion, appressorium morphogenesis and cuticle penetration via the putrescine pathway, reflecting its specialized function in early infection of M. robertsii. These findings advance mechanistic understanding of agmatinase function in polyamine metabolism of entomopathogenic fungi, and provide a molecular target to boost their biocontrol efficacy. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Thrombin Generation Assessment of Four Anticoagulants in Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolic events (VTE) are a serious complication in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Currently, there is no consensus regarding anticoagulant treatment or prevention in this setting, and the role of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has not been extensively studied. The recent approval of DOACs for the treatment of VTE in children supports their further evaluation in pediatric patients with ALL. We prospectively evaluated the effects of four anticoagulant agents in 67 pediatric patients with ALL, compared with healthy controls, using the global coagulation assay thrombin generation (TG). The first 21 patients formed the calibration cohort, and we performed the primary TG analysis in the subsequent 46 patients. Measurements were performed before and after asparaginase therapy, with and without ex vivo spiking of the different anticoagulants. Low-molecular-weight heparin demonstrated preserved anticoagulant activity both before and after asparaginase therapy, with reductions of 29% and 31% in thrombin peak height, respectively, similar to healthy controls. However, the direct factor Xa inhibitors apixaban and rivaroxaban showed minimal anticoagulant effect (7%-13% reduction in thrombin peak height compared with reductions of 48%-59%, in controls). Notably, dabigatran, an oral direct thrombin inhibitor, demonstrated substantial anticoagulant activity before and after asparaginase therapy, with 180% and 134% prolongation of lag time, respectively, comparable to controls. These ex vivo pharmacodynamics findings support the anticoagulant activity of LMWH and dabigatran. The clinical efficacy of dabigatran in pediatric patients with ALL should be further investigated and confirmed in prospective in vivo studies.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Longitudinal FDG-PET reveals early hypermetabolism associated with astrocyte changes in TgF344-AD rats.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by alterations in brain glucose metabolism, classically showing [18F]FDG-PET hypometabolism in later stages. However, emerging evidence suggests a transient phase of glucose hypermetabolism early in the disease, for which biological basis remains unclear.

METHODS: We combined longitudinal and cross-sectional approaches in TgF344-AD rats and wild-type controls at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Longitudinal assessments included [18F]FDG-microPET imaging, behavioral testing, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarker analysis. Cross-sectional analyses included amyloid histopathology, western blot and ex vivo glutamate uptake measurements.

RESULTS: TgF344-AD rats exhibited increased cerebral glucose metabolism at 9mo, predominantly in cortical regions. This phase coincided with emerging cognitive impairment and early amyloid deposition. CSF analyses showed increased GFAP at 9-12mo and reduced S100B at 9mo, while microglial/inflammatory markers remained unchanged. WB confirmed region-specific GFAP alterations without changes in neuronal or synaptic markers. Glutamate uptake was increased in the cortex and hippocampus at 9mo.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify a transient phase of increased glucose metabolism early in disease progression, associated with astrocyte-related changes, suggesting that early hypermetabolism may reflect non-neuronal processes. This has implications for the interpretation of [18F]FDG-PET as a biomarker in early AD and for understanding early physiological responses to AD pathology.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Community Water Fluoridation in Queensland: A Population-Based Causal Analysis Following the 2008 Policy Change.
articles.abstract: Water fluoridation (WF) is an important preventive program against dental caries. Recent Cochrane reviews reported only limited new scientific evidence of WF. This research aimed to provide contemporary evidence on the causal relationship between WF and oral health. A causal framework was used to ensure methodological rigour in repeated cross-sectional, population-based studies of randomly selected 5 to 14 y old children in Queensland, thereby enabling controlled difference-in-differences (DiD) analyses. The primary exposure was access to WF, defined as newly fluoridated (New-WF; areas that became fluoridated since 2010), never fluoridated (No-WF), or long-term fluoridated areas (Long-WF). The outcomes were dental caries experience (decayed, missing, or filled tooth surfaces) and prevalence in the primary and permanent dentition, collected by dental examiners who were uniformly trained and calibrated during both phases. The DiD estimands were the differences in changes in outcomes between New-WF and the control (No-WF), estimated from multivariable regression models. Data of 5,407 children during 2010-2012 and 7,718 children during 2022-2024 were collected. Variations in key confounders (area and individual socioeconomic factors) were controlled for using inverse probability of treatment weights. Dental caries among children in New-WF had consistently declined relative to the control groups. In the primary dentition, the New-WF children had a 1.40-fold (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08 to 1.80) reduction in caries experience and a 1.28-fold (1.00 to 1.67) reduction in caries prevalence, equivalent to 1.1 fewer affected tooth surfaces and a 10.8% lower prevalence. In the permanent dentition, reductions were smaller: a 1.32-fold (0.95 to 1.84) reduction in caries experience and a 1.04-fold (0.81 to 1.33) reduction in prevalence. These findings show that WF is effective in preventing dental caries in children when disease levels are low and other preventive programs are available. This controlled DiD study provides robust contemporary scientific evidence of the effects of WF on dental caries, strengthening WF as a public health policy.

articles.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Is Associated With Lower Rates of Adhesive Capsulitis, Bursitis, Shoulder Stiffness, and Revision Shoulder Arthroscopy After Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (RCR) success is dependent on adherence to a structured postoperative rehabilitation protocol. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with worse outcomes after certain orthopaedic surgeries, but its impact on rehabilitation after RCR remains unclear. This study compared short-term outcomes after arthroscopic RCR in patients with and without ADHD.

HYPOTHESIS: Patients with ADHD will experience higher rates of postoperative complications within the first 12 months after arthroscopic RCR.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX Research Network, arthroscopic RCR cases from 113 healthcare organizations between January 2006 and January 2026 were identified and stratified by a preoperative ADHD diagnosis. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1 for age, sex, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, mood disorders, anxiety and stress-related disorders, and nicotine dependence. Outcomes at 3 months included revision shoulder arthroscopy, adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, and shoulder stiffness; 1-year outcomes also included deep infection and wound disruption. A Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction was applied to address multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 4740 patients were included per cohort. At 3 months, patients with ADHD demonstrated lower odds of bursitis (odds ratio [OR], 0.733; 95% CI, 0.592-0.908; P = 0.004; BH-adjusted P = 0.009) and shoulder stiffness (OR, 0.729; 95% CI, 0.629-0.844; P < 0.001; BH-adjusted P < 0.001). At 1 year, the ADHD cohort demonstrated lower odds of revision shoulder arthroscopy (OR, 0.798; 95% CI, 0.655-0.972; P = 0.03; BH-adjusted P = 0.04), adhesive capsulitis (OR, 0.676; 95% CI, 0.550-0.831; P < 0.001; BH-adjusted P < 0.001), bursitis (OR, 0.681; 95% CI, 0.578-0.802; P < 0.001; BH-adjusted P < 0.001), and shoulder stiffness (OR, 0.716; 95% CI, 0.625-0.820; P < 0.001; BH-adjusted P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: ADHD was associated with lower 3-month rates of bursitis and shoulder stiffness, and lower 1-year rates of adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, shoulder stiffness, and revision shoulder arthroscopy after arthroscopic RCR.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: In contrast to previous literature, ADHD was not associated with worse outcomes after arthroscopic RCR and was associated with lower rates of stiffness-related complications. These findings suggest further research is needed to inform patient counseling and surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Real-World MiniMed™ 780G Advanced Hybrid Closed-Loop Performance Across the Asia-Pacific Region.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetes mellitus (types 1 and 2) prevalence in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region has increased significantly. While real-world evidence demonstrates MiniMed™ 780G (MM780G) system effectiveness and safety in many countries, its use in the APAC region is not well reported. The present study explored MM780G system performance and glycemic outcomes in individuals with diabetes in the APAC region.

METHODS: CareLink™ personal data uploaded between January 2, 2020, and March 31, 2025, by consenting APAC MM780G system users (all ages) with ≥10 days of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data were de-identified, aggregated, and analyzed, including a subanalysis of those using recommended optimal settings (ROS; glucose target of 100 mg/dL with an active insulin time of 2 h, for ≥95% of time). Endpoints were compared between Australia/New Zealand (AUS/NZL) and APAC without AUS/NZL (APAC w/o AUS/NZL) and assessed across quartiles of user-announced total daily carbohydrate (TDCarb).

RESULTS: Compared to AUS/NZL (N = 17,382), APAC w/o AUS/NZL (N = 8,360) had clinically similar and favorable CGM-derived outcomes, despite a significantly greater mean TDCarb (210.5 g vs. 147.0 g, P < 0.001). Across increasing TDCarb quartiles, for both subregions, time in range improved (P < 0.001 for both), and time below range <70mg/dL (%TBR) was low (≤2.8%). ROS users showed further glycemic improvement with unchanged %TBR.

CONCLUSIONS: The MM780G system can effectively manage real-world APAC glycemia irrespective of different TDCarb.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of enavogliflozin in patients with type 2 diabetes: A 24-week prospective multicenter observational study in Korea.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of enavogliflozin as a single-pill formulation (Enavo group; enavogliflozin 0.3 mg) or fixed-dose combination with metformin (EnavoMet group; enavogliflozin 0.3 mg/metformin 1000 mg) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM) in Korean primary care.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, non-interventional observational study enrolled 8796 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus from 273 primary care clinics across Korea (Safety Set). The full analysis set comprised 8704 participants (Enavo: 7046; EnavoMet: 1658) with baseline and at least one post-baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measurement. The primary endpoint was HbA1c change at 24 weeks.

RESULTS: At 24 weeks, mean HbA1c decreased by -0.69 percentage points (95% CI: -0.71, -0.67) in Enavo (n = 7003) and -0.86 (-0.90, -0.82) in EnavoMet (n = 1648). In these paired cohorts, 1728 (24.7%) and 371 (22.5%), respectively, already had HbA1c <7.0% at baseline. Overall 24-week HbA1c <7.0% rates were 61.6% and 63.6%, combining maintenance and new attainment; <6.5% rates were 30.0% and 37.2%. Weight and systolic blood pressure decreased (-2.43/-2.73 kg; -3.05/-3.77 mmHg). Adverse events were recorded in 39 participants (0.44%); no serious events were recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: Enavogliflozin use was associated with decreases in HbA1c, body weight, and blood pressure over 24 weeks. Overall target rates include participants already below target at baseline and do not establish causal treatment effects.

articles.title: Traumatic Dental Injuries in Infants and Toddlers Under 4 Years of Age: Burden, Injury Patterns and Early Sequelae in a Hospital-Based Dental Emergency Service: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Traumatic dental injuries are a major cause of emergency dental visits during early childhood, yet comprehensive data in children under 4 years of age remain limited. This study aimed to describe the clinical burden, injury patterns, management, and early post-traumatic sequelae of traumatic dental injuries in children under 4 years of age attending a hospital-based dental emergency service.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using clinical records from the paediatric dental emergency service of Hospital HM Nens (Barcelona, Spain) between 2021 and 2025. Of 5516 paediatric emergency visits, 1125 involved children under 4 years of age. After excluding 47 visits because of unavailable or insufficient clinical records, 1078 evaluable visits were analysed. Trauma-related visits included visits in which dental trauma was the main reason for consultation, emergency consultations for post-traumatic sequelae, and trauma-related visits involving previously traumatized teeth. Descriptive statistics were performed, and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using the Wilson method.

RESULTS: Trauma-related conditions accounted for 743 of 1078 evaluable emergency visits (68.9%; 95% confidence interval: 66.1-71.6), of which 589 (79.3%) were visits in which dental trauma was the main reason for consultation. Periodontal injuries predominated, followed by hard tissue and combined injuries, mainly affecting the primary maxillary central incisors. Falls were the leading mechanism of injury, whereas educational settings and home were the most frequent locations. Soft tissue injuries commonly involved the lips, gingiva, and labial frenum. Non-operative management was the most frequent treatment. Post-traumatic sequelae accounted for 104 emergency visits, comprising 150 recorded sequelae. Previous healthcare contact was documented in a minority of patients before referral to the dental emergency service.

CONCLUSIONS: Traumatic dental injuries constitute a substantial proportion of hospital-based paediatric dental emergencies in children under 4 years of age and are frequently associated with early post-traumatic sequelae. These findings emphasize the importance of timely diagnosis, appropriate emergency management, structured follow-up, and preventive strategies for the primary dentition.

articles.title: Neutrophil-Derived Arg1 Impairs CD8+ T Cell Activity in Sepsis Through mTOR-Mediated Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This research aimed to elucidate the contribution of Arginase 1 (Arg1) to pediatric sepsis progression, specifically impacting the effector functions of CD8+ T lymphocytes.

METHODS: Arg1 expression was assessed in venous blood from pediatric sepsis patients (n = 21) and healthy volunteers (n = 21). Pharmacological inhibition of Arg1 was achieved using Nor-NOHA in both sepsis patients-derived neutrophils and LPS-stimulated healthy neutrophils, followed by co-culture with CD8+ T cells. Sepsis-derived neutrophils were also treated with hArg1 monoclonal antibody (mAb). CD8+ T cell viability, exhaustion markers (PD-1/TIM-3), mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP production, autophagy, and inflammatory cytokine secretion were systematically evaluated.

RESULTS: Arg1 expression was markedly upregulated in sepsis patients correlated positively with neutrophil counts but negatively with CD8+ T cell numbers and mitochondrial function. Strikingly, CD8+ T cells from Arg1-high patients exhibited increased PD-1+TIM-3+ double-positive populations. Both Nor-NOHA-mediated Arg1 inhibition and hArg1-mAb neutralization significantly restored CD8+ T cell mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), ATP production, and effector cytokine secretion, while concurrently reducing PD-1/TIM-3 expression.

CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that overexpression of Arg1 derived from neutrophils leads to a highly inflammatory response suggesting that Arg1 is a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in pediatric sepsis.

articles.title: Extent of Breastfeeding Challenges Relate to Lower Satisfaction and Success with Breastfeeding Following Term Births in the United States.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United States Preventive Services Task Force recommends research to examine how breastfeeding interventions impact emotional well-being. Many interventions aim to mitigate breastfeeding challenges to increase exclusivity and duration; how breastfeeding challenges influence emotional well-being remains poorly quantified. We examined the extent to which breastfeeding challenges relate to breastfeeding satisfaction and success in a U.S.

METHODS: We present a secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data collected in January 2026 from adults with term infants ≤2 years; any postpartum breast pump use; and proficiency in English/Spanish. Recruitment aligned sample demographics with prior national breastfeeding studies. Questions adapted from three Centers for Disease Control and Prevention surveys assessed sociodemographic, health, and breastfeeding factors, including common breastfeeding challenges. An adapted 5-point Likert scale measured breastfeeding satisfaction and success. Ten clinical and community partners reviewed survey content. Eight individuals with pump experience completed cognitive interviews. We used descriptive statistics, unadjusted ordinal logistic regression, and chi-square tests to compare satisfaction and success by any and specific breastfeeding challenges.

RESULTS: We included 712 individuals (77% response) from 48 states with a mean (standard deviation) age of 32 years (6.2). Ninety percent reported breastfeeding challenges (median: 2). Each additional breastfeeding challenge heightened one's odds of lower satisfaction (odds ratio [OR] 1.29, 1.17-1.43) and lower success (OR 1.15, 1.05-1.27) on a 5-point Likert scale. Low milk production was related to four- to fivefold lower odds of satisfaction and success. Milk overproduction was related to two- to threefold higher odds of satisfaction and success.

CONCLUSION: Breastfeeding challenges were prevalent and associated with lower odds of breastfeeding satisfaction and success.

articles.title: Enteric infections as HIV indicator conditions for HIV testing: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this umbrella review was to explore whether faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections should be indicator conditions for HIV testing.

METHOD: Four bibliographical databases (Medline, Emcare, Embase, CINAHL) were searched in May 2026 for systematic reviews written in English, exploring HIV in people with faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections. Two authors independently reviewed full-text publications, assessed risk of bias (Joanna Briggs toolkit) and performed a narrative synthesis to identify characteristics relevant to HIV indicator condition testing. Results were reported using the PRIOR guidelines and the review was registered on PROSPERO (ID:CRD420261387222).

RESULTS: There were 15 manuscripts in this umbrella review, all of which included study populations consisting exclusively of men who have sex with men (MSM). There were 10 032 MSM across 207 manuscripts that explored Shigella spp., Campylobacter spp., diarrhoeagenic E. coli, Salmonella spp., Giardia duodenalis, Entamoeba histolytica, Hepatitis A, Cryptosporidium spp., hepatitis E, Strongyloides stercoralis, Enterobius vermicularis, intestinal spirochaetosis (Brachyspiraspp.), Blastocystis spp. and enteric viruses. Living with HIV was observed in MSM with all enteric infections. Having a new diagnosis of HIV was seen in MSM with hepatitis A. Having Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, syphilis and other (or previous) sexually transmitted infections (STI); visiting sex on premises venues, and engaging in chemsex were also observed in MSM with enteric infections.

CONCLUSION: These data provide the best evidence to date that faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections in MSM are indicator diseases for HIV testing and testing for syphilis, hepatitis B and C and other STIs.

articles.title: Fractional Ablative Er:YAG Laser for Treatment-Refractory Trichophyton mentagrophytes Complex Infection.
Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke.
articles.abstract: Brain myeloid cells, including infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and microglia, play critical roles in ischemic brain injury, clearing debris and shaping neuroinflammation and neurological outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing and fate mapping with an MDM-specific Ms4a3creERT2-Ai14 mouse line, we identified serotonin receptor Htr2b+ MDMs as a crucial cell population involved in resolving neuroinflammation within the ischemic penumbra. Htr2b+ MDMs significantly accumulate in the peri-infarct region and exhibit enhanced phagocytosis and inflammation-resolving gene signatures. Mechanistically, Htr2b activation promotes nuclear translocation of Tfe3, a key lysosomal regulator, enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and supporting phagocytic activity. MDM-specific Htr2b ablation impairs debris clearance, exacerbates neuroinflammation and ischemic injury, whereas pharmacological agonism or Tfe3 activation restores lysosomal biogenesis in brain MDMs and improves post-stroke outcomes. Thus we demonstrate a previously unrecognized Htr2b+ MDM subset that integrates serotonin signaling to license intrinsic phagocytic function, alleviating ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: Dengue comes back even in vaccinated people - new clues.
Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

articles.title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism.
articles.abstract: The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors1. Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle2. Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia-reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

articles.title: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

articles.title: Rectus femoris ultrasound as a rapid bedside tool associated with 1-year hospitalization in cirrhosis: A retrospective study.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a common complication of liver cirrhosis and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes, including increased hospitalization. Ultrasonography (USG) has recently emerged as a practical bedside method for assessing skeletal muscle mass. This study aimed to investigate the association between rectus femoris thickness (RFT) and rectus femoris cross-sectional area (RFCSA) measured by USG and hospitalization in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 58 patients with cirrhosis followed at Hacettepe University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between August 2021 and April 2023. Demographic characteristics, clinical data, laboratory parameters, anthropometric measurements, and muscle USG findings were obtained from medical records. Patients were categorized according to hospitalization status. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent factors associated with hospitalization.

RESULTS: Patients with hospitalization had significantly lower body mass index and significantly higher Model for End-Stage Liver Disease sodium (MELD-Na) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 scores compared with those without hospitalization. RFT and RFCSA measured by USG were significantly lower in hospitalized patients (P = 0.011 and P = 0.032, respectively). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, RFT remained associated with hospitalization after adjustment for age, sex, and MELD-Na (OR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.63-0.96; P = 0.021). Similarly, RFCSA was associated with hospitalization (OR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.54-0.99: P = 0.043). MELD-Na score was also independently associated with hospitalization across the models.

CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-based rectus femoris measurements were associated with hospitalization in patients with cirrhosis. Bedside assessment of RFT and RFCSA may serve as a practical complementary approach for identifying patients at higher risk of hospitalization.

articles.title: Maternal Obesity Is Associated With Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Matched Electronic Health Record Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to define the prevalence of obesity in the first trimester of pregnancy among women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes.

METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.

RESULTS: Overall, 22.6% (64/283; 95% CI 17.7%-27.5%) of pregnancies in women with IBD met ethnicity-adjusted criteria for obesity. Increasing obesity class was associated with stepwise increases in gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), emergency caesarean section and high birthweight. Matching yielded 177 IBD pregnancies and 1062 controls. Obesity was independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome (OR 1.63; 95% CI 1.15-2.33; p = 0.007), whereas no statistically significant additional association was identified for IBD diagnosis alone (OR 0.74; 95% CI 0.53-1.03; p = 0.073). Among IBD pregnancies, aspirin was recommended in 39.3% (86/219). Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) was prescribed in 21.6% (19/88) of pregnancies classified post hoc as intermediate or high VTE risk.

CONCLUSION: More than one in five pregnancies in women with IBD were complicated by obesity. Obesity was strongly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas this study did not identify a significant additional effect attributable to IBD diagnosis alone. Preventive prescribing with aspirin and LMWH represents an opportunity for improved antenatal care.

articles.title: Concomitant Aveir AR and Micra AV2 Hybrid Leadless Implantation During Infected Pacemaker Extraction.
articles.abstract: Leadless pacing is an important option for patients with device-related infections. In those requiring dual-chamber support, reduced atrial battery longevity due to continuous implant-to-implant (i2i) communication remains a concern. While recent software updates now allow for the disablement of i2i communication when clinically appropriate, this mode does not provide atrioventricular synchronous pacing. We describe a case of a hybrid leadless system combining an atrial leadless pacemaker (Aveir AR, Abbott) and a second leadless pacemaker capable of atrial mechanical-sensed ventricular pacing (Micra AV2, Medtronic) in the setting of extraction of an infected transvenous pacemaker, providing atrial pacing with ventricular backup capability while preserving atrial device longevity.

articles.title: Insertable Cardiac Monitoring in Pediatric Patients: A Real-World Single-Center Experience With a New-Generation Device.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insertable cardiac monitors (ICMs) are increasingly used in pediatric patients, yet data on new-generation devices remain limited. The aim of this retrospective study was to describe a single-center real-world experience with a new-generation ICM in pediatric patients, focusing on procedural feasibility, sensing performance, transmission burden, and user experience.

METHODS: Consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing LUX-Dx ICM implantation between 2023 and 2025 were included. Procedural characteristics, sensing parameters, transmission patterns, diagnostic yield, reprogramming strategies, and patient/caregiver-reported experience were analyzed. Data are reported as median (25th-75th percentile) or mean ± standard deviation.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients underwent ICM implantation. Procedures were brief (6 ± 2 min) and complication-free. Electrical parameters were satisfactory and stable at discharge. Follow-up was 18 (6-23) months. A median of 2.7 transmissions per patient-month were received, of which 55% were alerts. Time from arrhythmia detection to transmission was 15 (3-21) hours. The number of episodes per patient was 4.8 (3.1-15.9) per month, with substantial inter-patient variability and bradycardia being the most frequent detection (80%). A diagnostic conclusion was reached in 79% of patients (positive: 45%, negative: 34%) at a median of 3 months. Reprogramming was performed in 90% of patients, mainly remotely (77%), and was predominantly directed toward reducing detection sensitivity. Patient and caregiver acceptance of remote monitoring was high.

CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric patients, new-generation ICM implantation was safe, well tolerated, and associated with stable sensing performance. Remote monitoring and reprogramming enabled timely diagnosis and individualized optimization, supporting the clinical utility of contemporary ICMs in this population.

articles.title: Assessment of healthcare professionals' perceptions regarding the implementation of a musical intervention in an intensive care unit.
Parathyroid Surgery After Kidney Transplantation: Operative Extent, Biochemical Outcomes, and Early Morbidity in a Contemporary Single-Center Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent hyperparathyroidism after kidney transplantation, especially with hypercalcemia, is associated with adverse allograft outcomes. We described operative extent, early morbidity, and follow-up calcium-PTH patterns.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 10 patients with a history of kidney transplantation who underwent parathyroid surgery during 2017-2025, including 1 receiving dialysis. Outcomes were summarized descriptively without inferential comparison.

RESULTS: Eight patients underwent limited parathyroidectomy (7 single-gland and 1 two-gland), and 2 underwent total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation. One limited procedure was a reoperation. A decrease in intraoperative PTH of at least 50% occurred at 10 or 30 minutes in 4 of 9 evaluable patients and at 30 minutes in 3 of 9. At approximately 1-year follow-up, 3 of 8 limited-resection patients had concurrent hypercalcemia and elevated PTH, 4 had isolated PTH elevation, and 1 had calcium and PTH within the reference intervals. Neither total-procedure patient had hypercalcemia or PTH elevation; 1 had calcium below the lower reference limit and the other had PTH below the lower reference limit. Early hypocalcemia occurred after both total procedures and no limited procedure; hypocalcemia was prolonged in 1 patient. No recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, confirmed cervical hematoma, reoperation for bleeding, surgical-site infection, or 30-day mortality occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small heterogeneous series, early hypocalcemia occurred only after total procedures, with a prolonged course in 1 patient. Follow-up calcium-PTH patterns varied across patients and renal-function states. These observations do not establish the superiority of either operative strategy.

articles.title: Preclinical Studies of MVT-100, A Novel Ultrasound Enhancing Agent.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Over the past decades, many investigations have used perfluorocarbon (PFC)-based contrast products to enhance ultrasound (US) imaging. Currently octafluoropropane (OFP), decafluorobutane, and sulfur hexafluoride or a combination of those gases is used for the preparation of ultrasound enhancing agents (UEA). This study reports the development of MVT-100, a novel microbubble ultrasound enhancing agent (UEA) designed for improved stability, safety, and imaging performance. The objective of these studies was to fully characterize and compare the biophysical, chemical and in vivo properties of the new UEA (herein referred to as MVT-100) as compared with the well-known and widely utilized UEA known as perflutren lipid microspheres (Perflutren) (commercialized under the name of Definity®).

METHODS: Analytical methods were used to characterize the MBs. Low mechanical index (MI) contrast-enhanced ultrasound was performed in mice and pigs.

RESULTS: Comparison of Perflutren MB with MVT-100 MB showed similarities of the products in their overall particle numbers, gas content, osmolality, pH and phospholipid concentrations. However, MVT-100 exhibited a zeta potential that was essentially neutral (+0.5 ± 0.1 mV), compared with the negative zeta potential of Perflutren (-4.2 ± 2.0 mV), a tighter size distribution and lower polydispersity index (0.114 ± 0.012 vs. 0.159 ± 0.036, p = 0.048). Under accelerated storage conditions (40°C for 4 weeks), MVT-100 demonstrated markedly greater lipid stability, with only 2.05% loss of total phospholipid content compared with 13.10% for Perflutren. Murine renal retention studies showed that MVT-100 MB exhibited significantly lower (∼2.5 fold) renal retention in the kidney as compared with Perflutren. In porcine studies, MVT-100 hemodynamic parameters were identical to those of Perflutren. Echocardiographic porcine studies showed that ventricular opacification and endocardial border delineation following MVT-100 administration were comparable between agents at early time points, with higher and more sustained opacification with MVT-100 at later time points (generalized linear mixed model: main effect of agent p < 0.001, time × agent interaction p < 0.001) and no evidence of a significant difference in acoustic shadowing between agents (p > 0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: MVT-100 is a novel UEA that exhibits promising properties as a new imaging agent for contrast echocardiography with appealing storage conditions.

articles.title: Advancing Dermal Microvascular Imaging: Ultra Micro-Angiography as a Novel Tool for Assessing Facial Skin in Healthy Adults.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Color Doppler ultrasonography has limitations in accurately observing dermal microvasculature in healthy adults. This study aimed to assess dermal microvascularity using ultra micro-angiography (UMA) and to compare the efficacy of color UMA (cUMA) and subtraction UMA (sUMA) in this context. Our findings suggest that UMA may be a valuable technique for evaluating the dermal microvasculature.

METHODS: In this multicenter, prospective investigation, 54 healthy adults (22 males and 32 females) were recruited to examine the facial dermis in the zygoma and buccal regions using UMA. Parameters such as dermal thickness, microvascular flow velocity, microvascular resistance, cUMA and sUMA were measured. The associations between cUMA or sUMA and dermal thickness, age and sex were analyzed using correlation statistics.

RESULTS: The facial dermis in the zygoma and buccal regions was thicker in males than in females, with statistically significant differences. In males, the peak systolic velocity and end-diastolic velocity were higher in both regions than in females, with significant differences. Contrarily, the resistance index did not differ significantly between the sexes. Both cUMA and sUMA showed a correlation with dermal thickness and sex but were independent of age. Notably, sUMA had a higher detection rate than cUMA, indicating its superior sensitivity in identifying the dermal microvasculature.

CONCLUSION: The dermal thickness and microvascular flow velocities varied significantly between the sexes, with sUMA proving more effective than cUMA in detecting the dermal microvasculature. These results indicate the potential of UMA as a robust tool for assessing the dermal microvasculature in healthy adults, suggesting broader applications in dermatological research, diagnostics and evaluation of disease treatment efficacy.

articles.title: Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Large-Vessel Vasculitis and Aortitis.
articles.abstract: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET/CT has emerged as a pivotal imaging modality for the diagnosis and management of large-vessel vasculitis (LVV) and aortitis. This review examines the current evidence and clinical applications of FDG-PET in giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, isolated aortitis, and infectious aortitis. Recent ACR/EULAR classification criteria now formally incorporate PET imaging findings, reflecting the modality's diagnostic importance. Meta-analyses report pooled sensitivities of approximately 80% to 84% and specificities of 87% to 89% for LVV diagnosis. The EANM/SNMMI joint procedural recommendations provide standardized protocols for patient preparation, image acquisition, and interpretation, including the use of visual grading scales.

articles.title: Valuable Role of Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Therapeutic Decision Making and Theranostics of Neurologic Disorders in Conjunction with Non-Fluorodeoxyglucose Tracers.
articles.abstract: Brain ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) is an important functional imaging modality for evaluating glucose metabolism. Over time, it has been observed that various metabolic patterns can support diagnoses, inform prognosis, guide therapeutic decision-making, and assess treatment response. Clinical applications span seizures, brain tumors, traumatic brain injury, neuroinflammatory and infectious disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and other chronic neurological conditions. Although FDG is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, its ability to characterize metabolism may contribute to treatment planning, particularly in molecularly targeted neuro-oncology. This chapter reviews established and investigational applications of brain FDG-PET, emphasizing disease characterization, therapeutic selection, and response assessment.

articles.title: Influence of non-thermal atmospheric plasma on the mechanical properties and phase stability of zirconia ceramics.
articles.journal: Dental materials : official publication of the Academy of Dental Materials
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of non-thermal atmospheric plasma (NTP) and blasting (BL) treatments on the flexural strength, phase transformation, and residual stress of zirconia ceramics.

METHODS: Bar-shaped specimens of 3Y-TZP (3Y, Classic Katana), 4Y-PSZ (4Y, STML Katana), and 5Y-PSZ (5Y, UTML Katana) were fabricated and assigned to untreated control, blasting (BL), or NTP groups (n = 10). Phase transformation was primarily assessed by Raman spectroscopy using untreated specimens as references, while XRD was used as a complementary technique for the BL- and NTP-treated specimens. Flexural strength (FS) and elastic modulus (E) were measured using a universal testing machine (1 mm/min, 5000 kgf load cell). Surface morphology was evaluated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Data were analyzed using Weibull statistics, two-way ANOVA, and Tukey's post-hoc test (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: Monoclinic phase formation was detected only in 3Y (7.1 ± 2.1%) and 4Y (1.7 ± 1.1%) zirconia after BL, while 5Y zirconia remained phase stable. No significant differences in FS or E were observed among the control, BL, and NTP groups within the zirconia composition. For both properties, 3Y exhibited the highest values, followed by 4Y and 5Y (p < 0.05). Weibull moduli did not differ significantly among the groups (p = 0.320). Positive Raman peak shifts consistent with relative compressive residual stress were observed in all BL-treated groups.

SIGNIFICANCE: Under the evaluated conditions, NTP did not produce detectable crystallographic or morphological alterations. However, its effectiveness as a pre-cementation treatment cannot be established because zirconia-resin bonding was not evaluated.

articles.title: Rehabilitation of elbow fractures and/or dislocations: An update on the current practice patterns of treating clinicians.
articles.journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elbow fractures and dislocations, though relatively uncommon, can result in long-term pain, stiffness, and disability, with hand therapists playing a key role in rehabilitation. New developments in assessment and intervention have been described in the literature since the previous published 2012 survey describing therapist practice patterns related to elbow rehabilitation.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this exploratory survey study was to investigate the current practice patterns of hand therapists in rehabilitating elbow fractures and/or dislocations.

STUDY DESIGN: Online survey research.

METHODS: A 51-item survey was developed by six certified hand therapists was distributed to active ASHT members to examine current rehabilitation practices for elbow fractures and/or dislocations. The anonymous, institutional review board-approved survey was administered via REDCap from April to June 2025 and assessed demographics, assessments, interventions, and orthosis use. Descriptive statistics and chi-square analyses were performed using REDCap, Excel, and SPSS, with significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Out of the total of 135 responses, ≤25% of hand therapist caseload was comprised of elbow fractures/dislocations. Most hand therapists reported therapy is typically initiated within 2 weeks and delivered twice weekly for a total of 16-20 visits. Nearly all respondents assessed active range of motion, edema, and activity of daily living status and administered the QuickDASH. Intervention strategies progressed initially from early immobilization and education to mobility, strengthening, and neuromuscular re-education. Orthosis utilization was primarily driven by range of motion limitations, with serial static orthoses most common. Experience level influenced visit volume, reliance on physician preference for orthoses, and discharge factors.

CONCLUSIONS: While traditional biomechanical approaches remain foundational, contemporary practice increasingly integrates biopsychosocial principles and advanced orthosis strategies, reflecting evolving clinical reasoning and knowledge translation across experience levels.

articles.title: Recovery of worsening renal function after acute heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Worsening renal function (WRF) is common during hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). However, the post-discharge trajectory of renal function in these patients remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the rate of WRF recovery after discharge and its prognostic significance.

METHODS: In a cohort of 2020 patients hospitalized for ADHF (TRI-AHF registry), serum creatinine was measured at admission, daily during hospitalization, and at 12 months after discharge. WRF was defined as a creatinine increase ≥0.3 mg/dL. Only patients who developed WRF during the index hospitalization were included. At the 12-month follow-up, WRF was classified as recovered if the change in creatinine from admission was <0.3 mg/dL, and persistent if ≥0.3 mg/dL. The primary endpoint was 5-year all-cause mortality after the 12-month creatinine reassessment.

RESULTS: During the study period, 331 patients (16%) experienced WRF. At 12 months, 157 (54%) had recovered WRF and 133 (46%) had persistent WRF. Older age, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and right ventricular dysfunction during hospitalization were independent predictors of persistent WRF. At 5-year follow-up after the 12-month assessment, recovered WRF was strongly associated with a lower risk of mortality compared with persistent WRF (adjusted HR=0.229, p < 0.001). The association between WRF recovery and improved survival was independent of prior chronic kidney disease and baseline creatinine, and appeared more pronounced in males than in females (p-int=0.034).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalized for ADHF who experienced WRF, 54% recovered renal function at 12 months. Recovery of WRF was associated with significantly better long-term survival compared with persistent WRF.

articles.title: Towards implementing genomic epidemiology for helminth control and elimination.
articles.abstract: Helminths, commonly referred to as parasitic worms, infect over a billion people and countless animals worldwide. Because they are major drivers of disease, understanding the epidemiology of helminth infections-what parasites are present, where they occur, and how they change over time-is key to controlling them. However, traditional diagnostic tools primarily measure infection status or intensity at a single time point, whereas effective control requires understanding changes over space and time, information these tools cannot directly capture. The increasing use of genomics is providing new, epidemiologically relevant insights into helminth population structure, transmission, zoonotic risk, and drug resistance. In this opinion article, we discuss the challenges and opportunities of applying genomics to helminth epidemiology, arguing that it will provide operationally meaningful information to support control efforts.

articles.title: Molecular imaging in adult spondylodiscitis: current evidence, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Adult spondylodiscitis is an infection of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies that may progress to paravertebral extension, epidural involvement, spinal instability, sepsis, and neurological compromise. Because clinical symptoms and laboratory markers are often nonspecific, imaging is central to diagnosis, assessment of disease extent, biopsy planning, and selective evaluation of treatment response. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains the first-line anatomical technique for early marrow, disc, epidural, and paraspinal disease, while computed tomography (CT) is valuable for osseous destruction, instability, and biopsy guidance. Molecular imaging complements these modalities by depicting biological activity rather than structure alone. Fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) is the most established molecular technique, offering high diagnostic performance, whole-body evaluation for multifocal or metastatic infection, and support for management when MRI is contraindicated, equivocal, or difficult to interpret after surgery. Its main limitations are limited pathogen specificity, uptake in sterile inflammatory or reparative processes, heterogeneous interpretation criteria, and uncertain thresholds for treatment monitoring. Emerging approaches, including hybrid positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI), fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) tracers, pathogen-targeted radiopharmaceuticals, quantitative PET biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI), remain investigational and require prospective validation of diagnostic and clinical utility. This review summarizes current evidence, clinical applications, limitations, and future directions for molecular imaging in spondylodiscitis.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical value of quantitative Na[18F]F PET/CT parameters to monitor therapeutic response in patients with benign metabolic bone diseases: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT is increasingly used to evaluate treatment responses in metabolic bone diseases (MBDs), where conventional serum biomarkers and structural imaging fail to show local dynamic changes. The performance and utility of Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT in these diseases, however, has not been fully explored. We systematically evaluated the contemporary use of quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT for measuring MBD treatment responses.

METHODS: Current review was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261413536) and follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for clinical studies using quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT in MBDs. Risk of bias was assessed via QUADAS-2, ROBINS-I and QUIPS. Results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies (n=14-72 patients; 358 total cases) met inclusion criteria, focusing on chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD, n=9 studies) and fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome (FD/MAS, n=4 studies). Two longitudinal studies evaluated therapeutic response: denosumab in FD/MAS yielded comparable reductions in total lesion metabolic activity across moderate (-64.9%) and high doses (-67.0%), while turnover-guided therapy in CKD-MBD significantly reduced bone kinetic flux (Ki). Remaining literature comprised cross-sectional and observational cohorts. Here, PET kinetic (Ki, FUR) and volumetric metrics (TV, TA, TLF) correlated strongly with bone formation rates and circulating biomarkers. Ki and background-adjusted uptake ratios (SUVR) discriminated bone turnover states with high accuracy (ROC AUC up to 0.98), outperforming serum parathyroid hormone in CKD-MBD. Reporting of reconstruction settings was highly variable; only one study explicitly noted EARL scanner accreditation and none documented compliance with EARL Standard 1 or 2. Risk of bias was primarily driven by small cohort sizes, attrition and unadjusted confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative Na[¹⁸F]F PET/CT provides high diagnostic accuracy for tracking regional turnover and treatment response in benign MBDs. However, clinical adoption is hindered by a lack of harmonized EARL-compliant protocols, unstandardized outcome metrics and a reliance on small, unadjusted cohorts.

articles.title: Companion animal nuclear medicine: A translational evidence map for dogs and cats.
articles.abstract: Companion animals occupy an increasingly important clinical and societal space, with dogs and cats often managed as family members and receiving advanced diagnostic and therapeutic care. Many veterinary nuclear medicine procedures are adapted from human practice, while naturally occurring canine and feline diseases provide opportunities for comparative and translational insight. This review mapped and synthesised the literature on nuclear medicine imaging and radionuclide therapy in dogs and cats, with emphasis on clinically mature applications and relevance to human nuclear medicine. A PRISMA-aligned systematic evidence map with focused narrative synthesis were undertaken. MEDLINE via PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched, with supplementary Google Scholar searching, reference-list screening and citation mining. Because of heterogeneity in species, indication, radiopharmaceutical, protocol, comparator and outcome reporting, formal meta-analysis was not performed. A total of 228 articles were included. The literature was predominantly imaging-focused, with 176 articles addressing imaging alone, 34 therapy alone and 18 both imaging and therapy. Feline nuclear medicine was dominated by thyroid disease, particularly thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism. Canine nuclear medicine was broader, including oncology PET/CT, osteosarcoma imaging and therapy, renal and hepatobiliary functional scintigraphy, portosystemic shunt imaging, neurology/behavioural imaging, thyroid carcinoma and radiosynoviorthesis. PET/CT was most prominent in canine oncology, while conventional scintigraphy remained important where functional information could not be replaced by structural imaging. Companion animal nuclear medicine is clinically useful and translationally relevant. Its most mature model is feline thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy, while its most dynamic future directions lie in canine oncology, molecular imaging and radiotheranostics. Closer collaboration between veterinary specialists and human nuclear medicine professionals may improve companion animal care while informing broader development of molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy.

articles.title: Imaging of myositis: An overview and update.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are heterogeneous autoimmune disorders that affect skeletal muscle and may involve the skin, lungs, heart, gastrointestinal tract, or be associated with malignancy. Imaging supports phenotyping, biopsy targeting, assessment of disease burden, and monitoring. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains the principal modality for muscle assessment, depicting edema, fascial and subcutaneous inflammation, fatty replacement, and atrophy without ionizing radiation. Whole-body MRI maps disease distribution, whereas quantitative techniques, including Dixon fat-fraction imaging and T2 mapping, provide objective measures of activity and chronic damage. Ultrasound offers a portable, inexpensive adjunct, although operator dependence and limited standardization restrict comprehensive assessment. For nuclear medicine, 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT provides a complementary whole-body measure of metabolism, potentially identifying muscle inflammation, interstitial lung disease, other systemic manifestations, and occult malignancy in selected patients. Physiologic muscle uptake and heterogeneous acquisition and quantification protocols limit specificity and prevent universal PET thresholds. Hybrid PET/MRI combines metabolic and structural characterization, but evidence supporting routine use remains limited. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET is an emerging pathway-targeted approach with preliminary evidence in muscle and myositis-associated lung disease. This review summarizes imaging patterns across major myositis phenotypes, contrasts established and investigational uses of MRI, ultrasound, FDG PET/CT, PET/MRI, and emerging tracers, illustrates important mimics and pitfalls, and proposes a practical multimodality imaging approach.

articles.title: The PRIMA Model: A Heuristic Multilevel Framework for the Clinical Evaluation and Management of Bruxism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bruxism is a multifactorial masticatory muscle behaviour with complex mechanisms and heterogeneous clinical expression, ranging from physiological to potentially harmful depending on its consequences. Frameworks such as the STAB enable structured data collection but were not designed to guide the interpretation of findings when management is clinically warranted.

OBJECTIVE: To present the PRIMA model (Pattern-Responsive Inference Model for Multidomain Assessment of Bruxism), an exploratory, hypothesis-generating framework intended to support-not replace-structured clinical reasoning.
