After prompt removal of the implanted central venous port, he received sequential antifungal therapy with micafungin, liposomal amphotericin B, voriconazole, and long-term itraconazole suppression. Blood cultures cleared, and serial transthoracic echocardiography showed no clinically significant progression of the tricuspid vegetation. At more than 590 days after diagnosis, he remains alive without recurrent fungemia while receiving oral itraconazole. This case suggests that nonsurgical management with source control, systemic antifungal therapy guided by clinical response and antifungal susceptibility information, and long-term azole suppression may be a feasible option for selected patients with E. dermatitidis FE when surgery is not possible.

articles.title: Delayed but not denied…. Interpreting late improvement in global longitudinal strain with aficamten in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Estimating the unmeasured: opportunities and limitations of nonexercise cardiorespiratory fitness assessment in heart failure.
Reframing Dietary Potassium Management in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Proportionate, Risk-Informed Approach for Multidisciplinary Practice.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Dietary potassium restriction is a longstanding component of nutrition care in chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its application often varies across practice settings and lacks consistent evidence for improved clinical outcomes. While clinicians routinely balance biochemical risk, nutritional adequacy, and patient context, the reasoning behind potassium-related decisions is rarely made visible in guidelines or multidisciplinary practice. This paper introduces the Proportionate Potassium Management Framework (PPMF), a practice-oriented model that supports transparent, risk-calibrated dietary decisions in CKD care. The framework prioritises systematic consideration of non-dietary contributors to hyperkalaemia and promotes selective, context-sensitive use of dietary restriction. Rather than prescribing uniform actions, the PPMF legitimises professional judgement as a core safety mechanism, offering a structure for documenting and justifying dietary decisions in complex, uncertain, or contested cases. In doing so, it aims to support nutritionally adequate, person-centred care without compromising biochemical safety or team accountability.

articles.title: Resting Energy Expenditure in Mechanically Ventilated Surgical-Trauma Patients With and Without Acute Kidney Injury: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare resting energy expenditure (REE) measured by indirect calorimetry (IC) in mechanically ventilated surgical-trauma critically ill patients with and without acute kidney injury (AKI); to evaluate differences in REE by sex, age, and body mass index (BMI); and to assess associations between REE, psoas muscle index (PMI) measured using computed tomography scans, and lean body mass (LBM) estimated by predictive equations.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary academic medical center included mechanically ventilated critically ill adults admitted between 01/01/2012 and 12/31/2023. Exclusion criteria were pediatric, pregnant, or incarcerated patients; quadriplegia, paraplegia, cystic fibrosis; abnormal respiratory quotients; Medical ICU admission; major burns (≥20% TBSA); parenteral nutrition initiated on or after IC; tracheostomy on admission; discharge or death while ventilated; or absence of a nutrition prescription.

RESULTS: Of 794 patients screened, 180 met inclusion criteria (AKI n=84; no AKI n=96). At baseline, patients with and without AKI differed significantly in age (59.9 vs 55 years; P = 0.046), BMI (32.2 vs 28.8 kg/m2; P = 0.046), CKD (23.8% vs 3.13%; P < 0.001), and serum creatinine (1.49 vs 0.84 mg/dL; P < 0.001). Of patients with AKI, 71.4% had stage I AKI and 20.2% required renal replacement therapy (RRT). No significant difference in mean REE was observed between patients with and without AKI (1,642 vs 1,665 kcal/day; P = 0.380) . REE was significantly higher in males compared with females (1,806 vs 1,425 kcal/day; P < 0.001), in patients aged 18-65 versus >65 years (1,768 vs 1,428 kcal/day; P = 0.002), and in obese versus non-obese patients (1,841 vs 1,500 kcal/day; P < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, higher BMI (P = 0.003) and male sex (P = 0.028) were independently associated with higher REE, while AKI was not. LBM estimated by predictive equations was more strongly correlated with REE than PMI (P < 0.001), and correlation strength did not differ by AKI status.

CONCLUSIONS: Measured REE did not differ between ventilated surgical-trauma patients with and without AKI. REE differed by sex, age, and obesity status, and AKI was not associated with within-group differences. BMI and sex were identified as independent predictors of REE. Estimated LBM was strongly correlated with REE independent of AKI status. Given possible residual confounding, further investigation is needed.

articles.title: Optimizing Intraoperative Tissue Sampling in Hip and Knee Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Deep Bone Provides Higher Culture Yield in One-Stage Exchange.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a challenging complication after hip and knee arthroplasty. Accurate pathogen identification is essential for successful treatment, yet the optimal anatomical site for intraoperative microbiological sampling remains uncertain. This study evaluated whether microbiological yield differs by sampling location and whether this differs between hip and knee PJI.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 255 patients who underwent one-stage exchange for PJI (142 hips and 113 knees). Intraoperative specimens were categorized as deep bone, superficial bone, or soft tissue, and culture positivity rates were compared across sites. Generalized estimating equations evaluated the association between sampling site and culture positivity, adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), Charlson Comorbidity Index, and number of samples.

RESULTS: In hip PJI, culture positivity was 80.8 (273 of 338) for deep bone, 79.6 (370 of 465) for soft tissue, and 65.9% (135 of 205) for superficial bone; in knee PJI, positivity was 80.5 (248 of 308), 71.7 (279 of 389), and 65.4% (123 of 188), respectively. After adjustment, deep bone sampling had higher odds of culture positivity than superficial bone and soft tissue sampling (odds ratio [OR], 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05 to 2.25), with similar effects in both joints. Soft tissue sampling was more likely to yield positive cultures in hip than knee PJI (OR, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.27 to 3.78). Higher BMI was independently associated with lower culture positivity.

CONCLUSIONS: Deep bone sampling provided the highest microbiological yield in both hip and knee PJI, while superficial bone sampling consistently showed the lowest positivity. Soft-tissue sampling performed particularly well in hip PJI, supporting its complementary role during intraoperative microbiological sampling.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review Informed by a Systematic Search.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of mortality, and early identification of phenotypes, exacerbation risk, and treatment response remains challenging. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for improving prediction, classification, and monitoring in COPD. This narrative review, informed by a systematic search, evaluated current AI applications in COPD management.

METHODS: The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024502765) and reported with reference to PRISMA 2020 principles. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to May 2025. Eligible studies applied Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Deep Learning approaches to adult COPD populations for diagnostic, prognostic, monitoring, phenotyping, or disease management purposes. Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers, and methodological quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. AI demonstrated high discriminative accuracy for COPD diagnosis, exacerbation prediction, and mortality risk (mean Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve [AUROC] = 0.83), although methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation were common. Models integrating multimodal data generally outperformed single-domain approaches. Risk-of-bias assessment identified concerns related to small sample sizes, limited external validation, and incomplete reporting of model development and validation procedures.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence suggests that AI may support COPD diagnosis, prognostic prediction, and telemonitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, and inconsistent reporting standards continue to limit clinical translation. Further high-quality, externally validated studies are needed to support implementation in respiratory care.

articles.title: Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio and 28-Day Mortality in Older Postoperative ICU Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study With MIMIC-IV Replication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older postoperative intensive care patients have heterogeneous mortality risk related to acute illness severity, frailty, reduced physiological reserve. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) integrates routinely available markers of perioperative physiological stress, but its prognostic value remains uncertain.

METHODS: Patients aged ≥65 years admitted to postoperative intensive care unit were prospectively enrolled. LAR was measured at ICU admission, whereas APACHE II used the worst values during the first 24 hours. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. LAR was compared with lactate, albumin, blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, Prognostic Nutritional Index, and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet index. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, APACHE II score, Clinical Frailty Scale score, surgical urgency, and comorbidity burden. A harmonized replication analysis was conducted in MIMIC-IV surgical ICU cohort. Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples provided optimism-corrected estimates of discrimination, calibration, and overall model performance.

RESULTS: Among 647 patients, 79 (12.2%) died within 28 days. LAR showed the highest discrimination (AUC, 0.803; 95% CI, 0.753-0.851) and was independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR per SD, 3.40; 95% CI, 2.33-4.96). LAR slightly outperformed lactate as a single marker (ΔAUC, 0.029; p=0.002). Clinical models with LAR or lactate showed similar discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.885 vs 0.883; ΔAUC, 0.0014; 95% CI, -0.0071 to 0.0099; p=0.750). In MIMIC-IV, LAR remained independently associated with 28-day mortality (OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.28-1.94; AUC, 0.704).

CONCLUSIONS: LAR was independently associated with 28-day mortality and performed similarly to lactate when added to the 24-hour clinical model, supporting its role as a complementary biomarker. The association was reproduced in MIMIC-IV with attenuation.

articles.title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leaks in Necrotizing Pneumonia and Complex Pleuropulmonary Infections: A National Analysis of Safety and Efficacy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endobronchial valve (EBV) placement for persistent air leaks (PAL) in active pulmonary infection remains controversial due to foreign body concerns. We compared EBV outcomes in infected patients against non-infectious controls.

METHODS: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2023) for adults undergoing EBV placement for air leaks. Cohorts were stratified into non-infectious air leaks and complex pleuropulmonary infections. The primary outcome was clinical failure defined as mortality, surgical intervention, or new chest tube placement.

RESULTS: Of 1,760 weighted patients, 52.6% had non-infectious leaks and 47.4% complex infections. Complex infection patients had longer length of stay (24.9 vs 16.0 days, p<0.001) and higher hospital costs ($93,817 vs $46,669, p<0.001). In multivariate analysis, infection was not an independent predictor of failure (p=0.994); however, mechanical ventilation (aOR 3.00; p<0.001) was associated with clinical failure in the adjusted model, and MRSA pneumonia (aOR 3.90; p=0.030) was associated with clinical failure in a separate pathogen-adjusted analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Among EBV-treated hospitalizations, Complex Infection was not significantly associated with composite clinical failure after adjustment, though device extraction rates were notably higher in this cohort. Mechanical ventilation was associated with clinical failure in the main adjusted model, and MRSA was associated with clinical failure in a separate pathogen-adjusted analysis.

articles.title: The natural history of Mycobacterium abscessus in Cystic Fibrosis and the impact of Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium abscessus complex presents a challenge in cystic fibrosis patients, ranging from asymptomatic colonization to progressive pulmonary disease. Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulators, particularly elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor, have shown a potential impact on microbiological pathogens in patients' airways. Our study aimed to evaluate the natural history of Mycobacterium abscessus infection and the impact of the modulators in this population.

METHODS: A single center retrospective cohort study among 55 cystic fibrosis patients between 2000 and 2025, comparing 28 patients with Mycobacterium abscessus sputum isolation to 27 cystic fibrosis controls. Patients with pulmonary disease (n=12) were compared to colonized patients (n=16). Pulmonary function tests and body mass index were assessed longitudinally, and clinical and microbiological outcomes were recorded. We then reassessed Mycobacterium abscessus positive patients on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (n=20) and evaluated changes in microbiological outcomes.

RESULTS: Patients with pulmonary disease exhibited significant declines in lung function compared to controls (mean Δ forced expiratory volume in the 1st second -32.5% vs -4.9%; p = 0.020). Colonized patients showed no differences compared to controls (p=0.752). Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor treated patients demonstrated a marked reduction in culture positivity after initiation, with 85% eradication rates.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates the different natural history of Mycobacterium abscessus infection in cystic fibrosis patients between pulmonary disease versus colonized patients; pulmonary disease is associated with patient deterioration despite aggressive antibiotic regimens. We also suggest a marked association between elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor initiation and eradication of Mycobacterium abscessus from the sputum of both colonized patients and those with pulmonary disease.

articles.title: Generalizing clinical data to the community: Estimated population prevalence of inflammatory biomarkers and lung function among people with obstructive lung disease.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To estimate the real-world distribution of physician-assessed severity, spirometric characteristics and inflammatory biomarkers in adults with asthma and/or COPD by translating data from an observational study to a general population survey.

METHODS: We used data from Australian participants with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD from the observational NOVELTY study (NCT02760329) and a web-based survey of a nationally-representative population (ACTRN12619001572156); the survey included 57 patient-reported variables from NOVELTY. We developed an imputation model to estimate severity, spirometry and biomarkers in the population-based sample.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Participants with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD in NOVELTY (n=818) were similar to those in the general population (n=1,510), except for older age, less smoking and greater inhaled corticosteroid use. Estimated prevalence of mild disease was 54%(asthma, 95%CI 38.3-69.4), 42%(asthma+COPD, 95%CI 24.4-60.4) and 51%(COPD, 95%CI 30.5-70.6). Estimated prevalence of post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.7 was 39.8%(32.5-47.2), 53.9%(41.9-66.0) and 61.2%(51.0-71.4); of blood eosinophil count ≥0.3x109/L was 24.3%(14.4-34.3), 23.0%(8.2-37.7) and 20.6%(10.2-31.1), and of FeNO≥25ppb was 42.6%(31.9-53.3), 33.8%(21.4-46.1) and 32.4%(21.5-43.2), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first population-based estimates of disease severity, persistent airflow limitation and Type-2 biomarkers among Australian adults with asthma and/or COPD. Using a nationally-representative web-based survey together with a stratified observational study, we estimated that over half of community patients with asthma or COPD diagnoses had mild disease, and elevated FeNO was more prevalent than elevated blood eosinophils. The estimated prevalence of persistent airflow limitation (40% in asthma, only 61% in COPD) suggests potential for over/under-diagnosis in the community.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation as Rescue Therapy for Patients with Suspected High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) who cannot undergo computed tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) because of unstable hemodynamics, the optimal strategy, namely, prioritizing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or revascularization, remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether prioritizing ECMO is associated with increased survival rates.

METHODS: A total of 117 patients with suspected high-risk PE admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) at four ECMO centers were retrospectively enrolled (2013-2024).

RESULTS: Among these patients, 79 received ECMO (ECMO group), whereas 38 underwent thrombolysis therapy (thrombolysis group). The baseline and preintervention management characteristics were comparable between the groups. In-hospital mortality was lower in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (33/79, 41.8% vs 22/38, 57.9%), although the difference was not significant (P=0.15). Multivariate Cox analysis revealed that treatment with ECMO was associated with a reduced risk of in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio [HR]=0.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.79, P=0.006). An elevated pretreatment Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score was identified as an independent risk factor for mortality (HR=1.14, 95% CI 1.06-1.22, P<0.001). Kaplan‒Meier curves and log-rank tests revealed better 28-day survival in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (P=0.041). Among the 79 patients who received ECMO, 63 had CTPA-verified high-risk PE, with 34 surviving to discharge (34/63, 54.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: For hemodynamically unstable patients with suspected high-risk PE, prioritizing ECMO is a safe strategy that serves as an independent protective factor against in-hospital mortality, despite nonsignificant findings in unadjusted analyses. Larger studies are warranted to validate these results.

articles.title: Impact of Cranioplasty on Cerebral Blood Flow, CSF Dynamics, and Neurocognitive Recovery: A Prospective Imaging-based Study.
articles.journal: Journal of neurological surgery. Part A, Central European neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) is a life-saving procedure for severe traumatic brain injury and stroke but results in loss of cranial integrity, impaired cerebral blood flow (CBF), altered cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics, and cognitive dysfunction. Cranioplasty is believed to restore these physiological disturbances. However, prospective imaging-based evaluations remain limited in this context, particularly in Indian populations. This study prospectively assessed the impact of cranioplasty on CBF, CSF flow dynamics, and neurocognitive recovery.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted on 100 patients undergoing cranioplasty following DC. CBF was quantified using arterial spin-labeling MRI across bilateral frontal, temporal, parietal, and occipital lobes. CSF dynamics including peak positive velocity (PPV), peak negative velocity (PNV), and net flow were measured at the aqueduct and foramen of Magendie using phase-contrast MRI. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) preoperatively, early postoperatively, and at 3 months. Pre-post changes were analyzed using paired tests with significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Cranioplasty resulted in significant improvement in CBF across all lobes bilaterally (p < 0.001) with more pronounced gains on the ipsilateral side. CSF flow showed marked increase in PPV and PNV at both anatomical levels (p < 0.001) accompanied by improved net flow. MoCA scores improved significantly from baseline, with 90% of patients achieving scores in the normal cognitive range at 3 months (p < 0.001). No major postoperative complications were observed.

CONCLUSION: Cranioplasty significantly enhances cerebral perfusion, CSF dynamics, and cognitive function following DC. These findings underscore the physiological value of cranioplasty and support the integration of advanced imaging to guide postoperative recovery and optimize timing of reconstruction.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor activation attenuates chronic migraine-like behaviour: Sex-specific modulation of opioid- and endocannabinoid-related pathways.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Chronic migraine (CM) is a highly disabling condition that remains suboptimally treated. Metabolic disturbances may trigger migraine chronification, whereas impaired endogenous pain inhibition contributes to CM development. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), used for type 2 diabetes and obesity, show efficacy in chronic pain models. We evaluated the prophylactic effects of liraglutide, semaglutide and dulaglutide compared with propranolol (reference drug), potential opioidergic/endocannabinoid involvement and sex differences in a CM model.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Chronic migraine-like hypersensitivity was induced by repeated nitroglycerin administration in male and female mice. The prophylactic effects of GLP-1RAs and propranolol were examined using von Frey, acetone and orofacial glutamate tests. Body weight and glucose tolerance were monitored to evaluate metabolic safety. Potential opioidergic/endocannabinoid involvement in semaglutide-induced antinociception (selected GLP-1RA class representative) was assessed by pharmacological blockade and/or quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis of pain-related neurobiomarker mRNA expression in brainstem and trigeminal ganglia.

KEY RESULTS: Liraglutide, semaglutide and dulaglutide dose-dependently attenuated CM-like hypersensitivity in both sexes, with efficacy comparable to propranolol. GLP-1RAs did not affect metabolic parameters, whereas propranolol induced male-specific hyperglycaemia. Semaglutide-induced antinociception was partially sensitive to naloxone and was associated with sex-dimorphic, brainstem-specific transcriptional changes in opioid- and endocannabinoid-related pathways. Semaglutide increased Glp1r, Cnr1, Pomc, Pcsk1 and Pcsk2 mRNA expression in males, whereas it up-regulated Glp1r and down-regulated Faah and Mgll in females.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: GLP-1RAs exert class-wide antinociceptive effects in a preclinical CM model, with semaglutide-based analyses suggesting sex-specific modulation of central opioid- and endocannabinoid-related pathways. These findings support further investigation of GLP-1RAs as prophylactic strategies for migraine, particularly in individuals with metabolic comorbidities.

articles.title: Swimming and Shooting in Water Polo Players: Associations Between Shoulder Muscle Activation and Shoulder Pain.
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional study aimed to compare shoulder muscle activation patterns during front-crawl swimming and overhead throwing between water polo players with unilateral shoulder pain and matched asymptomatic players using surface electromyography analysis. A total of 16 water polo players were recruited and divided into 2 groups: athletes with unilateral shoulder pain (pain, n = 8) and asymptomatic controls (control, n = 8). Surface electromyography analysis highlighted activation of 9 muscles of the shoulder complex during the overhead shot task and front-crawl stroke task. During the overhead shot task, water polo players with shoulder pain showed lower activation of the serratus anterior (F1,14 = 6.767, P = .021, ηp2 = .326) and upper trapezius (F1,14 = 7.864, P = .014, ηp2 = .360) compared with controls. Lower activation of serratus anterior (F1,14 = 20.005, P = .001, ηp2 = .588) and upper trapezius (F1,14 = 18.287, P = .001, ηp2 = .354) was found in the pain group compared with controls, even during the front-crawl stroke task. Overall, these findings suggest water polo players with shoulder pain could present a reduced activation of scapular stabilizers during sport-specific tasks, which may contribute to altered scapulothoracic kinematics and increased shoulder injury risk.

articles.title: Dermatitis and Corynebacterium bovis infection in athymic nude rats (Rattus norvegicus).
articles.abstract: Corynebacterium bovis (Cb) is a bacterium that causes a flaking dermatitis characterized histologically by orthokeratosis, acanthosis, intracorneal bacterial colonies and variable dermal inflammation in immunodeficient mice. Although Cb has been shown to establish dermal colonization in rats, its impact on the skin of immunodeficient rats remains poorly defined. This case series characterizes cutaneous lesions in 22 naïve or experimentally manipulated NIH-Fox1rnu (nude) rats and evaluates the association between Cb infection and dermatitis over a 5-year period. Histologically, all rats had orthokeratosis and dermatitis/folliculitis, 21/22 had acanthosis, 15/22 had bacterial presence and 9/22 had transepidermal/transfollicular keratinocyte apoptosis. Additional variable findings included furunculosis, pustules, dermal oedema and perivascular dermatitis. Inflammatory infiltrates consisted of CD3-positive lymphocytes and Iba1-positive macrophages located predominantly at the dermoepidermal junction. Corynebacterium bovis was isolated from the skin of 15/22 affected rats, and in-situ hybridization confirmed intracorneal/intrafollicular colonies of Cb in 3/11 rats examined. Nude rats also developed cutaneous lesions that corresponded histologically with a lymphocytic dermatitis, the distribution of which was often independent of Cb colonies. This study documents the first spontaneous Cb infection with dermatitis in nude rats. The frequent isolation of Cb from the skin raises the question of whether alterations in the cutaneous microbiome of nude rats may contribute to the immune modulation of dermatitis, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Integrated query of three open-source bioinformatics tools to reveal clinical and molecular insights into environmental determinants of disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We have developed a suite of open-source clinical and biomedical informatics applications to facilitate translational science. The Integrated Clinical and Environmental Exposures Service (ICEES) provides regulatory-compliant access to integrated clinical and environmental exposures data. Reasoning Over Biomedical Objects linked in Knowledge Oriented Pathways (ROBOKOP) is a knowledge graph (KG)-based system for exploration of integrated and harmonized biomedical knowledge sources. Causal Activity Model (CAM) Knowledge Provider (KP) exposes causal inferences between biomedical entities and the connections between them. The applications are interoperable and can be queried via a common endpoint or independently to yield unique clinical and biomedical insights. In this study, we aimed to sequentially query the three independent applications to demonstrate their complementary nature and the value of a user-driven approach to derive mechanistic insights into environmental determinants of asthma, our application use case.

METHODS: We developed a use case on environmental determinants of asthma, focusing specifically on exposure to airborne particulate matter and its effects on asthma exacerbations. We framed our queries in the context of the proposed role of toll-like receptors (TLRs) in asthma. We first queried ICEES via an open application programming interface to examine the relationship between exposure to airborne particulate matter and asthma exacerbations among patients with chronic pulmonary disease. We then used the ICEES results as input for query of the ROBOKOP question-builder to explore biological mechanisms that might explain the ICEES-derived clinical observations on particulate matter exposure and asthma by way of establishing connections in the ROBOKOP KG that link particulate matter to asthma. The CAM KP user interface was queried to extend the mechanistic insights derived from ROBOKOP to identify causal relationships between the biomedical entities.

RESULTS: ICEES showed that exposure to high levels of airborne particulate matter was associated with an increase in asthma exacerbations, with African Americans showing higher overall rates of asthma exacerbations than Caucasians. ROBOKOP established connections between particulate matter and asthma by first establishing that a particulate matter - TLR4 - MYD88 connection exists in the ROBOKOP KG, as suggested in the literature, and then exploring genes and biological processes or activities that connect MYD88 to asthma. We highlight an example assertion that: particulate matter increases the response to TLR4, which physically and genetically interacts with MYD88, which catalyzes cytokine receptor binding by IL-5, which is genetically associated with asthma. CAM KP extended the ROBOKOP findings to identify a causal relationship between the TLR4 pathway and the immunologically relevant genes LY96, CD14, RELA, and TNF.

CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that user-driven sequential query of ICEES, ROBOKOP, and CAM KP provides a more complete understanding of the role of environmental determinants in disease than each service can provide independently. The three open applications are interoperable and complementary and together provide powerful tools to derive mechanistic insights into asthma and other diseases.

articles.title: Psychological predictors of work readiness among music students: The roles of career self-efficacy, career adaptability, and self-perceived employability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, music graduates have faced increasing challenges in the job market, with insufficient work readiness identified as one of the key influencing factors. However, empirical research on the antecedents of work readiness among music students in the Chinese context remains limited. This study aims to explore the effects of career self-efficacy, career adaptability, and self-perceived employability on the work readiness of Chinese undergraduate music students.

METHODS: Using a cross-sectional survey design, stratified convenience sampling was conducted across eight universities in China. A total of 427 questionnaires were collected, with 414 valid responses retained after excluding invalid ones. To investigate the relationship between various psychological variables and work readiness, as well as their relative explanatory power, this study employed descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression analysis to examine predictive relationships and the relative contributions of variables.

RESULTS: The findings revealed that all three variables were significantly associated with work readiness and explained a substantial proportion of its variance, with self-perceived employability showing the strongest predictive effect.

CONCLUSION: At the curricular level, this study proposes that integrating career planning modules and mock interviews into the curriculum can enhance music students' awareness of their employability. Furthermore, the study emphasises that universities should align their curriculum design more closely with market demands, thereby improving students' self-perceived employability and facilitating their smooth transition into the labour market. These findings contribute to informing music curriculum design and career guidance practices for music students in China.

articles.title: Metabolic and functional correlates of first transitions to low muscle strength and memory reserve across four longitudinal cohorts.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Muscle strength and episodic memory are linked in later life, but factors associated with their first transitions to low reserve remain uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed four longitudinal cohorts of adults aged 50-100 years with at least three synchronous strength and memory assessments. Participants entered follow-up when both cohort-standardized residual scores exceeded -1 SD. Continuous-time panel multistate models estimated muscle-first and memory-first transition intensities. Cohort-specific effects were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with Hartung-Knapp inference. The primary contrast was the ratio of covariate-specific intensity ratios (IRRs) for memory-first versus muscle-first transitions.

RESULTS: The primary analysis included 46,356 participants, with 6,036 first observed muscle-first, 8,539 memory-first and 897 both-low transitions. Older age was associated with a relative memory-first pattern (IRR ratio per 5 years 1.110, 95% CI 1.082-1.139); activities of daily living (ADL) limitation was associated with a relative muscle-first pattern (0.664, 95% CI 0.559-0.788). Diabetes was associated with higher intensities in both domains, but its pathway contrast remained uncertain (0.751, 95% CI 0.554-1.019; P=0.058). Age and ADL associations persisted after adjustment for baseline reserve and multimorbidity and when participants with two assessments were included. Age-specific SD thresholds attenuated the age contrast to 1.048 (95% CI 1.016-1.081). Diabetes findings varied with the low-reserve threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: Age and ADL limitation were associated with different relative patterns of first low-reserve transitions. Diabetes was associated with higher transition intensities in both domains without a clear pathway difference at the primary threshold. These observational associations do not establish a biological sequence or clinical screening thresholds.

articles.title: Mediating role of frailty in the association between systolic blood pressure trajectories and catastrophic health expenditure among middle-aged and older adults: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine hypertension management primarily targets acute cardiovascular events, frequently overlooking progressive physiological decline (frailty) and its economic implications. This study aimed to identify systolic blood pressure (SBP) trajectories and evaluate the mediating role of frailty in their association with catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among middle-aged and older adults.

METHODS: We analyzed 3996 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Group-based trajectory modeling identified SBP evolution patterns (2011-2015). The 2015 Frailty Index (FI), based on a 27-item deficit accumulation model, served as the mediator. The primary outcome was CHE in 2018, defined as annual household healthcare expenditure exceeding 40% of the household's capacity to pay. Mediation analysis quantified total, direct, and indirect effects.

RESULTS: Three SBP trajectories emerged: "Low-stable" (50.0%), "Moderate-increasing" (41.3%), and "High-decreasing" (8.7%). Compared with the Low-stable group, the High-decreasing trajectory was significantly associated with higher 2015 FI scores (β=0.029, P<0.001). A statistically significant indirect effect through frailty was observed for the association between the High-decreasing trajectory and CHE in 2018 (ACME = 0.0084, 95% CI: 0.0031-0.0100, P < 0.001), although the direct and total effects were not statistically significant. Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses using alternative CHE definitions and BMI trajectories.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty may be one pathway linking the High-decreasing SBP trajectory with subsequent household CHE. These observational findings support considering functional health alongside blood pressure in middle-aged and older adults. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal relationships and to assess whether incorporating frailty assessments into cardiovascular management improves clinical and socioeconomic outcomes.

articles.title: Assessing hemodynamic responses in patients undergoing oral surgery with vasoconstrictor-enhanced local anesthesia: a prospective comparative study between medically compromised and healthy participants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The present study deals with hemodynamic responses between different types of patients along different stages of operations.

METHODS: In a prospective clinical trial,(approved by the IRB approval number 275-15-ASF) and patient informed consent for the procedure, hemodynamic responses were evaluated before and during minor oral surgical procedures performed under local anesthesia. The study encompassed both medically compromised patients (experimental group) and healthy individuals (control group). Hemodynamic parameters, including blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation, were monitored. Statistical analysis was conducted to compare parameter fluctuations within each group and patient. Additionally, clinical indicators were documented using a visual analogue scale. Table 1 presents the characteristics of each group regarding age,gender, medical situation and sort of surgical procedure.

RESULTS: The study findings revealed consistent hemodynamic stability across all stages of the procedures. Patients in both groups maintained stable blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation levels prior to and during all stages of surgery. Medically compromised patients showed hemodynamic trends comparable to healthy controls. Local anesthesia with vasoconstrictors demonstrated stable profiles and pain management was effective.

CONCLUSION: Local anesthesia containing adrenaline (1:100,000) demonstrated safety in hemodynamic parameters of healthy and medically compromised patients undergoing minor oral surgery. Overall, hemodynamic fluctuations were minimal, underscoring both the efficacy and safety of using vasoconstrictor-containing local anesthetics for pain management in a controlled hypertension and other well-managed chronic conditions.

articles.title: Silver nanodot embedded waste PET nanofibres for efficient multifunctional air filter.
articles.abstract: This study focuses on conversion of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into ultrafine nanofibres with silver nanodots (AgND) (diameter 3.49 ± 0.94 nm) embedded within via electrospinning. Ultrafine PET (diameter 74 ± 15 nm) or PET-AgND (diameter 68 ± 17.4 nm) nanofibre-based membranes (basis weight 0.5 ± 0.02 g/m2, thickness 20 ± 1.4 μm), sandwiched between two spun-bond nonwoven layers, achieved a remarkable particle filtration efficiency (PFE) of 99.24-99.93% against 10-1000 nm particles, while maintaining pressure drop (ΔP) of 13 Pa at a face velocity of 5 cm/s. Such 3-ply filters demonstrated PFE > 99.5% against 350 nm particles with ΔP between 13-27 Pa over 28 consecutive filtration cycles. The PET-AgND membranes also demonstrated antibacterial efficacy of 99.78 ± 0.18% against Escherichia coli and 99.92 ± 0.02% against Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Washability assessments showed reduction of PFE from 99.7% to 57.6% with increment in pressure drop from 13 to 79 Pa, from unwashed till 9 washing-drying trials. The 3-ply filters also exhibited significant air permeability (64.4 ± 0.25 cm3/cm2-s), water vapor transmission rate (82.45 ± 2.7 g3/m2-h) coupled with prominent UV protection (79.5%). This study highlights a sustainable route for converting waste PET into high-performance, multifunctional, filter media.

articles.title: circGDI2 promotes epithelial IL-33 release and allergic airway inflammation in asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysregulated epithelial alarmin release is a key driver of chronic airway inflammation in asthma. Interleukin-33 (IL-33), released from activated airway epithelial cells, amplifies type 2 immune responses, yet the upstream mechanisms that link epithelial stress to IL-33 secretion remain incompletely defined. We investigated whether circGDI2 contributed to epithelial IL-33 release and allergic airway inflammation.

METHODS: circGDI2 expression was examined in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. Its functional role was evaluated in a house dust mite (HDM)-induced murine asthma model using adeno-associated virus-mediated circGDI2 knockdown, miR-103a-3p agomir, and NLRP3 siRNA. Molecular interactions were assessed by dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, and fluorescence in situ hybridization. NLRP3 inflammasome activation was monitored by cleaved caspase-1 p20, mature IL-1β, and IL-18 secretion, along with LDH release.

RESULTS: circGDI2 was upregulated in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. circGDI2 silencing alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and remodeling, and reduced type 2 immune responses in HDM-exposed mice. Mechanistically, circGDI2 sponged miR-103a-3p to derepress NLRP3 and promoted epithelial IL-33 release, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-1 p20 and mature IL-1β and IL-18 secretion together with only a limited and NLRP3-dependent increase in LDH release. Consistent with this, miR-103a-3p restoration, NLRP3 knockdown, or MCC950 treatment each attenuated airway inflammation and IL-33 release, confirming the circGDI2/miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 axis.

CONCLUSIONS: circGDI2 promotes allergic airway inflammation by enhancing epithelial IL-33 release through the miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 pathway. These findings support circGDI2 as an upstream regulator of inflammatory responses in experimental asthma.

articles.title: Research integrity throughout the research lifecycle and stakeholders: Part 5 - Considerations for intensive and critical care nursing.
Cross-cultural adaptation, consensus using Delphi method and content validity of the first French emergency department patient-reported experience measure.
articles.journal: Journal of epidemiology and population health
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aims of this study were 1) to perform cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM into the French ED PREM; 2) to seek consensus on this version using the Delphi method and 3) establish its content validity.

METHODS: This study was designed following the Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments guidelines. A cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM, renamed the French ED PREM, was performed. Consensus was sought through a Delphi method involving an expert committee, including the original developer and patient partners. Content validity was assessed with 50 patients and 7 healthcare professionals in the first round, and 10 patients in the second round, evaluating the relevance, comprehensibility, and comprehensiveness of the French ED PREM. The endpoint was an item-level content validity index (I-CVI) > 0.78 and a scale-level content validity index (S-CVI) > 0.90 without suggestions for revision.

RESULTS: Consensus was achieved in two rounds, with 100% expert participation and agreement. All French ED PREM items achieved a robust content validity (I-CVI > 0.78, S-CVI > 0,90) and demonstrated excellent agreement among evaluators beyond chance (k > 0.74).

CONCLUSION: Through a rigorous cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM, this international collaborative research has demonstrated the content validity of the French ED PREM. This work contributes to the international harmonization of patient experience measures and may facilitate future comparisons across healthcare systems.

articles.title: NLRP3 inflammasome dysregulation in chronic bacterial infections: mechanistic insights into treatment failure and relapse.
articles.abstract: Chronic and recurrent bacterial infections are a significant clinical issue despite the development of antimicrobial treatment. It is increasingly being shown that chronic host-based inflammatory dysregulation is also an integral cause of treatment failure and persistence of illness, and not just the consequence of microbial resistance. The NLRP3 inflammasome presents an important integrated platform linking tissue destruction, metabolic strain, and microbial detection to augmented inflammatory reactions. The ultimate goal of the review is to assess chronic bacterial infection as an inflammatory resolution dysfunction, and the example of persistent NLRP3 inflammasome dysregulation and the therapeutic consequences. In this review, the existing data on the canonical and non-canonical pathways of NLRP3 activation is summarized and the interplay between metabolic reprogramming, ionic flux, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy are all thought to contribute to the lowered activation thresholds in chronic infection. The disease-specific pathology of the prolonged IL-1β and IL-18 generation, destabilisation of the barricade and inflammatory feedback prolongation are common pathological themes in contexts like granulomatous lung disease, intracellular persistence syndromes, biofilm-associated infections and chronic airway colonisation. Inflammasome permissiveness and resolution are exacerbated by immunometabolic changes and microbiome imbalance.

articles.title: Association of Graft Laterality With Outcomes After Single Lung Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate whether graft side (right versus left) is associated with outcomes after single lung transplantation (SLT) and to contextualize this association with lung function and perioperative complications.

METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adults transplanted from January 2018 to July 2025 with interstitial lung disease (ILD) or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Survival was evaluated with Kaplan-Meier and Cox models adjusted for clinical covariates. Postoperative respiratory infection was modeled with logistic regression. Longitudinal forced expiratory volume in 1 s was summarized.

RESULTS: Of 530 transplants, 319 met criteria (ILD n = 224; COPD n = 95). Survival differed by procedure (log-rank P = 0.0013). Compared with double lung transplantation, right SLT had higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 2.92, 95% CI 1.82-4.67, P < 0.0001), while left SLT did not (HR 1.07, 0.60-1.91, P = 0.82). The excess hazard with right SLT persisted within interstitial lung disease (HR 2.27, 1.28-4.05, P = 0.005) and COPD (HR 2.87, 1.33-6.19, P = 0.007). Primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (HR 2.39, 1.39-4.11, P = 0.002) and acute kidney injury (HR 2.12, 1.33-3.38, P = 0.002) were independently associated with mortality. Respiratory infections were frequent (∼40%-53%) without a clear difference by side; longer operative time correlated with infection (odds ratio 1.16 per h, 1.02-1.32, P = 0.02). Forced expiratory volume in 1 s peaked at 12-18 mo and declined thereafter, with no separation by side.

CONCLUSIONS: Right-but not left-SLT was associated with inferior long-term survival versus double lung transplantation. The lack of side-specific differences in spirometry and infection suggests that other factors may be relevant to the observed association between laterality and survival. Multicenter studies with time-varying covariates and physiologic imaging are warranted.

articles.title: ESMO and ASCO Consensus on Good Clinical Practice Guideline E6(R3): A Step Forward Towards Streamlining Clinical Research.
articles.abstract: The growing administrative burden associated with clinical research has become a major challenge for investigators and research teams, contributing to increased costs, delays in trial implementation, and reduced research efficiency. In response, the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) have led multiple initiatives aimed at streamlining clinical research, identifying unnecessary bureaucracy and promoting more pragmatic, patient-focused approaches. In line with these initiatives from ESMO, ASCO and other stakeholders, the recent ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guideline E6(R3) has incorporated numerous changes to rationalise the administrative procedures in clinical research. The revised guideline places substantially greater emphasis on applying proportionality between processes and risks, the relevance of the data, and the reliability of results; avoiding unnecessary complexity and burden in clinical research; and incorporating input from investigators and patients into trial design and conduct. The guideline also clarifies several aspects of clinical trial operations, including informed consent procedures, re-consenting requirements, source documentation, and delegation practices, providing opportunities to reduce administrative burden without compromising participant safety or data integrity. Together, the initiatives led by ESMO, ASCO, and other stakeholders, alongside the principles embedded within GCP E6(R3), reflect the shared recognition that clinical research processes should focus on activities that protect data integrity and the rights and well-being of patients. Effective implementation of these principles will be critical to improving the efficiency, sustainability, and accessibility of clinical research.

articles.title: Boosting hybrid immunity with intranasal live-attenuated or intramuscular mRNA vaccination prevents SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 transmission.
articles.abstract: Rapid antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and waning immunity have reduced antibody-mediated neutralization, enabling breakthrough infections and sustained transmission despite widespread immunity. This highlights the need for variant-adapted booster vaccines. However, pre-existing immunity may influence the magnitude and specificity of immune responses induced by variant-adapted booster vaccination. Using the Syrian hamster model, we previously described a safe and efficient mucosal vaccination approach using live attenuated viruses (LAV) based on a "One-to-Stop (OTS)" codon modification strategy. Whether OTS vaccines are suitable as effective booster vaccines in the presence of pre-existing mucosal immunity remained unaddressed. Here, we modeled pre-existing hybrid immunity in Syrian hamsters using intramuscular bivalent mRNA vaccination followed by SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequently administered heterologous intranasal OTS-LAV or intramuscular mRNA XBB.1.5 booster vaccination. Both booster strategies significantly increased XBB.1.5-binding- and neutralizing antibodies systemically and at mucosal sites. In contrast, booster vaccination left SARS-CoV-2 specific T cell frequencies unchanged. While all hybrid-immune animals were protected from disease following XBB.1.5 challenge infection, virus transmission was completely blocked only after booster vaccination and was associated with the absence of infectious virus in nasal samples. Collectively, using OTS-LAV we provide a proof of concept that intranasal LAV vaccination can effectively boost pre-existing hybrid immunity and restrict viral transmission. These findings support the use of OTS-LAV as a heterologous booster strategy against SARS-CoV-2 and demonstrate that variant-adapted booster vaccination can efficiently limit transmission, a strategy highly desired for tackling emerging respiratory infections.

articles.title: Decrease in hospital ischemic strokes in older adults in France since 2019: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of epidemiology and population health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to update the epidemiology of ischemic stroke in one French region, the Centre-Val de Loire (CVL), to provide a comprehensive understanding of how stroke patterns evolved in an aging population with uneven access to medical care, compared to national data.

METHODS: Patients hospitalized for ischemic stroke between 2014 and 2022 were included from the national Hospital Discharge Database (PMSI - ICD-10 code I63). The crude hospitalization rates were stratified by sex and age. For the population ≥75 y.o., the average annual percentage changes of hospitalisation rates were calculated for two periods: 2014-2019 and 2020-2022, both for the CVL region and the national levels.

RESULTS: Similar trends were observed at the regional and national scale: after a rising period, the national number of patients with ischemic stroke stabilized around 90,000 by 2022 in France, giving an hospitalisation rate of 137/100,000 inhabitants, higher in men (151/100,000) and patients ≥75 y.o. (735/100,000). For the latter, a decreasing trend was observed after 2019, with average annual decreases of hospitalization rates of -2.8% and -4%, respectively.

DISCUSSION: This study was the first to document a consistent decline in hospital admissions for ischemic stroke in older adults from 2019 onwards, both in the CVL region and in France. This decline could be attributable, at least in part, to the loss of high-risk stroke patients during the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Microplastics contamination in cultured and wild molluscan seafood from the bay of Bengal coast: Ecosystem threats and consumer exposure risks.
articles.abstract: Microplastic contamination and associated polymer toxicity in mollusks are emerging concerns for ecosystem health and seafood safety in coastal environments. This study compares microplastic abundance, polymer composition, and exposure risks in wild and cultured populations of Crassostrea madrasensis, Perna viridis, and Telescopium telescopium from coastal Bangladesh. Microplastics were detected in all species, with mean abundances ranging from 0.68 ± 0.22 to 1.12 ± 0.10 items g-1. Fibres dominated, accounting for 77 to 94% of particles, with most measuring less than 500 μm. Transparent and violet particles were most common, indicating sources from textiles, ropes, and aquaculture materials. Polymer composition was determined using Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) with PE, PET, PS, EVA, Nylon, and PVA identified among the detected polymers. Polymer hazard index values were similar across groups (PHI 15.7-18.7, level II), whereas MPERI was higher in cultured than wild Crassostrea madrasensis (18.6 vs 16.1) but lower in cultured than wild Perna viridis (7.1 vs 17.7). Estimated human intake through mollusk consumption ranged from 0.28 to 0.47 items kg-1 day-1, corresponding to 6.2 × 103 to 1.0 × 104 items per person per year. The dominance of fine fibres and the presence of higher hazard polymers indicate potential chronic ecological stress and food safety concerns. These findings emphasize the need for improved aquaculture practices and targeted monitoring in coastal Bangladesh.

articles.title: HSPA12B modulates lung injury and neutrophil-related inflammatory responses in LPS-induced acute lung injury: a potential link to the PKC-PAD4 pathway.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are life-threatening conditions with high mortality. Excessive neutrophil activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related responses, together with pulmonary endothelial barrier impairment, are critical pathological features. Heat shock protein A12B (HSPA12B) has endothelial-protective and anti-inflammatory functions, but its relationship with the PKC-PAD4 pathway and neutrophil-associated lung injury remains unclear. In this study, we combined bioinformatics analysis with an LPS-induced ALI mouse model to examine whether HSPA12B expression is associated with PKC-PAD4 pathway activation and neutrophil-related lung injury. HSPA12B overexpression was associated with reduced pathological lung damage, lower levels of inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress markers, as well as decreased lung-tissue levels of PKC, PAD4 and neutrophil-associated markers (CitH3, MPO, NE). Conversely, HSPA12B knockdown was accompanied by elevated protein levels of PKC, aggravated lung injury, and further upregulation of these markers; transcriptomic analysis of lungs from HSPA12B-knockdown mice revealed enrichment of the neutrophil extracellular trap formation pathway. These findings indicate that HSPA12B is functionally linked to the PKC-PAD4 cascade and neutrophil-mediated lung injury in LPS-induced ALI. Of note, the PKC-PAD4 link is proposed rather than directly demonstrated, and that isoform-specific and activity-level evidence is still lacking. This study identifies HSPA12B as a potential upstream regulatory node for further mechanistic investigation, providing a basis for future HSPA12B-targeted studies in ALI/ARDS.

articles.title: Cross-Database Generalization of a Single-Feature Threshold Model for Congestive Heart Failure Detection from Short-Term Heart Rate Variability.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the transferability of interpretable single-feature threshold models across the five evaluated databases for congestive heart failure (CHF) detection from short-term heart rate variability (HRV), and to compare their performance with optimized multi-feature classifiers.ApproachTwenty HRV features from 60-second inter-beat interval windows in five databases were evaluated using leave-one-database-pair-out nested cross-validation with six outer-test sets and their corresponding outer-development sets. Within each outer-development set, directions and thresholds were fitted on inner-train sets, and features were selected according to mean inner-validation F1 score. The selected model was refitted on the complete outer-development set. The most frequently selected feature was further evaluated across the six outer-test sets with separately fitted directions and thresholds. Eight multi-feature classifiers were optimized and evaluated using the same data splits. Performance was assessed using record-balanced window-level metrics and database-stratified recording-level bootstrap confidence intervals.Main resultsThe short-term detrended fluctuation analysis scaling exponent (f14) was selected most frequently. The f14 threshold model achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.881 ± 0.038), F1 score (0.718 ± 0.079), and sensitivity among the evaluated single-feature and multi-feature models. Among the eight multi-feature classifiers, Random Forest achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.858 ± 0.067). SignificanceAn interpretable single-feature threshold model showed strong CHF-Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR) discrimination in the five evaluated databases. f14 was the strongest candidate in this evaluation, although its thresholds varied across outer-development sets and its clinical specificity requires further validation.

articles.title: Monocortical locking screws in the tibial diaphysis maintain tibial plateau angle and support osteotomy union after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy in dogs.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of distal monocortical locking screw fixation on construct stability and bone healing following tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO) in dogs. We hypothesized that monocortical fixation would result in acceptable maintenance of tibial plateau angle (TPA) of < 5° and satisfactory osteotomy union.

METHODS: Medical records from a companion animal referral hospital between December 8, 2021, and February 23, 2024, were retrospectively reviewed. Dogs were included if TPLO was performed for cranial cruciate ligament insufficiency using monocortical screws in the distal tibial segment and complete radiographic follow-up was available. Change in TPA between postoperative and follow-up radiographs were recorded. Bone healing was assessed using the modified Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures. Associations between outcomes and clinical variables were evaluated with linear regression models.

RESULTS: A total of 117 dogs met the inclusion criteria. Median change in TPA during healing was 2.15° (95% CI, 1.70° to 2.65°), and no evaluated variables were associated with TPA change. Median modified Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures score was 10 (range, 4 to 12), consistent with satisfactory radiographic union at a mean follow-up time of 43 days. The overall complication rate was 8.5%, including an infection rate of 2.6%.

CONCLUSIONS: Use of monocortical distal tibial screws within a titanium alloy conical locking TPLO system was associated with acceptable maintenance of TPA and satisfactory radiographic union scores.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Monocortical distal tibial fixation may provide sufficient stability to support osteotomy healing per manufacturer recommendations. Additional studies are needed to evaluate outcomes for different locking systems, patient size categories, screw combination, and longer-term follow-up periods.

articles.title: Measured, not labelled: un-analyzable input versus misclassification in single-lead wearable ECG.
articles.abstract: Wearable single-lead ECG has expanded arrhythmia screening, but many recordings are inconclusive, and each corpus defines that word differently. We ask how much deployment error is un-analyzable input rather than misclassification when analyzability is measured with one instrument.Approach. We evaluate three diagnostic databases in-domain and leave-dataset-out under a strict loss counting windows carrying each corpus's inconclusive label as errors unless deferred. We score analyzability with an unsupervised morphological criterion calibrated against three experts on free-living ECG. Reference unreadability is sparse and imbalanced: only seven of 15 subjects contain an unreadable window and one supplies 88% of all unreadable windows. Thresholded sensitivity and every prevalence or true-share correction are therefore exploratory.Main results. The criterion flags almost all expert-unreadable windows but only subsets of the windows labelled inconclusive by their corpora: an inconclusive rate measures convention as much as signal. At tau_a = 0.50, criterion-positive windows are 8.1%, 56.7% and 69.6% of the strict proxy loss on Holter, handheld and patch. The true-share point intervals lie below 50% on handheld and above it on patch, but joint calibration-and-sampling envelopes span 50% on both and still do at the Youden threshold 0.60. On handheld, the calibration-only envelope is more than twice as wide as the corpus-sampling-only envelope. Gate-versus-confidence ordering changes with the accounting and corpus; no general selective-risk advantage of the gate is established.Significance. Corpus labels, criterion flags and latent expert unreadability must not be conflated. A gate can win by predicting a labelling convention, and this retrospective study validates neither transfer to smartwatch dry electrodes nor improvement in patient outcomes. Measure the inconclusive rate with a stated criterion on the raw signal; do not inherit it from a corpus label.

articles.title: Causal Inference with Missing Exposures and Missing Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Missing data are ubiquitous in public health research. When estimating causal effects, there are well-established methods to address bias to due missing outcomes. Commonly, causal estimands are defined under hypothetical interventions to "set" the exposure and to prevent missingness. We demonstrate how this framework can be extended to missing exposures. We further extend this framework to incorporate missingness on the baseline outcome, which induces missingness on the population of interest (e.g., persons at-risk). To do so, we highlight Counterfactual Strata Effects, a general class of causal estimands where the focus population is subject to missingness and/or impacted by the exposure. They are termed such because the estimand involves conditioning on a counterfactual variable. For each setting, we present the causal model, relevant counterfactuals, causal estimand, and identification result. We demonstrate with a real-data example to investigate the effect of alcohol consumption on the risk of incident tuberculosis (TB) infection in rural Uganda. We highlight the use of TMLE with Super Learner for estimation and inference and discuss the practical consequences of our approach.

articles.title: Invasive RV pressure-volume loops show hemodynamic benefits of reducing lung hyperinflation in COPD.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Right heart dysfunction is a common complication in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Endoscopic lung volume reduction (ELVR) using Zephyr® valves improves lung function by reducing emphysema-induced hyperinflation, providing clinical benefits beyond enhanced pulmonary mechanics. Magnetic resonance imaging studies suggest that alleviating lung hyperinflation may also positively affect left heart function. We hypothesized that ELVR may also improve right heart function.

RESEARCH QUESTION: This study evaluated right heart function after ELVR in patients with COPD using invasive pressure-volume loop analysis.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Eleven patients with severe COPD underwent baseline right heart catheterization because of suspected pulmonary hypertension, and pressure-volume loop analysis. Eight patients underwent ELVR, followed by right heart function reassessment 12 weeks post-procedure.

RESULTS: Pre-ELVR, pulmonary artery pressures ranged from 23 to 32 mmHg, vascular resistance was 2.2-4.8 WU, and significant impaired pressure-volume indexes were observed compared to reference data. Post-ELVR, lung hyperinflation improved significantly, with a reduction in the Residual Volume /Total Lung Capacity (RV/TLC) ratio. RV/TLC changes correlated with improvements in end-diastolic pressure-volume relationships (r=0.82, P=0.02) and the time constant of relaxation Tau (r=0.84, P=0.01). Functional outcomes, such as 6-minute walk distance and dyspnea scores, were driven by stroke work and diastolic parameters, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single center study, endoscopic lung volume reduction with associated improvement in hyperinflation led to significant improvement in exercise capacity and in right ventricular function.

articles.title: Postoperative hospital discharge readiness of elderly patients: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate the readiness of elderly patients for discharge from the hospital after surgery.

DESIGN: This study is of a descriptive cross-sectional design and was reported using The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) framework.

METHOD: The study was conducted between October 2024 and May 2025 with 283 patients aged 65 and over in the adult surgical clinics of a university hospital. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form and the Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale-Short Form. Descriptive statistics were used in the analysis of the data, and Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Bonferroni tests were used for nonparametric comparisons.

RESULT: Although 78.4% of patients reported receiving sufficient information regarding discharge and 76.3% felt ready for discharge, only 56.5% were determined to be ready according to the scale. The mean total score of the Scale was found to be 7.20±1.87; the lowest score was in the coping ability subscale, and the highest score in the expected support subscale. Education level and receiving sufficient information about discharge statistically significantly affected the level of readiness for discharge. Total and all subscale scores of the scale differed significantly across surgical clinics (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that readiness for discharge in elderly surgical patients cannot be determined solely by subjective perceptions but requires structured, multidimensional assessment. Nursing-led interventions focused on strengthening coping skills and delivering systematic discharge education play a critical role in promoting safe, effective, and sustainable care transitions in clinical practice.

articles.title: A Conserved Root-Knot Nematode Effector Interacts with Plant Kinesin Light Chain-Related Proteins to Promote Parasitism.
articles.abstract: Root-knot nematodes (RKNs) are obligate plant parasites that establish biotrophic interactions with a wide range of host plants, causing major crop losses worldwide. During infection, RKNs secrete effector proteins from their esophageal glands into root tissues via a stylet. These effectors target specific subcellular compartments and manipulate host cell functions to induce the formation of hypertrophied and multinucleated giant cells, which serve as feeding sites essential for nematode development. Here, we describe a new RKN-specific effector, EFFECTOR17 (EFF17), conserved in the five most damaging RKN species: Meloidogyne incognita, M. enterolobii, M. arenaria, M. javanica, and M. hapla. In situ hybridization showed that EFF17 genes are specifically expressed in the esophageal glands of various RKN species. Silencing EFF17 in M. incognita reduced its reproduction on Nicotiana benthamiana, supporting a contribution to parasitism. Yeast two-hybrid and split luciferase assays revealed that MiEFF17 interacts with tomato and Arabidopsis KINESIN LIGHT CHAIN RELATED (KLCR)/CELLULOSE-MICROTUBULE UNCOUPLING (CMU) proteins. Arabidopsis klcr mutants developed significantly fewer egg masses. Our findings propose that EFF17 manipulates KLCR function to promote parasitism. [Formula: see text] Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). This is an open access article distributed under the CC BY 4.0 International license.

articles.title: Awareness of and Hypothetical Willingness to Use Long-Acting Injectable Cabotegravir and Associated Factors Among Oral Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Users Who Obtained the Medicine Online in China: Web-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective for HIV prevention, but its real-world impact depends on sustained adherence. Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) may reduce the burden of daily or event-driven pill use. In China, many oral PrEP users obtain medication online, but little is known about their prior CAB-LA awareness or willingness to consider it.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA, reported barriers and facilitators, and associated factors among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed baseline data from the Real-world E-consumer Cohort of Oral PrEP (RECOPE), a prospective cohort in China. Participants completed a self-administered web-based questionnaire assessing prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness after standardized CAB-LA information, sociodemographic characteristics, recent sexual behaviors and sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnosis, and oral PrEP-related characteristics. Modified Poisson regression with robust SEs estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs. Primary regression analyses were restricted to sexually active participants.

RESULTS: Among 621 oral PrEP users, the mean age was 29.9 (SD 6.4) years; all were assigned male sex at birth, and 608 (97.9%) identified as men. Overall, 216 of 621 (34.8%, 95% CI 31.1%-38.6%) participants reported prior CAB-LA awareness. After receiving standardized information, 428 of 621 (68.9%, 95% CI 65.2%-72.4%) participants expressed hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA if it became available in China. Convenience was the most frequently reported facilitator among willing participants (395/428, 92.3%), whereas high cost was the most frequently reported barrier among those who did not express willingness (123/193, 63.7%). In adjusted analyses, event-driven PrEP users had a lower prevalence of prior CAB-LA awareness than daily PrEP users (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.86), whereas participants who had switched oral PrEP regimens in the past 3 months had higher prior awareness (aPR 1.34, 95% CI 1.07-1.68). Hypothetical willingness was more prevalent among participants reporting an STI diagnosis in the past 3 months (aPR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.39) and chemsex (aPR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26), whereas higher PrEP-related stigma was associated with slightly lower willingness (aPR 0.99 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 0.98-0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: Among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online, prior CAB-LA awareness was limited, whereas hypothetical willingness was common after standardized information was provided. Prior awareness differed by oral PrEP regimen and recent regimen switching, whereas willingness was associated with recent STI diagnosis, chemsex, and PrEP-related stigma. Convenience was a major appeal, while cost remained an important barrier. These findings support improving access to balanced PrEP information and addressing practical barriers as long-acting PrEP becomes more widely available.

articles.title: Bioinspired Hydroxyapatite-Mineralized Silk Fibroin/Ionic Liquid Interpenetrating Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications.
articles.abstract: Surgical site infection remains a critical barrier to successful bone tissue engineering, and silk fibroin (SF)-based scaffolds, despite their excellent biocompatibility, lack intrinsic antibacterial activity. Here, we report a multifunctional biohybrid nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) with an antibacterial imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer, 1-vinyl-3-hexylimidazolium bromide ([C6VIm]Br), fabricated via a bioinspired bidirectional freeze-casting strategy followed by in situ biomineralization with hydroxyapatite (HAp). Successful methacrylation (degree of substitution = 35%) and ionic liquid synthesis were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy, while FT-IR, TGA/DTG, and XRD analyses verified the formation of the interpenetrating SF/IL network and progressive HAp deposition, with mineral content rising from 12.1 to 32.9 wt % over successive mineralization cycles. SEM imaging and elemental mapping revealed a highly interconnected, anisotropic porous architecture with uniform calcium/phosphorus distribution, closely emulating native bone microstructure, and mineralization enhanced the swelling capacity to approximately 170%. Biologically, the ionic liquid component conferred potent, additive-free antibacterial activity against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, while HAp incorporation improved MG-63 osteoblast-like cell adhesion and the viability of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), with MSC viability exceeding 120% of the control in the mineralized sample. All formulations exhibited hemolysis well below accepted safety limits, confirming excellent hemocompatibility. By combining intrinsic antibacterial function, bioinspired anisotropic architecture, and biomimetic mineralization within a single platform, this work offers a promising, metal- and antibiotic-free strategy for infection-resistant scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, with significant potential for advancing bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of an Electronic Medical Record-Based Machine Learning Model for Frailty Prediction in Hospitalized Patients: Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is prevalent among hospitalized patients and is associated with increased risk of complications, prolonged hospitalization, higher mortality, and health care costs. Existing frailty screening tools, including the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) and Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), have limitations related to subjectivity, resource intensity, or reliance on retrospective data, limiting their use in routine acute care. Early identification of frailty is critical to support targeted interventions and resource allocation, yet scalable approaches for predicting frailty early during hospital admission remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This paper evaluates whether routinely collected electronic medical record (EMR) data available within the first 72 hours of admission can be used to predict frailty in hospitalized patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using routinely collected EMR data from the Royal Adelaide Hospital (RAH), including overnight admissions with a length of stay of at least 72 hours between July 2023 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the HFRS (score >4). Predictors were derived from EMR data available within 72 hours of admission, including demographics, medications, laboratory results, nursing assessments, and medical and allied health consult orders. Data were split into training (21,436/26,824, 80%) and test (5388/26,824, 20%) sets. Multiple machine learning models were trained, with the F2-score as the primary optimization metric. Model performance was evaluated using the F2-score, recall, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, and clinical utility analyses.

RESULTS: This study included 26,824 admissions, of whom 9427 (35%) were classified as frail. The final XGBoost (XGB) model achieved an F2-score of 0.755 (95% CI 0.741-0.768), an AUROC of 0.777 (95% CI 0.764-0.790), and a recall of 0.873 (95% CI 0.857-0.887) on the test dataset, with good calibration and an expected-to-observed ratio close to 1 (0.996, 95% CI 0.963-1.028). Key predictors included polypharmacy, laboratory results (including creatinine, albumin, and sodium), allied health consult orders, and nursing assessment data. Model performance was lower at 24 hours postadmission and improved by discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: An EMR-based frailty prediction model using data available at 72 hours postadmission can identify patients with frailty early in their hospital stay, supporting targeted interventions and operational planning. Reduced performance in Indigenous patients highlights the need for culturally validated frailty indices and ongoing evaluation of equity in predictive modeling.

articles.title: Acute and Chronic Cardiovascular and Neuromuscular Effects of Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
