articles.abstract: Low-load blood flow restriction resistance training (BFR-RT) may offer a lower-load alternative to conventional resistance training for older adults, but its cardiovascular responses and neuromuscular benefits remain incompletely characterized. To synthesize the acute cardiovascular responses and chronic cardiovascular and neuromuscular effects of low-load BFR-RT in older adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials, including parallel-group and crossover designs, comparing low-load BFR-RT with no-exercise/passive control or conventional non-BFR resistance training were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twenty-seven studies were included. Acutely, BFR-RT increased systolic blood pressure versus no exercise (MD, 5.30 mmHg; 95% CI, 0.48 to 10.12) and increased diastolic blood pressure (MD, 5.23 mmHg) and mean arterial pressure (MD, 5.81 mmHg) versus conventional resistance training, while heart rate, stroke volume, and cardiac output were not significantly different. Chronically, resting cardiovascular and endothelial outcomes were largely unchanged. Versus no exercise, BFR-RT significantly improved knee-extension, leg-extension, and leg-press 1RM and quadriceps cross-sectional area. Comparisons with conventional resistance training were mixed and outcome-specific. Low-load BFR-RT improves selected neuromuscular outcomes in older adults, particularly relative to no exercise, while cardiovascular responses are comparator-dependent and chronic vascular effects appear largely neutral. These findings support cautious, individualized application rather than assumptions of cardiovascular superiority or equivalence to conventional resistance training.

articles.title: Reduced-Intensity Haploidentical Bone Marrow Transplantation in Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease: BMT CTN 1507.
articles.abstract: This is a multi-center, single-arm, phase-II, trial (NCT03263559) of haploidentical bone marrow transplant (BMT) for children with severe sickle cell disease (SCD). Eligible participants were children 5.00 - 14.99 years of age with stroke (silent or overt), abnormal transcranial Doppler cerebral arterial velocity > 200 cm/sec with intracranial vasculopathy, severe acute chest syndrome (ACS) or recurrent vaso-occlusive pain. The primary outcome was 2-year event-free survival (EFS; alive and disease-free). The transplant regimen included hydroxyurea 30mg/kg/day (Day-60 to Day-10), followed by thymoglobulin, thiotepa, fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and total body irradiation (200 cGy). Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis included post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy), sirolimus and mycophenolate mofetil. Forty-one participants were enrolled from 18 sites and 95% (39/41) proceeded to BMT. The median age at enrollment was 12.5 years; 98% (38/39) had hemoglobin SS disease, and 82.1% (32/39) had donors mismatched at 4 HLA-loci. The most common indication for BMT was a qualifying neurological event in 69% (27/39), including 15 with overt stroke. Nine participants had recurrent vaso-occlusive pain and 5, severe ACS. The 2-year EFS and overall survival were 79.3% (95% CI: 62.8%, 89.1) and 94.5% (95% CI: 79.7%, 98.6%), respectively. FEV1% predicted increased from 79.5 to 95.7 at 2 years (p=0.014), and eGFR declined from 174 to 127 mL/min/1.73m2 (p<0.001), indicating resolved hyperfiltration. No new or progressive cerebral infacts were detected by serial brain MRI per central adjudication (n=22). While graft failure and GVHD negatively impacted EFS, reduced-intensity haploidentical BMT with PTCy is a promising therapy for children who lack a matched sibling donor.

articles.title: Impact of Chatbot-Based Cognitive Training on Cognitive Function and White Matter Integrity in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive training may enhance cognition and support brain health during aging, but few trials have evaluated readily accessible chatbot-based programs with neuroimaging outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a chatbot-based cognitive training program on white matter microstructural organization and cognition in cognitively unimpaired older adults.

METHODS: In a single-blind randomized controlled trial, 72 cognitively unimpaired older adults were assigned to chatbot-based cognitive training (30 min/day, 5 days/week for 12 weeks; n=37) or a no-intervention control (n=35). Diffusion tensor imaging at baseline and 12 weeks quantified fractional anisotropy (FA) in predefined white matter tracts, and cognition was assessed with the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery.

RESULTS: Groups were comparable at baseline. After 12 weeks, the training group showed significantly less FA reduction than controls in the bilateral tapetum and right posterior thalamic radiation, surviving false discovery rate control (P<.05). The training group also improved on Paired Associates Learning (PAL), an episodic memory measure (P=.04). PAL improvement was positively associated with FA change in the right posterior thalamic radiation and right sagittal stratum (false discovery rate-adjusted P=.04 for each).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that a 12-week chatbot-based cognitive training program may support episodic memory and the relative maintenance of white matter microstructural organization in selected pathways in cognitively unimpaired older adults, consistent with a brain-maintenance framework.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CRIS KCT0004630; https://tinyurl.com/4xfesb68.

articles.title: Neck-Specific Exercises With Internet Support Versus Standard Neck-Specific Exercise for the Treatment of Chronic Whiplash-Associated Disorders: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is currently scarce information about the cost-effectiveness of interventions for individuals with chronic whiplash-associated disorders (WAD) or of internet-based exercise programs for neck pain, including WAD.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the cost-effectiveness of a 3-month neck-specific exercise program with internet support in combination with 4 physiotherapy visits (neck-specific exercise with internet support [NSEIT]) compared with the same exercises performed twice a week (24 times) at a physiotherapy clinic (neck-specific exercise [NSE]) for individuals with chronic WAD.

METHODS: This was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial of the cost-effectiveness of the interventions among 140 individuals with chronic moderate to severe WAD with 3- and 15-month follow-up. The main outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER).

RESULTS: At the 15-month follow-up, the total costs calculated for NSEIT and NSE were SEK 12,882 (95% CI 17,406.30-8358.42) and SEK 40,087 (95% CI 51,764.32-28,410.96), respectively (SEK 1=US $0.10 as of October 6, 2026). The health-related quality of life (HRQoL) score at 15 months was 0.662 (95% CI 0.73-0.59) and 0.711 (95% CI 0.77-0.65) for NSEIT and NSE, respectively. The ICER for HRQoL was SEK 555,209.80 per point when the NSEIT group was compared with NSE. The internet-based intervention was less costly and less effective than NSE at the 15-month follow-up. The cost-effectiveness acceptability curve showed that at a willingness to pay threshold of SEK 500,000 per point, there was a moderate probability (0.57) of the intervention being cost-effective with a loss of HRQoL. One-way sensitivity analysis showed that the health care costs of individuals receiving NSE and NSEIT affected the ICER.

CONCLUSIONS: NSEIT intervention-an eHealth intervention for chronic WAD-was less costly and less effective compared with NSE. Health care costs associated with both interventions affected the ICER; therefore, patients' overall well-being should also be considered when treating chronic WAD. Even though the cost effectiveness acceptability curve showed that the cost savings from NSEIT outweighed the lost health outcomes, the reliability of the findings was limited by the exclusion of presenteeism costs, patients' self-reported health care use, and the small difference in health outcomes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03022812; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03022812.

articles.title: Perceived Ratings of AI-Generated and Expert-Reviewed vs Clinician-Developed Virtual Cardiology Patient Scenarios Among Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used in medical education, but creating high-quality cases requires clinical expertise, iterative revision, and alignment with educational objectives. Generative AI may support VP authoring, but direct comparisons between AI-generated and clinician-developed cases delivered within the same educational setting remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare medical students' learner-perceived ratings of 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed virtual cardiology patient scenario with those of 1 clinician-developed virtual cardiology patient scenario delivered through the same mobile platform.

METHODS: A randomized, participant-blinded 2-arm controlled study was conducted in October 2025 during scheduled fifth-year emergency medicine course sessions. Eligible participants were fifth-year medical students who had completed the cardiology course. Students were assigned 1:1 to complete either a clinician-developed VP (CD-VP; n=64) or a ChatGPT-generated VP (GPT-VP; n=67). Both scenarios followed a shared acute coronary syndrome blueprint and were delivered through the same mobile-optimized app (mobile VPs app [MobiViP]) with identical interface structure and branching logic. The GPT-VP was generated using GPT-5 and refined through iterative follow-up prompting under expert review; direct manual rewriting was prohibited. After completion, students completed a mandatory 19-item questionnaire covering realism and validity, cognitive load, self-reported learning and reflection, and engagement and satisfaction. Analyses included reliability testing, 1-sample tests against a neutral midpoint, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations. Full scenario content and development details are provided as multimedia appendices.

RESULTS: A total of 131 complete questionnaires were analyzed, with no item-level missing data. Mean subscale scores in the CD-VP group were 3.81 (SD 0.64) for realism and validity, 3.67 (SD 0.74) for cognitive load, 3.64 (SD 0.73) for self-reported learning and reflection, and 4.16 (SD 0.64) for engagement and satisfaction; corresponding GPT-VP scores were 4.11 (SD 0.56), 3.03 (SD 0.76), 3.86 (SD 0.77), and 4.28 (SD 0.58), respectively. Compared with the CD-VP, the GPT-VP received higher ratings for realism and validity (Mann-Whitney U=1503.0; P=.003) and lower cognitive load ratings, indicating a lower perceived burden (Mann-Whitney U=1070.5; P<.001). Self-reported learning and reflection showed a marginal difference between groups, with a higher rating for the GPT-VP (Mann-Whitney U=1719.0; P=.05), whereas engagement and satisfaction did not differ significantly (Mann-Whitney U=1922.5; P=.31). Internal consistency was acceptable to good for most subscales, although internal consistency for the realism and validity subscale in the GPT-VP group was moderate (Cronbach α=0.67).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center randomized study, 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed cardiology VP scenario was rated similarly to or more favorably than 1 clinician-developed scenario in selected learner-perceived domains. Future research should expand to objective learning, retention, development workload, and scalability outcomes.

articles.title: Percutaneous Echo-Guided Cervical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Cannulation by Intensivists in Neonates and Children.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Cervical cannulation is the standard approach for venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in neonates and small children but is traditionally performed surgically. We report our initial experience with bedside percutaneous ultrasound- and echocardiography-guided cervical VA-ECMO cannulation performed by intensivists. Three pediatric patients underwent percutaneous right common carotid artery and internal jugular vein cannulation. Vascular access, guidewire advancement, tract dilation, and cannula positioning were guided by ultrasound and transthoracic echocardiography. Median age was 5 months (range, 20 days-6 years) and median weight 7 kg (range, 3-15 kg). Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was initiated for extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation in two patients and refractory cardiogenic shock in one. Cannulation was successful in all patients without surgical conversion, with a median skin-puncture-to-flow time of 32 minutes (range, 28-35). Target flow (>100 ml/kg/min) was achieved in two patients. No major cannulation-related vascular or cardiac complications occurred. Two patients died on ECMO, while one survived without signs of stroke on follow-up magnetic resonance imaging. Vascular integrity was documented by postmortem examination or Doppler follow-up. Bedside percutaneous echo-guided cervical VA-ECMO cannulation by experienced intensivists appears technically feasible in pediatric patients. Further studies are needed to establish safety, reproducibility, effectiveness, and potential advantages over conventional surgical cannulation.

articles.title: Identification and characterization of pathogens causing oat anthracnose in China.
articles.abstract: Oat anthracnose is a destructive global disease that severely compromises grain yield and forage quality. To determine its distribution, severity, and principal etiology in China, field surveys were conducted across major oat-producing regions. Anthracnose was endemic across all surveyed regions, reaching peak severity in central Inner Mongolia, northern Shanxi, and northwestern Hebei (maximum disease index of 68.31). Early infection manifested as small, circular, yellow-to-brown foliar lesions surrounded by water-soaked halos. These spots expanded into fusiform or irregular dark brown lesions featuring central black acervuli. Similar symptoms occurred on stems, glumes, sheaths, and leaf-sheath junctions. A total of 162 pathogenic isolates were obtained from 16 oat survey sites. Pathogenicity testing of 50 representative isolates confirmed their ability to infect oat leaves, reproducing field symptoms and yielding falcate conidia within necrotic tissues. Interestingly, while only falcate conidia developed in vivo, isolates produced both falcate and oval conidia on potato sucrose agar. Multi-locus phylogenetic analysis (four gene loci) combined with morphological evaluations resolved all 31 representative isolates as Colletotrichum cereale. These findings establish that C. cereale is the dominant pathogen driving oat anthracnose in China. Furthermore, this study provides the first documentation of conidial dimorphism in C. cereale alongside its symptomatic manifestation on oat glumes and stems.

articles.title: Population genetics of Fusarium graminearum, causal agent of Fusarium Head Blight, provide insight into patterns of inoculum dispersal in wheat fields.
articles.abstract: Fusarium graminearum is the primary pathogen responsible for Fusarium Head Blight (FHB) in cereals, causing yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. The present study investigated the genetic diversity and population structure of F. graminearum from wheat grains and maize residues, considered as the primary inoculum source of FHB. A total of 588 isolates from four different fields were genotyped using a sequence-based microsatellite genotyping method of 34 SSR markers (SSRseq) and characterized for chemotype distribution. The results revealed high genetic diversity with 453 distinct multilocus genotypes (MLGs) without significant genetic differentiation by geographic location or substrate, suggesting a single metapopulation at the regional scale. This absence of substrate genetic differentiation strongly supports residue-borne inoculum contributing to FHB infection, although field-specific dispersal pattern from residues to grains was not demonstrated. The findings underscore the importance of maize residues as a critical inoculum source and highlight the need to consider both local and regional sources in FHB management.

articles.title: Mind Your Heart-A Web-Based Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet and Mindful Eating Intervention for Working Adults at Elevated Cardiovascular Risk: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet (DASH) diet supports heart health; yet, many find it difficult to follow in community settings. Mindful eating can improve adherence, but in-person programs are time-consuming and not always accessible. eHealth offers an accessible, scalable alternative that may increase engagement and compliance.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the feasibility of a DASH eHealth program focused on mindful eating and the preliminary changes in eating behaviors, diet quality, and health outcomes.

METHODS: Participants were recruited from a university workplace via email and flyers and randomly assigned to either a web-based DASH diet education program (Diet Only) or the Mind Your Heart (MYH) intervention. The MYH program included the same DASH curriculum plus additional mindful eating instruction, guided practice, and specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time frame (SMART) goal setting. Both interventions were fully asynchronous, self-guided, and lasted 6 weeks on the Desire2Learn (D2L) Brightspace platform, with no personalized coaching or counseling. Baseline and postintervention assessments involved in-person measurements of anthropometrics, blood pressure, and blood biomarkers. Participants recorded their diets electronically over 3 days using MyFitnessPal (MyFitnessPal, Inc) and completed validated questionnaires on mindful eating using the Mindful Eating Behaviors Scale (MEBS), eating behaviors using the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire Revised 21-item (TFEQ-R21), motivation for regulated eating using the Regulated Eating Behaviors Scale (REBS), and perceived stress using the Perceived Stress Scale 10-item (PSS-10). During the intervention, automated ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) were sent electronically 3 times weekly to monitor eating behaviors in real time.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven participants (mean BMI 31.93 SD 7.25, 34/37, 91.9% female, 31/37, 83.8% White) were randomized into groups. Among the 36 who remained enrolled, the mean curriculum completion was 85.9%, SD 21.4; 31 (86.1%) completed≥60% of assigned content, and 32 (88.9%) completed at least half of the scheduled EMA prompts. Thirty-four participants attended the postintervention assessment and completed the questionnaires and the blood pressure assessment, although paired baseline and postintervention data were not available for all anthropometric measures and biomarkers. Participants reported no adverse events, and research staff observed none. Although no significant between-group differences were observed for DASH adherence, anthropometric measures, blood pressure, or cardiometabolic biomarkers, participants in the MYH group showed greater improvements than the Diet Only group in TFEQ-cognitive restraint (mean difference in change 0.39, 95% CI 0.06-0.72; Hedges g=0.81; P=.02) and REBS-controlled regulation (mean difference in change 3.59, 95% CI 0.01-7.16; Hedges g=0.68; P=.05).

CONCLUSIONS: A fully asynchronous digital mindful eating plus DASH education intervention and associated research procedures were feasible among working adults at elevated cardiovascular risk. Preliminary changes in eating behaviors suggest that mindful eating warrants further evaluation, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample and feasibility design. Larger, adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed.

articles.title: Quantum Sensing Technologies for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection in Biomedical Diagnostics from Fundamental Principles to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Quantum sensing technologies offer unprecedented detection sensitivities down to single-molecule, attomolar detection limits and thus are emerging as transformative tools for ultra-sensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics. This comprehensive review synthesizes insights from over 380 plus studies to provide recent advances in quantum sensor platforms, examining the fundamental quantum mechanical principles that enable enhanced sensitivity, and surveys a diverse range of quantum sensing technologies along with their applications across the biomedical field. Specifically, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, quantum dots, superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), and other quantum sensing modalities applied to biomarker detection for cancer diagnostics, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious disease detection are reviewed. Further, the key technical challenges that hurdle their clinical translation are critically evaluated. The review results demonstrate that quantum-enhanced biosensors have achieved detection limits of the order of magnitude below conventional methods. Intrinsic to their capabilities, several quantum sensing platforms have progressed to clinical testing and early commercialization efforts. Specifically, for point-of-care diagnosis, early disease detection, and personalized medicine.

articles.title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins.
articles.abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

articles.title: Conservative Management of Kidney Failure.
articles.abstract: The default therapy for end-stage kidney disease is often dialysis, but for those with advanced age and multimorbidity, it may not provide significant benefit to longevity or quality of life. Conservative management (CM) is a holistic care pathway for those whose care preferences do not align with dialysis. CM aims to optimize quality of life over the disease course as patient priorities evolve and their disease progresses. Components of CM include customized chronic kidney disease care, symptom management, and navigation of transitions of care, including end-of-life care. Nephrology clinicians are the central providers of CM and ideally collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to provide medical, psychosocial, and spiritual care.

articles.title: Communicating Climate-Related Risks via Storytelling and Statistics.
articles.abstract: Strategies are needed to effectively communicate the public health effects associated with climate change-amplified events, e.g., floods, wildfires, and heat waves. This review explores ways to translate complex statistics and present other critical aspects of climate change using storytelling (through narratives, exemplars, and images) to engage people and maximize comprehension and healthy behaviors. We also examine how to shape the strategy or strategies used based on audience characteristics such as adult age, numeracy, literacy, and ideology. We delineate the key psychological levers through which these strategies work-effort reduction, emotions, psychological distance, efficacy, and presence of relevant numbers-and propose a barrier-matched framework to choose communication approaches. We also illustrate key concepts with case studies. Developing long-term capacity to deliver effective messages is one step toward empowering people to act safely in response to threats, build a more resilient society, enhance quality of life, and save money and lives.

articles.title: Glaucoma Treatment Trends in Australia Over a 10-Year Period.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterise trends in the use of selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), glaucoma surgery and medication prescribing in Australia between 2015 and 2024.

STUDY DESIGN: Nationwide, population-based cross-sectional analysis.

METHODS: Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) procedure claims and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS)/Repatriation PBS dispensing data were analysed from 2015 to 2024. Procedure and prescription rates were expressed per 100,000 Australian residents using Australian Bureau of Statistics population estimates.

RESULTS: Between 2015 and 2024, 344,370 SLT procedures were recorded. Rates rose from 127 to 150 per 100,000 (β = 1,335 procedures/year; 95% CI 969-1,701; p < 0.001). Annual glaucoma medication prescriptions decreased from 4,167,417 to 3,390,394 (17,498 to 12,466 per 100,000), without a statistically significant linear trend (β = -52,005/year; 95% CI - 104,373-363; p = 0.051). Overall, 113,466 glaucoma surgeries were recorded: annual procedures increased from 4,953 (20.8 per 100,000) to 15,334 (56.4 per 100,000). Minimally invasive glaucoma surgeries (MIGS) increased from 2,177 in 2017 to 10,501 in 2024, compared with 4,080 to 4,386 filtration procedures and 292 to 409 drainage device procedures. Negative binomial regression found no significant annual rate trends for MIGS (IRR 1.16; 95% CI 0.86-1.57; p = 0.34), filtration procedures (IRR 1.00; 95% CI 0.81-1.24; p = 0.97), or drainage devices (IRR 1.03; 95% CI 0.83-1.28; p = 0.79). Optometrists' share of glaucoma prescriptions increased from 1.25% to 5.63%.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate changing glaucoma treatment trends in Australia. SLT and MIGS procedure volumes increased as medication prescriptions declined, while optometrists accounted for an increasing proportion of medication prescribing.

articles.title: Beyond Abstinence: How Integrated Multidisciplinary Management Improves Long-term Post Liver Transplant Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease is the leading indication for liver transplantation (LT). We assessed long-term alcohol relapse after LT within a program using an integrated multidisciplinary team for relapse monitoring and prevention before and after transplantation, without requiring a predefined abstinence period.

METHODS: In 2018, we established a prospective program in which all patients with associated liver disease were evaluated and followed before and after LT by a multidisciplinary team embedded within the transplant program. We reviewed long-term outcomes as part of this program between 2018 and 2023.

RESULTS: A total of 165 recipients were transplanted since the inception of the program. Posttransplant alcohol relapse occurred in 21 patients (12.7%), of whom 57.1% had mild alcohol consumption, 4.8% moderate, and 33.3% severe. Median time to relapse was 9.4 mo (5.9-30.2). Ethyl glucuronide positivity confirmed relapse in 20 of 21 patients, and 17 endorsed alcohol use. All patients had access to addiction psychiatry follow-up and relapse prevention therapy embedded within their posttransplant care. Those who relapsed were offered intensification of relapse prevention therapy and 16/21 engaged in regular follow-up. Only 6 patients (3.6%) reported ongoing alcohol consumption at last follow-up, while all others reestablished abstinence. No significant differences in outcomes were observed between groups. No alcohol-related deaths or graft losses occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary fully integrated team along with individualized approach to candidate evaluation with follow-up pre- and post-LT is critical to successful outcomes and results in a much lower rate of relapse at long-term post-LT.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Hepatic Artery Thrombosis and Stenosis After Pediatric Liver Transplantation: Results From the HEPATIC Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors of hepatic artery complications (HACs), including thrombosis (HAT) and stenosis (HAS), after pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) are not well characterized. This study aimed to assess the incidence and risk factors of HACs after pLT and quantify the screening effort required to identify a single HAC.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter analysis using the HEPATIC registry, including pLTs from 32 centers over a 20-y period. HAC incidence was assessed across subgroups defined by pLT indication, recipient age, donor type, transplant era, and annual center volume. Timing of HAC occurrence and the number needed to screen were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 11 443 pLTs, HACs occurred in 4.8% (HAT 3.6%; HAS 1.2%). Most HACs developed within the first-month posttransplant (82.4%), with HAT peaking in the first 2 wk, whereas HAS was more evenly distributed. The overall incidence increased in 2012-2021 (5.3%), with rising HAS and stable HAT rates. Modifiable factors included living donor transplantation (3.4%) and high-volume centers (3.8%), both associated with lower HAC rates, whereas whole grafts in infants <1 y with biliary atresia (15.3%) were associated with higher incidence (all P < 0.001). Patient-related risk factors included retransplantation following previous HACs (11.3%) and noncirrhotic metabolic diseases (7.6%, both P < 0.001). The number needed to screen ranged from 173 to 1907 and was lower in high-risk groups.

CONCLUSIONS: HACs occurred in 4.8% of pLTs, with recent increases driven by HAS. Infants <1 with biliary atresia receiving whole grafts and patients undergoing retransplantation after prior HACs were at the highest risk.

articles.title: Beyond FEV1: Alveolar Nitric Oxide Within an Integrated, Noninvasive Model for CLAD Surveillance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) remains the major limitation to long-term survival after lung transplantation. Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a noninvasive marker of airway inflammation, but its clinical role after lung transplantation remains uncertain. This study investigated whether multiple-flow FeNO parameters may support CLAD risk stratification in lung transplant recipients.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational study of 114 lung transplant recipients. At the time of FeNO assessment, 45 patients had CLAD, 9 had acute cellular rejection, and 60 were clinically stable. FeNO was assessed at multiple expiratory flows to derive proximal and distal nitric oxide parameters.

RESULTS: Alveolar nitric oxide concentration (CalvNO) was significantly higher in patients with CLAD than in clinically stable recipients and showed the best discrimination among FeNO-derived variables for prevalent CLAD (area under the curve [AUC], 0.849; optimal cutoff, 7.7 ppb). A model combining CalvNO, diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide, residual volume/total lung capacity, and forced expiratory volume in 1 s showed good diagnostic performance (AUC, 0.88). Among initially stable recipients, 9 developed CLAD during follow-up. Baseline CalvNO was associated with incident CLAD in exploratory time-to-event analysis (hazard ratio, 1.35 per 1 ppb increase), with an AUC of 0.889 and a cutoff of 7.12 ppb. Microbiological status modified FeNO interpretation, particularly for proximal indices, whereas CalvNO remained more consistently associated with CLAD in colonized and microbiologically negative patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple-flow FeNO-derived CalvNO is a biologically plausible and clinically promising noninvasive biomarker for CLAD risk stratification. Its most defensible application is as part of integrated surveillance combining FeNO-derived parameters, pulmonary function, lung volumes, diffusion capacity, and structured assessment of infection or other reversible conditions.

articles.title: Clinical and Laboratory Factors Associated with Renal Complications Following High-Voltage Electrical Burns: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-voltage electrical burns cause deep tissue injury, rhabdomyolysis, and acute kidney injury (AKI), but factors associated with renal complications are incompletely characterized. We investigated clinical and laboratory characteristics associated with dipstick-defined presumptive myoglobinuria, AKI, and renal replacement therapy (RRT) after high-voltage electrical burns.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 37 male patients with high-voltage electrical burns (≥1000 V) treated at a tertiary burn center. Demographics, injury severity, outcomes, surgical interventions, and admission and 48-hour laboratory parameters were compared using nonparametric univariable tests. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses explored the discriminatory performance of selected variables. As 48-hour serum creatinine contributed to AKI ascertainment, it was not considered an independent AKI biomarker.

RESULTS: Dipstick-defined presumptive myoglobinuria was present in 30 patients (81.1%), AKI occurred in 9 (24.3%), and RRT was required in 3 (8.1%). Patients with AKI had greater TBSA and higher CK, serum myoglobin, and troponin I concentrations than patients without AKI. Among variables available at admission, CK showed the highest discrimination for AKI (AUC 0.925, 95% CI 0.822-0.993), followed by troponin I (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.814-0.992) and TBSA (AUC 0.907, 95% CI 0.776-0.992). The increase in serum creatinine over 48 hours was considered part of AKI ascertainment rather than an independent diagnostic marker.

CONCLUSIONS: Renal complications after high-voltage electrical burns were associated with greater burn severity and more pronounced laboratory abnormalities. Among admission variables, CK, troponin I, and TBSA showed high discriminatory ability for AKI. These findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts).

CONCLUSION: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

articles.title: Potential Synergistic Association of Donepezil and Metformin With COVID-19 Mortality in Dementia Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with dementia face markedly elevated mortality from COVID-19. Both donepezil and metformin have anti-inflammatory effects and are associated with improved outcomes in respiratory viral infections, but whether their combined use is associated with lower COVID-19 mortality remains unknown.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) data enclave, including adults aged ≥65 years with primary SARS-CoV-2 infection. We evaluated the association between donepezil monotherapy (5 mg or 10 mg) and COVID-19 mortality using 1-to-1 propensity score-matched analyses. Analyses were stratified by diabetes and metformin use.

RESULTS: Among patients with dementia, 30-day mortality was lower in patients receiving donepezil 5 mg compared with matched untreated controls (10.3% vs 13.2%; p = 0.00046) and similarly for 10 mg (10.3% vs 13.4%; p = 0.0014). Among patients with dementia and diabetes, donepezil-metformin use was associated with the lowest mortality, approaching levels in matched individuals without dementia or diabetes. Metformin or donepezil alone was associated with modest reductions. Among donepezil users, those with diabetes treated with metformin had lower mortality than those without diabetes (30-day: 7.6% vs 10.2%, p = 0.016; significant only after FDR correction). No significant mortality differences by diabetes or metformin use were observed among dementia patients not receiving donepezil.

CONCLUSIONS: Donepezil use was associated with reduced COVID-19 mortality in older adults with dementia, with findings consistent with a potential synergistic association with metformin. These findings warrant further study of cholinergic modulation, alone or with metabolic therapies, to reduce severe COVID-19 outcomes.

articles.title: Quantification of Antibiotic Concentration at the Site of Infection: Analytical Challenges and Current Practices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantifying antibiotic concentrations at infection sites is challenging because of invasive sampling and complex matrices. Despite limited knowledge, target-site data are crucial for optimizing dosing, minimizing resistance, ensuring safer strategies, and reducing toxicity risks through adequate target attainment.

METHODS: This review aims to provide an overview of the most commonly reported challenges associated with quantifying target-site concentrations of antibiotics. Antibiotics were selected as the focus because of their use in hospital and outpatient settings. An extensive literature search was conducted using Embase.com. After title and abstract screening of 828 articles, 398 articles were included for full-text screening, and 72 were included based on relevance to analytical challenges in target-site quantification. Reported challenges were categorized in subgroups: sampling difficulties, sample heterogeneity, unavailability of free drug concentrations, drug complexities, and others.

RESULTS: Direct measurement of antibiotic concentrations at infection sites is constrained by invasive procedures and complex analytical methods. Key challenges include sampling heterogeneity, difficulty in obtaining samples, and the lack of free drug concentration data. Several opportunities have been proposed to address these challenges.

CONCLUSIONS: We recommend updating international validation guidelines to include standardized tissue sampling protocols, encouraging the commercial sectors to develop reference standards and blank materials for alternative matrices, and promoting the use of minimally invasive techniques, such as microneedle biosensors, to improve the accuracy and safety of target-site quantification. These advances offer promising avenues to enhance antimicrobial therapy optimization despite current.

articles.title: Multi-omics reveals evolution from CD7-negative T cell dysregulation to EBV-positive LPD after CD7 CAR-T therapy.
articles.abstract: EBV activation specifically occurs in a subset of patients following CD7 CAR-T therapy, subsequently leading to EBV-positive lymphoproliferative disorder (EBV+ LPD), descriptively referred to as post-CD7 CAR-T lymphoproliferative disorder (PCLD) in this study. To comprehensively characterize PCLD, we employed single-nucleus RNA sequencing, ATAC sequencing, and Stereo-seq to perform multi-omic spatial profiling of PCLD, and compared it with classical post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), EBV-negative diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV- DLBCL) and normal lymph nodes. Infiltrating T cells in PCLD are uniquely characterized by CD7 negativity, exhibiting limited proliferation upon infection stimulation and impaired antiviral activity against EBV. Macrophages are recruited in an attempt to sustain viral clearance; however, the Macro_IDO1 subset emerges as the dominant macrophage population, exhibiting an immunosuppressive phenotype marked by elevated IDO1 expression. Spatially, macrophages, predominantly Macro_IDO1, aggregate to form an immunosuppressive niche that restricts T-cell infiltration and is enriched for inhibitory ligand-receptor interactions, including the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. T-cell function is further compromised, enabling sustained EBV infection of B cells and driving malignant transformation. EBV-driven B cells undergo plasmacytic differentiation and sustained proliferation, actively remodeling the microenvironment. This study provides a comprehensive molecular characterization of lymphoproliferative disorder following CD7 CAR-T therapy, elucidates spatial tumor-immune interactions, mechanisms of EBV-driven B-cell transformation and potential intervention strategies.

articles.title: Pace-dependent reorganisation of shoulder-hip coordination in front crawl swimming.
articles.abstract: Shoulder and hip roll are distinct but coordinated components of body roll during front crawl swimming, yet shoulder-hip coordination has largely been examined using discrete measures. This study applied continuous relative phase (CRP), Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM), and complementary coupling analyses to a previously published kinematic dataset, to examine shoulder-hip coordination during sprint and 400 m pace front crawl. Three-dimensional kinematic data from 15 national-level male swimmers were analysed during non-breathing stroke cycles at sprint (25 m) and 400 m pace. SPM revealed pace-dependent differences in shoulder- and hip-roll waveforms, with roll angle more positive at sprint pace during mid-stroke and at 400 m pace during the stroke-transition region. Mean CRP shifted from slightly shoulder-leading at 400 m pace (3.08 ± 3.14°) to hip-leading at sprint pace (-3.44 ± 6.47°; p < 0.001). Sprint swimming also exhibited greater coordination variability (SD CRP: 18.02 ± 6.20° vs. 10.68 ± 2.51°) and weaker shoulder-hip coupling (0.92 ± 0.04 vs. 0.97 ± 0.01). Coordination differences were concentrated in the recovery phase, whereas the push phase was unaffected by pace. Non-breathing cycles performed under sprint and 400 m pace conditions were characterised by distinct shoulder-hip coordination patterns rather than uniform differences in rotation magnitude.

articles.title: Adjunctive Intracoronary rhTNK-tPA During Primary PCI and Early Regional Left Ventricular Function in STEMI Patients With High Thrombus Burden: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with high thrombus burden often shows impaired myocardial perfusion despite successful epicardial recanalization. Intracoronary recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator (rhTNK-tPA) may reduce microvascular obstruction and preserve ventricular function, but evidence is limited.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 136 STEMI patients with high thrombus burden undergoing primary PCI between May 2022 and February 2025. Patients receiving intracoronary rhTNK-tPA (n=62) were compared with controls receiving standard PCI alone (n=74). The primary endpoint was left ventricular regional wall motion status within 7 days after PCI, assessed by WMSI and normal ventricular wall motion. Secondary endpoints included cTFC, ST-segment resolution, final TIMI flow grade, and clinical and safety outcomes.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable. The rhTNK-tPA group had lower WMSI values (P<0.001) and a higher incidence of normal ventricular wall motion (41.7% vs. 19.6%; P=0.014). rhTNK-tPA was also associated with lower post-PCI cTFC (18.18 ± 6.91 vs. 21.24 ± 9.20; P=0.033) and higher ST-segment resolution (83.9% vs. 68.9%; P=0.043), while final TIMI grade 3 flow was similar. In multivariable analysis, rhTNK-tPA was independently associated with lower odds of ventricular wall motion abnormalities (OR=0.214; 95% CI, 0.106-0.433; P<0.001). MACE were infrequent, and no intracranial hemorrhage occurred.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive intracoronary rhTNK-tPA during primary PCI was associated with better early preservation of regional wall motion and improved reperfusion indices without an observed increase in major bleeding.

articles.title: Retraction Statement.
articles.abstract: The article "Omission of a Bladder Flap during Cesarean Birth in Primiparous Women" [Gynecol Obstet Invest. 2018;83(6):564-568; https://doi.org/10.1159/000481283] by Berna Aslan Cetin, Begum Aydogan Mathyk, Sibel Barut, Yelda Zindar, Kerem Doga Seckin, and Pinar Kadirogullari has been retracted by the Publisher and the Editors.After publication of this article, concerns were raised about the statistics reported in Table 1 and an Expression of Concern was published while the investigation was ongoing [1].The authors state that they identified errors in the reported values for BMI, gestational age at birth, birth weight, total operating time, incision to delivery time, blood loss, preoperative hemoglobin, postoperative hemoglobin, postoperative urinary retention, postoperative residual urine volume, and first urination time after catheter removal. The Editor determined that the errors alter the conclusions of the article, and therefore, the article is being retracted.Begum Mathyk, on behalf of all authors, disagreed with the retraction statement.

articles.title: Thematic Structure of Preterm Infant Pain Research: A Topic Modeling Analysis Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm infants experience frequent painful procedures in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), yet the overall thematic structure of this extensive body of research remains unclear and has not been systematically characterized.

METHODS: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling was applied to 879 English abstracts retrieved from international databases (Web of Science, PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase) and regional databases in September 2024. Term frequency-inverse document frequency weighting was used to identify core keywords, and silhouette coefficients were used to determine the optimal number of topics. Topic labels were validated through expert consultation with experienced NICU nurses.

RESULTS: Five themes were identified: physiological and behavioral pain assessment (13.4%), nursing practice and pain management (26.6%), pain-related stress and neurodevelopment (13.0%), pharmacologic interventions (14.4%), and nonpharmacologic interventions (32.5%). Among the core keywords identified, "Premature Infant Pain Profile" was the most frequently occurring term (n = 569).Implications for Practice and Research: Although preterm pain research encompasses assessment, intervention, and developmental perspectives, studies addressing pain-related neurodevelopment were represented less frequently in the literature (13.0%). Nonpharmacologic interventions (32.5%) and nursing practice and pain management (26.6%) accounted for the largest proportions, underscoring the central role of NICU nurses. In practice, integrating family-centered, evidence-based pain management strategies into routine NICU care is essential. Future research should further examine the long-term developmental impact of repeated pain exposure in preterm infants.

articles.title: A pilot study of a computed tomography volumetric analysis technique to determine severity of injury and prognosis for OTA 42A-C open tibial diaphyseal fractures.
articles.journal: Bulletin of the Hospital for Joint Disease (2013)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This pilot study evaluated a novel computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric analysis tool for open tibial fractures. We hypothesized that the volumetric injury ratio (VINJ/VUNINJ), a quantitative comparison of injured with contralateral uninjured limb segments, would correlate with clinical outcomes and serve as a prognostic marker.

METHODS: A retrospective review of a tibial fracture registry was conducted at a single academic institution (2014-2024). Eligible patients were older than 18 years old with preoperative bilateral lower extremity CT imaging, high-energy injuries, and ≥6 months of follow-up. Demographics, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), injury features, and outcomes including fracture-related infection (FRI), amputation, and nonunion were collected. Tissue volume was measured at the fracture midpoint and 5 cm proximal and distal, with corresponding contralateral measurements. VINJ/VUNINJ was calculated, and logistic regression estimated complication risk. The primary endpoint was a composite complication (FRI, amputation, or nonunion). Discrimination was assessed using AUROC and compared with the Gustilo-Anderson (GA) classification via the DeLong test. The Youden Index identified an optimal risk threshold. Power analysis estimated sample size requirements for a future validation study.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 36.1 ± 13.5 years). GA distribution: 60% II, 6.7% IIIa, 26.7% IIIb, and 6.7% IIIc. The volumetric model (log[p/(1-p)] = -110.964 + 100.011 × VINJ/VUNINJ) demonstrated a trend toward improved discriminatory ability compared with the GA model (AUROC: 0.944 vs 0.769, P = 0.068). A Youden-derived threshold (0.539) classified 5 patients (33.3%) as high-risk; all developed complications compared with 10% in the low-risk group (100% vs 10%, P = 0.001). Power analysis indicated that detecting a twofold increase in complications would require ∼23 patients per arm (46 total).

CONCLUSION: This pilot study introduces a CT-based volumetric ratio as a quantitative tool for risk stratification in open tibial fractures. Findings suggest superior prognostic accuracy compared with GA, supporting prospective validation in larger patient cohorts.

articles.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition.
articles.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

articles.title: Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses.
articles.abstract: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ+ T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

articles.title: Controlled human infection with Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites elicits antibodies against mosquito salivary protein SG1L3.
articles.abstract: Human malaria infections begin with the injection of Plasmodium sporozoites via mosquito saliva. Whole sporozoite immunizations have been used as a model to study immune responses to malaria parasites, having culminated in circumsporozoite protein (CSP)-targeting vaccines and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). However, antibody responses targeting non-CSP antigens on the sporozoite surface remain poorly characterized. Here, we isolated single B cells from a human volunteer immunized by Plasmodium falciparum-infected mosquito bites, who had acquired non-CSP-specific antibodies that recognize sporozoites. We identified two mAbs that recognize the surface of P. falciparum sporozoites, but do not bind to CSP. Using immunoprecipitation followed by mass-spectrometry, we found that the target of these mAbs is not a P. falciparum protein but the mosquito salivary protein SG1L3. We observed that recombinant SG1L3 binds to P. falciparum sporozoites. However, the SG1L3-specific mAbs and SG1L3-specific polyclonal antibodies from this volunteer, as well as polyclonal antibodies raised against recombinant SG1L3 in rabbits, fail to block liver stage infection in vitro, making this an unlikely target for functional antibodies. We observed that inhabitants from an area with intense Anopheles exposure in Burkina Faso can have antibodies against SG1L3, and that antibody titers increase with age. In conclusion, we identified the first human mAbs against a mosquito saliva protein that binds to the surface of sporozoites. Future work should assess whether naturally acquired antibodies against this protein may be used as a serological marker of mosquito exposure.

articles.title: Defective viral genomes of porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus type 2: Generation, characterization and interference effects on viral replication.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus type 2 (PRRSV-2) is a major swine pathogen that causes substantial economic losses worldwide. Defective viral genomes (DVGs) are important regulators of viral replication, persistence, and evolution in many RNA viruses. However, the characteristics and functions of DVGs generated during PRRSV-2 infection remain unknown. Here, we systematically analyzed publicly available high-throughput sequencing datasets and characterized DVGs generated during both in vitro and in vivo PRRSV-2 infection. We found that PRRSV-2 preferentially generates large deletion DVGs, particularly in porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs), and that DVG formation is associated with microhomology sequences, RNA secondary structure and AU-rich sequences. Break positions were enriched in the GP5/M genomic region, whereas rejoin positions clustered predominantly within the nsp1/nsp2 genomic region of the PRRSV-2 genome. Notably, the deletion events within the same gene were highly enriched in the nsp2 region, where multiple naturally occurring nsp2 deletion sites overlapped with DVG junction sites. These findings suggest that DVG-associated recombination may contribute to the formation of PRRSV-2 nsp2 deletion variants. Functionally, PRRSV-2-derived DVGs exhibited potent broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple prevalent PRRSV-2 lineage strains and PRRSV-1. Overall, our findings provide the first systematic characterization of PRRSV-2 DVGs, reveal a potential evolutionary link between DVGs and nsp2 deletion variants, and highlight the antiviral potential of PRRSV-2 DVGs.

articles.title: Ultrasound neuromodulation hypotheses on the directionality of effects and community resource.
articles.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a promising non-invasive technique for brain stimulation and focal neuromodulation. Research with humans and animal models has raised the possibility that TUS can be biased towards enhancing or suppressing neural function. Here, we first collate a set of hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects and conduct an initial meta-analysis on available healthy human participant TUS studies reporting stimulation parameters and outcomes (n=47 studies, 52 experiments). In initial exploratory analyses with univariate tests, we find that parameters, such as the intensity and continuity of stimulation (duty cycle, DC) show statistical trends towards likely TUS neural enhancement or suppression of function. Machine-learning analyses were limited by the currently small sample size. Given that human TUS sample sizes are expected to increase, predictability on the directionality of TUS effects could improve if a database is available. Therefore, we establish an inTUS database and resource for the systematic reporting of TUS parameters and outcomes to assist in greater precision in TUS use for brain stimulation and neuromodulation. The paper concludes with a selective review of human clinical TUS studies illustrating how hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects could be developed for empirical testing in the intended clinical application, not limited to the examples provided.

articles.title: On real-time calibrated prediction for complex model-based decision support in pandemics: Part 1.
articles.abstract: Infectious disease models are used to predict the spread and impact of outbreaks of a disease. Like other complex models, they have parameters that need to be calibrated, and structural discrepancies from the reality that they simulate that should be accounted for in calibration and prediction. Whilst Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques have been applied to infectious disease models before, they were not routinely used to inform policymakers in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. In this paper, we will argue that during a fast moving pandemic, models and policy are changing on timescales that make traditional UQ methods impractical, if not impossible to implement. We present an alternative formulation to the calibration problem that embeds model discrepancy within the structure of the model, and appropriately assimilates data within the simulation. We then show how UQ can be used to calibrate the model in real-time to produce disease trajectories accounting for parameter uncertainty and model discrepancy. We apply these ideas to an age-structured COVID-19 model for England and demonstrate the types of information it could have produced to feed into policy support prior to the lockdown of March 2020.

articles.title: Practice Patterns and Staffing Models for Nonoperating Room Anesthesia in the Intensive Care Unit: An Exploratory Survey of the Membership of the American Society of Anesthesiologists Committee on Critical Care Medicine.
Fast probabilistic whitening transformation for ultra-high dimensional genetic data.
articles.abstract: Statistical methods often make assumptions about independence between the samples or features of a dataset, yet correlation structure is ubiquitous in real data. In statistical genetics, correlation between regression summary statistics due to linkage disequilibrium (LD) between nearby variants complicates downstream analysis. Many methods use LD reference panels to account for this correlation. Whitening transformations comprise a family of methods to remove correlation structure, and are used implicitly by many common models. Here we propose a probabilistic model for data whitening, and propose parameter estimates and efficient algorithms to improve statistical and computational performance. In an application to impute z-statistics from unobserved genetic variants from a genome-wide association study of schizophrenia, the probabilistic whitening transformation, had the lowest mean square error while being up to an order of magnitude faster than other methods. Using this approach, we also identify tandem repeats that explain genetic regulatory signals for disease-relevant genes. Analyses are implemented in our novel open source R packages decorrelate and imputez.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.
articles.abstract: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: Undescended Testes in Medically Complex Children: Evaluating A Common Urologic Condition Through a Multi-Disciplinary Lens.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Undescended testis (UDT) is a common genitourinary anomaly in boys. Orchiopexy before 18 months of age is recommended to preserve fertility and reduce testicular cancer risk. However, these recommendations are based on results of outcome studies for otherwise healthy boys and may not be readily applicable for those with developmental and/or genetic disorders for whom anesthetic and surgical risks may be increased and intervention may offer limited benefit. UDT management in boys with complex medical conditions warrants unique considerations, and data-driven guidelines are lacking. In this review, we explore this challenging clinical dilemma through a multi-disciplinary lens.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was performed by specialists in pediatric anesthesia, endocrinology, genetics, oncology, urology, and development-behavioral pediatrics. Iteratively refined structured literature searches of the MEDLINE database, GeneReviews®, and online books were performed via PubMed. Anesthetic and surgical risks, fertility potential, testicular cancer risk, and ability to perform self-testicular exams as dictated by the patient's expected cognitive development were evaluated for healthy boys and boys with Down syndrome (DS), Prader Willi syndrome (PWS), Cerebral Palsy (CP), Fragile X, Neurofibromatosis Type 1, Williams syndrome, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, Rett syndrome, Angelman syndrome, Tuberous sclerosis, and Smith-Magenis syndrome. The results were then evaluated by a bioethicist.

RESULTS: For children with complex medical conditions, potential harms of intervention are not theoretical. Surgery may expose the child to substantial anesthetic and surgical risks for which their underlying conditions make them especially vulnerable. The ethical threshold for intervention may therefore be higher especially if certain benefits such as fertility remain uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Management of UDT for medically complex boys is nuanced and warrants a multidisciplinary approach to thoroughly assess the risks and benefits of proceeding with, deferring, or declining orchiopexy. Multidisciplinary input will best facilitate individualized care that focuses on the specific needs of each child and appropriately respects parental discretion in determining management that is most in line with the child's long-term quality of life.

articles.title: MRI BRAIN lesions and growth after antenatal steroids in preterm infants: Does timing matter?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) are widely used to improve outcomes in preterm infants, with known benefits on respiratory morbidity and intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH). However, the effect of ACS timing on brain injury and development remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the impact of a complete course of ACS (ccACS), with particular attention to timing, on brain lesions, growth, and neurodevelopment in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this historical cohort study, all VLBW infants admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Clinical data, including timing of ACS administration, were collected. The primary outcome was the occurrence of brain injury on MRI at term-equivalent age, including IVH, white matter lesions (WML), and cerebellar hemorrhage (CBH). Secondary outcomes were brain growth and maturation on MRI and neurodevelopment at 2 years assessed using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales. Outcomes were compared between infants with and without ccACS and according to different administration-to-birth intervals.

RESULTS: A total of 189 infants were included, of whom 139 (73.5%) received ccACS. Infants exposed to ccACS had a lower incidence of WML (p = 0.02) and moderate/severe IVH (p = 0.04). In extremely preterm infants (<28 weeks), IVH was significantly less frequent when ccACS was administered within 7 days before birth (p = 0.006). No significant differences were observed in brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 years.

CONCLUSIONS: A complete course of ACS was associated with unadjusted lower rates of brain injury in VLBW infants, particularly when administered within 7 days before birth in extremely preterm infants, without adverse effects on brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopment at 2 years.

articles.title: Intraductal and Cribriform Carcinoma of the Prostate: A Clinical Companion to the GUPS/ISUP Consensus Guidelines.
Hemocompatible Glycogen-Tissue Plasminogen Activator Complexes for Enhanced Blood Clot Dissolution.
articles.abstract: Thrombosis and embolism remain leading causes of death worldwide, driven by blood clots that obstruct vascular flow. Current treatments rely on intravenous injections of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) to dissolve clots, however, free tPA has severe limitations, including poor targeting, and risks of bleeding and hemorrhage. In this work, we look to overcome these limitations with targeted, biodegradable, and hemocompatible glycogen nanoparticles. We develop glycogen-heparin hybrids for complexation with tPA, along with peptide-based targeting towards activated platelets. Our strategy involves leveraging the inherent hemocompatibility of glycogen, with minimal synthetic modifications for targeted delivery of tPA to blood clots. In human blood, the glycogen hybrids have minimal interaction with immune cells, and did not trigger inflammatory or coagulation responses at therapeutic concentrations. Furthermore, they remain biodegradable towards glucosidases inherently in the human body. This design enables thrombus targeting and localized tPA delivery, thereby improving fibrinolytic efficiency relative to free tPA, with steady breakdown kinetics. This was also observed for blood clots subjected to thrombolysis under vascular flow-like conditions. Overall, our approach offers a promising treatment strategy for thrombosis, which improves the therapeutic efficacy of tPA, whilst maintaining excellent hemocomptability.

articles.title: Wireless Electrical Stimulation via a Conductive Hydrogel Scaffold Synergizes With Stem Cell Transplantation Therapy to Promote Traumatic Brain Injury Repair.
articles.abstract: Electrical stimulation (ES) offers a robust approach to boost the efficacy of stem cell transplantation therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders. Notably, wireless technology blends convenience with the elimination of infection risk posed by wired connections, but the challenge lies in the integration of wireless-enabled stimulation materials and stem cell carriers. Here, we describe a flexible annular conductive dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (HAD)/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/carbon nanotube‌ (CNT) hydrogel that acts as a secondary coil to realize wireless ES via electromagnetic induction, while also serving as a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold carrier for endogenous neural stem cells (NSCs). Established on the annular HAD/PVA/CNT hydrogel with high conductivity and good biocompatibility, wireless ES significantly enhances neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Furthermore, transplantation of the NSC-laden annular hydrogel into a traumatic brain injury (TBI) rat model modulates the behaviors of both exogenous and endogenous neural cells. The combined therapy of wireless ES and NSC transplantation promotes neuronal differentiation in both the injury zone and hippocampus in association with the PI3K-Akt pathway, reduces post-traumatic inflammatory responses, and effectively restores motor and memory functions in TBI rats. This study offers a promising therapeutic strategy of integrating wireless ES with stem cell transplantation therapy for brain injury repair.

articles.title: Phase-Programmed Microneedles Enable Sequential Hydrogen and Quercetin Release for Scar-Reduced Regeneration of Burn Wounds.
articles.abstract: Burn wounds complicated by bacterial infection and fibrotic scarring remain a major clinical challenge, demanding therapeutics capable of coordinated infection control, inflammation modulation, and tissue regeneration. Here, we report a phase-programmed microneedle (MN) patch (QR/AB-MNs) that enables spatiotemporally controlled release of ammonia borane (AB) and quercetin (QR) to achieve synergistic antimicrobial and anti-fibrotic therapy. The MNs comprise a poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) shell encapsulating QR and a sulfobutylether-β-cyclodextrin (SBECD) core loaded with the H2-releasing prodrug AB. Upon exposure to the mildly acidic wound microenvironment, the system triggers sustained generation of hydrogen (H2) and AB degradation products, effectively eliminating bacteria and biofilms while mitigating oxidative stress. Subsequently, gradual PLGA degradation ensures prolonged QR release, suppressing fibroblast hyperproliferation and TGF-β mediated collagen deposition, thereby preventing hypertrophic scarring. In murine and rabbit burn models, QR/AB-MNs markedly accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation and bacterial burden, restored skin appendages, and yielded scar-reduced regeneration with native-like collagen architecture. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that QR/AB-MNs orchestrate a broad anti-fibrotic transcriptional program, concurrently attenuating pro-fibrotic signaling, cell-extracellular matrix interactions, and collagen synthesis. Collectively, this programmable MN platform integrates redox modulation, anti-infective therapy, and matrix remodeling to achieve comprehensive, scarless-like healing of infected burn wounds.

articles.title: XChrom: A Cross-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Prediction Model Integrating Genomic Sequence and Cellular Context.
articles.abstract: Single-cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single-cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outperforms existing methods in cross-region and cross-cell predictions, and uniquely enables cross-both predictions. It also supports cross-sample prediction when batch effects are properly corrected. Cross-species analyses demonstrate XChrom's robust performance and its ability to capture evolutionarily conserved regulatory rules. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients, XChrom accurately identifies transcription factor activities in novel but related cell states and reveals pathogenesis-associated regulatory alterations. XChrom is available as an open-source Python package, facilitating single-cell transcriptional regulation research.

articles.title: Beliefs about Hereditary Susceptibility to Cancer and Desire to Know about a Genetic Predisposition: An Analysis of the NCI Health Information National Trends Survey.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study characterized beliefs about hereditary susceptibility to cancer and desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer in a nationally representative survey of US adults.

METHODS: Adjusted regression models using weighted survey analysis of NCI HINTS 2020 data assessed predictors of how much respondents (1) believe genes that are inherited determine whether a person will develop cancer and (2) would want to know if they had a genetic change that increases their chance of getting cancer.

RESULTS: On average, respondents endorsed between "somewhat" and "a lot" for how much hereditary susceptibility determines cancer risk. Respondents believed that hereditary susceptibility to cancer, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes were similar (Means= 1.83-1.85, all p>0.6). Individuals who had health insurance (β=-0.42 - -0.37, p=0.017-0.021) and previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p<0.001) believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer, whereas those who self-reported good health believed in less hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.16, p=0.022). Individuals who believed in greater hereditary susceptibility to cancer (β=0.14, p=0.001), previously sought cancer information (β=-0.19, p=0.002), had a family history of cancer (β=-0.19, p=0.005), were less fatalistic (β=-0.08, p=0.036), and were Hispanic (β=-0.25, p=.009) or Black (β=-0.47, p<0.001) endorsed a greater desire to know about a genetic predisposition to cancer.

CONCLUSIONS: Efforts are needed to improve understanding of hereditary susceptibility, address fatalistic beliefs and misinformation, facilitate disclosure of family cancer history indicative of a potential genetic predisposition to cancer.

IMPACT: Efforts are needed to improve access to genetic counseling and testing through education and targeted interventions.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
