Effect of vutrisiran on components of health status in transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy: the HELIOS-B study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Vutrisiran was shown to maintain overall health status, as measured by the 23-item Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-overall summary score (KCCQ-OSS), in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in HELIOS-B. We assessed individual KCCQ components to better contextualize changes in KCCQ-OSS in a manner relevant to patients and clinicians.

METHODS: In this analysis of HELIOS-B, a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of vutrisiran in ATTR-CM, we assessed treatment effect on mean score changes from baseline to 30 months for each 23 KCCQ components (scaled from 0 [worst] to 100 [best]) using a multivariable linear regression model. We further assessed overall changes in KCCQ-OSS as a function of age in both treatment groups to estimate the age-equivalent benefit observed.

RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B, 486 completed KCCQ assessment both at baseline and 30 months (age: 75 ± 6 years; 93% male; 91% wild-type ATTR; baseline KCCQ-OSS: 74.6 ± 18.9). Vutrisiran, compared with placebo, was associated with more favourable changes in most KCCQ components (median: +3.8, range: -0.9 to +7.6). The greater differences favouring vutrisiran were observed in 'hurrying or jogging', 'walking on level ground,' and 'discouraged/down with heart failure'. Similar or greater benefits with vutrisiran were observed in patients not on tafamidis at baseline. KCCQ-OSS at 30 months was inversely related to age, with vutrisiran shifting the age-KCCQ-OSS relationship by approximately 11 years (95%CI: 3-20 years).

CONCLUSIONS: In HELIOS-B, vutrisiran was associated with improvement in a wide range of individual KCCQ components, with the greatest benefits observed in physical limitations and quality-of-life domains.

articles.title: Heart failure care in India.
Survival benefit after successful tricuspid valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in patients with high TRI-SCORE-insights from the EuroTR registry.
Enhancing heart failure care through registries: lessons learned from Nordic Countries' implementation of guidelines.
articles.abstract: This review evaluates the role of heart failure (HF) registries in the Nordic countries-Sweden, Denmark, Norway, and Iceland-in the implementation of the European Society of Cardiology's guidelines for guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). It critically examines how these registries facilitate clinical practice and enhance patient outcomes through their design, data collection methods, and the evaluation of key metrics related to GDMT implementation over time. We highlight the nurse-led models adopted by these registries, which emphasize quality benchmarks and feature real-time feedback mechanisms regarding the application of GDMT. Between 2021 and 2024, registry population-weighted estimates revealed significant increases in the utilization of key therapies: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists rose from 51% to 72%, sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors from 20% to 81%, and sacubitril/valsartan from 22% to 32%. The use of beta-blockers and renin-angiotensin-system inhibitors remained consistently high at 91% and 94%, respectively. These shifts were linked to better treatment outcomes. The findings underscore that HF registries play a crucial role in enhancing care quality through established drug therapies for HFrEF, offering a model for integrating data-driven methodologies into HF management. Future utilization and expansion of these registries are vital for tackling healthcare disparities and refining treatment strategies for HF patients.

articles.title: Impact of acoramidis on clinical stability in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: observations from ATTRibute-CM.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Acoramidis is an oral transthyretin (TTR) stabilizer that achieves near-complete (≥90%) TTR stabilization. This post-hoc analysis evaluated response categories based on NT-proBNP concentration and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) changes among participants with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in the phase 3 ATTRibute-CM trial.

METHODS: Clinically meaningful improvement (CMI) was defined as a decrease from baseline to Month 30 in NT-proBNP of >700 ng/L and >30%, and separately, a 6MWD increase of >35 m.

RESULTS: Data from 611 participants were analysed (409: acoramidis; 202: placebo). Median baseline NT-proBNP and 6MWD values were 2273 ng/L and 365 m in the acoramidis group and 2274 ng/L and 352 m in the placebo group, respectively. A significantly higher proportion of participants in the acoramidis group reached CMI in NT-proBNP or 6MWD (22.7%) compared with the placebo group (8.9%; OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.8-5.1; P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Acoramidis led to CMI from baseline in NT-proBNP concentration or 6MWD in a considerable proportion of participants with ATTR-CM. These findings suggest that the treatment paradigm of ATTR-CM may evolve from slowing disease progression to achieving improvement.

articles.title: Balancing blood pressure and catecholamine support is critical in heart failure-related cardiogenic shock patients.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is often treated with catecholamines titrated to an adequate target mean arterial pressure (MAP) while minimizing adverse effects. We aim to assess the optimal catecholamine dose/MAP balance in heart failure-associated CS (HF-CS).

METHODS: Patients with HF-CS were retrospectively enrolled from 16 tertiary centres in 5 European countries (2016-2021; NCT03313687). Dosage was quantified by inotropic scores (epinephrine, norepinephrine, and dobutamine). Associations of baseline and seven-day summarized dosage with intensive care unit (ICU) discharge (mixed-effects logistic regression) and 30-day mortality (Cox regression) were analysed. Potential catecholamine/MAP target ratios for optimized outcomes were assessed in models adjusted for age, sex, pH, lactate and prior resuscitation, stratified by centre.

RESULTS: N = 704 patients: median age 63 years, 74% male, 34% post-resuscitation, median lactate 5.2 mmol/l. Of these, 53% were discharged from ICU, 48% died within 30 days. Higher inotropic scores independently predicted a lower probability of ICU discharge (baseline score: OR 0.78 [95%-CI 0.69-0.88]; summarized score: OR 0.46 [0.38-0.56]; both P < .001) and higher risk of 30-day mortality (baseline score: HR 1.27 [1.15-1.40], summarized score HR 1.83 [1.60-2.09]; both P < .001). A score/MAP ratio <0.403 µg/kg/min/mmHg was associated with higher ICU discharge odds (ceiling effect); a < 0.426 µg/kg/min/mmHg with lower 30-day mortality hazards (no ceiling effect). Lowering catecholamine doses by accepting reduced MAP targets was linked to better outcomes.

CONCLUSION: In HF-CS, higher catecholamine support independently associates with worse outcomes. Accepting lower blood pressure targets to reduce catecholamine dosage may improve outcomes. Validation in randomized controlled trials is urgently needed.

articles.title: Mitral regurgitation in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction: insights from GALACTIC-HF.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Given the emerging role of transcatheter valve repair in HFrEF patients with moderate/severe secondary mitral regurgitation (MR), we evaluated the prevalence and outcomes related to MR in the GALACTIC-HF trial.

METHODS: The randomized GALACTIC-HF trial compared the efficacy and safety of omecamtiv mecarbil to placebo in 8232 patients with HFrEF, with a primary composite outcome of a first HF event or cardiovascular death.

RESULTS: Of 7998 patients (97.2%) with baseline data on MR, 5782 (72.3%) had no MR, 970 (12.1%) had mild MR, and 1221 (15.3%) had moderate MR (only 25 had severe MR). Patients with moderate MR had a higher risk of the primary outcome than those without MR (adjusted HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.01-1.23); risk was not higher in patients with mild MR. The association between moderate MR and the primary outcome was most prominent in patients with less severe HF (milder NYHA class, higher LVEF, and lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) compared to more severe HF. In adjusted analyses, MR was not associated with mortality, and the results of all analyses remained consistent after including patients with severe MR. The beneficial treatment effect of omecamtiv mecarbil versus placebo on clinical outcomes was not modified by MR. Over 80% of patients with moderate/severe MR fulfilled the broad inclusion criteria for COAPT and RESHAPE-HF2.

CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, almost 15% of patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction had moderate MR, which was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome.

articles.title: Response to letter regarding the article 'Clinical profiles and prognostic impact of residual intravascular and tissue congestion in acute heart failure'.
Letter regarding the article 'Clinical profiles and prognostic impact of residual intravascular and tissue congestion in acute heart failure'.
Vascular health after quitting smoking or switching to e-cigarette use: a systematic review of prospective studies with GRADE assessment.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This systematic review aims to evaluate the effects of smoking cessation or switching to exclusive electronic cigarette (EC) use on vascular function in adult smokers, using prospective evidence from clinical studies.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase on 13 October 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental designs, and prospective cohort studies reporting quantitative or narrative data on vascular outcomes [i.e. pulse wave velocity (PWV), augmentation index (AIx), and flow-mediated dilation (FMD)], after smoking cessation or switching to ECs. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Results were synthesized qualitatively. Certainty of the evidence was determined using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Twenty-three studies involving a total of 11 702 participants were included: 14 cohort studies, 5 quasi-experimental, and 4 RCTs. Overall, smoking cessation was consistently associated with improvements in PWV, AIx, and FMD, with some effects observable within 1 month and sustained up to 24 months. The overall certainty of evidence was very low, except for a moderate level of certainty derived from RCTs investigating FMD. Improvements were seen across different cessation methods, including pharmacotherapy and ECs. RCTs on ECs reported significant improvements in FMD irrespective of nicotine content, suggesting that combustion rather than nicotine may be the primary driver of vascular impairment. Sensitivity analyses excluding lower-quality RCTs confirmed the primary findings.

CONCLUSION: Smoking cessation appears to improve vascular function, as reflected by early favourable changes in endothelial and arterial stiffness markers; however, the overall certainty varies from moderate to very low, according to the outcome. These findings are consistent with the biological plausibility of cardiovascular benefit from sustained smoking abstinence.

articles.title: Presentation and Prognosis of Cryptococcosis Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission in France: The CRYPTO-ICU Study.
authors: GRRR-OH (Groupe de Recherche en Réanimation Respiratoire en Onco-Hématologie)
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryptococcus causes life-threatening opportunistic infections in immunocompromised hosts. Data on the most severe cases requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study of patients admitted to 30 French ICUs for severe cryptococcosis between 2000 and 2022.

RESULTS: Among 151 patients included, 56.9% were patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Cases in patients without HIV became increasingly prevalent over time (51.3% in 2012-2022 vs 32.4% before 2012); 82.5% were receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Central nervous system infection was predominant (91.1%), followed by lung infection (39.7%). Fungemia occurred in 59.8% patients, and 75.2% had disseminated infection. Neurological failure was the leading organ impairment at admission (75.5%) followed by respiratory failure (47.7%), acute kidney injury (41.7%), and shock (24.5%). The median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score was 4 (interquartile range, 2-7). Invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and renal replacement therapy were required in 54.9%, 34.4%, and 18.5% of patients, respectively. At day 90, 94% of patients requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressors were deceased, compared to 38.7% with invasive ventilation alone and 17.2% without any organ support (P < .001). Overall, 90-day mortality reached 49.6%. SOFA score (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.04 [95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02-1.06]), admission between 2000 and 2012 (aHR, 2.30 [95% CI, 1.36-3.89]), disseminated infection (aHR, 2.32 [95% CI, 1.15-4.67]), and initiation of antifungal therapy before ICU admission (aHR, 0.38 [95% CI, .22-.63]) were independently associated with 90-day mortality, whereas HIV serostatus was not (aHR, 0.93 [95% CI, .47-1.84]).

CONCLUSIONS: Severe cryptococcosis requiring ICU admission affects an increasing number of patients without HIV and is associated with high, though declining, mortality. Early diagnosis and treatment are mandatory to improve prognosis.

Rationale and design of Ticagrelor with Aspirin Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Combined with Intravenous Thrombolysis in Patients with Ischemic Stroke (TAPIS): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled trial.
Diagnostic Yield of Repeat Blood Cultures and Risk Factors for Bloodstream Infection in Persistent Febrile Neutropenia.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal frequency of repeat blood cultures in persistent febrile neutropenia (FN) remains unknown. This study aimed to identify opportunities for blood culture diagnostic stewardship in persistent FN.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with hematology/oncology diagnoses and an FN episode lasting >3 days. Generalized estimating equation logistic regression models were used to evaluate risk factors for new bloodstream infection (BSI) after FN day 3.

RESULTS: Among 620 patients, the median FN duration was 5 days, with a median of 12 blood culture bottles collected per patient. On FN day 1, 25% of patients had a positive blood culture; on FN days 2-9, <5% of patients per day had a new organism isolated. Among 31 new organisms isolated after FN day 3, 8 (26%) were contaminants. Of 503 patients with ≥1 blood culture collected after FN day 3, 19 (4%) had a new BSI after FN day 3. FN onset in the peri-hematopoietic cell transplant period (from day -7 to day +30) was associated with lower odds of new BSI after FN day 3 (odds ratio, 0.18 [95% confidence interval, .04-.71]; P = .01). Thirty-six patients died within 30 days after FN day 3, including 4 with a new BSI after FN day 3; 1 death was attributable to BSI after FN day 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Detection of new BSIs after FN day 3 was uncommon, demonstrating the low diagnostic yield of repeat blood cultures after FN day 3. FN episodes in the peri-hematopoietic cell transplant period may be a potential focus for blood culture diagnostic stewardship initiatives.

Stroke medicine: what's next?

The prognostic value of expiratory carbon monoxide level for outcome prediction after myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess the prognostic value of expiratory carbon monoxide (CO) levels in patients admitted for myocardial infarction (MI).

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective study, expiratory CO levels were measured upon admission in consecutive patients hospitalized for MI across 39 centres. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause death. Secondary outcomes included 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACEs: cardiovascular death and recurrent MI) and in-hospital major adverse events (MAEs: death, severe ventricular arrhythmia, cardiogenic shock, and the need for mechanical ventilation). The prognostic value of expiratory CO levels was further evaluated using machine learning (ML) analysis. Among 717 patients (64 ± 13 years; 75% males; 33% active smokers; 43% ST-elevation MI), elevated expiratory CO levels (>11 ppm) were found in 79 patients (11%). Patients with elevated CO levels had a higher rate of 1-year all-cause mortality compared with those without (16.5% vs. 5.2%, P < 0.001). Elevated CO levels were independently associated with 1-year all-cause death across various adjustment models: comorbidities [odds ratio (95% confidence interval): 3.6 (1.7-7.5)], clinical parameters of in-hospital severity [4.5 (2.3-8.8)], and respiratory parameters [6.3 (3.1-12.8)]. Elevated CO levels were also independently associated with a significant increase in 1-year MACEs and in-hospital MAEs. Machine learning analysis identified CO level as one of the most important predictors of adverse events, compared with other known prognosticators.

CONCLUSION: This is the first study to demonstrate that elevated expiratory CO levels upon admission are independently associated with an increased risk of 1-year all-cause mortality, 1-year MACEs, and in-hospital MAEs in patients hospitalized for MI.

articles.title: Smoking and the risk of sudden cardiac arrest in young-aged adults: a Korean nationwide population-based study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Smoking is a risk factor for cardiovascular events. Regarding the different aetiology of sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) in younger individuals compared with the elderly, we investigated the linkage between smoking and the risk of SCA in young-aged adults.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this retrospective analysis, an observational longitudinal cohort was obtained from the national health screening database in South Korea. Adults aged between 20 and 39 years who underwent health screening from 2009 to 2012 were included. Smoking status was categorized as non-smokers, ex-smokers, and current smokers. The burden of smoking was classified as mild (<10 pack-years), moderate (<20 pack-years), and heavy smokers (≥20 pack-years). The primary outcome was the occurrence of SCA during follow-up. Among 6 293 672 individuals, the mean age was 30.8 years, and the median follow-up duration was 9.7 years. Comorbidities such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, or dyslipidaemia were rare. Non-smokers were most prevalent (55.2%), followed by current smokers (34.8%) and ex-smokers (10.1%). The incidence of SCA increased from non-smokers (0.06 per 1000 person-years), ex-smokers (0.08), to current smokers (0.14). Current smokers showed increased risk of SCA compared with non-smokers (adjusted hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.57-1.81, P < 0.001). The risk of SCA was not increased in ex-smokers (0.96, 0.86-1.07, P = 0.420). Higher smoking burden was associated with accelerated risk of SCA (adjusted hazard ratio in heavy smokers 2.15, 1.90-2.43, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In young-aged adults, current smoking was associated with significantly increased risk of SCA in long-term follow-up. The risk of SCA showed a dose-dependent association with cumulative burden of lifetime cigarette exposure.

articles.title: Differentiating central fever from infectious fever in intracerebral haemorrhage.
Association between chronic opioid exposure and cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Chronic opioid exposure (COE) is linked to adverse health outcomes, but its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to summarize published evidence on CVD risk associated with COE, including prescription opioids, opium use, and opioid use disorder (OUD).

METHODS AND RESULTS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews registration (CRD42024573206), we searched multiple databases for relevant human studies reporting associations between COE and CVD. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression explored associations by COE type, CVD outcome, and potential moderators. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Exposures. Seventeen studies (1 676 000 participants) met inclusion criteria, with 13 studies contributing 22 effect sizes to meta-analysis. Chronic opioid exposure was associated with increased CVD risk (pooled OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.12-2.70), though substantial heterogeneity was observed. Cerebrovascular accidents (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.45-2.35) and ischaemic heart disease (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.40-1.63) showed the strongest associations. Opium use had a significant association with CVD, whilst findings for OUD and prescription opioids were less consistent. Meta-regression identified study design as a key moderator.

CONCLUSION: Chronic opioid exposure is associated with increased risk of CVD, particularly cerebrovascular accidents and ischaemic heart disease. Given the global opioid and CVD burden, targeted interventions and integrated care approaches are needed. Findings are limited by heterogeneity and risk of bias in published studies. Further high-quality research should explore pathophysiological mechanisms, causality, dose-response relationships, and the potential reversibility of CVD risk following opioid cessation.

articles.title: When the smoke clears: the enduring threat of tobacco in stable coronary artery disease.
Caregivers' impact in heart failure: a cross-sectional study.
Smoking trajectories and residual cardiovascular risk in patients with stable coronary artery disease: an international cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: There is a variety of smoking habits trajectories in patients with established stable coronary artery disease (CAD), with unclear consequences on cardiovascular (CV) events. We aimed to clarify the impact of smoking cessation and reduction on long-term cardiovascular outcomes in stable CAD patients, evaluating whether quitting at any stage still provides significant benefits and to what extent.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The CLARIFY registry included 32 378 outpatients with stable CAD. Smoking history and status were recorded annually during the 5-year follow-up. In active smokers, we studied the effect of smoking cessation or reduction. In former smokers, we analysed the timing of smoking cessation relative to CAD diagnosis and residual CV risk based on years of abstinence. The primary outcome was a composite of CV death and MI. At inclusion, 46.2% of patients were former smokers and 12.5% current smokers. Amongst active smokers, smoking cessation in the stable phase of the disease was associated with improved outcomes, irrespective of timing (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.42-0.76, P < 0.001). However, smoking quantity reduction was not associated with improved CV outcomes. Among former smokers, 55.7% had quit within a year of CAD diagnosis. Each additional year of smoking post-CAD diagnosis increased CV risk. Former smokers never returned to the CV risk level of never smokers, regardless of years of abstinence.

CONCLUSION: In stable CAD patients, smoking cessation is associated with significantly better CV outcomes and survival, irrespective of the timing of cessation, and should therefore always be a priority. Smoking reduction was not associated with improved CV outcomes. Most former smokers quit within a year of CAD diagnosis, and CV risk increases with each subsequent year of active smoking.

LAY SUMMARY: In a cohort of over 32 000 patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) with a 5-year follow-up, the evolution of smoking habits revealed that:Quitting smoking at any point-even years after diagnosis-is associated with a 50% reduction in the risk of subsequent cardiovascular events and death. However, only 12% of active smokers quit each year on average. Conversely, reducing the number of cigarettes without fully quitting is not associated with a lower risk of adverse cardiovascular events.Most former smokers quit within a year of their CAD diagnosis, with cardiovascular risk increasing for each additional year of continued smoking afterward. Finally, former smokers never returned to the cardiovascular risk level of never smokers, regardless of years of abstinence.

articles.title: Occasional smoking is a risk factor for myocardial infarction in the population-based Tromsø Study, 2001-21.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: While the association between daily smoking and myocardial infarction (MI) risk is well-established, little is known concerning the relationship between occasional smoking and MI risk. In this Norwegian study, we aimed to investigate the risk of first-time MI among occasional smokers over a 20-year follow-up period.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective cohort study, data on smoking habits and relevant risk factors were collected from 15 617 participants enrolled in the fifth and/or sixth survey of the Tromsø Study. Participants were followed up for the first MI from 2001 to 2021. Smoking, age, marriage/cohabitant status, body mass index, hypertension, cholesterol, alcohol consumption, education, physical activity, and sex were included as covariates in Cox proportional hazard models. At baseline, 9.2% of participants were occasional smokers. Over the follow-up period, 1297 participants experienced their first MI. Adjusted for covariates, we observed a 41% increased MI risk among occasional smokers compared to never smokers [hazard ratio (HR) 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.11-1.80]. We noted a dose-response relationship in the hazards of smoking, categorized as never, former, occasional, and daily. Compared with never smokers, the relative risk of MI in occasional smokers was twice as high in women (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.43-3.04) and 11% higher in men (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.81-1.52).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights an elevated risk of MI among occasional smokers, with higher relative risk in women. The result emphasizes that there is no safe threshold for smoking, underlining the importance of smoking cessation.

articles.title: Low serum thyroid-stimulating hormone levels may be an early predictor of sepsis.
From consensus to evidence: Bridging the gap in pharmacotherapy for insomnia and sleep dysfunction in Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: This letter commends the Parkinson Study Group for their comprehensive consensus on sleep in Parkinson's disease while addressing critical gaps in insomnia and depression management. It emphasizes the need for evidence-based pharmacotherapies, avoiding off-label sedating antidepressants, and prioritizing rigorously designed clinical trials for non-motor sleep disturbances.

articles.title: Efficacy of Personalizing Cognitive Remediation for Schizophrenia by Targeting Impairments in Early Auditory Processing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESES: Early auditory processing (EAP) deficits are common but not universal in schizophrenia, are linked to impairments in higher cognitive functions and when improved are associated with downstream cognitive improvements. Assessment of baseline EAP training need provides an opportunity for cognitive remediation (CR) programs to personalize treatment and optimize impact. This confirmatory efficacy study examined the differential benefit of EAP training for those with and without baseline EAP deficits. Hypotheses were: (1) Only EAP impaired (EAP-) patients would benefit more from CR that included EAP training, (2) cognitive gains made by EAP- patients during CR that included EAP training would mediate the relationship between gains in EAP and functional capacity.

STUDY DESIGN: 184 outpatient adults diagnosed with schizophrenia were classified as having intact (n = 91) or impaired (n = 81) EAP and randomized to CR with restorative exercise plans that either included EAP training (n = 89) or did not (n = 83). Cognitive and functional outcomes were measured post-treatment and 3 months later.

STUDY RESULTS: Across CR treatment conditions, cognitive gain effect size was moderate. Treatment condition did not significantly impact EAP, cognitive, or functional outcomes for either EAP group at final endpoint. EAP improved significantly but modestly for EAP- patients across conditions. Cognitive gains did not mediate the relationship between EAP gains and functional capacity.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the value of CR for people with schizophrenia, demonstrate that EAP deficits are malleable, and that cognitive and functional gains can occur for EAP impaired patients, regardless of whether EAP training is provided.

articles.title: Fulminant Streptococcus canis-associated necrotizing cellulitis requiring hindlimb amputation in an immunosuppressed dog with diabetes mellitus.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: A 6-year-old neutered male Pomeranian with diabetes mellitus receiving chronic multidrug immunosuppressive therapy was presented with rapidly progressive swelling and hemorrhagic discoloration of the left hindlimb. The dog had febrile neutropenia and distributive shock, and cytology revealed septic suppurative inflammation with intracellular cocci. Despite stabilization and broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, the lesion progressed proximally, prompting hindlimb amputation for source control. Histopathology confirmed severe necrotizing cellulitis with vasculitis, and Streptococcus canis was isolated from tissue and surgical-site exudate. Subsequent wound management included additional debridement of residual devitalized tissue and negative pressure wound therapy. The dog remained clinically well at the 61-day follow-up. This case illustrates that canine necrotizing cellulitis without fascial involvement can progress rapidly and require aggressive surgical source control.

articles.title: Birthweight discordance and within-pair clustering of severe neonatal morbidity in twins in the neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Morbidity may cluster within twin pairs, but birthweight discordance (BWD) may relate differently to pairs with one or both twins affected.

AIMS: To quantify co-twin morbidity concordance and examine associations between BWD and pair-level outcome patterns.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective single-center secondary cohort analysis.

SUBJECTS: 742 complete co-twin pairs admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

OUTCOME MEASURES: A composite of neonatal morbidities classified pairs as both non-severe, discordant, or both severe. BWD associations were estimated using multinomial logistic regression.

RESULTS: There were 401 both-non-severe, 152 discordant, and 189 both-severe pairs. Cohen kappa was 0.55 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.49-0.61), and the co-twin recurrence risk ratio was 4.48 (95% CI 3.66-5.46). In the main model, adjusted odds ratios for BWD ≥25% were 2.70 (95% CI 1.31-5.57) for discordant pairs and 1.99 (95% CI 0.94-4.23) for both-severe pairs. The two associations did not differ statistically (ratio of odds ratios 1.36, 95% CI 0.68-2.72; P = 0.387). The affected infant was lighter in 50.3% of unequal-weight discordant pairs (95% CI 42.0-58.6%). Congenital malformation was associated with being the affected co-twin (conditional odds ratio 6.75, 95% CI 2.36-19.29).

CONCLUSIONS: Neonatal morbidity clustered within NICU-admitted twin pairs. BWD ≥25% was associated with discordant morbidity in the main model, but the association was not evident at the 20% threshold or after additional covariate adjustment. Congenital malformation, but not birthweight rank, was a within-pair correlate of morbidity.

articles.title: Improving Hand Hygiene to Reduce Healthcare Associated Infections in Neonatal Wards: WHO Multimodal Strategy, Rwanda.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are major causes of preventable neonatal morbidity and mortality. Suboptimal hand hygiene (HH) compliance among healthcare workers (HCWs) remains a key, modifiable driver of infection transmission. At the University Teaching Hospital of Kigali (CHUK), neonatal HAI incidence increased from 16% in 2023-2024 to 24% in July 2024-January 2025, whereas HH compliance was 39.7% without neonatal ward specific improvement program.

PURPOSE: Improve HH compliance among HCWs by ≥50% and reduce neonatal HAI incidence by ≥10% through implementation of the WHO Multimodal HH Improvement Strategy (MMHHIS).

METHODS: An 18-week pre-post quality-improvement project guided by the Plan-Do-Study-Act model (October 2025-January 2026) in neonatal wards (neonatology/neonatal intensive care unit [Neo/NICU], Neonatal Surgery). Intervention included system change, staff training (N = 60), contextual workplace reminders, weekly audits with structured feedback (3494 opportunities), and leadership engagement. Process measures included knowledge scores and infrastructure compliance, outcomes included HH compliance and HAI rates.

RESULTS: HCWs' HH knowledge improved from 64.07% to 86.40%. All 13 infrastructure elements were achieved and sustained with 100% compliance. HH compliance increased from 31.9% to 88.0%. Neonatal HAI rates decreased from 10.1% to 3.9% (61.4% relative reduction) in Neo/NICU and from 42.6% to 24.4% (42.7% reduction) in Neonatal Surgery.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: WHO MMHHIS is feasible, effective in improving compliance and reducing HAIs and scalable approach within CHUK and similar settings.

IMPLICATIONS FOR RESEARCH: Additional research on long-term sustainability and cost-effectiveness across settings.

articles.title: What Clinical Signs Are Associated With Mortality and Sepsis in Infants Aged 0 to 59 Days?
Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes ("AI scribes") are purported to reduce emergency department (ED) documentation burden, but ED evidence is largely single-site, uncontrolled, or self-reported, with exposure inferred rather than measured. We evaluated AI scribe use among attending emergency physicians across a multisite network, with exposure and outcomes read directly from the electronic health record.

METHODS: Across 20 EDs (3 academic and 17 community), AI scribe use was flagged per note from the patient consent statement within the ED note. Analyses were restricted to attending physicians and, to isolate the physician's own documentation, excluded teaching encounters and attestation notes identified from standardized attestation text. Endpoints, computed over the mature-adoption window (December 2025 onward, when Epic audit-log data are retained), were active time in the note (primary), note length, note-start time, completion lag, and 72-hour ED return. Within-physician models (physician and calendar-month fixed effects, clustered by physician) compared each adopter's AI-scribed notes with their own unassisted notes, adjusting only for pre-exposure case mix.

RESULTS: Among 275 attending physicians, 31% of encounters were AI-scribed. Physicians spent less active time in AI-scribed notes (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min-2.4 minutes after adjustment), started them about 15 minutes later (median 31 versus 17 minutes after first seeing the patient, and produced notes about 14% longer [median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters; within-physician +629 characters]). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1).

CONCLUSION: Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

articles.title: Who's on Airway? Trainee Tracheal Intubation Frequency and Outcomes Within the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine (NEAR4PEM).
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: We aimed to describe trainee performance and tracheal intubation outcomes in academic pediatric emergency departments.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study of intubations performed between January 2021 and December 2023, using data from the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine. Eligible encounters included children who underwent intubation with the first-attempt proceduralist identified as an emergency medicine resident, a pediatric resident, or a pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellow. The primary outcome was first-attempt success. The secondary outcome was adverse airway outcomes, defined as desaturation or tracheal intubation-associated adverse events. We compared intubation outcomes across trainee groups.

RESULTS: Over the 1,404 encounters during the study period, 642 (48%) were primary intubations performed on pediatric patients by an emergency medicine, pediatric or PEM trainee. A total of 343 (53%) first attempts were by emergency medicine residents, 254 (40%) by PEM fellows, and 45 (7%) by pediatric residents. The overall trainee first-attempt success rate was 471/642 (73%). First-attempt success by emergency medicine residents (75%) and PEM fellows (74%) were similar, and higher than first-attempt success by pediatric residents (58%). After accounting for potential confounders, there was no difference between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows in first-attempt success (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 to 1.28) or adverse airway outcome (aOR 1.4, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.18). In adjusted analysis, pediatric residents had a lower first-attempt success (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.82) and a higher adverse airway outcome (aOR 2.14, 95% CI 1.08 to 4.27) than emergency medicine residents.

CONCLUSION: There was no difference in first-attempt success and adverse airway outcomes between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows. Pediatric residents have lower first-attempt success and higher adverse airway outcomes than emergency medicine residents.

articles.title: Renal Denervation to Enable Kidney Transplant Listing in Resistant Hypertension Patient on Hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is often poorly controlled in patients with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and evidence for renal denervation in this population remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 38-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis because of thrombotic microangiopathy who developed refractory hypertension with recurrent hypertensive emergencies despite 6 antihypertensive agents and aggressive ultrafiltration, precluding kidney transplant listing. After a thorough secondary hypertension work-up, he underwent off-label catheter-based bilateral renal denervation, after which his blood pressure improved substantially, hypertensive emergencies ceased, and he was subsequently added to the transplant waitlist.

CONCLUSION: Renal denervation may serve as adjunctive therapy to help dialysis patients with resistant hypertension reach transplant candidacy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Understand the limitations of pharmacologic and dialytic therapy for blood pressure control in dialysis-dependent patients. Appreciate how refractory hypertension may serve as a barrier to kidney transplant listing and how renal denervation may address it.

articles.title: Transcatheter Closure of Congenital RCA-Replacing Aorto-Right Ventricular Tunnel.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aorto-right ventricular tunnels are rare congenital anomalies. Complete replacement of the right coronary artery (RCA) by such a tunnel is exceptionally uncommon.

CASE SUMMARY: A 58-year-old woman presented with progressive dyspnea. Echocardiography showed left ventricular dilatation and reduced systolic function. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated the absence of a native RCA ostium and a large tunnel arising from the right coronary sinus, following the expected RCA course and draining into the right ventricle. The distal right coronary territory was supplied by the left anterior descending artery collaterals. Transcatheter closure was performed via a retrograde transaortic approach using a 14/12-mm ventricular septal defect occluder, achieving complete tunnel exclusion without compromising coronary perfusion.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is a rare transcatheter closure of a congenital RCA-replacing aorto-right ventricular tunnel and supports further evaluation of this proposed procedural strategy. Because this is a single-case experience, the approach is considered hypothesis-generating rather than validated.

articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation

articles.title: Transition From CIWA-Ar to a Brief Alcohol Withdrawal Scale-based Protocol in General Medical Inpatients: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The Brief Alcohol Withdrawal Scale (BAWS) is a shorter alternative to the Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol, revised (CIWA-Ar), but the two have not been compared in general medical inpatients. We evaluated a transition from CIWA-Ar to BAWS in this population.

METHODS: Interrupted time series study of adults admitted from the emergency department to internal medicine with alcohol withdrawal syndrome, April 2021-April 2023. In April 2022, CIWA-Ar was replaced by BAWS, bundled with risk stratification and a phenobarbital pathway requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission for intravenous dosing. Primary outcomes (total sedative exposure in lorazepam equivalents, length of stay, inflation-adjusted cost) were analyzed as weekly series with segmented regression; secondary outcomes were ICU transfer, 30-day readmission, in-hospital mortality, and discharge against medical advice.

RESULTS: Of 23,506 encounters, 1341 were eligible. The transition produced no immediate (level) or sustained (slope) change in total sedative exposure (level -2.9 mg, 95% CI: -8.4 to 2.6), length of stay (-0.40 d, 95% CI: -1.5 to 0.69), or cost (0.027, 95% CI: -0.040 to 0.096), and was not associated with ICU transfer (OR 1.61, 95% CI: 0.83-3.19), 30-day readmission (OR 1.16, 0.87-1.54), in-hospital mortality (OR 1.32, 0.32-5.88), or discharge against medical advice (OR 0.90, 0.58-1.37); unadjusted phenobarbital use and ICU transfer increased.

CONCLUSIONS: Replacing CIWA-Ar with BAWS did not change total sedative exposure, length of stay, cost, or clinical outcomes in general medical inpatients. BAWS can be adopted safely, although the ICU requirement for intravenous phenobarbital may have offset potential resource gains.

articles.title: Prediction Model with Serum RBP4 and Clinical Features for Postoperative Recurrence of Intrahepatic Bile Duct Stones: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative recurrence of intrahepatic bile duct stones is common and is influenced by biliary stricture, cholangitis, and metabolic inflammation; however, a validated preoperative prediction tool is lacking. A nomogram combining serum retinol-binding protein 4 (RBP4) with clinical and imaging features was constructed and temporally validated to assess individualized recurrence risk. In a single-center retrospective cohort of 571 patients with complete stone clearance (2015-2022), split into development (n = 357) and temporal validation (n = 214) cohorts, the outcome was imaging-confirmed recurrence ≥6 months after surgery. A Cox nomogram with RBP4 modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for age, albumin, eGFR, history of cholangitis, bilobar involvement, biliary stricture, stone diameter, and diabetes, was internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Model performance was assessed using the C-index, time-dependent AUC, Brier score, calibration, and decision curve analysis and was compared with that of a clinical-only model. Over 1,695 person-years of follow-up, 184 recurrences occurred (1-year and 3-year recurrence rates: 8.96% and 31.84%, respectively). RBP4 showed an independent nonlinear association with recurrence (P < 0.001) and consistent results in sensitivity analyses. The nomogram provided clear risk stratification (log-rank P < 0.001) and good calibration. AUCs were 0.78 and 0.76 in the development cohort and 0.74 and 0.72 in the validation cohort at 1 and 3 years, respectively; corresponding C-indices were 0.76 and 0.72. Adding RBP4 significantly improved model fit (P < 0.001) and yielded net benefit across threshold probabilities ranging from 10% to 30%. Preoperative RBP4, combined with clinical and imaging features, may facilitate individualized estimation of 1-year and 3-year recurrence risk, with acceptable performance in temporal validation, although external validation remains necessary.

articles.title: Long Non-Coding RNA H19 Protection Against Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury in Diabetic Mice Through Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1 Alpha Signaling.
articles.abstract: Diabetes can aggravate myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI), but the role of long non-coding RNA H19 (lncRNA H19) is still unclear. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of lncRNA H19 on MIRI in diabetic mice. C57BL/KsJ db/db diabetes mice and db/+ normal mice (n = 40/group) were divided into sham operation, ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), and I/R+Lv-H19 (lentivirus-mediated H19 overexpression) groups. Echocardiography evaluation of cardiac function and Evans Blue/triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining were used to determine the infarct area; terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) and caspase-3 to detect cell apoptosis; western blot to detect autophagy markers (LC3-II/I, p62) and HIF-1α protein expression; and dual luciferase reporter genes to validate the competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanism. H19 expression in the hearts of diabetic mice after I/R was significantly lower than that of normal mice (P < 0.05). H19 overexpression significantly improved cardiac function (left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening restored to near-normal levels), reduced infarct size, and lowered serum CK, CK-MB, and LDH levels (P < 0.05). H19 overexpression regulated autophagic flow (LC3-II/I ratio and p62 expression reversal) and inhibited caspase-3 activity (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, H19 acts as a ceRNA for miR-4735-3p, releasing its inhibition of hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha (HIF-1α) and activating the HIF-1α signaling pathway. The results of this study provide mechanistic insight into the molecular processes underlying myocardial I/R injury in diabetic mice and identify LNCRNA H19 as a candidate target for further preclinical research.

articles.title: Pathogen Spectrum and Epidemiological Characteristics Detected by Multiplex Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification in Elderly Patients in Guangzhou.
articles.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality in the elderly. This study aimed to investigate the distribution and epidemiological features of 10 common respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) in elderly patients in Guangzhou, China, from 2022 to 2024, to support precise clinical management, rational antimicrobial use, and regional infection control. A cross-sectional study was performed, enrolling 4,010 elderly patients who underwent respiratory pathogen testing by multiplex LAMP from April 2022 to March 2024 at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital. Multiplex LAMP was used to detect 10 major pathogens. Epidemiological characteristics were analyzed across genders, ages, seasons, months, specimen types, and departments. At least one pathogen was detected in 1,474 (36.76%) patients. Single detection was dominant (72.18%, 1,064/1,474). The detection rates of Haemophilus influenzae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Staphylococcus aureus, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Escherichia coli, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were 11.40%, 10.75%, 8.10%, 5.89%, 5.41%, 3.02%, 2.66%, 2.64%, 0.56%, and 0.33%, respectively. The detection rates of Kpn and Mtb were significantly higher in males (P < 0.05). Significant age-group differences were observed for Sau, Eco, Pae, Aba, and Sma (P < 0.001) and for Kpn (P = 0.028). Kpn and Pae showed significant seasonal variation (P < 0.05). Pae positivity peaked in April 2022 (36.54%). Significant differences across specimen types and departments were observed for several pathogens (P < 0.05). Haemophilus influenzae was the most prevalent pathogen detected by multiplex LAMP in this elderly cohort in Guangzhou. Single-pathogen detection was the predominant pattern. These findings provide a basis for empirical antimicrobial therapy and regional epidemiological surveillance in elderly patients undergoing respiratory pathogen testing.

articles.title: Intra-wound Vancomycin Powder for Surgical Site Infection Prophylaxis in Spinal Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Surgical site infection remains a consequential complication of spinal surgery despite intravenous antibiotic prophylaxis, maintenance of normothermia, glycemic control, and meticulous surgical technique. Applying vancomycin powder directly into the wound before closure achieves high local drug concentrations with minimal systemic absorption and was hypothesized to lower surgical site infection rates compared with standard intravenous prophylaxis alone. Five databases were searched through May 2026 for comparative studies of patients undergoing spinal surgery in which one group received intra-wound vancomycin powder at wound closure and a concurrent control group did not. Of 2,765 records, 700 remained after duplicate removal, 96 full texts were assessed, and 14 studies met all eligibility criteria, comprising 9,802 patients: 4,516 received vancomycin powder and 5,286 served as controls. Four studies were randomized trials and ten were nonrandomized cohorts. Odds ratios were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect method, with random-effects estimates reported alongside. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Vancomycin powder was associated with lower odds of overall surgical site infection (odds ratio 0.55; 95% confidence interval 0.44 to 0.70), deep infection (0.50; 0.37 to 0.68), and superficial infection (0.55; 0.32 to 0.93). The direction of effect persisted across seven sensitivity analyses and a leave-one-out analysis, with no funnel plot asymmetry detected. However, the association was driven by nonrandomized studies; when restricted to the four randomized trials, it was no longer statistically significant (0.73; 0.45 to 1.18). Intra-wound vancomycin powder is therefore associated with fewer surgical site infections in spinal surgery, but the evidence is of moderate certainty, and adequately powered randomized trials remain necessary.

articles.title: Association of Butylphthalide Combined with Antiplatelet Therapy with Functional Recovery After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke, but functional outcomes remain suboptimal, and real-world evidence regarding adjunctive butylphthalide therapy is limited. This single-center retrospective observational study evaluated the association between adjunctive butylphthalide plus antiplatelet therapy and functional recovery after IVT in 118 patients with acute ischemic stroke treated between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were classified by post-thrombolysis treatment: 62 received butylphthalide plus standard antiplatelet therapy, and 56 received standard antiplatelet therapy alone. After propensity score matching, 52 patients were retained in each group. The primary outcome was 90-day functional prognosis, with a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2 defined as a favorable outcome. Secondary outcomes included National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, infarct volume, cerebral blood flow (CBF) perfusion recovery, serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), plasma D-dimer (D-D), Barthel Index (BI) score, and adverse events. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with poor 90-day functional prognosis. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the matched groups (all P > 0.05). At 90 days, the butylphthalide combination group had a higher rate of favorable functional prognosis than the antiplatelet-only group (73.1% vs. 48.1%, P = 0.009). The combination group also had lower NIHSS scores, smaller infarct volumes, lower hs-CRP and D-D levels, better CBF perfusion recovery, and higher BI scores (all P < 0.05). Adverse event rates did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.631). Multivariable analysis identified the treatment regimen as independently associated with 90-day functional prognosis (P = 0.009). Adjunctive butylphthalide plus antiplatelet therapy after IVT was associated with better 90-day functional recovery in this retrospective cohort; however, the observational design does not permit causal inference, and the safety findings are limited to the prespecified events reported here.

articles.title: Radionuclide Imaging for Tracking Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy in Knee Osteoarthritis: Current Status and Pathways to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disease, and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy has emerged as a promising regenerative treatment option. However, the clinical translation of MSC therapy faces significant challenges, particularly in effectively monitoring the in vivo behavior of MSCs, including their survival, biodistribution, and functional integration. This review provides a comprehensive examination of the current landscape of radionuclide imaging techniques, particularly positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), for tracking MSCs in the treatment of KOA. It outlines the primary challenges associated with these imaging methods, including limitations related to radiotoxicity, tracer efflux, and the precision of quantitative cell tracking. Furthermore, the review discusses the potential of multimodal imaging and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automated analysis to address these challenges, facilitating more accurate and functional monitoring of MSCs and their therapeutic effects. The review concludes by outlining future research directions, with an emphasis on the development of improved labeling methods, optimized imaging technologies, and enhanced integration of AI into clinical applications. These advancements are crucial for bridging the gap between preclinical findings and clinical practice, ultimately establishing radionuclide imaging as a potentially valuable tool for the clinical management of KOA.

articles.title: Isolation of Ventricular Cardiomyocytes from the Annual Killifish Nothobranchius furzeri for Whole-Cell Patch Clamp Recordings.
articles.abstract: Isolated working cardiomyocytes remain the standard approach for studying cardiac electrophysiology. Single-cell preparations allow for direct investigation and precise measurement of ionic currents and action potentials without the structural complexity of intact cardiac tissue. Nothobranchius furzeri (African turquoise killifish) has rapidly emerged as a prominent model organism for gerontological research due to its exceptionally short lifespan and similarities in aging mechanisms with mammals, including humans. This species combines practical advantages such as small size, inexpensive husbandry, and a rapid life cycle with translational relevance. N. furzeri exhibits age-dependent declines in locomotor activity, cognition, and organ function, accumulation of molecular hallmarks of aging, and sensitivity to pharmacological treatments that modulate lifespan and healthspan. However, investigating the functional decline of the aging heart requires a reliable method to obtain high-quality, viable cells suitable for demanding single-cell techniques. This study optimized a previously described protocol for the isolation of Danio rerio cardiomyocytes to ensure consistent recovery of healthy working myocytes from both young and senescent N. furzeri. This protocol describes the isolation of ventricular cardiomyocytes from N. furzeri specifically optimized for the whole-cell patch clamp technique. The article demonstrates how to efficiently excise the heart, perform enzymatic dissociation of the myocardium by retrograde perfusion, and store the isolated cardiomyocytes. We discuss the selection of enzymes required to digest the extracellular matrix and intercellular junctions without compromising ion channel structure. Freshly isolated cardiomyocytes are suitable for high-resolution electrophysiological assays, including action potential recordings and measurements of major inward and outward ionic currents across age groups. The article also addresses the features of cardiomyocyte isolation in fish that differ from standard mammalian isolation procedures.

articles.title: Admission Albumin-Corrected Anion Gap and Subsequent Tricuspid Regurgitation Velocity Elevation After COPD Exacerbation.
articles.abstract: Admission albumin-corrected anion gap (ACAG) may reflect metabolic stress during an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but its relationship with subsequent pulmonary vascular abnormalities is unclear. This study included 294 adults hospitalized with AECOPD between January 2022 and November 2024 in a single-center retrospective cohort. Participants had baseline tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV) <3.4 m/s and at least one follow-up echocardiogram. The primary endpoint was first detected TRV ≥3.4 m/s within 12 calendar months after discharge. During available follow-up, 105 participants (35.7%) reached the endpoint and 12 died before detection. Each 5 mmol/L higher ACAG was associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.17 (95% CI, 1.51-3.11) and a cause-specific hazard ratio of 1.66 (95% CI, 1.34-2.05). A sensitivity analysis using TRV >3.4 m/s identified 99 events and gave an adjusted odds ratio of 1.90 (95% CI, 1.32-2.75). Adding ACAG to the clinical reference model increased the cross-validated area under the curve from 0.803 to 0.829; the extended-model calibration slope was 0.823. Among participants without a detected event, the last readable echocardiogram occurred a median of 323 days after discharge. Admission ACAG was associated with subsequent TRV elevation and provided modest additional discrimination in this cohort. Its availability in routine admission testing makes it a candidate for further evaluation in post-exacerbation risk assessment, with prospective external validation needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Stem Cell Educator Therapy for Ex Vivo Immune Modulation of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells in Patients with Long COVID.
articles.abstract: Long COVID, generally defined as clinical symptoms persisting for 3 months or longer following severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, affects multiple organs and systems. At least 400 million people globally are living with long COVID, with symptoms including persistent fatigue and brain fog. Currently, long COVID care mainly consists of symptomatic management and supportive approaches, with no validated effective treatments available that address the underlying inflammation. Stem Cell Educator (SCE) therapy is a treatment developed to modulate immune responses. This protocol describes SCE therapy and its application in patients with long COVID to evaluate safety, clinical outcomes, and immunological changes. During SCE therapy, a patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) are collected by leukapheresis and co-cultured with adherent cord-blood-derived multipotent stem cells (CB-SC) in vitro, after which the "educated" PBMC are returned to the patient's circulation via infusion. SCE therapy has previously been evaluated in clinical studies for type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune diseases. Twenty-five patients with long COVID (15 males and 10 females) received SCE therapy. Five patients experienced mild adverse effects during apheresis, and one patient reported itching during infusion. Brain fog and fatigue disappeared in 21 of 25 patients following treatment, and most participants reported feeling refreshed, energized, and mentally clear. Flow cytometry demonstrated reductions in inflammatory markers, including interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β)-positive cells and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 16 (CXCL16)-positive cells. These findings demonstrate the application of SCE therapy in patients with long COVID and provide preliminary clinical and immunological observations supporting further evaluation of this approach.

articles.title: Microvascular Obstruction After Reperfusion in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Structured Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) restores epicardial coronary flow in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but microvascular and tissue-level reperfusion may remain impaired. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined microvascular obstruction (MVO) and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) both mark severe reperfusion injury but reflect distinct tissue processes. This structured narrative review synthesizes evidence on MVO mechanisms, multimodal phenotypes, and interventions. Available evidence implicates interacting contributions from distal embolization, endothelial barrier and vasomotor dysfunction, pericyte-mediated capillary constriction, immunothrombosis, and tissue edema. IMH reflects more extensive microvascular destruction with erythrocyte extravasation. Angiography, electrocardiography, invasive physiology, angiography-derived indices, echocardiography, and CMR assess different pathophysiologic levels. Discordance between modalities is therefore not necessarily contradictory. Across trials, improvements in surrogate endpoints have often not translated into long-term clinical benefit, partly because of mechanistic heterogeneity and misaligned treatment timing and endpoints. A conceptual, reperfusion-centered T- to T5 research framework is proposed for serial within-patient assessment. It links early physiology, inflammatory and thrombotic biomarkers, acute-phase CMR, and long-term remodeling. Future trials should align mechanistic enrichment, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to establish a continuous evidence chain from target engagement to clinical outcomes.

articles.title: A Visual Protocol Integrating Dynamic Albumin, Prealbumin, and Transferrin Trajectories into Fluid and Nutritional Reassessment in Sepsis.
articles.abstract: This study developed a visual management approach for early fluid resuscitation in sepsis based on dynamic stratification of albumin, prealbumin, and transferrin. The retrospective analysis included 100 patients after propensity score matching. Measurements of the three proteins at T0, T6, T24, and T72 were considered together with fluid exposure, fluid responsiveness, and tissue perfusion indicators to derive a composite score and dynamic phenotypes; these results were then used to standardize reassessment, fluid management, and nutritional evaluation. Compared with conventional management, visual management showed numerically lower additional crystalloid administration during 3-6 h and total intravenous input during 0-24 h (median difference -6.70 mL/kg, 95% confidence interval -18.20 to 2.30; adjusted p = 0.091), as well as more frequent fluid-responsiveness assessments and an earlier first assessment, although none of these comparisons remained statistically significant after multiplicity adjustment. The prealbumin group-by-time interaction did not remain statistically significant after adjustment for multiplicity, and the composite-score findings were not interpreted due to unresolved scoring discrepancies. The visual management group had higher lactate clearance at 24 h in the exploratory 95-comparison Bonferroni sensitivity analysis (adjusted p = 0.040), whereas net fluid-balance differences at 24 h and 72 h did not remain statistically significant. Time to the resuscitation target was not significantly different in the 24 h censored Cox analysis (hazard ratio 1.509, 95% confidence interval 0.948-2.403; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.166), and no statistically significant differences were identified in organ-support requirements or mortality. This approach may offer a standardized framework for fluid reassessment and nursing decisions after initial resuscitation, although its clinical value requires confirmation in prospective, multicenter studies.

articles.title: Non-Invasive Neuromodulation for Post-Stroke Anxiety Symptoms: An Umbrella Review and Evidence Mapping of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke anxiety can impair rehabilitation, participation, and quality of life. This umbrella review mapped systematic reviews on non-invasive neuromodulation for anxiety symptoms after stroke. PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception through June 1, 2026. Published reviews with quantitative anxiety results were eligible, including reviews in which anxiety was secondary to pain, sleep disturbance, or depression. Reporting completeness, methodological quality, and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Seven reviews were mapped, comprising six pairwise meta-analyses and one Bayesian network meta-analysis. Selected estimates suggested symptom improvement, whereas others showed no clear difference. All reviews had low or critically low methodological quality. Interpretation was limited by overlapping trials, small outcome-specific sample sizes, heterogeneous interventions, and inconsistencies across source reports. Anxiety-score changes in populations recruited for other post-stroke conditions do not establish a direct effect on clinically defined post-stroke anxiety. Source-level population eligibility and certainty judgments require particular scrutiny when mixed neurological populations contribute to pooled estimates. Non-invasive neuromodulation remains investigational for post-stroke anxiety. Current evidence does not support routine use of a specific protocol or replacement of standard multidisciplinary stroke care. Future trials should prospectively define anxiety, standardize stimulation and sham procedures, and assess sustained benefit and safety.

articles.title: Emergency Surgery and Preoperative Frailty with Postoperative Pulmonary Complications in Elderly Patients Undergoing Major Abdominal Surgery.
articles.abstract: This single-center retrospective study investigated associations of emergency surgery and preoperative frailty with postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) in elderly major abdominal surgery patients. Of 350 initially recruited patients at The First Hospital of Jiaxing (Mar 2024-Mar 2025), 294 were eligible after screening and stratified into PPCs (n = 53) and non-PPCs (n = 241) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified PPC predictors; interaction analysis evaluated their joint effect. Receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated the predictive performance of individual indicators and the combined model. Between-group disparities were identified in age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, smoking, diabetes, emergency surgery, preoperative frailty, assess respiratory risk in surgical patients in Catalonia (ARISCAT) score, infusion volume, and postoperative day 1 visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score (all P < 0.05). The PPCs group had higher rates of emergency surgery (P = 0.002) and preoperative frailty (P < 0.001). Patients with both emergency surgery and preoperative frailty had a 35.7% PPCs rate (P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, ARISCAT score, postoperative day 1 VAS pain score, emergency surgery, and preoperative frailty as independent factors associated with PPCs (all P < 0.05). Emergency surgery and preoperative frailty were both independent risk factors for PPCs, and their combination showed a significant multiplicative interaction [interaction odds ratio (OR) = 1.363, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.010-1.832, P = 0.044], yielding a joint OR notably higher than either factor alone. A combined model including age, emergency surgery, preoperative frailty, ARISCAT score, and postoperative day 1 VAS score achieved an area under the curve of 0.894 (95% CI: 0.833-0.956), which was higher than any single indicator (all P < 0.05). Preoperative frailty was associated with PPCs more strongly than emergency surgery in this cohort, and the two factors showed a joint association; assessment and intensified care are recommended.

articles.title: Foundation Models in Gastroenterology: Emerging Applications and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Foundation models are being investigated in gastroenterology because the specialty already generates multimodal data, including endoscopy videos, pathology slides, abdominal images, laboratory results, molecular profiles, and longitudinal clinical notes. This review examines where these models may be useful in emerging applications, where evidence remains limited, and what is required before wider clinical deployment. Large language models (LLMs) can support document organization, report generation, guideline retrieval, and patient communication, but fluent output can conceal errors. Endoscopic models are beginning to move beyond single-task polyp detection towards reusable visual pretraining across gastrointestinal sites and procedures. Pathology and radiology foundation models may assist with biomarker prediction, image segmentation, and tumor detection, although performance remains sensitive to staining, scanners, acquisition protocols, and case mix. The immediate goal is not to build a single model that covers the entire specialty. Rather, gastroenterology needs systems that are locally validated, auditable, privacy-aware, uncertainty-calibrated, and sufficiently focused to remain within clinical responsibility.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided High-Voltage Long-Duration Pulsed Radiofrequency of the Suprascapular Nerve for Persistent Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain.
articles.abstract: Hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP) is a common complication after stroke that can interfere with upper-limb rehabilitation. Persistent cases may respond inadequately to conventional conservative treatments or suprascapular nerve blocks. This article describes a standardized ultrasound-guided high-voltage long-duration pulsed radiofrequency (HL-PRF) protocol targeting the suprascapular nerve. Ultrasound is used to identify the suprascapular notch, surrounding anatomical structures, and adjacent vessels. A radiofrequency cannula is advanced to the target under real-time guidance, and its position is confirmed by sensory and motor stimulation. HL-PRF is then delivered at 99 V for 6 min while the temperature is maintained at or below 42 °C. The clinical outcomes presented here are illustrative observations from two patients with persistent HSP and do not represent findings from a controlled clinical study. In both cases, lower resting and movement-evoked pain scores and increased shoulder passive range of motion were observed at the 1-month follow-up. Pain scores at the 3-month telephone follow-up remained below baseline values. No procedure-related adverse events were observed or documented in either case during the available follow-up period. These cases are included to illustrate the clinical application and potential outcomes of the protocol rather than to establish efficacy. This protocol provides a detailed procedural framework for ultrasound-guided HL-PRF of the suprascapular nerve in patients with persistent HSP.

articles.title: Anterior Versus Posterior Circulation Acute Ischemic Stroke and 3-Month Cognitive Profiles: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is common, but its pattern may differ between vascular territories. This single-center cohort included adults with first-ever, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed acute ischemic stroke admitted between May 2022 and June 2024. Infarcts were classified as anterior or posterior circulation, and cognition was assessed in person at 3 months using the Beijing version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). The primary PSCI definition was an education-adjusted MoCA score <26, with a sensitivity analysis using <22. Of 173 enrolled patients, 167 completed follow-up (91 anterior and 76 posterior circulation infarctions). PSCI occurred in 50/91 (54.9%) and 27/76 (35.5%) patients, respectively (p = 0.012). The unadjusted odds ratio was 2.21 (95% confidence interval, 1.18-4.14), and the adjusted odds ratio was 2.18 (95% confidence interval, 1.06-4.49; p = 0.035). With the <22 cutoff, the corresponding prevalences were 31.9% and 15.8%, and the adjusted odds ratio was 2.43 (95% confidence interval, 1.06-5.54; p = 0.035). After false-discovery-rate correction, differences in visuospatial/executive, naming, delayed-recall, language, abstraction, and orientation performance remained, whereas attention did not differ. Cognitive outcomes differed between vascular-territory groups despite similar global disability scores; these group-level associations do not establish a causal effect of territory or a domain-specific diagnosis.

articles.title: Associations of International Normalized Ratio and Hematocrit With Stroke Status and Machine Learning Mortality Prediction in Critical Care Databases.
articles.abstract: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability. This retrospective cohort study evaluated associations of international normalized ratio (INR) and hematocrit (Hct) with stroke status in 29,831 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Stroke status was identified using predefined International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revision codes. INR and Hct were defined using the first measurements within 24 h after ICU admission. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, quartile analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Primary analyses used complete-case cohorts, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. A post hoc exploratory secondary analysis among patients with stroke used Cox regression to identify six prognostic variables for machine learning-based prediction of ICU mortality. Stroke proportions decreased across increasing INR quartiles and increased across increasing Hct quartiles. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in INR was associated with lower stroke odds, with odds ratios (ORs) of 0.105-0.395 across cohorts, whereas each 1-percentage-point increase in Hct was associated with higher stroke odds (ORs, 1.076-1.103). RCS analyses supported overall associations but not consistent nonlinearity after full adjustment. Multiple-imputation results were directionally consistent. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.669-0.766), 0.670 (95% CI, 0.603-0.737), and 0.630 (95% CI, 0.557-0.703) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. INR was inversely associated and Hct positively associated with stroke status. These observational associations require cautious interpretation; the exploratory ICU mortality analysis provides a complementary prognostic perspective among patients with stroke.

articles.title: Predicting 30-day mortality in upper gastrointestinal bleeding using APUA components and lactate: Development and internal validation.
articles.abstract: Early mortality risk assessment is crucial for acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB). This study sought to develop and internally validate a prediction model using age, pulse, urea, and albumin (APUA) components, and to assess the added value of admission lactate levels. This retrospective, single-center study included 700 adults presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute UGIB between 2018 and 2025, excluding confirmed variceal hemorrhage. We developed multivariable logistic regression models, both with and without lactate, using continuous APUA components to predict 30-day all-cause mortality. Complete-case analyses evaluated discrimination, calibration, and net benefit, with internal validation performed using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Fifty-two patients (7.4%) died within 30 days. Lactate was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 1-mmol/L increase, 1.455; 95% confidence interval, 1.270-1.667). Adding lactate significantly increased the apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.693 to 0.777 (AUC difference, 0.084; p = 0.003) and improved the optimism-corrected concordance statistic from 0.670 to 0.756. Calibration and overall predictive accuracy also improved, and decision curve analysis showed a higher net benefit across most evaluated thresholds. Furthermore, lactate enhanced the apparent discrimination of three established comparator scores. While the APUA-component model demonstrated modest discrimination, incorporating lactate significantly improved its predictive performance. Independent external validation is necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Eosinophilic myocarditis in platelet-derived growth factor receptor α-rearranged myeloid neoplasm with central nervous system involvement: a case report.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammatory condition caused by eosinophilic infiltration of the myocardium, often associated with systemic or hematologic disorders.
