Among males, higher morning cortisol levels were observed in relation to exposure to PM10 (β = 0.058; 95% CI = 0.003, 0.112), NOx (β = 0.070; 95% CI = 0.017, 0.123), and noise (β = 0.120; 95% CI = 0.024, 0.215), while inverse associations were found with greenness (e.g. for NDVI 500 m β = -0.165; 95% CI = -0.263, -0.067). Similar findings were observed for evening cortisol. In contrast, females exhibited opposite trends. NDVI was significantly positively associated with higher evening cortisol levels during the summer, particularly for NDVI within 100 m (β = 0.326; 95% CI = 0.063, 0.590), while no seasonal pattern was observed in relation to air pollutants or road traffic noise. Several sex-by-exposure interactions remained significant after false discovery rate correction, whereas season-specific patterns did not.

IMPACT: This study investigates how multiple residential environmental exposures, air pollution, road traffic noise, and greenness, relate to salivary cortisol as a biomarker of stress in young adulthood. Using detailed individual-level exposure modelling and a well-characterised population-based birth cohort, we assess both morning and evening cortisol and examine single and combined exposure impact. While overall associations were largely null, exploratory post hoc subgroup analyses suggested potential sex-specific differences in the associations between environmental exposures and salivary cortisol, whereas evidence for seasonal differences was weaker and did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. The findings highlight the importance of considering multiple environmental exposures and susceptibility factors when evaluating stress-related biological mechanisms in young adults.

SIGNIFICANCE: We found no overall associations between environmental exposures and salivary cortisol in young adults, although exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential sex-specific differences.

Association between childhood maltreatment and body composition: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the evidence on the association between child maltreatment and body composition indicators.

METHOD: Original studies examining child maltreatment before 18 years of age as the exposure and body composition as the outcome were eligible. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, Scopus, PsycINFO and Web of Science databases, without language or date restrictions, up to 23 April 2026. Screening was conducted independently by two reviewers using the Rayyan platform, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Data were extracted into a standardized spreadsheet, and study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and its adapted version for cross-sectional studies. Owing to substantial methodological heterogeneity in exposure and outcomes assessment, a qualitative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: Of 2993 records identified, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria, published between 2015 and 2026, with sample sizes ranging from 75 to 151,143 participants, aged 3-90 years, and most studies (n = 9) conducted in high-income countries. Three studies had a longitudinal design, five were cross-sectional, and four reported cross-sectional analyses within longitudinal design. Nine studies found a positive association between child maltreatment and increased adiposity, particularly among adults in high-income countries, with physical abuse being the most frequently implicated exposure. Total and visceral body fat were the most frequently assessed outcomes.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the need for further research on the relationship between maltreatment and adiposity in children, adolescents, and populations from low- and middle-income countries, as well as for longitudinal studies to clarify the specific effects of different types of maltreatment and inform targeted prevention strategies.

LIMITATIONS: Most included studies relied on retrospective assessment of child maltreatment, and substantial heterogeneity across studies precluded quantitative synthesis. This study was supported by the Coordination for the Improvement of Higher Education Personnel (CAPES) through the PROEX Program. PROSPERO REGISTRATION : CRD42024581666.

articles.title: FLAT-WHITE: from target trial emulation to federated high-throughput causal machine learning using decentralized real-world data.
articles.abstract: Randomized clinical trials remain the gold standard for evaluating treatment effects but are often infeasible for rapidly assessing drug repurposing opportunities, particularly in complex conditions such as Alzheimer's disease. Target trial emulation (TTE) provides a principled framework for causal inference with electronic health records and, when coupled with modern machine learning, enables scalable analyses across distributed health systems. We present FLAT-WHITE (Federated Lossless Algorithm for Target Trial Emulation with Overlap Weighting for Healthcare Data Integration via Trusted and Efficient Communication), a novel federated causal machine learning pipeline for high-throughput treatment effect estimation without sharing patient-level data. FLAT-WHITE is a one-shot, lossless algorithm, requiring a single communication round while achieving results equivalent to centralized pooled analyses. With overlap weighting on the propensity score, it robustly addresses heterogeneity in treatment assignment and ensures valid causal inference in decentralized settings. We demonstrate FLAT-WHITE in a Alzheimer's drug repurposing study, scanning 181 candidate drugs using data from four health learning systems encompassing approximately 150,000 patients with mild cognitive impairment. Findings were validated externally in 339,180 patients from the TriNetX global research network. FLAT-WHITE enables rapid, large-scale, and secure evaluation of treatment effects and establishes a foundation for collaborative clinical research across diverse healthcare systems.

articles.title: Reconstructive management of an extensive myelomeningocele defect using allogeneic fascia lata as temporary biological coverage: a case-based mini-review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extensive myelomeningocele defects may be difficult to reconstruct when tension-free primary skin closure cannot be achieved, and an appropriate local flap is not available. In such cases, various biological materials and dermal substitutes have been used. Allogeneic fascia lata is a mechanically robust tissue with established use in reconstructive surgery, but its use as temporary superficial biological coverage for extensive myelomeningocele defects has not been specifically described.

CASE DESCRIPTION: We report a term male newborn weighing 3.5 kg with a 16 × 10 cm thoracolumbosacral myelomeningocele and insufficient surrounding skin to achieve tension-free primary closure. After neural repair and watertight dural closure, the defect was covered with allogeneic fascia lata obtained from the Tissue Bank of Hospital de Pediatría "Prof. Dr. Juan P. Garrahan" and used as temporary biological coverage. During follow-up, progressive granulation tissue formation and centripetal epithelialization from the skin margins were observed, with complete epithelial coverage achieved at four months. At one-year follow-up, the reconstructed area remained stable, with no local infection or need for additional reconstructive procedures.

CONCLUSIONS: Banked allogeneic fascia lata may be a salvage option for temporary biological coverage of extensive myelomeningocele defects when conventional reconstructive options are not feasible. Potential advantages include mechanical strength, avoidance of donor-site morbidity, and immediate availability in centers with institutional tissue banks, with potential logistical and economic benefits compared with commercially manufactured substitutes. These findings are based on a single case and do not establish comparative efficacy, safety, or reproducibility of the technique.

articles.title: White matter fiber bundles enable robust conduction and time-critical signaling despite axon caliber variation.
articles.abstract: Axon caliber determines signal conduction velocity and varies within and across the bundles that form the brain's wiring. Our knowledge of this organization derives largely from 2D histology, assuming cylindrical axons whose calibers are described by their radius. However, recent 3D histology reveals substantial along-axon variability in radius, calling into question 2D-derived insights into axon radius and conduction velocity. We show in 450,000 3D axon reconstructions from male rats that-despite this individual variation-axon bundles possess stable radius distributions at the ensemble level. These distributions are faithfully captured by 2D cross-sections and yield robust conduction velocity predictions, as along-axon variability has only a modest effect. Conduction in large axons is particularly stable, supporting time-critical signaling. With 2D sampling validated, we leverage 46 million human corpus callosum axons from 2D histology to determine sample size requirements across neuroscience applications. Our findings show how axonal organization gives rise to stable ensemble statistics and conduction, explaining and reinforcing decades of 2D histology-based research.

articles.title: Longitudinal Skin Bacterial Cluster Associated With Protection Against Allergic Co-Morbidity in Pediatric Atopic Dermatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is an inflammatory skin condition that often portends the development of allergic comorbidities. Despite evidence supporting the role of the skin microbiome in AD, its temporal patterns and associations with risk or protection for allergic co-morbidity remain unclear. Our objective is to characterize core species of the pediatric AD bacterial microbiome, assess microbial networks and clusters, and identify global microbial changes relevant to AD and the atopic march.

METHODS: We performed metagenomic shotgun sequencing on 353 non-lesional skin samples from children in the Mechanisms of Progression of Atopic Dermatitis to Asthma in Children (MPAACH) cohort across 5 annual visits. We assessed taxonomic composition and analyzed longitudinal skin microbial patterns with progression to allergic co-morbidities.

RESULTS: We identified 436 distinct species. Shannon diversity and richness declined with age, and socioeconomic factors explained the variance in species composition. Staphylococcus aureus (SA) was more abundant in severe AD. Cluster 5, comprised of typically gut-associated microbes, was more abundant in non-sensitized children who did not develop allergic co-morbidities over time.

CONCLUSIONS: Our analyses revealed key patterns in core taxa, diversity and abundance of the skin microbiome over time in early life and highlighted previously unexplored factors such as socioeconomic status as key contributors to the variability in species composition. Abundance of SA confers risk, while gut-associated microbes may offer protection, influencing the clinical trajectory of AD and the atopic march. Thus, these results provide a novel and comprehensive understanding of the temporal dynamics of the skin microbiota in pediatric AD.

articles.title: Exercise-induced lactylation in WDR41 initiates autophagy and improves fatty liver diseases.
articles.abstract: Excess lipid accumulation and a sedentary lifestyle are associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but the causal mechanisms and preventive methods are not fully understood. Macroautophagy/autophagy is a lysosomal degradation pathway robustly induced by exercise and plays a key role in lipid metabolism. Understanding the mechanisms by which exercise activates autophagy and elicits metabolic benefits in the liver will provide important insights into the pathogenesis of MAFLD. Here, we discovered negative correlations between expression and lactylation of WDR41 (WD repeat domain 41) and pathogenesis of a series of human hepatic metabolic diseases. We found that WDR41 was a pro-autophagy protein that underwent lactylation in response to autophagy-inducing conditions, such as exercise. WDR41 was lactylated at lysine 319 (K319), a modification facilitated by LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) upon autophagy induction, and delactylated by SIRT2 (sirtuin 2). Lactylated WDR41 promoted autophagy initiation by directly interacting with the autophagy proteins ATG13 (autophagy related 13) and RB1CC1/FIP200 (RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1) and driving the ULK1 (unc-51 like autophagy activating kinase 1) complex assembly. Physiologically, WDR41 and WDR41K319 lactylation, were important for exercise-induced improvements in insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism against excess lipid accumulation in the liver. Thus, we demonstrated that WDR41 lactylation at K319 is an important regulatory mechanism by which exercise regulates autophagy and hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism.

articles.title: Survey of the human proteostasis network: translation, protein folding, and organelle-specific systems.
articles.abstract: The condition of having a healthy, functional proteome is known as protein homeostasis, or proteostasis. Maintaining proteostasis is the province of the proteostasis network, which consists of the cellular components that regulate protein synthesis, folding, localization, and degradation. The proteostasis network is a fundamental functional unit in biology with relevance to many diseases. Despite its importance, the human proteostasis network has until now lacked a precise definition, limiting our ability to interrogate proteostasis, integrate multiomic datasets, compare results across studies, or model proteostasis dysfunction in disease. To address this limitation, we have operationally defined the human proteostasis network by providing a comprehensive, annotated, and manually curated list of its components classified into nine Branches based on their function and localization - cytonuclear proteostasis, ER proteostasis, mitochondrial proteostasis, nuclear proteostasis, proteostasis network regulation, translation, extracellular proteostasis, the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and the ubiquitin-proteasome system - which we present in a series of three manuscripts of which this is the first. Overall, the proteostasis network annotation encompasses 3,151 components described by 4,043 annotations. Here, we present the 1,190 components that make up the first seven of these Branches, which comprise the compartment-based proteostasis network (cytonuclear, ER, mitochondrial, nuclear, and extracellular proteostasis), proteostasis network regulation, and translation. These Branches include chaperones, folding enzymes, systems for trafficking proteins, organelle-specific degradation systems, and the cell's translation machinery. This work provides a framework that will facilitate insights into how proteostasis is preserved in health, lost in aging and disease, and how it could be restored through pharmacological intervention.

articles.title: Management and Outcomes of Bleeding Ectopic Varices in Patients With Liver Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Pooled Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding ectopic varices is a rare but life-threatening complication in patients with clinically significant portal hypertension and liver cirrhosis, with limited evidence available to guide treatment decisions.

AIM: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of current therapies for bleeding ectopic varices.

METHODS: A systematic review with pooled analysis was performed based on searches conducted in Embase, MEDLINE and Cochrane Library databases. Case series, retrospective and prospective studies including adults with a history of liver cirrhosis or portal hypertension presenting with bleeding ectopic varices were included. Individual patient data on interventions, rebleeding, complications and mortality were pooled and summarised using descriptive analysis. No conventional meta-analysis was conducted due to the heterogeneous nature of included studies.

RESULTS: 44 studies (15 non-consecutive case series, 25 single-arm retrospective cohort studies, 3 double-arm retrospective cohort studies and 1 single-arm prospective study) involving 458 patients met selection criteria. Alcohol-related liver disease (38.7%), viral hepatitis (18.8%) and primary sclerosing cholangitis (15.7%) were the most common aetiologies. Child-Pugh A, B and C cirrhosis accounted for 29.7%, 46.7% and 23.5% of patients, respectively, and the pooled median Model for End Stage Liver Disease score was 14.0 (IQR 10.0-20.8). The most reported sites of ectopic varices were duodenal (27.7%), rectal (27.3%) and stomal/peri-stomal (23.1%). Endoscopic sclerosant injection appeared to have a lower rebleeding rate than band ligation in the treatment of bleeding rectal varices (3.3% vs. 33.3%). Across variceal subtypes, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with variceal embolisation, was observed to have a lower rebleeding rate than TIPS alone. The pooled all-cause mortality following small bowel, rectal and stomal variceal bleeding were 25.0%, 42.9%, and 66.6%, respectively, over a median follow-up period of 354 (IQR 120-780) days. Small sample sizes, missing data and significant heterogeneity between studies limited data quality.

CONCLUSION: Bleeding ectopic varices frequently recurs and carries high mortality. An individualised approach in conjunction with early multidisciplinary team discussions is essential in achieving favourable patient outcomes.

articles.title: Cross-Ancestry Polygenic Prediction of Bipolar Disorder and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in India.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part B, Neuropsychiatric genetics : the official publication of the International Society of Psychiatric Genetics
articles.abstract: Most genetic studies of psychiatric disorders have been conducted predominantly in populations of European ancestry, limiting evidence for the transferability of polygenic scores (PGS) to other populations. This cross-sectional study evaluated the predictive performance of European-derived PGS for bipolar disorder (BD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in an Indian sample. Participants (N = 2531) included individuals with BD (N = 463), OCD (N = 554), and controls (N = 1514) recruited from hospital- and community-based samples. Genotyping was performed using the Illumina Global Screening Array. PGS were derived from the summary statistics of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies using two Bayesian methods, PRS-CS-auto and SBayesRC. Principal component analyses demonstrated genetic overlap of the study population with other South Asian populations. BD PGS showed significant predictive performance, explaining approximately 6%-7% of liability-scale variance with PGS-only AUCs of ~0.71. OCD PGS showed lower but significant predictive performance, explaining ~2%-3% of variance with AUCs of approximately 0.59. Bayesian approaches showed better predictive performance than conventional clumping-and-thresholding. These findings demonstrate that European-derived psychiatric PGS can retain predictive information in an Indian population, although performance differed between disorders. The application of Bayesian PGS methods in this Indian cohort supports their utility for cross-ancestry prediction, while reinforcing the need for larger genomic studies in South Asian and other underrepresented populations.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Untargeted metabolomics reveals L-Lysine depletion as a host-directed therapeutic target in Toxoplasma gondii infection" [Acta Tropica (2026) 108279].
Thromboembolic risk associated with desmopressin use in patients with central diabetes insipidus.
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: From pathophysiology to a practical approach to diagnosis and treatment.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome with increasing prevalence, driven by aging and cardiometabolic comorbidities. It is better understood as a disorder of elevated filling pressures, impaired cardiovascular reserve, recurrent congestion, and systemic multiorgan dysfunction than as heart failure with normal systolic function. Diagnosis remains probabilistic and requires integration of symptoms, natriuretic peptides, echocardiographic structural and functional abnormalities, and, when resting findings are inconclusive, exercise or invasive hemodynamic testing. Treatment has evolved from symptom control toward phenotype-oriented care. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are foundational therapy, finerenone expands options for selected patients, and obesity is now a modifiable therapeutic target. This review summarizes current mechanisms, diagnostic pathways, and treatment strategies, with emphasis on practical clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Syphilis: clinical, diagnostic and therapeutic update.
articles.abstract: Syphilis remains a major global public health concern due to the sustained increase in incidence observed over recent decades, particularly among high-risk populations. Its broad clinical spectrum and ability to mimic numerous dermatological and systemic diseases continue to make it a relevant diagnostic challenge in dermatological practice. This review summarizes the main epidemiological, microbiological, clinical, diagnostic, and therapeutic aspects of Treponema pallidum infection, with special emphasis on mucocutaneous manifestations and recent advances in molecular diagnostic techniques. Current therapeutic strategies, clinical and serological follow-up, and special situations such as neurosyphilis, ocular syphilis, pregnancy, and HIV infection are also reviewed. Finally, emerging preventive challenges are discussed, including doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (DoxyPEP), antimicrobial resistance, and future perspectives in vaccine development.

articles.title: Evaluation of the management of patients with suspected epileptic seizures in emergency departments: The EPI-Lepsie study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: In France, epileptic seizures account for approximately 1.6% of emergency department (ED) admissions, nearly 60% of which involve patients with known epilepsy. At least half of these patients could potentially be managed on an outpatient basis. Despite established national guidelines, data on actual ED practice patterns and guideline adherence remain scarce.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the management of adult patients presenting with suspected epileptic seizures across French EDs, and to identify clinical and organisational determinants of hospitalisation.

DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: The EPI-Lepsie study was a national, multicentre, prospective observational study. Consecutive adult patients (age≥18 years) admitted to 93 French EDs over a three-day period (18-21 May 2021) with suspected epileptic seizures were enrolled through the Initiative Recherche Urgence (IRU) network of the Société française de médecine d'urgence (SFMU).

OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS: The primary outcome was hospitalisation at ED discharge. Secondary outcomes included EEG performance, access to neurological consultation, post-discharge follow-up, and 30-day outcomes. Hospitalisation determinants were assessed by mixed logistic regression (ED as random intercept), adjusted for age, sex, seizure aetiology, risk factors, neuroimaging, and EEG results.

MAIN RESULTS: Among 350 included patients (61.8% male; median age 50 years [IQR: 33-68]), EEG was requested in 102 cases (29.1%) but performed in only 54 (15.4%). Neurological consultation was requested in 163 patients (46.6%) and obtained in 146 (41.7%). After ED care, 210 patients (60.2%) were discharged home, of whom 133 (66.5%) had no scheduled neurological follow-up. Hospitalisation occurred in 128 patients (36.6%). In multivariate analysis, abnormal neuroimaging was the strongest independent predictor (adjusted OR 8.70, P<0.0001). Failure to perform a requested EEG was associated with hospitalisation in 81.2% of cases versus 46.3% when EEG was completed. Inter-centre variance accounted for 19.9% of total variance.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that a substantial proportion of epilepsy-related ED admissions do not require hospitalisation. Improving access to EEG and neurological consultation, combined with standardised risk-stratification pathways for patients with known epilepsy, could meaningfully reduce avoidable admissions and enhance continuity of care.

articles.title: Accuracy of complete arch implant intraoral scans: A systematic review of different technique categories compared with the conventional splinted open tray method.
articles.abstract:
STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: The accuracy comparison results between a conventional impression and an intraoral scan for a complete arch implant are mixed and unclear.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this systematic review was to compare the accuracy of different categories of complete arch implant intraoral scan techniques with the conventional abutment-level splinted open tray impression technique.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A comprehensive search of the PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases was conducted to identify eligible studies. Complete arch implant scan techniques were classified into 5 categories: IOS-O, regular intraoral scan only; IOS-SA, intraoral scan with scan aid; IOS-CHS, intraoral scan with horizontal scan bodies oriented toward the center of the arch to reduce scan span; IOS-CISP, intraoral scan with auxiliary structures followed by calibration with a high-accuracy scan of the auxiliary structures to correct stitching errors in the intraoral scan; IOS-IPG, intraoral photogrammetry. The accuracy outcomes were extracted and analyzed using both descriptive statistics and meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on short implant span (span within premolar to premolar) and long implant span (span longer than premolar to premolar).

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies, including 22 in vitro studies and 1 clinical study, were included in the present systematic review. IOS-O was investigated in 22 studies, IOS-SA in 10 studies, 2 studies for IOS-CISP, 1 study for IOS-CHS, and no available study for IOS-IPG. Descriptives analysis showed that IOS-O and IOS-SA presented better accuracy than the conventional approach in short implant spans but worse accuracy in long implant spans. IOS-CISP showed better accuracy than the conventional approach in long implant spans. Meta-analysis also showed that IOS-O and IOS-SA were more accurate than the conventional technique for short spans but that the conventional technique was more accurate for long implant spans.

CONCLUSIONS: In an in vitro setting, IOS-O and IOS-SA demonstrated higher accuracy than the conventional technique in short-span implant scans. In long-span implant scans, conventional techniques were more accurate than IOS-O and IOS-SA. IOS-CISP appeared to be more accurate than conventional techniques in long spans, but the evidence is limited. Studies comparing IOS-CHS and IOS-IPG with conventional approaches are insufficient.

articles.title: The First Notes of Injury: Biomarkers of Aminoglycoside Nephrotoxicity in Young CF Patients (PIANO-CF) Compared to Healthy Controls.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: People with CF (pwCF) have historically been treated often and with prolonged intravenous aminoglycosides courses, which are known to cause nephrotoxicity. Despite this, kidney impairment in pwCF is often under-recognised, in part due to limitations of traditional serum markers such as creatinine. This study aimed to explore the utility of urinary biomarkers in detecting aminoglycoside-induced nephrotoxicity in pwCF, and to compare biomarker profiles with healthy children.

METHODS: In the PIANO-CF study we evaluated renal biomarkers in three groups: (A) children with cystic fibrosis aged 0 to less than 7 years receiving intravenous aminoglycoside, (B) clinically stable children with cystic fibrosis not receiving intravenous aminoglycoside, and (C) age-matched healthy controls (HC). A total of 29 pwCF were prospectively recruited during hospital admissions for intravenous aminoglycoside, and 65 pwCF provided urine samples from a biobank. We also recruited 269 healthy children. To compare biomarkers between groups, we used a generalised estimating equation.

FINDINGS: Children with cystic fibrosis had significantly lower urinary kidney injury molecule-1 (uKIM-1; 126.7 pg/mL lower) and urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (uNGAL; 7.07 ng/mL lower) than healthy controls (HC). For pwCF receiving intravenous aminoglycosides, uKIM-1 and uNGAL increased 1.9-fold and 2.05-fold respectively, despite stable serum creatinine (sCr); however, only three children (10%) met pRIFLE criteria for acute kidney injury (AKI), precluding formal assessment of biomarker sensitivity or specificity for AKI detection. No correlation was found between serum and urinary biomarker levels. No association was found between prior aminoglycoside exposure and uKIM-1 levels.

IMPLICATIONS: These exploratory findings reveal a distinct urinary biomarker signature in children with cystic fibrosis compared to healthy controls, and demonstrate that uKIM-1 and uNGAL increase with intravenous aminoglycoside exposure despite stable sCr. These observations support the need to establish CF-specific biomarker reference ranges and to design adequately powered prospective studies to formally assess the utility of these biomarkers in detecting aminoglycoside-induced nephrotoxicity.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Based Mortality Prediction for Mechanically Ventilated Liver Failure Patients: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop a mortality prediction model for patients with liver failure who require mechanical ventilation (MV) in ICU.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study utilized data from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV (v3.0) databases. Variables included demographics, liver function markers, ventilator parameters, severity scores, comorbidities, use of vasoactive drugs and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) as well as length of ICU and hospital stay. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Five machine learning algorithms were applied: logistic regression, decision tree, Bagging, neural network, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and calibration plots. Predictive factors were ranked for the best-performing model by importance.

RESULTS: A total of 2336 patients were identified from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV databases. On the test set, the AUC values for each model were as follows: logistic regression (0.836), decision tree (0.768), neural network (0.774), Bagging (0.854), and XGBoost (0.875). Calibration curves showed good agreement for all models except the neural network. Among the 5 algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive performance. The top 5 predictors identified were length of hospital stay, SAPS II score, use of vasoactive drugs, total bilirubin and length of ICU stay.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning-based models can effectively predict in-hospital mortality in liver failure patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Among the 5 algorithms tested, the XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance.

articles.title: Telehealth Utilisation Among Black Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the 2022 Health Information National Trends Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Telehealth has expanded access to health care, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic. However, disparities in telehealth use persist among racial and ethnic minorities, including Black adults, who face higher rates of chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension. Barriers such as limited digital health literacy, a preference for in-person care, and systemic inequities may hinder telehealth adoption in this population. Nurses play a vital role in assessing, educating, and advocating for patients navigating digital health platforms. This study assessed the prevalence of telehealth use among Black adults in the United States, identified key barriers and facilitators, and examined predictors of telehealth utilisation. Implications for nursing practice were explored to inform strategies for improving digital access and equity.

METHOD: We analysed data from the 2022 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) using descriptive statistics to explore telehealth prevalence, barriers, and facilitators. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of telehealth use. Weighted analyses ensured nationally representative results.

RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1,044 respondents, representing approximately 32 million Black adults after applying sample weights. Over the past 12 months, 36.5% (standard error [SE], 3.0) of Black adults used telehealth. Among those offered telehealth but opting out, 89.5% (SE, 4.4) preferred in-person care. Key facilitators included convenience (64.6%; SE, 4.6), avoiding hospital-acquired infections (52.0%; SE, 4.0), and provider recommendations (70.0%; SE, 4.0). Adults aged 31-45 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.1; p=0.050) and 46-60 years (aOR 2.1; p=0.047) had higher odds of telehealth use than those aged 18-30 years. Black adults with cardiometabolic conditions were three times more likely to use telehealth than those without such conditions (aOR 3.0; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Telehealth use among Black adults is motivated by convenience and health concerns but hindered by a strong preference for in-person care. These findings underscore the need for culturally tailored, nurse-led interventions that address digital health literacy and patient engagement, particularly among those without existing chronic conditions. Nurses are uniquely positioned to assess readiness for telehealth, provide personalised education, and advocate for equitable access to digital care. Future nursing research should explore innovative telehealth models that centre patient preferences and reduce digital exclusion in underserved populations.

articles.title: International recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study aims to develop international recommendations for the use of imaging in the diagnosis and assessment of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR).

METHODS: An international, multidisciplinary task force of 30 members from 12 countries was convened; the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standard operating procedures were followed. Six clinical key questions addressing the role of imaging (ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) in diagnosis, monitoring, outcome prediction, and technical aspects in PMR were the basis for a systematic literature review. Recommendations were formulated based on evidence and expert opinion and refined iteratively until consensus was achieved. The level of agreement was assessed by voting.

RESULTS: Three overarching principles and 7 recommendations were developed. PMR remains primarily a clinical diagnosis. Imaging is neither required to confirm PMR in patients with a high clinical probability of the disease nor to exclude PMR in case of low clinical probability. Imaging is most useful in patients with intermediate pretest probability (ie, atypical presentations or suspected alternative/overlapping conditions). No single imaging modality demonstrated sufficient accuracy to be recommended as a first-line test; therefore, imaging should be individualised according to clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, access, and local expertise. Vascular imaging should be performed when overlap with giant cell arteritis is suspected, whereas systematic screening for subclinical vasculitis is not supported by current evidence. Utilising imaging for disease monitoring or outcome prediction is currently not recommended.

CONCLUSIONS: These recommendations provide the first evidence-based guidance for the use of imaging in PMR, reinforcing clinical assessment as the cornerstone of diagnosis and positioning imaging as a context-driven adjunct.

Chronic Wounds as Biofilm Ecosystems: Modernizing Microbiology Beyond Planktonic Paradigms.
articles.abstract:
SIGNIFICANCE: Chronic wound infections, including diabetic foot infections, are increasingly recognized as biofilm-associated polymicrobial ecosystems rather than simple planktonic infections. However, routine microbiological workflows remain largely optimized for acute infections, creating a mismatch between laboratory diagnostics and the biological organization of chronic infection.

RECENT ADVANCES: Growing evidence from biofilm biology, microbial ecology, and molecular microbiology has demonstrated that chronic wound infections are characterized by structured microbial communities, physiological heterogeneity, and enhanced antimicrobial tolerance. Advanced diagnostic approaches have improved understanding of microbial diversity and biofilm-associated persistence beyond what is captured by conventional culture alone.

CRITICAL ISSUES: Conventional microbiological workflows may incompletely resolve the microbial populations most relevant to chronicity, recurrence, and treatment failure. Key limitations include sampling strategy, tissue processing, incubation conditions, anaerobic recovery, and reliance on planktonic susceptibility testing. The discrepancy between minimum inhibitory concentration-based testing and biofilm-associated antimicrobial tolerance highlights an important gap between laboratory assessment and infection biology.

FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Modernization of chronic wound microbiology requires a transition from pathogen-centered planktonic models toward biofilm-aware, ecosystem-oriented approaches. Integration of optimized sampling, culture-based diagnostics, selective molecular tools, surgical source control, and antimicrobial stewardship may improve diagnostic resolution, support more rational antimicrobial use, and enhance long-term clinical outcomes.[Figure: see text].

articles.title: Lipidic obstruction of sinusoids (LOS): a potentially serious complication of steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: During routine examination of specimens from patients with steatotic liver disease (SLD), we repeatedly observed a peculiar phenomenon characterized by obstruction of the hepatic sinusoids by lipid vacuoles (lipidic obstruction of sinusoids, LOS). These changes were reminiscent of pseudopeliotic steatosis (PPS), a complication following liver transplantation (LT), but notably occurred outside this context. The aim of our study was to identify diagnostic indicators for LOS and to determine its clinical significance.

METHODS: Liver specimens routinely sent to our institute between 2019 and 2024 with SLD were examined for LOS. The extracellular nature of the fat and the compression of the sinusoids were demonstrated by ancillary stains (Gomori, CD68, collagen IV). The extent of the LOS was quantified by measuring the area and maximum diameter of fat lakes. The clinical course of patients with LOS was retrospectively evaluated and correlated with the histological findings.

RESULTS: LOS was observed in eight patients, ranging from focal to very extensive extracellular fat. The diagnosis was based on routine histology, supplemented by collagen IV stain highlighting double contours of sinusoids. The morphological findings suggested that lipidic obstruction of the hepatic sinusoids was a key pathophysiological factor. LOS was associated with liver necrosis and activation of macrophages. Patients with LOS exhibited a variable clinical course, ranging from subclinical to severe, including LT or even death. The extent of fat lakes correlated with the severity of the clinical course.

CONCLUSIONS: We suggest the term LOS for a particular pattern of liver damage that can occur in SLD outside the transplantation setting and may lead to impaired hepatic blood flow. LOS is associated with a variable clinical presentation, ranging from subclinical to fatal. Clinicians and pathologists should be aware of this complication of SLD, which is diagnosed by liver histology.

Clinical Experience of Iptacopan in Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
articles.abstract: Iptacopan, an oral Factor B inhibitor, is approved for the treatment of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH). In clinical trials it was safe and effective but real-world data, particularly in patients with associated bone marrow failure, remain limited. A retrospective, multicenter study was conducted in patients with PNH who received iptacopan monotherapy in the UK and France between July 2021 and July 2025. Patient demographics, prior treatment and indication for switch were collected, as were hematological parameters at baseline, 3, 12 and 24 months. Outcomes included breakthrough hemolysis, infections, thrombotic events, treatment discontinuation and death. A total of 151 patients were included with a median treatment duration of 238 days. Iptacopan produced significant increases in mean hemoglobin, from 104 g/L at baseline to 127 g/L at 3 months, with improvements sustained to 24 months. A total of 76% achieved a hemoglobin ≥ 120 g/L by 12 months, compared with 21.9% at baseline, with transfusion independency in 88%. There was no statistical difference in responses between patients with and without history of bone marrow failure. Breakthrough hemolysis occurred in 6.6% of patients, with a mean hemoglobin fall of 24 g/L. Suspected bacterial infections occurred at a rate of 0.18 per patient-year, but there were no meningococcal or pneumococcal infections. There were no thromboses, and no deaths related to iptacopan. This cohort demonstrates that iptacopan produces sustained improvements in patients with PNH, irrespective of prior complement inhibition or history of bone marrow failure. Longer follow-up is needed to characterize long-term efficacy and infection risk.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Missed Nursing Care and Trust in Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study of Patient, Nurse, and Ward Level Factors.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the relationship between patient-reported missed nursing care and trust in nurses and to identify patient-, nurse-, and ward-level factors associated with trust in nurses.

DESIGN: A descriptive cross-sectional study.

METHODS: The study was conducted with 356 hospitalised patients from medical and surgical inpatient wards. Data were collected using the Patient Information Form, Nurse and Ward Information Form, MISSCARE Survey-Patient and Trust in Nurses Scale. Descriptive and inferential statistics were performed using SPSS 27. Reporting was guided by the STROBE checklist.

RESULTS: The communication dimension of missed nursing care was significantly associated with trust in nurses. Hierarchical regression analyses showed that communication-related missed care remained independently associated with trust after controlling for patient-, nurse-, and ward-level factors. In contrast, nurse- and ward-level characteristics, including patient-to-nurse ratio, bed turnover rate, nurse age, professional experience, and overtime, were not significantly associated with trust. Among patient characteristics, only employment status was identified as a significant predictor of trust. No significant differences in trust or missed nursing care scores were observed across wards.

CONCLUSION: Communication-related missed nursing care was independently associated with trust in nurses. The findings suggest that patients may place greater importance on communication experiences than on structural characteristics when evaluating nursing care and developing trust in nurses.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Interventions aimed at strengthening nurse-patient communication, patient information sharing, and therapeutic interactions may contribute to improving patients' trust in nurses. Communication-related missed care should be considered an important quality indicator in inpatient settings.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients contributed to this study by completing the survey instruments.

IMPACT: Evidence regarding the relationship between patient-reported missed nursing care and trust in nurses remains limited. Communication-related missed nursing care was independently associated with lower trust in nurses, whereas nurse- and ward-level characteristics were not significantly associated with trust. The findings may support nurses, nurse managers, and healthcare organisations in prioritising communication-focused quality improvement initiatives to strengthen patient trust in inpatient care settings.

articles.title: Prevalence of occult hepatitis B infection among blood donors from 2015 to 2025: A meta-analysis based on testing modalities and temporal trends.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) remains an important concern for global blood safety. Published studies have reported inconsistent OBI prevalence among blood donors, and the influencing factors remain unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled OBI prevalence and explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrieved eligible studies published from 2015 to 2026. Pooled prevalence was calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were conducted by testing method, study period, sample size, region, and national hepatitis B virus (HBV) screening conditions. Publication bias and result robustness were assessed via multiple statistical approaches.

RESULTS: Significant between-study heterogeneity was identified. All subgroup analyses produced statistically significant interaction results (p for interaction ≤ 0.015). The prevalence of OBI varied remarkably across subgroups stratified by HBV-DNA testing method, research period, sample size, geographic region, national HBV endemicity, and blood screening level. The pooled OBI prevalence was higher in the 2023-2024 subgroup, although this likely reflects geographic confounding rather than a genuine temporal increase. No substantial publication bias was detected, and the overall pooled estimate was stable. High residual heterogeneity still persisted in all stratified subgroups.

CONCLUSION: OBI is prevalent among global blood donors and affected by detection techniques, study period, sample size, region, and local screening capacity. Standardized molecular testing and long-term surveillance are recommended to reduce transfusion-transmitted HBV risks and ensure blood safety.

Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints.

DESIGN: Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial.

SETTING: 26 UK hospitals.

PARTICIPANTS: 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat.

RESULTS: 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group.

CONCLUSION: This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN Registry ISRCTN10236011.

articles.title: Atovaquone prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in immunosuppressed patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases: Incidence and clinical characteristics of a breakthrough case-A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data on Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) incidence and the clinical characteristics of breakthrough infection in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases under glucocorticoid-containing immunosuppressive therapy receiving atovaquone oral suspension remain scarce.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated PCP incidence and investigated the clinical characteristics of a breakthrough case in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases on glucocorticoids receiving 1,500 mg/day atovaquone oral suspension for prophylaxis (March 2013-March 2025).

RESULTS: Of 699 patients prescribed atovaquone oral suspension for prophylaxis, 128 were eligible. One patient developed PCP over a median observation period of 147 days, yielding an incidence rate of 0.69 per 100 person-years (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.02-3.83). This breakthrough case was a 73-year-old male treated with prednisolone, upadacitinib, and intravenous cyclophosphamide. Enteral nutrition (500 kcal, 20-g fat) was provided before atovaquone oral suspension; 65 days after atovaquone initiation, it was switched to a formulation providing 300 kcal and 6.7-g fat. Twenty-seven days later, PCP was diagnosed based on dyspnea, bilateral ground-glass opacities, elevated serum β-D-glucan, and polymerase chain reaction detection of P. jirovecii in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.

CONCLUSION: Atovaquone oral suspension 1,500 mg/day was associated with a PCP incidence rate of 0.69 per 100 person-years in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases receiving glucocorticoid therapy. Review of the clinical characteristics of the breakthrough case raised the hypothesis that decreased dietary fat intake may have contributed to breakthrough PCP, suggesting that fat content at administration may warrant attention. Prospective studies incorporating atovaquone plasma concentration monitoring are needed to test this hypothesis.

articles.title: DPP3 as a Biomarker in Patients with Cardiovascular Critical Illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (DPP3) exerts vasodilatory and myocardial depressant effects in preclinical models and is a potential therapeutic target in cardiogenic shock (CS).

METHODS: Patients admitted to the CICU at Brigham and Women's Hospital were enrolled in a biorepository with samples collected at CICU admission. Using samples from 2017-2023, DPP3 was measured using an immunoluminometric assay (4TEEN4). Shock, defined by hypotension and end-organ hypoperfusion, was adjudicated as CS (classic or vasodilatory) or distributive (DS). Controls were CICU patients without shock. Models were adjusted for age, sex, eGFR, and SOFA score.

RESULTS: Of 1082 CICU patients, 381 (35.2%) had CS, 70 (6.5%) had DS, and 618 (57.2%) were non-shock controls. DPP3 values were higher in CS (median, 42.7 [Q1-Q3, 25.6-84.3] ng/mL) than in non-shock controls (31.8 [20.2-57.2] ng/mL; p<0.001) but, nevertheless, were elevated (>30 ng/mL) in 53.6% of non-shock controls. CICU patients with DPP3 >30 ng/mL had higher in-hospital mortality (19.9% vs. 8.4%; OR 2.7 [95% CI 1.8-4.0]; p<0.001), with a consistent pattern across CS, DS, and non-shock patients (p-interaction=0.72) and across CS etiologic subgroups (p-interaction=0.18). In adjusted analyses including both shock and non-shock patients, DPP3 showed a graded association with mortality across quartiles (adj-OR Q4 vs. Q1: 3.0 [1.6-6.1]; p<0.001), and at a 30 ng/mL threshold (adj-OR: 2.1 [1.4-3.4]; p=0.001).

CONCLUSION: Among critically ill CICU patients, DPP3 was elevated in shock and non-shock states and was associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings support a potential role for DPP3 as a biomarker for risk stratification and a possible target for therapy.

articles.title: HFSA Scientific Statement on Right Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Right heart failure (RHF), both acute and chronic is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically significant syndrome across the spectrum of cardiovascular disease. Estimates suggest RHF complicates >25-30% of hospitalizations for acute decompensated HF and is nearly universal in advanced pulmonary hypertension (PH) (1) Despite recent diagnostic and therapeutic advancements, RHF remains associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and impaired quality of life. Addressing RHF requires dedicated strategies tailored to its pathophysiology, including early identification, risk stratification, and novel therapies. (2) While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the topic remain limited, there has been increasing emphasis on early recognition and management of RHF (especially in the setting of left ventricular [LV] failure). In addition, there is an expanding role for temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in acute RHF and percutaneous tricuspid interventions in chronic RHF. Yet, the field remains limited by its under-recognition, lack of standardized definitions, and limited therapeutic options, which underscore the urgent need for consensus and guidance.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Biomimetic Hydrogel with Antibacterial and Antifibrotic Properties for Scar Minimizing Repair of Infected Skin Wounds.
articles.abstract: Infected wounds are characterized by persistent bacterial colonization, which exacerbates inflammation, interferes with extracellular matrix remodeling, and ultimately leads to hypertrophic scarring. Conventional wound dressings offer limited antibacterial durability, immune regulation, and regenerative support, thereby restricting their ability to prevent fibrosis. In this study, we engineered a biomimetic dual-crosslinked network hydrogel (GH-L-VP@PDA) constructed from phenylboronic-acid-modified gelatin methacrylate (GelMA-PBA) and thiolated hyaluronic acid (HA-SH), incorporating the antimicrobial peptide LL-37 and verteporfin-loaded polydopamine nanoparticles (VP@PDA). By integrating LL-37 and VP@PDA nanoparticles, the hydrogel enables coordinated therapy, providing early antibacterial protection and sustained regulation of Yes-associated protein (YAP)-mediated fibrotic remodeling. Consequently, the hydrogel simultaneously regulates infection, inflammation, and fibrotic remodeling, promoting regenerative healing while attenuating excessive fibrosis. Furthermore, benchmarking against commercially available wound dressings demonstrated the favorable therapeutic performance of GH-L-VP@PDA in infected wound treatment. This work presents an intelligent-network therapeutic platform that targets infection-associated fibrosis through YAP-mediated remodeling, providing a strategy for infected wound repair with attenuated fibrotic remodeling. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Infected wound healing remains challenging due to the interplay among bacterial infection, persistent inflammation, and excessive fibrosis. Here, we developed a biomimetic dual-crosslinked hydrogel composed of phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin methacrylate, thiolated hyaluronic acid, LL-37, and verteporfin-loaded polydopamine nanoparticles. The hydrogel integrates antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and antifibrotic properties, with the latter associated with YAP regulation. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated its potential to control infection, modulate inflammation, promote angiogenesis, and improve collagen remodeling and tissue regeneration. Comparisons with commercial wound dressings further supported its therapeutic potential. This study provides a multifunctional hydrogel strategy for coordinated regulation of infected wound healing.

articles.title: Stroke Risk Prediction in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: Simplicity, Complexity, and the Modern Paradigm Shift.
Combined bipolar and unipolar voltage mapping to identify epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The utility of unipolar voltage (UV) mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains undetermined.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed combined bipolar voltage (BV) and UV mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation (PFA).

METHODS: Thirty patients with atrial fibrillation underwent initial PFA-PVI with a pentaspline catheter under fluoroscopic guidance. Within the isolated PV antrum (BV <0.1 mV), transmurally ablated regions and epicardial breakthrough regions were defined by UV <1.08 mV and UV ≥1.08 mV, respectively. Unipolar electrogram features were investigated to identify epicardial breakthrough regions.

RESULTS: Seventeen patients had 27 epicardial breakthrough regions, yielding 276 local unipolar electrograms (QR pattern: n=160; RS pattern: n=116). QR electrograms were distributed broadly within the isolated PV, whereas RS electrograms occurred exclusively around the isolation boundary. QR electrograms, indicating possible epicardial breakthrough, had significantly higher UV amplitudes than RS electrograms (median: 1.64 vs. 0.70 mV; P<0.001). The UV amplitude cutoff distinguishing these morphologies was 1.15 mV (sensitivity, 91.9%; specificity, 84.5%; area under the curve [AUC], 0.922; P<0.001). Among 245 local unipolar electrograms around the isolation boundary, excluding QR electrograms, RS electrograms had higher UV amplitudes and steeper negative intrinsic deflection slopes than non-RS electrograms, suggesting possible intramural conduction gaps. Respective cutoffs were 0.48 mV (sensitivity, 83.6%; specificity, 86.8%; AUC, 0.923; P<0.001) and 0.020 mV/ms (sensitivity, 97.4%; specificity, 94.5%; AUC, 0.992; P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Combined BV and UV mapping provides additional information for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions at PFA application sites.

articles.title: Left bundle branch pacing vs left ventricular septal pacing in the same patients with heart failure and left bundle branch block.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) are considered to be acceptable as left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) strategies. The differences in cardiac mechanical performance between LBBP and LVSP in the same patients with heart failure (HF) and left bundle branch block (LBBB) are yet to be determined.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to compare mechanical function and resynchronization effect of LBBP and LVSP as CRTP modalities.

METHODS: Fourteen patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and typical complete LBBB who received cardiac resynchronization therapy pacing (CRTP) implantation were enrolled. All patient implantation with two ventricular pacing leads, enabling both LBBP and LVSP. Acute cardiac function and resynchronization effect were assessed by echocardiography and electrocardiography to compare the differences in LBBB mode, LBBP mode, and LVSP mode within the same patients undergoing CRTP.

RESULTS: Both pacing modes significantly reduced QRS duration (QRSd) and left ventricular activation time (LVAT) versus LBBB (all P<0.001), with LVSP yielding wider QRSd than LBBP (P<0.001). LBBP showed better performance in LV mechanical synchrony parameter (SDI) than LVSP, and both pacing modes were superior to that of LBBB condition (all P < 0.001). LVEF increased significantly with both pacing modes, with a greater increase observed in LBBP compared to LVSP. No significant differences in right ventricular function were observed among the three modes.

CONCLUSION: In this pilot study of patients with HF and LBBB, both LBBP and LVSP significantly improved left ventricular hemodynamics and mechanical synchrony without compromising RV function. LBBP potentially has superior left ventricular hemodynamic effects to LVSP.

articles.title: Acute effects of cardioneuroablation on ventricular arrhythmia inducibility and refractoriness in patients with functional bradyarrhythmias. The Roman 4 study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardioneuroablation (CNA) is a promising method to treat functional bradyarrhythmias. However, whether CNA-induced decrease in the parasympathetic drive to the heart may occur proarrhythmic in the future is not known.

OBJECTIVE: To assess acute effects of CNA-induced total vagal denervation on QT interval as well as invasively measured ventricular effective refractory period (VERP), ventricular action potential duration (VAPD) and vulnerability to ventricular arrhythmias.

METHODS: CNA was performed using anatomical approach by means of electro-anatomical mapping and intracardiac echocardiography. Intra-procedural efficacy was assessed using extracardiac vagal stimulation. QTc and QTd intervals were measured from surface ECG. VAPD and VERP were measured from ablation electrode in right ventricle. Measurements were performed at four time-points: at baseline, immediately after CNA, after atropine injection, and finally after isoproterenol bolus.

RESULTS: 80 patients (51 females, mean age 42 ± 14 years) underwent CNA. Polymorphic ventricular tachyarrhythmias were induced in 2 females who had pre-existing cardiac conditions. Changes in QTc depended on the method used for correction. Using the Bazett formula, QTc was significantly prolonged, however using the Framingham, Fridericia and Hodges corrections, these changes were much less pronounced or non-significant. QTd remained unchanged across all measurements. The VERP and VAPD values remained unchanged after CNA and after atropine whereas they became significantly shorter following isoproterenol injection.

CONCLUSION: The present study did not demonstrate evidence of acute electrophysiological changes suggesting increased ventricular arrhythmogenicity after CNA in patients without structural heart disease. However, long-term follow-up is needed to confirm lack of proarrhythmic effects of CNA.

articles.title: Methods for evaluating living guidelines: Early guidance based on practical experience.
authors: ALEC Methods and Processes Working Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To provide guidance for designing and conducting process and impact evaluations for living guidelines; drawing on the practical experiences of the Australian Living Evidence Collaboration (ALEC) and its member groups.

METHODS: In this paper, we describe and reflect upon the methods for evaluating living guidelines, providing practical advice drawing on our experiences conducting diverse evaluations of three living guidelines developed by the ALEC and its member groups - the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management, the Australian Guidelines for the Clinical Care of people with COVID-19, and the Australian Pregnancy and Postnatal Care guidelines. We describe and outline preliminary methods for 1) process evaluations to assess and refine living guideline processes and outputs as guideline development is underway; and 2) impact evaluations to explore if and how living guidelines are being used, their value and the impacts they are having. Our guidance includes economic evaluations to assess the economic costs and benefits of developing and maintaining living guidelines.

CONCLUSION: Process and impact evaluations have been pivotal in underpinning improvements in the ALEC living guideline methods and processes, including the format, content and dissemination of the living guidelines, and our engagement with key stakeholders. Conducting thorough evaluations throughout the cycle of living guideline development and maintenance provides crucial information about the facilitators and enablers, strengths and weaknesses in the process of living guideline production and implementation. The methods described here can be tailored by guideline development programs and applied to evaluate living guidelines across diverse topics and settings.

articles.title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI).

RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Outcomes of single-branched TEVAR with cervical debranching for zone 0 and zone 1 aortic arch repair: A VQI analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. Mean age was 73.8±8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7±12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. Median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion Type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair.

CONCLUSIONS: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

articles.title: SphK1/S1P signaling network: From molecular mechanism to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) is a key rate-limiting enzyme in the sphingolipid metabolic network. It generates sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) by catalyzing the phosphorylation of Sphingosine (Sph). It plays a key regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes such as cell proliferation, survival, migration, inflammatory response and immune regulation. SphK1 closely connects intracellular lipid metabolism with extracellular GPCR signaling network, forming a complex "inside-out" signal transduction system. In this review, we focus on the current understanding of SphK1, including its structure characteristics, activation mechanism and signal transduction pathway. We also review the roles of SphK1 pathway in tumor, inflammation and immunity, cardiovascular, nervous system, digestive system, respiratory system and metabolic disease. Establishing a correlation between SphK1 or the SphK1/S1P signal axis and targeted drugs such as inhibitors, agonists, even some natural Chinese medicines, provides important theoretical support for understanding the potential of SphK1 as a therapeutic target. Finally, we propose future research directions based on current advances and shortcomings.

articles.title: Early Detection of Cerebral Palsy in Ireland: A National NICU Implementation Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To implement standardized early cerebral palsy (CP) detection pathways nationally across all tertiary neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) follow-up programs in Ireland, with the aim to reduce the median age of CP diagnosis to ≤12 months corrected age.

STUDY DESIGN: Active implementation framework methodology was used to adapt the US CP Early Detection and Intervention Network toolkit for the Irish context (May 2023-Dcember 2025). Pathways, criteria, and assessment schedules were standardized. Baseline data from a retrospective cohort of high-risk infants cared for at each site over a 1-year period 30 months prior to implementation were collected. The primary outcome was age at CP diagnosis. Process measures included the proportion having pre-specified standardized assessments. Balancing measures were selected to monitor for potential unintended consequences of the adjusted assessment schedule and an earlier diagnosis and included clinic attendance at 3-4- month corrected age and parent feedback. Baseline (pre-implementation) and prospective (post-implementation) cohorts were compared using control and run charts and standard statistical tests.

RESULTS: 1161 high-risk infants were included (374 baseline, 787 post-implementation). Median age at CP diagnosis decreased from 24 (IQR:16-30) to 7 months (IQR:5-11) corrected age (P<0.001). Process measures improved, with assessments performed in the neonatal and 3-4-month periods at 88-90.6% by study end (all P<0.001 vs. baseline). Parental feedback was generally positive, with opportunities identified for improving information delivery.

CONCLUSIONS: National implementation of early CP surveillance was feasible across tertiary NICU programs in Ireland and reduced median age of diagnosis to 7 months. Future work must establish feasibility beyond tertiary settings and work to incorporate pathways into national priorities to ensure sustainability.

articles.title: A putative oxidoreductase, Rv1714 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, predicted as a short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase, exhibits a pro-inflammatory response.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Proteins and proteomics
articles.abstract: Oxidoreductases are a class of enzymes that transfer electrons in various biological pathways and reactions, at the expense of cellular NADPH/NADH. Because oxidoreductases are involved in numerous energy metabolism pathways, many of these enzymes have been identified as potential drug targets. Although oxidoreductases have been implicated in energy metabolism pathways and are crucial for the survival and pathogenicity of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), their comprehensive characterization remains limited. In the present study, one uncharacterized and putative oxidoreductase, Rv1714, was identified in the H37Rv proteome. This putative oxidoreductase was conserved across pathogenic and opportunistic mycobacterial species and was predicted to be a virulence factor essential for the pathogenicity. Rv1714 displayed homology with the short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase (SDR) family. The recombinant Rv1714 was purified to homogeneity, and its structural properties were explored using CD and fluorescence spectroscopies, as well as bioinformatics tools. The sequence and structural homologies revealed the characteristic features and conservation of the active site with the SDR family of proteins. Possible substrates were explored using docking, simulation, and MMPBSA calculations. Furthermore, in vitro studies using macrophage cell lines demonstrate that recombinant Rv1714 significantly enhances the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, suggesting that Rv1714 may play a critical role in modulating the host's innate immune response during infection. The stimulation of these cytokines is associated with the activation of the NF-κB pathway. Altogether, this is the first report on the putative oxidoreductase Rv1714 of M.tb, highlighting its structural features and its key immune-modulatory function involved in shaping host inflammatory responses during infection.

articles.title: Glycyrrhizic acid-Cu2+ reinforced chondroitin sulfate/carboxymethyl chitosan injectable dual-network hydrogel with multi-bioactivity and enhanced mechanical strength for burn wound healing.
articles.abstract: The effective recovery of burn wounds is a major clinical challenge. Since available wound dressings are limited, rapid wound healing is still difficult to achieve. Injectable hydrogels present remarkable advantages over traditional hydrogels in dealing with irregular wounds, which have attracted extensive research. However, injectable hydrogels face the challenges of insufficient mechanical strength and poor adhesion. To address the issues, a dual-network hydrogel (DOCGC) with levodopa-modified oxidized chondroitin sulfate (L-Dopa-OCS) and carboxymethyl chitosan (CMC) as the matrix, combined with glycyrrhizic acid (GA) and Cu2+ for self-assembly, was designed. This strategy not only optimized the mechanical properties of the hydrogel, but also achieves synergistic effect of anti-inflammation, angiogenesis and anti-infection for burn wounds. The in vitro experiments confirmed that the introduction of levodopa enhanced the tissue adhesion ability of hydrogel. Meanwhile, with the support of GA and Cu2+, the DOCGC hydrogel exhibited enhanced mechanical strength. Crucially, the DOCGC hydrogel showed favorable biocompatibility and antibacterial activity. In the mouse deep second-degree burn model, the application of DOCGC hydrogel achieved a more rapid progression of wound healing. Overall, our results suggested that DOCGC hydrogel with multi-bioactive and excellent gel properties presented a promising solution for treating burn wounds.

articles.title: Lipid Profile and Liver Enzyme Alterations in HIV-Positive Patients Receiving Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy in South-Eastern Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Analysis and Implications for Pharmacogenetic Research.
articles.abstract:
