INTRODUCTION: Cavitation-associated adverse events in MR-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) thalamotomy are uncommon but potentially serious. We report a case of acute "electric-shock" sensation during an alignment/verification sonication followed by thalamic T2 hyperintensity/edema after a redo ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) thalamotomy. We discuss plausible biophysical mechanisms and risk-reduction strategies.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old woman with essential tremor underwent repeat MRgFUS five months after her initial treatment. During the 4th alignment/verification sonication (planned 200 W, 20 s; measured power approximately 192 W), cavitation monitoring triggered a halt at 19.2 seconds after 2037 J was delivered. Despite a maximum target temperature <50 °C, the patient immediately reported an "electric-shock" sensation. Post-procedure, she developed right-sided sensory symptoms, mild dysarthria, and hypogeusia. Early MRI showed irregular thalamic hyperintensity consistent with edema, but without confirmed off-target thermal rise on intra-operative thermometry.

CONCLUSION: The most plausible pathogenesis is mechanically mediated injury from cavitation-related acoustic activity. We hypothesize that substantial overlap with the prior ablation zone was the primary predisposing factor, potentially augmented by calcification-related scattering, No-Pass Region (NPR)-driven aperture distortion, occult skull marrow changes, and standing-wave formation. We discuss biophysical mechanisms and propose physics-guided safeguards for redo procedures.

articles.title: Role of Substance P in physiological and pathological states of the pancreas.
articles.abstract: Background Substance P (SP), a neuropeptide acting mainly through its high-affinity neurokinin-1 receptor (NK-1R), is a key signaling molecule in the pancreas. It is integral to the neuro-pancreatic axis, but its role shifts dramatically between physiological and pathological states. Summary Acting through NK-1R, SP plays various roles in the pancreatic physiological state and disease state. Under physiological conditions, SP contributes to the regulation of exocrine and endocrine functions. In pathological settings, SP signaling exerts effects on modulation of immunity, β-cell preservation and insulin sensitivity in diabetes, triggers neurogenic inflammation and chronic pain in pancreatitis, and enhances malignant behaviours and perineural invasion in pancreatic cancer. Key Messages Functioning as an important regulator, SP maintains physiological balance in health yet drives disease progression in diabetes, pancreatitis, and pancreatic cancer. The SP/NK-1R axis has therapeutic potential with its beneficial actions.

articles.title: Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Stroke: A Narrative Review of Pathophysiological Links, Clinical Evidence, and Diagnostic Implications.
articles.abstract: Background Sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) has long been hypothesized as a potential early warning sign of posterior circulation stroke, yet the causal association and clinical implications remain highly controversial. Summary This narrative review synthesizes current peer-reviewed evidence on the pathophysiological links, epidemiological associations, diagnostic strategies, and integrated management of SSNHL and stroke. Current findings demonstrate that anatomical and pathophysiological overlaps support the biological plausibility of this association, which is predominantly mediated by the vertebrobasilar circulatory system. Shared vascular and prothrombotic factors, including dyslipidemia, hyperhomocysteinemia, and MTHFR gene polymorphisms, may further contribute to the observed association. Clinically, SSNHL may present as an initial manifestation of posterior circulation infarction in a small subset of patients, particularly those with accompanying neurological symptoms or multiple vascular risk factors; however, existing epidemiological data are inconsistent, and there is insufficient evidence to define SSNHL as an independent predictor of stroke in the general population. Key Messages This review concludes that risk stratification and interdisciplinary collaboration between otolaryngologists and neurologists are critical in clinical practice: for high-risk SSNHL patients, timely neurovascular evaluation is warranted to enable early detection of cerebrovascular disease, and future large-scale prospective cohort studies and combined audiological-neurological assessment models are needed to clarify the causal relationship and optimize clinical pathways.

articles.title: A Diagnostic-Focused Mobile Stroke Unit Model Integrated with Emergency Medical Services for Scalable Prehospital Stroke Care.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mobile stroke units (MSUs) have demonstrated important clinical benefits in acute ischemic stroke, but broad implementation remains constrained by resource, staffing, and operational barriers. This article describes an emergency medical services (EMS)-integrated diagnostic-focused MSU (DF-MSU) model designed to improve implementation feasibility and scalability.

METHODS: A conceptual design approach was used based on findings from a previous global survey of MSU programs. The model was guided by three design principles: cost reduction, operational simplification, and integration with existing EMS while preserving the CT-based diagnostic function of MSUs.

CONCLUSION: The DF-MSU model separates CT-based diagnosis from treatment and transport, which are integrated with existing EMS systems. After CT evaluation in the DF-MSU at the emergency scene or rendezvous point, the patient is transferred to an EMS vehicle, where the physician and, when available, the nurse provide diagnosis-specific treatment and continued care during transport. This EMS-integrated model may reduce resource requirements, staffing needs, and operational complexity, and may offer a feasible and scalable alternative in regions where conventional MSU deployment is challenging.

articles.title: Try this at home: A systematic review of patient satisfaction with stroke telerehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke rehabilitation improves patient outcomes, but requires timely delivery, sufficient intensity, and adequate participation in appropriate therapies for maximal effectiveness. Unfortunately, many patients experience barriers to accessing conventional in-person rehabilitation. Telerehabilitation may increase access to care and is increasingly used in clinical settings, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. However, little is known about patient satisfaction with telerehabilitation. The objective of this systematic review was to examine patient satisfaction with post-stroke motor telerehabilitation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, and PsycINFO databases were searched from database inception to July 2025 inclusive. Two independent reviewers screened articles using the following inclusion criteria: English-language, full-text articles, reporting patient satisfaction outcomes with telerehabilitation for persons with stroke receiving upper or lower limb motor rehabilitation. Studies reporting only caregiver, but not patient satisfaction, were excluded. Study quality was assessed using the PEDro rating scale where appropriate.

RESULTS: After removing duplicates, 225 unique articles were reviewed. Nineteen studies published between 2007-2025 met inclusion criteria, assessing 811 individuals (n= 4-188, median 24) across 13 countries. Most studies were conducted in the outpatient setting; three were in both outpatient and inpatient settings. Fourteen studies (74%) examined telerehabilitation in the chronic phase post-stroke, two in the acute phase, two in the subacute phase, and one in both acute and subacute. Ten studies used telerehabilitation for upper limb motor impairment, two for lower limb, and seven for both. Eight controlled trials (seven randomized control trials and one non-randomized control trial) were assessed for quality with PEDro scores ranging from 4-8 (median 6). Assessment tools for patient satisfaction varied significantly between studies. Eight unique validated satisfaction tools were used across studies. All studies reported high patient satisfaction ratings with virtual motor telerehabilitation.

CONCLUSION: Although this review found that patient satisfaction ratings were high among studies of telerehabilitation for post-stroke motor impairment, there are few high-quality motor telerehabilitation studies, and none focused on satisfaction as their main outcome. Given the importance of telerehabilitation for removing barriers to care, future research should use standardized tools to explore patients' and providers' satisfaction in addition to evaluating efficacy.

articles.title: Polarity-Selective Engineering of In-Gap States in Amorphous Silicon Nitride via Distinct Structural and Electronic Origins.
articles.abstract: Precise control of trap states in amorphous dielectrics requires identifying the fundamentally different physical origins of hole and electron trapping. Here, in amorphous silicon nitride (a‑SiNx), we demonstrate a dual-origin mechanism where the two trap polarities arise from decoupled structural and electronic mechanisms, enabling polarity-selective engineering of charge storage behavior. Multi-spectroscopic characterization reveals that hole traps are dictated by structural disorder, where Si-rich nanoclusters form a percolating network whose cluster-size statistics exhibit power-law scaling characteristic of disordered connectivity. In contrast, electron traps are governed by electronic-level alignment, where Hf incorporation lowers the Fermi level, activates deep in-gap states, and introduces additional shallow levels near the conduction-band edge-without perturbing the optimized nanocluster states. By linking structural topology and electronic alignment to polarity-resolved trapping, this work establishes a unified physical picture of trap polarity in disordered dielectrics and provides a practical design route for next-generation charge-trap memories and amorphous nitride/oxide electronic systems.

articles.title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

articles.title: Weekly Journal Scan: PREMIUM evidence that aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention is unjustified and unsafe.
Micro- and nanoplastics in acute coronary thrombosis: exposure, enrichment, or a dual mechanism?
Perspectives on Self-Management and Digital Tools for Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes in Flanders: Qualitative Focus Group Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) is one of the leading chronic diseases worldwide, requiring effective long-term self-management (SM) to improve health outcomes and reduce complications. Although structured diabetes pathways exist in Belgium, national reports indicate that adherence to the recommended diabetes follow-up and routine monitoring remains suboptimal. Digital health technologies have shown promise in supporting SM; however, little is known about how stakeholders within the Flemish health care system perceive opportunities to improve SM and implement digital health interventions.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore stakeholders' perspectives on improving diabetes SM and the potential role of digital tools in supporting people with T2DM in the Flemish health care system.

METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using 2 online semistructured focus group discussions with 19 stakeholders, including health care professionals (HCPs) from primary, secondary, and tertiary care settings; researchers; digital health experts; and an individual living with T2DM. Participants were recruited using maximum variation purposive sampling followed by snowball sampling. The discussion guide was informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and current evidence on diabetes SM and digital health. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated from Dutch into English, analyzed using Braun and Clarke's 6-phase reflexive thematic analysis, and supported by NVivo (QSR International).

RESULTS: Five key themes were identified: (1) Empowerment through education, (2) Tailoring education to individual needs, (3) Multidisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, (4) Opportunities for digital technology in self-management, and (5) Regional and national systemic limitations. Participants consistently emphasized that effective diabetes SM may extend beyond patients' individual behaviors and depends on tailored education, coordinated multidisciplinary care across the health care sectors, supportive organizational structures, and supportive health policies. Digital health technologies were perceived as valuable tools to facilitate patient education, communication, information sharing, and continuity of care. However, participants also highlighted that successful implementation depends on addressing broader organizational and system-level barriers, including fragmented digital infrastructures, limited interoperability, and regulatory constraints within the Belgian health care system.

CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholders viewed improving diabetes SM as a shared responsibility between patients, HCPs, and the health care system. While digital health technologies may strengthen SM support, their value depends on how well they complement existing care processes and address contextual implementation challenges. These findings provide context-specific insights that may inform the development and implementation of digital interventions for T2DM in Belgium and similar health care settings. Further qualitative research involving a larger and more diverse sample of people living with T2DM is warranted to better understand patient experiences and support needs.

articles.title: A GCN1-independent activator of the kinase GCN2.
articles.abstract: Mutations of EIF2AK4, which encodes the eIF2α kinase GCN2, cause a severe inherited form of pulmonary hypertension called pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). Some pathogenic variants of GCN2 are amenable to pharmacological reactivation by low concentrations of ATP pocket-binding inhibitors. Kinase inhibition at modestly elevated concentrations limits the clinical utility of these drugs against PVOD. We therefore performed an in cellulo chemical screen for GCN2 activators and identified three structurally distinct compounds with low micromolar stimulatory activities. Unlike previously described GCN2 activators, one of these molecules activated GCN2 independently of GCN1. Modelling supported by structure activity screens suggested it binds within the ATP pocket of GCN2, but unlike existing ligands does not protrude inward into the allosteric pocket or outward into the solvent. This overcomes a key requirement of other GCN2 activators.

articles.title: Tracking West Nile virus dynamics using viral loads from trapped mosquitoes.
articles.abstract: Mosquito-borne virus transmission is increasing globally. Due to a lack of effective vaccines or targeted treatments, mitigation relies on reducing human exposure to infectious mosquitoes. Entomological surveillance provides estimates of human risk by quantifying the prevalence of arboviruses in mosquito populations. Testing of pooled mosquitoes via RT-qPCR is often used to infer infection prevalence; however, these data are often binarised and ignore semi-quantitative cycle threshold (Ct values) that may provide valuable information on virus kinetics, mosquito infectiousness, and ultimately human risk. West Nile virus (WNV) is a globally distributed arbovirus and endemic to the United States. In this study, we analysed pooled Ct values from retrospective mosquito surveillance and found substantial variation that could not be explained by laboratory factors alone. To understand how underlying viral load and epidemiological dynamics might explain this variation, we developed a multi-scale model linking pooled Ct values to heterogeneous within-host viral kinetics in mosquitoes and birds and seasonal transmission dynamics. Our modelling suggests that Ct values from positive pools might reflect a mixture of potentially infectious and non-infectious mosquitoes, indicating that a substantial proportion of PCR-positive mosquitoes might not contribute to transmission. We then developed a method to estimate mosquito infection prevalence using only pooled Ct values that distinguishes infectious from non-infectious prevalence. Estimates of overall prevalence were comparable to standard methods using binarised data and remained accurate at higher prevalences where standard approaches fail. Overall, these findings demonstrate that entomological viral load data reflect biologically meaningful variation in mosquito infection status that is lost through binarisation. Accounting for heterogeneous mosquito viral kinetics can improve interpretation of surveillance data and estimates of transmission risk, with implications for arbovirus surveillance beyond WNV.

articles.title: Linking pedestrian behavior and safety at urban midblock crossings: A surrogate safety indicator-based analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pedestrian safety at midblock sections remains a major concern in urban traffic environments, especially in developing countries where crossings often occur outside designated facilities. This study aims to develop a proactive framework for assessing pedestrian safety using surrogate safety indicators and to establish the relationship between pedestrian behavior and safety performance.

METHODS: Pedestrian-vehicle interaction data were extracted from video recordings at three midblock locations with high pedestrian activity. Key surrogate safety indicators, including post-encroachment time (PET), time to collision (TTC), and maximum deceleration rate (MDR), were estimated to assess conflict severity. Serviceability indicators such as accepted gap, rejected gap, pedestrian waiting time, and crossing time were also analyzed. A predictive model was developed to estimate surrogate safety indicators based on these serviceability parameters.

RESULTS: The results indicate that PET is an effective surrogate indicator for evaluating pedestrian safety. Rejected gap showed a strong positive influence on PET, while increased pedestrian waiting time significantly reduced safety levels. Gap acceptance analysis revealed a relatively low critical gap, indicating risk-prone crossing behavior among pedestrians. The developed model successfully establishes a direct relationship between pedestrian behavioral characteristics and safety outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrates that surrogate safety indicators provide a reliable and proactive approach for evaluating pedestrian safety at midblock sections. The proposed framework enables identification of high-risk locations and supports planners and engineers in implementing targeted pedestrian safety improvements.

articles.title: Willingness and comfort to distribute HIV self-testing kits among people living with HIV in Bhutan: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Partner testing among people living with HIV is critical for HIV case detection but faces socio-cultural barriers. HIV self-testing (HIVST) remains underutilised in partner notification services (PNS). We examined factors associated with willingness and comfort to distribute HIVST. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Bhutan. Socio-demographic and behavioural characteristics were collected. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression assessed willingness and comfort in HIVST distribution. Among 377 adults, 72.2% aged 35-64 years, 59.9% were married. HIVST awareness (38.7%) and prior HIVST use (13.3%) were low. 53.1% were willing to distribute HIVST, with greater comfort towards spouses (66.0%) than non-spousal partners (21.0-40.1%). Willingness was associated with HIVST awareness (AOR = 2.40; 95% CI: 1.19-4.83) and valuing disclosure (AOR = 2.55; 95% CI: 1.11-5.84), while indirect distribution was associated with lower willingness (AOR = 0.13; 95% CI: 0.06-0.28) and comfort (AOR = 0.03; 95% CI: 0.01-0.15). Lower comfort was associated with social stigma (AOR = 0.13; 95% CI: 0.07-0.25) and being previously married (AOR = 0.25; 95% CI: 0.13-0.47), whereas healthcare discrimination was associated with greater comfort. Willingness and comfort are distinct but complementary constructs shaping index-based HIVST distribution within PNS. Strategies addressing stigma, disclosure, and partner type may improve partner testing.

articles.title: Two Older Adult Patients With Anorexia and Cachexia Following Refractory Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare Complex Pulmonary Disease Given Acupuncture Treatment to Improve Appetite and Food Intake.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Refractory Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) is often complicated by anorexia, weight loss, and cachexia. This report describes 2 older adult patients with anorexia and cachexia following refractory MAC-PD given acupuncture treatment to improve appetite and food intake. CASE REPORT Case 1 was a man in his 70s with cavitary nodular bronchiectatic MAC-PD diagnosed 7 years earlier based on the 2007 American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America (ATS/IDSA) criteria. His chest radiographic lesions had progressively worsened, with persistent smear positivity despite multidrug chemotherapy. He developed complete anorexia and eating-related dyspnea; his body weight decreased to 35.4 kg (body mass index [BMI] 11.8 kg/m²). Case 2 was a woman in her 60s who was diagnosed with nodular bronchiectatic MAC-PD with cavities, which developed into a giant cavity, 4 years earlier. She developed severe anorexia and postprandial dyspnea, and her body weight was 31.0 kg (BMI 13.2 kg/m²). Both patients received manual acupuncture at CV12, ST36, LU9, and individualized points 3 times weekly for 3 weeks. Appetite on a 100-mm visual analog scale, energy intake, body weight, and serum albumin improved in both patients. Sputum acid-fast bacillus (AFB) smear status and radiographic findings were unchanged. No adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS Nine acupuncture sessions over 3 weeks improved appetite, dietary intake, and nutritional indices in 2 cachectic patients with refractory MAC-PD without altering bacteriological or radiological disease activity. Acupuncture merits consideration as adjunctive care for anorexia in this setting. Controlled studies are needed.

articles.title: Linking Circulating Metal Levels to Cytokine Signatures in Total Joint Arthroplasty Patients.
articles.abstract: Arthroplasty may significantly improve the quality of life; however, wear and corrosion of metallic biomaterials can lead to the release of metal ions and particles, contributing to immune responses. Circulating metals may influence cytokine production, but systemic biomarkers of implant-related inflammation remain elusive. This study aimed to quantify systemic metal levels and cytokines to identify potential immunological signatures in patients exposed to arthroplasty metals. Peripheral blood samples from 150 patients scheduled for either primary or revision arthroplasty were analyzed. Whole blood multi-metal levels were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Plasma levels of 47 cytokines were quantified using a bead-based multiplex immunoassay. Cytokine patterns were examined via clustering and correlated with metal levels, adjusting for age, sex, prosthetic joint infection, lymphocyte count, C-reactive protein levels, and season. Blood levels of cobalt, chromium, titanium, niobium, and zirconium were significantly elevated in patients with arthroplasty implants, compared to arthroplasty-naïve controls. Selective correlations were observed, notably cobalt with IL-8 and multiple metals with IL-15. Cytokine clustering identified four distinct modules representing systemic immune activity. Multivariable linear regression modeling revealed associations of metal exposure with IL-1RA, IL-8, IL-15, and the proinflammatory cluster after adjusting for age, sex, periprosthetic joint infection status, inflammation markers, and season. This study shows that arthroprosthetic metal exposure is associated with systemic elevation of selective cytokines. Blood-based cytokine profiles may serve as biomarkers for monitoring implant-related immune activation, providing insights into mechanisms of systemic inflammation, yet must be interpreted within the context of multifactorial influences.

articles.title: Determinants of Successful Mobile Smoking Cessation Interventions: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, digital interventions for smoking cessation have seen increasing use, but program completion rates vary widely. Therefore, understanding the factors associated with program completion in cessation programs is critical for evaluating the feasibility and acceptability of the digital intervention program.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to identify the predictors (sex, age group, and health) of program completion in a cognitive behavioral therapy-based mobile smoking cessation program.

METHODS: Participants enrolled in Adiquit, a mobile app-based smoking cessation program, were classified as completers if they had entered the Withdrawal-Relapse phase and had reported no lapse for 15 consecutive days or had finished all program sessions. User data for this study covered the period from launch through July 2024. Users who did not meet the completion criteria by the end of the study were classified as noncompleters. Predictors were assessed during the Entry and Equilibrium phases, including demographic characteristics, psychosocial factors, and early engagement metrics. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with completion.

RESULTS: The three strongest predictors of program completion, as identified by the multivariate model, are higher early engagement (session attendance and screen time), stronger perceived social support, and positive prequitting feelings.

CONCLUSIONS: The results of this study will help clarify the variables that lead to successful completion of such a digital intervention program, as well as their importance by sex, age group, health status, and employment status.

articles.title: Ravulizumab monotherapy for anti-CFH antibody-associated aHUS in an elderly patient: a case report highlighting individualized clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy caused by complement dysregulation. Although anti-complement factor H (CFH) autoantibodies are a well-recognized cause of aHUS, their occurrence in elderly patients is rare, and optimal management in this population remains unclear. We report the case of an 85-year-old man who presented with acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, alongside severe hypertension. ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and no secondary causes of thrombotic microangiopathy were identified, leading to a clinical suspicion of complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). At the time of clinical decision-making, anti-CFH antibody status was not yet available;serum creatinine trends during hemodialysis could not reliably indicate intrinsic renal recovery, and hematological markers, although improving, did not clearly indicate complete resolution of hemolysis. Following an individualized risk assessment regarding plasma exchange (PEX) and immunosuppressive therapy in an octogenarian, ravulizumab was selected as the initial treatment due to its etiology-independent mechanism of action. Following initiation, hematological parameters continued to improve, and renal function gradually recovered, allowing discontinuation of hemodialysis. Subsequent testing revealed elevated anti-CFH antibody levels without pathogenic complement gene variants, confirming the diagnosis of anti-CFH antibody-associated aHUS. This case highlights that, in clinical settings with diagnostic uncertainty, ravulizumab monotherapy may be considered as an individualized initial approach in exceptional cases where PEX and immunosuppression are judged unsuitable based on clearly documented patient-specific risks, and requires careful follow-up including serial anti-CFH antibody monitoring and consideration of immunosuppression if antibody titers persist or relapse risk remains high.

articles.title: Sonic hedgehog-matrix metalloproteinase crosstalk in neurovascular ageing and stroke: a potential mechanistic link.
articles.abstract: Neurovascular ageing is a major contributor to cerebrovascular vulnerability and poor stroke outcomes in older adults. Progressive deterioration of the neurovascular unit (NVU), driven by oxidative stress, neurovascular coupling dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, inflammageing, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy compromises neurovascular resilience and increases susceptibility to ischemic injury. Among the molecular pathways implicated in these processes, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are important regulators of neurovascular remodeling, BBB integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Although these pathways have largely been investigated independently, emerging evidence suggests potential bidirectional interactions between Shh signaling and MMP activity. In particular, Shh/Gli1 signaling has been associated with regulation of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in experimental models, whereas MMP-2 can disrupt SCUBE2, an extracellular regulator of Shh ligand presentation, providing a potential mechanism for reciprocal pathway modulation. This review examines the Shh-MMP axis as a potential mechanistic link between neurovascular ageing and ischemic vulnerability, integrating current evidence to evaluate how dysregulation of these pathways may contribute to BBB dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, neuroinflammation, and impaired neurovascular repair. We further discuss the potential therapeutic implications of modulating the Shh-MMP axis to preserve neurovascular resilience and improve cerebrovascular outcomes in the ageing brain, while highlighting the importance of temporal and cell-specific targeting.

articles.title: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: feasibility, practical benefits, and surgical pitfalls from a single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe surgical outcomes, technical considerations, and feasibility of redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery using initial cases as a reference cohort.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective review of minimally invasive mitral valve surgery performed between January 2014 and January 2024 was conducted. Perioperative data, mid-term survival, and cardiac-related events were assessed in both initial and redo groups.

RESULTS: A total of 647 patients were included: 30 in the redo group and 617 in the initial group. The redo group had higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II scores (p < 0.001). In the redo group, 26 (86.7%) had undergone previous cardiac surgery via sternotomy, and 18 (60.0%) had previous mitral valve surgery. The operative time was longer in the redo group (p = 0.041), while the cross-clamping time was longer in the initial group (p = 0.019), and cardiopulmonary bypass time was comparable between groups (p = 0.95). Intubation time (p = 0.049), intensive care unit stay (p = 0.020), and in-hospital stay (p = 0.003) were longer in the redo group. However, there were no significant differences in postoperative chest tube output for 24 h (p = 0.32) or blood transfusion requirements (p = 0.087). The overall survival rates at 5 years were 70.7% (95% CI: 41.0%-87.0%) vs. 92.0% (95% CI: 88.0%-94.0%) for the redo and initial groups, respectively. Freedom from cardiac-related events did not significantly differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was feasible despite higher surgical risk and longer operative times. Early and mid-term cardiac-related outcomes appeared acceptable, although overall survival was lower in redo cases.

articles.title: Dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether dual antiplatelet therapy improves survival and major ischemic outcomes, and whether it increases major bleeding, compared with aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin plus a platelet adenosine diphosphate receptor inhibitor with aspirin alone after coronary artery bypass grafting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding. Risk ratios were pooled with random-effects models.

RESULTS: Nine randomized trials involving 3,516 patients were included. Eight trials involving 3,496 patients reported all-cause mortality. Dual antiplatelet therapy was not associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (risk ratio 0.77, 95% confidence interval 0.34-1.75), myocardial infarction (risk ratio 0.92, 95% confidence interval 0.56-1.50), stroke (risk ratio 0.68, 95% confidence interval 0.33-1.43), or major adverse cardiovascular events (four trials, 3,054 patients; risk ratio 0.69, 95% confidence interval 0.41-1.16). Major bleeding was increased in the primary analysis (risk ratio 2.28, 95% confidence interval 1.48-3.52), but this association was attenuated after exclusion of the largest contemporary trial.

CONCLUSIONS: In randomized evidence, dual antiplatelet therapy did not clearly reduce mortality or major ischemic events after coronary artery bypass grafting compared with aspirin alone. Routine, unselected use is not supported, and individualized postoperative antiplatelet decisions remain warranted.

articles.title: Anatomy-Aware Effects of Biliopancreatic-Limb Length in Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Trials labelled "long" biliopancreatic limb (BPL) test different Roux-en-Y gastric bypass configurations. We separated fixed-alimentary-limb BPL extension, reciprocal limb reallocation, distalization, and compound changes. The registered primary outcome was 12-month HbA1c in baseline type 2 diabetes. Eighty reports represented 39 studies (14 randomized trials, 25 cohorts). Primary HbA1c differences were - 0.18% points (95% CI - 0.59 to + 0.23) for fixed-limb extension and - 0.33 (- 0.60 to - 0.06) for reallocation; these classes were not pooled. Two fixed-limb trials (146 participants) yielded a secondary 12-month percentage total weight-loss difference of + 0.36 points (- 0.60 to + 1.32). Glycemic evidence remains sparse and configuration-specific. Fixed-limb evidence is inconsistent with a 5-point weight-loss gain but does not exclude smaller effects or identify the isolated BPL effect. KEY POINTS: • Only three of 14 RCTs tested fixed-AL BPL extension; one measured the CC. • Primary 12-month HbA1c could not be pooled within an anatomical class. • Fixed-total reallocation suggested a modest HbA1c package effect. • Allocation shifts and distalization cannot identify an isolated BPL effect.

articles.title: MASLD Cluster Derived Outcomes after Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery: a Retrospective Single-Center Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has become the most common chronic liver disease and is strongly associated with obesity. A novel approach of categorizing subtypes of MASLD has been proposed recently. Intent of this study was to investigate the influence of these clusters on weight loss and diabetes outcomes of metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We retrospectively analysed all patients undergone primary Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) between 2015 and 2025 in a german tertiary obsesty center. We performed the cluster differentiation proposed by Raverdy et al. along with a correlation of histolophathologic findings from liver biopsies collected during surgery and evaluated weight loss and diabetes remission at 12, 24 and 60 months after surgery.

RESULTS: Overall, 588 out of 850 patients met the inclusion criteria for sufficient clustering of whom 49 were assigned to the cardiometabolic, 52 to the liver specific and 487 to the control cluster. Baseline characteristics differed regarding age, HbA1c, and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) (HbA1c: 8.4 in the cardiometabolic vs 6.2 liver specific; p < .001) between clusters. Liver fibrosis was found in 65% of the cardiometabolic, 41,4% in the liver specific cluster and 16.4% in the control cluster (p < .001). Postoperative complications did not differ between clusters. Total body weight loss (%TBWL) at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months was 22.1%, 19.7%, 17.9% and 18.7% in the cardiometabolic cluster vs. 29.5%, 29.9%, 29.3% and 25.2% in the liver specific cluster (p < .001). Secondary worsening of T2DM occurred in 36% at 24 months 37.5% at 60 months in the cardiometabolic cluster but in 0% in the liver specific (both p < .001).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative data-driven clustering for MASLD identifies distinct types of MASLD in MBS candidates, correlating with histological results. Cluster subtypes are associated with weight loss and diabetes outcomes with inferior outcomes for the cariometabolic cluster. These findings may have an impact on the risk-benefit ratio and on expectation management of MBS.

KEY POINTS: Data-driven MASLD Clustering is reproducible in MBS candidates and correlates with histological findings. Cluster subtypes are associated with weight loss and diabetes outcomes after MBS. Patients assigned to cardiometabolic cluster show inferior weigth loss and diabetes outcomes. Clustering may impact individual treatment planning, expectation management, and targeted follow-up strategies.

articles.title: Type 2 Diabetes Relapse after Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass and Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remission after bariatric surgery may not be durable, and relapse after initial remission is an increasingly important outcome. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the risk of T2DM relapse after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) versus sleeve gastrectomy (SG) in patients with obesity and T2DM who achieved postoperative remission.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to April 20, 2026. Eligible studies included adults with obesity and preoperative T2DM who underwent primary RYGB or SG and reported T2DM relapse after remission. Hazard ratios (HRs) and odds ratios (ORs) were pooled separately using random-effects models. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or Cochrane risk of bias tool.

RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 11 cohorts and 24,228 patients were included; 9,674 underwent SG and 14,554 underwent RYGB. The mean age was 49.5 years, 31.4% were male, the mean BMI was 47.7 kg/m², and the mean T2DM duration was 5.7 years. Compared with SG, RYGB was associated with a significantly lower risk of T2DM relapse in HR-based analyses (HR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.59-0.76; P < 0.0001; I² = 23.1%) and OR-based analyses (OR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.52-0.76; P < 0.0001; I² = 0%). Subgroup analysis, sensitivity analysis, and publication-bias analysis supported the robustness of the findings.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that RYGB was associated with a lower risk of T2DM relapse after initial remission than SG. However, given the predominantly retrospective nature of the available evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in well-designed prospective studies.

articles.title: Short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT in interstitial pneumonia: a vascular dimension that stratifies risk independently of the GAP score.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Risk in interstitial pneumonia (IP) is assessed routinely by the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) score from pulmonary function and the tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) on echocardiography. This study evaluated whether the percent perfusion defect (%PPD) on short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold (STDIBH) pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT carries prognostic information that neither captures.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-one consecutive patients with IP who underwent STDIBH perfusion SPECT/CT between 2012 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was a composite major adverse event (MAE) of all-cause death, acute exacerbation of IP, respiratory-failure hospitalization, and initiation of home oxygen therapy. Association was assessed by Cox regression and discrimination by censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: MAE occurred in 66 of 91 patients (72.5%) over a median follow-up of 45.9 months. %PPD was associated with MAE after adjustment for the GAP score and antifibrotic therapy (adjusted hazard ratio 1.2304 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.0568-1.4325; P = 0.008), and, in exploratory analyses, for TRPG and the GAP score together (1.2058, 1.0314-1.4096; P = 0.019). It showed no significant correlation with TRPG (Spearman r = 0.164; P = 0.140). Time-dependent discrimination did not differ significantly between %PPD and the GAP score at 6, 12, and 24 months, and adding %PPD to the GAP score changed the Harrell C-index from 0.692 to 0.719 (difference 0.027, 95% CI - 0.009 to 0.107). %PPD was obtained in all 91 patients and the GAP score in 68 (74.7%).

CONCLUSION: In IP, %PPD measures a dimension of risk that the GAP score does not capture, and exploratory analyses suggest that echocardiography does not capture it either. %PPD is obtainable when the GAP score is not. Its discrimination did not differ significantly from that of the GAP score, and adding it to the GAP score did not significantly improve discrimination.

articles.title: Therapeutic effect of quercetin on airway remodeling of ovalbumin-induced asthmatic mice via inhibition of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway.
articles.abstract: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited treatments for airway remodeling. Quercetin has anti-inflammatory potential, but whether it acts through the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic effect of quercetin on asthma in a mouse model and the associated underlying molecular mechanism. Various doses of quercetin were employed to intervene in a mouse model of asthma. Alterations in inflammation-related indicators and mtDNA in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), pathological changes in lung tissue, and activation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway were detected. The STING agonist DMXAA was utilized to verify whether quercetin could enhance the relevant indicators in the mouse asthma model by suppressing the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Finally, BEAS-2B cells were treated with TGF-β to mimic the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process of asthmatic epithelial cells. Quercetin, a STING overexpression vector and ethidium bromide intervention were used to analyze whether quercetin inhibited the TGF-β-induced EMT process in BEAS-2B cells by suppressing the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Quercetin treatment effectively mitigated inflammatory infiltration and airway remodeling in a mouse model of asthma, and the therapeutic effect was most pronounced at a high dose. Additionally, quercetin treatment inhibited the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway in asthmatic mice. Treatment with DMXAA reversed the therapeutic effect of quercetin in the mouse model of asthma. At the cellular level, quercetin inhibited TGF-β-induced EMT in BEAS-2B cells by suppressing the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Thus, quercetin can ameliorate inflammatory infiltration and airway remodeling in a mouse model of asthma, potentially by suppressing the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway.

articles.title: Chest Radiotherapy Associated Cardiotoxicity: An Update.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Chest radiotherapy has improved cancer survival in various thoracic malignancies, including breast cancer, Hodgkin lymphoma, and lung cancer. However, inadvertent radiation exposure to the heart is associated with a broad spectrum of cardiovascular toxicities, collectively termed radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD). We aim to review the pathophysiology of RIHD and the current evidence for their incidence, risk factors, clinical management, and prevention strategies.

RECENT FINDINGS: RIHD is mediated by oxidative stress, DNA damage, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and progressive fibrosis, leading to accelerated atherosclerosis, myocardial stiffening, valvular degeneration, pericardial disease, and arrhythmias. The risk, timing, and severity of cardiovascular complications are influenced by radiation dose and distribution, age at exposure, baseline cardiovascular risk, and concomitant cardiotoxic therapies. While younger patients may experience prolonged latency before clinical disease onset, older individuals and those with pre-existing cardiovascular disease often develop complications earlier, reflecting radiation-mediated acceleration of underlying pathology. This review summarizes the epidemiology, latency, clinical presentation, surveillance strategies, and management of the different forms of RIHD. It also discusses contemporary approaches to risk mitigation, including advances in radiation delivery techniques, aggressive cardiovascular risk factor modification, lifestyle interventions, and emerging pharmacologic strategies.

articles.title: Individual and District-Level Determinants of Suicide: A Multilevel Case-Control Study in Seoul.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Despite the implementation of various governmental mental health measures, suicide and mental illness remain critical public health challenges in South Korea. This study investigates the effects of individual and policy-level factors on suicide risk, aiming to provide empirical evidence to strengthen mental health interventions and suicide prevention strategies. A case-control study design was employed using three-level generalized linear mixed models to address the hierarchical panel structure of medical data. The analysis used nationally representative cohort data and metropolitan-level mental health statistics from 2017 to 2019, covering both individual and regional dimensions. A total of 1122 observations from 462 individuals were analyzed. Significant group differences were found in variables such as age, sex, disability status, insurance type, mental illness diagnosis, insurance premium quantile, registered patient status, and regional mental health budget. Multilevel modeling revealed that suicide risk increased over time and was notably higher among individuals with lower socioeconomic status and greater mental health vulnerability. Policy-related factors, particularly mental health budget allocations, were also significantly associated with suicide risk. The findings highlight the importance of identifying high-risk populations and implementing proactive, well-funded mental health policies to reduce suicide rates and improve mental health outcomes at both national and local levels.

articles.title: Expression, purification, and diagnostic evaluation of the recombinant matrix protein of peste des petits ruminants virus.
articles.abstract: Peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV) causes a highly contagious and economically devastating disease of small ruminants, particularly sheep and goats. Serological evaluation using recombinant protein-based Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) is essential for monitoring PPRV infection and assessing eradication programs. Although recombinant nucleoprotein (N) is widely used for serological evaluation, investigation of additional viral proteins may provide alternative antigenic platforms for PPRV antibody detection. The matrix (M) protein plays a central role in viral assembly by linking viral surface glycoproteins with ribonucleoprotein complexes. However, recombinant expression of full-length M protein in Escherichia coli (E. coli) is challenging because of low or truncated expression and inclusion body formation, often requiring complex refolding procedures. In this study, full-length M protein from the Nigeria 75/1 vaccine strain was successfully overexpressed as inclusion bodies (IBs) in E. coli and solubilized using N-lauroyl sarcosine (NLS) without refolding. The solubilized protein was purified by nickel-affinity chromatography, yielding 2.1 mg/L bacterial culture, and confirmed as a 38-kDa protein by sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) and Western blotting. An indirect ELISA was developed using purified M protein and optimized with commercial control sera. Optimal conditions were achieved with 1 µg/mL antigen and 1:20 serum dilution. Using pre-confirmed field sera, the assay demonstrated 94.59% sensitivity and 92.45% specificity at a cut-off of 0.25. Comparison with the commercial ID Screen® PPR Competition ELISA showed comparable performance and strong agreement. These findings demonstrate the recombinant PPRV M protein as a feasible diagnostic antigen for PPRV antibody detection which requires further validation for large scale application.

articles.title: Serial bedside retinal optical coherence tomography angiography in sepsis associated circulatory dysfunction.
Three-week ileostomy closure after colorectal surgery: a multicenter randomized trial of technical and postoperative outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of temporary ileostomy closure following restorative colorectal surgery remains controversial. Although previous randomized studies have demonstrated the feasibility of early closure in carefully selected patients, the influence of closure timing on operative complexity has not been prospectively evaluated. This multicenter randomized controlled trial compared a standardized 3-week ileostomy closure strategy with conventional delayed closure, with particular emphasis on technical and postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter randomized controlled trial, 224 patients undergoing restorative colorectal resection with temporary diverting ileostomy were randomized to either early ileostomy closure at 3 weeks (n = 112) or conventional delayed closure (n = 112). Eligibility for reversal required rigorous confirmation of anastomotic healing using standardized clinical and endoscopic assessment, with selective computed tomography using rectal contrast when clinically indicated. The primary outcome was operative complexity, evaluated using operative duration, intraoperative adhesion severity, and the requirement for extended adhesiolysis. Secondary outcomes included postoperative morbidity, Clavien-Dindo complication grade, length of hospital stay, readmission, reoperation, re-diversion, and delay in adjuvant chemotherapy.

RESULTS: Baseline demographic, clinical, and operative characteristics were comparable between the study groups. Early ileostomy closure was associated with significantly shorter operative duration (90 ± 12 vs. 130 ± 18 min; P < 0.001), substantially lower intraoperative adhesion severity (P = 0.04), and a markedly reduced requirement for extended adhesiolysis (5.4% vs. 21.4%; P < 0.001). Overall postoperative morbidity, Clavien-Dindo grade distribution, postoperative length of stay, readmission, reoperation, and mortality were comparable between groups. Delays in adjuvant chemotherapy occurred only in the early-closure group (3.6%), were limited to 1-4 weeks, and all affected patients subsequently commenced the planned oncologic treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with confirmed anastomotic healing, 3-week ileostomy closure is a technically feasible and safe strategy following restorative colorectal surgery. Compared with conventional delayed closure, reversal at 3 weeks significantly reduced operative complexity without compromising short-term postoperative outcomes. These findings support selective implementation of a standardized 3-week ileostomy closure strategy and identify operative complexity as a key determinant when selecting the optimal timing of ileostomy reversal.

articles.title: Periodontitis Beyond ASCVD: Emerging Cardiovascular Phenotypes in Perio-Medicine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis is increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory disease with systemic implications beyond the oral cavity. Within perio-medicine, its association with cardiovascular disease has been extensively investigated, particularly in relation to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). However, the field is now expanding toward a broader and more phenotype-specific cardiovascular framework.

OBJECTIVE: This narrative review critically examines how the periodontitis-cardiovascular field has evolved from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a broader spectrum of cardiovascular phenotypes, with particular emphasis on differences in evidence maturity, contemporary mechanistic concepts, and unresolved translational questions.

METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Evidence from mechanistic, observational, and interventional studies was qualitatively synthesized according to its contribution to established clinical associations, supportive mechanistic evidence, emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, and unresolved questions regarding causality and clinical translation.

RESULTS: The association between periodontitis and coronary atherosclerotic disease represents the most mature component of the literature, with substantial observational and meta-analytic support, while ischemic cerebrovascular disease is also supported by consistent but more heterogeneous evidence. Beyond ASCVD, atrial fibrillation and heart failure currently represent the most developed emerging cardiovascular phenotypes, whereas evidence concerning abdominal aortic aneurysm and venous thromboembolism remains more preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Contemporary mechanistic models extend beyond bacteremia and systemic inflammation to include endothelial dysfunction, thrombo-inflammatory signaling, trained immunity, immune-cell trafficking, functional dysregulation of the oral microbiome, and shared biological vulnerabilities. However, these pathways differ markedly in cardiovascular-specific evidentiary maturity and should not be interpreted as equivalent evidence of human causality. Periodontal therapy can improve inflammatory biomarkers, endothelial function, selected metabolic parameters, and blood pressure in specific populations, but a persistent translational gap remains between surrogate-marker improvement and demonstrated reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Periodontitis may also contribute to chronic systemic inflammatory burden in susceptible individuals, although its role within cardiovascular residual inflammatory risk remains an emerging hypothesis.

CONCLUSIONS: The periodontal-cardiovascular field is evolving from a predominantly ASCVD-centered model toward a phenotype-specific continuum of evidence maturity. Periodontitis is best interpreted as a potential modifier of cardiovascular vulnerability rather than as an established causal determinant. Future research should prioritize adequately powered cardiovascular-outcome trials, standardized periodontal phenotyping, and prospective validation of emerging phenotypes and mechanistic frameworks before periodontal information can be considered clinically actionable for cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Patient experiences with hereditary cancer genetic test result release in the setting of the 21st Century Cures Act final rule.
articles.abstract: The 21st Century Cures Act Final Rule is a federal law recently implemented in the United States of America which prompted a practice shift among genetic counselors who historically disclosed genetic testing results by directly speaking with patients. Herein, we report participant experiences following a single-center's approach of patients selecting provider-facilitated versus immediate release of hereditary cancer genetic testing results in the electronic health record preceding provider review. A voluntary survey was sent to patients who completed pre-test genetic counseling and hereditary cancer genetic testing within the University of Pennsylvania Health System. Responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Participants (n = 153) were predominately White (77%), female (81%), obtained Master's or Doctoral degrees (47%), and a median age of 60 (range 22-81). Participants across both result release cohorts did not differ in demographics, indication for testing, answers to knowledge-based questions or initial emotional responses. When asked about release preference for future genetic testing, most participants preferred provider-facilitated electronic portal message or a phone call. Of the participants who initially elected immediate release, only 18% (20/113) would again elect immediate release for future genetic tests. Participants across results release cohorts predominately elect for provider-facilitated release for future genetic testing, suggesting provider involvement may benefit patient disclosure experience.

articles.title: The Impact of Antibiotic Initiation Timing in Children with Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: A Post-Hoc Analysis of an Observational Study.
authors: Paediatric Acute Critical Care Asian Network (PACCMAN)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to examine the association between early antibiotic initiation and clinical outcomes in children admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

METHODS: We conducted a post-hoc analysis of a multicentre observational study across nine Asian PICUs. Children with severe CAP were categorized into early (≤ 6 h) or late (> 6 h) antibiotic initiation groups (early and late antibiotic groups, respectively) relative to PICU admission. The primary outcome was PICU mortality; secondary outcomes were 28-day ventilation-free days (VFD) and intensive care unit-free days (IFD). Multivariable analyses adjusted for country as fixed effect, age, Paediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM 3) score and comorbidities, when feasible.

RESULTS: Among the 544 paediatric patients included in the analysis, median age was 14.0 [interquartile range (IQR) 4.0-34.0] months and the PIM 3 score was 0.3 (IQR 0.0-6.8) %. Viral and bacterial pathogens were isolated in 206 (37.9%) and 145 (26.7%) patients, respectively. Almost all patients [537 (98.7%)] received antibiotics, with 475 (87.3%) and 62 (11.4%) patients in the early and late antibiotic groups, respectively. Late antibiotic initiation was associated with higher PICU mortality [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 5.19, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.94-13.88, P < 0.01], septic shock requiring inotropic support (aOR 3.25, 95% CI 1.45-7.28, P < 0.01) and multi-organ failure (aOR 4.60, 95% CI 2.11-10.04, P < 0.01). No significant associations were observed between late antibiotic initiation and VFD or IFD.

CONCLUSION: In critically ill children with severe CAP, initiating antibiotics within 6 h of PICU admission was associated with improved outcomes. This 6-h window may serve as a practical benchmark for quality improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Metabolic Syndrome in Adults with Polysomnography-Confirmed Obstructive Sleep Apnoea: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and metabolic syndrome (MetS) are prevalent cardio-metabolic conditions which frequently coexist. Growing evidence indicates a positive association between OSA and MetS, but up-to-date global data are lacking, leaving the true strength of the association uncertain. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to provide an updated and comprehensive synthesis of evidence on the risk of MetS in adults with polysomnography (PSG)-confirmed OSA.

METHODS: A systematic review and three-level random-effects meta-analysis were conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Searches were performed of the Ovid MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), CINAHL (Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature), Cochrane and Embase databases, yielding 8072 records. Studies reporting either odds ratios (OR) for MetS in adults with PSG-confirmed OSA compared to those without OSA, or with data to calculate these, were eligible for inclusion. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoBANS (Risk of Bias Assessment tool for Non-randomised Studies) tool. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were performed to explore sources of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: A total of 68 studies from 24 countries with 74 relevant effect sizes were included (24,663 adults with PSG-confirmed OSA; 11,423 without OSA). Adults with OSA had over threefold higher odds of MetS compared with those without (odds ratio 3.33, 95% confidence interval 2.86-3.87; p < 0.0001). Substantial heterogeneity was noted (I2 = 73.8%). Study design, geographic region, MetS definition/criteria, Apnoea-Hypopnea Index OSA diagnostic threshold and publication year significantly moderated the pooled estimate (all p < 0.05). A larger body mass index difference between groups was associated with higher odds of MetS (β = 0.14, t = 4.03, p < 0.001), whereas a higher proportion of male participants was associated with lower odds of MetS (β = - 0.01, t = - 2.81, p < 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with PSG-confirmed OSA have over threefold higher odds of having MetS, consistently across diverse populations. Thus, early and routine metabolic screening is recommended for all adults with OSA. Future research should incorporate longitudinal and genetic data to explore causal links between OSA and MetS.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251073055.

articles.title: Phenotyping of Arrhythmia-induced Cardiomyopathy: From Bench to Bedside and Back.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy (AIC) is an increasingly recognized and potentially reversible cause or modifier of heart failure. This review summarizes experimental and clinical evidence with a focus on atrial fibrillation (AFib)-induced left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies demonstrate that AIC extends beyond tachycardia alone and involves rhythm irregularity, loss of atrioventricular synchrony, altered calcium handling, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and substrate vulnerability. Clinical trials demonstrate the superiority of rhythm control therapy by catheter ablation in patients with AFib and heart failure. Emerging data illustrate the importance of phenotyping of AIC according to myocardial substrate and individual ventricular response to AFib. AIC should be considered as a heterogeneous spectrum. Refined phenotyping may improve prediction of recovery and guide specific and individual therapy.

articles.title: Paediatric Fentanyl Population Pharmacokinetics: A Scoping Review of Published Models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND PURPOSE: Fentanyl is a highly lipophilic opioid widely used within paediatric peri-operative and intensive-care settings, yet dosing is commonly titrated empirically because of substantial pharmacokinetic variability across developmental stages and clinical contexts. Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models provide a quantitative framework to characterise variability, but these have not been systematically synthesised. This scoping review aimed to identify and summarise published paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl, to compare model structures and covariate effects.

METHODS: We searched Embase and MEDLINE databases from database inception to 17 February 2026 for paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl. Two reviewers independently screened papers and extracted data in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines.

RESULTS: Fourteen paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl were identified. Infants (64%, 9/14) and patient populations spanning multiple age groups (e.g., inclusion of infants and children) (64%, 9/14) were most frequently studied. Intravenous fentanyl was modelled in all studies. Two-compartment structures predominated (79%, 11/14). Body weight was the most consistently retained covariate (79%, 11/14), while maturation functions based on postnatal or postmenstrual age were frequently required in neonatal and infant cohorts (50%, 5/10). Other covariates (e.g., obesity, concomitant CYP3A modulators, and genetic factors) were variably explored and inconsistently retained.

CONCLUSION: Within the existing fentanyl literature, important evidence gaps remain, particularly beyond intravenous administration. Existing models highlight body weight and developmental maturation as principal determinants of clearance and distribution. Evidence remains limited to intravenous administration, with no model data of non-intravenous routes and under-representation of dynamic covariates and external validation. Addressing these gaps will support robust model-informed precision dosing of fentanyl in children.

articles.title: Don't Wait- Ablate! Catheter Ablation in Patients with Advanced Heart Failure and Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexist and mutually accelerate disease progression through complex hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and structural interactions. Although earlier rhythm-control strategies failed to demonstrate mortality benefit, largely due to limitations of antiarrhythmic drug therapy, catheter ablation has fundamentally altered the therapeutic landscape.

RECENT FINDINGS: The CASTLE-AF trial established catheter ablation as a disease-modifying therapy in patients with AF and HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), demonstrating reductions in mortality and HF hospitalization. More recently, the CASTLE-HTx trial extended these findings to patients with end-stage HF eligible for heart transplantation (HTx) or left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy. Catheter ablation has demonstrated a marked reduction in mortality and the need of an urgent HTx, or LVAD implantation compared with medical therapy alone. Subsequent subanalyses further refined risk stratification and identified patient subsets deriving the greatest benefit. Therefore, catheter ablation has received a class 1 recommendation for patients with AF and HFrEF. According to recent clinical evidence supporting early rhythm control through catheter ablation in advanced HF, it leads to a paradigm shift in the management of this high-risk population: in selected patients with AF and advanced HF, clinicians should not delay referral-"Don't wait, ablate."

articles.title: Evaluation of Our Family Our Future: A Randomized Clinical Trial of a Family Resilience Intervention to Prevent Adolescent HIV/STI Infection and Depression in South Africa.
articles.abstract: Adolescents account for the majority of new HIV infections in South Africa and those with depressive symptoms are at elevated risk. Engaging families in preventive efforts is vital, but no effective interventions in South Africa integrate a family-based approach to adolescent HIV/STI prevention and depression. We report on results from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) testing the efficacy of Our Family Our Future, a family resilience intervention designed to address adolescent risk for depression, HIV and STIs. 879 adolescents (ages 14-16) in a high HIV prevalence urban setting near Cape Town, South Africa participated in a 2-arm, parallel, single-blinded RCT. Adolescents (along with one adult family member) were randomized to Our Family Our Future or to a control group. This analysis evaluates the intervention's efficacy in reducing (1) depressive symptoms, (2) HIV/STI incidence, (3) sexual debut, rates of vaginal and anal sex, and condomless sex. Data were collected via smartphone at baseline, 6 and 12 months. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale; HIV was gathered through dried blood spot samples, STIs through urine samples; vaginal sexual debut, anal sexual debut, rates of vaginal and anal sex, and condomless sex was gathered through self-report. A post-hoc analysis examined the "dosage" effect of session attendance on outcomes. Of 879 adolescents, 444 were randomized to the control group and 435 to the intervention. Retention rates were 81-84% at 6 months and 90-98% at 12 months. Intervention participants completed 88-98% of their assigned sessions. Primary outcomes showed no significant differences in HIV/STI incidence or most sexual behaviors at 6 or 12 months, but vaginal sex prevalence was lower in the intervention group at 12 months (55% vs. 65%, p = 0.007). Condom use and sexual debut rates were similar between groups. Depression scores were higher in the intervention group at 6 months (p = 0.004) but not at 12 months. Session attendance had no significant impact on depression or sexual behavior outcomes. Our Family Our Future showed mixed efficacy. The intervention reduced the number of adolescents engaging in vaginal sex at 12 months but had no effect on delaying sexual debut, reducing unprotected sex, or HIV/STI acquisition. Depression scores did not differ between groups at 12 months. Despite these mixed results, the reduction in sexual risk behavior suggests that family-based interventions hold promise and warrant further development.

articles.title: Does raised ICP play a role in cognitive outcome in scaphocephaly?
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract: Scaphocephaly, the cranial deformity resulting from premature fusion of the sagittal suture, represents the most common form of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis (Bosnian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences p. 110-6, 2018). Surgical correction is typically performed to normalize cranial morphology and reduce the risk of intracranial hypertension. However, the association between elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) and long-term neurocognitive outcomes remains unclear (Bosnian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences p. 110-6, 2018; Child's Nervous System p. 689-95, 2020). Some studies report an increased prevalence of learning and neuropsychological difficulties in children with sagittal synostosis, yet a direct causal relationship with elevated ICP has not been clearly demonstrated. Evidence suggests that while elevated ICP occurs in a subset of patients, cognitive differences likely arise from a multifactorial interaction between cranial restriction, brain development, and underlying biological mechanisms rather than ICP alone.

articles.title: Influenza vaccination effectiveness in children with underlying medical conditions: a case-control study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Children with underlying medical conditions are at increased risk of severe influenza outcomes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of influenza vaccination for children and adolescents with underlying medical conditions. We conducted a multicentre case-control study over three influenza seasons (2021/22, 2022/23; 2023/24) in Spain. Hospitalized children and adolescents aged 6 months to 17 years with underlying medical conditions were included. Cases were patients hospitalized with acute respiratory infection (ARI) and laboratory-confirmed influenza. Two different hospitalized control groups were included: test-negative controls and non-ARI controls. Adjusted vaccination effectiveness (VE) was estimated using multivariate logistic regression. A total of 274 children were included (66 influenza cases and 208 controls), 21.5% of whom were vaccinated. VE against influenza-associated hospitalization was not statistically significant in the overall study population. In immunocompetent children, adjusted VE was 80.6% (95% CI: 36.7-95.9) considering all controls and 81.7% (95% CI: 39.3-95.9) considering with test-negative controls. No statistically significant VE was observed among immunocompromised children. Results were consistent after excluding SARS-CoV-2-positive participants. No significant effectiveness were found by age group, influenza type or subtype, or time since vaccination.

CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccination provided protection against influenza-related hospitalization among immunocompetent children with underlying medical conditions. The low proportion of vaccinated children among hospitalized cases highlights the need to improve influenza vaccination uptake among children with underlying medical conditions and to further evaluate preventive strategies for immunocompromised children.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children with underlying medical conditions are at increased risk of influenza-related hospitalization. • Despite influenza vaccination recommendations, vaccination coverage among children with underlying medical conditions remains suboptimal.

WHAT IS NEW: • Seasonal influenza vaccination was associated with protection against influenza-related hospitalization among immunocompetent children with underlying medical conditions. • The low proportion of vaccinated children among hospitalized cases highlighting missed prevention opportunities and the need to improve vaccination uptake and explore alternative preventive strategies for immunocompromised children.

articles.title: "Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: Review of Latest Management Approaches".
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes recent advances in the management of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) since the 2023 Neurocritical Care Society and American Heart Association/American Stroke Association guidelines, with a focus on strategies targeting secondary brain injury and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI).

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies evaluated early lumbar cerebrospinal fluid drainage for clearance of subarachnoid blood, endothelin receptor antagonism and localized nicardipine delivery for vasospasm prevention, and liberal red blood cell transfusion strategies to optimize cerebral oxygen delivery. Advances in multimodal neuromonitoring may facilitate earlier detection and treatment of secondary brain injury. Artificial intelligence models integrating clinical and imaging data have demonstrated promising accuracy for early outcome prediction. New evidence supports an approach to aSAH management extending beyond prevention and treatment of large-vessel vasospasm. Although previous strategies have demonstrated better physiological outcomes, uncertainty remains in their effects on functional outcomes. Future research should focus on targeting the multiple processes underlying secondary brain injury.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171).
