No significant between-group differences were observed in delirium incidence, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, or safety outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Among older mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis, a low-use physical restraint strategy did not improve days alive without delirium or coma but was associated with more ventilator-free and coma-free days. These findings suggest that reducing restraint use may facilitate short-term recovery, although the safety of restraint minimization requires further evaluation.

TRAIL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1900025850.

articles.title: Clinical assessment and relationship of retinal fluorophores and microvascular modifications in early diabetic retinal disease in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify macular microvascular modifications and retinal fluorophores in early diabetic retinal disease (DRD) in type 1 diabetes mellitus (DM1), and to explore their interrelationship.

METHODS: One-hundred twenty-one subjects with DM1 and no diabetic retinopathy (noDR) or mild/moderate non-proliferative DR (NPDR) underwent optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT-angiography (OCT-A), and spectrally resolved fundus autofluorescence (Sr-FAF). OCT-A was analyzed for perfusion/vessel density (PD/VD), fractal dimension (FD), vessel length density (VLD), geometric perfusion deficits (GPD), and foveal avascular zone metrics in the superficial and deep capillary plexuses (SCP/DCP). Sr-FAF green and red emission fluorescence component (GEFC/REFC) intensities in 9 ETDRS macular sectors were quantified. Mann-Whitney U test was used for group comparisons and Pearson's coefficients for correlations between OCT-A and Sr-FAF.

RESULTS: One-hundred four eyes (50 noDR, 54 NPDR) were included. NPDR eyes showed lower PD, VD, FD, and VLD and higher GPD (p<0.001) in DCP vs noDR. GEFC intensity was higher in NPDR vs noDR in the nasal (p<0.01) and inner inferior (p=0.009) sectors and in the whole macular region(p=0.04); REFC intensity was higher in NPDR vs noDR at the fovea and in the inner nasal sector (p=0.01). In NPDR, DCP perfusion metrics correlated positively with GEFC and REFC values; in noDR, weak negative correlations were documented.

CONCLUSIONS: Quantification of minor retinal fluorophores with Sr-FAF and microvascular assessment may provide novel insights into early DRD in DM1. Opposing correlation trends across disease stages suggest dynamic vascular-metabolic interactions. Sr-FAF may serve as a biomarker of retinal metabolic status, warranting further validation.

articles.title: Pediatric obesity pharmacotherapy: a practical guide for general pediatricians.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Multimodal treatment approaches to pediatric obesity, including pharmacotherapy, are now recommended as part of an early intervention strategy to improve long-term health outcomes. However, barriers to prescribing obesity medications limit patient access to them. This review summarizes practical approaches to pediatric obesity pharmacotherapy tailored for the general pediatrician, based on evidence and expert opinion.

RECENT FINDINGS: The American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of pediatric obesity calls for early, individualized intervention, including consideration of pharmacotherapy. Available obesity medications include those that are Federal Drug Administration (FDA)-approved for this indication and those that are used "off-label" with FDA approval for other indications.

SUMMARY: Obesity pharmacotherapy should be considered an adjunct to lifestyle interventions for pediatric obesity. Readiness to prescribe these medications is influenced by physician comfort, practice infrastructure, and access-related barriers. Specialty training (i.e., endocrinology, gastroenterology, obesity medicine) does not have to be a requirement for managing obesity.

articles.title: Sagliker Syndrome: A Case Series and Literature Review With Clinical Characteristics, Post Parathyroidectomy Biochemical Trajectories and Hungry Bone Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical, biochemical, radiological, histopathological, and postoperative characteristics of patients with Sagliker syndrome.

METHODS: Three patients with dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease and Sagliker syndrome who underwent parathyroidectomy at our institution were retrospectively analysed. A literature review identified six published reports with detailed clinical, biochemical, radiological, surgical, and postoperative data suitable for comparative analysis.

RESULTS: All three patients presented with progressive diffuse craniofacial skeletal remodelling characterised by maxillomandibular enlargement, facial widening, and severe secondary hyperparathyroidism. Preoperative intact parathyroid hormone concentrations ranged from 2258 to 4750 pg/mL, accompanied by marked hyperphosphatemia and elevated alkaline phosphatase levels consistent with advanced high-turnover bone disease. Sequential clinical imaging demonstrated progression from preserved facial morphology to severe craniofacial deformity following end-stage renal disease. Radiologic findings included osteitis fibrosa cystica, acro-osteolysis, and salt-and-pepper skull appearance. All patients developed severe postoperative hungry bone syndrome requiring intensive calcium and calcitriol supplementation following parathyroidectomy. Published reports demonstrated a highly concordant results with prolonged dialysis exposure, female predominance, severe biochemical hyperparathyroidism, diffuse craniofacial involvement, and frequent postoperative hypocalcemia.

CONCLUSIONS: Early recognition and optimal management of CKD-MBD is pivotal in preventing severe, irreversible complications, including craniofacial deformities.

articles.title: AdhE Regulates the Adaptation Ability of Streptococcus mutans to Oxidative Stress and Heat Stress.
articles.abstract: Understanding how S. mutans adapts to environmental stresses is key to deciphering its cariogenic virulence. Here, we report that alcohol-acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (AdhE) modulates the stress adaptability in S. mutans by regulating a metabolic-acetylation axis. We demonstrated that overexpression of adhE sensitizes S. mutans to H2O2 and high temperature, impairing planktonic growth and biofilm integrity under oxidative and heat stress. Mechanistically, AdhE functions as a potential acetyl-CoA (Ac-CoA) synthase, with its overexpression elevating intracellular Ac-CoA levels. Quantitative acetylomics revealed that elevated Ac-CoA drives extensive protein acetylation, hyperacetylating 340 proteins. Protein interaction network analysis identified core antioxidant enzymes (Tpx, Dpr, TrxA/B, AhpC) and heat-shock chaperones (DnaJ, GroEL, ClpE) as major targets, linking hyperacetylation to compromised stress defenses. Crucially, in a rat caries model, adhE overexpression attenuated the cariogenic virulence of S. mutans, reducing oral colonization and caries severity, an effect exacerbated by H2O2 challenge. Collectively, these findings uncover AdhE as a metabolic regulator that bridges Ac-CoA availability, global protein acetylation, and stress adaptation, offering new insights into posttranslational control of bacterial fitness and potential anti‑caries targets.

articles.title: Is retinal vein occlusion an underrecognized paraneoplastic sentinel of lymphoma? A systematic review and meta-analysis of ocular-haematological interactions.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between retinal vein occlusion (RVO) and lymphoma across two complementary evidence components: a qualitative clinical synthesis of RVO occurring in patients with lymphoma and a quantitative synthesis of subsequent cancer outcomes in patients with RVO. For the qualitative synthesis, the population comprised patients with lymphoma and RVO and no comparator was required. For the quantitative synthesis, RVO was the exposure, individuals without RVO formed the comparator, and the prespecified outcomes were overall cancer and lymphoma incidence. Secondary outcomes were ocular, haematological, biochemical, immunological and protein-related clinical findings.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: RVO is a common cause of visual morbidity typically linked to vascular risk factors. Its role as a sentinel manifestation of haematological malignancy remains underrecognized. Early recognition of lymphoma-associated RVO supports timely systemic diagnosis and coordinated ophthalmic-haematological evaluation, particularly in atypical or bilateral presentations lacking conventional vascular risk factors.

METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant review (PROSPERO CRD420251134925) searched PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library and Google Scholar from inception to 21 July 2026. Eligible original human studies comprised case-based reports for qualitative synthesis and observational cohort or registry-based studies for quantitative synthesis. Case reports were appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) criteria and non-randomized studies with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool. Hazard ratios (HRs), odds ratios (ORs) and standardized incidence ratios (SIRs) were analysed as log-transformed relative-effect estimates using fixed-effects and random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran Q.

RESULTS: Twenty-six studies were included: 19 case-based publications describing 24 RVO cases with lymphoma and 7 observational studies contributing to quantitative synthesis. Central RVO (CRVO) predominated, often with bilateral severe visual impairment, optic disc swelling, diffuse haemorrhages and macular oedema. Recurrent systemic findings included anaemia, hyperviscosity, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and immunoglobulin M (IgM) paraproteinaemia. Meta-analysis demonstrated increased overall cancer risk (pooled log effect size 0.198; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.141-0.255; p < 0.001; I2 = 21.6%; ≈22% increase) and lymphoma risk (OR 1.50; 95% CI 1.08-2.09; p = 0.015; I2 = 58.9%). Age was not a significant study-level moderator (p = 0.93).

CONCLUSION: RVO, particularly atypical or bilateral CRVO, represents a clinically informative ocular presentation associated with lymphoma in the reviewed evidence. The combined ocular, haematological and quantitative findings support mechanistic links involving hyperviscosity, thrombosis, leucostasis and infiltration. Targeted systemic evaluation is warranted in high-risk presentations.

articles.title: An immune-inflammatory and thyroid function machine learning model for predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes: Development in a retrospective cohort and external validation in a prospective cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maternal thyroid dysfunction is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, yet thyroid status alone stratifies individual risk poorly and the immune-inflammatory contribution is rarely incorporated into prospectively validated prediction tools. We aimed to develop and externally validate a model predicting a composite adverse pregnancy outcome from antenatal thyroid and cytokine markers.

METHODS: The model was developed in a retrospective cohort (n = 650; 131 events, 20.2%) and externally validated in an independent prospective cohort (n = 150; 26 events, 17.3%). Fifteen antenatal candidate predictors common to both cohorts were considered. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection; LASSO-logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, and a support-vector machine were compared by repeated stratified cross-validation. Discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); calibration and clinical utility were also assessed, with internal-external cross-validation (IECV) as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: LASSO retained three predictors: thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-10 (IL-10). LASSO-logistic regression was selected (development cross-validated AUC 0.762, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.692-0.846). On external validation, the model achieved an AUC of 0.750 (95% CI 0.647-0.848), exceeding a thyroid group-only reference model (AUC 0.625); the Brier score was 0.127, and the calibration slope was 1.77. Random 10-fold IECV gave a pooled AUC of 0.761 (95% CI 0.720-0.800). Higher IL-6 was associated with increased risk and higher IL-10 with decreased risk.

CONCLUSION: A parsimonious three-marker model combining TPOAb, IL-6, and IL-10 showed moderate discrimination for adverse pregnancy outcomes and outperformed thyroid status alone. Calibration requires refinement, and validation in larger multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Late Obesity-Driven Subcutaneous ICD Geometric Failure: Salvage With Sub-Serratus Generator Repositioning.
articles.abstract: S-ICD efficacy depends on extracardiac shock vector geometry. We report late obesity-associated geometric deterioration after substantial weight gain. Rising shock impedance prompted reassessment at generator replacement, revealing pocket dehiscence, adipose interposition, and generator superficialization. Because fibrosis precluded parasternal lead mobilization by simple traction, sub-serratus generator repositioning improved the PRAETORIAN score and shock impedance. Despite a subsequent rise to 130 Ω, defibrillation succeeded with a 65 J shock. S-ICD geometry should be considered dynamic, particularly after major changes in body habitus.

articles.title: His Bundle Pacing via the Atrial Port of a Dual-Chamber ICD: Programming Solution for Undersensing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: His-bundle pacing connected to the atrial port of a dual-chamber ICD may lead to sensing failure and unsafe pacing.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old man with permanent atrial fibrillation, alternating rapid and slow ventricular rates despite medication, symptomatic pauses longer than 6s, and a dual chamber ICD (His lead in the RA port; DF4 lead in the RV port) presented with palpitations. ECG and 24-hour Holter demonstrated intermittent His-channel undersensing with pacing on the T-wave peak. Interrogation showed small His electrograms followed by a prominent, constant ventricular far-field signal on the atrial channel. We turned off far-field protection after V-sense, intentionally used the ventricular far-field signal for sensing of His lead, and disabled related discrimination algorithms.

CONCLUSION: A dual-chamber ICD with a His-bundle pacing lead may be associated with complex programming challenges, and targeted reprogramming can avoid lead revision or reimplantation.

articles.title: Marshall Vein Ethanol Infusion and Mitral Isthmus Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation With Durable Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical significance of adding vein of Marshall ethanol infusion (VoM-EI) and mitral isthmus (MI) ablation to left atrial posterior wall isolation (LAPWI) during repeat ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) despite durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains unclear. We assessed whether this combined strategy improves sinus rhythm maintenance.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 80 consecutive patients with AF who underwent repeat ablation despite durable PVI after prior PVI-only procedures and received either LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation or LAPWI alone.

RESULTS: Of the 80 patients, 27 underwent LAPWI plus VoM-EI and MI ablation (VoM-EI group) and 53 underwent LAPWI alone (control group). During a median follow-up of 591.5 days, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence did not differ significantly in the overall cohort on unadjusted analysis but was higher in the VoM-EI group among patients with persistent AF (log-rank p = 0.041). After multivariable adjustment, the combined strategy was associated with a lower risk of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence in patients with persistent AF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.38; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.92; p = 0.03) and in the overall cohort (HR 0.37; 95% CI 0.14-0.86; p = 0.02), mainly driven by persistent AF. Propensity score matching showed a similar association (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.11-0.75; p = 0.01). Major complication rates did not differ between the groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with persistent AF despite durable PVI, adding VoM-EI and MI ablation to LAPWI was associated with lower atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence than LAPWI alone. Because the two components were applied together, this finding is hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Fluorescence Encoding-Enabled Multiplexed Droplet Digital Recombinase Polymerase Amplification-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Rapid Screening of Lower Respiratory Tract Infection-Associated Bacterial Pathogens.
articles.abstract: Digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a assays enable accurate nucleic acid quantification; however, their multiplexing capacity is inherently limited by signal confounding arising from the promiscuous trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a effectors. To overcome this limitation, we developed a fluorescence encoding-enabled multiplexed droplet digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a (FLEMD-CRISPR) assay that integrates combinatorial fluorescence encoding, deterministic droplet pairing within a calabash-shaped microwell array, and a machine learning-assisted decoding pipeline. In FLEMD-CRISPR, small-volume fluorescence-encoded CRISPR/Cas12a droplets, each assigned a unique spectral signature corresponding to a specific crRNA, are one-to-one paired with large-volume RPA droplets. Following RPA amplification and droplet merging, Cas12a-mediated reporter cleavage occurs only in droplets containing target amplicons. The decoding pipeline then localizes droplets, classifies their colors to assign crRNA identities, and finally detects positive signals, enabling high-throughput, hands-off analysis of the entire droplet array. FLEMD-CRISPR enabled simultaneous quantification of nucleic acid targets from eight major lower respiratory tract infection-associated bacterial pathogens, showing strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.9987-0.9998) and consistent detection efficiency (slopes = 0.9849-1.0198) relative to single-plex digital PCR. The complete workflow, from sample preparation to final readout, can be completed within 2 h. Clinical validation using 30 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples showed that the bacterial detection outcomes of FLEMD-CRISPR were highly concordant with standard-of-care culture, achieving 100% (20/20) positive percent agreement and 99.1% (218/220) negative percent agreement. By enabling panel reconfiguration through simple modifications of the droplet encoding library, FLEMD-CRISPR provides a flexible platform for the development of highly multiplexed digital CRISPR assays.

articles.title: Wearable Sweat Biosystem with Dual Diffusion-Limiting Interface for Dynamic Hyperlactatemia Management in Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Hyperlactatemia is a critical indicator of tissue hypoperfusion, metabolic dysfunction, and an adverse prognosis in critically ill patients. Yet conventional monitoring depends entirely on intermittent, invasive blood sampling, which cannot capture the dynamic metabolic fluctuations required to guide timely clinical interventions. Herein, we report a wearable sweat-sensing device built on a dual-diffusion-limiting architecture for the continuous and accurate assessment of clinical hyperlactatemia. This system synergistically modulates lactate diffusion in sweat through a silane-network-encapsulated lactate oxidase layer coupled to a polyvinyl chloride layer. This design effectively delays enzyme saturation, extending the linear detection range for sweat lactate to 0-60 mM and thereby fulfilling the stringent requirements of critical care monitoring. The device also integrates real-time pH and temperature calibration to safeguard measurement accuracy in complex physiological environments. Moreover, linear mixed-effects analysis of 82 paired samples from 33 critically ill patients demonstrated a strong association between sweat and blood lactate levels, with a marginal R2 of 0.840. Sweat lactate effectively identified hyperlactatemia and predicted in-hospital mortality, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.943 and 0.785, respectively. The integrated iontophoresis-microfluidics module further ensures high consistency with bedside arterial blood gas analysis, as validated by a marginal R2 of 0.811. Together, these results establish sweat biosensors as a promising platform for continuous metabolic monitoring, resuscitation assessment, and objective prognostic stratification in critical care settings.

articles.title: pH-Programmed Poly(amino acid) Nanoparticles for Mucus-Penetrating and Bacteria-Targeted Eradication of Helicobacter pylori.
articles.abstract: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4-6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6-7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

articles.title: Visualizing Mycoplasma with Nanometer Resolution without Compromising Viability.
articles.abstract: This work represents a step toward the elucidation of the biological mechanisms underpinning live cell physiology with nanometer resolution. Using low-energy (30 keV), low-fluence, probe-corrected, integrated differential phase-contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy, in conjunction with a liquid flow cell, genetically engineered Mycoplasma strains, M. mobile and M. pneumoniae, which are among the smallest self-replicating cells, were scrutinized with nanometer resolution without compromising viability. Following exposure to a 30 keV electron beam, viability was scored at a lethal fluence to 50% (LF50) of the population at LF50 > 4,700 e-/nm2 by expression of an inducible fluorescent reporter, which is in stark contrast with the LF50 < 57 e-/nm2 observed at a beam energy of 300 keV. The higher LF50 at the lower beam energy of 30 keV afforded a wide window for high-resolution imaging of cell physiology. In this window, the mechanisms for "gliding" motility in Mycoplasma, which are supposed to be essential to infection and mediate attachment to a host, were visualized with nanometer resolution.

articles.title: Changing National and Regional Trends in Drug Use-Associated Infective Endocarditis From 2016 to 2022.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug use-associated infective endocarditis (DUA-IE) is a life-threatening condition that has increased alongside opioid injection. Recent shifts in drug use patterns and access to harm reduction and addiction treatment necessitate updated national estimates to assess disease burden.

METHODS: Using a representative sample of US hospitalizations from 2016 to 2022, we estimated national trends in DUA-IE hospitalizations among adults, stratified by year, drug category (opioids, stimulants, both, other), and census division. Logistic regression assessed the marginal probability of stimulant-associated endocarditis by individual (age, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance) and hospital characteristics (location/teaching status, bed size, census division). Analyses accounted for survey design and were weighted to provide national estimates.

RESULTS: An estimated 118 190 DUA-IE hospitalizations occurred from 2016 to 2022, peaking in 2020 (n = 18 735) before declining annually through 2022 (n = 15 345). From 2016 to 2022, opioid-only hospitalizations decreased (49.4%-39.9%), while co-use of opioids and stimulants (22.6%-28.6%) and stimulant-only hospitalizations (14.7%-18.3%) increased. Regional trends varied, with stimulants surpassing opioids in several Western divisions. Logistic regression models showed rising probability of stimulant-involved DUA-IE, highest in Western divisions (Pacific: 0.59 [95% CI .56-.62] vs New England: 0.34 [95% CI .31-.38]).

CONCLUSIONS: Drug use-associated infective endocarditis epidemiology is shifting, with overall hospitalizations declining but stimulant use emerging as a key driver, particularly in the Western United States. Current harm reduction and treatment efforts may be reducing DUA-IE hospitalizations, but targeted strategies addressing stimulant use are urgently needed.

articles.title: Target Trial of Semaglutide Versus Dulaglutide or Liraglutide in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the comparative effectiveness of semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide in patients with diabetes receiving maintenance hemodialysis.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Using 2011-2022 U.S. Renal Data System and Medicare data, we emulated a target trial evaluating semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide in patients receiving hemodialysis. Overlap weights were used to adjust for confounders. Fine-Gray models were used to assess death on dialysis and hospitalization. A generalized estimating equation was used for repeated measures of body weight.

RESULTS: We identified 1,312 semaglutide and 2,601 dulaglutide or liraglutide users. After overlap weighting, the effective sample size was 3,200 patients (mean age 61; 63% White; 28% Black; 52% male; median [interquartile range] BMI 34 [29-40] kg/m2; median follow-up 1.1 [0.6-1.9] years). Semaglutide versus dulaglutide or liraglutide was associated with a mortality on dialysis subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) of 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.97; 1-year cumulative incidence 11% vs. 13%) and all-cause hospitalization sHR of 0.91 (95% CI 0.83-0.99; 1-year incidence 57% vs. 62%). Body weight loss was higher with semaglutide (-4.8%, 95% CI -5.3% to -4.2%) at 1 year vs. -3.4%, 95% CI -3.9% to -3.1%). Direct comparisons of semaglutide versus dulaglutide showed similar results for mortality (sHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.97) and hospitalization (sHR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.97), but semaglutide versus liraglutide showed no statistically significant benefit for mortality or hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with diabetes receiving hemodialysis and equipoise between semaglutide and dulaglutide or liraglutide, semaglutide may be the preferred glucagon-like peptide 1 agent compared with dulaglutide.

articles.title: Safety of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes, but safety data in older adults remain limited. We evaluated the real-world safety of SGLT2is compared with dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) among individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a population-based, active-comparator, new-user cohort study using administrative health databases from British Columbia, Canada. We included individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes initiating SGLT2is or DPP-4is between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2023. Primary outcomes were infection, diabetic ketoacidosis, acute kidney injury, fall, fracture, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox regression with propensity score-based standardized mortality ratio weighting was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: The study included 4,997 SGLT2i initiators (median age, 79 years; 37% women) and 1,289 DPP-4i initiators (median age, 82 years; 50% women). Compared with DPP-4i initiation, SGLT2i initiation was associated with lower risks of acute kidney injury (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.95) and all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.98), with no difference in risk of infection. No differences were observed in risk of diabetic ketoacidosis, falls, or fractures, although CIs were compatible with both benefit and harm.

CONCLUSIONS: In individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2i initiation was not associated with increased risk of harm compared with DPP-4i initiation, although estimates were imprecise for some outcomes. These findings may support consideration of SGLT2is as a treatment option in this population.

articles.title: Sleeper agents: asymptomatic Acinetobacter colonization and underlying mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii and other Acinetobacter species are a growing public health concern because they commonly cause healthcare-associated infections. Acinetobacter spp. are often multi-drug resistant, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, understanding the reservoirs for Acinetobacter spp. in healthcare settings is particularly important to infection control. Acinetobacter spp. are known to asymptomatically colonize the human gut, skin, and respiratory flora, and recent work has found the prevalence of Acinetobacter colonization is high in patients in healthcare environments, such as hospitals and long-term care facilities. Patients colonized by A. baumannii are at increased risk of developing clinical infections, including by the same strains. Additionally, multiple studies report transmission of A. baumannii strains to other patients in the same healthcare setting. Recent mechanistic studies on A. baumannii gut colonization have found that the microbiota, host immunity, and diet contribute to colonization resistance in animal models. Here, we review the epidemiologic evidence for asymptomatic colonization as a clinically important reservoir for A. baumannii and examine the nascent study of the molecular mechanisms of Acinetobacter colonization. We discuss future prospects for understanding Acinetobacter colonization that may help develop strategies to support colonization resistance and prevent infections.

articles.title: Influenza A (H1N1) and SARS-CoV-2 Transmission in Airplanes: Quanta Profiles and Infection Control.
articles.abstract: Airborne transmission of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2 (ancestral strain) poses critical challenges in confined high-occupancy spaces, including aircraft, public transit, and institutional settings. Population-level quanta generation rate profiles, quantifying infectious particle emissions, are vital for assessing airborne infection risk but are poorly characterized. Short-range transmission complicates risk assessment due to variable close-contact scenarios. We estimated these profiles from 40 airplane outbreaks (14 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, 26 SARS-CoV-2) using a novel heterogeneity matching method and an integrated Wells-Riley model combining short- and long-range transmission, calibrated via Monte Carlo simulations. Results reveal super-emitter-driven variability. A new metric, close time equivalents for standardizing close-contact exposure, was calculated for 23 outbreaks (6 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, 17 SARS-CoV-2). Outbreak-derived quanta rates align with viral-load-based estimates, though the latter show greater variability. The population-level ventilation distribution compiled from commercial Boeing and Airbus cabin studies supports the robustness of the estimates. Impractical clean air equivalents for mitigating super-emitter transmission necessitate mask-wearing, effectively reducing close-contact and long-range transmission. These findings inform public health strategies for confined spaces and emerging variants.

articles.title: Powerhouses of lethality: mitochondria in macrophage antimicrobial activity.
articles.abstract: Macrophages employ multiple strategies to dispatch phagocytosed microbes, including bombardment with toxic compounds and radicals, or the deprivation of key nutrients. The lethality of macrophages depends on their ability to regulate levels of microbicidal effectors and proper targeting of these effectors to the phagosome, where many intracellular pathogens are detained. Mitochondria play important roles in establishing an antimicrobial phagosomal environment in macrophages, playing roles in both the production and targeting of these effectors. In response to infection, the mitochondrial network undergoes dramatic structural and functional perturbations that modulate macrophage microbicidal potential. As central coordinators of cellular metabolism, mitochondria control the abundance of metabolites that can either be toxic to ingested microbes or necessary for their growth. Mitochondria are also prolific producers of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which play direct roles in killing microbes and serve as signaling molecules to coordinate antimicrobial responses. While mitochondria are also known to play extensive roles in regulating cytokine production and proinflammatory responses, this review will focus on highlighting mechanisms by which mitochondria manipulate the macrophage microbicidal milieu.

articles.title: Neutrophil remodeling during chlamydial infection: recognition, survival, inflammatory signaling, and tissue injury.
articles.abstract: Chlamydia species are obligate intracellular bacteria with a biphasic developmental cycle. They cause trachoma, urogenital tract infection, community-acquired pneumonia, and zoonotic respiratory disease. A common feature of these conditions is not simply infection but the combination of persistence, recurrent inflammation, and tissue injury. Neutrophils arrive early at infected tissues and can initiate phagocytosis, degranulation, reactive oxygen species production, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation through pattern-recognition receptors, complement receptors, and Fc receptors. That response is not uniformly beneficial. When recruitment is excessive or poorly resolved, neutrophils can amplify inflammation, weaken epithelial barriers, and contribute to fibrosis and chronic immunopathology. Here, we review Chlamydia-neutrophil interactions as a staged biological process: recognition, recruitment, effector activation, apoptosis delay, inflammatory amplification, negative feedback, and tissue injury. Particular attention is given to TLRs, NF-κB, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, the NLRP3 inflammasome, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and IL-10/JAK-STAT-related feedback. We distinguish evidence obtained directly from neutrophils from evidence inferred from epithelial cells, macrophages, PBMCs, animal tissues, or other pathogen systems. This distinction is essential because mechanisms supported in one cell type or one chlamydial species cannot be transferred automatically to another. A more precise view of this network may refine current models of chlamydia-host interaction and pathogen persistence and help frame future studies on stage-specific immunomodulation.

articles.title: Baroreceptor Dysregulation Mediated via Neurohormonal Mechanisms in Heart Failure and its Influence on Renal Function: Potential Role of Baroreflex Activation Therapy.
articles.abstract: Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT), which electrically stimulates carotid sinus baroreceptors to modulate autonomic tone, has emerged as a novel adjunct to guideline-directed medical therapy for resistant hypertension and heart failure. Beyond its established cardiovascular benefits, emerging preclinical and early-phase clinical data suggest that BAT may favorably influence renal function and cardiorenal interactions. By suppressing sympathetic nervous system activity and downregulating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, BAT improves renal hemodynamics and may counteract key mechanisms leading to diuretic resistance. The latter represents a common and clinically significant challenge in patients with advanced heart failure, in whom impaired renal perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and tubular remodeling all contribute to reduced diuretic responsiveness and worsening kidney function. Early evidence indicates that BAT may preserve glomerular filtration rate, reduce proteinuria and improve urinary sodium excretion, suggesting potential renoprotective effects and a therapeutic role in mitigating diuretic resistance. However, these findings remain limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and heterogenous study populations across diverse clinical settings. This review synthesizes key physiologic mechanisms linking baroreflex signal modulation to renal outcomes and evaluates available clinical data. While BAT offers established cardiovascular benefits in heart failure, its renoprotective and diuretic-sparing potential remains investigational and lacks validation from randomized clinical trials. Dedicated prospective large-scale randomized studies are essential to establish long-term renal efficacy across the cardiorenal disease spectrum.

articles.title: Factors associated with receipt of prescription medication for menopause-related symptoms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of patient- and clinician-level factors and receipt of prescription medication for menopause-related symptoms in a large academic health care system.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women aged 40-55 years seeking care for menopause-related symptoms in any outpatient encounter with family medicine, internal medicine, endocrinology, and OB/Gyn from 2016 to 2023. Prescriptions associated with menopause-related ICD-10 diagnoses were extracted. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression were used to evaluate the association of patient- and clinician-level characteristics and receipt of prescription treatment.

RESULTS: We identified 5,491 women with an outpatient encounter with an associated ICD-10 code for menopause-related symptoms. Relative to White women, Black women were less likely to receive any prescription treatment for menopause-related symptoms (OR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.67-0.95), including systemic estrogen (OR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.47-0.87); however, were more likely to receive SSRIs (OR: 1.49, 95% CI: 1.04-2.14). Relative to patients seeking care within OB/Gyn settings, patients were less likely to be prescribed any treatment by internal medicine (OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.36-0.56), family medicine (OR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.14-0.40), and endocrinology clinicians (OR: 0.23, 95% CI: 0.14-0.40).

CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates differential prescribing patterns for menopause-related symptoms with respect to race, insurance status, and clinician specialty. Our results underscore the need for equitable care for women experiencing menopause symptoms.

articles.title: Polypharmacy and Glycemic Status in Individuals with Diabetes and Pre-diabetes: Iranian Multi-Center Osteoporosis Study 2021.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study examined the association between polypharmacy and glycemic status among adults aged ≥ 50 years.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included 1,117 participants from the 2021 Iranian Multi-center Osteoporosis Study (XXX). Data on sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, clinical and biochemical measures, and medication use were collected using standardized questionnaires, physical examinations, laboratory assessments, and direct observation of medication packages. Polypharmacy was assessed using thresholds of ≥ 3 and ≥ 5 concurrent medications. Weighted prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between polypharmacy and glycemic status, with adjustment for relevant demographic and health-related factors.

RESULTS: Polypharmacy was more common in individuals with diabetes than in those with pre-diabetes (≥ 3 medications: 49.89% vs. 28.25%; ≥ 5 medications: 26.28% vs. 9.82%).The mean number of medications was also higher among individuals with diabetes than among those with pre-diabetes (2.94 vs. 1.58). Among individuals receiving antidiabetic medications, polypharmacy defined as ≥ 5 medications was associated with higher odds of uncontrolled diabetes [adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.49, 3.29]. Each additional medication was also associated with higher odds of uncontrolled diabetes (AOR = 1.20; 95% CI: 1.12, 1.28).

CONCLUSION: Polypharmacy was associated with poorer glycemic control among adults aged ≥ 50 years. The association between polypharmacy and uncontrolled diabetes was particularly evident among those using ≥ 5 medications. These findings highlight the importance of considering overall medication burden when managing diabetes in this population.

articles.title: Metagenomic and thermodynamic mapping of Ny-Ålesund, Arctic microbiota: harnessing low temperature biohydrogen production.
articles.abstract: Biohydrogen produced by psychrophilic dark fermentation has lower energy requirements than conventional methods. In this study, kinetic, thermodynamic, and functional metagenomic analyses were conducted to determine the profiles of microbial consortia from Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, incubated at 4°C and 20°C in the presence or absence of the methanogenic inhibitor 2-bromoethanesulfonate. Biogas potential values derived from volumetric analyses indicated that pure biohydrogen (>95.6%) was produced, while also confirming the presence of these consortia adapted to operate with lag phases of 4-7 days and exhibiting temperature sensitivity coefficients (Q10) <2.0 at 4°C. While thermodynamic analysis indicated that methanogenic inhibition theoretically disrupted syntrophic electron transfer and yielded a higher activation energy, both anaerobically fermentative acetic and butyric acid pathways remained exergonic. Community succession was observed in functional metagenomic analyses, marked by the enrichment of fermentative genera (Clostridium, Enterobacter, and Klebsiella) harboring the genetic potential for the pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) and formate hydrogenlyase (FHL) pathways. Metagenomic enrichment for the genes encoding cold-shock defense (cspA, dnaK) and putative electron-bifurcating complexes (rnf, ech) highlights the combined genetic potential to sustain viability and overcome thermodynamic limits at all incubation temperatures. Overall, the biochemical characteristics of native Arctic consortia provide evidence of their potential to serve as viable biocatalysts for biohydrogen production, currently under laboratory batch conditions at low temperatures.IMPORTANCEBiohydrogen production is a potentially sustainable energy source that offers new options for generating carbon-neutral renewable energy. Traditionally, biohydrogen production methods require substantial, continuous heating energy input. This publication describes the examination of the "underutilized" biohydrogen production potential of microbial communities in the Arctic region (Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard) that have separately evolved genetic adaptations necessary to maintain metabolic functions at sub-zero temperatures. Psychrophilic dark-fermentation experiments, combined with thermodynamic modeling and metagenomic analyses, show how unique cold-adapted microorganisms can produce high-purity biohydrogen gas at extreme ambient temperatures under laboratory batch conditions, highlighting a fundamental baseline that could inform future efforts to reduce the energy footprint of biofuel production. While long-term reactor stability and scalability remain to be validated, this work bridges the divide between observational Arctic microbiology and foundational green energy research, demonstrating that the discovery of extreme microbial environments holds promise for developing low-energy biological processes.

articles.title: Global diversification and regional spread of Candidozyma (Candida) auris clades: a comparative genomic epidemiology review of the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific.
articles.abstract: Candidozyma auris (formerly Candida auris), first described in 2009, has spread to 82 countries across 6 continents, with more than 84,000 cumulative colonization and infection cases reported through December 2025. Whole-genome sequencing has resolved the species into six deeply divergent clades (I-VI) that differ geographically and in antifungal susceptibility. This minireview synthesizes peer-reviewed literature and public health surveillance data on whole-genome-sequencing-confirmed clade distribution and susceptibility across the United States, the European Union/European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Latin America and the Caribbean, Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf region, Canada, Singapore, Australia, and New Zealand. Clades I and III are now the most geographically widespread outbreak-associated lineages, documented across nearly every region reviewed. The United States has diversified from early clade I dominance to a four-clade landscape by 2013-2022 (clade I, 56.0%; clade III, 29.4%; clade IV, 14.1%; and clade II, 0.5%). Latin America remains the principal reservoir of clade IV; Saudi Arabia and the Gulf region are dominated by clade I, and the discovery of clade VI in Singapore and Bangladesh illustrates continuing genomic diversification. Clade I carries the highest burden of multidrug and pan-resistance; clade III shows high fluconazole resistance but lower echinocandin resistance; and clade IV, historically associated with lower resistance, is now rising. Because regional antifungal resistance largely reflects clade composition rather than independent regional drift, clade-aware surveillance should directly inform local stewardship, diagnostic inclusivity, and regulatory bridging across markets.

articles.title: Photo Quiz: Nomadic nematode-an unusual cause of diarrhea and respiratory failure.
AI/ML-enabled sepsis prediction systems: laboratory considerations from development to deployment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis prediction algorithms based on machine learning are increasingly embedded in electronic health record systems, and clinical laboratories have been largely absent from their development, validation, and governance. This is a consequential gap. Laboratory variables are central inputs to most deployed sepsis artificial intelligence (AI) tools, and routine analytical events such as platform transitions, reagent reformulations, and reference interval updates can shift the distributions of these inputs. Such distribution shifts are a recognized cause of degraded model performance; however, the effects of laboratory-specific changes remain insufficiently characterized for sepsis tools in clinical use. Neither clinical teams nor laboratories are currently well positioned to detect these effects. This review is written for clinical laboratorians who encounter these tools in practice or are asked to evaluate them for implementation. We describe the data sources used as model inputs and how analytical context, preanalytical variability, and ordering patterns influence model behavior. Five deployed algorithms with real-world implementation evidence are profiled alongside the broader preclinical landscape, including early warning systems, mortality and complication prediction models, and sepsis subtyping research. Development and implementation pitfalls are reviewed with attention to laboratory-specific considerations, and the regulatory and governance landscape is addressed with emphasis on where laboratorian involvement is most needed. Controlled outcomes data supporting currently deployed tools remain limited, and reported performance frequently does not replicate at external sites. Laboratorians bring expertise in analytical quality, data provenance, and change management that is not replicated elsewhere on implementation teams. As the field moves toward sepsis subtyping, continuous monitoring, and local model calibration, laboratorian expertise in analytical quality and monitoring will become increasingly central to how these tools are built, deployed, and maintained.

articles.title: Identification of Microplastics by Calcined Sand Assisted Ambient Laser Desorption Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry.
articles.abstract: Electrospray ionization (ESI) and laser desorption ionization (LDI) exhibit inherent limitations when applied as standalone ion sources for the mass spectrometric analysis of microplastics (MPs). Herein, we report an ambient laser desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry platform, CSAA-LESI-MS, using low-cost, readily available, and eco-friendly calcined sand as the matrix. This system achieves qualitative and quantitative identification of MPs with varied optical and physicochemical characteristics, including strongly and weakly light-absorbing, polar and nonpolar MPs. Efficient ionization of all analyzed polymers was achieved within 1.2 s, affording nanogram-level limits of detection (LODs) and limits of quantification (LOQs) with correlation coefficients (R2) all exceeding 0.98. Seven representative polymer classes, including polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polyamide 6 (PA6), poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET), polylactic acid (PLA), and poly(oxymethylene) (POM), yielded abundant, well-resolved backbone-specific fingerprint spectra. A total of 15 suspected particles were further distinguished successfully by PPMC-based spectral matching against polymer reference libraries. The CSAA-LESI-MS method provides a versatile, economical, and precise ambient mass spectrometry approach feasible for environmental MP analysis.

articles.title: Modeling the Epstein-Barr virus lifecycle in the rabbit.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a human gammaherpesvirus that establishes a lifelong, persistent infection in greater than 90% of people worldwide. EBV has lacked an animal model that depicts the viral lifecycle in B cells and epithelial cells, allows for the investigation of immune responses, and models persistence in a host. EBV establishes a robust infection in immunosuppressed rabbits, resulting in widespread infection of the spleen and the development of splenomegaly. Within the spleen, follicle formation was altered as a result of EBV infection. Similar magnitudes of infection were observed in immunosuppressed rabbits infected with the B95-8 and Akata viral strains. In immunocompetent rabbits, spleen morphology appeared similar to that of mock-infected rabbits. Rabbits infected with B95-8 and Akata viruses developed antibody responses to the EBNA family of proteins in a comparable manner to human infection. Akata infections were more consistent in both the immunosuppressed and immunocompetent studies, whereas B95-8 infections resulted in variable magnitudes of infection and immune responses. The persistence of EBV in rabbits and whether the full lifecycle of EBV in lymphocytes can be replicated remain to be further examined.

IMPORTANCE: The human gammaherpesvirus Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 90% of the global population and is associated with lymphomas and carcinomas. EBV develops a lifelong, persistent infection in its host, avoiding immune detection by limiting the expression of its productive and latency genes. Currently, the EBV field lacks an animal model that can have persistent infection and immune responses to the virus during the course of infection. We demonstrated that rabbits mount an immune response to EBV infection over 6 months and may be a good model of persistent infection, although the viral genome remained below our limit of detection similar to humans.

articles.title: Combined application of Pseudomonas chlororaphis strains and zinc suppresses Alternaria alternata leaf spot in chili pepper.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chili pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) is a vital vegetable crop susceptible to yield loss from Alternaria alternata (Fr.), Keissl., which causes leaf spot/blight and fruit rot. Harnessing beneficial rhizobacteria offers an eco-friendly strategy to enhance plant resilience to biotic stressors. In vitro screening identified Pseudomonas chlororaphis strains viz., P. chlororaphis subsp. aurantiaca (ARS-38) and P. chlororaphis subsp. chlororaphis (RP-4) as potent antifungal strains, inhibiting A. alternata growth by 62% and 64%, respectively. In a zinc (Zn)-amended medium, their antifungal activity increased further, reducing fungal growth by 70% with individual strains and 93% when combined. Microscopy revealed fungal growth inhibition linked to conidia and conidiophore disintegration. In planta under open-field pot conditions, A. alternata infection resulted in 100% disease incidence (DI) and altered histochemical, photosynthetic, and enzyme responses. Treatment with ARS-38 + RP-4 in Zn-amended soil enhanced plant resistance by increasing lignin and phenolic accumulation and reducing enzyme activities, resulting in a 96% reduction in DI. Zinc supplementation improved plant health and enhanced disease suppression when combined with the bacterial strains. Combining rhizobacteria with Zn (2 mg/kg) emerges as a promising strategy to mitigate Alternaria leaf spot disease and enhance biostress tolerance in chili plants.

IMPORTANCE: Biological control offers a sustainable approach for reducing fungal diseases while limiting reliance on chemical fungicides. This study shows that two Pseudomonas chlororaphis strains, ARS-38 and RP-4, combined with low-level zinc supplementation, strongly suppress Alternaria alternata, an important chili pepper pathogen. The combined treatment reduced fungal growth in vitro and substantially decreased disease development in plants while improving structural, physiological, and biochemical responses associated with plant health. The findings demonstrate the potential value of integrating beneficial rhizobacteria with micronutrient supplementation for sustainable disease management and provide a basis for further development of microbial-micronutrient strategies for crop protection.

articles.title: The ESX-2 type VII secretion system is required for Mycobacterium tuberculosis survival under nutrient starvation and for reactivation from dormancy.
articles.abstract: ESX type VII secretion systems of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) export proteins that are essential for bacterial virulence and adaptation to the host. While ESX-1, ESX-3, and ESX-5 have been extensively characterized, the physiological role of ESX-2 and its impact on host-pathogen interactions remain largely unexplored. Experimental evidence suggests that the esx-2 expression is regulated by WhiB5, a transcriptional regulator induced in in vitro nutrient-starvation conditions, and required for Mtb reactivation in the mouse infection model. This study aimed at characterizing the ESX-2 secretion system, with a focus on its role in Mtb adaptation/survival under nutrient-related stress conditions and in virulence. The analysis of the esx-2 gene expression profiles revealed an upregulation of selected esx-2 genes during Mtb cultivation in nutrient-depleted media or upon reactivation from a hypoxia-induced dormancy status. Consistently, the characterization of a panel of Mtb ESX-2 mutant strains (inactivated for selected esx-2 genes encoding ESX-2 components or deleted for the entire esx-2 locus) demonstrated an involvement of ESX-2 in Mtb survival in nutrient starvation and in promoting Mtb growth after reactivation from dormancy. Moreover, the intracellular growth kinetics of ESX-2 mutants in ex vivo models (THP-1 and A549 cells) and their attenuation profiles in the severe combined immunodeficient mice indicated that a functional ESX-2 is required for optimal Mtb replication inside the host. Overall, these findings identify ESX-2 as a modulator of Mtb survival under selected nutrient-starvation-related stress conditions peculiar to intracellular environments, thus contributing to the intracellular and in vivo Mtb growth.IMPORTANCEESX-2 is the second most recently evolved ESX secretion system in mycobacteria, largely conserved in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and other slow-growing pathogenic mycobacteria. Among the ESX secretion systems, ESX-2 is the least extensively characterized, and to date, its function is largely unknown. This study provides novel experimental evidence of the impact of ESX-2 on Mtb physiology and host-pathogen interaction. A functional ESX-2 is required for Mtb survival under hostile conditions, such as nutrient limitation conditions, and is involved in Mtb growth reactivation from a dormant state in vitro. Moreover, the observed role of ESX-2 in promoting Mtb replication in cellular and animal models emphasizes the impact of this secretion system in Mtb adaptation to the human host.

articles.title: Natural variation of hypervirulent Klebsiella pathogenicity loci among Taiwan bloodstream isolates.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major cause of both nosocomial and community-acquired infections, with hypervirulent (hvKP) strains causing severe disease in healthy individuals. In Southeastern Asia, diabetes mellitus is a recognized risk factor for hvKP-associated pyogenic liver abscesses. hvKP virulence is typically attributed to carriage of a large virulence plasmid encoding siderophore biosynthesis (iuc, iro) and mucoid regulator (rmpA, rmpA2) genes. Here, we analyzed 50 bloodstream isolates from Taipei, Taiwan, to investigate genomic and phenotypic characteristics of isolates from patients with or without diabetes mellitus. In diabetic patients and patients with liver abscesses, hvKP biomarkers were found in 66% (n = 33) and 64% (n = 32) of isolates, respectively. While we expected hvKP isolates to be overrepresented in this collection, we observed extensive diversity among hvKP pathogenicity loci, with strains of typical ST23 hvKP lineages carrying incomplete KpVP-1 virulence plasmids. This hvKP biomarker diversity is typically found in classical multidrug-resistant lineages that have acquired portions of the virulence plasmid. Phenotypic assays showed that hvKP biomarkers did not strictly predict hypermucoviscosity, capsule and siderophore production, or survival in serum. Loss of rmpA consistently eliminated hypermucoviscosity and reduced virulence in a murine pneumonia model, whereas aerobactin loss did not. In vivo studies demonstrated variations in virulence that could not be explained solely by differences in the number of hypervirulence-associated loci. These findings highlight the complexity of K. pneumoniae pathogenesis and demonstrate that while canonical biomarkers effectively distinguish hvKP from classical K. pneumoniae, they are insufficient to predict variation in virulence among hvKP strains. Our findings provide insight into the virulence spectrum of strains carrying incomplete plasmid configurations.IMPORTANCEK. pneumoniae poses a global health threat due to the convergence of antimicrobial resistance and hypervirulence. We identified substantial diversity in virulence plasmid content, including incomplete virulence plasmids within archetypal hvKP lineages, and showed that phenotypic and in vivo virulence traits cannot be fully explained by the presence or absence of individual hypervirulence-associated loci. While canonical biomarkers such as rmpA and iuc are widely used to distinguish hypervirulent strains, our analysis demonstrates that no single biomarker is sufficient to reliably predict pathogenic potential and that virulence depends on specific locus combinations and broader context. These findings highlight a critical gap in our understanding of hvKP pathogenesis, underscoring the need for more nuanced frameworks to evaluate virulence. This work has important implications for clinical diagnostics, surveillance, and risk assessment of emerging K. pneumoniae strains worldwide.

articles.title: Seasonal changes of respiratory infections in Northern Finland 2019-2024: evaluation of different diagnostic tests in rapidly changing epidemiological environment.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: In primary health care, respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are one of the major causes of seeking medical attention. Diagnostic RTI laboratory tests provide information for both treating an individual patient as well as more generally epidemiological disease distribution of a given infection. In the case of SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, a diagnostic qPCR assay was rapidly developed in 2020, and the virus-specific test was subsequently incorporated into multiplex PCR tests that also detect other common seasonally occurring viruses, including influenza A and B, and RS-virus. We provide here the data on epidemiological distribution of 23 microbes between 2019 and 2024 in Northern Finland. While coronavirus was the most prominent detected microbe, adenovirus, RS-virus, influenzas, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, and Bordetella pertussis/parapertussis were also commonly detected microbes. The incorporation of multiplex PCR into diagnostics of RTI, particularly in primary health care, will provide more epidemiological data; however, the cost-effectiveness of laboratory tests compared with data availability remains to be clarified.

IMPORTANCE: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are one of the major causes of health care visits. The role of laboratory diagnostics is important, as RTIs have numerous etiological pathogens, and the clinical symptoms may be similar. The distinction between viral and bacterial infections is important to avoid unnecessary antibiotic treatments. The data from RTI testing provide a wide perspective on the epidemiological situation before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic and provides insights into the differences in detection rates between age groups.

articles.title: Impact of doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis on sexually transmitted infections within a statewide community healthcare system.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the impact of doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis (DoxyPEP) prescribing on sexually transmitted infection (STI) incidence proportion in an underserved population receiving care from a statewide community healthcare system.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study was conducted using pharmacy and electronic health records data between 4 May 2021 and 1 April 2025. Primary outcome was the overall STI incidence proportion during 12 months prior to and following DoxyPEP initiation. Secondary outcomes included categorizing bacteria and site-specific STIs and exploring the association between DoxyPEP, preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and STI incidence proportion.

METHODS: Pharmacy dispensing reports and patient demographic information were combined with EHR laboratory-confirmed STI results for review and analysis. Patient data were included if the DoxyPEP prescription was written by an Equitas Health provider and dispensed by the in-house pharmacy, and at least one documented STI test during the 12 months before and after the DoxyPEP initiation. Data were excluded if the prescription originated from an outside provider or was sold after 1 April 2025.

RESULTS: Overall STI incidence proportion decreased from 30.5% preintervention to 17.6% postintervention (P < 0.001) for the 1,111 included patients. Reductions were observed in chlamydia (17.3-3.1%, P < 0.001) and syphilis (3.5-0.6%, P < 0.001), while gonorrhea incidence decreased slightly (16.9-15.2%, P = 0.24). Rectal and urine chlamydia infections experienced the largest decline, and no association was found with PrEP use.

CONCLUSION: DoxyPEP use was associated with a significant reduction in overall STI incidence proportion in a high-risk population, supporting this prevention strategy.

articles.title: Does infection progression of Mycobacterium abscessus depend on sex, age, and mouse strain?
articles.abstract: The lack of a reliable chronic murine model limits drug evaluation against Mycobacterium abscessus. Existing models show discrepancies, especially regarding host factors such as mouse strain, sex, and age. To address this issue, we compared infection establishment and progression in BALB/cJRJ and C57BL/6NCrl mice across sexes and ages using a clinically relevant alginate bead-based model that mimics biofilm-like infection. BALB/cJRJ mice showed more sustained infection and lower variability, with no significant sex- or age-related differences. Based on these results, and taking into account the higher prevalence of nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infections in female patients, as well as practical considerations, 5- to 6-week-old female BALB/cJRJ mice are appropriate for the M. abscessus bead model.IMPORTANCENontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), including Mycobacterium abscessus, are increasingly recognized as opportunistic pathogens in humans. The urgent need for new anti-M. abscessus therapies is hindered by the lack of standardized and reproducible chronic murine infection models, as well as by discrepancies in the literature regarding the influence of host factors (mouse strain, sex, and age). Here, we systematically compared lung infections in the two most commonly used immunocompetent mouse strains, BALB/cJRJ and C57BL/6NCrl, across sexes and two age groups (5-6 vs 8-10 weeks), using the alginate-beads infection model. We identified 5-to 6-week-old female BALB/c mice as the most suitable conditions for implementing the M. abscessus beads model, providing more sustained infection and lower variability. Our findings clarify the impact of host-related variables and provide guidance for improving the standardization and reproducibility of murine models used in preclinical evaluation of anti-NTM therapies.

articles.title: IL-6 Blockade with Clazakizumab is Associated with Low Myeloid Cell Activation and Increased Type 2 Immune Responses in Non-survivors of COVID-19.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: IL-6 inhibitors have been associated with reduced mortality in severe COVID-19 in randomized clinical trials, but the comprehensive immunological impact of IL-6 blockade in the setting of an acute viral infection is poorly understood.

METHODS: To gain insight into the systemic immune response to IL-6 inhibition in COVID-19, we utilized samples from patients who participated in a randomized placebo-controlled trial of clazakizumab, a direct anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody, in severe COVID-19 in the pre-vaccine era. We applied multidimensional measurements of cytokines, chemokines, whole blood transcriptomes, and high-dimensional immune-metabolic flow cytometry to samples before and after treatment to study the changes in immune signatures after IL-6 blockade and to identify pathways associated with positive clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Clazakizumab was associated with a distinct myeloid activation signature and type 2 (T2) cytokine response. Non-survivors who received clazakizumab demonstrated a decoupling of these two clazakizumab-associated phenotypes, exhibiting the most pronounced T2 response coupled with less myeloid activation. Furthermore, elevated baseline levels of the emergency myelopoiesis related cytokine, IL-27, were strongly associated with non-survival after receipt of clazakizumab.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that specific biomarkers may identify patients most likely to benefit from IL-6 blockade and could lead to more personalized applications in COVID-19 and other inflammatory conditions in which IL-6 targeted therapies are in use.

articles.title: An update on novel and included taxa and revised taxonomic status of bacteria isolated from domestic companion and agricultural animals.
articles.abstract: The recognition of novel bacteria continues to expand with the decreased cost and rapid adoption of whole genome sequencing for bacteria. A review of newly identified bacterial species and revisions to bacterial nomenclature from 2025 was performed. New members of families Staphylococcaceae, Streptococcaceae, Actinomycetaceae, Pseudomonadaceae, and Pasteurellaceae were recognized in 2025. While most novel organisms identified in 2025 were isolated from normal microbiota of the skin or gastrointestinal tract of healthy animals, there were some notable new taxa, including Macrococcus psychrotolerans sp. nov., which carries a mecB determinant from Staphylococcus aureus. In addition, Buchananella felis sp. nov., isolated from cases of feline pyothorax, becomes the second member of the genus Buchananella, alongside Buchananella hordeovulneris. Within the gram-negative organisms, a new Pseudomonas species and a novel member of Pasteurellaceae, namely, Rodentibacter abscessus sp. nov. isolated from abscesses in pet hamsters, was recognized. Additions to spiral or curved bacteria included Campylobacter canis sp. nov. and Helicobacter gastrocanis sp. nov. Proposed revisions to seven bacterial taxa are briefly described.

articles.title: Clinical significance of different Histoplasma genotypes in human histoplasmosis: insights from a multicenter study from Québec comparing North American (NAm2) with Latin American (LAmA) isolates.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Histoplasmosis is recognized as endemic in Québec; however, no molecular epidemiological studies have been conducted to date. The clinical significance of identifying Histoplasma capsulatum genotypes remains unclear. We performed a retrospective multicenter study of 67 culture-confirmed histoplasmosis cases from four major academic hospitals in Québec between 1988 and 2014. Multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) was performed on isolates, and clinical data were analyzed for genotype-specific associations with demographics, clinical presentations, and outcomes. Most isolates belonged to either the North American clade 2 (48.1%) or Latin American clade A (39.2%), highlighting both endemic and imported disease patterns in Québec. A novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) was identified, which was unique to Québec and accounted for 61% of the NAm2 isolates, but was not associated with significantly different clinical outcomes compared with other NAm2 strains. In multivariate analysis, disseminated disease was independently associated with immunosuppression (OR 14.18, P = 0.001), male sex (OR 6.01, P = 0.035), and LAmA genotype (OR 5.02, P = 0.031). Severe outcomes (intensive care unit admission, intubation, death, or amphotericin B use) were associated with immunosuppression (OR 4.48, P = 0.023), with a non-significant trend with LAmA infections (OR 3.06, P = 0.069). This first molecular characterization of histoplasmosis infections in Québec suggests a dual epidemiology, with locally acquired NAm2 and LAmA infections more often associated with travel or origin from endemic regions outside Québec. Host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype requires further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

IMPORTANCE: Histoplasmosis is an important dimorphic fungal infection in North America. Although Québec is a recognized endemic region, its molecular epidemiology has not been previously characterized, and the clinical relevance of different Histoplasma genotypes remains uncertain. In this multicenter study, we performed multi-locus sequence typing with detailed clinical data from 67 culture-confirmed cases diagnosed between 1988 and 2014. This represents the first molecular characterization of clinical Histoplasma isolates from Québec and the largest Canadian cohort examining the association between molecular genotypes, clinical presentation, and outcomes. We identified both North American NAm2 (Histoplasma ohiense) and imported Latin American LAmA (Histoplasma suramericanum) lineages, suggestive of a combination of locally acquired and travel-associated infections. We also identified a novel NAm2 sequence type (ST81) that appears unique to Québec, suggesting possible regional circulation. The LAmA genotype was associated with disseminated histoplasmosis, whereas immunosuppression was the principal predictor of severe outcomes. Overall, host factors were associated with disease severity, while the potential contribution of fungal genotype warrants further study. These findings highlight the value of molecular characterization for understanding the epidemiology of histoplasmosis in endemic settings.

articles.title: Geographic source attribution of Salmonella serovar Infantis REPJFX01 through core SNP and phylogeographic analyses.
articles.abstract: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Infantis is globally widespread. Salmonella Infantis REPJFX01 is a persisting multidrug-resistant strain associated with U.S. sporadic illnesses and outbreaks linked to chicken consumption and international travel. Previous work demonstrated that REPJFX01 isolates from the United States and South America are closely related. Here, we expanded that work to show that REPJFX01 isolates are distributed beyond the United States and that distinct single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are associated with certain locations. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that REPJFX01 isolates formed two major groups: (i) a paraphyletic group primarily containing South American and Asian isolates, and (ii) a monophyletic group primarily containing U.S. isolates. We identified one core SNP that can be used to assign REPJFX01-like isolates to the South America/Asia group with 99% sensitivity and 96% specificity. Time-calibrated phylogenetic analysis indicated that the most recent common ancestor of REPJFX01 existed in Peru circa 2009. Phylogeographic analysis suggests that REPJFX01 spread from South America to the United States in a single dissemination event circa 2010. Hence, our results suggest that SNP identification can be used to generate hypotheses on whether an infection with REPJFX01 was acquired domestically or outside of the United States prior to case interviews. Furthermore, identifying potential events leading to the dissemination of REPJFX01 can support the development and deployment of specific public health actions, like enhanced surveillance of imported products.IMPORTANCESalmonella Infantis REPJFX01 is a persisting multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain that has caused thousands of human illnesses in the United States linked to consumption of chicken and international travel. Here, we demonstrate through phylogeographic analyses that REPJFX01 has spread beyond the United States due to three major spread events originating from Peru, the United States, and South Korea. We also identified genetic markers (SNPs) that can be used for fast geographic attribution of new clinical isolates, facilitating prioritization of cluster investigations. Thus, this study indicates that S. Infantis REPJFX01 is a global hazard and highlights the possible role of import and export events in the dissemination of MDR Salmonella across the globe.

articles.title: Sensitivity and specificity of a rapid, point-of-care assay distinguishing bacterial from viral infections in acute care settings.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Differentiating between bacterial and viral infections is essential in the emergency department (ED) to guide appropriate antibiotic treatment. Recent assays, such as the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared MeMed BV assay, can help with this distinction. The MeMed BV assay measures three host immune proteins-Tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-related apoptosis-induced ligand, Interferon (IFN)-γ-induced protein 10, and C-reactive protein-in blood samples. The results are combined into a score from 0 to 100, where a higher score indicates a higher likelihood of a bacterial infection and a lower score suggests a viral infection or other non-bacterial causes. The study evaluates the feasibility of using the MeMed BV assay-generated score to help clinicians decide whether to order blood cultures in emergency departments, as well as assessing the accuracy of the MeMed BV assay in distinguishing between bacterial and viral infections in ED patients. The assay's performance was also compared with standard biomarker tests and white blood cell (WBC) counts for predicting bacterial infections. This study included 203 illness episodes, of which a total of 108 were associated with bacterial infection (25 had a positive blood culture; 107 had a non-blood sample positive for a bacterial pathogen) and 18 were associated with a viral pathogen. Combined, the MeMed BV assay's "high bacterial likelihood" and "moderate bacterial likelihood" scores yielded a sensitivity and specificity of 87% and 32%, respectively, in correctly identifying any bacterial infection; the scores had a sensitivity and specificity of 95% and 25%, respectively, in correctly identifying bacteremia. The future of differentiating between bacterial and viral infections is moving toward integrated diagnostic methods. To address antibiotic resistance, future diagnostics will leverage host immune response biomarkers, advanced molecular panels, and machine learning techniques. This will enable rapid and accurate results at the point of care.

IMPORTANCE: Distinguishing between bacterial and viral infections in healthcare settings can be challenging, as patients often present with similar symptoms and clinical features. In recent years, several new biomarkers have emerged as promising targets for algorithm-based tests designed to differentiate between these types of infections. An increasing number of FDA-approved assays that utilize these biomarkers have entered the market, employing various algorithms. These tests are being used in different clinical settings, such as emergency rooms, to assist clinicians in making accurate diagnoses and prescribing antibiotics appropriately. It is essential for clinicians to correctly order and interpret the results of these assays to fully realize their potential. Our study demonstrates that when such an assay is not used within the FDA-approved context, it does not achieve its full effectiveness.

articles.title: Validation of the 2020 Japanese classification criteria for juvenile dermatomyositis and polymyositis in a pediatric cohort in Japan.
authors: Research Committee on Autoimmune Diseases (Polymyositis/Dermatomyositis Subcommittee), Health and Labour Sciences Research Grant for Intractable Diseases, Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan
articles.abstract:
