Blood pressure, serum and urine biochemistries, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation, in vitro ubiquitination assays, and molecular docking were performed. Klhl3 S486G mice were crossed with Wnk4-/- mice to test WNK4 dependence.

RESULTS: Both knock-in strains exhibited typical PHAII features despite unchanged KLHL3 levels, with enhanced SPAK/OSR1-NCC phosphorylation, increased Cab39 levels, and unchanged WNK1/4 expression. Under high-salt loading, Klhl3 S486 knock-in mice maintained severe PHAII phenotypes, with persistently elevated Cab39 and NCC levels despite decreased WNK4 expression. Critically, Wnk4 deletion failed to rescue PHAII phenotypes in Klhl3 S486G mice, demonstrating that Klhl3 S486 mutations drive PHAII independently of WNK4. In vitro, human KLHL3 S433D/S433G mutations reduced KLHL3-Cab39 association and Cab39 ubiquitination, with a corresponding increase in Cab39 abundance. Deletion mapping identified KLHL3 residues 428 to 437 and Cab39 residues 314 to 324 as key determinants of the KLHL3-Cab39 association.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the integrity of Ser486 itself, rather than its phosphorylation state, is required for KLHL3-mediated Cab39 ubiquitination and define a WNK4-independent PHAII mechanism driven by impaired Cab39 degradation and consequent SPAK/OSR1-Na+-Cl- cotransporter activation.

articles.title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear.

METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants (P≤1×10-4). Cis-expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed.

RESULTS: We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes (C4B, HLA-C, and HLA-DQB1) demonstrated convergent evidence across genome-wide association study, gene regulation, and expression-trait analyses. C4B expression was positively associated with hypertension and systolic blood pressure, while HLA-C showed negative associations with hypertension, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. HLA-DQB1 expression was specifically associated with diastolic blood pressure, suggesting trait-specific effects.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight immune-related pathways as key mediators linking hypertension and preeclampsia. Integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data provides a framework for identifying functionally relevant loci and advancing mechanistic insights into cardiometabolic and pregnancy-related disorders.

articles.title: Effect of Baxdrostat on Cortisol Responsiveness in Hypertension: Phase 2 Results.
An injectable self-healing hydrogel with cytokine-regulating and antioxidant activities for accelerating diabetic wound repair.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds remain a formidable clinical challenge owing to persistent hyperglycemia, excessive oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and protracted inflammation. Herein, we developed a multifunctional hydrogel, designated QCS/4-FPBA/BC, integrating anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, injectable, and self-healing properties. The hydrogel was constructed using a quaternized chitosan (QCS) crosslinked with 4-formylphenylboronic acid (4-FPBA) via dynamic Schiff base and borate ester bonds, conferring favorable injectability and self-healing capacity, while the intrinsic quaternary ammonium cations of QCS endowed it with inherent antibacterial activity. Baicalein-cerium nanoparticles (BC NPs) were further loaded in situ into the hydrogel network to enable efficient and sustained scavenging of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). As a multifunctional platform, the QCS/4-FPBA/BC hydrogel exhibited robust anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophages, as shown by decreased TNF-α and IL-6 levels and increased IL-10 expression. It also influenced macrophage phenotype, reducing the M1-associated iNOS signal while augmenting the M2-associated CD206 signal. In addition, treatment with the hydrogel upregulated VEGF in HUVECs and elevated collagen I in L929 cells, indicating pro-angiogenic and pro-matrix-synthesis capabilities. With these combined attributes, including ROS scavenging, antimicrobial action, inflammatory cytokine rebalancing, and promotion of vascular and fibroblast functions, the QCS/4-FPBA/BC hydrogel offers a comprehensive strategy for diabetic wound management and holds great promise for improving healing outcomes.

articles.title: The art of public engagement in type 1 diabetes research.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Patient and public involvement (PPI) is increasingly recognised as an important component of research, while public engagement provides opportunities to communicate research and stimulate dialogue with wider audiences. In preclinical type 1 diabetes (T1D) research, complex scientific concepts can present particular barriers to engagement across different ages and experiences.

METHODS: We describe two creative public engagement initiatives-a colouring book and a glass art project-and discuss how PPI and lived-experience perspectives helped shape their development.

CONCLUSIONS: These examples illustrate how artistic approaches can make basic science more accessible and create opportunities for dialogue between researchers and people affected by T1D.

articles.title: Oral Health-Related Adverse Events of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As the clinical use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) continues to grow for the management of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal protection, noncirrhotic fatty liver disease, and weight management, their potential implications for oral health need to be considered.

OBJECTIVES: This study examined oral health-related adverse events (AEs) associated with GLP-1 RAs using postmarketing data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

METHODS: FAERS reports for available GLP-1 RAs, exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide, were screened from their initial market introduction through December 2025, identifying 364,274 total AE reports, of which 31,195 (8.6%) involved oral, craniofacial, or dental manifestations.

RESULTS: Tirzepatide, despite being one of the most recently approved GLP-1 RAs, accounted for the highest overall AE volume, and semaglutide demonstrated the largest proportion of oral health-related AEs. A disproportionality analysis revealed a significant drug-specific signal for dry mouth of semaglutide, while vomiting, regurgitation, and reflux-related events produced a significant signal across all 5 drugs. Sensory disorders, including dysgeusia and taste disturbances, also demonstrated significant proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) and reporting odds ratios (RORs) for several GLP-1 RAs. Association analysis of AEs showed significant associations between vomiting and taste disturbances, as well as between dry mouth and dysgeusia, particularly with semaglutide and dulaglutide.

CONCLUSION: This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

articles.title: Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Across Nutritional Status Categories in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Heart Failure: A Secondary Analysis of the PANDA II Trial.
Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.

METHODS: A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

articles.title: Immune cell phenotypes across tissues in people with HIV.
articles.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes our current understanding of immune cell phenotypes across human tissues in the context of HIV infection, with particular emphasis on insights from postmortem studies.

RECENT FINDINGS: Rapid autopsy cohorts enable systematic collection of multiple anatomical sites within hours of death, including tissues inaccessible during life. Together with biopsy studies, these approaches have revealed tissue-specific phenotypes and functions of HIV-susceptible cells, of long-lived HIV reservoir cells that are the main barrier to cure, and of CD8+ T cells and NK cells as effectors that can recognize and eliminate HIV-infected cells.

SUMMARY: Immune cell phenotypes relevant to HIV susceptibility, persistence, and antiviral control diverge across anatomical sites and differ substantially from their counterparts in peripheral blood.

articles.title: The use of glucagon-like peptide-1 agonists as a treatment for obesity in older people: risks and benefits.
articles.journal: Current opinion in clinical nutrition and metabolic care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Obesity is an increasingly important health problem in older adults (≥65 years) and is associated with osteoarthritis, impaired mobility, reduced quality of life, cardiovascular disease, and other age-related comorbidities. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the benefits and risks of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) therapy in older adults.

RECENT FINDINGS: GLP-1 RAs, initially developed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), have emerged as effective pharmacological options for weight reduction and cardiovascular risk reduction. Studies suggest that GLP-1 RAs have clinically meaningful weight loss in older adults, with efficacy comparable to that observed in younger populations. In addition, selected GLP-1 RAs have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits, including reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which may be particularly relevant in older individuals with a high burden of cardiovascular disease. Nevertheless, several concerns should be considered before treatment initiation, including gastrointestinal intolerance, sarcopenia-related muscle loss, ophthalmologic complications, and hypoglycaemia when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas. Furthermore, polypharmacy and age-related physiological changes may increase the likelihood of clinically relevant drug interactions.

SUMMARY: Current evidence indicates that GLP-1 RAs may represent a valuable therapeutic option for carefully selected older adults, particularly those with severe obesity and cardiometabolic comorbidities.

articles.title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS-Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)-mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS-eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non-canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD-knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS-mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of pulsed field ablation of atrial fibrillation: a primer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Catheter ablation is increasingly used as a primary or first-line rhythm-control strategy in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging catheter ablation modality that offers comparable clinical effectiveness as thermal ablation whilst avoiding safety events related to thermal injury and improving procedural efficiency. PFA may be associated with increased equipment costs. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEA) help inform adoption of newer technologies such as PFA within healthcare systems with limited resources.

RECENT FINDINGS: Accordingly, our review provides a primer for CEA and examines the evidence for PFA. Recent studies have demonstrated that PFA is at least as effective as conventional thermal ablation (radiofrequency or cryoballoon) in treating AF and may be an effective first-line rhythm control therapy. PFA is associated with shorter procedural times which increases throughput and may help to offset higher equipment costs.

SUMMARY: Preliminary work suggests that PFA is likely cost-effective but findings must be interpreted with caution as there are a limited number of CEA and follow-up was generally limited to 1 year post ablation. Additional CEA across healthcare jurisdictions with longer time horizons are required to confirm these findings and may inform uptake of PFA.

articles.title: K-MIMIC and the next stage of multimodal critical care data.
Relationships between technology addiction, musculoskeletal discomfort, and life satisfaction among university students: A cross-sectional analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe rapid integration of technology into daily life has raised concerns about physical and psychosocial health. Problematic smartphone and internet use may coexist with prolonged static postures and musculoskeletal discomfort among university students.ObjectiveTo examine the relationships of smartphone and internet addiction with academic performance, musculoskeletal discomfort, life satisfaction, and health-related quality of life among university students.MethodsThis descriptive cross-sectional study began in 2020 and included 473 university students (258 males, 215 females). Validated questionnaires assessed smartphone and internet addiction, musculoskeletal discomfort, health-related quality of life, and life satisfaction. Grade point average was recorded. Descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlations were used.ResultsSmartphone and internet addiction scores showed weak and negligible positive correlations with musculoskeletal discomfort, respectively (r = 0.111 and r = 0.091). Both scores were weakly associated with poorer health-related quality of life. Internet addiction scores were weakly associated with lower life satisfaction; the association for smartphone addiction scores was not statistically significant. Neither score was significantly associated with grade point average.ConclusionHigher smartphone and internet addiction scores were associated with greater musculoskeletal discomfort and poorer health-related quality of life, although the associations were small.

articles.title: The Cohered GP Training Model: A systematic review and complexity-informed synthesis of general practice training.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: General practice (GP) training is central to the development of the primary care workforce but is often described as a bounded educational programme rather than a process shaped by clinical work, workplace culture, and wider service conditions.

AIM: To examine how GP training is represented in the literature and to develop a complexity-informed conceptual model of GP training.

DESIGN AND SETTING: Systematic review and complexity-informed synthesis of studies relating to GP training in primary care contexts.

METHOD: Empirical and conceptual studies were identified through systematic searching and analyzed using thematic synthesis, informed by complex adaptive systems and Cohered Emergent Theory.

RESULTS: Three thematic areas were identified: GP-patient interactions, GP-professional interactions, and training intricacies. Four cross-cutting insights emerged: complexity in everyday training, the influence of power and hierarchy, the importance of diversity and adaptability, and the shaping role of wider system pressures. These informed the Cohered GP Training Model, which conceptualizes GP training as a dynamic system in which outcomes emerge from the degree of coherence between trainee formation, educational relationships, patient care encounters, workplace and team ecology, and the wider primary care system.

CONCLUSION: GP training is best understood as a relational and system-embedded process rather than a discrete educational intervention. The model may help explain variation in training quality across settings and offers a conceptual basis for improving training environments and workforce development.

articles.title: Bacteroides fragilis Enterotoxin Activates NLRP3 Inflammasomes through NF-κB Signaling and Mitophagy Suppression in Intestinal Epithelial Cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF) induces acute and chronic inflammatory pathology through its toxic factor B. fragilis enterotoxin (BFT). Although inflammasomes are critical for maintaining intestinal homeostasis and modulating inflammation, their roles remain poorly characterized during ETBF infection. This study investigated the pathways involved in inflammasome formation in BFT-exposed intestinal epithelial cells (IECs).

METHODS: Human colon epithelial cells HCT-116 and CCD 841 CoN were used as IEC models. To investigate inflammasome formation and activation, BFT-treated cells were analyzed by immunoblotting, disuccinimidyl suberate cross-linking, immunofluorescence microscopy, colocalization assays, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

RESULTS: BFT stimulation significantly upregulated the expression of NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3), pro-interleukin (IL)-1β, pro-IL-18, and cleaved caspase-1 in both cell lines. Inflammasome complexes were confirmed by apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC) oligomerization and colocalization of ASC with NLRP3, accompanied by increased IL-1β and IL-18 secretion. Two pathways were involved in inflammasome activation: first, nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling regulated NLRP3, pro-IL-1β, and pro-IL-18 expression, promoting caspase-1 activation; second, p53/BAG5 axis activation suppressed Parkin-mediated mitophagy and drove reactive oxygen species accumulation, engaging the inflammasome complex.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that the formation of inflammasomes may occur via two pathways, namely, NF-κB-mediated signaling and p53/BAG5-associated suppression of mitophagy.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of mirror therapy using different delivery media on motor recovery of the upper limb and hand in stroke patients: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare the effects of mirror therapy delivered through different media on upper limb and hand motor recovery in stroke patients using a network meta-analysis.Data sourcesFive electronic databases were searched from inception to 7 September 2026.Review methodsMethodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2.0). A Bayesian framework was applied for network meta-analysis, and evidence quality was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.ResultsThirty trials involving 1212 participants were included, covering three mirror therapy modalities. Network meta-analysis showed that, compared with control group, virtual reality-based mirror therapy (mean difference [MD] = 8.75; 95% credible interval [CrI]: 4.56 to 13.30), digital screen-based mirror therapy (MD = 6.95; 95% CrI: 3.18 to 10.48), and traditional mirror therapy (MD = 5.29; 95% CrI: 2.58 to 7.70) significantly improved upper limb motor function. For hand motor function, virtual reality-based mirror therapy was superior to the control group (MD = 4.65; 95% CrI: 1.06 to 8.16) and traditional mirror therapy (MD = 3.77; 95% CrI: 0.54 to 7.14). Virtual reality-based mirror therapy consistently ranked as the most effective intervention. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.ConclusionVirtual reality-based mirror therapy showed the most favourable exploratory effect estimates, but the relative efficacy of different delivery media remains uncertain because most comparisons were indirect and the certainty of evidence for hand motor function was very low. Head-to-head trials are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: HGVD: Human Genetic Variation Database update 2026 with sequencing of 4344 genetically diverse Japanese individuals.
articles.abstract: Population-scale genome resources remain biased toward European ancestry, limiting variant interpretation in underrepresented populations. Here, we expanded the Human Genetic Variation Database (HGVD), a free Japanese allele-frequency resource launched in 2013. HGVD v3.1 integrates 1209 exomes with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 3135 Japanese individuals selected by principal component analysis (PCA) to span genetic diversity, providing aggregate variant statistics for 4344 individuals, 3248 genotyped individuals, and expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) from 300 individuals. For research and clinical use, HGVD provides coordinated JBrowse-based browsers for GRCh37/hg19, GRCh38/hg38, and T2T-CHM13. The non-GRCh37 variant tracks were generated by liftOver from the GRCh37 call set. Variant frequencies, sample counts, and coverage are available across assemblies, whereas eQTL annotations are currently available only on hg19. A downloadable, graph-genome-ready structural-variant release is provided, and the new pathSTR portal reports population-level distributions for 68 medically relevant tandem-repeat loci, derived by applying STRdust to long-read Oxford Nanopore data from 1019 individuals of the 1000 Genomes Project remapped to T2T-CHM13. HGVD v3.1 supports population-matched interpretation of rare pathogenic and pharmacogenomic variants, comparison of repeat-expansion alleles with long-read reference distributions, and structural-variant-aware reference construction, supporting precision medicine for Japan and East Asian populations. HGVD is available at https://www.hgvd.genome.med.kyoto-u.ac.jp/.

articles.title: One Household, Two Emotional Worlds: An Exploratory Dyadic Study of Social Participation After Stroke.
Serum secretome signatures for risk of hepatocellular carcinoma and fibrosis progression in chronic liver diseases in the U.S.
Long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes in type 2 diabetes: final results of the prospective DM-FibroScan Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: International guidelines recommend routine liver assessment in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the long-term clinical implications remain unclear. We aimed to characterise the long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes across the vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) spectrum in T2D.

METHODS: The prospective DM-FibroScan Study consecutively enrolled adults with T2D in Hong Kong during 2013-2014. Baseline controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) were assessed.

RESULTS: 1,862 patients were followed for a median of 11.9 years (interquartile range 11.5-12.1). The 10-year cumulative incidence of liver-related events (LREs) was 1.1% (95% CI 0.7-1.7), lower than those of all cause mortality (21.1% [19.2-22.9]), cardiovascular events (12.5% [11.0-14.2]), malignancies (9.7% [8.3-11.1]), and end-stage kidney disease (9.0% [7.7-10.3]). Most participants (84.2%) had baseline LSM <10 kPa and a low LRE incidence (0.4 [0.1-0.8] per 1,000 person-years), with cardiovascular events predominated (14.1 [12.2-16.2] per 1,000 person-years). Patients with LSM >15 kPa (5.3%) exhibited a markedly higher LRE incidence (12.2 [6.1-21.8] per 1,000 person years), approaching the incidences of malignancies and ESKD. LRE incidence per 1,000 person-years was 1.9 in patients with LSM regression (≥10 to <10 kPa) and 28.0 in those with persistently elevated LSM. Patients with elevated baseline LSM also showed higher incidences of extrahepatic outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: LREs were relatively uncommon in the overall T2D population but increased substantially with advanced fibrosis. This study provides natural history data across the VCTE spectrum in a relatively unselected T2D cohort and supports integrating fibrosis assessment into routine T2D care.

articles.title: O-GlcNAcylation of GSDMD promotes mitochondrial dysfunction and hepatocyte injury in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Cell-membrane gasdermin D (GSDMD) plays a key role as a pyroptosis executor of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). However, the mitochondrial translocation of GSDMD occurs even during the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver (MASL) phase, which involves mainly hepatic steatosis without tremendous inflammatory responses or sustainable hepatic cell death; the underlying mechanism is unknown. We investigated the role of GSDMD in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

METHODS: Liver tissues from patients with MASLD and control subjects were obtained to evaluate GSDMD expression and distribution. GSDMD△hep mice and their floxed littermate controls, GSDMDfl/fl mice, were fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet (HFHCD) for 4 and 12 weeks to develop MASL or MASH, respectively. Additionally, GSDMD△hep mice were administered an adeno-associated virus 8 (AAV8) vector expressing wild-type GSDMD (GSDMD-WT) or GSDMD O-GlcNAcylation site mutants (GSDMD-T174/S178A) and were provided with an HFHCD or a methionine-choline-deficient diet.

RESULTS: GSDMD expression and mitochondrial translocation were increased in patients and experimental mice with MASLD. The translocation of GSDMD-NT to mitochondria impaired the mitochondrial membrane potential and promoted the leakage of cytochrome c and mitochondrial DNA, thus inducing early hepatocyte apoptosis, and was required for pyroptosis in MASLD. O-GlcNAcylation at T173/T175 (in humans) or T174/S178 (in mice) of GSDMD was responsible for GSDMD mitochondrial translocation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Targeting O-GlcNAcylation with Celecoxib suppressed GSDMD mitochondrial translocation and the development of MASLD.

CONCLUSIONS: Targeting mitochondrial GSDMD-mediated programed cell death (PCD) pathways may provide new insights into the potential theoretical basis for MASLD interventions.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and adverse outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic viral hepatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are a novel class of anti-diabetic drugs that can treat obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). T2D and chronic viral hepatitis (CVH) frequently coexist and worsen liver and non-liver outcomes, but effective pharmacological therapies are limited. We aimed to evaluate the effect of GLP-1RA on liver and non-liver complications among patients with T2D and CVH in the United States.

METHODS: Patients with T2D and CVH initiating GLP-1RA were included (2013-2022) in Merative™ Marketscan® Research Databases. Primary outcomes included (1) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhosis, and (2) cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and non-liver cancer. Cox proportional hazards models were conducted to estimate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).

RESULTS: A total of 9,499 patients with T2D and CVH were included after 1:4 propensity score matching. Compared with non-GLP-1RA (N=7,366), GLP-1RA use (N=2,133) was associated with significantly lower risks of any liver-related outcomes (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.57-0.87; P=0.001), HCC (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.93; P=0.028), cirrhosis (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.56-0.86; P<0.001), CKD (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53-0.84; P<0.001). A trend toward a lower risk of CVD (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66-1.03; P=0.089) and non-liver cancer (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53-1.01; P=0.055) was observed among GLP-1RA users, although the association did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and CKD among patients with T2D and CVH, with nonsignificant trends toward lower risks of CVD and non-liver cancer.

articles.title: Catheter-related complications in children with burns: A retrospective clinical study on 103 central venous access devices.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Central venous access devices (CVADs) are often indispensable for treating burns in children. Early and late complications related to CVAD placement may result in prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity and mortality, and increased cost of care.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study describes catheter-related outcomes in children with burns who underwent CVAD insertion and were managed with standardized insertion and maintenance practices. The primary outcome was the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI), expressed per 1000 catheter days.

RESULTS: A total of 103 CVADs in 81 patients admitted to our pediatric burn unit (mean age 5.1 years, mean TBSA 22.3%) were analyzed: 39 centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs), 47 femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs), and 17 peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs). All CVADs were non-valved, non-cuffed, power-injectable polyurethane catheters; 84.5% were tunneled. The median dwell time was 18.3 days, for a total of 1883 catheter days. The incidence of CRBSI was 1.1 episodes per 1000 catheter days. Unscheduled removal due to catheter-related complications occurred in 11.7% of CVADs. No symptomatic catheter-related thrombosis was reported.

CONCLUSIONS: In children undergoing CVAD placement as a part of burn care, catheter-related complications were infrequent in this cohort managed with a standardized insertion and maintenance approach. These descriptive findings could serve as a basis for future prospective studies.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of CagriSema in Type 2 Diabetes: A Dose- and Comparator-Specific Systematic Review and Bayesian Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CagriSema combines cagrilintide with semaglutide and may improve glycaemic control and body weight in Type 2 diabetes. We evaluated its dose- and comparator-specific efficacy and safety.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Analyses were stratified by CagriSema dose and comparator. For HbA1c and body weight, efficacy/trial-product estimands were aligned where sufficiently reported, with treatment-policy estimates examined in sensitivity analyses. Bayesian random-effects models generated posterior medians and 95% credible intervals (CrIs).

RESULTS: Six trials representing 4554 potentially eligible participants with Type 2 diabetes were included. Compared with placebo, CagriSema 2.4 mg produced between-group differences of -1.87 percentage points in HbA1c (95% CrI, -2.08 to -1.62) and -12.69 percentage points in percentage body-weight change (95% CrI, -13.78 to -11.61). Versus semaglutide 2.4 mg, the additional HbA1c reduction was modest and uncertain (-0.21 percentage points; 95% CrI, -0.62 to 0.11), whereas additional body-weight reduction remained probable (-5.84 percentage points; 95% CrI, -10.08 to -2.15). Gastrointestinal adverse events and adverse-event-related discontinuation were increased versus placebo (RR, 2.27 [95% CrI, 1.81 - 3.00] and 3.16 [1.50 to 6.87], respectively), while estimates versus semaglutide were less precise.

CONCLUSIONS: CagriSema provides substantial glycaemic and body-weight benefits versus placebo. Its incremental advantage over dose-matched semaglutide is more evident for body-weight reduction, while comparative gastrointestinal tolerability and discontinuation risk remain uncertain.

articles.title: Are high flow arteriovenous fistulas necessary?
articles.abstract: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access for haemodialysis but may develop excessive flow. High-flow arteriovenous fistulas (HFAs) are common in practice, although their prevalence is difficult to establish because definitions and management strategies remain inconsistent. HFAs are associated with systemic complications, including high-output cardiac failure, left ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary hypertension and local complications including ischaemia, dialysis inefficiency, aneurysmal degeneration and venous stenosis or occlusion. Assessment and management remain poorly defined, particularly in patients with mild or subclinical disease. This narrative review provides an updated overview of the definition, pathophysiology, clinical consequences, assessment and management of HFAs, with particular emphasis on continuing areas of uncertainty.

articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life.

METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.title: α-Hydroxybutyrate and Cardiovascular Outcomes in People Living With Type 2 Diabetes: An EXSCEL Post Hoc Analysis.
Artificial intelligence early-warning systems for sepsis: From risk scores to bedside action.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundSepsis remains a leading cause of preventable mortality in critical care. Timely recognition is essential for effective bundle-based management, and artificial intelligence-enabled early-warning systems (AI-EWS) may facilitate earlier detection by converting electronic health record and bedside monitoring data into actionable risk estimates.ObjectiveThis review aimed to synthesize recent advances in the development, validation, and real-world deployment of AI-EWS for sepsis and to identify the factors that determine their clinical benefit at the unit level.MethodsWe conducted a structured narrative review based on a targeted search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar from database inception to December 2025. Search terms combined artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning with sepsis and early-warning score or prediction. Priority was given to studies addressing prospective performance, clinical implementation, alert fatigue, workflow integration, governance, and regulation.ResultsAI-EWS may identify sepsis risk earlier than traditional scoring systems; however, retrospective discrimination alone does not ensure clinical benefit. Effective deployment depends on prospective calibration, site-specific threshold setting, precision-recall trade-offs, manageable alert budgets, and integration with nurse-centered workflows, standardized order sets, escalation pathways, and feedback loops. Major implementation risks include alert fatigue, data drift, and limited transportability. Silent-mode trials, group-aware recalibration, regular calibration and drift audits, throttle and rollback rules, and auditable change logs can help mitigate these risks.ConclusionAI-EWS should be evaluated as clinical interventions rather than solely as predictive models. Calibrated risk communication, unit-specific operating points, human-centered workflow integration, and accountable governance are essential for achieving safe, equitable, and measurable improvements in sepsis care.

articles.title: Clinical and molecular dynamics during the resolution of human experimental gingivitis: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This scoping review evaluates the recovery pattern of host responses, in terms of immune regulation and tissue remodeling, in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) during experimental gingivitis (EG) resolution phase.

METHODS: Electronic database and hand searches were conducted to screen the literature published from January 1960 to December 2024. The selected studies were randomized and non-randomized controlled trials evaluating the changes of clinical parameters and host responses in GCF mediators during EG, focusing on the baseline and the resolution phase. Due to the heterogeneity of the included studies, a meta-analysis was not conducted. Evidence quality and risk of bias were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 17 studies with 303 volunteers met the inclusion criteria, analyzing four clinical parameters and 58 biomarkers in GCF samples. Pro-inflammatory cytokines and mediators associated with tissue remodeling, such as IL-1α, IL-1β, MMP-8, and ALP increased during EG induction and decreased during EG resolution, similar to the trends in the clinical parameters. In contrast, the levels of MIP-1β and IL-10 were reduced during EG induction and elevated during EG resolution. In addition, the levels of IL-1β and ALP were able to return to baseline level at the end of the resolution phase.

CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review showed that, following an average EG resolution period of 7 to 21 days, clinical signs of inflammation improved or restored. Notably, IL-1β and ALP exhibited a return of levels to their pre-disease (baseline) state, suggesting their potential as indicators for monitoring dynamic changes in inflammatory status at the molecular level during EG resolution.

articles.title: Conditional Associations of ApoB and LDL-C With Incident Type 2 Diabetes in UK Biobank: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Although closely correlated, apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects atherogenic particle number, whereas low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) measures cholesterol carried by LDL particles. We examined whether their associations with incident Type 2 diabetes (T2D) diverged after accounting for each other.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included UK Biobank participants recruited in 2006-2010 without identified baseline diabetes. ApoB and LDL-C were assessed in baseline blood samples, and incident T2D was ascertained through 19 December 2022. Cause-specific Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) per 10 mg/dL higher concentration. Primary models used the same participants and nonlipid covariates, with each biomarker entered individually and both entered in one model. Additional analyses assessed combined metabolic adjustment and time-varying associations.

RESULTS: Among 402 144 participants followed for 5.33 million person-years, 16 537 developed T2D. ApoB and LDL-C were highly correlated (r = 0.958). When modelled individually, HRs per 10 mg/dL were 1.059 (95% CI: 1.052-1.066) for apoB and 1.018 (95% CI: 1.013-1.023) for LDL-C. When included together, summary HRs over the full follow-up were 1.502 (95% CI: 1.468-1.537) for apoB and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.745-0.772) for LDL-C. Combined cardiometabolic and HbA1c adjustment attenuated both conditional associations, with HRs of 1.151 (95% CI: 1.122-1.181) for apoB and 0.890 (0.873-0.908) for LDL-C. Time-varying HRs at Years 1 and 10 were 1.658 and 1.464 for apoB, and 0.691 and 0.777 for LDL-C, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher apoB at a given LDL-C was associated with a higher hazard of incident T2D, whereas higher LDL-C at a given apoB was associated with a lower hazard.

articles.title: Effect of Roy Adaptation Model-Based Patient Education on Self-Efficacy, Immunosuppressive Therapy Adherence, and Adaptation to Chronic Disease in Patients With Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global health challenge requiring strict medication adherence to prevent complications. The Roy Adaptation Model (RAM) provides a nursing framework to guide patients toward holistic adaptation during this process.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to examine the effect of RAM-based patient education on self-efficacy, immunosuppressive adherence, and adaptation to chronic disease in patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy.

METHODS: The quasi-experimental study included 78 patients (39 intervention and 39 control) comprising new renal transplant recipients and patients with CKD initiating immunosuppressive therapy for the first time at a university hospital. The intervention group received individualized education based on the RAM's 4 adaptation modes, supported by an educational booklet, while the control group received routine care. Data were collected at baseline, 1, and 3 months. Self-efficacy, medication adherence, and adaptation to chronic disease were measured using validated instruments.

RESULTS: RAM-based education was associated with significant improvements in all primary outcomes compared to the control group (with effect sizes of ηp2 = 0.19 for adherence, ηp2 = 0.72 for adaptation, and ηp2 = 0.12 for self-efficacy; P < .05). Medication adherence in the intervention group improved over time. Significant effect sizes were observed in all sub-dimensions of disease adaptation and self-efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: Educational interventions grounded in the RAM appear to support treatment adherence, self-efficacy, and adaptation in kidney patients. Integrating the RAM into nursing practice may offer a structured framework for patient-centered care, may assist in chronic disease management, and may support patients' active engagement in care.
