Artificial intelligence in upper-limb, language and cognitive neurorehabilitation after stroke.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being increasingly integrated into upper-limb, language and cognitive neurorehabilitation research and there is interest in where the research currently lies along the pipeline towards clinical implementation and real-world impact.

RECENT FINDINGS: Across these three domains of neurorehabilitation, the research into the use of AI has shown clear potential to enhance assessment, personalize rehabilitation and extend access to care but is yet to demonstrate clinical utility and superiority over other digital rehabilitation approaches. There remain concerns about small and selective datasets being used for modelling, privacy and equity issues and sustainable implementation. It is suggested that AI should be positioned as an important tool in the clinical infrastructure rather than an autonomous clinical decision maker within clinical practice.

SUMMARY: Future research across these neurorehabilitation domains should consider implementation risks and needs early in the research pipeline, by using ethical principles and guidelines to ensure transparency and consumer involvement in AI research and implementation into clinical practice.

articles.title: FXIa inhibitors and secondary stroke prevention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke face a substantial residual risk of recurrence despite antiplatelet therapy, while conventional anticoagulation is unsuitable due to an unacceptably high bleeding risk. Activated factor XI (FXIa) inhibition promises anticoagulant efficacy while sparing hemostasis. We appraise the evidence of FXIa-inhibitors in secondary stroke prevention considering the pivotal OCEANIC-STROKE trial.

RECENT FINDINGS: Phase-2 trials of asundexian and milvexian were reassuring on safety but neutral on imaging-based endpoints, establishing that covert infarcts are a poor surrogate. In the phase-3 OCEANIC-STROKE trial, asundexian added to single or dual antiplatelet therapy reduced recurrent ischemic stroke by 26%, consistently across subtypes, without any excess of major bleeding or intracranial hemorrhage. By contrast, asundexian was inferior to apixaban in atrial fibrillation, a result attributable to dose, comparator, and setting. Consistent with this, the monoclonal antibody abelacimab, which achieves near-complete FXIa-inhibition, reduced bleeding relative to rivaroxaban in atrial fibrillation, though its effect on thromboembolic events has not been established.

SUMMARY: FXIa-inhibition is the first anticoagulant strategy preventing recurrent stroke after noncardioembolic ischemic stroke without a bleeding penalty. Confirmation of a class effect from further trials is awaited, alongside questions of duration, deeper inhibition, and use in other cardiovascular indications.

articles.title: Fasting triglyceride-glucose index and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: an observational study of metabolic risk in singleton pregnancies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the fasting TyG index and gestational hypertension/preeclampsia (GH/PE) in singleton pregnancies.

METHODS: This observational study included 175 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies examined during routine antenatal care between 11 and 35 weeks of gestation from January 2023 to December 2024. Women with pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, renal disease, gestational diabetes mellitus or major systemic disorders were excluded. Clinical, anthropometric and fasting biochemical data were collected, and the TyG index was calculated as ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed.

RESULTS: Thirty-nine women (22.3 %) developed GH/PE. Compared with women with physiological pregnancies, women with GH/PE had higher pre-gestational BMI, gestational weight change, blood pressure, fasting glucose, triglycerides and TyG index values (all p≤0.018). The TyG index correlated positively with mean arterial pressure (r=0.20, p=0.027) and gestational week at assessment (r=0.35, p<0.001). Higher TyG index values were associated with increased odds of GH/PE (OR=3.75, 95 % CI 1.79-7.85). A TyG cut-off of 8.6 showed 58.97 % sensitivity and 69.85 % specificity, with an AUC of 0.69 (95 % CI 0.59-0.79).

CONCLUSIONS: In this antenatal cohort, the fasting TyG index was associated with GH/PE and showed moderate discriminatory ability. The TyG index should not be used as a stand-alone diagnostic test, but it may complement BMI and routine clinical assessment in identifying women with increased metabolic susceptibility to hypertensive pregnancy disorders.

articles.title: Clinical prediction models: from foundational concepts to practical application.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical prediction requires formalizing uncertainty into a statistical model. However, persistent confusion between prediction and inference, and between traditional (stepwise) and modern (penalized) development strategies, leads to unstable, poorly calibrated, and overfit models. A structured statistical framework is essential.

METHODS: This article is a structured, didactic tutorial that explains the core concepts of clinical prediction models. It covers the definition of a prediction model, the fundamental strategies for its construction, and the essential framework for its evaluation, illustrated through an applied example using real-world clinical data.

RESULTS: The tutorial illustrates model development using the GUSTO-I dataset (n=40,830). Penalized methods (LASSO [Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator] and Elastic Net) retained established clinical predictors and shrank the two independently generated synthetic noise variables to zero in this worked example. The LASSO model (λ1SE) achieved strong discrimination (AUC 0.818; 95 % CI: 0.803-0.832), with a Brier score of 0.058. Calibration analysis revealed a slope of 1.28, indicating underdispersion of predicted risks consistent with the stronger shrinkage applied at λ1SE in this worked example. Calibration-in-the-large was 0.011 on the logit scale, indicating negligible average-level miscalibration. Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit than the default strategies at all evaluated thresholds from 0.02 to 0.50.

CONCLUSIONS: This guide equips clinicians with a rigorous methodological framework for the critical appraisal and interpretation of modern clinical prediction models.

articles.title: [Effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with autoimmune hepatitis and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease].
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease. Methods: Patients with autoimmune liver diseases (AILD) [including AIH, primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), and overlap syndrome] complicated with coronary heart disease who underwent PCI at Tianjin Medical University Second Hospital between January 2019 and December 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, they were divided into mycophenolate mofetil group and non-mycophenolate mofetil group according to postoperative use of mycophenolate mofetil, and followed up until March 31, 2026 to compare the baseline characteristics of the two groups of patients. Firth penalized likelihood-corrected Cox regression models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with all-cause death as the competing event) were used to evaluate the association between mycophenolate mofetil use and ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease (because few patients with PBC and PSC received mycophenolate mofetil, this analysis only included patients with AIH and overlap syndrome). The Benjamini-Hochberg method was applied for multiple comparison correction to calculate the FDR q values. A 1∶1 propensity score matching (PSM) was employed to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot survival curves to compare the ISR-free survival rates. Sensitivity analysis was performed on all AILD patients to validate the robustness of the results. Results: A total of 172 patients with AILD complicated with coronary heart disease were enrolled, including 48 cases (27.9%) in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 124 cases (72.1%) in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The follow-up duration [M(Q1, Q3)] was 13 (7, 16) and 10 (5, 16) months respectively. The proportion of patients with hyperlipidemia [12.5% (6/48) vs 32.3% (40/124), P=0.009] and diabetes mellitus [8.3% (4/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.007] were lower in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group, while the proportion of patients with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP)>0.8 mg/L [47.9% (23/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.010], previous use of prednisone [79.2% (38/48) vs 22.6% (28/124), P<0.001] and azathioprine [54.2% (26/48) vs 9.7% (12/124), P<0.001] were higher than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [59.5 (35.5, 76.8) vs 43.0 (32.0, 52.7) U/L, P=0.002] and immunoglobulin G (IgG) [19.6 (15.0, 26.0) vs 15.2 (14.0, 16.8) g/L, P=0.006] were higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group. Among 100 patients with AIH and overlap syndrome (82 and 18 cases, respectively), mycophenolate mofetil use was associated with a reduced risk of ISR in both Firth-corrected Cox regression model and competing risk model (Firth-corrected Cox model: HR=0.17, 95%CI: 0.04-0.51, FDR q=0.004; competing risk model: sHR=0.14, 95%CI: 0.05-0.43, FDR q=0.003). After PSM (40 cases in each group), there was no statistically significant difference in all covariates between the two groups (all SMD<0.1). After PSM, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that the follow-up duration was 12 (7, 15) months in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 8 (3, 17) months in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The 12-month ISR-free survival rate was higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group (97.0% vs 64.5%, P<0.001). In the sensitivity analysis, mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR (Firth-corrected Cox regression model: HR=0.29, 95%CI: 0.09-0.73, FDR q=0.030; competing risk model: sHR=0.26, 95%CI: 0.10-0.72, FDR q=0.022). Conclusion: Mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease.

articles.title: [Analysis of the disease remission outcomes and the associated factors of deep remission in patients with Crohn disease receiving ustekinumab therapy].
articles.abstract: Objectives: To analyze the disease remission outcomes and the associated factors of deep remission in patients with Crohn disease (CD) receiving ustekinumab (UST) therapy. Methods: The clinical data of patients with active CD who underwent UST therapy at the Department of Gastroenterology, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between January 2021 and January 2026 were retrospectively collected. After the first intravenous induction therapy with UST (6 mg/kg), the patients received routine subcutaneous maintenance therapy (90 mg), and optimized therapy (including shortening the dosing interval or adjusting the drug) was performed in those patients with poor early response or secondary loss of response during follow-up. At week 44 of therapy, clinical remission [Harvey-Bradshaw index (HBI)≤4 scores], mucosal healing [simplified endoscopic score for Crohn disease (SES-CD)≤2 scores or absence of ulcers], and transmural healing (bowel wall thickness≤3 mm, normalized blood flow signal, clear bowel wall stratification, and absence of mesenteric fat hypertrophy) were evaluated, and simultaneous achievement of the above three criteria was defined as deep remission. The clinical remission rate, mucosal healing rate, transmural healing rate, and deep remission rate at week 44 were calculated. According to whether deep remission was achieved at week 44 of UST therapy, the patients were divided into the deep remission group and the non-deep remission group, and the differences in baseline characteristics were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression model analysis was used to identify the associated factors for the deep remission at week 44 of UST therapy. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was further employed to determine the cut-off values of associated factors for predicting the deep remission at week 44. Results: A total of 156 patients were enrolled, including 100 males and 56 females, with a confirmed age at diagnosis [M (Q1, Q3)] of 29 (24, 35) years. At week 44 of therapy, the clinical remission rate was 73.1% (114/156), mucosal healing rate was 46.2% (72/156), and transmural healing rate was 32.7% (51/156). There were 46 and 110 patients in the deep remission group and non-deep remission group, respectively, with a deep remission rate of 29.5%. Compared with the non-deep remission group, the proportion of patients with colonic disease location [32.6% (15/46) vs 7.3% (8/110), P<0.017], the non-stricturing and non-penetrating disease behavior [87.0% (40/46) vs 38.2% (42/110), P<0.017] and the baseline albumin level [(43.3±3.8) vs (40.0±5.3) g/L, P<0.001)] were higher in the deep remission group. However, the baseline bowel wall thickness [5.1 (4.1, 5.5) vs 6.2 (5.4, 9.0) mm, P<0.001] and the proportion of patients receiving optimized therapy [15.2% (7/46) vs 50.0% (55/110), P<0.001] were lower in the deep remission group. Multivariable logistic regression model analysis indicated that stricturing or penetrating disease behavior (OR=0.23, 95%CI: 0.07-0.65), baseline albumin level (OR=1.13, 95%CI: 1.02-1.26), and baseline bowel wall thickness (OR=0.56, 95%CI: 0.37-0.77) were the associated factors for the deep remission at week 44 of UST therapy in CD patients. ROC curve analysis indicated that the cut-off value of baseline albumin level for deep remission at week 44 of UST therapy was 41.2 g/L, the baseline albumin level≥41.2 g/L predicted deep remission with a sensitivity of 82.6% and a specificity of 50.9%. Based on clinical applicability, when the baseline bowel wall thickness was set at 6.0 mm as the clinical reference threshold, the sensitivity and specificity of predicting deep remission with baseline bowel wall thickness<6.0 mm were 84.8% and 64.5%, respectively. Conclusions: UST therapy can achieve favorable disease remission outcomes in CD patients, with a deep remission rate of 29.5%(46/156) at week 44. Stricturing or penetrating disease behavior, baseline albumin level<41.2 g/L, and baseline bowel wall thickness≥6.0 mm were the associated factors for deep remission at week 44 of UST therapy in CD patients.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on testosterone supplementation to alleviate aging-related symptoms in men (2026 edition)].
authors: Male Health Branch of Chinese Health Management Association
articles.abstract: Aging is frequently accompanied by a variety of symptoms and changes in physiological indicators that impair men's quality of life. Alleviating aging-related symptoms and improving quality of life in men has become an important public-health goal. Testosterone levels gradually decline in men with advancing age. Accumulating evidence in recent years suggests that exogenous testosterone supplementation may ameliorate selected aging-related symptoms and enhance men's health status. This consensus was developed by the Male Health Management Branch of the Chinese Health Management Association, bringing together experts from endocrinology, andrology, traditional Chinese medicine, nutrition and other disciplines. Based on the latest evidence-based medical evidence, 21 recommendations were formulated focusing on key issues including ameliorating aging-related symptoms, appropriate candidates, risk assessment, medication strategies and monitoring protocols of testosterone supplementaion. It aims to provide guidance for clinicians on the scientific and standardized application of testosterone supplementation to alleviate aging-related symptoms in men.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on practice of echocardiography in adult pulmonary hypertension (2026 edition)].
authors: Pulmonary Vascular Group of Chinese Medical Doctor Association of Cardiology
Specialized Committee of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Rehabilitation of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a clinical syndrome characterized by elevated pulmonary arterial pressure and increased pulmonary vascular resistance, which eventually leads right failure or even death. Early screening and diagnosis are the core steps to improve prognosis, and early assessment of right heart changes is a key component of risk assessment and treatment strategies. Echocardiography has long been recommended as the first-line screening tool for PH and the most widely used non-invasive modality for right heart structure assessment. It is the most important routine examination throughout the PH disease course. However, there is no unified national standards for echocardiographic assessment of PH, resulting in vastly different results. On this basis, the Pulmonary Vascular Group of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association of Cardiology, the Chinese Society of Echocardiography and the Specialized Committee of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Rehabilitation of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine organized experts in relevant fields to draft Expert consensus on practice of echocardiography in adult pulmonary hypertension (2026 edition), resulting in seven recommendations. The consensus provides a step-by-step interpretation of the acquisition and assessment of essential and optional parameters, using standard images as references, with the aim of offering unified and standardized operational guidance for echocardiographers and other relevant professionals.

articles.title: [Advances and perspectives in precision classification of diabetes].
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus comprises a group of highly heterogeneous diseases that differ in pathogenic mechanisms and clinical phenotypes, for which traditional classification systems fall short of meeting the demands of precision diagnosis and treatment. Recent genomic studies have uncovered the distinct genetic backgrounds of different diabetes subtypes, driving the development of novel classification tools such as genetic risk scores. Owing to its stability, inherent accessibility, and lifelong applicability, genetic information serves as an important complement to existing diagnostic systems. This expert forum discusses recent advances in the application of genetic factors to diabetes classification, highlighting the translational value of genomics from genes to clinical practice and offering new perspectives for individualized precision medicine.

articles.title: Reduction of aflatoxin contamination in maize kernels mediated by host-induced gene silencing.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Aflatoxins produced by some species of Aspergillus pose a significant threat to global food safety, because they contaminate a variety of crops including maize. In this study, we used host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) to reduce aflatoxin accumulation in maize upon infection with Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus. Two RNAi constructs were designed and introduced into maize, one targeting two essential fungal genes involved in ergosterol biosynthesis (CYP51A and CYP51B) and the other targeting three aflatoxin biosynthesis genes (AflC, AflD, and AflR). The presence of RNAi transgenes was confirmed in 17 and 14 independent lines possessing the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi construct and the AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi construct, respectively. Most transgenic lines had single-locus integrations and one or two copies of the transgene. Transgene expression varied considerably among the lines. Small RNA sequencing confirmed the production of siRNAs from the HIGS trigger sequences. Levels of CYP51A, AflC, AflD, and AflR transcripts in Aspergillus spp. were successfully decreased upon infection of transgenic maize. However, significant reduction in the level of CYP51B transcripts was not achieved and the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi transgene had no discernible effect on fungal growth in infected maize. In contrast, we observed significant reductions in aflatoxin accumulation in four AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi transgenic lines infected with A. flavus and in two transgenic lines infected with A. parasiticus. Notably, one AflC/AflD/AflR transgenic line exhibited minimal aflatoxin contamination upon kernel infection with A. parasiticus. These results demonstrate the potential of HIGS to reduce aflatoxin production in mature corn kernels.

articles.title: c-FLIP loss links arrest of gene expression to TNFα-dependent antiviral guard immunity.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Cells sense infection through dedicated receptors, yet these surveillance pathways are often subverted by pathogen-encoded virulence factors. Guard immunity provides complementary defense by rapidly killing infected cells in response to infection induced stress. However, the symptoms of infection frequently resemble noninfectious stress, raising the question of how they are distinguished. Using quantitative transcriptomics, proteomics, and global translation measurements during viral infections in vitro and in vivo, we show that infection globally suppresses host gene expression and prevents direct antiviral responses. However, the resulting proteostatic stress does not activate guard immunity unless tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) is present. We identify the anti-apoptotic protein c-FLIP as a guard for gene expression integrity: its loss sensitizes cells to TNFα, triggering cell death and limiting viral spread. Modeling demonstrates that TNFα and c-FLIP loss function as a biological AND-gate, providing specificity and speed. These findings show how cells integrate internal stress signals with external inflammatory cues to improve the fidelity of death decisions, and how this circuitry may misfire during noninfectious inflammation.

articles.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

articles.title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water's dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

articles.title: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

articles.title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains-carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)-as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of specific high-risk EBV lineages and their synergistic interaction with host immune susceptibility. This provides a definitive genetic framework for precision population screening and early diagnosis of NPC in the endemic regions.

articles.title: A tunable immune-evasion function of Zika virus NS5 governs viral fitness and pathogenesis.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Type I interferon (IFN) signaling is a central antiviral defense, with STAT2 driving the expression of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) to restrict viral infection. Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus evade this pathway through nonstructural protein 5 (NS5)-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of STAT2, yet the contribution of this immune-evasion strategy to viral fitness and pathogenesis remains incompletely defined. Here, using a multistep mutational scanning strategy that jointly assessed STAT2 degradation and viral RNA replication, we identified a single NS5 residue, L162, as uniquely permissive to substitution that abolishes STAT2 degradation without compromising intrinsic replication functions. Substitution of L162 with alanine or glycine (L162A or L162G) selectively disrupted NS5 recruitment of the ZSWIM8-CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby preserving STAT2 stability and restoring IFN signaling. Recombinant ZIKV carrying these mutations exhibited reduced replication and enhanced ISG induction in human cells, defects fully rescued by STAT2 knockout. In A129 mice (type I IFN receptor deficient), mutant and WT viruses replicated comparably, but in human STAT2 knock-in mice, ZIKV-NS5L162G exhibited markedly reduced viral loads and disease. In pregnant human STAT2 knock-in mice, the mutant also reduced placental and fetal viral burdens and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Notably, infection with ZIKV-NS5L162G elicited robust neutralizing antibody and T cell responses that conferred protection against WT challenge. Together, these findings establish NS5-mediated STAT2 degradation as a central determinant of ZIKV immune-evasion, viral fitness, and pathogenesis and highlight disruption of NS5-STAT2 antagonism as a promising strategy for antiviral intervention and rational attenuation.

articles.title: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: One of the key events in the HIV-1 life cycle is reverse transcription (RT), during which single-stranded viral RNA (ssRNA) is converted into double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). This process occurs inside the mature HIV-1 capsid and, once it reaches a critical threshold, drives capsid rupture. This uncoating is essential for infection because it releases viral genetic material into the host cell nucleus. Despite its importance, many mechanistic details of this process remain to be fully understood. To address this gap, we develop a multiscale computational method for simulating RT inside the capsid, termed Coarse-Grained Kinetic Monte Carlo (CG-KMC). CG-KMC stochastically adds deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs) to the coarse-grained RNA model, enabling stepwise growth of DNA inside the HIV-1 capsid. We implement this method within an integrative coarse-grained framework that combines a "bottom-up" capsid model with a "top-down" representation of the viral RNA/DNA genome. Our simulations phenomenologically capture and predict diverse capsid rupture pathways during RT. The resulting ruptured structures closely match previously identified cryo-ET images. We further perform an extensive analysis of the rupture process, examining its mechanistic and kinetic aspects as well as the role of capsid-DNA interactions. Our findings illuminate how different capsid-DNA conditions give rise to distinct rupture pathways, which differ from ruptures due to simple outward pressure expansion models from within the capsid.

articles.title: Biotic response networks are an important organizer of the transcriptome in wild Arabidopsis thaliana populations.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Extensive laboratory experimentation has revealed conserved molecular pathways controlling growth and stress responses in plants, yet how these programs operate in natural settings remains poorly understood. We have investigated the organization of the transcriptome in wild populations of Arabidopsis thaliana by sampling plants across 60 natural sites in Europe and North America over two seasons. Transcriptomes varied extensively among individuals and were only weakly structured by geography or season. No groups of plants stood out due to clear biotic or abiotic stress signatures known from the laboratory. While only a small portion of transcriptome variance was explained by disease symptoms or environmental and phenotypic variables, infection-associated signals accounted for the largest share of the explainable fraction. Biotic-response networks identified in controlled laboratory conditions were well conserved in wild transcriptomes, while other networks, including abiotic-response networks were substantially reorganized in wild plants. Together, these results indicate that while certain transcriptional modules are easily reidentified when moving from the wild to controlled conditions, many regulatory relationships differ in these two contexts, highlighting how ecological complexity shapes transcriptome organization in natural populations.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of albuterol-budesonide versus albuterol alone in asthma: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of the recently approved fixed-dose combination of albuterol-budesonide as reliever therapy in patients with asthma.

METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through June 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling patients aged ≥12 years with asthma and comparing albuterol-budesonide with albuterol alone or standard reliever therapy were included. Outcomes included severe exacerbation risk, number and annual rate, forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV₁) at week 12, systemic corticosteroid exposure, and adverse events. Hazard ratios (HRs), relative risks (RRs), and mean differences (MDs) were used as appropriate. Evidence certainty was assessed using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Three RCTs comprising 6,134 participants were included. Albuterol-budesonide significantly reduced severe exacerbation risk (HR = 0.72; 95% CI: 0.58-0.89; p = 0.002), number (RR = 0.64; 95% CI: 0.49-0.82; p = 0.0006), and annual rate (RR = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.51-0.89; p = 0.006). FEV₁ improved significantly (MD = 80.19 mL; 95% CI: 46.46-113.92; p < 0.0001), while annual systemic corticosteroid exposure decreased (MD = -39.33 mg; 95% CI: -62.77 to -15.89; p = 0.001). Adverse events were comparable between groups (RR = 0.99; 95% CI: 0.94-1.04; p = 0.61). GRADE certainty ranged from low to high across outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Albuterol-budesonide reduces severe asthma exacerbations and systemic corticosteroid exposure while improving lung function without increasing adverse events. However, the limited number of trials and heterogeneity in some outcomes warrant cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Very Young ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Associated With Chronic Nonmedical Anabolic-Androgenic Steroid Use: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) before the age of 40 years is uncommon and warrants a comprehensive evaluation of potential etiologies. Chronic nonmedical anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with endothelial dysfunction, accelerated atherosclerosis, and a prothrombotic state, all of which may contribute to premature coronary artery disease. A 29-year-old man with no known medical history and approximately two years of nonmedical testosterone and stanozolol use presented with acute chest pain. Electrocardiography revealed an anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated a thrombotic total occlusion of the mid-left anterior descending coronary artery. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention restored coronary blood flow. The patient presented with Killip class II acute heart failure requiring temporary continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and inotropic support. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30-35%, with anterior and apical hypokinesia. Admission laboratory tests revealed marked atherogenic dyslipidemia (total cholesterol, 302 mg/dL; low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 250 mg/dL; high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 29 mg/dL; triglycerides, 113 mg/dL; and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 273 mg/dL). In addition to the culprit lesion, nonobstructive atherosclerotic plaques were identified in other coronary segments. At the one-month follow-up, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol had decreased to 85 mg/dL following statin therapy and the reported discontinuation of AAS use. At three months, the patient remained clinically stable, although LVEF remained at 30%. AAS exposure may have contributed to accelerated atherosclerosis and coronary thrombosis in a susceptible young individual. However, alternative causes of MI at a very young age should be systematically considered.

articles.title: Associations of Early Pregnancy Contaminant Exposure with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Mediation by Metabolic Pathway Perturbations.
articles.abstract: Early pregnancy exposure to environmental contaminants is a known risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the metabolic pathways linking specific chemical categories to disease pathogenesis remain largely unknown. To address this gap, we conducted a meet-in-the-middle mediation analysis within a prospective birth cohort, leveraging a nested case-control study (116 GDM cases, 232 controls) with 182 contaminants across 11 chemical categories and 702 metabolites measured in early pregnancy serum samples. Seven individual contaminants showed significant associations with GDM risk, with BHT-COOH exhibiting the strongest effect (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.59-3.45). Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression indicated a positive mixture association with GDM, with Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) providing a complementary assessment of mixture effects. Notably, we identified 506 exposure-metabolite pairs with significant mediation and consistent directionality, providing a comprehensive profile of candidate metabolic intermediates in the associations between contaminant exposure and GDM. Pathway-level analysis identified six candidate metabolic pathways with significant mediation effects, among which the phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis pathway showed the largest mediation estimate, accounting for 75.5% of the DEHP/DNOP-GDM association. Similar pathway-level mediation effects were observed for both individual contaminants and the mixture exposure index. Collectively, these findings identify potential metabolic intermediates linking early pregnancy contaminant exposure to GDM and provide hypotheses for further epidemiological and experimental validation.

articles.title: Risk Factors, Ischemic Delay, and In-Hospital Outcomes by Sex in Adults Aged 18-50 Years with STEMI Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Exploratory Single-Center Cohort.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe sex differences in cardiovascular risk factors and reperfusion delays and explore in-hospital outcomes in adults aged 18-50 years with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHOD: This retrospective single-center cohort included 497 consecutive patients (71 [14.3%] women) treated during 2023-2024. Hard major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) comprised all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or stroke. A nonstandard expanded clinical deterioration composite additionally included incident cardiogenic shock and, among patients admitted in Killip class I, incident heart failure. Sex comparisons and Firth penalized logistic models were exploratory.

RESULTS: Mean age was 40.7 +- 5.3 years. Current smoking was more frequent in men (69.0% vs 39.4%; P < 0.001), whereas obesity was more frequent in women (54.9% vs 26.8%; P < 0.001). Age-adjusted median symptom-to-first-medical-contact, first-medical-contact-to-device, and total ischemic times were 46, 10, and 48 minutes longer in women, respectively (all P < 0.001). Hard MACCE occurred in 21 patients (4.2%), incident heart failure occurred in 13 of 390 eligible patients (3.3%), and the expanded composite occurred in 46 patients (9.3%). The expanded composite occurred in 12 of 71 women and 34 of 426 men (16.9% vs 8.0%; unadjusted P = 0.025), and incident cardiogenic shock occurred in 7 women and 13 men (9.9% vs 3.1%; unadjusted P = 0.015). In the parsimonious baseline model, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for female sex was 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-5.42), attenuating to 1.90 (95% CI, 0.83-4.18) after adding admission Killip class ≥II.

CONCLUSION: Women had a different risk-factor distribution and longer documented ischemic delays. The association between sex and the expanded composite was sensitive to adjustment for baseline clinical severity. Sex-specific outcome estimates are hypothesis-generating given the small female subgroup and event counts. The retrospective single-center design, absence of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable care- and referral-pathway variables limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Bee Sting-Associated Kounis Syndrome Presenting as Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report and Systematic Review with Age-Based Analysis.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS) is an uncommon acute coronary syndrome triggered by allergic or hypersensitivity reactions. Bee stings are a recognized precipitant, although the available evidence is largely limited to case reports and small case series. We present a 44-year-old man with probable bee sting-associated KS and systematically review published cases, including an exploratory age-based comparison using ≤45 years as the cutoff for myocardial infarction in younger individuals. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE) and Scopus were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 recommendations. A total of 47 patients were included, comprising 46 previously reported cases and our index case. The mean age was 55.7+-13.0 years, and 39/47 patients (83.0%) were male. Symptoms developed within 30 minutes in 29/47 patients (61.7%), and chest pain occurred in 41/47 (87.2%). Type II KS predominated (29/43, 67.4%), while ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) occurred in 37/47 patients (78.7%), and revascularization was performed in 27/47 (57.4%). Cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, and rhythm or conduction disturbances occurred in 11/46 (23.9%), 5/46 (10.9%), and 7/46 patients (15.2%), respectively. Recovery at the last reported assessment was documented in 45/46 patients (97.8%), with no reported deaths. No follow-up data were available after the index patient left the hospital against medical advice approximately five hours after presentation. Thirteen patients (27.7%) were aged ≤45 years; age-stratified descriptive analyses did not reveal clear differences in most clinical characteristics; however, interpretation was limited by the small number of younger patients. Bee sting-associated KS may cause severe acute coronary presentations, including in younger individuals. Given the case-based and heterogeneous nature of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in systematically collected cohorts.

articles.title: Consensus on the Use of Intrathecal Gene Therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrathecal (IT) delivery of gene therapy is an emerging strategy for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), aiming to enhance central nervous system targeting while potentially reducing systemic exposure. The new administration route of onasemnogene abeparvovec is associated with a distinct safety profile, including dorsal root ganglia toxicity, and requires structured monitoring beyond existing intravenous guidelines, including planning for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up in pediatric and adult care as well as structured transition protocols.

METHODS: We expanded the existing intravenous monitoring guideline by incorporating surveillance for potential dorsal root ganglia-related adverse effects. The protocol integrates clinical, laboratory, electrophysiological, imaging, and long-term follow-up recommendations.

RESULTS: The protocol defines pre-treatment assessment, peri-procedural management, and longitudinal follow-up in both pediatric and adult care settings, with emphasis on proactive evaluation of dorsal root ganglia function and structured transition of adolescents treated before adulthood to specialized multidisciplinary adult neurology services.

CONCLUSION: A structured, multimodal monitoring approach-including dorsal root ganglia surveillance, multidisciplinary long-term follow-up, and coordinated transition from pediatric to adult care-is essential for the safe implementation of IT onasemnogene abeparvovec in SMA.
