Our findings highlight the contribution of cardiac dysfunction to morbidity and support routine cardiac assessment in patients with severe cutaneous adverse reactions. Larger prospective studies and national drug reaction registries are needed to better define the burden and guide care.

articles.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Oral NLRP3 Inhibition With Ruvonoflast Among Individuals at Elevated Cardiovascular Risk.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nucleotide oligomerization domain-, leucine-rich repeat-, and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is a key sensor of diverse exogenous stimuli linked to noncommunicable diseases including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Early clinical data with the oral NLRP3 inhibitor ruvonoflast suggested lowering of biomarkers of systemic and central nervous system inflammation.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to assess anti-inflammatory efficacy and safety of ruvonoflast in participants with residual inflammatory risk and high atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.

METHODS: In a double-blind Phase 1b trial, we randomly allocated individuals with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) ≥2.5 mg/L and body mass index ≥30 to ≤40 kg/m2, plus dyslipidemia, hypertension, or type 2 diabetes, to oral ruvonoflast (225 mg twice daily; n = 40) or matching placebo (n = 23). Both groups were maintained on a 2,000 kcal/d diet. The primary endpoint was change in hsCRP at Day 28 (ratio to baseline), analyzed using a Bayesian analysis of covariance. Additionally, change in hsCRP ratio to baseline over time was analyzed using a mixed-effects model with repeated measures. Change from baseline in inflammatory biomarkers and body weight were secondary endpoints analyzed with mixed-effects model with repeated measures and ANCOVA, respectively. Safety and tolerability were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Of 63 participants (mean age: 52.6 years; 71.4% female; 69.8% White) randomized, 59 completed the study. Median hsCRP at baseline was 5.7 mg/L (IQR: 3.9-9.8 mg/L). The primary endpoint of hsCRP reduction was met with a posterior probability of >99% for superiority of ruvonoflast over placebo at Day 28. Between-group differences favoring ruvonoflast were significant from Day 3 onward (P ≤ 0.001); at Day 28, geometric least-squares mean reduction in hsCRP was 82.2% (95% CI: 75.9%-86.8%) with ruvonoflast vs 37.2% (95% CI: 7.0%-57.6%) with placebo. hsCRP returned to baseline 7 days post-treatment discontinuation. Ruvonoflast significantly lowered key secondary biomarkers interleukin-6 and fibrinogen vs placebo at Day 28 (P < 0.001). Treatment groups had comparable mean percentage body weight reductions at Day 28. Serious treatment-emergent adverse advents were similar between groups, but 4 (10%) ruvonoflast-treated participants discontinued treatment due to transient, reversible treatment-emergent adverse advents, vs none in placebo.

CONCLUSIONS: Oral NLRP3 inhibition with ruvonoflast significantly reduced hsCRP with concurrent reductions in inflammatory biomarkers in participants with elevated inflammatory risk. Ongoing Phase 2 trials of larger size and longer duration will further characterize the therapeutic potential of ruvonoflast. (Effects of NT-0796 in Obese Participants at Risk of Cardiovascular Disease; NCT06129409).

articles.title: Cold Carbonated Water Reduces Interference from Extracardiac Gastric Activity During 82Rb PET in Patients.
articles.abstract: Cold carbonated water is a simple, inexpensive preparation that could plausibly reduce gastric uptake through a combination of gastric distension, altered motility from CO2, and reduced mucosal perfusion from cooling. To our knowledge, this approach has not been investigated in the setting of 82Rb PET myocardial perfusion imaging. Methods: We conducted a same-day, within-subject study of 20 patients undergoing surveillance for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction and included 20 additional patients from the same cohort who did not receive the intervention. Each patient underwent 2 rest 82Rb PET scans; between scans, each drank up to 500 mL of cold carbonated water. Gastric spillover was assessed in 3 ways: subjective comparison (better/worse/unchanged), a 4-level semiquantitative interference severity score, and quantitative myocardial-to-extracardiac (MYO/EXT) ratios using voxel- and contour-based region-of-interest methods. Results: Severity scores shifted lower after the intervention (P = 0.003). The scores for 11 of 20 patients improved, 9 were unchanged, and none worsened. MYO/EXT uptake ratios increased with both region-of-interest methods (voxel: from 1.67 ± 0.61 to 1.98 ± 0.50, P = 0.041; contour: from 1.60 ± 0.34 to 1.82 ± 0.37, P = 0.006). Readers judged improvement in 75% and 80% of cases, respectively, with 75% concordance. In contrast, the nonintervention group showed no significant differences in semiquantitative scores or MYO/EXT uptake ratios between scans. Conclusion: Cold carbonated water reduced gastric interference during rest 82Rb PET myocardial perfusion imaging across visual and quantitative metrics. The intervention is simple and well tolerated. Larger, controlled studies, especially during stress imaging, are warranted.

articles.title: Anticoagulation Alone or With Antiaggregation in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Exposure to polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics elicits renal injury with limited compensation and associated intestinal alterations: A time-resolved multi-omics study.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) are emerging contaminants of toxicological concern. However, the temporal progression of PET-NPs-induced renal injury during repeated oral exposure remains poorly understood. Male C57BL/6 J mice received PET-NPs at 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 14, 28, or 56 days to characterize time-dependent nephrotoxicity and intestinal alterations. Fluorescence imaging detected gastrointestinal signals at all time points and a time-dependent increase in renal fluorescence following administration of Nile red-labeled PET-NPs. PET-NPs exposure was associated with impaired intestinal barrier integrity and altered gut microbial composition. Renal assessments revealed functional impairment, tubular injury, inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, and lipid peroxidation. Integrated renal transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identified alterations in inflammatory signaling, redox homeostasis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid metabolism. Mean TUNEL positivity was numerically highest at 28 days and remained elevated relative to controls at 56 days. At 56 days, tubular injury, renal dysfunction, and inflammation persisted alongside increased Ki-67 positivity. Although the renal Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant axis was activated, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and renal injury indicated insufficient antioxidant compensation. Repeated oral PET-NPs exposure elicited time-dependent nephrotoxicity characterized by inflammatory-redox-lipid metabolic remodeling and constrained antioxidant compensation. These findings provide a time-resolved multi-omics framework for assessing PET-NPs-associated renal hazards following repeated oral exposure.

articles.title: Evaluation of community-based mass dog deworming and public health education for the control of Toxocara spp. infection in household dogs in Vietnam.
articles.journal: Comparative immunology, microbiology and infectious diseases
articles.abstract: Toxocara spp. are neglected zoonotic nematodes that commonly infect dogs and represent an important public health concern. However, evidence on community-based control interventions remains limited. This study aimed to compare mass deworming of dogs and cats with public health education in reducing Toxocara spp. infection in household dogs. A community-based controlled intervention study was conducted between February and July 2025 in eight hamlets in Krong Nang district, Dak Lak Province, Vietnam. Four hamlets were assigned to mass deworming of pets with fenbendazole, and four to public health education. Dog fecal samples were collected at baseline and after three months and examined by copromicroscopy and polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The primary outcome was PCR-detected T. canis prevalence, and arithmetic mean infection intensity in eggs per gram (EPG). The analysis included 557 dog observations across baseline and follow-up surveys. After three months, the deworming group showed greater descriptive reductions in copromicroscopy- and PCR-detected Toxocara spp. prevalence and EPG than the education group. The relative reduction in PCR-detected T. canis prevalence was descriptively greater in the deworming group (22.1%, 95% CI: -11.4-47.3) than in the education group (3.3%, 95% CI: -39.2-34.1). However, mixed-effects logistic regression found no statistically significant intervention effect on PCR-detected T. canis infection over the three-month follow-up. Although no statistically significant intervention effect was detected, mass pet deworming showed larger descriptive reductions in Toxocara spp. infection than public health education. Further studies are needed to evaluate integrated strategies combining regular deworming, education, and environmental hygiene, which may help reduce environmental contamination and zoonotic transmission.

articles.title: CT perfusion-derived arterial input function dispersal versus echocardiographic left atrial enlargement in acute stroke.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Arterial input function (AIF) dispersal on brain computed tomography (CT) perfusion reflects delayed cerebral contrast transit and is associated with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We hypothesized that delayed contrast transit through the LA due to LA enlargement may prolong AIF, independent of LVEF.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack from the prospective INSPIRE registry (December 2020-June 2024) who underwent multimodal CT including brain perfusion CT (CTP), as well as transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) within 90 days of stroke. On TTE, left atrial (LA) enlargement was defined as area ≥ 24 cm² and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) as < 50%. Prolonged AIF dispersal from CTP was defined as ≥ 29 s from scan onset to the end of AIF (return to baseline). Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusted for clinical and cardiac covariates.

RESULTS: Among 172 patients, prolonged AIF was observed in 50 (29.1%), LA enlargement in 52 (30.2%), and reduced LVEF in 28 (16.3%). In multivariate analysis including both variables, LA enlargement (≥24 cm²: OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.66-8.52, p = 0.002) and reduced LVEF (OR 3.35, 95% CI 1.21-9.27, p = 0.020) were independently associated with prolonged AIF dispersal.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Both LA enlargement and reduced LVEF were associated with prolonged AIF dispersal, suggesting that AIF delay on CTP is a useful screening tool to identify stroke patients with cardiac dysfunction.

articles.title: Lithium in the Prevention of Postpartum Recurrence of Mood Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Women with bipolar disorder are at increased risk for relapse/recurrence during the postpartum period. This risk decreases with prophylactic pharmacologic treatment, compared to those who remain medication-free. Lithium use in preventing relapse has been studied extensively in individuals with bipolar disorder, though its specific use in the postpartum has not received as much attention. Objective: The aim of this systematic review (CRD420261357096) was to estimate risk of postpartum relapse, specifically in women with bipolar disorder who received lithium prophylactically versus those who discontinued it during pregnancy. Study Selection: Following PRISMA guidelines, reviewers screened 45 studies focused on women with bipolar I or II disorders from searches of PubMed, PsycINFO, and Cochrane databases conducted on April 2, 2026, that were written in English. Data Extraction: Two independent observers extracted data using a data extraction form created on Covidence. Random-effects meta-analysis of recurrence proportions, between-study variance, heterogeneity, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results: Eight studies (554 women) providing information on the prophylactic effect of lithium during the postpartum period, and 2 studies evaluating the impact of lithium discontinuation on postpartum relapse, were identified. The pooled recurrence proportion was 0.21 (95% CI 0.15-0.29) in lithium-treated patients and 0.41 (95% CI 0.33-0.50) in lithium-untreated patients. The most common timing of prophylaxis initiation was during pregnancy (51.9%). Studies examining the impact of lithium discontinuation provided indirect evidence of its effectiveness in preventing postpartum recurrence. Conclusion: Findings from our meta-analysis suggest that lithium is effective in preventing postpartum recurrence of mood disorders; however, caution is warranted when interpreting study results because of confounding by indication and limited literature.

articles.title: Effect of glucagon-like-peptide-1 receptor agonists on major cardiovascular outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like-peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are an antihyperglycemic group of drugs that have emerged as potentially preventing the risk of cardiovascular events. This meta-analysis assesses the effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists on cardiovascular outcomes. A detailed search of existing literature was based on MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov. The search included all the studies from inception to February 2026. Statistical analyses were performed using the RevMan software, and a random-effects model was used to conduct the meta-analysis. Data were represented via forest plots, and dichotomous outcomes were evaluated using the Mantel-Haenszel method. This meta-analysis includes 12 randomized control trials (RCTs) with 82,669 patients. The analysis showed that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce risk of cardiac death [relative risk (RR): 0.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.96, p=0.003, I²=0%], all-cause mortality (RR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.93, p<0.00001, I²=0%), stroke (RR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.77-0.94, p=0.001, I²=0%), non-fatal stroke (RR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.79-0.96, p=0.005, I²=0%) and revascularization (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95, p=0.007, I²=59%). There was no statistically significant reduction in myocardial infarction (MI) (RR: 0.92, 95% CI: 0.84-1.01, p=0.09, I²=42%), fatal MI (RR: 1.15, 95% CI: 0.80-1.66, p=0.44, I²=0%), non-fatal MI (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.82-1.01, p=0.09, I²=51%), fatal stroke (RR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.55-1.00, p=0.05, I²=0%), heart failure hospitalization (RR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.85-1.03, p=0.20, I²=17%), or hospitalization for unstable angina (RR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.85-1.12, p=0.71, I²=0%). This meta-analysis demonstrates that GLP-1 receptor agonists have a significant impact on cardiovascular death. More thorough RCTs with longer follow-up periods are required to completely understand the possible cardiovascular advantages of GLP-1 receptor agonists.

articles.title: High-resolution computed tomography imaging of pulmonary changes and relation with disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease with a wide spectrum of pulmonary manifestations, some of which may remain clinically occult. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) is an important imaging modality for detecting and characterizing these abnormalities. This study aimed to evaluate the spectrum of thoracic HRCT abnormalities in patients with RA and examine their association with disease activity and inflammatory markers. A prospective, analytical, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2021 to January 2022, including 63 adults with RA fulfilling the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria. Clinical characteristics, disease activity assessed using the Disease Activity Score 28-erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), inflammatory markers, and thoracic HRCT findings were recorded and analyzed. Of the 63 patients, 45 (71.4%) were women, and the mean age was 45.3±13.4 years. HRCT abnormalities were detected in 36 (57.1%) patients, with usual interstitial pneumonia-pattern interstitial lung disease (22.2%) and ground-glass opacities (19.0%) being the most frequent findings. Patients with abnormal HRCT findings had significantly higher DAS28-ESR scores, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rates, and longer disease duration compared with those with normal HRCT findings (all p<0.001). C-reactive protein positivity (p<0.001) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody positivity (p=0.012) were also significantly associated with HRCT abnormalities, whereas age and sex showed no significant associations. Pulmonary abnormalities detected by HRCT were common in patients with RA and were associated with greater disease activity, systemic inflammation, and longer disease duration. These findings highlight the importance of respiratory assessment in patients with RA, particularly those with active disease.

articles.title: [Effect of postoperative nutritional supplementation on the reduction of clinical complications in geriatric patients with hip fracture: a retrospective study in a hospital setting].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The high incidence of hip fractures among the elderly population in Spain, with an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 cases annually, represents a serious public health issue due to high mortality rates and associated complications, particularly in malnourished patients. The objective of this paper was to assess the effectiveness of nutritional supplementation as part of postoperative treatment in elderly patients with hip fractures.

METHODS: A study was conducted at the University Hospital of León with a sample of 497 patients aged between seventy-five and one hundred five years. Clinical records were used to collect data on functional status prior to the fracture, nutritional support, and clinical outcomes. Statistical analysis was performed to identify associations between nutritional supplementation and the occurrence of postoperative complications.

RESULTS: Protein supplements were prescribed more frequently to patients who were completely dependent (27.1 %) and to those who required a great deal of assistance to walk or were unable to walk (25.5 %), with statistically significant associations (P=0.001 and P=0.005, respectively). Furthermore, their prescription was significantly associated with complications during hospitalisation, such as the need for a blood transfusion (P<0.001), respiratory failure (P<0.001), heart failure (P<0.001) and malnutrition (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The prescription of nutritional supplements on discharge was more common among patients with greater functional dependence and who had experienced complications during their hospital stay. No significant differences were observed by gender. These results reinforce the importance of an individualised nutritional assessment in older people with hip fractures.

articles.title: Prevalence of pathogenic bacterial contamination on healthcare worker identification badges.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited evidence exists on how healthcare worker (HCW) identification badges may become contaminated with microorganisms encountered in healthcare environments.

AIM/OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was twofold: (1) to determine the prevalence of bacterial contamination, including pathogenic organisms, on HCW identification badges, and (2) to examine badge-use factors associated with bacterial accumulation.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional correlational study was conducted at a large community academic health network in eastern Pennsylvania. Bacterial swab specimens were collected from the front and back of 110 identification badges worn by HCWs who provided direct patient care on medical-surgical and critical care units. A questionnaire collected demographic data and badge-use behaviors from participants. Ten new, unused badges served as controls.

FINDINGS/RESULTS: Among the badges studied, 4/110 (3.6%; 95% CI, 1.0%-9.0%) HCW badges and 0/10 control badges yielded organisms associated with human infection. The organisms recovered were Acinetobacter radioresistens, Pantoea agglomerans, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Aerococcus viridans. Non-pathogenic bacterial growth was detected on all 120 badges, with colony counts ranging from <100 to >10,000 CFU/mL. The small number of positive badges precluded meaningful analysis of associations between badge-use factors and contamination.

DISCUSSION: Despite universal microbial contamination, recovery of organisms associated with human infection from HCW identification badges was infrequent. These findings suggest that clinically significant bacterial contamination of HCW identification badges may be less common than previously reported. Routine badge cleaning and adherence to hand hygiene practices remain reasonable infection prevention measures.

articles.title: RHBDF2 stabilizes SEC62 to sustain MDR1 biosynthesis and chemoresistance in breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aims of the study were to elucidate the regulatory role of rhomboid family protein 2 (RHBDF2) in breast cancer chemoresistance and the underlying molecular mechanisms to provide a theoretical basis and research direction to facilitate the development of potential therapeutic interventions.

METHODS: Chemoresistance and apoptosis assays, and mouse tumor-bearing models were used to evaluate the correlation between RHBDF2 expression and breast cancer chemoresistance. Doxorubicin accumulation, rhodamine efflux, immunohistochemical staining, Western blot, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to validate the regulatory relationships in protein expression and function for RHBDF2, MDR1 (ABCB1), and SEC62 (a critical component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane insertion machinery). Immunofluorescence staining and immunoprecipitation assays were employed to determine the molecular mechanisms underlying RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis-mediated regulation of breast cancer chemoresistance.

RESULTS: The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis constitutes the core regulatory pathway in breast cancer chemoresistance. When RHBDF2 is highly expressed, it binds to heat shock cognate protein 70 (HSC70), a central chaperone-mediated autophagy receptor, thereby blocking the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62, maintaining SEC62 protein levels, and promoting membrane integration of MDR1 to enhance drug resistance. Under downregulated RHBDF2 expression, the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62 increases, leading to impaired MDR1 function and substantially reduced cellular drug resistance.

CONCLUSIONS: The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis is the core signaling pathway that governs chemoresistance in breast cancer. Targeted interventions against key molecules or related signaling nodes in this axis can provide a theoretical basis for developing novel therapeutic strategies to reverse chemoresistance, with great clinical translational value.

articles.title: Vulture populations, seasonal dynamics, and conservation threats in the Urban landscape: a case study in Jimma, Southwest Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Vultures play an indispensable ecological role in maintaining ecosystem balance through the rapid removal of carrion and the provision of critical ecosystem services. Of the 16 Old World vulture species, Africa supports 11, with eight species recorded in Ethiopia. However, urbanization and associated anthropogenic pressures may threaten these essential scavengers. This study assessed vulture species composition, observed abundance, seasonal variation, and conservation threats in Jimma City, southwestern Ethiopia, during the dry season (January-March) and wet season (May-July) of 2022. Data were collected through systematic field observations, questionnaire surveys, and key informant interviews and were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Four globally threatened species were recorded: hooded, white-backed, rüppell's griffon, and lappet-faced vultures, underscoring the urgent need for targeted conservation interventions. Vulture counts varied significantly between seasons (P < 0.001), with higher counts recorded during the wet season. Mean dry-season counts were 264 ± 9 for hooded, 191 ± 29 for African white-backed, 17 ± 3 for Rüppell's griffon, and 4 ± 1 for lappet-faced vultures. The corresponding wet-season counts were 408 ± 57, 266 ± 25, 29 ± 4, and 7 ± 1, respectively. The hooded vulture had the highest relative abundance, accounting for 57% of recorded observations, whereas the lappet-faced vulture accounted for 1%. Observed counts also differed significantly among study sites (P < 0.001). Key threats identified include electric shock associated with power-line infrastructure, habitat loss, poisoning, and limited public awareness. These findings highlight the vulnerability of urban vulture populations and emphasize the need for integrated conservation strategies that prioritize habitat protection, incorporate urban planning considerations, and actively engage local stakeholders.

articles.title: Digital transformation in nursing education: students' satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and challenges with interactive e-books.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the increasing integration of digital tools in nursing education, interactive e-books have emerged as innovative resources that promote engagement, flexibility, and active learning. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness in enhancing nursing students' satisfaction and academic self-efficacy, as well as the challenges affecting their use, remains limited.

AIM: This study aimed to assess nursing students' satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books.

METHODS: A mixed-methods design was employed among 500 undergraduate nursing students at Capital University, Egypt. Quantitative data were collected using validated instruments measuring satisfaction and academic self-efficacy. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were used to examine relationships between variables, while multiple linear regression analysis was conducted to identify key predictors of both outcomes. In addition, qualitative data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed thematically to explore students' perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books.

RESULTS: The majority of students reported high levels of satisfaction (72.2%) and self-efficacy (63%). A strong positive association was observed between satisfaction and self-efficacy. Multiple linear regression analysis identified academic performance (GPA) as a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.185, p < 0.001) and self-efficacy (β = 0.198, p < 0.001). Prior training was also a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.142, p = 0.014) and self-efficacy (β = 0.155, p = 0.005). Age and academic level were additionally significant predictors across both models, whereas gender was not statistically significant (p > 0.05). The regression models explained a moderate proportion of variance in both outcomes, emphasizing the multifactorial nature of satisfaction and self-efficacy in technology-enhanced learning environments. Qualitative findings revealed key barriers, including technical limitations, content navigation difficulties, limited access to devices and internet connectivity, cognitive overload, and insufficient digital literacy.

CONCLUSION: Interactive e-books can enhance nursing students' satisfaction and self-efficacy; however, their effectiveness depends on students' academic preparedness, technological accessibility, and system design. Addressing identified barriers and strengthening digital readiness are essential for optimizing the integration of interactive e-books in nursing education.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Meal-induced changes in cardiometabolic peptides in the context of acute cardiovascular diseases and glucose metabolism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natriuretic peptides (NPs) and copeptin are established cardiovascular biomarkers which can partly affect human metabolism. However, impact of human metabolism on their postprandial regulation in high-risk patients remains insufficiently understood. We aimed to characterize meal-induced changes in MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, and copeptin and to assess how these dynamics relate to acute cardiovascular (CV) events, type 2 diabetes (T2D) and insulin resistance (IR).

METHODS: Within the BeLOVE cohort, a subset of 373 participants with acute coronary syndrome, stroke or very high chronic CV risk underwent standardized study-specific mixed-meal testing approximately 3 months after the acute event or 1 month after enrollment for the chronic high-risk group. Fasting and 120-min postprandial concentrations of MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, copeptin, insulin and glucose were assessed. Structural equation models were used to evaluate direct and indirect associations of acute CV events, T2D, and IR (HOMA-IR) with fasting levels and postprandial changes, adjusted for age, sex and BMI.

RESULTS: MR-proANP showed the most pronounced meal-induced suppression. NT-proBNP demonstrated only minor and inconsistent postprandial changes. For all peptides, fasting concentrations were the main determinant of their postprandial changes. A recent acute CV event was associated with higher fasting NP levels (MR-proANP: standardized β = 0.22 [0.09; 0.34]; NT-proBNP: β = 0.28 [0.15; 0.41]), but not substantially with their postprandial changes after accounting for their baseline levels. T2D showed no consistent association with fasting or postprandial NP responses. In contrast, higher HOMA-IR was associated with lower fasting MR-proANP (β=-0.19 [-0.30; -0.07]) and a stronger postprandial decline (β=-0.18 [-0.33; -0.04]). Similarly, higher HOMA-IR was linked to lower fasting NT-proBNP (β=-0.15 [-0.28; -0.03]) but showed no clear association to its postprandial change. Copeptin dynamics were largely independent of acute CV disease and metabolic status.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients after a recent ACS or stroke, postprandial MR-proANP dynamics are linked to insulin resistance, rather than diabetes status. In contrast, the limited postprandial variability of NT-proBNP and the largely fasting-related changes of copeptin make these markers less suited for capturing short-term metabolic responses. Together, these findings highlight the value of postprandial phenotyping for understanding cardiometabolic regulation and support further evaluation of MR-proANP as a potential biomarker in future prospective studies with cardiovascular outcomes across subjects with and without acute CV event.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was approved by the institutional ethics committee (EA1/066/17) and registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016852).

articles.title: Gestational age-stratified analysis of HALP score and complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices in retinopathy of prematurity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the temporal profile and discriminative performance of the hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score and complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), with analyses stratified by gestational age.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 139 preterm infants born at ≤ 32 weeks of gestation who were admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of Malatya Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between May 2022 and December 2025. Infants were stratified into ≤ 30-week and 30-32-week gestational age groups. CBC parameters obtained during the early postnatal period (days 2-4) and, when available, at postnatal month 1 (days 28-32) were analyzed. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), and HALP score were calculated. Comparisons were performed according to ROP status within gestational age strata. Discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and associations with ROP were examined using logistic regression adjusted for gestational age and birth weight.

RESULTS: ROP developed in 30 infants (21.6%), including 10 requiring treatment. The ≤ 30-week group had a higher incidence of ROP than the 30-32-week group. Early postnatal inflammatory indices were not associated with ROP. At postnatal month 1, infants born at ≤ 30 weeks who developed ROP had lower albumin and LMR values, together with higher SII, SIRI, AISI, and NLR values, with ROC AUCs ranging from 0.73 to 0.82. After adjustment for gestational age and birth weight in all infants with available month-1 data (n = 86; 30 ROP events), significant associations with ROP persisted for SII, SIRI, NLR, LMR, and neutrophil count. HALP score and PLR demonstrated limited discriminative performance. Interpretation of month-1 findings in the 30-32-week group was limited because of substantial missing follow-up data.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, CBC-derived inflammatory indices measured at postnatal month 1 were more discriminative than early postnatal measurements, particularly among infants born at ≤ 30 weeks of gestation. These findings suggest that selected inflammatory indices may serve as adjunctive biomarkers for ROP risk assessment in very preterm infants; however, external validation in larger prospective multicenter studies is required before clinical implementation.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Effects of collagenase treatment on protein profiles and ultrastructure of llama spermatozoa.
articles.abstract: Proteolytic enzymes such as collagenase are commonly used to improve handling and processing of llama semen; however, their molecular or structural effects on sperm remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of two collagenase concentrations (0.02 and 0.2%) on sperm quality, protein profile, and ultrastructure of llama spermatozoa. Ejaculates were incubated with collagenase and compared with raw semen through conventional semen analysis, 1D SDS-PAGE followed by protein sequencing and identification, as well as scanning and transmission electron microscopy. Semen incubation with 0.02% collagenase resulted in a significant decrease in oscillatory motility (P < 0.05) and showed a tendency toward increased progressive motility, without affecting total motility, vigour, or sperm protein profile. Ultrastructural analyses revealed preserved membrane integrity, although spermatozoa exhibited different degrees of acrosomal loss. In contrast, 0.2% collagenase significantly decreased oscillatory motility and increased progressive motility (P < 0.05), while completely eliminating thread formation. This treatment yielded changes in the sperm protein profile, including the disappearance of a ∼95 kDa band and the appearance of a ∼45 kDa band, suggesting collagenase-associated protein modification and/or degradation. These bands were identified as heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) isoforms and lactotransferrin, respectively. Moreover, high collagenase concentration was associated with an increased proportion of detached heads and ultrastructural damage, including acrosomal loss and plasma membrane disruption in the sperm head and tail. In conclusion, low collagenase concentrations appeared to exert minimal effects on sperm ultrastructure and protein composition, whereas higher concentrations induced molecular and structural alterations that could potentially compromise semen fertility.

articles.title: Explainable artificial intelligence in clinical decision support systems: a systematic review of techniques, clinical applications, evaluation, and future directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as an important approach for improving the transparency and interpretability of artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support systems (CDSSs). However, evidence regarding the models and explainability techniques used in healthcare, their clinical evaluation, methodological quality, and progression toward real-world implementation remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the current evidence on XAI-enabled CDSSs, with particular emphasis on AI and XAI methods, clinical applications, validation, explainability evaluation, implementation, and methodological limitations.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261449460). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception through 30 June 2026 (searches run on 15 July 2026). Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles that applied artificial intelligence within healthcare clinical decision support systems, incorporated at least one explainability or interpretability technique, and demonstrated a direct role in clinical decision-making or decision support. Studies limited to prediction, classification, diagnosis, or prognostic modeling without a decision-support component were excluded. Two reviewers jointly screened titles and abstracts, independently assessed full texts, and independently extracted data using a standardized form informed by the CHARMS checklist. Risk of bias and applicability of prediction model studies were assessed using PROBAST, and reporting completeness was evaluated against relevant TRIPOD + AI recommendations where applicable. Due to substantial clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with SWiM guidance.

RESULTS: Of 2008 identified records, 68 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Publications increased substantially in 2025-2026, accounting for 47 of the 68 included studies. China and India contributed the largest number of studies (11 each), followed by the United States (10). Critical care/intensive care medicine and cardiology were the most frequently represented clinical specialties (13 studies each). Numeric patient-level sample size was reported in 35 studies. Among these, the median sample size was 973 (IQR 303-10,015; range 57-106,449), while the mean was 11,944, indicating a markedly right-skewed distribution. Internal validation was reported in 51 studies (75.0 %), whereas external validation was reported in 17 studies (25.0 %). Most systems remained at the research-prototype stage (n = 63, 92.6 %). One study (1.5 %) reported pilot testing in a clinical workflow, while only two studies (2.9 %) reported real-world or routine clinical deployment. Implementation status was unclear or not reported in two studies (2.9 %). Of the 63 studies for which PROBAST was applicable, 3 (4.8 %) were judged at low overall risk of bias and 3 (4.8 %) at high risk; the remainder were rated Unclear mainly because of incomplete reporting. Five studies describing non-prediction CDSS designs were classified as PROBAST not applicable. Clinician involvement was reported in 53 studies. Formal user studies with structured evaluation protocols were reported in 39 studies (57.4 %), but rigorous assessment of effects on decision quality or patient outcomes remained rare.

CONCLUSIONS: XAI-enabled CDSS research has expanded rapidly, yet remains largely confined to model development and technical explainability rather than rigorous clinical translation. Although SHAP and gradient-boosting methods currently predominate, external validation, real-world deployment, standardized evaluation of explanation quality, and meaningful human-centered assessment are still limited. Future work must prioritize multicenter external validation, transparent reporting, rigorous assessment of explanation fidelity and stability, active clinician and patient involvement, and prospective evaluation of effects on decision-making and patient outcomes. Closing the gap between algorithmic performance and clinically meaningful utility is essential for the safe, trustworthy, and responsible adoption of these systems.

articles.title: Association of sinonasal symptoms with health-related quality of life in peri- and postmenopausal women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The menopausal transition is characterized by a progressive decline in estrogen levels. This can trigger physiological alterations in the sinonasal mucosa and potentially lead to the development of sinonasal symptoms affecting women's quality of life. Our study examines associations between scores on the Sinonasal Outcome Test-22 (SNOT-22) and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in peri- and postmenopausal women without chronic rhinosinusitis.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey, conducted via the REDCap database, was offered by email to women aged ≥40 years. A total of 901 women were eligible for participation. The survey instrument covered: i) age, menopause status, age at menopause, smoking status, diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis or prior nasal surgery, use of medications (for arterial hypertension, hypothyroidism, depression, insomnia, allergies or asthma), use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs specifically, and use of menopausal hormone therapy; ii) the SNOT-22, which was included to evaluate sinonasal symptoms; and iii) the Cervantes Short-Form scale (Cervantes SF), to assess HRQoL.

RESULTS: The overall mean score on the SNOT-22 was 34.8 ± 18.7. There were significant differences in the SNOT-22 domains nasal (p = 0.003) and emotion (p = 0.008) between peri- and postmenopausal women. There were correlations between total SNOT-22 score and scores on the following Cervantes SF domains: 1, Menopause and health (r = 0.710; p < 0.001); 2, Psychological (r = 0.706; p < 0.001); 3, Sexuality (r = -0.091; p = 0.006); and 4, Couple relations (r = -0.129; p < 0.001). A higher SNOT-22 total score was independently associated with poorer HRQoL (β = 0.432; 95% CI = 0.399-0.465).

CONCLUSIONS: Both peri- and postmenopausal women without chronic rhinosinusitis had high scores on the SNOT-22 scale. There were differences between peri- and postmenopausal women in the SNOT-22 nasal and emotion domains. There was an independent association between a higher SNOT-22 total score and a poor HRQoL.

articles.title: Physiological responses of the invasive mussel Mytella strigata to atmospheric heatwaves under a simulated tidal cycle.
articles.abstract: Atmospheric heatwaves increasingly threaten intertidal bivalves and ecosystems they support, yet the thermal responses of the highly invasive mussel Mytella strigata remain poorly understood. In this study, mussels were exposed to a simulated tidal regime for five days, with aerial temperatures of 32 °C (control) or 40 °C (heatwave) during low tide. Transcriptomic analysis identified 2497 DEGs, including 1157 upregulated and 1340 downregulated genes. These genes were primarily enriched in protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, MAPK signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, and carbohydrate metabolism. Heat shock proteins and endoplasmic-reticulum quality-control genes were upregulated, indicating enhanced proteostasis maintenance. The upregulation of genes involved in the mitochondrial respiratory chain suggested an increased capacity for ATP production. Meanwhile, the differential expression of cellulase, β-glucosidase, and phosphoglucomutase indicated substantial carbohydrate metabolic remodeling. Our findings suggest that M. strigata responds to heatwave exposure through coordinated proteostasis regulation, metabolic remodeling, and antioxidant defense. Increased catalase activity accompanied by reduced malondialdehyde content suggests that antioxidant compensation effectively limited lipid peroxidation, potentially contributing to the thermal tolerance and persistence of this invasive mussel.

articles.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence supports a pathogenic role for impaired energy metabolism in organ damage. Genetic diseases provide opportunities to investigate these mechanisms, as exemplified by Fabry disease (FD), caused by an α-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency and globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, with cardiomyopathy as the leading cause of death. Beyond Gb3 storage, impaired energy metabolism may contribute to cardiomyopathy. Here, we demonstrate mitochondrial dysfunction in FD heart and its therapeutic targeting. Using a humanized FD mouse model (R301Q-Tg/GLA knockout), embryonic fibroblasts, and neonatal and adult cardiomyocytes, we found impaired mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, increased reactive oxygen species, and a vicious cycle aggravating lysosomal dysfunction. These defects progressed with age, causing accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, energetic failure, apoptosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction. L-arginine, promoting NO/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial rescue, prevented cardiac abnormalities. Our findings identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of FD cardiomyopathy and reveal the lysosome-mitochondria axis as a targetable pathway in FD and beyond.

articles.title: NT-proBNP and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With HFrEF According to Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From QUEST.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Chinese traditional medicine qiliqiangxin (QLQX) improves outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.

OBJECTIVES: This post hoc analysis of the QUEST (Qiliqiangxin in Heart Failure: Assessment of Reduction in Mortality) trial assessed the efficacy and safety of QLQX according to baseline N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels, and examined whether the prognostic value of baseline NT-proBNP varied by atrial fibrillation (AF) status.

METHODS: QUEST enrolled 3,110 patients with HFrEF and NT-proBNP ≥450 pg/mL, and followed them for a median of 18 months. The primary outcome was cardiovascular (CV) death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization. NT-proBNP was analyzed by quartiles and as a continuous variable.

RESULTS: Median baseline NT-proBNP was 1,731 pg/mL. Higher baseline NT-proBNP independently predicted greater risk of the primary outcome (adjusted HR for Q4 vs Q1: 4.03 [95% CI: 3.12-5.20]). The prognostic value of baseline NT-proBNP for all outcomes was consistent irrespective of AF status. At 3 months, QLQX reduced NT-proBNP by 10% compared with placebo. The HRs for the primary composite with QLQX vs placebo were 1.13 (95% CI: 0.73-1.76), 0.76 (95% CI: 0.54-1.06), 0.73 (95% CI: 0.55-0.95), and 0.75 (95% CI: 0.59-0.95) from the lowest to the highest NT-proBNP quartiles, respectively (Pinteraction = 0.48). Results were consistent for CV death, HF hospitalization, and total HF hospitalizations, and when NT-proBNP was modeled continuously (all Pinteraction ≥ 0.30).

CONCLUSIONS: The treatment effect of QLQX on CV events was consistent across the spectrum of baseline NT-proBNP in HFrEF. Baseline NT-proBNP strongly predicted the risk of CV outcomes and mortality, irrespective of AF status. (Qiliqiangxin in Heart Failure: Assessment of Reduction in Mortality [QUEST]; ChiCTR1900021929).

articles.title: Does Race Still Matter in Heart Failure?
Fabry's Disease, Valvular Disease and Infective Endocarditis: A Rare Intersection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis may present with nonspecific systemic symptoms that mimic other conditions, creating diagnostic challenges in high-risk patients.

CASE SUMMARY: A 44-year-old man with advanced Fabry disease, bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, and a chronic Port-A-Cath presented with fever, chills, and malaise shortly after pegunigalsidase alfa infusion, initially raising concern for an infusion reaction. Persistent methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia prompted further evaluation, revealing right-sided native tricuspid valve infective endocarditis with septal leaflet perforation and severe tricuspid regurgitation. Prosthetic aortic valve involvement remained clinically suspected despite nondiagnostic imaging. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multifocal septic embolic infarctions. He received targeted intravenous antibiotics, catheter removal, multidisciplinary care, and cardiothoracic surgical evaluation, with continued medical management recommended.

CONCLUSION: This case emphasizes maintaining suspicion for infective endocarditis despite a plausible alternative diagnosis and highlights the role of multimodality imaging in guiding management.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent S aureus bacteremia should prompt evaluation for infective endocarditis in high-risk patients even when symptoms initially suggest a plausible alternative diagnosis. Multimodality imaging and multidisciplinary assessment are essential when initial imaging is nondiagnostic or clinical findings suggest embolic complications.

articles.title: Salvage Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve With Aspiration Thrombectomy in a Young Adult With Repaired CHD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthetic mitral valve degeneration in adults with repaired congenital heart disease (CHD) can produce rapid hemodynamic collapse and is challenging when surgery and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) are unavailable.

CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old woman with congenital mitral stenosis and multiple ventricular septal defects initially palliated as a single ventricle, then converted to biventricular circulation, with prior mechanical and bioprosthetic mitral valve replacements (the latter for menorrhagia, outside our care), presented in cardiogenic shock with prosthetic mitral stenosis and acute left atrial thrombus. Hypoplastic peripheral vessels precluded MCS. Salvage valve-in-valve was performed with bilateral cerebral protection, FlowTriever thrombectomy (Inari Medical), and a 26-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).

DISCUSSION: Transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve can be lifesaving in adults with repaired CHD when intracardiac thrombus is present, and MCS is unavailable.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In highly selected, life-threatening presentations without alternatives, salvage transcatheter mitral intervention may be considered despite intracardiac thrombus. Peripheral vascular anatomy must be evaluated preprocedurally in complex CHD.

articles.title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort.

METHODS: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management.

RESULTS: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model.

CONCLUSIONS: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

articles.title: Access to Assisted Reproductive Technology Services in Brazil: A Descriptive Analysis of SisEmbrio Data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To conduct a descriptive analysis of data from the National Embryo Production System (SisEmbrio) to characterize access to assisted reproductive technology (ART) services in Brazil.

METHOD: Data from SisEmbrio for the period from 2020 to 2024 were used, along with data from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics, Google Maps, and clinical guidelines on ART.

RESULTS: The data showed growth in the number of ART centers, as well as increases in the number of frozen embryos and completed cycles during the study period. Following the increase in embryo cryopreservation, a higher absolute number of ART procedures was observed among women aged ≥35 years. The analysis also showed that most clinics are privately operated and that their geographic distribution is concentrated mainly in large urban centers.

CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that access to ART services in Brazil remains limited. SisEmbrio data reaffirm barriers previously identified in the literature. These challenges restrict the expansion of access and underscore the need for structural changes to promote greater equity in care for the target population.

articles.title: Exercise attenuates hypertension-induced renal dysfunction alongside changes in purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension-induced renal dysfunction is associated with endothelial dysfunction and changes in purinergic signaling. Exercise training can attenuate hypertension-related disturbances in purinergic pathways, but its effects on renal purine metabolism and purinergic receptor expression remain poorly understood. We investigated these responses in L-NAME-induced hypertensive rats.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats were assigned to Control, Exercise, L-NAME, and Exercise L-NAME groups (n = 10/group). Hypertension was induced by chronic Nω-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) administration, and exercise consisted of 6 weeks of swimming training. Blood pressure, renal nitric oxide metabolites (NOx), renal function, serum ATP, renal ATP, ADP, and AMP hydrolysis, ADA activity, and renal expression of purinergic enzymes and P1, P2X, and P2Y receptors were evaluated.

RESULTS: L-NAME increased blood pressure, serum ATP, urea, and creatinine and reduced renal NOx concentrations. Hypertensive animals showed increased CD39 and ADA expression, increased ATP hydrolysis and ADA activity, reduced A1 and A2A receptor expression, and increased P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Exercise attenuated serum ATP accumulation, changes in renal purine-metabolizing enzyme activities, and ADA expression; preserved A2A and P2X1 expression; and attenuated increases in P2X4 and P2X7 expression. Significant correlations among serum ATP, creatinine, A2A, and P2X7 expression occurred exclusively in L-NAME-treated animals.

CONCLUSIONS: L-NAME-induced hypertension is associated with renal dysfunction, changes in renal purine metabolism, and selective changes in purinergic receptor gene expression. Swimming training attenuated several of these responses and improved renal function. These findings identify renal purine metabolism and A2A and P2X7 receptor expression as potential pathways associated with exercise-induced protection that warrant further mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: System Delay and Mortality in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicentre, Retrospective, Observational Study in Seoul.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prompt recognition and early management of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are crucial for improving outcomes. This study investigates the association between system delay and in-hospital mortality in patients with STEMI.

METHODS: Using data from the Seoul GOLDEN-time emergency medical system registry, a multicentre retrospective registry in Seoul, this study analysed patients with STEMI who were transported to an emergency department via emergency medical service for cardiac complaints between July 2020 and December 2022. System delay included the response time (first medical contact to an ambulance on the scene), scene time (ambulance on the scene to departure), scene-to-door time (departure to hospital arrival), and door-to-balloon time.

RESULTS: Among 654 patients with STEMI who received percutaneous coronary intervention, survivors had shorter overall system delay, prehospital time, scene time, scene-to-door time, and door-to-balloon time than non-survivors. A system delay > 127.5 minutes was associated with high mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.07; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-4.13). Prolonged prehospital time (aOR, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.16-4.95), scene time (aOR, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.24-5.75), and door-to-balloon time (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.09-4.39) were each independently associated with mortality.

CONCLUSION: Prolonged system delays were associated with increased in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the need for a comprehensive, system-level approach to reducing system delay across the entire STEMI care pathway.

articles.title: Home-Based Primary Care for Aging Populations in Korea: Practices, Competencies, and Training Demands of Providers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As the Korean population ages rapidly, the need for home-based primary care (HBPC) is increasing, particularly among individuals with mobility limitations. In 2022, the Korean government launched Home-Based Primary Care for Long-Term Care Recipients (HBPC-LTC), but data on its operational status, service scope, and educational needs are limited.

METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted from October 21 to November 1, 2024. A total of 57 out of 95 certified HBPC-LTC centers (60.0%) responded to the survey. The survey collected data on institutional characteristics, service delivery, operational challenges, and training requirements. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze the data.

RESULTS: Most HBPC-LTC centers are private clinics, with limited public sector participation. Services focus on prescribing medications, consultations, and wound care, while few provide advanced procedures or 24-hour care. Centers reported difficulties with staffing, patient recruitment, and collaboration with administrative systems. Participation in palliative care and integrated service programs remains low. Although most providers completed basic training, there was a strong demand for multidisciplinary and practice-based education. International comparisons revealed insufficient systemic support in Korea, including standardized service guidelines and coordinated governance.

CONCLUSION: HBPC-LTC centers provide essential services but face challenges in workforce structure, service scope, inter-agency collaboration, and training. Strengthening Korea's HBPC-LTC model requires expanded institutional support, improved infrastructure, and tailored education programs that reflect clinical complexity.

articles.title: Prevalence, Diagnostic Role, and Clinical Features of Zinc Transporter 8 Autoantibody in Korean Children and Adolescents With Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zinc transporter 8 autoantibodies (ZnT8As) are biomarkers of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). We evaluated its prevalence, diagnostic utility, and clinical characteristics in Korean children and adolescents with diabetes.

METHODS: ZnT8A levels were measured in 288 patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) (aged < 19 years, diagnosed with DM between 2019 and 2025) at two tertiary hospitals and in 100 healthy controls (19-39 years). The ZnT8A positivity cutoff was ≥ 15 U/mL. Clinical features were compared between ZnT8A-positive and ZnT8A-negative patients across diabetes subtypes.

RESULTS: The study included 178 patients with T1DM (60.4%, mean age 9.7 years), 110 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (39.6%, mean age 14.1 years), and 100 controls. The positivity rates in patients with T1DM, T2DM, and controls were 94.9%, 1.8%, and 5.0% for any islet autoantibodies; 74.7%, 0%, and 0% for ZnT8A; 74.7%, 0%, and 5.0% for autoantibody to tyrosine phosphatase-related islet antigen 2 (IA-2A); 62.4%, 1.8%, and 0% for autoantibody to glutamic acid decarboxylase (GADA); and 23.6%, 0%, and 0% for insulin autoantibody (IAA), respectively. Among patients with T1DM, the proportions of individuals who were positive for only a single autoantibody were as follows: 2.8% for ZnT8A alone, 4.5% for IA-2A alone, 3.9% for GADA alone, and 2.2% for IAA alone. ZnT8A-positive T1DM patients were younger and more often prepubertal compared to ZnT8A-negative T1DM patients.

CONCLUSION: ZnT8As are highly prevalent in younger, prepubertal Korean patients with T1DM and absent in patients with T2DM and healthy controls, suggesting its strong diagnostic specificity.

articles.title: 3D network carbon nanotube film supported FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy nanoparticles for integrated adsorption and detoxification of sulfur mustard simulant.
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) films with interconnected three-dimensional (3D) networks are ideal porous scaffolds for high-entropy alloy (HEA) immobilization, enabling integrated adsorption and detoxification of chemical warfare agents. Herein, FeCoNiCrMn HEA nanoparticles (50-150 nm) were uniformly anchored on 3D CNT film networks via ultrafast carbothermal shock (CTs) within 55 ms. The obtained FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs show a single-phase face-centered cubic structure with near-equiatomic composition and multivalent metal sites. At 25 °C and 50% RH, the composite delivers a high equilibrium adsorption capacity of 636 mg g-1 for 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (2-CEES) vapor, a sulfur mustard simulant. A 98.5% degradation efficiency is reached within 12 h via a tandem redox pathway: reductive dechlorination of 2-CEES to hydroxyethyl ethyl sulfide followed by partial C-S bond oxidation, with C-S cleavage as the rate-limiting step. This work provides an ultrafast strategy to construct HEA/carbon nanotube composites and highlights their potential as advanced carbon-based materials for chemical warfare agent detoxification.

articles.title: Pixel classifier-based image analysis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis in mice.
articles.abstract: Image analysis in histologic assessments has increasingly gained traction in comparative pathology and biomedical research. However, application has been limited by a knowledge gap, particularly for veterinary pathologists without a strong background in coding-intensive image analysis. This study describes a quantitative image analysis pipeline for liver pathology in a special diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) mouse model, using the existing open-source, graphic user interface-based program QuPath. A machine learning-based pixel classifier was trained on annotations made in 7 digitized hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides to detect normal hepatocytes, macrosteatosis, microsteatosis, vessels, and inflammation. Macrosteatosis annotations were then segmented via pixel thresholding to quantify lipid droplets. Post-processing pixel thresholding was applied to quantify fibrosis in picrosirius red-stained slides and lipid droplets in H&E-stained slides. Results were benchmarked against traditional manual grading by the nonalcoholic steatohepatitis activity score (NAS). Our results revealed a significantly larger macrosteatosis area percentage in MASH diet mice than in regular diet controls. The percentage areas for steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis strongly correlated with increasing histopathologic scores. Unlike traditional ordinal severity scoring like NAS, this approach generates continuous, quantitative data suitable for parametric statistical analysis. This method is scalable and accessible, requires no coding expertise or commercial software, and offers a blueprint for generating truly quantitative histopathology data to veterinary pathologists and others engaged in MASH research.

articles.title: Emerging insights into amino acid metabolism in the heart: implications for cardiovascular diseases and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: As a metabolically versatile organ, the heart is capable of generating energy from a wide range of substrates. Although fatty acid and glucose metabolism in the heart have been extensively studied, the contribution of amino acid metabolism to cardiac physiology and disease is gaining increasing attention. A range of amino acids, including branched-chain amino acids, glutamine and glutamate, asparagine, glycine, tryptophan and alanine, play integral roles in signalling pathways that orchestrate key adaptive and maladaptive changes in the myocardium, under both physiological and pathological stress. Dysregulation of these pathways is associated with cardiovascular disease such as heart failure, hypertension, myocardial infarction and atherosclerosis, via mechanisms involving impaired mitochondrial function, oxidative stress and inflammation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of amino acid metabolism in the heart, including sulphur amino acids, their role in relation to cardiovascular disease and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting amino acid metabolism in the heart. Finally, this review also discusses current and ongoing clinical trials targeting amino acid metabolism with the aim of finding potential therapeutic targets in cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: The Goldilocks Principle in Neonatal Fluids: Finding the Just-Right Balance.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract: The impact of disrupted fluid balance on outcomes in critically unwell children and adults is well described. Recent literature in neonates has demonstrated that both fluid overload and excessive postnatal fluid losses are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. However, neonates present unique challenges in measuring fluid balance as well as defining, preventing and treating fluid overload due to developmental changes in renal physiology, high trans-epidermal losses, nutritional requirements and limitations in available renal replacement therapies. In the neonatal intensive care unit, significant variations exist in renal physiology and expected fluid shifts between neonates of differing gestational and chronological ages, as well as in the neonate's underlying co-morbidities. As such, approaches to fluid balance should be individualised to each patient. Recognition of fluid balance as a vital sign, with implications as relevant as a patient's cardiorespiratory status, provides an important opportunity to improve outcomes. In this scoping review we discuss neonatal renal and fluid balance physiology, and present contemporary best practice strategies for measuring fluid balance. We explore the currently available prevention and treatment options for fluid overload in Australia and New Zealand as well as technological advances in neonatally-adapted haemodialysis (HD) and continuous renal replacement therapies emerging internationally.

articles.title: The fight of innate immunity and abnormal cannabinoids against Candida infection.
articles.abstract: Candida species represent the most clinically significant fungal pathogens in humans, with invasive candidiasis carrying a mortality of 30%-40% in critically ill patients despite modern antifungal therapy. The innate immune system - through the coordinated and specific activities of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, mast cells and eosinophils - constitute the primary and most consequential biological defence against Candida invasion. Abnormal cannabinoids (Abn-CBDs), a structurally distinctive class of synthetic lipid compounds with non-psychoactive properties and regioisomeric configurations, critically distinct from classical cannabinoids in their independence from CB1 and CB2 receptor signalling, have emerged as a novel and pharmacologically compelling class of antifungal compounds. This review integrates the current understanding of innate immune cell antifungal mechanisms with the emerging pharmacology of abnormal cannabinoids, examines the direct antifungal and immunomodulatory properties of Abn-CBDs, and critically addresses the tripartite contest between innate immunity, abnormal cannabinoids and Candida's formidable evasion repertoire.

articles.title: How Does Mobile Health Impact Exclusive Breastfeeding in Populations Facing Vulnerability or Disparity? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions have been identified as effective technologies for promoting exclusive breastfeeding (EBF). However, it is still unclear how mHealth impacts different populations, especially those in situations of vulnerability and/or disparity.

OBJECTIVES: To analyze the impact of mHealth interventions on promoting EBF in populations in situations of vulnerability and/or disparity, compared with usual breastfeeding care.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review with meta-analysis. Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) were systematically identified through searches of the PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2 statistics. Statistical analyses were conducted using the R software.

RESULTS: Of the 965 studies retrieved, 18 RCTs were incorporated into the qualitative synthesis, and 15 RCTs were incorporated into the meta-analysis. mHealth effectively increased EBF at 3 months postnatal (RR = 1.21; 95% CI: [1.10-1.33]; p = 0.001; I2 = 64.2%, GRADE: high), corresponding to 129 (95% CI: 61-202) additional cases per 1000 participants, with direct counseling showing the most consistent effect among intervention types. In infants <2 months, mHealth also demonstrated efficacy in increasing EBF, but the certainty of this evidence was considered low. There was no effectiveness in the other periods analyzed.

CONCLUSIONS: Although mHealth interventions have the potential to increase EBF in populations in situations of vulnerability and/or disparity, this effectiveness has proven to be limited. There is a need for mHealth interventions that focus on crucial periods related to breastfeeding cessation, consider the impact that vulnerabilities may have on the success of maintaining breastfeeding across different contexts, including the most complex ones (multiple vulnerabilities), and account for intervention type and intensity, prioritizing direct counseling delivered through high-intensity modalities.

articles.title: Beyond Individual Responsibility: A Qualitative Study of Capability, Motivation, and Opportunity for Self-Management in Early-Onset Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of the study was to explore daily experiences of age-specific unmet needs among adults with early-onset type 2 diabetes across the care trajectory.

METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design was used. Participants were recruited from university-affiliated endocrinology clinics and online diabetes communities and via self-referral in Korea. Thirty-five adults (54.3% men) with early-onset type 2 diabetes were included. Interviews (40-90 minutes) were conducted between June 2023 and February 2024 in person (n = 12) or via video calls (n = 23). Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with investigator triangulation.

RESULTS: Findings were synthesized using the capability, opportunities, and motivation-behavior model. Capability developed cumulatively through repeated trial-and-error attempts and vicarious experiences, strengthening over time. Opportunity reflected a health care context characterized by early diabetes detection but less focus on prevention and follow-up treatment. Motivation, shaped by illness perceptions, health care provider support, and evolving self-identity, facilitated the link between capability and opportunity.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified age-specific educational and support needs among individuals with early-onset type 2 diabetes. Optimal care requires multifaceted strategies, including person-centered coaching, provider training, age-specific education content, supportive services and environments, and tailored public health messaging, to promote self-management. Interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for implementation.

articles.title: Thirteen years of environmental surveillance of ESKAPE organisms and Escherichia coli in an equine hospital: Informing infection control.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacteria from the ESKAPE group (i.e., Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter species) and Escherichia coli are frequently multidrug-resistant and can be associated with healthcare-associated infections, an increasing concern for veterinary settings.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the environmental prevalence of ESKAPE and E. coli on surfaces which can act as reservoirs of infection in clinical areas in equine hospitals.

STUDY DESIGN: Observational study.

METHODS: Routine environmental sampling was performed in one busy equine hospital with Swiffer® wipes to screen surfaces from high-risk areas (e.g., surgical theatres, intensive care unit [ICU], isolation unit), equipment (e.g., endotracheal tubes) and high-touch areas (e.g., keyboards) following selective species-specific protocols for each target organism. Monitoring hand-hygiene of hospital staff and students was by hand-plate sampling. After a pilot phase E. faecium was excluded from routine screening.

RESULTS: Nine hundred and ninety-five environmental and hand-plate samples were collected from April 2010 to February 2023. The overall E. coli-SKAPE (E. coli, methicillin-resistant S. aureus [MRSA], K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa and Enterobacter spp.) prevalence was 37.9%, where E. coli was the most (and K. pneumoniae the least) common target organism identified (18.0% and 1.7% respectively). E. coli was most prevalent in general stables and yards (37.7%) and offices (25.7%). Enterobacter spp. was the main organism in the environmental samples from ICU (24.2%) and isolation unit (22.9%, along with E. coli). Concerningly, hand-plate sampling showed that MRSA was the most common organism detected on hands (8.4%), followed by A. baumannii (5.2%) and E. cloacae (3.9%); however, E. coli, P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae were not found in these samples.

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Inconsistent sampling limited longitudinal analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: We generated baseline environmental contamination data and demonstrated high E. coli-SKAPE hospital surface and hand contamination, informing infection control to prevent environment-to-patient cross-transmission.

articles.title: Use of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1 Receptor Agonists, and DPP-4 Inhibitors in Incident Hyponatremia in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Target Trial Emulations.
articles.abstract: Hyponatremia poses risks in type 2 diabetes, yet comparative electrolyte safety across glucose-lowering therapies remains unclear. We evaluated the risk of incident hyponatremia associated with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors in real-world practice. Using electronic health records from 155 healthcare organizations in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted multicenter active-comparator, new-user target trial emulations with 1:1 propensity score matching. For each pairwise comparison, adults with type 2 diabetes initiating either drug class, with no record of either class during the preceding 365 days, were included. The primary outcome was incident hyponatremia (ICD-10-CM E87.1 or serum sodium ≤ 135 mmol/L); sensitivity outcomes included diagnosis-only, laboratory-only, and stricter laboratory thresholds. Among more than 300,000 matched pairs per comparison, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were each associated with a 15% lower hazard of hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors (hazard ratio [HR], 0.850; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.842-0.858 and HR, 0.847; 95% CI: 0.838-0.856). The lower risk persisted at stricter sodium thresholds and across clinically relevant subgroups, including patients with heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or high-risk medications use. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were broadly comparable (HR, 0.962; 95% CI: 0.952-0.971). Positive and negative control outcomes were consistent with expectations. Overall, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were associated with a lower risk of incident hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors. These real-world findings provide reassurance regarding the electrolyte safety of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs, complementing their established cardiorenal benefits.

articles.title: No transfusion-transmitted cytomegalovirus infections in neonates receiving leukoreduced-only blood products.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm, very low birth weight (VLBW) neonates have worse outcomes from cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, which can be transfusion-transmitted (TT-CMV). Mitigation strategies include leukoreduction (LR) and using CMV seronegative donors, which are costly and logistically challenging. We aim to characterize the risk of TT-CMV using the LR-only strategy.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This is a retrospective review of all VLBW preterm neonates treated over a 50-month period at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Patients were characterized by CMV status and grouped by blood products received. CMV infection was classified as congenital and excluded, or postnatal, of which potential exposures were identified. Odds ratios (OR) for postnatal infection were calculated and a Firth penalized logistic regression was performed.
