RESULTS: Nine hundred and sixty-three patients were included, of whom seven were excluded for congenital CMV. Among the remainder, 333 received red blood cells (RBCs), 16 received platelets, and 132 received both. There were no cases of postnatal CMV in the non-transfused or platelet-only groups, two cases in the RBC-only group (OR 7.2, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.3-149.8; p = .20), and three cases in the platelet and RBC group (OR 25.7, 95% CI 1.3-500.8; p = .03). Accounting for birth weight and gestational age eliminated the association between transfusion and postnatal CMV (OR 2.8, 95% CI 0.2-450.3; p = .53).

DISCUSSION: There were no demonstrable cases of TT-CMV in 481 preterm, VLBW infants who received leukoreduced-only blood products. In five cases of postnatal CMV, alternative sources of exposure were present. dLR-only is a safe TT-CMV mitigation strategy and is more logistically manageable than alternatives.

articles.title: Cost-utility analysis of comprehensive periodontal management for chronic kidney disease progression in Chinese adults with periodontitis in China: A seven-state Markov cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Observational evidence suggests that periodontitis is associated with the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in Chinese adults, and that periodontal care may be associated with a lower risk of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Because this evidence is observational rather than causal, whether comprehensive periodontal management is a cost-effective use of resources in CKD remains uncertain and has not been formally evaluated within the Chinese healthcare system.

METHODS: We developed a seven-state Markov cohort model (CKD stages G1-G5/ESRD + Death) for a Chinese adult cohort aged 50 years at entry. Three strategies were compared: usual care (UC), scaling and root planing plus periodontal maintenance (SRP), and comprehensive intensive management (CIM). Clinical parameters were derived from verified published sources. Costs (CNY 2024) and health utility values (EQ-5D-5L, Chinese tariff) were extracted from peer-reviewed literature. Model outcomes included discounted lifetime costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 40-year horizon with a 3.5% annual discount rate. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was CNY 90,000/QALY (approximately 1× Chinese GDP per capita, 2024). Sensitivity analyses included one-way deterministic sensitivity analysis (DSA), probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA; n = 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations), expected value of perfect information (EVPI), budget impact analysis (BIA), and a break-even time-horizon analysis. In addition, the CKD transition probabilities were re-derived from published longitudinal cohort data (C-STRIDE; a 10-year Taiwanese integrated kidney-care cohort) and cross-checked against an externally validated Asian multi-state Markov model; multi-factor scenario, threshold and value-of-information analyses were added; and the comprehensive-management strategy was decomposed against the EFP S3-level guideline, including a conservative scaling-and-root-planing-only floor.

RESULTS: In the early CKD subgroup (G1-G2 dominant), SRP and CIM produced incremental cost-utility ratios (ICURs) of CNY 217,600/QALY and CNY 109,700/QALY, respectively, both exceeding the WTP threshold (not cost-effective). In the advanced CKD subgroup (G3-G4 dominant), both SRP and CIM were dominant strategies (lower lifetime costs and higher QALYs vs UC), driven by substantial cost savings from avoided dialysis (SRP: -CNY 21,100; CIM: -CNY 40,300 per patient over 40 years). The probability of cost-effectiveness at WTP = CNY 90,000/QALY was 27%-32% (early CKD) versus ≥ 97% (advanced CKD). For advanced CKD, the break-even time horizon was 5 years. The EVPI was CNY 1190/patient for early CKD, indicating that further research is economically justified. Under the literature-anchored parameters, the advanced-CKD result remained robustly dominant across scenarios, probabilistic (probability of cost-effectiveness ≈ 99.9%) and conservative scaling-only analyses, whereas the early-CKD result was sensitive to the contested assumptions (probability of cost-effectiveness ≈ 50%) and is therefore reported as exploratory.

CONCLUSIONS: Under a set of exploratory assumptions-and conditional on the observational (non-causal) association between periodontal scaling and reduced ESRD risk-comprehensive periodontal management may be economically attractive in patients with advanced CKD (G3-G4), where the result was robust to literature-anchored transition probabilities and to scenario, probabilistic and conservative scaling-only analyses. In early CKD, the cost-effectiveness is uncertain (probability of cost-effectiveness ≈ 50%). These exploratory scenario analyses identify early CKD as a high-value target for a future randomized controlled trial rather than a basis for immediate policy mandates.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Gum disease (periodontitis) and kidney disease (chronic kidney disease, CKD) are both very common in China and are linked: people with severe gum disease progress to kidney failure faster. This study used a computer model to ask whether treating gum disease is worth the cost for the Chinese health system. We compared three approaches-no extra gum care, standard deep cleaning, and intensive gum treatment-in patients with different stages of CKD. For patients with moderate-to-advanced CKD (stages G3-G4), intensive gum treatment saved money and improved health at the same time, mainly because it delayed the need for dialysis, which costs around CNY 95,000 per year. The savings paid for the treatment within 5 years. For patients with early CKD (stages G1-G2), gum treatment was not cost-effective under cautious assumptions, but became cost-effective when realistic upper-end estimates were used. The uncertainty around the early-CKD result is large enough to justify a clinical trial in China. These exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive periodontal care may be economically attractive in advanced CKD and warrant confirmation in a prospective study before any change to China's national health-insurance (NHSA) policy; because the underlying evidence is observational, they do not by themselves establish that periodontal treatment slows kidney disease progression.

articles.title: Oral health knowledge and diagnostic confidence among non-dental healthcare professionals: A comparative study between Chile and Spain.
articles.abstract: Oral health is increasingly recognized as a key component of general health; however, non-dental healthcare professionals often lack the knowledge and confidence required to address it. This study aimed to compare oral health knowledge, perceptions, and diagnostic confidence among non-dental healthcare professionals in Chile and Spain.A cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals in both countries using a culturally adapted and validated questionnaire. The survey assessed training, perceived importance of oral health, self-reported confidence, and diagnostic ability through clinical scenarios. Descriptive statistics, chi-square and t-tests, and linear regression analyses were performed. A total of 420 participants were included (Spain: 212; Chile: 208), of whom 58.8% were physicians. While most participants (93.1%) recognized the importance of oral health assessments, the majority reported low confidence in diagnosis (76.7%) and management (84.1%). Prior training was limited, particularly in Spain (0.5% vs. 48.1% in Chile; p<0.001). Chilean participants achieved higher diagnostic scores than Spanish participants (3.30 vs. 2.50; p<0.001), and physicians outperformed nurses and other professionals (3.12 vs. 2.60; p<0.001). Recognition was high for aphthous ulcer (95.5%) but substantially lower for conditions such as stomatitis (31.7%) and xerostomia (50.7%). Most participants (94.8%) reported a need for additional training. Non-dental healthcare professionals demonstrate substantial gaps in oral health knowledge and confidence despite recognizing its importance. Strengthening undergraduate and postgraduate education, alongside structured interprofessional collaboration, is essential to improve early detection, referral, and comprehensive care, particularly in aging populations with an increasing burden of oral disease.

articles.title: Family Physicians Prescribing Physical Activity in Kansas: Frequency, Motivation, and Resources Desired.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeThis study aimed to assess how frequently family physicians in Kansas prescribe physical activity (PA), what motivates them to do so, and what resources they deem necessary for effective PA prescription.DesignA cross-sectional survey was distributed through a preexisting mailing list that physicians had previously signed up for.SettingFamily medicine practices across the state of Kansas.ParticipantsOf the 393 physicians contacted, 66 initiated the survey and 62 completed it, yielding a 16% response rate.MeasuresThe survey assessed PA prescription frequency and methods, and the importance of various resources (eg, community programs, insurance coverage, current procedural terminology (CPT) codes).AnalysisDescriptive statistics and inferential tests (likelihood ratio chi-square, Fisher's exact) were conducted. Bonferroni and False Discovery Rate corrections addressed multiple comparisons. Significance was set at P < .05.ResultsOf the 62 physicians who completed the survey, 95% (n = 59) reported assessing patients' PA levels; among all 66 physicians who began the survey, 95% (n = 63) reported prescribing at least one form of PA. Most common methods for assessing and prescribing PA included: conversation (83%), recommendation (73%), and referral to programs (38%); only 5% wrote formal prescriptions. Community program availability was very important to 48% and insurance coverage was very important to 21%. Electronic referrals and CPT codes were minimally important to most.ConclusionAlthough reported PA prescription is common, written prescriptions are uncommon. Community-based, evidence-supported programs and insurance coverage are key motivators. Given the low response rate, findings likely reflect a self-selected group of respondents rather than family physicians in Kansas broadly. Limited sample size and potential question ambiguity limit generalizability.

articles.title: From catheter to infection: Risk factors for central venous catheter-related infections in the intensive care unit.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A substantial proportion of critically ill patients require central venous catheterization, with infection being the most significant complication. Catheter-related infections may increase ICU length of stay, morbidity, and mortality. This study aimed to identify factors contributing to these infections.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 1985 central venous and hemodialysis catheters meeting predefined inclusion criteria. Catheters were classified by insertion site as femoral, internal jugular, or subclavian. Catheter-related infections were assessed as percentages and as incidence per 1000 catheter-days. Infection risks were compared using relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Catheter-related infection occurred in 309 catheters (15.6%). Infection rates did not differ significantly by insertion site when analyzed as percentages (femoral 16.7%, internal jugular 15.3%, subclavian 13.6%; p = 0.474). However, incidence analysis accounting for dwell time showed a higher infection incidence in femoral catheters (13.9 per 1000 catheter-days). Compared with subclavian catheters, femoral catheters had a significantly increased infection risk (RR 1.56; 95% CI 1.07-2.28).

CONCLUSION: Central venous catheter-related infections are more frequent in femoral sites in a time-dependent manner. Early replacement of femoral catheters is important to reduce infection risk. In clinical practice, prevention strategies should consider not only the insertion site but also expected duration of use, frequency of access, catheter type, patient characteristics, and infection control measures.

articles.title: Recurrent Conjunctival Nodule Followed by Spontaneous Extrusion of Onchocerca lupi: A Rare Zoonotic Filarial Infection.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract: Onchocerca lupi is a zoonotic nematode primarily affecting dogs, rarely causing human ocular infections. This report presents a rare case of human ocular O. lupi infection from Türkiye with a distinct clinical feature. A 19-year-old woman presented with a 2-week history of redness in her right eye. Examination revealed a subconjunctival nodule in the superotemporal quadrant. Orbital MRI showed a heterogeneous hypointense lesion in the right upper eyelid. Following an excisional biopsy and topical treatment, symptoms partially regressed, and the patient was monitored. One year later, she returned with recurrent hyperemia and mucopurulent discharge. During a conjunctival swab collection, a subconjunctival nematode was observed and extracted. Microscopic analysis confirmed adult O. lupi morphology, showing a multilayered cuticle with undulating annular ridges. This case contributes valuable insights into the literature regarding recurrent nodular presentation and delayed spontaneous extrusion.

articles.title: Molecular Screening of Arthropod-Borne Pathogens in Domestic Cats from Northeast of Mexico: First Report of Infection and Coinfection in the Country.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cat-associated pathogens transmitted by arthropods are of global public and veterinary health importance. Cats, as well as dogs, have historically coexisted with humans in rural and urban environments. However, studies on microorganisms associated with cats are much less extensive than those on dogs.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Therefore, the present study aims to document natural infections of Anaplasma, Bartonella, Ehrlichia, and Rickettsia in cats (Felis catus) using PCR in northeastern Mexico. Blood samples were collected from cats with the support of the Canine and Feline Control Centers and veterinary clinics. Specific pathogens were amplified by PCR, and some positive samples were sequenced.

RESULTS: A total of 250 cats were obtained from three municipalities in Nuevo Leon, Mexico. Specific PCR testing showed that 33.6% (84/250) cats tested positive for at least one of the pathogens. The overall natural pathogen infection rates were Ehrlichia with 20.8% (52/250), followed by Anaplasma with 8% (20/250), Bartonella with 3.2% (8/250), and Rickettsia with 1.6% (4/250). Phylogenetic analysis placed the Bartonella sequence within a well-supported B. quintana clade. The partial 16S rRNA sequence obtained from Ehrlichia was conservatively classified as Ehrlichia sp. closely related to E. chaffeensis.

CONCLUSION: These findings document exposure or infection of cats with multiple arthropod-borne bacteria and support continued molecular surveillance using additional discriminatory loci.

articles.title: Prolonged Sedentary Behavior and Cardiometabolic Risk in Older Women With and Without Type 2 Diabetes: The SitWise Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) significantly increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in women. Sedentary behavior (SB) may confer risks independent of physical activity. This study examined associations between SB accumulation patterns and cardiometabolic risk markers in older women with and without T2D. We hypothesized that prolonged sedentary bouts (≥60 minutes) would correlate with poorer risk profiles.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of women aged 60-76 years of similar body mass index with (n = 9) and without (n = 11) uncomplicated T2D. Accelerometers assessed total SB and time in bouts ≥60 minutes. Risk markers included insulin sensitivity (Matsuda Index and glucose infusion rate [GIR]) and skeletal muscle microvascular function (near-infrared spectroscopy-derived oxygen saturation). Linear regression models adjusted for physical activity and T2D status.

RESULTS: Each 1-hour increase in sedentary bouts ≥60 minutes corresponded weakly, though not statistically significantly, with decreased GIR (95% confidence interval [CI] [-1.24, 0.07], p = 0.08). Other associations differed by diabetes status: in women with T2D, the Matsuda index increased by 1.65 per hour of prolonged SB (95% CI: [0.45, 2.85], p = 0.02). Conversely, muscle oxygen saturation during exercise showed a T2D-specific decline; for every additional hour in ≥60-minutes bouts, oxygen saturation was lower by -0.74% (95% CI: [-1.25, -0.23], p = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged SB was associated with lower insulin sensitivity regardless of diabetes status and with impaired muscle oxygenation during exercise in women with T2D. Future research should determine if targeting SB accumulation patterns can reduce CVD risk in older adults with T2D.Sedentary Behavior in Older Women With and Without Type 2 Diabetes (SitWise); NCT04262128; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04262128.

articles.title: Methadone to manage pain in pregnancy at Te Toka Tumai Auckland City Hospital: A retrospective observational analysis.
articles.abstract: Pain during pregnancy is common, yet evidence-based management remains limited. While non-pharmacological treatments are first-line, severe pain may necessitate pharmacological intervention. Methadone is well studied for opioid use disorder, but its role in acute pain management during pregnancy is less defined. This retrospective observational study examined pregnant patients prescribed low-dose methadone for pain management between January 2022 and December 2023 at a tertiary multidisciplinary pain service. Patients receiving opioid substitution therapy were excluded. Data on methadone dosing, pain scores, maternal side effects, and neonatal outcomes were analysed. Twenty-three patients were identified, with 22 included in the analysis. The mean gestation at methadone initiation was 29.7 weeks (standard deviation 5.1), and the median starting dose was 5 mg per day (interquartile range 2.5 to 5). Pain severity decreased significantly: the proportion reporting severe pain at rest fell from 82% to 14% at 48 hours (absolute risk reduction (ARR) 68%, number needed to treat (NNT) 2), and the proportion reporting severe pain with movement fell from 95% to 32% (ARR 64%, NNT 2), with sustained improvement at 4 weeks. Side-effects included sedation (14%) and nausea (23%) and were generally well tolerated. Among 19 neonates, no cases of neonatal abstinence syndrome were observed. Six required neonatal intensive care unit admission, but none for opioid withdrawal. These findings suggest that low-dose methadone, when used within a closely monitored multidisciplinary setting, may provide effective pain relief in the pregnant patient without significant neonatal harm. However, this high level of oversight may limit generalisability to other care settings. Further research is warranted to guide safe implementation and optimise dosing.

articles.title: Prognostic significance of nucleated red blood cells in trauma patients.
articles.abstract: Nucleated red blood cells are early erythroid precursors typically confined to the bone marrow. Their appearance in peripheral blood reflects stress erythropoiesis and has been linked to hypoxia and systemic inflammation. While nucleated red blood cells have prognostic value in sepsis and critical illness, their significance in trauma remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of nucleated red blood cells during the first 10 days in the intensive care unit following severe trauma, and their association with 30-day mortality. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including 1636 adult trauma patients admitted to the Reims Level-1 Trauma Center between January 2019 and March 2025, recorded in the TraumaBase© registry. Nucleated red blood cell counts were measured daily for the first 10 intensive care unit days. K-means clustering identified four nucleated red blood cell phenotypes based on temporal patterns. Outcomes included 10- and 30-day mortality, incidence of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Survival analyses used Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, Injury Severity Score, Simplified Acute Physiology Score II, and the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, and propensity-weighted regression assessed dichotomised nucleated red blood cell status. Nucleated red blood cells were detected in 221 patients (13.5%). Phenotype classification revealed: transient early nucleated red blood cells (phenotype 1), single peak (phenotype 2), multiple intermittent peaks (phenotype 3), and persistent elevation (phenotype 4). Phenotype 2 was associated with reduced 10-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.06, 95% confidence intervals 0.01-0.46), while phenotype 4 exhibited markedly increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.6, 95% confidence intervals 2.23-41.4, P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell+ patients had higher risks of acute respiratory distress syndrome, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and 30-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves confirmed significant differences in survival across phenotypes (log-rank P < 0.001). Nucleated red blood cell presence, particularly persistent elevation, identifies trauma patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes. Routine, daily nucleated red blood cell monitoring may serve as a simple, low-cost prognostic tool in intensive care unit trauma care. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and integrate nucleated red blood cell dynamics into risk stratification.

articles.title: Current nutrition practices and additional reimbursement of intensive care units in Japan: A cross-sectional survey study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A unique reimbursement for early nutrition intervention was introduced in Japan to promote guideline-adherent nutrition practices in intensive care units. However, the current status of nutrition therapy implementation across Japanese intensive care units remains unclear.

METHODS: This cross-sectional survey study investigated intensive care units nationwide, led by the Japanese Society of Intensive Care Medicine. Facility characteristics, nutrition management structure, nutrition practices (nutritional assessment, nutrition planning, therapy implementation, and monitoring), and dietitian involvement were assessed. We examined relationships between reimbursement claim status and nutrition practices.

RESULTS: Among 337 intensive care units, most performed nutritional assessment using at least one standardized tool and planned nutrition targeting 25-30 kcal/kg/day for energy and 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day for protein. Enteral nutrition-related practices were widely implemented. Of these, 255 intensive care units (75.7%) claimed the reimbursement; incentivized units more frequently implemented written enteral nutrition protocols, dietitian-conducted nutritional assessments, dietitian-led enteral nutrition design, and enteral nutrition initiation within 48 h. However, Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition assessment, indirect calorimetry, written protocols for parenteral nutrition/diarrhea/constipation, dietitian-led parenteral nutrition design, and post-intensive care unit nutritional follow-up remained limited even in incentivized units.

CONCLUSION: In Japan, reimbursement incentives were positively associated with higher implementation of nutritional assessment, enteral nutrition-related practices, and dietitian involvement. To further advance specialized nutritional care, simultaneous system development may be warranted.

articles.title: Oral Irrigation and Microbiome Remodeling after Oral Cancer Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Patients with oral cancer undergoing free flap reconstruction face significant surgical trauma, making the prevention of postoperative wound infection and the maintenance of oral microecological balance critical. This study systematically evaluated oral microbiome changes before and after surgery and assessed the effectiveness of postoperative oral irrigation using 2 different regimens. In an exploratory randomized controlled trial, 60 patients were assigned to receive oral irrigation with either bipolar water or a combination of hydrogen peroxide and sodium bicarbonate solution. Saliva and irrigation samples were collected at 7 time points, preoperatively and before and 5 minutes after oral irrigation on postoperative days 1, 4, and 7, and analyzed using specialized sequencing techniques to determine microbial abundance and diversity. Clinical outcomes, including wound infection rates and patient comfort, were also recorded. The results indicated that surgical treatment reduced the diversity of the oral microbiota and altered its composition. Before surgery, the oral cavity was dominated by potentially pathogenic taxa, which shifted toward oral resident microorganisms postoperatively. Continued oral irrigation promoted a transition from an unstable, anaerobic-enriched state toward a relatively stable community structure dominated by facultative anaerobes. While no differences were observed between the 2 groups regarding wound infection rates or microbial composition, the bipolar water group reported higher patient comfort and required shorter irrigation times. Furthermore, the bipolar water group maintained more stable microbial diversity, whereas the hydrogen peroxide group exhibited more pronounced fluctuations and higher fungal detection rates. In conclusion, surgery induces early microbial imbalance, but staged oral irrigation facilitates the stabilization of the oral microecosystem. Bipolar water is an effective alternative for perioperative care, helping to maintain microbial stability while improving the patient experience.

articles.title: Regional Impact of a Specialist Pediatric Palliative Care Program on Health Care Utilization and Cost: A Population-Level Difference-in-Differences Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to pediatric palliative care (PPC) is a universal human right, yet most children-in-need globally go without. Costs remain a primary barrier to program development, yet research regarding the economic impact of programs is inconsistent and inconclusive.

OBJECTIVES: To examine health care utilization and costs among regional pediatric decedents during the development of a specialist PPC program.

DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study using linked administrative databases and a difference-in-differences analytic approach.

SETTING/SUBJECTS: Ontario, Canada, 2010-2018. 3,892 pediatric decedents (aged 31 days to 18 years) across Ontario, including 737 from Southcentral Ontario (SCO), the catchment wherein a specialist PPC program was initiated in 2016.

MEASUREMENTS: Primary outcomes were total health care days and total costs in the last year of life. Secondary outcomes included acute care days and costs, intensive care unit (ICU) days, and location of death. Difference-in-differences regression estimated incident rate ratios (IRRs) for days, mean relative differences (MRDs) for costs, and odds ratios for location of death. Counterfactual models estimated region-level impact.

RESULTS: Relative to the remainder of Ontario, the SCO cohort experienced decreased total costs (MRD 0.63; 95% confidence intervals [CIs] 0.49-0.81), acute costs (MRD 0.62; 95% CI: 0.48-0.80), and ICU days (IRR 0.56; 95% CI: 0.38-0.83) following initiation of the program. Counterfactual analysis estimated a cumulative regional cost reduction of $15.6 million CAD over three years, representing 0.87% of all regional pediatric expenditures.

CONCLUSIONS: A specialist PPC program was associated with lower end-of-life costs at the population level, supporting investment in and evaluation of scalable PPC models.

articles.title: Melatonin Mitigates Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity by Targeting the USP18/PKM2 Axis Without Compromising Antitumor Efficacy.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a widely used chemotherapeutic drug, yet its clinical value is constrained by pronounced cardiotoxicity. Although melatonin is known to protect the heart, how it counters DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), and whether it interferes with chemotherapy, remains unclear. Here we set out to define how melatonin protects the heart during DOX treatment and to test whether this protection holds in tumor-bearing animals. We used acute and chronic DIC mouse models together with a syngeneic melanoma-bearing model, and combined transcriptomic profiling, pharmacological intervention, cardiomyocyte-specific USP18 overexpression and knockout, co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, ubiquitination assays, and PKM2 inhibitor treatment. Melatonin markedly improved cardiac function, an effect exerted mainly via the MT1/2 receptors. Mechanistically, DOX activated STAT1, which in turn drove myocardial USP18 upregulation. USP18 bound PKM2 and stabilized it through removing K33-linked ubiquitin chains while favoring K27-linked ubiquitination-thereby aggravating cardiac injury. Overexpressing USP18 specifically in cardiomyocytes worsened DIC and abolished the protection conferred by melatonin, whereas deleting USP18 or inhibiting PKM2 reproduced melatonin's benefits. Notably, in bearing melanoma or lymphoma, melatonin relieved DIC without weakening the antitumor activity of DOX. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized cardioprotective pathway and provide preclinical support for melatonin as a safe adjunct therapy in cardio-oncology.

articles.title: Molecular confirmation of Leishmania infantum infection in the sand fly vector Phlebotomus neglectus (Diptera: Phlebotominae) in Slovenia.
articles.abstract: Leishmania infantum is the primary causative agent of zoonotic leishmaniasis in Europe and is transmitted by phlebotomine sand flies. Although Slovenia is not considered endemic, competent vectors and canine infections have been documented, suggesting conditions that may allow local transmission. During the 2023 sand fly season, 145 phlebotomine sand flies were collected at a farm site in Cetore, Slovenian Istria, and identified morphologically as Phlebotomus neglectus, P. perniciosus and P. mascittii. Female sand flies were grouped into eight monospecific pools and screened for Leishmania DNA by kinetoplast DNA real-time PCR. One pool of P. neglectus females collected in July tested positive, with a low cycle threshold value indicating a high parasite DNA load. Species-level identification using ITS-1 and hsp70 PCR-RFLP, followed by sequencing, confirmed the parasite as L. infantum. This study provides the first molecular confirmation of L. infantum in phlebotomine sand flies from Slovenia. The finding of L. infantum DNA in a proven vector species represents an early warning signal and highlights the need to implement entomological and molecular surveillance programmes in Slovenia.

articles.title: STING/Type I Interferon Pathway Activation Confers Multimodal Therapeutic Benefits in Osteomyelitis.
articles.abstract: Osteomyelitis is an inflammatory bone disease caused by pathogenic microorganisms and characterized by severe pain, extensive bone destruction, and reduced antibiotic efficacy due to local abscess formation. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of activating the STING (stimulator of interferon genes) pathway in osteomyelitis. In murine femoral osteomyelitis models induced by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), STING agonists alleviate osteomyelitis-associated pain, suppress infection-induced bone destruction, and reduce local abscess formation. These effects depend on host STING/type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and involve three mechanisms: inhibition of nociceptor activation by pathogens, suppression of osteoclast differentiation and function without affecting osteoblast activity, and downregulation of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), leading to reduced neutrophil recruitment and abscess formation. By reducing abscess formation as a physical barrier, STING agonists enhance the antibacterial efficacy of conventional antibiotics such as vancomycin at the site of infection. In summary, these findings suggest that the synergistic mechanisms activated by STING represent a promising therapeutic target for alleviating pain and improving clinical outcomes in osteomyelitis.

articles.title: EXPRESS: BENEFITS OF CONTRAST-ENHANCED COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OVER PLAIN COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY FOR HEAD TRAUMA IN 41 CATS.
articles.journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate whether contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) provides clinically useful information beyond Plain computed tomography (PCT) in cats with head trauma, and whether this benefit is influenced by the radiologist's level of experience.

METHODS: Forty-one cats that underwent head CT with both pre- and post-contrast sequences were included. Images were independently reviewed by three radiologists with different experience levels, assessing extracranial soft tissue injuries, bone fractures, and intracranial abnormalities. Intra- and interobserver agreements were analyzed using Cohen's kappa statistics.

RESULTS: Substantial to almost perfect agreement was obtained for extracranial soft tissue injuries and bone fractures. The most commonly fractured sites were the temporomandibular joints, hard palate, mandibular bones, and pterygoid bones. For intracranial lesions such as hemorrhage and cerebral edema, intra- and interobserver agreements were low and variable, regardless of contrast use or reviewer experience. There was no significant difference found between PCT and CECT for any of the three categories.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: These results suggest that contrast medium injection is not useful for assessment of bone fractures and extracranial soft tissue and that computed tomography of the head is poorly reliable for intracranial lesions in cats presented for trauma.

articles.title: CNTN4: A Possible Candidate Gene for Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
articles.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
articles.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a significant role in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), though findings vary substantially across studies. Using gut microbiome data from a genome-wide association study of 5,959 participants and summary statistics from 46,351 ASD and 55,374 ADHD cases, we conducted bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses with inverse variance weighting as the primary method. Reverse MR analysis assessed potential reverse causality. We annotated single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with SNP-nexus to identify associated genes, followed by Gene Ontology (﻿GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses to characterize their functional roles. Seventeen gut microbial taxa showed causal associations with ASD risk, while 27 were linked to ADHD. Reverse MR analysis revealed associations between aSD and species Desulfovibrio piger as well as species Bacillus U, but no reverse causality was detected for ADHD. Biological annotation identified five novel conserved genes in host-microbiome interactions shared by ASD and ADHD, with CNTN4 emerging as a common candidate gene. These findings support a potential causal relationship between gut microbiota and ASD/ADHD risk while uncovering novel conserved genes implicated in host-microbiome interactions for both disorders.Lay AbstractDistinct gut microbiota profiles were observed in individuals with ADHD and ASD. Seventeen microbial species showed significant associations with ASD, while 27 were linked to ADHD. CNTN4 emerged as a potential candidate gene shared across both neurodevelopmental conditions and host-microbiome interactions.

articles.title: fNIRS-VFT is a complementary tool to 18F-FDG PET in presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy: an exploratory study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate presurgical localization of the epileptogenic zone (EZ) and preservation of postoperative cognitive function are two critical but often competing goals in epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This study aimed to (1) evaluate the complementary value of functional near-infrared spectroscopy during a verbal fluency task (fNIRS-VFT) alongside interictal 18F-FDG PET for presurgical EZ localization; and (2) explore whether task-based fNIRS functional connectivity is associated with postoperative verbal memory decline.

METHODS: We retrospectively included patients with DRE who underwent epilepsy surgery between December 2022 and December 2023 and completed both interictal PET and fNIRS-VFT assessments. All analyses in this study were descriptive, and no robust inferential statistical testing was performed. For the localization outcome, concordance between PET hypometabolism and fNIRS-VFT hypoactivation was analyzed in patients who achieved seizure freedom two years after surgery. For the memory outcome, post- vs. pre-operation change of task-based fNIRS functional connectivity was compared between patients with and without clinically significant postoperative verbal memory decline (≥ 4 point reduction on Auditory Verbal Learning Test delayed recall).

RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were included in this study. Among 20 patients achieving seizure freedom, PET demonstrated concordant lateralization with the EZ in 14 cases (70%), including 11 with accurate localization; fNIRS-VFT showed concordant lateralization in 9 patients (45%), with 4 accurate localizations including one case in whom PET failed to lateralize the EZ, indicating the complementary value of fNIRS-VFT. Among 19 patients with complete memory data, four showed significant postoperative decline. These patients exhibited more pronounced alterations in task-related functional connectivity, particularly involving frontopolar, dorsolateral prefrontal, premotor, and temporal regions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, descriptive analysis, interictal 18F-FDG PET showed higher concordance with lateralization of surgical areas compared with fNIRS-VFT among patients with DRE. Nevertheless, fNIRS may provide complementary information for cases with inconclusive PET findings. Additionally, changes of task-based fNIRS connectivity may be correlated with postoperative verbal memory alterations. These preliminary findings suggest that fNIRS-VFT may provide complementary information in selected cases, which warrants validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Characterization and treatment of ischemic stroke in patients with infective endocarditis: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a common and serious complication of infective bacterial endocarditis. This study aimed to characterize the frequency, clinical and pathological features, treatment strategies, and outcomes of patients with stroke due to infective endocarditis.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed from database inception to October 2022 for studies reporting on stroke in patients with infective endocarditis and performed a meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 122 studies comprising 270,211 patients with infective endocarditis were included. Ischemic stroke occurred in 21% and hemorrhagic stroke in 5% of patients. Stroke was observed in 32% of patients with mitral valve endocarditis, 25% with aortic valve, and 11% with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality (OR 2.35; 95%CI 1.74-3.16). Staphylococcus and Streptococcus species were most frequently associated with stroke (33% and 25%, respectively). The risk of stroke did not differ significantly between patients with and without pre-existing antithrombotic therapy (37% vs. 24%; OR 1.24, 95%CI 0.75-2.06). Successful reperfusion was achieved in 80% of patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy, although mortality remained high at 49%.

CONCLUSIONS: Stroke is a common complication of infective bacterial endocarditis and has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. It occurs most frequently in patients with mitral valve endocarditis and in those with infections caused by staphylococcal pathogens. Stroke risk was not reduced in patients with pre-existing antithrombotic therapy, supporting discontinuation where no other indication exists. Mechanical thrombectomy in patients with endocarditis-related large vessel occlusion achieves high recanalization rates; however, overall clinical outcomes remain poor in this population.

articles.title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive reperfusion strategy, residual disease burden and plaque vulnerability both influence clinical recovery. The residual SYNTAX score (rSS) quantifies untreated macroscopic coronary artery disease, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) resolves microscopic plaque architecture, notably thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA). This pilot study explored the descriptive characteristics and short-term outcomes associated with combining rSS and OCT-derived TCFA in a highly selected STEMI cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective observational pilot study included 30 patients with STEMI who underwent primary PCI and culprit lesion OCT evaluation at a tertiary care center. Patients were stratified into four groups according to the presence of culprit TCFA and the post-PCI rSS threshold ( ≤ 4 vs. > 4): group 0 (TCFA absent, rSS > 4), group 1 (TCFA absent, rSS ≤ 4), group 2 (TCFA present, rSS > 4), and group 3 (TCFA present, rSS ≤ 4). The primary clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiac events (MACE)-a composite of all-cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, heart failure hospitalisation, and ischemic stroke-assessed over 3 months.

RESULTS: The cohort (mean age, 54.5 ± 10.1 years; 83.3% male, 40% with diabetes mellitus) had a 53.3% prevalence (16 of 30) of culprit lesion TCFA. Complete or reasonable revascularization (rSS ≤ 4) was achieved in 12 patients (40.0%). The overall cumulative 3-month MACE rate was 30.0% (9 of 30). MACE occurred in 1 of 7 patients (14.3%) in group 0, 1 of 7 (14.3%) in group 1, 4 of 11 (36.4%) in group 2, and 3 of 5 (60.0%) in group 3 (Fisher exact test, P = 0.23; log-rank P = 0.38). Patients with TCFA accounted for 7 of 9 clinical events (77.8%). Given the small subgroup sizes (n < 12), multivariable predictive risk modeling was not performed.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot cohort of STEMI patients undergoing PCI, the presence of OCT-derived TCFA was descriptively associated with higher short-term adverse event rates across both complete and incomplete revascularization strata. Given the small sample size and clear indication bias, these findings are strictly hypothesis-generating and support the need for adequately powered prospective registries to evaluate dual anatomical-biological risk stratification.

articles.title: Anemia and high-output cardiac hypertrophy in Tanzania and Haiti: a cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face a growing burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) that is not fully explained by traditional risk factors like hypertension. Anemia is highly prevalent in LMICs and may be an important non-traditional CVD risk factor. We evaluated the association between anemia and preclinical CVD, including left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and other echocardiographic measures, in two diverse LMIC settings.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of data from two separate cohorts of adults in Mwanza, Tanzania (n = 999; data collected 2022-2023) and Port-au-Prince, Haiti (n = 3,005; data collected 2019-2021). Participants underwent clinical examinations, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. Models assessing the relationship between anemia and echocardiographic outcomes were adjusted for age, sex, HIV status, blood pressure, and body mass index.

RESULTS: Anemia prevalence was 23% in Tanzania and 32% in Haiti. Despite lower blood pressure and BMI among anemic participants, moderate/severe anemia were strongly associated with higher LVMI and LVH in both cohorts. In combined analyses, moderate/severe anemia were associated with LVMI increases of 8.4 g/m² and 29.7 g/m², respectively. Anemia was also associated with echocardiographic changes characteristic of a high-output cardiac state, including increased cardiac and stroke volume indices. Moderate/severe anemia was associated with18.2% of LVH cases in Tanzania and 9.1% in Haiti, and 34.4% among people with HIV.

CONCLUSIONS: Anemia was independently associated with high-output cardiac hypertrophy in two distinct LMIC populations, underscoring anemia as a potentially modifiable CVD risk factor. Enhanced anemia screening and management could serve as a vital strategy to mitigate the rising burden of CVD in these regions.

articles.title: Acute measles encephalitis in adults: a case series in Vietnam.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute measles encephalitis is a rare but severe complication of measles, particularly in adults, and carries high mortality and a substantial risk of neurological sequelae. Two mechanisms are recognized: direct viral invasion of the brain, termed primary measles encephalitis, and an immune-mediated postinfectious process, termed acute postinfectious measles encephalitis. Most descriptions come from children, and the presentation, pathogenesis, and management of adult disease remain poorly defined.

CASE PRESENTATION: We describe four adults (aged 34-45 years) admitted with fever, rash, and altered mental status. Acute measles infection was confirmed by serum measles-specific IgM or measles virus RNA on real-time reverse-transcription PCR. Measles virus RNA was detected in cerebrospinal fluid in Case 1, indicating primary measles encephalitis. Case 2 was initially mistaken for varicella because of an atypical vesicular rash. Case 3 developed quadriparesis and sphincter dysfunction with electromyographic evidence of bilateral S1 radiculopathy; spinal imaging was not performed. Case 4 showed progressive thalamic and temporal lesions on magnetic resonance imaging. Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis ranged from 57 to 1046 cells/µL, and improved in most patients within 3 days of intravenous immunoglobulin. Two patients recovered without neurological sequelae, one survived with residual deficits, and one died from persistent cerebral injury complicated by multidrug-resistant septic shock.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults, acute measles encephalitis may reflect a biphasic process that combines direct viral neuroinvasion with immune-mediated inflammation, rather than a purely postinfectious phenomenon. Intravenous immunoglobulin was temporally associated with clinical and biochemical improvement, but its therapeutic role cannot be established from a case series and requires controlled study.

articles.title: Sequential decision-making in endovascular stroke therapy: benefit and harm of the next retrieval attempt after failed reperfusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After failed reperfusion in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), interventionalists must outweigh the expected benefit of an additional retrieval attempt with the outcome of the current angiographic result. Framing EVT as an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem, the present study provides a per-pass evaluation of the expected benefit of EVT continuation versus procedural termination after unsuccessful reperfusion, based on large-scale real-world registry data.

METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened. Inclusion criteria were (1) age ≥ 18 years, (2) anterior circulation LVO, (3) 1-15 retrieval attempts and (4) availability of relevant clinical data. Primary endpoint was the rate of good functional outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. For each retrieval attempt, patients were stratified into successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) and persistent occlusion (mTICI 0-2a). The net expected benefit of EVT continuation, Δ(k), was defined as the difference between the mRS 0-2 rate at pass k + 1, and the mRS 0-2 rate for unsuccessful reperfusion at pass k. A positive Δ(k) indicates that continuation is favored at that decision node k. The pass at which Δ(k) first becomes non-significant identifies the empirical, optimal stopping threshold.

RESULTS: Among 9,495 included patients, successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) was achieved in 8,405 (89%), and 3,428 (36%) achieved good functional outcome at 90 days. Up to six retrieval attempts, Δ(k) was positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), indicating that continuation of EVT was associated with superior expected outcome at each of these decision points. At pass seven, Δ(k) became negative and lost statistical significance (p = 0.53), identifying this as the empirical optimal stopping threshold.

CONCLUSION: Continuation of EVT up to six retrieval attempts confers a significant functional benefit over termination after unsuccessful reperfusion. These findings provide a decision-theoretic basis for individualized intraprocedural decision-making and suggest that functional independence can be achieved beyond conventionally assumed pass thresholds.

articles.title: Human Engineered Heart Tissues Reproduce Trigger- and Substrate-Driven Mechanisms of Ventricular Tachycardia.
articles.abstract: Human iPSC‑derived engineered heart tissues (EHTs) are used to model cardiac physiology and drug responses, yet whether they reproduce tissue‑scale ventricular arrhythmia mechanisms remains unclear. We combined modified milliPillar EHT fabrication with high-resolution dual-channel voltage/Ca2+ optical mapping. Baseline electrophysiology showed action potential durations (APD) within the range reported for human ventricles and conduction velocities approximately half of human longitudinal values, with rate‑dependent restitution of APD and Ca2+ transient duration, conduction slowing, and physiologic AP-Ca2+ latency. To interrogate a trigger arm of ventricular tachycardia (VT), we modeled acquired long-QT syndrome (aLQTS; hERG blockade with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia) in EHTs from two hiPSC lines. aLQTS EHTs developed VT-like episodes with beat‑to‑beat instability. Early afterdepolarizations propagated heterogeneously, generating triggered activity, tissue acceleration, APD dispersion, wavebreak, and rotor formation. These were short and self-terminating (median 0.4 s) and clustered at head/neck region curvatures. To test whether a fixed spatial substrate supports prolonged reentry, we developed a reproducible focal cryoinjury model. After injury, all tissues developed VT-like episodes, and 70% anatomically anchored rotors at the border; three persisted beyond 10 s, a recording-limited lower bound. Dual voltage/Ca2+ mapping at this resolution establishes EHTs as a non-animal platform for mechanistic study of both trigger- and substrate-driven ventricular arrhythmias.

articles.title: Correction: GPR109A controls neutrophil extracellular traps formation and improve early sepsis by regulating ROS/PAD4/Cit-H3 signal axis.
Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.

METHODS: We genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed.

RESULTS: In the primary cluster-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Clinical performance of different types of posterior bulk-fill resin composite restorations in permanent teeth: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bulk-fill resin composites were developed to overcome limitations of incremental placement techniques: time consumption and air bubble entrapment. They are available in different viscosities, including high-viscosity (sculptable) and low-viscosity (flowable). Furthermore, practitioners deploy various techniques, such as sonic activation and preheating, to reduce the viscosity of bulk-fill resin composites. However, few studies have evaluated the clinical performance of different bulk-fill resin composite types. Consequently, this systematic review aimed to evaluate and compare the clinical performance of sonic-activated, preheated, and flowable bulk-fill resin composites versus conventional high-viscosity bulk-fill materials in permanent posterior teeth, regarding the following parameters: functional (retention, marginal adaptation, and anatomic form), esthetic (marginal discoloration, color match, and surface texture), and biological parameters (secondary caries and postoperative sensitivity).

METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. An electronic search of PubMed and ScienceDirect identified clinical trials published between 2015 and 2025 that compared different types of bulk-fill resin composites. Clinical studies evaluated any cavity class in permanent posterior teeth with at least a one-year of follow-up. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and a standardized, pilot-tested data extraction form. Included variables were study characteristics, sample size, type of restorative material, evaluation criteria, follow-up duration, and clinical outcomes. The modified Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool was used to assess the quality of the selected studies.

RESULTS: Out of 1041 records, 33 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, with six randomized controlled trials (RCTs) finally included. Overall, no significant differences were observed among bulk-fill resin composite types regarding retention, surface texture, anatomic form, secondary caries, or postoperative sensitivity. Some trends suggested slightly better marginal adaptation for flowable or preheated composites. Additionally, one included study reported no significant differences between Class I and Class II restorations.

CONCLUSIONS: Different types of bulk-fill resin composites perform similarly for most functional and biological parameters, with marginal adaptation and discoloration being the parameters requiring further long-term investigation.

articles.title: Gut relief revisited: plecanatide in chronic idiopathic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation - a systematic review and meta-analysis with GRADE assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) are prevalent gastrointestinal disorders with limited effective treatment options. CIC affects approximately 14% of the population worldwide, particularly women, and is marked by difficult defecation, while IBS-C also includes abdominal pain as a core of symptom. Plecanatide, a guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist approved in 2017, has shown promise in improving stool consistency and symptoms; however, its optimal therapeutic dose remains unclear.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted through (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase) for randomized controlled trials comparing plecanatide with placebo until August 2025. Primary outcomes included changes in complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs), spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs), and stool consistency.

RESULTS: Plecanatide significantly increased the changes in complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs) across all reported doses with mean differences (MDs) of (0.75, 0.92, 0.80, and 1.00, (P < 0.00001), with the greatest improvement observed at the 9 mg dose. Moreover, spontaneous bowel movements (SBMs) improved significantly at 1, 3, and 6 mg, with (MDs: 0.97, 1.50, and 1.58, (P < 0.00001). Stool consistency and reduction in abdominal pain and bloating were observed particularly at 3-6 mg. Furthermore, plecanatide demonstrated consistent efficacy across all doses, with both 1 mg and 9 mg showing significantly greater improvements in CSBMs and SBMs compared to the 0.3 mg dose. Diarrhea was the most frequent adverse event and the primary reason for treatment discontinuation, while other safety outcomes were not significantly affected.

CONCLUSION: Plecanatide is generally well-tolerated in the treatment of CIC and IBS-C, with the 3 mg dose, offering the best balance between efficacy and safety. This meta-analysis supports its use as a viable treatment option, though diarrhea remains a dose-related concern.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered prospectively with PROSPERO (Registration number: CRD420251066097, Date of registration: 2025-6-10).

articles.title: Maternal Hyperglycemia Disrupts Cerebral Cortex Development Through the Foxp1-Dll1-Notch Axis.
articles.abstract: Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring, but the mechanisms by which it affects fetal brain development remain incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of pregestational diabetes mellitus (PGDM), we found that maternal hyperglycemia was associated with reduced cortical thickness and altered cortical lamination. These abnormalities were accompanied by changes in neural stem cell differentiation and asymmetric division, as well as impaired neuronal migration and dendritic development. Transcriptomic analysis identified the transcription factor Foxp1 as markedly downregulated in the PGDM embryonic cortex. Restoring Foxp1 expression in vivo substantially alleviated the observed cortical abnormalities. Mechanistic experiments showed that Foxp1 represses transcription of the Notch ligand Delta-like 1 (Dll1) and attenuates Notch signaling. Together, these findings implicate the Foxp1-Dll1-Notch axis as one pathway contributing to disrupted corticogenesis in the PGDM model and provide insight into how an adverse intrauterine metabolic environment affects embryonic brain development.

articles.title: Textbook outcomes after colon and rectal cancer surgery: results of a multicentre national study.
articles.abstract: Textbook outcomes (TO) are a composite measure of ideal postoperative outcomes. Using a multicentre national study, we aimed to describe the rate and associated factors with TO for colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Stage I-III colorectal cancer who underwent curative surgery were retrospectively identified from 80 centres from 2018 to 2021 using a large national study dataset. Recurrent, synchronous, and metastatic cancer, urgent surgery, and SARS-CoV-2 infection were excluded. TO include radical resection (R0, CRM-), > 12 lymph nodes yield, adequate length of stay (LOS ≤ 75th°), no 30-day mortality, and no Clavien-Dindo ≥ III morbidity. 13842 patients were included: 9869 with colon (TO: 67%) and 3973 with rectal cancer (TO: 53%). TO were not achieved the most by inadequate lymph node yield, Clavien-Dindo classification ≥ III, and prolonged postoperative LOS. In colon cancer surgery the use of laparoscopy was the strongest predictor (OR 2.21), along with being female (OR 1.25), cT1-T2 and cT3-T4a (vs. T0-Tis) stages (OR 1.66 and OR 1.86), and cN2 (vs. N0 or N1) stage (OR 1.23) for achieving TO after colon cancer surgery. Age ≥ 65years, pulmonary comorbidities, alcoholic hepatopathy, previous CRC, anticoagulants, left-sided cancer, ASA score > 2, centre volume, additional surgery, conversion, intraoperative surgical complications, ileostomy, and mild postoperative complications only (Clavien-Dindo ≤ II) were negatively associated. In rectal cancer, female sex (OR 1.26) and high rectal cancer (OR 1.84) were positively associated, while age ≥ 75years, previous CRC, T4b stage, intraoperative surgical complications, and mild postoperative complications were negatively associated. This study reports rates and factors independently associated with TO for colon and rectal cancer using a large multicentre cohort.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for confirming endotracheal tube placement in prehospital and critical care transport: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has demonstrated high pooled diagnostic accuracy for endotracheal tube (ETT) placement confirmation in adult Emergency Departments and Intensive Care Units,, but its translation to pre-hospital and Critical Care Transport (CCT) environments is unclear. We mapped the published evidence on POCUS-based ETT placement confirmation in transport, organized around six axes: clinical indication, transport modality, operator training, impact on management, technical barriers, and patient-oriented outcomes. Scoping review per the Joanna Briggs Institute 2020 framework, reported per PRISMA-ScR. Nine sources searched January 1st, 2015-May 12th, 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Europe PMC, Consensus.app, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and forward-citation tracking. Dual independent screening and charting were performed in Covidence with built-in conflict adjudication. From 2447 unique records, 51 met final inclusion. One primary study evaluated diagnostic performance in adult patients in an out-of-hospital setting. The remaining 50 records comprised contextual primary studies and secondary evidence, including cadaver and simulation studies, training evaluations, feasibility implementations, and reviews. Distribution by modality was skewed toward ground emergency medical services (EMS); rotor-wing helicopter EMS (HEMS) evidence was predominantly training-based; fixed-wing evidence was essentially absent. Operator profiles in transport-relevant studies were predominantly paramedic, flight medic, or flight nurse, mismatched against the physician-dominant pooled in-hospital meta-analytic estimates. No included study measured patient-oriented outcomes. Evidence supporting POCUS-based ETT confirmation in pre-hospital and critical care transport remains limited. Most studies addressed training, simulation, feasibility, or implementation rather than diagnostic performance in transported patients, and none demonstrated an effect on patient-oriented outcomes. Transport-specific prospective studies are needed before hospital-derived diagnostic-accuracy estimates can be generalized to transport practice.

articles.title: Is the Proust phenomenon fact or fiction? A systematic review and meta-analysis of odor-evoked autobiographical memory.
articles.abstract: Odors are widely believed to be the most powerful trigger for autobiographical memory (AM). This meta-analysis provides the first comprehensive meta-analytic test of this claim, known as the Proust phenomenon. Eighteen experimental/quasi-experimental studies were included in this meta-analysis. Olfactory cueing was compared with a variety of cueing modalities, and seven key characteristics of evoked AMs (specificity, vividness, emotional intensity, pleasantness, rarity, evocativeness, and age of AMs) were assessed. Olfactory cues showed a greater effect (advantage) over other cue types for emotional intensity, pleasantness, evocativeness, and age of AMs. Sample size was negatively associated with effect sizes for emotional intensity, pleasantness, and rarity, although the overall effect for rarity was not significant. Higher proportions of females and more recent publication years were each associated with smaller effects for evocativeness and pleasantness, respectively. Subgroup analyses showed that the advantage of olfactory cues for emotional intensity was stronger in within-subject than between-subject designs. Moreover, their advantage in terms of pleasantness was greatest relative to label cues, followed by visual and auditory cues. Although olfactory cues showed an advantage for four characteristics of AMs, these results do not fully confirm the Proust phenomenon. Overall, these findings suggest that the olfactory advantage is selective rather than universal, and future studies should clarify the conditions under which it emerges.

articles.title: A Comparative Outcome Review of Abdominoplasty Following Massive Weight Loss.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominoplasty after massive weight loss has higher complication rates than for other reasons. It is unclear if outcomes vary by method of weight loss, especially with increasing use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists.

METHODS: One hundred seventy-six patients had abdominoplasty after massive weight loss by a single surgeon. The main comparison was bariatric procedures (gastric sleeve, bypass, banding; n=118) versus diet and exercise (n=47). Complications were re-examined and reclassified. Logistic regression adjusted for BMI, resection weight, and diabetes.

RESULTS: Thirty-one patients (17.6%) experienced major complications (readmission or return to theatre). major complications were more common after bariatric than diet and exercise weight loss (22.0% vs. 8.5%; OR 3.04, p=0.046). Gastric bypass had the highest risk (39.1%; OR 6.91, p=0.007), based on a small subgroup (n=23), and is hypothesis-generating. After adjustment for BMI, resection weight, and diabetes, the difference was not significant (adjusted OR 2.33, p=0.16). Discrimination was modest for any complication (AUC 0.550) and better for major complication (0.674).

CONCLUSIONS: Major complication rates are higher after bariatric than after diet and exercise weight loss, but this difference is largely explained by residual obesity at surgery. Body mass index was the most consistent modifiable factor. Gastric bypass patients should be counselled specifically about the elevated risk.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors http://www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Exercise alleviates skeletal muscle dysfunction in COPD by regulating mitochondrial function via apelin/AMPK signaling.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common respiratory disorder characterized by persistent airflow limitation, with skeletal muscle dysfunction (SMD) representing a major extrapulmonary manifestation. Exercise training has positive effects on skeletal muscle strength, mass, and physical activity in patients with COPD, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether apelin mediates the protective effects of exercise on COPD-related SMD. Mouse models of COPD with SMD and cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-treated C2C12 cells were established. Mice underwent exercise or adeno-associated virus (AAV)-shApln intervention, while CSE-treated C2C12 cells were subjected to apelin overexpression and/or AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) knockdown. Muscle function, skeletal muscle mass, histopathology, apelin expression, cell viability, ATP production, mitochondrial function, and related protein expression were evaluated. Apelin expression was significantly downregulated in mice with COPD complicated by SMD and in CSE-treated cells. Apelin overexpression rescued the CSE-induced decrease in cell viability, ATP levels, mitochondrial content, and citrate synthase activity and the downregulation of PGC-1α and Tom20 expression via AMPK activation. Exercise increased apelin expression, improved muscle function and mitochondrial activity, and reduced Atrogin-1/MuRF1 expression; these effects were abolished by apelin knockdown. Collectively, these findings suggest that exercise alleviates COPD-related SMD by enhancing mitochondrial function through the apelin/AMPK pathway, highlighting this pathway as a potential therapeutic target for COPD-associated SMD.

articles.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations Provide Insights into the Paradox of Newer Prosthetic Aortic Valves.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) is defined by the estimated orifice area divided by body surface area (BSA), or iEOA. Small iEOA predicts poor outcomes with surgical bioprosthetic valves (SBV), but balloon-expandable valves (BEV) and self-expanding valves (SEV) have more variable results.

OBJECTIVES: Assess effect of geometry of the valve on overestimation of gradients and methods for adjusting for body size other than BSA.

METHODS: Computational fluid dynamic simulations of SBV, BEV and SEV, with 25 different variations of anatomic and valve sizes for each valve type determined peak stenosis velocity and peak and total valve gradients. The relationship between stroke volume and body size measures was analyzed using data from the Atherosclerosis Risk In Communities study.

RESULTS: Doppler peak velocity correctly estimated the total gradient for SBV (slope = 1.01) but overestimated the gradient for BEV (slope = 1.19) and SEV (slope = 1.42). The gradient across the valves varied even with identical dimensions, with SBV being highest, BEV lower, and SEV lowest. BSA had a fair correlation with stroke volume (r = 0.6030), but lean body mass (r = 0.6494) and fat-free mass (r = 0.6631) were better and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) area was best (r = 0.7570).

CONCLUSIONS: Geometry of the valve has a major impact on hemodynamics with very different results with identical dimensions. LVOT area was better way to adjust for body size than BSA. Two measures based on LVOT velocity and area are proposed as an alternative to implement these results. If these findings are confirmed with in-vitro and in-vivo studies, the approach could allow more accurate prediction and evaluation of PPM.

articles.title: Large language models for computational social science.
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming computational social science. This Review examines how LLMs now serve four distinct research roles: subjects that simulate human behaviour, assistants that automate analysis, collaborators that generate hypotheses and evaluators that audit and improve research quality. We analyse recent advances across sociology, political science, psychology, anthropology, economics and related fields, revealing how LLMs accelerate discovery while creating new methodological paradigms. This transformation arrives as society itself becomes saturated with artificial intelligence agents-making LLMs both our research tools and authentic research subjects. Yet fundamental challenges persist. LLMs struggle with causal inference and raise urgent ethical concerns about privacy and misinformation, and their ability to reproduce social complexity remains uneven and unproven. We identify critical research directions for harnessing LLMs' potential while addressing their limitations. As artificial intelligence reshapes human society, understanding this transformation requires the very tools driving it-a recursive challenge that will define the future of social science.

articles.title: Within-family heritability estimates for behavioural and disease phenotypes from 500,000 sibling pairs of diverse ancestries.
articles.abstract: Quantification of the direct effect of genetic variation on human behavioural traits is important for understanding between-individual variation in socioeconomic and health outcomes but estimates of their heritability can be biased by between-family indirect genetic effects. By contrast, using within-family variation in DNA sharing is robust to most confounding factors including shared environmental effects and population stratification. Yet, accurate estimates for most traits are not available using this design, and none for non-European ancestry populations. Here we analyse approximately 500,000 sibling pairs with diverse genetic ancestries and obtain within-family heritability estimates for 14 phenotypes, including two well-studied model traits: height (0.70 ± 0.03) and BMI (0.49 ± 0.03). For behaviour, we find significant within-family heritability for smoking initiation (0.34 ± 0.05), alcohol consumption (0.18 ± 0.04), number of children (0.27 ± 0.11) and personality ('talk versus listen', 0.48 ± 0.13). In addition, we estimated large heritability for type 2 diabetes (0.43 ± 0.06) and asthma (0.34 ± 0.06), whose risk factors include behavioural traits. Overall, we show concordant estimates across ancestry groups and highlight a significant contribution of shared environmental effects for behaviour and type 2 diabetes risk, which may have inflated between-family estimates. Altogether, our results provide within-family evidence that genetic variation is associated with variation in complex traits, common disease and exposures. Our heritability estimates are concordant across genetic ancestries, lower than those from twin-based studies, yet larger than has been accounted for by genome-wide association studies so far.

articles.title: Rethinking thrombosis prevention in systemic lupus erythematosus.
Lack of ancestral SARS-CoV-2 imprinting promotes Omicron sublineage BA.3.2.2 infection in children.
articles.abstract: The ongoing SARS-CoV-2 evolution is constrained by population-level immune imprinting. Recent genomic surveillance revealed an unexpected demographic shift with the Omicron sublineage BA.3.2.2 being predominant in paediatric populations globally. Here we show that this paediatric susceptibility arises from the absence of immune imprinting against ancestral SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan strain. Serological analyses reveal a failure to neutralize BA.3.2.2 in young children with no ancestral strain exposure. Single-B-cell sequencing analyses demonstrate that BA.3.2.2 evades Omicron-specific Class 1/4 neutralizing antibodies that target the ACE2-binding site, encoded by immunoglobulin heavy-chain variable (IGHV) germline genes IGHV2-5 and IGHV5-51, which dominate in weakly imprinted individuals. BA.3.2.2 remains susceptible to broadly cross-reactive Class 1 antibodies, encoded by IGHV3-53/66, typically enriched in adults with strong Wuhan-strain imprinting, such as mRNA vaccine recipients. Together, these findings show that classic immune imprinting provides superior protection against a highly divergent variant, explaining the age-biased transmission of BA.3.2.2, and informing future paediatric vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Risk Prediction in Postmenopausal Women With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: An Observational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important risk factor for cardiovascular events, yet performance of cardiovascular prediction models are understudied in the CKD population, including women with CKD.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the performance of multiple cardiovascular prediction models, the Framingham, Adult Treatment Panel (ATP) III, ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), QRISK3, and PREVENT models, in women with and without CKD.

DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study (Women's Health Initiative Biomarker Studies).

PARTICIPANTS: 21,548 postmenopausal women ages 50-79 without cardiovascular disease, including 1,095 with CKD defined by eGFR < 60 mL/min per 1.73 m2.

MAIN MEASURES: Model discrimination by C-statistic. Calibration by clinically relevant decision-making thresholds. Included events varied by model: Framingham model outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), angina, or coronary heart disease (CHD) death; ATP III model outcomes included fatal and nonfatal CHD; PCE and PREVENT model outcomes included CHD or ischemic stroke; QRISK3 model outcomes included CHD, stroke, or transient ischemic attack.

KEY RESULTS: Number of cardiovascular events varied based on outcome definition. For the non-CKD group, events ranged from 846 (4.1%) for ATP III to 1,435 (7.0%) for QRISK3; for the CKD group, events ranged from 93 (8.5%) for ATP III to 145 (13.2%) for QRISK3. Discrimination by C-statistic ranged from 0.57 for the Framingham model to 0.67 for PREVENT in the CKD group; in the non-CKD group, C-statistics ranged from 0.61 for the Framingham model to 0.71 for QRISK3 and PREVENT. Calibration was generally poor in both CKD and non-CKD groups, with underprediction for women with CKD across most models, as well as underprediction for women without CKD for the PREVENT model.

CONCLUSION: Common cardiovascular risk prediction models have poor discrimination and calibration in women with CKD; the PREVENT model generally underpredicted risk for women with and without CKD.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Immune surveillance of cellular damage: lessons from Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.abstract: Innate immune systems must detect infection rapidly and reliably, yet pathogens can often evade direct recognition by host pattern-recognition receptors. An alternative and increasingly appreciated strategy is damage-driven immune surveillance, whereby hosts detect pathogen-induced perturbations to essential cellular and tissue functions rather than microbial molecules themselves. This mode of detection is particularly prominent in Caenorhabditis elegans, which lacks professional immune cells and most canonical innate immune receptors, and therefore relies extensively on monitoring disruptions to core homeostatic pathways. Perturbations to protein translation, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, genome and nucleolar integrity, lysosomal homeostasis, and Golgi function can all trigger immune responses.
