Recent studies have further uncovered roles for inter-organelle communication, effector-triggered surveillance of lysosome-related organelles, and physiological signals such as intestinal distension in regulating immune activation. Here, we integrate these advances into an organelle- and tissue-centric framework and explore parallels with other organisms to identify emerging and potentially conserved principles of damage sensing in innate immunity. These findings highlight the surveillance of cellular homeostasis as a central strategy for immunity that operates beyond canonical pattern-recognition mechanisms.

articles.title: Temporal trends and clinical factors associated with ketamine infusion in hospitalized infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize temporal trends in ketamine infusion use in extremely preterm infants with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (sBPD) and identify associated clinical factors.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a 15-year (2010-2024) retrospective cohort study of extremely preterm infants with sBPD. Time was analyzed as a categorical variable in three 5-year epochs. Ketamine exposures were described, and multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between time periods and use, adjusting for clinical characteristics.

RESULTS: Among 8888 infants with sBPD, 112 (1.3%) received ketamine infusion, with use increasing over time and rising most sharply between 2020 and 2024. Pulmonary hypertension (adjusted odds ratio, aOR 5.47, 95% CI 1.65-18.09), stage II/III necrotizing enterocolitis (aOR 2.06, 1.24-3.43), and tracheostomy (aOR 8.32, 3.50-19.77) were independently associated with use.

CONCLUSIONS: Ketamine infusions in sBPD are uncommon but have increased over time, particularly since 2020. Use is associated with markers of greater illness severity.

articles.title: Association of winter indoor-temperature variability with 5-year changes in home blood pressure: the Smart Wellness Housing Cohort Survey in Japan.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Cold indoor temperatures acutely raise blood pressure, but their long-term effects remain uncertain. We investigated whether winter indoor-temperature levels and temporal variability were associated with 5-year changes in home blood pressure. This nationwide cohort included 700 adults from 483 households with complete data. Living-room temperature was measured at 10-min intervals, and home blood pressure was measured twice each morning and evening for 2 weeks in winter at baseline and at the 5-year follow-up. Linear mixed-effects models with household random intercepts were adjusted for baseline blood pressure, individual covariates, and mean indoor temperature in analyses of variability. Mean and minimum indoor temperatures were not associated with 5-year changes in systolic or diastolic home blood pressure. In contrast, a 10 °C/day higher cumulative indoor-temperature variation was associated with 0.42 mmHg (95% confidence interval, 0.04-0.80) and 0.27 mmHg (0.01-0.54) greater increases in systolic and diastolic home blood pressure, respectively. Each additional daily indoor-temperature swing ≥3 °C and ≥5 °C was associated with 0.32 mmHg (0.004-0.636) and 0.49 mmHg (0.04-0.93) greater increases in systolic blood pressure, respectively. A model-based comparison of cumulative indoor-temperature variation values 1 standard deviation above versus below the mean yielded an estimated difference of 1.47 mmHg (0.13-2.81) in the 5-year change in home systolic blood pressure. The sensitivity analysis yielded broadly consistent results. Greater winter indoor-temperature variability was associated with larger 5-year increases in home blood pressure independently of mean indoor temperature. Clinical Trial Registration URL: http://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm . UMIN Clinical Trials Registry, Trial No. UMIN000042196.

articles.title: Associations of skin sympathetic nerve activity with orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Excessive sympathetic activity may contribute to orthostatic hypertension and nocturnal hypertension. However, evidence on associations between skin sympathetic nerve activity (SKNA), assessed noninvasively using neuECG, and these hypertension phenotypes is limited. In this cross-sectional observational study, simultaneous SKNA and supine-to-standing blood pressure (BP) measurements were performed among outpatients with hypertension to examine these associations. Average SKNA (aSKNA) during supine and standing periods, and the percentage change in aSKNA from supine to standing (aSKNA%-changesupine-to-standing) were calculated. Orthostatic hypertension was defined as a supine-to-standing BP increase ≥20/10 mm Hg or conversion from <140/90 mm Hg to ≥140/90 mm Hg. Nighttime home BP was measured for 7 consecutive days; nocturnal hypertension was defined as nighttime BP ≥ 120/70 mm Hg. Associations of SKNA measures with orthostatic and nocturnal hypertension were examined using logistic regression analyses. A total of 141 participants (mean age, 67.6 years; 53.9% men) were included in the analyses. aSKNA%-changesupine-to-standing was correlated with standing SBP (rs = 0.221) and nighttime SBP (rs = 0.280). The adjusted odds ratio (OR) (95% CI) for orthostatic hypertension comparing the highest with the lowest tertile of aSKNA%-changesupine-to-standing was 2.18 (0.89-5.35). The corresponding OR for nocturnal hypertension was 2.74 (1.01-7.41) after adjustment for age and sex, and the corresponding OR for nondipping and riser patterns was 3.70 (1.38-9.90). In the current analysis, greater standing-induced increases in aSKNA tended to be associated with orthostatic and nocturnal hypertension, suggesting the potential role of SKNA in characterizing hypertension phenotypes associated with excessive sympathetic activity.

articles.title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats.
articles.abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

articles.title: Multifaceted role of genetic and epigenetic architecture of glucose homeostasis and diabetes.
articles.abstract: Glucose homeostasis depends on coordinated genetic and epigenetic regulation of pancreatic beta-cells, insulin-sensitive tissues, and neuroendocrine circuits. This review synthesises evidence from over 600 GWAS loci and the primary literature published between 2008 and 2026, and emerging single-cell functional genomics, CRISPR-based perturbation screens, deep-learning variant-effect predictors (DeepSEA, Enformer, AlphaGenome), and polygenic risk frameworks to explain insulin secretion, insulin signalling, and diabetes susceptibility, converting GWAS associations into mechanistic insight and genotype-guided precision therapies.

articles.title: A biomimetic nanoparticle coordinates antibacterial and immunomodulatory functions to promote periodontal regeneration.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by pathogenic microbial communities and an imbalanced host immune response, finally leading to progressive breakdown of periodontal soft and hard tissues. Current treatments primarily target infection but often fail to resolve inflammation or support subsequent tissue repair. Hence, we developed NMm@MINO, a biomimetic nanoparticle constructed by coating minocycline-loaded gelatin nanoparticles with a hybrid neutrophil-macrophage membrane. NMm@MINO formed a stable core-shell structure with a hydrodynamic diameter of (261.53 ± 11.59) nm and a membrane shell thickness of ~21 nm, maintaining colloidal stability for 30 days. Minocycline release was protease-responsive, with ~50% payload released within 2 h under gelatinase exposure and reaching equilibrium at ~8 h. In vitro, NMm@MINO achieved > 99% killing efficiency against Porphyromonas gingivalis and Staphylococcus aureus. Simultaneously, NMm@MINO reprogrammed polarization by downregulating M1-associated transcripts (Nos2, Tnf, Il1b, and Cd86) and upregulating M2-associated markers (Mrc1, Arg1, and Tgfb1), corroborated by decreased iNOS and increased CD206 immunofluorescence. NMm@MINO further enhanced osteogenesis (upregulating Alpl, Spp1, Runx2), suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis (reduced TRAP staining and downregulated Acp5, Tnfrsf11a, Ctsk, Fos, and Mmp9; decreased c-Fos immunofluorescence), and promoted fibroblast migration with increased Collagen I immunofluorescence. In a ligature-induced rat periodontitis model (days 3, 7, and 14), local NMm@MINO reduced inflammation (IL-6/CRP IHC; decreased Il6, Crp, and Il1b), improved collagen remodeling (H&E/Masson; increased Col1a1), and mitigated alveolar bone loss (micro-CT: CEJ-ABC, BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, and Tb.Sp) while modulating osteoclast/osteogenic markers (TRAP, RANKL/OPG IHC; Acp5, Tnfsf11, Tnfrsf11b, and Runx2). Collectively, NMm@MINO coordinates antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and pro-regenerative actions for periodontitis therapy.

articles.title: ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis.

METHODS: ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2-modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity.

RESULTS: In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF.

CONCLUSIONS: In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

articles.title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk.

METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum.

RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS (P=0.784).

CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

articles.title: Reply to: Prostate-specific membrane antigen-PET-defined oligoprogressive castration-resistant prostate cancer: is metastasis-directed therapy ready for prime time?
Global disparities in prevalence, aetiology, motor impairment severity, access to health care, and mortality in childhood cerebral palsy: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To map and synthesize the global literature on socioeconomic and structural inequalities in cerebral palsy (CP).

METHOD: A scoping review according to the framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley was conducted and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, World Health Organization Global Medical Index, African Journals Online, Scopus, Science Direct, Web of Science, and Wiley Online Library databases were searched. A manual search of Google Scholar was also conducted to capture grey literature. Observational studies reporting disparities in CP across high-income countries (HICs) and low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) were included. Data were extracted and synthesized narratively across five prespecified domains of inequality: prevalence, aetiology, severity, access to health care, and mortality.

RESULTS: Forty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Registry-based studies from HICs reported a birth prevalence of CP ranging from 1.4 to 2.5 per 1000 live births, most recently estimated at 1.6 per 1000 live births (95% confidence interval = 1.5-1.6). Registry-based prevalence in LMICs remained scarce, with estimates of up to 3.4 per 1000 live births and period-prevalence of 2.3 to 3.7 per 1000 children. A modelled estimate of 16.2 per 1000 children aged under 5 years has been reported in the World Health Organization African Region. Preventable causes, such as hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, kernicterus, and infection, were more frequently reported in low-resource settings, whereas preterm birth as a major risk factor was predominantly reported in HICs. Socioeconomic disadvantage, lower parental education, and minority ethnic status were associated with greater functional severity, higher comorbidity burden, and unmet health care needs. Physiotherapy was the main form of care reported in many LMICs. Studies from LMICs generally reported lower survival estimates and higher mortality rates than those from HICs. However, comparisons were limited by differences in study populations, severity profiles, and methodological approaches.

INTERPRETATION: This review identified pronounced disparities in CP across prevalence, severity, access to health care, and survival in diverse settings. The findings highlight important gaps in the evidence base and underscore the need for further research to better understand the mechanisms underlying these disparities and to inform equity-oriented health policies.

articles.title: An Electron Defect Engineering-Based Nanoparticle to Precisely Trigger Peroxynitrite Release to Synergistically Eliminate Bacteria and Alleviate Inflammation.
articles.abstract: The threat of bacterial infections such as Glaesserella parasuis and Streptococcus suis urges the development of advanced therapeutic strategies. To address this challenge, HAPC was designed with cascading responsiveness. When exposed to 640-660 nm red light, the electron-deficient porphyrin-zirconium MOF (PCN-224) can effectively use its natural photosensitive nature to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) and trigger subsequent reactions. Within the acidic conditions at the infection site, arginine (Arg) was triggered to release nitric oxide (NO), which may subsequently interact with ROS to form peroxynitrite (ONOO-) putatively contributing to enhanced antibacterial activity. The MIC for SS was just 0.25 µg/mL, making it four times more efficient than the free antibiotic CIP. Our study suggests that ONOO- potentially influenced the primary inflammatory pathway NF-κB and decreased the transcription levels of inflammatory mediators with TNF-α decreased by 10-fold for and IL-1β by 2.5-fold for respectively, ensuring antibacterial and anti-inflammatory responses at the same time. Experiments in vivo indicated that HAPC treatment could successfully clear bacteria from the infection site and hasten wound recovery, eventually decreasing the wound area to around 3%. This research showed that HAPC, via a proposed cascade mechanism originating from its material properties, offers a highly efficient, biosafe approach to combat zoonotic drug-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: Exploring Genetic and Biological Interconnections Between Neuroticism, Psychological Distress, Insomnia, and C-Reactive Protein: Insights From the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part B, Neuropsychiatric genetics : the official publication of the International Society of Psychiatric Genetics
articles.abstract: Psychobehavioral and physical health traits often co-occur. Although previous studies have identified associations between neuroticism, psychological distress, insomnia, and inflammatory biomarkers such as C-reactive protein (CRP), it remains unclear whether there is a genetic basis to these associations, and which biological pathways are involved. This study aimed to explore pleiotropy between psychobehavioural and physical traits and examine underlying biological pathways. To identify shared SNPs, we applied CPASSOC SHet and genomic SEM to GWAS summary statistics from the UK Biobank (Neale Lab; Nneuroticism = 293,006; Ndoctor visits for distress = 358,693; Ninsomnia = 360,738; NCRP = 358,693). Pathway enrichment analyses were done to explore relevant biological pathways based on positional and eQTL annotations. We used colocalization data to evaluate sharing of genetic signals between pairs of traits. Genetic correlations were moderate to high among neuroticism, distress visits, and insomnia, but low between CRP and each psychobehavioral trait. In the multitrait analyses, we did not observe any genomic region with genome-wide significant variants for all traits, although we identified a few regions with markers that reached genome-wide significance in the cross-trait analysis and had p-values < 0.001 for all traits. Enrichment analysis highlighted 8p23.1, a polymorphic inversion region enriched for immune and developmental genes. Colocalization supported multiple shared causal variants among psychobehavioral traits, with limited sharing with CRP. These findings suggest that co-occurrence between psychobehavioral and systemic inflammation traits is only weakly explained by shared common-variant genetics, emphasizing nongenetic mechanisms.

articles.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined.

OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH.

METHODS: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models.

CONCLUSIONS: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

articles.title: Voice Disorders: A Defining Problem.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Reported voice disorder prevalences vary widely across studies due to population heterogeneity and differences in operational definitions of voice disorders employed by those studies. The objective of this study was to compare responses to five questions using previously published operational definitions of voice disorder to each other and to measures of voice impact, and elicit definitions of "voice disorder" and potential reasons for care-seeking from nonclinical persons.

METHODS: A cross-sectional convenience sample of adult attendees of the Minnesota State Fair completed a survey including five different operational definitions of a voice disorder, items targeting measures of functional voice impact, and qualitative reflections. Responses to the five operational definitions were analyzed using percent agreement and kappa coefficients, with descriptive statistics used to correlate definitions with measures of functional voice impact. Free-text responses were coded systematically to identify common themes and subthemes.

RESULTS: In 795 participants, comparison between operational definitions showed prevalence of voice disorders ranging from 4%-7% currently, 7%-15% in the past 12 months, and 39%-62% lifetime. Across operational definitions, percent agreement ranged from 70%-95%, with kappa coefficients 0.37-0.77. Mean VHI-10 scores among respondents reporting a current voice problem on any operational definition were 12.2-14.5 (SD=6.0-7.7). A total of 577 participants indicated a positive response to one or more operational definitions. Of these, 48 individuals (8.3%) reported having sought care. Free-text responses regarding what constitutes a voice problem and what would prompt care-seeking highlighted pain/discomfort as a salient theme. This theme is rarely represented in established operational definitions and functional voice impact scales.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of voice problems measured using existing operational definitions was generally concordant with other ways to assess voice impact, but the specific definition wording meaningfully impacted prevalence estimates, especially across long time horizons. Future studies are needed to further elucidate care-seeking motivations and the importance of including pain/discomfort in voice problem prevalence estimates.

articles.title: Duplicated Inferior Vena Cava in Living Kidney Donor: Lessons From Two Cases With Contrasting Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Duplicated inferior vena cava (IVC) is a rare congenital anomaly. In living‑donor nephrectomy, a left‑sided duplicated IVC may be mistaken for an enlarged gonadal vein and inadvertently ligated, risking acute venous outflow obstruction.

CASE REPORTS: We report 2 contrasting cases of living kidney donors with duplicated IVC below the level of the left renal vein. In Case 1, the anomaly was not recognized preoperatively and the duplicated IVC was clamped intraoperatively, causing immediate renal vein distension. Prompt recognition and clamp removal averted thrombosis. In Case 2, the duplicated IVC was identified prospectively by computed tomographic angiography and meticulously preserved, allowing uneventful recovery.

CONCLUSION: These cases highlight the critical need for systematic preoperative imaging review and intraoperative vigilance to distinguish a duplicated IVC from a gonadal vein by its larger caliber, medial course, and connection to the iliac system. Awareness of this variation is essential to prevent iatrogenic injury and ensure donor safety.

articles.title: Prediction of Double-Expressor Lymphoma in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Using a Non-invasive Model Based on [18F] FDG PET/CT and Stacking.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an interpretable multimodal model integrating deep learning radiomics with clinical data using baseline [18F] FDG PET/CT for non-invasive identification of the double-expressor lymphoma (DEL) in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The histopathological reference standard for DLBCL diagnosis and DEL subtyping was immunohistochemistry according to the 2016 WHO. Patients from January 2019 to July 2025 were retrospectively enrolled and randomly divided into training and test sets at 7:3, and a patient-level analysis was performed. Clinical, radiomics and deep learning features were extracted. After LASSO selection, individual and fusion models were constructed. Statistical analyses were performed using Python (3.6), and p-value < 0.05 was considered significant. Model performance was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC), calibration and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP and a nomogram were used for interpretation.

RESULTS: A total of 143 patients (82 males, 61 females, median age 61.5 years) were enrolled. ViT_KNN model achieved a test AUC of 0.936 (95%Cl 0.856-1.000), outperforming clinical (AUC 0.857, 95%Cl 0.722-0.993) and radiomics (AUC 0.706, 95%Cl 0.547-0.865) models. Late fusion, especially Stacking_LR, achieved the best performance (AUC 0.948, 95%Cl 0.865-1.000, accuracy 95.3%, specificity 100%, sensitivity 88.2%). Calibration and DCA confirmed clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis highlighted deep learning features as most influential. The Stacking_LR nomogram offers an intuitive clinical tool.

CONCLUSION: Deep learning radiomics based on baseline [18F] FDG PET/CT enables effective non-invasive identification of DEL. The stacking ensemble strategy enhances multimodal fusion and provides a highly accurate, interpretable tool for DLBCL risk stratification.

articles.title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines.

OBJECTIVE: Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference.

OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS AND STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.

articles.title: Economic Evaluation of Surgical Management for Urolithiasis: A Systematic Review of Comparative Cost Analyses from EAU endourology.
authors: European Association of Urology Section of Endourology and the Young Academic Urologists Working Group Endourology and Urolithiasis
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Urolithiasis is a growing burden on health care systems. Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL), retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS), and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) are the main interventional options; however, their comparative cost-effectiveness is not fully established.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically review comparative research assessing the economic outcomes of these treatment modalities.

EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was performed for studies published between January 2010 and December 2025 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261303193). Eligible studies included cost analyses, cost-minimization, cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, and cost-benefit analyses comparing ESWL, RIRS, and/or PCNL. Risk-of-bias assessment used the Bias in Economic Evaluation checklist. All costs were adjusted for 2% annual inflation and converted to 2026 US dollars.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Of the 1861 records identified, 18 studies met inclusion criteria: ESWL versus RIRS (n = 9), ESWL versus PCNL (n = 2), RIRS versus PCNL (n = 4), and three-way comparisons (n = 3). Six studies assessed cost-effectiveness, six assessed cost-utility, and six were cost analyses. In ESWL versus RIRS comparisons, randomized trials reported approximately US $1251 lower costs for ESWL at 6 mo with small quality-adjusted life year (QALY) losses (-0.018 to -0.021), whereas long-term claim data showed higher 7-yr cumulative costs for ESWL (US $4647) compared with RIRS (US $4273). In ESWL versus PCNL studies, ESWL had lower per-patient costs (US $647-747 vs US $1307-1478) despite higher initial stone-free rates with PCNL. In RIRS versus PCNL evaluations, UK trials reported mean 12-mo costs of US $7722 for RIRS and US $6654 for PCNL, with PCNL showing an 87% probability of cost-effectiveness at US $29 152/QALY. Studies showed substantial heterogeneity in time horizons (2 wk to 7 yr), perspectives, and costing methods; only one-third performed probabilistic sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Comparative economic value among stone treatments is highly context-dependent: ESWL tends to be less costly in the short term (<12 mo), whereas RIRS may offer better long-term value for smaller stones through lower retreatment rates, and PCNL appears more cost-effective for larger stones in some settings. However, substantial study heterogeneity and methodological limitations restrict the generalizability of these findings.

PATIENT SUMMARY: We reviewed studies comparing the costs of the three main treatments for kidney stones: extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy, ureteroscopy (ie, retrograde intrarenal surgery), and percutaneous nephrolithotomy. We found that shock wave therapy costs less upfront but often requires repeat procedures, whereas ureteroscopy offers better long-term value for smaller stones, and percutaneous nephrolithotomy is most cost-effective for larger stones. More rigorous and longer-term studies are needed before firm recommendations can be made for all patients.

articles.title: The Business and Economic Case for "AI" in Radiology: A Radiologist's Perspective.
articles.abstract: AI is the current technological gift that will certainly change what radiologists do-but how, exactly? There are major differences between this new technology and previous technological advances. CT, MRI, US, PET-all generated fundamentally new types of images, more images, better images. They enabled medical imagers to see extraordinarily important clinical findings that had never been seen. The added clinical value of these new technologies quickly became standard of care, with appropriate reimbursement mechanisms, primarily new fee-for-service Clinical Practice Terminology codes. These technologies also provided more work for radiology departments-quickly becoming the bulk of our core diagnostic work. In contrast, what we call AI today does not generate fundamentally new types of images that add intrinsically novel or clinically critical information, though they may add operational efficiency. Based on this opinion, I do not believe that there will be additional reimbursable Clinical Practice Terminology codes to fund today's AI. Their administrative and operational advantages are welcome and needed, but they will have to be paid for by greater operational efficiencies.

articles.title: Defining sustained treatment benefit in low-renin hypertension with adrenal incidentalomas.
Sex and gender perspective in Intensive Care Medicine. An outstanding issue.
Perceived sustainability and alternatives to the on-call model in intensive care medicine: A survey of intensivists in the Community of Madrid.
Prevalence and prognostic significance of intracranial lesions assessed with MRI in infective endocarditis patients: Data from the Vesuve study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) is a life-threatening disease. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is efficient to detect cerebral IE related lesions, which are known to worsen prognosis. Systematic use of MRI remains controversial due to insufficient scientific evidence. This work was aimed at clarifying the prognostic value of this imaging method in the context of IE.

METHODS: The VESUVE study is a retrospective registry of patients with definite IE according to the modified Duke criteria, who had a brain MRI and were hospitalized between the 1st of November 2015 and the 15th of February 2019 in a Lyon University Hospital. All MRI were analyzed by the same senior neuroradiologist. Prognosis was evaluated by the mortality rate at 6 months.

RESULTS: Among 212 patients, 162 were considered to have an abnormal MRI (76.4%). Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) was present in 125 patients (60.4%), intracranial hemorrhage in 8 patients (3.8%), hemorrhagic transformation in 41 patients (19.5%), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) in 26 patients (12.4%), cerebral microbleed in 130 patients (62.5%), intracranial mycotic aneurysm in 10 patients (5.1%), sulcal microaneurysm in 45 patients (23.6%) and abscess in 3 patients (1.5%). Mortality rate at 6 months was 19% (37 patients deceased). AIS (26.9% mortality, 31 patients deceased, OR 5.11) and SAH (44% mortality, 11 patients deceased, OR 4.32) were linked to mortality.

CONCLUSION: The presence of AIS or SAH on brain MRI is independently linked to mortality in IE patients. This strengthens the prognostic value of MRI in the assessment of IE.

articles.title: Role of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis of chronic constrictive pericarditis revealed by Pick's syndrome: A case report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic constrictive pericarditis (CCP), or Pick's syndrome, is a rare but severe inflammatory disease of the pericardium, often difficult to distinguish from restrictive cardiomyopathy without multimodality imaging. In sub-Saharan Africa, tuberculosis remains the leading cause.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with a history of post-partum hypertension, admitted for a three-month history of exertional dyspnoea, lower-limb oedema and retrosternal chest pain in a febrile, tuberculosis-suggestive context. Examination revealed isolated right heart failure with a pericardial knock. Echocardiography and cardiac MRI showed pericardial thickening and circumferential detachment, bi-atrial dilatation and a septal bounce, with late gadolinium enhancement and T1/T2 mapping consistent with active pericardial inflammation, confirming an evolving, inflammatory form of CCP. Coronary CT angiography excluded coexisting coronary disease and revealed tuberculous pulmonary sequelae. Under corticosteroids, antituberculous therapy and symptomatic management, the patient improved clinically, allowing pericardiectomy to be deferred.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the value of cardiac MRI in the early diagnosis of inflammatory, potentially reversible forms of CCP, helping to avoid upfront surgery and guide targeted medical management, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions.

articles.title: [LDL-c and residual cardiovascular risk in patients with coronary artery disease].
articles.abstract: In secondary prevention, current therapeutic management of dyslipidemia primarily aims to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) levels, as LDL-c is a major driver of atherosclerosis. Elevated LDL-c levels are also one of the main modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. LDL-c lowering is directly, proportionally, and linearly associated with a reduction in cardiovascular events, with no apparent threshold effect. However, patients with chronic coronary syndrome or those who have recently experienced an acute coronary event are still generally undertreated and achieve guideline-recommended targets in only one out of four cases. This article aims to explore the underlying causes of and potential solutions to this therapeutic gap, which is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Treatment adherence varies considerably across studies (randomized controlled trials or real-life studies), as well as across geographical settings, and appears to be approximately 60%. However, non-adherence to treatment alone does not explain the low proportion of patients achieving LDL-c treatment targets, which remains at approximately 25%. The underlying reasons are complex and multifactorial. Paradoxically, although the expanding therapeutic armamentarium allows for increased substantial LDL-c reductions, this has not translated into a corresponding improvement in target attainment. Therapeutic inertia may arise at the patient, physician, and healthcare system levels. Furthermore, patient education and the therapeutic alliance should remain central to patient management and should be regularly reinforced and individualized.

articles.title: [The South African Flag Sign (SAFS) is a deadly diagnosis not to miss. About eleven cases].
articles.abstract: Between 2025 and 2026, our emergency medical service managed 850 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI); eleven (1.3%) of them presented the SAFS on electrocardiogram. This pattern is a rare electrocardiographic finding typically associated with the first diagonal (D1) branch occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery 1. It was first described by S. Sclarovsky in 1994, who reported a special form of anterior wall myocardial infarction characterized by ST-segment elevation (STE) in non-contiguous leads DI, aVL, and V2 with reciprocal changes in DIII and aVF 2. In 2016, Littman coined the term 'South African flag sign' to denote a visual mnemonic device or aid for this ECG pattern, with the objective of facilitating earlier detection of 'high lateral' myocardial infarction (MI) 3. We report eleven cases that exhibited this pattern to highlight the electrical aspect and especially its severity.

articles.title: Position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología on the early detection and timely referral of gastrointestinal cancer (esophagus, stomach, and colon) in primary care.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gastrointestinal cancer, particularly esophageal, gastric, or colon cancer, is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in Mexico. There are substantial delays in the early identification and timely referral of primary care patients, resulting in more advanced-stage diagnoses and poorer clinical outcomes. Our aim was to issue a position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología (AMG) to guide primary care physicians in the identification of alarm features, risk stratification, and timely referral of patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary group of 20 specialists in the fields of gastroenterology, oncology, endoscopy, epidemiology, and public health, from both public and private institutions, developed the position statement through a structured consensus process. Clinical statements were drafted and voted on, they were organized by cancer type (esophageal, gastric, and colorectal), and three clinical algorithms were designed to support decision-making in primary care.

RESULTS: Thirteen statements were issued on alarm features, risk factors, recommended diagnostic studies, and risk-stratified referral pathways (urgent, priority, and elective). The role of upper endoscopy and high-quality colonoscopy as diagnostic procedures of choice was emphasized, clearly distinguishing them from population-based screening strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: This position statement provides a practical, evidence-based, expert consensus-informed guide, adapted to the Mexican healthcare setting, whose aim is to implement prevention strategies, reduce diagnostic delays, improve early detection, and optimize the referral of primary care patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer.

articles.title: [Translated article] Complications associated with parenteral nutrition in hospitalized patients.
articles.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malnutrition is common in hospitalized patients. Parenteral nutrition is a therapeutic alternative to meet the nutritional requirements of patients in whom the gastrointestinal tract is unavailable or non-functional. This therapy has been associated with a wide range of infectious, mechanical and metabolic complications. The aim of the study was to assess the incidence of these complications.

METHOD: A prospective multicenter observational study in hospitalized adult patients receiving parenteral nutrition ≥72 h was conducted. Follow-up was performed until one week after the discontinuation of parenteral nutrition. Data were collected from electronic medical records and parenteral nutrition validation programs (Kabisoft and Clinus). Risk of malnutrition was determined according to MUST or CONUT criteria. The main variables were: incidence of catheter-related bacteriemia, catheter-tip colonization, phlebitis, thrombosis, catheter obstruction, catheter malposition, pneumothorax, hyperglycemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, hepatobiliary disorders and refeeding syndrome. A descriptive analysis was performed using SPSS v23 software.

RESULTS: Sixty patients were included, with a median age of 68 (28-90) years, 48.3% men and a body mass index of 26.2 ± 6.6 kg/m2. Of these, 61.7% were surgical patients and 46.7% were at low risk of malnutrition. Parenteral nutrition was administered for a median of 10 (3-40) days, 90.0% through central access. Patients received a mean of 18.4 ± 5.0 kcal/kg/day (74.7% of requirements), 1.1 ± 0.4 g/kg/day of protein, 2.4 ± 0.7 g/kg/day of glucose, and 0.5 ± 0.2 g/kg/day of lipids. Of them, 35% received concomitant enteral nutrition. Overall, 80.0% experienced at least one complication: metabolic (71.7%), mechanical (18.3%), and infectious (10.0%). Incidences were: hepatobiliary alteration (61.7%), hyperglycemia (48.3%), phlebitis (13.3%), catheter occlusion (8.3%), catheter-related bacteriemia (8.3%), hypertriglyceridemia (1.7%), hypercholesterolemia (1.7%), and colonization (1.7%). Gram-positive microorganisms were the most frequently isolated.

CONCLUSIONS: Although complications associated with parenteral nutrition occur, the rate of serious complications, such as infections, is low. While most patients experienced at least one complication, metabolic events were the most common, and they are generally easy to detect and manage. The incidence of mechanical complications, mainly phlebitis and catheter occlusions, was moderate.

articles.title: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndrome: A practical guide for clinicians.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndromes comprise a group of disorders affecting both the central and peripheral nervous systems, with an increasing incidence likely attributable to increased clinical awareness and continuous advances in diagnostic methods. These conditions are characterized by an aberrant immune response and often require the involvement of multiple specialties, including neurology, pediatrics, oncology, immunology, and intensive care medicine. In this review, we aimed to provide clinicians with essential knowledge for recognizing clinical syndromes suggestive of these entities, thereby facilitating the establishment of an appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic approach.

articles.title: [Cancer or chronic infection: Diagnostic challenges of pulmonary botryomycosis].
Hyperglycemia-induced hemiballismus: Case report with extended outpatient follow-up.
articles.abstract: Hyperglycemia-induced hemiballismus is a rare involuntary movement disorder that can result from uncontrolled blood glucose. Often the movements are reversible with corrected blood glucose, but occasionally they persist despite improved glycemic control. Several case reports have been published that follow the initial inpatient management of this condition, but little has been reported regarding long-term management, especially in the setting of persistent movements. This case report provides a unique perspective, as it follows a patient diagnosed with hyperglycemia-induced hemiballismus in an outpatient setting for a period of over two years.

articles.title: Medicalising the Human Cell Atlas for musculoskeletal disease: towards a translational roadmap.
articles.abstract: The Human Cell Atlas (HCA) has fundamentally changed the way biologists describe human tissues. However, its greatest promise for musculoskeletal (MSK) practitioners lies ahead: to convert cellular maps into clinically actionable knowledge. MSK diseases are common, heterogeneous, and often insufficiently stratified by current diagnostic labels. The same label, such as rheumatoid arthritis, can conceal distinct cellular mechanisms, tissue niches, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Conversely, apparently different disorders such as tendinopathy or fibrotic capsulitis can share convergent stromal, immune, vascular, or neuronal programmes. A MSK-HCA therefore should not be conceived as a passive reference catalogue. It should be 'medicalised': designed from the outset to connect tissue atlases with clinical phenotypes, imaging, biospecimens, genetic risk, biomarkers, perturbation experiments, and interventional trials. In this review, we describe how single-cell, single-nucleus, spatial, and multiomic approaches are beginning to map MSK tissues from development to ageing and from health to disease. We highlight examples in embryonic skeletal development, bone marrow, muscle ageing, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, tendon disease, and inflammatory fibrosis and show how these data can reframe disease taxonomy around pathogenic cell states rather than organ-level labels alone. We propose a translational roadmap in which atlases define healthy reference coordinates, identify disease-enriched cell states, nominate biomarkers and therapeutic targets, and then learn from clinical trial outcomes. For clinicians, the MSK-HCA offers a route to mechanism-led diagnosis and patient stratification; for scientists, it provides a shared coordinate system for testing how genes, cells, and tissue microenvironments generate disease. Medicalising the HCA could make cellular medicine a practical foundation for precision rheumatology and regenerative MSK therapy.

articles.title: Analytical Performance of the Sysmex XF-1600 Flow Cytometer in Routine Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Flow cytometry systems are increasingly used for the identification and quantification of lymphocyte subpopulations, supporting the diagnosis and monitoring of hematological and immunological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of the novel Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer for lymphocyte subpopulation quantification in peripheral blood, including precision, carryover, and agreement with established laboratory methods.

METHODS: Peripheral blood samples from routine clinical workload were analysed in the hematology laboratory. Analytical performance was assessed by evaluating precision (repeatability and reproducibility) and carryover. Absolute lymphocyte and leukocyte counts obtained using the XF-1600 automated sample preparation and volumetric counting system were compared with the Sysmex XN-series hematology analyser, while lymphocyte subset quantification was compared with the Navios flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter).

RESULTS: The XF-1600 showed coefficients of variation below 6% for major lymphocyte populations, including CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, CD19+, and CD16+/CD56+ cells. No carryover was detected. Comparison with the Sysmex XN analyser showed strong correlation for leukocyte and lymphocyte counts (Spearman's ρ = 0.986 and 0.993, respectively). Comparison with the Navios flow cytometer demonstrated high correlation across lymphocyte subpopulations (Spearman's ρ > 0.9 for most parameters). Bland-Altman and Passing-Bablok analyses showed good agreement between methods, although some parameters were not fully interchangeable.

CONCLUSION: The Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer demonstrated good analytical performance for lymphocyte subset quantification, with high precision and strong agreement with routinely used laboratory methods. The integration of automated sample preparation and volumetric counting may support standardization of immunophenotyping workflows in clinical laboratories.

articles.title: Snare-Guided Repositioning of a Vascular Plug Device for Device-Related Hemolytic Anemia.
Pulmonary Artery Dissection Identified by Optical Coherence Tomography in Takayasu Arteritis.
ROBIN to the Rescue: Balloon Laceration for LVOT Obstruction After Incomplete LAMPOON in Valve-in-Ring TMVR.
Cerebral Embolism in Transfemoral Carotid Artery Stenting Using Proximal Protection and MicroNet-Covered Stents: PROXGUARD Study.
Pulmonary Index of Microcirculatory Resistance: A Novel Hemodynamic Index for Invasively Assessing the Pulmonary Microvasculature.
Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization.

OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

articles.title: Beyond Procedural Success: Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation After Edge-to-Edge Repair in Perspective.
Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11).

CONCLUSIONS: recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

articles.title: Pulmonary Pressure Trajectories After Mitral TEER: Beyond Baseline Risk.
Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH.

METHODS: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH.

RESULTS: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH.

CONCLUSIONS: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

articles.title: The Second Generation of Coronary Lithotripsy.
Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.

METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed.

RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]).

CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation.

REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).

articles.title: Fathers matter: evidence on the role of father involvement for early development of rural Chinese sons and daughters.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregiver involvement in cognitively stimulating play is critical for children’s early development. Nevertheless, the role of fathers remains underexplored, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. This study examines the role of father involvement for developmental outcomes of sons and daughters under age 3 in rural Chinese households.

METHODS: In July 2024, we surveyed a randomly selected sample of 6–24 months old and their caregivers (n=592) in an east coast province in China. Children’s cognition, language and motor development was measured using the Third Edition of the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development (Bayley-III). Father and primary caregiver involvement was assessed with the play activities scale, family care indicators. Given that most fathers (96.1%) in the study sample are non-primary caregivers, while mothers (72.0%) and grandmothers (22.8%) hold most primary caregiving roles, the study focuses on non-primary caregiving fathers. Multivariate linear regression models were used to assess relationships of Bayley-III scores with father and primary caregiver involvement.

RESULTS: Involvement of non-primary caregiving fathers is low (ie, less than half the level of primary caregiver involvement). Less than 20% of fathers frequently tell stories or read books to their children. Children with more involved fathers (ie, above-median engagement in play activities) have, on average, Bayley-III composite cognitive, language and motor scores that are 5.1, 7.5 and 3.6 points higher than children with less involved fathers (ps<0.05). The results also provide suggestive evidence that father and primary-caregiver involvement each contribute to early language development, with their contributions accumulating when both are involved. Finally, contrary to traditional son preferences, fathers are found to engage more attentively with daughters, potentially as a result of changing times and cultural mores.

CONCLUSIONS: Encouraging father involvement may serve as a promising approach to support young children in reaching developmental potential in rural China.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN13421990.

articles.title: Spontaneous triple flexion response following acute pontine infarct.
Association of exercise with phenotype and arrhythmic outcomes in gene-elusive arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death in young adults and athletes. It is mostly genetically determined, with causal variants predominantly affecting desmosomal genes. Approximately one-third of patients remain gene-elusive despite extensive testing. Gene-elusive patients often report significantly higher lifetime exercise exposure than those with desmosomal ACM, suggesting a disproportionate role of exercise in this subgroup, also termed ‘exercise-induced ACM’. Yet, the effect of exercise history on the clinical characteristics and prognosis of this phenotype remains scarce.

METHODS: In this retrospective, single-centre cohort study, we included patients with definite or borderline ACM and negative genetic testing for ACM-associated genes. Exercise exposure was quantified with a standardised sports activity survey or from medical records. Competitive athletes were defined by an exercise exposure ≥24 metabolic equivalent of task-hour/week for ≥6 consecutive years and regular participation in competitive events. Life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias (LTVA) were defined as sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation or appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapies.

RESULTS: 46 patients (26 athletes, 20 non-athletes) were followed for a median of 7.5 years. At diagnosis, most athletes (77%) had definite right-ventricular ACM, compared with only 40% of non-athletes (p=0.025). Compared with non-athletes, athletes had a larger end-diastolic right-ventricular volume, while other imaging findings did not differ significantly. Athletes showed a distinct electrical phenotype with a shorter QTc (424 ms vs 449 ms, p<0.001), more T-wave inversions (4.0 vs 2.40, p=0.047) and a higher hazard of LTVA, death or heart transplantation during follow-up (HR 2.67, 95% CI 1.11 to 6.44, p=0.029).

CONCLUSION: In gene-elusive ACM, a history of competitive athletic participation was associated with more extensive repolarisation abnormalities, larger right ventricular volumes and a higher hazard of adverse outcomes during follow-up. These associations require validation in prospective multicentre cohorts, particularly regarding the relationship between exercise exposure and arrhythmic risk.

articles.title: Stage-dependent timing of relative and absolute treatment benefit in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), treatment effects are often delayed and stage-dependent, which complicates interpretation of a single HR. The timing of relative and absolute benefit at each stage is unclear. We examined stage-specific treatment effects of tafamidis using complementary time-to-event analyses.

METHODS: Individual patient-level data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves of the Tafamidis in Transthyretin Cardiomyopathy Clinical Trial long-term extension and analysed by National Amyloidosis Centre (NAC) stage. Time to benefit (TTB) was estimated from flexible parametric (Royston-Parmar) models with time-varying treatment effects, providing time-varying HRs and absolute risk reduction and was cross-checked with truncated Cox and restricted mean survival time (RMST) trajectory analyses.

RESULTS: Effects differed by NAC stage. Tafamidis reduced mortality in NAC1 (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.73) and NAC2 (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.86); no effect was seen in NAC3. Hazard reduction was early and consistent in NAC1 but delayed in NAC2. HR-based TTB was 36 months in NAC1 and 50 months in NAC2 and was not reached in NAC3. RMST-based TTB occurred later (38 and 61 months). At maximum follow-up, RMST gain was 17 months in NAC1, 13 months in NAC2 and 1 month in NAC3.

CONCLUSIONS: Survival benefit from tafamidis is stage-dependent, appearing earlier and lasting longer in less advanced disease. In intermediate-stage disease, relative effects preceded—and at times diverged from—absolute survival gains. These data support early initiation of therapy and the use of complementary analytical approaches alongside the conventional HR.

articles.title: Joints and brain: a multisystem puzzle in a child.

[Efficacy and safety of domestic semaglutide injection in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with metformin: a multicenter, randomized, controlled phase 3 equivalence clinical trial].
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of domestic semaglutide injection in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) inadequately controlled with metformin. Methods: This multicenter, randomized, positive-controlled phase 3 equivalence clinical trial enrolled patients with T2DM from 39 research centers in China between March 13, 2024, and April 9, 2025. Central randomization was performed using interactive response technology, and the subjects were stratified according to their glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels (<8.5% and ≥8.5%) and randomly divided into an experimental group (domestic semaglutide injection) and a control group (original semaglutide injection) at a ratio of 1∶1. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in HbA1c at week 32, with an equivalent threshold of ±0.4%. The key secondary endpoints included HbA1c change from baseline at week 20, the proportion of patients with HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% at 20 and 32 weeks, and the evaluation of safety. Efficacy endpoints were analyzed in the full analysis set (FAS), and safety endpoints were analyzed in the safety set (SS). Changes from baseline in HbA1c were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures; the proportions of subjects with HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% were compared using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel χ2 test; and safety endpoints were analyzed using Fisher's exact test. Results: Both the FAS and SS included 481 patients, with 241 in the experimental group and 240 in the control group. After 32 weeks of treatment, the least squares mean (LSM) (95%CI) changes from baseline in HbA1c were -1.80% (-1.93%--1.68%) in the experimental group and -1.85% (-1.98%--1.72%) in the control group, with a difference of 0.05% (-0.13%-0.23%)(both one-sided P<0.001). Similarly, equivalence was demonstrated at week 20, with an intergroup difference (95%CI) of 0.08% (-0.10%-0.26%) for the change from baseline in HbA1c (both one-sided P<0.001). The proportions of patients achieving HbA1c<7.0% or HbA1c≤6.5% showed no statistically significant differences between the two groups. The incidence of overall adverse events was comparable between the two groups [85.06% (205/241) vs 83.33% (200/240)], and the incidences of drug-related hypoglycemic events were 0.41% (1/241) and 2.50% (6/240), respectively, with no statistically significant differences (both P>0.05). Conclusions: In patients with T2DM inadequately controlled by metformin, domestic semaglutide injection demonstrated glucose-lowering efficacy equivalent to original semaglutide injection over the 32-week short-term period, with generally similar overall safety profiles between the two groups.
