articles.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
articles.abstract: The Chinese guidelines for the diagnosis and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (2026 revision) were developed by the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Groups of the Chinese Thoracic Society and the Chinese Association of Chest Physicians. Building on the 2021 edition, this revision incorporates evidence published over the past five years and experience from COPD prevention and management in China, and provides comprehensive updates on disease definition, etiology and pathogenesis, case finding, diagnosis and comprehensive assessment, stable COPD management, diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbations, comorbidity management, and future research directions. The guideline primarily applies the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, supplemented by the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence, to assess the certainty of evidence and develop recommendations. It offers practical recommendations for the diagnosis and management of COPD across 22 clinical questions. It aims to promote early identification, standardized diagnosis and treatment, and comprehensive management of COPD, and therefore to improve the standardized care and reduce the disease burden of COPD in China.The 22 key clinical questions and corresponding recommendations are summarized as follows.Question 1: Given the current underdiagnosis of COPD, which strategies can improve early diagnosis?Recommendation 1: We recommend active and opportunistic case finding to identify individuals at high risk of COPD and facilitate early diagnosis. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 2: Which parameters should be assessed when selecting initial pharmacotherapy for patients with COPD?Recommendation 2: Patients with COPD should undergo individualized assessment based on symptom burden and exacerbation risk and be classified into groups A, B, or E. Additional assessments should include the severity of airflow obstruction on pulmonary function testing, comorbidities, and biomarkers such as the peripheral blood eosinophil count. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 3: How should the mMRC and CAT scores be used for symptom assessment in the ABE classification?Recommendation 3: Symptoms of COPD should be assessed using the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale and/or the COPD Assessment Test (CAT). Results from the two instruments may be discordant: the mMRC scale focuses on dyspnea, whereas the CAT is more suitable for a comprehensive assessment of multiple symptoms. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 4: Should chest CT be included in the initial assessment of COPD?Recommendation 4: Chest imaging should be included in the initial assessment of COPD, with chest computed tomography (CT) preferred. (2B/conditional recommendation)Question 5: What are the key preventive measures targeting exposure to risk factors?Recommendation 5: Smoking cessation interventions should be actively provided to all patients with COPD. Clean fuels, effective ventilation, nonpolluting stoves, and similar measures are recommended to reduce harmful environmental exposures; occupational protection should also be strengthened to avoid continued exposure to potential irritants. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 6: How should vaccination be recommended for patients with COPD?Recommendation 6: Annual influenza vaccination is recommended. Regular pneumococcal vaccination with PPSV23 is also recommended, with PCV20 or PCV21 as options for susceptible individuals; the specific pneumococcal vaccination schedule should follow product-specific prescribing information. (1A/strong recommendation). Vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap), and herpes zoster is suggested. (1A/conditional recommendation)Question 7: How should initial pharmacotherapy be selected according to the ABE classification and the peripheral blood eosinophil count?Recommendation 7: Initial pharmacotherapy should be selected according to symptoms, exacerbation risk, and the peripheral blood eosinophil count. For patients in group E, regimens that reduce the risk of future exacerbations should be prioritized. When the peripheral blood eosinophil count is ≥300 cells/μl, triple inhaled therapy[inhaled corticosteroids(ICS) plus long-acting β2 agonists (LABA) plus long-acting muscarinic antagonists(LAMA)] is recommended to achieve a state of low disease activity characterized by freedom from exacerbations. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 8: What are the indications for adding an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy?Recommendation 8: The addition of an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy is recommended for patients with COPD who have any of the following features: (1)≥1 moderate or severe COPD exacerbation per year; (2) a blood eosinophil count ≥300 cells/μl, or ≥100 cells/μl during follow-up assessment; or (3) a history of asthma or concomitant asthma-like features. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 9: How should a standardized pathway for follow-up assessment and pharmacological treatment adjustment be established for patients with stable COPD?Recommendation 9: During follow-up pharmacotherapy, treatment adjustment should be guided by two core treatable traits: persistent dyspnea and the occurrence of exacerbations. For patients with persistently poor symptom control, bronchodilator therapy should be optimized stepwise after inhaler technique, adherence, and the effects of comorbidities have been assessed. For patients who continue to experience exacerbations, the addition, continuation, or cautious withdrawal of ICS should be guided by the current regimen and peripheral blood eosinophil count. Biologic therapy is appropriate for selected high-risk populations. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 10: How should treatment be optimized and adjusted for patients already receiving ICS+LABA therapy?Recommendation 10: Patients receiving ICS+LABA may continue the regimen if their condition is stable. If exacerbations persist, escalation to triple therapy with ICS+LABA+LAMA is recommended. For patients with COPD who are at high risk of pulmonary infection, including mycobacterial infection, withdrawal of ICS and a switch to dual bronchodilator therapy should be considered to reduce the risk of further infections. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 11: What are the indications for biologic therapy in patients with COPD?Recommendation 11: For patients who continue to experience recurrent exacerbations despite ICS+LABA+LAMA therapy, inhaled medication use, comorbidities and other contributing factors should be assessed, and biologic therapy should be selected on an individualized basis according to features such as the peripheral blood eosinophil count and the presence of chronic bronchitis. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 12: How should an inhaler device be selected according to individual patient characteristics?Recommendation 12: The most appropriate inhaler device and medication should be selected according to whether the patient has adequate inspiratory flow, hand-mouth coordination, and the ability to inhale independently, as well as the characteristics of the device and medication. Training in inhaler technique and individualized assessment should be reinforced. (4/strong recommendation)Question 13: How should pulmonary rehabilitation be implemented for patients with COPD?Recommendation 13: Dynamic pulmonary rehabilitation assessment is recommended before treatment and at different stages during treatment, including clinical, functional, nutritional, and psychological assessments. Pulmonary rehabilitation should be initiated as early as possible in patients with stable COPD who have no absolute contraindications. For patients with acute exacerbations of COPD, pulmonary rehabilitation should be provided early during hospitalization and after discharge. An individualized rehabilitation prescription should be developed according to assessment findings and may include airway clearance techniques, breathing training, aerobic and resistance exercise, positioning, and respiratory support. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 14: What are the indications and treatment regimen for oxygen therapy in stable COPD?Recommendation 14: Long-term oxygen therapy is recommended for patients with COPD and severe resting hypoxemia, defined as either (1) PaO2≤55 mmHg(1 mmHg=0.133 kPa) or SpO2≤88% at rest, or (2) PaO2 of 55-60 mmHg or SpO2 of 88%-89% at rest together with pulmonary hypertension, peripheral edema suggestive of congestive heart failure, or polycythemia (hematocrit>55%). Oxygen should be administered for at least 15 h/day to maintain PaO2 ≥60 mmHg and/or SpO2 ≥90%. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 15: What are the indications for noninvasive ventilation in stable COPD?Recommendation 15: Long-term noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is suggested for patients with severe chronic hypercapnia and a history of hospitalization for acute respiratory failure, or for those with persistent daytime hypercapnia (PaCO2>53 mmHg). (1B/strong recommendation)Question 16: Which pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions can reduce mortality in patients with COPD?Recommendation 16: Smoking cessation, pharmacotherapy (fixed-dose triple therapy), and nonpharmacological interventions, including pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term oxygen therapy, noninvasive ventilation, and surgical lung volume reduction, are recommended to reduce mortality in patients with COPD. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 17: How should bronchoscopic interventional therapies be selected for patients with COPD?Recommendation 17: Bronchoscopic interventions, including endobronchial valves and thermal vapor ablation, are recommended for selected patients with advanced emphysema and COPD. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 18: What are the indications for lung transplantation in patients with COPD?Recommendation 18: For patients with very severe COPD (progressive disease with a BODE index of 7-10 who are not candidates for lung volume reduction surgery), referral for lung transplantation may be considered if at least one of the following is present: (1) a history of hospitalization for an acute hypercapnic exacerbation (PaCO2>50 mmHg); (2) pulmonary hypertension and/or cor pulmonale despite oxygen therapy; or (3) FEV₁<20% predicted together with DLCO<20% predicted or homogeneous emphysema. (3B/conditional recommendation)Question 19: How should systemic corticosteroids be used for acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 19: For moderate or severe acute exacerbations of COPD, low-dose, short-course systemic corticosteroid therapy is suggested; routine prolongation of treatment or use of high-dose systemic corticosteroids is not recommended. Nebulized budesonide may be considered as an alternative for patients with contraindications to systemic corticosteroids or a high risk of adverse reactions. (Very low-quality evidence/weak recommendation)Question 20: How should high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy be used in the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 20: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy is suggested for patients with an acute exacerbation of COPD who have persistent hypoxemia, cannot tolerate NIV or have contraindications to NIV, require sequential oxygen therapy after NIV, or require prevention of reintubation after extubation. In patients with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure who meet the indications for NIV, HFNC should not replace NIV as the preferred initial treatment. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 21: What are the indications for noninvasive ventilation in the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 21: NIV is recommended for patients with an acute exacerbation of COPD who have any of the following: (1) respiratory acidosis (PaCO2 ≥6.0 kPa or 45 mmHg and arterial pH≤7.35); (2) severe dyspnea with clinical signs of respiratory muscle fatigue and/or increased work of breathing, such as use of accessory respiratory muscles, paradoxical thoracoabdominal motion, or intercostal retraction; (3) persistent hypoxemia despite oxygen therapy; or (4) a need for sequential invasive-noninvasive mechanical ventilation. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 22: What measures are recommended to prevent acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 22: After an acute exacerbation, the management plans for COPD and its comorbidities should be evaluated, and appropriate measures should be implemented to prevent further exacerbations, particularly peri-discharge management, long-term standardized pharmacotherapy, smoking cessation, vaccination, and nonpharmacological interventions such as pulmonary rehabilitation. (4/strong recommendation).

articles.title: Early Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor and Mortality in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet the optimal timing of initiation in routine clinical practice remains uncertain. We investigated the impact of early initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis on mortality and HF hospitalization.

METHODS: Using Danish nationwide register data from July 2020 to August 2024, adults with incident HFrEF eligible for SGLT2i therapy were identified. A target trial comparing initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis versus no SGLT2i initiation during this 30-day period was emulated. The analysis used a clone-censor-weight design with follow-up starting at HFrEF diagnosis. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality, and HF hospitalization was assessed as a secondary outcome.

RESULTS: Among 10,346 patients with incident HFrEF, 3268 (31.6%) initiated an SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis and 7078 (68.4%) did not initiate the treatment during this 30-day window. About 226 deaths occurred among SGLT2i initiators and 637 deaths among non-initiators. Compared with non-initiation, initiation of SGLT2i within 30 days was associated with lower one-year risks of both death (RD -1.1 percentage points; 95% CI (-2.0 to -0.2)) and HF hospitalization (RD -3.4 percentage points; 95% CI (-3.9 to -2.9)).

CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of an SGLT2i within 30 days of HFrEF diagnosis was associated with lower one-year mortality and HF hospitalization compared with no initiation. These findings support prioritizing early SGLT2i initiation as part of foundational therapy for HFrEF in routine clinical practice.

Dysphagia in infective and non-infective exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infection and sepsis have been identified as potential risk factors for dysphagia in hospitalised patients, but their contribution relative to that of respiratory dysfunction is unclear. We used acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) as a clinical model to test whether infection is independently associated with dysphagia.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of adults admitted with acute COPD exacerbations to a National Health Service (NHS) trust in Manchester, UK, between 2022 and 2023. Admissions were classified as infective (n=4474) or non-infective (n=608); patients with sepsis (n=556) were identified within the infective cohort. The primary outcome was new-onset dysphagia during the index admission; secondary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and length of stay (LOS). Regression models were adjusted for age, sex, frailty and Charlson Comorbidity Index.

RESULTS: Dysphagia was recorded in 2.93% of infective versus 0.99% of non-infective admissions (unadjusted OR 3.03, 95% CI 1.33 to 6.89; p=0.008). Infection remained independently associated with dysphagia (adjusted OR (aOR) 2.46, 95% CI 1.08 to 5.64; p=0.033), in-hospital mortality (aOR 3.84, 2.34 to 6.31; p<0.001) and longer LOS (β 3.06 days, 1.92 to 4.20; p<0.001). Within the infective cohort, sepsis was independently associated with dysphagia (aOR 1.70, 1.09 to 2.65; p=0.019), mortality (aOR 3.13, 2.51 to 3.90; p<0.001) and prolonged LOS (β 5.39 days, 4.13 to 6.64; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: In acute COPD exacerbations, infection was independently associated with dysphagia, with the highest prevalence in sepsis. Infection may contribute to dysphagia risk beyond respiratory dysfunction alone, supporting targeted swallowing assessment in infective exacerbations, particularly when complicated by sepsis.

Prognostic value of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) for major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of cardiovascular death, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification. The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) is a novel integrated biomarker that captures the synergistic effects of metabolic and inflammatory pathways by combining C-reactive protein (CRP), triglycerides (TG) and glucose. However, its prognostic value for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with CAD remains unclear.

METHOD: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 1533 newly diagnosed CAD patients stratified by admission CTI tertiles (T1: <8.744, n=511; T2: 8.744–9.367, n=512; T3: ≥9.367, n=510). The primary endpoint, MACE (397 events), was confirmed via medical records and follow-up. Group comparisons were performed using ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis or χ2 tests, as appropriate. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to assess the independent association between CTI and MACE, with sequential adjustment for confounders. Kaplan-Meier curves and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were applied. Analyses were conducted using SPSS 26.0, with a two-sided p<0.05 considered significant.

RESULTS: In the fully adjusted Cox model, elevated CTI remained significantly associated with an increased risk of MACE (per 1-unit increase: HR 1.851, 95% CI 1.632 to 2.098; p<0.001). Compared with the lowest tertile (T1), the highest CTI tertile (T3, ≥9.367) was associated with a significantly higher MACE risk (HR 1.936, 95% CI 1.538 to 2.437; p<0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a dose-dependent relationship (log-rank p=0.001). ROC curve analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.698 (95% CI 0.666 to 0.769), with an optimal CTI cut-off of ≥9.49 (sensitivity 53.9%, specificity 79.8%). Sensitivity analyses adjusting for potential mediators confirmed the robustness of these findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Based on Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, CTI is an independent predictor of MACE risk in patients with CAD. CTI offers superior prognostic value over its individual components and may assist in risk assessment. However, larger prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility before routine application.

Cancer incidence following platelet count and C-reactive protein testing across ethnic groups in English primary care: a cohort study of 5 million patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether the association between platelet count or C-reactive protein (CRP) results and 1-year cancer incidence varies by patient ethnicity.

DESIGN: Cohort study using routinely collected health records from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum, Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care and National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service.

SETTING: English primary care, with linkage to secondary care records and national cancer registry data.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged 40 years or older with a recorded ethnicity, no previous malignancy, and a platelet count or CRP test recorded between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2017. Ethnicity was categorised as white, Asian, black, other or mixed.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome measures were 1-year cancer incidence following platelet count or CRP testing and variation in the association by ethnicity. Secondary outcome measures were 1-year site-specific cancer incidence and stage at diagnosis.

RESULTS: The study included 4 901 450 patients with a platelet count record and 811 559 with a CRP record. One-year cancer incidence was highest among white patients and lowest among Asian patients. Following a normal platelet count, 1-year cancer incidence was 1.3% (95% CI 1.3 to 1.3%) for white patients and 0.63% (0.60 to 0.66%) for Asian patients; following thrombocytosis, incidence increased to 3.9% (3.8 to 4.0%) and 1.8% (1.5 to 2.1%), respectively. After a normal CRP result, cancer incidence was 1.5% (1.4 to 1.5%) for white patients and 0.81% (0.73 to 0.90%) for Asian patients, rising to 3.6% (3.5 to 3.7%) and 1.9% (1.7 to 2.2%) for a high CRP result, respectively. No significant interactions were found between ethnicity, blood test result and overall cancer diagnosis, and similar ORs were observed across all ethnic groups. However, for colorectal cancer, black patients with abnormal results showed higher ORs compared with white patients, relative to a normal result. The OR for thrombocytosis was 11.1 (7.8 to 15.6) for black patients versus 5.7 (5.4 to 6.0) for white patients (interaction p value<0.001), and for raised CRP was 4.1 (2.6 to 6.6) for black patients versus 2.5 (2.3 to 2.7) for white patients (interaction p value=0.043).

CONCLUSIONS: This large primary care study provides reassurance that thrombocytosis and raised CRP appear to have broadly consistent associations with 1-year cancer incidence across ethnic groups in UK primary care.

Construction and External Validation of a Predictive Nomogram for Premature Unplanned Discontinuation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in the ICU.
articles.journal: Therapeutic apheresis and dialysis : official peer-reviewed journal of the International Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To develop and validate a 2-h early-warning nomogram for the risk of unplanned discontinuation of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in elderly intensive care unit (ICU) patients.

METHODS: This study retrospectively enrolled elderly CRRT patients from two tertiary hospitals (2022-2024) via convenience sampling for model development. Predictive performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with goodness of fit assessed by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test; an external cohort (Jan-Aug 2025) was used for clinical applicability.

RESULTS: The unplanned CRRT discontinuation rate reached 27.4% in the modeling cohort and 32.8% in an external temporal validation cohort (n = 247 sessions). Independent predictors included hypotension, therapeutic intervention scoring system (TISS) score, transmembrane pressure (TMP) at 2 h > 86 mmHg, and diagnosis. The model demonstrated robust predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.860 (training) and 0.865 (validation), good calibration (Brier scores: 0.107 internal, 0.127 external), and clinical net benefit across thresholds per decision curve analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: The model demonstrates robust discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit, with readily available variables indicating substantial potential for valuable clinical applications.

articles.title: Impact of air pollution exposure in early life on lung function development in the COPSAC cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term exposure to ambient air pollution has been associated with reduced lung function in children and may also impair lung function development in early life.

OBJECTIVES: We examined associations of long-term exposure to air pollution with lung function at age 6 and lung function development from early childhood until young adulthood.

METHODS: We modelled concentrations of the particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter less than 2.5 μm (PM2.5) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) from multiple sources at the home addresses of the participants (N=846) of the Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood cohorts from 2000 and 2010 in Denmark. Lung function was measured by spirometry and plethysmography repeatedly from 3 to 18 years of age. Associations were estimated with adjusted linear mixed-effects regression models.

RESULTS: A higher long-term exposure to air pollution in early life was associated with reduced lung function at age 6. For instance, an IQR of 2.2 μg/m3 increment in postnatal exposure to PM2.5 was associated with a 2.70% (95% CI 4.27% to 1.10%) lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) and 7.30% (95% CI 1.87% to 13.07%) higher specific airway resistance. This mirrored reduced lung function and increased airway resistance development rates throughout childhood. Associations for airway restrictions were stronger for males than females.

CONCLUSIONS: Early life exposure to ambient air pollution was associated with the development of reduced lung function and increased airway resistance throughout childhood.

articles.title: Completeness of individual characteristic data in UK pulmonary rehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Inequalities in the enrolment and completion of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) across individual characteristics persist. Accurate data collection of individual characteristics supports services to identify and address these inequalities. This study assessed the completeness of individual characteristic data in a UK National Respiratory Audit Programme dataset of 88 446 individuals assessed March 2019–September 2023. Age, gender and index of multiple deprivation quintile were consistently collected (<1% missing). Ethnicity and Medical Research Council dyspnoea score had substantially higher levels of missing data (14% and 7%, respectively). Improving data completeness may support health inequalities to be identified and addressed in PR services.

articles.title: Nationwide study of blood eosinophils in COPD: impact of exacerbations and corticosteroids.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blood eosinophils are increasingly used as biomarkers to guide inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) and biologic therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the long-term stability of eosinophil count and the impact of proximate clinical events remain uncertain. This study examines the longitudinal stability of blood eosinophil counts in a nationwide cohort of COPD patients and identifies acute exposures temporally linked to eosinophil measurement variability.

METHODS: We used routinely collected Danish national registry data including 63 517 patients with COPD aged ≥40 years with ≥4 eosinophil measurements during 2–6 years of follow-up (median 3.4). Eosinophils were categorised as <0.15, 0.15–0.29 and ≥0.30×10⁹/L. Logistic regression assessed associations between stability and clinical exposures, adjusting for baseline eosinophils, age, sex, comorbidities, oral corticosteroid (OCS) use, antibiotics and exacerbations. Transitions were visualised with Sankey diagrams.

RESULTS: Overall, 26% of patients remained within the same eosinophil category across all repeated measurements (stable patient phenotype), while 74% experienced ≥1 category shift. Baseline eosinophils ≥0.30×10⁹/L predicted phenotypic stability (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.63 to 1.77). Severe exacerbations, OCS and antibiotics prior to testing were associated with individual measurement variability, yet >80% of unstable measurements occurred without these exposures. Among patients with an unstable phenotype, 39.7% shifted once, 43.2% two times and 17.1% three times. Use of triple inhaler therapy (long-acting beta-agonist, long-acting muscarinic antagonist, ICS) was slightly more common among in the unstable group.

CONCLUSIONS: Blood eosinophil counts in COPD are highly dynamic, with most patients shifting categories over time independent of clinical exposures. Single eosinophil measurements may be unreliable for guiding therapy; repeated assessments could improve identification of patients most likely to benefit from type 2 inflammation-targeted treatments.

articles.title: Clinical characterisation and therapeutic insights from a single-centre cohort of seven patients with Gorham-Stout disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gorham-Stout disease (GSD) is an ultra-rare disorder of progressive osteolysis and lymphatic proliferation, with poorly defined clinical features, optimal imaging and treatment. This study characterises the clinical spectrum, imaging findings and therapeutic responses in a single-centre GSD cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed seven patients with GSD at the National Center for Respiratory Medicine (2019–2024). Data included demographics, clinical presentation, laboratory, pathology, multimodality imaging (CT, bone scintigraphy, 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) and 18F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (18F-FAPI) positron emission tomography (PET)/CT, lymphoscintigraphy) and follow-up.

RESULTS: Patients (six males, one female; median age 27 years) commonly presented with dyspnoea (5/7) and universal pleural effusion (7/7, including four chylothoraces). Extensive osteolysis (ribs, spine, pelvis) occurred without significant bone pain in most cases. 18F-FAPI PET/CT showed intense uptake (maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax) 4.0–17.6) in lesions, superior to 18F-FDG PET/CT (SUVmax<2.5 in 6/7). Lymphoscintigraphy confirmed central lymphatic leakage in all tested patients. Histopathology revealed D2-40-positive lymphatic proliferation. Individualised treatment included sirolimus (one patient, clinical and radiological improvement), alendronate (one patient, stable disease) and supportive care (five patients, symptomatic improvement over a 15-month median follow-up).

CONCLUSIONS: GSD often presents with chylothorax and respiratory symptoms rather than bone pain. 18F-FAPI PET/CT is superior to FDG for assessing activity and monitoring response. Whether mammalian target of rapamycin inhibition or antiresorptive therapy improves outcomes cannot be determined from this small series; our single-patient observations with sirolimus and alendronate are hypothesis-generating only. Multidisciplinary, individualised management with advanced imaging is essential.

articles.title: 'The prevalence of exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction (EILO) among children with asthma': a study protocol of a prospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Exercise-induced symptoms are common within the paediatric population and can hamper participation in sports and play, negatively impacting cardiorespiratory activity and social interaction. Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) is a prevalent and well-known cause of exercise-induced symptoms. Especially in children with asthma, exercise-induced symptoms are often primarily attributed to EIB, although other causes of exercise-induced symptoms are numerous. In patients with exercise-induced laryngeal obstruction (EILO), narrowing of the larynx during exercise causes symptoms similar to those of EIB. The reported prevalence of EILO among adults with asthma ranges from 13% to 47%, whereas EILO prevalence among the general adolescent population is 5%–8%. Currently, the prevalence of EILO among asthmatic adolescents has not yet been investigated. In this study, we aim to investigate the prevalence of EILO among adolescents with asthma. Knowledge of EILO prevalence in this specific group can help to determine the position of the continuous laryngoscopy during exercise (CLE) test in diagnostic guidelines for adolescents with asthma.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This study protocol describes a prospective cross-sectional study that aims to include 200 participants from the outpatient paediatric department of Medisch Spectrum Twente (Enschede, The Netherlands) and Haukeland University Hospital (Bergen, Norway). Consecutive participants referred for an exercise challenge test (ECT) to evaluate their asthma will be informed and asked to participate. Reasons for non-participation or exclusion will be registered. Participants are eligible for inclusion if they are between 12 and 18 years of age and have asthma confirmed with at least one objective lung function test during the last 2 years. Demographic background variables and comorbidities will be collected. Included children will undergo both an ECT and CLE test within a time frame of 1 month. The primary outcome is the prevalence of EILO in the study population of adolescents with asthma, calculated as a percentage with a 95% CI.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval has been granted and the study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06480084). Study results will be presented at medical conventions and in peer-reviewed scientific journals.

Polymicrobial anaerobic meningitis with ventriculitis involving Solobacterium moorei and Slackia exigua: A case report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Anaerobic bacteria are uncommon causes of bacterial meningitis. We report a rare case of polymicrobial anaerobic meningitis with ventriculitis involving Slackia exigua and Solobacterium moorei, both oral anaerobes. A 41-year-old woman presented with headache, vomiting, and impaired consciousness. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was consistent with bacterial meningitis, and cultures yielded S. exigua and S. moorei, identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, with S. exigua confirmed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Blood cultures showed polymicrobial bacteremia, including S. exigua, Streptococcus anginosus, and Desulfovibrio falkowii. The identification of D. falkowii was performed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and corroborated by whole-genome sequencing. Untreated dental caries, periodontitis, and sinusitis were considered potential portals of entry. The patient responded favorably to continued antimicrobial therapy with ampicillin/sulbactam and metronidazole. This case highlights the clinical relevance of rare oral anaerobes in central nervous system infections. It underscores the polymicrobial nature of anaerobic meningitis and illustrates the potential value of combining conventional culture, matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, and molecular methods in identifying uncommon pathogens.

articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After the COVID-19 pandemic-related interruption of influenza activity, season-specific data on resistance-associated substitutions and treatment outcomes remain important.

METHODS: A prospective multicenter observational study during the A(H1N1)pdm09-dominant 2024-2025 season in Japan evaluated resistance-associated substitutions, post-treatment virus isolation, and fever and other influenza-related symptom durations in outpatients treated with baloxavir or neuraminidase inhibitors. Respiratory samples were collected before treatment and on days 5 and 10; isolated viruses were analyzed by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing for resistance-associated polymerase acidic protein (PA) and neuraminidase (NA) substitutions. Symptoms were recorded using self-reported diaries.

RESULTS: Of 101 outpatients, 88 (87.1%) had A(H1N1)pdm09 infection, 6 (5.9%) A(H3N2), and 7 (6.9%) B/Victoria. Baloxavir was administered to 70 patients and neuraminidase inhibitors to 31. Pretreatment PA I38V, which does not affect baloxavir susceptibility, was detected in two A(H3N2) viruses; no other targeted PA or NA substitutions were detected. Among patients with A(H1N1)pdm09 infection, day-5 virus isolation was less frequent after baloxavir than after oseltamivir (10.2% [6/59] vs. 40.0% [8/20], p = 0.005). No PA substitutions were detected after baloxavir, whereas NA H275Y was detected after oseltamivir on day 5 (15.0%, 3/20) and day 10 (5.0%, 1/20). Fever and other symptom durations were comparable between baloxavir and oseltamivir, with no significant differences after stratification by age group or day-5 virus isolation status.

CONCLUSIONS: During the A(H1N1)pdm09-dominant 2024-2025 season, baloxavir showed a favorable virological profile, with less frequent day-5 virus isolation than oseltamivir and no detected treatment-emergent PA E23X/I38X substitutions. Influenza-related symptom durations were comparable between baloxavir and oseltamivir.

articles.title: Association of Estimated GFR at the Time of Peritoneal Dialysis Catheter Insertion With Dialysis-Related Complications.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Guidelines recommend waiting for uremia- or volume-related symptoms before initiating dialysis for chronic kidney disease (CKD), irrespective of modality. We speculated that the use of these guidelines may promote greater peritoneal dialysis (PD) related complications following PD catheter placement. This study investigated whether lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) at the time of PD catheter insertion was associated with greater PD-related complications.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients represented in the North American PD catheter registry.

EXPOSURES: EGFR levels at the time of PD catheter insertion categorized as ≤9 ml/min/1.73 m2 or >9 ml/min/1.73 m2.

OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was PD-related complications within 90 days of insertion, and the secondary outcome was the conversion of dialysis modality to hemodialysis.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cause-specific proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 1,537 patients with PD catheter insertions, 67% had a pre-dialysis eGFR ≤ 9 ml/min/1.73 m2 and 33% an eGFR >9 ml/min/1.73 m2. Patients with eGFR ≤9 were younger, more likely to be female, and had fewer comorbidities. The risk of complications in the eGFR ≤9 ml/min/1.73 m2 group was 22% versus 18% in the eGFR >9 ml/min/1.73 m2 group (p-value 0.4). Within the eGFR ≤9 ml/min/1.73 m2 group, when eGFR was modeled as a continuous variable, there was a 10% higher risk of complications for each 1 ml/min lower eGFR (aHR was 1.10; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.19). Starting PD within 30 days of insertion was associated with an increased risk of experiencing complications (aHR 3.15, 95% CI 1.48, 6.67). Common PD-related complications included flow restrictions (7%), leaks (3%), and pain (3%). There was no detectable difference in conversion to hemodialysis between the groups, aHR 0.93 (95% CI 0.60 to 1.45).

LIMITATIONS: eGFR values were not standardized and were not assessed at dialysis initiation. No assessment of pre-dialysis care. Impact of embedded catheters.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter study, the risk of PD-related complications was greater at lower eGFR levels among patients with eGFR <9 ml/min/1.73 m2 at the time of catheter placement. Initiating PD during the first 30 days after catheter insertion was also associated with increased risk. These findings suggest that inserting PD catheters and initiating PD at higher eGFRs may minimize clinical complications during the early period of PD treatment.

articles.title: High-Intensity Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation for Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: A Triple-Blind Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive neuromodulation for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) holds promise, but high-level evidence is lacking, partly due to the challenge of targeting single brain regions in a condition with diverse lesions and multi-network dysfunction.

OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS) on cognitive function in patients with PSCI.

METHODS: In this triple-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, PSCI patients were randomized to receive either active or sham Hi-tACS. The tACS group received active Hi-tACS at 15 mA and 77.5 Hz for 40 minutes, twice daily, 5 days a week for 2 weeks. The sham group used identical devices without current delivery. The primary outcome was the change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included Digit Span Test and cerebral oxyhemoglobin (HbO) concentration changes measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

RESULTS: The tACS group (n=34) showed higher MoCA response rates than the sham group (n=34) immediately after treatment (73.5% vs 38.2%, P=0.003) and at the 4-week post-treatment follow-up (88.2% vs 55.9%, P=0.003). Improvements in forward and backward digit span were also greater in the tACS group at both assessments. The intention-to-treat analysis of all 70 randomized participants yielded results consistent with the per-protocol analysis. Exploratory fNIRS analyses identified greater HbO increases in the left, right, and medial prefrontal regions in the tACS group at T1 after FDR correction (all q=0.033), whereas no regional difference remained significant at T2.

CONCLUSION: Hi-tACS improved global cognition and working memory in patients with PSCI and was generally well tolerated. Exploratory fNIRS findings suggested possible accompanying changes in cortical activation and network organization but did not establish a neurophysiological mechanism. Importantly, as a broad-network stimulation approach, Hi-tACS may reduce reliance on selecting a single precise target, a potential practical advantage in heterogeneous PSCI.

articles.title: Entamoeba invadens infection contributes to juvenile mortality in captive sea turtles.
articles.abstract: Sea turtles are globally threatened marine reptiles, and infectious diseases are increasingly recognized as important causes of juvenile mortality. However, the etiology and pathogenesis of many diseases, including amoebiasis, remain poorly understood. Systemic amoebic lesions have been reported in sea turtles, yet the causative Entamoeba species has never been identified at the species level using molecular methods. We therefore investigated the etiology and pathogenesis of fatal amoebiasis using carcasses of 15 captive juvenile sea turtles (three loggerhead, Caretta caretta, and 12 green turtles, Chelonia mydas), integrating histopathological and molecular approaches. Histopathology revealed severe necrotizing enteritis, hepatitis, and pneumonia with abundant amoebic trophozoites and cysts. Polymerase chain reaction, Sanger sequencing, and in situ hybridization identified Entamoeba invadens in the intestine, liver, and lungs; 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing also detected E. invadens in fecal and intestinal samples. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the sea turtle-derived sequence clustered with E. invadens sequences from other reptile hosts. Bacterial and fungal aggregates were also observed within necrotic lesions, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing detected diverse bacterial communities without a consistently dominant taxon, consistent with secondary microbial translocation following intestinal barrier disruption rather than primary bacterial infection. These findings provide the first evidence that E. invadens causes fatal systemic amoebiasis in juvenile sea turtles and are consistent with polymicrobial invasion following parasite-induced intestinal damage. This study establishes a pathological and molecular basis for diagnosing systemic amoebiasis in sea turtles and has important implications for wildlife disease ecology and sea turtle conservation.

articles.title: A framework to characterize uncertainty for dose extrapolation from in vitro bioassays.
articles.abstract: New approach methods (NAMs) can accelerate chemical assessment and reduce reliance on animal testing, but their application requires quantitative extrapolation of bioactive in vitro concentrations to equivalent in vivo doses. Confidence in quantitative in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (Q-IVIVE) is impacted by uncertainty in both the in vitro concentration and the toxicokinetic parameters used for reverse dosimetry. We propose a framework to: (1) define the processes used to derive an administered equivalent dose (AED); (2) identify uncertainty sources; (3) characterize uncertainty in the data and models; and (4) propagate these uncertainties to the AED. The framework distinguishes nominal assay concentrations from blood- or plasma-equivalent concentrations that account for chemical disposition and compositional differences between in vitro and in vivo media. Parameter-specific uncertainty factors can be derived from experimental variability, model performance statistics, simulations, or expert judgement and combined using a semi-probabilistic approach. Illustrative chemical-space analyses show that nominal and blood-equivalent concentrations may be comparable for some hydrophilic, non-volatile chemicals but can differ by more than two orders of magnitude for hydrophobic or volatile chemicals. The framework provides a systematic, and tiered basis for evaluating confidence in calculated Q-IVIVE doses and supports the application of NAM data in chemical hazard and risk assessment. Ongoing chemical-specific case studies will evaluate implementation of the framework, verify the validity of the simplifying assumptions, and identify opportunities for refinement.

articles.title: Activation of PDZ-Binding Kinase Contributes to Airway Remodeling in Asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway remodeling is an important pathological feature of refractory asthma. PDZ-binding kinase (PBK), as a serine/threonine protein kinase, has been extensively studied in various biological processes. However, the role of PBK in airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs) proliferation and airway remodeling remains unclear. In addition, sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) has been proven to play a key role in the progression of airway remodeling. The present study aims to investigate whether PBK mediates S1P-induced ASMCs proliferation and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

METHODS: Ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthmatic rats and primary cultured ASMCs were employed in the study. Inflammatory factor production, airway resistance assessment, histological staining and immunohistochemical staining were conducted to evaluate the development of asthma. CCK-8 and EdU assays were used for the measurement of cell proliferation. Western blotting and Ubiquitination assay were used to detect protein expressions.

RESULTS: PBK was up-regulated in lungs of OVA-induced chronic asthmatic rats and mediated airway remodeling. Targeting PBK could alleviate airway wall thickness and ASMCs hyperplasia in asthma model. In cultured ASMCs, S1P reduced ubiquitin-mediated degradation of PBK by down-regulating STUB1 leading to PBK protein accumulation. Meanwhile, S1P induced PBK phosphorylation and activation, which further led to the activation of protein regulator of cytokinesis 1 (PRC1) by increasing its expression and phosphorylation, finally promoting ASMCs proliferation.

CONCLUSIONS: Activation of PBK contributes to ASMCs proliferation and airway remodeling in the development of asthma. S1P upregulates PBK expression by suppressing STUB1-mediated proteasome-degradation and elevates PBK activity through increasing its phosphorylation. Activation of PBK further stimulates PRC1 expression and phosphorylation leading to ASMCs proliferation. Targeting PBK might be an effective therapeutic strategy for asthma.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rh2 attenuates post-myocardial infarction heart failure by modulating the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial fibrosis and oxidative stress are key drivers of post-myocardial infarction heart failure (post-MI HF). Ginsenoside Rh2 (GRh2) has shown cardioprotective potential, but its role in post-MI HF and the underlying mechanism remain unclear.

METHODS: Mice with permanent left anterior descending artery ligation were treated with GRh2 (10 mg/kg/day, gavage) or enalapril for 28 days, cardiac function (echocardiography), fibrosis (histology/immunohistochemistry) and cardiac injury markers were assessed. Cardiac transcriptomes were sequenced to identify enriched pathways. H9C2 cardiomyoblasts and human iPSC-derived cardiac organoids were subjected to oxygen glucose deprivation (OGD) and treated with GRh2 with or without the TGF-β receptor agonist SRI-011381 (SRI), viability, oxidative stress, apoptosis, fibrosis and TGF-β/Smad2 signalling were measured.

RESULTS: In vivo, GRh2 treatment markedly improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial fibrosis in mice with post-MI heart failure. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the TGF-β signaling pathway was substantially enriched. In vitro, GRh2 treatment significantly improved cell viability and reduced oxidative stress and fibrosis in OGD-exposed H9C2 cardiomyocytes and cardiac organoids. These protective effects were strongly associated with the suppression of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway.

CONCLUSIONS: GRh2 can improve myocardial function and alleviate fibrosis, oxidative stress and cell apoptosis after MI. In cells and organoids, these protective effects depend on the inhibition of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway, suggesting that this pathway is a potential mediator of the cardiac protective effect of GRh2.

articles.title: Volumetric absorptive microsampling for steroid monitoring in congenital adrenal hyperplasia: Can capillary blood measurements reliably be converted to plasma concentrations?
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Steroid hormone monitoring is essential in endocrine conditions such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), but conventional venous sampling is invasive and often impractical, particularly in children. Capillary microsampling using volumetric absorptive microsampling (VAMS) offers a minimally invasive alternative, suitable for home sampling. However, before embarking on application in patients, it is important to set up a clinical validation study to assess whether -and how- blood (VAMS-based) steroid hormone concentrations can be converted to concentrations in the reference matrix, plasma. Previously described, validated LC-MS/MS methods were used to determine the concentrations of androstenedione (4-AD), 17α-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) and 11-ketotestosterone (11-KT) in paired venous (liquid and dried) and capillary samples collected from 43 healthy adults and 41 children with diabetes. Steroid concentrations were compared across matrices, and capillary VAMS results were converted to plasma values using the hematocrit (hct), derived from dried blood. No methodological differences were observed between dried and liquid (venous VAMS vs. whole blood) samples (>82% within ±20%). Capillary (cVAMS) vs. venous VAMS (vVAMS) samples showed good agreement for 4-AD and 17-OHP but higher variability, particularly for 11-KT. Converting cVAMS values to plasma concentrations using the hct resulted in clinically acceptable agreement with actually measured plasma concentrations for 4-AD, 17-OHP and 11-KT (with 87%, 94% and 72% of the differences within the clinical acceptance limits). While for 11-KT, unexplained differences between the two study populations were apparent, a proof-of-concept application in 5 CAH patients showed good agreement for all analytes. Our results suggest that fingerprick VAMS can be explored as an alternative strategy to conventional plasma collection for monitoring 4-AD, 17-OHP and 11-KT in CAH patients. Nevertheless, assessment of the clinical validity in a larger CAH patient cohort is warranted to confirm the applicability of VAMS as a tool for decentralized steroid monitoring in these patients.

articles.title: sST2 augments the prognostic value of risk stratification in patients with connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2018 World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH) introduced a risk stratification tool for assessing the severity of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), aiding treatment decisions. However, risk stratification in connective tissue disease-associated PAH (CTD-PAH) patients often faces challenges, particularly in distinguishing intermediate-risk patients.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) as an addition to risk stratification in patients with CTD-PAH.

METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 84 CTD-PAH patients diagnosed by right heart catheterization. Baseline risk was stratified using the 2018 WSPH risk model, and clinical data were collected through chart reviews. The primary endpoint was clinical worsening. Statistical analyses included t-tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, chi-square tests, Fisher's exact tests, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox regression models, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis.

RESULTS: (1) No significant difference in event-free survival was observed between patients classified as low or intermediate risk using the 2018 WSPH risk model. (2) An sST2 concentration ≥ 35 ng/mL was associated with an increased risk of clinical worsening in low- and intermediate-risk patients. (3) Patients with sST2 levels that maintained or elevated above 35 ng/mL over one year exhibited significantly lower event-free survival rates compared to those with decreased levels.

CONCLUSION: sST2 adds prognostic value to risk stratification in CTD-PAH patients, particularly for those in the low- and intermediate-risk group. Monitoring changes in sST2 levels over time may offer additional insights into patient prognosis, though these findings are suggestive and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Integrated Exosomal miRNA and metabolomics model for predicting sarcopenia in patients with malignant tumors.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a common, underdiagnosed complication in malignant tumor (MT) patients, leading to poor treatment tolerance and shortened survival. This study aims to construct and validate a comprehensive prediction model by integrating exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) and metabolomics biomarkers.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 236 MT patients (February 2020-December 2023) was analyzed. Independent risk factors (IRFs) were identified via logistic regression to establish Model 1. Exosomal miRNAs (qRT-PCR) developed Model 2, while differential serum metabolites (LC-MS/MS) built Model 3. Model 4 integrated Models 2 and 3. Performance was assessed using ROC and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Sarcopenia incidence was 59.32% (140/236). Multivariate analysis identified BMI, diabetes status, and NRS2002 score as IRFs (p < 0.05). Exosomal profiling showed significantly elevated miR 15, miR 21, and miR 223, and downregulated miR 27a, miR 29b, and miR 33a (p < 0.05). Metabolomics identified 10 upregulated and 4 downregulated metabolites (p < 0.05). Model 4 demonstrated the highest accuracy, with AUC 0.992 (95% CI: 0.971-0.999), sensitivity 94.96%, and specificity 97.91%, outperforming other models. DCA confirmed Model 4 provided the greatest standardized net clinical benefit.

CONCLUSION: An integrated model combining exosomal miRNA and metabolomic biomarkers offers excellent predictive performance for sarcopenia in MT patients, facilitating early identification and precision care.

articles.title: Bacillus BS08 and BA08 isolated from the grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) intestine improve growth performance and enhance resistance to GCRV-II infection in grass carp.
articles.abstract: Probiotics provide multiple benefits, including promoting digestion, activating the immune system, and exerting antiviral effects. Grass carp reovirus (GCRV) infection has caused serious economic losses in grass carp aquaculture, highlighting the urgent need for effective prevention and control strategies. In our study, 31 Bacillus including 23 Bacillus subtilis (BS) and 8 Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (BA), and 52 Lactococcus lactis (LL) were isolated from the intestine of grass carp. Hemolysis assay showed that all the 83 strains were non-hemolytic. Antibiotic susceptibility assay using 22 common antibiotics showed that 29 Bacillus and 29 Lactococcus lactis were resistant to fewer than four antibiotics. All 29 Bacillus could produce cellulase, protease, and amylase. Acid-producing assay showed that 10 randomly selected Lactococcus lactis exhibited acid-producing capacity. Four strains, BS08, BA08, LL01, and LL06, were selected for evaluation of their in vitro anti-GCRV activity. Metabolites derived from these strains significantly inhibited GCRV-II replication in grass carp snout fibroblast (PSF) cells. Furthermore, grass carp diets were supplemented with BS08, BA08, LL01, and LL06 for 30 days. Dietary supplementation with all four strains significantly promoted growth performance and upregulated the expression of immune-related genes, including IL-8, IL-1β, and TNF-α. Notably, BS08 and BA08 exhibited higher final survival rates following GCRV-II infection, with relative percent survival (RPS) values of 50% and 58.33%, respectively. Overall, dietary supplementation with BS08 and BA08 significantly improved growth performance and reduced GCRV-II viral loads, while showing a trend toward improved survival following GCRV-II infection in grass carp, suggesting their potential as functional feed additives.

articles.title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR.

RESULTS: BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice.

CONCLUSION: BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

articles.title: Intestinal Candida albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance via IL-17A and Trem2+ macrophages.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Whether intestinal fungal dysbiosis contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. We investigated how gut Candida albicans influences HCC progression, immune remodeling, and response to ICI therapy.

METHODS: Fecal and tumor samples from patients with HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls were analyzed using ITS2 sequencing, immune profiling, and correlation analyses. Mechanistic studies focused on four complementary autochthonous murine HCC models and cell-based assays, integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, genetic and pharmacologic perturbations, Kaede photoconversion, fungal antigen recall assays, antifungal treatment, and anti-PD-1 therapy.

RESULTS: Fecal C. albicans abundance was higher in HCC patients and was associated with advanced disease, shorter overall survival, and reduced durable clinical benefit. Across HCC models, C. albicans gavage increased tumor burden and induced a Th17/IL-17A-skewed microenvironment characterized by Trem2+ macrophage accumulation and impaired CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Antifungal treatment attenuated tumor progression, whereas IL-17A blockade or deficiency largely abrogated C. albicans-associated tumor promotion. Mechanistically, IL-17A induced tumor-derived MCP-1 through ACT1-TRAF6-TAK1 signaling to recruit macrophages and upregulated PAI-1, which activated TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to promote an immunosuppressive Trem2+ macrophage state. These macrophages limited CD8+ T cell recruitment and effector function through coordinated CXCL10 repression and GAL-1 induction, while potentially reinforcing Th17 responses through IL-1β and IL-6. Kaede photoconversion demonstrated enhanced mesenteric lymph node-to-liver Th17 trafficking, while fungal antigen recall assays revealed preferential Th17 responsiveness to C. albicans. C. albicans also impaired anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo, whereas antifungal treatment partially restored therapeutic responsiveness.

CONCLUSIONS: Intestinal C. albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance through an IL-17A-Trem2+ macrophage circuit, supporting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Intestinal fungal dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a component of the gut-liver axis, but its functional contribution to HCC has remained poorly defined. Our study identifies intestinal Candida albicans as a promoter of HCC progression in experimental models and delineates an IL-17A-MCP-1/PAI-1-Trem2+ macrophage circuit that links fungal exposure to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity and reduced response to PD-1 blockade. These findings are relevant to researchers and clinicians seeking microbiome-associated determinants of HCC progression and immunotherapy resistance. Fecal C. albicans abundance and components of this immune circuit may warrant evaluation as biomarkers for patient stratification and as potential targets for combination therapy. However, the clinical associations reported here are based on modest observational cohorts, and antifungal treatment was tested as a proof-of-concept intervention in mice. Larger prospective studies and more selective therapeutic approaches will therefore be required before these findings can inform clinical management.

articles.title: HbA1c trajectories and the risk of liver-related events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus - Reply to Correa et al.
A Novel Zonal Classification and Risk-Adapted 3P Strategy for Microsurgical Management of Jugular Foramen Tumors: Anatomical Study and a Comparative Clinical Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Jugular foramen (JF) tumors remain surgically challenging owing to proximity to lower cranial nerves and vessels. We introduce a pathology-agnostic JF-Zonal classification based on a triangular pyramid defined by four bony landmarks that converts imaging-defined extension into modular corridors, integrated with a risk-adapted "3P" strategy (precision planning, preoperative rehearsal, personalized performance).

METHODS: We conducted an anatomical study and a retrospective clinical comparison. Eight cadaveric heads (16 sides) were dissected; two blinded raters tested inter-rater reliability. Thirty-two JF tumor patients treated with the classification and 3P protocol (2020-2025) were compared with 39 historical controls (2012-2019).

RESULTS: Zone assignment agreement was substantial (quadratic-weighted kappa, 0.78; unweighted, 0.52); complexity grade agreement was almost perfect (0.82). Tumors were classified as Zone 0 (25%), Zone II (16%), and Zone III (59%), with no Zone I cases. Gross total resection (GTR) was achieved in 69% and GTR or near-total resection (NTR) in 94%, versus 59% (P = .001). New permanent cranial nerve deficits occurred in 13% versus 36% (P = .030). Multivariable analyses supported an independent association of the 3P protocol with higher resection extent and lower cranial nerve morbidity. Follow-up Karnofsky Performance Scale score was higher (90 vs 85, P = .039).

CONCLUSIONS: The JF-Zonal classification translates tumor extension into corridor combinations; with the 3P protocol, it was associated with improved resection extent and reduced cranial nerve morbidity. The historical-control design precludes causal inference; findings are hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is required.

articles.title: Developing Consensus on the Diagnosis and Management of Cauda Equina Syndrome: A Modified Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cauda equina syndrome (CES) necessitates urgent intervention to prevent permanent neurological damage. Current literature calls for decompression within 48 hours of symptom onset. Great heterogeneity exists in criteria informing surgical decision-making. Unified consensus statements may provide clarity in these topics.

METHODS: We performed a modified Delphi study to investigate CES diagnosis and management. A 30-question survey was distributed to 18 spine surgeons, addressing diagnosis, sensorimotor/bladder/bowel findings, and surgical decision-making. Consensus was ≥ 80% agreement (agree/strongly agree) or ≤ 20% agreement (consensus to opposite statement) on a 4-point Likert scale. Teleconferences and final survey followed to clarify contentious statements.

RESULTS: 18 responses were received (15 neurosurgeons, 3 orthopedic surgeons). 17 statements achieved final consensus, pertaining to diagnosis (4), sensorimotor findings (4), bowel/bladder function (1), and surgical management (8). In our practice, 100% consensus was achieved for sensorimotor findings in CES comprising a constellation of symptoms, including pain and/or paresthesia and/or lower extremity motor weakness, and for time to decompression to be informed by duration and severity of symptoms. 94% consensus was achieved on one of the following symptoms required to diagnose CES: lower extremity motor dysfunction, bowel/bladder dysfunction, or saddle anesthesia, in addition to confirmatory MRI.

CONCLUSION: We present institutional consensus on key factors in CES symptom identification and operative management. Our local findings highlight the importance of recognizing the heterogeneous presentation of CES and the utility of combining symptom acuity with clinical context for operative planning. We hope they spur further discussion in CES management on a national scale.

articles.title: Telmisartan attenuates gentamicin-induced ototoxicity and modulates oxidative stress and RhoA/ROCK-associated signaling in mice.
articles.abstract: Gentamicin-induced ototoxicity involves oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cochlear hair-cell injury. This study evaluated the protective effects of telmisartan and their association with RhoA/ROCK signaling in mice. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to normal control, gentamicin control, gentamicin plus fasudil (2 mg/kg), or gentamicin plus telmisartan (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg) groups (n = 10). Auditory function was assessed by auditory brainstem response, while locomotor and gait performance were evaluated using open-field and gait tests. Cochlear oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, RhoA activation, ROCK1/2 mRNA expression, and ROCK-associated protein phosphorylation were assessed using colorimetric assays, ELISA, fluorescence imaging, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting. Hair-cell integrity was evaluated by MYO7A immunofluorescence, quantitative counting, and histopathology. Gentamicin elevated auditory thresholds, prolonged shock-avoidance response latencies, impaired locomotor and gait performance, increased intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and reduced antioxidant defenses. It also increased iNOS, NF-κB, active RhoA, ROCK1/2 expression, and phosphorylation of ROCK-associated proteins while reducing MYO7A-positive hair-cell density. Fasudil and telmisartan attenuated these alterations, with higher telmisartan doses generally providing greater protection, although responses were not uniformly dose-dependent. Telmisartan also preserved sensory epithelial organization and cochlear hair-cell density. Telmisartan attenuated gentamicin-associated auditory and cochlear injury, with effects associated with reduced oxidative and inflammatory stress and modulation of RhoA/ROCK-related signaling. Further pathway-specific and clinically relevant studies are required.

articles.title: Subacute administration of human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells is associated with neurobehavioral improvement, myeloid immune modulation, and altered HMGB1 dynamics after experimental ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Cell therapy using human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hUCMSCs) is attracting attention as a promising treatment strategy for ischemic stroke. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and associated biological changes following hUCMSC administration during the subacute phase using a mouse model of permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Based on our previous findings showing an increase in CD163-positive brain immune cells after hUCMSC administration, we hypothesized that subacute hUCMSC treatment would be associated with changes in myeloid immune responses and high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) dynamics. hUCMSCs were administered intravenously two weeks after MCAO induction. Ischemic brain and systemic immune responses were evaluated at the 3rd, 4th, and 5th weeks post-MCAO using flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL), Evans Blue assay, Western blotting, and ELISA. Neurobehavioral outcomes were also assessed during the subacute and chronic phases after MCAO. Subacute hUCMSC administration was associated with improved neurobehavioral outcomes after ischemic stroke. Brain immune-cell analyses showed treatment-associated changes in CD163/CD204 co-expression and intracellular HMGB1 accumulation, while peripheral myeloid populations also exhibited changes in CD163 expression within Ly6C subsets. These findings indicate that neurobehavioral improvement following hUCMSC administration was accompanied by local and systemic myeloid immune changes and altered intracellular HMGB1 dynamics.

articles.title: Comparison of Meropenem-based triple therapy vs Minocycline-based Triple therapy for Carbapenem Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Ventilator Associated Pneumonia - A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) resulted from Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) poses serious treatment challenges. Our objective was to assess two triple medication combinations for VAP caused by CRAB.

METHODS: This prospective observational research was performed in the critical care unit of an academic medical center from January 2024 to March 2025. Two hundred adult patients with culture-proven CRAB-VAP were enrolled and treated with either minocycline-polymyxin-sulbactam or meropenem-polymyxin-sulbactam. Various outcomes assessed were clinical recovery, 7 and 28-day mortality, microbiological eradication, duration of ICU and hospital stay.

RESULTS: The clinical recovery rates were comparable in both groups (54% minocycline vs. 47% meropenem, p=0.322). The microbiological eradication rate was similar (39 % ) at day 28 in both groups. Patients treated with the minocycline regimen had significantly shorter ICU stay (16 vs. 18 days, p=0.003) and hospital stays (24 vs. 28 days, p<0.001) than the meropenem group. There was no significant difference between 7-day mortality (21% vs. 32%, p=0.078) or 28-day mortality (46% vs. 53%, p=0.322).

CONCLUSION: Minocycline-based triple therapy was comparable to meropenem-based therapy in treating CRAB-VAP, with potential advantages in reducing duration of ICU and hospital stay. Minocycline may be a suitable alternative for CRAB-VAP in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Risk of Adverse Kidney Outcomes in Families with MASLD: A Population-Based Multigenerational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but whether the CKD excess risk extends to MASLD family members is unknown.

METHODS: Nationwide multigenerational cohort study involving family members of all Swedish adults with biopsy-proven MASLD (1969-2017) and matched general population comparators. In total, 37,250 MASLD first-degree relatives (FDRs: parents, siblings, offspring) and 9,159 MASLD spouses, as well as 194,327 comparator FDRs and 46,582 comparator spouses were followed until 2021. The primary endpoint was a composite of chronic kidney disease (CKD) diagnosis, kidney failure with replacement therapy (KFRT), or death from CKD. Cox regression was used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs).

RESULTS: Over a median of 18.8 years, the incidence rate of the composite adverse kidney outcome was higher in MASLD FDRs vs. comparator FDRs (137 vs. 123/100,000 person years (PYs); aHR=1.11, 95%CI=1.01-1.21). Risk estimates for each single component were increased but did not attain statistical significance: CKD (aHR=1.10, 95%CI=0.99-1.21), KFRT (aHR=1.17, 95%CI=0.96-1.41), and death from CKD (aHR=1.25, 95%CI=0.68-2.30). Risks were most pronounced among siblings (aHR=1.21, 95%CI=1.03-1.42). MASLD spouses also had an increased risk of the primary endpoint (25 vs. 20/100,000PY; aHR=1.12, 95%CI=0.97-1.30).

CONCLUSIONS: First degree relatives of individuals with biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease have a slightly higher risk of adverse kidney outcomes, but absolute risks are low and do not motivate systematic screening. A similar risk increase in spouses, albeit statistically non-significant, may be compatible with a contribution of shared lifestyle and metabolic factors, although genetic and environmental influences cannot be definitely disentangled.

articles.title: Sleep and Sedentary Behavior Predict Severity in MASLD but Not MetALD/ALD: A Compositional Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Daily movement behaviors are typically analyzed in isolation, ignoring their inherent competition for time within the 24-hour day. We examined whether the 24-hour composition of sleep, sedentary time, and physical activity was associated with liver stiffness in adults with steatotic liver disease (SLD) METHOD: This cross-sectional analysis used NHANES 2017-2018 data from 1,080 adults with SLD (889 MASLD, 101MetALD, and 90 ALD). Sleep, sedentary time, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and other waking activity were modelled using isometric log-ratio coordinates in survey-weighted regression with log-transformed liver stiffness measurement (LSM). Isotemporal substitution analyses estimated LSM changes from reallocating 30 minutes between behaviors.

RESULTS: In MASLD, a greater sedentary time relative to active behaviors was associated with 5.79% higher LSM (95% CI 1.14-10.66%; p=0.027) after sociodemographic adjustment, attenuating after cardiometabolic adjustment (3.73%; p=0.086). Greater sleep relative to all other behaviors was independently associated with 15.55% lower LSM (95% CI -27.33% to -1.86%; p=0.044), persisting after full adjustment (-14.38%, 95% CI -25.58% to -1.49%; p=0.047). Replacing 30 minutes of sedentary time with sleep was associated with a larger LSM reduction (-1.69%, 95% CI -2.98% to -0.39%; p=0.011) than replacement with MVPA (-0.83%, 95% CI -1.32% to -0.33%; p=0.001). Among former drinkers, sedentary-to-sleep reallocation was associated with 2.24% lower LSM (95% CI -3.78% to -0.67%; p=0.005); among low drinkers, sedentary-to-MVPA reallocation was associated with 1.32% lower LSM (95% CI -2.19% to -0.44%; p=0.004). No substitution was significant in MetALD or ALD.

CONCLUSIONS: The 24-hour self-reported movement behavior composition is associated with liver stiffness in MASLD, with sedentary and sleep balance showing associations in opposite directions. This supports a personalized, whole-day approach to behavioral counseling in MASLD management.

articles.title: Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up.

RESULTS: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline.

INTERPRETATION: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

articles.title: The Syndrome of Inappropriate Mineralocorticoid Receptor Activation includes Hypertension.
