Molecular epidemiology of dengue virus in the Bangka Belitung Islands, Indonesia, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) infection poses a major global health challenge with a rising number of infections worldwide. In Indonesia, molecular epidemiological studies have been limited, focusing primarily on Java Island, which has led to a sufficiency in comprehensive data of DENV characteristics. During the COVID-19 pandemic, fewer DENV epidemiological studies were conducted, further leaving a gap in our understanding of viral circulation during this period. Characterization of DENV serotypes, genotypes, and nucleotide substitutions is essential for improving clinical management and informing vaccine strategies. This study employed a cross-sectional design with consecutive sampling of suspected dengue patients from a private clinic and hospital in Bangka-Belitung, Indonesia, between 2019 and 2023. Patients with fever and two or more clinical symptoms of DENV infection were included. DENV infection was confirmed by NS1 antigen test, and positive samples were further analyzed for DENV serotypes by RT-PCR, followed by envelope gene analysis for phylogenetic characterization. Out of 92 suspected dengue infections, 74 cases (80.43%) were confirmed for DENV infection via RT-PCR, NS-1, or IgM antibody tests, with the majority of confirmed dengue cases occurred in children. DENV-3 was found to be the most dominant serotype (38.71%), followed by DENV-1 (11.83%), which aligns with previous studies characterizing the serotypes of circulating DENV strains. Phylogenetic analysis of DENV (1-4) during the COVID-19 pandemic revealed that these strains clustered into a distinct groups under the same genotypes as earlier outbreaks. This molecular epidemiology and seroprevalence data provide valuable insight into the circulating DENV strains in Indonesia. AUTHOR SUMMARY: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, one of the countries with the highest dengue burden worldwide. Although DENV is endemic throughout the Indonesian archipelago, information on the genetic diversity and circulation of DENV is still limited in many regions outside Java Island. Bangka Belitung Province is an understudied area where molecular epidemiological data are largely unavailable, making it difficult to understand local transmission patterns and support evidence-based control strategies. In this study, we investigated DENV infections in Bangka Belitung before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. We analyzed clinical samples from patients with suspected DENV infection to determine circulating serotypes and genetic characteristics of the virus. All four DENV serotypes were detected, with DENV-3 identified as the predominant serotype throughout the study period. Phylogenetic analyses showed that the circulating viruses belonged to genotypes that have been reported previously in Indonesia, indicating ongoing endemic transmission and genetic diversity within the country. Our findings provide the first comprehensive molecular epidemiological data on DENV circulation in Bangka Belitung. These results contribute to a better understanding of dengue transmission dynamics in Indonesia and highlight the importance of continuous molecular surveillance to detect viral introductions, monitor genetic changes, and support DENV prevention and control programs.

articles.title: The Myocardial Footprint and the Coronary Culprit: What Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Can and Cannot Establish in MINOCA.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis in which cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) defines the myocardial phenotype, separates ischemic injury from nonischemic mimics, and quantifies the burden of injury, yet usually cannot establish the coronary mechanism that produced it. Paired studies of CMR and intracoronary imaging show that the myocardial footprint and the coronary culprit often fail to correspond, because each test observes a different biological target within its own window of visibility, and a negative result cannot exclude transient or functional mechanisms such as spasm, embolism, or microvascular dysfunction. We synthesize evidence on imaging timing, quantitative tissue characterization, stress perfusion, multimodality reclassification, prognosis, and mechanism-guided treatment, and indicate the type of evidence supporting key claims. On this basis, we propose a conceptual framework, not an evidence-based guideline, that expresses mechanistic confidence in graded terms, places that judgment within an integrated heart-team report, and reserves further testing for questions likely to change diagnosis, treatment, or follow-up.

articles.title: Quinoclamine, a repurposed agricultural algicide, functions as a multi-target quorum sensing inhibitor to attenuate Pseudomonas aeruginosa virulence and potentiate antibiotic efficacy.
articles.abstract: The widespread overuse and misuse of antibiotics have precipitated a global antimicrobial resistance crisis, compounded by a dwindling pipeline of novel antibiotic discovery. As the quorum sensing (QS) system tightly mediates bacterial colonization and pathogenicity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, QS-targeted anti-virulence therapy has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics. In this study, through an integrated approach combining virtual screening and systematic experimental validation, we identified quinoclamine as a candidate QS inhibitor and comprehensively characterized its anti-virulence efficacy via in silico, in vitro, and in vivo assays. Molecular docking analysis predicted that quinoclamine simultaneously interacts with three core QS regulators: LasR, RhlR, and PqsR. In vitro experiments demonstrated that quinoclamine significantly inhibited key QS-controlled virulence factors including pyocyanin and extracellular proteases, as well as biofilm formation and bacterial motility, without affecting bacterial growth. Quantitative real-time PCR confirmed that quinoclamine downregulated QS-associated virulence genes and competitively blocked autoinducer-receptor binding. Furthermore, quinoclamine exhibited synergistic bactericidal activity with five clinical anti-pseudomonal antibiotics. Additionally, quinoclamine has moderate disruptive capacity against pre-formed mature biofilms, and partially potentiates the bactericidal efficacy of ciprofloxacin against sessile bacteria embedded within biofilms. The in vivo protective efficacy was validated across three infection models: C. elegans fast-killing, C. elegans slow-killing, and mouse acute pulmonary infection. Impressively, the combination of quinoclamine and 1/2 × MIC ciprofloxacin further improved host survival in all three models and reduced bacterial burden in mouse lung lesions. Collectively, these findings characterize quinoclamine as a promising QS inhibitor with broad anti-virulence activity, and provide robust experimental support for the development of QS-targeted anti-virulence therapies against P. aeruginosa infections.

articles.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps in Ischemic Stroke: Thrombolysis Resistance, No-Reflow, and Hemorrhagic Transformation.
articles.abstract: Recanalization is central to acute ischemic stroke treatment. However, reopening an occluded artery does not always restore microvascular perfusion, and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) can occur regardless of recanalization success. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) may help explain these discordant outcomes because they act within occlusive thrombi, the downstream microcirculation, and the neurovascular interface. This review examines the roles of NETs in thrombolysis resistance, no-reflow, and hemorrhagic injury. Within thrombi, NET-associated chromatin reinforces clot architecture and limits fibrinolysis. Intravascular NETs may impede downstream microvascular flow after recanalization, while NET-related inflammatory signaling may aggravate blood-brain barrier disruption and HT. These findings implicate NETs in impaired recanalization, incomplete tissue reperfusion, and hemorrhagic injury and support their evaluation as an adjunctive target during reperfusion therapy.

articles.title: Nanoparticles for cardiovascular diseases: identifying and overcoming barriers in translating preclinical success to clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as versatile platforms for drug delivery in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models by stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques, promoting safe and efficient thrombolysis, and mitigating ischemia-reperfusion injury. These advances highlight the maturation of cardiovascular nanomedicine; however, translation to clinical practice remains limited. This gap between laboratory success and clinical adoption reflects broader challenges in nanomedicine design, including suboptimal delivery to diseased tissues, limited efficacy of single therapeutic payload-based strategies in addressing the multifaceted inflammatory pathways driving CVDs, NPs' immunogenicity, and scale-up feasibility. Addressing these barriers is particularly critical in CVDs, where therapeutic success depends on precise engagement with multiple molecular and cellular drivers of disease. This review discusses the evolving landscape of cardiovascular nanomedicine, focusing on four aspects. First, we highlight advances in NPs bioengineering strategies, such as refined targeting moieties, optimized physicochemical properties, and responsiveness to endogenous and external stimuli that enhance organ- and cell-specific delivery in atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Second, we discuss analytical innovations that improve characterization and control of NPs' biodistribution, enabling more rational targeting. Third, we evaluate therapeutic payloads, emphasizing how RNA-based and immunomodulatory agents represent a meaningful step toward clinical translation. Fourth, we outline approaches to addressing persistent challenges in safety and scalable manufacturing. Together, these developments establish a foundation for translating NP design principles into practical cardiovascular therapies. With continued progress in targeted delivery, clinical safety, and production scalability, cardiovascular nanomedicine is increasingly well-positioned to translate preclinical advances to transformative patient outcomes.

articles.title: JTH in Clinic: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis of Pediatric Patients at Risk of VTE.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract: As the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases in hospitalized children, there is an urgent need to improve VTE prevention strategies in this population. Implementation of thromboprophylaxis, which includes mechanical and pharmacological interventions, varies in practice due to limited pediatric-specific data and, until recently, a lack of evidence-based guidelines. However, recent randomized clinical trials and well-designed multicenter observational studies have provided improved evidence on the safety and efficacy of anticoagulants for VTE prevention in specific pediatric subpopulations supporting the development of risk assessment models to help identify subgroups of children at high risk for VTE. Based on these data, the American Society of Hematology and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis recently developed the first evidence-based guideline for anticoagulant prophylaxis in children at risk of VTE. While this guideline is an exciting step towards preventing VTE-associated harm, VTE prevention remains complex due to unique pediatric risk factors and changing physiology with age, resulting in heterogeneous VTE and bleeding risk profiles. In this case-based review, we apply the new guideline and supporting evidence to guide decisions regarding the use of thromboprophylaxis in pediatric cases commonly encountered in clinical practice, highlighting the nuances of VTE prevention in critically ill children. We review the complex decision-making process required prior to initiation of pharmacologic prophylaxis, including assessment of VTE risk, bleeding risk, and shared decision-making with families. Additionally, we highlight the importance of multidisciplinary teams in VTE prevention and anticoagulant stewardship, as well as the similarities and differences in pediatric versus adult practice.

articles.title: Differential Modulation of PPAR-γ and Aromatase by Pharmacotherapeutics in Danio rerio Ovaries: Mechanistic insights for PCOS Therapy.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a multifaceted reproductive endocrinopathy characterized by oligo/anovulation, cystic ovaries, and disrupted steroidogenesis. Inhibition of aromatase during steroidogenesis may be linked to dysregulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ), which could lead to aberrant estradiol synthesis and contribute to PCOS pathophysiology. Therefore, we speculate that activation of PPAR-γ with propionic acid may, in part, help restore normal steroidogenesis. However, the expression levels of aromatase and PPAR-γ were not clearly understood with the currently used drugs (for PCOS) and propionic acid. Therefore, this study investigated ovarian expression of PPAR-γ and aromatase in zebrafish (Danio rerio) treated with various drugs (metformin, letrozole, clomiphene citrate, and the novel molecule, propionic acid) under normal conditions. Fifty female zebrafish were divided into five groups and treated with DMSO (control), metformin, letrozole, clomiphene citrate, and propionic acid for 14 days, followed by analysis of aromatase and PPAR-γ expression using RT-qPCR. Metformin treatment downregulated aromatase expression and upregulated PPAR-γ, whereas letrozole-mediated regulation of aromatase and PPAR-γ was reversed. Clomiphene citrate treatment upregulated both PPAR-γ and aromatase. Notably, propionic acid also upregulated both PPAR-γ and aromatase, suggesting a potential role as an ovarian microenvironment modulator. Further, molecular docking analysis of all compounds with PPAR-γ and aromatase revealed differential binding affinities, with metformin and propionic acid forming more hydrogen bonds than letrozole and clomiphene citrate. Collectively, these findings suggest that propionic acid may modulate ovarian steroidogenesis by regulating aromatase and PPAR-γ.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index as a marker of association of diabetic foot ulceration in patients on chronic haemodialysis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Diabetic patients on haemodialysis (HD) are vulnerable to protein-energy wasting (PEW) and severe microvascular complications. Although the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) is widely used to assess nutritional status in chronic kidney disease (CKD), its value as a comprehensive marker for clinical deterioration and disease progression of diabetic foot (DF) within this cohort remains largely unexplored. Here, we evaluate baseline nutritional status via the GNRI and determine its prospective association with adverse clinical trajectories, localised complications, and secondary morbidities in diabetic patients on chronic HD.

METHODS: This retrospective, longitudinal cohort study focused on 53 adult patients with diabetes mellitus in a chronic HD program between May 2017 and November 2024. Nutritional status was evaluated using the GNRI equation adapted to HD, using a cut-off point of ≤91.2 to identify malnutrition or high nutritional risk. Clinical history, biochemical parameters, longitudinal nutritional evolution, and DF-related events (hospitalisations and amputations) were recorded over a 12-month follow-up period, whereas all-cause mortality was tracked throughout the entire study observation period (up to 6 years). Multivariate binary logistic regression, multiple linear regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival models were applied.

RESULTS: The prevalence of DF was 41.5% (n = 22). Patients with DF presented significantly lower baseline GNRI values compared with individuals without DF (90.49 ± 7.49 vs. 96.06 ± 5.54; p = 0.003). Multivariate binary logistic regression revealed that baseline GNRI was independently and inversely associated with the presence of DF (OR = 0.803; 95% CI: 0.682-0.946; p = 0.009), indicating a 19.7% reduction in the probability of presenting DF for each one-unit increase in the GNRI. Lower GNRI values correlated significantly with a larger number of hospital admissions (ρ = -0.468; p < 0.001) and a higher frequency of minor distal amputations (ρ = -0.284; p = 0.039). Furthermore, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with baseline malnutrition had significantly lower survival over time compared with well-nourished individuals (Log-Rank p < 0.001). According to multiple linear regression, body mass index (p = 0.041), haemoglobin (p = 0.036), and serum creatinine (p = 0.004) were independently and positively associated with the GNRI.

CONCLUSIONS: Malnutrition evaluated by the GNRI is highly prevalent and independently associated with an adverse clinical trajectory in diabetic patients on chronic HD. The GNRI serves as a robust marker of severe secondary outcomes, significantly correlating with higher hospitalisation rates, minor distal amputations, and overall mortality. Ultimately, the GNRI constitutes a simple, reproducible, and comprehensive tool for nutritional risk stratification and the optimisation of multi-disciplinary preventive strategies in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in predicting a low TAPSE/sPAP ratio in hemodialysis patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling is a major determinant of cardiovascular outcomes in hemodialysis patients, yet simple and accessible biomarkers capable of identifying early RV-PA impairment remain limited. The Systemic Inflammation Response Index (SIRI) has recently emerged as a promising inflammatory marker, but its relationship with RV-PA coupling has not been previously explored. This study aimed to evaluate the association between SIRI and the TAPSE/sPAP ratio in hemodialysis patients.

METHODS: A total of 111 patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis were enrolled. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed after the midweek dialysis session to assess TAPSE and sPAP. Patients were categorized into two groups according to the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (<0.55 vs. ≥0.55). Laboratory parameters, including SIRI and SII, were recorded. Group comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and ROC analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Patients with a TAPSE/sPAP ratio <0.55 exhibited significantly higher sPAP and lower TAPSE values, indicating impaired RV-PA coupling. SIRI levels were also significantly elevated in this group (median 1.50 vs. 1.15). Although SIRI did not remain an independent predictor in multivariable analysis, it demonstrated a modest discriminatory ability in ROC analysis (AUC 0.630), with an optimal cut-off value of 1.50.

CONCLUSION: Elevated SIRI levels are associated with increased pulmonary artery pressure, reduced right ventricular systolic function, and a lower TAPSE/sPAP ratio in hemodialysis patients. As a low-cost and easily obtainable biomarker derived from routine laboratory tests, SIRI may provide supportive information regarding RV-PA coupling impairment. Larger prospective studies are warranted to clarify its clinical utility.

articles.title: Update of a Living Network Meta-Analysis Comparing Non-compounded Polidocanol 1% Endovenous Microfoam (Varithena) Ablation versus Endovenous Thermal Ablation in Chronic Venous Insufficiency.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when polidocanol endovenous microfoam was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence.

METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference.

RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). Polidocanol endovenous microfoam was not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.42 to 1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean 28 months, range 12-72 months) showed similar results (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.45 to 1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with polidocanol endovenous microfoam versus endovenous thermal ablation (odds ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.29 to 2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific quality of life or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation (standardized mean difference [Hedges' g] 0.04, 95% confidence interval -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference.

CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam is not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation and endovenous thermal ablation for a composite of disease-specific quality of life and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

articles.title: Key determinants of overnight hospital stay after total hip arthroplasty.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de cirugia ortopedica y traumatologia
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is a highly effective procedure, with demand projected to increase significantly due to population ageing. Fast-track protocols aim to optimize perioperative management, enhance recovery, and reduce length of stay (LOS). However, LOS variability remains a concern. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of perioperative factors on LOS in patients undergoing primary THA at our institution.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study at a single tertiary-care center included a stratified random sample of 300 primary THAs performed between January 2018 and December 2022 (100 per surgical approach: direct lateral [DL], posterolateral [PL], direct anterior [DAA]). Collected variables were age, sex, BMI, ASA class, laterality, surgical approach, use of tranexamic acid, preoperative laboratory values (hemoglobin, hematocrit, albumin, glucose), chronic anticoagulation, and surgical timing. The primary outcome was length of stay (LOS); prolonged LOS was defined as > 1 postoperative night. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using the Chi-square test. Statistical significance was set at P ≤ .05. The statistical analysis was primarily descriptive and exploratory, focusing on identifying associations between perioperative variables and prolonged length of stay.

RESULTS: Among the 300 patients, 142 (47.3%) were discharged after an overnight stay, whereas 158 (52.7%) experienced prolonged LOS. Female sex (P = .003), lower preoperative hemoglobin and hematocrit levels (P < .001), and chronic anticoagulant therapy (P = .01) were significantly associated with prolonged LOS. Conversely, the DAA was associated with shorter LOS (P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Prolonged LOS was associated with female sex, anemia, and chronic anticoagulant therapy. Likewise, the DAA was associated with a shorter LOS, although these findings should be interpreted with caution due to the retrospective and exploratory nature of the study.

articles.title: Genetic GHSR deficiency and LEAP2 treatment enhance the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide in male mice in a metabolic state-dependent manner.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Liraglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist that lowers glycemia and is used to treat type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. Activation of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) increases glycemia. We aimed to determine whether GHSR inhibition enhances the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We investigated the acute glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide in mice with genetic GHSR deletion or pharmacological GHSR blockade under fed, fasting, and postprandial conditions. We also examined the potential cellular basis of this interaction in murine islets using transcriptomic and immunolabeling approaches and in human pancreatic tissue using a publicly available transcriptomic dataset.

KEY FINDINGS: Liraglutide similarly reduced glycemia in ad libitum-fed GHSR-null and control mice. Following food deprivation, liraglutide more effectively attenuated postprandial increases in glycemia in male, but not female, GHSR-null mice than in control mice. Liraglutide reduced glycemia in fasted GHSR-null male mice but not in WT males. In male mice, pretreatment with a LEAP2 (liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2) analog, an endogenous GHSR antagonist and inverse agonist, enhanced the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide under postprandial and fasting conditions. GHSR and GLP-1R showed limited co-expression in murine islets. In human islets, their co-expression was also limited and enriched in δ-cells, but was also detected in β-cells, where the proportion of GHSR+/GLP-1R+ cells was higher in donors with T2D.

SIGNIFICANCE: GHSR inhibition enhances liraglutide's glucose-lowering effects in a sex-dependent manner, highlighting GHSR as a potential target to improve GLP-1R agonist efficacy.

articles.title: Subcutaneous Progesterone versus Vaginal Progesterone Supplemented with Intramuscular Progesterone Every Third Day in Programmed Vitrified-Warmed Blastocyst Transfer Cycles.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare ongoing pregnancy rates between subcutaneous progesterone and vaginal progesterone supplemented with intramuscular progesterone every third day in programmed frozen embryo transfer cycles.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SUBJECTS: Six hundred twenty patients undergoing their first vitrified-warmed blastocyst transfer with a programmed protocol at a single tertiary center between March 2018 and June 2023; no exclusion criteria were applied.

EXPOSURE: Following 10 to 12 days of estradiol valerate 6 mg/day, 451 patients received subcutaneous progesterone 25 mg every 12 hours, and 169 patients received vaginal progesterone gel 90 mg every 12 hours supplemented with intramuscular progesterone 50 mg every third day (days 1, 4, and 7 of progesterone start). The regimens were used during sequential, nonoverlapping calendar periods.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ongoing pregnancy rate. Serum progesterone was measured on the fifth day of progesterone administration (one day before transfer), 4 to 5 hours after the morning dose. Associations between serum progesterone and ongoing pregnancy were evaluated using regimen-specific percentile categories and continuous modeling. Adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression.

RESULTS: Ongoing pregnancy rates were 53.6% versus 54.4% in the subcutaneous and vaginal plus intramuscular groups, respectively (crude risk difference: -0.9 percentage points; 95% CI: -9.5 to 7.9). After covariate adjustment, standardized risks were 53.6% and 56.2%, respectively (adjusted risk difference: -2.6 percentage points; 95% CI: -12.0 to 6.7; aRR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.81-1.13). Median serum progesterone was 23.48 ng/mL (interquartile range 18.72-29.46) versus 22.90 ng/mL (interquartile range 18.50-29.40), respectively (p=0.543). Neither the percentile-based analyses nor continuous modeling identified a clear association between serum progesterone concentration and ongoing pregnancy within the observed ranges.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in ongoing pregnancy was observed between subcutaneous progesterone 25 mg every 12 hours and vaginal progesterone 90 mg every 12 hours supplemented with intramuscular progesterone 50 mg every third day. Serum P4 distributions overlapped between groups. However, the study design and statistical imprecision preclude causal inference and conclusions of equivalence or non-inferiority.

articles.title: Glycosylated steroidal saponins suppress HNSCC progression by targeting the RAS-ERK pathway.
articles.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by high incidence, pronounced invasiveness and metastasis, and poor prognosis, underscoring an urgent need for novel and effective therapeutic strategies. Natural steroidal saponins serve as promising anti-tumor leads, yet prior work only reports their downstream ERK suppression, lacking upstream regulators and systematic glycosylation-related structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis. This study focused on diosgenin and its two glycosylated derivatives. Firstly, in vitro cell proliferation, apoptosis and invasion assays combined with an in vivo subcutaneous xenograft model were performed to verify anti-HNSCC activities of the candidate compounds. Subsequently, core genes were screened via network pharmacology and machine learning, and validated by molecular docking, pull-down and Western blotting. All three compounds exhibit significant anti-HNSCC activity in vitro and vivo, which increases progressively with the number of glycosyl groups. Combined network pharmacology and machine learning analyses screened out 11 core genes, based on which a stable diagnostic prediction model was constructed. Molecular docking verified that the three saponins can stably bind to and suppress EPHB4 and ADAM17. The Raf1-RBD pull-down assay further confirmed that these saponins markedly reduce the level of intracellular active RAS and specifically downregulate ERK phosphorylation, ultimately restraining the malignant progression of HNSCC. This work reveals the RAS-MAPK inhibitory axis by targeting EPHB4 and ADAM17 of glycosylated steroidal saponins for the first time and highlights glycosylation as a critical activity-boosting moiety, supporting RAS-targeted lead discovery and structural optimisation against HNSCC.

articles.title: Intracellular pH modulates the mechanosensitivity of OSCA/TMEM63 ion channels.
articles.abstract: Mechanosensitive (MS) channels are essential transducers that convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals. OSCA/TMEM63 proteins constitute a conserved family that serves as mechanical and osmotic stress sensors, yet the mechanisms by which the chemical microenvironment modulates their gating remain unclear. Here, we identify intracellular pH as a potent and side-specific regulator of OSCA/TMEM63 activity. Using patch-clamp electrophysiology, we demonstrate that OSCA/TMEM63 currents are reversibly tuned by pH: intracellular acidification suppresses channel activity, whereas alkalinization markedly potentiates it. This regulation is mediated by a pronounced shift in the mechanical activation threshold, thereby effectively tuning channel sensitivity. Our findings establish intracellular pH as a conserved modulator of OSCA/TMEM63 mechanosensitivity, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how the intracellular chemical milieu is coupled to osmo/mechano sensing.

articles.title: The myeloid transcription factor PU.1 acts through three distal and proximal enhancers to drive TNF induction in human alveolar macrophages.
articles.abstract: Macrophages are activated by infection via TLR signaling and produce pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF. However, enhancers regulating TNF transcription in human macrophages have not been well investigated. Here, using next-generation sequencing methods, we identify six candidate enhancers within a 131 kb region around the TNF locus in primary human alveolar macrophages. Three enhancers -distal -16kbTNF, -7.1kbTNF, and proximal enhancer PETNF -directly regulate TNF transcription upon TLR3 stimulation. Deletion of the distal -16kbTNF enhancer led to a 73% reduction in TNF gene transcription in response to poly(I:C) stimulation. Additionally, deletion of the -7.1kbTNF enhancer resulted in a 41% reduction in TNF mRNA, while deletion of the PETNF enhancer resulted in a 52% reduction. A high-throughput reporter assay identified DNA fragments that drive enhancer activity. Mutagenesis analysis of transcription factor binding motifs revealed that PU.1-binding sites are required for enhancer activity. Further analysis demonstrates that PU.1, rather than EGR1 or AP-1, is the master regulator, regulating TNF enhancer activities and TNF transcription. This study shows that PU.1 plays a critical role in driving TNF enhancer activity and mRNA expression in human macrophages.

articles.title: Beneficial effects of nicorandil on exercise capacity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction patients with concomitant coronary microvascular dysfunction.
articles.journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies have suggested a beneficial effect of nicorandil on coronary microcirculation. The present study investigated whether nicorandil improved exercise endurance as well as clinical outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) patients with concomitant coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).

METHODS: In this randomized and controlled trial, 113 HFpEF patients with concomitant CMD were enrolled and allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either nicorandil or serve as controls for 24 months. Enrollment criteria included the absence of significant epicardial coronary artery stenosis and the presence of CMD, defined as a coronary flow reserve (CFR) of < 2.0 as assessed by myocardial contrast echocardiograpgy (MCE). The primary outcome was the change in exercise endurance assessed by the 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). Secondary outcomes included changes in CFR, serum NT-proBNP levels, quality of life (SF-36 Health Survey), and a composite of clinical cardiovascular events (all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization). (https://www.chictr.org.cn: ChiCTR2200067078).

RESULTS: Over the 24-month follow-up, patients in the nicorandil group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in exercise endurance, compared to the control group. This improvement was accompanied by significant enhancements in CFR, reductions in NT-proBNP levels, and higher quality-of-life scores. For the composite cardiovascular endpoint, a non-significant trend toward fewer events was observed in the nicorandil group (P=0.059). Nicorandil treatment was well-tolerated, and no serious adverse events were reported during the study period.

CONCLUSION: In patients with HFpEF and concomitant CMD, nicorandil treatment demonstrated benefits by significantly improving exercise endurance, CFR, NT-proBNP levels, and quality of life.

articles.title: Machine learning-based stability optimization design and virtual screening of the anti-pulmonary fibrosis peptide DR3penA.
articles.abstract: The novel anti-fibrotic peptide DR3penA, previously developed by our research group, demonstrates substantial therapeutic potential; however, its inherent limited metabolic stability in vivo, attributable to its linear structure, hinders clinical translation. Although cyclization represents a key strategy for enhancing peptide structural rigidity, exhaustive trial-and-error exploration across the vast chemical modification space entails prohibitive computational and experimental costs. In this study, we constructed a machine learning-assisted virtual screening framework for the rational optimization of peptide stability and bioactivity. This framework integrates a stability prediction model with an ensemble bioactivity prediction model based on XGBoost and LightGBM, and employs comprehensive scoring alongside Pareto front analysis to perform multi-objective screening of candidate analogs. Computational evaluation showed that, under leakage-audited cluster splitting, the stability XGBoost model exhibits strong ranking capability (test Spearman ρ = 0.751; NDCG@10 = 0.969), and the XGBoost-LightGBM ensemble achieves high predictive performance for a pan-peptide bioactivity proxy (test R² = 0.822). A virtual library of 95 analogues was generated by predefined chemical rules; cyclization sites were enumerated rather than discovered de novo, and the models were used to rank these schemes. Three analogues (DR3penA_001, _011, and _076) were nominated as a representative panel covering distinct cyclization chemistries, rather than the three highest composite scores. Altogether, this hierarchical, leakage-aware framework enables stability-prioritized, multi-objective nomination of DR3penA analogues and provides a transferable, data-driven strategy for peptide redesign.

articles.title: Diagonal Earlobe Crease (Frank's Sign) and Atrial Fibrillation: A Review of the Sparse Evidence Against an Established Coronary Artery Disease Association.
Prevalence and Timing of Palliative Care Provision For Decedents with Heart Failure - Trends from 2016 to 2022.
Donor-Recipient Sex Mismatch is Associated with Severe Primary Graft Dysfunction after Heart Transplantation.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between sex and primary graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HT) remains unclear. We evaluated whether recipient sex and donor-recipient sex matching are associated with severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) in a contemporary, multicenter cohort.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the International PGD Consortium comprised of adult HTs from 2010 to 2024 across 14 centers. Associations between sex-related variables and severe PGD were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and adjusted for ischemic time, pre-transplant durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), dialysis, congenital heart disease, and predicted heart mass (PHM) ratio.

RESULTS: Among 3,994 recipients, 1,030 (25.8%) were female. Female recipients were younger (54 vs. 57 years) with fewer comorbidities, and less frequently bridged on a durable LVAD (19.8% vs. 29.1%). Although female recipients had a lower incidence of PGD than male recipients (7.1% vs. 9.4%), recipient sex was not independently associated with PGD after multivariable adjustment. Female donor to male recipient sex mismatching had the highest PGD incidence of 11.5% and was associated with a 43% increase in the odds of severe PGD (p=0.030). While sex-mismatch was associated with an increased incidence of PGD, size mismatch by PHM ratio was not an independent predictor.

CONCLUSION: In this large international registry, donor-recipient sex mismatch, specifically among male recipients of female donor hearts, was independently associated with severe PGD, even when appropriately size matched. These findings inform risk stratification for development of severe PGD after HT.

articles.title: Resource Utilization and Forecasting in Heart Failure Patients with Durable Left Ventricular Assist Devices.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Heart failure patients treated with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) require significant resource utilization. Patient volume and contact points based on implant volume remain poorly quantified. We retrospectively reviewed 268 patients implanted with a durable LVAD at a single, experienced center from 2011 through 2022 and recorded survival, telephone encounters, office visits, and all-cause hospitalizations. Telephone encounters peaked at 10.4 per patient-month and declined to approximately 5 after 24 months; 66% were anticoagulation-related. Office visits peaked at 3.0 per patient-month and declined to approximately 0.7 after 18 months. Hospitalizations decreased from 2.7 per patient-year in year 1 to approximately 1 by year 5. Five-year survival with HeartMate 3 (HM3) was 61.4%. Applying HM3 survival to constant annual implant volumes yielded estimated 5-year censuses of 39, 96, and 193 surviving patients for 10, 25, and 50 annual implants, respectively. These findings may inform LVAD program capacity and staffing.

articles.title: Rethinking Transplant Risk in Adults with a Failing Fontan Circulation.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

articles.title: Ferritin-displayed engineered sCAR1 nanoparticles as a receptor-decoy antiviral strategy against Coxsackievirus B-associated inflammation.
articles.abstract: Coxsackievirus Group B (CVB) remains an important cause of severe disease in infants and young children, including viral myocarditis and meningitis, yet no licensed vaccine or virus-specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Here, we engineered soluble Coxsackievirus and adenovirus receptor (CAR) ectodomains and displayed the optimized receptor decoy on ferritin nanoparticles to generate a potent anti-CVB3 entry inhibitor. Wild-type soluble CAR ectodomains neutralized CVB3 but were limited by homodimerization and by residual binding to endogenous CAR/JAML, which was associated with dose-dependent mitogenic activity. Guided by structural information, we introduced mutations that abolished dimerization and CAR/JAML binding while preserving, and further improving, viral neutralization. Ferritin display of the optimized sCAR1 mutant enhanced multivalent presentation, systemic persistence, and tissue delivery. The resulting sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin nanoparticle achieved IC50 values of 413 ng/mL in Vero cells and 140 ng/mL in SH-SY5Y cells. In neonatal BALB/c mice, prophylactic administration of sCAR1 Mu+Ferritin (200 μg, 6 h before challenge) conferred 68.75% protection against lethal CVB3 infection (103.5 CCID50), reduced viral burden in the liver, spleen, brain, and heart, and alleviated myocarditis and neuroinflammation without sustained cytokine activation. Cross-neutralizing activity against CVB1 further supports the breadth of this receptor-based platform. These findings identify ferritin-displayed engineered CAR nanoparticles as a safety-optimized and mutation-resilient antiviral strategy for CVB infections.

articles.title: Small molecules inhibit hepatitis B and D virus infection by binding the small surface antigen.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Current therapies for chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection effectively suppress viral replication but do not achieve a functional cure. Targeting viral entry represents a promising strategy to complement existing treatments.

METHODS: Small-molecule compounds were identified through structure-based virtual screening targeting SHBs (small hepatitis B surface antigen). HBV infection models using HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes were established to investigate the antiviral activities and underlying mechanisms of these compounds in vitro. Molecular docking analyses were performed to predict the potential binding regions of the small molecules with SHBs. In addition, we performed mutagenesis based on the predicted interaction residues, followed by functional assays to validate the docking predictions.

RESULTS: Assays in the HBV infection model showed that isotretinoin, ciprofibrate, and caffeic acid significantly reduced HBsAg, HBeAg, and HBV pregenomic RNA levels when administered concurrently with HBV infection. Biophysical and biochemical assays demonstrated that these compounds interacted with SHBs. In addition, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis-based functional assays suggested that the interaction sites may involve the AGL region. Mechanistically, the compounds mainly acted during the early stage of infection and reduced HBV attachment and internalization-associated signals. In addition, these compounds inhibited HDV infection, supporting their activity against HBV envelope-mediated viral entry.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that these small molecules are promising candidates for developing novel entry inhibitors targeting SHBs, which may enhance therapeutic options against HBV and HDV.

articles.title: Impact of minimally processed versus milled whole grains on glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes: A 12-week randomised trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whole grains are widely promoted within a healthy diet, with dietary advice encouraging the replacement of refined grains with whole grains. However, data from small trials indicates that milling or processing whole grains may influence the glycaemic response.

OBJECTIVE: To identify if clinically relevant HbA1c differs with processed (milled) or less processed (unmilled) whole grain intakes in type 2 diabetes management.

METHODS: We conducted a 12-week randomised parallel trial in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants received free and delivered whole grain foods that differed in degree of processing. Each intervention was of four foods from whole grain wheat, rice, and oats, in sufficient amounts (4.5-9kg per fortnight) to accommodate family size. Participants were advised to replace the grain foods they normally consumed with the provided products. The primary outcome was glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). All analyses were performed using an intention-to-treat approach, with outcome variables investigated using a generalised linear model.

RESULTS: 160 adults with type 2 diabetes (mean age 58.5 ± 11.5 years; BMI 33.7 ± 7.3 kg/m2; HbA1c 56.4 ± 14.3 mmol/mol) were randomised, with 143 (89%) providing end-of-intervention blood samples. HbA1c was lower following the less processed whole grain intervention compared with the more processed whole grain intervention (mean difference -2.2 mmol/mol, 95% CI -4.2, -0.1), despite no change observed in body weight between interventions. Whole grain, refined grain, and nutrient intakes did not differ between groups, with intervention foods providing approximately 20% of dietary energy. Among the secondary or exploratory outcomes, improvements were indicated only in self-reported bowel habits with less processed whole grains.

CONCLUSIONS: Less processed whole grain foods were associated with improved glycated haemoglobin compared with more processed whole grain foods in adults with type 2 diabetes. These findings indicate that the degree of grain processing influences metabolic outcomes, support food reformulation, and distinguishing between refined grains, milled whole grains (wholemeal), and intact whole grains in dietary guidance, food marketing and labelling.

articles.title: Metabolic phenotyping identifies early interindividual variation in infant energy expenditure with implications for obesity risk.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major public health crisis. Early identification of metabolic traits that increase individual risk are emerging. As such, identification of variability in early energy expenditure would reveal the need for precision nutritional approaches from birth.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interindividual variability in components of energy expenditure for the purpose of understanding early nutritional considerations in very young infants.

METHODS: Infant participants (<3 months of age) underwent extensive energy expenditure phenotyping using a combination of doubly labeled water for total daily energy expenditure and a novel infant metabolic chamber for sleeping energy expenditure. Descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients, and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to assess reliability and characterize variability, predictors, and phenotypes of energy expenditure. We identified interindividual variability in total, mass-adjusted, and fat-free mass adjusted energy expenditures. Energy phenotypes (thrifty and spendthrift) were assigned based on the residuals between measured and predicted energy expenditure from metabolic mass. Discrepancies between measured energy expenditure and predicted by national dietary recommendations for infants (2023 DRI) were evaluated.

RESULTS: Total daily and sleeping energy expenditures were 368±60 kcal/d and 250±60 kcal/d, respectively. Energy expenditure related to activity accounted for 21±9% of total measured. Age (r=.59), weight (r=.83), length (r=.75), and fat-free mass (r=.82) were positively associated with sleeping energy expenditure. We identified 40% of measured infants with a thrifty energy phenotype, classified as having sleeping energy expenditure under that predicted by cohort age, sex, and fat and fat-free mass. Mean prediction error of the 2023 DRI from our cohort was 10±7% and was positively associated with the amount of energy expenditure attributed to activity.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings warrant further comprehensive metabolic phenotyping studies in young infants to understand how early energy expenditure tracks through the life course and influences obesity risk as well as the thorough evaluation and refinement of infant nutritional recommendations.

articles.title: Sociocultural disparities in diabetic complications within Canada: a longitudinal cohort study of 680,000 women followed after pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of sociocultural status on the risk of diabetes and diabetic complications among women from a large Canadian province.

METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study of sociocultural disparities in diabetes and diabetic complications among 681,875 women from Quebec, Canada with pregnancies between 2006 and 2023. We measured sociocultural disparities using linguistic status, comparing the anglophone minority of Quebec with the francophone majority. Outcomes included diabetic cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications that led to admissions anytime during follow-up. We accounted for patient characteristics and used Cox regression models to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for each diabetic complication, contrasting anglophones relative to francophones.

RESULTS: Compared with francophones, anglophones were 1.27 times more likely to develop diabetes in the long-term period following pregnancy (95% CI 1.15-1.39). Anglophones were more likely to be admitted for diabetic cardiovascular (HR 1.94, 95% CI 1.45-2.60), renal (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.10-1.89), and metabolic complications (HR 1.50, 95% CI 1.13-1.99). Anglophones with gestational diabetes (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.16-2.66) and preexisting morbidity (HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.11-4.27) were particularly at risk of developing cardiovascular complications. Anglophones who were socioeconomically disadvantaged were also at risk of diabetic cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Sociocultural disparities in the development of diabetic complications are present in Quebec, Canada, with anglophone women having a greater risk of cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications than francophone women in the long term.

articles.title: Persistent Enterococcus faecium bacteremia with emergence of daptomycin resistance and unexpected resistance mutations.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Persistent bacteremia due to Enterococcus spp., without an identifiable source of infection, is a well described phenomenon. Although often the preferred therapeutic agent, daptomycin resistance may develop resulting in clinical failure. In North American isolates, mutations in the LiaFSR gene complex (specifically LiaR W73C and LiaS T120A) are associated with daptomycin resistance; however these mutations also correlate with daptomycin-β-lactam synergistic activity. The case presented in this report had persistent vancomycin-resistant E. faecium bacteremia despite 26 days of daptomycin and β-lactam therapy. Initial daptomycin MICs were 2-4 µg/ml, and rose to 8 µg/ml during therapy. Whole genome sequencing revealed a mutation in the LiaFSR gene complex (S19F of LiaR) previously reported only in Australian isolates. While other mutations involving LiaFSR are associated with synergy between daptomycin and β-lactams, clinical failure of combination therapy was observed in this case. Whenever possible, additional microbiological and genomic testing should be performed on isolates of E. faecium presenting with refractory bacteremia.

articles.title: Lifetime Management of Aortic Stenosis: Expert Review of Evidence and Consensus Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery Guidelines introduced a Class I recommendation for transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in selected patients aged 70 years or older with tricuspid aortic stenosis and suitable anatomy, while surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains recommended in younger low-risk patients. In patients with long expected survival, this framework requires careful consideration of valve durability, future reintervention, and patient preferences. This expert review, developed by the Italian Cardiac Surgery Working Group, examines contemporary evidence and consensus recommendations from a lifetime-management perspective.

METHODS: We performed a narrative, evidence-based synthesis of randomized trials, trial-based meta-analyses, and propensity-matched real-world registries comparing transfemoral TAVI and SAVR, with primary emphasis on low-risk patients. Lower-intermediate-risk evidence was included only when directly relevant to lifetime management, durability, or reintervention.

RESULTS: Evidence suggests that treatment effects are time-dependent: early non-inferiority of TAVI may attenuate with longer follow-up, particularly in patients with substantial life expectancy. Randomized durability data remain limited, whereas propensity-matched real-world registries have suggested possible higher late mortality after TAVI in younger, lower-risk populations. Reintervention after a transcatheter-first strategy may be associated with increasing technical complexity and procedural risk over time.

CONCLUSIONS: This review supports appropriate application of current guidelines through a pragmatic framework for individualized, Heart Team-based decision-making. Transfemoral TAVI is often appropriate in patients with limited life expectancy or recognized high surgical risk when anatomically feasible. In patients with long expected survival, SAVR should retain a central role as an important reference strategy.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Risk of Arrhythmias: A Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmias are often associated with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity, which significantly influence their onset and progression. In this context, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have garnered attention for their potential benefits, with emerging evidence indicating that GLP-1 receptor activation might offer antiarrhythmic effects.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of all GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists on the incidence of new-onset arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS: A comprehensive search of databases was conducted from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) focusing on patients with diabetes or obesity receiving GLP-1 RAs or co-agonists. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Interventions were ranked using the p-score cumulative rank, ranging from 0 (worst) to 1 (best).

RESULTS: A total of 94 RCTs involving 155,989 patients were included, comparing 12 GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists. Subcutaneous semaglutide emerged as the most effective intervention, significantly reducing AF incidence compared with placebo (RR 0.82; 95% CI: 0.68 to 0.99), and compared with tirzepatide (RR 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37 to 0.88). In contrast, dulaglutide was associated with an increased risk of AF, while lixisenatide was associated with a decreased risk in atrioventricular blocks. For AF, semaglutide presented a p-score of 0.7885, while tirzepatide and dulaglutide scored 0.1830 and 0.1750, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Among GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists, subcutaneous semaglutide is highlighted as the most effective intervention for reducing the risk of AF. Further studies focusing on arrhythmic outcomes are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Association of Completion Imaging Modalities and Carotid Endarterectomy Outcomes in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Completion imaging after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) confirms technical success and identifies defects requiring correction. However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: CEAs performed between 2012-2024 in the VQI were analyzed. Completion imaging was categorized as none, Doppler, duplex ultrasound, or angiography. Intraoperative re-exploration rates were compared across modalities to assess detection of technical defects requiring revision. Postoperative outcomes were analyzed among patients who required re-exploration. Inverse probability weighted (IPW) logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios. Temporal trends were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 208,786 CEAs, 24% had no completion imaging, 48% used Doppler, 24% duplex, and 4% angiography. Angiography had the highest intraoperative re-exploration rate (none 0.9%, doppler 0.9%, duplex 2.3%, angiography 3.6%; p<0.001). Among the 2,723 patients who required re-exploration, postoperative stroke occurred in 8.3% with no imaging, 12.5% with doppler, 3.7% with duplex, and 22.5% with angiography (p<0.001). In IPW-adjusted analyses, intraoperative duplex was associated with significant reduction in postoperative stroke compared to: no imaging (aOR 0.43, 95%CI 0.27-0.69), doppler (aOR 0.28, 95%CI 0.19-0.40), and angiography (aOR 0.13, 95%CI 0.09-0.20), all p<0.001. Overall, Angiography had the worst stroke outcomes. Doppler and angiography performed worse than duplex across additional endpoints, including ipsilateral stroke, TIA, any neurological event, return to OR, and 30-day mortality. Despite the stronger safety profile of duplex, it remains underused, as most CEAs performed in the last 15 years have utilized doppler or no imaging.

CONCLUSIONS: Re-exploration and stroke outcomes after completion imaging reflect each modality's safety and efficacy in detecting significant technical defects. Duplex ultrasound demonstrated the lowest stroke rates and overall complications compared with angiography, doppler, and no imaging, suggesting its superior efficacy and safety. Doppler showed intermediate performance, while angiography carried the highest risk among patients who required re-exploration. Despite strong evidence favoring duplex, the majority of surgeons performing CEAs still rely on doppler or omit any completion imaging. Greater use of duplex ultrasound and incorporation of intraoperative duplex assessment into vascular training may improve intraoperative assessment, although further prospective evaluation is warranted.

articles.title: New paradigms in Hepatitis D: screening, treatment, and the path to cure.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis D virus infection, also known as chronic hepatitis delta, remains the most severe form of chronic viral hepatitis, associated with accelerated liver disease progression, cirrhosis, decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Recent years have seen major advances in screening strategies and antiviral therapies for hepatitis D. This review discusses evidence supporting broader hepatitis D screening among hepatitis B surface antigen-positive individuals and practical considerations for implementation across epidemiological settings, and reviews current and emerging treatments - entry inhibition (bulevirtide), prenylation inhibition (lonafarnib), immune-modulatory therapies (pegylated interferons), and hepatitis B surface antigen-targeting approaches (tobevibart, elebsiran, brelovitug, nucleic acid polymers) - focusing on treatment response and durability of viral suppression. In conclusion, emerging therapies have substantially improved antiviral efficacy, shifting the focus of hepatitis D management from on-treatment suppression toward durable off-treatment control and functional cure, changing the diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management of chronic hepatitis D.

articles.title: Oral Maintenance Anti-Hypertensives for Severe Systolic Hypertension: A Controlled Before and After Quality Improvement Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A systolic blood pressure (SBP) threshold  160 mmHg is used in pregnancy for acute anti-hypertensive treatment; however, this was initially adapted from expert opinion and guidelines for non-pregnant adults support a SBP  180 mmHg. We compared adverse maternal outcomes using a SBP threshold of  180 mmHg versus  160 mmHg for acute anti-hypertensive treatment, while treating SBPs between 160-179 mmHg (DBP  110 mmHg) with oral maintenance anti-hypertensives.

STUDY DESIGN: We performed a Quality Improvement before and after non-inferiority study (NCT05881252) of singletons  20 weeks' with SBP  160 mmHg at a single Level 4 medical center. In the before group, acute antihypertensives (intravenous [IV] labetalol/hydralazine or rapid-acting oral nifedipine) were given for persistent SBP  160 mmHg (or DBP  110 mmHg). In the after group, oral maintenance antihypertensives (labetalol or extended-release nifedipine) were given if persistent SBP between 160-179 mmHg (DBP  110 mmHg) and acute antihypertensives for persistent SBP  180 mmHg (or DBP  110 mmHg). The primary outcome was a composite of congestive heart failure, pulmonary edema, cerebrovascular accident, acute kidney injury, or myocardial infarction. Bayesian analysis was performed using a non-inferiority margin of 4% and 1% (posthoc sensitivity analysis).

RESULTS: We studied 1,002 individuals (410 in before; 592 in after) with severe hypertension. The primary outcome occurred in 2.9% of the before and 1.9% of the after group (0.72 median relative risk, 95% credible interval 0.36-1.46) with an 82% probability of risk reduction in the after group and > 99.9% probability that the risk difference in the after group was < 4% (99% for a 1% margin). Use of acute antihypertensives per individual treated decreased almost 3-fold in the after group (mean 1.7 doses versus 0.6, p<0.01) Conclusion: In our population, treating SBPs between 160-180 mmHg with oral maintenance antihypertensives resulted in to a non-inferior rate of maternal adverse outcomes and decreased the use of.

articles.title: Observational Study of Cannabis Use Among Pregnant Women Who Used Nicotine.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize perceptions of cannabis use and motivations for use among a cohort of pregnant women who used nicotine.

DESIGN: Descriptive observational.

SETTING: Prenatal clinics in Kentucky where cannabis was illegal at the time of data collection.

PARTICIPANTS: Pregnant women (N = 81) who used nicotine.

METHODS: We surveyed participants at each trimester. Participants completed routine clinical urine drug screening and self-report use measures for cannabis use. We report descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Of the 81 participants, 18.5% (n = 15) self-reported cannabis use in the past 30 days and 21% (n = 17) tested positive for cannabis on routine prenatal urine drug screening. Most participants believed that cannabis use was acceptable during pregnancy (83.8%, n = 67) and not a health hazard at all (61.7%, n = 50). Common motivations for use among those who self-reported included reduced stress (93.3%, n = 14), aid for sleeping (66.7%, n = 10), and reduced fear (66.7%, n = 10). In addition, 60% (n = 9) reported use to relax or relieve physical or emotional pain.

CONCLUSIONS: Changing perceptions regarding the acceptability of cannabis use in the prenatal period place pregnant women and their children at risk of harm. Our findings demonstrate a critical need for future research and clear public health messaging about the risks of cannabis use during pregnancy.

articles.title: Association between Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Intraocular pressure-related outcomes: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic metabolic disorder with potential ocular manifestations. Emerging evidence suggests a relationship between MASLD and glaucoma; however, findings remain inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the association between MASLD and intraocular pressure (IOP) related outcomes.

METHODS: We retrieved relevant articles from four databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane) and adhered to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The primary outcomes were the proportion with glaucoma and the mean IOP among individuals with MASLD compared with those without fatty liver disease. A meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence interval (CI) in IOP between the fatty liver and non-fatty liver groups, using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Five observational studies involving more than 370,000 participants were included, with four retrospective and one prospective cohort. Across studies, individuals with fatty liver consistently demonstrated higher IOP and a greater risk of glaucoma-related outcomes compared with those without fatty liver disease. Increasing severity of fatty liver was associated with higher IOP in three studies. A meta-analysis comprising 23,625 participants (7,409 with fatty liver and 16,216 healthy) demonstrated a significantly higher mean IOP in patients with fatty liver (MD: 0.81 mmHg; 95% CI: 0.51-1.10; p=0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that patients with MASLD have higher intraocular pressure. Individuals with MASLD may represent a high-risk population warranting ophthalmic screening and closer metabolic risk assessment.

articles.title: Platelet Factor 4 and Corresponding Antibodies in Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract: Antibodies directed against platelet factor 4 (PF4) are increasingly recognized as key mediators of immunothrombosis. In heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), these antibodies emerge following exposure to the polyanion heparin, whereas in vaccine-induced immune thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (VITT), they arise in response to vector-based vaccination or (adeno)viral infections. In both settings, anti-PF4 antibodies promote platelet activation and enhance inflammatory and thrombotic processes. PF4 itself has also been implicated in atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease (CVD), although clinical studies investigating this link have yielded inconsistent results. We review the current knowledge on the roles of PF4 and anti-PF4 antibodies in atherosclerosis and CVD and discuss preclinical and clinical evidence for their relevance in the perioperative setting, for disease progression and antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: [Delphi consensus on criteria justifying prolonged inpatient stay in hand surgery hybrid DRG cases and short-stay DRGs﻿].
articles.journal: Handchirurgie, Mikrochirurgie, plastische Chirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Handchirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Mikrochirurgie der Peripheren Nerven und Gefasse : Organ der V...
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hybrid DRGs were introduced to reimburse suitable, predominantly surgical services across inpatient and outpatient sectors and to promote ambulatory care, short-stay DRGs will follow﻿. However, postoperative situations still arise in which continued inpatient treatment may be medically necessary despite the generally ambulatory character of the procedure. To date, specialty-specific criteria justifying a hospital stay beyond the second postoperative night have been lacking in hand surgery. The overarching aim is to ensure patient safety by maintaining bed utilization decisions on the basis of medical rather than administrative considerations.

METHODS: A two-round Delphi survey was conducted among hand surgery experts, each with several years of experience (Tang Level III). The survey was based on 21 criteria, predefined by a consensus group of the German Society for Hand Surgery (DGH), covering domains relevant to postoperative care. For each item, participants rated on a 5-point Likert scale whether it justified prolongation of the inpatient stay. In addition, each criterion was categorized as an objectively measurable/score-based circumstance, a circumstance-dependent factor, or a major criterion. Consensus was defined as at least 75% agreement.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven individuals participated in the first round and 21 in the second round. Consensus was reached for 19 of 21 criteria that they justified prolongation of the inpatient stay. Among the criteria reaching consensus, eight were classified as major criteria and six as circumstance-dependent factors; for five criteria, no final traffic-light category could be agreed upon.

CONCLUSION: This Delphi survey identified a specialty-specific set of clinically plausible criteria that may justify inpatient treatment beyond the second night in hand surgery Hybrid-DRG cases or short-stay DRGs﻿. The findings are intended to support greater decision-making certainty for healthcare providers as well as payers and to avoid perverse incentives in patient triage at the interface between Hybrid DRGs and inpatient DRGs.

articles.title: Clinical Efficacy of Inferior Turbinate Outfracture Combined with Low-Temperature Plasma Radiofrequency Ablation in Obese Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome Complicated with Nasal Obstruction.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the long-term clinical efficacy of combined inferior turbinate outfracture and low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation on nasal ventilation, continuous positive airway pressure tolerance, sleep status and body mass index (BMI) in obese patients with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) complicated with bilateral inferior turbinate hypertrophy, whose BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2.MethodsThis single-center retrospective study enrolled a total of 40 obese OSAHS patients with bilateral inferior turbinate hypertrophy treated at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Liangxiang Hospital from August 2023 to August 2024. All subjects received combined inferior turbinate outfracture and low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia. Outcome indicators including nasal airway resistance, apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), visual analogue scale (VAS) for nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) tolerance and BMI were detected before surgery, 1 month, 6 months and 1 year postoperatively. Polysomnography, anterior rhinomanometry and standardized scale assessment were performed uniformly at each follow-up time point. Intra-group comparisons between preoperative and postoperative data were analyzed by paired t-test; P < 0.05 was defined as statistically significant.ResultsAll 40 patients completed the 1-year standardized follow-up without loss to follow-up. Compared with preoperative baseline levels, nasal airway resistance, AHI, ESS scores and BMI were significantly decreased at 1, 6 and 12 months after surgery (all P < 0.05), while VAS scores reflecting nCPAP tolerance increased markedly (all P < 0.05). Nasal airway resistance remained stable at a low level within one year after operation. AHI and BMI were further reduced at postoperative 1 year compared with 1 month after surgery (P < 0.05), and ESS scores achieved the optimal improvement at postoperative 6 months.ConclusionObservations from this case series suggest that the combined inferior turbinate outfracture and low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation may represent a feasible minimally invasive surgical option for obese OSAHS patients with nasal obstruction, inferior turbinate hypertrophy and documented CPAP intolerance. Within this cohort, we observed postoperative reductions in nasal airway resistance, AHI, ESS scores and BMI, accompanied by improved self-reported nCPAP tolerance. However, we cannot quantify how much of these improvements stem from nasal surgery versus weight loss, CPAP use or other unmeasured factors. A reduction in BMI cannot be interpreted as evidence that surgery induces weight loss. The hypothesis of a positive therapeutic cycle remains speculative, as data regarding diet, exercise, weight-loss interventions and objective CPAP usage were not collected. No postoperative infection or active bleeding was observed in the present cohort; nevertheless, other potential complications were not systematically assessed, so the safety profile of this procedure cannot be fully determined. This surgical approach avoids the high perioperative risks of traditional extensive pharyngeal surgery and provides a potential observational reference for obese OSAHS patients with severe nasal stenosis.

articles.title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.

INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.

FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.
