articles.title: Multimorbidity among older people in three African countries: a population-based cross-sectional study in The Gambia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity is intricately associated with global ageing and presents a key challenge for health systems and individuals. Despite growing recognition of this challenge, the gap in robust, comparable, population-level evidence on multimorbidity in Africa remains substantial. We aimed to describe multimorbidity among older people across five African sites in three countries representing different epidemiological and health-care contexts.

METHODS: In this population-based cross-sectional study, we recruited adults aged at least 40 years in rural and urban The Gambia, rural and urban South Africa, and urban Zimbabwe (Feb 10, 2022 to Sept 2, 2024). Participants were stratified by site, age-band (40-54 years, 55-69 years, and ≥70 years), and sex. We included 5296 adults (median age 60 years, 53% were women) and recorded their self-reported medical conditions and current medications. We further assessed their height, weight, blood pressure, blood glucose, mental health symptoms, HIV status, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We defined multimorbidity as having two or more of 26 chronic conditions. Multimorbidity prevalence was calculated weighted to each country's national population. We evaluated the risk factors for multimorbidity and associations of multimorbidity with HRQoL; multimorbidity clusters were described using latent class analysis.

FINDINGS: 1926 (36%) of 5296 adults had multimorbidity. The weighted prevalence of multimorbidity was 36% (95% CI 35-37), ranging from 6·6% (5·1-8·1) in rural The Gambia to 62·0% (58·7-65·3) in urban South Africa. Across the three countries, education level, wealth, smoking, alcohol consumption, and BMI were the lowest in The Gambia and the greatest in South Africa, with a rural-urban gradient. Diabetes, hypertension, HIV, mood disorders, arthritis, and fragility fractures were the most common multimorbidity components. People with multimorbidity had lower HRQoL than those without multimorbidity. In Zimbabwe and South Africa, cardiometabolic (42-57% of the population) and HIV-related (25-48% of the population) multimorbidity clusters emerged, characterised by component diseases, risk factors, and associations with HRQoL.

INTERPRETATION: Multimorbidity was found to be common among older people in five study settings in three African countries, with notable trends across sites. The high prevalence of multimorbidity in urban South Africa might foreshadow future trends across the African region as the continent's demographic and health transition advances, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated multisectoral strategies to address multimorbidity.

FUNDING: Wellcome, National Institute for Health Research, and Medical Research Council.

articles.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation.
articles.abstract: RNA viruses encode multiple layers of information within a single molecule, which functions simultaneously as a template for protein synthesis and as a structured regulatory RNA. These structures control key aspects of viral gene expression, govern host interactions, and mediate immune evasion. Although the prevalence of RNA structure in viral genomes is now well established, only recently have functional and mechanistic studies begun to uncover how these elements act as regulatory modules that shape infection outcomes. With their compact genomes and experimentally tractable life cycles, RNA viruses represent powerful model systems for uncovering the fundamental building blocks of riboregulation and illuminating principles of gene control conserved across eukaryotes. Here, we review current mechanistic understanding of RNA structure-based regulation across diverse viral families and draw parallels to structure-mediated gene control in eukaryotic transcriptomes, highlighting RNA structure as a central regulatory layer in gene expression with broad therapeutic and synthetic biology potential.

articles.title: UBT251, a novel triple GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptor agonist, in adults with type 2 diabetes: A multicenter, randomized phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: This phase 2 trial included 211 Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (mean age 48.4 years; 131 participants were male). Participants received once-weekly subcutaneous UBT251 (2 mg, 4 mg [initial dose 0.5 mg], 4 mg [initial dose 1 mg], or 6 mg), 1 mg semaglutide, or placebo for 24 weeks. At week 24, UBT251 achieved least-squares mean changes in glycated hemoglobin of -2.16% (95% CI, -2.39 to -1.92) to -1.98% (95% CI, -2.31 to -1.64), versus -1.77% (95% CI, -1.99 to -1.54) for semaglutide and -0.66% (95% CI, -0.90 to -0.41) for placebo (placebo-adjusted differences: -1.50% to -1.32%; all p < 0.001). UBT251 significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, 2-h postprandial glucose, and waist circumference versus placebo (all p < 0.001). Weight reduction with UBT251 was significantly greater than both placebo and semaglutide (all p < 0.05). Gastrointestinal events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events. These findings support further phase 3 evaluation of UBT251. Registration: CTR20250029; NCT07163624.

articles.title: Genetic Heterogeneity of Asthma Across Sex, Age at Onset, and Disease Severity.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology

articles.title: Cerebral palsy and intrapartum hypoxia: current evidence and the position of Korean Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine.
articles.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) has long been associated with intrapartum hypoxia; however, contemporary evidence indicates that acute hypoxic-ischemic events during labor account for only a minority of cases. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and causation assessment of CP, focusing on the limitations of electronic fetal monitoring, umbilical cord pH, low Apgar scores, and cesarean delivery as predictors or preventive measures for CP. Prematurity, intrauterine infection and inflammation, placental pathology, perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, and genetic factors are important associated factors or contributory pathways in CP, although their population-attributable contributions remain uncertain. Recent genomic studies have identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in approximately one-quarter to one-third of affected children, challenging the traditional assumption that unexplained CP is attributable to intrapartum events. Current evidence indicates that isolated fetal heart rate abnormalities, acidemia, or neonatal encephalopathy alone are insufficient to establish intrapartum hypoxia as the cause of CP. The Korean Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine emphasizes that causation assessments should rely on strict criteria, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and integrated interpretation of antenatal, intrapartum, neonatal, neuroimaging, placental, and genetic findings. A multifactorial and evidence-based approach is essential for rational clinical assessment, appropriate counseling, and avoidance of unnecessary defensive obstetric practices.

articles.title: Geographic Variations and Determinants of Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Among Indonesian Adults: Evidence From the 2023 Indonesian Health Survey.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The rising burden of prediabetes and Type 2 diabetes (T2D) in Indonesia, along with geographic disparities and age-related risk patterns, remain inadequately understood. The present study used nationally representative data to examine determinants, geographic variations and age and sex related glycaemic probability patterns.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study using data from the Indonesian Health Survey 2023 on individuals aged ≥ 15 years (n = 37,157). Analysis was performed using survey weighting and multinomial logistic regression. Non-linear age relationships were modelled using generalized additive models (GAM), and regional variations were visualized using choropleth maps.

RESULTS: A total of 37.4% of respondents were classified as normoglycaemia, 41.6% as prediabetic and 20.9% as having T2D. The main determinants of prediabetes included age ≥ 45 years (aOR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.40-1.57), males (aOR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.44-1.67), obesity (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI: 1.37-1.55), hypertension (aOR = 1.35; 95% CI: 1.27-1.43) and dyslipidemia (aOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.24-1.38). The main determinants of T2D were age ≥ 45 years (aOR = 7.13; 95% CI: 5.63-9.04), dyslipidemia (aOR = 2.51; 95% CI: 2.10-3.00), hypertension (aOR = 1.77; 95% CI: 1.50-2.09) and obesity (aOR = 1.65; 95% CI: 1.35-2.01). The GAM showed a non-linear and accelerated increase in the probability of T2D in older age. Geographically, the burden of dysglycaemia is more concentrated in western Indonesia, indicating regional disparities in risk distribution.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate significant geographic variation and key determinants of prediabetes and T2D, supporting region-specific prevention strategies, risk-based screening and equitable public health policies to strengthen diabetes prevention and control in Indonesia.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes of combined ESWT-based conservative therapy in lipedema: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundLipedema is a chronic condition that is increasingly being detected and gaining public awareness; however, strongly validated therapeutic options are lacking.ObjectivesGiven need for appropriate lipedema management approaches and demand for new studies and methods, this investigation aimed to compare effects of a combined treatment consisting of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT), manual lymphatic drainage (MLD), intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC), and lifestyle recommenda-tions to a 5-week pre-treatment period prior to treatment in patients with lipedema.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective evaluation of patients undergoing a 5-week pre-treatment period with lifestyle recommendations followed by a 5-week treatment period (10 sessions) with a standardized protocol including ESWT, MLD and IPC. Circumference measurements at three designated points on the lower extremities were recorded at start and end of pre-treatment period and before and after treatment.ResultsData from 55 female patients (age: 46.9 ± 11.9 years; body mass index: 29.54 ± 7.33 kg/m2) who completed both the 5-week pre-treatment lifestyle-only observation period and the subsequent 5-week combined treatment period were analyzed. Comparison of changes in lower extremity circumference measurements between the two periods demonstrated significantly greater reductions during the combined treatment period at five of the six evaluated measurement sites.(p < 0.05).ConclusionIn this retrospective cohort study, combined use of ESWT, MLD, IPC, and lifestyle recommendations was associated with improvements in lower extremity circumference measurements; however, due to its non-randomized design, causal inferences cannot be made. Further randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify individual and combined effects of these treatments.

articles.title: Patterns of Postdischarge Heart Failure, Ischemic, and Bleeding Events After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) have improved, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, ischemic events, and major bleeding remain clinical challenges in patients with severe aortic stenosis.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the incidence, timing, and prognostic impact of these events after TAVR.

METHODS: This two-center retrospective registry included 988 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR. Patients were grouped according to the first clinical event after discharge: HF hospitalization, ischemic events (myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke), major bleeding, or the event-free group. The timing of the first postdischarge event and all-cause mortality after the first event were evaluated.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 665 days after discharge, 165 patients (16.7%) experienced any of these events. As first events, HF hospitalization, ischemic events, and major bleeding occurred in 80 (8.1%), 32 (3.2%), and 53 (5.4%) patients, respectively, whereas 823 (83.3%) were in the event-free group. Among patients with a first postdischarge event, major bleeding occurred earliest among the 3 event groups. One-year all-cause mortality after the first event was high across groups (HF hospitalization, 31.5%; ischemic events, 30.4%; major bleeding, 25.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who experienced a first postdischarge event after TAVR, major bleeding occurred earlier than HF hospitalization or ischemic events. Once a first postdischarge event occurred, subsequent all-cause mortality was high across the 3 event groups. These findings suggest that event timing should be considered and careful clinical reassessment may be warranted when a first postdischarge event occurs after TAVR.

articles.title: Heat-waves during teleost's embryogenesis induce epigenetic and gill remodeling responses in rainbow trout.
articles.abstract: The increasing frequency of heat-waves within the current climate change scenarios represents a major emerging stressor for aquatic organisms, yet the adaptive responses at molecular level during early life stages remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of an experimentally induced heat-wave (H-W) during early development of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) on survival, incidence of deformities, gill histomorphology, and epigenetic regulation. Fertilized eggs were reared under control conditions (11-12 °C) until hatching. A subset of hatched embryos was exposed to a 15 days H-W (+6.8 °C maximum anomaly) while others remained at 13 ± 1 °C. Fish exposed to the H-W showed lower survival and a higher incidence of deformities, particularly craniofacial abnormalities, while juvenile growth was similar between groups. Exposure to the H-W did not induce the expression of classical heat shock genes, whereas antioxidant defense genes were differentially regulated, suggesting a redox imbalance response. Using enzymatic methyl-sequencing (EM Seq) at single-base resolution, we identified widespread and context-dependent DNA methylation differences in juvenile gills, with hundreds of differentially methylated regions predominantly in HCG and exhaustive contexts. Functional enrichment analyses revealed significant alterations in pathways related to ion transport and osmoregulation, including IgSF cell adhesion signaling. At the juvenile stage, histological analyses showed increased chloride cell area and filament thickness in exposed fish, consistent with a potential enhancement of osmoregulatory capacity. These findings suggest that early-life thermal stress may result in epigenetic alterations linked to physiological traits, highlighting DNA methylation as a potential mechanism underlying developmental plasticity to climate-related stressors in fish.

articles.title: Doxycycline versus azithromycin in combination with beta-lactams for hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia: A propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Azithromycin plus a beta-lactam is a commonly used empiric regimen for hospitalized community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Concerns about azithromycin resistance and patient-specific safety considerations have increased interest in doxycycline as an alternative; however, comparative effectiveness data for these two regimens remain scarce.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (240 healthcare organizations; data accessed June 14, 2026), we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with CAP between January 2016 and December 2023. Doxycycline plus beta-lactam recipients were compared with azithromycin plus beta-lactam recipients following 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching (11,906 patients per group).

RESULTS: Thirty-day and 90-day all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (HR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.95-1.12; and HR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.98-1.14, respectively), whereas 180-day mortality was modestly but significantly higher in the doxycycline cohort (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.16; p = 0.014). Doxycycline-based therapy was associated with a consistently lower risk of antibiotic escalation at all time points assessed (RR: 0.59-0.65; p < 0.001). The 30-day risk of incident sepsis was significantly higher with doxycycline (RR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.03-1.61; p = 0.024). ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor use, and Clostridioides difficile infection did not differ significantly between the two groups.

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality was detected between doxycycline plus beta-lactams and azithromycin plus beta-lactams. This finding does not establish equivalence or noninferiority. Secondary findings, including 30-day sepsis and 180-day mortality, were exploratory and require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

articles.title: Evaluating the impact of intraoperative neuromonitoring on neurological outcomes and extent of resection in pediatric supratentorial brain tumor surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical resection of pediatric supratentorial brain tumors requires balancing maximal tumor removal with preservation of neurological function. Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) methodologies and indications are well-established in adults but remain understudied in children, whose developing brains pose unique challenges. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the impact IONM on extent of tumor resection and postoperative neurological deficits in pediatric supratentorial brain tumor surgery.

METHODS: A systematic review of studies was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251101609). Studies published between January 1990, and June 2025 were included. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed with I2 statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 41 studies comprising 1,908 pediatric patients were included. The pooled gross total resection (GTR) rate was 76.9% (95% CI: 69.1-82.6) in the monitored group, compared with 52.8% (95% CI: 45.2-60.4) in the unmonitored group. The pooled incidence of postoperative neurological deficits was 15.1% (95% CI: 8.7-22.8) in the monitored group and 23.1% (95% CI: 12.4-38.8) in the unmonitored group. Stratified analyses showed that eloquent cortex involvement was associated with lower GTR rates and higher neurological deficits; however, these associations appeared less pronounced in monitored cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: These descriptive pooled estimates suggest that IONM may be associated with higher GTR rates and lower postoperative neurological deficit rates in pediatric supratentorial brain tumor surgery, particularly in eloquent brain regions. However, because the included studies did not directly compare monitored and unmonitored patients within the same cohorts, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal benefit of IONM. Rather, they provide a foundation for future prospective comparative studies to evaluate the potential impact of IONM and to develop pediatric-specific protocols aimed at preserving long-term neurological function.

articles.title: Trends in utilization of cervical cancer screening and screening-associated services in a multi-organizational research network in Chicago, Illinois, US.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chicago has a high degree of care fragmentation, with multiple large health systems and numerous safety-net systems. Fragmentation may be why the west and south areas of Chicago have high incidences of cervical cancer despite high self-reported screening rates. This study assesses utilization of cervical cancer screening-associated tests and procedures across seven health systems in Chicago between 2012 and 2022.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included females aged 15+ years enrolled in one or more health systems in the CAPriCORN network. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, geolocation, linear mixed-effects model, and Poisson regression. Proportions and trends in utilization by year of test modalities (cytology alone, cytology and human papillomavirus (HPV) test [cotest], HPV test alone, colposcopy, and cervical procedures [cone biopsy, loop electrosurgical excision procedure, and ablation]) were calculated and stratified by Chicago's six geographic zones. The time between screening utilization was compared by age, Chicago zone, and change in health system.

RESULTS: Of 1.20 million in the study cohort, 53.6% had only 1 screening test during the 11-year study period; 22.9% had 2 tests, and 22.9% had 3 or more. Individuals in Chicago who changed health systems between two consecutive screening tests had a longer median interval between tests compared with those who did not change (34 versus 15.4 months).

CONCLUSIONS: Over half of the cohort only had one screening test and may be underscreened. Switching health systems more than doubled the time interval between screening tests compared with patients who remained in the same system.

articles.title: Assessing PPE donning and doffing competence in healthcare workers: A utility-based structured narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare workers remain at high risk of infection when performing personal protective equipment (PPE) donning and doffing, particularly when procedures are executed incorrectly. Despite their importance, assessment methods vary substantially, and few have been evaluated. This review synthesised and examined published hospital-based PPE assessment methods and evaluated their educational utility using van der Vleuten's framework, encompassing validity, reliability, educational impact, acceptability, and cost.

METHOD: A structured narrative review was undertaken to capture heterogeneous study designs related to the topic area. Searches across CINAHL, PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar (February-April 2026) were conducted. Inclusion criteria consisted of empirical studies assessing donning and doffing performance among hospital-based healthcare workers (2014 - 2026). A best-fit framework approach was used to map each assessment method to van der Vleuten's utility framework.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies met inclusion criteria, representing five assessment approaches: checklists (n = 15), video review (n = 6), fluorescent marker contamination (n = 7), MS2 bacteriophage (n = 1), and artificial intelligence-assisted (AI) assessment (n = 1). Checklist-based assessment demonstrated the strongest overall utility due to feasibility, low cost, and broad acceptability, though evidence for validity and reliability was limited. Fluorescent markers provided high educational impact through visible contamination feedback but had reduced ecological validity. Video review and bacteriophage methods showed moderate utility, while AI-assisted approaches offered emerging promise. Methodological inconsistencies across studies limited comparability.

CONCLUSION: No single optimal method exists for assessing PPE competence in hospital settings. Checklists remain the most feasible option for routine infection-control practice but require stronger validation. Multimodal approaches incorporating real-time contamination-feedback tools may enhance educational impact and overall utility.

articles.title: Mitral annular plane systolic excursion as a prognostic marker in critical illness: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac dysfunction is common in critical illness, yet conventional indices such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) may fail to detect early impairment. Mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE), a marker of longitudinal function, may provide prognostic information, but its role in critical illness remains uncertain.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating MAPSE in critically ill adults. Studies were included if MAPSE could be dichotomized using prespecified cutoffs (10 or 12 mm). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included 28-30-day mortality and exploratory measures of cardiac function and organ support. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS and certainty of evidence with GRADE.

RESULTS: Ten observational studies including 1313 patients were analyzed; 414 (31.5%) had reduced MAPSE. Most patients had sepsis or septic shock. Reduced MAPSE was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (37.7% vs 11.7%; RR 4.81; 95% CI 1.28-18.04; p = 0.02; I2 = 70.6%), with consistent effects across both cutoffs (p = 0.111) and adequate information size on trial sequential analysis. Reduced MAPSE was also associated with lower LVEF (MD -13.0%; 95% CI -20.6 to -5.4; p < 0.01; I2 = 94.6%), but not with 28-30-day mortality or exploratory outcomes. Certainty of evidence was low for in-hospital mortality and very low for secondary and exploratory outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Reduced MAPSE was associated with higher in-hospital mortality and may be a bedside marker of myocardial dysfunction. Given the limitations of the available evidence, MAPSE remains a hypothesis-generating marker requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: Lesions and tumours of the cuboid bone: A case series of 16 patients from a tertiary orthopaedic centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bony lesions of the tarsal bones in general and, more specifically, the cuboid are rare and therefore sparsely covered in the existing literature as well as uncommonly seen in radiology. Combined with nonspecific clinical symptoms, they can be challenging to identify and characterise on imaging. Prompt and accurate diagnosis is paramount because the responsible entities include malignant tumours. To our knowledge, this is among the largest case series of cuboid lesions reported.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 16 patients presenting to a tertiary orthopaedic oncology centre with lesions of the cuboid bone was conducted by a musculoskeletal radiologist with over 20 years of experience. Key radiological and demographic features were extracted and compared within and across pathologies to identify common and distinguishing features. Descriptive statistics were calculated (counts, percentages, median and interquartile range); inferential tests were not performed because of the small sample.

RESULTS: A total of 16 patients were included, with 13 females (81%) and 3 males (19%). Median age at diagnosis was 48.5 years (IQR 46.5), with the youngest two patients presenting at 8 years of age. Two lesions (13%) were metastases (one lung and one colon), two (13%) were giant cell tumours (GCT) and two (13%) were Ollier's disease; every other diagnosis occurred once. All radiological features were extracted and compared.

CONCLUSION: Despite their rarity, cuboid lesions do occur and present with a wide range of pathology. This case series compares the key identifying features of such lesions to inform radiologists' future practice when approaching cuboid lesions, supporting appropriate diagnosis.

articles.title: mRNA vaccine encoding multimerized AIV-M2e fused to MHC-II invariant chain motif and Pan-DR epitope confers protection against H9N2 virus in chickens.
articles.abstract: Avian influenza viruses (AIVs) remain a major threat to global poultry health and production. The risk of cross-species transmission among diverse AIV subtypes poses a significant challenge to disease control, underscoring the need for vaccines that provide broad and durable protection. However, existing inactivated and vector-based vaccines provide limited cross-subtype coverage and durable immunity against antigenically diverse AIVs. In contrast, the success of mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 has accelerated vaccine development by enabling rapid, flexible, and scalable vaccine design compared with conventional platforms. We designed an mRNA vaccine encoding four tandem repeats of the conserved influenza M2 ectodomain (4xM2e), fused to the chicken invariant chain (Ii) motif and a 13-amino-acid universal Pan-DR-binding epitope (PADRE). We hypothesized that this design would enhance anti-M2e antibody responses while promoting efficient antigen processing and CD4+ T-helper cell activation, thereby inducing systemic and mucosal immunity against AIV infection in chickens. The mRNA construct was delivered via standard lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), and vaccine efficacy was evaluated following intramuscular (IM) and intranasal (IN) administration. Our data demonstrated a modest increase in systemic and mucosal antibody responses, accompanied by enhanced T-cell proliferation and increased CD4+ and γδ+ T-cell populations. Following challenge with A/turkey/Wisconsin/1/1966/H9N2 virus, vaccinated birds exhibited significantly reduced viral shedding regardless of the route of administration. Histopathological analysis further demonstrated largely preserved pulmonary architecture with minimal inflammation, demonstrating effective maintenance of mucosal barrier integrity. To assess the cross-protective potential and functional activity of anti-M2e antibodies, we demonstrated in vitro heterosubtypic recognition of PR8/H1N1 and confirmed their functional relevance by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Together, our findings demonstrate that the present mRNA vaccine construct, encoding a structurally optimized multimerized M2e protein fused to PADRE and the Ii motif, represents a safe and effective vaccine strategy with the potential to confer broad protective immunity against AIV infection in chickens.

articles.title: Invasive candidiasis caused by Candida tropicalis in an endangered Ryukyu long-furred rat (Diplothrixlegata).
articles.abstract: The Ryukyu long-furred rat (Diplothrix legata) is an endemic rodent species restricted to the Ryukyu Islands, Japan, and is classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List. In 2024, a debilitated rat bearing a wound suggestive of a snakebite was found in the wild on Amami Oshima Island and was admitted to a veterinary hospital, where it subsequently died despite supportive care. Histological and ultrastructural examinations revealed coagulative necrosis with a proliferation of yeast-like fungi in the liver and kidneys. Polymerase chain reaction analysis of lesions identified the causative agent as Candida tropicalis, a dimorphic yeast. The injury and the associated high-stress conditions following transfer to a captive environment and corticosteroid administration for the management of a suspected venomous snakebite may have contributed to immunosuppression, predisposing the animal to opportunistic infections with C. tropicalis. To our knowledge, this is the first report of natural C. tropicalis infection in a member of the Muridae family, and invasive candidiasis caused by C. tropicalis is a potentially fatal opportunistic infection in injured wildlife.

articles.title: Intraoperative hypotension and postoperative acute kidney injury: Evidence and controversies.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains one of the most common serious complications after noncardiac surgery, and intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is consistently identified as a modifiable risk factor. Observational studies show a consistent, roughly dose-response association between IOH, particularly at mean arterial pressures below 60-65 mmHg, and postoperative AKI, with stronger associations in patients with limited renal reserve. Definitions of IOH vary widely, which complicates the comparison of studies and the translation of thresholds into clinical targets. Randomized trials of individualized or higher blood pressure targets have generally not confirmed a kidney-protective benefit, and pooled analyses with trial sequential analysis have not demonstrated that higher targets reduce AKI. This narrative review examines how IOH definitions evolved, summarizes the conflicting intervention evidence, and assesses the controversies that shape current practice. The review concludes that avoiding severe and sustained hypotension remains reasonable, whereas current randomized trial evidence does not support a general kidney-protective benefit of higher or individualized blood pressure targets. This conclusion is provisional and is tempered by the methodologic and causal uncertainties.

articles.title: Trends and disparities in sepsis-related mortality among adults with hypertension in the United States, 1999-2025: A CDC WONDER analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis coexisting with hypertension imposes a substantial healthcare burden in the United States, yet its longitudinal mortality trends and disparities remain poorly documented. This study established mortality trends and identified high-risk populations over 27 years of surveillance.

METHODS: The CDC WONDER database was searched for sepsis-related deaths among hypertensive patients between 1999 and 2025. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 population, overall and by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, and urbanization level. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate the annual percent change (APC).

RESULTS: Of 429,656 deaths, 53.5% occurred in women, 76.4% in hospitals, and approximately 60% in adults aged 75 years and older. Crude mortality rates rose steeply across age strata, from 1.74 per 100,000 at 45-54 years to 13.28 at 65-74 years, 32.62 at 75-84 years, and 83.31 at 85 years and older; age-adjusted rates are not applicable to age strata or to place of death, which are reported as crude rates and counts, respectively (Table 1). The overall AAMR rose from 2.0 (95% CI 1.9-2.0) in 1999 to 6.2 (95% CI 6.1-6.2) in 2025 (cumulative AAMR 4.3), through an initial surge (1999-2001; APC 24.82; P < 0.000001), a plateau to 2018 (APC 1.20; P = 0.064), a pandemic-related rise (2018-2021; APC 16.94; P < 0.000001), and a decline thereafter (2021-2025; APC -3.39; P = 0.010). Cumulative AAMR was higher in men than in women (4.7 vs. 4.0; 2025 rates 7.1 vs. 5.4). By race and ethnicity, cumulative AAMR was highest in non-Hispanic (NH) Black adults (9.5), followed by Hispanic and NH American Indian or Alaska Native adults (both 5.5), NH Asian or Pacific Islander adults (3.8), and NH White adults (3.6); Hispanic adults showed a single uninterrupted increase (APC 2.49; P < 0.000001), unlike the segmented trajectories of all other groups. Regionally, cumulative AAMR was highest in the South (5.0), followed by the West (4.2), Northeast (4.0), and Midwest (3.4). Nonmetropolitan AAMR (4.4) exceeded metropolitan AAMR (4.3), having overtaken it at mid-study. State-level rates varied nearly eight-fold, from 1.48 (Maine) to 11.82 (Oklahoma). All segment trends were statistically significant (P < 0.05) except the plateau or stable-period segments in each stratum and the post-2021 changes among NH Black adults and in the metropolitan and Midwest strata; segment-level APCs with 95% CIs and P values for every variable are provided in Supplementary Table 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Sepsis-related mortality among hypertensive adults rose markedly from 1999 to 2025, following a nonlinear, pandemic-amplified trajectory that fell disproportionately on older adults, non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic populations, the South, and rural areas. Closing these persistent, place-based disparities will require coordinated clinical and public health action.

articles.title: To probe or not to probe - Inappropriate urinary catheterization in the emergency department: Epidemiology, indications, and the potential impact of bladder ultrasound.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indwelling urinary catheterization is a common invasive procedure performed in emergency departments (EDs), yet inappropriateness rates in this setting generally exceed those observed in medical and surgical wards, ranging from 26% to 72% in published series. Inappropriate catheterization contributes to a substantial burden of potentially preventable catheter-associated urinary tract infections and non-infectious complications.

AIM: This narrative review examines the epidemiology of urinary catheter misuse in EDs, recalls the clinical indications defined by reference guidelines, and discusses the role of interventions and bladder ultrasound, performed with automated scanners or point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), in catheterization decision-making.

METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists and inclusion of key guidelines regardless of publication date.

FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS: Interventions combining education with decision-support tools have been associated with less inappropriate catheterization. Bladder ultrasound, while valuable for confirming functionally suspected retention, may promote volume-based catheterization decisions at the expense of functional clinical reasoning, a mechanism not yet formally evaluated in ED-specific studies and identified as a research priority.

articles.title: Mental health experiences of frontline health workers in Sierra Leone: A qualitative study using the Framework Method.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frontline health workers in Sierra Leone have endured pandemics and recurrent infectious and maternal emergencies under chronic under-resourcing, yet the psychological burden they carry remains poorly understood. This study explored how they experience and cope with mental health challenges during and after emergency response.

METHODS: A qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 42 purposively sampled frontline health workers across three districts and eight professional cadres. Sample size was guided by information power rather than saturation. Data were analysed using the Framework Method, indexing all transcripts into a matrix of 42 participants by 17 categories. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research.

RESULTS: Charting produced 17 categories under four themes: the weight of witnessing, stigma and social fracture, coping in the margins, and institutional abandonment. Distress was patterned rather than uniform: accounts of stigma between cadres came mainly from burial and laboratory staff, and accounts of enforced family separation from those deployed away from home. Two categories, both specified in advance, were populated across the whole sample: fear of infection, and absent or token formal support; no participant described employer-provided psychosocial support as adequate and sustained.

CONCLUSIONS: Frontline health workers in Sierra Leone described heavy and largely unaddressed psychological burdens, and asked directly for prompt hazard pay and sustained recognition. Read with the conceptual frameworks and literature, their accounts make a case for building structured psychosocial support into emergency preparedness and universal health coverage planning, as an obligation to the workforce and a condition of its retention.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-based therapies for obesity-associated metabolic complications: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge and a key driver of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic syndrome. Although pharmacological therapies and bariatric surgery have improved both short- and long-term outcomes, with GLP-1 receptor agonists now demonstrating cardiovascular and heart-failure benefits beyond weight reduction (SELECT, SUMMIT), durable and broadly applicable treatments for all patients remain limited. In this context, mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapies, particularly adipose-derived MSCs, have gained increasing attention due to their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties demonstrated in preclinical models. Experimental studies suggest that MSCs influence adipose tissue remodeling, immune cell polarization, insulin sensitivity, and energy homeostasis predominantly through paracrine mechanisms, including the release of cytokines and extracellular vesicles, rather than long-term engraftment or differentiation. However, accumulating evidence indicates that obesity itself profoundly impairs endogenous MSC function through oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, raising important concerns regarding the feasibility of autologous MSC-based approaches in obese individuals. Critically, no randomized controlled trial has evaluated MSC therapy for obesity with weight loss, body composition, or obesity-related clinical outcomes as primary endpoints; the available human evidence addresses glycemic control in type 2 diabetes and metabolic complications. In this review, we summarize current mechanistic insights, preclinical findings, and clinical data on MSC-based interventions for obesity-associated metabolic disorders, while critically discussing key biological, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges. Finally, we define the prerequisites for rational translation - standardized potency assays, obesity-specific early-phase trials with active comparators, objective body-composition endpoints, hemocompatibility testing, and long-term surveillance.

articles.title: Targeting protective renin-angiotensin system pathways in pulmonary emphysema: Preclinical evidence for resolving inflammation and restoring lung homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide and still lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. Current pharmacological treatments primarily alleviate symptoms and reduce exacerbations, but have limited ability to prevent progressive lung destruction or promote tissue repair. Increasing evidence indicates that beyond the classical cardiovascular functions of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), it additionally plays a central role in regulating pulmonary inflammation, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodelling, cellular senescence and endogenous repair mechanisms. Experimental studies have shown that both pharmacological inhibition of the ACE/Ang II/AT1 axis and activation of the protective AT2 receptor and ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas pathways attenuate multiple pathological processes involved in COPD progression. In this review, we comprehensively discuss the current preclinical evidence supporting pharmacological manipulation of the RAS in experimental models of pulmonary emphysema, highlighting the anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-fibrotic, pro-resolutive and regenerative mechanisms associated with these therapeutic strategies. We further discuss emerging evidence indicating that activation of protective RAS pathways not only suppresses inflammation, but also promotes tissue repair through modulating autophagy, inflammasome activation, cellular senescence and endogenous regenerative signalling. These findings collectively position protective RAS modulation as a promising disease-modifying strategy for COPD and provide a strong rationale for future translational and clinical studies aimed at restoring pulmonary homeostasis.

articles.title: Relationship between the executive function on walking motor imagery and actual walking ability in stroke patients: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke walking impairment reflects both motor and higher-order cognitive deficits. We examined whether executive function mediates the association between walking-related motor imagery accuracy and actual walking performance and kinematics in patients with subacute hemiparetic stroke. Thirty inpatients underwent mental chronometry, involving timed imagined and actual maximum 10-m walks, and the discrepancy between the two was expressed as the Index of Walking Performance (IWP), with values near zero indicating high accuracy. Participants were categorized into overestimation and underestimation groups. Executive function was assessed with the Trail Making Test Part B (TMT-B). Walking outcomes included maximum 10-m walking time, the Timed Up and Go test (TUGT), and paretic peak knee flexion during stance and swing phases. Mediation analyses with TMT-B as the mediator were conducted both without covariates and after adjustment for age and position sense. Higher IWP values were associated with longer TMT-B times, slower maximum 10-m walking and TUGT, greater paretic stance-phase, and smaller swing-phase knee flexion. The overestimation group showed slower maximum 10-m walking and smaller swing-phase knee flexion than the underestimation group. Unadjusted models showed full mediation for the TUGT and stance-phase knee flexion, partial mediation for swing-phase knee flexion, and no mediation for the maximum 10-m walking time. After adjustment, these indirect effects were attenuated, and their confidence intervals included zero, whereas associations of IWP and TMT-B with the walking outcomes remained significant. Executive function may therefore contribute to the association between walking motor imagery accuracy and actual walking performance, although its mediating role remains preliminary.

articles.title: Potential Role of the α7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor in Intestinal Morphological and Functional Alterations of Offspring Programmed by Maternal Obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal intestinal morphology and dysbiosis contribute to metabolic disease development. Maternal obesity increases offspring susceptibility to gut dysfunction. The α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR), encoded by Chrna7, is a key mediator of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway and modulates intestinal immunity and cell proliferation. However, the role of cholinergic signaling in offspring intestinal development remains unclear.

METHODS: 5-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were fed a control (SC, 10% fat) or a high-fat diet (HFD, 45% fat) before and during pregnancy and lactation. The small intestines of fetal (e20) offspring were analyzed for inflammatory markers and tight junctions (Claudin-1, Claudin-2, Occludin, Zonula occludens-1). Additional evaluations at weaning (d28) included histomorphometry, intestinal transit and permeability assays, and microbiota analysis. Chrna7⁻/⁻ mice were evaluated for histomorphometry and intestinal permeability.

RESULTS: Maternal HFD disrupted the intestinal morphology and function of offspring, resulting in shorter villi, reduced mucosal thickness and goblet cell proportion, reduced α7nAChR expression, and increased permeability. While male HFD-O exhibited an increased Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, female HFD-O presented a significant reduction in Akkermansia and Verrucomicrobiota abundance, though they displayed an early adaptive response in tight junction expression at e20. Chrna7⁻/⁻ mice exhibited similar intestinal morphological alterations, recapitulating most features observed in offspring of HFD-fed dams.

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal HFD programs a vulnerable intestinal phenotype in offspring characterized by significant structural and moderate functional and microbiota reprogramming. The phenotypic similarities between HFD-O and Chrna7-/- suggest a potential involvement of this receptor in shaping offspring gut health, offering potential targets to prevent diet-induced intestinal dysfunctions.

articles.title: The secret life of dialysis catheters: A qualitative study of intensive care nurses' experiences of managing dialysis catheters.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Australian intensive care units (ICUs), approximately 9000 patients require renal replacement therapy annually for acute kidney injury. This requires a large-bore dialysis catheter to facilitate effective extracorporeal blood flow. However, these catheters have the highest failure rate of all central venous catheters used in ICU at 7-20%. While catheter insertion and renal replacement therapy guidance is evidence-based, there is limited guidance for post-insertion catheter care and troubleshooting.

OBJECTIVE: To explore ICU nurses' experiences managing dialysis catheters, and how existing policies and bedside practices influence nurses' decision-making.

METHODS: Qualitative, descriptive design. Registered nurses with experience caring for patients undergoing dialysis were recruited between November 2024 and January 2025. Data were collected through small group, semi-structured interviews and analysed using inductive content analysis.

FINDINGS: Eighteen clinicians participated across three focus groups, with a mean of 10.6 years' experience in dialysis catheter care. Two themes were identified: (1) Troubleshooting is complex, characterised by reliance on experiential knowledge, time sensitive decision-making, and balancing risk against benefit; and (2) The hidden cost, reflecting the stress, unrecognised labour and financial burden associated with troubleshooting catheter dysfunction.

CONCLUSION: The absence of evidence-based guidance to manage troubleshooting and catheter dysfunction places substantial burden on ICU nurses. Evidence-based troubleshooting decision tools may have the potential to improve dialysis efficiency, reduce healthcare-associated risks and workforce stress.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Effective post-insertion management of dialysis catheters requires clear, evidence-informed policy, particularly regarding safe, appropriate troubleshooting techniques. A structured hierarchy of interventions may enable efficient clinician response to catheter dysfunction and improve post-insertion care and reduce complications. Targeted education and skills training are essential to strengthen clinical judgement in time-critical situations. Improved interdisciplinary communication is also needed to ensure medical teams better understand the workload and clinical risks associated with managing dialysis catheters.

articles.title: The mediating role of depression in the association between social participation and frailty among older adults with PSCI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the relationships among depressive symptoms, social participation, and frailty in older adults with post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), and to examine the potential mediating role of depressive symptoms in the association between social participation and frailty.

METHODS: Convenience sampling was used to recruit older adults with PSCI from a tertiary grade-A hospital in Hebei Province, China, between August and November 2024. A comprehensive survey was conducted using a general information questionnaire, the 5-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-5), the Tilburg Frailty Indicator, and the Impact on Participation and Autonomy questionnaire. Mediation analysis was performed using the PROCESS macro in SPSS, and significance was tested using the Bootstrap method.

RESULTS: A total of 262 questionnaires were distributed, of which 6 were excluded because of errors, omissions, or missing data. The final sample consisted of 256 valid questionnaires, yielding an effective response rate of 97.71%. Frailty among older adults with PSCI was positively correlated with depressive symptoms (r = 0.49, P < 0.01) and social participation scores (r = 0.60, P < 0.01). Social participation scores were also positively correlated with depressive symptoms (r = 0.48, P < 0.01). Additionally, depressive symptoms played a significant mediating role in the association between social participation and frailty, accounting for 20.96% of the total effect.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that social participation is directly and indirectly associated with frailty among older adults with PSCI, with depressive symptoms serving as an important mediating pathway.

articles.title: Poorer bereavement outcomes among companion animal owners are associated with unexpected death or describing the pet as a partner or soulmate.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether circumstances surrounding companion animal death and the owner-companion animal relationship were associated with bereavement outcomes.

METHODS: Cross-sectional survey data from 4,902 bereaved companion animal owners were analyzed. Multivariable regression models examined associations of cause of death, euthanasia, presence at death, and owner-reported relationship with the companion animal with grief severity, severe depression, anxiety/insomnia, social dysfunction, and somatic symptoms, adjusting for pet attachment and demographic and loss-related characteristics. Model sample sizes ranged from 4,099 to 4,758.

RESULTS: Unexpected death, compared with natural or anticipated death, was associated with greater grief (unstandardized regression coefficient [B] = 2.49; 95% CI, 1.81 to 3.18), severe depression (B = 1.16; 95% CI, 0.59 to 1.73), anxiety/insomnia (B = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.32 to 1.35), social dysfunction (B = 0.97; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.37), and somatic symptoms (B = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.94). Describing the companion animal as a partner or soulmate versus a best friend was also associated with poorer outcomes across all 5 domains (B = 0.60 to 1.26). Euthanasia was associated with lower grief (B = -0.95; 95% CI, -1.46 to -0.44) and depression (B = -0.76; 95% CI, -1.19 to -0.32). Presence at death was not associated with any outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected death and a partner/soulmate relationship were consistently associated with poorer bereavement outcomes.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Veterinary practices should strive to ensure that owners experiencing an unexpected loss receive the same opportunities for follow-up and bereavement support as those whose companion animals undergo euthanasia.

articles.title: Open-Source, High-Speed and High-Resolution Data Acquisition Platform for Biopotential Recordings and Neural EIT applications.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Biopotential measurement devices, such as EEG, ECG, and EMG recorders, are available in low-cost, open-source implementations with standard specifications. However, high-end systems remain expensive and predominantly proprietary, limiting accessibility and customization by research laboratories. In addition, neurophysiology techniques such as bioimpedance-based Fast Neural Electrical Impedance Tomography (FN-EIT) also rely on these systems for data acquisition. This work aimed to develop an open-source biopotential recording system using off-the-shelf components that achieves performance comparable to high-end devices.

APPROACH: We designed our system to provide simultaneous sampling over 32 channels, 24-bit resolution, 10 kHz bandwidth, 50 kHz sampling rate, and battery-powered operation while reducing cost by two orders of magnitude. System performance was evaluated comparatively against a reference device. Initial validation involved benchtop recordings in saline solution and standard non-invasive biopotential measurements (ECG and EMG). Further in-vivo validation was performed by recording evoked electrophysiological responses and FN-EIT traces from the sciatic nerve of a rat during tibial branch stimulation.

MAIN RESULTS: EMG recordings showed comparable RMS peak amplitudes (814±153 µV vs. 897±113µV, p=0.07), while ECG-derived heart rates closely matched between systems (64.8±4.0 bpm vs. 65.1±3.1bpm, p=0.54). During in-vivo recordings, compound action potentials exhibited comparable amplitudes and morphology (129±26 mV vs 128±25 mV, P=0.15). FN-EIT recordings showed strongly correlated baseline voltages (R>0.93, P=0.11), sub-microvolt noise levels (0.83±0.36µV vs. 0.42±0.25µV, p<0.05), and comparable impedance variations (0.006±0.002% vs 0.005±0.003, P>0.05). FN-EIT images of functional activity recorded with the novel device closely matched reference ones, exhibiting a 98.5% overlap in activated area.

SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed open-source device has the potential to broaden research access to customizable, high-specification data acquisition hardware and facilitate wider adoption of specialized neural recording techniques such as FN-EIT.

articles.title: Exploring the potential of DL for Chagas disease screening using chest x-rays.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chagas disease remains an important public health problem, particularly in Latin America, where chronic infection frequently leads to cardiac involvement and associated structural changes. Recent advances in deep learning (DL) have enabled automated image analysis of chest X-ray (CXR) in several clinical applications, yet little is known about its applicability to Chagas disease. However, the potential of these methods for Chagas disease screening remains largely unexplored.

APPROACH: In this study, we investigate the feasibility of DL models to identify patients with Chagas disease from CXR images. A private dataset of CXRs was used to train and evaluate several convolutional neural network architectures.

MAIN RESULTS: Among the evaluated models, EfficientNet-B4 achieved the best overall performance metrics, with accuracy of 0.655 ± 0.026, precision of 0.653 ± 0.041, recall of 0.700 ± 0.157, F1-score of 0.664 ± 0.076, and AUC of 0.727 ± 0.015.

SIGNIFICANCE: These results indicate that CXRs contain subtle imaging features associated with chronic Chagas disease that can be partially captured by DL models, although the overall discriminative performance remains moderate. While CXR-based DL models are unlikely to serve as a standalone diagnostic tool, they may have potential as complementary screening or triage tools, particularly in settings where chest radiographs are routinely acquired and access to specialized diagnostic testing is limited.. These findings highlight both the feasibility and the limitations of applying artificial intelligence to support Chagas disease screening using routinely acquired radiographic images.

articles.title: Signaling pathways of macrophages during Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and potential anti-tuberculosis therapeutic targets.
articles.abstract: The innate immune response is the body's first line of defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. Innate immune cells, macrophages and associated signaling pathways play an important immune regulatory role during Mtb infection. The different phenotypes of macrophages with the transition between them are associated with the pathological process of tuberculosis. It is therefore important to study the regulatory mechanism of macrophage signaling pathways in specific pathological contexts. Mtb strategically manipulates macrophage signaling pathways to steal host cell machinery and evade immune recognition. In this review, we systematically summarize the important signaling pathways implicated in the interaction between macrophages and the Mtb pathogen. Further, we summarize how the various pattern recognition receptor-regulated signaling pathways and the major signaling transduction pathways and immune effector mechanisms are orchestrated during Mtb infection. Additionally, we analyze the regulatory roles of non-coding RNAs in these pathways, involving both epigenetic and metabolic machinery. Lastly, we highlight promising host-directed therapeutic strategies aimed at augmenting anti-tuberculosis immune responses by integrating recent advances in clinical immunotherapy, which might help circumvent Mtb drug resistance and enhance immunotherapy.

articles.title: Exogenous resolvin D2 alleviates diabetic neuropathic pain by regulating microglial fatty acid metabolism and phenotypic polarization.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP) is a common and intractable complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Distinct from traditional NF-κB or MAPK inflammatory pathways, resolvin D2 (RvD2) alleviates DNP through metabolic reprogramming-a novel mechanism that remains largely unexplored. Untargeted metabolomics analysis of the spinal cord from DNP model mice and RvD2-treated mice revealed significant alterations in fatty acid oxidation (FAO)-related metabolites between the two groups. Functionally, RvD2 effectively alleviated hyperalgesia in DNP mice and ameliorated the FAO dysfunction associated with a pro-inflammatory microglial state. Mechanistically, RvD2 upregulated the expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) and carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1a (CPT1a), thereby activating the PPARα/CPT1a axis to enhance FAO. This metabolic shift consequently augmented ATP production, suppressed reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and diminished succinate accumulation, which in turn blocked hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α)-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling. Concurrently, RvD2 elevated the acetyl-CoA pool, promoting histone acetylation and chromatin accessibility at the promoters of pro-resolving polarization-related genes, which drove microglia toward a pro-resolving phenotype. Notably, the specific CPT1a inhibitor etomoxir partially reversed these protective effects of RvD2. In conclusion, RvD2 alleviates DNP by driving microglial pro-resolving polarization through a CPT1a-mediated metabolic-epigenetic axis, providing a promising therapeutic target and a potent candidate agent for the clinical management of DNP.

articles.title: From compliance to measurable safety: Multisite benchmarking of radioprotection performance in private radiotherapy facilities in Morocco.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy delivers intentional high-dose exposures with narrow therapeutic margins; therefore, radioprotection must function as a measurable safety system spanning governance, engineered controls, occupational monitoring, and patient safety barriers. Multicentre key performance indicator (KPI)-based benchmarking remains limited in Morocco, particularly within the private sector.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, multisite benchmarking study across ten private radiotherapy centres in Morocco. A structured radioprotection framework was developed using a systems-based, risk-informed approach aligned with international safety and modern radiotherapy quality management principles. Centre-level KPIs were defined a priori in a data dictionary (unit, reference period, evidence sources) and collected via a standardised questionnaire supported by documentary verification. KPIs covered governance and training, occupational protection, incident learning and improvement systems, patient safety barriers and verification steps, machine and patient-specific quality assurance (QA), and high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy preparedness (where applicable). Descriptive statistics were reported as medians, interquartile ranges, and ranges.

RESULTS: Governance maturity was variable: 80% of centres reported a designated Radiation Protection Officer (RPO) and 70% a documented radiation protection (RP) programme/local rules; 30% reported an International Organization for Standardization (ISO)-certified or otherwise accredited quality management system (QMS) and 20% had conducted a safety-culture survey within the last two years. Training coverage was moderate-to-high (median 82.5%) with induction within 30 days at 77.5%. Patient time-out checklists were universal (100%), while pretreatment plan/chart review and second contour checks were reported by 60% each; in-vivo dosimetry availability was limited (30%). Independent monitor unit (MU)/dose check coverage was high (median 97.5%), whereas patient-specific QA coverage and machine QA adherence showed wider dispersion (medians 87.5% and 82.5%, respectively). Incident learning remained heterogeneous: a formal reporting system was present in 60%, with median 9.5 reports/year and high near-miss share (median 62.5%); root-cause analysis (RCA) completion and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) timeliness varied (median 65% and 65 days). Occupational dosimetry compliance was generally high (median 93.5%), with higher mean effective dose in radiotherapy technologists (RTTs) than physicists and radiation oncologists.

CONCLUSION: KPI benchmarking across ten private Moroccan centres identified strong frontline safety practices (time-out, MU checks, high dosimetry compliance) alongside gaps in structured governance maturity (accredited QMS, safety culture measurement), incident learning capability, and selected high-reliability QA barriers. These findings support targeted, data-driven improvement plans that are practical for RTT-led implementation and compatible with evolving national safety expectations.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Radiotherapy must follow strict safety measures because it uses high doses of radiation to treat cancer. This study reviewed safety practices at ten private radiotherapy centres in Morocco using a standard set of quality and safety measures. This study found that routine safety checks and staff radiation monitoring were generally strong, but some centres had fewer systems for quality management, incident learning, and quality assurance. This matters because improving these areas can help make cancer treatment safer for patients and staff.

articles.title: Migraine burden and occupational impact among corporate employees attending neurology clinics in Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
articles.journal: International journal of occupational safety and ergonomics : JOSE
articles.abstract: Objectives. Migraine is a leading cause of disability worldwide, yet remains underdiagnosed in low and middle-income countries. This study assessed the clinical features, triggers, management patterns and occupational impact of neurologist-diagnosed migraine among corporate employees in Skardu, Pakistan. Methods. A cross-sectional study of adult corporate employees with neurologist-confirmed migraine was conducted at neurology outpatient clinics in Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan. Data were collected via a validated questionnaire on demographics, clinical features, triggers, occupational impact and management. Non-parametric tests and multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of high occupational impact, reported as adjusted odds ratios and p values. Results. Most participants were female (72.4%) and aged 26-35 years (43.0%), with migraine without aura being the most common (40.6%). The mean migraine burden was high (58.9 ± 13.6) and varied significantly by gender, age and management. Poor management (34.7%) and reliance on Over-the-Counter (OTC) analgesics (65.3%) were common. Work impact was substantial, with 44% reporting moderate-to-severe absenteeism and 55% presenteeism. High occupational impact was independently predicted by higher migraine burden, frequent attacks (>6/month), stress, sleep deprivation, environmental stressors, poor management and information technology-sector employment. Conclusion. Among corporate employees in Skardu, migraine causes significant absenteeism and workplace impairment; addressing triggers and improving specialist care can reduce disability.

articles.title: When Source Control Is Not Enough: Bilateral Adrenal Hemorrhage After Group A Streptococcal Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection.
articles.abstract: Refractory septic shock following adequate surgical source control presents a major clinical challenge. While persistent vasopressor dependence in necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTI) is frequently attributed to ongoing tissue necrosis or overwhelming cytokine release, acute primary adrenal failure due to Waterhouse-Friderichsen Syndrome (WFS) represents an underrecognized, reversible etiology. We report a 41-year-old male who developed fulminant right upper extremity Group A Streptococcus (GAS) necrotizing fasciitis requiring emergent forequarter amputation. Despite definitive source control, targeted antitoxin antimicrobial therapy, and guideline-directed resuscitation, he experienced persistent vasopressor-dependent shock. On postoperative day 5, CT imaging revealed new-onset bilateral adrenal hemorrhage. The initiation of stress-dose hydrocortisone led to rapid hemodynamic stabilization and successful recovery. Surgeons must maintain a high index of suspicion for acute adrenal crisis in postoperative ICU patients with refractory shock despite source control, rather than solely driven by ongoing sepsis.

articles.title: Delayed incidental dural tears from subfascial drains after spine surgery: illustrative cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Placement of a subfascial drain following open spine surgery is common practice to mitigate postoperative complications, including epidural hematoma, seroma formation, surgical site infection, and wound dehiscence. The authors present 3 cases in which subfascial Hemovac drains were associated with postoperative durotomy following otherwise uncomplicated lumbar surgeries.

OBSERVATIONS: Three patients who underwent single-level lumbar surgery requiring postoperative drain placement subsequently developed CSF leaks, presumed to be secondary to intracorporeal drain movement consistent with the Euler buckling theory.

LESSONS: In patients undergoing uncomplicated single-level lumbar spine surgery, consideration should be given to the use of a silicone Jackson-Pratt drain rather than a compression-resistant polyvinyl chloride Hemovac drain. In a small surgical bed, a shorter and more compliant drain may be sufficient, whereas a stiff drain may act as a trocar. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE2640.

articles.title: Be aware of the tuft of hair: traumatic lumbar intradural hematoma following spinal anesthesia in a case of occult spinal dysraphism. Illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal intradural hematoma is a rare but potentially devastating complication of spinal anesthesia. Known risk factors include anticoagulation, coagulopathies, spinal trauma, tumors, infections, and congenital spinal anomalies.

OBSERVATIONS: The authors report the case of a 27-year-old postpartum female who developed acute bilateral lower limb weakness 3 days post-cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. On examination, she had a tuft of hair in the midline of the low back. MRI of the whole spine revealed a lumbosacral intradural hematoma with incidental findings of spinal dysraphism-diastematomyelia and tethering of the spinal cord. Emergency surgical evacuation was performed, but the patient was left with persistent neurological deficits.

LESSONS: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion and performing a thorough preanesthetic spinal evaluation when cutaneous stigmata suggestive of occult spinal dysraphism are present. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26343.

articles.title: Acute visual deterioration following endoscopic transsphenoidal resection of a pituitary adenoma secondary to a de novo cyst of normal pituitary origin: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pituitary adenomas (PAs) are common benign intracranial neoplasms. Transsphenoidal resection is the standard of care for symptomatic tumors, with surgical complications including CSF leakage, infection, hormonal disturbances, and postoperative hematomas leading to visual decline. Rapid postoperative cyst development leading to acute visual deterioration is a rare but potentially significant complication.

OBSERVATIONS: A 63-year-old female with headaches and pulsatile tinnitus presented with a large PA compressing the optic apparatus. Transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) via an endoscopic endonasal approach was performed. On postoperative day 6, the patient experienced rapid onset of bitemporal hemianopsia, and imaging revealed a new suprasellar cystic lesion. The patient underwent emergency craniotomy for cyst resection, with pathological analysis demonstrating a nonneoplastic anterior pituitary gland. A systematic literature review of rapid cyst formation following TSS yielded only 1 article for inclusion. No cases of a postoperative cyst of normal pituitary gland origin were identified.

LESSONS: Visual decline following TSS is typically due to a sellar/suprasellar hematoma, abscess, or CSF accumulation. Few reports attribute acute postoperative visual deterioration to the development of a secondary pituitary mass, typically due to PA recurrence or formation of a suprasellar cyst. Emergency cyst resection via a transcranial approach resulted in restoration of vision and preservation of pituitary function, supporting aggressive surgical management. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26459.

articles.title: Automation of sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and vitrification in IVF: insights from a proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can key embryological procedures, including sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and blastocyst vitrification, be automated?

SUMMARY ANSWER: Individual automated systems enabling sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and embryo vitrification demonstrated feasibility in a small proof-of-concept study.

WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Automated systems for specific IVF procedures have shown promise, with recent reports of successful births following automated gamete isolation and ICSI.

STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Prospective proof-of-concept study evaluating five automated systems nicknamed 'Pearls'. Each system automated one of the following procedures: sperm preparation via swim-up (Pearl 1-SU); sperm preparation by a dish-based approach called horizontal swim-out (Pearl 1-HSO), oocyte retrieval, and denudation (Pearl 2); sperm selection and laser immobilization and piezo-ICSI (Pearl 3); and blastocyst vitrification (Pearl 5). The study enrolled patients undergoing treatment at Hope IVF, Guadalajara, Mexico, between October 2023 and October 2024, with data collection on pregnancy outcomes being completed in October 2025.

PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Thirty-two patients or oocyte donors each underwent a single egg retrieval following minimal or mild ovarian stimulation. One patient was excluded from the study due to poor ovarian response. Oocytes were prospectively allocated to treatment with a single automated system: Pearl 1-SU (n = 20), Pearl 1-HSO (n = 37), Pearl 2 (n = 34), Pearl 3 (n = 57), with sibling oocytes treated manually per standard protocol. In the case of the automated vitrification system (Pearl 5), sibling blastocysts produced following manual ICSI were assigned to either manual or automated (n = 10) vitrification.

MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Pearl 1-SU and Pearl 1-HSO automated sperm preparation systems achieved fertilization rates of 90% (18/20) and 73% (27/37), and sibling oocytes injected with manually prepared sperm achieved 60% (6/10) and 75% (18/24) fertilization. Usable blastocyst rates were 55.5% (10/18) and 70.4% (19/27) for the automated systems, and 50% (3/6) and 66.7% (12/18) for manual preparation. Pearl 2 automated oocyte retrieval and denudation resulted in a fertilization rate of 79.4% (27/34) and a usable blastocyst rate of 48.1% (13/27); manual procedures achieved 66.7% (26/39) and 76.9% (20/26) fertilization and blastocyst formation rates, respectively. Pearl 3 automated ICSI resulted in a fertilization rate of 59.6% (34/57), while this rate in sibling oocytes injected manually was 80% (36/45). Usable blastocyst formation rates were 58.8% (20/34) for automated and 61.1% (22/36) for manual ICSI. Thirty-five single embryo transfers from the automation group resulted in 16 clinical pregnancies and 16 live births in 26 patients (Pearl 1-SU = 3/6; Pearl 1-HSO = 4/7; Pearl 2 = 4/7; Pearl 3 = 4/13; Pearl 5 = 1/2). Two extremely preterm deliveries in the Pearl 1 group, associated with severe pre-eclampsia and vaginal/urinary infection, respectively, led to neonatal and infant deaths. No transfers involved embryos from the manual group for Pearl 1. One embryo transfer from the manual group of Pearl 2 resulted in a negative pregnancy. In the Pearl 3 manual group, four single blastocyst transfers in four patients resulted in four live births; in the Pearl 5 manual control group, three transfers in three patients resulted in two negative pregnancy results and one early pregnancy loss.

LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: The small sample size and pilot design of this study do not allow statistical comparisons between sibling oocytes from automated and manual treatment groups. The automated systems did not achieve complete autonomy, and several tasks required direct operator intervention or execution through digital control. Pearl 5 encountered technical limitations that require further development before additional clinical evaluation. Although the two extremely preterm births that led to neonatal and infant deaths occurred in the context of clear obstetric complications, they compel collection and analysis of extensive technical and biological data from the automated systems in future studies and close monitoring of all pregnancies and births resulting from these novel procedures.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: These results show the feasibility of integrating individual automated systems into an IVF laboratory as experimental standalone tools, allowing a stepwise evaluation. The modular approach, once shown to be efficacious, may provide a practical pathway toward broader laboratory automation and enable laboratories to address specific bottlenecks and standardize operations.

FUNDING: The study was sponsored by Conceivable Life Sciences, New York, NY, USA.

DISCLOSURES: A.C.-B. is an employee, shareholder, and company officer at Conceivable Life Sciences and a shareholder in IVF 2.0 and Hope IVF Mexico. A.V.A. has no conflicts of interest to declare. G.M.-R. is a stock option holder in Conceivable Life Sciences and has received consulting fees from Conceivable Life Sciences and IVF 2.0. A.F.-S.F. is an employee and stock option holder at Conceivable Life Sciences. E.H.-M. is an employee and stock option holder at Conceivable Life Sciences. A.Á.L. is an employee and stock option holder at Conceivable Life Sciences. D.J.S.-G. has no conflicts of interest to declare. N.C.-B. is a stock option holder in Conceivable Life Sciences and has received consulting fees from the company; he is also an employee, shareholder, and company officer at Embryotools. A.M. is a shareholder and company officer at Conceivable Life Sciences and holds shares in TMRW Life Sciences. M.A. is a stock option holder at Conceivable Life Sciences and has received consulting fees and travel support from the company; she has also received consulting fees from TMRW Life Sciences.
