G.S. is an employee and stock option holder at Conceivable Life Sciences. J.C. is an employee, shareholder, stock option holder, and company officer at Conceivable Life Sciences. Furthermore, several authors declare inventorship on multiple US patents and pending applications relating to IVF automation technology: 12,349,940 B2 (automated oocyte denudation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., A.Á.L., A.M., J.C.), 12,245,793 B2 (robotic handling systems; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., E.H.-M., A.M., J.C.), 12,178,475 B1 (automated sperm preparation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., A.M., G.S., J.C.), 12,180,441 B1 (laboratory workflow automation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.M., J.C.), 12,268,418 B2 (automated oocyte preparation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., A.Á.L., N.C.-B., A.M., J.C.), 12,310,625 B2 (automated ICSI; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., E.H.-M., N.C.-B., A.M., J.C.), 12,253,516 B2 (optical systems for IVF automation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., A.M.), 12,226,125 B2 (automated vitrification; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., A.F.-S.F., N.C.-B., A.M., G.S., J.C.), and 12,478,405 B2 (automated dish-based sperm preparation; A.C.-B., G.M.-R., N.C.-B., J.C.). Pending applications cover automated dish preparation technology (A.C.-B., G.M.-R., N.C.-B., M.A., A.M., J.C.), automated oocyte denudation (A.C.-B., G.M.-R., N.C.-B., J.C.), automated vitrification systems (A.C.-B., E.H.-M., N.C.-B., A.M., J.C.), and cumulus-oocyte complex detection technology (A.C.-B., G.M.-R., J.C.).

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06074835 (ClinicalTrials.gov, 4 October 2023).

articles.title: Pharmacy students' perception of OSCE exam clinical skills and competencies assessment.
articles.journal: The International journal of pharmacy practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate pharmacy students' perceptions of Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) content, assessment, logistics, and formative and summative components, and to identify factors associated with perceived clinical competency development following OSCE participation.

METHODS: A cross-sectional census study was conducted among pharmacy students at Zarqa University, Jordan (n = 123). Data were collected online using Microsoft Teams and analyzed using descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, correlation analyses, and multiple linear regression.

KEY FINDINGS: Most students reported that OSCE cases were aligned with taught content (77.3%) and effectively assessed communication (75.6%), clinical skills (76.4%), and applied knowledge (70.1%). The OSCE was perceived as superior to written examinations for evaluating clinical skills (79.7%) and as a fair measure of clinical competence (77.3%); however, it was also viewed as more stressful (58.5%) and challenging to prepare for (61.0%). Formative assessment activities were perceived positively and were associated with enhanced confidence, motivation, and preparedness. Students reported improvements across multiple professional competencies, particularly in communication, problem-solving, medication review, and collaborative practice. Perceived competency gains were strongly associated with formative assessment perceptions (r = 0.739, P < .001) and moderately associated with summative assessment attitudes (r = 0.626, P < .001), and both significantly predicted perceived competency development (R2 = 0.662, P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: OSCEs were perceived positively and were associated with substantial perceived competency development among pharmacy students. Structured formative assessment emerged as a key contributor to perceived competence gains, supporting the integration of OSCEs within undergraduate pharmacy curricula, even in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Understanding State Public Health Agency Structure and Governance as They Relate to Workforce Recruitment Systems.
articles.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to examine how state public health agency governance and structure relate to recruitment systems such as hiring laws, recruitment barriers, and workforce practices.

DESIGN: This cross-sectional study uses secondary data from the 2022 Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO) Profile Survey and the 2023 Public Health Hiring Laws Dataset. Descriptive statistics and bivariate analyses were conducted to assess relationships between governance, structure, and recruitment systems.

SETTING: State public health agencies in the United States.

PARTICIPANTS: 50 US state health departments.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Associations between governance type (centralized, decentralized, mixed) and agency structure (free-standing vs. umbrella) with statutory hiring requirements, reported recruitment barriers, adoption of workplace practices, and distribution of responsibility for human resource (HR) functions.

RESULTS: Governance and agency structure were not significantly associated with statutory hiring requirements, including use of hiring lists, civil service examinations, or merit-based criteria. Most reported recruitment barriers did not vary by governance or structure. One exception was difficulty advertising or engaging qualified applicants, which was reported more frequently among decentralized states compared with mixed governance states. Agency structure was associated with certain workforce practices: free-standing agencies were more likely than umbrella agencies to report employee recognition programs and physical wellness programs. Responsibility for HR functions was often shared between public health agencies and centralized administrative entities, with notable ambiguity in benefits administration, occupational health and safety, and labor relations. Agencies in which public health retained sole responsibility for selected HR functions were also more likely to report implementation of workforce development and employee engagement practices.

CONCLUSIONS: Governance and agency structure were largely not associated with recruitment-related factors. However, variation in HR authority and workplace practices suggests organizational arrangements may shape workforce management. Strengthening the public health workforce may require aligning HR authority with workforce priorities alongside improvements to administrative infrastructure and hiring systems.

articles.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a transformer-based model for generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis by modeling long-range temporal dependencies and complex relationships in heterogeneous EHR data and to examine its interpretability.

METHODS: We developed the Biomarker-Aware Transformer for AKI (BAT-AKI), which integrates multidimensional embeddings capturing temporal dynamics, textual descriptions, hierarchical ontology structures, and semantic relationships in EHRs. To enhance sensitivity to AKI-related biomarker fluctuations, BAT-AKI combines masked language modeling with a novel biomarker abnormality-aware pretraining task. The model was pretrained and fine-tuned for 4 tasks: AKI onset, early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality. Pretraining and internal validation used data from the National Patient-Centered Clinical Research Network (PCORnet) site, with external validation across 3 additional sites.

RESULTS: BAT-AKI achieved the strongest overall discrimination, outperforming baseline models in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) on most tasks. For AKI onset prediction, it achieved an AUROC of 0.8549 (95% CI 0.8433-0.8658) and an AUPRC of 0.6041 (95% CI 0.5786-0.6292), exceeding the second-best baseline by 2.8% in AUROC and 8.1% in AUPRC. Across prognostic tasks, BAT-AKI achieved AUROCs of 0.6006 (95% CI 0.5703-0.6318), 0.6080 (95% CI 0.5745-0.6397), and 0.8017 (95% CI 0.7708-0.8311) and AUPRCs of 0.7036 (95% CI 0.6690-0.7388), 0.7417 (95% CI 0.7082-0.7765), and 0.5063 (95% CI 0.4422-0.5684) for early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality, respectively, corresponding to relative gains of 2.4% to 6% in AUROC and 3.7% to 4.1% in AUPRC over the second-best baseline. Performance remained stable across external cohorts, with AKI onset AUROCs ranging from 0.7754 (95% CI 0.7677-0.7827) to 0.7989 (95% CI 0.7885-0.8092) and AUPRCs ranging from 0.4777 (95% CI 0.4631-0.4924) to 0.5687 (95% CI 0.5495-0.5871), corresponding to relative improvements of 3.7% to 5.3% in AUROC and 16.8% to 25.3% in AUPRC over the transformer baseline. In a low-resource setting using only 2% of the fine-tuning data, BAT-AKI achieved an AUROC of 0.7898 (95% CI 0.7759-0.8036) and an AUPRC of 0.4903 (95% CI 0.4640-0.5178) for AKI onset prediction, exceeding the second-best baseline by 4.2% in AUROC and 10.9% in AUPRC. Visualization of embeddings, attention patterns, and integrated-gradient feature attributions highlighted clinically meaningful relationships and patient-specific trajectories.

CONCLUSIONS: BAT-AKI provides generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis with consistent discrimination across institutions, while offering interpretability insights into its predictions, supporting its potential for early warning and AKI care optimization.

articles.title: Association of Screen Time With Physical and Mental Health in University Students: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Screen use is almost universal, and numerous studies have highlighted both the benefits and the risks of this digital integration. However, evidence on the association between screen time and health outcomes among university students remains inconsistent. Substantial methodological variation has limited the synthesis and interpretation of existing findings.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) quantify the associations between screen time and health outcomes as primary analysis; (2) quantify the association between screen time and physical (sleep quality, eye health, weight-related) and mental health outcomes (depression, psychological distress/stress, combined mental health, and well-being); and (3) identify study-level characteristics that explain between-study heterogeneity by using subgroup and meta-regression analyses.

METHODS: PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched, with final searches conducted on July 11, 2026, and reference lists were additionally screened. Eligible studies included university students aged 17 years or older, assessed screen time as duration, and reported physical or mental health outcomes with sufficient statistical data for effect-size calculation. We followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) checklist. Data were synthesized in RStudio using the restricted maximum likelihood estimator and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustments. Subgroup analyses and meta-regressions was examined. Small-study effects, leave-one-out, and influence diagnostics were also conducted.

RESULTS: A total of 82 studies (83 independent samples; 161,340 participants) were included. Longer screen time duration was significantly associated with poorer health outcomes overall (k=83; r=0.175, 95% CI 0.133-0.217; P<.001; 95% prediction interval -0.184 to 0.493), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2=98.35%; Q82=4744.45; P<.001). Pooled associations were similar for mental health (k=38; r=0.176, 95% CI 0.124-0.227) and physical health outcomes (k=45; r=0.177, 95% CI 0.108-0.243) and broad health domain did not significantly moderate the association (P=.96). Within mental health, outcome type significantly moderated the association (P=.03). The association was the strongest for depression (k=21; r=0.230, 95% CI 0.167-0.291) and was weaker for well-being (k=7; r=0.040, 95% CI -0.146 to 0.223). Combined mental health outcomes were also significant (k=8; r=0.170, 95% CI 0.076-0.261), whereas stress was not (k=2; r=0.103, 95% CI -0.222 to 0.407). Within physical health, screen time was significantly associated with poorer sleep quality (k=26; r=0.120, 95% CI 0.083-0.158) and eye health outcomes (k=16; r=0.277, 95% CI 0.089-0.446), but not weight-related outcomes (k=3; r=0.071, 95% CI -0.222 to 0.351); differences across physical outcome types were not significant. Study-level moderators did not meaningfully explain the remaining heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater screen time was associated with poorer health outcomes among university students, but the magnitude of association varied across specific outcomes and substantial unexplained heterogeneity remained. The predominance of cross-sectional designs, self-reported screen time, and sparse evidence for some outcomes limits causal inference and precision. Future research should prioritize longitudinal designs and standardized measurement approaches.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024539034; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024539034.

articles.title: Effects of a Virtual Interactive System (People's War Against Pandemic) on Emergency Preparedness for Major Emerging Infectious Diseases Among Adolescents: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The epidemiological situation of major emerging infectious diseases (MEIDs) continues to be severe. This requires each country and region to be vigilant, strengthen cooperation, and take effective prevention and response measures. This highlights the public's demand for education on health and safety measures. Virtual interactive systems have played a critical role in many fields. Consequently, we designed and developed a virtual interactive system (People's War Against Pandemic) aimed at training the public to respond to MEID outbreaks.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a novel storyline-driven virtual interactive system (People's War Against Pandemic) in enhancing emergency preparedness and infectious disease health literacy among adolescents.

METHODS: A single-blind (outcome assessors blinded), 2-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in a secondary vocational school from October 2023 to December 2023 in Luzhou, Sichuan. A total of 120 adolescents were recruited through on-site recruitment and were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n=60) and the control group (n=60). The intervention group was trained using a virtual interactive system and traditional lectures, whereas the control group received only traditional lectures. Self-reported questionnaires assessing emergency preparedness for MEIDs and infectious disease health literacy were used to evaluate the effect of the virtual interactive system before and after the intervention. Repeated-measures ANOVA was used to scrutinize variations in outcome indicators across time points within and between groups.

RESULTS: The results showed that emergency preparedness and infectious disease health literacy scores improved in both the control and intervention groups. Additionally, emergency preparedness and infectious disease health literacy scores in the intervention group were higher than those in the control group (P<.001). A repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant group, time, and group × time interaction effects in emergency preparedness and infectious disease health literacy scores.

CONCLUSIONS: The virtual interactive system was effective in improving adolescents' self-reported emergency preparedness and infectious disease health literacy in the face of MEIDs.

articles.title: Telemedicine in Rheumatology in the United States: A Scoping Review of Modalities, Outcomes, and Costs in Support of a Hybrid Model of Care.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical rheumatology : practical reports on rheumatic & musculoskeletal diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shortages and geographic maldistribution of rheumatologists limit access to rheumatology care in the United States. Tele-rheumatology grew from targeted rural and Veterans Affairs programs into mainstream practice during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, and its postpandemic role remains unsettled.

OBJECTIVE: To map the modalities, settings, and reported outcomes of telemedicine in US rheumatology.

DESIGN: Scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (Supplemental Digital Content 1, https://links.lww.com/RHU/A996) reporting.

SETTING: MEDLINE/PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixty US reports from 48 programs involving adults and children with rheumatic diseases, caregivers, and rheumatology clinicians.

INTERVENTION: Video and telephone visits, clinic-to-clinic telemedicine, electronic consultation (eConsult), remote monitoring, and hybrid care.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Access, clinical effectiveness, patient and clinician experience, cost, safety, and equity.

RESULTS: Telemedicine reduced travel and patient-borne costs, improved appointment completion, and shortened the path to specialist input through eConsult triage. Disease activity was comparable to in-person care in established patients, and structured telephone and e-visit programs improved gout treatment targets. In the largest randomized trial, satisfaction and medication toxicity monitoring were lower with telemedicine; remote joint assessment remained unreliable; and uptake was lower among older, non-English-speaking, Black, and low-income patients. Health-system savings are unproven.

LIMITATION: Predominantly observational, pandemic-influenced evidence.

CONCLUSION: Telemedicine complements rather than replaces in-person rheumatology care. A hybrid model anchored by face-to-face evaluation, with structured visit selection and safety monitoring, should be tested in pragmatic trials with full economic and equity evaluation.

articles.title: Using rare coding variants in SLC5A2 to explore the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on cardiorenal outcomes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are agents originally developed as glucose-lowering drugs but now widely used to improve cardiorenal outcomes, including in patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease regardless of diabetes status. However, their exact mode of action remains unclear. Here, we investigated the association of loss-of-function (LoF) and other rare coding variants in the SLC5A2 gene, as a genetic model of altered SGLT2 function, with 13 cardiometabolic and renal traits and clinical outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 442 570 European ancestry participants from the UK Biobank with exome sequence and phenotype data were included. We applied SAIGE-GENE+ for gene-based and single-variant association tests in the full study population and in individuals with heart failure, renal failure, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). A total of 52 LoF variants in SLC5A2 were identified. Rare variants in SLC5A2 were associated with decreased uric acid (PCauchy = 4.98 × 10-13) and with increased haematocrit (PCauchy = 1.67 × 10-5), haemoglobin (PCauchy = 1.60 × 10-5), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (PCauchy = 9.88 × 10-4). One frameshift variant (rs267607067) was significantly associated with increased haemoglobin (β = 0.33 [95% CI 0.15-0.51]; P-value = 2.40 × 10-4) and another (rs768095044) with decreased uric acid (β = -0.31 [95% CI -0.49 to -0.13]; P-value = 4.22 × 10-4). In patients with T2D, the rare variants within SLC5A2 were also associated with a lower probability of having heart failure (PCauchy = 4.00 × 10-4).

CONCLUSION: Rare genetic variants in SLC5A2 were associated with increased haemoglobin and decreased uric acid. These variants were also associated with a lower probability of heart failure among participants with T2D, providing tentative genetic support for a cardioprotective effect of SGLT2 inhibition.

articles.title: Risk of serious infection, myocardial infarction, stroke, and thromboembolic events in patients in the United States with ulcerative colitis treated with tofacitinib compared with biologic treatments.
Changes in Anthropometric, Metabolic, and Micronutrient Features Among Patients with Severe Obesity Awaiting Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Due to high demand for metabolic and bariatric surgery, patients often face significant waiting periods before undergoing the procedure. This study aimed to investigate trends in weight and metabolic changes among patients with severe obesity awaiting surgery, given the potential impact of preoperative metabolic changes on perioperative outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with severe obesity who had been waiting for metabolic and bariatric surgery for at least six months. Weight, body composition analysis parameters, and biochemical tests were recorded every six to eight weeks for these candidates.

RESULTS: Among the 2926 patients studied, the average age was 39.7 years, with 74.8% being women. The mean weight was 124.65 kg, while the mean BMI was 46.14 kg/m². Seventy-five percent of the patients had obesity-related comorbidities. Adjusted models based on generalized estimating equations (GEE) approach showed that weight, FBS, insulin, and TG have an increasing trend over time. Male sex was associated with significantly higher weight (+25.78 kg), FBS (+4.11 mg/dL), insulin (+8.47 µIU/mL), TG (+15.39 mg/dL), SGPT (+17.59 IU/L), and SGOT (+6.93 IU/L), as well as lower HDL (-3.89 mg/dL), and a small but statistically significant increase in BUN. Age showed small but significant effects, with increases linked to reduced weight, insulin, TG, and SGPT, but slightly higher FBS, LDL, HDL, and BUN values. Dyslipidemia was significantly associated with higher TG (+38.20 mg/dL), while type 2 diabetes mellitus was linked to large increases in FBS (+61.63 mg/dL) and TG (+18.04 mg/dL) and a decrease in LDL (-7.50 mg/dL). The presence of cardiovascular disease was related to higher insulin (+7.22 µIU/mL), but lower TG (-4.02 mg/dL) and LDL (-13.84 mg/dL).

CONCLUSION: Lengthening the waiting time for surgery can lead to worsening glycolipid status and weight gain in patients. Therefore, if possible, reducing wait times or providing more regular and thorough nutritional and psychological consultations can improve metabolic conditions, resulting in better outcomes after surgery.

articles.title: A new semi-automated, motility-based screening assay for discovery of compounds with activity against the juvenile stage of Fasciola hepatica.
articles.abstract: Fasciola hepatica is a trematode parasite responsible for fasciolosis, a liver disease that affects humans and livestock worldwide. Together with other food-borne trematode infections, fasciolosis is considered a neglected tropical disease. Further, it imposes substantial agricultural losses due to infections in ruminants. No vaccine is currently available, and control heavily relies on drug treatment, especially with triclabendazole (TCBZ). However, the intensive use of TCBZ over the past four decades has led to increasing rates of treatment failures and the emergence of drug-resistant parasites. Therefore, the identification of new treatment options is an urgent priority. The currently available toolset for drug screening, however, is limited. To address this need, we established a novel, semi-automated, standardized, and objective screening assay based on motility monitoring of newly excysted juveniles using microscopic live imaging. The assay was validated by testing a panel of ten compounds with known anthelmintic properties, amongst them TCBZ (IC50: 1.5 µM) and the new activator of the F. hepatica transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPMPZQ) ion channel, benzamidoquinazolinone (IC50: 1.05 µM). In addition to these two compounds with known activity against F. hepatica, three compounds were identified as particularly promising with a fast onset of action and IC50 values in the nanomolar range: the salicylanilides MMV665807 (IC50: 44 nM), niclosamide (IC50: 32 nM), and its ethanolamine salt, niclosamide ethanolamine (IC50: 9 nM). Complementary live/dead staining revealed that only TCBZ displayed parasiticidal activity, while the other compounds, although leading to parasite paralysis, did not lead to parasite death within 72 hours. Scanning electron microscopy of drug treated parasites did not reveal any significant damage at concentrations corresponding to the IC50s, but strong phenotypes were visible at 20 µM. The presented motility assay provides a robust method for the discovery of novel anthelmintic compounds and facilitates the ongoing effort to combat fasciolosis.

articles.title: L-Histidine resensitizes multidrug-resistant bacteria to carbapenems by inhibiting New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase activity.
articles.abstract: Plasmid-mediated New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)-producing Gram-negative pathogens have severely undermined the clinical utility of carbapenems, the last-resort antibiotics for multidrug-resistant infections. Given the limited pipeline of novel antibiotics, there is an urgent need for more effective anti-infective strategies. Through untargeted metabolomics and function screening, we find that L-histidine (L-His), a key downregulated metabolite in NDM-positive bacteria, remarkably restores carbapenem susceptibility. Mechanistically, L‑His acts through two complementary pathways: (i) direct competitive inhibition of NDM enzymatic activity via zinc chelation at the active site, and (ii) upregulation of the nickel ion transport gene cluster nikABCDE, which increases intracellular Ni2+ accumulation and further suppresses NDM function through non‑competitive inhibition. Overexpression of nikA potentiates the bactericidal activity of meropenem, whereas deletion of nikAB attenuates the synergistic effect of L‑His and meropenem. In a murine peritonitis‑sepsis model, co‑administration of L‑His with meropenem significantly improves survival and reduces bacterial burden, with a favorable safety profile. Collectively, our findings reveal L‑His as a multi‑mechanistic metabolic adjuvant that combines direct enzyme inhibition with disruption of metal homeostasis, positioning it as a promising therapeutic strategy against NDM‑positive carbapenem‑resistant infections.

articles.title: Type I interferon signaling promotes early innate control of Borrelia burgdorferi infection.
articles.abstract: Borrelia burgdorferi, the causative agent of Lyme disease, elicits a robust type I interferon (IFN-I) response that has been strongly associated with chronic inflammatory manifestations such as Lyme arthritis. Although IFN-I is known to be induced early during infection, its functional role in the initial stages of B. burgdorferi infection remains unclear. Here, we identify a protective role for IFN-I signaling in the early control of B. burgdorferi. At 5 days post-challenge, mice lacking the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1) exhibited markedly elevated spirochetal burdens at the site of inoculation, indicating that IFN-I signaling contributes to restricting early bacterial expansion. By 10 days post-challenge, IFNAR1 deficiency resulted in significantly increased bacterial loads in the skin and a trend toward higher loads in heart tissues, while joint burdens remained unaffected. Mechanistically, IFN-I signaling enhanced macrophage uptake of B. burgdorferi, phagosomal processing, and intracellular killing, while also modulating inflammatory cytokine responses and promoting macrophage recruitment to the inoculation site. Conversely, pharmacological activation of IFN-I signaling augmented macrophage antimicrobial function and improved bacterial clearance. Together, these findings establish IFN-I as a key component of early host defense against B. burgdorferi and reveal a time-dependent role for IFN-I signaling in Lyme disease pathogenesis, with protective functions during early infection that contrast with its pathogenic effects at later stages.

articles.title: Newly developed monoclonal antibodies for marmoset immunosuppression enable KSHV lytic replication and salivary shedding: A promising model for KSHV pathogenesis studies.
articles.abstract: Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) is the causative agent of Kaposi sarcoma, a malignancy that primarily affects immunocompromised individuals, and is also linked to multiple other diseases. Progress in understanding KSHV pathogenesis and developing effective vaccines or therapies has been severely limited by the lack of a reliable in vivo model that recapitulates infection, persistence, and disease. Previous work suggested that the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), a small New World primate, can support KSHV infection and pathogenesis, but the reproducibility and utility of this model has not been rigorously established. Here, we sought to validate the common marmoset as a non-human primate model for KSHV studies by evaluating viral infection under both immunocompetent and immunosuppressed conditions. We first tested the use of intravenous and oral tacrolimus-based immunosuppression, confirming infection in challenged marmosets but also encountering tacrolimus dosing inconsistencies and toxicity. To overcome these limitations, we developed and validated a targeted immunosuppression approach using two novel mouse-marmoset chimeric monoclonal antibodies, anti-CD4 [TAWA] and anti-CD8 [OCHO], to selectively deplete T cell subsets. Altogether, we demonstrated across four independent experiments that KSHV can establish systemic infection in both immunocompetent and immunosuppressed conditions marmosets, evidenced by viremia in peripheral blood mononuclear cells, detectable seroconversion, and tissue persistence. The chimeric antibodies mediated efficient, subset‑specific depletion of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and enabled a quantifiable, well‑tolerated immunosuppressive regimen. Moreover, we showed for the first time that monoclonal antibody-treated marmosets exhibit KSHV shedding in saliva and lytic replication, indicating that infection in this model is not merely latent but supports a full, human‑like replication cycle. Together these findings validate the common marmoset as a susceptible and translationally relevant non-human primate for studying KSHV infection and introduce a practical immunosuppressive tool for dissecting viral pathogenesis and immunity in vivo, providing a platform for testing vaccine and therapeutics.

articles.title: Hepatitis E in suspected acute hepatitis cases in Brazil: A comparison with hepatitis A.
authors: Ornelas Pereira Salvador de Oliveira D
articles.abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an underrecognized cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide, with growing public health relevance, particularly in settings where routine diagnostic testing is limited. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is another epidemiologically related hepatitis virus, but few studies have directly compared these infections in Brazil. This study aimed to (1) determine the frequency of acute hepatitis E (AHE) and evaluate the contribution of HEV infection to the burden of hepatitis among patients with suspected acute disease attended in public healthcare institutions in Brazil; (2) assess the prevalence of acquired immunity to HEV and HAV; and (3) compare demographic characteristics, risk factors, and clinical-laboratory findings associated with HEV and HAV infections. We enrolled 1,721 adults (≥18 years) with suspected acute hepatitis from 16 Brazilian states between October 2019 and May 2023. Serum samples were tested for anti-HEV IgG/IgM and anti-HAV IgG/IgM by immunoassay and for HEV and HAV RNA by RT-PCR. Demographic, behavioral, clinical, and laboratory data were collected using a standardized questionnaire. Group comparisons were performed using univariate analyses and logistic regression, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Anti-HEV IgG was detected in 89 individuals (5.2%), whereas anti-HAV IgG was detected in 1,352 (78.6%). Anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence was higher in the South, Southeast, and Central West regions and among heterosexuals, and it increased with age, reaching 13.0% among individuals aged ≥65 years. Seropositivity was associated with markers of previous exposure or immunity, including HAV, HBV, Leptospira, and Toxoplasma. A total of 124 acute hepatitis cases were identified: 16 (12.9%) AHE and 108 (87.1%) acute hepatitis A (AHA). Compared with AHA cases, AHE cases occurred in older individuals and were more frequent among women and heterosexual participants. All AHA cases occurred in urban areas, whereas AHE cases were observed in both urban and rural settings. AHA cases showed higher aminotransferase levels and more frequent jaundice than AHE cases. HEV accounts for a small but distinct proportion of suspected acute hepatitis cases in Brazil and shows epidemiological and clinical characteristics that differ from HAV. Incorporating HEV testing into routine diagnostic algorithms may improve etiological clarification and surveillance of acute hepatitis.

articles.title: The Trichomonas vaginalis pseudocyst is a viable cell stage with a distinct transcriptome and an intact membrane.
articles.abstract: Trichomonas vaginalis is the causative agent of trichomoniasis, the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection (STI). Despite its prevalence, low levels of public knowledge and research funding and the absence of T. vaginalis screening or control programs have led to its categorization as a "neglected" STI. Unlike other STIs in the USA, prevalence increases with age, peaking among individuals in their 40s. Both a motile trophozoite stage and a non-motile pseudocyst state have been described for the parasite, although it was long debated whether the latter is a quiescent stage or a degenerate form on its way to cell death. Here we characterize the T. vaginalis pseudocyst by flow cytometry, membrane integrity assays, transcriptomics, and reversion studies. Pseudocysts were induced by culturing trophozoites in acidic media or in iron depleted media, with a variety of resulting survival rates. Flow cytometry studies showed that pseudocysts have intact cell membranes and express phosphatidylserine on their cell surface. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting studies also identified distinct sub-populations of parasites, revealing the importance of using pure live pseudocyst cultures in reversion studies. Pseudocysts were transcriptionally active for several days and had consistent subsets of genes with increased expression compared to trophozoites, although decreased transcription of genes involved in metabolism. Comparative transcriptomics of pseudocysts and trophozoites of two T. vaginalis strains revealed distinct cell states. Combined, our results provide evidence that the pseudocyst cell state is a stress-induced stage of T. vaginalis that can remain viable for days, with implications for a role in persistent infections.

articles.title: Initial fixed low-versus moderate-dose hydroxyurea assignment in the long-term follow-up of the SPRINT cohort.
articles.abstract: In this pragmatic long-term follow-up of the SPRINT randomized trial cohort, rates of recurrent stroke and all-cause mortality did not differ significantly by an initial fixed low- versus moderate-dose of hydroxyurea over 4.9 years, with events clustering in the first year.

articles.title: Long-Term Epidemiological Surveillance Integrated with Data Science and Multimodel Approaches Advances Understanding of Polerovirus SCYLV Dynamics in Colombian Sugarcane.
articles.abstract: The Polerovirus Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) causes one of the most economically important viral diseases of sugarcane worldwide, including Colombia, where sugarcane is a strategic crop and the virus has high phytosanitary relevance but limited epidemiological characterization. This study provides the first integrative quantitative and multimodel epidemiological assessment of SCYLV in the country, using a 22-year surveillance dataset (1999 to 2020) from Colombia's main sugarcane-producing region. The analysis integrated data science, classical statistics, machine learning, and spatial epidemiology to identify temporal trends, spatiotemporal aggregation, and environmental and agronomic drivers of disease risk. Data science procedures supported data curation, exploratory analysis, and detection of patterns in SCYLV presence-absence, incidence, and prevalence across the historical series. Risk factor identification used logistic regression modeling of presence-absence data to estimate adjusted associations, and the machine learning framework modeled both presence-absence (classification) and incidence (regression) to capture nonlinear interactions. Spatiotemporal dynamics were assessed using presence-absence data in a space-time permutation model fitted to a Poisson-type distribution and the Knox test. SCYLV presence-absence and incidence were significantly associated with varietal susceptibility, with CC 01-1940 and SP 71-6949 showing the highest case burden climatic variability, with major outbreak clusters coinciding with strong El Niño-Southern Oscillation anomalies of both phases (El Niño in 2007 and 2015/2016 and the strong 2010/2011 La Niña), meteorological conditions (temperature, wind speed, and vapor pressure), vegetation greenness (normalized difference vegetation index), and soil properties (pH, cation exchange capacity, sand content, and nitrogen). The Knox test identified a high-risk spatiotemporal window for SCYLV spread, with relative risk > 10 concentrated within 4.5 km and 4 days after a confirmed positive case, highlighting a critical range for targeted surveillance and rapid preventive action. This integrative workflow provides a reproducible, data-driven foundation for delineating differential risk zones and supports evidence-based strategies for the integrated management of SCYLV in Colombian sugarcane systems, with transferable methodological value for long-term surveillance analyses of other aphid-transmitted viruses.

articles.title: Nanozyme-Amplified Closed Bipolar Electrochemical Colorimetric Platform for Multiplexed Visual Detection of Sepsis Biomarkers.
articles.abstract: Early diagnosis of sepsis urgently requires the development of novel electrochemical sensing platforms for rapid, sensitive, and multiplexed measurement of inflammatory biomarkers at the point of care. Herein, we report a closed bipolar electrochemical (cBPE) colorimetric platform that couples nanozyme-catalyzed redox cycling at the sensing pole with Prussian blue (PB) electrodeposition at the signal pole. Bimetallic Au@Pt nanozymes (Au core, porous Pt shell) catalyze the reduction of [Fe(CN)6]3- by ammonia borane (NH3·BH3) with a specific activity of 310 U mg-1, which is 12-fold higher than that of the Au core, and an apparent catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) of 2.7 ×107 M-1 s-1, determined under the first-order kinetic regime. Sepsis biomarkers captured on immunomagnetic beads and labeled with detection antibody-conjugated Au@Pt nanozymes were magnetically enriched at the cBPE anode, where the nanozyme-generated [Fe(CN)6]4- was re-oxidized to [Fe(CN)6]3-, sustaining a redox cycle that amplifies the Faradaic current. Charge conservation across the cBPE converts this current into an equivalent cathodic flux in a physically separated signal chamber, where Fe3+ reduction drives deposition of a blue PB film whose grayscale intensity increases monotonically with target concentration and is read by the naked eye. The spatially addressable cBPE array allows interleukin-6 (IL-6), C-reactive protein (CRP), and serum amyloid A (SAA) to be assayed in parallel, with the limits of detection of 0.83, 2.69, and 1.82 ng mL-1, respectively. In clinical serum samples from healthy controls (n = 11) and sepsis patients (n = 11), all three biomarkers were significantly elevated in the sepsis patients, with an area under the ROC curve of 0.82-1.00, demonstrating discriminative performance in real samples. The proposed cBPE-based electrochemical colorimetric platform integrates catalytic signal amplification, wireless multiplexing, and visual readout, offering a practical route toward point-of-care detection of sepsis-associated biomarkers.

articles.title: From structural repair to biomechanical compatibility: Aortic stiffness after open and endovascular aortic repair.
articles.abstract: Evaluation of aortic repair has traditionally prioritised perioperative safety, exclusion of the diseased segment and durability. As endovascular treatment expands to younger patients, attention is turning towards the biomechanical compatibility of prosthetic grafts with the native aorta. Native aortic compliance supports Windkessel function, whereas grafts create a compliance transition that may accelerate pulse-wave transmission, alter wave reflection and increase left-ventricular load. This narrative review distinguishes established evidence from emerging concepts after open surgical repair, endovascular aneurysm repair and thoracic endovascular aortic repair. Carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) is the accepted reference non-invasive measure of regional aortic stiffness; cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived segmental pulse-wave velocity and distensibility provide complementary information. Brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity, the cardio-ankle vascular index, and augmentation index assess different territories or haemodynamic properties and are not interchangeable with cfPWV. Left-ventricular strain and mass are downstream cardiac outcomes. Clinical evidence generally reports increases in measured arterial-stiffness indices after endovascular repair, whereas findings after open repair are heterogeneous. Treatment length, landing-zone location, oversizing, anatomy and baseline vascular phenotype may be as important as graft fabric or stent-frame category. Conflicting comparisons of polyester and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene arise from small, non-randomised studies using non-equivalent endpoints and do not support a reliable ranking of commercial devices. Emerging 4D-flow CMR, simulation and compliant graft materials illustrate a shift from structural exclusion alone towards compliance-aware repair, but evidence of improved outcomes remains insufficient. Future studies should use standardised longitudinal stiffness, blood-pressure and cardiac assessments and relate biomechanical changes to hypertension, ventricular remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Comparing Pinch and Point Poses for Single-Stroke Drawing in Virtual Reality.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
articles.abstract: This paper presents an investigation of bare-hand input for drawing single strokes in extended reality. Through two user studies, we compared two hand poses: pinch and point, across three surface types: a physical surface, a virtual surface, and no surface (free space). We evaluated the participant-produced strokes based on geometric and algebraic properties, performance, and subjective experience. Despite the common use of point poses for direct interaction with 2D content, our results showed that the pinch pose outperformed the point pose across most metrics. We discuss the strengths and limitations of each hand pose for bare-hand stroke input and provide insights into the role of surfaces in drawing tasks within extended reality.

articles.title: DeviCare: Dosage Deviation-Aware and Regulated Medication Recommendation.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Medication recommendation based on electronic health records (EHRs) is a critical research area in healthcare, aiming to support clinical decision-making by leveraging patients' historical visit data. Although prior studies have acknowledged the importance of fine-grained medication administration events, they primarily rely on physician-prescribed dosages while overlooking the discrepancy between prescribed and actual administered dosages, resulting in the loss of essential clinical semantics. To address this issue, we propose DeviCare, a novel framework that explicitly models dosage deviation as a fine-grained clinical signal and integrates it into a dosage deviation-regulated learning framework for medication recommendation. Specifically, we extract dosage deviations from multi-event temporal sequences and introduce an adaptive calibration mechanism to regulate representation shifts induced by dosage variations, thereby enhancing recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on the MIMIC (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care)-III and MIMIC-IV datasets demonstrate that DeviCare consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple evaluation metrics, validating the effectiveness of modeling dosagedeviation in medication recommendation tasks.

articles.title: LF-NET: A Low-Frequency Self-Supervised Model for Coronary Artery Disease Detection From Phonocardiogram Signals.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As myocardial infarction or stroke maybe the first manifestation of CAD, there is a critical need for early, non-invasive pre-screening. Heart sounds, recorded as phonocardiogram (PCG) signals, provide a low-cost diagnostic avenue. However, CAD-related murmurs are low in both frequency and intensity, rendering them inaudible during traditional auscultation. Deep learning has shown promise for PCG-based CAD classification, yet limited dataset sizes have driven reliance on fine-tuning foundation models. Models such as Wav2Vec 2.0, HuBERT, and EnCodec are pre-trained primarily on speech and environmental audio, while others like OPERA utilise respiratory sounds. Consequently, their feature representations are biased toward higher-frequency content and may be suboptimal for low-frequency PCG analysis. To address this, we propose LF-NET and LF-NET2D; self-supervised frameworks pre-trained on low-frequency ocean sound recordings that share similar frequency range with PCG signals. An energy-based noise removal algorithm is integrated into the proposed framework to extract the cleanest PCG segments from recordings obtained in real clinical environments with typical hospital noise. After fine-tuning, these lightweight models achieve comparable single-channel accuracy to existing foundation models while using fewer parameters and outperform them in multichannel configurations. Fusing LF-NET with OPERA-CE yields a state-of-the-art subject-level accuracy of 80.88% on the current 296-subject practically challenging dataset, approximately 3% higher than standalone existing foundation models.

articles.title: Successful Treatment of an Infant With Severe Combined Immunodeficiency and Ganciclovir-Resistant Cytomegalovirus Disease With Maribavir Followed By Subsequent Graft Recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory and resistant cytomegalovirus infection occurring in young infants has few effective treatments.Observations: A 2-month-old infant with severe combined immunodeficiency experienced graft failure following umbilical cord hematopoietic stem cell transplant due to cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. Following treatment with foscarnet, ganciclovir, and viral-specific cytotoxic T-lymphocyte therapy, ganciclovir resistance developed, viremia was persistent, and CMV disease developed. Maribavir was added with resolution of CMV disease and improvement in the viral load. Evaluation for repeat transplant revealed late engraftment, which ultimately led to immunologic recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: Maribavir is a novel antiviral therapy for refractory CMV infection, including in young infants.

articles.title: Retroperitoneal Nodal Metastasis Detected by Diffusion-Weighted Imaging in Paraspinal Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate lymph node evaluation is critical in rhabdomyosarcoma, yet small or metabolically inactive nodal metastases often evade detection on conventional imaging, such as fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography-computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT).

OBSERVATIONS: We report a 6-year-old girl with paraspinal alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma whose para-aortic lymph node exhibited diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) hyperintensity but lacked FDG uptake at diagnosis. The node was interpreted as reactive and was not sampled. Nine months after first-line therapy, relapse in the same para-aortic region was histologically confirmed as nodal metastasis.

CONCLUSIONS: DWI may reveal nodal metastases not identified by FDG-PET/CT or size criteria, underscoring cautious interpretation of DWI-positive, FDG-negative nodes in trunk rhabdomyosarcoma.

articles.title: Correction: Effects of Fu brick tea polysaccharides on gut microbiota and fecal metabolites of HFD/STZ-induced type 2 diabetes rats.
articles.abstract: Correction for 'Effects of Fu brick tea polysaccharides on gut microbiota and fecal metabolites of HFD/STZ-induced type 2 diabetes rats' by Xiangnan Zhang et al., Food Funct., 2023, 14, 10910-10923, https://doi.org/10.1039/d3fo04215d.

articles.title: Once-Weekly Insulin Icodec: A Review of its Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Properties.
articles.abstract: Insulin icodec is a novel long-acting basal insulin engineered for once-weekly administration. Structural modifications enhance reversible albumin binding and slow insulin receptor binding, resulting in protracted exposure and glucose-lowering effect. The clinical pharmacology of icodec was characterised using consistent methodology across populations with type 2 or type 1 diabetes. Icodec has a half-life of approximately 7 days and pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles covering the full weekly dosing interval. It displays dose-proportional exposure, week-to-week predictability, with an intra-individual coefficient of variation in total exposure of 5.9%, and a comparable glucose-lowering effect independent of injection region. Following treatment initiation, icodec clinical steady state is achieved after 3-4 weeks-this can be reduced by 1 week if the first icodec dose is 50% increased. If, unintentionally, a too high insulin dose is administered, hypoglycaemia risk with icodec is comparable to that of daily basal insulin, including robust physiological counter-regulation to hypoglycaemia. During exercise or prolonged fasting, glucose metrics remained within recommended targets, with no clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia, and supplemental glucose, when required, effectively prevented clinically relevant hypoglycaemia. The pharmacological properties of icodec are preserved across patient characteristics, without a clinically relevant impact of age, sex, diabetes type, race, ethnicity, renal or hepatic impairment, serum albumin or anti-insulin icodec antibody level. These findings support predictable, sustained basal insulin coverage suitable for once-weekly administration. This review summarises the evidence on icodec pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties and discusses how these characteristics translate into clinical benefits and specific clinical considerations compared with existing once-daily basal insulin.

articles.title: The Evolving Landscape of Neonatal Care and Research : Based on 14th Dr. I. C. Verma Excellence in Research Award Delivered as Oration on 4th October 2026.
articles.abstract: Neonatology has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past six decades, evolving from a discipline focused predominantly on preventing neonatal death to one increasingly concerned with quality of survival, neurodevelopment, family-integrated care and long-term health. Despite substantial progress, neonatal mortality remains a major global health challenge. In 2024, approximately 2.3 million newborns died globally, with the highest mortality rates in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. India has achieved a substantial decline in neonatal mortality, from 28 to 17 per 1000 live births between 2015 and 2023, accompanied by rapid expansion of facility-based newborn care. However, prematurity, low birth weight, intrapartum complications, infection, antimicrobial resistance, inequitable access, workforce constraints and inadequate long-term follow-up remain major challenges. The epidemiology of neonatal disease is also changing, with increasing survival of extremely premature infants and greater recognition of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, retinopathy of prematurity, brain injury and developmental impairment. Neonatal research is similarly moving from descriptive epidemiology and rescue therapy towards prediction, prevention, precision medicine and implementation science. The next decade should prioritize prevention of prematurity, precision sepsis management, respiratory and brain protection, nutrition and gut health, Kangaroo Mother Care, zero separation, artificial intelligence and predictive analytics, long-term outcomes and affordable innovations. The ultimate measure of neonatal care should move beyond survival to enabling every newborn to develop and reach their full potential.

articles.title: Second-Generation Combined Oral Contraceptives Induce Early Cardiovascular Risk Through Inflammatory and Oxidative Vascular Remodeling.
articles.abstract: Second-generation combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs), particularly formulations containing ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel, remain widely used because of their effectiveness and affordability in middle and low-income countries. However, concerns persist about their cardiovascular safety. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of a second-generation COCP on systolic blood pressure (SBP), inflammatory biomarkers, oxidative stress, vascular mediators, and vascular histology in female Sprague-Dawley rats. Twenty-four female Sprague-Dawley rats were acclimatized and randomly assigned to control, low-dose (1.1 µg/kg/day), and high-dose COCP (11 µg/kg/day) groups. Treatments were administered orally for six weeks. SBP and body weight were monitored before and after treatment. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and lipid profile were measured. Renal vascular homogenates were analyzed for nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), endothelin-1 (ET-1), nitric oxide (NO), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase, catalase (CAT), and glutathione. Histological examination was performed on the renal and thoracic arteries. The SBP increased by 4.6% in the low dose and 21.8% in the high dose (p < 0.05). High-dose treatment significantly increased CRP, TNF-α, and NF-κB levels, indicating enhanced systemic and vascular inflammation. Vascular MDA and CAT increased in both treated groups, suggesting oxidative stress with compensatory antioxidant activation. Low-dose COCP increased ET-1 levels, while the NO and lipid profiles showed no significant changes across the treated groups. Both doses produced marked structural alterations in the renal and thoracic arteries. The dose-dependent rise in vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, and SBP suggests early cardiovascular risk is mediated primarily by inflammatory vascular remodeling rather than by overt dyslipidemia.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with prolonged treatment courses of chronic hepatitis E.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is a relevant complication in immunocompromised patients and remains therapeutically challenging due to variable response to ribavirin (RBV). We aimed to identify clinical and biochemical factors associated with prolonged or unsuccessful treatment courses.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 41 patients with chronic HEV infection (HEV RNA detectable ≥ 12 weeks) treated between 2016 and 2024 were analyzed. Prolonged treatment (> 12 weeks), retreatment, or persistent viremia were defined as complicated treatment courses.

RESULTS: The median patient age was 54 years. Ten patients (24.4%) were female. Transaminases were elevated at the time of diagnosis with a median ALT of 118 U/l and GGT of 127 U/l. Median elastography was 6.2 kPa. 4 patients died; 30/37 patients (81%) required ribavirin treatment. Out of those, HEV cure occurred after 12 weeks of ribavirin treatment in 16 patients (53.3%), whereas eleven patients (36.6%) needed longer treatment courses or retreatment. Three patients (10%) have an ongoing HEV infection. Male sex (p = 0.03) and age > 50 years (p = 0.04) were associated with complicated treatment courses. Both normal and high ALT levels (> 200 U/L) at baseline had poorer outcomes, and a BMI < 28 kg/m2 was linked to prolonged viremia.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, older age, male sex, and distinct ALT patterns were associated with complicated treatment courses. However, these exploratory findings require cautious interpretation given the limited sample size, heterogeneous patient population, and potential confounding. A subset of patients exhibits persistent infection despite therapy, underscoring the need for improved antiviral strategies and individualized management.

articles.title: Respiratory syncytial virus in adults aged ≥ 50 years in the Netherlands: a database and time-series modelling analysis (2013-2020).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant yet historically understudied contributor to acute respiratory infection (ARI) in older adults. This study aimed to quantify ARI-associated hospital admissions and estimate RSV-related burden of disease in secondary care in the Netherlands using time-series modelling.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study (1 July 2013 to 29 February 2020) utilised routinely collected primary and secondary care data from the PHARMO Data Network. ARI-associated hospital admissions in patients aged ≥ 50 years, identified via International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes, were described in terms of patient and clinical characteristics and healthcare resource utilisation. The number and annual rate of RSV- and influenza-associated ARI and lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) hospital admissions by age and risk group were estimated using a Quasi-Poisson regression model.

RESULTS: There were 97,279 ARI admissions in 63,420 patients. Estimated RSV-associated ARI hospital admission rates ranged from 0.70/1,000 person-years (PY) to 1.92/1,000 PY in adults aged ≥ 50 and ≥ 75, respectively. RSV-associated LRTD admissions varied from 0.63/1,000 PY to 1.73/1,000 PY in these groups. Hospitalisation rates were higher in high-risk individuals. Estimated RSV admissions were up to six times higher than observed. During peak months, up to 30% of ARI (20% of LRTD) admissions were attributable to RSV. RSV-coded admissions had an average length of stay of 7-8 days, and 30% of patients experienced all-cause readmission within 90 days.

CONCLUSION: The substantial hospitalisation burden of RSV calls for prioritisation of RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination, alongside influenza and other causes of ARI and LRTD.

articles.title: Interleukin-6 Blockade in Refractory Neuro-Behçet's Disease: A Systematic Literature Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This review aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of interleukin (IL)-6 inhibition in neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) refractory to standard immunosuppressive therapy.

METHODS: This systematic literature review was performed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. The PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science databases were searched for studies on the efficacy of IL-6 blockade in patients with refractory NBD. We also identified cases of NBD with recurrently elevated IL-6 levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) during tumor necrosis factor (TNF) alpha therapy at our institution.

RESULTS: We identified 11 studies including 25 patients with NBD who were treated with tocilizumab. No eligible studies of other IL-6-targeted agents were identified. Among the 24 patients evaluated for response, 22 (91.7%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 74.2-97.7%) were classified as responders. Reduction of the glucocorticoid dose was achieved in at least 75.0% (18/24, 95% CI 55.1-88.0%) of patients receiving concomitant glucocorticoid. Adverse events were infrequently reported (infusion reaction, cytopenia, infections), and one responder experienced worsening mucocutaneous inflammation. Two cases identified at our institution had recurrent neurological symptoms with high CSF IL-6 levels and an incomplete response to TNF inhibitor therapy, requiring repeated hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: IL-6 blockade is a promising option for patients with refractory or recurrent NBD who have failed conventional therapies. Given the limited quality of the current evidence, prospective studies are needed to clarify the long-term efficacy and safety of IL-6-targeted therapy in NBD.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000058445.

articles.title: Evaluating the antiviral effects of polygonum cuspidatum nanoparticles against enterovirus 71 in vitro and in vivo.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus 71 (EV71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) and is associated with severe neurological complications in young children. However, effective antiviral therapeutics remain limited. In this study, nanoparticles derived from Polygonum cuspidatum (NPC) were prepared and their antiviral activity against EV71 was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. Cytotoxicity and antiviral assays in human rhabdomyosarcoma (RD) cells demonstrated that NPC exhibited substantially lower cytotoxicity than the crude extract while maintaining comparable antiviral potency against EV71. NPC treatment markedly reduced EV71-induced cytopathic effects and significantly decreased viral RNA levels, as confirmed by indirect immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR. In an EV71-infected ICR suckling mouse model, oral administration of NPC significantly improved survival, attenuated clinical disease scores and body weight loss, and reduced viral loads in muscle and brain tissues in a dose-dependent manner. Histopathological analysis revealed alleviated tissue injury in the NPC-treated mice. These findings suggest that nanonization improves the therapeutic index of P. cuspidatum and support further investigation of NPC as a potential plant-derived antiviral candidate for EV71 infection.

articles.title: miR-125b-5p alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by targeting PTP1B to inhibit the endoplasmic reticulum stress-pyroptosis axis.
articles.journal: In vitro cellular & developmental biology. Animal
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SALI) is a severe complication of sepsis with high mortality, and the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenesis remain incompletely elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role and molecular mechanism of miR-125b-5p in SALI by targeting protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B). The rat alveolar macrophage cell line NR8383 was stimulated with 1 μg/mL lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to establish an in vitro SALI cell model. High-throughput transcriptome sequencing was used to screen differentially expressed miRNAs associated with PTP1B, and qRT-PCR was performed for validation. The direct binding between miR-125b-5p and PTP1B was verified by a dual-luciferase reporter assay in 293 T cells. A rat model of SALI was established by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) in 6-8 week-old male SD rats, which were randomly divided into the sham operation group (Sham), SALI model group (Model), Model + miR-125b-5p agonist negative control group (Model + NC), and Model + miR-125b-5p agonist group (Model + Agonist). The pathological changes of lung tissues were observed by HE staining. The mRNA expressions of miR-125b-5p, PTP1B, IL-1β, and IL-18 were detected by qRT-PCR. The protein expressions of Cleaved-Caspase-1, CHOP, GSDMD, Cleaved-GSDMD, and PTP1B were measured by Western blotting (WB). High-throughput sequencing and qRT-PCR validation identified five miRNAs with potential interaction with PTP1B, among which miR-125b-5p and miR-185-3p were significantly downregulated, while miR-351-5p, miR-125a-5p, and miR-345-3p were significantly upregulated in the LPS-induced NR8383 cell model (all P < 0.05). The dual-luciferase reporter assay confirmed that miR-125b-5p directly bound to the 3'UTR of PTP1B, and this binding significantly reduced the luciferase activity of the wild-type PTP1B reporter vector ( < 0.05). In the in vivo SALI model, HE staining showed severe lung tissue damage in the Model group, including thickened alveolar walls, massive inflammatory cell infiltration, and pulmonary interstitial hemorrhage, while the Model + Agonist group exhibited significantly alleviated pathological damage with no obvious lesions. qRT-PCR results showed that compared with the Sham group, the mRNA expressions of PTP1B, IL-1β, and IL-18 were significantly increased, and miR-125b-5p was significantly decreased in the Model group (all P < 0.05); these changes were significantly reversed in the Model + Agonist group compared with the Model + NC group (all P < 0.05). WB results demonstrated that the protein levels of Cleaved-Caspase-1, CHOP, GSDMD, Cleaved-GSDMD, and PTP1B were significantly elevated in the Model group relative to the Sham group (all P < 0.05), and miR-125b-5p agonist treatment markedly downregulated the expression of these proteins (all P < 0.05 vs. Model + NC group). MiR-125b-5p is a protective miRNA in SALI, and its agonist can effectively alleviate CLP-induced lung tissue damage in rats. The underlying mechanism may be that miR-125b-5p directly targets PTP1B to inhibit the activation of the endoplasmic reticulum stress-pyroptosis axis, thereby reducing inflammatory response and pyroptotic cell death in lung tissues. This study identifies a novel miR-125b-5p/PTP1B regulatory axis, providing a potential molecular target for the clinical treatment of SALI.

articles.title: Depression and antidepressant use are associated with prolonged recovery and increased opioid dependence following ulnar nerve transposition.
articles.abstract: Depression is common among patients with cubital tunnel syndrome and may adversely influence surgical recovery. This study evaluates the impact of depression and antidepressant use on postoperative complications following ulnar nerve transposition (UNT). A retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults undergoing primary UNT between 2005 and 2025 were identified and stratified by depression status. Three 1:1 propensity-matched analyses were performed to evaluate the impact of (1) depression status, (2) antidepressant use among depressed patients, and (3) specific antidepressant subclasses. Matching controlled for demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included 90-day medical and postoperative complications and 1 year pain-related outcomes and opioid dependence. After matching, 11,821 patients were included in each cohort. Depression was associated with significantly higher 90-day medical morbidity, including infection (RR 1.39, P = 0.0008), acute postoperative pain (RR 1.28, P < 0.0001), emergency department utilization (RR 1.37, P < 0.0001), and increased need for PT evaluation (RR 1.21, P < 0.0001) and orthopedic aftercare (RR 1.11, P = 0.001). At 1 year, depressed patients demonstrated higher rates of persistent elbow pain (RR 1.16, P < 0.0001) and nearly double the risk of opioid dependence or abuse (RR 1.88, P < 0.0001). Among patients with depression, preoperative antidepressant use was associated with higher 1-year opioid dependence (RR 1.66, P = 0.007) and persistent pain (RR 1.21, P = 0.001). SSRI use specifically was linked to increased long-term pain (RR 1.17, P = 0.001) and opioid dependence (RR 1.31, P = 0.023). TCA use was associated with higher 90 day ED visits (RR 1.20, P = 0.022), while atypical antidepressants were associated with increased acute postoperative pain (RR 1.42, P = 0.004). Depression was associated with adverse postoperative outcomes after UNT. Antidepressant use, particularly SSRIs, was associated with higher long-term pain and opioid-related risk; however, these associations may reflect underlying depression severity rather than a direct pharmacologic effect.

articles.title: Generalized anxiety disorder may lead to increased healthcare utilization following total hip arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychiatric comorbidities are increasingly recognized as modifiers of arthroplasty outcomes. However, the effect of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) on outcomes following total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains underexplored.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the PearlDiver national database to identify patients who underwent primary, unilateral THA for osteoarthritis between 2010 and 2022. Patients with <90-day follow-up were excluded. Among 278,655 eligible patients, 17,422 (6.2%) had a preoperative diagnosis of GAD. These patients were propensity score-matched 1:1 (caliper 0.2) to patients without GAD, resulting in 34,844 matched THAs. Primary outcomes included 90-day emergency department (ED) visits, readmissions, reoperations, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) at 90 days, 1 and 2 years, and revision procedures at 1 and 2 years. Annual trends in GAD prevalence among THA patients were also analyzed.

RESULTS: GAD was associated with significantly increased odds of 90-day ED visits (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.21; 95% CI, 1.13-1.29; P<0.001) and 90-day reoperations (AOR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05-1.37; P=0.006). No differences were observed in readmissions, PJI, or revision rates at any time point. GAD prevalence among THA patients rose from 0.54% in 2010 to 10.14% in 2022-a 19-fold increase (R2=0.99, P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative GAD is associated with higher risk of 90-day ED visits and reoperations following THA. The rising prevalence of GAD suggests that preoperative mental health status may be relevant to perioperative risk stratification and supports further study of targeted optimization strategies in patients undergoing THA.

articles.title: Skeletal Muscle in Vulnerable Populations Receiving Cardiorenal-Metabolic Therapies: SGLT2 Inhibitors, Incretin-Based Therapies, and the Challenge of Precision Medicine.
articles.abstract: The introduction of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and incretin-based therapies has transformed the management of obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease by delivering substantial metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal benefits. However, their effects on skeletal muscle have become a growing area of interest. While SGLT2 inhibitors induce modest weight loss, their catabolic metabolic effects have prompted questions regarding skeletal muscle preservation, particularly in individuals with limited physiological reserve. Conversely, the profound weight loss achieved with incretin-based therapies has raised concerns about accompanying reductions in lean tissue and their potential functional consequences. In this narrative review, we critically evaluate the available evidence regarding the effects of these therapeutic classes on skeletal muscle, integrating findings from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and mechanistic investigations. We compare their distinct biological mechanisms; summarize clinical evidence on changes in muscle quantity, quality, strength, and physical performance; and discuss their implications for older adults; individuals with frailty, sarcopenia, or sarcopenic obesity; and patients with heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Overall, current evidence indicates that both SGLT2 inhibitors and incretin-based therapies preferentially reduce adipose tissue, whereas the accompanying reductions in lean tissue are generally proportional to the magnitude of weight loss. Importantly, reductions in lean tissue should not be equated with treatment-induced sarcopenia, as current evidence does not consistently demonstrate clinically meaningful impairment in muscle strength or physical performance. Nevertheless, the populations most susceptible to skeletal muscle dysfunction remain underrepresented in clinical trials. We discuss a phenotype-based approach that integrates skeletal muscle health into therapeutic decision-making and outline practical strategies-including resistance exercise, adequate protein intake, and individualized monitoring-to preserve muscle function during treatment. Future research should prioritize standardized functional outcomes and dedicated studies in vulnerable populations to enable precision cardiorenal-metabolic medicine.

articles.title: Islet Function Phenotyping-Based Heterogeneity in New-Onset Type 2 Diabetes: Clinical Importance and Baseline Metabolic Phenotype in a Large-Sample Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As a result of a variety of pathophysiological mechanisms, type 2 diabetes displays notable clinical heterogeneity. However, large cohorts of newly diagnosed patients are still needed to validate systematic classification based on basic clinical indicators and its clinical significance. Patients with new-onset type 2 diabetes were divided into four pathophysiological subtypes based on HOMA-IR and HOMA-β. Each subtype's clinical traits, metabolic profiles, and cross-sectional complication risk were assessed.

METHODS: A total of 21,340 patients who had just received a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and were not receiving treatment were included. HOMA-IR and HOMA-β were computed. The overall medians were used as cut points to split patients into four groups: group 1, high resistance low secretion (HRLS); group 2, high resistance high secretion (HRHS); group 3, low resistance low secretion (LRLS); and group 4, low resistance high secretion (LRHS). The groups were compared in terms of prognosis, islet function, metabolic markers, and demographics.

RESULTS: There were notable clinical and metabolic variations among the four groups. The HRLS group (n = 2743) had the highest risk of complications, the lowest disposition index, and the worst metabolic indicators. With the highest insulin levels and a moderate disposition index, the HRHS group (n = 7935) demonstrated typical metabolic syndrome. The LRLS group (n = 7927) demonstrated severe insulin secretory defects, as evidenced by their moderate disposition index, good sensitivity, and poor secretion. The LRHS group (n = 2735) had the highest disposition index and the least severe metabolic abnormalities. All intergroup comparisons had a p value < 0.001.

CONCLUSION: Type 2 diabetes subtypes with different pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical prognoses can be effectively identified by simple classification based on HOMA-IR and HOMA-β, which offers a useful framework for precision medicine.

articles.title: Sirolimus and Immunoglobulin Replacement Therapy in Patients with Activated Phosphoinositide 3-Kinase Delta Syndrome (APDS): A Systematic Literature Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS) is an ultra-rare disease associated with immunodeficiency and immune dysregulation. Management may include sirolimus and immunoglobulin replacement therapy (IRT); neither is specifically approved for APDS in the USA. This systematic literature review evaluated the effectiveness and safety of sirolimus and IRT in patients with APDS.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched through July 2025, supplemented by grey literature and bibliographic searches. Eligible records reported treatment outcomes in patients with APDS receiving sirolimus and/or IRT. Quality assessment was performed; findings were narratively synthesized.

RESULTS: Seventy-nine records (82 publications) were included: 69 case reports of 103 patients, 8 retrospective cohort studies, and 2 case series, describing 136 treatment regimens. No prospective studies were identified. Evidence was dominated by case reports (87.3% of records), assessed as low-to-moderate quality. Most records did not include pre- and post-treatment data, comparators, or clearly defined outcomes. Infections were the most commonly reported outcome (44 records), with improvement reported in 59.5% of patients in cohort studies and in 50.0% of regimens in case reports, although improvement was rarely defined. Lymphoproliferation outcomes (35 records) showed no improvement in 35.7-43.8% of patients in cohort studies and in 50.0% of regimens in case reports, although improvement definitions and pre- and post-treatment data were limited. Progression to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation occurred in 12.9% of patients. In all patients receiving sirolimus in cohort studies, renal/hepatic toxicity was reported in 19.2-25.0% of patients and discontinuation from any cause was reported in 25.0-34.6% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Despite numerous records, the effectiveness of sirolimus and IRT cannot be reliably quantified from the published APDS literature, which largely consists of low-to-moderate quality case reports. More methodologically rigorous studies are needed to inform treatment strategies for these therapies in APDS.

articles.title: Disparities in Environmental Chemical Concentrations and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes by Race and Ethnicity and Country of Birth: Examples from the MIREC Study.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Research investigating disproportionate exposure or susceptibility in racialized and immigrant pregnant people is limited. To address this gap, we quantified disparities in environmental chemical concentrations and pregnancy complications by two indicators: (1) race and ethnicity and (2) country of birth. Our objectives were to (1) quantify descriptive differences in chemical concentrations and prevalence of outcomes and (2) assess heterogeneity in the chemical-outcome associations by our two indicators of disparity.

METHODS: Using data from a pan-Canadian longitudinal pregnancy cohort study (2008-2011), we assessed disparities in three case studies based on prior publications that examined associations between: (1) arsenic and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (n = 1255), (2) lead and preterm birth (PTB) (n = 1847), and (3) perfluorohexane sulfonate (PFHxS) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) (n = 1739). Chemicals were measured in first trimester blood samples; lead was also measured in third trimester samples. Pregnancy complication data were extracted from medical charts. We calculated geometric mean (GM) chemical concentrations by each disparity indicator and assessed differences via one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). We calculated the prevalence of each health outcome by disparity indicator and assessed differences using Chi-square tests.
