Using multivariable models, we assessed heterogeneity by stratifying results and calculating measures of interaction on the additive (Relative excess risk due to interaction [RERI]) and multiplicative scales.

RESULTS: Compared to White participants, non-White participants had 16% higher GM arsenic concentrations and 15-20% higher GM lead concentrations lead. Foreign-born participants had 23% higher GM arsenic concentrations and 29-37% higher GM lead concentrations compared to Canadian-born participants. Prevalence of GDM was greater for non-White compared to White participants (14% vs. 7.2%) and for foreign-born compared to Canadian-born participants (11% vs. 7.9%). Foreign-born participants experienced heightened susceptibility to the effects of lead on risk of PTB (RERI: 0.67, 95%CI: 0.01-1.27). In contrast, PFHxS concentrations were lower in non-White (33%) and foreign-born participants (34%) relative to their counterparts. Prevalence of HDP was also lower in non-White compared to White participants (6.8% vs. 11%) and in foreign-born compared to Canadian-born participants (5.8% vs. 11%).

CONCLUSIONS: We identified absolute and relative disparities in prenatal chemical concentrations and prevalence of pregnancy complications in three case studies from a Canadian pregnancy cohort. Our findings provide impetus for future biomonitoring studies that: (a) are larger and more inclusive of racialized and foreign-born populations, (b) use validated tools to directly measure discrimination and structural inequities, and (c) apply intersectional statistical methods.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a prognostic model for predicting periodontitis progression using clinical and behavioural factors.
articles.abstract: To develop and internally validate the PERI-Score, a pragmatic prognostic index for estimating 36-month periodontitis progression from routinely available clinical, systemic, and behavioural information. In this prospective single-centre cohort study, 350 consecutive adults with periodontitis received non-surgical periodontal therapy and were followed for 36 months during supportive periodontal therapy (SPT). Progression was operationally defined as clinical attachment loss, represented by an increase (worsening) in clinical attachment level (CAL) of ≥ 2 mm at ≥ 20% of assessable matched sites. The PERI-Score was developed using Cox proportional hazards modelling. Performance was evaluated using a stratified 70:30 development/internal-validation split and 1,000 bootstrap resamples; both subsets originated from the same cohort and therefore represent internal validation. A total of 118 progression events were observed (33.7%). The strongest predictors were Stage III/IV periodontitis (HR 2.64), active smoking (≥ 10 cigarettes/day; HR 2.31), PPD ≥ 5 mm at ≥ 4 sites (HR 2.18), SPT non-compliance (< 75% attendance; HR 2.08), and Grade C periodontitis (HR 1.92), with additional contributions from HbA1c ≥ 7.0%, CAL ≥ 5 mm at ≥ 4 sites, BOP ≥ 30%, Class II/III furcation involvement, FMPS ≥ 30%, and age ≥ 50 years. The internal-validation AUC was 0.843 (95% CI 0.786-0.900), and observed progression increased across the three PERI-Score strata. The PERI-Score is an internally validated candidate prognostic model for 36-month progression during treated periodontal care. It combines baseline disease severity and susceptibility with modifiable systemic and behavioural factors and a longitudinal marker of SPT adherence. It may support risk communication and structured monitoring, but independent multicentre external validation is required before its thresholds are used to determine treatment or recall protocols.

articles.title: Admission Circulating microRNAs and Residual Congestion in Very Elderly Patients With Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: Associations With miR-223-3p and miR-423-5p.
articles.abstract: MicroRNAs may provide information about decongestion in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). We examined associations with residual congestion and diuretic treatment intensity. In 145 adults with ADHF, seven admission serum miRNAs were quantified by RT-qPCR. Residual congestion at 48 h required at least 2 of: VExUS score ≥ 1, clinical congestion score ≥ 3, or NT-proBNP ratio ≥ 0.70. Logistic and robust log-linear models assessed residual congestion and intravenous loop-diuretic dose intensity. Residual congestion occurred in 69 patients (47.6%). In complete-case models (n = 119), higher miR-223-3p expression was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.36-0.91), whereas higher miR-423-5p expression was associated with higher odds (adjusted OR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.00-2.38). Neither was independently associated with diuretic dose intensity. miR-223-3p showed the more consistent exploratory association with early residual congestion; evidence for miR-423-5p was less robust. External validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Postmenopausal Hormone Replacement Therapy is not Associated with Increased Postoperative Complications After Breast Surgery: A Propensity Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast surgery and reconstruction rates in the USA continue to rise, with over 90% of new breast cancer diagnoses occurring in peri- or postmenopausal women. Despite the relevance of menopause to wound healing, postoperative outcomes in this population remain understudied. Estrogen hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may aid wound healing and menopausal symptoms, but carries prothrombotic risk. We investigate postsurgical outcomes after breast surgery and reconstruction among postmenopausal patients on HRTs compared to those without HRT use.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX database, we compared patients with and without HRT use within 1 year preceding breast reconstruction. Mastectomy and reconstruction procedures were identified using CPT codes. HRT use was identified using ICD-10 and RxNorm codes. Cohorts were propensity-matched for demographics and comorbidities. Risk differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for outcomes within 90 days postoperatively. Analyses were performed within TriNetX, with significance set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Two cohorts were generated, with 3750 HRT+ and 75503 HRT- patients. After propensity matching, two cohorts of 3750 patients each were created. After propensity adjustment, there was no significant association between HRT use and postoperative mortality, VTE, or wound healing complications, which were comparably low across all surgery types. Among patients undergoing autologous reconstruction, 1-year revision rates were higher in the HRT+ cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic hormone replacement therapy was not associated with an increased complications after breast reconstruction, including mortality, thrombosis, infection, and wound dehiscence. Further prospective studies across surgical populations are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Reply to "Time‑varying RLS and perinatal depression: concerns regarding model specification and causal inference".
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

articles.title: International multidisciplinary expert consensus on the clinical application of patient-specific subperiosteal implants: a modified Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To establish international multidisciplinary expert consensus on the clinical application of patient-specific subperiosteal implants across indications, surgical workflow, prosthetic rehabilitation, outcomes and complications, and follow-up and maintenance.

METHODS: A modified two-round web-based Delphi study was conducted in accordance with established methodological guidance and ACCORD. Evidence-informed preliminary statements were developed by a multidisciplinary core group. International experts rated each statement on a five-point Likert scale and could provide comments. Consensus was defined as ≥ 75% agreement. Non-consensus or substantively revised statements were redistributed in Round 2.

RESULTS: Of 58 invited experts, 23 participated in Round 1 (39.7% response); 22 returned for Round 2 (95.7% retention), with 21 providing valid statement-level ratings. In Round 1, 30 of 43 statements (69.8%) achieved consensus. Round 2 evaluated 15 revised statements (13 non-consensus and two substantively refined), of which 12 (80.0%) achieved consensus. The final set comprised 40 consensus statements across five domains. Agreement was strongest for surgical workflow and follow-up and maintenance, whereas uncertainty persisted regarding indications and outcomes and complications. No consensus was reached on previous head and neck radiotherapy, locking screw fixation systems, or the frequency of mechanical complications.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an evidence-informed multidisciplinary framework for the clinical use of patient-specific subperiosteal implants. It supports careful patient selection, digitally integrated and prosthetically driven planning, individualized rehabilitation, and structured long-term follow-up, while identifying priorities for further clinical research.

articles.title: Safety profiles of tocilizumab and tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis: a propensity score-weighted comparative analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) and targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) have been the primary advanced treatment options for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in Taiwan since 2010. Tocilizumab is an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor (IL-6Ri), whereas tofacitinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi). The two medications have similar mechanisms and efficacy. We compared the safety outcomes of tocilizumab and tofacitinib in patients with RA in real-world clinical settings.

METHODS: Patients with RA at any period between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database and followed until 2020. Propensity score stabilized weighting was used to balance the baseline characteristics of the tocilizumab and tofacitinib groups. The incidences of safety outcomes, specifically all-cause mortality, cancer, coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, overall venous thromboembolism (OVT), tuberculosis (TB), joint replacement events, and herpes zoster infection, were compared between the study groups.

RESULTS: A total of 1074 patients with RA who were administered tocilizumab (n = 463) or tofacitinib (n = 611) were included in this study. The mean follow-up duration was 1.96 years in the tocilizumab group and 1.98 years in the tofacitinib group. A substantially lower incidence rate of herpes zoster infection (per 100 patient-years) was observed in the tocilizumab group (3.125) than in the tofacitinib group (6.875), with a hazard ratio of 0.455 (95% CI = 0.289-0.716; P = 0.0007). All-cause mortality, CHD, stroke, total hip replacement, and TB infection were similar between the two medication groups.

CONCLUSION: Although tocilizumab (an IL-6 receptor inhibitor) and tofacitinib (a JAK inhibitor) effectively modulate the immune response through distinct mechanisms, a lower herpes zoster incidence rate was observed in the tocilizumab group. No statistically significant differences were detected for the other evaluated safety outcomes and mortality rates between the two groups, although the relatively small number of events resulted in wide confidence intervals. Key Points • For moderate to severe RA patients concerned about herpes zoster risk, the tocilizumab group had a lower incidence rate than the tofacitinib group. • In real-world settings, RA patients with tocilizumab or tofacitinib had comparable incidence rates of other safety concerns and mortality.

articles.title: Considering "First Do No Harm" in Hypertension Management.
Naxos disease: current insights from early clinical observations to genetics and precision medicine.
articles.abstract: Naxos disease is the prototype of the Naxos disease cardiocutaneous spectrum, a group of inherited desmosomal disorders characterised by distinctive hair and skin abnormalities that precede the development of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM). Since its original clinical description in 1986 and the subsequent identification of the first ACM-causing gene (JUP), Naxos disease has provided fundamental insights into the pathogenesis, diagnosis and management of inherited desmosomal cardiomyopathies. This review provides current insights into the evolving clinical spectrum, encompassing the characteristic cutaneous signature, early electrical abnormalities, progressive structural myocardial remodelling, inflammatory ("hot-phase") episodes, ventricular arrhythmias and heart failure. We discuss the expanding genotype-phenotype relationships involving JUP, DSP and DSC2, highlighting how distinct genetic substrates influence ventricular involvement, disease severity and clinical outcomes while sharing common desmosomal mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on early clinical recognition, multimodality imaging, genetic diagnosis, risk stratification and lifelong multidisciplinary management. Finally, we discuss the emerging role of international collaborative registries, including NAXCARE, in generating prospective real-world evidence to refine genotype-informed surveillance, improve risk prediction and support precision medicine. Nearly four decades after its original description, Naxos disease has evolved from a rare inherited syndrome into the prototype of desmosomal cardiomyopathy, demonstrating how careful clinical observation can drive molecular discovery, precision medicine and improved patient care.

articles.title: Myocardial contraction fraction and mortality in cardiac amyloidosis: a prospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) often remains normal in cardiac amyloidosis (CA) because declines in stroke volume (SV) parallel reductions in end-diastolic volume. The myocardial contraction fraction (MCF), the ratio of SV to myocardial volume, has been proposed as superior to LVEF in predicting mortality in CA.

METHODS: Thirty patients with confirmed CA underwent echocardiography and were followed for a mean of 18.2 ± 5.8 months. MCF was calculated from standard two-dimensional echocardiographic measurements. Cox proportional hazards modeling with Lasso-penalized selection was used to evaluate the association of MCF with all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Mean age was 70.1 ± 8.6 years; 76.7% were male. Thirteen patients (43.3%) died. MCF was lower among those who died compared with survivors (21.9% vs 38.2%; p < 0.0001); 87.5% of patients with MCF ≤ 25% died, compared with 27.3% of those with MCF > 25%. MCF ≤ 25% was independently associated with mortality (HR: 5.456; 95% CI: 1.628-18.29; p = 0.006); modeled as a continuous variable, each 5-percentage-point increase in MCF was associated with lower mortality (HR: 0.57; p = 0.002), while MAPSE < 10 mm and grade 3 diastolic dysfunction were retained in the multivariable model but did not reach significance after penalization.

CONCLUSIONS: MCF ≤ 25% demonstrated numerically greater discriminative ability for all-cause mortality compared with LVEF (C-statistic 0.83 vs 0.71) and was the only echocardiographic parameter to remain an independent predictor after Lasso-penalized multivariable adjustment. These hypothesis-generating findings, from a small single-centre cohort, require validation in larger, subtype-specific studies.

articles.title: High-fat diet-induced MAFLD is associated with sleep architecture disruption via hippocampal neuroinflammation and bifurcated IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling in mice.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological associations between metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and sleep disturbances point to shared mechanisms, yet the underlying central pathways remain unexplored. We hypothesized that high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MAFLD disrupts sleep architecture via hippocampal neuroinflammation and dysregulation of the IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling axis. Male BALB/c mice were fed a control diet (CD) or a 60% HFD for 16 weeks to induce MAFLD. Sleep-wake architecture was assessed by 24-h EEG/EMG recordings. We evaluated hepatic steatosis, serum cytokines, hippocampal histology, and hippocampal pro-inflammatory cytokines. Hippocampal expression and phosphorylation of IRS-1 (Ser307), Akt (Ser473), and mTOR (Ser2448) were analyzed by Western blot. HFD-fed mice developed hepatic steatosis, elevated liver enzymes, and increased serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β). These mice exhibited reduced non‑rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep duration, severe sleep fragmentation (reflected by increased bout numbers and shorter mean bout durations), and diminished NREM sleep delta power. Cosinor analysis revealed a dampened circadian rhythm of NREM sleep delta power. In the hippocampus, HFD induced neuronal injury, elevated TNF-α and IL-1β levels, accompanied by a bifurcated signaling profile: increased p-IRS-1 (Ser307), decreased p-Akt (Ser473), and elevated p-mTOR (Ser2448). Our findings identify a putative liver-hippocampus-sleep axis in which MAFLD-driven systemic inflammation and hippocampal IRS-1/Akt/mTOR dysregulation are associated with profound sleep disruption, providing a framework for future mechanistic validation. Targeting this axis may offer new therapeutic strategies for sleep disorders in MAFLD.

articles.title: Melatonin suppresses astrocyte reactivity and Mitigates cognitive deficits induced by a high-carbohydrate, high-fat diet in rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-carbohydrate and high-fat (HCHF) diets may impair cognitive function through neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and astrocyte activation. This study investigated the effects of melatonin on memory impairment and astrocyte reactivity in rats with diet-induced metabolic syndrome.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Adult male Wistar rats were fed an HCHF diet for eight weeks, followed by daily oral melatonin treatment (5, 10, or 30 mg/kg) for four weeks while continuing the diet. Working memory was assessed using the Y-maze spontaneous alternation test. Hippocampal and hypothalamic tissues were evaluated for proinflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity. HCHF feeding caused weight gain, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, impaired working memory, increased neuroinflammation and oxidative damage, and astrogliosis in both brain regions. Melatonin did not improve glucose tolerance or lipid profiles at any dose. However, working memory performance in melatonin-treated rats was comparable to that of controls at all doses. Melatonin also reduced GFAP-positive astrocytes, proinflammatory cytokine levels, and lipid peroxidation, while increasing superoxide dismutase activity. These effects were mainly dose-dependent in the hippocampus, whereas memory improvement showed no clear dose-dependent pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: Melatonin improved working memory and reduced astrocyte reactivity, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress in rats fed an HCHF diet, without improving systemic metabolic abnormalities. These findings suggest that melatonin may protect against diet-induced brain injury through mechanisms related to astrocyte activation, inflammation, and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Variation in Health State Utility Values Across Preference-Based Instruments: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Behavioural Risk Factors.
articles.journal: Applied health economics and health policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health economic evaluations require health state utility values (HSUVs) to estimate quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). However, HSUVs derived from different preference-based instruments, valuation methods and value sets may not be directly comparable, which can affect interpretation of economic evaluations. Although reference cases, such as that of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), specify a preferred instrument, such as the EQ-5D, alternative measures are frequently used in practice. Using behavioural risk factors as an applied case, this study examined variation in HSUVs across instruments and synthesised utility estimates for body mass index (BMI) and smoking categories.

METHODS: A systematic review of population-based observational studies published between 2009 and 2024 was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and EconLit. Random-effects meta-analyses were used to estimate pooled HSUVs by instrument type and risk factor category. Mixed-effects meta-regression models explored associations between behavioural risk factors, health-related quality of life (HRQoL) instrument type and variation in HSUVs while accounting for clustering of multiple estimates within studies. Preference-based instruments included the EQ-5D, Health Utilities Index (HUI), Short Form 6-Dimension (SF-6D) and Quality of Well-Being (QWB) scale. Given the anticipated heterogeneity across studies, pooled estimates were used to describe variation in reported HSUVs.

RESULTS: Forty-four articles were included, contributing 186 utility estimates across five instrument categories. Substantial variation in HSUVs was observed across instruments with consistent patterns evident across BMI and smoking categories. Relative to the EQ-5D-3L, the HUI, SF-6D and QWB yielded systematically lower utility values. The EQ-5D-5L yielded higher values in the BMI model, but the corresponding estimate in the smoking model was not statistically significant. Variation associated with instrument categories, which may also reflect related valuation and derivation differences, was comparable, and in some cases greater than, differences observed across BMI and smoking categories, although substantial between-study heterogeneity remained (I2 > 90%). Lower HSUVs were observed among individuals who were underweight, overweight or obese compared with those of normal weight and among former and current smokers compared with never smokers. Former smokers reported lower values than current smokers, consistent with selection effects. Alcohol use was reported in too few studies to support reliable instrument-stratified pooling, and reported values overlapped substantially across drinking categories.

CONCLUSIONS: Reported HSUVs varied systematically across preference-based instruments, with differences comparable to, and in some cases exceeding, those associated with behavioural risk factors. Because instrument versions, value sets, valuation methods, mapping procedures and population characteristics could not be fully separated, these differences should be interpreted as reflecting broader utility measurement and valuation approaches rather than independent instrument effects. Utility-source selection should be transparently justified, aligned with relevant reference-case recommendations and explored through sensitivity analyses where alternative credible inputs are available.

articles.title: From what the dentist sees to artificial intelligence in bone endocrinology, Endobridge, and much more.
Imaging Features and Prognosis of Anti‑Sez6l2 Encephalitis: A Longitudinal Cohort Study and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Anti-Seizure-Related 6 Homolog Like 2 (Sez6l2) encephalitis is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by cerebellar ataxia and cognitive impairment. The 13 previously reported cases included in our systematic analysis focus on adults, leaving gaps in pediatric demographics, longitudinal multimodal imaging markers, and effective management of refractory cases. This study aimed to expand the clinical spectrum, evaluate multimodal imaging in localizing neuroinflammation/monitoring response, and assess the efficacy of combined first- and second-line immunotherapy. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of five Sez6l2-antibody-positive patients (aged 15-72 years) alongside a systematic review (N = 18). Clinical severity (mRS, CASE, MMSE, MoCA), structural MRI, and 18F-DPA714 PET/MRI mapped neuroinflammation and monitored therapeutic response. Our cohort features the first documented adolescent case. All five patients presented with ataxia and cognitive deficits. While MRI revealed cerebellar atrophy in three patients, 18F-DPA714 PET/MRI detected microglial activation in the cerebellum (n = 4) and bilateral mesial temporal lobes (n = 1), mapping precisely to clinical phenotypes. Longitudinally, clinical improvement paralleled a 7%-8% reduction in cerebellar tracer uptake in Case 1. Patients receiving combined first- and second-line immunotherapy (efgartigimod, ofatumumab; n = 3) achieved pronounced cognitive and psychiatric recovery. Conversely, first-line therapy alone yielded limited efficacy in the 66-year-old patient with established atrophy, while the adolescent showed more favorable responsiveness. The systematic review (N = 18) confirmed universal ataxia (100%), frequent cognitive impairment (72%), and significant residual disability (median mRS 4). This study expands the demographic spectrum of Sez6l2 encephalitis to adolescents and provides cohort-based evidence for multimodal imaging in localizing neuroinflammation/monitoring response, highlighting combined immunosuppressants as possible new therapeutic options.

articles.title: Pathogenicity of Aspergillus nidulans isolated from the liver of diseased goat (Capra hircus).
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
articles.abstract: Aspergillus nidulans, an environmentally ubiquitous opportunistic pathogen, can induce invasive aspergillosis in humans and animals, with numerous human infection cases documented. Here, we isolated A. nidulans strain XM06 from the liver of a diseased goat with suspected fungal infection. XM06 formed dark‑green colonies with white fluffy margins and a powdery center on PDA, and PCR amplification yielded products corresponding to putative homologous virulence genes, including Cat1, Alp2, and Aspf1. Using a mouse infection model, we characterized its pathogenic potential. The infected mice exhibited reduced body weight and average daily feed intake (P < 0.05), with morbidity and mortality rates of 66.7% and 33.3%, respectively. In infected animals, the organ indices of the liver, spleen, lung, kidney and brain were elevated, while the intestinal index was reduced (P < 0.01). No intergroup difference was observed for the heart index (P > 0.05). Fungal burdens were highest in the spleen and liver (P < 0.05). Histopathological lesions including congestion, necrosis and inflammatory infiltration were observed in multiple organs. Antifungal assays revealed small inhibition‑zone diameters for amphotericin B and comparatively larger inhibition zones for itraconazole, caspofungin and voriconazole against strain XM06. This work provides preliminary pathological and in vitro drug-response data for goat-derived A. nidulans, offering baseline information for studying animal invasive aspergillosis. Notably, our mouse infection assay only demonstrates the pathogenic potential of XM06 and cannot confirm that this isolate caused the original disease outbreak in goats.

articles.title: A targeted stewardship intervention improves the adequacy of antipseudomonal therapy after implementation of the EUCAST 2019 clinical category redefinitions.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the adequacy of antipseudomonal therapy in hospitalised patients following implementation of the 2019 EUCAST clinical category redefinitions through a multidisciplinary strategy.

METHODS: A mixed-design study was conducted in a university hospital. Adult inpatients with documented Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection and available antimicrobial susceptibility and treatment data were included. Two study periods were defined: a pre-intervention retrospective/training period and a post-intervention period. Primary outcome was adequacy of antimicrobial therapy. Secondary outcomes included clinical and microbiological variables.

RESULTS: A total of 169 patients were included (78 pre-intervention and 91 post-intervention). Median age was 69 years (IQR 60-79), Charlson comorbidity index 5 (IQR 3-7) and SOFA score 3 (IQR 2-5). Analyses were adjusted for baseline differences between groups. Adequacy of antipseudomonal therapy increased significantly after the intervention (25/78 vs 79/91, p < 0.001). Interrupted time analysis (ITS) showed the intervention was associated with a marked and statistically significant immediate increase in the adequacy of antipseudomonal therapy (OR, 13.13; 95% CI, 1.73-113.25; p=0.015) after adjustment for time, SOFA score and infection type; without increased meropenem use. No significant differences were observed in mortality, readmissions or survival. Despite higher baseline severity in the post-intervention group, length of hospital stay was significantly shorter (OR = 0.98, p < 0.05). A non-significant trend toward fewer acquired resistance mutations was observed, consistent with improved local antipseudomonal susceptibility.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of the 2019 EUCAST clinical category redefinitions, supported by coordinated interventions from Microbiology and Infectious Diseases specialists, was associated with a marked improvement in adequate antipseudomonal therapy without increased meropenem use or adverse clinical outcomes. The trend toward reduced resistance emergence suggests this strategy is ecologically safe and sustainable.

articles.title: The prognostic value of a laboratory-based frailty index (FI-Lab) in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections: a multicentre cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections remain a major cause of mortality despite advances in antimicrobial therapy. Frailty, reflecting cumulative physiological decline, may strongly influence outcomes beyond age or comorbidity. This study evaluated whether a 30-item Frailty Index-Laboratory (FI-Lab), calculated within 48 h of admission, independently predicts early (7-day) and short-term (30-day) mortality among hospitalized patients with CRAB infections.

METHODS: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study including adults with microbiologically confirmed CRAB infection admitted to four Infectious Diseases Units in Apulia, Italy (Bari, Foggia, Taranto-Moscati, Bisceglie) between January 2020 and August 2025. The FI-Lab, derived from 30 biochemical parameters, quantified the proportion of abnormal laboratory values (range 0-1). Cox regression models assessed associations between FI-Lab and mortality, adjusting for age, comorbidity, SOFA score, septic shock, infection site, therapy type, and other covariates.

RESULTS: Among 199 patients (mean age 70 ± 15 years; 38.2% male), the median FI-Lab was 0.56 (IQR 0.45-0.68). Seven-day, 30-day, and in-hospital mortality were 12.6%, 19.1%, and 20.6%, respectively. Each + 0.10 increase in FI-Lab was associated with higher 7-day (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.22-1.89), 30-day (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.36-2.08), and in-hospital (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.32-2.01) mortality (all p < 0.01). Patients with respiratory infections had significantly higher 30-day mortality than those with bloodstream infections (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.05-2.51, p = 0.029). No mortality difference was observed between cefiderocol- and colistin-based regimens. FI-Lab demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUC = 0.89 for 30-day mortality).

CONCLUSIONS: The FI-Lab independently predicted early and short-term mortality in CRAB infections, outperforming traditional indices and highlighting the prognostic weight of biological frailty. The strong impact of respiratory infection and the absence of therapy-related differences suggest that host vulnerability may outweigh antimicrobial choice in determining outcomes. FI-Lab, easily derived from routine tests, could be integrated into clinical algorithms for early risk stratification in multidrug-resistant infection.

articles.title: Characterization of airway mucus using quantitative MRI: an in vitro proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A characteristic of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is mucus hypersecretion. In this proof-of-concept study, we aimed to characterize airway mucus using a quantitative ultrashort echo time (UTE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequence in a controlled in vitro synthetic mucus model to establish a technical foundation for future in vivo studies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: UTE double-echo steady-state (UTE-DESS) was performed to acquire the signal from free induction decay-like signal and spin/stimulated echo-like signal echoes; quantitative MRI parameters (T1, T2, and diffusivity) were estimated. Synthetic mucus phantoms were prepared using mucin (0.20%, 0.50%, and 1.0%) mixed with xanthan gum (0.10%, 0.25%, and 0.50%) to replicate the viscoelastic properties of human laryngeal mucus, and samples were embedded in 1% agar for imaging.

RESULTS: The mucus phantoms with varying concentrations of mucin and xanthan exhibited visual differences in color and opacity. Estimated T1 values were 2.23 ± 0.16, 2.37 ± 0.20, and 2.09 ± 0.18 s (mean ± standard deviation) for the three tubes with relative mucus concentrations of 1, 2.5, and 5, respectively. Corresponding T2 values were 806.6 ± 105.6, 687.4 ± 78.0, and 475.0 ± 41.3 ms, while diffusivity values were 2.36 ± 0.14, 2.31 ± 0.18, and 2.33 ± 0.18 µm2/ms for the three tubes. Only the T2 relaxation times showed a significant linear correlation with mucus concentration (r = -0.9998, p = 0.0112).

CONCLUSION: UTE-DESS MRI could be feasible for characterizing airway mucus. T2 relaxation time showed a strong inverse correlation with increasing mucus concentration, indicating its sensitivity to mucus content.

KEY POINTS: Question Can a novel quantitative ultrashort echo time MRI sequence noninvasively characterize airway mucus properties and overcome conventional lung imaging limitations in muco-obstructive diseases? Findings In this controlled in vitro model, UTE-DESS MRI mapping demonstrated that T2 relaxation times alone showed a strong inverse correlation with increasing mucus concentrations. Relevance statement This exploratory proof-of-concept establishes a technical foundation for radiation-free, noninvasive T2 mapping to monitor and phenotype chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and other mucoobstructive lung diseases in future in vivo studies.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist-associated weight loss in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is associated with adverse metabolic effects - including increased fat mass, decreased lean muscle mass, and insulin resistance - that may attenuate the efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). This study evaluated GLP-1 RA-associated weight loss outcomes in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 269 breast cancer patients at a single academic center receiving concurrent GLP-1 RA and adjuvant endocrine therapy. GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy data were obtained from electronic medication reconciliation lists and pharmacy dispense reports. Patients were required to have initiated GLP-1 therapy during the study period and to have received concurrent GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy for at least one year. The primary outcome was percentage weight change from GLP-1 initiation to 12 months (± 2 months). Secondary outcomes included proportions achieving ≥ 5%, ≥ 10%, and ≥ 15% weight loss.

RESULTS: Mean one-year percentage weight loss was - 4.5% (95% CI: -6.0% to - 3.0%; -3.9 kg; 95% CI: -4.96 to - 2.93 kg), significantly below the 10-20% observed in postmenopausal subgroups of GLP-1 randomized trials (all p < 0.001). Only 21.3% achieved ≥ 10% and 10.4% achieved ≥ 15% weight loss. Weight loss differed significantly by GLP-1 agent (p = 0.003); semaglutide (- 5.8%) and tirzepatide (- 4.7%) outperformed dulaglutide (+ 0.1%), which is approved for type 2 diabetes only. Higher baseline weight was associated with greater absolute loss (r = - 0.19, p = 0.002), though percentage weight loss did not differ significantly by baseline BMI category (p = 0.303). PR-negative patients lost more than PR-positive patients (- 8.2% vs. -4.2%; p = 0.021, d = 0.46). Type 2 diabetes was present in 70.6% of patients; T2DM status was not significantly associated with weight loss on t-test (p = 0.288), though patients without T2DM were numerically more likely to achieve ≥ 15% loss (21.5% vs. 5.8%).

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RAs produce statistically significant but substantially attenuated weight loss in breast cancer patients on concurrent endocrine therapy. GLP-1 agent selection significantly influences outcomes. Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

articles.title: A closer look at LATE: a Case Report on a subtly evolving neurodegenerative disorder.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE) often presents in older adults with a hippocampal-type amnestic syndrome that is clinically indistinguishable from Alzheimer's disease (AD). In the era of anti-amyloid therapies, misdiagnosis carries therapeutic consequences.

METHODS: Single-patient case report. The patient provided written informed consent and all data included in this paper are de-identified.

RESULTS: A 71-year-old with isolated episodic memory impairment underwent neuropsychological testing, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) AD biomarkers, and 18F-FDG PET in 2021. Baseline findings showed preserved global cognition, negative AD biomarkers, and mild bilateral medial temporal hypometabolism. Over the subsequent years, episodic memory declined, while daily function and other cognitive domains remained intact. MRI demonstrated bilateral medial temporal atrophy. Repeat CSF examination showed negative AD biomarkers, whereas NfL levels were markedly elevated. On repeat 18F-FDG PET, bilateral medial temporal hypometabolism progressed, while inferolateral temporal metabolism-usually reduced in AD-remained preserved.

DISCUSSION: The slowly progressing isolated amnestic profile, medial temporal-predominant neurodegeneration, high CSF NfL level, and persistently negative AD biomarkers supported the diagnosis of LATE. LATE should be actively considered in elderly patients with a hippocampal-type amnestic syndrome and negative AD biomarkers. This requires a high index of suspicion, but it is increasingly critical to avoid ineffective therapies and to refine clinical trial selection.

articles.title: HSV-1 ICP0 expression induces formation of nuclear TDP-43 assemblies.
articles.abstract: Toxic cytoplasmic aggregates containing the nuclear RNA-binding protein TDP-43 form in several neurodegenerative diseases; however, the molecular triggers driving aggregation remain unclear. Epidemiological evidence has linked latent and reactivating herpes simplex virus type-1 (HSV-1) infections to neurodegenerative disease onset, but it is unknown if HSV-1 infection impacts TDP-43 subcellular distribution. Here, we demonstrate that HSV-1 infection of epithelial cells and DRG-derived neurons results in nuclear TDP-43 redistribution and TDP-43 accumulation within distinct nuclear assemblies. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 was not detected under these conditions. Nuclear TDP-43 assembly occurred early in infection and was dependent upon expression of the critical ICP0 regulatory gene. Remarkably, ectopic ICP0 expression in uninfected cells was sufficient for nuclear TDP-43 assembly. Thus, expression of a single viral gene product encoded by a near ubiquitous human herpesvirus can alter TDP-43 nuclear localization. Moreover, our work identifies a potential mechanistic link between herpesvirus infection and neuronal disease factor mislocalization.

articles.title: Post-Translational Protein Acylation in Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia and is strongly associated with stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Aging is a major risk factor, while atrial electrical, structural, and metabolic remodeling drive AF progression. Emerging evidence highlights protein lysine acylation as an important regulatory layer linking metabolism with epigenetic and signaling pathways in AF, including acetylation, propionylation, lactylation, 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation, succinylation, and malonylation. These modifications have been implicated in the regulation of ion channel activity, mitochondrial metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibroblast activation, which may contribute to atrial remodeling and arrhythmogenesis. This review summarizes current advances in acylation-mediated mechanisms and discusses the potential therapeutic implications of modulating acylation-related enzymes, such as sirtuins, histone deacetylases, and acyltransferases. Understanding acylation regulatory networks may provide a basis for exploring acylation-associated biomarkers and therapeutic targets in AF.

articles.title: Pre-culture and culture-informed exploratory prognostic analyses of surgical intervention in fungal keratitis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the etiologic distribution and temporal trends of culture-proven fungal keratitis and to explore clinical and microbiological factors associated with surgical intervention.

METHODS: Retrospective observational study of eligible culture-proven fungal keratitis cases identified at a tertiary referral center in Mexico City, Mexico, from 2012 to 2024. Laboratory-based surveillance analyses included 222 fungal isolates, comprising 113 institutional and 109 external referral isolates. Prognostic analyses were restricted to 91 institutional cases with complete follow-up and outcome data. The primary outcome was surgical intervention during follow-up. Two exploratory multivariable logistic regression models were evaluated: a pre-culture clinical model using variables available at presentation and a culture-informed model additionally incorporating microbiological etiology. Internal validation was performed using leave-one-out cross-validation.

RESULTS: Fusarium spp. was the most frequent organism (52.3%), followed by Aspergillus spp. (18.0%), Candida spp. (15.3%), and other fungi (14.4%). Temporal analyses suggested between-year variation in Candida spp., but no statistically significant linear trends were detected for any fungal group. In the prognostic cohort, 57/91 eyes (62.6%) required surgical intervention. The pre-culture model included presenting visual acuity and time to diagnosis; the culture-informed model additionally included Fusarium spp.

INFECTION: LOOCV AUROCs were 0.68 and 0.70 for the pre-culture and culture-informed models, respectively; corresponding calibration slopes were 0.55 and 0.59, indicating overly extreme predicted risks.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline visual acuity, diagnostic delay, and Fusarium spp. infection were associated with surgical intervention in fungal keratitis. Modest discrimination and calibration limitations indicate that further model development and external validation are needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and preventive behaviors regarding myopia among adults in Palestine: a cross-sectional online convenience-sample survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myopia is a growing cause of visual impairment and ocular morbidity, yet evidence concerning public understanding and preventive behavior in Palestine is limited. This study assessed awareness, knowledge, attitudes, and preventive behaviors regarding myopia among adults recruited online in Palestine and examined associated sociodemographic and eye-health characteristics.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from 14 November to 30 December 2025. Adults aged at least 18 years who resided in Palestine, completed the Arabic questionnaire, provided electronic consent, and did not report a healthcare-related occupation or field of study were eligible. The final analysis included all eligible respondents, irrespective of prior awareness of myopia. Domain scores were analyzed continuously using descriptive statistics, Welch group-comparison tests, Pearson correlations, and forced-entry multivariable linear regression with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Of 702 submitted forms, 594 were eligible after exclusion of 11 non-consenting submissions, five later exact duplicate response patterns, and 92 respondents with explicit healthcare-related occupations or studies. The sample was predominantly aged 18-29 years (83.5%), female (75.8%), and tertiary/postgraduate educated (85.9%). Prior awareness of myopia was reported by 585 participants (98.5%, 95% CI 97.1%-99.2%). Mean knowledge, attitude, and preventive-behavior scores were 49.26 ± 7.04 of 66 (74.6% of the maximum), 37.06 ± 4.84 of 48 (77.2%), and 15.86 ± 2.71 of 24 (66.1%), respectively. Cronbach's alpha was 0.673, 0.588, and 0.367, respectively. Knowledge and attitude were moderately correlated (r = 0.402, 95% CI 0.332-0.467; p < 0.001), whereas correlations involving preventive behavior were negligible and non-significant. In adjusted analysis, female sex, tertiary/postgraduate education, employment, and clinician-diagnosed myopia were associated with more favorable attitude scores. Preventive-behavior findings were exploratory because of poor internal consistency.

CONCLUSION: In this young, highly educated, digitally reached non-healthcare sample, normalized attitude and knowledge scores exceeded the preventive-behavior score. The findings are descriptive of the recruited sample and should not be interpreted as population estimates for Palestinian adults. Representative mixed-mode studies, formal Arabic validation, and locally evaluated primary-care, school, optometrist-led, and digital eye-health interventions are needed.

articles.title: New Record of Raillietiella furcocerca (Pentastomida: Raillietiellidae) in Bothrops atrox from the Brazilian Amazon: Morphological Characterization and Infection Sites.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to document the occurrence of Raillietiella furcocerca infecting Bothrops atrox in the Lower Amazon region, State of Pará, Brazil, providing morphometric characterization, infection descriptors, and new insights into extrapulmonary infection sites.

METHODS: A total of 48 B. atrox specimens were examined between 2009 and 2011 (Tapajós National Forest) and 2023-2024 (Santarém and Belterra). Pentastomes were recovered during necropsy, counted, measured, and morphologically identified. Parasitological descriptors (prevalence, mean abundance, and mean intensity) were calculated alongside a literature review of pentastome-snake interactions in the Neotropics.

RESULTS: Nine host specimens were infected ([Formula: see text]), yielding an overall prevalence of 18.8%, a mean abundance of 0.48, and a mean intensity of 2.56. Pentastomes were recovered from both the lungs and the coelomic cavity, actively attached to visceral serosa and associated with focal tissue lesions.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first quantitative parasitological baseline for R. furcocerca in B. atrox from the Amazonian biome and confirms the coelomic cavity as a viable antemortem extrapulmonary infection site and provide update literature review and distribution mapping on pentastomids infection in Neotropical snakes.

articles.title: Crisis Interventions for Children and Adolescents with Depression and Suicidality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review the evidence on crisis services for children and adolescents experiencing acute psychopathological crises, particularly severe depression, suicidal ideation, self-harm, and suicidal behaviour, and to examine their effectiveness in reducing symptoms, improving family functioning, and preventing hospitalisation.

RECENT FINDINGS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. Searches of PubMed, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and ClinicalTrials.gov identified 15 eligible studies evaluating 15 crisis interventions. Four interventions targeted suicidal ideation and self-harm through brief, structured approaches, demonstrating reductions in suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts, and emergency department visits. Seven family-focused interventions (evaluated in eight studies) improved communication, family cohesion, and reduced hospitalisation rates. Three interventions aimed to stabilise crises and facilitate linkage with community services, improving continuity of care and decreasing emergency service utilisation. One residential intervention (evaluated in two studies) showed mixed findings, with some behavioural improvements but limited effects on internalising symptoms. Current evidence suggests that crisis services might be a promising alternative to hospitalisation for children and adolescents experiencing acute mental health crises. These interventions provide intensive support within the young person's natural environment, promote family involvement, and were associated with reductions in suicidal ideation, depressive symptoms, emergency visits, and hospital admissions. Despite promising findings, the evidence base remains limited, largely observational and heterogeneous, and causal conclusions cannot be drawn. Future research should directly compare different crisis service models and include long-term follow-up to determine the most effective approaches and their sustainability over time.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal Helminths in Brown Bears in Erzurum, Türkiye: Biological Bridge, a Threat to Humans.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Changes in land use, habitat fragmentation, and global climate fluctuations are reshaping pathogen circulation dynamics by increasing the permeability of the interface among wildlife, domestic animals, and humans. In this context, wild mammals play a crucial role as natural reservoirs for parasites and sources of environmental contamination. The primary aim of this study is to microscopically and molecularly identify gastrointestinal helminth eggs detected in bear fecal samples, as well as adult parasites found in two dead bears.

METHODS: A total of 333 fecal samples were collected from four locations in Erzurum, Türkiye, and examined microscopically; helminth eggs were further identified by molecular methods. Two dead bears were examined post-mortem for adult parasites.

RESULTS: Baylisascaris transfuga (23.7%), Uncinaria stenocephala (3%), and Dicrocoelium sp. (19.5%) were detected in the 333 fecal samples collected from four locations. Furthermore, B. transfuga (in both animals), U. stenocephala (in one animal), and D. dendriticum (in one animal) were identified following post-mortem examinations.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that bears may act as reservoirs for parasitic agents, playing an active role in the persistence of pathogens in the environment and their transmission to different hosts. The findings of this study need to be examined from a One Health perspective, which focuses on biological transmission networks within ecosystems rather than on infection foci alone, to assess risks to public and animal health.

articles.title: Prosthetic mesh infection after abdominal wall hernia repair: a medico-legal analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mesh infection is a rare but potentially devastating complication of abdominal wall hernia repair, often requiring prolonged treatment, repeated surgery, and, in selected cases, mesh explantation. Although its clinical management has been extensively investigated, the medico-legal implications of mesh-related infections remain poorly explored. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiological, clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and medico-legal features of Italian litigation concerning mesh infection following abdominal wall hernia repair.

METHODS: A retrospective review of publicly available Italian judicial decisions concerning mesh infection after hernia repair was performed. Clinical, microbiological, surgical, and legal variables were extracted, including patient and procedural characteristics, microbiological findings, treatment strategies, court-appointed technical expert (Consulente Tecnico d'Ufficio, [CTU]) assessments, judicial reasoning, and litigation outcomes.

RESULTS: Fourteen judicial decisions, corresponding to 13 distinct clinical episodes, were identified. Inguinal hernia repair was the most frequent procedure (38.5%), followed by incisional (30.8%), umbilical (23.1%), and femoral (7.7%) hernia repair. Staphylococcus aureus was the most isolated pathogen, while infection onset ranged from the early postoperative period to several years after implantation. Most patients ultimately required mesh explantation after failure of conservative treatment. A causal relationship between perioperative management and infection was established in 6 of 13 cases (46.2%) and excluded in the remainder. Across the judgments, CTU assessments consistently relied on temporal, topographical, and clinical criteria, together with evaluation of compliance with infection-prevention measures and perioperative documentation. Liability was more frequently associated with the inability to demonstrate adherence to accepted preventive standards than with the occurrence of infection itself. Alleged deficiencies in informed consent were common but did not independently result in compensation.

CONCLUSIONS: Mesh infection should not be regarded as evidence of malpractice. Rather, judicial assessment depends on rigorous evaluation of causation, documentation of infection-prevention measures, and compliance with accepted standards of care. This study highlights the central role of multidisciplinary expert evaluation in medico-legal disputes involving mesh infection and underscores the need for greater integration between contemporary surgical evidence and medico-legal criteria when assessing healthcare-associated infections following hernia repair.

articles.title: Prognostic role of selective beta-1 blockers in patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer care and prognosis. Beta-adrenergic activation contributes to cancer initiation and progression. While non-selective beta-blockers were found to improve the efficacy of ICIs therapy, the role of beta-1 (β1)-selective beta-blocker (β1B) is unknown. We aimed to evaluate the association between baseline selective β1-blocker therapy and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular immune-related adverse events (CV irAEs) among patients treated with ICIs.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center study including patients diagnosed with cancer and treated with ICIs therapy.

RESULTS: Among 2409 patients, 591 (25%) were pretreated with β1B. Patients in the β1B group were older (72 ± 9 vs. 64 ± 13 years, p < 0.001) with a higher prevalence of cardiac risk factors and CV diseases including ischemic heart disease (40% vs. 8%, p < 0.001), heart failure (HF) (9% vs. 2%, p < 0.001) and atrial fibrillation (AF) (15% vs. 3%, p < 0.001). Patients pretreated with β1B showed significantly increased all-cause mortality (68% vs. 57%, p < 0.001) and CV irAEs (14% vs. 7%, p < 0.001), mainly HF (7% vs. 3%, p < 0.001) and AF (7% vs. 3%, p < 0.001). In a multivariate analysis, β1B remained a strong independent predictor for all-cause mortality (Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.21 [95% CI 1.05-1.39]), p = 0.010), however, not for CV irAEs (HR 1.22 [95% CI = 0.84-1.77], p = 0.290). The association between baseline selective β1-blocker treatment and increased all-cause mortality was consistent among patients with or without baseline CV disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline β1B therapy may be an independent predictor of increased all-cause mortality in patients treated with ICIs.

articles.title: Comparative assessment of residual DNA quantification methods in human acellular dermal grafts: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Human acellular dermal grafts (HADGs) are widely used in regenerative medicine and tissue banking because of their biocompatibility and structural support. Residual DNA is an important quality attribute for assessing cellular material removal, and its interpretation should be integrated with evaluation of extracellular matrix (ECM) integrity and scaffold performance. A systematic review (search date: October 15, 2025) of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and grey literature was conducted. English-language in vitro or experimental studies (2010-2025) reporting quantitative residual DNA levels and at least one structural, functional, or biological assessment were included. Data on decellularization protocols, DNA quantification methods, analytical sensitivity, validation, and scaffold performance were extracted. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria from 1,250 screened records. Residual DNA varied with decellularization method and quantification technique. Enzymatic and hybrid protocols achieved near-complete DNA removal (> 98%) while preserving extracellular matrix (ECM) structure, basement membrane integrity, and cytocompatibility. Fluorometric and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) assays offered higher sensitivity and reproducibility than spectrophotometry, which often overestimated DNA content. Detergent- or alkaline-only methods showed greater variability and sometimes compromised ECM integrity or cell attachment. HADG quality and translational suitability are strongly influenced by decellularization and the DNA quantification approaches. Evidence supports enzymatic or hybrid methods integrating nuclease treatment with controlled detergent exposure, combined with sensitive DNA assays, as the most effective framework for standardized quality assessment, regulatory compliance, and reproducible clinical application.

articles.title: Does the "switch the plane" strategy improve outcomes? Anterior vs. posterior repair for recurrence after prior inguinal hernia repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recurrent inguinal hernia remains a common challenge in abdominal wall surgery. Current guidelines from the European Hernia Society recommend repairing recurrent inguinal hernias through the previously unoperated anatomical plane ("switch the plane" strategy), supporting a posterior repair after failed anterior repair. Although this strategy is widely adopted in clinical practice, the evidence supporting its superiority remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate surgical outcomes after recurrent inguinal hernia repair according to the anatomical plane of the index and subsequent repair.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Databases including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and LILACS were searched for studies evaluating surgical repair of recurrent unilateral inguinal hernia. Comparative studies assessing posterior versus anterior repair were included for pooled comparative meta-analysis. Outcomes included hernia recurrence, chronic postoperative inguinal pain, surgical site infection (SSI), and seroma. Meta-analyses were performed in R studio using random-effects models, with results reported as odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Additional single-arm meta-analyses were conducted to estimate pooled outcome proportions among studies evaluating posterior repair after prior anterior repair and posterior repair after prior posterior repair.

RESULTS: After screening 14,197 records, 35 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the review. These studies comprised 4,902 patients, predominantly male (97.9%), with a mean age of 57.2 years. Six studies compared posterior versus anterior repair after prior anterior repair. Recurrence was assessed in six studies (869 patients; 63 events), with no statistically significant difference between approaches (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.39-1.27; I²=7.5%). Chronic postoperative pain was assessed in five studies (722 patients; 92 events), with no statistically significant difference in the primary analysis (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.22-1.00; I²=52.7%), although posterior repair was associated with significantly lower odds in the RCT-only sensitivity analysis (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.16-0.81; I²=44.1%). SSI was assessed in five studies (604 patients; 14 events), with significantly lower odds following posterior repair (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.07-0.79; I²=0%). Seroma was assessed in three studies (386 patients; 15 events), with no significant difference between approaches (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.26-2.29; I²=0%). Among studies evaluating posterior repair after prior anterior repair, recurrence was assessed in seventeen studies (3,551 patients; 59 events), with a pooled rate of 2% (95% CI 0.01-0.03; I²=16.5%); chronic postoperative pain in fifteen studies (3,396 patients; 137 events), with a pooled rate of 3% (95% CI 0.01-0.06; I²=65.3%); SSI in fifteen studies (3,370 patients; 25 events), with a pooled rate of 1% (95% CI 0.00-0.02; I²=76.3%); and seroma in fourteen studies (3,339 patients; 110 events), with a pooled rate of 5% (95% CI 0.03-0.07; I²=74.5%). Among studies evaluating posterior re-repair after prior posterior repair, recurrence was assessed in eleven studies (316 patients; 8 events), with a pooled rate of 1% (95% CI 0.00-0.06; I²=0%); chronic postoperative pain in eight studies (224 patients; 19 events), with a pooled rate of 6% (95% CI 0.02-0.15; I²=0%); SSI in seven studies (231 patients; 3 events), with a pooled rate of 1% (95% CI 0.00-0.04; I²=0%); and seroma in eleven studies (316 patients; 21 events), with a pooled rate of 6% (95% CI 0.03-0.12; I²=34.8%). Only one study evaluated anterior repair following prior posterior repair, precluding quantitative synthesis.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in recurrence was identified between posterior and repeat anterior repair, while posterior repair was associated with significantly lower odds of SSI. Chronic postoperative pain also favored posterior repair, with a significant reduction observed in the RCT-only sensitivity analysis despite the primary analysis not reaching statistical significance. These findings support the guideline-recommended use of posterior repair following failed anterior repair. Posterior re-repair after prior posterior repair may also be feasible in selected cases, although the evidence remains predominantly observational. Evidence for anterior repair following prior posterior repair remains limited to a single study, precluding definitive conclusions regarding the complete "switch the plane" strategy.

STUDY REGISTRATION: A review protocol for this systematic review was registered at PROSPERO CRD420261375949.

articles.title: Exposure to antidepressant and antipsychotic medicines in pregnant women and risk of gestational diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antidepressants and antipsychotics are commonly prescribed for psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and severe anxiety disorders. Psychotropic medications are increasingly prescribed during pregnancy to manage severe mental illnesses. Concerns have been raised about their metabolic side effects, including the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze existing evidence on the risk of GDM development in pregnant women with prenatal exposure to two common psychotropics, antipsychotics and antidepressants.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Web of Science, up to June 2025, identifying observational studies reporting GDM outcomes following the use of psychotropic medicines during pregnancy. Eligible studies were reviewed, and pooled relative risks (RRs) were calculated using a random-effects model, with subgroup analyses based on medication classification.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included in this review and meta-analysis. The pooled adjusted RR for GDM among women exposed to any antipsychotics and antidepressants during pregnancy was 1.43 (95% CI: 1.17,1.69), and 1.19 (95% CI: 1.10,1.27). Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) were associated with a significantly higher risk of GDM (RR = 1.6, 95% CI: 1.23, 1.97). First-generation antipsychotics showed no statistically significant association.

CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to antipsychotics, particularly SGAs, and antidepressants is associated with an increased risk of GDM. Clinicians should consider these risks when prescribing psychotropic medications during pregnancy and ensure appropriate metabolic monitoring.

articles.title: Dissecting the shared genetic architecture of adipose tissue aging and aging-related lipid-metabolic dysfunction: a multivariate genomic analysis.
articles.abstract: Adipose tissue aging is increasingly recognized as a systemic process involving altered fat distribution, ectopic lipid deposition, and metabolic dysfunction, yet its shared genetic architecture remains incompletely characterized. In this study, we constructed a latent multivariate genetic phenotype of adipose tissue aging by integrating genome-wide association summary statistics for seven adipose- and metabolism-related traits, including visceral adipose tissue volume, abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue volume, thigh subcutaneous adipose tissue volume, liver proton density fat fraction, fasting insulin, adiponectin, and leptin. Using Genomic Structural Equation Modelling, we derived a latent phenotype termed mvAdiposeAge and further characterized its genetic and biological relevance through genome-wide association analysis, FUMA-based functional annotation, MAGMA gene-level analysis, transcriptome-wide association analysis, expression fine-mapping, pathway and tissue enrichment analyses, and Mendelian randomization. The Genomic SEM model supported a shared genetic dimension linking adipose distribution, ectopic lipid accumulation, and adipose-related metabolic traits. Genome-wide analysis identified a prominent signal at chromosome 16q12.2, with rs1421085 in the FTO region emerging as the lead variant. MAGMA identified 49 FDR-significant genes, while transcriptome-wide analysis prioritized 11 genes, with FOCUS fine-mapping highlighting expression-mediated signals involving FTO, RPGRIP1L, and AKTIP. Functional enrichment implicated neurotrophin signalling, synaptic organization, cAMP signalling, immune and phagocytic processes, endocrine regulation, and metabolic pathways, with tissue enrichment suggesting prominent brain-region-specific signals. Mendelian randomization further supported positive associations of adiposity-related traits with mvAdiposeAge and an inverse association with cognitive performance. These findings highlight mvAdiposeAge as a latent genetic factor capturing shared genetic variation across adipose-related phenotypes relevant to aging and provide a framework for further investigating their systemic biological associations.

articles.title: Outdoor thermal comfort in K-12 schools: a systematic literature review.
articles.abstract: As children spend many hours outdoors for play, learning, and physical activity, the thermal quality of schoolyards has become an increasingly critical concern for public health and educational design, particularly under exposure to thermal extremes and climate change. This systematic review analyzes 35 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, identified through five online databases, to synthesize the current state of knowledge on outdoor thermal comfort (OTC) in K-12 schools. Findings show a strong focus on mitigating summer heat stress, particularly in primary schools within Mediterranean and humid subtropical climates. Most studies rely on field measurements combined with numerical simulations, typically using objective indices, while increasingly incorporating subjective measures such as behavioral adaptation. Across climates, vegetation and shading consistently emerge as the most effective mitigation strategies. By identifying research gaps, methodological trends, and dominant interventions, this review underscores the need for more comprehensive research on schoolyard thermal environments. It also provides practical guidance for architects, urban planners, and school administrators by outlining climate-responsive intervention priorities. Overall, this review highlights that improving outdoor thermal comfort in school settings is not merely an environmental design challenge but a cross-disciplinary issue at the intersection of public health, education, and climate adaptation. It calls for a shift from purely technical approaches toward integrated, participatory, and policy-oriented frameworks that position thermal comfort as a core component of school infrastructure.

articles.title: Candidate DNA methylation markers for gestational diabetes: findings from technical and biological validation in a South African population.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) increases risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Using Genome-wide Beadchip arrays, we previously reported differential methylation of 1046 CpG sites in women with GDM. This study aimed to validate three candidate CpG sites in an independent cohort of South African women with and without GDM. DNA methylation was assessed in maternal peripheral blood collected at < 28 weeks of gestation, at three top-most significant CpG sites within Calmodulin Binding Transcription Activator 1 (CAMTA1), Kelch domain-containing protein 3/ Male-Enhanced Antigen 1 (KLHDC3/MEA1), and Collectin Subfamily member 10 (COLECT10), using bisulfite pyrosequencing, in a technical validation group (12 GDM and 12 non-GDM), and an independent biological validation group (46 GDM and 135 non-GDM). Associations between differentially methylated CpGs and maternal clinical characteristics were assessed. Technical validation confirmed decreased methylation at cg23643951 (CAMTA1; -1.53-fold; p = 0.04) and cg21910650 (KLHDC3/MEA1; -1.57-fold; p = 0.004), and increased methylation at cg16306629 (COLECT10; 4.5-fold; p = 0.003) in women with GDM, consistent with the original array findings. No significant differences were observed in the biological validation group. Within the technical validation group, cg21910650 methylation was inversely correlated with fasting glucose (rho=-0.625; p = 0.015) and 1 h OGTT (rho=-0.555; p = 0.034), while cg16306629 was positively correlated with fasting glucose (rho = 0.709; p = 0.006). Technical validation confirmed differential methylation at three CpG sites, though these findings were not reproduced in the larger biological validation group, highlighting the need for validation in independent cohorts. Associations between CpG methylation with glucose concentrations suggest a potential association with glucose regulation during pregnancy, providing a foundation for future validation of these CpG sites as biomarkers for GDM.

articles.title: Non-invasive ventilation for general paediatricians.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Over the past two decades, non-invasive ventilation (NIV) has transitioned from being primarily used in specialist intensive care units to becoming a standard intervention in high dependency units, general paediatric units, emergency departments, and increasingly, patients' homes. Despite this expansion, many general paediatricians still perceive NIV as outside their primary expertise. With this review, we aim to address that gap and equip general paediatricians with the knowledge and confidence to appropriately initiate NIV, monitor its effectiveness, and recognise when escalation of care is required. We narratively reviewed the physiological rationale for non-invasive respiratory support (NRS), including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and the two principal modalities of NIV-continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP)-and summarised disease-specific evidence from recent literature, including randomised trials, systematic reviews, and international consensus statements. This is a narrative rather than a systematic review: we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Paediatric Respiratory Reviews for English-language publications from January 2018 to June 2026 using the terms "non-invasive ventilation", "high-flow nasal cannula", "CPAP", "BiPAP", and "children", supplemented by references already known to the authors, and selected articles for relevance and recency, prioritising randomised trials, systematic reviews, and consensus statements. HFNC is an oxygenation device rather than a ventilatory device, and its mechanism, clinical applications, and therapeutic goals differ from CPAP and BiPAP. We introduce the Indications, Contraindications, Equipment, Mode and settings, Assessment and monitoring, Next steps (ICEMAN) framework as a practical tool for structured and safe initiation of NIV in routine clinical practice, and apply it across bronchiolitis, acute severe asthma, pneumonia and hypoxaemic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease, and obstructive sleep apnoea.

CONCLUSION: The essential requirements to initiate NIV outside the PICU are well-trained staff, appropriate monitoring, a reliable oxygen supply, and a clear plan for escalation to a higher level of care. Selection of patients for NIV outside the PICU requires careful attention to indication, contraindications, equipment, monitoring, and escalation pathway by using frameworks like ICEMAN.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • HFNC, CPAP, and BiPAP are established, physiologically distinct respiratory therapies now used well beyond the PICU.

WHAT IS NEW: • The ICEMAN framework, updated with PALICC-2 ARDS criteria, gives non-specialists a structured, teachable approach to safe NIV initiation.

articles.title: Early serum electrolyte profiles in pediatric sepsis and their association with mortality.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Electrolyte disturbances are common in pediatric sepsis. This study aimed to identify early electrolyte patterns and evaluate their association with hospital mortality. A retrospective cohort of 1,589 pediatric sepsis patients (30 days-18 years) from the Shanghai Children's Hospital PICU sepsis database (2014 to present) was analyzed. Based on the first electrolyte panel (sodium, potassium, chloride, magnesium, calcium, and phosphate) measured within 24 h of PICU admission, patients were classified into three clusters using k-means clustering. Five Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between the three cluster subtypes and hospital mortality. Three distinct clusters were identified: Cluster 1 (high sodium, and chloride; n = 436), Cluster 2 (balanced electrolytes; n = 713), and Cluster 3 (low sodium, chloride, and calcium; n = 440). Overall mortality was 9.63%. Cluster 3 showed higher mortality than Cluster 2 (11.59% vs. 7.43%, Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.052). In multivariable Cox regression, Cluster 3 was associated with increased mortality risk (Model 3: HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.08-2.38), after adjusting for age, biomarkers, shock, and immunosuppression.

CONCLUSIONS: Early electrolyte profiling identifies a high-risk subtype (Cluster 3) characterized by lower levels of sodium, chloride, and calcium, which is associated with higher mortality in pediatric sepsis. The result suggests further investigation could focus on whether targeted early correction of these electrolyte disturbances can improve sepsis outcomes.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Electrolyte imbalances are highly prevalent in critically ill patients and have been increasingly recognized as prognostic markers in sepsis. Multiple studies have established single electrolyte levels as independent predictors of sepsis mortality, such as hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and hyperphosphatemia.

WHAT IS NEW: • The current results support early electrolyte profiling as a readily accessible, low-cost strategy for risk stratification in pediatric sepsis. Cluster 3 (lower levels of sodium, chloride, and calcium) appears to identify a high-risk subgroup with mortality rates exceeding 11%, even after accounting for major confounders.

articles.title: Adjunctive topical mitomycin C during endoscopic dilation for pediatric caustic esophageal stricture: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Caustic esophageal stricture is a major cause of pediatric dysphagia requiring repeated dilation. We assessed whether adjunctive topical mitomycin C (MMC) improves dysphagia resolution and reduces dilation sessions in children.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL (inception through May 17, 2026) for randomized controlled trials comparing dilation plus topical MMC with dilation alone in children with caustic esophageal stricture. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed; the single eligible adult RCT was reported narratively.

RESULTS: Three pediatric RCTs (221 patients; 110 MMC, 111 control) were pooled. MMC was associated with higher odds of dysphagia resolution (OR 7.82; 95% CI 4.17-14.65; I²=0%), and fewer dilation sessions (MD - 3.01; 95% CI - 3.30 to - 2.73; k = 2; I²=0%). No MMC-attributable adverse events occurred across 110 pooled MMC exposures, or 128 including non-pooled controlled evidence. Effects were robust in sensitivity analysis (OR 6.86; 95% CI 3.34-14.10).

CONCLUSION: In pediatric caustic esophageal stricture, adjunctive topical MMC improves dysphagia resolution and reduces dilation burden. Multicentre RCTs with longer follow-up remain needed.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261351544.

articles.title: HER2 protein expression patterns in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
articles.abstract: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma (GBCa) and extrahepatic bile duct cholangiocarcinoma (ECCa) are aggressive malignancies. For unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease, systemic therapy is the only treatment option. Survival rates remain dismal, thus a better understanding of their molecular biology and study of potential targeted therapies are important unmet needs.
