The tissue agnostic approval of HER2-targeted therapy for medications such as trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd) for tumors with strong (3+) HER2 expression by immunohistochemistry has motivated interest in HER2 expression among these tumor types. We sought to study the frequency and clinicopathologic features of HER2 expression in GBCa and ECCa. A 14-year retrospective analysis was performed on GBCa and ECCa, including metastatic cases. HER2 immunohistochemistry (Ventana, clone 4B5) was performed on eligible cases and interpreted using the CAP/ASCO gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scoring guidelines. Clinicopathologic features were assessed with respect to HER2 immunoreactivity, and HER2 scoring agreement was calculated using weighted kappa statistics. There were 59 total cases (GBCa n = 43, ECCa n = 16), with five cases demonstrating strong (3+) HER2 reactivity (8.5%), 22 cases showing 1 + or 2 + immunoreactivity (37.3%), and 32 with a score of 0 (54.2%). HER2 score was higher in metastases compared to corresponding primaries in 7/18 events (38.9%). Among factors considered, histologic grade differed most significantly by HER2 score, with negative cases more likely to be poorly differentiated (p = 0.006). HER2 status was not significantly associated with clinical outcomes (3-year PFS, all-cause mortality). The study describes the frequency and clinicopathologic correlates of HER2 expression in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

articles.title: Chest tube fixation strength depends on suture caliber and fixation technique rather than tube diameter: a biomechanical cadaver study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest tube dislodgement remains a relevant complication in emergency, trauma, and intensive care medicine. In a previous biomechanical study, the Modified Johannesburg technique using Mersilene USP 1 demonstrated superior fixation strength compared with other chest tube fixation techniques. The present study aimed to determine whether suture size, suture material, and chest tube diameter influence fixation strength.

METHODS: A prospective interventional biomechanical cadaveric study was performed using fresh porcine thoracic wall specimens. A total of 320 load-to-failure tests were conducted under standardized laboratory conditions. Two fixation techniques, Modified Johannesburg and Purse String, were compared using two chest tube diameters (20/28 Ch) and four non-absorbable braided suture configurations: Mersilene USP 1, Mersilene USP 2 - 0, Silk USP 1, and Silk USP 2 - 0. Each experimental group consisted of 20 specimens. Specimens were tested in a uniaxial testing machine until construct failure. Force [N] and elongation [mm] at failure were measured. The experiments were videotaped, and the failure mechanism was analyzed.

RESULTS: The Modified Johannesburg technique demonstrated significantly higher pull-out forces compared to the Purse String technique (125.0 vs. 66.4 N; p < 0.001), as did larger suture sizes (USP 1 vs. 2 - 0; p < 0.001) and Mersilene compared to Silk (114.6 vs. 76.9 N; p < 0.001). Chest tube size had only a very small and inconsistent effect on pull-out strength. The predominant failure mode was suture rupture (94.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Chest tube fixation strength is significantly influenced by fixation technique, suture size, and suture material. The effect of chest tube diameter on fixation strength appeared negligible. The Modified Johannesburg technique, size 1 sutures, and Mersilene material provided superior biomechanical stability. Since failure occurred predominantly by suture rupture, the suture appears to represent the weakest link of the fixation construct.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine in CKD: myths, facts, and evidence.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is increasingly used among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in regions where healthcare resources, accessibility and cultural acceptance influence treatment choices. However, its role in the treatment of CKD remains controversial, with conflicting perceptions ranging from therapeutic promise to concerns regarding unproven efficacy and potential toxicity. In this review, we critically examine some myths and facts surrounding TCM use in CKD through the framework of evidence-based medicine. Randomized evidence remains limited, but a few trials have reported clinically relevant signals. In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD, the multicenter SCHEMATIC trial found that add-on Rehmannia-6-based Chinese medicine was associated with a slower decline in eGFR over 48 weeks. In membranous nephropathy, an earlier multicenter randomized trial of Shenqi particle reported reductions in proteinuria and remission outcomes comparable with conventional immunosuppressive therapy. These findings are hypothesis-supporting rather than definitive: neither trial established a reduction in kidney failure, cardiovascular events or mortality, and independent confirmation is lacking. Importantly, safety should not be inferred from natural origin or historical use. Product quality, botanical authentication, pharmacokinetics, toxicological evaluation, herb-drug interactions and pharmacovigilance are essential components of responsible clinical evaluation. Future research should move beyond the broad question of whether 'TCM works' and instead focus on product-specific assessment using rigorous trial methodology, standardized manufacturing, precision CKD phenotyping and internationally applicable outcome measures. Chinese herbal medicines should neither be dismissed solely because they are traditional nor accepted solely because they are natural. Their future role in CKD care should be determined by the same principles applied to any therapeutic intervention: reproducible quality, demonstrated clinical benefit and an acceptable benefit-risk profile.

articles.title: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

articles.title: Restoring patients' voice in intensive care: augmentative and alternative communication for human-centred care.
Pathway-level secretome modulation in bronchial epithelial spheroids following indoor dust exposure.
articles.abstract: As humans spend most of their time indoors, they are continuously exposed to an array of indoor air pollutants. While exposure to individual indoor air pollutants may often occur at low levels, cumulative exposure to indoor air pollutants contributes substantially to the human exposome. Chronic inhalation of indoor air pollutants has been associated with multiple respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and respiratory infections. In this study, the cellular effects of an acute indoor dust exposure using a three-dimensional airway epithelial model were investigated. Bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE14o-) were cultured as spheroids and exposed to reference indoor dust (SRM 2585; 0-200 µg/mL) for 24 h. Metabolic activity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and secretome profiles were assessed. Indoor dust exposure did not induce morphological alterations or significant reductions in metabolic activity. Instead, a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS was observed. Cytokine analysis revealed selective cytokine modulation, while untargeted proteomics identified limited changes in individual protein abundance. Instead, pathway-level analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial differentiation-related pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that a 24 h indoor dust exposure may elicit subtle cellular responses rather than overt cytotoxicity or inflammatory activation. This study highlights the applicability of integrating functional, immunological, and proteomics-based approaches with 3D airway models to investigate cellular responses to complex environmental particle mixtures. However, direct extrapolation to human exposure scenarios is limited by uncertainties regarding effective cellular dose, particle localization and environmental representativeness. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations.

articles.title: Association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of long-bone fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of extremity long-bone fractures.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 601 adults who underwent internal fixation for extremity long-bone fractures and completed at least 12 months of follow-up. METS-IR was calculated using pre-operative body mass index, fasting blood glucose, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Potential confounders were selected by LASSO logistic regression with ten-fold cross-validation. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the independent and nonlinear associations between METS-IR and fracture nonunion. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed to examine whether the association was consistent across different clinical subgroups.

RESULTS: Of the 601 patients, 139 developed nonunion. METS-IR was higher in patients with nonunion than in those who achieved union (45 ± 5 vs. 36 ± 5, P < 0.001). After adjustment for LASSO-selected covariates, each one-unit increase in METS-IR was associated with higher odds of nonunion (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.24-1.38; P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant overall association and evidence of nonlinearity (P for overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.037). The association was generally consistent across sex, diabetes status, injury mechanism, and reduction method, while an interaction was observed for age (P for interaction = 0.029).

CONCLUSION: Higher METS-IR was independently associated with fracture nonunion and showed a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. METS-IR may provide additional metabolic information for identifying patients at increased risk of impaired fracture healing.

articles.title: IgA nephropathy: gut microbiome insights and unmet needs in pediatrics.
articles.abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerulopathy worldwide and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure in children and young adults. Well-established pathogenic pathways include genetic susceptibility, intrinsic B-cell glycosylation abnormalities, complement activation, and immune dysregulation, and accumulating evidence further places the gut microbiome at the center of IgAN pathogenesis via the gut-kidney axis. A critical evidence gap defines the field: no prospective cohort has characterized the gut microbiome in pediatric primary IgAN. This conceptual narrative review synthesizes well-validated mechanistic data from adult cohorts-most notably microbial-mediated IgA1 deglycosylation-and extrapolates these findings to pediatric populations through the lens of the developmental entanglement framework, which accounts for the synchronized maturation of the gut microbiome, mucosal immunity, and renal structure in early life. Using an adapted Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, we separately rate evidence quality for adult and pediatric populations, explicitly mark all pediatric extrapolations as unvalidated, and cautiously appraise indirect evidence from pediatric IgA vasculitis with nephritis (IgAVN). We further evaluate the translational potential of microbiome-guided strategies, and conclude with a pragmatic, stepwise research agenda centered on foundational cohort studies and emerging technologies to address the evidence gap. Closing this deficit will enable the development of non-invasive biomarkers and safe, mechanism-targeted therapies to prevent progressive renal failure in children with IgAN.

articles.title: Graphic novels for pediatric hypertension: enhancing health literacy and medication adherence through visual storytelling pilot study.
Hot topics in acute colonic diverticulitis: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Acute diverticulitis represents a heterogeneous clinical condition whose management has significantly evolved over the past decades. The traditional paradigm of routine surgical intervention has progressively shifted toward a more tailored, patient-centered approach integrating non-operative strategies, interventional radiology, and selective surgery. This narrative review, based on current literature and expert discussion from an international symposium, aims to summarize the most relevant "hot topics" in the management of diverticulitis, particularly in complicated forms. Conservative treatment remains the cornerstone for selected patients with early-stage disease, supported by accurate clinical and radiological stratification. Antibiotic therapy has also evolved, with increasing emphasis on shorter treatment courses and antimicrobial stewardship. The management of specific radiological findings, such as pericolic extraluminal air, has been refined, supporting non-operative approaches in stable patients while highlighting the importance of correct staging. Interventional radiology plays a key role in the treatment of diverticular abscesses, allowing effective sepsis control and reducing the need for emergency surgery. In the surgical field, the choice between Hartmann's procedure and primary anastomosis is now driven by patient-related factors rather than disease stage alone, while laparoscopic peritoneal lavage and damage control surgery represent alternative strategies in selected scenarios. Technical controversies, including vascular ligation, extent of resection, and intraoperative adjuncts, remain unresolved, particularly in emergency settings. Elective surgery has shifted from a rule-based to a quality-of-life-driven indication, emphasizing shared decision-making. Finally, robotic surgery is emerging as a feasible option in selected patients, although its role remains limited by logistical and organizational factors. Overall, the management of acute diverticulitis requires a multidisciplinary, individualized approach aimed at balancing short-term safety with long-term functional outcomes.

articles.title: Vessel Dependent Myocardium at Risk on Coronary CT Angiography Validated Against Dynamic CT Myocardial Perfusion Imaging.
articles.abstract: Accurate assignment of myocardial territories supplied by individual coronary arteries on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is essential for estimating myocardium at risk. Validation of coronary-based myocardial segmentation has been limited by co-registration challenges with perfusion imaging as the reference standard. By reconstructing coronary angiograms directly from the dynamic CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI), we ensured inherent co-registration between coronaries and perfusion maps. Vessel-specific myocardial territories were assigned using a minimum cost path (MCP) and validated against MBF-derived perfusion defects from the same acquisition. In 22 patients with 27 well-defined ischemic territories MCP-assigned territories showed moderate spatial overlap with CT-MPI-derived hypoperfusion (Dice coefficient 0.72 ± 0.13) with strong surface area correlation (r = 0.81, p < 0.001). Agreement was highest in the left anterior descending (LAD) territory. MCP-based tessellation using inherently co-registered CCTA and CT-MPI enables accurate vessel-specific myocardium-at-risk assessment and offers a promising platform for anatomical-functional integration in coronary disease.

articles.title: Oxalate Nephropathy in a patient with Neuroendocrine tumor receiving Long-acting Octreotide.
articles.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with 177Lu-DOTA-TATE along with long-acting Octreotide is an established treatment for metastatic neuroendocrine tumours (NETs). Renal dysfunction following PRRT is usually attributed to radiation-induced nephrotoxicity. A 55-year-old man with metastatic somatostatin receptor-positive NET, diagnosed in April 2023, initially received long-acting octreotide, external beam radiotherapy, and six cycles of etoposide chemotherapy. Persistent disease on Ga-68 DOTA-TATE PET imaging in November 2024 prompted treatment with four cycles of 177Lu-DOTA-TATE PRRT between February and December 2025, along with monthly long-acting octreotide injections. Baseline renal function was normal and remained stable at a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL till December 2025. He was referred to nephrology in March 2026 with an asymptomatic rise in serum creatinine to 2.3 mg/dL. Evaluation revealed subnephrotic proteinuria (820 mg/day), normal-sized kidneys, bland urinary sediments. PRRT-related nephrotoxicity and acute interstitial nephritis were initially considered. Kidney biopsy demonstrated extensive tubular calcium oxalate crystal deposition along with acute interstitial inflammation. In the absence of other identifiable causes of enteric hyperoxaluria, octreotide-induced pancreatic exocrine insufficiency was suspected as the most likely aetiology. The patient received a short course of corticosteroids in view of interstitial inflammation in the biopsy. Serum creatinine declined to 1.5 mg/dL on follow-up. Early recognition is critical, as progressive renal dysfunction may compromise eligibility for PRRT, a cornerstone treatment for NETs.

articles.title: Mechanism of Action of Qingjin Huazhuo Formula in Treating Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Based on Proteomics, Traditional Chinese Medicine Component Analysis, and Network Pharmacology.
articles.abstract: Qingjin Huazhuo Formula (QJHZF) is a traditional Chinese medicinal prescription used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). To investigate its mechanism of action, a COPD rat model with phlegm heat and blood stasis syndrome was established by combining cigarette smoke exposure and passive swimming. After model confirmation, QJHZF was intragastrically administered at 10.9 g/kg/day for 14 days. The serum inflammatory cytokines and pulmonary oxidative stress indicators in rats were measured using ELISA and biochemical assays, respectively. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was performed for proteomic analysis of lung tissues and identification of QJHZF components. Network pharmacology predicted potential targets for COPD treatment. After identifying the core targets through intersection analysis of proteomic targets and network pharmacology targets, qRT-PCR and molecular docking were subsequently employed for validation. Results indicate that QJHZF can inhibit inflammation and reduce oxidative stress associated with COPD. Overall, 114 differentially expressed proteins were identified. In QJHZF, 160 active compounds were identified, with 2,178 possible QJHZF targets involved in COPD treatment. A total of 29 compounds targeting 28 core targets were ultimately identified as the key constituents of QJHZF in treating COPD. qRT-PCR and molecular docking confirmed their pivotal role. KEGG enrichment analysis showed significant enrichment of the core targets in 15 pathways implicated in COPD-related inflammation and oxidative stress. Therefore, this study provides preliminary evidence for a multi-level network of 29 components - 28 targets - 15 pathways through which QJHZF treats COPD, laying a valuable foundation for further in-depth investigation.

articles.title: Intracardiac thrombus and multiple venous thromboses revealing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Nephrotic syndrome is associated with a hypercoagulable state, leading to an increased risk of potentially severe thromboembolic events. Although venous thromboses predominantly involve the renal veins and deep veins of the lower extremities, intracardiac thrombosis remains an exceptionally rare manifestation, particularly as the initial presenting feature. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia and recent cholecystectomy, who was admitted for lower-limb edema and hematuria of two weeks' duration. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multiple thrombotic events, including deep vein thrombosis of the lower extremities, partial thrombosis of the left renal vein, and a left ventricular intracardiac thrombus measuring 23 × 20 mm. Laboratory investigations demonstrated nephrotic syndrome with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 10 g/g and hypoalbuminemia of 23 g/L, associated with stage 2 acute kidney injury. Immunological testing was negative, including anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) antibodies. Kidney biopsy established the diagnosis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Management consisted of therapeutic anticoagulation, diuretic therapy, and corticosteroid treatment, resulting in progressive clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights the exceptional occurrence of a left ventricular thrombus associated with multiple venous thromboses as the presenting manifestation of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. It underscores the importance of systematically investigating underlying glomerular disease in patients presenting with multiple or unusual thrombotic events, particularly in the presence of significant proteinuria.

articles.title: Development and Characterization of VNARs Targeting Edwardsiella piscicida GAPDH.
articles.abstract: Edwardsiella piscicida is an intracellular bacterial pathogen that causes edwardsiellosis in Japanese flounder and poses a serious threat to aquaculture. Surface-localized glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) has been implicated in bacterial adhesion and immune recognition, making it a promising antigenic target for infection control. In this study, we generated shark-derived variable domains of immunoglobulin novel antigen receptors (VNARs) targeting recombinant GAPDH from E. piscicida and evaluated their potential as antibody-based agents for controlling edwardsiellosis. A banded houndshark (Triakis scyllium) was immunized with recombinant GAPDH, and anti-GAPDH VNARs were subsequently isolated from the spleen using a combination screening method. Three VNAR clones, designated 2 - 1, 3 - 2, and 4-11, exhibited concentration-dependent binding to recombinant GAPDH and retained their binding activity after exposure to high temperatures or acidic conditions. Epitope binning indicated that the three clones recognized non-overlapping epitopes. Among the tested fish-pathogenic bacteria, clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 preferentially bound Edwardsiella species, including E. piscicida and E. anguillarum. In GAPDH activity assays, the combination of clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 showed the strongest inhibition of recombinant GAPDH activity, with an IC50 of 9.5 ng/ml. The same combination also most effectively inhibited E. piscicida growth in vitro, with an IC50 of 13.6 µg/ml. In a Japanese flounder challenge test, combined administration of clones 2 - 1 and 4-11 resulted in a final survival rate of 91.7%. These findings suggest that anti-GAPDH VNARs may provide a promising antibody-based strategy for the control of edwardsiellosis in aquaculture.

articles.title: Cumulative incidence of chronic rhinosinusitis and association with allergic multimorbidity in a tertiary center cohort of patients with allergic rhinitis: a long-term analysis.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic rhinitis (AR) affects up to 50% of adults globally. This study was undertaken to evaluate cumulative incidence of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) in patients with AR and to investigate the association between CRS and clinical features of AR, sensitization patterns, concomitant atopic comorbidities and AR severity.

METHOD: This retrospective, observational, multicenter study included consecutive adult patients with a diagnosis of AR without CRS at first assessment. Data covering clinical information from AR onset to the last follow-up were collected.

RESULTS: Out of the 198 patients included (54.0% female, median age at AR diagnosis 19 years old, IQR 11-30), CRS developed in 65.2% of patients during follow-up. Among those who developed CRS, 51.2% had radiological confirmation, and 31.0% were diagnosed with CRS with nasal polyposis (CRSwNP). Multivariate analysis revealed no independent predictors of CRS at the time of AR diagnosis (Hazard ratio (HR) with [95% confidence intervals (CI)] 1.24 [0.68-2.25], age at AR diagnosis (per year change) 1.00 [0.98-1.02], atopic morbidities 1.81 [0.8-4.11], and polysensitization 0.76 [0.8-1.58]). At last follow up (median 19 [IQR 9-29] years from AR diagnosis), AR was moderate-persistent in 47.4%. Patients with CRSwNP have a higher proportion of asthma (77.5% vs 43.8%, p=0.0005) and ASA hypersensitivity (27.5% vs. 5,6%, p=0.0010) as compared to CRSsNP. Overall, only CRS was independently associated to moderate-persistent AR at last follow-up (HR 2.90 [1.51, 5.56]).

CONCLUSION: Almost two-thirds of subjects with AR develop CRS during the disease course. Years after AR diagnosis, CRS is the only independent factor associated with moderate-persistent AR, increasing almost three times its risk.

articles.title: Integrated Atrial Mechanics-Biomarker Profiling Predicts Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Improvement in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: Improvement of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is a relevant phenotype in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but its substrate remains unclear. In 175 HFrEF patients followed prospectively for 24 months with serial echocardiography, left atrial (LA) strain and 16 biomarkers, LVEF improvement (increase ≥ 10 points to > 40%) occurred in 80 patients (45.7%). Improvers were more often women and non-ischaemic, with smaller LV volumes, better LV longitudinal strain, shorter atrial conduction time and lower ANP, relaxin-2 and COL4A1; baseline LA volume and strain did not differ. An exploratory eight-variable model had apparent and optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.93 and 0.84. NT-proBNP and LA reservoir strain diverged progressively between groups. Improvement was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.25; 95% CI 0.08-0.75) and fewer heart failure hospitalisations (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.18-0.78). LVEF improvement reflects progressive atrial and neurohormonal reverse remodelling rather than favourable baseline atrial mechanics.

articles.title: Heterogeneous responses to embryonic critical period perturbations within the Drosophila larval locomotor circuit.
articles.abstract: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.

articles.title: Readability, understandability and actionability of BAUS and EAU patient education materials for common non-oncological urological conditions.
articles.abstract: Background and AimsPatient education materials (PEMs) support patient understanding and engagement in care. This study evaluated the readability, understandability and actionability of non-oncological urological PEMs produced by the British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) and the European Association of Urology (EAU), and explored agreement between human and AI-assisted PEMAT-P assessment.Methods and ResultsA cross-sectional descriptive analysis assessed eight matched PEMs relating to urinary tract infection, urinary incontinence, benign prostatic enlargement/lower urinary tract symptoms, and nocturnal polyuria. Readability was assessed using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), and Gunning Fog Index. Understandability and actionability were assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-P). Mean FKGL was 11.85 ± 2.77, SMOG 13.24 ± 2.39, Gunning Fog 14.09 ± 3.22, and FRE 48.5 ± 13.32. All materials exceeded the recommended reading level. Mean PEMAT-P understandability and actionability were 91.0% and 88.3%. Human-AI item-level agreement for understandability and actionability was 83.6% and 81.8%; Cohen's κ was 0.25 and 0.23, and Gwet's AC1 was 0.79 and 0.76.ConclusionThe materials exceeded recommended reading levels despite variable PEMAT-P scores. Human vs AI differences remained, requiring further evaluation of PEMs to establish the potential role of AI as an adjunct to human PEMAT-P assessment.

articles.title: Preventing Low-Value Admission for Suspected Osteomyelitis: A Teachable Moment.
Enhancing visual interpretability and explainability in functional survival trees and forests.
articles.abstract: Functional survival models are key tools for analyzing time-to-event data with complex predictors, such as functional or high-dimensional inputs. Despite their predictive strength, these models often lack interpretability, which limits their value in practical decision-making and risk analysis. This study investigates two key survival models: the functional survival tree (FST) and the functional random survival forests (FRSFs). It introduces novel methods and tools to enhance the interpretability of FST models and improve the explainability of FRSF ensembles. Applications to simulated data and to a real intensive care dataset illustrate that the proposed approaches provide post-hoc graphical and functional summaries that facilitate the interpretation of FSTs and the explanation of forest-level predictions.

articles.title: Changing Patterns of Transient Ischemic Attack Evaluation in US Emergency Departments.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For US patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with transient ischemic attack (TIA), guidelines recommend resource-intensive multimodal evaluation to optimize secondary stroke prevention. These resources are not available in all EDs, and national patterns of ED TIA care are not well described.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate national trends in ED TIA care, including discharge practices, imaging use, and associated costs, and to assess patient- and hospital-level factors associated with these patterns.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective repeated cross-sectional study of ED visits using the 2013-2021 National Emergency Department Sample of the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project, a weighted, nationally representative annual sample of ED visits in the US. TIA and stroke encounters during the study period were identified among patients aged 18 years or older by a first-listed International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision or Tenth Revision code for TIA or stroke diagnosis. Analyses were performed from October 2024 to April 2026.

EXPOSURES: Calendar year.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: ED discharge; imaging use among discharged TIA encounters; and inflation-adjusted ED cost per discharged encounter.

RESULTS: This study included 2 151 408 (95% CI, 2 107 855-2 194 960) weighted ED visits for TIA (1 194 630 [55.5%] female; mean [SEM] age, 69.8 [0.05] years). Adjusted models found the predicted probability of discharge increased from 45% (95% CI, 43%-46%) in 2013 to 66% (95% CI, 64%-68%) in 2021 (P < .001 for trend). During this time, mean ED charges increased from $1746 (95% CI, $1662-$1830) to $2755 (95% CI, $2674-$2836) per encounter (P < .001 for trend). Imaging use among discharged TIA encounters increased substantially, including computed tomography angiography (predicted probability, 4% [95% CI, 3%-4%] in 2013 vs 45% [95% CI, 42%-47%] in 2021; P < .001 for trend) and magnetic resonance imaging (predicted probability, 17% [95% CI, 16%-19%] in 2013 vs 53% [95% CI, 50%-55%] in 2021; P < .001 for trend). Rate of discharge was higher in rural encounters than in urban encounters for all years studied, and the rate of magnetic resonance imaging use was lower.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cross-sectional study demonstrates a shift in TIA care over time that suggests increased use of the ED to expedite evaluation for TIA that previously occurred during a brief hospitalization. This approach has consequences in terms of cost and ED throughput and may not be as feasible in rural hospitals as it is in urban hospitals.

articles.title: Orforglipron for Type 2 Diabetes and Pancreatic Risk Assessment-Reply.
Orforglipron for Type 2 Diabetes and Pancreatic Risk Assessment.
Maternal Autoimmune Diseases During Pregnancy and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy may influence the long-term risk of immune-mediated diseases in offspring, but the relative contributions of prenatal and familial factors to offspring type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between a broad spectrum of maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy and offspring T1D, and to compare the associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study included children identified from national health registers who were born in Sweden between 2001 and 2014, and were followed up from birth until T1D diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from November 2025 to June 2026.

EXPOSURE: Parental autoimmune diseases diagnosed before or during pregnancy, identified from national health registers.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident T1D in offspring. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs for offspring T1D were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models. Associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases before childbirth with offspring T1D were directly compared, and cousin analyses were performed to assess the potential role of shared familial factors.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 10 273 (0.71%) of the 1 455 645 included individuals (51.4% male and 48.6% female; median [IQR], age 15.3 [11.9-19.0] years) developed T1D. Maternal autoimmune disease during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D (adjusted HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.46-1.68); paternal autoimmune disease before childbirth showed a similar association (adjusted HR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.37-1.67). No overall difference was observed in maternal-paternal comparisons (ratio of HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.92-1.17), but heterogeneity was observed across specific disease categories. A clear gradient in T1D risk was observed according to parental T1D status, with the highest risk among offspring with both parents affected, followed by paternal T1D only and maternal T1D only. In cousin analyses, the association with maternal autoimmune disease was attenuated but persisted (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.08-1.50).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this population-based cohort study, maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D. Comparable associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D suggest a role of shared familial susceptibility, while disease-specific differences indicate that some conditions could have parental-specific effects, suggesting contributions from shared familial susceptibility and potential intrauterine mechanisms.

articles.title: Internet Intervention for Functional Seizures: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Functional seizures (FS) are a common and disabling presentation in neurology clinics, but evidence-based treatments are difficult to access in Australia and in many regions globally. A brief, scalable, internet-delivered intervention could narrow this treatment gap.

OBJECTIVE: To compare a self-guided and a therapist-guided internet-based intervention for FS, each delivered alongside standard care, with standard care alone.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a 3-arm, parallel, randomized clinical trial conducted between February 2022 and April 2024, with follow-up through to 12 months after randomization. The location was a specialist outpatient clinic in Melbourne, Australia. Included were adults (≥18 years) with a documented diagnosis of FS confirmed by video electroencephalogram monitoring and at least 4 seizures per month, excluding comorbid active epilepsy.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to a self-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, therapist-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, or standard care alone. Re-PROGRAM is an internet-based intervention developed for FS, comprising 5 structured sessions integrating lifestyle factors, seizure management techniques, and elements of cognitive behavioral, acceptance and commitment, and dialectical behavior therapy.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was monthly seizure frequency at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after randomization, recorded by daily prospective seizure diary, with retrospective estimates used for incomplete records. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, quality of life, psychosocial functioning, and somatic symptoms.

RESULTS: Of 220 individuals screened for eligibility, 107 (mean [SD] age 36.0 [12.4] years; 89 female [83%]) were randomized. Of these participants, 96 contributed to the full analysis set (29 self-guided, 34 therapist-guided, 33 standard care). The self-guided arm produced significantly greater overall reductions in monthly seizure frequency than standard care (rate ratio [RR], 0.35; 95% CI, 0.18-0.69; Holm-Bonferroni [HB] method P = .006), with sustained between-group effects at 6 weeks (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76; HB P = .02), 6 months (RR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12-0.78; HB P = .04), and 12 months (RR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.16-0.78; HB P = .03). The self-guided arm also showed greater improvements in anxiety than standard care at all 3 time points and in depression and mental quality of life at 1 or more time points. The therapist-guided arm showed greater improvement in anxiety at 6 months, but reductions in seizure frequency did not reach statistical significance. Direct comparison between the 2 active arms showed no significant difference in seizure reduction (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.33-1.36). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of the primary findings. No adverse events occurred in any arm.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial show that in adults with FS, a self-guided internet-based intervention reduced seizure frequency and improved anxiety relative to standard care, offering a scalable option for patients unable to access specialist psychological care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Identifier: ACTRN12622000262707.

articles.title: Maternal Autoimmune Diseases and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes.
Traumatic cardiac tamponade: Most delayed presentation.
Diastolic Function From Artificial Intelligence-Derived Electrocardiography in Mitral Annulus Calcification.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a validated artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model for left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) can provide prognostic risk stratification in patients with significant mitral annulus calcification (MAC).

METHODS: We included patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography and electrocardiography within 1 week between September 1, 2001, and April 30, 2023, and were not included in the AI-ECG LVDF training data set. Significant MAC was defined by consensus echocardiography criteria. Patients were assigned to 3 myocardial disease (MD) categories by the AI-ECG LVDF algorithm grading: normal/grade 1 LVDF (MD-1), grade 2 LVDF (MD-2), and grade 3 LVDF (MD-3). The analysis focused on prognostic stratification in this clinically distinct population. The primary end point was all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Of 2506 patients with significant MAC (mean age, 77 years; 64.1% female), 709 (28.3%) were classified as MD-1, 1510 (60.3%) as MD-2, and 287 (11.5%) as MD-3. Advanced MD grade correlated with older age, male sex, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher rates of comorbidities, and worse LVDF echocardiographic parameters. During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 1059 (42.3%) patients died. Multivariable survival analysis found MD-2 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.19 to 1.64) and MD-3 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92) to be independently associated with higher mortality risk, also after adjustment for mitral inflow diastolic pressure gradients.

CONCLUSION: Myocardial disease grading derived from AI-ECG LVDF is independently associated with increased mortality risk in patients with significant MAC, underscoring its potential value in identifying high-risk patients in this challenging clinical population.

articles.title: Empirical Estimation of the Discount Rate for Pharmacoeconomic Evaluation in China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The discount rate is a key parameter in pharmacoeconomic evaluation. This study aims to empirically estimate a discount rate for pharmacoeconomic evaluations in China.

METHODS: The discount rate was calculated using both the social opportunity cost (SOC) method and the social rate of time preference (SRTP) method, and then a final rate was derived by weighting them. Annual national time-series data from 2001 to 2024 were used for the empirical analysis. Data were mainly obtained from the China Statistical Yearbook, the China Household Survey Yearbook, and the official websites of the People's Bank of China and the National Bureau of Statistics.

RESULTS: Empirical results showed that the discount rates derived from the SOC and SRTP methods are 1.24% and 9.00%, respectively. The discount rate derived from the consumption-based SRTP method was higher than that obtained from the investment-based SOC method. Using a weighted average approach with weights of 0.59 (SOC) and 0.41 (SRTP), we obtain an overall discount rate of 4.43%. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the final estimate is moderately sensitive to the choice of consumption growth proxies and time windows. The weighted average rate spans 2.94% to 6.62% across parameter scenarios and 3.52% to 9.66% across sub-period windows; the latter is widened by earlier high-growth periods, with recent windows close to the 4.43% central value.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides updated empirical evidence on the discount rate for costs in pharmacoeconomic evaluations in China. The central estimate of 4.43%, with a sensitivity range of 2.94% to 9.66%, serves as an empirical reference for future reassessment of the discount rate.

articles.title: Fournier's Gangrene-Associated ECG-Pickelhaube Sign: The Evanescent STEMI-Mimic.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The spiked helmet sign (SHS), or Pickelhaube sign, is a rare pseudo-ST-segment elevation pattern described in critically ill patients without acute myocardial infarction.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with class III obesity and diabetes presented in septic shock from extensive Fournier's gangrene. After emergent debridement, telemetry showed anterior ST-segment elevation prompting ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) activation. Serial electrocardiograms demonstrated pre-QRS baseline elevation merging with the QRS and transient anterolateral ST-segment elevation consistent with the Pickelhaube sign. Troponins remained normal, and contrast echocardiography showed hyperdynamic systolic function without regional wall-motion abnormalities. ST elevation resolved spontaneously within 30 minutes, and angiography was deferred. He required vasopressors, continuous venovenous hemofiltration, repeated debridement, and wound vacuum-assisted closure before discharge to long-term acute care.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates the Pickelhaube sign during Fournier's gangrene with septic shock. Recognizing its morphology and evolution, along with biomarkers, echocardiography, and clinical context, can distinguish pseudo-STEMI from acute coronary occlusion and avoid unnecessary angiography.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: The Pickelhaube sign can occur in severe necrotizing soft-tissue infection and septic shock and may closely mimic acute STEMI. Serial electrocardiograms, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography, and hemodynamic context help distinguish this pseudo-STEMI pattern from acute coronary occlusion.

articles.title: AAOLCA in a Child Presenting With Fever and Cardiac Arrest: Diagnostic Overlap With Acute Myocarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anomalous aortic origin of the left coronary artery (AAOLCA) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly causing myocardial ischemia and sudden cardiac death. Despite differing in pathophysiology from acute myocarditis, AAOLCA can present with a clinically indistinguishable acute picture.

CASE SUMMARY: We report an 11-year-old child with no prior cardiac history presenting with fever (40 °C), syncope, cardiac arrest, and cardiogenic shock. Elevated troponin and reduced ejection fraction initially suggested acute myocarditis, which could not be excluded. Atypical features-absent arrhythmia, rapid biomarker normalization, and fluctuating ventricular function-prompted further evaluation. Echocardiography and coronary angiography identified AAOLCA with a hemodynamically significant intramural segment; dynamic ischemia was confirmed during angiography. Surgical unroofing resulted in clinical recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: AAOLCA should be considered when pediatric myocarditis presents atypically. Echocardiography is essential. When concurrent myocarditis cannot be excluded, surgical timing should be individualized; here, a period of stabilization preceded definitive repair.

articles.title: Re: Dogra et al.: Outcomes with Endogenous Endophthalmitis from Candidal versus Bacterial Sepsis (Ophthalmol Retina. 2026. In press. doi: 10.1016/j.oret.2026.07.016).
The effectiveness of ergonomic gloves to reduce hand-arm vibration exposure: A case study of grass mowers.
articles.abstract: Background: The use of vibrating power hand tools can lead to Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS). Objective: This quasi-experimental research aimed to determine the effectiveness of ergonomic gloves in reducing vibrations from lawn mowers. Methods: The research instruments were questionnaires. Additionally, this study used a hand and arm vibration meter (SVANTEK SV106A) to measure vibration levels. A repeated-measures design with three conditions (without gloves, with cotton gloves, and with ergonomically designed gloves) was employed in 15 participants. Data was analyzed with Repeated-measure ANOVA, and descriptive statistics. Results: Comparison of average daily vibration levels showed that A(8) vibration while using ergonomic gloves (x̄ = 3.50 m/s2) was less than using cotton gloves (x̄ = 4.89 m/s2), and bare hands (x̄ = 5.23 m/s2) had statistically significant differences of p-value = 0.002 and p-value = 0.003, respectively. Notably, despite the reduction achieved with ergonomic gloves, the A(8) vibration exposure (3.50 m/s2) remained above the Exposure Action Value (EAV) of 2.5 m/s2, emphasizing the need for supplementary administrative controls. Additionally, 80% of participants indicated a moderate level of satisfaction regarding the ergonomic gloves. Conclusion: This study demonstrated how agriculturalists and workers can utilize this low-cost, anti-vibration glove prototype constructed from cotton gloves stitched with NBR foam. Furthermore, manufacturing companies can utilize the findings of this study to conduct further research on designing affordable and highly accessible anti-vibration gloves.

articles.title: Retroperitoneal infection and vascular complications: A diagnostic blind spot.
International Expert Consensus on Demulcents as Mucosal Barriers in Upper Respiratory Tract Infections.
articles.abstract: PurposeDemulcents form protective mucoadhesive films on oropharyngeal mucosa and provide symptomatic relief in upper respiratory tract infections, yet their mode of action, clinical indications, and desirable properties remain poorly defined. An international advisory board convened on 19 February 2026 comprising experts in otorhinolaryngology, phoniatrics, and pharmacology from Germany, Croatia, Colombia, and Ecuador. The panel reviewed preclinical data, alongside targeted literature evidence, and discussed clinical experiences with demulcents and their use in patients.Major findingsReviewed clinical studies suggested symptomatic benefit, particularly in reducing throat irritation, dryness, and cough-associated discomfort, although the available evidence remains limited. Consensus was achieved across four domains: (I) mechanism of action - local physical barrier formation through mucoadhesive film; (II) clinical indications - common cold with sore throat and dry cough, laryngopharyngeal reflux, vocal fatigue, allergy-related irritation, and post-operative throat discomfort; (III) desirable properties - rapid onset, prolonged mucosal contact, acceptable taste, and broad safety profile; (IV) research priorities - prospective studies evaluating complication reduction using symptom scales and objective endpoints such as antibiotic prescriptions and healthcare utilization.ConclusionsTogether, experts agreed that demulcents represent a rational treatment approach to symptomatic upper respiratory symptom management through local barrier formation.

articles.title: Bamboo-Inspired Homogeneous Porous Aerogel via Gas Foaming Assisted by Freeze-Drying for High-Sensitivity Flexible Pressure Sensors.
articles.abstract: Flexible piezoresistive sensors are pivotal in personalized healthcare. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and a broad linear range remains a formidable challenge owing to rapid structural densification of porous materials. Inspired by the multiscale composite structure of bamboo, this study addresses the existing challenge by proposing a novel MXene aerogel sensor, reinforced by compounding cellulose nanofiber (CNF) Several instances of CNFs (which were introduced during copyediting) have been reverted back to CNF, consistent with our original submission where the abbreviation was defined as cellulose nanofiber (CNF). Corresponding grammatical adjustments are made to match this usage. This change only standardizes the abbreviation and does not alter any scientific content. and bamboo cellulose. By leveraging a uniform conductive network constructed on CNF (simulating bamboo parenchyma cells to disperse the vascular bundles) and the supporting effect of the bamboo cellulose skeleton (mimicking vascular bundles to provide support), premature collapse is effectively resisted. Moreover, inspired by the hollow cell cavity structure of bamboo, a stable porous architecture is constructed via gas foaming and freeze-drying, enabling it to effectively reconcile the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and the detection range. The sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 148.29 kPa-1 (0-15 kPa) and a wide effective working range extending up to 100 kPa. This superior electromechanical performance enables the precise detection of full-spectrum physiological signals ranging from subtle pulse waveforms to large-scale joint movements and facilitates assistive rehabilitation for post-stroke finger therapy via human-computer interaction. Augmented by a support vector machine algorithm, the sensor has a wireless sleep monitoring capability and achieves a high classification accuracy of 96.5% in identifying distinct breathing states. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant application potential in next-generation intelligent home health management systems.

articles.title: Long-term Glycemia and Risk of Death in Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes: A UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mortality risk is increased in cystic fibrosis (CF)-related diabetes, but its relationship with long-term glycemia is unclear.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Using UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry data, we estimated the association between updated interval mean hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and mortality using Poisson regression to estimate mortality rates adjusted for age and sex and rate ratios adjusted for age, calendar year, sex, BMI, pulmonary function, and use of CF transmembrane conductance regulator modulators.

RESULTS: Of 4,477 individuals contributing 31,311 person-years of follow-up, 758 died. Mortality rates increased progressively with higher updated interval mean HbA1c values. Compared with HbA1c ≤42 mmol/mol, adjusted mortality rate ratios were 1.41 (95% CI 1.15-1.73) for HbA1c >42-53 mmol/mol, 1.66 (95% CI 1.33-2.07) for HbA1c >53-69 mmol/mol, and 1.93 (95% CI 1.53-2.43) for HbA1c >69 mmol/mol.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher HbA1c was associated with a clinically and statistically significant increase in mortality among individuals with CF-related diabetes.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Perioperative Management and Follow-Up After Mandibular Distraction Osteogenesis in a Neonate With Severe Pierre Robin Sequence: A Report.
articles.abstract: This case describes the multidisciplinary perioperative management and 7-month follow-up of a neonate with severe Pierre Robin sequence (PRS) who underwent mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO), with a particular focus on difficult-airway management, distraction-device care, nutritional support, and recovery of oral feeding. The clinical course, multidisciplinary perioperative management, and postdischarge follow-up of this neonate were retrospectively reviewed, and the case was prepared in accordance with the CARE case-report guideline. After surgery, mandibular advancement was achieved and upper-airway patency improved. The infant was successfully extubated on postoperative day 10, remained clinically stable on spontaneous breathing, and maintained an SpO₂ above 95%. No wound infection, pressure injury, or other major postoperative complication was documented during hospitalization. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6, and 7 months after discharge showed continued somatic growth and stable airway status; however, recovery of oral feeding was slower, and nasogastric tube feeding remained necessary for an extended period. This case suggests that perioperative care after MDO in severe PRS should address the difficult airway, distraction-device management, nutritional support, and functional rehabilitation in parallel. Improvement in airway anatomy and recovery of oral feeding may follow different time courses; therefore, airway recovery should not be used as the sole predictor of oral-feeding recovery. In infants with complex airway and feeding problems, multidisciplinary collaboration can provide a practical framework for integrating specialist assessment and longitudinal care.

articles.title: Simple is Best: Direct Skin Grafting of Dura After Radical Debridement of Frontal Osteomyelitis.
articles.abstract: Frontal defects with chronic implant infection, calvarial osteomyelitis, and dural exposure are difficult to reconstruct. A 54-year-old man presented with chronic purulent frontal wounds and exposed cranial hardware after previous fracture fixation. After combined neurosurgical and plastic surgical debridement, all hardware and infected bone were removed. Bilateral supratrochlear-based forehead flaps covered viable exposed calvarium. Two adjacent residual defects over intact, fibrotic, visibly vascular dura were covered directly with a split-thickness skin graft. Fibrin sealant was used to improve graft-bed contact and reduce fixation sutures over the dura. At 6 weeks, the reconstruction remained stable without wound-related or neurological complications. This case supports a recipient-bed-based salvage strategy after complete source control: vascularized tissue for exposed calvarium and direct skin grafting for small areas of intact vascular dura when more complex reconstruction is undesirable.

articles.title: American Epilepsy Society/Congress of Neurological Surgeons Epilepsy Surgery Clinical Practice Guideline.
articles.abstract: This practice guideline from the American Epilepsy Society and the Congress of Neurological Surgeons provides evidence-based recommendations for surgical treatment of epilepsy for adults and children. It is an update to previous practice parameters published by the Academy of Neurology in 2003. The multidisciplinary panel addressed resective procedures for mesial temporal epilepsy, neocortical epilepsy, and resection/disconnection of hypothalamic hamartoma. It also examined evidence for callosotomy in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. It did not intentionally address neurostimulation treatment. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Education methodology, and it was also used for decision making. This guideline considers not only seizure outcomes but also other critical and important outcomes. Seizures, quality of life, mortality, adverse events, and verbal memory loss were considered critical outcomes, whereas other neuropsychological deficits besides verbal memory loss (ie, naming, fluency), neuropsychiatric, and social outcomes were considered important outcomes.

articles.title: In Vivo Study of Topical Bimatoprost, Latanoprost, Travoprost in Comparison with Minoxidil on Hair Growth in C57BL/6 Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alopecia significantly affects psychological well-being and social functioning. Standard treatments, like minoxidil and finasteride, are limited by delayed efficacy, need for lifelong use, and adverse effects. Prostaglandin analogs (PGAs), originally developed for ocular hypertension, have shown promise in promoting hair growth. This study compares their effects with minoxidil in a murine model.

AIM AND OBJECTIVES: To compare the effects of bimatoprost, latanoprost, and travoprost on hair growth in C57BL/6 mice, with evaluation of hair density, follicle diameter, and growth rate using minoxidil as the comparator.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: After Institutional Animal Ethics Committee approval, 40 male C57BL/6 mice (aged 6-7 weeks, weighing 20-25 g) were randomized into five groups ( n = 8 in each group): (1) vehicle control, (2) minoxidil 5%, (3) latanoprost 0.005%, (4) bimatoprost 0.03%, and (5) travoprost 0.004%. Drugs were applied topically to shaved dorsal skin daily for 28 days. Hair growth was assessed by follicle density, bulb diameter, and area of regrowth using ImageJ from photographs taken on days 1, 7, 15, and 28.

RESULTS: All PGAs significantly increased hair density compared to vehicle control (vehicle control: 1.50 ± 0.55 vs. latanoprost: 7.50 ± 1.69, bimatoprost: 7.75 ± 2.87, travoprost: 6.87 ± 3.40; P = 0.001). Latanoprost and bimatoprost showed higher hair density than minoxidil (3.75 ± 2.87; P = 0.038 and 0.010, respectively). Hair follicle diameter was greater with PGAs (latanoprost: 53.12 ± 5.30, bimatoprost: 51.87 ± 7.52, travoprost: 48.12 ± 3.47 μm) versus vehicle control (27.91 ± 5.57 μm, P = 0.001) and minoxidil (38.12 ± 5.46 μm, P = 0.001). Bimatoprost showed the greatest regrowth by day 28, while latanoprost demonstrated earlier onset by day 15. PGAs also caused darker pigmentation and longer hair.

LIMITATIONS: The present study duration was limited to 4 weeks. Minoxidil (positive control) did not show noticeable hair growth because its effects usually take 6-8 weeks to appear.

CONCLUSION: Topical PGAs improved key hair growth parameters. Bimatoprost and latanoprost showed early and superior efficacy by day 28.

articles.title: Peer review for clinicians and researchers: A practical guide.
articles.journal: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association
articles.abstract: Peer review is the process by which scholarly work, research findings, or scientific ideas are critically evaluated by independent experts within the same field. Peer review acts as a fundamental quality assurance mechanism that helps safeguard the scientific literature by identifying methodological weaknesses, ensuring the relevance and rigor of research questions, and verifying that conclusions are supported by appropriately conducted studies and valid analyses. This article provides an overview of the editorial workflow, examines the essential components of a high-quality peer review, and discusses the advantages and limitations of various peer-review models. It further presents a structured framework for systematic manuscript appraisal and outlines the ethical principles that underpin responsible reviewing. Finally, the article proposes a strategic roadmap for the Saudi Gastroenterology Association to establish sustainable reviewer-training pathways, with the goal of cultivating a new generation of Saudi researchers and reviewers capable of contributing to and leading the global scientific discourse.

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Image-Guided Aspiration Techniques for Periprosthetic Hip Infection: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Image-guided fluid aspiration is a key component in the diagnostic work-up of suspected prosthetic joint infection of the hip (PJI). Fluoroscopy, ultrasound (US), and computed tomography (CT) are frequently employed to guide aspiration; however, comparative evidence regarding their diagnostic performance and procedural outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the diagnostic accuracy and technical performance of these modalities.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL were searched for studies evaluating fluoroscopy-, US-, or CT-guided hip aspiration to aid PJI diagnosis. Outcomes of interest included diagnostic performance, dry tap rates, and procedural characteristics. Dry tap rates were pooled by modality using random-effects meta-analysis of proportions. Due to heterogeneity in reference standards, diagnostic accuracy outcomes were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Ten studies comprising 1,574 hip aspirations were included (647 fluoroscopy, 831 US, 96 CT). Sensitivity ranged from 0.52-0.89 for US and 0.27-0.83 for fluoroscopy, with consistently high specificity (≥0.75) across modalities. CT-guided aspiration demonstrated sensitivity of 0.67 and specificity of 0.98 in a single study. Pooled dry tap rates were lower for US (17%, 95% CI 4-30%) compared with fluoroscopy (27%, 95% CI 9-45%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²>97%).

CONCLUSIONS: Reported specificity is comparable between ultrasound- and fluoroscopy-guided hip aspiration for PJI. Ultrasound-guided aspiration demonstrates higher reported sensitivity and lower dry tap rates, although interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in reference standards.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This review provides a focused synthesis of comparative evidence on imaging modalities for hip aspiration in PJI. It highlights a potential diagnostic and practical advantage of ultrasound-guided aspiration.

articles.title: Early Response of Five Wine Grape Cultivars to Agrobacterium vitis Infection Suggests a Role of STS in Plant Defense.
articles.abstract: Crown gall disease, caused by Agrobacterium vitis, is a global threat to viticulture that severely compromises vine vigor and berry quality. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying grapevine resistance, five cultivars were inoculated with A. vitis strain A10 under controlled greenhouse conditions. Pathological assessments revealed divergent disease progression patterns among cultivars in which Yan73 (Y73) and Muscat Blanc (MB) exhibited higher resistance, whereas Y73 displayed mild disease development. Conversely, Merlot (ML), Cabernet Sauvignon, and Chardonnay showed rapid symptom development, and ML was identified as the most susceptible, characterized by the highest incidence and severity. Given that bacterial pathogens such as A. vitis are notoriously difficult to eradicate after infection, characterizing the early infection phase is critical for effective management. Comparative transcriptional analysis (RNA-seq) was conducted to capture the early molecular responses across these cultivars. Differentially expressed genes shared among cultivars were significantly enriched in pathways related to plant-pathogen interaction, stilbene biosynthesis, and responses to oxygen levels. Notably, ethylene signaling and response pathways were predominantly enriched in the relatively resistant cultivars Y73 and MB, suggesting their pivotal role in early defense. Further investigation into the stilbene synthase (STS) pathway revealed that its primary catalytic product, resveratrol (Res), serves as a key defensive metabolite. In vivo assays demonstrated that exogenous Res treatments significantly attenuated disease incidence and severity in a dose-dependent manner. Overall, this study outlines the early immune response of grapevine to A. vitis infection and highlights the importance of STS and ethylene pathways in resistance, providing potential targets for breeding crown gall-resistant grape cultivars.

articles.title: Toward a Unified Nomenclature for Endoscopic Spine Surgery: A Call for Multi-Society Consensus.
Illness in Children Presenting to the Emergency Department After International Travel: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis From the University Hospital of Helsinki, Finland.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We characterized infections after international travel and identified predictors of severe infection to refine management.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of children aged 0-18 years presenting to Helsinki University Hospital Emergency Department within 90 days of international travel between January 1, 2015, and January 26, 2025.

RESULTS: Among 921 patients (median age 5.1 years), 59.6% were travellers visiting friends and relatives (VFR), 31.7% outbound tourists, 7.3% migrants and 1.4% visitors to Finland. Sub-Saharan Africa was the most common travel destination (46.3%). The leading diagnoses were diarrhoea (36.0%), viral (22.6%) and respiratory infections (21.3%); 8.2% of infections were tropical and 15.3% potentially severe. Independent predictors of severe infection were migrant status, fever, travel from South-Central Asia, presentation > 5 days after return, and male sex. Malaria was diagnosed in 3.3% of patients, and only 22.4% of eligible travellers received adequate prophylaxis. Extended-spectrum β-lactamase producing organisms were frequent in Salmonella typhi infections and Escherichia coli pyelonephritis.

CONCLUSION: The main reason for paediatric travel was visiting friends and relatives. Migrants presented more frequently with potentially life-threatening infections. Only 22% of eligible travellers received adequate malaria chemoprophylaxis. Antimicrobial resistance represents a significant concern among paediatric travellers.

articles.title: The Proteasomal Switch as a Kinetic Battleground for Influenza A Virus Pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: AbstractInfluenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a high-stakes competition for proteostatic control. While the host reconfigures its degradative machinery for defense, the virus simultaneously hijacks host proteostatic and degradative pathways to facilitate replication and evade immunity. Central to this conflict is the proteasomal switch, a process in which constitutive proteasome subunits (β1, β2, β5) are replaced by their inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i) to form the immunoproteasome (iP). Although iP is classically recognized for optimizing MHC class I antigen presentation, emerging evidence reveals more nuanced roles in IAV infections. This review synthesizes current knowledge on iP as an effector of host defense and target for viral subversion. We synthesize emerging evidence and propose working models detailing how IAV proteins may selectively interfere with proteasomal subunits to stabilize pro-viral factors. Furthermore, we examine the hypothesis that the iP functions alongside broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD), and autophagic pathways as a proteostatic buffer to mitigate proteotoxic and oxidative stress in the infected epithelium. By evaluating how age-related proteostatic decay and viral subversion could impair cellular clearance machinery, we provide a conceptual framework for understanding how proteasomal dysregulation contributes to acute lung injury and the chronic inflammatory state termed as inflammaging. Finally, we propose a hypothesis-generating, biphasic framework for timing-dependent proteasomal modulation, contrasting preclinically supported late-stage β5i inhibition against the theoretical concept of early-stage activation to highlight translational hurdles in severe influenza.

articles.title: Phase 1b study of miricorilant in patients with presumed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Miricorilant, an oral nonsteroidal selective glucocorticoid receptor modulator, is being investigated as a therapy that modulates hepatic cortisol activity in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). This phase 1b study evaluated miricorilant's efficacy and safety.

APPROACH AND RESULTS: Seventy patients with presumed MASH received oral miricorilant daily (30-150 mg) or intermittent (100-200 mg once, twice, or thrice weekly) dosing regimens for 12 or 24 weeks. Across dosing regimens, reductions in relative liver fat content (LFC) ranged from 10.1% to 76.6%. Improvements in MASH liver function markers and the enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF) score were observed across regimens. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE) leading to drug interruption/discontinuation occurred in 12.9% of patients (n=9) each; most were due to aminotransferase elevations during an excessively rapid drop in LFC (up to 70.2% at week 6) and in patients receiving daily dosing. Intermittent dosing enabled more patients to complete 12 weeks of treatment without discontinuation due to TEAEs. Intermittent dosing with miricorilant 100 mg twice weekly had the best benefit-risk profile; this cohort demonstrated a mean LFC reduction of 28.2% at week 12, with a corresponding decline in liver enzymes (ALT, -3.8 U/L; AST, -6.0 U/L). Patients in this cohort also had numerical improvement in lipid profiles, glycemic markers, and fibrosis biomarkers.

CONCLUSIONS: Intermittent miricorilant dosing of 100 mg twice weekly achieved meaningful reductions in LFC and improved liver health markers with a favorable safety profile. This regimen is being evaluated in the phase 2b MONARCH study (NCT06108219).

articles.title: Role of Extrinsic Doping of Mg2+ on Crystallographic and Morphological Transition in CdO Nanoparticles under Acoustic Shocked Conditions.
articles.abstract: The role of extrinsic dopants in acoustic shock wave-induced phase transitions of solids remains unclear. Herein, we report the crystallographic structural stability of the Mg-doped CdO nanoparticles under acoustic shocked conditions to understand how extrinsic doping of Mg2+ manipulates the critical pressure for the B1-B2 transition compared to pure CdO NPs. From the XRD results, Mg-CdO remains stable in the B1 phase at 200 shocks, whereas the B1-B2 transition occurs in pure CdO at 200 shocks. Even in the absence of structural transitions, sphere-to-hexagonal honeycomb morphological changes are observed, which bring some considerable modifications in the vibrational, optical, and magnetic properties of the Mg-CdO NPs. The values of optical band gap energy are determined as 2.30, 2.23, and 2.22 eV for 0, 100, and 200 shocks, respectively, and the saturation magnetization values are found to be 0.14, 0.33, and 0.14 emu/g for 0, 100, and 200 shocks, respectively. The observed findings demonstrate that the presence of Mg2+ enhances the critical pressure for the B1-B2 transition compared to pure CdO. Moreover, the observed morphological changes are discussed based on the shock wave-induced thermal conductivity-driven superheating concepts.

articles.title: PDI-Spot: A Robust Representation Learning Framework for Identifying Energetic Hotspots in Protein-DNA Complexes.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: The binding affinity of protein-DNA complexes is concentrated within a subset of interface residues, called "hotspots", which are critical for maintaining stable interactions. Therefore, identifying these energetic anchors is essential for elaborating on how mutations disrupt transcriptional regulation and for identifying druggable regions within disease-associated interfaces. In this study, we introduce our novel prediction model, PDI-Spot, that leverages representation learning to capture the complex features of protein-DNA interfaces. Unlike traditional methods that rely on limited, handcrafted descriptors, PDI-Spot extracts high-dimensional, structure- and sequence-driven representations to achieve better predictive performance. We trained the PDI-Spot model on a curated protein-DNA complex data set and rigorously validated its performance on an independent test set to ensure generalizability across different structural families. Following the extraction of residue-level embeddings, an optimal feature set was identified through a combined approach of minimum redundancy maximum relevance and multilayer perceptron architectures. By training a neural network on the optimal feature set, we developed a robust predictive framework for hotspot identification. On an independent test set, PDI-Spot achieved an AUROC of 0.809, an F1-score of 0.667, and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.625. We also verified via permutation tests that PDI-Spot captures biologically meaningful patterns beyond random chance. PDI-Spot consistently demonstrates competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, providing a reliable model for mapping the energetic landscapes of protein-DNA interfaces. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/ebsrn0/pdi-spot.git.

articles.title: A σB-dependent sRNA provides a repressor function to the general stress response in Clostridioides difficile.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile is an anaerobic, gram-positive gastrointestinal pathogen that poses a significant health threat worldwide. A recent RIL-seq characterization of the Hfq-mediated RNA-RNA interactome revealed that small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators of virulence-related processes in C. difficile, including the initiation of sporulation. In the model Proteobacteria species E. coli and S. enterica, sRNAs often function as non-coding elements in vital stress responses mediated by alternative sigma factors, acting as repressors within these regulatory networks. However, whether this principle is broadly conserved across bacterial phyla remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that the Hfq-dependent sRNA SrsA is part of the regulatory network of the alternative sigma factor σB, which governs the general stress response in Firmicutes. Consequently, SrsA is highly expressed during the transition from exponential to stationary phase and under infection-related stress conditions, such as oxidative stress. We show that SrsA represses a highly conserved small protein family that regulates sporulation and three genes in the methyl-fixing branch of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway (WLP). Infection of mice further revealed that SrsA contributes to disease severity and bacterial recovery from antibiotic treatment in an acute and relapse mouse model of C. difficile infection.
