In summary, our data suggest that integrating SrsA into the σB regulon helps coordinate sporulation and vital metabolic pathways of C. difficile in response to infection-relevant stress conditions.IMPORTANCEThe central role of sRNAs as non-coding arms of stress responses represents a paradigm of sRNA function in Gammaproteobacteria. However, it remains unclear how broadly this regulatory principle is conserved across the bacterial tree of life. In our study, we identified the sRNA SrsA as a non-coding regulator involved in the sigma B-mediated stress response to nutrient limitation and radical stress in the intestinal pathogen Clostridioides difficile. We demonstrate that SrsA suppresses the production of a conserved family of spore regulators and of enzymes of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, establishing a role in regulating sporulation and gut colonization. Our work provides novel insights into the regulation of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, which is usually associated with autotrophic bacteria, and highlights the metabolic flexibility this anaerobic gut pathogen has evolved to survive in a nutrient-limited and inflamed gut environment.

articles.title: Dengue virus-2 triggers Epstein-Barr virus replication in primary B cells by co-opting the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis.
articles.abstract: The intricate interplay between co-infecting viral pathogens within a host can significantly influence disease outcomes. Dengue virus (DENV), a globally prevalent arbovirus from the Flaviviridae family, and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), a ubiquitous human herpesvirus, share extensive geographical overlap, yet their potential interactions remain largely uncharacterized. This study elucidates a novel molecular mechanism whereby DENV-2 infection triggers disruption of EBV latency. We systematically demonstrate that DENV-2 infection consistently induces EBV lytic gene expression and viral replication in diverse cellular contexts, including epithelial cell lines and, critically, in primary human B lymphocytes-the principal reservoir of latent EBV. Mechanistically, we establish that the substantial burden of DENV-2 protein synthesis and replication induces profound endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, activating the unfolded protein response (UPR). Through pharmacological inhibition and genetic knockdown, we dissect the three UPR branches and identify the IRE1-XBP1 signaling axis as the indispensable pathway for this phenomenon. DENV-2 infection promotes the endoribonuclease activity of IRE1, leading to the unconventional splicing of XBP1 mRNA into its transcriptionally active isoform, XBP1s. Depletion of IRE1 or XBP1 attenuated DENV-induced BZLF1 expression, whereas ectopic XBP1s expression increased BZLF1 transcription. Our findings delineate a precise virus-host-virus signaling model in which an acute RNA virus engages a cellular stress pathway to promote entry into the EBV lytic program and viral genome amplification. This provides a new paradigm for understanding the pathobiology of dengue fever and the complex dynamics of the human virome.IMPORTANCEThis research uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular dialog between two of the world's most common viral pathogens. By demonstrating that dengue virus infection can awaken dormant Epstein-Barr virus, this study provides a mechanistic basis for the long-suspected but poorly understood complications arising from viral co-infections. We pinpoint a specific cellular stress pathway, the IRE1-XBP1 axis of the unfolded protein response (UPR), as the critical molecular switch. This discovery is significant because it not only explains how an acute viral illness can trigger the reactivation of a latent, potentially oncogenic virus but also opens new avenues for therapeutic intervention. Understanding this intricate interplay could lead to novel strategies for managing severe dengue and other diseases where viral co-infection is a contributing factor to pathogenesis.

articles.title: The Association Between Perioperative Enhanced Care Unit Characteristics and Surgical Cancelation: A Nationwide Observational Study.
authors: Pan-London Perioperative Audit and Research Network Committee, The REPACC Study Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients referred for postoperative care within enhanced care units in the United Kingdom are less likely to have their surgery canceled than those referred to critical care. Presently, it is unclear whether this association remains when examined at an individual hospital level, and whether specific structure and process features of enhanced care services influence cancelation rates within a facility.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, observational study documenting clinical and organizational features of enhanced and critical care facilities in the United Kingdom. Features of interest included resource protections, staffing, and clinical scope. Sites with availability of both enhanced and critical care facilities, with >10 referrals to enhanced care during the study period, were selected for analysis. Cancelation rates of elective surgery within these facilities were quantified over a 3-month period between September 1, 2023, and November 30, 2023. Rates were defined as the number of elective cases canceled divided by the number of elective referrals to each facility. Multilevel regression was used to explore relationships between structure and process features of enhanced care units and surgical cancelation, using a two-level model with cases nested within hospitals to account for institutional confounding.

RESULTS: Complete data were available for 65 sites, of which 28 had an enhanced care facility with sufficient activity for analysis, representing 4112 patients referred to enhanced or critical care. In most institutions, surgical cancelation rates were lower within their enhanced care facility than in critical care. Enhanced care units with beds reserved exclusively for elective cases (odds ratio [OR], 0.54 [0.39-0.76]; P < .001) and clinical care involving multiple specialities (OR, 0.48 [0.33-0.69]; P < .001) were associated with reduced odds of cancelation. On the other hand, enhanced care units that permitted admission of emergency cases (OR, 1.61 [1.06-2.43]; P = .024) were associated with a greater odds of cancelation.

CONCLUSIONS: Structure and process features of enhanced care pathways are associated with cancelation rates among high-risk surgical patients in the United Kingdom. These findings may explain why cancelation rates in enhanced care are typically lower than within critical care and may have important policy implications.

articles.title: Hepatitis E virus infections in immunocompromised patients.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYHepatitis E virus (HEV) is an important cause of viral hepatitis globally. Historically considered an acute and self-limiting illness, HEV has emerged as a significant pathogen in various immunocompromised patient groups in the last 15 years. Vulnerable patients include transplant recipients, people living with advanced HIV infection, and patients with hematological malignancies, rheumatological disorders, or autoimmune diseases. These individuals are vulnerable to chronic hepatitis and extrahepatic manifestations due to HEV. These risks are also relevant to emerging modalities of immunosuppression such as new targeted drug therapies and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies. Besides unique clinical implications, immunocompromised hosts have also been at the center of new developments in the hepatitis E field on zoonotic reservoirs, transmission routes, disease models, and pathogenesis. In this review, we present a comprehensive integrative summary of the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management strategies of HEV infections in immunocompromised hosts.

articles.title: Novel roles of the Epstein-Barr virus BRRF1 protein in post-transcriptional RNA regulation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: In lytic infection, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) proteins manipulate cellular processes in multiple ways to facilitate virion production and overcome host antiviral responses. Here, we screened a library of EBV lytic proteins for those that manipulate or localize to cellular processing bodies (PBs), known to play important roles in RNA surveillance and miRNA-mediated translational control. One EBV protein, BRRF1, was identified that partially localized to PBs, and affinity purification-mass spectrometry experiments showed that it interacted with the CCR4-NOT complex-a known component of PBs with multiple roles in post-transcriptional mRNA regulation. The CNOT9 subunit of CCR4-NOT was sufficient to bind BRRF1, and its downregulation diminished BRRF1 interaction with the CNOT1 scaffold protein, indicating its importance in mediating the CCR4-NOT interaction with BRRF1. A BRRF1 double-point mutant was generated that failed to bind CNOT9 or interact with CCR4-NOT and was used to assess the importance of the BRRF1-CCR4-NOT interaction. Luciferase reporter assays identified multiple roles for BRRF1 in post-transcriptional regulation, including polyadenylation-dependent destabilization effects and interference with miRNA function, the latter of which was dependent on BRRF1 binding to CCR4-NOT. In addition, mRNA sequencing experiments comparing cells with and without BRRF1 expression identified multiple transcripts affected by BRRF1, some of which were at least partly dependent on the BRRF1-CCR4-NOT interaction. These include Claudin 6, whose transcripts and protein were downregulated by BRRF1 expressed on its own, as well as in lytic infection. Thus, we have identified multiple roles for BRRF1 in post-transcriptional mRNA regulation, some of which involve interaction with CCR4-NOT.

IMPORTANCE: To efficiently generate virions, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) must manipulate cellular processes to optimize the environment and overcome host antiviral defenses. Through unbiased screening methods, we have identified an EBV protein (BRRF1) that localizes to cellular bodies, which play key roles in mRNA regulation, and that interacts with a cellular complex with multiple critical roles in post-transcriptional mRNA regulation. As expected from these interactions, we found that BRRF1 has multiple previously unknown roles in disrupting mRNA levels and translation. Interestingly, one of the transcripts targeted by BRRF1 is Claudin 6, which has multiple roles in cancers, leading to increased cell proliferation and invasion. Our study provides additional insight into how EBV proteins manipulate cells to promote infection and affect oncogenesis.

articles.title: RasGAP and Crk bind Anaplasma phagocytophilum effector AteA at tyrosine-phosphorylated EPLYA motifs.
articles.abstract: Host cell signaling networks play critical roles in responding to bacterial infections. Intracellular pathogens manipulate these signals to establish a replicative niche in the host cell. Vector-borne rickettsial pathogens, such as Anaplasma phagocytophilum, encounter the dual challenge of interfacing with cell signaling in both the mammalian host and the tick vector Ixodes scapularis. A central feature that enables A. phagocytophilum survival in both mammals and ticks is the type 4 secretion system (T4SS), which secretes effector proteins into the host cell to manipulate biological processes. Only a few A. phagocytophilum T4SS effectors have been experimentally tested, primarily in mammalian cells. While AteA has been identified as the first T4SS effector known to be essential for A. phagocytophilum survival in the tick, its molecular targets in the tick remained unknown. Here, we investigated AteA interactions with tick cell proteins and a possible mechanism of AteA activation. AteA contains multiple EPIYA-like short linear motifs with the consensus sequence EPLYA. Other known bacterial EPIYA motif effectors, including AnkA from A. phagocytophilum, target mammalian phosphotyrosine signaling proteins. We found that AteA is tyrosine-phosphorylated at EPLYA motifs by the non-receptor tyrosine kinases Src and Abl in eukaryotic cells and during tick infection. Protein pull-down assays revealed that Ixodes SH2 domain-containing proteins, RasGAP and Crk, preferentially interact with phosphorylated AteA EPLYA motifs. RasGAP and Crk have interconnected roles in cell signaling, suggesting that A. phagocytophilum targets these pathways during infection of the arthropod vector.IMPORTANCETick-borne diseases are on the rise globally, linked to changes in climate, land use, and human-animal interactions. Interrupting vector-borne transmission requires understanding how the vector and pathogens interact. Recent studies have shown ticks detect and respond to pathogens through cellular immune and stress signaling pathways. We previously demonstrated that the tick-borne bacterium Anaplasma phagocytophilum encodes a tick-specific secreted effector, AteA, that is essential for the pathogen's survival in the tick. Here, we showed that AteA is phosphorylated by tick cell kinases, which promotes binding to host cell SH2 domain-containing proteins that are integral to cellular signaling networks. Understanding how these interactions affect signaling pathways in the tick will be essential if interventions targeting the vector are to be developed.

articles.title: When anticoagulation fails: recurrent right-heart thrombosis in aggressive pancreatic cancer-associated Trousseau syndrome.
Safety of the Use of Interpolation Flaps in Combination With Random Pattern Flaps or Skin Grafts for Repair of Post-Mohs Surgical Defects: A Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reconstruction after Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) for large or complex defects may require combination techniques, including interpolated flaps plus local flaps and/or skin grafts. Outcomes after combination repairs are not well-characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To assess postoperative complications associated with combination repairs using interpolation flaps with local flaps or full-thickness skin grafts (FTSG).

METHODS AND MATERIALS: A single-center retrospective review of patients who underwent MMS with reconstruction using an interpolated flap plus a local flap and/or skin graft from January 1, 2018, to August 1, 2025, was performed. Demographic, tumor, and reconstructive data were collected. Primary outcomes included postoperative complications within 3 months.

RESULTS: Twenty-one patients met inclusion criteria. The most common combination repair was a cheek-to-nose interpolation flap plus a local flap. Pain requiring prescription analgesia occurred in 23.81% of patients. Three patients (14.29%) experienced partial (2) or total (1) flap necrosis. Infection rate was 9.52% (2/21). No bleeding, dehiscence, hospitalizations, or emergency visits were observed.

CONCLUSION: Combination reconstruction seems safe in the outpatient setting with low rates of major complications, supporting its use for complex defects while emphasizing counseling regarding pain and flap viability.

articles.title: Complementary and Alternative Medicine Use in Diabetes Management Among Older Adults in the United States: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The current review synthesizes literature on complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) use in older adults with diabetes by applying Andersen's Behavioral Model to identify predisposing, enabling, and need factors, and health behaviors, with implications for research and practice.

METHOD: Seven databases were searched for English articles (1990 to 2024) on older adults' CAM use in diabetes care. Some elements of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses and Garrard's Matrix Method were used.

RESULTS: Fourteen articles were synthesized. Higher education and race were key predisposing factors, with CAM prevalence ranging from 25% annually to 88% daily. Disclosure was low. Need factors were mainly symptom relief. Common CAM categories included energy healing, prayer, herbs, and mind-body therapies.

CONCLUSION: Findings revealed low disclosure yet substantially varied CAM use, emphasizing the need for clinicians to discuss CAM for safe diabetes care, and aligned with Andersen's model guiding communication. Qualitative research on CAM use and disclosure is vital for safe integration.

articles.title: Temporal trends in oral anticoagulant prescribing in patients with atrial fibrillation and advanced chronic kidney disease: insights from the CRAFT registry.
Genetic Parameters and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Reproductive Traits in Egyptian Buffalo.
articles.journal: Journal of animal breeding and genetics = Zeitschrift fur Tierzuchtung und Zuchtungsbiologie
articles.abstract: Reproductive efficiency is a crucial factor in the sustainability and profitability of buffalo production systems. However, genetic improvement of reproductive traits is challenging due to low heritability, environmental sensitivity, limited recording, and shrinking reference populations caused by crossbreeding. This study aimed to estimate genetic parameters and detect the genomic architecture of key reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo using pedigree-based analyses and genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Over a 44-year period (1980-2024), reproductive records from five Egyptian experimental herds were analysed. The dataset comprised 2843 buffalo cows, sired by 140 bulls and out of 1328 dams. In total, 2359 records were available for age at first calving (AFC), 10,478 for gestation length (GL), 7966 for calving interval (CI), 6705 for days open (DO), and 12,909 for calving ease (CE) and stillbirth (SB). For genome-wide association analysis, 275 Egyptian buffaloes were genotyped using the Affymetrix Buffalo 90 K array, and 66,295 high-quality SNPs were retained after quality control. De-regressed proofs derived from pedigree-based genetic evaluations were used as response variables in a mixed linear model implemented in the rMVP package. Genome-wide association analysis identified putative genomic regions associated with GL, CI, CE, and SB, whereas no genome-wide significant associations were detected for AFC and DO. Functional annotation and QTL enrichment analyses were subsequently used to provide exploratory biological context for the identified genomic regions. Heritability estimates were generally low: 0.16 for AFC, 0.06 for GL, 0.02 for CI, 0.02 for DO, 0.18 for CE, and 0.06 for SB. Manhattan plots revealed that 15 genomic regions containing significant SNPs were identified on chromosomes 2, 4, 10, 12, 13, 15, 19, 20, and 25 for the reproductive traits of GL, CI, CE, and SB. These findings provide preliminary evidence of genomic regions potentially contributing to variation in reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo, although the relatively small number of genotyped animals limits the power to detect and validate small effect loci. Seven significant genomic regions on chromosomes 10, 13, 15, 20, and 25 were associated with the GL trait. Additionally, three suggestive SNPs mapped to chromosomes 2 and 19 were associated with the CE trait, and three suggestive SNPs mapped on chromosome 12 were significantly associated with the SB trait. The results of KEGG enrichment analyses and QTL classification analyses for reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo suggest that candidate genes within known QTL may be involved in complex biological networks involving immune competence, cellular homeostasis, and systemic physiological resilience. Among the enriched pathways, Fc gamma R-mediated phagocytosis, protein export, viral myocarditis, and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) were highlighted. Most annotated genomic regions (QTL) were related to reproductive traits (63.4%), followed by 17.3% for milk production traits, 9.95% for general production traits, 3.47% for meat and carcass traits, 3.71% for body conformation and robustness exterior traits, and 2.08% for health traits.

articles.title: A phase 2b/3 trial of saroglitazar in primary biliary cholangitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Saroglitazar, a dual PPAR alpha/gamma agonist, improved serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels in patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in a phase 2a clinical trial.

METHODS: EPICS-III is a phase 2b/3 adaptive, double-blind, randomized controlled trial in patients with PBC who had an inadequate response to or were intolerant of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA). In phase 2b, 37 participants received placebo or saroglitazar magnesium 1 or 2 mg for 16 weeks. Saroglitazar magnesium 1 mg (0.97 mg of saroglitazar) was selected for phase 3, which randomized 148 patients to saroglitazar (n=97) or placebo (n=51) for 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was biochemical response at week 52, defined as ALP <1.67 x ULN with ≥15% reduction from baseline and total bilirubin below ULN; the key secondary endpoint was ALP normalization.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics in the phase 3 efficacy population were comparable except for higher baseline ALP and other liver biochemistries in the saroglitazar group. Biochemical response was achieved in 56.7% versus 9.8% with placebo (difference, 48.0%; 95% CI, 35.3 to 60.8; p<0.001). Among participants with baseline ALP ≤3xULN, biochemical response rates were 79.0% versus 14.3%, and 83.1% versus 14.7% in the per-protocol analysis. ALP normalization occurred in 8.2% with saroglitazar versus 0% with placebo (difference, 8.5%; 95% CI, 2.9 to 14; p=0.016). Among participants with baseline 5-D Itch score ≥12, the week-24 treatment difference was -3.2 points (95% CI, -5.66 to -0.82) but was not maintained at week 52. Adverse events occurred in 81.1% with saroglitazar versus 90.5% with placebo, and serious adverse events occurred in 6.3% and 11.1%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Saroglitazar 0.97 mg significantly improved biochemical response and ALP normalization and was well tolerated over 52 weeks.

articles.title: Sedation Versus General Anesthesia During Pediatric Electrophysiology Studies: A Paired Comparison.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic strategy may influence tachycardia inducibility during pediatric electrophysiology studies, but direct paired comparisons between sedation and general anesthesia remain limited.

METHODS: This prospective paired-comparison study included 51 pediatric patients aged 5-21 years with supraventricular tachycardia undergoing electrophysiology study under both procedural sedation and general anesthesia during the same session. Procedural sedation consisted of midazolam, fentanyl, and supplemental propofol boluses as needed. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and fentanyl and maintained with sevoflurane. Tachycardia inducibility and electrophysiological parameters were compared between anesthetic conditions using paired analyses.

RESULTS: Overall tachycardia inducibility was higher during sedation than during general anesthesia (40/51 [78.4%] vs. 29/51 [56.9%], p = 0.007). No significant differences were observed in atrial effective refractory period, ventricular effective refractory period, atrioventricular nodal Wenckebach point, jump, echo interval, or ventriculoatrial block duration. In patients with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, inducibility decreased from 84.0% during sedation to 60.0% during general anesthesia (p = 0.109). In the Wolff-Parkinson-White/atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia subgroup, inducibility decreased from 73.1% to 53.8% (p = 0.063), and the accessory pathway effective refractory period, measured by extrastimulus pacing, was prolonged under general anesthesia (p = 0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: Procedural sedation was associated with greater overall tachycardia inducibility than general anesthesia during pediatric electrophysiology studies. The AVNRT and WPW/AVRT subgroups showed numerically lower inducibility under general anesthesia in the same direction as the overall finding, although these subgroup differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings support individualized anesthetic planning that considers the arrhythmia substrate, the need to preserve inducibility for mapping and post-ablation validation, and patient-specific requirements for procedural stability.

articles.title: Association of MASLD With Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation remains common. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a cardiometabolic condition and has been linked to incident AF, but its association with AF recurrence after catheter ablation remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to determine whether MASLD is associated with recurrent AF after catheter ablation METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus till July 2026 for studies that included adults with AF undergoing catheter ablation and compared the risk of AF recurrence between those with and without MASLD. A random-effects model was used to synthesize HRs and corresponding 95% CIs. Between-study variability was evaluated with the I2 measure, with additional subgroup analyses stratified by AF type and MASLD diagnostic method.

RESULTS: Six studies comprising 2921 patients (894 with MASLD) were included. MASLD was significantly associated with an increased risk of AF recurrence after ablation (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.39-2.64; p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 69.7%). The association remained significant in both paroxysmal (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.36-2.33) and persistent AF (HR 1.61, 95% CI 1.26-2.05), with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.58). Studies using imaging-based diagnosis of MASLD showed a significant association, whereas the association was not significant when the Fatty Liver Index was used, with no evidence of a difference between diagnostic-method subgroups (p = 0.47) CONCLUSION: MASLD is associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence after catheter ablation and may help identify patients at greater risk of recurrence. Further prospective studies are needed to provide a more comprehensive understanding of this association.

articles.title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Brugada Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmogenic disorder responsible for approximately 4% of sudden cardiac deaths. Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists and increases the risk of inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapies. Antiarrhythmic drugs are often limited by proarrhythmic effects, creating an unmet therapeutic need.

PURPOSE: We evaluated whether pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) reduces AF recurrence and provides effective rhythm control in patients with BrS and AF.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception until February 14, 2026. We included studies reporting outcomes of PVI in patients with BrS and AF. The primary endpoint was freedom from AF after ablation. Secondary endpoints included AF recurrence, changes in inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks before versus after ablation, and procedural complications. Pooled proportions and risk differences were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: A total of 2149 records were initially identified. After screening and eligibility assessment, Five studies comprising 214 participants overall, including 124 patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG, were included in the final analysis. The mean age of participants ranged from 45.8 ± 15.5 to 57 ± 10 years, and the proportion of male patients ranged from 33.3% to 100% across studies. PVI significantly reduced inappropriate defibrillator shocks (pooled risk difference -0.35). Freedom from AF was achieved in 82% of patients. The pooled recurrence rate was 36%. A spontaneous type 1 electrocardiographic pattern was present in 10% of patients, and 32% had a family history of sudden cardiac death. Procedural complications were uncommon across studies.

CONCLUSION: PVI was associated with favorable rhythm-control outcomes and acceptable procedural safety in patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG and AF. Inappropriate ICD shocks were less frequent after ablation, supporting PVI as a clinically relevant rhythm-control strategy in this challenging population. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Parental coping and child psychosocial adaptation in pediatric Wilson disease.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric data on psychosocial adaptation in Wilson disease remain limited. In particular, the relationship between parental psychosocial functioning and child quality of life and adaptation is still insufficiently understood.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 50 children with Wilson disease and one parent of each child. Children completed the Revised Children's Quality of Life Questionnaire (KINDL-R) and the JSR coping questionnaire. Parents completed the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28), Brief Coping Orientation to Problems Experienced (Brief COPE), Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS), and the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). Canonical correlation analysis was used to examine multivariate associations between child and parent variable sets.

RESULTS: The full canonical model was statistically significant, and five canonical functions were extracted; however, only the first function reached statistical significance (Rc = 0.802, Wilks' λ = 0.202, p = 0.001). This function linked parental problem-focused, emotion-focused, and avoidance coping, together with general psychological distress, with child dispositional active, social, and emotion-focused coping, total quality of life, and, to a lesser extent, internalizing problems. Redundancy indices supported the practical interpretability of the identified parent-child psychosocial pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial adaptation in children with Wilson disease appears to be meaningfully related to parental psychosocial functioning, particularly parental coping patterns and general psychological distress. These findings support a family-oriented approach to psychosocial assessment and care in pediatric Wilson disease.

articles.title: Beyond the reservoir: rethinking wildlife contributions to Fasciola transmission in multihost landscapes.
articles.abstract: Wildlife infection with Fasciola spp. has been documented across diverse mammalian taxa and ecological settings; however, the epidemiological significance of these infections remains difficult to determine. Serological exposure, parasite DNA, adult fluke recovery, coproantigen detection, and egg shedding represent different diagnostic states and support various levels of inference. In Fasciola transmission, a patent definitive host is only one part of an indirect cycle that also requires eggs to reach wet or aquatic habitats, compatible lymnaeid snails to become infected and amplify the parasite, and susceptible hosts to ingest the viable metacercariae. From this critical perspective, we ask when wildlife infection actually contributes to persistence or transmission to a defined target population. We used the wildlife reservoir paradox to describe situations in which measured wildlife infection is poorly aligned with the realised transmission contribution, and distinguished four context-dependent functions: incidental hosts, amplifying contributors, interface connectors, and maintenance components. We then evaluated how lymnaeid identity and ecology, environmental and hydrological connectivity, and molecular evidence could strengthen or limit reservoir attribution. Finally, we refined Fasciola Interface Management (FIM) into an operational five-step workflow that asks who contaminates, where snail amplification occurs, which target populations are connected to those sites, where parasite flow can be disrupted, and whether transmission subsequently declines. The central argument is that wildlife reservoir status should be attributed to populations within defined transmission systems, not inferred from host positivity alone.

articles.title: Evaluation of an automated faecal egg count system for enumeration of ascarid ova in chickens.
articles.abstract: Ascarid infection contributes to economic losses in chicken farming, requiring targeted parasite control strategies informed by faecal egg counts (FECs). Manual FECs are time-consuming and require specialised training and so are a good target for automation. This study aimed to optimise a new automated FEC system for ascarid ova in chickens (the Parasight All-in-One [AIO]) and compared its performance to the most common manual test used in the field - the McMaster.Automated counts using the AIO were compared to McMaster counts for correlation, agreement, sensitivity, and precision. Pooled faecal samples from 23 layer houses were collected and run in triplicate for three methods: AIO Bulk Prep (6 g subsample), AIO Single Prep (1 g subsample), and McMaster.There was a strong correlation between AIO and McMaster counts, regardless of sample preparation method (Bulk Prep: R2 = 0.931, p < 0.001; Single Prep: R2 = 0.801, p ≤ 0.001), and AIO counted approximately 15-24× as many ova. Bland-Altman plots indicated good agreement between both AIO methods and McMaster with no obvious bias.The larger number of ova counted by AIO was associated with elevated detection frequency. When 30 repeated counts of the same 10 eggs/gram sample were performed by McMaster and both AIO methods, positivity frequencies of 23.3% and 96.7% were obtained for McMaster and AIO, respectively, for the Single Prep method and 33.3% and 96.7%, respectively, for the Bulk Prep method. Precision was also significantly higher for both automated methods compared to McMaster (p ≤ 0.001; p ≤ 0.004).

articles.title: Music-based interventions for people with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis.
authors: supported by Cochrane Kidney and Transplant
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: People receiving haemodialysis for kidney failure experience substantial symptom burden, including anxiety, depression, and pain, which adversely affect physical function and quality of life. Music-based interventions are increasingly used as non-pharmacological strategies to address these symptoms; however, their effectiveness and the certainty of the evidence remain unclear. An updated systematic review of recent randomised controlled trials (RCTs) is therefore warranted.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of music-based interventions on fatigue, blood pressure, depression, pain, anxiety, stress, quality of life, and sleep quality in people with kidney failure receiving haemodialysis.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus and two trials registers up to 16 May 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included RCTs involving participants with kidney failure undergoing haemodialysis, comparing music-based interventions with controls where music-based interventions were not provided (e.g. standard care, headphones without music intervention, or video). We excluded studies involving temporary haemodialysis for acute kidney injury or other conditions.

OUTCOMES: We examined the impact of music-based interventions on fatigue, blood pressure, depression, and pain over the short term (up to four weeks), medium term (four weeks to six months), and long term (more than six months). These outcomes were prespecified as critical outcomes for GRADE assessment and included in the summary of findings table. Other important outcomes included anxiety, sleep quality, stress and quality of life.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane risk of bias 2 tool (RoB 2) to assess bias in the RCTs.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome using meta-analysis, where possible, applying a restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects model. We measured outcomes as mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs when all included studies used the same outcome scale, or standardised mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs when different outcome scales were used. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of evidence for critical outcomes.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of 27 studies involving 1584 participants, of which 24 studies (1467 participants) contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Comparator interventions included usual care, no intervention, headphones without music or white noise, and video interventions. The studies took place in 13 countries and territories across Asia, Europe, North America, and South America.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Critical outcomes Fatigue Music-based interventions may reduce short-term fatigue (measured on the 10-point Piper Fatigue Scale) compared with usual care or other comparator interventions (MD -3.14, 95% CI -3.83 to -2.45; 1 study, 62 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on medium-term fatigue (SMD -1.99, 95% CI -3.92 to -0.06; I² = 91%; 2 studies, 86 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated fatigue in the long term. Blood pressure The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on short-term blood pressure (mmHg) (MD -5.95, 95% CI -10.56 to -1.34; I² = 70%; 8 studies, 674 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on medium-term blood pressure (MD -2.00, 95% CI -14.21 to 10.21; 1 study, 16 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated blood pressure in the long term. Depression The included studies evaluated depression using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Patient Health Questionnaire-9, Beck Depression Inventory and Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Music-based interventions may reduce depressive symptoms compared with usual care or other comparator interventions over the short term (SMD -0.88, 95% CI -1.51 to -0.25; I² = 84%; 6 studies, 489 participants; low-certainty evidence) and medium term (SMD -0.81, 95% CI -1.42 to -0.19; I² = 43%; 5 studies, 203 participants; low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated depression in the long term. Pain The included studies measured pain using the VAS, Kidney Disease Quality of Life Short Form, and McGill Pain Questionnaire. Music-based interventions may reduce short-term pain compared with usual care or other comparator interventions (SMD -0.89, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.15; I² = 92%; 8 studies, 675 participants; low-certainty evidence). No studies evaluated pain in the medium or long term.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Music-based interventions may reduce fatigue, depressive symptoms, and pain in people undergoing haemodialysis in the short term compared with usual care or other comparator interventions. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of music-based interventions on blood pressure in the short term. In the medium term, music-based interventions may reduce depressive symptoms, but the evidence is very uncertain about their effects on fatigue and blood pressure. No studies reported long-term outcomes for these critical outcomes. Further large, well-designed RCTs with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the effects of music-based interventions for this population.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review was funded (in part) by Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (Grant numbers: 22H03554, 19K03092, 24K06239).

REGISTRATION: Protocol (2025) available via 10.1002/14651858.CD016139.

articles.title: Microsporidiosis After Solid Organ Transplantation: A Multi-Species Case Series.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microsporidiosis is an uncommon opportunistic infection in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Case-level data on multi-species disease and management remain limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed SOT recipients with microsporidiosis at Mayo Clinic from January 2000 through February 2026. Cases were identified by text search and institutional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) records. Clinical, microbiologic, treatment, immunosuppression, and outcome data were abstracted.

RESULTS: Ten recipients were identified: six kidney, two kidney-pancreas, and two heart recipients. Eight had enteritis and two had disseminated disease. Enterocytozoon bieneusi caused seven infections; the remaining cases were Encephalitozoon sp. enteritis, disseminated E. cuniculi, and disseminated Anncaliia algerae. All enteritis cases experienced diarrhea; seven experienced weight loss, five developed acute kidney injury, and five required hospitalization. The most common treatment administered was nitazoxanide (n = 6). Among these three achieved clinical remission, one improved without documented remission, and two had transient or partial improvement followed by recurrent diarrhea. Among four patients whose antimetabolite was held, reduced, or replaced at or before treatment, all improved clinically. In the two initially treated without antimetabolite modification, responses were transient or incomplete. Both Encephalitozoon infections achieved clinical remission with albendazole. Disseminated A. algerae was fatal.

CONCLUSIONS: Microsporidiosis after SOT demonstrated a species-associated clinical spectrum: E. bieneusi was confined to enteritis, whereas non-E. bieneusi species caused both enteric and disseminated disease. In E. bieneusi enteritis, nitazoxanide improved symptoms, but responses were incomplete when antimetabolite therapy was continued. Encephalitozoon infections responded to albendazole, whereas disseminated A. algerae was refractory and fatal.

articles.title: Clinical Features Associated with Timing of Identification of Congenital Cytomegalovirus.
articles.abstract: The objective was to study perinatal and clinical factors associated with early vs delayed diagnosis of congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV). We conducted a cross-sectional caregiver-reported survey of children with cCMV aged 12 months to <11 years. The timing of diagnosis was categorized as early (<31 days of life) or delayed (≥31 d). Prenatal and perinatal features, neonatal signs, and clinical indications prompting cCMV testing were compared by timing of diagnosis using descriptive and bivariate analyses. Among 181 children, 133 (73.5%) were diagnosed before 31 days and 48 (26.5%) later. Early diagnosis was associated with suspected prenatal CMV infection (38.3% vs 8.3%), neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission or prolonged hospitalization (50.4% vs 8.3%), and abnormal brain imaging at birth (58.6% vs 18.8%) (all P < .001). Early testing was more commonly prompted by abnormal prenatal ultrasound (33.8% vs 8.3%), NICU admission or severe illness (33.8% vs 0%), and abnormal newborn examination (48.9% vs 22.9%). Delayed diagnosis was more commonly prompted by late-onset hearing loss (29.2% vs 0.8%) and developmental concerns (33.3% vs 5.3%) (all P ≤ .002). Failed hearing screening did not differ between groups (39.6% vs 39.8%; P = .97). Timing of cCMV diagnosis reflects differences in clinical recognition and testing pathways rather than absence of signs.

articles.title: Preliminary Exploration of the Hepatoprotective Effect of Nanocrystalline Curcumin Against Traumatic Hemorrhagic Shock-Induced Liver Injury in a Desert Dry-Heat Environment: A Network Pharmacology-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock (THS) under desert dry-heat conditions can exacerbate secondary liver injury, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic interventions. This study investigated the protective effects of nanocrystalline curcumin (NC-Cur) against THS-induced liver injury in a desert dry-heat environment and explored its potential molecular mechanisms. Network pharmacology, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were used to identify candidate targets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations examined curcumin-protein interactions. Forty male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control, model, solvent, or NC-Cur treatment groups (n = 10 each). The model, solvent, and treatment groups underwent traumatic hemorrhagic shock under desert dry-heat conditions. Hepatic injury was assessed by histopathology, serum aminotransferases, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and Western blotting. Network analysis identified 116 overlapping targets, with heat shock protein 90 alpha A1 (HSP90AA1), AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) prioritized as the core targets. Docking predicted favorable interactions with all three proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations supported stable binding between curcumin and HSP90AA1. Compared with untreated model rats, NC-Cur-treated rats showed attenuated hepatic histopathological injury, reduced alanine and aspartate aminotransferases, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, and malondialdehyde, and increased superoxide dismutase. Western blotting indicated reduced HSP90AA1 and increased phosphorylated AKT1 expression after NC-Cur treatment, with changes also observed in BCL-2 expression. These findings suggest that NC-Cur may alleviate liver injury associated with THS under desert dry-heat conditions in male rats, potentially involving HSP90AA1-AKT1-BCL-2-related signaling.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of volatile sedatives in critically ill patients receiving mechanical ventilation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Volatile sedatives are increasingly utilised for sedation in critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Despite numerous randomised controlled trials and observational studies comparing volatile sedation to intravenous sedation, questions regarding its safety and efficacy persist. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases for studies published up to July 2025. The analysis included randomised controlled trials and observational studies that compared the use of volatile sedation with intravenous sedation in patients admitted to the intensive care unit for mechanical ventilation. Eligible studies involved adults aged ⩾18 years, requiring mechanical ventilation, and utilising either volatile or intravenous sedatives. They also needed to report at least one outcome of interest: incidence of delirium, mortality, intensive care unit length of stay, or duration of mechanical ventilation. From 3182 identified publications, fifteen studies were included in the systematic review. Volatile sedation was not associated with a significant difference in the incidence of delirium compared to intravenous sedation (risk ratio 0.72; 95% confidence interval 0.38-1.34), mortality (risk ratio 0.97; 95% confidence interval 0.80-1.17), intensive care unit length of stay (mean difference 0.28 days; 95% confidence interval -1.74 to 2.30), or duration of mechanical ventilation (mean difference -37.20 h; 95% confidence interval -78.60 to 4.20). Volatile sedation was not associated with significant differences in mechanical ventilation duration, delirium incidence, intensive care unit length of stay, or mortality compared to intravenous sedation. Further large-scale, high-quality randomised trials are needed to clarify its clinical benefit in critical care settings.

articles.title: The Raine Study: a multigenerational Western Australian birth and life-course cohort advancing research on the developmental origins of health and disease.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.abstract: The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework has transformed understanding of how early-life exposures shape health across the life course, yet populations from Oceania remain underrepresented in this research. The Raine Study is a globally unique, multigenerational longitudinal pregnancy cohort established in Western Australia, one of the world's most geographically isolated regions. The study recruited 2900 pregnant women (Generation1) in 1989, which resulted in 2868 live births forming Generation 2, and is now currently recruiting Generation 3 (the children of Generation 2). This paper describes the evolution of the Raine Study from its origins as a pregnancy cohort grounded in DOHaD to a comprehensive life-course and multigenerational research resource. This resource has led to key research findings that have informed international clinical guidelines and national and state health policies across areas including prenatal development and care safety, neurodevelopment, cardiometabolic health, obesity, liver disease, physical activity, mental health, sedentary behaviour, sleep, and assisted reproductive technologies. Central to the Raine Study's success is a longstanding commitment to participant partnership and engagement, resulting in exceptional retention and strong consumer involvement in governance and research prioritisation. The Raine Study demonstrates the critical value of well-characterised, place-based cohorts for advancing DOHaD and life-course science and provides a globally significant resource to inform prevention strategies, precision medicine, and public health policy across generations.

articles.title: Liver function following preterm birth: long-term implications for metabolic health.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.abstract: Preterm birth affects one in ten infants and represents one of the major early life insults with long-term health implications. Among the organs most disrupted is the liver, crucial for metabolism, detoxification and general systemic function. While the early clinical signs like neonatal cholestasis are well documented, the molecular mechanisms underlying hepatic dysfunction remain poorly characterised. In this review, we explore the potential hepatic molecular alterations associated with preterm birth that may influence early life programming of metabolic dysfunction. First, we present normal liver function and the potential effect of preterm birth on liver development and function. Second, we review metabolic adaptation in the neonatal period following preterm birth and highlight findings of perturbed circulating and tissue metabolites in both preterm human cohorts and animal models. These altered metabolites are associated with disruption of glucose and insulin homeostasis; alterations in lipid metabolism and lipoprotein profiles; impaired bile acid metabolism; perturbations in amino acid and protein metabolism; oxidative stress and antioxidant imbalance; as well as hormonal, growth factor and immune dysregulation. Finally, we examine whether these metabolic perturbations resolve or persist during maturation and consider their potential contribution to adverse metabolic outcomes later in life. Although many of the metabolic perturbations appear to normalise, evidence suggests persistent alterations in insulin signalling and lipid metabolism. Despite growing evidence across the life course following preterm birth, the molecular mechanisms linking early hepatic alterations with later adverse metabolic outcomes remain poorly defined. Epidemiological studies nevertheless demonstrate increased risks of insulin resistance, dyslipidaemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and type 2 diabetes in individuals born preterm.

articles.title: Essential fatty acid status and cognition in children with chronic intestinal failure.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Children with chronic intestinal failure (CIF) are at risk of cognitive delays, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Essential fatty acid deficiency (EFAD) may impair brain development. Lipid restrictions in home parenteral nutrition (HPN) used to prevent intestinal failure-associated liver disease may increase EFAD risk. We assessed EFA status and cognitive functioning in children with CIF and examined associations with EFAD.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional cohort study, children aged 4-17 years with CIF receiving HPN were included. EFAD was defined as a triene-to-tetraene ratio >0.007 with low linoleic and α-linolenic acid and elevated mead acid. Cognition was assessed using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (Fifth Edition) or Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence (Fourth Edition); Full-Scale Intelligence Quotient (FSIQ) and index scores were compared with normative data and between EFAD and non-EFAD groups. EFA status was measured in erythrocyte membranes by gas chromatography.

RESULTS: 17 of 23 eligible children participated (74%); 5 (29%) met EFAD criteria. Mean FSIQ was 90.7 ± 18.1 (p = 0.051 vs. normative mean). In children with EFAD, multiple cognitive domains were significantly lower than normative means. Compared with non-EFAD children, children with EFAD had a lower Cognitive Proficiency Index and Working Memory Index (CPI: 81.2 ± 6.3 vs. 103.8 ± 18.3, p = 0.018; WMI: 88.8 ± 9.9 vs. 108.0 ± 13.7, p = 0.013).

CONCLUSIONS: EFAD was common in children with CIF and associated with lower working memory and processing efficiency. These findings support optimizing parenteral lipid provision to meet EFA requirements and considering EFAD screening. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Family Resilience and Coping in Disasters, Pandemics, and Large-Scale Crises: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disasters, large-scale crises, and prolonged adversities such as pandemics can place sustained psychosocial pressure on families and disrupt everyday family functioning. Although family resilience is increasingly used to explain why some families adapt better than others, the evidence base is dispersed across conceptual, empirical, and intervention-focused work.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science and included peer-reviewed studies that examined family resilience or family coping in disaster, pandemic, or sustained adversity contexts. Study selection followed PRISMA 2020 principles. Data were extracted using a standardized form and synthesized using narrative and thematic approaches.

RESULTS: Forty-two studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Across contexts, family resilience was most often described as a dynamic, system-level process that involves shared meaning-making, organizational flexibility, and effective communication. Parenting practices repeatedly emerged as a key pathway linking family resilience to child adjustment. Resilience-oriented family interventions reported overall beneficial effects across disaster, pandemic, and serious illness contexts, with no evidence of harm.

CONCLUSIONS: Family resilience is a critical contributor to psychosocial adaptation during disasters and large-scale crises. Interventions that strengthen family-level processes-especially communication, coping skills, and supportive parenting-may offer a scalable approach to improve preparedness, response, and longer-term recovery.

articles.title: Breakout Session 9: Physical Environment.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract: The physical environment of an alternate care facility (ACF) spans safety, security, infection prevention, emergency management, hazardous materials, and fire and life safety, and it proved inseparable from patient safety, staff wellbeing, and operational continuity. Symposium participants summarized operational lessons from establishing and sustaining ACFs across convention centers, hotels, tents, and other non-traditional spaces. Participants reported that effective sites integrated clinical staff into security and de-escalation rather than relying on law enforcement alone, controlled access through single monitored entrances, and managed both the internal care space and the external perimeter as part of patient care. Multidisciplinary walkthroughs were essential to identifying physical hazards before activation. Persistent challenges included the absence of smoke compartments in open and temporary structures, unverified ventilation and negative-pressure performance, unreliable power and connectivity, and environments lacking day-night differentiation that contributed to patient delirium. Recommended best practices include engineering environmental controls in advance, embedding infection prevention, wellness, and safety functions from activation, and protecting staff through dedicated respite and decompression space.

articles.title: The impact of pre-pregnancy underweight on the risk of perineal and anal sphincter injury in nulliparous women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perineal injury is a common complication of vaginal delivery with maternal consequences. Although the effects of obesity are established, the impact of underweight on perineal and obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI), remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to determine the association between pre-pregnancy underweight and the risk of non-severe perineal injury (NSPI) and OASI in nulliparous women.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single, tertiary medical center including nulliparous women aged 18-45 years with singleton term vaginal deliveries (≥37 weeks) and pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) <25 kg/m2 between 2012 and 2024. Women with diabetes were excluded. The cohort was divided into underweight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2) and normal BMI groups. The primary outcome was NSPI, and the secondary outcome was OASI. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess independent associations.

RESULTS: Overall, 32 112 women were included, 12.9% of whom were underweight. Underweight women had lower birthweights and lower rates of induction and occiput-posterior presentation (all P < 0.05). NSPI occurred slightly less frequently among underweight women than among women with normal BMI (81.5% vs 84.3%, P < 0.001), whereas OASI was more common (1.1% vs 0.8%, P = 0.033). In the fully adjusted model, underweight BMI was associated with slightly lower odds of NSPI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.905; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.825-0.994) and higher odds of OASI (aOR 1.641; 95% CI 1.179-2.286). Additional factors associated with OASI in the fully adjusted model included higher birthweight per 100 g increment (aOR 1.132; 95% CI 1.096-1.169), occiput-posterior presentation (aOR 2.815; 95% CI 1.806-4.386), prolonged second stage (aOR 1.590; 95% CI 1.158-2.182), and vacuum-assisted delivery (aOR 2.304; 95% CI 1.666-3.187).

CONCLUSION: Pre-pregnancy underweight was associated with slightly lower odds of NSPI but higher odds of OASI.

articles.title: Impact of genotype on childhood bile salt export pump deficiency in Indian Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis registry.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A mutation in the ABCB11 gene causes the bile salt export pump (BSEP) deficiency. We aimed to study the genotype-phenotype correlation and the native liver survival (NLS) of BSEP deficiency among Indian children.

METHODS: The data were retrieved from the Indian Progressive Familial intrahepatic Cholestasis (PFIC) registry.

RESULTS: Among those enrolled in the registry, BSEP deficiency was the commonest (138/447, 30.9%) disorder. Among the 116 biallelic mutations, BSEP India1 (biallelic missense mutations) were present in 55 (47.4%) cases, whereas BSEP India2 (protein truncating mutation in at least one allele) in 17 (14.6%) cases, and BSEP India3 (biallelic protein truncating mutations) was seen in 44 (39.7%) cases, respectively. Of the 110 cases who presented with jaundice, in 36 (32.7%) cases jaundice resolved on urosdeoxycholic acid. Of the total, 91 with pruritus, grade 3 and 4 of pruritus was present in 54 (59.3%) cases, 43 (47.25%) cases did not resolve on medical management. On analysis of variance, median values of serum albumin (F-statistics 4.75, p = 0.011) were significantly lower in BSEP India3 versus BSEP India1 within the group. Risk predictive factors at baseline for death and LT were BSEP India3 (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 6.1, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.9-19.3, p = 0.002) and grade 3 and 4 of pruritus (adjusted OR 5.9, 95% CI 2-17.1, p < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed that non-resolution of jaundice, higher grade of pruritus and BSEP India3 was associated with significantly shorter duration of NLS. There were 49 likely novel mutations in various combinations and 2 PTMs (c.2115C>A [p.Tyr705Ter] and c.3659_3660del [p.Ser1220Ter]) as part of BSEP India3 genotype, were shown to be associated with death and liver transplantation (LT) in this Indian cohort.

CONCLUSION: BSEP deficiency/ABCB11 mutation was the commonest PFIC seen in the registry. Risk predictive factors at baseline for death and LT were BSEP India3 and grades 3 and 4 of pruritus.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05704517 (retrospective study).

articles.title: The Effectiveness and Safety of Deep Sedation Protocols for Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep sedation (DS) is increasingly utilized during pulsed field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF), but the optimal electrophysiologist-led sedation regimen remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To compare sedative effectiveness and safety of three electrophysiologist-led DS protocols.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study, AF patients undergoing focal-form PFA received (1) midazolam + fentanyl (Midazolam group), (2) flurbiprofen axetil + midazolam + fentanyl (Flurbiprofen group), or (3) dexmedetomidine + fentanyl (Dexmedetomidine group). The primary endpoint was the achievement of the target sedation level at ablation initiation (Ramsay Sedation Score ≥3). Secondary endpoints included intraoperative pain, sedation difficulty, operator satisfaction, and sedation-related adverse events.

RESULTS: 166 patients (mean age, 62.2 ± 10.8 years; 62.7% male; 48.2% with paroxysmal AF) were enrolled, with 53, 67, and 46 patients included in the Midazolam, Flurbiprofen, and Dexmedetomidine groups, respectively. The primary outcome occurred more frequently in the Flurbiprofen (73.1%) and Dexmedetomidine (82.6%) groups compared to Midazolam (47.2%) (overall p < 0.001); Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine group did not differ significantly. Intraoperative pain scores were lowest with Dexmedetomidine (overall p < 0.001). Both Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine groups showed lower sedation difficulty and higher operator satisfaction than the Midazolam group (both overall p < 0.001). Dexmedetomidine was associated with more intraoperative hypotension (overall p = 0.047).

CONCLUSION: Electrophysiologist-led DS protocols with Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine were associated with higher target sedation attainment than the specific low-dose Midazolam regimen during PFA, but Dexmedetomidine is linked to higher hypotension rates, warranting caution.

articles.title: Mid-trimester sum-estimated fetal weight and gestational diabetes risk in twin pregnancies.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is more prevalent in twin pregnancies, yet screening strategies remain largely based on singleton data. In the present study, we aimed to evaluate whether the mid-trimester sum of estimated fetal weights (sum-EFW) at the anatomy scan is associated with subsequent GDM in twin pregnancies.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of twin pregnancies undergoing routine mid-trimester ultrasound (2010-2025) at a tertiary center. Sum-EFW was calculated as the combined estimated fetal weight of both fetuses. The primary outcome was GDM. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed discriminative performance and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors.

RESULTS: Among 728 women, 70 (9.6%) developed GDM. Sum-EFW was higher in GDM pregnancies (1177 ± 187.9 vs. 1103 ± 178.8 g; P = 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated modest discriminative ability (area under the curve [AUC] 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.55-0.69; P = 0.001). After adjustment for gestational age, discrimination was similar (AUC 0.586; 95% CI: 0.518-0.655; P = 0.013), with sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 47.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) 12.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 93.1% at the optimal threshold. A cutoff of 1130 g identified a higher-risk subgroup (14.3% vs. 6.3%; P = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, maternal age ≥ 30 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.45; 95% CI: 1.10-5.45), body mass index (BMI) ≥30 (aOR 5.48; 95% CI: 2.33-12.85), and sum-EFW ≥1130 g (aOR 3.21; 95% CI: 1.41-7.34) were independently associated with GDM.

CONCLUSION: In twin pregnancies, a higher mid-trimester sum-EFW is independently associated with subsequent GDM. These findings suggest that combined fetal growth may reflect early metabolic alterations in twin gestations. Discrimination remains modest, limiting use as a screening or risk-stratification tool.

articles.title: Female Life Stages for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Management in Girls and Women: A Case-Based Approach.
authors: American Heart Association Cardiovascular Health in Girls and Women Science Advisory Group
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death among women in the United States and worldwide, yet current approaches to prevention and management do not fully account for female-specific biology. To address this need, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, published a Presidential Advisory defining the Female Life Stage construct, which defines four distinct stages across the life course: Perimenarche (Stage 1), Ovarian Cycling (Stage 2), Perimenopause (Stage 3), and Postmenopause (Stage 4), with pregnancy including the time before and after (Peripregnancy period) recognized as a distinct life period when cardiovascular risk may be modified.1 To provide examples of how this framework and the accompanying consensus guidance published in an accompanying Scientific Statement can be translated into a personalized care approach, this special report presents six hypothetical cases spanning the Female Life Stages, including adolescence and young adulthood, the peripartum period, midlife, perimenopause, and postmenopause.2 These cases illustrate how a female-specific life course framework that reflects hormonally-mediated physiologic transitions can promote earlier recognition of cardiovascular risk, guide cardiovascular screening and inform cardiovascular management. The cases underscore how hormonal health (e.g., menstrual cycle assessment, pregnancy planning and prevention, assessing and managing perimenopausal and postmenopausal symptoms) and psychosocial health (e.g., anxiety, depression, disordered eating) have cardiovascular implications. Moreover, this approach integrates well-established female-specific cardiovascular risk factors (e.g., premature menopause and adverse pregnancy outcomes), in addition to less well-recognized risk factors (e.g., early menarche, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome). We also review key evidence to inform a patient-centered approach to exogenous hormone therapy and associated cardiovascular risks for a variety of indications, including management of abnormal uterine bleeding, ovarian suppression, pregnancy prevention, and menopausal symptoms. By contextualizing the Female Life Stage framework within practical case scenarios, this article provides clinicians with a structured, evidence-based approach to improve cardiovascular prevention and management for girls and women.

articles.title: Stereoselectivity of photoinduced interaction of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug S-ketoprofen with (L/D)-Trp-Leu-Pro-Phe peptide in solution studied by NMR, CIDNP and molecular dynamics simulation.
articles.abstract: The stereoselectivity of chiral drug interactions with enzymatic active sites and cellular receptors is a subject of significant scientific interest. This interest is driven, firstly, by the pronounced differences in the therapeutic activity of drug enantiomers and, secondly, by the emerging role of amino acid chiral inversion in peptides associated with pathologies such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and type II diabetes. To probe the fundamental steps of such biomolecular interactions, electron transfer (ET) serves as a well-defined elementary chemical process. Prior investigations of photoinduced ET in chiral donor-acceptor dyads, incorporating (S)-ketoprofen and (L/D)-tryptophan, have revealed stereoselective and spin-selective phenomena. Extending this work, the present study examines the interaction of (S)-ketoprofen with the L- and D-enantiomers of tryptophan within the tetrapeptide tryptophan-leucine-proline-phenylalanine (WLPF), in homogeneous non-aqueous solutions. Utilizing NMR spectroscopy, chemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization (CIDNP) to detect transient paramagnetic intermediates, and molecular modeling, we have demonstrated that (S)-ketoprofen exhibits stereoselective interaction with the peptide epimers. Furthermore, it was shown that the D-epimer of the peptide has a greater tendency to aggregation than the L-epimer. The stereoselective light-induced formation of the ketoprofen ketyl radicals provides a plausible mechanistic basis for ketoprofen's phototoxic side effects.

articles.title: Ab initio diabatic potential energy matrix for the lowest-lying singlet states of HCN responsible for collisional excitation/quenching of CN(X2Σ+/A2Π) with H.
articles.abstract: In hyperthermal chemistry, electronically excited cyano radicals (CN) are considered as a key radiative source in the shock boundary layer in front of supersonic (re)entry vehicles. To correctly model radiative heating in such extreme environments, it is necessary to understand collisional excitation and quenching rates. Although quenching of CN(A2Π) to CN(X2Σ+) with various collision partners has been investigated experimentally, a quantitative understanding of the nonadiabatic transitions in such electronically inelastic scattering has not been achieved. In this work, a full-dimensional diabatic potential energy matrix (DPEM) for the three lowest-lying singlet A' states of HCN, namely the 1 1A', 2 1A', and 3 1A' states, is developed based on multi-reference configuration interaction calculations. The DPEM provides valuable insights into the quenching/excitation of CN(X2Σ+/A2Π) via collisions with H in the singlet manifold.

articles.title: Acute liver failure as the presenting manifestation of infiltrative hepatocellular carcinoma: a diagnostic challenge.
articles.abstract: We present the case of a patient with no prior diagnosis of liver disease who presents with acute liver failure in the context of hepatocellular carcinoma.

articles.title: Are intervention effects on fruit and vegetable intake maintained after 48 months of follow-up? A randomised controlled community trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether participants from a transtheoretical model-based intervention maintained increases in fruit and vegetables (FV) intake 48 months after baseline.

DESIGN: Randomised controlled community trial.

SETTING: A Brazilian primary health care service.

PARTICIPANTS: Primary health care service users. The control group (CG) received usual care, and the intervention group (IG) received usual care and a 7-month collective intervention to promote FV intake. We analysed individuals with positive changes 12 months after baseline (baseline intake <400 g/d with any increase at 12 months or baseline intake ≥400 g which remained ≥400 g at 12 months, n 2·232). Outcomes were FV intakes at 36 and 48 months after baseline compared to previous intakes to identify maintenance. We used generalised estimating equations models to assess time and intervention effects in follow-up intake.

RESULTS: Participants were mostly adult women. We identified decreases of 54.4 g/d in fruit intake and 38.5 g/d in vegetable intake at 36 months and increases of 6.9 g/d in fruit intake and 23.4 g/d in vegetable intake at 48 months. According to adjusted models, at 36 months, CG and IG participants presented similar decreases in FV intakes, which means initial changes in the IG were not maintained. At 48 months, small increases in intakes were also similar between IG and CG.

CONCLUSIONS: Intervention participants did not maintain initial changes on FV intake in the long term, and boosters might be necessary to maintain initial increases.

articles.title: Rising mortality from small intestinal cancer in Spain, 1999-2023: joinpoint and age-period-cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Small intestinal cancer is a rare neoplasm whose mortality has been increasing in several high‑income countries, yet long‑term patterns in Spain remain poorly described.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to analyse temporal trends and decompose the effects of age, period, and birth cohort on small intestinal cancer mortality in Spain between 1999 and 2023.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A population-based time-series study was conducted using national mortality data from the National Statistics Institute. Age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population. Joinpoint regression was used to identify significant trend changes, and age-period-cohort modelling was applied to quantify the contributions of biological aging, calendar period, and generational effects.

RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, the ASMR rose significantly in men (0.43 to 0.81 per 100,000; average annual percentage change: 2.1%) and more modestly in women (0.30 to 0.38 per 100,000; AAPC: 1.1%). The increase was driven almost entirely by individuals aged 50 years and older, while rates in those under 50 remained low and stable. Age-period-cohort analysis revealed a significant net drift (1.07% per year) and strong birth cohort effects in men, with mortality risk increasing for successive generations born through the mid-20th century. In women, the rise was primarily attributed to the age effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Small intestinal cancer mortality in Spain is increasing, particularly among men and older age groups. The significant cohort effect in men suggests that shifting environmental or lifestyle exposures are contributing to the growing burden of this malignancy.

articles.title: The Madrid Declaration on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Innovation, equity, and transformation of the health-system response to the metabolic disease challenge of the 21st century.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and one of the most clinically important manifestations of systemic metabolic dysfunction. Rather than a condition confined to the liver, MASLD represents an early marker of risk within the cardio-hepato-renal-metabolic continuum and an opportunity to intervene before irreversible organ damage becomes established. The Madrid Declaration on MASLD emerged from the meeting 'Innovation and Equity in the Management of MASLD', held on 4 March 2026 at the headquarters of the Spanish General Medical Council, with the endorsement of the Council and several scientific societies. In line with resolution WHA79.4, adopted by the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly in May 2026, the Declaration sets out a ten-point framework for a health-system and policy response commensurate with the scale of the challenge. It calls for MASLD to be recognised as a public health priority and explicitly integrated into national strategies for noncommunicable diseases. Key proposals include early detection and risk stratification using non-invasive tools in primary care, supported by stepwise referral pathways that ensure an effective clinical response after detection. The Declaration further advocates value-based care and risk-proportionate interventions, reserving specialist care for people at greatest risk of progression and currently authorised disease-specific pharmacotherapies for appropriately selected patients with non-cirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis. Equity is positioned as a structural principle of care, alongside stigma-free communication, integrated multidisciplinary models of care, and transparent evaluation against verifiable targets. The Declaration calls on policymakers, institutions, scientific societies, health professionals, and civil society to act in a coordinated and evidence-based manner.

articles.title: From Baveno VII to Baveno VIII: key innovations in risk stratification and personalized care for portal hypertension.
articles.abstract: Portal hypertension is a major determinant of disease progression and clinical outcomes in cirrhosis. The Baveno consensus has progressively moved its focus from the treatment of established complications towards earlier risk stratification, prevention of decompensation and modification of the natural history of the disease. Baveno VIII consolidates and extends this approach across the different stages of advanced chronic liver disease. Non-invasive assessment of clinically significant portal hypertension is refined through the incorporation of spleen stiffness measurement and probabilistic models, while longitudinal assessment emphasizes the importance of updating risk according to the most recent evaluation. In compensated disease, prevention of first decompensation remains centred on aetiological treatment and carvedilol in patients with clinically significant portal hypertension, together with management of relevant modifiable factors. In decompensated cirrhosis, greater emphasis is placed on preventing further decompensation and considering transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) earlier in the disease course, with individualized patient selection, stent diameter and strategies to prevent and manage post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy. Management of acute portal hypertension-related bleeding is further refined, particularly regarding the timing of pre-emptive TIPS and the treatment of gastric varices and vascular gastric lesions. Finally, updated criteria for hepatic recompensation establish durable clinical recovery as a meaningful therapeutic goal.
