These advances support a more individualized approach to portal hypertension, integrating disease stage, risk of progression and response to treatment throughout the course of cirrhosis.

articles.title: First bite syndrome: A systematic review of clinical features and evidence-based diagnostic criteria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: First bite syndrome (FBS) is a distinct painful condition. Due to limited recognition and the absence of standardized diagnostic criteria, FBS is frequently misdiagnosed. This study systematically reviews the literature on FBS to comprehensively characterize its clinical presentation and propose evidence-based diagnostic criteria using pooled individual patient-level data.

METHODS: An exhaustive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL from database inception to March 1, 2026. Peer-reviewed case reports and case series published in English describing patients of FBS were included. Based on critical appraisal of the literature and pooled individual patient-level data, diagnostic criteria for FBS were developed.

RESULTS: Seventy-one studies comprising 150 individual cases were included. Of these, 56% (84/150) were male, and the mean age was 50.7 ± 15.7 years. The most common precipitating factor was prior surgical intervention. Pain was typically localized in and around parotid region, triggered by the first bite of a meal, and diminished with subsequent mastication. It was most often unilateral, severe, sharp or electric-shock-like, and lasted for seconds. Approximately two-thirds of patients experienced complete resolution, with a median symptom duration of 360 days (interquartile range [IQR] 90-817.5 days).

CONCLUSIONS: FBS exhibits a highly consistent and reproducible clinical phenotype. The proposed diagnostic criteria provide an evidence-based framework and may aid recognition of this distinct pain disorder.

articles.title: Fabrication of barium titanate-loaded pH-responsive hydrogels for piezocatalytic antibacterial activity and osteoimmune regulation.
articles.abstract: Infected bone defects represent a persistent clinical challenge due to recurrent bacterial infection, inflammatory immune imbalance, and impaired osteogenesis. Conventional piezoelectric or antibacterial biomaterials often lack microenvironment responsiveness, leading to off-target effects, insufficient biosafety, and limited osteoimmune regulation. Here, a pH-responsive chitosan/β-glycerophosphate hydrogel loaded with barium titanate (BTO) nanoparticles is constructed for ultrasound-driven piezocatalytic antibacterial activity and osteoimmune regulation. The optimized hydrogel achieves rapid gelation, strong bone interfacial adhesion, favorable injectability, self-healing performance, and pH-sensitive swelling behavior, which selectively enhances the exposure and catalytic activity of BTO in acidic infectious microenvironments to realize on-demand reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and reduce unnecessary oxidative damage. Under ultrasonic stimulation, BTO nanoparticles effectively produce hydroxyl radicals and singlet oxygen to eradicate both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria without antibiotics or toxic metal components. Meanwhile, the composite hydrogel suppresses pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization while promoting anti-inflammatory M2 polarization, and significantly enhances the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells. This intelligent design integrates pathology-triggered responsiveness, piezocatalytic sterilization, biocompatibility, and immune-osteogenic regulation, providing a novel and translatable strategy for efficient infected bone defect repair.

articles.title: Real-world diagnosis and treatment of individuals with migraine in the United States: The Migraine Insights in Diagnosis and Treatment (MIND) study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to describe the real-world diagnosis and treatment patterns of individuals newly diagnosed with migraine in the United States (US).

BACKGROUND: Over 10% of adults in the US are living with migraine. Recent data from large, population-based studies on the diagnosis and treatment of migraine among individuals in the US who are newly diagnosed with migraine are lacking.

METHODS: The Migraine Insights in Diagnosis and Treatment (MIND) study is a retrospective cohort study conducted using the Optum® Market Clarity database. The study included individuals with a first migraine diagnosis between July 1, 2018, and June 30, 2021 (index date), who were ≥18 years old on the index date, had ≥12 months of pre-index and ≥36 months of post-index continuous claims enrollment, and no diagnosis of migraine or use of migraine-specific medications in the pre-index period. Outcomes included index migraine diagnosis (e.g., migraine type, setting of diagnosis, specialty of the diagnosing healthcare provider [HCP]), and use of medications to treat migraine (e.g., medications indicated for acute treatment, prevention, or both; other analgesics). Medications were further subcategorized into migraine-specific acute (triptans, gepants, ergots, and ditans) and preventive (gepants and calcitonin gene-related peptide [CGRP] targeted monoclonal antibodies [mAbs]) medications. All analyses were descriptive in nature.

RESULTS: The study database included 911,128 individuals newly diagnosed with migraine, of whom 154,353 met all study eligibility criteria. Mean age was 46.1 years, 81.1% were female, and 66.3% were commercially insured. Common comorbidities included anxiety (40.5%), depression (28.2%), and sleep disorders (26.9%). The most common HCP specialty for the index migraine diagnosis was primary care (47.0%), followed by neurology (18.0%), and other (15.3%); diagnosis most often occurred in outpatient (89.5%) settings, followed by inpatient (7.7%), and emergency department (2.8%). Only 16.2% of individuals had a diagnostic test within 30 days before or after their index migraine diagnosis. A total of 111,345 (72.1%) individuals filled a prescription for a migraine medication in the 3 years after their index diagnosis, including 94,198 (61.0%) who received a medication for acute treatment and 62,596 (40.6%) who received a medication for prevention. The most commonly used acute migraine medication types prescribed first were NSAIDs (62.8%) and triptans (35.0%), while for prevention, it was beta blockers (23.2%) and anticonvulsants (21.6%). Migraine-specific preventive medications, CGRP-targeted mAbs (8.1%) and gepants (1.2%), were used first less frequently. A total of 71,199 (46.1%) individuals filled a prescription for an opioid in the 3 years after the index diagnosis of migraine, while 19,359 (12.5%) filled a prescription for butalbital.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the frequent utilization of medications that are not migraine-specific, both for acute treatment and preventive management of migraine. Increased efforts towards education for the optimal management of migraine should be implemented.

articles.title: Of bicuspid aortic stenosis, women, and fibrosis: At last, new computed tomography-derived insights into 2-sinus bicuspid aortic valve stenosis.
Nutrient intake during the parenteral-to-enteral transition and longitudinal growth faltering in very preterm infants.
articles.abstract: The transition from parenteral to enteral nutrition can expose preterm infants to nutrient deficits. We characterized nutrient intake during this transition phase and investigated nutritional and clinical factors linked to longitudinal growth faltering (GF). This single-center, retrospective-prospective observational study included 190 surviving infants born before 32 weeks of gestation who achieved full enteral feeding and completed at least 30 days of follow-up. Growth faltering (GF) was defined as a decrease in weight Z-score exceeding 1.2 standard deviations from birth to discharge or 40 weeks postmenstrual age, whichever came first. We analyzed combined parenteral and enteral nutrient intakes across various enteral-volume intervals. Multivariable logistic regression was used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), estimated via bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrapping. GF occurred in 84 infants (44.2%), with the most significant interval-specific Z-score decline observed between enteral volumes of 30 and 160 mL/kg/day. In unadjusted comparisons, infants experiencing GF had longer transition periods and greater average daily and cumulative energy and protein deficits during the first 30 days. However, none of the 39 volume-specific nutritional comparisons remained significant after Bonferroni correction. Faster enteral advancement was associated with a lower likelihood of GF (aOR 0.69 per 1 mL/kg/day; 95% CI 0.57-0.78). Higher protein intake at 80 to less than 120 mL/kg/day showed an exploratory association with lower odds of GF (aOR 0.39 per 1 g/kg/day; 95% CI 0.15-0.81). Male sex was associated with higher odds of GF, though with imprecise estimation (aOR 9.82; 95% CI 3.56-72.89). The association with late-onset sepsis was less stable (aOR 3.26; 95% CI 0.97-21.46). These findings advocate for close monitoring of combined nutrient intake during the transition period, though they do not establish causality. The observed association with protein intake requires independent confirmation.

articles.title: Phylogenomics of Cypriniformes, the most diverse order of freshwater fishes: consensus, challenges and limitations.
articles.abstract: Cypriniformes, the most species-rich order of freshwater fishes (∼5,000 species), represents a key lineage for understanding vertebrate diversification in freshwater ecosystems. This clade includes several highly miniaturized and understudied lineages whose phylogenetic placements have long remained contentious. Here, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Cypriniformes with complete family-level representation and broad genus-level coverage, encompassing 316 species comprising approximately 30% of all described genera. Our dataset integrates 257 newly assembled genomes with publicly available resources and analyzes multiple sets of genome-wide markers using both concatenation-based and coalescent-aware approaches. The general concordance among analytical frameworks indicates that the backbone topology of Cypriniformes is now established, allowing clear identification of well-supported clades and regions of persistent conflict. Our results strengthen the evolutionary relationships of several miniaturized lineages, while identifying recalcitrant relationships shaped by both biological processes and model artefacts that can yield superficially similar patterns of phylogenetic conflict. Our study substantially expands genomic representation and establishes a phylogenomic foundation for future comparative, developmental, and evolutionary research in this freshwater radiation.

articles.title: A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
authors: American Heart Association; American Academy of Pediatrics; American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists; and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

articles.title: CCR2-Dependent Myeloid Cell Recruitment Links Post-MI Heart Failure to Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is a common complication of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). Myeloid inflammation is a major hallmark of both the local cardiac and systemic post-MI response, with resident and recruited monocyte-derived macrophages orchestrating each step of the ensuing inflammatory cascade, from clearance of dead cardiomyocytes to scar tissue formation. Similarly, myeloid inflammation is a key feature of the PH lung, driving remodeling of small pulmonary vessels. We thus hypothesized that MI-induced systemic myeloid inflammation contributes directly to the development of PH-LHD.

METHODS: We assessed expression of inflammatory adhesion molecules, as markers of vascular inflammatory activation and myeloid cell recruitment pathways, in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, PH-LHD, as well as in a PH-LHD rat model. We then induced MI and subsequent HF in 8- to 10-week-old female C57BL/6J mice via permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. HF mice were then treated with a CCR2 (C-C chemokine receptor 2) antagonist to block monocyte recruitment and the development of PH-LHD was assessed at 6 weeks post-MI by a combination of invasive hemodynamics, flow cytometry, echocardiography, and lung histology.

RESULTS: Expression of key inflammatory adhesion molecules, including VCAM1 and SELE, was increased in PH-LHD lungs from humans and rats. Following early post-MI development of HF with reduced ejection fraction, mice exhibited increased numbers of circulating monocytes, lung monocytes, and lung interstitial macrophages, as well as PH-LHD by 6 weeks, characterized by right ventricular hypertrophy, elevated right ventricular pressures, and lung vascular remodeling of small-to-medium-sized pulmonary vessels. Administration of the selective CCR2 antagonist RS102895 from day 10 post-MI to reduce monocyte tissue recruitment attenuated lung vascular remodeling, right ventricular systolic and diastolic pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and lung adhesion molecule expression at 6 weeks, compared with vehicle-treated controls, without improving the underlying left-sided HF.

CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

articles.title: AMPK-dependent mechanisms mediate the protective effects of grape pomace extract in obesity-associated chronic renal disease in mice.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated kidney disease involves metabolic dysfunction accompanied by lipotoxicity, inflammation, and fibrosis. We previously showed that grape pomace extract (GPE), a polyphenol-rich byproduct of winemaking, exerts renoprotective effects in obese mice; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aims to investigate whether adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) mediates the protective effects of dietary GPE supplementation in high-fat diet (HF)-induced obese mice. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed a standard diet (16% calories from fat) or a HF (60% calories from fat) with or without GPE (300 mg per kg body weight per day) for 16 weeks. A subset of animals was treated with compound C (CC), a widely used AMPK inhibitor, during the last 4 weeks. GPE attenuated HF-induced body weight gain, visceral adiposity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and renal dysfunction, while improving histopathological alterations. Mechanistically, GPE restored renal AMPK phosphorylation, increased autophagy markers (increased LC3-II/LC3-I ratio and Beclin-1 levels) and reduced renal lipid accumulation. In addition, GPE enhanced levels of the mitochondrial biogenesis regulator PGC-1α, while attenuating oxidative stress (Nox4, 4-HNE, and oxidant species production), inflammatory signaling (NF-κB-NLRP3 pathway), and renal fibrosis. Notably, pharmacological AMPK inhibition reversed the GPE effect, leading to worsening of renal injury, autophagy impairment, increased lipid deposition, and exacerbation of fibrotic and inflammatory markers. These findings demonstrate that AMPK activation is a mediator of the metabolic and renoprotective effects of GPE, positioning GPE as a promising functional food ingredient for attenuation of obesity-associated kidney disease.

articles.title: Agricultural waste-derived sweat sensor integrated into wettability-tunable microfluidics for noninvasive metabolic evaluation.
articles.abstract: Wearable sweat patches allow real-time and noninvasive monitoring of metabolism through sweat biomarker analysis. However, challenges related to sweat collection efficiency and the lack of sustainable sweat sensors impede the widespread adoption of sweat analysis. Here, we report the design of a wearable sweat patch integrating an agricultural waste-derived sweat sensor for sensitive sweat uric acid (UA) and glucose (Glu) analysis and surface wettability-controlled microfluidics for efficient sweat collection. We evaluate the performance of the wearable patch for the noninvasive monitoring of UA and Glu in sweat. We also validate the usability of the wearable patch in assessing metabolic status in metabolic disorders including gout and diabetes.

articles.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
authors: American Heart Association; American Academy of Pediatrics; American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists; and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
articles.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

articles.title: Impact of age and frailty on the effect of a multimodal individualized long-term intervention after stroke: the last-long trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The LAST-long randomized trial tested a multidimensional, stroke coordinator-led, community-based intervention and found no overall functional benefit. Because most participants had mild stroke symptoms, whether older or frailer subgroups benefited was examined.

METHODS: In this single-blinded RCT at 4 Norwegian hospitals (2019-2022), 301 participants were randomized 1:1 to monthly stroke-coordinator meetings for 18 months (structured risk assessment and individualized goals) or to standard care.

PRIMARY OUTCOME: modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 18 months.

SECONDARY OUTCOMES: mortality, cognition, ADLs, physical function, fatigue, and quality of life. Older age: ≥ 80 years; frailty: Frailty Index ≥ 0.2. Linear and logistic regression tested age- and frailty-intervention interactions.

RESULTS: mRS data were available for 268 participants (136 intervention, 132 control). Mean age 71.1 (SD 12.4); 66 (24.6%) ≥ 80; 89 (33.2%) frail. Age modified the intervention effect on mRS: among participants ≥ 80, favourable outcome was less likely with intervention vs control (23.4% vs 57.0%, p = 0.004). For secondary outcomes, the intervention improved Trail Making Test B in younger participants (-32.2 s, 95% CI -58.0 to -6.4, p = 0.015) with a significant age-intervention interaction (p = 0.019). No frailty-intervention interaction was found.

CONCLUSIONS: Age - but not frailty - modified response to the intervention, indicating differential effects in older participants.

CLINICAL TRIALS: gov identifier: NCT03859063.

articles.title: Genetic evidence linking gout to increased risk of epilepsy: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While observational studies have explored the association between gout, uric acid (UA) levels, and the risk of epilepsy, their findings remain inconsistent.

OBJECTIVES: To clarify the potential causal relationship, we performed a Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a bidirectional MR analysis using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary data. Epilepsy data were sourced from the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), gout data from the FinnGen consortium and a GWAS of clinically defined gout and its subtypes, and UA data from the BioBank Japan (BBJ) and a genome-wide meta-analysis of serum UA levels in Japanese individuals. The inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method served as the primary causal inference approach. To ensure robustness, we complemented this with 3 additional methods: MR-Egger, weighted median, and MR using Robust Adjusted Profile Score (MR-RAPS) - the latter specifically employed to account for potential weak instrument bias due to the limited number of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) included in this analysis.

RESULTS: Our analysis identified a causal association between genetically predicted gout and an increased risk of epilepsy (odds ratio (OR) = 1.014, 95% confidence interval (95% CI): 1.011-1.017, p < 0.001), generalized epilepsy (OR = 1.009, 95% CI: 1.000-1.018, p = 0.042), and focal epilepsy (OR = 1.044, 95% CI: 1.002-1.088, p = 0.041) in Europeans. In contrast, UA levels showed no significant association with epilepsy or its subtypes in this population. Similarly, neither gout nor UA levels were linked to epilepsy in East Asians. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the robustness of the primary findings.

CONCLUSIONS: This MR study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal role of gout in increasing the risk of epilepsy, including generalized and focal epilepsy, in European populations. In contrast, genetically predicted UA levels showed no significant association with epilepsy. These findings support a potential role of gout in epilepsy risk and warrant further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Ward Failure After Severe Rib Fracture: What Unplanned ICU Transfer Teaches Us About Early Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSevere rib fractures are a major cause of morbidity and mortality after blunt thoracic trauma. The decision to directly admit these patients to the intensive care unit (ICU) vs initial ward placement remains debated. An unplanned ICU transfer may reflect delayed recognition of deterioration and worsen outcomes.MethodsAdult patients (≥18 years) with isolated severe thoracic injury (thorax AIS ≥3, AIS ≤1 in all other body regions) due to blunt trauma that resulted in one or more rib fractures were identified in the ACS Trauma Quality Improvement Program database from 2013-2021. Patients were stratified by admission pathway: direct ICU admission or unplanned ICU transfer from the ward. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust standard errors was employed to adjust for potential confounding.ResultsAmong 52,332 patients who sustained isolated severe thoracic injury with rib fractures and were admitted to the ICU, 1830 (3.5%) experienced an unplanned ICU transfer. Adjusted analyses confirmed increased risks of mortality (RR 3.35, 95% CI 2.89-3.88), pneumonia (RR 2.68, 95% CI 2.08-3.45), ARDS (RR 4.52, 95% CI 3.42-5.97), and mechanical ventilation (RR 3.21, 95% CI 2.98-3.47) with unplanned admission.ConclusionsUnplanned ICU admission is independently associated with markedly worse outcomes in isolated severe thoracic injury with rib fractures. These findings suggest that improved early risk stratification may help identify patients at increased risk of subsequent unplanned ICU transfer.

articles.title: Workroom contact networks: implications for COVID-19 and other respiratory infections.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how physician workroom size affects healthcare professional contact networks and the risk of respiratory virus transmission.

DESIGN: Prospective observational study with agent-based simulations.

SETTING: Two physician workrooms of differing size (internal medicine, 208.7 sq ft; cardiology, 112.6 sq ft) in a large academic hospital.

METHODS: We deployed wireless sensor networks over 18 days in internal medicine and 14 days in cardiology workrooms. Physicians, residents, and medical students wore proximity-sensing badges during work shifts. Contacts were defined as two healthcare professionals within six feet, based on calibrated received signal strength indicators. Contact networks were generated in one-minute intervals. We simulated respiratory disease spread using a Susceptible-Infected (SI) model across varying transmission probabilities and estimated infection risk at different room densities.

RESULTS: Average occupancy was 2.7 persons in internal medicine and 2.3 in cardiology. Despite lower occupancy, the smaller cardiology room exhibited greater contact density: healthcare professionals in the smaller room had higher mean and median numbers of contacts. SI simulations showed consistently higher risk of secondary infections in the cardiology room, even at lower transmission probabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: Workroom size significantly affects healthcare professional contact density and infection risk. Smaller rooms increased opportunities for transmission despite lower average occupancy. Designing larger workrooms, limiting occupancy, or reconfiguring shared spaces may reduce infection transmission in healthcare facilities.

articles.title: Germicidal ultraviolet to reduce transmission of respiratory infections indoors: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory infections that transmit through air contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality. Although preclinical data on germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) for air treatment are promising, its real-world effectiveness remains incompletely understood.

PURPOSE: Review effectiveness and safety of GUV for preventing respiratory infection transmission.

DATA SOURCES: Medline, Embase, Global Health, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Engineering Village, Epistemonikos, Scopus, and Environmental Science Collection from inception through December 2025.

STUDY SELECTION: Studies of GUV with a comparator, measuring human outcomes including respiratory infections, absenteeism, or adverse events.

DATA EXTRACTION: At least two investigators extracted data.

DATA SYNTHESIS: We identified 57 reports describing 40 studies published between 1940 and 2025: 30 non-randomized controlled trials, 4 randomized controlled trials (RCTs), 4 case series, 1 cohort study, and 1 cross-sectional study. Non-randomized studies indicated GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air (measles and chickenpox), although results were mixed for undifferentiated respiratory illnesses and absenteeism. Two RCTs were inconclusive or showed only modest effects. Safety monitoring in 16 studies identified no increased eye or skin irritation from properly installed GUV. All studies had at least one threat to validity; 89% were non-randomized, and 83% lacked statistical power calculations.

LIMITATIONS: Heterogeneous study designs, interventions, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Several older clinical studies indicated that GUV reduces infections with high transmissibility through air, but its broader effectiveness against respiratory infection remains uncertain. Inconclusive results may reflect methodological and epidemiological limitations rather than true ineffectiveness. Adequately powered RCTs with robust clinical endpoints are needed.

REGISTRATION: https://osf.io/fg6qx.

articles.title: The Triple Burden: Tramadol, NSAIDS, and Energy Drinks Among Agricultural Workers in La Gomera, Guatemala: An Anthropological Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Agriculture is a major economic activity in Guatemala. Workers in sugarcane, banana, and African palm plantations face high risk of chronic kidney disease of non-traditional causes (CKDnT). During 2021- 2023, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) implemented a project in Guatemala to provide comprehensive care for CKDnT. The frequent use of potentially nephrotoxic substances, such as medications and energy drinks, was documented. This qualitative study, conducted during 2023, aimed to understand this practice and its relation to agricultural work.

METHODS: Interviews, focus group discussions, and pile sorting technique were implemented for data collection. Participants (n = 24) were plantation workers (n = 13), supervisors (n = 5), labor authorities (n = 2), and healthcare staff (n = 4). Interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed. Deductive and inductive thematic analysis was performed using NVivo.

RESULTS: Three core themes emerged: (1) substances, motivations, practices of use, and availability, with tramadol, energy drinks, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs commonly consumed in various ways (drunk, swallowed, inhaled, or spread on cigarettes to be smoked) to sustain labor; (2) work dynamics and its relation to the use of substances; and (3) perception of health risks related to the use of substances.

DISCUSSION: Piecework payment systems incentivize high production, framing substance use as a necessity to increase energy and manage pain and fatigue. Use of medications and other substances was described as socially accepted and normalized. Addressing CKDnT requires structural interventions and culturally adapted health promotion strategies.

CONCLUSION: Agricultural work dynamics in Guatemala contribute to the use of medications and substances that influence agricultural workers health. Structural causes, including factors such as poverty, instability, and social dynamics, further hinder substance discontinuation. Further interdisciplinary research is needed to deepen the understanding of this practice and its relationship with the high prevalence of CKDnT.

articles.title: Clinical course of rhabdomyolysis by etiology: Findings from a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rhabdomyolysis is a complex syndrome with varying severity. Few studies compare outcomes by etiology, and prospective data are limited. We aimed to assess whether the clinical course of rhabdomyolysis differs according to etiology and whether this may aid early risk stratification.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, 310 adults with creatine kinase ≥ 5,000 U/L and/or myoglobin ≥ 1,000 ng/mL were included. Muscle injury was categorized as traumatic or non-traumatic; the latter further divided into exertional and non-exertional. Primary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI), kidney function after 3 months, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: AKI occurred in 108 (35%) patients: 82 (60%) in the non-exertional group, 21 (55%) in the traumatic group, and 5 (4%) in the exertional group. The odds of AKI were higher in the non-exertional (OR 39, 95% CI: 13 - 116) and traumatic groups (OR 29, 95% CI: 9 - 89) compared to the exertional group. Stage III AKI occurred in 36 (12%) patients, mainly in the non-exertional group, with increased odds. No significant difference was found between the traumatic and exertional groups. Reduced kidney function after 3 months was observed in 3 patients - 2 in the non-exertional group and 1 in the traumatic group. Seven (2%) patients died, all in the non-exertional group.

CONCLUSION: The non-exertional group was associated with the highest risk, followed by the traumatic group, while exertional rhabdomyolysis generally had a milder course. Etiology may help identify patients at increased risk and support early clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Disproportionate reporting of acute renal events and chronic kidney disease with proton pump inhibitors and the potassium-competitive acid blocker vonoprazan: A time-to-onset and signal-detection analysis of the FAERS and JADER databases.
articles.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize renal injury reporting, separately for acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD), for proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and the potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB) vonoprazan. Reporting was analyzed in the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2014Q1 - 2024Q4) and JADER (April 2004 through the April 2025 release), defining acute renal events (referred to as AKI) and CKD by MedDRA/J v28.0 preferred terms. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) (signal = lower 95% confidence interval limit > 1) was the primary disproportionality measure, with the proportional reporting ratio and information component used as supportive measures; H2-receptor antagonists served as an active comparator class, time-to-onset was modeled with the Weibull distribution, and analyses were stratified by sex, age, and comorbidity.

RESULTS: PPIs showed disproportionate reporting of AKI and CKD in both databases (FAERS overall ROR 5.21 and 13.21; JADER 1.25 and 1.76), concordant across measures and after excluding pre-existing renal disease. Signals for vonoprazan were weaker and database-dependent (no FAERS CKD signal, ROR 0.92; weak JADER signal, 1.95). Time-to-onset was short in JADER (median 35 days); FAERS onset estimates were unreliable (median 1,520 days). The PPI signals persisted after excluding vonoprazan or dexlansoprazole.

CONCLUSION: Disproportionate reporting of AKI and CKD was observed for PPIs across two databases. These hypothesis-generating findings support renal monitoring and periodic reassessment of long-term acid suppression. The renal safety profile of vonoprazan remains inconclusive, and exposure-based studies are warranted.

articles.title: Preoperative 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography maximum standardized uptake value is independently associated with overall survival in surgically resected undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) is the most common adult soft tissue sarcoma subtype, with heterogeneous survival despite optimal surgery. We evaluated whether the preoperative maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) is independently associated with overall survival (OS) in surgically resected UPS.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 79 patients with localized UPS who underwent curative resection between 2015 and 2023. Preoperative SUVmax, tumor grade (French Federation of Cancer Centers Sarcoma Group), tumor size, and Ki-67 index were assessed. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors for OS.

RESULTS: The median age was 59 (range: 18-92) years; 53.2% of patients were male, and 59.5% of tumors were high grade. The median tumor size, Ki-67 index, and SUVmax were 60 mm, 60%, and 10, respectively. At a median follow-up of 58.9 months, median OS was not reached. In univariable analysis, tumor size (P = 0.007), Ki-67 (P = 0.001), SUVmax [hazard ratio: 1.08 per unit, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.04-1.10, P = 0.001], and high grade (P = 0.003) were associated with worse OS. In multivariable analysis, only SUVmax remained independently associated with OS (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.06 per unit, 95% CI: 1.02-1.10, P = 0.002), whereas grade, size, and Ki-67 did not retain significance.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT SUVmax is independently associated with OS in surgically resected UPS and provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological parameters.

articles.title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. This study aimed to characterize the cellular and spatial features of plaque instability at both single-cell and subcellular resolution.

METHODS AND RESULTS: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on carotid endarterectomy samples from patients with clinically and histologically classified stable or unstable plaques, consisting of more than 53,000 cells. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and T-lymphocytes accounted for ∼85% of plaque-resident cells, with unstable plaques showing increased abundance of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs, GZMK+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, and antigen-presenting macrophages. In contrast, stable plaques were enriched in contractile and fibroblast-like VSMCs, alongside MRC1+ resident-like macrophages. To then spatially map these populations, CosMx™ high-plex spatial transcriptomics was integrated utilizing the unprecedented whole-transcriptome (∼18,934 targets) Human Discovery RNA panel. This revealed a distinct spatially disorganized plaque architecture in unstable plaques, characterized by infiltration of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs and effector T-lymphocytes distributed across both the fibrotic cap and lipid core, alongside distinct multicellular microenvironments enriched for adaptive immune engagement. This was in contrast to stable plaques, which exhibited more structured, macrophage-dominant spatial microenvironments and neighborhoods. We lastly profiled ∼90,000 paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess the plaque macroenvironment. PBMCs surrounding unstable plaques displayed exclusive enrichment of CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes and effector T-lymphocytes, which were depleted surrounding stable plaques. Ligand-receptor interaction analyses within CCL and CXCL-mediated pathways revealed enhanced immune-stromal signaling between PBMC-derived monocytes and plaque-resident VSMCs in the unstable plaque group, with coordinated chemokine-driven interactions indicating a shift toward VSMC- and T-lymphocyte mediated recruitment of circulating immune cells.

CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate that carotid plaque instability is driven by spatially coordinated expansion of inflammatory VSMCs and effector immune cells within the plaque and from the circulation, with a shift from predominantly innate immune-dominant characteristics in stable plaques toward adaptive immune-enriched responses in unstable conditions. This integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approach refines an integrated immune-stromal framework linking local plaque remodeling with systemic immune activation, highlighting key tissue-resident and circulating contributors to instability and establishing a foundation for mechanism-informed diagnostics and targeted therapeutic strategies beyond stenosis severity.

articles.title: NOR-1 is an upstream regulator of Ca2+ homeostasis and calmodulin kinase II-dependent arrhythmogenesis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Dysregulation of NOR-1 has been reported in cardiovascular diseases associated with altered calcium handling. We therefore investigated how NOR-1 affects calcium homeostasis and arrhythmogenesis to identify the underlying mechanisms.

METHODS: We assessed the expression of NOR-1 and calcium regulatory proteins in myocardial samples from humans and mice that overexpress human NOR-1 in the heart (TgNOR-1). Gene promoter activity was determined by transient co-transfection assays. Calcium imaging, patch-clamp recordings and immunofluorescent labeling was performed in mouse cardiomyocytes. Experimental data were used for mathematical modeling. Arrhythmias were induced in vivo by an epinephrine/caffeine challenge.

RESULTS: In human cardiac samples, mRNA levels of genes coding for SERCA2a, CASQ2, TN-C1 and PLB correlated with those of NOR-1, while TgNOR-1 mice exhibited higher cardiac levels of these calcium regulatory proteins than wild-type animals (WT). NOR-1 increased luciferase activity driven by the proximal promoter of both human and mouse genes. Calcium transients were smaller in TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes while L-type calcium current and SR calcium content were unchanged. Mathematical modeling revealed that more calcium binds to CASQ2 and is released from the SR in TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes, but the resulting calcium transient is smaller because more calcium is buffered by TN-C1. Furthermore, NOR-1 transgenesis increased the level of reactive oxygen species and CAMKII oxidation, as well as RyR2 phosphorylation at Ser-2814, which led to a higher incidence of calcium waves and afterdepolarizations in resting TgNOR-1 cardiomyocytes. In electrically paced myocytes, NOR-1 transgenesis promoted extra-transients at low frequencies and calcium alternans at high frequencies. Importantly, these derangements in intracellular calcium handling concurred with a dramatic increase in epinephrine/caffeine-induced bidirectional ventricular tachycardia in TgNOR-1 mice. Moreover, the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine and the CAMKII inhibitor KN-93 attenuated arrythmia in TgNOR-1 mice and arrhythmogenic calcium release in isolated myocytes.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight NOR-1 as an upstream regulator of CAMKII-oxidation underlying arrhythmia induced by defective calcium homeostasis, pointing to therapies targeting CAMKII as a means to attenuate arrhythmia triggered by pathological upregulation of NOR-1.

articles.title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Changing health impacts of global ozone exposure.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
articles.abstract: As part of the second Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report (TOAR-II), we synthesize global observations and observationally constrained estimates of surface-level ozone (O3) with contemporary literature to characterize the global distribution and trends of long-term O3 exposure, focusing on two health-relevant metrics and health impacts attributable to long-term exposure. The highest 2016-2020 surface-level O3 concentrations are observed or estimated in South Asia, eastern China, and parts of the Middle East and North Africa. From 2000 to 2020, O3 declined across southeastern North America and parts of Eastern Europe, while the largest increases occurred in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Global premature mortality from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) attributable to long-term O3 exposure nearly doubled between 2000 and 2020, reaching approximately 500 000 deaths annually. This overall increase obscures decreasing attributable deaths across North America and Europe and increasing deaths across large parts of the Global South. To spur high-quality, robust research on O3 health impacts, we summarize state-of-the-science practices for conducting health impact assessments (HIAs) and characterizing associated uncertainty. We also call for expanded in situ monitoring, improved health datasets and epidemiologic evidence, and sustained precursor emission reductions to clarify and limit the growing global health burden of O3 under climate change and demographic shifts. This article is part of the theme issue 'Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II'.

articles.title: Psychometric Properties of the Turkish Version of the Preterm Infant Breastfeeding Behavior Scale (PIBBS).
articles.journal: Journal of human lactation : official journal of International Lactation Consultant Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm infants often experience difficulties in breastfeeding due to immature sucking and coordination skills, making reliable assessment tools essential for guiding effective clinical care and interventions.

AIM: This research was carried out to conduct the Turkish validity and reliability study of the Preterm Infant Breastfeeding Behavior Scale (PIBBS).

METHOD: The sample of the methodological study consisted of premature babies and their mothers with a gestational age of 33-37 weeks, hospitalized in the Neonatal Intensive Care Units and Gynecology and Obstetrics wards of Bursa City Hospital. Demographic/Obstetric and Neonatal Characteristics Form, PIBBS, and Bristol Breastfeeding Assessment Scale (BBAT) were used to collect research data.

RESULTS: The Content Validity Index at the Item Level was between 0.89 and 1, and the Content Validity Index at the Scale Level was 0.963. A positive and high correlation was found at the level of (r = 0.868; p < 0.001) between the total score of PIBBS and BBAT. A very strong positive correlation was observed between the first PIBBS measurement score and the retest second PIBBS measurement score (r = 0.841; p < 0.001). Kappa values for each item of PIBBS were between 0.805 and 0.933. Cronbach's Alpha reliability coefficient was 0.893.

CONCLUSION: Health professionals who care for preterm infants can be trained on the use of PIBBS in the evaluation of sucking skills of preterm infants and its use can be made widespread.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors across the spectrum of myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most.

METHODS: Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI.

PRIMARY OUTCOMES: all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

articles.title: Temporal trends in infectious risk among multiple myeloma patients treated with daratumumab: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Anti-cluster of differentiation 38 (Anti-CD38) monoclonal antibodies such as daratumumab are widely used in multiple myeloma (MM), yet the timing and magnitude of infectious risk remain incompletely defined. We performed an individual patient-level meta-analysis of six randomized trials (N = 2989) comparing daratumumab- versus non-daratumumab-containing regimens in newly diagnosed and relapsed/refractory MM, assessing infectious events over 2 years. Daratumumab-treated patients had higher rates of any-grade (79% vs. 61%) and grade ≥3 infections (29% vs. 20%) than controls, with risk peaking in the first 3 months (42% vs. 36%, p = 0.001) before plateauing. After adjustment, daratumumab was independently associated with grade ≥1 (odds ratio [OR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10-1.57), respiratory (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.11-1.71) and grade ≥3 (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.08-2.00) infection by 3 months. Daratumumab-treated patients had a higher rate of infection over 2 years (adjusted incidence rate ratio 1.60, 95% CI 1.47-1.73) and more frequently experienced recurrent infections (33% vs. 22% with multiple any-grade infections; 11% vs. 7% with multiple grade ≥3 infections). Preventive strategies were underused, with <20% of patients with severe respiratory infections receiving immunoglobulin replacement. These findings identify an early window of infectious vulnerability with daratumumab and support temporally targeted prevention and monitoring strategies in contemporary MM care.

articles.title: Prediction of Unfavorable Functional Status at Hospital Discharge in Older Adults with Traumatic Brain Injury : Model Development and Internal Evaluation.
articles.journal: Annals of geriatric medicine and research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) in older adults is an increasing public health burden. An early risk assessment of poor functional outcome can help guide prognosis and communication. The objective of the present study was to develop and internally validate a prediction model for poor functional status at discharge from the hospital for older adults with TBI.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study included 3,193 patients aged ≥65 years with TBI. The Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) was used to evaluate the functional status of the patient at hospital discharge and was dichotomized as favorable (GOS 4-5) or unfavorable (GOS 1-3). Logistic regression was used to analyze candidate predictors; then, backward selection with the Akaike Information Criterion was used for multivariable analysis. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was used to measure discrimination, and the calibration intercept, calibration slope, and Brier score were used to measure calibration. Optimism-corrected performance was estimated using 1,000 bootstrapped resamples in the internal validation. Bootstrap inclusion frequencies were used to evaluate the predictor-selection stability.

RESULTS: Among 3,193 patients, 224 (7.0%) had poor functional outcomes. Warfarin use, motor weakness, hypotension, category of GCS, pupillary response, basilar skull fracture, acute subdural hematoma, contusion/intracerebral hematoma, intraventricular hemorrhage, and basal cistern obliteration were predictor variables retained in the final model. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.964 (95% CI, 0.948-0.979). After 1,000 bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.962 with a calibration intercept of -0.001 and the calibration slope of 0.959.

CONCLUSION: The model demonstrated strong discrimination with limited optimism after bootstrap internal validation. External validation in independent populations is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Mapping Risk of Mental Disorders and Substance Use Among Conflict-Affected IDPs in the Majority World: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: The International journal of social psychiatry
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: According to the latest Global Report on Internal Displacement, there has been a 51% increase in internally displaced persons (IDPs) over the past five years, with most conflict-related displacements occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The World Health Organization estimated a 22% prevalence of mental disorders among conflict-affected populations in LMICs. Despite their particular vulnerability, research has largely focused on refugees in high-income countries, leaving gaps in understanding mental health risks faced by IDPs. This scoping review aims to map evidence on factors associated with mental disorders and substance use among IDPs in the majority world.

METHOD: The search included PubMed and Global Index Medicus (GIM), with supplementary searches in Google Scholar and relevant gray literature sources, including International Organization for Migration reports. Studies published in English and Spanish between 2014 and 2024 were included.

RESULTS: Relevant studies across Sub-Saharan Africa, Southwest Asia and North Africa (SWANA), Asia, and the Americas met the inclusion criteria. Findings showed that post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety were the most frequently studied mental disorders, while studies on substance use were more limited. The reported risk factor themes included loss and violence, health status and access, displacement conditions, trauma-related psychological factors, demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, social/governmental support, and resilience.

CONCLUSION: The studies mostly followed observational and cross-sectional quantitative designs, limiting causal inference and emphasizing the need to focus on qualitative and longitudinal approaches to better understand the long-term impacts of displacement on mental health and substance use.

articles.title: Joint Association of Longitudinal Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator Patterns and Hypertension Status with Incident Stroke Among Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages 0-3: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of longitudinal single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) patterns for stroke, particularly when considered in combination with hypertension (HTN), remains unclear among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.

AIMS: This study aimed to examine the association of combined longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status with incident stroke among adults with CKM syndrome stages 0-3.

STUDY DESIGN: A nationwide prospective cohort study.

METHODS: We included adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKM stages 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. SPISE was calculated at Waves 1 and 3, and incident stroke was ascertained through Wave 5. K-means clustering was used to identify longitudinal SPISE patterns, which were dichotomized as persistently low or non-persistently low. Participants were then cross-classified according to longitudinal SPISE pattern and baseline HTN status. Cumulative SPISE exposure was calculated from repeated SPISE measurements. Cox models were used to examine associations with incident stroke. Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-performance analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: Among 4,443 participants, 348 incident strokes occurred. A persistently low longitudinal SPISE pattern was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke than a persistently high pattern [hazard ratio (HR), 2.29; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.59-3.29]. Compared with the group with no HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern, stroke risk was higher in the group with no HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.12-1.95), the group with HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.10-2.23), and the group with HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.84-3.26). Higher cumulative SPISE exposure was inversely associated with incident stroke (HR per 1-unit increment, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93-0.97), with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. Incorporating the combined longitudinal SPISE pattern and HTN status increased the apparent C-index from 0.612 to 0.646. However, optimism-corrected discrimination was comparable between the combined model and the HTN-only model.

CONCLUSION: The combination of longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status identified a subgroup at the highest risk of incident stroke in this CKM population.

articles.title: Associations Between Perceived Social Support and Subjective and Structural Dimensions of Family Functioning Among Married Mothers of Children Receiving Psychiatric Treatment.
articles.journal: The International journal of social psychiatry
articles.abstract: BackgroundFamily functioning is closely associated with children's mental health, particularly in child psychiatry settings where caregiving demands are high. Perceived social support is recognized as a protective factor associated with coping processes, yet its relationship with family functioning remains complex and multidimensional.AimsThis study aimed to examine subjective and structural dimensions of family functioning among married mothers accompanying children receiving psychiatric treatment and to explore their associations with perceived social support.MethodThis quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted with 189 married mothers in a child psychiatry clinic in Türkiye. Data were collected using a sociodemographic information form, the Family APGAR Scale, the Family Assessment Device, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Descriptive statistics, bivariate Pearson correlation analyses, multivariate analyses of variance, and univariate between-subjects analyses were performed.ResultsAfter multiple-comparison correction, family support positively correlated with Family APGAR scores and was negatively associated with dysfunction across five dimensions. Total support was associated with Family APGAR scores and three FAD dimensions, while significant-other support was associated with affective responsiveness. No support indicator was associated with behavioral control. Family APGAR total scores showed strong negative associations with several FAD dimensions, although the magnitude varied across domains. The Family APGAR and FAD therefore captured related but non-identical aspects of family functioning, with the former reflecting subjective global perceptions of family functioning and the latter structural and functional processes across specific family domains. Multivariate analyses further indicated that Family APGAR total scores, FAD general functioning, and total perceived social support varied across selected sociodemographic and clinical characteristics.ConclusionsThe findings support a multidimensional understanding of family functioning. Family-centered assessment in child psychiatry should consider both subjective perceptions and structural and functional family processes. Because the study was cross-sectional, no conclusions can be drawn regarding temporal, causal, or reciprocal relationships.

articles.title: Achieving Risk-Specific Absolute LDL-C Threshold with PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Real-World, Single-Center Analysis.
articles.journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors emerged as an effective treatment for hypercholesterolemia in clinical trials, however real-world evidence shows considerable heterogeneity. We aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of injectable PCSK9 inhibitors in real-world patients.

METHODS: Our retrospective analysis included 45 consecutive adults, 18 (40%) men, mean age 57.4 years, inadequately controlled on, or intolerant to, statins and/or ezetimibe, and newly initiated on alirocumab 75 mg or 150 mg, evolocumab 140 mg, or inclisiran 284 mg. Biochemical parameters and adverse events were recorded at baseline and when LDL-C reached the risk-specific absolute threshold or the lowest LDL-C closest to it after starting PCSK9 inhibitors (<55 mg/dL very high, <70 mg/dL high cardiovascular risk, per European Society of Cardiology). LDL-C was also assessed at standardized time points (3, 6, 12, 18, 24 months).

RESULTS: At 3 and 6 months, LDL-C decreased by a median of 54.4% and 59.2% (both p < 0.001), with 52.4% and 50.0% of patients below threshold. The best LDL-C reduction was 66.9% (from 145 mg/dL to 50 mg/dL; p < 0.001) at a median time to first documented threshold attainment of 5 months. In an exploratory analysis, no significant association was detected between LDL-C reduction and sex, diabetes, statin intensity or ezetimibe use. No clinically relevant hepatic or muscular toxicity was attributed to PCSK9 inhibitors.

CONCLUSION: In real-world patients aiming to achieve the absolute LDL-C threshold on PCSK9 inhibitors, treatment was associated with marked LDL-C reduction after a median of 5 months.

articles.title: Dynamic Energy-Dissipating Interface Design Reconciles Thermal Performance with Interfacial Reliability.
articles.abstract: Highly filled thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for reliable heat dissipation in high-power electronics, yet restricted polymer chain mobility and reduced interfacial conformability make it difficult to achieve high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and crack-growth resistance simultaneously. We propose a dynamic energy-dissipating interface (DEDI) strategy that coordinates favorable interfacial affinity, stable chemical anchoring, and dynamic bulk energy dissipation to improve interfacial stability and crack resistance in highly filled TIMs. γ-Methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane (γ-MPS) provides stable chemical anchoring at the substrate interface, while urethane-associated polar interactions contribute to favorable interfacial affinity. Reversible disulfide and hydrogen-bond interactions within the bulk network promote deformation accommodation and mechanical energy dissipation. Surface-modified Al2O3/ZnO hybrid fillers form a multiscale network that provides efficient heat-transfer pathways. The resulting PSM-60-1.2 exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3.88 W·m-1·K-1, an adhesion strength of 4.25 MPa, and an adhesion energy of 3080.04 J·m-2. Combined experimental and finite-element analyses support coordinated interfacial stabilization, bulk energy dissipation, and enhanced thermomechanical deformation accommodation. After 100 thermal shock cycles between -40 and 150 °C, PSM-60-1.2 shows a 6.0 °C increase in maximum steady-state temperature, compared with 16.2 °C for the commercial thermally conductive adhesive, with less interfacial cracking and low-viscosity liquid infiltration. The DEDI design offers a molecular strategy for combining high thermal conductivity, high adhesion energy, and long-term thermomechanical reliability in highly filled TIMs.

articles.title: Demographic Data Concordance: A Prospective Observational Study of Adolescents, Caregivers, and the Electronic Health Record.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: (1) To measure the concordance of patient demographic data in the electronic health record (EHR); and (2) to determine the level of agreement for patient demographic data between patient report-EHR and patients-caregivers.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a prospective observational survey of 295 patients (age 12 to 17 years) and caregiver dyads presenting to a pediatric emergency department. The primary outcome was concordance, reporting kappa statistics with 95% CI, of caregiver-reported patient race, ethnicity, and sex and the EHR. Secondary outcomes were concordance between: (1) patient report and EHR and (2) patient and caregiver report, including gender identity and preferred language. We surveyed dyads on the perceived impact of demographic characteristics on emergency care and caregivers on preferences for reporting data.

RESULTS: For caregiver and EHR report of race, there was substantial agreement for Asian (κ=0.65, 95% CI: 0.44-0.86), Black/African American/African (κ=0.76, 95% CI: 0.66-0.86), and White (κ=0.66, 95% CI: 0.58-0.75) race and moderate agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=0.53, 95% CI: 0.44-0.61). Patient report and the EHR had similar concordance for race and poor agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=-0.17, 95% CI: -0.22 to -0.12). For patients and caregivers, there was strong concordance for race, ethnicity, language, and gender identity. Caregivers were more likely than pediatric patients to report that demographic factors affected emergency care. Most caregivers did not have preferences about demographic data reporting methods.

CONCLUSIONS: Concordance of patient race and ethnicity data in the EHR was variable and should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Bilateral Xanthogranulomatous Pyelonephritis in a Patient With Spina Bifida and Neurogenic Bladder: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGP) is a rare chronic inflammatory renal infection associated with urinary obstruction, recurrent infections, and progressive renal parenchymal destruction. Bilateral involvement is exceedingly uncommon and associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients with neurogenic bladder and impaired longitudinal urologic follow-up. CASE REPORT A 30-year-old man with spina bifida complicated by neurogenic bladder requiring intermittent catheterization presented with respiratory distress, profound anemia, and progressive functional decline. Imaging demonstrated severe bilateral hydronephrosis, diffuse renal parenchymal destruction and calcifications, and right-sided staghorn calculi, consistent with advanced bilateral XGP. The patient rapidly developed septic shock and acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Percutaneous nephrostomy drainage yielded purulent material, and cultures grew Morganella morganii, Candida parapsilosis, and Candida tropicalis. His hospital course was complicated by dialysis-dependent renal failure, recurrent respiratory failure, and prolonged ventilatory dependence. Definitive surgical intervention was considered but deferred because of severe anatomical deformities, clinical instability, and prohibitive operative risk. After prolonged hospitalization, he was discharged to a long-term acute care facility but later died from complications related to tracheostomy. CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates the severe clinical consequences of advanced bilateral XGP in a high-risk patient with neurogenic bladder. The coexistence of recurrent infection, urinary obstruction, and disrupted longitudinal follow-up is consistent with recognized risk factors for upper urinary tract deterioration, although their individual contribution to this patient's disease progression cannot be established. The case underscores the management challenges that arise when bilateral renal destruction and systemic instability limit definitive source-control options.

articles.title: Early outcomes after complete atrioventricular septal defect repair beyond one year of age: a single-centre comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete atrioventricular septal defect is usually repaired during early infancy, but delayed referral remains common where access to specialised congenital cardiac surgery is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare early outcomes after repair in patients aged 12 months or younger and those older than 12 months.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included 81 patients who underwent repair between 2020 and 2024. All patients evaluated for repair underwent cardiac catheterisation, and those with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance underwent vasoreactivity testing with 100% oxygen and inhaled nitric oxide. In-hospital mortality, major complications, pulmonary artery pressure, atrioventricular valve regurgitation, and perioperative outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Thirty-five patients were aged 12 months or younger and 46 were older than 12 months. Median ages were 8 and 14 months, respectively. In-hospital mortality occurred in 3 of 35 and 4 of 46 patients, respectively. Major complications occurred in 6 of 35 and 11 of 46 patients. No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, major complications, ventilation duration, ICU stay, pulmonary artery pressure, or early atrioventricular valve regurgitation. Confidence intervals around mortality and major-complication estimates were wide.

CONCLUSION: Repair beyond 12 months was feasible in selected patients considered operable after invasive assessment, but in-hospital mortality remained substantial and estimates were imprecise. These findings do not establish equivalence and should not support intentional delay of repair.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Central Retinal Artery Occlusion: A Canadian Neurology Perspectives Survey.
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
articles.abstract: This is the first Canadian study to examine practice patterns and perceptions of central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) management among neurologists. An online survey was distributed nationwide to neurologists practicing in hyperacute stroke in Canada. Of 64 respondents, over half reported never having provided thrombolysis, although there was willingness to provide it if patients met the criteria. Ophthalmology support was deemed necessary in most cases of suspected CRAO to facilitate thrombolysis; however, virtual consultation would always be accepted by 41% of providers. These survey findings help to understand multidisciplinary practice patterns to develop educational strategies and inform future frameworks to guide care for patients with CRAO.

articles.title: Infectious complications and microbiological patterns following Versius assisted robotic surgery: a cohort study from Pakistan.
articles.abstract: Infectious complications following robot-assisted surgery are relatively rare and unexplored, particularly in low and middle-income countries. We aimed to evaluate post-procedure infections and perioperative microbiological pattern among patients undergoing Versius-assisted robotic surgery in Pakistan. We conducted a retrospective cohort study in patients undergoing Versius-assisted robotic surgery at a quaternary care centre in Lahore, Pakistan. Patients were recruited from April 2023 to February 2024. Post-procedure infections were defined as compatible clinical features along with a positive microbiological culture. Pre and post-operative microbiological findings were evaluated using univariable analysis. Among 105 patients, 8 (7.6%) developed confirmed post-procedure infection. Preoperative urine cultures were obtained in 60 patients, of whom 16 (26.7%) had positive results. Postoperative cultures were obtained in 59 patients, of whom 19 (32.2%) had positive results. A positive pre-operative culture was associated with post-operative culture positivity (OR 9.07, 95%CI 1.72 - 47.68, p = 0.009), but was not significantly associated with culture-confirmed postoperative infection (OR 4.85, 95%CI 0.73 - 32.22, p = 0.112). A history of an infected kidney was associated in exploratory univariable analysis with post-procedure infection (OR 10.77, 95%CI 2.29 - 50.54, p = 0.004). Culture-confirmed postoperative infections were documented in 7.6% of patients. A history of an infected kidney was associated with postoperative infection in exploratory unadjusted analysis. These findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Emergency undocking in robotic surgery: an international Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract: Emergency undocking in robotic surgery is an uncommon but high-stakes event. Published protocols are predominantly single-institution and specialty-specific, and no multidisciplinary cross-specialty consensus exists. This study aimed to establish expert consensus on the definitions and procedural steps of safe emergency undocking. A four-round modified Delphi study was conducted with an international panel of robotic theatre team members. Round 1 used open-text questions to generate themes; Rounds 2 to 4 presented binary statements (Yes / No / Unable to rate), with a pre-specified threshold of 80% agreement and Unable to rate responses excluded from the denominator. Items below threshold, or reaching threshold with substantive comments, were revised and re-presented. Fifty-two experts from 10 countries consented and completed Round 1. The panel comprised lead or experienced console surgeons (53.8%), first assistants (30.8%), surgical care practitioners (9.6%), anaesthetists (3.8%), and one industry representative (1.9%). Response rates were 80.8%, 80.8%, and 76.9% for Rounds 2 to 4 respectively. Thirty-seven statements reached consensus, comprising two definitions, six common pathway items, 18 controlled undocking items, and 11 uncontrolled undocking items. Of the 37 statements, 25 were classified as platform-agnostic and 12 as platform-dependent. Three role-allocation items were deferred to a planned subsequent round. This Delphi process produced 37 consensus statements defining controlled and uncontrolled emergency undocking and the steps for each. The panel was predominantly United Kingdom-based and surgical, and included no scrub or circulating practitioners. The resulting framework requires simulation and clinical validation before implementation.

articles.title: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction: is it the new Ariadne's string?
articles.abstract: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction (HFsnEF) is an emerging and incompletely characterized phenotype within the heart failure (HF) spectrum. Although no universally accepted LVEF threshold for HFsnEF has been established and different definitions have been used across published studies, for the purposes of this review HFsnEF is operationally defined as HF with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 65%. Importantly, a supranormal LVEF should not be interpreted as evidence of enhanced ventricular performance. Patients with HFsnEF may exhibit smaller left ventricular (LV) volumes, concentric remodeling, increased myocardial stiffness, impaired longitudinal deformation, reduced stroke volume and preload reserve, and elevated filling pressures, particularly during exercise. HFsnEF is unlikely to represent a single disease entity; rather, it encompasses heterogeneous pathophysiological substrates and clinical phenotypes, including hypertensive and cardiometabolic remodeling, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), and other conditions associated with hyperdynamic ventricular function. Accordingly, the diagnostic evaluation should extend beyond recognition of an elevated LVEF and systematically identify the underlying phenotype and potentially treatable causes through comprehensive echocardiography, myocardial deformation imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, disease-specific testing, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic assessment when indicated. Therapeutic evidence specific to HFsnEF remains limited. No randomized clinical trial has specifically evaluated conventional HF pharmacotherapy in a population prospectively defined by LVEF > 65%; therefore, evidence for conventional HF and cardiometabolic therapies is derived predominantly from broader HFpEF populations or subgroup analyses and should be regarded as indirect rather than definitive evidence for HFsnEF. In contrast, recognition of specific underlying diseases, particularly ATTR-CM, HCM, and significant valvular heart disease, may permit evidence-based disease-specific treatment. This review summarizes the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical phenotypes of HFsnEF and proposes a practical phenotype-guided approach to diagnosis and management. Standardized definitions and prospective trials specifically addressing patients with LVEF > 65% are needed to establish evidence-based therapeutic strategies for this population.

articles.title: Diffuse osteosclerosis in acute megakaryoblastic leukemia on [18 F]FDG-PET/CT.
Cardiovascular resilience in centenarians.
articles.abstract: Centenarians - individuals aged ≥100 years - provide a unique human model for understanding resilience to cardiovascular ageing. Although cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, including hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease, are common in centenarians, their onset is typically delayed relative to that in individuals aged 80-100 years. Centenarians characteristically have structural changes in the heart and vessels, including concentric left ventricular remodelling, increased myocardial stiffness and vascular ageing, but often without the expected burden of myocardial infarction or overt heart failure.
