Their cardiometabolic profile is generally favourable, marked by preserved insulin sensitivity in cohorts with a low prevalence of diabetes mellitus, mid-range lipid levels and a low prevalence of obesity. Centenarians also have a distinctive inflammatory and gastrointestinal phenotype, characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation with elevated anti-inflammatory signalling, a gut microbiome that more closely resembles that of younger adults, and preserved intestinal barrier integrity. Genetically and epigenetically, exceptional longevity reflects highly polygenic contributions, selective maintenance of genomic stability and markedly younger epigenetic age compared with chronological age. In this Review, we summarize data on the cardiovascular system among centenarians by framing observations of longevity as a composite of delayed pathology, adaptive compensation and survivorship selection. Understanding the biological, behavioural and environmental mechanisms underlying cardiovascular resilience in extreme longevity might inform strategies to extend cardiovascular healthspan across all ages.

articles.title: Comparison of visual estimation of ventricular systolic function with quantitative echocardiographic markers in newborn infants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatologist-performed echocardiography (NPE) is increasingly practiced. NPE operators typically use visual estimation of systolic function and, if indicated, confirm function using quantitative echocardiographic markers. This exploratory study aims to compare the concordance between qualitative and quantitative echocardiographic markers among NPE and non-NPE operators.

METHODS: We studied a cohort of newborn infants, undergoing routine NPE by the authors at Homerton University Hospital and Aberdeen Maternity Hospital from April 2024 to October 2024. Blinded NPE and non-NPE operators independently assessed left and right ventricular systolic function visually. We compared visual estimation with standard quantitative echocardiographic markers such as shortening fraction, Simpson's ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain for left ventricle and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and fractional area change for right ventricle. We examined the concordance between visual estimation and quantitative echocardiographic markers for biventricular systolic function.

RESULTS: Sixty infants with a mean (SD) gestation and birth weight of 34 (6.2) weeks and 2311 (1319) grams respectively were examined. Sensitivity testing for all echocardiographic parameters ranged from 25% to 80% whereas specificity ranged from 38% to 78%. Sensitivity increased with worsening grades of LV dysfunction defined using shortening fraction. While concordance between NPE and non-NPE operator was generally limited across most echocardiographic parameters, test-retest reliability was acceptable for several quantitative measures, including Simpson's ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain and right ventricular fractional area change.

CONCLUSION: Visual estimation may be a useful bedside tool for detecting severe ventricular dysfunction in newborn infants; however; quantitative echocardiographic measures are likely to improve the assessment of mild to moderate dysfunction. Further studies should confirm these findings in a larger cohort with a higher representation of infants with ventricular dysfunction.

articles.title: A systematic review of the spectrum of magnetic resonance imaging features of degenerative thoracic myelopathy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Degenerative thoracic myelopathy (DTM) encompasses a range of degenerative pathologies associated with symptomatic spinal cord compression. Diagnosis is achieved through clinical history, examination, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). A comprehensive review of the MRI features of DTM and their clinical significance is currently lacking. The objective was therefore to synthesise current evidence.

METHODS: A systematic review was performed adhering to PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE and Embase were searched. Screening, data extraction and risk of bias assessments were performed in duplicate. A qualitative synthesis was conducted following the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) guidelines.

RESULTS: Of 7937 records, 59 papers studying 2940 patients satisfied inclusion criteria, including one cross-sectional and 58 cohort studies. DTM was most common in the lower thoracic spine (62.5%, 880/1409), with a roughly equal prevalence in the upper (18.2%, 256/1409) and middle regions (19.4%, 273/1409). Ossification of the ligamentum flavum (OLF) was the most common pathology (71.4%, 2065/2893), followed by intervertebral disc herniation (20.1%, 582/2893) and ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) (19.7%, 569/2893). Measurements of spinal canal compromise were described in 55.5% of patients (1631/2940) and spinal cord signal change in 30.0% (881/2940). Spinal canal compromise, spinal cord signal change, OLF, OPLL and multilevel disease were associated with greater DTM severity and poorer functional recovery.

CONCLUSION: Ligamentous pathologies are significantly more prevalent than disc related pathologies in the DTM literature. Spinal cord signal change and extent of spinal canal compromise correlate with clinical outcomes. Standardisation of terminology for imaging features and study design are required to improve future research.

articles.title: Pharmacist-Led Medication Titration for Cardiometabolic Disease: Evidence, Equity, and Scale.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review community-based pharmacist-led medication titration across cardiometabolic conditions and the infrastructure needed to deliver this model at scale.

RECENT FINDINGS: This review reframes cardiometabolic medication optimization as a continuum from passive gap identification to active longitudinal medication management. Registries, dashboards, audit and feedback, electronic health record alerts, and inpatient initiation can identify undertreatment or prompt prescribing, but they do not provide infrastructure for dose adjustment, monitoring, adherence support, and medication-access navigation. Pharmacist-led, team-based models occupy the active end of this continuum. The strongest evidence is in hypertension, with meaningful blood pressure reductions; in heart failure, interdisciplinary titration programs more directly address target-dose achievement than alerts or decision-support tools. Emerging data extend this framework to diabetes, lipidology, and obesity. Value-based care provides a reimbursement framework to support these services. Pharmacist-led titration can close gaps between therapies and delivery, but scaling requires equity-focused implementation, flexible staffing, population health infrastructure that connects artificial intelligence-enabled patient identification to action, and sustainable reimbursement.

articles.title: Laparoscopic versus open approaches for ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement is the standard treatment for pediatric hydrocephalus. While the open approach has been traditionally used, laparoscopic-assisted techniques have gained increasing attention. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of laparoscopic versus open approaches for VP shunt placement in children through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to March 2026. Comparative studies evaluating laparoscopic versus open VP shunt placement in pediatric patients were included. Primary outcomes included operative time and length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes included distal revision rate, overall revision rate, infection rate, and overall complications. Pooled mean differences (MD) and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using Review Manager 5.4.

RESULTS: A total of 8 studies involving 9184 patients (1151 laparoscopic and 8033 open) were included. There were no significant differences in operative time or length of hospital stay. The distal revision rate and infection rate were also comparable between groups. However, laparoscopic surgery was associated with a significantly lower overall revision rate (OR = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.45-0.92; P = 0.02) and fewer overall complications (OR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.44-0.88; P = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic-assisted VP shunt placement is a safe and effective alternative to the open approach in pediatric patients. It may reduce overall revision rates and postoperative complications without increasing operative time or infection risk. Further high-quality prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Dose-Response Effects of Exercise Training on Circulating Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF): A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is involved in neuroplasticity, but circulating BDNF is not a validated surrogate for brain BDNF. We synthesised randomised controlled trials comparing chronic exercise with a non-exercising control. Change-score standardised mean differences (Hedges' g) were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp inference. The analysis included 48 trials, 56 exercise-versus-control comparisons and 2361 unique participants. Shared control sample sizes were apportioned across comparisons, with trial-cluster robust sensitivity analyses. Exercise increased circulating BDNF on average (g = 0.41, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.57; p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 67.0%; 95% prediction interval - 0.54 to 1.36). Serum-based comparisons yielded g = 0.27 (95% CI 0.10 to 0.44) and plasma-based comparisons g = 0.69 (0.37 to 1.00); the matrix moderator was significant in the primary analysis (p = 0.017) but not under trial-cluster robust inference (p = 0.065). Population, modality and intervention duration were not significant primary moderators. In the joint dose model (33 comparisons from 29 trials), neither total prescribed exercise volume (β = 0.037 per 1000 min, p = 0.614) nor vigorous versus moderate intensity (β =  - 0.190, p = 0.361) was associated with the BDNF effect. Weekly-volume and quadratic analyses did not establish a dose-response relationship. The overall effect remained positive after restricting sampling to approximately ≥ 24 h after exercise (g = 0.35, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.58). Egger's test indicated small-study effects (p = 0.011). The certainty of evidence was very low. Chronic exercise is associated with an average increase in circulating BDNF, but heterogeneity, methodological limitations and uncertain moderator effects prevent a biomarker-specific exercise prescription or an inference of increased central BDNF. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261448624.

articles.title: HDL-C as a mediator of PPCP-related kidney function decline in community-dwelling elderly: a mixture analysis approach.
articles.abstract: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) are widespread environmental contaminants, but their associations with kidney function and lipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. This study included 2758 adults aged ≥ 60 years in Anhui Province, China, during 2022-2023 and used a cross sectional design. Urinary concentrations of 48 PPCPs and two metabolites were measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation. Individual associations were assessed using logistic and linear regression, and mixture associations using weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression. Restricted cubic splines examined nonlinear associations, and exploratory mediation analyses assessed the statistical contribution of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Among nine PPCPs with detection frequencies > 50%, doxycycline, enrofloxacin, acetaminophen, metformin, and cotinine were associated with lower eGFR after full adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Coefficients ranged from - 3.00 to - 0.93 mL/min/1.73 m2 per tenfold increase in urinary concentration. Tylosin and caffeine were positively associated with eGFR. The WQS index was inversely associated with eGFR, with metformin receiving the largest weight. HDL-C showed a positive nonlinear association with eGFR. Under the mediation model assumptions, HDL-C statistically accounted for 12.21-29.30% of the associations involving enrofloxacin, metformin, and acetaminophen, and 13.78% of the mixture association. The indirect association for cotinine was nonsignificant. These findings remain exploratory. Prospective studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and address possible reverse causation.

articles.title: Salivary 1H NMR metabolic profiling of diabetic patients with and without periodontitis: an exploratory pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis is a widespread chronic inflammatory condition that frequently coexists with diabetes mellitus (DM). Identifying non-invasive biomarkers is essential for early detection, targeted therapy, and better understanding of the bidirectional relationship between these two diseases. This study aimed to investigate salivary metabolomic profiles in diabetic individuals with and without periodontitis to identify candidate metabolites associated with periodontitis in patients with diabetes.

METHODS: This pilot study compared salivary 1H NMR metabolomic profiles of patients with diabetes with and without periodontitis (n = 13 per group). Unstimulated whole saliva was collected from both groups. Partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) was applied to differentiate between the groups. Spectral variables with VIP > 1 were selected for metabolite annotation, followed by metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) to identify dysregulated metabolic pathways.

RESULTS: Using the PLS-DA model, a total of 78 discriminating variables were identified, leading to the annotation of ten key metabolites: glycolic acid, thymidine, tyramine, deoxyguanosine, cytidine, uridine, NADPH, ADP, serotonin, and nicotinate. MSEA revealed significant pathway disturbances, with pyrimidine metabolism emerging as a notably enriched pathway.

CONCLUSION: The metabolomics study of saliva using 1H NMR showed distinct metabolic disturbances, particularly in pyrimidine metabolism, in diabetic periodontitis. Although these altered metabolites could serve as potential candidates for non-invasive biomarkers, independent validation from a large cohort is still required before they can be translated into clinical diagnostic use.

articles.title: The Illusion of Recovery From Atrial Fibrillation, a Review of Postcardioversion Anticoagulation Guidelines.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in clinical practice and an independent, well-established risk factor for ischemic stroke. However, restoring sinus rhythm via cardioversion does not eliminate this risk. Cardioversion itself transiently increases thromboembolic risk more than 10-fold, driven by atrial stunning, a state in which the left atrium and left atrial appendage remain mechanically dysfunctional despite normalized electrical activity seen on an electrocardiogram. Retrospective data show that thromboembolic events are clustered heavily within the first 2 weeks postcardioversion, supporting the near-universal recommendation of at least 4 weeks of continued therapeutic anticoagulation postcardioversion for AF duration more than 12 to 48 hours, regardless of baseline stroke risk score. Beyond this initial 4-week recommendation, the decision to continue anticoagulation is based on a comprehensive assessment of the patient's thromboembolic risk profile, rather than rhythm status or cardioversion success. Multiple trials have demonstrated a significant increase in the incidence of ischemic strokes in patients who had a premature discontinuation of anticoagulation postcardioversion. Additionally, having a prior stroke, the heaviest weighted risk-stratification variable, favors indefinite anticoagulation regardless of postcardioversion rhythm outcome. Current guidelines provide a framework for approaching postcardioversion anticoagulation, including a fixed 4-week anticoagulation course encompassing the atrial stunning period, followed by individualized risk-stratification to determine the indication for continued anticoagulation. Nevertheless, future research is still required to better elucidate whether anticoagulation can be safely discontinued after completion of the recommended 4-week postcardioversion anticoagulation course in patients with a prior AF-related stroke.

articles.title: Early Custody Mortality: Operational Safeguards for Nursing Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals entering U.S. jail face elevated mortaility risk, particularly during the earliest stages of detention.

AIMS: To examine national mortality patterns to identify timing- and mechanism-specific risk concentrations and their implications for forensic nursing practice and early-custody care.

METHODS: We conducted a descriptive analysis of Bureau of Justice Statistics mortality data to identify stable patterns in timing (≤24 hr, ≤7 days, ≤30 days), mechanisms of death, and distribution across the early-custody period. Findings were translated into operational domains relevant to intake and early-custody management from a nursing perspective.

RESULTS: Mortality risk was highly concentrated in early custody. Approximately 40% of deaths occurred within 1 week of admission, more than half of suicides occurred within 30 days, and about 12% occurred within 24 hours. Suicide was the leading cause of death, with ~90% involving hanging or suffocation. Drug and alcohol intoxication deaths clustered on the first day of detention.

DISCUSSION: Early custody represents a predictable and concentrated nursing and public health risk window. The convergence of suicide risk, substance-related mortality, and uneven implementation of nursing-sensitive practices suggests that booking and early detention should be treated as structured clinical events. Screening, observation, withdrawal management, and medication continuity may serve as important operational safeguards to strengthen early-custody mortality prevention.

articles.title: Herpes Zoster and Cardiovascular Disease: An Unexpected Association.
articles.abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ), the reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus (VZV), is increasingly being recognized as more than a dermatologic and neurologic disease. In recent years, multiple meta-analyses have linked HZ infection to a clinically significant increase in the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and other major adverse cardiovascular events, an effect that is most pronounced in the first days to weeks following the acute HZ infection, with a gradual decrease in risk over time. The proposed mechanism centers on a productive viral infection of arterial walls, a phenomenon described as VZV vasculopathy, with transmural inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and thrombosis, all superimposed on the systemic inflammatory and prothrombotic state that accompanies the acute HZ infection. The evidence for an association between HZ infection and cardiovascular events has grown stronger with recent multiple large cohort studies demonstrating that patients who received HZ vaccination had a significantly lower rate of major adverse cardiovascular events, MI, stroke, heart failure, and arrhythmia. However, while these cohort studies have helped researchers identify the potential association of HZ vaccination and reduced cardiovascular risk, there remains a need for a randomized controlled trial to establish causality between these factors. Currently underway, a randomized controlled trial is directly evaluating whether HZ vaccination in a large population lowers the incidence of cardiovascular events, including stroke, MI, and cardiovascular death. Nevertheless, the 2026 American College of Cardiology guidelines now include a strong recommendation for HZ vaccination given the growing body of evidence regarding the association of HZ vaccination with cardiovascular events.

articles.title: Characteristics and Treatment Utilisation Patterns of Individuals Using Tirzepatide for Type 2 Diabetes in Germany.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study describes real-world characteristics and utilisation patterns of tirzepatide among adults with type 2 diabetes in German office-based practice.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study analysed data from the CompuGroup Medical Healthcare Database. Cohort 1 initiated tirzepatide between 1 December 2023 and 31 March 2024 and cohort 2 between 1 July and 30 September 2024. A subgroup of cohort 1 with ≥ 6 months' follow-up data and uninterrupted tirzepatide use (cohort 1a) was also analysed. Descriptive statistics summarised baseline characteristics, prior therapy, and dosing patterns.

RESULTS: Cohort 1 included 1223 individuals and cohort 2 included 2300; mean (± standard deviation) age was 59 ± 12 and 60 ± 12 years, respectively, and approximately 54% were male. Comorbidities, especially hypertension and dyslipidaemia, were frequent. Most individuals had prior insulin and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) treatment (cohort 1, 72.1%; cohort 2, 59.6%). A total of 458 individuals had 6 months' follow-up (cohort 1a). The most common starting dose was 2.5 mg (71.2%). Use of higher doses gradually increased over time, with 5.0 mg becoming the most prevalent; at 6 months, 35.9% of individuals received 5.0 mg and 18.6% received 10.0 mg.

CONCLUSION: This first comprehensive real-world study of tirzepatide use in Germany showed tirzepatide initiation primarily after GLP-1 RA and/or insulin therapy. Most individuals remained on 5.0 mg, with a notable proportion escalating to 10.0 mg. Cohort characteristics were generally similar to those in the SURPASS trials, supporting the relevance of trial findings to clinical practice.

articles.title: Choosing Cardiovascular Assessment and Risk-Prediction Tools Across the Care Pathway: A Clinician-Oriented Review.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate and efficient risk stratification essential across the care pathway. Numerous tools support emergency triage, disease assessment, procedural decision-making, long-term prevention, atrial fibrillation management, and evaluation of functional status, but no single model is applicable across all clinical settings or populations. This clinician-oriented review categorizes and critically compares commonly used cardiovascular assessment and risk-prediction tools, including History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events, and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction for emergency triage; Agatston, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery for anatomical and clinical assessment; European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation, Society of Thoracic Surgeons, and Revised Cardiac Risk Index, for procedural risk; and Framingham, the pooled cohort equations implemented in the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Risk Estimator, Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, QResearch Cardiovascular Risk Algorithm 3, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs for long-term prediction. Congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke/transient ischemic attack (2 points), congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 (2 points), diabetes, stroke/TIA (2 points), vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category (female), and hypertension, abnormal renal/liver function, stroke, bleeding history, labile international normalized ratio, elderly, drugs/alcohol, are discussed in the context of atrial fibrillation, alongside New York Heart Association and the Seattle Angina Questionnaire as measures of functional status and quality of life. For each tool, we examine its clinical purpose, principal variables, strengths, limitations, practical applications, and areas of overlap. Differences in implementation across healthcare systems and patient populations are considered to support context-appropriate selection. Persistent limitations include poor standardization, reliance on data that may be unavailable in resource-constrained settings, limited transportability, and incomplete integration into clinical workflows. Greater harmonization, external validation, digital automation, and the careful incorporation of biomarkers and artificial intelligence may support more accessible, dynamic, and personalized cardiovascular risk assessment.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Self-Expanding Versus Balloon-Expandable Valves in Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis, with self-expanding valves (SEV) and balloon-expandable valves (BEV) representing the two major platforms. However, their comparative clinical and hemodynamic performance remains uncertain. We systematically searched four electronic databases through August 2026 for studies comparing SEV and BEV in patients undergoing TAVR. The primary outcomes were permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and change in mean pressure gradient (MPG), while secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, paravalvular leakage (PVL), heart failure hospitalization, coronary obstruction, and prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). Twenty-three studies involving 21,609 patients were included. Compared with BEV, SEV was associated with a significantly greater reduction in MPG (MD -4.48, 95% CI -5.29 to -3.67; P < 0.0001) and lower risks of moderate (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.42-0.75) and severe PPM (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.44). Conversely, SEV was associated with higher risks of PPI (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.14-1.72; P < 0.0001), moderate-to-severe PVL (RR 2.28, 95% CI 1.65-3.14; P < 0.0001), and a small but significant increase in all-cause mortality. No significant differences were observed in MACE, stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or coronary obstruction..

articles.title: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Skin Tear Management: Educational Needs of Senior Nursing Students in a Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maintaining skin integrity is a critical nursing responsibility, yet skin tears remain one of the most underrecognized wounds in clinical practice. This study aimed to assess senior nursing students' knowledge regarding skin tears and to identify educational and experiential factors influencing their competence and perceived preparedness.

METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional descriptive design study was conducted with 610 senior nursing students from 4 universities. Data were collected using the Student Information Form and a validated version of the Skin Tear Knowledge Assessment Instrument. Descriptive and inferential statistics examined associations between knowledge scores and demographic or educational characteristics.

RESULTS: Students demonstrated a moderate overall level of knowledge regarding skin tears (mean score = 8.62 ± 2.74; standardized = 50.7%). The highest scores were observed in classification and observation, and the lowest in treatment and etiology. Female students, those who had taken elective wound care courses, and those with clinical exposure to skin tear cases scored significantly higher (P < .05). Only 7% of students considered their knowledge sufficient, whereas 81% expressed a desire for further training.

CONCLUSIONS: Senior nursing students demonstrated significant gaps in their understanding of skin tear etiology, prevention, and treatment, highlighting unmet educational needs in undergraduate nursing programs. Addressing these gaps through structured, competency-based strategies-such as simulation-based wound care training, International Skin Tear Advisory Panel-guided instruction, and supervised clinical experiences-may improve students' clinical reasoning and readiness for evidence-based practice. Strengthening educational exposure to skin tear management has the potential to enhance early recognition and prevention in clinical settings, ultimately contributing to improved patient outcomes.

articles.title: Prevalence of food insecurity in households with children under 5 years of age in Ecuador: analysis of the national child malnutrition surveys.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the national prevalence and distribution of food insecurity (FI) among households with children younger than 5 years in Ecuador and to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) using two consecutive nationally representative surveys.

DESIGN: This cross-sectional study employed descriptive statistics and Tobit regression models using STATA v17.

SETTING: We used secondary data from the National Survey on Child Malnutrition in Ecuador, including food security (FS) information for 2022-2023 and 2023-2024, to construct the prevalence time series.

PARTICIPANTS: We analysed data from 19 187 households (22 260 children) surveyed in the first round and 20 186 households (23 187 children) surveyed in the second round.

RESULTS: FIES showed adequate reliability in both rounds (Rasch reliability 0·80 and 0·79). Seven of eight FIES items showed significant reductions between rounds. The prevalence of moderate-or-severe FI remained high, decreasing from 40·79 % in 2022-2023 to 39·18 % in 2023-2024 (p = 0·239). Severe FI declined significantly from 4·83 % to 3·52 % (p = 0·002). In both rounds, FI was more prevalent in rural areas, the Amazon region, priority territories, Indigenous and Afro-descendant populations and households experiencing poverty or unmet basic needs. In 2023-2024, FI was associated with priority area residence, Indigenous ethnicity, poverty due to unmet basic needs, older child age groups and stunting.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite reductions in severe FI, nearly four in ten households with young children in Ecuador continue to experience moderate-or-severe FI, with persistent territorial, ethnic and socio-economic inequalities. Integrated policies linking FS, child nutrition and poverty reduction are needed.

articles.title: Bacterial distribution and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of ascitic fluid isolates from dogs and cats in Japan.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Septic peritonitis is a life-threatening condition in dogs and cats, requiring appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Thus, knowledge of local bacterial epidemiology and antimicrobial susceptibility is crucial. However, large-scale comparative data in Japan are lacking. This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated bacterial isolates from canine and feline ascitic fluid samples submitted to a diagnostic laboratory in Japan between October 2022 and March 2026. Bacterial distribution was evaluated in 673 isolates from 496 ascitic fluid samples, and antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed for Enterobacterales, Enterococcus spp., and anaerobic bacteria. Gram-negative bacilli were the most frequently isolated bacterial group (55.6%), followed by gram-positive cocci (29.6%) and anaerobic bacteria (12.0%). Escherichia coli was the most frequently isolated bacterium (39.4%). Dogs had significantly higher isolation rates of Enterobacterales, whereas anaerobic bacteria were significantly more prevalent in cats. Polymicrobial infection rates were similar between the two host species. Antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of Enterobacterales and Enterococcus spp. were largely comparable between dogs and cats. Amikacin exhibited the highest antimicrobial activity against Enterobacterales, whereas enrofloxacin demonstrated limited activity against Enterobacterales and Enterococcus spp. Chloramphenicol exhibited potent activity against all major bacterial groups. Feline anaerobic isolates were significantly more susceptible to cefmetazole and clindamycin than canine isolates. To our knowledge, this is the first large-scale epidemiological study of bacterial distribution and antimicrobial susceptibility in canine and feline ascitic fluid isolates in Japan. These findings provide valuable epidemiological evidence to guide the selection of appropriate antimicrobial therapy in canine and feline abdominal infections.

articles.title: Correction to: 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, in collaboration with the European Renal Association (ERA): Developed by the task force on the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC).
The Bag Is Not Always Bad: Intrahospital Spread of 2-Step Urinary Tract Infection Screening.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Urine cultures are frequently collected in hospitalized children for urinary tract infection (UTI) screening, despite often being unnecessary, invasive, and resource intensive. We aimed to decrease the proportion of unnecessary urine cultures in admitted children aged 90 days to 24 months from 65% to 45% over 1 year.

METHODOLOGY: The Model for Improvement guided problem understanding and change ideas. The main intervention included a 2-step UTI screening pathway previously implemented at our institution's emergency department with emphasis on completing point-of-care urinalysis (UA) on noninvasive urine bag sample. If positive for pyuria, bladder catheterization was performed for urine culture. Additional interventions included electronic medical record order set, education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and alignment with the institution's Choosing Wisely program. The primary outcome was the proportion of urine cultures completed without preceding positive UA screen. The balancing measure was the number of missed UTIs. Analysis used Statistical Process Control charts.

RESULTS: Baseline data (April 2020-March 2021) demonstrated that 65% of urine cultures were collected without a preceding positive UA. Postintervention data (April 2021-January 2025) demonstrated a decreased proportion of urine cultures collected without preceding positive UA screen from 65% to 22%. Special cause variation was detected 1 year following implementation of the pathway with sustained change during the study period. There was no increase in missed UTIs.

CONCLUSIONS: Process standardization using 2-step UTI screening pathway reduced unnecessary invasive urine culture collection in hospitalized children. The novel spread of this initiative to inpatient pediatric units aligns with best practices promoting high-value care.

articles.title: Same Class, Different Risk? Dapagliflozin versus Empagliflozin and Genitourinary Safety in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are guideline-directed therapy for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but comparative genitourinary safety data for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in HFpEF-treated populations remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare 6-month symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI), asymptomatic bacteriuria, and other genitourinary adverse events among patients newly initiated on dapagliflozin or empagliflozin for HFpEF.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-centre comparative cohort study included 239 adults with physician-documented HFpEF retained after a requirement for at least 6 months of continuous follow-up: 113 received dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily and 126 received empagliflozin 10 mg once daily. The original outcome of any documented bacteriuria/UTI was separated into symptomatic UTI and asymptomatic bacteriuria. Risk differences and 95% confidence intervals were calculated; a multivariable logistic model of the original documented bacteriuria/UTI composite adjusted for age, sex, and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

RESULTS: Any documented bacteriuria/UTI occurred in 21/113 (18.6%) dapagliflozin-treated participants and 25/126 (19.8%) empagliflozin-treated participants. Symptomatic UTI occurred in 4/113 (3.5%) and 5/126 (4.0%), respectively; 17/113 (15.0%) and 20/126 (15.9%) had documented asymptomatic bacteriuria. The risk difference for the composite, calculated as empagliflozin minus dapagliflozin, was 1.3 percentage points (95% CI -8.9 to 11.2). The adjusted odds ratio was 1.62 (95% CI 0.76-3.45; p = 0.208). Other genitourinary events were uncommon and estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically detectable between-group difference was found in symptomatic UTI, asymptomatic bacteriuria, or the original composite outcome. Confidence intervals were wide and compatible with clinically meaningful differences in either direction. These exploratory findings require confirmation in prospective multicentre studies with standardized culture ascertainment and complete follow-up.

articles.title: Technology use in youth with type 1 diabetes and language of care other than English.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Our primary aim was to describe continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and insulin pump use in youth with T1D with a preferred language of care other than English (LOE) and examine associations between diabetes technology use and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) in this population.

METHODS: We assessed baseline technology use for youth with LOE and T1D seen in diabetes clinics at a single center between February 2022 and February 2023. A two-sample t-test was used to compare HbA1c values between groups. A linear regression model was used to examine differences in HbA1c between the 3-level technology groups with Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons.

RESULTS: Ninety-four youth with T1D and LOE with complete data on technology use were included in analysis. At baseline 66 % were using diabetes technology with 42 (45 %) using CGM only, 1 (1 %) using insulin pump only, 19 (20 %) using both insulin pump and CGM, and 32 (34 %) not using any technology. HbA1c was significantly lower in the technology use group (Mean=9.1 %, SD=2.4) compared to the non-technology use group (Mean=10.5 %, SD=2.2) (p=0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite advances in technology for diabetes management, about one-third of youth with T1D and LOE were not using any diabetes technology. Diabetes technology use in this group was associated with lower HbA1c. Further work should be done to increase diabetes technology use in youth with T1D and LOE.

articles.title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess mimicking Bartter syndrome in infancy.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess (AME) syndrome is a rare monogenic disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the HSD11B2 gene encoding 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2). Deficient enzyme activity results in cortisol-mediated activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor, leading to low-renin hypertension. Because affected infants frequently present with polyuria and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, AME syndrome is often misdiagnosed as Bartter syndrome, resulting in significant diagnostic delay.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 13-month-old girl presented with polyuria, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypercalciuria, and failure to thrive and was initially managed as Bartter syndrome. During follow-up, persistent hypertension accompanied by markedly suppressed plasma renin activity and aldosterone levels prompted evaluation for monogenic hypertension. Urinary steroid analysis demonstrated a markedly reduced cortisone-to-cortisol ratio (0.02), consistent with 11β-HSD2 deficiency. Next-generation sequencing of the HSD11B2 gene identified a homozygous likely pathogenic splice-site variant, c.665-1G>A, confirming the diagnosis of AME syndrome. Treatment with spironolactone, amlodipine, potassium supplementation, and dietary salt restriction achieved blood pressure control and improved electrolyte abnormalities.

CONCLUSIONS: AME syndrome should be included in the differential diagnosis of infants presenting with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and polyuria, particularly when hypertension is detected. Systematic blood pressure assessment is essential in this clinical context, as early recognition of this monogenic disorder may prevent long-term cardiovascular and renal complications.

articles.title: Clinical detection and attribution of common disease in exposed populations.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Routine clinical assessment may misdiagnose or underdiagnose diseases such as chronic kidney disease (CKD), asthma, and pulmonary fibrosis when it fails to account for work and environmental exposure risks. Existing research addresses these diagnostic failures separately, and no published review organizes the diagnostic challenge by stages. In this study, we reviewed the evidence on exposure-informed assessment and developed a clinical framework that illustrates the stages of diagnostic loss.

CONTENT: Building on the principles of the HIV care cascade, we conducted a framework synthesis. We searched Europe PMC, web-based sources, grey literature, and major burden-estimation reports for literature published from January 2000 onward. All the identified studies were categorized into six stages, namely clinical detection; disease classification; etiological attribution; reporting or compensation; death registration; cause-of-death coding. These studies were also further subdivided based upon the type of evidence provided; whether they showed changes in individual patient diagnoses or were solely derived from population trends or associated clinical findings.

SUMMARY: Sixty-one sources contributed 64 findings. One study documented a change in individual diagnoses after systematic exposure assessment. At the population level, two studies found associations between exposure and increased prevalence of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Other studies described exposure-disease relationships including instances of gaps in screening and reporting, and limitations of gathering mortality records and accurately estimating disease burden. At the patient level, the evidence was sparse.

OUTLOOK: This synthesis is hypothesis-generating. Routine clinical assessment may miss or misattribute common diseases when exposure history is treated as peripheral, instead of as a major part of the initial risk model. The clinical framework developed in this study demonstrates instances in which exposure-informed care could alter detection, classification, attribution, and management. Further studies are needed to establish and fully integrate it into clinical care.

articles.title: Long-term Performance of Bilateral Internal Thoracic Artery Grafts in Young Adults.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Coronary artery disease (CAD) in young adults is uncommon but associated with substantial long-term morbidity. Limited evidence exists regarding the long-term outcomes of bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) grafting in this population. This study evaluates perioperative and long-term outcomes of BITA revascularization in young adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and compares survival outcomes with those of the general population.

METHODS: A retrospective single-center observational study was conducted in 67 young patients (39 ± 3 years) who underwent BITA grafting for multivessel CAD. Perioperative outcomes, long-term overall survival, major adverse cardio-cerebral events (MACEs), and repeat revascularization were assessed. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Further survival analysis was conducted using an age- and sex-adjusted general population matched for age, sex, and calendar year.

RESULTS: BITA grafting was associated with very low perioperative morbidity. The median follow-up was 17 years, with an estimated overall survival at 20 years of 74% (0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.52-0.87) and freedom from MACEs at 20 years of 70% (0.70, 95% CI: 0.49-0.84). Sternal wound complications were infrequent (1.5%).

CONCLUSION: BITA revascularization in young adults demonstrates excellent long-term survival, with survival comparable to that of the age- and sex-matched general population during the first 15 years after surgery, along with durable event-free outcomes, supporting its use as a durable revascularization strategy in this population.

articles.title: In brief: An expanded indication for Afrezza.
articles.journal: The Medical letter on drugs and therapeutics

articles.title: Cross-scanner validation and time-stability analysis of STARE, a blood-free quantification tool for brain imaging with irreversible PET tracers.
articles.abstract: Objective. 'Gold standard' blood-based quantification of dynamic18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) data has limited practical clinical applications due to cost and complexity of data collection and analysis. We previously presented a blood-free quantification alternative, STARE (source-to-target automatic rotating estimation), that was validated on18F-FDG data acquired on an ECAT EXACT HR+ scanner. Here, we extend that initial work by applying STARE to within-subject data acquired with both a Siemens Biograph mCT scanner and a portable Brain Biosciences CerePET scanner.Approach. Performance was assessed by comparing regional net influx rates (Ki) estimated using STARE and the standard blood-based Patlak approach. Twenty participants underwent 60 min brain18F-FDG scans, on two different days, once in each scanner. The time-stability of both STARE- and Patlak-basedKiestimates was evaluated by applying each method to the first 20 (STARE only), 30, 40, and 50 min of data.Main results. STARE demonstrated high correlation with PatlakKiestimates, particularly in the Biograph mCT (r= 0.82-0.93 (within-region)), with lower correlation in the CerePET (r= 0.27-0.62 (within-region)). In the Biograph dataset, STARE showed small deviations from the 60 min estimates across all evaluated durations (20 min and above), whereas deviations increased with shorter durations in CerePET data. The Patlak approach showed smaller changes across abbreviated scan durations in both datasets.Significance. STARE shows potential as a noninvasive alternative to traditional blood-based quantification of dynamic18F-FDG PET brain data, facilitating shorter, blood-free acquisition. This advancement could make dynamic18F-FDG PET brain imaging more accessible and comfortable for patients, potentially facilitating broader clinical adoption.

articles.title: Minimally invasive quantification of [18F]MC225 PET using constrained simultaneous estimation of the input function.
articles.abstract: Objective.[18F]MC225 is a PET radiotracer used to assess P-glycoprotein function at the blood-brain barrier. [18F]MC225 PET quantification requires arterial catheterization to obtain the plasma input function, an invasive procedure. The simultaneous estimation of the input function (SIME) has been proposed as a method for estimating the plasma input function, however, it requires at least one venous or arterial blood anchor. Long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET scanners enable a variation of the SIME algorithm, the constrained SIME (cSIME), that incorporates information from whole-blood activity, potentially eliminating the need for blood sampling. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of cSIME for quantifying [18F]MC225 in the brain using a clinical dataset.Approach.Dynamic data from seven subjects scanned on a LAFOV PET system following injection of [18F]MC225 were included. The cSIME method was used to estimate the plasma input function of each subject. A whole-blood input function extracted from the ascending aorta was used as the initial estimate, and multiple brain regions were simultaneously fitted to estimate the parameters required to convert the whole-blood input function into a plasma input function. Volume of distribution (VT) values were calculated using both the ground-truth and cSIME-estimated plasma input functions with a reversible two-tissue compartment model.Main results.Without a blood anchor,VTestimates using the cSIME plasma input function resulted in relative differences ranging between approximately -26% and 11% compared to theVTestimates obtained with the ground-truth plasma input function. Incorporating one blood anchor as anchor at 60 min reduced these relative differences up to 11%.Significance.The findings of this study suggest that cSIME may help reduce the invasiveness of quantitative [18F]MC225 PET studies. The clinical relevance of the observed bias will ultimately depend on its magnitude relative to disease-related differences in kinetic parameters expected in patient populations.

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days.

METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days.

RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days.

CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT05684796.

articles.title: A generalized phenomenological model of oxygen depletion for FLASH particle radiotherapy: evidence fromin vitrodata.
articles.abstract: Objective.Ultra-high dose rate (uHDR: FLASH) radiotherapy reduces normal tissue toxicity while preserving tumor control. The oxygen depletion hypothesis posits that rapid oxygen consumption during FLASH irradiation transiently reduces radiosensitivity. However, experimental measurements suggest oxygen depletion may be limited, particularly under normoxia. This study quantitatively assesses the adequacy of this hypothesis in reproducing experimentally observed sparing effects by comparing mechanistic simulations within vitrocell survival data across a wide range of irradiation conditions.Approach.We developed a phenomenological framework for radiolytic oxygen depletion incorporating temporal dose delivery, dose rate, and linear energy transfer (LET). LET dependence was included through oxygen consumption efficiency and the maximum oxygen enhancement ratio. For direct comparison, simulation results were linked to clonogenic cell survival using a damage reduction factor (DRF) derived from the linear-quadratic model. Simulated DRFs were compared with experimental DRFs from six independentin vitrostudies involving electrons, protons, helium ions, and carbon ions over broad ranges of LET, oxygenation, and dose rates using parity plots, residual analyses, stratified weighted statistics, and correlation analyses.Main results.Under most irradiation conditions, simulated DRFs remained close to unity (minimum values approximately 0.96), indicating limited predicted protection from oxygen depletion. Conversely, experimental DRFs exhibited substantially larger deviations. Stratified analyses revealed systematic discrepancies between simulated and experimental DRFs across oxygenation, LET, and dose rate, with pronounced disagreement under normoxia, high LET, and uHDRs. Residual analyses demonstrated underestimation of the sparing effect by the model. Correlation analyses showed statistically insignificant associations between simulated and experimental metrics.Significance.The oxygen depletion model considered in this work insufficiently reproduces the observed sparing effect under thein vitroconditions considered. Additional biological and physicochemical mechanisms likely play a significant role. This framework provides a quantitative basis for evaluating alternative mechanisms and integrating future experimental data toward a more complete understanding of FLASH radiotherapy.

articles.title: Nonparametric prioritization of breath VOC signatures for differential diagnosis of asthma, bronchiectasis, and COPD.
articles.abstract: Accurate differentiation among asthma, bronchiectasis, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease remains a major clinical challenge due to overlapping symptoms and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches. This study proposes a nonparametric cumulative distribution function (CDF)-based framework combined with permutation testing to analyze volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath as non-invasive biomarkers for respiratory disease characterization. Breathomics data obtained via gas chromatography-MS from 121 patients were analyzed following log2transformation of VOC intensities. The analytical scope included not only shared VOCs but also pair-specific and disease-exclusive compounds. The discriminative ability of each VOC was assessed by comparing class-specific empirical cumulative distributions with null distributions generated through 10 000 random permutations. Permutation-based CDF rankings were generated for core and pairwise VOCs, whereas disease-exclusive VOCs were characterized descriptively using within-group medians and interquartile ranges. To evaluate classification utility, progressively reduced VOC subsets were assessed using Random Forest (RF) and Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) under repeated stratified cross-validation. Results showed that a reduced set of highly ranked VOCs preserved substantial classification performance, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed prioritization strategy. Candidate VOCs were then suggested based not only on their ranking scores, but also on biological interpretation and support from previously reported literature. Overall, the CDF and permutation-based approach provide an interpretable and model-independent framework for biomarker discovery in respiratory diseases.

articles.title: Redefining Photosensitizers Functionality Through Consensus-Assisted Integration of Orthogonal Antibacterial Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Photodynamic antimicrobial therapy (PDAT) offers a promising bactericidal strategy via light-triggered reactive oxygen species (ROS), yet conventional photosensitizers (PSs) typically lack sustained inhibitory activity. Herein, we attempt to redefine the functionality of PSs through a consensus-assisted design strategy that integrates deep learning and molecular docking to embed orthogonal antibacterial mechanisms into a single PS molecule. Specifically, a near-infrared hemi-cyanine PS IHcy-OH is found to unite PDAT with interference of filamentous temperature-sensitive mutant Z (FtsZ) protein, which is essential for bacterial division. By conjugating IHcy-OH with a responsive arm, IHcy-PbE is rationally designed and synthesized to achieve infection responsiveness, rapid light-controlled bactericidal activity, and long-time bacterial inhibition. While such integration typically requires complex multi-component platforms, this strategy successfully unlocks the multifunctional potential of a single PS molecule. Consistent with its design, IHcy-PbE could inhibit methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) in the dark and exert robust PDAT efficacy upon exposure to hydrogen peroxide and light. This work helps to transform PSs from ROS-dependent killing agents into therapeutics with orthogonal antibacterial mechanisms, establishing a proof-of-concept for a generalizable PSs design paradigm.

articles.title: Fetal cardiac function before labor predicts adverse perinatal outcome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Current antepartum surveillance based on fetal biometry and cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) has limited ability to identify fetuses at risk of intrapartum compromise, as adverse outcomes may occur despite normal growth and Doppler findings. This study evaluated whether quantitative fetal cardiac geometry and myocardial deformation assessed before induction of labor can identify high-risk fetuses with normal CPR at increased risk of adverse perinatal outcome.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 53 singleton high-risk pregnancies undergoing medically indicated induction of labor were included. All fetuses had normal admission cardiotocography and CPR. Before induction, fetal cardiac function was assessed using FetalHQ software from a subcostal four-chamber-view cine loop. Measurements included four-chamber-view circumference, global sphericity index, global longitudinal strain (GLS), and left- and right-ventricular free wall strain. The primary outcome was a composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO), including abnormal intrapartum cardiotocography requiring cesarean delivery, umbilical artery pH<7.10, base excess >10 mmol/L, or neonatal intensive care unit admission.

RESULTS: CAPO occurred in 13/53 pregnancies (24.5 %). Compared with unaffected fetuses, those with CAPO showed reduced four-chamber-view circumference (100.4 [98.8-105.4] vs. 120.3 [110.8-133.0]; p=0.049), lower global sphericity index (1.15 [0.88-1.24] vs. 1.34 [1.24-1.37]; p=0.014), impaired GLS (p=0.001), and reduced left ventricular free wall strain (p=0.001). Right ventricular free wall strain showed a similar trend (p=0.085).

CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative fetal cardiac assessment identifies high-risk fetuses with normal CPR who subsequently develop adverse perinatal outcomes. Fetal cardiac geometry and myocardial deformation may provide additional information on cardiovascular reserve and improve pre-induction risk stratification.

articles.title: Subcutaneous insulin treatment for mild pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis: an evaluation of treatment duration and length of stay.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although intravenous (IV) insulin remains the standard treatment for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), subcutaneous (SC) insulin has been suggested as an alternative for uncomplicated DKA. We compared treatment duration, hospital length of stay (LOS) and adverse events in children with mild DKA treated with a SC insulin protocol to those of children treated with an IV insulin protocol.

METHODS: We reviewed medical records of children with mild DKA admitted to a children's hospital before and after introduction of a SC insulin protocol. Children treated with the SC protocol received daily basal insulin along with rapid-acting insulin every 4 h. We compared outcomes for children treated with SC insulin to those of children treated with IV insulin.

RESULTS: Twenty two children were treated with SC insulin and 29 with IV insulin. In the SC group vs. the IV group, mean protocol duration (17.1 ± 8.6 vs. 13.5 ± 4.6 h) and LOS (34.9 ± 16.7 vs. 37.8 ± 23.6 h) were not significantly different (p=0.07 and p=0.63, respectively). There were no significant differences in adverse events frequency between groups. No child treated with SC insulin required a change to IV insulin treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment of children with uncomplicated mild DKA with SC insulin is safe and effective without prolonging LOS.

articles.title: Menstrual cycle-related variations in insulin requirements and glycemic control during automated insulin delivery in adolescents with type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data on menstrual cycle-related metabolic variability in adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D) using automated insulin delivery (AID) systems are scarce. We aimed to quantify cycle-dependent differences in insulin requirements and glycemic outcomes in this population.

METHODS: In this retrospective observational cohort study, adolescents with T1D aged 12.0-17.9 years who were at least 1 year postmenarche and had used AID for ≥6 months were included. Menstrual cycles were tracked using smartphone applications, and nine complete cycles per participant were analyzed. Insulin delivery and continuous glucose monitoring data were extracted from Glooko. Outcomes included total daily insulin dose (TDD), time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), mean glucose, glucose coefficient of variation (CV), and recorded carbohydrate intake. Linear mixed-effects models were used.

RESULTS: Fifty-one adolescents contributed 459 menstrual cycles. Mean age was 14.7 ± 1.8 years, and median HbA1c was 7.2 % (interquartile range 6.8-7.5 %). TDD was higher during the luteal than the follicular phase (1.05 vs. 0.95 U/kg/day; mean difference +0.10 U/kg/day, 95 % CI 0.05-0.15; p<0.001). The luteal phase was associated with reduced TIR (-6.3 %, p=0.001), increased TAR (+5.5 %, p=0.01), higher mean glucose (+12.5 mg/dL, p=0.03), and higher CV (39.4 vs. 35.0 %, p=0.03). TBR and carbohydrate intake did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: In adolescents with T1D who menstruate and use AID systems, insulin requirements and glycemic control vary across the menstrual cycle, with increased insulin demand and hyperglycemia during the luteal phase. These findings highlight clinically relevant cycle-related metabolic variability despite the use of AID.

articles.title: Ultrasound-based prediction of fetal hyperinsulinemia: development of a fetal metabolic score.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with fetal hyperinsulinemia, excessive adiposity, and adverse perinatal outcomes; sonographic markers of fetal adiposity, liver enlargement, and septal thickening may allow direct assessment of fetal metabolic adaptation. This study aimed to develop an ultrasound-based fetal metabolic score (FMS) estimating the risk of fetal hyperinsulinemia.

METHODS: The FMS was developed from a prospective cohort of 223 pregnant women (128 with GDM, 95 controls). Sonographic markers of neonatal hyperinsulinemia were identified using umbilical cord C-peptide above the 75th percentile as the reference outcome: thigh soft tissue thickness, abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness, fetal liver length, and interventricular septal thickness. Odds ratios from logistic regression were converted into weighted integer coefficients, and continuous measurements were categorized by gestational age-adjusted percentiles into a composite score.

RESULTS: Fetuses of GDM mothers showed significantly greater abdominal adiposity, liver length, and interventricular septal thickness than controls. Thigh soft tissue thickness (OR 1.62; 95 % CI 1.25-2.09; p<0.001), abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness (OR 1.57; 95 % CI 1.23-1.99; p<0.001), fetal liver length (OR 1.06; 95 % CI 1.02-1.11; p=0.004), and interventricular septal thickness (OR 1.35; 95 % CI 1.01-1.82; p=0.040) independently predicted elevated cord blood C-peptide. The FMS ranged from 0 to 44 points, integrating weighted contributions from adiposity, visceral growth, and cardiac remodeling markers.

CONCLUSIONS: The FMS is a novel ultrasound-based approach for estimating fetal hyperinsulinemia risk. By integrating multiple manifestations of the fetal metabolic response to maternal hyperglycemia, it may assess fetal metabolic health more comprehensively than conventional biometry alone.

articles.title: Multidimensional compliance and outcomes in gestational diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between a composite multidimensional compliance score and glycemic control, maternal complications, and neonatal outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to evaluate these associations after adjusting for potential confounders.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 360 women with GDM, diagnosed between October 2023 and January 2026 at Guiyang Second People's Hospital. A weighted compliance score (1-3) was calculated based on blood glucose monitoring, diet, physical activity, prenatal visits, and medication adherence. Participants were grouped by compliance: high, moderate, and low. Multivariate logistic regression adjusted for age, BMI, insulin use, and mobile health app use, with multiple comparisons corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg method.

RESULTS: Most baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable across compliance groups, though insulin therapy use,and mobile health application utilization differed significantly. Glycemic target achievement differed markedly: 76.23 % in the high-compliance group vs. 22.46 % in moderate and 2.00 % in low compliance. Third-trimester HbA1c was significantly lower in the high-compliance group (5.45 % ± 0.30 %) compared with moderate (5.75 % ± 0.34 %) and low (6.04 % ± 0.46 %) group. In multivariate logistic regression, low compliance was independently associated with increased odds of macrosomia, large-for-gestational-age, preterm birth, and neonatal intensive care unit admission compared with high compliance (all p<0.01). Gestational weight gain was inversely associated with compliance level.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher compliance with multiple GDM management strategies was associated with better blood sugar control and fewer maternal and neonatal complications, highlighting the value of comprehensive, integrated care.

articles.title: Ready for transition, but ready for outcomes? Discordance between transition readiness and metabolic control in adolescents with type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transition from pediatric to adult care is a critical period for adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). This study aimed to evaluate transition readiness and its association with glycemic outcomes, and to analyze factors affecting readiness in adolescents with T1DM.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 75 adolescents with T1DM aged 17-21 years. Transition readiness was assessed using a diabetes-adapted 23-item questionnaire based on the Transition Readiness Assessment Questionnaire (TRAQ). Clinical and demographic data were collected retrospectively. Associations between transition readiness scores and HbA1c levels, categorized using two clinically relevant thresholds, as well as demographic and clinical variables, were analyzed.

RESULTS: The mean transition readiness score was 83.91 ± 14.46. Higher scores were observed in communication and self-management domains, whereas lower scores were noted in healthcare navigation and transition-specific readiness. Transition readiness scores were not associated with HbA1c levels across different classifications. Diabetes duration was positively correlated with readiness scores (r=0.311, p=0.007), while no significant association was found with age or gender. Technology use (continuous glucose monitoring and insulin pump) was not associated with transition readiness.

CONCLUSIONS: Transition readiness in adolescents with T1DM appears to be a multidimensional construct that is not directly reflected by glycemic control. This discrepancy between perceived readiness and clinical outcomes suggests that transition assessments should extend beyond subjective measures and incorporate broader functional domains, including healthcare navigation and real-life independence.

articles.title: Midwives' perspectives on risk classification in the German maternity record (Mutterpass): an exploratory survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Risk stratification in pregnancy based on Catalogue A in the German maternity record (Mutterpass) represents an established component of antenatal care. The aim of the study is to explore the perspectives and opinions of German midwives on the current risk classification during pregnancy.

METHODS: Between May and July 2025, midwives across Germany were surveyed using the online REDCap platform regarding their opinions on the current risk classification in pregnancy. As part of the FeMaR (Fetomaternal Risk Score) project, this exploratory survey among healthcare professionals was conducted prior to the development of a future pregnancy risk stratification model. Participation was anonymous and voluntary, with one response permitted per device. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Data from 220 midwives were included in the analysis. More than half of respondents reported that the current risk classification is largely subjective and lacks specificity. Suggested approaches for further development included weighting individual risk factors, re-evaluating risk over the course of pregnancy, and enabling a more differentiated assessment of individual risk constellations. Midwives additionally emphasized the relevance of social determinants of health, experiences of violence, physical activity, and dietary habits in the context of pregnancy risk stratification.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support existing evidence that pregnancy- and birth-related risks vary substantially depending on individual risk factors and may change over the course of pregnancy. From the midwives' perspectives, there appears to be a need for more differentiated and dynamically adaptable approaches to pregnancy risk stratification in future clinical care.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes after prophylactic and ultrasound-indicated emergency cervical cerclage.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes after prophylactic and ultrasound-indicated emergency cervical cerclage.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all the women who underwent McDonald cervical cerclage at a tertiary medical center during 2010-2024 and delivered at ≥23 weeks. Women were categorized according to the clinical timing and urgency of cerclage placement: prophylactic cerclage, placed electively based on obstetric history before cervical change was detected; and ultrasound-indicated emergency cerclage, performed for ultrasound-detected cervical shortening in the absence of contractions, bleeding, ruptured membranes, or physical examination-detected cervical dilation.

RESULTS: Cerclage was performed earlier in the prophylactic (n=127) than the emergency (n=52) group (14.1 ± 1.2 vs. 18.4 ± 3.2 weeks, p<0.001). Significant differences were not observed between the groups in the mean gestational age at cerclage removal (37.1 ± 3.4 vs. 37.2 ± 3.4 weeks, p=0.614) or the mean gestational age at delivery (38.0 ± 3.2 vs. 37.0 ± 3.6 weeks, p=0.885). Nor did the proportions differ significantly of spontaneous preterm birth <37 weeks (18.1 vs. 19.2 %, p=1.00) or <32 weeks (7.1 vs. 5.8 %, p=1.000). Neonatal outcomes, including birthweight, admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, respiratory complications, and neonatal mortality, were comparable. Multivariable analysis confirmed that cerclage, whether prophylactic or emergency, was not independently associated with spontaneous preterm birth <37 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Emergency cerclage was not associated with worse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared with prophylactic cerclage in this cohort, suggesting that, in selected patients, it may be a reasonable management approach.

articles.title: Higher prevalence of islet-related autoantibody positivity in obese Chinese children and adolescents.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The prevalence of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has increased along with rising incidence of childhood obesity. This study aims to investigate the prevalence of islet-related autoantibodies among obese children in China.

METHODS: The study enrolled patients with moderate to severe obesity aged under 18 years who were admitted between 1 January 2019 and 30 April 2024. Glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody, insulin autoantibody, islet cell autoantibody, zinc transporter 8 autoantibody, and insulinoma-associated protein 2 autoantibody, were measured through chemiluminescent immunoassay. A comparative analysis was conducted of the indicators for glycemic metabolism among the three subgroups, defined according to their autoantibody status.

RESULTS: Among the 1,826 obese children included, 10.9 % were positive for at least one autoantibody, significantly higher than the normal-weight population (1.86 %, p<0.001). Positive results for two autoantibodies were observed in 1.9 % of obese children, statistically higher than in the general population (0.39 %, p<0.01). The HbA1c level of the two antibody positive groups was statistically higher than that of the antibody negative group (5.8 % vs. 5.6 %, p=0.012). No statistical difference was observed among the three groups regarding anthropometric indicators, biochemical parameters and indicators of glucose metabolism.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of islet-related autoantibodies is higher in obese children, which may contribute to an increasing susceptibility to T1DM. The study underscores the necessity for screening in obese children, as this may facilitate early intervention for T1DM.

articles.title: Multi-marker inflammatory risk assessment after acute coronary syndrome.
Association between thyroid peroxidase antibody positivity and the risk of perinatal depression: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Perinatal depression (PND) impacts a substantial subset of females globally and confers significant risk to maternal-infant health and offspring development, but current evidence on the association between thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) positivity and the risk of PND is uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the association between TPOAb positivity and the risk of PND.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and PsycINFO from their inception to March 1, 2025. Cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies evaluating the association between TPOAb positivity and the risk of PND were included. This meta-analysis was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 checklist. The risk of bias in the included studies was assessed by the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Data synthesis was performed using random-effects model and fixed-effects model.

RESULTS: After screening, 11 studies with 10,559 patients were eligible. The pooled relative risk (RR) indicated that females positive for TPOAb exhibited a significantly higher risk to develop PND (RR=1.52, 95 %CI [1.16-1.99], p<0.05). A moderate degree of heterogeneity was presented among the included studies (I2=52 %).

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis demonstrated that perinatal TPOAb positivity is associated with an increased risk of PND. However, given the moderate heterogeneity and the limited number of included studies, future well-designed prospective studies assessing TPOAb positivity at specific time points during pregnancy are warranted to improve the quality of evidence.

articles.title: Microbiological profile and clinical correlates of post-cesarean surgical site infections.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the microbiological profile of post-cesarean surgical site infection (SSI) wound cultures, examine associations between specific pathogens and clinical or surgical characteristics, and delineate institutional wound culture collection practices.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study including women with positive wound cultures from clinically diagnosed post-cesarean SSIs between 2012 and 2024. Microorganisms were categorized into designated pathogen groups based on taxonomic classification and clinical relevance. Each microorganism group was compared with all remaining cases. Demographic, obstetric, surgical, laboratory, and outcome variables were analyzed using appropriate univariate statistical tests.

RESULTS: A total of 207 positive wound cultures were analyzed. The most frequently isolated organisms were Enterobacterales (30.4 %), Staphylococcus aureus and β-hemolytic streptococci (27.1 %), and coagulase-negative staphylococci (20.3 %). Enterobacterales infections were significantly associated with obesity (BMI >35), meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and longer intervals from rupture of membranes to labor onset. Non-fermenting Gram-negative organisms were strongly associated with subcutaneous tissue approximation and intradermal skin closure. Coagulase-negative staphylococci were associated with fewer established risk factors, suggesting possible contamination or colonization. Only Enterobacterales infections demonstrated a statistically significant, though clinically modest, increase in peak white blood cell count. No significant differences were observed in other severity markers or clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Routine wound cultures in post-cesarean SSIs provide limited information regarding disease severity. However, specific pathogen profiles are associated with distinct obstetric and surgical characteristics, suggesting that selective culture use may be informative in high-risk clinical contexts. These findings may help improve institutional wound-culture practices and inform future studies on culture-guided management strategies.

articles.title: Basal plate remodeling in vascular-metabolic pregnancy disorders.
articles.abstract:
