A total of 312 organizations with active websites meeting the eligibility criteria across countries were identified, and their websites reviewed. Content relevant to young dementia carers was identified in 28% (n = 86) of the websites, with uneven availability of resources across Europe and very limited resources in some countries. Most contents addressed five categories: Diagnosis & symptoms, Uncertainty & family distress, Changes in roles, Stigma & isolation and Identifying need for support. A lack of tailored resources to support young dementia carers was identified, particularly in relation to two categories: Grief & loss and Education & life planning. Only a minority of websites included young dementia carer-specific content. These websites primarily focused on general support needs and explanations of dementia, while key areas such as guidance on school, career, and life planning remain underdeveloped. There is a need for greater recognition of young dementia carers, clearer terminology, and more developmentally appropriate and practically oriented resources to strengthen online support for these carers across Europe.

articles.title: A systematic review of deforestation outcomes in potential other effective area-based conservation measures across Latin America.
articles.journal: Conservation biology : the journal of the Society for Conservation Biology
articles.abstract: Recognizing conservation contributions from areas outside protected areas (PAs), including other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), is increasingly central to meeting global biodiversity targets. However, little is known about which areas could qualify as OECMs and whether they support forest conservation. Focusing on Latin America, we conducted a systematic literature review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines synthesizing 93 peer-reviewed studies published through 2024 that assess the effectiveness of OECMs outside formal PA systems in reducing deforestation. First, we identified and classified area-based measures that may qualify as potential OECMs into six types based on their conservation objectives and characteristics: strict biodiversity conservation areas, set-aside areas for ecosystem services, Indigenous peoples' territories, local communities' territories, other managed sustainable-use areas, and ancillary conservation areas. Second, we synthesized the available evidence on their effectiveness in reducing deforestation. Indigenous people's territories were the most frequently evaluated, whereas strict biodiversity conservation areas have received relatively little attention. Methodologically, most evidence relied on nonexperimental comparisons of forest-cover trends; quasi-experimental designs were less common but provide stronger causal inference of conservation effectiveness. Disaggregating outcomes by comparator type revealed important patterns: Indigenous territories most consistently showed reduced deforestation relative to both PAs and non-PAs, whereas local communities' territories showed more favorable outcomes relative to non-PAs than to PAs. Set-aside areas for ecosystem services showed predominantly negative outcomes, largely reflecting weak enforcement. Despite this evidence base, very few of these areas have been formally recognized as OECMs, highlighting a disconnect between available research and reporting under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Bridging this gap will require stronger causal evidence, broader geographic coverage, and inclusive recognition processes that account for the governance rights of those who manage these territories.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles improve islet β-cell metabolic function via miRNA-mediated regulation of Ankyrin-B expression.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Mesenchymal stromal-cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) improve islet function, which may be mediated in part through the delivery of microRNAs (miRNAs) to β-cells. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we identified the most abundant MSC-EV miRNAs, their relative transfer to β-cells and the extent to which Ankyrin-B (Ank2) may represent a downstream target mediating the beneficial effects of EVs on islet function.

METHODS: Mouse islets were treated with MSC-EVs, and changes in islet miRNAs were assessed using small RNAseq. miR-21a-5p showed the highest content, and subsequent bioinformatic analysis identified Ank2 as one of its predicted target genes. Expression levels of Ank2 mRNA were assessed by bulkRNA sequencing, while Ank2 protein was quantified by immunoblotting. Knockdown of Ank2 by siRNA was used to evaluate its role in islet function. Cell viability was measured using live/dead staining, oxygen consumption was quantified with a Seahorse analyser, and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion was determined by radioimmunoassay.

RESULTS: MSC-EV treatment of islets was associated with elevated β-cell miR-21a-5p mRNA levels. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses identified Ank2 as a predicted downstream target of miR-21a-5p. Treatment of mouse islets with MSC-EVs was associated with increased Ank2 mRNA and protein expression, which was accompanied by improved β-cell metabolic function and enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Ank2 knockdown caused a significant reduction in β-cell ATP-coupled respiration.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify a novel miRNA-mediated mechanism underlying the beneficial effects of MSC-EVs on islet function and support the development of MSC-EV-based cell-free strategies to enhance islet function for diabetes therapies.

articles.title: Periodontitis and systemic disease: A clinical perspective.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a common chronic inflammatory disease that has traditionally been considered primarily within the domain of dentistry. Increasing evidence, however, associates periodontitis with systemic inflammatory conditions, particularly atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Dysbiotic subgingival microbial communities, disruption of the periodontal epithelial barrier, transient bacteremia, microbial products, and locally generated inflammatory mediators provide biologically plausible pathways through which periodontal inflammation may influence systemic vascular biology. Epidemiologic and mechanistic studies support an association between periodontitis and cardiovascular disease, although direct causality has not been established. Importantly, periodontal treatment has been associated with improvement in endothelial function and reductions in selected systemic inflammatory biomarkers, but evidence that treatment prevents myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular mortality remains insufficient. For the practicing internist, the principal message is therefore both practical and appropriately cautious: Periodontal health should be recognized as one component of overall health, and closer collaboration between physicians and dental professionals may strengthen preventive care. This Perspective reviews the clinical evidence linking periodontitis with systemic disease, using cardiovascular disease as the principal example, and considers its implications for prevention, interdisciplinary care, and future research.

articles.title: Preoperative Muscle Mass and 1-Year Diabetes Remission After Metabolic Surgery: Associations Across Remission Definitions.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate 1-year T2DM remission and preoperative factors associated with remission across different outcome definitions following metabolic surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with T2DM and a preoperative BMI ≥ 27.5 kg/m2 who underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy. The primary outcome was consensus-defined diabetes remission at the assessment closest to 12 months, defined as HbA1c < 6.5% measured ≥ 3 months after discontinuation of all glucose-lowering medications. Secondary outcomes were stringent biochemical normoglycaemia and remission at all three postoperative assessments.

RESULTS: Among 70 patients, 56 (80.0%) achieved consensus-defined remission and 24 (34.3%) achieved stringent biochemical normoglycaemia at 1 year. Shorter diabetes duration was independently associated with consensus-defined remission (adjusted OR [aOR], 0.24; 95% CI: 0.06-0.65), whereas absolute total muscle mass (TMM) was not (aOR, 1.24; 95% CI: 0.54-2.97). For stringent biochemical normoglycaemia, shorter diabetes duration, higher fasting C-peptide and greater absolute TMM were independently associated with the outcome. Residualized muscle mass (RMM) was also associated with this outcome in exploratory sensitivity analyses. Adding muscle measures to the ABCD and IMS scores improved cross-validated discrimination for this stringent outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative muscle mass was not associated with consensus-defined diabetes remission but was associated with stringent biochemical normoglycaemia after metabolic surgery. Adding either absolute TMM or RMM to established remission scores improved cross-validated discrimination for this stringent outcome; however, these findings remain exploratory and require external validation.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric Outcomes Associated With GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use in Medicare Beneficiaries With Type 2 Diabetes: Variation by Treatment Pattern and Obesity Status.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors are expressed in brain regions governing mood, reward and stress, yet the neuropsychiatric effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) therapy remain poorly characterized. We estimated associations between GLP-1 RA use and neuropsychiatric disorders and variation by obesity status and treatment pattern.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This population-based cohort study used claims data from Medicare enrolees with Type 2 diabetes mellitus. GLP-1 RAs were compared with other second-line glucose-lowering medications and evaluated across four treatment patterns: monotherapy, switch, escalation and augmentation. Eight neuropsychiatric outcomes were examined using 1:1 propensity score-matched, covariate-adjusted stratified Cox regression with time-varying covariates.

RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with a small increase in aggregate psychiatric disorder risk (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 1.04; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.03-1.06; 1.7 excess events/1000 person-years), of uncertain clinical significance given the large cohort size. Risk was elevated for depression (HR = 1.11; 3.0 excess events/1000 person-years) but reduced for substance use disorders (HR = 0.84; 4.1 fewer events/1000 person-years), dementia (HR = 0.87; 2.8 fewer) and suicidal/self-harm (HR = 0.81; 0.4 fewer events/1000 person-years). Associations varied by treatment pattern: monotherapy showed elevated psychiatric (HR = 1.43) and elevated emotional symptom (HR = 1.32) risks; escalation also exhibited elevated psychiatric risk, whereas switch and augmentation demonstrated reduced or null risks.

CONCLUSIONS: Rather than a uniform class effect, the neuropsychiatric profile of GLP-1 RA appears context-dependent, differing by treatment pattern, obesity status and outcome examined. Elevated risk with monotherapy or escalation may reflect baseline clinical differences rather than pharmacological effect. Reduced risks of substance use disorders, dementia and suicidal/self-harm are reassuring.

articles.title: A Practical Treatment Platform Version 3.0 for Using Angiotensin Receptor Blocker-Based Single-Pill Combinations in Patients With Hypertension.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Elevated blood pressure (BP) is the leading cause of cardiovascular disease and a major contributor to mortality, affecting almost one third of the adult population worldwide. Despite strong scientific evidence, guidelines and multiple therapeutic options, many patients remain undertreated or uncontrolled, largely due to poor medication adherence and medical inertia. Complexity of multi-pill regimens contributes significantly to non-adherence, whereas single-pill combinations (SPCs) improve adherence and persistence, accelerate BP control, and promote better long-term outcomes than multiple combinations. Appropriate selection of SPC in individual hypertensive patients may be a difficult though very important task for physicians. Thus, development of tools that may facilitate use of SPC in clinical practice is desirable. Among renin-angiotensin system blockers, olmesartan (OM) has demonstrated sustained efficacy, favourable tolerability, both as monotherapy and in SPCs with amlodipine and/or hydrochlorothiazide, which are available in multiple dosages. The present OM-based platform builds on earlier frameworks and incorporates guidelines' updates complemented by a systematic review of available literature. This "3.0" proposal expands patient categorization to include comorbidities or complications often overlooked in clinical practice guidelines, providing a practical, evidence-based approach to support individualized hypertension management complementing guideline recommendations.

articles.title: Quantitative Sciences in the Model-Informed Era: From Parallel Functions to a Shared Decision System.
articles.abstract: Model-informed drug development increasingly depends on collaboration among clinical pharmacology, statistics, pharmacometrics, and quantitative systems pharmacology. Yet functional silos, distinct leadership structures, and divergent goals can reduce collaboration to late, parallel deliverables that constrain decision architecture. This Perspective defines a shared decision system as an operating model in which quantitative and clinical disciplines jointly define the question, context of use, evidentiary role, uncertainty standards, and accountability for model-informed evidence.

articles.title: The Pesticide Pyrethroid Metabolite 3-Phenoxybenzoic Acid (3-PBA) Impairs Human Cardiac Nav1.5 and Action Potential Depolarization.
articles.abstract: Pyrethroid insecticides (PYRs) are widely used worldwide, and their primary metabolite, 3-phenoxybenzoic acid (3-PBA), serves as a near-ubiquitous biomarker of human exposure to PYRs. While epidemiological data consistently link urinary 3-PBA to increased cardiometabolic risk and coronary heart disease, the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms of its direct potential cardiotoxicity remain unexplored. Parent PYRs are known to exert cardiotoxic effects by enhancing the late sodium current (INa-L) and inducing arrhythmia, but the direct effect of 3-PBA on heart excitability has not been previously investigated. This study demonstrates that 3-PBA interacts with human cardiac Nav1.5 expressed in Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK293) cells, and significantly increases INa-L in a concentration-dependent manner with an EC50 of 51.3 ± 5.1 µM. The metabolite does not alter the voltage dependence of activation and inactivation, but it significantly delays the recovery from inactivation of the peak sodium current. In human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (CM-hiPSCs) and adult rat ventricular myocytes, 3-PBA reduced maximal depolarization rate (dV/dt), indicating impaired depolarization dynamics and reduced peak sodium current. At the organ level, acute exposure in isolated rat hearts did not significantly alter standard ECG parameters. Collectively, these findings suggest that 3-PBA is not electrophysiologically inert but directly modulates cardiac sodium channel function, although at supraphysiological concentration. This provides new evidence of the biological activity of 3-PBA and suggests that its cardiotoxic potential may become clinically relevant under conditions of high dose and chronic exposure or in susceptible populations.

articles.title: Improving Haemorrhage Prediction in General Ward Patients by Incorporating Patterns of Change Derived From Routine Ward Measurements.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate whether patterns of change derived from routine ward measurements provide additional predictive value beyond the most recent clinical measurements for haemorrhage prediction in general ward patients.

DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Among 16,197 adult patients admitted to general wards in three university-affiliated hospitals in South Korea, 1152 (7.1%) experienced haemorrhage, whereas 15,045 (92.9%) did not. Three machine-learning algorithms evaluated three feature sets based on the most recent clinical measurements, patterns of change or both. Models were trained and internally validated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. Predictive performance was compared across feature sets using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity and F1-score. Shapley Additive Explanations were used to interpret the best-performing model.

RESULTS: Models using both recent measurements and patterns of change showed small but statistically supported improvements in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve compared with models using recent measurements alone. Shapley Additive Explanations identified neutrophil count, platelet count, white blood cell count, urine output and vital signs as key predictors.

CONCLUSION: Patterns of change derived from routine ward measurements provided complementary predictive information for haemorrhage prediction in general ward patients beyond the most recent clinical measurements. Routinely collected ward data may therefore contain additional predictive information not captured by the most recent values alone.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Machine-learning models combining recent clinical measurements with patterns of change may support risk stratification in general ward patients; prospective evaluation is needed to determine their clinical utility.

IMPACT: The study examined whether patterns of change improve haemorrhage prediction. These findings suggest that routinely collected ward data may provide additional predictive information beyond the most recent clinical measurements. The potential value of this information for nursing surveillance and timely intervention warrants prospective evaluation.

REPORTING METHOD: Transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis-artificial intelligence (TRIPOD + AI).

articles.title: Evaluating the Impacts of Inflammatory Proteins on the Risk of Alzheimer's Disease.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that inflammation contributes to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the relationship between circulating inflammatory proteins and AD remains incompletely understood. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess the associations of 91 circulating inflammatory proteins with AD. The discovery stage protein GWAS included 14,824 participants, and the validation stage analysis used UK Biobank data from 54,219 participants. The AD dataset comprised 85,934 cases and 401,577 controls. The inverse variance weighted (IVW) method was the primary approach, complemented by weighted median, MR-Egger, heterogeneity, and pleiotropy analyses. MR estimates from both stages were subsequently combined by meta-analysis, followed by drug-gene interaction analyses. In the discovery stage, four proteins showed nominal associations with AD: AXIN1 (OR = 1.082, P = 0.026), NGF (OR = 1.061, P = 0.048), CXCL11 (OR = 0.952, P = 0.017), and TNFRSF9 (OR = 0.946, P = 0.048). However, none survived FDR correction (FDR = 0.799). In the validation stage, only TNFRSF9 reached nominal significance (OR = 0.870, P = 0.031), which did not survive FDR correction (FDR = 0.125); AXIN1 showed an opposite direction. Meta-analysis provided suggestive pooled estimates for CXCL11 (OR = 0.956, P = 9.34 × 10⁻3), TNFRSF9 (OR = 0.926, P = 0.034), and NGF (OR = 1.061, P = 0.034), but these should not be regarded as independent confirmation. DGIdb analysis identified interactions between the genes of interest and various drugs or compounds. These findings provide exploratory genetic evidence linking circulating inflammatory proteins to AD, but robust replication was not established after multiple testing correction and requires further validation.

articles.title: A Malaysian Expert Consensus on The Identification, Evaluation, and Pharmacological Management of Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy (DSPN), the most common form of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), is a chronic complication of diabetes associated with sensory loss, foot ulceration, lower-limb amputation, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality. Despite its substantial clinical burden, DSPN remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in Malaysia. This consensus aimed to develop practical, evidence-informed recommendations for screening, diagnosis, and management of painful and non-painful presentations of DSPN tailored to the Malaysian healthcare setting.

METHODS: An expert panel comprising 11 endocrinologists from public and private healthcare institutions in Malaysia was convened. Draft recommendations were adapted from international and local guidelines for Malaysian clinical practice. Consensus development involved pre-meeting review and anonymous voting, followed by structured face-to-face discussion. Consensus was defined as ≥80% agreement.

RESULTS: The panel finalized 61 consensus statements covering screening, diagnosis, sensory examination, and treatment. Recommendations emphasize annual screening for all individuals with diabetes and clinical examination to detect sensory deficits, including in individuals without painful symptoms. Assessment should include multiple bedside tests to evaluate small- and large-fiber function and loss of protective sensation. Recommended tests include the 10-g monofilament, vibration and pin-prick testing, and the Ipswich Touch Test, particularly in resource-limited settings. Assessment of painful and non-painful symptoms should complement rather than replace objective examination. Validated screening questionnaires, including the Malay-language PainDETECT may support assessment. Management includes optimization of glycemic control, lifestyle interventions, adjunctive pathogenetically oriented therapies such as alpha-lipoic acid, and evidence-based pharmacological treatments including pregabalin, gabapentin, duloxetine, and tricyclic antidepressants. Routine opioid use is discouraged.

CONCLUSIONS: This Malaysian expert consensus provides practical, context-specific recommendations for early detection, diagnosis, and management of DSPN. By adapting international guidance to local healthcare realities, these recommendations aim to improve care consistency, reduce DSPN-related complications, and enhance patient outcomes in Malaysia.

articles.title: Respiratory health risks associated with humidifier disinfectant exposure in South Korea: A systematic review and meta-analysis with exposure-response evaluation.
articles.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Humidifier disinfectants (HDs) were used as household biocidal products to prevent microbial growth in humidifiers and were withdrawn from the South Korean market in 2011 following recognition of associated health risks. Although epidemiological studies have reported associations between HD exposure and various respiratory diseases, the overall strength of evidence and exposure-response relationships have not been comprehensively quantified.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically review and quantitatively synthesize observational studies to evaluate the association between HD exposure and respiratory diseases and to assess exposure-response relationships across multiple exposure metrics.

METHODS: PubMed, Excerpta Medica Database, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature were searched through September 19, 2025. The primary outcome was the pooled odds ratio (OR) for respiratory disease risk among exposed versus non-exposed individuals. Secondary outcomes assessed exposure-response relationships using categorical and continuous exposure metrics.

RESULTS: Seventeen observational studies conducted in South Korea were included. HD exposure was associated with a markedly increased risk of respiratory diseases (pooled OR 7.02, 95% CI 1.97-24.98), with the strongest association observed for lung injury (pooled OR 94.53, 95% CI 61.31-145.73). Age-stratified subgroup analyses exhibited significantly elevated risks across adult, pediatric, and mixed-age populations. Exposure-response analyses demonstrated significant associations across multiple categorical exposure metrics, including usage duration, daily usage hours, cumulative use hours, airborne concentration, cumulative exposure level, longer use during sleep, and HD use during sleep. Continuous exposure analyses indicated that affected individuals had significantly longer cumulative use hours than unaffected individuals (pooled standardized mean difference 0.197, 95% CI 0.069-0.325).

SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides quantitative evidence supporting strong associations between HD exposure and respiratory diseases and demonstrates consistent exposure-response relationships across multiple exposure metrics, supporting a causal relationship between inhalational exposure to HDs and adverse respiratory outcomes.

IMPACT STATEMENT: This study provides comprehensive quantitative evidence that humidifier disinfectant exposure is strongly associated with respiratory diseases and demonstrates consistent exposure-response relationships across multiple exposure metrics. These findings strengthen causal inference for inhalational toxicity of humidifier disinfectants and highlight the importance of exposure assessment in environmental health risk evaluation. The results provide important evidence for environmental health policy, risk assessment, and prevention strategies for inhalation exposure to household biocidal products.

articles.title: The macrophage as a neuroimmune sensor and effector: neural control of inflammation across tissues and disease.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Once viewed mainly as scavengers of innate immunity, macrophages are now recognized as constitutive partners of the nervous system. In neural tissue their identity is instructed by neurons and glia, and in turn they shape neural function - pruning synapses, tuning neuronal excitability, and executing the autonomic commands that restrain inflammation.

PURPOSE: Here we advance a mechanistic model built on three principles: that neural and glial signals specify macrophage identity on a shared myeloid template; that the macrophage is a bidirectional sensor-effector node within autonomic reflex arcs, both relaying neural output and generating the cytokine signals that afferent nerves detect; and that this sensor-effector arc is modular, recurring across brain, spleen, gut, heart, and adipose tissue. We give particular attention to the afferent limb of the inflammatory reflex, which now extends beyond the vagus to nociceptors and to the carotid body, an arterial chemoreceptor that senses circulating inflammatory signals and recruits a sympathetic anti-inflammatory pathway, and to the stress-responsive circuitry through which sympathetic outflow drives myelopoiesis, neuroinflammation, and sickness behavior. We then turn to disease, in which macrophage function is altered by a diseased or aged niche in neurodegeneration, chronic pain, gut-brain disorders, and metabolic disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Whether the neuroimmune circuits described here are themselves disrupted in these conditions, rather than merely coexisting with them, is largely untested, and we outline what such evidence would require. We close by arguing that tuning these circuits, rather than broadly suppressing macrophage activity, is the more plausible therapeutic goal.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Brain on fire: Why intracerebral hemorrhage requires a firefighting strategy beyond single therapeutic targets.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) remains the most lethal form of stroke and lacks an established neuroprotective therapy. Secondary injury after ICH reflects interacting processes, including hematoma expansion, hemolysis-derived toxicity, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, perihematomal edema, oxidative stress, and regulated cell death. Although mechanistic single-target studies remain essential for defining biological relevance, treatment windows, target engagement, and safety, ICH is unlikely to be adequately addressed by any one intervention alone. Using the analogy of a "fire in the brain," this perspective proposes a coordinated, time-sensitive firefighting framework: Rapid blood-pressure management and hemostatic reversal can limit continued bleeding. Hematoma evacuation can remove biological fuel in selected patients. Interventions targeting lipid peroxidation and oxidative injury may limit secondary combustion. Inflammation- and edema-directed therapies may contain harmful heat. Enhancement of endogenous hematoma clearance may promote resolution and repair. Imaging and biomarkers can support phenotyping, monitoring, and treatment selection. Emerging signals from care bundle, minimally invasive evacuation, and experimental combination studies support the testing of staged, biologically rational add-on strategies rather than fixed therapeutic cocktails. The goal is not to deploy all the tools at once, but to match appropriate interventions to the evolving biology, phenotype, timing, feasibility, and care context of each hemorrhage.

articles.title: Evaluation of Potential Prognostic Biomarkers for Identifying Adults Hospitalised with COVID-19 at Increased Risk of Adverse Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Elevated levels of circulating cytokines and immune cells are often observed in patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), some of which have been associated with disease severity and clinical outcomes across various medical interventions. We evaluated 50 biomarkers and immune cell types in blood from patients in a randomised controlled trial and hypothesised that baseline inflammatory cytokines and haematologic markers would be associated with COVID-19 severity and outcomes, and a composite biomarker score derived through statistical and machine learning capturing complementary immune pathways could provide stronger prognostic value than individual biomarkers.

METHODS: COMMUNITY was a phase 3, randomised, adaptive-platform study in adult patients hospitalised with COVID-19 with clinical severity grade 2-5 (8-point ordinal scale), enrolled November 24, 2020, to June 4, 2021. An exploratory biomarker analysis used clinical laboratory assessments and serum cytokine data collected from baseline up to day 29 (or discharge) from patients randomised to placebo or apremilast + standard of care (baseline only). Healthy volunteers and ambulatory patients with COVID-19 (not part of the study) were evaluated for comparison.

RESULTS: Interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, IL-10, and tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNFα) were higher at baseline in 378 hospitalised patients than healthy volunteers or ambulatory patients. These cytokines and several haematological markers (including neutrophil count and percentage) showed positive associations with clinical severity and were inversely associated with clinical outcomes. A composite score was derived from baseline IL-6 levels and percentage of neutrophils and showed a strong association with patient overall survival. With a tertile cutoff at which composite scores ≤ 72.1 indicate high-risk patients, the estimated hazard ratio of mortality from COVID-19 infection was 14.3 (95% confidence interval 4.1, 49.3; P < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: This novel composite score was strongly associated with overall survival in adults hospitalised with COVID-19 and showed improved performance over its individual components.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: EudraCT 2020-002594-10; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT04590586 ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04590586 ).

articles.title: Combined Immune-Peptide Nanofiber with HSP70/AKT/mTOR Axis Blockade Enhances Photothermal Immunotherapy, Inhibiting Tumor Growth and Recurrence.
articles.abstract: Although immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies have shown clinical benefit, ICBs exert limited effects on most "immune-cold" solid tumors, i.e., tumors with low immune infiltration. Photothermal immunotherapy (PTIT) converts "cold" tumors into "hot" tumors, thereby enhancing immune responses and improving ICB efficacy. Hence, developing a strategy that can integrate PTIT and ICB treatment is desirable. In this study, we designed a unique carrier-free PSP@IR-CF3 nanofiber, self-assembled from the programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) targeting immune-peptide NTGYFYGDQ (PSP) and a PTIT agent (IR-CF3). The nanofibers enable precise tumor targeting and immune checkpoint inhibition by specifically binding to PD-L1 on the tumor cell surface, also providing an NIR-mediated photothermal effect. Combining PSP@IR-CF3 nanofibers with NIR induced mild PTIT, which effectively activated the tumor immune microenvironment and suppressed tumor growth with lower immunotoxicity. Additionally, we identified activation of the heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) /AKT/mTOR axis following PTIT, suggesting a potential role in post-treatment tumor survival and recurrence. By incorporating the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, the combination treatment further enhanced therapeutic efficacy and reduced tumor recurrence.

articles.title: When treatment advances faster than ethics: New ethical lines in paediatric neurology.
Preventive Effect of Smoking Cessation on Diabetes Onset: A Target Trial Emulation Approach.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Smoking cessation may transiently increase diabetes risk through weight gain, but its temporal trajectory remains unclear. We evaluated the long-term effect of smoking cessation on incident diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using a sequential-cohort design with repeated annual enrollment. Using annual health checkup data of Japanese employees from 2008 to 2022, we newly enrolled, at each annual assessment, and started follow-up individuals aged 40 years or older who were currently smoking and free of diabetes. Inverse probability weighting was used to adjust for baseline confounding in every sequential cohort. We estimated cumulative risks for quit-smoking and persistent-smoking groups, and their differences and ratios.

RESULTS: From 52 880 unique participants, a total of 331 701 participants were followed-up in the sequential cohorts, with a mean (standard deviation) age of 49.1 (5.7) years, and 25 749 developed diabetes. The risk ratio (95% confidence interval) for diabetes in the quit-smoking group relative to the persistent-smoking group was 1.15 (1.07-1.24) at 3 years and 0.95 (0.85-1.06) at 15 years. Per-protocol analyses showed a similar pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: Smoking cessation was associated with a short-term increase in diabetes risk, but this excess risk diminished over time, and no long-term increase in risk was observed. These findings support sustained smoking cessation as metabolically beneficial in the long term.

articles.title: Evaluating the role of metabolic surgery versus GLP1 agonists in patients living with obesity and chronic kidney disease - a systematic review.
articles.journal: The surgeon : journal of the Royal Colleges of Surgeons of Edinburgh and Ireland
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic surgery and glucagon-like petide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1) have renoprotective effects. Unlike GLP1 agonists, metabolic surgery is not endorsed as a therapeutic strategy for patients living with obesity, concurrent type-II diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD).

AIMS: To perform a systematic review to evaluate the renal outcomes of metabolic surgery and GLP1 agonists in patients living with obesity, T2DM and CKD.

METHODS: A systemic review was performed as per PRISMA guidelines. Basic descriptive statistics were performed using SPSS v26.0.

RESULTS: Overall, 6 studies met eligibility criteria, including three retrospective studies, two Markov Model analyses, and one randomized clinical trial. Data from 2487 patients were included [metabolic surgery: 48.7% (1210/2487) vs GLP1 agonists: 51.3% (1277/2487)]. Relative to GLP1 agonists, metabolic surgery significantly reduced CKD progression [21.7% (40/183) vs. 45.1% (109/242),P = 0.006] and renal failure development [24.0% (44/183) vs. 43.8% (106/242),P = 0.048], while also increasing microalbuminura remission [82.4% (42/51) vs. 46.9% (23/49), P < 0.001] and CKD remission [82.4% (42/51) vs. 55.1% (27/49),P < 0.001]. Metabolic surgery also significantly increased patient eligibility for transplantation [19.7% (192/976) vs. 2.1% (22/986),P < 0.001]. Two recent Markov analyses were performed to simulate the impact of metabolic surgery and GLP1 use in increasing patient eligibility for transplantation; 14.7% and 4.8% of simulated patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy and GLP1 therapy would successfully undergo renal transplant at 5-years respectively.

CONCLUSION: Compared to GLP1 agonists, metabolic surgery seemingly serve in reducing the risk of CKD progression and renal failure development in patients living with obesity, T2DM and CKD, while also increasing patient eligibility for transplant.

articles.title: Extensive Arterial Thrombosis Complicating Acute Pancreatitis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Arterial thrombosis is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of acute pancreatitis, with poorly defined clinical characteristics. This paper presents a case of extensive large-artery thrombosis complicating acute interstitial edematous pancreatitis along with a literature review. A 61-year-old man with acute interstitial edematous pancreatitis superimposed on chronic pancreatitis underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography four weeks after the initial presentation because of persistent dyspepsia. The imaging revealed pancreatic pseudocysts and extensive arterial thrombosis involving the thoracic and abdominal aorta, bilateral internal iliac arteries, and the left subclavian artery. The patient was treated with systemic anticoagulation, resulting in radiologic resolution. A literature review identified 11 previously reported cases of acute pancreatitis-associated arterial thrombosis. Including the present case (n=12), five cases occurred in interstitial edematous pancreatitis, while seven developed in acute necrotizing pancreatitis. The aorta and major visceral arteries were the most frequently involved vessels. Arterial thrombosis was detected within the first week in seven cases, whereas five cases were diagnosed later, including one as late as 60 days. Arterial thrombosis can occur in necrotizing and interstitial pancreatitis and may present either early or later in the disease course. Awareness and timely imaging may facilitate prompt recognition and management.

articles.title: [KASID Guidelines for Sexuality, Fertility, Pregnancy, and Lactation in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 2026].
authors: Guidelines Committee of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID)
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is commonly diagnosed during the reproductive years, making sexuality, fertility, pregnancy, and lactation central to long-term care. Misconceptions about heritability, fertility, and medication safety contribute to voluntary childlessness and discontinuation of effective therapy during pregnancy. Accumulating evidence indicates that disease activity, rather than IBD itself or most maintenance therapies, is the major determinant of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, supporting a paradigm centered on remission before and throughout pregnancy. Meanwhile, newer biologics and small molecules have been incorporated into clinical practice despite limited human reproductive safety data. Uncertainties persist regarding drug continuation, disease monitoring, mode of delivery, breastfeeding, and live vaccination in infants exposed to biologics in utero, highlighting the need for guidance tailored to the Korean national immunization program. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases therefore developed the first guideline in Korea addressing sexuality, fertility, pregnancy, and lactation in patients with IBD. Recent international guidance informed the scope and key questions; however, all evidence was independently reviewed and synthesized, and all recommendations were developed de novo using the GRADE methodology. Given limited randomized trial evidence in pregnancy, evidence synthesis relied primarily on systematic reviews, pregnancy registries, and large cohort studies. Consequently, the certainty of evidence for all recommendations was low or very low. All statements underwent a modified Delphi consensus process. The final guideline comprises 40 statements across 11 chapters: 23 recommendation statements, 9 evidence statements, and 8 expert consensus statements. This guideline supports individualized care throughout the reproductive continuum.

articles.title: [KASID Guidelines for the Medical Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis: 2026].
authors: Guidelines Committee of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID)
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease with an expanding therapeutic landscape and increasing clinical complexity. This guideline was developed by the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) to provide updated, evidence-based recommendations for the medical management of adult patients with UC in Korea. Guideline development used the GRADE-ADOLOPMENT approach, with source guidelines appraised using AGREE II. Key questions were formulated using the PICO framework, source guidelines and consensus documents published from 2017 through 2025 were appraised, and targeted literature searches covering January 2020 through April 2026 were conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and KoreaMed. The guideline addresses induction and maintenance therapy for mild-to-moderate and moderate-to-severe UC, management of acute severe UC, indications for surgery, use of biosimilars and subcutaneous formulations, and treatment optimization and sequencing. Recommendations were formulated based on structured evidence review and Evidence-to-Decision considerations, and were finalized through a modified Delphi consensus process and external review. The final recommendations emphasize objective disease control, individualized treatment selection, timely escalation or surgery in acute severe UC, and shared decision-making based on efficacy, safety, comorbidities, prior treatment exposure, patient preference, drug accessibility, and the Korean healthcare context. This guideline is intended to support consistent, practical, and patient-centered care and to improve long-term outcomes for adults with UC.

articles.title: [KASID Guidelines for the Medical Treatment of Crohn's Disease: 2026].
authors: Guidelines Committee of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID)
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by a heterogeneous clinical course and the potential development of irreversible bowel damage. Its therapeutic landscape has evolved substantially with the introduction of biologics and small molecules that target diverse inflammatory pathways, as well as new formulations and biosimilars of established biologics. These advances have expanded treatment options and enabled more ambitious therapeutic goals beyond symptomatic improvement, including corticosteroid-free remission, endoscopic healing, and prevention of disease progression. However, selecting and positioning therapies remain challenging because of differences in disease severity and phenotype, prior treatment exposure, safety considerations, patient preferences, and limited evidence from direct comparative studies. Additionally, important uncertainties remain regarding combination therapy with immunomodulators, treatment de-escalation, switching between originators and biosimilars, and management of perianal fistulizing disease. To provide evidence-based and clinically applicable recommendations, the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases developed updated clinical practice guidelines for the medical management of adult patients with CD. This guideline was developed using a GRADE-ADOLOPMENT approach that combined the adaptation of high-quality existing guidelines with de novo development based on newly identified evidence. The certainty of the evidence and strength of the recommendations were assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. The guideline addresses conventional therapies, immunomodulators, biologics, small molecules, biosimilars, alternative formulations, combination and de-escalation strategies, and perianal fistulizing disease. These recommendations are intended to support individualized therapeutic decision-making and improve the quality of care for adult patients with CD.

articles.title: [KASID Guidelines for Diagnosis and Monitoring of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 2026].
authors: Guidelines Committee of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID)
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by heterogeneous disease presentations and clinical courses. Accurate diagnosis and appropriate disease monitoring play an important role in improving long-term outcomes by preventing misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment; enabling early detection of disease progression, treatment failure, and disease-related complications; and facilitating timely adjustment of treatment strategies. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) developed guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD in adults, reflecting the Korean clinical setting, to support clinical decision-making and improve the quality of patient care. To develop these guidelines, existing international clinical practice guidelines and expert consensus statements were comprehensively reviewed, along with updated evidence relevant to each clinical topic. Final recommendations were established through expert consensus using a modified Delphi process. These guidelines address major clinical areas in the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD, including initial diagnosis and baseline assessment, assessment of disease extent and activity, disease monitoring in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, nutritional assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. These guidelines are intended to support individualized clinical judgment and should be applied flexibly, taking into account not only individual patient characteristics and clinical circumstances but also available resources, access to diagnostic and monitoring modalities, regulatory requirements, and reimbursement policies.

articles.title: [Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Tissue Acquisition of Pancreatic Solid Tumors].
articles.journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
articles.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition for pancreatic solid tumors has become essential in diagnostic practice. Although endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) has demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, its cytology-based samples often limit histologic evaluation, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing. To overcome these limitations, end-cutting fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) needles-notably Franseen and fork-tip designs-were developed to obtain well-preserved core tissue. These needles improve diagnostic accuracy, tissue adequacy, and sampling efficiency compared with FNA or reverse-bevel devices. Technical refinements have also improved outcomes. Fanning and torque maneuvers enhance tissue sampling across heterogeneous tumors, while aspiration strategies such as slow-pull, wet suction, and heparinized wet suction optimize core tissue preservation and reduce blood contamination. Macroscopic on-site evaluation confirms specimen adequacy, often reducing required needle passes without cytopathology support. Although generally safe, endoscopic ultrasound-guided sampling may cause bleeding, infection, pancreatitis, or rare needle-tract seeding. Careful needle selection, minimizing needle passes, and attention to anatomical relationships are crucial to mitigating these risks. Current evidence does not support routine prophylactic antibiotic use for solid lesions. As precision oncology increasingly relies on molecular profiling and next-generation sequencing, reliable procurement of high-quality tissue has become more important. This review summarizes advances in needle design, sampling techniques, on-site evaluation, antibiotic considerations, and complication management in endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue sampling of pancreatic solid tumors.

articles.title: Type III effector repertoires as a window into Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae evolution and Actinidia defense responses.
articles.abstract: Kiwifruit bacterial canker, caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa), represents a complex disease system in which closely related bacterial populations differ in host association, pathogenicity, genomic composition, and geographic distribution as evidenced by pandemic spread of biovar 3 after 2008. Closely related Psa lineages differ in host association, virulence, and distribution, yet these differences arise largely outside the conserved core genome. Mobile genetic elements remodel accessory regions, and acquisition, loss, and redundancy of type III effectors shape whether a lineage colonizes or is restricted by a given Actinidia genotype. Virulence is therefore a host-dependent property, not a fixed lineage rank. On the host side, genome assemblies, QTL mapping, and infection transcriptomics indicate that resistance reflects the timing and persistence of immune signalling rather than receptor presence alone, although few candidate receptors have been validated in planta. Durable resistance is most likely to derive from recognition of non-redundant effector functions and from immune hubs, such as RIN4, that multiple effectors target. Integrating pathogen population genomics, effector biology, and host immune genetics is the route to predicting which lineages will emerge next.

articles.title: Can Platelet Indices Predict Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections in ICU Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundUntil now, blood culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis of bloodstream infections (BSI). We investigated the diagnostic accuracy of complete blood count (CBC), particularly platelet indices, as a less expensive and more rapid alternative for the diagnosis of BSI, which allows for early proper antibiotic administration.MethodsA total of 169 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) from July 2023 to July 2025 who had suspected BSI and were tested via blood culture (BC). Patients were classified into a BSI group (n = 143) and a non-BSI group (n = 26). The BSI group was further classified into three subgroups as Gram negative bacteremia (n = 87), Gram positive bacteremia (n = 46) and candidemia (n = 10). Demographic parameters and hematological parameters were recorded and compared between the groups. To evaluate sensitivity and specificity, we constructed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.ResultsPatients with positive blood culture had significantly higher PCT, CRP, Neutrophil, PDW, MPV, MPV/PLT, PDW/PLT, and lower PWR, MPV/PCT, PDW/PCT & PLT/PCT compared to patients with negative blood culture. PLT/PCT, PCT, MPV/PCT, CRP, PDW & PDW/PCT have the highest AUCs (AUCs were 0.73, 0.71, 0.70, 0.69, 0.69 & 0.68, respectively). RDW, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT significantly increase, and platelet count significantly decreases among patients with Gram-positive compared to patients with Gram-negative bacterial infection. RDW, platelet, MPV/PLT & PDW/PLT have the highest AUC and accuracy in diagnosis of Gram-positive bacteria (AUC were 0.64, 0.62, 0.62 & 0.62, respectively).ConclusionThe RDW, platelet count, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT demonstrated the greatest accuracy in predicting Gram-positive bacterial infections.

articles.title: Can Emergency Physicians Identify Frozen Tissue on Ultrasound? Implications for Frostbite Management.
articles.abstract: IntroductionFrostbite injuries cause disfigurement and loss of functionality. The role of early imaging in management remains unclear because most modalities require infrastructure that prevents field application. Providers use point-of-care ultrasound to assess a range of soft tissue and musculoskeletal pathologies. The primary objective of this study is to determine the accuracy with which emergency physicians can identify frozen tissue on ultrasound.MethodsThree emergency medicine physicians evaluated whether porcine tissue was frozen or unfrozen by viewing standardized ultrasound clips. The team recorded clips of tissue thawing in a water bath from -10 to +10°C using a handheld ultrasound device. Each physician independently reviewed randomized clips and recorded their assessments. A 2 × 2 table was used to calculate the pooled sensitivity and specificity.ResultsEmergency medicine physicians reviewed 75 clips. They achieved a pooled sensitivity of 76% (95% CI 0.60-0.87) and a specificity of 87% (95% CI 0.68-0.96) for detecting frozen tissue compared with the tissue thermometer as the standard. Their results showed an overall accuracy of 80% (95% CI 0.69-0.88).ConclusionsIn this pilot study, emergency medicine physicians with advanced point-of-care ultrasound training identified frozen tissue on ultrasound 80% of the time. Future research should explore the sonographic features of frozen tissue in cases of frostbite and the test characteristics for sonographers with varying skill levels.

articles.title: Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Transabdominal Preperitoneal Inguinal Hernia Repair: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repair (r-TAPP) has been increasingly adopted, but whether it provides clinical advantages over conventional laparoscopic TAPP (l-TAPP) remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to provide an updated synthesis of randomized evidence comparing r-TAPP with l-TAPP.

METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and CENTRAL from inception through August 3, 2026, without language restrictions. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing r-TAPP with l-TAPP in adults undergoing inguinal hernia repair were eligible. We performed random-effects meta-analyses using risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We estimated between-study variance using restricted maximum likelihood and quantified heterogeneity using I2. We assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using RoB 2 and GRADE, respectively.

RESULTS: Five publications representing four independent RCTs comprising 401 patients were included. Of these, 195 patients underwent r-TAPP and 206 underwent l-TAPP. No statistically significant differences were observed in overall postoperative complications (RR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.45-1.78; I2 = 39.5%), conversion (RR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.09-10.91; I2 = 11.7%), operative time (MD: + 18.5 minutes; 95% CI: -8.4 to 45.5; I2 = 97.7%), seroma (RR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.08 to 2.03; I2 = 0%), hematoma (RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.12-3.41; I2 = 48.0%), or surgical site infection (RR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.03-3.14; I2 = 0%). Operative time showed substantial between-study heterogeneity, while estimates for postoperative complications were limited by sparse events and wide confidence intervals.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence has not demonstrated a clear clinical advantage of r-TAPP over l-TAPP for short-term outcomes. However, the available evidence remains limited by the relatively small overall sample size, sparse events, imprecision, and substantial heterogeneity in operative time. Larger multicenter randomized trials with standardized outcome definitions and longer follow-up are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist between approaches.

articles.title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at-risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.

articles.title: [Attention to the diagnosis and treatment of non-cirrhotic hyperammonemic encephalopathy after bariatric surgery].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Bariatric and metabolic surgery has become an effective intervention for the treatment of severe obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus, whose long-term efficacy and safety have been confirmed by substantial evidence-based medical data. However, with the annual increase in surgical volume, a series of rare but severe metabolic complications have been gradually recognized. Among them, non-cirrhotic hyperammonemia has attracted extensive attention due to its insidious onset, rapid progression and high mortality. Hyperammonemia after bariatric surgery is mainly characterized by significantly elevated blood ammonia and neuropsychiatric symptoms, with mostly normal liver function, and is easily misdiagnosed as cerebrovascular accident or psychiatric disorder. This article systematically reviews the clinical research progress of hyperammonemia after bariatric surgery in terms of epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, treatment and long-term management, aiming to improve clinicians' ability to identify and manage this disease, and reduce the risks of missed diagnosis, misdiagnosis and death.

articles.title: [Organ-preserving hemipelvic exenteration for low locally advanced rectal cancer].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the safety and clinical feasibility of hemi-pelvectomy in the treatment of low locally advanced rectal cancer. Methods: The surgical procedure comprised the following steps: (1) Laparoscopic exploration: no gross abnormalities were observed in the abdominopelvic peritoneum, liver, gallbladder, stomach, small intestine, or mesentery. (2) Open surgery: via the Marcille triangle approach, sequential resections were performed, including lateral pelvic wall resection, presacral dissection, pelvic floor resection, and intrapelvic lesion excision. En bloc resection encompassed the "low rectum + uterus/cervix + left hemipelvis (complete resection of the pelvic plexus nerves, with preservation of the left superior vesical artery and left S1-S5 nerve roots) + anterior S3/S4 presacral tissue," while the right pelvic plexus nerves were completely preserved. (3) Tissue reconstruction and pelvic wound closure: a modified Bacon procedure was employed for digestive tract reconstruction, a pedicled omental flap was used to isolate the anastomotic sites, and a biological mesh was applied to separate the abdominopelvic cavity. (4) Second-stage surgery: the prolapsed bowel segment was resected one month postoperatively.A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data (including the intra- and postoperative, and follow-up outcomes of the patients) of a 25-year-old female patient with low locally advanced rectal cancer who underwent hemi-pelvectomy at the Department of Colorectal Surgery, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Naval Medical University in November 2024. Results: The patient underwent an uneventful operation, with an operative time of approximately 6.5 hours and an estimated blood loss of approximately 400 ml. No intraoperative blood transfusion was required, and the patient returned safely to the general ward postoperatively. Postoperative pathology confirmed R0 resection, and no additional adjuvant chemoradiotherapy was administered. Postoperative recovery was favorable, with no severe complications such as abdominopelvic infection, empty pelvis syndrome (EPS), or intestinal obstruction. A second-stage operation was performed at 1 month postoperatively to resect the prolapsed bowel. At 6 months postoperatively, bladder function was normal, the Williams anal function score was grade B, and the quality-of-life score returned to the preoperative baseline. At 12 months postoperatively, the patient had 1-4 bowel movements per day and reported good satisfaction. At 18 months postoperatively, molecular residual disease (MRD) testing remained persistently negative, with no evidence of local recurrence. Conclusion: This preliminary experience suggests that hemi-pelvectomy for low locally advanced rectal cancer demonstrates acceptable clinical feasibility and safety.

articles.title: [Efficacy and safety of endoscopic treatment for anastomotic leakage following colorectal surgery: a systematic review].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aims to synthesize relevant literature on endoscopic treatment of anastomotic leakage after colorectal surgery, and evaluate the safety and efficacy of endoscopic therapies including over-the-scope clip (OTSC), endoscopic vacuum therapy (EVT) and covered stent for anastomotic leakage (AL) following colorectal surgery, so as to provide evidence-based support for clinical decision-making. Methods: Relevant studies on endoscopic treatment of AL after colorectal surgery were retrieved from Chinese and English databases. Two researchers independently screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. Given the significant clinical and methodological heterogeneity among the included studies, a meta-analysis was not performed, and a narrative synthesis was adopted to summarize the results. Results: A total of 38 studies involving 679 patients were included.In the OTSC group (10 studies, 81 patients), the clinical cure rate ranged from 57.1% to 100%.In the EVT group (20 studies, 452 patients), the clinical cure rate was 55.3%-100%, with a wide variation in healing time (1-114 days). In the covered stent group (8 studies, 146 patients), the clinical cure rate was 71.4%-100%; however, the incidence of device-related complications such as stent migration was relatively high. Conclusions: Endoscopic treatment is a feasible minimally invasive strategy for AL after colorectal surgery. OTSC, EVT and covered stents each have their own indications and complication profiles. Clinical selection should be individualized based on the defect characteristics and patient condition.

articles.title: [Efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists combined with bariatric surgery for obesity: a timing-stratified systematic review].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Objective: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists applied at different stages before and after bariatric surgery, and to compare the clinical benefits of preoperative use, early postoperative use, and rescue use after insufficient weight loss or weight regain according to medication timing. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase via Ovid were searched from inception to June 20, 2026. A relatively strict three-concept search strategy was used, consisting of terms related to bariatric surgery, GLP-1 receptor agonists and specific drug names, and perioperative or weight-management scenarios. Searches were mainly restricted to title and abstract fields, and animal-only studies were excluded. Clinical studies involving patients who underwent metabolic and bariatric surgery and received GLP-1 receptor agonists before or after surgery were included. Studies were classified into three groups according to medication timing: preoperative use, early postoperative use, and rescue use after insufficient weight loss or weight regain. Mean difference or standardized mean difference was used for continuous variables, and odds ratio was used for categorical variables. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. Results: A total of 27 studies were included in the systematic review, including 10 studies on preoperative use, 4 on early postoperative use, and 13 on rescue use after insufficient weight loss or weight regain. Among them, 13 studies were included in efficacy meta-analyses. Preoperative use of GLP-1 receptor agonists improved preoperative weight loss, with a pooled SMD of 0.52 (95%CI: 0.25-0.79, I²=0%, P<0.05). However, when postoperative weight loss at 12 months was assessed using body weight at surgery as the baseline, the percentage of total body weight loss at 12 months was 2.85 percentage points lower in the preoperative medication group than in the non-medication group (95%CI: -4.35 to -1.36, I²=37.7%, P<0.05). Active addition of GLP-1 receptor agonists around 1 month after surgery increased the percentage of total body weight loss at 6 months by an additional 3.62 percentage points (95%CI: 1.88-5.37, I²=0%, P<0.05). Initiation of GLP-1 receptor agonists around 6 months after surgery resulted in an additional weight loss of 7.48 kg during subsequent follow-up compared with controls (95%CI: 5.35-9.60, I²=34.6%, P<0.05). For rescue therapy, four randomized controlled trials showed that GLP-1 receptor agonists resulted in an additional 10.30 percentage points of endpoint percentage weight loss compared with placebo or usual care (95%CI: 6.40-14.20, I²=89.2%, P<0.05). Regarding safety, among studies that clearly reported event numbers, the pooled incidences of nausea, constipation, diarrhea, and vomiting were 25.3%, 19.0%, 9.2%, and 8.6%, respectively. Serious adverse events were uncommon. Conclusion: GLP-1 receptor agonists have timing-specific value in the comprehensive management of metabolic and bariatric surgery. Preoperative use can increase preoperative weight loss but does not enhance postoperative weight loss when body weight at surgery is used as the baseline. Early postoperative use may further amplify weight-loss benefits within the first postoperative year. Rescue use after insufficient weight loss or weight regain is supported by the strongest evidence. In terms of safety, adverse events are mainly gastrointestinal, and serious adverse events are uncommon.

articles.title: [Clinical application analysis of remote robot-assisted sleeve gastrectomy and bariatric anti-reflux surgery].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of remote robot-assisted sleeve gastrectomy with concomitant anti-reflux surgery. Methods: A descriptive case series study was conducted. We retrospectively enrolled 7 patients who underwent remote robot-assisted sleeve gastrectomy with concomitant anti-reflux surgery, which was collaboratively performed by Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region People's Hospital (operator side) and Aksu Prefectural First People's Hospital (patient side) from October 2025 to March 2026. Baseline characteristics, intraoperative parameters, intraoperative network performance, and 3 month postoperative followup data were collected. The outcomes analyzed included weight loss efficacy [percentage of excess weight loss (%EWL) and percentage of total weight loss (%TWL)], antireflux effect (GERDQ score), and incidence of complications. Results: A total of 7 patients undergoing remote bariatric surgery were enrolled, including 1 male and 6 females. Among them, 2 patients had a history of previous abdominal surgery, 2 had hypertension, 1 had diabetes mellitus, and 1 had reflux esophagitis. The mean age was (36.4±6.2) years. During remote surgery, the mean latency at the operator side and the patient side were (73.29±3.73) ms; the average packet loss rates were (0.06±0.03)% and (0.02±0.02)% respectively; the mean upload speed before and after master-slave operation were (190.89±81.98) Mbps and (71.22±10.28) Mbps;and the mean download speed before and after master-slave operation were (144.00±58.93) Mbps and (78.13±18.56) Mbps respectively. no operation lag or signal interruption occurred throughout the procedure. The mean preoperative body weight of the patients was (117.57±17.72) kg, and the mean body weight at 3 months postoperatively was (91.66±8.44) kg. The mean preoperative body mass index (BMI) was (41.74±4.48) kg/m², and the mean BMI at 3 months postoperatively was (32.67±2.64) kg/m². The median preoperative GERD-Q score was 8 (interquartile range, Q1, Q3: 6, 11), and the GERD-Q score at 3 months postoperatively was 6 (Q1, Q3: 6, 7). At 3 months after surgery, %TWL was (21.32±6.75)%, and %EWL was (53.47±13.89)%. In terms of postoperative complications, there were 2 cases of dysphagia (water swallowing test [WST] grade ≥ 2), 1 case of constipation, 2 cases of chest pain, 2 cases of alopecia, 2 cases of abdominal distension, and 1 case of vomiting. Among these patients, those with chest pain, abdominal distension, vomiting, and WST grade≥2 dysphagia achieved gradual and spontaneous resolution by 3 months postoperatively, while the symptoms of constipation and alopecia showed no significant improvement. Conclusion: Remote robot-assisted sleeve gastrectomy and sleeve gastrectomy with concomitant anti-reflux surgery are safe and feasible.

articles.title: [Renal function assessment and procedure selection in metabolic and bariatric surgery].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
articles.abstract: Obesity is an important risk factor for the development and progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), whereas CKD may increase perioperative risk in patients undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery. Surgical procedures differ in their effects on acute kidney injury, volume depletion, nephrolithiasis, enteric hyperoxaluria, nutritional status, and immunosuppressant exposure; therefore, kidney function assessment is essential for risk stratification and procedure selection. In patients with obesity, serum creatinine and cystatin C may be affected by muscle mass, adiposity, and inflammation, while body surface area indexing and postoperative changes in body composition may further complicate the interpretation of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Preoperative evaluation should establish whether kidney abnormalities are chronic and should include creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate and the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio as initial assessments. Measurement of cystatin C, measured glomerular filtration rate, or 24-hour urine analysis may be added when clinically indicated. Procedure selection should integrate CKD stage, albuminuria category, the trajectory of kidney function, previous acute kidney injury, the risk of nephrolithiasis or hyperoxaluria, dialysis and kidney transplantation plans, and the need for metabolic and antireflux efficacy. Sleeve gastrectomy is generally favored in patients with advanced CKD, those receiving dialysis, kidney transplant candidates, and patients at high risk of hyperoxaluria. Roux-en-Y gastric bypass may be considered after multidisciplinary assessment in patients with stable kidney function, low stone risk, and a greater need for metabolic or antireflux effects. Postoperative kidney function should be evaluated in conjunction with changes in body composition, albuminuria, glomerular hyperfiltration, and kidney-related clinical events. This review summarizes kidney function assessment, procedure selection, and postoperative reassessment in patients undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery.

articles.title: Time-Dependent Mortality Risk in Lean Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease During Long-Term Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: The prognosis of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains controversial. We investigated the long-term prognosis of lean MASLD and its time-dependent associations with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

METHODS: We analyzed 3568 participants with MASLD from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Because the proportional hazards assumption was violated for all-cause mortality, 10-year landmark and time-varying coefficient Cox analyses were performed. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) evaluated the association between body mass index (BMI) and early all-cause mortality, and subgroup analyses identified high-risk populations.

RESULTS: During a median 27.7-year follow-up, lean MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality within 0-10 years (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.29-2.20), but not thereafter (adjusted HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.87-1.25). No significant association between lean MASLD and cardiovascular mortality was observed during either pre-landmark (adjusted subdistribution HR [sHR], 1.45; 95% CI, 0.95-2.22) or post-landmark (adjusted sHR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.69-1.36) in the overall population. Time-specific HR demonstrated a gradual attenuation of the excess mortality association over follow-up. RCS demonstrated a nonlinear U-shaped association between BMI and early all-cause mortality. Excess early mortality risks were particularly evident among males aged ≥ 60 years and participants with baseline FIB-4 ≥ 1.30.

CONCLUSIONS: Lean MASLD conferred a time-dependent excess risk of all-cause mortality, predominantly within the first decade of follow-up, but was not robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality in the overall population. Older males and patients with elevated FIB-4 scores represented high-risk phenotypes.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Doxorubicin-Etoposide-Methylprednisolone (DEP)-Based Regimens in Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare but severe hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation. Etoposide-containing regimens are established in paediatric HLH, but evidence in adults remains limited. Doxorubicin-etoposide-methylprednisolone (DEP)-based regimens have shown promising results; however, their efficacy and safety have not been systematically evaluated. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of DEP-based regimens in patients with HLH.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library and Embase through February 2026, with no language restrictions. We used random-effects proportional meta-analyses to estimate 4-week overall response rate (ORR), complete response (CR), partial response (PR) and overall survival (OS). Sensitivity analyses assessed the influence of potentially overlapping cohorts and of individual study arms.

RESULTS: Ten study arms from seven studies comprising 320 patients were included; all studies were conducted in China. Pooled ORR, CR and PR were 80% (95% CI, 75%-86%), 29% (95% CI, 23%-35%) and 49% (95% CI, 40%-57%), respectively, and were stable in sensitivity analyses. Pooled OS from four studies (164 patients) was 41% (29%-53%). Initial therapy achieved a higher CR than salvage therapy (39% vs. 24%; p = 0.0104), while ORR and PR were comparable. Response rates were consistent across age groups, HLH subtypes and regimen variations. Toxicity was generally manageable, with infection representing the most frequent adverse event.

CONCLUSION: DEP-based regimens are associated with high response rates in HLH, predominantly in the relapsed and refractory setting. The higher CR rate observed with initial use compared with salvage here is likely to be confounded by indication and does not support frontline use. Prospective multi-centre comparative studies are required to determine the efficacy and tolerability of DEP-based therapy.

articles.title: Hypogammaglobulinemia and Infection After Rituximab in Pemphigus, With Divergent Desmoglein Antibody and Immunoglobulin Kinetics: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
