articles.abstract: Pemphigus is a rare autoimmune blistering disease for which rituximab is a first-line treatment, yet most safety data derive from lymphoma and rheumatoid arthritis cohorts. This study assessed hypogammaglobulinemia and infection during rituximab treatment, the baseline predictors of new-onset hypogammaglobulinemia, and whether desmoglein antibody titers and total immunoglobulin levels fall together. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, the records of 97 patients given rituximab for pemphigus between January 2015 and June 2026 were reviewed. Patients who received intravenous immunoglobulin were excluded, leaving 69 patients for outcome analyses. Among 51 patients with a normal baseline immunoglobulin G level, new-onset hypogammaglobulinemia, defined as a fall below 700 mg/dL after treatment, occurred in 5 (10%), and no patient reached the severe threshold of 400 mg/dL. Seven further patients were already below 700 mg/dL before treatment. Patients who developed new-onset hypogammaglobulinemia were older and had lower baseline immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M levels (areas under the curve 0.85, 0.83, and 0.81). Patients with hypogammaglobulinemia had received more corticosteroid per cycle, so a contribution of corticosteroids cannot be excluded. Late-onset neutropenia was not detected (0 of 69). Infection occurred in 5 of 69 patients (7%) and severe infection in 2 of 69 (3%). 6 months after induction, desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 antibody titers had fallen to 16% and 19% of baseline (p < 0.001), whereas immunoglobulin G remained at 97% (p = 0.46), independently of hypogammaglobulinemia. Hypogammaglobulinemia remained mild and the serologic response was not mirrored in total immunoglobulin levels. Advanced age and low baseline immunoglobulin levels are candidate markers of risk. These findings come from a retrospective single-center cohort and require confirmation in larger series.

articles.title: Fatal Neonatal mTORopathy: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of RRAGC-Associated Long-Olsen-Distelmaier Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe cardiac condition characterized by the enlargement and impaired contraction of the heart's ventricles. Pediatric cases often present unique challenges due to their rarity and the complexity of underlying genetic causes. This study presents the first documented case of a Colombian patient with neonatal DCM, bilateral congenital cataracts, focal epilepsy, and hyperlactatemia. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in the RRAGC gene, establishing the diagnosis of Long-Olsen-Distelmaier syndrome, a rare mTOR-related disorder characterized by syndromic cardiomyopathy and multisystem involvement. Additionally, we review the clinical and molecular characteristics of previously reported cases in the literature.

articles.title: The decoction of licorice, ginseng, and dry ginger demonstrates anti-pulmonary fibrosis activity through modulation of the pyroptosis pathway.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic progressive lung disease that causes damage to the lung structure and respiratory failure. Currently, there is no effective cure for this condition. The "Licorice dried ginger ginseng soup" (LGGS) recorded in Volume 3 of "Xianzheng Bingzhi" is a traditional prescription used to treat lung atrophy. However, the pharmacological mechanism of its effect on pulmonary fibrosis has not been studied yet.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to explore the protective effects of LGGS when administered separately as silica and bleomycin in the mouse lung fibrosis model, to reveal its mechanism of action, and to focus on the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD signaling pathway.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis were induced in C57BL/6 mice using silica and bleomycin, respectively, and LGGS was administered as intervention. Lung function, histopathology, and serum metabolites were evaluated. The major component contents in LGGS were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Western blotting was performed to verify the molecular mechanism.

RESULTS: LGGS significantly reduced the degree of pulmonary fibrosis in both silica- and bleomycin-induced mouse models, improved lung function, and decreased hydroxyproline (HYP) content in lung tissues. The established HPLC method effectively determined the main components with good linearity. LGGS down-regulated the protein expression of α-SMA, COL1, Caspase-1, GSDMD, and NLRP3.

CONCLUSION: LGGS exerts anti-pulmonary fibrosis effects, potentially by inhibiting the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis pathway. The HPLC method is accurate and reliable, providing a basis for quality control of LGGS.

articles.title: Gut microbiome-mediated associations between dietary intake and type 2 diabetes in a Korean population.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is influenced by multiple risk factors, including dietary intake, which may affect disease risk through interactions with the gut microbiome. This study sought to identify microbial features that mediate these associations in a Korean population.

METHODS: Data from 1,347 participants aged 30-64 years were analyzed. Dietary intake was assessed using a food frequency questionnaire, and gut microbiome profiles were generated by 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing of the V3-V4 region. MaAsLin2 and mediation analyses were then performed.

RESULTS: Forty-eight amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) were associated with T2D. Lachnospira ASV054, Romboutsia B ASV190, and Clostridium T ASV104 were inversely associated with T2D and statistically mediated the associations of bread, starchy food, and kimchi intake with T2D, respectively (q < 0.001). Clostridium T ASV104 also exhibited indirect effects opposite to the direct effects of rice cake and ultra-processed food (UPF) intake on T2D (q < 0.05), suggesting suppressive effects.

CONCLUSIONS: Several gut microbial features inversely associated with T2D partially mediated diet-T2D associations and exhibited suppressive effects for rice cake and UPF intake. These findings suggest that the gut microbiome may play an important role in mediating associations between dietary intake and T2D.

articles.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals enhanced host inflammatory responses associated with TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway during infection with the ASFV CN/SC/2019 pA104R-K5R.
articles.abstract: The African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a highly contagious double-stranded DNA virus that belongs to the Asfarviridae family. Structurally, ASFV is more complex than other viruses and encodes numerous proteins within each layer. These proteins modulate viral replication in the host via a range of complex molecular mechanisms. Among them, the putative histone-like protein pA104R, which is a late viral protein, plays a crucial role in several stages of the viral life cycle. Our previous study demonstrated that lysine 5 (K5) of pA104R is essential for mediating ubiquitination-induced degradation of pA104R, and that the K5R mutant virus caused severe host inflammation in vivo. However, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we examined the mechanism by which the pA104R mutant strain enhances ASFV replication in the host at the transcriptome level. Compared with the WT group, the mutant strain group induced more severe host inflammation by increased expression of inflammatory mediators associated with the TNF-α/NF-κB pathway and the NLRP3 inflammasome, as shown by transcriptome sequencing and Western blot. The results also suggested that ASFV CN/SC/2019 pA104R-K5R induced distinct transcriptional changes in multiple innate immune-related genes. Additionally, the ELISA results demonstrated a higher level of inflammation in cells infected with the mutant strain. This evidence suggested its potential to enhance inflammatory pathology, though further in vivo studies are needed to confirm this. This study provides new insights into the functions of key structural proteins of ASFV in viral replication and host immune modulation. It also offers important theoretical support for elucidating ASFV pathogenic mechanisms.

articles.title: Identification of small molecule inhibitors of Ebola virus by use of a biologically contained virus system.
articles.abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe illness with high mortality for which limited therapeutic options are available. Identifying new antiviral drugs that target viral proteins is essential for improving prevention and treatment strategies. In this study, we screened a library of 2,620 small molecules enriched for reported inhibitory activity against cellular and viral helicases to identify phenotypic inhibitors of a biologically contained virus, Ebola∆VP30 virus, in Vero cells stably expressing VP30 protein. Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC50 values. Two of these compounds completely inhibited EbolaΔVP30 virus infection, interfering with either virus entry or replication. Although these preliminary screening hits require further optimization and in vivo validation, their identification opens new avenues for anti-Ebola virus drug discovery.

articles.title: Preliminary proteome characterization of the aqueous humor across four cataract subtypes.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize proteomic alterations in the aqueous humor (AH) across cataract subtypes and to identify subtype-specific pathological signatures for molecular stratification. Four-dimensional data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry was performed for comprehensive proteomic profiling of AH samples from 40 cataract patients in this pilot study. Functional annotation using Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses elucidated biological pathways. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses were applied to identify Differentially Abundant Proteins (DAPs), and orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (O-PLS-DA) was used to screen candidate discriminatory signatures. A total of 1905 proteins were identified, predominantly enriched in pathways related to inflammatory and immune responses, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix organization, and energy metabolism. Compared with age-related cataract, 96, 119, and 272 candidate DAPs were identified in diabetic cataract, high myopic cataract, and cataract with anterior capsule fibrosis, respectively, among which 24 proteins were identified as shared signatures across these subtypes. By integrating top-ranked DAPs with high-VIP molecules from the O-PLS-DA model, we identified 32 candidate proteins for discriminating between cataract subtypes. These findings delineate subtype-associated candidate proteomic signatures in AH, providing valuable insights that facilitate mechanistic stratification and support the identification of subtype-specific therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Ultra-early diagnosis recently developments of acute myocardial infarction: Emerging biomarkers and advanced sensing technologies.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Currently, myocardial infarction is commonly detected via traditional biomarker analysis, electrocardiography, and echocardiography. In general, conventional clinical approaches are limited by insufficient early-stage sensitivity and time-consuming procedures, thereby delaying therapeutic interventions. To address the above-mentioned drawbacks, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in both ultra-early biomarkers and novel high-sensitivity detection platforms. A panel of ultra-early biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity (e.g., GPBB, cMyC, cfDNA, MPO, D-dimer, miRNAs, and lncRNAs) is explicitly identified in this review. Recent progress in nano-based, graphene-based, and chemical biosensors for biomarker detection is further elaborated. The application of these biosensors delivers amplified signal outputs, enhanced sensitivity, shortened detection time, multiplex detection capability, and successful miniaturization of detection devices. This review also analyzes the integration of artificial intelligence models with conventional diagnostic modalities (electrocardiography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging) and gold-standard diagnostic methods (biomarker testing, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, coronary computed tomography). Such integrated analytical strategies enable objective, rapid, and early diagnosis. When embedde into wearable monitoring devices, these technologies support non-invasive and continuous real-time monitoring and generate preemptive clinical alerts with ultra-high signal sensitivity. Ultimately, this article establishes a comprehensive framework for the ultra-early diagnosis of myocardial infarction by integrating screened ultra-early biomarkers and innovative high-sensitivity detection techniques.

articles.title: Single-molecule and long-read sequencing reveals structural diversity of hepatitis B virus haplotypes including mutations, deletions, and splicing.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) exhibits diverse pathological states during chronic infection. While defective genomes with deletions and splicing have been sporadically reported, the quasispecies structure and their role in disease progression have remained unclear due to technical constraints of conventional short-read sequencing.

METHODS: Using rolling circle amplification (RCA)-nanopore long-read sequencing, we analyzed near full-length HBV genomes (approximately 3.2kb) at the single-molecule level from 6 serum samples obtained from 5 patients. Haplotypes were reconstructed from reads with point mutations, and structural linkages with deletions and splicing were evaluated.

RESULTS: Diverse haplotypes (three to five per patient) involving mutations across the HBV genome, predominantly in putative immune-targeted regions (core, preS, and surface), were detected in all cases, along with variants containing different deletions and splicing patterns. Notably, in chronic hepatitis and hepatocellular carcinoma cases, a substantial portion (29.5-71.3%) of circulating HBV DNA consisted of deletion and splicing variants, which clustered significantly in specific haplotypes (p < 2.8 × 10⁻⁵). Longitudinal changes in haplotype composition involving point mutations and different deletion/splicing patterns were observed in one patient before and after HBeAg seroconversion.

CONCLUSIONS: HBV exists as a population comprising multiple haplotypes with mutations, deletions, and splicing interconnected and dynamically changing according to disease state. Monitoring circulating splicing variants and haplotype dynamics may serve as novel biomarkers for disease understanding. This single-molecule long-read analysis elucidates the molecular basis of HBV quasispecies evolution.

articles.title: Stereotactic arrhythmia radiotherapy or STAR - What is out there now and where are we heading?
How Task Load Modulates the Effect of State Anxiety on Working Memory and Its Neural Mechanisms: Evidence from Verbal and Spatial Modalities.
articles.abstract: The impact of state anxiety on working memory (WM) and its neural mechanisms, especially the role of task load, remain uncertain. To address this issue, we conducted two experiments to examine how state anxiety affects WM under different task loads and whether these effects are consistent across verbal and spatial modalities. State anxiety was elicited using the threat-of-shock paradigm, while participants alternately completed n-back tasks (1-back and 3-back) under safe and threat conditions, with brain activity monitored via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). In Experiment 1 (verbal n-back), anxiety did not affect 1-back accuracy but improved 3-back accuracy. Neurally, anxiety reduced activation in the right posterior parietal cortex (PPC) and left premotor cortex (PMC) during the 1-back task. In contrast, during the 3-back task, anxiety enhanced activation in the bilateral ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, and right PPC, and increased the brain network's small-world property and normalized clustering coefficient. In Experiment 2 (spatial n-back), anxiety impaired 1-back accuracy but enhanced 3-back accuracy. Neurally, anxiety reduced left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC)-PMC connectivity during the 1-back, but enhanced this connectivity and bilateral dlPFC-left PPC connectivity during the 3-back, along with increased global efficiency and decreased normalized characteristic path length of brain networks. In summary, anxiety effects varied with task load, with different patterns observed in verbal and spatial WM, and their neural mechanisms involve changes in executive control network activity. These findings are interpreted through the Top-Down Emotion Control Perspective and the Two-Component Model of Anxiety.

articles.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation attenuates post-stroke dysphagia by modulating microglial polarization via the endothelial VWF/PI3K-Akt axis.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke dysphagia is a common complication with limited treatment options. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (ta-VNS) has shown neuroprotective effects. This study investigated whether ta-VNS improves swallowing function and alleviates neuroinflammation by modulating microglial M1/M2 polarization, examining the role of von Willebrand factor (VWF) in endothelial-microglial crosstalk. A rat model of transient bilateral middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established. Rats received ta-VNS for 3 weeks, and swallowing function, neurological deficits, and inflammatory markers were assessed. Microglial M1 (CD16) and M2 (CD206) polarization in the white matter was examined by immunofluorescence. RNA-seq was used to identify candidate genes. In vitro, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model was applied to hCMEC/D3 endothelial cells co-cultured with HMC3 microglia, and VWF was knocked down using shRNA to evaluate its effect on microglial polarization and inflammation. ta-VNS significantly improved body weight, food/water intake, and swallowing function (reduced latency and increased swallowing frequency) in transient middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. ta-VNS reduced levels of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-10, attenuated microglial activation, suppressed M1 (Iba-1+CD16+) microglia, and enhanced M2 (Iba-1+CD206+) polarization in rat whiter matter. RNA-seq revealed downregulation of VWF after ta-VNS, with enrichment in the PI3K-Akt pathway. In vitro, OGD/R upregulated VWF, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, endothelial apoptosis, and permeability. Knockdown of VWF in endothelial cells shifted co-cultured microglia from M1 toward M2 phenotype and reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β while increasing IL-10. ta-VNS can improve post-stroke dysphagia and reduce neuroinflammation by promoting M2 microglial polarization. Endothelial VWF may be a key downstream mediator of this process.

articles.title: Sepsis-associated efferocytosis deficiency: Molecular mechanisms and novel therapeutic targets.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in critical care, sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality driven by a profoundly dysregulated host immune response. Increasingly, defective efferocytosis-the fundamental physiological process for clearing dead cells-has been identified as a critical catalyst in sepsis pathophysiology. Under normal conditions, efferocytosis resolves inflammation and maintains tissue homeostasis. However, during sepsis, the efferocytotic capacity of phagocytes is severely paralyzed. This clearance failure results in a massive accumulation of apoptotic and necrotic cellular debris within the tissue microenvironment, triggering an unabated release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Consequently, this substrate overload sustains a self-amplifying inflammatory storm that accelerates tissue injury and precipitates multiple organ failure. In this review, we dissect the diverse modalities of programmed cell death in sepsis and map the subsequent breakdown of the core, multi-step efferocytotic machinery. We systematically explore the molecular basis of efferocytosis failure across distinct organ-specific complications, including acute lung injury, sepsis-associated encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and septic cardiomyopathy. Finally, we evaluate emerging targeted therapies aimed at restoring efferocytotic efficiency, highlighting a crucial conceptual shift from primarily suppressing inflammation to actively promoting its resolution and repairing host immunity.

articles.title: Adipocytes upregulate endothelial miR-21 to promote angiogenesis and alleviate acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe condition with high morbidity and mortality, often progressing to chronic kidney disease. During AKI progression, the regulation of hypoxic stress and promotion of angiogenesis are crucial. The role of systemic hypoxia in modulating renal repair remains incompletely understood. This study investigates how hypoxic adipocytes promote angiogenesis in early-stage AKI. Conditioned medium was collected from hypoxic adipocytes to simulate paracrine effects. Endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation were assessed using CCK-8, scratch wound, Transwell, and Matrigel assays. Expression of miR-21, SPRY1, and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was measured by qPCR and western blotting. In a mouse model of renal ischemia-reperfusion injury, conditioned medium was administered by injection. Renal injury, fibrosis, and peritubular capillary density were evaluated by histology and immunofluorescence. Conditioned medium from hypoxic adipocytes significantly enhanced endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation, accompanied by increased miR-21 and decreased SPRY1 expression. Mechanistically, miR-21 promoted angiogenesis by suppressing SPRY1 and activating the ERK/MAPK pathway. In vivo, conditioned medium restored peritubular capillary density, reduced fibrosis and tubular damage, and improved renal recovery following ischemia-reperfusion injury. The results indicate that hypoxic adipocytes promote vascular repair in AKI through a paracrine mechanism involving the upregulation of miR-21 in endothelial cells and activation of the SPRY1/ERK/MAPK axis. This pathway represents a promising therapeutic target for AKI.

articles.title: Sex- and Age-Specific Descriptive Patterns in Ischemic Stroke Incidence and Mortality Among Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study (2000-2018).
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite global advancements in stroke prevention, it remains unclear if benefits are shared equally. This study investigates intersectional descriptive patterns in ischemic stroke incidence and 30-day mortality among patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in Taiwan, focusing on sex-specific temporal trends.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the National Health Insurance Research Database in Taiwan. Using propensity score matching, we compared outcomes between patients with and without T2D. Cox proportional-hazard models were employed to assess risks, stratified by sex and age to identify specific vulnerable populations.

RESULTS: The absolute incidence of ischemic stroke declined substantially between 2000 and 2018 in both patients with T2D (from 102.50 to 38.52 per 10,000 person-years) and those without T2D (from 40.14 to 17.81 per 10,000 person-years). Despite these reductions, patients with T2D consistently had higher incidence rate-based relative risk of ischemic stroke than those without T2D. In women, the relative risk increased to 2.86 during 2015-2018. Among participants younger than 60 years, both absolute incidence and the corresponding risk estimates decreased over time, whereas the relative risk remained persistently elevated among older participants. Absolute 30-day mortality also declined markedly in both groups, although women with T2D exhibited an increased relative mortality risk during the most recent recruitment period (2015-2018).

CONCLUSIONS: While overall stroke incidence in Taiwan has declined, temporal progress varies by age and sex. Relative stroke risk has narrowed among younger individuals but remained stable or descriptively higher among elderly women with diabetes. Further research is needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and guide tailored prevention strategies.

articles.title: Automated and spatially resolved quantification of phage-mediated lysis intensity in spot assays using a resolution-independent image-analysis platform.
articles.abstract: Macroscale evaluation of bacteriophage host range frequently relies on visual interpretation of spot inoculation assays, in which clearing is recorded using qualitative or ordinal categories including +++, ++, +, and -. These categories are rapid and practical but compress continuous image variation and can introduce observer-dependent disagreement, particularly for weak and intermediate reactions. This study presents an open-source computer-vision platform that applies a defined image-reading procedure to arrayed phage spot assays by converting local clearing into a deterministic numerical measurement. The analytical signal is calculated from the relative grayscale-intensity difference between a predefined central spot region and spatially matched peripheral bacterial-lawn regions, providing local background normalization instead of reliance on absolute image brightness. Spatial positions are defined from plate anchors and proportional grid interpolation, allowing the same analytical logic to be applied to images with different dimensions after appropriate plate-specific calibration. The platform provides a continuous normalized spot-clearing score and an optional ordinal representation for compatibility with conventional reporting. Validation comprised 84 predefined spot reactions independently scored by four observers and four repeated computational analyses of identical image input. Manual scoring showed the greatest dispersion for weak and intermediate clearing, whereas automated re-analysis showed high repeatability. Automated scores also showed strong monotonic concordance with manual consensus. The platform is intended as a quantitative image-analysis layer for completed spot assays. The score does not measure plaque diameter or plaque number and does not independently establish productive phage infection, for which efficiency of plating (EOP) or other biological assays remain necessary.

articles.title: Association of therapeutic antimicrobial class with incidence of acute complications and recurrent infection following non-severe streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While penicillin or amoxicillin is mostly recommended for treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis, other antimicrobials are sometimes used. The objective of this study was to assess risk of developing invasive diseases, complications, and recurrent infection among those with streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis treated with different classes of antimicrobials.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study used TriNetX, a database with multicenter electronic health records. The incidence of acute complications and recurrent infection among patients with streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis was compared between the penicillin and non-penicillin groups following propensity score matching.

RESULTS: Initially, 313,143 and 56,893 patients in the penicillin and non-penicillin groups were identified, and 56,402 participants from each group were matched. The HRs were 0.69 [0.53-0.89]; p=0.004 for invasive disease or acute complication, 0.97 [0.92-1.0.2]; p=0.256 for clinical recurrence, 1.03 [0.97-1.09]; p=0.325 for microbiological recurrence, and 1.01 [0.82-1.25]; p=0.912 for glomerulonephritis or hematuria, suggesting comparable results in penicillin group. These outcomes were also comparable between the first- and third-generation cephalosporin groups.

CONCLUSION: The study findings indicated penicillin or amoxicillin should be the first-line treatment for streptococcal pharyngitis and tonsillitis. While cephalosporins were associated with fewer recurrent infection, a judicious use of the third-generation cephalosporin is required in specific cases where prevention of recurrence is required from an antimicrobial stewardship perspective.

articles.title: Democratizing AI-assisted bedside echocardiography: Why governance and workflow matter more than the machine.
External Ventricular Drainage for Refractory Intracranial Hypertension in Traumatic Brain Injury: Efficacy, Safety, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is commonly used to manage refractory intracranial hypertension following traumatic brain injury (TBI), yet its efficacy, timing, and prognostic value remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term efficacy of EVD in controlling intracranial hypertension in TBI patients.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study including consecutive adult patients with TBI who underwent EVD placement for refractory intracranial hypertension between 2020 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, radiological, surgical, and ICP data were collected. Trauma severity was assessed using the ISS and the SOFA score. EVD efficacy was defined as a sustained reduction in mean ICP below 20 mmHg for at least 24 hours. Functional outcome was assessed at 1 year using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS).

RESULTS: Fifty-three patients were included (51±18 years; 75% male). Median ICP significantly decreased after EVD placement (30 [25-35] vs. 15 [10-35] mmHg; p<0.01). Sustained ICP control was achieved within the first 24 hours in 25 patients (47%), whereas 28 (53%) did not reach control, including 8 patients (29%) with transient improvement. Patients with uncontrolled ICP had higher pre-EVD ICP values and greater injury severity scores. Normal basal cisterns were more frequent in the controlled group. One-year mortality was 70%, and 32% of the patients with controlled ICP had a GOS 4 at 12 months. EVD-related complications occurred in four patients (8%).

CONCLUSION: EVD significantly reduces ICP in selected TBI patients, but sustained control occurs in fewer than half of cases and appears associated with baseline injury severity. Prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Computer Vision for Postural Assessment in Brain Injury Rehabilitation.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and preliminarily evaluate a clinician-led, computer vision (CV)-based system for point-of-care postural assessment in people with acquired brain injury (ABI) undergoing inpatient rehabilitation.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study incorporating clinician-led co-innovation, usability testing, feasibility assessment, clinical utility analysis, and analytical validation against three-dimensional motion capture.

SETTING: Tertiary inpatient neurorehabilitation hospital.

PARTICIPANTS: Rehabilitation clinicians (n=10), individuals with ABI (n=20; 60% female; age 45.0 ± 17.7 years), and neurologically intact controls (n=12).

METHODS: Occupational therapists, physical therapists, engineers, and rehabilitation scientists co-developed a markerless CV workflow for seated and standing postural assessment. Usability, feasibility, therapy-related change, analytical validity, and associations with clinician-reported measures were evaluated.

RESULTS: Clinicians reported excellent usability (System Usability Scale: 85.3 ± 12.3). All participants with ABI completed testing without adverse events, and all posture metrics were successfully acquired. During inpatient neurorehabilitation, seated cervical lateral flexion (β = -0.084°/day, 95% CI: -0.163 to -0.005, p = 0.037) and standing trunk lateral flexion (β = -0.096°/day, 95% CI: -0.152 to -0.040, p = 0.0008) decreased significantly over time, indicating improvements in postural alignment. CV metrics correlated with clinician-rated postural abnormalities, including unsupported sitting trunk displacement (ρ = 0.531, p = 0.023), pelvic displacement (ρ = 0.501, p = 0.034), and head/neck displacement (ρ = 0.482, p = 0.043). Agreement with motion capture was strong for cervical and trunk lateral flexion (ICC[A,1] = 0.83 for both).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-led co-innovation produced a usable, feasible, and clinically meaningful CV tool that captured therapy-related postural change and aligned with clinician-reported impairments in ABI.

articles.title: Targeted exome sequencing Delineates Subtype-Specific genetic Architecture and BMPR2-Associated Prognosis in Chinese paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) exhibits greater genetic enrichment in children than in adults; however, genotype-phenotype correlations in Chinese paediatric PAH remain poorly defined. We performed targeted exome sequencing of 16 PAH-associated genes in 154 children with PAH at Beijing Anzhen Hospital (2010-2023) and interpreted variants under a calibrated, point-based ACMG/AMP framework. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants were identified in 38 patients (24.7 %): 23 BMPR2 (60.5 %), 7 TBX4 (18.4 %), 5 ACVRL1 (13.2 %), 2 SOX17 (5.3 %), and 1 GDF2 (2.6 %). Thirty variants were upgraded from the baseline automated InterVar classification, including five BMPR2 missense variants reclassified through the PP2 criterion. An additional 42 patients (27.3 %) harboured variants of uncertain significance (VUS) only. P/LP carriers presented with more severe baseline haemodynamics than benign or likely benign (B/LB) carriers, with higher pulmonary vascular resistance indices and lower cardiac indices. Among the 43 patients with available follow-up data, P/LP carriers exhibited significantly worse event-free survival than B/LB carriers and non-carriers (10-year estimate 47.7 % vs. 78.5 %; HR 3.70, 95 % CI 1.04-13.20; log-rank p = 0.0309), an effect largely attributable to BMPR2 variants (HR 4.83, 95 % CI 1.29-18.04). In contrast, VUS carriers resembled B/LB carriers and non-carriers (HR 0.84, p = 0.8436). Thus, the calibrated variant-classification framework substantially increased the diagnostic yield in Chinese paediatric PAH, uncovered an under-recognised contribution of BMPR2 missense variants, and enabled prognostic stratification across the three-tier pathogenicity spectrum.

articles.title: Integrative post-GWAS analysis prioritizes interferon-linked regulatory and splicing-associated variants at the TNFSF10 locus in systemic lupus erythematosus.
articles.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a genetically complex autoimmune disease characterized by interferon-driven immune dysregulation. Although TNFSF10/TRAIL has been implicated in immune regulation, genetic and transcript-level features linking interferon-related susceptibility loci to TNFSF10 remain unclear. Here, we performed an integrative post-GWAS analysis using SLE GWAS summary statistics from the Taiwan Precision Medicine Initiative, combined with pathway enrichment, motif annotation, population-specific linkage disequilibrium, GTEx eQTL/sQTL profiling, public SLE RNA-seq, GWAS-QTL colocalization, and chromatin regulatory datasets. Interferon-related genes IRF5, IRF8, and STAT4 showed putative regulatory links to TNFSF10 and population-dependent allele-frequency and linkage-disequilibrium patterns. Public SLE RNA-seq supported increased TNFSF10 expression in SLE. Downstream TNFSF10 variants, particularly near terminal intronic and 3'UTR regions, were associated predominantly with splicing QTL signals in immune-relevant tissues and overlapped with candidate regulatory annotations. Together, these findings support an integrative genomic framework for prioritizing candidate regulatory and splicing-associated features at the TNFSF10 locus in SLE.

articles.title: Randomized controlled trial evaluating a mHealth intervention to optimize self- and social-regulation for emerging adults with type 1 diabetes (FAMS-T1D): protocol and lessons learned.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emerging adults (EAs) with type 1 diabetes (T1D) are at high-risk for high distress, high glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and inconsistent use of continuous glucose monitors (CGMs). EAs are developing self-regulation skills needed to manage T1D and social-regulation skills needed to get support. The Family/Friend Activation to Motivate Self-Care intervention was adapted for T1D (FAMS-T1D) to support EAs' self- and social-regulation needs.

METHODS: FAMS-T1D involves 1) phone-based coaching to improve diabetes management goal pursuit and manage social relationships, 2) text messaging to facilitate goal attainment and support, and 3) optional text messaging to a support person (SP) to enhance social support. In a multisite randomized controlled trial (RCT), we are testing the efficacy of a 6-month intervention (compared to enhanced treatment as usual who receive educational materials and HbA1c testing) and evaluating sustained effects at 9- and 12-months in a diverse sample of EAs and SPs. We evaluate intervention effects on HbA1c, self-management, and diabetes distress and whether the effects occur through improvements in EAs' self-regulation and social-regulation. Among participants using CGM, we explore the effect of the intervention on time in range and effects of the intervention on characteristics of CGM use.

RESULTS: Recruitment began April 2023 and ended on time in October 2025 (N = 256 EAs, 185 SPs). We share lessons learned about recruiting EAs for a mHealth intervention RCT.

DISCUSSION: FAMS-T1D has the potential for high impact and reach to help EAs with T1D develop skills for this high-risk time of development.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05820477, NCT05854069.

articles.title: Global carbon isotope variability of commercial plastics: implications for microplastic source attribution and environmental forensics.
articles.abstract: Microplastic source attribution remains a major challenge because conventional analytical techniques primarily identify polymer types while providing limited information on the origin and environmental history of plastic materials. This study evaluates the potential and limitations of stable carbon isotope analysis (δ13C) for tracing common plastic polymers at the global scale. A total of 460 commercial plastic samples, including 233 polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles and 227 polyethylene (PE) caps, were collected from 59 countries across six continents and analysed by elemental analyzer - isotope ratio mass spectrometry (EA-IRMS). A preliminary thermal additive removal experiment showed systematic but minor isotopic shifts (∼0.3‰ for PET and ∼0.5‰ for PE), indicating a minor influence of additives on bulk δ13C values. Among petroleum-derived samples, PE exhibited a broad δ13C range from -35.2‰ to -24.0‰, with significant interregional variability and country-averaged values ranging from -33.9 ± 0.1‰ (Tunisia) to -25.9 ± 0.1‰ (New Zealand). Continental-scale comparisons revealed significant differences between several regions, consistent with regional differences in petrochemical feedstocks and production pathways. In contrast, PET displayed a narrower δ13C range (-33.1‰ to -26.2‰) and no significant interregional differences, consistent with a more homogeneous and globally integrated production system. Overall, the results demonstrate that stable carbon isotopes provide useful first-order constraints on broad PE source domains, while also highlighting important limitations related to overlapping isotopic domains and the globalization of polymer supply chains. Stable isotope analysis therefore represents a promising complementary tool for improving microplastic source attribution within multi-tracer environmental forensic frameworks.

articles.title: Understanding the perceived impact of a peer-led epilepsy self-management intervention in Uganda: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how adults with epilepsy in Uganda experienced epilepsy self-management, stigma, and care following participation in a peer-led intervention (SMART-U) compared to enhanced treatment as usual (ETAU).

METHODS: This qualitative study was embedded within an ongoing randomized controlled trial at two university neurology clinics. A purposive subsample from both study arms completed semi-structured interviews at 13 (n = 16) and 24 weeks post-intervention (n = 16). Interviews explored perceived benefits and challenges of care, self-management behaviors, stigma and recommendations for improvement. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Four themes emerged: barriers to self-management, self-management behaviors and attitudes, participant perspectives on care, and facilitators of self-management. Participants in both groups described significant structural and social barriers, including stigma, limited support, and challenges accessing care. However, SMART-U participants more frequently reported increased confidence, engagement in proactive self-management (e.g., stress management, planning around seizures), improved communication with providers, and greater ability to cope with stigma. In contrast, ETAU participants more often characterized epilepsy care as provider-driven, with fewer changes in attitudes or behaviors. Over time, SMART-U participants demonstrated clearer shifts toward self-efficacy and a more reflective understanding of epilepsy.

CONCLUSIONS: Peer-led self-management support may enhance engagement, coping, and self-efficacy among people with epilepsy in resource-limited settings. Addressing stigma and strengthening social and healthcare support may be critical for improving outcomes in low-middle income countries.

articles.title: Psychosocial difficulties in children of parents with epilepsy: A pilot case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that may affect family functioning. Although the psychosocial impact on children of parents with several chronic medical and neurological disorders has been studied, a notable gap remains regarding epilepsy. This pilot study aimed to examine psychosocial outcomes in children aged 6-17 years whose parents have epilepsy and to explore emotional and behavioral difficulties within a multifactorial framework.

METHODOLOGY: This observational pilot case-control study was conducted between 2023 and 2025 at neurology departments in Giresun and Erzurum. The epilepsy group (n = 45) was compared with a control group (n = 48) recruited from the same hospitals for non neurological reasons. Assessments included the Conners Parent Rating Scale (CPRS), Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), and Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), analyzed as continuous measures. Small sample size and risk of model overfitting precluded multivariable covariate adjustment; the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate procedure was applied to account for multiple testing.

RESULTS: Children of parents with epilepsy had higher rates of chronic medical conditions and ADHD diagnoses than controls. They also had higher SDQ emotional symptoms and hyperactivity/inattention scores, as well as higher CPRS total and problem related subscale scores. No significant between group differences were observed in total SDQ or PSS scores. In exploratory analyses by parental gender, children of fathers with epilepsy had higher SDQ total, emotional, and hyperactivity/inattention scores, as well as higher CPRS total and executive functioning scores. Fathers with epilepsy also reported higher PSS scores than mothers with epilepsy. Longer breastfeeding duration was inversely associated with CPRS total, hyperactivity/impulsivity, conduct, and peer relationship scores.

CONCLUSION: Children of parents with epilepsy showed differences in selected emotional and behavioral domains rather than global psychosocial impairment. Exploratory findings related to parental gender and breastfeeding duration should be interpreted cautiously. The small, non probability sample, baseline group differences, inability to control for key epilepsy specific clinical characteristics because of sample size constraints, limited assessment of epilepsy related factors, and potential residual confounding limit causal interpretation and generalizability. These preliminary, hypothesis generating findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies incorporating multiple informants and family related factors.

articles.title: Temporal trends and compartment-specific behaviour of 137Cs across five decades of environmental monitoring in tropical Malaysia.
articles.abstract: Long-term environmental surveillance of radiocesium (137Cs) in tropical regions provides important baseline data for assessing radionuclide behaviour under low-background conditions, yet multi-compartment synthesis studies from Southeast Asia remain scarce. This study presents a retrospective analysis of 137Cs activity concentrations across five environmental compartments: seawater (n = 609), soil (n = 483), sediment (n = 474), biota (n = 114), and airborne particulates (n = 20 seasonal records), in Malaysian environments spanning 1972-2024. Censored observations below analytical detection limits were treated using Regression on Order Statistics (ROS), with Limit of Detection (LOD) substitution sensitivity assessed under three scenarios (Xi = 0, LOD/2, LOD). A complementary statistical framework combining Mann-Kendall (MK) trend analysis, Pettitt change-point detection, cumulative sum (CUSUM) diagnostics, relative detectability metrics (SNR), and segmented regression was applied to characterise temporal structure and compartment-specific behaviour. A statistically significant monotonic decline was identified in seawater only (τ = -0.547, p = 0.002), however, a candidate change-point at 1995 (p = 0.026) was excluded from primary inference owing to a 9-year sampling gap (1987-1994; Table S3). Soil and biota exhibited declining tendencies (τ = -0.167 and -0.500, respectively) that did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05). Sediment results were excluded from trend inference as the direction of the apparent trend reversed between LOD substitution scenarios, indicating that the result is driven by the high proportion of censored values (74.7%) rather than the quantified data. Airborne observations (85% non-detect) were reported descriptively only. Indicative effective half-lives of 137Cs were estimated across all four compartments under a sensitivity analysis spanning five historically motivated starting years (Table S2). Seawater yields T½ (eff) = 27.7-30.8 yr across the primary fits, bracketing the physical half-life (30.17 yr), while biota yields T½ (eff) ≈ 12-19 yr, consistent with biological turnover superimposed on radioactive decay. Soil and sediment estimates are sensitive to starting year and are considered indicative only. Signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) were below 1 for soil (0.455), sediment (0.060), and biota (0.260); seawater showed marginal detectability (SNR = 1.35, consistent across all LOD substitution scenarios), reflecting the long-term declining trend rather than a post-2011 enrichment signal. Statistical inference is subject to inherent limitations of the analytical framework: the MK test has reduced power for episodic signals and censored-data-rich series; the Pettitt test assumes a single dominant change-point; and CUSUM results are treated as exploratory given irregular sampling intervals and high censoring rates in several compartments. The results document baseline temporal trajectories of 137Cs in a tropical low-background environment and highlight compartment-specific differences in temporal sensitivity, data sufficiency, and inferential reliability as central challenges for long-term radionuclide surveillance in tropical radioecology.

articles.title: Longitudinal assessment of pulmonary morphological patterns using structured serial chest radiography in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portable chest radiography is routinely available in mechanically ventilated ICU patients, yet serial findings are rarely standardized. We evaluated whether a structured morphological classification of serial chest radiographs could describe early radiographic evolution during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and explored associations with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Single-centre retrospective cohort of 57 adults receiving IMV ≥48 h in the ICU of Hospital General IESS Babahoyo, Ecuador (2018-2019). Radiographs from Days 1-5 of IMV were classified into 13 predefined predominant morphological categories; radiological change was defined as any modification of the predominant pattern relative to baseline. IMV duration, ICU length of stay, and mortality were analysed using an exploratory logistic regression model.

RESULTS: Radiographs were available for 57 patients on Days 1-2, 46 on Day 3, 39 on Day 4, and 34 on Day 5. Normal predominant patterns decreased from 52.6% at baseline to 14.7% on Day 5, while alveolar patterns increased from 10.5% to 35.3%. Thirty-two patients (56.1%) had documented radiological pattern change, first identified at a median of Day 2. Patients with documented change had longer IMV duration (5.5 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001) and ICU stay (8 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001). In the exploratory adjusted model, IMV duration was associated with documented change (adjusted OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.0-1.6; p = 0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: Structured serial chest radiography converted routine ICU images into comparable longitudinal morphological variables. Documented radiological change was common and frequently early; its association with longer IMV duration should be interpreted as concurrent and exploratory. Prospective multicentre studies are needed.

articles.title: Embracing uncertainty in refractory septic shock.
Valorisation of PET-rich mixed plastic waste using a cascading concept involving selective ammonolysis and catalytic pyrolysis.
articles.abstract: We report a cascading valorisation strategy for real polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-rich waste streams, combining selective ammonolysis of PET with catalytic pyrolysis of the non-PET residue. In this approach, PET-rich packaging waste is treated with ammonia in ethylene glycol to produce terephthaldiamide (TDA), while the remaining polyolefin (PO)-rich residue is subsequently upgraded to benzene, toluene, xylene (BTX), and light olefins over H-ZSM-5 catalyst. TDA is a valuable aromatic diamide and a potential precursor to p-phenylene diamine, a monomer used in the production of poly(p-phenyleneterephthalamide) (PPTA). For post-consumer PET trays, ammonolysis at 5 bar NH3, and 100 °C for 8 h, followed by a downstream separation procedure, resulted in an almost quantitative conversion of PET, yielding pure TDA as small crystals in 74 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content in the feed. The residue (mostly polyolefins) was converted to BTX (5 wt% on residue), and propene/butenes (19 wt%, on residue) using a catalytic in situ pyrolysis approach with H-ZSM-5 at 550 °C. The same strategy was applied to a PET-enriched, DKR-350 mixed-plastic packaging fraction, affording TDA in 71 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content, while catalytic pyrolysis of the residue produced BTX (3 wt%) and propene/isobutene (4 wt%) based on the residue. These results demonstrate that real PET-rich mixed plastic waste streams can be selectively upgraded into valuable aromatic diamide while retaining the non-PET fraction as a feedstock for petrochemical intermediates.

articles.title: Role of Gut Microbiota-derived Metabolites in the Pathogenesis and Progression of Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely linked with significant comorbidities and mortality. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived metabolites play a vital role in the initiation and progression of MASLD. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the role of these metabolites in the pathogenesis and progression of MASLD, including steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

METHODS: This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting of Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed/Medline, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included observational, interventional, animal, and in vitro mechanistic studies. Human observational studies were evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale, randomized controlled trials using the Cochrane risk of bias-2 (ROB-2) tool, and in vitro studies using a qualitative mechanistic approach. The risk of bias was assessed using the Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation (SYRCLE) tool for animal studies. Results were synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity in the data. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261293786).

RESULTS: A total of 28 studies were included. Alterations in bile acids, ethanol, fatty acids, and other compounds, such as indole derivatives, were associated with fibrosis, steatosis, steatohepatitis, and HCC. Bile acid levels vary with disease stage, while ethanol was reported to be generally high across studies. Different short-chain fatty acids have various roles in MASLD pathogenesis. Indole derivatives are capable of attenuating hepatic steatosis and inflammation. Altering the gut microbiota is also known to play a vital role in reducing the progression of liver cancer.

CONCLUSION: The gut microbiota-derived metabolites, particularly conjugated bile acids and endogenous ethanol, are highly promising and may play a fundamental role in the development and progression of MASLD, including steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and HCC. Further high-quality, well-designed studies in humans are warranted to evaluate their precise role and validate their use in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Endoscopic Prediction of Helicobacter pylori Infection: A High-accuracy Optic Evaluation.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is one of the most prevalent chronic bacterial infections worldwide. Literature describes several endoscopic signs that might predict H. pylori status. However, random biopsies according to Sydney system are still widely used for its determination. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of endoscopic characteristics in predicting H. pylori infection.

METHODS: This is a monocentric prospective study including all consecutive patients who underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in one-year timeframe. In each procedure regular arrangement of collecting venules (RAC), fundic gland polyps (FGPs), linear streaks, hematin spots, diffuse redness and intestinal metaplasia were described. H. pylori infection was histologically investigated.

RESULTS: A total of 421 patients were enrolled (F: 222, 52.7%, median age 54.1). The presence of RAC both in greater and in lesser curvature and FGPs were significantly associated with lower prevalence of H. pylori infection, by contrast, diffuse redness was associated with a higher prevalence (p<0.0001). Considering the interaction effect by the optical evidence of intestinal metaplasia, RAC and FGPs maintained their significance with an OR of 0.05 (0.02-0.13) and 0.11 (0.03-0.53), respectively. All the characteristics showed a high negative predictive value (>90%). AUROC of the whole diagnostic model was 0.893 (95%CI: 0.854-0.932).

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed endoscopic assessment has a high predictive capability for H. pylori infection. Notably, the presence of RAC and FGPs emerges as important and reliable indicators of H. pylori-negative status. These findings may represent a first step toward avoiding unnecessary biopsies, promoting a more accurate endoscopic examination centered on meticulous assessment of gastric mucosa.

articles.title: Genetic Features in a Case Series of Gastro-entero-pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Early diagnosis and the size of gastro-entero-pancreatic (GEP) neuroendocrine tumors (NET) represent prognostic factors in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1). We aimed to present the genetic features and clinical aspects of a case series of NET patients investigated at the National Institute of Endocrinology C.I.Parhon, Bucharest, Romania.

METHODS: 12 patients with NET and associated pathologies (from 9 families) were monitored during 2021-2025. The germline variants of the MEN1 gene were detected by Sanger sequencing and for two patients, next-generation sequencing analysis was used with a clinical exome kit (TruSight One sequencing panel, Illumina, San Diego, CA). The diagnosis of NET was confirmed by histopathologic analysis. Somatostatin receptor status was verified by immunohistochemistry on tumor samples as well as by functional imaging, in vivo.

RESULTS: In our group of NET patients, five patients presented a MEN1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant, one patient had two heterozygous variants of BLM gene suggesting Bloom syndrome diagnosis, and one patient had a BRCA1 variant; five patients were negative for germline clinically relevant variants for NET using aforementioned methods. According to the RECIST1.1 criteria at 1 year after the initiation of therapy, 2/7 presented stable disease, 1/7 partial response and 4/7 progressive disease, and death occurring in 2 cases. In our study, 7 clinically relevant variants were detected: two classified as pathogenic: one nonsense mutation (MEN1: c.778C>T, p.Gln260*) and one heterozygous large deletion in exon 7 (MEN1:c.928_974del, p.Lys310Trpfs*41), three likely pathogenic: MEN1:c.639C>A, p.Ala213=, MEN1:c.520_521insCA, p.His174ProfsTer12, BLM: c.1237_1240del, p.Glu413*, and two were described as variants with uncertain significance (VUS) (BLM:c.98+6T>G, BRCA1: c.4485-10A>G).

CONCLUSIONS: Advances in molecular medicine techniques, with the discovery of new genes, open the field to precision medicine, both for the prognosis of patients with a NET as well as the options of response to specific treatments.

articles.title: Early Hepatic Decompensation after ERCP in Patients with Cirrhosis: A Single‑center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis frequently require endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), yet the burden of early hepatic decompensation after ERCP remains insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including 67 adults with established cirrhosis who underwent therapeutic ERCP between January 2021 and December 2023. Hepatic decompensation events [ascites, hepatorenal syndrome/acute kidney injury (HRS-AKI), hepatic encephalopathy, variceal bleeding, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis] were assessed before ERCP and at 72 hours post-procedure during index admission. Ascites was systematically evaluated by ultrasound in all patients. Paired changes in Child-Pugh points and MELD-Na were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and paired categorical outcomes using exact McNemar tests. Predictors of post-ERCP decompensation were explored using univariable logistic regression followed by a reduced exploratory multivariable model.

RESULTS: Mean age was 65.2±11.0 years and 73.1% were male. Child-Pugh class A/B/C distribution was 19/35/13, with a median model for end-stage liver disease sodium (MELD-Na) of 13.0 [9.5-16.5]. Any hepatic decompensation was present in 23.9% of patients before ERCP and increased to 44.8% at 72 hours. Child-Pugh points increased from 7 (6-9) to 8 (7-9.5) (p<0.001), and MELD-Na from 13 (9.25-16.75) to 15 (10.00-18.00) (p<0.001). Ascites (23.9% to 38.8%, p=0.006) and HRS-AKI (1.5% to 10.4%, p=0.031) increased significantly. Baseline Child-Pugh score remained independently associated with 72-hour decompensation after adjustment for baseline decompensation status.

CONCLUSIONS: Early new or worsening hepatic decompensation within 72 hours after ERCP is frequent in patients with cirrhosis. Baseline liver severity should inform peri-procedural risk stratification and early post-procedure monitoring.

articles.title: Correction to "Fetal Sylvian Fissure Maturation in Congenital Heart Disease and Its Relation to Expected Brain Arterial Oxygen Saturation: A Longitudinal Study".
Cerebral Safety of Two Pulsed Field Ablation Workflows for Pulmonary Vein Isolation: Results From the Randomized TWOSOME MRI Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on silent cerebral events/lesions (SCE/SCL) following pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) are limited. This study aimed to assess the incidence of SCE/SCL using cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI) in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients undergoing PVI with two distinct PFA systems and workflows.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center TWOSOME MRI substudy, patients with paroxysmal AF were randomized 1:1 to single-shot or single-tip PFA. Single-shot PVI was performed using a pentaspline PFA catheter (single-transseptal access, PV-angiography, no 3D mapping) and single-tip PVI using a PFA generator with a focal ablation catheter (double-transseptal access, 3D mapping). A predefined consecutive cohort underwent 1.5-T cMRI 24 h after the procedure. SCE were defined as acute cMRI-detected lesions resolving on 6-week follow-up cMRI, and SCL as persistent lesions. Baseline characteristics, neurological symptoms, procedural data, and cMRI findings were assessed.

RESULTS: Fifty patients underwent cMRI (25 per group). Acute SCE were detected in 3/50 patients (6%; 95% CI 1.3-16.5), with 1/25 (4%) in the single-shot group and 2/25 (8%) in the single-tip group (p = 1.00). All SCE resolved on follow-up imaging, with no evidence of persistent SCL. One symptomatic stroke occurred in the single-shot group, unrelated to PFA, and was attributed to air embolization during transseptal puncture. No permanent neurological deficits occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cMRI study, both PFA workflows showed a low incidence of SCE without evidence of SCL or PFA-related neurological complications. Larger studies are required to compare cerebral safety profiles of PFA technologies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07175727 (clinicaltrials.gov).

articles.title: Nanocarriers for On-Demand Insulin Aspart Delivery: Integrated Control of Postprandial and Basal Glycemia in Type 2 Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus demands coordinated control of fasting and postprandial glycemia, and current clinical rapid-acting insulin aspart (IAsp) suffers from short action duration and hypoglycemia-related risks. We describe a glucose-sensitive insulin delivery system based on rigid amphiphilic methoxy poly(ethylene glycol)-polysalicylate (mPEG-PSA) copolymers synthesized by controlled ring-opening polymerization of salicylic acid O-carboxyanhydride, with a structure substantially different from conventional aliphatic polyesters. The 100-150 nm nanoparticles possessed favorable colloidal stability, ∼85% encapsulation efficiency and ∼20% drug loading, and IAsp bioactivity was well preserved. In vitro release followed glucose-dependent kinetics tuned by PSA hydrophobicity. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, IAsp@mPEG-PSA restored euglycemia within 0.5 h and maintained normoglycemia for up to 10 h without hypoglycemia, outperforming free IAsp and mPEG-PLA formulations in this animal model. The nanosystem realized glucose-activated on-demand insulin release to suppress repeated glucose spikes, accomplishing combined postprandial and basal glycemic regulation in rodents. This study presents mPEG-PSA as a promising polymeric candidate for glucose-responsive insulin delivery.

articles.title: Hirudin Extraction of Iranian Leech Saliva by Freezing and Lyophilization Methods.
articles.abstract: Leech saliva contains a diverse array of bioactive compounds, most notably hirudin, a potent natural thrombin inhibitor. Despite the clinical utility of hirudotherapy, inherent risks such as localized infection, uncontrolled hemorrhage, and leech migration limit its widespread application. To overcome these limitations, this study presents a refined extraction, partial purification, and stabilization protocol for hirudin-containing salivary extract derived from the Iranian leech, Hirudo orientalis. Saliva was harvested using 0.001 M arginine in 0.15 M saline under controlled temperatures (23 °C vs. 37-40 °C) and subsequently stored at 4 °C. The crude extract underwent fractionation/purification via centrifugation, followed by stabilization with sucrose, fructose, and mannitol, and final lyophilization (freeze-drying). Optimal extraction efficiency was observed at 37-40 °C. The short-term stability (44 days at 4 °C) and antibacterial efficacy of the resulting lyophilizate were evaluated using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) against authentic reference parameters and Brain Heart Infusion (BHI) broth assays. The findings demonstrate that this stabilization matrix preserves the short-term chromatographic profile and in-vitro biological activity of the salivary protein extract, providing a preliminary foundation for future in-vivo evaluation and development of standardized leech-derived biotherapeutics.

articles.title: Combined assessment of skeletal muscle mass and quality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a longitudinal study of physical function and complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Longitudinal changes in skeletal muscle mass and quality after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation remain unclear. This study used bioelectrical impedance analysis to assess these changes and their associations with physical function, infection, and acute graft-versus-host disease.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 111 adults who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Skeletal muscle mass index and phase angle, an indicator of muscle quality, were assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis before transplantation, 4 weeks after transplantation, and at discharge. Patients were assigned to four combined categories based on normal or low muscle mass and quality. Outcomes included 6 min walk distance, infection, and acute graft-versus-host disease.

RESULTS: Skeletal muscle mass index and phase angle decreased significantly after transplantation (p < 0.05), with phase angle declining earlier and more markedly. At discharge, 53.1% of patients were classified as Category 3. At 4 weeks, the decline in 6 min walk distance was significantly greater in Categories 2 and 3 than in Categories 0 and 1. In multivariable analyses, Categories 2 and 3 were independently associated with infection, whereas Category 3 was independently associated with acute graft-versus-host disease.

CONCLUSION: Skeletal muscle mass and quality deteriorated after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and low muscle quality was more closely associated with adverse outcomes. Pre-transplant bioelectrical impedance analysis-based assessment of muscle quality may help identify patients at risk of infection, acute graft-versus-host disease, and delayed physical recovery and may support further evaluation of prehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Anomalous papillary muscle insertion beyond hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: insights from reported cases.
articles.abstract: Anomalous insertion of the papillary muscle (APM) into the mitral valve leaflet is a rare congenital abnormality of the subvalvular apparatus. Most published reports describe direct papillary muscle insertion in association with obstructive physiology, particularly in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), where it contributes to left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and systolic anterior motion (SAM)-related mitral regurgitation. However, similar papillary muscle-leaflet continuity may also serve as a primary mechanical determinant of valve dysfunction in patients without a clinical diagnosis of HCM. This review synthesizes published reports of APM insertion across different clinical contexts and interprets them within a mechanism-oriented framework based on LVOT dynamics and functional role of the papillary muscle rather than disease labels. Available reports indicate a heterogeneous clinical spectrum in which hemodynamic manifestations reflect interactions among papillary muscle anatomy, mitral valve mechanics, and ventricular geometry. Although LVOT obstruction remains an important presentation, many cases show predominant mitral regurgitation due to leaflet tethering or, less commonly, functional mitral stenosis from impaired diastolic leaflet opening. These phenotypes arise from subvalvular mechanical restriction rather than primary leaflet pathology. Echocardiography plays a central role in diagnosis, yet APM insertion may be overlooked if assessment focuses primarily on leaflet morphology or Doppler findings. Transesophageal echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide complementary anatomical detail for accurate characterization and surgical planning. Greater awareness of this geometry-based interaction and adoption of a structured imaging approach may reduce diagnostic oversight and improve decision-making in patients with atypical mitral valve dysfunction.

articles.title: Prognostic associations between patient-reported outcomes and progression-free and overall survival in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%: results from the RATIONALE-305 trial.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In RATIONALE-305, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival (OS) versus placebo plus chemotherapy in advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC) with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor area positivity (TAP) score ≥ 5% and in all patients. Here, we present a three-component joint model (JM) developed to evaluate associations between patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and risk of progression-free survival (PFS) and OS events.

METHODS: Longitudinal PRO data were analyzed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22. The JM linked: (1) a linear mixed model (LMM) for change from baseline in PRO scores; (2) a Cox model for time to recurrent symptomatic deterioration (RS-D); and (3) a Cox model to evaluate the RS-D event frailty prediction of PFS and OS.

RESULTS: 475 patients in the PD-L1 ≥ 5% subgroup (tislelizumab + chemotherapy, n = 238; placebo + chemotherapy, n = 237) were evaluated. In PFS and OS LMMs, tislelizumab + chemotherapy versus placebo + chemotherapy was associated with improved GHS/QoL (global health status/quality of life) (p = 0.01) and reduced dietary restrictions (p = 0.05). In the OS LMM, tislelizumab + chemotherapy was associated with reduced upper GI symptoms (p = 0.01) and reductions in dietary restrictions (p = 0.02). RS-D in GHS/QoL, pain, and dietary restrictions were leading predictors of PFS risk. Across all QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22 domains, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly reduced the risk of progression or death (PFS HRs 0.55-0.65; 35-45% reduction) and death (OS HRs 0.65-0.73; 27-35% reduction); all p ≤ 0.01.

CONCLUSION: PROs have significant prognostic value for disease progression and survival in patients with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%.

REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT03777657 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov ).

articles.title: A mechanistic PK/PD model of fentanyl overdose and intranasal naloxone rescue incorporating receptor-level competition.
articles.abstract: To develop and evaluate a PK/PD model that mechanistically describes the competitive interaction between intravenous (IV) fentanyl and intranasal (IN) naloxone at brain μ-opioid receptors (MORs) and simulates reversal of respiratory depression. A compartmental PK/PD model incorporating central, peripheral, brain and nasal compartments was parameterized sequentially using human plasma concentration, PET MOR-occupancy, and controlled isohypercapnic ventilation data, supplemented by literature-derived constraints where direct estimation was not supported. Fentanyl-MOR binding and release were modeled kinetically, whereas naloxone binding was represented by a rapid-equilibrium relationship. A 1,000-member virtual ensemble was used to propagate parameter uncertainty, and Sobol global sensitivity analysis evaluated determinants of ventilation recovery. The model reproduced the component clinical datasets used for calibration and simulated rapid ventilation recovery after IN naloxone. Simulations indicated that the apparent nasal-to-brain pathway was an important contributor to early rescue, whereas the systemic pathway contributed minimally during the first minutes after dosing. In nominal simulations, recovery began when the free brain naloxone:fentanyl molar concentration ratio reached approximately 0.063. Sobol analysis showed that fentanyl MOR affinity and brain disposition dominated very early recovery, while naloxone MOR affinity and apparent nasal-to-brain allocation became increasingly influential over the subsequent 10-15 minutes. This PK/PD framework links drug disposition, receptor competition and ventilation response in a unified model. It provides a mechanistic platform for evaluating naloxone dose, repeat-dosing, and formulation strategies while explicitly accounting for parameter uncertainty and the limitations of controlled isohypercapnic calibration data.

articles.title: Trilobatin attenuates allergic airway inflammation via multi-target suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-3 signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic airway disease characterized by persistent inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and airway remodeling, largely driven by type 2 immune responses. Trilobatin (TLB), a flavonoid derived from Lithocarpus polystachyus (Sweet Tea), exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its therapeutic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms in asthma remain insufficiently elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the potential targets and mechanisms underlying the anti-asthmatic effects of TLB.

METHODS AND RESULTS: An integrated approach combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation was employed to investigate the mechanisms of TLB. Candidate TLB targets were identified and intersected with asthma-associated genes to construct a protein-protein interaction network, followed by functional enrichment analyses. Molecular docking highlighted caspase-3 (CASP3) and matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) as potential key targets with favorable binding affinities. These findings were further investigated in a house dust mite-induced murine model of asthma. TLB treatment alleviated airway inflammation and reduced proinflammatory cytokine production. Mechanistic analyses further indicated that TLB inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and CASP3-associated apoptotic signaling in lung tissue.

CONCLUSION: TLB alleviates allergic airway inflammation in experimental asthma, potentially through the coordinated regulation of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and CASP3-associated apoptotic signaling. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-asthmatic effects of TLB and support its further investigation as a potential therapeutic candidate for asthma.

articles.title: Thiopurines and vitamin K antagonist resistance: warfarin inhibits thiopurine S-methyltransferase.
articles.abstract: Vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) inhibit vitamin K epoxide reductase, reducing the synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors and increasing bleeding risk. Thiopurines, such as azathioprine (AZA) and 6-mercaptopurine (MP), are immunosuppressants commonly used in inflammatory bowel disease and other immune-mediated disorders. Case reports suggest a dose-dependent relationship between thiopurines and reduced INR levels, potentially contributing to VKA resistance. We present a case of a female patient with Sjögren's disease, Factor V Leiden thrombophilia and intermediate thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) metabolism who experienced VKA resistance associated with high 6-thioguanine nucleotide (6-TGN) levels. Despite phenprocoumon therapy, therapeutic INR levels were not maintained after multiple higher dosages (37.5 mg per week) of phenprocoumon which were much higher than patients' regular dose (15 mg/week). After reducing AZA dosage, her 6-TGN levels decreased significantly, and therapeutic INR was restored, suggesting a direct relationship between elevated 6-TGN levels and VKA resistance. An in vitro inhibition assay showed that warfarin inhibits TPMT, which could have contributed to higher 6-TGN levels. Potential mechanisms for thiopurine-induced VKA resistance include increased prothrombin activity, but may also theoretically be caused by alterations in gut microbiota reducing vitamin K synthesis, and interference with enzymes like VKORC1. Literature highlights cases where thiopurines lowered INR, leading to thrombotic events, particularly in female patients, suggesting a potential hormonal influence. Other cases also described that stopping thiopurines led to high INR levels, which led to bleeding. This case underscores the need for therapeutic drug monitoring in patients using both VKAs and thiopurines. Gender-specific factors may further contribute to VKA resistance and warrant additional research. Clinicians should remain vigilant in managing this complex interaction to optimize patient outcomes.

articles.title: Outcome-specific associations of remnant cholesterol with myocardial infarction and stroke across traditional risk factor burden.
articles.abstract: Remnant cholesterol (RC) is considered a contributor to residual cardiovascular risk, but whether its associations with specific cardiovascular outcomes vary according to the burden of traditional cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) remains uncertain. We investigated the associations of RC with myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke in relation to cumulative CVRF burden. We conducted a prospective analysis of 84,806 participants from the Kailuan cohort (baseline 2006) without prior cardiovascular disease. CVRF burden was categorized as 0, 1, 2, or ≥ 3 according to current smoking, overweight (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²), hypertension, and diabetes.
