Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for incident MI and stroke through 2021, and interaction terms were used to assess potential effect modification by CVRF burden. During a median follow-up of 15 years, 1,690 MI and 6,416 stroke events occurred. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest RC quartile was associated with higher risks of MI (HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.37-1.83) and stroke (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.11-1.28). In supplementary subtype analyses, the stroke association was mainly observed for ischemic rather than hemorrhagic stroke. The RC-MI association appeared stronger across higher CVRF-burden categories (highest vs. lowest quartile HRs: 1.16, 1.52, 1.67, and 1.80 for 0, 1, 2, and ≥ 3 CVRFs, respectively), whereas the corresponding stroke association was attenuated (HRs: 1.44, 1.29, 1.21, and 1.03). After noncardiovascular death was treated as a competing event, the stroke interaction was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (P for interaction=0.21). In this large prospective cohort, RC was associated with higher risks of both MI and stroke, with stronger and more consistent associations observed for MI. The pattern of association differed across levels of CVRF burden, suggesting that the clinical interpretation of RC may benefit from outcome-specific and risk-context-specific assessment.

articles.title: The retrieved venous thrombus as a translational platform: a methodologic roadmap for venous immunothrombosis.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy is now widely used for iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) across several device platforms, and every procedure yields intact human thrombus that is routinely discarded. Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2010 to August 2026) for studies addressing the biology, histopathology and translational analysis of mechanically retrieved venous thrombi, supplemented by reference-list, trial-registry and congress hand-searching. Published venous series remain small and largely confined to descriptive histology, disconnected from longitudinal outcomes. Intra-thrombus biology could address venous-specific questions that peripheral biomarkers and imaging alone cannot: post-thrombotic syndrome, incomplete recanalization, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and cancer-associated thrombosis. A device-agnostic framework is proposed, comprising structured intra-procedural sampling at the level of the case rather than the anatomical region, centralized specimen processing under harmonized quality standards, a tiered analytic pipeline anchored on quantitative immunohistochemistry, paired peripheral-biomarker collection, pre-specified hypotheses with feasibility-based sample sizes, and biobank infrastructure embedded in existing trial platforms. The equivalent programme in arterial thrombectomy supplies transferable methodology, subject to explicit boundary conditions. The retrieved venous thrombus is among the more underused translational specimens in vascular medicine. A standardized, registry-embedded characterization framework could accelerate progress toward precision venous thrombosis medicine.

articles.title: In-Hospital and One-Year Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Coronary Occlusion in Octogenarians.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Older patients often present with complex coronary artery disease alongside multiple comorbidities. There is limited data on the outcomes of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) in octogenarians. We aim to investigate the in-hospital and 1-year outcomes following successful CTO-PCI in octogenarians.

METHODS: Consecutive patients who had successful CTO-PCI at a single center between 01.2017 and 12.2022 were divided into two groups: octogenarians (age ≥ 80 and < 90 years, n = 123) and a control group (age < 80 years, n = 612). Periprocedural complications, in-hospital major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 1-year target lesion failure (TLF) were investigated.

RESULTS: Octogenarians had a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (96.7% vs. 91.2%, p = 0.036), atrial fibrillation (28.5% vs. 12.1%, p < 0.001), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (34.1% vs. 16.5%, p < 0.001) compared to younger counterparts. The rate of failed CTO recanalization was higher in octogenarians (18.5% vs. 8.2%, p < 0.001). Incidence of in-hospital MACCE and periprocedural complications was comparable between the study groups, except for a numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians (2.4% vs. 0.8%, p = 0.114), and a higher incidence of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) (11.4% vs. 4.9%, p = 0.006). At 1 year, TLF did not differ significantly between the study arms (16.2% vs. 12.3%, aHR 1.52; CI 0.81-2.84, p = 0.191). Notably, higher cardiac mortality rates were observed in the octogenarian arm (7.6% vs. 2.7%, HR 2.82; CI 1.13-7.08, p = 0.027).

CONCLUSION: Despite numerically higher in-hospital mortality in octogenarians, CTO-PCI in those patients was performed with comparable periprocedural, and acute adverse outcomes, as well as 1-year TLF, to their younger counterparts. Octogenarians remain inherently at a higher long-term mortality risk. Graphical Abstract available for this article.

GOV IDENTIFIER: NCT06957613 (retrospectively registered, 03/05/2025).

articles.title: Correction: Targeting the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway in type 2 diabetes mellitus: from ER stress signaling to therapeutic opportunity.
Analysis of mRNA and microRNA profiles in ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVAD support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac remodeling after myocardial infarction is common, and recovery from end stage ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) with left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy remains rare. Our goal was to identify micro-RNAs (miRNAs) associated with ICM and to evaluate responses to LVAD therapy to better understand epigenetic mechanisms regulating differential gene expression (DGE).

METHODS: RNAs were isolated from human myocardial tissues of ICM (n = 11) pre- and post-LVAD placement, along with non-failing (NF) controls (n = 6). Expressions were quantified by utilizing a targeted cardiac panel for mRNA and the nCounter Human v2 miRNA panel for miRNA. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) was performed with DGE. Targeted gene expression profile was validated by performing mRNA-seq.

RESULTS: Compared to NF controls, 33 in pre- and 32 genes in post-LVAD were differentially expressed. IPA of mRNA revealed that signals of inflammatory cytokines and blood pressure disorder were activated in pre-LVAD ICM, and norepinephrine and cells migration were triggered in post-LVAD ICM compared to NF controls. Inflammatory response and apoptosis of cardiomyocytes were inhibited in post compared to pre-LVAD. Relative to NF controls, 195 in pre- and 120 miRNAs in post-LVAD ICM were differentially expressed. IPA of miRNA showed that apoptosis and fibrosis of the heart were stimulated both in pre- and post-LVAD ICM. RNA-seq results validated the targeted gene expression.

CONCLUSIONS: In ICM, miRNA expression is linked to apoptosis and fibrosis pathways. These changes persist in post-LVAD therapy and contribute to ongoing changes in mRNA expression associated with Heart failure.

articles.title: Fully biodegradable ventricular septal defect occluders: from biomaterials to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most prevalent congenital heart disease (CHD), which is approximately 20% of all congenital cardiac defects. Although transcatheter closure of VSD is a favorable alternative to traditional open-heart surgery, conventional nitinol-based occluders carry permanent risks of atrioventricular conduction disturbances, device erosion, and nickel allergy, which precluded regulatory approval in the United States for perimembranous VSD. Fully biodegradable occluders represent an attractive solution, offering equivalent closure efficacy while eliminating the long-term risks due to a permanent metallic implant. Owing to favorable endothelization-degradation kinetics, biocompatibility, and mechanical performance, polydioxanone (PDO) and poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) have emerged as the superior framework and membrane materials, respectively. Clinical evidence from case series, retrospective cohort studies, and a multicenter randomized controlled trial suggests high procedural success and favorable short- to mid-term safety, with a low incidence of conduction disturbances following biodegradable VSD occluder implantation. In 2022, the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China has granted regulatory approval for the MemoSorb® device, which represents the first clinical available fully biodegradable VSD occluder. This review focuses on biomaterials science, structural design principles, preclinical animal studies, and the emerging clinical evidence of fully biodegradable VSD occluder.

articles.title: Immediate weight bearing after dual orthogonal plate fixation of clavicle fractures: a propensity-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether immediate weight bearing as tolerated (WBAT) following open reduction and internal fixation of clavicle fractures with a dual mini-fragmentation plate construct increases complications, implant failure, or worsens functional and patient-reported outcomes compared to a restricted weight-bearing protocol.

METHODS: Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent open reduction and internal fixation of a clavicle fracture were retrospectively identified and stratified into restricted weight-bearing or weight bearing as tolerated (WBAT) cohorts. Cohorts were matched for demographic and injury characteristics. All WBAT fractures were treated with dual orthogonal mini-fragmentation plate fixation, whereas restricted weight-bearing fractures were treated with either single- or dual-plate fixation. Outcomes included complications (infection, wound dehiscence, hardware prominence, implant failure, and loss of reduction) and PROMIS Physical Function and Pain Interference scores.

RESULTS: Among 378 initial patients, 93 were included after propensity score matching: 62 in the restricted weight-bearing group and 31 in the WBAT group. Complication rates were similarly infrequent between groups (all p ≥ 0.326), with no fixation failures or deep surgical site infections occurring in the WBAT group.

CONCLUSIONS: Early weight bearing as tolerated may be safe following dual mini-fragmentation plate fixation of clavicle fractures, with comparable complication rates, union rates, and patient-reported outcomes to restricted weight-bearing protocols. These findings support the use of early mobilization in patients with rigid internal fixation constructs and may facilitate improved functional recovery and earlier return to activity.

articles.title: Association between perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy and reoperation following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: A TriNetX database study.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia (HLD) impairs tendon healing and is associated with increased revision risk following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR). While statins may partially mitigate this effect, residual dyslipidemia may impair healing. Ezetimibe, through inhibition of intestinal cholesterol absorption, has demonstrated favorable effects on tendon healing in preclinical studies.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy is associated with improved postoperative outcomes following ARCR compared with statin monotherapy and patients without HLD.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult patients undergoing ARCR were stratified into three cohorts based on HLD status and perioperative (± 6 months) lipid-lowering therapy: (1) documented HLD treated with statin-ezetimibe prescriptions, (2) patients without documented HLD or lipid-lowering therapy prescriptions, and (3) documented HLD treated with statin monotherapy prescriptions. Primary comparisons were predefined between cohort 1 and cohorts 2 and 3. Propensity score matching (1:1) adjusted for demographics and comorbidities. Tear size and presence of fatty atrophy and fatty infiltration were not adjusted for. Outcomes occurring within 5 years included revision rotator cuff repair (RCR), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty, and secondary shoulder arthroscopy.

RESULTS: After matching, 1,066 patients were included in cohorts 1 and 2 and 1,114 patients in cohorts 1 and 3. Compared with patients without HLD, statin-ezetimibe therapy demonstrated similar rates of revision RCR (5.4% vs. 6.4%; RR 0.853; p = 0.358), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty (RR 1.227; p = 0.470), and secondary arthroscopy (RR 0.846; p = 0.260). Compared with statin monotherapy, statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower rates of revision RCR (5.6% vs. 8.0%; RR 0.697; p = 0.023) and secondary shoulder arthroscopy (7.3% vs. 9.6%; RR 0.757; p = 0.048), while arthroplasty rates remained similar (RR 1.261; p = 0.400).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with HLD undergoing ARCR, perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower reoperation rates compared with statin monotherapy and postoperative outcomes comparable to patients without HLD. These findings support further investigation of intensified lipid-lowering therapy, while accounting for tear size and fatty infiltration.

articles.title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018).

CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

articles.title: A randomized study comparing plant sterol- and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk with plain soymilk in adults with elevated LDL cholesterol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is an effective strategy to reduce coronary heart disease risk. Plant sterols/stanols, soluble fiber, and soy protein have each shown LDL-C-lowering effects. This study compared the effects of plant sterol-and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk (SFSM) versus plain soymilk (SM) on LDL-C over 8 weeks.

METHODS: A total of 242 adults aged ≥ 18 years with hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C > 130 mg/dL), either untreated or receiving stable lipid-lowering therapy were randomized to receive either plain soymilk (SM; n = 119) or plant sterol- and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk (SFSM; n = 123), with two 180-mL packs consumed daily for 8 weeks. Three participants discontinued the assigned intervention during the study (SM, n = 1; SFSM, n = 2); all three attended the week-2 visit and contributed post-baseline laboratory data, but had no week-8 measurements. Both products provided 5 g soy protein per 180-mL serving; SFSM additionally contained 1 g free plant sterol and 5 g inulin (soluble fiber), with a total dietary fiber content of 5.8 g per serving, corresponding to daily intakes of 2 g free plant sterol and 11.6 g total fiber. Fasting plasma glucose and lipid profiles were measured at baseline and at weeks 2, 4, 6, and 8. Dietary intake and physical activity were monitored throughout the study. The intention-to-treat analysis included all 242 randomized participants.

RESULTS: At week 8, SFSM group had a greater reduction in LDL-C than the SM group, with an adjusted between-group treatment effect of 5.5 mg/dL (95% CI 0.6 to 10.4, p = 0.028), favoring SFSM, after adjustment for baseline lipid values. No significant between-group differences were found in fasting plasma glucose, HDL-C, triglycerides, total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio, total energy intake, total fat intake, cholesterol intake, water consumption, or physical activity; however, fiber intake increased significantly more in the SFSM group.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the LDL-C-lowering benefit of plant sterol-and soluble fiber-enriched soymilk compared with plain soymilk over 8 weeks; however, secondary and subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously because they were exploratory in nature. Trial registration Clinical Trials Registry Identifier: (NCT02459314) Retrospectively registered on May 15, 2015; first posted June 2, 2015. The study was conducted from April 2013 to April 2014. The original protocol date 22 October 2012 is provided as supplementary material.

articles.title: Disulfiram attenuates paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis accompanied by changes in Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Paraquat (PQ) is a highly toxic herbicide that induces renal injury through oxidative stress and progressive fibrosis, contributing to chronic kidney disease. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy for accelerating therapeutic development. This study evaluated the nephroprotective potential of disulfiram (DSF), a clinically approved drug with emerging antioxidant and antifibrotic properties, against PQ-induced renal injury, including its association with changes in the expression of the Smad3 and Smad7 genes.

METHODS: Thirty-five male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to seven groups: Control, Vehicle, DSF20, PQ (1.5 mg/kg), and PQ co-treated with DSF (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg). Renal injury was evaluated using histopathology (H&E, PAS, and Masson's trichrome staining), α-SMA, serum biomarkers (BUN, creatinine, and uric acid), oxidative stress parameters (malondialdehyde [MDA], catalase [CAT], and glutathione peroxidase [GPx]), and Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression determined by qRT-PCR.

RESULTS: PQ exposure caused marked renal histopathological injury, increased α-SMA, increased oxidative stress, impaired renal function, and elevated fibrosis, accompanied by increased Smad3 and decreased Smad7 gene expression. DSF co-treatment, particularly at 10 mg/kg, significantly ameliorated these changes by reducing tissue injury, decreasing α-SMA-positive area% and collagen deposition, restoring antioxidant enzyme activity, lowering lipid peroxidation, improving renal function, and altering Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression toward PQ levels.

CONCLUSION: Disulfiram at an optimal dose of 10 mg/kg significantly attenuated PQ-induced renal injury and fibrosis, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and altered Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression. These findings support the potential of DSF as a repurposed therapeutic candidate for mitigating paraquat-induced renal injury and fibrosis. Further studies evaluating protein-level changes and activation of the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway are warranted to clarify the underlying molecular mechanisms.

articles.title: Safety, tissue adequacy, and diagnostic contribution of ultrasound-guided synovial biopsy: a retrospective multicenter observational study in a heterogeneous rheumatology cohort.
articles.abstract: To evaluate procedural safety as the primary outcome of ultrasound-guided synovial biopsy (UGSB) in a real-world, multicenter rheumatology setting. Secondary outcomes included technical tissue adequacy, histopathological yield, patient-reported outcomes, willingness to undergo repeat biopsy, clinical indications, and diagnostic contribution. This retrospective multicenter observational study included 87 patients who underwent UGSB for diagnostic or clinical indications. Demographic and clinical data, indication, biopsied joint, ultrasonographic findings, adverse events, and patient-reported outcomes using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS 0-10) for pain, swelling, and limitation of motion were collected pre- and post-procedure. Adverse events and willingness to undergo repeat biopsy were recorded. Diagnoses were classified as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), undifferentiated arthritis, or other rheumatologic diseases. Of the 87 patients (57.5% female; median age 46 years, IQR 17), 47.1% were diagnosed with RA, 31.0% had undifferentiated arthritis, and 21.8% had other rheumatologic conditions. The knee was the most frequently biopsied joint (69.0%). Ultrasonographic grade ≥ 2 synovitis was detected in 83.3% and power Doppler signal in 33.3% of the 54 patients with available US data. Adequate synovial tissue for histopathological evaluation was obtained in 90% of procedures. Post-procedural VAS scores demonstrated significant reductions in pain, swelling, and limitation of motion compared with pre-biopsy assessments (p < 0.001 for all). Ultrasonographic synovitis severity correlated with the histological Krenn synovitis score (greyscale ρ = 0.31, p = 0.036; effusion ρ = 0.48, p = 0.001). Adverse events were infrequent and predominantly mild; transient pain was the most common complication (19.5%). Sensory impairment and vasovagal reactions each occurred in one patient (1.1%). No tendon, vascular, ligament, or muscle injury, hemarthrosis, infection, or thromboembolic complications were observed. Sixty-seven patients (77.0%) reported willingness to undergo repeat biopsy if clinically indicated. Following completion of the overall diagnostic work-up-integrating clinical, laboratory, imaging, microbiological, and histopathological findings-the proportion classified as having undifferentiated arthritis decreased from 31.0% to 13.8%. UGSB is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated minimally invasive procedure with high patient acceptability and a high rate of adequate tissue acquisition across a broad spectrum of rheumatologic diseases. In selected patients with diagnostically challenging arthritis, synovial tissue analysis may provide histopathological or microbiological information that contributes to diagnostic clarification when integrated with the broader clinical work-up. These findings support the feasibility of UGSB in appropriately selected clinical settings and provide a basis for future prospective studies with standardized protocols.

articles.title: Targeting the epigenetic landscape of ECFCs: a new opportunity to enhance vascular repair.
articles.abstract: Endothelial colony-forming cells (ECFCs) are endothelial progenitor cells characterized by robust proliferative and vasculogenic capacities, making them promising candidates for therapeutic tissue revascularization. However, the clinical application of ECFCs is hindered by their functional impairment under pathological conditions, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Accumulating evidence indicates that aberrant epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, have been implicated in disease-associated ECFC dysfunction. In this review, we summarize current insights into the epigenetic regulation of ECFCs in pathological contexts, discuss epigenetic intervention strategies aimed at restoring ECFC function, and further highlight the therapeutic potential of ECFC-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) as carriers of epigenetic cargo that promotes vascular repair. Collectively, a deeper understanding of the epigenetic landscape of ECFCs and ECFC-derived EVs may facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approaches for vascular regeneration and accelerate the clinical translation of ECFC- and EV-based therapies.

articles.title: Reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation in women with iron deficiency: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oral iron supplementation is frequently limited by gastrointestinal side effects and reduced absorption associated with hepcidin-mediated regulation. This randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled study evaluated whether a reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation strategy could improve iron status in women with iron deficiency.

METHODS: Sixty-six iron-deficient women of reproductive age (18-50 years; serum ferritin < 30 ng/mL) were randomized to receive, for 42 days, either micronized, dispersible ferric pyrophosphate providing 21 mg of elemental iron every 48 h combined with a daily gut microbiota modulator, or sucrosomial ferric pyrophosphate providing 30 mg of elemental iron per day. The primary endpoint was serum ferritin, while secondary endpoints included serum iron, transferrin, transferrin saturation (TSAT), total iron-binding capacity (TIBC), hemoglobin, and red blood cell count.

RESULTS: Serum ferritin increased significantly over time in both groups (p < 0.001), with no significant differences between treatments. Comparable improvements were observed for serum iron, transferrin, TSAT, and TIBC, while hemoglobin remained stable throughout the study. Both interventions were generally well tolerated, with only mild transient gastrointestinal adverse events and no clinically relevant changes in inflammatory markers.

CONCLUSION: A reduced-dose alternate-day oral iron supplementation strategy achieved improvements in iron status comparable to standard daily supplementation despite lower cumulative iron exposure. These findings support the potential clinical relevance of physiologically informed low-dose iron supplementation strategies in women with iron deficiency.

articles.title: [The role of clinical inertia in the complex care of patients suffering from heart failure].
articles.abstract: Inertia refers to a lack of energy or helplessness; in the context of heart failure, clinical inertia can be understood primarily as the failure to initiate or optimize therapies known to reduce morbidity and mortality in patients not on optimized therapy. The aim of this review article is to provide an overview of the most recent guidelines and recommendations relevant to the topic, summarize the available international literature, and present the results of practical interventions that may also be feasibly implemented in Hungary. Heart failure remains a condition with an unfavorable prognosis; however, the use of modern, optimal, comprehensive, guideline-directed medical therapies may confer substantial prognostic benefit. In everyday clinical practice, clinical inertia is one of the main barriers to effective treatment, and the need to address it has also been emphasized in recent position statements of the European Society of Cardiology. The integration of multidisciplinary care, structured patient education, and targeted interventions is of fundamental importance in overcoming clinical inertia, optimizing treatment adherence, and improving long-term outcomes. Close follow-up and rapid up-titration of guideline-directed medical therapy in eligible patients are of particular importance and may significantly reduce the relative risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality. The use of telemedicine during follow-up, together with the broader exploitation of digital opportunities, provides contemporary clinicians with a range of new possibilities. Based on real-world data, interventions that favorably influence clinical inertia can also be successfully implemented in Hungary, yielding significant clinical benefit for patients with heart failure. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(43): 1719-1729.

articles.title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement.

METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression.

RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

articles.title: A large-scale consensus study of a diagnostic algorithm for canine and feline mammary tumor histopathology: An attempt to improve inter-observer agreement.
articles.abstract: Histological classification of mammary proliferative lesions in dogs and cats is essential for prognostic and predictive studies, as well as for comparative oncology; however, standardization of diagnoses is highly affected by substantial interobserver variability. In this study, a structured diagnostic algorithm based on the Davis-Thompson Foundation classification was assessed for the ability to improve interobserver agreement in the morphological diagnoses of mammary gland lesions in dogs and cats. Consensus diagnoses of 114 selected mammary lesions (91 canine, 23 feline) made by 16 veterinary pathologists with mammary tumor expertise were used as the gold standard, and 79 veterinary pathologists from 21 countries evaluated digitized whole slides in 2 rounds: a first reading without the algorithm and a second reading with the algorithm. Interobserver concordance was measured using unweighted kappa statistics for lesion category (hyperplastic/dysplastic, benign, malignant) and histological subtype. Across all lesions, agreement was higher for lesion category than for histological subtype. A slight improvement in concordance was observed when applying the algorithm, both for category (k = 0.72, before, and k = 0.73, after) and histotype classifications (k = 0.40, before to k = 0.42, after). Also, by using the algorithm, 73/79 raters (92%) modified at least 1 diagnosis and, among these, approximately two-thirds reached agreement with the gold standard in at least 1 case. Considering histotypes, malignant tumors with mixed epithelial and myoepithelial components showed persistently low agreement. Overall, the algorithm provided a reproducible diagnostic framework that may support training and improve standardization of canine and feline mammary tumor classification.

articles.title: Accidental overdose admissions and premature death: A large population-based data-linkage cohort study in New South Wales, Australia (PAVLOVA 4).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: People with substance use disorders have reduced life-expectancy; however, risks of premature death from injuries and natural causes following an accidental overdose are not well characterised. This study aimed to estimate risk of premature death (by cause and over time), and disease burden following hospitalised accidental overdose.

DESIGN: An observational study using the Poisoning And enVenomation Linkage to evaluate Outcomes and clinical Variation in Australia (PAVLOVA) cohort.

SETTING: A population-based data-linkage including admissions from all public and private hospitals in New South Wales, Australia (population ~8 million), 2011-2020.

PARTICIPANTS: 14 036 individuals [median age 43.5 years, interquartile range (IQR) = 29.4-61.8 years, 46.7% female, n = 6557] with an index non-fatal accidental poisoning, as defined by hospital coding, followed for a median of 3.9 years (IQR = 1.7-6.3). We restricted our analysis to people with accidental poisonings with prescription and illicit drugs that are associated with non-medical use and dependence, including opioids and benzodiazepines.

MEASUREMENTS: Standardised mortality ratio (SMR) by cause (natural causes stratified by body system, and external causes stratified by intent and mechanism), SMR over time (post-index poisoning), years of life lost (YLL) by cause, age and sex. SMR and YLL were calculated based on expected values generated using official statistics.

RESULTS: Of the 14 036 people included, there were 2588 deaths. Death was more likely in individuals with accidental poisoning compared with the general population [SMR = 3.5, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 3.4-3.7]. SMRs were highest for external causes (SMR = 12.8, 95% CI = 11.5-14.1), including accidental poisoning (SMR = 59.5, 95% CI = 51.7-67.3) and suicide (SMR = 10.5, 95% CI = 8.2-12.9). Death was also more likely across all natural causes, particularly infectious (SMR = 7.0, 95% CI = 5.1-8.9) and respiratory diseases (SMR = 6.2, 95% CI = 5.4-6.9). Median YLL per death was 21.2 (IQR = 10.0-35.6) and 15.2 (IQR = 7.2-30.2) for males and females, respectively. The main contributors to YLL were natural causes (64.0%): neoplasms (19.5%), circulatory (12.2%) and respiratory disease (11.1%). The remainder of YLL was from external causes (36.0%): mainly accidental poisoning (22.4%).

SUMMARY: People in New South Wales, Australia, who experience an accidental overdose appear to have an increased risk of death over subsequent years, but particularly in the first month, compared with the general population; however, accidental poisoning accounts for only 22% of years of life lost, with death from natural causes being much more common.

articles.title: An Integrated Housing Intervention for People Involved in the Criminal-Legal System: Contributors to Successfully Moving Along the Housing Continuum.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: People impacted by the criminal-legal system face challenges to securing and sustaining permanent housing. This study was designed to deliver an integrated housing, medical, and behavioral health services intervention to individuals with criminal-legal involvement.

METHODS: After a baseline needs assessment, participants were linked to services and completed quarterly study visits for up to 12 months. We used descriptive statistics to assess frequency and multivariate logistic regression to assess correlates of housing status at last follow-up.

RESULTS: Between June 2019 and November 2023, 187 participants were enrolled in Project CHANGE (Comprehensive Housing and Addiction Treatment Network of Greater New Haven). At baseline, 43% of participants were unstably housed, 37% were homeless, and the remaining resided in a shelter or institution. At the time of last follow-up, 49 participants (26.2%) reported improved housing outcomes, and an additional 121 participants' (64.7%) housing situation did not worsen. In multivariate models, individuals who were older (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.1; 95% CI, 1.0-1.1), unstably housed at baseline (AOR = 7.6; 95% CI, 3.8-15.9), and enrolled in the study for longer (AOR = 1.2; 95% CI, 1.1-1.3) had higher odds of being housed at last follow-up, whereas those with high-severity substance use had lower odds of being housed (AOR = 0.3; 95% CI, 0.1-0.6).

CONCLUSIONS: In this comprehensive program, integrated housing and health services were time and cost intensive but were associated with positive housing outcomes. People involved in the criminal-legal system face unique barriers to housing, particularly when compounded by substance use.

articles.title: A Blind Spot in US Public Health: The Case for Nocardia Surveillance.
Short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children represents a significant and growing global health burden. This study aims to report the short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted to assess outcomes in pediatric patients with various types of hemodialysis access. This prospective cohort study included all consecutive pediatric patients with ESRD who presented to the Vascular and Endovascular Surgery Department at a tertiary hospital from October 2022 to October 2023.

RESULTS: The study included 50 pediatric patients, with a mean age of 10.5 ± 5.7 years. The cohort was predominantly female 35 (70%), while males accounted for 15 (30%) The overall technical success rate remained high at 45 (90%). The failure rate was 5 (10%).

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that pediatric arteriovenous fistulas (predominantly autogenous), when carefully planned and executed, can achieve high primary success and patency rates, with manageable complications in children with end-stage renal disease.

articles.title: Interpreting the Association Between Lp-PLA2 and Platelet Activation in Coronary Artery Disease.
Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for a Neglected Type III Fracture of the Anterior Process of the Calcaneus in a Collegiate Hurdler: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFractures of the anterior process of the calcaneus (APC) are frequently misdiagnosed as ankle sprains and may progress to symptomatic nonunion. Degan type III APC fractures involve the calcaneocuboid joint and are conventionally managed surgically. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) has not previously been reported for this fracture type.Case presentationA 21-year-old male collegiate hurdler presented with a 2-year history of left lateral foot pain. Computed tomography confirmed a neglected Degan type III APC nonunion. After declining surgery, he underwent 9 sessions of focused ESWT (peak energy flux density 0.07-0.25 mJ/mm²) in 3-session sets over 19 weeks, combined with a 3-month sports restriction from the start of treatment. Pain resolved completely (visual analog scale 75/100 → 0/100), and he returned to competitive hurdling at 6 months after starting ESWT. Computed tomography at 14 months after ESWT initiation confirmed bony bridging.ConclusionExtracorporeal shock wave therapy was associated with clinical improvement and radiological healing in this individual case and may warrant further investigation as a non-surgical option in young athletes with a neglected Degan type III APC nonunion who decline surgery.

articles.title: Real-World Evaluation of a Near-Infrared Spectroscopy-based Noninvasive Glucose Monitoring Device in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-monitoring of blood glucose remains widely used in many individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D), although the burden of capillary testing often limits the frequency of measurements. Noninvasive technologies may improve glucose monitoring. This study evaluated the analytical performance and applicability of a near-infrared spectroscopy-based noninvasive glucose monitoring device.

METHODS: In this prospective, open-label clinical investigation, 52 adults with T2D performed 4 daily paired glucose measurements for more than 21 days using the investigational device and a reference capillary glucometer (Ascensia Contour Next). Following individualized calibration (10 paired measurements), post-calibration measurements within the 70 to 400 mg/dL range were included in the primary analysis. Accuracy was assessed using a combined mean absolute difference/mean absolute relative difference (MAD/MARD) metric, Parkes consensus error grid (CEG), and DTS error grid analyses.

RESULTS: Forty-eight participants were included in the primary analysis, contributing 2,616 paired post-calibration measurements. The mean age was 58.0 ± 9.9 years, and 31.3% were female. The overall combined MAD/MARD value was 16.3, calculated by applying MAD to paired measurements with reference glucose values <100 mg/dL and MARD to paired measurements with reference glucose values ≥100 mg/dL. Overall, 69.8%, 86.3%, and 94.5% of measurements were within ±20%, ±30%, and ±40% of reference values, respectively. Parkes CEG analysis classified 69.9% of measurements in zone A, 29.1% in zone B, 1.0% in zone C, and none in zones D or E. Accuracy improved after the first week. No device-related adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSION: The device demonstrated a favorable clinical risk profile, stable analytical performance, and good safety under real-world conditions. Although analytical precision remains lower than current continuous glucose monitoring systems, its fully noninvasive design supports further development as a complementary monitoring strategy for individuals with T2D unwilling or unable to use invasive monitoring technologies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07075796).

articles.title: Performance and Safety of a Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Pregnant Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Multicenter, Open-Label Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is increasingly important in pregnancies complicated by diabetes, where strict glycemic control is essential to prevent adverse outcomes such as fetal macrosomia and preterm birth. In gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)-which accounts for most of the diabetes in pregnancy-maternal hyperglycemia is the primary clinical concern. This study evaluated the accuracy and safety of a factory-calibrated CGM system over 15 days in pregnant women with diabetes, with most having GDM.

METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, open-label trial enrolled 60 pregnant women (95% GDM, 3.3% type 1 diabetes, 1.7% type 2 diabetes). Each participant wore 2 sensors simultaneously, 1 on each upper arm, for up to 15 days. Venous blood glucose reference values were obtained using a Biosen C-line GP+ analyzer. Accuracy was assessed by 20/20% agreement rate, Diabetes Technology Society (DTS) error grid analysis, and mean absolute relative difference (MARD). Safety and usability were also evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 2901 matched CGM-reference pairs were analyzed (1451 from left-arm sensors, 1450 from right-arm sensors). The 20/20% agreement rate was 96.6% (95% CI, 95.6%-97.5%) for the left arm and 96.8% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.7%) for the right arm. The overall MARD was 7.72% (95% CI, 7.33%-8.11%) for the left arm and 7.66% (95% CI, 7.27%-8.05%) for the right arm.

CONCLUSION: The CGM system demonstrated accurate, stable, and safe glucose monitoring over 15 days in pregnant women with predominantly GDM. Its strong performance supports its utility as a reliable tool for glucose monitoring during pregnancy.

articles.title: Porcine astrovirus induces endoplasmic reticulum stress-mediated autophagic degradation of MAVS to inhibit type I interferon production.
articles.abstract: Porcine astrovirus (PAstV) infection predominantly results in diarrhea and encephalitis in suckling piglets, yet the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, the PAstV1-GX1 strain, previously isolated, was utilized to infect PK-15 cells. The results demonstrated that PAstV infection induced pronounced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, as evidenced by the upregulation of HSPA5/GRP78 expression, and macroautophagy/autophagy, indicated by the increased conversion of MAP1LC3/LC3 from LC3-I to LC3-II and decreased expression of SQSTM1/p62. Pharmacological mitigation of ER stress effectively suppressed autophagy, suggesting that PAstV facilitates autophagy via ER stress. Further mechanistic investigations identified that PAstV infection selectively activated the EIF2AK3/PERK-EIF2S1/eIF2α-ATF4 pathway within the unfolded protein response, establishing this pathway as the pivotal upstream signal mediating autophagy. Through the screening of viral proteins, the capsid protein was identified as the primary viral component responsible for inducing ER stress and autophagy. This protein was concurrently localized to both mitochondria and the ER, where it interacted with the MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein). The capsid protein facilitated the degradation of MAVS via the autophagy pathway and an apoptosis-related pathway in a non-classical, caspase-3-independent manner, thereby suppressing the production of type I interferons. Modulating ER stress, autophagy, or apoptosis greatly impacted the capsid protein's suppression of type I interferons. This suggested that the capsid protein hindered type I interferon production by triggering ER stress, which activated autophagy and possibly apoptosis, resulting in MAVS degradation. These insights lay the groundwork for understanding PAstV's pathogenic mechanisms and aid in developing new antiviral treatments.

articles.title: Tricuspid Chordae Tendineae Rupture Detected After Repair of a Delayed Traumatic Left Ventricular Aneurysm: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Delayed traumatic cardiac rupture complicated by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture is an exceedingly rare clinical entity. We report this case to describe the temporal sequence of events from blunt myocardial contusion to left ventricular aneurysm formation and rupture, followed by secondary tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture. While the precise mechanism linking these events remains to be determined, we propose a potential pathophysiological connection. CASE REPORT A patient presented with rupture of a posterior left ventricular aneurysm 54 days after a fall from a height. The patient was emergently placed on venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for circulatory support and subsequently underwent surgical repair of the aneurysm. Postoperative echocardiography revealed new-onset tricuspid chordae tendineae rupture, prompting elective mechanical tricuspid replacement. Histopathological examination of resected valve tissues revealed chronic degenerative changes. To our knowledge, this is the first report documenting this temporal sequence of delayed left ventricular aneurysm rupture followed by tricuspid chordal rupture after surgical repair. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the importance of continued clinical and echocardiographic vigilance after severe blunt cardiac injury, particularly for detecting late-emerging structural complications such as aneurysm formation and valvular dysfunction. It also illustrates the potential utility of VA-ECMO as a critical bridging strategy to stabilize patients with traumatic cardiac rupture before surgical repair. The observed temporal association between aneurysm repair and subsequent tricuspid chordal rupture is noted, though the exact causal relationship and underlying mechanism remain uncertain.

articles.title: Respiratory pathogens across rural populations: general practice patients with community-acquired pneumonia, residents, and goat farmers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residents living near goat farms (< 2000 m) in the Netherlands have consistently shown an elevated risk of pneumonia, yet the pathogens underlying this association remain unknown. This study assessed the presence of 33 respiratory pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and fungi, across rural populations with different goat farm exposures.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included general practitioner (GP)-diagnosed pneumonia patients (PP; n = 108), non-farming rural residents without pneumonia (NFR; n = 200), and goat farm workers (GFW; n = 91). Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and analyzed by a multiplex and two additional PCR test targeting in total 12 bacteria, 20 viruses and 1 fungus. Between-group differences in detection were assessed by Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations between pathogen detection and residential proximity to goat farming and other covariates.

RESULTS: Presence of any of the examined pathogens was highest in the PP group (94.5%), followed by GFW (88.8%), and NFR (70%). The most frequently detected pathogens overall were Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and rhinovirus. Of these, M. catarrhalis and S. pneumoniae were significantly more often detected in PP, whereas Salmonella spp. and S. aureus were more frequently detected in GFW. Eight pathogens, including Coxiella burnetii, were not detected. Age, season of sampling, smoking and other covariates were significantly associated with certain bacteria and viruses. However, no associations were identified between residential proximity to goat farming and detection of specific pathogens in NFR and PP.

CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory pathogens were detected in nearly all PP, while substantial proportions of positives were also observed in GFW and NFR, likely reflecting (transient) colonization rather than active infection. Detection of the examined pathogens was not associated with residential proximity to goat farms, suggesting that these pathogens do not explain the observed increased pneumonia risk among nearby non-farming residents. As a substantial proportion of the Dutch population (~ 7%) lives within 2,000 m of a commercial goat farm, and goat farming is expanding globally, further research efforts, including microbiologic diagnostics and surveillance, are needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the increased pneumonia risk among nearby residents.

articles.title: [pMHCBind: predicting major histocompatibility complex class I-peptide interactions via protein large language models and hypergraph neural networks].
articles.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
articles.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules initiate CD8+ T cell immune responses by presenting antigenic peptides, a process fundamentally governed by the spatial interaction network mediated by multi-residue synergy between the binding groove and the peptide. Accurate modeling of this mechanism is crucial for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy. However, existing methods are largely confined to sequence-level modeling, failing to capture cross-residue higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained binding interface interactions. To address these challenges, we propose pMHCBind, a prediction model that integrates a protein language model with a hypergraph neural network. The model employs ESM-MSA-1b and ESM-2 to extract evolution-aware residue-level embeddings for MHC I molecules and antigenic peptides, respectively, and constructs a peptide-specific hypergraph based on spatial contact relationships to model higher-order interactions via hypergraph convolution. Subsequently, cross-molecular feature fusion is employed to characterize the interaction patterns on the binding interface for presentation ability prediction. In five-fold cross-validation on the NetMHCpan-4.1 benchmark dataset and the test performance on the Anthem independent test dataset, pMHCBind consistently outperforms a variety of state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics, including the area under receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR). Furthermore, interpretability analysis reveals that the model effectively identifies key interaction modes, such as hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and hydrophobic interactions, between the binding groove and the peptide, demonstrating strong structural interpretability. Collectively, pMHCBind provides a promising and biologically interpretable computational tool for neoantigen recognition in precision cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: [Genome-wide identification of PfLACS in Perilla frutescens and functional analysis of PfLACS1 mediating lipid synthesis].
articles.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
articles.abstract: Perilla frutescens (L.) Britt. is a characteristic oil crop rich in n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids in its seeds, holding significant potential for development and utilization. Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase (LACS) plays a crucial regulatory role in plant lipid metabolism by activating free fatty acids into fatty acyl-CoA. In this study, to deeply analyze the functional characterization of the LACS gene in perilla lipid synthesis and storage, PfLACS sequences were identified from the genomic and transcriptomic data of P. frutescens. Omics tools were employed to analyze their sequence characteristics, gene structures, and phylogenetic relationships. The activity of PfLACS1 was evaluated via the LACS-deficient strain YB525, and the function of PfLACS1 in lipid synthesis was analyzed through genetic transformation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and tobacco, as well as transient transformation in perilla cotyledons. A total of 12 PfLACS gene family members were identified and classified into five subfamilies based on sequence characteristics. Members within the same subfamily exhibited similar gene structures and conserved motifs in terms of type and number. The secondary structures of PfLACS were predominantly composed of α-helices and random coils. Transcriptome sequencing analysis revealed that 12 PfLACS were differentially expressed in developing perilla seeds, with PfLACS1 showing the highest expression level in seeds. Subcellular localization analysis indicated that PfLACS1 was localized to the endoplasmic reticulum. Yeast complementation assays confirmed that PfLACS1 could restore the functional deficiency in the LACS-deficient yeast strain YB525 and exhibited LACS activity. The results of heterologous expression indicated that overexpression of PfLACS1 led to a significant increase in total lipid content in both yeast and tobacco, accompanied by elevated levels of C16:1 and C18:1. Transient infection assays in perilla cotyledons further confirmed that overexpression of PfLACS1 significantly enhanced total lipid content. This study preliminarily confirms that PfLACS1 is involved in the activation of free fatty acids (especially C16 and C18) and fatty acid-related lipid metabolic processes, providing a theoretical basis for the genetic improvement and breeding of new varieties in P. frutescens and other oil-rich plants.

articles.title: [Genome-wide identification, expression profiling, and natural allelic variation analysis of the ckx genes in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor)].
articles.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
articles.abstract: Cytokinin (CK) is one of the essential plant hormones, and cytokinin oxidase (CKX) is the key enzyme for CK degradation. Currently, the ckx gene family of rice (Oryza sativa) and maize (Zea mays) have been characterized, while a genome-wide analysis of the ckx gene family in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) has not been reported. This study aims to identify the Sbckx gene family in sorghum, analyze its evolutionary characteristics and expression patterns, and screen for key genes. A combined approach of bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation was utilized to examine sorghum subjected to abiotic stress conditions: low nitrogen and drought, as well as biotic stress induced by infections of head smut pathogens and sugarcane aphids, and the expression levels of Sbckxs were measured. A total of eleven Sbckxs were identified from the sorghum genome, exhibiting uneven distribution across chromosomes SBI-01, SBI-03,SBI-04, SBI-06, SBI-07, SBI-09, and SBI-010 (notably, chromosome SBI-03 contained four genes arranged in a clustered pattern). The SbCKX family proteins all contained the FAD-binding and cytokin-binding conserved domains. They exhibited high homology with the CKX family of five species including maize and rice and were classified into five evolutionary groups based on phylogenetic analysis. The expression pattern of SbCKXs exhibited tissue specificity. Specifically, Sbckx1-3g and Sbckx4-3g demonstrated high expression levels in roots and seedlings, whereas Sbckx11-7g was exclusively expressed in the panicle. Under conditions of drought, low nitrogen availability, and head smut infection, the expression levels of certain genes were notably elevated. The predicted interacting proteins of SbCKXs were implicated in pathways associated with growth, development, and substance metabolism. DNA variant analysis of re-sequenced sorghum germplasm revealed a high frequency of non-synonymous SNPs and INDELs in Sbckx10-10g across multiple cultivars. This study is the first to systematically analyze the molecular characteristics, expression patterns, and allelic variations of the ckx gene family in sorghum, providing a theoretical basis for subsequent functional verification of Sbckxs and molecular breeding for improving the stress resistance and yield of sorghum.

articles.title: [Mechanism of electroacupuncture combined with antibiotics targeting dorsal motor nucleus of vagus nerve to activate vagus-adrenal axis, alleviate inflammatory response and reduce mortality in septic mice].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the mechanism by which electroacupuncture (EA) combined with antibiotics regulates the vagus-adrenal axis via the dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV), promotes catecholamine secretion, attenuates inflammatory storm, and improves survival rate in septic mice.

METHODS: Experiment 1:fifty C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into sham operation group, model group, antibiotic group, EA group, and EA + antibiotic group, with 10 mice in each group. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was performed to establish the sepsis model. Mice in the EA group received 15 min EA (10 Hz, 0.5 mA) at bilateral "Zusanli" (ST36), once daily for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the antibiotic group were intraperitoneally injected with imipenem-cilastatin sodium (30 mg/kg) every 12 h for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the EA+antibiotic group received EA and antibiotic treatment the same as the above. The 3-day survival rate and body weight changes of mice in each group were recorded. ELISA was adopted to detect serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). HE staining was used to observe pathological changes and the number of inflammatory cells in cecal tissues. Whole-brain optical clearing was performed to detect the expression of proto-oncogene c-Fos protein (c-Fos) in the DMV region. Experiment 2:fifty Chat-Cre mice were randomly assigned to sham operation + empty virus group, model + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group, with 10 mice per group. Corresponding viruses were injected into the DMV 3 weeks before model establishment. CLP operation was conducted 3 weeks after virus injection, followed by daily intraperitoneal injection of clozapine N-oxide (CNO, 3 mg/kg), combined with antibiotics or EA treatment (the same interventions and parameters as Experiment 1). Serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels were measured by ELISA;cecal inflammatory infiltration was evaluated via HE staining. Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) was applied to detect serum catecholamines including dopamine (DA), epinephrine (E), norepinephrine (NE), as well as their metabolites 3-methoxytyramine (3-MT), normetanephrine (NMN), and metanephrine (MN) levels. Immunofluorescence staining was used to quantify the counts of forkhead box protein P3 positive / cluster of differentiation 4 positive (FOXP3+/CD4+) cells in cecal tissues.

RESULTS: Experiment 1:compared with the sham operation group, the model group exhibited markedly decreased 3-day survival rate and body weight (P<0.000 1), elevated serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), and increased inflammatory cell infiltration in cecum (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model group, the EA + antibiotic group showed improved survival rate (P<0.05), alleviated body weight loss (P<0.000 1), decreased serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), reduced inflammatory cell infiltration (P<0.000 1), and elevated c-Fos positive cell density in DMV (P<0.000 1). Moreover, all above indicators were superior to those in the single EA or single antibiotic group to varying degrees. Experiment 2:in comparison with the sham operation + empty virus group, the model + empty virus group had higher serum inflammatory factor levels and more cecal inflammatory infiltrates (P<0.0001), and lower levels of catecholamines and their metabolites, as well as fewer FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecal tissues (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model + empty virus group, the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group displayed reduced serum inflammatory factors and relieved cecal inflammatory infiltration (P<0.000 1, P<0.01, P<0.05), accompanied by increased levels of catecholamines and metabolites, and more FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecum (P<0.01, P<0.05, P<0.001, P<0.000 1). Relative to the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, all the above indicators were reversed in the EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group (P<0.01, P<0.001, P<0.05, except for 3-MT).

CONCLUSIONS: EA at ST36 combined with antibiotics exerts optimal therapeutic effects on CLP-induced septic mice. The underlying mechanism may involve activating cholinergic neurons in DMV, regulating the vagus-adrenal axis to facilitate catecholamine secretion, suppressing excessive inflammatory response, and consequently elevating survival rate.

articles.title: A host-virus arms race over FAM134B in African swine fever virus infection.
articles.abstract: Although reticulophagy, the selective autophagy of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), restricts several RNA viruses, whether this pathway constrains DNA virus infection remains unknown. Recently, we found that FAM134B (family with sequence similarity 134 member B), an ER-resident cargo receptor that mediates reticulophagy, restricts African swine fever virus (ASFV), a large cytoplasmic DNA virus, by targeting the major capsid proteins p72 and pA137R for lysosomal degradation, thereby blocking capsid assembly at perinuclear viral factories. ASFV counters this restriction through the virulence factor pMGF300-2R encoded by the MGF300-2R gene of ASFV, which binds to FAM134B, recruits LC3B (microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta), an ATG8 (autophagy-related protein 8) family member, via the C-terminal LC3-interacting region (LIR) motif, and directs FAM134B into autophagic degradation. Deletion of the MGF300-2R gene in the ASFV genome restores FAM134B abundance, reduces viral replication, and attenuates virulence in pigs. These findings establish reticulophagy as a previously unrecognized antiviral barrier against a large DNA virus and reveal a host-virus arms race centered on the reticulophagy receptor.Abbreviations: ASFV: African swine fever virus; ER: endoplasmic reticulum; FAM134B: family with sequence similarity 134 member B; LC3B: microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta; LIR: LC3-interacting region; VFs: viral factories.

articles.title: Immobilization of neurotensin receptor through immunologic recognition between ALFA tag and nanobody for affinity-based ligand discovery.
articles.abstract: Fabrication of bioactive interface by immobilizing proteins with pharmacological importance onto a solid surface is instrumental for interrogating drug actions and discovery of new drug molecules. In current work, we have developed a hybrid method for the interface fabrication by using Halo-tagged nanobody as a bidirectional adaptor for simultaneous capture of ALFA-tagged proteins onto solid surface and capturing proteins of the interest with a fused short epitope sequence. To this end, we engineered G protein-coupled receptors with a fused ALFA tag comprised of 13 amino acids and an ALFA-specific nanobody (NbALFA) fused to a Halo tag for the covalent immobilization onto a silica surface chemically modified with the Halo substrate. This strategy was applied to incorporate β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR) into a silica sphere-based chromatographic stationary phase. Both salbutamol and methoxyphenamine showed specific retention profiles in the β2AR column with measured dissociation constant (Kd) as 58.50 μM and 115.20 μM respectively. We employed this strategy for human neurotensin receptor 1 (NTR1), a class A GPCR member involved in schizophrenia, diabetes, and cancer but with scarce verified ligands. The proved peptide ligands of NTR1 show retention time of 4.64 ± 0.04 min and 1.83 ± 0.05 min with Kd of 40.00 μM and 49.13 μM respectively in the NTR1 column. Extracts of Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (ZSS) were further applied to the NTR1 column and a natural product, spinosin, was discovered with estimated Kd of 5.16 μM and further identified by LC-MS. Molecular docking reveals that spinosin binds to orthosteric pocket of NTR1. Taken together, we developed a hybrid method for immobilizing GPCRs and fabricating the bioactive chromatographic column for measuring drug interactions and identified a new ligand binding to NTR1.

articles.title: Altered gut microbial dynamics and the antivascular remodeling effect of carnosine in hypobaric hypoxic pulmonary hypertension rats.
articles.abstract: Exposure to chronic hypobaric hypoxia provokes marked alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolome, yet the functional significance of histidine-derived metabolites in hypobaric hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains underexplored. Here, we employ 16S rDNA, metagenomic, and untargeted metabolomic sequencing to characterize longitudinal shifts in the fecal microbiota and metabolites during hypobaric hypoxic PH development in Sprague-Dawley rats. Fecal carnosine levels and the abundance of its producer, Ruminococcus bromii , both decrease significantly over 28 days of hypobaric hypoxia ( P < 0.05). Spearman correlation shows that carnosine is inversely correlated with the percentage of pulmonary arteriole media thickness (MT%; r = –0.8741, P < 0.001). Therapeutic supplementation with carnosine restores systemic and pulmonary antioxidant defenses and attenuates vascular remodeling without altering right ventricular pressures. In vitro , carnosine inhibits hypoxia‐induced pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell (PASMC) proliferation and migration and suppresses nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) accumulation. These findings reveal dynamic gut-lung crosstalk in hypobaric hypoxic PH and nominate carnosine as a metabolite‐based intervention to mitigate hypoxia‐driven pulmonary vascular remodeling.

articles.title: Prenatal phthalate exposure and early childhood asthma: a prospective birth cohort study from the Japan Environment and Children's study.
authors: Japan Environment Children’s Study JECS Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal phthalate exposure has been associated with allergic outcomes; however, evidence linking it to childhood asthma remains inconsistent. Using data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS), we examined the association between prenatal phthalate exposure measured during the first and second/third trimesters and current asthma in early childhood.

METHODS: Among 9,707 mother-child pairs with urinary phthalate measurements in both the first and second/third trimesters, 8,554, 8,048, and 7,722 singleton children with available asthma data were analyzed at ages 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. Current asthma was defined as wheezing in the past 12 months together with caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed asthma during that period (or ongoing asthma treatment). In the primary analyses, first-trimester, second/third-trimester, and average concentrations were analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for maternal allergy or asthma history, smoking, education, household income, parity, and recruitment center, with multiple imputation and false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional analyses included sex stratification, generalized estimating equations, mutually adjusted trimester-specific models, alternative asthma definitions, and quantile g-computation.

RESULTS: Current asthma prevalence was 6.4, 5.8, and 4.4% at 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. In the primary analyses, no associations remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Similarly, generalized estimating equation and quantile g-computation analyses showed no significant overall associations after FDR correction. In additional analyses after FDR correction, the average monomethyl phthalate (MMP) concentration was positively associated with International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC)-defined asthma at age 2, while first-trimester and average MMP concentrations were positively associated with later-confirmed age-2 asthma. These findings were not consistently observed across ages or analytic approaches.

CONCLUSION: Prenatal phthalate exposure was not consistently associated with current asthma in early childhood in this large Japanese birth cohort. Although certain MMP associations emerged in secondary and sensitivity analyses, the overall pattern of findings did not support a robust association.

articles.title: Neryl acetate modulates JNK signaling in streptozotocin-induced diabetic nephropathy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major complication of diabetes mellitus and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease. Oxidative stress and inflammation play key roles in DN progression and are associated with activation of the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) pathway. This study evaluated the nephroprotective effects of neryl acetate (NA) in streptozotocin-nicotinamide (STZ-NAD)-induced diabetic rats. Diabetes was induced in Wistar rats, followed by treatment with NA (25, 50, and 75 mg/kg). DN rats showed significant hyperglycemia, renal dysfunction, dyslipidemia, increased oxidative stress, and elevated inflammatory cytokines (p < 0.0001). NA treatment produced dose-dependent improvements, with 50 and 75 mg/kg significantly reducing blood glucose, improving renal function, restoring antioxidant enzyme levels, and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines, comparable to glimepiride. Histopathological findings confirmed marked recovery of renal architecture. These findings suggest that NA may attenuate oxidative stress and inflammation, thereby modulating upstream activators of JNK signaling and reducing renal injury. In conclusion, NA exhibits significant nephroprotective effects and may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for diabetic nephropathy.

articles.title: Stanniocalcin-PAPP-A-IGFBP-IGF axis and all-cause mortality risk in aged and middle-aged adults: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Growth hormone & IGF research : official journal of the Growth Hormone Research Society and the International IGF Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is associated with longevity, yet its activity is tightly regulated by IGF-binding proteins (IGFBPs) and the cleavage of IGF-IGFBP complexes, mediated by pappalysins (PAPP-A and PAPP-A2) and inhibited by stanniocalcins (STC1 and STC2). However, the association of these IGF-1-regulating proteins with mortality remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between serum STC-PAPP-A-IGFBP-IGF axis proteins and all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Scopus, following the JBI and PRISMA parameters for study inclusion through December 2025. Findings were analyzed using vote counting based on direction of effect and synthesized according to SWiM guidelines for systematic reviews without meta-analysis, given exposure heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024556008).

RESULTS: Thirty-eight observational studies were included across general and disease-specific cohorts, including cardiovascular, metabolic, cancer, and chronic kidney disease populations. Elevated IGFBP-1, IGFBP-2, and IGFBP-4 were associated with increased all-cause mortality, whereas higher IGFBP-3 was associated with lower risk. Overall, IGF-1 associations were inconsistent. Moreover, circulating PAPP-A was associated with increased all-cause mortality, with limited evidence suggesting a similar trend for STC2.

CONCLUSION: IGF-1 bioavailability-regulating proteins are associated with all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults. These findings suggest a role of IGF-1 signaling dysregulation through altered binary/ternary complexes in aging, supporting circulating STC-PAPP-A-IGFBP-IGF axis proteins as mechanistically grounded biomarkers for mortality risk stratification.

articles.title: Bayesian Survival Analysis for Heart Failure Clinical Trials in the Presence of Competing Risks.
Transcriptomics Identifies a Small Set of Circulating Biomarkers and Signaling Pathways Dysregulated in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is sometimes challenging to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) from other cardiomyopathies with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). At present, no circulating biomarkers to distinguish HCM have been established.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to identify plasma microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers unique to HCM.

METHODS: In this multicenter case-control study, the authors performed comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling in cases with HCM and controls with hypertensive LVH, transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), and aortic stenosis (AS). For each disease group, they chronologically split the patients into training and test sets. The authors identified miRNAs that were significantly (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05) upregulated or downregulated in HCM compared with hypertensive LVH. They made the same comparisons between HCM and ATTR-CM and between HCM and AS. They determined miRNAs that were consistently upregulated or downregulated in HCM throughout all 3 comparisons. Then, they selected miRNAs independently associated with HCM after adjusting for potential confounders. Using the selected miRNAs, the authors developed a logistic regression model to distinguish HCM in the training set. They calculated the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve in the test set.

RESULTS: The authors analyzed 2,656 miRNAs in patients with HCM (n = 294), hypertensive LVH (n = 321), ATTR-CM (n = 167), and AS (n = 38). They identified 3 miRNAs (miR-454-3p, miR-98-5p, and miR-5581-3p). The logistic regression model using the 3 miRNAs had an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97) with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.90 in the test set.

CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling identified a small set of circulating miRNAs to distinguish HCM from other cardiomyopathies with LVH.

articles.title: Development and validation of prediction models for heart failure with improved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 10-60% of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) patients may transition to heart failure with improved ejection fraction (HFimpEF), a clinically meaningful phenotype associated with better prognosis. However, existing prediction tools demonstrate suboptimal discrimination and poor clinical utility. We aimed to develop and validate interpretable models for HFimpEF prediction by comparing logistic regression with ensemble machine learning.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,257 HFrEF patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of USTC (March 2015-October 2023), split into training (n = 1,006) and internal validation (n = 251) sets. External validation used data from 310 patients across eight hospitals in Anhui Province (January 2024-January 2025). HFimpEF was defined as LVEF increase ≥10% to >40%.
