Five models were developed: data-driven logistic regression (Model 1); literature-based logistic regression (Model 2) with 5 common predictors validated in both BIOSTAT-CHF and ASIAN-HF cohorts; random forest (Model 3) and XGBoost (Model 4), both tuned via 5-fold cross-validation; and a simplified ensemble (Model 5) that averaged the predicted probabilities of Models 1, 3, and 4, then calibrated the average via logistic regression. Performance was assessed using AUC for discrimination, Brier score with calibration plots for calibration, decision curve analysis for clinical utility, and DeLong's test for model comparisons; SHAP analysis was applied for interpretability of Models 3 and 4.

RESULTS: Median age was 65 years (IQR 53-73); 69.9% were male. Multivariable analysis identified seven predictors: age (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.99), BMI (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.09), systolic blood pressure (per 10 mmHg increase, OR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.25), prior PCI (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.79), HDL-C (OR 2.48, 95% CI 1.36-4.50), FT3 (OR 1.21, 95% CI 1.02-1.45), and LVESD (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.99). In external validation, Model 5 showed superior discrimination (AUC 0.67 vs. 0.60 for Model 2, P = 0.004) but poorer calibration (Brier score 0.34). Model 1 demonstrated balanced performance (AUC 0.66, Brier score 0.23).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that ensemble learning methods provide a moderate enhancement in discrimination for HFimpEF prediction, while logistic regression models exhibit superior robustness and interpretability. We have developed an online tool (https://alslyy-wq.shinyapps.io/USTC-HF-HFimpEF-Prediction/) that integrates both methodologies to facilitate practical HFimpEF risk assessment.

articles.title: Assessing regional pulmonary response to methacholine and mannitol challenge in asthma patients using hyperpolarized helium-3 magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ventilation heterogeneity is a feature of asthmatic bronchoconstriction and contributes to airway hyperresponsiveness and disease expression. This study characterized ventilation heterogeneity using hyperpolarized helium-3 magnetic resonance imaging (HP-MRI) in patients with mild asthma following methacholine and mannitol inhalational challenge and determined whether topographical differences exist in the response to these different stimuli.

METHODS: Six patients with mild asthma were recruited (1 male, 5 females; age 35.3±11.4 years; BMI 22.8±3.0 kg/m2). Patients underwent HP-MRI and forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) at baseline and following crossover methacholine and mannitol challenge on separate days. Ventilation heterogeneity was assessed qualitatively and using ventilation defect percentage (VDP). Comparisons between the pre- and post-provocation scans, and the difference in regional changes induced by methacholine and mannitol were performed.

RESULTS: FEV1 was significantly reduced (p=0.0002) by methacholine (94.9±15.1 vs 70.2±9.7 %predicted) and mannitol (94.5±14.6 vs 73.8±18.1 %predicted). Accompanying this was a significant increase in VDP (p=0.02) from 8.5±4.5 to 19.8±6.9% after methacholine, and 8.4±3.4 to 17.8±6.3% after mannitol challenge. Regional differences were observed between the two provocation agents with methacholine having a larger impact on the peripheral airways (p=0.005) and mannitol on the central airways (p<0.05), despite comparable changes in FEV1 (p=0.62) and VDP (p=0.46).

CONCLUSIONS: Regional differences in ventilation heterogeneity exist when asthmatic airways are subjected to methacholine and mannitol challenge. These findings give new insights into the regional pathobiology of airflow obstruction in patients with asthma and highlight the role of HP-MRI as a valuable tool in understanding airway disease.

articles.title: Timing of diverting ileostomy closure after low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of early and delayed closure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare early and delayed diverting ileostomy closure after low anterior resection for rectal cancer, focusing on postoperative morbidity and recovery outcomes, and to assess the certainty of available evidence.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 26th April, 2026. Five comparative studies (four randomized trials and one prospective cohort; 512 participants) were included. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated overall post-closure morbidity as the primary outcome and severe complications, index-to-closure interval, postoperative hospital stay, operative time, and reoperation as secondary outcomes. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Overall morbidity occurred in 52/257 patients after early closure and 50/255 after delayed closure (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.66-1.71; τ²=0.12; I²=40%). Severe complications and reoperation did not differ statistically, with confidence intervals compatible with benefit or harm. The index-to-closure interval was 107.09 days shorter with early closure (95% CI - 153.01 to - 61.17; τ²=2023.39; I²=96%); this process measure was largely inherent to the group definitions. Hospital stay and operative time did not differ statistically.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in postoperative morbidity but does not establish equivalence. Early closure may be considered in selected patients after postoperative recovery and assessment of anastomotic integrity; however, these findings do not support routine early closure in all patients.

articles.title: Recurrent belly dancer dyskinesia in pregnancy with postpartum resolution.
articles.abstract: Belly dancer dyskinesia (BDD) is a rare movement disorder characterized by involuntary, repetitive contractions of the abdominal wall. Pregnancy-associated BDD is exceptionally uncommon, and recurrence in subsequent pregnancies has rarely been reported. We describe the case of a 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy who developed involuntary abdominal movements at 16 weeks. Her medical history included hypertension and multiple uterine fibroids. Neurological assessment, laboratory investigations, and spinal magnetic resonance imaging were unremarkable, and a clinical diagnosis of BDD was established. Symptoms persisted throughout pregnancy and resolved immediately after delivery. Two years later, during a second pregnancy, similar movements recurred at 15 weeks, again resolving completely after delivery. Recurrence during two consecutive pregnancies suggests a pregnancy-related trigger for BDD, and complete postpartum resolution highlights the self-limiting course of this benign condition.

articles.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the eHealth-faciLitated SMILe-integrated care model on treatment burden, quality of life and graft-versus-host disease after allogeneic stem cell transplantation: results of two European randomized controlled implementation studies.
articles.abstract: The SMILe Integrated Care Model (SMILe-ICM) has previously demonstrated feasibility, successful implementation, and promising effects on survival, re-hospitalization, and cost-effectiveness following allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT). To complement these findings and provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the intervention's effects, we evaluated patient-reported and clinical secondary outcomes from two RCTs. Data from two hybrid effectiveness-implementation RCTs conducted at two European alloSCT centers (Germany, Switzerland) were analyzed. Adult alloSCT recipients were randomized 1:1 to usual care (UCG) or the SMILe-ICM, a multicomponent intervention combining eHealth with advanced practice nurse-led self-management support. Treatment burden was assessed using the Patients' Experience of Treatment and Self-Management (PETS 2.0), HRQoL using the EQ-5D-5 L, and GvHD outcomes using EBMT-registry data. Analyses followed an intention-to-treat approach. The current study examined data from 152 patients (76 SMILe-ICM, 76 UCG). Treatment burden was lower in the SMILe-ICM group, with significant differences in five dimensions. Both groups' HRQoL improved over time without significant between-group differences. The cumulative incidence of acute GvHD was lower in the SMILe-ICM group than in the UCG (34.2% vs. 55.3%; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.33-0.88; p = 0.01); chronic GvHD did not differ significantly (p = 0.64). SMILe-ICM reduced treatment burden and was associated with a lower cumulative incidence of grades II-IV acute GvHD, while HRQoL and chronic GvHD did not differ significantly between groups. The acute GvHD finding warrants further investigation to determine whether and through which pathways integrated APN-led survivorship care may influence post-alloSCT clinical outcomes.

articles.title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
articles.journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses.

RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Estimated Small Dense LDL Cholesterol and Coronary Artery Disease in Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Recent evidence reports good agreement between measured and estimated small-dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (EsdLDL-C) using a readily applicable formula. Its clinical utility in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) has not yet been evaluated. We aimed to evaluate the sex-specific associations of pre-treatment EsdLDL-C with coronary artery disease (CAD) prevalence in adult patients with HeFH and its discriminative value beyond LDL-C.

METHODS: Data from consecutively recruited adults with a clinical diagnosis of HeFH from an ongoing registry (HELLAS-FH, n = 3,276) were analyzed. Patient demographics, lipid parameters, CAD risk factors, and CAD prevalence at registry enrollment were evaluated. EsdLDL-C was calculated at pre-treatment (i.e., before any hypolipidemic therapy initiation) using the Sampson equation.

RESULTS: EsdLDL-C was associated with an increased prevalence of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, a higher body mass index and triglycerides, and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. EsdLDL-C was also the strongest independent lipid-associated factor for CAD (OR: 1.24, p＜0.001). This association was more pronounced in women (OR 1.57, p＜0.001). EsdLDL-C showed higher CAD discrimination than LDL-C (AUC 0.611 vs. 0.522). Incorporating EsdLDL-C into the best discriminative model improved discriminative ability vs the core model (AUC 0.831 vs 0.828, p = 0.038) and overall model fit (ΔAIC) = -10.3). This incremental predictive value was driven predominantly by females (ΔAIC = -14.1; AUC 0.787 vs 0.769, p = 0.015).

CONCLUSION: In a large sample of patients with clinical HeFH, EsdLDL-C was incrementally associated with CAD beyond LDL-C. This finding was more pronounced in women. The clinical utility of this readily available lipid marker as a risk enhancer should therefore be further investigated.

articles.title: [Posterior periventricular white matter lesions as a clue to the diagnosis of folate deficiency with compound heterozygous MTHFR polymorphisms: a case report].
articles.abstract: An 18-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of persistent dizziness. Brain MRI revealed bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles. Subsequently, she developed distal paresthesia of the extremities and was admitted for further evaluation. Neurological examination demonstrated abnormal ocular movements in the primary gaze position, horizontal gaze-evoked nystagmus, gait instability, and distal sensory disturbance. There was no antecedent infection, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable. Based on the clinical course and findings, an autoimmune-mediated brainstem-cerebellar disorder was suspected, and high-dose intravenous corticosteroid therapy was administered, resulting in improvement of ocular abnormalities and gait disturbance. Meanwhile, further investigation of the incidental posterior periventricular white matter lesions-considered unrelated to the presenting symptoms-revealed low serum folate levels and compound heterozygous genotype of the MTHFR gene. Vitamin supplementation was initiated accordingly. Notably, the patient's father was also found to have the same MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype. This case suggests that bilateral periventricular white matter lesions adjacent to the posterior horns may represent an early radiological marker of folate deficiency associated with MTHFR gene compound heterozygous genotype, even in the absence of overt folate-deficiency symptoms. Recognition of this imaging pattern may facilitate early diagnosis and intervention, potentially preventing future neurological or systemic complications.

articles.title: [Acute management of minor ischemic stroke].
articles.abstract: This review summarizes acute-phase treatment for minor ischemic stroke, focusing on the latest evidence for reperfusion therapy and acute antithrombotic treatment. In patients with large vessel occlusion, the benefit of mechanical thrombectomy is not established and the risk of hemorrhage exists; therefore, indications should be judged carefully for each patient. Intravenous thrombolysis provides limited benefit in non-disabling cases, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) can be an option. For minor non-cardioembolic stroke, early DAPT is recommended, and the possible role of adding argatroban is promising, especially for suspected branch atheromatous disease. For cardioembolic stroke, early initiation of a direct oral anticoagulant is desirable in mild cases without a large infarct.

articles.title: [Eltrombopag-associated bilateral internal jugular vein thrombosis presenting with visual impairment and marked intracranial hypertension: a case report].
articles.abstract: We report an 86-year-old man with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who developed bilateral internal jugular vein (IJV) thrombosis during treatment with eltrombopag (EPAG). He had experienced multiple cerebral infarctions over several months, but their cause had remained undetermined and warfarin therapy had been continued. Nine days before admission to our hospital, he developed visual impairment, and ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral papilledema. He was admitted for further evaluation. Lumbar puncture demonstrated markedly elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (53 ‍cm H2O), suggesting intracranial hypertension, and contrast-enhanced MR venography demonstrated bilateral sigmoid sinus thrombosis and bilateral IJV thrombosis. Although early thrombotic changes were retrospectively identifiable on plain MRI obtained at the previous hospital, the diagnosis was delayed because we did not initially recognize the possibility of EPAG-associated thrombosis, and visual impairment persisted despite treatment. In patients receiving EPAG, thrombotic complications should always be considered, and careful assessment of abnormal intraluminal venous signals on plain MRI is important for early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: HSPA1B alleviates MEHP-induced developmental arrest of mouse preimplantation embryos by mediating ACSL4 ubiquitin degradation and suppressing lipid peroxidation.
articles.journal: The Journal of reproduction and development
articles.abstract: Lipid homeostasis is essential for the morula-to-blastocyst transition during mammalian preimplantation development, and excessive lipid peroxidation commonly induces developmental arrest at this stage. The heat shock protein HSPA1B participates in cellular proteostasis and lipid metabolism. However, its regulatory functions in early embryogenesis remain unclear. In the present study, knockdown of Hspa1b impaired blastocyst formation in mouse embryos. Proteomic screening suggested a physical interaction between HSPA1B and the lipid metabolic enzyme ACSL4, which was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation and cytoplasmic co-localization analyses in morula-stage embryos. Hspa1b depletion did not alter Acsl4 transcription, but stabilized endogenous ACSL4 protein, resulting in lipid droplet accumulation, elevated intracellular ferrous ion levels, and increased lipid peroxidation. Concurrent knockdown of Hspa1b and Acsl4 rescued embryonic developmental defects and restored lipid homeostasis. Mechanistically, HSPA1B mediates K48-linked polyubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of ACSL4. Exposure to mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP) triggered embryonic arrest, ACSL4 accumulation, and oxidative lipid damage, whereas Hspa1b overexpression ameliorated MEHP-associated embryonic toxicity. Overall, these results demonstrate that HSPA1B targets ACSL4 for K48 ubiquitination-dependent degradation to maintain lipid homeostasis required for blastocyst development. In addition, HSPA1B mitigated MEHP-induced injury in mouse preimplantation embryos by defining a regulatory axis for lipid metabolism and toxicant responses during early embryogenesis.

articles.title: May - Thurner syndrome: a case report of a lethal undiagnosed left iliac vein thrombosis.
articles.abstract: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS), also known as iliac vein compression syndrome, is a pro-thrombotic condition caused by the compression of the left iliac vein by the right common iliac artery, often resulting in deep vein thrombosis (DVT). MTS accounts for 2-5% of all DVT cases and is often underdiagnosed due to the difficulty of assessing the deep pelvic veins. We present the case of a 63-year-old female with a history of Crohn's disease and scoliosis, who developed lower limb pain and venous ulcers. Despite negative Doppler ultrasound and exclusion of other conditions such as diabetes and vasculitis, the patient deteriorated after a fall, leading to cardiogenic shock and death. Autopsy revealed a thrombus in the left iliac vein and an embolus in the inferior vena cava, causing fatal venous obstruction. Histological examination confirmed thrombotic formations in both sites and assigned the iliac thrombus to phase III of thrombus organization, indicating that it predated the terminal event by several days. This case underscores the importance of comprehensive evaluation in patients with lower limb ulcers and pain, as Doppler ultrasound alone may not detect deeper venous abnormalities such as MTS. Advanced imaging techniques, including multi-detector computed tomography venography or magnetic resonance venography, may be necessary to diagnose MTS in such cases, preventing life-threatening complications.

articles.title: ConComp: Constraining and compensating latent representations for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
articles.abstract: Semi-supervised learning has significantly advanced medical image segmentation under limited annotation scenarios. However, existing semi-supervised medical image segmentation (SSMIS) methods based on consistency regularization and pseudo-labeling may be affected by internal covariate shift (ICS), which may disturb feature stability and reduce pseudo-label reliability during training. In this work, we investigate how ICS affects feature stability and pseudo-label reliability in SSMIS. Based on this analysis, we propose ConComp, a unified framework that mitigates ICS from a statistical perspective by introducing distribution-aware latent constraints and compensating for latent distribution discrepancies. Specifically, we introduce a Distribution-Aware Feature Constraint (DAFC) mechanism that derives distribution-aware latent constraints from unlabeled feature statistics and residually integrates them into labeled features, thereby reducing changes in their distributions during training. In addition, we propose a Latent Distribution Discrepancy Compensation (L2DC) mechanism that treats the discrepancy between labeled and unlabeled representations as an informative signal to guide feature fusion, thereby compensating for missing structural cues and improving generalization. Extensive experiments on three challenging SSMIS benchmarks, including BraTS2019, LiTS2017, and Pancreas-NIH, demonstrate that ConComp consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/1jayyang/ConComp.

articles.title: Continuous Stellate Ganglion Block Bridging to Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in a Long QT Syndrome Neonate.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) with neonatal onset carries a high risk of drug-refractory ventricular arrhythmias. Continuous percutaneous left stellate ganglion block (PLSGB) as a bridge to left cardiac sympathetic denervation (LCSD) is unexplored in neonates.

CASE SUMMARY: We present a newborn female with in utero onset LQTS, complicated by functional 2:1 atrioventricular block and torsades de pointes (TdP). Despite pacemaker implantation, propranolol, and mexiletine, TdP recurred. At 25 days of life, continuous PLSGB with ropivacaine suppressed TdP. At 4 months, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)-LCSD was performed, with no ventricular arrhythmia recurrence in 24 months.

NOVELTY: First reported case of continuous PLSGB in a neonate with LQTS; among the few VATS-LCSD cases under 1 year.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Early sympathetic neuromodulation should be considered in high-risk pediatric LQTS when medical therapy fails, as a bridge to LCSD. VATS-LCSD is feasible and safe even under 1 year.

articles.title: Corticomuscular coupling alterations during task-dependent bimanual coordination after stroke: A multimodal functional near-infrared spectroscopy-surface electromyography analysis.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke bimanual coordination dysfunction severely impairs activities of daily living. However, the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly regarding central-peripheral coupling characteristics under different bimanual coordination tasks and their distinction from aging effects. This study included 32 chronic subcortical stroke patients and 29 healthy controls. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy and surface electromyography signals were synchronously acquired during the execution of symmetrical and asymmetrical bimanual coordination tasks. Analyzed indices included cortical activation patterns, functional connectivity, corticomuscular coupling characterized by transfer entropy, intermuscular coupling, and muscle synergies. Correlations between these indices and the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity and Modified Barthel Index were also evaluated. The results showed that during the symmetrical task, the ascending muscle-to-cortex connectivity was significantly reduced in the patient group, and this index was significantly positively correlated with the Modified Barthel Index. Brain functional connectivity and cortical activation were significantly increased in the patient group, and the connectivity from the ipsilesional prefrontal cortex to the contralesional SAC was significantly negatively correlated with Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity scores. Additionally, intermuscular coupling was significantly weakened, and muscle synergy patterns were abnormal in the patient group. During the asymmetrical task, no significant group differences in corticomuscular coupling were found, but brain functional connectivity and cortical activation were both significantly increased, and the connectivity from the ipsilesional supplementary motor area to the contralesional supplementary motor area was significantly positively correlated with MBI. Intermuscular coupling was significantly weakened, and muscle synergy patterns were abnormal. Attribution analysis suggested that cortical hyperactivation patterns and abnormal muscle synergies mainly reflect stroke effects, while abnormal sensory cortex activation and altered corticomuscular coupling may be influenced by both stroke and aging. This study suggests that post-stroke bimanual coordination impairment is closely related to selective damage to sensory feedback pathways, manifested as task-dependent reductions in ascending (muscle-to-cortex) corticomuscular coupling and compensatory cortical reorganization. Multimodal neurophysiological indicators may serve as potential quantitative tools for assessing upper limb function after stroke, but age-matched control studies are essential to dissociate stroke effects from aging effects.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided versus open surgical central venous access in children: A systematic review.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are essential in pediatric care for long-term venous access. While tunneled CVCs have traditionally been placed using open surgical venotomy or cut-down (OS), ultrasound-guided (USG) percutaneous insertion is widely used. However, no systematic review has yet evaluated pediatric evidence directly comparing both approaches. We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing USG and OS placement of CVCs in patients younger than 18 years. PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched until September 2025. The primary outcome was successful catheter placement; secondary outcomes included infection, thrombosis, venous diameter after catheter removal, and procedure duration. Five RCTs with 587 children were included. Placement success was comparable between techniques (97.5% USG vs. 95.7% OS; RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.96-1.05; moderate-certainty evidence). Infection rates did not differ significantly. USG was associated with a significantly lower risk of thrombosis (RR 0.34, 95% CI 0.14-0.82), consistently shorter procedure times, and better preservation of venous diameter, although the certainty of evidence for these outcomes was very low. USG placement achieves comparable success to OS but may offer procedural and vessel-preservation benefits.

articles.title: Myocardial infarction detection framework using cardiac motion estimation with deformable registration field.
articles.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Among them, myocardial infarction (MI), which is characterized by abnormal myocardial motion, remains a critically important condition to detect. Accurate diagnosis of MI requires detailed motion analysis; however, motion-based assessment is time-consuming and imposes a considerable burden on physicians. Moreover, most previous studies have relied on local motion descriptors or limited shape features, resulting in suboptimal detection performance.

METHODS: To address these limitations, we propose a deep learning framework, termed MambaMorph-Motion Infarction Detector (MMMID), for myocardial infarction detection from cardiac CT images. The proposed pipeline integrates semantic segmentation, sequential deformable registration using MambaMorph, and a DenseNet-based classification module to effectively leverage rich spatiotemporal myocardial motion information across the cardiac cycle.

RESULTS: The proposed method enables accurate tracking of myocardial motion aligned with anatomical structures by associating time-resolved motion fields with corresponding CT volumes. MMMID achieved an accuracy of 91.92% and an AUC of 0.9335 on an in-house cardiac CT dataset. Compared with the CT-only configuration, the integration of sequential motion fields improved recall, suggesting that motion information provides complementary diagnostic cues for myocardial infarction detection rather than replacing anatomical CT information.

CONCLUSION: The proposed framework enables myocardial infarction detection by jointly leveraging cardiac anatomy and estimated myocardial motion. Although CT appearance remained a strong source of discriminative information, sequential motion fields contributed complementary functional information, particularly for improving sensitivity to infarction cases. MMMID may serve as a supportive tool for automated cardiac CT analysis and could help reduce the burden of motion-based assessment in clinical workflows.

articles.title: Recommendations for the Multimodal Management of Malignant Bowel Obstructions: Results of a North American Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a challenging clinical problem requiring teams to balance complex oncologic disease, limited treatment options, and patient prognosis and values as they approach end of life. Presently, there is limited high-quality evidence to guide decision-making for MBO patients.

OBJECTIVE: A multidisciplinary modified Delphi process was undertaken to create guidance and support clinical decision-making in the medical and surgical care of this patient population.

METHODS: Multidisciplinary experts from all specialties regularly caring for MBO in Canada and the United States were invited for participation, including Acute Care Surgery, Surgical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, Gastroenterology, Radiology, Medical Oncology, and Palliative Care. Statements were evaluated through two rounds of surveys and a consensus meeting, with an a priori threshold of 80% agreement for approval.

RESULTS: Forty-nine final evidence-informed statements were included following expert consensus review pertaining to Patient Assessment, Medical Management, Surgical Management, and Palliative Management, in addition to a unifying definition of MBO. Consensus statements address aspects of complex MBO care, including but not limited to, optimal preoperative evaluation and multidisciplinary review; timing and use of steroids, motility, and antisecretory agents; contraindications to surgery; key facets of consent and perioperative decision making; framework for the nuanced use of gastrostomies and IV fluids in the end-of-life setting.

CONCLUSIONS: This Modified Delphi consensus provides multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the care of patients with this challenging problem. These expert approved statements provide much-needed clinical guidance to support best care balanced with patient values and avoidance of undue harm.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Trends in Suicide: Sociodemographic, Economic, and Environmental Factors.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Suicide is one of the world's leading public health problems, with more than 720,000 deaths annually. Suicide has traditionally been studied from an individual perspective. However, research has increasingly highlighted the influence of community-level factors on suicide risk. This study aimed to (1) analyze the spatial distribution of suicide mortality at the provincial level in Spain (2018-2022); (2) perform stratified analyses by sex and age group; and (3) compare suicide risk across different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. We used data from the Spanish National Institute of Statistics on 17,809 suicide deaths in 47 peninsular provinces between 2018 and 2022. Covariates included sociodemographic (e.g., aging rate, population density), economic (e.g., unemployment, GDP), and environmental (e.g., temperature) indicators. Bayesian hierarchical spatial Poisson regression models were fitted to estimate suicide risk and identify relevant contextual variables. The general spatial model revealed a higher risk of suicide in provinces with lower population density, higher aging rates, and lower health expenditure. Other covariates such as gross domestic product, unemployment, or temperature were associated with specific sex or age groups. Suicide risk was highest in the northwestern provinces and lowest in the central regions. Stratified analyses showed similar patterns across gender and age groups, and between time periods, with some variations in spatial distribution. This study reveals significant spatial heterogeneity in suicide risk across Spanish regions, influenced by sociodemographic, economic, and environmental factors. These findings underline the importance of regionally tailored suicide prevention policies, especially in aging and low-density areas with low health investment.

articles.title: Mechanistic Reorganization of Step Work in Hemiparetic Walking: Modeling and Center-of-Mass Power/Work Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-stroke hemiparetic gait is commonly characterized by reduced paretic propulsion and interlimb asymmetry, yet the mechanical consequences of severely insufficient push-off for gait regulation remain unclear.

METHODS: We examine how unilateral push-off deficiency reorganizes mechanical work across the gait cycle and regulates step length. We explored the mechanisms underlying how and why hemiparetic gait is expressed using a simple powered model and compared the model predictions against empirical data.

RESULTS: The model predicts a threshold behavior: when paretic push-off falls below ~ 25% of optimal, compensation shifts from post-transition restoration to pre-transition energy induction, and reduced paretic step length becomes mechanically favorable, which is also seen empirically. When paretic late-stance push-off is absent, early-stance positive work emerges, vertical COM motion collapses to a single pendular motion per stride, and paretic limb step length remains disproportionately short relative to speed. As limited paretic push-off emerges, COM undergoes double pendular motion per stride, and the four-phase COM power structure previously reported in able-bodied walking reappears. Reduced single-support duration and paretic positive work capacity constrains step length, which increases step length asymmetry and stance-phase energy dissipation. Paretic net COM work remains negative across speeds, whereas the nonparetic limb exhibits persistent positive net work.

CONCLUSION: Hemiparetic walking can be considered a constrained optimization problem in which decreased step length and phase-redistributed work may reflect mechanical adaptations to impaired transition mechanics, extending classical step-to-step transition and total step work theories to pathological gait.

articles.title: Mapping the prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus and multiple sclerosis in Middle East and North Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) prevalence has increased to medium-to-high levels in several countries of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), while Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) exposure as one of the most consistently reported MS risk factors is common throughout the region. This systematic review and meta-analysis descriptively mapped published estimates of MS prevalence and EBV seroprevalence alongside each other in MENA countries. We searched MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science until 18 June 2022. Observational studies reporting MS prevalence or EBV seroprevalence among healthy MENA populations were eligible. For quantitative EBV synthesis, we restricted analyses to studies reporting VCA-IgG seroprevalence to improve comparability across studies. Studies reporting the prevalence of specific type of MS or those assessing EBV infection by IgA antibodies or non-serological tissues or without a control arm representing general population were excluded. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools were used to determine the quality of the studies. The heterogeneity of studies was evaluated using I2 statistics. Results of the fix-effects meta-analysis were presented using prevalence and 95% confidence intervals. Of 4,323 records identified, 131 studies were included. The pooled MS prevalence was 51.02 per 100,000 population, and the pooled EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence was 75%. In time-stratified analyses, pooled MS prevalence increased from 12 per 100,000 in studies conducted up to 2000 to 58 per 100,000 in studies conducted from 2011 to 2022. Pooled EBV seroprevalence increased from 71 to 75% across the same periods. These findings suggest that the prevalence of both MS and EBV has increased over time, with a more pronounced increase observed for MS. Between-study heterogeneity was extreme for both outcomes (I2 = 100%), reflecting substantial variation in geography, populations, study methods, diagnostic approaches, and study periods. Published MS prevalence estimates and EBV VCA-IgG seroprevalence estimates showed co-occurring uprising patterns in the available MENA literature. Based on a probable ecological correlation between the increasing prevalence of MS and EBV, the preventive measures against EBV infection may potentially yield favorable outcomes in terms of MS prevention. Future longitudinal, population-based studies with standardized MS ascertainment and age-specific EBV serology are needed.

articles.title: Prediabetes and diabetes as drivers of fibrosis in MASLD: roles of obesity, adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Prediabetes and type 2 diabetes have been associated with more severe metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but not all individuals have the same risk and the metabolic drivers remain incompletely understood. To understand why, we examined the roles of obesity, adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance in the development of significant liver fibrosis (fibrosis stage ≥F2) in adults across the glycaemic spectrum.

METHODS: We performed a prospective, cross-sectional study in a real-world setting of adults attending primary care or endocrinology/diabetes clinics. Transient elastography was used to diagnose steatosis (controlled attenuation parameter ≥274 dB/m) and clinically significant liver fibrosis (vibration-controlled transient elastography liver stiffness measurement ≥8.2 kPa). When ≥F2 was suspected, MR-based imaging or liver biopsy was used to improve stratification. MASLD and significant fibrosis were compared across glycaemic and BMI categories and severity of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR; predominantly hepatic) and adipose tissue insulin resistance (assessed by adipose tissue insulin resistance [Adipo-IR]).

RESULTS: Among the 1446 participants, the prevalence of MASLD increased across glycaemic categories from 39% in participants with normoglycaemia, to 55% in those with prediabetes and to 68% in type 2 diabetes. Clinically significant fibrosis also increased across groups, being 1%, 6% and 12%, respectively. In prediabetes, clinically significant fibrosis was rare in lean or overweight individuals even though most had associated cardiometabolic risk factors, but this increased fourfold in individuals with obesity, particularly when associated with severe adipose tissue and systemic insulin resistance. Having obesity and type 2 diabetes had the highest prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis (16%), and again, mostly if associated with insulin resistance. Most participants with clinically significant fibrosis were in the highest quintiles of Adipo-IR or HOMA-IR (Q4-Q5).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: In a real-world cohort from primary care/endocrinology clinics, the prevalence of MASLD increased in a stepwise manner with glycaemic and BMI categories, but the prevalence of fibrosis did not increase in the same stepwise manner and remained rare in the absence of obesity, or in obesity without significant insulin resistance. Prediabetes was a risk factor for significant fibrosis mainly in individuals with obesity and significant insulin resistance. In the context of current guidelines, MASLD risk-stratification may be improved in primary care by establishing the metabolic impact of obesity/diabetes (i.e. assessing insulin resistance by HOMA-IR).

articles.title: Understanding diagnostic challenges and identifying priorities to tackle antimicrobial resistance in conflict zones.
articles.abstract: Armed conflict is a key driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Diagnostics are critical tools for limiting the impact of AMR where resources are limited. We analyse how conflict shifts the needs and deliverability of AMR diagnostics and identify opportunities to strengthen scope and capacity in these settings with persistent state-delivered health governance and policy. Key priorities include optimisation of robust diagnostic processing, workload and data sharing tools, and procurement policies suitable for resource-limited settings, including linked electronic workload and data-sharing tools with offline options, to support delivery of individual patient care, infection prevention and control, and surveillance.

articles.title: Better data in, better research out: the data problem in resistant hypertension research.
Impact of clinical risk factors on white matter microstructure in preterm-born infants: investigation with diffusion MRI and tractography at term-equivalent age.
articles.abstract: Premature birth occurs during a phase of intense brain maturation, making white matter (WM) particularly vulnerable to injury. Beyond major lesions, subtle and widespread microstructural alterations also contribute to later neurodevelopmental impairments. We aimed to characterize the impact of key clinical risk factors on global and tract-specific WM microstructure at term-equivalent age (TEA), using 3T-diffusion-MRI data of 111 infants born before 33 weeks of gestation. We implemented a tractography pipeline adapted for use in infants with heterogeneous brain anatomy, including macroscopic abnormalities and lesions, and extracted diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics in sensorimotor tracts: corticospinal tract (CST), superior thalamic radiation (STR), frontal aslant tract (FAT), forceps minor (FMI) and middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP). Associations with risk factors were assessed accounting for age at MRI or global WM microstructure. Tractography succeeded in most infants despite marked anatomical variability and/or overt lesions. Being a male, small for gestational age (SGA) at birth, encountering sepsis and having severe Kidokoro radiological score for WM were associated with altered global WM metrics. At the tract level, CST and STR showed the strongest susceptibility to SGA, prolonged parenteral nutrition, and Kidokoro score. In contrast, associations after adjustment for global WM microstructure suggested that FAT might be less vulnerable than other tracts to extreme prematurity, SGA and invasive ventilation. Findings were partially replicated in infants without macroscopic abnormalities, supporting the presence of WM dysmaturation even in the absence of visible injury. DTI metrics thus provide tract-specific biomarkers of early WM microstructure in preterm infants, which are sensitive to risk factors and could inform targeted prevention and intervention.

articles.title: The ascending aorta and vascular profile in recreational masters runners: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Endurance exercise remodels the large arteries, but whether a recreational training dose is sufficient to induce such remodelling is unclear. Masters recreational runners over 40 years are under-represented in this research. We compared the ascending aortic diameter and vascular profile of these runners with sedentary controls of similar age.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 42 masters recreational runners (at least 20 km per week for at least one year) and 27 sedentary controls, all over 40 years, free of cardiovascular disease and without bicuspid aortic valve or connective tissue disorder. We measured the ascending aortic diameter and left ventricular function by transthoracic echocardiography, and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and the ankle-brachial index (ABI) by oscillometry. Circulating collagen-turnover markers (CTX-I, MMP-2) were assayed. The aortic diameter was compared between groups by regression.

RESULTS: The ascending aorta was wider in runners (3.25 vs. 2.90 cm; p = 0.001; Cliff's delta 0.45). The difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex and height (beta 0.31 cm; p = 0.001) and in sensitivity analyses. No aortic diameter reached 4.0 cm; all remained within normal limits. The ABI was higher in runners (1.07 vs. 1.03; p = 0.007), and baPWV did not differ (p = 0.069); both stayed within normal limits. CTX-I and MMP-2 did not differ, and left ventricular function was preserved.

CONCLUSION: These findings are consistent with modest, exercise-associated aortic remodelling rather than overt aortopathy in recreational masters runners over 40 years.

articles.title: Maternal mid-pregnancy metabolic profiles and growth trajectories across the first 36 months of life in a UK multi-ethnic birth cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the influence of maternal mid-pregnancy metabolomic profiles on offspring anthropometric growth trajectories (weight, length/height, and BMI) across the first 36 months of life in a multi-ethnic birth cohort.

METHODS: This longitudinal study analyzed 1423 mother-child pairs from the Born in Bradford cohort. Using NMR, 147 metabolites were quantified in maternal fasting blood samples collected at 26-28 weeks of gestation. Children's growth trajectories for weight, length/height, and BMI across 0-36 months of life were modeled using latent class growth mixture models. Partial least squares discriminant analysis identified key maternal metabolites distinguishing growth trajectories, followed by linear mixed-effects regression examining associations with WHO growth z-scores adjusted for a minimal set of covariates (ethnicity and gestational diabetes mellitus, GDM).

RESULTS: Three distinct growth trajectories were identified for each anthropometric measure: normative, intermediate, and non-uniform (accelerated for weight and BMI or faltered for length/height). For each growth trajectory, between 30 and 41 metabolites were required to differentiate between trajectories within each anthropometric measure. Fourteen lipoprotein subclasses were required across weight, length/height, and BMI, with an additional 16 to 31 metabolites required in one or two trajectories. Numerous associations between metabolite levels and change in z-score anrthropometric measures were observed and validated within each growth trajectory (-0.47 to 1.5 for weight; -0.87 to 2.2 for height/length; and -0.85 to 1.8 for BMI; P < 0.05) per unit change in metabolite. South Asian ethnicity and GDM were associated with lower z-scores (-0.214 to -0.212 and -0.044 to -0.041 for weight; -0.061 to -0.045 and -0.104 to -0.101 for length/height; and -0.157 to -0.182 and -0.083 to -0.071 for BMI, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolomic profiles in mid-pregnancy, especially lipoproteins, characterize observed offspring growth in different directions and/or strengths in various growth trajectories from birth to 36 months of age.

articles.title: Ten rules to reduce noise and increase precision in imaging studies in rheumatology: a methodological viewpoint informed by narrative reviews.
articles.abstract: Imaging studies are ubiquitous in rheumatology. Research in imaging has throughout the years mainly focused on improving the sensitivity of imaging techniques and scoring methods. Remarkably little attention has been paid to constraining unwarranted noise (acquisition, measurement, and analytical error) in spite of strict regulatory guidance about noise reduction for new drug approval. Noise reduction in imaging depends on the application of several methodological rules. Scientific credibility of imaging results should not depend on the complexity and incomprehensibility of the reported statistical model (plus eye-catching P values), but rather on optimal signal-to-noise ratio, usually meaning less 'noise' at a given 'signal'. This viewpoint deals with noise reduction. Repeated scoring of existing images, correction of inappropriate prior scoring, correction of fallible previous analytical procedures and more, can all contribute to a more trustworthy and better result. In the current world of patient-reported clinical information, imaging data still stand out as being rather 'objective'. But the influence of scoring and analysis in terms of unwarranted noise by readers and data analysts cannot be disregarded. This viewpoint proposes 10 expert-based rules for noise reduction at the level of image scoring, database handling, and data analysis. These rules should be considered not-yet-validated methodological hypotheses that require empirical validation through comparative methodological research.

articles.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Use in Kidney Transplant Recipients With Post-Transplantation Diabetes Mellitus - A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have proved beneficial effects on cardiovascular risk and preservation of renal function in patients with diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, in addition to their glucose-lowering effects. This study aims to investigate whether SGLT2i was associated with a more favorable metabolic profile in kidney transplant recipients with post-transplantation diabetes mellitus (PTDM).

METHODS: In this observational study, patients receiving a kidney transplant between 2007 and 2021 in Norway were identified from the national transplant database. Patients who developed PTDM were identified through new- onset prescription of glucose- lowering treatment after kidney transplantation registered in Norwegian Prescription Database. PTDM patients were categorized whether glucose- lowering treatment included SGLT2i or not during the first 4 years after transplantation. Metabolic parameters at 5 years after transplantation reported to the Norwegian Renal Registry was compared in the 2 patient groups.

RESULTS: This observational study included 232 kidney transplant recipients with PTDM. Metabolic parameters at 5 years post-transplantation were compared among the SGLT2i-group (n = 39) and the control group (n = 193); median BMI (27.5 vs. 26.5 kg/m2, p = .22), diastolic blood pressure (80 vs. 79 mm Hg, p = .40), systolic blood pressure (129 vs. 132 mm Hg, p = .42), proteinuria-parameters (u-ACR 4.5 vs. 3.5 mg/mmol, p = .33), (u-PCR 26 vs. 13 mg/mmol, p = .29), HbA1c (52 vs. 49 mmol/mol, p = .11) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, 61 vs. 56 mL/min/1.73m2, p = .20).

CONCLUSION: Our study could not demonstrate improved metabolic parameters in PTDM patients treated with SGLT2-inhibitors at 5 years post transplantation.

articles.title: Trends in metabolic risk factor control and medication use among adults with type 2 diabetes in Taiwan, 2015-2024.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate 10-year trends in metabolic control and guideline-directed pharmacotherapy among adults with type 2 diabetes in Taiwan.

METHODS: Using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (2015-2024), we analyzed annual trends in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and medication use. Blood pressure (BP) was assessed via a nationwide Pay-for-Performance registry. Trends were evaluated overall and across subgroups with cardiovascular disease (CVD) or chronic kidney disease (CKD).

RESULTS: The treated population expanded from 1.58 to 2.27 million. Target achievement improved significantly: HbA1c <7.0% rose from 42.5% to 55.3%, and LDL-C <100 mg/dL from 54.3% to 69.0% (both p-trend <0.001). Among patients with all three measurements available, triple-factor control reached 18.2% by 2024. These gains coincided with rapid sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) uptake (from 3.3% in 2016 to 38.0% in 2024) and increased statin use. However, 23.5% of young adults (20-44 years) maintained poor glycemic control (HbA1c ≥ 8.5%). SGLT2i use was higher in patients with CVD (43.1%) or CKD (43.8%) than in those without the respective conditions (34.7% and 36.6%), while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use remained below 4%.

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic control in Taiwan improved substantially alongside adoption of newer therapies. Gaps among younger adults and high-risk cohorts highlight the need for targeted, risk-stratified management.

articles.title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

articles.title: Intestinal Phosphate Absorption and Phosphate Metabolism in Chronic Kidney Disease: Direct and Indirect Toxicity of Phosphate Additives in Ultra-processed Diets.
articles.abstract: In chronic kidney disease (CKD), intestinal phosphate absorption stays largely constant even as the kidneys lose the ability to excrete phosphate, creating a tendency toward positive phosphate balance. Rising fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) and parathyroid hormone (PTH) keep serum phosphate near normal until advanced CKD, but these same adaptations can cause systemic harm long before overt hyperphosphatemia develops. Ultra-processed foods worsen this burden through phosphate additives (Pi-additives) used as preservatives, emulsifiers, stabilizers, leavening agents, and moisture retainers. These additives are absorbed more readily than natural food phosphate and are poorly captured by nutrient databases. Therefore, true phosphorus exposure is easily underestimated. This perspective outlines 2 pathways of harm. The direct pathway involves PTH and FGF23 activation, vascular and soft-tissue calcification, endothelial dysfunction, disordered bone remodeling, faster CKD progression, and cellular senescence-effects documented in CKD and possibly relevant even with preserved kidney function. The indirect pathway reflects that Pi-additives rarely occur alone: they accompany added sugars, non-nutritive sweeteners, nitrites, emulsifiers, and preservatives in ultra-processed foods, combinations that may drive gut dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammation, and the formation of advanced glycation endproducts and other gut-derived toxins. We synthesize current understanding of phosphate homeostasis with mechanistic and epidemiologic evidence linking Pi-additives-alone and combined with other additives-to cardiovascular, skeletal, renal, and metabolic disease. Future research should move beyond single-additive safety testing toward evaluating additive mixtures, cumulative exposure, and food-matrix interactions. Better exposure assessment and transparent phosphorus labeling are essential to clarify the long-term health effects of these ubiquitous additives.

articles.title: Normal variants, pitfalls, and interpretation challenges of somatostatin receptor PET.
articles.abstract: Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET has become a central imaging tool in neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), with established roles in detection, staging, restaging, and selection of patients for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Despite its high sensitivity and target specificity, interpretation is not always straightforward. Physiological SSTR expression, focal variants of normal biodistribution, technical and administration-related artifacts, inflammatory conditions, and benign or malignant non-neuroendocrine lesions may all generate uptake that mimics NET involvement. Conversely, small lesion size, partial-volume effects, high physiological background, and genuinely low or absent receptor expression may reduce lesion conspicuity and lead to false-negative or underestimated disease. Interpretive challenges have also become more relevant as SSTR PET is increasingly used for quantitative, longitudinal, and theranostic assessment. Somatostatin analogue treatment can modify normal-organ biodistribution and lesion-to-background contrast, while liver and spleen uptake may vary substantially across serial examinations and should not necessarily be considered stable reference tissues. In addition, inter-lesional differences in receptor expression may have practical implications when SSTR PET is used to assess suitability for PRRT, because intense uptake in part of the disease does not necessarily imply adequate target expression across all clinically relevant lesions. This review summarizes the principal physiological variants and false-positive and false-negative findings encountered on SSTR PET and discusses contemporary pitfalls related to biodistribution, receptor heterogeneity, quantitative interpretation, and theranostic decision-making. Accurate interpretation requires integration of molecular, anatomical, and clinical information rather than reliance on isolated uptake intensity or a binary positive/negative classification.

articles.title: Association of insulin resistance surrogate indices with multimorbidity among postmenopausal women: cross-sectional and longitudinal evidence from NHANES and CHARLS with machine learning-based evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance (IR) is closely linked to multiple chronic diseases, but the comparative associations and discriminatory performance of different IR surrogate indices for multimorbidity in postmenopausal women remain unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed postmenopausal women from NHANES and CHARLS. Eleven IR surrogate indices were evaluated using weighted logistic regression in NHANES and Cox proportional hazards models in CHARLS. Dose-response relationships were examined using restricted cubic splines. Discriminatory performance was assessed using ROC analyses, including time-dependent ROC analyses for CHARLS. Machine learning models were additionally developed using NHANES data to classify prevalent multimorbidity.

RESULTS: In NHANES, most IR surrogate indices were positively associated with prevalent multimorbidity, whereas estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) showed a strong inverse association (OR = 0.28, 95% CI 0.21-0.37, p < 0.001). In CHARLS, eGDR was also inversely associated with incident multimorbidity in both baseline (HR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.73-0.84, p < 0.001) and cumulative analyses (HR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.58-0.77, p < 0.001). eGDR showed the highest discrimination among the evaluated indices in NHANES (AUC = 0.809) and in the CHARLS cumulative analysis (AUC = 0.634). Machine learning analysis in NHANES identified eGDR as the most important feature, and the optimal support vector machine model achieved an AUC of 0.835. Sensitivity analyses excluding hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia attenuated the eGDR associations in CHARLS.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple IR surrogate indices were associated with multimorbidity among postmenopausal women, with eGDR showing the most consistent inverse association across analyses. These indices may assist population-level risk stratification, although their clinical utility requires further external validation.

articles.title: The value of less: Rethinking heart failure therapy after effective rhythm control in AF-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Left bundle branch block: A marker before, a mediator of heart failure after aortic valve replacement?
Prognostic value of early post-admission pan-immune-inflammation value in Takotsubo syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation has been associated with adverse outcomes in Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), but the prognostic value of pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) has not been evaluated in this condition. We assessed whether PIV measured at days 3-5 provides prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 768 patients with TTS from two tertiary centers. PIV was calculated at admission and at days 3-5. A prespecified day-5 landmark analysis evaluated one-year major adverse clinical events (MACE), defined as all-cause death, heart failure events, arrhythmia requiring hospitalization, stroke, or acute myocardial infarction, and the incremental prognostic value of PIV at days 3-5.

RESULTS: The landmark cohort included 722 patients with 218 MACE events. In the primary complete-case analysis (n = 692; 206 events), PIV at days 3-5 was independently associated with MACE after adjustment for clinical variables and admission PIV (HR per doubling, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.16-1.42; p < 0.001), whereas admission PIV was not (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.86-1.02; p = 0.142). Adding PIV at days 3-5 to the clinical plus admission-PIV model increased the C-index from 0.659 to 0.682 (ΔC-index, 0.024; 95% CI, 0.005-0.043; bootstrap p = 0.015). The association was approximately linear on the log₂ PIV scale and robust across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: PIV measured at days 3-5 was independently associated with one-year MACE and provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical characteristics and admission PIV. Early post-admission PIV may represent a readily available adjunct to risk assessment, although external validation is required.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effect by splenic hypothermia in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether spleen-targeted remote administration of hypothermia (RAH) modulates splenic neutrophil release, attenuates neutrophil-driven cerebral inflammation, and preserves BBB integrity at early reperfusion after stroke.

METHODS: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent 2-h middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by 6-, 24- and 48- h of reperfusion. RAH was applied to the splenic region via surface cooling, with 1-min cycles administered at 5-min intervals. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, neutrophil infiltration, cytokine expression, BBB integrity, and apoptosis were assessed using neurobehavioral scoring, TTC staining, Western blotting, rt-PCR, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and TUNEL, respectively.

RESULTS: RAH rapidly reduced splenic temperature from 370 to 28 °C without altering body or brain temperatures. At 6 h reperfusion, splenic neutrophil release was suppressed and brain neutrophil infiltration decreased. RAH reduced early elevations of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. At 24 h, anti-inflammatory effects persisted and BBB integrity was preserved, restoring tight-junction and matrix proteins and suppressing BBB-damaging mediators. Compared to non-RAH stroked rats, RAH reduced apoptosis, body weight loss (9.1 ± 2.8 vs. 19.7 ± 7.2 g, p < 0.05), infarct volume (33.9 ± 4.1% vs. 53.6 ± 1.9%, p < 0.05), cerebral edema (11.2 ± 0.9% vs. 16.3 ± 1.3%, p < 0.05) and Evans blue extravasation (4.8 ± 0.2 vs. 9.8 ± 0.2 mg/g, p < 0.05), and improved neurological outcomes. RAH attenuated stroke-induced spleen weight loss and contraction, consistent with reduced splenic neutrophil mobilization.

CONCLUSIONS: RAH induces neuroprotection after ischemic stroke by suppressing splenic neutrophil activation and mobilization, thus attenuating peripheral-to-central inflammatory trafficking and preserving BBB integrity. These findings highlight spleen-targeted cooling may represent a promising early intervention to ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Causal interpretation of intraoperative blood loss as a mediator of surgical site infection.
Healthcare textile contamination along the post-laundering pathway: a multicentre study across a hospital network.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare textiles are recognised as potential reservoirs of microorganisms, yet contamination along the post-laundering pathway remains insufficiently characterised.

AIM: To assess microbiological contamination of healthcare textiles across a regional hospital network and identify sampling points with elevated contamination along the clean linen pathway.

METHODS: This multicentre observational study included nine healthcare-facility groups comprising 17 geographically distinct sampling sites. Paired microbiological samples from external and internal surfaces of clean textiles were collected at upstream reference points, ward storage (cabinets or shelves) and nursing carts using contact plates. Paired counts and proportions exceeding 12 CFU were compared using two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank and exact two-sided McNemar tests, respectively. Storage and textile-type associations were assessed using negative-binomial models adjusted for site, storage location and textile type, with sampling-batch-clustered robust standard errors.

FINDINGS: Of 784 ward textiles sampled, 774 had complete paired results (1,548 contact samples); 331 pairs (662 samples) were analysed at reference points. At ward level, external counts exceeded internal counts (median 5 [1-14] vs 0 [0-1] CFU; Wilcoxon p<0.001). The 12-CFU threshold was exceeded by 210/774 external (27.1%) versus 41/774 internal samples (5.3%; McNemar p<0.001). Contamination profiles varied markedly among sites. No clear association was detected between storage location and external counts (ward storage areas vs nursing carts: IRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.75-1.36; p=0.930). The estimate for internal counts was lower in ward storage areas, but remained inconclusive (IRR 0.62, 95% CI 0.37-1.02; p=0.060). External and internal CFU counts differed significantly across textile types after adjustment for site and storage location (external: F[7,110]=3.46, p=0.002; internal: F[7,110]=12.02, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Contamination patterns were consistent with exposure after laundering; site-specific profiles identified priorities for further investigation. Routine monitoring at laundry exit alone cannot identify where subsequent contamination occurs. Sampling successive stages of the clean-linen pathway may help identify potential recontamination points, guide targeted improvements and complement existing RABC programmes.

articles.title: Development and validation of a screening nomogram for nosocomial infection risk in hospitalized patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nosocomial infections increase patient morbidity, mortality, hospital stay, and healthcare costs. A practical tool for early risk screening at admission is lacking. We aimed to develop and validate a nomogram to estimate the risk of nosocomial infection upon hospitalization.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 177,860 patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (FAHSYSU) were randomly split into training (70%) and internal validation (30%) sets. An external validation set included 12,888 patients from Huangpu People's Hospital. Predictors were selected using LASSO regression and multivariable logistic regression. A nomogram was constructed and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: The developed nomogram demonstrated promising performance. The area under the curve (AUC) values for the training set and internal validation set were 0.750 (95% CI 0.747-0.753) and 0.743 (95% CI 0.724-0.762), respectively. For the external validation set, the AUC value was 0.702 (95% CI 0.669-0.734). Through analysis, we determined that the optimal cut-off value for the training set was 0.013. Furthermore, the decision curve analysis indicated that the nomogram exhibited significant clinical value within a threshold likelihood range of 0-0.11.

CONCLUSION: We developed and validated an admission-based screening nomogram for nosocomial infection. Given its high negative predictive value, the tool may assist clinicians in identifying patients unlikely to develop infection, thereby informing surveillance intensity and resource allocation.

articles.title: Sex differences in prevalence normalized mortality and risk attributable mortality indices for type 2 diabetes across the European Union.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To characterize sex-specific prevalence-normalized mortality and modelled risk-attributable mortality patterns for type 2 diabetes across the 27 European Union member states METHODS: We conducted an ecological analysis of Global Burden of Disease 2023 modelled estimates at two benchmark years, 2011 and 2021. Age-standardized mortality and prevalence rates were combined as a prevalence-normalized mortality ratio. Risk-attributable mortality was normalized to prevalence as a risk-attributable prevalence-normalized mortality index. Approximate intervals assumed independence between numerator and denominator and between sexes; country-level sex comparisons used Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction.

RESULTS: The unweighted country mean age-standardized mortality rate was higher in 2021 than in 2011, changing from 12.02 to 14.32 per 100,000 in men and from 8.84 to 10.08 per 100,000 in women; the corresponding prevalence means increased from 4,131.6 to 4,660.2 and from 2,875.3 to 3,178.6 per 100,000. Mean prevalence-normalized mortality changed modestly. No country-level sex comparison remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Tobacco-related indices were higher in men in all 27 countries and met the FDR criterion in 23 under the independence approximation; no other risk family contained corrected significant differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Across-country means describe member states rather than the population-weighted European Union. The tobacco-related index was consistently higher in men, a pattern compatible with established sex differences in tobacco exposure. Statistical evidence depends on unverified covariance assumptions. All indices are ecological summaries of modelled rates and must not be interpreted as individual mortality probabilities, causal effects, or evidence of independent sex-specific biological mechanisms.

articles.title: Association of Early Energy Gap With Activities of Daily Living and In-Hospital Complications in Patients With Acute Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Early nutritional adequacy may influence functional recovery and complications after stroke, but the clinical relevance of the magnitude of early energy deficit relative to estimated requirements remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined the association between the energy gap during the first 7 days after admission and discharge activities of daily living and in-hospital complications in patients with acute stroke.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 304 patients with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke (median age, 77 years [IQR, 66-85]; 46.7% male) who were admitted to a Japanese university hospital and hospitalized for at least 7 days. Energy gap was calculated as mean daily total energy intake, including oral, enteral, and parenteral nutrition, minus estimated energy requirements of 25 kcal/kg ideal body weight/day during the first 7 days after admission. The primary outcome was total Functional Independence Measure score at discharge, and the secondary outcome was the occurrence of in-hospital complications. Multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: The median energy gap was -2.7 kcal/kg/day. Patients with severe energy deficit had lower discharge Functional Independence Measure scores and a higher occurrence of in-hospital complications. In multivariable analysis, a higher energy gap was associated with a higher total Functional Independence Measure score at discharge (B = 0.54, 95% CI 0.17-0.91, P = 0.005) and lower odds of in-hospital complications (OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.86-0.96, P = 0.001). The association with in-hospital complications remained consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: A lower early energy gap was associated with poorer functional status at discharge and a higher occurrence of in-hospital complications in patients with acute stroke. These findings suggest that early energy gap may provide clinically relevant information regarding nutritional adequacy and clinical status.

articles.title: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy State of pathology: Insertional tendon tendinopathies.
articles.abstract: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT) is a common but disabling pathology affecting both athletes and older subjects. The aim of the present study was to provide a practical review of IA, addressing the following questions: What are the etiologies and pathophysiology? Etiology is multifactorial, involving anatomic aspects and especially posterosuperior calcaneal prominence, biomechanical aspects such as short triceps surae, pes cavus or hindfoot varus, extrinsic aspects of footwear and overtraining, and metabolic aspects. Pathophysiology, depending on the individual case, implicates true insertional tendinopathy and posterior bone-tendon impingement to varying degrees, often with pre-Achilles bursitis; the distinction is crucial to decision-making. Impingement or enthesopathy lead to progressive disorganization of the collagen matrix, pathologic neovascularization and mucoid degeneration of the tendon, often with intratendon calcifications and inflammatory retrocalcaneal bursitis. How to establish diagnosis? Diagnosis is primarily clinical, based on pain location, which is median in case of insertional tendinopathy and more lateral in case of posterior impingement with bursitis. Examination finds pain on palpation of the Achilles insertion, sometimes with local thickening, posterior tumefaction and painful restriction of ankle dorsiflexion. Tensing the tendon typically reproduces the pain. Functional tests may show restriction due to pain, without tendon tear. Weight-bearing X-ray, ultrasound and especially MRI analyze the respective roles of bone, tendon and bursa injury; weight-bearing CT can be contributive in some morphologically complex situations. Ultrasound reveals tendon thickening, hypoechogenic degenerative areas, hypervascularization on Doppler and associated bursitis. MRI shows lesion extension: intratendon degeneration, deep fiber involvement and retrocalcaneal inflammation. What are the non-operative treatments? Initial treatment is conservative, based on adapting weight-bearing and footwear, with exercises adapted to the form of the insertion, extracorporeal shock waves and rehabilitation. What are the surgical options and their expected results? In case of failure of well-conducted non-operative treatment, surgical strategy depends on lesion type, degree of posterior impingement, degree of tendon degeneration and degree of triceps surae stiffness. Expected results comprise pain relief, functional improvement on VISA-A score, and progressive return to activities, with timing depending on the technique and the initial level of activity. How to choose the surgical treatment? Surgical options comprise bone decompression, debridement and tendon reinsertion, flexor hallucis longus transfer and gastrocnemius lengthening depending on lesion type on clinical examination and imaging.

articles.title: Management of scalp psoriasis: Updated treatment recommendations from a Delphi consensus of 53 dermatologists from AEDV Psoriasis Working Group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scalp psoriasis affects approximately 80% of patients with psoriasis and presents therapeutic challenges related to treatment adherence, formulation selection, and quality of life. Updated management recommendations are needed.

METHODS: A Delphi consensus study involving 53 dermatologists from the Psoriasis Working Group of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (AEDV) was conducted. Following a literature review, experts evaluated 47 recommendations using a 7-point Likert scale, with consensus defined as at least 75% agreement or disagreement. Preferences for topical vehicles and systemic treatments were also assessed.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached on 34 recommendations. Topical corticosteroids, particularly high-potency agents, were recommended as first-line treatment.
