Combinations with vitamin D analogues were supported for initial and maintenance therapy, while keratolytic agents combined with corticosteroids were considered appropriate for severe scaling. Scalp-compatible formulations, including lotions, solutions, shampoos, gels, and creams using Polyaphron Dispersion (PAD) technology, were favored. Systemic treatment was considered appropriate for severe symptoms or impaired quality of life, with IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors receiving the highest preference scores (8.84 and 8.32, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi consensus provides updated, clinically applicable recommendations for scalp psoriasis management, emphasizing effective topical therapies, appropriate formulations, treatment adherence, and individualized systemic treatment selection.

articles.title: Outcomes Analysis of Low Back Pain Patients Managed Through a Spine Center Clinical Care Redesign Pathway: An Initial Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Back pain affects a large portion of the U.S. population, and delivering care in an efficient manner without compromising outcomes is of utmost importance for quality of life. One potential approach is to reinvent clinical pathways to streamline care and reduce the gaps evident between recommendation and actual practice, such as high uses of surgery and imaging.

PURPOSE: To compare outcomes of acute or acute-on-chronic low back pain patients treated through a value-based structured clinical care redesign spine pathway at The Hospital of Central Connecticut (THOCC) Spine Center versus patients treated by Hartford HealthCare (HHC) ambulatory care providers/clinics that did not participate in the clinical care redesign spine pathway.

STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Retrospective cohort study in the setting of ambulatory care referrals from primary care or community providers, urgent care, emergency department, walk-ins, or self-referral within HHC.

PATIENT SAMPLE: Acute or acute-on-chronic lumbar pain patients conservatively treated with at least three physical therapy (PT) visits OUTCOME MEASURES: Initial and follow-up Modified Oswestry Low Back Pain Disability Questionnaire (MDQ) and numeric pain rating scale scores; days of first provider to first PT visit, first provider visit to completion of the acute care episode; number of provider, PT, and outside specialist visits (orthopedics, neurosurgery, neurology), and imaging studies (x-rays) METHODS: Patients were identified by querying the rehabilitation outcomes management system (ROMS) database. Variables were collected via chart and ROMS database review. Mann-Whitney-U tests with α set at 0.05 were performed. Differences in dichotomous data between the two groups were analyzed with contingency Chi-square tests or Fisher's Exact tests. Because this was a retrospective analysis of an existing cohort, no a priori sample-size calculation was performed. The final sample represents all available patients meeting the prespecified eligibility criteria during the study period.

RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences between the 41 patients treated through the THOCC clinical care redesign spine pathway and the 33 patients treated in the standard non-spine care pathway regarding sex, race, ethnicity, diagnosis, initial pain or disability score, or Subgroups for Targeted Treatment (STarT) Back Tool risk category. Spine Center participants were significantly older than controls (median age 52 vs 43 years, p=0.0004, effect size 0.414). Compared with controls, Spine Center patients demonstrated significantly shorter median time from first provider visit to PT (2.5 days [IQR 1-6.5] vs. 19 days [IQR 8-39], z=-4.98, p<0.0001, effect size 0.591), shorter median episode duration (70 days [IQR 47.5-93.75] vs. 132 days [IQR 71-311], z=-3.04, p=0.0023, effect size 0.361), greater median improvement in pain scores (3- [IQR 1-5.5] vs. 2-points [IQR -0.75-3.75], z=2.07, p=0.0486, effect size 0.231), greater median number of provider visits (2 [IQR 2-3] vs. 1 visit [IQR 1-2.75], z=3.40, p=0.0007, effect size 0.398), fewer lumbar x-rays (0.073 per patient, median 0 [IQR 0-0], vs. 0.394 per patient, median 0 [IQR 0-1], z=-2.15, p=0.0313, effect size 0.250), and fewer outside specialist visits (0.463 visits per patient, median 0 [IQR 0-0], vs. 0.935 visits per patient, median 0 [IQR 0-2], z=-2.23, p=0.0258, effect size 0.263).

CONCLUSIONS: A clinical care redesign spine pathway may be associated with improved care efficiency and decreased use of selected services such as imaging and outside specialist visits. Additional studies with larger cohorts and multivariable analysis are warranted to further characterize the relationship between integrated spine center models and functional outcomes.

articles.title: Transcriptional Signatures Associated with Etiology of Post-Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Lung Injury.
articles.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (alloHCT) is a potentially curative therapy for many hematologic disorders but is frequently complicated by infectious and noninfectious pulmonary injury. Differentiating these etiologies is challenging in clinical practice, and it remains unclear whether response signatures can distinguish infectious from non-infectious lung injury following transplantation. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of whole-blood samples from 52 alloHCT recipients within 120 days of transplantation who developed lung injury due to bacterial, viral, or fungal pathogens as well as idiopathic pneumonia syndrome (IPS). We compared expression of genes and immune programs across etiologies of lung injury. Distinct transcriptional programs were observed across etiologies. Viral pneumonia showed enrichment of interferon and adaptive immune signaling pathways. Bacterial pneumonia demonstrated enrichment of innate immune and heme metabolism pathways. Fungal pneumonia exhibited the strongest enrichment of cellular proliferation pathways. IPS showed lower enrichment of immune signaling pathways than infectious etiologies. Transcriptomic responses differ between infectious and noninfectious lung injury following alloHCT. These findings highlight the potential utility of transcriptomic profiling to support diagnosis, guide therapeutic management, and risk-stratify patients following transplantation.

articles.title: From Microbial burden to host response dysregulation: toward host-centered precision medicine in severe pneumonia and pneumonia-associated sepsis.
Identifying the Optimal Respiratory Muscle Training Intervention for Heart Failure Patients: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory muscle training interventions have shown promising results in improving functional capacity, quality of life, and prognosis of heart failure patients. However, the optimal respiratory muscle training intervention for rehabilitation remains unclear.

METHODS: A systematic review and network meta-analysis was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library until September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effect of respiratory muscle training interventions on maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximum expiratory pressure (MEP), forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), six-minute walk test (6MWT), peak oxygen uptake (VO2max), quality of life, and dyspnea. Random-effect network meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled mean differences. Interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).

RESULTS: A total of 88 RCTs (5,757 participants) were included. Medium-intensity inspiratory muscle training (IMT) ranked highest for improving MIP (SUCRA: 89.8%). Combined aerobic and resistance exercise was optimal for MEP (SUCRA: 79.3%). Aerobic training showed the greatest benefit for FVC (SUCRA: 94.8%) and FEV₁ (SUCRA: 93.8%). Medium-intensity IMT was most effective for enhancing 6MWT performance (SUCRA: 81.6%). A combination of high-intensity IMT with aerobic training yielded the largest gains in improving VO2max (SUCRA: 74.7%), quality of life (SUCRA: 81.4%), and reducing dyspnea (SUCRA: 89.3%).

CONCLUSION: Respiratory muscle training interventions provide different benefits across key rehabilitation outcomes in heart failure. Accordingly, rehabilitation strategies may be optimized by aligning exercise modalities with patients' rehabilitation needs, preferences, and clinical profiles, rather than adopting a uniform prescription.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Bridging Intravenous Thrombolysis in the "Drip-and-Ship" Model for Anterior and Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The drip-and-ship paradigm extends access to endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) from primary stroke centers (PSC), particularly where comprehensive stroke centers (CSC) are limited, but transfer may delay reperfusion. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) before transfer for EVT in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026 for studies comparing IVT versus no IVT in patients transferred from PSC to CSC for EVT consideration. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Heterogeneity was quantified by I2 and prediction intervals (PI).

RESULTS: Sixteen observational studies involving 5,488 patients were included. In anterior circulation stroke, IVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (mRS 0-2; aOR 1.76; P=0.02; 95% PI 0.67-4.63, including the null) and lower 90-day mortality (aOR 0.52; P<0.0001). In posterior circulation stroke, IVT was associated with lower mortality (RR 0.74; P=0.04), but not improved functional outcomes. IVT was associated with higher early recanalization during transfer in anterior (RR 5.24; P<0.0001) and posterior circulation (RR 17.46; P<0.0001), without significant differences in post-EVT revascularization or intracranial hemorrhage. All included studies were observational, and certainty of GRADE evidence was very low.

CONCLUSION: IVT before transfer was associated with higher early recanalization and favorable clinical outcomes, particularly in anterior circulation stroke, without a detected increase in intracranial hemorrhage. Given the very-low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Identified methodological limitations also informed considerations for future research.

articles.title: Inferior Vena Cava Filters in Adolescents with Thromboembolic Disease: Technical Outcomes, Retrieval, and the Role of Skeletal Maturity.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage. Retrieval was attempted once the initial indication had resolved and anticoagulation was feasible.

RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in every case; mean caval diameter was 17.9 ± 3.0 mm. Retrieval was attempted in 22 of 26 filters and succeeded in 19 (86% of attempts, 79% by intent to retrieve, 73% overall). One successful retrieval required a second attempt with an adjunctive loop-snare maneuver. Median indwelling time was 89 days (range 1-489). All three unsuccessful retrievals occurred at Risser stage 3 or below (3 of 7 versus 0 of 15 attempted; P = .02), not explained by caval diameter (P = .33). Seven filters (27%) remained in situ. No periprocedural adverse events occurred. Both retained filters assessed by CT showed caval wall penetration, one with strut fracture and asymptomatic migration at 16 years; chronic caval occlusion developed in one patient.

CONCLUSION: Off-label IVCF placement in adolescents achieved high technical and retrieval success. Retrieval failure was confined to skeletally immature patients and was not explained by caval diameter. Strut fracture with migration at long-term imaging reinforces the need for timely retrieval.

articles.title: Study on the role of NLRP3 inflammasome in MSC-mediated repair of high-glucose-induced damage to testicular Sertoli cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive investigation on the efficacy of stem cell transplantation in repairing diabetic complications, stable repair has not yet been achieved. This study aimed to investigate whether bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells with inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome (BMSCsLV-shNLRP3) exhibit enhanced repair of high-glucose-induced damage to testicular Sertoli cells in vitro.

METHODS: BMSCs and testicular Sertoli cells were isolated from Sprague-Dawley rats. BMSCs were infected with shNLRP3 lentivirus (LV-shNLRP3) to downregulate NLRP3 expression. Testicular Sertoli cells were exposed to high glucose to establish an in vitro injury model and then cocultured with different groups of BMSCs. The expression of related proteins and genes, cell secretions, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were detected to evaluate whether the repair effect of BMSCs was improved after NLRP3 downregulation.

RESULTS: Testicular Sertoli cell function was significantly impaired under high-glucose conditions, characterized by decreased secretion of androgen-binding protein and inhibin B and decreased MMP. BMSC intervention partially restored the function of damaged testicular Sertoli cells, and BMSCsLV-shNLRP3 exhibited a stronger repair effect, improving the therapeutic and repair potential of BMSCs. Conclusions Downregulation of NLRP3 expression in BMSCs enhances their ability to repair high-glucose-induced testicular Sertoli cell damage, providing new avenues for the treatment of diabetes-induced impairment of male fertility.

articles.title: Cognitive reserve reconsidered: Asymmetry across proxies challenges a domain-general mechanism.
articles.abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) is a broad framework for explaining why individuals differ in cognitive functioning in the face of aging and neuropathology. One influential mechanistic account proposes that cognitively demanding life experiences such as education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities augment a domain-general cognitive capacity that subsequently provides resilience. We refer to this more specific claim as cognitive reserve augmentation (CRA). This narrative and conceptual review evaluates the inferential strength of the evidence for CRA, emphasizing prospective cohort studies as the strongest available observational design for evaluating causal hypotheses. Across meta-analyses, several putative reserve-building experiences show consistent protective associations; however, comparison across prospective cohort studies reveals a striking asymmetry: whereas education, occupational complexity, and cognitively stimulating activities predict reduced risk or delayed clinical diagnosis of dementia, bilingualism-also proposed as a reserve-building cognitive experience-does not. This pattern constrains the assumption that diverse cognitive experiences augment a common reserve mechanism. Life-course evidence further indicates that associations between traditional CR proxies and later cognitive functioning can be substantially attenuated when earlier cognitive ability is measured directly. We argue that these findings are compatible with multiple pathways involving selection, correlated socioeconomic and health factors, domain-specific knowledge and expertise, processing efficiency, and effects on brain and physical health, as well as possible changes in cognitive capacity. Distinguishing among these alternatives requires specifying what experience is proposed to change, which experiences should and should not produce that change, and which outcomes would challenge the proposed mechanism. CR may therefore remain useful as a broad descriptive framework even when evidence for CRA or another specified reserve mechanism is incomplete.

articles.title: Optimal combination of broadly neutralizing antibodies for HIV: Sensitivity ranking determines efficacy.
articles.abstract: Combination therapy with broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) holds great promise for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) functional cure, yet a critical question remains: when multiple bNAbs with distinct pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties are available, which combinations are most effective, and what determines their performance? To address this, we develop an impulsive differential equation model that incorporates three bNAb mechanisms, namely blocking viral entry, enhancing viral clearance, and stimulating cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) proliferation. We derive the basic reproduction number R0 and establish it as a threshold. Specifically, R0 < 1 ensures virus eradication, while R0 > 1 leads to persistent infection. Global sensitivity analysis ranks the six antibody-related parameters, with the dosing interval and clearance rate being the most influential, followed by dose, maximum efficacy, half-maximal concentration, and Hill coefficient. Guided by this ranking, we design antibody combinations and find that the dual regimen (long-half-life + high-efficacy) achieves clearance probabilities and delays viral rebound comparable to the triple combination (with the high-affinity antibody added). In contrast, combinations lacking the long-half-life antibody rebound earliest, confirming that the most sensitive parameters dominate treatment durability. Mechanistically, neutralization of viral entry is the primary driver of sustained suppression. CTL enhancement contributes only marginally when neutralization is intact, but provides a compensatory protective effect when neutralization is partially compromised. These findings establish a quantitative framework for rational bNAb combination design, showing that optimizing the most sensitive parameters matters more than simply increasing the number of antibodies.

articles.title: Delayed Risk Perception and Imitative Behavior Drive Epidemic Oscillations and Multistability: A Mathematical Modeling Study.
articles.abstract: This study develops a time-delay differential equation model that couples disease transmission with imitation dynamics. Perceived risk is linked to historical prevalence with a discrete time delay τ, to investigate how delay of risk perception shapes protective actions and epidemic evolution. The theoretical analysis reveals that in the absence of delay, the system converges to one of four equilibria. Once τ exceeds a critical threshold, a Hopf bifurcation induces periodic oscillations. Further increasing τ can lead to two distinct dynamical regimes: either bounded periodic solutions persist, or the system undergoes repeated stability switches, with equilibrium and periodic orbits alternating in stability. Under certain delays, multiple stable periodic solutions may coexist. Numerical simulations demonstrate that delay of risk perception critically determines the outbreak trajectory: with short delays, timely protective measures can mitigate epidemic size even under high transmission risk; with long delays, both infection levels and the proportion of individuals adopting protection exhibit persistent oscillations. Notably, in prolonged-delay scenarios, reducing the cost of protection may amplify epidemic fluctuations, causing a sharp rebound in prevalence after transient suppression. Thus, an effective public health strategy should simultaneously lower the cost of protection and shorten delays.

articles.title: FROM SIMPLICITY TO LUXURY: THE IMPACT OF DENTAL OFFICE STRUCTURE ON THE PROFESSIONAL'S IMAGE.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the visual appearance of a dental clinic is associated with differences in laypeople's perceptions of the dentist and the dental care provided.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, quantitative, and descriptive-analytical study was conducted with 120 participants aged between 18 and 65 years. Digital images of three dental offices - simple, intermediate, and luxurious were generated by artificial intelligence and evaluated through a questionnaire comprising six domains: trust, quality of care, hygiene and safety, furniture and equipment, technological updates, and recommendation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Friedman and Wilcoxon tests, chi-square, linear correlations, and effect sizes (Cramér's V and r).

RESULTS: The simple dental office presented substantially less favorable evaluations than the intermediate and luxurious environments. Significant differences were observed across the three environments (Friedman, p < 0.001), whereas direct comparisons between intermediate and luxurious environments showed no statistically significant differences after Bonferroni adjustment. This pattern indicates limited incremental differentiation between the two higher levels of environmental sophistication.

CONCLUSION: The physical structure of the dental office is a strategic element of credibility, directly impacting patient perception.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: A well-designed dental office enhances patients' perceptions of trust, quality, and professional competence. An intermediate-standard clinic may provide similar perceptual benefits to a luxurious environment, suggesting that functionality and organization are more important than excessive luxury.

articles.title: Oral and orofacial manifestations in immune-mediated systemic diseases: From clinical clues to targeted management.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated systemic diseases frequently produce oral and orofacial findings involving the mucosa, salivary glands, periodontium, temporomandibular joints, and masticatory or oropharyngeal function. These findings may precede systemic diagnosis, reflect disease activity or damage, result from treatment, or identify patients requiring urgent referral. This expert narrative review provides a phenotype-based diagnostic and management framework for oral and orofacial manifestations of major immune-mediated systemic diseases. We integrate disease-specific patterns with key mimics, required confirmatory investigations, diagnostic red flags, and referral urgency. Ulcerative, lichenoid/interface, vesiculobullous, sicca/salivary, periodontal, temporomandibular, vascular/ischemic, infectious, and drug-related presentations are distinguished according to whether diagnosis is primarily clinical or requires further investigation. Systemic-disease correlation is supported by microbiological, histopathological and imaging data. Characteristic examples include recurrent aphthous-pattern ulceration in Behçet disease, salivary hypofunction in Sjögren disease, microstomia in systemic sclerosis, strawberry gingivitis in granulomatosis with polyangiitis, jaw claudication in giant cell arteritis, and granulomatous oral disease in Crohn's disease. Management is organized around local symptomatic care, correction of trauma or secondary infection, topical treatment of confirmed local immune-mediated disease, guideline-directed systemic therapy when oral findings reflect active systemic disease, and urgent referral for suspected vascular ischemia, multisite blistering disease, airway or ocular involvement, progressive dysphagia, or rapidly enlarging salivary glands. This lesion-first approach is intended to improve early recognition and multidisciplinary coordination across rheumatology, internal medicine, immunology, dentistry, oral medicine and dermatology.

articles.title: Beyond the Gut: Genome-Characterised Salmonella Kentucky ST198 Urinary Tract Infection.
articles.abstract: Non-typhoidal Salmonella urinary tract infections (UTIs) are rare and may be linked to immunosuppression, chronic illnesses, or structural urinary tract abnormalities. Salmonella enterica serovar Kentucky (ST198) is a globally disseminated lineage associated with fluoroquinolone resistance and the acquisition of additional antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants. This is the first Indian case report of a rare UTI caused by Salmonella Kentucky ST198, resistant to both fluoroquinolones and extended-spectrum cephalosporins. This report emphasises the value of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) for serovar-level characterisation and resistance-gene discovery in uncommon Salmonella isolates, as well as the importance of off-label azithromycin use for treating UTI for a favourable outcome.

articles.title: A study on Helicobacter pylori in patients with gall bladder diseases in a tertiary care hospital in Central India: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, spiral bacterium primarily associated with gastric disorders such as peptic ulcer disease and gastric carcinoma, has been implicated in hepatobiliary diseases including cholelithiasis and gallbladder carcinoma.

AIM: To detect Helicobacter pylori in bile samples of patients with gallbladder diseases undergoing ERCP and to evaluate its association with clinical diagnosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study was conducted in the Departments of Microbiology and Gastroenterology at a Tertiary care hospital in Central India, from September 2023 to June 2025. Eighty-four patients with gallbladder and biliary diseases undergoing Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography were included. Bile samples were subjected to Rapid Urease Test (RUT), Modified Giemsa staining, culture, and real-time PCR targeting the vacA gene of H.pylori. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26.0, with p-value <0.05 considered significant.

RESULTS: Among 84 patients, 46/84 (54.76%) were females. Cholelithiasis was the most common diagnosis [63/84 (75.00%)]. RUT was positive in 56/84 (66.67%) samples, while Modified Giemsa staining demonstrated curved or spiral bacilli suggestive of Helicobacter species in 31/84 (36.90%) samples and PCR was positive in 28/84 (33.33%) samples. Modified Giemsa staining demonstrated curved or spiral bacilli suggestive of Helicobacter species in 22/28 (78.57%) PCR-positive cases, whereas RUT was positive in 24/28 (85.71%) PCR-positive cases. PCR positivity was 28.57% in cholelithiasis cases and 42.86% in gallbladder carcinoma cases, while Modified Giemsa positivity was 33.33% and 57.14% in cholelithiasis cases and gallbladder carcinoma cases, respectively. No H. pylori isolates were recovered by culture methods. Escherichia coli was the predominant biliary isolate in 17/59(28.81%) culture-positive samples.

CONCLUSION: Helicobacter pylori was detected in bile samples of Gallbladder and biliary disease patients. Modified Giemsa staining showed a stronger association with PCR, whereas RUT showed higher positivity among PCR positive samples. PCR remains a more species-specific molecular method for the detection of H.pylori.

articles.title: Exome Sequencing Reanalysis Improves Molecular Diagnosis in Genetic Cholestatic Liver Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The 2024 European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) guidelines recommend periodic reanalysis of exome data in genetic cholestatic liver diseases, although supporting evidence remains limited and optimal gene panel composition has not been established. We evaluated the molecular diagnostic yield of systematic reanalysis of clinical exome sequencing (CES) data and compared cholestasis-focused gene panels.

METHODS: Consecutive patients referred for CES at a tertiary center for suspected genetic cholestatic liver disease (January 2021 to February 2025) were included. The initial analysis (A1) was compared with a reanalysis (A2) using three in silico panels: the Cholestasis Nancy Panel (41 genes), the EASL 2024 panel (18 genes), and an LPAC panel (8 genes). The primary endpoint was the difference in likely pathogenic or pathogenic (LP/P) yield between A1 and A2. The secondary endpoint added variants of uncertain significance (VUS).

RESULTS: Among 86 patients (median age 35 years; 63% female; 83% adults), the LP/P yield increased from 30% (26/86) to 43% (37/86) (95% CI, 5-21; P=0.006). At reanalysis, the Cholestasis Nancy Panel provided an incremental diagnostic yield beyond the Cholestasis EASL 2024 core panel at both thresholds (43% vs 34%, P = 0.013; 69% vs 49%, P=0.0001). At the LP/P threshold, the incremental yield was significant for cholelithiasis/LPAC (P=0.004) but unchanged for unexplained cholestasis, Alagille syndrome, and BRIC/PFIC. At the VUS/LP/P threshold, the increase was also significant for unexplained cholestasis (P=0.003). SERPINA1 was the most frequently implicated gene.

CONCLUSIONS: Systematic CES reanalysis increases molecular diagnostic yield in genetic cholestatic liver diseases, particularly in clinically challenging presentations. Performed within an accredited CES platform, periodic reappraisal of data as knowledge evolves warrants integration into routine practice.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Temporal dynamics of bacterial communities in Spodoptera exigua during Heliothis virescens ascovirus 3 h infection.
articles.abstract: Ascoviruses are insect viruses that cause chronic disease in infected hosts. The infection results in the partition of infected cells into multiple virion-containing vesicles, where viral replication continues for weeks before mortality. The vesicles accumulate in the hemolymph (equivalent to blood). The interaction among the virus, the host, and the microbiome during infection is poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the temporal dynamics of whole-body bacterial communities in Spodoptera exigua larvae infected with Heliothis virescens ascovirus 3 h (HvAV-3 h) during early (12 hpi), late (48 hpi), and very late (96 hpi) viral replication stages. The 16S rRNA gene sequencing approach revealed that the HvAV-3 h-infected larvae encountered a decrease in the relative abundance of family Leuconostocaceae and genus Weissella and an increase in the relative abundance of family Acetobacteraceae and genus Acetobacter, when compared to the mock larvae. Moreover, the qPCR quantification demonstrated statistically significant decreases in the bacterial load during the late and very late stages of infection relative to the mock-infected larvae. In contrast, we detected statistically significant increases in the viral load with infection progress. We confirmed the presence of some of the identified bacterial genera, such as Bacillus sp. and Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB), in uninfected S. exigua whole-body samples using a culture-based approach. Further research will be needed to identify the specific roles of the identified bacterial communities and to clarify the mechanisms that contribute to controlling the host bacterial load. Future studies should consider examining different host tissue microbial communities in this system given the HvAV-3 h wide tissue tropism.

articles.title: One Year Survival of High-Risk Patients Undergoing Coronary Revascularization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In high-risk patients requiring coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) we sought to evaluate the differential impact of comorbid and cardiovascular risk factors on perioperative versus one year survival with the hypothesis that different phenotypes of perioperative risk may portend different longitudinal outcomes and that not all high-risk features are equivalent.

METHODS: The Society Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (ACSD) was used to assess all patients (n=75,385) ≥65 years of age undergoing isolated CABG with a predicted risk of mortality (PROM) greater than 4% (2012-2022). The database was linked with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) claims data to evaluate one-year mortality. Change in risk-adjusted odds ratios for 30-day and 1-year mortality were assessed using landmark analysis to identify variables associated with early versus late mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 67,376 (89.4%) patients survived 30-days of those 8,998 (13.4%) died between 30 days and one year. Liver disease and home oxygen were associated with increased mortality at both 30 days and 1 year. However, unresponsive state, prior CABG, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 6 hours, cardiogenic shock, and temporary mechanical support were associated with early mortality but exhibited no significant effects at 1 year. Finally, cancer, Medicaid coverage, and dialysis were initially neutral for 30-day mortality but emerged as independent risk factors for 1-year mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk CABG, prognostic determinants evolve over time. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating temporal risk dynamics into clinical decisions.

articles.title: Leishmania infection in dogs in Israel - A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Leishmania spp. are kinetoplastid protozoa that cause zoonotic disease in humans and animals. No large-scale cross-sectional survey has been performed to study canine leishmaniasis and its spatial distribution in Israel. We aimed to survey the prevalence and geographical distribution of Leishmania infection in dogs in Israel. Paired blood and sera were collected from domestic dogs at private clinics and animal shelters throughout Israel. Leishmania infection was determined by ELISA serology and blood qPCR targeting the kinetoplast minicircle (kDNA) and the ribosomal ITS1 region. Altogether, 1,392 paired samples were tested from dogs from all parts of Israel. Thirty nine of 1,392 (2.8%) dogs were seropositive to Leishmania. Leishmania spp. infection was detected in 35/1392 (2.5%) and 10/1392 (0.7%) dogs by kDNA and ITS1 qPCR, respectively. All ITS1 PCR-positive dogs were confirmed to be infected by Leishmania infantum after DNA sequencing. Seventy four of 1,392 (5.3 %) dogs were either seropositive or PCR-positive. ITS1 PCR-positive dogs were 20 times more likely to be seropositive than negative dogs (p < 0.001) while kDNA PCR-positive dogs were 5.1 times more likely (p = 0.003). Dogs with clinical signs suggestive of leishmaniasis had significantly higher prevalence of seropositivity (7.5%) compared to dogs without signs (2.2%; p= 0.001). This survey of Leishmania infection in dogs covering the entire region of Israel revealed widespread infection in the northern, central and mid-southern regions of Israel with dominance of sub-clinical infection. The risk of Leishmania infection warrants protection against vector sand fly bites and disease screening among dogs throughout Israel.

articles.title: Medicinal plants and functional foods with diuretic effects: a nutraceutical approach to cardiovascular health.
articles.abstract: Fluid and electrolyte balance is essential for cardiovascular homeostasis, and disturbances in renal sodium and water handling contribute to hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Although pharmacological diuretics remain a cornerstone of therapy, their long-term use may be limited by electrolyte disturbances, neurohormonal activation, and reduced tolerability in frail or polymedicated patients. This narrative review examines current experimental and clinical evidence on medicinal plants and functional foods with mild diuretic or renal-vascular effects, highlighting their potential role as adjunctive strategies. Several botanicals, including Hibiscus sabdariffa, Orthosiphon stamineus, Urtica dioica, and Taraxacum officinale, exhibit natriuretic, aquaretic, antioxidant, and vasorelaxant properties through multifactorial mechanisms. However, clinical evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and frequently derived from multicomponent formulations, hindering the attribution of specific effects. In addition, dietary sources such as potassium-rich foods, herbal infusions, and whole grains may modulate fluid balance and vascular function. Still, their interaction with standard diuretic therapy warrants careful consideration. Potential nutrient-drug interactions may result in either synergistic effects or adverse outcomes, including hyperkalaemia, dehydration, or altered drug absorption. Overall, selected medicinal plants and functional foods may provide supportive benefits in early-stage cardiovascular and metabolic conditions. Still, their clinical use should remain adjunctive and individualized, pending further standardized, well-designed clinical trials.

articles.title: Meloidogyne enterolobii effector transthyretin-like protein 1 targets plant heat shock protein 90 to manipulate host immunity and promote nematode parasitism.
articles.abstract: Meloidogyne enterolobii has a wide host range and high pathogenicity, making it one of the most economically damaging root-knot nematode species. Effectors secreted by M. enterolobii are key players in the cross-talk between nematode and its host. Here, we functionally characterize a transthyretin-like effector protein (MeTTL1) from M. enterolobii. In situ hybridization revealed that MeTTL1 was expressed specifically in the dorsal esophageal gland of M. enterolobii, with the peaked transcript levels during the early parasitic stage. Immunolocalization confirmed the in planta secretion of MeTTL1 throughout nematode migration and its accumulation inside the giant cells. Host-induced gene silencing of MeTTL1 decreased nematode parasitism, reducing gall numbers by 43.6% and nematode counts by 64.1%, whereas Arabidopsis plants overexpressing MeTTL1 exhibited increased susceptibility to M. enterolobii, with gall numbers increasing by 117.1% and nematode counts by 77.7%. Furthermore, MeTTL1 actively suppresses plant immunity by attenuating flg22-induced callose deposition, inhibiting Gpa2/Rbp1-triggered cell death, and downregulating defense-related genes. Luciferase complementation and co-immunoprecipitation assays demonstrated that MeTTL1 interacts with members of the plant Hsp90 family, which are known to be involved in plant immune responses. Moreover, we confirmed that the MeTTL1 C-terminal is critical for the interaction. Notably, Arabidopsis hsp90.3 mutants exhibited increased susceptibility to M. enterolobii, supporting the biological significance of the MeTTL1-Hsp90.3 association in parasitism. In conclusion, our study demonstrates that MeTTL1 one of the key virulence factors secreted by M. enterolobii, promoting nematode parasitism by targeting plant Hsp90 family proteins to suppress host immunity.

articles.title: Photon FLASH spares radiation-induced lung injury and pulmonary hypertension in a preclinical model.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) radiotherapy has shown significant promise in reducing normal tissue toxicities with equivalent tumour control compared to conventional (CONV) dose rates termed the FLASH effect. In this study, we compared radiation-induced lung injury and changes in the pulmonary circulation following localised right lung irradiation at UHDR and CONV exposures using photons.

METHODS: Acute and late pulmonary radiation responses were assessed in pneumonitis (C3H/NeJ) and fibrosis prone (C57BL/6) mice. 18 Gy was delivered to the right lung at CONV (0.05 Gy/s), FLASH (76.2 Gy/s) and FLASH split dose (FSD, average 2.6 Gy/s) exposures. Early responses (72 h and 4 weeks after irradiation) were investigated by immunohistochemistry (Ly6G, F4/80), fluorescence staining (EdU) and serum profiling (cytokines and lipid peroxidation assays). Fibrosis was assessed at 30 weeks after irradiation by cone-beam CT (CBCT) analysis and quantification of collagen, senescence (p21) and TGF-β levels. Changes in pulmonary vasculature and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was assessed in C57BL/6 mice at 30 weeks to characterise changes in the pulmonary circulation associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH).

RESULTS: At early timepoints, UHDR exposures led to reduced immune cell infiltration (neutrophils and macrophages) and tissue damage in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. Serum analysis supported FLASH sparing with decreased levels of markers associated with chronic inflammation and increased markers of tissue repair in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. At 30 weeks after irradiation at a UHDR, the lung parenchyma was structurally similar to controls (p = 0.33) with minimal collagen deposition supported by CBCT tissue density analysis. In contrast, CONV and FSD animals showed significant collagen deposition (p < 0.01) with thickened alveolar septa and reduced alveolar air spaces. UHDR exposures significantly reduced functional and histological metrics of PH (p < 0.05) compared to CONV.

CONCLUSIONS: UHDR photons significantly reduce radiation-induced pneumonitis and fibrosis with secondary effects on the pulmonary circulation sparing PH.

articles.title: Practical Prevention of Heart Failure Across Stages A and B: A Scientific Statement From the Japanese Heart Failure Society.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a growing health problem in Japan, associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, recurrent hospitalization, impaired quality of life, and increasing healthcare costs. Early prevention before the onset of signs and symptoms has therefore become a major priority in cardiovascular medicine. This scientific statement from the Japanese Heart Failure Society provides practical prevention strategies for patients with HF Stage A and Stage B in Japan. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarker-guided screening using brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) to facilitate earlier detection of Stage B (pre-HF) and identification of patients at increased risk of progression to symptomatic HF. The statement summarizes evidence-based management of major cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disorders associated with HF development, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, coronary artery disease, left ventricular dysfunction, valvular heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. It also addresses disease-specific approaches for optimizing blood pressure, glycemic control, renal protection, lipid management, and weight reduction. Preventive strategies include lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, serial reassessment of natriuretic peptide levels, and appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging and timely specialist referral. Because many patients at risk for HF are managed outside specialized cardiovascular centers, practical pathways for collaboration between cardiologists and non-cardiologist physicians are essential. The importance of timely referral, shared risk recognition, and multidisciplinary care is therefore emphasized. Implementation of clinically applicable prevention strategies may help reduce progression to symptomatic HF, facilitate earlier therapeutic intervention, and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Multi-scale causal inference and scenario prediction for carbon emissions from energy consumption in the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration.
articles.abstract: Accurately identifying the driving mechanisms of carbon emissions from energy consumption is crucial for regional low-carbon transition. However, existing studies predominantly focus on statistical regression or trend extrapolation, lacking systematic characterization of multi-scale causal mechanisms and comprehensive evaluation of multi-scenario pathways. Therefore, this study integrates multi-source data on socioeconomic conditions, land use, and climate in the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration (PRD) from 2000 to 2022. It constructs an integrated multi-source data-deep learning model evaluation-interpretability analysis -causal identification-scenario prediction. Key variables were identified using Sharpley Additivity Explanation (SHAP), followed by quantification of net effects and transmission pathways via causal graphs. Scenario prediction for carbon emissions from energy consumption (CE) were conducted using sub-scale optimal models. The results indicate (1) Scale-specific modeling indicates that the Sparrow Search Algorithm-optimized Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Network (SSA-ConvLSTM) performs best at the pixel scale, while the Ister-Transformer deep learning model-which integrates temporal and spatial features-is optimal at the county and city scales. These models can be utilized for rolling evaluation and calibration. (2) SHAP analysis reveals a "scale synergy-morphological threshold/saturation-efficiency offsetting" relationship. Causal inference further demonstrates that pixel-scale PGDP exerts a negative effect on carbon emissions. At the county scale, GDP and JCQ primarily influence emissions through population, while at the city scale, population's direct impact on emissions is most significant. (3) Scenario simulations indicate that policy implementation should be stratified: municipal-scale "total volume constraints," county-scale "compact development and stock efficiency enhancement," and pixel-scale "energy efficiency and technological offsetting." The integrated framework of causal identification-interpretative analysis-scenario forecasting proposed in this study provides robust support for scientific carbon emission prediction and regional low-carbon policy formulation.

articles.title: Da Chuanxiong extract modulates the Lands cycle to elicit spatially specific phospholipid remodeling against cerebral ischemia.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Da Chuanxiong (DCX), composed of Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort. and Gastrodia elata Bl. (4:1), is a classical Chinese herbal formula, traditionally used for headache and vertigo caused by wind pathogen and blood stasis. Modern clinical practice has extended its application to ischemic stroke. However, whether DCX exerts neuroprotection through Lands cycle-mediated phospholipid remodeling, particularly in a spatially specific manner, remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To demonstrate whether DCX elicits spatially specific phospholipid remodeling through Lands cycle activation, and to identify the brain-penetrating constituents responsible for this effect.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Protective effects of DCX were evaluated in pMCAO rats, and those of its brain-penetrating constituents were assessed in OGD/R-induced HT22 cells. Glycerophospholipid composition and spatial distribution were analyzed by targeted lipidomics and AFADESI-QQQ-MSI-based spatial metabolomics. Lands cycle enzyme expression was measured by RT-qPCR and western blotting.

RESULTS: DCX dose-dependently reduced infarct volume and attenuated neuronal damage, accompanied by decreased ROS and MDA, elevated GSH, and preserved mitochondrial membrane integrity. Lipidomic analysis revealed that DCX shifted phospholipids from peroxidation-prone PUFA-PLs to oxidation-resistant SFA/MUFA-PLs in a spatially specific manner, reducing PUFA-PLs from 90.7% to 82.9% and increasing SFA/MUFA-PLs from 9.3% to 17.1%. SFA-PLs were region-selectively restored in hippocampus and thalamus, and MUFA-PLs in the corpus callosum and internal capsule. Mechanistically, DCX concurrently upregulated PLA2G6, ACSL3, MBOAT2, and LPCAT1, consistent with Lands cycle-mediated deacylation and reacylation. Five brain-penetrating constituents (senkyunolide A, butylphthalide, levistilide A, ferulic acid, and gastrodin) modulated these enzymes in vitro.

CONCLUSION: This work provides the first evidence that DCX elicits spatially specific phospholipid remodeling toward oxidation-resistant species, an effect associated with Lands cycle activation and its brain-penetrating constituents. This remodeling may reduce peroxidation substrate availability and counteract lipid peroxidation in cerebral ischemia.

articles.title: Platelet-macrophage crosstalk in cardiac inflammation and remodeling.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
articles.abstract: Cardiac injury and chronic heart disease are increasingly recognized as multicellular processes driven by dynamic interactions between immune and thrombotic signaling networks. Although platelets and macrophages have been extensively studied individually, the molecular mechanisms through which their reciprocal interactions regulate cardiac inflammation and remodeling remain incompletely defined. A comprehensive understanding of this cellular crosstalk is needed to define the signaling pathways that couple acute injury responses to chronic maladaptive remodeling. Among these interactions, platelet-macrophage crosstalk has emerged as an important regulator of inflammatory responses and tissue remodeling within the injured myocardium. Beyond their traditional roles in hemostasis and innate immunity, platelets communicate with macrophages through adhesion molecules, soluble mediators, and extracellular vesicles, thereby modulating macrophage activation and functional reprogramming. Platelet-derived mediators, including P-selectin, CD40L, PF4 (CXCL4), CCL5, and platelet-derived extracellular vesicles, modulate macrophage inflammatory signaling, cytokine production, redox balance, metabolic reprogramming, and pro-fibrotic responses relevant to cardiac remodeling. During acute myocardial injury, these interactions facilitate immune-cell recruitment, efferocytosis, and tissue repair, whereas persistent platelet-macrophage communication promotes chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and progression to heart failure. This review summarizes current molecular insights into platelet-macrophage interactions, focusing on receptor-mediated signaling, extracellular vesicle cargo transfer, immunometabolic regulation, and redox-dependent pathways. We also discuss emerging evidence linking this axis to trained immunity and inflammatory memory and highlight potential molecular targets for modulating maladaptive immune remodeling in cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Early PEG-bHb resuscitation for hemorrhagic shock: Attenuation of acute kidney injury via the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic shock (HS) is a major cause of traumatic death, strongly influenced by resuscitation timing. This study explored the protective effects and mechanisms of early polyethylene glycol-conjugated bovine hemoglobin (PEG-bHb) resuscitation in HS treatment.

METHODS: Following subjecting HS, rats received PEG-bHb resuscitation at 0-30 min (R_30), 30-60 min (R_60), or 60-90 min (R_90), or conventional crystalloid-colloid solution as control. Hemodynamic, acid-base, and microcirculatory parameters, survival time, renal histopathology, and pimonidazole hypoxia staining were assessed to verify the resuscitation effect. Renal transcriptomic profiling was performed, followed by validation of inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial morphology, and Nrf2/HO-1 pathway activation. The Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 was used to confirm pathway involvement.

RESULTS: All PEG-bHb groups showed restoration of hemodynamic, acid-base, and microcirculatory parameters, yet R_30 and R_60 significantly prolonged survival (27.59 h, 28.03 h) versus HES (<4 h). Histopathological and pimonidazole hypoxia staining showed markedly attenuated renal injury and reduced renal tissue hypoxia after early resuscitation. Transcriptomic and validation results revealed that R_30 suppressed renal inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis, restored mitochondrial morphology, and activated the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Nrf2 inhibition by ML385 abolished these protective effects.

CONCLUSIONS: Early PEG-bHb resuscitation ameliorates HS-induced acute kidney injury and improves survival by activating the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.

articles.title: Bergenin attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy by inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis through modulation of the YAP signaling axis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetes mellitus-associated cardiac dysfunction arises from metabolic imbalance, oxidative stress, inflammation, maladaptive remodeling, and impaired cardiac performance. Bergenin (BER), a naturally occurring small molecule with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties, has shown therapeutic potential; however, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains unclear. This study investigated the cardioprotective effects of BER in DCM, with particular emphasis on oxidative stress, the Hippo-Yes-associated protein (YAP), and ferroptosis signaling axis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: DCM was induced in rats using a high-fat diet combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ). Diabetic rats received BER (25 or 50 mg/kg/day) or empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day). Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography, followed by histopathological and molecular analyses. To further investigate the underlying mechanisms, H9c2 cardiomyoblasts exposed to high glucose were used for in vitro assessment of oxidative stress, Hippo-YAP signaling, and ferroptosis-related markers.

KEY FINDINGS: In vivo, BER treatment significantly improved cardiac function, attenuated histopathological injury, and reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibrosis in diabetic rats. Consistent with these findings, in vitro, BER reduced reactive oxygen species generation, restored mitochondrial integrity, and prevented high glucose-induced injury in H9c2 cells. Mechanistically, BER modulated YAP signaling and suppressed ferroptosis-related changes. YAP silencing attenuated the protective effects of BER, supporting a critical role for YAP in mediating its anti-ferroptotic effects.

SIGNIFICANCE: These findings demonstrate that BER exerts cardioprotective effects against diabetes-associated cardiac dysfunction and provide mechanistic evidence implicating the YAP-ferroptosis axis in this protection. Further studies are warranted to establish its translational potential.

articles.title: Immunometabolic checkpoint: The dual regulatory role of macrophages in islet destruction in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Macrophage immunometabolic states are important determinants of inflammatory and reparative responses in type 1 diabetes (T1D). Within the diabetic islet, glycolysis, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, and metabolite-dependent epigenetic and post-translational mechanisms converge to regulate macrophage signaling, chromatin accessibility, and inflammatory output. M1-like/pro-inflammatory macrophages promote β-cell injury through nitric oxide and cytokine production, whereas M2-like/reparative states support efferocytosis, immune tolerance, and tissue homeostasis. These interconnected pathways form immunometabolic checkpoints that may be therapeutically targeted to reshape the islet immune microenvironment. Precision delivery strategies may further enable cell- and context-specific modulation while limiting systemic effects.

articles.title: Influence of dietary protein deficiency on the progression and resolution of CCl₄-induced liver damage.
articles.abstract: Malnutrition remains a major global health challenge and is associated with increased susceptibility to liver disease and impaired recovery following hepatic injury. This research assesses the impact of a low-protein diet (LPD) on mice subjected to carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄)-induced liver damage. How an established state of protein deficiency affects the temporal progression of liver injury and the subsequent process of hepatic recovery remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study investigated the influence of long-term dietary protein-deficiency on the progression and resolution of CCl₄-induced liver injury using a longitudinal experimental approach. A preliminary dose-selection study identified 2 mL/kg CCl₄ as the optimal dose in both dietary groups-normal diet (ND) and LPD. The time course of injury due to CCl₄ post-administration was assessed at 0-72 h. Injury was apparent by 1 h, reached a maximum at 24 h, and was more significant in the LPD group compared to the ND group. By 72 h, ND mice showed near-complete recovery, whereas liver injury persisted in LPD mice. Inflammatory markers (TNF-α and IL-6) indicated greater inflammatory responses in the LPD mice. Also, elevated PCNA and MDA levels in the LPD mice suggest that there was increased oxidative stress in addition to an increased compensatory cell proliferation response. Histopathological assessment revealed more extensive tissue damage, including necrosis, apoptosis, and delayed regenerative recovery, in LPD mice. Therefore, by defining the temporal pattern of liver injury and recovery, this study provides a framework for identifying optimal intervention windows and evaluating therapeutic strategies under protein-deficiency conditions.

articles.title: Not Immature, but Perfect for Age: The Hemostatic System of Infants and Children as a Physiological Masterclass.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract: The hemostatic system of neonates, infants, and children has historically and recently been described using the term "immature", a label that implies deficiency, incompleteness, or even developmental failure. We challenge that characterization. Drawing on more than three decades of advances in developmental hemostasis, we argue that the hemostatic system of healthy newborns, infants, and children is not underdeveloped, but rather precisely designed and calibrated for its physiological context. Age-specific changes reflected in reference ranges, and functional compensatory mechanisms, support the view that pediatric hemostasis represents a physiological masterclass in developmental adaptation, not an imperfect approximation of adult function. We examine the historical trajectory of this field, critique the use of outdated terminology, identify key conceptual gaps, and discuss the downstream consequences of mislabeling in the context of pediatric thrombosis and hemostasis. We conclude with a call for a revised lexicon that more accurately reflects the functional sophistication of the developing hemostatic system.

articles.title: Authors' reply to the letter: Antibiotic therapy for male urinary infections: antimicrobial stewardship policy or burden of adverse effects?
Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Long-Acting Lipoglycopeptides in Osteoarticular Infections: A Multidisciplinary Approach Integrating Therapeutic Drug Monitoring and Serum Bactericidal Titre During Dalbavancin Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoarticular infections (OAIs) require multidisciplinary management and prolonged antibiotic therapy. Long-acting (LA) antibiotics may simplify care and enable early discharge, but their use in OAIs remains off-label and data on prolonged regimens are scarce. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of LA antibiotics and explored the role of therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and serum bactericidal titres (SBT) as complementary tools to support individualized treatment.

METHODS: Prospective, single-centre observational study including adult patients with OAIs treated with dalbavancin (DAL) or oritavancin (ORI), with a predefined multi-dose regimen, between November 2023-April 2024. TDM and SBT assessments were performed exclusively in dalbavancin-treated patients at predefined time points, and concordance between the two approaches was evaluated.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were included (median age 62 years; 81.5% male): 22 (81.5%) received DAL and 5 (18.5%) ORI. Fracture-related infections (44.4%) and vertebral osteomyelitis (33.3%) were most frequent. Staphylococci were the predominant pathogens. Clinical cure was achieved in 21/27 patients (77.7%). DAL concentrations generally exceeded PK/PD efficacy thresholds, although greater interindividual variability was observed at later time points. SBT consistently indicated bactericidal activity. Concordance between TDM and SBT was high across time points (78.9-94.7%), particularly in S. aureus infections.

CONCLUSIONS: LA antibiotics facilitate the management of OAIs, allowing early discharge and outpatient treatment. TDM demonstrated that DAL concentrations remained adequate during prolonged regimens, while SBT showed high concordance with TDM and provided complementary functional information. These exploratory findings suggest that combined TDM and SBT may support individualized treatment strategies, warranting confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Empagliflozin Therapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract:
KEY POINTS: Empagliflozin 25 mg once daily for 12 months was safe and well tolerated in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease at high risk of rapid progression. Those randomized to empagliflozin had a greater rate of increase in total kidney volume over 12 months compared with placebo. There was no difference between groups in the chronic rate of change in eGFR, nor in change in vascular stiffness, symptoms, and copeptin.

BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce the risk of diabetic and nondiabetic kidney disease progression; however, their safety and efficacy in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) are undetermined.

METHODS: In this pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial, we assigned 50 participants, 18-55 years of age, with ADPKD, at high risk of progression, not treated with tolvaptan, to receive empagliflozin (25 mg once daily) or placebo in a 1:1 ratio for 12 months. Primary outcomes were medication safety and tolerability. Secondary outcomes were (1) change in height-adjusted total kidney volume; (2) acute and chronic slope of eGFR; and (3) changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, plasma copeptin levels, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and patient-reported outcomes.

RESULTS: Mean age was 42±7 years, and eGFR was 70±17 ml/min per 1.73 m2. Frequency of adverse events was similar between the 2 groups. Urinary tract infection occurred in 2 empagliflozin-treated patients versus none in placebo and AKI in 1 placebo-treated patient. In total, 96% of the participants in each group tolerated the full dose of the study drug. Among the secondary outcomes, rate of change in height-adjusted total kidney volume was significantly greater in empagliflozin-treated participants (10.5%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 8.2% to 12.7%) compared with placebo (5.1%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 3.0% to 7.3%; P = 0.001). There was a faster acute decline in eGFR at 1 month among the empagliflozin (-6.2 ml/min per 1.73 m2) versus placebo groups (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m2; P = 0.01), but no differences in eGFR change from 1 to 12 months (empagliflozin group: -0.77±1.44 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year versus placebo group: -2.87±1.96 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year; P = 0.4). No between-group differences were observed in changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, copeptin, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and ADPKD Impact Score.

CONCLUSIONS: Empagliflozin at 25 mg once daily was well tolerated by patients with ADPKD. Empagliflozin induced an expected acute decline in eGFR by 1 month, followed by stable eGFR. However, those treated with empagliflozin had a greater increase in kidney volume.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NAME AND REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05510115.

articles.title: S-layers as functional armours: structure, function and variability in Clostridioides difficile.
articles.abstract: Surface layers (S-layers) are paracrystalline protein lattices that serve as molecular exoskeletons and environmental interfaces across diverse bacteria and archaea. Despite their widespread occurrence, S-layers remain comparatively understudied. The available models do not fully represent the structural and physiological diversity of S-layers, and fragmented methodologies limit comprehensive functional comparisons and detailed characterisation. Recently determined high-resolution structural details for multiple variants of Clostridioides difficile S-layer provide a uniquely rich model system with functional links to antimicrobial resistance, phage recognition and immune evasion. In this review, we present C. difficile S-layers as extremely diverse, adaptable and multifunctional structures. We (i) summarise known S-layer roles in C. difficile infection; (ii) present a comprehensive comparison of their extremely diverse structures, including unique features and topological differences in lattice assemblies; (iii) propose quantitative metrics for comparative, structural analysis of these S-layers; (iv) outline S-layer pore size thresholds for the diffusion of metabolites essential for C. difficile growth; and (v) explore possible mechanisms underlying S-layer function and highlight the key outstanding questions.

articles.title: Evaluating the feasibility and impact of a remote, algorithm-based blood pressure titration program in postpartum women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: the postpartum algorithm for text-based hypertension management (PATH) randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal postpartum management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains unknown. This pilot randomized control trial explored feasibility and safety of an algorithmic, text-based intervention targeting a blood pressure (BP) < 130/80 mmHg (in accordance with American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association recommendations - ACC/AHA) on hypertension management at 6 weeks postpartum as compared with routine care.

STUDY DESIGN: 200 postpartum patients with HDP (excluding chronic hypertension) were randomized at hospital discharge for delivery or postpartum HDP admission from a tertiary care center in a 1:1 fashion to the intervention (targeting a blood pressure < 130/ 80 mmHg) or routine care. Patients and clinicians were blinded with respect to randomization.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who achieved normotension as defined by the ACC/AHA (systolic blood pressure < 130 mmHg). Secondary outcomes were frequency of medication titration, outpatient visits, and non-billable healthcare encounters.

RESULTS: The virtual intervention did not differ from routine care with respect to the primary outcome using office- ascertained BPs (72% intervention vs 74% routine care, p = 0.83). At 6 weeks postpartum, clinic systolic BP did not differ by group (121 mmHg vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.3), though home-reported SBPs during the same period were lower among those randomized to the intervention (119 mmHg vs 125 mmHg, p < 0.001). No adverse events occurred in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: As compared to routine care delivered at a tertiary care center, no differences were observed with respect to systolic BP at 6 weeks postpartum using a virtual, algorithm-based intervention. A high proportion of patients in both randomized groups achieving normotension by ACC/AHA targets without adverse events.

articles.title: Intraoperative and postoperative fluid administration is associated with transfusion in open arteriovenous malformation and aneurysm surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Red blood cell transfusion to manage hemodynamic instability or blood loss during and after open cerebrovascular surgery has been associated with postoperative complications, making transfusion avoidance an important quality-improvement target. Iatrogenic hemodilution from liberal crystalloid administration may contribute to perioperative anemia, but its relevance in open aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation (AVM) surgery is poorly defined. We investigated factors associated with receiving intraoperative and postoperative transfusion in these open cerebrovascular procedures and the association between transfusion and early postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective propensity-matched cohort study, patients who underwent open aneurysm or AVM surgery and received an intraoperative or postoperative red blood cell transfusion were matched 1:1 with non-transfused controls. Perioperative variables-including intraoperative and 72-h postoperative fluid administration, estimated blood loss, physiological parameters, comorbidities, and laboratory values-were compared using univariate analysis, and multivariable Firth logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with transfusion. To address the temporal relationship between fluid and transfusion, a time-anchored analysis compared pre-transfusion fluids received with fluids received by controls to the same time point. Intensive care unit and hospital length of stay were evaluated.

RESULTS: Fifty-six patients (28 transfused, 28 controls) were analyzed. Transfused patients received more intravenous fluid in the first 72 postoperative hours (13.1 ± 4.4 vs 9.8 ± 4.6 L, p = 0.009), and transfusion percentage increased across fluid quartiles (21 %, 50 %, 64 %, and 64 %; p for trend = 0.020). Transfused patients also had a higher American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class and longer operative duration. Similarly, in the time-anchored analysis, receiving more fluids was associated with transfusion (adjusted OR 1.28 per L, 95 % CI 1.14-1.45), including after additional adjustment for ASA class (OR 1.23, 95 % CI 1.08-1.40). Intensive care unit and hospital stays were longer among transfused patients, but the differences were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater fluid administration perioperatively was associated with receiving intraoperative or postoperative transfusion after open aneurysm and AVM surgery. These findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a contribution of iatrogenic hemodilution, and they support prospective evaluation of fluid management.

articles.title: Effect of circadian-oriented goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disruption and circadian rhythm disturbances are common in mechanically ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients and are associated with delirium, prolonged ventilation, and poor clinical outcomes. Conventional sedation strategies may further impair sleep architecture and circadian regulation. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of circadian-oriented, goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.

METHODS: This study enrolled 65 mechanically ventilated patients admitted to ICU at Suzhou Ninth People's Hospital between March 2024 and December 2024. Using convenience sampling, 33 patients admitted between March and July 2024 were allocated to the control group and received routine sedation and nursing care, while 32 patients admitted between August and December 2024 were formed the intervention group and received sedation management individualized according to circadian sleep-wake patterns. Sleep quality was assessed on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 after intervention using the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) and a portable sleep monitor. Delirium was evaluated by Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Sedative dosage, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU and hospital stay, , clinical improvement rate, complications, and hospitalization costs were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Sleep quality improved over time in both groups; however, Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire scores were significantly higher in the intervention group at all assessment points (p < 0.05). Patients receiving circadian-oriented sedation experienced shorter durations of mechanical ventilation, reduced ICU and total hospital stays, higher rates of clinical improvement, and lower hospitalization costs compared with the control group (p < 0.05). The incidence of complications, including delirium, was also significantly lower in the intervention group.

CONCLUSION: Sedation management aligned with circadian sleep-wake patterns significantly improves sleep quality, reduces sedative requirements, lowers delirium incidence, and shortens mechanical ventilation duration, demonstrating a favorable safety profile in mechanically ventilated patients.

articles.title: Antidepressant use in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care: Frequency of withholding and association with delirium-An observational study.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to explore antidepressant use in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care who were able to be given medicines enterally (i.e. via feeding tube). As a secondary observation, we examined whether withholding an antidepressant was associated with positive Confusion Assessment Method - Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) scores.

METHODS: A 12-month (1st Jan 2020 to 31st Dec 2020) retrospective cohort study was conducted in the ICU of a 484-bed tertiary referral hospital. Invasively ventilated patients capable of receiving enteral medicines were included.

RESULTS: Of invasively ventilated ICU patients prescribed antidepressants prior to admission, 93% had their antidepressants withheld (for part, or all) of their ICU stay and antidepressant withholding was associated with higher odds of a positive CAM-ICU score. Invasively ventilated patients who had an antidepressant withheld were over five times more likely to have had a positive CAM-ICU score during their ICU stay. Availability of a buccal dosage form or a dosage form that could be given enterally did not impact prescribing or administration of pre-existing antidepressants or facilitate swapping to an alternative antidepressant.

CONCLUSIONS: Antidepressant withholding is frequent in invasively ventilated patients in intensive care who were able to be given medicines enterally. An association was identified between antidepressant withholding and positive CAM-ICU scores, warranting further investigation. Given the observed association between antidepressant withholding and positive CAM-ICU scores, review of antidepressants management may be reasonable when managing invasively ventilated patients with positive CAM-ICU scores.

articles.title: CMAP as an electrophysiological biomarker in spinal muscular atrophy: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To appraise the evidence on compound muscle action potential (CMAP) as a biomarker in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA): responsiveness to therapy, correlation with motor function, diagnosis and prognostic value, and patterns across SMA types.

METHODS: Conducted per PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261476823). PubMed and Embase were searched to August 15, 2026 for studies reporting CMAP in genetically confirmed SMA. Findings were synthesized narratively across four pre-specified domains using a Synthesis Without Meta-analysis approach. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias with Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

RESULTS: Sixty-two studies (2513 participants across reports) were included. Following disease-modifying therapy, CMAP increased in 22 of 33 contributing studies (66.7%), was stable in 9 (27.3%), and showed a mixed pattern in 2 (6.1%); none reported a net decrease. All three disease-modifying therapies were associated with CMAP increase. CMAP correlated moderately to strongly with motor function scales and discriminated diagnostic or severity categories in 6 of the 11 studies that formally tested this. Risk of bias was low or low-moderate in 27 studies; small sample size and absence of a concurrent control group were the most frequent limitations.

DISCUSSION: CMAP rises in roughly two-thirds of treated cohorts and reflects disease severity, but floor, ceiling, and site-dependent effects limit its use as a standalone surrogate endpoint. Selecting the recording site by severity, adding a second site chosen on the same basis, and agreeing standardized acquisition and normative values would strengthen its role as a prognostic stratifier and a component of multimodal models.
