articles.title: Nurse-supported smartphone diabetes self-management in older adults.
articles.abstract: While medications, healthy diet, and weight management are essential elements of any type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) treatment plan, prescribing physical activity is a key aspect of person-centered diabetes management. Smart phone diabetes applications (apps) positively affect disease self-management in older adults. To optimize technology in healthcare, a 12-week DNP project introduced a free app titled Glucose Buddy Diabetes Tracker© and coaching to a population of adults who were age 60-75 and diagnosed with T2DM and had an elevated HgA1c of 7% or higher. A pre and posttest analyzed self-reported activity levels and quality of life measures after the digital health intervention. Although the sample was small, the results were promising. Data showed that self-reported quality of life improved, and sedentary time decreased by as much as three hours. This study captured the unique challenges and barriers associated with recruitment and active participation with digital health technology in older adults.

articles.title: Transverse development of premaxilla depending on the cleft type - a clinical study over 16 years in 217 patients.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract: Functional and aesthetic problems in children with cleft lip (CL), cleft lip/alveolus (CLA) and cleft lip/alveolus/palate (CLP) arise due to the affected transversal maxillary growth. This cross-sectional, retrospective, anonymized, descriptive study aims to demonstrate the influence of the cleft form on maxillary transverse development. Metric standardized parameters were collected annually for 234 patients over an observation period of 14 years. The transverse growth of the primary (premaxilla) was analyzed as a function of the cleft form (IBM SPSS Statistics Version 26). Patients with isolated CL served as controls. Despite different stages of development, there was no difference in the transverse development of the premaxilla in unilateral CL- and CLA-patients at the age of 16, while CLP-patients ultimately have a significantly smaller transversal premaxilla width. Bilateral cleft patients showed the same significantly reduced transversal development of the premaxilla, when the hard palate (CLP) was involved. The bilateral cleft forms showed significantly less width development overall. Due to the determined transversal growth inhibition in cleft patients with involvement of the hard palate and bilateral manifestation, continuous conservative growth-adapted treatment is necessary to maintain the compromised transversal growth of the maxilla.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with increased mortality in patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to diabetic foot.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes is a public health problem that has been increasing in recent years. Infected diabetic foot is established by the presence of inflammatory response data associated with ulcers or tissue loss. Multiple risk factors are associated with diabetic foot and the need for amputation secondary to infection.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective observational cohort study conducted between 2019 and 2024. A total of 403 patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to soft tissue infection due to diabetic foot were included. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables were analyzed between deceased and surviving patients.

RESULTS: A total of 403 patients were included (median age: 58 years, IQR: 50-67; 72.7% male). Overall, in-hospital mortality was 13.4% (54/403), primarily driven by septic shock (44.4%) and decompensated chronic kidney disease (33.3%). Surgical reintervention was required in 11.1% of cases. In multivariable analysis, age (OR=1.06), pre-existing cardiac disease (OR=7.17), bilateral amputation (OR=4.36), Clavien-Dindo complication grade (OR=2.67), and surgical reintervention (OR=6.46) were independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality. Baseline serum albumin exerted a protective effect (OR=0.20).

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality following supracondylar amputation for diabetic foot is independently associated with acute septic burden, admission hypoalbuminemia, cardiorenal comorbidity, and surgical reintervention, rather than long-term glycemic control. Early identification of this high-risk profile at admission is critical to prioritize prompt infection control and perioperative optimization.

articles.title: Hospital-based surveillance of vaccine-preventable diseases in children: a retrospective study in a Dutch tertiary hospital (2024-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) are a major cause of morbidity in children, despite established immunization programs. Surveillance of VPDs is essential to inform public health strategies and strengthen national immunization programs. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of using routinely collected hospital data for in-hospital surveillance of pediatric VPDs.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in the Netherlands from July 2024 to June 2025, before national implementation of RSV immunization. Children <18 years admitted with laboratory-confirmed infections caused by pathogens with available licensed vaccines were included, regardless of inclusion in the national immunization program. Feasibility was assessed based on case ascertainment, completeness of key variables and availability of vaccination information.

RESULTS: We included 99 children (103 VPD episodes; median age 0.6 years), of whom 60% (n = 59) required pediatric intensive care. Most hospitalizations were caused by respiratory infections, particularly RSV (n = 52) and influenza (n = 27). Case ascertainment required integration of multiple data sources, as 45% of children were tested outside the study hospital. Clinical variables were largely complete and vaccination status could be determined for 84% of episodes. Overall, 9% (n = 9) of VPD episodes occurred in fully vaccinated children. Most VPD episodes (76%; n = 78) occurred in children not vaccinated against the specific pathogen, mainly because they were too young or because the pathogen or serotype was not covered by the national immunization program or current guidelines.

CONCLUSIONS: Retrospective hospital-based surveillance of pediatric VPDs is feasible and provides key information to guide efforts to optimize the national immunization program. By capturing disease severity and vaccine preventability, it complements existing surveillance data in the Netherlands.

articles.title: A national blind spot: making children visible in Australian healthcare-associated infection surveillance.
articles.abstract: Healthcare-associated infection (HAI) surveillance makes preventable harm visible, supports benchmarking and directs infection prevention resources. In Australia, however, children and young people remain only partially visible within HAI data collections. This discussion paper argues that paediatric under-reporting is produced through four related mechanisms: exclusion, where children are omitted from burden estimates; aggregation, where paediatric patients are embedded within hospital-level or adult-oriented indicators; fragmentation, where relevant data are dispersed across jurisdictions, registries and clinical systems; and substitution, where administrative or disease-specific datasets are treated as proxies for paediatric HAI surveillance. These mechanisms limit the ability to estimate paediatric HAI burden, identify high-risk groups, evaluate prevention strategies and address inequities. Existing Australian systems demonstrate that paediatric infection surveillance is feasible, but current approaches lack national coherence, paediatric-specific denominators, consistent stratification and prevention-oriented data governance. A minimum viable national paediatric HAI surveillance program should begin with agreed definitions, sentinel sites, paediatric denominators, confidential benchmarking and staged reporting of priority modules. Making children visible in HAI surveillance is essential to improving safety, equity and accountability in paediatric healthcare.

articles.title: Bacterial coexistence induces excystment of Acanthamoeba castellanii: Implications for contact lens-associated infection risk.
articles.journal: Contact lens & anterior eye : the journal of the British Contact Lens Association

articles.title: Synthetic biology for heritable viral disease resistance in livestock.
articles.abstract: Synthetic biology is rapidly expanding the strategies available to engineer disease resistance in livestock. Genome editing of host factors required for pathogen entry or replication has generated complete or partial resistance in pigs, cattle, and chickens, culminating in the first regulatory approvals of PRRSV-resistant pigs. Another frontier is emerging in which synthetic antiviral circuits detect and suppress infection through programmable molecular responses. Precision editing tools, including base and prime editors, may enable resistance through smaller and more targeted genomic changes, while organoid and stem cell-derived cell cultures are accelerating pre-animal validation. This review examines recent advances in host-factor engineering, synthetic antiviral systems, and enabling platforms, and considers the challenges of commercial dissemination, regulation, and public acceptance. Together, these developments position engineered resistance as a potentially important component of integrated livestock disease control.

articles.title: TRIM65 deficiency exacerbates HFD-induced obesity in mice associated with elevated adipose tissue inflammation and lipid accumulation.
articles.abstract: Obesity is linked to metabolic and cardiovascular complications, such as atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes (T2DM), and hypertension. Despite current therapies alleviate certain clinical manifestations, effective disease-modifying targets remain scarce. TRIM65 (tripartite motif-containing 65) has been linked to carcinogenesis, immune modulation, and inflammatory responses, yet its role in obesity remains unknown. Here, we aimed to elucidate the pathophysiological function of TRIM65 in obesity and to reveal the molecular networks regulating this process. Our results demonstrated a significant decrease in TRIM65 expression under obese conditions. Notably, TRIM65 knockout mice exhibited exacerbated high fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity, as evidenced by marked increases in body and white adipose tissue (WAT) weight, enlarged adipocyte sizes, elevated systemic and tissue inflammation, and impaired glucose and insulin tolerance. Furthermore, knockout of TRIM65 aggravated HFD-induced dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, and liver injury. Mechanistically, TRIM65 deficiency triggered the ERK1/2-NF-κB signaling cascade, leading to a pro-inflammatory environment and aggravating insulin resistance. Simultaneously, TRIM65 deficiency enhanced the expression of adipogenic and lipogenic genes while diminishing that of lipolytic genes, culminating in increased lipid accumulation. Collectively, TRIM65 is established by our findings as a pivotal negative regulator that coordinately curbs lipid synthesis and inflammatory responses, thereby positioning it as an attractive therapeutic target for obesity and its metabolic complications.

articles.title: An α1D-adrenergic receptor vaccine protects against HFpEF in mice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a global clinical challenge with high mortality and restricted therapeutic options. Persistent sympathetic nervous system (SNS) overactivation, systemic metabolic dysregulation, and chronic inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF pathogenesis. We developed ADRQβ-004, a novel therapeutic vaccine targeting α1D-adrenergic receptor (α1D-AR), to evaluate its potential in mitigating HFpEF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A "two-hit" HFpEF mouse model was established in 6-week-old male ApoE-/- mice via high-fat diet and Nω- nitro-L-arginine methyl ester administration for 17 weeks. Mice were subcutaneously immunized with five doses of ADRQβ-004. We comprehensively assessed blood pressure, glucose/lipid metabolism, diastolic function, and cardiac remodeling. Pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) was specifically analyzed via histology, RNA-seq, and biochemical assays. Furthermore, a monoclonal antibody (ADR-004) was employed in an adipocyte-cardiomyocyte co-culture system to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. ADRQβ-004 elicited high and sustained titer of specific antibody, demonstrating robust immunogenicity. Vaccination significantly improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles in HFpEF mice. Morphological and functional analyses revealed that ADRQβ-004 markedly attenuated left ventricular remodeling, diastolic dysfunction, and myocardial mitochondrial impairment. Notably, the vaccine suppressed PAT inflammation and metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, blockade of α1D-AR via ADR-004 activated the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α signaling pathway in adipocytes, which subsequently modulated adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk, leading to enhanced myocardial mitochondrial function and improved HFpEF phenotypes.

CONCLUSION: The ADRQβ-004 vaccine ameliorates HFpEF by modulating adipocyte-cardiomyocyte crosstalk through the PPARβ/AMPK/PGC1-α pathway. These findings suggest that ADRQβ-004 may serve as a promising immunomodulatory strategy for HFpEF research.

articles.title: COVID 19 and fungal infection - A double disaster:a case series.
articles.abstract: The recent Coronavirus pandemic in 2019 [COVID-19] was associated with an increased risk of opportunistic fungal co-infection. This case series presents 5 autopsy-confirmed fungal co-infections identified in patients who died following COVID-19. Among the notable findings were Fusarium-associated fungal myocarditis and human infection with Hormographiella, an extremely rare pathogen found in COVID-19. To the best of our knowledge, the latter represents the first reported fungal co-infection with this pathogen in COVID-19. We also report the first postmortem diagnosis of invasive pulmonary mucormycosis in COVID-19 in Sri Lanka, confirmed with culture as Rhizopus spp. Postmortem examination, histopathological analysis and fungal culture revealed fungal infections that had not been suspected clinically or had been only partially characterized, and provided the microbiological and pathological evidence necessary for establishing the cause of death These findings highlight the medicolegal importance of thorough autopsy examination in severe COVID-19, especially in situations where opportunistic fungal infection may have contributed to death.

articles.title: Hemorheological optimization via isovolemic hemodilution in COVID-19 ARDS under chronic environmental hypoxia: A pilot proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic environmental hypoxia induces compensatory secondary erythrocytosis and elevated whole-blood viscosity, which may aggravate microvascular thromboinflammation in severe COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). We evaluated the feasibility, safety, and exploratory outcomes of isovolemic hemodilution (IVHD) in high-altitude COVID-19 ARDS.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 30 consecutive adult lifelong high-altitude residents (elevation 3,640 m) admitted to the ICU with severe COVID-19 ARDS on invasive mechanical ventilation. Seven patients underwent clinician-selected IVHD (controlled phlebotomy of 0.5-2.0 L with isovolemic crystalloid replacement over 6-12 hours), while 23 received conventional ICU management.

RESULTS: Baseline illness severity scores (APACHE II, PaO₂) were comparable. Admission hematocrit was 59% (55-66) in the IVHD group versus 52% (36-68) in conventional controls (p=0.065). IVHD achieved rapid hemorheological decompression at 72 hours, reducing hematocrit to 38% (32-46, p=0.015) and hemoglobin to 11 g/dL (10-15, p=0.015). ICU survival was 71.4% (5/7) in the IVHD cohort versus 8.7% (2/23) in conventional controls (Fisher's exact p=0.003; crude odds ratio 26.25, 95% CI 2.9-234.3). No procedural adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSION: Rapid hemorheological optimization via IVHD was feasible, safe, and associated with an exploratory survival signal in high-altitude COVID-19 ARDS, providing a physiological rationale for prospective randomized trials.

articles.title: Monitoring the incidence of hypotension and hypoxemia as systemic secondary insults in patients with catastrophic brain injury evolving to brain death. A prospective observational pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Maintenance of systemic homeostasis and prevention of secondary injury are a cornerstone of treatment in neurocritical care to prevent organ dysfunction and adverse clinical outcome. This is a pilot descriptive and hypothesis generating study aiming to measure and characterize the incidence of systemic hypotension and hypoxemia occurring during the intensive care unit (ICU) stay in patients with catastrophic brain injury potentially evolving to brain death.

METHODS: Adult patients admitted to ICU with catastrophic brain injury and Glasgow coma scale ≤5 have been enrolled. Arterial blood pressure and SpO2 were collected minute by minute from a central station connected to patients' bedside monitors.

RESULTS: We report on 24 patients recruited prospectively from the University Hospital of Messina, Italy as a part of a larger ongoing multi-centre study. Patient monitoring data ranged from 8-3000 hours (0.3-125 days). Admission diagnoses were intracerebral haemorrhage (N= 13), TBI (N=4), SAH (N=3), ischaemic stroke (N=3) and hypoxic encephalopathy (N=1). The proportion of valid monitoring time spent with secondary insults and the pressure time index (PTI) are presented and discussed. Day 3 and 4 demonstrated the largest number of secondary insults which were mainly hypotension. Patients who progressed to brain death (n = 9) or who died in ICU from cardiac complications (n = 7) exhibited a more severe and sustained hypotensive burden compared with patients alive at discharge (n = 8). This descriptive study proved useful for identifying an optimal window for tracking insults as well as piloting several key summary measures and visualisations which will be utilized in a larger multi-centre study.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with catastrophic brain injury, the incidence of hypotension remains the highest among systemic secondary insults in patients progressing to brain death and cardiac death.

articles.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).

RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

articles.title: Reply to "Risk of serious infection, myocardial infarction, stroke, and thromboembolic events in patients in the United States with ulcerative colitis treated with tofacitinib compared with biologic treatments".
Implementing the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set (v3) within the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) was a randomized clinical trial designed to prevent type 2 diabetes (T2D) in adults with prediabetes. The DPP Outcomes Study (DPPOS) is the 30-year follow-up of this cohort, focusing on T2D, prediabetes, and related complications. Cognitive assessments began in 2009 and expanded in 2022 to examine cognitive impairment, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD related dementias (ADRD), in the surviving cohort. To support these aims, the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set version 3 (NACC-UDSv3), the standardized framework used by Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, was implemented in DPPOS in 2022 to enable data sharing with NACC. These forms were complemented by cognitive tests administered in DPPOS. We aimed to integrate the NACC-UDSv3 into the existing longitudinal DPPOS framework while maintaining fidelity to its structure and developing automated reports to streamline cognitive outcomes adjudication.

METHODS: Items from the 16 NACC-UDSv3 data forms were compared with those already collected within DPPOS to integrate overlapping similar items, add missing NACC-UDSv3 items, and create a dataset harmonized with NACC-UDSv3. Forms were adapted for electronic data capture (EDC) using the MIDAS (Multimodal Integrated Data Acquisition System, George Washington University). Automated reports integrated current and prior neuropsychological scores to support adjudications. In the first wave of the DPPOS-AD/ADRD study, 1561 cognitive adjudications were successfully completed using the harmonized DPPOS and NACC-UDSv3 data implemented into MIDAS.

DISCUSSION: The DPPOS-AD/ADRD project demonstrated that NACC-UDSv3 can be successfully integrated into a long-standing longitudinal cohort not originally designed for AD/ADRD research. The harmonization, electronic capture, and automated adjudication processes may provide a practical framework for other cohorts seeking to incorporate NACC-UDSv3 to align with national AD/ADRD research standards.

articles.title: Strategies for Biologically Guided Vascular Repair in Neuroendovascular Therapy Extracellular Vesicles, Ultrasound Microbubbles, and Bioresorbable Scaffolds.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroendovascular devices can achieve immediate angiographic success yet fail at the site that ultimately matters: the healing vessel wall. Durable therapeutic benefit depends on stable endothelialization, organized thrombus remodeling, and resolution of inflammation rather than progression to thrombosis, restenosis, or recanalization.

SUMMARY: This review reframes vascular healing as the primary therapeutic target and synthesizes evidence supporting three complementary strategies for biologically directed device integration. Among these, bioresorbable scaffolds and surface-modified implants currently have the strongest neurovascular device evidence, though this evidence derives from extracranial animal models, demonstrating improved hemocompatibility, more favorable vascular integration, and reduced long-term foreign material exposure. Extracellular vesicles, including exosomes, combined with ultrasound microbubble-mediated delivery represent promising approaches for concentrating pro-repair signals at the device interface. However, supporting evidence remains largely extracranial, and clinical translation will require rigorous control of vesicle identity and manufacturing standards, evaluation under clinically relevant antiplatelet conditions, standardized acoustic dosing, and careful assessment of branch vessel and perforator safety. No published intracranial platform has yet integrated a biological payload, focal delivery, and temporary scaffolding into a single therapeutic system. We therefore propose a stepwise translational framework that evaluates each component incrementally using endpoints aligned with clinically relevant failure mechanisms.

KEY MESSAGES: Future neuroendovascular therapies should be evaluated not only by immediate angiographic success but also by their ability to promote durable vascular healing. Key translational endpoints include surface thrombogenicity, endothelial coverage and function, quality of vascular remodeling, and preservation of branch vessel patency. A biologically directed approach to device integration may improve the long-term durability and safety of intracranial endovascular therapies.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplant in the treatment of inflammatory bowel diseases: new perspectives on delivery, mechanism, and clinical positioning.
articles.abstract: The gut microbiota, a complex and dynamic community of microorganisms, has emerged as a crucial determinant of human health and well-being in recent years. This microbial ecosystem plays a pivotal role in various physiological processes, including nutrient metabolism, immune system regulation, and intestinal homeostasis. Disruptions in the composition and function of the gut microbiota have been implicated in a wide range of diseases, such as Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). The elucidation of the fundamental relationship between human disease and the gut microbiome has positioned fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as a transformative strategy in modern clinical practice. However, while FMT is increasingly explored for a diverse range of systemic diseases, its clinical implementation is relatively limited beyond the management of recurrent CDI. This review examines the evolving role of FMT within the therapeutic framework of chronic inflammation, focusing specifically on IBD. We compare the variable clinical outcomes in IBD with the highly successful model of recurrent CDI, highlighting mechanistic and clinical determinants of response in a different disease context. Additionally, we evaluate the progression of delivery strategies, from conventional fecal suspensions to standardized oral capsule formulations, and their implications for efficacy, safety, and scalability. Furthermore, we explore the diversifying clinical scenarios where FMT may be incorporated in the treatment paradigm of IBD, including primary treatment of active inflammation, prevention of relapse, and its place in combination with current immunosuppressive therapies.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Spns2 in regulating neuroinflammatory activation of microglia after cerebral ischemia in rats.
articles.abstract: Microglia, the resident innate immune cells of the brain, maintain central nervous system homeostasis but can also mediate inflammatory injury after ischemic stroke. Following ischemia, microglia can adopt pro-inflammatory M1- or reparative M2-like state; thus, regulating the balance between these phenotypes may be therapeutically relevant. Sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling regulates immune responses, angiogenesis, and endothelial barrier integrity. Enhanced sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling in activated microglia after ischemic injury may amplify inflammatory cascades. However, strategies targeting sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling are constrained by the heterogeneous expression of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors. Spinster homolog 2 (Spns2), a sphingosine-1-phosphate exporter, may provide an alternative target, although its role in ischemic stroke remains unclear. To investigate the role of Spns2 in post-ischemic neuroinflammation, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion was induced in Spns2-deficient (Spns2-/-) and wild-type rats. BV2 microglial cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation were used as an in vitro model. Spns2 mRNA expression in the peri-infarct penumbra increased after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion and peaked at 24 hours. Compared with wild-type rats, Spns2-/- rats showed lower neurological deficit scores, improved motor performance, and smaller infarct volumes. In the peri-infarct penumbra, Spns2 deficiency was associated with decreased expression of pro-inflammatory markers, increased expression of anti-inflammatory markers, and attenuated microglia-associated NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome signaling. In BV2 cells, Spns2 knockdown produced similar changes in inflammatory-marker expression and reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced NLRP3 inflammasome-associated signaling and oxidative stress. Spns2 knockdown reduced extracellular sphingosine-1-phosphate levels in BV2-cell culture supernatants, whereas exogenous sphingosine-1-phosphate supplementation increased the expression of inflammasome-associated inflammatory mediators in Spns2-knockdown BV2 cells. RNA sequencing identified Itga5 upregulation in Spns2-/- rats and showed that differentially expressed genes between Spns2-/- and wild-type rats were enriched in the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (Akt) signaling pathway. Increased Akt phosphorylation in Spns2-/- rats was further confirmed by western blotting. These findings indicate that Spns2 deficiency limits sphingosine-1-phosphate export and attenuates microglia-associated neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke. Itga5 upregulation and increased Akt phosphorylation may be associated with this neuroprotective effect. Collectively, our results provide a basis for further investigation of the Spns2-sphingosine-1-phosphate axis in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation alleviates post-stroke depressive symptoms by enhancing hippocampal CA1 neuroplasticity via upregulation of ALK5 expression.
articles.abstract: Poststroke depression critically hampers neurological recovery, and although transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation exhibits antidepressant potential, its mechanistic basis remains incompletely defined. Given that activin receptorlike kinase 5 (ALK5) regulates neuroplasticity through the Smad2/3/growth arrest and DNA-damage-inducible 45β (Gadd45b) axis, we postulated that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation alleviates poststroke depression via this cascade. Using a rat poststroke depression model established by middle cerebral artery occlusion combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress, we knocked down ALK5 in hippocampal CA1 area and administered 14-day transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation. Behavioral assessments, histopathological and ultrastructural analyses, neurotransmitter measurements, and immunoblotting for neuroplasticity markers revealed that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reversed post-stroke depression-induced ALK5 downregulation and concurrently ameliorated depressive-like behaviors, restored monoamine levels, and enhanced neuronal survival, dendritic arborization, and synaptic integrity. Crucially, ALK5 knockdown abolished all these beneficial effects and blocked transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulationmediated activation of the Smad2/3/Gadd45b pathway. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation exerts its anti-depressant and proneuroplastic actions in poststroke depression by engaging the hippocampal ALK5 signaling cascade, thereby supporting transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation as a promising therapeutic strategy for poststroke affective and functional recovery.

articles.title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produced primarily spherical nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 282.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.197, and a zeta potential of -12.2 mV. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles displayed minimal hemolysis (0.199%) while maintaining a stable hydrodynamic diameter during 30 days of storage. Spectroscopic analyses and a 50 ns molecular dynamics simulation promoted co-assembly via multiple noncovalent-driven interactions. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles effectively reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced viability loss and apoptosis in HT22 cells. In transient middle cerebral artery occlusion mice, Cy5.5-associated fluorescence was observed in brain tissue, whereas oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticle treatment reduced infarct volume and ipsilesional brain water content, preserved neurons, resulting in improved sensorimotor and spatial cognitive outcomes through day 28. Treatment promoted PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, elevated inhibitory phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3β at Ser9 and BCL-2 expression, and reduced BAX expression. These findings suggest that oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembly offers a promising preclinical formulation approach for multifactorial neuroprotection after ischemic stroke and supports further pharmacokinetic, safety, and pathway-causality studies.

articles.title: Development of a biomimetic manganese dioxide nanoreactor delivery system: Combination of biomimetic platelet/M2 microglia hybrid membrane with Astragaloside IV for the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Conventional nanotherapeutics suffer from rapid immune clearance and insufficient accumulation in ischemic lesions. To overcome these bottlenecks, a stimuli-responsive biomimetic immunomodulatory delivery system was engineered by fusing platelet and M2 microglial membranes onto hollow mesoporous manganese dioxide nanoparticles loaded with the neuroprotective drug Astragaloside IV. The results show that this integrated nanoplatform fully leverages the synergistic properties of its biomimetic shell. Tracing the nanoparticles with the fluorescent dye Did revealed that the integrated nanoplatform exhibited more pronounced fluorescent enrichment in ischemic brain tissue; both in vivo and ex vivo imaging supported its specific homing ability. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion, the platform significantly reduced the extent of cerebral infarction, alleviated neuronal damage caused by ischemia-reperfusion, and improved neurovascular integrity and neurological function. Furthermore, the platform mitigated oxidative stress in ischemic brain tissue, curtailed the inflammatory response, and facilitated a transition in microglial phenotype toward an anti-inflammatory and reparative state. Bioinformatics results indicate that this platform significantly alters gene expression profiles following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses further point to biological processes related to inflammation and immune regulation. These findings demonstrate that this biomimetic targeted nanoplatform integrates biomimetic targeting, reactive oxygen species scavenging, and immune modulation capabilities, thereby providing a new therapeutic platform technology for the precise delivery of therapeutic agents and the remodeling of the pathological microenvironment in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Infection history and TCR sequence features shape the breadth of TCR cross-reactivity.
articles.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire enables recognition of a vast array of pathogens, despite containing far fewer unique TCRs than the diversity of encountered epitopes. This potential contradiction is resolved by TCR cross-reactivity, whereby individual TCRs recognize multiple distinct epitopes. However, the features defining broadly cross-reactive TCRs remain poorly understood. Here we systematically analyze TCRs from mice sequentially infected with influenza viruses containing naturally occurring single amino acid variants of the DbNP366 epitope. We identify 967 unique paired TCR sequences across 18 infection histories and test 22 representative TCRs against 172 epitope variants, yielding 3,784 TCR-epitope interaction measurements. These TCRs exhibit a continuum of cross-reactivity, with infection history influencing both TCR sequence similarity and reactivity profiles. We find specific TCR sequence features associated with broader cross-reactivity, highlighting the interplay between epitope exposure, TCR diversity, and function, and providing insights into CD8+ T cell adaptability, immune memory, and vaccine design.

articles.title: Serum Soluble Programmed Death Ligand-1 (sPD-L1) as a Diagnostic Marker in Neonatal Sepsis: Authors' Reply-2.
Polydatin Attenuates Isoproterenol Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Association with Reduced Oxidative Stress, NOX2 Subunit Expression, and CaMKII-MEF2C Signaling.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation contributes to adverse cardiac remodeling and the progression of heart failure, with NADPH oxidase (NOX2)-derived reactive oxygen species (ROS) acting as key mediators of redox-dependent hypertrophic signaling. Sustained ROS generation can promote oxidative activation of Ca²⁺/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) and downstream myocyte enhancer factor 2 C (MEF2C)-mediated transcriptional reprogramming. Polydatin, a natural glucoside of resveratrol, has been reported to exert antioxidant and cardioprotective effects. However, its influence on the NOX2-ROS-CaMKII-MEF2C axis under chronic β-AR stimulation remains unclear. In the present study, male Wistar rats were assigned to control, isoproterenol (5 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 4 weeks), or isoproterenol + polydatin (100 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) groups. Cardiac hypertrophy was evaluated by morphometric indices, ANP and BNP mRNA expression levels, and histological analyses. Oxidative stress was assessed through NADH oxidase activity, protein carbonyl content, and total antioxidant status. Protein expression of NOX2 subunits (gp91phox, p22phox, p47phox, p67phox, p40phox) and components of the CaMKII-MEF2C pathway were determined by Western blot and reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Isoproterenol administration induced marked cardiac hypertrophy, elevated oxidative stress markers, increased expression of NOX2 regulatory subunits, and activated the CaMKII-MEF2C pathway. Polydatin treatment significantly attenuated hypertrophic indices, reduced NADH oxidase activity and protein carbonyl levels, restored antioxidant capacity, and suppressed p47phox, p67phox, p40phox expression along with p-CaMKIIThr286/CaMKII, ox-CaMKII/CaMKII ratios and MEF2C expression. These findings suggest that the attenuation of isoproterenol induced cardiac hypertrophy by polydatin is associated with modulation of oxidative stress, NOX2 subunit expression, and CaMKII-MEF2C signaling, although a causal role of this pathway remains to be established.

articles.title: Correction to: Optimizing endovascular therapies for acute ischemic stroke: evaluating efficacy in middle cerebral artery m2 segment occlusions.
Type of dialysis may influence the prognostic value of myocardial perfusion imaging in end stage renal disease: an observational [13N]NH3 PET/CT study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) exhibit an elevated risk of cardiovascular events, with imaging-based risk stratification becoming increasingly important. This study compares the prognostic utility of [13N]NH3 PET/CT assessing myocardial blood flow (MBF), coronary flow reserve (CFR) and coronary artery calcium score (CACS) as well as 3D carotid ultrasound (for carotid plaque burden; cPB) in hemodialysis (HD) versus peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients listed for kidney transplantation.

RESULTS: 41 ESRD patients (HD n = 31; PD n = 10; median follow-up 4.9 years) without known coronary artery disease underwent myocardial perfusion imaging with [13N]NH3 PET/CT, CACS, and 3D carotid ultrasound. HD patients exhibited lower myocardial stress blood flow (MBFstress) and CFR compared to PD patients (2.67 ± 0.67 vs. 2.97 ± 0.69; p = 0.24 and 2.5 ± 0.74 vs. 3.08 ± 1.12; p = 0.07). In the HD subgroup, only MBFstress correlated inversely with CACS and cPB (r = -0.32; p < 0.05 and r = -0.44; p < 0.05), whereas CFR did not (r=-0.14; p = 0.47 and r= -0.14; p = 0.44). On the other hand, both MBFstress and CFR were predictive of cardiovascular events in HD patients, although the number of events was low (n = 4). In contrast, PD patients exhibited only one single cardiovascular event in the follow-up and no significant imaging correlations were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: MBFstress and CFR may emerge as prognostic markers for cardiovascular events in HD patients whereas their prognostic power in PD patients remains uncertain. HD patients show more pronounced impairment in MBFstress and atherosclerotic plaque burden in the carotid artery, highlighting particularly this parameter as a prognostic marker in this group.

articles.title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This guideline establishes recommendations for the treatment of SWD.

METHODS: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) commissioned a task force of experts in sleep and circadian medicine to develop recommendations and assign strengths based on a systematic review of the literature and an assessment of the evidence using the GRADE process. The task force summarized the relevant literature and the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations supporting the recommendations. The AASM Board of Directors approved the final recommendations.

RECOMMENDATIONS: The following recommendations are intended as a guide for clinicians in choosing specific treatment(s) for symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or insomnia, and for circadian adaptation in adults with SWD. Each recommendation statement is assigned a strength (e.g., "Strong" or "Conditional"). For SWD, there were only "conditional" recommendations for or against (i.e., "We suggest…") and those requiring the clinician to use clinical knowledge and experience and consider the individual patient's values and preferences to determine the best course of action. Interventions in recommendation statements were compared to no treatment. Adults with SWD with symptoms of excessive sleepiness associated with work schedule: 1. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of armodafinil or modafinil taken 30 to 60 minutes prior to the night shift over no armodafinil or modafinil (Conditional recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence). 2. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of bright light over no bright light during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: Individuals with SWD who exhibit insomnia and daytime function impairments may also benefit from using bright light during their night shift. 3. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of caffeine taken prior to and/or during the night shift over no caffeine (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: Caffeine intake close to bedtime can disrupt sleep onset and quality, which may exacerbate symptoms of SWD. 4. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of a clockwise rotating shift schedule over a counterclockwise rotating shift schedule (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 5. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests taking a nap over no nap prior to the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: Sleep inertia occurring soon after the nap may temporarily increase sleepiness, decrease cognitive performance, and increase accident risk. Allowing adequate time for resolution of sleep inertia prior to driving or performing other safety-sensitive behaviors may be needed to reduce these risks. 6. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests either not eating or eating a snack rather than eating a full meal during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 7. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the combination of caffeine and bright light over the combination of no caffeine and no bright light (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: Caffeine intake close to bedtime can disrupt sleep onset and quality, which may exacerbate symptoms of SWD. 8. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the combination of taking a nap and caffeine over the combination of no nap and no caffeine prior to the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Adults with SWD with sleep disturbance/insomnia: 9. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia the AASM suggests the use of CBT-I over no CBT-I (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 10. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia following the night shift, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 11. In adults with SWD with sleep disturbance/insomnia, when transitioning from daytime to nighttime sleep, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin for night sleep following shift work (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 12. In adults with SWD who desire to take a nap prior to the first night shift, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin prior to the nap (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: Melatonin may temporarily increase sleepiness, decrease cognitive performance, and increase accident risk. Allowing adequate time for resolution of sleepiness prior to driving, returning to work or performing other safety-sensitive behaviors may be needed to reduce these risks. 13. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests the use of ramelteon or other melatonin receptor agonists over no melatonin receptor agonist (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 14. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests the use of suvorexant or other dual orexin receptor antagonists over no dual orexin receptor antagonists (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 15. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests against the use of triazolam and other benzodiazepines (conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation: 16. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the use of bright light over no bright light during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty).

REMARK: For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. 17. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the combination of bright light at night and fixed daytime sleep timing over the combination of no bright light and no fixed sleep timing (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. 18. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the combination of bright light at night, fixed daytime sleep timing, and reduced-light-transmittance glasses in the morning over the combination of no bright light, no fixed sleep timing, and no reduced-light-transmittance glasses (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Remark 1 : For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. Remark 2: Attention to driving safety is important when wearing reduced-light-transmittance glasses. Other considerations for adults with SWD: 19. In adults with SWD who are working either an 8-hour or 12-hour night shift, the AASM does not suggest working one shift duration over the other (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence).

REMARK: This recommendation does not consider other shift durations, rotation, or the number of consecutive shifts. This guideline did not look at shift durations exceeding 12 hours. The total number of hours worked per week ranged from 36 to 52.

articles.title: A reference-based approach using whole-brain segmentation for estimating blood activity concentration in CBV quantification.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images.

METHODS: Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling.

RESULTS: The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

articles.title: Hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension under isoflurane anesthesia.
articles.abstract: While dopamine and dobutamine are widely used in anesthetized dogs, clinical evidence supporting their use remains limited. We aimed to compare the hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension undergoing elective orthopedic surgery under fentanyl-isoflurane anesthesia. The pressor effects at clinical dosages (2-8 µg/kg/min) of dopamine (n = 15) and dobutamine (n = 15) for hypotension were compared and confirmed using the ramped-rate infusion protocol in 30 dogs. The following hemodynamic parameters measured by invasive arterial blood pressure and transesophageal echocardiographic monitoring were analyzed: heart rate (HR), systolic (SAP), mean (MAP), diastolic arterial pressure (DAP), stroke volume index (SVI), cardiac index (CI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). The proportion of dogs that achieved the treatment goal (MAP: 70-89 mmHg) was 93% (dopamine responders, 14/15 dogs) in the dopamine group and 53% (dobutamine responders, 8/15 dogs) in the dobutamine group, with a significantly higher probability in the dopamine group (P = 0.035, a risk difference of 40% [95% confidence interval: 8.2-63.9%]). In dopamine responders, significant increases were observed in SAP, MAP, DAP, SVI and CI, whereas no significant changes were observed in HR and SVRI. In conclusion, the pressor effect was more likely to be observed at the clinical dosage of dopamine than that of dobutamine for treating hypotension in isoflurane anesthetized dogs. This study was approved by the Nihon University Animal Medical Center Research and Trial Ethics Committee (approval number: 1-007; approval date: September 29, 2022).

articles.title: Effects of uridine on cardiomyocyte mitochondrial function in SHR in the early stage of hypertension.
articles.abstract: The development of heart failure due to hypertension is known to be accompanied by various mitochondrial dysfunctions. It has previously been established that the pyrimidine nucleoside uridine (U) exerts a protective effect on the structural and functional parameters of mitochondria under various pathological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the functional state of mitochondria in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) in the stage of the early hypertension and to investigate the effect of uridine on mitochondrial dysfunction associated with this pathology. A 30-mg/kg uridine was found not to affect blood pressure (BP) dynamics in SHR and WKY (Wistar Kyoto) animals. In SHR, the levels of thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS) in serum increased compared to WKY. SHR cardiac mitochondria showed decrease in respiratory control ratio compared to WKY mitochondria. Injection of uridine was accompanied by a respiratory rate decrease in the SHR + U group relative to the control. Uridine increased the levels of respiratory complexes IV and V subunits in SHR. The rate of H2O2 generation in SHR cardiac mitochondria to be restored to the control levels after uridine administration. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities in SHR decreased; herewith, uridine caused no statistically significant changes in SOD, GPx, and catalase (CAT) activities. This nucleoside was found not to affect the levels of mitochondrial ATP-sensitive potassium channel (MITOK) subunits in both animal strains studied. Thus, uridine exhibited antioxidant effects, contributing to partial normalization of cardiac mitochondrial function in SHR in the early stages of hypertension. This was probably due to modulation of the activity of mitochondrial transport systems, without the risk of hypertensive effects. These data justify further research into uridine as a cardiomyocyte protector. Hypertension, mitochondrial dysfunctions, uridine, oxidative stress, MITOK, SHR rats, OXPHOS.

articles.title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The purpose of this systematic review is to provide supporting evidence for a clinical practice guideline on the treatment of adults with shift work disorder (SWD).

METHODS: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine commissioned a task force of six experts in sleep and circadian medicine. A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and treatment trials in which treatments for the symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or sleep disturbance/insomnia in adults with SWD, and for circadian adaptation to shift work schedules was tested. Evidence from controlled laboratory trials of simulated shift work and of field-based trials of shift workers with and without a diagnosis of SWD was included. Statistical analyses were performed to determine the significance of critical and important outcomes and clinically meaningful thresholds were set to determine the clinical relevance of treatments on the outcomes examined, where possible. Finally, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) process was used to assess the evidence for making recommendations.

RESULTS: The literature search resulted in 3,045 articles; 118 studies provided data suitable for statistical analyses. The task force provided a detailed summary of the evidence along with the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations.

articles.title: Contemporary bulk-fill restorative materials under simulated asthma inhalation therapy: a comparative assessment of surface stability.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the surface stability of four contemporary bulk-fill restorative materials following simulated 21-day antiasthmatic inhalation therapy, and to investigate the relationships among the resulting surface changes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: One hundred ninety-two disc-shaped specimens (8 × 2 mm) were prepared from four bulk-fill restorative materials: a nanofilled composite (Filtek One Bulk), an alkasite (Cention Forte), a giomer (Beautifil-Bulk) and a self-cure composite (Stela Capsule) (n = 8 per subgroup). Specimens were exposed once daily for 21 days via nebulizer to budesonide, fluticasone, salbutamol, budesonide + salbutamol, or fluticasone + salbutamol, while the control specimens were stored in artificial saliva. Changes in color (ΔE00), gloss, microhardness and surface roughness were assessed relative to baseline. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests and Spearman correlations (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: Restorative material and inhaler group significantly affected all four parameters (p < 0.05). Salbutamol caused significantly greater changes than budesonide, fluticasone and the control in every material; the combination regimens were intermediate, and budesonide and fluticasone generally did not differ. The self-cure composite was the least stable and the nanofilled composite the most stable (except for color); microhardness loss increased significantly in the order Filtek One Bulk < Beautifil-Bulk < Cention Forte < Stela Capsule. All four surface parameters were strongly and positively correlated (ρ = 0.79-0.94; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Simulated antiasthmatic inhaler exposure degraded the surface of all bulk-fill materials in a material-dependent manner, with salbutamol exerting the greatest effect. The nanofilled composite showed the highest resistance.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For asthmatic patients, and especially frequent salbutamol users, a highly filled light-cured nanofilled composite appears preferable to a self-cure bulk-fill composite where surface durability is clinically important.

articles.title: Pharmacological downregulation of Fetuin-A attenuates TLR4-mediated neuroinflammation in aged rats with minimal hepatic encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Minimal hepatic encephalopathy (MHE) is a neurological complication associated with chronic liver disease characterized by subtle cognitive impairment and neuroinflammation, particularly in the aging population. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying age-associated MHE remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the role of Fetuin-A-mediated neuroinflammation and its potential as a therapeutic target in the management of MHE in old rats using pioglitazone in a thioacetamide (TAA)-induced MHE model in aged rats. Old male rats were administered TAA (50 mg/kg) for 14 days to induce MHE, followed by pioglitazone treatment (3 mg/kg) for 7 days. Western blot and immunofluorescence analyses revealed elevated hippocampal Fetuin-A expression in MHE rats, accompanied by activation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway and increased inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). Pioglitazone treatment significantly reduced Fetuin-A expression and was accompanied by reduced TLR4, MyD88 and nuclear NF-κB expression, and by decreased astrocyte activation Furthermore, histological and Golgi-Cox analyses demonstrated restoration of neuronal density, dendritic arborization, and spine density in the hippocampus of pioglitazone-treated old MHE rats. Behavioral analyses further confirmed the molecular and histological findings. Thus, elevated hippocampal Fetuin-A is associated with TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB activation in aged MHE rats, and its pharmacological reduction by pioglitazone is accompanied by reduced neuroinflammation, restored hippocampal cytoarchitecture and recovered recognition memory. A causal role for Fetuin-A remains to be established by direct perturbation.

articles.title: Endothelial mechanosensitive transcription factor NR4A1 induced by Piezo1 modulates thrombosis via PTGS2.
articles.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction-induced platelet activation contributes to thrombosis in major cardiovascular diseases. Endothelial cells sense hemodynamic shear stress via the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1, which determines their physiological functions. However, the downstream transcriptional pathways of Piezo1 linking mechanical force to endothelial function remain incompletely defined. Here, nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1) is identified as an endothelial mechanosensitive transcription factor induced by Piezo1 that modulates platelet activation and thrombosis. Mechanistically, shear stress is shown to activate Piezo1, resulting in calcium influx and the subsequent activation of protein kinase C δ (PKCδ), which activates extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) to induce NR4A1 transcription. NR4A1 then upregulates prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2) expression, leading to the increased production of prostacyclin and inhibition of platelet activation and thrombosis. In vivo, mice with endothelial cell-specific deletion of Nr4a1 exhibit greater thrombus weights and faster occlusion. These data establish the Piezo1/Ca2+/PKCδ/ERK/NR4A1/PTGS2 signaling cascade as a critical endothelial mechanotransduction pathway that senses physiological shear force to transcriptionally promote an antithrombotic state.

articles.title: β-defensin 130 Counteracts ETEC-K88 Infection in Mice: Mechanistic Insights from Gut Microbiome and LC-MS-Based Metabolomic Correlation Analysis.
articles.abstract: β-defensin 130 is a potential antimicrobial peptide candidate against enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)-K88 infection, but its in vivo mechanism remains unclear. In this study, the antibacterial activity of β-defensin 130 against ETEC-K88 was first evaluated in vitro, and membrane damage was observed by morphological disruption and PI uptake. Then, an ETEC-K88-infected mouse model was established and treated with β-defensin 130. Based on 16 S rDNA sequencing and LC-MS metabolomics, ETEC-K88 infection was shown to reduce gut microbial diversity and alter community structure. Correlation analysis revealed significant microbiota-metabolite interactions, β-defensin 130 treatment was associated with increased gut microbial diversity and partial recovery of the gut microbial community, increased beneficial Bacteroidota/Firmicutes, decreased pathogenic Proteobacteria, and partial reversal of infection-associated metabolic disturbances (e.g., upregulating L-tryptophan and linoleic acid). Collectively, these findings suggest that β-defensin 130 may alleviate ETEC-K88 infection by disrupting bacterial membranes, modulating gut microbiota, and partially restoring metabolic homeostasis, supporting its further development as a potential antimicrobial agent.

articles.title: Combination therapy of carbon dioxide laser with topical halometason cream and 308 nm excimer laser for the treatment of vitiligo: an optimized combined treatment protocol.
articles.abstract: The treatment for refractory non-segmental vitiligo (RNSV) remains unsatisfactory, particularly for acral vitiligo (AV) and phototherapy platform-stage vitiligo (PPV), despite the numerous treatment modalities available for vitiligo. The efficacy of a triple combination therapy comprising a 308-nm excimer lamp, a fractional CO2 laser, and a topical formulation was examined in this study. A better topical formulation and fractional CO2 laser settings were tested on 64 fresh human foreskin samples. At 15 mJ pulse energy and 10% coverage, the fractional CO2 laser and topical halometasone cream achieved a more widespread and consistent distribution with minimal side effects. The clinical trial included 98 individuals with 158 RNSV lesions. A total of 46 patients with 98 AV lesions and 52 with 60 PPV lesions were randomly assigned to T and C groups. T groups received fractional CO2 laser, plastic-wrapped halometasone cream, and 308-nm excimer lamp therapy. The C group received 308-nm excimer lamp, topical calcineurin inhibitor and halometasone cream (without fractional CO₂ laser). A twice-weekly 308-nm excimer lamp therapy was used for three months. In the T group of PPV, 50% of lesions were successful at the conclusion of the research, while only 10% of lesions in the C group of PPV were successful (P ≤ 0.000). Success was attained by 8.16% of lesions in the T group of AV, while only 6.12% of lesions in the C group of AV were successful (P = 0.425). The PPV is definitively influenced by the tripartite combination therapy of a 308-nm excimer lamp, topical halometasone cream, and fractional CO2 laser. The treatment duration of PPV can be shortened and the phototherapy platform stage can be avoided. Conversely, the combination treatment did not yield satisfactory results for vitiligo in the acral region.

articles.title: Changes in management of FETO-treated infants with severe CDH.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to evaluate changes in outcomes and management of infants with severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) undergoing fetoscopic endoluminal tracheal occlusion (FETO) across two eras, and to compare outcomes by side of defect over the last decade. Retrospective review of liveborn infants with severe CDH (observed to expected lung to head ratio [O/E LHR] < 0.25 left-sided; < 0.45 right-sided) who underwent FETO at King's College Hospital, London, UK, and survived to delivery. Fifty-eight infants were included across two 5-year periods (2002-2007 and 2020-2025). Survival improved from 44.1% to 70.8% (p = 0.044). Right-sided defects were more common in the second epoch (9% versus 54%, p < 0.001). All infants in the second era had echocardiography-guided inotropic and ventilatory management, which was not universally available earlier. In the second epoch surgical repair occurred later (4.0 versus 6.5 days, p = 0.018), repair by two-stage abdominal closure (laparostomy) increased from 0% to 77.8% (p < 0.001) and recurrence fell from 33 to 0% (p = 0.042). Mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy and admission were longer latterly. In thirty-one infants delivered between 2015 and 2025, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred in 67% of left-versus 92% of right-sided CDH, but at an earlier gestational age in left (p = 0.032). Left CDH infants had longer duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and hospital stay (p = 0.006) with no mortality difference (exploratory).

CONCLUSION: Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH infants improved from 44 to 71% alongside later repair, staged abdominal closure and echocardiography-guided management. Left-sided defects had greater respiratory morbidity and longer admission than right-sided defects without changing survival.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • FETO improves survival in severe left-sided CDH, but postnatal management has changed substantially since its introduction.

WHAT IS NEW: • Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH rose from 44 to 71% over two decades despite more right-sided defects. Repair occurred later, following haemodynamic and respiratory stabilisation (as guided by echocardiography) with staged abdominal closure in 77.8% of recent repairs; recurrence decreased from 33 to 0%. • Left-sided CDH infants had greater respiratory morbidity and length of stay than right-sided CDH infants, without a significant difference in mortality.

articles.title: Epidemiological, etiological, and antifungal resistance patterns of vulvovaginal Candida spp. infections in Cameroon: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is a common fungal infection, mainly due to Candida species, affecting two-thirds of women globally at least once in their lifetime. Here, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261368975) of the epidemiology, aetiology, and drug resistance profiles of vulvovaginal Candida infections and VVC in Cameroon. Databases were queried to identify all eligible papers. Data were extracted, and the quality bias of studies was assessed. Random effect models were used to estimate pooled proportions of primary outcomes. Thirty-four studies were included. The pooled proportions of vulvovaginal Candida infections and VVC were 33.3% (95% CI 25.5 - 41.6%, p < 0.0001) and 31.6% (95% CI 26.9 - 36.4%, p < 0.0001), respectively. Candida albicans (23.3%, 95%CI 17.9 - 29.1%, p < 0.0001) was the most frequently isolated causative species, followed by Nakaseomyces glabratus (formerly C. glabrata) (2.3%, 95%CI 0.9 - 4.2%, p < 0.0001) and Pichia kudriavzevii (formerly C. krusei) (1.3%, 95%CI 0.5 - 2.5%, p < 0.0001). Pregnancy status, diagnostic methods, and human immunodeficiency virus infection influenced the proportions of these species. Two primary azoles were least effective against C. albicans, with the following resistance levels: fluconazole (51.1%, 95% CI 21.2 - 80.7%, p < 0.0001) and itraconazole (50.5%, 95% CI 41.3 - 100%, p < 0.0001). Evidence of drug profiles for non-albicans species is limited. The findings highlight the substantial burden of VVC, the predominance of C. albicans, and high azole resistance in Cameroon. They underscore the need for standardised diagnostic approaches, broader epidemiological surveillance, and evidence-based preventive strategies.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of international guidelines for the management of chronic kidney disease mineral and bone disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) is a systemic complication of chronic kidney disease involving disturbances in mineral homeostasis, bone and skeletal physiology, and cardiac calcification. Several professional societies have issued guidelines that differ in scope, publication date, patient population, evidence/recommendation strength, and the clinical context in which they were developed. This critical review compares major international and regional guidelines, including KDIGO, KDOQI, NICE, JSDT, SLANH, KSN, CARI, ERBP, the Canadian Society of Nephrology, Chinese CKD-MBD guidance, and the 2025 KDIGO Controversies Conference.

METHODS: This review presents a structured critical comparison of major guidelines and consensus documents. We identified relevant guidelines and consensus documents using keywords related to CKD-MBD, KDIGO, KDOQI, NICE, PTH, phosphate, vitamin D, JSDT, SLANH, KSN, CARI, ERBP, Canada, and China through PubMed, Google Scholar, and the official websites of relevant organizations. We conducted the literature search on 10th February 2026. The search covered guideline and consensus documents published between January 2000 and February 2026. Comparisons were made regarding scope, monitoring, calcium and phosphate management, PTH, vitamin D, pharmacological treatments, certainty and strength of evidence or recommendations when available, and contextual factors.

FINDINGS: Although the key documents share similar general objectives of reducing bone and heart disease, they differ in how they monitor and manage biochemical abnormalities. The KDIGO 2017 guideline recommends focusing on trends rather than strict numbers for several aspects, including progressive or persistent abnormalities. In contrast, KDOQI 2003 offers a historical, target-oriented perspective, while NICE NG203 covers CKD more broadly and does not directly address CKD-MBD. The regional guidelines offer an additional perspective, especially for dialysis patients. The 2025 KDIGO Controversies Conference summary reevaluated new evidence collected after 2017, outlined gaps in the knowledge base, and suggested a more individualized approach involving mineral metabolism and CKD-related osteoporosis and heart disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Differences between CKD-MBD guidance documents should be viewed in light of publication date, scope, target population, evidence uncertainty, and healthcare system. Future guidance could be improved by paying more attention to patient-centered outcomes, standardized biochemistry, international perspectives, and resource availability.

articles.title: Fufang Xianzhuli Ye attenuates airway inflammation and epithelial injury in experimental asthma: involvement of PI3K-Akt and PPAR-γ signaling and associated lipid metabolic changes.
articles.abstract: Asthma is characterized by chronic airway inflammation and epithelial injury. Fufang Xianzhuli Ye (FXZLY) is a traditional Chinese medicinal formulation used for respiratory disorders. However, its pharmacological effects and underlying mechanisms in asthma remain incompletely understood. In this study, FXZLY was evaluated in an ovalbumin-induced murine model of asthma and an LPS-stimulated lung organoid model. Airway inflammation was assessed by bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cell analysis and lung histopathology. Lung transcriptomics and serum metabolomics were performed to characterize treatment-associated molecular alterations. In lung organoids, inflammatory cytokines, apoptosis-related genes, and PI3K-Akt and PPAR-γ signaling were examined. Pharmacological inhibition was further used to assess the functional involvement of these pathways. FXZLY reduced inflammatory cell infiltration in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and attenuated lung histopathological injury-related changes. Transcriptomic analysis identified changes in genes related to inflammatory responses, lipid metabolism, and cell survival. Serum metabolomic profiling showed partial reversal of lipid metabolic alterations, particularly those involving glycerophospholipid and linoleic acid metabolism. In LPS-stimulated lung organoids, FXZLY reduced the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α. It also decreased Bax and Caspase-3 expression while increasing Bcl2 expression. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 and the PPAR-γ antagonist GW9662 partially attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of FXZLY and reversed several FXZLY-associated changes in apoptosis-related gene expression. These findings support the functional involvement of PI3K-Akt and PPAR-γ signaling. Overall, FXZLY attenuated airway inflammation and epithelial injury in experimental asthma. Its effects were associated with partial reversal of lipid metabolic alterations and involved PI3K-Akt and PPAR-γ signaling. These results provide an experimental basis for further investigation of FXZLY in airway inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Effectiveness of leniolisib in reducing infections among patients with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase δ syndrome (APDS).
articles.abstract: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity characterized by clinical manifestations, including recurrent infections. This real-world, retrospective analysis evaluated patient-reported infection rates before and after leniolisib initiation. Patients (aged ≥ 12 years) newly initiating leniolisib therapy were eligible for inclusion. Data were retrieved from PANTHERx Rare Pharmacy. Patient-reported infection rates during the baseline period (one year before leniolisib initiation) were compared with infection rates after leniolisib initiation (observation period; from initiation to end of data or death) using generalized estimating equations Poisson regression models with robust standard errors.
