Patients who had an infection assessment collected via a standardized questionnaire during the baseline and observation periods were included in the analysis (N = 71); subgroups for baseline infection rates (lower and higher than the median) and age (12-17 and ≥ 18 years) were also evaluated. The mean (SD) rate of infections per patient-year (PPY) decreased significantly-by 68%-from 5.8 (5.1) during baseline to 1.9 (2.0) in the observation period (rate ratio [RR], 0.32; 95% CI, 0.24-0.42; P < 0.001); infections PPY decreased by 38% in patients with low baseline infection rates (RR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.43-0.89; P = 0.010) and 76% in those with high baseline infection rates (RR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.17-0.34; P < 0.001); infections PPY decreased by 70% in those aged 12 - 17 years (RR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.20-0.45; P < 0.001) and by 67% in those aged ≥ 18 years (RR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.23-0.49; P < 0.001). Real-world evidence demonstrated that leniolisib treatment provided a significant reduction in infection rates overall and among subgroups.

articles.title: Incidence, clinical presentation, and outcomes of Pasteurella infections: a population-based study in the North Denmark Region (2009-2023).
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pasteurella is associated with human infections following animal bites, though non-bite infections have been reported. Few population-based studies have examined the incidence, clinical presentation, and outcomes of Pasteurella infections.

METHODS: We identified patients with Pasteurella-positive clinical samples in the North Denmark Region (2009-2023). Medical records of hospitalized patients were reviewed for comorbidities, clinical presentation, surgical and antibiotic treatment, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: We identified 676 patients, of whom 375 were managed in general practice and 301 had a hospital contact. The annual incidence rate increased from 4.1 to 10.3 cases per 100,000 individuals (2009-2023). Pasteurella multocida (61%) predominated, followed by Pasteurella canis (26%), and 41% of samples were polymicrobial. Median age was 60 (IQR 47-70) years among patients with a hospital contact and 59 (IQR 42-70) years among those seen in general practice; 50% and 42% were male, respectively. Among patients with hospital contacts, 57% had underlying comorbidities. Clinical presentations included bite wound infections (59%), chronic wound infections (15%), lower respiratory tract infections (13%), concurrent or isolated bacteremia (6%), and other uncommon presentations (7%). Among patients with a hospital contact, 98% received antibiotic treatment, 65% surgical treatment, and 6% intensive care. The 30-day mortality was 2.7%.

CONCLUSION: The annual incidence of Pasteurella-positive samples increased over time. Almost half of the patients had a hospital contact, and two-thirds of these underwent surgical intervention. While animal bite was the most common exposure, Pasteurella was also detected in chronic ulcers and respiratory tract infections. The incidence of bacteremia and 30-day mortality were low.

articles.title: Optimization of a thermal shaker-aided quaking-induced conversion platform for the rapid detection of prion seeding activity in human samples.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is a rapidly progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disorder caused by the misfolding of the normal prion protein (PrPC) into its pathogenic form (PrPSc). Therefore, effective clinical management and infection control require diagnostic assays that combine sub-attomole sensitivity with a turnaround time compatible with routine practice. While real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) offers excellent analytical performance, its protracted reaction time and dependence on plate readers that integrate high-speed shaking with continuous fluorescence detection restrict its widespread implementation.　 METHODS: Endpoint QuIC (EP-QuIC) is an established alternative approach that utilizes vigorous shaking in a ThermoMixer® C and relies on a single endpoint fluorescence readout. In this study, we introduced minor modifications to assay conditions to enhance the speed, robustness, and reproducibility of EP-QuIC.

RESULTS: The refined assay detected prion seeding activity in sporadic CJD brain samples within 6 h-and, in some cases, as early as 2 h. Unlike RT-QuIC, problematic recombinant PrP batches that impaired assay reliability in RT-QuIC-exhibiting delayed kinetics and spontaneous ThT fluorescence in unseeded reactions-did not produce such effects in EP-QuIC. Instead, they yielded strong, specific fluorescence signals that clearly identified sCJD samples, demonstrating improved batch tolerance and diagnostic efficiency of this approach. When applied to CSF, the EP-QuIC assay showed 100% sensitivity and specificity.

CONCLUSION: The EP-QuIC assay has the potential as a rapid and reliable diagnostic tool for human prion diseases.

articles.title: Multiparametric imaging with dynamic 18 F-FDG PET shows increased breast glucose metabolism in patients with breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multiparametric PET separates tracer signal into bound and free fractions via reconstructions that reflect the net trapping rate (Ki) and apparent distribution volume (DV). This study aimed to investigate differences in background parenchymal uptake (BPU) between patients with and without breast cancer using multiparametric PET and to evaluate differences in primary tumor uptake according to hormone receptor status.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included female patients (n = 48) with newly diagnosed breast cancer and 146 patients without breast cancer. Patients with breast cancer under or after treatment and patients with bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Enrolled patients underwent whole-body dynamic PET and three quantitative indices representing BPU (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], Ki and DV) were calculated. The primary tumor uptake was calculated between estrogen- or progesterone-receptor-positive and -negative groups.

RESULTS: The mean SUVmax, Ki and DV of breast cancer cases were 1.39 ± 0.352, 4.88 × 10 - 3 ± 1.61 × 10 - 3 and 24.2 ± 15.4 respectively, whereas in control cases, mean SUVmax, Ki and DV were 1.10 ± 0.320, 3.96 × 10 - 3 ± 1.25 × 10 - 3 and 17.1 ± 10.8 respectively (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004). The areas under the curve from the ROC analysis for breast cancer presence were calculated as 0.727, 0.681 and 0.653 respectively. In addition, age-stratified analysis showed that SUVmax and Ki were significantly higher in patients with breast cancer than in patients without breast cancer. Regarding the primary tumor uptake, Ki was significantly higher in the estrogen receptor-positive group.

CONCLUSION: Multiparametric PET revealed that pure glucose metabolism is significantly elevated in the background mammary glands of patients with breast cancer, and the Ki in the primary tumor is associated with ER status. Dynamic PET imaging may be a useful imaging biomarker for the development of breast cancer.

articles.title: Prospective evaluation of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation for refractory ventricular tachycardia: initial clinical experience in Japan.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This prospective study evaluated the 1 year safety and efficacy of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) delivered using the CyberKnife system for refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in Japanese patients, in accordance with a prespecified clinical protocol.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three male patients with radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA)-refractory VT and structural heart disease, namely hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), were enrolled. A single fraction of 25 Gy was delivered to the target volume defined by multimodal image fusion. The primary endpoint was the absence of Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events within 12 months.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint was achieved, with no acute or subacute Grade ≥ 3 toxicities observed in any patient during the first year. Although all patients experienced a reduction in VT burden, the clinical course differed by etiology. Cases 2 (DCM) and 3 (ICM) showed typical responses, including delayed efficacy and late recurrence requiring repeat RFCA. In contrast, Case 1 (HCM), with a substantially larger target volume (133 mL), showed a rapid response but a progressive decline in left ventricular ejection fraction by myocardial scintigraphy, from 59.7% to 40.0%, during the 24 month extended follow-up.

CONCLUSION: STAR demonstrated preliminary feasibility as a noninvasive salvage therapy for refractory VT in this initial Japanese pilot experience. However, the late functional decline observed in Case 1 highlights the need for long-term follow-up and myocardium-sparing techniques for large target volumes. (jRCTs042230030).

articles.title: Spirituality and Religion in Diabetes Mellitus Research Across Asia: a Bibliometric Analysis of the Web of Science (1990-2026).
articles.abstract: Spirituality and religion may represent important dimensions of diabetes management, particularly in Asia, where cultural and religious beliefs are closely integrated into everyday life. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of the research on spirituality and religion in diabetes mellitus across Asia that was published between 1990 and 2026 using the Web of Science Core Collection. This study aimed to examine publication trends, research productivity, citation patterns, and thematic developments in this field. The bibliographic data were analyzed using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. A total of 383 publications were included in the final analysis, involving 1,743 authors across 241 journals, with an annual growth rate of 9.35% and a mean of 12.66 citations per document. India was the most productive country, accounting for 31.59% of publications. Six interconnected thematic clusters were identified, encompassing diabetes management and Ramadan fasting, cardiometabolic and lifestyle factors, self-management and psychosocial support, religion and spirituality and diabetes-related outcomes, psychosocial and behavioral determinants, and spiritual well-being and holistic health care. Overall, the research has expanded from predominantly clinical themes toward increasingly patient-centered and spiritual-psychosocial perspectives, highlighting opportunities for interdisciplinary, culturally sensitive, and holistic approaches to patient-centered diabetes care.

articles.title: Cardiomyocyte-targeted HSP60 modulates myocardial remodeling pathways and peripheral blood mononuclear cell mitochondrial membrane potential in hypertensive diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: Arterial hypertension and diabetes mellitus frequently coexist and synergistically accelerate adverse left ventricular remodeling through mitochondrial dysfunction, sterile inflammation, and extracellular matrix disorganization. Heat shock protein 60 (HSP60) is a mitochondrial chaperone involved in proteostasis and stress adaptation, but it remains unclear whether cardiomyocyte-restricted augmentation of HSP60 can modulate myocardial remodeling and influence systemic immune-cell bioenergetics. Male spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats were studied with or without streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Animals were assigned to WKY, SHR, WKY+HSP60, SHR+HSP60, WKY + DM+HSP60, and SHR + DM+HSP60 groups. HSP60 was delivered using an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector under the cardiac troponin T promoter. Myocardial remodeling was assessed by histomorphometry and Masson's trichrome staining, myocardial signaling by immunohistochemistry and RT-qPCR, and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial membrane potential by JC-1 flow cytometry. Cardiac HSP60 delivery showed a context-dependent pattern. In hypertensive diabetic rats, this pattern included altered NLRP3 subcellular localization, modulation of mitochondrial regulatory and inflammatory-fibrotic transcripts, and increased PBMC mitochondrial membrane potential. PBMC polarization inversely correlated with myocardial fibrosis. Normotensive and single-pathology groups did not show a comparable integrated response profile. These findings indicate that cardiomyocyte-targeted HSP60 overexpression is associated with remodeling-related changes in myocardium and peripheral immune-cell bioenergetics under combined hypertensive and diabetic stress. PBMC mitochondrial membrane potential may represent a candidate peripheral indicator of myocardial state in this preclinical setting.

articles.title: Exposomic Determinants in Heart Failure Among Older Adults - Mechanistic Links, Clinical Evidence, and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart failure (HF) in older adults emerges from the interplay between biological aging and the totality of environmental and behavioural exposures conceptualized as the exposome. Traditional cardiovascular risk factors and intrinsic cardiac pathology only partially explain HF burden, as chronic exposures to air pollution, traffic noise, temperature extremes, toxic metals and chemicals, artificial light at night, and adverse social environments, along with low greenness and walkability, substantially influence HF incidence, decompensations, and prognosis in older patients with multiple comorbidities.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recently, epidemiological studies have associated many of the exposomic factors with HF incidence and morbidity. Age‑related impairments of the myocardium and vasculature make them particularly vulnerable to external stressors. Mechanistically, aging, HF, and environmental factors converge on shared pathways including, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammaging, impaired autophagy and proteostasis, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence, dysregulated neurohormonal and circadian signalling, and fibrosis with maladaptive remodelling. Through these mechanisms exposome chronically accelerates cardiovascular aging and lowers the threshold for HF onset and progression. This review considers a shift from an organ‑centred view of HF in older adults to a systems‑level, life‑course perspective that explicitly incorporates exposomic determinants, and argues that reducing harmful exposures while promoting green space, physical activity, walkability, and healthy dietary patterns should be integral to HF prevention and management strategies in aging societies.

articles.title: Demographic and environmental factors associated with canine cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma development in Australia: a retrospective matched case-control analysis.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a common canine skin tumour that occurs more frequently in high ultraviolet (UV) environments. Despite Australia's consistently high UV exposure, large-scale epidemiological studies on canine cSCC are limited. This study investigates the frequency of canine cSCC in Australia, its geographic patterns relative to UV index, and its association with animal-level risk factors. A matched case-control study was conducted using records from the VetCompass database from 1st January 2014 to 31st December 2023. In total, 295 histopathologically confirmed cSCC cases and 1,180 matched controls were included. Frequency statistics of cSCC and animal-level risk factors associated with cSCC were analysed and spatial patterns were mapped. The highest proportions of cases were recorded in Queensland (39.7%) and New South Wales (39.3%), with increased frequency along coastal areas of both states. cSCC cases occurred most frequently on body regions caudal to the thorax (54.9%), in senior dogs (58.6%), in desexed males (45.1%), and in dogs with white mixed coat colour (43.7%). In the final multivariable model, senior (seven to 11 years old) and geriatric (12 + years old) dogs had significantly higher odds of cSCC than mature (two to six years old) dogs (odds ratio = 7.4 and 4.8, respectively; p ≤ 0.001). Risk was also markedly elevated in Dalmatians, bulldogs, Staffordshire terriers, and schnauzers compared with mixed breeds. Dogs with white or white mixed coats had higher odds of cSCC than dark-coated dogs (p ≤ 0.001). cSCC demonstrated anatomical and geographic patterns consistent with chronic UV exposure, with age, breed, and coat pigmentation emerging as risk factors.

articles.title: Trunk Acceleration and Lower-limb Kinematics after Cerebellar Stroke: Associations with Walking Speed and Clinical Ataxia Severity.
articles.abstract: The relationship between gait characteristics and clinical ataxia severity, after accounting for walking speed, remains insufficiently characterized following cerebellar stroke. We examined direction-specific trunk acceleration and lower-limb kinematics during comfortable walking. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 55 patients with subacute cerebellar stroke and 56 healthy controls. Inertial measurements quantified lower-limb kinematics, trunk acceleration root mean square (RMS; without speed normalization), and sample entropy (SampEn). Analyses included group-by-speed models, speed-matched one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping, and exploratory patient-only, speed-adjusted regressions and partial Spearman correlations with the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA). Patients walked more slowly, with lower anteroposterior and mediolateral RMS but higher anteroposterior and vertical SampEn. After speed adjustment, each five-point higher SARA score was associated with smaller peak limb flexion (- 1.01°; 95% confidence interval, - 1.99 to - 0.02) and less-negative extension (+ 1.21°; 0.08 to 2.34), both with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P = 0.045. None of the six full-cohort group-by-speed interactions met the adjusted significance criterion. In speed-matched comparisons (11 per group), significant waveform differences were confined to limb angles near the beginning and end of the gait cycle. In speed-adjusted rank analyses, vertical RMS correlated with SARA (partial ρ = 0.471) and limb angles, but the original-scale linear SARA coefficient remained uncertain. Vertical SampEn showed no clear association with SARA or limb kinematics. Higher ataxia severity was associated with smaller whole-limb excursions in speed-adjusted models. These exploratory findings support interpreting trunk acceleration magnitude and regularity alongside whole-limb movement and clinical severity.

articles.title: Diuretic therapy at the heart-kidney interface: from acute decongestion to long-term de-escalation in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Loop diuretics remain the cornerstone of decongestion in acute heart failure, yet their use in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is obscured by two competing errors: undertreating congestion because serum creatinine rises, and continuing or escalating diuretics after euvolaemia. This narrative review integrates established evidence and contemporary guidance into a phase-based cardiorenal decision framework. Congestion is framed as a continuum generated by sodium retention, redistribution of stressed blood volume, vascular and ventricular compliance, right-sided pressure, and renal sodium avidity-not as a binary distinction between pressure and volume overload. During acute decompensation, intravenous loop diuretics remain first-line therapy; early urine output and spot urinary sodium can identify inadequate response and support protocolized escalation. Acetazolamide or a thiazide-type diuretic can improve decongestion when loop response is insufficient, although renal and electrolyte surveillance is essential. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors should be initiated for disease modification after stabilization, but their context-dependent natriuretic effect does not replace loop diuretics in marked congestion. A creatinine rise during effective decongestion should be interpreted with residual congestion, haemodynamics, urine output, electrolytes, and evidence of kidney injury rather than through a universal threshold. After stabilization, implementation of foundational HFrEF therapy and reassessment of the minimum effective loop dose become priorities. Studies suggest that dose reduction or withdrawal is feasible in stable, euvolaemic patients, but event-powered evidence and validated outpatient biomarkers are lacking. Diuretics and disease-modifying therapy therefore have complementary, time-dependent roles: remove sodium when congestion is present, protect the kidney while recognizing hypoperfusion and intrinsic kidney injury, and de-escalate only after euvolaemia.

articles.title: 2026 International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines - key messages.
Sex differences in the association of late-life blood pressure decline with postmortem brain vessel pathology.
articles.abstract: Although hypertension is the leading modifiable risk factor for cerebrovascular disease, less is known about the relation of late-life change in blood pressure (BP) and cerebrovascular pathology beyond brain infarcts. Our previous work found sex-specific associations between declining systolic BP (SBP) and cognitive decline in late-life, suggesting that cerebrovascular pathology may be an upstream contributor to these sex differences. However, postmortem studies have not examined whether BP change differentially relates to vascular brain pathology in men and women, despite well-established sex differences in BP trajectories and cerebrovascular pathology. We examined associations between change in late-life BP and postmortem cerebrovascular (arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy) pathology from 2033 community-dwelling older adults (mean baseline age = 79.7 [SD = 7.1] years; 69% women) from four longitudinal cohort studies with brain autopsy (mean age-at-death = 89.8 [6.6] years). Person-specific late-life BP slopes estimated from annual clinical evaluations over an average of 9.1 [5.7] years were entered in ordinal regressions adjusted for age-at-death, sex, antihypertensive medication use, and BP slope × sex, age-at-death × sex, and BP slope × age-at-death interactions. Faster SBP decline was associated with greater severity of arteriolosclerosis (OR = 1.24, 95%CI 1.08-1.42) and atherosclerosis (OR = 1.41, 95%CI 1.22-1.63). A sex × SBP slope interaction (p = 0.01) revealed a stronger association of SBP decline with arteriolosclerosis severity in women than men. This longitudinal, clinical-pathologic study of older decedents showed sex differences in the association of declining SBP in late-life with severity of arteriolosclerosis, extending prior associations with cognitive decline to cerebrovascular pathology, and suggests potential for longitudinal BP monitoring for precision medicine approaches in cerebrovascular disease risk stratification.

articles.title: Role of suction ureteral access sheath in secondary flexible ureteroscopy for post-percutaneous nephrolithotomy residual stones: a single-center experience.
articles.abstract: Residual fragments persist in 15-30% of percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) cases and frequently lodge in anatomically unfavorable calyces, rendering shock wave lithotripsy less effective. This retrospective single-center study evaluated flexible suction ureteral access sheath-assisted retrograde intrarenal surgery (FANS-RIRS) as salvage therapy for post-PCNL residual stones. Between January 2020 and December 2025, 181 patients who underwent single-tract PCNL and subsequent RIRS within 3 months were enrolled (FANS, n = 103; conventional RIRS, n = 78). The FANS cohort presented with significantly poorer baseline renal function. After multiple imputation and multivariable adjustment for renal functional imbalances, FANS remained directionally associated with improved immediate stone clearance (fully adjusted OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.49-3.21). Non-inferiority analysis confirmed that FANS was statistically non-inferior for immediate stone clearance (risk difference + 5.7%, 95% CI - 7.6% to 18.5%). The one-month stone-free rate assessment was limited by low follow-up compliance (35.9%) and insufficient statistical power. The secondary procedure rate was directionally lower with FANS (5.9% vs. 11.5%). Operative time was longer in the FANS group (83 vs. 70 min, P = 0.015), but safety profiles were comparable. These findings suggest that FANS-RIRS is a viable salvage alternative for post-PCNL residual stones, particularly in higher-risk patients with poorer baseline renal function.

articles.title: Serum Netrin-1 and ultrasonographic hepatic steatosis severity in obese children and adolescents with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a preliminary study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a frequent hepatic complication of pediatric obesity, yet non-invasive circulating biomarkers associated with ultrasonographic steatosis severity remain limited. Netrin-1 is an immunometabolic regulator implicated in obesity-related inflammation and lipid metabolism, but prospective pediatric data in MASLD are scarce. In this preliminary prospective case-control study, 44 children and adolescents with obesity-related MASLD and 44 age- and sex-matched healthy controls with normal BMI were enrolled. Hepatic steatosis was assessed by ultrasonography, and serum Netrin-1 concentrations were measured by ELISA. Associations with ultrasonographic steatosis grade were evaluated using regression analyses, and discriminatory performance for moderate-to-severe ultrasonographic steatosis, defined as grades 2-3, was explored by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Serum Netrin-1 concentrations were significantly higher in children and adolescents with obesity-related MASLD than in healthy controls with normal BMI (633.9 vs 302.0 pg/mL; p < 0.001). Within the MASLD group, Netrin-1 concentrations were higher in participants with grade 2-3 steatosis than in those with grade 1 steatosis (828.9 vs 594.7 pg/mL; p < 0.001). Netrin-1 correlated positively with alanine aminotransferase (ρ = 0.669; p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance for moderate-to-severe ultrasonographic steatosis (AUC 0.827; 95% CI 0.699-0.955).

CONCLUSION: These preliminary findings suggest that serum Netrin-1 may represent an exploratory complementary biomarker candidate associated with ultrasonographic steatosis severity in pediatric MASLD. Larger multicenter studies including children and adolescents with obesity but without steatosis, together with quantitative imaging-based assessment, are required to validate these associations and determine the incremental clinical value of serum Netrin-1.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric MASLD lacks validated non-invasive circulating biomarkers for assessing hepatic steatosis severity. • Netrin-1 is an immunometabolic mediator implicated in obesity-related inflammation and lipid metabolism, but pediatric data in MASLD are scarce.

WHAT IS NEW: • In this preliminary prospective case-control study, serum Netrin-1 concentrations were higher in children and adolescents with obesity-related MASLD and were higher in those with grade 2-3 ultrasonographic steatosis than in those with grade 1 steatosis. • Serum Netrin-1 showed good exploratory discriminatory performance for moderate-to-severe ultrasonographic steatosis, suggesting that it may represent a complementary biomarker candidate requiring validation in larger independent pediatric cohorts.

articles.title: Multifactorial biomarker profiles in fatigued and non-fatigued post-COVID-19 patients: insights from a one-year follow-up.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare blood biomarkers across SARS-CoV-2 fatigue, non-fatigue, and control groups; assessed longitudinal biomarker changes; and identified genetic associations and biomarkers linked to post-COVID-19 fatigue.

METHODS: This longitudinal observational study followed individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection over a one-year period, stratifying them into fatigue (n = 27) and non-fatigue (n = 13) groups based on the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS). These groups were cross-sectionally compared with a non-infected control cohort (n = 27). Blood samples were collected at four time points to assess cytokines, hematological and biochemical markers, inflammatory indices, and matrix metalloproteinases. Selected functional polymorphisms were genotyped using PCR-RFLP. Group comparisons were conducted using generalized estimating equations, and genetic associations were evaluated using odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: At baseline, fatigued post-COVID participants had higher IL-6 (2.70 vs. 1.68 pg/mL, p < 0.001), IL-8 (6.09 vs. 3.68 pg/mL, p = 0.024), and hs-CRP (6.61 vs. 1.06 mg/L, p < 0.001) than controls. Across follow-up, the fatigued group showed higher IL-6 (mean difference [MD] 1.27 pg/mL, p = 0.009), IL-8 (MD 1.98 pg/mL, p = 0.017), and hs-CRP (MD 4.16 mg/L, p < 0.001) than the non-fatigued group. In exploratory genotype analyses, fatigue was associated with COMT rs4680 (OR 13.85, 95% CI 2.74-69.91), NR3C1 rs41423247 (OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.04-13.69), and MMP9 rs3918242 (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.06-0.67). Hs-CRP was significantly associated with FSS score (B = 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.21; p = 0.014).

CONCLUSION: Post-COVID fatigue was associated with persistent inflammation and genetic variation, supporting a multifactorial biological basis and highlighting hs-CRP as a potential marker requiring further validation.

articles.title: Long-term cost-effectiveness of CKD screening in middle-aged adults.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in Finland and frequently remains undiagnosed until advanced stages. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) slow CKD progression and reduce cardio-renal events when used in addition to Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System inhibitor (RAASi) treatment. We hypothesized that a one-time CKD screening program using measurements of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for identified CKD, would be cost-effective in Finland.

METHODS: We developed a cohort-based Markov model to simulate lifetime CKD progression in a Finnish cohort aged 55 years under two strategies: (1) current practice (no screening) and (2) one-time screening with follow-up and SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for screen-positive CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² and/or UACR ≥3 mg/mmol; confirmed on a repeat sample after ≥ 3 months to establish chronicity). All CKD stages (G1-G5, dialysis, transplant, and death) were included in the model, and screening could detect CKD at any stage, although the incremental detection was concentrated in earlier, previously undiagnosed stages (G1-G3). Outcomes included discounted costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), life years, and clinical outcomes (acute kidney function decline, heart-failure hospital days, dialysis and transplant patient-years, and deaths). Results are reported as means with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Screening increased discounted lifetime costs per person by €907 (95% CI €334-2 553) and QALYs by 0.14 (95% CI 0.07-0.31), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €6 478/QALY. Screening increased life years by 0.30. Screening reduced acute kidney function decline (0.88 vs 0.90 events/person), heart-failure hospital days (6.47 vs 6.69 days/person), dialysis exposure (0.29 vs 0.32 patient-years/person) and transplant exposure (0.13 vs 0.14 patient-years/person).

CONCLUSIONS: In Finns aged 55 years, one-time CKD screening with eGFR/UACR followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment improves long-term outcomes and is likely cost-effective.

articles.title: Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification is one of the complications related to chronic kidney disease, and there are correlations between vascular calcification and oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis. This study examined whether Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction (JQZYD) attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells and evaluated the contribution of NRF2-associated antioxidant signalling. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells were exposed to high-phosphate conditions and treated with JQZYD. Calcification was assessed by Alizarin Red S staining, calcium content, alkaline phosphatase activity, and osteogenic markers. Ferroptosis-associated changes were evaluated by BODIPY 581/591 C11 oxidation, intracellular Fe2⁺, glutathione, glutathione peroxidase activity, and GPX4/SLC7A11 expression. NRF2 activation was assessed by immunofluorescence and protein analysis. Ferrostatin-1, RSL3, and NFE2L2 silencing were used for mechanistic evaluation. Inflammatory mediators and conditioned-medium effects were also examined. JQZYD reduced high-phosphate-induced mineral deposition, osteogenic marker expression, lipid peroxidation, Fe2⁺ accumulation, and inflammatory responses. These changes were accompanied by increased glutathione peroxidase activity, greater NRF2 nuclear accumulation, higher GPX4 and SLC7A11 transcript abundance, and increased NRF2 and GPX4 protein abundance. Ferrostatin-1 reproduced several protective effects of JQZYD. RSL3 and NFE2L2 silencing partially attenuated JQZYD-associated protection, supporting contributions of GPX4-related lipid peroxide regulation and NRF2-associated signalling without establishing direct NRF2 regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. Conditioned medium from JQZYD-treated donor cells induced weaker inflammatory and calcific responses in recipient HASMCs, although the responsible mediators and potential contribution of residual treatment components remained unresolved. JQZYD attenuated high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes and accompanying oxidative and inflammatory responses in cultured HASMCs. NFE2L2 silencing supports NRF2 involvement without establishing direct regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. These findings are restricted to a cellular model and do not establish prevention of vascular calcification or therapeutic efficacy in CKD. Validation in CKD-relevant animal models and more physiologically complex vascular systems is required.

articles.title: Bispecific T-cell engagers beyond hematology: Expanding uses in solid tumors.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo review the mechanism of action, clinical efficacy, safety considerations and future development of bispecific T-cell engagers (BTCEs) in solid tumors.Data sourcesA literature search was conducted using PubMed for clinical trials leading to FDA approvals and major oncology conference proceedings through February 2026. Major ongoing clinical trials were identified through a search of clinicaltrials.gov. Search terms included "bispecific T-cell engager," "BiTE," "solid tumors," "tarlatamab," and "tebentafusp." Prescribing information was also evaluated.Data summaryBTCEs are antibodies designed to redirect cytotoxic T-cells toward tumor cells through binding of CD3 and tumor-associated antigens. FDA approvals of tebentafusp for HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma and tarlatamab for extensive stage small cell lung cancer have established utility of BTCE therapy in solid malignancies, with improved outcomes over conventional chemotherapy and immunotherapy. BTCEs have unique toxicities, such as cytokine release syndrome, that must be monitored and treated appropriately. Ongoing investigations are evaluating novel targets, optimized molecular constructs to overcome development challenges, including toxicity and tumor microenvironment barriers, as well as combination treatment strategies to improve the efficacy of BTCEs in solid tumors.ConclusionsTebentafusp and tarlatamab have established proof of concept for BTCE therapy in solid tumors, bridging the gap from hematologic malignancies. This class of therapy represents a promising platform for expanding applications across tumor types. Continued advances in target selection and strategies to overcome the tumor microenvironment and T-cell evasion barriers are expected to further expand the role of BTCEs in solid tumors.

articles.title: Silent Cardiac Progression in a Woman With Fabry Disease Despite Normal Baseline CMR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fabry disease in women may progress silently, and normal baseline cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) does not exclude subsequent cardiac involvement.

CASE SUMMARY: A 39-year-old woman with genetically confirmed Fabry disease and no prior disease-specific therapy had normal biomarkers, renal function, echocardiography, and CMR in 2022. In 2025, she developed acroparesthesias, reduced sweating, tinnitus, and constipation. Echocardiography showed increased left ventricular wall thickness. Follow-up CMR demonstrated preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, basal septal thickening to 14 mm, low native T1 (874 ms), extracellular volume of 26.9%, and new midwall late gadolinium enhancement. Enzyme replacement therapy was initiated.

DISCUSSION: Women with Fabry disease may develop structural cardiac involvement despite preserved systolic function and normal cardiac biomarkers, supporting individualized serial multimodality surveillance.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and normal cardiac biomarkers do not exclude Fabry cardiomyopathy; interval echocardiographic changes or symptoms should prompt repeat CMR and reassessment for disease-specific therapy.

articles.title: CCTA Roadmapping and OCT-Guided Multilesion PCI in Situs Inversus Dextrocardia.
articles.abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 68-year-old man with Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III angina underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), which delineated mirror-image coronary anatomy and left main trifurcation, providing a preprocedural anatomical roadmap. Angiography confirmed the anticipated lesions, demonstrated the small caliber of the ramus intermedius artery, favoring a stent-sparing strategy, and revealed an additional severe distal left anterior descending artery stenosis not clearly appreciated on CCTA. Optical coherence tomography further characterized the left anterior descending artery lesions, provided calcium scoring, and guided lesion modification and stent optimization. After intervention, final angiography showed TIMI flow grade 3.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CCTA provided a preprocedural anatomical roadmap in the setting of mirror-image coronary anatomy. Angiography and optical coherence tomography subsequently refined lesion-specific treatment and percutaneous coronary intervention optimization.

articles.title: An adversarial deep neural network for identifying non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundNon-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is rapidly becoming the most prevalent liver disease worldwide. The accurate identification of NAFLD patients and understand the molecular mechanism of initiating and driving disease progression remain limited.ObjectieThis study aims to develop a robust and accurate computational model for identifying NAFLD patients using mRNA expression profiles, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms that drive disease initiation and progression.MethodsWe introduce an adversarial deep neural network (ADNN) to identify NAFLD patients based on mRNA expression profiles, which uses adversarial learning techniques to take advantage of existing mRNA expression profiles in the GEO database. We compare the ADNN model with some traditional machine learning methods, such as random forest (RF), adaptive boosting (AdaBoost).ResultsThe area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of the ADNN model is 0.982, which is much higher than the machine learning models such as RF, SVM and deep neural networks. Meanwhile, by combining the ADNN model with the DeepLIFT algorithm, we calculate the importance score of genes and find that the DeepLIFT algorithm can identify genes that don't differ at the level of mRNA, but interact with other important genes. Such as GSTM1, with the greatest importance score and has no difference between control and NAFLD, but interacts with IGF1 and MEP1B.ConclusionTherefore, the ADNN model can not only identify NAFLD patients from healthy controls, but also help us better understand the disease mechanism of NAFLD.

articles.title: Diabetes mellitus accelerates preclinical Alzheimer's disease progression by amplifying the amyloid-to-tau pathway and attenuating brain-cognition resilience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDiabetes mellitus (DM) is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its stage-dependent effects on the ATN framework remain unclear.ObjectiveTo determine whether DM differentially affects clinical progression from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus MCI to AD, how DM modulates the ATN cascade, and the optimal follow-up for detecting structural-cognitive changes.MethodsWe analyzed longitudinal data from 1638 ADNI participants (765 CN, 71 with DM; 873 MCI, 91 with DM). Clinical progression was assessed by Cox regression. Annualized slopes of ATN biomarkers and cognition were estimated. Moderation analyses tested DM × predictor interactions on A→T (amyloid→tau) and N→C (neurodegeneration→cognition) pathways with FDR correction. Piecewise linear mixed models identified the optimal knot for structural-cognitive coupling.ResultsDM increased CN-to-MCI risk (adjusted HR = 1.73, p = 0.028) but not MCI-to-AD progression (adjusted HR = 1.10, p = 0.574). In CN, DM amplified amyloid-driven tau accumulation in entorhinal cortex (A→T interaction β = 0.77, FDR p = 0.043) and attenuated the protective effect of hippocampal volume on cognition (e.g., hippocampal volume slope × DM on MMSE slope: β = -0.19, FDR p = 0.031). These effects were absent in MCI (all FDR p > 0.05). A 36-month follow-up was the optimal window for detecting robust structural-cognitive coupling in the CN cohort, independent of DM status.ConclusionsDiabetes accelerates preclinical AD by amplifying A→T and eroding structural-cognitive resilience, but does not hasten progression from established MCI to AD. A minimum 36-month observation period is recommended for early-phase prevention trials.

articles.title: Mimics and Chameleons: A Patient with Accidental Hypothermia and Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAccidental hypothermia is an unintentional drop in core temperature below 35 °C, typically resulting from exposure to cold environmental conditions. Clinical presentations may vary widely depending on the severity of hypothermia and the presence of coexisting conditions complicating diagnosis and treatment. We report a case of accidental hypothermia caused by environmental exposure and associated with cardiogenic shock from a myocardial infarction with complete heart block.Case PresentationA group of ski tourers found a 62-y-old male skier at 3000 m in severe distress with abdominal pain, shivering, and profound exhaustion. On arrival at a mountain hut, he was agitated, then became unconscious and bradycardic with a weak femoral pulse. Once advanced medical equipment reached the hut, a 12-lead electrocardiogram showed an inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with complete third-degree atrioventricular block and a ventricular escape rhythm. The first measurable axillary temperature was 32.2 °C. Consciousness progressively improved, but bradycardia persisted during rewarming. The patient was evacuated 6 h after the diagnosis of acute STEMI. He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and was successfully treated with a stent.ConclusionsThis case illustrates that hypothermia and environmental factors can complicate the diagnosis of atypical presentations of life-threatening conditions, such as STEMI, and how unexpected clinical findings not fully explained by hypothermia may indicate the presence of an underlying condition. In such situations, hypothermia staging systems should be used with caution. Early electrocardiography, awareness of cognitive biases, and the use of safe rewarming practices are essential to ensure timely diagnosis and prevent complications.

articles.title: Comparison of the efficacy of daily versus weekly vitamin D supplementation on GOLD classification in COPD patients with vitamin D deficiency: An open-label randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), characterized by irreversible airflow limitation, markedly reduces expiratory airflow. COPD patients commonly suffer from vitamin D deficiency, which is strongly associated with reduced forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) and forced vital capacity (FVC).AimThis study compared the effects of weekly versus daily vitamin D supplementation on lung function in COPD patients with low baseline vitamin D levels.MethodsIn this open-label randomized clinical trial, 49 patients with COPD and baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels below 30 ng/mL were allocated to receive either daily 4000 IU or weekly 50,000 IU vitamin D3, in addition to standard COPD treatment, for 12 weeks.SummaryAfter the intervention, serum vitamin D levels increased in both supplementation groups, while lung-function measures also increased from baseline. Although the weekly group showed numerically higher post-intervention FEV1 and FEV1 percentage values, the between-group differences were not statistically significant after adjustment for baseline age (p = 0.079 for absolute FEV1; p = 0.981 for FEV1 percentage). We observed a significant association between post-intervention vitamin D levels and post-intervention FEV1 (R2 = 0.42, p < 0.001). These findings do not demonstrate superiority of the weekly regimen over the daily regimen, and larger randomized controlled trials are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist between dosing schedules.

articles.title: Short-term effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy and low-level laser therapy on clinical outcomes and ultrasonographic tendon thickness in lateral elbow tendinopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
articles.abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the short-term effects of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) on pain, elbow function, health-related quality of life, hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic extensor tendon thickness in patients with LET.ObjectiveIn this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind trial, patients with LET were randomly assigned to either ESWT or LLLT. Both groups received the same standardized home exercise program and lateral epicondylitis brace. Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE), Short Form-36 (SF-36), hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic evaluation were assessed before and after three weeks of randomisation.ResultsAt three weeks, the ESWT group demonstrated significantly lower post-treatment pain intensity (VAS) than the LLLT group (p = 0.004). ESWT was also associated with significantly better outcomes in PRTEE pain scores (p = 0.030), ultrasonographic tendon thickness (p = 0.021), and the Role Physical (p = 0.029) and General Health (p = 0.005) domains of the SF-36. No significant between-group differences were observed in hand grip strength, PRTEE function, PRTEE total score, or the remaining SF-36 domains.ConclusionWhen used as adjuncts to a standardized exercise program and LET brace, ESWT was associated with greater short-term pain reduction and more favorable outcomes in the PRTEE pain subscale, ultrasonographic tendon thickness, and selected domains of health-related quality of life compared with LLLT. These findings suggest that ESWT may offer greater short-term pain-related benefits than LLLT when both are added to exercise and bracing.

articles.title: The Association of Social Drivers of Health and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Discharge Delays in Children with Tracheostomy in a Single Center in Rural Minnesota.
articles.abstract: Introduction:As neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) survival improves, the number of children with tracheostomy, along with those who require home care nursing (HCN), is rising. Discharge delays (DD) are an issue, with an emotional or financial toll on children, families, and the health care system. We aimed to investigate whether social drivers of health like socioeconomic status (SES), race, sex, and medical factors such as gestational age influenced DD for children with tracheostomy.Materials and Methods:We conducted a retrospective chart review of children who underwent tracheostomy in the NICU during a 5-year period. Four authors reviewed electronic medical records for demographics, clinical information, and DD. SES was determined based on the HOUsing-based SocioEconomic Status (HOUSES) index. The Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman's correlation were used to assess the association between DD in days and independent variables. In addition, the cohort was divided into 2 groups based on DD ≥30 days to explore factors associated with it descriptively.Results:Sixteen children were included in the study (10 female, 6 male). Ten children were identified as White, and 3 as Black. Three children were not White or Black. Only one child did not experience DD. Median DD was 15 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 13-24; range 0-49). Three children had clinically significant DD (>30 days). The most common cause of DD was waiting for HCN (10/16, 63%, P = 0.065). Race (White versus Black versus other) was associated with DD (P = 0.045). Female sex (P = 0.039) was associated with significant DD, while birthweight (P = 0.19) and HOUSES index (P = 0.49) were not.Conclusion:DD is a common phenomenon in children with tracheostomy in the NICU, and lack of HCN is the major factor. Race and sex may play a role in DD. HCN shortages and other causes of DD should be further studied and addressed.

articles.title: RNA viruses as drivers of rapid diatom succession within a single bloom event.
articles.abstract: Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved. Here, using quantitative metatranscriptomics, we tracked temporal patterns of diatoms and associated viruses at near-daily resolution during the spring bloom in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea. We captured distinct phases and rapid restructuring within both the diatom community and cell-associated virosphere. Diatom transcriptional profiling indicated activation of stress and death pathways prior to taxon-specific demise. RNA viruses emerged as dominant players within the bloom, with fluctuations of putative diatom-infecting RNA viruses across intracellular and extracellular fractions revealing sequential waves of active virus infection that were consistent with virus-mediated diatom mortality. Correlation and codon usage analyses further implicated specific diatom taxa as putative hosts for the identified RNA viruses. Rather than a uniform 'boom and bust', the spring diatom bloom comprised a mosaic of overlapping successional waves of diatom and viral taxa unfolding on daily timescales. These findings support RNA viruses as drivers of diatom turnover, advancing our understanding of how viruses temporally structure diverse diatom assemblages and the biogeochemical trajectory of diatom blooms in marine systems.

articles.title: Endogenous panophthalmitis in a patient with diabetic kidney disease on haemodialysis: A vision-threatening manifestation of systemic infection.
articles.abstract: Endogenous endophthalmitis is a rare but devastating complication of haematogenous infection, with a higher risk in patients with diabetes mellitus and end-stage kidney disease receiving maintenance haemodialysis (MHD). We report a 40-year old man with diabetic kidney disease on MHD through a tunnelled dialysis catheter who presented with acute painful visual loss and was diagnosed with endogenous panophthalmitis. Blood, catheter blood and catheter-tip cultures grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, confirming a catheter-related bloodstream infection with ocular metastatic spread. Despite prompt intravitreal, systemic and topical antimicrobial therapy and removal of the infected catheter, the affected eye progressed to phthisis bulbi with permanent blindness. This case highlights the potential for vascular access-related bacteraemia to cause catastrophic ocular infection in patients receiving haemodialysis. Early recognition of endogenous endophthalmitis, prompt source control and coordinated ophthalmological, nephrological, and infectious disease management are essential to optimise outcomes.

articles.title: Dentists' Temporomandibular Disorder-Related Education, Knowledge, Attitudes and Behavior: How Do Personal and Educational Experiences Matter?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) affect 5%-12% of US adults. The objectives were to assess dentists' TMD-related education, knowledge, attitudes, and behavior and to explore whether TMD-related experiences were associated with these constructs.

METHODS: A total of 296 dentists responded to a survey. Descriptive statistics provided an overview of the results, and Pearson correlation coefficients described the relationships between dentists' TMD experiences, knowledge, attitudes, and behavior.

RESULTS: Only 17.2% were satisfied with classroom-based and 10.1% with clinic-based TMD-related education; 29.6% described their classroom-based and 17.8% their clinic-based education about TMD diagnosis positively; 37.7% were confident in their TMD-related knowledge, but 94.1% recognized their limitations when managing TMD. The majority agreed that TMD is a physical/anatomical problem (87.3%), behavioral problem (74.3%), psychosocial problem (71.6%), and that stress plays a role for TMD (93.1%). Most dentists had positive attitudes toward diagnosing TMD (82.8%), felt responsible for treating TMD (63.1%), regularly saw patients with TMD (58.2%), and screened patients for TMD (67%). Concerning treatments utilized, 63.3% used occlusal appliances, while only 23.6% prescribed medications. 43% had experienced TMD themselves. The more persons they knew with TMD, the more treatment-related knowledge they reported (r = 0.26; p < 0.001), the more positive were their attitudes (r = 0.16; p < 0.01), the more comfortable they were treating TMD (r = 0.25; p < 0.001), and the more they cared for patients with TMD (r = 0.34; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: TMD-related dental and continuing education should reconsider classroom- and clinic-based TMD training. Personal TMD experiences correlate with more positive attitudes and behavior. This should alert dental educators to the importance of engaging students and dentists in hands-on education.

articles.title: A critical review of the role of pharmacists in providing care to Indigenous peoples with diabetes mellitus.
articles.journal: The International journal of pharmacy practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indigenous peoples experience disproportionately higher rates of diabetes mellitus (DM) due to social, historical, and cultural factors. Pharmacists play important roles in DM care, but their involvement in caring for Indigenous peoples with DM is not well documented. This critical review aimed to describe pharmacists' involvement by systematically identifying the roles, barriers, facilitators, interventions, and pharmacists' vision for improving diabetes care for Indigenous peoples.

METHODS: A systematic search utilizing Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines was conducted across seven scientific literature databases and grey literature from inception to May 2026, using keywords related to pharmacists, diabetes, and Indigenous peoples. Data analysis was guided by the Two-Eyed Seeing Framework and the Framework for Diabetes in Canada.

RESULTS: Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. The key roles of pharmacists identified included screening, patient education, medication management, and supporting adherence. Barriers to pharmacists' service delivery included mistrust, lack of knowledge of Indigenous languages, and financial issues related to management. Facilitators included family engagement, motivational interviewing, home delivery for prescriptions, and customized information material in the Indigenous language. Recommendations identified to enhance pharmacists' delivery of services included cultural competency, financial support, and increased collaboration with Indigenous peoples and their families.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacists provide care for Indigenous peoples living with diabetes through medication management, education, and counselling. Various facilitators and barriers to the provision of these services were identified, which can be learned from to enhance future care. Further research is required to determine best practices to provide the best possible care in a culturally appropriate manner.

articles.title: Epigenetic aging in people with HIV across the life course: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
articles.abstract: Epigenetic aging algorithms are emerging tools for understanding the biological effects of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A growing body of literature has applied DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks in people living with HIV (PWH) across the life course, examining epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) in relation to HIV infection, antiretroviral therapy (ART), comorbidities, and clinical biomarkers (e.g., viral load, CD4 T-cell counts). This systematic review (Prospero: CRD420251126874) summarizes and synthesizes the current evidence on epigenetic aging in PWH across the life course and identifies critical knowledge gaps for future research. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Medline through June 26, 2026. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and assessed studies for risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We created a narrative synthesis of results and performed a random-effects meta-analysis of HorvathAge EAA. Fifty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. More than half (n = 33) examined EAA in PWH compared to an uninfected control population. We identified heterogeneity in study populations and design, biospecimens profiled, platforms used for DNA methylation analysis, and epigenetic clocks employed. Only 6 studies included participants younger than 18 years and no studies focused exclusively on individuals over 65 years. Only 10 studies examined longitudinal changes in EAA. Thirty-seven papers evaluated associations between EAA and comorbidities. A meta-analysis of HorvathAge EAA across 14 studies found a mean difference of 3.41 years (95%CI 2.22, 4.60) in PWH relative to controls. Current evidence supports accelerated EAA among PWH but highlights substantial methodological heterogeneity and important knowledge gaps. Longitudinal studies of EAA in PWH are needed in populations under 18 and over 65, to clarify the effects of ART, clinical biomarkers, and age-related comorbidities, and determine the clinical utility of epigenetic aging biomarkers.

articles.title: Early versus late venous thromboembolism in patients with newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurs in 20-30% and 9.2% of patients with glioblastoma and grade 3 IDH mutant (IDHmut) gliomas respectively, with highest risk during the first months post-surgery. We sought to identify risk factors for early versus late VTE in high-grade gliomas and evaluated the recently proposed 'GliomaPredictVTE' tool.

METHODS: We included 894 patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and grade 3-4 IDHmut gliomas from 2010-2023. Competing-risk analysis estimated VTE cumulative incidence (CumInc), segmented linear regression model identified the change-point between early versus late VTE, and competing-risk regression model identified significant risk factors. GliomaPredictVTE-predicted 6- and 12-month VTE risks were compared to observed CumInc.

RESULTS: The estimated 6- and 12-month VTE CumInc was 21.5% and 26.4%, respectively for IDHwt glioblastoma versus 6.3% and 8.3%, respectively for IDHmut gliomas. The VTE CumInc increased rapidly during the first 6 months post-surgery, followed by a more gradual rise thereafter, with a change-point around 6 months. On multivariable analyses, 'Early VTE' (within 6 months post-surgery) was significantly associated with older age, limb weakness, ambulation dependence, and radiotherapy alone; 'Late VTE' (6 months to 5 years) with older age and smoking. GliomaPredictVTE substantially underestimated VTE incidence in our population, with a mean predicted 6- and 12-month risks of 11.0% and 17.4%, versus observed CumInc of 19.9% (p < 0.001) and 23% (p = 0.008), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Distinct risk profiles between early and late VTE support prospective studies of primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients, particularly in the first 6 months post-surgery. GliomaPredictVTE significantly underestimates VTE incidence in this population.

articles.title: The mediating role of sleep blood pressure in the association between B-type natriuretic peptide and cardiovascular events: The Nagahama Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a risk marker for not only heart failure but also cardiovascular diseases (CVD). This study investigated the possible mediating role of sleep blood pressure (BP) in the association between BNP and CVD events.

METHODS: Data for 5,751 participants were obtained from the Nagahama Study, a longitudinal cohort study of the general Japanese population. Circulating BNP levels were determined from blood specimens. BP was measured at home in the morning and evening, and three times per night during sleep using a timer-equipped cuff-oscillometric device.

RESULTS: During the mean follow-up period of 9.4 years (54,350 person-years), 169 CVD cases were observed (Incidence rate: 31.1 per 10,000 person-year, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 26.7, 36.2). BNP levels ≥40 pg/mL were independently associated with CVD. The sleep BP-adjusted hazard ratio of high BNP for CVD was 1.80 (95% CI: 1.18, 2.74), while the awake home BP-adjusted hazard ratio was 1.92 (95% CI: 1.26, 2.91). Causal mediation analysis indicated a greater mediation rate of sleep SBP (14.3%, 95% CI: -2.8, 31.3) than awake home SBP (5.8%, 95% CI; -2.6, 14.2) in the association between BNP and CVD incidence. Factors associated with log-normalized BNP levels were age, sex, body mass index, sleep SBP, and nocturnal urination frequency.

CONCLUSION: Prognostic significance of BNP for CVD events was partially mediated by BP particularly BP during sleep.

articles.title: Hypervirulent Listeria isolated from a wild rabbit in Canada.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
articles.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is the causative agent of listeriosis, a major foodborne disease with a 30% mortality rate in humans. Although L. monocytogenes can infect animals, whether wildlife can serve as a reservoir remains understudied, especially in Canada. Here, we characterized an L. monocytogenes strain (W0463-24) extracted from a wild cottontail rabbit (Sylvilagus floridanus) submitted to the Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative at the University of Guelph. The rabbit had severe swelling of the head, multiple scabs around the muzzle and eyes, and was diagnosed with disseminated lymphoma, multifocal necrotizing hepatitis with gram-positive bacteria, and nematodosis. Liver and spleen were PCR-negative for Francisella tularensis, and liver was 4+ for L. monocytogenes on bacterial culture. Whole-genome analysis characterized isolate W0463-24 as sequence type 1 (ST1), clonal complex 1 (CC1), and lineage I. Multiple virulence and stress response genes were identified in silico, including the Listeria pathogenicity island 3 (LIPI-3). Invasion of human colon adenocarcinoma (Caco-2) cells in vitro was significantly greater with W0463-24 compared with wild-type strain 10403S. We found that this ST1, CC1, lineage I wildlife isolate has high pathogenic potential, emphasizing wildlife both as potential reservoirs and as populations vulnerable to L. monocytogenes infection.

articles.title: Improving rates of HIV testing in emergency departments in a health system using clinical decision support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a public health priority. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) recommends comprehensive screening for STIs and HIV, defined as testing for gonorrhoea/chlamydia (GC-CT), syphilis and HIV in persons undergoing STI evaluation. Many patients utilize emergency departments (EDs) for STI evaluation; however, HIV co-testing rates remain low. Electronic Health Record (EHR)-based clinical decision support (CDS) can help providers implement best practices. We assessed the impact of two CDS tools on HIV co-testing rates with GC-CT in freestanding EDs (FSEDs) of a statewide health system.

METHODS: CDS Interventions included Comprehensive STI Order Set made available 1/2024 and a Comprehensive STI Pathway made available 1/2025. We included FSED encounters for adult patients with GC-CT NAAT 1/1/2022-11/21/2025 and measured HIV co-testing rates. Process measures included overall CDS utilization by FSED type (urban Denver sites, Metro; outlying Colorado sites, Outlying; aggregated sites, All Sites). Analysis included statistical process control charts and descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: GC-CT testing occurred in 11 087 patient encounters between 1/1/2022 and 11/21/2025. HIV co-testing rates averaged 2.6% 2 years before the intervention (2022-2023). After the first intervention (2024), HIV co-testing rose to 13.1%, with a positive shift in SPC charts across All Sites, Metro and Outlying. After the second intervention (2025), HIV co-testing rose to 18.3%, with greater impacts at Metro FSEDs; positive shifts in SPC charts were seen across All Sites and Metro but not Outlying EDs.

CONCLUSIONS: EHR-based CDS was effective for increasing HIV co-testing in freestanding EDs.

articles.title: Beyond Conventional VV-ECMO: The Role of Veno-Pulmonary Support in Trauma-Associated ARDS With Right Ventricular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) after trauma can require extracorporeal support, however, the usual approach to ARDS is often complicated by associated injuries. Prone positioning may be limited by unstable fractures or other injuries, while traumatic intracranial hemorrhage and recent bleeding can make systemic anticoagulation difficult. At the same time, severe ARDS can substantially increase right ventricular afterload and lead to right ventricular dysfunction. Conventional venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) improves gas exchange and may reduce right ventricular afterload indirectly, but it still relies on native right ventricular forward flow. Veno-pulmonary (V-P) ECMO offers an alternative by combining extracorporeal gas exchange with direct right ventricular unloading. Most published experience, however, has involved conversion to V-P support after refractory right ventricular failure has already developed. This review examines the role of V-P ECMO in severe trauma-associated ARDS, focusing on right ventricular dysfunction, selection of the initial extracorporeal configuration, and anticoagulation when traumatic bleeding limits standard management. We also describe an illustrative multiply injured patient with severe ARDS, evolving right ventricular dysfunction, and traumatic subdural hemorrhage who received V-P ECMO as the initial configuration without systemic anticoagulation. Current evidence supports the feasibility of V-P ECMO but does not define when earlier direct right ventricular support is warranted. Trauma adds important constraints that make configuration and anticoagulation decisions particularly complex and deserving of further study.

articles.title: Characterization and analysis of osseous changes in murine jaws induced by chronic metabolic acidosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic metabolic acidosis (MA) is a growing clinical concern linked to the rising prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD). While MA is known to cause systemic bone loss, its specific effects on craniofacial tissues and the role of sexual dimorphism remain under-investigated.

METHODS: Male and female mice were subjected to a chronic acid challenge to model clinical MA. Raman spectroscopy and MicroCT were employed to evaluate the structural and compositional integrity of the maxilla and mandible, focusing on mineral crystallinity, carbonate content, and bone volume fraction.

RESULTS: Site-specific analysis revealed the maxilla to be significantly more vulnerable to acid perturbation than the mandible. This compositional shift is consistent with physicochemical mineral dissolution and may reflect alterations in bone remodeling. In contrast, the mandible's denser, more crystalline structure provided relative resilience to acid-induced changes. Furthermore, a significant sexual dimorphism was observed. Females demonstrated greater compositional sensitivity and a more pronounced decrease in mineral:matrix ratio compared to males.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the limitations of applying long-bone models to the craniofacial complex and underscore the need for clinical monitoring of oral health in patients with chronic metabolic disturbances.

articles.title: Toxin-responsive metal-organic framework nanocarriers for precision delivery of antimicrobial peptides against drug-resistant infections.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance has emerged as a major global healthcare challenge owing to the rapid rise in multidrug-resistant bacterial infections and the declining effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. Antimicrobial peptides have gained considerable attention as alternative therapeutic agents because of their broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, membrane-targeting mechanisms, immunomodulatory functions, and reduced susceptibility to resistance development. The clinical translation of antimicrobial peptides is limited by enzymatic degradation, poor stability, rapid clearance, systemic toxicity, and inefficient infection site targeting. In this context, metal-organic frameworks have emerged as effective nanocarriers for precision antimicrobial peptide delivery owing to their tunable porosity, high loading capacity, surface functionalization, and stimuli-responsive behavior. This review comprehensively discusses the molecular mechanisms of antimicrobial peptides, engineering strategies for metal-organic framework-based delivery systems, and toxin-responsive nanocarrier designs for selective antimicrobial therapy. Different toxin-responsive approaches, including lipid bilayer-disruptable systems, membrane-coated toxin-decoy metal-organic frameworks, phospholipase-triggered platforms, virulence-factor-amplified systems, and dual-responsive nanocarriers, are highlighted for their ability to achieve site-specific antimicrobial peptide release in pathogen-rich microenvironments. Furthermore, recent in vitro, in vivo, and preclinical studies demonstrating therapeutic efficacy against multidrug-resistant and biofilm-associated infections are reviewed. Toxin-responsive metal-organic framework nanocarriers represent an advanced precision nanomedicine strategy with considerable potential for combating drug-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Management Before Intravenous Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Rethinking Treatment Thresholds.
articles.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
articles.abstract: BackgroundElevated blood pressure (BP) is common after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but it is unclear if it should be lowered. Lowering elevated BP may compromise the ischemic brain, while the time taken to lower BP may delay or even exclude patients from receiving intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).AimTo review the rationale, guideline recommendations, and clinical evidence informing pre-IVT BP management, with a specific focus on patients presenting with a BP above the current guideline thresholds (BP ≥185/110 mmHg).Summary of reviewCerebral autoregulation is impaired in AIS, both in the core and penumbra, creating vulnerability to harm from both excessive hypertension and BP reduction. Major trials of early or intensive BP-lowering in AIS (INTERACT4, MR-ASAP, and RIGHT-2) have either shown neutral or harmful effects with BP reduction. In the TRUTH study, a cluster-based observational comparison, centers that actively treated elevated BP before IVT achieved higher IVT rates but no better 90-day functional outcome, with a non-significant trend toward worse outcomes in the active-treatment arm. No randomized trial has helped define the optimal systolic BP target, speed of reduction, preferred antihypertensive agent, or balance of risks vs. benefits of BP reduction. prior to IVT.ConclusionsCurrent practice on BP treatment prior to IVT is guided by historical thresholds and expert consensus rather than robust evidence. Major gaps persist with respect to causal associations, individualized treatment targets, and safe BP reduction strategies. Higher quality data are needed to establish evidence-based BP management for patients presenting ≥185/110 mmHg otherwise eligible for IVT, to uniform practice towards improved patient outcomes.

articles.title: Parasympathetic dysfunction assessed by deep-breathing CVR-R is associated with early discontinuation of oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes: A multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are widely used for type 2 diabetes, gastrointestinal intolerance frequently leads to early discontinuation. Predictors of oral semaglutide discontinuation remain poorly defined, and its formulation-specific dependence on gastric conditions may influence tolerability. We examined whether the coefficient of variation of R-R intervals (CVR-R) was associated with discontinuation within 6 months.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 203 consecutive patients initiating oral semaglutide between February 2021 and December 2024 were screened, and 61 were analyzed after exclusions. The Discontinuation Group (n = 21) discontinued because of nausea and/or vomiting within 6 months, whereas the Maintenance Group (n = 40) continued for ≥ 6 months. CVR-R was assessed at rest (CVR-R_rest) and during deep breathing (CVR-R_DB). Associations with discontinuation were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression; exploratory machine learning and time-to-event analyses were performed.

RESULTS: CVR-R_DB was lower in the Discontinuation Group than in the Maintenance Group (median 1.93% vs 3.26%, P < 0.001). CVR-R_DB remained independently associated with discontinuation after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR 0.191; 95% CI 0.071-0.512; P = 0.001; AUC 0.832) and further adjustment for neuropathy stage. The AUC was numerically higher for the age- and sex-adjusted model containing CVR-R_DB than for that containing CVR-R_rest (0.832 vs 0.699; DeLong P = 0.085). An internally derived CVR-R_DB cutoff of 2.55% stratified 6-month persistence (43.3% vs 87.1%; log-rank P < 0.001), and machine learning analyses prioritized CVR-R_DB.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower CVR-R during deep breathing was associated with early oral semaglutide discontinuation due to nausea and/or vomiting. CVR-R_DB may support risk stratification at initiation.

articles.title: Pharmacist role in transforming Alzheimer's care: Anti-amyloid therapy experience at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Anti-amyloid infusion therapies are a new and complex treatment option for patients with Alzheimer's disease. Use of lecanemab or donanemab requires specific diagnostic criteria and frequent ongoing monitoring that requires in-depth coordination of care. We describe how neurology clinical pharmacists were an integral part of adoption of anti-amyloid therapy at our institution. With implementation of this service by pharmacists, we describe the impact on patient outcomes for those receiving anti-amyloid infusions and several aspects of impact on the health system as a whole that pharmacists should anticipate with these complex infusions.

SUMMARY: Neurology clinical pharmacists dedicated to infusions therapies are responsible for many aspects of use of anti-amyloid therapies, including order entry, patient counseling, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) registry submission, infusion scheduling, and coordination of magnetic resonance imaging. At our institution, the first year of anti-amyloid infusions included 58 patients starting infusions. Safety and adverse effects, including amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, were similar to those previously reported in the primary literature. The majority of patients utilized Medicare as their primary coverage for infusions, and we describe successful navigation of the unique CMS registry requirement for billing.

CONCLUSION: Adoption of anti-amyloid therapies by a health system requires unique aspects of coordination not previously encountered. Clinical pharmacists are positioned to successfully coordinate care for patients receiving anti-amyloid infusions.

articles.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.
