METHODS: In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

articles.title: Intersecting pathways of postpartum depressive symptoms and recurrent binge eating after gestational diabetes: Findings from the LINDA-Brazil cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence and correlates of recurrent binge eating (RBE) and postpartum depression (PPD), and examine their association among women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included 699 women with prior GDM who participated in the postpartum baseline assessment of the LINDA-Brazil study. RBE was defined as self-reported recurrent episodes of consuming large quantities of food within a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of lack of control during these episodes. PPD was measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), with a cutoff score ≥13. Sociodemographic, obstetric, behavioral, and nutritional characteristics were obtained by interview. Associations were examined using Poisson regression models with robust variance.

RESULTS: Among the 699 participants, 272 (38.9%) presented RBE, and 184 (26.3%) had PPD. At least one of the two outcomes was identified in 49.4% of participants, and 15.9% presented both. RBE was more prevalent among younger women and those with postpartum weight retention greater than 5 kg. PPD was associated with lower household income, current smoking, parity, weight-related factors, and poor sleep quality, whereas current breastfeeding was associated with a lower prevalence. In the primary analysis, women with RBE had a higher prevalence of PPD than women without RBE (prevalence ratio [PR], 2.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.63-2.88).

CONCLUSION: RBE and PPD were common and frequently co-occurred among women with recent GDM. Women with RBE had approximately twice the prevalence of PPD compared with those without RBE. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between these conditions.

articles.title: Perfusion index as adjunct to SNAPPE-II for early risk stratification of sepsis-dominated adverse outcomes in neonates: Exploratory prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIllness-severity scores such as the Score for Neonatal Acute Physiology with Perinatal Extension-II (SNAPPE-II) discriminate mortality well but morbidity less well. Whether serial perfusion index (PI), a continuous bedside perfusion measure, adds prognostic information beyond SNAPPE-II is unknown, particularly in late-preterm and term populations in low- and middle-income countries.MethodsIn this exploratory prospective cohort, 50 neonates admitted within 12 hours of birth to a level-3 neonatal intensive care unit and requiring arterial blood-gas analysis were enrolled consecutively. SNAPPE-II used worst first-12-h values; PI was measured at 6, 12 and 24 hours. Outcomes were death, major morbidity (sepsis, necrotising enterocolitis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia) and their composite. Given eight deaths, multivariable models were exploratory, using Firth-penalised regression. Discrimination was compared by change in area under the curve (ΔAUC; DeLong and bootstrap confidence intervals) with optimism correction. Serial PI was analysed using a random-intercept linear mixed model with time × outcome interaction.ResultsMortality was 16.0% (8/50); major morbidity, exclusively sepsis, was 44.0% (22/50). Non-survivors had higher SNAPPE-II scores (median 50.5 vs 5.0) and lower PI at all time points (p < 0.001). SNAPPE-II discriminated mortality well (AUC 0.936); adding 6-h PI did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC 0.0015, 95% CI -0.029 to 0.032). For morbidity outcomes, 6-h PI improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.006 and 0.016), but ΔAUC confidence intervals included zero. Neonates with culture-proven sepsis (n = 6) had lower 6-h PI (median 0.76 vs 1.49, p = 0.014). PI trajectories did not diverge by outcome (time × outcome p = 0.671); values remained lower in non-survivors.ConclusionsIn this selected cohort, low PI was associated with illness severity and sepsis-dominated adverse outcomes but did not demonstrably improve discrimination beyond SNAPPE-II. Unblinded ascertainment precludes excluding incorporation bias. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant testing, with prespecified thresholds, blinded ascertainment and internal validation, in adequately powered multicentre studies of culture-proven sepsis.

articles.title: The Use of Effective Persuasive Strategies in Obesity Prevention Campaigns: A Content Analysis.
articles.abstract: Obesity prevalence in the United States has risen significantly, with uneven distributions across populations. Communication can play an important role in affecting health behaviors, and persuasion literature is clear on several evidence- and theory-based strategies, including efficacy, threat, emotional tone, use of graphics when presenting statistics, and narratives. Yet, little is known about the extent to which these strategies appear in obesity prevention efforts. This study examined the prevalence of key persuasive strategies in health communication: emotional appeals, narrative strategies, statistical and graphic evidence, and efficacy cues in U.S. obesity campaign messages. We analyzed 182 print materials from 25 campaigns in 2013 and 106 print materials from 20 campaigns in 2022. Findings reveal gaps in persuasive strategy use, suggesting many campaigns fail to maximize their potential impact. While efficacy messaging was more prevalent, narrative strategy, along with emotional appeals, was barely used across observed time points. This paper calls for more theoretically grounded persuasive campaign messages to address obesity in the U.S.

articles.title: Building Healthy Temples With Less Pressure: A Faith-Based Hypertension Control Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Hypertension disproportionately affects Hispanic/Latino communities in the United States, yet culturally tailored interventions that support sustained lifestyle modification and self-management remain limited. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of Building Healthy Temples with Less Pressure (BHT-LP), a faith-based, lay leader-delivered hypertension self-management intervention implemented in Hispanic church communities. Guided by social cognitive theory, BHT-LP included a Medical Moment and a 12-session hypertension self-management program delivered by trained Church Lay Health Leaders. Forty adults with hypertension or elevated blood pressure were recruited from two Hispanic churches in San Antonio, Texas, during 2021 to 2022. Participants completed baseline and post-intervention assessments, and focus groups were conducted at program completion. Twenty-nine participants completed both assessments. Mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure decreased modestly, although the changes were not statistically significant. Hypertension self-care behaviors, dietary quality, and physical activity improved, with aerobic activity increasing by 72 min/week (p < .01). Participants with excess weight experienced significant reductions in body weight and waist circumference. Qualitative findings indicated program acceptability, high trust in lay leaders, and increased motivation to monitor blood pressure and adopt healthier behaviors. These findings support the feasibility and promise of a spiritually integrated, lay leader-facilitated intervention for hypertension control and related health behaviors in Hispanic faith communities. The program's culturally grounded approach, group support, and integration of self-monitoring tools may offer a practical strategy for advancing community-based hypertension prevention and management.

articles.title: Human T cells from resistant hypertension patients promote hypertension via tnf in humanized mice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Preclinical studies suggest a pivotal role of adaptive immunity, particularly T cells, in hypertension. However, due to the multifactorial pathogenesis, there is still no definitive evidence for a causal role of T cells in the development of hypertension in humans. We sought to determine whether T cells from patients with treatment-resistant hypertension (TRH) directly modulate blood pressure and vascular function in vivo.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from TRH patients and healthy controls (HC) were adoptively transferred into immunodeficient NSG-(KbDb)^null mice. Hypertension was induced by angiotensin II infusion for 14 days and monitored continuously by radiotelemetry. Following T cell engraftment, blood pressure was assessed at baseline and during AngII infusion in both groups of recipient mice. At baseline, systolic blood pressure did not differ between both groups. However, mice receiving TRH-PBMCs developed a significantly higher systolic blood pressure following AngII compared with HC-PBMC recipients. Endothelial dysfunction in isolated perfused kidneys was more pronounced in AngII-challenged TRH-PBMC recipients compared to HC-PBMC recipients. TRH-PBMC recipients displayed elevated effector memory CD4+ T cells and Th17 frequencies in spleen and kidney, along with markedly increased renal expression of human T cell-derived TNF. Overnight incubation of mouse aortic rings with human TNF induced endothelial dysfunction, indicating a causal role of T cell-derived TNF. As a proof of concept, TNF inhibition attenuated AngII-induced hypertension in TRH-PBMC-engrafted mice.

CONCLUSIONS: T cells from patients with treatment-resistant hypertension promote an exaggerated hypertensive response and endothelial dysfunction in PBMC-engrafted humanized mice, promoted by TNF-mediated mechanisms. These findings provide evidence that T cell-derived TNF may contribute to the pathogenesis of human hypertension.

articles.title: COMPANION-002: A Randomized Phase 2/3 Trial of Tovecimig Plus Paclitaxel versus Paclitaxel Alone as a Second-line Therapy in Patients with Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with previously treated biliary tract cancer (BTC) have a short median overall survival (OS), and few treatment options. Tovecimig, a bispecific antibody to delta-like ligand-4 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A, was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in COMPANION-002, a randomized phase 2/3 study in pretreated patients with advanced BTC.

METHODS: Patients with advanced BTC with one prior systemic therapy were randomized to paclitaxel (80 mg/m2; days 1, 8 and 15) with or without tovecimig (10 mg/kg; days 1 and 15). The primary endpoint was RECIST v1.1-defined objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and OS. Crossover from the paclitaxel control arm to tovecimig plus paclitaxel was permitted following BICR-confirmed progression.

RESULTS: 168 patients were randomized 2:1 to tovecimig+paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). Tovecimig+paclitaxel significantly improved BICR-assessed ORR (18.0% vs 5.3%; P=.0228) and PFS (4.7 vs 2.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.44; P<.0001). Among 31 patients (54%) who crossed over, post-progression PFS (time from crossover to subsequent second progression) exceeded initial PFS (PFS from randomization to initial progression on paclitaxel; 3.5 vs 1.9 months; HR, 0.40; P=.0035). Overall, 142 patients (85%) received tovecimig; no difference in OS was observed (HR, 1.05; P=.779). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) with tovecimig+paclitaxel were hypertension (69.4%) and fatigue (66.7%). Grade ≥3 TEAEs occurred in 93.5% and 64.2% of patients treated with tovecimig+paclitaxel and paclitaxel alone, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Tovecimig combined with paclitaxel significantly improved ORR and PFS versus paclitaxel alone as second-line therapy for patients with BTC.

articles.title: Analysis of queries in an HIV drug-drug interaction checker to explore changes in prescribing patterns: A 5-year analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Careful consideration of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is critical as people with HIV age. We analysed queries submitted to the University of Liverpool HIV Drug Interactions Database to assess changes in prescribing patterns over 5 years.

METHODS: Queries submitted between January 2020 and December 2024 were extracted and categorized by year, antiretroviral agent, comedication class, interaction severity (green/yellow/amber/red) and country. Descriptive statistics and annual trends were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 7 274 301 queries from 48 countries were recorded, representing a 441% increase over the study period. Dolutegravir (21%) and bictegravir (20%) were the most queried antiretrovirals, and queries involving unboosted integrase inhibitors rose. The most queried comedication classes were antibacterials, lipid-lowering agents and supplements/vitamins. Amber and red DDIs declined by 6% and 3% between January 2020 and December 2024, while green increased by 9%.

CONCLUSIONS: Query volume rose markedly while DDI severity declined, likely reflecting broader use of modern antiretrovirals with more favourable interaction profiles. Continued vigilance and interaction-checking tools remain essential in HIV care.

articles.title: Investigation and Management of Neonates Presenting to Hospital With Fever: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: Guidelines for neonates presenting to the emergency department (ED) with fever, including fever at home, recommend a full septic work-up and prompt administration of parenteral antibiotics. However, compliance is unknown. We sought to determine rates of guideline compliance in this population, reasons for non-compliance and rates and outcomes of serious bacterial infection (SBI).

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of all neonates aged ≤ 28 days presenting to the ED with documented fever ≥   38°C. We extracted and analysed hospital data from an electronic medical record for guideline compliance, reasons for non-compliance, rates of SBI, and clinical outcomes. Our primary outcome was the rate of guideline compliance.

RESULTS: We included 475 patients, less than half (46.5%) of whom received guideline-compliant care. The primary contributor to guideline non-compliance was fever at home but no fever in the ED. Overall, 65/475 (15%) of patients had SBI, the majority of which were urinary tract infections (UTIs). 42/65 (64.6%) of patients with SBI had a confirmed concurrent viral infection. 107/475 (22.5%) were discharged home from ED, only one (0.9%) of whom was readmitted within 72 h.

CONCLUSIONS: Fewer than half of febrile neonates presenting to the ED receive guideline-compliant care, with the lowest compliance in infants who are febrile at home but not in the ED. Rates of SBI are high, and viral-bacterial co-infection is common. In some low-risk infants, a tailored approach to investigation and management may be suitable, though risk mitigation strategies and potential future guideline adaptation warrant further exploration.

articles.title: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder in Parkinson's Disease Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies suggested that Temporomandibular joint disorder (TMD) may be more prevalent in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD), but lack international standardized clinical assessment.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the correlation between the Diagnostic Criteria for TMD (DC/TMD) diagnosis and PD motor symptoms, and to investigate the presence of TMD in PD patients.

METHODS: 419 participants from the outpatient clinic of the Department of Neurology were enrolled. Patient's TMD status was diagnosed with DC/TMD. PD motor symptoms and severity were assessed by the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) part III and Modified Hoehn and Yahr scale (HY).

RESULTS: 45.6% of PD participants were diagnosed with TMD, with Anterior Disc Displacement with Reduction being the most common TMD subtype (27.4%), followed by Degenerative Joint Disease (6.9%). Compared to PD patients without TMD, those with TMD exhibited more advanced motor dysfunction (p = 0.043). Occurrence of Pain-related TMD was correlated with bradykinesia (rho = 0.135, p = 0.006) and axial symptoms (rho = 0.125, p = 0.010), while Intra-articular joint disorder was correlated with tremor (rho = 0.097, p = 0.047). PD patients with longer disease duration were associated with higher odds of TMD diagnosis (OR = 1.064, p = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: TMD subtypes are associated with specific motor manifestations in PD: pain-related TMD correlated with bradykinesia and axial impairment, whereas intra-articular joint disorders correlated with tremor. Multidisciplinary collaboration between dentists and neurologists is essential and may benefit the management for both PD and TMD.

articles.title: Therapeutic efficacy and systemic pharmacokinetics of a dual-drug hydrogel contact lens for sustained glaucoma therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional topical therapy for glaucoma is limited by poor ocular bioavailability, rapid precorneal drug loss, frequent dosing and systemic absorption through the nasolacrimal pathway, which may reduce therapeutic efficacy and increase the risk of adverse effects. Drug-eluting hydrogel contact lenses have emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enabling sustained ocular drug delivery.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy, ocular biocompatibility and systemic pharmacokinetic profile of an optimized dual-drug-loaded HEMA-based hydrogel contact lens delivering timolol maleate (TM) and brimonidine tartrate (BT) for sustained glaucoma management.

METHODS: Optimized hydrogel contact lenses composed of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), N, N-dimethylacrylamide (DMA), N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP) and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA) were fabricated by UV photopolymerization and loaded with TM and BT (4 mg/mL each). Ocular biocompatibility was assessed using the modified Draize irritation test. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a steroid-induced ocular hypertension New Zealand White rabbit model by monitoring intraocular pressure (IOP) for 24 h. Systemic drug exposure was determined by validated high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis of plasma samples, while ocular safety was further confirmed through histopathological examination.

RESULTS: The optimized hydrogel lens exhibited excellent ocular biocompatibility, with a maximum Draize score of 0.33 ± 0.12 that resolved completely within 48 h and no histopathological evidence of ocular tissue damage. In hypertensive rabbits, the dual-drug hydrogel lens maintained normotensive IOP (16.1 ± 0.8 mmHg) for 24 h, representing a 43.5% reduction from baseline and significantly outperforming conventional eye drops beyond 4 h (p < 0.01). Plasma concentrations of both TM and BT remained below the limit of quantification (<2.0 ng/mL) throughout the study, whereas conventional eye drops produced measurable systemic exposure (TM: 18.4 ± 2.1 ng/mL; BT: 8.2 ± 1.2 ng/mL), demonstrating effective minimization of systemic drug absorption.

CONCLUSION: The optimized dual-drug-loaded hydrogel contact lens provided sustained intraocular pressure reduction, excellent ocular biocompatibility and negligible systemic drug exposure compared with conventional topical therapy. These findings highlight its potential as a sustained ocular drug-delivery platform capable of improving therapeutic efficacy, reducing systemic adverse effects and enhancing long-term treatment adherence in glaucoma management. Further long-term preclinical investigations and clinical studies are warranted to support clinical translation.

articles.title: Investigating the TASK1 potassium channel in equine atrial myocardium as a potential treatment target for atrial fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common clinically relevant arrhythmia in horses, with limited pharmacological treatment options in both veterinary and human medicine. TASK1 potassium channels represent a promising atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target, but their relevance in horses has not been established. To characterize equine TASK1 (eqTASK1) channels regarding structural conservation, electrophysiological function, pharmacological sensitivity, cardiac expression pattern and in vivo electrophysiological effects of TASK1 inhibition.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Sixteen horses killed for non-cardiovascular reasons, of which 10 horses used for tissue harvesting and six horses for in vivo testing. Functional and pharmacological properties of eq TASK1 and human (hTASK1) channels were assessed in Xenopus laevis oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp recordings. Cardiac expression of eqTASK1 was analysed by qRT-PCR and immunoblotting, while in vivo electrophysiological studies were performed in anaesthetized horses before and after intravenous ketodoxapram administration.

KEY RESULTS: EqTASK1 and h TASK1 channels demonstrated high structural conservation, comparable potassium-selective background currents and preserved pharmacological sensitivity with species-dependent differences in potency. EqTASK1 expression was strongly enriched in atrial and nodal tissue, whereas ventricular expression was minimal. In vivo administration of ketodoxapram significantly prolonged atrial effective refractory periods from 275 ± 54 to 418 ± 94 ms without significant changes in heart rate or atrioventricular conduction parameters.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: EqTASK1 channels are highly conserved with human orthologs and display pronounced atrial-predominant cardiac expression. In vivo TASK1 inhibition prolongs atrial refractoriness in horses, supporting TASK1 as a translational atrial-selective antiarrhythmic target in both human and veterinary medicine.

articles.title: Dactolisib outperforms Rapamycin in potentiating apoptosis induced by XPO1, Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 blockade in preclinical glioblastoma models.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma resists therapy through interconnected survival programs. Combined XPO1, Bcl-2, and Mcl-1 inhibition (Eltanexor, Venetoclax, A1210477; EVA) enhances the efficacy of chemotherapy, yet resistance persists. We hypothesized that PI3K/AKT/mTOR (PAM) signaling drives adaptive escape. TCGA/GTEx analyses and immunohistochemistry indicated PAM pathway activation in glioblastoma, with AKT significantly overexpressed, whereas PIK3CA showed a clear trend towards higher expression, although it did not reach statistical significance. qPCR analysis showed that PAM-component expression was highest in patient-derived glioblastoma stem-like cells (GSCs). In U87, U251, and GSCs, the dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor Dactolisib combined with EVA and 5-Azacytidine reduced viability and induced apoptosis more effectively than any of the Rapamycin combinations, and the difference in apoptosis was most pronounced in U87 and GSCs. Dactolisib monotherapy shifted the cell cycle towards G1 with a reduced S-phase fraction. In CAM xenografts, [18F]FDG-PET/CT showed decreased tracer uptake, and Caspase-3 activation with PARP cleavage was detected only under EVA + Dactolisib treatment. Taken together, our results suggest that dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition with Dactolisib disables a critical adaptive survival axis, warranting further preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: Asymptomatic extragenital Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection among transgender women in Argentina: Prevalence, antimicrobial susceptibility, and molecular characterization.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAsymptomatic extragenital Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) infection contributes to ongoing transmission and may facilitate the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. This study aimed to determine NG prevalence, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and sequence types among transgender women (TGW).MethodsReal-time PCR (qPCR) and culture for NG were performed on pharyngeal and rectal swabs and first-void urine (FVU) samples from TGW attending Fundación Huésped in Buenos Aires, Argentina (August 2021-March 2022). Quantification cycle (Cq) values from qPCR-positive samples were used as a proxy for bacterial load. Culture-positive isolates underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing and NG multi-antigen sequence typing (NG-MAST). Participants were also tested for other sexually transmitted infections (STI) and sociodemographic and behavioral data were collected by questionnaire.ResultsWe included 117 TGW: median age 32 (IQR 29-39), 55% had not completed high school, 54% were currently engaged in sex work, 55% had ≥ 5 sexual partners in the last month, and 68% reported recreational substance use in the previous year. At baseline, 46% were living with HIV, 20% had active syphilis, and 6% extragenital chlamydia. Global NG prevalence (determined by positive qPCR) was 9% (10/117) with 9 rectal infections (8%; 9/116), one pharyngeal infection (1%; 1/117), and none detected in FVU. Only three of nine PCR-positive rectal samples yielded a positive culture. All isolates were susceptible to ceftriaxone and azithromycin and showed intermediate susceptibility or resistance to tetracycline. Sequence types (ST) were ST21119, ST8202, and ST21122. No associations were found between asymptomatic extragenital NG infection and sociodemographic/behavioral factors. Seventy percent of positive PCR samples had a Cq ≥ 28, suggesting lower bacterial loads.ConclusionAsymptomatic extragenital NG infection prevalence among TGW in Buenos Aires was 9%, with no infections detected in FVU, underscoring the importance of extragenital screening. Limited culture recovery highlights the potential value of complementary approaches to antimicrobial resistance surveillance.

articles.title: Ambulatory Episodic Hypertension in Parkinson's Disease With Orthostatic Hypotension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to determine whether ambulatory hypertensive episodes are associated with clinical outcomes in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) with neurogenic versus non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with PD with suspected orthostatic hypotension (OH) underwent 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in the home setting. The primary exposure was the number of hypertensive episodes across 24 hours. Neurogenic OH was defined by a heart rate response to orthostatic systolic blood pressure reduction of <0.5 beats/min/mmHg during standardized 3-minute orthostatic testing. The primary outcome was quality of life measured by the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 Summary Index (PDQ-39 SI). Secondary outcomes included orthostatic symptom burden and motor severity. Multivariable linear regression models with interaction terms were adjusted for age, sex, disease duration, and levodopa equivalent daily dose, with robustness assessed through multiple sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine patients with PD were included, 30 with neurogenic OH and 29 with non-neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. Among patients with neurogenic OH, a greater number of hypertensive episodes was associated with better quality of life, lower orthostatic symptom burden, and lower motor impairment scores. In patients with non-neurogenic OH, these associations were absent or occurred in the opposite direction. Associations were stronger during daytime than night-time periods and remained consistent in sensitivity analyses.

INTERPRETATION: In patients with PD and neurogenic OH, ambulatory hypertensive episodes were associated with better clinical outcomes, an association not observed in patients with non-neurogenic OH. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: Precursor-Encoded Metal-Free Carbon Dots Reshape the Bone-Regenerative Microenvironment: Materials Chemistry, Multiscale Mechanisms, and a Translational Roadmap.
articles.abstract: Bone-defect healing is a spatiotemporally coordinated continuum involving inflammatory initiation and resolution, redox re-equilibration, immune-cell state transitions, angiogenesis, osteogenic commitment of mesenchymal stromal/progenitor cells, and osteoblast-osteoclast coupling. Although metal-containing nanomaterials can enhance regeneration through ion release, catalysis, or photothermal effects, their performance is often constrained by local dose, oxidation state, release kinetics, and long-term accumulation. Metal-free carbon dots (CDs) combine nanoscale interfacial activity, programmable surface chemistry, electron-transfer capacity, intrinsic fluorescence, and scaffold compatibility and are consequently evolving from imaging probes into bioactive regulators of the bone-repair microenvironment. Following the sequence of precursor chemistry-carbonization reconstruction-surface state-protein corona/organelle response-tissue regeneration, this review compares CDs derived from citric acid, ascorbic acid, amino acids, curcumin, artesunate, yam, clove, ginger, and other natural or medicinal-food precursors. We critically examine context-dependent redox regulation, macrophage-state remodeling, osteogenic and epigenetic control, suppression of pathological osteoclastogenesis, infection control, and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Current evidence is limited by ambiguous structural identity, confounded activity attribution, correlation-dominant mechanisms, overextension from simplified models, and insufficient long-term safety assessment. Translation will require fractionation-based identity definition, multi-batch potency assays, target-protein capture, organelle tracking, genetic rescue, spatial omics, and quantitative integration of chemistry, local exposure, degradation/clearance, and regenerative efficacy. Particular attention is given to how CD surface states interact with collagen, fibrin, and glycosaminoglycan matrices to govern protein adsorption, local retention, matrix organization, and growth-factor presentation. A two-tier evidence roadmap is proposed, prioritizing fraction-resolved activity attribution, compartment-specific redox assays, post-formulation identity testing, and context-matched progression from screening defects to load-bearing and comorbidity models.

articles.title: Effect of Obicetrapib on Glycaemia and New-Onset Diabetes: Pooled Analysis of BROADWAY/BROOKLYN and an Updated Meta-analysis of CETP Inhibitor Trials.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: New-onset diabetes (NoD) is a recognised effect of statin therapy potentially influencing acceptance of intensive LDL-C-lowering. In contrast, cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibition has been associated with lower NoD risk in earlier trials. We assessed the effect of the highly selective CETP inhibitor obicetrapib on glycaemia and NoD, contextualised within an updated meta-analysis of CETP inhibitor trials.

METHODS: Individual participant data from the phase 3 BROADWAY and BROOKLYN trials were pooled across 1,700 participants without diabetes at baseline (899 normoglycaemic, 801 prediabetes; 38.8% women), randomised 2:1 to obicetrapib 10 mg or placebo for 52 weeks. The PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review identified six eligible trials reporting NoD. Pooled risk ratios were calculated using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect models, with prespecified subgroup analyses by baseline glycaemic status and CETPi potency, and trial-level meta-regression.

RESULTS: Obicetrapib did not increase HbA1c at week 52 vs placebo (LSMD -0.02%, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.00). NoD occurred in 6.4% (obicetrapib) versus 8.5% (placebo) (adjusted OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.47-1.03), directionally consistent across glycaemic strata. Restricted cubic spline analyses identified associations between HDL-C, apoA1 and Lp(a) changes and NoD risk, but not HbA1c change. In the meta-analysis, CETP inhibition was associated with a 16% lower risk of NoD (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Obicetrapib did not adversely affect glycaemia and was associated with a numerically lower risk of NoD, consistent with a CETP inhibitor class signal of a modestly lower risk. The PREVAIL trial will provide larger-longer evidence about obicetrapib and NoD.

articles.title: A 78-Year-Old Man With a Previously Stable Atherosclerotic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Presenting With Impending Rupture Following COVID-19.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture is a life-threatening condition. Although elective repair is generally guided by aneurysm size, impending rupture can occur when rapid aneurysmal expansion or periaortic inflammatory changes develop before overt hemodynamic deterioration. This report describes the case of a 78-year-old man with a previously stable 43-mm atherosclerotic AAA who presented with impending rupture after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). CASE REPORT A 78-year-old Japanese man with a known AAA under imaging surveillance developed fever and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction testing. Seven days later, he was admitted for recurrent fever, cough, poor appetite, and elevated inflammatory markers. His medical history included hypertension, heavy smoking, advanced chronic kidney disease, and diffuse atherosclerotic disease. The aneurysm had shown minimal growth over 2 years, with a stable maximum short-axis diameter of approximately 43 mm on serial computed tomography. After admission, C-reactive protein levels initially decreased but rose again on hospital day 11, accompanied by new-onset mild low back pain and no marked blood pressure elevation or hemodynamic instability. Repeat non-contrast abdominal computed tomography performed 18 days after COVID-19 diagnosis demonstrated rapid AAA expansion from 43 mm to 51 mm within 2 months, with periaortic fat stranding, consistent with impending rupture. Urgent endovascular aneurysm repair was performed before hemodynamic deterioration. The postoperative course was stable, and the patient was discharged without ischemic or procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS This case shows that a previously stable AAA can abruptly destabilize after recent COVID-19. Repeat imaging should be considered when inflammatory markers rise or new symptoms occur, even when symptoms are mild.

articles.title: Self-Reported Completeness of Neurological Documentation in Prehospital Emergency Care: Associations With Neurological Training and Professional Experience.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Neurological assessment is a critical component of prehospital emergency care, particularly in time-sensitive conditions including stroke and traumatic brain injury. Neurological documentation practices in this setting remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate self-reported completeness of neurological documentation among paramedics, then examine its associations with neurological training and professional experience. MATERIAL AND METHODS A cross-sectional study was conducted between June 2025 and March 2026 among 348 paramedics working in emergency medical services in southeastern Poland. Data were collected using a structured electronic questionnaire. Self-reported documentation completeness was assessed using a composite score based on the reported frequency of documenting 7 neurological examination elements rated on a 5-point Likert scale (range: 7-35). RESULTS Overall self-reported documentation completeness was moderate (mean score: 24.57). Respondents frequently reported documenting basic neurological parameters (eg, level of consciousness: 81.0%); more detailed components were reported less consistently. Only 9.2% of respondents reported consistently documenting temporal neurological changes. The greatest self-reported deficiencies involved documentation of temporal neurological changes and detailed focal neurological findings. Participation in neurological training was associated with higher completeness scores (26.20 vs 23.24; P<0.001). Self-reported documentation completeness was positively correlated with professional experience (ρ=0.359; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS Self-reported neurological documentation completeness among paramedics was moderate and selective; self-reported rates were lowest for dynamic and detailed focal neurological components. Participation in neurological training and greater professional experience were associated with higher self-reported documentation completeness scores. These findings suggest that standardized documentation protocols and targeted educational interventions contribute to more consistent neurological documentation practices in prehospital settings.

articles.title: Heart failure management and outcomes: what can we learn from Japan?
Transcriptional and phenotypic alterations of regulatory and effector T cells in type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by the destruction of pancreatic β-cells, in which the dysfunction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) contributes to impaired immune tolerance. However, Treg heterogeneity remains incompletely understood, which limits the effectiveness of current therapies. Here, we have integrated transcriptome, flow cytometry, glycemic correlation, and cross-model validation to characterize the dysregulation of Tregs and effector T cells (Teffs) in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced T1DM mouse model. Tregs exhibited a proliferative, effector-like, unstable lineage, and metabolic reprogramming features, marked by increased Melk, Prf1, Gzma and Hk2, and decreased expression of Tnfsf15, Irak3 and Zeb2 in T1DM, and alterations in the transcription-factor networks involving Nfatc2, Elk1, and Ahr. Flow cytometry further revealed that the frequency of splenic Tregs was significantly increased, accompanied by broad upregulation of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1), T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains (TIGIT), lymphocyte-activation gene 3 (LAG3), and T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3 (TIM3). Meanwhile, expression of glycoprotein A repetitions predominant (GARP) and latency-associated peptide (LAP) was decreased, whereas interleukin (IL)- 17 and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) secretion were increased, suggesting a Treg phenotype with high checkpoint expression and inflammatory features. Cross-model analyses identified concordant IL-15-, IL-36 A-, E2F-, and metabolic programs across the C57BL/6, non-obese diabetic (NOD), and human datasets, including shared genes Smad3, Mki67, and Cxcr4. Teffs also displayed a hyperactivated but transcriptionally imbalanced phenotype in T1DM. Collectively, our findings reveal transcriptional and phenotypic alterations in Tregs and Teffs, providing new insights into T-cell dysregulation and potentially informing the development of Treg-based immunotherapies in T1DM.

articles.title: β-Asarone Alleviates Post-stroke Neuroinflammation and Improves Mitochondrial Quality Via the BNIP3/BNIP3L-dependent Mitophagy Pathway.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with mitophagy playing a central role in post-stroke neurological dysfunction. β-Asarone, a major bioactive component derived from the traditional herb Acorus tatarinowii, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether β-asarone exerts neuroprotective effects against IS by modulating BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) cell model were established. Neuroprotective effects were evaluated using neurological behavioral scores, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, and Nissl staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Mitophagy was observed via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and fluorescence microscopy. Western blot (WB) analysis was performed to detect BNIP3/BNIP3L pathway proteins. Results showed that β-asarone enhanced mitophagy, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated post-stroke neuroinflammation. Conversely, the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) impaired mitophagic function, exacerbating ischemia-induced brain injury and inflammation, while β-asarone treatment reversed these detrimental effects. In summary, β-asarone mitigates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury after IS, at least partly through promoting BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for IS.

articles.title: Influence of perfusion pressure on image quality in postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) of coronary arteries: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of perfusion pressure in postmortem computed tomography angiography (PMCTA) on the visualisation of the coronary arteries. Coronary artery disease is a frequent cause of sudden cardiac death, and PMCTA is used alongside autopsy to assess the coronary arteries, including bypass grafts and stents. Reliable opacification of the coronary arteries is required to identify stenoses and acute occlusions and to assess their contribution to the mechanism of death. However, contrast distribution in PMCTA varies between cases, and perfusion-related artefacts can limit interpretation. Perfusion pressure is one parameter that can be controlled. An important step in this direction has been the recent demonstration that perfusion pressure can be continuously monitored during PMCTA. In this study of twelve postmortem cases (six evaluable), we examined three intravascular pressure groups (40, 60, and 80 mmHg) to assess coronary artery visualisation using a modified contrast agent pump with coupled real-time pressure monitoring and control. In this pilot study, 60 mmHg was the lowest perfusion pressure at which homogeneous coronary opacification with minimal perfusion-related artefacts was observed in all evaluable cases (two cases per pressure group). In one case a perfusion pressure of 80 mmHg depicted the peripheral coronary branches more completely, an observation that requires confirmation in a larger cohort. These findings may contribute to the methodological standardisation of pressure-based PMCTA protocols in forensic practice.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in health and disease.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻-GSH-GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia-reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.

articles.title: Varicella zoster vasculopathy presenting as bilateral subdural haematoma in an infant: case report of a rare case and literature review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection is typically benign in infants but may rarely cause neurological complications. The occurrence of chronic subdural haematoma following VZV infection in children has not previously been reported.

CASE DESCRIPTION: We report the case of a 6-month-old male infant who developed chicken pox with fever, irritability, and generalized vesicular rash. His rash and fever settled over 2 weeks, but he had persistent irritability, decreased feeding, intermittent vomiting, regression of developmental milestones, and developed progressive weight loss (50th to 9th centile). At 7 months, due to vomiting and persisting irritability, he was evaluated and found to have bilateral subdural collections resembling those typically seen following non-accidental injury. His subdural collections increased over next 3 weeks and he developed a tense fontanelle; therefore he underwent an ultrasound-guided trans-fontanelle aspiration yielding blood-stained fluid resulting in transient improvement. Rapid re-accumulation of the subdural collections necessitated bilateral burr-hole evacuation with creation of subdural pockets. Subsequent recurrence of the subdural collections was finally managed with a right-sided subduro-peritoneal shunt. His subdural fluid tested positive for VZV IgG which was indicative of previous VZV CNS encephalitis or vasculitis. On follow-up, the child recovered fully, regaining weight and developmental milestones.

CONCLUSION: Bilateral subdural haematoma following VZV infection in infancy is a rare and delayed but life-threatening complication which requires prompt recognition and intervention. It can mimic findings seen following non-accidental injury. Prolonged neurological symptoms following VZV infection should raise the possibility of intracranial complications and needs prompt investigation and management.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and hospital-based cost avoidance of single-port robotic surgery in gynecology: a large comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract: Single-port robotic surgery is increasingly used in gynecologic practice, yet large-scale comparative data describing both postoperative outcomes and the downstream use of hospital resources remain limited. In this study, we aimed to investigate postoperative outcomes and hospital-based economic analysis in single-port robotic surgery and laparoscopic surgery through a large-scale retrospective analysis. We retrospectively evaluated 8,243 consecutive patients who underwent minimally invasive surgery for benign or malignant gynecologic disease at Keimyung University Dongsan Hospital from April 2019 through December 2024. Conventional laparoscopy was performed in 6,109 patients and robotic-assisted surgery using the da Vinci Xi single-site or da Vinci SP platform in 2,134. Length of stay, transfusion, surgical site infection, postoperative complications, mortality, operative and anesthesia times, and 30-day readmission were compared. Hospital-based cost avoidance was estimated from differences in readmission, complications, and length of hospitalization. Compared with laparoscopy, robotic surgery was associated with shorter total hospitalization (2.54 vs. 3.18 days, P < 0.001) and postoperative stay (2.38 vs. 2.90 days, P < 0.001). Transfusion was less frequent after robotic surgery (0.6% vs. 2.5%, P < 0.001), whereas surgical site infection, postoperative complications, mortality, patient-controlled analgesia use, and 30-day readmission did not differ significantly. Operative room and anesthesia times were each approximately 8 min longer in the robotic group. Across 2,134 robotic procedures, differences in postoperative resource use corresponded to an estimated hospital-based medical cost avoidance of US$171,469 (US$80.4 per patient), with reduced length of stay accounting for more than 84% of the total. In this large real-world cohort, single-port robotic surgery was associated with shorter hospitalization and a lower transfusion rate than conventional laparoscopy, without a detectable increase in major perioperative adverse outcomes. The observed reduction in postoperative resource use was also associated with measurable hospital-based cost avoidance. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the clinical and economic value of single-port robotic surgery.

articles.title: Uniportal versus multiportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery for anatomical pulmonary resection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of perioperative recovery and surgical quality.
articles.abstract: Uniportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (uRATS) seeks to combine the dexterity of robotic platforms with reduced access trauma, yet its comparative value over multiportal RATS (mRATS) remains uncertain. We systematically evaluated perioperative recovery and surgical quality after anatomical pulmonary resection. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 2026. Comparative studies of uniportal/single-port versus multiportal robotic anatomical lung resection were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I V2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Nine non-randomised studies involving 813 patients were included, with seven studies rated at critical risk of bias. Postoperative complications occurred in 16.0% of uniportal and 30.2% of multiportal patients, with no statistically significant pooled difference (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.06; p = 0.069; I²=66%). No significant differences were identified in major complications, conversion, mortality, operative time, blood loss, chest-tube duration, length of stay, or lymph-node yield, or R0 resection. Uniportal surgery was associated with shorter console time (MD - 23.5 min, 95% CI - 35.6 to - 11.4) and lower postoperative day-1 pain (MD - 0.6 points, 95% CI - 0.9 to - 0.3). The 0.5- point pain difference was below commonly used thresholds for clinical importance and lost statistical significance when digitised values were excluded (p = 0.092). Available observational evidence does not demonstrate a clear difference in perioperative safety or surgical quality between uniportal/single-port and multiportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differences in length of stay and operative time by comparator port count, potentially reflecting confounding by operative era and experience. A possible reduction in console time and early postoperative pain was observed, but these findings were based on very-low-certainty evidence and were sensitive to individual studies.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists for antipsychotic-related overweight and metabolic dysregulation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antipsychotic-related overweight and metabolic dysregulation are highly prevalent among patients with severe mental illness. Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial metabolic benefits in the general population, their efficacy and safety in antipsychotic-treated patients remain unclear. This review aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of GLP-1RAs in patients with antipsychotic-related overweight and metabolic dysregulation.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating GLP-1RAs in adults receiving antipsychotic treatment. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to September 13, 2026. Primary outcomes included changes in body weight, body mass index (BMI), HbA1c, and total cholesterol. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs). This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261290294).

RESULTS: Eight RCTs involving 535 randomized participants were included. GLP-1RAs treatment was associated with significant reductions in body weight (MD = -6.54 kg, 95% CI: -9.80 to -3.29, P < 0.001, I2 = 92%), BMI (MD = -2.34 kg/m2, 95% CI: -3.34 to -1.34, P < 0.001, I² = 85%), HbA1c (MD = -0.32%, 95% CI: -0.39 to -0.26, P < 0.001, I² = 52%), waist circumference (MD = -5.22 cm, 95% CI: -6.55 to -3.88, P < 0.001, I2 = 27%), visceral fat mass (MD = -0.31 kg, 95% CI: -0.46 to -0.16, P < 0.001, I2 = 11%), and LDL-C (MD = -0.16 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.31 to -0.01, P = 0.03, I2 = 54%), whereas no significant effects were observed for total cholesterol, triglycerides, or HDL-C. Weight reduction was greatest with semaglutide, followed by liraglutide, and increased with longer treatment duration (both P for subgroup differences < 0.05). GLP-1RAs were associated with higher risks of nausea (RR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.20 to 2.16), vomiting (RR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.32 to 3.35), and constipation (RR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.23 to 4.47), but not of diarrhea, serious adverse events (RR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.49 to 1.06), all-cause discontinuation (RR = 1.05, 95% CI: 0.60 to 1.85), or discontinuation due to adverse events (RR = 2.14, 95% CI: 0.72 to 6.33). Psychiatric adverse events were infrequent and could not be pooled.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1RAs significantly improve weight-related and glycemic outcomes in antipsychotic-treated patients, at the cost of an increased risk of gastrointestinal adverse events. Their psychiatric safety could not be established owing to sparse data. Longer-term trials with standardized safety reporting are warranted.

articles.title: Nasal high-frequency oscillatory ventilation as primary respiratory support in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome: current evidence and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the standard initial therapy for respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and associated with failure rates of up to 50% in extremely preterm infants. Nasal intermittent positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV) has demonstrated consistent benefits over CPAP in reducing respiratory failure and intubation. Nasal high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (nHFOV) has also shown reduced treatment failure compared with CPAP, particularly in extremely preterm infants. However, direct head-to-head comparisons between nHFOV and NIPPV as primary support are lacking, and available evidence from indirect comparisons has low certainty. Both NIPPV and nHFOV represent viable advanced non-invasive ventilation options beyond CPAP, each with distinct physiological mechanisms and evidence profiles. The current evidence base supports the use of both modalities in clinical practice, but robust head-to-head randomized controlled trials comparing nHFOV and NIPPV as primary respiratory support are urgently needed to guide optimal clinical decision-making. What is Known: • CPAP is the standard first-line support for RDS but fails in up to 50% of extremely preterm infants. • Both NIPPV and nHFOV reduce treatment failure and intubation compared with CPAP. What is New: • Neither NIPPV nor nHFOV has proven superior to the other, as direct comparisons are few and of low certainty. Head-to-head RCTs of nHFOV vs. NIPPV as primary support in extremely preterm infants are urgently needed. • Modality choice should also be guided by local expertise, available equipment, and gestational age.

articles.title: Predicting diuretic response in acute heart failure: accurate forecasts, but better decisions?
Cavitary status and differential treatment response in refractory or severe Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease: Amikacin liposome inhalation suspension versus intravenous amikacin.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-based treatment, Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) often fails to achieve culture conversion. The current guideline recommends adding amikacin liposome inhalation suspension (ALIS) or intravenous amikacin (IV AMK) as intensifying treatment for refractory MAC-PD; however, no clear guidance exists for selecting these treatment options. We compared culture conversion between these agents and explored whether the difference varies by cavity status.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review from August 2019 to July 2025. Included were 57 patients with refractory or severe MAC-PD: 34 receiving ALIS and 23 receiving IV AMK. Treatment efficacy was evaluated by culture conversion within six months. We compared treatment efficacy across these agents and conducted a subgroup analysis by cavity status. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied, and the interaction between treatment group and cavity status was evaluated.

RESULTS: While no significant difference in overall culture conversion was detected (ALIS, 55.9%; IV AMK, 47.8%), IPTW-adjusted analysis showed opposite point estimates of hazard ratios (HRs) and a significant interaction with cavity status. The HRs for ALIS with reference to IV AMK were 2.50 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-8.27) without cavity and 0.62 (95% CI, 0.21-1.83) with cavity (p for interaction = 0.043). Furthermore, the upper lung zone cavity involvement showed a similar interaction (p for interaction = 0.012).

CONCLUSION: The difference in culture conversion between ALIS and IV AMK may vary according to cavity status. These findings require confirmation in larger cohorts restricted to refractory disease to optimize treatment selection.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease.

METHODS: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing.

FINDINGS: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related.

INTERPRETATION: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease.

FUNDING: Agios Pharmaceuticals.
