articles.title: [Midterm outcomes of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair mitral valve guided solely by transesophageal echocardiography].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To preliminarily evaluate the efficacy and safety of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair of the mitral valve (MV-TEER) guided solely by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Methods: A total of 46 patients with mitral regurgitation who underwent MV-TEER guided solely by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at Central China Fuwai Hospital of Zhengzhou University from January 2023 to January 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up was performed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after the procedure, including echocardiography, 6-minute walk test, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification, and grading of mitral regurgitation severity. Hospitalization for heart failure, repeat mitral valve intervention, and all-cause mortality were recorded. The cumulative incidence of rehospitalization for heart failure was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results: The median age of the enrolled patients was 67.5 (59.0, 73.0) years, and 29 patients (63%) were male. MV-TEER was successfully performed under sole TEE guidance in all 46 patients. The median follow-up duration was 15.80 (12.63, 20.64) months. The 1-year rehospitalization rate for heart failure was 20%, and 1 patient died of malignant arrhythmia. There was no repeat mitral valve intervention. At 1 year after the procedure, the left ventricular end-systolic diameter decreased significantly from (47.17±11.31) mm to (39.71±7.44) mm (P<0.05). The left ventricular end-systolic volume decreased from (87.02±20.63) ml to (72.18±17.30) ml (P<0.05), and the left ventricular ejection fraction improved from (44.98±11.78)% to (51.84±10.03)% (P<0.05). Five patients had mitral regurgitation grade 3+, while the remaining patients had grade less than 3+. Three patients were in NYHA functional class Ⅲ, 23 in class Ⅱ, and 19 in class Ⅰ. The 6-minute walk distance improved significantly from (298±78) m to (375±70) m (P<0.05). Conclusion: It is preliminarily demonstrated that MV-TEER guided solely by TEE is safe and effective, and patients have favorable midterm outcomes.

articles.title: [Two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography in radiotherapy-related right heart dysfunction and analysis of associated risk factors].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the impact of radiotherapy on right ventricular function using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) in patients with thoracic tumors, and to identify factors associated with radiotherapy-induced right ventricular dysfunction. Methods: Patients who received thoracic radiotherapy at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University between May 2021 and May 2022 were enrolled in this study. 2D-STE examinations were performed before, during (upon completion of half of the prescribed radiotherapy dose), and after radiotherapy (1 to 2days after the end of radiotherapy). The 2D-STE evaluation parameters included left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS). The difference between post-treatment RVFWLS and the baseline value (ΔRVFWLS) and the percentage change in RVFWLS were calculated. Right ventricular dysfunction was defined as a right ventricular fractional area change (FAC)<35% or tricuspid annular systolic peak velocity at the right ventricular free wall<10 cm/s. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed to investigate the associations of age, cardiac volume, radiotherapy parameters, and other factors with ΔRVFWLS and the percentage change in RVFWLS. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the predictive performance of the relevant factors for right ventricular dysfunction, and the Kaplan-Meier method was adopted for survival analysis. Results: A total of 40 patients were enrolled in this study, including 22 males, with a median age of 61.0 years. Compared with baseline, right ventricular FAC ((45.48±4.67)% vs. (51.75±6.55)%, P<0.05), LVGLS ((-16.83±2.99)% vs. (-18.85±3.00)%, P<0.05), and RVFWLS ((-25.69±2.29)% vs. (-28.86±1.26)%, P<0.05) decreased during treatment. These parameters remained lower than the baseline levels after treatment (all P<0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that mean heart dose (MHD) and patient age were linearly correlated with ΔRVFWLS and the percentage change in RVFWLS (all P<0.05). ROC curve analysis revealed that the area under the curve (AUC) of MHD for predicting right ventricular dysfunction was 0.984, with a cut-off value of 2 020 cGy; the AUC for patient age was 0.766, with a cut-off value of 56.5 years. The median follow-up duration was 82days, and 11 (28%) patients developed right ventricular dysfunction. The Kaplan-Meier survival curve indicated that the cumulative incidence of endpoint events was higher in patients aged ≥56.5 years than in those aged <56.5 years (Plog-rank=0.020). The cumulative incidence of endpoint events was higher in patients with an MHD ≥2 020 cGy than in those with an MHD <2 020 cGy (Plog-rank<0.001). Conclusions: 2D-STE allows early detection of right ventricular dysfunction. Patient age and MHD are factors associated with radiotherapy-induced right ventricular dysfunction.

articles.title: [Construction of a prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To construct a machine-learning-based prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: A total of 5829 patients with STEMI who underwent emergency PCI at the Emergency Critical Care Center of Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University, from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025, were enrolled. Patients were divided into the MACE group (524 cases) and the non-MACE group (5 305 cases) according to the occurrence of in-hospital MACE and were further divided into the training set (4 080 cases) and test set (1 749 cases) at a ratio of 7∶3. MACE included cardiogenic shock, severe heart failure, severe arrhythmia, acute stent thrombosis or recurrent acute myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and cardiogenic death. Demographic data, lifestyle-related factors, past medical history, admission vital signs, laboratory test results within 24 hours after admission, echocardiographic parameters, Killip classification, and coronary interventional data were collected. Univariate analysis and Lasso regression were performed to select variables for model construction. Five machine-learning algorithms, including support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression, random forest, naive Bayes, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were used to construct prediction models for in-hospital MACE. The optimal model was selected based on the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis were used to assess the probability calibration and clinical net benefit of the model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the contribution of each feature. Results: The patients were aged (58.1±12.3) years, and 4 875 (83.63%) were male. Fourteen variables were selected for model construction, including B-type natriuretic peptide, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-sensitivity troponin I, triglycerides, triglyceride-glucose index, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, glycated hemoglobin, creatine kinase-MB, smoking history, heart rate, Killip classification, and age. The XGBoost model yielded the best predictive performance, with an AUC-ROC of 0.992 and an AUPRC of 0.947, and exhibited favorable probability calibration and clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis demonstrated that the top five variables with the greatest contribution to model prediction were B-type natriuretic peptide, creatine kinase-MB, myoglobin, left ventricular ejection fraction, and triglyceride-glucose index. Conclusions: Machine-learning prediction models for in-hospital MACE after emergency PCI in patients with STEMI were successfully constructed and internally validated. The XGBoost model demonstrated good discriminative ability, probability calibration, and clinical net benefit and may serve as a reference for early in-hospital risk stratification and clinical decision-making in STEMI patients undergoing emergency PCI.

articles.title: [Clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical characteristics and prognosis of atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR). Methods: This was a single-center retrospective study. Patients hospitalized at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 2020 and March 2022 and diagnosed with significant functional mitral regurgitation were enrolled. According to the type of regurgitation, patients were divided into the AFMR group and the ventricular functional mitral regurgitation (VFMR) group. Clinical and echocardiographic data were compared between the two groups. The patients were followed up until April 2024. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was the composite of cardiac death and hospitalization for heart failure. Survival was compared between the two groups using Kaplan-Meier survival curves. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Results: The study cohort consisted of 269 patients, with a median age of 66.0 (57.5, 76.0) years, among whom 172 (63.9%) were male. Patients were divided into the AFMR group (n=61, 22.7%) and the VFMR group (n=208, 77.3%). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group had a higher proportion of female patients, older age, a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, lower prevalences of coronary artery disease, fewer patients with heart failure symptoms, and a lower proportion of prior visits to cardiovascular departments (all P<0.05). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group demonstrated significantly larger anteroposterior left atrial diameter, right atrial transverse diameter, and right ventricular transverse diameter, along with a higher LVEF and a higher prevalence of moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (all P<0.05). The follow-up duration was 24.6 (5.8, 37.6) months. The AFMR group exhibited lower all-cause mortality (21.3% (13/61) vs. 38.9% (81/208), P=0.011) and a lower rate of the composite endpoint of cardiac death and heart failure hospitalization (24.6% (15/61) vs. 42.8% (89/208), P=0.010) than the VFMR group. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis also revealed that the AFMR group had a higher cumulative event-free survival rate than the VFMR group (Plog-rank=0.002). Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression analysis demonstrated that age (HR=1.038, 95%CI 1.019-1.057, P<0.001), cerebrovascular disease (HR=2.014, 95%CI 1.200-3.382, P=0.008), AFMR (HR=0.341, 95%CI 0.175-0.667, P=0.002), and moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (HR=2.297, 95%CI 1.467-3.596, P<0.001) were independent predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Conclusions: Compared with VFMR, AFMR is more common among elderly patients, female patients, and patients with atrial fibrillation and is less frequently accompanied by heart failure symptoms. The rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure are both lower in the AFMR group than those in the VFMR group.

articles.title: [Dual association of peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death in patients with coronary artery disease: a large-scale cohort study].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and its clinical prognostic value in patients with coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and receiving clopidogrel. Methods: This was a single-center prospective cohort study. Consecutive patients with coronary artery disease who underwent PCI at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January and December 2013 were enrolled; those receiving dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel were included. Baseline data were collected, and platelet reactivity was assessed using thromboelastography. Patients were followed up for 5 years, with cardiac death as the endpoint. Baseline eosinophil count was analyzed as a continuous variable and was also categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4). Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze the association between eosinophil count and high on-treatment platelet reactivity. Multivariable restricted cubic spline models were used to analyze the dose-response relationship. Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed according to age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to assess the predictive value of eosinophil count for cardiac death. Results: A total of 6 524 patients were included. The mean age was (58.21±10.26) years, and 5 059 (77.54%) were male. Among them, 6 050 patients completed the 5-year follow-up, and 140 cardiac deaths (2.31%) occurred. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was negatively associated with the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (OR=0.94, 95%CI: 0.90-0.98, P=0.003). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the lowest quartile group (Q1), the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity was lower in patients in the highest quartile group (Q4) (OR=0.77, 95%CI: 0.65-0.91, P=0.003). Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis showed a linear negative correlation between eosinophil count and the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (P for overall=0.012, P for nonlinearity=0.362). Further subgroup analysis showed that the above association remained consistent across clinical subgroups stratified by age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels (all P for interaction>0.05). Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was positively associated with the risk of cardiac death (HR=1.14, 95%CI: 1.07-1.21, P<0.001). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the Q1 group, the risk of cardiac death was higher in patients in the Q4 group (HR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.25-3.59, P<0.001). Conclusions: In patients with coronary artery disease undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel, baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count showed a dual association with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death. A lower count was associated with an increased risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, whereas an elevated count was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiac death.

articles.title: [The incidence and 1-year prognosis of heart failure following myocardial infarction during hospitalization in patients with first STEMI].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the incidence of in-hospital heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) and 1-year mortality in patients with first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to compare the 1-year mortality risk among different types of HF. Methods: Data were derived from the Henan STEMI registry, which was a multicentre, prospective, observational study in central China. After excluding patients with a history of MI or HF, patients with first STEMI were divided into the HF and non-HF groups according to the occurrence of in-hospital HF. Based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measured on the last echocardiogram during hospitalization, patients with HF were classified into HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF≥50%), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF, LVEF 41%-49%), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF≤40%), and HF with missing LVEF. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed with the log-rank test. Multivariate Cox frailty models were used to analyze the associations of HF status (present vs. absent) and different LVEF subgroups with 1-year mortality, using the non-HF group as the reference. Results: A total of 4 737 patients with first STEMI were included in the final analysis, with a median age of 62.8 (52.4, 70.8) years, of whom 1 158 (24.4%) were female. During hospitalization, 1 978 cases (41.8%) developed HF following MI, including 268 (13.5%) with HFrEF, 309 (15.6%) with HFmrEF, 707 (35.7%) with HFpEF, and 694 (35.1%) with missing LVEF. A total of 3 967 (83.7%) patients completed the 1-year follow-up. The 1-year mortality was significantly higher among STEMI patients complicated by HF than in those without (23.3% (391/1 680) vs. 5.8% (132/2 287), log-rank P<0.001). Specifically, the rates were 29.6% (67/226) for HFrEF, 20.8% (53/255) for HFmrEF, 11.7% (72/615) for HFpEF and 34.1% (199/584) for HF with missing LVEF. Multivariate Cox frailty models identified in-hospital HF following MI as a risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR=2.13, 95%CI: 1.70-2.67). Notably, HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk of 1-year mortality (HR=1.59, 95%CI: 1.16-2.17), while the HF group with missing LVEF carried the highest risk (HR=2.49, 95%CI: 1.91-3.26). Conclusions: The incidence of HF following first STEMI during hospitalization was 41.8%, with a corresponding 1-year mortality of 23.3%. In-hospital HF following MI is a risk factor for 1-year mortality in patients with STEMI. Prognosis differed notably across HF subgroups: HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk, whereas patients with missing LVEF had the worst outcome.

articles.title: [Mechanism by which disulfiram improves cardiac function in HFpEF rats via the GSDMD/Drp1 signaling pathway].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of the gasdermin D (GSDMD)/dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) signaling pathway in cardiac injury and mitochondrial dynamic regulation in a rat model of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Methods: Twenty-four 8-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rats weighing 200-240 g were selected and randomly divided into four groups, with six rats per group: control group (regular chow and drinking water), HFpEF group (fed with 60% high-fat diet plus drinking water containing 0.5 g/L Nω-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester for 8 consecutive weeks), disulfiram group (intragastric administration of disulfiram at 50 mg·kg-¹·d-¹ on the basis of HFpEF modeling), and mitochondrial division inhibitor 1 (Mdivi-1) group (intragastric administration of Mdivi-1 at 30 mg·kg-¹·d-¹ on the basis of HFpEF modeling). H9C2 cardiomyoblasts were used for in-vitro experiments and assigned to four groups: normal cell group (cultured in routine complete medium with equal-volume vehicle), model group (treated with 12.5 mmol/L high glucose combined with 0.2 mmol/L palmitic acid for 12 h), disulfiram intervention group (40 μmol/L disulfiram added simultaneously with modeling), and Mdivi-1 intervention group (20 μmol/L Mdivi-1 added simultaneously with modeling). Echocardiography was performed to assess cardiac structure and function of rats in each group; a non-invasive blood pressure monitoring system was used to measure arterial blood pressure of rats; an exhaustive treadmill exercise test was performed to evaluate exercise tolerance of rats; HE, Masson, and wheat-germ agglutinin staining were used to assess myocardial histomorphology, collagen deposition, and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area; Western blot was used to detect the expression levels of GSDMD, cleaved GSDMD, Drp1, mitofusin (MFN) 1 and MFN2 in rat myocardial tissues and H9C2 cardiomyoblasts; enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and inflammatory factors, including interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 in rat myocardium; co-immunoprecipitation assay was performed to identify the interaction between GSDMD and Drp1 in myocardial tissues of HFpEF rats; immunohistochemical staining was used to determine myocardial GSDMD and Drp1 expression in rats. Results: Compared with the control group, the HFpEF group displayed a higher body weight ((364.50±20.98) g vs. (256.50±6.77) g), blood pressure (systolic blood pressure: (162.99±5.61) mmHg vs. (125.33±7.15) mmHg; diastolic blood pressure: (119.78±4.58) mmHg vs. (81.01±3.85) mmHg; 1 mmHg=0.133 kPa), left ventricular end-diastolic anterior wall thickness ((0.38±0.03) cm vs. (0.29±0.03) cm), left ventricular end-diastolic posterior wall thickness ((0.32±0.01) cm vs. (0.25±0.02) cm), left ventricular end-diastolic internal diameter ((0.78±0.03) cm vs. (0.67±0.01) cm), and the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (24.65±0.95 vs. 18.97±0.68). The HFpEF group also presented more severe myocardial fibrosis, larger cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area, elevated myocardial expression of GSDMD, cleaved-GSDMD and Drp1, as well as an increased phosphorylated-Drp1 (Ser616)/total Drp1 ratio. Higher myocardial levels of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide ((112.45±12.18) ng/L vs. (42.38±6.86) ng/L), IL-1β ((60.14±6.28) ng/L vs. (32.31±5.68) ng/L) and IL-18 ((82.52±7.11) ng/L vs. (56.77±5.02) ng/L) were observed in the HFpEF group than in the control group (all P<0.05). By contrast, the exhaustive treadmill running distance ((111.54±13.15)m vs. (268.75±11.79)m), ratio of early-to-late diastolic mitral inflow peak velocity (1.25±0.09 vs. 1.71±0.12) and the myocardial expression levels of MFN1 and MFN2 of HFpEF group were lower than the control group (all P<0.05). Co-immunoprecipitation assay confirmed a physical interaction between GSDMD and Drp1 in myocardial tissues of HFpEF rats. Compared with the HFpEF group, rats in the disulfiram and Mdivi-1 groups showed ameliorated cardiac diastolic dysfunction, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myocardial fibrosis, disordered myocardial mitochondrial dynamics and improved exercise tolerance (all P<0.05). Myocardial levels of GSDMD, Drp1, and the phosphorylated-Drp1 (Ser616)/total Drp1 ratio were lower in the disulfiram group than in the HFpEF group (all P<0.05). However, no statistically significant differences in myocardial GSDMD and cleaved-GSDMD expression were found between the Mdivi-1 group and the HFpEF group (all P>0.05). In-vitro experiments showed that, compared with the normal cell group, H9C2 cardiomyoblasts in the model group displayed higher expression of GSDMD, cleaved-GSDMD, Drp1, and phosphorylated-Drp1 (Ser616), as well as an increased phosphorylated-Drp1 (Ser616)/total Drp1 ratio. These parameters were significantly reduced in the disulfiram-intervention group relative to the model group (all P<0.05). Conclusions: A direct interaction exists between GSDMD and Drp1 in HFpEF. Drp1 may act downstream of GSDMD. The GSDMD/Drp1/mitochondrial fission axis serves as a key pathway mediating inflammation and energy-metabolism disorders in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Interventions with disulfiram and Mdivi-1 can ameliorate cardiac pathological alterations in HFpEF rats by regulating this pathway, which provides novel potential therapeutic targets for HFpEF.

articles.title: [The predictive value of left ventricular strain on cardiac magnetic resonance for adverse events in children and adolescent patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking in evaluating left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), as well as its prognostic value for adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. Patients with primary HCM aged ≤21 years who underwent standard CMR examination at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January 2010 and December 2018 were included. Baseline clinical and CMR data were collected, and follow-up was completed. The primary endpoint was composite adverse cardiovascular events, and the secondary endpoint was heart failure-related events. Patients were divided into the event group and the non-event group according to whether the primary endpoint occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Using the cohort median left ventricular GLS of -9.2% as the cut-off value, patients were stratified into the preserved GLS group (≤-9.2%) and the impaired GLS group (>-9.2%). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted, and the log-rank test was performed to compare survival differences between groups. Results: A total of 249 children and adolescents with HCM were included, aged (14.81±3.71)years, of whom 163 were males (65.5%). The follow-up duration was (66.59±33.00)months. Composite endpoint events occurred in 37 patients, including 17 heart failure-related events and 20 sudden cardiac death events; 212 patients remained event-free. After adjusting for confounders such as left ventricular ejection fraction and history of unexplained syncope, multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that the percentage of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and left ventricular GLS were independently associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.18, 95%CI 1.04-1.35, P=0.014; LGE extent: HR=1.12, 95%CI 1.06-1.18,P<0.001) and heart failure-related events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.52, 95%CI 1.18-1.96, P=0.001; LGE extent: HR=1.14, 95%CI 1.04-1.24, P=0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with impaired left ventricular GLS had lower cumulative event-free survival for both composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events compared with those with preserved GLS (log-rank all P<0.001). Conclusions: CMR feature-tracking can effectively assess left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary HCM. Left ventricular GLS and LGE percentage are independently associated with the risk of adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events in this patient population.

articles.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks.

METHODS: RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation.

INTERPRETATION: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.

FUNDING: Pharvaris.

articles.title: Targeted tuberculosis vaccination strategies in the United States: A modeling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) incidence in the United States has remained elevated above pre-pandemic levels since 2021, with over 85% of cases resulting from reactivation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. New vaccines that would prevent TB in adults are under development, but the potential health impact of a program prioritizing non-U.S.-born persons and persons with medical comorbidities, including persons living with HIV (PLWH), has not been evaluated.

METHODS: We developed a deterministic compartmental transmission model that simulates Mtb infection, transmission, and progression to TB in the U.S., stratified into four risk groups. We calibrated the model to 2024 U.S. TB surveillance data and estimated annual cases prevented, percent reduction in TB cases, and number needed to vaccinate (NNV) for targeted vaccination strategies under optimistic and conservative scenarios, varying vaccine efficacy, duration of protection, and vaccination coverage.

RESULTS: Under an optimistic scenario, vaccinating all high-risk groups (PLWH, non-U.S.-born persons, and persons with medical comorbidities) prevented 5385 cases per year (51.8% reduction, 95% UI: 35.2-66.8, NNV = 366). Under a conservative scenario, the same strategy prevented 1348 cases per year (13.0% reduction, 95% UI: 6.4-19.8, NNV = 510). Strategy rankings were preserved across all sensitivity and uncertainty analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Targeted vaccination of adults at high risk of progression from Mtb infection to TB disease can reduce U.S. TB incidence substantially. Strategies that include non-U.S.-born persons and PLWH are most efficient and impactful.

articles.title: Clinical development of human vaccine candidates against Shigella flexneri: a systematic review of clinical trials.
articles.abstract: Shigella flexneri remains a leading cause of shigellosis, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where it contributes substantially to childhood morbidity, mortality, and the growing burden of antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of vaccine research, no licensed vaccine against S. flexneri is currently available. This systematic review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate the clinical evidence regarding the safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of human S. flexneri vaccine candidates. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in major electronic databases following PRISMA guidelines to identify clinical studies evaluating S. flexneri vaccines. Twenty-four eligible clinical trials were included, encompassing live-attenuated, glycoconjugate, protein-based, generalized modules for membrane antigens (GMMA), and inactivated whole-cell vaccine platforms. Overall, most candidates demonstrated acceptable safety profiles and induced measurable systemic and, in several studies, mucosal immune responses. Glycoconjugate vaccines consistently generated durable humoral immunity, while live-attenuated vaccines elicited broader mucosal and cellular responses. However, considerable heterogeneity existed in vaccine formulations, dosing schedules, immunological endpoints, and follow-up periods, limiting direct comparisons across studies. Only one Phase III trial assessed clinical efficacy, highlighting the limited progression of vaccine candidates to advanced clinical evaluation. Collectively, the available evidence supports the continued development of several vaccine platforms. Large multicenter efficacy trials, standardized immunological outcome measures, and multivalent vaccine strategies will be essential to accelerate the development of an effective S. flexneri vaccine.

articles.title: Seasonal influenza vaccination coverage and population health burden in Europe during the 2019/2020 and 2021/2022 influenza seasons: an ecological panel analysis using principal-component-adjusted multivariable regression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have examined whether country-level seasonal influenza vaccination coverage is associated with population health burden. We assessed the associations of influenza vaccination coverage with all-cause mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) across countries participating in the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE).

METHODS: We conducted an ecological panel analysis using SHARE Waves 8 (2019-2020) and 9 (2021-2022) across participating EU/EEA countries, Switzerland, and Israel. Survey-weighted vaccination coverage and structural indicators were derived among adults aged ≥55 years. All-cause mortality, all-cause DALYs, lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) DALYs, and chronic disease-specific DALYs were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease database for the same age group. Principal component analysis (PCA) was performed on the pooled country-season dataset to summarize correlated structural covariates. Associations were estimated using linear mixed-effects models with country-specific random intercepts.

RESULTS: Mean vaccination coverage increased from 34.5% to 47.6% but remained below the EU target of 75% in many countries. After adjustment for period and PCA-derived covariates, a 1-percentage-point higher vaccination coverage was associated with 14.9 fewer all-cause deaths per 100,000 adults aged ≥55 years (95% CI: -22.8 to -7.1), 328.1 fewer all-cause DALYs per 100,000 (95% CI: -480.4 to -175.8), and 6.3 fewer LRTI DALYs per 100,000 (95% CI: -10.6 to -2.0). Subgroup-specific vaccination coverage was also inversely associated with diabetes DALYs (-12.1; 95% CI: -20.3 to -3.8).

CONCLUSIONS: In this two-period ecological analysis, higher country-level influenza vaccination coverage was inversely associated with mortality and DALY burden among adults aged ≥55 years. These findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating population-level associations rather than causal effects.

articles.title: Perceived influence of media campaigns and immunization awareness in rural Muzaffarabad, Azad Jammu and Kashmir: A cross-sectional evaluation of selection Bias in digital survey methodology.
articles.abstract: Despite ongoing Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) activities, immunization coverage (IC) in rural areas of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) remains below the herd-immunity threshold of 95%. This study assessed the perceived influence of media campaigns on immunization awareness among rural caregivers in Muzaffarabad and examined methodological implications of WhatsApp-based data collection in a partially connected population. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 300 parents/caregivers of children under five, using a WHO 30 × 10 cluster design across 30 rural Union Councils. Households were identified in person by Lady Health Workers (LHWs); the structured questionnaire was then administered via WhatsApp. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and chi-square tests were computed in IBM SPSS v.25. Social media was the most frequently used source of health information (M = 4.08), and awareness (M = 3.72) and perceived campaign effectiveness (M = 3.76) were moderately high. Media exposure was positively associated with awareness (r = 0.363, p < .001), and awareness was strongly associated with perceived effectiveness (r = 0.720, p < .001). The sample's self-reported vaccination rate (98.67%) was substantially higher than the district's official baseline (82%); we interpret this gap cautiously as consistent with, though not conclusive proof of, selection bias associated with digital survey administration, given the study's cross-sectional design and lack of a non-digital comparison arm. We propose a Hybrid Communication Model integrating social media, religious networks, and community health workers to strengthen immunization communication in rural AJK.

articles.title: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of three doses of an adjuvanted group B Streptococcus vaccine in older adults aged 55 to 75.
articles.abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) disease is an increasing medical burden in adults. The present phase 1 trial evaluated an adjuvanted GBS vaccine (GBS-AlpN) containing N-terminal domains of four alpha-like proteins (AlpNs) (Alp1N, Alp2/3 N, RibN and AlpCN) in 60 healthy adults and 30 with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes (O/D) aged 55 to 75 years of age. Participants received three intramuscular doses of GBS-AlpN or placebo (48:12 and 24:6) on Day 1, Week 4 and Week 24. Solicited local and systemic adverse events (AEs), unsolicited AEs, and serious AEs (SAEs) were collected. Geometric mean concentrations of antibodies to the four AlpN antigens, and seroconversion were determined. The median age was between 65 and 66 years with more females in the healthy groups and more males in the O/D groups. Mainly mild solicited local and systemic AEs were reported for 53 healthy and 26 O/D participants. Seven SAEs, all unrelated, were reported (three in the placebo group and four in the active groups). At least 1 unsolicited AE was reported by 43 healthy and 22 O/D participants. None of the severe unsolicited AEs were related. By Day 57 all participants except three, who received GBS-AlpN had seroconverted for all four AlpNs. The vaccine elicited robust and durable antibody responses, already after the second dose, with comparable results between subgroups. These findings support further clinical investigation for the optimal vaccination strategy to protect vulnerable older adults against GBS disease.

articles.title: Immunogenicity and safety of high-dose versus standard-dose quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in patients living with HIV: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Influenza remains a major cause of morbidity in people living with HIV (PLWH), and despite recommendations for annual vaccination with the standard-dose (SD) quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV4), immune responses are often suboptimal in this population. To address this gap, we conducted a randomized, single-blinded, controlled trial to compare the immunogenicity and safety of the high-dose (HD) IIV4 (60 μg, Efluelda, Sanofi) with the SD IIV4 (15 μg, Vaxigrip Tetra, Sanofi). Vaccinations were administered between August and December 2023, and seroprotection (SP) was defined as a hemagglutination-inhibition antibody titer ≥1:40 at one month post-vaccination. Adverse events (AEs) were actively monitored. Of 110 participants enrolled, 103 were included in the per-protocol analysis (52 HD; 51 SD). The mean age was 49.6 years, 63.1% were male, and the median CD4 count was 555 cells/mm3. Most participants were virologically suppressed (93.2%), and more than half were receiving integrase inhibitor-based antiretroviral regimens (57.3%). Overall, 50.5% of participants achieved SP to all four vaccine strains. The HD group demonstrated significantly higher overall SP compared with the SD group (61.5% vs. 39.2%, p = 0.02). In strain-specific analyses, a significantly higher seroprotection rate was observed for A/H3N2 (76.9% vs. 52.9%, p = 0.01). In multivariable logistic regression, receipt of HD IIV4 (OR 2.7, 95% CI 1.9-6.1, p = 0.02) and female sex (OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.1-5.9, p = 0.04) were independently associated with SP against all strains. AEs were reported in 55.8% of HD and 58.8% of SD recipients (p = 0.75), most commonly local reactions, with no severe vaccine-related events observed. In conclusion, HD IIV4 enhanced immunogenicity against the vaccine A/H3N2 strain compared with SD IIV4, without increasing the risk of adverse events compared to SD IIV4. These findings suggest that HD IIV4 may enhance immunogenicity in PLWH and warrant further investigation in studies evaluating clinical effectiveness (TCTR20230501002).

articles.title: A cluster-randomized trial of the school-based 'Superprotegidas' behavioral intervention to improve HPV vaccination uptake in Colombian girls.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the effect of Superprotegidas, a behavioral intervention designed to increase HPV vaccination rates among girls and their caregivers in a Colombian municipality, following the Phase III framework of the ORBIT Model for Behavioral Treatment Development.

METHODS: A two-arm randomized clinical trial was conducted with schools as the unit of randomization. The intervention, based on the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior model (COMB), included a pedagogical workshop for girls, a letter, an open chat, multimedia messages, and parental reminders.

RESULTS: A total of 77 girl-caregiver pairs (154 participants; girls aged 9-14) were enrolled: 42 pairs in the intervention group and 35 in the control group. Post-intervention vaccination rates were significantly higher in the intervention group (52.4%) compared to the control group (28.6%) (OR, 2.75 [95% CI: 1.06-7.12]). Predictors of vaccination, in addition to intervention participation, included lower girl's school level and higher scores on several behavioral drivers of the COM-B model (awareness of vaccine efficacy against cancer, awareness of vaccine safety, vaccine availability in schools, reflective motivation for cancer prevention, and automatic motivation related to vaccine advantages) as well as higher caregiver's self-efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that the Superprotegidas program increased HPV vaccination rates among age-eligible girls. As the program was implemented with existing program resources, and the findings also suggest that the program could be implemented in similar school-based settings.

articles.title: Multi-pathogen serosurveillance reveals correlated vaccination performance, waning tetanus immunity, and diphtheria boosting in Zambian children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaccination coverage estimates and case-based surveillance have limitations in evaluating immunization programs. Serosurveillance offers a complementary approach by directly measuring population immunity. We assessed whether serologic analyses across multiple antigens (i.e., measles, diphtheria, tetanus) could provide additional insights into vaccination program performance.

METHODS: We conducted a matched case-control study among children aged 2- to 10-years-old (n = 1286) in Zambia using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey. Using previously generated data on measles serostatus, measles seronegative children (i.e., "cases") were matched to measles seropositive children (i.e., "controls") on sex, age, HIV infection status, and province. Samples were tested for tetanus and diphtheria antitoxin IgG antibodies using commercial enzyme immunoassays. We estimated the odds of tetanus and diphtheria seropositivity by measles serostatus using conditional logistic regression and examined age-specific antibody dynamics.

RESULTS: Measles seronegative children had 1.7-fold increased odds (95% credible interval [CrI]: 1.3-2.1) of being tetanus seronegative compared to measles seropositive children. Diphtheria serostatus had no significant association with measles serostatus (odds ratio: 1.3; 95% CrI: 0.9-1.7). Tetanus seroprevalence declined monotonically with age. However, diphtheria seroprevalence initially declined through 5 years of age, then increased again beginning at 6 years of age despite the lack of vaccine booster doses given after the primary series in infancy, potentially from asymptomatic or subclinical infections.

CONCLUSIONS: Serologic analyses revealed measles serostatus was positively associated with tetanus serostatus (where seropositivity arises only via vaccination and not infection), suggesting children who are measles seronegative are more likely to have missed DTP vaccination. We additionally found that measles serostatus was not associated with diphtheria serostatus, suggesting that antibody responses to diphtheria continue to boost beyond infancy when DTP vaccination is given. Our findings support consideration of DTP booster doses in Zambia to address waning tetanus immunity and further investigation of potential diphtheria carriage and transmission.

articles.title: Which changes in adolescents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices following a school-based intervention in France increase HPV vaccination uptake and intentions? A mediation analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In France, human papillomavirus vaccine (HPVV) coverage among adolescents remains below the national objective. The PrevHPV randomised trial assessed three intervention components to improve HPVV coverage among adolescents: educational and motivational activities (EMM); vaccination campaigns (FA) in middle schools; and General Practitioner (GP) training. FA increased vaccine uptake, while EMM improved vaccine uptake or intention, as well as HPVV-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP). This secondary analysis aimed to assess whether the positive effect of EMM on HPVV uptake or intention was mediated by specific KAP improvements.

METHODS: A total of 2758 adolescents aged 13 to 15 years from 39 schools completed online questionnaires at baseline and 5 months post-intervention. We created binary variables for the outcome "gain in vaccine uptake or intention during follow-up" and for favourable changes in individual KAP items. We used mediation analyses to evaluate indirect effects of individual KAP items on the association between EMM and uptake/intention, adjusting for FA and GP components and accounting for school-level clustering.

RESULTS: EMM was associated with an increase in HPVV uptake or intention (OR:1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.41). The strongest significant mediation effects occurred via improved attitudes toward the vaccine's benefit-risk balance (indirect effect ORIE:1.14), vaccine safety (ORIE:1.12) and accessibility (ORIE:1.11), as well as for having discussed HPV vaccination with friends (ORIE:1.11) and for higher self-rated level of knowledge about the vaccine (ORIE:1.10).

CONCLUSION: These results help understanding the specific positive effects of co-constructed in-class educational activities and underpin the importance of improving vaccine-related attitudes - not only knowledge.

articles.title: Impact of different MMR vaccination strategies on mumps incidence in Jiangsu, China: A 20-year interrupted time series analysis based on 180,000 cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although China upgraded its mumps vaccine schedule to two doses, quantitative evaluations of real-world, population-level effects remain limited. This study systematically evaluated the immediate and long-term impacts of 1-dose and 2-dose measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination strategies on mumps incidence in Jiangsu Province.

METHODS: Statutory infectious disease surveillance data spanning 240 months from 2005 to 2024 in Jiangsu Province (183,490 cases) were collected. An interrupted time series (ITS) analysis was conducted using a generalized linear model (GLM) based on a negative binomial distribution. We evaluated the intervention effects of the vaccine policies while strictly controlling for autoregression, non-linear effects of meteorological factors, population dynamics, and the intensity of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs). Stratified analyses by age group and geographical region were also performed.

RESULTS: Following the introduction of the 1-dose MMR policy in 2008, no significant long-term downward trend in mumps incidence was observed across the province (IRR = 1.002, P = 0.773), and periodic outbreaks every 3 to 5 years persisted. Following the comprehensive implementation of the 2-dose MMR strategy in July 2020, the overall incidence exhibited a significant accelerated downward trend of 1.0% per month (IRR = 0.990, P = 0.019). Subgroup analyses revealed that the most heavily burdened 5-9 and 10-14 age groups experienced the most significant long-term declines (1.0% and 1.5% per month, respectively). Furthermore, the ≥15 years adult group, which was not directly targeted for vaccination, also showed a long-term reduction (0.9% per month), indicating a significant herd immunity effect. Additionally, the 2-dose policy successfully smoothed out regional incidence disparities, notably mitigating the compensatory outbreaks observed in Northern Jiangsu in 2019.

CONCLUSION: A 1-dose MMR immunization schedule is insufficient to interrupt periodic mumps outbreaks, and the transition to a 2-dose strategy was associated with a steady long-term decline in overall mumps incidence across Jiangsu Province, providing valuable real-world evidence to support the continuation and optimization of 2-dose MMR immunization schedules.

articles.title: Maternal pertussis vaccination uptake and reasons for non-vaccination among pregnant women in the Netherlands: a 5-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The maternal pertussis vaccination (MPV) was introduced in the Netherlands at the end of 2019. Despite its effectiveness, vaccine hesitancy remains, possibly influenced by factors such as age, education, employment, parity, native language, and country of birth. This study investigates associations between sociodemographic factors, MPV uptake, and reasons for declining the MPV among mothers of children born between January 2020 and March 2025.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from a preventive Youth Health Care Center, including 17.513 biological mothers. Since the end of 2023, reasons for declining MPV have been recorded, with retroactive recall from January 2023, yielding 768 reasons from 728 mothers. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between sociodemographic factors, MPV uptake, and reasons for not receiving the MPV.

RESULTS: Higher MPV uptake was associated with higher maternal age (ORs ranges between 1.78 [95% CI 1.52-2.09] and 2.70 [95% CI 2.24-3.25]) and employed mothers (OR 2.55, 95% CI 2.26-2.87). Lower MPV uptake was associated with lower education (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.37-0.46), parity (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.55-0.68), and being born outside the Netherlands (varying ORs between countries/(parts of) continents). Most reasons were not associated with sociodemographic factors. However, mothers aged ≥41 years were more likely (OR 2.61, 95% CI 1.16-5.88) to decline MPV due to concerns about vaccination during pregnancy. Mothers whose native language was not Dutch or English more often cited that they did not receive (right) information (on time) from healthcare workers (ORs ranges between 2.19 [95% CI 1.10-4.34] and 2.96 [95% CI 1.19-7.37]).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights not only how sociodemographic factors relate to MPV acceptance but also shows that reasons for MPV hesitancy cross through various sociodemographic groups. Findings offer new directions for targeted interventions to increase uptake and protect all newborns from pertussis.

articles.title: Vaccine- and infection-induced pneumococcal and DENV-NS1 antibodies reveal differential transplacental transfer and maternal-infant early exposure burden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women and their infants are vulnerable to severe infections with S. pneumoniae and dengue virus (DENV), for which early protection depends on maternally derived antibodies. Infection- and vaccine-induced responses may differ in quality and transfer, with implications for maternal immunization strategies. We evaluated isotype-specific antibody responses to pneumococcal vaccination and natural DENV infection in pregnant women and their infants and quantified early postnatal DENV exposure.

METHODS: In a longitudinal cohort in southern Colombia, a DENV-hyperendemic region, 140 low-risk pregnant women received either PPSV23 or Hib conjugate vaccine randomly in the third trimester. Circulating pneumococcal serotype 23F (Pn23F)-specific IgG and DENV NS1-specific IgG, IgM, and IgA were measured by ELISA in maternal, cord, and infant at delivery, 3, and 6 months; circulating NS1 was used to detect active DENV infection. Postnatal clinical follow-up was performed until 6 months of age.

RESULTS: PPSV23 increased maternal anti-Pn23F IgG, whereas anti-NS1 IgG from natural infection remained stable. Anti-Pn23F and anti-NS1 IgG were detectable in cord blood, but maternal-cord levels were strongly correlated for anti-NS1 IgG and not for anti-Pn23F IgG. Infant anti-NS1 IgG seropositivity declined from 99% at birth to 74% at 6 months, while anti-Pn23F IgG levels in infants of PPSV23-vaccinated mothers remained stable. Despite 99.1% maternal anti-NS1 IgG seroprevalence, 13.1% of infants developed anti-NS1 IgM or anti-NS1 IgA by 6 months, indicating early DENV infection without NS1 antigenemia or clinically apparent dengue.

CONCLUSION: Vaccine- and infection-induced antibodies showed antigen- and isotype-specific differences in transplacental transfer and postnatal persistence, revealing a high burden in the maternal and early infant populations. The emergence of NS1-IgA in infants demonstrates active postnatal DENV transmission and supports NS1-IgA as a sensitive marker for early infant exposure and serosurveillance in hyperendemic settings.

articles.title: Elucidating the role of pre-existing immunity in mucosal lymphoid architectural dynamics following live attenuated influenza vaccination.
articles.abstract: Mucosal immune responses in the upper respiratory tract are central to preventing influenza infection. The live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) is delivered intranasally, making it a valuable model for investigating mucosal immunity in humans. In this study, we examined structural and cellular changes in palatine tonsils following LAIV vaccination in cohorts of children and adults undergoing tonsillectomy. Using quantitative immunofluorescence microscopy, we assessed germinal centre and mantle zone architecture over time and quantified the distribution of IgG- and IgA-positive cells within these compartments. We also developed an in-situ staining approach to detect hemagglutinin-binding cells in paraffin-embedded tonsillar tissue. Age-dependent differences in lymphoid architecture following LAIV vaccination were observed 3 days after vaccination in children; germinal centre sizes appear smaller and IgG and IgA frequency peaks. In contrast, in adults, germinal centre sizes and IgG and IgA frequency gradually increase with increasing time post-vaccination. Mantle zone areas in children and adults increased following LAIV. In addition, hemagglutinin-binding cells were detected in tonsillar tissue, and in some instances co-localized with IgA. Pre-existing immunity influences immune kinetics; our results suggest children rapidly generate de novo germinal centres and class-switched antibodies, in contrast to adults who may expand preexisting germinal centres and trend toward gradual increases over time.

articles.title: Efficacy of lidocaine spray for pain reduction during rabies immunoglobulin infiltration: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) infiltration is essential but often intensely painful. This study primarily evaluated the efficacy of 10% lidocaine spray versus a placebo for pain reduction during needle penetration and RIG infiltration, while comparing adverse events and satisfaction levels as secondary objectives.

METHODS: This single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, superiority trial utilized a 1:1 allocation ratio among participants (18-65 years) requiring RIG at a university hospital in Bangkok. Patients with major organ disease, lidocaine contraindications, or recent analgesic use were excluded. A 100-mm Visual Analog Scale and 10-point Likert scale were used for pain (up to 30 min after RIG infiltration) and satisfaction assessment, respectively.

RESULTS: A total of 76 participants were randomized to the lidocaine or placebo group (n = 38 each). Baseline median pain intensity was similar between groups (lidocaine 18.0 (IQR: 4.0, 28.0) vs placebo 11.5 (IQR: 6.0, 28.0); p = 0.823 after adjusting for wound type and size). Compared with placebo, the lidocaine group reported significantly lower median pain during needle penetration (25.0 (IQR: 17.0, 42.0) vs 56.5 (IQR: 45.0, 75.0); adjusted median difference: -30.8 (95% CI: -43.6, -18.0); p < 0.001) and RIG infiltration (46.5 (IQR: 36.0, 81.0) vs 77.0 (IQR: 66.0, 90.0); adjusted median difference: -33.0 (95% CI, -47.3, -18.7); p < 0.001). No adverse effects were reported during the 30-min observation. Participant satisfaction was significantly higher in the lidocaine group (8.0 (IQR: 7.0, 9.0) vs 6.0 (IQR: 5.0, 6.8); p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Topical 10% lidocaine spray achieved statistically and clinically significant reductions in pain intensity during needle penetration and RIG infiltration compared with placebo. The intervention was well tolerated and associated with higher participant satisfaction. These findings support its use as a simple and efficacious option for procedural pain control in adults aged 18-65 years with the eligible small-to-moderate wound types evaluated in this study.

TRIAL REGISTRY: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20241127002).

articles.title: T-cell immunity in human herpesvirus vaccine development: research advances and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Human herpesviruses are widespread, establish lifelong latency, undergo intermittent or context-dependent reactivation, and cause diverse clinical manifestations. These features distinguish herpesvirus vaccine development from that for most acute infections. For indications involving latency, reactivation, or virus-associated disease, assessments based solely on the prevention of primary infection or on neutralizing-antibody responses do not capture all relevant mechanisms of immune control. Depending on the virus and indication, T cells may recognize infected or transformed cells, maintain immune surveillance, and limit viral replication, shedding, tissue injury, or disease progression. T-cell-directed strategies are therefore being investigated for therapeutic vaccination, protection of high-risk populations, prevention of reactivation-associated disease, and immunotherapy of virus-associated tumors. Using an indication-to-endpoint framework, this review compares preventive and therapeutic strategies and examines how antigen accessibility, tissue localization, host context, and endpoint selection influence whether measurable cellular immunogenicity translates into virological or clinical benefit across viruses and disease settings.

articles.title: Linker-mediated single-transcript mRNA vaccine expressing virus-like particles of enterovirus D68.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) causes pediatric respiratory illness and is linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), posing a global health threat. We have previously reported that an mRNA vaccine expressing a virus-like particle (VLP) of EV-D68, which co-administers two mRNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) encoding the viral structural protein P1 and viral protease 3CD, conferred protection against infection. Nonetheless, the requirement for two mRNA-LNPs presents challenges in manufacturing and quality control. Here, we investigated the potential of single mRNA constructs encoding both P1 and 3CD, connected by linker sequences. mRNA constructs encoding both P1 and 3CD in a single transcript were designed with linkers such as 2A peptides, 3CD protease cleavage sites (CS), combinations of 2A peptides and CS, or internal ribosome entry sites (IRES). Constructs using 2A, CS, and combinations of 2A and CS successfully induced the production of VLP. In contrast, mRNA with IRES failed due to modified nucleosides. Mice vaccinated with mRNAs that successfully expressed VLP developed neutralizing antibodies against EV-D68. They also demonstrated a protective effect against intranasal challenge, and their serum prevented neonatal mice from developing neurological symptoms caused by EV-D68 infection. These mRNA designs may reduce manufacturing complexity and cost, facilitating the development of effective EV-D68 mRNA vaccines.

articles.title: Safety and immunogenicity of mRNA-1345 revaccination at least 12 months following primary vaccination with a licensed protein subunit RSV vaccine.
articles.abstract: Protection from a single RSV vaccine dose is not lifelong, and revaccination may be needed to maintain it. This ongoing, phase 3, open-label trial evaluated revaccination with the RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 ≥12 months after primary vaccination with licensed protein subunit RSV vaccine in adults aged ≥60 years. Primary objectives were safety and immunogenicity. A total of 507 participants were enrolled. Revaccination was well-tolerated, with no safety concerns identified. Robust increases in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing antibody geometric mean titers were observed at Day 29. In a post hoc comparison of Day 29 titers following heterologous revaccination with those following primary mRNA-1345 vaccination in a subset of the pivotal efficacy study, geometric mean ratios for RSV-A and RSV-B were 0.952 (95% CI, 0.847-1.070) and 1.087 (95% CI, 0.964-1.226), respectively. These findings support revaccination with mRNA-1345 administered ≥12 months after primary vaccination with a licensed RSV protein subunit vaccine. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07117487.

articles.title: Impact of the HPV vaccination programme on anal HPV infection in gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men: multi-site enhanced surveillance study in specialist sexual health services in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A national human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) in England began in 2016. We evaluated the impact of this programme by monitoring the prevalence of type-specific HPV infections over time.

METHODS: Residual rectal swab specimens were collected from GBMSM aged ≤45 years undergoing chlamydia and/or gonorrhoea screening at 10 sexual health services (SHSs) between 2017-19 (Phase 1) and 2021-24 (Phase 2). Specimens were linked to data on sociodemographic characteristics, previous STI diagnoses, and HPV vaccination reported to the UK Health Security Agency's (UKHSA's) national STI surveillance system. Anonymised specimens were tested for type-specific HPV DNA using an in-house multiplex PCR and Luminex-based genotyping test. We compared the prevalence of vaccine-type HPV in each phase, and in those with and without any reported HPV vaccinations.

RESULTS: Data from 5,787 rectal swab specimens with HPV testing results were analysed: 3,291 in Phase 1 and 2,496 in Phase 2. There was a 36% decline in the prevalence of anal HPV16/18 infection between Phase 1 and Phase 2. Overall, the prevalence of HPV16/18 was similar in GBMSM with (16.6%; 95% CI 15.2-18.1) and without reported HPV vaccination (15.8%; 95% CI 14.5-17.1).

CONCLUSION: Eight years after HPV vaccination of GBMSM began, the prevalence of vaccine-type HPV in GBMSM has declined. Available data did not permit accurate estimation of vaccine effectiveness, likely due to the combined effects of underreporting of vaccinations, herd protection, and bias in vaccination uptake. These findings, albeit ecological, bode well for this targeted programme meeting its aim of reducing HPV-related diseases among GBMSM and reducing health inequalities.

articles.title: The platform trial in COVID-19 priming and BOOsting (PICOBOO): The reactogenicity of nine licensed COVID-19 vaccines delivered in immunocompetent adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PICOBOO is a randomised, Bayesian adaptive trial evaluating immunogenicity and reactogenicity of licensed COVID-19 vaccines in immunocompetent individuals aged >12 years. We present reactogenicity data for nine vaccines administered as additional doses within adult strata based on age cohort and primary vaccination regimen.

METHODS: Individuals who had not received a COVID-19 vaccine within three months were eligible. Participants were randomised within each stratum to receive a single vaccine dose. Reactogenicity events were recorded on days 1-7 following vaccination. Serious or medically attended adverse events (AEs), AEs of special interest, and AEs resulting in withdrawal were collected through day 28. Participants were followed until day 720.

FINDINGS: A total of 1049 COVID-19 vaccine doses were administered to 586 adults enrolled between March 2022 and September 2024. Of these, 335 (57%), 96 (16%), 97 (17%) and 58 (10%) were randomised one, two, three and four times, respectively. At least one local reaction was reported after 786 (75%) doses and at least one systemic reaction after 798 (76%) doses. Local reactogenicity ranged from 47% (110/236) with NVX-CoV2373 (Nvx) to 90% (131/145) with Moderna, while systemic reactogenicity ranged from 69% (162/236) with Nvx to 85% (121/143) with BNT162b2. Pain was the most common local reaction; headache, fatigue, myalgia, and chills were the most common systemic reactions. Severe reactogenicity events were rare.

INTERPRETATION: Reactogenicity events were common but rarely severe. Although reactogenicity appeared less frequent following Nvx than mRNA vaccines within strata, the trial was not powered for between-vaccine comparisons and findings should be interpreted descriptively.

FUNDING: Medical Research Future Fund (2014690/2016473) and The Snow Foundation.

articles.title: Secretory expression of tetrameric neuraminidase enhanced by signal peptide optimization elicits robust immunity against influenza infection in mice.
articles.abstract: Neuraminidase (NA), a key surface glycoprotein of influenza viruses, represents a more conserved antigenic target than hemagglutinin (HA) and has attracted interest as a potential target for vaccines with broader protective capacity. Nevertheless, the inefficient secretory production of tetrameric NA that maintain tetramer-like structural features remains challenging.Here, we developed an optimized signal peptide, opt-sp, by introducing valine and asparagine residues at the N-terminus of the Gaussia luciferase signal peptide (Gluc-sp) and incorporating a measles virus phosphoprotein-derived tetramerization domain. In a systematic comparison with three commonly used signal peptides, including tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), immunoglobulin G signal peptide (IgG-sp), and Gluc-sp, opt-sp was associated with increased relative secretion of NA protein under the tested expression conditions. Native PAGE analysis further suggested the presence of tetramer-like NA species. In mice，a DNA vaccine encoding opt-sp-fused NA elicited substantially stronger NA-specific humoral and cellular immune responses than constructs bearing conventional signal peptides and provided improved protection against homologous A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) challenge. These findings identify opt-sp as a promising signal peptide candidate for improving recombinant NA secretion and support further evaluation of this strategy for NA-based influenza vaccine development, including future studies of heterologous protection.

articles.title: Persistence of immune responses 5 years after vaccination with a single dose of typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) in Nepalese children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A single-dose typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) has been recommended in endemic settings. Here we report the 5-year immunogenicity results post a single dose of TCV in Nepal.

METHODS: We conducted a participant- and observer-blinded randomised trial (RCT) in Lalitpur, Nepal (2017-2021) (ISRCTN43385161). 20,019 children aged 9 months to ≤16 years were randomised to receive Typbar TCV (Vi-TT; Bharat Biotech International, India) or capsular group A meningococcal conjugate vaccine (MenA) in 2017-2018. After unblinding in 2020-2021, children were offered the alternate vaccine and were followed until 2025. A subgroup of 1500 participants (1000 Vi-TT, 500 MenA) were recruited into the immunogenicity cohort, who had blood samples taken at Day 0, Day 28, Month 18, Years 2, 4, and 5 post-baseline. The primary outcome is anti-Vi antibody responses.

RESULTS: The median age at TCV vaccination was 10.1 in the 2017/2018 cohort and 13.1 in the 2020/2021 cohort. The geometric mean concentration (GMC) of anti-Vi IgG was 2037.90 (95% CI: 1904.86-2180.23) at Day 28, dropping to 241.29 (220.27-264.31) at Month 18. At Year 5 post-vaccination, the GMC was 109.3 (98.65-121.10). The proportion of participants maintaining a ≥4-fold rise at Year 5 post-vaccination from baseline remained high (88%). Antibody decay was significantly slower in older children, females, and children with detectable baseline anti-Vi IgG, compared with their respective reference groups. Anti-Vi IgA was highly correlated with IgG (p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that anti-Vi immunity is sustained for at least 5 years post-vaccination. Children vaccinated at younger ages showed a faster decline, highlighting the need for further investigation into the optimal age for vaccination and the need for boosters.

FUNDING: Wellcome Trust.

articles.title: Preparation and functional evaluation of an alginate-targeted monoclonal antibody against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical-priority pathogen responsible for life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals, yet its extensive antigenic heterogeneity has impeded the development of immunotherapeutics. Alginate, a structurally conserved surface polysaccharide that forms the backbone of the biofilm matrix of mucoid P. aeruginosa strains in chronic infections, represents a compelling target. Here, we report the generation and functional evaluation of mAb 546B, a murine IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against the synthetic mannuronic acid tetrasaccharide epitope 1. This antibody bound to the surface alginate of both mucoid and nonmucoid P. aeruginosa strains and induced pronounced bacterial aggregation. Notably, 546B inhibited biofilm formation, disrupted established biofilms, and reduced the minimum inhibitory concentration of meropenem across multiple strains. In a bacterial clearance model, 546B monotherapy reduced lung bacterial burden compared to PBS controls, and its combination with meropenem achieved a marked reduction accompanied by significantly attenuated pulmonary inflammation and histopathological injury. In a lethal PAO1 pneumonia model, 546B alone improved the 7-day survival rate of mice, and combination with meropenem could further enhance the survival rate. These findings establish 546B as a promising monoclonal antibody that targets alginate-mediated biofilms, supporting its further development as a passive immunotherapeutic against P. aeruginosa infection.

articles.title: COVID-19 vaccine uptake among individuals with Down syndrome in the Unites States.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Individuals with Down syndrome are at increased risk for severe disease from acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, making them a priority group for COVID-19 vaccination. Data on vaccine uptake and factors associated with vaccination are needed to inform strategies to improve uptake in this vulnerable population.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate COVID-19 vaccine uptake and identify factors associated with vaccination among individuals with Down syndrome.

METHODS: The population included individuals with Down syndrome born during 1995-2021 and enrolled in the Tennessee Medicaid Program during the COVID-19 pandemic. We limited the study population to individuals who sought care at the Vanderbilt University Medical Center at least once between six months after their initial eligibility for the COVID-19 vaccine and October 1, 2024. Date and type of COVID-19 vaccine receipt were ascertained from the Tennessee Immunization Information System. Demographic and clinical characteristics associated with COVID-19 vaccine uptake and completion of the primary series were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 438 individuals with Down syndrome, 95 (22%), 88 (20%), 187 (43%), and 68 (16%) first became eligible for COVID-19 vaccine at age 16+, 12-15, 5-11, and 6 months-4 years of age, respectively. Overall, 152 (35%) received at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine; of these, 138 (91%) completed the primary series. Younger age and lack of influenza vaccination history-either never or during the pandemic-were strongly associated with a reduced likelihood of receiving COVID-19 vaccine or completing the primary series.

CONCLUSIONS: Only one-third of individuals with Down syndrome received any COVID-19 vaccine, indicating low uptake in this high-risk population. Readily available information on individuals' age and influenza vaccination history may help identify individuals at increased risk of remaining unvaccinated, thereby informing targeted strategies to improve coverage and reduce COVID-19-related morbidity.

articles.title: Incidence, risk factors, and association with vaccination of thrombocytopenia and immune thrombocytopenia (ITP): A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Brighton Collaboration published its standard harmonized case definition for thrombocytopenia in 2007 to facilitate collection of valid and reproducible vaccine safety evidence and enable valid comparisons across studies. A companion guide to this case definition (including background incidence, risk factors, evidence for or against an association with vaccination, medical codes, data collection forms, and algorithms to support level of diagnostic certainty assessment) was initially published in 2021 and updated in 2025 based on a formal scoping review. This article reports the results of this scoping review, summarizing current evidence regarding the background incidence of and risk factors for thrombocytopenia, including immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and its potential association with vaccination.

METHODS: Two PubMed searches were conducted in July 2024: one for background incidence and non-vaccine risk factors, and one for vaccine associations. Search results were screened and relevant data were extracted and added to the corresponding companion guide tables.

FINDINGS: Twenty-two articles contributed to the updated summary of background incidence, 36 articles contributed to the updated summary of non-vaccine risk factors, and 93 articles contributed to the updated summary of vaccine associations. Estimates of the background incidence of thrombocytopenia range between 1.6 and 92.1 per 100,000 person-years, depending on the study, region, and age range. Non-vaccine risk factors for thrombocytopenia include age, sex, genetics, season, geography, comorbidities, iatrogenesis, infection, medication, and food. While studies have consistently found an increased risk of ITP with measles-containing vaccines, and multiple studies found an increased risk following adenoviral COVID-19 vaccination, studies of other vaccines (including mRNA and inactivated COVID-19 vaccines) have largely found no association.

CONCLUSION: Though rare, thrombocytopenia has many risk factors, including vaccination against measles. This review should be useful to stakeholders attempting to assess the occurrence of thrombocytopenia across a variety of settings, including as an adverse event following immunization.

articles.title: Follow up immunogenicity of a mixed vaccination schedule with one dose of nonavalent and one dose of bivalent HPV vaccines 36 months post-vaccination among boys and girls.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following up on previously published short-term findings, we assessed the persistence of the immune response at 36 months following mixed-HPV vaccination schedules using one nonavalent (9vHPV) dose and one bivalent (2vHPV) dose (administered interchangeably) compared to a homologous two-dose 9vHPV schedule.

METHODS: Girls and boys aged 9-10 years were randomized (1:1) to receive (I) two doses of 9vHPV (n = 168 according-to-protocol (ATP)) or (II) a mixed schedule (n = 169 ATP) of 2vHPV + 9vHPV (n = 86) or 9vHPV + 2vHPV (n = 83) with a 6-month interval. The proportion of participants with detectable antibodies and geometric mean concentrations (GMCs) for HPV types 6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were measured using M9ELISA at 7 and 36 months after the first dose.

RESULTS: Antibodies to HPV16 and HPV18 persisted in all 337 participants (100%) at 36 months. Antibodies to the other 9vHPV-targeted types were detectable in 94-100% of participants vaccinated with a mixed schedule versus 100% for those vaccinated with a 2-dose 9vHPV schedule.
