GMCs for HPV16 and HPV18 were significantly higher in those vaccinated with a mixed schedule (9vHPV + 2vHPV and 2vHPV + 9vHPV) compared to the 9vHPV + 9vHPV schedule: 184.6 (145.5-234.3) and 151.7 (121.2-189.8) vs 97.7 (83.6-114.1) for HPV16, and 70.4 (53.5-92.7) and 72.7 (57.0-92.8) vs 40.3 (34.9-46.6) for HPV18. Additionally, the 9vHPV + 2vHPV mixed schedule resulted in higher GMCs when compared to the 2vHPV + 9vHPV schedule. GMC ratios (homologous/mixed schedules) decreased for HPV types not included in the bivalent vaccine, indicating that differences observed at 7 months were reduced at 36 months. Sex-stratified analyses showed no substantial differences between boys and girls.

CONCLUSION: Serological responses of mixed-HPV vaccination schedules are sustained for at least 36 months post-vaccination and comparable to a 2-dose 9vHPV schedule, for HPV16/18. These findings provide immunogenicity evidence supporting the feasibility of mixed 2-dose HPV schedules, while further research on clinical effectiveness and implementation is needed to inform policy decisions.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02567955).

articles.title: [Validity of the use of bioimpedance in the assessment of body composition in children and adolescents: a systematic review].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) is a non-invasive technique that estimates different body compartments, including fat mass, fat-free mass and total body water, and may complement traditional anthropometric measures. This review aimed to summarise the available evidence on the validity of BIA for assessing body composition in children and adolescents and to identify factors influencing its performance.

METHODS: A systematic review of diagnostic methods was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items in Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) recommendations. PubMed, EMBASE and the Cochrane Library were searched in February 2025 for studies published between 2010 and 2024. Validation studies in participants younger than eighteen years comparing BIA with reference methods, such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), isotope dilution, air-displacement plethysmography or multicomponent models, were included. Two reviewers independently screened records and full texts and extracted relevant information. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2, and findings were narratively synthesised.

RESULTS: Fifty-six studies were included; across fifty-three studies with quantifiable sample sizes, approximately 11,100 participants were evaluated. Reported correlations ranged widely (r=0.03-0.98), being higher when population-specific equations were derived in similar cohorts and lower in obesity, young athletes, infants and clinically complex groups, particularly when generic manufacturer equations were applied. Agreement analyses frequently showed clinically relevant individual discrepancies. In overweight/obesity, BIA tended to underestimate fat mass/%body fat and to overestimate fat-free mass. Reliability was high (ICC: approximately 0.93-0.98).

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence supports BIA as a non-invasive, reproducible and reliable tool, useful for group-level assessment, surveillance and, in particular, longitudinal monitoring of body composition in paediatric populations. It does not replace body mass index or reference methods, and its performance depends critically on the device, the equation applied and the clinical context; therefore, caution is warranted at the extremes of body composition, where population-specific equations are recommended. Nevertheless, given its feasibility and capacity to track change over time, BIA may provide complementary information on body composition and contribute to a more health- and cardiometabolic risk-oriented approach to obesity in children and adolescents when results are appropriately interpreted and communicated.

articles.title: Family Screening and Disease Predictors in Gene-Elusive Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family screening is recommended in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), but risk stratification of relatives of probands without pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (gene-elusive) remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to define the incidence, prognosis, and predictors of disease development in first-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands.

METHODS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands from 4 international referral centers who underwent baseline electrocardiography and echocardiography were included. The primary outcome was the development of the disease, defined as DCM or isolated left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction (LV ejection fraction: <50%). Major adverse cardiac events were exploratory secondary outcomes. Age-adjusted Cox models with family-clustered robust standard errors were used to identify disease predictors.

RESULTS: Among 292 relatives (median age: 36 years, 48% male), 14 (5%) were affected at baseline. During a median follow-up of 52 months, 21 additional relatives developed disease, corresponding to an incidence rate of 17 per 1,000 person-years. Familial DCM (HR: 4.24; 95% CI: 1.38-13.1; P = 0.012), QRS duration >120 ms (HR: 7.24; 95% CI: 2.25-23.3; P < 0.001), lower LV ejection fraction (HR: 3.73; 95% CI: 2.46-5.65; P < 0.001), and LV dilatation (HR: 6.19; 95% CI: 2.27-16.9; P < 0.001) were predictors of disease development. Age at diagnosis in probands significantly correlated with age at onset in relatives (r = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.55-0.92; P < 0.001). Major adverse cardiac events occurred in 9 patients (4%).

CONCLUSIONS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands have a relatively low but non-negligible risk of disease development. Familial clustering, electrocardiographic or echocardiographic abnormalities, and age of disease expression in the proband may help tailor surveillance intensity.

articles.title: The Halo Sign on Cardiac MRI in Recurrent Pericarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pericarditis can be difficult to manage. We describe the halo sign, a circumferential or regional rim of increased pericardial signal on T2-weighted imaging and/or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), and its evolution during rilonacept therapy.

CASE SUMMARY: Three patients with idiopathic, postcardiac injury, and autoimmune recurrent pericarditis underwent serial cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Baseline CMR demonstrated the halo sign with concurrent edema and LGE. Edema resolved with near-complete LGE regression in the idiopathic and postcardiac injury cases, permitting therapy discontinuation without recurrence. The autoimmune case showed persistent edema and LGE at 1 year, with improvement by 2 years.

DISCUSSION: Serial CMR demonstrated treatment response. Concurrent edema and LGE suggested active inflammation, whereas isolated LGE may reflect chronic inflammatory remodeling, neovascularization and/or fibrosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: The halo sign provides a simple descriptive framework for pericardial inflammation. Serial CMR, integrated with clinical findings and biomarkers, may distinguish active inflammation from chronic inflammatory remodeling and guide individualized therapy.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk profile and treatment patterns in patients with type 2 diabetes in specialized cardiology outpatient care in Colombia: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is strongly associated with cardiovascular morbidity, yet real-world evidence integrating cardiovascular comorbidities, metabolic characteristics, echocardiographic findings, and treatment patterns remains limited in Colombia. This study characterized the cardiovascular profile and treatment patterns of patients with T2DM attending specialized cardiology care and explored factors associated with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) >7%. A single-center, retrospective cross-sectional study included 138 adults with confirmed T2DM attending a high-complexity cardiology outpatient clinic in Barranquilla, Colombia, during 2023 to 2024. Patients were classified as HbA1c ≤7% or >7% using the most recent value documented at the latest outpatient visit. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and prescribed medication variables were evaluated. Univariable analyses were followed by an exploratory multivariable logistic regression model using the enter method. Mean age was 67.3 ± 11.5 years, 71.7% were male, and 70.3% had HbA1c >7%. Patients with HbA1c >7% were older (68.6 ± 11.6 vs 64.2 ± 10.9 years; P = .034) and had higher total cholesterol (203.5 ± 48.1 vs 181.7 ± 42.8 mg/dL; P = .010) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (124.9 ± 36.1 vs 106.0 ± 39.1 mg/dL; P = .010). Cerebrovascular disease occurred in 11.3% of patients with HbA1c >7% and none with HbA1c ≤7% (P = .034). The absence of prespecified echocardiographic abnormalities was less frequent with HbA1c >7% (15.5% vs 34.1%; P = .014). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was documented in 16.7% overall and was more frequent with HbA1c ≤7% (26.8% vs 12.4%; P = .037). In the exploratory multivariable model, total cholesterol was associated with HbA1c >7% (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per 10 mg/dL = 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.20; P = .033), whereas the absence of prespecified echocardiographic abnormalities was inversely associated (adjusted OR = 0.36; 95% CI, 0.15-0.88; P = .026). SGLT2 inhibitor use was not significant after adjustment (adjusted OR = 0.56; 95% CI, 0.20-1.58; P = .274). In this Colombian real-world cohort, HbA1c >7% was common. Higher total cholesterol was positively associated with HbA1c >7%, whereas the absence of prespecified echocardiographic abnormalities was inversely associated with this outcome. The association with SGLT2 inhibitor use did not persist after adjustment. These cross-sectional findings support integrated cardiometabolic assessment in specialized outpatient care.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH): A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) are increasingly prevalent liver diseases closely linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and cardiometabolic risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve hepatic and metabolic outcomes through weight reduction, improved glycemic control, and reductions in hepatic steatosis. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RAs in adults with MASLD or MASH.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for English-language studies published between January 2019 and December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with MASLD or MASH treated with GLP-1 RAs and reporting hepatic, metabolic, or safety outcomes. Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Nine studies involving 795 participants were included. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with significant reductions in liver fat content (mean difference [MD]: -3.17; 95% CI: -4.06 to -2.29), body weight (MD: -4.68; 95% CI: -6.88 to -2.47), alanine aminotransferase (MD: -15.17; 95% CI: -21.29 to -9.05), aspartate aminotransferase (MD: -9.89; 95% CI: -13.65 to -6.13), and HbA1c (MD: -0.78; 95% CI: -1.07 to -0.49). Adverse events were more frequent with GLP-1 RAs, particularly nausea and vomiting, while serious adverse events did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RAs are associated with meaningful improvements in hepatic steatosis, liver enzymes, body weight, and glycemic control in patients with MASLD or MASH. These findings support their potential role, particularly in patients with coexisting obesity or type 2 diabetes. However, further long-term, adequately powered trials are needed to clarify their effects on fibrosis regression, histological outcomes, and liver-related clinical events.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of risk factors for oral frailty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral frailty can lead to complications such as eating disorders and sarcopenia, thereby significantly impairing patients' health. While numerous studies have been conducted to identify risk factors for oral frailty, the results remain inconsistent due to variability in study populations, and certain risk factors remain controversial.

METHODS: Eight databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI (China National Knowledge Infrastructure), VIP (China Science and Technology Journal Database), CBM (China Biology Medicine disc), and Wanfang Databases, were thoroughly searched from database inception to August 1, 2024 to identify studies reporting risk factors for oral frailty. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using RevMan 5.4 to identify variables influencing the incidence of oral frailty.

RESULTS: A total of 14 studies involving 12,297 participants were included, among whom 4540 presented with oral frailty. Forty risk factors were extracted from these studies.Among them, 10 risk factors were eligible for meta-analysis, whereas the remaining 30 were excluded from the analysis due to being reported in fewer than 3 studies. The meta-analysis revealed that nine of the ten risk factors, namely age, gender, smoking, denture use, xerostomia, low oral health awareness, malnutrition, unbalanced diet, and physical frailty, were significantly associated with oral frailty.

CONCLUSION: This study identified risk factors for oral frailty and validated several factors already included in existing assessment scales, such as the use of dentures and xerostomia. Additionally, novel factors such as gender and age were identified. Taken together, these results may assist in the timely identification of individuals at risk for oral frailty and prevent its onset, as well as enhance current risk assessment tools.

articles.title: Minocycline in acute stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and trial sequential analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minocycline has emerged as a potential adjunctive neuroprotective therapy in acute stroke owing to its anti-inflammatory, antiapoptotic, and blood-brain barrier-stabilizing effects. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and selected safety-related outcomes of minocycline in acute stroke, including ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Major databases were searched through March 20, 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing minocycline with control or standard care in acute stroke. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were pooled with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using ROB 2, certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation, and robustness using trial sequential analysis.

RESULTS: Nine trials including 2186 participants were analyzed. Minocycline significantly reduced 3-month National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale scores in acute ischemic stroke (mean difference -2.43, 95% CI -4.42--0.44; P = .0169), but not in intracerebral hemorrhage. Functional independence at 3 months showed a favorable signal in ischemic stroke (modified rankin scale 0 to 2: risk ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.05-1.86; P = .0219), while favorable outcome defined as modified rankin scale 0 to 1 was not significantly improved. Barthel Index also favored minocycline in ischemic stroke, although overall results were not statistically significant. Mortality, recurrent vascular events, hemorrhagic transformation, hematoma volume, perihematomal edema, and Matrix Metalloproteinase-9levels were not significantly altered. Trial sequential analysis indicated insufficient evidence for definitive conclusions.

CONCLUSION: Minocycline may improve neurological recovery in acute ischemic stroke; however, these findings remain exploratory because of substantial heterogeneity, low-certainty evidence, and inconclusive trial sequential analysis. Larger standardized trials are required.

articles.title: Trends in mortality involving atrial fibrillation/flutter and renal failure in the United States, 1999-2023: A nationwide multiple-cause-of-death analysis.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF)/flutter and renal dysfunction commonly coexist and are associated with substantial cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk. Despite this clinical overlap, national mortality patterns among individuals whose death certificates record both conditions have not been well characterized over an extended period. We examined changes over time in deaths documenting both AF/flutter and renal failure and assessed whether these patterns differed across demographic and geographic groups among U.S. adults aged ≥ 45 years from 1999 to 2023. We queried the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple-Cause-of-Death database for death certificates of U.S. adults aged ≥ 45 years in which AF/flutter (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision I48) and renal failure (N17-N19) were both recorded. Either diagnosis could appear as the underlying or a contributing cause of death. Mortality rates were age-standardized to the 2000 U.S. population and expressed per 100,000 persons. Joinpoint regression was used to evaluate changes in annual age-adjusted mortality rates and to estimate annual percentage changes (APCs). The study included 392,927 death certificates meeting these criteria. The age-adjusted mortality rate increased from 6.3 per 100,000 in 1999 to 20.6 per 100,000 in 2023. Significant upward trends occurred during 1999 to 2012 (APC, 6.21%) and 2015 to 2023 (APC, 9.62%). Rates were higher among men than women throughout the study period. In 2023, the age-adjusted mortality rate was 22.55 per 100,000 among non-Hispanic White individuals, 19.91 among non-Hispanic Black or African American individuals, 14.31 among non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native individuals, 11.75 among Hispanic or Latino individuals, and 10.28 among non-Hispanic Asian or Pacific Islander individuals. The age-adjusted mortality rate for deaths documenting both AF/flutter and renal failure increased markedly among U.S. adults aged ≥ 45 years between 1999 and 2023. The magnitude of this mortality pattern differed by sex, race/ethnicity, and geographic location. Because the analysis is based on diagnoses documented on death certificates, the findings reflect population-level co-documentation of the 2 conditions and do not establish that either condition, alone or in combination, directly caused death. Individual-level studies are needed to determine the clinical and healthcare factors associated with these trends.

articles.title: Machine learning based predictive model for cardiovascular disease mortality risk in patients with stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.
articles.abstract: Patients with stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome are exposed to an elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality risk. However, large-sample, multidimensional prediction models for CVD mortality risk that integrate clinical indicators, as well as highly applicable supporting tools, remain lacking. A total of 2893 patients with stage 4 CKM were randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. The prediction model was constructed via variable screening using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator combined with multivariate Cox regression. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility of the model were evaluated with receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. A nomogram and web-based calculator were constructed. Six machine learning models were used to validate the model, and predictive factors were identified via SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis. Nine risk factors were ultimately identified for constructing the predictive model: age, gender, mobility difficulty, chronic kidney disease, anemia, neutrophil, blood urea nitrogen, albumin, and C-reactive protein. The model's discriminate ability on training set (C-index = 0.773) was comparable that on validation set (C-index = 0.779). Additionally, the model exhibited optimal performance in predicting 15-year CVD mortality (area under the curve = 0.871). The calibration curve demonstrated comparable fit, and decision curve analysis revealed that the nomogram score provided higher clinical benefit compared with any single variable. Participants with high nomogram scores exhibited a lower survival rate (log-rank test, P < .001). Among the 6 machine learning models, Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the best performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis further indicated that age and C-reactive protein made the greatest contributions to predicting CVD mortality risk. The CVD mortality risk prediction model developed for patients with stage 4 CKM demonstrated robust performance. This model may enable clinicians to identify high-risk patients early and to formulate individualized intervention strategies through a reliable decision support tool.

articles.title: Quality of Douyin videos on childhood asthma: A cross-sectional content analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the information quality of childhood asthma-related videos on the Douyin (China-market counterpart of international TikTok) short-video platform. On June 1, 2025 (Beijing time, logged-out, and non-personalized account context), we searched Douyin using the Chinese search term "," selecting the top 200 videos and ultimately including 175 videos for quality evaluation. Structured content integrity assessment tools and an instrument for judging the quality of written consumer health information on treatment choices (DISCERN) were used. The correlation between video quality and characteristics (duration, likes, comments, and shares) was analyzed. Two independent investigators performed title-and-content screening with predefined operational exclusion criteria. Inter-rater reliability was calculated before consensus adjudication. Most childhood asthma videos were created by self-identified health professionals. Content integrity scores were as follows: definition (0.325 ± 0.21), symptoms (0.521 ± 0.32), risk factors (0.294 ± 0.50), evaluation (0.425 ± 0.45), management (1.24 ± 0.47), and outcomes (0.864 ± 0.38). Among evaluated videos, 160 (91.4%) had a DISCERN score ≤50. Given that DISCERN was developed for written health information and has not been formally validated for short-form video, categorical labels ("fair," "poor," and "very poor") are interpreted descriptively only. No significant differences in DISCERN dimension scores were found across 3 sorting criteria. Duration-stratified analyses within the final n = 175 dataset showed that videos with 60 to 300 seconds exhibited higher DISCERN information-reliability and overall-quality scores compared with videos ≤60 seconds; the >300 seconds stratum contained only 4 videos, and only descriptive statistics are reported for this subgroup. Top-ranked subgroup analyses were subsets sampled from the primary 175-video dataset rather than independent samples. Our analysis reveals that the quality of the sampled set of childhood-asthma-related videos retrieved from Douyin is suboptimal and lacks comprehensive information; findings cannot be generalized to all childhood-asthma-related content hosted on this platform. These findings reflect content-level deficits rather than inherent hazards of the Douyin platform.

articles.title: The role of sexual mindfulness in enhancing sexual well-being among breast cancer survivors: A randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with a wide range of sexual disorders are vulnerable to negative sexual well-being due to complications from breast cancer treatment. This study aimed to investigate the impact of sexual mindfulness-based training on the sexual well-being of women with breast cancer.

METHODS: This randomized clinical trial was conducted in 2024 and involved a statistical population of women with breast cancer who had consulted comprehensive health service centers in Shahrekord, Iran. Among the referring women, 36 people were selected by convenience sampling. To investigate depression in the participants, the short-form Beck Depression Questionnaire was used, and 4 patients were excluded from the study due to severe depression. Then, the participants were randomly assigned to 2 study groups of 16 patients.Sexual mindfulness training was conducted in 8 sessions (90 minutes, once a week) for the intervention group at the reproductive and sexual health clinic in Shahrekord. Meanwhile, the control group was not subjected to planned intervention or training. A sexual well-being questionnaire was used to collect data for repeated measures analysis. Both groups were asked to complete the sexual well-being questionnaire before, immediately after, and 3 months after the intervention. Data were analyzed through independent samples T-test, analysis of covariance, and repeated measures analysis.

RESULTS: The findings showed that there was no significant difference in sexual well-being between the intervention and control groups before the intervention (P = .29). Immediately after the intervention, sexual well-being significantly increased in the intervention group, from 39.33 ± 25.56 to 56.17 ± 22.29 (P < .001); however, the corresponding between-group comparison was not statistically significant (P = .11). Three months after the intervention, sexual well-being was significantly higher in the intervention group (66.42 ± 13.79) than in the control group (51.92 ± 20.62; P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Sexual Mindfulness can be considered a therapeutic method in palliative care to improve sexual well-being in breast cancer patients.

articles.title: Retrospective evaluation of predictors and clinical impact of postoperative delirium in liver transplant recipients.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiology, predictors, and clinical outcomes of postoperative delirium (POD) in liver transplant (LT) recipients. Clinical data from 427 LT recipients from the Third Xiangya Hospital were retrospectively reviewed. The epidemiology (incidence, onset, and duration), predictors, and associated clinical outcomes of POD were analyzed using standardized delirium assessment tools and multivariate regression. POD occurred in 19.0% of recipients, with a median onset at 26.0 hours posttransplant. Multivariate analysis identified 4 independent pre and postoperative predictors, including a higher model for end-stage liver disease score and hepatic encephalopathy within 24 hours before LT, infection within 2 months prior to LT, and abnormal sodium within 1 hour after LT (all P < .05). In a sensitivity analysis treating early death or persistent coma as a composite outcome with POD (n = 436), the same 4 independent predictors were identified, with consistent effect estimates. Regarding clinical outcomes, POD was significantly associated with prolonged intensive care unit stays, extended mechanical ventilation requirements, and increased use of renal replacement therapy (all P < .01). Although recipients with POD showed higher 1- and 6-month all-cause mortality in unadjusted analyses, POD was not an independent predictor of mortality after adjustment for confounding factors. POD occurs frequently and early after LT, with identifiable pre and postoperative risk factors. While POD markedly increases perioperative morbidity and resource utilization, it does not independently predict short-term all-cause mortality in this cohort.

articles.title: Neonatal nemaline myopathy associated with NEB variants and a favorable 3-year outcome: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Nemaline myopathy (NM) is a rare congenital myopathy characterized by muscle weakness and hypotonia. Severe neonatal disease may involve respiratory failure and bulbar dysfunction. Variants in the nebulin gene (NEB) are a common genetic cause, but genotype-phenotype relationships and prognosis remain variable.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A female neonate developed cyanosis, bradycardia, respiratory distress, and hypotonia shortly after birth. She required invasive mechanical ventilation and later experienced recurrent respiratory deterioration, difficulty weaning from ventilatory support, poor feeding, vomiting and choking, weak sucking and swallowing, and diminished primitive reflexes.

DIAGNOSES: The clinical phenotype and trio whole-exome sequencing findings supported a clinical diagnosis of NM associated with NEB variants. Sequencing identified a maternally inherited pathogenic frameshift variant, c.23910_23911delAG (p.Arg7970SerfsTer9), and 2 missense variants classified as variants of uncertain significance: maternally inherited c.5615C>T (p.Pro1872Leu) and paternally inherited c.19550G>A (p.Arg6517His). Muscle biopsy, allelic phasing, and functional studies were unavailable; therefore, the molecular diagnosis was not definitive.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received invasive and noninvasive respiratory support, oxygen therapy, feeding and symptomatic management, serial neurological assessments, and neurological rehabilitation.

OUTCOMES: The Neonatal Behavioral Neurological Assessment score increased from 25 on day 7 to 30 on day 14 and 36 on day 28. Respiratory function, feeding, and muscle tone gradually improved, allowing respiratory support to be withdrawn. Denver Developmental Screening Test assessments performed at 6-month intervals after discharge identified no reported developmental abnormalities. At 3 years of age, no apparent hypotonia, movement disorder, or other clinically evident motor impairment was observed.

LESSONS: Neonatal NM associated with NEB variants may present with life-threatening respiratory and bulbar dysfunction yet be followed by a favorable early developmental course. Trio whole-exome sequencing may facilitate etiological evaluation, but NEB variants require cautious interpretation when histopathological, phasing, and functional evidence is unavailable. A severe neonatal presentation should not be regarded as indicating an invariably poor prognosis, and continued neuromuscular, respiratory, feeding, orthopedic, and developmental surveillance remains warranted.

articles.title: Identification of genetically supported candidate therapeutic targets for angina pectoris using mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract: Angina pectoris is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome that may reflect obstructive coronary atherosclerosis, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular dysfunction, or myocardial oxygen supply-demand imbalance. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to prioritize circulating proteins that may influence the broad risk of angina while distinguishing atherosclerosis-related pathways from other potential mechanisms. This study aimed to identify genetically supported candidate therapeutic targets for angina pectoris and characterize the relative strength and potential mechanisms of the evidence supporting each candidate. The primary analysis combined European cis-protein quantitative trait locus instruments with a broad genome-wide association study -defined angina phenotype. Steiger testing, Bayesian co-localization, phenotypic scanning, external validation, supplementary European trans- protein quantitative trait locus and Asian-ancestry analyses, phenotype-stratified MR, two-step mediation MR, enrichment analysis, bulk RNA-seq, protein-protein interaction analysis, and exploratory single-cell transcriptomic analyses were used to evaluate robustness and biological context. Seven protein-angina associations met the primary Bonferroni threshold; 6 proteins (LPA, TMEM106B, APOA5, TIRAP, PCSK9, and SWAP70) were retained after TGFB1 failed Steiger filtering. Independent external MR supported LPA in UK Biobank and LPA, PCSK9, and APOA5 in FinnGen. Phenotype-stratified analyses generally supported associations across stable angina, unstable angina, coronary artery disease, and myocardial infarction, although instrument availability and the strength of evidence differed among proteins. Two-step MR supported indirect pathways through coronary artery calcification for LPA, through LDL cholesterol for PCSK9, and through triglycerides for APOA5, but not through C-reactive protein for TIRAP. Exploratory single-cell analyses localized TMEM106B, TIRAP, and SWAP70 to relevant vascular and immune cell populations and provided limited, context-dependent functional support. LPA, PCSK9, and APOA5 have the strongest convergent genetic and external-replication evidence and appear to influence angina risk predominantly through atherosclerotic lipid-related pathways. TMEM106B, TIRAP, and SWAP70 remain potentially novel, genetically supported candidates with exploratory cellular evidence but without direct experimental validation. These candidates should not be considered established therapeutic targets until proteomic, functional, rescue, and clinical studies are completed.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of common adjuvant treatments after resection of colorectal liver metastases: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although adjuvant strategies such as systemic chemotherapy, regional nonsystemic chemotherapy, and ablation have been applied, the optimal adjuvant therapeutic strategy for resectable colorectal liver metastases remains uncertain in terms of overall survival and disease-free survival. This network meta-analysis aimed to determine the optimal adjuvant therapeutic strategy for patients with colorectal liver metastases.

METHODS: We searched potentially eligible studies in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure databases until July 2026. Pooled disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using R software.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies including 18 reports were included. For the DFS, except for adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (CT, HAIC) concomitant with intravenous CT, adjuvant CT and perioperative CT significantly improved DFS compared with surgery and adjuvant HAIC. There was no statistical difference between all therapeutic strategies for OS. Adjuvant HAIC concomitant with intravenous CT had the highest probability of being the best treatment for improving DFS (85.01%), followed by perioperative CT (11.75%) and adjuvant CT (3.17%); however, adjuvant HAIC concomitant with intravenous CT had the highest probability of being the best adjuvant treatment for improving OS (52.46%), followed by perioperative CT (40.25%) and adjuvant HAIC (5.25%).

CONCLUSION: Adjuvant CT may be the best for improving DFS, but perioperative CT may be the best for improving OS. However, the results should be validated further.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and 30-day unplanned cirrhosis readmissions: A nationwide Readmissions Database retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: 30-day unplanned readmissions after hospitalization for liver cirrhosis are common. Acute kidney injury (AKI) may be associated with higher early readmission risk. Using the Nationwide Readmissions Database 2016 to 2017, we identified adults with an index cirrhosis admission from January through November by International Classification of Diseases Tenth Revision Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. AKI was defined by N17.x during the index stay. Unplanned 30-day readmissions were identified after excluding planned readmissions and trauma-related hospitalizations. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for patient, clinical, and hospital factors. Among 1,68,816 index admissions, AKI occurred in 25.6%. Overall, 25.0% had unplanned 30-day readmission, higher with AKI than without (26.0% vs 24.2%; absolute difference 1.8 percentage points). AKI was independently associated with readmission (adjusted odds ratio 1.10, 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.16). AKI admissions had longer length of stay (median 6 vs 4 days), higher inflation-adjusted charges ($58,507 vs $32,587), and nonhome discharge (34% vs 16%; all P < .001). Readmissions occurred at a median of 12 days and had 7.72% in hospital mortality. Ascites and chronic kidney disease were strong predictors. AKI was associated with readmission among patients without chronic kidney disease but not among those with it (interaction P < .001). AKI during the index admission was associated with unplanned 30-day readmission, although the association was modest in magnitude, and marked a high-risk cirrhosis population with greater resource use. Because of the observational, retrospective design, causality cannot be established.

articles.title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of mortality in ICU patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure frequently coexist, and the mortality risk for patients with these comorbidities is significantly elevated in the intensive care unit (ICU) setting. Therefore, developing an interpretable model for early mortality prediction is crucial to improving the prognosis and management of these patients. This study developed models based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (3167 patients) and performed external validation using the eICU Collaborative Research Database (1781 patients). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression combined with the Boruta algorithm was used to screen clinical features within the first 24 hours of ICU admission. Based on the selected features, 5 machine learning models (eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Categorical Boosting, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine) were constructed and compared for their performance in predicting 28-day all-cause mortality. The optimal model was interpreted using the Shapley Additive Explanations framework. In internal validation, the Categorical Boosting model demonstrated the best overall performance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.788, with a sensitivity of 0.482 and a specificity of 0.900. In independent external validation, the model's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.739. Feature selection identified 14 key predictive variables. Shapley Additive Explanations analysis revealed that the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, Simplified Acute Physiology Score II score, anion gap, vasopressor use, and respiratory rate were the top 5 features contributing most to the model's predictions. This study developed and validated an interpretable machine learning model based on multicenter data for the early prediction of 28-day mortality risk in ICU patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure. The model demonstrates good discriminative ability and reasonable generalizability, with its interpretability analysis clarifying core predictive factors to aid in clinical risk stratification and intervention.

articles.title: Combined and simultaneous use of Nefecon and irbesartan in treatment-naïve primary IgA nephropathy: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Nefecon is a targeted-release formulation of the corticosteroid budesonide. It is specifically engineered to selectively target the ileal gut-associated lymphoid tissue to reduce galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) production and IgA immune complex formation. Irbesartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker that is widely used to reduce proteinuria in chronic kidney disease. The study aimed to investigate the effects of the concomitant administration of both drugs in treatment-naïve patients with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN). We conducted a retrospective study of 12 patients with primary IgAN at a single institution who received a 6-month combination therapy with Nefecon and irbesartan. Irbesartan was administered at a fixed dose of 150 mg/day, and Nefecon was given at a dosage of 16 mg/day. Treatment effectiveness was assessed by evaluating the alterations in 24-hour urinary protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). We measured the levels of Gd-IgA1 and analyzed the correlations between Gd-IgA1 and clinical outcomes. Linear mixed models assessed urinary protein, albumin, creatinine, and eGFR over time. Estimated mean urinary protein reductions from baseline were -28.28% (1 month), -32.78% (3 months), and -51.46% (6 months) (P < .001). eGFR was stable at 1 month (+4.08 mL/min/1.73 m2) but rose significantly at 3 months (+10.40) and 6 months (+8.80) (P = .009). Gd-IgA1 levels before and 1 month after treatment were 15.81 ± 1.43 and 15.16 ± 1.71 U/mL. Changes in Gd-IgA1 at 1 month correlated with changes in urinary protein (r = 0.664, P = .018). Urinary dysmorphic red blood cells decreased from 108.5 (37.5, 308.8) to 14 (6, 74.2) cells/μL at 6 months (P = .012). In treatment-naïve patients with primary IgAN, combined use of Nefecon and irbesartan was associated with reduced proteinuria and stable kidney function. However, given the single-arm design, these changes cannot be attributed to the combination itself and may reflect the effects of either agent alone, natural fluctuation of proteinuria, or regression to the mean. Although early changes in Gd-IgA1 correlated with reduced proteinuria, this exploratory finding requires confirmation. In addition, subgroup findings - such as the sex-based difference in proteinuria reduction - are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. These retrospective observational findings require confirmation in adequately powered controlled studies.

articles.title: The overall effects of virtual reality interventions on ICU patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients frequently experience psychological distress, pain, sleep disruption, and motor impairments. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising nonpharmacological adjunct to improve these outcomes, yet existing evidence remains fragmented and inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized recent clinical trials to evaluate the effectiveness of VR on mental health, pain, sleep, functional outcomes, and delirium in adult ICU patients.

METHODS: This review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (2020) guidance and was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42023482529). Eight databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published between January 2000 and September 2025. Eligible studies included adult ICU patients receiving immersive or non-immersive VR interventions. Primary outcomes were anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); secondary outcomes included pain, sleep quality, lower-limb function, and bedside balance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB tool, and certainty of evidence was graded using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Twenty randomized controlled trials were identified, involving a total of 1551 patients. This meta-analysis showed that VR intervention helped improve anxiety (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI: -1.00 to -0.35], P < .0001), depression (SMD = -0.46, 95% CI [-0.72 to -0.21], P = .0004), PTSD [mean difference = -5.48, 95% CI (-9.36 to -1.59), P = .006], lower-limb function score [mean difference = 2.83, 95% CI (1.99 to 3.67), P < .001] and sleep quality (SMD = 0.70, 95% CI [0.47 to 0.92], P < .0001), but had no significant effect on pain score (SMD = -0.57, 95% CI [-1.49 to 0.36], P = .23) and bedside balance score (SMD = 0.61, 95% CI [-0.44 to 1.66], P = .25). Most studies were assessed as having varying degrees of risk of bias. All evidence was rated from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSION: VR interventions may confer meaningful benefits for anxiety, depression, PTSD, and sleep quality in adult ICU patients, and may improve lower-limb function in selected populations. However, evidence for analgesic effects and bedside balance remains inconclusive. Standardized VR protocols, objective outcome assessment, and adequately powered multicenter trials are needed to clarify the clinical value of VR in ICU care.

articles.title: Central retinal artery occlusion preceding hemispheric ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of ischemic stroke that may signal underlying cerebrovascular or cardiac disease.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 52-year-old man developed sudden, painless vision loss in the right eye. Nine days later, he presented with left-sided weakness and speech difficulty, with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. His medical history included dilated cardiomyopathy, and electrocardiography revealed atrial fibrillation.

DIAGNOSES: Ophthalmologic examination and fluorescein angiography supported right CRAO. Computed tomography (CT) angiography at neurological presentation showed right internal carotid artery occlusion from its origin. CT perfusion demonstrated estimated infarct core and penumbral volumes of 37 and 186 mL, respectively.

INTERVENTIONS: Emergency mechanical thrombectomy with aspiration and adjunctive balloon angioplasty achieved expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade 2c reperfusion.

OUTCOMES: The NIHSS score improved to 2 at discharge, 7 days after admission. At 3 months, the modified Rankin Scale score was 1, although right-eye visual loss persisted.

LESSONS: CRAO warrants prompt cerebrovascular and cardiac evaluation, with reassessment when new neurological deficits develop. The nine-day interval between retinal symptoms and thrombectomy does not establish the duration of carotid occlusion or cerebral ischemia. The favorable individual outcome does not establish the efficacy of thrombectomy beyond 24 hours.

articles.title: Causal effects of educational attainment on respiratory diseases: A Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to assess the causal relationship between educational attainment and respiratory diseases using Mendelian randomization (MR). Datasets of educational attainment were obtained from the European Bioinformatics Institute and screened for genetic variants strongly associated with educational attainment according to the underlying assumptions of MR. Subsequently, the effect of these genetic variants on the risk of respiratory diseases was assessed using the inverse variance weighted method as the primary method of MR analysis, with MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode as secondary methods. Finally, MR-Egger intercept analysis, Cochran's Q test and sensitivity analysis were used to assess the horizontal pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and robustness of the results of the MR analyses, respectively. MR analysis provided genetic evidence consistent with a modest protective effect of higher educational attainment on the risks of bronchitis (odds ratio [OR] 0.962, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.949-0.975, P < .001), pneumonia (OR 0.966, 95% CI 0.953-0.979, P < .001), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (OR 0.896, 95% CI 0.873-0.919, P < .001), non-small cell lung cancer (OR 0.909, 95% CI 0.871-0.948, P < .001), and pulmonary embolism (OR 0.950, 95% CI 0.922-0.980, P < .001). MR-Egger intercept analyses provided no evidence of horizontal pleiotropy, and sensitivity analyses indicated that the results were robust. Higher educational attainment may have a protective effect against bronchitis, pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, non-small cell lung cancer, and pulmonary embolism, with genetic evidence consistent with a modest reduction in disease risk.

articles.title: Effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength and functional outcomes in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subacromial pain syndrome (SAPS) is one of the most common causes of shoulder pain and is frequently associated with rotator cuff dysfunction. Recent evidence suggests a close relationship between hand grip strength and rotator cuff muscle function, indicating that grip-strengthening exercises may enhance shoulder rehabilitation outcomes. To investigate the effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS.

METHODS: Thirty-six individuals with SAPS were randomly assigned to an experimental group (scapular stabilization exercise combined with grip strengthening; n = 18) or a control group (scapular stabilization exercise alone; n = 18). Both groups participated in exercise sessions 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index were assessed before and after the intervention.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and Shoulder Pain and Disability Index scores (P < .001). Significant Time × Group interaction effects were observed for all outcome measures (P < .001), indicating greater improvements in the experimental group.

CONCLUSIONS: Grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise may provide additional benefits for improving shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS.

articles.title: Executive dysfunction in COPD: prevalence and clinical correlates of cognitive impairment: A cross-sectional case-control study.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized, but its clinical correlates remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of mild cognitive impairment and dementia in COPD and identify associated clinical factors. In this cross-sectional case-control study, 86 patients with COPD and 61 age- and sex-matched controls aged ≥60 years were evaluated. Cognitive status was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and domain-specific cognitive tests, including the Stroop test. Clinical variables, including spirometric measures, resting oxygen saturation, dyspnea severity, and C-reactive protein, were recorded. Multivariable analysis was performed to evaluate factors associated with Stroop word-reading time. The overall distribution of cognitive status did not differ significantly between groups (P = .228). Mild cognitive impairment was numerically more frequent in the COPD group than in controls (30.2% vs 18.0%), whereas dementia rates were similar. Stroop word-reading time was significantly longer in the COPD group (P < .001). Within the COPD group, poorer cognitive performance was associated with lower resting oxygen saturation and greater dyspnea severity. In multivariable analysis, COPD status remained independently associated with longer Stroop word-reading time after adjustment for age, sex, smoking, C-reactive protein, and body mass index (B = 5.09, P = .004). Although the overall distribution of cognitive status and global cognitive screening scores did not differ significantly between groups, patients with COPD showed longer Stroop word-reading time. Lower resting oxygen saturation and greater dyspnea were associated with poorer cognitive performance within the COPD group. These findings suggest that domain-specific cognitive assessment may provide additional information beyond global cognitive screening; however, prospective studies are needed to confirm the clinical utility of these findings.

articles.title: A case report of pulmonary embolism following endoscopic cervical discectomy in an elderly patient with cervical disc herniation.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy (P-PECD) is a minimally invasive procedure for cervical spine disorders. Although it is associated with less surgical trauma and faster postoperative recovery, serious perioperative thromboembolic complications may still occur.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 65-year-old woman with cervical disc herniation, right upper limb pain, and multiple comorbidities underwent posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy after unsuccessful conservative treatment. On the 2nd postoperative day, she developed dizziness and decreased oxygen saturation. On the 3rd postoperative day, she complained of chest tightness.

DIAGNOSES: Laboratory testing revealed a markedly elevated plasma D-dimer level. Venous color Doppler ultrasound of both lower limbs demonstrated thrombosis in the bilateral calf muscular veins, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed multiple pulmonary emboli.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received oxygen therapy, continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin, and other supportive treatments. She was transferred to the intensive care unit for further monitoring and management.

OUTCOMES: The patient's respiratory and circulatory status gradually stabilized, and her chest tightness and dizziness resolved. She was subsequently transferred back to the pain ward and discharged in stable condition.

LESSONS: This case highlights that minimally invasive spinal surgery does not eliminate the risk of perioperative venous thromboembolism. Comprehensive preoperative thrombotic risk assessment, individualized perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy, appropriate thromboprophylaxis, early mobilization, and timely recognition and treatment of suspected APE are important for improving perioperative safety.

articles.title: Effect of Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet on cancer-related fatigue in anemic colon cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: A randomized controlled trial (CONSORT-compliant).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is one of the most common and distressing symptoms experienced by patients undergoing chemotherapy, and no gold standard for the treatment of CRF has been established. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet on CRF in patients with chemotherapy-induced anemia following colon cancer surgery.

METHODS: A total of 96 patients admitted to the intestinal surgery ward and daytime chemotherapy ward of a tertiary hospital from May 2021 to December 2022 who met the inclusion criteria were selected and randomly divided into 2 groups: 48 patients in the control group and 48 in the experimental group. The control group received standard treatment and nursing care for postoperative chemotherapy for colon cancer, while the experimental group followed the control group's regimen and additionally received the Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet for 21 consecutive days. Fatigue levels, blood counts, and inflammatory factors were compared before and after the intervention in both groups.

RESULTS: A total of 86 patients completed the study. After the intervention, the CRF scores in the experimental group were significantly lower than those in the control group (29.14 ± 2.58 vs 44.02 ± 4.25), with a between-group mean difference of -14.88 (95% confidence interval [CI], -16.38 to -13.38; P < .001). Hemoglobin levels were significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (115.26 ± 11.72 vs 106.52 ± 12.93), with a mean difference of 8.74 (95% CI, 3.45-14.03; P < .001). Red blood cell counts were also higher in the experimental group (mean difference 0.61; 95% CI, 0.44-0.78; P < .001). In addition, levels of inflammatory factors were significantly reduced, with interleukin-6 showing a mean difference of -16.28 (95% CI, -20.10 to -12.46; P < .001) and tumor necrosis factor-α showing a mean difference of -26.09 (95% CI, -29.80 to -22.38; P < .001).

CONCLUSION: The Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet was associated with improvements in CRF, hematological parameters, and inflammatory markers in patients with chemotherapy-induced anemia following colon cancer surgery. These findings suggest that it may have potential as a supportive nutritional intervention for managing CRF in this population.

articles.title: Effects of sensorimotor training combined with short foot exercise on knee and ankle gait kinematics in individuals with flatfoot: A preliminary study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Flatfoot, a common condition characterized by medial longitudinal arch collapse, alters foot and lower-limb mechanics. Sensorimotor training and short-foot exercises can improve postural stability and functional performance. However, their combined effects on gait kinematics remain unclear. This preliminary study evaluated the 6-week effects of combining these interventions on knee and ankle gait kinematics in individuals with flexible flatfeet.

METHODS: Thirty-two asymptomatic young adults with flexible flatfoot (14 males, 18 females; navicular drop ≥ 10 mm) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (sensorimotor training combined with short-foot exercises; n = 16) or a control group (sensorimotor training only; n = 16) using sealed opaque envelopes. Training was conducted 3 times per week for 6 weeks in a motion laboratory. Gait kinematics were assessed pre- and post-intervention using the VICON motion system. Outcomes included peak ankle inversion, eversion, dorsiflexion, and plantarflexion angles, knee internal and external rotation angles, and range of motion (ROM) in the sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes. Two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance was used for the analysis. The partial eta squared (ηp2) was reported as the effect size.

RESULTS: Baseline demographics (age, sex, and body mass index) were similar between groups (P > .05). Significant group × time interactions were observed for gait variables. The experimental group showed a significant increase in peak ankle inversion (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.53-2.71; P = .004; ηp2 = 0.244) and a decrease in peak eversion (95% CI: 1.68-4.89; P = .002; ηp2 = 0.279). Peak knee internal rotation significantly decreased (95% CI: -9.92 to -2.82; P = .006; ηp2 = 0.228). Reductions were also observed in sagittal plane ankle ROM (95% CI: -4.88 to -0.68; P = .001; ηp2 = 0.317) and transverse plane knee ROM (95% CI: -7.75 to -4.01; P = .003; ηp2 = 0.254). No significant changes were found in ankle dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, knee external rotation, or frontal plane ankle ROM (P = .088, .126, .766, .136, respectively; ηp2 = 0.003-0.094).

CONCLUSION: Combined sensorimotor and short-foot training more effectively improved gait kinematics than sensorimotor training alone, suggesting a promising non-surgical approach for managing flatfoot.

articles.title: Total sitting time and COPD in NHANES, with genetic evidence for leisure television watching: A cross-sectional and Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Observational total sitting time and genetically proxied leisure television watching are related but non-identical sedentary phenotypes. We examined their complementary associations with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and explored smoking and C-reactive protein as potential mediators of the genetic association. We analyzed adults aged 40 years or older in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013-2018 using survey-weighted logistic regression. Total sitting time was evaluated at 480 minutes/day, continuously per 60 minutes/day, and in 5 categories. Sensitivity analyses used a more specific COPD definition requiring self-reported physician-diagnosed COPD plus current respiratory prescription medication. Complementary two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), two-step MR mediation, and multivariable MR analyses evaluated leisure television watching, leisure computer use, and driving. Among 11,343 participants, 655 reported physician-diagnosed COPD. Sitting for at least 480 minutes/day was associated with prevalent COPD after multivariable adjustment (OR, 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03-1.74). Each additional 60 minutes/day was associated with an OR of 1.06 (95% CI, 1.01-1.12), and the OR for at least 600 versus <240 minutes/day was 1.78 (95% CI, 1.06-3.01; P for trend = .032). Findings persisted after additional physical-activity adjustment and with the more specific COPD definition. Genetically predicted LTW was associated with COPD (random-effects inverse-variance weighted OR per 1-standard deviation increment, approximately 1.5 hour/day, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.66-2.30; P = 5.27 × 10-16), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 35.9%). Two-step MR suggested approximate mediated proportions of 28.0% for smoking and 5.8% for C-reactive protein. Greater total sitting time was cross-sectionally associated with prevalent self-reported COPD, while genetically proxied LTW showed a complementary association with COPD risk. The observational finding remains vulnerable to reverse causation and misclassification, and the mediation and multivariable MR findings should be regarded as supportive and approximate rather than definitive because of heterogeneity, possible pleiotropy, and unquantified conditional instrument strength.

articles.title: Kinetically controlled proton removal via bio-inspired hybrid bilayer membrane functionalized electrode for ethylene glycol oxidation to generate C2 products.
articles.abstract: As a cornerstone of the circular carbon economy, the upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) relies on efficient monomer recovery and subsequent high-value transformation. While PET can be effectively broken down into ethylene glycol (EG) via scalable depolymerization techniques such as hydrolysis, alcoholysis, or pyrolysis, the subsequent electrochemical ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EgOR) faces a significant selectivity bottleneck. This reaction is governed by complex proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathways that typically favor C-C bond cleavage, resulting in low-value C1 products like formic acid and CO2. In this work, we overcome these limitations by employing a bio-inspired hybrid bilayer membrane (HBM) functionalized electrode to exert kinetic control over the proton removal rate. By precisely modulating the electrocatalytic microenvironment at the electrode interface, the HBM suppresses over-oxidation and steers the reaction toward the targeted generation of C2 products. We demonstrate the selective production of glycolic acid, a premium chemical in the cosmetics industry with a market value exceeding 25 times that of the EG feedstock. These results establish that regulating the kinetics of proton transfer via HBM technology is a transformative strategy for controlling reaction selectivity in complex oxidation pathways. This approach offers a potentially scalable, renewable-energy-powered route for upcycling plastic waste derivatives into high-value chemical outputs, providing significant translational value for sustainable resource recovery.

articles.title: Gallium-68 and zirconium-89 complexes of DFO-analogs for molecular imaging applications using PET/CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The β+-emitters gallium-68 (68Ga) and zirconium-89 (89Zr) are among the most widely used metallic radionuclides in nuclear medicine for diagnostic imaging by Positron Emission Tomography (PET). Inspired by nature's bacterial siderophore desferrioxamine-B (DFO), a number of structurally related oligohydroxamate-based chelators have been studied for the complexation of both radiometals and for applications in nuclear medicine. We report here the solid phase (sp) synthesis of a new member of this family of acyclic chelators, DFO*sp 3, and its comparison with DFO 1 (control) and DFO-analogs DFO* 2, and oxoDFO* 4 in vitro and in vivo.

RESULTS: DFO*sp 3 and oxoDFO* 4 were synthesized efficiently on solid support by applying different protective group strategies. The [68Ga]Ga- and [89Zr]Zr-labeled chelators 1-4 were obtained with high radiochemical yield and purity. They were also found to be of favorable hydrophilicity (logP <-2,2), high stability in the media tested, and low protein binding (with the exception of [68Ga]Ga-DFO 5 and [68Ga]Ga-DFO* 6). In vivo, the radiometal complexes 5-12 showed good serum stability, fast clearance predominantly by renal excretion and low uptake in organs and tissues. In vivo PET/CT imaging confirmed the results of the ex vivo biodistribution studies, leading to the acquisition of high-quality PET/CT images with a low signal-to-noise ratio.

CONCLUSION: The excellent in vitro and in vivo characteristics of [68Ga]Ga- and [89Zr]Zr-complexes of hydroxamate-based chelators 1-4 support their use in radiopharmaceutical development and diagnostic PET-imaging applications in nuclear medicine.

articles.title: Expanding the Evidence and Indications for Thrombectomy in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

articles.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.

RESULTS: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).

CONCLUSIONS: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.

RESULTS: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
articles.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. This narrative review (PubMed/MEDLINE searched through August 2026, supplemented by hand-searching and conference abstracts) appraises the evidence for AI applications across the MPN continuum. Artificial intelligence (AI), and its principal subfields, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), learn predictive patterns directly from data rather than from explicitly programmed rules, and are increasingly suited to this multidimensional complexity. Across the MPN continuum, AI has produced substantial technical progress across several domains: automated bone marrow biopsy analysis and continuous quantification of fibrosis and megakaryocyte morphology; peripheral blood- and complete blood count-based diagnosis, including blood-based prediction of marrow fibrosis and emerging liquid-biopsy approaches; quantitative disease assessment such as spleen volume segmentation; risk stratification for survival, thrombosis, disease progression, and post-transplant outcomes; therapy response prediction; in silico drug discovery; and natural language processing for large-scale mining of electronic health records; maturity and level of validation differ markedly across these domains. External validation is increasingly reported in selected applications, though most published models to date remain confined to internal or single-cohort validation, and prospective evaluation has been reported only for blood count-based fibrosis prediction. Correspondingly, to our knowledge, no tool has yet been shown to change clinical decision-making or improve patient outcomes, and predictive performance should not be conflated with clinical utility. As multimodal data integration, foundation models, and generative approaches mature, AI has the potential to support a faster, more objective, and more personalized diagnostic and decision-making pathway in MPN.

articles.title: Influence of pathological microenvironments on mesenchymal stem/stromal cell fate: role of long non-coding RNAs in bone-related diseases.
articles.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
articles.abstract: The bidirectional relationship between pathological microenvironments and mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) is known as a pivotal factor influencing the progression of bone-related disease and therapeutic outcomes. MSCs, characterized by their remarkable plasticity and excellent immunomodulatory abilities, play central roles in various physiological and pathological processes, especially in bone regeneration and repair. Under pathological conditions, such as osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, or bone tumors, the tissue microenvironment can significantly alter MSC behavior, leading to impaired differentiation, dysregulated immune responses, or abnormal tissue remodeling. This dynamic relationship is regulated by diverse molecular signals, where long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) emerge as critical regulators of MSC biology. LncRNAs influence MSC differentiation, immunomodulatory functions, and responses to microenvironmental cues through diverse molecular mechanisms. The systematic review elucidates the roles of various lncRNAs involved in different aspects of MSC biology under pathological conditions and their potential as therapeutic targets or biomarkers for bone-related disorders.

articles.title: Structure-guided development of G protein-biased apelin receptor agonists for cardiovascular disease.
articles.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
articles.abstract: Apelin receptor (APLNR) is a crucial G protein-coupled receptor that plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis; therefore, it represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. However, the activation of APLNR simultaneously engages inhibitory G protein (Gi)-mediated protective signaling and β-arrestin pathways that are associated with pathological cardiac remodeling, thereby imposing significant limitations and challenges for the therapeutic development of conventional balanced agonists. Recent advances in structural biology and pharmacology have provided valuable mechanistic insights into receptor activation and biased signaling. High-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures revealed the conformational basis of signal bias, enabling the rational design of fully G protein-biased agonists that retain cardiovascular benefits while avoiding hypertrophic effects. This review summarizes recent progress in APLNR signaling mechanisms and biased ligand development, highlighting a number of emerging strategies for the precision pharmacological targeting of this receptor.

articles.title: [Interpretation of the Oncology Society of Chinese Medical Association guideline for clinical diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer (2026 edition)].
articles.journal: Zhonghua zhong liu za zhi [Chinese journal of oncology]
articles.abstract: To promote the standardization of clinical diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer in China and to apply the latest evidence-based medical evidence to clinical practice, since 2018, the Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine of Shanghai Chest Hospital has taken the lead, in collaboration with more than 50 lung cancer treatment institutions and over 100 experts nationwide, to jointly draft the clinical practice guidelines for lung cancer, with annual updates. The newly added recommendations are primarily based on indications approved by the National Medical Products Administration of China. To enhance the practicality of the guideline, particular emphasis has been placed on adopting clinical research data derived from Chinese patients. Recently, the Clinical Practice Guidelines for Lung Cancer of the Oncology Society of Chinese Medical Association (2026 Edition) was published. To better present the key points of the guidelines to fellow professionals, this article provides a summary interpretation based on the latest version, covering screening, pathology and treatment for early-stage operable, locally advanced unresectable, and advanced-stage patients.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on detection and clinical application of alterations in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN genes (2026 edition)].
authors: Breast Cancer Expert Committee of China Anti-Cancer Association
Society of Tumor Pathology of China Anti-Cancer Association
Breast Cancer Expert Committee of National Cancer Quality Control Center
articles.journal: Zhonghua zhong liu za zhi [Chinese journal of oncology]
articles.abstract: Breast cancer is the most common malignancy among women worldwide, with a continuously increasing incidence, posing a major public health threat to women's health. In recent years, with advances in molecular biology and innovations in diagnostic and therapeutic technologies, the management of breast cancer has evolved from histopathological classification to an era of individualized precision medicine guided by molecular characteristics. PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations represent one of the key mechanisms underlying resistance to endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and anti-HER-2 therapies in hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER-2-) breast cancer. Data from China indicate that approximately 60% of patients with breast cancer harbor genetic alterations in PI3K/AKT pathway. Multiple agents targeting these alterations have been approved domestically and internationally, including the AKT inhibitor capivasertib and the PI3K inhibitors inavolisib and alpelisib, which have significantly improved survival outcomes in patients with corresponding genomic alterations. To standardize testing procedures and guide the rational use of targeted therapies, the Breast Cancer Expert Committee of China Anti-Cancer Association, the Society of Tumor Pathology of China Anti-Cancer Association, and the Breast Cancer Expert Committee of the National Cancer Quality Control Center jointly led a multidisciplinary panel of experts from breast surgery, medical oncology, pathology, pharmacy, and related fields to develop this consensus based on systematic literature searches of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, as well as Chinese databases such as CNKI and Wanfang, and guided by the GRADE evidence grading system. This consensus comprehensively addresses the clinical significance of PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN testing, technical specifications, therapeutic decision-making, adverse event management, and future research directions.
