It aims to provide a standardized framework for clinical practice and institutional workflow in this field, offering practical guidance for clinicians, pathologists, and healthcare institutions, and ultimately maximizing the benefits of precision medicine for patients with breast cancer.

articles.title: Alcohol Non-Abstinence and Hypertension as Independent Risk Factors for Esophageal Cancer Recurrence After Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol consumption is a well-established risk factor for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Recently, metabolic abnormalities have been reported as a risk factor for ESCC. However, the impact of these risk factors on recurrence after curative endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether alcohol consumption and metabolic abnormalities independently contribute to ESCC recurrence following curative ESD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study including 147 patients with ESCC who underwent curative ESD at four institutions between 2003 and 2021. Independent predictors of recurrence were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression. Risk stratification was further explored using decision tree analysis and Kaplan-Meier curves.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 2.34 years, 31 patients (21.1%) developed recurrence of ESCC. Cox regression analysis identified alcohol non-abstinence (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.01-4.76, p = 0.0123) and hypertension (HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.01-9.23, p = 0.0327) as independent predictors of recurrence. Decision tree analysis identified alcohol non-abstinence as the strongest classifier, followed by hypertension. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that abstainers or non-drinkers with hypertension had a recurrence risk comparable to that of non-abstainers, with 3-year recurrence rates of 28.2% in non-abstainers, 23.4% in abstainers/non-drinkers with hypertension, and 0.0% in abstainers/non-drinkers without hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Alcohol non-abstinence and hypertension independently increased the risk of ESCC recurrence after curative ESD. These findings support sustained alcohol abstinence and suggest that hypertension may help identify patients who require careful post-ESD surveillance. Whether blood pressure control reduces recurrence requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Unified alcoholysis-GC-MS/MS for simultaneous differentiation and quantification of polyester microplastics in water.
articles.abstract: Environmental waters now carry complex mixtures of polyester microplastics that vary in origin and biodegradability, including fossil-based and biodegradable polyesters, yet no method can simultaneously distinguish and individually quantify them. We present a unified alcoholysis method coupled with GC-MS/MS to quantify four polyester microplastics (PEMPs) in a single workflow. By selectively cleaving ester bonds in an alcohol medium, the method converts polylactic acid, polyethylene terephthalate, polyhydroxybutyrate and polybutylene succinate into four distinct, stable monomers. These monomers are directly determined by GC-MS/MS without derivatization. Under unified conditions (190 °C, 5 h), depolymerization efficiencies range from 15% to 90%. We calibrate directly between polymer mass and monomer signal intensity. Detection limits are 0.0462 μg/L for polylactic acid (PLA), 0.103 μg/L for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), 2.92 μg/L for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and 0.695 μg/L for polybutylene succinate (PBS). Spiked recoveries in lake water are 90-115%. In six lake samples, PLA constitutes over 75% of total PEMPs. This fingerprint points to consumer packaging as the dominant source. By circumventing particle morphology constraints and delivering polymer-specific mass concentrations, the method opens a direct route for source apportionment of coexisting fossil-based and biodegradable polyester microplastics.

articles.title: Impact of a robotic system for standardized bedside hygiene, surveillance and prevention on healthcare-associated infections and ward microbial pressure: A 24-month real-world study in an acute-care ward.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a major challenge in acute-care wards caring for frail and dependent patients. Repeated high-contact bedside care may create cumulative opportunities for microbial transfer, particularly in settings with high microbial burden and susceptible patients.

AIM: To evaluate whether a robotic system for standardized bedside hygiene, surveillance and prevention, designed to standardize and trace high-contact bedside care, was associated with reduced HAIs, lower ward microbial pressure and decreased clinically expressed microbial burden.

METHODS: We conducted a 24-month quasi-experimental before-during-after study in a single acute-care hospital ward. First admissions were recorded from January 2024 to December 2025. Patients admitted with infection or sepsis were excluded, leaving 813 patients at risk: PRE, n = 218; intervention, n = 294; POST, n = 301. The robotic system was implemented by existing ward staff without staffing changes. HAIs were defined as infections occurring at least 48 hours after admission. Ward microbial pressure was assessed using positive microbiological samples.

RESULTS: Thirty-four HAIs occurred. HAI incidence decreased from 6.88% in PRE to 2.04% during intervention, with partial increase to 4.32% in POST. Compared with PRE, the reduction during intervention was significant by chi-square test with Yates correction (chi-square = 6.28; p = 0.012) and confirmed by segmented Poisson regression. Ward microbial pressure and clinically expressed microbial burden decreased in parallel.

CONCLUSIONS: The robotic system was associated with reduced HAIs, lower ward microbial pressure and reduced clinically expressed microbial burden by improving the reliability and traceability of repeated high-contact bedside care in susceptible patients.

articles.title: Community Health Worker Coaching, Food Insecurity, and Physical Activity in the Healthy Food First Trial: A Causal Mediation and Longitudinal Analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether change in food insecurity (ΔFI) mediated the effect of a community health worker (CHW) intervention on physical activity (PA) among food insecure (FI) hypertensive adults, we conducted a secondary analysis of the Healthy Food First randomized clinical trial of food insecure adults with hypertension recruited from 364 North Carolina clinical sites. Participants were randomized to CHW coaching or no coaching within a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design. FI was measured at baseline and 12 months; total PA (MET-min/week) at 12 and 18 months. Mediation models estimated indirect (ACME), direct (ADE), and total effects (ATE) of CHW assignment on 12-month PA through ΔFI. Generalized estimating equations evaluated repeated PA by CHW assignment. CHW assignment was not associated with PA, and ΔFI did not mediate the relationship. Effects were small (ACME = 16.2; 95% CI -62.6, 121.8; ADE = -214.1; 95% CI -871.7, 484.5; ATE = -197.9; 95% CI -855.6, 500.8 MET-min/week). The proportion mediated was near zero (-8.2%; 95% CI -142%, 124%). GEE analyses similarly showed no association (B = 363.7 MET-min/week; SE = 302.8; P = 0.23). Modest improvements in FI alone may be insufficient to increase PA without additional PA supports. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05048836.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Suspected Fever and Clinical Escalation: A Pilot Study Evaluating the Impact in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dexmedetomidine, an alpha-2 agonist commonly used as a sedative agent in mechanically ventilated patients, has been associated with drug-induced fever. Concern for fever may prompt diagnostic evaluation and empiric antimicrobial therapy, potentially leading to unnecessary health care utilization.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study aimed to evaluate if dexmedetomidine use in mechanically ventilated medical intensive care unit (ICU) patients was associated with increased escalation of care compared with alternate sedative agents.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, matched cohort study included patients 18 years or older who were admitted to the medical ICU and required a sedative agent to facilitate mechanical ventilation. Patients receiving dexmedetomidine were matched 1:1 with patients receiving alternate sedative agents. The primary outcome was the composite outcome of initiation of diagnostic evaluation and/or antimicrobial escalation (IDEA).

RESULTS: A total of 150 patients were included (75 per group). Most patients were male (68%), and 45% had a primary diagnosis of respiratory failure. The primary outcome, IDEA, occurred in 53 patients (71%) receiving dexmedetomidine and 51 patients (68%) receiving alternate sedatives (P = .723). Fever occurred in 24 patients (32%) receiving dexmedetomidine compared with 17 patients (23%) receiving alternate sedatives. Median ICU length of stay was longer in the dexmedetomidine group (5 [interquartile range, IQR 1-8] vs 4 [IQR 1-5] days; [P = .002]). In-hospital mortality occurred in 14 patients (19%) receiving dexmedetomidine and 24 patients (32%) receiving alternate sedative (P = .060).

CONCLUSIONS: There was no statistically significant difference between escalation of care in the use of dexmedetomidine versus other sedatives in ICU patients.

articles.title: Comorbidity management in inflammatory rheumatic diseases: a dual-perspective survey of patients and rheumatologists.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comorbidities are major contributors to morbidity and mortality in patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs). We assessed real-world implementation of European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) points to consider for comorbidity management and perceptions of responsibility.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional anonymous online survey among patients with IRDs and rheumatologists in Germany. Two questionnaires assessed demographics, perceived responsibility for comorbidity management, and implementation of preventive measures across five domains: cardiovascular risk, infections, malignancies, depression, and osteoporosis. Responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and group comparisons (chi-square, Fisher's exact, Mann-Whitney U tests).

RESULTS: A total of 2,213 patients with IRDs and 140 rheumatologists participated. Patient-reported implementation of comorbidity management in routine care was low across all domains (mean 28.8%). Rheumatologists reported substantially higher implementation than patients across all domains, including blood pressure monitoring (83.6% vs 33.8%) and vaccination checks (77.9% vs 33.2%). Most rheumatologists (69.3%) reported that no structured comorbidity screening was in place. Reported barriers included lack of time (91.4%), unclear responsibilities (48.6%), staff shortages (40.0%), and lack of reimbursement (35.0%). Rheumatologists favoured shared responsibility with general practitioners (GPs) for documentation (61.4%) and screening (48.6%), whereas treatment was more often assigned to GPs alone (60.7%). Patients more frequently assigned primary responsibility to GPs, particularly for cardiovascular risk management (72.6%) and vaccinations (73.8%).

CONCLUSIONS: Comorbidity management in IRDs is poorly implemented in routine care, and perceptions of responsibility differ between patients and rheumatologists. Clearer role definitions, stronger guidance from rheumatology organisations, and practical tools are needed to improve implementation.

articles.title: Inhibiting MD2 activates AMPK-dependent PPARγ/NOX4 signaling to attenuate mitochondrial oxidative stress and relieve pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a severe vascular disorder, is closely associated with chronic inflammatory states and oxidative stress. Myeloid differentiation protein 2 (MD2), a key co-receptor of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), is well established in mediating various inflammation-driven pathologies. However, its role in pulmonary hypertension and its potential involvement in oxidative stress regulation remain unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: MD2 expression was upregulated in both PH patients and murine PH models. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of MD2 improved hemodynamic parameters, attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, and reduced right ventricular hypertrophy. MD2 inhibition significantly reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that suppression of the membrane protein MD2 activated intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, leading to enhanced peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activity. PPARγ, in turn, suppressed nuclear transcription of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), resulting in a marked reduction in mitochondrial oxidative stress.

CONCLUSION: This study indicates that MD2 may act as an upstream regulator of mitochondrial oxidative stress in PH. Inhibition of MD2 attenuates pulmonary hypertension through activation of the AMPK/PPARγ axis, which suppresses NOX4 mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress. Targeting MD2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for PH.

articles.title: Associations between infection and organ age gaps: results from the UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infection may have lasting influences in multiple organ systems, but its associations with organ-specific biological age remain unclear. We aimed to examine associations between infection burden (IB) and organ age gaps.

METHODS: Among 42,395 UK Biobank participants, qualifying infection diagnoses were identified from first occurrences data. The IB score was defined as the number of distinct infection diagnoses first recorded before baseline. Participants were classified according to whether at least one qualifying infection diagnosis had hospital inpatient data as its earliest-record source, and infections were grouped into eight predefined categories. Biological ages of 18 organs were calculated from plasma proteomics-based organ signatures, with higher organ age gap (OAG) indicating accelerated aging process. Linear regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to examine associations between infections and OAG.

RESULTS: Higher IB score was positively associated with OAG of 12 in 18 organs. IB-OAG associations were statistically significant for hospital-treated infections, but not for non-hospital-treated only infections. Among eight infected subcategories, sepsis showed the strongest and most widespread associations with OAG. Associations between IB score and OAG of heart, kidney, and pancreas were significantly nonlinear. In addition, associations were generally stronger for infection diagnoses first recorded in more recent time windows and weaker for diagnoses first recorded further in the past.

CONCLUSIONS: IB was associated with accelerated multi-organ aging, particularly for hospital-treated infections and sepsis. Our findings highlighted the critical roles of infection in organ aging, which provided clues to make tailored strategies for the prevention of aging related disorders.

articles.title: An integrated One Health surveillance approach to Dirofilaria spp.: Linking mosquito xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis and veterinary epidemiology.
articles.abstract: Dirofilaria immitis and Dirofilaria repens are mosquito-borne filarioid nematodes of veterinary and public health importance whose distribution is expanding across Europe. This study developed an integrated One Health surveillance framework combining mosquito monitoring, molecular xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis, and veterinary epidemiological data to assess Dirofilaria circulation and transmission dynamics. During the 2025 transmission season, mosquitoes were collected by the University of Parma in urban and peri-urban areas and by the Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale della Lombardia ed Emilia-Romagna (IZSLER) in rural areas. Female mosquitoes were morphologically identified and analysed in pools by Real-time PCR for D. immitis and D. repens DNA. Positive pools were screened for West Nile virus, Usutu virus, and insect-specific flaviviruses in order to detect possible co-infection parasite-virus. Blood-fed mosquitoes were individually analysed by mitochondrial 12S and 16S rRNA sequencing to identify vertebrate hosts. Veterinary practices across Emilia-Romagna were surveyed for canine and feline dirofilariosis during 2024-2025. Overall, 11,225 females belonging to eight species were collected and 181 pools analysed. D. immitis predominated in urban collections, whereas D. repens was more frequent in peri-urban and rural areas. Aedes albopictus was the principal positive species in urban environments, while Aedes caspius predominated in rural settings. Humans were the predominant blood-meal host, followed by dogs, horses, cattle, and birds. Veterinary and vector surveillance showed poor agreement, indicating complementary epidemiological information. These findings highlight complex transmission patterns and support integrated One Health surveillance to improve risk assessment and guide evidence-based prevention and control strategies for Dirofilaria and other vector-borne zoonoses.

articles.title: Determinants of orthoflavivirus tropism in humans: from cellular entry to organ-specific pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: Orthoflaviviruses, including dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Zika virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and yellow fever virus, cause a wide spectrum of diseases in humans despite sharing a similar genomic organization. These viruses pose a growing global threat as they are spreading widely, treatment options remain limited, and both climate change and expanding mosquito populations increase the risk of outbreaks worldwide. This review summarizes the determinants of their human tropism, the capacity to infect specific cell types, tissues, and organs. We synthesized current knowledge on how viral factors, including host factor utilization and immune cell trafficking, shape tropism across multiple layers. Central to this process are sequential host barriers that govern infection, including viral attachment, internalization, and replication. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing strategies to mitigate the global burden of these medically important pathogens.

articles.title: Myocardial External Efficiency and Energetic Adaptation After Heart Transplantation: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired myocardial energetics may contribute to graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HTX). We aimed to characterize early posttransplant myocardial external efficiency (MEE) and its relationship with mitochondrial capacity.

METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 22 HTX recipients underwent [11C]acetate positron emission tomography, echocardiography, biomarker testing, and high-resolution respirometry of endomyocardial biopsies once between week 1 and 3 and at 6 mo post-HTX. Temporal changes in positron emission tomography-derived MEE, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen consumption were evaluated within patients and compared with those of 20 control participants. Mitochondrial capacity was assessed only in HTX recipients.

RESULTS: MEE increased from 18 ± 5% to 21 ± 5% at 6 mo post-HTX (P = 0.003) but remained lower than in control participants (26 ± 6%, P < 0.0001). Cardiac output, myocardial oxygen consumption, and mitochondrial oxidative capacity did not change significantly over time. At 6 mo, both MEE and mitochondrial oxidative capacity correlated with left-ventricular global longitudinal strain (r = -0.49, P = 0.002; r = -0.58, P = 0.010, respectively). Furthermore, MEE was inversely associated with troponin I (r = -0.49, P = 0.030) and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (r = -0.35, P = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: MEE improved significantly from 1-3 wk to 6 mo after HTX. Both MEE and mitochondrial respiratory function were associated with left-ventricular contractile performance. Overall, these findings suggest alterations in myocardial energetics during early graft recovery and support a link between oxidative metabolism and graft performance.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of an mHealth intervention to improve hypertension control in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of a mobile health technology (mHealth) based care model to facilitate home blood pressure (BP) monitoring and remote hypertension management.

METHODS: We used a Markov microsimulation model to study health and cost outcomes for three hypertension control strategies: an mHealth-based care model (mGlide) vs. Enhanced Usual Care (EUC) vs. No-Intervention. We sampled patient characteristics from the mGlide randomized controlled trial (RCT) and randomly transitioned patients through three possible health states over a 10-year horizon with monthly cycles: 1) No Cardiovascular Event, 2) Cardiovascular Event, and 3) Deceased. We determined transition probabilities from literature, allowing the probabilities to vary by patient characteristics, including BP values. We evaluated health and cost outcomes across a range of plausible deterministic treatment effects (expected BP reductions) supported by the RCT. We performed probabilistic sensitivity analysis to assess cost-effectiveness while randomly varying the treatment effect magnitude.

RESULTS: The mHealth-based care model was cost-effective compared to No-Intervention and EUC across all deterministic scenarios. 10-year mortality absolute risk reductions ranged from 4.9-5.8% (vs No-Intervention) and 0.6-3.3% (vs EUC) across scenarios. In probabilistic sensitivity analysis, mHealth-based care (vs EUC) was less costly in 59.6% of iterations and had better health outcomes in 99.6%. Comparing all care models, mHealth-based care had the greatest net monetary benefit in 95% of iterations at $26,000/QALY and in 99% of iterations at $72,000/QALY.

CONCLUSIONS: In the current study, we estimated that mHealth-based care models can be cost-effective approaches to improve hypertension control in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Rifampicin-soaked versus bovine prostheses in the management of aortic graft infections: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic vascular graft and endograft infections (aortic VGEI) remain a rare but life-threatening complication following aortic reconstruction. This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction. Patients received either a bovine pericardial graft (n=21) or a rifampicin-soaked Dacron prosthesis (n=41). Survival, treatment failure, perioperative variables, and microbiology were analyzed.

RESULTS: Patients in the bovine and rifampicin groups were comparable in terms of age (72.57 vs. 73.58 years, p = 0.685) and sex distribution (85.71% vs. 73.17% male, p = 0.346). BMI, preoperative dialysis, and aortic clamping time were higher in the bovine group. Four treatment failures, defined as persistent or recurrent infection of the reconstructed aortic segment, occurred during follow-up; all were observed after reconstruction with rifampicin-soaked Dacron (4/41, 9.8%), whereas no treatment failure occurred in the bovine pericardial group (0/21). In-hospital mortality was comparable between groups (n=3:14.3% vs. n=8: 19.5%, p = 0.735). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in survival (p = 0.256) or treatment failure rate (p = 0.833). Candida spp. were the most frequent pathogens (27.8%) and significantly associated with secondary aorto-enteric fistula (p=0.003).

CONCLUSION: Survival and treatment failure rates were comparable, with a trend toward fewer infection-related complications after bovine pericardial grafting. Despite use in more complex cases, bovine grafts may represent a promising biological alternative.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Hydatid Cyst: A Rare Cause of Right Heart Failure in Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac hydatid cyst is a rare manifestation of Echinococcus granulosus infection, comprising fewer than 2% of all echinococcosis cases. Right ventricular (RV) involvement causing right heart failure is exceptionally uncommon.

CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old woman at 29 weeks of gestation with a history of pulmonary tuberculosis presented with exertional dyspnea and bilateral pedal edema for 3 months. Investigations revealed peripheral eosinophilia and elevated N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated right atrial and ventricular dilatation with a large cystic mass arising from the RV free wall. Cardiac Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed a multiloculated cystic mass with peripheral daughter cysts, with concomitant pericardial, pulmonary, and hepatic cysts, establishing the diagnosis of disseminated echinococcosis.

DISCUSSION: RV hydatid cyst is a rare but treatable etiology of right heart failure that poses unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges during pregnancy. This case underscores the importance of considering parasitic etiologies in endemic regions and demonstrates the feasibility of medical management as a temporary strategy during gestation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac hydatid cyst should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained right heart failure in patients from endemic regions. Peripheral eosinophilia and characteristic multiloculated cystic morphology on imaging are key diagnostic clues.

articles.title: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome in an Elderly Woman on a Haloperidol-Lithium Combination: A Diagnostic Challenge with Complete Recovery.
articles.abstract: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a rare but potentially fatal idiosyncratic reaction to dopamine-blocking agents, characterized by hyperthermia, generalized rigidity, autonomic instability, and altered consciousness. Its recognition is particularly difficult in elderly patients, in whom the presentation may be atypical and the differential diagnosis broad. We report a 76-year-old woman with chronic schizophrenia, maintained on haloperidol and lithium for approximately 3 months, who presented with high-grade fever (39.6°C), acute alteration in sensorium, and hypertension (170/110 mmHg). Examination revealed lead-pipe rigidity, bilateral tremor, and a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10/15. An initial working diagnosis of infectious encephalitis produced a diagnostic delay of 2-3 days; lumbar puncture and blood cultures were unremarkable, and creatine kinase peaked at 4120 U/L. NMS was diagnosed using diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders, fifth edition (DSM-5) and Levenson criteria. Both offending agents were withdrawn, and the patient was managed in intensive care with intravenous hydration, active cooling, bromocriptine, and lorazepam. She achieved complete neurological recovery by day 14 and was discharged without residual deficits. This case underscores that NMS must be considered early in any older patient on dopamine antagonists presenting with fever, rigidity, and altered consciousness and that the haloperidol-lithium combination carries a specific risk even at therapeutic lithium levels.

articles.title: Study of Serum Aldosterone, Serum, and Urinary Electrolytes in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients (>5 Years) and Their Correlation with Microvascular Complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes Mellitus is characterized by a shared phenotype of chronic hyperglycemia and bears a disproportionate burden in India with particularly high microvascular complication rates. While Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) dysfunction and electrolyte imbalances are known to exacerbate microvascular injury, their specific roles remain underexplored in cases of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), despite the documented prevalence of both hypoaldosteronism and hyperaldosteronism.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: The primary aim of this study was to assess the levels of serum aldosterone, serum electrolytes, and urinary electrolytes in T2DM patients with a disease duration of more than 5 years. The objective was to correlate these biochemical findings with the presence of microvascular complications, specifically retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional, observational, and analytical study was conducted at a tertiary care center in Western Maharashtra between September 2023 and February 2026. The study enrolled 120 adult participants aged 18 years or older who had T2DM for at least 5 years. Serum aldosterone levels were measured using a fully automated chemiluminescent immunoassay (CLIA), while serum and urinary electrolytes alongside osmolality were measured using ion-selective electrodes and osmometry. Microvascular complications were assessed using standard clinical criteria, which included dilated fundoscopy for diabetic retinopathy, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) for diabetic nephropathy, and clinical symptoms along with the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI) score for diabetic neuropathy.

RESULTS: The key finding of the study was a statistically significant inverse relationship between low serum aldosterone (<1.17 ng/dL) and the prevalence of diabetic neuropathy (p=0.023), suggesting hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism as a novel risk factor. Patients with diabetic nephropathy exhibited classical tubular dysfunction parameters, including significantly elevated serum osmolality (p=0.010), reduced urine osmolality (p=0.001), and reduced urinary potassium (p=0.006). Both the diabetic nephropathy and diabetic retinopathy groups showed elevated serum osmolality (p=0.010 and p=0.031 respectively), indicating osmotic stress-induced microvascular injury. There was a statistically significant positive correlation between the duration of diabetes and microvascular complications, though HbA1c and overall serum aldosterone levels did not show statistically significant direct correlations with complications or electrolyte levels.

CONCLUSION: The study identifies aldosterone deficiency as a novel, potentially modifiable, and early predictive marker for diabetic neuropathy. Furthermore, tubular dysfunction parameters such as elevated serum osmolality, reduced urine osmolality, and reduced urinary potassium can serve as early markers for nephropathy. These findings highlight the critical importance of integrating routine aldosterone and electrolyte testing in the diabetic population to enable earlier interventions and mitigate microvascular complications.

articles.title: Second-trimester Maternal Serum Insulin-like Growth Factor Binding Protein 4 to Sex Hormone-binding Globulin Ratio as a Predictor of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Prospective Observation Study from North India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ratio of maternal serum insulin-like growth factor binding protein 4 (IGFBP-4) to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) has emerged as a promising proteomic predictor, but validation in high-burden settings including India is limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the predictive value of the second-trimester IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio for spontaneous preterm birth (PTB) and association with fetomaternal outcome.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was carried out over a period of 1 year. A total of 190 singleton pregnant women between 16 and 21 weeks of gestation were enrolled. Maternal serum IGFBP-4 and SHBG levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) technique using an ELISA kit as per the producer protocol. Participants were followed till delivery and categorized into Group A preterm (delivery <37 weeks, n = 54) and Group B term (delivery ≥37 weeks, n = 136). Predictive accuracy (AUROC) of the ratio for PTB was assessed. Fetomaternal outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: The PTB rate was 28.4%, and the second-trimester IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio was significantly higher in Group A than Group B (0.619 ± 0.399 vs. 0.191 ± 0.242; P < 0.001). ROC analysis for the ratio at enrollment yielded an AUC of 0.906 (95% confidence interval: 0.859-0.952). At a cutoff >0.188, the ratio showed 94.4% sensitivity and 79.4% specificity for predicting PTB. A raised baseline ratio was significantly associated with spontaneous preterm delivery (86.1% preterm vs. 37.8% term, P < 0.001), similarly low birth weight (74.7% vs. 36.0%, P < 0.001), low 5-min Apgar (10.1% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.001), and increased neonatal intensive care unit admission (P = 0.031).

CONCLUSION: The second-trimester maternal serum IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio is a highly sensitive and specific predictor for spontaneous PTB. It also correlates strongly with adverse neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Outcome of Children with Diabetic Ketoacidosis Managed with the BSPED 2015 DKA Protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to report why children with diabetes develop diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and what is the clinical course and complications encountered while managing the patients with British Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetes (BSPED) 2015 guidelines.

METHODS: This was a hospital based prospective, observational study conducted at a tertiary care hospital comprising of a total of 44 episodes of DKA. The patients were diagnosed and classified as mild to moderate DKA or severe DKA based on BSPED 2015 guidelines. Serial monitoring was done as per guidelines till resolution of DKA.

RESULTS: A total of 44 DKA episodes were documented. Eighteen patients (41%) were diagnosed with diabetes for the first time during the episode. Most common presenting complaint was vomiting and abdominal pain. Insulin omission completely or in part for variable reasons was the most common precipitating cause. The mean duration of correction of DKA was 27.2 ± 2.82 h. The rate of change in mean random blood sugar, ketones, pH, and bicarbonates for every 4 h of treatment was 15 mg/dL, 0.5 mmol/L, 0.03, and 0.53 mEq/L respectively. Complications during treatment included hypokalemia in 11 patients (25%), followed by cerebral edema in six patients (13.6%).

CONCLUSION: We have described in detail the clinical course seen during treatment of DKA with BSPED 2015 protocol. It can be used to anticipate treatment course and complications in any patient being managed with this protocol. This can be objectively compared to any other protocol used during the management of DKA.

articles.title: Age, Gender, and Adherence in Low-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Reduction with Statin Therapy: A Real-world Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend achieving ≥50% reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in high-risk patients. Real-world data on response patterns, age and gender differences, and determinants of nonresponse remain limited. The aim of the study is to evaluate LDL-C reduction following statin therapy in routine clinical practice and to examine the influence of age, gender, and medication adherence on treatment response and cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: In this observational cohort study, adults initiated on statin therapy with documented baseline and follow-up lipid measurements were included. LDL-C levels were recorded at baseline and follow-up. The primary outcome was achievement of ≥50% LDL-C reduction.

RESULTS: In a total study population of 652 patients, statin therapy was associated with substantial early reductions in LDL-C that were largely maintained at 1 year. More than half of the patients achieved a ≥50% reduction, and nearly one-third achieved LDL-C levels <55 mg/dL. Patients >45 years demonstrated greater sustained LDL-C reduction compared with younger individuals. Numerical differences in LDL-C response were observed between men and women, although these were not statistically significant. Failure to achieve ≥50% LDL-C reduction appeared to be more closely associated with lower medication adherence rather than treatment intensity within this uniformly treated cohort. Greater proportional LDL-C reduction was associated with lower cardiovascular event rates during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In routine practice, approximately half of patients achieved ≥50% LDL-C reduction with high-intensity statin therapy. Adherence emerges as an important determinant of response. Age was associated with sustained response, whereas gender differences were not statistically significant. Nonresponse is primarily associated with modifiable treatment-related factors.

articles.title: Statin Utilization in High-risk Hypertensive Nigerians.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Individuals with high cardiovascular (CV) risk face major adverse CV events without statin use. However, the study of statin use among these populations in Nigeria remains limited. We examined statin use in high-risk hypertensives.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the data from 1040 patients in the Federal Medical Center Abuja Hypertension registry, recruited between 2016 and 2021. Statin use was examined among patients classified as high risk by the World Health Organization/International Society of Hypertension (WHO/ISH), the Predicting the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations, and the pooled cohort equation (PCE) scores.

RESULTS: The mean age of high-risk patients was 62.7 ± 9.3 years using the WHO/ISH model, with no difference between males and females. The prevalence rate of dyslipidemia of the total cohort was 70.7% (735), while the prevalence of statin use was 61.9% (78), 50.0% (119), and 43.3% (345) using the 10-year CV WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Furthermore, the proportions of those with high 10-year CV risk were 12.1% (126), 22.9% (238), and 76.6% (797) for the WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Adjusted multivariable logistic regression showed that increasing age (odds ratio [OR] =1.03 [confidence interval (CI): 1.01-1.05]), diabetes mellitus (OR = 2.45 [CI: 1.69-3.55]), and increased total (OR = 1.90 [CI 1.38-2.60]) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR = 1.83 [CI 1.32-2.52]) (P < 0.05) were the factors associated with statin use.

CONCLUSION: Our study revealed suboptimal statin utilization and significant CV risk scores disparities in identifying high-risk hypertensive patients. Co-ordinated efforts are crucial for enhancing statin use and developing locally validated CV risk prediction tools.

articles.title: The predictive value of the hemodynamic profile for survival in patients undergoing transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (M-TEER) represents a safe treatment modality for patients with high-grade mitral regurgitation (MR). While clinical decision-making concerning the referral of suitable candidates for M-TEER is guided primarily by clinical and echocardiographic parameters, the potential of hemodynamic parameters obtained at the time of screening in predicting treatment outcomes has not been sufficiently investigated.

METHODS: All patients who underwent M-TEER and who provided sufficient right heart catheterisation (RHC) data prior to M-TEER were enrolled for analysis. The investigated hemodynamic parameters were analysed descriptively and their associations with survival were estimated by univariable Cox regression analysis and Kaplan-Meier's analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 94 patients were analysed, of whom 92.6% (87/94) had concomitant pulmonary hypertension (PH). Analysis of the hemodynamic profile revealed that 46.8% (44/94) of patients had advanced-stage congestive heart failure with a cardiac index < 2 L/min/m2, and 68% (64/94) of patients had a cardiac power index <0.5 W/m2. According to the results of the Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses, a systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) > 60 mmHg and a mean right atrial pressure (RAP) > 20 mmHg were proven to be significant predictors of long-term survival after M-TEER.

CONCLUSIONS: Analysis of the hemodynamic profile, specifically the identified predictors, contributes to the improved identification of scenarios associated with a favourable prognosis in patients undergoing M-TEER.

articles.title: Prenatal ambient ozone exposure and risk of offspring congenital heart disease: A three-level meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association (1995)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to ambient ozone has been hypothesized to increase the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring; however, epidemiological evidence remains inconclusive.

OBJECTIVE: To quantitatively synthesize the available evidence on the association between prenatal ambient ozone exposure and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring, and to explore potential effect modifiers through subgroup analyses and meta regression.

METHODS: The PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase and CNKI databases were systemically searched from from 1970 until April 2026 to find articles related to offspring CHD and periconceptional ozone exposure. Inverse variance weighted random-effects multilevel models were conducted to pool estimates and stratify associations by heart defect type, country income level, study design, investigation time period, and data source. Dose-response relationships were examined via meta-regression and the heterogeneity and publication bias in relevant studies was also examined.

RESULTS: A total of 29 studies comprising 302 effect estimates were identified. The overall pooled odds ratio for the association between prenatal ozone exposure and CHD was 1.032 (95% CI: 1.004-1.060). Stronger associations were observed for transposition of the great arteries (OR =1.172), conotruncal defects (OR =1.134), and atrioventricular septal defects (OR =1.204). The embryonic period was the most susceptible exposure window (OR =1.064, 95% CI: 1.006-1.126). Stronger effects were found in upper-middle-income countries (OR =1.039), studies conducted after 2020 (OR =1.145), and hospital-based data (OR =1.112). Dose-response analysis suggested a 1% odds increase per 10 μg/m3 ozone increment, though not statistically significant. Considerable heterogeneity was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis suggests that prenatal ozone exposure may modestly increase CHD risk. The substantial heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized exposure assessment and further prospective studies.Implication Statement: This meta-analysis provides quantitative evidence that prenatal ozone exposure is associated with a modest increase in congenital heart defect risk, with stronger effects observed in upper-middle-income countries and more recent studies. The embryonic developmental window emerged as the most susceptible exposure period. These findings inform air quality management by identifying specific exposure windows and vulnerable populations for targeted intervention, and support the refinement of WHO ozone guidelines and national ambient air quality standards to better protect fetal health.

articles.title: Clinical Application of Dynamic Skin Temperature Monitor Combined With Structured Nursing Handover in Postoperative Flap Monitoring.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical application of a dynamic skin temperature monitor combined with structured nursing handover in postoperative skin flap monitoring and to assess its impact on the early identification of vascular crisis and flap prognosis.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 46 patients undergoing free flap transplantation in the Department of Orthopedics of a tertiary class A hospital between July 2025 and May 2026. Patients assigned to the preprotocol group (July 2025 to December 2025, n=29) received routine clinical monitoring and traditional verbal nursing handover. For the postprotocol group (January 2026 to May 2026, n=17), continuous skin temperature monitoring with a dynamic skin temperature monitor was implemented, alongside a structured nursing handover process based on the Microsurgery Skin Flap Postoperative Registration Form and an immediate notification mechanism for abnormal data. The primary outcomes included vascular crisis incidence and flap survival rate, while secondary outcomes covered the time from abnormality detection to intervention, handover completeness score, and nurse satisfaction.

RESULTS: Among the 46 patients undergoing free flap transplantation, the overall vascular crisis incidence was 17.4% (8/46). The postprotocol group had a lower vascular crisis rate compared with the preprotocol group (11.8% vs. 20.7%, P=0.441). Time from abnormality to detection was significantly shorter in the postprotocol group (15.5±4.9 min vs. 52.3±20.0 min, P=0.002), as was time from detection to intervention (22.0±9.9 min vs. 39.2±8.0 min, P=0.018). Handover completeness scores improved from 70.7±9.4% to 92.2±4.2% (P<0.001), and information omission items decreased from 3.1±1.3 to 0.3±0.7 (P<0.001). The AUC for temperature monitoring in diagnosing vascular crisis was 0.92 (95% CI: 0.86-0.98).

CONCLUSION: The combination of dynamic skin temperature monitoring and structured nursing handover was associated with earlier identification of vascular crisis, shorter detection-to-intervention intervals, and improved nursing handover quality in patients undergoing flap surgery. These findings suggest that the integrated protocol may be associated with improved postoperative outcomes. However, the retrospective before-and-after design cannot eliminate the interference of temporal trends and other secular confounding factors, which precludes definitive causal inference.

articles.title: Triglyceride-defined apolipoprotein B discordance after LDL-C and non-HDL-C goal attainment: a population-based NHANES analysis with CHNS consistency assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-C) reflect cholesterol mass, whereas apolipoprotein B (ApoB) reflects atherogenic particle number. We examined residual ApoB elevation after both cholesterol thresholds had been met and its distribution across triglyceride levels.

METHODS: We analysed the 2005-2016 fasting subsample of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) among adults aged 30-79 years. The primary subgroup had LDL-C <2.59 mmol/L [100 mg/dL] and non-HDL-C <3.36 mmol/L [130 mg/dL]; residual elevation was defined as ApoB ≥0.90 g/L [90 mg/dL]. NHANES estimates and regressions accounted for the complex survey design. CHNS 2009 provided an unweighted consistency assessment.

RESULTS: Of 10,451 NHANES participants, 3,132 met both thresholds and 163 had ApoB ≥0.90 g/L. Weighted prevalence was 5.4% (95% CI 4.4-6.4), rising to 18.2% with triglycerides ≥1.69 mmol/L [150 mg/dL], compared with 2.9% below this threshold. The clinical model yielded an odds ratio of 6.23 (95% CI 3.68-10.53; P<0.001). Prevalence varied by ApoB threshold (22.9% at ≥0.80 g/L; 0.9% at ≥1.00 g/L). In CHNS, corresponding triglyceride-stratified prevalences were 8.9% and 1.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: Residual ApoB elevation after simultaneous LDL-C and non-HDL-C threshold attainment was concentrated in adults with higher triglycerides. Triglyceride levels offer a readily available means of identifying a subgroup with substantially greater yield from ApoB measurement.

articles.title: Different Patterns of Progression in Nonproliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Findings From a 10-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Characterization of the 10-year progression of diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes was sought. We evaluated whether noninvasive optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) can identify eyes that progress and may develop vision loss. Of 222 participants, 62% completed the study, with 115 reaching the 10-year visit: 27% of eyes worsened, 50% remained stable, and 21% improved, based on Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study severity grading (2% unclassified); microvascular nonperfusion, measured using noninvasive OCTA, distinguished the eyes that worsened or remained stable from those eyes that improved. Progression of microvascular nonperfusion identified by OCTA enables identification of patients at higher risk for disease progression.

articles.title: Adjunctive Atypical Antipsychotics in Major Depressive Disorder: A Network Meta-Analysis Perspective and Consensus Panel Discussion.
articles.abstract: Objective: The goal of this consensus panel was to generate expert perspectives on the comparative efficacy, safety, tolerability, and clinical relevance of FDA-approved adjunctive atypical antipsychotics for adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) and inadequate response to antidepressant therapy. Participants: Five academic and clinical experts in psychiatry and psychopharmacology participated as panelists: Roger S. McIntyre, Andrew J. Cutler, Christoph U. Correll, Joseph F. Goldberg, and Stephen M. Stahl. The discussion was conducted as a closed expert panel. Evidence: The panel primarily discussed research findings from two recent network meta-analyses (NMAs) evaluating approved adjunctive atypical antipsychotics in MDD, supplemented by relevant published literature and panel expertise. The NMAs differed in study inclusion, treatment-node definitions, and analytical approaches to examine efficacy, acceptability, and safety. Panel discussion was used to contextualize the findings and address their clinical applicability and limitations. Consensus Process: The panel reviewed and discussed the NMA methodology, comparative efficacy and safety outcomes, effect modifiers, and implications for shared decision-making. The consensus manuscript was developed from the panel discussion and evidence review, with subsequent expert review and incorporation of relevant comments and revisions. Conclusions: The panel concluded that the two NMAs provide complementary and broadly concordant comparative evidence that can inform clinical decision-making. Treatment selection should integrate efficacy with tolerability, patient characteristics, preferences, and practical considerations. The panel emphasized earlier consideration of effective, FDA-approved adjunctive treatment when appropriate, while recognizing remaining relevant gaps in long-term, head-to-head, and phenotype-specific evidence. The panel did not endorse any particular agent.

articles.title: A Retrospective Evaluation of Safety Outcomes of Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate & Tranexamic Acid Versus Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Alone in Patients Requiring Emergent Anticoagulation Reversal.
articles.abstract: Utilizing four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) and tranexamic acid (TXA) concomitantly may theoretically elevate the risk of thromboembolism compared to either agent alone. Certain clinical situations arise where a patient may be a candidate for both TXA and 4F-PCC, such as trauma with major hemorrhage requiring anticoagulation reversal. In the absence of published literature, it is largely unknown whether coadministration of both agents increases the risk of thromboembolic events. The objective of this study was to explore safety outcomes of utilizing both 4F-PCC and TXA concomitantly in patients requiring emergent anticoagulation reversal due to a major hemorrhage. A single-center, retrospective chart review was conducted in adult patients who received 4F-PCC + TXA or 4F-PCC alone for emergent anticoagulation reversal of warfarin, apixaban, or rivaroxaban. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of thromboembolic events. The secondary endpoint was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Of the 110 patients included, 74 received 4F-PCC only and 36 patients received both 4F-PCC and TXA. The occurrence of thromboembolism was significantly higher in the 4F-PCC + TXA group compared to the 4F-PCC group (16.7% vs 2.7%; P = 0.0144). The incidence of all-cause in-hospital mortality was similar between groups [19.4% (4F-PCC + TXA) vs 10.8% (4F-PCC); P = 0.346]. The utilization of both 4F-PCC and TXA for patients with major hemorrhage requiring emergent anticoagulation reversal was associated with a significantly higher risk of thromboembolism than 4F-PCC alone. Clinicians should use caution when utilizing 4F-PCC and TXA concomitantly.

articles.title: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate measurement properties of Observational gait analysis (OGA) tools among neurological populations.

METHODS: PRISMA-COSMIN guidelines were followed. Articles included measurement properties studies for OGA tools in neurologic populations were included. Studies were rated as sufficient, insufficient, or indeterminate. Results were synthesized by the population and OGA tool.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight included articles performed 63 studies for 7 OGA tools that were synthesized in 42 results in stroke, multiple sclerosis and Parkison's disease. The Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), and Gait Assessment and Intervention tool (G.A.I.T) in stroke have been studied for all properties except measurement invariance, and all of them were sufficient except measurement error. Other OGA tools were tested in limited studies. All included tools have potential for recommendation; however, none was fully recommended for use.

CONCLUSION: WGS and G.A.I.T in stroke have the best potential for recommendation. They can be used at only group-level or cross-sectional analysis due to their large measurement error. Standardized observation methods and measurement invariance studies should be prioritized. Both WGS and G.A.I.T measure gait deviations through 14 and 31 items respectively, WGS provides more feasible assessment while G.A.I.T provides more detailed biomechanical analysis.

articles.title: Genetic polymorphisms of GLUT1 (rs841853) and MATE1 (rs2289669) are associated with metformin response in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metformin is first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes mellitus; however, over 30-40% of patients exhibit a suboptimal glycemic response. Metformin efficacy is governed by pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic processes. Cellular transport of metformin is influenced by Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and renal elimination by multidrug and toxin extrusion protein 1 (MATE1). This study examined GLUT1 rs841853 and MATE1 rs2289669 polymorphisms on metformin response.

METHODS: A total of 200 T2DM patients on metformin were recruited from Era's Medical College and Hospital, Lucknow. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical data were collected. Genotyping of GLUT1 rs841853 and MATE1 rs2289669 was performed by PCR-RFLP. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS v27.

RESULTS: GLUT1 GT and GG genotypes of rs841853 was higher in non‑responders than in responders (GT: 73.8% vs 66.0%) (OR =  2.494, q = 0.071) and (GG: 16.5% vs 12.4%) (OR =  2.975, q = 0.071). MATE1 A allele was higher in responders (28.3% vs 21.1%) with an OR of 0.628 (q = 0.219). Nominal significant associations in unadjusted analysis lost significance after multiple-testing correction. Gender-stratified analysis showed that female responders had a reduction in FBS, whereas non-responders had increased FBS, PPG and HbA1c levels in both males and females.

CONCLUSION: Findings emphasize a transporter-mediated pharmacogenetic approach and the potential value of combined GLUT1-MATE1 genotyping for individualized T2DM treatment.

articles.title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.

METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.

RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal Symptoms Among Agricultural Workers in Rural Communities of Loja, Ecuador.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal symptoms (MSS) are among the most common occupational health problems worldwide and disproportionately affect agricultural workers because of the physical demands of their work. However, evidence on MSS prevalence among farmers in Ecuador remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of MSS and examine its association with selected sociodemographic and occupational factors among agricultural workers in rural communities in Loja, Ecuador.

METHODS: A descriptive, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted among 103 farmers using the Standardized Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ). Descriptive statistics were used to estimate the 12-month prevalence of MSS, and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess associations with sociodemographic and occupational variables.

RESULTS: A high prevalence of MSS was observed, particularly in the lower back (78.6%), knees (64.1%), and neck (58.3%). Overweight was significantly associated with lower back pain and marginally associated with neck pain. No significant associations were found between MSS prevalence and occupational exposure variables, such as working posture or weekly working hours.

CONCLUSIONS: MSS are highly prevalent among agricultural workers in rural Ecuador. These findings highlight the need for preventive occupational health strategies to reduce musculoskeletal risk in agricultural settings.

articles.title: Climate Change and Workers' Health and Safety: An Umbrella Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This umbrella review synthesizes current evidence on the health and safety impacts of climate change among workers. In particular, it aims to identify the main workers' categories at the highest risk, the main health and safety outcomes, methodological limitations, and future directions reported in the literature, as well as preventive strategies described in recent reviews.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Systematic and scoping reviews addressing climate-related occupational health and safety outcomes were included. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Methodological quality was assessed using the ROBIS tool, and findings were synthesized in accordance with PRISMA and PRIOR guidelines.

RESULTS: Most of the available evidence concerns outdoor occupations, particularly agriculture and construction, where exposure to high temperatures is associated with increased risks of injuries and heat strain. Emerging data also highlight links with mental health, renal disease, and chronic conditions. However, the literature remains fragmented, with few meta-analyses and substantial heterogeneity. Preventive strategies have been proposed, but their implementation remains inconsistent.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence confirms that climate change has become a determinant of occupational health and safety. Future research should strengthen methodological coherence, adopt longitudinal approaches, and address vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching.

CONCLUSIONS: Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.

articles.title: Long-term effectiveness of the MiniMed™ 780G System in older individuals with type 1 diabetes: clinical observations over two years.
Developmental mechanisms contributing to non-linear firing dynamics in spinal motoneurons of the postnatal mouse.
articles.abstract: The intrinsic properties of spinal motoneurons support flexible movement, including the maintenance of postural tone. Motoneurons can produce sustained action potential output that outlasts synaptic input, a phenomenon traditionally attributed to persistent inward currents (PICs) mediated by sodium and calcium channels. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, we examined how specific ion channels contribute to PIC maturation and non-linear firing dynamics that allow motoneurons to sustain their output in fast and slow lumbar motoneurons across postnatal development in mice. PIC amplitude and non-linear firing dynamics increased after weight-bearing in fast but not slow motoneurons. Blocking NaV1.6 channels reduced PIC amplitude at both pre- and post-weight-bearing stages, whereas L-type calcium channel blockade only reduced PICs after weight-bearing emerged. However, reducing PIC amplitude by blocking these channels, either individually or in parallel, did not abolish sustained firing hysteresis, which may be because PICs are not yet fully established at this stage of postnatal development. Unexpectedly, activation of muscarinic receptors increased PIC amplitude while promoting adaptive firing dynamics, suggesting that PICs alone do not account for sustained firing hysteresis. We also found that pharmacological manipulation of potassium currents mediated by KCNQ and KV1.2 channels produced substantial changes in firing dynamics. Strikingly, blocking hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels promoted sustained firing dynamics and led to the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons. These results indicate that PICs and non-linear firing dynamics mature together and extend the current framework on non-linear firing dynamics of motoneurons to include additional voltage-gated ion channels. KEY POINTS: Persistent inward currents (PICs) and recruitment-derecruitment hysteresis increase in parallel in fast, but not slow, motoneurons following the onset of hindlimb weight-bearing. Increased expression or function of L-type calcium channels may contribute to enhanced PIC amplitude in fast motoneurons after weight-bearing emerges. Blocking NaV1.6 or L-type calcium channels did not reduce sustained firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. KCNQ channels oppose PICs and, together with KV1.2 channels, shape recruitment-derecruitment asymmetry, thereby modulating firing hysteresis in fast motoneurons. Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels generate a resting H-current that delays recruitment, modulates firing hysteresis, and prevents the emergence of self-sustained firing in fast motoneurons.

articles.title: The role of physical activity in post-stroke depression among European women and men aged 50 and older.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the associations between the frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity and depression among adults aged 50 years or older with a history of stroke.Design and settingCross-sectional study using data from Wave 9 (2021-2022) of the Survey of Health, Aging and Retirement in Europe.ParticipantsA total of 1323 adults aged 50 years or older with a history of stroke, residing in 18 European countries, were included.AnalysisBinary logistic regression models were used to examine associations between the weekly frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity and depression. Analyses were stratified by sex and adjusted for potential confounders.Main measurementsDepression was assessed using the 12-item European Depression Scale. Weekly moderate-vigorous physical activity frequency was categorized as <1 time per week, 1 time per week, or >1 time per week.ResultsAdjusted results showed that, for men, engaging in moderate physical activity once (odds ratio = 0.60) or more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.49) reduced the odds of depression. For vigorous physical activity, the benefit in men required a frequency of more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.61). Among women, moderate-vigorous physical activity significantly reduced the risk of depression only when performed more than once a week (odds ratio = 0.58 and 0.43, respectively).ConclusionIn individuals aged 50 or older with a history of stroke, the weekly frequency of moderate-vigorous physical activity was associated with lower odds of depression in both sexes. However, the benefits of this association vary by sex.

articles.title: Robustness Gap of Large Language Models in Nephrology.
Effects of red wine and its compounds on cardiac and endothelial function in human tissue.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although beneficial effects of red wine and its polyphenols have been described, data on direct effects on pulmonary arteries and human myocardium are sparse, and claims remain controversial given well-known alcohol-related harms.

AIMS: This study investigated acute and subacute effects of red wine, dealcoholized red wine and key polyphenols (trans/cis-resveratrol, caffeic acid, gallic acid) on human atrial and ventricular myocardium and pulmonary arteries.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In human atrial trabeculae and failing left ventricular slices from heart transplant recipients (n = 6), polyphenols increased developed force significantly (+39% caffeic acid, +27% gallic acid, +17% trans-resveratrol, +10% cis-resveratrol; control -34%, p < 0.05) and red wine (10-4: +18%) compared with control (-23%, p < 0.0001), without affecting diastolic properties or inducing arrhythmias. In failing human left ventricular myocardium, twitch amplitude increased over 7 days with alcoholic and dealcoholized red wine (p = 0.0177) compared with control, while preserving the negative force-frequency relationship and post-rest potentiation. In preconstricted human pulmonary arteries, red wines induced a rapid, sustained 80% relaxation independent of ethanol content. L-NAME reduced human pulmonary artery relaxation from 59% to 28% (p < 0.05), confirming partial endothelial nitric-oxide mediation.

CONCLUSION: Red wine and its bioactive compounds exert robust dual inotropic and pulmonary vasodilatory actions independent of alcohol. Dealcoholized red wine as an adjunctive strategy may represent a promising avenue toward integrated cardiopulmonary therapy in heart failure and precapillary pulmonary hypertension. A clinical trial (DARE-WINE-PH, DRKS00035605) is underway to validate acute haemodynamic effects in patients with precapillary pulmonary hypertension.

articles.title: Effect of a polynutraceutical juice (Indian gooseberry, ginger and curry leaves) as an adjunct to oral antidiabetic drugs on fasting blood glucose in type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDiabetes is an escalating global health priority, significantly impacting low- and middle-income countries like India.AimTo evaluate the effectiveness of a polynutraceutical juice comprising Indian gooseberry-ginger-curry leaves on fasting blood glucose (FBG) levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsA 1-month open-label randomized controlled trial was conducted among 120 adults with T2DM attending a non-communicable disease clinic in Puducherry, India. Participants were randomly allocated to receive either the polynutraceutical juice plus standard oral antidiabetic drugs (OADs) (n = 60) or OADs alone (n = 60). FBG was measured at baseline and after 4 weeks. Within-group changes were analysed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, between-group differences using Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons, and a post hoc analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was performed to adjust for baseline FBG, age and gender.SummaryOf the 120 randomized participants, 112 completed the study. The experimental group (n = 55) showed a significant reduction in FBG (mean decrease: 20.3 mg/dL; p < 0.001), whereas the control group (n = 57) showed no significant change (mean decrease: 4.7 mg/dL; p = 0.068). Between-group analysis demonstrated a significant advantage for the intervention (Bonferroni correction p = 0.012). However, after adjustment for baseline FBG, age and gender, the treatment effect was attenuated and did not reach conventional statistical significance (ANCOVA p = 0.060), although clinically meaningful reductions in FBG were observed. The polynutraceutical juice may provide clinically meaningful short-term improvements in FBG when used alongside standard OAD therapy. Larger placebo-controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Use of routinely collected administrative data to define pediatric critical care admission in British Columbia, Canada: a validation study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Administrative health data are essential for quantifying incidence and long-term outcomes associated with pediatric critical illness but rely on reliable capture and coding of hospitalizations with pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission. The accuracy of administrative data capture of pediatric critical care admission in Canada is unknown.

METHODS: We assessed the performance of the Discharge Abstract Database (DAD), which captures all hospitalizations in British Columbia, Canada for identifying pediatric critical care admission by comparing records to the Virtual Pediatric Systems (VPS, LLC, Los Angeles, CA), a prospectively collected database of PICU admissions at British Columbia Children's Hospital, British Columbia's only dedicated pediatric quaternary care hospital. We identified all hospitalizations for children younger than 18 years at British Columbia Children's Hospital between 2014 and 2023 and used presence of PICU days in the DAD to identify possible PICU admissions. We then matched the DAD records to the VPS records via exact admission date to determine the performance of this case definition (presence of PICU days) both overall, and across subgroups. We evaluated the accuracy of PICU admission characteristics and outcomes reporting in the DAD using VPS as the reference standard.

RESULTS: A total of 63,256 admissions were included, of which 8891 had an indicator for PICU admission in the DAD. Of these, 8729 had a positive validation record for PICU admission in the VPS database at British Columbia Children's Hospital. There were 123 admissions to the PICU in the VPS database that were not captured in the DAD. The case definition had excellent sensitivity (96.3%; 95% CI = 95.9, 96.7) and specificity (99.7%; 95% CI = 99.7, 99.7). Results were consistent across subgroups. DAD definitions of admission type, PICU length of stay, inter-hospital transfer status, receipt of invasive mechanical ventilation, and mortality all showed sensitivity and specificity ≥ 85%.

CONCLUSION: Using a large validation sample of PICU admissions from a quaternary care centre, we found that routinely collected administrative data on hospitalizations in Canada had high accuracy for classifying and characterizing PICU admissions.

articles.title: Workspace Layouts and Their Effects on Healthcare Staff Communication in Neonatal Intensive Care Units.
articles.abstract: BackgroundModern Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs) increasingly adopt single-family room (SFR) layouts with decentralized workspaces. While these designs support patient privacy and family-centered care, they can isolate staff and reduce opportunities for team communication.ObjectivesThis study examined a hybrid neighborhood layout combining decentralized nurse stations (DNSs) and centralized Huddle Stations within each neighborhood, focusing on their effects on staff communication.MethodsWe conducted onsite observations and shadowed 60 staff members, collecting 2,564 behavioral data points. Statistical analyses explored staff activities by role, communication type and mode, and location, with a focus on face-to-face interactions in various work areas. In addition, we conducted Space Syntax and targeted visual connectivity analyses between Huddle Stations, DNSs, patient rooms, and patient beds, and interpreted the findings alongside behavioral data.ResultsCommunication patterns differed by staff role and location. Huddle Stations served as communication hubs for non-physician staff members, supporting distinct communication types compared to DNSs and workrooms. Despite similar physical layouts, neighborhoods varied in mutual visibility between workstations and patient rooms. These differences suggest that staff may experience varying opportunities of social interaction based on patient room assignments.ConclusionsHuddle Stations anchor social interactions, and a neighborhood design that incorporates both DNSs and Huddle Stations can support staff communication in SFR-NICUs. Achieving equitable visual connectivity while accommodating role-based task patterns requires both spatial analysis and real-world observations when planning and designing future NICU environments.

articles.title: Toxicity assessment of ultra-processed foods on human erythrocytes and Drosophila melanogaster.
articles.abstract: BackgroundUltra-processed foods (UPFs) are recognized as major dietary risk factors associated with obesity, cardiovascular disease, cancer, type 2 diabetes, and mental health disorders. According to the NOVA classification, UPFs are industrial formulations containing additives such as colorants, flavor enhancers, emulsifiers, and sweeteners, which contribute to their low nutritional value and high energy density. Diets rich in UPFs can disrupt gut microbiota, promote inflammation and oxidative stress, and introduce genotoxic and carcinogenic risks through certain additives. Furthermore, packaging and contact materials may also contribute to adverse health effects.AimThis study evaluated the in vitro and in vivo toxicity of UPFs in human erythrocytes and Drosophila melanogaster, respectively.MethodsHydroalcoholic extracts were prepared from each UPF, and hemolytic activity was evaluated in human erythrocytes. In vivo toxicity was assessed in a wild type strain of Drosophila melanogaster, with average survival and sex ratio used as biomarkers.SummaryPulparindo®, Svelty® powdered milk, and the hot sauces Valentina® and Costa Brava® showed the highest hemolytic activity in human erythrocytes. Additives including sodium benzoate, synthetic antioxidants, and artificial colorants were linked to the observed toxicity. Evidence from Drosophila melanogaster supports these findings, underscoring the health risks of frequent UPF intake and the need for public policies promoting healthier food options in Mexico.

articles.title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear.

METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings.
