articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

articles.title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown.

METHODS: Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors.

RESULTS: Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction.

CONCLUSIONS: Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.

articles.title: Targeting Mediator Kinase Attenuates Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Enhancer Utilization.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by extensive transcriptional remodeling that contributes to the progression of heart failure. Preclinical models demonstrate that therapies targeting hypertrophic responses can mitigate disease severity. Recent evidence shows that failing human and murine hearts exhibit elevated mediator kinase expression, sufficient to drive eccentric hypertrophy and heart failure through activation of hypertrophic gene programs. Mediator kinase inhibition suppresses oncogenic transcription by altering enhancer utilization, suggesting similar mechanisms may attenuate pathological remodeling in the heart. This study investigates whether mediator kinase inhibition can blunt cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for heart failure.

METHODS: Two structurally unrelated mediator kinase inhibitors, Senexin A (SxnA) and CCT251545, were tested in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Hypertrophy was assessed by cell size measurements, RNA sequencing, and H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing.

RESULTS: Mediator kinase inhibition significantly reduced hypertrophic growth, attenuating cell size increases induced by phenylephrine (PE) and endothelin-1. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a dose-dependent suppression of PE-induced differentially expressed genes in Senexin A-treated cells. Mechanistically, PE stimulation enhanced RNA polymerase II pause release, whereas Mediator kinase inhibition did not alter this process. Epigenomic analysis showed that PE markedly increased the number of super-enhancers relative to vehicle treatment, while co-treatment with Senexin A reduced the total number of active enhancers. Nearest-neighbor analysis linked putative regulatory enhancers to key PE-responsive genes, and these enhancer signatures were blunted by SxnA.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that Mediator kinase inhibition counteracts hypertrophic growth and transcriptional reprogramming, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy to modulate pathological gene regulation in cardiac hypertrophy.

articles.title: Integrative Genomic Analyses Identify Collagen Type XXI Alpha 1 Chain and ENPEP-Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 Regulatory Pathways for Blood Pressure Variation in East Asian People.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes are common cardiometabolic disorders that may share genetic and environmental risk factors. However, the regulatory genes and tissue-specific mechanisms underlying blood pressure variations remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Leveraging a well-characterized prospective population-based cohort comprised of 27 308 participants from the SCHS (Singapore Chinese Health Study), we evaluated genome-wide genetic associations for 5 blood pressure traits: hypertension status, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure and pulse pressure. Additionally, we conducted a transcriptome-wide association study, integrating gene expression data from 49 tissues, followed by colocalization and fine-mapping to prioritize regulatory genes. Association of identified variants with incident diabetes was additionally evaluated in the longitudinal data.

RESULTS: We validated 10 blood pressure loci (P between 1.64×10-20-4.10×10-8) and identified an East Asian-specific splice donor variant at the COL21A1 gene associated with pulse pressure (rs149344559, P=6.78×10-10). Integrative analyses prioritized FGF5 in kidney cortex and ENPEP in pituitary tissue as candidate regulatory genes. The blood pressure-lowering allele at ENPEP (T allele, rs1879056) was associated with reduced risk of incident diabetes. Mediation analysis demonstrated that ∼20.1% of the genetic association with diabetes was mediated through mean arterial pressure (Pindirect-effect<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study refines genetic predispositions for blood pressure among East Asian individuals. We further delineate tissue-specific regulatory pathways underlying blood pressure variations and identify ENPEP-mediated dysfunctions linking blood pressure genetics to diabetes risk, underscoring integrated disease mechanisms.

articles.title: Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework.

RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations.

CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

articles.title: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.

articles.title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood.

METHODS: Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing.

CONCLUSIONS: PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

articles.title: Greater Neighborhood Resources Predict Reduced In-Hospital Death for Children With Heart Failure and Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with pediatric heart failure (HF) face significant morbidity and death. However, there are limited data describing neighborhood characteristics in pediatric patients with HF or exploring the relationship of these factors to resource use and clinical outcomes. We used the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (COI), a composite index of community resources pertinent to child health, to describe neighborhood characteristics for children with HF and identify its associations with in-hospital death.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Pediatric Health Information System, a national administrative database of tertiary care pediatric hospitals. Inpatient encounters between January 2014 and December 2024 for pediatric patients (aged <18 years) with HF and cardiomyopathy were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. The primary exposure of interest was the COI, and the primary outcome of interest was in-hospital death. Mixed logistic regression models were estimated, unadjusted and adjusted for administrative sex, age, race, and primary payor.

RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of index HF admissions in 7060 patients. Half of the cohort was in either the very low (n=2034 [29%]) or low (n=1521 [22%]) COI quintile. After adjustment, patients with a very high COI were less likely to experience in-hospital death than those living in very low COI neighborhoods (odds ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]; P=0.048).

CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of children admitted with HF have limited neighborhood resources. Those with higher neighborhood resources are more likely to survive to discharge, emphasizing the relationship between environmental factors and clinical outcomes in pediatric HF.

articles.title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS: Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination.

CONCLUSIONS: Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.

articles.title: Neuropsychological and Quality-of-Life Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage often have long-term neuropsychological disturbances. This study aims to characterize depressive symptoms, quality of life, and personality changes in a large cohort of survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included patients with a history of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from the Brain Aneurysm Foundation patient registry. Patients completed the Beck Depression Inventory-II and the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life scale, and family members completed the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Multiple linear regression was used to identify symptoms associated with reduced work productivity. Wilcoxon and chi-square tests were used to identify variables associated with severity of depressive symptoms and personality changes.

RESULTS: A total of 318 patients were included, with 242 completing the Beck Depression Inventory-II and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life, and 112 family members completing the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Moderate depressive symptoms were reported by 18% of patients, and severe symptoms were reported by 11%. Impairments in thinking, social roles, language, and energy were independently associated with reduced work productivity. Acquired personality disturbances were observed in 72% of patients for executive function, 44% for social behavior, 49% for hypomotivation, 50% for irascibility, and 72% for distress. Ruptured aneurysms in the anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery were associated with a trend toward a higher prevalence of moderate to severe depressive symptoms and executive personality changes.

CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms and personality changes are common after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, affecting work productivity. Recognizing challenges in thinking, social interactions, language, and vulnerability to pressure may help guide targeted interventions by families, employers, and health care providers.

articles.title: Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort.

METHODS: Proteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication.

RESULTS: MR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users.

CONCLUSIONS: Our genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.

articles.title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).

METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.

RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).

CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

articles.title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle-branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit.

METHODS: Twenty-four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within-subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd.

RESULTS: LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd, compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing, 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P<0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement (ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg; all P<0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18-29 milliseconds).

CONCLUSIONS: Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic-optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical-optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.

articles.title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit.

METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h).

RESULTS: The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction.

CONCLUSIONS: A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.

articles.title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown.

METHODS: We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules.

RESULTS: NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP.

CONCLUSIONS: NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

articles.title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma and microvascular complications in patients with type 2 diabetes achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol targets: a real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets, patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain at significant risk for microvascular complications. We aimed to investigate whether the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), a marker of atherogenic dyslipidaemia, is associated with these complications in a real-world cohort of patients with controlled LDL-C.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from community health centres in Shenzhen, China (2018-2024). We included 16,469 participants with T2DM and LDL-C<2.6 mmol/L at baseline, categorising them into tertiles (T1-3) based on baseline AIP. The primary outcome was a composite of incident diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, identified via ICD-10 codes. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to assess associations.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.6 years, 1,056 participants developed microvascular complications. We observed a graded association between AIP tertiles and the risk of microvascular complications. Participants in T3 had a significantly higher risk of total microvascular complications than those in T1 (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.15-1.56), while T2 showed no statistically significant increase in risk (HR = 1.10; 95% CI = 0.94-1.28). Specifically, compared to T1, T3 participants had significantly higher risks of diabetic nephropathy (HR = 1.62; 95% CI = 1.30-2.01) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (HR = 1.39; 95% CI = 1.13-1.70), while no statistically significant association was found for diabetic retinopathy risk (HR = 1.23; 95% CI = 0.93-1.63). In contrast, compared with T1 participants, those in T2 had higher risks of nephropathy (HR = 1.28; 95% CI = 1.02-1.59), but no statistically significant associations were found for diabetic peripheral neuropathy or diabetic retinopathy.

CONCLUSIONS: We found that AIP is independently associated with increased risk of microvascular complications, particularly diabetic nephropathy and diabetic peripheral neuropathy, even in T2DM patients achieving LDL-C targets. These results suggest that AIP may serve as a simple, lipid-based marker to help identify patients with residual microvascular risk beyond conventional LDL-C control.

articles.title: Risk factors for endometrial cancer incidence and regional and ethnic disparities in the USA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynaecologic cancer in the USA and a major cause of cancer-associated mortality among women. We aimed to identify the independent contributions of individual- and contextual-level factors to EC incidence.

METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal retrospective cohort study using anonymised data from women aged 18 years and above without EC included in the All of Us Research database before 1 January 2017. We followed participants from study entry until October 2023 (median follow-up = 6.6 years). We used mixed-effects Cox regression models to examine data from individuals nested within ZIP-code areas and states, analysing individual-level risk factors and neighbourhood-level socioeconomic predictors in addition to adjusting for area-level clustering.

RESULTS: Of 81,171 eligible women followed for 496,709 person-years, 778 (0.96%) developed EC. The risk of EC risk approximately thrice as high among women aged 50-59 years (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 2.92; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.20-3.88), 60-69 years (aHR = 2.97; 95% CI = 2.21-4.00), and ≥70 years (aHR = 2.86; 95% CI = 2.02-4.06) than among women under 40 years of age. Non-Hispanic White women had a 44% higher risk than non-Hispanic Black women (aHR = 1.44; 95% CI = 1.15-1.80). Obesity was associated with more than twice the risk of EC (aHR = 2.16; 95% CI = 1.85-2.52), while diabetes was associated with a 27% higher risk (aHR = 1.27; 95% CI = 1.06-1.51).

CONCLUSION: Individual-level factors, particularly age and obesity, were the main predictors of EC incidence. Prevention efforts should prioritise obesity reduction, age-specific screening awareness, and lifestyle modifications.

articles.title: The impact of kidney dysfunction on functional outcomes in a convalescent rehabilitation ward: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) impairs physical function and activities of daily living, yet the relationship between CKD severity and inpatient rehabilitation outcomes in patients who have not started dialysis remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 10 832 patients admitted to a convalescent rehabilitation ward between April 2014 and March 2023. Patients were stratified by CKD stage based on estimated glomerular filtration rate and grouped into  mild or no kidney dysfunction (stages 1-3a) and advanced kidney dysfunction (stages 3b-5). Functional outcomes were evaluated using the Functional Independence Measure at admission and discharge. Key outcomes were functional independence measure gain, functional independence measure efficiency (functional independence measure gain per hospital day), functional independence measure effectiveness (proportion of potential improvement achieved) and length of stay. Between-group and stage-based comparisons were performed using analysis of covariance adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: Among the 10 832 patients (mean age 73.1 ± 14.9 years), 3361 (31.0%) had CKD stages 3a-5. Individuals in the kidney dysfunction group were older and had lower serum albumin and hemoglobin than those in the non-kidney dysfunction group. Compared to patients with mild or no kidney dysfunction, those in the kidney dysfunction group had shorter length of stay (52.6 ± 31.7 vs 59.6 ± 39.4 days, P < .001), lower gain in functional independence measure (14.6 ± 14.4 vs 16.9 ± 15.5 points, P < .001), and reduced functional independence measure effectiveness (0.34 ± 0.35 vs 0.40 ± 0.39, P < .001), whereas functional independence measure efficiency did not differ between groups (P = .98).

CONCLUSIONS: Kidney dysfunction was independently associated with less functional improvement and worse functional independence measure effectiveness during convalescent rehabilitation, partially due to shorter hospitalization and reduced total rehabilitation dose. Tailored rehabilitation programs that address kidney dysfunction-related vulnerabilities, including nutritional and metabolic optimization, may enhance recovery outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Multidimensional sleep health: risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality, and mediation by plasma proteins.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep health is a recognised determinant of cardiovascular health, but most previous research has examined individual sleep traits in relation to cardiovascular disease and mortality. The molecular pathways linking multidimensional sleep health to these outcomes remain insufficiently explored. We aimed to examine these associations and identify circulating proteins showing potential mediation signals in these relationships.

METHODS: We analysed data on 257,509 individuals from the UK Biobank, including 26,984 with available plasma proteomic data. Using baseline questionnaire data collected by UK Biobank, we calculated a seven-component sleep health score (SHS) and derived data-driven sleep patterns using K-prototypes clustering. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to examine the associations of the SHS and, separately, the sleep patterns with incident coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation and heart failure, as well as cardiovascular and overall mortality. Lastly, we identified SHS-related proteins using linear regression, with representative proteins selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and mediation analyses performed.

RESULTS: Higher SHS was associated with lower risks of coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, cardiovascular mortality, and overall mortality, with the strongest associations observed for heart failure and coronary heart disease. Mixed sleep disturbance and non-restorative sleep patterns were associated with higher risks across multiple outcomes. Proteomic analyses identified 188 SHS-related proteins, mainly enriched in inflammatory, immune, and chemotactic pathways. Exploratory mediation analyses identified 34 proteins with potential mediation signals, among which HGF, IGF2R, and FABP4 showed recurrent cross-outcome signals.

CONCLUSIONS: Poor multidimensional sleep health was associated with higher cardiovascular disease and mortality risks, with exploratory proteomic analyses suggesting potential involvement of circulating proteins related to inflammation, immunity, chemotaxis, and metabolic dysregulation. These findings support multidimensional sleep assessment as a population-level prevention strategy and provide candidate molecular pathways for future mechanistic and interventional studies.

articles.title: Associated factors and outcomes of social activity restriction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a real-world longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social activity restriction has emerged as a new public health challenge; the factors associated with social activity restriction and its outcomes in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are not yet clear. In this study, we aimed to describe the clinical characteristics of socially restricted COPD patients and to evaluate the effects of social activity restriction on acute exacerbation and mortality.

METHODS: We included participants enrolled in the RealDTC study between December 2016 and August 2020. We collected data on demographics, degree of social activity restriction, lung function, Clinical COPD Questionnaire score, and mortality at four years. We used multivariable regression analyses to examine whether restricted social activity was associated with the risks of acute exacerbation and mortality.

RESULTS: We included 3,679 patients in total. Their mean age was 65.72 (standard deviation = 9.1) years, and 11.3% had restricted social activities. Older age, widowhood, GOLD grades 3-4, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease groups B and D, history of acute exacerbation, COPD Assessment Test score of ≥10, and Modified Medical Research Council score of ≥2 were independently associated with social activity restriction. By multivariable analysis, patients with restricted social activities had higher risks of future acute exacerbation (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.320; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.100-1.583, P = 0.003) and severe acute exacerbation (aOR = 1.299; 95% CI = 1.014-1.664, P = 0.038). Furthermore, restricted social activity was an independent risk factor for mortality (hazard ratio = 1.752, 95% CI = 1.298-2.364, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Restricted social activity was not uncommon among patients with COPD. Social activity restriction should be routinely assessed in COPD clinics as a simple marker to identify patients at increased risk of exacerbation and mortality. During future epidemics or pandemics, public health responses should be more flexible, risk-stratified, and patient-centred for individuals with chronic respiratory disease. Future interventional and policy studies are needed to determine whether systematic assessment of social activity restriction and targeted supportive programs can improve outcomes in socially restricted patients with COPD.

articles.title: Systemic sclerosis markedly impairs health-related quality of life: a single-centre tertiary cohort study with literature-based comparison to leading causes of global disease burden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune condition that significantly impacts the physical and mental health of affected individuals, disrupting their daily life and overall well-being. However, its impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has not been thoroughly compared to other chronic diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and stroke, the impact of which is clearly established. We explored how SSc influences HRQoL and compared its effect to that of six chronic diseases, considered the global leading causes of disease burden in high-income countries, and three common rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases.

METHODS: We collected HRQoL data from SSc patients enrolled in a cross-sectional observational study at The Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust, UK. We used the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 to measure HRQoL and compared the participants' scores to published data on unipolar major depression, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, lung cancer, osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain. Mean norm-based transformed scores (NBS) were compared for all eight SF-36 health domains.

RESULTS: The 121 SSc patients (106 female; mean age = 57 years, standard deviation = 12.3), disease duration mean = 9.50 years, standard deviation = 7.4) in our study reported significantly worse perceived general health (mean (x̄) NBS = 32.82) than the other nine diseases reported in the literature. Role limitations due to physical problems (x̄ NBS = 34.77) were comparable to stroke, RA, and lung cancer. Significant impairments were noted in bodily pain (x̄ NBS = 36), similar to osteoarthritis, RA, and lower back pain, as well as vitality (x̄ NBS = 39.69), comparable to RA. Emotional role limitations (x̄ NBS = 41.78) were second only to major depression, similar to stroke and RA.

CONCLUSIONS: We found that SSc has a substantial impact on HRQoL, resulting in significant physical and psychological impairment comparable to that experienced by patients with RA and stroke. These findings contextualise the burden of SSc and may inform future research and clinical practice aimed at improving patient care.

articles.title: Improving equity in respiratory disease outcomes in Africa using data-driven tools: National Institute of Health Care and Research's (NIHR) EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, influenza, asthma, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and COVID-19 are all prevalent in Africa, where they cause a very large burden on the population's health, but are managed by health systems with a limited capacity for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. They are also underlaid by substantial inequities in outcomes, with the poorest who have no access to care being affected the most. An interdisciplinary group of academics, policymakers, representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs), patients, and civil society are implementing a programme to address key respiratory diseases (RD) in five African countries where morbidity and mortality from RD is very large: Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, and South Africa. The aim is to build capacity, conduct quality research and an intervention trial, and engage communities and policymakers in order to achieve demonstrable and equitable reductions in morbidity and mortality from RD through evidence-based improvements in prevention, diagnosis, treatment, interventions, and policies. The EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project will map the landscape of respiratory medicine in partner countries through rapid reviews of the available literature and data; engage relevant in-country stakeholders; study patients' and providers' preferences and needs; identify research priorities using the Child Health and Nutrition Research Initiative method; and conduct summer schools for capacity building in data science and machine learning/artificial intelligence, in community engagement, and in advocacy for and the use of the Equitable Impact Sensitive Tool (EQUIST) and Pathways to Survival (PATHS) tool. The project will also assess national health system preparedness for emerging infections, identify bottlenecks for early response, assess oxygen capacity and security, study adherence to international guidelines, and conduct qualitative studies to understand barriers to seeking care. It will also explore the feasibility of delivering a pulmonary rehabilitation programme through a randomised controlled trial. Ultimately, the programme will link evidence with policy using the EQUIST and PATHS tools to improve equity in outcomes and identify bottlenecks that lead to morbidity and mortality from respiratory causes. Through high-level meetings, it will prioritise the implementation of equitable interventions that are appropriate to each African context and tailored to patients' needs. A team of social scientists and NGOs, joined by a team of researchers of diverse backgrounds, will engage communities, stakeholders and policymakers to build capacity through summer schools, and disseminate the results through a dedicated project website, the Journal of Global Health, the Journal of the Pan-African Thoracic Society, collaborating NGOs, and mainstream and social media.

articles.title: Milk-Volume Monitoring During Breastfeeding: Why Digital Innovation Needs Clinical and Biological Context.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract: Digital and biomedical technologies are increasingly reshaping maternal, neonatal, and lactation care. This perspective critically examines the clinical meaning, potential benefits, and possible unintended consequences of continuous digital milk-volume monitoring during breastfeeding, using a recently described compact wireless system as a case example. Milk-volume estimates may support clinical decision-making in selected settings, particularly neonatal intensive care and the care of late preterm, medically fragile, or feeding-compromised infants, when interpreted within a comprehensive lactation assessment that considers growth, hydration, feeding effectiveness, and maternal factors. Such interpretation is essential because milk volume alone cannot establish breastfeeding adequacy or capture the dynamic, biologically active, and compositionally variable nature of human milk. In physiological breastfeeding, routine numerical monitoring may medicalize a relational process by shifting attention from infant feeding cues, maternal confidence, and mother-infant interaction toward numerical targets, potentially reinforcing maternal anxiety. Collaboration between engineering and health sciences is therefore essential to ensure that digital monitoring enriches, rather than replaces, professional assessment within a shared clinical, biological, relational, and ethical framework.

articles.title: Metal-Organic Framework Assisted Sample Preparation Enables High-Depth Proteomics of Laser-Captured Trace Kidney Microregions.
articles.abstract: Region-resolved proteomics based on laser capture microdissection (LCM) enables molecular characterization of solid organ heterogeneity but is limited by severe protein loss and shallow coverage in trace tissue samples. Here, we adapted and optimized a quadruple boronic acid-rich lanthanide metal-organic framework (qMOFs)-aided sample preparation workflow (MASP) for LCM-derived trace kidney tissues and benchmarked its performance against conventional filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) across tissue inputs of 0.25-1.5 mm2. Notably, MASP identified at least 6248 protein groups from 0.25 mm2 of tissue, approximately three times the maximum number of 2042 protein groups identified by FASP from 1.5 mm2 of tissue. We further applied this workflow to region-resolved proteomic profiling of renal cortex and medulla in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) mouse model, identifying regional proteomic differences between cortical and medullary microregions and changes in mitochondrial protein abundance in cortical samples from Sham and CLP mice. This work extends MASP to microdissected solid tissues and provides a robust platform for high-depth region-resolved proteomics of heterogeneous organs, enabling systematic investigation of region-specific molecular alterations in disease.

articles.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
articles.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.

articles.title: A Rapid Lithium Ion-Based Transformation Method for Kluyveromyces lactis.
articles.abstract: Kluyveromyces lactis is a budding yeast host useful for recombinant protein production; however, its transformation often relies on electroporation due to the perceived low efficiency of chemical methods, thereby limiting throughput. In this study, we developed a robust, small-scale chemical transformation protocol (using 15 μL of competent cells) that achieves high efficiency, particularly with linear DNA. No significant differences in efficiency were observed between lithium chloride and lithium acetate, nor across concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 1.0 M, for making cells competent. The addition of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) during heat shock enhanced colony counts, while ethanol inhibited the process. When PCR fragments containing the optimized pan-genomic autonomous replication sequence (PanARS-OPT) were used for transformation, the transformation efficiency was approximately 7-fold higher than that of circular plasmids, yielding over 105 transformants/μg DNA. This high efficiency with linear DNA can be due to a potent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) activity in K. lactis. This rapid, "one-tube" method eliminates the need for plasmid construction and specialized equipment, offering a tool for rapid and high-throughput genetic engineering in K. lactis.

articles.title: Is segregation bad for your heart?: a natural experiment for residential racial segregation exposure during childhood and cardiovascular disease risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residential racial segregation is hypothesized to cause inequities in cardiovascular disease. Yet existing work is largely associational and has rarely tested longitudinal effects of childhood segregation on later CVD. Here, we leverage quasi-random urban planning decisions in Northern US cities prior to the Great Migration as an instrument for segregation as Black families moved North, providing a natural experiment.

METHODS: We followed Ananat's work showing railroad track configurations serve as an instrument for segregation at the metropolitan area level. We linked Ananat's data to the birthplaces of participants in the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (1968-1994, n=829 Black & 1,262 White), following them through 2023. Race-stratified accelerated failure time models used an instrumental variables design and cluster bootstrapping, progressively adjusting for other railroad features, socioeconomic status, and birth year.

RESULTS: Estimates suggest childhood residential segregation causally delays the onset of CVD or hypertension for White people but speeds it up for Black people, though confidence intervals and instrument strength varied across model specifications. Non-instrumented models directly adjusting for confounders yielded strongly attenuated results in the same direction.

CONCLUSION: Segregation is likely a cause of Black-White CVD inequities, not just a correlate. Causal designs across the life course are needed.

articles.title: Organizational Support and Burnout Among Rural Youth-Serving Professionals: Implications for Workforce Well-Being and Retention.
articles.abstract: Burnout among youth-serving professionals represents a growing concern for both workforce stability and public health, particularly in rural and underserved communities where professionals may face high emotional demands, trauma-exposed service environments, and limited organizational resources. This study examined associations among perceived organizational support, leadership, emotional work demands, work-family conflict, burnout, and job satisfaction among rural youth-serving professionals. A cross-sectional quantitative survey included 128 professionals working in juvenile justice, public health, probation, social service, administrative, and community-based youth-serving systems in rural regions of New York State. Recruitment was coordinated through Clinton County-based professional and organizational networks. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, reliability analyses, and multiple regression analyses were used to examine associations among study variables. Higher perceived organizational support and more positive leadership ratings were associated with lower burnout and greater job satisfaction, whereas emotional work demands and work-family conflict were associated with higher burnout and lower job satisfaction. The multivariable models accounted for 51% of the variance in burnout and 46% of the variance in job satisfaction. These findings highlight organizational and psychosocial workplace conditions that may be relevant to workforce well-being and retention in rural youth-serving systems.

articles.title: Hydrazone-derived PET/CHEF fluorescent probes for sensitive detection of cesium and strontium in real samples.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: In this study, two hydrazone-based probes, NSP ((E)-5-(diethylamino)-2-((2-(2,4-dinitrophenyl)hydrazineylidene)methyl)phenol) and NFH ((E)-N'-(4-(diethylamino)-2-hydroxybenzylidene)furan-2-carbohydrazide), were developed and synthesized for the specific detection of Cs+ and Sr2+ ions, respectively. Both probes were very sensitive, with low detection limits of 2.4 nM for Cs+ and 22 nM for Sr2+, along with high selectivity over other metal ions. The binding constant is 4.8 × 107 M-1 for NSP-Cs+ and 6.4 × 105 M-1 for NFH-Sr2+. Job's plot analysis confirmed a 1 : 1 binding stoichiometry between the probes and their corresponding metal ions. The NSP- and NFH-functionalized cotton swabs exhibit excellent stability, highlighting their potential for portable and on-site detection. Complementarily, their efficacy was demonstrated in actual samples, including water, soil, and vegetable matrices, achieving excellent recovery results.

articles.title: Identifying activities and participation domains with severe dependence using the ICF-based LIMOS-Br in chronic stroke.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify activities and participation domains with severe dependence based on LIMOS-Br (Lucerne ICF-based Multidisciplinary Observational Scale-Brazilian version) scores and to evaluate the clinical utility of the instrument in individuals with chronic stroke.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 100 post-stroke individuals. Functioning was assessed using the LIMOS-Br. Descriptive and severity-based analyses (scores 1-2; >20% frequency threshold) were performed to identify activities and participation domains with severe dependence. Clinical utility was assessed using the Clinical Utility Scale.

RESULTS: Severity-based analysis revealed a discrepancy between prevalence and severity. While limitations in climbing stairs (90%) and changing body position (79%) were highly prevalent, others were characterized by both high prevalence and substantial severity, including walking long distances (82% prevalence; 33% severe dependence) and moving around (85% prevalence; 24% severe dependence). These, together with fine hand use (35%), complex domestic tasks (29%), and writing (28%), were identified as domains with severe dependence, all exceeding the 20% threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: Community mobility, fine hand use, and complex domestic activities showed the greatest frequency of severe dependence in this sample. The LIMOS-Br showed preliminary evidence of clinical utility and provides a standardized ICF-based measure to complement rehabilitation planning in chronic stroke survivors.

articles.title: Antibiotic Resistance in India Over a Decade: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical and Molecular Evidence (2015-2025).
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a major global public health threat that compromises the effectiveness of antibiotic agents and increases morbidity, mortality, and health care costs. India faces a substantial AMR burden driven by high infectious disease prevalence, widespread antibiotic use, and variable surveillance capacity. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize evidence on antibiotic resistance patterns in India from 2015 to 2025, estimate the prevalence of resistance among major bacterial pathogens, evaluate molecular resistance determinants, and assess mortality associated with resistant infections. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, surveillance reports, and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies reporting antibiotic resistance data from India between January 2015 and December 2025 were included. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed independently by 2 reviewers. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of antibiotic resistance, molecular determinants of resistance, and mortality outcomes, and heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q and I2 statistics. Forty-six studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of antibiotic resistance was 55.7% (95% CI: 47.4%-63.9%; I2=98.6%). High resistance rates were reported among major gram-negative pathogens, particularly Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Molecular meta-analysis demonstrated a pooled prevalence of resistance-associated genes of 64.5% (95% CI: 46.0%-83.0%), with blaNDM, blaOXA-48-like, and blaKPC being the most frequently reported determinants. Mortality associated with resistant infections was 31.0% (95% CI: 18.2%-43.8%). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across all analyses. Available evidence indicates that antibiotic resistance remains a significant health care challenge in India. High levels of multidrug resistance, widespread dissemination of carbapenemase genes, and considerable mortality associated with resistant infections underscore the need for strengthened antibiotic stewardship, standardized surveillance, expanded molecular diagnostics, and coordinated public health interventions. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity and the predominance of studies from tertiary-care settings. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261406324).
