articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes

articles.title: Continuous-Flow Left Ventricular Assist Devices in Biventricular Configuration: A Systematic Review and Comparative Meta-Analysis of HeartMate 3 and HeartWare Biventricular Assist Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced biventricular heart failure may require durable biventricular assist device (BiVAD) support when heart transplantation is not immediately feasible or patients are ineligible for heart transplantation. We aimed to compare baseline characteristics, perioperative features, and clinical outcomes between patients supported with HeartMate 3-BiVAD (HM3-BiVAD) and HeartWare-BiVAD (HW-BiVAD).

METHODS: A systematic search was performed in October 2025 across MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and CINAHL. We identified studies of adult patients supported with dual HeartMate 3 LVAD and HeartWare HVAD continuous-flow pumps in a BiVAD configuration. Study-level data were pooled to compare patients supported with HM3-BiVAD and those with HW-BiVAD.

RESULTS: The proportion of females was significantly lower among HM3-BiVAD patients [HM3: 4.8% (95% CI: 1.2, 17.1) vs. HW: 22.5% (16.8, 29.4), p = 0.02], whereas patient age was comparable between groups [HM3: 47 (43, 52) years vs. HW: 48 (45, 50) years, p = 0.9]. Chronic kidney disease [HM3: 57.1% (23, 85.6) vs. HW: 10.9% (4.6, 23.6), p = 0.01] was more common among HM3-BiVAD patients. Concomitant right ventricular assist device (RVAD) placement was the predominant approach across both groups [HM3: 66.2% (35.5, 87.4) vs. HW: 78.5% (70.1, 85), p = 0.36]. Right atrium was used more frequently as RVAD implantation site in the HM3-BiVAD group [HM3: 96.7% (63.4, 99.8) vs. HW: 33.9% (19, 52.9), p = 0.01], whereas the right ventricle predominated in the HW-BiVAD group [HM3: 3.2% (0.2, 36.6) vs. HW: 64.5% (45.2, 80.1), p = 0.01]. Overall survival was significantly higher among HM3-BiVAD patients [78.1% (49.3, 92.9)] compared to HW-BiVAD patients [48% (40.6, 55.4); p = 0.05]. The mean follow-up was 274 (200, 349) days in patients with HM3-BiVAD and 210 (143, 277) days in HW-BiVAD patients (p = 0.21).

CONCLUSION: Patients with HW-BiVAD were characterized by a higher proportion of females and more frequent use of the RV as the RVAD implantation site, likely both due to the smaller device profile. HM3-BiVAD patients demonstrated higher post-implant survival despite a more severe preimplant clinical profile, suggesting a possible device-related advantage.

articles.title: Area Under the Curve vs Trough-Based Vancomycin Monitoring in Pediatric Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trough-based monitoring was previously the primary way to monitor vancomycin; however, 2020 vancomycin consensus guidelines recommend area under the curve (AUC)-based monitoring as the preferred strategy. Data regarding this approach remain limited in the pediatric population.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the proportion of pediatric patients achieving therapeutic vancomycin serum concentrations using AUC vs trough-based monitoring and evaluate the safety and efficacy of both strategies.

METHODS: This is a single-center retrospective cohort study comparing trough- and Bayesian AUC-based vancomycin monitoring. Patients aged 28 days to 18 years on vancomycin with at least 2 appropriately obtained levels were included. Patients were excluded for suspected or confirmed central nervous system infection, renal dysfunction at vancomycin initiation, neonate or postmenstrual age <44 weeks, or use of continuous vancomycin. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving therapeutic vancomycin serum concentrations. Secondary outcomes included proportion of patients achieving therapeutic goal by the second pharmacokinetic evaluation, time to therapeutic goal, 30- and 90-day all-cause mortality, number of dose adjustments, number of serum concentrations collected, proportion of appropriately timed serum concentrations, and incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI).

RESULTS: Eighty-six patients were included: 49 AUC and 37 trough. Overall target attainment was higher in the AUC group (95.9% vs 51.4%; P < .001). The AUC group had a lower final vancomycin dose (P < .001), fewer dose adjustments (P = .004), serum concentrations obtained (P = .02), and more appropriately timed serum concentrations (P = .02). Incidence of AKI and 30- and 90-day all-cause mortality did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Area under the curve monitoring was associated with higher therapeutic goal attainment, lower final vancomycin doses, higher percentage of appropriately timed serum concentrations, fewer serum concentrations drawn, and fewer dosage adjustments. These findings add pediatric-specific evidence supporting 2020 guideline recommendations and indicate Bayesian area under the curve monitoring is a feasible, resource-efficient strategy in this population.

articles.title: Genetic and functional analysis of CDH2 reveals new insights into CDH2-related disorders.
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pathogenic variants in CDH2 cause agenesis of the corpus callosum, cardiac, ocular, and genital syndrome (ACOGS). We aimed to define the clinical and molecular landscape of CDH2-related developmental disorders.

METHODS: Newly identified and previously reported families were analyzed for genotype-phenotype correlations; variants were assessed using protein modeling and splicing assays.

RESULTS: Screening identified 20 new families carrying (likely) pathogenic ((L)P) alleles (n=16) or high-priority variants of uncertain significance (VUS) (n=4), including 12 novel CDH2 alleles. The combined (L)P cohort (37 individuals) showed variable ACOGS core features (mean 3; range 1-5), along with abdominal wall and/or diaphragmatic hernias and nipple, spine or gastrointestinal anomalies, each seen in ∼20% of individuals. Novel ACOGS findings included ambiguous genitalia, female genital malformations and dilated cardiomyopathy. Missense variants, principally within extracellular cadherin domains, accounted for 86% of unique (L)P alleles with clusters in EC1 and EC4-EC5; the remainder produce late protein truncations or in-frame deletions. Disruption of calcium binding was predicted by modeling. Conversely, VUS were primarily nonsense-mediated decay-sensitive or deletions (71%), linked to neurodevelopmental, kidney or other anomalies.

CONCLUSION: We expand the ACOGS spectrum and highlight its striking clinical variability. Additionally, we identify a possible milder phenotype associated with CDH2 haploinsufficiency.

articles.title: Focus on the building, not the blocks.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society : JINS
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Difficulty with word finding is a pervasive symptom in aphasia and a common target of treatment. This review explored whether therapy-induced naming gains induce improvements to everyday (naturalistic) communication.

METHODS: Online databases were searched for naming interventions that also assessed discourse or functional communication, and for studies of therapies that directly treated them.

RESULTS: Among the studies that found word production gains following therapy, only about half found that the gains generalized to improved discourse or functional communication. However, discourse and functional communication can be improved by therapies that target them, and often improve word finding as well.

CONCLUSIONS: Generalization of rehabilitation is complex and difficult to achieve. If the therapeutic goal in aphasia is to improve everyday communication, then intervention research needs to shift focus from "building blocks" like word production to the building of discourse and functional communication.

articles.title: Hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenocortical responses to critical illness: new insights with clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Critical illness profoundly affects the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenocortical (HPA) axis. In the acute phase of sepsis and other critical conditions, systemic cortisol levels rise markedly, yet circulating ACTH is low. Peripheral adaptations - reduced cortisol metabolism, decreased cortisol-binding proteins, and tissue-specific modulation of glucocorticoid receptor signaling - rather than sustained central HPA axis activation generate compartmentalized increased cortisol actions. As illness persists beyond one week, patients transition into prolonged critical illness characterized by a central HPA suppression, impaired adrenocortical structure and function, together increasing the risk for ICU-acquired adrenal insufficiency beyond 4 weeks. Although glucocorticoids, in stress doses, remain widely used for shock reversal, they exacerbate this HPA suppression and aggravate acute and long-term complications of critical illness. A better mechanistic understanding is essential to guide targeted and adequately dosed therapies.

articles.title: Association between baseline mean perfusion pressure and mortality in ARDS may depend on age.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Association of Obesity With Intracranial Hemodynamic Alterations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity increases the risk of stroke and cognitive decline, but its association with intracranial arterial hemodynamics remains unclear. We examined whether obesity score is associated with intracranial signal-intensity gradient, a time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography-derived surrogate of arterial wall shear conditions, and whether this association differs by vascular territory.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 5618 adults who underwent comprehensive health screening, including intracranial time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography, in the Republic of Korea between 2012 and 2020. Body mass index was calculated from measured height and weight, and waist circumference was measured by health-screening staff on the same day as brain magnetic resonance angiography. An obesity score was calculated by assigning 1 point each for general and abdominal obesity, yielding scores of 0 (neither), 1 (either), or 2 (both). Arterial SIG and arterial radius were calculated using semiautomated 3-dimensional vessel segmentation. Lower SIG values were interpreted as reflecting reduced arterial wall shear conditions. Multivariable linear regression models assessed the association between obesity score and SIG across 11 intracranial arteries, adjusting for demographics, arterial radius, and cardiometabolic factors.

RESULTS: Among 5618 participants (mean [SD] age, 55.9 [8.6] years; 45.2% women), higher obesity score was associated with lower SIG across all intracranial arteries (P value for trend <0.001). In adjusted models, each 1-point increase in obesity score was associated with reduced SIG, including in the basilar artery (B=-0.26 [95% CI, -0.31 to -0.21]). The obesity-related reduction in SIG was greater in the posterior than anterior circulation and persisted after adjustment for arterial radius and cardiometabolic factors.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher obesity score was associated with reduced intracranial arterial SIG, consistent with adverse time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography-derived flow-related hemodynamic alterations. Greater reductions in the posterior circulation suggest territory-specific vulnerability, which may be associated with early cerebrovascular compromise in the context of obesity.

articles.title: Orbital Fractures and Traumatic Brain Injury: Mapping the Craniofacial Trauma Research Landscape.
articles.abstract: Orbital fractures and traumatic brain injury (TBI) frequently coexist after high-energy craniofacial trauma, but the literature connecting these injuries has not been comprehensively mapped. The authors performed a bibliometric analysis of the Web of Science Core Collection using a sensitivity-focused search combining orbital, midfacial, facial, and craniofacial fracture or trauma terms with TBI and intracranial injury terminology. Records spanning 1969 to 2026 were analyzed in Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer for publication trends, research categories, geography, institutions, authorship, citation impact, coauthorship, and keyword patterns. The search yielded 958 publications. Output remained limited until the early 21st century and increased more consistently after 2004, with notable recent peaks in 2021 and 2025. The United States led publication output (n=405), followed by India (n=71) and England (n=67). Surgery was the dominant Web of Science category, followed by Dentistry, Oral Surgery and Medicine and Clinical Neurology. Granick MS and Hoppe IC each contributed 13 publications, and Lee ES contributed 12. Keyword mapping emphasized management, trauma, facial fractures, and computed tomography. Much of the influential literature addresses orbital fracture and TBI within broader facial trauma or polytrauma rather than as a primary research question. Future studies should directly examine fracture pattern, intracranial injury, imaging, timing of reconstruction, and combined neurological and visual outcomes.

articles.title: Identification of a Novel EBF1-Expressing Disease-Associated Arterial Subpopulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating disease with a poor prognosis. However, only a limited number of palliative interventions are currently available. To address this unmet need, it is essential to understand the molecular causes of PAH by identifying unique disease-associated populations and their key molecular regulators during disease progression.

METHODS: We constructed a single-cell multiome data set at 4 distinct time points during the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) using endothelial cells isolated from the Sugen5416/hypoxia rat model. We assessed the conservation of novel disease-associated endothelial cells by reanalyzing previously reported single-cell RNA sequencing data from human patients with PAH. We validated the functional importance of EBF1 (early B-cell factor 1) in PAH by performing in silico simulations and an in vivo knockdown mediated by a pulmonary endothelium-targeting associated virus.

RESULTS: We found that PH progression gradually altered the transcriptional and epigenetic landscape of the pulmonary endothelium in a stage-specific manner, leading to the emergence of a novel disease-associated arterial endothelial population expressing EBF1. A similar endothelial subset was present in human patients with PAH. Immunofluorescence revealed that EBF1 expression was elevated in both human and rat lungs during PH progression. In silico simulations suggested that EBF1 is required for the pathogenic state, and the associated virus-mediated in vivo knockdown of Ebf1 ameliorated the pathological hallmarks of PH, including right ventricular systolic pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, when delivered either before the onset of PH or after its establishment.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified EBF1 as a key transcriptional regulator of a novel disease-associated population in both humans and rats. We further demonstrated that inhibiting EBF1 within the pulmonary endothelium ameliorates the pathological features of PH, suggesting that EBF1 and its transcriptional targets represent a novel and promising therapeutic avenue for PAH.

articles.title: Dual Versus Mono Antiplatelet Therapy in Mild Versus Moderate Ischemic Stroke: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ATAMIS Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prespecified post hoc analysis of the ATAMIS trial (Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Mild to Moderate Ischemic Stroke) aimed to investigate whether the benefit of dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone differs in patients with mild versus moderate stroke.

METHODS: Using data from the modified intention‑to‑treat population of the ATAMIS trial, eligible patients were divided into mild (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score 4-5) and moderate (NIHSS score 6-10) groups. The primary outcome was early neurological deterioration at 7 days, defined as an increase in the NIHSS score of ≥2 points from baseline. Safety outcomes included bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage within 90 days. Binary logistic regression, Cox regression, and generalized linear models were used as appropriate. Adjusted models included age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, onset-to-treatment time, stroke cause, and other imbalanced baseline variables. Treatment-by-baseline stroke severity interaction was assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 2915 patients were included, including 1992 (68.4%) with mild stroke and 923 (31.6%) with moderate stroke. Median age was 66 years (interquartile range, 59-73); 35.0% were women. Clopidogrel plus aspirin was associated with a significantly lower risk of early neurological deterioration compared with aspirin alone in the moderate stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.17-0.59]; P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed in the mild stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.66-1.41]; P=0.841). A significant interaction was identified between treatment effect and NIHSS score subgroup (Pinteraction=0.003). The occurrence of bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage was similar between treatment groups in both severity subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute mild-to-moderate ischemic stroke, the benefit of clopidogrel plus aspirin versus aspirin alone in preventing early neurological deterioration at 7 days may be greater among patients with moderate stroke (NIHSS score 6-10) than among those with mild stroke (NIHSS score 4-5), without an increased risk of bleeding. These findings suggest that baseline stroke severity may inform antiplatelet therapy selection, and warrant confirmation in future prospective studies.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02869009.

articles.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Is Associated With Adverse Short- and Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke and TIA: A Retrospective Cohort Study From the Bern Sleep-Stroke Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is common after ischemic stroke and has been associated with adverse outcomes, yet evidence from large stroke cohorts remains limited. We evaluated the association of SDB severity with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 3-month functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack admitted to Inselspital Bern between 2017 and 2021 who underwent in-hospital respiratory polygraphy. SDB severity was classified according to the apnea-hypopnea index as mild (5-<15 events/h), moderate (15-<30 events/h), or severe (≥30 events/h). Outcomes included all-cause mortality, first postindex MACCE, and modified Rankin Scale scores at 3 months. Multivariable Cox and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, vascular risk factors, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, intravenous thrombolysis, and mechanical thrombectomy.

RESULTS: Among 1083 patients (mean age, 66.0±14.5 years; 62.6% male), SDB (apnea-hypopnea index ≥5 events/h) was present in 819 patients (75.6%), including mild (29.8%), moderate (22.9%), and severe (22.9%). Median follow-up was 51.1 months (interquartile range, 39.1-67.8) for mortality and 47.7 months (interquartile range, 36.9-65.5) for first postindex MACCE; 178 deaths and 153 of 880 patients experienced a first postindex MACCE. Severe SDB was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.73 [95% CI, 1.04-2.89]). Mild, moderate, and severe SDB were associated with first postindex MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.03-3.06]; 2.20 [95% CI, 1.26-3.84]; and 2.16 [95% CI, 1.23-3.78], respectively; P for trend=0.009). Moderate and severe SDB were associated with unfavorable 3-month functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 1.74 [95% CI, 1.01-3.04] and 2.48 [95% CI, 1.45-4.31], respectively; P for trend <0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Severe SDB was independently associated with all-cause mortality, whereas SDB severity was associated with first postindex MACCE and unfavorable 3-month functional outcome. Acute-phase SDB assessment may improve prognostic risk stratification.

articles.title: MAPK15 induces cardiomyocyte senescence and atrial fibrillation by promoting mitochondrial calcium overload via palmitoylating Mcub at the C91 residue.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly age-related AF, is increasing rapidly with global aging. Cellular senescence is a key contributing factor to AF, yet the underlying mechanisms driving atrial cardiomyocyte senescence remain elusive. Although MAPK15 has recently been implicated in regulating epithelial cell senescence, its potential role in the heart remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the role of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF, and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We investigated the role and underlying mechanisms of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF by cardiac-specific overexpression or knockdown of MAPK15, as well as treatment with small-molecule inhibitors. A combination of transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation with mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, patch-clamp recording, optical mapping and intracardiac electrophysiology was employed both in vitro and in vivo. Findings were further validated using human atrial appendage specimens. Results showed that MAPK15 was closely associated with atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. Overexpression of MAPK15 aggravated senescence and promoted AF. Mechanistically, MAPK15 induced palmitoylation of mitochondrial calcium uniporter dominant negative subunit b (Mcub) at C91, causing its dissociation from the mitochondrial Mcu complex and translocation to the cytoplasm. This impaired inhibition of mitochondrial calcium uptake, leading to calcium overload, ROS overproduction, and cellular senescence. C91S mutation or palmitoylation inhibition (2-BP) reversed these effects. Subsequently, senescent cardiomyocytes showed increased triggered activity, fibrosis, and altered connexin43 distribution, facilitating AF onset. And serological analysis suggested that IL-17a may act as an upstream regulator of MAPK15.

CONCLUSION: Our findings identify MAPK15 as a novel regulator of atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. MAPK15 promotes mitochondrial calcium overload through palmitoylation of Mcub at C91, highlighting a new mechanistic axis linking mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and arrhythmogenesis.

TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Age-related atrial fibrillation is highly prevalent and frequently associated with adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events, constituting a significant global public health burden. In this study, we demonstrated at both in vivo and in vitro levels that the MAPK15-Mcub axis promotes atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and senescence-associated AF, which was further validated in atrial appendage tissues from clinical patients, enhancing the clinical translational relevance of our findings. Moreover, we identified circulating IL-17a as a potential upstream activator associated with MAPK15 signaling, suggesting its potential utility in preclinical screening and as an insightful clue for future immunomodulatory strategies. The development of small-molecule agents specially targeting MAPK15 or Mcub in cardiomyocytes may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for treating atrial myocyte senescence and AF.

articles.title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) based on fluctuating thermal regimes.
articles.abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determines sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. However, existing TSD reaction norms are derived from constant temperature laboratory conditions, leaving open the question of their applicability to natural conditions where incubation temperatures fluctuate. In this study, we developed a TSD reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) using fluctuating temperature treatments. We incubated eggs under five fluctuating temperature regimes, determined offspring sex using gonadal gene expression, and used the resulting sex ratios to fit reaction norms based on mean temperature and constant temperature equivalents (CTE). The reaction norms followed the canonical Female-Male-Female pattern of crocodilians. At lower incubation temperatures, our fluctuating-temperature reaction norms closely aligned with that derived from constant temperatures, suggesting that mean temperature and CTE statistics perform reasonably well in this range. However, at higher incubation temperatures, the range most relevant to climate warming projections, our reaction norms diverged substantially from constant temperature reaction norms with upper pivotal temperature estimates differing by up to 1.36°C. Because small thermal shifts at this critical transition can dramatically alter predicted sex ratios, these discrepancies carry real consequences for conservation forecasting. Our results underscore the importance of incorporating ecologically realistic thermal variation into TSD reaction norms and highlight the upper male-to-female transition as a priority for mechanistic study.

articles.title: Hyperoxia exposure disrupts alveolar development and cardiopulmonary transition in preterm pigs.
articles.abstract: Aim Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a major cause of chronic lung disease following preterm birth. We aimed to establish a normobaric hyperoxia-induced preterm pig model that reflects respiratory and cardiovascular consequences of BPD. Methods Preterm piglets (n=18) were delivered by caesarean section at gestational day 106 and exposed either to sustained hyperoxia (85% O₂) or ambient air for 94 hours. Data on echocardiography, pulmonary arterial pressure, and detailed lung and heart histopathology were collected. Results There was clear structural lung injury in hyperoxia-exposed piglets, with increased septal thickness, reduced alveolar density, higher mean linear intercepts and more alveolar necrosis (all p<0.05). Echocardiography revealed a higher prevalence of persistent ductus arteriosus (55.6% in BPD vs. 12.5% in controls; p=0.091). Histology showed right ventricular cardiomyocyte hyperplasia and hypertrophy in hyperoxia-exposed pigs, yet pulmonary arterial pressure was unaffected. Conclusion The preterm pig model recapitulates key physiological and structural hallmarks of "new BPD" and the broader chronic lung disease of prematurity. This model represents a promising platform for investigating mechanisms and interventions in preterm infants at risk of BPD.

articles.title: Caries experience in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, sharing several behavioral and metabolic risk factors with dental caries. While extensive research has explored links between periodontal disease and cardiovascular health, the association between dental caries experience and coronary artery disease is less understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize existing evidence regarding dental caries burden, measured by decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), among individuals with coronary artery disease.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in April 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies published from 1966 to 2025 were eligible if they assessed adult patients with CHD, ischemic heart disease (IHD), myocardial infarction (MI), or related conditions and reported dental caries experience using the DMFT index. Observational studies, including cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort designs, were included. Duplicate records were removed using specialized software. Two independent reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, resolving discrepancies by discussion. Data extraction included study characteristics, caries indices, and key findings. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: From 2339 records identified, 1677 unique studies were screened, leading to 38 full-text articles reviewed for eligibility. Ultimately, 4 studies met inclusion criteria, representing populations from Iran, Sweden, Poland, and India, with sample sizes ranging from 100 to nearly 4000 participants. All studies employed either cross-sectional or case-control designs. Findings generally indicated higher mean values of DMFT among individuals with coronary artery disease, particularly for missing teeth. Some studies showed significantly greater untreated decay and tooth loss in patients with coronary artery disease compared to controls, while restorative care levels were often similar between groups. The small number of studies and their observational nature limit definitive conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that patients with coronary artery disease may experience a higher burden of dental caries, primarily through increased missing and decayed teeth. These findings underscore the potential shared risk environment and highlight the importance of integrating oral health within cardiovascular prevention frameworks. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship and explore whether managing caries can contribute to cardiovascular risk reduction.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of carbonic anhydrase IX-targeted PET/CT for detection of clear cell renal cell carcinoma in patients with renal masses: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The preoperative differentiation of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from other renal masses remains challenging. Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a highly specific target for noninvasive ccRCC imaging. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CAIX-targeted PET/computed tomography (CT) for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Registers (up to 30 September 2025) was supplemented by a bibliographic review. Studies evaluating CAIX-PET/CT against histopathologically were included. Of 528 records, five studies (n = 544 patients) were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were synthesized using a univariate fixed-effects model; predictive values, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratio were also calculated.

RESULTS: For the detection of histopathologically confirmed ccRCC (vs. non-ccRCC renal masses), the pooled sensitivity was 85.5% [95% confidence interval (CI): 81.6-88.7] and specificity of 86.5 (95% CI: 80.4-90.9). The hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model yielded an area under the curve of 0.894. Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potential difference in diagnostic performance between the tracer subtypes.

CONCLUSION: This review provides low-certainty evidence that CAIX-targeted PET/CT is a highly accurate, noninvasive tool for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses in presurgical populations. Clinically, its high positive predictive value (94.6%) strongly 'rules in' disease, while its modest negative predictive value (~69%) limits its ability to 'rule out' malignancy. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings in broader clinical cohorts and for small-molecule agents.

articles.title: History of gastrointestinal symptoms with other glucose-lowering agents is associated with gastrointestinal adverse events after imeglimin initiation: A retrospective real-world study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: Imeglimin is an oral antidiabetic agent with a novel mechanism of action. Gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events (AEs) have been reported during imeglimin therapy. However, the factors associated with the occurrence of GI AEs have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the incidence of GI AEs and the factors associated with their occurrence following imeglimin initiation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center observational study included patients with type 2 diabetes who initiated imeglimin between September 16, 2021, and June 30, 2025, at our institution. Of the 254 patients who initiated imeglimin, 238 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Patients were classified into two groups according to the presence of GI AEs. Baseline characteristics were compared between the groups, and multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with GI AEs. Modified Poisson regression with robust error variance was conducted as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: GI AEs occurred in 77 (32.4%) patients. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that a history of GI symptoms associated with glucose-lowering agents other than imeglimin was independently associated with GI AEs (odds ratio 3.49, 95% CI 1.76-6.94). Modified Poisson regression with robust error variance showed similar results (risk ratio 2.04, 95% CI 1.45-2.88).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with a history of GI symptoms associated with glucose-lowering agents other than imeglimin may have a higher risk of developing GI AEs after imeglimin initiation. Incorporating this information into pre-treatment assessment may support clinical decision-making at imeglimin initiation.

articles.title: [Swimming induced pulmonary edema].
articles.abstract: This article describes the case of a previously healthy 23-year old male who developed swimming induced pulmonary edema (SIPE) during a 250 km swimrun race in Stockholm in September 2025. After 15 hours of combined running and swimming he developed dyspnea, cough, pink sputum, saturation of 65% on air, and crackles on lung auscultation. The patient was airlifted to the Karolinska University Hospital in Solna, where he received BiPAP treatment. An echocardiogram revealed no abnormalities apart from a discreet tricuspid regurgitation. The patient was discharged after 24 hours. In this article we briefly describe pathophysiology and diagnostic criteria. Our goal with this case report is to inform and alert physicians of this relatively rare condition, as we've noted a marked increase of patients presenting with SIPE in parallel to an increase in swimrun race participation in recent years.

articles.title: Lithium Amide: A Catalyst for Depolymerization.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of plastic materials leads to significant contamination of ecosystems, posing risks to both wildlife and human health. There is an urgent need for efficient, economical, and environmentally friendly catalysts to depolymerize plastic waste into value-added compounds. In this study, we utilized the easily accessible catalyst [Li{N(SiMe3}2]2.2(THF) and pinacolborane (HBpin) as a hydride donor to convert various types of plastic waste, biodegradable/non-biodegradable polyesters, and polycarbonates into respective borylated value-added alcohols under mild conditions without any pre-treatment, up to 99% yield. The borylated 1,4-benzenediol obtained from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization is characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction studies, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and routine spectroscopic techniques. Additionally, the catalyst has been employed for the depolymerization of mixed/contaminated waste plastics, achieving selective and excellent yields of the borylated alcohols. This catalyst facilitated the gram-scale depolymerization of PET into eco-friendly alcohols, such as 1,4-benzene-di-methanol and ethylene glycol, via the depolymerization of PET waste bottles. Furthermore, mechanistic studies supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations provide insights into the catalytic pathway. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of alkali metal-catalyzed depolymerization of esters and carbonates containing waste polymers via a homogeneous method.

articles.title: Understanding Nrf2 Function in Manganese Neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: The objective of the present review was to summarize and discuss recent findings on the effects of Mn exposure on Nrf2 signaling in the brain and its relationship with other molecular mechanisms of Mn neurotoxicity. The existing data show that Mn exposure interferes with Nrf2 signaling following a biphasic response model. Upon low-to-moderate dose or following short-term exposure, Mn activates Nrf2 signaling with subsequent upregulation of Nrf2-target antioxidant genes, which limit progression of Mn-induced oxidative stress. Evidence from Nrf2-deficient animal models support the essential role of Nrf2 in counteracting Mn-induced neuronal oxidative stress. In contrast, high-dose and/or long-term Mn exposure down-regulates Nrf2 signaling due to inhibition of SIRT1, REST1, and CYP1B1 expression, as well as upregulation of GSK-3β expression. The observed inhibition of Nrf2 signaling is associated not only with oxidative stress, but is also tightly related to Mn-induced neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, neurodegeneration, endoplasmic reticulum stress, ferroptosis, tau and amyloid-β accumulation, and dysregulated heat-shock protein expression. Although the existing data were derived from laboratory studies and environmentally irrelevant doses, it is assumed that Nrf2 signaling may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing Mn neurotoxicity.

articles.title: A Quality Improvement Initiative in Hospital-Based Speech-Language Pathology: Development and Evaluation of a Lean-Agile Management Model.
articles.journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital-based Speech-Language Pathology (SLP) plays a strategic role in the care of critically ill patients, particularly in dysphagia management. However, high service demand and limited resources highlight the need for structured management approaches. This quality improvement (QI) study describes the implementation of a Lean-Agile management model and the establishment of a baseline of clinical care indicators to support dysphagia management in a high-complexity hospital setting.

METHODS: This quality improvement initiative used a retrospective descriptive design and was conducted in a high-complexity quaternary public hospital in São Paulo, Brazil. The model comprised four phases: process mapping and value chain construction; clinical demand management using a Kanban-inspired prioritisation system; continuous monitoring through predefined process and outcome indicators; and evaluation through retrospective analysis of 1,312 adult ICU patients receiving dysphagia management between January 2024 and June 2025. Oral intake status was classified using the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS). Descriptive statistics were used, and proportions are reported with 95% confidence intervals (Wilson method).

RESULTS: The mean daily service coverage rate was 73%, corresponding to 33 patients seen per day out of a mean daily active demand of 45 patients across 100 ICU beds. The overall prevalence of dysphagia (FOIS 1-5) was 88.95% (95%CI: 87.1-90.5%), and dependence on an alternative feeding route at initial assessment (FOIS 1-3) was observed in 54.65% (95%CI: 51.9-57.3%) of patients. The favourable swallowing outcome rate was 80.55% (95%CI: 77.8-83.0%; N = 869), and the alternative feeding route weaning rate was 77.28% (95%CI: 73.4-80.8%; N = 493). Unfavourable outcomes were predominantly attributable to poor functional prognosis (52.05%) and clinical severity (30.41%), whereas process-related failures accounted for only 0.5% of the total sample.

CONCLUSION: The Lean-Agile management model provided a structured approach to organising SLP services in a high-complexity ICU setting and enabled the establishment of a baseline of dysphagia care indicators. Most unfavourable outcomes were attributable to patients' underlying clinical conditions rather than service-related factors. These findings may inform service planning and quality monitoring in similar hospital contexts, pending multicentre evaluation.

articles.title: Pelvic Insufficiency Fractures After Chemoradiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Incidence, Long-Term Outcomes, and Survivorship Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic insufficiency fractures, a late complication of chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer, can cause pain and functional impairment. Although most studies have reported incidence rates and risk factors, few have examined clinical presentation, long-term symptom burden, or the impact on survivorship.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of patients with cervical cancer treated with chemoradiotherapy from 2018 to 2024. We extracted clinical characteristics, treatment details, dosimetric parameters, imaging studies documenting pelvic insufficiency fractures, and clinical outcomes from the electronic medical record. We used the Kaplan-Meier method to estimate the probability of pelvic insufficiency fractures and univariate Cox regression to assess clinical and dosimetric factors associated with their development.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 153 patients (median follow-up: 41.4 months). After chemoradiotherapy, 18 patients (11.8%) developed radiologically confirmed pelvic insufficiency fractures (median time to diagnosis: 9.5 months; probability of pelvic insufficiency fracture at 24 months: 11.4%). PET-CT and/or MRI showed that most pelvic insufficiency fractures involved the sacrum. No statistically significant clinical or dosimetric predictors of pelvic insufficiency fractures were identified. All symptomatic patients (n = 15, 83%) required referral to pain-management services (median observed duration of symptoms: 37 months). No symptomatic patient achieved documented complete symptom resolution during the available follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Most pelvic insufficiency fractures presented with new-onset pelvic or sacral pain within two years of completing chemoradiotherapy. The lack of clinical or dosimetric predictors suggests a multifactorial etiology of fracture risk. Persistent pain, despite multimodal supportive care, led to long-term morbidity. These findings underscore the need for prospective studies to develop evidence-based preventive strategies, survivorship assessments, and management pathways.

articles.title: Treating Community Care as a High-Risk Transition: A Possible Hospital Medicine Agenda for the Veterans Health Administration.
articles.abstract: Expanded Veterans Affairs-purchased community care has improved options for veterans but has also changed the core work of Veterans Health Administration (VHA) hospital medicine. The most important inpatient problem is no longer simply optimizing the ward day; it is helping protect continuity across VHA hospitals, community emergency departments, intensive care units, skilled nursing facilities, home health, and primary care. This commentary argues that VHA hospitalists (inclusive of physician practitioners and advance practice practitioners), along with an interdisciplinary inpatient care team, should help treat cross-system transfers and postdischarge handoffs as high-risk transitions (vulnerabilities occurring due to change in care setting or care team), using VHA's learning-system capacity to measure, coordinate, and improve care across organizational boundaries.

articles.title: Reflections on Hurricane Katrina Two Decades Later: Findings From a Retrospective Population-Based Sample of Survivors.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize morbidity, health care-seeking, and medication-related needs among survivors of Hurricane Katrina.

METHODS: We used a two-stage sampling method to survey and interview 210 Hurricane Katrina survivors in Louisiana from 2006 to 2007. Interviews assessed injury, illness, environmental exposures, disaster-related damage, medication use, and health care-seeking behavior. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

RESULTS: Nearly 25% of respondents reported direct contact with hurricane-related floodwater. Nearly all experienced substantial property damage; wind (75.6%) and floodwater (67.5%) were the most common causes of damage. Before Hurricane Katrina, 70% of respondents reported good/excellent health; afterward, 35% reported worse health. Physical injury was reported by 17% of participants, emotional injury by 85%, and illness by 32%. Among those reporting injury/illness, 64% sought care for physical injuries, 21% for emotional injuries, and 63% for illnesses. Medication provision was common among those receiving care (70%-88%). Notably, 47% of respondents reported using at least one medication before the disaster, and 42% were unable to identify the specific medication they were taking.

CONCLUSIONS: Hurricane-related morbidity extends beyond health care system encounters and is likely underestimated by facility-based surveillance alone. Medication continuity and health care access represent important but understudied dimensions of disaster-related morbidity that remain relevant in contemporary disaster preparedness and response efforts.

articles.title: Metabolic biomarker levels before and after initiation of GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment among individuals with schizophrenia: interrupted time-series analysis.
articles.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that treatment with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) reduces body weight, waist circumference and haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels in patients with schizophrenia. However, because of participant selection in clinical trials, it remains unclear whether the beneficial metabolic effects of GLP-1RAs for patients with schizophrenia extend to real-world clinical settings.

AIMS: We investigated whether GLP-1RA treatment initiation was associated with reductions in HbA1c, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and triglyceride levels (the latter two as proxies for weight loss) in individuals with schizophrenia.

METHOD: We used the Danish nationwide registers to identify individuals with schizophrenia between 1996 and 2023. Among those, we identified individuals initiating GLP-1RA treatment. The main outcomes were changes in HbA1c, LDL and triglyceride levels following initiation of GLP-1RA treatment. Changes in HbA1c, LDL and triglyceride levels were visualised graphically and quantified with interrupted time-series analyses.

RESULTS: We identified 3042 individuals with schizophrenia who initiated a GLP-1RA. Initiation of GLP-1RA treatment for diabetes was followed by reductions in HbA1c, LDL and triglyceride levels of 11.4, 6.2 and 14.8%, respectively. Initiation of GLP-1RA treatment for overweight was followed by reductions in HbA1c, LDL and triglyceride levels of 3.4, 4.9 and 12.7%, respectively. All level changes were statistically significant (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of GLP-1RA treatment was followed by clinically meaningful reductions in HbA1c, LDL and triglyceride levels among individuals with schizophrenia. These findings suggest that the metabolic benefits of GLP-1RA treatment found in randomised clinical trials in schizophrenia extend to real-world clinical settings.

articles.title: Streptococcus constellatus-Associated Lemierre Syndrome Presenting With Cavitating Septic Pulmonary Emboli Managed by Video-Assisted Thoracoscopy.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Lemierre syndrome is a rare septic thromboembolic disorder. Although historically associated with Fusobacterium necrophorum, non-fusobacterial cases caused by Streptococcus constellatus can present with dominant thoracic sepsis and delayed recognition. CASE REPORT A 25-year-old previously healthy man from northern Ecuador presented with 7 days of dyspnea, productive cough, fever, and hemoptysis, with profound hypoxemia and respiratory distress. Chest computed tomography showed bilateral cavitating septic pulmonary emboli and necrotizing pulmonary infection, and cervical vascular imaging confirmed left internal jugular vein thrombosis. One blood culture set grew Streptococcus constellatus susceptible to penicillin and ceftriaxone; sputum and pleural fluid cultures were sterile. He required intensive care, endotracheal intubation, empiric piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin, escalation to meropenem plus vancomycin during clinical deterioration while resistant or polymicrobial infection was considered, therapeutic anticoagulation, and 2 video-assisted thoracoscopic procedures for empyema and a subsequent pulmonary abscess. After 4 weeks of intravenous antibiotics, he improved and was discharged on a direct oral anticoagulant for 1 additional month, remaining asymptomatic at short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Lemierre syndrome should be considered in young adults with severe sepsis and multifocal cavitating lung lesions, even without pharyngeal symptoms. Empiric therapy should initially cover oral aerobes and anaerobes; once penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus constellatus is confirmed and no co-pathogen is recovered, de-escalation to targeted beta-lactam therapy, such as penicillin G or ceftriaxone, should be considered together with drainage of empyema or abscess when present.

articles.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
articles.journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.

CONTENT: This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning.

SUMMARY: Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs.

OUTLOOK: Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the therapeutic efficacy of neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) in improving lower limb function and daily activities in post-stroke patients.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to April 20, 2025. Meta-analysis for continuous outcomes was performed using the inverse variance method under fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Ten studies (579 patients) were included. NMES significantly improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment (MD=3.40, P=0.001), ankle dorsiflexion ROM (MD=1.56, P=0.04), TUG (MD=-1.96, P=0.03), BBS (MD=10.78, P=0.005), PASS (MD=5.05, P<0.00001), and MBI (MD=13.29, P=0.02). Sensitivity analysis confirmed result robustness.

CONCLUSION: NMES effectively enhances motor function and activities of daily living in post-stroke patients, and may complement standard rehabilitation.

articles.title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Tuberculosis Treatment Adherence, Nonadherence, and Loss to Follow-up in Low- and Middle-income Countries: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020-compliant Systematic Review and Illustrative Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suboptimal adherence to tuberculosis (TB) treatment continues to undermine global TB control efforts, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In recent years, machine learning (ML) approaches have been explored as tools to predict adherence-related outcomes and guide targeted interventions.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to systematically review and synthesize the predictive performance of ML models for TB treatment adherence, nonadherence, and loss to follow-up.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Multiple databases were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies that used ML models to predict TB adherence-related outcomes and reported the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were included. We performed a random-effects meta-analysis of logit-transformed AUC values, along with assessments of heterogeneity, publication bias, sensitivity analysis, and risk of bias using the Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool.

RESULTS: Seven studies met inclusion criteria. The reported AUC values ranged from 0.72 to 0.95. The pooled AUC was 0.84 (95% confidence interval: 0.76-0.90), indicating good predictive performance. Substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 99.9%, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated stability of results. Egger's test showed no evidence of publication bias (P = 0.915). Most studies were judged to be at high risk of bias, particularly in the analysis domain.

CONCLUSION: ML models demonstrate promising ability to predict TB treatment adherence-related outcomes. However, variability in study methods and a high risk of bias underscore the need for standardized approaches and rigorous external validation.

articles.title: Intestinal Tuberculosis Masquerading as Metastatic Colonic Malignancy: A Diagnostic Dilemma in an Elderly Patient.
articles.abstract: Abdominal tuberculosis (TB) and colorectal malignancy have overlapping clinical, endoscopic, and radiological features leading to difficulty in diagnosis. We describe a case of abdominal TB mimicking colon cancer, with the added dramatic complication of false-positive positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) findings. Our patient is a 76-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and ischemic heart disease, describing a 2-month history of vomiting and loose stools, with symptoms of anorexia, weight loss, and progressive abdominal distension. Colonoscopy revealed circumferential ulceroproliferative growth at the transverse colon with luminal narrowing. On PET-CT scan, there were fluorodeoxyglucose-avid epiphrenic lymphadenopathy and peritoneal deposits suggesting metastatic colonic carcinoma. However, colonoscopic biopsy showed granulomatous ulcero-inflammatory change with multinucleated giant cells and positive acid-fast bacilli (AFB), but ruled out malignancy. GeneXpert MTB/RIF on sputum and ascitic fluid was negative. Ascitic fluid analysis revealed a low serum-ascites albumin gradient with high protein, consistent with tuberculous peritonitis. Antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated. At 8-week follow-up, the patient gained weight, and ascites had substantially regressed. This case highlights the critical importance of tissue biopsy with special staining in elderly patients from TB-endemic countries presenting with colonic lesions and PET-CT findings that mimic disseminated malignancy. AFB staining of colonoscopic biopsies should be a routine component of the diagnostic workup in such settings, and a negative GeneXpert should not exclude abdominal TB.

articles.title: Cardiac Involvement in Patients with Dengue Fever: A Clinical Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The highest incidence of dengue fever (DF) is seen in Southeast Asia, India, and the American tropics. Arboviruses represent a serious public health problem in tropical and subtropical regions of the world. Although dengue shock syndrome (DSS) has been attributed largely to decreased intravascular volume due to capillary leakage of plasma into the interstitial space, a few recent studies have reported that it may be due to cardiac involvement. Hence, the present study was planned to assess the cardiac manifestations of DF and to identify subclinical/latent cardiac involvement.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To study was to evaluate the various cardiac manifestations of DF along with its prevalence.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence and severity correlation of cardiac manifestations in dengue fever patients at a rural tertiary care center between January and December 2025. A total of 110 patients aged 13 years and older with confirmed dengue serology were enrolled after providing written informed consent. The study excluded individuals with pre-existing heart conditions, electrolyte imbalances, mixed infections, or medications affecting heart rate and rhythm. Data collection involved detailed clinical histories, daily vital sign monitoring, complete blood counts, cardiac enzyme assays, electrocardiograms, and 2D echocardiograms conducted after fever resolution. Cardiac involvement was identified through rhythm disturbances, enzyme elevations, and structural or electrical abnormalities, with patients classified according to WHO criteria following ethical approval.

RESULTS: In this study, out of the eight patients with DSS, six patients (75%) had positive troponin I. Eight patients were found to have DSS with 87.5% of them having raised CKMB levels compared to 42.3% and 39.5% in dengue hemorrhagic fever and DF, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac involvement in dengue can contribute to hemodynamic instability in dengue patients. ECG can prove a useful tool, especially in patients with hemodynamic instability to plan for more efficient management.

articles.title: Prevalence of Obesity and Hypertension and Their Association among Adolescent Girls Aged 14-16 years in an Urban Setting Private School: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study investigates the prevalence of obesity and hypertension (HTN) among urban adolescent girls (14-16 years) and explores the association between anthropometric measures and blood pressure (BP).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 257 girls from seven private schools in Karimnagar, Telangana, using a two-stage convenience-purposive sampling strategy. Anthropometric parameters, including body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, and waist-height ratio (WHtR), were recorded following standardized protocols. BP was measured using an automated sphygmomanometer and classified according to Indian Academy of Pediatrics guidelines. Statistical analyses employed Chi-square tests, analysis of variance, and logistic regression using SPSS version 25.0.

RESULTS: Among the participants, 16.3% were overweight, 5.4% obese, and 14.3% underweight, while 63.8% fell within the normal weight category. HTN prevalence was 19.5%, with an additional 8.2% showing elevated BP. Overweight and obesity were more frequent among the 15-16 years of age group compared with 14-15 years (26.1% vs. 19.5%). Logistic regression analysis showed that BMI was significantly associated with both systolic and diastolic HTN, while WHtR was significantly associated with systolic HTN (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a significant burden of overweight/obesity (21.7%) and HTN (19.1%) among urban private school girls aged 14-16 years in India. BMI was significantly associated with both systolic and diastolic HTN, while WHtR was associated with systolic HTN. These findings highlight an association between healthy weight status in adolescence and cardiovascular risk factors. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between obesity and HTN.

articles.title: Molecular Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacilli Isolated from Intensive Care Unit Patients in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) present a critical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), severely limiting therapeutic options. This study evaluated the prevalence and molecular resistance mechanisms of GNB in ICU patients.

INTRODUCTION: Hospital-acquired urinary tract infections are among the most common healthcare-associated infections in ICUs. The emergence of MDR Gram-negative bacilli has reduced available treatment options and increased morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate antimicrobial resistance patterns and characterize major resistance genes among Gram-negative bacilli isolated from ICU patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 2019 to 2022 across two tertiary centers in North India. We analyzed 427 non-duplicate MDR GNB isolates from ICU urinary samples. Identification followed standard biochemical protocols. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed through Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion as per Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Phenotypic detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), AmpC, and carbapenemase production was performed, alongside molecular characterization of resistance genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, blaNDM, blaIMP, blaVIM, blaOXA).

RESULTS: In the present study, most isolates originated from the medical ICU (66.0%). Most MDR GNB isolates were from males (52%), and the majority of patients belonged to the age group > 60 years. The predominant isolates were Escherichia coli (60%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (19%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12%). Alarmingly high resistance rates to Cephalosporins (>90%), Fluoroquinolones (>80%), and Carbapenems (70% overall) were observed. Overall, 40.9% of isolates were ESBL producers, 24.82% AmpC producers, and 13.81% Carbapenemase producers. Molecular analysis revealed a high prevalence of blaCTX M (100%), blaVIM (66%), and blaNDM (48%).

CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of diverse resistance mechanisms underscores the impact of indiscriminate antimicrobial use. Implementation of stringent antimicrobial stewardship and robust infection control practices is essential to mitigate the spread of MDR pathogens in critical care settings.

articles.title: Association Between Sputum Consistency and Extubation in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Severe Pneumonia Receiving Nebulized Antibiotic Therapy.
articles.abstract: Thick airway secretions may impair airway clearance and contribute to extubation failure in mechanically ventilated patients with severe pneumonia. Bedside sputum consistency assessment is commonly used in intensive care unit (ICU) practice, but its relationship with extubation outcomes remains insufficiently studied. Thus, we conducted a single-center prospective observational study of 80 mechanically ventilated adults with severe pneumonia who received nebulized sulfadiazine-polymyxin B as part of ICU care. Bedside sputum consistency was assessed using a semi-quantitative clinical scale before and after therapy. Change in bedside sputum consistency score was defined as the pre-treatment score minus the post-treatment score. The primary outcome was extubation success, defined as removal of the endotracheal tube without reintubation within 72 h. Nebulizer type, clinical characteristics, ventilator parameters, microbiological findings, and outcomes were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between changes in consistency and extubation success. Eighty patients were included: 27 received jet nebulization, 23 mesh nebulization, and 30 ultrasonic nebulization. Extubation success occurred in 50 patients. Patients with successful extubation had a greater improvement in the bedside sputum consistency score than patients without successful extubation (1.28 ± 0.78 vs 0.63 ± 1.00; p = 0.004). In a baseline-adjusted analysis, successful extubation was associated with a 0.63-point lower post-treatment score (adjusted mean difference, -0.63; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.21; p = 0.003). In the parsimonious multivariable analysis, greater improvement in the bedside sputum consistency score remained associated with successful extubation (OR, 2.90; 95% CI, 1.51-5.56; p = 0.001), whereas baseline score was not independently associated with the outcome. Nebulizer type was not significantly associated with extubation success. In conclusion, the mechanically ventilated patients with severe pneumonia receiving nebulized sulfadiazine-polymyxin B, greater improvement in bedside sputum consistency was associated with successful extubation. Bedside secretion assessment may provide useful supportive information during extubation readiness evaluation. Further controlled studies using standardized and objective rheological measurements are warranted.

articles.title: Quantifying the Functional Effect of Transmural Interpolation Strategies on Atrial Wave Propagation Using a Custom Open-Source Pipeline.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) management increasingly relies on patient-specific computational modeling to simulate arrhythmia mechanisms and optimize ablation strategies. However, predictive reliability is strongly influenced by accurate reconstruction of myocardial fiber architecture, which governs electrical anisotropy. Because patient-specific atrial fiber orientations cannot currently be acquired reliably in vivo using diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging (DT-MRI), alternative computational mapping strategies are required. This protocol presents a comprehensive, open-source pipeline for constructing patient-specific 3D models of the human left atrium with explicit transmural fiber reconstruction from high-resolution clinical computed tomography (CT) data. The methodology extends the Universal Atrial Coordinate (UAC) framework into the volumetric domain by solving the Laplace-Dirichlet problem to derive a continuous transmural coordinate. This enables transfer of atlas-based fiber orientations and subsequent interpolation across the atrial wall. Linear and threshold-based transmural interpolation strategies are quantitatively compared, and their effects on fiber orientation and macroscopic wavefront propagation are evaluated. Across all six models, the mean angular deviation between interpolation methods was 8.06 ± 1.13°. Electrophysiological simulations demonstrate that the choice of interpolation delayed activation in Region 1 by 2.0 ± 0.6 ms, corresponding to 6.1 ± 1.5 ms (p = 0.031 for both comparisons). The open-source pipeline and patient-specific CT-based atrial models provide a reproducible framework for evaluating the functional effects of transmural fiber reconstruction strategies.

articles.title: Compassion Fatigue in Emergency Department Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of Predictive Models.
articles.abstract: Compassion fatigue (CF) is a potential risk for Emergency Department (ED) nurses when workload increases, they experience repeated exposure to trauma or have a long-term emotional burden. A cross-sectional study was conducted to explore the connection between workload, trauma exposure, coping, and compassion satisfaction, and to assess the performance of logistic regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine for internal binary classification. The sample included 150 full-time registered ED nurses from three tertiary hospitals, who completed a structured self-administered questionnaire. The analyses encompassed descriptive statistics, group comparisons, multiple linear regression, train-test split (80:20), and stratified five-fold cross-validation. The relationships between workload and trauma exposure were positive (r = 0.75 and r = 0.62, respectively), while the relationships between coping mechanisms and compassion satisfaction were negative (r = -0.52 and r = -0.60, respectively) with CF. The four-predictor regression model explained most of the variance in CF (adjusted R2 = 0.852), with coping and compassion satisfaction being the strongest negative predictors (β = -0.25; β = -0.35), and trauma exposure and workload being the strongest positive predictors (β = 0.32; β = 0.42). Random Forest outperformed Support Vector Machine (accuracy 83%, ROC-AUC 0.83) and logistic regression (accuracy 80%, ROC-AUC 0.80) in terms of internal classification (accuracy 85%, precision 82%, recall 80%, F1-score 81%, ROC-AUC 0.84). These findings suggest that the following interventions can be used to reduce compassion fatigue among ED nurses: workload management, trauma-informed support, coping, and compassion satisfaction.

articles.title: Pelvic Ultrasonography for Idiopathic Central Precocious Puberty in Girls: A Retrospective Diagnostic and Temporal Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic central precocious puberty (ICPP) and premature thelarche (PT) may initially present with similar breast development. We evaluated pelvic ultrasonography as an adjunctive discriminator and reassessed a multivariable prediction model. This retrospective, single-center study included a development cohort of 175 girls evaluated from August 2022 to December 2024 (90 ICPP and 85 PT) and a temporal validation cohort of 90 girls evaluated from January to December 2025 (48 ICPP and 42 PT). Diagnostic classification was based on clinical assessment and the gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test. Distribution-appropriate group tests were used, with Holm adjustment within prespecified families. In the development cohort, all uterine and ovarian measurements differed between groups after adjustment (all adjusted P<0.001). Uterine transverse diameter (UTD) and uterine volume (UV) had areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.830 and 0.829, respectively. At the Youden-derived UTD cutoff of 18.5-19.0 mm, sensitivity was 73.3%, and specificity was 78.8%. A model combining UTD and UV had an apparent AUC of 0.913 and a 10-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.910. The final logistic model included height, bone age, UV, and ovarian volume; its apparent development-cohort AUC was 0.951, and its bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.944. Applied without coefficient updating to the temporal cohort, the model yielded an AUC of 0.914, a Brier score of 0.121, a calibration intercept of 0.699, and a calibration slope of 0.754. Pelvic ultrasonography can complement, but not replace, auxologic, hormonal, and stimulation-test assessment. The thresholds and model require prospective multicenter external validation before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Determination of Alcohol in Blood by Headspace Gas Chromatography (HS-GC): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Headspace gas chromatography (HS-GC) with flame ionization detection (FID) or mass spectrometry (MS) is the gold standard for blood alcohol concentration (BAC) analysis in forensic and clinical toxicology. Despite widespread adoption, the comparative analytical performance of both methods across validation studies has not been quantitatively synthesized. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from database inception through May 2026. Primary outcomes were precision (%CV), accuracy (%bias), and recovery (%). Secondary outcomes included limit of detection (LOD), limit of quantification (LOQ), linearity (R2), and measurement uncertainty. Risk of bias was assessed using the adapted QUADAS-2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed using RevMan5.4. Five hundred fifty-five studies were identified, of which 17 met the inclusion criteria. Pooled intra-assay precision was 1.88%CV (95% CI: 1.12-2.65) for FID and 1.22%CV (95% CI: 0.70-1.75) for MS (p = 0.16). Inter-assay precision was 1.61%CV (95% CI: 0.83-2.39) for FID and 2.20%CV (95% CI: 1.51-2.89) for MS (p = 0.26). Pooled accuracy (%bias) was 1.94% (95% CI: 0.89-2.98) for FID and 1.73% (95% CI: 0.38-3.08) for MS. Recovery was 96.37% (95% CI: 91.89-100.84) for FID and 92.46% (95% CI: 87.14-97.78) for MS. Subgroup analysis showed significantly better precision at mid (1.35%CV) and high (1.10%CV) concentrations compared to low (2.43%CV) concentrations (p = 0.02). Both HS-GC-FID and HS-GC-MS provide analytically reliable BAC measurements within internationally accepted performance criteria. The choice between detectors may be guided by confirmation requirements and laboratory resources rather than analytical superiority.

articles.title: Progress on the Anti-inflammatory Mechanisms of Moxibustion in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, is driven by persistent airway inflammation involving complex pathways. Despite advances in conventional therapies, challenges remain in the effective control of steroid-resistant inflammation and systemic complications. Moxibustion is a traditional Chinese therapy that has shown promise in alleviating COPD-related inflammation by targeting these pathways. Clinical studies have suggested that moxibustion can regulate inflammatory cells (macrophages, neutrophils, Th17 cells, and regulatory T [Treg] cells) and mediators (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8), and these mechanisms correlate with improved lung function, reduced exacerbations, and enhanced immune balance. However, current evidence is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous methodologies, and a lack of high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs), resulting in an unclear independent therapeutic efficacy of moxibustion for COPD. While preliminary findings highlight its potential as an adjunct therapy, rigorous multicenter RCTs are imperative with large sample sizes and standardized protocols to validate its anti-inflammatory efficacy, elucidate dose-response relationships, and comprehensively evaluate safety profiles. This review aims to integrate traditional medical theory with modern immune inflammation biology, and summarize progress on the mechanism of inflammation regulation of moxibustion in the treatment of COPD. It mainly puts forward the view that moxibustion may treat COPD through TLR4/NF-κB pathway and IL-33/ST2 pathway, and points out the limitations of the existing related research. It emphasizes the need for more direct mechanism explanation and clinical research to verify.

articles.title: Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Prioritizes Candidate Paraptosis-Related Genes in Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is among the most disabling complications of diabetes, but its molecular features and underlying biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Paraptosis, a non-canonical form of programmed cell death characterized by endoplasmic reticulum/mitochondrial swelling and cytoplasmic vacuolization, is associated with endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial stress, processes that are also implicated in diabetic neuropathy, but its potential involvement in PDPN remains unclear. This study applied an exploratory integrative strategy that combined peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic data from 12 patients with PDPN and 12 healthy controls, together with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from human peripheral nerve tissue (GSE266026), comprising samples from patients with DPN and traumatic limb amputation (TLA) comparators. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with a paraptosis-related gene set, and were prioritized using LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest. The biological context of the prioritized genes was further explored through immune infiltration analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization, single-cell characterization, and scTenifoldKnk-based computational virtual knockout analysis. Fifteen paraptosis-related differentially expressed genes were identified, with a significantly elevated paraptosis-related score in PDPN. AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 were prioritized by all three machine-learning methods. Computational immune-cell deconvolution estimated increased the estimated neutrophil abundance and decreased the estimated CD8⁺ T-cell and resting memory CD4⁺ T-cell abundance in PDPN blood, with distinct correlations between the three candidate genes and inferred immune-cell profiles. Mendelian randomization provided evidence consistent with a potential association between genetically proxied higher AKT1 expression and diabetic polyneuropathy risk. Single-cell analysis revealed cell type-specific expression patterns of the three candidate genes, while computational virtual knockout analyses predicted gene-regulatory perturbations involving immune-inflammatory, neuronal structural, and cell-adhesion pathways within the respective network backgrounds. This exploratory integrative analysis prioritizes AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 as candidate paraptosis-related genes associated with PDPN and provides a biological context for further mechanistic and experimental investigation.

articles.title: Establishment and Optimization of a Mouse Model of Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) severely impairs cardiac prognosis after revascularization for acute myocardial infarction. Standardized mouse left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) ligation models are widely used for MIRI research, yet conventional protocols rely on indwelling support tubes and secondary thoracotomy to restore reperfusion. Such procedures feature complicated operations, high risks of pneumothorax, severe thoracic trauma, and low batch modeling efficiency.
