To address these drawbacks, we established an optimized MIRI mouse model with a single thoracotomy and carbon-synthesis fishing line pull-out for reperfusion. Male C57BL/6 mice aged 6-8 weeks were divided into normal control (NC), traditional model (TM), and optimized model (OM) groups. Echocardiography, triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) and hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, as well as serum inflammatory cytokines, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), c-reactive protein (CRP), and myocardial injury marker cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels were detected to compare modeling efficacy. Identical cardiac function, serum inflammatory cytokines, myocardial injury marker, infarct size, and myocardial pathological morphology changes were observed between TM and OM groups. The OM group displayed more homogeneous infarct regions and higher serum myocardial injury markers and cardiac function injury, indicating milder non-surgical trauma. Compared with the traditional method, this optimized procedure shortens surgical and anesthesia time, avoids fatal intraoperative pneumothorax, accelerates post-operative recovery, and improves animal survival. In conclusion, the optimized model produces equivalent MIRI lesions with higher safety, efficiency, and reproducibility. It serves as an ideal alternative to classic modeling approaches.

articles.title: A Methodological Framework for a Large Language Model Virtual Companion for Older Adults at Risk of Social Isolation.
articles.abstract: Social isolation is consistently associated with depressive symptoms, loneliness, reduced quality of life, and limited social connectedness in older adults; however, standardized approaches are lacking for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence-based psychosocial interventions. Here, we report an integrated methodology for developing and evaluating a large language model (LLM)-driven virtual companion system that delivers personalized emotional support to older adults at risk of social isolation. The methodology includes: participant recruitment and eligibility screening, system deployment, personalized conversational configuration, emotion-aware interaction, intervention implementation, longitudinal outcome assessment, and statistical evaluation. As a proof-of-concept demonstration of the framework, we conducted a randomized controlled trial involving 160 older adults recruited from community settings and long-term care institutions. Older adults were randomly allocated into one of two groups: the intervention group received an 8-week LLM-driven virtual companion intervention, while the control group participated in routine social activities. We evaluated outcomes at baseline, Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12 using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), UCLA Loneliness Scale (UCLA-LS), the World Health Organization Quality of Life-Old Module (WHOQOL-OLD), Lubben Social Network Scale-6 (LSNS-6), and System Usability Scale (SUS). Representative findings showed good system usability (SUS = 78.6 ± 10.3) and favorable changes in depressive symptoms and loneliness, indicating the feasibility and practicality of the proposed methodological framework. The standardized workflow provides a reproducible protocol for the further development and evaluation of LLM-based digital mental health interventions for older adults in both community and long-term care settings.

articles.title: Jidesheng Snake Pills as Adjunctive Therapy for Snakebite: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Jidesheng Snake Pills are used in China as an adjunctive treatment for snakebite. However, the randomized evidence has not been critically synthesized with attention to endpoint definitions, intervention heterogeneity, duplicate reports, and source-data provenance. Seven Chinese and international databases were searched from inception through February 2026 and updated through 26 September 2026. Trial registries were searched during revision. Five unique randomized trials were included. Source-specific clinical-response definitions were reported separately, and a harmonized any-improvement analysis was designated post hoc. Continuous outcomes were synthesized using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Fixed-effect, leave-one-out, and population-restriction sensitivity analyses were also performed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) framework, and certainty was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Five trials involving 458 participants were included. Clinical-response definitions differed materially, so no primary pooled response estimate was calculated. Study-specific risk ratios ranged from 1.20 to 1.26. The post hoc harmonized estimate was 1.14 (95% confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.35; I2 = 7.9%). Swelling-resolution time was shorter on average by 1.64 days (95% confidence interval, 3.05 to 0.24 days shorter; I2 = 90.0%). However, every leave-one-out robust interval crossed the null. Hospital stay was shorter by 1.49 days (95% confidence interval, 2.38 to 0.61 days shorter; I2 = 0%). Two-study sensitivity analyses remained imprecise. C-reactive protein was summarized narratively because analytes, printed units, and assessment times were incompatible. Certainty was very low for every principal outcome. The trials suggest possible reductions in swelling-resolution time and hospital stay, but the clinical benefit remains uncertain. The evidence is small, methodologically weak, clinically heterogeneous, and indirect. Standardized interventions, patient-important outcomes, and structured safety assessment are required.

articles.title: Prognostic Factors for One-Year Adverse Outcomes in Chronic Coronary Syndrome with Concomitant Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexist, yet prognostic evidence for patients with both conditions remains limited. This retrospective cohort study evaluated factors associated with one-year adverse clinical outcomes and developed a clinical risk score in 214 hospitalized patients with CCS and concomitant COPD. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were collected, and patients were followed for one year. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), rehospitalization for heart failure (HF), or rehospitalization for acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) within one year. Independent prognostic factors were identified using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Model performance was evaluated through discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. During follow-up, 53 patients (24.8%) experienced the composite endpoint, including 7 all-cause deaths (3.3%), 8 non-fatal MIs (3.7%), 17 HF-related rehospitalizations (7.9%), and 21 AECOPD-related rehospitalizations (9.8%). Smoking history (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.962, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.093-3.521, P = 0.024), previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (HR = 2.017, 95% CI: 1.157-3.517, P = 0.013), higher Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) grade (HR = 1.488, 95% CI: 1.092-2.028, P = 0.012), and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (HR = 0.933, 95% CI: 0.893-0.975, P = 0.002) were independently associated with the composite endpoint. The model demonstrated a concordance index (C-index) of 0.736 and a one-year area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.773. Event-free survival differed significantly among the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (log-rank P < 0.001). These findings support integrated cardiovascular and respiratory risk assessment in patients with CCS and COPD. However, external validation is required before the risk score can be recommended for broader clinical application.

articles.title: Effects of E-Coach-Based Chronic Disease Management on Self-Management, Quality of Life, and Mental Health in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients.
articles.abstract: The study investigated the effects of E-Coach on self-management behavior, quality of life (QoL), and mental health of patients with maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). The study included 96 patients receiving regular MHD, and they were randomly assigned to receive either usual care (a UC group) or usual care plus E-Coach intervention (an E-Coach group). The E-Coach was implemented through a WeChat-based mini-application that provided health education, dietary and exercise guidance, medication reminders, and regular online counseling through text-based materials, videos, and interactive quizzes. After adjustment for baseline score, the self-management behavior score after 6 months remained significantly higher in the E-Coach group than in the UC group (analysis of covariance (ANCOVA): F(1, 93) = 6.3, p = 0.014, partial η2 = 0.06), with a mean difference of +11.6 (95%CI: 9.7 to 13.6; p < 0.001 by Bonferroni correction). The mean self-management behavior score increased from 57.1 to 78.3 points in the E-Coach group, representing a change of +21.2 points, compared with a change of +7.9 points (from 58.6 to 66.5 points) in the UC group. The between-group difference in change was +13.3 (95%CI: 9.9 to 16.5). As for the Kidney Disease Quality of Life-Short Form, the magnitude of score increase from baseline to 6 months was higher in the E-Coach group than the UC group, suggesting an improvement in patients' QoL. Regarding the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) and Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), the E-Coach group had a greater magnitude of score reduction from baseline to 6 months compared to the UC group, indicating a reduction in depressive and anxiety symptoms. The E-Coach group exhibited lower levels of potassium and phosphorus after 6 months than the UC group. The study demonstrates the superior effectiveness of E-Coach in enhancing self-management behavior, improving QoL, and alleviating depressive and anxiety symptoms in patients receiving MHD.

articles.title: Association of Family with Sequence Similarity 13 Member A Polymorphisms and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Risk.
articles.abstract: Prior evidence has linked DNA sequence variations in the FAM13A (family with sequence similarity 13 member A) locus to the onset of respiratory pathologies. Conducted as a hospital-based case-control investigation, this study sought to clarify whether selected single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in FAM13A influence the likelihood of developing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in older adults belonging to the Chinese Han population. The cohort comprised 541 participants, among whom 270 were diagnosed with COPD and 271 served as healthy comparators. DNA was isolated from peripheral blood leukocytes and genotyped by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS). Five SNPs-namely, rs2602119, rs1801915, rs11944668, rs3756050, and rs2869950-were evaluated through multivariable logistic regression modeling, while potential epistatic interactions were probed via multifactor dimensionality reduction (MDR). FPRP analysis was used to assess the noteworthiness of statistically significant associations, with an FPRP threshold of 0.2 and a prior probability level of 0.25. The variant C allele of rs2869950 was identified as a genetic risk factor for COPD susceptibility (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.07-1.77, p = 0.012; FPRP = 0.033). Similarly, the heterozygous TC genotype of rs2869950 was significantly associated with an elevated risk of COPD (TC vs. TT: OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.14-2.40, p = 0.008; FPRP = 0.025). Moreover, the FAM13A-rs2869950 variant was found to be significantly associated with an increased risk of COPD in specific subgroups, including females, smokers, drinkers, individuals older than 71 years, and those with a BMI below 24 kg/m2 (OR > 1, p < 0.05). MDR analysis indicated synergistic interactions among SNPs, with a four-locus model (rs2602119, rs1801915, rs11944668, and rs2869950) achieving a testing balanced accuracy of 0.5193 (training balanced accuracy, 0.6075) and perfect cross-validation consistency. Taken together, these data indicate that both the C allele and the TC genotype at rs2869950 constitute susceptibility factors for COPD in the population under investigation.

articles.title: Assessing Diabetes-Associated Bone Changes Using Chest Computed Tomography Radiomics and Extreme Gradient Boosting: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) provides quantitative information on bone that may reveal diabetes-associated skeletal changes not readily identified by routine image assessment. This study aimed to establish a prediction model for diabetes using chest CT radiomics features and identify bone features with the highest contributions to diabetes prediction. One hundred patients with diabetes and 100 healthy controls underwent chest CT. The thoracic vertebrae, scapulae, and sternum were automatically segmented using a convolutional neural network (CNN), and 93 radiomics features were extracted from each structure. Max-Relevance and Min-Redundancy (mRMR), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were successively used for feature selection and model development. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was evaluated using internal-validation data and an external-test cohort of 50 participants, including 25 patients with diabetes. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the XGBoost model. After mRMR, and LASSO, 17 features were selected. The model achieved AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90 on the internal-validation and external-test data, respectively. gldm_SmallDependenceLowGrayLevelEmphasis_T11, glcm_Idmn_T8, and gldm_LargeDependenceHighGrayLevelEmphasis_T4 showed the highest contributions to diabetes prediction in the SHAP analysis. Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels correlated with several bone CT features. These findings demonstrate that chest CT radiomics combined with interpretable machine learning can characterize diabetes-associated bone changes and distinguish patients with diabetes from healthy controls.

articles.title: A rare diagnosis during evaluation for metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease: Glycogen storage disease type Ia presenting during adolescence in a male with severe obesity.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a common comorbidity of pediatric obesity that predisposes patients to hepatocellular adenomas (HCAs). HCAs however are nonspecific to MASLD and warrant further evaluation. We present a case of a 16-year-old male with severe obesity, and persistently elevated liver enzymes, initially evaluated for MASLD. Imaging revealed multiple hepatic lesions consistent with HCAs, prompting further genetic evaluation. Trio exome sequencing identified biallelic variants in the glucose-6-phophatase gene, confirming a diagnosis of glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSD Ia). This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by overlapping features of MASLD and GSD Ia, particularly hepatic steatosis, HCAs, and metabolic syndrome. Initial management of MASLD with glucagon-like peptide-1 therapy was discontinued given risk for hypoglycemia, and the patient continues glucose monitoring and cornstarch therapy. This case emphasizes the importance of including inborn errors of metabolism in the differential diagnosis for multifocal HCAs and concerns with obesity treatments.

articles.title: Mindfulness-based perioperative care, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, and early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a prospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between perioperative care by mindfulness and sleep quality, autonomic regulation, inflammatory activity, and early recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmia (AT) following radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for atrial fibrillation (AF). This was a prospective assessor-blinded observational cohort study involving 124 patients with AF who underwent their initial radiofrequency catheter ablation from April 2023 to December 2025. Conventional perioperative care was provided to one group (n=62), while the other group (n=62) received mindfulness-based perioperative care. To reduce baseline imbalance, propensity score overlap weighting was implemented. Objective sleep architecture was assessed by overnight polysomnography and autonomic function was examined by HRV analysis. hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and MCP-1 were analyzed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Health related quality of life was determined based on the SF-36 questionnaire. Compared with conventional care, mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with greater observed changes in total sleep time (389.4 ± 43.8 vs. 365.7 ± 45.2 min, P=0.012), sleep efficiency (77.4 ± 7.2% vs. 71.2 ± 7.8%, P=0.004), sleep onset latency (27.1 ± 8.8 vs. 34.8 ± 10.5 min, P=0.009), and PSQI scores (7.2 ± 2.5 vs. 9.3 ± 2.9, P=0.006). The mindfulness group also showed lower inflammatory biomarker levels and differences in short-term autonomic indices, including a lower LF/HF ratio (1.39 ± 0.41 vs. 1.66 ± 0.54, P=0.005). Early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence occurred in 6 patients (9.7%) in the mindfulness-based perioperative care group and in 11 patients (17.7%) in the conventional care group, corresponding to a crude risk ratio of 0.55 (95% CI: 0.22-1.38). Mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with improved objective and subjective sleep quality, more favorable autonomic and inflammatory biomarker profiles, better postoperative quality of life, and a lower observed rate of early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for AF.

articles.title: A retrospective exploratory cross-sectional comparison of service evaluation outcomes between an Aotearoa and Australian secure youth forensic inpatient mental health service.
articles.journal: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
articles.abstract: AimTo compare demographic characteristics, diagnostic patterns, and discharge outcomes between an Aotearoa (Ngā Taiohi) and an Australian (Austinmer) secure youth forensic inpatient mental health service.MethodsA retrospective exploratory cross-sectional study of routinely collected service-level data for the first 98 and 113 consecutive admissions to Austinmer and Ngā Taiohi, respectively. De-identified data were compared with descriptive statistics and differences statistically examined.ResultsThere was no statistical difference in median age. Ngā Taiohi had a greater proportion of females. There was no significant difference in the rate of personality disorders (18% vs 11%) or psychotic disorders (62% vs 73%) between Ngā Taiohi and Austinmer, respectively. Māori were more likely to have a primary diagnosis of psychotic disorders (71%) compared to NZ Europeans (43%).Median lengths of stay were not significantly different. Ngā Taiohi patients were more likely to discharge to community care (59%) compared to Austinmer (43%). Readmission rates did not significantly differ between units.ConclusionsThis is the first study comparing youth forensic inpatient mental health services between Aotearoa and Australia, utilising service-level data. Similarities highlighted included age, primary diagnosis and Indigenous overrepresentation. Differences highlighted may reflect variation in terms of clinical service pressures between locations.

articles.title: When the abdomen misleads: Emphysematous pyelonephritis masquerading as pneumoperitoneum.
articles.abstract: A presentation in septic shock with tense abdominal distension and left flank pain, combined with a plain radiograph showing massive subdiaphragmatic free air usually suggests perforation of a hollow viscus. A CT scan obtained before laparotomy was undertaken, showing gas destroying the left renal parenchyma with extension into the pararenal space and rupture through the posterior parietal peritoneum with an intact gastrointestinal tract. Laparotomy was thus avoided; pneumoperitoneum is not always gastrointestinal in origin.

articles.title: Electrocardiographic Clues to Digoxin Toxicity in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians

articles.title: Heart failure in severe mental illness: an inequality hiding in plain sight.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians

articles.title: A scoping literature review: Identifying the comorbidities of Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThere are many co-occurring conditions of Alzheimer's disease (AD).ObjectiveThis scoping literature review aims to identify the comorbidities of AD found in the literature.MethodsWe conducted an extensive scoping search using PubMed for January 1, 2015 to June 10, 2025, yielding 461 articles. 39 articles met inclusion criteria. Descriptive statistics were completed on the extracted information.ResultsThe conditions identified encompass the body's major organ systems, with diabetes and hypertension appearing the most.ConclusionsThis scoping review highlights the large number of comorbidities associated with AD.

articles.title: Decision-making in biospecimen and biomarker research among African American participants: Procedure-specific perspectives including on the uniqueness of brain donation.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAfrican Americans are disproportionately affected by Alzheimer's disease (AD) but remain significantly underrepresented in research. While previous studies often assess these barriers to such research engagement using hypothetical scenarios, there is a need to focus on in vivo decision-making processesObjectiveTo identify the specific facilitators and barriers influencing African American participants' decisions to engage in or decline four types of biospecimen data collection: biomarker collection via MRI, PET, or lumbar puncture (LP), and brain donation.MethodsSemi-structured interviews were conducted with 41 participants (68.2% female; age range 58-84; average 68) recruited from the African Americans Fighting Alzheimer's in Midlife Study who had made the decision for or against these four types of research. A descriptive content analysis identified specific factors that influenced decision-making.ResultsAcceptability levels varied by procedure: MRI (80.5%) and PET scans (63.4%) were the most accepted, whereas LP (36.6%) and brain donation (34.1%) were the least. Common motivations included personal family experience with AD and a desire to benefit the African American community. Barriers for LP and MRI included perceived physical risk and claustrophobia, respectively. Brain donation emerged as a unique, family-centered decision rather than an individual one. A high percentage of participants (34%) remained undecided about brain donation due to concerns about family burden during end-of-life transitions and a lack of procedural information.ConclusionsThis examination of real-life research decisions confirmed prior findings and highlighted opportunities to improve outreach to African American community members, particularly regarding brain donation, which may require unique approaches.

articles.title: Epidemiology, autoimmune overlap and in-hospital outcomes of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies in Spain, 1997-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To define the epidemiology, autoimmune overlap and in-hospital outcomes of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) in Spain, separating true IIM from the symptomatic-myopathy code (G73.7), and to identify predictors of mortality and intensive-care (ICU) admission.

METHODS: Population-based analysis of the Spanish hospital-discharge registries (CMBD and RAE-CMBD, 1997-2024). Rates are hospitalization rates, not incidence or prevalence. True IIM comprised the DM/PM group (dermatomyositis, polymyositis and paraneoplastic DM codes), immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy/other (IMNM/Other) and inclusion body myositis (IBM). Estimates were verified against patient-clustered standard errors.

RESULTS: Of 36 732 episodes (8053 patients in 2016-2024, 9162 earlier), 34 228 (93.2%) were true IIM (DM/PM group 84.0%: 61.4% DM-coded, 35.7% PM-coded, 2.9% paraneoplastic; IMNM/Other 13.7%, IBM 2.4%). Hospitalization rose from 1.67 to 4.24 per 100 000/year, confined to ages ≥60. Coexisting autoimmune disease occurred in 13.7% (about one in seven). Mortality was 6.1% and stable. Predictors of death were advancing age (adjusted OR up to 7.97), malignancy, heart failure, interstitial lung disease (ILD), dysphagia and chronic kidney disease (C-statistic 0.77); ICU admission fell in the very elderly (OR 0.21), indicating ceiling-of-care de-escalation. Apparent protective effects of COPD and diabetes reflected collider bias. Within the DM/PM group, 29.4% were coded as polymyositis (M33.2), with more ILD, overlap and antisynthetase features but less malignancy, declining from 40% to 27%.

CONCLUSION: IIM hospitalizations doubled over 28 years, driven by IMNM recognition and ageing, with outcomes governed by acute complications and comorbidity rather than subtype. Symptomatic myopathy should be analysed separately and paraneoplastic dermatomyositis unified with idiopathic DM.

articles.title: A Case Report of Lyme Carditis Presenting as New-Onset Atrial Flutter in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Lyme disease (LD) is the most common vector-borne disease in the United States and has several well-known pathologic sequelae if not treated, including third-degree atrioventricular block. However, an association between Lyme carditis and atrial arrhythmias has been described in some cardiology literature but has not been reported in emergency medicine or wilderness medicine literature. This case report describes an older adult with new-onset atrial flutter with rapid ventricular rate in the setting of early disseminated LD, who ultimately was treated with antibiotics, had resolution of atrial flutter, and has had no recurrence. As cardiac inflammation secondary to organ infection may manifest as multiple forms of arrhythmia, this case report highlights the importance of considering LD as a differential diagnosis when treating tick-exposed patients with new cardiac arrhythmias, including atrial flutter.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of central nervous system persistence of morbilliviruses across host species reveals shared features with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a rare but always fatal neurological complication of measles, associated with persistent measles virus (MeV) infection of the central nervous system (CNS). MeV is detected in the brains of deceased SSPE patients as hypermutated viral genomes, which often contain premature stop codons in the matrix (M) gene and encode a hyperfusogenic fusion (F) protein. As a result, infected cells in the CNS cannot produce virions but rather transmit the viral ribonucleoprotein from cell-to-cell in a slow but progressive manner, which ultimately results in widespread MeV infection of the brain. However, our understanding of the pathogenesis of SSPE is constrained by the lack of animal models combined with a clinically silent incubation period of several years.

MAIN TEXT: In a recent publication in PNAS, Daniel Roji et al. analysed animal morbillivirus sequences detected in the brains of persistently infected hosts, including a lynx (canine distemper virus, CDV), two seals (phocine distemper virus, PDV) and a dolphin (cetacean morbillivirus, CeMV). The authors describe that the morbillivirus sequences detected in these animals contained unique mutational signatures. The CDV, CeMV and one of the PDV sequences encoded nonfunctional M proteins and hyperfusogenic F proteins, reminiscent of the mutational profile of MeV detected in SSPE patients. Therefore, the authors conclude that human and animal morbilliviruses associated with chronic neurological infections share key genotypic and phenotypic traits, and that thorough analysis of naturally occurring animal morbillivirus infections could improve our understanding of SSPE pathogenesis.

CONCLUSION: The comparison of neurological complications associated with human and animal morbillivirus infections as described by Daniel Roji et al. provides a unique One Health approach to understanding the drivers of SSPE. These findings may support the development of early diagnostics or an animal model for SSPE, providing an opportunity to test novel intervention strategies.

articles.title: A less invasive alternative to fenestration for selected localized postoperative empyema with persistent air leak: prolonged open drainage using a large-sized cut tube in two patients.
articles.journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative empyema with persistent air leak remains a challenging complication after pulmonary resection. Fenestration may be required in refractory cases but is highly invasive, particularly in high-risk patients. We report two patients successfully treated with prolonged open drainage using a large-sized cut tube without fenestration and propose clinical criteria for selecting suitable candidates.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 72-year-old man with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis developed Aspergillus empyema with persistent air leak after bullectomy for pneumothorax, and a 71-year-old man developed empyema with persistent air leak after left lower lobectomy and lingulectomy with bronchoplasty for lung cancer. Both were initially treated with closed chest drainage and antimicrobial therapy. On days 23 and 32, respectively, after infection was controlled, drainage volume decreased to < 50 mL/day, the empyema cavity became localized, and residual lung expansion remained stable despite persistent air leakage, the drainage tubes were cut and shortened to convert them to open drainage. CT confirmed that both cavities were anatomically separated from the pulmonary artery and other major hilar vessels. Both patients were subsequently managed as outpatients, and the empyema cavities gradually became obliterated by granulation tissue, allowing tube removal without fenestration. No recurrence occurred during 2 and 4 years of follow-up, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged open drainage with a large-sized cut tube may provide a less invasive alternative to fenestration in selected patients with postoperative empyema and persistent air leak. Suitable candidates may be characterized by controlled infection, low drainage volume, a localized empyema cavity, stable residual lung expansion, and anatomical separation from major hilar vessels.

articles.title: Clonal, regionally clustered spread-rather than vertical transmission-explains surges in fluoroquinolone‑resistant Campylobacter jejuni in Finnish broilers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Campylobacter jejuni is a major zoonotic foodborne pathogen, with poultry recognized as an important reservoir for human infection. Although antimicrobial use in Finnish broiler production is minimal, sporadic increases in fluoroquinolone- and tetracycline-resistant C. jejuni have been detected. We investigated the population structure, antimicrobial resistance, and transmission pathways of C. jejuni in Finnish poultry production.

RESULTS: A total of 333 C. jejuni isolates collected from breeder (n = 145) and broiler (n = 188) flocks during 2014-2019 were characterized using whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial resistance profiling, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), core-genome MLST (cgMLST), and phylogenomic analysis. Resistance to fluoroquinolones and tetracycline was concentrated in specific years and was strongly associated with particular lineages, especially ST-206 clonal complex (CC), whereas the predominant ST-45 CC was largely susceptible. Genomic clustering identified several resistant clones circulating among geographically proximate broiler farms, indicating regional horizontal dissemination. Resistant isolates from breeders were uncommon, and no genomic evidence supported vertical transmission of resistant strains from breeder to broiler flocks. Instead, resistance peaks were primarily attributable to clonal expansion of successful resistant lineages.

CONCLUSIONS: Transient increases in fluoroquinolone- and tetracycline-resistant C. jejuni in Finnish broiler production were driven mainly by regional clonal horizontal spread rather than vertical transmission from breeders to broilers. These findings highlight the value of genomic surveillance for detecting and tracking antimicrobial-resistant Campylobacter lineages and support the integration of molecular epidemiology into poultry surveillance and control programmes.

articles.title: Tumor volume may be a better indicator than diameter for occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinical stage-1 lung cancer.
articles.abstract: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

articles.title: Different intestinal bipartition procedures: early retrospective results from a multicenter Italian experience in 202 patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleeve gastrectomy with intestinal transit bipartition (SG-TB) represents an emerging metabolic bariatric strategy designed to enhance ileal stimulation while preserving physiological nutrient absorption. Different technical variants have been developed, but real world data from multicenter national experiences remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary outcomes of intestinal bipartition procedures in Italy.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included 202 consecutive patients who underwent Roux-en-Y Transit Bipartition (RYTB), One Anastomosis Transit Bipartition/ Single Anastomosis Sleeve-Ileal bypass (OATB/SASI), or Duodeno-Ileal Transit Bipartition (DITB) between July 2019 and November 2025 across 13 Italian metabolic bariatric centers. Primary outcomes were weight loss expressed as BMI change, percentage of excess weight loss (%EWL), and percentage of total weight loss (%TWL) at 3, 6 and 12 months. Secondary outcomes included weight related disorders resolution, perioperative outcomes, and complications.

RESULTS: Mean baseline BMI was 45.7 kg/m². At 12 months, BMI decreased to 31.9 kg/m², with a mean %EWL of 65.7% and %TWL of 30.9%. Primary RYTB achieved superior weight loss compared with conversional OATB (%EWL79.7% vs. 64.7%; %TWL 41.7% vs. 29.5%).At 12 months, remission rates were 58.5% for hypertension, 34.2% for type 2 diabetes (50% improved), 76.1% for OSAS, and 75% for dyslipidemia. Early complications occurred in 9.9% of patients, with major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥IIIb) in 1.5%. Readmission rate was 2.5%.

CONCLUSIONS: Intestinal bipartition procedures demonstrated effective weight loss, significant metabolic improvement, and a favorable safety profile in a real world multicenter setting, in our early (12 months) results. Primary procedures achieved more consistent weight loss, although conversional surgery provided clinically meaningful outcomes. Standardization of technical parameters, particularly common channel length, may further optimize results.

articles.title: Plan for Scale Out: Adapting a Diabetes Prevention Program for Implementation in Rural and Remote British Columbia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rural and remote communities in Canada face a higher incidence and risk of developing type 2 diabetes (T2D) compared to urban populations (Government of Canada SC, 2022). Small Steps for Big Changes is an evidence-based diabetes prevention program designed to support individuals at risk of T2D in adopting and maintaining sustainable changes to their diet and exercise through the application of behavior change techniques. To expand the reach of Small Steps for Big Changes and address the significant gap in T2D prevention resources in rural and remote communities, the program was scaled out to rural and remote community organizations across British Columbia. The aim of this study was to describe the process used to scale out Small Steps for Big Changes and to identify the program and implementation strategy (IS) adaptations made during the pre-implementation phase to support delivery.

METHOD: Adoption rates were analyzed and reported according to the adoption dimension of the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) framework (Glasgow et al., Am J Public Health 89(9):1322-1327, 1999 Sep) to describe the proportion of settings willing to deliver Small Steps for Big Changes. Data on adaptations were extracted from meeting notes and email correspondence. Adaptations to IS were identified by comparing these data to IS used in a previous Small Steps for Big Changes implementation project. All adaptations were deductively coded by two independent coders using the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications to Evidence-Based Interventions (S, Wiltsey Stirman et al., Implement Sci 14(1):58, 2019 Jun 6) and the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications to Implementation Strategies (CJ Miller et al., Implement Sci 16(1):36, 2021 Apr 7).

RESULTS: Three organizations in the Interior and two in the Northern region of British Columbia adopted Small Steps for Big Changes, representing adoption rates of 23% and 22%, respectively. Twenty-seven program adaptations were made with a primary goal of improving program oversight and quality improvement. 15 implementation strategy adaptations were identified and an additional 15 implementation strategies were added to support scale-out in attempts to improve reach, adoption, acceptability, or fidelity of the program.

CONCLUSION: These findings can inform targeted implementation efforts and guide decisions about scaling diabetes prevention programs, such as Small Steps for Big Changes, into diverse community settings.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Concordance of a BI-RADS-Output AI System in Mammography: A Retrospective Study of Radiologists-AI Collaboration.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: The identification of breast cancer using mammography and ultrasonography is influenced by inter-observer variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) models for breast classification have been investigated, but limited reports exist on Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS)-output AI systems. This study attempted to assess a BI-RADS-output AI system by comparing breast cancer detection rates among radiologist-only, AI-only, and combined interpretations, while also focusing on the AI's ability to identify cancers missed by radiologists and analyzing diagnostic concordance concerning imaging features and BI-RADS categories. A retrospective analysis was performed on 331 lesions from 321 consecutive breast cancer patients who underwent preoperative digital mammography and ultrasonography. McNemar's test was used to find the detection rates, and chi-square/Fisher's test, Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) analysis, and Kappa statistics were used to verify the diagnostic performance. The combined radiologist-AI interpretation achieved the highest cancer detection rate of 90.6%, which was higher than the radiologist's rate of 87.6% and the AI's rate of 84.0% (P < 0.05). The advantage was especially evident for BI-RADS 4B lesions, where AI alone decreased to 54.4%, while the combined method increased to 81.8%. AI found tumors that radiologists missed, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.840. There was a strong agreement for microcalcifications (κ = 0.827), but only a weak to moderate agreement for mass morphology and final BI-RADS classification (κ = 0.142-0.414). Although AI-radiologist agreement varied across different imaging features, their complementary strengths enabled improved cancer detection performance, supporting the role of BI-RADS-output AI systems as clinical decision-support tools rather than replacements for radiologists.

articles.title: Cardiac Image Segmentation Under Respiratory Motion Artifacts Using Different Modified U-Net Models.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Precise segmentation of cardiac magnetic resonance images (CMR) is essential to quantitative measurements of the heart, yet it is often affected by respiratory motion misregistration's and this is particularly common in free-breathing patient environments. These artifacts reduce the quality of the image and present a big challenge to traditional deep learning models such as the baseline U-Net. This paper carries out a systematic evaluation of the capabilities of four alternate U-Net architectures, Attention U-Net, Dense U-Net, Residual U-Net and Sharp U-Net, on CMR data with synthetically added motion artifacts of various intensities. To add synthetic artifacts, the deformation fields were employed that mimic the realistic breathing-induced deformations and obtained the clean, mild, moderate, and severe moving conditions. Hybrid loss function that combines Dice, Focal, and Tversky losses was used to train each model to create robustness to class imbalance and boundary degradation. The segmentation quality was assessed by the following evaluation metrics: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD) and Jaccard Index (JI). Their results show that Sharp U-Net had the best overall performance with the highest average DSC (0.927) and lowest HD (3.62 mm) in severe motion conditions. The region centered attention mechanisms were also capable of withstanding these in Attention U-Net. The dense and Residual U-Nets did not perform much better than the baseline, and did not perform as well when there were severe artifacts. These results show the significance of architectural improvements and motion consciousness instruction strategies in guaranteeing the dependable segmentation. The article provides a scalable and reproducible methodology to assess the performance of motion-robust deep learning models for CMR and adaptable for use in other clinical diagnostic applications where respiratory gating is not available. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and computationally practical approach to motion-robust cardiac MRI segmentation. Sharp U-Net achieved the highest segmentation performance under severe respiratory motion, with a DSC of 0.784, compared with 0.778 for Attention U-Net, while requiring a slightly higher inference latency of approximately 28-30 ms per 256 × 256 slice and GPU memory consumption of approximately 1.8 GB. This modest computational overhead represents a trade-off between improved boundary preservation and computational efficiency and should be considered when deploying the model in resource-constrained clinical environments. Across the clean, mild, moderate, and severe respiratory motion conditions, Sharp U-Net achieved an average DSC of 0.927. Under the most challenging severe-motion condition, the DSC decreased to 0.784, while maintaining an ASSD of 1.69 mm, sensitivity of 0.823, precision of 0.774, and RVE of 8.9%.

articles.title: Cancer Statistics 2026-A Shout-out and Challenge to the Source!
Bimekizumab in Chinese Patients with Active Non-Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis: 52-Week Results from the Phase 3 BE MOBILE 1 Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bimekizumab, a humanised monoclonal IgG1 antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin (IL)-17F in addition to IL-17A, was efficacious and well tolerated to 52 weeks in patients with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) in the global phase 3 multicentre study BE MOBILE 1. In this pre-specified analysis, we examine in more detail the efficacy and safety of bimekizumab in the Chinese subpopulation of patients with nr-axSpA from BE MOBILE 1.

METHODS: BE MOBILE 1 comprised a 16-week double-blind, placebo-controlled period and 36-week maintenance period. Patients with nr-axSpA were randomised to receive subcutaneous bimekizumab 160 mg every 4 weeks or placebo to week 16; thereafter, all patients received bimekizumab. Here we report efficacy and safety outcomes to week 52 for the Chinese subpopulation. No formal statistical comparisons were made; results should be interpreted as nominal.

RESULTS: Overall, 36/274 patients in BE MOBILE 1 were enrolled in China (bimekizumab-randomised 18; placebo-randomised 18); 32 completed week 52. A greater proportion of bimekizumab- vs placebo-randomised patients achieved Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) ≥ 40% response (38.9% vs 22.2%), ASAS partial remission (33.3% vs 11.1%), and Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score < 2.1 (77.7% vs 49.7%) at week 16. By week 52, improvements were comparable between bimekizumab-randomised and placebo-randomised patients who had switched to bimekizumab. Similar trends were observed for objective signs of inflammation, spinal pain, physical function, health-related quality of life, and peripheral manifestations. To week 52, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 33 bimekizumab-treated patients (91.7%), with upper respiratory tract infection the most frequent (10 patients [27.8%]). Four patients (11.1%) had serious TEAEs; four had fungal infections (11.1%; all Tinea). No patients experienced adjudicated inflammatory bowel disease or uveitis.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with nr-axSpA from China, bimekizumab showed rapid and sustained efficacy improvements to week 52 and was well tolerated, consistent with the global patient population. Graphical Abstract is available for this article.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT03928704.

articles.title: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain unclear. This systematic review of eight randomized controlled trials (n = 493) evaluating dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived bone mineral density reports findings separately for each agent, without pooling, because the trials evaluated four pharmacologically distinct agents differing markedly in weight-lowering potency. The evidence is sparse for every agent and is insufficient to establish the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in this population.

PURPOSE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the randomized evidence on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers in adults with overweight or obesity, reporting findings separately for each individual agent.

METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review (INPLASY202630076) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (January 2015 to July 2026). Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with mean baseline body mass index (BMI) > 25 kg/m², compared a GLP-1 RA with placebo or another antidiabetic therapy for ≥12 weeks, and reported BMD assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Because the included trials evaluated pharmacologically distinct agents that differ substantially in weight-lowering potency, results were synthesized narratively and reported separately by agent; no meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs (n = 493) were included. Three trials were at low risk of bias (Eriksson 2019; Hygum 2020; Hansen 2024) and five raised some concerns, principally regarding the randomization process and selective reporting; no agent is supported by more than one trial at low risk of bias. (Cai 2021 contributes two treatment arms assessed separately, giving nine comparisons in the risk-of-bias assessment.) Evidence was unevenly distributed across agents: semaglutide and dulaglutide were each evaluated in one trial, liraglutide in two, and exenatide in five. Five of the eight trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes, including all four that randomized an insulin comparator arm; three enrolled adults without diabetes, of which one was defined by obesity alone. By study-level mean baseline BMI, five trials lay in the obese range ( ≥ 30 kg/m²) and three in the overweight range (25 to <30 kg/m²). The single semaglutide trial (Hansen 2024; n = 64; low risk of bias), which produced the largest weight loss of any trial (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -6.8 kg vs placebo), reported reduced lumbar spine BMD (ETD - 0.018 g/cm², p = 0.007), reduced whole-body BMD (mean difference [MD] -0.02 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.03 to -0.01), and increased C-terminal telopeptide (CTX; MD 166.50 pg/mL; 95% CI 66.60 to 266.40). Liraglutide was evaluated at two doses with divergent results. At the weight-management dose of 3.0 mg daily, in the only trial conducted in adults with obesity and without diabetes (Jensen 2024; ETD - 6.7 kg vs placebo), lumbar spine BMD (MD - 0.019 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.034 to -0.004) and total hip BMD (MD - 0.013 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.024 to -0.002) were reduced. At the diabetes dose of 1.8 mg daily (Hygum 2020; -3.8 kg), no site changed materially (lumbar spine MD 0.00 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.01). Exenatide trials were inconsistent, ranging from 0.03 g/cm² (95% CI 0.02 to 0.03) at the lumbar spine (Renyuan 2015) to -0.04 g/cm² (95% CI - 0.15 to 0.07; Akyay 2023). Certainty of evidence was very low for every agent.

CONCLUSION: The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required.
