articles.title: How-I-do-it: bottom dock eTEP with bilateral TAR for incisional hernia after liver transplantation: early outcomes and feasibility.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incisional hernias represent a significant source of morbidity for patients following liver transplantation, and repair of these defects remains challenging. Transversus abdominis release (TAR) is a posterior component separation technique enabling wide sublay prosthetic reinforcement which is suitable for the treatment of complex incisional hernias. TAR can be used with the enhanced view totally extraperitoneal (eTEP) approach, with favorable outcomes in non-transplant patients being reported.

METHODS: This is a single center retrospective review of adult liver transplant recipients with incisional hernias who underwent robotic-assisted eTEP with bilateral TAR between December 2022 and July 2026. A comprehensive description of the surgical technique is included. Patient demographics, hernia characteristics, as well as clinical outcomes are also described.

RESULTS: Twenty-six liver transplant patients who underwent incisional hernia repair with eTEP and bilateral TAR met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 60 (IQR 55-65) and patients were predominately male (81%, n = 21). Median BMI was 28.1 (IQR 24-32) and patients were predominately ASA 3 (81%, n = 21). Median hernia length was 12 cm (IQR 9-15) and width was 15 cm (IQR 10-22). Median mesh length was 30 cm (IQR 30-35) and width was 30 cm (IQR 27-37). Mesh was fixated in 65% of patients (n = 17), predominantly with sutures (88%, n = 15). Drains were used in 92% of patients (n = 24). Median operative time was 381 min (IQR 230-517). There were no conversions to open or intraoperative complications. One patient was readmitted for a mild drain site infection which was medically managed with no other complications. Median length of stay was 2 days (IQR 1-3). Over a median follow-up period of 11 months (IQR 7-18) no patients experienced recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Patients with chevron incisional hernias following liver transplantation may be repaired with robotic-assisted eTEP with bilateral TAR. In a cohort of suitable candidates, we report favorable 30-day outcomes.

articles.title: SAGES surgical management of gastroparesis: systematic review and expert consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroparesis is a debilitating disease for which therapeutic strategies achieve variable success. This systematic review and consensus statements address the surgical management of medically refractory gastroparesis.

METHODOLOGY: A systematic review was conducted, with a literature search through December 31, 2024, addressing the surgical treatment of gastroparesis, including gastric electrical stimulation (GES), gastric per-oral endoscopic myotomy (GPOEM), pyloroplasty and pyloromyotomy, and gastrectomy. Studies assessing symptom resolution and changes in gastric emptying were extracted. The findings were subsequently presented to a panel of surgeons and gastroenterologists, some of whom are members of the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons (SAGES), with the patient partner perspective considered. Consensus statements were generated from the presented data and subsequent discussion for each of the four treatment options.

RESULTS: All consensus statements were based on expert opinion due to poor and heterogeneous datasets for each intervention. The panel judged GES, pyloroplasty, and pyloromyotomy, including gastric per-oral endoscopic myotomy, to be reasonable treatments for patients with medically refractory gastroparesis. The panel does not suggest surgical resection as a standard treatment option for medically refractory gastroparesis, but acknowledges that in specific patient cases, it may be reasonable.

CONCLUSIONS: The consensus views achieved provide guidance for surgical approaches to medically refractory gastroparesis. The panel also highlighted evidence gaps that warrant research to strengthen the evidence base for surgical treatment strategies for gastroparesis.

articles.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in neurology: biomarkers and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a shared downstream pathogenic mechanism across a wide spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from primary mitochondrial diseases to conditions including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, hereditary ataxias and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. This Review examines the role of mitochondrial biomarkers in improving diagnostic accuracy, patient stratification and monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response. Primary mitochondrial diseases are presented as proof-of-concept models of impaired oxidative phosphorylation, providing a framework for biomarker identification and validation with translational relevance to other neurological diseases. Mitochondrial biomarkers can be broadly categorized into four domains: fluid biomarkers, reflecting metabolic alterations and stress signalling; genetic biomarkers, capturing mitochondrial DNA integrity and dynamics; multi-omics approaches, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures; and imaging biomarkers, enabling in vivo assessment of structural and functional consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. Across disorders, these biomarkers reveal shared disturbances in bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial genome maintenance and inflammatory signalling. However, clinical implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, biological variability and reduced disease specificity. Integrated, multimodal biomarker strategies, combined with longitudinal validation, will be essential for supporting precision medicine and guiding the development of therapies to target mitochondrial pathways in neurology.

articles.title: The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
articles.abstract: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.

articles.title: Microbial Ethylene Glycol Metabolism: Pathways, Metabolic Engineering, and PET Upcycling.
articles.abstract: Ethylene glycol (EG) is an attractive non-sugar carbon source because it can be obtained from petrochemical routes, renewable production platforms, and the depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), thereby linking plastic upcycling with sustainable biomanufacturing. In recent years, substantial progress has been made in elucidating EG catabolism, including the initial oxidation of EG, native glyoxylate assimilation pathways, synthetic route design, and chassis engineering. Nevertheless, efficient and robust EG bioconversion is still limited by unfavorable thermodynamics, low catalytic efficiency, intermediate toxicity, and pathway-host incompatibility. In this Review, we summarize recent advances in three interconnected areas: the oxidation of EG to glycolaldehyde and its downstream processing; glyoxylate-centered native assimilation networks and their integration with central carbon metabolism; and synthetic pathways designed to improve carbon conservation and redirect carbon flux toward acetyl-CoA, central metabolites, and target products. We compare the tartronate semialdehyde pathway with the β-hydroxyaspartate cycle, discuss key design principles for synthetic modules, and highlight recent progress in chassis engineering, regulatory rewiring, and the direct conversion of PET hydrolysates. We further emphasize the ongoing transition from single-substrate EG utilization to integrated PET upcycling, in which mixed-monomer co-utilization, impurity tolerance, and aldehyde detoxification have emerged as major engineering targets. Overall, EG is becoming a promising platform substrate for connecting plastic waste recycling with green biomanufacturing, although further advances in enzyme discovery, pathway optimization, and pathway-host matching are still required.

articles.title: FibriLysins disrupt Staphylococcus aureus biofilms and abscess communities.
articles.abstract: The rise of antibiotic resistance, particularly among pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, necessitates innovative antibacterial strategies. Here we introduce FibriLysins, a class of engineered enzymes combining staphylokinase and endolysin, which dismantle fibrin-encapsulated multicellular staphylococcal communities, including biofilms and staphylococcal abscess communities (SACs). We characterized diverse staphylokinases, developing a library of 27 FibriLysins, with a 78% positive hit rate. The lead variant, FL-028, has significant antibacterial activity against prevalent clinical S. aureus isolates. In vitro, FL-028 reduced bacterial counts in SACs by 3.4 log and in biofilms by 2.3 log. In vivo, FL-028 exhibits superior efficacy in a mouse model of bone fracture-related infection, outperforming vancomycin by 1 log and eliminating SAC presence in tissues. FL-028 shows no adverse effects on bone healing, as confirmed by histological examination, mechanical testing and micro-computed tomography analyses. These preclinical findings highlight the potential of FibriLysins as a robust and safe therapeutic approach against difficult-to-treat staphylococcal infections.

articles.title: First person infected with rare Shamonda virus: what we know.
Population-specific transcriptomic bioactivity assessment of perfluorooctanoic acid using human liver spheroids and physiologically based toxicokinetic modeling.
articles.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) has been widely used in industrial and consumer products and was recently classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. However, uncertainties remain regarding transcriptomic bioactivity thresholds associated with liver effects and their variability across clinically relevant populations. In this study, previously published transcriptomic data obtained following 24-h and 10-day exposure of primary human liver spheroids (LS) to PFOA were integrated into a physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK), population-specific framework to estimate transcriptomic human equivalent doses (HEDs). In addition, exploratory concordance analysis was performed between PFOA-responsive genes and liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC)-associated transcriptomic profiles. Median transcriptomic HEDs ranged from 283 to 412 µg/kg body weight (bw)/week and were substantially higher than the estimated HEDs corresponding to the 95th percentile serum PFOA concentration in the U.S. population (0.0099 µg/kg bw/week) and the mean PFOA concentrations reported in human liver tissue samples (0.035 µg/kg bw/week). Obesity class III, cirrhosis Child-Pugh classes A and B, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease reduced transcriptomic HEDs by approximately 31-41% compared with the healthy population, although HEDs remained substantially above reference values. Gene-level analysis identified only a limited number of genes within the bioactivity exposure ratio range of 1-100. More than 50% of PFOA-responsive genes exhibited concordant expression patterns with LIHC-associated transcriptomic profiles. Although the biological significance of these overlaps remains uncertain, concordance significantly exceeded that expected by chance from a background gene set and was driven mainly by down-regulated genes. Overall, this study provides a population-informed framework for integrating transcriptomic bioactivity data with PBTK modeling in human-relevant assessment of PFOA-associated liver effects.

articles.title: Precision medicine for pediatric cardiomyopathy: lessons from pediatric oncology.
Registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia, 2015-2024: a Bayesian spatiotemporal mapping study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe temporal and geographic variation in registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia and its ecological association with multidimensional poverty.

METHODS: This nationwide ecological study analyzed 4,234 presumed suicide deaths at ages 10-19 during 2015-2024 from the national forensic register (INMLCF). Bayesian Poisson models smoothed rates across neighboring departments and years. Aggregate rates combined four sex-age strata. Separate national vital-statistics (DANE) analyses compared suicide-coded deaths with two scenarios including undetermined intent.

RESULTS: Male-to-female rate ratios (RRs) were 2.00 (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.86-2.15) at ages 15-19 and 1.05 (0.93-1.18) at ages 10-14. Total posterior rates were 4.54 (4.22-4.87) per 100,000 in 2015 and 5.23 (4.86-5.60) in 2024; no adjacent-year change had a 95% CrI excluding zero. Putumayo, Arauca and Amazonas exceeded 10 per 100,000 in 2024. Fifteen INMLCF departments had a probability > 0.95 of rates above the national comparator in all ten years. The pooled Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) RR per standard deviation was 0.84 (0.74-0.94). Including usable DANE undetermined-intent deaths increased the strict count by 22.18%; the expanded pooled MPI RR was 1.04 (0.93-1.17).

CONCLUSION: Registered mortality varied by age, sex and department. MPI associations and geographic classifications depended on registration source and case definition. The findings do not establish protection from poverty and support strengthening adolescent surveillance and death classification.

articles.title: [Postgraduate training in anesthesiology in Germany : Challenges and perspectives].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postgraduate medical training in anesthesiology in Germany faces a variety of challenges, including high competency requirements, staffing shortages, the implementation of competence-based training programs and the potential long-term effects of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic.

METHODS: This secondary analysis focuses on the German subgroup of a survey conducted by the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC), as reported by Dow et al. Using descriptive statistics, the study analyzed training conditions, supervision, workload, pandemic-related impacts on training and the consideration of work abroad and examined these factors within a European context.

RESULTS: A total of 140 doctors in training from Germany completed the questionnaire. Although the results largely align with European trends, only a comparatively small proportion of respondents (38%) reported receiving adequate supervision. With a median of 50 working hours per week and regular overtime, the workload is high and 37% reported considering working abroad. Whilst the majority reported no significant pandemic-related disruption to their training, a substantial minority reported restrictions on acquiring practical skills or a lack of opportunities to catch up on missed content.

DISCUSSION: The findings underscore the need for improved supervision, competence-based training concepts, and adequate staffing. Coordinated measures by all relevant stakeholders, from hospital management to professional societies, appear necessary to improve the training and working conditions associated with the consideration of working abroad.

articles.title: Synchronous co-infection drives lineage representation in influenza A virus populations.
articles.abstract: RNA viruses evolve through replication errors that generate diversity but can also trigger cellular antiviral responses, creating an inherent tension between adaptation and host control. Influenza A virus biology adds to this complexity through genome segmentation, which enables reassortment but also creates infection heterogeneity through incomplete genome expression and packaging defects, and through superinfection exclusion, which restricts complementation. Together, these constraints would be expected to limit the consistent expansion of individual variants, yet the influenza A virus continues to adapt in nature, suggesting that specific infection contexts may allow disproportionate lineage amplification. To identify such contexts, we paired in vitro single-cell transcriptomics with viral lineage tracking to link infected cellular environments to viral output dynamics. We find that lineage enrichment predominantly occurs during synchronous coinfection, when multiple viral genomes occupy the same cell, and viral output is increased. These findings identify a timing-dependent condition under which lineage representation can shift, and predict that traits increasing burst output or the likelihood of synchronous coinfection may disproportionately shape population composition.

articles.title: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0-99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

articles.title: Blood pressure control before and after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage: a stroke service audit and strategies for improvement.
articles.abstract: In a retrospective audit of 89 adults with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) at a tertiary neuroscience centre, fewer than 60% met the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) blood pressure (BP) target in the year before their haemorrhage, despite most carrying a known diagnosis of hypertension. Blood pressure control and antihypertensive prescribing improved after ICH, yet most survivors remained above the European Stroke Organisation (ESO) secondary-prevention target, and the first documented community BP check occurred a median of 62 days after discharge. These findings expose primary- and secondary-prevention gaps spanning the whole care pathway and lend support to a structured, protocolised uptitration pathway after discharge, combining remote BP monitoring with pharmacist- or nurse-led dose escalation.

articles.title: AAV-mediated delivery of leptin but not adiponectin improves metabolic health in a pre-clinical mouse model of congenital generalised lipodystrophy.
articles.abstract: Lipodystrophies are a group of disorders featuring reduced adipose tissue mass or function, which often leads to significant metabolic disease, reduced lifespan and impaired quality of life. Individuals with congenital generalised lipodystrophy (CGL) have severely reduced adipose tissue mass. The loss of healthy systemic lipid storage typically causes hepatic steatosis and lipoatrophic diabetes. In addition, adipocyte-secreted hormones including leptin and adiponectin are dramatically reduced. Leptin has critical roles regulating appetite and broader effects on lipid and glucose metabolism. Daily injection with recombinant leptin is currently the only specific, approved treatment for CGL. The consequences of adiponectin loss in these patients are not fully understood. Likewise, the potential therapeutic benefit of adiponectin delivery is unclear. Here we examine the effect of delivering leptin or adiponectin by adeno-associated virus (AAV) as a potential gene therapy treatment for metabolic disease in CGL using a well-characterised murine model of the condition. AAV-mediated leptin delivery significantly improved hepatic steatosis and hyperinsulinemia. However, adiponectin delivery did not lead to any observed beneficial effects. This demonstrates that gene therapy approaches may have the potential to offer long-term delivery of leptin in individuals with lipodystrophy, without the need for continuous supply of perishable therapeutics and painful daily injections.

articles.title: Assessment of teachers' knowledge, awareness, and response to students with asthma in Greater Cairo schools.
articles.abstract: Bronchial asthma remains a significant public health challenge, especially among school-aged children. Schoolteachers are often the initial responders to asthma attacks, making their role vital for early symptom recognition and first aid provision. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the knowledge, awareness, and response of schoolteachers to students with asthma. Between March 2024 and October 2024, a self-administered questionnaire was created on Google Forms and distributed to schoolteachers through WhatsApp groups of private and public schools across different districts in Greater Cairo. The questionnaire consisted of three sections assessing: (1) teachers' experience and demographics, (2) basic knowledge of asthma, and (3) knowledge related to first aid response in an asthma attack. A total of 634 schoolteachers participated in the study. Of these, 361 (57%) reported having previously taught students with bronchial asthma, whereas only 176 (27.8%) had witnessed a student having an acute asthma attack before. A majority of participants (445/634, 70.2%) correctly identified the short-acting beta agonist (SABA) inhaler or nebulizer as appropriate first aid for an acute asthma attack. However, only 187/634 (29.5%) reported knowing the correct technique for using SABA inhalers or nebulizers during an asthma attack. More than half of the participants, 362/634 (57.1%), provided appropriate answers regarding the etiology of the disease, specifically whether it was a contagious disease or not. There was no statistically significant association between teachers' knowledge level and their sociodemographic characteristics. Teachers in Greater Cairo demonstrated fair knowledge and awareness regarding asthma. However, they did not fully understand appropriate first-aid responses, a gap that underscores the need for more asthma education programs.

articles.title: Impact of altered heme oxygenase-1 in caring for preterm neonates: navigating the unknown.
articles.abstract: Heme-oxygenase-1 (HO-1) is a key regulatory factor in organ development, organ function, cellular metabolism, heme processing, and bilirubin production. HO-1 homeostasis is crucial for healthy pregnancy and fetus. Dysregulation of HO-1 adversely affects placentation, yolk sac development, cardiovascular development, immune function, angiogenesis, microcirculation, alters the oxidoreductive balance, and is associated with adverse respiratory outcomes and necrotizing enterocolitis. The impact of HO-1 on neonatal neurodevelopment is unknown and is currently being investigated by our laboratory. In this review, we will discuss the morbidities associated with HO-1 dysregulation and importantly, we will navigate the unknown. We will highlight how infection or inflammation affect HO-1 homeostasis, its implications on neonatal morbidities at the limits of viability, summarize the relevant basic, translational, clinical and epidemiologic studies. We will conclude with proposing new approaches for the future, filling the gap between what is currently known and unknown. IMPACT: What does this article add to the existing literature? HO-1 pathway is relevant to pregnancy, fetus, neonatal, and later life outcomes. Provides comprehensive organ systems-based evaluation of Heme-oxygenase-1 in pregnancy, fetus, extreme preterm, and periviable neonates. Highlights how environmental factors, including infection, inflammation resulting in systemic dysregulation of HO-1 affects major neonatal morbidities. Underscores that novel investigations to close the knowledge gap are forthcoming to transform the HO-1 field.

articles.title: An ontology-based safe drug prescription method for controlling diabetes.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundDiabetes is a chronic disease also known as a non-communicable disease that cannot be completely cured but can be controlled through medication, or by maintaining a balanced diet and regular physical activity. Many drugs are available to control diabetes, but these drugs need to be carefully prescribed by the experienced physicians because the drugs may have side effects as well as adverse reactions.ObjectiveWe propose an ontology-based safe drug prescription method for diabetes that assists physicians in prescribing appropriate drugs by considering their side effects and interactions with other drugs, diseases and foods.MethodsThe proposed framework was implemented by creating an ontology by integrating drug-related information which includes side effects, drug interactions with other drugs, diseases and foods from different sources. We developed a Java-based user interface through which information on drug side effects, drug interactions and uses of the drugs can be retrieved using SPARQL queries.ResultsThe inferred results using SWRL rules and SPARQL queries were converted to a questionnaire that was validated by four physicians, and achieved the highest agreement score of 92.8%. The ontology-based model was also evaluated for consistency on HermiT and Pellet reasoners.ConclusionPatients with diabetes frequently have comorbidities requiring multiple medications, which increases the risk of adverse drug reactions. The constructed ontology provides a knowledge base to support physicians in identifying drug side effects and interactions. The Ontology incorporates knowledge related to causes of diabetes including impaired insulin secretion, insulin resistance and other causes based on obesity-related factors.

articles.title: Platelet-Loaded Anisotropic Cryogel for Rapid Hemostasis and Infected Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Skin wounds require complex interventions to overcome hemorrhage, infection, and delayed repair, which are multifunctional needs that current dressings rarely meet. Herein, we developed a platelet-loaded hyaluronic acid/gelatin (HA/GEL/P) anisotropic cryogel with integrated hemostatic, antibacterial, and regenerative properties. The anisotropic cryogel prepared through directional freezing exhibited aligned fibrous microstructures that facilitated the directed cell migration and proliferation. Concurrently, bioactive molecules released by activated platelets promote rapid hemostasis and synergistically enhance cell proliferation, angiogenesis and antibacterial effects. In a mouse wound model infected with Staphylococcus aureus, HA/GEL/P significantly accelerated wound closure by optimizing vascular and immune microenvironments to promote organized extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Histological analysis confirmed reduced infection and inflammation, coupled with improved collagen deposition and re-epithelialization. These results highlight the HA/GEL/P anisotropic cryogel as a promising multifunctional dressing for complex wound healing and advanced biomedical applications.

articles.title: Hearing function in virologically suppressed persons living with HIV: Results from the HELO study.
articles.journal: European annals of otorhinolaryngology, head and neck diseases
articles.abstract:
AIM: Hearing function is highly sensitive to aging and may represent a marker of neuro-sensory decline. Whether well-controlled HIV infection is associated with altered auditory function remains uncertain.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Cross-sectional exposed-non-exposed study including 100 antiretroviral therapy (ART)-treated persons living with HIV (PLHIVs) (≥10 years of infection and ≥5 years of sustained viral suppression <20 copies/mL) and 95 age- and sex-matched HIV-uninfected controls (HUCs). All participants underwent comprehensive audiological assessment including pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, auditory brainstem responses (ABR), and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Analyses were adjusted for age using multivariable models.

OBJECTIVES: To assess peripheral and brainstem auditory function in PLHIVs with long-term, tightly controlled virological suppression compared with HUCs. The primary objective was to compare pure-tone hearing thresholds in the better-hearing ear.

RESULTS: No clinically meaningful differences were observed between groups in pure-tone thresholds, speech audiometry parameters, ABR findings, or MRI small-vessel disease features. Mean air-conduction thresholds were 26.4±10.2dB in PLHIVs and 27.1±9.8dB in HUCs (P=0.52). Age-adjusted analyses showed no association between HIV status and auditory outcomes despite longstanding HIV infection. ABR wave latencies and interpeak intervals were comparable across groups. No significant correlation was found between auditory measures and global cognitive performance. Although some speech audiometry differences reached nominal significance levels, none met the predefined conservative significance threshold used to account for multiple testing.

CONCLUSION: Peripheral and brainstem auditory function were similar in virologically suppressed PLHIVs and HUCs. These findings suggest that, under current treatment conditions, well-controlled HIV infection is not associated with clinically meaningful peripheral or brainstem auditory dysfunction. Subtle auditory alterations cannot be completely excluded and may require more sensitive longitudinal or speech-in-noise assessments.

articles.title: Time course of acute spontaneous urticaria with treatment initiated within seven days of onset.
articles.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous urticaria (SU) persisting for ≤6 weeks is classified as acute SU (ASU) and tends to remit shortly, whereas SU persisting for >6 weeks is classified as chronic SU (CSU) and is likely to last longer. However, 6 weeks to separate them is based on the traditional clinical practice, and the time of pathological conversion from ASU to CSU remains unclear.

METHODS: We aimed to retrospectively analyze the time course of 1029 patients with SU in whom treatment was initiated within 7 days of onset. Time to complete control (no symptoms with medication) and time to remission (no symptoms without medication) were analyzed, in association with age, preceding acute infection, and treatment initiation day.

RESULTS: Of the 1029 patients, 902 were analyzed for time to complete control and 877 for time to remission. The survival rate of patients without remission rapidly decreased during the first 16 days and slowly declined thereafter. No sex-related differences were observed between the groups. Preceding acute infection, age <30 years, and earlier treatment initiation were associated with better prognosis in terms of both time to complete control and time to remission. Among patients with ASU who initiated treatment within 7 days of onset, those who started treatment by day 4 were more likely to achieve remission within 6 weeks than those who started on days 5-7.

CONCLUSIONS: ASU pathogenicity may change at around 16 days, rather than at 6 weeks. Early treatment initiation for ASU may be beneficial in preventing CSU progression.

articles.title: Real-world Data to Assess the Applicability of Randomized Controlled Trials in Newly Metastatic Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concerns persist regarding the applicability of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) to real-world clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the generalizability of RCTs using data from PIONEER.

DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Trial eligibility criteria were extracted from RCTs enrolling patients with mHSPC published between 2013 and 2023 and identified through a literature review. Patients with newly diagnosed mHSPC were identified from insurance claim databases mapped to the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model.

OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS AND STATISTICAL ANALYSES: The proportion of patients failing to meet at least one RCT eligibility criterion was assessed for each trial. The proportion of men receiving RCT-investigated treatments who would have been ineligible for the corresponding trials was estimated.

RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Overall, 12 trials were identified. From ∼398 000 patients with prostate cancer included in three databases, we identified 32 585 newly diagnosed mHSPC cases. The percentage of patients who would have been excluded from each RCT ranged between 8.6% and 55%. The percentage of patients who would be excluded from all trials ranged between 5.9% and 12% and increased to 26-44% when excluding the HORRAD trial. The most common reasons for exclusion were anemia (16-29%), heart failure (6.2-13%), and renal failure (3.9-19%). Between 18% and 52% of the patients receiving a drug would have been excluded from RCTs evaluating that drug. Limitations include database representativeness, incomplete clinical data, and limited generalizability to metachronous mHSPC.

CONCLUSIONS: Up to half of real-world patients with newly diagnosed mHSPC would have been ineligible for RCT participation, yet many received therapies despite trial ineligibility. This highlights the need for more inclusive and representative research and a comprehensive examination of real-world data for clinical decision-making.

PATIENTS SUMMARY: Up to half of real-world patients with newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer would have not been eligible for participation in clinical trials. A substantial proportion of patients receiving trial-tested therapies in routine clinical practice would have been excluded from the corresponding randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Substance use profiles predict health outcomes among U.S. adults with diabetes: Implications for primary care screening and intervention.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Substance use is common among adults with diabetes yet remains poorly characterized in terms of co-occurring patterns. This study sought to identify distinct substance use profiles among U.S. adults with diabetes, characterize factors associated with profile membership, and examine their clinical relevance.

METHODS: Data were from the 2022-2023 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (n = 89,889; 6805 with diabetes). Latent class analysis identified substance use profiles. Multinomial logistic regression examined demographic, socioeconomic, and mental health characteristics associated with profile membership. Weighted regression models evaluated associations between membership and health indicators.

RESULTS: Three profiles emerged: Low/Non-Use (67.6%), Cannabis and Binge Drinking (24.4%), and Polysubstance Use (8.0%). Higher-risk membership was associated with male sex, mental health burden, and urban residence; marriage and college education were protective. Both higher-risk classes were more than twice as likely to report poor self-rated health. Polysubstance Use class members had significantly higher odds of hospitalization (OR = 1.46).

CONCLUSIONS: Substance use among adults with diabetes is heterogeneous and linked to measurably worse health status outcomes including poorer self-rated health and higher hospitalization risk. These findings support routine, risk-stratified screening for substance use and mental health in diabetes care and may help inform targeted interventions.

articles.title: Placental adaptation to maternal overnutrition as an evolutionary trade-off.
articles.journal: Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM
articles.abstract: The mammalian placenta is genetically identical to the fetus, exposing it to unique selective pressures. In humans, placental evolution has been explored through the lens of nutritional scarcity, with selective pressures assumed to diminish as resources increase. Here, we challenge this assumption, arguing that maternal overnutrition constitutes a distinct and underappreciated selective pressure. Maternal inability to maintain fuel homeostasis exposes the fetus to nutrient overload, elevating fetal insulin and oxygen demand. Selection has favored placental adaptive responses to the resulting oxygen deficit, with insulin as the mechanistic core. However, the role of fetal hyperinsulinemia in protecting brain oxygen supply comes at the cost of excess fetal adiposity. This trade-off carries downstream health risks, including obstetric risks, preterm birth, and intergenerational metabolic disease.

articles.title: Coronary artery calcium comes of age: From risk marker to treatment threshold.
18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET in Infective Endocarditis and Device-Related Infections.
articles.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly in patients with prosthetic valves and cardiac devices, where echocardiography may be inconclusive. This review highlights the complementary role of advanced imaging, with a specific emphasis on 18F-FDG PET/computed tomography (CT). PET/CT has emerged as a critical adjunct, improving diagnostic sensitivity, particularly in prosthetic valve endocarditis and infections of cardiac implantable electronic devices. Beyond cardiac assessment, PET uniquely enables whole-body evaluation for extracardiac infection and septic emboli. Incorporation of PET findings into contemporary diagnostic algorithms enhances accuracy, facilitates early diagnosis, and supports treatment monitoring, thereby influencing clinical decision-making in complex IE cases.

articles.title: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography with Computed Tomography in Pediatric Non-oncological Conditions: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: This article examines the expanding role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography with computed tomography (PET/CT) in pediatric non-oncological conditions, moving beyond its established oncologic use. It outlines radiation dosimetry principles unique to children-emphasizing the As Low as Reasonably Achievable principle, reduced tracer activity, and low-dose CT protocols-given their heightened radiosensitivity. In pediatric neurology, FDG PET/CT aids evaluation of drug-refractory epilepsy (temporal and extratemporal foci) and neuronal migration/proliferation anomalies like focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), polymicrogyria, and hemimegalencephaly.

articles.title: Vulvar infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum: case report and literature review.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Histoplasmosis is a systemic mycosis caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. Genital involvement is exceptional and has not been previously reported in Spain.

METHODS: We report a case of vulvar infection by H. capsulatum and review the literature to identify additional cases.

RESULTS: Four cases of vulvar histoplasmosis were identified, including the present one. All occurred in immunocompromised patients, mostly with HIV infection, and presented as vulvar lesions suggestive of neoplasia or sexually transmitted infections. In our case, a 38-year-old woman with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, presented with a lesion suggestive of carcinoma. The diagnosis of histoplasmosis was confirmed by histopathology, fungal culture and molecular techniques, identifying H. capsulatum var. duboisii. All cases received antifungal therapy with favorable outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Vulvar histoplasmosis is an exceptional entity that may mimic other diseases, particularly in immunocompromised patients, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis.

articles.title: [Pulmonary infiltrates associated with chronic elevation of blood circulating monocytes].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) is a clonal myeloid neoplasm with myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features. Although inflammatory and extramedullary manifestations occur, pulmonary involvement is rare. We describe steroid-responsive pulmonary and systemic inflammatory involvement revealing CMML.

CASE REPORT: A 74-year-old man with a 3-year history of unclassified inflammatory polyarthritis presented with fever, hypoxemic respiratory failure, inflammatory wrist and ankle arthralgia, and pruritic maculopapular lesions. He required 5L/min oxygen. Laboratory studies showed CRP 216mg/L, hemoglobin 9.5g/dL, leukocytes 17.2G/L, and monocytosis 8G/L. Chest computed-tomography (CT) revealed a right lower-lobe mixed opacity, smooth interlobular septal thickening, and micronodules. Bronchoalveolar lavage was lymphocyte-predominant and sterile; antinuclear antibodies and anti-neutrophil cytoplasm antibodies were negative. Empirical piperacillin-tazobactam and diuretics did not improve inflammation or oxygen requirement. Skin biopsy showed an angiocentric infiltrate consistent with clonal monocytic infiltration. Bone marrow examination demonstrated dysmyelopoiesis, monocytic hyperplasia, and 11.5% blasts, confirming CMML. Sequencing with next generation sequencing identified DNMT3A, IDH2, SRSF2, RUNX1, and ASXL1 mutations. Prednisone 0.3mg/kg/day led to oxygen weaning, disappearance of fever, arthritis and rash, reduction in inflammatory markers and monocytosis and complete CT resolution of the interstitial lung disease within 7 days.

CONCLUSION: CMML-associated inflammatory pulmonary disease should be considered in unexplained infiltrates in patients suspected with CMML or persistent monocytosis after exclusion of infection, overload, and autoimmune disease.

articles.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of White Matter Hyperintensity Beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System for Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the additional prognostic value of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 1085 patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and brain magnetic resonance imaging between November 2018 and December 2022. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the predictive values, and the C-statistic was employed to determine their discriminatory power.

RESULTS: 170 (15.7%) patients experienced MACE during a median follow-up of 63.1 months. WMH remained a significant and independent risk factor for predicting MACE after adjustments with clinical variables alone or with CAD-RADS. In the training set, the clinical-CAD-RADS-WMH model showed area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.719, 0.740, and 0.776 for predicting MACE at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The model showed a consistent performance trend with AUCs of 0.819, 0.836, and 0.823 in the test set over 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. Both the addition of WMH to the clinical model and to the clinical plus CAD-RADS model significantly increased the C-statistic index (p = 0.007, p = 0.038 in the training set and p = 0.002, p = 0.004 in the test set). These trends continued to be present when WMH was analyzed as a continuous variable.

CONCLUSION: An elevated WMH was related to a higher risk of MACE in patients with suspected or established CAD. Moreover, WMH demonstrated additional prognostic value for MACE beyond CAD-RADS.

articles.title: Mapping human genetic associations to drug targets in valvular heart disease: an integrative evidence synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Valvular heart disease (VHD) lacks disease-modifying pharmacological therapies. Drug repurposing guided by human genetics may help identify therapeutic opportunities. We aimed to integrate human genetic associations, drug-target information, and clinical evidence to identify repurposing opportunities and prioritise potentially druggable targets across the VHD spectrum.

METHODS: We retrieved VHD-associated genetic variants from the NHGRI-EBI Genome-Wide Association Studies Catalogue and Ensembl, interrogated annotated genes in the Open Targets Platform, and evaluated linked drugs through structured searches of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251071741).

FINDINGS: We identified 1464 genetic associations corresponding to 844 unique variants and 582 candidate genes. Of these genes, 431 had tractability information and 51 had linked compounds, comprising 388 distinct pharmacological agents, 273 in phase 3 or 4 of clinical development. Drug-linked targets were concentrated in aortic stenosis. Clinical evidence supported therapeutic potential for 14 drugs, with preclinical or mechanistic cardiovascular support for eight additional drugs and adverse cardiovascular signals for four. An exploratory evidence-weighted framework prioritised targets according to genetic-functional evidence, tissue and mechanistic context, and translational tractability.

INTERPRETATION: This genetics-informed evidence synthesis identifies drug-repurposing opportunities and a substantial gap between genetically supported targets and available therapies. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for mechanistic validation and future valve-focused studies.

FUNDING: Limburg Clinical Research Centre of UHasselt, Jessa and ZOL; British Heart Foundation; National Institute for Health and Care Research; UK Research and Innovation; European Research Council; Horizon Europe.

articles.title: Growth and burnout in NICU nurses after experiencing adverse event trauma: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the association between posttraumatic growth (PTG) and occupational burnout among neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) nurses.

METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study (February-April 2026) enrolled 660 registered NICU nurses across 18 Chinese provinces. PTG was quantified using the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory (PTGI; 0-100), and burnout was assessed via the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS; 0-132). Multivariable linear regression, smooth curve fitting, and two-piecewise linear regression characterized the exposure-outcome relationship, adjusting for demographic, workload, and event-specific covariates.

RESULTS: After multivariable adjustment, PTG exhibited a significant inverse association with burnout (adjusted β = -0.42; 95% CI: -0.48 to -0.35). Threshold analysis identified an inflection point at a PTGI score of 46; below this threshold, PTG was not significantly associated with burnout (β = 0.13; P = 0.16). At or above 46 points, each 1-point increase in PTGI score was associated with a 0.60-point lower burnout score (adjusted β = -0.60; 95% CI: -0.69 to -0.52), with a slope 43% steeper than the conventional linear estimate.

CONCLUSION: PTG was associated with lower burnout scores in a threshold-dependent pattern among NICU nurses. The 46-point PTGI score should be considered provisional and requires longitudinal and interventional validation before clinical use.

articles.title: The effect of using a dragon-themed nebulizer mask on treatment application duration, adherence, and fear in children presenting to the emergency department: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nebulizer therapy can be distressing for young children, increasing fear, reducing cooperation, and prolonging treatment. This study examined the effects of a dragon-themed nebulizer mask on treatment duration, adherence, and fear in children receiving inhalation therapy in the pediatric emergency department.

METHODS: This parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted between January and March 2026 in the pediatric emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Istanbul. A total of 140 children aged 3-6 years requiring nebulizer therapy were randomized to either the intervention group (dragon-themed nebulizer mask, n = 70) or the control group (standard care, n = 70). Data were collected using the Demographic Information Form, Fear Scale, and Treatment Duration and Adherence Assessment Form. The researcher-nurse recorded outcomes. The study followed CONSORT guidelines and was registered as a clinical trial (Clinical Trial ID: NCT06568120).

RESULTS: Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between the groups (p > 0.05). The intervention group had significantly lower fear scores (p < 0.001, d = 3.05; 95% CI: 2.56-3.54) and shorter treatment duration (p = 0.012, d = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.14-0.81) than the control group. No significant between-group differences were observed in behavioral responses, including crying, treatment refusal, anger, or mask removal (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The dragon-themed nebulizer mask reduced fear and shortened treatment duration in preschool children receiving inhalation therapy in the pediatric emergency department. Child-friendly medical equipment may therefore represent a simple, low-cost strategy to improve treatment adherence and the overall treatment experience.

articles.title: Emerging Antiplatelet Agents: Revised Applications, Novel Targets, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Current antiplatelet therapies reduce thrombotic, particularly atherothrombotic events but remain constrained by bleeding risk, residual ischemic events, and pharmacokinetic or pharmacogenomic limitations. This review first evaluates the evolving strategies to optimize established agents, including P2Y12 monotherapy, genotype-guided de-escalation, aspirin formulation research, and aspirin in cancer chemoprevention. Second, it examines emerging agents designed for prehospital use in acute myocardial infarction and CYP2C19-independent clopidogrel alternatives aimed at improving global access. Finally, novel molecular targets including glycoprotein VI, protease-activated receptor 4, 12-lipoxygenase, and glycoprotein Ibα that aim to decouple thrombosis from hemostasis are discussed.

articles.title: The Unfinished Story of Megakaryopoiesis.
articles.abstract: Since their nineteenth-century discovery, megakaryocytes (MKs) and the platelets they produce have remained among the least understood lineages in hematology. Understanding megakaryopoiesis and thrombopoiesis is essential for deciphering hematological disorders and developing platelet biomanufacturing and cell-based therapies. We revisit MK and platelet biogenesis, from MK emergence from hematopoietic stem cells to platelet release through proplatelet formation and cytoplasmic fragmentation. The growing complexity of differentiation pathways challenges the classical hierarchical view of hematopoiesis. Many concepts established in mice remain insufficiently validated in humans, motivating 3D bioengineered models for disease study that may rewrite key chapters in human platelet biology.

articles.title: Epidemiological impact of Neospora caninum in Victorian dairy farms: Modelling effective control strategies.
articles.abstract: Neospora caninum is a major cause of abortion in cattle worldwide, causing significant economic losses. Despite Victoria's critical role in Australian dairy production, little is known about the local epidemiology of N. caninum and the effectiveness of control measures. This study aimed to evaluate infection dynamics and management strategies in Victorian dairy farms. Field data were collected from five dairy farms in Gippsland, including 1029 cow and calf samples. Vertical, horizontal and colostral transmission were assessed through longitudinal monitoring. Diagnostic performance of PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was compared. Deterministic and stochastic epidemiological models were developed and calibrated using local data to simulate infection dynamics and the impact of management strategies, including 'Test and Cull' and testing of replacement animals under varying biosecurity conditions. Prevalence of N. caninum was 36.7% in cows, 25.7% in calves and 32.3% overall. Vertical transmission occurred in 43% of calves from infected cows, while horizontal and colostral transmission contributed to 16% of infections in calves from uninfected cows. Longitudinal monitoring revealed 8.3% of previously negative dams seroconverted during gestation. PCR and ELISA showed poor concordance, highlighting their complementary role in surveillance. Model projections indicated rising prevalence under baseline conditions, particularly in closed herds. The 'Test and Cull' strategy consistently reduced prevalence, achieving <15% herd prevalence within 10 years, with further reductions under enhanced biosecurity. Testing replacement animals was effective only in herds sourcing their stock externally.

Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban and Rivaroxaban During Extended Anticoagulation for Venous Thromboembolism: A Non-randomised Post Hoc Comparison Within the RENOVE Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Some evidence reported that rivaroxaban use is associated with a higher risk of clinically relevant bleeding (CRB) than apixaban during the first months of treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE). We aimed to determine whether the risk of CRB is higher with rivaroxaban than apixaban during extended treatment, either at full or reduced dose.

METHODS: The RENOVE open-label randomised controlled trial compared full-dose versus reduced-dose of apixaban or rivaroxaban in patients who had completed at least 6 months of full-dose treatment for VTE and required extended anticoagulation. Drug choice was not randomised. In this post-analysis, the primary outcome was centrally-adjudicated CRB events. Treatment effects were estimated using crude hazard ratio (HR), adjusted HR, and an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW).

RESULTS: Among 2768 enrolled patients, 1513 received rivaroxaban (755 full-dose, 758 reduced-dose) and 1255 apixaban (630 full-dose, 625 reduced-dose). Median age was 62.6 versus 66.5 years and proportion of female was 32.1% versus 38.7%, respectively. Median follow-up was 37 months. The 5-year cumulative incidence of CRB was 11.7% with rivaroxaban and 13.7% with apixaban (adjusted-HR 0.90 [95%CI 0.70-1.17], HRIPTW 0.92 [0.70-1.21]). The incidence of major bleeding, recurrent VTE, composite outcome, arterial thromboembolic events, and all-cause death were similar. Serious adverse event not related to VTE and CRB was 7.7% and 10.8%, respectively (adjusted-HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.57-0.97], HRIPTW 0.76 [0.55-1.04]).

CONCLUSIONS: During extended anticoagulation, no difference in clinically relevant bleeding or recurrent VTE was observed between rivaroxaban and apixaban, although that non-randomised treatment allocation possibly influenced outcomes.

Development of an implementation package for asthma medication optimisation in the emergency department (AMEND): an evidence, theory and person-based approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Salbutamol is the most commonly prescribed inhaler for adults discharged from the emergency department (ED) with uncontrolled asthma. However, newer options, for example, maintenance and reliever therapy, are now recommended due to growing concerns over risks linked to salbutamol overprescription. Transitioning to new inhalers requires support for both patients and healthcare professionals (HCPs). This paper outlines how we developed an implementation package based on evidence, theory and the person-based approach to support asthma medication optimisation in the ED.

METHODS: The purpose of this study was to use person-based intervention development methods in a three-phase process: (1) understanding behaviour—collating and synthesising evidence from in-depth interviews with the target population (patients and HCPs); secondary deductive analysis using the theoretical domains framework to understand barriers and facilitators to prescribing; developing guiding principles and logic model based on underlying theory; (2) identifying behavioural content and implementation options—behaviour change techniques were selected and translated into intervention content; (3) intervention materials developed and refined with input of stakeholders.

RESULTS: We identified modifiable target behaviours for HCPs to support guideline-based care in the ED. These included identifying eligible patients, communicating rationale, providing patients with inhaler and resources and communicating changes to primary care. Key theoretical domains included knowledge, skills, addressing beliefs about consequences and targeting professional role perceptions. These domains were targeted through a clinical decision aid and training materials for ED HCP, template discharge summary for primary care and visual and written materials for patients. Minor refinements were made based on stakeholder feedback (six ED doctor think-aloud interviews; two patient workshops with eight and five participants respectively; and 12 survey responses to final draft of video).

CONCLUSION: We developed an intervention grounded in theory, evidence and stakeholder feedback aimed at promoting and supporting delivery of guideline recommendations.

articles.title: Profound thrombocytopenia and transient leucoerythroblastosis following hip fracture surgery.
articles.abstract: An elderly man underwent hip fracture surgery with pre-/postoperative heparin anticoagulation; the platelet count fell to 5×109/L (nadir); haematopathology blood film review identified leucoerythroblastosis (circulating normoblasts, leucocyte left-shift) and schistocytosis (red cell fragments). Although screening platelet factor 4 (PF4)/heparin enzyme-immunoassay for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) antibodies yielded a strong-positive result, the confirmatory serotonin-release assay gave an atypical profile (strong serum-induced serotonin-release but only partial inhibition by platelet Fc receptor-blocking monoclonal antibody). Bilateral lower-limb deep-vein thrombosis prompted treatment with therapeutic-dose fondaparinux and high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) for presumptive ‘autoimmune HIT’ (aHIT), that is, HIT featuring both heparin-dependent and heparin-independent platelet-activating anti-PF4/heparin antibodies. Persistent thrombocytopenia, recurrent fibrinogen decrease and d-dimer increase indicated refractoriness to IVIG, with pulmonary embolism also identified; ultimately, additional IVIG was followed by complete recovery. Further laboratory evaluation confirmed a diagnosis of severe aHIT. A novel finding was the transient appearance of leucoerythroblastosis, compatible with overt disseminated intravascular complicating severe aHIT.

Association between allergic diseases and autism spectrum disorder: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition increasingly linked to immune dysregulation and chronic low-grade inflammation. Allergic diseases, including asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis and food allergy, are generally associated with immune dysregulation and type 2 inflammatory responses predominantly involving T helper 2-related pathways. Epidemiological evidence also suggests a possible association between ASD and allergic diseases. However, existing studies differ in population characteristics, allergic phenotypes, diagnostic definitions, case ascertainment methods and strategies for confounding control. As a result, the available evidence remains fragmented and the findings are not fully consistent. Therefore, an updated and comprehensive synthesis is needed to integrate observational evidence and examine the associations between multiple allergic diseases and ASD.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol adheres to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 guidelines. We will systematically search PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL and APA PsycINFO, supplemented by searches of grey literature sources. We will search for studies published from 1 January 2011 to the date of the final search. Only English-language publications will be eligible for inclusion. Observational studies (cohort, case-control and cross-sectional) evaluating associations between ASD and allergic diseases will be included. Study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment and certainty-of-evidence assessment will be performed independently by two reviewers. Disagreements will be resolved by discussion, with persisting discrepancies adjudicated by a third senior reviewer. For effect estimates, the most fully adjusted estimates will be prioritised. ORs, risk ratios, HRs and prevalence ratios will be log-transformed. Analyses will be conducted in Review Manager (RevMan, V.5.4). A fixed-effect model or a random-effects model will be selected according to the degree of heterogeneity. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses and publication bias assessment will also be performed. When meta-analysis is not appropriate, the findings will be summarised using a narrative synthesis approach.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: No ethical approval is required as this study is based on published literature only. This protocol has been registered with Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251119984). Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conference presentations.

articles.title: Effectiveness of intravenous paracetamol plus ibuprofen versus intravenous paracetamol plus metamizole for pain in children with acute pancreatitis at tertiary referral centres in Poland: a multicentre randomised controlled trial protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an acute inflammatory process characterised by premature activation of pancreatic proenzymes leading to pancreatic parenchymal injury and, in some cases, distant organ involvement. The incidence of AP in children has risen significantly over recent decades, reaching approximately 13 cases per 100 000 children per year in Europe, with idiopathic aetiologies being the most common. Effective pain management is central to AP treatment, yet high-quality evidence on analgesic strategies in the paediatric population is lacking. The aim of the study is to assess the effectiveness and tolerance of pain treatment in paediatric AP using intravenous paracetamol in combination with ibuprofen or paracetamol in combination with metamizole.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: In this prospective, multicentre, randomised interventional study, children aged 3–18 years with AP defined by the INternational Study Group of Pediatric Pancreatitis: In search for a cuRE (INSPPIRE) criteria and moderate to severe abdominal pain will be allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous paracetamol combined with either ibuprofen or metamizole. Pain intensity will be measured at baseline using validated, age-appropriate scales (Numerical Rating Scale or Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability). The primary outcome is the proportion of participants achieving a pain score below 4 points 60 min after treatment initiation. Secondary outcomes include length of hospital stay, opioid use within 48 hours expressed as morphine milligram equivalents per kilogram, and changes in pain intensity at 6, 24 and 48 hours. Analyses will be conducted on a per-protocol basis using appropriate parametric or non-parametric methods.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of the Medical University of Warsaw, Poland (protocol version: 5 August 2025, KB/45/A/2025). Study findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences.

Efficacy and safety of double plasma cytokine adsorption system with sequential low-volume plasma exchange in treating acute-on-chronic liver failure complicated by sepsis: protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) and sepsis are both life-threatening clinical syndromes that frequently coexist. Patients with ACLF complicated by sepsis experience significantly higher mortality rates, yet therapeutic options remain limited. This randomised controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the double plasma cytokine adsorption system with sequential low-volume plasma exchange (DPCAS+LPE) in patients with ACLF complicated by sepsis.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a multicentre, prospective, open-label, parallel-group, randomised clinical trial. A total of 192 patients with ACLF complicated by sepsis will be recruited from five hospitals in China. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to either the intervention group or the control group. Both groups will receive standard medical treatment and three sessions of artificial liver support system (ALSS) therapy administered every other day. The intervention group will receive two sessions of DPCAS+LPE followed by one session of plasma exchange (PE), while the control group will receive three sessions of PE. The primary outcome is the 4-week mortality rate. Secondary outcomes include the 12-week mortality rate; longitudinal changes in Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease and Chinese Group on the Study of Severe Hepatitis B-associated ACLF II scores; and the Vasoactive-Inotropic Score at weeks 1, 2, 3 and 4 post baseline. Furthermore, the clearance rates of various cytokines and lactate will be measured after the first ALSS session. Safety will be assessed by documenting and managing all adverse events throughout the study.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the medical ethics committee of the Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (approval no: II2024-204-06). The trial will be conducted in strict accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and the Good Clinical Practice guidelines. The results of this study will be disseminated through presentations at national and international hepatology or critical care conferences and through publication in peer-reviewed journals. The findings will also be shared with relevant clinical stakeholders to inform future treatment guidelines for ACLF and sepsis.

TAICHIKNEE trial: protocol for an embedded pragmatic, individually randomised group-treatment trial of remotely delivered Tai Chi for knee osteoarthritis across US healthcare systems.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Symptomatic knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of chronic pain and disability and is associated with substantial healthcare utilisation and costs. In-person Tai Chi, a multidimensional mind-body exercise, is recommended as a non-pharmacological therapy for knee OA; however, delivery through in-person classes may limit scalability across US healthcare systems. Remote delivery may reduce logistical barriers and facilitate integration into routine care, but evidence regarding its effectiveness and implementation in real-world healthcare settings remains limited. We describe the protocol for TAICHIKNEE, an embedded pragmatic trial evaluating remotely delivered group Tai Chi plus routine care vs routine care alone for adults with symptomatic knee OA.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: TAICHIKNEE is a 12-month, fully decentralised, embedded pragmatic, individually randomised group-treatment trial with an effectiveness-implementation hybrid type 1 design conducted across five US healthcare systems. The trial will randomise 480 adults aged ≥50 years with symptomatic, clinician-diagnosed knee OA in a 1:1 ratio within six sequential cohorts, stratified by healthcare system and sex. Participants assigned to Tai Chi will receive 24 live, instructor-led 60-minute videoconference sessions over 12 weeks in addition to routine care; control participants will continue routine care. The cohort randomisation date defines time zero for both groups. The primary outcome is Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain at 3 months, analysed using a partially nested mixed-effects model that accounts for clustering within Tai Chi classes and adjusts for baseline WOMAC pain and prespecified covariates. Key secondary outcomes are Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Pain Interference and SF-12 health-related quality of life scores at 3 months, and knee joint injections over 12 months. Safety will be assessed throughout the 12-month follow-up. The implementation evaluation will concurrently assess intervention fidelity, stakeholder perspectives and participant and instructor experiences using Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research-informed stakeholder interviews, fidelity assessments and surveys to identify factors influencing implementation and inform future sustainment and spread across healthcare systems.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval was obtained from the Tufts University Health Sciences Institutional Review Board (IRB) (STUDY00003780), serving as the single IRB of record for all participating sites. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conferences and stakeholder engagement activities across healthcare systems. De-identified participant-level data and study materials will be shared in accordance with applicable data-sharing policies, participant consent, IRB requirements and the approved data-sharing plan.

Respiratory Infections in Patients Eligible for Pediatric Palliative Care: An Ongoing Challenge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in pediatric care have increased the survival of children with life-limiting conditions, leading to a growing population requiring pediatric palliative care (PPC). Respiratory tract infections are among the leading causes of hospitalization in these patients. This study aimed to describe the features of respiratory infections in children eligible for PPC.

METHODS: The present study is a monocentric retrospective study including pediatric patients eligible for PPC with an Assessment of Complex Clinical-Care Needs in Pediatrics (ACCAPED) score ≥30 who were followed by a third-level hospital in Bologna, Italy. Hospitalizations for respiratory infections occurring between January 2019 and February 2025 were analyzed. Clinical, microbiologic, laboratory and therapeutic data were collected.

RESULTS: Among 319 eligible PPC patients, 99 experienced at least 1 infectious hospitalization, accounting for 117 admissions due to respiratory infections in 56 children. Lower respiratory tract infections predominated (86.3%), with viral pathogens identified in most cases. Respiratory support required escalation in 76.9% of admissions, while 6% required pediatric intensive care, and mortality was 1.7%. Pseudomonas aeruginosa was the most frequently isolated bacterial pathogen, especially among tracheostomized patients. Multivariate analysis identified an Assessment of Complex Clinical-Care Needs in Pediatrics score ≥75 [odds ratio (OR): 2.43; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.04-5.68; P = 0.041] and C-reactive protein ≥8 mg/dL (OR: 3.85; 95% CI: 1.48-10.00; P = 0.0058) as independent predictors of respiratory support escalation.

CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory infections represent a major cause of hospitalization in children receiving PPC. High clinical complexity and elevated inflammatory markers independently predict worsening respiratory status, supporting their use for early risk stratification and individualized management.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents.

DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, observational study.

SETTING: Thirteen ICUs in Poland.

PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%).

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

articles.title: Invasive Meningococcal Disease in Hospitalized Children in Argentina, 2020-2024: Clinical, Epidemiologic and Molecular Findings From a Multicenter Active Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) is a low-incidence but high-impact infection associated with substantial mortality and sequelae. Following MenACWY vaccine introduction into Argentina's National Immunization Program in 2017, updated data on residual disease burden are needed.

METHODS: A multicenter active hospital-based surveillance study was conducted in 6 pediatric sentinel units in Argentina (January 2020-December 2024) in children younger than 15 years with suspected IMD. Cases were confirmed by culture and/or polymerase chain reaction from a normally sterile body site. Hospital discharge rates were calculated per 10,000 discharges. Whole-genome sequencing and genetic Meningococcal Antigen Typing System were used to characterize strains and estimate theoretical 4CMenB coverage.

RESULTS: Among 234,264 pediatric hospital discharges, 27 confirmed IMD cases were identified (overall rate: 1.2 per 10,000; 95% confidence interval, 0.8-1.7). Annual rates showed no consistent pattern between children younger than 2 years and those 2 years or older. The case-fatality rate was 14.8% (4/27); all deaths occurred in previously healthy children younger than 5 years and were associated with sepsis and a fulminant course (hospital stay ≤1 day). Of 20 cases with a determined capsular group, 19 (95%) were B and 1 (5%) was C; no capsular group Y or W cases were identified. Theoretical 4CMenB coverage by genetic Meningococcal Antigen Typing System was 77.3%, driven by ST-162 clonal complex predominance.

CONCLUSIONS: IMD in Argentina continues to predominantly affect young children and is associated with elevated case-fatality amid fulminant sepsis. Serogroup B predominates in the post-MenACWY era, and high estimated 4CMenB coverage supports evaluation of serogroup B vaccination as a complementary prevention strategy.

articles.title: Long-term Sequelae in Children With Invasive Meningococcal Disease, Chile 2009-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Around 30% of survivors of invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) may develop long-term sequelae; data from Latin America remain scarce. This study aimed to estimate the proportion of long-term sequelae in pediatric IMD survivors and associated factors.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional outcome evaluation included children diagnosed with IMD (2009-2019) in 2 hospitals in Santiago, Chile. Between October 2022 and April 2023, 40 IMD survivors and 42 age- and sex-matched children without IMD or central nervous system infection underwent standardized physical, neurocognitive, audiologic and functional assessments conducted independently. Prevalence ratio (PR) and adjusted PR (aPR) were estimated with modified Poisson regression with standard errors.

RESULTS: Median ages were 10 (interquartile range [IQR] 9-13) and 11 (IQR 9-14) years in the exposed and unexposed groups; 70% and 64.3% were male. Sequelae occurred in 70% of exposed; the corresponding clinical findings were present in 16.7% of unexposed children (PR, 4.20; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.07-8.51).
