Neurologic (55%), dermatologic (25.0%) and hearing (20.5%) sequelae predominated. This association remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, caregiver education and socioeconomic status (aPR, 3.75; 95% CI: 1.83-7.69). Children with sequelae had a lower quality of life than those without sequelae (62% and 8%, P = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Pediatric survivors of IMD in Chile face a high burden of long-term sequelae. Sustained multidisciplinary follow-up and preventive strategies, including vaccination, are essential to reduce disability and improve quality of life.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry.
authors: National Emergency Airway Registry for Children (NEAR4KIDS) investigators as a subgroup of Pediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators (PALISI)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs).

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs.

PATIENTS: Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs.

INTERVENTIONS: Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%).

CONCLUSIONS: TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.

articles.title: The Patient Safety Room of Horrors: An Innovative Simulation for Engaging Patient Support Team Members in Orientation.
articles.journal: Journal for nurses in professional development
articles.abstract: The Patient Safety Room of Horrors is an innovative simulation-based learning activity developed to enhance orientation for Patient Support Team members. Learners worked in teams to identify 22 embedded safety hazards across categories such as patient identification, infection prevention, pressure injury, and fall prevention. Feedback from over 1,200 participants demonstrated increased engagement, teamwork, knowledge, and confidence. This approach offers nursing professional development practitioners a scalable, interactive method to reinforce patient safety principles during orientation.

articles.title: Metabolic Syndrome Is Associated With Worsened Clinical Outcomes in Individuals With Necrotizing Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract:
GOALS: Evaluate the relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and clinical outcomes in individuals with necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) and infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN).

BACKGROUND: MetS affects a significant proportion of the global population and is associated with low-grade systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation. This has implications for several disease processes, but the impact of MetS on patients with NP is not well characterized.

STUDY: A retrospective cohort study of patients admitted with NP at a single tertiary center was performed. MetS was defined as meeting any 3 of the following criteria: BMI ≥30 kg/m2, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, blood pressure ≥130/85 mm Hg, and low HDL (<40 mg/dL men, <50 mg/dL women). The need for intensive care, hospital length of stay, development of organ failure, and mortality were compared in patients with NP with or without MetS. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of IPN.

RESULTS: A total of 276 (154 MetS, 55.8%) patients were identified. Individuals with MetS more frequently required ICU-level care (38.3% vs. 17.2%; P<0.001) and longer length of stay (9.0 vs. 5.0 d; P=0.029). There was a higher risk of sepsis in those with MetS (27.5% vs. 15.6%; P=0.019), as well as respiratory failure (31.2% vs. 18%; P=0.013), renal failure (35.7% vs. 21.3%; P=0.009), and in-hospital mortality (17.5% vs. 8.2%; P=0.024). The incidence of IPN was higher in patients with MetS (39.6% vs. 23.0%; P=0.003).

CONCLUSION: The presence of MetS in individuals with NP was associated with worsened outcomes, including increased incidence of IPN, sepsis, organ failure, ICU admission, and mortality during index hospitalization.

articles.title: Intermittent Fasting in Metabolic Syndrome: Clinical Evidence, Molecular Mechanisms, and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: The objective for this narrative review was to synthesize and critically assess the clinical evidence, molecular mechanisms, and future directions of intermittent fasting (IF) for managing metabolic syndrome (MetS). Metabolic syndrome is a complex cardiometabolic disorder associated with abnormal dietary patterns, epigenetic regulation, and gene activity, and characterized by central adiposity, insulin resistance, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Intermittent fasting regimens, including time-restricted eating, alternate-day fasting, and the 5:2 fasting regimen, are promising nutritional interventions. Nonetheless, large, randomized trials have reported mixed clinical outcomes, and critical uncertainties persist regarding clinical effectiveness, molecular mechanisms, and whether benefits arise from fasting timing or weight-loss-driven energy restriction. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in major databases through July 2026. Articles, including those reporting on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant preclinical mechanistic investigations in MetS, were selected and their data synthesized. Findings show that certain IF regimens produce modest improvements in body weight, waist circumference, and selected cardiometabolic risk markers; however, effects on glycemic control, lipid profiles, and liver-related end points are heterogeneous across trials. Observed clinical responses vary by fasting protocol, participant phenotype, and adherence, and high-quality human mechanistic data remain limited. Mechanistic insights, largely derived from preclinical models, highlight circadian rhythm synchronization and nutrient-sensing network modulation as key biological pathways. Important unresolved controversies cover protocol optimization, long-term adherence, and inter-individual metabolic variability. Intermittent fasting may serve as a feasible nonpharmacological adjunct intervention for MetS and related conditions, yet existing evidence is inconsistent. Translation toward precision lifestyle medicine requires resolution of ongoing controversies, improved evaluation of evidence quality, development of personalized fasting protocols, and rigorous assessment of long-term safety and sustainability across diverse patient populations.

articles.title: Experiences of self-advocacy in patients with chronic kidney disease: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To reveal the essence of self-advocacy experiences among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), aiming to describe the fundamental structure of these experiences.

METHODS: A descriptive phenomenological qualitative approach with purposive sampling was adopted. From December 2023 to January 2024, 10 patients with CKD from the Department of Nephrology at a tertiary Grade A hospital in Dalian were recruited for semi-structured interviews. The interview guide was based on a conceptual framework of self-advocacy and the data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method.

RESULTS: Five main themes and 16 subthemes were identified: (1) Difficulty in Accessing Health Information and Divided Health Awareness (e.g., poor health information access, polarization in health awareness, and personality traits); (2) Initial Disorientation and Resistance to the Disease (e.g., disease rejection, disease uncertainty, negative emotional experiences, multidimensional conflicts between illness and life, and self-perceived burden); (3) Seeking Strength through Social Support and Peer Communication (e.g., seeking external support and communication with fellow patients); (4) Growth through Struggle and Self-Rebuilding from Passivity to Initiative (e.g., active resistance to the disease, avoiding negative impacts, building positive mentality, and accumulating disease experience); and (5) Self-Prioritization and Expression of Will (e.g., protection of self-rights and self-prioritization).

CONCLUSION: Self-advocacy among patients with CKD develops through complex, long-term interactions between health-related and social factors. Over time, patients may shift from passive recipients of care to active managers of their health, reflecting greater prioritization of their own needs.

articles.title: Effect of data-driven gating on the quantification of prostate cancer metastases in 68Ga-PSMA- and ¹⁸F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PSMA PET/CT using 18F‑DCFPyL and 68Ga‑labelled tracers is central to prostate cancer staging, but 68Ga‑PSMA may show reduced sensitivity and quantitative accuracy, partly due to respiratory motion and lower spatial resolution. Device-based motion‑correction methods have limitations. Data‑driven gating (DDG) offers a hardware‑free alternative, though its impact on PSMA PET, especially 68Ga‑PSMA has not been systematically evaluated. To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of the DDG motion-correction method in 68Ga-PSMA and 18F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT, focusing on metastatic lymph node, lung, and bone lesions, and to assess its robustness across tracers.

METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with biopsy‑proven prostate cancer who underwent 68Ga‑PSMA or 18F‑DCFPyL PSMA PET/CT for primary staging or biochemical recurrence and had metastatic disease. Motion correction was applied using the OncoFreeze AI™ data‑driven gating (OFAI‑DDG) method. Metastatic lesions were segmented semi‑automatically, and SUV metrics, image noise, and contrast‑to‑noise ratio were quantified by anatomical site in both OFAI-DDG and static images. Qualitative image quality was independently scored by two experienced readers. Statistical analyses included non‑parametric tests, Bland-Altman agreement, regression analyses, tracer comparison, and inter‑reader reliability assessment.

RESULTS: After exclusions, 23 68Ga‑PSMA and 40 18F‑PSMA patients were analyzed, yielding 133 and 192 metastatic lesions, respectively. OFAI‑DDG reconstruction significantly increased SUVmean and SUVmax compared with static imaging for both tracers across bone, lymph node, and lung lesions (p < 0.0001), with the largest gains in lung lesions. CNR improved for most lesion types, and image noise was significantly reduced. Qualitative analysis showed better image quality, sharpness, and noise with OFAI‑DDG, with high inter‑reader agreement. OFAI‑DDG performance was robust across tracers and largely independent of lesion location.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that OFAI‑DDG significantly improves PSMA PET/CT image quality and quantitative accuracy compared with standard static imaging. The improvements were observed for both 68Ga‑PSMA and 18F‑PSMA tracers, indicating tracer‑independent robustness. The OFAI‑DDG simplified the workflow and reduced time used for patient set-up, while enhancing lesion visualization and quantitative reliability without altering lesion detection, supporting its clinical value for metastatic prostate cancer imaging.

articles.title: Longitudinal Changes and Responsiveness of the Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome Scale in Patients with Acute Cerebellar Stroke.
articles.abstract: Cognitive and affective disturbances due to cerebellar lesions are termed cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome (CCAS). Although CCAS is frequent after acute cerebellar stroke, CCAS-Scale responsiveness during acute hospitalization remains unclear. Objective: To examine longitudinal changes and responsiveness of the CCAS-Scale and compare its changes with global cognitive function, ataxia, and activities of daily living (ADL). In this single-center prospective observational study, 21 patients with first-ever cerebellar stroke were assessed 7 days after onset and at discharge (median, 21 days) using the CCAS-Scale, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), and Functional Independence Measure (FIM). Changes were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, standardized response mean (SRM), and Spearman's rank correlation. Median CCAS-Scale score increased from 71 to 72 (p = 0.018), and failed items decreased from 4 to 3 (p = 0.035). Definite CCAS decreased from 81.0% to 66.7%, and all patients had at least possible CCAS at discharge. The SRM was 0.52 (95% CI, 0.20-0.88), indicating moderate responsiveness, whereas SARA and FIM showed large and MMSE small responsiveness. CCAS-Scale change correlated with FIM change (rho = 0.44; p = 0.046) but not with SARA or MMSE. The CCAS-Scale showed a statistically significant change and moderate responsiveness. However, the median score increased by only 1 point (71 to 72), and the 95% CI for the SRM was relatively wide, suggesting that the clinical significance of this change should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Fractional CO₂ laser combined with intradermal and topical platelet-rich plasma for hypertrophic scars: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study compared the clinical efficacy and safety of fractional CO₂ laser combined with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) delivered by intradermal injection plus topical application versus fractional CO₂ laser alone for the treatment of hypertrophic scars.

METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded trial, 120 patients were assigned to a combined group (laser + PRP, n = 60) or a control group (laser + saline, n = 60). Four sessions were delivered at 4-6-week intervals. The primary outcome was Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) total score. The prespecified primary endpoint was the between-group difference in VSS total score at T4 (6 months after the final treatment session). Secondary outcomes included POSAS scores, ultrasound-measured scar thickness, patient satisfaction, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant VSS improvement (both P < 0.001). The combined group had significantly lower VSS total scores than the control group from T1 onward (P = 0.036 at T1; P < 0.001 at T2 and T4; P = 0.007 at T3; estimated between-group difference at T4 -1.85 points, 95% CI -2.48 to -1.22, from the primary mixed-effects model) and lower POSAS scores from T1 onward (P = 0.022 at T1; P < 0.001 at T2, T3, and T4) than the control group. Ultrasound-measured scar thickness was lower in the combined group at 3 months (P = 0.045); at 6 months the difference was attenuated and of borderline statistical significance (P = 0.042-0.065 across missing-data approaches). Patient satisfaction was higher in the combined group (P < 0.001). Procedural pain was greater in the combined group (mean between-group difference 1.34 points on a 0-10 VAS; P < 0.001). Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation was numerically lower in the combined group (18.33% vs. 33.33%; P = 0.094).

CONCLUSION: Fractional CO₂ laser combined with intradermal and topical PRP provided greater improvement in clinical scar scores than laser alone, with an acceptable safety profile. The advantage in ultrasound-measured thickness at 6 months was of borderline statistical significance. These findings support PRP as a potential adjunct for hypertrophic scars.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical considerations of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in prosthetic joint infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) has emerged as a promising complementary method for pathogen detection in prosthetic joint infection (PJI). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of mNGS and conventional microbiological culture.

METHODS: A systematic review and bivariate diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-DTA guidelines. PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, WoS and the CNKI database were searched. Eligible studies evaluated shotgun mNGS in suspected or confirmed PJI, used a recognized reference standard for diagnosis, and reported sufficient data to construct 2 × 2 contingency tables for mNGS and conventional culture. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a bivariate random-effects Reitsma model.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies comprising 1,579 cases were included, of which 982 were classified as PJI and 597 as non-PJI. When pooled separately, mNGS had a sensitivity of 84.3% (95% CI 77.3-89.4%) and specificity of 91.5% (95% CI 88.4-93.9%), compared with 66.0% (95% CI 60.1-71.4%) and 95.6% (95% CI 92.8-97.4%), respectively, for conventional culture. The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve was 0.941 for mNGS and 0.930 for culture. Sensitivity analyses did not change the overall findings.

CONCLUSION: When analysed separately, mNGS demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity than conventional culture. Overall diagnostic performance assessed by SROC was comparable between the two methods. These findings suggest that mNGS may provide complementary microbiological information. Nevertheless, microorganisms detected exclusively by mNGS should be interpreted cautiously and in conjunction with other clinical and laboratory findings.

articles.title: Transient focal neurological episodes in cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related convexity subarachnoid hemorrhage.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Convexity subarachnoid hemorrhage (cSAH) is recognized as a cause of transient focal neurological episodes. These episodes can closely mimic transient ischemic attacks (TIAs). We report a case of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA)-related cSAH presenting with recurrent transient monoparesis.

CASE DESCRIPTION: An elderly patient with a history of hypertension was admitted to our hospital because of recurrent episodes of transient left upper limb monoparesis. Initial diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI) demonstrated a focal hyperintensity over the right frontal convexity. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) revealed a focal hypointense signal at the corresponding area, consistent with cSAH. Video recordings of the left upper monoparesis were available, but the episodes were clinically indistinguishable from TIAs. Antiseizure treatment with levetiracetam was initiated, but the episodes persisted. After the addition of clobazam, no further episodes were observed.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that CAA-related cSAH may present with recurrent transient monoparesis that closely mimics TIA. Careful evaluation of susceptibility weighted imaging is important for recognizing the underlying hemorrhagic lesion in patients with recurrent stereotyped TFNEs.

articles.title: Comprehensive insight into the anti-dyslipidemic and pancreatic lipase inhibition activities of Clematis flammula L. and Fraxinus angustifolia Vahl. extracts using two animal models.
articles.abstract: Clematis flammula and Fraxinus angustifolia leaves are commonly used in Algeria to treat inflammatory diseases, with potential hypolipidemic effects that have not been investigated so far. The present study explored the in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo hypolipidemic effects of ethanolic leaf extracts from both plants using two animal models (mice and rabbits) with distinct lipid metabolism. Dyslipidemia was induced by oral administration of Triton X-100, once daily for three consecutive days. Immediately after each Triton X-100 administration, animals received plant extracts (100 and 200 mg/kg bw) or atorvastatin (10 mg/kg bw). Anti-lipase and anti-HMG-CoA reductase activities were evaluated using in vitro and ex vivo assays. Triton X-100 induced marked alterations in serum lipid profiles, characterized by increased LDL-C, VLDL-C, and total cholesterol levels, which were improved by C. flammula and F. angustifolia extracts, particularly at 200 mg/kg bw. While F. angustifolia exhibited greater hypolipidemic efficacy, the lack of improvement in total cholesterol in mice treated with C. flammula, in contrast to rabbits, may suggest species-dependent differences in lipid metabolism, potentially involving CETP-mediated cholesterol transport, which requires further experimental confirmation. In vitro anti-lipase assays showed greater inhibitory potency for F. angustifolia (IC50 = 3.55 µg/mL) than C. flammula (IC50 = 12.10 µg/mL). Both extracts inhibited HMG-CoA reductase activity by over 60% in vitro and ex vivo, with IC50 values of 90.06 and 96.57 µg/mL for F. angustifolia and C. flammula, respectively. Histological examination further supported the hypolipidemic effects of both extracts. Overall, these findings highlight C. flammula and F. angustifolia as promising natural sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in managing hypercholesterolemia and dyslipidemia.

articles.title: GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease: outcomes, mechanisms, and emerging clinical applications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have shown cardiovascular benefits beyond their established role in treating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This review evaluates recent clinical evidence, potential mechanisms, and the expanding use of GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease.

METHODS: We reviewed major randomized clinical trials assessing cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure outcomes, along with related mechanistic studies and clinical guidelines published through July 2026.

RESULTS: Early trials, including LEADER, SUSTAIN-6, and REWIND, reported 12%-26% reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with T2DM. More recent trials have extended these findings to other populations. SELECT showed a 20% reduction in MACE among individuals with obesity and established cardiovascular disease but without diabetes, while FLOW demonstrated a 24% reduction in its primary kidney composite outcome. SOUL reported a 14% reduction in MACE with oral semaglutide, and SUMMIT showed a 38% reduction in cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure with tirzepatide. SURPASS-CVOT found tirzepatide to be noninferior, but not superior, to dulaglutide for MACE. These benefits likely involve several mechanisms beyond glucose lowering and weight loss, although gastrointestinal adverse effects still remain a concern.

CONCLUSIONS: Growing clinical evidence supports the use of GLP-1-based therapies beyond diabetes management, particularly in patients with cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or obesity-related heart failure. Further studies will be needed to understand their mechanisms better, long-term safety, and optimal use in clinical practice.

articles.title: Implications of the 2017 change in the French death certificate for the accuracy of mortality statistics worldwide.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating between types of deaths is crucial because it allows us to better understand and prevent them, and it is essential to bringing justice to homicide victims. While there is extensive knowledge about the ways in which identifying manner of death can go wrong, the advocated solutions of more training and resources have not been put to the test. A peculiarity of the French death investigation system, along with a change in the French death certificate in 2017 allow us to test the efficacy of more specific instructions as a type of training as a solution to inaccurate information on types of deaths.

METHODS: Using nationwide French death certificates information available through the Epidemiological Center on Causes of Death (CépiDC) from 2016 until 2019, we conducted a before-and-after natural experiment to establish whether the 2017 change impacted the quality of mortality statistics in France. We ran logistic regression models on the likelihood that a medicolegal investigation was conducted, as well as on the quality of ICD codes for causes of death.

FINDINGS: The 2017 change in the French death certificate led to a two-fold increase in medicolegal investigations as well as an almost 10% increase in the quality of ICD codes of causes of death nationwide.

INTERPRETATION: The more specific instructions provided through the changes to the French death certificate led to improved mortality statistics, thereby providing support for the hypothesis that more training increases the quality of mortality statistics. Future research should establish dose-response, as well as focusing on policy implications beyond the French context.

articles.title: Sensory neuron-derived CGRP ameliorates kidney injury and fibrosis via monocytes and macrophages.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and its progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain major unmet clinical challenges for which effective therapies are lacking. Although sensory neurons are recognized as key regulators of tissue injury and repair via neuroimmune crosstalk, their organization and function within the kidney are poorly understood. Here, we delineate a renal neuroimmune axis in which nociceptive neurons protect against ischemia-reperfusion (I/R)-induced kidney injury. Using whole-organ tissue clearing and three-dimensional imaging, we mapped an extensive network of nociceptive sensory fibers throughout the renal parenchyma. Ablation of TRPV1+ nociceptors aggravated renal dysfunction, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis after I/R, whereas chemogenetic activation conferred protection. Mechanistically, the sensory neuropeptide calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which is upregulated after injury, acts via the CALCRL-RAMP1 receptor complex on monocytes/macrophages, engaging the cAMP-PKA pathway to suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression, thereby limiting myeloid infiltration and tubular injury. Importantly, we also found reduced renal CGRP abundance in kidneys from individuals with diabetes and older adults, who are at high risk for AKI and CKD, as well as in corresponding mouse models. In these vulnerable settings, exogenous CGRP more effectively reduced I/R-induced kidney injury. Our findings establish a dorsal root ganglia-kidney neuroimmune circuit that restrains I/R-induced renal inflammation and identify CGRP signaling as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate AKI and its progression to CKD, particularly in high-risk diabetic and elderly populations.

articles.title: Arrhythmic events and genetic variants as drivers for Takotsubo Syndrome: a patient-specific atrial stem-cell model.
articles.abstract: Takotsubo Syndrome (TTS) is an acute, potentially life-threatening condition often complicated by ventricular dysfunction and arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is common in TTS patients and associated with increased mortality. However, the arrhythmic mechanisms, genetic variability underlying TTS, and personalised therapy remain unclear. We generated induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from TTS patients and provoked TTS-like events by isoprenaline (Iso) stimulation. Compared with controls, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs exhibited enhanced diastolic sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca²⁺ leak and increased arrhythmogenic potential following Iso exposure. Iso-induced stress further increased systolic Ca²⁺ transient amplitude and reduced phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) activity in TTS iPSC-CMs. Under baseline conditions, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs demonstrated unchanged Ca2+ transient amplitude, reduced diastolic Ca2+, elevated SERCA2 activity with faster Ca²⁺ decay compared to controls, which could be explained by increased phosphorylation of PKA-specific phospholamban S16. In contrast, ventricular TTS-iPSC-CM showed increased L-Type Ca2+ current density, but reduced Ca2+ transient amplitude with increased resting Ca2+ leak and reduced PDE4 activity post-Iso-exposure. In atrial TTS iPSC-CMs, the PDE4 activator MR-L2 restored PDE4 activity, normalised several defects in Ca²⁺ handling and prevented arrhythmias more efficiently than the β-blocker metoprolol. Genetic analyses identified variants in the Ca²⁺ handling genes AHNAK and CASQ2 in TTS. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we generated isogenic rescue and mutation-insertion lines, confirming a causal role of p.P5390T in catecholamine-induced arrhythmogenic phenotypes in atrial TTS iPSC-CMs. Our findings support a mechanistic link between genetic predisposition to an excessive catecholaminergic stress response, dysregulated PDE/cAMP signalling, and atrial arrhythmogenesis in TTS-CMs, identifying PDE4 as a potential therapeutic target in this critical condition.

articles.title: Altered GABAB receptor sensitivity in heavy drinkers indexed using a TMS-based biomarker: a randomized controlled experimental medicine trial.
articles.abstract: Metabotropic γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptors (GABABRs) are implicated in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and represent a promising therapeutic target. However, robust biomarkers of GABABRs target engagement and sensitivity in humans are lacking. We examined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-derived cortical inhibition and growth hormone (GH) release as measures of GABABR function, and whether heavy alcohol use is associated with altered responses to pharmacological GABABR activation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 31 healthy volunteers (16 heavy drinkers, 15 light drinkers) received baclofen 30 mg, baclofen 60 mg, or placebo across three sessions. Long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), short-interval intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation were assessed with paired-pulse TMS at baseline and ~60 min post-dose. Baclofen blood concentrations and plasma GH levels were measured. Baclofen produced dose-dependent increases in GH release, confirming neuroendocrine GABABR engagement. The LICI response to baclofen differed between groups: In light drinkers, baclofen at 30 mg potentiated LICI, and a similar potentiation was seen at 60 mg, indicating that a plateau may have been reached. In contrast, in heavy drinkers, a potentiation of LICI similar to that in light drinkers was seen at 30 mg baclofen, but was absent at the 60 mg dose despite comparable pharmacokinetics, suggesting altered GABABR function. Effects were selective for GABABR-mediated inhibition, with no consistent modulation of short-interval intracortical inhibition or corticospinal excitability. Acute baclofen administration reveals altered GABABR sensitivity in heavy drinkers, with preserved responses at lower doses but reduced response under stronger agonist stimulation. LICI and GH release provide complementary biomarkers of central and peripheral GABABRs engagement and may support translational development of mechanism-based treatments for AUD.

articles.title: Comparison of Data-Driven Phenotyping Systems for metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Implications for Treatment Response.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although emerging classification systems address the pathophysiological heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the implications of these subtypes for treatment responses remain unclear. We systematically evaluated three phenotyping frameworks for stratifying responses to lifestyle management.

METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 618 patients with MASLD who received 48 weeks of guideline-based lifestyle management. The classification systems assessed were metabolic clusters-mild obesity/dyslipidemia-associated MASLD (MODM), age-related MASLD (AM), severe insulin resistance-associated MASLD, high lipoprotein(a)-associated MASLD (HLPAM), and severe mixed hyperlipidemia-associated MASLD (SMHLM); hepatic and cardiometabolic traits (control, liver-specific, and cardiometabolic); and biochemical patterns (hepatocellular, mixed, and cholestatic). The primary endpoints were responses in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) (≥30% relative liver fat reduction), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (≥17 IU/L decrease), and liver stiffness measurements (LSM) (≥1-stage improvement in the LSM-defined fibrosis stage).

RESULTS: Metabolic clusters demonstrated significantly greater temporal stability than the hepatic and cardiometabolic trait and biochemical pattern systems (62.8% vs. 56.6% vs. 53.4%, P=0.003). The HLPAM cluster demonstrated an attenuated MRI-PDFF response (odds ratio [OR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.79), while the AM cluster showed a lower ALT response (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18 to 0.62), and the MODM cluster displayed a superior LSM response compared to the others (all P<0.05). Moreover, the liver-specific cluster showed better MRI-PDFF, ALT, and LSM responses than the control cluster. However, biochemical patterns selectively stratified ALT responses, with the hepatocellular pattern demonstrating a greater response than the mixed and cholestatic patterns.

CONCLUSION: Metabolic cluster-based MASLD subtypes exhibited differential responses to lifestyle management, supporting the integration of metabolic subtyping into clinical algorithms to optimize management.

articles.title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young's modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15-18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

articles.title: Residual vulnerability after decompensated heart failure: what remains unmet after the 2026 ESC guidelines for the management of heart failure?
Practical consideration for the application of continuous glucose monitoring in older adults with insulin treated diabetes.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract: The increased prevalence of diabetes among older individuals presents challenges for delivery of effective care for each older person with diabetes, for their families, and for healthcare providers. Along with established risks for microvascular and macrovascular disease, diabetes in older adults is also associated with risk factors for cognitive impairment and dementia, depression and physical frailty. Many of these risk factors are linked to hypoglycaemia, which in turn can be related to polypharmacy and overprescribing in older individuals. Use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) technology is proven to prevent hypoglycaemia and can mitigate many averse outcomes of frailty, both in type 1 diabetes (T1D and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Similarly, use of CGM improves glucose stability, reducing risks for vascular complications of diabetes. Intrinsic capacity (IC) is a concept used in geriatric medicine to provide an objective composite of physical and mental capacities that an older individual can draw on. Reduced IC is associated with a number of CGM metrics, including time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), rather than hypoglycaemia. Use of CGM can also facilitate telemedicine for adults with diabetes and frailty, reducing the burden of clinic attendance and increasing the frequency of healthcare contacts, further increasing the quality of care and quality of life for older individuals with diabetes. Given the significant benefits, the application of CGM alongside geriatric principles can be proposed to improve overall care and outcomes for people with diabetes.

articles.title: Denosumab Biosimilars Versus Denosumab in Postmenopausal Osteoporosis: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Denosumab is one of the first-line drugs for postmenopausal osteoporosis with high risk of fracture, but the cost limits its use. Denosumab biosimilars are a more affordable solution, though it is underutilized due to hesitation among clinicians and patients due to concerns for differences in efficacy and safety.

METHODS: We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing efficacy and safety of denosumab biosimilars to denosumab. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane databases and Clinical Trials.gov were searched for studies comparing denosumab biosimilars to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis. We pooled mean differences (MD) for continuous outcomes and risk ratios (RR) for binary outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using REML-based I2 statistics and Cochran's Q test. Statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.6.0.

RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs comprising 5595 participants were included, of whom 2825 participants (50.5%) received biosimilars. There was no statistical difference between percent change from baseline at 6 and 12 months respectively for lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD), total hip, femoral neck BMD between the two groups. Similarly, change in C-telopeptide, procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide levels at 1, 6 and 12 months from baseline and vertebral fractures were similar between the two groups. There was no difference between the two groups in terms of safety outcomes including treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE), grade ≥ 3 TEAEs.

CONCLUSION: Denosumab biosimilars were comparable in efficacy and short-term safety compared to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

articles.title: First evidence of measles virus detected from exhaled breath in humans.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Measles is among the most transmissible human infections, yet direct capture of measles virus from an infected person's exhaled breath has not been described. We assessed whether measles virus RNA can be detected from exhaled breath using facemask sampling (FMS).

METHODS: We studied a 23-year-old unvaccinated woman with laboratory-confirmed measles (throat-swab RT-qPCR positive on day 5 post symptom onset). From day 10 post symptom onset, longitudinal sampling was performed for six consecutive days with duplicate specimens collected at each timepoint from the throat, face, cutaneous lesions and exhaled breath using a surgical mask fitted with polyvinyl alcohol sampling strips (FMS). Dissolved mask strips and swab eluates underwent RNA extraction followed by RT-qPCR targeting measles nucleoprotein and haemagglutinin genes, with human RNase P as a sample adequacy control. Quantification was derived from nucleoprotein-gene standards and normalised per strip or per 100 μL of swab eluate.

RESULTS: Measles virus RNA was consistently detected in exhaled breath captured by FMS and remained >10ˆ4 genome copies per sampling strip despite sampling beginning 10 days after symptom onset. During FMS collection, the participant reported no respiratory symptoms and did not vocalise. RNA kinetics differed by sampling site: throat and facial swabs increased even after complete rash resolution, whereas cutaneous-lesion swabs yielded comparatively low RNA levels. FMS kinetics diverged from throat swabs over time, suggesting distinct patterns of virus emission across compartments.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first empirical evidence that measles virus RNA can be captured directly from the exhaled breath of an individual with measles. Although RNA detection does not confirm infectious virus, persistent high-level exhaled RNA supports FMS as a practical, non-invasive tool to study measles respiratory emission and may inform understanding of transmission and the duration of potential contagiousness. Empirical sampling of different respiratory compartments may help refine infection-prevention guidance during resurgent outbreaks.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-defined visceral adiposity beyond Body Mass Index is associated with insulin resistance and early glycemic dysregulation in adults without diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: - To determine whether magnetic resonance imaging-quantified visceral adiposity beyond that expected from body mass index (BMI) is associated with adverse metabolic phenotypes in adults without diabetes and more strongly than abdominal subcutaneous fat.

METHODS: - This community-based cross-sectional study included 474 adults aged 40-65 years without diabetes. Visceral fat area (VFA) and subcutaneous fat area (SFA) were measured by magnetic resonance imaging. Sex-specific BMI-adjusted residual phenotypes were constructed, and associations with oral glucose tolerance test-derived metabolic outcomes were examined using multivariable regression.

RESULTS: - Each 1-SD increase in BMI-adjusted VFA was associated with a lower Matsuda index (β=-0.41), higher log HOMA-IR (β=0.10), higher 2-hour glucose (β=0.22 mmol/l), greater glucose area under the curve (β=16.34 mmol/l × min), and lower oral disposition index (β=-9.10). BMI-adjusted SFA was not significantly associated with these outcomes. BMI-adjusted VFA was also associated with WHO-defined prediabetes (OR=1.32) and isolated impaired glucose tolerance (OR=1.33), with stronger associations than BMI-adjusted SFA, but not with ADA-defined prediabetes (OR=0.89, 95% CI 0.70-1.12).

CONCLUSIONS: - Visceral adiposity beyond BMI identified an adverse fat-distribution phenotype characterized by reduced insulin sensitivity, impaired post-load glucose handling, and inadequate β-cell compensation. Regional fat distribution may refine obesity phenotyping beyond BMI.

articles.title: Metagenomic Insights into Microplastic Micro-interfaces: Transforming Pollutants and Spreading Resistance.
articles.abstract: Microplastic micro-interfaces (MPMI) in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) serve as critical hubs for microbial colonization, pollutant transformation, and antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. In this study, a large-scale genome-resolved metagenomic approach was employed to reconstruct 463 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from biofilms established on polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP) within a municipal WWTP. Taxonomic profiling revealed that MPMI selectively enriched strict anaerobes and uncultured taxa, driving a profound ecological shift from the surrounding water and indicating the formation of localized hypoxic micro-niches. Functionally, the MPMI microbiome constructed a highly integrated metabolic network. Key dominant lineages were found to synergistically couple aromatic hydrocarbon degradation (via the shikimate pathway and β-oxidation) with complex carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycling, while deploying energy-efficient nucleotide salvage strategies to ensure biofilm stabilization under nutrient stress. Crucially, horizontal gene transfer (HGT) emerged as a fundamental mechanism for functional diversification, facilitating the active cross-genomic exchange of key adaptive traits associated with pollutant metabolism and biofilm regulation. Furthermore, MPMI harbored a highly diverse resistome comprising 36 ARG categories and 289 subtypes, highlighted by the critical genomic co-localization of mobile elements and clinical resistance markers (e.g., mcr-5.1, mupA) in core colonizers. Ultimately, these genomic insights elucidate the MPMI as a profound ecological hotspot driving the concurrent adaptation of metabolic networks and the resistome, thereby exacerbating the risks of ARG dissemination in aquatic environments.

articles.title: Preconception and Early-Pregnancy Serum Metal(loid) Concentrations in Relation to Gestational Glucose Regulation: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Although metal(loid) exposure during pregnancy has been increasingly studied, evidence remains limited on whether serum metal(loid) concentrations measured before conception are related to glucose regulation during pregnancy. In this prospective cohort study, serum concentrations of multiple metal(loid)s were measured during the preconception period and early pregnancy. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) was diagnosed using a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 gestational weeks, and fasting, 1-h, and 2-h plasma glucose (PG) levels were assessed as continuous outcomes. Generalized linear regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, Bayesian kernel machine regression, and a multiple informant model were used to characterize individual, nonlinear, joint, and period-specific associations. During the preconception period, higher nickel (Ni) and lead (Pb) concentrations were associated with higher 2-h PG, whereas strontium (Sr) was inversely associated with fasting PG. During early pregnancy, cadmium (Cd) and titanium (Ti) were positively associated with 1-h PG, whereas Sr was inversely associated with 2-h PG. BKMR analyses were broadly consistent with several element-specific associations identified in the single-metal analyses. The multiple informant model also indicated that associations differed between the preconception and early-pregnancy measurement periods for some metal(loid)s. Overall, serum metal(loid) concentrations measured during the preconception and early-pregnancy periods showed period- and element-specific patterns of association with gestational glucose measures, supporting the need to consider preconception exposure in future studies.

articles.title: Clinical triage concordance of a point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay using the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) assays have demonstrated good analytical agreement with central laboratory (CL) testing, it remains uncertain whether they yield the same clinical triage decisions. We evaluated the clinical concordance of a POC hs-cTnI assay with a CL assay using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h algorithm.

METHODS: This prospective diagnostic agreement study included 127 patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute coronary syndrome. The primary outcome was concordance of patient classification according to the 0/1-h algorithm, assessed using the quadratic weighted kappa (κ) statistic. Secondary outcomes included quantitative agreement assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, and analytical comparability between whole blood and plasma on the POC platform.

RESULTS: Overall, 114/127 patients (89.8%) were assigned to the same triage category (κ = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.878-0.964). All 13 discordant classifications (10.2%) occurred between adjacent categories, with no CL rule-in patient classified as POC rule-out. Quantitative agreement between assays was good (ICC = 0.882; 95%CI 0.835-0.917), with a mean bias of -5.27 ng/L. Whole blood and plasma showed close agreement (ICC = 0.999; 95%CI 0.998-0.999), with a mean bias of 0.50 ng/L.

CONCLUSIONS: The POC assay showed high clinical concordance with CL-based ESC 0/1-h triage classification, with all discordances confined to adjacent categories. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of POC hs-cTnI testing under routine bedside conditions.

articles.title: Protocol for DNA extraction from QuantiFERON-TB gold tubes for PCR and sequencing applications.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) remains a significant barrier to global TB control and elimination efforts. The QuantiFERON-TB Gold (QFT) assay is commonly used for the diagnosis of LTBI. However, blood collected in QFT tubes is seldom utilized for molecular and genetic analysis due to the presence of heparin and a dense gel barrier that hinders efficient DNA extraction. To address this limitation, we aimed to develop a method for directly isolating high-quality DNA from blood in QFT tubes, eliminating the need for additional blood sampling and enabling their use in both diagnostic and molecular workflows. In this study, DNA was extracted from blood in EDTA and QFT tubes using a hybrid approach that combined manual lysis with three commercial kits: Thermo Scientific GeneJET, QIAamp DNA Blood Kit, and FavorPrep™ Blood Genomic DNA Extraction Kit. DNA concentration and purity were measured with a Multiskan SkyHigh Microplate Spectrophotometer, while integrity was assessed through agarose gel electrophoresis. Two nucleic acid amplification techniques (NAATs), ARMS-PCR and whole exome sequencing (WES) were performed to validate applicability of extracted DNA for molecular biology applications. We did not find any differences in the quantity, quality, or application of PCR or sequencing for DNA extracted from EDTA or QFT tubes. The extracted DNA from both EDTA and QFT tubes exhibited A260/280 ratios of 1.7-1.9 and concentrations ranging from 4.9 to 118.5 μg/mL, indicating an adequate yield and purity. Intact genomic DNA and PCR product bands on agarose gel indicated suitability for downstream applications. Additionally, WES produced 6.47-8.71 GB of data per sample, with 42.8-57.7 M reads and GC content between 49.29% and 52.54%. Sequencing metrics were consistently strong, with Q20 values exceeding 98.6% and Q30 values above 95%. Our study presents an optimized and reproducible protocol for DNA extraction suitable for downstream PCR and sequencing technologies. This protocol provides economical and practical strategy to integrate LTBI diagnosis with genomic research, particularly beneficial in resource-limited settings. This study introduces a novel analytical workflow applicable to diagnostic laboratory settings, enabling the integration of routine LTBI immunodiagnostic testing with downstream genomic analysis. The approach supports improved utilization of clinical specimens in laboratory medicine and may facilitate future biomarker and precision diagnostics research.

articles.title: QUALITY OF PROTEIN IN DIFFERENT FOOD SOURCES IN THE CONTEXT OF CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Plant-based diets have gained increasing attention in the management of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet concerns persist regarding the quality of plant-derived proteins. Traditionally, animal-based proteins have been regarded as high biological value proteins, while plant proteins have been labeled as low biological value, contributing to misconceptions about their nutritional adequacy. In this narrative review, we challenge these assumptions by presenting emerging evidence on the nutritional quality of plant proteins, strategies to enhance their amino acid profiles, and their relevance in the context of CKD. Furthermore, we discuss the health effects of plant versus animal proteins on kidney function, muscle mass, and gut microbiota. Alternative protein sources such as edible insects and mushrooms are also examined for their potential nutritional and environmental contributions. Our findings highlight that well-planned, plant-predominant diets can meet protein and amino acid needs across all stages of CKD without compromising muscle or metabolic health.

articles.title: PET-Guided Dose Escalation for Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL).

RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms.

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

articles.title: Secondary Pneumonia Among Non-Communicable Disease Inpatients: A Retrospective Administrative Surveillance Study from a Chinese Tertiary Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary pneumonia is an important inpatient complication, yet its burden among patients hospitalised for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in China remains poorly characterised. We aimed to quantify this burden and its association with in-hospital mortality and prolonged length of stay (LOS).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of 31,470 NCD inpatient records from a tertiary hospital in southwest China (2023 to 2025). Secondary pneumonia was identified by ICD-10 code J18 in any secondary diagnosis field. Three logistic regression models with patient-level clustered robust standard errors examined (1) factors associated with secondary pneumonia, (2) its association with in-hospital death, and (3) its association with LOS exceeding 10 days. A respiratory failure/ventilation coding proxy was included in Model 1 and excluded from Models 2 and 3 as a potential mediator.

RESULTS: Secondary pneumonia was identified in 2.94% of eligible admissions (n = 925), highest among admissions with neoplasms (6.15%). After adjustment, it was independently associated with in-hospital death (OR 3.15, 95% CI 1.75 to 5.67, p < 0.001) and LOS exceeding 10 days (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.49 to 2.08, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Secondary pneumonia was identified in 2.94% of NCD admissions and was independently associated with in-hospital death and prolonged LOS, with the highest coded prevalence among admissions with neoplasms. These findings support closer monitoring and evaluation of secondary pneumonia in NCD inpatients as a target for hospital quality improvement.

articles.title: High Exposure of Intravenous Alemtuzumab is Associated with Increased Risk of Adenovirus reactivation in Patients with Non-Malignant Disease Undergoing Allogeneic HCT.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alemtuzumab, a recombinant humanized immunoglobulin G1 monoclonal antibody directed against human CD52, is a widely used serotherapy strategy in pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) in non-malignant diseases (NMD) to help reduce the risk of graft rejection (GR) and graft versus host disease (GVHD). Excessive exposure to alemtuzumab potentially delays immune reconstitution and increases the risk of infections.

METHOD: We conducted a retrospective analysis at a single institution of 95 pediatric patients with NMD who underwent HCT and received intravenous alemtuzumab as part of their conditioning regimen between 2012-2024. Individualized alemtuzumab pharmacokinetic parameters, including pre- and post-HCT area under the curve (AUC) and day 0 concentrations, were estimated using a validated population pharmacokinetic model.

RESULTS: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis identified thresholds that associated with increased adenoviral infection of 55 mcg/mL*day for pre-HCT AUC and 10 mcg/mL*day for post-HCT AUC. Baseline absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) was the strongest determinant of post-HCT alemtuzumab concentrations. Higher pre- or post-HCT alemtuzumab exposure was associated with significantly more adenovirus reactivation (pre-HCT: 32.6% vs. 8.2%, p=0.007; post-HCT: 34.5% vs. 10.7%, p=0.008) and 2 or more viral reactivations (pre-HCT: 24% vs. 6%, p=0.023; post-HCT: 28.2% vs. 6.8%, p=0.008) during the first 180 days post-HCT. Higher pre-HCT exposure was also associated with increased HHV-6 reactivation (6.2% vs 23.7%, p=0.028). Alemtuzumab exposure was not associated with GR, graft loss, mixed chimerism, acute or chronic GVHD, transplant-related mortality (TRM), event-free survival (EFS), or overall survival (OS). Lower day 0 alemtuzumab concentrations (≤0.77 mcg/mL) were associated with more patients reaching CD4 recovery by day 180 (88.2% vs 56.9%, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher pre- or post HCT alemtuzumab levels are associated with a higher risk of adenovirus reactivation. Individualized, model-based alemtuzumab dosing may reduce excessive post-transplant exposure while maintaining excellent engraftment and survival outcomes. Targeting lower post-HCT alemtuzumab exposure may decrease viral complications without compromising transplant success, supporting pharmacokinetic-guided dosing strategies in pediatric HSCT for nonmalignant diseases.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Admission to the Intensive Care Unit and Mortality in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are at risk of requiring intensive care unit (ICU)-level care following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Risk factors for admission to the ICU and outcomes are, however, poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To assess risk factors associated with ICU admission in such patients, identify variables associated with ICU mortality, and analyze the outcome of ICU survivors in comparison to HCT recipients not admitted to the ICU.

STUDY DESIGN: Here, we retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 1,265 adults with MDS/AML or AML who received an allograft while in first or second remission between 2006 and 2023.

RESULTS: The cumulative incidence of ICU admission was 9.2% on day +100 after HCT. HCT-comorbidity index (hazard ratio [HR]=1.15, P=0.005), treatment-related mortality (TRM) score (HR=1.07, P=0.004), and graft from an HLA-mismatched donor (HR=2.19, P=0.018) were independently associated with ICU admission. Within 100 days of ICU admission, 50 patients (43%) died; poor performance status (odds ratio [OR]=5.45, P=0.005), higher TRM score (OR per one unit increase=1.14, P=0.035), and secondary AML (OR=2.71 P=0.035) were associated with increased day +100 mortality after ICU admission. In a landmark analysis, patients admitted to the ICU during the first 100 days after HCT and alive at day +150 had significantly higher NRM (HR=2.36, P<0.001) after multivariable adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Together, these results highlight that ICU admission is common after allografting in adults with AML and is associated with high mortality. Identification of patients at increased risk may, ultimately, help develop possible preventive strategies and allow testing in particularly vulnerable individuals.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks of sex hormone therapy: from contraception to transgender care.
articles.abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolism is increased with combined oral contraceptives, rises with the dose of ethinylestradiol, and is higher with desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone or cyproterone acetate than with levonorgestrel; the determinant is not the generation of the pill but the residual androgen-receptor activity of the progestin, which modulates the hepatic effect of the estrogen. Age over 35 years, obesity, smoking and a family history of thrombosis amplify it. Pills based on a native estrogen have a more limited hepatic impact and rank below most ethinylestradiol combinations in contemporary cohorts, but their clinical safety is not demonstrated and no comparative outcome data exist for estetrol/drospirenone. Androgenicity is not a general marker of venous safety: injectable depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, given alone at supraphysiological doses, carries an increased risk. Myocardial infarction and stroke are also more frequent, but against a very low background - about 21 additional strokes and 10 additional infarctions per 100,000 person-years, four times fewer than the venous excess - and, unlike venous events, independent of progestin type. Menopause hormone therapy increases venous thromboembolic risk, especially in the first year; the route of administration is the main determinant, transdermal estradiol with micronized progesterone appearing safest. In cisgender men, testosterone deficiency carries increased cardiovascular risk, and randomized and real-world data support the safety of transdermal replacement, although more pulmonary embolism and atrial fibrillation have been observed. In trans women, observational data show an increased risk of stroke and venous thromboembolism, particularly with oral estradiol and cyproterone acetate, whereas recent large-scale data show no excess of major cardiovascular events with testosterone in trans men. The practical consequences are specific: no combined pill is acceptable after a venous thromboembolic event, with a thrombogenic mutation or with migraine with aura, native-estrogen pills included; transdermal estradiol should be preferred for menopause and feminising hormone therapy; and haematocrit should guide the dose and route of testosterone.

articles.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with REML estimation of between-study variance (ORs); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI).

RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (8 studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%.

CONCLUSIONS: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

articles.title: A Vascular Surgery and Primary Care Partnership for Improving Resident Training in Peripheral Artery Disease Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis, establishment of best medical management, and timely specialty referral for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain ongoing challenges. In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care.

STUDY DESIGN: A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions. A pre-session survey assessed self-rated knowledge, practices, attitudes, and medical training regarding PAD, followed by a truncated post-session survey. The responses were grouped as high vs. moderate/low. Descriptive statistics and the McNemar Exact test were used for paired sample comparison.

RESULTS: Thirty-one residents completed both surveys (65% IM, 35% FM, 58% male, and 77% first- or second-year trainees). Pre-session data revealed gaps in knowledge with few residents rating their understanding as "high." Post-session, there was a significant increase across all measured areas (p<0.001). Notably, improvements were seen in the number of residents who felt highly confident in diagnosing PAD (from 16.1% to 90.3%), using a vascular Doppler (6.5% to 83.9%), ordering non-invasive testing (from 6.5% to 83.9%), performing a lower extremity pulse exam (from 12.9% to 87.1%), managing PAD for amputation prevention (from 12.9% to 71.0%), and referring to a vascular specialist (from 25.8% to 83.9%).

CONCLUSION: Resident knowledge and confidence improved significantly as a result of a singular educational session. This collaborative model between vascular surgery educators and primary care residency programs demonstrates an adaptable framework that successfully addresses a gap in PAD management training.

articles.title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Mixed Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease With a Horizontal Aorta: Return of Spontaneous Circulation Only After Left Ventricular Unloading.
articles.abstract: A 74-year-old man with mixed bicuspid aortic valve disease, combining severe calcific stenosis with severe regurgitation, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 26% presented in normotensive cardiogenic shock with anuria and an arterial lactate of 12 mmol/L. Computed tomography showed a fibrocalcific left-right raphe and an aortic angulation of 66 degrees. Emergency transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation was undertaken. The delivery system could not be advanced across the aortic arch despite escalation of guidewire support, and ventricular fibrillation degenerated into pulseless electrical activity refractory to resuscitation. Peripheral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established, after which a 29 mm self-expanding prosthesis was implanted with an acceptable haemodynamic result and patent coronary ostia. Pulseless electrical activity nonetheless persisted. Return of spontaneous circulation followed only after a microaxial pump was advanced retrogradely across the freshly deployed prosthesis under fluoroscopic guidance alone, establishing an ECMELLA configuration. The patient died of multiorgan failure two days later. This sequence identifies continued left ventricular loading, rather than any residual valve lesion, as the reason resuscitation failed, and argues for anticipating unloading when extracorporeal support is instituted across a valve just rendered competent in a severely dysfunctional ventricle. The outcome appeared determined by end-organ injury already established before intervention.

articles.title: Recasting Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Through Contemporary Analytical Frameworks: An Integrated Analysis Using the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List 2024 and AWaRe Classification in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Saurashtra, Western India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Indian antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance rarely uses contemporary global frameworks, and Saurashtra is under-represented in the national evidence base. We applied the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (BPPL) 2024 and the WHO AWaRe (Access-Watch-Reserve) classification to institutional surveillance data, with national and global benchmarking.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 2,195 non-duplicate clinical bacterial isolates (May-October 2024) at a 1,200-bed government tertiary care teaching hospital. Susceptibility testing followed CLSI M100-S33 (VITEK 2 Compact; Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion); multi-drug resistance (MDR) followed Magiorakos criteria. Isolates were assigned to BPPL 2024 tiers by resistant phenotype, and agent-level resistance was grouped by AWaRe 2023 category. MDR correlates were explored by multivariable logistic regression. The isolate was the unit of analysis; proportions describe cultured isolates, not infections or patients.

RESULTS: Isolates meeting Critical-priority phenotypes numbered 1,192 (54.3% of the isolate pool): third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (n = 1,086; 49.5%; ceftriaxone resistance 78% in E. coli and 61% in K. pneumoniae) and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (n = 106; 4.8%). High-priority phenotypes accounted for at most 228 isolates (10.4%). Within the Access group, Enterobacterales resistance was high to ampicillin (89.7% in E. coli) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (77-83%) but lower to gentamicin (22-33%); Watch-group fluoroquinolone resistance was 47-73%. Meropenem resistance in E. coli (1%) and K. pneumoniae (7%) was markedly lower than ICMR AMRSN 2023 national estimates (40% and 54%). MDR was present in 58.6% of isolates and was independently associated with ICU admission, age >60 years, tracheal-aspirate specimens, and surgical-department admission.

CONCLUSIONS: Reading isolate-level surveillance data through the BPPL 2024 and AWaRe frameworks adds a priority- and stewardship-oriented layer to the conventional antibiogram. These proportions describe cultured isolates, not the frequency of resistant infection in patients. The low Enterobacterales carbapenem resistance relative to national benchmarks warrants multi-center, consumption-linked confirmation.

articles.title: Vericiguat prevents hepatic inflammation and microcirculatory dysfunction in the early phase of sepsis in mice.
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with persistent microcirculatory dysfunction driving progressive organ injury despite optimal macrocirculatory support. Vericiguat, a soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator approved for chronic heart failure, enhances nitric oxide signaling, promoting vasodilation and supporting endothelial integrity. Based on this profile of action, we hypothesized that vericiguat improves hepatic microcirculatory perfusion in sepsis and thereby mitigates liver injury. Male C57BL/6J mice underwent sham surgery (n = 8) or cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). CLP-treated mice received either vericiguat (3 mg/kg body weight; n = 8) or dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) 50% as vehicle control (n = 8). Six hours later, the livers were examined by means of intravital fluorescence microscopy, followed by immunohistochemical and plasma analyses. Vericiguat significantly reduced leukocyte-endothelial cell interactions and macromolecular leakage in the microcirculation of septic livers. Moreover, it reduced sinusoidal perfusion failure and normalized the expression of the extracellular matrix marker perlecan. Plasma analyses did not reveal marked differences between vericiguat- and vehicle-treated septic mice, most probably due to the early observation time point after CLP. Taken together, these findings suggest that vericiguat may represent a promising drug in sepsis, potentially preventing early hepatic inflammation and microcirculatory dysfunction.

articles.title: Polyethylene glenospheres in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty have greater long-term implant survivorship than metallic glenospheres: A New Zealand Joint Registry Study.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is increasingly common and clinically effective. Conventional-bearing rTSA (CB-rTSA) employs a metallic glenosphere articulating with a polyethylene humeral liner. Inverted-bearing rTSA (IB-rTSA), using a polyethylene glenosphere with a metallic or ceramic humeral liner, was developed to eliminate polyethylene wear debris at the scapular neck and thereby reduce polyethylene-induced osteolysis and the severity of scapular notching. Comparative data on survivorship and patient-reported outcomes between these configurations remain limited. This study compared implant survival, revision risk and functional outcomes between CB-rTSA and IB-rTSA designs.

METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study identified all primary rTSA procedures performed in New Zealand between January 2007 and December 2024 from the New Zealand Joint Registry. Revision-free implant survival and postoperative function, measured by the Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS), were analysed. Patients were grouped by bearing configuration: polyethylene glenosphere (IB-rTSA) and metal glenosphere (CB-rTSA). Subgroup analyses compared SMR Reverse Polyethylene and SMR Reverse Metal (LimaCorporate, Italy) with other CB-rTSA designs, predominantly Delta Xtend (DePuy Synthes, USA). Revision rates per 100 component-years were calculated, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared revision risk, adjusting for age, sex and diagnosis.

RESULTS: A total of 8,601 rTSA procedures were included: 3,437 (40.0%) using a polyethylene glenosphere and 5,164 (60.0%) a metallic glenosphere. Indications for surgery were comparable between groups, whereas the sex distribution differed significantly. Unadjusted revision rates per 100 component-years were higher for the metal group (0.71) than the polyethylene group (0.46) (P = .001). The adjusted hazard ratio for polyethylene compared with metal was 0.57 (95% CI 0.43 - 0.75), representing a 43% lower revision rate.
