In secondary, unadjusted cause-specific analyses, polyethylene glenospheres were associated with fewer revisions for deep infection (0.11 vs 0.20 per 100 component-years; P = .031) and dislocation (0.09 vs 0.16; P = .045). Mean OSS at 6 months, 5 years and 10 years were similar between groups, with no statistically or clinically significant differences.

CONCLUSION: In this large national registry study, IB-rTSA using a polyethylene glenosphere was associated with significantly lower revision rates than conventional metal glenosphere designs, with no statistically or clinically significant differences in patient-reported functional outcomes. In secondary, unadjusted cause-specific analyses, polyethylene glenospheres were also associated with lower rates of revision for deep infection and dislocation. Although it could not be examined using registry data, this lower revision burden may relate to the absence of polyethylene-induced osteolysis and consequently less pronounced scapular notching.

articles.title: Targeting the Vein of Marshall in the Modern Era: Do We Still Need Ethanol?
Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.

METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.

RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.

CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

articles.title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.

OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.

METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.

RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.

CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

articles.title: An MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for linking behavioral neurophysiology and stimulation-evoked fMRI in non-human primates.
articles.abstract: Local electrophysiology and microstimulation reveal site-specific neural activity and physiological effects but do not directly link these local effects to whole-brain responses from the same target site. We developed an MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for macaques that enables CT/MRI-based localization, postoperative depth adjustment, neural recording, microstimulation during behavioral testing, and subsequent electrical microstimulation combined with functional MRI (EM-fMRI) using the same implanted electrode. The system supported local field potential recording, a stimulation-induced reduction in pupil size, and distributed stimulation-evoked blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) responses. This approach provides a practical framework for linking local neural activity and stimulation-induced physiological responses with whole-brain responses at the same target site.

articles.title: The Lysine Methyltransferase SETDB1 Alleviates Methionine- and Choline-Deficient Diet-Induced Steatohepatitis by Suppressing Ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disorder, with its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), characterized by steatosis, inflammation, hepatocyte injury, and fibrosis. However, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed an in vivo CRISPR screen in Cas9 mice fed a methionine- and choline-deficient (MCD) diet to identify epigenetic regulators of MASH. SETDB1 emerged as a key modulator: hepatocyte-specific loss of Setdb1 exacerbated steatosis, inflammation, ductular reaction, and fibrosis, whereas Setdb1 overexpression markedly alleviated these pathological features. Notably, human liver samples showed decreased SETDB1 expression with advancing MASLD. Furthermore, SETDB1 deficiency increased hepatic ferroptosis by upregulating ACSL4, aggravating MASH pathology, whereas ACSL4 knockout reduced liver injury in the absence of SETDB1. SETDB1 overexpression protected against liver damage by repressing ACSL4. Therefore, the SETDB1-ACSL4-ferroptosis axis regulates MASH progression and represents a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Exercise Capacity, Muscle Mass, and Quality of Life in Pediatric Patients with Fontan Circulation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how measures of cardiac, vascular, and muscle health relate to Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory TM (PedsQL) score in a cohort of children and adolescents with Fontan circulation.

STUDY DESIGN: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from children and adolescents (8-19 years) with Fontan circulation enrolled in a prospective study. Participants underwent a series of tests, including a cardiopulmonary exercise test, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry measures of appendicular lean mass index (ALMI, kg/m2), leg dynamometry, and the 23-item PedsQL. The survey quantifies Physical, Emotional, Social, and School functioning into 1 total score and 2 summary scores for physical and psychosocial health.

RESULTS: 135 patients (median age 12.7 [IQR 10.2, 15.6] years) completed the baseline visit. Median time from Fontan operation was 8.7 years [IQR 5.9, 12.0]. Peak VO2 was 1309 [IQR 1070, 1670] mL/min, and indexed peak VO2 was 31.1 [IQR 25.2, 36.1] mL/kg/min. Physical and Psychosocial PedsQL summary scores were 78.1 [IQR 67.2,90.6] and 76.7 [IQR 63.3, 90], respectively, and the total score was 76.1 [IQR 65.2, 88.0]. Absolute peak VO2 was weakly correlated with PedsQL Physical Summary Score (ρ=0.21, P=0.015), but indexed peak VO2, % predicted peak VO2, and Fontan-specific peak VO2 z-score were not ALMI z-score was -0.84 [IQR -1.56, -0.14] and positively correlated with total PedsQL score (ρ=0.28, P=0.001) and the Physical Functioning domain (ρ=0.30, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle mass was associated with quality of life in children with Fontan circulation. The association between VO2 and physical function was attenuated with body-size normalization.

articles.title: Life's Essential 8 Cardiovascular Health Characteristics in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the cardiovascular health (CVH) characteristics in children and adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) using a modified version of the American Heart Association (AHA) Life's Essential 8 criteria and examine differences in CVH by CHD complexity.

STUDY DESIGN: This single-center, cross-sectional study included youth 8-19 years old with CHD and an available total cholesterol within 3 years of a clinic visit. Patients were categorized into simple, moderate, or complex anatomic groups according to AHA anatomic classification guidelines for CHD. Modified CVH scores were calculated using 3 to 5 CVH metrics: nicotine exposure, body mass index (BMI), blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure. The association between anatomic complexity and CVH was assessed using multivariable linear regression.

RESULTS: The study cohort included 629 patients. Modified CVH scores were low or moderate in 46.1% of patients, with prevalent low or moderate scores in blood lipids (49.4%), blood pressure (42.4%), and BMI (31.9%). Median CVH scores differed across anatomic groups (simple 83 vs moderate 78 vs complex 84, P=0.01). Complex CHD was associated with a higher (more favorable) modified CVH score and blood pressure score than moderate CHD and a higher blood lipids score than simple and moderate CHD.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite vulnerable cardiac anatomy, almost half of youth with CHD had suboptimal CVH, with prevalent deficits in blood lipids, blood pressure, and BMI. Complex CHD anatomy was associated with a more favorable CVH profile. These findings highlight the need to incorporate health screening and promotion into the routine care of the pediatric CHD population.

articles.title: Cellular senescence and vascular ageing in pulmonary hypertension: Molecular mechanisms, therapeutic strategies, and translational endpoints.
articles.abstract: Increased right ventricular afterload, persistent pulmonary vascular remodelling, and the development of right heart failure are the hallmarks of pulmonary hypertension (PH). In PAH, therapies targeting the prostacyclin, nitric oxide-cyclic guanosine monophosphate, and endothelin pathways improve clinical status and haemodynamics, although established vascular remodelling frequently remains incompletely reversible. This review summarises data suggesting that the residual remodelling load in PH is influenced by vascular ageing, specifically stress-induced premature senescence-like phenotypes in pulmonary vascular wall cells. Endothelial repair failure, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell secretory amplification, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, senescence-associated secretory phenotype signalling, and mechano-metabolic reprogramming are examined as interconnected processes that attenuate vascular plasticity and consolidate disease progression. Pharmacological strategies discussed include senolytic and senomorphic approaches, activin/TGF-β superfamily modulation exemplified by sotatercept, matrix- and mechanotransduction-directed interventions, and metabolic modulation. Finally, vascular ageing-informed PH studies are proposed to incorporate concordant endpoints that align molecular target engagement with pulmonary vascular mechanics, right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling, right ventricular function, and safety outcomes.

articles.title: Photothermal-responsive Biomimetic Xenon Nanobubbles for Spatiotemporally Targeted Therapy of Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) involves persistent oxidative stress, exacerbated inflammation, and neuronal apoptosis. However, the therapeutic efficacy of current neuroprotective agents is severely restricted by the blood-brain barrier, which hinders their effective delivery to ischemic brain tissue. Although xenon (Xe) exhibits well-documented neuroprotective properties, its rapid diffusion and short in vivo retention limit its ability to match the evolving pathology of stroke. Therefore, developing Xe-based delivery systems with enhanced lesion targeting and controllable release is essential to fully harness the therapeutic potential of Xe for IS. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-coated Xe nanobubbles (Xe-MNBs), namely ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs and IR 820@Xe-MNBs, which respectively carry lipophilic and hydrophilic photosensitizer analogues. Compared with IR 820@Xe-MNBs, ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs exhibited a higher Xe payload, with a measured Xe content of 56.8 μL/mL. Combined in vivo and ex vivo fluorescence imaging demonstrated rapid brain-associated accumulation of the biomimetic nanobubbles within 5 min after intravenous administration. The cranial fluorescence signal of ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs was approximately 3.2-fold higher than that of IR 820@Xe-MNBs, indicating a more pronounced early brain-associated fluorescence signal in the ischemic lesions. Upon near-infrared light irradiation, the photothermal effect triggered nanobubble disruption and Xe release in vitro, enabling externally controlled gas release. Treatment further attenuated oxidative damage and neuronal apoptosis while preserving neuronal integrity in the ischemic brain. Collectively, this work integrated inflammation-associated biomimetic targeting with photothermal-responsive Xe delivery, providing a promising strategy for spatiotemporally regulated gas therapy of IS. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1. Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced differentiation of THP-1 cells was employed to construct biomimetic nanobubbles (NBs), endowing them with enhanced adhesion to inflamed endothelial cells and improved targeting of ischemic brain lesions. 2. By integrating fluorescence imaging with photothermal activation, spatiotemporally regulated delivery of xenon (Xe) was achieved, thereby enabling precise therapeutic intervention for ischemic stroke (IS). 3. Compared with the IR 820-based system, ADS 815EI-loaded, macrophage membrane-coated Xe nanobubbles (ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs) exhibited a higher Xe-loading capacity, greater stability, and more pronounced brain accumulation at early time points, highlighting their potential for therapeutic intervention during the early treatment window after IS.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Coronary Artery Calcification Score for Long-Term Risk of Stroke, Atrial Fibrillation and Mortality: Analysis of Real-World Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) score has been implicated in cardiovascular risk assessment, yet its role in predicting incident ischaemic stroke (IS), atrial fibrillation (AF), and all-cause mortality in the general population remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between CAC score and these outcomes using real-world hospital and community data.

METHODS: We included adults who underwent CAC scoring at our local hospital between May 2010 and May 2018. CAC scores were classified into CAC Data and Reporting System (CAC DRS) categories (0-3) based on Agatston scoring. Study outcomes included incident IS, new-onset AF, and all-cause mortality, with follow-up data obtained from medical record linkage. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, restricted cubic spline models, and Cox proportional hazards models were employed to evaluate associations between CAC score and outcomes, adjusting for potential confounders. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness.

RESULTS: We included 2,175 patients (mean age: 51.47, SD 11.05 years, 62.7% female). During a mean follow-up of about 10 years, 42 (1.9%) patients had incident IS and 126 (5.8%) died, while 135 (6.4%) of 2122 patients developed new-onset AF. No significant association of CAC score and clinical outcomes was evident on Kaplan-Meier survival analysis or restricted cubic spline analysis. On multivariable analysis, CAC DRS category 2 was significantly associated with an increased risk of IS (HR = 2.82, 95%CI: 1.02-7.84, p=0.047), while no significant associations were observed for AF or all-cause mortality. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the increased IS risk in CAC DRS 2 (HR = 2.89, 95%CI: 1.04-8.04, p=0.042), but no significant associations for AF or all-cause mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: CAC is not independently associated with AF and all-cause mortality in the general population. Moderate CAC burden (CAC DRS 2) may be associated to increased IS risk, warranting further research on its role in cerebrovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: A live-cell medium-throughput assay for quantifying lipid accumulation in hepatocytes.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global health burden contributing to the high prevalence of associated metabolic diseases such as cardiovascular disease and thus global mortality rates. MASLD is diagnosed by ≥ 5 % lipid accumulation in the liver, and candidate therapies are often evaluated for lipid lowering effects. Current cell-based lipid imaging approaches rely on fixed-cell staining with dyes such as BODIPY 493/503, limiting the ability to dynamically monitor lipid accumulation in living hepatocytes. To gain a better understanding of the effect of different culture conditions and pharmacological interventions on lipid dynamics, we have developed a live-cell assay of fatty acid stimulated lipid accumulation based on BODIPY 493/503, using two hepatocyte cell lines (HepG2 and AML12) in a simplified workflow. This workflow was validated by its success in helping characterise the lipid lowering activity of known pharmacological agents under different conditions and as a function of time. The agents included impact both lipid biosynthesis (diacylglycerol acyltransferase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibitors) and metabolism (THR-β agonist). Collectively, this assay enables the temporal interrogation of hepatic lipid dynamics and represents a valuable tool for screening and characterising emerging MASLD therapeutics.

articles.title: Essential oil from Angelica sinensis Radix attenuates ischemic stroke via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK pathway: insights from network pharmacology and molecular mechanism evaluation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: As a traditional herbal remedy, the root of Angelica sinensis has long been used to treat headaches, strokes, and dementia. As the primary active ingredient in A. sinensis, A. sinensis essential oil (ASEO) also plays a significant role in the therapy of stroke. Although ASEO has shown clear therapeutic effects, its specific mechanism of preventing ischemic stroke still needs to be further clarified.

AIM OF THE STUDY: Through network pharmacological analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experimental verification, this study investigated the protective effects of ASEO against stroke and elucidated the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used to analyze the chemical composition of ASEO. Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats were administered different doses of ASEO to evaluate its therapeutic effects. The therapeutic effects were evaluated using behavioral, histopathological, and immunofluorescence assays. In addition, using network pharmacology techniques, the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the treatment of ischemic stroke with ASEO have been preliminarily elucidated. HT22 cells treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) were used as an in vitro model. Subsequently, the key signal transduction pathways involved in the therapeutic effects of ASEO against ischemic stroke were further validated using multiple experimental approaches, including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), flow cytometry, Western blotting, pathway-specific pharmacological inhibition and PKG-specific siRNA knockdown.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven compounds were identified from ASEO by GC-MS. In vivo experiments demonstrated that ASEO treatment exerted significant protective effects on MCAO/R rats by improving impaired neurological function, reducing cerebral infarct volume, alleviating neuronal apoptosis, and modulating the expression of apoptotic proteins. Mechanistically, network pharmacology studies suggested that the protective mechanism of ASEO may involve the cGMP/PKG and MAPK signaling pathways. Subsequent experiments confirmed that ASEO inhibited neuronal apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK axis both in vivo and in vitro. Importantly, both pharmacological inhibition and siRNA-mediated genetic knockdown of PKG significantly attenuated the protective effects of ASEO against OGD/R injury in HT22 cells.

CONCLUSION: ASEO exerts its anti-ischemic stroke effect by attenuating apoptosis via the cGMP/PKG/MAPK signaling pathway, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application in ischemic stroke therapy.

articles.title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD: current evidence and challenges in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by a complex pathophysiology driven by intertwined metabolic and hepatic pathways, enabling the identification of multiple therapeutic targets and a rapidly expanding drug development pipeline. This review summarizes the current and emerging therapeutic landscape for MASLD and discusses key challenges for clinical implementation. The imminent availability of several new therapies is expected to pose important clinical challenges, particularly in accurately identifying patients most likely to benefit. Currently, resmetirom and semaglutide are the only two drugs conditionally approved for patients with fibrosis stages 2-3, pending final phase 3 outcomes, and represent the main liver-directed and metabolic-focused therapeutic strategies, respectively. Treatment selection should follow a phenotype-based approach integrating metabolic profile and liver disease stage. Non-invasive tests are central for assessing treatment eligibility; however, strategies incorporating metabolic risk profiling and longitudinal monitoring will be essential to optimize real-world management of MASH.

articles.title: Therapeutic advances in chronic hepatitis B and Delta: where are we now and where are we headed?
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (HBV) and delta (HDV) infections remain major global health challenges. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and bulevirtide, a recently approved entry inhibitor, effectively suppress HBV and HDV replication, respectively, thereby reducing the risk of liver-related complications. However, they rarely induce functional cure, defined as sustained HBsAg loss, and generally require long-term administration. This limitation is primarily driven by the persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) and integrated HBV DNA, which are not targeted by existing treatments. A broad range of novel therapeutic strategies is currently under investigation. Virus-directing agents, including small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, nucleic acid polymers, and capsid assembly modulators, have shown promising antiviral activity. However, their efficacy as monotherapy remains modest, with HBsAg loss observed at moderate rates and mainly among patients with a favorable baseline profile. Combination strategies integrating direct antivirals with immune modulation (therapeutic vaccines, toll-like receptor agonists or monoclonal antibodies) may represent a promising pathway to increase the rates of functional cure. In HDV infection, emerging phase 3 combination strategies are also showing promising results, supporting a shift toward more effective, multi-targeted treatment approaches. Building on these advances, the convergence of novel antivirals and immune-modulating strategies, together with precision biomarkers, makes functional cure a realistic long-term objective in HBV and HDV infection.

articles.title: Survival Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Decade of Treatment in a Western Tertiary Referral Center.
authors: Erasmus MC Hepatocellular Carcinoma Collaborative Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a challenging malignancy with various available treatments. This retrospective study provides clinical outcomes on staging, treatment, and overall survival (OS) of HCC patients.

METHODS: All included patients were diagnosed between 2013 and 2022. OS was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, stratified by BCLC stage and diagnosis period.

RESULTS: A total of 1,306 patients were analyzed: 9.1% BCLC-0, 44.3% BCLC-A, 19.1% BCLC-B, 17% BCLC-C, and 10.4% BCLC-D. Median OS (mOS) for the cohort was 19.7 months (95% CI 16.9-23.0), ranging from 86.1 months (95% CI 47.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.4 months (95% CI 1.7-3.4) for BCLC-D. Poor survival was associated with Child-Pugh (CP) classification (CP-B: HR1.49, 95% CI 1.17-1.89, CP-C: HR2.45, 95% CI 1.57-3.81), and portal vein tumor thrombosis (HR1.75, 95% CI 1.19-2.58). In 2013-2017, 609 patients (46.6%) were diagnosed with mOS of 21.7 months (95% CI 18.4-25.1), while 697 patients (53.4%) in 2018-2022 had mOS of 18.9 months (95% CI 14.8-22.7). Stratified by BCLC stage, mOS in 2013-2017 ranged from 86.1 months (95% CI 41.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.9 months (95% CI 2.2-5.7) for BCLC-D. In 2018-2022, mOS was 59.8 months (95%CI 44.2-not reached) for BCLC-0, and 1.8 months (95% CI 1.4-3.1) for BCLC-D.

CONCLUSIONS: Our clinical data from a consecutive decade-long HCC cohort support the evolution of staging and survival data in HCC management, with CP classification, portal vein tumor thrombosis, and treatment modality as key survival predictors.

articles.title: [Translated article] What's new in spinal instrumentation-related infections.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de cirugia ortopedica y traumatologia
articles.abstract: Infections associated with spinal instrumentation represent one of the most complex complications in spine surgery and frequently involve biofilm-forming pathogens that compromise the effectiveness of antimicrobial therapies. Diagnosis - particularly in chronic cases - requires the use of advanced microbiological techniques, such as implant sonication, next-generation metagenomic sequencing, and prolonged culture incubation. Therapeutic strategies depend on the chronicity of the infection and the stability of the implant, ranging from surgical debridement with retention of osteosynthesis material to staged delayed re-instrumentation. Empirical antibiotic therapy should be initiated promptly and subsequently adjusted according to microbiological results. Prevention remains a fundamental pillar and includes strict perioperative optimization. Favorable outcomes rely on early detection, a multidisciplinary team approach, and individualized surgical and antimicrobial management based on accurate clinical and radiological assessment.

articles.title: Early functional outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy in patients with large vessel occlusion and active cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evaluating mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large vessel occlusion stroke (LVOS) and active cancer (AC) is challenging because cancer-related mortality substantially affects conventional functional outcomes. This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MT and non-MT groups. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores at 2 weeks, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients who died from cancer progression within 2 weeks of stroke onset was also performed. LVOS was defined as ischemic stroke with occlusion of the intra- or extracranial internal carotid artery, middle cerebral artery (M1 or M2 segments), or basilar artery.

RESULTS: Among 72 patients with LVOS and AC (median age, 76 years; 36 women), 32 (44%) underwent MT (28 MT alone, and 4 MT procedures combined with intravenous thrombolysis), whereas 3 patients in the non-MT group received intravenous thrombolysis alone. At 2 weeks, MT was significantly associated with a favorable shift in mRS distribution (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-9.97; p = 0.020). In a sensitivity analysis excluding cancer-related deaths, this association remained significant, with a larger effect size (adjusted OR, 6.21, 95% CI, 1.89-20.47; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: MT was associated with improved early functional outcomes in patients with LVOS and AC.

articles.title: Evolutionary Characteristics and Immune Response of Il-17 Ligand and Receptor Families in Megalobrama amblycephala Following Aeromonas hydrophila Infection.
articles.abstract: The Il-17 ligand family members (Il-17s) and their receptors (Il-17rs) are core immune regulatory gene families against bacterial infection in vertebrates, while their evolutionary characteristics and immune functions remain poorly understood in Megalobrama amblycephala. This study systematically identified Il-17s and Il-17rs in M. amblycephala, analyzing their evolutionary characteristics and immune response mechanisms. Sequence alignment and domain analysis showed that all Il-17s contained the conserved Il-17 domain, while most Il-17rs possessed the SEFIR domain. Furthermore, these genes showed isoform-specific distribution characteristics in gene structure and conserved motifs. Phylogenetic and Collinearity analyses indicated that the Il-17rs in teleosts had undergone significant gene duplication, subject to strong purifying selection pressure, with il-17d and il-17rd1 demonstrating the highest evolutionary conservation. Notably, M. amblycephala lacked the teleost-specific il-17n but retained il-17bl, which is absent in many other teleost species. Following A. hydrophila challenge, il-17a/f1 was significantly upregulated in systemic immune organs such as the spleen and trunk kidney, while il-17c exhibited the strongest response in mucosal immune tissues like the gills, demonstrating distinct tissue-specific regulation. This study clarifies the evolutionary rule and immune function of Il-17 family in M. amblycephala, providing a theoretical basis for exploring the immune mechanism of bacterial diseases in fish.

articles.title: Collateral Sensitivity in Bacteria: Phenomenon, Mechanisms, Modulators and Therapeutic Prospects.
articles.abstract: The rapid proliferation and infection of multidrug-resistant bacteria pose a significant threat to global public health. The gradual increase in drug resistance, primarily driven by the inappropriate use of antibiotics, underscores the urgent need for developing novel therapeutic approaches for drug-resistant bacterial infections. Collateral sensitivity (CS) describes the phenomenon whereby bacteria resistance to a specific antibiotic increases susceptibility to other antibiotics. In some cases of antibiotic resistance, CS can provide rapid and effective guidance for clinical drug use by detecting the lowest drug sensitivity concentration of resistant bacteria. In order to prevent or mitigate the emergence of drug-resistant bacteria, it is crucial to thoroughly investigate the underlying mechanisms of CS. This article discusses recent research progress on the CS phenomenon, its mechanisms, influencing factors, and the therapeutic potential of CS in bacteria.

articles.title: Neurodegeneration in Sub-Saharan Africa: Intersections of Biological Ageing, Genomic Diversity and the Lifetime Exposome.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are emerging as an important consequence of population ageing in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), but their scientific relevance extends beyond a projected rise in case numbers. SSA combines exceptional human genomic diversity with marked heterogeneity in vascular and metabolic risk, infection, nutrition, occupational exposures, air pollution, and access to health care. This combination creates an underused setting in which to study why biological ageing produces neurodegeneration in some individuals but relative resilience in others. This review critically synthesises evidence on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal degeneration, Huntington's disease and related disorders, focusing on the intersection between hallmarks of ageing, disease-specific proteinopathies, ancestry and the lifetime exposome. Age-associated loss of proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired autophagy, chronic inflammation, neurovascular injury and genomic/epigenomic instability provide a mechanistic scaffold on which genetic susceptibility and cumulative exposures may act. Yet African evidence remains dominated by cross-sectional clinical phenotyping; neuropathology, longitudinal biomarkers, multi-omics and measured environmental exposures remain sparse. Recent African-ancestry Parkinson's disease genomics and emerging plasma biomarker studies demonstrate that ancestry-inclusive molecular neuroscience is feasible and can generate findings not predictable from European-ancestry datasets. The next phase should therefore move beyond documenting underdiagnosis toward longitudinal, biologically anchored cohorts that integrate phenotype, genomics, blood biomarkers, neuroimaging, exposomics, digital measures and health-system outcomes. This review proposes a research framework centred on biological ageing, gene-environment interaction and resilience. Such work would improve the validity of prevention, diagnosis and therapeutic translation in African populations while contributing globally to a more complete biology of neurodegenerative ageing.

articles.title: Myocardial Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder with Anxious Distress: Evidence from Oxygenation-Sensitive CMR and Entropy Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with major depressive disorder with anxious distress (MDD-A) frequently experience cardiovascular symptoms (CVS), which are associated with impaired quality of life and poorer long-term prognosis. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate myocardial alterations in MDD-A patients using oxygenation-sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (OS-CMR) and mapping-derived entropy analysis, and to explore their associations with CVS as well as the severity of depressive and anxiety symptoms.

METHODS: In this prospective study, 58 consecutively enrolled medication-naïve patients with MDD-A diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria and 61 healthy controls were included. All participants underwent CMR examinations at 3.0T. Left ventricular (LV) function, native T1 and T2 values, T1-entropy and T2-entropy, LV strain parameters, and oxygenation-sensitive signal intensity change (OS-SI%) were measured and compared between the two groups. Associations between CMR-derived parameters and CVS, anxiety symptom severity, and depressive symptom severity were assessed separately. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with MDD-A exhibited significantly higher T1-entropy (8.3 ± 0.3 vs. 7.5 ± 0.3, p < 0.001) and T2-entropy (9.2 ± 0.4 vs. 8.1 ± 0.3, p < 0.001), whereas OS-SI% was significantly lower (11.4 ± 7.5% vs. 14.5 ± 4.5%, p = 0.007). After adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, and heart rate, multivariable regression analyses revealed that OS-SI% was inversely associated with HAMD scores (β = -0.205, p = 0.043) and HAMA scores (β = -0.453, p < 0.001), and inversely associated with CVS (OR= 0.801, p = 0.002). T1-entropy (β = 4.105, p = 0.022) and T2-entropy (β = 2.793, p = 0.042) were positively associated with HAMD scores.

CONCLUSION: OS-SI% and mapping-derived myocardial entropy measures may serve as valuable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for assessing early myocardial alterations in patients with MDD-A.

articles.title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO).
articles.journal: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes.

METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

articles.title: Longitudinal analysis of structural biomarkers for disease progression in intermediate age-related macular degeneration: a MACUSTAR study report.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the prognostic impact of qualitative and quantitative structural biomarkers including their topographic distribution for progression to geographic atrophy (GA) or neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in eyes with intermediate AMD (iAMD) within the longitudinal part of the MACUSTAR study (NCT03349801).

DESIGN: Longitudinal, prospective low-interventional European multicenter cohort study.

SUBJECTS: 577 eyes of 577 study patients with iAMD.

METHODS: Study eyes with iAMD underwent multimodal retinal imaging at each study visit followed by a standardized grading of structural biomarkers, including presence of subretinal drusenoid deposits (SDDs), vitelliform lesion, pigmentary abnormalities (PAs), refractile deposits, pigment epithelium detachment (PED), non-exudative choroidal neovascularization (nCNV), incomplete (i) retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (RORA), complete (c) RORA, and hyperreflective foci presence (HRF). Automated assessment of the retinal pigment epithelium drusen complex (RPEDC) volume and HRF area including their topographic distribution based on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging was conducted using a deep-learning based algorithm. Disease progression (GA/nAMD) was assessed at each study visit up to a follow-up time of 4 years. Multivariable time-discrete hazard models were used to evaluate the biomarkers' relevance for disease progression in the entire OCT volume, the central 3 mm disk, and the central subfield of the Early Treatment Diabetes Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) Grid.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Disease progression to GA/nAMD, hazard ratios of structural biomarkers for disease progression RESULTS: A total of 577 study eyes of 577 iAMD study patients (mean age 72.01 ± 7.01 years, 66.1 % female, median follow-up 3 years) were included. Disease progression was detected in 82 eyes (9.01 %), 37 (6.4 %) progressed to GA, and 45 (7.7 %) to nAMD. Inside the central 3 mm presence of SDDs, PED, nCNV and cRORA conferred overall risk for progression, whereas PAs, RPEDC volume, iRORA, cRORA were associated with risk for progression to GA. Only nCNV volume increased risk for nAMD.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural biomarkers indicate risk for iAMD progression and may differentiate eyes progressing to GA from eyes progressing to nAMD. Biomarker topography impacts their prognostic relevance and needs to be considered in clinical trial design.

articles.title: Nailfold capillary alterations in pediatric asthma: evidence of peripheral microvascular involvement.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway vascular remodeling is well described in asthma, but whether it extends to the peripheral microcirculation is unknown. Nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) allows non-invasive assessment of the microvasculature.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate NVC findings in children with asthma and their associations with disease characteristics.

METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted in children aged 8-18 years with asthma at a tertiary pediatric allergy clinic. NVC was performed at 200 × magnification per the EULAR protocol. Findings were compared with age-specific reference values from healthy children using identical methodology.

RESULTS: Thirty-six children with asthma (mean age 12.01 ± 2.66 years; 66.7% male) were enrolled. Versus healthy references, patients had lower capillary density (p < 0.0001), with greater capillary loop diameter (p = 0.03) and width (p < 0.001). Dilated and tortuous capillaries were also more frequent (p < 0.003). Capillary density correlated inversely with BMI SDS (r = -0.33, p = 0.047). Moderate asthma was independently associated with lower capillary density (p = 0.03). Non-inhalant-sensitized patients had lower capillary density (p = 0.02), with greater capillary loop diameter (p = 0.01) and intercapillary distance (p = 0.03). Microhemorrhages (p < 0.01) as well as non-specific patterns (p = 0.02) were also more frequent in this group. Neither giant capillaries nor a scleroderma pattern was detected in any participant.

CONCLUSION: Children with asthma show distinct peripheral microvascular alterations on NVC, more pronounced with greater severity, higher BMI, and a non-atopic phenotype. NVC may enable non-invasive vascular phenotyping in pediatric asthma.

articles.title: S2 Sacral root Schwannoma: Laparoscopic Excision with ICG.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate intravenous ICG-assisted fluorescence mapping as an assistive tool for improving surgical precision and tissue differentiation during laparoscopic S2 root schwannoma excision.

SETTING: Tertiary center specializing in an advanced laparoscopic surgery.

PARTICIPANTS: A 63-year-old woman presented with severe left-sided S2 dermatomal and pudendal pain and progressive neurologic findings. Her surgical history was notable for prior excision of endometriosis. Preoperative T2-weighted pelvic MRI demonstrated a 3-cm intrapelvic mass arising from the left S2 sacral root, consistent with a schwannoma.

INTERVENTIONS: Laparoscopic excision of the S2 sacral root schwannoma was performed with intravenous ICG fluorescence mapping (0.25 mg/kg, 15 minutes pre-dissection) (1). Intraoperatively, the schwannoma demonstrated unexpectedly low fluorescence intensity relative to surrounding peripheral nerves and vascular structures, diverging from previously reported patterns of tumor hyperfluorescence. This hypofluorescence provided additional visual contrast alongside standard anatomic landmarks during dissection, without complication. At 6-month follow-up, electric shock-like pain had decreased and pudendal pain had improved from baseline. Deep tendon reflexes remained intact, and MRI confirmed no residual mass.

CONCLUSION: Pelvic schwannomas involving deep sacral nerve roots are rare and diagnostically challenging (2,3). This case highlights a stepwise neuropelveological approach (4) - from anatomic identification of the S2 root to interfascicular neurolysis and nerve-sparing excision - as a reproducible framework for safe laparoscopic management. Notably, ICG fluorescence mapping did not follow the expected pattern of tumor hyperfluorescence (5); the schwannoma instead appeared hypofluorescent relative to adjacent vascularized tissue.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential of lactate-based interventions in cardiac disease: metabolic and hemodynamic mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Lactate, once disregarded as metabolic waste, is now recognized as a metabolite with important roles in oxidative metabolism and cardiovascular physiology. Cardiomyocytes readily oxidize lactate, allowing it to serve as an efficient myocardial energy substrate. On this basis, exogenous lactate administration has been explored in acute cardiac disease. Across animal models and clinical studies, lactate infusion consistently increased cardiac output and improved perfusion. The underlying mechanisms varied with dose and disease state, but involved reduced afterload, enhanced myocardial contractility, and context-dependent chronotropic effects. Mechanistic data support arterial vasorelaxation, venous contraction, and positive inotropy, with links to myocardial energetics and immunometabolic signaling. Overall, available evidence supports lactate as a potential metabolic and hemodynamic adjunct, while highlighting the need for further studies.

articles.title: Distal Reinterventions after Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER): A Report from a Prospective Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER).

METHODS: From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months.

RESULTS: Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative).

CONCLUSIONS: Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

articles.title: Right Heart Failure Pheno-Endotype Drives Prognosis after Tricuspid Valve Surgery.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tricuspid valve surgery is neither complex nor time-consuming yet is associated with high surgical mortality. Our goal was to characterize heterogeneity of right heart variables and manifestations of right heart failure in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation and evaluate survival after tricuspid valve surgery.

METHODS: From 1/2007 to 1/2014, 522 adults with severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent cardiac surgery. Median follow-up was 3.7 years. Right heart morphology and function variables were measured de novo from stored echocardiographic images. To discover possible pheno-endotypes, unsupervised cluster analysis was performed by sidClustering.rfsrc using preoperative clinical, morphologic, ventricular function, and hemodynamic variables. Variable priority classification was used to characterize resulting pheno-endotypes. Post-surgery survival was assessed by cluster.

RESULTS: Three pheno-endotype clusters were identified, each with distinct 10-year survival: Cluster 1 (n=220), predominantly patients with left-sided disease, 59%; Cluster 2 (n=78), predominantly patients with the most dilated right ventricles (diastolic area 42±10 cm2), 46%; and Cluster 3 (n=224), predominantly patients with worse right ventricular dysfunction (fractional area change 30%±12%), 21% (worst prognosis). Elevated model for end-stage liver disease with sodium was the most important predictor of time-related mortality and separated Clusters 1 and 2 from Cluster 3.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients presenting for cardiac surgery with severe tricuspid regurgitation cluster into 3 pheno-endotypes, illustrating clinical presentation and patient heterogeneity and predicting distinctive prognosis. Right heart function and right heart failure severity need to be recognized to guide patient selection and management.

articles.title: MAF Transcription Factors: Emerging Key Players in Cardiovascular Health and Disease.
articles.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and their complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The regulatory role of transcription factors provides a crucial avenue for investigating the mechanisms underlying these diseases. The MAF transcription factor family is a key member of the AP-1 superfamily, comprising two subfamilies: large MAFs (including MAFA, MAFB, MAF [c-MAF], and NRL) and small MAFs (including MAFK, MAFG, and MAFF). Different members exhibit distinct cellular expression patterns and functions within tissues: small MAFs members show high expression in cardiac tissue, participating in core pathological processes such as myocardial antioxidant stress, inflammatory response, and lipid metabolism disorders. They are closely associated with common cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure, myocardial fibrosis, atherosclerosis, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Large MAFs are more widely distributed across other tissues and cell types. For instance, MAFB is primarily expressed in macrophages, pancreatic α-cells, neurons, and microglia. MAF regulates cell differentiation and immune responses in diverse tissues, including the lens, pancreas, and kidney. MAFA and NRL are specifically expressed in pancreatic β-cells and retinal photoreceptor cells, respectively. However, preliminary evidence suggests that large MAFs may play a significant role in maintaining physiological homeostasis and driving pathological progression within the cardiovascular system. Therefore, this review will first summarize research progress on small MAFs in the cardiovascular system, and then discuss the potential biological roles of large MAFs, particularly MAFB and MAF, in maintaining physiological homeostasis and driving pathological progression within the cardiovascular system. Finally, we lay out future paths for elucidating the roles of MAFs, particularly large MAFs, in the cardiovascular system.

articles.title: Effect of Microvascular Disease on Re-amputation Risk after Unilateral Amputation due to Diabetes or Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between manifestations of microvascular disease (MVD) and other factors on re-amputation risk within 12 months following incident unilateral lower extremity amputation.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 8 924 patients with first unilateral transmetatarsal, transtibial, or transfemoral amputation secondary to diabetes and or peripheral arterial disease, identified through a Veterans Affairs database. Re-amputation was defined as any subsequent ipsilateral soft tissue or bony revision or amputation to a higher level. The presence of MVD was determined using a composite variable that required the involvement of each subcomponent (neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy), and also by evaluating each of the subcomponent MVD variables separately. Twenty-nine additional risk factors were evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of re-amputation. A competing risk analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of re-amputation. The effect of risk factors on re-amputation risk was estimated by computing subdistribution hazard ratios (sub-HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The twelve month re-amputation risk was 38.0% (transmetatarsal), 27.2% (transtibial), and 14.1% (transfemoral). The combined MVD variable was not significantly associated with re-amputation risk. However, re-amputation after transmetatarsal amputation was significantly elevated in patients with retinopathy, leukocytosis, or those who were on kidney dialysis, with the highest risk in those with all three (sub-HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.8 - 2.6). Similarly, for transtibial patients, the risk was higher in the presence of retinopathy, leukocytosis, and kidney dialysis, and in those with a prior ipsilateral revascularisation and those on warfarin. The highest risk was observed in those with all factors present (sub-HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.7).

CONCLUSION: This study identified an important association between the pre-amputation diagnosis of retinopathy and risk for subsequent failure of primary healing and need for re-amputation. Presence of retinopathy should be considered when evaluating potential failure of healing during amputation level decisions.

articles.title: Outcomes of Total Endovascular Repair of Aortic Arch and Thoraco-abdominal Aortic Aneurysms in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group in a Selected Group of Patients with Extensive Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to report outcomes of total endovascular aortic repair (TEAR) using arch branched endovascular aortic repair (aBEVAR) and thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).

METHODS: Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included. The primary outcome was aortic related mortality (ARM). Secondary outcomes included stroke and or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), spinal cord ischaemia (SCI), and freedom from target artery (TA) instability, re-interventions, and new cardiovascular events (CVEs) within 1 year.

RESULTS: Of 98 patients scheduled for TEAR, 95 (97%) completed both stages, including 46 (48%) with chronic post-dissection aneurysms and 49 (52%) with degenerative aneurysms. A multistage approach with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was used in all patients, with a median interval between stages of 11 months (interquartile range [IQR] 5, 14). One (1%) rupture occurred between the staged procedures (successfully managed with off the shelf TAAA multibranch stent graft). Custom made and off the shelf TAAA FBEVAR devices were used in 79 (83%) and 16 (17%) patients, respectively. There were 12 (13%) stroke and or TIAs (aBEVAR, ten; TAAA FBEVAR, two); five (5%) had a modified Rankin Scale score > 3. Sixteen patients (17%) experienced SCI (aBEVAR, two; TAAA FBEVAR, 14) with three cases (3%) of paraplegia. Four patients (4%) died within thirty days; these were the only cases of ARM. Median follow up was 32 months (IQR 3, 61). Of 67 patients (71%) with available one year follow up, there were six (9%) with TA instability and five (7%) CVEs. Estimated three year survival was 79 ± 5% with a cumulative incidence of re-intervention of 31 ± 6%.

CONCLUSION: Multistage TEAR with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was associated with low ARM, re-intervention, and TA instability. Stroke and SCI remain significant and must be carefully weighed during patient selection and treatment.

articles.title: Tetramethylpyrazine enhances angiogenesis in diabetic hindlimb ischemia by modulating the THBS1/PI3K/AKT signaling axis and reversing aberrant expression of MFN1/FIS1-related mitochondrial fusion-fission proteins.
articles.abstract: [BACKGROUND]: Type 1 diabetes with hindlimb ischemia (T1DM-HLI) is a prevalent diabetic microvascular complication characterized by impaired angiogenesis. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) demonstrates therapeutic potential in vascular disorders, but its role in T1DM-HLI remains unclear. [PURPOSE]: This study investigates the protective effect of TMP on impaired angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI and underlying mechanisms. [METHODS]: We evaluated TMP's effects on angiogenesis, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial fusion/fission balance in streptozotocin-induced and femoral artery-ligated T1DM-HLI mice and high-glucose-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). RNA sequencing identified key molecular mechanisms. Molecular docking predicted an interaction between TMP and thrombospondin-1 (THBS1). We show that TMP rescues impaired angiogenesis and disordered mitochondrial dynamics, effects possibly mediated through suppression of THBS1 and activation of the PI3K/AKT axis. [RESULTS]: TMP restored hindlimb perfusion and promoted vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA)-driven angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI mice, while enhancing HUVEC proliferation, migration, and tube formation. It attenuated oxidative stress and reversed aberrant expression of proteins to mitochondrial fusion and fission. RNA sequencing revealed the THBS1/PI3K/AKT axis may play a central role in mediating the therapeutic effects of TMP. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between TMP and THBS1, identifying THBS1 as a candidate target of TMP. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed TMP treatment reduced THBS1 expression and increased PI3K and AKT phosphorylation. [CONCLUSION]: Our findings demonstrate that TMP may reverse dysregulated expression of mitochondrial fusion-fission proteins and enhance angiogenesis in T1DM-HLI by inhibiting THBS1 and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway, supporting TMP as a therapeutic candidate for diabetic hindlimb ischemia.

articles.title: Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of the Novel Vancomycin Derivative LYSC98.
articles.abstract: LYSC98 is a novel synthetic derivative from chemical modification of vancomycin. In this study, the antibacterial efficacy of LYSC98 was systematically evaluated against multiple clinically significant pathogens using Minimal Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) determination and murine systemic and neutropenic thigh infection models. LYSC98 was active against Gram-positive strains, with MICs generally higher or comparable to vancomycin against vancomycin susceptible isolates; however, it demonstrated elevated activity against vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE), with MICs more than 8 folds lower than vancomycin. In both animal models, LYSC98 was active against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (VISA), penicillin-intermediate S. pneumoniae (PISP), penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae (PRSP), and VRE. In the systemic infection model, the median effective doses (ED50s) of LYSC98 against MRSA, VISA, PISP, PRSP, and VRE strains were significantly lower than those of vancomycin, and either not significantly different from or significantly lower than those of teicoplanin. In the neutropenic thigh infection model, two intravenous administrations of LYSC98 at 2, 4, and 8 mg/kg achieved 2.30-4.93 log10 CFU/thigh reductions against MRSA strains relative to the 24 h infection control, significantly greater than vancomycin at the corresponding doses; relative to the bacterial burden at the start of therapy (2 h control), net killing was achieved at 4 and 8 mg/kg against both strains, whereas at 2 mg/kg the burden remained at or above baseline. These results indicate that, within the strains, doses and models tested, LYSC98 is active against the Gram-positive species examined and is more effective than vancomycin in selected infection models.

articles.title: Resolving the dual nature of NADPH oxidase 4 in cardiac fibrosis for selective therapeutic targeting: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a common route leading to heart failure and arrhythmia. However, there are no cardio-selective antifibrotic drugs currently approved. NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), which predominantly produces hydrogen peroxide and requires no cytosolic activator subunits, is regulated by expression, protein stability and post-translational modification. Its intracellular organelle localisation makes it a potential redox-medicine target. Setanaxib, the first dual NOX1/NOX4 inhibitor under clinical development, is not NOX4-selective and remains unapproved. This narrative review of MEDLINE literature presents genetic, mechanistic, pharmacological and clinical evidence of associations between NOX4 and cardiac fibrosis in cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, including effects of cardiovascular drugs. NOX4 can have pro-fibrotic effects through TGF-β1/Smad activation, regulated cardiomyocyte death, inflammatory signals and atrial/ventricular ion-channel remodelling. Yet, genetic studies report divergent findings reflective of context-dependent influences. NOX4 in the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes may promote autophagy and survival, whereas persistent high NOX4-derived ROS in stressed myocardium results in mitochondrial injury and fibrosis. Endothelial NOX4 seems mainly protective. Dual NOX1/NOX4 inhibition and preferential NOX4-targeting have been shown to have antifibrotic effects in pre-clinical cardiac models, although there is no clinical evidence. Divergences may be explained on four axes: ROS level, subcellular compartment, cell type and disease-state. A reasonable approach to translating NOX4-targeted pharmacology into cardiac antifibrotic therapy would be to adopt strategies that are specific to compartment and cell type.

articles.title: Sinomenine pretreatment ameliorates septic acute lung injury through α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-dependent inhibition of glycocalyx degradation and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is an organ dysfunction syndrome driven by microbial invasion, characterized by endothelial barrier damage, microcirculatory failure, and hyper-inflammation. Sinomenine (SIN), an alkaloid from Sinomenium acutum, has been demonstrated to alleviate sepsis by suppressing inflammation and modulating metabolism. However, its effects on the endothelial barrier and its underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. This study explores the effects of SIN on the endothelial glycocalyx and endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) in septic acute lung injury (ALI) and elucidates the critical role of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP). The sepsis model was induced via cecal ligation and puncture, and cellular inflammation was modeled in HUVECs and RAW264.7 cells with LPS. IHC, ELISA, and Evans blue assay were employed to assess pulmonary glycocalyx degradation and vascular permeability. Molecular docking and Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) were performed to validate the interaction between SIN and α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. WB and qRT-PCR were used to detect CAP, EndMT, and inflammation markers. These assays showed that SIN can directly bind to α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor in a manner analogous to acetylcholine (ACh), while exhibiting a more sustained anti-inflammatory effect. SIN pretreatment activates the CAP by upregulating CAP-related molecules to inhibit the inflammatory response, downregulates the glycocalyx-degrading enzymes HPSE and MMP9 to reduce glycocalyx degradation, and inhibits TGF-β/NOX4-mediated EndMT. However, AAV6-mediated specific knockdown of pulmonary Chrna7 significantly weakened these effects. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that SIN pretreatment alleviates ALI and endothelial barrier damage by inhibiting α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor-dependent glycocalyx degradation and EndMT.

articles.title: Pharmacological activation of vitamin D receptor by paricalcitol attenuates ferroptosis-associated myocardial injury after ischemia-reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and characterized by oxidative damage to membrane phospholipids. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis contributes to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI), a condition that worsens cardiac damage following restoration of blood flow to the ischemic myocardium. This study aimed to investigate the role of ferroptosis in MIRI and to determine whether pharmacological activation of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) by paricalcitol modulates ferroptosis-associated cardiac injury. Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion was induced in mice by transient ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery followed by reperfusion. Cardiac function was evaluated by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Ferroptosis-related pathways were analyzed through transcriptional profiling of antioxidant and iron-regulating genes, lipidomic assessment of oxidized phospholipid species, and ultrastructural mitochondrial evaluation. Complementary in vitro experiments were performed using human AC16 cardiomyocyte-like cells under ferroptotic stress. Ischemia-reperfusion led to a sustained deterioration of cardiac structure and function and induced several alterations consistent with ferroptosis activation, including changes in ferroptosis-related gene expression, accumulation of oxidized phospholipid species, and mitochondrial structural abnormalities. Pharmacological activation of VDR by paricalcitol attenuated ferroptosis-related transcriptional alterations, reduced lipid peroxidation, and mitigated mitochondrial structural damage, collectively limiting ferroptosis-associated cardiomyocyte injury and early ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction. These findings suggest that VDR activation limits ferroptosis-associated cardiac injury during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion and may represent a pharmacologically relevant strategy to mitigate cardiac damage linked to ferroptosis.

articles.title: Host life history traits as drivers of viral infection in European bats.
articles.abstract: Bats are recognized as natural reservoirs of a wide range of viruses. Understanding the factors that determine patterns of viral occurrence in reservoir species, particularly viral richness and viral detection frequency, is essential for explaining host-pathogen dynamics and anticipating public health risks. In this study, we evaluated the influence of life-history traits on viral frequency (defined as the proportion of positive detections across studies) in European bats for six important viral groups (Adenoviridae, Herpesviridae, Papillomaviridae, Filoviridae, Coronaviridae, and the genus Lyssavirus within Rhabdoviridae) through a systematic review, identifying 7,037 publications, of which 155 met the inclusion criteria. These studies focused primarily on three species: Cnephaeus serotinus, Myotis daubentonii, and Pipistrellus pipistrellus. We detected a phylogenetic signal in viral frequency only for the family Adenoviridae and genus Betacoronavirus, suggesting that these viral groups have a particular evolutionary affinity with their hosts. Viral frequency was associated with bats' environmental breadth and body size, although these relationships were not consistent across all viral groups. Instead, each viral group was associated with a distinct set of host life-history traits, reflecting -most probably- differences in their ecology and evolutionary history. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the ecological drivers of viral frequency are virus-specific rather than universal.

articles.title: Control of M. tuberculosis infection requires CD28 to generate lung-homing T cells and CTLA-4 to limit immunopathology.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb)-specific CD4 T cells differentiate into protective lung parenchyma-homing and non-protective intravascular subsets, but the signals that instruct these fates are poorly understood. Here we show that CD28 co-stimulation regulates host protection during Mtb infection. Cd28-/- mice are susceptible to Mtb infection, displaying higher bacterial loads and reduced survival compared to wild type mice. Cd28-/- Mtb-specific T cells expand normally but are skewed towards the lung intravascular phenotype. CD4 T cells primed in the absence of CD28 co-stimulation in B7 deficient hosts are unable to confer protection upon adoptive transfer into B7WT Mtb-infected T cell deficient mice, despite restoration of CD28:B7 signaling in the recipients. B7-1/2 expression by infected lung macrophages is not required for bacterial control, suggesting that B7:CD28 interactions in the T cell priming phase are required for host protection. In contrast to CD28 deficiency, lack of CTLA-4 increases lung parenchymal Mtb-specific CD4 T cell responses. However, CTLA-4 is required on both effector and Treg cells to limit detrimental host responses during Mtb infection. These findings show that the B7/CD28/CTLA-4 axis is central to host protection in Mtb infection, as it drives differentiation of protective T cells and limits detrimental inflammation by otherwise protective T cells.

articles.title: Current status of the watch-and-wait organ preservation strategy in rectal cancer in Spain: Results of a national survey. On behalf of the Spanish Association of Coloproctology.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Organ preservation strategies, particularly the watch-and-wait (W&W) approach in rectal cancer, have gained increasing international interest in recent years. However, their implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions. The aim of this study was to evaluate the degree of use of W&W in hospitals across Spain.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted through a national survey addressed to general surgeons involved in rectal cancer management. The questionnaire was designed using Google Forms® and distributed through the Spanish Association of Surgeons (AEC) and the Spanish Association of Coloproctology (AECP). The development of the survey followed the methodological recommendations of the Checklist for Reporting Of Survey Studies (CROSS). The statistical analysis included descriptive statistics and a univariate analysis to identify factors associated with the use of W&W.

RESULTS: A total of 154 valid responses were obtained. Among respondents, 102 surgeons (66%) considered W&W a safe strategy. Seventy (45%) reported offering W&W in a protocolized manner, while 40 (26%) applied it without a formal protocol. Forty-four participants (29%) did not offer this option, and opposition from the multidisciplinary tumor board was the main limiting factor (30 cases, 60%). Univariate analysis showed that W&W use was associated with specialized colorectal units (P =  .001), national accreditation as a colorectal unit (P =  .01), and higher case volume (P = .02). Most survey participants (92.3%) emphasized the need for further education and training in W&W and rectal cancer.

CONCLUSIONS: The implementation of W&W in Spain remains limited and heterogeneous. Enhanced training and standardized criteria may facilitate broader implementation.
