Clinical Characteristics, 90-Day Functional Outcomes, Antimicrobial Susceptibility, and Exploratory Genomic Analysis of Invasive Human Streptococcus suis Infection: A Multicenter Retrospective Study in China.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Streptococcus suis is a zoonotic pathogen; survivors of invasive infection may have persistent auditory or vestibular sequelae. To address limited multicenter evidence from China, we characterized 90-day outcomes, antimicrobial susceptibility, and exploratory genomic findings.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 34 patients with invasive S. suis infection at eight hospitals in four Chinese provinces (2017-2025). Unfavorable outcome was defined as death within 90 days or persistent sequelae at day 90. Minimum inhibitory concentrations were reinterpreted using CLSI viridans-group streptococcal surrogate breakpoints; six recoverable isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing.

RESULTS: Acute cochleovestibular involvement occurred in 11/27 (40.7%) patients with meningitis and 0/7 with nonmeningitic bacteremia/sepsis. Unfavorable outcomes occurred in 17/34 (50.0%) patients, including two deaths; 12/32 (37.5%) survivors had hearing-related sequelae. Acute cochleovestibular involvement was more frequent among patients with unfavorable outcomes (64.7% versus 0%; P < 0.001). All evaluable isolates were susceptible to penicillin (21/21), cefotaxime (19/19), and ceftriaxone (5/5). Resistance was observed in 17/20, 16/20, and 20/20 isolates tested for erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline, respectively. Sequence types were ST1 (n = 3), ST7 (n = 2), and ST25 (n = 1); epf and sly were each detected in five isolates, and mrp in four.

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial hearing-related morbidity supports structured audiological follow-up. Clinical associations and genomic findings remain exploratory and do not establish independent prognostic value or genotype-phenotype causality.

articles.title: International comparison of neurosyphilis-related guidance for lumbar puncture, CSF interpretation, treatment, and follow-up: a systematic review.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare international neurosyphilis guidance across lumbar puncture (LP), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) interpretation, treatment, and follow-up.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and official sources for guidance documents containing adult neurosyphilis recommendations, published or updated from January 1, 2003, through September 2, 2026. Two reviewers independently coded clinical recommendations, and four appraisers independently assessed guideline quality using AGREE II.

RESULTS: Thirty-two guidance sets were included. Preferred penicillin therapy was specified in 29/32 (90.6%) and serologic follow-up in 30/32 (93.8%). LP was recommended for neurologic presentations in 25/32 (78.1%), but for ocular and otic syphilis in 14/32 (43.8%) each; none recommended LP solely for a high serum nontreponemal titre or HIV infection. CSF nontreponemal and treponemal testing were addressed in 21/32 (65.6%) and 18/32 (56.3%). CSF white blood cell count and protein were each mentioned in 22/32 (68.8%), whereas explicit adult numeric thresholds were provided in 14/32 (43.8%) and 9/32 (28.1%). Repeat CSF assessment was recommended in 12/32 (37.5%) and conditionally recommended in 8/32 (25.0%). Median AGREE II scores were highest for clarity of presentation (89.6%) and scope and purpose (82.6%) and lowest for editorial independence (35.4%) and rigour of development (41.1%).

CONCLUSIONS: Penicillin-based preferred regimens were widely specified, whereas guidance remained heterogeneous for LP decisions, CSF interpretation, and post-treatment monitoring. For ocular or otic syphilis, recommendations for neurosyphilis-level treatment should be distinguished from recommendations for baseline LP.

articles.title: Clinical Features and Real-World Management of Enterococcus faecium Infective Endocarditis: A Nationwide Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enterococcus faecium infective endocarditis (IE) is uncommon, therapeutically challenging, and poorly characterized. We aimed to define its clinical phenotype, outcomes, and treatment patterns.

METHODS: We performed a prospective multicenter observational study using the Spanish GAMES registry. Episodes of E. faecium IE diagnosed from 2008 through 2024 were compared with IE caused by other etiologies.

RESULTS: Among 7014 episodes of IE, 71 (1.0%) were caused by E. faecium. Compared with other etiologies, patients with E. faecium IE were older, had a greater comorbidity burden, and more often had nosocomial acquisition. This syndrome more frequently involved native valves and was associated with more acute kidney injury, but fewer intracardiac complications and lower surgical requirements, although mortality did not differ when compared with other pathogens. Sepsis and surgery indicated but not performed were risk factors for in-hospital death. Treatment was heterogeneous, utilizing several distinct regimens whose clinical use in IE is newly reported.

CONCLUSIONS: E. faecium infective endocarditis predominantly affects frail, healthcare-exposed patients and has a distinctive phenotype characterized by native-valve predominance, frequent renal complications, and fewer intracardiac lesions, yet persistently high mortality. These findings help define the clinical profile of this entity and support evaluation of alternative treatment strategies.

articles.title: Targeting coagulation factor XI/XIa for anticoagulation therapy: from mechanism to drug development.
articles.abstract: Coagulation Factor XI (FXI) and its activated form FXIa have been identified as important regulators of thrombin amplification, contributing substantially to pathological thrombosis while exerting a relatively limited role in physiological hemostasis, making it an attractive target for low-hemorrhagic antithrombotic therapy. In recent years, FXI/FXIa-targeted therapeutics have rapidly advanced in clinical trials and represent a promising strategy for precision anticoagulation. This review systematically summarizes the structural features, biological functions, and mechanistic roles of FXI/FXIa in thrombosis, followed by structure-guided drug design, major therapeutic modalities, and clinical translation. Clinical evidence is critically evaluated to highlight both the opportunities and limitations of FXI/FXIa-targeted therapies across different thrombotic indications. Furthermore, key challenges, including selectivity optimization, disease-dependent efficacy, and the physiological functions of FXI beyond coagulation, are discussed. A more comprehensive understanding of FXI biology will be essential for defining the long-term safety, therapeutic window and clinical positioning of FXI/FXIa-targeted anticoagulants.

articles.title: HSP27, cell stress, and hormesis: From mammals to humanized yeast models.
articles.abstract: Hormesis is a biphasic dose-response phenomenon characterized by beneficial or stimulatory effects at low exposure levels to a stressor, followed by inhibitory or toxic effects at higher doses. This effect is related to the level of oxidative stress in the cell. Human HSPB1 (HSP27) is a small heat shock protein involved in the oxidative stress response, whose overexpression correlates with increased longevity in mammalian models. HSP27 protects neurons from damage caused by protein aggregation observed in neurodegenerative diseases; however, this same survival capability also favors tumor cells, hindering chemotherapeutic treatment. This review describes HSP27 and demonstrates that the humanized yeast model can aid in understanding the function of this protein, which protects neurons and enhances tumor survival. HSP27 exhibits a dose-dependent hormetic effect when expressed at varying levels in yeast. This expression-dependent response enhances longevity, proteasome activity, and resistance to thermal and oxidative stresses. The humanized yeast model may help elucidate the relationship between the quaternary structure of the protein and its hormetic effect. In addition, the humanization of partial or complete pathways involved in both neurodegenerative diseases and apoptosis may provide a way to identify small molecules that enhance neuronal protection and potentially inhibit HSP27's pro-survival function in cancer treatment.

articles.title: Epidemiological modeling and optimal intervention strategies for seasonal scrub typhus infection in human population mediated by mites and rodents.
articles.abstract: Scrub typhus is a re-emerging vector-borne disease of significant public health concern, particularly in endemic regions where seasonal factors strongly influence transmission dynamics. Individuals engaged in agricultural and field-based activities are particularly vulnerable to increased exposure to infected mites, especially during the monsoon season, thereby underscoring the importance of adopting appropriate preventive measures to reduce transmission risk. Motivated by this, we developed a mathematical model with optimal control to describe the transmission dynamics of scrub typhus in humans, incorporating a seasonally varying transmission rate in the human population. The proposed model ensures positivity and boundedness of solutions, with disease persistence characterized by the basic reproduction number and equilibrium stability examined analytically. The scrub typhus incidence data from Mizoram, India, spanning January 2021 to December 2022 is utilized for data fitting and estimation. It is found that the proposed full model outperforms the sub-models in terms of goodness-of-fit statistics, with AIC (234.71), AICc (251.63), and BIC (246.49) and Akaike weight (0.84505), thereby providing stronger support for its selection. It is found that scrub typhus infection dynamics are highly sensitive to the β2 and β3 transmission rates, where the infection peak is observed during the monsoon season. This study may provide valuable information to guide policymakers in implementing evidence-based approaches for the prevention and control of scrub typhus infection.

articles.title: Monkeypox on a disc: Portable centrifugal microfluidic platform for multi-assay colorimetric LAMP.
articles.abstract: Monkeypox is currently the most important orthopoxvirus infection in humans. The increase in the number of cases, combined with its potential social impact and international spread, led the World Health Organization (WHO) to classify it as the most recent Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Although mainly endemic in resource-limited countries, quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) remains the gold standard for detection but is challenging due to the need for specialized instrumentation. To address this, we propose an instrument-friendly molecular assay based on colorimetric Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP), performed on a multi-assay polystyrene-toner (PST) centrifugal device. The new analytical device was designed to include chambers for loading the LAMP mixture and samples, interconnected channels for mixing them, and separate chambers for simultaneous LAMP amplification and visual detection of each sample. When evaluated in a panel of real clinical samples, compared to qPCR, the assay based on visual detection demonstrated 100.00% specificity, 91.67% sensitivity, and 95.83% accuracy, which increased to 100% accuracy when digital image analysis was employed, with a total analysis time of approximately 60 min. The relative simplicity of the assay may facilitate its implementation in resource-limited settings and contribute to expanding access to molecular detection of monkeypox.

articles.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitor use during or after acute kidney injury and the risk of major adverse kidney events and Mortality: A systematic review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and pharmacologic strategies to improve outcomes after AKI remain limited. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have established cardiovascular and renal benefits, but their role during or after AKI remains less clearly defined.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420261298733). Six databases were searched through February 9, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with established AKI, compared SGLT2i use with control or nonuse, and reported at least one clinical outcome. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse kidney events (MAKE). Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and odds ratios (ORs) from crude event counts for MAKE.

RESULTS: Seven studies were included (six observational, one randomized). SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.59-0.71; I2 = 32%; three cohorts) and lower odds of MAKE (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.88; I2 = 91%; five studies), but the MAKE estimate was not robust to exclusion of individual studies and MAKE definitions varied. Kidney replacement therapy (two studies) was not pooled. The randomized trial (n = 200) was inconclusive for mortality (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.12-1.29) and MAKE (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.52-1.67). Certainty of evidence was very low.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use during or after AKI was associated with lower mortality and MAKE in observational studies (very low certainty of evidence), whereas the only randomized trial was too small to be conclusive. Confounding by indication is likely, and the evidence remains limited by heterogeneity and the predominance of observational data. Randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Personalised dupilumab therapy in severe asthma: real-world dosing interval prolongation among early responders.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In severe uncontrolled asthma, dupilumab has been shown to reduce exacerbations and symptom burden. In other type 2 conditions, the dosing interval has been successfully prolonged while maintaining disease control.

OBJECTIVE: Here, we aim to assess if dupilumab dosing intervals can be prolonged in severe asthma while maintaining disease control.

METHODS: 24 dupilumab early responders underwent a trial of dosing interval prolongation. We assessed spirometry, symptom control and exacerbations at baseline pre-biologic(Visit(V)1), post biologic with the licensed 2 week dosing(V2) and then following prolonging the dosing interval(V3). Bonferroni corrected pairwise comparisons were made between time points.

RESULTS: Mean (SEM) baseline demographics were: age 50.4 years (2.9); BMI 30.6kg/m2(1.00). No patients were on maintenance OCS. The median duration between V1-V2 was 6.7 months followed by 8.6 months between V2-V3. The median(range) prolonged dosing interval at V3 was 4(2-6) weeks. There were significant differences for all outcomes comparing V1 vs either V2 or V3, but no significant difference between V2 vs V3. The mean(95%CI) values for V1, V2 and V3 respectively were: FEV1 % predicted 79.3% (70.6, 88.1), 93.5%(86.8, 100.2) and 94.2% (87.2, 101.1); FeNO 94.1ppb (73.0, 115.2), 22.8ppb (17.7, 27.9) and 24.9ppb (17.7, 30.6); Eosinophils 857cells/μL (697, 1017), 473 cells/μL (336, 610) and 500 cells/μL (344, 656); ACQ-6 3.0 (2.6, 3.6), 0.7 (0.5, 0.9) and 0.5 (0.3, 0.6); AER 3.8 (3.0, 4.5), 0.0 and 0.0.

CONCLUSION: The majority of dupilumab early responders were able to successfully prolong their dosing interval while maintaining disease control. This in turn may have implications for drug costs and patient convenience.

articles.title: A Link Between Immunoglobulin M Levels and Overwhelming Post-Splenectomy Infection Risk in a National Asplenia Cohort.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI) is a rare complication of asplenia that is frequently fatal. OPSI risk remains elevated in patients with asplenia who receive the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP)-recommended vaccines, suggesting additional variables influence OPSI risk.

OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical and immunologic factors associated with OPSI in individuals with anatomic or functional asplenia.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of 2,992 individuals with physician-confirmed anatomic or functional asplenia and identified 47 OPSI cases. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were analyzed to identify independent risk factors for OPSI. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed predictive values of immunoglobulin levels, and time from asplenia index date to OPSI was summarized among cases.

RESULTS: Streptococcus pneumoniae accounted for 89% of OPSI episodes. Prior to OPSI, most patients had documented receipt of asplenia-targeted vaccines corresponding to the bacterial species causing their specific infections. IgM <61.5 mg/dL was present in 86.7% (39/45) and 15.0% (164/1093) of patients with and without OPSI, respectively (p<0.001). In adjusted analysis, IgM <61.5 mg/dL (aOR 26.05 [9.28-73.13], p<0.001) was associated with OPSI. Serum IgM discriminated between patients with and without (AUC 0.92) with a cutoff of <61.5 mg/dL demonstrating an 86.7% sensitivity and 85.0% specificity for OPSI.

CONCLUSION: Low serum IgM was strongly associated with OPSI and may help identify patients requiring closer surveillance and management.

articles.title: Mepolizumab reduces oral corticosteroid use across distinct severe asthma phenotypes: 2-year REALITI-A study.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids (OCS) remain widely used in the treatment of severe asthma despite their adverse effects. Add-on biologic therapy offers the potential for minimizing OCS exposure.

OBJECTIVE: This post hoc analysis of REALITI-A assessed the effect of mepolizumab on OCS use among subgroups of patients with severe asthma based on allergic/omalizumab-eligible phenotype and type-2 biomarker status.

METHODS: REALITI-A was a prospective 2-year observational study among adults initiating mepolizumab for severe asthma. Endpoints assessed at 2 years were: change from baseline in daily maintenance OCS (mOCS) and total OCS dose, the proportion of patients discontinuing mOCS, the proportion of patients with 0 mg/day daily mOCS and total OCS dose, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 scores, and clinically significant exacerbations. Outcomes were stratified by prior omalizumab use, omalizumab eligibility, baseline blood eosinophil count (threshold [<300/≥300 cells/μL] and category [<150/≥150-<300/≥300-<500/≥500 cells/μL]), baseline immunoglobulin E (IgE; <60/≥60-<190/≥190-<550/≥550 KU/L), atopic status (yes/no/unknown) and baseline fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO; <25/≥25-<50/≥50 parts per billion).

RESULTS: Overall, 822 patients were included, with 39% receiving mOCS at baseline. For both mOCS and total OCS, median dose reductions after 2 years from baseline were 70-100% across all subgroups. Also, after 2 years, 44-71% of patients across subgroups had discontinued mOCS and 37-68% had 0 mg total OCS dose.

CONCLUSION: These data highlight mepolizumab's effectiveness in reducing real-world OCS use across a broad range of patients with severe asthma, irrespective of omalizumab eligibility and baseline blood eosinophil count, IgE, atopic status, and FeNO.

articles.title: Statins and chronic liver disease progression: methodological concerns about time-dependent exposure and model specification.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: Evaluating skeletal muscle in chronic liver disease: remaining challenges.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle alterations are increasingly recognized as determinants of prognosis in chronic liver disease, and computed tomography (CT) has made their assessment widely accessible. However, interpretation of these measurements raises several challenges. First, myosteatosis is usually inferred from low CT muscle attenuation, which has not been validated against intramuscular fat content in cirrhosis. Second, muscle alterations may differ according to the aetiology of liver disease, and studies pooling aetiologies may obscure aetiology-specific patterns. Third, "sarcopenia" is frequently incorrectly used for low muscle mass alone, whereas incorporating muscle function, better predicts adverse outcomes in chronic liver disease. Addressing these issues is necessary before muscle quality can become a reliable clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Delphi Consensus on Periprosthetic Surgical Irrigation: Irrigation Solution Selection and Comparative Effectiveness.
Sterile Dilute Povidone-Iodine Irrigation in Orthopaedic Surgery: Evidence, Consensus, and Future Directions.
Physical activity levels two years after total knee arthroplasty and preoperative patient characteristics: a secondary analysis of the MOVE randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: At one year after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), patients are less physically active than age-matched peers, but physical activity (PA) trajectories two years after TKA are unclear. This study examined PA levels from baseline to two years post-TKA, quantified return to baseline PA levels over time, and evaluated associations between baseline participant characteristics and post-TKA PA levels.

METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial. Participants (n = 135) aged 50 to 85 years undergoing primary unilateral TKA wore accelerometers preoperatively and 10 weeks, six months, and two years post-TKA to characterize light PA, moderate-vigorous PA (MVPA), and steps/day. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize PA levels. Repeated measures models estimated PA levels over time. The percentage of participants who returned to or exceeded baseline PA levels over time was quantified. Multivariate logistic regressions modeled return to baseline PA levels over time to evaluate associations with baseline participant characteristics. All models controlled for age, sex, and treatment group.

RESULTS: There was an increase of 8% steps/day and 0.75% MVPA from baseline to two years post-TKA. At two years post-TKA, 54.2, 53.1, and 55.6% of participants returned to baseline light PA, MVPA, and steps/day levels. Higher baseline PA levels were associated with lower odds of returning to baseline levels at all timepoints for MVPA (10 weeks odds ratio (95% confidence interval): 0.62 (0.46 to 0.84); six months: 0.55 (0.40 to 0.76); two years: 0.52 (0.36 to 0.75)), as well as light PA and steps/day (all P-values < 0.05). Baseline body mass index, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index scores, and Functional Comorbidity Index were associated inconsistently with PA levels.

CONCLUSION: While on average, PA levels increased from baseline to two years post-TKA, participants who have higher baseline PA levels had reduced odds of returning to the same level. These findings suggest TKA and current rehabilitation may not fully address PA, and additional support (e.g., behavioral guidance or tailored rehabilitation) may be needed.

articles.title: Delphi Consensus on Periprosthetic Surgical Irrigation: Product Preparation, Sterility, and Implementation.
Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched 1:3 to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including periprosthetic joint infection and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.

Delphi Consensus on Periprosthetic Surgical Irrigation: Clinical Evidence, Indications, and Recommendations.
Delphi Consensus on Periprosthetic Surgical Irrigation: Technique and Intraoperative Administration.
Mannose attenuates CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by reducing oxidative stress through AMPK-dependent NRF2 signaling.
articles.abstract: Mannose, a naturally occurring hexose, has been implicated in the regulation of metabolism and inflammation. Although emerging evidence suggests its therapeutic potential in liver diseases, the mechanisms by which mannose modulates liver fibrosis, particularly in relation to oxidative stress, remain poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of mannose in liver fibrosis and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. A CCl4-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis was established with mannose administered in drinking water. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to explore potential mechanisms. Hepatic oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) signaling were evaluated. NRF2 function was assessed using the inhibitor ML385 in vivo and in primary mouse hepatocytes (PMH). The involvement of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) was further examined in PMH using Compound C. The results showed that mannose markedly attenuated liver fibrosis and injury, accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and decreased inflammatory and pro-fibrotic mediators. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses indicated enhanced NRF2 signaling in mannose-treated livers. ML385 largely abolished the protective effects of mannose in vivo and in vitro, supporting a functional role of NRF2 signaling. Mechanistically, mannose increased AMPK phosphorylation, whereas Compound C suppressed NRF2 signaling and reversed its antioxidant effects. Moreover, conditioned medium from mannose-treated PMH attenuated hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, suggesting that mannose primarily protects hepatocytes and indirectly limits HSC activation. Mannose alleviates liver fibrosis by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation, at least in part through an AMPK-dependent NRF2 signaling pathway. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the anti-fibrotic effects of mannose and support further investigation of its potential as a nutritional intervention for liver disease.

articles.title: Equity in Asthma Research: A Meta-Analysis on Participant Diversity in U.S. Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The increasing diagnosis of asthma in the United States has disproportionately affected historically marginalized groups, leading to higher healthcare costs and more missed days due to illness. Despite ongoing improvements, there is a significant gap in comprehensive diversity analyses within current clinical trials for asthma.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the degree of relevant demographic reporting in current clinical trials concerning asthma.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the reported sex, age, and race/ethnicity of participants in all asthma-related clinical trials in the U.S. published from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2023. We extracted all clinical trials for sex, age, and race. A participation-to-disease representation ratio (PDRR) was determined for each demographic and qualitative assessment was determined from the summation of the score.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of the initial 1757 search returns, 116 were eligible for full-screen extraction based on our criteria. In regard to sex, 39 trials (39/116, 33.6%) have an overall representation rating of Good. Only 1 trial (1/116, 0.8%) was given a rating of Good for overall race/ethnicity representation. Age group data was rarely reported, with only 2 trials (2/116, 1.7%) reporting inclusion of older adults.

CONCLUSIONS: While current U.S.-based asthma clinical trials are making noticeable progress in sex/gender inclusivity, there are still significant shortcomings in the inclusion and reporting of non-white racial and ethnic groups. It is imperative that future asthma clinical trials address this limitation to ensure equitable treatment for all populations.

articles.title: Predicting Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-associated Interstitial Lung Disease: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating Quantitative CT and Clinical Features.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognosis of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD) is poor, and current strategies for predicting its development are limited. This study aimed to use machine learning to integrate quantitative computed tomography (QCT) and clinical features to predict PPF in patients with IIM-ILD.

METHODS: We retrospectively included 180 IIM-ILD patients, of whom 86 developed PPF. We randomly assigned patients to training and validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and univariate analysis were employed to select the most predictive features. We independently trained 8 machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curves, area under the curve (AUC) values, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: 16 key clinical features and 7 QCT variables were selected for model development. The 10 variables with the highest contribution values were subsequently selected for the PPF prediction model. The clinical variables included Krebs von den Lungen-6, interleukin-6, percent-predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second, carcinoembryonic antigen, ferritin, CD3+ T cells, natural killer cells, and CD19+ B cells. The QCT signatures included ILD Honeycomb Volume (%) Lt Lower + Rt Lower and ILD Consolidation Volume (%) Whole Lung. Among the 8 machine learning algorithms, the Random Forest model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.680-0.925) in the training cohort and 0.943 (95% CI: 0.866-0.982) in the validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: The integration of QCT and clinical features using machine learning offers a potential non-invasive approach for predicting PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. This strategy may facilitate the early identification of individuals at high risk of PPF and potentially support timely clinical intervention.

articles.title: Macrolides and immunomodulation.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Macrolides are widely used antibiotics, but their clinical benefits in the setting of infection and sepsis span beyond their antimicrobial spectrum. They possess immunomodulatory properties, characterized, across preclinical models, by effects on macrophage M1/M2 polarization, autophagy, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, cytokine release, and bacterial virulence factors. In hospitalized CAP, macrolide and beta-lactam combination therapy confer survival benefit, as supported by observational studies and meta-analyses, and reinforced by a recent randomized trial. In non-CAP sepsis, three randomized trials using adjunctive clarithromycin demonstrated earlier resolution of infection, prevention of secondary sepsis episodes and a signal of improved survival, among the most severely ill patients. With a low risk of serious adverse events clarithromycin showed a cost-effective profile, compared to placebo. Mechanistic data, derived largely from biomarker analyses of these trials, point to a reversal of sepsis-induced immunoparalysis, including restored antigen presentation, monocyte reprogramming, and upregulation of cholesterol biosynthesis pathways, alongside. It is hypothesized that, depending on the timeline of infectioand on host response, macrolides have a role of immune "regulator" rather than purely anti-inflammatory properties.

articles.title: End-of-Life Pathways and Limitation of Life-Sustaining Treatment in Children with Pre-existing Neurological Disorders: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Limitation of life-sustaining treatment (LSTL) is an important component of pediatric end-of-life care, but its use in children with pre-existing neurologic disorders remains insufficiently described. We aimed to characterize end-of-life pathways, LSTL practices, and decision-making processes in this population.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of children with pre-existing neurologic disorders who died in a tertiary pediatric hospital between 2015 and 2024. Clinical characteristics and end-of-life care were compared between children with and without LSTL preceding death.

RESULTS: Of 37 included children, LSTL preceded death in 24/37; 8/37 died after brain death and 5/37 after unsuccessful resuscitation. Compared with children without LSTL, those with LSTL were less often admitted for acute neurological conditions (2/24 vs. 6/13, p = 0.013) or receiving invasive mechanical ventilation at death (9/24 vs. 11/13, p = 0.014), and more often died on the pediatric ward (15/24 vs. 0/13, p < 0.001) or had received pediatric palliative care (7/24 vs. 0/13, p = 0.038). Among children with LSTL, most decisions were documented during clinical stability (15/24), involving a median of four physicians; a do-not-resuscitate order was documented in 16/24 cases.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, LSTL was the most frequent end-of-life pathway among children with pre-existing neurologic disorders. Decisions were often documented before terminal deterioration and were usually multidisciplinary. These findings suggest that earlier advance care planning, structured, individualized documentation, and closer integration between pediatric neurology and pediatric palliative care may contribute to improving the quality and consistency of end-of-life care.

articles.title: Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method.
articles.journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: The introduction of state-of-the-art tube, detector, and image reconstruction techniques has made ultra-low-dose CT (ULD-CT) of the lungs technologically feasible, resulting in radiation exposure comparable to that of chest X-rays. Due to its high-contrast structures, the lung as target organ is generally well suited for reducing radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic accuracy, which could already be shown for the earlier development of low-dose CT (LDCT). The current state of the literature already demonstrates significant benefits of ULD-CT for the diagnosis of respiratory diseases, including COPD, pneumonia, interstitial lung disease, pediatric lung disease, as well as in interventional procedures. It is expected that ULD-CT will significantly expand the range of indications for CT and, in certain areas, will be able to replace chest X-rays as the initial imaging modality once its availability in institutions increases. Limitations currently arise from the known dependencies of quantitative methods on radiation exposure and image noise, and the fact that in-depth validation has not yet taken place.

KEY POINTS: · Ultra-low-dose computed tomography (ULD-CT) reduces radiation exposure to the level of a conventional chest X-ray through the latest tube, detector, and reconstruction technologies.. · ULD-CT can already be used for the diagnosis of solid pulmonary nodules, pneumonia, and chronic inflammatory airway diseases.. · Especially in children and immunosuppressed patients, ULD-CT should be considered for monitoring the progression of inflammatory lung diseases.. · There is insufficient evidence for the use of ULD-CT in interstitial lung diseases.. · In the future, ULD-CT could replace conventional chest X-ray for many indications in thoracic imaging..

CITATION FORMAT: · Wielpütz MO, Stiller W, Bayerl N et al. Ultra-Low-Dose Computed Tomography of the Lung: Evidence and Prospects of a New Method. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2977-0644.

articles.title: Auscultation for pre-exercise screening in the horse.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the highlights of cardiac auscultation of the equine athlete in the context of pre-exercise screening for cardiac adverse event prevention.

ANIMALS: Horses.

METHODS: Tutorial description.

RESULTS: Description of the highlights of cardiac auscultation of the equine athlete in the context of pre-exercise screening for cardiac adverse event and exercise-associated sudden death prevention.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Cardiac adverse events and exercise-associated deaths are problems that affect horses' health, riders' safety, and the public perception of welfare during equestrian sports. Screening before participation in sports has helped decrease the incidence of sudden death in humans. We believe auscultation may be a high-yield, low-cost strategy to improve equine welfare and a key component of a prevention program for exercise-associated sudden death in equine athletes. What we describe here highlights that an irregularly irregular rhythm is atrial fibrillation until proven otherwise and is the main target of pre-exercise auscultation. Concerning murmurs are the second target; multiple examples of audio, video, and electrocardiograms are shown.

articles.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.

METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.

INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

FUNDING: Novartis.

articles.title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression.
articles.abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: Cholera rapid diagnostic test performance at the host-microbe interface: a prospective longitudinal study in Bangladesh.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective cholera outbreak response requires accurate bedside rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) because of poor laboratory access. Formative studies suggest that cholera diagnostics have multiple vulnerabilities, including target degradation by virulent bacteriophage (phage) specific to Vibrio cholerae and antibiotics. Our study objectives were to evaluate the performance of RDTs as a function of these antimicrobials to improve deployment and guide future diagnostic development.

METHODS: In this prospective longitudinal study, participants were enrolled at seven hospitals across Bangladesh from March 13, 2018, to April 9, 2019. Inclusion criteria were participants aged 2 months or older with uncomplicated diarrhoeal disease. Exclusion criteria were the presence of severe comorbidity or the absence of participant or guardian consent or assent. Stool samples were analysed using culture, quantitative PCR (qPCR), and mass spectrometry. The primary outcome was RDT performance (eg, sensitivity and specificity) as a function of phage detection. Exploratory outcomes were the effects of antibiotics and disease severity on RDT performance.

FINDINGS: 2574 participants were enrolled, and for 2078 samples, all assays were completed for analysis of the primary outcome. 394 samples without RDT data and 102 samples without qPCR data were excluded. Using the current gold standard of culture or qPCR positivity for V cholerae, we found that phage detection had no effect on RDT performance. When the diagnostic criteria were expanded to include phage detection, RDT sensitivity decreased from 0·46 (95% CI 0·41-0·51) to 0·38 (0·34-0·43), and the odds of RDT positivity among patients with cholera decreased with phage exposure (odds ratio 0·428; 95% CI 0·296-0·613). Antibiotics were detected in more than 80% of samples using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, limiting assessment of their effects on RDT performance. Among patients with moderate and severe dehydration, large increases in sensitivity and specificity were observed. We estimated that restricting RDT use to patients with severe dehydration and no reported antibiotic exposure increased sensitivity by 50% compared with unrestricted RDT use. If the presence of phage is considered a diagnostic proxy for V cholerae infection, then RDTs might not detect an additional 17% of cholera cases.

INTERPRETATION: Cholera RDTs have limitations that require consideration during global deployments. Inclusion of phage detection in diagnostic criteria might improve case detection, although this requires further research in diverse settings. The implications of these findings likely extend to other diseases in which diagnostics share similar vulnerabilities.

FUNDING: Wellcome Trust (DFID grant), NIH, and Thrasher Research Fund.

articles.title: Antibiotic overuse and mortality in patients hospitalised for COVID-19: a global cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Global antibiotic use during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact remain unclear. This study analysed antibiotic use, bacterial co-infections, and the association between antibiotic use and in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalised for COVID-19, using a WHO database.

METHODS: We conducted a multicountry cohort study using anonymised patient-level data from The WHO Global Clinical Platform for COVID-19. Data were collected across 64 countries in all six WHO regions between January, 2020, and October, 2023. The study included hospitalised patients of all ages with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We obtained patient-level data from standardised WHO case report forms completed prospectively or retrospectively and from harmonised national registries, research studies, and hospital databases. Patients without a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis or missing information on hospital admission date, antibiotic use, or outcome were excluded from the analysis. Patients were followed up from hospital admission until death, discharge, transfer, or 28 days, whichever occurred first. Follow-up data were collected at hospital discharge or death by the treating facility and entered into the platform. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality, and we analysed this outcome using Cox proportional hazards models with a shared frailty term to account for country-level clustering.

FINDINGS: The median age of the study population was 61·9 years (±21·7), with 198 223 women and 251 990 men with data available on antibiotic use. Of the 592 898 patients enrolled, 451 291 (76·1%) had data on antibiotic use and were included in the descriptive analysis; 122 854 had complete data on empirical treatment type, of whom 47 359 (38·5%) were included in the regression analysis. Among the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use, 341 125 (75·6%) received antibiotics, more frequently in severe to critical cases than in mild to moderate cases (80·5% vs 71·6%). Prescribing was highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (83·0%) and African (82·7%) regions and lowest in the Western Pacific region (32·8%), declining in the European region and region of the Americas but increasing in the African region between 2020 and 2022. Treatment was predominantly empirical and involved Watch antibiotics of the WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve classification. Clinically suspected co-infections were reported in 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 patients; among those with positive cultures, 1815 (42·8%) of 4237 had multidrug-resistant bacteria. In the unadjusted analyses, empirical antibiotic use was associated with higher mortality across severity strata. After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24).

INTERPRETATION: Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Biomarker tests for invasive Candida infection in critically ill patients in the UK (A-Stop): a multicentre diagnostic test accuracy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current practice of empirical antifungal treatment for suspected invasive Candida infection in the intensive care unit (ICU) leads to overtreatment. Biomarkers might better target treatment; however, their diagnostic accuracy in this patient group is uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether a biomarker or a combination of biomarkers has sufficiently high negative predictive value (NPV) to enable early cessation of empirical antifungal treatment in patients in ICUs.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic test accuracy study, we recruited patients who had been started on empirical antifungal treatment for suspected candidiasis and had blood cultures drawn within 24 h of starting treatment from 43 UK ICUs. We tested a research blood sample, collected within 24 h of the standard-of-care care blood culture (ie, within 48 h of starting empirical antifungal treatment), with three DNA detection tests (Fungiplex, T2Candida, and CandID) and one (1,3)-β-D-glucan test (Fungitell). We assessed the accuracy of these tests against an international consensus definition of proven invasive Candida infection and a constructed reference standard for proven or probable infection. The primary outcome was NPV for exclusion of proven Candida infection; we also reported sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios.

FINDINGS: Among 4005 patients screened, 1251 were enrolled. A total of 1225 participants, recruited between April, 2018 and Feb, 2023, were evaluable, among whom 54 (4·4%) had proven invasive Candida infection. The median duration of antifungal treatment was 9 days (IQR 5-15), and survival at 28 days was 76·8%. The index tests had similar NPVs: 96·6% (95·3-97·6) for Fungiplex, 97·1% (94·7-98·6) for T2Candida, 96·7% (95·4-97·8) for CandID, and 97·2% (95·5-98·4) for Fungitell; however, sensitivity varied widely among the tests, from 27·5% to 68·6%. The optimal test combination was Fungitell and CandID, which had an NPV of 97·5% (95·7-98·7) and a sensitivity of 75·0%. Combining these biomarkers with standard-of-care blood culture testing further increased the NPV to 98·6% (97·0-99·4), with a sensitivity of 85·1%.

INTERPRETATION: No single biomarker had sufficiently high sensitivity to justify stopping empirical antifungal treatment. Combining Fungitell and CandID with standard-of-care blood culture testing could provide a sufficiently high NPV to allow early cessation of empirical antifungal treatment in this patient group, thereby reducing overtreatment, although this gain in sensitivity is accompanied by a reduction in specificity. Randomised trials are needed to confirm the clinical and cost-effectiveness of this diagnostic strategy before it is adopted in practice.

FUNDING: UK National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Technology Assessment Programme and the Research Charitable Trust Fund of the Belfast Health & Social Care Trust.

articles.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC.

METHODS: MASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24). There were two serious adverse events attributable to SBRT; grade 2 small bowel obstruction and grade 3 pancreatitis.

INTERPRETATION: In patients with high-risk, localised PDAC, the addition of SBRT to chemotherapy was associated with significantly reduced locoregional recurrence without a significant increase in toxicity and warrants further investigation in larger studies.

FUNDING: Medical Research Future Fund, Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group, National Health and Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Centre (University of Sydney), and Gut Cancer Foundation, New Zealand.

articles.title: Safety and immunogenicity of an adenoviral-vectored vaccine against Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever in the UK (CCHF01): an open-label, first-in-human, non-randomised, phase 1 clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are no approved vaccines for Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), which remains a WHO priority pathogen for vaccine development. We evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of ChAdOx2 Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF), a novel, non-replicating adenoviral-vectored vaccine, in a first-in-human phase 1 clinical trial.

METHODS: CCHF01 was an open-label, first-in-human, non-randomised, phase 1 trial conducted at a single centre, the University of Oxford Centre for Clinical Vaccinology and Tropical Medicine in Oxford, UK. Healthy adults aged 18-55 years, with no confirmed or suspected previous CCHFV infection and no known clinically significant medical comorbidities, received two intramuscular doses of ChAdOx2 CCHF administered 12 weeks apart. Six participants were enrolled into a lead-in cohort (cohort 1). 40 participants were enrolled in cohort 2 and stratified by previous vaccination with a ChAdOx-vectored vaccine: cohort 2A (ChAdOx exposed; n=20) and cohort 2B (ChAdOx naive; n=20). Primary outcomes were safety and tolerability, assessed in all participants who received at least one vaccine dose. Secondary outcome was CCHFV glycoprotein-specific binding antibody responses, assessed at prespecified timepoints in participants who received two vaccine doses with available data. The trial was registered on the ISRCTN registry (ISRCTN12 351 734) and is now complete.

FINDINGS: Between Aug 31, 2023, and Jan 31, 2024, 46 adult participants aged 18-55 years were enrolled. Of these, 44 received the second vaccine dose; two were discontinued from further vaccination: one due to persistent neutropenia and one following a mild self-limiting allergic reaction after the first vaccination. Solicited local adverse events occurred in 30 (65%) of 46 participants after the first vaccination and 30 (68%) of 44 after the second vaccination, and solicited systemic adverse events occurred in 39 (85%) of 46 participants after the first vaccination and 28 (64%) of 44 participants after the second vaccination. Reactogenicity was predominantly mild, with injection-site pain and fatigue being the most commonly reported local and systemic adverse events. No serious adverse events were reported. Median CCHFV glycoprotein Gc-specific IgG response was 26·17 arbitrary units (AU) 28 days after first vaccination and was 88·20 AU 28 days after second vaccination. Median GP38-specific IgG response was 92·74 AU 28 days after first vaccination and 1064·13 AU 28 days after second vaccination.

INTERPRETATION: ChAdOx2 CCHF demonstrated acceptable tolerability and induced CCHFV-specific humoral immune responses in this phase 1 trial. These findings provide proof of principle for vaccination against CCHFV and support further clinical development of this vaccine. The effect of previous ChAdOx-vectored vaccination on immunogenicity could not be conclusively determined because of the study sample size and age differences between groups.

FUNDING: UK Research and Innovation.

articles.title: Bacteria inside kidney tumors associate with myeloid inflammation and disease progression: A TRACERx Renal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intratumoral bacteria are increasingly recognized as active contributors to neutrophil-driven inflammation and disease progression in solid tumors. Yet, in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), where myeloid inflammation is a key feature of aggressive disease, live bacterial presence, their intratumoral distribution, and interaction with the tumor microenvironment remain unexplored.

METHODS: We genetically characterized the microbiome of primary ccRCC tumors across two independent cohorts (TRACERx: 616 samples, 143 patients; The Cancer Genome Atlas [TCGA]: 511 samples and patients), confirming live bacterial presence through culture. Multi-regional sampling enabled within-tumor analysis of bacterial distribution. Associations with the tumor microenvironment were explored at scale using bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) across both cohorts and corroborated in depth through spatial transcriptomics and in vitro infection assays.

FINDINGS: Across both cohorts, the commensal Cutibacterium emerged as the dominant genus, accumulating in discrete niches enriched toward the tumor center and associating with more advanced (TRACERx p = 0.024; TCGA p = 0.0011) tumors and shorter progression-free survival (TRACERx p = 0.0022; TCGA p = 4.4 × 10-4). Both across and within tumors, Cutibacterium accumulation associated with neutrophil recruitment and myeloid inflammation. In vitro, Cutibacterium induced sustained expression of neutrophil-attracting chemokines in macrophages, recapitulating patient tumor findings.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish intratumoral bacteria as novel prognostic components of the ccRCC tumor microenvironment and suggest an active role in shaping local myeloid inflammation, laying the groundwork for investigating their potential as therapeutic targets.

FUNDING: This work was supported by the Francis Crick Institute (Cancer Research UK, MRC, Wellcome Trust). TRACERx Renal is funded by Cancer Research UK (C50947/A18176).

articles.title: Secretory bile salt hydrolases regulate niche displacement and gut colonization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus.
articles.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) residing in the gut are major causes of hospital-acquired infections worldwide. Bacteria belonging to the Bacteroidales order have been linked to protection against VRE, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, we identify an important role for Bacteroidales species in mediating resistance to VRE through a distinct subtype of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) that retain an uncleaved N-terminal signal peptide. This subclass of BSHs harbored by Bacteroides species promotes VRE inhibition through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. Mechanistically, the N-terminal signal peptide is required for extracellular enzyme release, DCA production, and VRE growth inhibition. In the presence of VRE, Bacteroidales species producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE from its ecological niche through DCA production. These results reveal a previously unknown regulatory role for BSHs in VRE colonization and suggest therapeutic approaches for individuals at risk of VRE infection.

articles.title: NF-κB phosphorylation controls enhancer selection to shape the inflammatory gene program.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. Genes linked to these enhancers, including inflammatory mediators, were selectively impaired in S276A macrophages. Although antiviral responses remained intact, Rela Ser276Ala mice resisted endotoxin shock but were susceptible to bacterial infection. Thus, NF-κB responses are functionally partitioned by enhancer architecture: phosphorylation-sensitive sites define a latent enhancer compartment with NF-κB-dominated regulatory architecture, whereas primed sites are embedded in broader networks of lineage-determining and inducible TFs, yielding distinct biological outputs.

articles.title: Taurine lowers inflammaging by regulating the NLRP3 inflammasome in macrophages.
articles.abstract: Whether a decline in taurine drives aging is debated, and despite high millimolar intracellular concentrations, its function as a potential guardian of cytosolic homeostasis is unclear. Here, we show that aging increases circulating taurine concentrations in humans and mice. Further elevating taurine in aged mice enhances health span, engaging anti-inflammatory pathways previously linked to youthfulness, and reduces mortality from sepsis and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, suggesting an enantiostatic response. Mechanistically, diverse NLRP3-specific "danger signals" induce taurine efflux from macrophages as a proximal step to activate the inflammasome and the resultant pyroptosis. Taurine restoration in macrophages prevents NLRP3-induced trans-Golgi network disassembly, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Conversely, lowering taurine biosynthesis combined with reduced bioavailability in macrophages exacerbated inflammasome activation. In humans, sustained caloric restriction elevates adipose tissue taurine and is accompanied by lower inflammation. Together, we identify taurine as an immunometabolic rheostat that links danger sensing to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suggesting taurine-based strategies to alleviate inflammaging and inflammasomopathies.

articles.title: Panama's Infectious Disease Legacy: Implications for Renewed Military Cooperation and Force Health Protection.
articles.abstract: Tropical infectious disease is a recurrent threat to Force Health Protection throughout the U.S. military presence in Panama. This article recounts some of the notable contributions of the U.S. military in the discovery, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases in hopes of informing future risk assessment and mitigation.

articles.title: Interrogating imidazo[2,1-b]thiazole-4-thiazolidinone hybrids as antidiabetic leads: molecular cartography, pharmacokinetic profiling and rodent therapeutic response.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of new therapeutic agents targeting key enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism. In this study, ten novel imidazo-thiazole-thiazolidinone hybrids were designed, synthesized and their structural integrity was confirmed through 1H NMR and 13C NMR along with mass determination by HREI-MS. After characterization, each derivative was subjected to in-vitro evaluation using acarbose (reference) to assess their anti-diabetic potential through the inhibition of key enzymes. Compound 3 and 6 with IC50 values 3.20 ± 0.20 μM, 2.10 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and 3.70 ± 0.30 μM, 2.60 ± 0.20 μM for α-glucosidase acted as the excellent inhibitors, markedly affecting rate of enzymatic reactions, with kinetic studies revealing their mode of inhibition. The SAR analysis revealed key substituents enhanced ligand-enzyme affinity, supported by molecular docking showing their specific binding. Furthermore, in-vivo cytotoxic assessment in rat models was performed to examine toxicological aspects and biocompatibility of synthesized compounds. Pharmacophore modeling, DFT calculations and MD simulations were also conducted to provide mechanistic insights. Comprehensive ADMET analysis including bioavailability, toxicity prediction, oral suitability and drug-likeness together with in-vivo safety evaluation complemented the in-vitro and computational findings, demonstrating these imidazo-thiazole based thiazolidinone derivatives hold promise as effective therapeutics against diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and risk of type 2 diabetes: Evidence from the E3N-generations cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evidence on hysterectomy and the risk of type 2 diabetes is limited, particularly regarding age at surgery. We assessed whether hysterectomy, with or without bilateral oophorectomy, is associated with incident type 2 diabetes, and whether this association is modified by age at surgery.

STUDY DESIGN: We followed 82,472 women from the E3N-Generations cohort, free of diabetes at baseline in 1992, until 2008 (median follow-up 16 years). Hysterectomy and oophorectomy were modelled as time-dependent exposures. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox models with age as the time scale, adjusted for lifestyle, metabolic, and reproductive factors.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Incidence of type 2 diabetes.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 2318 women developed type 2 diabetes. In fully adjusted models, hysterectomy combined with bilateral oophorectomy was associated with a higher risk of type 2 diabetes (hazard ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.43) compared with women who underwent neither procedure, whereas hysterectomy alone was not (1.06, 0.91-1.24). Bilateral oophorectomy alone was not associated with the risk of incident type 2 diabetes. The association with hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy was strongest among women operated on before age 45 (1.70, 1.35-2.15); it was similarly elevated when the age threshold was changed to 40 (1.54, 1.08-2.20). There was significant heterogeneity by age at surgery for hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy (p = 0.001) and for hysterectomy alone (p = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: Hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy was associated with an increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes, independently of conventional metabolic risk factors. This excess risk was particularly pronounced among women who underwent surgery before age 45.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Acupuncture combined with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation vs repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation alone for recovery of hemiparesis after ischemic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis" [Neuroscience 616 (2026) 73-91].
PHLDA3 deficiency attenuates neonatal sepsis-associated acute lung injury and is associated with reduced endoplasmic reticulum stress and NF-κB activation.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis often causes acute lung injury (ALI), but the underlying molecular mechanisms of ALI have not been elucidated. Pleckstrin homology-like domain family A member 3 (PHLDA3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in inflammatory signaling, yet its role in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI has not been explored. Here, we established a neonatal polymicrobial sepsis model via intraperitoneal injection of cecal slurry (CS) and investigated the role of PHLDA3 in ALI using CRISPR/Cas9-generated constitutive PHLDA3 knockout (PHLDA3 KO) mice. CS induced time-dependent upregulation of PHLDA3 in neonatal lung tissues. CS triggered significant increases in the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in lung tissues, impairing vascular integrity and causing severe alveolar damage. These harmful effects were alleviated by PHLDA3 KO. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein processing pathways. CS activated ER stress and unfolded protein response via PERK/eIF2α/ATF4 and ATF6 axes, which were attenuated by PHLDA3 deletion. Pharmacological induction of ER stress by thapsigargin (TG) reversed the protective effects of PHLDA3 KO, whereas ER stress inhibitor 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) mitigated inflammation and lung injury. In macrophage models, PHLDA3 knockdown was associated with reduced LPS-induced ER-stress-related signaling, NF-κB activation, and inflammatory responses, whereas TG attenuated these effects. Collectively, these findings indicate that constitutive PHLDA3 deficiency is associated with attenuated neonatal sepsis-associated lung injury, reduced ER-stress-related signaling, and decreased NF-κB activation, and support further investigation of PHLDA3 in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI.

articles.title: Highly selective depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate plastic via Au/attapulgite dual-site synergy.
articles.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
articles.abstract: The chemical recycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into high-value terephthalic acid (TPA) under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we construct a dual-active-site Au/ATP catalyst via electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) by supporting Au on inexpensive attapulgite (ATP). Under optimal conditions (200 °C, 1 MPa Ar, 4 h), this catalyst achieves near-complete conversion of PET with a terephthalic acid (TPA) yield of 91.76 ± 1.65%, and is also effective for actual waste plastic bottle flakes. The EMSI stabilizes Au nanoparticles, modulates Lewis acidity to suppress side reactions, and enables selective ester-bond cleavage without affecting the benzene ring or CC bonds. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), work-function analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the EMSI effect drives electron transfer from Au to ATP, generating Auδ+ species. These species can effectively polarize the CO bond to generate an electron-deficient intermediate. Meanwhile, ATP provides an adsorption and activation platform for H2O, promoting the generation of nucleophilic *OH. The synergy of these two sites enables highly performance depolymerization. This work provides a sustainable strategy for polyester chemical recycling and the value-added upgrading of low-grade mineral resources.

articles.title: Long-term communication and swallowing disability in adults with persistent critical illness following COVID-19: A mixed-methods observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the lived experience of communication and swallowing disability in adults with persistent critical illness following COVID-19.

METHODS: A mixed-methods study. Semi-structured interviews were conducted alongside patient-reported communication and swallowing outcome measures.

SETTING: Participants were recruited from a registry-embedded COVID-Recovery study. All patients were eligible if they were ≥ 18 years, positive PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and had persistent critical illness. This was defined as admission to ICU for >10 consecutive days with invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 24 h.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Semi-structured interviews were used to explore communication and swallowing disability. Additional patient-reported outcomes were assessed with the Dysphagia Severity Rating Scale and the La Trobe Communication Questionnaire. General function outcomes were evaluated with the WHODAS 2.0, EQ-5D-5L, HADS, MoCA-Blind, IADL and IES-6.

FINDINGS: Of the 113 participants followed up, 29/113 (26%) reported communication or swallowing disability, and of these 17/29 (59%) consented to semi-structured interviews. From the 16 participants who answered questions about communication function 100% self-reported difficulty in ≥1 communication domain, including expressive language 13/16 (81%), voice 13/16 (81%), receptive language 9/16 (56%) and speech 5/16 (31%). Although all participants were consuming an oral diet and most with nil texture restrictions (13/17,76%), many reported ongoing swallowing concerns regarding safety and efficiency. Impacts of these new disabilities were beyond physical function and impacted on their activities and participation. Recovery was unclear, prolonged and compounded by judgement from others. Participants navigated their own recovery journey and whilst some were well supported, others described critical healthcare gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: We identified approximately one quarter of people admitted to ICU for COVID-19 related critical illness with a length of stay of 10 days or more report ongoing communication and swallowing disability at 6 months. The impacts continued well beyond hospital discharge and highlight a need to specifically address swallowing and communication in recovery pathways.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Specific assessment of communication and swallowing function is essential for individuals who experience persistent critical illness.

articles.title: Phase II study of cabozantinib in recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy (CABOCOL).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The antiangiogenic pathway is an effective target for recurrent uterine cervical carcinoma (rCC). This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of cabozantinib monotherapy for rCC.

PATIENTS & METHODS: This open-label phase II study (NCT04205799) enrolled patients with rCC who previously received platinum-based chemotherapy. Patients received oral cabozantinib (60 mg daily) until progression or discontinuation from any cause. The main objective was based on joint primary endpoint of efficacy (3-month disease control rate, DCR3) and safety (proportion of patients with grade ≥ 2 (CTCAE v5.0) gastro-intestinal (GI) perforation, GI-vaginal and/or genito-urinary (GU) fistula events) according to a Bryant-and-Day design. Key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), duration of response (DOR) and safety.
