RESULTS: Among 57 patients enrolled, 54 received cabozantinib: median age was 55.5 years, 18 patients (33.3%) had received more than two prior lines of treatment; 28 patients (51.9%) had been previously treated with bevacizumab. Median duration of follow-up was 8.9 months. DCR3 was 46.3% [95% CI, 32.8-60.3]. Fistula/perforation occurred in 5 (9.3%) patients. Objective response rate was 9.3%, with a median DOR of 2.5 months. Median PFS was 2.8 months (95% CI, 2.5-4.6). Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 51.9% of patients, most commonly asthenia (15%), hypertension (9%) and mucositis (6%). Dose reductions and treatment interruptions were reported in 26 (48%) and 24 (44%) patients, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Cabozantinib demonstrates efficacy comparable to other anti-angiogenic monotherapy in rCC; however, modest benefit and toxicity do not support further monotherapy development.

articles.title: Ancient disease and One Health: Integrating ancient -omics and paleopathology to address contemporary infectious disease risks within One Paleopathology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore methodological complications of One Paleopathology and highlight potential pathways for accommodating, circumventing, and overcoming these challenges.

MATERIALS: We review published research and present two case studies on 1) recovering avian influenza virus sequences from formalin-fixed, ethanol-preserved tissues in wild waterfowl and 2) reconstructing oral microbiomes from dental calculus in California sea lions.

METHODS: We synthesize methodological challenges identified in the literature and use case studies to examine limitations associated with preservation, sample selection, pathogen and microbiome recovery and analysis, and interpretation.

RESULTS: The case studies illustrate challenges in recovering endogenous ancient RNA and DNA from historic animal specimens, including degradation, contamination, limited reference databases, and substrate-specific constraints. They also demonstrate how integrating diverse data types and sources can complicate interpretation of past host-environment-animal-plant-pathogen (HEAPP) interactions.

CONCLUSIONS: One Paleopathology offers valuable opportunities to integrate evolutionary, One Health, paleopathological, and ancient -omics perspectives, but requires careful consideration of methodological constraints and ethical imperatives.

SIGNIFICANCE: Addressing the highlighted complications can strengthen One Paleopathology's ability to generate insights relevant to contemporary infectious disease research, public health, clinical practice, and pandemic preparedness.

LIMITATIONS: Sample availability and molecular preservation, reference databases, and current analytical methods constrain our abilities to identify microbes involved in past HEAPP interactions.

SUGGESTIONS FOR FURTHER RESEARCH: Future research should expand genetic sequence and microbiome reference libraries, improve sampling and authentication strategies, identify optimal substrates for molecular analysis, and model ethical science for integrating diverse evidence within One Paleopathology.

articles.title: Trends in Oral Anticoagulant Prescribing for Atrial Fibrillation and Active Cancer in UK Primary Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation is essential in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and cancer, but recent real-world evidence on oral anticoagulant (OAC) use remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to describe recent OAC-prescribing trends and identify factors associated with OAC initiation in patients with AF and active cancer in UK primary care.

METHODS: Using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, we identified patients aged ≥50 years with incident AF (cohort entry) between 2010 and 2023 and active cancer diagnosed in the year before cohort entry. We calculated OAC initiation rates in the year following AF diagnosis among eligible patients (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2) using Poisson regression, overall and stratified by OAC type, age, sex, and cancer characteristics. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with OAC initiation.

RESULTS: Among 12,254 eligible patients, 6,940 (56.6%) initiated an OAC. OAC initiation rates rose from 89 per 100 person-years in 2010 to 385 per 100 person-years in 2023 (adjusted rate ratio: 4.32; 95% CI: 3.78-4.93), driven by increased direct oral anticoagulant prescribing. By 2023, apixaban and edoxaban predominated. OAC initiation did not differ by age and sex but was less common in patients with lung cancer (HR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.67-0.82), metastatic cancer (HR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.51-0.87), and dementia (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.64-0.88).

CONCLUSIONS: In the last decade, OAC initiation has substantially increased among eligible patients with AF and active cancer, driven by direct oral anticoagulant uptake. However, OAC initiation remained lower among patients with lung cancer, metastatic cancer, or specific comorbidities.

articles.title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD.

OBJECTIVES: This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety.

METHODS: Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response.

RESULTS: Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

articles.title: Systemic Inflammation and Adverse Heart Failure Outcomes: Insights From the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between systemic inflammation (SI) and outcomes among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) is uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between SI and clinical and economic outcomes among individuals with HFpEF/HFmrEF.

METHODS: We identified Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) testing from 2008 to 2022. We classified Veterans as with SI (hsCRP 2-10 mg/L) and without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L). The primary outcome was the 3-component major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) outcome of death, HF hospitalization, and HF-related emergency department encounters. Additional outcomes included acute care utilization and costs. We evaluated the adjusted associations between SI and clinical outcomes, acute care utilization, and costs via Cox regression, negative binomial regression, and gamma regression, respectively.

RESULTS: We identified 49,986 Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient hsCRP levels. We compared 8,696 (17.4%) Veterans without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L) and 25,352 (50.7%) Veterans with SI (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L and ≤10 mg/L Over a median follow-up of 3.4 years (IQR: 1.8-5.8), MACE incidence was 15.1/100 patient-years (95% CI: 14.9-15.4) among those with SI vs 11.8/100 patient-years (95% CI: 11.4-12.1) among those without SI (P < 0.001). After adjustment, SI was associated with increased MACE (HR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.24-1.33). SI was also associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations (incidence rate ratio: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.137-1.246) and $9,112 (95% CI: $6,135-$12,089) in additional per-patient costs over 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with HFmrEF/HFpEF, SI is associated with increased adverse clinical outcomes and higher costs.

articles.title: The Duke Clinically Linked Electrocardiogram and Arrhythmia Repository.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (ECG) algorithms are becoming increasingly powerful tools in the clinical world, allowing for earlier and subclinical detection of ubiquitous and harmful pathologies. However, the strength of these algorithms is directly informed by the strength of the data sets on which they are trained, and there is a growing need for large-scale, diverse, publicly available ECG repositories. The Duke Clinically Linked ECG and Arrhythmia Repository is a large-scale ECG database containing over 5 million clinically acquired ECGs linked to longitudinal clinical data. Its strengths-including demographic diversity, large sample size, linked clinical databases, breadth of represented conditions, access to linked procedure codes, various options for data export, and ease in creating targeted subcohorts-position it as a significant tool in the artificial intelligence-ECG research landscape. This Methods paper outlines the demographics and structure of this database and explores promising research applications of this resource.

articles.title: Spatial differentiation and urban environmental associations of avian co-occurrence network roles: Evidence from Guangzhou, China.
articles.abstract: Urban bird conservation requires information on where species occur, how they are positioned within community networks, and how their distributions relate to urban environmental conditions. Using Guangzhou as a case study, this research analyzed 41,346 bird records through co-occurrence network analysis, spatial statistics, robustness assessment, and environmental association modeling. The main results were as follows: (1) 43 network-important avian species were identified. Module Hubs (n = 21) primarily supported within-module cohesion, Network Hubs (n = 7) occupied highly connected positions across modules, and Connectors (n = 15) distributed their associations among multiple modules. These categories represent topological positions rather than classical ecological functions. Bootstrap and jackknife tests indicated relatively persistent network participation, although exact role assignments remained sensitive to resampling. (2) Network-role groups showed distinct spatial patterns: Module Hubs clustered in forest-wetland patches, Network Hubs in southern coastal wetlands, and Connectors in urban transition zones and corridor-like habitats. (3) Environmental associations were role-specific. Module Hubs were primarily associated with water-system area ratio, landscape fragmentation, and broader development-related conditions; Network Hubs were associated with water-system area ratio and habitat quality; and Connectors showed a consistent negative association with nighttime light. Sensitivity analyses indicated that some individual urbanization-related pathways were sensitive to observation effort and spatial specification and were therefore interpreted cautiously. These results show that combining network roles with spatial and environmental information can support differentiated urban bird management while avoiding direct inference of ecological function or species-level conservation priority from co-occurrence topology alone.

articles.title: Knowledge and attitudes toward advance directives among ICU nurses.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: End-of-life decision-making in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) may be hindered not only by the absence of advance directives (ADs), but also by limited knowledge among ICU nurses. The aim of this study was to analyse knowledge and attitudes regarding advance directives among ICU nurses.

METHOD: An observational, descriptive, cross-sectional and multicentre study was conducted among ICU nurses working in public hospitals in Las Palmas (Spain). An anonymous electronic questionnaire was used. Statistical analysis was performed using R Core Team 2024.

RESULTS: A total of 229 responses were obtained from a population of 260 professionals, yielding a response rate of 88.1%. Most participants were women (75.6%) and had a median of 6 years of ICU experience (interquartile range: 3-14). Overall, 87.7% reported not having received specific training on advance directives (ADs). Although attitudes toward ADs were highly favorable (scores above 9/10), the level of knowledge was limited, particularly regarding legal aspects, procedures, documentation, and content.

CONCLUSIONS: A discrepancy exists between nurses' favorable attitudes toward ADs and their limited practical knowledge. The implementation of targeted training programs, along with the development of institutional protocols, could enhance the integration of ADs into ICU clinical practice.

articles.title: Airway mucus plugs and ventilatory support during exacerbations, with subsequent outcomes, in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or emphysema.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway mucus plugs are associated with airflow obstruction and exacerbations in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, their roles during exacerbations remain unclear. This study aimed to examine whether mucus plugs during exacerbations are associated with ventilatory support requirements and prognosis in patients with COPD.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients with COPD, defined by airflow limitation on spirometry or emphysema on computed tomography (CT), who presented to the emergency department, and were diagnosed with COPD exacerbation. Mucus plugs during exacerbations were visually assessed on CT and analyzed in relation to the need for ventilatory support (primary outcome).

RESULTS: Of 86 patients with a median mucus plug score of 3.5 (interquartile range, 1-7), 26 (30.2%) received ventilatory support. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, a higher mucus plug score (odds ratio [OR], 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.59) and higher C-reactive protein level were significantly associated with the need for ventilatory support. In a Cox proportional hazards model, a higher mucus plug score (hazard ratio [HR], 1.17; 95% CI, 1.07-1.29) and long-term oxygen therapy use were significantly associated with a shorter time to re-exacerbation or all-cause death within 1 year. Mucus plugs significantly decreased from the exacerbation to the recovery phases in a sub-analysis of 20 patients who underwent CT in both phases.

CONCLUSION: A higher mucus plug score was associated with the need for ventilatory support and poorer clinical outcomes, suggesting that mucus plugs may impair ventilation and worsen the prognosis of COPD exacerbations.

articles.title: Ischemic stroke after bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and influenza vaccination during the 2022-2023 season: a multi-site self-controlled case series study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) detected a statistical signal for ischemic events (ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack) following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination through prospective surveillance during 2022-2023. Although multiple studies from other surveillance systems and countries reported no increased risk, important methodological limitations remained. This U.S. study addressed those limitations by evaluating the ischemic stroke risk following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, and their same-day coadministration using an event-dependent self-controlled case series (SCCS) design.

METHODS: Study outcomes included first-ever ischemic stroke (primary outcome), first-in-1-year ischemic stroke (secondary outcome), and ischemic events (exploratory outcomes), identified using ICD-10-CM codes in inpatient and emergency department settings during September 1, 2022-March 31, 2023, among individuals aged ≥12 years across eight VSD sites. Analyses were conducted separately for Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna bivalent vaccines, with relative incidences (RI) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated for 1-21-day and 1-42-day risk intervals, using person-time outside these intervals as the control period. Subgroup analyses were performed by age group (12-64, ≥65 years) and history of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection.

RESULTS: A total of 6510 first-ever ischemic strokes were identified among more than 6.8 million participants. Among recipients of Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, no statistically significant increased risk of first-ever ischemic stroke was observed following bivalent COVID-19 vaccination (RI = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.63-1.41), influenza vaccination (RI = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.82-1.10), or same-day coadministration (RI = 1.15; 95% CI: 0.88-1.49) within 1-21-day risk intervals; findings were similar for 1-42-day intervals. Comparable null results were observed for Moderna vaccine and across all subgroups, secondary, and exploratory outcomes.

CONCLUSION: No increased risk of ischemic stroke was found following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, or their coadministration in this multi-site SCCS study. These findings are consistent with previous studies and underscore the importance of continued vaccine safety monitoring.

articles.title: Operative Timing and Physiologic Predictors of Outcomes in Blunt Small Bowel and Mesenteric Injury.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blunt small bowel and mesenteric injury (BSBMI) is uncommon and difficult to diagnose early, and delayed surgical intervention for BSBMI has been associated with increased morbidity. However, the relative prognostic contribution of surgical timing compared with physiologic factors such as age and serum lactate level remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative outcomes and identify independent predictors of adverse outcomes in surgically managed BSBMI.

METHODS: This 10-y retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent surgery for BSBMI at an advanced-level trauma center in central Taiwan from January 2013 to December 2022. Patients with penetrating trauma, nonoperative management, high-grade solid organ injury, or major extra-abdominal injury were excluded to minimize confounding. Outcomes included postoperative morbidity, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS) (LOS ≥30 d). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of each outcome. Model performance and multicollinearity were assessed using standard diagnostic measures.

RESULTS: A total of 67 patients were included, with a median age of 52 y. Traffic-related mechanisms accounted for the majority of injuries. Overall mortality was 7.5%, and postoperative morbidity occurred in 31.3% of patients. Surgical delay ≥8 h was associated with significantly higher morbidity (43.8% versus 20.0%) and a higher rate of prolonged hospital LOS (LOS ≥30 d: 40.6% versus 11.4%). On multivariable analysis, surgical delay ≥8 h independently predicted postoperative morbidity (odds ratio [OR], 3.45, P = 0.036) and prolonged hospital LOS (OR, 5.98, P = 0.025). Increasing age was independently associated with morbidity, ICU admission, and prolonged hospital LOS (all P < 0.05), while higher initial serum lactate levels independently predicted ICU admission (OR, 1.04, P = 0.022) and prolonged hospital LOS (OR, 1.06, P = 0.016). All multivariable models demonstrated acceptable discrimination, with no evidence of multicollinearity.

CONCLUSIONS: In surgically managed BSBMI, delayed operative intervention, older age, and elevated initial serum lactate level were independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. These findings suggest that timely surgical decision-making, together with early physiologic risk stratification, may be important in optimizing outcomes for this diagnostically challenging injury.

articles.title: Wound problems and infections after major joint arthroplasty : national survey results from primary and secondary care in the UK.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Early postoperative wound problems following major joint arthroplasty (MJA) are common, yet comprehensive guidelines for superficial surgical site infections (SSIs) are lacking. This study aimed to explore healthcare professionals' views and management strategies for early wound problems after MJA.

METHODS: A national cross-sectional online survey was distributed to orthopaedic surgeons, microbiologists, general practitioners, physiotherapists, and nursing staff involved in MJA care. The survey explored perceptions of wound problems, along with diagnostic and management approaches, and sought to identify any evidence gaps. Results were reported with descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Of 111 respondents (51% orthopaedic surgeons), 90% were involved in managing early MJA wound problems. Most (94.6%) considered early wound problems serious. Skin reactions (32.4%) and superficial wound infections (28.8%) were the most frequently cited causes. Respondents generally believed superficial infections could not be clinically distinguished from deep infections, but could be managed with oral antibiotics in primary care. However, a need for further evidence was expressed, particularly regarding diagnostic utility, intervention thresholds, and clear guidelines to differentiate superficial from deep infections. Common superficial infection signs included red skin and localized swelling, while deep infections were thought to present with fever and deep pain.

CONCLUSION: Healthcare professionals recognize the seriousness of early postoperative wound problems, frequently encountering skin reactions and superficial SSIs. While superficial infections are often managed nonoperatively, there is a clear demand for high-level evidence and comprehensive guidelines to improve differentiation and management. This should ultimately enhance patient outcomes, reduce the time to correct diagnosis and management, and limit the need for unnecessary treatments and associated complications.

articles.title: Abrogation of EMP1 Mitigates MASH-Associated Hepatic Fibrosis through Suppression of the JAK/STAT Signaling Axis.
articles.journal: Biochemistry and cell biology = Biochimie et biologie cellulaire
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by fibrogenesis, posing high risks for cirrhosis and cancer. Epithelial membrane protein 1 (EMP1) is a biomarker in fibrosis, but its role in MASH is unclear.EMP1 expression was assessed in MASH mouse models (MCD/HFD-induced) and human MASH specimens. The functional effects of EMP1 silencing and overexpression were evaluated in vivo, focusing on steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, the interaction between EMP1 and the JAK/STAT pathway was examined. EMP1 expression was significantly upregulated in both murine MASH models and human MASH liver tissues compared to healthy controls. Functionally, in vivo silencing of EMP1 markedly attenuated hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammatory infiltration, and fibrogenesis in mice fed MCD or HFD. Conversely, EMP1 overexpression exacerbated MASH progression, with a pronounced effect on fibrogenesis. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that EMP1 promotes the phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3 via its specific interaction with JAK2, whereas silencing EMP1 disrupts JAK2-mediated activation of downstream signal transducers. This inhibition of the JAK/STAT axis resulted in the suppression of hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, a key event in fibrogenesis. Our findings establish EMP1 as a critical pathogenic mediator in MASH-related fibrosis. By directly regulating the JAK2/STAT1/3 signaling axis in HSCs, EMP1 promotes fibrogenesis, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of MASH.

articles.title: Thrombin-mediated AutoRegulation of FVIII-mimetic antibodies enabling dynamic control of the hemostatic response.
articles.abstract: Emicizumab has transformed hemophilia A (HA) management by enabling effective subcutaneous prophylaxis independent of inhibitor status. However, its constitutive activity and lack of sensitivity to anticoagulant feedback contribute to excessive thrombin generation under certain conditions, particularly when combined with bypassing agents, a liability increasingly recognized as a class effect of FVIII-mimetic antibodies. We engineered an "AutoRegulated" (AR) FVIII-mimetic antibody by integrating a short thrombin cleavable peptide sensitive to the proteolytic activity of thrombin in the hinge region of both emicizumab arms. Insertion of the peptide did not impair structural integrity and biological function with AR-emicizumab demonstrating EC50 values of FVIII-mimetic activity and correction of blood loss in HA mice comparable to the parental emicizumab. However, the presence of thrombin-mediated AR enabled thrombin-responsive proteolytic inactivation upon exposure to supra-physiological thrombin levels, whereas the parental emicizumab remained unaffected. The dynamic control provided by AR efficiently reduced the procoagulant effects induced by co-administration of activated Prothrombin Complex Concentrates (aPCC). In thrombin generation assays, AR-emicizumab significantly attenuated the excessive thrombin peak observed with emicizumab. Similarly, in vivo, the presence of thrombin-mediated AR prevented platelet consumptive coagulopathy and reduced the microvascular pulmonary thrombosis induced by the parental molecule without affecting the systemic levels of the therapeutic antibody. This on-demand self-limiting mechanism aligns therapeutic activity with local hemostatic needs, may offer a promising therapeutic approach for HA patients, while establishing a generalizable strategy to improve the safety profile of next-generation hemostatic biologics.

articles.title: Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure.

METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79).

CONCLUSIONS: The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

articles.title: Virtual Reality for Delirium Prevention in Intensive Care Unit Nurses and Mechanically Ventilated Patients: Descriptive Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who are on mechanical ventilation are at high risk of developing delirium. Virtual reality (VR) technology, as an emerging intervention method, shows promising application prospects in delirium prevention, but its specific experience in clinical practice still requires in-depth exploration.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to explore the real experiences of ICU nurses and mechanically ventilated patients in participating in VR delirium prevention, with the aim of providing practical evidence for the optimization and application of this technology in clinical practice.

METHODS: A descriptive qualitative research design was adopted. From March to June 2025, using purposive sampling, participants were selected from the internal medicine, surgery, central, and respiratory ICU departments of a tertiary hospital in Zhengzhou. A total of 73 patients on mechanical ventilation were screened. Among them, 49 were excluded due to not meeting the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) or Barthel Index (BI) score criteria, 5 had delirium at the time of enrollment, 1 was excluded due to visual impairment, and 2 voluntarily withdrew during the study. Finally, 16 patients on mechanical ventilation and 16 nurses were included for semistructured interviews. Data analysis was conducted using the inductive content analysis method.

RESULTS: Through the analysis of the interview data, a total of 3 main themes and 14 subthemes were extracted. In terms of perceived benefits, patients experienced an immersive environment and a sense of empowerment driven by tasks, while nurses felt the convenience of resource integration, the intimacy of the nurse-patient relationship, and a sense of professional significance. In terms of perceived challenges, patients faced difficulties with the interaction interface and physical and mental obstacles, while nurses encountered difficulties in communication assessment and responsibility definition. In terms of perceived needs, patients expected personalized content design and continuity of nursing services, while nurses suggested differentiated content adjustment, comprehensive functional integration, and standardized safety management.

CONCLUSIONS: The participants expressed a positive attitude towards the prevention of delirium based on VR and reported various perceived benefits, challenges, and needs. Future research should prioritize content personalization, functional integration, and safety management. Meanwhile, it is necessary to recognize the limitations of this technology in specific target populations. For those who do not meet the inclusion criteria, adaptive alternative intervention measures should be developed to promote the precise and sustainable application of VR-based delirium prevention.

articles.title: Feasibility of a Co-Designed Personalized Cognitive Reablement Program Delivered via Digital Voice Assistants for Older Adults Living With Early-Stage Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home-based reablement programs have improved everyday functioning for people living with early-stage dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the substantial time commitment required for delivery by health professionals has created a barrier to widespread implementation. Digital technology could facilitate delivery, but traditional devices such as smartphones and tablets present usability challenges for this population. We have co-designed a cognitive reablement program, VOICE-COG, that can deliver personalized interventions broadcast via voice-controlled digital voice assistants (DVAs).

OBJECTIVE: This pilot nonblinded randomized controlled trial examined the feasibility and potential effectiveness of VOICE-COG for older adults living with dementia or MCI to guide the design of a full-scale trial.

METHODS: Older adults (aged 60-85 years) with a self-reported diagnosis of dementia or MCI (N=30) were recruited via Facebook or the StepUp-for Dementia Research database and randomized to either a DVA intervention (n=15) or control (n=15) group for 12 weeks. Each participant randomized to the intervention group and their care partner met with a psychologist via Zoom to select 2 or 3 personalized goals from the VOICE-COG program. The personalized program was input into the software (BuddyLink) by researchers for broadcast via a DVA (Amazon Alexa Show 8). Participants in the control group received enhanced usual care, consisting of treatment as usual, plus weekly informational emails. Primary feasibility outcomes were recruitment, retention, device-recorded adherence, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). Secondary outcomes were self-reported by the participant and care partner via web-based Qualtrics forms and included the Goal Attainment Scale-Light (GAS), changes in participant mood, cognition, and everyday functioning, and carer burden.

RESULTS: The recruitment rate was 86% (30/35) and the retention rate was 97% (29/30), with 1 participant in the intervention group lost to follow-up. Adherence to the VOICE-COG program ranged from 29% to 100% (mean 70%, SD 17%). The VOICE-COG program was rated as marginally acceptable (mean SUS score 56.3, SD 18.1). After 12 weeks, 60% (9/15) of the intervention group reported having met or exceeded their goals (GAS-Light t-score ≥50; mean 57.6, SD 15.4). The intervention group had a significantly higher increase in Multifactorial Memory Questionnaire-Strategy subscale score compared with control, mean difference 5.0 (95% CI 0.03-10.1, P=.049), representing a medium effect size (d=0.55). There were no other significant differences between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: This co-designed VOICE-COG program, delivered via DVAs, was feasible for older adults living with early-stage dementia or MCI, resulting in most participants meeting their reablement goals and increases in the use of memory strategies. System usability issues should be addressed in future adequately powered trials.

articles.title: The Impact of Telemedicine Interventions on Maternal and Fetal Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) has a rising global prevalence and brings short-term and long-term adverse risks for mothers and fetuses. Conventional in-person GDM care is limited by time and geographic barriers, often resulting in suboptimal compliance and delayed individualized interventions. Telemedicine is increasingly applied in GDM management; however, randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence remains inconsistent.

OBJECTIVE: The study aims to pool data from RCTs to quantify the effects of telemedicine on glycemic control and pregnancy-related outcomes in women with GDM and to inform optimized clinical management.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to August 16, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Meta-analyses were conducted in Stata 18.0. For heterogeneous outcomes, 95% prediction intervals (PIs) were calculated to estimate effect ranges for future studies. Heterogeneity was explored via leave-one-out sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses. The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) framework rated evidence certainty. Publication bias was evaluated for outcomes reported in ≥10 studies.

RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs (3055 women with GDM) were included. Pooled estimates suggested that telemedicine may reduce fasting glucose (mean difference [MD] -0.26, 95% CI -0.42 to -0.09, 95% PI -0.93 to 0.42; P=.002), 2-hour postprandial glucose (MD -0.50, 95% CI -0.87 to -0.14, 95% PI -1.84 to 0.84; P=.007), and gestational weight gain (MD -0.78, 95% CI -1.40 to -0.17, 95% PI -2.83 to 1.26; P=.01). Telemedicine was also associated with lower risks of cesarean section, emergency cesarean section, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, and neonatal respiratory distress. No significant differences were found for hemoglobin A1c, preterm birth, or neonatal intensive care unit admission. Notably, fasting glucose, 2-hour postprandial glucose, and gestational weight gain exhibited very high unexplained heterogeneity (I²>90%), with their 95% PIs crossing the null value despite statistically significant pooled effects. The GRADE certainty of evidence was very low to low across all assessed outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Telemedicine may improve selected glycemic and perinatal outcomes for women with GDM and may serve as a promising supplementary option for prenatal care, particularly in resource-limited settings where routine in-person follow-up is difficult to implement. Nevertheless, the apparent benefits for glycemic control and gestational weight gain remain tentative due to extreme, unexplained between-study heterogeneity and 95% PIs crossing the null. Based on current evidence, telemedicine should not completely replace standard antenatal care. Future well-designed, large-sample RCTs are warranted; such trials should adopt standardized definitions for telemedicine interventions, fully report intervention components, and conduct long-term follow-up to verify sustained maternal and neonatal clinical benefits.

articles.title: Orofacial Strength in a Typically Developing Pediatric Population: A Comparison of the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument and Tongueometer.
articles.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pressure-based assessments of tongue strength are becoming increasingly common in dysphagia management. However, whether different manometric devices produce comparable measurements for the same tasks, particularly in pediatric populations, remains insufficiently clarified. The purposes of this study were to establish age- and sex-specific reference values for tongue, buccal, and lip strength in a pediatric population using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (IOPI) and the Tongueometer (TO) and to systematically examine the effects of device, age, and sex on these measurements, as well as the level of agreement between the two devices.

METHOD: A total of 330 typically developing children and adolescents aged 8-18 years were included. For all participants, anterior and posterior tongue strength, buccal strength, and lip (interlabial) strength were measured using both the IOPI and TO. Device, age, and sex effects were examined using mixed factorial analyses of variance. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges for both devices were reported using descriptive statistics. The agreement between devices was assessed using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman plots, while the relationship between devices was assessed using linear regression analysis.

RESULTS: Across all parameters, the TO consistently produced lower pressure values than the IOPI. Additionally, the correlation between all measurements obtained with both devices was moderate to strong. Lin's CCC values indicated poor agreement for all measurements, and Bland-Altman analyses demonstrated systematic bias between devices. Age had a strong main effect on tongue, lip, and buccal strength measurements obtained from both devices, whereas sex effects were generally limited and observed for buccal and lip strength measured.

CONCLUSIONS: The IOPI and TO systematically produce different pressure values in pediatric populations and should not be used interchangeably. Accordingly, this study provides age- and sex-specific reference values for both devices to support device-specific interpretation of tongue and orofacial strength measurements in children and adolescents. The results also indicate that age is a stronger determinant of tongue and orofacial strength during childhood and adolescence than sex.

articles.title: Evaluation of a Clinical Protocol-Guided Chatbot to Support Telecarers in Diabetes Management: Embedded Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic condition that requires ongoing self-management. While chatbots offer scalable monitoring and management, evidence on their integration into structured hospital tele-support workflows, where patient engagement and digital readiness may differ from those in standalone digital interventions, remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the design of a clinical protocol-guided chatbot, Sharing Information with Users on Diabetes Actions and Interventions (Siu Dai), and evaluate its feasibility, usability, and acceptability among patients and telecarers within a hospital tele-support program.

METHODS: We used an embedded mixed methods design (QUAL [quan]) guided by the World Health Organization (WHO) monitoring and evaluating digital health interventions and the theoretical framework of acceptability. Through a co-design process involving clinicians, researchers, telecarers, and developers, the chatbot was aligned with established clinical protocols. It featured 7 precall sessions designed to collect patient data, generate summary reports for staff, and deliver targeted educational content. Patients (≥21-year-old individuals with T2DM) and telecarer nurses (with experience ≥6 mo) were recruited from an existing tele-support program. Data sources included interviews, online surveys (5-point Likert scale), and chatbot usage logs. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically; quantitative data were summarized descriptively to supplement and contextualize the qualitative findings.

RESULTS: Fourteen participants (7 patients and 7 telecarers) completed both interviews and surveys and were included in the analysis. Patients (mean age 45.3, SD 15.4 y) had a median diabetes duration of 10 (IQR 3-25; range 1-30) years, and all were digitally literate. Telecarers had a median of 5 (IQR 4-9) years of telehealth experience. Quantitatively, patients showed high engagement, completing 79% of started sessions with a median completion time of 2 minutes and 58 seconds. Patient satisfaction was high, with 86% (6/7) willing to recommend the tool; however, telecarer endorsement for universal rollout to patients in other clinical programs or outpatient clinics was more cautious (3/7, 43%). Qualitative findings revealed 5 themes: (1) perceptions of chatbot usability, (2) alignment and integration into telecarers' processes, (3) factors influencing acceptability of the chatbot, (4) perceived efficacy of the chatbot for T2DM self-management and care delivery, and (5) suggested improvements and enhancements. Integrated findings revealed that the chatbot was usable and functioned as a precall support tool that optimized the personalization of tele-support sessions. However, its perceived efficacy in self-management behavior was limited by this cohort's extensive experience with T2DM management. Key barriers to adoption included administrative burden for telecarers due to a lack of electronic medical record integration and content redundancy for patients. Suggested enhancements included multilingual support and adaptive content catering to different levels of disease-specific literacy.

CONCLUSIONS: A clinical protocol-guided chatbot is feasible for hospital tele-support, complementing rather than replacing human care. It automates routine assessments and reinforces education, but future iterations must prioritize workflow integration and adaptive content to sustain engagement.

articles.title: Comparing hemolysis among extracorporeal pumps: A large-scale retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundHemolysis is a frequent and clinically relevant complication during extracorporeal life support (ECLS, or ECMO), associated with acute kidney injury, systemic inflammation, and increased mortality. Direct comparisons between pumps regarding hemolysis are limited. This study evaluated and compared hemolysis profiles among several devices in clinical practice.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study adult patients who received veno-arterial (V-A) or veno-venous (V-V) ECMO between January 2020 and December 2023 (N = 230). Patients were categorized by one of four ECMO pump types, and hemolysis was assessed using lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and plasma-free hemoglobin (pfHb) as primary markers. Multivariable linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze associations between pump type and hemolysis, adjusting for several covariates including revolutions per minute (RPM), hematologic indices, ECMO mode, and severity scores.ResultsPartial thromboplastin time (p < 0.005), hemoglobin (p < 0.001), and use of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, p < 0.001) were positively correlated with both LDH and pfHb concentrations and hemolysis, while fibrinogen (p < 0.03) was inversely correlated. Without RPM adjustment, NovaLung exhibited the highest LDH (680.3 U/L) and pfHb (29.4 mg/dL), followed by the Cardiohelp, Rotaflow, and CentriMag. In the RPM-adjusted analysis, LDH was highest in Cardiohelp (737.4 U/L), followed by the Rotaflow, CentriMag, and NovaLung; whereas pfHb was highest in Cardiohelp (25.8 mg/dL), followed by the Rotaflow, NovaLung, and CentriMag.ConclusionsThis study provides a clinical associations of the safety and performance of four centrifugal pumps in real-world ECMO practice in adults. We demonstrate that pump-specific RPM may be potentially correlated with hemolysis during ECMO in clinical practice, illustrating that the diagonal pump, which operated at the highest RPMs, was associated with the highest hemolysis in models without the RPM adjustment. Future studies are warranted to further clarify the impact of hemolysis on outcomes.

articles.title: Protective Effects of PD-L1-Overexpressing MSCs and Their Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: This study was conducted to address the urgent need for novel therapies for type 1 diabetes. We investigated whether programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (PD-L1-MSCs) and their extracellular vesicles (PEVs) can modulate immune responses and protect pancreatic islets, and whether these effects depend on PD-L1 signaling. Our results demonstrate that both PD-L1-MSCs and PEVs suppress T-cell activity, enhance regulatory T-cell populations, delay the onset of diabetes, and reduce immune cell infiltration in pancreatic islets. These findings suggest that PD-L1-MSCs and PEVs represent promising therapeutic strategies for type 1 diabetes by promoting immune tolerance and preserving β-cell function.

articles.title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways.
articles.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type-specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

articles.title: NAD+ metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

articles.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8+ T cell fates through the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 axis.
articles.abstract: CD8+ T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8+ T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8+ T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8+ T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8+ T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

articles.title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain.
articles.abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

articles.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection.
articles.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (Ifnar1-/-) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/-) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/- dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ-responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

articles.title: Early Experience of a Dedicated Outpatient Palliative Hepatology Clinic: Referral Patterns, Patient Characteristics, and Outcomes.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: Background and AimsDedicated outpatient palliative hepatology clinics remain uncommon despite the substantial symptom burden of advanced liver disease. We describe the early experience of a newly established outpatient palliative hepatology clinic.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients scheduled for an initial consultation during the first months of clinic operation. Demographic and clinical characteristics, referral indications and sources, symptoms, advance care planning, follow-up, and outcomes were collected from the electronic medical record and summarized using descriptive statistics.ResultsAmong 26 scheduled patients, median age was 60 years (IQR, 41-71), median MELD 3.0 was 21 (IQR, 14-30), and 23 (89%) had prior cirrhosis-related hospitalization(s). Common referral indications included supportive care needs (81%), goals-of-care discussions (65%), and symptom management (39%). Referrals primarily came from hepatology/gastroenterology (54%) and inpatient palliative care (31%). Eighteen patients (69%) attended; 4 (15%) died before their scheduled appointment. Among those evaluated, pain and nausea were most common (56% each). Goals-of-care discussions occurred in 67%, advance directives were discussed in 72%, and surrogate decision makers in 83%. During a median follow-up of 192 days, 61% returned for follow-up and 33% died. Median time from the initial clinic visit to death was 51 days.ConclusionsPatients referred to our palliative hepatology clinic had advanced disease and substantial supportive care needs. High rates of goals-of-care and advance care planning among those evaluated highlight the potential value of dedicated palliative hepatology clinics.

articles.title: The management of patients with positive non-tuberculous mycobacterium cultures at a local centre in New Zealand-a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We aimed to assess whether management of patients with positive non-tuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) cultures at Palmerston North Hospital aligns with international guidelines.

METHOD: We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients with positive mycobacterial cultures between 1 December 2020 and 1 December 2022 in the MidCentral Region. Electronic records were reviewed for microbiological sampling, radiological assessment, treatment decisions, monitoring and outcomes. Management was compared with the 2017 British Thoracic Society and 2020 American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America guidelines.

RESULTS: Fifty-four adult patients were included. Thirty-two (59%) met microbiological criteria for NTM pulmonary disease, and 22 (41%) met full diagnostic criteria. Fifty (93%) had at least two sputum samples sent, with 43 (80%) of these sent on separate days. The median number of days from sputum positivity to computed tomography (CT) was 63 days. Of those that met diagnostic criteria, 13 patients were offered treatment, 11 commenced therapy and five achieved culture conversion. Ten patients discontinued therapy. Reasons for treatment cessation were multifactorial and included persistent culture positivity, medication intolerance, medication interactions and radiographic improvement. Surveillance sputum monitoring during treatment was documented in 64% of cases. Sensitivity testing was performed in 40% of those who were treated for Mycobacterium avium. Treatment duration was variable with a median duration of 762 days.

CONCLUSION: Management was broadly consistent with international guidelines. Improvements are needed in microbiological sampling completeness, sensitivity testing, timely CT imaging and treatment monitoring. These findings highlight opportunities to standardise NTM diagnostic and follow-up pathways in a regional New Zealand centre.

articles.title: Health complexity, metabolic health and service use in a high need primary care population in Aotearoa New Zealand: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this study was to understand the characteristics, health complexity and intensity of service provision for patients aged 16 years or older enrolled in a high-need practice.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study used routinely collected data from an urban Very Low Cost Access practice serving a high-need population in Cannons Creek, Porirua, Aotearoa New Zealand. All patients aged ≥16 years enrolled for a 12-month period were included. Demographic, clinical, biological, medication and service use variables were extracted, and individuals were categorised into normoglycaemia, prediabetes and diabetes groups. Analyses used descriptive statistics, age-standardised rates and comparative assessments of health complexity and service utilisation.

RESULTS: The population (n=4,715) was predominantly Pacific, with most living in areas of high socio-economic deprivation and 25% classified with prediabetes or diabetes. Younger adults with diabetes had disproportionately high HbA1c and elevated albuminuria. Long-term conditions (LTCs), particularly obesity-related conditions, increased progressively across the glycaemic spectrum, with twofold to fourfold higher rates in dysglycaemia. Prediabetes and diabetes groups had similar LTC profiles. Service use increased with worsening dysglycaemia, with individuals with diabetes having nearly double the consultation rates, triple the prescription counts and markedly higher emergency department and ambulatory sensitive hospitalisation rates.

CONCLUSION: Dysglycaemia and multiple LTCs are common and resource-intensive in this population. Together, these data highlight the urgent need for proactive, well-resourced, equity-focussed primary care models to address metabolic risk, LTCs and high service demand.

articles.title: Perspectives on weight-loss pharmacotherapy among Māori and Pacific adults with overweight or obesity in Aotearoa New Zealand: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this study was to examine the perceived acceptability of obesity medicines (OMs) among Māori and Pacific health consumers in Aotearoa New Zealand and identify key concerns that may influence acceptance.

METHODS: An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted with 216 Māori and Pacific adults, 190 of whom were living with overweight or obesity. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics to summarise participant characteristics and key outcomes, alongside multivariable logistic regression. A mediation analysis was performed using a non-parametric bootstrapping procedure.

RESULTS: Descriptive analyses show that the majority of participants viewed OMs as an acceptable tool for weight management; however, common concerns included cost, effectiveness, subsequent weight gain, unknown impacts on the body and long-term dependence. Patterns were similar by gender, although limited male representation restricted comparisons. Multivariable analyses showed that administration method (oral vs injection) significantly mediated ethnic differences in acceptability, with Pacific participants expressing higher concern compared to Māori.

CONCLUSION: Although OMs were broadly acceptable among Māori and Pacific participants, concerns about their use may influence uptake and sustained use. Addressing these barriers, together with administration-related concerns that may contribute to ethnic differences in acceptability, may support more equitable implementation of OMs. Future research could use longitudinal and qualitative designs to explore how cultural and contextual factors shape perspectives over time. These findings highlight an opportunity to improve obesity care and health outcomes for Māori and Pacific people by supporting more accessible and culturally appropriate integration of OMs into care pathways.

articles.title: RES NPs/GelMA Sustained-Release Cryogel Modulates Macrophage Arachidonic Acid Metabolism and Angiogenic Microenvironment Promoting Diabetic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Refractory chronic diabetic wounds severely impair quality of life. Their delayed healing is mainly driven by impaired angiogenesis and persistent inflammation caused by infection and excessive ROS. Resveratrol (RES) has anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Here, we developed a dual-mechanism sustained-release system for RES to promote diabetic wound healing. RES was converted into nanoparticles (RES NPs) to improve cellular uptake and bioavailability, then encapsulated in GelMA cryogel microspheres (CMS) for injectable, sustained release. This system downregulated NF-κB signaling, reduced ROS, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and COX2, thereby inhibiting arachidonic acid metabolism and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. Meanwhile, AMPK activation restored endothelial cell function, enhanced angiogenesis, and supported new vessel formation. Overall, this strategy accelerated high-quality wound repair in diabetic conditions.

articles.title: HIV-1 cell-to-cell infection of macrophages escapes restriction by the BST-2 host cell factor independently of the Vpu counteracting viral protein.
articles.abstract: As HIV-1 target cells, macrophages can be infected by cell-to-cell virus transfer from infected T cells through cell-cell fusion leading to the formation of virus-productive multinucleated giant cells (MGCs). We recently demonstrated that this route of infection escaped host cell restriction acting on the early steps of the viral life cycle. Here, we investigated whether restriction factors acting on late steps of HIV-1 replication were also bypassed in virus cell-to-cell infection of macrophages. We focused on the impact of the interferon(IFN)-induced factor BST-2/tetherin acting on virus release, a process counteracted by the Vpu viral protein. We show that deletion of Vpu did not significantly affect HIV-1 cell-to-cell infection of IFN-stimulated macrophages, and virus assembly in virus containing compartments was not affected in MGCs. Accordingly, depletion of BST-2 in IFN-stimulated macrophages had no impact on virus cell-to-cell transfer, formation of MGCs and virus production. However, cell-to-cell infection of macrophages was still sensitive to the nelfinavir protease inhibitor, whereas we previously showed that this route of infection was resistant to antiviral drugs acting on early steps of virus replication. Our results show that HIV-1 cell-to-cell infection of macrophages escapes restriction factors acting on both early and late steps of the virus life cycle, but displays resistance to antiviral drugs specifically acting on the early steps of virus replication.

articles.title: Epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of a large-scale upsurge of dengue in the rohingya refugee camps and host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, 2021 to 2024: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue emerged as a new public health threat in the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, in 2021 and expanded into large-scale upsurges in subsequent years. Evidence on dengue epidemiology and clinical presentation in protracted refugee settings remains limited, despite the need for stronger outbreak preparedness and case management in these contexts.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of the dengue upsurge among Rohingya refugees and surrounding host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, and to identify predictors of inpatient admission and diagnostic positivity patterns.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study used anonymized surveillance data from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) dengue patient database. Rapid diagnostic test (RDT)-confirmed dengue cases identified across 36 IOM-supported health facilities in Ukhiya and Teknaf between 1 October 2021 and 31 December 2024 were included. Demographic, epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory variables were summarized using descriptive statistics. Weekly case counts were aggregated by epidemiological week and calendar year, and epidemic growth and decay phases were modelled using phase-specific Poisson regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with inpatient admission, while separate models examined associations between delay in presentation and RDT positivity patterns, adjusting for age and sex.

RESULTS: A total of 35,581 RDT-confirmed dengue cases were reported, of which 90.2% occurred among Rohingya refugees. The median age was 17 years (IQR 7-30), and 46.0% of cases were among children aged 0-14 years. Annual caseload increased from 1,011 in 2021-11,752 in 2022, 10,669 in 2023 and 12,149 in 2024, with seasonal peaks during the monsoon period and progressively later peaks and longer epidemic tails over time. Poisson models showed decreasing growth rates across years (r = 0.449 in 2021 to r = 0.091 in 2024) with increasing doubling times, while decay rates remained broadly comparable (halving time ~4.4-6.0 weeks). Overall, 8.0% of cases required inpatient admission, 1.3% were referred, and four deaths were reported (case fatality <0.1%). In multivariable analysis, inpatient admission was associated with older age (≥60 vs 0-14: aOR 2.48), delayed presentation (aOR 1.06 per day), refugee status (aOR 1.43), fever ≥38°C at presentation (aOR 1.13), presence of any WHO warning sign (aOR 28.87), and chronic co-morbidity (aOR 6.63). Males had lower odds of admission than females (aOR 0.87).

CONCLUSION: Sustained dengue preparedness is required in Cox's Bazar, including strengthened surveillance, community-based early referral, targeted monitoring of high-risk groups, environmental vector control, and phase-appropriate use of NS1 and IgM/IgG diagnostics to reduce missed diagnoses and prevent progression to severe disease. These findings highlight the need for a policy shift from episodic outbreak response toward sustained dengue preparedness in humanitarian settings, including strengthened surveillance systems, integrated diagnostic strategies, community-based early referral, and coordinated vector control interventions.

articles.title: Temporal Patterns of Multimorbidity Progression Among Inpatients With a Recorded Hypertension Diagnosis Across Three Counties in Rural Henan, China: Retrospective Cohort Study Using Temporal Network Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a key driver of multimorbidity; however, its role in shaping dynamic disease progression, especially in rural populations, remains underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize temporal patterns of multimorbidity progression among inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis and to examine whether these patterns differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county.

METHODS: We analyzed electronic health record data from 34,099 inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis across 3 rural counties in Henan, China (2019-2023), constructing a temporal comorbidity network of 250 disease nodes and 1512 disease transitions. Statistical validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, case-dropping, and permutation tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, insurance type, and county.

RESULTS: The temporal comorbidity network revealed a densely interconnected core involving hypertension, atherosclerotic heart disease, and cerebral infarction, with type 2 diabetes occupying a bridging position between cardiovascular and multisystem disease clusters. The ordering of dominant recorded pathways differed by sex (earlier coronary involvement among female inpatients vs more direct progression to stroke among male inpatients), was more complex in inpatients older than 70 years of age, and was more diffuse among those covered by urban-rural resident insurance compared with urban employee insurance.

CONCLUSIONS: Multimorbidity among inpatients with recorded hypertension followed structured and heterogeneous temporal patterns that differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions formed the principal recorded progression pathways, while type 2 diabetes connected cardiovascular pathways with broader multisystem complications. These findings support further evaluation of risk-stratified and locally adapted approaches to chronic disease prevention and longitudinal care.

articles.title: Schistosomiasis as an urban disease: 13 years of studies in the neighborhoods of Salvador, BA, Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid urbanization in Brazil has shifted the epidemiological landscape of parasitic diseases, such as schistosomiasis and malaria. Although typically considered a rural infection, Schistosoma mansoni transmission persists in urban settings where sanitation and water access remain uneven. This study investigates the persistence and dynamics of urban schistosomiasis across neighborhoods of Salvador, Bahia, Brazil.

METHODS: Between 2011 and 2024 cross-sectional surveys were conducted to identify neighborhoods with the highest prevalence in the major metropolitan area of Salvador, Bahia. A total of 6,863 residents provided demographic information and Kato-Katz examination of at least one stool sample. We conducted demographic surveys and stool examination on 3,964 individuals who were re-examined on up to three occasions at intervals ranging from 1-5 years.

FINDINGS: The overall prevalence of initial examination was 7%. Regardless of treatment intervals, the community-wide prevalence declined by more than half and did not rebound. Apparent Incidence decreased to <0.5%/year following a second period of treatment. In nearly all communities, most infections occurred among individuals born in Salvador with no travel history outside the city.

INTERPRETATION: Overall, the study provides one of the first individual-level longitudinal assessments of schistosomiasis persistence in an urban Brazilian setting, combining repeated parasitological surveys with demographic and environmental data across multiple neighborhoods. These findings indicate that schistosomiasis transmission in Salvador is largely local rather than imported. The decline in prevalence coincides with observed community-level improvements in sanitation and reduced contact with surface water. f prevalence rates were applied across the population of Salvador, this city could be considered one of the state's most important endemic areas.

articles.title: Vector competence of Aedes albopictus and Culex quinquefasciatus for Oropouche virus.
articles.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an arthropod-borne virus transmitted mainly by Culicoides paraensis midges in Latin America and the Caribbean, though evidence suggests occasional transmission by mosquitoes. Oropouche fever has been reported primarily in the Amazon Basin since the 1950s. In 2024, the number of Oropouche fever cases rose sharply and spread beyond the Amazon region, which has been associated with the emergence of a new reassortant OROV strain. We assessed whether increased case numbers could be explained by enhanced replication or transmission of the reassortant strain in peri-urban Culex quinquefasciatus and Aedes albopictus. Laboratory colonies established from Salvador, Brazil were orally exposed to the ancestral OROV strain BeAn 19991 or the contemporary strain 240023 (10⁴-10⁶ PFU/mL), and viral replication was quantified in bodies, legs, and saliva. To evaluate the influence of mosquito genotype on infection outcomes, infection rates were compared between Ae. albopictus from Salvador City (Brazil) and Houston (USA). In Cx. quinquefasciatus, the outbreak strain replicated less efficiently than the historical strain at low viral doses but not at high infection doses. Regardless of strain or dose, vector competence was extremely low, with only 0-1% of mosquitoes exhibiting infectious OROV particles in their saliva after extrinsic incubation. Conversely, Ae. albopictus showed consistently higher body infection rates for the 240023 strain than for BeAn 19991 at both low and high doses. However, overall transmission potential remained limited: only 0-6.4% of leg or saliva samples were positive across OROV strains and doses. The higher infection rates of the 240023 strain was consistent across both Ae. albopictus genotypes, but infectious saliva was detected only in mosquitoes from the Salvador line (up to 20%) and not in the Houston line (0%). Taken together, this suggests that the recent geographic expansion of OROV is unlikely to be driven by a vector shift from midges to these mosquitoes. Importantly, our findings do indicate higher infectivity of the 240023 strain in Ae. albopictus across different mosquito lines which may have future implications for further adaptation to OROV.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of fluoroquinolones in the treatment of human brucellosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brucellosis is a major zoonotic infection worldwide, with the highest burden reported in the Mediterranean region. The therapeutic role of fluoroquinolones in this disease continues to be controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of fluoroquinolone-containing regimens compared with standard non-fluoroquinolone regimens for the treatment of human brucellosis.

METHODS: In accordance with PRISMA recommendations, this systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of fluoroquinolone-based regimens for treating brucellosis. It was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251142019). A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was carried out, including studies published through August 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing fluoroquinolones with conventional therapies (such as doxycycline with streptomycin or rifampicin) were included. Therapeutic failure, relapse, adverse events, and time to defervescence were the main outcomes. To compute pooled risk ratios and mean differences with 95%CIs, data were analyzed using STATA v18. The GRADE method and the RoB 2 tool were used to evaluate the risk of bias and the certainty of the evidence.

RESULTS: The analysis comprised 9 clinical studies with 602 brucellosis patients. When compared to standard regimens, fluoroquinolone-based regimens were linked to a significantly higher risk of therapeutic failure (RR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.26-3.51; P = 0.004) and a higher, though not statistically significant, risk of relapse (RR = 1.88, 95% CI: 0.94-3.74; P = 0.07). No statistically significant between-study heterogeneity was observed for either outcome (I² = 0%). Subgroup analyses showed a significantly increased risk of therapeutic failure in patients with uncomplicated brucellosis and in studies with treatment durations >8 weeks, although between-subgroup differences were not statistically significant. On the other hand, no statistically significant difference in adverse events was observed between fluoroquinolone-based and standard regimens under the random-effects model (RR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.29-1.33; P = 0.22). Although the point estimate favored fluoroquinolone-based regimens, the confidence interval included the null effect. Fluoroquinolone-based regimens were also associated with a significantly longer time to defervescence compared with standard regimens (MD = 1.20 days, 95% CI: 0.66-1.74; P < 0.001). The certainty of evidence was moderate for therapeutic failure, and time to defervescence, and low for relapse and adverse events according to the GRADE evaluation.

CONCLUSION: Compared with conventional doxycycline-based combinations, fluoroquinolone-based regimens were associated with a higher risk of therapeutic failure and longer time to defervescence, while the overall risk of relapse did not differ significantly. No significant difference in adverse events was observed with the random-effects model, although the point estimate favored fluoroquinolone-based regimens. Overall, these findings do not support the routine use of fluoroquinolones as first-line therapy for adult brucellosis. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed.

articles.title: Association of the free triiodothyronine to thyroxine ratio with acute post-stroke cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: International journal of psychiatry in clinical practice
articles.abstract:
