OBJECTIVE: Thyroid dysfunction is recognised as a modulator of cognitive outcomes in stroke survivors. The free triiodothyronine (FT3)/free thyroxine (FT4) ratio remains unexplored in post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI). This study aimed to investigate the association between the FT3/FT4 ratio and PSCI.

METHODS: Five hundred and twenty-three patients with ischaemic stroke were enrolled. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Participants were stratified into PSCI (n = 272) and non-PSCI (n = 251) groups based on education-adjusted MMSE thresholds. Thyroid hormone levels were measured, and the FT3/FT4 ratio was categorised into tertiles.

RESULTS: Patients with PSCI exhibited significantly higher FT4 (p < 0.001) and lower FT3 (p < 0.001) levels compared to non-PSCI patients, resulting in a reduced FT3/FT4 ratio (p < 0.001). Logistic regression revealed that the lowest tertile of the FT3/FT4 ratio was independently associated with PSCI (OR = 2.135, p = 0.002). The FT3/FT4 ratio demonstrated superior discriminative ability compared to FT3 (p = 0.047) or FT4 (p = 0.021) alone, as indicated by a larger area under the curve (AUC).

CONCLUSIONS: A reduced FT3/FT4 ratio is independently associated with PSCI in the acute phase of ischaemic stroke, identifying it as a potential risk marker for PSCI.

articles.title: Dose-response relationship of exercise intervention on cognitive function in patients with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on cognitive function in stroke patients and to explore the dose-response relationship based on metabolic equivalent minutes per week (MET·min/week).

METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted from database inception through 25 August 2026, across five electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library), two clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform [ICTRP]), and a gray literature database (ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global). A nonlinear dose-response model was used to examine the association between weekly exercise dose (MET·min/week) and improvement in cognitive function after stroke.

RESULTS: Eighteen articles (19 RCTs; 1,324 patients) were included. Exercise interventions were associated with improvements in global cognitive function (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI 0.14-0.36, p < 0.001). Between-subgroup differences were significant for exercise modality (p = 0.047), but not for exercise frequency, intervention duration, session duration, or time since stroke. The dose-response curve suggested a potentially nonlinear association between weekly exercise dose and cognitive effects within the observed dose range, with a relatively high model-predicted effect at approximately 465 MET·min/week (Hedges' g = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.26-0.73).

CONCLUSIONS: Exercise interventions were associated with improvements in post-stroke cognitive function. Dose-response analysis suggested a potentially nonlinear association between weekly exercise dose and cognitive effects, with a relatively high effect estimate at approximately 465 MET·min/week. However, this finding was exploratory and requires further validation.

articles.title: Feasibility of 2% Taurolidine Lock Therapy in 1-2 Fr Neonatal PICCs: A Three Patient Case series.
articles.abstract: Introduction Catheter-related bloodstream infection remains a major complication of neonatal central venous access. Although taurolidine lock therapy has been used in neonatal populations, experience with taurolidine locking in ultra-small (1-2 Fr) neonatal peripherally inserted central catheters (n-PICCs) remains extremely limited. This study describes the feasibility of repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy in neonates requiring prolonged central vascular access. Methods We retrospectively reviewed three neonates who received repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy during routine care in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit. Locks were administered using a standardized local protocol for therapeutic or prophylactic indications. Collected data included catheter characteristics, lock administration and aspiration, flushing requirements, catheter patency, adverse events, and clinical outcomes. Results Taurolidine lock therapy was performed in 1-2 Fr n-PICCs, with all 30 planned procedures completed. Aspiration after the dwell period was unsuccessful in every procedure, requiring flushing of the residual solution. Catheter patency was maintained, with no occlusion, thrombosis, mechanical complications, or taurolidine-related adverse events. Bloodstream infection resolved with concomitant systemic antimicrobials in the therapeutic case, while no catheter-related bloodstream infection occurred during prophylactic locking. Conclusion This preliminary clinical experience demonstrates the technical feasibility of repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy in ultra-small n-PICCs while maintaining catheter patency. The consistent inability to aspirate the lock solution represents an important practical observation for future investigation. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the feasibility and safety of taurolidine lock therapy as a catheter-preserving strategy in neonates. A multicentre randomized controlled trial is planned to further investigate this approach.

articles.title: Trends in the etiologies and outcomes of idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury in the united states: The DILIN prospective registry, 2004 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is an infrequent cause of liver disease. The aim of this study is to report on temporal changes in the etiology and outcomes of idiosyncratic DILI in the United States DILIN Prospective study.

METHODS: The presenting clinical features and outcomes of consecutive high causality DILI cases followed for 6 months at multiple DILIN sites from 2004 to 2024 were compared over time and by suspect drug class, age, sex, and prior chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

RESULTS: Amongst the 1983 high causality cases, median age was 52 years, 59% were female, 54% had hepatocellular injury and antibiotics (41%) were the leading drug class. The median peak total bilirubin, INR and severity scores decreased significantly over time, as did the proportion of cases attributed to antimicrobials, including isoniazid and nitrofurantoin, and to central nervous system agents. In contrast, the proportion of herbal and dietary supplement (HDS) and antineoplastic drug cases (including checkpoint inhibitors), increased significantly. Patients with CLD had higher mortality compared to non-CLD patients. Pediatric patients presented more frequently with hepatocellular injury but had a lower overall and liver related mortality compared to adults. Oncology DILI patients had a 6-month mortality rate of 30% with most deaths attributed to non-liver related causes.

CONCLUSIONS: Over the past 20 years, a decreasing proportion of DILI cases are attributed to antibiotics while an increasing proportion are attributed to HDS products and antineoplastics. Oncology patients and those > 65 years old have significantly higher overall and liver-related mortality.

articles.title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

articles.title: Single-cell landscape of alcohol-related hepatitis reveals serum amyloid a hepatocytes as key drivers of disease pathogenesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Alcohol-related hepatitis (AH) is a severe form of alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). The cellular subpopulations that contribute to AH and dynamics remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify key cellular subpopulations and their interactions in AH and explore key mechanisms contributing to disease pathogenesis.

APPROACH RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed starting from liver biopsies from patients with AH, early-stage ALD, and healthy individuals. Immunofluorescence was used to validate protein expression of selected markers. Liver biopsy-derived organoids were generated and exposed to a conditioned medium recapitulating AH (AH-medium) to assess serum amyloid A (SAA) secretion by ELISA. Circulating SAA levels were measured in plasma samples obtained from patients at different stages of ALD. Our analysis revealed an atlas of several cell subpopulations of AH, including hepatocytes expressing SAA, scar-associated (SA) endothelial cells, Fibulin-3+ mesenchymal cells, SA-macrophages expressing MMP19, activated CD4+ and stressed/effector CD8+ T cell subsets, and hyperactivated neutrophils expressing FPR2. Cell-communication analysis predicted a strong SAA-FPR2 interaction between hepatocyte and neutrophil subpopulations in AH. We confirmed that AH-hepatocytes secreted SAA in organoid cultures after stimulation with AH-medium. We also found out that circulating SAA levels were elevated in AH and were associated with reduced survival.

CONCLUSIONS: The SAA-FPR2 pathway emerges as a potential mediator of inflammation in AH, offering potential therapeutic targets for this severe disease. This study provides new insights into the cellular heterogeneity and dynamics in ALD progression, dissecting AH at a single-cell level.

articles.title: Fulminant necrotizing enterocolitis associated with severe RSV infection in a preterm infant following Nirsevimab prophylaxis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis with the monoclonal antibody Nirsevimab has shown high efficacy in preventing severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants. However, the sequences of immunopathological phenomena leading to breakthrough infections and the role of RSV in causing extrapulmonary disease remain poorly understood. We report on a former preterm infant who developed an unusually severe form of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) requiring multiple emergency laparotomies and prolonged intensive care treatment in the context of severe RSV-bronchiolitis 22 days after passive immunization with Nirsevimab. RSV RNA was retrospectively detected using a validated RSV PCR assay in resected intestinal tissue obtained during the acute disease phase but was not detected in tissue collected during later surgical reconstruction. Our case highlights the need for clinicians to maintain a high index of suspicion for intestinal complications in infants with severe RSV infection. Although these findings raise the possibility of intestinal RSV involvement, a causal relationship between Nirsevimab prophylaxis, antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and NEC cannot be established from this single case. Confirmation in additional clinical and translational studies is required. Further clinical and translational studies are required to clarify the potential role of RSV in intestinal disease and the mechanisms underlying severe breakthrough infections.

articles.title: Moderate Elevation of Ambient Temperature Alleviates Growth Reduction Caused by Phosphorus Deficiency in Lotus japonicus Under Hydroponic Conditions.
articles.abstract: High-temperature stress driven by global warming and phosphorus (P) deficiency resulting from the depletion of phosphate rock reserves pose serious threats to modern agriculture. However, our understanding of the combined effects of these stresses on plants remains limited. In this study, we employed a hydroponic culture system to investigate the physiological and transcriptomic responses of the model legume Lotus japonicus to simultaneous moderate high-temperature and low-P conditions. Both elevated temperature and low-P individually reduced shoot biomass. Under low-P conditions, shoot biomass remained significantly lower than in P sufficient plants. However, the relative reduction was smaller under elevated temperature than under favorable temperature. L. japonicus exhibited enhanced root-secreted acid phosphatase activity in under low-P alone and displayed an increased organic acid (e.g. malate and citrate) exudation rates under elevated temperature, irrespective of the P supply. Root transcriptome analysis identified up-regulation of the PEPC1 gene, encoding phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, suggesting its potential involvement in organic acid root exudation. Additionally, elevated temperatures promoted metal ion translocation and uptake, increased anthocyanin accumulation, and enhanced carbohydrate transport in shoots. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that low-P stress altered heat shock protein expression, potentially associated with reduced ATP availability. These findings demonstrate that L. japonicus employs distinct and overlapping strategies to adapt to the combined stresses of elevated temperatures and P deficiency. These strategies include the adjustment of root exudation patterns, nutrient transport, and stress-responsive gene expression.

articles.title: Beyond sleep duration: nighttime glucose in gestational diabetes mellitus.
SEMAGLUTIDE TREATMENT IN TWO VERY YOUNG CHILDREN WITH SEVERE EARLY-ONSET OBESITY.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monogenic obesity comprises a group of rare genetic disorders characterized by severe early-onset obesity and hyperphagia. Pharmacological treatment options for severe early-onset obesity remain limited, particularly in young children.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report two children younger than 6 years of age with severe early-onset obesity, including one with genetically confirmed monogenic obesity, who showed reductions in BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment. Case-1: A 4.5-year-old girl with a homozygous ADCY3 (c.1102G>A) variant presented with severe obesity, hyperphagia, hypertension, hepatosteatosis and Blount's disease. Baseline BMI was 48.0 kg/m2 (+5.5 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.125 mg/week and titrated to 1.5 mg/week. After 18 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.5 to +4.1 (-25.5%), accompanied by improved in hyperphagia and resolution of left ventricular hypertrophy. No significant adverse effects were observed, and linear growth remained age appropriate. Case-2: A 3.3-year-old boy with hyperphagia, severe obesity and dyslipidaemia was diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY). Clinical Exome Sequencing identified no causative variant for obesity. Baseline BMI was 32.6 kg/m2 (+5.7 SDS). Semaglutide was initiated at 0.0625 mg/week and gradually titrated to 2.0 mg/week. After 21 months, BMI-SDS decreased from +5.7 to +4.4 (-22%). Treatment was generally well tolerated, with normal linear growth.

CONCLUSION: This two cases describe reductions BMI-SDS during semaglutide treatment in very young children with severe early-onset obesity, including one child with genetically confirmed ADCY3-related monogenic obesity. These findings suggest a potential clinical benefit of semaglutide in this young population, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

articles.title: Current aspects in surgical treatment of advanced heart failure with future durable mechanical circulatory support.
articles.journal: European surgical research. Europaische chirurgische Forschung. Recherches chirurgicales europeennes
articles.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, resulting in an increasing demand for long-term treatment options for patients with end-stage heart failure. While heart transplantation is the gold standard, donor organ shortage continues to be a major limitation, particularly in countries with opt-in consent systems. Summary Durable mechanical circulatory support (dMCS) devices have emerged as a critical therapy for patients with advanced heart failure, either as a bridge to transplantation or as destination therapy. Technological innovations over recent decades have transitioned from pulsatile to continuous-flow systems, with the HeartMate 3 currently representing the only long-term left ventricular support, due to its superior hemocompatibility, clinical outcomes, and full magnetic levitation. However, limitations persist, especially regarding right-sided and biventricular support, driveline infections, and patient quality of life. This review provides a comprehensive overview of both currently approved and investigational dMCS devices, highlighting key engineering features, hemocompatibility advancements, and the status of ongoing clinical trials. Emerging devices such as the Corheart 6, BrioVAD, EvaHeart 2, CorWave, FlowMaker, and TorVAD aim to enhance physiologic support, minimize shear stress, and enable full implantability. Additionally, novel concepts for biventricular and total heart replacement, including BerlinHeart Excor, reBEAT, DuoCor BiVAS, SynCardia, Emperor and BiVACOR are discussed. Key Messages •HeartMate 3 remains the only approved LVAD in Europe following HVAD withdrawal. •Next-generation devices aim to improve hemocompatibility, reduce complications, and support full implantability. •Options for biventricular or right heart failure remain limited, but novel concepts are emerging.

articles.title: Bridging the Evidence Gap: A Call to Action for Anticoagulation Research in Pediatric Burned Patients on Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Although early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improves respiratory complications in unburned populations, it remains a rarely utilized rescue therapy in pediatric burn care, averaging just 3 to 6 cases annually worldwide despite a promising 53-62% survival rate. This underutilization stems from a profound therapeutic paradox: the high bleeding risks and need for coagulation inherent to burn wounds with necessary surgical debridement directly conflict with the systemic anticoagulation required to prevent ECMO circuit thrombosis. Importantly, emerging evidence demonstrates that systemic anticoagulation may not be an absolute requirement for veno-venous ECMO. Despite this, no guidance exists for anticoagulation management specifically in pediatric burned patients. A scoping review spanning three databases identified no studies describing a coagulation strategy developed or validated for this population. Addressing this evidence gap is essential to safely transition ECMO from a late rescue modality to an earlier, evidence-based intervention capable of reducing mortality in this patient population. We therefore call for (1) a multicenter collaboration to aggregate sufficient case volume for meaningful analysis; (2) a prospective collection of serial viscoelastic and conventional coagulation data in pediatric burned patients on ECMO to characterize the temporal evolution of coagulopathy on circuit; and (3) the development and validation of coagulation management protocols tailored to this population. Until such evidence exists, pediatric burned patients will continue to be denied a therapy that offers meaningful survival-not because ECMO does not work-but because we have not yet determined how best to manage coagulation while on circuit.

articles.title: The Variable Presentation and Diagnostic Pitfalls of Autonomous Thyroid Nodules in Pediatrics: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroid nodules are less common and more likely to be malignant in children than in adults. Data on pediatric autonomous thyroid nodules (ATN) are scarce.

METHODS: Retrospective descriptive study. Twelve-year single-center case series of 12 patients (8 females) diagnosed with ATN at median age 15.7 years (3.6-17.3). A thirteenth patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma and hyperthyroidism was reported and described in the study but their data were not included in the descriptive statistics due to uncertainty regarding the autonomous nature of their nodule.

RESULTS: Over half the patients presented with a goiter and/or palpable nodule (72.7%). Symptoms of hyperthyroidism were present in 75%. Laboratory findings included suppressed serum TSH (100%). Free T4 was either normal (92.7%) or elevated (8.3%) with elevated total T3 (33.3%). Positive thyroperoxidase or thyroglobulin auto-antibodies were reported in three (25%) and one (8.3%) patients respectively. Two patients (16.7%) had TSH receptor antibodies at baseline. On ultrasound, thyroid nodule sizes were 2-4 cm (75%) or above 4 cm (25%). TIRADS scores were: 1 (8.3%), 2 (33.3%), 3 (8.3%), 4 (25%) or 5 (25%). Findings typical of ATN were detected in 10 of 11 patients (90.9%) on scintigraphy. Cytopathology was available on 8 nodules from 5 patients. Bethesda classifications were: II (n=2), III (n=3), IV (n=1), and V (n=1). Molecular analysis showed activating TSH receptor mutation in three of five tested patients. Ten patients completed surgery: total thyroidectomy (n=1) or lobectomy (n=9). Pathology was consistent with benign nodules in 9 cases. In one, the ATN was benign, but pathology detected incidental thyroid microcarcinoma in the same lobe.

CONCLUSIONS: The presentation of children with ATN is highly variable. Clinical signs of hyperthyroidism may not be present initially and the interpretation of laboratory and imaging data could be complicated by confounding factors . Multicenter studies are needed to establish the frequency of malignancy in pediatric ATN and better understand its pathophysiology.

articles.title: Polycystin dysfunction and cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD.
articles.abstract: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is one of the most common inherited kidney disorders characterized by the progressive formation of renal cysts. It is a systemic disease with significant extra-renal manifestations. Among these, cardiac electrical abnormalities are increasingly recognized as clinically important yet underappreciated contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond cyst formation, pathogenic variants in PKD1 or PKD2, which encode polycystin-1 (PC1) and polycystin-2 (PC2), respectively, interfere with calcium homeostasis, mechanotransduction, and mitochondrial function in both kidney and heart tissues. These molecular changes trigger a cascade of pathological events, including RAAS activation, TGF-driven fibrosis, and oxidative stress, leading to structural and electrical remodeling of the heart. These alterations contribute to cardiac electrical remodeling, manifesting clinically as QT interval and corrected QT (QT/QTc) prolongation, left ventricular hypertrophy, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and other electrocardiographic abnormalities. Despite growing evidence, cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD remain understudied in clinical practice. Early detection of subclinical cardiovascular abnormalities may be facilitated by electrocardiographic monitoring, cardiac imaging, and complementary biomarker assessment. Additionally, findings from iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte models support the translational potential of personalized drug-screening platforms. This review summarizes current evidence linking polycystin dysfunction to cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD by integrating molecular mechanisms with experimental and clinical findings. It also highlights the need for integrated cardio-renal approaches to improve cardiovascular surveillance, risk stratification, and future therapeutic development in ADPKD.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of the Laboratory-based Liver Frailty Index (Lab-LFI)-a prediction model for frailty in patients with cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Frailty, as measured by the Liver Frailty Index (LFI), is a well-established predictor of outcomes in cirrhosis, but testing requires in-person encounters. We sought to develop a blood-based biomarker index that correlates with frailty.

APPROACH AND RESULTS: Seven serum/plasma analytes (myostatin, IL-6, growth differentiation factor-15 [GDF-15], testosterone, leucine-rich alpha-2 glycoprotein [LRG1], fetuin-A, and IGF-1) were measured by ELISA in 527 ambulatory cirrhosis patients. "Frail" was defined as LFI≥4.4. The cohort was split in half; the "Lab-LFI" was developed using LASSO regression in the training set and validated in the test set. Other machine learning methods (generalized additive model [GAM], Random Forest, and XGBOOST) were considered to compare discrimination. Of 527 patients (median age 59, MELD 14), 114 (21.6%) were frail. All seven biomarkers were associated with frailty. In the test set, Lab-LFI's c-statistic was 0.80 (95% CI 0.74-0.87) for frailty. The GAM, random forest, and XGBOOST approaches produced similar discrimination (c-statistics 0.79-0.82); as such, the LASSO model was chosen for maximum interpretability. Addition of clinical variables to the LASSO model, including MELD labs and sex, did not improve discrimination (c-statistic 0.79, 95% CI 0.72-0.85). Patients were stratified by Lab-LFI using a cutpoint maximizing Youden's index; after adjusting for MELD and liver disease etiology, the high-risk group had higher pre-transplant death/waitlist dropout (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.17-2.68, p=0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: We developed and internally validated the Lab-LFI, a frailty prediction model consisting of 7 laboratory-based biomarkers. Lab-LFI enables blood-based assessment of physical function, as MELD does with liver function.

articles.title: Benefits and risks of induction immunosuppression in pediatric autoimmune liver disease from SPLIT Registry.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract: The optimal induction regimen for pediatric liver transplantation (LT) in patients with Autoimmune Liver Disease (AILD) is not well-defined. This study compared outcomes between corticosteroids only, anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG), and IL-2 receptor antagonists (IL2RA; Basiliximab/Daclizumab). A retrospective review of 445 pediatric LT recipients with AILD (Autoimmune hepatitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, or autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis) was conducted using the SPLIT database. Re-transplants were excluded. Primary outcomes included biopsy-confirmed rejection, culture-proven infection, graft loss, and mortality. Baseline demographics were comparable across groups. At 30 days post-LT, the IL2RA group demonstrated a significantly lower rate of biopsy-confirmed rejection (11.2%) compared to corticosteroids only (20.9%) and ATG (28%; p=0.05). Conversely, the ATG group experienced a significantly higher incidence of culture-proven infections between days 30-90 (42.9%) compared to corticosteroids only (10.2%) and IL2RA (17.9%; p=0.03). In multivariable-adjusted models, ATG induction was associated with a 10-fold higher risk of sub-acute culture-proven infection at 30-90 days (aOR=10.0, 95%CI: 1.4-71.8, p=0.02) compared to corticosteroids alone. However, neither ATG (aOR=0.47) nor IL-2RA (aOR=0.63) significantly altered the odds of early acute rejection at 0-30 days (p>0.30). No significant differences were observed in graft loss, mortality, disease recurrence, or post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder up to five years post-transplant. In pediatric AILD, induction with IL2RA significantly reduces early acute rejection without increasing infection risks or compromising long-term graft and patient survival.

articles.title: Serum ammonia improves early risk stratification beyond West Haven criteria in acute liver failure.
authors: US Acute Liver Failure Study Group
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The prognosis of patients with acute liver failure (ALF) presenting with low grade hepatic encephalopathy (HE) defined by the West Haven criteria (WHC) is difficult to establish. We studied the association between HE severity, assessed by WHC and serum ammonia, with outcomes across different age groups.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the prospective multicentre United States ALF Study Group registry (2000-2016). Exposures were WHC and serum ammonia on day 1 post inclusion. Endpoints were transplant-free survival (TFS) and mortality due to cerebral events on day 21. Findings were validated in a different and more recent (2010-2023) European cohort.

RESULTS: Among 1092 patients, median age was 39 years and 526 (48.2%) had acetaminophen toxicity. On day 1, 968 (88.6%) patients were in the intensive care unit and 669 (61.3%) were receiving any specific organ support (ventilation vasopressors, or renal replacement therapy). TFS and cerebral mortality on day 21 were 45.2% and 6.3%, respectively. Patients with hyperammonemia (≥50 µmol/L) on day 1 had lower TFS on day 21 than others, both for WHC grades 1-2 (53.0% vs. 65.2%) and 3-4 (31.8% vs. 60.9%). Higher ammonia on day 1 was independently associated with lower TFS on day 21, irrespective of WHC grade (odds ratio of 0.958 per each 10 µmol/L increment). Ammonia on day 1 of ≥100 µmol/L showed a significant threshold effect for TFS or cerebral mortality on day 21. Patients with <40 years had the highest probability of cerebral mortality on day 21.

CONCLUSIONS: In ALF, serum ammonia may help to define HE and assess prognosis earlier, irrespective of WHC grade. Patients with early serum ammonia of ≥100 µmol/L require optimized monitoring and treatment.

articles.title: Unusual Gastric Metastases in the Setting of Recurrence of Pancreatic NET: Dual Tracer PET/CT and Theranostic Approach.
articles.abstract: Gastric metastases from neuroendocrine tumors (NET) are infrequently encountered. Commonly, locally advanced pancreatic NET can involve stomach resulting in inoperable presentation. We herein present a case of gastric wall metastatic disease in postoperative pancreatic NET, which was identified on [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE-PET/CT as recurrence of disease after prolong progression-free period. [18F]F-FDG avidity of the lesions on [18F]F-FDG-PET/CT indicated requirement of chemotherapy alone, or in combination with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Hence, dual-tracer PET/CT imaging proved important in identifying unusual metastatic disease site and deciding therapeutic strategies in GEP-NET after a long follow-up period following surgical removal of primary disease.

articles.title: DINO-EEG: Montage-Robust Event-Level Seizure Detection in Scalp EEG.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Manual review of long-term clinical electroencephalography (EEG) remains a major bottleneck for large-scale seizure screening in intensive care and epilepsy monitoring settings. Most automated seizure detection methods formulate this task as epoch-level classification, which does not directly provide clinically relevant event boundaries. In addition, many existing systems are sensitive to montage configuration and channel availability, which limits their use in routine clinical practice. We present DINO-EEG, a channel- wise framework for event-level seizure detection in scalp EEG. The method processes each EEG channel independently and directly predicts seizure onset and offset using an object-detection formulation, after which channel- wise detections are aggregated into global seizure events. This design targets two practical goals: direct event-level output and improved robustness to variability in electrode configuration. On the Temple University Hospital EEG Seizure Corpus (TUSZ) v2.0.3, evaluated under the event-based SzCORE (Seizure Community Open-Source Research Evaluation) framework, DINO-EEG achieved an event-based F1 score of 0.641, with a mean sensitivity of 0.663 at 12.5 false positives per 24 hours (FPs/24 h) in seizure subjects, while yielding 4.7 FPs/24 h in seizure-free subjects. The method also remained stable under mild-to-moderate channel dropout and retained seizure detection capability during direct transfer to the CHB-MIT and Siena datasets without retraining. These results suggest that channel- wise event detection is a practical and clinically aligned strategy for automated seizure detection in retrospective EEG review workflows.

articles.title: Q-AortaECG: A Quantum-Inspired Multi-Agent 12-Lead ECG System for Early Triage of Acute Aortic Syndrome.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed recognition may occur because the presenting symptoms and electrocardiographic phenotypes often overlap with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, and other emergency diagnoses. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) remains the confirmatory standard, but the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is usually obtained earlier, is universally available at triage, and may carry distributed signatures of malperfusion, ischemia mimicry, autonomic stress, conduction delay, and hemodynamic compromise. We developed Q-AortaECG, a classically implemented quantum-inspired multi-agent ECG system that integrates multiscale waveform representations, specialist ECG agents, density-state uncertainty fusion, a variational-circuit style consensus layer, and a safety-gated multidisciplinary team-style report for early AAS triage. The system was evaluated in three suspected-AAS/CTA-evaluable cohorts comprising 1,251 patients, including 467 with CTA-, surgery-, or autopsy-confirmed AAS. Across 700 locked-test patients, Q-AortaECG achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.881 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.852-0.908), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.695-0.790), sensitivity of 0.955 (231/242; 95% CI, 0.920-0.977), specificity of 0.721 (330/458; 95% CI, 0.677-0.761), positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.643, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.968 at the prespecified high-sensitivity threshold. Performance remained consistent in external retrospective validation and prospective silent-run evaluation, although AUPRC decreased in the lower-prevalence prospective cohort. Ablation experiments supported the contributions of self-supervised ECG pretraining, agent specialization, density-matrix uncertainty fusion, and differential diagnosis modeling. In a counterbalanced paired reader study, Q-AortaECG assistance improved overall clinician sensitivity from 0.696 to 0.870 while preserving specificity (0.851 ver sus 0.846). In prospective silent-run analysis, counterfactual alerts would have advanced the median time to the correct diagnostic pathway from 187 to 61 minutes among initially unsuspected AAS presentations. These findings support ECG first, calibrated, safety-gated decision support as an early warning scaffold for AAS triage, while preserving CTA and expert imaging interpretation as the diagnostic standard.

articles.title: An evaluation of marnetegragene autotemcel for the treatment of severe leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I (LAD-I) is a rare primary immunodeficiency caused by pathogenic variants of the ITGB2 gene, which encodes the β2 integrin subunit (CD18). Deficient CD18 expression on neutrophils impairs their migration to sites of infection, resulting in recurrent, severe infections that can be fatal if left untreated. The gene therapy marnetegragene autotemcel (marne-cel) aims to restore CD18 expression in myeloid cells by delivering a functional copy of the ITGB2 gene using a self-inactivating lentiviral vector.

AREAS COVERED: This article reviews the design of the marne-cel vector, its clinical administration protocol, and reported efficacy outcomes. It also examines safety considerations, including long-term follow-up monitoring with a focus on integration site analysis. Despite its clinical promise, the article highlights challenges related to the sustainable commercialization and broad accessibility of gene therapy.

EXPERT OPINION: Marne-cel represents a potentially curative treatment option for patients with severe LAD-I who lack a suitable matched donor. Clinical data demonstrate durable restoration of CD18 expression alongside a favorable safety profile. However, sustaining availability post-authorization remains a significant challenge due to high costs and logistical complexities. Ensuring equitable and long-term access will require systemic changes beyond pricing strategies, including sustained investment in global healthcare infrastructure.

articles.title: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing in ischemic cardiomyopathy reveals common transcriptional profile underlying end-stage heart failure.
PROTAC degraders for lymphoid malignancies - current status and future directions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite remarkable advances in targeted therapy, some patients with lymphoid malignancies develop resistance to all available treatment modalities. Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate both catalytic and scaffolding protein functions of disease-causing proteins, offering a strategy to overcome this resistance.

AREAS COVERED: This review discusses the mechanisms of PROTAC activity, current preclinical and clinical data across lymphoid malignancies, and challenges for this emerging therapeutic class. PubMed, Google Scholar, and major hematology conference proceedings (ASH, ASCO, EHA) from 2017 to April 2026 were reviewed. Search terms included combinations of: PROTAC, targeted protein degradation, cereblon, von Hippel-Lindau, combined with individual disease terms and target names.

EXPERT OPINION: Among PROTACs, BTK degraders, tacabrutideg (BGB-16673) and bexobrutideg (NX-5948), have demonstrated overall response rates exceeding 75% in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL. The STAT3 degrader KT-333 and the IKZF1/3 degrader cemsidomide (the so-called molecular glue) have shown proof-of-concept clinical activity in T-cell and Hodgkin lymphomas. The durability of responses, long-term safety and predictive biomarkers have yet to be defined.The ongoing phase III trial of tacabrutideg will likely determine whether PROTACs become an established treatment option in lymphoid malignancies.

articles.title: Texturing Behavior-Empowered PANI-Wrapping C-Fe2O3 Hierarchical Microarchitectures for Wearable Ammonia and Pressure Sensing.
articles.abstract: Simultaneously monitoring ammonia (NH3) leakage and human motion is desirable for safeguarding astronauts' safety in spacecraft equipped with NH3-driven propulsion, in which stable and selective NH3 sensing combined with reliable pressure detection is highly required. However, little is reported on a sensing material that synergistically presents the required NH3 and pressure sensing. Here, wearable NH3 and pressure sensing has been developed using PANI-wrapping carbon-intermixed Fe2O3 hierarchical microarchitectures (PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs), which have been synthesized by employing fern-shaped C-Fe2O3 HMAs with trunk/branches as structural precursors, followed by conformal PANI-wrapping. Beneficially, PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs present a wide detection range of 0.1 ppm-10 v/v%, 167-day-long stability and high selectivity toward NH3. Further, a pressure sensor prototype has been constructed by laminating PET tapes onto the HMAs-integrated flexible electrode, revealing an excellent pressure-dependent response and machine-learning-assisted human-motion recognition. Such superior dual sensing is attributed to the texturing behavior, in which conformal texturing of PANI along the hierarchical surface of C-Fe2O3 HMAs establishes heterojunctions with a built-in electric field to amplify resistance modulation, while fern-shaped HMAs with trunk/branches provide abundant active interfaces and electron transport pathways. Practically, a wearable dual-sensing device that integrates flexible NH3 and pressure sensor prototypes has been built with reliable dual-sensing responses.

articles.title: Spatial variation in morphological traits of natural Haloxylon ammodendron populations on the eastern margin of the Badain Jaran Desert.
articles.abstract: Spatially explicit information on morphological variation within natural Haloxylon ammodendron populations remains limited. We examined size-associated morphological and spatial variation in a natural population on the eastern margin of the Badain Jaran Desert. Plant height, crown diameter, and stem-base diameter were measured for 1,151 individuals. Based on the lower and upper quartiles of stem-base diameter, individuals were classified into small, intermediate, and large stem-base diameter classes. Descriptive statistics and geostatistical analyses were used to characterize morphological variation and model spatial dependence. Mean plant height and crown diameter increased across the small, intermediate, and large stem-base diameter classes. The interpolated maps showed spatial variation in all measured traits. Plant height and crown diameter exhibited partially similar spatial patterns, whereas stem-base diameter showed a different spatial pattern. The fitted semivariogram parameters also differed among traits and diameter classes. The observed differences represent size-associated morphological and spatial variation rather than independently validated age-dependent changes. Because soil moisture, groundwater depth, local topography, wind fields, and plant interactions were not directly measured, the environmental mechanisms underlying the observed patterns remain unresolved.

articles.title: Screening for Cough Variant Asthma Using the TabPFN Model on Routine Laboratory Data in a Multicenter Cohort: Prospective Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cough variant asthma (CVA) is a prevalent but underdiagnosed subtype of chronic cough, largely due to the limited accessibility of pulmonary function tests in primary care.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and prospectively validate an interpretable machine learning model using routine laboratory data to facilitate accessible CVA screening.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter study combining retrospective model development and prospective validation using data from January 2021 to August 2025. The study included 3 sets-a retrospective development set (n=533; 428 training and 105 internal testing) and 2 prospective validation sets (internal validation: n=59 and external validation: n=78). In total, 54 routine biochemical, coagulation, and hematological markers were analyzed. A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was developed and benchmarked against extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Performance was evaluated via area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, and specificity. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to assess interpretability and clinical utility.

RESULTS: In external validation, TabPFN achieved an AUC of 0.858 (95% CI 0.763-0.943), accuracy of 79.5%, sensitivity of 71.4%, and specificity of 86%. XGBoost achieved a higher external AUC of 0.912 (95% CI 0.842-0.982) and sensitivity of 91.4%, but lower accuracy (75.6%) and specificity (62.8%) at the fixed 0.5 probability threshold. TabPFN retained higher AUCs than XGBoost in internal testing (0.964 vs 0.890) and temporal validation (0.925 vs 0.846). DCA demonstrated that TabPFN provided higher net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities, with the range varying across validation cohorts. SHAP analysis identified serum sodium (Na) and prothrombin time international normalized ratio as the leading predictors, followed jointly by mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration and red cell distribution width-SD, which showed the same rounded mean absolute SHAP value at the reported 2-decimal precision, and elevated sodium levels (>141 mmol/L) were associated with increased predicted risk.

CONCLUSIONS: The TabPFN model demonstrated robust prospective performance as an accessible screening tool for CVA, with balanced threshold-dependent classification performance across validation cohorts. Although TabPFN showed higher discrimination than XGBoost in internal and temporal validation, XGBoost achieved a higher AUC in the external cohort, indicating that neither model uniformly outperformed the other across all performance dimensions.

articles.title: Macrophage activation syndrome is associated with high in-hospital mortality in patients with lupus.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo study the clinical features and outcomes of macrophage activation syndrome in lupus.MethodsThis was a retrospective study conducted in a tertiary care referral centre from 2017 to 2022. Consecutive hospitalised adult-onset SLE patients diagnosed with MAS, fulfilling the Parodi criteria with ferritin >500 ng/ml were included. All the other hospitalised SLE patients without MAS served as controls. Clinical and immunological features and in-hospital mortality was compared between the 2 groups. Risk factors for mortality in MAS patients were determined performing univariate and multivariate analyses with a stepwise logistic regression.ResultsOf 623 hospitalisations in 451 SLE patients, 86 met the case definition for MAS and 526 served as controls. MAS occurred at the time of SLE diagnosis in 54 (62.9%). MAS was associated with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, cytopenia, and elevated transaminases. Disease activity (clinical SLEDAI 2K) was significantly higher in MAS (mean 13.7 ± 6.5 vs. 8 ± 5.9 (p < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was higher in the MAS compared to the control group [13 (15%) vs 6 (1%), p < 0.001]. Mortality in MAS was associated with higher ferritin (12092.9 ± 2826.5 vs 3993.6 ± 735, <0.001) and aspartate aminotransferase (544 ± 239 vs 167.66 ± 27.28U/L, p < 0.001), seizures (p = 0.035), altered mental status (p = 0.004), shock (p < 0.001), intensive care unit admission (p < 0.001), and mechanical ventilation (p < 0.001). On multivariate regression analysis -ferritin >2400{OR-8.1 95% CI: (1.46-44.85) p - 0.017} and seizures {OR-7.3 95% CI: (1.2-44.29) p - 0.030} were associated with mortality in MAS.ConclusionsMAS is a rare complication of active lupus identified by fever, elevated ferritin, liver transaminases and cytopenia and is associated with high in hospital mortality.

articles.title: The 'road to gold' in open-water swimming: insights on performance and stroke mechanics regulation from longitudinal race analysis of the 5-km 2024 world champion.
articles.abstract: Open-water swimming (OWS) performance relies on reshaping stroke mechanics as race demands escalate towards a decisive end-spurt. How world-class swimmers implement this high-grading strategy in competition remains unknown. This study establishes the first biomechanical framework of a World Championship (WCH) victory by integrating inter-swimmer benchmarking, longitudinal intra-swimmer profiling, and 3D kinematic variabilities analysis of the 2024 5-km WCH winner (FONLO). FONLO and seven elite swimmers were monitored over 2022-2024 during 15 international races using a sacrum-mounted inertial sensor. Cycle-to-cycle stroke rate (SR) and jerk cost (JC) were modelled with locally estimated scatterplot smoothing to derive an international top-4 stroke mechanics template and to profile FONLO's races, including end-spurt dynamics. During the WCH win, intra- and inter-cyclic 3D kinematic variabilities were quantified via double functional decomposition. The WCH victory accentuated the top-4 J-shaped dynamics, with delayed time above mean SR and JC and greater modulation ranges across race phases. Maximal stroke mechanics variability characterised the win, including a 340% JC surge triggering a 27-s sprint. Kinematic modelling revealed stable intra-cyclic patterns with breathing-related asymmetries and increased inter-cyclic variability in the final lap. World-class OWS success emerges from precisely timed stroke regulation and controlled variability, preserving smoothness until an explosive final sprint.

articles.title: Correction to: Non-obstructive coronary artery disease upon multi-detector computed tomography in patients presenting with acute chest pain-Results of an intermediate term follow-up.
Mindful Awareness and Stress Associations Among People Living With the Effects of Stroke and their Partners: Findings From a Daily Diary Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, significantly affecting the health of individuals post stroke and their partners. Both people living with the effects of stroke (PLWS) and their partners experience elevated stress. Therefore, this daily diary study examined day-to-day variations in stress and its association with mindful awareness as a potential protective factor against stress within and between PLWS and their partners.

METHODS: Eighty-six community-dwelling couples (67±10 y old, 50% female) in Canada, with one partner living with the effects of stroke, reported their daily stress, their partners' stress, and their own mindful awareness every evening for up to 14 days.

RESULTS: Distinguishable dyads models showed that individuals reporting that their partners felt more stressed (daily and overall), and whose partners felt more stressed (daily and overall) reported more daily stress themselves. In contrast, when individuals reported more mindful awareness (daily and overall), they reported less daily stress. PLWS also reported less daily stress when their partners reported more overall mindful awareness. However, this dyadic association was not found in the other direction or for daily mindful awareness.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest dyadic associations of daily stress between partners and indicate that mindful awareness may reduce daily stress within individuals. Within the dyad, PLWS seemed to benefit from their partners' mindful awareness. Results highlight the significant role of the partner for PLWS and emphasize the need to consider how interpersonal dynamics vary, particularly in couples managing medical conditions.

REGISTRATION: The study was preregistered at OSF (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/XTV2H).

articles.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
articles.abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

articles.title: Steatotic Liver Disease Is Becoming a Higher Priority Worldwide.
Osteoporosis Screening Gaps Among Patients Undergoing Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is associated with elevated complication rates after lumbar fusion surgery. Despite this, osteoporosis remains both underscreened and undertreated in the United States. Currently, rates of dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DEXA) screening before lumbar fusion surgery are unknown, as is the proportion of patients who, after being diagnosed with osteoporosis, receive appropriate treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess osteoporosis screening and treatment rates among patients undergoing lumbar fusion surgery.

METHODS: Patients older than 50 years undergoing lumbar fusion for lumbar stenosis with degenerative spondylolisthesis were identified using the TriNetX database. Patients receiving surgery for indications of malignancy or infection, as well as those with diagnoses of osteoporosis before the screening window, were excluded. The prevalence of DEXA scans in the 2 years before fusion was calculated for the overall cohort and for high-risk cohorts defined by Endocrinology Society guidelines. A secondary analysis assessed rates of osteoporosis treatment among patients receiving preoperative DEXA scans.

RESULTS: Of 46,104 patients who underwent lumbar fusion surgery, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a preoperative DEXA scan in the 2 years before their fusion. Women were more likely to receive DEXA scans than men (OR, 3.93; 95% CI, 3.64 to 4.23; P < 0.001). Only 5.6% of high-risk men and 17.5% of high-risk women received preoperative DEXA screening. Among patients diagnosed with osteoporosis after DEXA screening, only 11.0% received anabolic therapy and 23.1% received antiresorptive therapy.

CONCLUSION: Despite most patients undergoing lumbar fusion being at risk of osteoporosis (and eligible for screening), a small minority were screened using DEXA in the 2 years before surgery. Efforts are warranted to increase the prevalence of DEXA screening so that osteoporosis is appropriately diagnosed and treated before lumbar fusion surgery.

articles.title: Global Heart Failure Burden Increased Between 1990 and 2023.
ACC Releases Guidance for Managing Resistant Hypertension.
The cardiovascular risk of metabolically healthy obesity: an inflammatory perspective.
articles.journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) is a heterogeneous phenotype characterized by preserved traditional metabolic markers despite excess adiposity. However, accumulating evidence suggests that MHO may not be uniformly benign and may confer increased long-term cardiovascular risk through inflammatory and adipose tissue-mediated mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on cardiovascular risk in MHO, focusing on visceral adiposity, ectopic fat, and immune metabolic pathways. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. Across the reviewed evidence, MHO is frequently associated with the progression to metabolically unhealthy obesity, although transition rates and cardiovascular risk estimates vary according to MHO definitions. Visceral and ectopic fat are associated with subclinical atherosclerosis, coronary calcification, and cardiovascular events, including in individuals without overt metabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding heart failure and ventricular dysfunction remains limited and inconsistent. Low-grade inflammation and adipose immune remodeling, including NLRP3 inflammasome activation, provide plausible mechanisms, although human evidence remains predominantly observational. Key gaps include inconsistent MHO definitions, limited longitudinal imaging and biomarker integration, population diversity, and lack of validated MHO-specific risk models. Standardized phenotyping and prospective validation of inflammation-based risk stratification are required.

articles.title: Putting the Brakes on Nuclear Rupture-Driven Remodeling in LMNA Cardiomyopathy.
Saving the Capillaries: FGFR1/KLB and MFG-E8 in Diabetic Hearts.
Fifty Shades of Calpain: Couplon Breakdown in Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia and Beyond.
Disease duration and C-peptide at onset are key determinants of long-term residual β-cell function in children with type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Residual β-cell function (RBCF) may persist in a subset of children with long-standing type 1 diabetes (T1D), offering metabolic benefits. We aimed to evaluate factors that determine the long-term persistence of RBCF.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective study from July 2024 to December 2025 to assess RBCF in children with long-standing (≥7 years) T1D. Stimulated C-peptide (SCP) was measured 90 min after the mixed-meal tolerance test. Patients were grouped into RBCF-preserved (SCP ≥0.01 nmol/L) or RBCF-depleted (SCP <0.01 nmol/L). RBCF determinants, such as age, sex, ketoacidosis at onset, serum C-peptide concentration at diagnosis, number of pancreatic autoantibodies at diagnosis, glycemic control, and disease duration, were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Seventy-two children (mean age 15.4 ± 3.3 years, 54 % boys) with a mean T1D duration of 9.8 ± 2.1 years were studied. RBCF was preserved in 30.6 % (22/72) of children. Shorter disease duration (median 8.8 vs. 9.7 years, p=0.027) and higher C-peptide at onset (0.17 vs. 0.04 nmol/L, p<0.001) strongly predicted preservation. Older age at T1D onset (7.3 vs. 4.9 years) showed a trend toward better-preserved RBCF, but the association did not attain statistical significance (p=0.11). Ketoacidosis at onset, the number of autoantibodies, and glycemic control did not affect RBCF persistence.

CONCLUSIONS: RBCF persists in about one-third of children with long-standing T1D, suggesting that endogenous insulin production does not vanish completely after diagnosis. Higher C-peptide levels at clinical onset strongly predicted long-term RBCF-preservation, suggesting that patients with a larger initial β-cell reserve are better poised for long-term endogenous insulin synthesis.

articles.title: Current Challenges in Atopic Dermatitis: An Italian Delphi Consensus with a Special Focus on Moderate Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, inflammatory skin disease clinically characterized by eczematous lesions and severe itch, significantly affecting the patients' quality of life. AD is classified as mild, moderate, or severe according to the extent and severity of these lesions. While therapeutic protocols for mild and severe AD are well-defined, the moderate stage represents a clinical 'gray zone' characterized by inconsistent management. It is frequently mismanaged, oscillating between undertreatment and the indiscriminate use of traditional systemic therapies. The moderate stage of AD requires a tailored approach to maximize topical treatments efficacy, avoid the side effects of systemic drugs, while remaining ready to escalate therapy if needed.

METHODS: An Italy-based, expert-Delphi consensus was used to: (1) reach a consensus on moderate AD classification criteria; (2) characterize the disease-specific burden in these patients; (3) identify key elements and concerns in moderate AD treatment; and (4) identify the therapeutic and management-related unmet needs of this subset of patients.

RESULTS: Agreement was reached for 26 final statements, which included highlighting a significant disease burden also for patients with moderate AD.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings underscore a misalignment between the actual disease burden of moderate AD and current regulatory reimbursement criteria. In Italy, the restricted access to innovative systemic therapies for this specific patient population represents a critical healthcare gap.

articles.title: Dual vs. Triple Therapy in Asthma: Are We Ready to Move Beyond ICS-LABA?
articles.abstract: Triple therapy for asthma containing long-acting beta-agonist (LABA), long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA), and inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) is a newer option for asthma management, especially when all three components are combined in a single inhaler (SITT: single-inhaler triple therapy), which promotes better adherence than multiple inhalers. There are questions as to its efficacy beyond the ICS/LABA combination, and evidence certainly shows that it will improve lung function, decrease exacerbations, and potentially help with symptoms. Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) suggests these are Step 5 therapies, as they add on to medium-dose ICS/LABA. Fortunately, these compounds are quite safe and well tolerated. GINA recommendations for Step 5 will be reviewed, including particularly the place for LAMA addition as add-on therapy to ICS/LABA, and novel potential clinical applications will be reviewed.

articles.title: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Authors' Reply 2.
Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

articles.title: The Role of Digital Twins in Clinical Trials: A New Perspective on Methodological and Statistical Challenges.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remain the gold standard for evaluating medical interventions, yet they face persistent methodological challenges: patient dropout, inadequate sample sizes, premature termination, missing data, and the limitations of indirect treatment comparisons. The emergence of digital twin technology-computational patient representations that generate simulated clinical trajectories statistically indistinguishable from real-world data-offers a promising methodological complement to address these limitations.

APPROACH: We synthesize evidence from key methodological literature, regulatory guidance (ICH E9(R1), FDA, EMA), and proof-of-concept studies across oncology, neurology, and Alzheimer's disease. A taxonomy of in silico clinical trial approaches provides the organizational framework. This article is a narrative perspective rather than a systematic review; no predefined search strategy, database range, or inclusion/exclusion criteria were applied.

RESULTS: Digital twins may provide complementary methodological approaches across nine trial challenges: model-based sensitivity analyses for missing (MNAR) outcomes; Bayesian and posterior predictive modeling of partially observed longitudinal outcomes; prognostic covariate adjustment and virtual augmentation to improve efficiency; prospective simulation of futility stopping rules; prospective calibration of efficacy stopping boundaries; individualized control-arm (ICA) construction; hybrid augmented and synthetic control strategies; pre-trial protocol optimization through in silico simulation; and population-adjusted indirect treatment comparison.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital twins represent an emerging methodological ecosystem rather than isolated tools. Their methodological potential depends on consistent validation and explainability standards; frameworks for detecting algorithmic bias; clarification of regulatory acceptance criteria; and comprehensive data infrastructure addressing representativeness gaps. Digital twin approaches should be viewed as complementary to-not replacements for-established randomized trial methodology.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Microhook Ab Interno Trabeculotomy Combined with Cataract Surgery in Older Patients with Glaucoma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence regarding minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in very old patients remains limited, making surgical decision-making challenging in this population. We investigated age-related differences in the safety and efficacy of microhook ab interno trabeculotomy combined with cataract surgery (combined µLOT).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study in Japan included 67 consecutive glaucomatous eyes of 67 patients who underwent combined µLOT and were followed for at least 6 months. The cohort comprised 27 male and 40 female patients. Patients were divided by median age into younger (< 76 years, n = 32) and older (≥ 76 years, n = 35) groups. Qualified success was defined irrespective of postoperative glaucoma medication use and without the need for additional glaucoma surgery, and was evaluated using three intraocular pressure (IOP) criteria: criterion A, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 18 mmHg; criterion B, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 15 mmHg; and criterion C, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 13 mmHg.

RESULTS: The mean age of the older group was 82.5 years. At 6 months, qualified success probabilities were 94.0%, 82.1%, and 60.0% for criteria A, B, and C, respectively. Although the older group had higher qualified success under criterion C (71.4% vs. 46.9%; nominal P = 0.04) and lower IOP from week 2 to month 6, age was not independently associated with surgical failure in multivariable Cox analyses. Higher preoperative IOP, hypertension, and antithrombotic therapy showed exploratory associations with failure. Postoperative hyphema, transient IOP elevation, corneal endothelial cell loss, and systemic complications were not increased in the older group.

CONCLUSION: Combined µLOT provided favorable short-term IOP control without an increased complication burden in older patients, although baseline medication burden may have confounded the age-group comparison. These real-world findings provide clinically relevant evidence for surgical decision-making in very old patients and may be informative for other aging societies.

articles.title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
articles.abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

articles.title: Delayed diagnosis of MEN1 after kidney transplantation: unrecognized pre-transplant features and implications for clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), characterized by multiglandular endocrine tumors such as hyperparathyroidism (HPT), is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations of the MEN1 gene. In patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), abnormalities in calcium-phosphate metabolism may obscure this diagnosis, making the recognition of MEN1 challenging. A 68-year-old man with end-stage renal disease underwent an ABO-compatible living-donor kidney transplantation (KT); however, persistent hypercalcemia prompted further evaluation, which revealed recurrent HPT with bilateral parathyroid enlargement. Pre-transplant imaging revealed an adrenal adenoma and a pancreatic tail lesion. Subsequent pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of MEN1. A retrospective review of the patient's medical history revealed several pre-transplant findings suggestive of MEN1 that had not been recognized. This case highlights that MEN1 may remain unrecognized in KT candidates owing to the occurrence of metabolic abnormalities also associated with CKD. The early recognition of MEN1 in KT candidates with recurrent or multiglandular hyperparathyroidism may improve pre-transplant risk assessment and enable appropriate long-term oncological surveillance.

articles.title: IL-6 Blockade for Antibody-Mediated Transplant Rejection: What Does the Evidence Say?
articles.journal: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy
articles.abstract: Two of the most significant challenges in transplantation medicine are human leukocyte antigen sensitization, which limits access to kidney transplantation for patients with end-stage kidney disease owing to the lack of effective desensitization strategies, and chronic active antibody-mediated rejection (cAMR), a major cause of allograft dysfunction and graft loss following transplantation. Despite its substantial clinical significance, there remains a lack of high-quality evidence and well-established therapeutic algorithms for the management of cAMR, while many patients continue to be excluded from kidney transplantation because of immunological barriers. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that plays a central role in both innate and adaptive immune responses. Beyond its immunological functions, IL-6 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of a wide range of conditions, including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, and various neurological disorders. Consequently, targeting the IL-6/IL-6 receptor signaling pathway has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy in transplantation medicine, particularly for desensitization protocols and the treatment of cAMR. However, the current evidence base is restricted to studies evaluating tocilizumab and clazakizumab, with clinical benefits remaining inconsistent across studies. Limited evidence is available regarding the desensitization effectiveness of tocilizumab monotherapy. In cAMR, the phase III IMAGINE trial found no improvement in kidney function with clazakizumab despite reduced C-reactive protein. Current evidence does not support a routine IL-6 pathway blockade in cAMR, while further studies are required to prove the potential benefits in desensitization. In this narrative review, we comprehensively examine the role of IL-6 in the pathophysiology of kidney transplantation and critically appraise the available clinical evidence regarding IL-6/IL-6R-targeted therapies for the management of human leukocyte antigen sensitization and cAMR.

articles.title: Loneliness relates to smaller hippocampal subfield volumes in individuals with elevated plasma pTau217: results from IGNITE.
articles.abstract: Loneliness is associated with cognitive decline and dementia risk, but the role of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology in its associations with medial temporal lobe (MTL) morphology remains unclear. We examined whether loneliness was related to total hippocampal volume, hippocampal subfields, and entorhinal cortex (ERC) volumes, and whether plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) moderated these relationships. We analyzed baseline data from cognitively unimpaired older adults aged 65-80 years enrolled in IGNITE. Loneliness was assessed using the revised UCLA Loneliness Scale. Structural 3 T MRI included a high-resolution T2-weighted hippocampal sequence. Hippocampal subfields and ERC volumes were extracted using ASHS, and FreeSurfer estimated total hippocampal volume and intracranial volume. Participants were classified as pTau217-positive or negative using an Aβ-PET-calibrated threshold (> 0.46 pg/mL). Covariate-adjusted linear regression models tested loneliness associations and loneliness×pTau217 interactions. We included 601 participants (69.8 ± 3.7 years; 72.2% female; 76.4% White); 582 had usable pTau217 data, of whom 28.9% were pTau217-positive. pTau217 moderated associations with CA3 (β =  - 0.215, 95% CI - 0.381 to - 0.048) and ERC (β =  - 0.167, 95% CI - 0.318 to - 0.016), with negative associations observed among pTau217-positive but not pTau217-negative participants. Greater loneliness was associated with smaller total hippocampal volume (β =  - 0.077, 95% CI, - 0.147 to - 0.007, p = 0.031), but not with individual subfields. Loneliness showed biomarker-dependent associations with MTL subfields, suggesting that pTau217-defined biological risk may modify links between psychosocial factors and neuroanatomical vulnerability. This biomarker-informed framework may help explain heterogeneity in prior loneliness-neuroimaging findings.Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02875301.

articles.title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
articles.abstract:
