BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Early selective deep capillary plexus impairment at diagnosis in children with type 1 diabetes: an OCT angiography study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinal microvascular dysfunction may precede clinically visible diabetic retinopathy in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), but whether it is detectable at diagnosis remains unclear.

AIMS: To evaluate retinal microvascular alterations at T1DM diagnosis using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and assess associations between deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density and metabolic severity.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 50 children with newly diagnosed T1DM (100 eyes) and 50 age- and sex-matched controls (100 eyes). OCTA was performed using 6×6-mm macular and 4.5×4.5-mm optic disc scans. Vessel density (VD) was assessed in the superficial capillary plexus (SCP), DCP, and radial peripapillary capillary network. Foveal avascular zone metrics and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness were also analyzed. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for inter-eye correlation. Subgroup analyses were performed by HbA1c level and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) severity.

RESULTS: SCP VD did not differ significantly between groups. DCP VD was lower in T1DM eyes in the whole image (53.1±3.0% vs 54.6±2.8%, p=0.006), parafoveal region (54.0±3.1% vs 55.8±2.9%, p=0.002), and perifoveal region (53.4±3.0% vs 54.7±2.8%, p=0.02). Peripapillary VD and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness were similar. Higher HbA1c was independently associated with lower DCP VD, which also declined with increasing DKA severity.

CONCLUSIONS: DCP impairment is detectable at T1DM diagnosis before clinically visible diabetic retinopathy. OCTA may provide a sensitive, noninvasive biomarker of early retinal microvascular involvement in pediatric T1DM.

articles.title: The medical and surgery outcomes of pulmonary hydatid cyst disease: A 12-year multidisciplinary experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hydatid cyst disease (PHCD) remains a significant public health problem in endemic regions.

AIMS: To evaluate the demographic, serological, radiological, and surgical characteristics of patients with PHCD and to identify factors associated with hepatic involvement and postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 515 consecutive patients who underwent surgical treatment for PHCD at Dicle University Faculty of Medicine between 2013 and 2025. Demographic characteristics, cyst features, indirect fluorescent antibody (IFA) test results, concomitant hepatic involvement, surgical procedures, postoperative outcomes, and complications were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 515 patients, 275 (53.4%) were male and 240 (46.6%) were female. Female patients were significantly older than male patients (28.0 ± 18.0 vs. 23.8 ± 18.4 years, p = 0.002). Hepatic involvement was significantly associated with positive IFA test results (p < 0.001), bilateral pulmonary disease (p < 0.001), multiple pulmonary cysts (p < 0.001), female sex (p = 0.045), and left-sided pulmonary involvement (p = 0.019). Blood group distribution was not associated with hepatic involvement (p = 0.773), although IFA positivity differed significantly among ABO blood groups (p = 0.006). Larger cyst size was associated with longer hospital stay (r = 0.130, p = 0.003) and prolonged drainage duration (r = 0.094, p = 0.034). Perforated cysts were associated with increased hospital stay (r = 0.180, p < 0.001) and drainage duration (r = 0.139, p = 0.002). Pediatric patients had significantly larger cysts than adults (p = 0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Positive IFA results, multiple pulmonary cysts, and bilateral lung involvement are associated with concomitant hepatic hydatid disease. Cyst size and perforation status significantly influence postoperative recovery, particularly hospital stay and drainage duration. Surgical treatment provides excellent outcomes with low reoperation rates and no disease-related mortality in experienced centers.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory infections, mostly viral, are a leading cause of childhood hospitalization. Rapid antigen tests are fast but cover few viruses; multiplex PCR detects many more. The value of reflex PCR after a negative antigen test is uncertain.

AIMS: To compare the diagnostic yield of antigen testing alone and with reflex multiplex PCR, and to describe the viral spectrum, age associations, and antibiotic exposure.

METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort, 245 children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory infection (October 2022-October 2023) underwent a five-target rapid antigen test; antigen-negative children had reflex multiplex PCR at the physician's discretion. This was a diagnostic-yield study under partial verification; sensitivity and specificity were intentionally not estimated.

RESULTS: A virus was detected in 140 of 245 children (57.1%); antigen testing alone identified 59 (24.1%). Of 186 antigen-negative children, 99 underwent reflex PCR and 81 (81.8%) were positive (48 with a missed panel-covered virus, 33 with off-panel viruses only). Rhinovirus/enterovirus, not covered by antigen testing, was most frequent (27.9% of identified children). Antibiotics were given to 198 children (80.8%), with no significant difference by viral detection (p = 0.103). Blood cultures and atypical bacterial targets were negative in tested children; typical respiratory bacteria were not systematically investigated.

CONCLUSIONS: A negative antigen test did not exclude a respiratory virus; reflex PCR improved detection, varying by virus and age. With selective testing, the yield is a lower bound. Antibiotic exposure was high regardless of viral detection; its appropriateness could not be judged without systematic bacterial testing.

articles.title: Higher relapse rate after stopping tenofovir alafenamide compared with entecavir; but not tenofovir disoproxil fumarate in HBeAg-positive patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: This study compares the hepatitis B virus (HBV) relapse rates after discontinuation of entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), or tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) therapy in HBeAg-positive patients.

METHODS: This study was a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected cohort comprising 427 HBeAg-positive patients without cirrhosis who received entecavir (n=200), TDF (n=133), or TAF (n=94) were enrolled. All patients met the Taiwan National Health Insurance stopping criteria for antiviral therapy.

RESULTS: At 156 weeks, the cumulative incidences of virological relapse and clinical relapse, and retreatment were higher in the off-TAF group (85.3%, 73.7%, and 76.6%, respectively) than in the off-entecavir group (58.0%, 45.5%, and 38.9%, respectively) (all p <0.001). Compared with the off-TDF group (74.6%, 64.4%, and 58.8%, respectively), the off-TAF group showed comparable rates of virological relapse (p=0.139) but significantly higher rates of clinical relapse (p=0.042) and retreatment (p=0.003). The median time to clinical relapse was earlier in patients discontinuing TAF than in those discontinuing entecavir or TDF (17, 42, and 24 weeks, respectively). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that TAF therapy was an independent risk factor for virological relapse, clinical relapse, and retreatment compared with entecavir, but not with TDF; these findings remained consistent after propensity score matching. Among patients with clinical relapse, HBeAg seroreversion was more frequent in the off-TAF group than in the off-entecavir (73.0% vs. 51.4%, p <0.001) and off-TDF groups (73.0% vs. 56.8%, p=0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuation of TAF therapy was associated with earlier and higher HBV relapse rates compared with entecavir, but not TDF, in HBeAg-positive patients.

articles.title: Boldine enhances hyperthermia-induced apoptosis in AGS gastric cancer cells in association with attenuation of the HSF1-HSP stress response.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer presents therapeutic challenges owing to treatment resistance and stress adaptation. This study investigated whether boldine enhances mild hyperthermia-induced cytotoxicity in AGS gastric cancer cells and evaluated its association with attenuation of the heat shock response involving heat shock proteins (HSPs) and heat shock factor 1 (HSF1).

METHODS AND RESULTS: AGS cells were pretreated with boldine (1 h) and exposed to 37-43 °C (30 min). Combined treatment reduced viability, wound closure, and colony formation more than single treatments. The apoptotic fraction increased from 8.08% in untreated controls to 28.79% with boldine alone and 3.55% with hyperthermia alone, reaching 46.33% after cotreatment. Cotreatment altered cell cycle distribution (S and G2/M fractions), increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and enhanced MAPK phosphorylation. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) pretreatment reduced ROS levels and apoptotic cell fraction while partially restoring HSP27 expression. Boldine suppressed HSP expression-most notably HSP27-and attenuated HSF1 phosphorylation under hyperthermia. In NCI-N87 cells, confirmatory experiments showed higher apoptosis after cotreatment, whereas hyperthermia did not further reduce viability or alter HSP levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Boldine enhances hyperthermia-induced apoptosis in AGS gastric cancer cells in association with attenuation of the HSF1-HSP stress response and ROS accumulation, supporting boldine as a potential thermosensitizing adjunct in gastric cancer therapy.

articles.title: Evaluation of Myocardial Blood Flow Using 18F-flurpiridaz PET: Established Applications with Pharmacologic Stress and Roadmap for Exercise Stress Implementation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recently approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, 18F-flurpiridaz for positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) enables high-quality assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF). Its half-life of approximately 110 min supports regional distribution and allows unit-dose delivery. These features make this probe well suited for MBF quantitation and expand access to quantitative cardiac PET at smaller centers.

RECENT FINDINGS: During pharmacologic stress, absolute MBF and myocardial flow reserve provide incremental diagnostic information beyond relative perfusion imaging. These measures have been validated across multiple methods and software platforms. Further study of this tracer under peak exercise may provide clinically relevant assessment of myocardial demand-induced changes in flow. Potential investigational approaches include artificial intelligence (AI)-derived virtual MBF, exercise-adjusted standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) surrogate, and direct kinetic modeling during in-scanner ergometry. While conceptually promising, limitations inherent to exercise-based approaches in stress MBF and/or MFR estimation highlight the need for pragmatic research strategies before potential clinical applicability.

articles.title: Cold-Water Immersion for Post-exercise Recovery: An Overlap-Aware Umbrella Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cold-water immersion (CWI) is widely used after strenuous exercise, but review-level findings vary by outcome, comparator, recovery window, population, and protocol. Reuse of the same primary studies across reviews can also exaggerate apparent consistency.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scopus from inception to 30 January 2026 for systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and network meta-analyses of post-exercise CWI. Fourteen reviews were included. Primary-study overlap was quantified using the corrected covered area (CCA) overall and for outcome-specific study-to-review mappings. Because overlap was high and review-level estimates were statistically dependent, we did not perform second-order meta-analysis. Source-verified estimates were synthesized in a structured, overlap-aware format. Methodological quality was assessed with AMSTAR 2.

RESULTS: Of the 14 included reviews, 13 provided quantitative estimates, whereas one review provided narrative evidence on heart rate variability (HRV). Overall CCA was 12.68% (high); 99 of 165 primary-study families appeared in at least two reviews. Outcome-specific CCA was 15.03% for delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS; very high) and ranged from 0.00% for interleukin-6 (IL-6) to 25.00% for C-reactive protein (CRP). It was not calculable for HRV, because one review contributed. AMSTAR 2 confidence was low in 2 reviews and critically low in 12. DOMS showed the most consistent favorable pattern: source-review standardized mean differences ranged from -1.04 to -0.37, although the largest estimate was soccer-specific and its 95% prediction interval crossed zero. Because DOMS evidence was highly redundant across the contributing reviews, this apparent consistency does not represent independent replications. Findings for objective performance and biochemical outcomes were inconsistent, time-dependent, or comparator-dependent.

CONCLUSIONS: Within the available review-level evidence, CWI was associated with the most consistent reduction in self-reported short-term post-exercise DOMS, but the clinical importance of the observed effects remains uncertain. Evidence does not support a uniform benefit across objective performance or inflammatory outcomes. Protocol observations, including commonly studied temperatures and durations, are descriptive and should not be interpreted as an optimized prescription. Trial Registration PROSPERO CRD420261332482.

articles.title: Comparative Proteomics of Extracellular Vesicles of Two Species of Mucorales Reveals Species-Specific Cargo.
articles.abstract: Rhizopus arrhizus is one of the most common etiological agents of mucormycosis worldwide, whereas Mucor irregularis has been reported with a relatively high frequency in China, exhibiting clear regional characteristics. However, the molecular basis underlying their differential host responses remains incompletely understood. Fungal extracellular vesicles (EVs) play diverse biological roles across fungal species and have emerged as important carriers of bioactive cargos that modulate host-pathogen interactions. In this study, we compared features of EVs derived from R. arrhizus and M. irregularis and evaluated their immunomodulatory effects. EVs were isolated from PBS suspensions collected from fungal cultures via differential ultracentrifugation, followed by physical and proteomic characterization. Quantitative proteomics via DIA (data independent acquisition) identified 246 EV-associated proteins showing species-specific detection or quantitative abundance differences between the two species. In the murine footpad infection model, R. arrhizus induced more severe local lesions than M. irregularis, whereas EVs from M. irregularis elicited substantially higher pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in RAW 264.7 macrophages in vitro. Collectively, our results demonstrate marked divergence between R. arrhizus and M. irregularis in EV size, protein composition, and macrophage responses, providing a comparative resource for further investigation of EV-associated factors in Mucorales-host interactions.

articles.title: Targeting STING to attenuate autophagy-mediated airway remodeling in asthma.
articles.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is critical for antiviral and intracellular antibacterial immune defense and is involved in pulmonary fibrotic diseases. However, the role of STING in regulating autophagy and airway remodeling in asthma remains unclear. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced mouse model of asthma airway remodeling was established. Expression levels of STING and autophagy-related gene 5 (ATG5) in lung tissues were detected. The effects of STING inhibitor C-176 on autophagy and airway remodeling were evaluated in vivo. In human bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells stimulated with interleukin (IL)-13, the relationships among STING, autophagy, and cellular fibrosis were investigated in vitro. In OVA-challenged mice, C-176, chloroquine (CQ), and dexamethasone (DX) reduced airway hyperresponsiveness and eosinophil counts. C-176 and CQ alleviated inflammatory cell infiltration, mucus secretion, and collagen deposition, and suppressed autophagy and fibrosis in airway epithelium. In IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, C-176, ATG5 inhibition, or PERK pathway inhibition downregulated autophagy and fibrosis‑related markers. STING upregulation in airway epithelial cells promotes autophagy and subsequent airway remodeling in asthma. Inhibition of STING or autophagy attenuates these pathological changes, indicating a potential therapeutic target for asthma.

articles.title: Photodynamic inactivation and photodynamic therapy for viral pathogens: a systematic review of antiviral efficacy, mechanisms, and translational boundaries.
articles.journal: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Viral infections pose a persistent global threat, driven by emerging pathogens and rising antiviral resistance. Photodynamic inactivation (PDI) and photodynamic therapy (PDT) generate reactive oxygen species via a photosensitizer (PS) and light, offering broad-spectrum antiviral potential. However, evidence on efficacy remains fragmented and spans mechanistically distinct applications ranging from ex vivo pathogen reduction to localized clinical treatment. This systematic review synthesizes available data on photosensitizer-mediated antiviral effects, therapeutic applications, and limitations, explicitly distinguishing PDI (ex vivo/environmental inactivation) from PDT (in vivo treatment).

METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for studies published between January 1990 and April 2026. Peer-reviewed original articles evaluating the antiviral effects of photosensitizer-mediated PDI or PDT in vitro, in vivo, or in clinical settings were included. Studies employing direct UV irradiation without a photosensitizer or light-independent antiviral mechanisms were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis. Two reviewers independently screened studies, assessed eligibility, and extracted data. Due to substantial heterogeneity in viral targets, photosensitizers (PSs), light parameters, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools.

RESULTS: Of 242 records, 30 studies (22 in vitro/ex vivo, 4 animal, and 4 clinical) were included. PDI achieved multi-log reductions against enveloped viruses, while non-enveloped viruses required higher PS concentrations and light doses. Common PSs included methylene blue, porphyrins, phthalocyanines, and Rose Bengal, riboflavin, and ruthenium complexes. Based on the limited and heterogeneous clinical data available, the safety profile of PDI in transfusion-related applications and PDT in mucocutaneous applications appears promising but remains to be conclusively established.

CONCLUSION: Photosensitizer-mediated PDI exhibits potent in vitro antiviral activity, particularly against enveloped viruses, through oxidative damage to viral components. However, the evidence is almost entirely preclinical, and current evidence does not support conventional PDT as a clinically feasible treatment for systemic viremia; its most realistic antiviral applications remain localized accessible infections and ex vivo pathogen reduction. Future extracorporeal or targeted light-delivery strategies may eventually expand these boundaries, but no such approach has yet been clinically validated. Further clinical studies are warranted for specific indications, particularly ex vivo blood product decontamination and localized mucocutaneous infections.

articles.title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.

RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

articles.title: A Whole-Heart Fluid-Structure Interaction Model for Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair in Primary Mitral Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary mitral regurgitation (MR) resulting from chordal rupture leads to acute volume overload and elevated left atrial pressure. Transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (TMVr) devices can effectively reduce MR, but their impact on global cardiac mechanics and diastolic filling remains difficult to predict. This study develops a whole-heart FSI framework for TMVr by extending a previously developed whole-heart model to represent chordal rupture and edge-to-edge repair and to quantify their structural and hemodynamic consequences.

METHODS: A three-dimensional FSI model of the heart derived from cardiac CT imaging was used to simulate three conditions: healthy baseline, chordal rupture-induced MR, and post-TMVr. The immersed finite element-difference method enables fully coupled simulation of blood flow, valve dynamics, and myocardial contraction. Hemodynamic metrics, including regurgitant fraction (RF), left atrial pressure (LAP), stroke volume (SV), stroke work (SW), and pressure-volume relationships, were compared with clinical reference data.

RESULTS: Chordal rupture produced moderate-to-severe MR (RF = 38%) and doubled left atrial V-wave amplitude, consistent with clinical observations. After TMVr, the central regurgitant jet produced by chordal rupture was eliminated, RF decreased to 21%, and LAP returned to near-baseline levels. However, the double-orifice valve configuration generated dual high-velocity inflow jets and reduced diastolic filling.

CONCLUSION: The repair effectively reduces regurgitation and atrial pressure while also influencing diastolic filling and ventricular output. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both regurgitation reduction and inflow characteristics when assessing TMVr outcomes and demonstrate the potential of patient-specific computational modeling for procedural planning and optimization.

articles.title: Identification and validation of stable reference genes for RT-qPCR analysis in blood samples from golden Syrian hamsters under different immunological conditions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The golden Syrian hamster is the main experimental model for leptospirosis. However, there are no validated reference genes for reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) analysis of blood samples.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The expression stability of 11 candidate reference genes was evaluated in hamster blood under distinct immunological conditions, including Leptospira interrogans infection and different immunization strategies. Stability was assessed using BestKeeper, geNorm, NormFinder, and the comparative ΔCt method, with the consensus ranking calculated using the RefFinder approach implemented in the RefSeeker R package. The most stable reference gene was ppia, followed by gapdh and ppib, whereas actb was the least stable gene in the ranking. Normalization of tnf-α expression using actb resulted in an approximately 10-fold overestimation compared with ppia, demonstrating the impact of reference gene choice on data interpretation.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support ppia as a reliable reference gene for RT-qPCR normalization in hamster blood under both infection and vaccination conditions.

articles.title: The AGT M235T variant and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system parameters in a predominantly hypertensive elderly black South African cohort: a hypothesis-generating descriptive case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a key cardiovascular risk factor, with its pathogenesis remaining incompletely understood. Blood pressure (BP) regulation involves the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), including the Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), Angiotensin I (Ang I) and Angiotensin II (Ang II). The rs699 variant (M235T) may influence BP via the RAAS.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the relationships between the rs699 genotypes, RAAS parameters, BP, Body mass index (BMI) and gender in a black elderly population.

METHODS: Data were collected from 48 participants aged ≥60 years, using World Health Organization (WHO) obesity guidelines and South African Hypertension Society (SAHS) 2019 standards for HTN categories. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS version 27 and Python 3.14.

RESULTS: Most participants possessed the rs699 variant (GG: 93.8%, AG: 4.2%). ACE levels were low in 64.6%, while Ang II was elevated in the same percentage. The majority were classified as hypertensive and obese. No significant associations were found between the rs699 variant and ACE, Ang I, Ang II, HTN, BMI or gender, though BMI showed sex-related differences in females.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest no significant association of the rs699 variant on RAAS or cardiometabolic parameters within the study population, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings require validation in larger and more diverse populations, as meaningful statistical inferences cannot be drawn from the current data.

articles.title: Microbial inoculants enhance crop yield, photosynthesis and disease suppression in China: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Microbial inoculants (MIs) represent a nature-based alternative to chemical fertilizers and pesticides, promoting crop growth and offering a promising route toward low-carbon development. To evaluate the effects of MIs on crops in China, we conducted a meta-analysis based on 1110 effect sizes derived from 172 studies, with the evidence base dominated by peer-reviewed Chinese-language literature. Overall, MIs application significantly increased crop growth by 23.45% (P < 0.001), with the harvest yield sub-indicator showing a 14.92% relative increase. This response was also significantly moderated by fertilization strategy (F(1) = 6.80, P = 0.009). Neither the composition of MIs (bacterial, fungal, or mixed) nor their source (commercial or non-commercial) exerted a significant moderating effect on the yield response of crops. The photosynthesis was also significantly enhanced under MI application, with an average increased by 18.53% (P < 0.001). The MIs source (F(1) = 6.69, P = 0.009), MIs application method (F(3) = 3.22, P = 0.022), MIs application frequency (F(1) = 4.59, P = 0.032) and fertilization strategy (F(1) = 11.41, P < 0.001) significantly affected the response pattern. The MIs application significantly suppressed disease incidence by 46.90% (P < 0.001), and decreased the disease index by 51.87% (P < 0.001). The disease incidence response differed significantly (F(1) = 4.42, P = 0.035) between commercial MIs (-66.98%) and non-commercial MIs (-41.09%). The disease index response was significantly affected by crop subclass (F(6) = 5.59, P < 0.001) and marginally affected by fertilization strategy (F(6) = 3.57, P = 0.059). Furthermore, when focused on bacterial MIs, the multi-strain MIs significantly outperformed single-strain in growth promotion (P = 0.022) and disease index suppression (P = 0.004). These results highlight the potential of MIs to improve crop performance, and their efficacy warrants further investigation under diverse field conditions to optimize their practical application.

articles.title: The predictive value of 99mTc-MIBI SPECT/18F-FDG PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging in patients with unrevascularized coronary chronic total occlusion and left ventricular dysfunction.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To explore the predictive value of hibernating myocardium detected by single photon emission computed tomography (SEPCT)/positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging for the adverse cardiovascular events in unrevascularized chronic coronary total occlusion (CTO) patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Additionally, we explore whether hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory can independently predictive outcomes. Patients with at least one unrevascularized CTO on coronary angiography and LV dysfunction and who underwent rest 99mTc-MIBI SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging as well as 18F-FDG PET myocardial metabolic imaging were enrolled. All patients were followed up through telephone interviews and review of medical records. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, the extents of hibernating myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories, the extent of total scarred myocardium, and the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were calculated according to the segmental perfusion/metabolism score and the segmental assignment of coronary dominance and the results of coronary angiography. The Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between the extent of hibernating or scarred myocardium and adverse cardiovascular events. Seventy eight patients were included in the final analysis. The median follow-up duration was 70.2 (27.7, 80.3) months. The extent of total hibernating myocardium and the extent of hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory were both independent predictors for cardiac death [hazards ratio (HR) = 1.289, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.083-1.533, P = 0.004; HR = 1.262, 95% CI 1.022-1.557, P = 0.030] and the composite endpoint events (HR = 1.190, 95% CI 1.032-1.372, P = 0.016; HR = 1.273, 95% CI 1.025-1.581, P = 0.029). The extent of hibernating myocardium in the non-CTO territory, the extent of total scarred myocardium, the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were all not associated with the outcome. 99mTc-MIBI /18F-FDG SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging has an important predictive value for prognosis in unrevascularized CTO patients with LV dysfunction. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, especially hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory, was an independent predictor for adverse cardiovascular events.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA and Acute Myocarditis: A Comparative Multiparametric Evaluation.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and acute myocarditis (AM) often present with overlapping clinical features and biomarker profiles, making early differential diagnosis challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference modality for etiological assessment through functional evaluation and multiparametric tissue characterization. The aim of this study was to compare clinical and CMR characteristics of patients with MINOCA and suspected AM, and to identify imaging features enabling accurate differentiation. We retrospectively analyzed 127 consecutive patients undergoing CMR (February 2021-October 2024): 62 with suspected MINOCA and 65 with suspected AM. Clinical data, laboratory findings, ECG, and CMR parameters (cine imaging, T1/T2 mapping, extracellular volume [ECV], and late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) were assessed. MINOCA patients were older (median 59 years) and predominantly female (64.5%), whereas AM patients were younger (median 29 years) and mainly male (81.5%). AM was associated with higher troponin and inflammatory markers. Among patients initially referred with suspected MINOCA, LGE was present in 50.0%, compared with 93.8% of those referred with suspected acute myocarditis (p < 0.001). MINOCA showed predominantly ischemic LGE patterns, while AM exhibited non-ischemic subepicardial or mid-wall LGE with myocardial edema. CMR confirmed myocardial infarction in 48.4% of patients and identified alternative diagnoses in 41.9%, while 9.7% had normal CMR findings. Multiparametric CMR reliably distinguishes ischemic from inflammatory myocardial injury in patients with chest pain, elevated troponin, and non-obstructive coronaries. Early CMR integration improves diagnostic accuracy and supports tailored management.

articles.title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

articles.title: Traversing the labyrinth: multimodality imaging of Kawasaki disease with saccular coronary artery aneurysms.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD), an acute vasculitis of childhood, is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in developed countries with approximately 25% of untreated cases resulting in coronary artery aneurysms (1). Treatment during the acute phase with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and aspirin reduces the prevalence of coronary artery abnormalities; long-term management with thromboprophylaxis, beta blockers, statins, or surgical coronary artery bypass is determined based on coronary Z score, response to treatment, and evidence of myocardial ischemia throughout surveillance (2). The presented case highlights the severe complications of KD, necessity of multimodality imaging, and long-term management in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Sequential multimodality imaging-guided transseptal strategy for cryoballoon ablation in cor triatriatum sinister.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To describe a sequential multimodality imaging strategy for transseptal access during cryoballoon ablation in a patient with cor triatriatum sinister (CTS).

METHODS: A 55-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and CTS underwent preprocedural cardiac computed tomography (CCT), followed by real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast confirmation, and fluoroscopic guidance during the procedure.

RESULTS: CCT demonstrated pulmonary vein drainage into a Proximal Chamber (Posterior-Superior), separated from the Distal Chamber (Anterior-Inferior) by a membrane. Real-time TEE identified and confirmed an anterosuperior transseptal site, with septal tenting before needle passage. After a single BRK needle puncture, contrast confirmed access to the pulmonary-vein-containing chamber, allowing advancement of the FlexCath Advance catheter (Medtronic) and cryoballoon isolation of all 4 pulmonary veins without procedural complications.

CONCLUSION: In CTS, transseptal access should be tailored to the individual atrial anatomy. Sequential use of CCT, real-time TEE, contrast, and fluoroscopy can provide complementary information at the successive stages of the procedure.

articles.title: Gene expression, MMGBSA, molecular and induced-fit docking of Bambusa vulgaris phytocompounds in endoplasmic reticulum stress induced by streptozotocin.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) has been linked to insulin resistance and diabetes mellitus. Bambusa vulgaris, a tropical bamboo species widely used in traditional medicine, is used to reduce oxidative stress and as an antidiabetic agent. This study investigates the effect of B. vulgaris on ERS-related gene expression and conducts a computational analysis of B. vulgaris phytocompounds.

METHODS: ERS was induced intraperitoneally by 60 mg/kg streptozotocin (STZ) dissolved in citrate buffer. Thirty experimental rats (n = 5) were divided into six groups: control, ERS control, metformin (100 mg/kg), and B. vulgaris aqueous extract (BV) orally administered groups (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg). Fasting blood glucose was monitored with a glucometer; RT-PCR was used for gene expression after 21 days of treatment. Molecular and induced-fit docking, free binding energy, and ADMET profiling of B. vulgaris compounds with PERK were evaluated using Schrödinger.

RESULTS: GRP78, CHOP, ATF4, and PERK mRNA expressions were markedly (p < 0.05) upregulated relative to the control upon induction with STZ after 72 h. BV (50 and 100 mg/kg) significantly downregulated these genes' expression compared with untreated ERS rats. Luteolin and chlorogenic acid had the lowest docking scores (-10.764 kcal/mol and - 10.725 kcal/mol), with strong induced-fit scores and free binding energies (-42.2 kcal/mol and - 39.33 kcal/mol, respectively). Both comply with Lipinski's rules of drug-likeness. Isovitexin has the lowest free binding energy - 50.91 kcal/mol.

CONCLUSION: This work suggests that BV and its compounds downregulate genes associated with ERS and promote normoglycemia.

articles.title: Dissecting polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome heterogeneity (PMOS): multi-omics, AI subtyping, and precision management.
articles.abstract: Polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is the most common endocrine disorder, affecting 8-12% of women of reproductive age and increasing the risk of infertility, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease. However, traditional symptom-based diagnostic criteria do not fully capture the underlying biological diversity of PMOS. Recent research using multi-omics and artificial intelligence (AI) has revealed that PMOS is best understood as a syndrome with multiple subtypes. Data-driven clustering of clinical variables consistently identifies four major subtypes: HA-PCOS, OB-PCOS, SHBG-PCOS, and LH-PCOS. Each subtype shows unique hormonal, metabolic, and genetic features, including distinct patterns in lipid, amino acid, and energy metabolism. Immune system disruptions and impaired blood clot breakdown in the ovarian environment are also notable features. Novel findings suggest that altered lactate metabolism and changes in histone lactylation may contribute to granulosa cell dysfunction, although further studies are needed to confirm these mechanisms. Machine learning models that integrate clinical, metabolic, and genetic data have achieved high diagnostic accuracy and can provide interpretable results. Potential targeted therapies, such as GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, N-acetylcysteine, and NK3R antagonists, have been proposed for specific subtypes, but have yet to be validated in clinical trials. Remaining challenges include small and homogeneous study cohorts, limited long-term data, and barriers to care in low-resource settings. Overall, recognizing PMOS as a syndrome with distinct subtypes highlights the promise of AI-powered, personalized approaches for more effective and equitable management.

articles.title: Cellulose acetate nanoparticles: impacts of concentration and exposure time on the biochemistry and hematology of juvenile Colossoma macropomum.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the physiological impacts of acute-exposure of tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) to different concentrations of cellulose acetate nanoparticles at different sampling times. A total of 120 juvenile C. macropomum (38.91 ± 5.57 g and 13.76 ± 0.74 cm in total length) were distributed in 12 tanks of 150 L, in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The juveniles were kept in water containing cellulose acetate nanoparticles (CANs) at four different concentrations (treatments): 0 mg L-¹, 0.01 mg L-¹, 0.10 mg L-¹ and 1.00 mg L-¹. Blood samples were collected after 1 and 24 h of exposure. The juveniles were then relocated to a tank with clean water, where they remained for another 24 h, after which a new blood sample was collected (24 h). Hemoglobin, serum protein and globulin were reduced after 1 h of exposure for the group exposed to 1.00 mg L-¹ of CANs. Glucose levels increased after 24 h for the groups exposed to 0.10 and 1.00 mg L-¹. Urea increased after 1 h for the groups exposed to 0.10 and 1.00 mg L-¹. Triglycerides and cholesterol were reduced both after 1 h and 24 h of exposure for the 1.00 mg L-¹ group, returning to baseline levels at 24 h. The activities of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase were altered after 24 h. Albumin was lower after 1 h and 24 h compared to after 24 h for the 1.00 mg L-¹ group. Exposure of juvenile C. macropomum to CANs caused transient physiological changes, with partial recovery being observed after transfer to clean water.

articles.title: Mucosal disease associated with BVDV-1b and BVDV-1e in cattle in Southern Brazil.
articles.abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) is an important pathogen of the global cattle industry. Fetal infection during the period of immunotolerance may result in the birth of persistently infected (PI) animals. In such animals, the emergence of or superinfection with cytopathic variants may trigger mucosal disease (MD). The objective of this study was to characterize the anatomopathological and virological aspects of two cases of MD. Animal 1, a 24-month-old presented with diarrhea, weight loss, lameness, sialorrhea, and oral and cutaneous lesions. Animal 2, a four-month-old, exhibited weight loss, intermittent diarrhea, and dehydration. Both animals were submitted to necropsy, and tissue samples from all organs were collected for histopathological evaluation. For BVDV detection, serum samples were subjected to RT-PCR and amplified products were submitted to Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Liver and spleen fragments were used for viral isolation in MDBK cell cultures. Immunohistochemistry using the panpestiviral monoclonal antibody 15C5 was performed to detect BVDV antigen. Anatomopathological examination of Animal 1 revealed ulcerative glossitis, erosive stomatitis, erosive and ulcerative esophagitis as well as erosive and ulcerative rumenitis, erosive abomasitis, and ulcerative and crusting dermatitis affecting the nasal planum and the distal limb region. In Animal 2, ulcerative rumenitis, erosive abomasitis, and lymphoid depletion in the ileal Peyer's patches were observed. Both animals were positive for BVDV in immunohistochemistry and classified as BVDV-1e and BVDV-1b based on phylogenetic analysis. Viral isolates from both cases induced cytopathic effect between 48 and 96 h post-inoculation. This study demonstrates distinct lesion patterns in unrelated cases of MD associated with BVDV-1e and BVDV-1b in cattle, constitutes the first report of typical MD associated with these subgenotypes in Brazil.

articles.title: Identical consensus genomes of bovine coronavirus in respiratory and enteric specimens from a single cow and sequence variation after cell culture passage.
articles.abstract: Bovine coronavirus (BCoV) causes respiratory and enteric diseases in cattle, but the relationship between viral genetic variation and anatomical distribution remains unclear. We compared BCoV genomes detected in a tracheal swab and diarrheic intestinal content from the same adult cow. The two clinical specimens had identical 31,015-nt consensus genomes. After five passages in HRT-18 cells, the recovered tracheal isolate differed at three consensus-level amino acid positions (HE N104D, S Q179K, and S E965D) and showed marked within-sample heterogeneity. These findings highlight the importance of direct sequencing of clinical specimens because cell-culture passage can alter viral population composition.

articles.title: Association between cancer cachexia and treatment-related adverse outcomes in patients with gastrointestinal cancers: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cachexia represents a critical nutritional problem, especially among patients with gastrointestinal cancer, and is potentially linked to unfavorable outcomes. Nevertheless, the influence of cancer cachexia on treatment-related adverse events in these patients remains insufficiently incorporated into current understanding. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the association between cancer cachexia and treatment-related adverse outcomes in patients with gastrointestinal cancers.

METHODS: Five electronic databases were searched for relevant studies. Cohort studies investigating the association of cachexia with postoperative complications, chemotherapy-related adverse events, radiotherapy-related adverse events, length of hospital stay, and readmission in patients with gastrointestinal cancers were included.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies involving 27,473 participants were included. Cancer cachexia was significantly associated with higher odds of postoperative complications (odds ratio [OR] 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.11-1.72) and prolonged length of hospital stay (mean difference = 2.09, 95% CI = 0.91-3.26). No significant association was observed between cancer cachexia and chemotherapy-related adverse events (OR = 1.42, 95% CI = 0.57-3.54). All pooled analyses showed considerable to substantial heterogeneity. No studies evaluating radiotherapy-related adverse events and only one study evaluating readmission met the inclusion criteria; therefore, these outcomes could not be quantitatively synthesized.

CONCLUSIONS: Cancer cachexia was associated with an increased risk of postoperative complications and prolonged length of hospital stay in patients with gastrointestinal cancers. However, because of the substantial heterogeneity and the very low certainty of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted with caution and cannot be considered definitive.

articles.title: Biomarkers and future directions for immunotherapy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: The mechanisms of resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) have 3 interconnected levels, which provide information to guide different biomarker strategies. There is a critical clinical need, as objective response rates continue to be < 10%. We suggest a biomarker stratification model on the basis of clinical actionability. POLE/POLD1 mutations, recommended by the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology for Colon Cancer (Version 1.2025), represent true genomic "hard" indicators. While the benefit of ICI-containing combination regimens was predicted by the Immunoscore-IC in the AtezoTRIBE trial, the ANICCA-class II study recently questioned the value of anti-PD-1 monotherapy. Defects in homologous recombination repair HRR), ctDNA kinetics and subtyping of CMS1 show promise but need to be prospectively validated. TMB, however, has shown no consistent value as a single biomarker, and MSIs, such as transcriptomic signatures or PD-L1 combined positive scores, have not been proven to be useful. Future prospects involve multiomics algorithms that integrate immune profiling and stromal determinants, liver-directed sensitizing approaches and serial ctDNA monitoring of acquired resistance as viable strategies for further patient selection. These data collectively pave the way toward moving away from the "cold tumor" paradigm and toward dynamic, host-integrated testing for precision immunotherapy in MSS CRC.

articles.title: Acute Pain Management in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes current approaches to pain assessment and pharmacologic therapy in the intensive care unit (ICU) and evaluates the expanding role of regional anesthesia (RA).

RECENT FINDINGS: Contemporary ICU analgesia emphasizes systematic pain assessment and multimodal therapy while avoiding unnecessary deep sedation. RA provides targeted, opioid-sparing analgesia for localized pain but is limited by coagulopathy, infection, altered anatomy, and practical considerations. Fascial-plane blocks may provide useful alternatives in selected patients. Thoracic epidural and paravertebral techniques remain options for selected patients but may cause hypotension and clinically significant bleeding. Ultrasound-guided techniques, including erector spinae, serratus anterior, parasternal, rectus sheath, and transversus abdominis plane blocks, expand analgesic options. Continuous catheter techniques may extend analgesia when prolonged pain is anticipated. However, evidence in heterogeneous ICU populations remains limited, and much of the current evidence is derived from perioperative or trauma populations rather than general medical ICU cohorts. Further ICU-specific comparative trials are needed to define patient selection and clinically meaningful outcomes.

articles.title: Disulfide-oxidized HMGB1 mutant construction and its mechanism in AMI-induced myocardial injury.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.

articles.title: Prophylactic neurectomy versus nerve preservation in open inguinal hernia repair for prevention of chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic postoperative inguinal pain remains an important source of disability after open inguinal hernia repair. The review evaluated whether planned prophylactic neurectomy reduces chronic pain compared with nerve preservation in adults undergoing elective open anterior repair.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Ovid MEDLINE were searched from January 2000 through March 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing intentional neurectomy of one or more inguinal nerves with preservation during open anterior repair were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios and standardized mean differences.

RESULTS: Seventeen randomized trials were included. At the longest follow-up, chronic postoperative inguinal pain occurred in 166 of 1779 participants after neurectomy and 294 of 1627 after preservation (9.3% vs. 18.1%; RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.25-0.55; I² = 69.2%). Associations favored neurectomy at 3, 6, and 12 months or longer. Moderate-to-severe chronic pain remained statistically uncertain. Sensory loss or change increased, while groin numbness remained similar. Acute pain and rescue analgesic use were lower. Health-related quality of life, recurrence, and surgical complications did not differ meaningfully.

CONCLUSION: Prophylactic neurectomy was associated with less chronic pain but more sensory disturbance and no measurable quality-of-life benefit. Incomplete reporting of nerve identification in control procedures, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity preclude routine use. Existing trials could not identify patients most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Epigallocatechin gallate inhibits rabies virus glycoprotein‑mediated infection in vitro.
articles.abstract: Rabies is one of the most lethal zoonotic disease and causes approximately 60,000 human deaths annually. The high cost of immunoglobulin prophylaxis and the need for cold chain maintenance highlight the need for accessible antiviral strategies, particularly in resource-limited settings. Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the major polyphenolic compound of Camellia sinensis, has broad-spectrum antiviral activity. We therefore investigated its activity against Rabies virus (RABV). Because RABV requires BSL-3 containment, we first used a recombinant Vesicular Stomatitis Virus pseudotyped with RABV glycoprotein (pRABV) as a surrogate. EGCG inhibited pRABV infection in a concentration-dependent manner, with an EC50 of approximately 0.15 µg/mL and a selectivity index > 551.72. Time-of-addition, attachment, and entry assays showed that EGCG reduced pRABV infectivity when present during viral adsorption or after pre-incubation with viral particles, whereas no inhibition was observed when cells were treated before infection or after virus internalization. Viral infectivity remained almost completely abolished in a virucidal assay even after EGCG was diluted below its effective antiviral concentration, supporting a direct and irreversible effect on viral particles. EGCG activity was further confirmed using authentic RABV and disease-relevant cell types, including myotubes and neurons. Overall, these findings indicate that EGCG inhibits early stages of the RABV replication cycle, primarily by interfering with viral attachment and directly affecting viral particles. Further studies are needed to define the molecular basis of this interaction and assess the therapeutic potential of EGCG against RABV.

articles.title: The perceptions of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation decision-making in patients with hematologic malignancies: a qualitative systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains the primary curative option for many hematologic malignancies, yet its substantial risks make the treatment decision highly complex and high stakes for patients. Although current qualitative studies have explored how patients perceive HSCT, a comprehensive synthesis of these insights is still lacking. This study synthesizes existing research on patient perceptions of HSCT to guide shared decision-making in clinical practice.

METHODS: A literature search was conducted across eight databases: PubMed, CINAHL, PsycARTICLES, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global, spanning from their respective inceptions to February 2026. The Joanna Briggs Institute criteria for qualitative research were utilized to evaluate the quality of the studies, and a content analysis approach was employed to integrate the findings.

RESULTS: A total of 20 studies were included, yielding 4 new integrated findings: (1) constrained choices; (2) decision-making embedded in relational contexts; (3) the hidden toll: financial constraints and logistical hurdles; (4) concerns about restricted social participation and threats to identity caused by transplantation.

CONCLUSION: HSCT decision-making is shaped not only by clinical risks and benefits, but also by constrained choice, relational contexts, practical circumstances, and concerns about future life. SDM-based decision support should therefore extend beyond information provision to clarify patients' understanding of the decision space, identify factors that constrain choice, and address the values and longer-term concerns that matter to them.

articles.title: Protective effect of N-acetylcysteine on oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy in colorectal cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (OIPN) is a dose-limiting adverse effect of FOLFOX chemotherapy in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We aimed to evaluate the protective effect of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) against OIPN. Additionally, we investigated its mechanistic effects on serum biomarkers including total antioxidant capacity (TAC), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and neurotensin.

METHODS: Forty-six patients with stage III or high-risk stage II CRC receiving adjuvant modified FOLFOX-6 chemotherapy were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either oral NAC 1200 mg (effervescent tablets or granules) or placebo one hour before each oxaliplatin infusion for four cycles. Serum levels of TAC, IL-6, and neurotensin were measured before and after treatment. Neuropathy was assessed using the FACT/GOG-NTX-12 and NCI-CTCAE scales, and pain was estimated by using the Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form.

RESULTS: Neurotensin was significantly decreased in the NAC group compared to controls after treatment (P < 0.001), and was significantly lower post-treatment versus pre-treatment in the NAC group (P = 0.001). IL-6 was significantly reduced in the NAC group versus controls after treatment (P < 0.001), and significantly decreased post-treatment in both groups (P < 0.05). FACT/GOG-NTX-12 and NCI-CTCAE scores were significantly lower in the NAC group at the end of the first two cycles and at the end of treatment (P < 0.05). Pain interference, but not pain severity, was significantly reduced in the NAC group at both time points (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: NAC administration during FOLFOX chemotherapy significantly reduced OIPN severity, pain interference, and serum levels of IL-6 and neurotensin, suggesting both clinical and mechanistic neuroprotective effects.

CLINICAL REGISTRATION: The study was is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT07391163).

articles.title: STN-SNr co-stimulation in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of motor and freezing-of-gait outcomes.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Freezing of gait (FoG) and axial impairments often persist in Parkinson's disease despite optimized medication and subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS). We systematically reviewed whether adding substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) stimulation improves motor and FoG outcomes.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 and PROSPERO registration (CRD420261343479), six databases were searched through 1 May 2026. Primary outcomes compared STN-SNr co-stimulation with STN-only stimulation; stimulation-off or baseline comparisons were secondary. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. UPDRS-III and FoG were pooled as mean differences (MDs) and Hedges' g, respectively, accounting for paired data and within-study dependence. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: Ten studies (nine randomized trials and one observational study) included 109 unique evaluable participants; two single-patient case reports were summarized narratively. UPDRS-III showed no between-group difference across seven studies (73 participants; MD - 0.10, 95% CI - 1.01 to 0.81; I² = 0%; low certainty). FoG showed no additional benefit across six studies (86 participants; Hedges' g - 0.23, 95% CI - 1.04 to 0.59; I²_total = 85.6%; very low certainty). Secondary baseline comparisons favored co-stimulation for UPDRS-III (MD - 13.55) and FoG (Hedges' g - 0.60), but did not isolate an incremental SNr effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Low-certainty evidence suggests no clinically important difference in global motor outcomes, while very-low-certainty evidence does not demonstrate a consistent additional FoG benefit. Improvements versus stimulation-off or baseline cannot establish an incremental SNr effect. Larger phenotype-stratified trials with objective gait endpoints and systematic adverse-event reporting are needed.

articles.title: Targeting the gut-liver axis and gut microbiome in pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: current evidence and future directions.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease in children, closely linked to the rising prevalence of childhood obesity and metabolic syndrome. Increasing evidence highlights the central role of the gut-liver axis and the gut microbiome in disease pathogenesis, offering potential targets for therapeutic modulation. This review aims to summarize current evidence on interventions targeting the gut-liver axis and the gut microbiome in pediatric MASLD and explore emerging strategies in this field. This narrative review was undertaken after searching PubMed and Embase databases for available up-to-date literature on pediatric MASLD and therapeutic interventions targeting the gut microbiome and gut-liver axis, including dietary therapy, prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and pharmacological therapies. Dietary interventions, including low-free-sugar and Mediterranean-style diets, improve hepatic and metabolic outcomes, although microbiome-mediated benefits remain unproven in children. Probiotics and synbiotics show modest and variable effects, with heterogeneity in strains, dosing, and outcomes limiting definitive conclusions. Evidence for FMT in pediatric MASLD is absent, with only indirect evidence from adolescent obesity and other pediatric diseases. Pharmacological therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and farnesoid X receptor agonists, have demonstrated metabolic and hepatic benefits primarily in adult populations, while effects on microbial metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, and bile acid signalling provide potential mechanisms linking these therapies to the gut-liver axis. Although microbiome-mediated mechanisms have been proposed, direct evidence linking these therapies to microbiome changes in pediatric MASLD is currently lacking. Emerging approaches such as precision nutrition, engineered probiotics, and bacteriophage therapy offer potential avenues for targeted modulation of disease-relevant pathways.

CONCLUSION: Therapeutic modulation of the gut-liver axis and the gut microbiome represents a biologically plausible and evolving strategy in pediatric MASLD. Current pediatric evidence remains limited, and robust, well-designed clinical trials incorporating microbiome profiling and clinically meaningful endpoints are needed to establish efficacy and enable personalized, therapeutic strategies.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric MASLD is increasing in prevalence, and alterations in the gut-liver axis and the gut microbiome are known to contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease by influencing various disease-relevant pathways such as intestinal permeability, bile acid signaling, hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrogenesis.

WHAT IS NEW: • This review provides current evidence for interventions targeting the gut microbiome and gut-liver axis in pediatric MASLD including dietary modulation, probiotics, and pharmacological interventions and highlights new approaches such as precision nutrition, engineered probiotics, bacteriophage therapy, and personalized treatment strategies.

articles.title: Beyond infection: the longitudinal impact of genitourinary tuberculosis on urologic and reproductive health.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To address the limited understanding of the long-term morbidity of genitourinary tuberculosis (GUTB), by characterizing the clinical course and risk of urologic events (UE) both preceding and following GUTB diagnosis.

METHODS: This retrospective age-, sex- and comorbidity-matched cohort study evaluated all patients with GUTB in Merative Marketscan (2011-2021). Patients were followed throughout enrollment to capture comorbid diseases (pulmonary tuberculosis and HIV) and urologic events (diagnoses and procedures). Events- and diagnoses-of-interest that occurred both prior and after GUTB diagnosis were included. UEs were classified as low-grade events, high-grade events, or infertility. Multivariable cox proportional hazards models compared the risk of UEs over time.

RESULTS: 1503 patients with GUTB were identified. Mean patient age was 43 years. Most patients were otherwise healthy (63% CCI ≤ 1). GUTB was associated with 2.5-fold the risk of high-grade UE prior to diagnosis (HR 2.5, p < 0.001) and 2.7-fold the risk after diagnosis (HR 2.7, p < 0.001). It was also associated with two-fold the risk of low-grade UE prior to diagnosis (HR 2.0, p < 0.001) and a 1.6-fold after diagnosis (HR 1.6, p < 0.001). Infertility risk was significant among GUTB patients in the pre-diagnosis setting (HR 2.6, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: GUTB is associated with a substantial increase in urologic morbidity, with elevated risks of low- and high-grade events before and after diagnosis, suggesting a prolonged and perhaps unrecognized subclinical disease course. The increased risk of infertility prior to diagnosis highlights importance of considering GUTB in unexplained infertility, particularly in TB-endemic regions.

articles.title: Molecular Characterization of Feline Leukemia Virus from Cats in Shelters in the Metropolitan Region of Recife, Pernambuco, Northeast Brazil.
articles.abstract: This research aimed to conduct an epidemiological-molecular study of feline leukemia virus (FeLV) infection in cats from shelters in the Metropolitan Region of Recife (MRR), Pernambuco, Northeast Brazil. Blood samples from 260 cats from 18 shelters located in 5 municipalities within the MRR were analyzed. DNA samples from peripheral blood were subjected to Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) to detect FeLV proviral DNA. PCR-positive samples were sequenced and analyzed using BLAST software for phylogenetic tree construction. The prevalence of infection in cats was 9.6% (25/260). Among the 18 sampled shelters, 33.3% (6/18) had cats positive for FeLV. It was observed that 60% (3/5) of the investigated municipalities had felines positive for FeLV infection. Among the positive cats, males accounted for 52% (13/25) and females for 48% (12/25). Of the 22 sequenced samples, 18 sequences were used as queries for an online BLAST search to build a dataset. This study is pioneering in the state of Pernambuco and demonstrates the prevalence of FeLV infection in felines living in shelters in the Metropolitan Region of Recife, PE. Based on these results, we recommend vaccinating any cat with outdoor access in the study region. Understanding the prevalence of FeLV in Pernambuco provides insights into the local situation and helps develop effective hygienic-sanitary programs in feline shelters in the MRR, contributing to increased awareness of responsible pet ownership and reducing FeLV transmission among community felines.

articles.title: Eugenol Activity Against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus: Biofilm Disruption and Additive Interactions with Antibiotics.
articles.abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria and their ability to form biofilms represent significant challenges in infection control. This study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of eugenol (Eug) against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus from food and clinical sources. Antibacterial activity was assessed using disk diffusion, broth microdilution (MIC/MBC), and bacterial growth kinetics. Antibiofilm activity was measured by crystal violet staining, CFU enumeration, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Checkerboard assays evaluated the combinatorial effect of Eug with ciprofloxacin and oxacillin. Eug exhibited inhibition zones of 13-22 mm and MIC/MBC values of 1000-2000 µg/mL. Subinhibitory concentrations significantly delayed bacterial growth. Biofilm biomass was reduced by up to 90% in E. coli and 80% in S. aureus, with SEM confirming structural alterations. Checkerboard assays revealed additive interactions with antibiotics. These findings provide additional evidence of Eug's antibacterial properties and support further investigation into its combinatorial effects with antibiotics against biofilm-associated challenges.

articles.title: Immediate vs delayed extubation after pediatric liver transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: PALISI Liver Failure Special Interest Group
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Immediate extubation (IE) in the operating room following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is increasingly adopted in adults but pediatric evidence remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify factors associated with IE and compare outcomes between IE and delayed extubation (DE) after pediatric OLT. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 30, 2025. Studies comparing IE and DE in pediatric OLT recipients were included. Outcomes included reintubation, mortality, thrombosis, reoperation, tracheostomy, PICU, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Random-effects meta-analysis was pre-specified for all outcomes; sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Twelve retrospective single-center studies comprising 1323 patients (1158 unique children after accounting for two center-level cohort overlaps) were included. IE was associated with lower odds of reintubation (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59) and mortality (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18-0.68); both estimates were confirmed by a correction-free Peto odds ratio (0.29 and 0.31, respectively). No significant differences were observed for thrombosis or reoperation. IE was associated with shorter PICU LOS (SMD - 0.88, 95% CI - 1.39 to - 0.37), hospital LOS (SMD - 1.16, 95% CI - 2.00 to - 0.31). Donor-type subgroup analyses showed effect sizes in the same direction as the overall analysis for PICU and hospital LOS, but none of the within-subgroup estimates reached statistical significance. Meta-regression identified intraoperative transfusion differences as predictor of hospital LOS (β =  - 0.045, p = 0.006, R2 = 57.1%), a pattern more consistent with confounding by indication than with a beneficial mechanism of transfusion itself.

CONCLUSIONS: IE was associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter LOS in pediatric OLT, but these findings derive exclusively from retrospective studies at high risk of selection bias, and causality cannot be established. Children undergoing IE were likely older and in better preoperative condition; hospital LOS findings are particularly susceptible to confounding. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these outcomes benefit.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Delayed extubation with prolonged mechanical ventilation has been standard after pediatric orthotopic liver transplantation. • Immediate extubation in the operating room is increasingly used after adult liver transplantation experiences. • Pediatric evidence on immediate extubation comes from single-center retrospective studies.

WHAT IS NEW: • This meta-analysis of 12 studies found immediate extubation associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter length of stay. • These associations likely reflect selection bias rather than a proven causal benefit. • Immediate extubation appears feasible and safe in selected children, but prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine patients benefiting from this approach.

articles.title: Alarmingly high multidrug resistance among Helicobacter pylori isolates from gastric biopsies in Egypt: phenotypic characterization and clinical correlation.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is a major cause of chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and gastric cancer, while increasing antimicrobial resistance has become a major challenge to successful eradication. This study investigated the phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of H. pylori isolates from Egyptian patients and evaluated their associations with clinical characteristics. Gastric biopsy specimens were collected from 60 patients undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. H. pylori was isolated by culture under microaerophilic conditions and identified using conventional phenotypic methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed by the disk diffusion method against commonly prescribed antibiotics. H. pylori was successfully isolated from 20 of 60 patients. Gastritis and gastric ulcer were significantly associated with culture positivity (p = 0.002 and p = 0.035, respectively), whereas no significant associations were observed for other clinical manifestations. All isolates (100%) were multidrug-resistant (MDR), and 90% were resistant to both clarithromycin and amoxicillin.
