Although higher isolation rates were observed among male patients and those aged ≥ 60 years, neither sex nor age was significantly associated with multidrug resistance (p > 0.05). These findings demonstrate an alarming prevalence of MDR H. pylori isolates in Egypt, emphasizing the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance surveillance and susceptibility-guided eradication strategies to improve treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Aorto-Pulmonary Shunt Creation in Congenital Heart Disease: Different Indications, Various Modifications, but Common Technical Challenges.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous creation of an aorto-pulmonary (AP) shunt has been explored in preclinical models for over 15 years, yet its clinical application remains limited. Surgical AP shunts are widely used to augment pulmonary blood flow in cyanotic congenital heart disease, but repeated thoracic operations and general anesthesia carry substantial risks in critically ill or surgically complex patients. A less invasive transcatheter alternative could therefore represent a transformative option. We report a case series of two pediatric patients in whom a percutaneous connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery was successfully established. Indications were severe cyanosis due to compromised pulmonary blood flow in one child and suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension requiring decompression in the other. The procedures were technically feasible and resulted in the intended immediate hemodynamic effects, either by enhancing pulmonary perfusion or by enabling right-to-left shunting for right heart decompression. Conceptually, percutaneous AP shunt creation parallels the transcatheter Potts shunt, which is increasingly recognized as a therapeutic option in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Both approaches establish controlled communication between the aorta and pulmonary artery, adapted to distinct physiological settings. Our report represents, to our knowledge, the first description of percutaneous AP shunt creation to improve pulmonary blood flow and oxygenation in congenital heart disease, as well as the first percutaneous connection between the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery. These cases illustrate the technical feasibility of catheter-based AP shunt creation in selected pediatric patients and support further evaluation of this approach.

articles.title: Maternal Anxiety Surrounding Fetal Cardiac Evaluation: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Fetal echocardiography has transformed prenatal cardiac diagnosis, yet the emotional burden of referral and evaluation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify maternal anxiety before and after fetal cardiac evaluation (FCE), identify clinical predictors of anxiety, and assess whether anxiety changes following evaluation and consultation regardless of outcome. In this prospective cohort study, 117 pregnant women undergoing initial or follow-up FCE completed pre- and post-consultation assessments using a seven-item symptom inventory adapted from the Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SASRQ; score range 7-42). Participants were classified as anxious or non-anxious by direct self-report. Scores were compared with paired t-tests; exploratory multivariable models adjusted for clinical, demographic, and referral covariates, including prior pregnancy loss, psychiatric history, and diagnostic outcome. 80% of participants (94/117) reported anxiety about the FCE before evaluation; prior pregnancy loss was associated with anxious state (p = 0.049). Following FCE and consultation, mean symptom scores in the anxious group fell from 15.07 to 9.03, a 6.04-point (40.1%) reduction (p < 0.001), with reductions across symptom domains regardless of diagnostic outcome. Scores in the non-anxious group did not change significantly (8.48 to 7.87; p = 0.27). Most women referred for FCE report anxiety before evaluation. FCE with consultation was associated with a substantial reduction in anxiety symptoms in these women, irrespective of whether a cardiac abnormality was found. Although the uncontrolled pre-post design cannot establish causation, these findings suggest that diagnostic clarity and expert consultation may themselves be anxiety-reducing and support evaluation of integrated psychosocial care models in fetal cardiology.

articles.title: Contact Aspiration Versus Combined Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion: Clinical Severity and First-pass Recanalization Are Associated with Outcome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) carries high rates of death and disability despite endovascular therapy, and the optimal technique remains unclear. We compared contact aspiration (CA) alone with combined CA plus stent retriever (CA + SR) and identified factors associated with first-pass reperfusion and 3‑month outcome.

METHODS: In the prospective multicenter SARA-3 registry, the primary outcomes compared between CA and CA + SR were first-pass recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3) and 3‑month functional independence. Secondary outcomes were final recanalization, procedural time, safety, 24‑h NIHSS, and mortality. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) were assessed by Firth penalized logistic regression, with first-line technique forced in as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Among 68 patients (median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] 11), 50 (73.5%) received CA and 18 (26.5%) CA + SR. The two techniques showed no statistically significant differences in reperfusion, safety, or 3‑month unfavorable outcome (48% vs. 53%; underpowered), but CA was faster (21 vs. 38 min; P = 0.007). Admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.08 per point; P = 0.004) and first-pass mTICI 2b-3 (OR 0.06; P < 0.001) were independently associated with outcome; their combination discriminated well (area under the curve 0.83). Forcing technique into the model did not change these associations (CA + SR adjusted OR 1.19; P = 0.81). No baseline characteristic was independently associated with first-pass reperfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: CA and CA + SR showed no statistically significant difference in 3‑month outcomes, but CA was faster. First-line technique was not associated with functional outcome; instead, outcome reflected baseline stroke severity and first-pass reperfusion, which defined prognostic groups that may aid risk stratification if externally validated.

articles.title: Comparative outcomes of uni-portal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery and unilateral biportal spinal endoscopy for far-lateral lumbar disc herniation involving the foraminal region: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and efficacy of unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (UBE) and uniportal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery (UNSES) in patients with far-lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH) involving the foraminal region.

METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 102 patients with foraminal-region FLLDH who were treated between January 2022 and October 2024. Among them, 43 patients underwent UNSES and 59 underwent UBE. Perioperative variables were recorded. Back and leg pain visual analog scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) scores, Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) scores, and modified Macnab outcomes were compared between groups preoperatively and at each postoperative follow-up. Preoperative and postoperative day 1 computed tomography images were analyzed to assess changes in foraminal area.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed successfully. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups. Operative time was significantly shorter in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P < 0.001). In both groups, VAS scores for back and leg pain and ODI scores improved significantly from baseline at all postoperative follow-up time points (all P < 0.05). However, these outcomes did not differ significantly between the groups at any postoperative follow-up time point.On postoperative day 3, the JOA score was significantly higher in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P = 0.031). JOA scores did not differ significantly between the groups at 3, 6, or 12 months after surgery. Imaging analysis showed that the foraminal area increased postoperatively in both groups. On postoperative day 1, the foraminal area was significantly greater in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P = 0.017). Surgical-site infection occurred in one patient in the UBE group and two patients in the UNSES group. Neurologic symptoms or signs were observed in four patients in the UBE group and three patients in the UNSES group. These manifestations gradually resolved during follow-up after symptomatic treatment. Recurrence was observed in one patient in the UBE group and two patients in the UNSES group. At the final follow-up, clinical outcomes assessed using the modified Macnab criteria did not differ significantly between the groups.

CONCLUSION: Both UNSES and UBE resulted in significant pain relief and functional improvement in patients with foraminal-region FLLDH. Compared with UBE, UNSES was associated with shorter operative time and greater foraminal enlargement. However, long-term clinical outcomes were comparable between the two techniques.

articles.title: Psychological distress associated with glaucoma: potential predictors and contributing factors.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Glaucoma is a chronic, progressive optic neuropathy and one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. Beyond visual impairment, the disease can impose a considerable psychological burden. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between glaucoma and psychological distress, and to identify clinical and psychosocial predictors that may contribute to heightened risk, with the aim of informing management strategies to improve patients' quality of life.

METHODS: A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted involving 107 glaucoma patients treated at the University Eye Clinic Cologne. Data were collected using a standardized questionnaire, including demographic and clinical variables as well as the validated Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multiple linear regression to identify predictors of psychological burden.

RESULTS: 25.23% of patients exhibited mild to severe depressive symptoms according to PHQ-9 scores. Significant predictors of higher psychological burden were increased disease preoccupation (β = 0.237, p = 0.007), stronger fear of blindness (β = 0.315, p < 0.001), and poorer self-rated general health status (β = -0.382, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate a strong link between glaucoma and psychological distress. These results highlight the need to consider psychosocial factors alongside intraocular pressure in glaucoma management. Interdisciplinary care involving ophthalmologists, psychologists, and nursing staff may improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Rise of Lower Respiratory Tract Infections Other than Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Emergency Room: Results from the Season (2024/25) of the RISE Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) are a major cause of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations. Although respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and rhinovirus (RV) are common etiological agents, pathogen-specific data from pediatric emergency settings remain limited.

METHODS: This prospective surveillance study quantified ARI-related ED visits, described pathogen-specific epidemiology, and assessed attendance and hospitalization rates as well as the distribution of lower versus upper respiratory tract infections (LRTI/URTI) in children younger than 60 months in two pediatric EDs in Berlin between November 1, 2024 and May 31, 2025. Respiratory pathogens were identified using nasopharyngeal swab samples tested by multiplex real-time RT-PCR (QIAstat-Dx® Respiratory Panel Plus).

RESULTS: Within the study period 4042 ARI-related ED visits occurred. A total of 310 children were enrolled in our study (median age 18 months); 115 (37.1%) had LRTI and 195 (62.9%) URTI. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 271 children (87.4%). The attendance rate for RSV was 24.4% (66 cases), for FLU 25.8% (70 cases), and for RV 29.5% (80 cases). Overall, 93 children (30.0%) were hospitalized, including 65 with LRTI and 28 with URTI. Hospitalization rates were highest for RSV infections (26/65, 40.0%) and RV infections (28/65, 43.1%), and lower for FLU infections (13/69, 18.8%). Hospitalization due to LRTI predominated among children with RSV (24/26, 92.3%) and RV infections (20/28, 71.4%), whereas FLU infections were less frequently observed (7/13, 53.9%). Furthermore, younger age, a history of pneumonia, a history of bronchiolitis, and the absence of breastfeeding were associated with hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to the previous season, in which RSV was associated with the highest attendance and hospitalization rate, we observed a high burden of RV infections in the 2024/2025 season. These findings may impact surveillance strategies, clinical management, and future public health strategies.

articles.title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone exacerbates mitochondrial energy dysregulation and cardiac remodeling with involvement of the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) is linked to the progression of heart failure (HF); however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the regulation of HF and myocardial energy metabolism.

METHODS: In vitro, cardiomyocytes were treated with TSH to assess pathological stress markers and mitochondrial energy metabolism. In vivo, a SCH model was established in thyrocyte-specific TSHR knockout mice, with concurrent isoproterenol (ISO)-induced HF. Serum FT4 and TSH levels, cardiac function, and myocardial energy metabolism (ATP levels, mitochondrial ultrastructure, key metabolic enzymes) were evaluated. Cardiomyocyte-specific TSHR knockout mice were used to confirm findings, and the involvement of the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway was investigated in vitro.

RESULTS: In vitro, TSH treatment increased the expression of pathological stress markers in cardiomyocytes. It also induced alterations in energy substrates, decreased ATP levels, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. In vivo, compared to the ISO group, mice in the SCH + ISO group exhibited more severe cardiac structural damage and functional impairment, accompanied by aggravated energy metabolism remodeling and mitochondrial dysfunction-characterized by lower ATP content, exacerbated mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, increased glycolysis, and decreased aerobic glucose oxidation. Notably, cardiomyocyte-specific TSHR knockout mitigated cardiac damage and metabolic remodeling in HF mice induced by ISO. Further mechanistic studies suggest that the AMPK/PGC-1α signaling pathway is involved in the regulation of TSH-mediated mitochondrial energy metabolism and cardiac remodeling.

CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that SCH exacerbates HF progression and further implicate TSH/TSHR signaling in the regulation of myocardial energy metabolism.

articles.title: Combined multimodal monitoring during neonatal transition in preterm infants: feasibility, safety and post-implementation evaluation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The transitional period involves major cardiovascular adaptations that could affect cerebral perfusion. Combined multimodal monitoring (CMM) may provide a more comprehensive physiological assessment than individual monitoring modalities. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of CMM integrating near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), targeted neonatal echocardiography (TNE), and head ultrasound (HUS) during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions following its implementation. Prospective observational cohort study. Participants underwent continuous NIRS and aEEG monitoring, two TNE assessment and one HUS during the first 72 h of life. Feasibility was defined as acquisition of ≥ 75% of intended NIRS and aEEG recording time, and completion of all imaging studies. Safety outcomes included TNE-related procedural intolerance and NIRS-related skin reactions. Healthcare professionals completed a post-implementation survey assessing acceptability and perceived clinical usefulness. Forty-seven infants were included. Overall CMM feasibility was 78.7%. Individual monitoring completion was 93.6% for NIRS, 95.7% for aEEG, 89.3% for TNE and 100% for HUS. Transient desaturations occurred in 7.9% of 89 TNE assessments, while mild NIRS-related erythema occurred in 11.3% of monitored infants. Healthcare professionals reported favorable perceptions of CMM, particularly regarding clinical relevance and complementarity with standard monitoring.

CONCLUSION: CMM was feasible and well tolerated during the first 72 h of life in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and was perceived favorably by healthcare professionals. Future studies are needed to explore its impact on clinically relevant outcomes.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • The transitional period in preterm infants involves complex cardiovascular and cerebral adaptations associated with an increased risk of brain injury. • Individual monitoring modalities (NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS) provide complementary information on cardiovascular and cerebral physiology but are commonly assessed separately.

WHAT IS NEW: • Structured CMM integrating NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS is feasible and well tolerated during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation. • Healthcare professionals perceive CMM as clinically relevant and complementary to standard monitoring, supporting further evaluation of integrated multimodal assessment in neonatal care.

articles.title: TRIM27 enhances NF-κB/MAPK activation by ubiquitinating and degrading TRAF3 to drive asthma-induced airway inflammation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease, and airway epithelial cell injury is closely associated with disease progression. TRIM27, as an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plays a significant role in immune-inflammatory responses. This study aims to investigate the role of TRIM27 in airway epithelial cell injury and inflammation.

METHODS: House dust mite extract (HDM)-induced mouse or 16HBE cell models were constructed to simulate asthma in vivo and in vitro. Lung histopathological injury was assessed via HE and PAS staining. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) inflammatory cell counts and ELISA were used to measure inflammation levels. Cell viability and apoptosis was detected by CCK-8, flow cytometry and TUNEL staining. RT-qPCR and Western blot were employed to detect related gene and protein expression.

RESULTS: TRIM27 was upregulated in both in vivo and in vitro asthma models. TRIM27 knockdown alleviated HDM-induced lung histopathological damage in mice, reduced goblet cell hyperplasia and inflammatory cell infiltration, and decreased inflammatory cytokine levels. In vitro experiments showed that TRIM27 knockdown partially restored HDM-induced decline in cell viability, inhibited apoptosis, ROS generation, and inflammatory cytokine release. Mechanistic studies revealed that HDM stimulation activated the NF-κB/MAPK pathway, while TRIM27 knockdown suppressed its activation. Further research demonstrated that TRIM27 activates the NF-κB/MAPK pathway by promoting TRAF3 ubiquitination and degradation. TRAF3 knockdown can weaken the beneficial effects of TRIM27 knockdown.

CONCLUSION: TRIM27 activates the NF-κB/MAPK signaling pathway by promoting TRAF3 ubiquitination and degradation, thereby exacerbating airway epithelial cell injury and inflammatory response, and promoting asthma progression.

articles.title: Oral versus intranasal probiotics for nasal microbiome modulation: a comparative review of route-dependent mechanisms and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Probiotic modulation of the nasal microbiome can be achieved through oral administration, which relies on the gut-nose axis and systemic immunomodulation, or direct intranasal instillation, which provides immediate local action. Despite growing evidence, no systematic comparison of these routes has been published. This narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence comparing oral versus intranasal probiotic strategies to inform route selection based on disease pathophysiology and strain-specific efficacy. We evaluated randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic studies investigating probiotic interventions delivered via either route for upper respiratory conditions including allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis, and pediatric respiratory infections. Orally administered probiotics may exert nasal effects through two mechanisms: (i) systemic immunomodulation via gut-derived short-chain fatty acids and tryptophan metabolites, supported by clinical data for Weizmannia coagulans BC99 and by a randomized controlled trial in children with perennial allergic rhinitis for Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis CCFM111; and (ii) direct oropharyngeal-to-nasopharyngeal trafficking, exemplified by a slow-release chewable Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG formulation that trafficked to the nasopharynx in 41% of users after 8 weeks, with a decrease in nasal IL-13 observed in both probiotic and placebo groups, and improved symptom control in the probiotic group. The B. longum and Lactobacillus plantarum combination NVP-1703 reduced type-2 cytokine ratios in children. Intranasal probiotics, including Bacillus spore sprays and Streptococcus salivarius 24SMB/S. oralis 89a, have shown pathogen displacement and clinical benefit in individual trials involving pediatric acute rhinosinusitis and otitis media, adenoid hypertrophy, and granulomatosis with polyangiitis-associated chronic rhinosinusitis, although within-group improvements in the latter were not consistently confirmed in between-group comparisons. However, a multi-strain Lactobacillus nasal spray failed in a crossover trial in seasonal allergic rhinitis, and a lactic acid bacterial spray of honeybee origin showed no benefit in chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps, underscoring the importance of strain-disease matching. Route selection may tentatively be guided by disease pathophysiology: systemic type-2-driven conditions may favor oral immunomodulation, while acute localized dysbiosis may favor intranasal delivery. Priority research includes direct comparative trials, microbiome-based stratification, and sustained-release formulations. Until then, clinical decision-making must rely on mechanistic plausibility and strain-specific data.

articles.title: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia in Italian children: a road map through a single center's experience.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, biochemical, and molecular characteristics of pediatric patients with suspected familial hypercholesterolemia (FH, OMIM #143890) and to investigate whether the presence of pathogenic low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) variants is associated with differences in lipid profile severity and treatment initiation compared with inconclusive genetic findings. We report the clinical, biochemical and molecular data of 382 patients diagnosed in a single pediatric center. Patients carrying pathogenic low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) variants exhibited significantly more severe dyslipidemia compared with those with inconclusive genetic findings, particularly in terms of elevated LDL-C, the hallmark of FH. No significant differences were observed in age, weight, height, or body mass index, confirming that lipid abnormalities are primarily attributable to genetic factors. Treatment uptake was higher in the pathogenic group, with 87% initiating statin-based therapy compared with 50% in the inconclusive group, suggesting that a confirmed genetic diagnosis may improve treatment adherence.

CONCLUSION: Pathogenic variants in the LDLR gene are associated with a more severe lipid profile and a higher likelihood of initiating lipid-lowering therapy. These findings support the clinical value of genetic testing in familial hypercholesterolemia, both for improving diagnostic accuracy and for promoting earlier therapeutic intervention and adherence.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Familial hypercholesterolemia is a common, treatable genetic disorder, and early diagnosis with lipid-lowering therapy from childhood reduces lifelong cardiovascular risk. • Most cases of heterozygous FH are caused by pathogenic LDLR variants, but data on treatment uptake in children are limited.

WHAT IS NEW: • In 382 Italian children, those with pathogenic LDLR variants had higher LDL-C than those with inconclusive genetic results. Their lipid profiles also differed depending on the exon and protein domain affected. • Treatment was started in 87% of children with a confirmed genetic diagnosis and in 50% of those with inconclusive results. This suggests that genetic confirmation may help families accept treatment.

articles.title: Latent class analysis of CT-based phenotypes in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and pulmonary involvement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary manifestations of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) are highly heterogeneous, and a standardized CT-based classification is currently lacking. This study aimed to evaluate whether latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings can identify phenotypes with clinical and prognostic relevance in patients with EGPA.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 140 patients with EGPA and pulmonary involvement between 2014 and 2025. Chest CT findings were independently evaluated by two thoracic radiologists and analyzed using LCA to identify CT-based phenotypes. Reproducibility and clinical applicability were assessed by having radiologists reassign patients to phenotypes based on LCA-derived CT patterns while blinded to the original LCA assignments. Baseline characteristics and one-year clinical and radiological outcomes were compared across phenotypes. Modified Poisson regression was used to assess clinical relapse risk.

RESULTS: LCA identified four distinct phenotypes: bronchial (32.1%; airway-predominant abnormalities), infiltrative (20.7%; parenchyma-predominant abnormalities), mixed (14.3%; combined bronchial and infiltrative features), and nonspecific (32.9%; without a dominant bronchial or infiltrative pattern). The bronchial and infiltrative phenotypes showed more favorable short-term outcomes, whereas the nonspecific phenotype mainly showed stable outcomes. The mixed phenotype remained associated with a higher risk of one-year clinical relapse after adjustment for age, sex, and baseline treatment. Radiologist reassignment showed excellent inter- and intra-observer agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.85 and 0.87).

CONCLUSION: LCA enables the identification of CT-based phenotypes with distinct clinical characteristics and short-term outcome patterns in EGPA, suggesting potential prognostic value and a practical role in clinical management.

KEY POINTS: QuestionCan latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings identify imaging phenotypes of pulmonary involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)? FindingsLCA identified four CT-based phenotypes (bronchial, infiltrative, mixed, and nonspecific), each characterized by distinct clinical and radiological features and short-term outcome patterns. Clinical relevanceCT-based phenotyping may help characterize pulmonary disease heterogeneity in EGPA and identify patients, particularly those with the mixed phenotype, who may require closer monitoring for clinical relapse.

articles.title: Performance of AI-based models in prenatal detection of trisomy 21 via ultrasonography: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the performance, strengths, and limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) models for trisomy 21 classification and risk prediction, and for enabling ultrasound tasks, using fetal ultrasound.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through October 2026, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. Original, peer-reviewed studies that developed or validated AI models for trisomy 21 classification or risk prediction, or for enabling ultrasound tasks (nuchal translucency and facial marker measurement, segmentation, and plane recognition), using human fetal ultrasound images or ultrasound-derived measurements and reporting quantitative performance metrics were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias with PROBAST (prediction-model studies) and QUADAS-2 (enabling-task studies), resolving disagreements by consensus. Studies were categorized by primary task and synthesized narratively, without meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included: eight image-based classifiers, seven marker-based risk models, and four enabling-task studies. Image-based classifiers reported accuracies of 84-98.3% and AUCs of 0.95-0.985. Marker-based models reported AUCs of 0.84-0.983; detection rates of 90-100% at false-positive rates of about 3.6-3.9% came from one research group, whereas the largest cohort reported a sensitivity of 84% at a false-positive rate of 2.28%. Enabling-task studies were evaluated with task-specific metrics and were not compared with classification performance. Ten of fifteen prediction-model studies were at high risk of bias, mainly in the analysis domain; seven reported only image counts, and leakage between training and test data was likely in six. Most studies were retrospective with limited external validation.

CONCLUSION: Reported performance of AI models for trisomy 21 is high but comes mostly from retrospective, internally validated studies, and benefits for screening performance, invasive testing, or operator dependence have not been demonstrated. No study compared AI with cell-free DNA screening, so the role of these tools within current screening pathways remains undefined. Prospective, multicenter validation with karyotype-confirmed outcomes and standardized reporting is needed before clinical integration can be supported.

articles.title: Bacterial and fungal pathogens in adult dacryocystitis: a retrospective study from a tertiary medical center in southern Taiwan.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the microbiological spectrum of dacryocystitis in southern Taiwan, with emphasis on polymicrobial and fungal infections, and to inform treatment based on regional susceptibility patterns.

METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with culture-proven dacryocystitis who underwent lacrimal surgery at a tertiary medical center in southern Taiwan from 2014 to 2024. Routine fungal culture was implemented after July 2018. Only intraoperative specimens obtained under sterile conditions were analyzed to minimize contamination.

RESULTS: Among 216 dacryocystitis cases (102 acute and 114 chronic), 179 (82.9%) were culture-positive. Staphylococcus aureus and Cutibacterium acnes were commonly identified in acute cases, whereas Pseudomonas aeruginosa and S. epidermidis were more frequent in chronic cases. After routine fungal culture was implemented, fungi were detected in 19 of 154 cases (12.3%), predominantly in chronic cases. Oxacillin resistance was observed in 13 of 36 S. aureus isolates (36.1%), while most Gram-negative isolates remained susceptible to gentamicin, amikacin, and piperacillin-tazobactam.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate a diverse microbial spectrum in adult dacryocystitis, including Gram-negative, polymicrobial, and fungal involvement, particularly in chronic disease. The observed antimicrobial resistance patterns suggest that Gram-positive-focused empirical therapy may not provide adequate coverage. Comprehensive microbiological evaluation, including fungal culture, together with consideration of local susceptibility patterns may improve treatment selection, particularly in chronic or refractory dacryocystitis.

articles.title: Radiation Dose Assessment in Routine Adult Computed Tomography Examinations: A Multi-center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT) plays an essential role in diagnosing and imaging various body structures, but it continues to be one of the most frequent sources of medical radiation exposure. Diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) represent critical values for radiation dose monitoring and dose optimization.

OBJECTIVE: The study aims to investigate levels of radiation dose in adult routine CT examinations in Saudi Arabia and establish local diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) for head, chest, and abdomen/pelvis CT studies.

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cross-sectional analysis involving 300 routine CT examinations was carried out on adults. The dataset includes 100 head CTs, 100 chest CTs, and 100 abdomen/pelvis CTs from two hospitals in Saudi Arabia during the period of April-July 2025. Dose descriptors (CTDIvol, DLP) were collected based on CT dose reports; E was calculated. Radiation dose distributions were summarized using descriptive statistics, and local DRLs were established using the 75th percentile of CTDIvol and DLP values. Dose levels were compared with published national and international reference values.

RESULTS: The local diagnostic reference levels (CTDIvol and DLP) were 52.07 mGy and 949.41 mGy cm for head CTs, 11.04 mGy and 576.12 mGy cm for chest CTs, and 14.73 mGy and 805.63 mGy cm for abdomen/pelvis CTs. Compared with the relevant reference levels, the CTDIvol was 13.2% lower than the EC reference level for head CT, 8.0% lower than the SFDA national DRL for chest CT, and 5.2% higher than the SFDA national DRL for abdomen/pelvis CT.

CONCLUSION: The established DRLs for the routine adult CT exams are consistent with the current standards set for radiation dose monitoring and optimization. The continuous surveillance of radiation exposure and the optimization of image acquisition protocols should be done in order to improve patient radiation protection without image quality being compromised.

articles.title: Summary cerebral small-vessel disease score mediates white-matter microstructural and perfusion changes in mild cognitive impairment: a diffusion kurtosis imaging and arterial spin labeling study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The summary cerebral small-vessel disease (CSVD) score reflects brain-damage severity, but its relationship with white-matter (WM) integrity and cerebral perfusion remains unclear. Here, we aimed to explore how this score links WM microstructure and cerebral blood flow (CBF).

METHODS: We included 31 patients with CSVD and mild cognitive impairment (CSVD-MCI) and 31 matched healthy controls. Diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) and three-dimensional arterial spin labeling were used with tract-based spatial statistics to assess group differences in axial kurtosis, mean kurtosis (MK), radial kurtosis (RK) and CBF. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses and mediation effects analyses were performed.

RESULTS: CSVD-MCI patients showed widespread WM damage and reduced CBF. In the bilateral superior corona radiata (SCR), the summary CSVD score was negatively correlated with MK, RK, and CBF, whereas MK and RK were positively correlated with CBF. Mediation analysis revealed that the summary CSVD score statistically accounted for indirect effects of CBF on MK and RK in the SCR.

CONCLUSION: In CSVD-MCI, reduced CBF, higher cumulative lesion burden, and WM microstructural damage were linked in a tract-specific pattern. The summary CSVD score statistically accounted for part of the association between CBF and DKI-derived WM metrics in the SCR, supporting its role as an imaging marker that integrates vascular and structural injury.

articles.title: Promising therapeutic interventions for preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity in sepsis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Endothelial Glycocalyx (eGCX) degradation is a major pathophysiological event in sepsis, contributing to endothelial dysfunction, vascular permeability, inflammation, microvascular thrombosis, and organ failure. Despite its importance, eGCX-targeted therapies are not currently incorporated into standard sepsis management. This systematic review summarized clinical and preclinical evidence on therapeutic and experimental strategies aimed at preserving or restoring eGCX integrity in sepsis. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched through August 2026. Eligible human and animal studies evaluated eGCX-directed interventions in sepsis or experimental sepsis models. Outcomes included circulating biomarkers such as syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan, microcirculatory measures including perfused boundary region, and structural assessment by microscopy. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, SYRCLE, and ROBINS-I. Twenty-one studies were included, comprising 17 animal and 4 human studies. Interventions included ascorbic acid, sulodexide, doxycycline, activated protein C, heparin-based therapies, antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin, therapeutic plasma exchange, colivelin, liposomal nanocarriers of preassembled eGCX, and rhamnan sulfate. Several interventions reduced eGCX shedding, improved endothelial barrier or microvascular function, and, in some experimental models, preserved or restored eGCX ultrastructure. Overall, the eGCX represents a promising therapeutic target in sepsis; however, most evidence remains preclinical, and well-designed clinical studies using standardized eGCX outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Controlled adherence with long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine: determinants and clinical impact of injection-schedule adherence in the Spanish RELATIVITY cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine (CAB+RPV LA) transforms adherence from daily self-administered oral therapy to scheduled healthcare system-supported injections. The real-world determinants and consequences of injection schedule adherence remain incompletely defined.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study within the RELATIVITY program, combining retrospective data collection for participants already receiving CAB+RPV LA with prospective follow-up of new initiations that included virologically suppressed adults who initiated CAB+RPV LA in routine care in Spain. Injection-schedule adherence was calculated using a proportion-of-days-covered framework adapted to long-acting injectable ART, based on the proportion of evaluable injections administered within a predefined ± 7-day target window, and categorized as complete (100% of evaluable injections within the target window), high (90-99.9%), or suboptimal (<90%; including early and/or late injections outside the target window). Univariable associations with noncomplete injection-schedule adherence were assessed, whereas adjusted determinants of late injection outcomes were evaluated using multivariable models. The time to the first late injection and the time to definitive discontinuation were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox regression. A separate multivariable logistic regression model evaluated the occurrence of two or more late injections. An exploratory cross-validated prediction model was developed to estimate the risk of noncomplete injection-schedule adherence.

RESULTS: Among 3349 participants, 3280 had evaluable injection-schedule data. Complete injection-schedule adherence was observed in 2309/3280 (70.4%), high adherence in 948/3280 (28.9%), and suboptimal adherence in 23/3280 (0.7%). At least one late injection occurred in 1254 participants (38.2%), whereas two or more late injections occurred in 436 (13.3%). Adherence remained high across age, sex, nationality, comorbidity burden, substance use, previous virological failure, oral lead-in, and baseline CD4+/CD8+ strata. In univariable analyses, baseline characteristics showed limited associations with noncomplete adherence. In adjusted models of late-injection outcomes, center volume, prior ART duration, foreign nationality, BMI, and comorbidity burden showed small-to-moderate associations. Virological failure remained infrequent across adherence categories. The exploratory prediction model showed limited discrimination (cross-validated AUC, 0.53), indicating that baseline variables alone were insufficient for clinically useful prediction.

CONCLUSION: In this large real-world cohort, CAB+RPV LA achieved very high injection-schedule adherence and rare suboptimal adherence. Baseline characteristics had limited ability to predict schedule deviations, supporting CAB+RPV LA as a controlled-adherence strategy, the success of which depends on reliable delivery systems as much as patient selection.

articles.title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.

articles.title: External validation of the renal angina index for early prediction of severe acute kidney injury in critically ill children: a prospective cohort study from Vietnam.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill children and is associated with poor outcomes. The Renal Angina Index (RAI) has been proposed as an early risk stratification tool, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study in the pediatric intensive care unit of Vietnam National Children's Hospital from October 2024 to June 2025. Children aged 1 month to under 18 years were included if RAI could be calculated within 24 h of admission. The primary outcome was severe AKI at 72 h, defined as KDIGO stage 2-3. Secondary outcomes included incident AKI, kidney replacement therapy, and PICU mortality. Predictive performance was evaluated using ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 314 children were included. Severe AKI developed in 56 (17.8%) patients. RAI showed good discrimination for severe AKI (AUC 0.790; 95% CI 0.741-0.834), with sensitivity of 78.6% and specificity of 70.5% at a cutoff of ≥8. For incident AKI, the AUC was 0.752 (95% CI 0.643-0.861). RAI outperformed serum creatinine and fluid overload in predicting severe AKI. RAI ≥ 8 remained independently associated with severe AKI (adjusted OR 7.40; 95% CI 2.51-21.78; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: RAI showed acceptable performance for early prediction of severe AKI in critically ill children and may serve as a practical bedside risk stratification tool in resource-limited PICU settings.

articles.title: From AKI to AKD: extending the window of kidney assessment after bloodstream infection in children.
When to stop kidney replacement therapy in critically ill children: current evidence and practical considerations from a pediatric critical care nephrology perspective.
articles.abstract: Kidney replacement therapy (KRT) is a life-saving intervention for critically ill children with severe acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the optimal timing of KRT liberation remains uncertain, and decisions regarding treatment discontinuation are among the least standardized aspects of AKI management. Whereas the timing of KRT initiation has been extensively investigated, evidence guiding KRT liberation in children remains scarce. Successful liberation requires balancing the risks of premature discontinuation against those of unnecessarily prolonged extracorporeal support. KRT liberation is best conceptualized as a process requiring both clinical readiness and sufficient renal recovery. Current pediatric evidence indicates that urine output is the clinical variable most consistently associated with successful liberation, whereas other factors, such as structural kidney biomarkers, are promising but have yet to be validated. Adult studies provide valuable physiological and conceptual insights but cannot be directly extrapolated to children because of important developmental and disease-specific differences. A structured approach based on predefined renal recovery criteria, interpreted within the individual patient's clinical context, may improve the consistency of liberation decisions while awaiting prospective pediatric studies capable of defining evidence-based liberation strategies.

articles.title: Health economic evaluation of polytrauma treatment in the current aG-DRG system - Results of a Level I Trauma Center.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resource-intensive polytrauma care is associated with high treatment and readiness costs and poses a financial challenge for hospitals. The aim of this retrospective single-center study of the years 2020 to 2022 was to analyze polytrauma reimbursements and costs.

METHODS: Based on billing and clinical data of 201 polytrauma cases from a German University Hospital and Level I Trauma Center, revenues and costs of the eleven MDC 21 A polytrauma DRGs were analyzed. Ratios of the revenue in relation to LOS, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs as well as personnel costs were calculated. Contribution margins were determined as an upper-bound estimate.

RESULTS: DRG reimbursement was highest for the most severely injured patients (50,852 €, DRG W36Z). It was lowest for patients who died within five days (2,214 €, DRG W60Z) or without surgeries (4,056 €, DRG W61B). The contribution margin was also highest for the most severely injured patients (52,775 €, DRG W36Z). Revenues in relation to ICU LOS (3,455 €/day, DRG W36Z) and ventilation time (238 €/hour, DRG W01B) were lowest for the most severe polytraumas. Regarding OR time and implant costs, reimbursement was lowest for injuries of the spine, pelvis and extremities with 62 €/min (DRG W02B) and 5 €/€ (DRG W02A).

CONCLUSION: Treatment of polytrauma patients with long ICU stay, extended mechanical ventilation and multiple injuries of the extremities, pelvis and spine is not adequately reflected by the current per-case reimbursement in relation to the resources used (ICU days, ventilation hours, OR time and implant costs).

articles.title: Beyond POCT05: A Consensus Guideline for Evaluating Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems in a Connected, Regulated Era.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology

articles.title: Supramolecular Barrel-Stave Anion Channel With Hydroxyl-Rich Selectivity Filter.
articles.abstract: In naturally occurring CLC channels, the hydroxyl groups of serine (Sercen) and tyrosine (Tyrcen) that orient toward the central region of the pore are important for Cl- selectivity. Herein, artificial anion channels with a hydroxyl-rich selectivity filter are reported based on the self-assembly of (R)-(-)-mandelic acid-based derivatives. It was envisaged that multiple monomers would self-assemble in a transmembrane orientation, stabilised by intermolecular hydrogen bonds between the hydroxyl and amide groups of the scaffold, thereby forming the half-channel. Further, the antiparallel, tail-to-tail assembly of two such units would form the channel. Among the derivatives tested, the octyl chain-containing compound 1c exhibited the highest transmembrane transport activity and chloride selectivity. This transport relies on channel-mediated antiport, featuring an average channel diameter of 3.9 ± 0.1 Å and a single-channel conductance of 16.0 ± 0.8 pS. The 1H NMR titration experiment confirmed the major involvement of hydroxyl protons (OH) in chloride binding. Geometry optimisation shows that 1c (17.553 Å) can span half the egg yolk phosphatidylcholine lipid bilayer. Further geometry optimisation confirmed that the pentameric assembly is best suited to form the hydroxyl-rich hydrogen-bonded selectivity filter and to recognise Cl- within the cavity.

articles.title: Arthrodesis of the Thumb Metacarpophalangeal Joint: Tension Band Wiring Versus Intramedullary Screw Fixation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Tension band wiring (TBW) and intramedullary (IM) screw fixation represent two well-established methods for thumb metacarpophalangeal (MP) joint arthrodesis. Studies comparing these methods have included small sample sizes and reported inconsistent findings. The objective of this study was to provide a descriptive comparison of the 1-year union, clinical success, and complication rates for both methods.

METHODS: This retrospective review examined all cases of TBW and IM screw thumb MP arthrodesis at a single institution between January 2012 and August 2024. Exclusion criteria included fusion of nonthumb MP joints, <90 days of follow-up, revision fusions, and incomplete medical records. Data collection occurred via chart review. The 1-year union, clinical success, and complication rates were reported for TBW and IM screw groups.

RESULTS: One hundred twenty-one patients were fused with TBW and 31 with IM screw. Of those with radiographs at final follow-up, union was observed in 80/89 (90%) TBW constructs and 20/27 (74%) IM screws. Clinical success was noted in 112/121 (93%) TBW cases and 24/31 (77%) IM screw cases. Re-arthrodesis was required in 3/121 (2%) TBW cases and 5/31 (16%) IM screw cases. Removal of hardware (ROH) was noted in 27/121 (22%) TBW cases and 2/31 (6%) IM screw cases. Overall complication rates were 48/121 (40%) with TBW and 10/31 (32%) with IM screws. Reoperation occurred in 29/121 (24%) TBW constructs and 8/31 (26%) IM screw fixations, with ROH representing 26/29 (90%) TBW reoperations and re-arthrodesis representing 5/8 (63%) IM screw reoperations.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective descriptive study without inferential statistics, union occurred in 90% and 74% of TBW and IM screw arthrodesis cases, respectively. Reoperation was required in 24% of TBW cases and 26% of IM screw fixations. ROH represented the majority of TBW reoperations, whereas re-arthrodesis represented the majority of IM screw reoperations.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic IV.

articles.title: An Unexpected Cause of STEMI in Partially Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon but clinically relevant nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Adult patients with congenital heart disease may be particularly vulnerable when residual intracardiac shunts, atrial enlargement, and atrial arrhythmias coexist.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with partially repaired tetralogy of Fallot, residual ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting, and new-onset atrial fibrillation presented with inferior STEMI. Coronary angiography revealed distal right coronary artery occlusion with a large thrombus burden, in the absence of significant atherosclerotic disease. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy was successfully performed, with clinical and electrocardiographic improvement.

DISCUSSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy for STEMI due to CE in an adult patient with congenital heart disease with residual intracardiac shunt.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In adult patients with congenital heart disease with STEMI, CE should be suspected when intracardiac shunts and embolic risk factors coexist.

articles.title: Intractable Pulmonary Edema After PCI: An Extremely Rare Iatrogenic Mechanical Cause.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent aortic valve injury following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a rare but catastrophic complication that can cause acute severe aortic regurgitation (AR) and heart failure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 49-year-old man developed recurrent acute pulmonary edema after a failed staged PCI for chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe eccentric AR caused by a 7-mm injury to the noncoronary cusp and left cusp confirming iatrogenic cusp laceration. He underwent successful surgical repair with pericardial patch reconstruction and coronary artery bypass grafting, with excellent recovery.

DISCUSSION: Literature on catheter-induced aortic valve injury is sparse. This case highlights a rare cause of post-PCI shock where prompt echocardiography guided lifesaving surgical intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Not all post-PCI cardiac decompensation is ischemic. Severe AR from iatrogenic aortic cusp injury, though rare, should be promptly excluded.

articles.title: Two-Port Endoscopic Left Atrial Myxoma Resection Under Ventricular Fibrillation Without Aortic Cross-Clamping.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a reproducible 2-port, 3-dimensional totally endoscopic technique for left atrial myxoma resection under ventricular fibrillation without aortic cross-clamping.

KEY STEPS: Peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass is established through femoral cannulation. After 2 right thoracic ports are positioned, ventricular fibrillation is induced, the left atrium is opened, and a left atrial vent is inserted. The tumor is removed en bloc with an adequate septal margin. Continuous carbon dioxide insufflation, titrated venting, a gently blood-filled left atrium, and transesophageal echocardiography-guided de-airing provide embolic protection.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Aortic regurgitation, interatrial shunting, inappropriate venting, tumor fragmentation, and prolonged fibrillatory arrest can compromise safety.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In carefully selected patients, a short fibrillatory interval can simplify 2-port myxoma resection by avoiding aortic clamping, root cannulation, and cardioplegia. Meticulous left-heart decompression and de-airing are essential.

articles.title: Pacing Rate Acceleration in Right-Sided Heart Failure: Insight From an On-Off-On Clinical Course.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment options remain limited for patients with right-sided heart failure (RHF) and severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Whether higher heart rate is beneficial in patients with RHF remains unclear.

CASE SUMMARY: A 74-year-old woman with RHF and severe TR experienced marked hemodynamic and symptomatic improvement after increasing her permanent pacing rate from 60 to 90 beats/min. At 3 months, rate reduction to 60 beats/min provoked symptom recurrence within 3 days; restoring the rate to 90 beats/min promptly relieved symptoms. At 6 months, left ventricular ejection fraction remained preserved and right ventricular size remained reduced, although TR remained severe.

DISCUSSION: This case suggests that increasing the pacing rate may optimize right-sided heart hemodynamics and improve symptoms in selected patients with RHF, although further validation is needed.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: An on-off-on response to pacing-rate adjustment-symptoms improving with higher rates and worsening at lower rates-supports a potential beneficial effect of heart rate elevation in selected patients with refractory RHF.

articles.title: Acute Mitral Regurgitation With Unilateral Pulmonary Edema: Preferential Pulmonary Venous Loading From an Eccentric Jet.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute severe mitral regurgitation (MR) can cause rapidly progressive asymmetric pulmonary edema that mimics pneumonia.

CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old man presented with fever, dyspnea, and a new pansystolic murmur. Within hours, he developed hypoxemic respiratory failure. Serial chest imaging captured rapid progression from subtle right hilar vascular prominence to extensive right-predominant airspace opacification. Echocardiography showed posterior leaflet chordal rupture with a flail P2 segment and a severe eccentric MR jet directed toward the right pulmonary venous inflow, with systolic flow reversal in a sampled right pulmonary vein. Mitral valve repair produced marked clinical and radiographic improvement.

DISCUSSION: Concordance among the MR jet trajectory, pulmonary venous abnormalities, and edema distribution supported preferential right pulmonary venous loading. Recognition of this pattern helped distinguish asymmetric cardiogenic pulmonary edema from pneumonia.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Rapidly evolving focal pulmonary opacification with a new systolic murmur should prompt urgent echocardiography.

articles.title: Femoral-to-Carotid Shunting During Carotid-Access TAVR in Moyamoya-Pattern Vasculopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid access is an alternative for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with prohibitive transfemoral anatomy, but it may cause cerebral hypoperfusion with impaired intracranial collateral circulation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, extensive comorbidities, and unsuitable transfemoral access underwent TAVR. Neuroimaging demonstrated moyamoya-pattern intracranial vasculopathy with limited collateral reserve. During left carotid exposure, test occlusion caused a >50% decline in cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy despite blood pressure augmentation. A femoral-to-carotid arterial shunt was established to maintain cerebral perfusion. A 26-mm self-expanding Evolut FX+ valve was successfully implanted via left carotid access, with excellent hemodynamics and no neurologic complications.

DISCUSSION: This approach demonstrates a novel cerebral protection strategy for selected patients with compromised cerebrovascular reserve.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Carotid-access TAVR in moyamoya-pattern vasculopathy carries hypoperfusion risk. Real-time near-infrared spectroscopy may detect intolerance to carotid clamping, while femoral-to-carotid shunting may offer cerebral protection.

articles.title: Congenital Long QT Syndrome Type 2: Delayed Diagnosis After a Decade of Seizure-Like Episodes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) is typically diagnosed in youth. Recognition in advanced age is rare and may be delayed when arrhythmic syncope mimics epilepsy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 93-year-old man with recurrent convulsive syncope presented with marked QT prolongation, notched T waves, and pause-dependent torsades de pointes/pulseless ventricular tachycardia initiated by premature ventricular contractions. Four years earlier, torsades de pointes had been attributed to mild hypokalemia and famotidine, although QTc interval remained prolonged after correction. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic KCNH2 frameshift variant, confirming congenital LQTS type 2. Advanced age, chronic kidney disease, and bradyarrhythmia likely reduced repolarization reserve. An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was discussed but not pursued after a goals-of-care discussion; leadless pacing was used to reduce pauses, and beta-blocker therapy continued.

DISCUSSION: Congenital LQTS may remain occult into advanced age when acquired factors reduce repolarization reserve.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Persistent QT prolongation after reversible factors are corrected should prompt consideration of congenital LQTS regardless of age.

articles.title: High-Grade Atrioventricular Block and Recurrent Cardiac Arrest in Suspected Isolated Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis may cause advanced atrioventricular block, ventricular dysfunction, and sudden cardiac death. Isolated cardiac presentations are diagnostically challenging when histologic confirmation and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography are unavailable.

CASE SUMMARY: An 18-year-old woman with recurrent syncope developed high-grade atrioventricular block and recurrent brady-asystolic cardiac arrest requiring temporary transvenous pacing. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated regional septal thickening, basal to midseptal midmyocardial late gadolinium enhancement and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 38.9%. No extracardiac sarcoid pattern or biopsy target was identified. Giant cell myocarditis and inherited cardiomyopathy remained important alternative diagnoses. She received corticosteroid therapy and subsequently underwent cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac sarcoidosis should remain a diagnostic consideration in young patients with malignant conduction disease and inflammatory cardiomyopathy, while important mimics must be actively considered.

articles.title: Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.

OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.

RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).

CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

articles.title: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Gene Variants in Southeastern Türkiye with Identification of Rare Malton Genotypes in a Multicenter Real-world Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Alpha-1 antitrypsin (A1AT) deficiency is a hereditary disorder associated with an increased risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and remains underdiagnosed worldwide. Data from Southeastern Türkiye are limited, particularly in geographically and demographically underrepresented regions of the country. This study aimed to investigate the frequency and spectrum of A1AT gene variants in a real-world multicenter cohort from Southeastern Türkiye.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 1,008 patients who underwent targeted genetic testing for A1AT deficiency between 2022 and 2026 at two tertiary centers. Demographic characteristics, smoking status, pulmonary function parameters, and clinical diagnoses were evaluated. A1AT genotypes were classified as normal or variant, the latter including both common and rare alleles.

RESULTS: A1AT variants were identified in 6 patients (0.6%), including the MZ, Lowell, and Malton alleles; one patient carried the rare homozygous Malton/Malton genotype. All variant carriers had COPD. Half of the variant-positive patients were never-smokers, and several demonstrated severe airflow limitation corresponding to Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease stages 3-4 disease. The overall prevalence of A1AT variants was low and consistent with frequencies previously reported in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern populations. However, the detection of rare alleles highlighted the genetic heterogeneity of A1AT deficiency and suggested that sole reliance on common allele screening may contribute to underrecognition.

CONCLUSION: Although the prevalence of A1AT variants was low, their detection among high-risk individuals, including never-smokers and patients with severe COPD, underscores the clinical importance of targeted genetic testing. The identification of rare genotypes such as Malton/Malton supports the need for comprehensive genetic evaluation strategies. This study provides important regional data from Southeastern Türkiye and emphasizes the need for larger multicenter studies to better define the epidemiology and clinical impact of A1AT variants.

articles.title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity.
articles.abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil's metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

articles.title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4+ responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4+ response was strongly T helper 1 (TH1)-polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-α and minimal TH2 cytokines. Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F-specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

articles.title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved sasF gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when S. aureus colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for S. aureus resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of sasF are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper S. aureus surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity.
articles.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How E. faecalis evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how E. faecalis biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that E. faecalis biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of E. faecalis, which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis. We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid-independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

articles.title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface.
articles.abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning-based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

articles.title: Current and emerging sublingual immunotherapies for dust mite allergy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: House dust mites (HDMs) are the most prevalent inhalant allergens globally, inducing a spectrum of allergic diseases including allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma, which substantially impair patients' quality of life. Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) is recognized as a promising disease-modifying intervention for HDM-related allergic disorders.

AREAS COVERED: This paper presents a narrative review of up-to-date clinical evidence regarding SLIT for HDM allergy (HDM-SLIT), covering its therapeutic efficacy, patient selection criteria, dose optimization strategies, safety profiles, underlying immunological mechanisms, and unresolved clinical challenges.

EXPERT OPINION: HDM-SLIT has been established as a disease-modifying therapy for HDM-induced AR and asthma, with supporting evidence demonstrating its clinical efficacy, favorable safety profile, and long-lasting tolerability. Future developments in precision allergology, including multiomics-derived biomarkers and digital health applications, show considerable potential to guide clinical decision-making. However, the translation of these advances into routine clinical practice remains limited by gaps in insurance reimbursement, suboptimal patient adherence, inconsistent regulatory standards across regions, insufficient product standardization, and inequitable access to healthcare resources.

articles.title: Composite sleep patterns and the allergy-related composite outcome among American and Chinese older adults: exploration of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms commonly co-occur in older adults, but their associations with heterogeneous allergy-related outcomes and the role of depressive symptoms remain unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,562 participants aged ≥60 years from NHANES 2005-2006. A composite sleep pattern combined sleep duration, trouble sleeping, and diagnosed sleep disorders. The allergy-related composite outcome comprised elevated total immunoglobulin E and seven questionnaire-assessed disease or symptom outcomes. Survey-weighted logistic regression evaluated associations. Depressive symptoms were assessed with a modified 8-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8), and statistical mediation examined indirect associations through its continuous score. We also conducted a complementary longitudinal analysis in 6,146 Chinese older adults from CHARLS.

RESULTS: Poor versus healthy sleep was associated with higher odds of the allergy-related composite outcome (OR 2.100; 95% CI 1.328-3.322), wheeze (OR 2.148; 95% CI 1.296-3.559), and sneeze (OR 1.636; 95% CI 1.135-2.357). The estimated indirect association through depressive symptoms represented 22.5% of the total association. In CHARLS, impaired sleep quality was associated with incident asthma (OR 1.689; 95% CI 1.254-2.275), and the corresponding indirect association through depressive symptoms represented 28.3% of the total association.

CONCLUSION: Poor sleep was associated with heterogeneous allergy-related outcomes among US older adults, while CHARLS provided complementary longitudinal evidence for incident asthma. Depressive symptoms statistically accounted for part of the observed sleep-allergy association.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Coronary Embolism: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon cause of acute myocardial infarction, and the optimal postdischarge antithrombotic strategy remains uncertain.Retrospective multicenter study including patients with definite or probable CE. Three groups of patients were identified: (1) requiring specific management, (2) with atrial fibrillation (AF), and (3) with no indication for oral anticoagulation (OAC). The latter two groups were further classified according to the antithrombotic treatment received, and long-term outcomes (composite of recurrent CE, stroke, systemic embolism, cardiovascular or all-cause death, and major bleeding at 5 years) were subsequently evaluated.A total of 489 patients were considered. Among 189 patients with AF, 85 received direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and 104 vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). VKA users showed a higher rate of the composite endpoint compared with DOACs (40 vs. 18%, p < 0.001), with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. In multivariable analysis, VKA therapy remained independently associated with worse outcomes (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.9, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.02-3.5; p = 0.04). In the 182 patients without an indication for anticoagulation, 115 received antiplatelet therapy and 67 received OAC. Those treated with OAC had a higher incidence of the composite outcome (16 vs. 7%, p = 0.049), with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. Multivariable analysis confirmed OAC as an independent predictor of adverse prognosis (HR: 3.4; 95% CI: 1.2-9.7; p = 0.02).In patients with CE, stratification based on underlying etiology and embolic risk before hospital discharge might serve as a decision-making approach for determining optimal antithrombotic strategies and improved clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Phenotyping Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction in Japan　- Position Paper on Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is rapidly increasing in Japan in parallel with population aging, rising from just over half of all heart failure cases in 2015 to approximately 54% in 2025 and projected to reach nearly 57% by 2040-2050. HFpEF is a multifactorial syndrome shaped by diverse clinical and pathophysiological drivers.
