Principal Findings: Under assumptions of heterogeneous treatment effectiveness by race, guidelines without race adjustment decreased life expectancy among non-Hispanic Black adults by 0.4 years, increasing the life expectancy gap with non-Hispanic white adults from 4.1 to 4.5 years. Hypertension control among non-Hispanic Black adults also worsened. Years with uncontrolled hypertension increased by 0.8 years, widening the disparity with non-Hispanic white adults from 1.7 to 2.5 years. Assuming no racial heterogeneity, these effects were diminished: life expectancy decreased by 0.1 years and years with uncontrolled hypertension increased by 0.2 years, less than one-half and one-quarter of the effects observed under assumptions of heterogeneous treatment effectiveness by race. Conclusions: The potential effects of removing race-adjusted antihypertensive treatment guidelines depended on assumptions of racial heterogeneity in treatment effectiveness. Our findings highlight the importance of understanding drivers of previously observed racial differences when considering modifying antihypertensive treatment guidelines.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Pruritus, Fatigue, and Sleep Disorders in MASLD Negatively Affects Health-related Quality of Life and Work Productivity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with health-related quality of life (HRQL) impairment, which can be exacerbated by pruritus, fatigue, and/or sleep disorders. We assessed the prevalence of significant pruritus, fatigue, and sleep disorders in patients with MASLD and evaluated their association with HRQL and work productivity loss.

METHODS: Patients with MASLD were prospectively enrolled into the Global NAFLD/MASLD Registry. Clinical and HRQL (per CLDQ-MASH and WPAI:SHP questionnaires) data were analyzed according to the presence of significant pruritus, significant fatigue, and sleep disorders.

RESULTS: A total of 8034 patients with MASLD from 39 countries (age 54±12 years, 46% male, 50% type 2 diabetes, 39% advanced fibrosis) were included. At baseline, 25% reported significant pruritus, 35% significant fatigue, and 34% sleep disorders, and 10% had all 3 symptoms. Patients with fatigue, pruritus, or sleep disorder were more likely to be female, have higher BMI, more metabolic comorbidities, and greater psychiatric burden. At 1-year follow-up, over half of the patients with baseline symptoms continued to experience them, and 14% to 18% developed de novo symptoms. Multivariate analyses showed that significant pruritus and sleep disorders each independently predicted fatigue [OR=9.51 (8.0-11.3)] when both conditions were present. Pruritus was a strong predictor of sleep disorders [OR=2.90 (2.6-3.3)]. All 3 conditions, especially fatigue, were independently associated with significantly impaired HRQL and work productivity loss.

CONCLUSION: Clinically significant fatigue, pruritus, and sleep disorders are common in MASLD, having a negative impact on HRQL and a substantial economic burden.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of Machine-Learning Models for Individualized Prediction of Hearing Recovery in Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss.
articles.journal: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate a pragmatic machine-learning model for predicting hearing recovery in sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) using routinely available baseline clinical variables and standard audiometry.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective prognostic study.

SETTING: Tertiary teaching hospital in China.

PATIENTS: Adults with idiopathic SSNHL evaluated between January 1, 2017, and August 31, 2025, who had pretreatment and follow-up audiometry. The final cohort included 1097 patients contributing 1205 affected ears.

INTERVENTIONS: Routine clinical management, including systemic and/or intratympanic corticosteroid therapy according to contemporary clinical practice and physician judgment.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Hearing recovery on follow-up audiogram classified by the 2015 Chinese guideline and Siegel criteria and dichotomized at clinically relevant thresholds. Primary model selection was based on overall performance across the 3 Chinese guideline-defined binary outcomes.

RESULTS: Six algorithms were compared using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation, within-fold imputation, calibration assessment, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation. Tree-based models outperformed logistic models overall. In the primary models excluding treatment variables, LightGBM showed consistent performance across Chinese guideline-defined outcomes. ROC AUCs were 0.873 for full recovery, 0.797 for important recovery and better, and 0.753 for minor recovery and better, with corresponding accuracies of 89.07%, 78.99%, and 69.87%. Under Siegel criteria, LightGBM achieved ROC AUCs of 0.889 for complete recovery, 0.807 for partial recovery and better, and 0.782 for slight improvement and better. Performance was similar in sensitivity models incorporating treatment variables. The most influential predictors were age, baseline hearing thresholds, audiogram configuration, and vertigo.

CONCLUSIONS: A LightGBM model based on easily collected baseline clinical and audiometric variables showed useful internal performance for predicting hearing recovery in SSNHL and may support early, individualized prognostic assessment, pending external and prospective validation.

articles.title: Complete, But Not All at Once: Older Adults and Timing of Nonculprit Revascularization in STEMI.
Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR.

METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy.

RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016).

CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

articles.title: From chatbot to clinical copilot: the role of generative artificial intelligence in nuclear medicine reporting and data extraction.
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming clinical documentation workflow. This scoping review evaluates the emerging role of LLMs in nuclear medicine and molecular imaging, as recent literature suggests increasing evaluation of newer LLM architectures alongside GPT-4. We conducted a scoping review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Lens, and Google Scholar was performed from January 2023 to January 2026. Studies were included if they applied LLMs to nuclear medicine tasks (PET/computed tomography, single-photon emission computed tomography, and scintigraphy). General radiology studies were only included if separate nuclear medicine data were extractable. A total of 14 studies were included. While the GPT-4 family remains the most studied, recent literature includes increasing evaluation of non-GPT models, with several studies reporting comparable performance in specific tasks. In data extraction tasks, such as tumor-node-metastasis staging for breast cancer, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and DeepSeek have demonstrated performance comparable or superior to GPT-4o. The applications are primarily categorized into generative reporting (drafting impressions) and data extraction (structuring unstructured text). However, limitations persist: LLMs struggle with dynamic curve analysis (e.g. renal scintigraphy) and visual interpretation. Safety remains a concern, with one study reporting an 8% rate of potentially harmful responses in patient education scenarios. LLMs are evolving from experimental chatbots into capable 'Clinical copilots' that can significantly reduce administrative burden through automated reporting and data structuring. However, because of risks of hallucinations and domain-specific limitations in dynamic imaging, human oversight remains non-negotiable. Future research must focus on multimodal integration and multicenter prospective validation.

articles.title: Nicotine dependence and physical function: a comparison between current smokers with and without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who seek cognitive-behavioral therapy.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Smoking is a chronic disease characterized by nicotine dependence that affects the physical and mental health of millions of people worldwide. This study compared the degree of nicotine dependence, general fatigue, lung function, functional exercise capacity (FEC), and quality of life (QoL) in smokers with and without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who were seeking cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). This cross-sectional study involved 53 smokers (27 in the COPD group and 26 in the noCOPD group). Participants underwent a FEC assessment using the Glittre-ADL test (TGlittre), as well as pulmonary function analysis via spirometry and impulse oscillometry (IOS) to detect small airway disease (SAD). Participants also completed the following assessments: the Fagerström test for nicotine dependence (FTND), the Richmond test for motivation to quit smoking, the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F) scale, and the Short Form 36 (SF-36). When the two groups were compared, the noCOPD group had a slightly higher median FTND and Richmond test scores, though the differences were not statistically significant (p=0.537 and p=0.449, respectively). The COPD group showed lower values for all evaluated parameters (p≤0.008), but no difference was detected between the groups regarding IOS. SAD was present in 74% of COPD group participants and 73% of noCOPD group participants, with no statistically significant difference (p=0.934, Cramer's V=0.01). Participants with COPD took longer to complete the TGlittre tasks (p=0.011). There were no significant differences between the groups on the FACIT-F scale (p=0.964) or the SF-36, except for the "physical functioning" domain, which was worse in the COPD group (p=0.018). In conclusion, individuals seeking CBT exhibit a high degree of nicotine dependence, regardless of COPD status. SAD is detected in approximately three-quarters of these individuals, regardless of COPD status. Furthermore, low FEC is more common in people with COPD, though general fatigue and QoL are impaired in smokers with and without COPD.

articles.title: Long-Term Exercise Training for Liver Enzymes and Liver Fat in Adults With Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease: A Multilevel Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to quantify long-term exercise effects on liver enzymes and liver fat content in adults with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and explore dose-response patterns and modifiers.

METHODS: Four databases were searched through May 28, 2026. Three-level random-effects models accounted for dependent effect sizes and were supplemented by sampling variance-covariance models that explicitly addressed correlations arising from shared comparator groups. CR2 cluster-robust variance estimation was additionally used for small-sample robust inference. Robustness was further examined using influence, sensitivity, publication-bias, and trim-and-fill analyses. Subgroup, meta-regression, dose-response, and XGBoost-SHAP analyses were conducted. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE.

RESULTS: Sixteen randomized controlled trials were included. Exercise was associated with lower ALT (MD = -6.01, 95% CI -11.88 to -0.15; p = 0.045) and liver fat content (SMD = -0.47, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.27; p < 0.001), whereas AST was not significant. After CR2 correction, liver fat remained significant, but ALT did not. Exploratory analyses suggested possible heterogeneity related to exercise frequency, intervention duration, age, and participant type, but these findings were limited by the small number of studies and multiple comparisons. A favorable cumulative dose near 16 h was near the data boundary, not a prescription target.

CONCLUSION: Long-term exercise was associated with lower liver fat content in adults with NAFLD. ALT reduction remains possible but uncertain; AST evidence is insufficient, and dose-response findings require confirmation.

articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Methods Evaluation and Recommendations for Reporting Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the completeness of methodological reporting in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-based clinical trials, and based on our findings, to propose a standardized reporting framework to improve reproducibility and transparency.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a search to assemble a study sample of CGM-based clinical trials published between 2019 and 2024. Articles were identified via PubMed and screened based on predefined eligibility criteria. We measured the presence or absence of reporting elements across seven core methodological features essential for reproducibility, spanning CGM device characteristics, data platforms, data extraction processes, preprocessing and transformation methods, handling of missing data, CGM metrics, and analytic approaches. Data were manually extracted by trained reviewers, with quality assurance performed on a subset of records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize reporting completeness.

RESULTS: A total of 248 studies met inclusion criteria. On average, studies reported 4.39 (SD 1.22) of the seven core methodological features. Reporting was highest for CGM metrics (100%), analytic methods (100%), and device make/model (96%). In contrast, key elements of the CGM data pipeline were frequently underreported, including data extraction processes (56%), preprocessing methods (43%), handling of missing data (32%), and CGM data platform (30%). Only 6% of studies reported all seven features. These findings demonstrate substantial heterogeneity and consistent gaps in reporting practices across CGM clinical research within the literature sampling frame.

CONCLUSIONS: Incomplete reporting of CGM data pipelines limits reproducibility, comparability, and the clinical and computational utility of CGM-derived outcomes. We propose a preliminary, candidate CGM-specific reporting checklist to standardize documentation of data acquisition, processing, and analysis. Adoption of a refined, consensus-based version of such a framework may strengthen methodological rigor, support regulatory and clinical interpretation, and enhance the reliability of CGM data for emerging digital health and artificial intelligence applications.

articles.title: Ten-Year Longitudinal Changes in Nailfold Videocapillaroscopy Findings and Clinical Features in Systemic Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether 10-year changes in nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) findings are associated with changes in clinical characteristics in systemic sclerosis (SSc). This retrospective single-center study included 84 patients with SSc who underwent NVC assessment at baseline and after 10 years. NVC patterns were classified as normal, non-specific, early, active, or late. Patients were categorized by longitudinal NVC changes. Associations of NVC-change groups with changes in clinical characteristics including modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS), digital ulcers, interstitial lung disease, percent predicted vital capacity (%VC), and percent predicted diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (%DLco) were examined. Over 10 years, NVC findings improved in 19 patients, remained unchanged in 41, and worsened in 24. Change in mRSS differed significantly among the groups, with greater improvement in the improved group than in the unchanged group (p = 0.0140) and the worsened group (p = 0.0161). Changes in digital ulcers were not associated with NVC-change groups. Among 47 patients with longitudinal %DLco data, Δ%DLco differed significantly among the groups, with the greatest decline in the worsened group (p = 0.0067), whereas Δ%VC did not differ significantly. NVC-change group was significantly associated with mRSS at 10 years after adjustment for baseline mRSS and disease duration (p = 0.0291), but not with Δ%DLco after adjustment for interstitial lung disease and pulmonary hypertension at 10 years (p = 0.0684). In conclusion, long-term NVC changes may occur in both directions may reflect the long-term course of skin sclerosis.

articles.title: Exploring the associations between food insecurity, eco-anxiety, sustainable and healthy eating behaviors, and life satisfaction among nutrition and dietetics students in Türkiye.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food insecurity may intersect with sustainable eating, eco-anxiety, and subjective well-being, but evidence among dietitians is limited. This cross-sectional study examined these associations among 2027 nutrition and dietetics students recruited through multicenter departmental networks in Türkiye. Participants completed the Sustainable and Healthy Eating Behaviors Scale, Adult Food Security Survey Module, Ecological Anxiety Scale, and Contentment with Life Assessment Scale. Group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and sequential multivariable linear regression were used.

RESULTS: Overall, 1381 students (68.1%) were food secure and 646 (31.9%) were food insecure. Compared with food-secure students, food-insecure students had lower sustainable and healthy eating behavior scores [3.93 (3.11-4.53) vs. 4.09 (3.48-4.74); |rrb| = 0.132], higher ecological anxiety [16.50 (13.00-22.00) vs. 13.00 (8.00-17.00); |rrb| = 0.321], and lower life contentment [19.00 (16.00-22.00) vs. 22.00 (19.00-26.00); |rrb| = 0.422] (all P < 0.001). In fully adjusted models, higher food insecurity scores were associated with lower sustainable and healthy eating scores (beta = -0.073, P = 0.002), higher ecological anxiety (beta = 0.279, P < 0.001), and lower life contentment (beta = -0.305, P < 0.001); adjusted R-squared values were 0.040, 0.093, and 0.128, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Food insecurity was associated with less favorable sustainable and healthy eating behaviors, greater eco-anxiety, and lower life contentment among nutrition and dietetics students. Effect sizes ranged from small to moderate, and the cross-sectional design does not permit causal inference. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Occupational well-being of biomedical scientists in academic medical centers.
articles.journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Scientific faculty at academic medical centers face unprecedented challenges, but limited evidence exists to guide supportive strategies. This study compares the prevalence and drivers of burnout and professional fulfillment in faculty scientists and physicians.

METHOD: A validated survey assessing occupational burnout, professional fulfillment, intent to leave one's institution, and associated drivers was collected in scientists and physicians from 7 U.S. organizations participating in the Healthcare Professional Well-being Academic Consortium from March 2022 to May 2024. Data analysis included descriptive statistics and hierarchical multivariable regression to examine differences in occupational well-being outcomes by faculty type.

RESULTS: In total, 10,032 respondents (2,231 scientists; 7,801 physicians) were included (response rate: 47.4%). Overall, 35.4% of scientists and 40.8% of physicians met criteria for burnout (p<.001), and 43.8% of scientists and 37.2% of physicians met criteria for high professional fulfillment (p<.001). In contrast, 37.3% of scientists expressed intent to leave vs 34.9% of physicians (p=.01). On 0-10 scales, scientists reported more alignment between personal and organizational values (mean score 5.18 vs 4.76; p<.001), greater sense of control over schedule (mean score 6.07 vs 4.04; p<.001), and less negative impact of work on personal relationships (mean score 2.84 vs 3.41; p<.001) vs physicians. In multivariable regression models, adjustment for differences in control over schedule between scientists and physicians led to reversal of the relationship between faculty type and burnout and professional fulfillment, with higher relative rates of burnout and lower rates of professional fulfillment in scientists vs physicians.

CONCLUSIONS: The authors found that rates of occupational burnout were lower and professional fulfillment higher in scientists vs physicians. Despite these differences, intent to leave was more common in scientists relative to physicians. Key drivers appeared to mediate these differences in occupational well-being, laying the groundwork for potential interventions to support scientists in academic medical centers.

articles.title: Embolic complications of cardiac myxoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of frequency, clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution and outcomes in contemporary cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumours and embolise, causing stroke, acute coronary syndrome, limb ischaemia, and visceral infarction. Although previous reviews examined clinical features and embolic risk factors, the frequency, anatomical distribution, management, and outcomes of myxoma-related embolisation have not been comprehensively synthesised.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, and PubMed from inception to February 2026 for observational studies reporting embolic complications of confirmed cardiac myxoma; small (≤10-patient) and pre-2000 case series were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions estimated patient-level embolic prevalence and event-level anatomical distribution.

RESULTS: Across 47 studies (4,964 patients), pooled embolic prevalence was 19.7% (95% CI 16.7-23.1; I²=75.4%, 95% CI 62.8-87.5). Cerebral events predominated (75.6%), followed by peripheral limb (17.0%). Pooled early mortality was 1.9% (95% CI 1.3-2.7). Villous morphology and high tumour mobility were more associated with embolisation than size. Recurrence was uncommon (crude rate 2.0%) and mainly in familial disease or Carney complex.

CONCLUSION: Embolism is common and predominantly cerebral. Villous surface and tumour mobility were more consistently associated with embolisation than size and may inform the urgency of resection. However, evidence is retrospective; the optimal timing after embolic presentation remains undefined, and prospective validation is required.

articles.title: Magnetic Thermal Ablation Combined with Temporally Coordinated CpG Immunotherapy Promotes cDC1-Dependent Immune Priming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) imposes a major global health burden, with current ablation techniques limited by invasiveness and post-treatment recurrence. Here, size-controllable, polylactic acid/iron oxide magnetic microspheres containing 30% Fe3O4 (P@Fe30 MSs) were fabricated via shirasu porous glass membrane emulsification for transarterial magnetic thermal ablation (MTA). The optimized microspheres exhibit superior magnetothermal performance under an alternating magnetic field, effectively killing tumor cells and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Mechanistically, MTA-induced tumor disruption cooperates with the TLR9 agonist CpG ODN to accelerate dendritic cell maturation and promote a tumor-TDLN immune-priming cascade, featuring CD103+ cDC1 enrichment and CCR7-associated cDC1 migration dynamics, functional CD8+ T-cell activation, and systemic memory-associated immune remodeling. Crucially, direct evaluation of CpG timelines reveals that early post-MTA CpG administration significantly outperforms delayed delivery, validating a transient post-ablation immune-priming window. Furthermore, experiments in Batf3-/- mice confirm that this systemic antitumor immunity strictly depends on a cDC1- mediated priming pathway. Finally, preclinical validation in an orthotopic rabbit VX2 liver tumor model demonstrates excellent transarterial feasibility, localized metabolic tumor suppression via 18F-FDG PET imaging, and a favorable safety profile. This work establishes a remotely activated transarterial ablation platform that coordinates with temporal innate immunotherapy to drive systemic cDC1-dependent antitumor responses.

articles.title: Quantized Analog Inference Hardware Enabled by MoS2-Hf1-xZrxO2 FeFET Synapses.
articles.abstract: Analog in-memory computing can accelerate edge-AI inference by executing vector-matrix multiplication directly in memory crossbars, but practical analog deployment is constrained by finite weight resolution and stochastic programming. Here we demonstrate program-pulse-engineered MoS2-Hf1-xZrxO2 (HZO) ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) synapses and a hardware-consistent quantized machine-learning workflow for noise-robust analog inference. The device integrates an atomically thin monolayer MoS2 channel, representing ultimate body-thickness scaling in advanced logic roadmaps, with a CMOS-compatible HZO ferroelectric gate stack. Operating in a near-coercive regime, trains of identical potentiation/depression pulses yield gradual and reversible multi-level conductance updates with ∼100 states, enabling array-realistic programming without per-device program-and-verify. Systematic pulse engineering provides knobs to tune update granularity and dynamic range, and enables offset control of the usable conductance window via asymmetric depression conditions. Crucially, we quantify cycle-to-cycle write variability using state-dependent ΔG statistics and incorporate the measured quantization levels and noise directly into training and evaluation. Using MNIST as a benchmark, noise-aware quantization-aware training outperforms post-training quantization across quantization levels and noise scaling, sustaining up to ∼97% test accuracy under low precision and elevated noise. These results connect measured programming physics to robust quantized analog inference and establish practical device-algorithm co-design principles for scalable FeFET-based synaptic hardware.

articles.title: Quantifying physical rehabilitation demand as a foundational piece to modelling physiotherapy workforce on UK ICUs.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract: The Guideline for Provision of Intensive Care Services version 3 (GPICS3) emphasises the need for physiotherapy staffing models that reflect local service demands and minimum standards rather than specified ratios. Therefore, demand for each activity required to meet GPICS3 minimum standards must be quantified. Provision of physical rehabilitation is one such, but it is unknown what proportion of patients require it each day. Post-hoc analysis of mobility data from 960 patients across 84 UK ICUs was undertaken to calculate rehabilitation demand. It was 45.3% of patients but varied substantially by ICU speciality. National staff-to-bed ratios therefore risk inaccurately quantifying staffing requirements to meet minimum standards.

articles.title: Developing a digital heart failure symptom management intervention using the preparation phase of the Multiphase Optimization StraTegy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persons with heart failure (HF) often experience bothersome symptoms in daily life, which can negatively affect their health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Self-care e.g. to monitor and manage symptoms, is essential in HF management. Self-care can stabilize the disease, reduce symptoms, and improve outcomes. However, patients often find it difficult to recognize and manage symptoms due to various factors. Consequently, many people delay acting until their symptoms become too severe to manage by themselves. This highlights the need for timely engagement in symptom monitoring and interpretation to enable early and appropriate responses. In the SympTom mAnagement and self-caRe (STAR) study, we prepare (phase 1), optimize (phase 2), and evaluate (phase 3) a digital intervention using the Multiphase Optimization StraTegy (MOST). The STAR intervention supports patients with HF in recognizing their symptoms and taking timely, appropriate actions.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to describe the MOST preparation phase of the STAR intervention, including its development of the underlying conceptual model, identification of candidate components and optimization criterion, and assessment of intervention feasibility to inform the subsequent optimization phase.

METHODS: We conducted four sequential activities from the preparation phase of MOST: (1) developing a conceptual model; (2) identifying candidate components; (3) identifying optimization criterion; and (4) conducting a feasibility study of the digital STAR intervention with patients with HF and HF nurses.

RESULTS: The conceptual model includes four candidate components; a basic component, symptom awareness training, symptom management counselling, and symptom management experiments. We expect these components to influence behavioral outcomes such as reduced symptom burden and hospitalizations, and improved self-care and HRQOL. The set of candidate components were specified at two levels (low versus high) by varying intensity, frequency, or mode of delivery while maintaining consistent core content. Ten patients with HF and 5 HF nurses tested the STAR intervention in the feasibility study. The STAR intervention was perceived as feasible from both a patient and nurses' perspective. Patients rated the intervention as clear, user-friendly and structured. Participants valued personal support from HF nurses and perceived it as important for continued use of the intervention. The feasibility findings provide concrete input to refine the intervention prior to the optimization trial.

CONCLUSION: The STAR intervention is feasible and acceptable to both patients with HF and HF nurses. Combined with the conceptual model, linking components to underlying mechanisms and outcomes, the findings provide us a solid foundation for optimizing the STAR intervention in a subsequent optimization trial.

articles.title: The use of three murine genetic models of Alzheimer's disease reveals efficacy of 4',5,7-trihydroxyisoflavone in alleviating cognitive deficits and reducing levels of amyloid-beta and hyperphosphorylated tau protein.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite intensive studies on developing therapies for Alzheimer's disease (AD), there is still a need to improve the treatment efficacy. Results of recent studies indicated that genistein (4',5,7-trihydroxyisoflavone) was effective in an autophagy stimulation-dependent improving of cognitive deficits and reducing levels of amyloid-beta and hyperphosphorylated tau protein in brains, when employing a streptozotocin-induced rat model of the sporadic form of AD. Despite those encouraging results, the above-mentioned model has its limitations, mainly related to the rapid and inducible character of the symptoms caused by streptozotocin, induction of other effects (like diabetes) by this toxin, and the requirement for invasive administration of this compound to the brain, in contrast to naturally occurring AD. Thus, in this study, we hypothesized that genistein might be effective in reducing symptoms of AD in well-defined genetic models of this disease and tested the efficacy of this compound.

RESULTS: Three genetic models of AD were employed, including mouse lines 5xFAD, THY-Tau22, and 3xTg-AD. Orally administered genistein (at the dose of 150 mg/kg/day) considerably alleviated cognitive deficits (in spatial memory, learning, and long-term memory) of AD animals as estimated using the Morris water maze and the novel object recognition tests. Moreover, significantly reduced levels of amyloid-beta and hyperphosphorylated tau protein in plasma and brains were detected in genistein-treated AD animals relative to those treated with water.

CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that genistein revealed significant efficacy in ameliorating symptoms occurring in murine genetic models of AD. Thus, further studies towards the development of a genistein-based treatment for this disease are substantiated.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Interprofessional education in palliative care: a theory-informed evaluation of a storyline-based curriculum for health and social care students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interprofessional education (IPE) in palliative care is essential for fostering collaborative, patient-centred practice. However, existing programs often underrepresent non-medical professions and insufficiently address spiritual care, ethical reflection, and experiential learning, despite the relevance of these aspects to comprehensive, holistic palliative care. This study evaluates an innovative interprofessional curriculum integrating the Canadian Interprofessional Health Collaborative (CIHC) framework, Social Identity Theory (SIT), and Transformative Learning Theory (TLT), designed to promote holistic, values-based learning through narrative-based, experiential methods.

METHODS: A mixed-methods design was employed in the second implementation cycle (summer term 2025) of the course 'Interprofessional Collaboration in Palliative Care' at Hochschule Hannover, involving 25 students from medicine, nursing, social work, and religious education. A quantitative survey assessed knowledge, attitudes, and skills, while two focus groups explored learning experiences and interprofessional collaboration within the course. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and inductive-deductive qualitative content analysis (Kuckartz & Rädiker) with MAXQDA 2024.

RESULTS: A total of 19 students participated in the survey, and 10 students took part in the two focus groups. Students reported high satisfaction with the course structure, practical orientation, and the storyline method, which facilitated engagement and team-based learning. The survey showed particularly positive ratings for social and communication skills, knowledge of other professional groups, and team-oriented problem solving. Qualitative analysis revealed eleven sub-codes allocated to three deductive main codes: (1) the course's narrative design enabled deep reflection on professional identity and ethical responsibilities; (2) underrepresentation of medical and nursing students in some groups risked professional hierarchies; (3) students expressed a strong desire for more balanced professional representation, discipline-specific content, and clinical experiences, such as visits to hospices or contact with patients.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that a theoretically grounded, narrative-based IPE curriculum can support interprofessional competence and reflection on professional roles in palliative care. However, challenges remain in ensuring equitable professional representation and integrating authentic clinical experiences. Future programs must reflect time limitations, balance narrative engagement with discipline-specific depth and integrate structured clinical placements or simulated patient encounters to fully prepare students for the complex, collaborative realities of palliative care practice.

articles.title: Predictors of physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify predictors of physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. Participants underwent assessment of physical performance using the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), the 60-second sit-to-stand (60s-STS) test, handgrip strength, bone mineral density (BMD) by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), and clinical and laboratory variables. Participants were classified according to changes in SPPB score between baseline and follow-up. The minimal detectable change (MDC) of the SPPB was used as the criterion for defining physical performance decline. Statistical analysis included Student's t-test, the Mann-Whitney test, and chi-square tests. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable penalized logistic regression with Firth correction were used to identify predictors of physical performance decline.

RESULTS: Of the 103 participants, 18 (17.5%) experienced physical performance decline after a mean follow-up of 18.6 ± 10.1 months. Compared with those who maintained physical performance, participants with physical performance decline were older and had lower total and femoral bone mineral density and poorer performance on the 60s-STS test at baseline. In the multivariable penalized logistic regression analysis, lower femoral BMD (OR: 0.997; 95% CI: 0.991-0.999) and longer hemodialysis vintage (OR: 1.009; 95% CI: 1.001-1.039) were independently associated with physical performance decline.

CONCLUSION: This prospective study showed that lower femoral bone mineral density and longer hemodialysis vintage were independently associated with physical performance decline in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. These findings underscore the potential value of longitudinal physical performance assessment and may help identify patients at greater risk of functional decline.

articles.title: Prediction of death by neurologic criteria in patients with non-traumatic acute brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust predictors of death by neurologic criteria (DNC) after non-traumatic acute brain injury remain insufficiently defined. We therefore aimed to systematically synthesize the available evidence on prediction of DNC in non-traumatic brain injury.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched to August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, case series and registry data. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when sufficient comparable data for the same prognostic factor were available from at least two studies. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: The database search identified 2,091 records. Eighteen studies comprising reported study cohorts of 9,070 participants were included. Quantitative synthesis included four studies (n=1,738), comprising two post-cardiac arrest and two stroke cohorts. In stroke populations, CT markers of severe intracranial mass effect were associated with a more than threefold increased odds of DNC (pooled OR 3.14, 95%CI 1.98-4.96; p<0.0001; I2=0%), while in post-cardiac arrest cohorts lower gray-white matter ratio values were associated with progression to DNC (pooled mean difference -0.15, 95%CI -0.22 to -0.07; p<0.001; I2=72%).

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on predictors of DNC after non-traumatic acute brain injury remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous, with only a small number of studies providing robust analyses. Across these studies, CT-based markers - particularly indicators of diffuse cerebral edema or intracranial mass effect - show the most reproducible associations with progression to DNC.

articles.title: Heart-reactive antibody levels differentially associate with ventricular function in hereditary cardiomyopathies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: gCMP are a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. While agonistic anti-β1-adrenergic receptor antibodies (anti-β1AR-ECII) have a recognized pathogenic role in idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), the relevance of HRA in gCMP remains unclear.

METHODS: One hundred gCMP patients with confirmed genetic variants in cardiomyopathy genes were compared with 100 age- and sex-matched healthy individuals. Antibody reactivities were quantified using bead-based flow cytometric assays against cardiac antigens: The second extracellular loop of the β1 adrenergic receptor (β1AR-ECII), Troponin I3 (TPI3), Tropomyosin 1 (TPM1), Myosin heavy chain 6 and 7 (MYH6, MYH7) and Myosin light chain 7 (MYL7).

RESULTS: gCMP patients showed higher anti-TPI3 and lower anti-TPM1 antibody levels compared to controls indicating increased induction of the former and loss of the latter in gCMP patients. Age and sex influenced HRA patterns in both groups. Anti-MYH6 and anti-TPM1 antibody levels were negatively associated with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), both overall and within specific gCMP subtypes, including hypertrophic and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Additionally, anti-MYH6 antibody levels were negatively associated with right ventricular function, measured by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE).

CONCLUSION: Our findings stress the diagnostic potential of HRA profiling and indicate that gCMP patients might profit from therapeutic targeting of HRA.

articles.title: Drug-coated balloons in coronary disease: meta-analysis comparing sirolimus- and paclitaxel-coated technologies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are a key alternative to drug-eluting stents for coronary artery interventions, offering the advantage of drug delivery without permanent implants. Both paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs) and sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) are valuable treatment options. This systematic review and meta-analysis compare the efficacy and safety of sirolimus-coated versus paclitaxel-coated balloon catheters in patients with coronary artery disease.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines, searching five databases. We exclusively included RCTs. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using fixed-effects or random-effects models, with sensitivity analysis performed in cases of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Eight trials involving 1043 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant difference between SCB and PCB for late lumen loss (MD 0.06, 95% CI [-0.02 to 0.14]). Only two outcomes showed statistically significant differences favoring PCB: reducing late lumen enlargement (RR 0.66, 95% CI [0.49-0.87], P = 0.004) and, after sensitivity analysis, lowering binary restenosis rates in de novo lesions CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis shows SCB and PCB have similar safety and efficacy in coronary artery interventions, with no significant differences in most outcomes. However, PCB outperforms late lumen enlargement and binary restenosis rates in de novo lesions. Similar outcomes across sirolimus formulations indicate other factors influence success. Both balloon types appear safe and effective, though PCB may retain certain advantages in specific scenarios. Larger, longer-term studies are needed to establish the optimal drug-coated balloon strategy for different patient populations.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Beyond Anticoagulant Exposure: Determinants of Mortality After Gastrointestinal Bleeding Across DOAC, Warfarin and Non-Anticoagulated Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Reported outcomes after gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in anticoagulated patients are inconsistent, and comparisons with non-anticoagulated patients are limited. We assessed whether anticoagulation status was independently associated with mortality after GIB and identified predictors of death.

METHODS: We analysed 11,387 consecutive adults with acute GIB over 25 years (n = 500 direct oral anticoagulant [DOAC], n = 353 warfarin, n = 10,534 non-anticoagulated). All-cause mortality at 30 days and 1 year was modelled using overlap-weighted logistic regression, with complete mortality follow-up through the Israeli National Population Registry.

RESULTS: Anticoagulated patients were older (median age 81.7 [DOAC] and 75.1 [warfarin] vs. 58.4 years), had greater comorbidity and higher crude mortality than non-anticoagulated patients. After overlap weighting, neither DOAC nor warfarin was significantly associated with mortality (30-day OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.81-3.21 for DOAC and 1.30, 95% CI 0.56-3.02 for warfarin; 1-year OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.62-1.31 and 1.08, 95% CI 0.69-1.69). At 30 days, mortality was associated with age, haemodynamic shock (OR 4.25) and Internal Medicine ward admission (OR 4.55); at 1 year, with age, renal failure, Internal Medicine ward admission and inversely with male sex. Anticoagulation was resumed at discharge in 37.8% of survivors.

CONCLUSIONS: Neither DOAC nor warfarin was significantly associated with 30-day or 1-year mortality after GIB, including when bleeding severity and admitting ward were excluded from the outcome model. Thirty-day mortality was associated with severity at presentation, whereas 1-year mortality was associated with underlying patient characteristics. Resumption was not significantly associated with mortality or readmission for recurrent bleeding.

articles.title: Sustained Versus Minimal GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Exposure and Metabolic Outcomes in Older Adults Without Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare changes in body mass index (BMI) categories after sustained versus minimal glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) exposure in older adults with obesity and without diabetes. A secondary aim was to compare changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) categories among those with paired HbA1c measurements.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort study within Clalit Health Services, Israel. Adults aged ≥ 65 years without diabetes, with baseline BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 and paired BMI measurements, were classified as minimal (1-2 dispensations) or sustained (≥ 3) exposure. The primary outcome was BMI category improvement. Secondary outcomes were relative BMI change, HbA1c category change in the paired-HbA1c subset, and incident diagnosed diabetes. BMI improvement was modelled by logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, socioeconomic status and comorbidity.

RESULTS: Of 13 387 patients (69% female), 11 121 (83%) had sustained and 2266 (17%) minimal exposure. BMI category improved in 55% of the sustained versus 30% of the minimal group (p < 0.001; median change -8% vs. -2%). Among 7392 with paired HbA1c, HbA1c improved in 34% versus 20% (sustained vs. minimal; p < 0.001), and 65% versus 37% of those with prediabetes became normoglycaemic. Diabetes diagnosis was less frequent with sustained exposure (2.5% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001). Adjusted for measured confounders, sustained exposure was associated with BMI improvement (OR: 2.77, 95% CI: 2.51-3.06).

CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with obesity and without diabetes, sustained versus minimal GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with greater improvement in BMI and HbA1c categories and a lower incidence of diabetes. These findings describe observed changes after treatment initiation, not a proven causal treatment effect.

articles.title: Reduced Risk of MASLD and Cardiometabolic Disease Following Renal Denervation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autonomic dysfunction increases the risk of cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renal denervation reduces renal sympathetic nerve activity and lowers blood pressure independent of long-term pharmacotherapy, with potential downstream effects on metabolic and hepatic pathways. We aimed to evaluate the impact of renal denervation, compared with intensive antihypertensive therapy, on cardiometabolic disease risk.

METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using the TriNetX global federated health research network. Eligible participants were adults with hypertension (ICD-10 code I10) who were treated with either renal denervation therapy and pharmacological treatment (identified via ICD-10 or Current Procedural Terminology codes), acting as the treatment group, or an intensive pharmacological antihypertensive regime (four of a beta blocker, calcium channel blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin II receptor blocker, alpha blocker or diuretic), acting as the control group. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced the treatment and control groups, accounting for confounding variables. The primary outcome was of MASLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), while secondary outcomes included T2D, CKD and a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): sudden cardiac death, ischaemic heart disease (IHD), cerebrovascular accident (CVA), peripheral vascular disease (PVD) and heart failure (HF). Cox regression generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: After matching, 1735 patients remained in each group, with well-balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 42 vs. 41 years; standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.05; 52.6% vs. 54.3% male; SMD 0.03). After PSM, renal denervation was associated with a lower risk of MASLD (HR 0.38 [0.29, 0.51]), T2D (HR 0.21 [0.13, 0.33]), CKD (HR 0.26 [0.20, 0.35]), MACE (HR 0.46 [0.34, 0.62]), IHD (HR 0.56 [0.39, 0.80]), CVA (HR 0.33 [0.20, 0.52]) and HF (HR 0.39 [0.25, 0.62]).

CONCLUSION: Control of the sympathetic nervous system with renal denervation therapy in patients with resistant hypertension is associated with a lower risk of incident CKM syndrome including MASLD, T2D, CVD and CKD, supporting the role of autonomic dysfunction in the progression of cardiometabolic disease.

articles.title: The Variability in the Pharmacokinetics of Follitropin Alfa: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive research on the pharmacodynamics of follitropin alfa, a comprehensive synthesis of its pharmacokinetic variability is lacking. Understanding the interindividual and intraindividual variability in the pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa may help inform dosing strategies by reducing variability in systemic exposure. This systematic review aimed to characterise the variability in the pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa.

METHODS: Embase, PubMed, Scopus and citation mining of included articles were searched from database inception to 10 November 2025. Studies performed in humans, published in English which reported the pharmacokinetics, route of administration and dosing regimen of follitropin alfa were eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: Fifteen eligible studies were evaluated. The pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa were described by a two-compartment model following intravenous administration, and a one-compartment model with first-order absorption after intramuscular or subcutaneous administration. Follitropin alfa exhibited dose-proportional pharmacokinetics. Moderate interindividual variability (26-42%) in apparent clearance was reported following multiple subcutaneous administrations. Body weight influenced the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneously administered follitropin alfa. Comparable pharmacokinetic characteristics of follitropin alfa were observed across (i) originator and biosimilar preparations, (ii) healthy and infertile individuals, and (iii) subcutaneous and intramuscular routes of administration.

CONCLUSIONS: Weight-based dosing of follitropin alfa may reduce pharmacokinetic interindividual variability. However, whether this reduction in variability translates into more consistent ovarian response remains unclear and requires further investigation.

articles.title: Application and Improvement of YOLO11 for Carotid Plaque Detection in Handheld Ultrasound Images.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Early and accurate detection of carotid plaques is clinically significant for stroke risk assessment and primary care screening. To address challenges such as low resolution, small target size, and blurred boundaries in handheld ultrasound images of carotid plaques, this paper proposes an improved YOLO11n model named YOLO11-MGD. The model introduces the C2PSA_Mona module to suppress interference from normal anatomical structures and incorporates the C3k2_GCConv module to enhance global context modeling capabilities, thereby alleviating semantic fragmentation caused by heterogeneous plaques. Additionally, it integrates a Dynamic Head to achieve joint dynamic attention allocation across scale, space, and task dimensions, and it designs the Inner_MPDIoU loss function to improve bounding box regression accuracy for irregular plaques. Experimental results show that on a self-constructed dataset containing 2078 carotid plaque images, YOLO11-MGD achieves a mean mAP50 of 93.16%, outperforming several mainstream object detection models. While maintaining its lightweight advantage, the proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy and robustness of carotid plaque detection in low-quality ultrasound images and demonstrates good application value for primary care stroke risk screening.

articles.title: TriKey AutoRefine: A Stability-Aware Framework Built on Pan-organ Segmentation Radiomics for Chronic Kidney Disease Staging.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Accurate and generalizable imaging‑based staging of chronic kidney disease remains challenging due to segmentation variability, feature instability, and heterogeneous clinical presentations. To address these gaps, a clinically aligned pan‑organ radiomics workflow for multi‑class chronic kidney disease staging was proposed. A total of 587 subjects from 3 centers were included, with chest and abdominal computed tomography scans paired with clinical and body-composition measurements. Segmentation‑induced variability was quantified within the pan‑organ segmentation system, revealing systematic anatomical and feature‑level patterns that enabled the construction of a robust and generalizable feature foundation. Building on these observations, the TriKey autorefine framework was introduced as a structured refinement strategy incorporating Shapley additive explanations guided refinement, clinically informed class weighting, and automatic parameter optimization. Using this framework, strong performance was achieved across chronic kidney disease staging tasks. In the standard 5‑class setting, high discriminative ability was obtained: training macro area under the curve 0.925 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.923-0.927); validation macro area under the curve 0.875 ± 0.0087 (95% CI 0.858-0.892). In the clinically actionable 4‑class grouping, even stronger performance was observed, with a mean macro area under the curve of 0.915 ± 0.0060 (95% CI 0.903-0.927). Interpretability was further supported through radiomics-clinical correlation analyses, which confirmed that the selected pan organ features correspond to measurable physiological variations associated with chronic kidney disease progression. This study demonstrates a robust, interpretable, and clinically grounded pan‑organ radiomics pipeline for chronic kidney disease staging, providing a generalizable foundation for future pan-organ radiomics research in nephrology and broader clinical imaging applications.

articles.title: Platelet-rich plasma for knee osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of structural outcomes.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the impact of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) on imaging-based structural outcomes in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026 evaluating imaging-based structural effects of PRP in knee OA. Risk ratio (RR) was used to evaluate binary outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) or mean differences (MDs) for continuous endpoints, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: A total of 12 RCTs involving 1,200 patients were included. PRP was associated with greater improvement in patellofemoral cartilage thickness/volume compared with control treatments (SMD 0.94; 95% CI, 0.53 to 1.34), whereas no significant differences were observed for medial tibial cartilage thickness/volume or cartilage defect progression. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based structural scores showed no between-group differences in Whole-Organ Magnetic Resonance Imaging Score (WORMS) osteophytes or subchondral cysts, although PRP demonstrated a significant reduction in bone marrow edema (SMD - 0.40; 95% CI, - 0.71 to - 0.09). Synovitis did not differ overall between groups (SMD - 0.22; 95% CI, - 0.43 to 0.00).

CONCLUSION: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, PRP demonstrated limited and inconsistent effects on imaging-based structural outcomes in knee OA, and did not confer significant and consistent benefits in medial tibial cartilage measurements, cartilage defect progression, synovitis, or most WORMS domains. The favorable findings observed for patellofemoral cartilage and bone marrow edema should be interpreted with caution. Thus, the findings do not provide clear evidence supporting PRP as a structural disease-modifying treatment, and additional high-quality RCTs using standardized imaging endpoints are warranted.

articles.title: Exploring perspectives and engagement in space surgery: a survey of SAGES members.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SAGES' space surgery task force was created in 2023 in response to the potential increased need for surgical intervention in space as humanity seeks to establish larger and more permanent populations in space environments. This task force sought to assess the needs, limitations, and anticipated challenges of surgical care in space environments and to offer leadership opportunities by surveying the SAGES membership.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of the SAGES membership soliciting respondent's experience in aerospace medicine and related fields, as well as members' interests within space surgery and their opinions about the future surgical needs of space explorers. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographics, interests, and preferences, and narrative review and thematic analysis were used to analyze open-ended responses.

RESULTS: Survey response rate was 6.1%. Most respondents were attending minimally invasive or general surgeons. Experience was reported in telehealth, artificial intelligence, austere environment surgery, and military medicine. Greatest interest was expressed in the application of robotic technologies in space. Respondents wished to participate in technical skills workshops and to view presentations by astronauts on space medicine as part of the future activities of the task force at SAGES annual meetings. Themes identified as challenges to space surgery included microgravity, resource limitations, remote surgery, training, and specific medical concerns. Future areas of focus included technology and innovation, protocol/system design, adjustment to medical standards, and training programs.

CONCLUSION: This survey identified a strong interest among the SAGES membership in leading the conversation surrounding space surgery as humanity expands beyond low earth orbit. Numerous opportunities, challenges, and new directions were identified by respondents that will guide the future activities of the task force.

articles.title: A prospective controlled study assessing postpartum breastfeeding in women with type 2 diabetes: lower rates associated with elevated BMI rather than diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Breastfeeding is associated with metabolic benefits for women with type 2 diabetes and their infants, yet breastfeeding rates in these women are poorly described. Obesity is associated with type 2 diabetes and lower breastfeeding rates, making it difficult to disentangle the effects of type 2 diabetes vs obesity on breastfeeding. The primary objective was to examine breastfeeding rates in women with type 2 diabetes compared with normoglycaemic women with either (1) matched BMI or (2) normal BMI. The secondary objective was to examine variables associated with breastfeeding.

METHODS: Pregnant women with type 2 diabetes (cases) or normoglycaemia (controls) were prospectively recruited. Each case was matched with two controls by age and parity and either (1) matched or (2) normal (18-25 kg/m2) BMI. Data were collected from in-person surveys antenatally, medical records and a 4 month postpartum telephone survey. Analysis included descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: Four months of breastfeeding data were available for 29 women with type 2 diabetes, 29 BMI-matched controls and 28 normal-BMI controls. Breastfeeding rates were similar in women with type 2 diabetes and BMI-matched controls, but both rates were significantly lower than those in normal-BMI controls. 'Full' breastfeeding rates were 24%, 38% and 64% in women with type 2 diabetes, BMI-matched controls and normal-BMI controls, respectively, and were not different between women with type 2 diabetes vs BMI-matched controls (p=0.26) but were lower in women with type 2 diabetes vs normal-BMI controls (p=0.002). 'Any' breastfeeding rates were 55%, 54% and 82% in women with type 2 diabetes, BMI-matched controls and normal-BMI controls, respectively, again showing no difference between women with type 2 diabetes vs BMI-matched controls (p=0.79) but were lower in women with type 2 diabetes vs normal-BMI controls (p=0.03).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Maternal obesity, rather than type 2 diabetes, may be the major determinant of reduced breastfeeding rates 4 months postpartum.

articles.title: Congenital heart disease confers gestational age-dependent risks of mortality and morbidity in preterm infants.
authors: Children’s Hospital Neonatal Consortium Cardiac Focus Group
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the incremental risks of mortality and major neonatal morbidities associated with congenital heart disease (CHD) beyond prematurity alone.

STUDY DESIGN: Secondary analysis of two North American neonatal registries (2010-2022) including infants <35 weeks' gestation: 11,221 with CHD from the Children's Hospitals Neonatal Consortium and 720,846 without CHD from the Vermont Oxford Network. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes were major neonatal morbidities.

RESULTS: Preterm infants with CHD had fourfold higher odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 4.0, 95% CI 3.76-4.21). Mortality was similar at ≤26 weeks' gestation, but the relative impact of CHD increased with advancing gestational age. CHD was associated with significantly increased risks of severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, intraventricular hemorrhage, and necrotizing enterocolitis.

CONCLUSION: The impact of CHD on mortality is gestational age dependent, with prematurity predominating at the lowest gestational ages and CHD increasingly driving mortality as gestational maturity improves.

articles.title: A complementary proteomics and cardiac magnetic resonance approach to characterize right ventricular remodeling after tetralogy of Fallot repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can develop right ventricular (RV) dilation and failure. We sought to utilize an untargeted serum proteomics approach to characterize the proteome signature associated with RV dilation in repaired TOF to improve the understanding of mechanistic drivers of RV remodeling.

METHODS: Patients with repaired TOF undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging were recruited. Groups were based on indexed RV end-diastolic volume (RVEDVi). Serum proteomics identified differentially abundant proteins (p value < 0.05), and pathway enrichment identified functional pathways.

RESULTS: Fourteen TOF adolescents (median age 16 years; IQR 15, 18) were divided into Group 1 (n = 9; median RVEDVi 146 ml/m2; IQR 139, 164) and Group 2 (n = 5; median RVEDVi 114 ml/m2; IQR 104, 130). Group 1 had a higher indexed RV stroke volume (85 ml/m2 vs. 59 ml/m2, p = 0.023) with a similar RV ejection fraction. Group 1 had altered regulation of genes in multiple pathways, including glucose and fatty acid metabolism and antioxidant response.

CONCLUSION: Patients with repaired TOF and moderate-severe RV dilation have a distinct serum proteomic profile despite preserved ejection fraction, which may reflect alterations in fuel sources and oxidative stress. These hypothesis-generating findings are a first step in the integration of proteomics into clinical management.

IMPACT: An untargeted serum proteomics approach to identifying altered protein profiles associated with CMR-defined RV dilation is a novel approach to characterizing right ventricular remodeling after tetralogy of Fallot repair. RV dilation after repair of tetralogy of Fallot is associated with a specific proteomic profile suggesting adaptive and maladaptive remodeling. Identification of dysregulated proteins associated with RV remodeling provides insight into the mechanisms leading to ventricular failure after tetralogy of Fallot repair. With additional data from future larger studies, serum proteomics evaluation may assist in prognostication and clinical decision making in patients after tetralogy of Fallot repair.

articles.title: Collaborative role of muscle ultrasonography and subjective global-nutritional assessment in pediatric end-stage renal disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional well-being in childhood chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a multidisciplinary problem. Nevertheless, reliable nutritional status assessment considering underlying pathogenesis remains challenging. So, we aimed to assess the collaborative role of quadriceps muscle ultrasonography and subjective global nutritional assessment (SGNA) in evaluating childhood end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis (ESRD-HD).

METHODS: Sixty-eight children with ESRD-HD were enrolled in addition to 68 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent nutritional screening through SGNA, 24-h dietary recall estimation, anthropometric measurements, evaluation of protein energy wasting (PEW), and quadriceps muscle ultrasonography.

RESULTS: SGNA identified malnourishment in 85.3% of ESRD-HD children, while reduced/low muscle mass (LMM) by ultrasound was estimated in 73.6%, compared to PEW documentation in 70.6% of them. Total caloric intake discriminates LMM at a cutoff level of ≤34.022 kcal/kg/day with 93.75% sensitivity and 85.0% specificity and revealed a significant association with both PEW and LMM on regression analysis. Concerning concordance with muscle ultrasonography, SGNA had statistically good agreement, unlike anthropometric parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: Inadequate dietary intake, though highly prevalent, is still underestimated in CKD children with a negative impact on muscle mass. Also, SGNA, through combining objective anthropometry with nutrition-focused assessment, could represent a potential role for nutritional status evaluation.

IMPACT: Despite the absence of single gold standard assessment tool, PEW remains a prevalent, multifactorial nutritional comorbidity in CKD children that necessitates continuous nutritional monitoring. Quadriceps muscle ultrasound can detect changes in body composition associated with CKD, that cannot be determined just by objective anthropometry. SGNA, a simple malnutrition screening tool, showed a potential role in early prediction of both physical growth and body composition abnormalities. Dietary management for children with ESRD-HD should pay attention to total caloric, carbohydrate, and fat intakes, not just protein intake, for actual growth and body composition support.

articles.title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood.

METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development.

RESULTS: White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors.

CONCLUSION: In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population.

IMPACT: In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

articles.title: Primary preventive interventions to reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia in neonatal intensive care units: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess preventive strategies for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in mechanically ventilated (MV) neonates.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched in June 2025. Eligible studies evaluated primary VAP-prevention interventions in neonates receiving MV. Outcomes included odds ratios (ORs), incidence rate ratios (IRRs), and incidence rate differences (IRDs).

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies involving 6,301 neonates were included. Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with lower VAP occurrence (OR = 0.40, 95% CI 0.28-0.57; I² = 37%). MV-adjusted analyses showed lower incidence (IRR = 0.56, 95% CI 0.43-0.73) and 8.33 fewer VAP cases per 1000 MV-days (IRD = -0.0083, 95% CI -0.0127 to -0.0039). Oral care was associated with lower VAP odds (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; I² = 3%). Evidence for other interventions was limited and heterogeneous.

CONCLUSIONS: Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with lower neonatal VAP rates, although heterogeneous bundle composition and non-randomized designs limit causal interpretation. Oral care was also associated with lower VAP odds, but confidence in the magnitude of effect is limited by small-study effects, inconsistent subgroup findings, and variable diagnostic criteria.

IMPACT: This study provides the most comprehensive synthesis to date focused exclusively on VAP in ventilated neonates, incorporating ventilator-day-adjusted outcomes. By using robust meta-analytic methods across diverse study designs, it clarifies which interventions have consistent evidence and which remain uncertain. Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with meaningful relative and absolute reductions in neonatal VAP. The findings support further evaluation and implementation of bundle-based quality-improvement strategies. Uncertainty regarding the magnitude of benefit from oral care and the need for higher-quality controlled studies.

articles.title: Low prevalence of celiac disease in French children, a nationwide study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are differences in prevalence and incidence across Europe without updated data for France. The aim of this study was to fill this gap obtaining epidemiological data of French children with celiac disease (CD).

METHODS: We used the French Health Data System (SNDS) to identify <18-year-old patients with CD between 2011 and 22. CD identification: 1/hospitalization stay for CD, or 2/ status of CD as long-term disease, or 3/serological diagnosis (two tests for transglutaminase antibodies (TGA) within 13 months and one endomysium antibodies (EMA) test within seven months after a TGA test).

RESULTS: 41690 children with CD were identified over 2011-2022. The male-to-female sex ratio was 0.88. In 2022, the national prevalence was 0.15% among children, ranging from 0.08% in the North-West to 0.25% in the South-East of France. The incidence rate ranged from 12.4 in 2020 to 17.4 per 100000 children in 2012, with a median age increasing from six in 2011 to seven in 2015. Comorbidities included thyroid disease (1.7%), and type 1 diabetes (9.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of pediatric CD is low in France, with differences across regions. However, the age at diagnosis and the female predominance are in agreement with recent studies.

IMPACT: This nationwide study revealed a lower prevalence of CD in French children than in other European countries, with regional variations. The study confirmed the female predominance and the age of seven at diagnosis. These data should be useful to give screening advices, looking for CD even in older children with atypical signs.

articles.title: Discordance between actual care and recommendations by a reinforcement learning model for sepsis.
articles.abstract: Fluid and vasopressor management of sepsis requires a complex set of sequential treatment decisions tailored to individual responses. We examined the frequency and implications of disagreement between reinforcement-learning (RL), using the AI Clinician as a test example, and actual clinical decisions. A novel discordance score was defined as the Euclidean distance between clinical team actions and RL-recommended treatments (range 0 to 5.66), across 25 treatment options of vasopressors and intravenous (IV) fluids. Among 30,678 ICU patients with sepsis cared for across 309,415 time-epochs, discordance was more common among epochs of patients with SOFA > 6 than those with SOFA < 6, and for intravenous fluid choices than for vasopressors. After multivariable adjustment, greater discordance was associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 1.11, 95%CI: 1.05,1.18) in the SOFA strata > =6 but not for SOFA < = 4 (adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.02, 95%CI: 0.97,1.08).

articles.title: Optic nerve sheath decompression-related perioptic pseudocysts: histo-biochemical features.
articles.abstract: Two patients (Female; 9 and 32 years in age) with papilledema secondary to venous sinus thrombosis underwent bilateral medial transconjunctival optic nerve sheath decompression for visual loss. Postoperative imaging revealed perioptic cystic lesions in 3 eyes associated with persistent papilledema and increased retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. For treatment, the cystic lesions were excised through a transconjunctival approach after aspiration of their fluid content. The cystic fluid, analyzed by gel electrophoresis, tested positive for beta-2 transferrin, confirming its cerebrospinal fluid origin. Histological examination demonstrated acellular fibrotic membranes lacking meningeal cells. Surgical excision resulted in resolution of papilledema and normalization of retinal thickness in all eyes. These findings support the classification of such lesions as perioptic pseudomeningoceles and further suggest that optic nerve sheath decompression exerts its effect through cerebrospinal fluid drainage.

articles.title: Firstline treatment with ruxolitinib versus best available therapy in patients with polycythemia vera: results from the randomized RuxoBEAT trial.
authors: German Study Group for Myeloproliferative Neoplasms (GSG-MPN)
articles.abstract: Ruxolitinib (RUX) is approved as second-line treatment for HU-intolerant/-resistant patients with polycythemia vera (PV). Here, we assessed RUX vs. best available therapy (BAT) as first-line treatment in PV in the randomized multicenter RuxoBEAT clinical trial (NCT02577926). Crossover from BAT to RUX was possible after 6 months. Baseline characteristics in the RUX (n = 44) and BAT (n = 34) arms were comparable.
