The primary endpoint, the clinico-hematologic complete response (CR) rate at month 6, was not met (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 1.000). Analyses of secondary and exploratory endpoints showed that RUX was significantly more effective than BAT in improving hematocrit, splenomegaly, and patient-reported pruritus and fatigue, but less effective in reducing platelet counts. Compared to baseline, JAK2V617F variant allele frequency decreased significantly in both RUX and BAT groups at 6 months. The time on treatment (p < 0.001) and duration of treatment (p = 0.022) were significantly superior for RUX vs. BAT during the 24-month study period. There were no new safety signals. These findings demonstrate that RUX did not lead to higher CR rates than BAT and suggest that RUX may induce clinically meaningful additional disease improvements in first-line therapy of PV patients.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Peroxynitrite activates NLRP3 inflammasome and contributes to hemorrhagic transformation and poor outcome in ischemic stroke with hyperglycemia" [Free Radic. Biol. Med. 165, (2021), 171-183].
Neonatal mechanical ventilation.
authors: Grupo Patología Respiratoria y Ventilación Neonatal de SENeo
articles.abstract: Neonatal mechanical ventilation is a cornerstone in the management of respiratory failure in newborns (NBs), particularly in preterm infants, in whom pulmonary and neurologic increases their vulnerability to ventilation-induced lung injury. At present, the primary objective of respiratory support is to ensure adequate ventilation while minimizing lung and brain injury through lung-protective strategies and careful oxygen titration. Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is currently the first-line approach for both initial respiratory support and post-extubation care, as it reduces the need for invasive ventilation and the incidence of ventilator-induced lung injury. Multiple modalities and devices are available, and their selection should be individualized according to the underlying disease, gestational age, and clinical response. The selection of the appropriate interface and ventilatory settings and patient-ventilator synchronization are of utmost importance. Noninvasive ventilation failure should be preceded by systematic optimization and requires well-defined criteria for timely therapeutic escalation. Conventional mechanical ventilation continues to be necessary in more severe cases. Its use should be synchronized and volume-targeted whenever possible, as this strategy has been shown to reduce major complications such as pneumothorax, intraventricular hemorrhage, and the composite outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia. High-frequency oscillatory ventilation serves as a rescue strategy in refractory cases and selected clinical condition, relying on the maintenance of lung recruitment with extremely low tidal volumes. Finally, ventilatory management of the most common neonatal respiratory conditions-such as respiratory distress syndrome, meconium aspiration syndrome, air leak syndrome, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia-requires a dynamic, individualized approach focused on lung protection from the earliest hours of life.

articles.title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT in Tuberculosis and Other Granulomatous Diseases (except Sarcoidosis and Fungal Disease).
articles.abstract: Granulomatous inflammation consists mainly of activated macrophages, epithelioid cells, and lymphocytes, which have high glucose metabolism and therefore show increased 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) uptake on PET/computed tomography (CT). This makes FDG PET/CT useful in detecting and mapping granulomatous disease, including clinically silent or extrapulmonary involvement. It is particularly crucial in tuberculosis, where it can help identify active disease, guide biopsy, assess treatment response, and detect dissemination. FDG PET/CT also has applications in granulomatous vasculitis such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis, nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, inflammatory bowel disease, and foreign body or postsurgical granulomas. However, increased FDG uptake is nonspecific and requires clinical correlation.

articles.title: Clinical applications of remote patient monitoring.
articles.journal: Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
articles.abstract: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) utilizes a variety of technologies that enable rapid transmission of health data, allowing healthcare providers to manage medical conditions outside the hospital setting. As an increasingly important component of pediatric telehealth and healthcare delivery, RPM has been successfully implemented across multiple specialties. This review highlights RPM programs at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP), including initiatives in cardiology, neonatology, primary care, gastrostomy tube care, and neurology. These programs have demonstrated success in reducing unnecessary hospitalizations and emergency department visits, increasing access to care and subspecialty follow-up, and lowering mortality among children with chronic diseases. The review also examines the digital health technologies that support these programs. In addition, artificial intelligence is playing an expanding role in RPM through predictive alerts, risk stratification, and agentic monitoring tools that enable more personalized and proactive care. Despite these benefits, important challenges remain, including disparities in digital literacy, language barriers, and licensing restrictions. We propose that a hybrid care model integrating RPM, digital health technologies, and in-person visits provides a comprehensive framework for pediatric healthcare delivery. As RPM continues to expand across pediatric subspecialties, the development of telehealth "neighborhoods" may help strengthen medical homes for children with complex chronic conditions. Such models have the potential to improve clinical outcomes, enhance care coordination, and reduce healthcare disparities among vulnerable pediatric populations.

articles.title: The changing long-term clinical course of deep vein thrombosis in the direct oral anticoagulant era.
How to investigate abnormalities in selenium plasma concentrations in humans - Diagnostic algorithms.
articles.journal: Journal of trace elements in medicine and biology : organ of the Society for Minerals and Trace Elements (GMS)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selenium is an essential trace element involved in antioxidant defence, thyroid hormone metabolism, immune regulation and cellular homeostasis. Both selenium deficiency and selenium excess are associated with clinically significant disease; however, interpretation of abnormal plasma selenium concentrations is challenging because selenium status is influenced by nutritional, inflammatory, environmental, genetic and systemic factors.

OBJECTIVE: To critically synthesise the available evidence on the causes, laboratory assessment and clinical interpretation of abnormal plasma selenium concentrations in humans, and to develop practical diagnostic algorithms for routine clinical use.

METHODS: A focused literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, OMIM and reference lists of relevant publications from database inception to August 2026. Original human studies evaluating selenium biomarkers, deficiency, toxicity, laboratory assessment, environmental exposure and clinical management were preferentially included. Evidence was synthesised qualitatively because of heterogeneity in study design and outcomes.

KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Plasma selenium remains the most widely available biomarker but reflects recent intake and is influenced by systemic inflammation. Alternative biomarkers, including whole-blood selenium, erythrocyte selenium, glutathione peroxidase activity and selenoprotein P, provide complementary information but have important clinical limitations. Elevated selenium concentrations are most commonly associated with excessive supplementation, selenium-rich foods, occupational and environmental exposure, whereas low concentrations are linked to malnutrition, malabsorption, chronic inflammatory disease, chronic kidney or liver disease, bariatric surgery and alcohol misuse.

CONCLUSION: This review proposes practical diagnostic algorithms to support investigation of abnormal plasma selenium concentrations in routine clinical practice. Prospective validation, harmonisation of laboratory methods and reference intervals, and evaluation of emerging biomarkers are required to improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Microbiology-guided antimicrobial prophylaxis, surgical site infection and delivery of adjuvant chemotherapy after resection of perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infection (SSI) is the dominant morbidity after resection of perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA). Preoperative biliary instrumentation results in biliary colonisation with antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms, limiting the effectiveness of standard perioperative prophylaxis. Whether microbiology-guided prophylaxis improves outcomes, and whether sepsis compromises adjuvant chemotherapy delivery, is unknown.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing resection of pCCA at a UK tertiary centre (2009-2026). Routine intraoperative bile culture informed changes in institutional antimicrobial prophylaxis in 2019 from cefuroxime and metronidazole to teicoplanin and piperacillin-tazobactam. The primary outcome was SSI. In patients resected from April 2017, when adjuvant capecitabine became routine, chemotherapy receipt and timing were compared by SSI status.

RESULTS: Seventy-four patients were managed prior to the revised protocol and 58 thereafter. Biliary colonisation was near-universal (92 vs. 88%). Resistance to cefuroxime/metronidazole was detected in 70% of culture-positive baseline patients, and 14% for the revised regimen. SSI fell from 42/74 (57%) to 17/58 (29%; p = 0.003), driven by organ/space infections (46 vs. 24%; p = 0.033), and remained associated with the revised protocol after adjustment (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.72). Among 67 post-BILCAP-era patients, chemotherapy began within 12 weeks in 16% with SSI compared to 50% without; among recipients, median time to first cycle was 104 vs. 78 days (p = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: Microbiology-guided prophylaxis was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in SSI. Reducing septic complications does not just limit perioperative morbidity, but avoids delay in adjuvant chemotherapy.

articles.title: Knowledge, self-management, and health-related quality of life among Omani adults with generalized epilepsy: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess epilepsy-related knowledge, self-management (SM) practices, and health-related quality of life (HR-QoL) among Omani adults with generalized epilepsy and to examine the correlations between these variables.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 Omani adults with epilepsy attending three tertiary hospitals in Muscat. Knowledge was measured using the Epilepsy Knowledge Scale-19, SM practices using the Epilepsy Self-Management Scale, and HR-QoL using the Quality of Life in Epilepsy-31. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential statistics with a significance level of p ≤ 0.05.

RESULTS: Slightly more than half of the participants were male (52.5%), with ages ranging from 18 to 75 years (M = 33.29). Overall, participants demonstrated poor knowledge (M = 7.81/19), acceptable SM skills (M = 131.60/190), and low HR-QoL (M = 56.55/100). A significant positive correlation was found between knowledge and HR-QoL (r = 0.261, p < 0.001), whereas the correlations between knowledge and SM skills and between SM practices and HR-QoL were not significant (p = 0.710 and p = 0.104, respectively). Female gender, unemployment, presence of comorbidities, older age (≥ 50 years), and more frequent recent seizures were all significantly associated with lower HR-QoL (p ≤ 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Omani adults with epilepsy exhibit poor knowledge, only acceptable self-management skills, and low HR-QoL. The positive association between knowledge and HR-QoL highlights the need to strengthen epilepsy-related education. Culturally tailored educational and self-management support for patients, families, and the wider public is required to improve knowledge, optimize self-management, and enhance HR-QoL in Oman.

articles.title: Inferior vena cava filter-related thrombosis: Mechanisms, clinical features, prevention, diagnosis, and risk-stratified management.
articles.abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters can provide mechanical protection from pulmonary embolism in selected patients who cannot receive anticoagulation, but filter-related thrombosis is an important complication. A uniform definition is lacking. Thrombus in the filter region may represent emboli captured by the filter, extension of pre-existing deep vein thrombosis, or local thrombus formation around the device. Filter-induced flow disturbance and vessel-wall responses may contribute to local thrombosis, although direct mechanistic evidence in humans remains limited. Reported occurrence varies substantially because study populations, imaging schedules, and outcome definitions differ. Clinically detected caval thrombosis or thrombotic occlusion is uncommon in large databases and prospective cohorts. Planned imaging before retrieval, however, often detects small intrafilter thrombi, most of which are asymptomatic. Accordingly, the clinical importance of an imaging-detected thrombus depends on whether it is accompanied by meaningful caval obstruction or symptoms. Prevention should continue throughout the filter life cycle. Filters should be used only for a time-limited, evidence-based indication. Anticoagulation should be resumed when a separate indication persists and bleeding risk permits, and retrieval should be assessed once filter-mediated pulmonary embolism protection is no longer required. Structured follow-up can help prevent loss to care. Management of established thrombosis should be guided by symptoms, impaired caval outflow, thrombus progression and chronicity, bleeding risk, and the need for filter retrieval. Anticoagulation remains foundational when indicated for active venous thromboembolism. Catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, or combined treatment may be considered for selected symptomatic, progressive, or obstructive cases, but most supporting studies are nonrandomized. Future studies require standardized minimum reporting and patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: Hypoxemia and pulmonary infiltrates during T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody therapy: A pulmonary and critical care framework.
articles.abstract: T-cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have rapidly expanded treatment options for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, B-cell lymphomas, and small-cell lung cancer. Their off-the-shelf availability, step-up dosing, repeated administration, and migration into outpatient and community settings distinguish them from autologous chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. These same features increasingly bring patients to pulmonary and critical care teams. Patients receiving BsAbs may present with fever, hypoxemia, pulmonary infiltrates, pneumonia, cytokine release syndrome (CRS), secondary antibody deficiency, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, respiratory viral disease, pulmonary edema, pulmonary embolism, malignant pulmonary involvement, or suspected drug-induced lung injury. Existing guidelines provide essential CRS grading, rechallenge, and infection-prevention recommendations but do not fully address the bedside pulmonary differential diagnosis, indications for bronchoscopy, ventilatory escalation, or intensive care unit (ICU) triage. This focused narrative review synthesizes pivotal trials, current prescribing information, consensus statements, real-world studies, and pulmonary literature. We emphasize two overlapping risk windows: early step-up dosing, in which CRS and infection must be evaluated and treated in parallel, and later or prolonged therapy, in which infection, target-specific immune deficits, and noninfectious mimics become dominant considerations. A timed approach using oxygen trajectory, computed tomography pattern, host immune deficits, microbiologic data, and selective bronchoscopy may reduce diagnostic anchoring and improve multidisciplinary care.

articles.title: Applicability and parameter optimization of the SASNIP algorithm for background subtraction of gamma spectra measured with NaI(Tl) detectors.
articles.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
articles.abstract: The accuracy of gamma spectrum background subtraction directly governs the reliability of radionuclide quantitative analysis. The step-approximation statistics-sensitive nonlinear iterative peak-clipping (SASNIP) algorithm has been verified for background removal of gamma spectra collected by high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors, yet its adaptability and optimal parameter configuration for low-resolution thallium-doped sodium iodide (NaI(Tl)) scintillation gamma spectra have not been systematically studied. In this paper, two groups of measured 152Eu gamma spectral datasets-original raw spectra with complex scattering backgrounds and scattering-corrected spectra after scattering component elimination-are employed to investigate how the two core parameters of SASNIP, namely the window width scaling coefficient t and iteration termination threshold, affect background subtraction accuracy. The mean absolute relative deviation (MARD) of net counting rates of multiple characteristic peaks and the standard deviation (SD) of absolute relative deviations were adopted as evaluation metrics for the accuracy of calculated net peak areas. Experimental results indicate that the window width scaling coefficient t dominates the overall background subtraction performance; quantification accuracy improves first and then deteriorates as t increases. When t is fixed, varying the iteration termination threshold does not lead to an obvious monotonic change in subtraction accuracy. Although raw spectra and scattering-corrected spectra differ greatly in background complexity, the optimal parameter combination applicable to both datasets is unified: scaling coefficient t = 0.8 and iteration termination threshold of 0.5%. This work confirms that the SASNIP algorithm achieves stable, accurate background stripping for NaI(Tl) gamma spectra.

articles.title: An inversion-forward method for γ-ray spectrum background subtraction based on the ML-EM inversion algorithm.
articles.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
articles.abstract: γ-ray spectrum analysis is one of the widely used techniques in the field of nuclear radiation detection. Background subtraction from γ-ray spectra can improve the quantitative accuracy of γ-emitting radionuclides. To address the limitation of traditional methods in accurately subtracting backgrounds from complex γ-ray spectra, particularly those containing overlapping peaks, this paper proposes an inversion-forward method for γ-ray spectrum background subtraction based on the Maximum Likelihood-Expectation Maximization (ML-EM) inversion algorithm. A 4″ × 4″×16″ thallium-doped sodium iodide (NaI(Tl)) detector was used to acquire γ-ray spectra containing information from 241Am, 137Cs, 60Co, 152Eu, 133Ba, and 22Na. Focusing on 241Am, 137Cs, and 60Co while treating the other nuclides as interference sources, the proposed method was applied for background subtraction. The results were compared with those obtained using the Maestro32 software and the Statistics-sensitive Nonlinear Iterative Peak-clipping (SNIP) method. The results demonstrate that the background subtraction accuracy of the proposed method is significantly superior to the other two methods. After background subtraction, the maximum absolute deviation of the calculated activities of 241Am, 137Cs, and 60Co (where the 241Am characteristic peak overlaps with that of 133Ba, and the 60Co characteristic peaks overlap with those of 152Eu, 133Ba, and 22Na) from the reference values is only 5.6%, compared to 48.8% for Maestro32 and 72.5% for the SNIP method.

articles.title: High-fidelity Monte Carlo dosimetry of radiosensitive organs in head and neck CT: A virtual TLD study with comprehensive statistical uncertainty analysis.
articles.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify absorbed doses to six critical head and neck organs (occipital lobe, temporal lobe, hypothalamus, thalamus, parotid gland, and both eyes) during head CT using high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulation as an ethical alternative to in vivo dosimetry.

METHODS: A voxelized phantom was generated from DICOM images of the RANDO phantom. A realistic X-ray tube (135 kVp) was modeled in GEANT4 (v11.1.3) to simulate clinical head CT protocols. Seventy-four virtual GR-200 thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs) were placed at predefined organ coordinates, and 2 × 108 primary photons were tracked. Descriptive statistics (mean, SD, SEM, 95% CI, CV%) and non-parametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis followed by Mann-Whitney U with Bonferroni correction) were applied to the raw dose distributions.

RESULTS: The parotid gland received the highest mean dose (25.83 mGy) and the right eye the lowest (19.10 mGy). The temporal lobe exhibited the smallest variability (CV = 0.39%), while the right eye showed the largest (CV = 11.52%). The Kruskal-Wallis test revealed highly significant differences among organs (H = 62.34, p = 1.5 × 10-11). Pairwise comparisons indicated that the parotid gland dose was significantly higher than both eyes (p ≈ 3.2 × 10-4), whereas no significant difference existed between the two eyes (p = 0.86) or between occipital and temporal lobes (p = 0.43). Dose ratios relative to the thalamus ranged from 0.824 (right eye) to 1.114 (parotid gland).

CONCLUSION: The statistically robust organ-dose estimates validate the GEANT4-based model and align with previous experimental data. Monte Carlo simulation with strategically placed virtual TLDs offers a powerful, ethical tool for precise dose assessment, providing a valuable reference for protocol optimization and radiation protection in head and neck CT.

articles.title: Upadacitinib for the Management of Atopic Dermatitis in Patients Aged ≥60 Years: A Long-Term Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) in the elderly is increasing worldwide and presents therapeutic challenges due to age-related comorbidities that often contraindicate systemic therapies. Although oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors show efficacy in moderate-to-severe AD, older adult patients are underrepresented in clinical trials, and regulators recommend caution in this population.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, observational study at 15 Italian university hospitals, including patients with moderate-to-severe AD aged ≥60 years treated with upadacitinib 15 or 30 mg once daily, to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of this selective JAK1 inhibitor at weeks 16, 32, 52, and 104.

RESULTS: Seventy-two patients were included (mean age 65.9 ± 6.4 years); 48/72 (66.7%) of patients showed a classical flexural phenotype; 34/72 (47.2%) presented with head-and-neck involvement. Upadacitinib led to marked and sustained improvement in both clinician-and-patient-reported outcomes, with mean Eczema Area and Severity Index decreasing from 23.9 ± 9.2 at baseline to 1.5 ± 3.0 at week 52 and 0.9 ± 2.5 at week 104. Mean itch-Numeric Rating Scales (NRS) decreased from 8.2 ± 2.0 at baseline to 1.0 ± 1.9 at week 52 and 1.0 ± 2.4 at week 104, with concomitant amelioration in sleep-NRS (6.5 ± 3.1 to 0.5 ± 1.6 and 0.3 ± 1.3) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (16.8 ± 6.9 to 1.6 ± 4.2 and 1.0 ± 3.2). Adverse events occurred in 37/72 (51,4%) patients and included dyslipidemia in 22/72 (30.6%) patients, creatine phosphokinase elevation in 15/72 (20.8%), and blood count abnormalities in 13/72 (18.1%); they were mostly mild and manageable. Overall, 16/72 patients (22.2%) discontinued treatment, including 11/72 (15.3%) due to AEs.

CONCLUSIONS: In our multicenter real-world cohort of patients aged ≥60 years, upadacitinib demonstrated rapid, sustained efficacy and an overall favorable safety profile through 104 weeks, supporting its long-term use in clinical practice with appropriate monitoring.

articles.title: Bronchoscopic phenotypes and anatomical airway involvement in invasive tracheobronchial aspergillosis without classic immunosuppression: association with in-hospital mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic relevance of visual bronchoscopic phenotyping and airway lesion extent in invasive tracheobronchial aspergillosis (ITBA) without classic immunosuppression remains unclear. This study aimed to describe the clinical, radiological and bronchoscopic features of ITBA, and to evaluate the association between visual bronchoscopic assessment and in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at National Lung Hospital in Hanoi, Vietnam, from January 2023 to December 2025. Adult patients with histopathologically proven ITBA lacking classic immunosuppressive factors were included. On bronchoscopy, patients were dichotomised by the predominance of pseudomembranes and an airway involvement score was calculated to assess the extent of the lesions.

RESULTS: The study included 31 patients with proven ITBA (mean age 61.4 years; 83.9% male). Diabetes (41.9%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (29.0%) were the most common comorbidities, and 16.1% of the cohort were immunocompetent. Bronchoscopy revealed the pseudomembranous phenotype in 61.3% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 29.0%. While the pseudomembranous phenotype was more frequent among deceased patients than survivors (88.9% vs. 50.0%), this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.101). In contrast, deceased patients had a significantly higher median airway involvement score (3 points vs. 2 points; p = 0.007), indicating more extensive disease. No major procedural complications occurred.

CONCLUSION: ITBA can manifest in patients without classic immunosuppression. Beyond the diagnostic utility, bronchoscopy may provide prognostic relevance for this selected cohort, particularly through evaluation of the anatomical extent of airway involvement, rather than visual bronchoscopic phenotyping.

articles.title: Telemonitoring for high-risk pregnancies (PregnaDigit EU): an international hybrid type 2 study protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Healthcare systems worldwide are under increasing pressure from workforce shortages, rising costs and growing demands for care. Obstetric care is also affected because high-risk pregnancies require frequent in-hospital monitoring. This strains the healthcare system and reduces the quality of life for patients. Telemonitoring offers a promising solution by shifting care from hospital to home, thereby addressing these demands without compromising care quality. Despite demonstrated benefits, implementation remains limited due to challenges not anticipated in controlled research settings. Aiming to facilitate international implementation of telemonitoring as the new standard of care, we established the PregnaDigit EU consortium. In this consortium, we investigate clinical outcomes, patient experience, healthcare consumption and implementation of telemonitoring in high-risk pregnancies across four European hospitals. Ultimately, our goal is to ensure that pregnancy care remains accessible to all while reducing pressure on the healthcare system.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multicentre, prospective, hybrid type 2 implementation study is performed at four tertiary centres in three European countries: University Medical Centre Utrecht and Erasmus Medical Centre Rotterdam in the Netherlands, Vall d’Hebron University Hospital in Spain and Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden. This study design allows for the simultaneous evaluation of clinical and implementation outcomes of telemonitoring. Eligible participants are ≥18 years with a singleton pregnancy and gestational age of at least 24+0 weeks requiring frequent cardiotocography (CTG) monitoring for a high-risk pregnancy according to local protocols. The telemonitoring care pathway comprises self-recorded home CTG and blood pressure measurements, which are reviewed by trained professionals who provide same-day feedback and clinical management via teleconsultation. Additionally, the care pathway includes standardised outpatient care and additional assessments, such as ultrasounds and laboratory testing, per local protocol. The primary clinical outcome is a composite of adverse perinatal and maternal events. Secondary clinical outcomes include all individual components of the primary clinical outcome, additional adverse perinatal events and healthcare consumption outcomes. The primary implementation outcomes are assessed using the taxonomy of Proctor et al during three sequential phases: pre-implementation, implementation and post implementation. In the post implementation phase, care pathways before and after telemonitoring implementation are mapped using Metro maps as the foundation for a Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing analysis. For data analysis, clinical outcomes are summarised by descriptive statistics. Implementation outcomes are compared across countries and inclusion groups, which are reported as relative risks with 95% CIs. A p value <0.05 is considered statistically significant.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval was waived in the Netherlands following an independent quality assessment in the University Medical Centre Utrecht. In the Vall d’Hebron University Hospital, the study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee (PR(AMI)455/2024). In Karolinska University Hospital, the study protocol was approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (2024–08685-02/2024-04982-01/2025-01056-02).

articles.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a remote blood pressure monitoring pharmacist-led telehealth programme in an emergency department transition care clinic: a pilot randomised controlled trial.
Cost-effectiveness of adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy for fibromyalgia: an economic evaluation alongside a single-centre randomised controlled trial in Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibromyalgia is a chronic, polysymptomatic syndrome associated with widespread pain, fatigue, functional impairment and a substantial economic burden. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy has demonstrated neuromodulatory, anti-inflammatory and neuroplastic effects in clinical and preclinical studies; however, no prior evaluation has examined its cost-effectiveness in the treatment of fibromyalgia.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the cost-effectiveness of hyperbaric oxygen therapy as an adjunct to standardised clinical care for fibromyalgia in Brazil, using data from a randomised clinical trial and deterministic economic model.

DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: A cost-effectiveness evaluation was conducted alongside a single-centre, assessor-blinded, sequential-group, randomised clinical trial at the Department of Rheumatology at Juiz de Fora Federal University in Brazil, applying a 4-month decision-tree model and deterministic sensitivity analyses. The subjects were 56 women aged 18 to 70 years with a diagnosis of fibromyalgia according to the 2016 revisions of the American College of Rheumatology criteria. The intention-to-treat analysis included all participants.

INTERVENTIONS: Standardised clinical management combined with hyperbaric oxygen therapy at 2.3 atmospheres absolute for 90 min, 5 sessions per week for 32 to 40 sessions. The early start group received the intervention during weeks 0–8, and the delayed start group during weeks 8–16.

OUTCOMES: Direct medical and non-medical costs: quality-adjusted life-years derived from utilities obtained through deterministic mapping of the 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey to the European Quality of Life 5 Dimensions instrument using Brazilian valuation weights.

RESULTS: At 8 weeks, the mean total costs were US$1068.46 for standardised care and US$2477.59 for hyperbaric oxygen therapy, with utilities of 0.477 and 0.630, respectively. The incremental cost was US$1409.13 for a gain of 0.153 quality-adjusted life-years, yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of US$9210 per quality-adjusted life-year. At 16 weeks, the costs increased to US$2136.93 for standardised care and US$3546.06 for hyperbaric oxygen therapy, with utilities of 0.477 and 0.642, respectively. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio improved to US$8540 per quality-adjusted life-year, reflecting an incremental gain of 0.165 quality-adjusted life-years. Both incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were below the Brazilian willingness-to-pay threshold of US$9315 per quality-adjusted life-year, although the 8-week estimate was only marginally below this threshold. Deterministic sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness, with treatment costs and utility gains exerting the most significant influence on model outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Within the assumptions of this deterministic analysis, hyperbaric oxygen therapy added to standardised clinical management met the Brazilian cost-effectiveness criterion for fibromyalgia from the healthcare provider perspective, although it was not a dominant strategy and the 8-week estimate was close to the applied threshold. Multicentre evaluations incorporating directly measured utilities, probabilistic modelling and longer time horizons are warranted.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee and assigned the number 53058421.9.0000.5133 (Version 4).

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: This study was registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials under RBR-6prps8g, with a Universal Trial Number of U1111-1278-3224.

articles.title: Health literacy level and influencing factors among the French Scleroderma Association (ASF) members: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Health literacy (HL) refers to the ability to access, evaluate, apply and communicate information to promote, maintain and improve one’s health. Our primary objective was to assess HL level among the French Scleroderma Association (ASF) members using two validated questionnaires, FCCHL14 (Functional, Communicative and Critical Health Literacy scale 14) and HLS-EU16 (European Health Literacy Survey Questionnaire). The secondary objectives were to identify factors associated with HL and to explore the correlation between the two HL questionnaires.

DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional study based on self-administered online questionnaires.

SETTING: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) patients were recruited among adherent members to the ASF, via their electronic newsletter.

PARTICIPANTS: We included ASF members who completed the study and both self-administered HL questionnaires, provided that they had no more than two missing answers on each form. This represented 296 patients of whom 89% were women with an average age of 63.

INTERVENTIONS: The questionnaires were available online for 3.5 months. The total estimated time to answer the 57 questions was about 35 min. Anonymous data were collected using LimeSurvey software.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Descriptive analyses were performed to assess the population characteristics and the HL level. The FCCHL14 questionnaire was interpreted as a continuous variable whereas HLS-EU16 score determined three levels of HL (insufficient, average and satisfactory). Comparisons were made between HL scores based on patient characteristics. Secondary, potential associated factors were included in a multivariate analysis with an alpha threshold at 0.05. Spearman’s correlation coefficient was used to state correlation between the two HL scores.

RESULTS: The studied population demonstrated an excellent proficiency in French language for 69% of cases, a high level of education for 64% and high social status for 48%. Patients were mainly followed at an expert centre in autoimmune diseases (58%). The FCCHL14 questionnaire indicated an excellent global, FCCHL with a mean global score of 11.3/15. HLS-EU-Q16 showed insufficient HL in 26.7%, average in 30.4% and satisfactory in 43%. FCCHL14 score was higher among women (p=0.034), people declaring affluent social status (p=0.028) and with a higher study level (p<0.01). HL according to HLS-EU-Q16 was associated with an excellent social status (p=0.044), proficiency in French (p=0.018) and level of information about SSc (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, ASF members had adequate HL level assessed with two French validated HL questionnaires. A better HL was associated with female sex, a good social status, higher study level and an excellent French language skill. Moreover, adequate HL was associated with a high level of knowledge about SSc and with a follow-up in expert centres. This study has recruitment and self-selection biases since it only concerns patients who are ASF members and, by definition, motivated to learn more on their disease, and with access to a high level of information. Thus, these results cannot be generalised to the entire population suffering from SSc in France.

articles.title: Multidimensional evaluation of AI for integrated panvascular disease management: benchmarking against consensus guidelines on lipid, metabolic and antithrombotic therapy (2024-2025).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of large language models (LLMs) in the comprehensive management (CM) of panvascular disease (PVD) across dimensions of language complexity, comprehensibility, actionability and information reliability.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional benchmark evaluation study using a standardised clinical question bank derived from Chinese expert consensus statements on PVD management.

SETTING: Four mainstream LLMs (DeepSeek-V.3.2, Doubao-1.8, Kimi-K2 and Qwen3-Max) were evaluated using 50 standardised clinical questions covering dyslipidaemia management, metabolic regulation, antithrombotic therapy and CM. The evaluation was conducted using the publicly available versions of the models in January 2026.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcomes were differences among LLMs in nine validated readability metrics, including the Automated Readability Index, Flesch Reading Ease Score, Gunning Fog Index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, SMOG Index, Linsear Write, Dale-Chall Readability Score and Spache Readability Formula. Secondary outcomes included understandability, actionability and overall scores assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), information quality assessed using the DISCERN instrument, and correlations between readability and core evaluation metrics.

RESULTS: A total of 200 artificial intelligence (AI)-generated responses were included in the analysis. Significant differences were observed among the AI models across all four evaluation metrics (PEMAT-Understandability Score (PEMAT-U), PEMAT-Actionability Score, PEMAT-Total Score (PEMAT-T) and Mean DISCERN Score (M Dis Score); all p<0.001). Qwen3-Max achieved the highest median scores for PEMAT-U and PEMAT-T, whereas DeepSeek-V.3.2 achieved the highest median M Dis Score. Content category had a limited influence on evaluation outcomes, with an overall difference initially observed only for PEMAT-U; however, this difference was no longer significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction (FDR-adjusted p=0.136). Stratified analyses showed that intermodel differences were generally consistent across content categories, although the difference in PEMAT-U for the CM and cross-cutting issues category was no longer significant after FDR correction (FDR-adjusted p=0.052). Overall, model type was associated with substantial differences in PEMAT-P and DISCERN scores, whereas content category exerted a comparatively limited effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Mainstream LLMs generate structured management recommendations with varying characteristics across readability, understandability, actionability and information quality. As this study focused on structural and linguistic attributes rather than clinical accuracy, the conclusions are limited to instrument-based assessments. Future research should validate real-world clinical utility and patient comprehension to ensure safe AI integration.

articles.title: Cannabis legalisation and cardiovascular hospitalisations in the United States: nationwide difference-in-differences analysis, 2012-2018.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the association between legal recreational cannabis sales (hereafter ‘legalisation’) and cardiovascular hospitalisations. This study leverages a natural experiment wherein legalisation began earlier in the Western census region of the United States (January 2014) versus non-Western regions (November 2018).

DESIGN: Using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS), we performed a difference-in-differences analysis of the association between legalisation and hospitalisation rates for six cardiovascular diagnoses, a positive control (cannabis-related diagnoses) and two negative control diagnoses (opioid-related and urinary stones).

SETTING: US states before (2012–2013) and after (2014–2018) legalisation in the Western region

PARTICIPANTS: Hospitalised individuals in the Western region had a median age of 51 years, 57% were female and 43% were non-white. In other regions, the median age was 55 years, 57% were female and 33% were non-white.

EXPOSURE: Legal recreational cannabis sales.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASUREMENTS: Annual hospitalisations per capita for atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF), heart failure (HF), myocardial infarction (MI), ischaemic stroke, venous thromboembolism (VTE) and ventricular tachycardia (VT).

RESULTS: In this fully adjusted analysis, each year of legalisation was associated with the following relative change in hospitalisation rates expressed as change in the incidence rate ratio (∆IRR): cannabis-related diagnoses (∆IRR 1.138, 95% CI 1.066 to 1.214, p<0.001), AF (∆IRR 1.023, 95% CI 1.010 to 1.035, p<0.001), HF (∆IRR 1.037, 95% CI 1.029 to 1.046, p<0.001), MI (∆IRR 1.031, 95% CI 1.014 to 1.048, p<0.001), ischaemic stroke (∆IRR 1.011, 95% CI 0.999 to 1.024, p=0.078), VTE (∆IRR 1.009, 95% CI 0.999 to 1.020, p=0.066) and VT (∆IRR 1.019, 95% CI 0.993 to 1.046, p=0.161). For falsification testing, there was no change in hospitalisations for urinary stones (∆IRR 1.006, 95% CI 0.986 to 1.027, p=0.535) or opioid-related diagnoses (∆IRR 0.966, 95% CI 0.927 to 1.006, p=0.091).

CONCLUSIONS: Legalisation was associated with increased hospitalisations for AF, HF and MI. Global legalisation trends may result in epidemiologically and economically important increases in cardiovascular healthcare use.

articles.title: Developing a consensus patient safety curriculum for junior doctors in Taiwan: a modified Delphi protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While international frameworks guide patient safety education, their impact depends on local training structures and sociocultural context. In Taiwan, patient safety training has not yet been consolidated into a coherent curriculum, and hierarchical, blame-oriented norms may discourage incident reporting and learning. The aim of this research programme includes establishing expert consensus on the core content for a Taiwan-contextualised patient safety curriculum for junior doctors through an adapted Delphi study.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol outlines an online modified Delphi study with three phases: (1) document analysis of international frameworks to draft curriculum statements; (2) patient and public involvement and engagement to refine statement relevance and clarity; and (3) a multiround Delphi survey. Phases I and II were completed as preparatory phases to develop the Delphi questionnaire for use in Phase III. Phase III is underway, and we are inviting 80–100 multidisciplinary experts in Taiwan, anticipating 11–30 respondents in the final round. Expert panellists are rating statements with free-text comments. Between rounds, controlled feedback will provide summary statistics and analysis of free-text comments to inform subsequent ratings. Consensus was prespecified as median ≥4 and IQR ≤1, supported by ≥70% of respondents rating 4–5. If a consensus is not reached, a further round will be conducted. Free-text data will be analysed qualitatively to support interpretation and implementation considerations.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approvals for the consensus survey were obtained in the UK and Taiwan. Outputs will include endorsed curriculum content and implementation insights to guide future curriculum development. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conferences.

articles.title: Real-world comparison of jak inhibitors and TNF inhibitor cycling in axial spondyloarthritis patients after TNFi failure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study compared drug survival and clinical outcomes between tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) cycling and switching to a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) patients after initial TNFi failure.

METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal observational cohort study included 123 axSpA patients fulfilling the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) criteria, followed in a tertiary rheumatology clinic. After failure of the first TNFi, patients were directed to either a second TNFi or a JAKi based on clinical evaluation. Notably, JAKi therapy was considered for patients with inadequate response to one or two prior TNFi agents. Drug survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and group comparisons were made using the log-rank test.

RESULTS: Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly shorter drug survival in the JAKi group compared to the TNFi group (p < 0.001). In the TNFi group, higher CRP levels were associated with prolonged drug survival (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.83-0.99; p = 0.035), while primary non-response to the first TNFi predicted earlier discontinuation of the second TNFi (HR: 2.1; 95% CI: 1.08-3.14; p = 0.033). In the JAKi group, prior failure of two different TNFi agents was associated with a lower risk of discontinuation (HR: 0.04; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: Following prior TNFi failure, TNFi cycling was associated with longer observed drug survival compared with JAKi therapy. However, given the retrospective design and differences in prior treatment exposure, this finding should be interpreted as a descriptive real-world observation rather than definitive evidence of comparative effectiveness. JAK inhibitors may still represent a viable option for selected refractory patients with multiple prior TNFi failures.

articles.title: Azygos Venous Pressure and Respiratory Modulation of CSF-Venous Pressure Gradients in SIH and IIH patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The azygos system is a major drainage pathway of the thoracic spinal venous network and may participate in the regulation of spinal CSF resorption. CSF-pressure disorders such as spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) related to a CSF-venous fistula (CSFVF) and idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) could therefore be influenced by the hemodynamics and the pressure of this system. However, azygos pressure and its respiratory modulation remain poorly characterized.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 54 consecutive patients who underwent combined venous and CSF pressure measurements between September 2025 and February 2026. Forty-five patients were investigated for SIH/CSFVF and 9 for IIH. Pressures were recorded in the azygos system, intracranial venous sinuses, right atrium (CVP), and lumbar CSF compartment. Dynamic measurements were obtained during resisted inspiration, breath holding, and Valsalva. Values are reported as mean ± SD or median [IQR], as appropriate. Paired respiratory changes were assessed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

RESULTS: Overall, median azygos pressure was 8.0 [6.0-9.8] mm Hg and was modestly but significantly higher than CVP: 6.5 [4.0-8.0] mm Hg; median paired difference, +2.0 [1.0-3.0] mm Hg; p < .001. Azygos pressure did not differ significantly between SIH/CSFVF and IIH groups: 8.0 [6.0-9.0] versus 9.0 [8.0-10.0] mm Hg; p = .34. Level-by-level measurements in 25 patients showed only limited cranial pressure decline, with median pressure of 8.0 [6.0-9.0] mm Hg in the caudal L2-T10 segment and 7.0 [5.0-8.0] mm Hg in the cranial T9-T5 segment; p = .007. Resisted inspiration produced the largest CSF-azygos gradient, increasing from 0.0 [-3.0 to 5.0] to 12.0 [11.0-15.0] mm Hg, primarily because azygos pressure decreased from 7.0 to -6.0 mm Hg while CSF pressure remained stable.

CONCLUSIONS: In the investigated population, median azygos pressure was 8mmHg, close to CVP, and stable along the spinal axis. Resisted inspiration markedly increased the CSF-azygos gradient by lowering azygos pressure, providing a hemodynamic explanation for improved CSF-venous fistula conspicuity during resisted-inspiration myelography.

Defending the drip: the case for intravenous fluids in severe acute malnutrition.
Validation and modification of a short-term survival index using shock index and consciousness in terminal cancer patients: a multicentre prospective cohort study.
Acute ward culture can delay transitions to comfort-focused care for dying patients.
Therapeutic-dose enoxaparin for suspected deep vein thrombosis in the immediate post-caesarean period complicated by severe wound haemorrhage: the role of protamine sulfate in a clinical dilemma.
Dual biological therapy in a patient with severe asthma and nasal polyposis.
Obstructive cholestasis without biliary dilatation from a hepatic cyst.
articles.abstract: Simple hepatic cysts are usually benign and asymptomatic but may rarely cause cholestasis from biliary compression. We report a man in his 70s with a recurrent large haemorrhagic hepatic cyst who developed right upper quadrant pain, early satiety, dark urine and marked obstructive-pattern liver injury despite repeated CT and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography showing no intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Percutaneous aspiration produced partial biochemical improvement, but symptoms and cholestasis persisted with cyst recurrence. Definitive robotic cyst fenestration resulted in rapid improvement and sustained resolution of hyperbilirubinaemia at follow-up. This case highlights that cyst-related biliary obstruction may be clinically and biochemically significant even without ductal dilatation on imaging. In patients with compatible symptoms, cholestatic liver chemistry abnormalities and a cyst anatomically capable of biliary compression, absence of ductal dilatation should not exclude cyst-related obstruction.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 uPAR PET/CT in Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer shows wide variability in outcomes after curative-intent resection. 18F-FDG PET/CT is indispensable for staging but primarily reflects glucose metabolism rather than the invasion-related tumor biology that may contribute to recurrence. 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 PET/CT images the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface mediator of local invasion and metastatic spread. We assessed whether preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT is prognostic for postoperative recurrence. Methods: We conducted a single-center cohort study of patients with resectable lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were prospectively enrolled to undergo preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT in addition to standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor SUVmean and SUVmax were measured for both tracers, and tumor tissue uPAR expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry (H-score). Postoperative recurrence was the primary endpoint and was analyzed in a competing-risks framework with death as a competing event. The primary prognostic analyses evaluated 68Ga-uPAR SUVs, 18F-FDG SUVs, and uPAR H-score as continuous variables using univariable cause-specific Cox models. A 1.5-y horizon was used for exploratory Youden-derived high versus low groups, for which cumulative incidence of recurrence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Trial registration number is NCT02755675 Results: Thirty-seven patients comprised the analysis cohort, of whom 14 developed recurrence during a median follow-up of 2.38 y (interquartile range, 1.97-8.20 y). Four patients died without prior recurrence. 68Ga-uPAR uptake correlated with tumor tissue uPAR expression, whereas 18F-FDG uptake did not. As continuous prognostic factors, higher 68Ga-uPAR SUVmax (hazard ratio, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.34-3.49; P = 0.002) and higher uPAR H-score (hazard ratio, 1.04 per unit; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; P = 0.017) were associated with recurrence; 68Ga-uPAR SUVmean showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.053), whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic. Exploratory 1.5-y threshold analyses showed greater early recurrence in the high SUVmean and high H-score groups; the SUVmax comparison did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion: Preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET uptake reflected tumor uPAR expression and was associated with early postoperative recurrence, whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic in this cohort. These findings suggest that uPAR PET captures invasion-related tumor biology that is not fully reflected by glucose metabolism imaging. External validation is required.

articles.title: Head-to-Head Comparison of 18F-SynVest-1 PET and 18F-FDG PET in the Differentiation of Patients with Cognitive Decline.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Although 18F-FDG PET is commonly used in the differential diagnosis of cognitive decline, synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A PET may offer a more direct assessment of synaptic integrity and address limitations associated with 18F-FDG, such as sensitivity to sensory stimuli and glycemic variations. In this study, a head-to-head comparison of 18F-SynVesT-1 and 18F-FDG was performed for differentiating causes of cognitive decline in a tertiary clinical setting. Methods: Patients with cognitive decline referred for 18F-FDG PET were recruited to undergo 18F-SynVesT-1 PET/MRI (49 ± 26 d after 18F-FDG PET). Diagnosis was determined by routine clinical follow-up (median, 11 mo) and classified as Alzheimer disease (AD), frontotemporal degeneration (FTD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), other neurodegenerative disorders (ONDs), or nonneurodegenerative disorders (NoNDs). Volume-wise and voxelwise semiquantitative analyses were performed using tracer-specific healthy volunteers. Diagnostic accuracy for both tracers was evaluated through logistic regression and by consensus from 3 readers. Noninferiority was defined by an area-under-the-curve margin (ΔAUC) of -0.10 within a 95% CI, using the clinical follow-up diagnosis as the gold standard. Results: Ninety-four patients were included: 44 with AD, 12 with FTD, 4 with DLB, 5 with ONDs, and 29 with NoNDs. Volume-wise and voxelwise analyses showed that, in patients with AD and DLB, reductions in the temporoparietal and precuneus/posterior cingulate were less pronounced with 18F-SynVesT-1 PET than with 18F-FDG PET (e.g., posterior cingulate in AD, -10% vs. -20%). In FTD, the most impacted areas showed greater variability, typically affecting the anterior temporal and frontal cortices, depending on the FTD subtype. Visual assessment showed lower sensitivity for AD with 18F-SynVesT-1 PET than with 18F-FDG PET (0.57 vs. 0.73) with equal specificity (0.76), whereas quantitative analysis yielded a lower area under the curve (0.71 vs. 0.81; ΔAUC, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.21 to 0.01). For FTD, 18F-SynVesT-1 visual classification yielded similar sensitivity and specificity (0.58 and 0.90) compared with 18F-FDG (0.50 and 0.93) but a lower quantitative area under the curve (0.64 vs. 0.76; ΔAUC, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.27 to 0.04). Conclusion: 18F-SynVesT-1 PET enabled accurate classification of disease-specific patterns of cognitive decline. Although classification performance for FTD was similar to that of 18F-FDG PET, the lower effect size in neocortical binding resulted in lower sensitivity for AD. Larger study samples are needed to formally evaluate tracer noninferiority in this clinical context for all subgroups.

articles.title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

articles.title: Clinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

articles.title: Preclinical PET Imaging of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Tumors with Heterogeneous HER2 Expression.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has clinical activity in human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low and -ultralow tumors in addition to HER2-positive tumors. However, no consistent correlation has been observed between traditional HER2 scoring criteria and response to T-DXd in HER2-low and HER2-ultralow tumors. There is a need for complementary approaches to monitor T-DXd delivery in vivo and potentially improve understanding of which tumors may benefit from T-DXd therapy. This study evaluated tumor uptake of radiolabeled T-DXd in tumors with varying HER2 protein levels using PET in treatment-naïve tumors and during T-DXd therapy. Methods: Chelator-conjugated T-DXd or trastuzumab was prepared via conventional lysine conjugation and radiolabeled with 64Cu. The binding and in vitro cytotoxicity of the conjugates were determined in cancer cell lines. PET/CT was performed across 11 tumor models (representing 5 tumor types), including cell xenografts, patient-derived xenografts, and syngeneic models in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Image-based tumor uptake of the radiolabeled antibodies was quantified in all models. In the treatment studies, mice bearing CT26-hHER2 tumors that express heterogeneous HER2 with an immunohistochemistry score of 2+ levels received weekly coinjections of therapeutic T-DXd (6 mg/kg) together with imaging-dose [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd (4 mg/kg), corresponding to a total T-DXd administered dose of 10 mg/kg. Results: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd was obtained at a radiochemical purity of at least 98%. Purified [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd bound to cells in a concentration-dependent manner and had a positive correlation between HER2 protein levels and bound T-DXd. Conjugation of T-DXd to NOTA did not affect T-DXd binding or cytotoxicity in cancer cells. [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd mean tumor uptake varied across models (7.45 ± 1.28 to 19.10 ± 2.50 %ID/mL), and the mean uptake was similar to that of the parental antibody 64Cu-labeled trastuzumab. Preimaging doses of either trastuzumab or pertuzumab did not affect [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake in tumors. There was a positive correlation between the change in [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake and the change in tumor volume between weeks 1 and 2 of T-DXd treatment (P < 0.01) in CT26.hHER2 tumors grown in immunocompetent mice. Conclusion: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd PET detects antibody-drug accumulation in tumors with low HER2 protein levels and may provide an early imaging biomarker associated with response. These studies show the potential of using HER2-targeted imaging in preclinical models to noninvasively assess antibody-drug conjugate delivery and explore imaging-based biomarkers associated with T-DXd response.

articles.title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth.

RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

articles.title: AD-Smart: Alzheimer's trial will test diabetes and ADHD drugs on patients.
Electrode-Modiolar Distance as a Determinant of Cochlear Implant Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the relationship between electrode-modiolar distance (EMD) and cochlear implant (CI) performance across speech/perceptual, electrophysiological and programming outcomes and to characterize the dose-response effect of EMD.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Human studies reporting CT- or CBCT-derived EMD and CI outcomes were included. Effect sizes were transformed to odds ratios (ORs) and pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup, sensitivity and dose-response analyses were performed. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies comprising approximately 1181 implanted ears were included. Reduced EMD was associated with significantly higher odds of favourable CI outcomes (pooled OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 1.89-2.45; p < 0.001; I2 = 0%). Consistent effects were observed for speech/perceptual outcomes (OR = 2.23), electrophysiological measures (OR = 2.80 after sensitivity adjustment) and programming parameters (OR = 1.72). Dose-response modelling demonstrated a monotonic gradient, with each 1 mm increase in EMD associated with a 20%-30% reduction in the odds of favourable outcomes (OR per mm ≈0.72; p < 0.001). No significant publication bias was detected (Egger's p = 0.056).

CONCLUSION: Electrode-modiolar proximity is a strong and consistent determinant of CI performance with a clear dose-response relationship, supporting its role as a clinically actionable imaging biomarker for optimizing electrode selection, surgical strategy and individualized programming.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420261380236.

Gut Health Claims and Monetization Features on TikTok: Cross-Sectional Analysis.
articles.journal: Online journal of public health informatics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: TikTok has emerged as a major source of health information, yet concerns persist regarding content accuracy and monetization features. Gut health content is particularly vulnerable to misinformation.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the relationship between creator profession ("medical" vs "nonmedical") and the quality of gut health claims and monetization features on TikTok.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study screening 412 unique TikTok creator accounts identified using the keywords "guthealth," "gutcleansing," and "digestion." The final sample included 174 publicly accessible individual creators with at least 5000 followers and identifiable, relevant profession information. One video per creator was analyzed. Creator profession was categorized as medical or nonmedical, and health claim quality was coded as high, moderate, or poor. Monetization features (Showcase, Subscription, and external links) were assessed.

RESULTS: Nonmedical creators were more likely than medical creators to present poor- or moderate-quality health claims (adjusted prevalence ratio 2.33, 95% CI 1.50-3.62). Most creators (160/174, 92%) exhibited at least 1 monetization feature, and Showcase use was greater among nonmedical creators (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.57, 95% CI 1.02-2.42). Videos containing moderate- and poor-quality health claims received 3 times the expected likes as videos containing high-quality claims.

CONCLUSIONS: Among the sampled creators, nonmedical creators were more likely to present poor- or moderate-quality gut health claims, and lower-quality claims were associated with higher like counts. These findings highlight a misalignment between information quality and like counts on social media.

articles.title: Co-Designing a Digital Platform for the Management of Modifiable Risk Factors and Comorbidities in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: Mixed Methods Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical guidelines recommend integrated, person-centered care with control of modifiable risk factors and coexisting conditions in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but many receive insufficient risk factor management. Digital health technologies may provide valuable support in addressing this gap.

OBJECTIVE: Our aim was to evaluate the usability of a co-designed digital platform for supporting person-centered management of modifiable risk factors in individuals with AF.

METHODS: This mixed methods usability study was conducted at a tertiary university hospital in Sweden between March and April 2025. Eligible participants with AF were recruited to evaluate the co-designed digital platform using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and semistructured interviews analyzed with inductive manifest content analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 22 patients were included (mean age 67.7, SD 7.6 y); 32% (7/22) were female, the mean BMI was 27.7 (SD 3.6) kg/m2, 65% (14/22) had paroxysmal AF, 36% (8/22) had persistent AF, and the median AF duration was 26 (IQR 13.3-72.8) months. Relevant comorbidities were hypertension (17/22, 77%), heart failure (8/22, 36%), diabetes mellitus type 2 (3/22, 14%), and ischemic heart disease (4/22, 18%). Usability was rated high, with a median SUS score of 78.8 (IQR 63.8-86.9), indicating above-average user acceptance. Participants' requirements were summarized into 4 main categories and 10 subcategories. First, they valued a clear layout, simple design, and easy navigation. Second, they appreciated positive content, which is informative, inclusive, and motivating. Third, they requested personalized information on different aspects and provided on different levels. Fourth, they desired individualized medical recommendations that are personalized and flexible but open to individual choice.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants found the usability acceptable and valued specifically a clear layout, positive content, personalized information, and individualized medical recommendations.

articles.title: Auditory Biofeedback Gait Training in Individuals With Chronic Ankle Instability: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) develops in a large majority of patients with lateral ankle sprain (LAS), who often experience recurring injuries, residual feelings of instability, and abnormal neuromuscular patterns. Specifically, gait alterations are common in those with CAI and considered a contributing factor to poor long-term ankle joint health. Yet, there are no evidence-based gait-training protocols targeted to improve biomechanics, which may improve long-term outcomes related to ankle joint health and patient satisfaction.

OBJECTIVE: This study protocol introduces a progressive auditory biofeedback (ABF) gait-training program aimed to improve short- and long-term lower extremity biomechanics and talar cartilage outcomes and reduce the frequency of ankle-giving-way episodes and recurring injuries.

METHODS: This study is a multisite randomized controlled trial (RCT) with a target enrollment of 100 patients with CAI into a control group (n=50, 50%) or an ABF gait-training program (n=50, 50%). Both groups will complete a progressive 6-week (12-session) protocol comprising walking, ruck marching, and running on a treadmill. Lower extremity kinematics and kinetics, talar cartilage characteristics (via ultrasonography), self-perceived dysfunction and instability, and number of recurring sprains will be assessed prior to intervention, immediately after intervention, and 6 and 12 months postintervention. Finally, the frequency of ankle-giving-way episodes in the 6 months prior to intervention will be compared to the frequency of episodes at the 6- and 12-month time points to determine a longitudinal difference in ankle-giving-way episodes.

RESULTS: The study was funded in September 2024 and prospectively registered through ClinicalTrials.gov on March 10, 2025. The first participant was enrolled in May 2025. As of August 2026, 118 individuals had been recruited and 19 participants enrolled. Recruitment will remain open until September 2027, and study completion is expected in September 2028. Data processing is projected to continue through September 2028, with the final report published in June 2029.

CONCLUSIONS: This study will be the first RCT of ABF gait training to assess the immediate and long-term effects on lower extremity biomechanics, ankle joint health, and patient-reported outcomes in patients with CAI. Results from this study will advance the knowledge of long-term joint health that may be associated with poor outcomes post-LAS.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06868316; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06868316.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107775.

articles.title: Fingered Citron Extract Ameliorates Diabetes-Related Depression via Targeting SRC-Mediated Insulin Signaling and Neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Diabetes-related depression (DD) is a challenging comorbidity characterized by self-reinforcing interactions between metabolic dysfunction and affective disturbance, while conventional antidepressants and glucose-lowering drugs often yield suboptimal outcomes with adverse effects. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of fingered citron extract (FCE), traditionally used for metabolic and inflammatory conditions, in alleviating DD and elucidated its underlying mechanisms. Using a DD mouse model induced by high-fat diet, streptozotocin, and chronic unpredictable mild stress, we administered FCE at varying doses and employed a multimodal approach including behavioral tests, biochemical assays, UPLC-MS/MS, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and cellular validation. The results showed that FCE significantly reversed weight loss, reduced fasting blood glucose, and ameliorated depressive-like behaviors. It also restored 5-HT, DA, NE, and BDNF, lowered glutamate and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), and increased anti-inflammatory IL-10. UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified 34 serum-absorbed bioactive constituents, and integrated analyses highlighted neohesperidin (NH) and SRC as a candidate active constituent-target axis. FCE suppressed pancreatic SRC overactivation, improved pancreatic and brain insulin (INS) related signaling, and these molecular changes were associated with behavioral recovery. In vivo pharmacodynamic validation further showed that NH partially reproduced the metabolic, behavioral, and biochemical effects of FCE in DD mice. In high-glucose-induced MIN6 cells, NH enhanced insulin secretion, mitigated reactive oxygen species accumulation, and restored mitochondrial membrane potential, whereas these protective effects were markedly attenuated after SRC knockdown.
