Collectively, these findings suggest that FCE ameliorates DD, at least in part, through NH/SRC-mediated regulation of insulin signaling and neuroinflammation, supporting its potential as a multi-target natural therapeutic candidate for DD.

articles.title: Confocal microscopy-based radial profile analysis for submitochondrial protein localization.
articles.abstract: Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles whose functions depend on membrane proteins. Identifying whether proteins localize to the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) or inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) is important but often requires specialized techniques. Here, we developed a confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM)-based radial profile analysis for the localization of submitochondrial proteins. Based on this method, cytochrome c oxidase subunit 4 (COX4), adenine nucleotide translocase 2 (ANT2), mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and calcium-activated potassium channel subunit alpha-1(KCa1.1) signals were spatially distinct from translocase of outer mitochondrial membrane 20 (TOM20) signals in isolated mitochondria. Moreover, osmotic shock increased the apparent spatial separation between OMM- and IMM-associated signals, making it easier to distinguish translocase of inner mitochondrial membrane 23 (TIM23) or pore-forming subunit of the mitochondrial ATP-gated potassium channel (MITOK) signals from TOM20 signals in isolated mitochondria. Our approach provides a practical screening tool for assessing submitochondrial protein localization without specialized instrumentation or expertise.

articles.title: Measurement differences explain much of the variation in adherence and persistence after ischemic stroke, and standardized estimates are lower: a systematic review with meta-regression.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Continued use of secondary prevention medications after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack is an important component of long-term management. Reported estimates of adherence and persistence vary considerably across studies, limiting comparison and interpretability. Although some variation may reflect differences in patient behavior, inconsistencies in operational definitions and measurement approaches are also likely to contribute. We sought to examine sources of heterogeneity and to derive standardized estimates using a common reference measurement framework.

STUDY DESIGN AND SETTING: We searched bibliographic databases, dissertations, and trial registries from inception to September 10, 2025, for routine-care studies reporting adherence or persistence to secondary prevention medications after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. Cutoff-based proportions were extracted. We used 3-level hierarchical Bayesian models to characterize heterogeneity and multivariable meta-regression to evaluate associations with measurement specifications, follow-up window, medication class, region, and study-level characteristics. From the fitted model, we derived estimates standardized to a prespecified reference specification: pharmacy or administrative data, moderate definition stringency, and a 9- to 15-month follow-up window.

RESULTS: The review included 141 studies; 101 (432 estimates; 976,020 participants) contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Unstandardized pooled estimates suggested that 74.1% of patients were adherent and 76.8% were persistent. Heterogeneity was substantial, with explained variation concentrated more in the measurement-related Assessment and Administration domains than in reported Patient characteristics. Under the common reference specification, the model-based estimates were lower, at 53.7% for adherence and 48.2% for persistence. Standardized persistence declined from 63.3% at 1 to 4 months to 28.1% beyond 30 months. Adjusted estimates were generally lower in Asia; persistence was numerically lowest for anticoagulants, although credible intervals were wide and overlapping.

CONCLUSION: A large proportion of the heterogeneity reported in medication adherence and persistence after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack appears to be attributable to methodological non-equivalence in how these outcomes are defined and measured. When evaluated within a standardized framework, suboptimal medication continuation appears more common than conventional pooled estimates indicate. Meaningful surveillance and benchmarking require longitudinal, standardized, and transparent measures of medication continuation rather than reliance on discharge prescribing alone.

articles.title: Epigenetics of HFRS: Linking Immunity, Pathogenesis, and Vaccine-Induced Protection.
articles.abstract: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Old World hantaviruses, including Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV), is an important public-health concern, particularly in Asia. Clinical manifestations range from febrile illness to vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, haemorrhage and acute kidney injury. The mechanisms underlying variation in disease severity and the variability and durability of vaccine-induced immunity remain incompletely understood. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin regulation and non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, can influence antiviral immunity and immune-cell function in several biological settings; however, their specific contributions to HFRS remain insufficiently characterized. This structured narrative review examines hantavirus-specific evidence alongside relevant findings from other viral infections and vaccination settings, focusing on inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, regulatory non-coding RNAs, trained immunity and potential applications in vaccinology. Experimental HTNV studies and clinical investigations of regulatory RNAs have identified candidate pathways associated with hantavirus-host interactions; however, these findings do not establish that epigenetic mechanisms determine HFRS severity or clinical outcomes. Similarly, preclinical hantavirus vaccine studies and early clinical evaluations provide evidence regarding immunogenicity and safety but do not demonstrate epigenetic mediation of protective immunity. Findings from Andes virus (ANDV), associated primarily with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), and other viral systems are therefore considered comparative or contextual evidence, not directly generalizable to HFRS. This review identifies critical knowledge gaps and outlines how longitudinal, cell-resolved epigenomic profiling, functional validation and integrated multi-omics could clarify causal mechanisms, explain interindividual variation in disease outcomes and vaccine responses, and establish the potential translational value of epigenetic biomarkers and interventions.

articles.title: Francophone Expert Consensus on Onco-Sexological Care for Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although it is well known that prostate cancer treatments have a significant impact on sexuality and intimate relationships, this aspect is not given sufficient consideration in clinical practice. Thus, to date, there is no Francophone guideline on the onco-sexological care for prostate cancer. We therefore decided to proceed with a formalized expert consensus, using the method recommended by the French National Authority for Health. The aim was to provide the French urology and sexual medicine community with practice guidelines applicable to all patients treated for prostate cancer, regardless of the treatment, throughout the care pathway.

METHODS: Twenty-five international experts met online for the consensus. A research committee carried out a comprehensive literature review and prepared the 64 statements submitted to the rating group. After one round of scoring, 58 recommendations were validated in July 2025, having achieved a consensus of more than 70% among the experts.

RESULTS: The consensus focused on Informing patients and partners, assessing and treating sexual dysfunction and distress, providing lifestyle and psychosocial recommendations, as well as organisational and public health considerations. It is recommended that an oncosexological care pathway include: pre-treatment information, standardised screening based on patient-reported outcomes, early post-treatment assessment with regular reassessments, and access to a multidisciplinary care pathway.

CONCLUSIONS: The expert consensus on Onco-Sexological Care for Prostate Cancer led to the development of clinical guidelines based on the available literature and expert opinion. To achieve this, professionals must mobilize all available resources within the community and the cancer care network.

articles.title: Beyond LDL-C: A Case-Based Review of Complex Dyslipidemia.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is clinically heterogeneous, and LDL-C alone may not fully capture atherogenic particle burden, metabolic risk, treatment response, or inherited disease. This case-based review presents three dyslipidemia phenotypes that illustrate common diagnostic and management challenges. The first case describes diet-sensitive LDL particle and lipoprotein insulin resistance changes despite LDL-C values near conventional targets in a patient with subclinical coronary atherosclerosis. The second highlights persistent low HDL-C and HDL particle number despite substantial LDL-C reduction with non-statin and incretin-era therapies in the setting of obesity and strong family history. The third demonstrates genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia due to a pathogenic LDLR variant despite absent classic physical stigmata. Together, these cases support a phenotype-driven approach that integrates LDL-C, ApoB or LDL particle number, diet response, metabolic context, imaging, medication tolerance, and selective genetic testing to individualize dyslipidemia risk assessment and treatment.

articles.title: Electrophysiological remodeling in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy MYBPC3 R943X mutant in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and modulation by IKto-targeting drugs.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death, often driven by pathogenic variants in sarcomeric genes such as MYBPC3. The precise electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in HCM, particularly in the context of MYBPC3 truncating mutations, remain incompletely defined, hindering the development of targeted therapies. Here, we leveraged human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) carrying the MYBPC3 p.R943X mutation to systematically characterize action potential remodeling and evaluate the efficacy of ion-channel-modulating drugs.High-throughput optical AP assays revealed that R943X mutant hiPSC-CMs exhibit profound baseline electrophysiological disruption, with a marked reduction in normal AP profiles and increased incidence of pro-arrhythmic morphologies, including AP prolongation, early afterdepolarizations, and delayed afterdepolarizations, compared to isogenic non-diseased controls. Pharmacological profiling demonstrated that NS-5806, a Kv4 channel modulator, exerts a biphasic, dose-dependent effect in non-diseased isogenic control cells and partially restores normal AP morphology in R943X mutants by enhancing repolarizing current and suppressing AP prolongation. In contrast, Acacetin, an ITo and late Na+ current inhibitor, preserved electrical stability in non-diseased isogenic control cells but conferred limited and dose-sensitive rescue in mutants, with higher concentrations exacerbating arrhythmic features. These findings provide direct evidence that targeted augmentation of transient outward K+ current can selectively mitigate mutation-induced arrhythmogenic remodeling in hiPSC-CMs modeling HCM. Our study highlights the therapeutic promise, and challenges, of precision ion-channel modulation in genetic cardiomyopathy and establishes a scalable platform for genotype-guided drug discovery.

articles.title: When Swallowing Triggers VT.
articles.abstract: We describe a case of swallowing-induced ventricular tachycardia in a young, otherwise healthy male with a structurally normal heart which was refractory to multiple anti-arrhythmic medication and was successfully treated with ablation of a cardiac ganglion in the crux of the heart. We use this case to describe an unusual disease presentation and highlight current evidence related to evaluation and management of ventricular arrhythmias and add to the limited body of evidence related to swallowing induced tachycardia.

articles.title: Clinical Implementation of Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve for Revascularization Guidance: Initial Multicenter United States Experience.
articles.abstract: Real-world data on the adoption and clinical performance of angiography-derived physiology in the United States (U.S.) remain limited. We evaluated the implementation of FFRangio (CathWorks, Tel Aviv, Israel) and associated clinical outcomes across a multicenter U.S. healthcare system. We performed a multicenter observational cohort study across 4 centers involving consecutive adult patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography in whom FFRangio was performed in at least 1 coronary vessel based on clinical indication. The primary endpoint was target-vessel failure (TVF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction and target vessel revascularization during follow-up, stratified by FFRangio values >0.80 versus ≤0.80. A total of 675 vessels in 469 patients were assessed by FFRangio; 240 (36%) had values ≤0.80 and 435 (64%) >0.80. Among lesions with FFRangio ≤0.80, 182 (76%) underwent PCI, 27 (11%) CABG, and 32 (13%) were managed medically. Among lesions with FFRangio >0.80, revascularization was deferred in 406 (92%), with 22 (5%) undergoing PCI and 12 (3%) CABG. The LAD was the most frequently treated vessel (51%). At a median follow-up of 10.2 months, the incidence rate of TVF was 1.55% per 100 lesion-years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-3.36) in the FFRangio >0.80 group versus 6.30 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI, 3.25-11.0) in the FFRangio ≤0.80 group (hazard ratio [HR] 4.61, 95% CI: 1.61-13.2; p=0.002). Among deferred lesions with FFRangio >0.80, TVF rate was 1.73 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI: 0.64-3.77). In conclusion, FFRangio supported safe deferral of revascularization and risk-stratification, with low event rates among lesions with values >0.80.

articles.title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: a Report from the MARS Registry.
articles.abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Prior bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11.0%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs. 10.1%, p=0.17). Major bleeding (BARC ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25.0% vs. 12.5%, p=0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted OR 2.18, 95% CI 0.43-8.71, p=0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after cardiac surgery and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

articles.title: Mapping cellular senescence in heart failure: knowledge evolution, mechanistic modules, and senotherapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cellular senescence is increasingly recognized as a mechanistic link between cardiovascular ageing, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, and heart failure (HF) progression. However, the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and translational frontiers of senescence research in HF remain incompletely mapped.

OBJECTIVE: This study mapped the global research landscape of cellular senescence in HF from 2005 to 2025 by integrating dual-database bibliometric analysis with BERTopic-based semantic topic modelling.

METHODS: English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After field verification, standardization, and deduplication, 479 publications were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, SCImago Graphica, Pajek, Python, and Microsoft Excel were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses. PubMedBERT-based embeddings and BERTopic were applied to identify latent semantic themes from titles, abstracts, and keywords.

RESULTS: Publications increased rapidly after 2020, with 336 papers published between 2020 and 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the corpus. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with the United States showing higher collaboration strength and accumulated citation counts within the analysed dataset. Co-citation analysis identified foundational studies in senescence biology, senolytics, cardiovascular ageing, and HF remodelling. Keyword evolution showed a shift from oxidative stress, cardiac stem/progenitor cell senescence, and vascular cell senescence toward inflammation, metabolic remodelling, biomarkers, HF phenotypes, and senotherapeutics. BERTopic identified 17 substantive topics, with Cardiac and Cardiovascular Aging as the largest theme, followed by Cardiac Fibrosis and Fibroblast Activation, SASP-related Cardiovascular Senescence, Cardiac Regeneration, and Doxorubicin Cardiotoxicity.

CONCLUSION: Bibliometric and semantic analyses indicate growing research interest in cell-type-specific senescence, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, HF phenotype heterogeneity, biomarkers, and senotherapeutics. These findings highlight opportunities for integrating mechanistic research with clinical investigation. Future studies should prioritize cell-specific senescence atlases, multidimensional biomarkers, comorbidity-aware HF stratification, and cautious evaluation of senotherapeutics in HF subgroups with evidence of senescence-associated pathology.

articles.title: Microglia disulfidptosis contributes to worsening of diabetic retinopathy induced by acute hypoglycemia.
articles.abstract: The early worsening of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is associated with rapid declines in blood glucose levels during diabetes treatment, yet its pathogenesis remains poorly understood. This study aims to investigate the role of acute hypoglycemia (AH) in microglial disulfidptosis and the underlying mechanisms during DR progression. Using single-cell sequencing, we identified SLC7A11high microglia. Glucose deprivation further upregulated SLC7A11 expression in microglia, leading to excessive cystine uptake, NADPH depletion, and disulfide stress, which also activated Rac1-WRC signaling, driving F-actin contraction and plasma membrane detachment, ultimately inducing disulfidptosis and elevating pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in microglia. In vivo, SLC7A11 was highly expressed by retinal microglia in AH mice, and AH exacerbated retinal vascular leakage, structural disorganization, and microglial cell death in the retinas of AH mice. Collectively, these findings suggest that glucose deprivation triggers microglial disulfidptosis, providing a potential mechanism by which hypoglycemia exacerbates early DR deterioration, and identifying possible therapeutic targets for intervention.

articles.title: FeNO-Guided Care Improves Asthma Control in Atopic and Non-Atopic Underserved Hispanic/Latino Children.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology

articles.title: Efficacy of blood flow restriction combined with low-intensity aerobic training in patients with COPD: Study protocol for the BREATH randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airflow limitation, which reduces exercise capacity. Although current guidelines recommend moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise to achieve optimal physiological adaptations, many patients cannot sustain the required intensity, limiting overall therapeutic benefit. This study protocol aims to evaluate the effects of combining blood flow restriction (BFR) with aerobic training on exercise capacity, cardiopulmonary function, and health-related quality of life in patients with COPD, compared with conventional aerobic training or usual care.

METHODS: We will conduct a single-center, prospective, parallel-group randomized controlled trial. 45 clinically stable patients with COPD (GOLD stages II-IV) will be recruited. Eligible participants must have had no acute exacerbations in the past two months and be able to participate in the exercise training program. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: usual care, conventional aerobic training (60-80% VO₂ peak), or BFR-enhanced aerobic training (40-50% VO₂ peak, with 40-80% arterial occlusion pressure). All exercise sessions will be supervised, three times per week for eight weeks. The primary outcome is exercise capacity. Secondary outcomes include pulmonary function tests, respiratory muscle strength, diaphragmatic ultrasound, heart rate variability, and health-related quality-of-life questionnaires.

PLANNED OUTCOMES: BFR-enhanced aerobic training may be a safe and effective rehabilitation option for COPD patients who cannot tolerate high-intensity exercise. The BREATH trial is expected to provide essential evidence for clinical care by integrating BFR training into pulmonary rehabilitation. This approach could inform future management strategies for exercise intolerance among patients with COPD.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study has been approved by the Institutional Review Board (approval number: B-ER-113-298) and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (registration number: NCT06756646).

articles.title: Design and rationale of a multicenter randomized trial assessing strategies for catheter ablation of persistent atrial fibrillation- The STAR AF 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of catheter ablation procedures for the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the success rates of PVI are limited for patients with persistent AF. Yet, the optimal ablation strategy beyond PVI alone in patients with persistent AF remains to be established.

STUDY DESIGN AND OBJECTIVES: The STAR AF 3 trial is an international multicenter prospective, single-blind, blinded endpoint, clinical trial that includes patients with persistent AF of more than 3 months duration referred for a first catheter ablation procedure. Enrollment will occur at 33 centers in Europe, Canada, Australia, USA and Japan. The aim of this study is to compare the strategy of PVI alone with two strategies that add ablation to PVI: PVI+drivers ablation and PVI+posterior wall isolation. Patients will be equally randomized into one of these three ablation strategies. Patients will be followed up for 18 months. The primary endpoint will be the time to first recurrence of documented atrial tachyarrhythmia (atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia) between 91 days and 18 months after a single ablation procedure. An atrial tachyarrhythmia will qualify as a recurrence if it lasts 30 s or longer and is documented by 12-lead electrocardiogram, electrocardiographic rhythm strips, or transtelephonic monitor recordings. Although a post-ablation blanking period of 3 months will be observed, a repeat left atrial ablation procedure done at any time will also qualify as a primary endpoint event. Enrollment is completed and a total of 617 patients have been recruited into the trial. The trial is registered at the Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04428944) CONCLUSIONS: The STAR AF 3 trial is a large multicenter randomized trial assessing the optimal ablation strategy for patients with persistent AF.

articles.title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.

OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes.

METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline.

CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

articles.title: CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ.

METHODS: We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL.

CONCLUSION: Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

articles.title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms.

METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device.

RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

articles.title: Undiagnosed Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Hidden in Explanted Hearts: Insights from a Single Tertiary Center.
Mitral Valve Prolapse and Ventricular Arrhythmia Risk in TTN-Mediated Cardiomyopathy: A Single Center Experience.
Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.

METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.

RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.

CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

articles.title: Transvenous Lead Extraction Without Dedicated Surgical Back up in Low-Risk Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is associated with major complications that could require immediate surgical rescue. These procedures are performed in an EP lab or hybrid OR with the presence of a surgical team on standby. We have designed an institutional protocol that permits performance of TLE in low-risk situations, in an EP lab without dedicated surgical back-up.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate outcomes of TLE in low-risk patients METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent low-risk TLE at Emory Healthcare between 2010-23. Low-risk TLE were defined as an extraction of a pacing or ICD lead with a dwell time >= 1 and <= 5 years or a lead < 1 year that required extraction tools.

RESULTS: Among 482 patients who met the criteria, the average lead age was 2.8 ± 1.2 years. The mean number of targeted leads per patient was 1.6±0.7. Extraction tools were required in 33.1% of cases. Major complications occurred in 0.83% of patients (n=4): 2 pericardial effusions requiring pericardiocentesis, 1 pneumothorax and 1 death from cardiogenic shock in an end stage heart failure patient. The patients with pericardial effusions and pneumothorax were part of a procedure that required lead revisions and the insertion of 1 or more new leads. No patients required surgical rescue.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that, in selected "low-risk" patients, TLE can be performed safely in an experienced EP lab at centers with on-site cardiac surgery but without a dedicated surgical standby team, potentially reducing resource utilization in resource-limited healthcare environments.

articles.title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.

RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

articles.title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.

OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.

METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.

RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).

CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.

METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.

RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.

CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

articles.title: Left Atrial Reservoir Strain To Identify Advanced Atrial Cardiomyopathy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) is a novel marker of left atrial (LA) function. We hypothesized that LASr can be used to identify atrial cardiomyopathy in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between LASr and invasive and non-invasive markers of atrial cardiomyopathy in AF patients.

METHODS: We prospectively recruited patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF and preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction scheduled for catheter ablation. Resting transthoracic echocardiography was performed focusing on the left atrium (LA). Participants were dichotomised into two groups: reduced LASr (<20%) and preserved LASr (≥20%). Markers of LA cardiomyopathy were compared between these two groups; invasive markers included mean LA pressure, mean LA voltage and LA compliance whilst non-invasive markers included LA volumes and NT-pro BNP.

RESULTS: A total of 91 patients were enrolled. Patients with reduced LASr (n=31) were older (69.4±8.9 vs 59.6±11.3 years, p<0.001), and more commonly female (45.2 vs 18.3%, p=0.007). Reduced LASr correlated with lower LA compliance (0.28±0.16 vs 0.42±0.25mm/mmHg, p<0.001), higher LA pressure (14.8±3.81 vs 13.1±4.46mmHg, p=0.031), and lower LA voltage (1.65±1.35 vs 3.12±1.57mV, p<0.01). On non-invasive assessment, reduced LASr was also associated with higher NT-proBNP levels (479 [200-1073] vs 121 [58-256] pg/ml p<0.001) and larger LA volumes (38.5±11.5 vs 32.6±7.7 mL/m2, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: In patients with symptomatic AF, reduced LASr is associated with a more advanced atrial cardiomyopathy involving hemodynamic, mechanical and electrical atrial dyfsfunction. LASr may therefore provide a useful non-invasive marker of atrial cardiomyopathy in AF.

articles.title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated.

OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%.

RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

articles.title: Zero-fluoroscopy approach to left atrial appendage closure using intracardiac echo guidance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) with the Watchman™ device is typically performed with the use of transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy. LAAC guided by intracardiac echo (ICE) without the use of fluoroscopy has not been previously described.

OBJECTIVE: In this series, we describe the safety and feasibility of Watchman™ implantation using only ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy.

METHODS: 214 patients undergoing LAAC with the Watchman FLX™ or Watchman FLX™ Pro device and using a planned fluoroscopy-free approach were studied. ICE was used for echocardiographic imaging in all cases. TEE was not used in any cases. Fluoroscopy was used as a bail-out approach when it was felt to be clinically necessary by the operator. Peri-procedural, 45-day, and 1-year efficacy and safety outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: In 203/214 patients (94.8%), LAAC was completed without the use of fluoroscopy. Bail-out fluoroscopy was required in 11/214 patients (5.1%). Successful device implantation was completed in 212/214 patients (99.1%). The rate of any peri-device leak at 45 days post-procedure was 11.6%. Procedural complications were limited to one pericardial effusion and one case of ventricular tachycardia.

CONCLUSION: LAAC with the Watchman™ device using ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy appears to be safe and effective. The rates of procedural success, complications, and peri-device leaks on 45 day follow up were consistent with that seen in pivotal clinical trials. Further studies are needed to assess the broader applicability of this technique.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.

METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.

RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).

CONCLUSIONS: VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.

articles.title: Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling.

METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122).

RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004).

CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

articles.title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.

OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.

METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.

RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type.

CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

articles.title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model.

RESULTS: Among 1,991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

articles.title: Schisandrin B attenuates the platelet activation-thrombosis cascade through inhibition of Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT and Extracellular signal-regulated kinase-Talin-mediated integrin αIIbβ3 signaling.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Schisandrin B (Sch B), a principal bioactive lignan derived from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. exhibits diverse pharmacological activities. This traditional Chinese medicine possesses therapeutic value for treating symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and a faint, nearly imperceptible pulse caused by deficiency of both qi and yin.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch B on platelet activation and thrombosis, employing a combination of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and comprehensive in vitro and in vivo functional assays.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Platelet aggregation and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) release were assessed using a lumi-aggregometer. Flow cytometry was used to evaluate Sch B's effects on P-selectin expression and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Platelet adhesion, spreading, and clot retraction assays were performed to analyze outside-in signaling. Potential targets and signaling pathways of Sch B were predicted through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and these predictions were further investigated using western blot analysis. In vivo, the effects of Sch B on thrombus formation were evaluated using murine models.

RESULTS: Sch B significantly suppressed platelet aggregation, granule release, adhesion, spreading, P-selectin expression, and PAC-1 binding. Western blot further analysis revealed that Sch B reduced the phosphorylation of key signaling molecules, such as Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), AKT, Extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK), Talin1, and β3 integrin. In a mesenteric arterial thrombosis model induced by ferric chloride (FeCl3), Sch B significantly prolonged the time to stable thrombus formation. However, it did not significantly effect coagulation parameters or tail-bleeding time in mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Sch B inhibits platelet activation by interfering with the PI3K/AKT/ERK-Talin signaling pathway, thereby attenuating thrombus formation. This supports its potential as an antiplatelet agent with a favorable safety profile.

articles.title: Platycodon Decoction alleviates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease associated inflammation with potential dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The traditional Chinese medicine formula Platycodon Decoction (PD) is known to be effective to alleviate respiratory system-related symptoms, its effect and integrated mechanism for treating COPD requires elucidation.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to systematically address the pharmacology of PD in treating COPD through analyzing how PD inhibiting the intracellular inflammatory pathway and intercellular interactions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PD composition was ascertained via LC-MS/MS. PD-induced organ damage was assessed through an acute toxicity test. Following the intervention of PD, body weight, lung index, sputum volume, pulmonary function, expression of inflammatory factors, pulmonary tissue injury, mucus secretion, and MUC5AC expression of the COPD-modeled mice were measured. PD's impacts on the levels of inflammatory factors, cellular activity, proliferation, cell cycle, reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and inter-cellular communication were assessed through Beas-2b human bronchus epithelial cells and THP-1 human macrophage. The PD-associated, COPD relevant inflammatory pathways were analyzed through network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics and then verified through Western blots. The involved cells for cell receptor identified by network pharmacology was analyzed by single-cell sequencing and verified by molecular dynamics and Western blot.

RESULTS: The acute toxicity assessment provided preliminary evidence of PD tolerability under the tested conditions. Fifty compounds were identified in PD. Animal experiments demonstrated that PD can decrease the inflammatory levels and alleviate excessive mucus secretion in mice. In vitro cell experiments indicated that PD can efficiently abate inflammation and oxidative stress within the COPD-related airway microenvironment and diminish epithelial-macrophage interactions. Integration of single-cell and network pharmacology analyses identified ADGRE5 as a candidate receptor that may mediate epithelial-macrophage interactions. PD treatment reduced PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and was accompanied by decreased ADGRE5 expression.

CONCLUSIONS: PD alleviates inflammation in COPD, potentially involving dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.

articles.title: Toxicological Effects of Polyethylene Terephthalate Microplastics on Chronic Kidney Disease: An Integrative Bioinformatics, Network Toxicology, and Machine Learning Study.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are widely distributed in human organs, including the kidney, brain, and liver, where they induce oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. However, the toxicological effects of MNPs on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we employed an integrated approach combining bioinformatics, network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential impacts of polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) on CKD. A total of 191 CKD-related targets were obtained from the GEO database, while 875 potential targets of PET-MPs were identified using PubChem, ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and the SEA Search platform. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning, seven core targets were ultimately identified. KEGG pathway enrichment and Gene Ontology (GO) analyses indicated that PET-MPs may exert effects by modulating immune- and inflammation-related pathways as well as energy metabolism. Molecular docking revealed high-affinity interactions between the PET-MP-derived small molecules and the core targets, suggesting direct interference with cellular activities that could influence CKD progression. This computational framework not only elucidates potential molecular mechanisms of MNP-induced nephrotoxicity but also identifies candidate targets for therapeutic intervention, aligning with the scope of machine-learning-driven drug molecule design.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with exertional dyspnea in severe asthma: data at inclusion from the French RAMSES cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate the prevalence of exertional dyspnea in a French cohort of patients with severe asthma and to explore associated factors, with a focus on biologics.

METHODS: RAMSES is a French, multicenter, prospective cohort of patients with severe asthma. The primary outcome was exertional dyspnea defined by a modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) score ≥2. Secondary outcomes were mMRC score ≥1 and ≥ 3. To study factors associated with exertional dyspnea, logistic regressions were performed. We hypothesized that the potential effect of biologics on exertional dyspnea relied on improved asthma control, and explored it through a mediation model.

RESULTS: A total of 569 participants from the RAMSES cohort were included. Among them, 360 (65.5%) had uncontrolled asthma and 307 (54.1%) were treated with biologics. The prevalence of exertional dyspnea defined by an mMRC score ≥1, ≥2 and ≥ 3 was respectively 73.8 [70.2; 77.4] %, 48.5 [44.4; 52.6] % and 21.6 [18.2; 25] %. The Asthma Control Test (ACT) score was the factor most strongly associated with exertional dyspnea (mMRC score ≥2) (OR = 0.8 [0.74; 0.86] for 1-point increase). Biologic therapy was associated with a lower rate of exertional dyspnea (OR = 0.46 [0.25-0.84]), with the effect largely mediated by an improvement in the ACT score (mediation ratio: 63.4% [5.1-254.2]) CONCLUSION: Our results highlight the high prevalence of dyspnea-related disability in severe asthma, justifying considering this treatable trait as a priority therapeutic goal. Exertional dyspnea was associated with uncontrolled asthma and biologics, primarily through asthma control.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and mortality and liver-related outcomes in patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2-i1) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus, but their safety and clinical impact in advanced liver disease remain uncertain because patients with cirrhosis were underrepresented in major trials.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX research network, we identified adults with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity and compared outcomes according to SGLT2-i exposure. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 5,128 matched pairs were analyzed. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included all-cause hospitalization, ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, and variceal bleeding.

RESULTS: In the matched cohort, SGLT2-i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.78), hospitalization (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.89), ascites (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.77), spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.87), and variceal bleeding (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.99), with no difference in hepatic encephalopathy.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, SGLT2-i use was associated with improved survival and fewer liver-related complications.

articles.title: ISG-15 promotes de novo HBV infection after pediatric liver transplant via IL-18/STAT1 from HBcAb-positive donors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Liver transplantation is the main therapy for pediatric end-stage liver disease, but use of hepatitis B core antibody-positive (HBcAb+) grafts increases the risk of de novo hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We examined whether ISG-15 promotes de novo HBV through IL-18/STAT1 signaling.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical data and conducted proteomics analysis. Liver biopsy specimens were randomly selected from eight pediatric recipients who developed de novo HBV infection and from 10 pediatric recipients who did not develop de novo HBV infection, after liver transplantation was performed between 2018 and 2019. In proteomic comparisons between the de novo and non-de novo HBV groups, we identified 5027 proteins, including 221 differentially expressed proteins. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses were conducted to evaluate functional associations.

RESULTS: Differentially expressed proteins were primarily involved in the immune response, viral defense, and cell adhesion processes. In vitro experiments using small interfering RNA and plasmid transfection to knock down and overexpress ISG-15 in hepatoblastoma (HepG2.2.15) cells demonstrated that ISG-15 overexpression significantly enhanced cell proliferation and migration, whereas ISG-15 knockdown inhibited these biological processes. Treatment with the STAT1 inhibitor fludarabine and the agonist 2-nitropropane further confirmed that ISG-15 promotes HBV replication by regulating the IL-18/STAT1 signaling axis.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this study provide experimental evidence that can help in understanding the role of ISG-15 in HBV infection and offer potential targets for clinical intervention to prevent de novo HBV infection after liver transplantation using HBcAb-positive grafts.

articles.title: Preventing steatotic liver disease through physical activity: The benefits beyond weight loss.
Serum apoptosis inhibitor of macrophage is associated with radiologic severity in pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex disease.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex disease (MAC-PD) is a chronic infection with variable severity and treatment responses. It lacks blood biomarkers that reflect disease burden and early treatment-related biological activity. We evaluated whether serum apoptosis inhibitor of macrophage (AIM), a macrophage-derived soluble protein, is associated with radiologic severity and changes during treatment in MAC-PD.

METHODS: This prospective observational pilot study included 18 female patients with MAC-PD who received guideline-based therapy (GBT) for at least 6 months. Serum AIM levels were measured at baseline and 6 months. Radiologic severity and symptom burden were assessed using Nodules-Infiltration-Cavities-Ectasis (NICE) score and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Assessment Test (CAT), respectively. C-reactive protein, Krebs von den Lungen-6, surfactant protein D, and albumin levels were analyzed as comparator markers.

RESULTS: Serum AIM was associated with the NICE score at baseline (Spearman's ρ = 0.648, 95% CI 0.260-0.856, p = 0.004) and after 6 months (ρ = 0.701, 95% CI 0.348-0.880, p = 0.001). AIM levels decreased after treatment (median, 420.1-331.7 ng/mL; p = 0.015). NICE scores decreased (median, 9-8; p = 0.077), but the change did not reach statistical significance. CAT scores decreased (median, 11-6; p = 0.007). The percentage change in AIM was not significantly associated with absolute changes in CAT or NICE scores.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum AIM was associated with radiologic disease burden in patients with MAC-PD at baseline and 6 months and decreased during the first 6 months of GBT. Larger studies are needed to further evaluate its clinical utility.

articles.title: A nomogram for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with coagulase-negative staphylococcus bloodstream infections.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) have emerged as significant pathogens in bloodstream infections (BSIs). Currently, no validated models exist for specifically predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with CoNS-BSIs.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on adult patients with CoNS-BSIs using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) database. Participants were randomly allocated into a training set (n = 366) and a validation set (n = 157). Demographic characteristics, severity scores, comorbidities and laboratory examinations from the first 24 h of ICU admission were analyzed. The optimal predictive variables for establishing a nomogram were screened through univariate, multivariate logistic regression and stepwise regression analyses. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA) and clinical impact curve (CIC).

RESULTS: Among 523 patients enrolled, the overall in-hospital mortality was 22.9%. Four independent predictors were incorporated into the nomogram: age (OR = 1.04), anion gap (AG: OR = 1.11), total bilirubin (TBil: OR = 1.26) and respiratory failure (OR = 1.97). The area under the curve (AUC) values in the training set and validation set were 0.758 and 0.823, respectively. The P-values of the calibration curve in two sets were 0.258 and 0.432. The DCA curves were above the two extreme curves. The CIC analysis revealed a high concordance between predicted high-risk cases and observed clinical events when the risk threshold exceeded 60%.

CONCLUSION: Age, AG, TBil and respiratory failure were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality among patients with CoNS-BSIs. The nomogram based on these four parameters demonstrated good performance and clinical utility for risk assessment.

articles.title: Healthy default beverage policies: A comprehensive inventory and comparative analysis of enacted and proposed policies across U.S. state and local jurisdictions.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous evaluations of healthy default beverage (HDB) policies showed inconsistent implementation and enforcement. No study has described and compared implementation and enforcement provisions in enacted and proposed policies to identify gaps impacting policy success.

OBJECTIVE: To identify and examine trends in enacted and proposed U.S. local and state HDB policies; compare implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions across policy status and jurisdictional levels; evaluate alignment with Healthy Drinks Healthy Kids (HDHK) recommendations; and illustrate how enacted policies changed during committee review.

DESIGN: This study identified enacted and proposed local and state policies through systematic searches of policy databases (American Legal Publishing Code Library, Municode, NexisUni, Westlaw), websites, and literature in September 2024. Policies were reviewed for inclusion, and a jurisdiction's final policy version coded for key characteristics. Enacted policy's legislative websites were separately searched for accompanying documents (e.g., committee reports).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The outcomes were number of enacted and proposed policies; frequency of implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions; HDHK recommendations alignment; and committee-required changes to enacted policies.

STATISTICAL ANALYSES PERFORMED: Intercoder agreement was calculated with Cohen's kappa, and descriptive statistics summarized policy contents. As a case-study, accompanying documents from state-level enacted Hawaii and Illinois policies were qualitatively reviewed.

RESULTS: This inventory included 86 policies (28 local, 58 state) from 2015-2024. After excluding duplicate state-level bicameral policies and counting each re-introduction of a policy across legislative sessions as an additional policy, there were 65 unique policies. Policies were enacted in 28 local jurisdictions and 4 states, and proposed (not enacted) in 14 states. Implementation, evaluation, and enforcement provisions were uncommon across jurisdictions and statuses. Equity provisions appeared only in local policies. No policies completely met HDHK recommendations. Accompanying documents illustrated how the legislative process strengthened or weakened policy provisions in Hawaii and Illinois.

CONCLUSIONS: HDB policies are increasingly enacted across U.S. jurisdictions. Strengthening implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions may enhance policy effectiveness in reducing children's restaurant sweetened beverage intake.

articles.title: Influence of exercise on arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy associated with the p.Ser329Argfs*23 variant in the PKP2 gene.
Arrhythmias detected by implanted cardiac rhythm recorders in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Arrhythmias are a common complication of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM). We sought to characterize the prevalence, risk factors, and prognosis of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM using implantable loop recorders (ILRs).

METHODS: ILRs were implanted in 49 patients with ATTR-CM (84% male; median age, 73.2 [66.2-78.8] years; 71% wild-type, 51% with known atrial fibrillation [AF]). Factors associated with the development of AF or pacemaker implantation were analyzed, and clinical outcomes were compared with those of a contemporary cohort of patients with 125 ATTR-CM without an ILR.
