RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 37.2 [26.6-41.1] months, an advanced conduction disorder (ACD) prompting pacemaker implantation was detected in 16 individuals (33%) and new-onset AF was detected in 17 patients (71% of those without previous AF). Patients with new-onset AF more frequently had wild-type ATTR-CM. Those who needed pacemaker implantation were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and right bundle branch block, and a longer PR interval. Compared with patients without an ILR, early detection of arrhythmias by ILR was not associated with a prognostic benefit in terms of survival (P = .57), reduction of syncope (P = 1), heart failure admissions (P = .34), or embolic events (P = .999).

CONCLUSIONS: Although a higher incidence of arrhythmias was identified through ILR monitoring in patients with ATTR-CM, no significant benefits were observed in terms of survival or other hard clinical endpoints. Significant differences were identified in patients who developed new-onset AF and ACD. These differences should be considered during the clinical follow-up of this population.

articles.title: Lipid metabolism and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and progressive disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and progressive narrowing of the pulmonary arteries. Recent studies have shown that changes in lipid metabolism and lipid action play an important role in the pathogenesis of PAH, involving membrane integrity, energy metabolism, inflammatory response, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Lipoprotein receptor deficiency further exacerbates inflammation, fibrosis, and associated pathological processes in PAH. This review summarizes the role of many lipid-active substances and their signaling pathways in the pathogenesis of PAH, sorting the biomarkers related to the severity and prognosis of PAH and discussing the potential application of drug therapy targeting lipid metabolism in managing PAH. This review aims to identify clinically relevant lipid molecules and candidate biomarkers, and to provide new insights and potential targets for precision oriented diagnosis and treatment of PAH.

articles.title: WTAP/YTHDC1-mediated m6A modification of P4HA1 suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis and ameliorates MASLD by activating AKT signaling.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global metabolic epidemic with limited therapeutic options. Prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunit alpha 1 (P4HA1) has been implicated in glucose metabolism, but its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in MASLD remain unknown. In this study, we established a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASLD mouse model and a free fatty acid (FFA)-induced steatosis model in HepG2 cells. We found that P4HA1 was significantly downregulated in both HFD-fed mouse livers and FFA-treated HepG2 cells. P4HA1 overexpression ameliorated HFD-induced glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and hepatic steatosis. Mechanistically, WTAP-mediated m6A modification of P4HA1 mRNA, recognized by the m6A reader YTHDC1, stabilized P4HA1 transcripts. Moreover, P4HA1 directly bound the PH domain of AKT, enhanced AKT phosphorylation at Thr308 and Ser473, promoted FoxO1 nuclear exclusion, and suppressed gluconeogenic gene transcription. In vivo WTAP overexpression restored P4HA1 expression and AKT activity, recapitulating the protective effects. Collectively, this study establishes a novel WTAP/YTHDC1-m6A-P4HA1-AKT signaling axis in MASLD pathogenesis, identifies P4HA1 as a protective metabolic regulator whose downregulation promotes excessive gluconeogenesis and lipid accumulation, and suggests that targeting this axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for MASLD.

articles.title: Diabetes mellitus mortality in Brazil, 2000-2031: Rising number of deaths with stable age-standardized rates.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To describe trends in diabetes mellitus (DM) mortality in Brazil, estimate it to 2031, and determine how much of the expected change results from population growth and aging versus changes in mortality risk.

METHODS: National death records with DM as the underlying cause (ICD-10 E10-E14) for 2000-2023 were analyzed. Crude and age-standardized rates were estimated with a Bayesian age-period model and projected to 2031. Trends were assessed with Prais-Winsten regression.

RESULTS: Brazil recorded 1,320,831 DM deaths over 24 years (2000-2023), and 749,809 DM deaths are projected over 8 years (2024-2031). The national age-standardized rate (all rates per 100,000) was 27.13 in 2022-2023 and is projected at 29.30 in 2030-2031, not a significant change. Of Brazil's five regions, the Northeast (34.70) and North (32.22) had the highest projected rates. Rates increased significantly only in the North and among men nationwide. Population growth and aging explain three-quarters of the 60,280 additional deaths projected for 2030-2031 versus 2022-2023.

CONCLUSIONS: DM deaths in Brazil are expected to rise through 2031, mainly due to population growth and aging, while age-standardized rates rise only in the North and among men. Health resources should prioritize long-term DM care for older adults and prevention in these groups.

articles.title: Association of quantitative computed tomography - derived hepatic fat with an oral glucose tolerance test - derived insulin clearance surrogate in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIM: . - To examine associations of quantitative computed tomography-derived hepatic, visceral, subcutaneous, and pancreatic adiposity with an oral glucose tolerance test-derived insulin clearance surrogate in adults with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: . - This retrospective cross-sectional study included 166 adults not receiving exogenous insulin before admission. The molar C-peptide-to-insulin area-under-the-curve ratio from 0 to 120 minutes was used as the clearance surrogate. Multivariable regression was performed, with hepatic fat and visceral fat area prespecified as primary exposures and Holm correction applied to primary-model P values.

RESULTS: . - Each one-standard-deviation higher hepatic fat was associated with an 8.44% lower clearance surrogate (95% confidence interval, -12.69% to -3.98%; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Visceral fat area showed a directionally inverse association that did not meet the multiplicity-adjusted threshold (-6.13%; 95% confidence interval, -12.29% to 0.46%; Holm-adjusted P = 0.067). The unconditional hepatic-fat association with insulin area under the curve did not meet the false-discovery-rate-adjusted threshold (adjusted P = 0.066); the C-peptide-conditioned analysis was treated as exploratory. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.380).

CONCLUSION: . - Higher quantitative computed tomography-derived hepatic fat was associated with a lower oral glucose tolerance test-derived insulin clearance surrogate in adults with type 2 diabetes. The observed pattern across adiposity measures is hypothesis-generating and does not establish that hepatic fat is a stronger correlate than other depots; prospective confirmation using direct or model-based measures of insulin clearance is needed.

articles.title: Fetal brain volumes in complete vascular ring: A cross-sectional MRI study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between complete vascular ring (CVR) and prenatal brain development remains poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To compare global and regional fetal brain volumes between fetuses with CVR and controls, accounting for gestational age (GA), fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 70 prenatally diagnosed CVR fetuses and 200 GA-matched controls with normal brain anatomy (22-37 weeks) underwent 1.5-T fetal MRI. Motion-corrected three-dimensional brain reconstructions were generated by slice-to-volume registration, and 19 regions were automatically segmented using a deep-learning pipeline. Linear regression included continuous GA, group, their interaction, fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight. Regional-to-intracranial volume ratios and sensitivity analyses incorporating maternal body mass index were evaluated. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

RESULTS: At the 28-week reference age, adjusted supratentorial brain, cortical gray matter, white matter, thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular volumes were smaller in the CVR group (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P < 0.05). Intracranial volume did not differ significantly. Thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular proportions were also smaller. No group-by-GA interaction survived correction in the primary model.

CONCLUSIONS: CVR was associated with differences in selected fetal brain volumes, including regional differences relative to intracranial volume. Larger longitudinal studies with postnatal follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Lung-brain-axis-mediated mechanisms of sepsis-associated encephalopathy secondary to lower respiratory tract infection: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) represent one of the most frequent causes of sepsis. Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), a serious complication of sepsis, markedly increases patient mortality and the risk of long-term cognitive impairment. The emerging concept of the lung-brain axis offers a novel framework for understanding the pathogenesis of SAE. Unlike general reviews covering all-cause sepsis-associated encephalopathy, this review specifically focuses on SAE secondary to LRTI, and discriminates its unique epidemiological, clinical and mechanistic signatures from SAE triggered by abdominal, urinary or bloodstream infection. This review systematically summarizes the epidemiological characteristics of SAE induced by LRTIs, the anatomical and immunological basis of lung-brain interactions, and key pathological mechanisms including neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, neurotransmitter imbalance, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Additionally, it highlights advances in biomarker research and clinical management strategies. By integrating evidence from molecular‑biology and neuroimaging studies, this article describes how pulmonary infections drive brain dysfunction via neural, immune, and endocrine pathways. These findings provide a theoretical foundation to support early diagnosis and targeted therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Escalation of Resting Heart Rate and Tachycardia as a Response to Thoracic Radiotherapy: Implications for Cardiovascular Outcomes after Radiotherapy.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac toxicity is a well-recognized, but poorly understood complication of radiotherapy (RT). In non-oncological settings, there is an established relationship between resting heart rate and cardiovascular health.

OBJECTIVES: To study the incidence and pattern of resting heart rate (rHR) as an early sign of cardiotoxicity among patients with non-metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed serial rHR measurements of consecutive patients with locally advanced NSCLC treated with definitive chemoradiation (CRT) over 6-7 weeks of daily radiation treatments followed by immunotherapy (durvalumab) between 2017-2022. Radiation dose to the heart and 17 cardiac substructures were extracted. Associations between heart rate elevation, tachycardia, cardiac substructure dose and outcomes were evaluated using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) and regression analysis.

RESULTS: We identified 110 patients, 56.4% with pre-existing heart disease. Median follow-up was 33.6 months. Median age was 70.4 years. Median rHR increased significantly during RT, rising from 81.5 bpm to 93 bpm at end of RT (p < 0.0001), remaining elevated in 30.6% of patients 12 months post-RT. Tachycardia incidence rose from 11.2% at baseline to 36.5% at 1-month post-RT (p < 0.0001). After adjusting for comorbidities, higher mean sinoatrial node (SAN) dose was associated with higher rHR elevation, delayed HR recovery and persistent tachycardia (all p < 0.05). Higher rHR during and after RT (β = 0.23, p = 0.005, and β = 13.49, p = 0.049, respectively), as well as the incidence of tachycardia episodes during RT were associated with increased odds of developing an arrhythmia (OR, 2.97, 95% CI, 1.17-7.52, p = 0.022).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated rHR and tachycardia are observed during and after RT for NSCLC and are associated with higher mean SAN dose. HR elevation was associated with increased risk of de novo arrhythmias, suggesting that heart rate may represent a non-invasive biomarker of subclinical cardiac injury. Prospective studies might be warranted to test the potential of routine HR monitoring and proactive dose reductions to the SAN to enable early detection and help mitigate the risk of post-treatment arrhythmia.

articles.title: Preconditioning induces ischemic tolerance by attenuating ferroptosis: involvement of the m6A-dependent FTO-IGF2BP1/3-ACSL4 regulatory Axis.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemic preconditioning (CIP) confers robust protection against subsequent ischemic stroke by enhancing brain ischemic tolerance. Although ferroptosis is increasingly recognized as a critical pathogenic mechanism in stroke, the role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification in its regulation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the involvement of m6A signaling in the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of CIP using complementary in vivo mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) models. We found that CIP significantly attenuated ischemia-induced neuronal ferroptosis in vivo, whereas OGD preconditioning (OGDP) recapitulated these anti-ferroptotic effects in HT22 cells. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), a key executor of ferroptosis, was markedly upregulated following ischemic injury, whereas CIP effectively suppressed this increase. Similarly, OGDP attenuated OGD-induced ACSL4 upregulation in HT22 cells. Importantly, ACSL4 overexpression significantly attenuated the protective effects of OGDP against OGD-induced ferroptosis. Mechanistic analyses in HT22 cells revealed that OGD downregulated the m6A demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) and upregulated m6A readers insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding proteins (IGF2BPs), including IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, thereby stabilizing ACSL4 mRNA and promoting ferroptosis. OGDP alleviated these effects by restoring FTO expression, reducing IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3 levels, and enhancing m6A-dependent ACSL4 mRNA decay. Together, these findings demonstrate that CIP induces ischemic tolerance and attenuates ACSL4-associated ferroptosis. Mechanistic studies in neuronal cells further identify the m6A-dependent FTO-IGF2BP1/3-ACSL4 axis as a potential regulatory mechanism contributing to OGDP-induced ferroptosis resistance.

articles.title: Chitosan-functionalized Ajuga integrifolia-mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles for antidiabetic and anti-inflammatory applications: An integrated In Vitro, In Vivo, and In Silico study.
articles.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disease characterized by high blood glucose levels (BGL), while inflammation is an adaptive physiological response which is triggered by adverse conditions, including infection and tissue damage. In the present study, Ajuga integrifolia (AI) mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles (AI-ZnO NPs) were prepared and functionalized with chitosan (CS). The synthesized AI-ZnO and CS-ZnO NPs were characterized using advanced techniques. UV-Visible spectroscopic analysis showed a prominent peak of AI-ZnO at 361 nm, which blue-shifted to 347 nm with CS coating. Functional groups were identified using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), while particle morphology and size were characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS). X-ray Diffraction (XRD) confirmed the hexagonal wurtzite structure. Laminin, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), Islet Amyloid Polypeptide (IAPP), and alpha-glucosidase were docked with chitosan, yielding distinct binding energies as well as varying interaction residues, interaction types, and distances. The in vitro antidiabetic and anti-inflammatory assays showed considerable potential, with inhibition ranging from 12.1 ± 2.01% to 89.46 ± 0.77%. The in vivo antidiabetic and anti-inflammatory experiments were performed in a murine model. BGL increased markedly from the normal baseline (95 mg/dl) to about 224 mg/dl within 24 h of alloxan administration. 40 mg/kg of CS-ZnO showed the highest potential, lowering the BGL to 121 ± 2 mg/dl. The ear edema decreased from 0.35 mm to 0.26 mm with 40 mg/kg of CS-ZnO. The histopathological images also confirmed the medicinal potential of the test samples, which may serve as alternative medicinal agents in the future.

articles.title: The functional anatomy of caveolae across cell types.
articles.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
articles.abstract: Caveolae are 50-100nm, cholesterol- and sphingolipid-enriched invaginations of the plasma membrane, assembled from caveolin and cavin proteins. They are not generic vesicles distributed equally across mammalian tissues, but cell-type-specific membrane organelles whose abundance, molecular composition and physiological roles vary widely. This review synthesises the evidence for caveolae across the cellular landscape and treats distribution, signalling and disease as a single axis. Endothelial cells, adipocytes and muscle cells represent the highest-density systems, where caveolae support transcytosis, membrane tension buffering, lipid handling, contractile signalling and ion-channel organisation. Fibroblasts are also a well-supported non-endothelial model, with genetic and functional evidence linking caveolin-1 and cavin-1 to caveola formation, integrin mechanosensing, matrix production and fibrosis; by contrast, direct evidence for fibrocytes remains sparse. In epithelia, glia, immune cells, stromal cells and cancer cells, caveolin expression must be distinguished from the verified presence of bona fide caveolae. This distinction is particularly important for telocytes, mature neurons, lymphocytes and tumour cells, where caveolin-based markers, non-caveolar scaffolds and context-dependent loss of cavin proteins complicate interpretation. Disease phenotypes mirror this cellular specificity: mutations or dysregulation lead to muscle caveolinopathies, pulmonary arterial hypertension, lipodystrophy, vascular and blood-brain barrier dysfunction, fibrosis, altered host-pathogen entry, and cancer phenotypes. A cell-type-resolved view therefore complements mechanism-centred accounts of caveola mechanics and helps explain why one caveolin-cavin module can generate divergent physiological and pathological outcomes.

articles.title: Diet-induced diabetes driven by proinsulin misfolding reversed by β-cell rest.
articles.abstract: Diet modification can be beneficial in the treatment of type-2 diabetes; but different dietary management approaches can have different impact on pancreatic islet β-cells. Congenic male mice carrying one Ins2-R(B22)E allele (encoding a proinsulin that is predisposed to misfolding, plus three alleles encoding WT proinsulin) develop diabetes prompted by high fat diet-induced weight gain, with exacerbation of β-cell ER stress. Here we sought to understand how β-cell rest could bring about reversal of diabetes. For this, we transitioned two groups of diabetic mice for 5-weeks of a lower caloric-density diet (normal chow ad lib) or alternatively, the same high fat diet alternating with fasting every other day. Both approaches yielded sets of animals that consumed the same total calories; both blocked further body weight gain leading to the same final body weight; both maintained the same energy expenditure; and both exhibited the same whole-body insulin sensitivity. However, diabetes was selectively reversed in animals fed high fat diet alternating with fasting, accompanied by significantly increased islet insulin content, and increased circulating insulin. Blood glucose and serum insulin levels oscillate in animals fed every other day; our data suggest β-cell rest on the fasting day. Mechanisms associated with recovery included decreased islet phospho-eIF2α, accompanied by increased proinsulin synthesis without a corresponding increase of the ER chaperone BiP. We conclude that one of the key features leading to the phenotype of enhanced β-cell maturity involves enhanced insulin biosynthesis without a concomitant increase in β-cell ER stress.

articles.title: Robot-assisted vs. conventional gait training for balance and gait speed after stroke: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Journal of sport and health science
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balance and gait impairments are common disabling consequences of stroke and central targets of rehabilitation. Robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) can deliver repetitive, task-specific, and quantifiable walking practice, yet its comparative effectiveness over conventional gait-oriented training remains uncertain.

METHODS: We searched 8 English- and Chinese-language databases from inception through June 2, 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing lower-limb RAGT with conventional therapeutic training after stroke. Primary outcomes were balance, assessed with the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) and Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and gait speed. Reports from the same or potentially overlapping trials were linked to minimize participant double-counting. Change-from-baseline mean differences (MDs) were synthesized using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-adjusted 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, sensitivity analyses, small-study effects, and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) certainty of evidence were evaluated.

RESULTS: We included 258 eligible reports representing 240 trial-level units. Post-intervention pooled estimates favored RAGT for BBS (MD = 6.03 points; 95%CI: 5.14-6.93), direction-reversed TUG (MD = 3.04 s; 95%CI: 1.02-5.06), and gait speed (MD = 0.080 m/s; 95%CI: 0.061-0.100). However, between-study heterogeneity was very high across primary outcomes (I² = 89.8%-98.1%), all 95% prediction intervals included the null, and GRADE certainty was low. Sensitivity analyses attenuated key estimates: excluding add-on/extra-RAGT designs reduced the BBS and gait-speed effects, and restriction to reports with PEDro scores ≥ 6 attenuated all 3 primary-outcome estimates, with the TUG 95%CI including the null. Durability evidence was sparse, and most follow-up primary-outcome estimates included the null.

CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that RAGT may provide post-intervention improvements in balance and gait speed after stroke, but their magnitude, consistency, clinical importance, and durability remain uncertain. High heterogeneity, null-inclusive prediction intervals, attenuation in sensitivity analyses, and limited follow-up data argue against interpreting RAGT as clinically superior to conventional therapy. RAGT may be considered an individualized adjunct to gait-oriented rehabilitation when it increases task-specific practice without replacing therapist-directed care.

articles.title: Early Outcomes of Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis in Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Nordic Multicentre Study.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the feasibility and early clinical outcomes of the Gore thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) in the treatment of aortic arch pathologies.

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions. Primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day mortality, and overall survival, while endoleak occurrence, primary target vessel patency, stroke, and spinal cord ischaemia (SCI) were secondary.

RESULTS: Sixty-four patients (median age 73 years [interquartile range 59, 77]; 69% men) were included. Indications for treatment included degenerative aneurysm (n = 26; 41%), chronic dissection (n = 18; 28%), subacute dissection (n = 11; 17%), and acute dissection (n = 9; 14%). The left subclavian artery was the target vessel in 59 cases (92%), followed by the brachiocephalic trunk in three (5%) and the left common carotid artery in two (3%). Technical success was achieved in 95% of cases (n = 61), with failures attributed to two type Ia endoleaks and one type IIIa endoleak. Thirty day mortality was 3% (n = 2). Early unplanned re-interventions occurred in four patients (6%). No strokes or SCI were observed. Median follow up was 6 months (2, 10). No late mortality was observed, and primary patency of all branches was 100%. One late unplanned re-intervention, unrelated to the TBE device, was required. During follow up, 12 patients (19%) had endoleaks, including type II (n = 4), type Ia (n = 4), type Ib (n = 2), type III (n = 1), and type V (n = 1). Estimated freedom from type Ia endoleak at 12 months was 93 ± 3%, while estimated overall survival at 12 months was 97 ± 2%.

CONCLUSION: TBE demonstrated high technical success and acceptable early outcomes across a range of aortic arch pathologies. However, the relatively high rate of endoleaks and need for early re-interventions highlight the importance of careful patient selection and close continuous post-operative surveillance.

articles.title: Quantifying prevalence ratios for asthma, respiratory, and systemic symptoms associated with dampness and mold among school staff: Interpretation of NIOSH DMAT scores.
articles.abstract: Indoor dampness and mold (D/M) are prevalent and represent a significant exposure linked to adverse health outcomes among building occupants. We analyzed 6492 room D/M scores collected from 50 schools using the NIOSH D/M Assessment Tool (DMAT) to quantify the association between D/M exposure and health outcomes, including self-reported physician-diagnosed asthma, and respiratory and non-respiratory symptoms, among 1529 school staff. Prevalence ratios and 90% confidence intervals were estimated via logistic regression with conditional standardization and the delta method. Generalized additive models showed approximately log-linear exposure-response relationships for most outcomes, with statistically significant but slight nonlinearity detected for shortness-of-breath (SOB) attacks, coughing attacks, and building-related dizziness/lightheadedness. Under this log-linear specification, each one-unit increase in DMAT score was associated with a 7-12% increase in the prevalence of asthma and respiratory symptoms, including wheeze, SOB, cough, and stuffy/itchy nose, and with a 6-16% increase in systemic symptoms, including difficulty remembering, confusion, and dizziness/light headedness, and headache, at α = 0.10. A DMAT score of 2.0 was estimated as a preliminary score for increased surveillance, based on an assumed log-linear exposure-response relationship for post-hire onset asthma, its observed prevalence, and DMAT score distribution in the schools. Scores of 2.0 or higher may indicate need for more frequent D/M surveillance and occupant health awareness. For rooms/areas with observed damage, early identification of water-intrusion sources and timely remediation should be considered. Future epidemiologic studies using DMAT will be valuable for further assessing exposure-response relationships and refining the interpretation of DMAT scores.

articles.title: Environmental toxicants associated with cardiovascular disease and a novel LE8 indicator approach for screening potential cardiovascular toxicants.
articles.abstract: Environmental chemicals are emerging as inducers of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but identifying CVD-relevant toxicants across the exposome remains challenging. In this study, we analyzed 149 environmental chemicals from the 2013-2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey using analyte-specific survey-weighted single-pollutant models, mixture analyses, mediation and interaction analyses, and network toxicology to identify CVD-relevant toxicants. Adjusted data found no direct CVD correlations for many chemicals. Yet, using Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score (which covers diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension) as a quantitative cardiovascular health index revealed inverse associations with 41 chemicals after multiple-testing correction. These chemicals mainly included several volatile organic compound (VOC) metabolites, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), and aromatic amines. BKMR analysis further suggested potential CVD associations for selected exposure mixtures, particularly serum metals and urinary PAHs. Exploratory mediation analysis identified significant positive indirect associations through LE8 for 37 chemicals, most of which showed directionally consistent patterns. Interaction analyses also indicated that several exposure-CVD associations may vary by LE8 health behaviors, with smoking-related interactions particularly evident for PAH- and VOC-related chemicals. Network toxicology linked LE8-associated toxicants to CVD-relevant pathways and protein modules involving vascular, cardiometabolic, inflammatory, and hemostatic processes, with PTGS2, ESR1, and MAPK1 among the most frequently connected genes. These findings support LE8 as a effective cardiovascular health indicator, and provide a framework for identifying CVD-relevant chemicals from the exposome via LE8.

articles.title: Effect of bimodal signal biofeedback on the supraglottic swallowing maneuver in patients with post-stroke dysphagia: A randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of bimodal signal biofeedback combining an accelerometer and a nasal airflow sensor on the supraglottic swallowing maneuver in patients with post-stroke dysphagia.

DESIGN: Prospective Randomised Controlled Trial.

SETTING: Single rehabilitation hospital.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients with post-stroke dysphagia.

INTERVENTION: Patients with post-stroke dysphagia were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the control group or the experimental group. The control group received conventional swallowing rehabilitation therapy, including supraglottic swallowing training. The experimental group received the same conventional rehabilitation and supraglottic swallowing training, but was additionally provided with bimodal biofeedback during the maneuver sessions. The training intensity was 30 min/day, 6 days/week, for two consecutive weeks.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Outcome measures included the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), the Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), and temporal and kinematic parameters derived from videofluoroscopic swallowing studies (VFSS). All VFSS parameters were defined and measured according to established protocols. Assessments were conducted at baseline, immediately after the 2-week intervention, and at a one-month follow-up after treatment.

RESULTS: A total of 30 patients were enrolled in the study (15 in the experimental group and 15 in the control group), with no attrition in either group. At both the post-treatment and one-month follow-up assessments, FOIS scores in the experimental group were significantly higher than those in the control group (p < 0.001). Additionally, the percentage of PAS scores ≥ 6 was significantly lower in the experimental group than in the control group after the intervention (p = 0.026).

CONCLUSION: The findings of this study suggest that supraglottic swallowing maneuver assisted with bimodal biofeedback can lead to significant improvements in swallowing function for patients with post-stroke dysphagia.

articles.title: The Effect of Pet Companionship on Clinical Symptoms in Migraine.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder aggravated by anxiety, sleep disturbance, and chronic stress. Prospective evidence linking pet‑keeping to migraine prognosis is scarce. This study evaluated longitudinal associations of pet ownership with migraine symptoms, comorbidities, and medication use, as well as clinical changes after initiating or stopping pet ownership.

METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study enrolled 3017 International Classification of Headache Disorders‑3 (ICHD‑3)‑defined migraine patients with 2‑year standardized follow‑up. Participants were categorized bydynamic pet‑keeping status. Longitudinal outcomes included migraine severity, attack frequency, anxiety, sleep quality, quality of life, and medication utilization; analyses adjusted for baseline imbalances and missing data.

RESULTS: Continuous pet ownership was associated with lower migraine attack frequency, reduced pain severity, decreased medication utilization, alleviated anxiety and sleep disturbances, and improved migraine-specific quality of life over 2-year follow-up (all P<0.001). Dog ownership correlated with more favorable clinical profiles versus cat or other pet ownership (P<0.05). New pet acquisition was associated with significant within-subject improvements in clinical outcomes, whereas discontinuation of pet keeping correlated with the reversal of most clinical benefits. Greater total daily human-pet interaction time exhibited graded associative correlations with clinical improvement magnitude.

CONCLUSION: Stable pet companionship, particularly dog ownership, is favorably associated with improved migraine-related symptoms, comorbid psychological and sleep disturbances, and reduced medication demand. Discontinuation of pet ownership correlates with the attenuation of these observational outcomes. Pet companionship may serve as a feasible non-pharmacological adjuvant consideration for comprehensive migraine management.

articles.title: Leucine-rich α-2-glycoprotein 1 as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target in sepsis: A review.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is primarily characterized by a dysregulated host immune response. Identifying specific biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets has become a critical focus and key challenge in current research. Serum leucine-rich α-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) is significantly elevated in sepsis. We aim to elucidate the potential roles of LRG1 in sepsis and its associated organ dysfunction as a specific biomarker for early diagnosis, prognosis assessment, or as an intervention target. This review summarizes the underlying mechanisms by which LRG1 contributes to the pathogenesis and progression of sepsis, particularly through its involvement in inflammation regulation, vascular function, and cell survival. Additionally, it consolidates current knowledge on LRG1 in sepsis, highlights its clinical application potential, and provides new support for precise diagnosis, prognostic evaluation, and targeted therapy. In conclusion, LRG1 emerges as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for sepsis, playing a crucial role throughout the disease's onset, progression, and prognosis. This review offers new perspectives on LRG1 research and its application in sepsis.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Volume Indexing in Athletic Brazilian Sport Horses Using Body Weight.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) volume assessment evaluates cardiac size and remodelling in horses. Single-plane Simpson method of discs (SMOD) provides volumetric measurements requiring body size normalization.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: We described LV volumes using SMOD in healthy Brazilian Sport Horses (BH) and evaluated thoracic-girth-estimated body weight (BWe) versus scale-measured weight (BWs) for indexing.

METHODS: Thirty BH horses (15 males, 15 females; 4-16 years) underwent echocardiography. LV end-diastolic (LVEDV), end-systolic volumes (LVESV), and ejection fraction (EF%) were obtained using SMOD. Body weight was scale-measured and estimated via thoracic girth formula. Volumes were indexed to BWs, BWe, and a 500-kg reference.

RESULTS: Mean LVEDV was 1060 ± 154 mL (95% CI: 1003-1118), LVESV 318 ± 77 mL (95% CI: 290-347), and EF 70.0 ± 5.4%. Overall, BWe was associated with BWs (R² = 0.61; P < 0.0001) with mean bias of +33.25 kg (limits of agreement: -37.59 to +104.09 kg), mean absolute error of 39 ± 28.83 kg, and percentage error of 8.92 ± 7.27%. LVEDV/BWs averaged 2.30 ± 0.29 mL/kg and LVEDV/BWe 2.15 ± 0.26 mL/kg. Normalization to 500 kg yielded LVEDV[500] of 1151 ± 146 and 1069 ± 131 mL, and LVESV[500] of 346 ± 83 and 321 ± 70 mL (BWs; BWe). Indexed variables showed moderate to strong linear association between methods. In this sample, no sex or age differences were detected.

CONCLUSION: Body weight normalization improved interindividual comparability. While BWe offers a practical field alternative, estimation errors warrant caution in individual evaluations, making BWs preferred.

articles.title: Letter to the editor: Causal inference and treatment selection in metastatic spinal disease with spinal instability neoplastic score 7-12.
Response to the letter to the editor: Causal inference and treatment selection in metastatic spinal disease with SINS 7-12.
Development and Evaluation of a Two-Stage Machine Learning Multivariable Model to Support Clinical Decision-Making in Thrombophilia Management.
articles.abstract: Thrombophilia is a disease characterized by an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. In this single-center, retrospective study, we evaluated the use of a two-stage machine learning (ML) model to predict the thrombophilia risk category and subsequent anticoagulation recommendation. The model was trained and tested using clinical and laboratory data obtained from 496 patients who underwent a complete thrombophilia work-up at the University Hospital Bonn between 2019 and 2024. The hybrid nature of the diagnostic categories, which combine ordinal classes including thrombophilia diagnosis, severity, and treatment recommendations and categorical classes (e.g. antiphospholipid syndrome), necessitated a two-stage approach. First, XGBClassifier was used to distinguish between the two classes, and then an ordinal-specific XGBOrdinalV2 model was used. Performance was assessed across 100 random 80/20 train-test splits. For exact class prediction (primary analysis), mean macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, and precision were 58%, 91%, and 56.2% for diagnosis and 54.4%, 91.3%, and 58.5% for treatment. Performance was highest for frequent classes and poor for rare high-risk classes. When predictions within one adjacent class were accepted (secondary analysis), macro-averaged sensitivity was 91.9% and 86.2%, respectively. Antiphospholipid antibody status, age at first thrombosis, and unprovoked thrombosis were the most influential features for diagnosis. Model predictions and physician decisions were concordant in 395 of 496 patients (79.6%). This study demonstrates that ML models can support standardized thrombophilia management and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Contact Allergy to Textile Dye Mix in Italy: A SIDAPA Multicentre Observational Study.
authors: SIDAPA Study Group SIDAPA Study Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disperse dyes, widely used in synthetic textiles, continue to represent a cause of allergic contact dermatitis despite restrictive European regulations.

OBJECTIVES: To assess prevalence, clinical features, and exposure patterns of Italian patients with positive reactions to the Textile Dye Mix (TDM) 6.6% pet., and to contextualise these findings within European surveillance data and current regulatory frameworks.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective multicentre study was performed using the SIDAPA database on patients consecutively patch-tested with the SIDAPA baseline series from January 2020 to March 2025 in 10 Italian dermatology centres. Demographic, clinical, and occupational data were statistically analysed.

RESULTS: A total of 7633 patients were included. Positive reactions to TDM were found in 281 patients (3.68%), mainly females (77.22%). The mean age was 46.43 ± 17.66 years. Clinical relevance was established in 59.79% of reactions, mainly non-occupational (89.88%). Disperse Orange 3 (tested in 22 TDM positive patients) resulted positive in 14 patients (63.64%). Co-sensitization with para-phenylenediamine occurred in 54.8% of TDM-positive subjects.

CONCLUSIONS: The observed prevalence (3.68%) exceeds that of previous Italian (1.5%) and European (2%-3%) studies, possibly reflecting imports from non-EU countries with limited chemical regulation and e-commerce channels that bypass controls. Improved traceability, updated patch test formulations, and REACH compliance enforcement are essential to mitigate this growing dermatological concern.

articles.title: Endoscopic ultrasound in hepatology: A European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided techniques are increasingly applied in hepatology, including for tissue acquisition, vascular access, pressure measurement, and selected therapeutic interventions. However, adoption remains heterogeneous because of variability in technical approaches, devices, outcome definitions, operator expertise, and the quality of available evidence.

METHODS: This European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review summarizes the current evidence on selected EUS-guided techniques in liver disease and portal hypertension, including liver stiffness assessment, focal liver lesion characterization and sampling, EUS-guided liver biopsy, EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement, therapy for gastric varices, and portal vein sampling for liquid biopsy applications. Evidence was identified through a structured literature search up to April 2026, and recommendation statements were graded using the GRADE framework.

RESULTS: Eight ESGE statements were developed. The available evidence supports selected use of EUS-guided shear wave elastography and contrast-enhanced EUS as adjunctive techniques; EUS-guided liver biopsy and EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement as complementary approaches in selected patients and expert centers; and EUS-guided treatment of gastric varices as a valid alternative to direct endoscopic injection where appropriate expertise is available. Portal vein sampling remains investigational. Across the indications, the evidence base is limited by small studies, heterogeneous techniques, variable outcome definitions, and limited prospective comparative data.

CONCLUSIONS: This review provides an evidence-based framework for the selective use of EUS-guided techniques in hepatology and portal hypertension. Wider adoption will require standardized techniques, structured training, consistent outcome definitions, and prospective comparative studies.

articles.title: Cold versus hot snare endoscopic mucosal resection for 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence for cold snare endoscopic mucosal resection (CS-EMR) in 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps is scarce. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare CS-EMR against hot snare EMR (HS-EMR) in this setting.

METHODS: We enrolled patients with 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps from 15 centers. Eligible polyps were individually randomized (1:1) to CS-EMR or HS-EMR. The primary outcome was histologic complete resection, analyzed in modified intention-to-treat (mITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations (noninferiority margin -10%). Secondary outcomes included en bloc resection, intraprocedural and delayed adverse events, and resection time.

RESULTS: 216 patients with 233 eligible polyps were included (CS-EMR 116; HS-EMR 117). In the mITT analysis, complete resection was 90.4% in the CS-EMR group and 93.2% in the HS-EMR group (difference -2.7%, 95%CI -9.8 to 4.3), showing noninferiority of CS-EMR vs. HS-EMR. PP results were consistent (CS-EMR 93.3%; HS-EMR 93.2%; difference 0.2%, 95%CI -6.7 to 7.1). CS-EMR was noninferior for 10-14-mm polyps (94.3% vs. 94.0%; 95%CI -6.8 to 7.2) but not for 15-19-mm polyps (78.6% vs. 90.9%; 95%CI -30.4 to 5.8), although interaction was not significant. En bloc resection rates and resection time were similar between groups. Intraprocedural bleeding was more frequent with CS-EMR (19.1% vs. 3.4%), whereas delayed bleeding was rare (0.0% vs. 0.9%), and no perforation occurred in either group.

CONCLUSION: CS-EMR was noninferior to HS-EMR for histologic complete resection of 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps, but its applicability to 15-19-mm lesions remains uncertain.

articles.title: NeuroTest: a benchtop testbed for evaluating sensing-capable electrophysiology and neurostimulation systems.
articles.abstract: The development of increasingly complex implantable neuromodulation devices requires extensive benchtop validation and testing prior to in vivo implementation. Our goal is to enable this in vitro testing by creating a benchtop system that is accessible, easy-to-use, and functions reliably across academic and industry environments, reducing discordant results that arise from discordant approaches. Furthermore, such a system paves the way for standardizing benchtop characterization of future implantable systems by establishing a repeatable and comparable methodology for validating these devices and their capabilities. Approach. We describe the NeuroTest Board (NTB), a low-cost, open-source device that combines a low-noise current source waveform generator with a high-precision data acquisition system. We provide information on its architecture, operation, and performance as an initial benchmark of the potential capabilities of the system. Main results. We demonstrate the use of the NTB to assess electrophysiology systems in two separate applications. In one case, we assess a commonly used laboratory system (the RHD2132 headstage and Open Ephys data acquisition system), while the second case characterizes an investigational neuromodulation device in development for human use (the CorTec Brain InterChange). Following this initial sensing characterization, we explore stimulation-related artifacts that would hamper in vivo data collection. With the NTB, we develop and evaluate artifact mitigation strategies for each system, thus demonstrating an example application of this benchtop testbed. Significance. The ability to test neuromodulation devices against a common benchmark will enable faster development of novel therapeutics by increasing inter-institutional reliability and decreasing troubleshooting time.

articles.title: Silent Ears, Failing Heart: Dilated Cardiomyopathy in an Infant With LARS2-Related Perrault Syndrome Type 4 (PRLTS4).
articles.abstract: We report a 19-month-old girl with molecularly confirmed Perrault syndrome type 4 (PRLTS4), due to a homozygous LARS2 variant (c.457A>C, p.Asn153His), who developed dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 21%) at 2 months of age despite a normal neonatal echocardiogram, alongside bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss and global developmental delay. No second causative cardiac variant was identified. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of dilated cardiomyopathy in molecularly confirmed LARS2-related PRLTS4, expanding the recognised phenotypic spectrum of this disorder and supporting cardiac surveillance in affected infants.

articles.title: Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management.
articles.journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND BACKGROUND: Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) is a rare but clinically important cause of mesenteric ischemia. It most often affects the superior mesenteric vein and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Nonspecific symptoms often delay diagnosis. Severe disease courses may occur in the presence of intestinal infarction.

OBJECTIVE AND BACKGROUND: The aim of this article is to provide a structured overview of the etiopathogenesis, imaging findings, and interventional radiological treatment options for MVT.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative, literature-based review taking into consideration current guidelines, radiological imaging protocols, and endovascular techniques.

RESULTS: The pathogenesis of MVT can be classified according to Virchow's triad, including hypercoagulability, stasis, and endothelial injury. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the method of choice for diagnosis. It demonstrates thrombosis as a contrast filling defect within the portomesenteric venous system and allows assessment of bowel viability. Important CT findings include bowel wall thickening, mesenteric edema, ascites, and the halo or target sign. Pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas suggest transmural ischemia and indicate the need for immediate surgical management. Systemic anticoagulation is the cornerstone of treatment. Mechanical thrombectomy, local thrombolysis, stent angioplasty, and, where appropriate, TIPS placement may be considered in complex or prolonged clinical courses.

CONCLUSION: Early interdisciplinary, imaging-guided management is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. CT guides further management by detecting thrombosis and assessing bowel viability. Interventional radiological recanalization is not a first-line treatment, but it may represent an important escalation strategy in selected patients.

KEY POINTS: · Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon but clinically relevant cause of mesenteric ischemia.. · Early interdisciplinary diagnostic work-up is essential to prevent irreversible intestinal ischemic injury.. · Contrast-enhanced CT represents the key imaging modality, enabling both detection of venous thrombosis and assessment of bowel viability.. · In the absence of contraindications, systemic anticoagulation constitutes the cornerstone of treatment.. · Surgical management is indicated in the presence of suspected transmural bowel necrosis or clinical signs of peritonitis.. · Interventional radiological recanalization techniques may be considered as an escalation strategy in selected patients..

CITATION FORMAT: · Camp LC, Weber M, Arndt H. Mesenteric Vein Thrombosis and Its Interventional-Radiological Management. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2965-8425.

articles.title: From Microbiome Profiling to Clinical Translation: Designing microbiome studies for clinical actionability.
articles.abstract: Microbiome research has identified many highly valuable associations between microbial communities and factors such as diet, antibiotics use, lifestyle, inflammation, infection and chronic disease. However, many findings remain difficult to translate into clinical practice because they are only association-based and vulnerable to confounding. Many studies also often lack reproducibility. Comparisons between "dysbiotic" and "healthy" microbiome states can be misleading because microbiome profiles are shaped by factors such as diet, medication, geography, host genetics, demographics, disease severity and reverse causation. Moreover, there remains no universally accepted definition or consensus regarding what constitutes a ''healthy'' microbiota. What in one individual may be considered a healthy mix of species may not necessarily serve another individual whose diet and lifestyle is completely different. The microbiome research must move beyond descriptive profiling toward clinically actionable and mechanistically informed study designs. The key barriers include small cohort sizes, inconsistent sample collection and treatment, differences in sequencing methods, constantly evolving bioinformatic pipelines, limited availability of raw data, and differences between OTU- and ASV-based analyses. To support a large-scale population studies and meta-analysis a transparent reporting along with shared analytical workflows are essential for progress in this field. Microbiome signatures should not only be reproducible, biologically plausible and modifiable but also linked to the treatment decisions or improved outcomes. This requires longitudinal modelling, external validation, mechanistic studies, and eventually interventional or pragmatic trials. The need for standardisation and reproducibility in microbiome research is widely recognised. This paper builds on that foundation by proposing an actionability-focused framework for designing translational microbiome studies. Using Type 2 Diabetes treatment as a worked example demonstrates that microbiome features should be evaluated not only for their statistical associations, but also for the additional predictive value they provide beyond established clinical variables.

articles.title: Association of Altered Anteriorization of Electroencephalographic Alpha Oscillation During Transition to Unconsciousness With Postoperative Delirium: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium.

METHODS: This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review.

RESULTS: Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency.

CONCLUSIONS: Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

articles.title: Urban water, sanitation, and hygiene service gaps in Ethiopia: Potential public health risks and policy implications.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study is to investigate urban Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) service gaps, their socio-demographic determinants, and public health and policy implications in Ethiopia STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional mixed methods study design was conducted.

METHODS: A survey of 384 purposively selected urban households across 16 cities in eight regions and one city administration was conducted using multi-stage stratified sampling. Data was collected via structured questionnaires, 38 institutional surveys of water utilities, 25 key informant interviews, and 70 focus group discussions. Quantitative data were analysed with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression (SPSS v25); qualitative data underwent thematic analysis with methodological triangulation.

RESULTS: Although 87.8% of households used piped water, 71.2% faced access barriers, 71.4% experienced intermittent supply, and 48.7% consumed <20 L/capita/day. Sanitation relied on pit latrines (80.3%), but 62.4% had never been emptied. Only 26.9% of households had both water and soap at handwashing stations. Significant associations existed between household tenure and sanitation quality (χ2 = 14.82, p = 0.001), gender and hygiene access (p = 0.013), education and handwashing facilities (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.52-3.54, p < 0.001), and female-headed households and handwashing (OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.10-2.51, p = 0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: Urban WASH failures exacerbate water-washed and fecal-oral disease risks and violate constitutional rights to a clean environment. Strengthened infrastructure, equitable service delivery to informal settlements, fecal-sludge management, and hygiene subsidies are urgently required.

articles.title: Florence Nightingale as a pioneer of applied statistics: Data, visualization, and the foundations of modern healthcare quality improvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Florence Nightingale (1820-1910) is widely recognized as the founder of modern nursing, yet her influence extends into applied statistics, data visualization, and data-driven reform.

PURPOSE: This conceptual historical analysis reframes Nightingale as an early applied statistician, emphasizing her systematic data collection, analytic reasoning, and innovative graphics to influence health policy and institutional change.

METHODS: Drawing on nineteenth-century developments in statistical graphics and her collaboration with William Farr, the article moves beyond the polar area diagram to examine her broader graphical and tabular toolkit. It then considers how her mortality data can be reinterpreted using interrupted time-series methods, comparative dashboards, and modern hospital safety analytics, while noting limitations of nineteenth-century data systems.

DISCUSSION: By linking Nightingale's work to contemporary infection prevention, hospital harm surveillance, and performance dashboards, the analysis positions her as an early architect of data-driven quality improvement.

CONCLUSION: Nightingale's work underscores nursing's longstanding role in evidence-based leadership and systems reform.

articles.title: Reappraising Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Patients With Cancer.
Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies.

RESULTS: Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF (<50 years) more often had alcohol-related mental and behavioral disorders, gout, and dilated cardiomyopathy, while older patients (>60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations.

CONCLUSIONS: This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

articles.title: Predictors of HIV reservoir size and decay dynamics in early-treated paediatric infection: a prospective, multicentre longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early antiretroviral therapy (ART) after perinatal HIV infection can restrict reservoir size and diversity, offering potential for remission. We evaluated HIV-1 DNA dynamics up to four years of age and predictors of reservoir size in early-treated African children.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre cohort study, infants with perinatal HIV from South Africa, Mozambique, and Mali who initiated ART before 6 months of age and within 3 months of diagnosis were enrolled. Children were followed at 2, 6, 12, and 24 weeks, then biannually for 4 years. Total HIV-1 DNA in PBMCs was quantified longitudinally by droplet digital PCR in 207 children. The main outcomes were HIV-1 DNA reservoir size at year 3 (log10 copies/million PBMC) and longitudinal HIV-1 DNA decay. Multivariable models were developed to identify predictors of reservoir size using generalised additive regression models, and decay dynamics were evaluated using mixed-effects Poisson models including random intercepts and viral load slopes.

FINDINGS: Of 207 children, 155 (75%) had >12 months of follow-up. HIV was diagnosed at a median age of 31 days (IQR: 0, 47) and ART started at 33 days (IQR: 23.5, 69.5). Nineteen of 155 (12.3%) had undetectable HIV-1 DNA at year 4. Median decay rate was -0.020 log10 copies/million cells/month (-0.212/year). Smaller reservoirs at year 3 were associated with lower pre-ART viral load (β = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.09, 0.43) and faster first-year HIV-1 DNA decay rate (β = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.02, 2.19), with trends toward smaller reservoirs among females (β = -0.41, 95% CI: -0.87, 0.04) and larger reservoirs among children whose mothers reported social challenges (β = 0.42, 95% CI: -0.04, 0.87). Faster decay correlated with longer time on ART, lower serial viral loads, sustained viral suppression >12 months, earlier ART initiation, and region (Mali). Maternal health issues correlated with slower decay. Eleven "excellent controllers" maintained durable viral suppression, immunological control, and undetectable total HIV-1 DNA at last follow-up.

INTERPRETATION: Early virological parameters may help identify children likely to develop smaller HIV reservoirs. Early ART is key to faster reservoir reduction. Maternal health issues influence reservoir decay, reflecting a parental legacy effect. Sex differences should be further explored to understand mechanisms of reservoir control. Children with sustained virological suppression, preserved immune status, and undetectable total HIV-1 DNA may represent candidates with favourable characteristics for HIV remission strategies, as these factors have been associated with a reduced burden of persistent HIV infection and have been observed in rare cases of post-treatment control.

FUNDING: EPIICAL consortium through ViiV Healthcare and Penta Foundation.

articles.title: Infant gut microbiome neuroactive pathways link to social disadvantage, toddler neurodevelopment, cognitive and behavioural outcomes: a longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early life is a critical window for co-development of the brain and gut microbiome (GM). Evidence supports a role for the GM in brain development, but longitudinal human data remain limited, particularly regarding the influence of social disadvantage (SD), a powerful determinant of child mental health and neurodevelopment. Here, we examine longitudinal relationships between the GM and neurodevelopmental outcomes over the first three years of life, and the impact of SD on them.

METHODS: We sequenced and analysed stool samples of 187 children, collected at 5 timepoints over 4-36 months of life (MOL; 905 samples) using a whole-metagenome sequencing approach. Associations between GM-derived Gut-Brain Modules (GBM) and neuroactive potential were assessed using generalised linear mixed models, adjusting for covariates. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were evaluated by Bayley-III (cognitive, language, and motor), and neurobehavioural dysregulation and externalising/internalising-behaviour by the Infant-Toddler Social and Emotional Assessment (ITSEA) and Preschool Age Psychiatric Assessment (PAPA).

FINDINGS: Temporal changes were observed in GBMs, including glutamate/GABA synthesis and degradation pathways, as well as short-chain fatty acids. GM community structure and GBMs were significantly associated with concurrent and later Bayley-III outcomes, most consistently for cognition and language (FDR < 0.10). Several GBMs were associated with both neurobehavioural outcomes and SD, including S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) synthesis, butyrate synthesis, and glutamate and GABA synthesis II (FDR < 0.10). A partial mediating effect between SD and 36 MOL language outcomes was observed using SAM synthesis at 4 MOL (β = -0.042, P = 0.048).

INTERPRETATION: This longitudinal cohort study of GM neuroactive metabolic capacity across early transitional developmental windows reveals a dynamic pattern of GM-derived neuroactive metabolic pathways and identifies specific pathways associated with later neurodevelopmental (cognitive, language) and neurobehavioural outcomes, even after controlling for important covariates. These pathways are shaped by the socioeconomic status of mothers, starting with in-utero exposure, and GBMs partially mediated this effect. The study identifies microbial pathways associated with both SD and neurodevelopmental outcomes, highlighting potential biological processes that may contribute to neurodevelopmental risk and warrant further investigation.

FUNDING: This work was supported by the National Institute of Mental Health, March of Dimes, Children's Discovery Institute, National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, and National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences.

articles.title: Evidence-based assessment of parental needs in neonatal intensive care.
Incidence and clinical impact of venous thromboembolism during immunotherapy for gynecologic cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with gynecologic cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with ICI at a single institution between January 2017 and April 2026. The primary outcome was the development of VTE from ICI initiation through one month after the final cycle. Incidence, clinical characteristics, risk factors, and healthcare utilization were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 458 patients who received ICI therapy, 37 (8.1%) experienced a VTE. Deep vein thrombosis was the most common event (48.6%, n = 18), followed by pulmonary embolism (40.5%, n = 15). The median time from ICI initiation to VTE was 1.43 months (IQR, 0.70-2.93). Endometrial cancer was the most common disease site among patients with VTE (54.1%, n = 20). Smoking history differed significantly between groups (p < 0.01). ICI monotherapy was more common among patients who experienced VTE compared with those who did not (64.9% vs. 44.9%, p = 0.020), and patients with VTE had received fewer total lines of therapy (2.4 vs. 3.3, p = 0.008). Most events required emergency department evaluation (64.9%, n = 24) and hospitalization (59.5%, n = 22), and ICI therapy was delayed in 24.3% (n = 9) of cases. Breakthrough thrombosis was observed in 18.9% (n = 7) of patients receiving anticoagulation.

CONCLUSION: VTE occurred in 8.1% of gynecologic cancer patients receiving ICI, was early in onset, and carried significant clinical burden. These data can guide provider awareness and patient counseling when initiating ICI in this population.

articles.title: Low-grade serous ovarian cancer: 2026 expert consensus report.
articles.abstract: Low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) is a rare epithelial malignancy characterized by frequent mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway alterations, hormone receptor expression, relative resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy, and a prolonged, relapsing clinical course. Since publication of the 2023 international expert consensus, significant advances have reshaped the management of both newly diagnosed and recurrent disease. The 2026 LGSOC Consensus Conference convened an international multidisciplinary panel of experts in the field to review emerging evidence and update recommendations across pathology, molecular testing, translational biology, frontline and recurrent treatment, imaging, treatment-associated toxicity, regulatory strategy, patient advocacy, and future research priorities. Recommendations were informed by contemporary clinical evidence, multidisciplinary discussion, and patient perspectives. The updated consensus incorporates practice-changing data from NRG-GY019 supporting chemotherapy-containing postoperative therapy as the current reference approach for stage II-IV disease while recognizing selected circumstances in which endocrine monotherapy may represent individualized de-escalation. It also integrates recent advances in recurrent disease, including the US Food and Drug Administration's accelerated approval of avutometinib in combination with defactinib for KRAS-mutated LGSOC, emerging evidence supporting endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibition, and refined guidance for biomarker-directed treatment selection, imaging assessment, toxicity management, and patient-centered survivorship. The panel emphasizes treatment-specific biomarker interpretation, multidisciplinary care, central pathology review for clinical trials, and the continued need for prospective studies addressing treatment sequencing, predictive biomarkers, and quality-of-life outcomes. This updated international consensus provides an evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of LGSOC while identifying priorities for future clinical research and drug development.

articles.title: A cross-sectional survey exploring experiences in accessing hormone replacement therapy following risk-reducing surgery for individuals with hereditary ovarian cancer risk.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the current landscape of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to treat surgical menopause following bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) in individuals with hereditary ovarian cancer risk in British Columbia, Canada. We aimed to describe current use of HRT, identify factors associated with HRT use and identify potential barriers for uptake and access.

METHODS: Individuals with germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in an ovarian cancer susceptibility gene were identified through the BC Cancer Hereditary Cancer Program (HCP) Progeny database. A cross-sectional survey was administered to collect participant demographics, personal and family cancer history, and participant experiences with HRT. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the sample and logistic regression used to explore associations between sociodemographic variables and reported HRT use. Open text fields were analyzed using inductive quantitative content analysis.

RESULTS: In total, 374 responses were received from 1284 potential participants (29.1% response rate). Of participants who have had a BSO, 41% (101/245) report HRT use. In open-text responses, 22% of participants reported lack of support by healthcare professionals and 26% described gaps in counselling about HRT and surgical menopause. In the regression analysis, HRT use was less likely in individuals who: were of increasing age, reported a history of any cancer type and who reported receiving no counselling about HRT (all p < 0.0011 after Bonferroni correction).

CONCLUSION: Barriers to HRT access and uptake exist for individuals at increased risk of ovarian cancer. Together this data indicates that patients require additional support in this area particularly as it relates to education and resources.

articles.title: Pulmonary diffusion capacity to select patients for echocardiographic evaluation of pulmonary hypertension in interstitial lung disease: Impact of interstitial lung disease phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treprostinil inhalation for pulmonary hypertension (PH) with interstitial lung disease (ILD) has increased the importance of PH screening. We aimed to determine whether pulmonary function tests performed for ILD management could identify patients with possible PH on echocardiography, according to ILD subtype.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, patients with ILD who underwent pulmonary function tests and echocardiography within three months were enrolled consecutively. The correlation between pulmonary function test results and peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV) was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. We defined possible PH as peak TRV > 2.8 m/s. The screening performance for possible PH was evaluated using ROC analysis.

RESULTS: In total, 278 patients were analysed. Among pulmonary function test values, percent predicted diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (%DLCO) most significantly correlated with TRV (ρ = -0.468, p < 0.001). In the ROC curve analysis for identifying possible PH, %DLCO exhibited the highest area under the curve (AUC) of 0.750. The AUC for combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE), idiopathic interstitial pneumonias (IIPs), and collagen vascular disease-related interstitial pneumonia (CVD-IP) were 0.856, 0.747, and 0.671, respectively. Among patients with IIPs, the AUC was higher when Brinkman Index was ≥600 than when it was <600 (0.881 vs 0.620).

CONCLUSIONS: Based on numerical trends, %DLCO showed potentially high screening performance in patients with CPFE or IIPs with a history of heavy smoking. Echocardiographic evaluation for possible PH may be warranted in this population with reduced %DLCO.

articles.title: Noninvasive respiratory therapy: A physiology-oriented approach across acute, chronic, home, and palliative care settings.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive respiratory therapy has evolved from a strategy used to avoid endotracheal intubation in selected forms of acute respiratory failure into a broader framework encompassing acute care, chronic respiratory failure, sleep-disordered breathing, home respiratory support, pulmonary rehabilitation, and palliative care. The term now encompasses conventional oxygen therapy, high-flow nasal cannula therapy, continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel noninvasive ventilation, home noninvasive ventilation, home high-flow therapy, and positive airway pressure therapy for sleep-related breathing disorders. This review proposes a physiology-oriented approach. Rather than selecting a device solely according to the disease, clinicians should identify the dominant physiological problem: impaired oxygenation, alveolar hypoventilation, upper-airway obstruction, increased work of breathing, respiratory muscle fatigue, impaired secretion clearance, or the need for comfort-oriented support. In acute care, noninvasive ventilation is well established for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure due to COPD exacerbations and for acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema, whereas high-flow nasal cannula therapy, continuous positive airway pressure, and noninvasive ventilation require more careful selection in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. In chronic care, home noninvasive ventilation and home high-flow therapy should be understood as components of long-term respiratory care systems rather than as simple device prescriptions. Practical success depends on appropriate interface selection, leak control, humidification, patient-device synchrony, airway clearance, patient education, and safe monitoring. A physiology-oriented and patient-centered framework may improve the appropriate use of noninvasive respiratory therapy across the continuum of care.

articles.title: Dynamic chest radiography-derived low-motion area ratio as a potential exploratory quantitative biomarker of idiopathic pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (iPPFE) is a rare type of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia characterized by upper-lobe-predominant pleural and subpleural fibrosis. Dynamic chest radiography (DCR) enables real-time assessment of respiratory motion using quantitative parameters such as diaphragm excursion, projected lung area, and low-motion area (LMA). However, its clinical utility in iPPFE remains unclear. We evaluated whether DCR-derived parameters, particularly the LMA ratio, reflect respiratory mechanical abnormalities in iPPFE.

METHODS: In total, 302 patients who underwent DCR were retrospectively analyzed. After excluding patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema, or preoperative thoracic malignancy, 107 patients were classified into the iPPFE, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, other interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), and control groups. The clinical characteristics, pulmonary function, and DCR parameters of the four groups were compared. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with iPPFE.

RESULTS: The iPPFE group had a significantly lower diaphragm excursion and change in projected lung area, and a significantly higher LMA and LMA ratio than the other groups. A low body mass index (BMI) and a high LMA ratio were independent factors associated with iPPFE.
