The difference in the LMA ratio remained significant after propensity score matching for age, sex, BMI, and %FVC between patients with iPPFE and those with non-iPPFE ILDs.

CONCLUSIONS: The LMA ratio is independently associated with iPPFE and may serve as an exploratory biomarker of impaired respiratory mechanics in iPPFE.

articles.title: From discovery to innovation in animal health: meeting report of the second DIAH conference.
articles.journal: Biologicals : journal of the International Association of Biological Standardization
articles.abstract: The second Discovery to Innovation in Animal Health (DIAH) Conference, held in Bruges, Belgium, brought together academic researchers, start-ups, industry, investors, regulators and funders to accelerate translation of scientific discoveries into veterinary products. The conference highlighted that successful translation requires early alignment between researchers and industry, sustained public-private funding and realistic market assessment. A clear target product profile, target-species proof-of-concept data, preliminary safety information, intellectual property protection, manufacturing plans and early regulatory dialogue were identified as central elements of an investable development package. Companion-animal markets are expanding rapidly in different segments, particularly products for age-related chronic diseases, behavioural disorders, and specialised diagnostics, while livestock innovation remains driven by prevention of infectious disease, antimicrobial and antiparasitic resistance, climate pressures and labour constraints. Emerging technologies presented included digital monitoring and artificial intelligence, alternatives to antimicrobials, novel antiparasitics, monoclonal antibodies and nanobodies, stem-cell and gene therapies, advanced vaccine platforms and mucosal delivery systems. Start-ups are increasingly important sources of innovation, but require credible commercial strategies, realistic valuation, scalable manufacturing and appropriate partnerships. Early engagement mechanisms offered by regulatory agencies can clarify evidence requirements and support development of novel therapies. Overall, DIAH demonstrated that multidisciplinary collaboration, shared terminology and early integration of scientific, regulatory, manufacturing and commercial perspectives are essential to de-risk innovation and deliver impactful animal health solutions.

articles.title: Clinical factors associated with noninvasive ventilation-associated pneumonia in acute respiratory failure: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is preferred to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) as treatment for acute respiratory failure due to its lower complication rate, but NIV may still be associated with serious complications such as nosocomial pneumonia. However, risk factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate factors associated with NIV-associated pneumonia in patients treated with NIV for acute respiratory failure in a respiratory intensive care unit.

METHOD: In this prospective cohort study, we followed adult patients who were admitted to a respiratory intensive care unit in a tertiary hospital for acute respiratory failure. None of the patients had pneumonia on admission. All patients were treated with NIV and monitored daily for the development of nosocomial pneumonia, which was defined using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia.

RESULT: Among 191 eligible patients admitted between March 2023 and May 2024, 84 developed NIV-associated pneumonia. Age was not independently associated with pneumonia development. In multivariable analysis, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and longer NIV duration were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia. Patients who developed pneumonia also had longer ICU stay and higher rates of antibiotic modification.

CONCLUSION: In patients receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure, poor oral hygiene, poor secretion control, and prolonged NIV exposure were independently associated with NIV-associated pneumonia, whereas chronological age, sepsis, and frailty were not. These findings suggest that clinical factors related to bedside care and NIV exposure may be more relevant to pneumonia development than age alone.

articles.title: Estimating progress on hepatitis C elimination targets among people in contact with drug services in Scotland: National retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scotland's HCV elimination strategy has focused efforts on scaling up treatment in community-based settings, with population-based surveys indicating substantial reductions in HCV prevalence among people who inject drugs. We aimed to evaluate progress against World Health Organization (WHO) elimination targets using a national virtual cohort of individuals in contact with drug services in Scotland.

METHODS: The cohort was formed utilizing national administrative databases (including opioid agonist therapy prescribing, drug-related hospitalizations and specialist drug treatment) and linked to HCV databases to ascertain diagnosed infection status during January 2015-March 2024. Multi-state and logistic regression models were used to estimate undiagnosed infection among individuals not tested during follow-up.

RESULTS: Among 78,444 individuals who attended drug services, 15,851 (20.2%) had died or migrated during follow-up. Among 62,593 remaining in the prevalent cohort, 12,553 had been diagnosed with HCV, with 86.8% treated. We estimated 2415 (95% CI 1827-3467) individuals had undiagnosed HCV; thus, 83.2% (77.0%-86.9%) of infection had been diagnosed. Prevalence decreased by an estimated 71.7% (66.0%-75.1%), accounting for estimated undiagnosed infection. During January 2015-March 2024, estimated (diagnosed and undiagnosed) HCV incidence was 1.73 (1.56-2.05) and 2.13 (1.97-2.46) per 100 person-years for the overall cohort and those with a recent opioid-related drug service attendance, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Scotland has made significant progress towards HCV elimination targets, with high levels of diagnosis and treatment achieved among people in contact with a broad range of drug services. Further, we demonstrate that linkage of administrative data has an important role to play in evaluating progress on HCV elimination.

articles.title: Consensus on current clinical workflow and future use of 3D models in parotid gland tumor surgery: A Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: MRI-based 3D models provide patient-specific spatial information on the relationship between parotid gland tumors and the facial nerve. However, their potential role in clinical practice and the level of support for their implementation remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the level of consensus among surgeons on the current clinical workflows in parotid gland surgery and the future role of 3D models.

STUDY DESIGN: We used a three-round Delphi study to explore consensus among surgeons performing more than five parotid surgeries annually. Round 1 consisted of semi-structured interviews about parotid surgery, innovations, and the use of 3D models. Inductive analysis was used to formulate statements and questions for round 2. In rounds 2 and 3, participants rated the questions and statements on a 7-point adjective scale.

RESULTS: A panel of 15 surgeons, including 9 otolaryngologists and 6 oral and maxillofacial surgeons from nine Dutch hospitals, completed all study rounds. Partial consensus was observed for 10% of statements in round 3. Trends toward greater importance of both MRI scanning and 3D model use were identified in cases involving malignancy, facial nerve dysfunction, deep lobe tumors, fixed tumors, non-palpable tumors, and indications for a mastoidectomy. Stronger trends toward importance were observed for using 3D models in preoperative planning and patient counseling than in their use during surgery.

CONCLUSION: Although consensus was limited, this study identified indications for MRI use and highlighted the perceived value of 3D models in parotid gland tumor surgery.

articles.title: Neuroinflammatory mechanisms and pharmacological modulation of the lung-brain axis in post-viral pulmonary sequelae.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent respiratory sequelae following acute viral infections, exemplified by but not limited to coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), represent a major unmet clinical challenge. Conventional anti-inflammatory strategies frequently fail to resolve these chronic symptoms, suggesting that additional pathogenic mechanisms, particularly neuroinflammatory processes, remain unaddressed.

MAIN BODY: This review synthesizes current evidence establishing neuroimmune axis dysfunction as an important mechanistic contributor to post-viral pulmonary sequelae, including chronic cough, airway hyperresponsiveness, and fibrotic remodeling. We systematically examine how viral infection alters the nervous system, and how these neural changes initiate and perpetuate neuroimmune axis dysfunction, subsequently orchestrating aberrant peripheral immune activation while impairing lung repair processes. Moreover, we critically appraise the emerging pharmacological landscape targeting this neuroinflammatory axis, spanning neuropeptide receptor antagonists, neuromodulation, and other mechanism-based strategies aimed at restoring neuroimmune homeostasis.

CONCLUSION: This review identifies neuroimmune axis dysfunction as a potential driver of persistent pulmonary sequelae and underscores the need for therapeutic strategies tailored to disease stage and clinical phenotype to enhance clinical translation.

articles.title: Efficacy of whole-body vibration training in the management of patients with COPD: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often presents with skeletal muscle dysfunction, which worsens prognosis. Whole-body vibration training (WBVT) has been proposed as an adjunct to pulmonary rehabilitation, but evidence of its clinical efficacy remains inconsistent.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of WBVT on functional capacity, muscle strength, pulmonary function, and quality of life in individuals with COPD.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. Only randomized controlled trials were included. Outcomes assessed included 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), five-repetition sit-to-stand test (5STS), pulmonary function, and quality of life.

RESULTS: Fifteen RCTs met the inclusion criteria. WBVT significantly improved functional capacity measured by the 6MWD (MD = 34.35 m; 95% CI: 13.67,55.04; GRADE: very low). Subgroup analysis revealed a clinically meaningful improvement compared with usual care (MD = 75.97 m; 95% CI: 58.65,93.30), but not when compared with active exercise interventions. For the 5STS, a clinically relevant gain was observed versus usual care (MD = -5.95 seconds; 95% CI: -10.76, -1.14), with no significant difference compared to conventional exercise. No statistically significant effects were found for FEV₁ or quality of life. Most trials presented high risk of bias, and evidence certainty ranged from low to very low.

CONCLUSION: WBVT may offer benefits in walking distance and sit-to-stand performance only when compared with no rehabilitation exposure, a scenario that is unrealistic in contemporary clinical practice given the strong evidence supporting structured exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation for COPD management.

articles.title: Expert consensus on the clinical and organizational use of VNS therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy in the United Arab Emirates: a single-round modified Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects over 50 million people worldwide, and approximately one third of patients develop drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), a major driver of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulatory treatment option for DRE, but local guidance on its use in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) remains limited. This study aimed to establish an expert consensus to define best practices for the effective and efficient use of the VNS in the UAE setting.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary Task Force conducted a literature review and developed 25 evidence- and experience-informed statements, which were refined during an in-person expert meeting to ensure clinical relevance for the UAE context. Statements were rated through a single-round modified Delphi process involving UAE neurologists and neurosurgeons. Participants rated their agreement with each statement using a 7-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement, corresponding to ratings of 6-7. Statements with 60-69% agreement were classified as moderate agreement but were not considered to have reached consensus.

RESULTS: Fifty-six experts completed the Delphi round, corresponding to a 75.7% response rate. Item-level denominators varied across statements. Eighteen of 25 statements reached consensus, six demonstrated moderate agreement, and one did not reach consensus. Strong agreement was observed for patient selection, safety, structured parameter optimization, and multidisciplinary care pathways. Moderate agreement emerged for presurgical evaluation, timing of implantation, and selected clinical scenarios.

CONCLUSION: Building on existing international guidance and previous Delphi work in other settings, this study provides a UAE-specific description of expert agreement and variability on the clinical and organizational use of VNS for DRE. The findings may inform future local pathway development and identify areas requiring clearer definitions, prospective data collection, and further evidence generation.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: This study asked expert clinicians in the United Arab Emirates to rate 25 statements on the clinical and organizational use of vagus nerve stimulation for drug-resistant epilepsy. Vagus nerve stimulation is an adjunctive treatment that aims to reduce seizure burden and improve patient-centred outcomes; it should not be interpreted primarily as a treatment intended to achieve complete seizure freedom. Eighteen statements reached the prespecified consensus threshold, while six showed moderate agreement and one did not reach consensus. Experts showed agreement on several areas, including multidisciplinary care, safety considerations, MRI compatibility, structured follow-up, and individualized programming. However, agreement was more limited for some topics, including expected responder rates after one year, timing of implantation, selected programming criteria, and quality-of-life effects independent of seizure reduction. These findings identify areas where expert views are aligned and areas where practice remains variable. They may support the development of more consistent local care pathways, while highlighting topics that require further clinical evidence and local guidance.

articles.title: Adult aphasic status epilepticus: A systematic review and patient-level synthesis of clinical phenotypes and multimodal diagnostic evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is an uncommon manifestation of focal status epilepticus in which aphasia is the sole or predominant clinical feature. Recognition may be difficult because consciousness can be relatively preserved, convulsive activity may be absent, and the presentation can mimic acute stroke.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize diagnostic phenotypes of adult ASE and synthesize clinical, electrographic, and neuroimaging features across published cases.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and patient-level synthesis of adult ASE cases. Eligible patients were adjudicated as definite or probable ASE using prespecified criteria. Clinical phenotype, electroencephalographic (EEG) findings, neuroimaging, initial diagnostic impressions, treatment, and language outcomes were extracted.

RESULTS: Ninety-nine publications contributed 168 adults with ASE, including 89 definite and 79 probable cases. Aphasia was the sole manifestation in 42.9% and predominant in 57.1%, while consciousness was preserved in 78.0%. Ictal EEG activity or electrographic status epilepticus was documented in 53.0%, and 41.7% had supportive epileptiform abnormalities. Among cases with interpretable EEG laterality, 92.7% were left-lateralized. Peri-ictal MRI abnormalities occurred in 41.2% of performed interpretable studies. Among 55 patients with interpretable functional perfusion or metabolic imaging, hyperperfusion was reported in 32. FDG-PET hypermetabolism was treated as a distinct metabolic finding. Stroke or transient ischemic attack was the most frequent reported initial impression (44.2%). Complete language recovery was reported in 77.4% of evaluable patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Published adult ASE cases show a heterogeneous phenotype in which recognition commonly rests on concordance between language disturbance and focal EEG abnormalities, with peri-ictal imaging providing complementary evidence. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy of individual features or multimodal combinations.

articles.title: Systemic cytokine signatures associated with volcanic emisions exposure and respiratory disease after the cumbre vieja eruption-ashes project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In September 2021, the eruption of the Tajogaite volcano on La Palma (Spain) released large amounts of toxic gases and particulate matter over three months. This study, part of the ASHES Project, analyses the serum cytokine profile and its relationship with exposure to these pollutants in general population, asthma patients, and occupationally exposed workers.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 102 participants (69 women; median age 50 years) were included. Structured interviews were conducted, and serum samples were collected to quantify 48 biomarkers related to TH1, TH2, and TH17 inflammatory responses (Olink®). Participants were classified into three groups: healthy population (n = 66), occupationally exposed workers (n = 13), and asthmatic patients (n = 23). Comparisons were performed between healthy population vs. asthmatics and healthy population vs. occupational group.

RESULTS: Occupationally exposed workers showed the highest exposure (median 10 h), compared with 6 h in the healthy population and 5 h in asthmatics (p = 0.006). This group, with highest exposure, had increased levels of IL-2, IL-7, IL-17A, and IL-17F compared with the general population. Asthmatic patients showed higher levels of IL-2, IL-7, TNFSF12, CXCL10, IL-17C, CCL3, and CCL4, and lower levels of IL-15 and MMP12 (p < 0.05). A strong positive correlation between IL-4 and exposure time (r = 0.7935, p < 0.0001), and negative correlations with CCL8, CXCL11, and TNF-α were observed in asthmatics.

CONCLUSIONS: Volcanic emissions are associated with exposure- and disease-dependent immune responses. Asthmatics show heightened TH1/TH2/TH17 activation, while highly exposed workers display a TH17-skewed profile, with the general population maintaining a balanced response, suggesting greater vulnerability in asthma patients.

articles.title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).

METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.

CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

articles.title: MSC-Integrated CuPB-BTB Coaxial Nanofibrous Scaffold for pH-Responsive Infection Monitoring and Antibacterial-Regenerative Wound Therapy.
articles.abstract: The healing process of chronic wounds is often hindered by recurring bacterial infections, inflammation, and inadequate tissue regeneration, which necessitates the development of innovative dressing materials capable of both infection detection and treatment. Herein, we report the development of a coaxial nanofiber scaffold made up of PCL-gelatin integrated with copper-doped prussian blue nanoparticles (CuPB), bromothymol blue (BTB), and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for concurrent pH-sensitive detection of infection, drug delivery, and tissue regeneration. The coaxial architecture allowed compartmentalized integration of functional elements within the scaffold while preserving its biomimetic fibrous structure for wound dressing application. The release of CuPB nanoparticles, which serve as the source of the antibacterial copper component, imparted antibacterial properties, while BTB facilitated visual colorimetric detection of infection-associated pH changes, allowing real-time monitoring of wound status. The addition of the MSCs further augmented the regenerative potential of the scaffold through the paracrine mediated modulation of inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling. In vitro assessment indicated the cytocompatibility, MSC compatibility, and hemocompatibility of the scaffold, with hemolysis less than 2%. In vivo assessment revealed that MSC-loaded CuPB-BTB coaxial nanofibers promoted wound healing more efficiently than the control group. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses further revealed improved tissue organization, enhanced angiogenesis as evidenced by VEGF expression, and increased α-SMA associated tissue remodeling. Hence, this multifunctional scaffold represents a promising theranostic wound dressing capable of integrating infection monitoring, antibacterial action, and MSC-mediated tissue regeneration for chronic wound management.

articles.title: Beyond Bubble Wrap for the Heart: Gas Exchange and Respiratory Support in Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

articles.title: Corrigendum to "MOVIN in ICU: An observational study of Mobilisation On Vasopressors and INotropes in intensive care" [Heart & Lung Volume 77 (2026) May-Jun;102751].
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

articles.title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

articles.title: Prediction model-based comparison of medial stabilized and cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty: A two-phase study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medial stabilized (MS) inserts have been introduced to improve knee kinematics and mid-flexion stability in total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, direct comparisons between MS and cruciate-retaining (CR) designs are often confounded by patient-related factors.

PURPOSE: To compare postoperative knee flexion between MS and CR designs using a prediction model-based counterfactual framework.

METHODS: This retrospective two-phase study included patients who underwent primary TKA at a single institution. In Phase 1, a multivariable regression model was developed using 129 CR-TKA cases to predict 1-year postoperative knee flexion based on preoperative and intraoperative variables. Internal validation was performed using 10-fold cross-validation, and model performance and calibration were assessed using out-of-fold predictions. In Phase 2, the validated model was applied to MS-TKA cases to estimate the postoperative flexion expected under a hypothetical CR condition. Predicted CR flexion and observed MS flexion were compared using paired t-tests.

RESULTS: In the CR cohort (n = 129), the mean difference between predicted and observed postoperative flexion was 0.07° (95% confidence interval (CI), -1.5 to 1.7°; P = 0.996). Ten-fold cross-validation demonstrated moderate predictive performance (R2 = 0.218, mean absolute error = 7.78°, root mean squared error = 9.84°). In the MS cohort (n = 24), observed postoperative flexion (120.0 ± 10.5°) did not differ significantly from the predicted CR flexion (122.5 ± 6.5°), with a mean paired difference of -2.43° (95% CI, -6.59 to 1.73°; P = 0.239).

CONCLUSION: The CR-based prediction model demonstrated moderate internal predictive performance within the study cohort. Within the limitations of this exploratory analysis, no statistically significant difference in postoperative knee flexion was detected between observed MS-TKA outcomes and the flexion predicted under hypothetical CR conditions. Larger externally validated studies with adequate statistical power are required before definitive conclusions regarding implant-specific differences can be drawn.

articles.title: Hypoglycemia and Clinical Outcomes in Non-Diabetic Adults Hospitalized with Acute Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoglycemia in hospitalized adults without diabetes is often considered incidental, but acute infection may disrupt glucose homeostasis.

AIMS: To determine the incidence of hypoglycemia in adults without diabetes hospitalized for acute infection and evaluate its association with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 64,871 adults without diabetes admitted for acute infection between 2010 and 2025 at a tertiary academic center. Patients with diabetes or prior glucose-lowering therapy were excluded. Mild hypoglycemia was defined as 55-69 mg/dL and severe hypoglycemia as < = 54 mg/dL. Outcomes included 30 and 90 d mortality, clinical deterioration, and ICU admission.

RESULTS: Hypoglycemia occurred in 8,827 patients (13.6%): 5,684 (8.8%) had mild and 3,143 (4.8%) had severe hypoglycemia. Mortality increased by hypoglycemia severity. For 90 d mortality, adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were 1.30 (95% CI, 1.20-1.42; p <0.001) for mild and 1.73 (95% CI, 1.57-1.91; p <0.001) for severe hypoglycemia. For 30 d mortality, aORs were 1.19 (95% CI, 1.07-1.33; p <0.001) and 1.70 (95% CI, 1.51-1.91; p <0.001), respectively. Achievement of subsequent normoglycemia following hypoglycemia was associated with lower observed mortality, whereas transition to hyperglycemia was associated with worse outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults without diabetes hospitalized for acute infections, hypoglycemia is common and associated with mortality in a severity-dependent manner. Glycemic overshoot after correction may identify an additional high-risk state, supporting careful glucose monitoring and controlled correction during acute illness.

articles.title: Initiation of Medical Therapy for Storage Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: De-novo anticholinergic or beta-3 agonist (Ach/B3a) initiation for storage lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) is a clinically significant but understudied outcome after benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) surgery. We estimated procedure-specific cumulative incidence of Ach/B3a medication initiation and identified associated patient- and procedure-level factors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using Michigan statewide claims data (2017-2022) from the Michigan Value Collaborative, Ach/B3a-naive patients who underwent BPH surgery were identified. Procedures included transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP), laser photovaporization (PVP), laser enucleation of the prostate (LEP), robotic waterjet therapy (RWJT), prostatic urethral lift (PUL), water vapor thermal therapy (WVTT), transurethral microwave thermotherapy (TUMT), prostatic artery embolization (PAE), and simple prostatectomy (SP). De-novo Ach/B3a initiation was defined as a prescription fill for an Ach/B3a between 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis; Cox proportional hazards models identified associated factors.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 11,519 Ach/B3a medication-naive patients. Twelve-month cumulative incidence ranged from 5.7% (TUMT) to 11% (PVP). On multivariable analysis, PVP was associated with higher hazard of initiation compared to TURP (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.25-1.79). Prior BPH medication use, and prior anticoagulation use were associated with higher hazard of initiation, while preoperative catheter dependence was associated with lower hazard.

CONCLUSIONS: In this statewide cohort of Anticholinergic and Beta-3 agonist naive patients undergoing contemporary BPH procedures, de-novo Ach/B3a medication initiation was uncommon but procedure-specific, with 12-month cumulative incidence ranging from 5.7% - 11%, with PVP carrying the highest hazard. These findings provide real-world benchmarks to guide counseling across contemporary BPH interventions.

articles.title: Ethics of Telerehabilitation in Supportive Cancer Care Through a Responsible Innovation Lens.
articles.abstract: In recent years, remote exercise services ("telerehabilitation") have been increasingly explored and implemented, including in supportive cancer care, on the promise of greater convenience, access independent of geographic location, reduced infection risk, and cost savings. Ethical commentary on telehealth in general is substantial, but sustained discussion of questions specific to telerehabilitation remains comparatively sparse. As contributors to PREFERBALE-II, a European Union-funded project evaluating live-remote exercise for people recovering from cancer treatment, we sought practical guidance on how to deliver such services responsibly, and found little to work with. This prompted this viewpoint, which sets out our own position as researchers and clinicians engaged in this work. We draw on a purposive sample of professional guidance documents, which were assembled through our professional networks and a supplementary web search, and on a narrative reading of qualitative studies chosen to represent accounts of benefits as well as burdens. We read these documents through an analytical lens of responsible innovation. We make 3 arguments. First, the ethical content of current telerehabilitation guidance is largely confined to the products and processes of innovation, covering safety, privacy, consent, and compliance, while the question of purpose, that is, whether, for whom, and why remote rehabilitation should be offered at all, is left largely unasked. Anticipation appears only implicitly, and reflexivity, inclusion, and responsiveness barely at all. Responsibility is repeatedly delegated to individual professionals without commensurate structural support. Second, the situated experience of users and professionals forms part of the ethics of telerehabilitation and is not merely data to be assessed. Reported benefits and burdens depend on social context, including age, digital literacy, connectivity, caregiver availability, language, and sensory or cognitive impairment, so an equity claim made for the modality in general may not hold for the individual patient. Third, the ethics of telerehabilitation consequently has to be institutionalized across 3 overlapping domains: the interpersonal and experiential quality of remote care, the legal and institutional conditions of delivery, and the positioning of telerehabilitation within health systems. We address these arguments primarily to rehabilitation professionals and the associations and standard-setting bodies that issue guidance for them, and secondarily to digital health and ethical, legal, and social implications researchers, policymakers, and health-system decision-makers who commission or implement such services. We offer an agenda for a broader ethics conversation across professional societies, curricula, and affected publics, together with observations from a consortium put forward as hypotheses for study.

articles.title: Development of Guidelines for Hospital Adoption of Wearable Telemonitoring Systems in Chronic Disease Management: Protocol for a Multiphase Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The integration of wearable device-based telemonitoring into hospital systems presents a transformative opportunity for chronic disease management, particularly in settings such as Indonesia facing a high burden of noncommunicable diseases. However, widespread adoption is hindered by multifaceted operational barriers, including workflow integration, data management, and unclear adoption pathways, highlighting a critical need for structured, evidence-based guidance.

OBJECTIVE: This study protocol aims to develop a role-specific adoption guideline for integrating wearable telemonitoring systems into routine workflow in Indonesian hospitals for chronic disease management.

METHODS: An exploratory sequential mixed methods design is employed across 3 phases. Phase 1 involves a critical interpretive synthesis of the literature to synthesize evidence on wearable technology adoption to populate the Domain-by-Actor matrix. Phase 2 comprises qualitative semistructured interviews with 32 to 44 key stakeholders (administrators, IT staff, and clinicians) from 4 purposively selected hospitals in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, to explore contextual barriers and facilitators. Phase 3 uses a modified nominal group technique with a panel of 12 experts to build consensus and finalize the guideline.

RESULTS: As of December 13, 2025, this study is in progress. Ethical approval has been obtained. The critical interpretive synthesis (phase 1) is completed, yielding preliminary thematic data on adoption factors. Data collection for the qualitative interviews (phase 2) has commenced, with interviews conducted at 1 hospital and administrative permissions secured for 2 sites. Recruitment and data collection are ongoing.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol offers a systematic methodology to bridge the gap between digital health pilot studies and routine use in clinical operations. By mapping complex adoption factors onto an anticipated Domain-by-Actor matrix, the proposed study has the potential to guide sustainable, role-specific wearable telemonitoring integration across diverse hospital structures.

articles.title: Barriers and Enablers to Asynchronous Secure Messaging Use in Hospital-Based Ambulatory Specialty Clinics in Ontario, Canada: Convergent Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of virtual care, including patient-to-provider asynchronous secure messaging (ASM). However, while ASM offers access and convenience, the surge in message volume can increase physician workload and contribute to burnout. Furthermore, it has raised additional concerns about message appropriateness, medicolegal liability, and sustainability of this communication virtual care modality.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to explore the experience with ASM in Ontario in specialty ambulatory care to inform current practice support strategies. We sought to characterize messaging usage quantitatively while also exploring experience with messaging, contextual barriers, and facilitators qualitatively.

METHODS: We used a convergent mixed methods design, analyzing aggregated electronic health record (EHR) usage and qualitative interview data. The study was conducted at a large ambulatory care hospital in Ontario, Canada, across four high-messaging specialty clinics: mental health, rheumatology, dermatology, and surgery. Quantitative data (October 2019 to Octtober 2022) included message volumes, response patterns, and timing. Semistructured interviews with physicians, nurses, administrative staff, and patients (n=19), conducted in 2022 explored ASM workflows, barriers, and facilitators. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, stratified by clinic. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, informed by an interpretative phenomenological orientation. Findings from the two strands were then compared to identify areas of convergence and divergence.

RESULTS: Message volumes surged post pandemic, particularly in mental health, ranging from about 6000 in surgery, rheumatology, and dermatology to close to 13,000 messages in mental health across the study period. Message rate per patient per month was 0.6 (SD 0.2; mental health), 0.5 (SD 0.2; rheumatology), 0.2 (SD 0.2; dermatology), and 0.2 (SD 0.1; surgery). Physicians averaged 12.6 (SD 8.0) messages/month (rheumatology) and 7.6 (SD 4.4) messages/month (mental health) in clinics without nursing support. Nurses handled 27.4 (SD 11.6) messages/month (surgery) and 19.2 (SD 14.1) messages/month (dermatology). Three percent (1263/38,370) to 10% (3619/36,022) of provider messages were sent outside regular hours. The majority of conversations (2156/6859, 46% to 6913/13,615, 62%) had only a single reply. Physicians reported challenging experiences due to increased workload, lack of compensation, and poor integration into local clinical workflows. High patient-to-physician ratios and limited nursing support for message triage were associated with a poor messaging experience. Patients and administrative staff valued messaging for its convenience, accessibility, and efficiency. A key finding was insufficient engagement across all user groups in decisions about messaging implementation.

CONCLUSIONS: The study highlights a disconnect between the high perceived value of ASM for patients and administrative staff and the challenging experiences of physicians. Successful implementation requires thoughtful integration into care models, clear guidelines for appropriate use, and proper triage and "channel management" to guide patients to appropriate modalities. Future research should explore triaging algorithms as part of a digital front door, specialty-specific variations, and the crucial role of nursing staff in message channel management.

articles.title: Public Awareness, Attitudes, and Practices Toward Digital Health Surveillance in Malawi: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital surveillance systems are increasingly recognized as essential tools for enhancing early outbreak detection, reporting, and response, especially in low-resource settings. The COVID-19 pandemic unveiled the critical role of digital health surveillance systems in timely detection, monitoring, and responses to public health threats. However, successful implementation depends on public awareness, acceptance, and willingness to participate. Limited evidence exists on how the public perceives and interacts with digital surveillance in Malawi.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to assess the awareness, attitudes, and practices of adult Malawians toward digital surveillance during pandemics and epidemics.

METHODS: A cross-sectional quantitative study design was used. Data were collected in 10 selected districts (Chitipa, Mzimba South, Kasungu, Lilongwe, Salima, Balaka, Thyolo, Phalombe, Blantyre, and Chikwawa) of Malawi that had high and low levels of cholera and COVID-19 disease burden. The survey recruited 1174 participants who were 18 years or older at the time of data collection. Descriptive statistics were computed using R statistical software. Ethical approval was obtained from the National Health Sciences Research Committee prior to data collection.

RESULTS: A total of 1174 participants were surveyed, 65% (n=768) were female, and the mean age was 36.9 (SD 14.26) years. Only 59% (n=697) demonstrated awareness of digital surveillance systems, though 51% (n=603) had smartphones and 41% (n=477) used mobile phones. A positive attitude was observed in 89% (n=1044) of respondents, with most believing digital reporting could improve outbreak control, and 80% (n=939) were confident in privacy and data security. Practices related to digital reporting were low, with only 18% (n=211) having ever reported health symptoms through any digital platform.

CONCLUSIONS: Enhancing digital health surveillance literacy, promoting inclusivity, and ensuring accountability will improve readiness for future pandemics through digital surveillance systems. Hence, there is a need for nationwide community sensitization programs to raise awareness about the benefits of digital health surveillance.

articles.title: Wireless Home Blood Pressure Monitoring With Health Coaching for Hypertension Management at a Federally Qualified Health Center: Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility and Acceptability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Only approximately half of adults with hypertension, a leading cardiovascular risk factor, achieve blood pressure (BP) control, with persistent disparities among low-income and minority populations. Wireless home BP monitoring (HBPM) with remote patient monitoring can improve BP control, but evidence is limited in medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic populations served by federally qualified health centers (FQHCs).

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of wireless HBPM among predominantly Hispanic adults with hypertension receiving FQHC care. Comparing BP outcomes between wireless and conventional HBPM was a secondary exploratory objective.

METHODS: We conducted a 6-month, 2-arm randomized controlled pilot feasibility and acceptability trial nested within the San Diego: Heart Attack and Stroke Free Zone program. Adults aged ≥18 years with uncontrolled or newly diagnosed hypertension (BP ≥140/90 mm Hg) were enrolled across 3 FQHC networks and randomized 1:1 by unrestricted simple randomization to wireless HBPM (Bluetooth cuff and cellular hub; weekly transmitted summaries reviewed by health coaches) or standard HBPM (home monitor with paper log). Both arms received standardized health coaching. The primary outcomes were feasibility (proportion of 210 expected BP readings transmitted) and acceptability (postintervention satisfaction survey in the wireless arm). Exploratory analyses compared BP outcomes between arms among participants with >2 BP measurements.

RESULTS: Of 316 recruited participants, 290 (92%) were eligible, and 200 (63%) were analyzed (wireless: n=73, 23%; and standard: n=127, 40%); arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The mean age was 61 years (SD 9.1), 57% (115/200) were women, and 51% (n=102) self-identified as Hispanic, with no significant baseline differences between arms. Among analyzed wireless-arm participants, 86% (63/73) transmitted multiple readings (mean 160.6, SD 129.1) over 6 months, corresponding to 76.2% (160/210) of expected readings among transmitting participants and 66% across all 73; only 5% (7/127) of standard-arm participants returned paper logs. Of 60 respondents (82.2% response rate), 95% (n=57) agreed or strongly agreed that the device was easy to set up and use. Both arms showed significant within-arm BP reductions at 6 months (P<.001). At 6 months, 63% (46/73) of the wireless arm and 74% (94/127) of the standard arm achieved systolic BP <140 mm Hg (P=.08; adjusted odds ratio, standard vs wireless, 1.6, 95% CI 0.78-3.4; P=.19). These exploratory comparisons were not powered and do not constitute evidence of equivalence.

CONCLUSIONS: Among analyzed participants, wireless HBPM was feasible, and survey respondents reported high acceptability in a medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic FQHC population. Feasibility among all randomized participants could not be estimated because arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The absence of a between-arm difference in BP control is not evidence of equivalence because this pilot was not powered to compare clinical effectiveness; the BP findings are hypothesis generating.

articles.title: Trends and Correlates of Maternal Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in the United States, 2016-2024.
articles.abstract: Objectives. To examine trends and correlates of maternal chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis in the United States. Methods. We analyzed US National Vital Statistics System data for women with singleton live births during 2016 to 2024 (n = 32 382 428). We estimated annual age-adjusted prevalence, assessed trends with joinpoint regression, and identified correlates with multivariable logistic regression. Results. Chlamydia and gonorrhea prevalence peaked in 2021; syphilis prevalence increased from 0.09% in 2016 to 0.37% in 2024. Chlamydia prevalence was highest among adolescents. Non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native, and non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian/other Pacific Islander women had high chlamydia and syphilis prevalence. All 3 infections were more common among women who smoked during pregnancy, initiated prenatal care late, were insured by Medicaid, or received Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children benefits. Conclusions. Enhanced preconception counseling, early prenatal care, testing, treatment, and partner services are needed in populations with a high prevalence of maternal sexually transmitted infections. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print October 22, 2026:e1-e11. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308774).

articles.title: Aptamer-Functionalized Pro-Photosensitizers for Targeted Elimination of Drug-Resistant Bacterial Biofilm Infection by Sequentially Activated Photodynamic-Antibiotic Therapy.
articles.abstract: Drug-resistant bacterial infections seriously threaten public health, and the formation of a biofilm barrier plays an important role. Drug-resistant biofilms are difficult to remove because the penetration and specificity of traditional antimicrobial drugs are poor, and the microenvironment in the inner layer of biofilms is hypoxic. Herein, we developed activatable aptamer-functionalized pro-photosensitizers (APMB) by modifying the clinical photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) with an aptamer that can specifically bind to drug-resistant bacteria. The APMB can simultaneously achieve imaging-guided efficient anti-infection and biofilm destruction, thereby increasing the therapeutic efficiency of the treatment of bacterial biofilm infections. Additionally, we co-loaded APMB and the antibiotic metronidazole (MNZ) into hydrogels to prepare a degradable microneedle patch, which can utilize photodynamic effects to eliminate biofilms under normoxic conditions and potentiate the hypoxic microenvironment to activate the antibacterial activity of MNZ, ultimately resulting in the synergistic killing of deep-seated bacteria. To summarize, this simple and intelligent phototheranostic molecular platform improves deep anti-infection efficacy through the synergistic effect of sequential activation while decreasing systemic toxicity, thereby providing a promising avenue for clinical translation to combat antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Differences in donation after circulatory determination of death (DCD) liver donor management. An international survey initiated by the international liver transplantation society (ILTS), society for the advancement of transplant anesthesia (SATA), and liver intensive care group of europe (LICAGE).
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract: We conducted a survey to evaluate variability in determination of death and management of Donation after Circulatory Determination of Death (DCD) liver donors across different countries. 153 centers from 17 countries were included (48.4% US, 51.6% non-US). Most reported using onset of hemodynamic instability, rather than withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy (WLST), as the beginning of the waiting time for decision making related to organ acceptance (76.1% US vs. 47.1% non-US). Actual and maximum acceptable waiting times were comparable between groups (43.7 vs. 50.2 and 50.8 vs. 60.3 min, respectively), frequently exceeding limits defined by national policies. Onset of hemodynamic instability was most commonly defined using systolic blood pressure (SBP) alone (51.4% US vs. 31.6% non-US) or a combination of SBP and oxygen saturation (SpO2) (41.6% US vs. 56.6% non-US). Less commonly, centers used SpO2 (4.2% vs. 3.9%) or arrythmia alone (1.4% US vs. 0.0% non-US). Thresholds for SBP and SpO2 were similar between US and non-US centers (SBP 80 mmHg; and 80% for both). Sedation and analgesia for donor comfort was used less frequently in US centers compared to non-US centers (27.8% vs. 48.1%, p=0.02). Decision-making regarding waiting time was more commonly performed by a multidisciplinary team outside the US (26.1% vs. 52.0%). Over half of US and non-US centers reported using machine perfusion in over 50% of DCD grafts (64.9% vs. 51.9%). When used, normothermic regional perfusion cannulation was more commonly initiated after declaration of death (71.6% US vs. 62.0% non-US). These findings demonstrate substantial variability in DCD donor management. Standardization of definitions and practices, particularly with regard to exclusion of hemodynamic stability period from Warm Ischemic Time (WIT), may improve consistency in decision-making related to organ acceptance.

articles.title: The hidden burden of endoscopy in Saudi Arabia: Burnout, musculoskeletal injury, and emotional impact of complications among endoscopists.
articles.journal: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopy is central to gastrointestinal care but is associated with significant occupational stressors, including high workload, physical strain, and psychological impact following complications. Data on endoscopist wellbeing in the Middle East remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of burnout, musculoskeletal symptoms, and emotional consequences of complications among endoscopists in Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: A national cross-sectional survey was conducted between October and November 2025 among licensed endoscopists across Saudi Arabia. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, workload, musculoskeletal symptoms, burnout indicators, complication experience, emotional impact, and institutional support. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 76 endoscopists participated. High workload was common, with 73.7% performing ≥20 procedures per week and 78.9% working ≥41 hours weekly. Musculoskeletal symptoms were reported by 64.5% (49/76). Burnout-related indicators included frequent fatigue (28.9%) and emotional exhaustion (17.1%). Working ≥41 hours per week was independently associated with frequent fatigue. A significant complication was reported by 64.5%, with psychological effects including sleep disturbance (56.6%), intrusive thoughts (27.6%), and loss of confidence (35.5%). Avoidance of similar procedures occurred in 35.5%, while 60.5% reported no formal debriefing or institutional support.

CONCLUSION: Endoscopists in Saudi Arabia experience a substantial physical and psychological burden, compounded by limited institutional support. Targeted interventions, including ergonomic training, structured debriefing, and peer-support programs, are needed to improve clinician wellbeing and sustain endoscopy services.

articles.title: Clinically Motivated Redesign of the Pennsylvania State University Child Ventricular Assist Device.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Building on validated in vitro and chronic in vivo testing of the Penn State University (PSU) Child Ventricular Assist Device (CVAD), the four-bladed prototype rotor (Rev 0.0) was redesigned using established analytical and computational methods to improve hydraulic efficiency while preserving hemodynamic performance and biocompatibility. Applying turbomachinery principles at the nominal operating condition (3 liters/minute [LPM], 8,000 revolutions/minute [RPM]), a five-bladed design (Rev 1.0) was created with an ideal inflow angle (β1 = 41.0°) and outflow angle (β2 = 27.4°). In silico simulations of Rev 1.0 across the prototype's operating range (7,000-9,000 RPM, 1-5 LPM) demonstrated an approximately 40% improvement in hydraulic performance. The Rev 1.0 rotor was then evaluated on a benchtop mock circulatory loop using fresh ovine blood, confirming the in silico gains. The normalized index of hemolysis (NIH), measured at two clinically relevant conditions (1.5 LPM and 3.3 LPM, both at ~80 mm Hg), was 0.052 ± 0.054 and 0.047 ± 0.033 mg/dL, respectively, and high-molecular-weight multimers of von Willebrand factor were preserved within normal to borderline ranges. By achieving target flows and pressures at approximately 1,000 RPM lower speeds, the redesign reduces power requirements and enables longer untethered operation, advancing a fully implantable PSU CVAD toward a critical unmet need in pediatric advanced heart failure.

articles.title: Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes and Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) are often observed in patients undergoing ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the relationship between AF ablation and PVCs is uncertain. The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence of frequent PVCs before and after catheter ablation of AF.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing ablation of AF at two tertiary centers. All patients undergoing initial or repeat ablation of AF were eligible. Patients were followed in AF clinics before and after ablation with routine ambulatory ECG monitoring.

RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 421 patients (mean 63 years, 33% female, 57% paroxysmal). At baseline, 18.4% and 4.7% had ≥ 1% and ≥ 5% PVCs respectively. In the 179 days post-ablation, 9.0% developed new onset ≥ 1% PVCs, whereas 10.9% of patients had regression from ≥ 1% to < 1% PVCs. In the total follow up period of 2 years, there was a significant increase in the proportion of patients with ≥ 1% PVCs. Multivariable modeling revealed baseline PVC burden and hypertension as the only predictors of an increasing PVC burden in the post-ablation period.

CONCLUSION: Frequent PVCs are highly prevalent among patients undergoing AF ablation. However, there was no signal of an increase in frequent PVCs in the immediate post-ablation period.

articles.title: Heparin Retention and Dispersion Following Injection of Locking Fluid in an Acute Hemodialysis Catheter: A Simulation Study.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Heparin locking is used to maintain patency of acute hemodialysis catheters; however, unintended leakage of locking solution into the systemic circulation may increase bleeding risk. Ideally, locking solution would remain confined to the catheter lumen, maintaining patency while minimizing systemic anticoagulation, yet the mechanisms governing heparin retention and dispersion remain inadequately understood. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics simulations incorporating non-Newtonian blood flow and species transport were performed using a microcomputed tomography-derived model of an acute dual-lumen hemodialysis catheter to evaluate the effects of injection rate, venous blood flow, and lock volume. Injection of the manufacturer-recommended 1.4 ml lock volume over durations of 0.5-5 seconds resulted in 13-16% (900-1100 U) of injected heparin entering the systemic circulation, yielding transient therapeutic systemic heparin concentrations. Rapid injections increased distal penetration of the locking solution and improved heparin retention (from 84% to 87%). Heparin clearance following injection occurred in two phases consisting of rapid early convective washout followed by prolonged slow diffusive clearance. Reducing lock volume substantially decreased systemic heparin exposure while preserving therapeutic intraluminal heparin concentrations. These findings provide mechanistic insight into catheter locking behavior and suggest that optimization of lock volume may reduce unintended systemic anticoagulation while maintaining catheter patency.

articles.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity.
articles.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

articles.title: Clinician adherence to peri-procedural warfarin bridging guidelines for patients with atrial fibrillation enrolled in an anticoagulation management service.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 AHA/ACC/HRS guidelines recommend against peri-procedural bridging of warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based solely on CHA₂DS₂-VASc score without additional thromboembolic (TE) risk factors. At our institution, decisions regarding bridging in moderate-to-high TE risk AF patients who require anticoagulation interruption incorporate patient-specific factors.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate adherence to institutional peri-procedural guidelines and associated TE and bleeding events.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study included AF patients receiving warfarin for stroke prevention enrolled in the anticoagulation management service. Patients had moderate-to-high TE risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5 or other TE risk factors) and underwent moderate-to-high bleeding risk procedures between August 2023 and August 2024. Major outcomes included a composite of TE events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents, or transient ischemic attack) and a composite of International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB) events within 30 days post-procedure. Minor outcomes included individual components of the composite outcomes and adherence to the institutional guideline.

RESULTS: Of the 145 procedures, bridging therapy was used in 87 (60%) and omitted in 58 (40%), with 92.4% compliance to institutional guidance. No TE events were observed. Of 21 bleeding events, one ISTH major bleed occurred in the bridging group and was attributed to the procedure, while 20 were CRNMB events. There were 15 (17.4%) CRNMB events in the bridging group and 5 (8.6%) in the non-bridging group.

CONCLUSION: High adherence to institutional bridging guidelines was observed. A trend towards fewer bleeding events with no increased TE events was found in the non-bridging group in patients with moderate-to-high TE risk.

articles.title: Vulnerable transitions in family caregiving after treatment of congenital heart disease in children: a qualitative journey-mapping study.
Quantitative analysis of major elements in logging cuttings using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy and a dual-scale attention residual network.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) has emerged as a new technique for elemental logging because it allows for the simultaneous detection of multiple elements rapidly and with almost no loss. However, the application of this technology in logging cuttings still faces significant challenges. Complex logging conditions and contaminated core samples can lead to significant baseline drift and noise, obscuring useful information in element signatures and reducing the accuracy of quantitative analysis of key elements in cuttings. To enhance the accuracy and robustness of LIBS, this study proposes a novel method that combines LIBS with the Dual-Scale Attention Residual Network (DSARNet) model. LIBS data from 603 samples were collected and preprocessed through smoothing and denoising, baseline correction, and dimensionality transformation prior to modeling. The prediction model utilises the DSARNet model, which primarily comprises two components: a shallow feature fusion module and a deep feature extraction module. The shallow feature fusion module consists of two parallel convolutional branches operating at different scales and an attention-based feature fusion module. The deep feature extraction module comprises two parallel symmetric residual branches and a prediction section. The experimental results show that, compared with traditional machine learning algorithms and the ResNet deep learning model, the DSARNet model performs the best in terms of both root mean square error (RMSE) and R2 values. The R2 values for the predicted values of Na, Al, Fe, P, and S are 0.9267, 0.9542, 0.9066, 0.9454 and 0.8372, respectively. This indicates a significant improvement in performance and confirms that this technology has broad application prospects and great potential for widespread adoption in the field of core logging.

articles.title: Multi-Dot/Icm effector mutants reveal distinct host responses in Legionella infected macrophages.
articles.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, an accidental and severe form of pneumonia. The replication of L. pneumophila within alveolar macrophages requires the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system that translocates more than 330 bacterial effector proteins into the infected host cell. Many Dot/Icm effectors possess eukaryotic-like domains and manipulate host processes by functional mimicry. However, only a minority of effectors have been fully characterized. Redundancy among effector protein activities and host targets has complicated functional characterization of individual effector proteins. To explore the collective impact of Dot/Icm effectors on host cell processes, we created a library of 14 L. pneumophila genomic mutant strains lacking effector-rich regions (a total of 85 effector genes deleted) and used the multi-deletion mutants to interrogate host-pathogen interactions. While none of the mutants exhibited a defect in intracellular replication in THP-1 macrophages, several were attenuated in amoebae, including a mutant lacking a predicted amino acid transporter. In THP-1 cells, we observed that wild-type L. pneumophila 130b triggered a strong inflammatory and cellular stress transcriptional response in macrophages, whereas six mutants displayed reduced interferon signalling and one mutant displayed a marked decrease in the global expression of host heat shock response (HSR) genes. Through the creation of further sub-deletions, we found that the Dot/Icm effector kinase LegK4 was responsible for induction of the host HSR via the canonical transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1). Infection of THP-1 macrophages deficient in HSF1 revealed a potential role for the host HSR in the early stages of L. pneumophila infection. Together, these results reinforce the utility of multi-gene deletions to identify Dot/Icm effector phenotypes and the importance of the host HSR to L. pneumophila infection.

articles.title: From Awareness to Action: A Knowledge-Intended Practice Gap in Stroke Decision-Making Among Egyptian Medical Students and House Officers: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and early recognition is critical for effective management. Despite growing awareness, the extent to which knowledge is translated into appropriate clinical practice among medical trainees remains uncertain. This study aims to assess stroke-related knowledge, attitude, and intended practice (KAP) among Egyptian medical students and house officers, and to identify gaps between knowledge and clinical decision-making.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to March 2026 utilizing a structured, self-administered questionnaire derived from previously validated instruments. Participants were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling using a Google Forms questionnaire disseminated via online platforms and university networks. The survey assessed knowledge of stroke risk factors and warning signs, attitudes toward stroke severity and outcomes, and intended responses to suspected stroke scenarios. Knowledge and attitude scores were calculated, and associations among variables were examined using multivariate regression models.

RESULTS: Among the 1,065 participants, awareness of stroke was notably high, with nearly all recognizing it as a medical emergency (99.4%) and the majority reporting prior awareness (96.9%). Although classic stroke symptoms were widely recognized, atypical presentations were less well identified. Positive attitudes were present in 68.6% of participants, and adequate knowledge of warning signs and risk factors was observed in 86.9% and 81.4%, respectively. Nevertheless, inappropriate intended practices remained prevalent in simulated scenarios, with 23.4% indicating they would administer aspirin and 32.6% opting for self-transport. Multivariate analysis showed that prior training significantly predicted knowledge, while demographic factors influenced attitudes. Importantly, the observed inverse association between knowledge and intended practice highlights a concerning disconnect, emphasizing the need for interventions that bridge this knowledge-action gap.

CONCLUSION: Although participants generally demonstrated favorable stroke knowledge, this did not consistently translate into appropriate intended practice. These findings suggest that knowledge alone may not be sufficient to ensure appropriate emergency decision-making and support consideration of competency-based educational approaches. Future interventional studies are warranted to evaluate their effectiveness.

articles.title: Incidence of Pediatric Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State: A Prospective National Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) is a severe diabetic emergency, typically seen in adults with type 2 diabetes, but with high morbidity described in the limited pediatric cases available in the literature. Existing estimates of pediatric HHS incidence are primarily derived from administrative datasets and may be affected by diagnostic misclassification. We sought to determine the minimum incidence, clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of pediatric HHS.

METHODS: Approximately 2,700 pediatricians and pediatric subspecialists were surveyed monthly from June 2023 through May 2025 to identify cases of pediatric HHS, via the Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program. Cases were adjudicated using predefined biochemical criteria, including severe hyperglycemia, elevated serum osmolality (>320 mOsm/kg), and absence of significant acidosis. Detailed clinical data were collected for confirmed cases.

RESULTS: Twenty-four cases were reported during the 24-month surveillance period. Following case adjudication, seven cases met diagnostic criteria for HHS, corresponding to a minimum annual incidence of 0.059 cases per 100,000 child-years (95% CI 0.024-0.122). Median age at presentation was 14.8 years, and all cases occurred in individuals with newly diagnosed or previously unrecognized diabetes. Common precipitating factors included infection, trauma, and surgery. Most patients required intensive care admission, with a median hospital stay of six days. Frequent complications included acute kidney injury and hypokalemia, and one patient required intervention for suspected cerebral injury, although no deaths were reported. Half of initially reported cases were subsequently reclassified as hyperosmolar diabetic ketoacidosis, highlighting challenges in the recognition and classification of pediatric hyperglycemic emergencies.

CONCLUSION: National surveillance in Canada identified lower incidence of HHS, indicating that prior estimates based on administrative data likely overstate rates due to misclassification of hyperglycemic emergencies.

articles.title: The association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract: Introduction: Parental health numeracy is relevant to pediatric asthma management because caregivers often interpret medication quantities, risk information, and peak-flow thresholds. Objective: This study examined the adjusted association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 400 parents or legal guardians of children with physician-diagnosed asthma at the University of Jordan Hospital between May and August 2024. The children had a median age of 6 years (IQR: 3-11). Parental numeracy was assessed using the Arabic version of the Asthma Numeracy Questionnaire (Ar-ANQ), and adherence was assessed using the Arabic version of the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5). Results: The median Ar-ANQ score was 3 (IQR: 1-4), and 178 children (44.5%) were classified as having high medication adherence. In adjusted logistic regression, each one-point increase in the Ar-ANQ score was associated with greater odds of high adherence (adjusted OR = 1.404, 95% CI: 1.179-1.672, p < 0.001). Parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence. Conclusion: Higher parental health numeracy was associated with greater odds of high medication adherence, whereas parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence.

articles.title: Supportive Evidence for A Framework-Guided, Provider-Engaged Recruitment Approach to Representative Cohort Enrollment in Pediatric Epilepsy Research.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Enrolling cohorts that are representative of affected populations remains a challenge in neurogenetic research. However, few studies describe reproducible recruitment approaches for achieving representative cohorts. We aimed to recruit a representative cohort of pediatric patients with epilepsy who had not previously received conclusive sequencing results for research genetic sequencing.

METHODS: Patients with epilepsy referred for research genetic sequencing within a single healthcare system (2021-2023) were enrolled. Recruitment and engagement strategies were guided by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework and addressed provider-reported barriers to research participation (e.g., language proficiency, transportation, healthcare access). We directly evaluated differential enrollment across relevant demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. We compared the enrolled cohort with the institutional child neurology epilepsy population. We also compared the enrolled cohort with North Carolina's statewide population estimates to aid in the interpretation of findings.

RESULTS: Of 156 eligible patients, 95 (61%) enrolled. We found no statistically significant differences in measured characteristics between enrolled and non-enrolled eligible patients. The study cohort did not differ from the institutional population with respect to insurance status (p=.781), preferred language (p=.865), race (p=.548), or rurality (p=.689). Compared with statewide population estimates, there were no significant differences in preferred language (p=.362), race (p=.173), ethnicity (p=.907), or rurality (p=.212), although the cohort included a higher proportion of publicly insured participants and fewer uninsured participants (2% vs. 10.4%; p<.001). Hispanic/Latino representation was lower than the institutional population (10.5% vs. 19.0%; p=.041) but comparable to the statewide population (10.9%; p=.907). Over half of enrolled participants (54%) resided in counties with high economic distress. Among individuals who declined participation, travel or distance was the most frequently reported barrier (13/45, 29%).

CONCLUSION: We used a framework-guided, provider-engaged recruitment approach to enroll a cohort of pediatric epilepsy patients prioritized for genetic sequencing whose sociodemographic characteristics appear to reflect the institutional and statewide populations across most measured domains. Measured characteristics were not found to be associated with study enrollment. Findings provide supportive evidence for implementing and evaluating similar recruitment approaches that may improve representativeness and reduce selection bias in neurogenetic and neurological research.

articles.title: National Trends in Open vs Percutaneous Tracheostomy Among U.S. Hospitalizations for COPD Exacerbation, 2016-2022.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract: Background National utilization and short-term outcomes of open surgical tracheostomy (OST) versus percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) in adults hospitalized for COPD exacerbation are uncertain. Methods Adult hospitalizations not coded as elective, with a primary diagnosis of COPD exacerbation and tracheostomy, in the U.S. National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022) were classified as OST or PDT using ICD-10-PCS approach codes. Utilization trends, in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), and inflation-adjusted charges were compared using survey-weighted multivariable models and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), with further adjustment for timing, coded severity, and pandemic period. Results Of an estimated 2,970 hospitalizations (594 sampled), 36.5% involved PDT. Annual volumes declined for PDT (215 to 115; P-trend=0.023) and OST (480 to 165; P-trend=0.003). In-hospital mortality was 13.5% (PDT 14.3% vs OST 13.0%; P=0.662). Mortality was higher in 2020-2022 than in 2016-2019 among OST hospitalizations (21.3% vs 10.2%; P=0.006) but not among PDT hospitalizations (18.3% vs 12.7%; P=0.29); annual trends did not differ significantly between approaches (P for interaction=0.061). After adjustment, PDT was not associated with mortality (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.68-1.66), LOS (-0.63 days; 95% CI, -4.19 to 2.94), or charges (ratio, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.85-1.12); estimates were consistent with IPTW, timing and severity adjustment, exclusion of 2020, and within both periods. Conclusions Both OST and PDT volumes declined. No significant association was detected between approach and short-term outcomes, although estimates were imprecise. The mortality increase within OST hospitalizations, concentrated in the pandemic period, warrants cautious interpretation given potential changes in case mix, treatment selection, pandemic-related practice, and unmeasured severity.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of the Solitaire™ and React™ Devices from India's First Multicenter Mechanical Thrombectomy Registry.
articles.abstract:
