INTRODUCTION: There is a low utilization of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in India and lack of a nationwide registry or data. This registry aimed to study the systems of care, functional outcomes, and cost effectiveness of MT treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).

METHODS: Patients were treated with Solitaire™ X and/or React™ catheter as the primary device/s. Subjects with AIS due to large vessel occlusion, within 24 hours of symptom onset with the Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) score >5 and the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) ≥6 were included. An independent Core lab and clinical events committee assessed outcomes. Good functional outcome was defined as modified Rankin score of 0-2 at 90 days. Successful revascularization was defined as the modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) ≥ 2b. Performance measures included door to needle time, door to groin puncture time, and groin puncture to recanalization time. A cost-effectiveness model was also developed.

RESULTS: Of the 200 patients screened, 190 (mean age, 59.6±14.35 years) were included. The mean baseline NIHSS score was 14.7 ± 5.38, median door to needle time was 50 (10-173) mins, door to groin puncture time was 99 (11- 478) mins, and groin puncture to revascularization time was 40 (10-170) mins. The first pass mTICI≥2b was 127 (66.8%) and the final pass mTICI≥2b was attained in 167 (87.9%). A good functional outcome was seen in 123 (65.8%) patients. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4 (2.1%). Device and/or procedure-related serious adverse events occurred in 27 (14.2%). Combined therapy of MT and Intravenous Tissue Plasminogen Activator [IV-tPA]was cost-effective compared with MT alone with an expected gain of 1.5 QALYs.

CONCLUSIONS: This study results are comparable with global clinical registries and randomized clinical trials with favorable functional outcomes and excellent first pass and final recanalization. Combined therapy (MT + IV-tPA) was cost-effective compared to MT or IV-tPA alone.

articles.title: Osteoporosis causes Nephrolithiasis: A Bidirectional Two-sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
articles.abstract: Background Epidemiological evidence suggests a strong association between osteoporosis (OP) and nephrolithiasis (NL), yet the causal direction of this relationship remains debated. This study aimed to elucidate the bidirectional causal relationship between OP and NL using a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach. Methods We utilized genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from Taiwan Biobank (TWB; osteoporosis: 14,507 cases/ 79,846 controls; nephrolithiasis: 6,318 cases/ 88,035 controls) and BioBank Japan (BBJ; osteoporosis: 9,794 cases/ 159,138 controls; nephrolithiasis: 11,699 cases/ 155,328 controls). Genetic instruments were selected using a suggestive genome-wide threshold of p-value < 1.0 x 10-5, followed by LD clumping and weak-instrument filtering. The primary causal estimates were calculated using the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method. Sensitivity analyses, including weighted median, MR-Egger regression, and MR-PRESSO, were performed to evaluate the robustness of the results and assess pleiotropy. Results In total, 46 SNPs were used for OP-causing-NL in the TWB-to-BBJ analysis, 10 SNPs for OP-causing-NL in the BBJ-to-TWB analysis, 14 SNPs for NL-causing-OP in the TWB-to-BBJ analysis, and 10 SNPs for NL-causing-OP in the BBJ-to-TWB analysis. In the analysis assessing the effect of OP on NL, using genetic instruments from BBJ and outcome data from TWB, we observed a significant causal association (IVW β = 0.211, 95% CI: 0.039-0.384, p = 0.016). This finding was corroborated by the weighted median (p = 0.043) and robust MR-Egger (p = 0.025) analyses, with no evidence of directional pleiotropy (MR-Egger intercept p = 0.858). Conversely, in the reverse analysis, NL did not show a significant causal effect on OP risk in either cohort configuration (IVW p > 0.05). Conclusions Our findings provide suggestive evidence that osteoporosis causally increases the risk of nephrolithiasis, whereas nephrolithiasis does not causally affect osteoporosis risk. Clinically, patients with osteoporosis may represent a high-risk population warranting screening for urinary tract stones.

articles.title: Acute Kidney Injury Among Patients with Drug Overdose-Involved Hospitalizations - United States, 2016-2025.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a serious, often underrecognized complication among patients hospitalized for drug overdose. Although overdose mortality has recently declined in the United States, less is known about whether serious nonfatal complications, including AKI, have followed similar trends. Adjusted percentages of hospitalizations of patients with drug overdose and AKI were calculated using hospital discharge data during 2016-2025. The percentage with a severe inpatient course (i.e., acute dialysis, respiratory compromise, shock or hypotension, or in-hospital death) was also calculated. Among 1,297,847 drug overdose-involved hospitalizations, AKI was documented in 448,136 (34.5%). The percentage of patients with AKI was 28.2% among those aged ≤24 years, 37.4% among those aged ≥65 years, 29.4% among females, and 38.1% among males. AKI among patients with a drug overdose-involved hospitalization increased during 2016-2022 (annual percent change [APC] = 2.69%) and decreased during 2022-2025 (APC = -5.11%). Among patients with a drug overdose-involved hospitalization and AKI, 273,093 (60.9%) experienced a severe inpatient course, including 68.1% of persons aged ≤24 years, 56.1% of those aged ≥65 years, 61.9% of females, and 60.4% of males. The percentage of drug overdose-involved hospitalizations with a severe inpatient course increased during 2016-2023 (APC = 1.82%), before decreasing during 2023-2025 (APC = -2.89%). Disproportionately severe inpatient courses among younger patients, who might have more years of life at risk for developing chronic kidney disease or kidney failure after AKI, warrants continued attention to early kidney injury detection after drug overdose, postdischarge linkage to care, and overdose prevention through improved access to substance use treatment.

articles.title: The Contrast Order: An Order-Based Image Quality Criterion for Nonlinear Beamformers.
articles.abstract: Many modern ultrasound beamformers report improved image quality when evaluated using classical criteria like the contrast ratio and contrast-to-noise ratio, which are based on summary statistics of regions of interest (ROIs). However, nonlinear beamformers and post-processing methods can substantially alter these statistics, raising concerns that the reported improvements may reflect changes in dynamic range or remapping rather than a reflection of true information gain, such as clutter suppression. Introduced recently, the generalized contrast-to-noise ratio (gCNR) is designed to address these concerns, but it requires implementation-dependent density estimation. We propose herein a new, simpler, image quality criterion, called the contrast order (CO), defined as the expected value of the sign of the difference in brightness between two ROIs. The CO is invariant under all strictly monotonic transformations of the image values, as it depends only on their relative ordering, and is interpretable as the probability that one ROI is brighter than the other minus the probability that it is darker. Unlike the gCNR, the CO has a simple unbiased estimator whose variance provably decreases with the number of samples in each ROI. We further propose the effective contrast ratio (ECR), which calibrates the contrast order to the familiar contrast ratio such that the two coincide under ideal Rayleigh-speckle statistics. Together, the CO and ECR provide order- and sign-preserving, dynamic-range-invariant criteria for evaluating lesion contrast, offering a principled alternative to classical and newer image quality criteria when assessing modern beamformers.

articles.title: Uncertainty-guided Multitask Mean Teacher Model for Hybrid ASPECTS Scoring of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: The Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment decision-making in acute ischemic stroke. Recent hybrid scoring methods that combine ASPECTS prediction with auxiliary lesion segmentation have demonstrated great potential by enhancing the model's discriminative power through multitask learning. However, their performance is still limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the insufficient exploitation of shared information across tasks, posing challenges for precise and robust stroke assessment. In this paper, we propose a novel semi-supervised hybrid ASPECTS scoring framework (Semi-HAS) built upon an uncertainty guided multitask mean teacher architecture, which leverages readily available unlabeled data to enhance ASPECTS scoring. Specifically, a dedicated task interaction component is introduced in Semi-HAS to explicitly extract lesion-related complementary information from the auxiliary segmentation task. The proposed component is meanwhile coordinated with a cross-task alignment loss to successfully facilitate collaboration between different tasks for more consistent ASPECTS prediction. Furthermore, we design an adaptive uncertainty estimation for both tasks to generate dual uncertainty maps for mitigating noise introduced by unlabeled data. As a result, this innovative strategy effectively guides cross-model consistency learning for transferring trustworthy knowledge from teacher to student model and improving scoring accuracy for complex anatomical conditions. Extensive experiments on both public and in-house datasets demonstrate that Semi-HAS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by achieving superior scoring accuracy across ASPECTS regions and providing reliable patient level assessments, highlighting its promise in facilitating clinical ASPECTS evaluation and promoting personalized treatments.

articles.title: Impact of hypothermia level on neurological and renal outcomes in emergency aortic surgery: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTemperature management during emergency surgery for acute aortic syndrome is critical for neurological, renal, and systemic protection. Recent European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines recommend moderate hypothermia with antegrade cerebral perfusion for hemiarch procedures. Nevertheless, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) remains common. This study evaluates neurological and other postoperative outcomes across different intraoperative temperature ranges.MethodsA single-centre retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing surgery for acute aortic syndrome between 2018-2023. Demographic, intraoperative, and postoperative data on mortality, hospitalization, neurological, renal outcomes, and blood product usage were collected. Patients were stratified by intraoperative temperature: deep (≤20°C), low-moderate (20.1-24°C), high-moderate (24.1-28°C), and mild (>28°C) hypothermia. Logistic regression identified predictors of binary adverse outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using 24.0°C as the threshold in hemiarch surgery patients.ResultsA total of 175 patients (median age 64 years; 37% female) were included; of whom 89% underwent hemiarch replacement. Cardiopulmonary bypass duration decreased progressively with warmer intraoperative temperatures, ranging from 270.5 minutes in deep hypothermia to 164 minutes in mild hypothermia. The 30-day mortality was 18.9% (n = 33/175), and the overall stroke rate was 19.4% (n = 34/175). Among patients undergoing hemiarch repair, warmer temperatures were associated with lower stroke incidence (mild hypothermia 11%) compared with high-moderate (8.8%), low-moderate (26%), and deep hypothermia (27%) (p = 0.049), and with shorter intensive care admission (p = 0.036). However, multivariate regression showed that the four-category comparison did not reach significance for the assessed outcomes once adjusted for confounding variables. A sensitivity analysis at 24.0°C showed an independent association with reduced stroke risk (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.64, p = 0.005).DiscussionOur findings support current EACTS recommendations favouring moderate-to-mild hypothermia for hemiarch replacement, with potential protective effects. Further studies should determine the optimal temperature strategy for patients undergoing total arch replacement.

articles.title: Prehospital antibiotics and 28-day mortality in sepsis: where does the adjusted benefit come from?
Covered Stent Assisted Coil Embolisation of a Rare Splenomesenteric Artery Aneurysm - A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSplenomesenteric artery aneurysms are a rare clinical entity occurring in <1% of the population, where the splenic artery originates from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). These aneurysms carry a high risk of rupture due to exposure to high-flow hemodynamic stress near the SMA origin.Case PresentationA 76-year-old female was incidentally diagnosed with a 1.6 cm saccular splenomesenteric aneurysm during investigation for sepsis. The patient underwent successful endovascular exclusion using a combination of a microvascular plug and coil embolisation to address the aneurysm 'front' and 'back' doors, while a covered stent was deployed in the SMA to prevent coil prolapse and preserve mesenteric perfusion. Follow-up at 3 months confirmed successful exclusion with preserved visceral flow.DiscussionDue to the rarity of this anatomical variant, documented in less than 60 cases in English literature, no standardised treatment algorithm exists. This study adds to the literature by demonstrating procedural innovation, refining management strategies and advocating for early intervention for such conditions.

articles.title: Interpreting persistent vasopressor dependence during VA ECMO weaning.
Economic evaluations in emergency medicine: a 25-year systematic review of patient-level cost-effectiveness analyses (2000-2025).
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) face rising demand and resource constraints. Cost-effectiveness analyses (CEAs) can inform resource allocation, but patient-level CEAs in emergency care remain methodologically heterogeneous. This review aimed to identify and describe patient-level CEAs in emergency care between 2000 and 2025, appraise their methodological quality, and explore temporal trends and evidence gaps. This systematic review was reported according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and gray literature were searched for patient-level CEAs of clinical or organizational interventions across prehospital, ED, and postemergency settings. Data were synthesized narratively across key methodological domains. Methodological quality of the economic evaluations was assessed using the quality of health economic studies (QHES) instrument. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed. Forty-seven studies were identified, of which 96% were conducted in EDs. Infectious diseases and ED crowding were the most addressed topics, followed by cardiovascular conditions and trauma, although a broad range of issues was covered. Studies were mainly conducted in high-income countries and evaluated organizational or diagnostic interventions. Healthcare system or hospital perspectives and short time horizons predominated. QHES scores were moderate-to-high (mean: 80.0, SD: 9.2, range: 56-96), with substantial variability and only a weak exploratory temporal trend toward higher scores. Prehospital and postemergency settings were underrepresented. Patient-level CEAs in emergency medicine are increasing, with many studies achieving high QHES scores, but remain heterogeneous in scope and methods. This review highlights the range of interventions evaluated and the methodological features relevant to interpreting economic evidence in emergency care.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Early Onset Hypertension in the US.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early onset hypertension is often overlooked despite its association with lifelong cardiovascular disease risk. We developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict early onset hypertension in US adults using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, incorporating demographic, socioeconomic, health care utilization, and comorbidity features.

METHODS: We analyzed data on adults aged 55 years or younger. Hypertension was defined by International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification code number I10 or self-reported physician diagnosis at or before age 55 years. Eighty-four variables were screened; Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator reduced the set to 45 variables. Extreme gradient boosting was trained with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F2 score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC), and area under the precision-recall curve (PR AUC). We assessed fairness across subgroups and used Shapley Additive Explanations to quantify feature influence.

RESULTS: Among 9,850 adults, 1,647 (weighted prevalence, 15.2%) had hypertension. Discrimination was strong, with a ROC AUC of 0.807 (95% CI, 0.787-0.827), PR AUC of 0.486 (95% CI, 0.439-0.530), recall of 0.848 (95% CI, 0.816-0.878), and F2 score of 0.606 (95% CI, 0.578-0.634). Key predictors included older age, high body mass index, and a diagnosis of high cholesterol. Fairness analyses showed slightly higher true positive rates for Hispanic (+0.11) and Asian (+0.08) people, with performance for African American people modestly lower than that for White people.

CONCLUSION: Both medical and nonmedical predictors contributed meaningfully, with high cholesterol particularly influential among adults older than 40 years and race and ethnicity especially important among African American adults. Prospective validation and routine fairness audits are warranted to ensure equitable benefit across populations. This interpretable model supports recall-oriented screening to identify younger adults at risk of hypertension for further evaluation and early intervention.

articles.title: Structural remodeling and activation of the hdeAB and proVWX operons in response to pH and salt stress.
articles.abstract: Escherichia coli is highly sensitive to acid and osmotic stress but adapts by modulating the expression of stress-responsive genes. Nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs) play key roles in DNA organization and sensing environmental changes. The histone-like nucleoid structuring protein H-NS is an NAP acting as a global regulator of stress genes. H-NS may alter local chromatin structure to modulate the expression of such genes in response to environmental stress. The H-NS homolog suppressor of td phenotype A (StpA) co-regulates several target genes, but its role is poorly defined. To investigate the regulatory interplay between these two proteins, we examined transcription, DNA binding, and chromatin structure at two regulated operons, hdeAB and proVWX, in E. coli following exposure to acid and salt shock. Our results show that H-NS senses pH and osmotic cues to remodel chromatin and relieve repression, while StpA-in part-compensates for H-NS loss, particularly at proVWX, highlighting a coordinated regulatory network.

articles.title: Video Decision Support and Advance Care Planning in Older Adults With Advanced Kidney Disease: The VIDEO-KD Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) face consequential decisions about whether to initiate dialysis, yet advance care planning (ACP), the communication that prepares patients for such decisions, is documented infrequently in ambulatory settings.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a video decision aid about treatment options for advanced CKD, combined with patient-created video declarations, increases ACP documentation among older adults with advanced CKD.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial was conducted at 12 ambulatory clinics from June 2021 to March 2025, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were adults 65 years or older with advanced CKD. Outcome assessors were masked to group assignment. Data were analyzed in April 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: Intervention participants viewed a certified video decision aid depicting 3 treatment options for advanced CKD (hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and conservative kidney management) and then created a video declaration, a recorded statement of goals, values, and treatment preferences in video, audio, or written format, that was sent to their treating clinician. Control participants received usual medical care.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was ACP documentation in the electronic health record within 12 months of enrollment or death, whichever came sooner. Documentation was ascertained by validated natural language processing-assisted human adjudication. Prespecified secondary outcomes included documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options and stated treatment preferences.

RESULTS: A total of 453 patients were included (228 intervention [50.3%] and 225 control [49.7%]; mean [SD] age, 78.8 [6.4] years; 190 women [41.9%]; 4 American Indian or Alaska Native [1.1%], 8 Asian [1.8%], 38 Black [8.4%], 35 Hispanic or Latino [7.7%], 3 Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander [0.7%], and 375 White [82.8%] individuals). At 12 months, ACP documentation was higher in the intervention group than the control group (56.6% vs 40.0%; rate difference, 16.6%; 95% CI, 7.5%-25.7%; P < .001), as was documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options (46.1% vs 31.6%; rate difference, 14.5%; 95% CI, 5.6%-23.4%; P = .001). After viewing the video, fewer intervention participants than controls at enrollment were undecided about treatment (30 of 227 [13.2%] vs 92 of 223 [41.3%]), and more preferred conservative kidney management (115 of 227 [50.7%] vs 71 of 223 [31.8%]; P < .001 for the overall distribution).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that, among older adults with advanced CKD, a video decision aid increased ACP documentation and reduced the proportion of patients who were undecided about treatment.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04347629.

articles.title: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist's framework.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Older adults with type 2 diabetes require treatment that balances cardiovascular and kidney protection against hypoglycemia, treatment burden, undernutrition, and functional vulnerability.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review considers PubMed-indexed literature and ClinicalTrials.gov records covering January 2010-October 2026, with targeted updating on 12 October 2026. It examines sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide, and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Age-stratified outcome evidence is distinguished from whole-trial results and the limited evidence in adults aged 80 years or older. Body-composition findings, neurodegenerative outcomes, kidney-protective treatment, and pharmacist-supported regimen modification are critically appraised.

EXPERT OPINION: Organ protection and glycemic simplification should be considered separately. Frailty is not synonymous with kidney impairment, and reductions in lean mass do not establish treatment-induced sarcopenia. Weight-neutral therapy remains useful when weight loss is undesirable. A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

articles.title: The Veterans Affairs Pentoxifylline in Diabetic Kidney Disease (VA PTXRx) Study: Baseline Characteristics.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Experimental and clinical data suggest that the non-specific phosphodiesterase inhibitor pentoxifylline (PTX) reduces proteinuria and may delay the progression of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). However, no large-scale randomized clinical trial has determined whether PTX can reduce end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and mortality in DKD.

DESIGN: VA PTXRx is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter clinical trial designed to test the hypothesis that PTX, when added to usual care, prolongs the time to kidney failure or death in type 2 diabetic (T2D) participants with DKD compared to usual care plus placebo. Enrolled participants at very high risk for ESKD and/or death were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either PTX 400 mg twice daily or matching placebo using randomly permuted blocks with stratification for site, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone (RAAS) inhibitor use, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage. The study is event-driven, requiring 646 primary events (ESKD (chronic dialysis or transplantation) or death) to achieve 80% power to detect a relative risk reduction of 19% with PTX.

BASELINE RESULTS: Between December 2019 and November 2025, 2376 participants at 34 VA sites in the USA were randomized. The mean age at randomization was 72.3 years (SD 7.7), with 97% being male. The mean baseline eGFR was 33.3 mL/min/1.73 m2 (SD 9.4). The median urinary albumin to creatinine ratio (UACR) was 401 mg/g (IQR 122-1076). At baseline, the usage of RAAS inhibitors was 80.0%, sodium-glucose transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors 52.9%, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists 33.2%, and finerenone 3.0%. The majority (88%) of participants had stage 3B or 4 CKD (eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73m2).

CONCLUSIONS: The results, anticipated in 2027, are expected to determine whether PTX is a treatment option for patients with high-risk DKD. Because PTX is a generic medication, it is inexpensive in many health systems, which would facilitate access if it proves effective. Trial Registration: This study is registered with clinicaltrials.gov (Identifier: NCT03625648).

articles.title: Pentoxifylline for chronic kidney disease in people with diabetes: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Pentoxifylline is an inexpensive anti-inflammatory agent tested in diabetic kidney disease for four decades; prior meta-analyses report reduced albuminuria. Whether it is secure, extends to kidney function, or reaches hard outcomes is unclear; we hypothesized the surrogate evidence might be conclusive and the hard-outcome evidence not.

METHODS: We reviewed randomized trials of oral pentoxifylline in diabetic kidney disease to June 2026, without language restriction. Co-primary surrogate outcomes were albuminuria (ratio of means) and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) change (mean difference); the primary hard outcome was end-stage kidney disease or death (risk ratio). We pooled with random-effects models, assessed risk of bias with RoB 2, and report a prediction interval and trial sequential analysis with every estimate.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included, 32 contributing data. Albuminuria fell by about a third (ratio of means 0.69, 95% CI 0.50-0.94; 22 studies contributing 23 comparisons), but heterogeneity was extreme (I2 97%), the prediction interval 0.15-3.10, and only 53% of the required information had accrued, with no boundary crossed. Over ≥ 12 months, GFR changed 4.49 mL/min/1.73 m2 more favorably with pentoxifylline than with control (0.84-8.14; 5 studies contributing 5 comparisons); in two trials at low or some-concerns risk of bias it was 2.96 (-15.34 to 21.26), with 11% of the required information accrued. For end-stage kidney disease or death, 29 events in 6 studies contributing 7 comparisons gave a risk ratio of 0.90 (0.46-1.77), 3% of that required. Gastrointestinal adverse events were three times as common (3.00, 1.94-4.64); serious ones were not (0.83, 0.56-1.22).

CONCLUSIONS: Pentoxifylline reduces albuminuria, but the effect is heterogeneous, depends on which trials are counted, and may not reappear in a new trial. Kidney failure and death have scarcely been tested. The priority is an adequately powered, long-term trial reporting hard endpoints; gastrointestinal intolerance should be anticipated.

articles.title: A Descriptive Case Series of Pericarditis Treatment After Trauma With Colchicine Monotherapy Versus Other Treatment.
articles.abstract: Limited data exist describing the optimal treatment of pericarditis after acute blunt or penetrating trauma. Treatment with high-dose nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID), colchicine, or corticosteroids may not be feasible due to concomitant injuries. This was a retrospective, single-center, descriptive case series at a large, academic, Level 1 Trauma Center over a 10-year period. Patients admitted to the trauma service with a diagnosis of pericarditis at any point during index admission were eligible for inclusion. Groups were defined as colchicine-based treatment (monotherapy or combination) and any therapy besides colchicine, including no medications (surgical). The primary endpoint was therapy escalation defined as treatment modification, chart note documenting therapy failure, rehospitalization, repeat pericardial surgical intervention, or documentation of recurrent pericarditis. Secondary outcomes were treatment intolerance documented in a chart note including gastrointestinal bleed (GIB) and acute kidney injury (AKI). Eleven patients with traumatic pericarditis were included. Four (36%) patients received colchicine-based therapy: monotherapy (2, [50%]) or combination with NSAID (2, [50%]). Seven (63%) patients received non-colchicine treatment: 2 (29%) NSAID alone; 5 (71%) surgical management without medication. There were no occurrences of therapy escalation in either group. Treatment intolerances occurred in 1 (25%; AKI) patient in the colchicine group and 3 (43%; AKI, 2 [29%], GIB, 1 [14%]) patients in the non-colchicine group. Pericarditis is a rare complication after trauma, and no patients in this case series demonstrated treatment escalation. Additional, larger sample studies are necessary to guide optimal treatment in this uncommon but important population.

articles.title: Evaluation of 68Ga Labeling Strategies and Thermostability of HER2-Targeted Nanobody NB46.
articles.abstract: The HER2-targeted nanobody NB46 was evaluated for labeling strategy flexibility and thermostability. Random and site-specific 68Ga labeling strategies were compared. Both conjugates exhibited high HER2 affinity, comparable to unmodified NB46. Cellular uptake, pharmacokinetics, micro-PET/CT imaging, and biodistribution in HER2-positive and HER2-negative tumor-bearing mice revealed no significant differences between the two strategies. NB46 retained HER2 affinity at temperatures up to 90 °C, demonstrating exceptional thermostability. Both conjugates achieved >95% radiochemical yields at all tested temperatures. Micro-PET/CT imaging showed sustained high tumor uptake with renal clearance as the primary elimination pathway. Blocking studies confirmed that NB46 and trastuzumab competitively bind to HER2. Elevated labeling temperatures did not compromise tumor targeting but resulted in a mild increase in renal uptake, notably for the random conjugate at 90 °C. These findings suggest that random labeling may represent a simpler, equally effective alternative for 68Ga-NB46 preparation, and confirm the excellent thermostability of this nanobody scaffold.

articles.title: Maleimide-Thiol Conjugation Enables the Optimization of 68Ga-Labeled CAIX Targeting PET Probes.
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a well-established biomarker of tumor hypoxia and an attractive target for molecular imaging. Despite the development of small-molecule CAIX-targeting positron emission tomography (PET) probes, most exhibit high normal-organ uptake and suboptimal tumor-to-background contrast. Moreover, their application in hypoxic tumors remains insufficiently explored. Herein, we reported four 68Ga-labeled CAIX-targeting probes based on the acetazolamide (AAZ) scaffold, employing distinct conjugation strategies, including amide coupling and maleimide-thiol ligation. All probes demonstrated detectable tumor uptake in vivo. Among them, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 displayed the highest tumor uptake (14.67 ± 3.06 %ID/g) and tumor-to-kidney ratio (1.69 ± 0.41) at 1 h in subcutaneous OS-RC-2-bearing mice, along with high tumor uptake in HT-29-bearing mice (2.98 ± 0.28 %ID/g at 1 h). Overall, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 demonstrates favorable imaging characteristics, with high tumor uptake and high tumor-to-normal organ ratios, representing a promising candidate for imaging CAIX-overexpressing tumors and supporting clinical translation.

articles.title: High-Affinity Y1 Receptor Theranostics: First-in-Class Stabilized Nonapeptides for Breast Cancer Imaging and Therapy.
articles.abstract: Theranostic agents integrate diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities into a single molecular platform, offering an advanced approach to personalized medicine. The neuropeptide Y1 receptor (Y1R) is a promising target for breast cancer theranostics given its overexpression across multiple disease stages. Building on the Y1R-selective antagonist [Lys2, Arg4]BVD-15, we report the systematic development of stabilized nonapeptide analogues through strategic modifications. Lead candidates were radiolabeled in >95% radiochemical purity and showed Y1R binding affinities up to 60-fold higher than the parent peptide, no detectable plasma degradation over 90 min, and half-lives of 42-55 min in liver and kidney homogenates. PET-CT imaging in HEK-Y1R and MCF-7 tumor models demonstrated selective tumor uptake, peaking at 19.2% ID/g in HEK-Y1R tumors, with biodistribution studies confirming specific tumor accumulation and progressive clearance over 48 h. Therapeutic evaluation of lead candidate [177Lu]Lu-31 in HEK-Y1R tumor-bearing mice showed dose-dependent tumor growth inhibition, supporting this peptide class as Y1R-targeted radionuclide therapeutics.

articles.title: [18F]ApaScan: A 2-Pyridinylbenzimidazole PET Tracer with Highly Selective Binding to Human Aldosterone-Producing Adenoma Tissue.
articles.abstract: Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) is overexpressed in aldosterone-producing adenomas (APAs) and represents a promising PET target for the noninvasive localization of APA lesions in primary aldosteronism. To address this need, we synthesized and evaluated 2-pyridinylbenzimidazole analogues for their ability to bind to human APA (hAPA) tissue. Based on initial binding assays, five analogues were selected and radiolabeled with fluorine-18 for autoradiographic and saturation binding studies. Among them, [18F]3 ([18F]ApaScan) exhibited high-affinity binding to hAPA homogenates (KD = 8.4 nM) with no measurable specific binding to normal adrenal (hNA) homogenates, demonstrating excellent tissue selectivity for hAPA over hNA. Quantitative autoradiography using [18F]3 further confirmed a high hAPA-to-hNA tissue binding ratio of 18. In normal rats, [18F]3 displayed rapid adrenal uptake, efficient clearance without prolonged retention, and no skeletal accumulation. Taken together, these results suggest that [18F]3 has the potential to be developed into a PET tracer for localizing APAs in primary aldosteronism.

articles.title: Frespaciguat (MK-5475): A Novel Inhaled Soluble Guanylate Cyclase Stimulator for Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with COPD.
articles.abstract: Soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulators are a validated therapeutic approach for pulmonary vasodilation; however, oral agents can cause systemic hypotension and may worsen ventilation-perfusion mismatch in pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (PH-COPD). To address these limitations, we applied a property-driven medicinal chemistry strategy to develop an inhaled sGC stimulator that maximizes pulmonary exposure while minimizing systemic exposure. Structure-activity relationship and pharmacokinetic studies identified high systemic clearance and low permeability as key determinants of pulmonary selectivity. These insights led to the discovery of compound 15 (frespaciguat, MK-5475), a subnanomolar sGC stimulator with a prolonged target residence time and >200-fold unbound lung-to-plasma exposure following inhalation. In a rat chronic hypoxia-induced PH model, frespaciguat produced dose-dependent reductions in pulmonary arterial pressure with minimal systemic hemodynamic effects and pharmacodynamic activity persisting >24 h after a single dose. These findings and early clinical data support the development of frespaciguat as an inhaled pulmonary-selective sGC stimulator for PH-COPD.

articles.title: Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled Heterodimers for Dual Integrin αvβ3 and PARP1-Targeted Tumor Imaging.
articles.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity limits the diagnostic performance of molecular imaging probes targeting a single biomarker. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and preclinical evaluation of 68Ga-labelled heterodimeric radiotracers co-targeting integrin αvβ3 and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) through a proposed "binding-anchoring" concept strategy. Conjugating the tumor-penetrating iRGD peptide with the PARP1 inhibitor niraparib and incorporating an albumin-binding moiety yielded the lead probe [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance supported nanomolar target-binding capability of the corresponding non-radiolabeled precursors. In the 4T1 breast cancer model, [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP exhibited a tumor uptake of 7.29 ± 0.28% ID/g at 1 h, approximately 4-5-fold higher than that of the corresponding single-target probes. Cytotoxicity, haemolysis and histopathological analyses confirmed excellent biocompatibility. These findings established [68Ga] Ga-NY-Dual-IP as a promising PET probe for precise tumor imaging and potential clinical translation.

articles.title: Preclinical Evaluation of 89Zr-Labeled Anti-Nectin-4 Antibody for Enhanced PET Imaging in Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the preclinical performance of a novel 89Zr-labeled anti-Nectin-4 monoclonal antibody, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282, for PET imaging of bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC). [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 was prepared via p-isothiocyanatobenzyl-desferrioxamine (p-NCS-Bn-DFO) conjugation, achieving a radiolabeling yield exceeding 70%, radiochemical purity ≥95% post-purification, and specific activity of 36.10-63.72 GBq/μmol. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 selectively accumulated in Nectin-4-positive cells and tumors, with uptake blocked by the unlabeled MW282 antibody. Small-animal PET/CT imaging revealed sustained tumor uptake in SW780 xenografts, with a high SUVmean value of 4.46 ± 0.02 at 120 h p.i. Owing to hepatobiliary clearance, the kidney and bladder uptake was minimal, yielding excellent imaging contrast. The probe demonstrated high specificity, prolonged tumor retention, and negligible bladder background, making it a promising immuno-PET probe for precise imaging of BUC and warranting further clinical translation.

articles.title: Summarizing Replicate Data from Medicinal Chemistry Assays.
articles.abstract: In medicinal chemistry, compounds of interest are tested in key assays multiple times to increase confidence in measured values. These replicate data are summarized into a single value for consideration by the project team. Different methods of summarizing replicate data can lead to different estimates of compound activity, different rank orderings of compounds, and potentially different decisions about which compounds to advance. Using an inappropriate summary method can result in misleading estimates that could impact the success of a project. It is not always obvious what method is appropriate for a given endpoint. This perspective outlines considerations for identifying an appropriate summary method and provides recommendations for 82 bioassay endpoints defined in the BioAssay Ontology.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Biphenyl Derivatives with Therapeutic Potential for Atrial Fibrillation by Synergistically Inhibiting NaV1.5 Late Na+ Current and K+ Current.
articles.abstract: To overcome the side effects of conduction block and QT prolongation associated with antiatrial fibrillation (AF) drug dronedarone, a novel class of dual IKr and late sodium current (late INa) inhibitors was developed through computational modeling, chemical modification, and electrophysiological screening. Lead compound 8b retained potent IKr inhibition (IC50 = 1.5 μM) comparable to dronedarone. Crucially, 8b avoided dronedarone's peak INa inhibition while enhancing late INa suppression (IC50 = 2.5 μM) to counteract excessive QT prolongation and avoid conduction block. Compound 8b exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic properties (T1/2 = 5.02 h, F = 110% in mice, p.o.) and high ion channel selectivity. In an ex vivo rabbit heart model of AF, 8b demonstrated antiarrhythmic efficacy. Furthermore, 8b was effective in treating doxorubicin-induced heart failure in mice, a condition where dronedarone shows no therapeutic benefit. Collectively, 8b could serve as a potential new class III antiarrhythmic candidate.

articles.title: Transitioning towards life-cycle management and burden monitoring of atrial fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses a significant burden on public health, being associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. In most cases, disease progression follows a continuum, ranging from a predominantly electrical disorder to late stages characterized by profound disruption of atrial architecture and advanced atrial cardiomyopathy.

AREAS COVERED: Common cardiovascular risk factors play a pivotal role in the progression and self-perpetuation of AF by promoting left atrial remodeling, creating the substrate necessary for the maintenance of the arrhythmia. Correction of these risk factors, together with rhythm-control strategies, can delay and, in some cases, interrupt disease progression while improving patients' quality of life. Catheter ablation, when combined with life-style modifications and risk factors management, has the potential to positively modify the arrhythmogenic substrate that favors AF and could promote reverse atrial remodeling.

EXPERT OPINION: Comprehensive management of risk factors and comorbidities, together with novel ablation techniques (e.g. pulsed field ablation) and the development of atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drugs, may further improve AF care. In addition, redefining long-term rhythm control success from freedom from AF recurrence to AF burden may allow better patient stratification, inform therapeutic decisions, and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Vascular smooth muscle cell abundance is a hallmark of Castleman Disease.
articles.abstract: Castleman disease (CD) is an inflammatory disorder characterized by lymphadenopathy with distinctive histologic features, yet its pathophysiology remains poorly understood. This delays diagnoses and limits treatments, leading to additional morbidity and mortality. We used single- cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize lymph nodes from unicentric CD (UCD) compared with non-specific inflammatory lymphadenopathies. While hematopoietic cells showed few compositional or transcriptional differences, lymph node stromal cells exhibited marked alterations in UCD, most notably an increased abundance of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and broadly increased stromal signaling activity. A generalized linear model distinguished histologically indeterminate lymph nodes resembling UCD from non-specific inflammation most accurately using stromal rather than hematopoietic cell composition. Immunohistochemical staining for the VSMC marker CD146 (Melanoma Cell Adhesion Molecule, MCAM) further discriminated UCD from other causes of lymphadenopathy. Together, these findings identify increased VSMC abundance as a hallmark of UCD and suggest that this stromal signature can be leveraged to improve pathologic diagnosis and patient stratification.

articles.title: Trends in Mortality of Patients with Central Venous Catheters versus Arteriovenous Accesses for Hemodialysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines favor arteriovenous (AV) access over central venous catheters (CVCs) for hemodialysis due in part to lower infection risk. Nevertheless, most patients initiate hemodialysis with a CVC. We used US Renal Data System data to evaluate whether the comparative mortality risk of these vascular access strategies has changed over time among patients with incident kidney failure.

METHODS: In this observational study, we evaluated community-dwelling, functionally independent adults (aged 18-85 years) initiating hemodialysis with a CVC in 2013-2022, excluding those with a maturing AV access to prevent immortal time bias. We used the clone-censor-weighting approach, a causal inference method for evaluating dynamic treatment patterns, to compare continuous CVC use versus transition to an AV access. Inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted discrete-time pooled logistic regression modeled the 18-month cumulative risk of death by hemodialysis initiation year, with modality changes treated as competing events.

RESULTS: Among 536,836 incident patients, 71,443 and 63,875 deaths occurred in the CVC and AV access groups, respectively. From 2013 to 2022, the adjusted 18-month cumulative risk of death declined from 26.8% to 21.3% in the CVC group, and from 20.9% to 17.1% in the AV access group. Correspondingly, the absolute risk difference comparing CVC versus AV access attenuated by nearly 30% (from 5.9 [95% CI 5.4, 6.3] to 4.2 [95% CI 3.9, 4.5] deaths per 100 patients), whereas the relative risk declined by 3% (from 1.28 [95% CI 1.26, 1.30] to 1.25 [95% CI 1.23, 1.27]). Bloodstream infection-related deaths showed similar declining risk patterns, with a proportionally larger attenuation in absolute risk difference and a greater decline in relative risk between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality rates declined among patients initiating hemodialysis with a CVC over the past decade, which has led to a reduction in the absolute excess risk associated with continued CVC use.

articles.title: Polygenic risk score identifies alternative etiologies in misdiagnosed cases of primary adrenal insufficiency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) is commonly caused by autoimmunity in adults, known as autoimmune Addison's disease (AAD). Autoantibodies against 21-hydroxylase are a hallmark of AAD but are absent in some patients diagnosed with AAD, posing a challenge to their clinical management.

METHODS: We tested a polygenic risk score for AAD (PRS14AAD) to prioritize seronegative patients for etiologic reevaluation. The PRS14AAD was calculated in patients diagnosed with AAD but lacking 21-hydroxylase autoantibodies (n = 124). Patients with low (n = 35) or high (n = 10) genetic susceptibility to AAD underwent clinical re-evaluation and whole-genome sequencing.

RESULTS: Of the 34 patients with low PRS14AAD, 14 (41%) were re-diagnosed with non-autoimmune adrenal insufficiency, whereas no alternative etiologies were identified in patients with high PRS14AAD. The low PRS group included six patients (17%) with confirmed monogenic PAI and eight patients (23%) with adrenal insufficiency due to either tuberculosis or non-primary causes. Notably, four of the six confirmed monogenic cases developed PAI in adulthood, consistent with late-onset disease caused by hypomorphic variants. Additionally, seven patients (20%) carried genetic variants suspected of causing monogenic disease.

CONCLUSION: These findings support considering genetic evaluation in patients with seronegative PAI, regardless of the age at diagnosis.

articles.title: Patiromer Efficacy across Kidney Function and Hyperkalemia Subgroups in Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: A DIAMOND Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the DIAMOND (Patiromer for the Management of Hyperkalemia in Subjects Receiving RAASi Medications for the Treatment of Heart Failure) trial, patiromer enabled optimization of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) for patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and current or recent hyperkalemia. Impaired kidney function substantially increases hyperkalemia risk due to impaired potassium excretion. Therefore, in this post hoc analysis, we examined the efficacy of patiromer across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups.

METHODS: We classified all patients randomized to patiromer (N=439) or placebo (N=439), after successful run-in optimization, into 4 subgroups according to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <45 vs ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 (trial eligibility criterion: ≥30 mL/min/1.73m2) and baseline hyperkalemia (≤5.0 vs >5.0 mEq/L; trial required K >5.0 or prior RAASi discontinuation for hyperkalemia).

RESULTS: Patiromer reduced adjusted mean change in serum potassium (primary outcome) across all subgroups, with the largest effect in patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and hyperkalemia (-0.28 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.38 to -0.18, P<0.001) and the smallest in those with eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 and normokalemia (-0.08 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.12 to -0.04, P<0.001; Pinteraction <0.001). Patiromer reduced time-to-first hyperkalemia consistently across subgroups. Patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and baseline hyperkalemia derived the numerically greatest effect in prevention of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist down-titration (hazard ratio 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.84, P=0.02) and had the highest win ratio for hyperkalemia-related morbidity-adjusted outcomes (3.03, 95% CI 1.96-4.70, P<0.001). However, Pinteraction values for these secondary endpoints were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Patiromer reduced serum potassium across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups, with greater effect in patients with reduced kidney function and baseline hyperkalemia. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in potassium-lowering effects of patiromer across subgroups, although the analysis is exploratory and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Sotatercept in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A GRADE-Assessed Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials with Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel therapy targeting this pathology. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess its efficacy and safety in PAH. A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating Sotatercept in adults with PAH. Data were pooled using random-effects models to estimate mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Four RCTs enrolling 921 patients were included. Compared with placebo, Sotatercept significantly improved 6-minute walk distance (MD 30.54 m, 95% CI 4.05-57.04, P=0.02), WHO functional class (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.37-2.15, P<0.00001), multicomponent improvement (RR 2.77, 95% CI 1.45-5.29, P=0.002), pulmonary vascular resistance (MD -197.01 dyn⋅s⋅cm-5, 95% CI -213.16 - -180.86, P<0.00001), and reduced clinical worsening events (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.21-0.38, P<0.00001). There were no significant differences in NT-proBNP levels or all-cause mortality. Safety analysis showed lower risks of serious adverse events (AEs), peripheral edema, and right ventricular failure, but higher rates of bleeding, epistaxis, and drug-related AEs. Sotatercept demonstrated meaningful clinical benefits in exercise capacity, hemodynamics, and disease progression among patients with PAH, with a generally acceptable safety profile. These findings support Sotatercept as a promising adjunct to standard therapy, though longer-term trials are needed to confirm durability and survival impact.

articles.title: Metal-supported versus conventional ultra-fine chest drains after pulmonary resection: a historical cohort study of drainage outcomes and placement learning curves.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Ultra-fine chest drains are susceptible to kinking and obstruction. We compared drainage outcomes and device-placement learning curves for a 10-F metal-supported, multi-side-port drain and a conventional 12-F drain after pulmonary resection.

METHODS: This single-centre historical cohort comprised 5,235 patients treated between 2006 and 2023. A conventional drain was used in 2,614 patients during 2006-2017, whereas 2,621 patients received the metal-supported drain during 2018-2023. The co-primary outcomes were additional catheter drainage and encapsulated pleural effusion. Firth logistic regression adjusted for age, gender, BMI, and ASA score. For the learning-curve analysis, a designated observer timed the first 261 consecutive procedures after adoption of each device, from the initial skin puncture to fixation of the final drain.

RESULTS: Additional catheter drainage was required in 7/2,621 (0.3%) patients in the metal-supported group and 30/2,614 (1.1%) in the conventional group (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.24, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.10-0.51; P < 0.001). Encapsulated pleural effusion occurred in 15/2,621 (0.6%) versus 34/2,614 (1.3%) patients, respectively (aOR 0.44, 95% CI 0.24-0.79; P = 0.006). Mean total placement time was 24.1±7.8 min with the metal-supported drain and 44.3±7.7 min with the conventional drain. The CUSUM curves reached their peaks at cases 90 and 71, respectively, and then declined. Although drainage duration, length of stay, and pain differed statistically, the absolute differences were small.

CONCLUSIONS: The metal-supported drain was associated with fewer drainage-related reinterventions, fewer encapsulated pleural effusions, and shorter placement times. Because device use was determined by treatment era, residual temporal confounding precludes firm causal inference.

articles.title: CT low attenuation area quantification versus visual scoring for early pulmonary emphysema detection in lung cancer screening.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans.

METHODS: A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

RESULTS: Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

articles.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations.

RESULTS: All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03164473.

articles.title: Tailoring carbon nitride nanoarchitecture and cellular interactions through hydrothermal alkaline etching.
articles.abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is a versatile material for biomedical, energy, and environmental applications. Bulk g-C3N4 is commonly used as a precursor for nanoscale objects, yet systematic links between synthesis conditions, nanostructure morphology, surface chemistry, and biological response remain limited. Here, we fabricated a palette of carbon nitride nanostructures via hydrothermal alkaline etching. By varying the hydroxide (LiOH, NaOH, or KOH) and reaction conditions, etching yields carbon nitride quantum dots (CNQDs), carbon nitride nanowires (CNNWs) and their networks, as well as larger flakes and sponge-like objects. Automated transmission electron microscopy image analysis supported this comparison by converting heterogeneous micrographs into object-level morphology and particle-size statistics. The hydroxide type also influenced surface chemistry: LiOH and KOH promoted more extensive oxidative functionalization, whereas NaOH yielded surfaces with lower levels of carboxyl groups and a larger amount of weakly bound OH species. All nanostructured carbon nitride samples showed high biocompatibility across multiple cell lines after 24 h incubation at 200 µg mL-1. Specifically, immortalized human cervical adenocarcinoma (HeLa) cell viability was essentially unchanged. Metabolic activity likewise remained near control levels in HeLa, immortalized human lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cells, immortalized mouse microglial (BV2) cells, human acute monocytic leukemia (THP-1)-derived macrophages, and immortalized mouse embryonic fibroblast (3T3) cells. Cellular accumulation in HeLa cells varied markedly with the preparation conditions of the nanostructured carbon nitrides. Notably, smaller nanostructures did not necessarily exhibit higher cellular accumulation, indicating that morphology and surface chemistry, in addition to particle size, influence cellular interactions. CNNW networks, with or without entangled CNQDs, may contribute more strongly to cell-associated fluorescence than isolated CNQDs. Overall, this work provides a practical route to tune carbon nitride nanostructures for bioimaging applications.

articles.title: Towards a consensus on the definition and nature of meta-therapy in voice therapy: Current state and future directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Meta-therapy is the nuanced relational dialogue employed by clinicians to facilitate effective and efficient behavioural change. Introduced within the context of voice therapy and recently applied in other domains of speech-language pathology, meta-therapy continues to evolve conceptually. This article presents a preliminary effort towards consensus-building about meta-therapy.

METHOD: A structured expert consensus development process was conducted with voice-specialised speech-language pathologists using elements of a modified Nominal Group Technique and developmental pre-Delphi construct refinement. Sixteen clinicians and three facilitators participated in a three-hour online meeting incorporating presentation, guided discussion, case-vignette analysis, and anonymous polling to refine conceptual boundaries of meta-therapy. Four additional co-authors reviewed the meeting recording. These 23 and two additional speech-language pathologists with prior exposure and expertise in meta-therapy contributed to iterative manuscript drafting and revision.

RESULT: Meta-therapy may distinguish experienced from novice voice clinicians. We refined the definition and disambiguated meta-therapy from indirect and direct therapy, counselling, and education. We proposed the function and role of meta-therapy in the context of voice therapy, next steps, and future directions.

CONCLUSION: This work represents the first attempt to seek consensus on how to define and operationalise meta-therapy as it pertains to voice therapy. Many concepts presented here should apply to other domains of behavioural therapy within the speech-language pathology field and in other rehabilitative fields. This work may guide future research in meta-therapy, including formal attempts to achieve consensus about the definition and nature of meta-therapy.

articles.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Mavacamten in Canada: Insights from the MAVEN Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Previous studies have demonstrated the efficacy and safety of mavacamten in patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), primarily outside of Canada, with limited Canadian real-world data evidence. The MAVEN study aimed to describe the real-world effectiveness of mavacamten in Canadian patients with oHCM.

METHODS: This multi-center, retrospective physician survey of patient charts included 115 patients with oHCM who initiated mavacamten between January 2023 and November 2024 across five Canadian sites. Effectiveness was assessed by changes in clinical characteristics and outcomes, including New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, resting and Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract (rLVOT and vLVOT, respectively) gradients, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), from treatment initiation to the most recent available assessment.

RESULTS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were consistent with previously published data (median age 63.0 years; 66.1% aged ≥ 60 years; 51.3% male, 48.7% female patients; 57.4% NYHA class II, 42.6% NYHA class III). Median baseline rLVOT and vLVOT gradients were 44.0 and 78.0 mmHg, respectively, and median LVEF was 65.0%. Overall, 72.7% of patients improved by ≥ 1 NYHA functional class. Median reductions in rLVOT and vLVOT gradients were - 25.5 (interquartile range [IQR]: - 61, - 8) mmHg and - 51.0 (IQR: - 83, - 24) mmHg, respectively, while median LVEF changed by - 3.0% (IQR: - 8, 0). Mavacamten was discontinued in 8.7% of patients, including 2.6% due to treatment-emergent adverse events. Reductions in LVEF < 50% were observed in 6.1% of patients, and no patient experienced an LVEF < 30%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this first Canadian real-world study of mavacamten effectiveness, treatment was associated with improvements in symptoms and LVOT obstruction. Reductions in LVEF < 50% were observed in a minority of patients, with no cases of LVEF < 30%. Given the retrospective design and heterogeneous follow-up of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Graphical abstract available for this article.

articles.title: A lightweight progressive residual convolutional network for interpretable arrhythmia classification.
articles.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
articles.abstract: Arrhythmia poses a serious threat to human health, necessitating research into automated diagnostic methods. Although advances have been made in arrhythmia classification using deep learning, existing models often suffer from high computational cost and poor interpretability, limiting their clinical applicability. To this end, this paper proposes a lightweight progressive residual convolutional attention network (DResCA). Through the synergistic design of stage-adaptive downsampling and channel attention, this network reduces parameter redundancy while enhancing deep ECG feature extraction. To enhance clinical interpretability, template matching and attention visualization are employed to reveal the key ECG regions underlying the model's diagnoses. Five-class classification experiments on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the model achieves 98.35% accuracy and 97.99% macro-F1 score while maintaining fewer parameters than mainstream deep learning models. These characteristics provide a practical technical pathway for real-time arrhythmia detection on wearable edge computing devices.

articles.title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification.

METHODS: In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).

RESULTS: Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).

CONCLUSION: The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

articles.title: Pneumothorax rates following cardiac surgery with versus without continuous serratus anterior plane catheters: a secondary analysis of trial data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate to severe pain is common after cardiac surgery, especially in the first two postoperative days. Inadequate pain control may prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay, may increase cost, and contributes to chronic pain. Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols prioritize multimodal analgesia, including regional anesthesia techniques. In a recent randomized trial with continuous serratus anterior plane (SAP) catheters, we found unexpectedly high pneumothorax rates. To address this, we aimed to design a propensity-score-matched comparison using patients from the same institution to control for institutional practice patterns, surgical techniques, and patient demographics that could confound comparisons with published literature rates from other centres.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of RCT data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort. We compared the pneumothorax rates in patients receiving continuous SAP catheters in our previous Cardiac-Serratus Anterior Plane (Cardiac-SAP) trial with those in a retrospective institutional database cohort of patients receiving standard care undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy. The two groups were propensity score matched in a 1:20 ratio based on age, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and pre-existing respiratory disease. We analyzed univariate comparisons using Fisher's exact test or the percentile bootstrapping method.

RESULTS: We matched 50 patients from the Cardiac-SAP trial to 989 retrospective cohort patients. After matching, the SAP catheter group was associated with a significantly higher risk of pneumothorax (12% vs 3%; odds ratio, 5.3; 95% confidence interval, 2.1 to 13.6; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences for other outcomes, including ICU readmissions, length of ventilation, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Patients who developed a pneumothorax had longer ventilation time and longer hospital stays.

CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggest that SAP catheter use as a part of a randomized trial for cardiac surgery was associated with a higher rate of pneumothorax in trial participants than in a historic cohort of a similar population, though causality is unclear. Differences in monitoring within the trial and the inherent risks in this population may have contributed.

articles.title: Disentangling direct and weight-mediated effects of physical activity on health-related quality of life in a 12-month real-world digital lifestyle intervention.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine whether participation in a 12-month digital lifestyle program was associated with increased physical activity and whether physical activity was associated with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) independently of weight loss.

METHODS: Self-reported weight and height were used to calculate body mass index (BMI). Physical activity (metabolic equivalent of task hours, MET-h/day) was assessed using a web-based questionnaire at baseline, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. HRQoL was measured with the RAND-36 at baseline, 6, and 12 months yielding eight domains and physical and mental component scores. Longitudinal mixed-effects models and mediation analyses were used to examine associations between physical activity, BMI, and HRQoL over time.

RESULTS: In 1732 individuals (82.9% women, median age 52 years, BMI 39.0 kg/m2), estimated marginal mean physical activity increased from 2.16 to 3.06 MET-h/day (p < 0.001). Periods of higher-than-usual physical activity were associated with lower BMI within individuals (B = - 0.032, 95% CI - 0.053 to - 0.012). Higher physical activity was also associated with better scores in most HRQoL dimensions, including physical and mental component scores. Indirect associations via BMI were largely limited to physical domains, whereas direct associations predominated: 84.9% of the total association with physical functioning and 88.0% of that with bodily pain were attributable to the direct pathway.

CONCLUSION: Participation in a digital lifestyle program was associated with increased physical activity, and physical activity was associated with better HRQoL largely independently of weight change, although follow-up was incomplete and the magnitude of the individual associations was modest. Physical activity merits attention as a treatment goal alongside weight management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (Clinical Trials Identifier NCT04019249). Registration date 12 Jul 2019. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Biomarker Ratio Concordance with Amyloid Positron-Emission Tomography: A Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker ratios (amyloid-β [Aβ]42/Aβ40, phosphorylated-tau [pTau]/Aβ42, and total tau [tTau]/Aβ42) are lower-cost alternatives to amyloid positron-emission tomography (PET) for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis. Among these CSF biomarker ratios, it is not clear whether concordance with amyloid PET is highest with Aβ42/Aβ40, pTau/Aβ42, or tTau/Aβ42. To evaluate this, we conducted a diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.

METHODS: Medline and Embase were searched for articles published between January 2008 and February 2026 reporting concordance of ≥ 1 CSF biomarker ratio with amyloid PET. Statistical analyses were performed using the bivariate model of Reitsma with the R package mada v0.5.11.

RESULTS: This quantitative meta-analysis comprised 38 studies, including a total of 7504 participants, with 35 studies available for statistical analysis. All three CSF biomarker ratios (Aβ42/Aβ40, pTau/Aβ42, and tTau/Aβ42) were highly concordant with amyloid PET. However, the pTau/Aβ42 ratio showed numerically higher overall percent agreement with amyloid PET positivity (90.4%) versus Aβ42/Aβ40 (89.5%) or tTau/Aβ42 (89.2%), a significantly higher area under the curve (0.955) versus Aβ42/Aβ40 (0.921, p value for difference 0.018), and a significantly lower false positive rate (0.116) versus Aβ42/Aβ40 (0.153, p value for difference 0.015).

CONCLUSION: pTau/Aβ42 showed the highest overall concordance with amyloid PET positivity and the lowest false positive rate versus Aβ42/Aβ40 or tTau/Aβ42.

articles.title: Development of a risk score to predict encephalitis by Herpes Simplex Virus and Varicella Zoster Virus.
articles.abstract: Encephalitis guidelines recommend repeating a lumbar puncture (LP) 3-7 days after an initial negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) herpes simplex virus (HSV) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test in patients with high suspicion for HSV or varicella zoster virus (VZV), but this subgroup has not been specified. Retrospective observational study of 602 adults with encephalitis from 2002 to 2023 from two large U.S. healthcare systems. Multivariate logistic regression models were developed and internally validated to identify clinically relevant and statistically significant features predicting HSV, VZV, and combined HSV/VZV encephalitis. HSV and VZV encephalitis were diagnosed in 103 (17.1%) and 43 (7.14%), respectively. Independent predictors for HSV acute presentation, new temporal lobe abnormalities on MRI, and hemorrhage on brain MRI. For VZV, predictors were immunosuppression, Charles Comorbidity Index > 2, and absence of seizures on presentation. For HSV/VZV, predictors included age ≥ 50 years, immunocompromise, acute presentation, CSF lymphocytosis, new temporal lobe abnormalities on MRI, hemorrhage on brain MRI, and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) ≥ 13 (P < 0.05). Patients were classified into 3 categories: low-risk (0 points), intermediate-risk (1 point), and high-risk (≥ 2 points). The area under the receiver operating curve was 0.675, 0.734, and 0.583 for the HSV, VZV, and HSV/VZV models, respectively. The risk score can help identify patients with an initial negative PCR who would benefit from a repeat LP (intermediate- or high-risk) and may support discontinuing acyclovir in low-risk patients.

articles.title: CLU attenuates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by inhibiting Bax-mediated mitochondrial damage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) is typified by unchecked inflammation and widespread cell death, yet the underlying molecular pathways are still unclear.

METHODS: Differentially expressed genes were identified from the GSE10474 dataset.
