Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis was employed to identify hub genes, and expression validation was carried out. An in vitro model of ALI caused by sepsis was applied to confirm CLU expression. CLU expression was assessed by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. To investigate the function and mechanism of CLU expression, functional assays such as cell viability assays, flow cytometry, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), cytochrome c (Cyto c) release, and Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) assays, ATP content, and mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) were carried out.

RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified six hub genes (CDKN1A, HIST1H3F, HLA-DQB1, CD74, VDAC1, and CLU) as downregulated in sepsis-induced ALI. The reduction of CLU expression in the ALI model was validated by experimental validation, whereas its overexpression decreased apoptosis and restored cell viability. Mechanistically, CLU interacted with Bax and inhibited its translocation to mitochondria, which may contribute to Cyto c release, preserving ATP content and ΔΨm, maintaining mitochondrial morphology, and reducing ROS accumulation. Crucially, the protective effect of CLU was attenuated by overexpressing Bax, which resulted in increased apoptosis, lower cell viability, increased reactive oxygen species, and worsened mitochondrial damage.

CONCLUSION: Our in‑vitro findings suggest that CLU could mitigate apoptosis in the sepsis‑induced ALI cell model, at least partly through modulating Bax‑dependent mitochondrial damage. These results point to CLU as a possible treatment target for ALI caused by sepsis.

articles.title: Readiness for precision medicine: pharmacogenomic literacy among adults surveyed in the United Arab Emirates: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacogenomics is increasingly being incorporated into precision medicine to support safer and more effective drug therapy. As the clinical use of pharmacogenomic testing expands, public understanding of its purpose and limitations becomes increasingly important. However, information on pharmacogenomic literacy among the general population in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is scarce.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess pharmacogenomic literacy among adults in the UAE using the Minnesota Assessment of Pharmacogenomic Literacy (MAPL) and to examine sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with pharmacogenomic literacy.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between March and May 2026 among adults living in the UAE. Pharmacogenomic literacy was measured using the validated 15-item MAPL. Scores were classified as low, moderate, or high according to Bloom's cut-off criteria. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics and MAPL responses. Ordinal logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with pharmacogenomic literacy. Associations were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: A total of 626 individuals participated. The mean MAPL score was 8.1 (95% CI 7.9-8.2). Overall, 59.4% of participants had low pharmacogenomic literacy, 36.6% had moderate literacy, and 4.0% had high literacy. Participants generally showed good knowledge of basic genetic concepts, but important misconceptions were identified regarding the clinical role of pharmacogenomic testing. More than 60% incorrectly believed that pharmacogenomic testing could identify the best medication, predict responses to all medicines, or establish a medical diagnosis. Previous experience with genetic testing was associated with higher pharmacogenomic literacy (OR = 2.43, 95% CI 2.09-2.83; p < 0.001). Participants aged 35-44 years had slightly lower odds of higher literacy than those aged 45 years or older (OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.82-1.00; p < 0.05). No significant associations were observed for sex and employment status.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacogenomic literacy among adults in the UAE was limited despite a reasonable understanding of basic genetic principles. The largest knowledge gaps concerned the clinical applications and limitations of pharmacogenomic testing. Previous genetic testing experience was associated with better literacy. These findings support accessible educational initiatives and patient-centered communication to promote informed use of pharmacogenomics as precision medicine becomes more widely implemented.

articles.title: Thulium laser-assisted delivery of growth factors for treating androgenetic alopecia - a randomized, controlled, clinical study.
articles.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common form of hair loss and can significantly impact quality of life. Emerging non-invasive treatments include laser-assisted delivery of biomimetic growth factor-based serums. The aim of the study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of non-ablative fractional laser (NAFL)-assisted delivery, with or without adjunct red light therapy, in patients with AGA. In this pilot study, patients were randomly assigned to: (I) NAFL-assisted serum delivery plus red light therapy (triple), (II) NAFL-assisted serum delivery alone (dual), or (III) NAFL plus red light therapy without serum (EBD-only). Primary outcomes were hair density and thickness. Secondary outcomes included patient satisfaction, tolerability, and adverse events. Hair density increased in all groups, with greater improvement in the triple (25.6 ± 7.0 %) and dual (22.7 ± 3.4 %) groups compared to EBD-only (4.9 ± 9.2 %). Hair thickness improved in both serum groups but not in the EBD-only group. Clinical outcomes were similar between triple and dual treatments, though satisfaction was higher with triple therapy. No severe adverse events occurred. Preliminary evidence suggests that NAFL-assisted delivery of biomimetic growth factors is a safe and effective non-invasive treatment for AGA.

articles.title: Are adropin gene expression levels a precursor to type 2 diabetes mellitus in prediabetic patients?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated the relationship between adropin and glucose metabolism by evaluating ENHO gene expression and serum adropin levels in individuals with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), prediabetes, and healthy controls, and their potential as biomarkers for early diagnosis.

METHODS: A total of 107 participants were enrolled, including 40 T2DM patients, 26 with prediabetes, and 41 healthy controls. Serum adropin levels were measured using ELISA, and ENHO gene expression levels were assessed by quantitative real-time PCR from peripheral blood samples. Biochemical parameters, including glucose, HbA1c, insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, cholesterol, HDL, and LDL, were analyzed. Statistical comparisons between groups, correlation, logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: ENHO gene expression levels were significantly higher in the prediabetes group than in controls and T2DM, whereas it was lower in T2DM patients than in controls. Serum adropin levels were significantly elevated in the T2DM group compared with prediabetes and controls, but no difference was observed between prediabetes and controls. Glucose was negatively correlated with ENHO expression in prediabetes and with serum adropin in T2DM. ENHO expression was a significant predictor of T2DM progression, demonstrating high diagnostic potential.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that ENHO gene expression level may increase in prediabetes as a compensatory mechanism, whereas it decreases in T2DM, indicating disease progression. The paradoxical elevation of serum adropin in T2DM may reflect metabolic alterations. ENHO expression could serve as a potential biomarker for identifying individuals at risk of developing T2DM, warranting further large-scale studies.

articles.title: Administration-order effects in head-to-head comparisons of the EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L descriptive systems: evidence from a randomised general-population panel in Great Britain.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L are commonly compared within the same questionnaire, but answering one may influence responses to the other. We randomised administration order to estimate descriptive properties before exposure to the alternative version and quantify order effects.

METHODS: In Wave 11 of the Understanding Society Innovation Panel, respondents were randomised to the EQ-5D-5L-first condition (n = 952), the EQ-5D-3L-first condition (n = 961), or the EQ-5D-5L-only condition in the late questionnaire position (n = 983). Outcomes included the full-health ceiling, response distributions, and Shannon informativity.

RESULTS: When each version was answered in the early questionnaire position, the full-health ceiling was 52.1% for the EQ-5D-3L and 35.4% for the EQ-5D-5L (difference 16.7% points, 95% CI 12.2 to 21.3), and the EQ-5D-5L was more informative on every dimension. Moving the EQ-5D-5L to the late position without prior EQ-5D-3L exposure changed its ceiling by 2.5 points (95% CI -2.0 to 7.0), whereas prior EQ-5D-3L exposure at the same position raised it by 12.8 points (8.2 to 17.4). Among interviewer-present interviews, the EQ-5D-5L ceiling was 34.5% without prior EQ-5D-3L, 43.0% after the EQ-5D-3L without noticing repetition, and 53.2% among those who noticed.

CONCLUSION: The EQ-5D-5L order effect arose predominantly from prior EQ-5D-3L exposure rather than questionnaire position and was stronger among respondents who noticed the repetition, consistent with response contamination. Studies comparing instruments within one questionnaire should randomise and report administration order.

articles.title: Impact of remote management using patient-reported outcomes on pain and anxiety after breast biopsy: the BIO-PSY randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although breast biopsy is a routine procedure, it often triggers significant pain and anxiety. Pre-procedural distress has been associated with increased pain and discomfort, and persistent post-biopsy distress may affect psychological and treatment-related outcomes. However, post-biopsy care still lacks standardized follow-up. This study evaluated whether remote monitoring using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) triggering targeted interventions could improve pain and anxiety management after breast biopsy.

METHODS: BIO-PSY was a French, monocentric, open-labelled, randomized controlled trial. Patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing breast biopsy were randomized (1:1:1) to daily phone-based PROs (phone contact with a psycho-oncologist for 3 days), e-PROs (electronic interface for 3 days), or standard care. Alerts generated based on PROs thresholds prompted tailored interventions. The primary endpoint was pain on day 4 (0-10 numerical rating scale, phone-assessed). Secondary outcomes included pain at day 10; anxiety and perceived aesthetic impact (days 4 and 10); insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index) at day 10; and strategies for symptoms management.

RESULTS: Among 193 patients, pain was negligible (median = 0), stable, and not statistically different between arms at day 4 and 10 (p > 0.05). The proportion of patients with clinically significant anxiety was lower in the experimental arms than in the control arm at day 4 (p < 0.001) and was lower at day 10 only in the phone-based PRO arm (adjusted p = 0.008).

CONCLUSION: Pain after breast biopsy was well controlled across all arms. Remote monitoring using PROs may reduce anxiety, especially with human intervention, supporting its integration into routine post-biopsy care.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04456920 (registered on June 23, 2020).

articles.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
articles.abstract: The implementation of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin assays has significantly improved the prompt diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Nevertheless, early risk stratification and the swift diagnosis of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain challenging. We report a machine-learning-integrated NLRC3/cTnT dual-analyte time-resolved fluorescent lateral-flow immunoassay biosensor for quantitative ACS screening and discrimination of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) from unstable angina (UA). The biosensor uses europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel lateral-flow setup to simultaneously detect NLRC3 and cTnT within 20 min. The original serum sample is diluted separately for each channel, with 100 µL of the diluted sample applied to each. The optimized NLRC3 and cTnT assays demonstrated strong quantitative performance, precision, minimal cross-reactivity, and acceptable interference resistance. In clinical evaluation, NLRC3 alone identified ACS with 80.5% accuracy but was less effective in distinguishing AMI-UA. By combining NLRC3 and cTnT using a Naïve Bayes classifier, the dual-analyte biosensor improved to 84.6% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity, and 87.8% accuracy for AMI-UA discrimination. This study introduces a dual-pathophysiology lateral-flow biosensor that merges inflammatory-risk and myocardial-injury detection, providing a practical POCT method for decentralized ACS triage.

articles.title: Molecular-genetic mechanisms of cerebral arteriovenous malformations: A systematic review of germline, somatic and experimental evidence.
articles.abstract: Cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are high-flow vascular anomalies that carry a considerable burden of haemorrhagic morbidity. Work over the past decade has shown that both inherited syndromes and apparently sporadic lesions can be traced to alterations in a handful of signalling pathways, but the relevant evidence sits awkwardly between human genetic studies, animal models, and molecular profiling experiments. To bring together the current evidence on the molecular and genetic underpinnings of cerebral AVM formation, clinical course, and candidate therapeutic targets. We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from inception to 1 January 2026. Records were screened, and full texts assessed, by two reviewers working independently. Studies were eligible if they reported genetic, molecular, or epigenetic data on cerebral AVMs. Because of substantial heterogeneity in designs and outcomes, evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Of 343 records, 44 primary studies (28 clinico-genetic and 16 experimental) together with 20 reviews and meta-analyses met inclusion. Inherited AVM syndromes largely reflected germline variants in the TGF-β/BMP network (ENG, ACVRL1, SMAD4, GDF2/BMP9) or in arteriovenous-specification regulators (RASA1, EPHB4); penetrance was incomplete and there was support for local modifying "second-hit" events. Resected sporadic cerebral AVMs often carried somatic activating mutations in the RAS/MAPK cascade-mostly KRAS, less often BRAF-at low variant allele fractions that demanded high-sensitivity assays. Endothelial-specific activation of KRAS or BRAF reproduced AVM-like phenotypes in vivo and showed MEK-ERK dependence. Susceptibility variants (notably at 9p21/ANRIL), inflammatory mediators, extracellular-matrix remodelling, and epigenetic changes appear to fine-tune lesion behaviour and haemorrhagic risk. Syndromic predisposition and clonal somatic events in endothelium converge on a small set of developmental signalling axes that govern angiogenesis and vessel-wall maturation. Diagnostics anchored in this biology, together with pathway-targeted therapy, now need prospective evaluation, paired with standardised approaches for detecting low-level mosaicism.

articles.title: Bolus-only versus bolus plus continuous infusion hydromorphone for refractory cancer pain: a prospective, multicenter, randomized noninferiority trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Refractory cancer pain (RCP) remains difficult to manage despite guideline-based therapy. Patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) is increasingly used, yet the optimal administration mode remains unclear.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, randomized, non-inferiority trial, patients with refractory cancer pain were enrolled between December 1, 2018, and August 31, 2022, and randomly assigned to either a bolus-only PCIA group (Group B) or a bolus plus continuous infusion group (Group BC). Pain intensity was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). The primary endpoint was the pain relief rate at 72 h after PCIA initiation, defined as the proportion of patients achieving a ≥ 50% reduction in resting pain intensity from baseline. Non-inferiority was evaluated using the 90% confidence interval (CI) for the between-group difference, with a predefined non-inferiority margin of - 10%.

RESULTS: A total of 226 patients were randomized. with 104 assigned to Group B and 111 to Group BC. Both groups showed significant reductions in resting NRS scores and breakthrough cancer pain (BTcP) NRS scores from T1 to T6 compared with baseline (all P < 0.05). At 72 h, the pain relief rate was 89.4% in Group B and 94.2% in Group BC. The between-group difference yielded a 90% CI of - 11.2% to 1.1%, which crossed the predefined non-inferiority margin. Therefore, non-inferiority of Group B compared with Group BC was not demonstrated. The incidence of PCIA-related adverse events was comparable between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: Non-inferiority of bolus-only PCIA compared with bolus plus continuous infusion was not established. Nevertheless, both PCIA administration modes provided effective analgesia and demonstrated favorable safety profiles in patients with refractory cancer pain.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR1800020014. Registered 19 November 2018, https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=32731.

articles.title: Translational applications and clinical utility of organoids in ovarian cancer: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and the rapid emergence of platinum resistance. Traditional treatment selection relies on population-level guidelines that often fail to account for individual tumor heterogeneity. Patient-derived organoids have emerged as potential functional avatars for personalized therapy, providing a real-time read-out of tumor sensitivity.

METHODS: This systematic review synthesized data from 13 studies evaluating the feasibility, histological fidelity, and clinical concordance of ovarian cancer patient-derived organoids. Studies were assessed for quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and QUADAS-2.

RESULTS: A pooled analysis identified a mean success rate of 71% for obtaining patient-derived tumor organoids in early passages, with short-term assays showing high feasibility for immediate therapy guidance. Because the majority of the included studies relied on short-term cultures, these figures represent early-passage obtention rather than the true "establishment" of stable, cryopreservable lines that can be propagated beyond five passages. Indeed, a direct comparison of establishment rates for such long-term lines was precluded by the inconsistent reporting of total sample sizes (denominators) across the included publications-an important reporting gap that should be addressed in future studies. While 92.3% of studies reported high concordance between PDTO drug sensitivity and patient outcomes for platinum and PARP inhibitors, critical discordance in specific models suggests that growth robustness does not always guarantee predictive accuracy.

CONCLUSION: PDOs represent a robust platform for functional drug screening within a clinically actionable 21-day window. To move into routine practice, the field requires standardized proficiency testing, harmonized reporting of establishment denominators, and the integration of complex stroma-containing models to better reflect the tumor microenvironment.

articles.title: Re: Prognostic significance of the prothrombin time-international normalized ratio to albumin ratio in cancer patients with complication of sepsis: a retrospectively cohort study.
Clinical and serological features according to anti-DFS70 antibody status in undifferentiated connective tissue disease: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to compare demographic, clinical, laboratory, and autoantibody profiles between anti-dense fine speckled 70 (DFS70)-positive and -negative patients with undifferentiated connective tissue disease (UCTD). We retrospectively analyzed 284 UCTD patients followed at a tertiary rheumatology centre between January 2017 and December 2024. Patients fulfilling established classification criteria for a defined connective tissue disease were excluded. Patients were stratified according to anti-DFS70 status. Group comparisons were performed, and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. A multivariable logistic regression model was additionally used to evaluate the potential confounding effect of hydroxychloroquine use. Of 284 patients, 75 (26.4%) were anti-DFS70 positive and 209 (73.6%) were negative. After false discovery rate correction, arthritis/arthralgia was more frequent in the anti-DFS70-negative group than in the positive group (81.8% vs. 61.3%, adjusted p = 0.034), as was homogeneous ANA pattern (33.5% vs. 12.0%, adjusted p = 0.034). In multivariable analysis, homogeneous ANA pattern remained associated with anti-DFS70 negativity after adjustment for hydroxychloroquine use (OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.16-6.30, p = 0.021), whereas arthritis/arthralgia did not remain statistically significant (OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.95-3.90, p = 0.071). Anti-DFS70 negativity in UCTD was associated with homogeneous ANA pattern. Clinical associations, particularly arthritis/arthralgia, should be interpreted cautiously because of potential confounding by treatment exposure. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify the clinical significance of anti-DFS70 status in UCTD.

articles.title: [Psychotherapeutic interventions for reducing stress in patients with cardiac arrhythmias].
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain asymptomatic, but they can also be experienced as palpitations or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) shocks that feel existentially threatening. Even harmless arrhythmias can trigger intense anxiety reactions, including traumatic processing. Therefore, in addition to cardiological diagnostics and treatment, an integrative psychocardiological perspective is needed. From a cardiological point of view, the symptom burden should be reduced, for example, by avoiding substances that promote arrhythmias, treating underlying diseases, and-particularly in ICD patients-optimizing potassium levels. Psychoeducation is central: patients should understand why extrasystoles may be experienced as missed beats, strong palpitations, or a sensation of the "heart beating up into the throat." Equally important is discussing the vicious circle of anxiety: tension, worry, and self-monitoring lower the threshold for perception; perceived cardiac symptoms then intensify anxiety and autonomic arousal. Since these signals are interoceptive, avoidance is not possible, and patients should be taught routines that help them break out of the anxiety cycle. Special attention should be given to patients after an ICD shock or cardiac arrest. They may develop posttraumatic stress disorder induced by the cardiac event (CDI-PTSD). Supportive communication, realistic hope, and basic psychosomatic or psychocardiological interventions can reduce nocebo effects and anxiety spirals. In addition, this approach may help identify patients whose need for treatment should be discussed within a "Psycho-Cardio-Team" that still needs to be established.

articles.title: What's new in trauma critical care?
authors: ESICM Trauma and Emergency Medicine Section

articles.title: Principles of drug dosing for obese patients in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The increasing prevalence of severe obesity in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has led to several challenges with medication dosing. Doses listed in product labels or tertiary references typically do not account for the pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic variability encountered with obesity, leading to the potential for treatment failure or an adverse effect. The purpose of this review is to provide guidance for ICU clinicians when crafting pharmacotherapy regimens in critically ill patients with extreme obesity.

METHODS: A literature search was performed to identify relevant articles pertaining to the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of medications in obese patients. Articles describing both general treatment principles and medication specific assessments were retrieved. Bibliographies were searched for additional publications.

RESULTS: Evidence guiding medication use in critically ill obese patients is limited by the small number of patients with more extreme forms of obesity, the lack of clinical outcome measurements, and the few studies that are specific to the ICU. Obesity-related alterations in pharmacokinetic parameters, such as apparent volume of distribution and drug clearance, may hinder attainment of pharmacodynamic targets. Individualized dosing strategies are essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review provides dosing recommendations for selected ICU medications and proposes a practical framework to guide medication dosing decisions in this patient population.

CONCLUSION: Drug dosing in critically ill obese patients should be individualized by assessing pharmacokinetic variability and whether pharmacodynamic goals can be achieved. Selecting the correct weight for weight-based calculations or dose for fixed regimens is paramount for achieving these goals. Consultation with a clinical pharmacist may be beneficial.

articles.title: Dual-layer spectral CT-derived iodine and extracellular volume biomarkers for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in Fontan-associated liver disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived normalized iodine concentration and extracellular volume fraction for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in patients with Fontan-associated liver disease.

METHODS: This single-center exploratory retrospective study included 23 patients with Fontan-associated liver disease who underwent both liver biopsy and delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT between January 2021 and December 2023. Normalized iodine concentration was calculated as hepatic iodine concentration divided by aortic iodine concentration. Hematocrit-adjusted extracellular volume fraction (ECV) was calculated from delayed-phase iodine-density maps. Histologic fibrosis stage based on the METAVIR system was used as the reference standard. Associations between CT biomarkers and fibrosis stage were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test, and Spearman correlation. Diagnostic performance for advanced fibrosis (≥ F3) and cirrhosis (F4) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: Histologic fibrosis stages were F1 in 4 patients, F2 in 2, F3 in 9, and F4 in 8. ECV was higher in advanced fibrosis stages, with median values of 39.21% in F1, 37.15% in F2, 42.72% in F3, and 46.78% in F4. ECV differed significantly among fibrosis stages (p = 0.014), showed a significant ordered trend (p < 0.001), and correlated positively with histologic stage (ρ = 0.666, p < 0.001). IC-normalized showed a weak positive correlation with fibrosis stage, but the ordered trend did not reach statistical significance. For advanced fibrosis, ECV showed promising preliminary discrimination, with an AUC of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.766-1.000). For cirrhosis, ECV showed an AUC of 0.833 (95% CI, 0.655-1.000), with sensitivity of 87.5%, specificity of 80.0%, and negative predictive value of 92.3% at a cutoff of 43.45%.

CONCLUSION: In this single-center exploratory study, delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived ECV showed a significant association with histologic fibrosis severity and promising preliminary discrimination for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in Fontan-associated liver disease. External validation in larger, independent Fontan cohorts is required before clinical application.

articles.title: The early diagnostic value of emergency laboratory indicators in patients with acute compartment syndrome after tibiofibular fractures.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) is a serious complication after tibiofibular fractures, which may cause muscle necrosis or even amputation due to challenges in making a prompt diagnosis. Therefore, this study tries to investigate its potential biomarkers from emergency blood tests.

METHODS: Data on patients with tibiofibular fractures from January 2016 to January 2026 were gathered from three Level I trauma centres and categorized into ACS and non-ACS groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) analysis was used to reduce the impact of potential confounding variables. Then, univariate, logistic regression, and ROC curve analyses, as well as a nomogram prediction model, were performed to examine predictors of ACS.

RESULTS: After PSM analysis, 260 patients were assigned to each group. Even though univariate analysis identified several indicators related to ACS, logistic regression analysis demonstrated that creatine kinase [CK, p < 0.001, OR = 1.003, 95% CI (1.002, 1.004)], creatine kinase myocardial band [CK-MB, p < 0.001, OR = 1.171, 95% CI (1.125, 1.219)], and C-reactive protein [CRP, p < 0.001, OR = 1.259, 95% CI (1.150, 1.377)] are predictors. Furthermore, ROC curve analysis identified 1219.5 U/L, 34.5 U/L, and 13.5 mg/L as the optimal cut-off values to diagnose ACS in patients with tibiofibular fractures. Our model predicts with an AUC of 0.8519 [95% CI (0.8184, 0.8813)], showing consistent calibration and effective clinical application as evidenced by decision curve analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: The levels of CK, CK-MB, and CRP were found to be potential biomarkers for ACS, with their optimal cut-off values identified. Our nomogram prediction model can accurately predict ACS in patients with tibiofibular fractures. We still need large sample data to validate these results.

articles.title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).

CONCLUSIONS: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

articles.title: Aveir VR for Atrial Leadless Pacing in Young Patients.
articles.abstract: Atrial Leadless pacemaker implantspresent a new treatment for sinus node dysfunction in complex cardiac anatomies. The Aveir-VR single chamber pacemaker can be placed in the atrium to control atrial flutter, or in the ventricle to control bradycardia. In this case report, we present four cases of the implantation of the Aveir VR in the atrium of male pediatric patients to treat sinus node dysfunction. Retrospective review of patients with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and atrially placed Aveir-VRs was performed at UC Davis between April 2024 and April 2026. Femoral access was the route of implantation for all 5 patients. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was used in all cases. The patients' ages ranged between 14-17-years and follow-up appointments were held between 1-23-months. Immediately post-procedure, impedances were 380-1460 Ohms, thresholds at 0.4 ms were 2.25-3.5 V, and P-waves were between 1.7-3 mV. Follow-up impedance was between 390-720 Ohms for the patients, thresholds were 0.5-1.25 V at 0.2-0.4 ms, P-waves were between 4.5-9.1 mV, and pacing percentages were between 12-69%. This case series demonstrates the successful implant of Aveir VR leadless pacemaker in five young patients for sinus node dysfunction.

articles.title: Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Children and Adolescents with Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Celiac disease (CD) is recognized as a systemic disorder extending beyond the gastrointestinal tract, with evidence of subclinical cardiovascular involvement emerging even in childhood. We aimed to evaluate myocardial function in children with CD compared to healthy controls, and to investigate whether echocardiographic parameters differ according to gluten-free diet adherence. This cross-sectional case-control study included 142 children with CD and 120 healthy controls. Conventional and advanced echocardiography were performed in all participants. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI) z-score was used for all echocardiographic outcomes. Patients were stratified by anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (anti-tTG IgA) into tTG-negative (n = 55), borderline (n = 13), and positive (n = 74) subgroups. Ejection Fraction (EF) and Fractional Shortening (FS) were modestly but significantly reduced in CD patients, while left ventricular (LV) dimensions and LV mass were not significantly different. All Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) parameters were significantly impaired in CD patients, including elevated Myocardial Performance Index (MPI) and E/e' ratios at both septal and lateral mitral annulus (p < 0.001). Myocardial function was impaired across all serological subgroups compared to controls, with no significant differences among celiac subgroups in multivariable analysis. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability of MPI between celiac patients and healthy controls, after adjustment for age, sex and z-score BMI. Children with CD demonstrate significant subclinical myocardial dysfunction, detectable by TDI, independently of serological disease activity. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to establish the long-term cardiovascular implications and the role of routine cardiac monitoring in this population.

articles.title: Patient-Centered Value Elements in the Economic Evaluation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Targeted Review of Cost-Effectiveness Analyses.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the extent to which economic evaluations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease treatments incorporated patient-informed value elements (PIVEs) and value flower elements (VFEs), and to examine their association with economic outcomes.

METHODS: A targeted search of PubMed, Embase, and the Tufts Cost-Effectiveness Analysis Registry identified full-length economic evaluations of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease treatments published between 2018 and 2026. Studies were reviewed for inclusion of PIVEs and VFEs. Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and exploratory linear regression analyses examined associations between PIVEs, VFEs, and economic outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 58 studies, 57 were cost-effectiveness or cost-utility analyses conducted from a healthcare system perspective (n = 49). Physical endurance was included in all studies, whereas other PIVEs, including side effects (n = 17), access to care (n = 17), explanation of benefits and risks (n = 13), new therapeutic options (n = 11), and willingness to pay (n = 5), were less commonly considered. Among VFEs, quality-adjusted life-years (n = 55) and net cost (n = 57) predominated, while adherence-improving factors (n = 18), productivity (n = 14), reduction in uncertainty (n = 3), and severity of disease (n = 1) were inconsistently incorporated. Only one study reported direct patient engagement. Exploratory analyses found no consistent association between inclusion of PIVEs or VFEs and economic outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Economic evaluations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease treatments predominantly relied on net costs and quality-adjusted life-years, with limited incorporation of broader PIVEs or VFEs and rare patient engagement. The influence of broader value elements on economic outcomes remains uncertain. Future research should evaluate challenges to incorporating context-relevant PIVEs and VFEs and their implications for economic evaluation and healthcare decision making.

articles.title: Pediatric Gastroenterology.
Ginsenoside Rg3 attenuates hyperuricemia-associated AKI by upregulating CPT1A and suppressing NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis.
articles.journal: In vitro cellular & developmental biology. Animal
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia-associated acute kidney injury (HUA-AKI), a frequent complication of chronic hyperuricemia, is driven by oxidative stress, inflammation, and pyroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells. Ginsenoside Rg3, a principal bioactive compound derived from Panax ginseng, possesses anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory activities; however, its therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms in HUA-AKI remain elusive. In this study, an HUA-AKI mouse model was established via intraperitoneal injection of potassium oxonate combined with oral hypoxanthine, and an in vitro model using uric acid (UA)-stimulated HK-2 cells. Rg3 treatment markedly improved renal function, reduced tubular injury, and alleviated oxidative stress without altering serum UA levels. Transcriptomic profiling identified 229 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) reversed by Rg3, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis revealed significant inhibition of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and pyroptosis pathways, alongside upregulation of the carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A)-mediated fatty acid oxidation pathway. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmed that Rg3 upregulated CPT1A expression and suppressed activation of NLRP3, cleaved caspase‑1, gasdermin D N‑terminal fragment (GSDMD‑NT), as well as the release of interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 in both mouse kidney tissues and HK-2 cells. Notably, co-administration of the CPT1A inhibitor sodium taurocholate (STC) partially abolished the renoprotective effects of Rg3, as demonstrated by restored cell viability, elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, re‑elevation of pyroptosis-related proteins and cytokines, and reappearance of membrane pore formation and rupture under transmission electron microscopy. Collectively, our findings suggest that Rg3 may ameliorate HUA‑AKI, at least in part, through CPT1A upregulation and subsequent suppression of the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD axis, positioning Rg3 as a promising therapeutic candidate for HUA-AKI.

articles.title: Impact of exposure to environmental chemicals on the occurrence of molar incisor hypomineralisation and developmental enamel defects in children: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European archives of paediatric dentistry : official journal of the European Academy of Paediatric Dentistry
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children are particularly susceptible to environmental toxins because of their immature metabolic and detoxification systems. Disturbances during enamel formation may result in molar incisor hypomineralisation (MIH) and developmental defects of enamel (DDE). This systematic review evaluated the association between exposure to environmental pollutants and the occurrence of MIH and DDE in children.

METHODS: The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251149569). A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, EBSCO Host, and Web of Science identified observational studies published up to 2025.

RESULTS: Of 384 records identified, 9 studies met the eligibility criteria, including three cohort, one case-control, and five cross-sectional studies. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Pollutants evaluated included polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and furans (PCDD/Fs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), particulate matter (PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀), and phenols and phthalates. Studies investigating PCBs and PCDD/Fs generally reported positive associations between prenatal or early postnatal exposure and increased occurrence or severity of MIH and DDE. Higher dioxin concentrations in maternal milk were also associated with more frequent and severe enamel hypomineralisation, with dose-response relationships reported in some studies. Evidence regarding PFAS was congener- and sex-specific, whereas findings for ambient air pollution, phenols, and phthalates were limited and inconsistent.

CONCLUSION: Available evidence suggests an association between exposure to environmental pollutants and developmental enamel defects, particularly following exposure to persistent organic pollutants. However, heterogeneity in exposure assessment, diagnostic criteria, study design, and confounder adjustment limits the certainty of the evidence. Well-designed longitudinal studies using standardised diagnostic criteria and biomarker-based exposure assessment are needed to clarify these associations and determine potential causal relationships.

articles.title: Integrating Scalability and Equity into Hypertension Remote Patient Monitoring Program Design.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) for hypertension combines home blood pressure (BP) monitoring with electronic transmission of BP readings and clinical support. RPM has the potential to improve BP control and reduce hypertension disparities, but because it depends on devices, connectivity, digital literacy, and sustained engagement, it may also worsen inequities if not intentionally designed. This review examines barriers to equitable RPM implementation and strategies to address them.

RECENT FINDINGS: RPM can improve hypertension control and extend care beyond traditional clinical settings, but its effect on health equity depends on program design. Equity should be treated as a core design principle. Future research should evaluate differential reach, engagement, effectiveness, and sustainability across populations and identify payment models that support equitable implementation at scale. Barriers to equitable RPM implementation occur at patient, clinician, health system, and policy levels. Key challenges include limited access to technology, language barriers, out-of-pocket costs, inadequate cuff sizing, unmet social needs, clinician workload, referral bias, infrastructure limitations, reimbursement variability, and the digital divide. Emerging evidence suggests that equity-focused strategies can improve reach and engagement, including provision of cellular-enabled devices, reduced patient costs, culturally and linguistically tailored support, team-based care, registry-based outreach, and routine monitoring of enrollment and outcomes across demographic groups. High-resource, low-resource, and hybrid RPM models each offer distinct advantages and tradeoffs in balancing scalability, sustainability, and equity.

articles.title: Novel Imaging Techniques Prior to Surgical Management of Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of novel imaging modalities in working up invasive bladder cancer prior to surgical management and their potential role in guiding treatment decisions.

RECENT FINDINGS: Multiple new imaging modalities, including VI-RADS and Biparametric MRI have been developed to better guide management of invasive bladder cancer. There lacks a comprehensive review of these modalities and their diagnostic performance. We performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through 2025. Studies reporting sensitivity and specificity of novel imaging for muscle invasion detection or nodal staging were included. Quality assessment used the QUADAS 2 tool. Thirty three studies encompassing 4,689 patients were included. Twenty three studies evaluated the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System for muscle invasion detection, achieving median sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 82% at a threshold of three or greater and 84% and 92%, respectively, at four or greater. Nine studies assessed positron emission tomography for nodal staging, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrating superior sensitivity (23 to 81%) compared to conventional computed tomography (13 to 47%). Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers showed the highest sensitivity (82 to 100%) with specificity of 82 to 90%. One radiomics study achieved 73% sensitivity and 84% specificity for lymph node detection. Novel imaging modalities demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for bladder cancer staging. The Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System provides reliable muscle invasion assessment with threshold dependent performance. Positron emission tomography with fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers substantially improves nodal staging over conventional computed tomography. Integration of these modalities may optimize patient management, including use or omission of neoadjuvant therapy and consideration for organ sparing approaches. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.

articles.title: When to Start Oral Anticoagulant Therapy Post-Stroke: From Common to Rare Conundrums.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes recent evidence on when to start oral anticoagulant therapy following stroke, including both common and rare clinical conundrums.

RECENT FINDINGS: While previous recommendations based on Diener's rule suggested waiting up to 12 days based on stroke severity and neuroradiological findings, newer data support earlier initiation or resumption of anticoagulation, particularly for mild and moderate ischemic strokes, generally within 4 days. In patients with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation resumption involves weighing thromboembolic risk against recurrent hemorrhage risk, requiring individualized decisions regarding whether and when anticoagulation should be resumed. Clinical recommendations for post-stroke anticoagulation emphasize early, individualized initiation of direct oral anticoagulants for mild-to-moderate ischemic strokes based on neuroimaging. After intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation is generally restarted within 4 to 8 weeks for atrial fibrillation, with earlier resumption potentially warranted in selected high-thromboembolic-risk patients, particularly those with mechanical heart valves.

articles.title: Nut Consumption, Kidney Function, Chronic Kidney Disease and Mortality: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This systematic review evaluates the association between nut consumption and kidney health outcomes, including kidney function markers and chronic kidney disease (CKD) incidence, prevalence, and mortality. Given the nutritional benefits of nuts and the growing burden of CKD, we aimed to assess whether nut consumption is associated with kidney-related outcomes and to assess the strength and consistency of the available evidence.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent observational studies and cohort analyses provide emerging but heterogeneous evidence on the relationship between nut intake and kidney outcomes. Higher nut consumption and substitution of red and processed meat with nuts are associated with lower CKD risk or prevalence in some populations. However, findings for specific kidney function markers, such as estimated glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria, remain inconsistent across studies. Nuts have also been evaluated within plant-based dietary indices and through biomarker-based approaches, yielding complementary but non-uniform results. Evidence in individuals with established CKD or high-risk populations is limited. Overall, variability in exposure definitions, outcome measures, and study populations contributes to uncertainty in the strength and consistency of associations. Current evidence suggests that nut consumption, particularly when nuts replace red and processed meat, may be associated with favorable kidney-related outcomes in some populations. However, the evidence is predominantly observational and does not establish causality or an optimal level of nut consumption for kidney health. The heterogeneity in study design and outcome assessment further constrains definitive conclusions. Future research should prioritize well-designed prospective studies and randomized controlled trials to establish causality, clarify dose-response relationships, and determine the role of nuts in CKD-specific dietary recommendations for its prevention and management.

articles.title: A case of lysozyme-induced nephropathy with improved renal function following treatment for chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.
articles.abstract: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) is a myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by persistent peripheral blood monocytosis. Although renal involvement can occur in patients with CMML, it may be overlooked. In addition, renal impairment is not included among the current criteria for initiating treatment for CMML.We report the case of a 75-year-old man with lysozyme-induced nephropathy that was initially considered to be diabetic nephropathy. He had a 20-year history of diabetes mellitus and presented to our hospital with weight loss and progressive anemia. After further evaluation, he was diagnosed with CMML. However, CMML-directed therapy was not initiated because he did not meet the treatment criteria, and he was managed with supportive care. At that time, renal dysfunction was already present, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] of 36.6 mL/min/1.73 m2, but it was attributed to diabetic nephropathy. Renal function subsequently deteriorated, and non-albumin-dominant proteinuria was observed. Kidney biopsy revealed lysozyme-induced nephropathy. Disease-directed therapy for CMML was initiated with the aim of preserving renal function. Treatment of the underlying disease resulted in improvement in renal function (eGFR 10.2 to 17.8 mL/min/1.73 m2), thereby avoiding dialysis despite advanced kidney failure. This case highlights the importance of considering lysozyme-induced nephropathy in the differential diagnosis when renal dysfunction occurs in patients with myeloid neoplasms accompanied by monocytosis. Furthermore, renal involvement in CMML may represent a clinically significant organ manifestation that can justify CMML-directed therapy, even when conventional hematological indications for treatment are not met.

articles.title: Determining the minimal important difference of EQ-5D-5 L utility values in CIDP patients using data from a large clinical trial.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by limb weakness and sensory disturbances. This study aimed to estimate the minimal important difference (MID) of EQ-5D-5 L utility values in CIDP patients.

METHODS: ADHERE, the largest CIDP trial to date, demonstrated the efficacy of efgartigimod. In Stage A (open-label; n = 322), patients received efgartigimod for up to 12 weeks or until evidence of clinical improvement (ECI). Patients with ECI entered Stage B, receiving efgartigimod (n = 111) or placebo (n = 110) for up to 48 weeks. An open-label extension (OLE) included 229 patients treated for up to 48 weeks. Disability was assessed using the adjusted INCAT (aINCAT) score (0-10). EQ-5D-5 L and aINCAT were recorded at baseline and end of Stage A. Perceived improvement was captured using the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Anchor-based methods were applied to estimate the MID: mean utility change for patients reporting "a little better" on PGIC; mean utility change in patients with a 1-point aINCAT decrease; regression of utility change versus aINCAT change; receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curve. A distribution-based estimate was also derived (0.5x baseline SD).

RESULTS: MID estimates were 0.11 (PGIC), 0.14 (1-point aINCAT decrease), 0.10 (regression), 0.10 (ROC), and 0.14 (distribution-based). In the OLE, 66.5% of patients achieved the MID by week 12 (n = 188).

CONCLUSION: The PGIC-based MID (0.11) aligns with estimates in other conditions and supports interpretation of utility changes in future evaluations. Most patients in the OLE achieved this threshold, indicating sustained quality-of-life improvement with efgartigimod.

articles.title: Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization Identifies Therapeutic Targets for Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke carries substantial residual risk despite acute revascularization and secondary prevention, and small-vessel disease (SVD) lacks specific preventive therapy. Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) identifies circulating proteins whose lifelong modulation alters stroke risk.

METHODS: We screened 589 conditionally independent cis-pQTLs from the INTERVAL study against four GIGASTROKE outcomes: any ischemic stroke (AIS), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), cardioembolic stroke (CES), and SVD. Wald ratio estimates were corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) within each outcome, with a pooled cross-outcome correction as a sensitivity analysis. FDR-significant associations underwent colocalization (approximate Bayes factor; H4 > 0.80), replication in the independent deCODE pQTL cohort, cell-type expression validation in a human brain vascular single-nucleus atlas (65,479 nuclei), and phenome-wide safety screening.

RESULTS: Ten protein-outcome associations reached FDR < 0.05; nine replicated in deCODE and eight colocalized at H4 > 0.80, with two further pairs (ABO-LAA, cyclin H-CES) in the suggestive range (H4 0.70-0.80). For SVD, higher SPATA20 raised risk (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.24-1.73, p = 5.3 × 10⁻⁶), and higher KDELC2 lowered risk (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.91, p = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴). A protective cyclin H signal for CES passed outcome-wise FDR (q = 0.046) but not the pooled correction (q = 0.059) and is reported as preliminary. ABO, MMP-12, and SWAP70 confirmed earlier reports; SCARA5 failed colocalization and replication and was excluded. Colocalization confirmed the lead liabilities for MMP-12 (atopic dermatitis, two cohorts) and SWAP70 (rheumatoid arthritis) as on-target effects; two further liability associations (allergic asthma, ER-negative breast cancer) did not meet the colocalization threshold and remain hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSIONS: Proteome-wide MR prioritizes two SVD-associated proteins: SPATA20 (risk-raising; now independently confirmed across screens) and KDELC2 (protective; newly reported). Both require replication on orthogonal proteomic platforms and functional validation before therapeutic development.

articles.title: Patients with MASH experience worse health-related quality of life: a multinational real-world study using LiverMultiScan.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), is increasing globally. Assessment of health-related quality of life (HRQoL), alongside non-invasive tests (NITs), may support identification of patients requiring closer clinical management. This multinational real-world randomised controlled trial evaluated associations between HRQoL (using the EQ-5D) and multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) markers of liver disease.

METHODS: RADIcAL-1 included 802 patients (453 male) with suspected MASLD/MASH from Germany, Netherlands, Portugal and UK. Participants completed the EQ-5D-5 L at baseline, 2, 6 and 12-months. EQ-VAS was derived to assess overall health. Between-group comparisons (imaging vs. standard-of-care) were assessed using t-tests, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, obesity, diabetes and hyperlipidaemia. MASH was defined as corrected T1 (cT1) ≥800ms and liver fat as proton density fat fraction (PDFF) ≥ 10%. High-risk MASH was cT1 ≥ 875ms.

RESULTS: Within the imaging arm, patients with MASH reported lower HRQoL across all EQ-5D dimensions and EQ-VAS compared with MASLD. Baseline utilities ranged from 0.81 (Coimbra) to 0.90 (Ulm) and this range decreased at month 12 from 0.82 (Coimbra and UK) to 0.90 (Ulm). These findings remained after adjustment for comorbidities. Patients with high-risk MASH reported up to 12% more complaints in all EQ-5D dimensions compared to all others. Increasing cT1 was associated with 29% higher odds of reporting anxiety/depression. An 80ms increase in cT1 was associated with 0.023-point decrease in EQ-5D utility (p = 0.039). Due to COVID-19, 12-month response rates varied across sites (22-81%).

CONCLUSION: mpMRI-defined MASH is associated with worse HRQoL independent of key metabolic comorbidities. These findings support the use of imaging biomarkers for disease stratification and for identifying patients with greater clinical burden, with potential implications for management and monitoring strategies.

articles.title: Social Participation in Community Dwelling Minority Stroke Survivors: Decolonizing Research.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Minority stroke survivors experience difficulties in access to rehabilitation due to a combination of systemic factors; lack of understanding of their cultural beliefs by health professionals; their colonial thinking and experiences; and they are underrepresented in social participation research. To address the disparity, this paper discusses how research on social participation of community dwelling minority stroke survivors could embrace decolonization.

RECENT FINDINGS: Decolonization of research in social participation can be achieved when minority stroke survivors are engaged in genuine trust and co-production of knowledge with social science researchers. Improvements in uptake and continuation of social participation are sustained when such reciprocal relationships take place. There is a need for cultural competence and humility amongst healthcare professionals working in stroke rehabilitation with minority stroke survivors.

articles.title: Female-specific reliance on endothelial FoxO1 governs vascular resilience and metabolic adaptation to obesity.
articles.abstract: Sex differences in adipose tissue vascular remodeling critically influence susceptibility to obesity-associated metabolic disease, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we identify Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1) as a sex-dependent regulator of endothelial function, with female endothelial cells (EC) expressing higher levels of FoxO1 and depending on it to maintain vascular remodeling and metabolic homeostasis. Accordingly, FoxO1 loss in females disrupted angiogenesis, and promoted adipocyte hypertrophy, weight gain and glucose dysregulation, whereas opposite effects have been reported in males. This phenotype was associated with a shift in the endothelial transcriptome toward a male-like state, consistent with loss of female protection against diet-induced metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, FoxO1 inhibition exerted time-dependent effects, with short-term suppression promoting proliferation and sustained inhibition reducing proliferation and inducing metabolic dysfunction. Although also observed in males, these effects were more pronounced in female EC, which also selectively exhibited mitochondrial dysfunction, increased oxidative stress and DNA damage accumulation, culminating in a senescence-like arrest. Antioxidant treatment partially rescued this phenotype, implicating oxidative stress as a driver of female-specific vulnerability. These findings reveal a sex-dependent divergence in FoxO1 function and identify endothelial FoxO1 as a determinant of opposing vascular and metabolic responses to obesogenic stress.

articles.title: Familiar name, unfamiliar reality: a case study of heat illness knowledge gaps among Japanese junior high and high school students.
articles.abstract: Early recognition of exertional heat illness (EHI) is critical for preventing severe outcomes. However, the relationship between perceived knowledge and actual understanding remains unclear. This study investigated the recognition and correct matching of EHI and its symptoms among Japanese junior high and high school students. A paper-based, self-administered questionnaire was distributed under conditions of anonymity and voluntary participation. The questionnaire included recognition of the term "EHI" and its condition types and severity classifications (mild, moderate, and severe). EHI knowledge was evaluated by asking students to select all symptoms corresponding to each EHI condition and severity classification from a predefined list, based on previous guidelines. Valid responses were obtained from 533 junior high and 646 high school students. Almost all students recognised the term "EHI," with most reporting school health education as the primary source of learning. However, correct matching of EHI types with their associated symptoms was low (junior high school/high school): 1.9/3.1% for heat syncope, 22.1/26.9% for exercise-associated muscle cramps, 4.1/7.9% for exertional heat exhaustion, and 0.4/0.5% for exertional heat stroke. These results indicate that, although recognition of EHI terminology was nearly universal, correct matching of symptoms was extremely low. These findings reveal a substantial gap between perceived knowledge and actual understanding of EHI. This discrepancy may lead to delayed recognition and inappropriate responses in real-world situations, potentially increasing the risk of adverse outcomes during heat exposure. Addressing this gap may be important for improving safety and public health preparedness in school-based settings.

articles.title: Clinical and radiographic success of bioflex versus stainless steel crowns using the hall technique in primary molars: a 12-month randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The present study evaluated and compared the clinical and radiographic success of BioFlex crowns (BFCs) versus stainless-steel crowns (SSCs) using Hall Technique (HT) in primary molars.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-arm randomized controlled trial included 74 healthy children aged 4-6 years with ICDAS 3-5 carious mandibular second primary molars. Each child contributed one tooth and was randomly assigned (1:1) to receive BFCs or SSCs using the HT. Baseline examination, radiographs, plaque, and gingival indices were recorded. Crowns were cemented with resin-modified glass ionomer. Primary outcomes were clinical and radiographic success; secondary outcomes included plaque and gingival indices, child and parental satisfaction. Evaluations were performed up to 12 months.

RESULTS: At 12 months, no statistically significant difference in success rates was detected between the groups (BFCs 91.9% vs. SSCs 94.6%; RR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.86-1.10). SSCs had a higher gingival index at 1 week (MD = - 0.32, 95% CI: -0.56--0.08). BFCs showed higher plaque at 6 months (MD = 0.30) and 12 months (MD = 0.41). Child satisfaction favored BFCs (MD = - 0.67), with greater parental satisfaction for color (MD = 1.73) and overall satisfaction (MD = 0.41).

CONCLUSIONS: BFCs are an esthetic alternative to SSCs when used with the HT. They showed no significant differences in short-term clinical success but higher child and parental satisfaction. However, perforation risk and greater plaque accumulation indicate the need for careful case selection and longer-term evaluation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered in the clinicaltrials.gov registry (# NCT06847646).

articles.title: Locus coeruleus abnormalities on neuromelanin-sensitive MRI in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging (NM-MRI) enables in vivo assessment of locus coeruleus (LC) integrity, but findings in Parkinson's disease (PD) vary across cohorts and methods. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus from inception to 5 September 2026 and pooled independent PD-healthy control (HC) comparisons using random-effects models. Sixty-five reports were included, of which 17 contributed to at least one main pooled outcome. The primary LC-signal analysis included 14 independent cohorts (1,078 participants with PD and 543 HCs) and showed lower LC signal in PD (Hedges' g = - 0.95, 95% confidence interval (CI) - 1.32 to - 0.57; P = 0.00011). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 88.4%), and the 95% prediction interval crossed zero (- 2.28 to 0.38). The LC-volume analysis included five independent cohorts (215 participants with PD and 134 HCs) and likewise showed lower values in PD (g = - 0.87, 95% CI - 1.13 to - 0.62; P = 0.00071; I2 = 0%). The negative mean LC-signal effect was preserved across sensitivity analyses, but every specification-level prediction interval crossed zero. Of the 65 reports, 64 yielded 243 secondary-outcome records, of which 102 contained directly usable quantitative information; however, no additional outcome cluster simultaneously met the criteria for construct compatibility, cohort independence and numerical poolability. LC NM-MRI shows group-level differences in PD, but LC-signal differences vary across settings. These comparisons do not establish individual diagnostic accuracy. Clinical translation will require harmonized acquisition, analysis and reporting, together with independent, multicentre and longitudinal validation. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261498031).

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Argatroban as an Adjunct to Antiplatelet Therapy in Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a life-threatening condition. Argatroban can limit thrombus progression and improve AIS's functional outcomes. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of argatroban in combination with antiplatelet therapy compared to control.

METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched. Primary outcomes were Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2 and composite hemorrhage; secondary outcomes included mRS (0-1), early neurological deterioration (END), change in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, mortality, intracranial and organ hemorrhage. A random-effects model was used, with risk ratios (RRs) reported for binary outcomes, while mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes at 95% confidence intervals (CI) and a p-value of 0.05.

RESULTS: 17 studies were included with a total of 51,703 and 18,759 patients in the argatroban and control group, respectively. The primary outcomes, mRS (0-2), and composite hemorrhage showed no significant difference between argatroban and control (RR: 1.03, CI: 0.97-1.10, p = 0.26 and RR: 1.10, CI: 0.98-1.23, p = 0.11, respectively). However, argatroban significantly reduced END (RR: 0.48, CI: 0.30-0.75, p < 0.05) and favored mRS (0-1) with RR:1.22 (CI: 1.01-1.48, p = 0.03). The change in NIHSS score and incidence of mortality, stroke recurrence, intracranial and organ hemorrhage was comparable between the two groups. Subgroup analyses by antiplatelet drug in the intervention and comparison groups confirmed that argatroban showed the most pronounced results when combined with DAPT. While the overall pooled analysis did not demonstrate increased hemorrhagic risk, subgroup analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials revealed a significant increase in composite and intracranial hemorrhage with argatroban. GRADE assessment of RCT-derived evidence indicated very low to high certainty across all outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Argatroban as an adjunct to antiplatelet therapy did not significantly improve overall functional outcome (mRS 0-2) or reduce composite hemorrhage compared with antiplatelet therapy alone. However it appears safe and may reduce END significantly.

articles.title: Clinical safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fospropofol disodium for sedation: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fospropofol disodium (fospropofol) is a water-soluble prodrug of propofol with a distinct pharmacological and tolerability profile. However, evidence regarding the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fospropofol across broader sedation contexts and different comparators remains insufficiently synthesized. This systematic review summarized current research findings on fospropofol to clarify its clinical role and guide future research.

METHODS: This systematic review was registered prior to initiation (PROSPERO CRD42023477740). Comprehensive searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via Ovid, Embase via Ovid, ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 26 August 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating fospropofol for sedation and reporting extractable efficacy or safety outcomes were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated according to the GRADE approach. Meta-analysis was performed for clinically comparable evidence groups, with other findings synthesized according to SWiM principles.

RESULTS: This systematic review included 10 original studies, comprising six procedural-sedation trials and four trials for ICU sedation. Quantitative synthesis was conducted for two comparable evidence groups, whereas the remaining outcomes were synthesized narratively. In three endoscopic procedural-sedation trials, fospropofol 6.5 mg/kg achieved a higher sedation success than 2 mg/kg (RR 3.27, 95% CI 2.62-4.08). In mechanically ventilated ICU patients, hypotension risk did not clearly differ between fospropofol and propofol (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.67-1.28). Procedural studies showed a dose-dependent pattern in sedation efficacy, whereas ICU studies generally reported comparable target-sedation attainment between fospropofol and comparator sedatives. Paresthesia/pruritus was commonly reported, while rates of cardiorespiratory adverse events varied across settings and doses and showed no consistent comparative advantage for fospropofol. Evidence for injection pain and satisfaction was limited. Certainty of evidence ranged from high to very low, mainly because of risk of bias and imprecision.

CONCLUSIONS: Fospropofol can provide effective sedation across procedural and ICU settings, but its efficacy and safety profiles vary according to dose, comparator, and clinical setting. Higher doses may improve procedural-sedation efficacy but may also increase adverse effects in some settings. Current evidence does not establish a consistent cardiorespiratory safety advantage for fospropofol over other sedatives, and further adequately powered randomized trials are needed to clarify its comparative safety and optimal clinical role.

articles.title: Spiradenocarcinoma in Brooke-Spiegler syndrome: radiology-pathology correlation of synchronous benign and malignant dermal adnexal tumors.
articles.abstract: Spiradenocarcinoma is a rare dermal adnexal malignancy often arising from a pre-existing benign spiradenoma and may occur sporadically or in the setting of the autosomal dominant genodermatosis Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome (BSS). Imaging descriptions of spiradenoma and spiradenocarcinoma are scant, with no literature to date describing comparative imaging features of benign and malignant tumors to the best of our knowledge. We report a case of a 64-year-old patient with a rapidly enlarging right frontal scalp mass and a relatively indolent left parietal scalp mass in addition to innumerable small head and neck nodules. MRI for preoperative planning demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement and markedly reduced diffusion in both lesions, while 18F-FDG PET-CT showed marked FDG avidity (SUVmax = 16.3) in the frontal mass but mild uptake in the parietal mass (SUVmax = 2.1). Histopathology confirmed the frontal mass to be a low-grade spiradenocarcinoma and the left parietal lesion a benign spiradenoma. Genetic testing confirmed BSS. This case illustrates the clinical-radiologic-pathologic correlation of spiradenocarcinoma in the context of BSS, a rare clinical and radiologic mimic of NF1, and highlights that rapid growth and FDG avidity may help the reporting radiologist to differentiate spiradenocarcinoma from spiradenoma in patients with BSS.

articles.title: DELPHI expert consensus-derived factors influencing the early use of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies in treatment-naïve patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To gather expert consensus regarding initiation of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies (HET) amongst treatment-naïve relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients in France.

METHODS: The study leveraged the Delphi method to gauge consensus amongst an expert panel of 31 neurologists. Eight clinical cases with demographic, clinical and imaging characteristics were presented, prompting the experts to respond if they would recommend monoclonal HET. Additionally, potentially influential parameters were changed one at a time to assess whether the experts would recommend monoclonal HET. After a first round, an e-workshop was conducted to discuss non-consensual statements, which were re-submitted for rating (Round 2). Characteristics influencing monoclonal HET initiation were evaluated.

RESULTS: 31/31 experts responded to both rounds. Consensus for or against monoclonal HET was reached for 89/108 (82.4%) statements. Factors that systematically led to monoclonal HET initiation were high brain lesion load (>20 lesions), ≥2 spinal cord lesions, ≥3 gadolinium-enhancing lesions and ≥3 infratentorial lesions. A single spinal cord lesion, in combination with other factors (which, in isolation, often but not always led to monoclonal HET), systematically led to monoclonal HET recommendation.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that the panel of French neurologists favoured monoclonal HET initiation amongst treatment-naïve RRMS patients with high radiological disease activity, whereas clinical characteristics played a complementary role.

articles.title: Fireplace-related injuries in children with special emphasis on neurotrauma: a retrospective study from a paediatric tertiary care centre in the UK.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Paediatric fireplace-associated trauma is an infrequent but potentially life-threatening accident. Though, fireplace is a part of most households in regions with long winters, fireplace-associated trauma is not studied extensively. This study examines the demography and clinical characteristics of children sustaining fireplace injuries, with special attention to neurosurgical injuries.

METHODS: This is a single-centre retrospective observational study carried out at a tertiary care paediatric centre, encompassing all paediatric admissions with fireplace-related accidents between January 2020 and December 2025. Patient demographics, mechanism, type and severity of injury, treatment modality, complications, hospital stay and outcome were systematically recorded and descriptively analysed.

RESULTS: Two hundred four paediatric patients were admitted with head injury during the study period, 15 (7.4%) of whom were following fireplace accidents. Boys comprised the majority (66.7%) of the cohort, with a mean age of 3 years. Structural collapse of the fireplace onto the child was the predominant mechanism (73%). Multisystem involvement was documented in 10 (66.7%) patients, with cranial injury being predominant (47%). Three patients sustained severe head injury. Surgical management was required in 10 patients, requiring a total of 21 surgeries. The median hospital stay was 2 days with mean intensive care unit (ICU) occupancy of 2.8 days. There were 2 mortalities (13.3%) with 2 patients (13.3%) requiring prolonged rehabilitation.

CONCLUSION: Although fireplace injuries constitute a small proportion of paediatric trauma admissions, they cause considerable morbidity and mortality due to multisystem involvement. Mandatory anchorage of freestanding fireplace structures and investment in caregiver-targeted safety education can reduce the incidence of these preventable accidents.
