articles.title: TSPO-PET binding in vivo reflects increased phagocytic microglia at post mortem in people with frontotemporal dementia.
articles.abstract: Brain inflammation is a key feature of frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Positron emission tomography (PET) of the 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) is widely used as an in vivo proxy for neuroinflammation, but whether the elevated signal reflects microglial, astrocytic or vascular pathology remains controversial, and this has not previously been resolved in FTD using matched ante mortem imaging and post-mortem tissue. We paired ante mortem [11C]PK11195 TSPO-PET with quantitative post-mortem neuropathology in 10 individuals with FTD (5 FTLD-tau, 5 FTLD-TDP) and 5 age- and sex-matched controls, combining CD68 immunohistochemistry across 17 brain regions, multiplex immunofluorescence pairing TSPO with microglial/macrophagic (IBA1, CD68), astrocytic (GFAP) and endothelial (CD31) markers in three frontotemporal cortical regions, and three-dimensional single-cell reconstruction of individual microglia. CD68 area fraction was elevated in FTD relative to controls, predominantly in white matter, and was positively associated with regional TSPO-PET-binding potential across the cohort (β = 8.66, P < 0.001), with comparable slopes in FTLD-tau and FTLD-TDP. Total tissue TSPO-area fraction was likewise increased in FTD and tracked regional PET binding in two independently processed slide sets. Of the four cell-type markers, only the CD68-TSPO co-localised fraction was positively associated with the PET signal (β = +0.0041, P = 0.015, PFDR = 0.062), with null or negative associations for IBA1, GFAP and CD31. At single-cell resolution, IBA1+ microglia that were also CD68+ carried more absolute TSPO and were larger than CD68- microglia, without an increase in the TSPO fraction of cell volume. The elevated TSPO-PET signal in FTD, therefore, likely reflects an increased burden of CD68+ phagocytic microglia rather than TSPO expression in other cell types, supporting TSPO-PET as a microglial-burden biomarker across both FTLD-tau and FTLD-TDP.

articles.title: Transfer timing is not independently associated with ECMO utilization in outborn congenital diaphragmatic hernia: a severity-adjusted analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether time from birth to arrival at a tertiary extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)-capable center is independently associated with ECMO utilization among outborn neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We hypothesized that longer transfer intervals would be associated with greater ECMO utilization after adjustment for disease severity and anatomic characteristics.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of outborn neonates with CDH transferred to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit with ECMO capability. Transfer interval was analyzed using multivariable logistic regression adjusting for CDHSG postnatal score and anatomic characteristics.

RESULTS: Among 46 neonates, 21 (45.7%) required ECMO and 25 (54.3%) did not. Infants requiring ECMO had greater CDHSG postnatal scores and more frequent intrathoracic liver herniation. After adjustment, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization (aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.50-1.23). Intrathoracic liver herniation remained independently associated (aOR 8.65, 95% CI 1.52-49.38), whereas CDHSG score did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSION: Within the transfer intervals observed, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization. These findings suggest that transport duration alone may be less informative than underlying disease characteristics in this cohort.

articles.title: Nano-Emulsification and Soft Gel Encapsulation to Improve the Delivery of Anti-Diabetic Drug Ertugliflozin-L-Pyroglutamic Acid via SNEDDS: An In Vitro Assessment using RP-HPLC.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aim to develop and evaluate a novel soft gelatin capsule formulation of Ertugliflozin-L-Pyroglutamic Acid (ERT) using a self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (SNEDDS) to enhance its solubility, physicochemical stability, and in vitro drug dissolution relative to the commercial Steglatro® tablets.

SIGNIFICANCE: Poor aqueous solubility and limited dissolution behavior are two major challenges that hinder the therapeutic performance of many antidiabetic drugs. Herein, for the first time we formulated ERT as a SNEDDS-based soft gelatin capsule, providing a promising strategy for enhancing oral drug delivery system that manages Type 2 diabetes more efficiently.

METHODS: ERT was encapsulated in a SNEDDS formulation matrix of Labrasol® (surfactant), PEG-200 (co-surfactant) and cardamom oil in an optimized ratio. Stability studies were conducted across varied pH ranges, mimicking the gastrointestinal tract environment. Advanced characterization techniques, including AFM, DLS, Zetasizer and FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed consistent particle size and desirable morphological attributes. RP-HPLC as per ICH guidelines evaluated dissolution profile and assay recovery against the commercial Steglatro® tablets.

RESULTS: The optimized ERT-SNEDDS soft gel formulation demonstrated high stability across various pH conditions, with an assay recovery of 98.78 ± 0.04%. The complete dissolution profile (CDP) at three different pH values (0.1 N HCl, pH 4.5 and pH 6.8 buffers) showed significantly superior in vitro drug release compared to established Steglatro® tablet.

CONCLUSION: The developed SNEDDS based soft gelatin capsule demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics and rapid in vitro dissolution of ERT, supporting its potential as an alternative lipid-based oral dosage form to the marketed tablet.

articles.title: Effect heterogeneity of loneliness and social support on incident hypertension in older, normotensive populations.
articles.abstract: Although social isolation is known to impact those with cardiovascular disease, its relationship with incident hypertension is unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, we used data from the All of Us research program. Participants were enrolled between May 2017-April 2023, aged 50+ years, and had at least 60-days of EHR data pre-index date. We identified incident hypertension during follow-up. Those classified as hypertensive at or prior to the index date were excluded. We defined low social support and loneliness as binary variables. Using causal forests, we estimated treatment effects as unweighted and overlap-weighted risk differences (RD). A total of 24,720 participants with a median follow-up of 2.6 years were included. While loneliness and social support were not significantly associated with incident hypertension in the overall population, causal forests revealed meaningful effect heterogeneity, with socially isolated male (RD: 0.038, 95% CI 0.002 to 0.075; overlap-weighted RD: 0.027, 95% CI -0.005 to 0.059) and Gay or Lesbian participants (RD: 0.108, 95% CI 0.011 to 0.205; overlap-weighted RD: 0.11, 95% CI 0.008 to 0.211) experiencing a significantly elevated risk. This illustrates how machine learning, when embedded within epidemiologic frameworks, can detect subgroup vulnerability that other approaches may obscure, enabling targeting of limited resources.

articles.title: Clinical impact of a rapid urine diagnostic algorithm combined with antimicrobial stewardship in patients with suspected urinary sepsis.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early appropriate antimicrobial therapy is a key determinant of outcome in sepsis, yet conventional urine culture takes 24-48 hours. We evaluated the clinical impact of a rapid microbiological algorithm applied directly to urine, combined with antimicrobial stewardship, in patients with suspected urinary sepsis.

METHODS: Prospective quasi-experimental two-phase cohort study at a tertiary hospital. In adults with simultaneous urine and blood cultures, an initial observational phase formed the comparison cohort (conventional culture), and a second phase the intervention cohort, in which urine underwent Gram stain, laser-nephelometry growth detection (Alfred 60/AST), MALDI-TOF-MS identification, rapid susceptibility testing, and immunochromatographic ESBL and carbapenemase detection, with immediate reporting and recommendations by an infectious diseases specialist. Multivariable models (logistic and negative binomial) were adjusted for age, sex, Charlson index, department and qSOFA.

RESULTS: We included 594 patients (297 per cohort). The algorithm achieved organism identification in 92.6% of cases, with a median turnaround time of 7.25 versus 75.0 hours (p<0.001), and 98.6% agreement with culture. Overall mortality was 6.1% versus 11.1% (p=0.039). After adjustment, the intervention was associated with significant reductions in hospital stay (IRR 0.82; p=0.012), days of therapy (IRR 0.79; p<0.001), intravenous antibiotics (IRR 0.83; p=0.001), need for ICU admission (OR 0.42; p=0.003) and overall mortality (OR 0.44; p=0.011).

CONCLUSIONS: A rapid urine diagnostic algorithm, integrated with an expert stewardship intervention, was associated with lower antibiotic consumption and improved outcomes in suspected urinary sepsis. Combining rapid diagnostics with expert advice appears key to translating microbiological information into effective therapeutic decisions.

articles.title: [Integration of beta-lactam therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) into routine clinical practice within an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP)].
articles.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCCIÓN: La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de antibióticos beta-lactámicos para el ajuste de dosis y la consecución de objetivos farmacocinéticos/farmacodinámicos es una estrategia destinada a optimizar la dosificación en pacientes críticos y en pacientes con características especiales. El objetivo de este estudio es describir la actividad llevada a cabo durante el año 2023 en nuestro hospital, en colaboración con todos los departamentos clínicos implicados: el Servicio de Análisis Clínicos (Farmacocinética y Microbiología), el Servicio de Farmacia y la Unidad Territorial de Infección Nosocomial, en el marco de un Programa de Optimización de Antimicrobianos.

MÉTODOS: Estudio retrospectivo observacional descriptivo sobre la aplicación de la monitorización terapéutica de betalactámicos. Los clínicos solicitan una interconsulta al Servicio de Farmacia para iniciar la monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos. Una vez que el paciente alcanza el estado estacionario, se obtiene una muestra de sangre. Si se realizan ajustes de dosis, se vuelve a medir el nivel plasmático tras 24-48 horas. Todas las determinaciones de niveles plasmáticos realizadas durante 2023 se registraron en una hoja de cálculo Excel, junto con las modificaciones del tratamiento derivadas de los niveles plasmáticos medidos. Se definió un nivel óptimo como una concentración cuatro veces superior a la concentración mínima inhibitoria (CMI) del microorganismo causante sin alcanzar niveles tóxicos.

RESULTADOS: Se realizaron un total de 717 determinaciones en 487 pacientes; el 43,3% ingresaron en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos, mientras que el resto estaban hospitalizados en otros servicios. Se realizaron ajustes de dosis en el 34,6% de los pacientes críticos, en comparación con el 32,6% en los pacientes no críticos. En el 79.3% de los pacientes con aislamientos microbiológicos, se alcanzó el objetivo terapéutico de mantener concentraciones libres del fármaco por encima de la CMI del patógeno.

CONCLUSIÓN: La monitorización terapéutica de los niveles plasmáticos de betalactámicos podría ser una herramienta útil para la optimización de la dosis y la consecución de los niveles plasmáticos óptimos.

INTRODUCTION: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of plasma levels of beta-lactam antibiotics for dose adjustment and achievement of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic targets is a strategy aimed at optimizing dosing in critically ill patients and in patients with special characteristics. The aim of this study is to describe the activity carried out during the year 2023 at our hospital, in collaboration with all the clinical departments involved: the Clinical Analysis Department (Pharmacokinetics and Microbiology), the Pharmacy Department, and the Territorial Nosocomial Infection Unit, within the framework of an Antimicrobial Stewardship Program.

METHODS: This is a retrospective observational descriptive study about the TDM of beta-lactam antibiotics. Clinicians request a consultation with the Pharmacy Department to initiate therapeutic drug monitoring of beta-lactam plasma levels. Once the patient reaches steady-state conditions, a blood sample is collected. If dose adjustments are made, a new plasma level is measured after 24-48 hours. All plasma level determinations performed during 2023 were recorded in an Excel spreadsheet, along with treatment modifications derived from the measured plasma levels. An optimal level was defined as a concentration four times higher than the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the causative microorganism without reaching toxic levels.

RESULTS: A total of 717 determinations were performed in 487 patients; 43.3% were admitted to the Intensive Care Unit, while the remainder were hospitalized in other departments. Dose adjustments were made in 34.6% of critically ill patients, compared to 32.6% among non-critical patients. In 79.3% of patients with microbiological isolates, the therapeutic target of maintaining free drug concentrations above the MIC of the pathogen was achieved.

CONCLUSION: TDM of beta-lactam plasma levels is a useful tool for dose optimization and achievement of therapeutic target.

articles.title: Genetic Pulmonary Hypertension Combined With Biventricular Heart Failure: Role of AQP1 Gene Mutation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aquaporin-1 (AQP1) mutations are a rare cause of heritable pulmonary artery hypertension. The clinical manifestation remains poorly defined, and coexisting left ventricular dysfunction has not been reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 34-year-old man presented with severe pulmonary arterial hypertension and biventricular dysfunction. Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous AQP1 mutation, c.551T >C (p.Ile184Thr), not previously reported; family screening confirmed the same variant in his mother and daughter. After 6 months of guideline-directed medical therapy and endothelin receptor antagonist therapy, pulmonary artery pressure decreased significantly, and functional capacity improved.

DISCUSSION: Biventricular impairment raises 2 hypotheses: septal dyskinesia secondary to right ventricular overload, or myocardial impairment because of altered AQP1 channel function. The favorable response suggests targeted pulmonary vasodilator therapy may benefit in this rare genetic subset.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: AQP1 mutations should be considered in genetic workup of pulmonary arterial hypertension and may coexist with left ventricular dysfunction responsive to endothelin receptor antagonist therapy.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Medical Therapies for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding in Adolescents and Young Adults With Bleeding Disorders.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) females with bleeding disorders (BDs) frequently experience heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB), posing substantial clinical challenges. Data comparing the efficacy of specific hormonal treatment options in this population remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of AYA females (≤21 years) with BD and HMB referred to a multidisciplinary Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology-Pediatric Hematology joint clinic between November 2016 and December 2023. Treatment efficacy was defined as achieving a patient-reported significant reduction in or cessation of menstrual bleeding. The primary objective was to compare the efficacy of different hormonal and hemostatic therapies.

RESULTS: Among 121 AYA females with BD, von Willebrand disease was the most common diagnosis (67.0%). HMB developed within 1 year of menarche in 79.3% of cases, and 73.6% received their BD diagnosis only after HMB onset. Combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) were the most common initial therapy (62.8%), yet 58.7% required switching to alternative regimens. Oral progestins demonstrated the highest efficacy (89.8%), followed by levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (81.5%) and OCPs (65.5%). Only 17.4% achieved complete amenorrhea, though most experienced clinically meaningful bleeding reduction. Treatment efficacy differed significantly across modalities (p < .001).

DISCUSSION: Progestin-based therapies, particularly norethindrone and norethindrone acetate, offer superior bleeding control and should be considered first-line treatment in AYA with BD. Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system and OCPs are also effective alternatives. Given the difficulty of achieving complete amenorrhea, clinical goals should prioritize meaningful bleeding reduction that supports quality of life. Early multidisciplinary referral is recommended to optimize individualized care.

articles.title: Baveno VI criteria validation and development of a new non-invasive strategy for varices rule-out in patients with HCC (SAPHE-R: Stiffness, ALBI, Platelets, HEpatocellular carcinoma Rule).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Accuracy of Baveno criteria for avoiding endoscopy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncertain, and systematic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (UGE) may not be necessary. We evaluated Baveno VI criteria performance in this population and developed an alternative non-invasive rule to exclude esophagogastric varices of any grade, rather than high-risk varices (HRV).

METHODS: Patients with BCLC 0-C HCC and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) from Italian Liver Cancer (ITA.LI.CA) database, with available liver stiffness measurement (LSM), UGE, and blood tests within six months of diagnosis, were included. Independent predictors of varices identified by logistic regression were combined through grid-search to derive a rule-out strategy (SAPHE-R), validated by bootstrap-resampling and in an independent cohort (Vienna).

RESULTS: The derivation cohort comprised 598 patients (age, 69 years; male sex, 75.3%; viral etiology, 69.3%; BCLC 0/A, 77.9%; ALBI 1, 54.2%; varices, 33.4%; HRV, 11.2%). Baveno VI criteria missed 8.5% of varices and 6.0% of HRV, sparing 31.1% of UGE. Independent predictors of varices were incorporated into SAPHE-R (LSM≤16 kPa, platelet count ≥160×10⁹/L, ALBI grade 1), which missed 4.0% of varices (HRV 3.0%, spared UGE 17.6%). In the validation cohort (n=149), SAPHE-R missed 4.8% of varices (HRV 3.1%, spared UGE 14.8%). Results remained consistent in sensitivity analyses. In an exploratory analysis, no HVPG-defined CSPH was observed among SAPHE-R rule-out patients (0/22).

CONCLUSIONS: Baveno VI criteria showed suboptimal performance in patients with HCC and cACLD, whereas SAPHE-R provided a reliable non-invasive strategy to rule out varices, facilitating variceal risk assessment in patients with HCC.

articles.title: Extrinsic risk factors for tendinopathy: bridging the basic and clinical research divide.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Tendon injuries frequently affect the Achilles, rotator cuff, and the tendons of the wrist extensors originating at the lateral epicondyle. Until recently, terms for tendon degeneration, disease, and injuries were debated between the basic research and clinical communities, creating barriers to advances in knowledge. Aside from acute traumatic rupture in healthy tendon, in the current 'omic age, most tendon disease, including ruptures in chronic disease, exists along a tendinopathy spectrum. While intrinsic factors such as sex, genetics, and aging are unmodifiable, extrinsic factors impact tendon health, and have been extensively evaluated in both basic and clinical research. However, these fields do not always ask aligned research questions, leading to unanticipated gaps in understanding the impact of extrinsic factors on tendon health. The aim of this study was to provide a detailed and cohesive review of these gaps between current clinical and basic science research.

METHODS: We analyzed extrinsic risk factors for tendinopathy by searching PubMed utilizing search terms related to tendinopathy, various anatomic sites, and various extrinsic risk factors. Reviewed literature was separated into basic science and clinical research. Current knowledge was summarized and gaps identified between fields.

RESULTS: Several extrinsic risk factors are directly connected to the onset of tendinopathy whether through upregulation of systemic inflammatory mediators or direct effects on tendon structure and function.

CONCLUSIONS: There is much work to be done to explain the mechanisms of action highlighted by clinical data, particularly when considering the complexity of disease and associated comorbidity.

articles.title: Non-enzymatic role of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 in regulating adenosine 2A receptor in MAFLD.
articles.abstract: Non-catalytic function of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP4) plays a crucial role in inflammation and immune regulation in the body; however, its significance in metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) remains largely unknown. We sought to examine the effects of Dpp4 disruption on aspects of MAFLD and to elucidate underlying mechanisms. Wild-type (WT), Dpp4-disrupted, and DPP4 inhibitor-treated C57BL/6J male mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 weeks to establish MAFLD. Hepatic steatosis and liver proinflammatory responses were assessed. Furthermore, bone marrow-derived macrophages from different genotypes were co-cultured with mouse hepatocytes to assess their roles in inflammatory and metabolic responses in vitro. Upon HFD feeding, Dpp4-disrupted mice exhibited significantly attenuated hepatic steatosis and inflammation compared to both DPP4 inhibitor-treated and control WT mice. In vitro, Dpp4-deficient macrophages demonstrated a reduced proinflammatory phenotype. Consequently, these macrophages elicited less fat deposition in co-cultured wild-type hepatocytes. Mechanistically, Dpp4 deficiency significantly upregulated the protein abundance of the adenosine 2A receptor (A2AR) while markedly reducing adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels in both liver tissues and bone marrow-derived macrophages. Our results demonstrate that genetic disruption of Dpp4, unlike its pharmacological inhibition, ameliorates MAFLD progression. This protective effect is mediated through a novel non-catalytic mechanism involving the upregulation of A2AR and downregulation of ADA, which collectively inhibit macrophage-driven inflammation.

articles.title: Clusters of modifiable dementia risk factors at mid-life and late-life and their association with incident dementia: A prospective cohort study of 246,968 adults.
articles.abstract: BackgroundModifiable dementia risk factors rarely occur in isolation, yet their co-occurrence and clustering remain poorly characterized, limiting identification of high-risk individuals and development of targeted strategies.ObjectiveTo identify clusters of ten modifiable risk factors in mid-life (45-65 years) and late-life (>65 years), and to examine their association with incident dementia.MethodsData were drawn from the 2012 Dutch Public Health Monitor Survey (mid-life: n = 121,120; late-life: n = 125,848), with dementia follow-up through 2023. Ten modifiable risk factors: obesity, hypertension, diabetes, hearing loss, visual loss, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol consumption, smoking, loneliness, and depression, were used to derive clusters using latent class analysis. Cox proportional hazards models examined the association between late-life clusters and incident dementia.ResultsIn mid-life (mean age, 55.7 ± 6.2 years), four risk factor clusters were identified: cardiometabolic, substance use, psychosocial, and lower risk. In late-life (mean age, 73.9 ± 6.4 years), four clusters were identified: cardiometabolic, substance use, psychosocial and physically inactive, and lower risk. After adjustment for sociodemographic factors, the psychosocial and physically inactive cluster was associated with the highest hazard of dementia (hazard ratio (HR), 1.23; 95% CI, 1.16-1.32), followed by the substance use (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.09-1.24) and the cardiometabolic cluster (HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.07-1.18).ConclusionsDistinct risk factor clusters were identified at both mid-life and late-life; the psychosocial and physically inactive cluster carried the highest risk of dementia. These findings underscore the importance of considering risk factor clustering when designing targeted interventions to reduce dementia risk across the life course.

articles.title: Diagnostic reclassification under the AA-2024 biological framework: A real-world comparison with ATN 2018 using cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) has evolved from a syndromic diagnosis to a biologically defined entity supported by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers. The Alzheimer's Association 2024 (AA-2024) criteria are expected to expand biological AD classification compared with the 2018 NIA-AA AT(N) framework.ObjectiveTo compare biological AD classification using the AT(N) 2018 framework and the AA-2024 criteria in a real-world cohort.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective study including 146 consecutive patients evaluated for cognitive impairment in a tertiary neurology center who underwent CSF biomarker testing (Aβ42, Aβ40, Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio, phosphorylated tau, and total tau). Each patient was classified according to AT(N) 2018 and AA-2024 criteria. Diagnostic distributions, reclassification patterns, and agreement (Cohen's κ) were analyzed. Group comparisons used Wilcoxon rank-sum and Fisher's exact tests.ResultsUnder AT(N) 2018, 40/146 (27.4%) patients met biological AD criteria, whereas AA-2024 classified 72/146 (49.3%) as AD. Reclassification occurred exclusively from non-AD to AD (32 patients, 21.9%), with no reverse reclassification. Agreement was moderate (κ = 0.57). Concordant AD cases (AD+/AD+) showed lower Aβ42/Aβ40 ratios and higher total and phosphorylated tau levels than reclassified cases (AD-/AD+) (all p < 0.001), as well as higher neurodegeneration marker positivity (70% versus 25%; p < 0.001). Final clinical AD diagnosis was assigned to 98% of concordant cases versus 38% of reclassified cases (p < 0.001).ConclusionsAA-2024 increases biological AD classification by identifying amyloid-positive individuals with lower tau burden and clinical heterogeneity, underscoring the need to integrate biomarker-based definitions with clinical and longitudinal assessment.

articles.title: Cardiomonostack: A postoperative heart failure risk prediction model for total hip arthroplasty driven by ensemble learning.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundAccurate perioperative risk prediction remains challenging because of class imbalance, cohort heterogeneity, unstable probability estimates and limited interpretability.ObjectiveTo develop and externally evaluate CardioMonoStack, an ensemble architecture integrating heterogeneous base learners, branch-level monotonicity priors, stacked meta-learning and feature-dependent residual logit correction.MethodsWe conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 1911 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing total hip arthroplasty across five healthcare databases. CardioMonoStack was developed using MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, validated in INSPIRE, and externally tested in eICU and MOVER. Performance was assessed using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, threshold-dependent classification measures, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Interpretability was examined using SHAP, interaction and individual conditional expectation analyses.ResultsCardioMonoStack achieved the highest AUROC point estimates among evaluated models in eICU (0.790; 95% CI 0.711-0.865) and MOVER (0.866; 95% CI 0.761-0.949), with AUPRC values of 0.569 (95% CI 0.415-0.717) and 0.571 (95% CI 0.328-0.792), respectively. Calibration and net benefit varied across cohorts and comparators. Omission of L3 increased Brier-score and log-loss point estimates in both external cohorts; paired confidence intervals supported these differences in MOVER but were inconclusive in eICU. SHAP analyses prioritised blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, age, and metabolic and demographic factors.ConclusionCardioMonoStack is a candidate framework for estimating in-hospital heart-failure risk after total hip arthroplasty. Despite promising external discrimination, prospective validation, local recalibration, and clinical impact evaluation are required before implementation.

articles.title: Price elasticity of cannabis demand in legal adult-use cannabis markets: Evidence from retail scanner data in the United States.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cannabis for adult use is legally sold in nearly half of states in the United States, yet little is known about how cannabis demand responds to price changes or whether excise taxes can effectively influence cannabis demand in legal markets. This study aimed to (1) assess trends in market share and prices of cannabis flower products and (2) estimate the price elasticity of demand for cannabis flower products in adult-use markets in the United States.

DESIGN: Secondary data analysis of retail scanner data from point-of-sale systems in a nonrandom sample of cannabis retailers, projected to represent statewide sales from 2020 to 2023. Descriptive statistics assessed trends in product market share and prices. Two-stage least squares models with state and time fixed effects estimated the price elasticity of demand for flower products, using state-level cannabis excise taxes as an instrumental variable for retail prices.

SETTING: Ten states with legal adult-use cannabis markets in the United States.

CASES: A total of 864 616 product-state-quarter level observations on cannabis flower sales, including dried flower and pre-roll products.

MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was quantity demanded in grams. The primary explanatory variable was tax-exclusive retail price per gram. The instrumental variable was state-level standardized excise tax per gram.

RESULTS: Cannabis flower products remained the dominant category in adult-use markets, accounting for over 50% of total sales. The median price per gram declined from $8.23 to $6.12 over the 4-year study period. Using the instrumental variable approach, the price elasticity of demand for cannabis flower products was estimated at -2.29 (95% confidence interval = -2.61 to -1.89), indicating that a 1% decrease in price was associated with a 2.29% increase in quantity demanded.

SUMMARY: In legal adult-use cannabis markets in the United States, cannabis flower product prices declined by 26% from 2020 to 2023. Demand was highly price elastic, as a 1% decrease in price was associated with more than a 2% increase in quantity sold in retail markets. Continued price declines may lead to increased cannabis demand, but this effect could be potentially counterbalanced by well-designed excise tax policies.

articles.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and preeclampsia risk: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Insulin resistance plays a role in preeclampsia (PE), yet the clinical utility of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between the TyG index and PE, as well as its diagnostic accuracy. We searched eight databases for observational studies published from inception to December 31, 2025. Data were synthesized using random-effects models, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses addressing heterogeneity. Our analysis included 12 studies involving 103,702 pregnant women. A higher TyG index was linked to increased odds of PE, with a pooled odds ratio of 1.85 (95% CI: 1.48-2.32). Significant heterogeneity was observed across studies (I² = 71.2%). In five studies, the pooled sensitivity was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.49-0.78), specificity was 0.58 (95% CI: 0.50-0.65), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.59-0.68), suggesting limited discriminatory power. Limitations included substantial heterogeneity, a predominance of Chinese populations, and TyG measurements taken near or after PE onset in some studies. While the TyG index is an exploratory metabolic marker associated with PE, these findings do not confirm its prospective predictive value or support its use as a standalone screening tool. Its incremental contribution to multivariable prediction models requires prospective validation in diverse populations, using standardized measurement timing and predefined thresholds.

articles.title: Age-stratified mortality following operative management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT/OBJECTIVE: Postoperative mortality following traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) remains substantial, yet the combined influence of neurologic completeness and age on survival is poorly characterized in operatively treated patients. This study evaluated age-stratified mortality after surgical management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cSCI.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using risk ratio analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards.

SETTING: Global federated electronic health record database (TriNetX).

PARTICIPANTS: Adults who underwent surgery for traumatic subaxial cSCI, identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes, with injury classified as complete or incomplete (n = 5,477).

INTERVENTIONS: Operative management of traumatic subaxial cSCI.

OUTCOME MEASURES: All-cause mortality at 3, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Independent predictors of mortality were identified via Cox regression.

RESULTS: Complete cSCI was associated with significantly higher mortality at 3 months (10.73% vs. 7.7%; RR 1.39), 6 months (12.5% vs. 9.2%; RR 1.36), and 1 year (14.7% vs. 11.2%; RR 1.31) (all P < 0.001). Mortality differences were most pronounced in patients aged 61-80 years, with approximately twofold higher risk in complete injuries. Increasing age, male sex, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality.

CONCLUSION: Complete traumatic cSCI carries significantly higher postoperative mortality than incomplete injury, particularly among patients aged 61-80 years. These findings underscore the combined prognostic impact of neurologic severity and age, and may guide perioperative counseling and risk stratification, but should not be interpreted as demonstrating formal age-dependent effect modification.

articles.title: Respiratory Syncytial Viral Infections Among Hospitalized Youth With Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes substantial risk to all infants, but its impact on youth with SCD (Y-SCD) is underexplored. With newer, highly effective RSV monoclonal antibodies (RSV-mAb), research is needed to inform their use in Y-SCD. This single-center study of Y-SCD aged 0-21 years identified 667 hospitalizations that included RSV testing. Of these, 5% were positive for RSV, and 68% occurred in Y-SCD beyond their first RSV season. Intensive care, positive pressure ventilation, and transfusion were required in 21%, 32%, and 21% of hospitalizations, respectively. Findings indicate that multicenter studies are warranted to determine if RSV-mAbs improve outcomes in Y-SCD.

articles.title: NH2 Measurements during the Pyrolysis and Oxidation of Ammonia/Propane Mixtures in a Shock Tube.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. A
articles.abstract: Ammonia/propane pyrolysis and oxidation mixtures were studied using NH2 laser spectroscopy to obtain NH2 time histories in a shock tube. An NH3 diagnostic based on a quantum cascade laser was used to verify the initial ammonia concentrations, while a 597.375-nm laser diagnostic measured NH2 in the post-reflected shock region. A 75/25% (by volume) ammonia/propane pyrolysis mixture, diluted in 99% argon, was tested between 1682 and 2926 K at near-atmospheric pressure. Three elementary reactions─C3H8 ⇆ C3H7 + H, NH3 + H ⇆ NH2 + H2, and NH2 + H ⇆ NH + H2─were identified as influential for accurately modeling NH2. Additionally, mixtures composed of 75/25% ammonia/propane with O2 in 99% argon were tested at equivalence ratios of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 between 1318 and 2404 K. Four key reactions, namely C3H8 + M ⇆ C2H5 + CH3 + M; NH3 + H ⇆ NH2 + H2; NH3 + OH ⇆ NH2 + H2O; and O2 + H ⇆ O + OH, heavily influenced the production of NH2 at early time scales, with CH4 + M ⇆ CH3 + H + M and H2 + O ⇆ H + OH being responsible for the delayed destruction of NH2. The data presented in this study are available in the supplementary material for chemical kinetics modeling validation.
