articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

articles.title: Chaperonopathies as Disorders of Disorder: The Role of Intrinsically Disordered Regions in Proteostasis Dysfunction.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
articles.abstract: Molecular chaperones are central regulators of the proteostasis network, ensuring proteome integrity through protein folding, the prevention of aggregation, and targeted degradation. These mechanisms are essential for limiting proteotoxic stress and preventing the accumulation of pathogenic proteins. Consequently, chaperone dysfunction is linked to various diseases including genetic chaperonopathies caused by pathogenic mutations. The most commonly affected chaperones include small heat shock proteins (sHSPs; HSPB1, HSPB3, HSPB5, HSPB8), Hsp60 (HSPD1), Hsp70 (HSPA9/mortalin), and the CCT/TRiC complex. sHSPs are ATP-independent chaperones critical under stress conditions and are characterized by intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), particularly in flexible terminal regions. Although structurally important, IDRs are frequently targets of disease-associated mutations. In this study, intrinsic disorder in chaperones linked to genetic chaperonopathies was analyzed using bioinformatics tools, followed by a focused evaluation of highly disordered proteins and their disease associations. The results highlight intrinsic disorder as a conserved and functionally essential feature. HSPB1 and HSPB8 show high disorder levels, consistent with roles in neural proteostasis and neuropathies. HSPB3 and HSPB5 exhibit moderate disorder but harbor mutations linked to muscle and cardiac diseases. In contrast, HSPB6 dysfunction is mainly driven by post-translational modifications, rather than mutations. Overall, genetic chaperonopathies can be viewed as intrinsic-disorder-related diseases.

articles.title: A novel digital intervention to support mental and sexual wellbeing after stroke and brain injury: A feasibility randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the feasibility of a novel digital self-management intervention (HOPE4ABI) supporting mental and sexual wellbeing for stroke and acquired brain injury survivors.DesignParallel, 1:1 allocation, two-arm feasibility randomised controlled trial.SettingOnline.ParticipantsU.K.-based adults (n = 53) living with any type of acquired brain injury, sustained at least 3 months prior to trial entry.InterventionParticipants were randomly assigned to the self-guided (n = 26) or group-facilitated (n = 27) 8-week online intervention. All participants received identical information and intervention content, but peer-to-peer interactions and facilitation were only available in the group-facilitated arm.Outcome measuresPrimary outcomes were rates of recruitment, retention, engagement and acceptability, measured against a priori criteria. Secondary outcomes were scores on measures of mental wellbeing, sexual wellbeing and quality of life, recorded at baseline, 8 weeks and 6 months.ResultsThe recruitment rate was acceptable (n = 53/73; 72.6%). At 6 months, questionnaire data were available for n = 45/53 (84.9%), thus meeting the progression criteria. Neither the engagement criteria (52.3%, n = 23/44), nor acceptability criteria (75.7%, n = 28/37) were met, and were explored further in post-intervention interviews. Six-month follow-up data showed improvements in mental wellbeing, sexual wellbeing and quality of life relative to baseline.ConclusionsOn balance, a definitive RCT is warranted to evaluate the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of the intervention. The primary feasibility outcomes of recruitment and retention rate met the progression criteria, and engagement and acceptability issues were addressed through participant feedback. There were signals of efficacy noted across all outcome measures at 6-month follow-up.ISRCTN Reg NoISRCTN46988394.

articles.title: Fatigue Interventions in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Heart Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a significant yet under-addressed symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and heart diseases, impairing quality of life. This systematic review aims to investigate the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions, including exercise and psychosocial support, in managing fatigue in COPD, ischemic heart disease, and heart failure, providing evidence to guide clinical practice.

METHODS: This systematic review is registered in PROSPERO and follows the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, MEDLINE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO.

RESULTS: The pooled meta-analysis with all studies had an overall mean difference of -11.93 [-15.63; -8.24]. Physical activity had the largest effect (-17.01 [-24.40; -9.61]), while combined psychosocial and physical activity interventions were insignificant. Results remained unchanged after sensitivity analysis.

CONCLUSION: Meta-analyses highlight the effectiveness of non-pharmacological rehabilitation interventions, particularly physical activity, in managing fatigue. Psychosocial interventions show potential but may be less effective. Future research should optimize strategies, explore fatigue mechanisms, and address patient needs to improve intervention efficacy.

articles.title: Neonatal Common Atrioventricular Valve Replacement After Failed Staged Biventricular Repair.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Balanced complete atrioventricular septal defect (cAVSD) with aortic coarctation (CoA) is generally considered amenable to staged biventricular repair (BVR). However, anatomic suitability does not necessarily guarantee functional stability. We report a 3.5-kg neonate with balanced cAVSD (Rastelli type A), severe common atrioventricular valve regurgitation (CAVVR), and CoA. Preoperative echocardiography indicated suitability for BVR. At 9 days of age, arch repair and pulmonary artery banding (PAB) were performed. However, weaning the patient from cardiopulmonary bypass was impossible because of profound hypotension, and transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated worsening of CAVVR. PAB adjustment and removal were ineffective. Intraoperative inspection revealed a severely dysplastic valve morphology incompatible with durable repair. After myocardial recovery with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, the patient was converted to a univentricular pathway. The patient subsequently underwent common atrioventricular valve replacement, Damus-Kaye-Stansel anastomosis, and right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery shunt placement. Postoperative ventricular function was preserved without residual regurgitation. This case underscores the importance of flexible intraoperative decision-making guided by direct valve assessment and timely strategic conversion in high-risk neonates with cAVSD and severe CAVVR.

articles.title: Reviewer Comment on Barrette et al. "Use of Telestroke Prior to Endovascular Stroke Treatment in Canada: Results from the Optimise Registry".
articles.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques

articles.title: The START-SIAPAV-PAD Registry - Rationale, study design, and baseline characteristics of an ongoing Italian multicentre registry.
articles.abstract: Background: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with a high burden of cardiovascular and limb events, yet guideline-directed medical therapy remains suboptimal. The START-SIAPAV-PAD registry was designed to describe characteristics, management and clinical history of patients with PAD in Italy. Baseline characteristics and treatment are reported. Patients and methods: START-SIAPAV-PAD is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry enrolling consecutive adults with PAD managed at 20 Italian Vascular centres, starting in February 2023. Standardised electronic case-report forms collect demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, haemodynamic parameters, vascular anatomy, therapies. Follow-up is planned for a minimum of 3 years. PAD severity is classified according to the Leriche-Fontaine scale, and risk-factor targets follow the 2024 ESC guidelines. Results: The present analysis includes 517 patients (72.0% male; median age 71 years) with a high prevalence of hypertension (79.2%), dyslipidaemia (85.0%), diabetes (36.9%), smoking (96.1% current or former) and chronic kidney disease (21.2%). Nearly half reported a walking distance <200 m, 77.5% had a resting ankle-brachial index ≤.80, and 17.2% presented with Leriche-Fontaine stage IV. Femoropopliteal disease was most frequent (69.8%), with multilevel involvement in 43.4%. Previous revascularisation was common, major amputation was rare. LDL cholesterol target (<55mg dL) was achieved in 27.9% of patients despite lipid-lowering therapy in 82.1%. Dual pathway inhibition, advanced lipid-lowering therapies, supervised exercise and structured smoking-cessation programmes were insufficiently adopted. Conclusions: In a population with advanced PAD and multiple risk factors we observed a substantial gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Longitudinal follow-up will assess outcomes and opportunities to improve PAD management.

articles.title: Association between the cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose index and the incidence of new-onset diabetes in patients with chronic gastrointestinal diseases: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the association between the cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose (CHG) index and the incidence of diabetes in patients with chronic gastrointestinal diseases (CGID).

METHODS: This study utilized data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) for the period 2011-2020. The association between the CHG index and new-onset diabetes was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Restrictive cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to examine the dose-response relationship, and time-window analysis assessed the time-dependence of predictive performance. The independent contributions of individual components of the CHG index were investigated using a two-axis decomposition (metabolic burden axis and lipid protection axis).

RESULTS: This study enrolled 1,870 CGID patients who were free of diabetes at baseline. During the follow-up period, 289 participants (15.5%) developed new-onset diabetes. CHG index was associated with the risk of new-onset diabetes (HR per 1-SD increase = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.28-1.61). RCS analysis showed no nonlinear relationship (P-nonlinear = 0.773). Time-window analysis showed that the predictive performance of the CHG index increased over time (HR for 0-5 years = 1.33 vs HR for 5-9 years = 1.62, P-interaction <0.001). Two-axis decomposition analysis revealed that the 'high metabolic burden-low lipid protection' group had the highest risk of diabetes (HR = 2.00).

CONCLUSIONS: The CHG index is an independent risk factor for new-onset diabetes in CGID patients, showing a linear dose-response relationship and time-dependent predictive performance.

articles.title: Outcomes Following Operative Management of Distal Humerus Nonunions.
authors: and the Evidence-Based Musculoskeletal Injury and Trauma Collaborative (EMIT)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe outcomes after distal humerus nonunion surgery and to identify risk factors for failure in the same population.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective case series.

SETTING: Seven, academic, level I trauma centers.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Included were patients who underwent operative repair of a distal humerus (OTA/AO 13) nonunion and were ≥18 years old. Patients were excluded if they had clinical or serologic signs of infection prior to nonunion repair, or if their follow-up was less than 180 days and their surgery could not otherwise be classified as a success or failure.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: This study measured the rate of recalcitrant nonunion and complications following distal humerus nonunion surgery. It additionally evaluated associations between union rate and demographics, injury characteristics, and nonunion surgery characteristics.

RESULTS: Fifty-four patients with distal humerus nonunion were identified. Of the 30 included patients (mean age 47.5 (range 22-71), 18 (60%) male), 7 (23.3%) failed to unite after their index nonunion surgery at a study institution. Thirteen patients (43.3%) experienced one or more postoperative complications. While twenty-one of the 30 (70%) included patients initially sustained an open distal humerus fracture, all 7 patients (100%) who developed a recalcitrant nonunion initially sustained an open fracture. The use of bone graft or bone graft substitute relative to no graft, patient age, body mass index, smoking status, diabetes, and initial OTA/AO fracture classification were not associated with nonunion repair success rate (all p>0.05).

CONCLUSION: This multicenter series challenged the concept that union rates are high, defined by the authors as >90%, following distal humerus nonunion surgery. Though limited by a small sample size that precluded multivariate regression, this study's bivariate analysis suggests that an initially open distal humerus fracture may increase the risk of recalcitrant distal humerus nonunion. Modifiable risk factors were not associated with the success rate of nonunion surgery. These findings can be used to better inform patients' expectations of results and complications following distal humerus nonunion surgery.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic level III.

articles.title: Editorial Commentary: Expert Opinion on Unloader Brace Derived From a Modified Delphi Consensus Study: A Guide to Support Decision-Making in the Practice.
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract: A Delphi expert consensus process is a method to achieve a consolidated consensus derived from expert opinions regarding a conflicting issue without the accumulation of high-quality evidence in the literature. Recent literature has employed this analytical methodology to attain expert-derived recommendations regarding the role of unloader bracing in the management of knee osteoarthritis. There have been several biomechanical studies positively supporting the efficacy of this treatment modality; however, randomized controlled trials showing its clinical benefit are still limited. Although there are some inherent limitations included in this type of analysis, several statements and recommendations made about the use of unloader bracing across nonoperative and surgery-related applications help physicians make clinical decisions in practice.

articles.title: Yi-Qi-Bu-Shen Recipe Alleviates Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: Network Pharmacology Prediction and In Vivo Evidence.
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common chronic complication of diabetes that severely impairs quality of life. The Yi-Qi-Bu-Shen Recipe (YQBS) alleviates diabetic complications, but its mechanism against DPN remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the underlying mechanism of YQBS against DPN using network pharmacology and to verify its effects on peripheral nerve injury and modulation of the AGE-RAGE/NF-κB signaling pathway in vivo. Active components of YQBS were computationally screened via the TCMSP database, potential targets were predicted using GeneCards and OMIM, and key pathways were analyzed by KEGG enrichment. Molecular docking was performed to assess binding affinities. In animal experiments, streptozotocin-induced DPN rats were randomized into control, model, low-dose YQBS, and high-dose YQBS groups. After 12 weeks, nerve conduction velocity, sciatic nerve pathology, nerve repair-related proteins, and RAGE/NF-κB p65 phosphorylation were evaluated. Network pharmacology predicted quercetin, β-sitosterol, and formononetin as major active components, PTGS2 and NOS2 as core targets, and AGE-RAGE/PI3K-Akt as key pathways. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding affinities. Animal experiments confirmed that YQBS significantly improved nerve conduction, alleviated nerve damage, upregulated repair proteins, and inhibited RAGE expression and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation. In conclusion, YQBS ameliorates DPN in rats, with suppression of AGE-RAGE/NF-κB pathway activation.

articles.title: The reporting of dental studies involving animal models requires improvement.
articles.abstract: Poor reporting of animal model studies undermines their value and contributes to research waste. In this study, reporting adherence of dental animal studies in relation to the ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines was assessed. A Medline via PubMed search to identify studies published between 1st January 2018 and 31st December 2025 was performed. Descriptive statistics, frequency distributions for the responses to each item and mean values for adequate reporting per ARRIVE item were calculated. A sum score was determined by adding the responses per item and sub-questions. Linear regression between overall score and study characteristics was performed. A total of 896 studies were assessed. The mean overall reporting score was 46.7 (SD 7.7). The reporting of items pertaining to sample size, eligibility, randomisation, blinding, outcome measures, statistical methods, experimental procedures, results, animal care and monitoring and protocol registration was sub-optimal. Publication year and the introduction of the updated guidelines were associated with an improvement of the overall summary score. The involvement of a statistician and reporting in relation to ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines were associated with higher reporting scores. To reduce research waste and improve research transparency, a collaborated effect is required from journal editors and researchers to improve the reporting of studies involving animal models.

articles.title: Impact of splenic red pulp macrophages on hematopoiesis and their therapeutic effects against sepsis.
articles.abstract: Patients with sepsis frequently experience dysregulation of hematopoietic function in the bone marrow-spleen axis, resulting in hematologic abnormalities, including anemia and leukopenia. We hypothesized that red pulp macrophages (RPMs) in the spleen contribute to hematopoiesis through the bone marrow-spleen axis in septic patients. We established the sepsis model by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) surgery, and performed bone marrow transplantation (BMT) and splenic RPMs transplantation (RPMT) after CLP. We evaluated splenic RPMs, hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs; LSK cells), and multipotent progenitor 3 cells (MPP3) proliferation and immunomodulatory properties. We performed splenic transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) to uncover the mechanisms by which RPMs exert therapeutic effects against sepsis. Sepsis-induced myelosuppression at 24h and MDSCs accumulation at 72h were detected. Both BMT and RPMT effectively restored splenic RPMs and suppressed MDSCs, with RPMT exerting a greater effect on LSK and MPP3 proliferation. RNA-seq confirmed that both BMT and RPMT attenuated sepsis-associated inflammation. Notably, RPMT exerted more targeted effects on hematopoietic cell lineage, cell cycle progression, and energy metabolism than BMT. This study demonstrates that splenic RPMs play a crucial regulatory role in hematopoiesis through the bone marrow-spleen axis during sepsis.

articles.title: Interventions to address the effects of climate change on human health in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
articles.abstract: Climate change poses disproportionate threats to human health in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet comprehensive evidence on implemented interventions remains under-researched. Understanding the scope and characteristics of existing climate-health interventions is essential for informing policy priorities and action in the region. We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. We systematically searched Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed empirical studies on climate-health interventions in SSA, with no date restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened 3009 records. A total of 36 studies reporting 350 interventions were included. The majority of the studies (83.3%) focused exclusively on adaptation, while a smaller proportion (16.7%) combined both adaptation and mitigation strategies. Four overarching intervention categories were identified inductively from the included studies, each comprising distinct but conceptually related sub-categories: health systems strengthening and governance; disease surveillance, monitoring, and early warning; environmental health and infrastructure; and community resilience and social wellbeing. Vector-borne diseases, particularly malaria, constituted the primary health focus, while heat-related illnesses, occupational health, and mental health received limited attention. Studies mostly reported interventions in West Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa, and multi-regional settings, with Central Africa receiving limited attention. The evidence is predominantly rural-focused (n = 18; 50%), with urban-focused studies accounting for 10 studies (27.8%) and mixed urban-rural settings for the remaining 8 (22.2%). Notably, no dedicated study investigated interventions specifically targeting coastal areas. People-centred interventions predominated over nature-based solutions. Key evidence gaps included cross-sectional study designs limiting causal inference, insufficient cost-effectiveness evaluations, limited integration of indigenous knowledge, and inadequate attention to gender-specific and occupational vulnerabilities. Policy efforts must go beyond disease-specific responses toward integrated strategies addressing multiple climate-health pathways while prioritising underrepresented regions and mitigation opportunities to build comprehensive, equitable climate resilience across the region.

articles.title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Lifestyle Plus Sleep Extension Intervention on Adults With Prediabetes and Short Sleep.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short sleep duration is a modifiable barrier to diabetes prevention, yet no adequately powered trials have tested whether integrating a behavioral sleep intervention into a lifestyle intervention improves glycemic or weight loss outcomes in adults with prediabetes.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of a lifestyle versus a lifestyle plus sleep intervention on glucose control and weight loss in adults with prediabetes and habitual short sleep duration.

METHODS: In this two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, adults with A1c-confirmed prediabetes and actigraphy-confirmed short sleep duration completed two clinic visits and 2-week at-home monitoring periods, including actigraphy-estimated sleep and continuous glucose monitoring. The 8-week intervention was delivered one-on-one via a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act-compliant videoconferencing platform. The primary outcome was change in the percentage of time sensor glucose was above tight range (> 140 mg/dL). Secondary outcomes included actigraphy-estimated sleep parameters, self-reported sleep quality and daytime sleepiness, and body weight. We compared pre- to post-intervention changes between groups using a modified intention-to-treat approach.

RESULTS: Among 196 participants, we found no significant between-group difference in the primary glucose outcome. Both groups achieved significant within-group increases in sleep and reductions in body weight, with no significant between-group differences for either outcome. The lifestyle plus sleep group showed significantly greater improvements in self-reported sleep quality and daytime sleepiness compared to the lifestyle group. Sleep onset advanced significantly only in lifestyle plus sleep group, though the between-group difference did not reach statistical significance. A post hoc analysis found that earlier sleep onset, regardless of group assignment, was independently associated with greater weight loss, whereas changes in sleep duration were not.

DISCUSSION: Adding a behavioral sleep intervention to a lifestyle intervention did not improve glucose control. However, advancing sleep onset time predicted greater weight loss, independent of sleep duration or group assignment, identifying circadian timing as a promising and modifiable target for diabetes prevention. Prospective trials powered to test sleep timing interventions on metabolic outcomes are warranted.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes.

METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified. Secondary diagnosis codes captured VTE subtypes. Primary analyses compared mortality and major complications in ANP with versus without VTE; secondary analyses compared outcomes by subtype.

RESULTS: Among 110,225 ANP hospitalizations, 12.25% had VTE. ANP with VTE had higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.89, P<0.001), longer length of stay (adjusted mean difference 10.7 d, P<0.001), and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference $151,685, P<0.001). VTE was associated with higher rates of mesenteric ischemia, gastric varices, upper GI bleeding, AKI, sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, ARDS, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion, and ICU admissions. On subtype analysis, DVT (aOR 2.39, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 1.45, P=0.001) were associated with higher mortality; SVT was not significantly associated with mortality, though the analysis was limited by few events. PVT was most strongly associated with mesenteric ischemia (aOR 8.28, P<0.001), whereas gastric varices were most associated with SVT (aOR 11.37, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 3.73, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: VTE in ANP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, systemic complications, and resource utilization, with substantial heterogeneity across subtypes. DVT-associated ANP showed higher rates of systemic complications, whereas PVT and SVT showed distinct territory-specific vascular-complication patterns. Prospective studies should evaluate phenotype-specific anticoagulation strategies.

articles.title: Physical Simulated Y-Site Compatibility of Hypertonic Saline with Vasoactive Medications Commonly Used in Pediatric Intensive Care.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Critically ill pediatric patients often receive multiple IV medications concurrently. Due to limited vascular access in these patients, there is frequent Y-site coadministration. Incompatibility of medications can result in particulate formation, which poses serious clinical risks such as microvascular obstruction and organ dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate the Y-site compatibility of vasoactive medications with 12% hypertonic saline.

METHODS: This study simulated Y-site compatibility of 12% hypertonic saline by preparing 1:1 mixing ratios of commonly used medications in pediatric concentrations. Medications that were analyzed included epinephrine, dopamine, norepinephrine, vasopressin, milrinone, alprostadil, and sildenafil. Analysis was completed using visual inspection, pH testing at 0 and 4 hours, and light obscuration to determine particulate counts. Particulate counts were assessed at ≥10 µm and ≥25 µm. Compatibility was defined using USP <788> thresholds.

RESULTS: Of the seven vasoactive medications analyzed in combined with hypertonic saline, six met established compatibility criteria. The range of pH changes among all medications was -0.06 to +0.16, indicating stability over time and limited risk of meaningful acid-base alterations. Sildenafil was the only combination tested that demonstrated incompatibility with 12% hypertonic saline.

CONCLUSION: This report evaluated the compatibility of vasoactive medications at specific pediatric concentrations with 12% hypertonic saline, demonstrating incompatibility with only sildenafil 0.8 mg/mL. Epinephrine 100 mcg/mL, dopamine in D5W 3.2 mg/mL, alprostadil in D5W 20 mcg/mL, vasopressin in D5W 1 unit/mL, milrinone in D5W 200 mcg/mL, and norepinephrine 32 mcg/mL were all compatible with 12% hypertonic saline.

articles.title: Smoking cessation interventions in adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To assess the effects of smoking cessation interventions, compared with no intervention, usual care, placebo, or alternative interventions, on sustained abstinence from smoking in adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), or co-occurring ADHD and ASD. Secondary objectives To assess whether the effects of smoking cessation interventions differ between adults with ADHD, ASD, and co‑occurring ADHD and ASD. To assess whether intervention effects vary according to participant characteristics (e.g. ADHD or ASD symptom profiles, co‑occurring mental health conditions, and alcohol- or substance-use disorders). To assess the safety and acceptability of smoking cessation interventions, including serious and non-serious adverse events and treatment discontinuation.

articles.title: Long-term Cost-Effectiveness of an Automated Insulin Delivery System Versus Multiple Daily Injections of Insulin Plus Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Children and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes in Hong Kong.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
AIM: The MiniMed 780G (MM780G) automated insulin delivery (AID) system has been shown to improve glycemic control in people with type 1 diabetes (T1D). The aim was to determine the long-term cost-effectiveness of the MM780G versus multiple daily injections of insulin plus continuous glucose monitoring (MDI+CGM) in people with T1D in Hong Kong.

METHODS: The analysis was performed using the IQVIA Core Diabetes Model. The primary analysis was performed in adults with HbA1c ≥8%, from a payer perspective over a time horizon of 60 years and annual discount rate of 3%. Clinical input data were sourced from a clinical trial, wherein HbA1c reductions from baseline (9.04%) of 1.54% and 0.2% were assumed for MM780G and MDI+CGM, respectively. A secondary analysis was performed for a cohort of children/adolescents starting treatment at <18 years.

RESULTS: In the adult base case analysis, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) for MM780G versus MDI+CGM was HKD 348 927 (USD 44 759) per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained. In the pediatric analysis, the ICER for MM780G versus MDI+CGM was HKD 300 466 (USD 38 543) per QALY. The use of MM780G was predicted to result in reductions in the incidence of diabetes-related complications in both analyses.

CONCLUSION: Over a long-term time horizon, the use of MM780G was projected to improve clinical outcomes versus MDI+CGM. The MM780G was found to be cost-effective versus MDI+CGM in adults with T1D in Hong Kong who are not achieving glycemic targets; benefits were more pronounced in pediatric users, underscoring the value of initiating AID therapy at a younger age.

articles.title: Upadacitinib and Warfarin Drug Interaction Resulting in Significantly Increased International Normalized Ratio: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe a case report of upadacitinib interaction with warfarin, resulting in a supratherapeutic international normalized ratio (INR).

SUMMARY: A 41-year-old female with a history of severe refractory atopic dermatitis was initiated on upadacitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. She additionally had a history of mechanical mitral valve replacement for which she was maintained on warfarin with a target INR of 2.5-3.5. After nearly a week of concomitant upadacitinib 15 mg and warfarin, with no other changes in medications or food, her INR increased to 9.3, for which she was sent to the emergency department and received oral vitamin K. Her INR returned to baseline and upadacitinib was discontinued. Several weeks later, due to refractory atopic dermatitis symptoms, she took another two doses of upadacitinib and her INR increased to 4.7. She was instructed to take no further upadacitinib, her INR subsequently normalized with warfarin dose modification, and her atopic dermatitis therapy was changed.

CONCLUSION: Upadacitinib labeling does not include interaction with systemic anticoagulation nor increases in INR. The mechanism of this interaction remains to be elucidated, but an imbalance in pro-thrombotic and anti-thrombotic activity from various downstream cytokine inhibition may play a role. Clinicians should be aware of this potential paradoxical effect in patients on systemic anticoagulation who are initiating JAK inhibitors.

articles.title: Clonal expansion of CD8+ effector T cells in patients with calcific aortic valve disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a complex cardiovascular pathology, culminating in aortic stenosis and heart failure with no effective treatment strategy, except invasive surgery. While inflammation may contribute to valvular fibro-calcific pathology and T cells have been identified within the leaflets, their contribution to CAVD pathogenesis remains unclear.

METHODS & RESULTS: Disease-staged whole-tissue proteomics (n=16) confirmed a pro-inflammatory T cell driven signature, with immunohistochemistry (n=10) and immunofluorescence (n=8) conducted on control and CAVD valves to confirm T cell localization to calcified regions. Flow cytometry immunophenotyping (n=20) was was performed using valvular tissue and corresponding peripheral blood from the same individuals. Single cell RNA sequencing and paired single T cell receptor sequencing was conducted on an additional 4 patients on CD45+, CD3+, CD4+ or CD8+ T cells. T cell signaling was identified through unsupervised clustering. Tissue resident memory (TRM) T cells were detected within the valve, exhibiting a highly cytotoxic, activated, and terminally differentiated phenotype. This pan-pro-inflammatory signal was differentially identified in T cells originating from the valve tissue, and not observed in the blood, indicative of an adaptive, local and non-systemic inflammatory signature in CAVD patients. T cell receptor analysis detected hyperexpanded clones within the CD8+ T cell central memory (TCM) population, with TRM cells comprising most of the large and medium clonal expansion within the T cell population. Clonal expansion was more prominent in valve tissue, with expanded clones largely confined to their tissue of origin. Clonal interaction network analysis demonstrated the greatest proportion of clones originating from CD8+ TCM and TRM populations, exhibiting a tissue resident, cytotoxic environment within the valve.

CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, the data define distinct T cell subpopulations in CAVD and implicate specific antigenic epitopes driving clonal expansion of valvular T cells, supporting a central role for antigen-driven, autoimmune-like inflammation in disease propagation.

articles.title: Endothelial restoration of aortic valve homeostasis resolves interstitial fibro calcific remodeling in aortic stenosis.
Tracking severe asthma improvement with biologic therapy using spirometry and impulse oscillometry: a real-world study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe asthma patients receiving biologic therapy require accurate functional assessment and longitudinal monitoring. Spirometry and impulse oscillometry (IOS) may provide complementary information on lung function. The aim of this study was to compare spirometry and IOS in severe asthma patients treated with biologics, evaluating their concordance and clinical relevance, and to assess longitudinal changes in asthma control, oral corticosteroid (OCS) use, exacerbations, and healthcare utilization over 18 months.

METHODS: In this real-world dual-centre longitudinal study, 40 patients with severe asthma treated with biologic therapy underwent spirometry and IOS at baseline and after 6, 12, and 18 months. Functional findings were compared between the two techniques and correlated with asthma control, OCS use, exacerbations, hospitalizations, and healthcare utilization.

RESULTS: Significant clinical improvement was observed over 18 months, with reductions in exacerbations, hospitalizations, healthcare utilization and OCS use, alongside improved ACT scores. FEF25-75% showed partial functional improvement and significant correlations with IOS indices, particularly R5-R20 (r=-0.52 to -0.65) and AX (r=-0.30 to -0.54), supporting the complementary role of oscillometry in longitudinal assessment.

CONCLUSIONS: Biologic therapy significantly reduced the clinical burden of severe asthma. IOS may provide complementary information alongside spirometry for longitudinal functional monitoring in real-life setting.

articles.title: Predictive Value of the HALP Score for Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery.
articles.abstract: Post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, occurring in 20% to 40% of patients and significantly increasing morbidity. The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score, a composite nutritional-inflammatory index, is a prognostic marker in cardiovascular disease. However, its predictive value for POAF remains unestablished. We aimed to evaluate the predictive performance of 5 nutritional-inflammatory indices (HALP, Naples score, Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index [SII], neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio [NPAR], and C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte [CALLY] index) for POAF and internally validate a novel prediction model incorporating HALP. Among 448 patients undergoing CABG, POAF occurred in 131 (29.2%). The HALP score demonstrated the highest discriminative ability (area under curve [AUC] 0.812), significantly (P < .001) outperforming Naples (AUC 0.676), NPAR (AUC 0.730), SII (AUC 0.726), and CALLY (AUC 0.684). Adding HALP to the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-derived base model significantly improved discriminative ability (AUC 0.813-0.897; P < .001) and net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities. The combined model achieved a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.885 with a calibration slope of 0.909, reflecting excellent internal validity. HALP was the strongest POAF predictor in the combined model. The HALP-integrated model showed excellent performance, offering a practical tool for preoperative POAF risk stratification.

articles.title: Mock Circulatory Loop With Autoregulated Renal Circulation Based on Perfusion Pressure for Circulatory Support Devices Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal hypoperfusion, driven by reduced mean arterial pressure or increased venous congestion, contributes to acute kidney injury in cardiogenic shock. Assessing cardiovascular support strategies for patients with cardiogenic shock requires controlled platforms such as mock circulatory loops (MCLs). However, most MCLs lack renal autoregulation or do not account for venous pressure, risking inaccurate renal flow estimation. Here, we describe how to implement a perfusion pressure-based autoregulated renal circulation within an MCL.

METHODS: A renal circulation was integrated into an existing biventricular MCL. Renal vascular resistance was dynamically adjusted according to a perfusion pressure-renal flow relationship. Autoregulation performance was quantified by mean square error between measured and theoretical renal flow. Left, right, and biventricular cardiogenic shock were simulated. Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) support and fluid doses were used as clinically relevant interventions to modify the arterial and venous determinants of perfusion pressure.

RESULTS: Renal autoregulation closely reproduced the target relationship, with mean square error 0.001 (L/min)2. Increasing ECMO flow increased perfusion pressure through higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) and lower mean right atrial pressure (MRAP) across all ventricular failure phenotypes. Conversely, fluid doses increased both MAP and MRAP, with the magnitude of MRAP elevation varying by ventricular failure phenotype and partially offsetting the increase in MAP, resulting in smaller increases in perfusion pressure. Renal flow responses reflected perfusion pressure rather than arterial pressure alone.

CONCLUSION: Renal flow-perfusion pressure autoregulation can be accurately implemented in an MCL. Incorporating such renal autoregulation improves physiological fidelity of MCLs and evaluation of cardiovascular devices.

articles.title: Comparative lifestyle factors and outcomes of an intensive interprofessional lifestyle medicine program versus usual care in Medicare and commercially insured musculoskeletal patients with chronic disease.
articles.journal: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle medicine (LM) uses evidence-based interventions to reduce chronic systemic inflammation, a driver of chronic diseases and painful musculoskeletal conditions. Medicare beneficiaries represent a high-risk population for chronic systemic inflammation and may benefit from receiving care through an intensive LM program (ILMP).

OBJECTIVE: To compare baseline lifestyle factors and outcomes (1) between Medicare and commercially insured patients completing an ILMP, and (2) between Medicare patients completing an ILMP and Medicare patients receiving usual care (non-ILMP).

DESIGN: Retrospective exploratory study of repository data.

SETTING: Tertiary orthopedic center.

PATIENTS: A total of 204 Medicare and 322 commercially insured patients entered the ILMP from May 2023 to May 2025; of these, 101 Medicare and 130 commercially insured patients completed the program and were included in this study (50% vs. 40% completion rate; p = .040). A third group of 90 Medicare patients with similar conditions received usual care during this same time frame.

INTERVENTIONS: The ILMP virtually integrates individual and group visits with an interprofessional team, with patient-identified health goals.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Goal attainment; changes in weight, pain, physical/mental health, and metabolic labs from program enrollment to completion.

RESULTS: Compared to commercially insured ILMP patients, Medicare ILMP patients were older (70 ± 7 vs. 55 ± 10 years, p < .001) and had higher rates of ≥2 lifestyle-related chronic diseases (96% vs. 85%; p = .015), hypertension (72% vs. 54%; p = .010), hyperlipidemia (59% vs. 40%; p = .001), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (33% vs. 18%; p = .015) at baseline. Medicare and commercially insured ILMP patients reported similar use of program services, goal attainment, and outcomes. Compared to the Medicare usual-care group, the Medicare ILMP group had similar baseline characteristics but achieved greater weight loss (10 ± 14 lbs vs. 1 ± 4 lbs; p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: An interprofessional ILMP delivered virtually is feasible and effective for Medicare patients with musculoskeletal conditions and lifestyle-related chronic diseases, despite having a greater baseline disease burden compared with commercially insured patients.

articles.title: Patient-derived neomorphic SEPTIN6 mutations induce hematopoietic stem cell senescence underlying congenital neutropenia and myelodysplasia.
articles.abstract: Septins are RAS-like GTP-binding proteins involved in cytoskeletal organization and cellular division. We previously described 2 pediatric patients harboring SEPT6 germline mutations (GM1: SEPT6 c.1282T>C and GM2: SEPT6 c.1282T>A) presenting with congenital neutropenia associated with the development of myelodysplastic syndrome. In one patient, an additional somatic mutation (SM: SEPT6 c.43C>T) was detected at a low allelic fraction in the BM. Here, we describe the consequences of these mutations for hematopoiesis. Transgenic expression or gene editing of GM1 or GM2 in human CD34+ cells led to enlarged, multinucleated cells associated with accelerated exhaustion and premature senescence of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). Senescence defects were associated with the upregulation of mTOR phosphorylation, and pharmacologic inhibition of the mTOR pathway resulted in rescue of senescence. In parallel, HSPCs exhibited marked mitochondrial abnormalities, including increased expression of OPA-1, a key regulator of mitochondrial fusion, and enhanced oxygen consumption during mitochondrial respiration. Introduction of the SM in cis with GM1 mitigated all observed defects. Collectively, our findings demonstrate a gain-of-function mechanism underlying marrow failure in patients carrying germline SEPT6 mutations and suggest that acquisition of a secondary somatic SEPT6 variant may confer a compensatory effect within hematopoietic cells.

articles.title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
articles.journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified.

RESULTS: Mean age was 59.2 ±17.2 years, with a slight female predominance (54.2%). Only 78 patients (28.1%) had QTcF-confirmed prolongation despite all meeting QTcB inclusion criteria. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +31.7 ms between QTcB and QTcF (SD 18.9; 95% limits of agreement: -5.3 to +68.7 ms), strongly correlated with heart rate (r=0.92, p<0.001): the overcorrection increased from +3.6 ms at heart rate <70 bpm to +64.4 ms at >110 bpm. QTcB normalized on the follow-up ECG in 68.2% of patients. In a complete-case multivariable model (n=96 with available serum bicarbonate), no variable reached conventional statistical significance; serum bicarbonate (OR=1.121 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.991-1.268; p=0.069) and hypertension (OR=2.522; 95% CI: 0.875-7.275; p=0.087) showed borderline associations with QTcF-confirmed prolongation. In an exploratory analysis of the diabetic subgroup (n=148), peripheral neuropathy (DN4 ≥4) was associated with a 15.8 ms higher mean QTcB (age-adjusted 95% CI: 4.7-27.0 ms; p=0.006).

CONCLUSION: Bazett's formula substantially and heart-rate-dependently overestimates QT prolongation compared with the Framingham formula, a discrepancy now precisely quantified. QT prolongation in hospitalized internal medicine patients is predominantly acquired and reversible. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was associated with higher QTcB values in an exploratory analysis. Serum bicarbonate showed only a non-significant trend toward association with QTcF-confirmed prolongation after complete-case multivariable adjustment; this hypothesis warrants confirmation in prospective studies with complete acid-base characterization before any clinical application.

articles.title: Framework for combined functional and computational assessment of variant pathogenicity in the sodium leak channel NALCN.
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The sodium leak channel nonselective (NALCN) is the pore-forming channel component of the NALCN channelosome. This protein complex generates a depolarizing sodium leak in various tissues and contributes to respiratory and circadian rhythms, locomotion, and sleep. De novo and inherited variants of NALCN can lead to severe developmental syndromes referred to as CLIFAHDD and IHPRF1, respectively. Although variants of uncertain significance (VUS) have been studied in heterologous expression systems before, there is no generally accepted framework for how to assess or predict variant pathogenicity.

METHODS: We functionally and computationally characterize 19 VUS detected in CLIFAHDD and IHPRF1 patients to establish a robust analysis to classify suspected disease-causing variants. Specifically, we employ multiple parameters derived from two-electrode voltage-clamp electrophysiology recordings and predicted protein stability and conservation scores.

RESULTS: We show that this approach is capable of distinguishing benign common variants from both gain- and loss-of-function (GoF/LoF) variants. Additionally, our work provides insight into the molecular mechanism underlying specific variants and the unusual propensity of NALCN missense variants to result in GoF phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: We anticipate that this experimental and computational framework will aid assessment of variant pathogenicity of NALCN and other components of the channelosome in the future.

articles.title: Simultaneously leveraging individual- and summary-level external data in clinical trials.
articles.abstract: With the growing availability of external data (e.g., real-world data (RWD) and historical data), there is increasing interest in integrating external data into Randomized Controlled Trials (RCT), especially for rare diseases with high unmet medical needs where traditional clinical trials would be impractical and/or unethical. However, despite the increasing availability of external data, the level of detail varies across sources, as some provide individual-level patient records while others offer only aggregated summary statistics, often due to privacy and regulatory constraints. Most existing statistical methods focus on leveraging either individual-level or summary-level external data exclusively, with relatively few approaches addressing the simultaneous integration of both data types. Therefore, we propose a Bayesian method that integrates existing approaches for borrowing individual-level and summary-level external data to augment the control arm of RCT, enabling their joint use through Bayesian updating. Specifically, we combine inverse probability weighting (IPW) with Bayesian power prior for individual-level data, and the unit information prior (UIP) for summary-level data. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains type I error control at the nominal level and improves statistical power, while remaining straightforward to implement. Its flexible structure also allows the components of the proposed method to be replaced with alternative existing methods that leverage either individual-level or summary-level external data, thereby enabling the integration of both data types to effectively synthesize external information.

articles.title: Infection following therapeutic plasma exchange: A large-scale descriptive cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) is a procedure done for a broad variety of indications in which plasma proteins, including immunoglobulins, are removed. Current literature evaluating the risk of infection following TPE is limited to small single center studies, specific care contexts, or single indications.

METHODS: We conducted a descriptive retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX federated EHR network. Patients who underwent TPE were identified. Those with qualifying infection codes 30 days or 7 days prior to their TPE procedure were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of "any serious infections" within 30 days of the index TPE, with further analysis of five individual infection types. Opportunistic fungal infections were also assessed.

RESULTS: Among 22,993 patients, the composite 30-day proportion of infection following TPE was 6.3% (95% CI, 6.0%-6.6%), with the most common infections being sepsis at 2.2% (95% CI, 2.1-2.4), pneumonia at 2.0% (95% CI, 1.9-2.2), and urinary tract infection at 2.3% (95% CI, 2.1-2.5). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses using a 7-day washout and by era of index TPE. The opportunistic fungal infection proportion at 30 days was infrequent, 1.1% (95% CI, 1.0-1.2). Kaplan-Meier analysis did not show pronounced peri-procedural clustering.

CONCLUSION: These hypothesis generating findings in a large cohort of over 22,000 patients covering various indications across multiple care settings are roughly consistent with prior literature and indicate further studies with comparator groups are needed to clarify whether TPE independently increases infection risk.

articles.title: Mortality outcomes and their predictors in patients with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii bacteraemia: a prospective cohort study from South India.
articles.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) bloodstream infections (BSIs) are associated with high mortality, yet predictors of early mortality remain inadequately studied.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study of patients with CRAB-BSI from July 2021 to December 2023. Patients ≥18 y of age with CRAB bacteraemia were included. Clinical, microbiological and treatment data were collected. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of 7-d mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 154 patients were included. The 7- and 30-d mortality rates were 57.1% and 76.6%, respectively. Common BSI sources included hospital-acquired pneumonia (51.3%) and vascular catheters (29.2%). Only 37% received appropriate empirical therapy. On multivariable analysis, type 2 diabetes mellitus (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.35, p=0.031), inotrope requirement at BSI onset (aOR 3.11 [95% confidence interval 1.28 to 7.56], p=0.013) and higher tigecycline minimum inhibitory concentration in Vitek-2 (aOR 2.50, p=0.040) were independent predictors of early mortality. Vascular catheter-related BSI (aOR 0.25, p=0.003) was associated with lower early mortality. The association between appropriate targeted therapy (aOR 0.21, p=0.001) and mortality was interpreted cautiously because of potential survivor bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Early mortality in patients with CRAB-BSI is linked to host factors, severity of illness and antimicrobial resistance. Catheter-associated BSI, likely reflecting the feasibility of source control, was associated with improved outcomes. Appropriate targeted therapy was also associated with survival, which should be interpreted cautiously because of potential survivor bias.

articles.title: Predicting high-risk novel benzodiazepines: A surveillance study of novel benzodiazepine detections and a case series of bromazolam exposures in New South Wales, Australia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Novel benzodiazepines are increasingly detected in poisonings. Their relative toxicities remain poorly defined, complicating public health responses. Bromazolam has emerged in recent reports of severe poisoning. We sought a method to identify higher-risk novel benzodiazepines, and to describe the clinical effects of bromazolam exposures.

DESIGN: A prospective observational surveillance study examined time trends in laboratory-confirmed detections of benzodiazepines of interest (novels plus alprazolam) using police drug seizure data and a clinical surveillance program from January 2019 to December 2024. A case series described hospitalised patients with confirmed bromazolam exposure between January 2022 and December 2024.

SETTING: Population-based study in New South Wales, Australia.

CASES: All laboratory confirmed detections of benzodiazepines of interest in blood, urine or physical drug samples were included. Forty-eight hospitalised patients with confirmed bromazolam exposure were included in the case series, and eight additional hospitalised patients with alprazolam exposures.

MEASUREMENTS: Annual detections of benzodiazepines of interest in clinical and physical drug samples were recorded. Relative toxicity was estimated with a pooled risk ratio (RR) of clinical to physical detections for each benzodiazepine. A minimum clinical dataset described the demographics, clinical effects, drug co-detections, treatments and outcomes of bromazolam and alprazolam-related hospital presentations. Secondary analyses measured the relationship between clinical effects and bromazolam blood concentrations and opioid co-detection.

RESULTS: The median number of benzodiazepines of interest detected was 265/year in physical drug samples (range 230-301) and 16/year in clinical samples (range 11-36). Bromazolam was the most common novel benzodiazepine detected in clinical (52/118) and physical (382/1590) samples. Pooled RRs were highest for etizolam [RR = 1.84, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) = 1.39-2.43], bromonordiazepam (RR = 1.70, 95% CI = 0.74-3.92), flualprazolam (RR = 1.48, 95% CI = 0.50-4.39) and bromazolam (RR = 1.22, 95% CI = 0.85-1.73). In 2024, there were no detections of etizolam or flualprazolam in clinical cases, compared with bromazolam (n = 29; 80.6% of cases) and bromonordiazepam (n = 7; 19.4% of cases). Among the 48 hospital cases with bromazolam detected, severe outcomes were frequent, including coma (36/48), respiratory failure (34/48) and endotracheal intubation (25/48). Polysubstance use was common (47/48). Bromazolam blood concentrations were poorly predictive of clinical effects. Opioid co-detection was not associated with statistically significantly worse outcomes.

SUMMARY: The incidence of novel benzodiazepine detections in New South Wales, Australia, increased between January 2019 and December 2024. Bromazolam is a current concern due to increasing detections and severe clinical outcomes; however, polysubstance use likely contributed to clinical outcomes. Bromonordiazepam may be an emerging concern.

articles.title: AASLD AGA clinical Practice Guideline on management of primary biliary cholangitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care.

METHODS: The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations.

RESULTS: The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Determining the Optimal Treatment Strategy for Patients With Combined Aortic Stenosis and Mitral Regurgitation.
Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.

METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti-factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35-3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55-1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24-2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44-1.25]; P=0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25-4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38-3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84-1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28-4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

articles.title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification.

METHODS: We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55-39.30]; P=0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68-9.24]; P<0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19-5.34]; P=0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events (P=0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15-0.82]).

CONCLUSIONS: In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification.

articles.title: Association of Hemispheric Laterality With Neurosurgical Intervention in Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Posthoc Bayesian Analysis of ATACH-2 and ERICH.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemispheric laterality influences clinical management in stroke. Given the increasing enthusiasm for surgical management of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), we evaluated the association of hemispheric laterality with the likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention and subsequent 90-day functional outcomes.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis included 3477 patients with supratentorial ICH from 2 prospective studies: the ATACH-2 trial (Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage II), conducted at 110 sites in the United States, Japan, China, Taiwan, South Korea, and Germany (2011-2015), and the ERICH study (Ethnic/Racial Variations of Intracerebral Hemorrhage), conducted across 19 centers in the United States (2010-2015). The primary outcome was neurosurgical intervention (hematoma evacuation, decompressive craniectomy, or other craniotomy). Secondary outcomes included external ventricular drain placement, 90-day modified Rankin Scale score, and EuroQOL domains. Hierarchical Bayesian regression models estimating the association between ICH laterality and outcomes were adjusted for age, admission Glasgow Coma Scale, ICH location, ICH volume, and intraventricular hemorrhage.

RESULTS: Of 3477 patients, right hemispheric ICH was associated with a higher likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention (adjusted odds ratio, 1.65 [95% credible interval, 1.28-2.14]) and external ventricular drain placement (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% credible interval, 1.04-1.44]) compared with left hemispheric ICH. This association was directionally consistent across ICH locations, study cohorts, and prior specifications. Despite the lower rates of surgical intervention in left hemispheric ICH, there was no meaningful difference in 90-day functional outcomes in patients with left and right hemispheric ICH.

CONCLUSIONS: Right hemispheric ICH is associated with a higher likelihood of neurosurgical intervention compared with left hemispheric ICH, though 90-day functional outcomes remain similar between groups. Although these findings highlight a potential laterality-associated variation in neurosurgical intervention, residual confounding from unmeasured anatomic severity and family preferences cannot be excluded. Prospective studies are needed to delineate the explicit clinical and prognostic drivers of surgical decision-making to optimize treatment allocation in ICH.
