articles.title: Contemporary US Practice Patterns Regarding Anticoagulation and LAA Closure in ICH Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal secondary stroke prevention remains uncertain for patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Anticoagulation reduces ischemic stroke in AF but increases hemorrhage. Left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion is emerging as an alternative to anticoagulation, but few data exist on its safety in patients with ICH. Amid this uncertainty, little is known about US practice patterns in this scenario.

METHODS: We performed a study using linked electronic health record, pharmacy, and insurance claims data on >11 million patients at 29 US healthcare organizations, each with multiple hospital sites, in the TriNetX Linked platform. Validated International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes were used to identify adults with AF hospitalized for ICH during 2016 to 2024. To identify antiplatelet and anticoagulant prescriptions, we used RxNorm codes, a standardized drug naming system from the National Library of Medicine. LAA occlusion was defined using validated Current Procedural Terminology codes. Kaplan-Meier statistics were used to calculate cumulative rates of therapy utilization from discharge through 5 years. We created 3 mutually exclusive treatment groups with censoring at LAA occlusion for analyses of antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy and at anticoagulation for analyses of antiplatelet therapy.

RESULTS: We identified 2276 patients with AF hospitalized with ICH. Their mean age was 65.4 (±12.8) years, 40.6% were female, median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 5 (interquartile range, 5-6), 19.6% had Medicare, 26.9% received an anticoagulant prescription within 90 days before ICH, and half were discharged home or to an acute rehabilitation facility. Cumulative 5-year rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%-64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%-46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%-7.6%) for LAA occlusion. LAA occlusion rates did not differ by index ICH date (P=0.88).

CONCLUSIONS: In a contemporary, multicenter US cohort of patients with ICH and AF, 60% were prescribed anticoagulation after discharge, and the remainder were mostly treated with antiplatelet therapy only. These findings suggest widespread use of different secondary stroke prevention strategies in patients with AF and ICH.

articles.title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information.

CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

articles.title: Bioadaptor Implantation in Complex Calcified Coronary Lesions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcified coronary lesions remain among the most challenging subsets in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) because of their morphological complexity. Restoring physiological vasomotion and vascular remodeling is an emerging goal in PCI.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with severely calcified coronary lesions treated with PCI. Lesion preparation included rotational atherectomy was performed in 2 of 3 cases, followed by implantation of a bioadaptor-a sirolimus-eluting cobalt-chromium hybrid stent system. In 1 case, a super high-pressure OPN balloon was used for postdilatation. Six-month follow-up angiography showed favorable outcomes with sustained vessel patency in all cases.

DISCUSSION: This is the first case series reporting bioadaptor use in heavily calcified coronary lesions. Adequate lesion preparation is essential for procedural success and clinical outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In this case series, bioadaptor implantation in severely calcified coronary lesions was feasible, with favorable short-term outcomes at 6 months. In calcified lesions, more aggressive lesion preparation than for conventional drug-eluting stents may be required, as adequate calcium modification is a prerequisite for full device expansion and for realizing the bioadaptor's long-term functional benefits after uncaging.

articles.title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.

METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).

RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.

CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

articles.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.

RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.

CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

articles.title: Filling the Gap: A Multicenter Evaluation of Listeriosis and Mortality Predictors in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to characterize invasive listeriosis in Türkiye and identify predictors of in-hospital mortality. This multicenter retrospective observational study included adult patients with laboratory-confirmed Listeria monocytogenes infection from 26 centers between 2015 and 2024. Clinical, demographic, laboratory, and treatment data were collected. Patients were classified based on infection type. Univariate analyses were followed by multivariable logistic regression to determine independent predictors of mortality. A total of 129 patients were included (mean age 62.1 ± 16.9 years; 65.9% male). The in-hospital mortality rate was 54.8%. Deceased patients were older and had more frequent comorbidities. Bacteremia without central nervous system involvement was more common among nonsurvivors. Lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores, lower platelet counts, higher CRP levels, and more frequent blood culture positivity were observed in patients who died. In multivariable analyses, higher GCS scores were associated with lower odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.71 per 1-point increase, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.86), as were higher platelet counts (adjusted OR: 0.94 per 10,000/µL increase, 95% CI: 0.89-0.99), whereas blood culture positivity was associated with higher odds of mortality (adjusted OR: 3.19, 95% CI: 1.04-9.82). Invasive listeriosis is associated with high mortality in Türkiye. Admission GCS score, platelet count, and blood culture positivity were independently associated with mortality and may help identify patients at increased risk of death.

articles.title: Dihydromyricetin as an Antibiofilm and Antibacterial Agent Against Streptococcus agalactiae.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus) is a leading causative agent of sepsis, pneumonia and meningitis in neonates and is also a major pathogen responsible for bovine mastitis, posing a substantial threat to food safety and public health via the dairy production chain. The ability of S. agalactiae to form biofilms in the host enhances its resistance to conventional antibiotics and host immune defenses, thereby contributing to persistent and chronic infections. This study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial, antibiofilm, and combined antibacterial effects of dihydromyricetin (DMY) against the S. agalactiae strain GBS2 isolated from bovine mastitis. DMY exhibited significant antibacterial activity against GBS2, with a minimum inhibitory concentration and minimum bactericidal concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. Crystal violet staining and confocal laser scanning microscopy analyses demonstrated that DMY effectively inhibited and disrupted biofilm formation, resulting in looser and less dense biofilm structures compared to untreated controls. Furthermore, reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) results revealed that DMY modulated the transcript levels of biofilm-associated genes (csrR, srtA, fbsC, cpsE, and luxS). Additionally, DMY markedly potentiated the antibacterial effect of penicillin G, ciprofloxacin, oxacillin, and vancomycin. These findings suggest that DMY could serve as a natural antibiofilm agent for controlling S. agalactiae contamination in the dairy industry, thereby contributing to the prevention of foodborne infections and reducing reliance on conventional antibiotics.

articles.title: The Development and Preliminary Testing of a Dyadic Brief Shared Decision-Making and Motivation Interviewing Intervention for Early Adolescents with Asthma and Their Caregivers.
articles.abstract: Introduction:Shared decision-making (SDM) interventions have been shown to improve asthma control in adults but are less studied in pediatric-caregiver dyads. Because asthma imposes a disproportionate burden on Black and Hispanic adolescents, we adapted an adult asthma SDM intervention to minoritized dyads.Materials and Methods:Focus groups informed adaptation of the intervention. Feasibility, for example, intervention fidelity, and clinical outcomes, for example, effect of the active intervention on shared decision-making (SDM-9) scores and Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ) scores were assessed. Post-trial interviews assessed acceptability of study components based on implementation metrics.Results:Nine focus groups were conducted with 25 adolescents (36% female; 84% Hispanic; mean age = 12.7 years) and 20 caregivers (95% female; 90% Hispanic; mean age = 39.8 years) to adapt the intervention to dyads. Sixty adolescents (aged 10-14 years; 53% female; 77% Hispanic; mean age = 11.3 years, caregivers (90% female; 77% Hispanic; mean age = 39.4 years), and dyads were enrolled in the trial. Clinician interventionists (n = 7) were randomized to the active SDM or dose-matched attention control condition. Feasibility was demonstrated by high fidelity to intervention delivery, high retention of subjects, and high rates of data collection. No outcomes were significant for example, ACQ: β = 0.15, 95% confidence interval -0.22, 0.51, P = 0.43, although adolescents in the active arm reported higher SDM scores relative to controls (β = 3.35 P = 0.14). Adolescents, caregivers, and clinicians completing posttrial interviews found the study acceptable.Discussion:The intervention was feasible and acceptable. Although no significant health improvements were detected, targets for future refinements, for example, in-person-only intervention delivery and enrollment of younger children, warrant testing to determine if a dyadic SDM may be a useful patient-centered strategy for underserved pediatric populations.Contribution to the Literature:While an SDM intervention was feasible and acceptable, refinements are needed to translate SDM improvements to behavior change that impact asthma outcomes.

articles.title: Predictors of recurrent stroke among patients with lacunar stroke receiving intensive blood pressure control: a secondary analysis of the secondary prevention of small subcortical strokes trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) lowering to <130 mm Hg is recommended in contemporary secondary stroke prevention guidelines; however, it did not significantly reduce overall recurrent ischemic stroke in the Secondary Prevention of Small Subcortical Strokes (SPS3) trial. In this post hoc secondary analysis of participant-level SPS3 trial data, we sought to identify baseline predictors of recurrent ischemic stroke among patients with lacunar stroke assigned to the lower SBP target in SPS3.

METHODS: This post hoc secondary analysis included SPS3 participants randomized to the lower SBP target (<130 mm Hg). The primary outcome was centrally adjudicated recurrent ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Candidate predictors were evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 1501 participants (41.1% aged ≥ 65 years; 60.8% were men), 120 (8.0%) experienced recurrent ischemic stroke over a median follow-up of 3.49 years (interquartile range, 1.80-5.08), corresponding to an incidence rate of 2.43 events per 100 person-years. In unadjusted comparisons, recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with diabetes mellitus (44.2% vs 34.2%; p = .036), coronary artery bypass grafting/coronary stent (9.2% vs 4.1%; p = .018), Black race (24.2% vs 14.4%; p = .007), elevated serum creatinine (14.2% vs 7.7%; p = .022), aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (44.2% vs 28.5%; p < .001), large-vessel atherosclerosis (29.3% vs 17.9%; p = .004), and lower prevalence of a subcortical qualifying stroke (21.7% vs 46.1%; p < .001). In multivariable analysis, aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.14-2.50; p = .009) and large-vessel atherosclerosis (HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.08-2.413; p = .020) were independently associated with recurrence. Randomization to aspirin plus clopidogrel was not associated with recurrent ischemic stroke (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.75-1.57; p = .661).

CONCLUSIONS: In SPS3 participants assigned to intensive SBP control, 8.0% experienced recurrent ischemic stroke. Aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke and large-vessel atherosclerosis remained independent predictors of recurrence. These findings may help identify patients who require preventive strategies beyond intensive SBP lowering.

articles.title: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

articles.title: Glycerine drives acute lung-function impairment and airway inflammation after e-cigarette aerosol exposure in mice.
articles.abstract: Electronic cigarettes generate an aerosol by heating an e-liquid based on propylene glycol (PG) and/or glycerin (VG), with or without nicotine and flavourings. Their acute respiratory effects, particularly with respect to asthma, remain poorly defined. We exposed ovalbumin-sensitised female BALB/c mice, which were subsequently challenged with ovalbumin ('asthmatic') or saline ('non-asthmatic'), to one of four e-cigarette aerosols (PG or VG, each with 0 or 12 mg/mL nicotine) for 30 s. Airway resistance (Raw), tissue damping (G) and tissue elastance (H) were measured once/minute for 60 min using the forced oscillation technique. A second e-cigarette aerosol was given at the 30-min mark. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was taken for assessment of cellular inflammation. Group sizes were 4-9 mice (n = 53 for lung mechanics and 57 for BAL). All aerosols acutely increased Raw, G and H, and excipient was the dominant determinant. VG produced substantially larger increases than PG across most parameters and exposures (P < 0.0001, except airway resistance after the first exposure, P = 0.0569), responses approximately doubled after a second exposure, and allergic sensitisation augmented the repeated-exposure mechanical response. Nicotine was not required for these effects and, where significant, attenuated them. In BAL, granulocytic inflammation was confined to asthmatic mice and was greater with VG than PG. Acute e-cigarette aerosol exposure is not innocuous; e-liquid composition, especially the excipient, is a key determinant of acute respiratory effects independent of nicotine.

articles.title: Changes in the apoptotic index, along with gene and protein expression levels, in splenomegaly due to portal vein stenosis in rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The spleen is an important peripheral immune organ, and splenomegaly (SM) is a common complication of portal hypertension. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying splenic apoptosis remain poorly understood.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A portal vein stenosis-induced SM model was established in Sprague-Dawley rats, using a sham-operated (SO) group as the control. Apoptotic changes in splenic tissue cells were evaluated using the terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay, immunohistochemistry staining, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) analysis, and western blot analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with the SO group, the SM group had a significantly higher proportion of apoptotic cells and higher mRNA expression levels of the pro-apoptotic Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9 genes, whereas the proportion of apoptotic cells and mRNA expression levels of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 were significantly lower in the SM group. The protein expression levels of pro-apoptotic Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9 were significantly increased in the SM group compared with the SO group. Transmission electron microscopy imaging revealed that macrophages of rats with SM had swollen mitochondria, marginated chromatin, and pyknotic nuclei.

CONCLUSION: In rat SM, the concurrent activation of pro-apoptotic pathways and anti-apoptotic pathways leads to increased cell apoptosis. This suggests that an imbalance in the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio promotes apoptosis through the mitochondrial pathway.

articles.title: One-Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited.

AIMS: We compared 1-year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non-ACS patients.

METHODS: The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non-ACS patients.

RESULTS: From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non-ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST-segment elevation MI, 33.9% non-ST-segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post-procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow-limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non-ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non-ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06-3.17, p = 0.03). All-cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13-3.75, p = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year TLF and all-cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non-ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real-world clinical settings.

REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.

articles.title: Unrecognised acute appendicitis presenting as sudden unexpected death: A forensic case report.
articles.abstract: Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency in children. While typically presenting with abdominal pain localised to the right iliac fossa, fever and gastrointestinal symptoms, young children may exhibit atypical or delayed manifestations. Failure to recognise these subtle presentations can result in rapid progression to life-threatening complications.

articles.title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier.
articles.abstract: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

articles.title: Invasive fungal diseases in immunocompetent adults: emerging patterns and clinical challenges.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) have traditionally been regarded as complications of classical immunosuppression. However, IFDs are increasingly recognized in adults who are apparently immunocompetent or non-neutropenic, particularly in the setting of severe viral pneumonia, critical illness, diabetes, structural lung disease, surgery, trauma or burns, injection or inhalational drug use, invasive devices, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and previously unrecognized immune dysregulation.

OBJECTIVE: This narrative review summarizes emerging patterns and clinical challenges of IFD in apparently immunocompetent adults, integrating invasive molds, endemic dimorphic fungi, and invasive yeasts.

KEY OBSERVATIONS: The current landscape includes influenza- and COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis, COVID-19-associated mucormycosis, acute invasive mold disease in critically ill patients, tissue-injury- and trauma-associated mold infections, severe endemic mycoses after relevant environmental exposure, and an expanding spectrum of invasive yeasts. The label "immunocompetent" often conceals situational immune dysfunction or an undiagnosed inborn or acquired immune defect. Cohort data are available for several non-classical host groups, whereas evidence for truly healthy adults remains dominated by small series and case reports.

CONCLUSION: In adults without classical immunosuppression, IFD should be suspected when clinical deterioration occurs in the setting of acute illness, disruption of skin or mucosal barriers, indwelling catheters, healthcare exposure, unusual clinical syndromes, relevant geographic exposure, or unrecognized immune defects.

articles.title: Causal inference in oral health research: Beyond statistical significance toward a causal framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral health research has adopted sophisticated statistical methods, yet studies routinely present adjusted associations as causal effects. The problem is not statistical competence but the absence of explicit causal reasoning. This commentary proposes a principled framework for causal reasoning in oral health research.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative synthesis of foundational and recent literature on causal inference, drawing on texts describing the potential outcomes and counterfactual frameworks, the ICH E9(R1) regulatory addendum on estimands, study design, directed acyclic graphs, and recent applications of causal methods in oral health research; recurring principles were organized into a sequential four-pillar framework, illustrated throughout with a worked example examining periodontal treatment and cardiovascular disease.

RESULTS: First, the question is framed through abductive reasoning and translated into a precisely defined estimand. Second, study design is aligned with that estimand by specifying the population, exposure contrast, and time origin so that the data reflect the intended causal comparison. Third, counterfactual reasoning and directed acyclic graphs clarify the conditions under which causal conclusions are warranted, guiding principled adjustment. Fourth, estimation and inference are used to evaluate evidence for the estimand, and results are interpreted with explicit attention to the assumptions required for causal claims CONCLUSION: We propose a cultural shift in oral health research where causal effects are precisely defined, identification assumptions are explicitly defended, and structural uncertainties are acknowledged. This framework reveals that statistical sophistication cannot substitute for careful causal reasoning. Advanced methods such as multivariable regression, propensity scores, and machine learning can allow robust estimation of causal effects but do not replace the need for a prior causal reasoning and identification assumptions. The question is not whether analyses are statistically correct, but whether causal effects are well-defined and assumptions are explicit. Applying this framework would make causal assumptions transparent, acknowledge uncertainty inherent in observational research, and clarify when experimental designs become necessary.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: This commentary argues that oral health research has a fundamental problem: studies use sophisticated statistics but still present associations as if they were causal findings. Better math alone doesn't fix flawed reasoning. The authors propose a four-pillar framework to address this. First, researchers should use abductive reasoning to frame a precise causal question that specifies the exposure, population, outcome, and comparison of interest. Second, study design should be aligned to that question. Third, causal assumptions must be made explicit using counterfactual thinking and directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), which clarify confounders, mediators, and colliders. Finally, statistical estimation and inference should come last, quantifying uncertainty about a pre-specified causal quantity, not generating causal meaning on their own. The bottom line: no statistical method, however advanced, can substitute for explicit causal reasoning. The real question in oral health research is not whether the analysis is statistically correct, but whether the causal effect is clearly defined and the underlying assumptions are honestly defended.

articles.title: The Efficacy of Trocar-Assisted Percutaneous Abscess Drainage for Patients with Severe Acute Pancreatitis Complicated by Infected Pancreatic Necrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Traditional percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD) does not always achieve satisfactory therapeutic effects in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) complicated by infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN). We modified the conventional PCD therapy by employing Trocar-assisted percutaneous abscess drainage (TA-PAD) combined with double-lumen catheter negative-pressure irrigation and drainage for the treatment of patients with SAP with IPN and compared its efficacy with that of traditional PCD.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from patients with SAP complicated with IPN at Jinling Hospital between June 2018 and February 2024. Patients were divided by procedure into two treatment groups: the modified TA-PAD with negative-pressure irrigation group and the conventional PCD group, for comparative efficacy analysis.

RESULTS: Among the 74 patients, Comparison between the TA-PAD (n = 48) and PCD (n = 26) groups confirmed that TA-PAD was superior, yielding a lower mortality rate (12.5% vs. 34.6%, p = 0.024), shorter hospitalization (p = 0.006), reduced costs (p = 0.01), fewer re-interventions (20.8% vs. 57.7%, p < 0.001), and fewer catheters required (1 (1-2) vs. 2 (1-2.25), p = 0.029). Furthermore, the TA-PAD group demonstrated more significant improvements in infection markers, including body temperature, C-reactive protein, and white blood cell count.

CONCLUSION: The modified TA-PAD procedure combined with double-lumen catheter negative-pressure irrigation and drainage significantly outperformed conventional PCD in treating patients with SAP with IPN. The study demonstrates significant reductions in mortality, hospital stay, treatment costs, and procedural burden, alongside a superior resolution of infection markers within one week post-intervention.

articles.title: Pah in the era of obesity: navigating phenotypes of pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vasculopathy whose phenotype has shifted over the decades from young women to older patients with cardiometabolic comorbidities. Obesity is among the most prevalent and clinically consequential of these comorbidities, affecting 24-40% of patients in contemporary PAH registries.

AREAS COVERED: We review the epidemiology of obesity and its impact on PAH; the definition of obesity and the limitations of body mass index; the effects of obesity on adipose, cardiovascular and respiratory systems; its association with health disparities; the clinical approach to the patient with obesity and suspected pulmonary hypertension (PH), including right heart catheterization with provocative maneuvers and esophageal manometry; comorbid conditions and the obesity paradox; and management, including weight loss, PAH-specific therapy, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and sleep-disordered breathing. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE was performed for articles published from database inception to September 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: Obesity has implications in the origin, symptoms, diagnosis and management of PH. Accurate characterization of PH in obese patients depends first on measuring and reporting pressures that reflect true transmural hemodynamics. Incretin-based therapy and activin signaling inhibition are promising therapeutic directions, but dedicated trials in patients with obesity and pulmonary hypertension are needed.

articles.title: scTraitReg: a single-cell multi-omic database of trait-relevant transcription factor eRegulons.
articles.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) identify loci associated with human diseases and disease-related traits, but the regulators and cellular contexts linked to these signals remain difficult to resolve. We present scTraitReg, a database of trait-relevant transcription factor (TF) eRegulons-TFs with their target genes and linked cis-regulatory regions-at single-cell resolution. scTraitReg integrates 655 sets of curated GWAS summary statistics covering 122 Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) disease terms with 111 human single-cell multi-omic datasets profiling RNA and chromatin accessibility in the same cells. The resource spans 34 tissues, 252 cell types, 2 081 538 cells, and 2208 curated GWAS-single-cell analysis pairs. Across these analyses, it contains 2 840 939 TF-cell-type records for 886 regulators; 67 666 records met all three criteria-cell-type specificity, genetic relevance, and the trait-associated regulon score-and were included as candidate trait-relevant eRegulon records. Each record links to the TF-target regulatory network with its cis-regulatory regions, cell-type-resolved evidence, per-cell regulon module scores, and target-gene enrichment, all available as downloadable tables. Users can search by disease, tissue, cell type, or regulator and examine these associations through interactive visualizations. scTraitReg thus provides a searchable and reusable resource linking genetic associations to cell-type-specific regulatory programs, and is freely available at https://www.sctraitreg.bio/.

articles.title: Hospital Specialization and Geographic Access as Determinants of Pediatric Emergency Mortality: A Nationwide Multilevel Study in South Korea.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine individual, hospital, and community-level determinants of in-hospital mortality-defined as death during the emergency department visit or after hospitalization at the same hospital-among critically ill pediatric emergency patients in South Korea.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the National Emergency Department Information System, comprising 26,206 pediatric patients (aged ≤18 y, triage levels 1 to 2) at emergency medical centers in 2021, using multilevel logistic regression. The null model confirmed substantial between-hospital [intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)=0.17] and between-community (ICC=0.01) variation, justifying the multilevel approach.

RESULTS: Overall, in-hospital mortality was 2.3%. At the individual level, compared with self-transport, patients arriving by 119 ambulance (OR=2.73, 95% CI: 1.85-4.05) and private ambulance patients (OR=3.14, 95% CI: 1.72-5.73) had higher odds. Intentional and unintentional injuries showed 2.06-fold and 2.97-fold higher odds versus noninjury, respectively. Consciousness level showed a dose-response association (coma: OR=228.64). Severe illness was associated with a 4.94-fold higher odds ratio. At the hospital level, higher critically ill proportions were associated with lower mortality (≥10%: OR=0.43), while hospitals with ≥45 combined pediatric and neonatal intensive care beds had higher odds (OR=2.43), likely reflecting case-mix concentration. At the community level, metropolitan cities showed higher odds (OR=1.64), while a higher Timely Relevance Index (TRI; percentage of residents accessing care within 60 min) was associated with lower mortality (≥95%: OR=0.55).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric emergency mortality was associated with factors across all 3 levels. Risk-adjusted performance metrics are needed for tiered systems, and timely geographic access supports distributed initial stabilization capacity.

articles.title: Online high-dose hemodiafiltration: a path towards improved clinical outcomes and green dialysis.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: There are concerns that online high-dose hemodiafiltration (HDF) is particularly resource-intensive and environmentally challenging. It has recently been suggested that HDF consumes more water and generates more plastic waste than expanded hemodialysis (HDx) using medium cut-off membranes. To further address this matter, we examined the available evidence on water use and plastic waste generation across high-flux hemodialysis, HDx, and HDF.

RECENT FINDINGS: Our analysis reveals that plastic waste generation is lowest with HDF and highest with HDx: modern HDF dialyzers weigh on average 36% less than MCO dialyzers, and online HDF requires no saline bags, together saving approximately 68-123  kg of plastic per 1000 sessions compared to HDx. Regarding water, online high-dose HDF may use less water than HD or HDx if dialysate flow is minimized/optimized (-8% vs. hemodialysis at standard European dialysate flow; -12.6% in a US setting). Individualization of dialysate flow reduces water consumption by a further 27.8% without compromising dialysis adequacy.

SUMMARY: Despite the suggestive 'high-dose' attribute in its name, online high-dose HDF with optimized dialysate flow may use less water and generates substantially less plastic waste than HDx. These findings challenge the view that HDF adoption is environmentally costly and indicate that HDF is a meaningful step towards green dialysis.
