articles.title: Hyponatremic-Hypertensive Syndrome as a Rare Manifestation of Renovascular Hypertension: A Case Series.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Hyponatremic-hypertensive syndrome is a rare but distinctive manifestation of renal ischemia caused by unilateral renal artery stenosis. It is characterized by severe arterial hypertension accompanied by hyponatremia, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and polyuria, resulting from complex interactions between the ischemic kidney and the contralateral functioning kidney. Owing to its rarity and potentially life-threatening course, early recognition and appropriate management are crucial. The purpose of this report is to highlight the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic outcomes in pediatric patients. CASE REPORT We describe the cases of 2 girls, aged 4 and 9 years, who presented with severe hypertension and electrolyte disturbances secondary to unilateral right renal artery stenosis. Both patients exhibited typical biochemical features, including hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and elevated renin-aldosterone activity. Imaging studies confirmed significant unilateral renal artery stenosis due to fibromuscular dysplasia, with renal asymmetry. In the younger patient, progressive clinical deterioration and complete renal artery occlusion necessitated nephrectomy, resulting in resolution of hypertension and electrolyte abnormalities. In the older patient, percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty was successful, leading to normalization of blood pressure, restoration of renal size symmetry, and sustained clinical remission at 1-year follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Hyponatremic-hypertensive syndrome should be considered in any child with severe hypertension accompanied by electrolyte disturbances, polyuria, and polydipsia. These 2 cases of girls with fibromuscular dysplasia underscore the importance of early recognition and individualized management strategies in pediatric renovascular hypertension. Prompt diagnosis and definitive treatment of renal artery stenosis, either by revascularization or nephrectomy when appropriate, can be curative and prevent severe morbidity. It is important to note that the course of HHS can vary among patients depending on their age, the severity, and the location of the stenosis.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes and Complications of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) in Adult Patients With COVID-19 in Central and Eastern Europe: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a rescue therapy for severe COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). International datasets do not consistently report Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) separately. We aimed to assess mortality, clinical characteristics, and complications of ECMO-treated COVID-19 patients across the CEE region. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a systematic review with single-arm meta-analyses of observational studies. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from January 2020 to August 2025 for studies reporting ECMO outcomes in adult (≥18 years) COVID-19 patients from CEE countries, with at least 10 ECMO-treated patients. Conference abstracts and overlapping cohorts were excluded. The study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251077593). RESULTS Twelve studies included 802 patients from 6 countries. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 65% (95% CI 0.57-0.72; I²=70.6%; 10 studies; n=691), and ICU mortality was 61% (95% CI 0.47-0.74; I²=85.8%; 7 studies, n=526). Country-level in-hospital mortality estimates were 54% for the Czech Republic and 76% for Poland but were descriptive because of the small number of studies and wide CIs. Mean pre-ECMO mechanical ventilation duration was 4.8 days (95% CI 3.7-5.8; I²=4.4%), ECMO duration was 17.8 days (95% CI 12.8-22.9; I²=79.8%), and ICU length of stay was 23.6 days (95% CI 7.5-39.7; I²=92.6%). Serious bleeding occurred in 40% (95% CI 22-61%; I²=85.7%). Certainty was very low for all pooled outcomes. CONCLUSIONS These CEE-specific estimates provide regional benchmarks, but substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty limit international comparisons and country-level interpretation. Standardized regional registries, prospective multicenter data, harmonized complication reporting, and long-term outcome assessment are needed.

articles.title: Associations between complication risk perception, gender role stress, and symptom management self-efficacy in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to examine the associations among complication risk perception, gender role stress, and symptom management self-efficacy in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and to identify factors associated with these constructs.

METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional study was performed at the endocrinology outpatient clinic of a hospital. The sample consisted of 500 Type 2 DM patients (250 women, 250 men). Study data were gathered through the Individual Information Form (IIF), Risk Perception Survey-Diabetes Mellitus Scale (RPS-DM), Symptom Management Scale for Self-Efficacy (SMSSE), Feminine Gender Role Stress Scale (FGRSS), and Masculine Gender Role Stress Scale (MGRSS). The data were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney test, Kruskal-Wallis H test, Spearman correlation coefficients, and binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: It was determined that both in women and men, it was found that as gender role stress increased, composite and environmental risk perceptions increased, and symptom management self-efficacy decreased (p < 0.001). According to logistic regression analysis, when risk knowledge increases in women, self-efficacy will increase (OR: 0.595), and composite risk perception will decrease (OR: 7.377). When composite risk perception increases in men, self-efficacy will decrease (OR: 16.933).

CONCLUSIONS: Complication risk perception and gender role stress were associated with symptom management self-efficacy among patients with Type 2 DM, with these associations differing by sex. Future interventional studies are needed to determine whether addressing these factors improves symptom management for self-efficacy. The findings may also help nurses recognize sex-specific differences when planning individualized patient care.

articles.title: Structural Valve Deterioration in End-Stage Renal Disease Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has revolutionized the management of aortic stenosis (AS), particularly for high-risk and inoperable populations. Nevertheless, patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who require TAVR present a unique clinical challenge. These patients tend to have a high burden of comorbidities, as well as chronic uremia, that purportedly predispose them to a higher risk of more frequent and rapid structural valve deterioration (SVD). This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the mechanisms, incidence, and clinical outcomes of TAVR SVD in the ESRD population. In doing so, we summarize the pathophysiology for SVD in this patient population, contextualize the reported rates of TAVR SVD, and summarize the limited literature describing the clinical outcomes for these patients. We posit that clinical management for ESRD patients must focus on proactive, multidisciplinary surveillance and the integration of predictive modeling to optimize the timing of rescue interventions. Finally, we underscore the importance of better understanding the underlying mechanisms that accelerate TAVR SVD in uremic conditions.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic Modeling and Dosing Simulations of Temocillin in Children With Urinary Tract Infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temocillin, active against most extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales, is increasingly considered a carbapenem-sparing option for Gram-negative infections. Despite a recommended pediatric dose of 25-50 mg/kg/d in 2 administrations, its pharmacokinetics in children remain ill characterized. This study aimed to characterize temocillin pharmacokinetics in young children with urinary tract infections using population pharmacokinetic modeling and to evaluate target attainment using Monte Carlo simulations.

METHODS: Eligible patients contributed 1-2 blood samples collected at different time points, providing coverage of the dosing interval through an ethically acceptable sparse sampling strategy. Total and unbound temocillin plasma concentrations were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and data were used for pharmacokinetic modeling. Probabilities of target attainment were calculated using Monte Carlo simulation.

RESULTS: Pediatric patients (6-34 months) hospitalized with urinary tract infection received temocillin at a dose of 25 mg/kg twice daily. Thirty unbound and 33 total plasma concentrations collected from 30 patients were available for analysis. A 1-compartment structural model including nonlinear protein binding was supported. Population pharmacokinetic estimates fell within the corresponding 95% confidence intervals and were consistent with bootstrap medians, supporting model stability. Clearance and volume of distribution were estimated at 2.81 L/h and 10.3 L, respectively. Interindividual variability of clearance was determined to be 21.2% in the population. Modeling predicted that the studied regimen would provide a >90% probability of target attainment against organisms with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≤2 mg/L when targeting 40% of the dosing interval with free-drug concentrations above the MIC (40% fT>MIC).

CONCLUSION: Although sparse sampling limits parameter precision, characterization of interindividual variability, and covariate evaluation, these data may serve as an exploratory reference to inform preliminary dosing considerations in this pediatric population.

articles.title: Unexpected Death in a Preschool Child: Forensic Assessment of Acute Myocarditis on Left Ventricular Hypertrophy.
articles.journal: The American journal of forensic medicine and pathology
articles.abstract: Myocarditis is an inflammatory disease of the myocardium with a highly variable clinical spectrum, ranging from mild or subclinical forms to severe manifestations, including heart failure, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. In this article, we report a case of sudden death in a 4-year-old child in whom autopsy and histopathologic investigations identified myocarditis developing on a substrate of left ventricular hypertrophy. Given the lack of pathognomonic symptoms in myocarditis, maintaining a high index of clinical suspicion is paramount for ensuring timely admission. Early diagnosis is crucial to initiating treatment before clinical deterioration occurs. Furthermore, implementing standardized and systematic autopsy analysis is essential to maximizing the diagnostic yield in cases of unexpected death in childhood. In the absence of a unified investigative framework and multidisciplinary approach, postmortem examinations risk remaining incomplete, potentially leaving critical pathologic findings undetected.

articles.title: Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database.
articles.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated for their predictive performance: Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), XGBoost and LightGBM. Additionally, we assessed the prognostic capability of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Model discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). To enhance model interpretability, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to elucidate the relative importance of predictor variables.

RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 7716 patients, with 1357 (17.6%) experiencing in-hospital mortality. Among the machine learning models evaluated, GBDT exhibited superior predictive performance achieving an AUC of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.769-0.814). This performance surpassed that of other machine learning algorithms and the conventional SOFA score. SHAP analysis provided valuable insights into the hierarchical importance of various clinical and demographic features contributing to the GBDT model's predictions.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning approaches in accurately predicting in-hospital mortality among ICU patients with sepsis and diabetes mellitus. These advanced analytical techniques outperform traditional scoring systems such as SOFA. The integration of SHAP values enhances model interpretability, potentially facilitating the adoption of these predictive tools in clinical practice. Further multi-center validation studies and prospective trials are warranted to confirm the generalizability of these results and to explore the clinical impact of implementing such models in diverse healthcare settings.

articles.title: Costs of caregiving after stroke: beyond the financial burden.
Exploring the application value of preoperative femoral artery and vein cannulation in redo cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the clinical value of preoperative femoral vessel cannulation in redo cardiac surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 106 patients who underwent redo cardiac surgery in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. According to the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) cannulation technique adopted, the patients were divided into the Femoral Cannulation group (n = 79) and the Traditional Central Cannulation group (n = 37). Preoperative baseline data, intraoperative CPB-related parameters, blood product consumption, and the incidence of postoperative complications were recorded and compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences in preoperative baseline data or intraoperative parameters between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Similarly, no significant statistical differences were found in postoperative mortality, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization rate, acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence, or cognitive dysfunction incidence between the two groups. However, compared with the Traditional Central Cannulation group, the Femoral Cannulation group had significantly lower intraoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion volume and a significantly lower incidence of major cardiovascular injuries (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In redo cardiac surgery, preoperative femoral vessel cannulation can significantly reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular injuries and the demand for intraoperative blood transfusion, which is worthy of promotion and application in clinical practice.

articles.title: When 2D is not enough: 3D transesophageal echocardiography revealing a multifenestrated atrial septal defect.
The contribution of LepA to virulence and host cell invasion in Salmonella Typhimurium.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: LepA is one of the most conserved proteins and is found in nearly all bacteria as well as in eukaryotes. Mutation of lepA increases antibiotic tolerance in Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and rifampicin-resistant clinical mycobacterial isolates. However, the physiological function and its role in virulence of LepA remain elusive, particularly considering that LepA is non-essential under laboratory conditions.

METHODS: We investigated the lepA gene of Salmonella Typhimurium for its role in bacterial invasion of host cells. Invasion assays using lepA mutants were performed in macrophages (J774) and epithelial cells (Caco-2 and HT29-MTX), both in the presence and absence of mucus. In addition, virulence gene induction, motility, and pathogenicity in a Galleria mellonella infection model were assessed.

RESULTS: The lepA deletion strain showed reduced invasion in all cell types regardless of mucus, indicating its essential role in the invasion process and in the initial survival within macrophages. Deletion of lepA also resulted in decreased induction of virulence-associated genes and reduced pathogenicity in Galleria mellonella.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide important insights into the molecular determinants of Salmonella Typhimurium virulence and contribute to a deeper understanding of the conservation of LepA across organisms.

articles.title: Glomerulonephritis before and after BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine rollout: biopsy-based trends, histopathological spectrum, and temporal associations.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: mRNA-based vaccines developed against the COVID-19 pandemic have been reported to trigger immune-mediated glomerular diseases in rare cases. However, it remains unclear whether these cases have a direct causal relationship with the vaccine or whether they result from the "unmasking" of latent pathologies. This study aims to compare biopsy-based proportions and the histopathological spectrum of glomerulonephritis (GN) before versus after the rollout of the Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT162b2) mRNA vaccine, and to explore temporal associations between vaccination/infection and GN presentation among biopsied patients.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study conducted at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital, renal biopsy data from the periods before (April 1, 2020- March 31, 2021) and after (April 1, 2021- March 31, 2022) mRNA vaccination were compared. GN diagnosis rates, subtype distributions, and the temporal relationship between symptom onset and vaccination/infection were analyzed. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify risk factors for GN development.

RESULTS: Among patients undergoing native kidney biopsy, the proportion of biopsies yielding GN was higher in the post-rollout period than in the pre-rollout period (70.5% vs 60.2%; biopsy-based OR 1.58, p = 0.026). However, in a temporal-proximity analysis based on the interval from vaccination to biopsy, the GN proportion among patients biopsied within 3 months of vaccination (68.5%) was similar to that of patients biopsied >3 months after vaccination or unvaccinated (67.6%) (OR = 1.04; p = 1.00). In the histopathological spectrum, the proportion of IgA Nephropathy (IgAN) increased from 16.5% to 26.2% (p = 0.040); exploratory subtype analyses suggested higher IgAN odds in the temporally proximate group (unadjusted OR = 2.57; p = 0.0129).

CONCLUSION: Our biopsy-based analyses suggest no higher odds of GN among patients biopsied within 3 months of vaccination compared with other biopsied patients, and the observed post-rollout changes may reflect diagnostic awareness and an unmasking phenomenon rather than a direct vaccine effect. The observed increase in IgAN diagnoses warrants further investigation in larger, population-based studies and should be interpreted cautiously given potential confounding and multiple comparisons.

articles.title: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) signaling in visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue: implications for obesity and metabolic disease-a narrative review with a structured literature search.
articles.abstract: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide is one of the principal incretin hormones involved in the regulation of glucose homeostasis, lipid metabolism, and adipocyte function. Increasing evidence indicates that its biological actions differ substantially between adipose tissue depots. The aim of this narrative review with a structured literature search was to summarize current evidence on the role of GIP in visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), incorporating preclinical, clinical, and genetic data. Animal studies have demonstrated that VAT is characterized by higher expression of the GIP receptor (GIPR) and greater sensitivity to the lipogenic and proinflammatory effects of GIP. Activation of GIPR in VAT promotes lipid accumulation, inflammation, and insulin resistance. Conversely, pharmacological blockade or genetic deletion of GIPR confers protection against diet-induced obesity and leads to improvements in metabolic parameters. In SAT, GIP exerts more heterogeneous and metabolically context-dependent effects that differ according to insulin sensitivity and obesity status. Moreover, under specific conditions, GIP may promote lipolysis in SAT, distinguishing its actions in this depot from those observed in VAT. These observations may help explain the efficacy of dual and triple incretin receptor agonists, including tirzepatide and retatrutide, which produce significant improvements in body weight and metabolic outcomes. Collectively, current evidence supports a depot-specific and context-dependent role of GIP in adipose tissue biology and underscores the therapeutic potential of targeting the GIP/GIPR axis in obesity and metabolic disease.

articles.title: Phase 3 Antifibrotic-Directed Therapy Outcomes in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Beyond FVC Decline.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phase 3 evidence for antifibrotic-directed therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) has expanded, but direct head-to-head trials are lacking. Forced vital capacity (FVC) decline remains the principal trial outcome, although it may not fully capture clinically relevant differences among therapies.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials of antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. FVC effects versus placebo were descriptively summarized using standardized 48-52-week estimates. All-cause treatment discontinuation and all-cause mortality were analyzed using placebo-controlled odds ratios. Sensitivity analyses assessed follow-up duration, background antifibrotic therapy, and trial-level consistency.

RESULTS: Ten trials including 5,386 randomized participants were included. Pirfenidone and nintedanib showed consistent reductions in FVC decline versus placebo. Inhaled treprostinil showed a favorable FVC signal in the combined TETON-1/2 evidence, largely as add-on therapy with background antifibrotic treatment. Without background antifibrotic therapy, several therapies showed directionally favorable but imprecise FVC effects, without evidence of equivalence. Nintedanib and inhaled treprostinil were associated with higher odds of all-cause treatment discontinuation versus placebo: OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.02-1.88) and OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.08-1.78), respectively. Pirfenidone was the only therapy associated with lower odds of all-cause mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.31-0.83), based on published pooled ASCEND/CAPACITY mortality data and the Japanese phase 3 trial.

CONCLUSIONS: FVC decline remains essential but may not fully distinguish antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. Integrating FVC effects, background therapy, treatment continuation, and mortality provides a cautious, context-dependent framework for interpreting expanding phase 3 evidence.

articles.title: Impact of phytosphingosine-enriched experimental toothpaste on dental enamel integrity: a combined in vitro and in situ investigation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the effects of a phytosphingosine-enriched toothpaste (PET) versus a commercial toothpaste on dental enamel using in vitro and in situ approaches.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In vitro, bovine enamel specimens were assigned to one of three brushing agents, artificial saliva, Colgate Total 12, or PET and subjected to simulated brushing (40, 280, 600, and 1,200 cycles), each representing the estimated brushing exposure for 1, 7, 15, and 30 days, respectively. Each group of specimens were evaluated at all time points throughout the 30-day period. Surface roughness and microhardness were measured. In situ, 14 volunteers used appliances containing enamel samples, brushed with the same toothpastes. Roughness, microhardness, and biofilm accumulation were assessed. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterized enamel surfaces post-treatment.

RESULTS: In vitro, PET showed lower surface roughness than saliva at 7 days (p < 0.05) and results comparable to the commercial product. Microhardness reduction was significantly greater with PET than with the commercial toothpaste at all evaluated time points (p < 0.05). In situ, no significant differences in roughness or microhardness were observed among groups (p > 0.05). However, PET significantly reduced biofilm compared to saliva (p < 0.05). AFM revealed smooth surfaces with both PET and the commercial product.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the PHS-enriched toothpaste did not adversely affect enamel integrity and resulted in significantly lower biofilm coverage on enamel, suggesting its potential for use in preventive oral care formulations.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study suggests that a phytosphingosine-enriched toothpaste is a promising option for preventive dentistry, as it resulted in lower biofilm accumulation on enamel without compromising enamel integrity. Given the central role of biofilm in the development of caries and periodontal disease, these findings provide scientific support for the future development of safer oral hygiene products as alternatives to conventional agents such as triclosan and chlorhexidine.

articles.title: The effect of telephone-based education and counselling on stoma adjustment and complication severity in individuals with a colostomy: a randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of telephone-based education and counselling on stoma adjustment and complication severity in individuals with a colostomy.

METHODS: A randomised controlled trial was conducted with patients assigned to the telephone-based education and counselling group (education group) or the control group receiving routine stoma care. Data were collected over a three-month follow-up period using validated measures of stoma adjustment and complication severity.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. At three months, the education group had significantly higher acceptance and total stoma adjustment scores and significantly lower complication severity scores than the control group. No significant between-group differences were found in anxious preoccupation, social engagement, or anger scores.

CONCLUSION: At three months, participants receiving telephone-based education and counselling had higher stoma adjustment scores and lower complication severity scores than those receiving routine care. Integrating structured nurse-led telephone follow-up into routine practice may strengthen continuity of post-discharge care.

articles.title: Patterns and predictive factors of hearing loss following microvascular decompression for hemifacial spasm: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Microvascular is a safe and effective therapeutic intervention for hemifacial spasm; however, its potential association with hearing impairment remains a concern. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, patterns, and risk factors of hearing loss following microvascular decompression in patients with hemifacial spasm. In accordance with PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science from inception to April 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients undergoing microvascular decompression for hemifacial spasm with preoperative and postoperative objective hearing assessments. Data on hearing outcomes and potential risk factors (e.g., brainstem auditory evoked response, cerebellar manipulation, and compressing vessels) were extracted. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model, and meta-regression was used to explore potential moderators. Eleven studies (N = 4,014) met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of permanent postoperative hearing loss was 2.60% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.13%-5.87%), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 87.4%). Subgroup analysis revealed a higher prevalence in prospective studies (n = 4; 5.29%) compared to retrospective studies (n = 7; 1.97%), although the difference was not statistically significant. Most studies concluded that brainstem auditory evoked response monitoring, particularly changes in wave V latency or amplitude, consistently predicted hearing impairment. Excessive cerebellar retraction (greater depth, distance, and duration) was significantly associated with an increased risk of hearing loss. Study-level data regarding the type of compressing vessel were insufficient and inconsistently reported across the included studies, precluding reliable meta-regression analysis. Permanent postoperative hearing loss was estimated to occur in approximately 2.6% (range: 1.1%-5.9%) (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.13%-5.87%) of patients undergoing microvascular decompression for hemifacial spasm, although the pooled estimate remained unstable because of substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 87.4%), limiting the precision of this estimate. The risk is primarily influenced by intraoperative cerebellar manipulation and brainstem auditory evoked response changes. Meticulous surgical technique and intraoperative neuromonitoring can reduce the risk of this complication.

articles.title: Provider Knowledge and Utilization of Anal Cancer Screening: A Single Institution Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.abstract: In 2024, the International Anal Neoplasia Society (IANS) published the first consensus guidelines for anal cancer screening, outlining recommendations for patients who are most impacted by anal cancer. This study assesses provider knowledge and practice of these guidelines. A 37-item cross-sectional survey was distributed electronically to physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants across ten specialties within a single health system. The survey assessed familiarity with anal cytology, guideline knowledge, screening practices, and barriers to screening. Descriptive statistics and bivariate analyses compared primary care providers (PCPs) to subspecialists. 87 providers completed the survey (62% physicians, 21% nurse practitioners, 17% physician assistants); 60% were Primary Care Physicians (PCPs) and 40% subspecialists. 55% had never heard of the IANS guidelines, and 76% had never performed an anal Pap test. Among the 70 providers completing the knowledge assessment, the median score was 10/20 (Inter Quartile Range (IQR) 8-12). Providers performed worst when identifying screening recommendations for solid organ transplant recipients (7% correct) and cisgender women with HIV (13% correct). No significant differences were found between PCPs and subspecialists across any measure. Qualitative responses identified scope of practice uncertainty (78%), lack of training (20%), and limited access to high-resolution anoscopy (9%) as primary barriers. Provider knowledge and utilization of anal cancer screening guidelines remain critically low across specialties. These findings highlight the urgent need for institution-wide education, standardized ordering pathways, and clear referral processes to improve screening rates.

articles.title: "It cannot depend solely on the parents"-professionals' perspectives on patient journeys of children with chronic conditions across health and social care in Germany.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Professionals in healthcare, social services and the education system are confronted with a growing number of children with chronic conditions. Complex treatment plans, care coordination and cross-system care needs result in additional demands on professionals. This study aimed to explore professionals' perspectives on the patient journeys of children with chronic conditions in Germany and identify opportunities to improve care.

METHODS: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews conducted from May 2023 to February 2024. A purposive sample of professionals working with children with chronic conditions (attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, developmental disorders, cerebral palsy, bronchial asthma, type 1 diabetes) was recruited from the health, social care, and education systems in Germany. Sampling was guided by an assessment of thematic saturation. Data were analysed using structuring qualitative content analysis.

RESULTS: Twenty-two professionals participated, including physicians (n = 7), therapists (n = 8) and social workers and counsellors (n = 7). Care was perceived as fragmented, difficult to navigate, and poorly coordinated across health, social care, and education systems. Key barriers included long waiting times, unclear care pathways, and limited interprofessional communication. Greater difficulties in navigating care and support were perceived among families facing socioeconomic disadvantage or language barriers.

CONCLUSION: Professionals perceived current care structures as insufficiently meeting the needs of children with chronic conditions, particularly where families face greater barriers to navigating services. Strengthening cross-system coordination and accessibility may improve patient journeys. Future research should examine how barriers vary according to socioeconomic circumstances and across stages of the patient journey and evaluate condition-independent approaches to improving care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register, ID: DRKS00032139, on 07 November 2023.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Research on patient journeys of children with chronic conditions has primarily focused on individual, often rare, conditions. • Evidence spanning multiple chronic conditions and the healthcare, social services, and education systems remains highly limited.

WHAT IS NEW: • Drawing on diverse professionals' perspectives, this study provides a cross-system, cross-condition view of paediatric patient journeys. • It identifies common barriers to care coordination and access across systems and diagnoses, highlighting actionable opportunities for integrated care.

articles.title: Biliary Giardiasis Presenting with Unique Image Findings of the Distal Bile Duct: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 79-year-old immunocompetent man was referred to our hospital due to elevated hepatobiliary enzyme levels. Imaging revealed shaggy homogeneous thickening of the distal bile duct with a common bile duct stone. Bile cytology revealed Giardia lamblia, leading to a diagnosis of biliary giardiasis. He had consumed well water contaminated with wild animal feces, which is considered a potential or suspected source of a G. lamblia infection. After stone removal and metronidazole monotherapy, the hepatobiliary enzyme levels normalized. Biliary giardiasis can occur even in immunocompetent individuals, and shaggy homogeneous thickening of the bile duct may be a noteworthy finding of biliary giardiasis.

articles.title: A Diphenhydramine Overdose Mimicking Encephalitis, Complicated by Acute Kidney Injury Associated with Anticholinergic Urinary Retention: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 26-year-old man presented with fever, an altered consciousness, tremor, mydriasis, tachycardia, and a dry oral mucosa and was empirically treated for suspected encephalitis. A rapid neurological improvement and anticholinergic findings prompted the reconsideration of intoxication. A family assisted room search revealed empty over-the-counter medication bottles, and he later reported ingesting 2.4 g of diphenhydramine at once. Acute kidney injury developed in association with diphenhydramine-induced urinary retention, and his urine output and renal function improved after catheterization. In encephalitis-like presentations with systemic anticholinergic signs, a diphenhydramine overdose should be considered, a collateral medication history should be sought, and urinary tract obstruction should be assessed if the renal function worsens.

articles.title: Secondary Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis after Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in the Setting of an Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Secondary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (SPAP) is rare and often results in poor outcomes; therefore, it is crucial to diagnose and treat it appropriately. A 23-year-old man who received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) 18 months before presentation was diagnosed with SPAP after allo-HSCT in the setting of an RSV infection. The patient's respiratory symptoms improved after treatment for RSV infection, and SPAP gradually improved during the follow-up period. This case suggests that SPAP should be considered in post-HSCT patients with persistent respiratory symptoms or radiological abnormalities in the setting of an RSV infection.

articles.title: Protective mechanisms against murine coronavirus infection in individual mice and its transmission between mice.
articles.abstract: Murine coronavirus, commonly known as mouse hepatitis virus (MHV), is a representative pathogenic virus in mice. MHV infection in mice is used as a model for viral infections and is utilized to analyze the mechanisms of protection and transmission. By establishing MHV-specific T cell clones and conducting adoptive transfer experiments in infected mice, it was demonstrated that T cells play a crucial role in the protection against MHV infection and that cytotoxic T lymphocytes induce apoptosis in infected cells and suppress viral production. Furthermore, studies using IFN-γ-deficient C57BL/6 mice demonstrated exacerbation of acute hepatitis, establishment of persistent viral infection, and subsequent death due to subacute granulomatous serositis resembling feline infectious peritonitis in cats, possibly in association with persistent infection and the emergence of immune-escape variants. In contrast, all MHV-infected IFN-γ-deficient BALB/c mice died within a short period due to acute fulminant hepatitis, indicating that genetic background differences significantly influence disease progression. Furthermore, in vitro studies demonstrated that BALB/c mouse hepatocytes are more susceptible to MHV than C57BL/6 mouse hepatocytes. Additionally, the mode of transmission of MHV was experimentally analyzed, and clearly correlated with viral growth in the intestine. Other studies have explored a wide range of topics in relation to MHV infection, including autoimmune responses, genetic susceptibility, and the maintenance of pluripotency in MHV-infected embryonic stem cells. MHV has also been utilized as a surrogate virus for COVID-19 research.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms in vascular cognitive impairment: A comparative study between CADASIL and sporadic small vessel disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are common in cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), but their patterns across genetic and sporadic forms remain incompletely characterized. We compared NPS prevalence, correlates, and caregiver distress in vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) due to cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) and sporadic SVD.

METHODS: Patients with VCI due to CADASIL or sporadic SVD were recruited from the Taiwan-Associated Genetic and Non-genetic Small Vessel Disease cohort. NPS were assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory. Clinically significant NPS were defined as a frequency multiplied by severity score of 2 or higher. Group differences were examined using logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Clinical and imaging correlates were analyzed separately for each group, and caregiver distress was evaluated using linear regression.

RESULTS: Among 245 VCI patients (100 CADASIL, 145 sporadic SVD), clinically significant NPS were frequent (72% vs. 63%, p = 0.133). Affective subsyndromes were more common in CADASIL (42% vs. 26%, p = 0.040). In CADASIL, dyslipidemia was associated with higher odds of NPS (adjusted OR = 4.63, p = 0.005), whereas anterior temporal involvement was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR = 0.29, p = 0.020). In sporadic SVD, dementia severity was the strongest correlate of NPS. Psychotic and apathy subsyndromes increased with dementia severity in both groups, whereas affective subsyndromes did not. Caregiver distress correlated strongly with symptom severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.42-0.70).

CONCLUSIONS: NPS are highly prevalent in VCI due to CADASIL and sporadic SVD, with affective symptoms particularly prominent in CADASIL.

articles.title: Thermal ablation in posterosuperior liver segments: Is this an indication to laparoscopic approach?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: Primary liver tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and colorectal cancer liver metastases, can be treated with liver thermal ablation (LTA). Current evidence comparing percutaneous LTA (P-LTA) and laparoscopic LTA (L-LTA) is inconclusive, and data on lesions in the posterosuperior (PS) liver segments are scarce. This study aimed to compare early local recurrence rates between percutaneous and laparoscopic thermal ablation, with a focus on PS liver segments.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included all consecutive patients treated with P-LTA or L-LTA between 2010 and 2024. The primary outcome was early local recurrence (≤ 6 months); secondary outcomes were subgroup analyses of HCC nodules and microwave ablation-treated nodules.

RESULTS: The study included 101 nodules in 69 patients. Overall morbidity was higher after L-LTA, whereas chronic liver disease was more common among P-LTA patients. Early local recurrence was significantly lower after L-LTA (7% vs. 25%), and this difference was accentuated in the PS liver segments (4% vs. 33%). Multivariable analysis identified the percutaneous approach and a lesion size > 3 cm as predictors of early local recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: L-LTA appears more effective in reducing early local recurrence, particularly in the PS segments, although P-LTA remains less invasive. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Recipient severity, not the donor operative approach, is associated with bleeding and transfusion after adult living donor liver transplantation: A fixed final-hemostasis-surgeon cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: The determinants of bleeding after living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) are difficult to isolate, because the surgeon who achieves final hemostasis varies. We characterized postoperative bleeding and intraoperative transfusion in a cohort with a single final-hemostasis surgeon.

METHODS: We reviewed 156 consecutive adult LDLTs (2016-2019) in which one surgeon performed biliary reconstruction, final hemostasis, and closure. The primary outcome was postoperative bleeding of Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ IIIa; intraoperative red blood cell transfusion was secondary. The source and the operative field of every event were determined from the operative records.

RESULTS: Bleeding occurred in 16 recipients (10.3%; median postoperative day 1.5). An identifiable source was found in all 16, and none was coagulopathic. Sources were in the recipient hepatectomy field (9), on the graft from vessels divided during donor hepatectomy (2), the closure field (2), a vascular anastomosis (1), and remote (2). No patient who bled died or lost the graft. On Firth penalized logistic regression, the estimates were largest for Model for End-stage Liver Disease (MELD) score (odds ratio 1.072, p = 0.062) and previous hilar surgery (odds ratio 3.133, p = 0.057). Transfusion was associated with MELD score (p < 0.001) and platelet count (p = 0.012), but not with laparoscopic donor hepatectomy (p = 0.954).

CONCLUSIONS: With the final-hemostasis surgeon held constant, bleeding arose from discrete anatomical sources rather than coagulopathy, whereas transfusion reflected recipient severity and thrombocytopenia. Neither was associated with the donor approach, although two events arose from graft-side vessels, and equivalence cannot be established.

articles.title: Equitable outcomes for critically urgent living donor liver transplantation in acute alcoholic hepatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: The justification for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) for acute alcoholic hepatitis (AAH) remains debated, particularly in urgent settings. We compared outcomes of recipients undergoing urgent LDLT for AAH versus other causes and identified predictors of mortality.

METHODS: We analyzed 317 adults in the Korean national registry who underwent urgent LDLT from 2017 to 2021 within seven days of emergency approval. AAH was defined using National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism criteria, excluding coexisting liver disease. Recipient, donor, and perioperative variables were compared between the AAH (n = 114) and non-alcoholic groups (n = 203). Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and predictors of death using Cox regression.

RESULTS: AAH recipients had more severe decompensation, particularly hepatorenal syndrome and ascites. One-, two-, and three-year survival rates were 90.1%, 86.5%, and 86.5% in the AAH group versus 83.1%, 79.6%, and 77.9% in the non-alcoholic group (log-rank p = 0.321). Overall, 66 recipients (20. 8%) died. Pretransplant ventilator support (hazard ratio [HR] 1.954), donor age ≥ 55 years (HR 3.134), and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality, whereas AAH did not (HR 0.765, 95% confidence interval 0.440-1.329; p = 0.341).

CONCLUSIONS: AAH did not independently predict mortality following urgent LDLT. Instead, outcomes were influenced by the recipient's pre-surgery condition and the characteristics of the donor and graft, suggesting that the procedure is justified when candidates are carefully selected.

articles.title: Acute heart failure in emergency settings.
articles.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

articles.title: Inflammaging in older patients with cancer undergoing surgery: implications for anesthetic management.
articles.abstract: Population aging has increased the number of patients aged 65 years or older with cancer undergoing surgery; however, chronological age alone does not adequately capture perioperative vulnerability. Inflammaging, a chronic low-grade inflammatory state that accompanies aging, may provide a biological framework for understanding the heterogeneity of perioperative risk. Senescent-cell accumulation and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype contribute to persistent inflammatory signaling, while age-related immune remodeling produces an "immune paradox" involving heightened inflammatory signaling despite impaired immune effector function. Surgical stress may act as a second hit in this pre-existing state by amplifying damage-associated molecular pattern signaling, neuroendocrine activation, and perioperative immune dysfunction. These changes provide plausible links to impaired antitumor immune surveillance, infection, pulmonary complications, delirium, and delayed recovery but do not establish an inflammaging-mediated causal pathway to clinical outcomes. In this review, established perioperative care is discussed along with investigational approaches to immune-inflammatory modulation. Relevant approaches include prehabilitation, pathways for enhanced recovery after surgery, opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia, regional anesthesia, individualized anesthetic selection, and selected pharmacological adjuncts. Preoperative assessment of sarcopenia, serum albumin, and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio may complement the assessment of physiological vulnerability but does not specifically quantify inflammaging. Future studies should evaluate biomarker-guided risk stratification and determine whether anesthetic interventions have different effects according to biological aging and inflammaging status.

articles.title: Whether to hold and what to measure: perioperative euglycemic ketoacidosis in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used for type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, including in patients without diabetes. Their ketogenic effects may be amplified perioperatively by fasting, surgical stress, and volume loss, resulting in ketoacidosis without marked hyperglycemia. Reported frequencies depend on ascertainment. Where ketones were measured against a diagnostic threshold, cohorts reported 0-1.8% in non-cardiac and mixed populations and 0-15.1% in cardiac surgery; one prospective study using a lower threshold (≥ 0.6 mmol/L) reported a far higher figure, and studies without ketone measurement reported surrogate metabolic-acidosis endpoints of 30-41%. None of these are comparable incidence estimates. Severe and fatal cases have been reported. Because plasma glucose may be normal, diagnosis requires attention to acid-base status and ketones. Quantitative blood β-hydroxybutyrate is preferred when SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i)-associated ketoacidosis is suspected; urine ketone tests may screen when blood testing is unavailable, but a negative result does not exclude it. Perioperative guidance remains inconsistent: some bodies recommend withholding SGLT2i for 3 days (4 days for ertugliflozin), whereas others support risk-stratified continuation in selected patients under specified fasting and dietary conditions. No randomized trial has compared continuation with discontinuation using perioperative ketoacidosis as an endpoint; observational evidence remains limited and conflicting, and ketone thresholds and monitoring intervals lack prospective validation. This review summarizes evidence on recognition, diagnosis, withholding, monitoring, and postoperative restart.

articles.title: Anesthetic considerations for pediatric liver transplantation.
articles.abstract: Liver transplantation is an established treatment for children with end-stage liver disease, acute liver failure, and selected metabolic and malignant conditions. Small circulating volume, limited thermoregulatory and metabolic reserve, interruption and recovery of hepatic function, and graft-recipient size mismatch affect perioperative care. This narrative review examined how these features inform preoperative assessment, anesthetic preparation, management across the operative phases, and recovery. Cardiopulmonary assessment identified associated anomalies and functional impairment that affect tolerance of induction and reperfusion. Intraoperative management combined assessment of blood loss, vascular tone, and ventricular function with serial evaluation of temperature, electrolyte and glucose levels, and hemostasis. Systemic hemodynamic measurements were interpreted alongside graft-specific inflow and outflow assessment, and fluid responsiveness was distinguished from a clinical need for fluid. Postoperative management included respiratory readiness, unresolved metabolic and circulatory disturbances, renal function, and analgesia. The evidence was interpreted according to population, design, and setting. Pediatric guidelines chiefly addressed candidate evaluation and postoperative care, while much intraoperative evidence came from small observational cohorts or extrapolation from pediatric intensive care and adult transplantation. The recipients with the smallest body size and children with acute liver failure, metabolic disease, or repeat grafts require further adaptation. This review emphasized preparation for predictable disturbances and reassessment after intervention, while avoiding the application of study-specific thresholds or protocols.

articles.title: Salicylic Acid-Induced MdTGA9-MdERF138-MdHCT Module Is Associated with Lignin Deposition and Improved Anthracnose Resistance in Autotetraploid Apple.
articles.abstract: Apple anthracnose, caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, severely threatens global apple production. Autotetraploid 'Hanfu' apples show stronger anthracnose resistance than diploids, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study identified a novel salicylic acid (SA)-regulated lignin biosynthesis signaling pathway that is closely associated with the enhanced resistance in autotetraploid 'Hanfu' apples. Autotetraploid apples accumulated higher endogenous SA levels, and the SA-responsive transcription factor MdTGA9 was markedly induced by both SA treatment and C. gloeosporioides infection. Mechanistically, MdTGA9 acts as a nuclear transcriptional activator to directly bind to the MdERF138 promoter and activate its expression. MdERF138 then transactivates the lignin biosynthetic gene MdHCT, thereby promoting lignin accumulation. Functional verification showed that MdTGA9 overexpression in apple calli, fruits and leaves significantly enhanced anthracnose resistance, and MdERF138 and MdHCT were confirmed as positive regulators of this resistance. Collectively, this study reveals a previously uncharacterized MdTGA9-MdERF138-MdHCT regulatory cascade that integrates SA signaling and lignin-based physical defense, which accounts for the enhanced disease resistance of autotetraploid apple. These findings provide valuable gene resources and a new molecular mechanism for disease-resistance breeding in apple.

articles.title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care.

METHODS: For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane's RoB tools.

RESULTS: We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22). Compared to usual care, DHIs supporting care integration had significant reductions in the odds of CVD events (OR: 0.74 [0.59, 0.92], df=5, p=0.02), but not in all-cause mortality or readmissions.

CONCLUSIONS: Although this review shows that DHIs supporting care integration were associated with reduced CVD events compared to usual care, the current evidence remains concentrated primarily on person-centred care integration, with limited studies evaluating broader dimensions of care integration at organisational and systemic levels. These findings highlight the important evidence gaps of DHIs in supporting more comprehensive and system-level integration in cardiovascular care. Further research is necessary to understand the influence of DHI modality and function on effectiveness of care integration.

articles.title: Strategy Sets the Scene: Genetic architecture of linalool resistance in Botrytis cinerea.
articles.abstract: Botrytis cinerea is a necrotrophic fungal pathogen that infects thousands of plant species. During infection, these diverse plant hosts produce different specialized metabolites that can inhibit pathogen growth and shape pathogen fitness. However, the genetic architecture of pathogen resistance toward individual host defense metabolites remains poorly understood. To address this question, we exposed 83 B. cinerea isolates to the metabolite linalool and quantified physiological and structural responses. Exposure revealed extensive phenotypic diversity across isolates. Population structure analysis using genome-wide SNP data showed little genetic subdivision despite diverse hosts and geographic location. Genome-wide association identified 98 genes of interest associated with membrane transport and stress response regulation. Genetic associations were stronger for morphological traits than for physiological traits, suggesting that hyphal architecture may have a complex genetic architecture contributing to linalool resistance. Together, these results establish natural variation in linalool response and provide candidate loci for understanding how generalist pathogens respond to host-derived chemical defenses.

articles.title: Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).

METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF).

RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF.

CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

articles.title: Early to mid-term outcomes of the custom-made 3D-printed triflange acetabular component (aMace) : the largest UK dual-centre study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Various techniques have been described to manage massive acetabular bone loss in revision hip arthroplasty. The aMace system has gained popularity due to its custom design, which aims to restore the hip centre of rotation and provide initial mechanical stability in cases of large, non-contained defects. This study aimed to assess the short- and mid-term outcomes of patients who underwent revision surgery using the aMace system.

METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of all patients who underwent aMace implantation at two revision centres between June 2013 and October 2022, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Data collected included demographic details, indications for surgery, bone loss classification, reconstruction details, reoperations, complications, and functional outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 52 patients underwent revision surgery, with a median follow-up of 51 months (IQR 36 to 72). The mean age was 72.9 years (40 to 87), and 86.5% (45/52) of patients were female. The mean BMI was 25.3 kg/m² (18.2 to 34.7), and the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists grade was III. Most patients had Paprosky type 3B 65.3% (34/52) or 3A 34.6% (18/52) defects. The main indications for revision were aseptic loosening 69.2% (36/52), infection 15.3% (8/52), and periprosthetic fracture 13.4% (7/52). Single-stage revision was performed in 76.9% (40/52), and 67.3% (35/52) underwent both cup and femoral component revision. Dual-mobility bearings were used in 76.9% (40/52) of cases, including 90% (36/40) of single-stage revisions, and 86.5% (45/52) had a metal-on-polyethylene articulation. No aMace components were revised. The 30-day mortality rate was 1.9% (1/52). The overall reoperation rate was 5.7% (3/52), primarily for periprosthetic femoral fracture and dislocation. Leg length discrepancy occurred in 9.6% (5/52). Two cases of sciatic nerve palsy were transient and resolved during follow-up. Statistically significant improvements in pain and mobility were observed (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Our findings support the aMace system for significant acetabular bone loss and pelvic discontinuity, with satisfactory mid-term outcomes and low complications. We recommend these procedures in specialist centres with multidisciplinary team involvement.

articles.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection - Advances, Challenges, and the Road Ahead.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

articles.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren's Disease.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.

METHODS: We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.

RESULTS: Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

articles.title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in stroke: the relationship between clearance failure and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Stroke triggers a complex secondary injury cascade, in which neuroinflammation plays a central role. The glymphatic system is a perivascular clearance network that facilitates cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and removes metabolic waste from the brain. Recent studies suggest that glymphatic dysfunction is not simply a consequence of stroke, but also contributes to disease progression. Impaired glymphatic clearance promotes the accumulation of damage-associated molecular patterns, inflammatory mediators, and toxic metabolites within the brain parenchyma, sustaining both innate and adaptive immune responses. At the same time, inflammatory signaling, immune cell infiltration, and vascular injury progressively disrupt perivascular architecture and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization, leading to further impairment of glymphatic transport. As a result, glymphatic dysfunction and neuroinflammation reinforce each other, contributing to cerebral edema, persistent inflammation, and neurological deterioration after stroke. In this review, we summarize current evidence linking glymphatic dysfunction to neuroinflammation in both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. We discuss the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying this interaction and preclinical therapeutic approaches that may help preserve or restore glymphatic function after stroke. A better understanding of the relationship between glymphatic dysfunction and neuroinflammation may reveal new therapeutic opportunities for improving neurological recovery after stroke.

articles.title: Whole blood hemolysis detection on the GEM® Premier™ 7000: performance across hemoglobin A, S, and F.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Point-of-care blood gas analyzers are essential in critical care settings but remain vulnerable to pre-analytical interferences, particularly hemolysis, which may lead to erroneous potassium results. The GEM® Premier™ 7000 incorporates an onboard hemolysis detection system based on multi-wavelength co-oximetry, allowing direct estimation of free hemoglobin in whole blood samples. This study evaluated the analytical performance of this system across different hemoglobin variants, including fetal hemoglobin (HbF) and hemoglobin S (HbS).

METHODS: Fifty patient samples undergoing routine arterial blood gas and biochemical testing were analyzed using the GEM® Premier™ 7000, and Atellica Solution analyzers. Experimental hemolysis was induced to evaluate the performance of the onboard hemolysis detection system. In a second step, hemoglobin overload experiments using HbA0, HbF, and HbS were performed in samples from 10 healthy volunteers to assess the robustness of hemolysis detection across different hemoglobin variants.

RESULTS: Experimental hemolysis significantly increased the hemolysis index and potassium concentrations measured on the GEM® Premier™ 7000, with median hemolysis index values rising from 1 to 6 and median potassium concentrations from 3.6 to 9.8 mmol/L (p<0.001). The GEM® Premier™ 7000 accurately detected increasing concentrations of free HbA0, HbS, and HbF throughout the overload experiments.

CONCLUSIONS: The integrated hemolysis detection system reliably detected clinically significant hemolysis in whole blood samples, supporting more reliable point-of-care blood gas testing.

articles.title: Planned biologic discontinuation in severe asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Biologic agents targeting IgE, IL-5/IL-5Rα, IL-4Rα, and TSLP have transformed severe asthma outcomes, yet it remains unresolved whether planned discontinuation is safe once sustained control is achieved. We therefore compared the risk of exacerbation after planned biologic discontinuation with that of continued therapy in patients with severe asthma.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched from inception to June 2026, and reference lists were hand-searched. RCTs and observational cohort studies were eligible if they enrolled patients (≥12 years) with severe asthma who achieved sustained control on an approved biologic (≥12 months) before planned discontinuation or tapering. Non-response-driven discontinuation and studies with ≤10 participants were excluded. The primary outcome was uncontrolled asthma or exacerbation within 12 months. Secondary outcomes included symptom scores, lung function, biomarker rebound, and resumption rate of biologics.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies were included (3 RCTs [n=897], 2 non-randomized comparator cohorts [n=77], 17 single-arm cohorts, 1 mixed-biologic registry [n=118]). Two randomized withdrawal trials, XPORT (omalizumab; risk ratio [RR] 1.59; 95% CI, 1.11-2.27) and COMET (mepolizumab; RR 1.29; 95% CI, 1.03-1.61), yielded a pooled RR of 1.36 (95% CI, 1.13-1.65; I² = 0%; moderate certainty). An exploratory pool adding DESTINATION (tezepelumab; RR 1.22; 95% CI, 0.88-1.68; nonequivalent comparator) yielded RR 1.32 (95% CI, 1.13-1.56). No eligible dupilumab or reslizumab study was identified. Biomarker rebound followed class-specific kinetics. Baseline eosinophilia ≥300 cells/μL and exacerbation burden predicted relapse, with no withdrawal syndrome.

CONCLUSION: Biologic discontinuation in severe asthma carries a moderate-certainty increased exacerbation risk. Because universal de-escalation criteria cannot yet be defined, decisions should be individualized, guided by eosinophil count, exacerbation history, remission duration, and biomarker trajectory, until prospective trial data become available.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420261440934.

articles.title: National trends in antimicrobial consumption in Nepal, 2016-2023: an ecological analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize class-specific national antimicrobial consumption patterns in Nepal from 2016 to 2023 and explore monotonic and linear temporal patterns, differences between the 2016-2019 and 2020-2023 periods, and the influence of selected high-consumption years.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective ecological analysis of five antimicrobial classes using annual national consumption expressed as Defined Daily Doses per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). Descriptive statistics summarized consumption; Mann-Kendall tests and linear regression explored temporal patterns; an exploratory period comparison assessed 2016-2019 versus 2020-2023; and sensitivity analyses assessed the influence of selected years.

RESULTS: Antibacterial agents had the highest mean consumption at 48.6 defined daily doses per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID). Considerable year-to-year variability was observed across antimicrobial classes, with limited evidence of sustained temporal trends over the short observation period. Anti-tuberculosis drug consumption showed evidence of an upward monotonic pattern in the Mann-Kendall analysis. However, this finding was not supported by a statistically clear linear trend and was sensitive to exclusion of the 2023 value. Exploratory comparisons of the 2016-2019 and 2020-2023 period showed imprecisely estimated differences in antibacterial and antifungal consumption.

CONCLUSION: National antimicrobial consumption in Nepal exhibited substantial class-specific and annual variation over 2016-2023. The short observation period constrains inference about sustained long-term trends. In particular, the apparent increase in anti-tuberculosis drug consumption warrants cautious interpretation given its sensitivity to 2023, rather than providing definitive evidence of a persistent increase.

articles.title: Low-Titer O+ Whole Blood Implementation in the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City and Tulsa: Significance, Success, & Sharing Lessons Learned.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Over 300 emergency medical services (EMS) organizations across the United States have implemented transfusion programs for traumatic injuries using packed red blood cells, platelets, plasma, or whole blood before hospital arrival. Beginning in December of 2022, the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City (OKC) and Tulsa began carrying low-titer O-positive whole blood (LTOWB) for adult patients in traumatic hemorrhagic shock, specifically those exhibiting elevated shock indexes. We aim to describe establishing our prehospital LTOWB program and its first two years of operations across OKC and Tulsa.

METHODS: We used an observational study design and retrospective descriptive analysis of patients receiving LTOWB by paramedic transfusion from the Emergency Medical Services Authority Ambulance Service, Oklahoma City Fire Department, or Tulsa Fire Department between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2025. Descriptive analysis and univariate logistic regression quantify the relationship of patient characteristics against survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge outcomes.

RESULTS: Penetrating trauma was the most common mechanism of injury recorded for patients receiving EMS LTOWB (71.6%). Following LTOWB transfusion, prehospital vital signs (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index) significantly improved (p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure improvement conferred 9.7 times greater odds of survival to hospital arrival (95% CL 1.6-58.6). Occurrence of prehospital traumatic arrest was significantly related to lower odds of survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge (OR 0.01 and OR 0.03, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Transfusion of LTOWB in a large, urban EMS system in the Southwestern United States confers a positive benefit to patients with measurable improvement in median systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index. Continuous review of cases and misses empowered our system in dynamic protocol adjustments to best meet our population's needs. Patients often had secondary deterioration during transit, illustrating that blood transfusion "bought" temporary time during transport of critically injured patients to definitive care.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated with Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using de-identified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary TKA between December 1, 2006, and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction (MI), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), venous thromboembolism (VTE), or pulmonary embolism (PE) were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative MI, DVT, VTE, and PE. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 RAs had a significantly lower risk of MI (25/11,246 vs. 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325-0.858). GLP-1 RAs use was also associated with a reduced risk of DVT (74/11,319 vs. 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533-0.966) and VTE (133/11,040 vs. 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617-0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of PE between groups (49/11,352 vs. 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580-1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 RA use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of MI, DVT, and VTE following TKA in this large, nationally representative cohort.

articles.title: Serum CitH3 and PTX3 levels for early prediction of acute respiratory distress syndrome following severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract:
