BACKGROUND: Prior literature has highlighted issues regarding the supply and adequacy of nephrologists to meet increasing demands. This study analyzed disparities in the supply, demand, and adequacy of nephrologists across the United States (US).

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis of nephrologists leveraged the Health Workforce Simulation Model from 2025 to 2037. Nephrologist workforce adequacy was defined as the ratio of supply over demand. Supply and demand were defined as the number of full-time equivalent nephrologists working and needed, respectively.

RESULTS: From 2025 to 2037, growth in the demand for nephrologists (15 780 to 18 860 full-time equivalents, 19.5% increase) exceeded growth in the supply of nephrologists (14 600 to 14 810 full-time equivalents, 1.4% increase). As a result, nephrologist workforce adequacy was projected to decrease over the study period from 92.5% to 78.5%. By 2037, non-metropolitan areas had lower adequacy of nephrologists when compared with metropolitan areas (24.8% vs 86.7%). The South had the lowest nephrologist workforce adequacy, and the Northeast had the highest (68.0% vs 106%). By 2037, the states with the lowest projected nephrologist workforce adequacy were Montana (28.6%), Alaska (33.3%), Idaho (40.0%), North Dakota (50.0%), and Wyoming (50.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Workforce shortages are anticipated in nephrology with notable disparities identified in non-metropolitan areas, the South, and identified states. Future work is needed to implement strategies that improve nephrologist workforce adequacy across the US.

articles.title: Renal steatosis in the tubulointerstitial compartment in primary glomerulopathies: biopsy evidence and correlation with disease severity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While dyslipidemia is a well-established systemic risk factor in glomerular diseases, the clinical and histopathological relevance of compartmental intrarenal lipid deposition in primary glomerulonephritis (GN) remains insufficiently elucidated. Recent evidence suggests that lipid accumulation may directly contribute to glomerular and tubulointerstitial injury via pro-inflammatory and oxidative mechanisms.

METHODS: In this single-center, cross-sectional analysis, we examined 31 adult patients with biopsy-proven primary GN-IgA nephropathy (IgAN), membranous nephropathy (MN), and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis/minimal change disease (FSGS/MCD)-diagnoses. Renal tissue specimens were subjected to Oil Red O staining to quantify lipid accumulation within tubular, interstitial, and vascular compartments. Clinical parameters and laboratory indices were assessed. Histopathologic correlations were performed using Oxford MEST-C classification (for IgAN) and Interstitial Fibrosis and Tubular Atrophy (IFTA) scoring.

RESULTS: Intrarenal lipid deposition was prevalent across compartments: tubular (84%), interstitial (74%), and vascular (61%). In IgAN patients, both the extent and morphology of tubular steatosis were strongly correlated with composite MEST-C scores (P < .01). In MN, tubular lipid burden was significantly associated with systolic blood pressure and proteinuria levels (P < .01). Notably, interstitial and vascular lipid accumulation demonstrated positive associations independent of systemic lipid levels. In FSGS/MCD cases, tubular steatosis correlated with both low density lipoprotein (LDL) and interstitial lipid scores (P < .01), whereas vascular lipid presence was linked to the degree of proteinuria (P < .05).

CONCLUSIONS: Intrarenal lipid deposition is a prevalent histological finding in primary GN and correlates with both structural injury and clinical disease burden. These findings support the hypothesis that local lipid accumulation may represent a pathophysiologically relevant biomarker of disease activity.

articles.title: From inference to proof: nanopore sequencing confirms zoonotic Neisseria Zoodegmatis peritonitis after cat bite-related contamination in a patient on automated peritoneal dialysis.
articles.abstract: Peritoneal dialysis (PD)-associated peritonitis caused by zoonotic pathogens is uncommon and diagnostically challenging. Neisseria zoodegmatis, a Gram-negative coccobacillus residing in the oral flora of cats and dogs, has been reported only once previously in PD-associated peritonitis, with zoonotic transmission inferred but unproven. We report the case of a 90-year-old patient receiving automated PD who developed peritonitis following cat bite-related transfer-set damage, with partial response to empirical therapy and subsequent relapse. Conventional culture and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry identified N. zoodegmatis, confirmed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing from colony isolates and PD effluent. Intermediate β-lactam susceptibility prompted escalation to carbapenem-based therapy. Third-generation nanopore sequencing demonstrated N. zoodegmatis as the dominant organism in PD effluent and identified the identical species in feline saliva, establishing molecular concordance. Sustained remission required strict environmental control. This is the second reported case of Neisseria zoodegmatis PD-associated peritonitis and the first one with molecular proof of zoonotic transmission, highlighting the selective role of long-read sequencing in complex or relapsing peritonitis, the need for antimicrobial reassessment after suspicion of pet-related contamination, and the importance of environmental intervention in preventing recurrence.

articles.title: Trigeminal neuralgia: a primer for dental practitioners.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a severe neuropathic facial pain disorder that is frequently misdiagnosed in dental settings, leading to delays in appropriate management and unnecessary irreversible dental procedures. This narrative review aims to synthesize current knowledge on the pathophysiology, diagnostic challenges, and management of TN, with particular emphasis on issues relevant to dental practitioners involved in the differential diagnosis of orofacial pain.

DATA SOURCES: A comprehensive literature search was conducted using the PubMed database, covering studies published between January 2000 and July 2026. Eligible sources comprised controlled clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected case reports addressing diagnostic approaches and therapeutic strategies for TN. Findings were synthesized thematically to highlight clinical relevance, emerging therapies, and persisting gaps in care.

CONCLUSION: TN remains a complex disorder with a substantial impact on quality of life. Accurate diagnosis relies on careful clinical history, recognition of characteristic pain features, and exclusion of odontogenic sources of pain, often requiring iterative assessment over time. Pharmacologic therapies, including carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine, remain first-line treatments, while surgical interventions-particularly microvascular decompression-offer durable relief in refractory cases. Dental professionals play a critical gatekeeping role in early recognition, exclusion of dental pathology, and timely referral to medical specialists. Optimal management of TN requires an interdisciplinary approach integrating neurology, neurosurgery, dental specialties, and psychosocial care to minimize misdiagnosis, avoid unnecessary dental interventions, and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Concurrent administration of BCMA and GPRC5D CAR T cells for advanced multiple myeloma.
articles.abstract: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)- and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D)-directed therapies have shown high efficacy in the treatment of relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, with multiple new immune therapies now approved. Preclinical studies have shown that the expression of BCMA and GPRC5D is heterogeneous in malignant plasma cells. We conducted a phase 1 dose-escalation trial of the BCMA chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy MCARH125 alone or in combination with the GPRC5D CAR T-cell therapy MCARH109 in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Patients were treated across 3 dose levels, with the primary objective of establishing the safety of concurrent infusion. We treated 15 patients across 3 dose levels, including 6 patients who received MCARH125 alone and 9 patients treated with the concurrent infusion of MCARH125 and MCARH109. One patient each with MCARH 125 alone and the coinfusion of MCARH125 and MCARH109 developed immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome. There were no instances of grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome or immune effector cell-associated neurologic syndrome. The overall response for coinfusion was 78%, with a median progression-free survival of 18.2 months. Correlative analysis suggests that antigen loss may be an important mechanism of resistance even with dual-antigen targeting, and we show, to our knowledge for the first time that expansion of 1 CAR population may limit expansion of the second population because patients treated with dual CARs had significantly less BCMA CAR expansion compared with patients treated with BCMA CAR alone, despite equivalent BCMA CAR T-cell doses at infusion. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05431608.

articles.title: Silver diamine fluoride versus conventional restorative treatment for dental caries in primary teeth of children: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early childhood caries remains a major public health burden, and silver diamine fluoride (SDF) has emerged as a minimally invasive option for managing cavitated lesions in primary teeth. This meta-analysis compared SDF with conventional restorative treatment for caries control in children.

METHOD AND MATERIALS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched from January 2010 to June 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing SDF (30% to 38%) with conventional restorative approaches, including atraumatic restorative treatment and glass ionomer-based restorations, in children with caries in primary teeth. The primary outcome was caries arrest or lesion inactivity; outcomes based solely on restoration survival were summarized separately. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and pooled estimates were calculated using Hartung-Knapp random-effects models, with prespecified sensitivity analyses for outcome compatibility and clustering.

RESULTS: Eight randomized trials involving 12,445 teeth/surfaces from 8,507 children were included. Seven trials involving 12,265 teeth/surfaces from 8,317 children contributed to the primary caries arrest meta-analysis. No statistically significant difference was observed between SDF and conventional restorative treatment (risk ratio [RR] = 1.25, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.78), with considerable between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 96.1%). Exploratory subgroup analyses by unit of analysis, SDF concentration, application frequency, comparator type, setting, and follow-up did not resolve the heterogeneity. The treatment-time analysis included only two studies and favored SDF.

CONCLUSIONS: Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in caries arrest between SDF and conventional restorative treatment in primary teeth; however, considerable heterogeneity and wide confidence intervals limit confidence in the pooled estimate and preclude conclusions of equivalence. SDF may be practical when minimally invasive care is preferred or conventional restorative treatment is difficult to deliver, but treatment selection should also consider esthetic staining, child cooperation, caregiver preferences, and retreatment needs.

articles.title: Effects of transcranial direct current stimulation on nicotine use disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a viable non-invasive approach to counter nicotine addiction. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to investigate the effects of tDCS on smoking behaviors in nicotine use disorder (NUD) and explore neuroimaging findings related to these effects.

METHODS: Systematic review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines shortlisted 21 studies. Primary outcome measures were effects of tDCS vs sham on smoking (i) craving, (ii) consumption, and (iii)accompanying neuroimaging results. Random effects meta-analysis was conducted on 6 comparisons for smoking craving and 13 comparisons for smoking consumption. Anodal and cathodal stimulations were evaluated as moderator variables via meta-regression. Five studies with neuroimaging data supporting tDCS effects on smoking behaviors were reviewed. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation methodology was applied to assess evidence quality.

RESULTS: Compared to sham, tDCS produced a small reduction in nicotine craving (Hedges' g = -0.26, 95%CI [-0.51, -0.01]) with moderate certainty, and moderate reduction in consumption (Hedges' g = -0.48, 95%CI [-0.79, -0.17]) with low certainty; all within the first day post-stimulation. Moderator analyses did not identify specific electrode placements that effectively reduce nicotine craving or intake. Five studies evaluated tDCS effects on smoking behaviors with neuroimaging support namely functional magnetic resonance imaging, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, and electroencephalography, providing additional insights to neurobiology of nicotine addiction.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that tDCS may be associated with changes in craving and consumption in NUD. Further research is required to establish efficacy, identify key moderators, and integrate neuroimaging to explore tDCS effects in smoking cessation.

IMPLICATIONS: Our study adds to the current knowledge on the efficacy of tDCS in smoking cessation. It highlights the need for larger studies to further strengthen efficacy, identify key moderators and integrate neuroimaging to elucidate tDCS' mechanisms underlying successful smoking cessation.

articles.title: Antiphospholipid syndrome is a platelet factor 4-centric immunothrombotic disorder.
articles.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an immunothrombotic disorder, frequently attributed to autoantibodies that bind β2-glycoprotein I (β2GPI). A study showed that the platelet-specific chemokine, platelet factor 4 (PF4), binds to β2GPI, enhancing recognition of β2GPI by APS antibodies. APS antibodies induce the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), webs of decondensed chromatin that bind both PF4 and β2GPI. We propose that PF4 bridges β2GPI to NETs (and other PF4-targeted polyanions), leading to the formation of prothrombotic PF4:β2GPI:NET immunotargets in APS. Dynamic light-scattering studies of isolated immunoglobulin G from 4 patients with triple-positive APS show formation of PF4:β2GPI:NET complexes that bind APS antibodies. NETs released in a microfluidic system bound β2GPI, but only in the presence of PF4, forming a multimolecular APS antigenic target. Whole blood infused through a photochemically injured, endothelium-lined microfluidic channel formed platelet-, fibrin-, and complement-rich thrombi that bound APS antibodies only in the presence of PF4. Thrombi were reduced in size if either ADAMTS13 or DNase I was infused. In a murine APS model, wild-type and transgenic mice expressing human PF4 (hPF4) ± FcγRIIA developed more intense neutrophil rolling along veins and more extensive thrombus formation after laser injury to cremaster arterioles and venules, whereas mice lacking PF4 did not. Three antigenically distinct anti-hPF4 monoclonal antibodies blocked thrombosis in vitro and neutrophil rolling and thrombosis in vivo. Our studies provide new insights into the basis of APS that has mechanistic parallels to other known PF4 immunothrombotic disorders and offer potential diagnostic and nonanticoagulant therapeutic strategies for clinical management.

articles.title: Clinical performance of resin infiltration and different sealant modalities in noncavitated pits and fissures: a split-mouth randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical performance of resin infiltration and different pit and fissure sealants in young permanent molars.

METHOD AND MATERIALS: This split-mouth randomized controlled trial evaluated 128 permanent molars with noncavitated occlusal lesions (ICDAS 0-2) in 32 children aged 7 to 14 years. Teeth were randomly allocated to four groups (n = 32 per group): resin infiltration (Group A), moisture-tolerant resin sealant (Group B), flowable nanohybrid composite (Group C), and a combination of group A and C (Group D). Outcomes assessed were ICDAS scores, DIAGNOdent values, marginal integrity, marginal discoloration, and retention at baseline, 6, and 12 months using generalized estimating equations (GEE) (P .05).

RESULTS: Significant reduction or stabilization in ICDAS scores occurred over time across all groups (P .001). Group A demonstrated significantly higher likelihood of ICDAS stabilization than Group C (OR 1.85; 95% CI 1.10-3.12; P = .021). Group D showed significantly lower lesion progression than Group B (OR 1.72; 95% CI 1.05-2.95; P = .034). At 12 months, retention was high, with only six teeth requiring revision (Group A, n = 1; Group B, n = 2; Group C, n = 3; Group D, n = 0). No significant intergroup differences in DIAGNOdent values or marginal integrity were observed (P > .05).

CONCLUSION: All four evaluated modalities demonstrated significant short-term cariostatic activity. Infiltration-based approaches, particularly the combination approach, demonstrated superior clinical performance by yielding minimal lesion progression, high retention rates, and the lowest incidence of clinical revision in high-caries-risk children.

articles.title: Effects of exposure to negative and positive social media content about vaping and nicotine addiction on beliefs and intentions to use e-cigarettes among young adults in the United States: results from a randomized controlled experiment.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Noncommercial social media content presents vaping and nicotine addiction in both positive and negative terms. The effect of exposure to this content on young adults' attitudes, beliefs, and intentions to vape is unknown.

METHODS: We randomized 1816 US young adults to view a series of real (ie, not simulated), noncommercial, publicly accessible social media videos about nicotine addiction of the same valence (positive, negative, or control unrelated to nicotine addiction). Exposures included both YouTube and TikTok videos that had been uploaded to the YouTube platform. We explored associations between the social media exposure and intentions to use or quit e-cigarettes or cigarettes and related normative beliefs.

RESULTS: Controlling for tobacco use and sociodemographic characteristics, the positive valence group had 49% higher adjusted odds (1.49, 95% CI = 1.08 to 2.04, P = .014) of reporting intentions to vape, but not smoke, compared with the control group. The negative valence group reported higher intentions to quit smoking, but not quit vaping, after adjustment (β = 1.36, 95% CI = 0.38 to 2.34, P = .007). Further, the negative valence group estimated a higher prevalence of peer vaping (β = 3.26, 95% CI = 0.33 to 6.19, P = .029) compared to the control group after adjustment. Injunctive normative beliefs were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Brief exposure to videos that showed nicotine addiction in a favorable light was associated with greater vape intentions among young adults; content of different valences had differential impacts on subjective norms measures. Findings suggest the importance of actions to limit exposure to tobacco-related content on social media.

IMPLICATIONS: In this randomized controlled experiment of US young adults, exposure to social media content that glamorized vaping was associated with nearly 50% higher odds of reporting intentions to vape. Findings add to a growing body of literature suggesting that noncommercial social media content about e-cigarettes influences behavioral intentions, beliefs, attitudes, and/or use of e-cigarettes among young people.

articles.title: Anbalcabtagene autoleucel (PD-1 and TIGIT knockdown CD19 CAR T-cell therapy) for relapsed or refractory LBCL: the CRC01-01 trial.
articles.abstract: Anbalcabtagene autoleucel (anbal-cel) is a CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy incorporating dual PD-1 and TIGIT knockdown to enhance antitumor function and durability. We report results from a phase 1 and 2 study in patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. In phase 2, 79 patients received anbal-cel, and its efficacy was evaluated in 73 patients. The complete response (CR) and partial response rates were 67.1% and 8.2%, respectively. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 6.04 months (95% confidence interval, 4.34-16.46), and the 6-, 12-, and 18-month PFS rates were 50.9%, 41.1%, and 35.2%, respectively. Median overall survival (OS) was not reached, with 12- and 18-month OS rates of 66.6% and 57.3%, respectively. CAR T-cell expansion (Cmax) was significantly greater in responders than in nonresponders (median Cmax, 20 403 vs 8580 copies per μg). Patients were categorized into long-term response (LR) group or non-LR group based on sustained CR at 6 months. Reduced PD-1 and TIGIT expression on CAR+ T cells was observed in the LR group. Most patients (97.5%) experienced grade ≥3 adverse events, most commonly neutropenia (93.7%), followed by thrombocytopenia (41.8%) and anemia (30.4%). Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurological events occurred in 57.0% and 13.9% of patients, respectively. Grade 3 CRS occurred in 8.9% of patients, with no grade 4 events reported, and grade ≥3 neurological events occurred in 3.8% of patients. Serious infections occurred in 25.3% of patients, including grade 5 infection reported in 3 patients. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04836507.

articles.title: Avatar-led digital health intervention for sexual and gender minority young adult smoking cessation: randomized controlled pilot trial.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accessible, culturally-tailored interventions are needed to address the high prevalence of cigarette smoking and the challenges to cessation experienced by sexual and gender minority (SGM) young adults. This study evaluated, in a randomized, controlled pilot trial, the acceptability, preliminary cessation-related outcomes, and impact on theory-based change processes of the SGM-tailored, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-based Empowered, Queer, Quitting, and Living (EQQUAL) digital program relative to the National Cancer Institute's Smokefree.gov program.

METHODS: Participants were SGM young adults, aged 18-30, who smoked at least weekly. Participants were randomized 1:1 to either EQQUAL or Smokefree.gov, both of which included a web app and text messaging. Outcomes were assessed at 3 months post-randomization, and smoking abstinence was biochemically-verified.

RESULTS: The sample included 124 participants (n = 63 in EQQUAL, n = 61 in Smokefree.gov). On the primary acceptability outcomes, overall satisfaction was descriptively higher in the EQQUAL arm (68.8% vs. 60.0%; odds ratio [OR] = 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.50 to 2.78), and EQQUAL usability ratings exceeded the acceptable benchmark score of 68. The average number of EQQUAL digital sessions completed was 1.4 (of 6). On the primary cessation outcomes, biochemically-verified 7-day point prevalence abstinence was higher in EQQUAL than Smokefree.gov (11.1% vs. 4.9%; OR = 1.89, 95% CI = 0.45 to 9.66). Change in readiness to quit and cigarettes per day were similar between arms, as were outcomes of theory-based change processes.

CONCLUSIONS: EQQUAL demonstrated potential benefits over Smokefree.gov on acceptability and cessation, albeit with a lack of robust effect on theory-based change processes. Increased engagement with the web-based portion of the program may be needed to improve outcomes.

IMPLICATIONS: Accessible and effective smoking cessation interventions for sexual and gender minority young adults are needed to address the high prevalence of smoking in this population. This pilot randomized controlled trial demonstrated promising acceptability and cessation outcomes of the Empowered, Queer, Quitting, and Living program, a digital smoking cessation intervention tailored for sexual and gender minority young adults. A larger trial of the intervention is now warranted.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05847673.

articles.title: Randomized controlled trial of a group-based smoking cessation intervention for adults with serious mental illness.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI) have elevated morbidity and mortality, largely attributable to increased cigarette smoking. Effective smoking cessation interventions remain a critical need for this population. This study tested the Parks and Recreation Quit Smoking Program (PARQuit), a multi-component treatment program for adults with SMI. The aims were to compare the effectiveness of the PARQuit physical activity (PA) and PARQuit sedentary groups on smoking cessation, smoking reduction, and psychiatric symptom reduction.

METHODS: Ninety-nine participants with SMI were randomized to a PA intervention or a sedentary control group, each receiving pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement therapy or Bupropion Sustained Release) and cessation counseling for 12 weeks in the United States, from 2019 through 2025. The PARQuit PA group engaged in game-based group exercise (50 min, 3 times/week), whereas the PARQuit sedentary group participated in sedentary group activities. Outcomes included smoking cessation (measured at baseline, 6, and 12 weeks) and psychiatric symptoms assessed via the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale.

RESULTS: At baseline, participants smoked a mean of 76 cigarettes per week, declining to 35 cigarettes at 12 weeks. Both groups showed a significant linear decline in cigarette consumption over time (mean change: -3.7 cigarettes/week; 95% CI, -5.2, -2.4), with no significant between-group difference. Smoking abstinence increased significantly (McNemar χ2 = 5.33, P < .05). Psychiatric symptoms decreased continually, with scores dropping by 0.29 units per week (95% CI, -0.50, -0.09) in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Although there were no significant differences between study groups, both study groups showed a significant reduction in cigarettes smoked each week and in psychiatric symptoms. Group-based counseling and pharmacotherapy likely contributed to these improvements. Future research should assess longer-term outcomes in sustaining smoking cessation. Clinical Trials Registration Number: NCT03950427.

IMPLICATIONS: This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a multi-component smoking cessation program for adults with serious mental illness that integrates group-based counseling and nicotine replacement therapy. It highlights significant reductions in cigarette consumption and psychiatric symptoms across both active and control conditions, emphasizing the importance of tailored interventions for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Secondary prevention and cardiac rehabilitation in patients with chronic coronary syndromes: long-term management and treatment.
articles.abstract: Patients with chronic coronary syndromes deserve high attention and tailored management for the effective reduction of the residual cardiovascular risk. Long-term secondary prevention strategies are the key to reaching this goal and mitigating the overall cardiovascular burden. Four pillars should be the cornerstones of the management of patients with chronic coronary syndromes: lifestyle interventions, cardiac rehabilitation, risk factor control and achievement of treatment targets, and guideline-directed medical therapy. These interventions should be personalized to achieve prevention and treatment goals in order to improve prognosis and health-related quality of life. Herein, we present a state-of-the-art review on the comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment and secondary prevention among patients with chronic coronary syndromes. In addition, we provide practical guidance for the management of this patient population in complex clinical scenarios and specific groups, including those with heart failure, older adults, sex-specific considerations, high bleeding risk, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Pharmacogenetics of incretin-based therapies.
articles.abstract: Interindividual variability in the efficacy of various glucose-lowering drugs has been previously reported and partly explained by genetic variants. The aim of this review was to summarize currently available information on pharmacogenetic studies of the efficacy of incretin-based therapies such as glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (GLP1RA) and dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4i) inhibitors. Several missense variants of the GLP1R gene have been associated with the effects of GLP1RA or DPP-4 inhibitors on glycaemic compensation or weight. Pharmacogenetic effects have also been reported for several type 2 diabetes-associated loci, such as TCF7L2, THADA, MTNR1B, CDKAL1, KCNQ1, KCNJ11, and PAM in candidate gene approach studies. Genome-wide pharmacogenetic studies have identified new genes with potentially relevant pharmacogenetic effects (CTRB1/2, ARRB1, PRKD1). Although none of these genetic associations are currently used in guiding the treatment choices in clinical practice, they offer valuable insights bringing us a little closer to precision medicine.

articles.title: Combined Chatbot and Counselor Support for Smoking Cessation in China: A Pilot, Mobile-Based, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Smoking cessation services in China remain unevenly accessible and underutilized. Chatbots offer a cost-effective and scalable alternative to provide cessation support. This two-arm, community-based, randomized controlled pilot trial assessed the feasibility of a chatbot-supported smoking cessation intervention and explored the potential added benefit of personalized counselor support.

METHODS: Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 71) or a control group (n = 71). Both groups received chatbot-moderated WeChat group support, while the intervention group additionally received one-on-one cessation support from trained counselors for 3 months. The primary outcome was bio-verified abstinence at 6 months. Secondary outcomes included bio-verified abstinence at 3 months, self-reported point prevalence of abstinence (PPA), and smoking reduction. Feasibility outcomes included eligibility, consent, retention, and engagement rate.

RESULTS: By intention-to-treat analysis, bio-verified abstinence was higher in the intervention group compared to the control group at 3 months (18.3% vs. 11.3%; risk ratio [RR] 1.62, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72-3.69) and 6 months (15.5% vs. 9.9%; RR 1.57, 95% CI = 0.64-3.83), though these differences were not statistically significant. Self-reported PPA and smoking reduction were similar between groups.

DISCUSSION: The pilot trial demonstrated that combining chatbot-delivered cessation support with personalized counselor via WeChat was feasible and well accepted in community settings. Although abstinence outcomes were not significant, findings suggest that supplementing chatbot support with counselor guidance may enhance engagement and cessation outcomes. This pilot provides preliminary evidence for integrating automated and human-supported approaches into scalable community cessation programs in China.

IMPLICATIONS: (1) This study showed that a combined chatbot and counselor support model is feasible and acceptable for smoking cessation in community settings in China. (2) The high engagement and retention rates suggest that chat-based support can be effectively integrated into routine community health services. (3) Although differences in smoking abstinence were not statistically significant, the findings point to potential added benefits of incorporating personalized counselor support on top of chatbot interventions. (4) These results support further research to optimize and scale up combined chatbot and counselor interventions for smoking cessation in broader community populations in China.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05777005.

articles.title: How to Implement a Ketogenic Diet Therapy in Developing Countries: Colombian Consensus on Ketogenic Diet Therapy Use in the Management of Adults with Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Drug-resistant epilepsy affects up to one-third of patients with epilepsy and is associated with higher morbidity, mortality, trauma events, psychosocial challenges, and decline in quality of life. In Latin America, disease burden is high and access to advanced therapies remains limited. Ketogenic Diet Therapy (KDT) has been shown to be beneficial in adults, but its implementation requires standardized protocols and experienced multidisciplinary teams. This study aimed to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations to guide the indication, implementation, and follow-up of KDT in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy through expert consensus in Colombia.

METHODS: A modified version of the Nominal Group Technique was used to develop, discuss, and vote on management concepts. Clinical questions were structured using the PICO framework. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed and EMBASE for articles published since 2015, and the evidence was integrated with the experience of a multidisciplinary expert panel.

RESULTS: Twelve recommendations were issued, covering commercial formulas, induction and follow-up protocols, individualized dietary interventions, safety, diagnostic support, nutritional supplementation, and drug-diet interactions. The consensus highlights the need for interdisciplinary teams, structured education, early adherence strategies, and close follow-up, and the role of enteral emergency formulas in intensive care settings.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence around KDT shows it can be implemented safely as an adjunctive treatment for adults with drug-resistant epilepsy and is reasonable to consider following the failure of two adequate antiseizure medications. Structured implementation may reduce seizure frequency, improve quality of life, and reduce the pharmacological burden. Multicenter prospective studies are needed to further assess efficacy, safety, and resource utilization. These recommendations contribute to closing the gap between evidence and clinical practice.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Diseases and Type 2 Diabetes: 2nd Edition.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with multiple comorbidities, the most important being cardiovascular (CV) diseases (CVDs) and especially coronary artery disease (CAD), peripheral artery disease (PAD), stroke, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) [...].

articles.title: Disease Knowledge Assessed by RAKE-T and Its Sociodemographic and Clinical Correlates in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis Receiving Biologic and Targeted Synthetic DMARDs: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Disease-related knowledge is important in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), particularly for patients receiving biologic (bDMARD) or targeted synthetic (tsDMARD) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. This study aimed to assess disease knowledge using the Turkish version of the Rheumatoid Arthritis Knowledge Assessment Questionnaire (RAKE-T) in patients receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy and to investigate its sociodemographic and clinical correlates. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 230 patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy at four rheumatology centers. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were recorded, and disease knowledge was assessed using the 45-item RAKE-T. Linear or robust regression analyses, as appropriate, were used to evaluate factors associated with total and domain-specific scores, except for the single-item comorbidity domain, which was analyzed using binary logistic regression. Results: The mean total RAKE-T score was 61.77 ± 19.00. Older age was associated with lower total RAKE-T and disease knowledge domain scores (p = 0.033 for both). University education or higher was associated with higher total RAKE-T scores (β = 14.503, p < 0.001) and higher scores in the disease knowledge, pharmacological treatments, non-pharmacological treatments, and adaptive skills domains. Place of residence was associated with disease knowledge, self-care, and adaptive skills scores. Disease duration, duration of biologic therapy, sex, marital status, and previous biologic agent use were not significantly associated with total or domain-specific RAKE-T scores. Conclusions: Among patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy, disease knowledge was associated with age, educational level, and place of residence, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with disease duration or duration of biologic therapy. These findings suggest that longer disease or treatment experience should not be assumed to correspond to greater disease knowledge and support periodic reassessment of educational needs and individually tailored patient education.

articles.title: Initial Clip Selection and Outcomes After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: Background: Whether the initial clip type selected during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) of the mitral valve-grasping width and arm length-independently influences procedural and echocardiographic outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 138 consecutive patients undergoing mitral TEER. The first implanted clip was classified as narrow standard-length (NT), long narrow-arm (XT), or long wide-arm (XTW). Determinants of initial clip selection and its association with procedural success (residual mitral regurgitation [MR] ≤ 1+), post-procedural transmitral gradient, and the need for ≥2 clips were assessed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Results: Median age was 74.0 (66.0-80.0), 74.5 (66.0-82.5), and 75.0 (70.0-79.0) years, and median LVEF was 35.0% (30.0-50.0), 30.0% (25.0-45.0), and 40.0% (25.0-45.0), for the NT, XT, and XTW groups, respectively; 66% of patients overall were male. An XTW clip was implanted first in 61.6% of patients. XTW selection was independently associated with larger effective regurgitant orifice area, lower LVEF, longer posterior leaflet length, and secondary MR (all p < 0.05), whereas NT selection favored younger age, smaller orifice, and higher LVEF. After adjustment for these factors, no statistically significant independent association was detected between initial clip type and residual MR ≥2+, post-procedural transmitral gradient, or the need for additional clips (all p > 0.05); however, confidence intervals were wide. On univariable analysis, larger left atrial size and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation were associated with residual MR ≥ 2+, but neither remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Initial clip selection was associated with valve anatomy, LVEF and MR etiology. No statistically significant independent association between initial clip type and procedural or short-term echocardiographic outcomes was detected in this cohort. Given the observational design, confounding by indication, limited sample size and wide confidence intervals, clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded, and these findings do not establish the superiority or equivalence of any clip-selection strategy.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Afterload Across the Pulmonary Hypertension Spectrum.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) performance is the major determinant in pulmonary hypertension (PH). RV afterload is typically assessed using pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) and pulmonary arterial (PA) compliance, overlooking the dynamic component of pulsatile load. Characteristic impedance serves as a measurement of the opposition to pulsatile flow in the proximal arteries. Combined post- and precapillary PH (CpcPH) represents a growing and therapeutically challenging subgroup whose hemodynamic profile remains incompletely characterized. Our aim was to comprehensively describe RV afterload components across the PH spectrum and to evaluate their associations with RV morphology and function. We applied the time-domain method reported in literature to calculate characteristic impedance in a prospective cohort of 78 patients with PH undergoing right heart catheterization and cardiac magnetic resonance. PVR, PA compliance, and characteristic impedance were assessed and compared across precapillary PH (PAH and CTEPH), isolated post-capillary PH (IpcPH), or CpcPH. IpcPH exhibited higher compliance (2.3 mL/mmHg [1.9-3.4]) and lower impedance and PVR (84.5 [63.8-112.2] and 186.0 dyn.s.cm-5 [139.4-208.0] respectively). CpcPH showed intermediate values (1.8 mL/mmHg [1.0-2.7]; 120.4 [88.3-177.7] and 384.8 dyn.s.cm-5 [257.5-627.9]) between IpcPH and precapillary PH (1.4 mL/mmHg [1.1-2.1], 182.5 [123.4-231.4] and 524.1 [367.9-714.5] dyn.s.cm-5), with values closer to the precapillary end of the spectrum. We concluded that CpcPH occupies an intermediate hemodynamic phenotype within the PH spectrum, with some patients showing substantial overlap in afterload components with PAH and CTEPH patients. We observed that characteristic impedance provided complementary information on RV afterload beyond conventional metrics, supporting its integration into multimodal hemodynamic assessment.

articles.title: Oteseconazole (VT-1161) for the Management of Dermatophyte Toenail Onychomycosis: A Review of Phase II Trial Subgroup Efficacy and Extended Follow-Up Safety.
articles.abstract: Oteseconazole, a synthetic tetrazole antifungal, provides pharmacological advantages that suggest it can be a safe and effective treatment for Trichophyton rubrum onychomycosis. A Phase II study of oteseconazole (VT-1161) for onychomycosis demonstrated good efficacy and safety up to Week 60 in the dosing regimens tested: 300 mg for 12 weeks; 300 mg for 24 weeks; 600 mg for 12 weeks and 600 mg for 24 weeks (all given once daily for 2 weeks, then once weekly for remaining weeks). Additional analysis of efficacy was performed using patient factors that can impact onychomycosis. Similar efficacy rates were found across all four regimens tested. Patient factors (<50 years of age, <50% affected nail area) were more strongly associated with improved outcomes than dose escalation of oteseconazole but did not necessarily predict better overall outcomes. No significant safety concerns were found up to Week 60. New extended follow-up data from Week 60 to Week 96 demonstrated long-term plasma retention of oteseconazole with no additional oteseconazole-related adverse events. Accordingly, clinical photographic assessment at Weeks 72 and 96 showed improvement in the target toenail; however, the number of evaluable patients was limited (n = 22), and mycology testing was not performed. The tetrazole structure of oteseconazole significantly reduces the risk of drug-drug interaction compared to traditional azoles (itraconazole, fluconazole). The favorable safety and efficacy profile suggests oteseconazole could be a potential alternative to itraconazole for onychomycosis at any of the tested doses.

articles.title: Genetic Insights into the Comorbidity of Congenital Heart Disease and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Focus on Copy Number Variations.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) frequently co-occur, indicating that cardiac and neural phenotypes can arise from shared developmental disturbances rather than exclusively from the physiological consequences of heart disease. Copy number variations (CNVs) provide a major genomic basis for this overlap, but their effects extend beyond changes in protein-coding gene dosage. This review synthesizes evidence from recurrent CNV syndromes, genomic cohorts, developmental studies, and experimental models to define how CNVs jointly influence heart and brain development. We examine four interconnected mechanisms: dosage alteration of pleiotropic and multiple genes, disruption of non-coding regulatory elements, remodeling of non-coding RNA networks, and reorganization of three-dimensional chromatin architecture. We further describe how developmental timing, cell-type-specific regulatory context, additional genomic variants, cardiac physiology, and clinical exposures shape incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. Together, these findings support a layered model in which a primary CNV establishes cross-organ susceptibility, whereas genetic and developmental modifiers determine whether CHD, NDD, or both become clinically manifest. Clinically, CNV diagnosis can inform neurodevelopmental surveillance, multisystem management, and genetic counseling. Genotype-first longitudinal cohorts, developmental multi-omics, parallel cardiac and neural models, and prospective clinical studies will advance individualized risk prediction and intervention.

articles.title: Novel Techniques and Emerging Technologies in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Structured, Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Chronic total occlusions (CTOs) represent one of the most technically demanding areas of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Despite advances in equipment and operator expertise, CTO PCI remains associated with lower procedural success rates and a higher risk of complications than non-CTO PCI. This review summarizes emerging techniques and technologies designed to improve procedural efficiency, safety, and outcomes in contemporary, personalized patient care. Recent innovations span multiple domains of CTO PCI. The minimalistic hybrid approach (MHA) aims to reduce vascular complications by minimizing the number of access sites and the sheath size. Novel perforation management strategies, including the cut balloon technique (CBT) and the condom technique, offer simple, low-cost options for distal vessel sealing, supported so far only by small series and technical reports. Advanced re-entry methods, such as tip-detection, antegrade dissection and re-entry (TD-ADR), integrate intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) to enhance precision. HydroDynamic contrast recanalization (HDR) revisits hydraulic dissection with a controlled, microcatheter-based contrast strategy whose safety profile remains to be established. The microcatheter anchor technique (MAT) has been proposed to facilitate retrograde CTO PCI in post-CABG anatomy. New plaque-modifying strategies, including RODIN-CUT and ORCAS, leverage high-pressure cutting balloon inflations under real-time IVUS guidance. Additional technologies, such as Plasmawire™, Shockwave Javelin®, and Hertz Contact intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), may expand the armamentarium for crossing and modifying complex CTO lesions, although CTO-specific clinical data are very limited (for Javelin, a 20-patient first-in-human coronary series). CT coronary angiography (CTCA) continues to improve pre-procedural planning, while drug-coated balloons (DCBs) show promise in selected de novo CTO lesions, although the evidence remains limited to retrospective series. Taken together, this rapid pace of innovation is steadily widening the procedural toolkit available for CTO PCI and may improve outcomes. Evidence for most of these techniques comes from case reports, small single-center series, and early-phase single-arm studies. It suggests feasibility in selected patients, but safety data are limited, and some reports signal concerns, including tamponade after the cut balloon technique and a higher perforation rate in a registry of the Carlino technique. The place of these techniques in routine practice will become clear only once larger, multicenter trials are completed.

articles.title: Physiology-Guided Management of Acute Right Ventricular Failure and Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Patients: Hemodynamic Phenotypes, Ventilator Interactions, and Rescue Strategies.
articles.abstract: Patients with acute right heart failure or pulmonary hypertension require cautious resuscitation because the right ventricle is highly preload-sensitive and has a narrow therapeutic window; both hypovolemia and volume overload may worsen hemodynamics. Echocardiographic guidance can help optimize fluid administration. The management of right heart failure also includes increasing contractility and reducing systemic afterload with inodilators such as dobutamine and milrinone. In cases of high pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) contributing to right heart failure, the use of selective pulmonary dilators can decrease the right ventricular afterload, while largely avoiding the systemic hypotension associated with intravenous vasodilators. Hypoxemia, hypercapnia, and acidosis may increase PVR, while sedation, intubation, and positive-pressure ventilation (PPV) may reduce preload, precipitating hemodynamic collapse. When possible, noninvasive respiratory support may be cautiously used to optimize oxygenation and ventilation and avoid intubation. With either form of PPV, airway pressures should be minimized to reduce the risk of hemodynamic compromise. Additionally, preload should be carefully optimized; hypotension-inducing sedatives, such as propofol, should be minimized; vasopressors should be readily available. In ARDS complicated by acute cor pulmonale, a right ventricular-protective ventilation strategy should be considered alongside conventional lung-protective ventilation. This approach emphasizes limiting excessive plateau and driving pressures, avoiding severe hypercapnia and hypoxemia, and carefully titrating positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) to prevent excessive increases in PVR and right ventricular afterload. In patients with right-to-left intracardiac shunting, elevated right-sided pressures may worsen shunt flow and cause refractory hypoxemia that responds poorly to increasing FiO2 and ventilation pressures. Management should therefore focus on reducing PVR, optimizing right ventricular function, and limiting factors that increase right-sided pressures.

articles.title: The Improvement in the Clinical Management of Patients Undergoing Palliative Care After Training the Primary Care Team by a Specialized Team: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Background: Primary Health Care plays an important role in the provision and coordination of palliative care in many healthcare contexts. Education and training of healthcare professionals are relevant strategies to support the delivery of quality palliative care. Objective: To evaluate whether training healthcare professionals working in Primary Health Care improves symptom assessment and clinical management of patients eligible for palliative care. Methodology: Systematic review conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with a protocol registered on the PROSPERO platform under the number CRD420261370621. The eligibility criteria were structured according to the PICO approach: population composed of healthcare professionals working in primary care; educational interventions in palliative care; comparator without training or with different modalities; outcomes of symptom assessment and clinical control. The searches were conducted in seven databases: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, SciELO, and LILACS. Results: Eight studies were included in the review, with varied designs: a pilot randomized clinical trial, a quasi-experimental study, two evaluations of educational programs, a feasibility study, a retrospective population cohort, and two qualitative approaches. The findings revealed a generalist predominance in the provision of palliative care: 95% of the care was provided by generalists, 53% of patients did not receive identifiable palliative care in the last year of life, and specialists were virtually nonexistent in rural areas, where family doctors were responsible for nearly all care. Conclusions: Training of primary care teams is necessary, but insufficient on its own. Although it improves the confidence and knowledge of professionals, there is no robust evidence that it sustainably transforms patient clinical outcomes. The problem is structural: there is a lack of adequate clinical time, compatible remuneration, integration with specialists, and support infrastructure. It is necessary to go beyond education and promote reforms in the healthcare system so that palliative care in primary care is effectively qualified.

articles.title: Bronchial Thermoplasty in Severe Asthma: Bridging Randomised and Real-World Evidence: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Bronchial thermoplasty (BT) reduces airway smooth muscle and may benefit severe asthma, but its role alongside biologics remains unclear. We assessed randomised and real-world evidence on efficacy and safety. Methods: We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies of BT in adults with severe uncontrolled asthma, analysing them separately. Results: Twenty studies were included (five RCTs, 15 observational). In RCTs, BT improved asthma-related quality of life (AQLQ;MD, 0.69; 95% CI 0.30-1.09), asthma control (ACQ; MD,-0.64; 95%CI, -1.10 to -0.19), and morning peak expiratory flow (MD, 20.62 L/min; 95% CI, 4.92-36.32), but did not improve rescue medication use or symptom-free-days. BT increased the risk of hospitalisation during the treatment period (RR, 3.50; 95%CI, 1.26-9.68), with no significant excess thereafter. Real-world studies showed improvements in AQLQ (MD,1.38; 95%CI, 0.97-1.80), ACQ (MD,-1.24; 95%CI, -1.86 to -0.62), and annualised exacerbation rates (MD, -3.79 exacerbations/patient-year; 95%CI, -6.98 to -0.61). Evidence suggested a possible, inconsistent corticosteroid-sparing effect; data on biologics and long-term safety were limited. Conclusions: BT improved asthma-related quality of life and control, mainly in trials without sham controls, but increased short-term hospitalisation risk. Real-world findings were similar but came from uncontrolled studies. BT is not an established alternative to biologics, but may suit carefully selected patients with severe asthma who cannot use or do not respond to them.

articles.title: The effect of azelastine on basal forced expiratory volume in one second in asthmatics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Nearly 5 to 10% of asthmatics show a problematic drug tachyphylaxis, featuring the need for new therapies. Bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) are expressed in the airway tract, and their activation leads to multiple antiasthma effects. Azelastine, an antihistaminic drug with a strong bitter taste, is used to treat allergic rhinitis but is frequently prescribed for asthma. The present study aims to evaluate the bronchodilator effect of azelastine in asthmatic patients. We searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus databases from inception to April 1, 2026. Studies investigating the effect of azelastine on baseline forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of asthmatic patients, compared to a placebo, were included. Mean differences between the two arms were calculated using a random effects model. The systematic search retrieved 145 articles, of which 8 met the inclusion criteria. Azelastine improved FEV1 by 7.57% compared to placebo (p<0.001). The heterogeneity was low (I2=0%), and the overall methodological quality of the selected studies was high, except in four studies, where a risk of bias was observed due to deviations from the intended intervention. Meta-regression analysis showed no significant impact of age, sex ratio, and baseline FEV1 on the global effect size (p>0.05). Azelastine treatment improves FEV1 in asthmatic patients. These results support the previously reported bronchodilator benefits of azelastine through TAS2Rs activation. However, more clinical studies are still needed to explore the therapeutic potential of TAS2R-targeted treatments in asthma.

articles.title: [Awake prone positioning in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure].
articles.abstract: Prone Positioning (PP) improves oxygenation and reduces mortality in intubated patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome. Meanwhile, non-invasive oxygenation strategies have reduced the need for intubation in patients with Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure (AHRF). During the Covid-19 pandemic, the limited availability of invasive mechanical ventilation prompted interest in research on awake PP for non-intubated patients. Encouraging results in this population have led to ongoing studies investigating the benefit of PP for other causes. This simple and low-cost therapy could improve the management of non-intubated patients with AHRF. However, maintaining PP for a sufficient duration to achieve clinical benefit remains a major challenge.

articles.title: [Gabapentinoids and COPD : analgesia or asphyxia ?].
articles.abstract: Gabapentinoids are widely prescribed for patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), despite safety warnings issued by several regulatory agencies regarding their potential respiratory depressant effects. Three large observational studies conducted in Canada, United Kingdom and Japan have been published between 2024 and 2025. They have consistently reported an association between the initiation of gabapentinoid therapy and a 20 to 40 % increase in the risk of COPD exacerbations. This review summarizes these findings, discusses their interpretation, their limits, and the implications for clinical practice.

articles.title: [Non-pharmacological management of chronic heart failure].
articles.abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) requires precise diagnosis and management combining pharmacological treatments and non-pharmacological interventions. Although their level of evidence remains variable, their place in the management of CHF is now well established. This article summarises data on the main non-pharmacological interventions in patients with stable CHF. Current data remain insufficient to justify systematic fluid restriction, while moderate sodium restriction proves preferable to strict restriction. Structured therapeutic education, exercise-based rehabilitation programs, and multidisciplinary management improve quality of life, reduce hospitalizations and, for certain interventions, mortality.

articles.title: Co-occurrence of aortic dissection and polycystic kidney disease: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection is a rare and often fatal condition which arises when there is aortic wall weakening. Multiple risk factors could lead to this condition, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan's, Ehlers-Danlos and Loeys Dietz syndromes, as well as smoking, cocaine usage, bicuspid aortic valve, pregnancy and trauma. Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a rare condition characterized by the development of multiple renal cysts, which is caused by genetic abnormalities leading to autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance. However, the presentation of both pathologies simultaneously is rare and has been infrequently reported.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a death attributed to the co-occurrence of both conditions, involving a 19-year-old Caucasian male with no known past medical history, who collapsed during sexual intercourse. Post-mortem examination revealed hemopericardium with an aortic dissection, which was associated with PKD. The heart and the great vessels were sent to the author's place of practice for a detailed cardiovascular pathology examination.

CONCLUSION: This case is a reminder to all forensic and clinical pathologists that an extremely uncommon manifestation can occur; therefore, a meticulous approach should always be adopted before corroborating a cause of death, especially in young individuals. The relationship between both conditions in this case remains uncertain; however, PKD may represent an associated finding and possibly a predisposing factor rather than a direct causal mechanism. The co-occurrence of both pathologies raises the likelihood of an underlying predisposition to vascular pathology and may have implications for the screening and clinical evaluation of surviving blood relatives.

articles.title: Association of Blastocystis subtype 3 with elevated IL-8-mediated inflammation in patients with irritable bowel syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of Blastocystis in the pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains controversial, with emerging evidence suggesting subtype-specific differences in pathogenicity. Interleukin-8 (IL-8), a key pro-inflammatory chemokine, has been implicated in mucosal immune activation in both IBS and parasitic infections.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between Blastocystis subtypes and clinical manifestations of IBS, with a particular focus IL-8 as part of the systemic pro-inflammatory immune response associated with functional GIT disorders and intestinal infections.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 298 symptomatic patients attending a tertiary gastroenterology clinic were evaluated using Rome IV criteria for IBS diagnosis. Identification of Blastocystis in stool samples was done by direct microscopic examination. Subtype identification using PCR and subtype-specific sequence-tagged site primers were also performed. A balanced random selection was used to compare serum IL-8 levels between Blastocystis-positive IBS patients and an equal number of randomly selected Blastocystis-negative IBS patients. Clinical, biochemical, and demographic variables were analyzed in relation to infection status and subtype distribution.

RESULTS: IBS was diagnosed in 197 out of 298 participants (66.1%), among whom 57 (28.9%) were positive for Blastocystis. Subtype analysis revealed a predominance of subtype (ST) 3 (86%), followed by ST1 (14%). Serum IL-8 levels were significantly higher in Blastocystis-infected IBS patients compared to non-infected controls (129.24 ± 56.28 vs. 26.28 ± 9.28 pg/mL, P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified younger age, diarrhea, and spring presentation as independent predictors of Blastocystis infection.

CONCLUSIONS: IBS is frequently associated with Blastocystis infection, particularly with subtype ST3. Serum levels of IL-8 are higher in Blastocystis-infected IBS patients as compared to uninfected ones. Statistical comparison between IL-8 levels in both subtype groups revealed no significant difference, despite the higher numerical values among the ST3 group. The potential aggravating effect of blastocystosis on IBS symptomatology and the relation between individual subtypes and the pro-inflammatory cytokine response require further mechanistic and longitudinal studies to clarify the causal relationship between Blastocystis subtypes and IBS pathogenesis. In addition, local inflammatory markers should be used to study local immune modulation and identify molecular effectors implicated in the pathogenesis of Blastocystis in IBS -infected patients.

articles.title: Synoptic reporting of cytoreductive surgical procedures for patients with peritoneal malignancy based on the PSOGI-ESGO-ISSPP consensus.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery (CRS), for peritoneal malignancies (PM) is performed with the goal of achieving a CC-0 resection. However, the extent of peritonectomy and type of visceral resections (oncological versus non-oncological) performed during CRS vary among surgeons and lack standardization. The classification of peritonectomy procedures was revised by a consensus among some of the most experienced CRS surgeons in the world, defining the subdivisions and boundaries of each procedure. A format of documenting the extent of peritoneal resection was created which is an important research tool. To precisely report the extent and complexity of CRS, other aspects like the extent of exploration of the abdominal cavity and occult peritoneal spaces, the peritoneal disease extent and the visceral resections performed should be documented in a uniform manner. In the era of precision medicine, CRS needs to be standardized as much as possible. Thus, the working group for the Lyon consensus has created a form for synoptic reporting for CRS in an effort to further standardize CRS and facilitate future research. This form incorporates the surgical Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) including morphological appearance of PM, peritonectomy procedures and extent of peritoneal resection, visceral resections (oncological versus non-oncological), lymphadenectomy, extra-abdominal resections, abdominal wall resections, reconstruction procedures, and residual PCI. An online platform has been developed to generate structured operative reports incorporating all the details in this form (www.crs-report.com). Synoptic reporting will facilitate research and help define surgical strategies. It will help classify CRS according to its complexity clarifying formulation of recommendations for perioperative care.

articles.title: Treatment-associated structural connectome reorganization following high-frequency rTMS in major depressive disorder: A low- and high-order connectivity study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is an established treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), but associated changes in structural-connectome topology remains unclear. Specifically, higher-order structural connectivity (HOSC), defined by similarities between regional structural connectivity profiles, may provide information beyond direct low-order structural connectivity (LOSC).

METHODS: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data were acquired from 23 patients with MDD before and after 10-Hz rTMS and from 30 matched healthy controls (HCs). LOSC networks were constructed based on deterministic tractography, whereas HOSC networks were derived from similarities between regional LOSC profiles. Graph-theoretical analysis and network-based statistics were employed to characterize topological and subnetwork differences.

RESULTS: Depressive symptoms decreased significantly after treatment. Global LOSC topology remained stable, whereas HOSC showed case-control differences in network segregation and post-treatment differences in small-world organization relative to HCs. Network-based analysis revealed focal strengthening of a left insula-hippocampal-inferior temporal component in LOSC and distributed HOSC variation involving cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry, particularly the thalamus and caudate. Nodal analyses further identified treatment-associated centrality changes involving the thalamus and hippocampus.

CONCLUSION: High-frequency rTMS treatment was associated with coordinated structural-connectome variation across low- and high-order network organization in MDD. These findings should be interpreted as treatment-associated changes rather than effects attributable specifically to rTMS and suggest that HOSC may provide a complementary representation of network variation accompanying clinical improvement.

articles.title: Tiotropium and clinically important deterioration in mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a post hoc win ratio analysis of the Tie-COPD study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinically important deterioration (CID) has been used to assess chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) progression by time-to-first-event analysis. However, this does not reveal the clinical importance of the CID components. The win ratio may provide a complementary assessment by comparing outcomes according to a prespecified hierarchy. We reanalysed data from the Tie-COPD studywith win ratio to assess the overall treatment benefit associated with tiotropium in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD.

METHODS: In this exploratory post hoc study, the unmatched win ratio method was applied to the outcomes observed in the Tie-COPD study comparing 18 µg tiotropium with placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD over 24 months. CID was defined as an occurrence of moderate-to-severe exacerbation, an increase of ≥2 units in COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score or a decrease of ≥100 mL in the forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). We evaluated the win ratio across all possible hierarchies of CID components. Exploratory inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW), and covariate-adjusted IPCW (CovIPCW) analyses were performed to account for censoring. Subgroup analyses were performed with stratification by sex, smoking status, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease stage, CAT score and modified Medical Research Council score at baseline.

RESULTS: Of the 841 randomised patients, 771 were included in the full analysis set (tiotropium=388; placebo=383). With the clinical hierarchy of CID defined by FEV1, exacerbation and CAT, the win ratio was 2.26 (95% CI 1.87 to 2.73, p<0.001), and the net benefit was 0.35 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.44, p<0.001). Win ratios were greater than 1 across all hierarchies, subgroups and censoring-adjusted analyses. No treatment-by-subgroup interaction was detected (all p for interaction >0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post hoc analysis, tiotropium was associated with a greater overall treatment benefit than placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD. This benefit was also observed in patients with mild disease or fewer respiratory symptoms. The direction of the findings was consistent across alternative CID hierarchies and censoring-adjusted analyses.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT01455129.

articles.title: Early pancreatic stone protein kinetics and subsequent inflammatory outcomes in extremely preterm neonates: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate pancreatic stone protein (PSP) levels in extremely preterm neonates and their association with early-onset sepsis (EOS), late-onset sepsis (LOS), and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC).

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective longitudinal study, evaluating serial PSP, C-reactive protein (CRP), and white blood cell (WBC) count during the first ten days after birth.

RESULTS: Thirty extremely preterm neonates with a mean gestational age of 26.5 ± 1.8 weeks and a mean birth weight of 890 ± 304 g were enrolled. PSP increased significantly 48 h before LOS presentation, with a diagnostic accuracy higher than that of CRP and WBC (AUROC 0.711, 0.567, and 0.538, respectively). PSP levels also increased from 72 h before NEC onset, with a better discriminatory ability than CRP and WBC (AUROC 0.851, 0.648, and 0.616, respectively).

CONCLUSION: PSP may represent a promising early biomarker for LOS and NEC in extremely preterm neonates. Larger multicenter studies are required to validate these findings.

articles.title: Metabolic Effect of the Emergent Pollutant and Endocrine Disruptor Bisphenol A in Male BALBc/AnN Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bisphenol A (BPA) is an endocrine-disrupting chemical with estrogenic properties that affects various tissues. It has been linked to chronic and inflammatory diseases, such as diabetes and metabolic syndrome.

AIM: To investigate the obesogenic effects of a single neonatal administration of BPA on obesity and its underlying mechanisms in mice.

METHODS: We established a neonatal BPA administration model in mice and measured various biochemical parameters. We also analyzed retroperitoneal, mesenteric, and gonadal fat depots using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In addition, to provide a translational context, we measured the serum BPA levels in male obese patients.

RESULTS: Neonatal BPA administration in mice induced chronic dimorphic obesity and metabolic syndrome only in male mice. These findings were also reproducible in obese male patients, who exhibited higher concentrations of this endocrine-disrupting chemical than their non-obese counterparts. In addition, the results showed that the number of adult male mice was significantly higher in the BPA-treated group compared with the control and vehicle groups. Metabolic and biochemical parameters, such as adipose tissue, cholesterol, triglycerides, and glucose, were also significantly higher in mice that received BPA in the neonatal stage.

CONCLUSION: Single neonatal BPA administration could be used as a novel strategy in the study of obesity.

articles.title: Impact of an Extra Virgin Olive Oil-enriched Diet in Diabetic Dams on the Decidua of offspring Prone to Gestational Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During early pregnancy, the decidua supports embryo development and maternal adaptations to pregnancy. Maternal diabetes programs gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in offspring, and a pro-oxidant intrauterine environment has been implicated. Diets enriched with extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) can provide antioxidant effects. This study hypothesized that EVOO-enriched diets administered to pregestational diabetic pregnant rats (F0) would confer beneficial effects on the decidua of their early-pregnant offspring (F1), who are prone to developing GDM.

AIMS: To evaluate signaling pathways and pro-oxidant state markers in the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams who either received or did not receive a 6% EVOO-enriched diet during the F0 pregnancy.

METHODS: Rats with mild diabetes and controls were fed diets with or without 6% EVOO during F0 pregnancy, and their 9 d pregnant offspring were then evaluated. Markers of decidual function (prolactin, PPAR and mTOR pathways) and the pro-oxidant state were evaluated in the decidua.

RESULTS: Despite normal maternal glycemia and progesterone levels, the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams exhibited reduced prolactin and mTOR pathway activity. PPAR levels decreased, while microRNAs that regulate their expression increased. These alterations were not prevented by the EVOO-enriched diet provided in the F0 generation. Levels of FABP4 (involved in decidualization and a marker of a pro-oxidant state) and lipoperoxidation were increased in the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams. The EVOO-enriched diet prevented these alterations.

CONCLUSION: Maternal diabetes programs impaired markers of decidualization and the pro-oxidant state in early-pregnancy offspring. These alterations were partially ameliorated by maternal diets enriched with EVOO.

articles.title: Home non-invasive ventilation in chronic respiratory failure: Evidence-based guidelines.
articles.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
articles.abstract: Home non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is used across a range of causes of chronic respiratory failure, but patient selection and management are disease-specific. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations on initiating, titrating, and monitoring long-term home NIV across different disease spectrums. The panel reviewed studies from international databases, relevant guidelines, and reference lists. The panel refined recommendations through two rounds of consensus and graded them using the Indian Chest Society framework. In chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), home NIV is recommended for eligible patients with persistent daytime hypercapnia, including those who remain hypercapnic 2 to 4 weeks after an exacerbation. High-intensity bilevel ventilation should be titrated to achieve a meaningful reduction in arterial carbon dioxide. In neuromuscular disorders, respiratory muscle weakness or hypoventilation warrants timely assessment for NIV, alongside evaluation of interface tolerance and secretion clearance. For stable obesity hypoventilation syndrome with severe obstructive sleep apnoea, continuous positive airway pressure is generally the preferred initial treatment; NIV is appropriate when severe obstructive sleep apnoea is absent or continuous positive airway pressure fails or is not tolerated. The guidelines also address heart failure with sleep-disordered breathing, chest-wall deformity, interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis, post-tuberculosis lung disease, central hypoventilation syndromes, and palliative care. Across indications, management should include individualised ventilator settings, objective assessment of ventilation, patient and caregiver education, and structured follow-up. Where evidence is limited, recommendations reflect expert consensus and should be applied in the context of patient goals, clinical feasibility, and available resources.

articles.title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl-carboxyl C-C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C-C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity.
