The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

articles.title: Ultrafast Aqueous Photoinduced Electron/Energy Transfer Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain Transfer Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly: Wavelength-Dependent Morphologies and Scalable Nanoparticle Preparation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Photoinduced electron/energy transfer-reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (PET-RAFT) polymerization offers a powerful route to oxygen-tolerant polymer synthesis under visible light, yet slow polymerization rates remain a persistent bottleneck for further development. Here, we report an aryloxy xanthate chain transfer agent (CTA) bearing a 2-naphthyloxy Z group that unlocks ultrafast aqueous PET-RAFT polymerization under orange light irradiation. The system achieves an apparent propagation rate constant (kpapp) of 0.89 min-1, reaching high monomer conversion (>80%) within 2 min while maintaining good control over polymerization (Đ ≤ 1.2). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the enhanced polymerization rate originates from the low fragmentation energy barrier of the CTA anionic radical. Leveraging this performance, we applied the system to photoinduced polymerization-induced self-assembly (photo-PISA), achieving ultrafast formation of well-defined polymeric nanoparticles within 1 min without prior deoxygenation and with tunable morphologies accessible by varying formulation conditions. Strikingly, photo-PISA exhibited a pronounced wavelength dependence: long-wavelength irradiation produced well-defined vesicles, whereas short-wavelength irradiation yielded irregular aggregates. This behavior is attributed to superior light penetration and spatial uniformity at longer wavelengths, establishing wavelength-tunable light-field uniformity as a handle for the accessible PISA morphology. These findings establish the 2-naphthyloxy xanthate CTA as a versatile platform for scalable and high-throughput photo-PISA, opening new avenues for the rapid and oxygen-tolerant fabrication of functional polymeric nanomaterials.

articles.title: Multisource Coronary Artery Fistula Draining Into the Coronary Sinus: Multimodality Imaging and Surgical Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Multisource CAF draining into the coronary sinus is exceptionally uncommon and anatomically complex.

CASE PRESENTATION: A woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided heart failure. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and invasive coronary angiography, demonstrated multisource CAFs arising from the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery draining into the coronary sinus with diffuse aneurysmal coronary dilatation. The patient underwent surgical ligation of the dominant right CAF with concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty. Postoperative imaging demonstrated successful closure of the dominant right CAF with thrombus formation within the ligated fistulous tract, whereas the smaller left circumflex artery fistula persisted, and serial follow-up demonstrated clinical improvement.

CONCLUSION: Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and postoperative surveillance of complex CAF. Surgical repair remains an effective treatment strategy for anatomically complex fistulas associated with significant hemodynamic consequences.

articles.title: Temporal Trends and Autopsy Correlates of Duty-Related Cardiac Death in Firefighters.
Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.

OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.

METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.

RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

articles.title: Near Real-Time Quantitative Ultrasound Imaging Using an Ultra-Portable Handheld Ultrasound System.
articles.abstract: Clinical ultrasound is widely used because of its low cost, portability, safety, and real-time imaging capability, making it well suited for point-of-care applications. However, conventional B-mode imaging is inherently qualitative and primarily sensitive to tissue morphology. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) methods exploit information contained in backscattered radiofrequency (RF) signals to extract fundamental acoustic tissue properties, such as the backscatter coefficient (BSC) and attenuation, which more directly quantify tissue microstructure and provide complementary information to B-mode imaging. Although QUS methods have been implemented on conventional cart-based ultrasound scanners, their integration into portable handheld systems remains limited. Motivated by the growing availability and clinical potential of ultra-portable ultrasound devices, this protocol presents a QUS imaging pipeline implemented on the DKPOC probe (portable linear ultrasound probe; Vermon SA, Tours, France), which interfaces directly with a laptop through a USB-C connection. The protocol integrates multiple QUS processing methods based on spectral analysis and envelope statistics of RF data acquired using focused-wave or plane-wave transmit modes. QUS processing begins with a user-defined region of interest (ROI). The reference phantom method is used to estimate the BSC and attenuation within sliding sub-ROIs. Model-based fitting of the estimated BSC is then performed to extract tissue microstructure-related parameters, including effective scatterer diameter and effective acoustic concentration. In addition, envelope statistics parameters are estimated using three probability density functions. Computed QUS parameter maps are displayed as translucent color overlays on corresponding B-mode images. The workflow is implemented in a numerical computing software-based graphical user interface, enabling near real-time QUS processing, parameter map visualization, interactive parameter adjustment, and rapid evaluation of different processing configurations. The pipeline is adaptable to different imaging sequences and ultrasound probes, providing a practical framework for quantitative point-of-care ultrasound imaging and clinician-led QUS studies in human subjects.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Endovascular Treatment for HIR- and Collateral-Screened Ultra-Long Window Anterior Circulation LVO: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the clinical value of combined hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) and collateral evaluation for patient selection and prognostic assessment in endovascular therapy (EVT) among anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO) patients within the 6-24 h extended time window. This prospective cohort analysis enrolled 152 LVO patients treated with EVT between January 2022 and June 2024. HIR was defined as the volume ratio of Tmax >10 s to Tmax >6 s hypoperfusion. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale, with scores ≥3 classified as favorable. According to the HIR cutoff (≤0.4) and collateral status, patients were divided into four subgroups: Group A (dual favorable), Group B (favorable HIR/poor collaterals), Group C (poor HIR/favorable collaterals), and Group D (dual unfavorable). All participants received standard EVT and adjunct medical therapy for comparative outcome analysis. Groups A (n = 42), B (n = 38), C (n = 35), and D (n = 37) differed significantly in baseline stroke severity and perfusion parameters, with Group D presenting larger ischemic cores, extensive hypoperfusion, and higher NIHSS scores (P < 0.05). Group A achieved the highest 90-day favorable functional rate (69.0%), alongside minimal infarct progression and superior reperfusion (88.1%) (P < 0.001). Favorable HIR (OR = 3.274, P = 0.002) and collateral status (OR = 3.516, P = 0.001) were independent protective factors. The combined model (AUC = 0.84) exhibited better predictive performance than single-index evaluation. Group A also had lower sICH and 90-day mortality than Group D (P < 0.05). Combined HIR and collateral assessment offers a feasible imaging stratification approach for ultra-long-window LVO patients. Dual favorable imaging features predict favorable post-EVT efficacy and safety, assisting individualized clinical decision-making for delayed EVT candidates.

articles.title: Extremely Severe Aortic Stenosis Mimicking Cardiac Amyloidosis on Multimodality Imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac amyloidosis is increasingly recognized in older patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet advanced pressure-overload remodeling can produce overlapping imaging features that confound noninvasive diagnosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed extremely severe calcific aortic stenosis, increased left ventricular wall thickness, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated elevated native T1 and extracellular volume with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging showed Perugini grade 1 uptake. Despite clinical suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, noninvasive findings remained inconclusive. The patient underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with intraoperative myocardial biopsy, which demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis without amyloid deposition, consistent with advanced pressure-overload remodeling rather than infiltrative disease.

DISCUSSION: Extremely severe aortic stenosis can mimic cardiac amyloidosis across multiple imaging modalities. Histologic confirmation remains essential when noninvasive findings are discordant or inconclusive.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Severe aortic stenosis may closely mimic cardiac amyloidosis on multimodality imaging. Histological confirmation can be decisive in resolving diagnostic uncertainty.

articles.title: Expanding the Electrosurgical Toolbox in Structural Heart Intervention.
The Cascading Hazard of Delayed-Presentation STEMI Unmasked by a Stroke.
Hydroxychloroquine Cardiotoxicity Mimicking Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis in a Patient With HFpEF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is an immunomodulatory drug used in systemic lupus erythematosus and other rheumatologic disorders, with rare but potentially severe cardiotoxic effects.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with subacute worsening chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, and neuropathy. Electrocardiogram showed low voltage; echocardiogram revealed moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with reduced global longitudinal strain without apical sparing. Coronary angiography was normal. Technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy showed focal grade 2 uptake. Endomyocardial biopsy revealed widespread myocyte hypertrophy and lysosomal curvilinear bodies consistent with HCQ cardiotoxicity.

DISCUSSION: HCQ is a long-term medication used in connective tissue diseases. Patients with rheumatologic conditions are at increased risk for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of HCQ use. Recognition of insidious organ toxicity can be challenging. HCQ toxicity can cause infiltrative pathology and mimic transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Endomyocardial biopsy is key for definitive diagnosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In patients with an equivocally positive technetium-99m pyrophosphate scan and chronic HCQ use, endomyocardial biopsy should be considered to differentiate drug toxicity from transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

articles.title: Residual Communications After Surgical Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Complementary Roles of TEE and CCTA.
Systemic Amyloidosis After Liver Transplantation From a Donor With Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acquired transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis after domino liver transplantation is rare and may manifest years after the procedure, with neurologic involvement.

CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man received a liver from a donor with TTR amyloid polyneuropathy. Twelve years later, he developed paresthesias, diarrhea, and blood pressure lability. Electroneuromyography showed a length-dependent, predominantly axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, with absent sympathetic skin responses, indicating autonomic involvement. Abdominal fat pad biopsy was Congo red positive, and TTR genetic testing was negative. Cardiac involvement was absent. He was treated with pregabalin and fludrocortisone, and patisiran was indicated as disease-modifying therapy.

DISCUSSION: The association of progressive neuropathy, dysautonomia, gastrointestinal manifestations, and domino transplantation favored acquired TTR amyloidosis over diabetic neuropathy. Reported cases show onset after 5-10 years, with neuropathy preceding cardiac disease.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Domino transplant recipients require long-term follow-up, even with negative genetic testing and no initial cardiomyopathy, to enable early diagnosis and monitoring of systemic progression.

articles.title: Dasatinib and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: When Cardio-Oncology Meets the Pulmonary Circulation.
Retrospective Nomogram Development for Postoperative Pulmonary Complications After Robotic-Assisted Anatomical Segmentectomy.
articles.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) remain among the most common adverse events following thoracic surgery, contributing to increased morbidity and prolonged hospital stay. With the growing adoption of robotic-assisted thoracic surgery for anatomical segmentectomy, procedure-specific data on PPC risk stratification remain limited. This retrospective cohort study aimed to evaluate risk factors for PPCs in patients undergoing da Vinci robotic-assisted anatomical segmentectomy and to develop and chronologically validate a nomogram-based prediction model using a homogeneous robotic cohort. The study included 200 patients in the development cohort and 102 patients in the temporal validation cohort. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed in the development cohort, and a three-variable prediction model incorporating age ≥65 years, smoking history, and forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) <70% predicted was evaluated. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and calibration slope. Overall, 64 of 302 patients (21.2%) developed PPCs. In the development cohort, age ≥65 years was independently associated with PPCs (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 2.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.29-5.44, P = 0.008), whereas smoking history (adjusted OR 1.91, 95% CI 0.93-3.91, P = 0.079) and FEV1 <70% predicted (adjusted OR 1.51, 95% CI 0.74-3.10, P = 0.259) were not statistically significant after adjustment. The three-variable model had an AUC of 0.69 (95% CI 0.60-0.78) in the development cohort and 0.85 (95% CI 0.76-0.92) in the temporal validation cohort. These findings support the potential value of a simple preoperative risk model, but external multicenter validation is required before broader clinical application.

articles.title: Herbal-Cake-Separated Moxibustion Ameliorates Renal Fibrosis and Associated Bone Injury in Rats via the TGF-β1/Smad Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is the main pathological basis for chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression and is often accompanied by decreased bone density and impaired bone microstructure. The TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway may be a common intervention target for kidney and bone injury. This study evaluated the effects of herbal-cake-separated moxibustion (HCSM) on renal fibrosis and bone damage in CKD rats and explored its potential mechanism. CKD was induced by adenine gavage combined with a high-protein diet. Successfully modeled rats were randomly assigned to model, HCSM, and SIS3 groups (n = 6 each), with an additional control group (n = 6). The control and model groups received no intervention. The HCSM group received treatment at Pishu (BL20) and Shenshu (BL23), whereas the SIS3 group received intraperitoneal SIS3 (2.5 mg/kg every 2 days). Treatment comprised three 12-day courses separated by 2-day intervals. Renal injury was assessed by kidney function, kidney index, and histopathology. Western blotting measured TGF-β1, Smad2/3, p-Smad2/3, and BMP-7 expression, and micro-computed tomography assessed femoral bone density and microstructure. Compared with controls, model rats showed significantly increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine (Scr), and kidney index (p < 0.0001); marked renal fibrosis; increased TGF-β1, p-Smad2/3, and Smad2/3; decreased BMP-7; reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular number; and increased trabecular separation. Compared with the model group, HCSM and SIS3 improved renal function and histopathology, increased BMD and trabecular number, reduced trabecular separation, suppressed TGF-β1/Smad signaling, and increased BMP-7 expression. These findings indicate that HCSM may improve renal fibrosis and associated bone damage by enhancing BMP-7 expression and inhibiting TGF-β1/Smad signaling.

articles.title: Seated Modified Liuzijue Training for Rehabilitation of a Patient with Respiratory Impairment During the Recovery Phase of Stroke: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Patients in the recovery phase after stroke may present with respiratory impairment and abnormal breathing patterns, which can limit exercise tolerance and affect quality of life. This case report describes a 6-week seated modified Liuzijue breathing training program implemented in a patient with respiratory impairment during the recovery phase of stroke. Considering the patient's post-stroke motor dysfunction and balance limitations, the traditional standing Liuzijue protocol was adapted to a seated format, with simplified upper-limb movements and individualized breathing rhythm. The patient completed the 6-week training program in conjunction with conventional rehabilitation. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included pulmonary function parameters, respiratory-related quality of life, general health-related quality of life, and routine laboratory monitoring. After the intervention, tidal volume (TV), vital capacity (VC), and forced vital capacity (FVC) increased relative to baseline. The post-intervention changes in St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) scores suggested an improvement in the patient's perceived respiratory-related and overall quality of life. This case primarily demonstrates that a seated modified Liuzijue protocol was feasible to implement and was well tolerated throughout the 6-week intervention in this individual patient, without clinically relevant training‑related adverse events. However, because this was an uncontrolled single-case observation conducted during the stroke recovery phase and the patient received concurrent conventional rehabilitation, the observed pre-post changes cannot be attributed specifically to seated modified Liuzijue. These findings should be regarded as preliminary evidence of procedural feasibility and clinical changes that warrant confirmation in controlled studies with larger samples and direct physiological measurements.

articles.title: Surgery as Metabolic Therapy: Expanding the Role of Gastrointestinal Surgery Beyond Anatomical Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal surgery comprises procedures used to treat diseases and injuries of the digestive tract. Evidence now shows that some gastrointestinal procedures are also systemic metabolic interventions. Bariatric and metabolic surgery intentionally treats obesity and associated metabolic disease and can improve type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and cardiometabolic risk, sometimes before substantial weight loss occurs. Other procedures, including hepatectomy, pancreatic resection, and bowel resection, are generally performed for non-metabolic indications; their metabolic consequences may be adaptive, neutral, or adverse, including pancreatogenic diabetes and intestinal failure. This narrative review examines how major gastrointestinal operations affect whole-body metabolism and discusses metabolic phenotyping for personalized patient selection, preoperative optimization, postoperative management, and long-term monitoring. The review highlights bariatric and metabolic surgery as the reference model while distinguishing its established therapeutic effects from the metabolic consequences of other resections. It proposes that surgery should be considered both a correction of anatomy and a perturbation of physiology, enabling plans that preserve structural integrity, support metabolic adaptation, and limit metabolic harm.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a 24-Hour Landmark Model for 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis-Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) carries substantial short-term mortality. Differences in predictor timing, validation design, and comparators complicate evaluation of published prediction models. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 955 adults with sepsis-associated ARDS who reached a 24-h landmark after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. All-cause mortality was assessed by day 28 from ICU admission. Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-only logistic regression, conventional multivariable logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared. The multivariable models used 26 candidate predictors (30 encoded parameters). Five repetitions of five-fold outer cross-validation with three-fold inner tuning provided held-out predictions. Evaluation included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, classification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Held-out tree-based Shapley additive explanations described XGBoost predictions. Among 955 patients, 474 (49.6%) died. AUCs based on averaged held-out probabilities were 0.732 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.698-0.761) for LASSO, 0.729 (0.696-0.761) for conventional regression, 0.709 (0.674-0.740) for XGBoost, 0.707 (0.673-0.739) for random forest, and 0.581 (0.545-0.617) for SOFA alone. The LASSO-minus-conventional-regression AUC difference was 0.003 (95% CI, -0.003 to 0.010). Intervals resampled fixed predictions without refitting. LASSO had a Brier score of 0.209, calibration intercept of -0.001, and slope of 1.065. The final equation retained age, Charlson Comorbidity Index, arterial oxygen partial pressure/fraction of inspired oxygen ratio, SOFA, lactate, bilirubin, other infection site, and vasopressor use. LASSO provided moderate discrimination without a clear advantage over conventional regression. The separately tuned final equation requires source-data verification, external validation, and prospective clinical-utility assessment before clinical use.

articles.title: Extended Ceftriaxone Prophylaxis and Postoperative Inflammation and Infection-Related Symptoms After Ureteral Lithotripsy with Negative Urine Cultures.
articles.abstract: Postoperative inflammatory and infection-related manifestations can occur after rigid ureteroscopic lithotripsy (RUL), including in patients with negative preoperative urine cultures. Whether extending prophylaxis improves outcomes for clinically confirmed infections remains uncertain. To explore differences in postoperative inflammatory markers and infection-related manifestations between an extended preoperative ceftriaxone regimen and a single prophylactic dose in culture-negative patients undergoing RUL. This single-center exploratory study included 252 analyzed patients and was reported as randomized. The extended-regimen group (n = 122) received ceftriaxone at 2 g intravenously every 12 h for 3-7 days before surgery; the single-dose group (n = 130) received 2 g intravenously 30-60 min before surgery. No prospective sample size or power calculation was performed. WBC, NEUT%, CRP, and PCT were assessed preoperatively and on postoperative days 1 and 3. Exploratory, unadjusted time-specific comparisons were calculated from the reported summary statistics; these do not constitute a longitudinal repeated-measures analysis. Clinical manifestations, surgical complications, and discharge SF-36 scores were also summarized. Postoperative mean WBC, NEUT%, CRP, and PCT values were lower in the extended-regimen group on days 1 and 3 (all unadjusted, summary-based p < 0.001). Preoperative WBC also differed (p = 0.040), and stone diameter differed between groups (p = 0.025). The reported symptom composite occurred in 20/122 patients (16.4%) and 39/130 patients (30.0%), respectively (two-sided Fisher's exact p = 0.012). Group-specific confirmed-infection rates were not reported. Selected SF-36 domain scores were higher at discharge. Numerical longitudinal-model outputs and ceftriaxone-related adverse-event frequencies were not reported. Extended ceftriaxone prophylaxis was associated with lower postoperative inflammatory-marker values and fewer reported infection-related manifestations. These exploratory findings do not establish prevention of confirmed postoperative infection, equivalent ceftriaxone safety, or a basis for recommending routine prolonged prophylaxis. Confirmatory studies with prespecified analyses, verified infectious endpoints, and complete safety reporting are needed.

articles.title: Additional Functional Exercise Training Improves Knee Recovery After Meniscus Repair: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated whether adding functional exercise training (FET) to conventional rehabilitation improves postoperative knee recovery after meniscus repair. In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 96 patients who underwent meniscus repair between April 2023 and September 2024 were randomly assigned to conventional rehabilitation (CON; n = 48) or conventional rehabilitation plus FET (n = 48) using a computer-generated randomization sequence. All participants completed the 6-month follow-up and were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Outcomes assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 6 months included the Lysholm rating scale (LRS), International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score, visual analog scale (VAS) pain score, range of motion (ROM), prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), passive 60° position sense, and 60° motion sense; postoperative complications within 1 month were also recorded. At 6 months, ROM was greater with FET than with CON (134.36° ± 3.04° vs. 127.62° ± 3.66°; mean difference, 6.74°; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.37-8.10; adjusted P < 0.001). After Holm-Bonferroni adjustment for multiple secondary comparisons, IKDC scores were higher with FET at 1 and 6 months, LRS scores were higher at 1 month, and VAS scores were lower at both follow-up assessments. PGE2 and 5-HT levels and passive 60° position-sense error and 60° motion-sense values were lower with FET at 1 month. Differences in ROM at 1 month and passive 60° position sense at 6 months did not remain statistically significant after multiplicity adjustment. No significant between-group differences were observed at 6 months for LRS, PGE2, 5-HT, or 60° motion sense, and postoperative complication rates did not differ significantly between groups. Adding FET to conventional rehabilitation may improve postoperative recovery after meniscus repair, with the strongest evidence supporting improved ROM. Findings for secondary outcomes require cautious interpretation and further validation, particularly given the retrospective trial registration and multiplicity of secondary outcomes.

articles.title: Assessment and Reversibility of Hepatic Abnormalities in Heart Failure: Liver in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.

articles.title: Early white blood cell count changes and 30-day mortality in acute pulmonary embolism.
articles.abstract: Serial complete blood count (CBC) measurements are standard for acute pulmonary embolism, yet the prognostic significance of early changes remains unclear. This study investigated whether these changes enhance mortality prediction beyond baseline values and a restricted set of clinical predictors. We retrospectively evaluated ten CBC-derived measures using a 72-hour landmark in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality within 30 days of admission, following the landmark. Nested logistic models incorporated baseline values and log-ratio changes between 0-<24 and 24-<72 hours post-admission, applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction. The top-performing model underwent 1,000-resample bootstrap validation and was subsequently applied without modification to an independent hospital cohort. Among 5,556 landmark-eligible development patients, white blood cell count (WBC) demonstrated the strongest association. In 4,531 patients with 546 deaths, the adjusted odds ratio for a one standard-deviation increase in WBC change was 1.35 (95% CI, 1.22-1.48). The full model's optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.766. For 266 external patients with 41 deaths, the AUC was 0.824 (95% CI, 0.736-0.899). Adding WBC change to a model already containing baseline WBC altered the AUC by 0.0035 (95% CI, -0.0262 to 0.0350), without a clear improvement in the Brier score. The calibration slope was 1.50, indicating an underestimation of risk in the highest-risk quintile. In conclusion, while early WBC change correlated with subsequent mortality, its incremental predictive value was not externally validated. Further prospective, multicenter evaluation is essential before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Construction Trade Work Is Associated With Accelerated Decline in Kidney Function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Construction workers are exposed to airborne particulates, organic solvents, and metals-agents linked to elevated risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Few studies have evaluated whether construction trade work is associated with longitudinal changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), a key indicator of kidney function. This study examined the relationship between construction-related exposures and eGFR decline.

METHODS: The cohort included 9192 participants in the Building Trades National Medical Screening Program (BTMed). An index of exposure to vapors, gases, dusts, and fumes (VGDF) was developed (measure = standard deviation increases in the log index). Mixed models estimated annual eGFR decline (mL/min/1.73 m2 per year) while adjusting for established CKD risk factors. Sensitivity analyses used inverse propensity score weighted (IPSW) regression to balance covariates between construction trade workers and an internal comparison group. Secondary analyses assessed CKD incidence using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Construction work was significantly associated with faster annual eGFR decline (-0.22, 95% CI = -0.33 to -0.11). VGDF exposure was also associated with greater decline (-0.07, 95% CI = -0.09 to -0.05). CKD incidence was associated with construction work (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.05-2.03) and VGDF exposure (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 1.00-1.16). IPSW analyses supported these findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Construction trade work and VGDF exposure were associated with accelerated eGFR decline and increased CKD incidence, indicating broad renal impacts of mixed construction-related exposures. Primary and secondary prevention efforts to reduce VGDF exposures and to identify workers with rapid eGFR decline may help reduce the risk of progression to end-stage renal disease.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Complications in Pregnancy and Biological Ageing in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic complications in pregnancy may alter the intrauterine environment, influence offspring biological ageing and potentially increase the risk of chronic diseases later in life.

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine associations between diabetes in pregnancy, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, maternal BMI and metabolic syndrome, and offspring biological ageing markers, including telomere length and DNA methylation.

DATA SOURCES: Studies were retrieved from PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus and Web of Science.

STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Study characteristics, exposures and outcomes were independently extracted and summarised.

SYNTHESIS: Standardised mean differences in telomere length were calculated using Hedges' g, and random effects meta-analysis was applied to pool effect estimates.

RESULTS: Of the 123 studies, 90 assessed DNA methylation, 28 reported telomere length and 5 reported both outcomes. No differences in telomere length were observed in offspring exposed to gestational diabetes (7 studies) or hypertensive disorders (14 studies). Each unit increase in maternal BMI was associated with a 0.27% decrease in offspring telomere length (3 studies). Exposure to cardiometabolic complications was associated with aberrant DNA methylation patterns in genes related to cardiometabolic pathways. Higher mean methylation level was reported in cord blood (2 studies) and placenta (7 studies) following exposure to diabetes and hypertensive disorders.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher maternal BMI was associated with slightly shorter offspring telomeres, while no differences were observed following exposure to gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders. Altered DNA methylation in cardiometabolic genes suggests epigenetic effects of in utero exposure, although heterogeneity in biospecimens and measurement methods limits definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Vaccination in Pregnancy with the Bivalent Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Elicits Significant Specific IgA, IgG, and Secretory Antibody Titers in Human Milk.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The RSVpreF vaccine, licensed for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated lower respiratory tract disease in infants <6 months via maternal immunization, protects infants through transplacental-transferred antibodies. Additional benefits may be conferred via vaccine-induced antibodies in human milk, but milk was not collected in clinical trials. Here, we implemented a longitudinal, observational study to characterize RSV-specific antibodies in milk of lactating individuals who did or did not receive RSVpreF in pregnancy.

METHODS: Between September 2023 and February 2025, milk samples were self-collected from 73 vaccinated and 28 unvaccinated consented individuals during the first month postpartum and frozen until assessment by Luminex-based multiplex immunoassays. This study compared milk immunoglobulin G (IgG), immunoglobulin A (IgA), and total secretory antibody titers against RSVpreF and RSV G between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups using linear models adjusted for maternal age, race/ethnicity, infant daycare attendance, and presence of older children in the home. As prespecified in the study's statistical analysis plan, the threshold for significance in this interim analysis was set at <0.0001, after adjustment for the primary multiple endpoints.

RESULTS: Mean human milk IgA, IgG, and total secretory antibody titers to RSVpreF were found to be 11- to 31-fold higher in vaccinated versus unvaccinated individuals (p-adjusted < 0.0001). Antibody titers to RSV G (not a vaccine antigen, therefore indicative of responses from prior RSV infection) were not different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: High vaccine-induced secretory antibodies may be particularly important since secretory antibody is the most durable antibody class in milk and mucosa and therefore most likely to provide ongoing protection for infants.

articles.title: Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine Use Among U.S. Children: National Health Interview Survey 2012 and 2022.
articles.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: A recent report of traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM) utilization by U.S. children found increased usage across 2007, 2012, and 2022 by age, sex, and race/ethnicity. Here, we examine cross-sectional changes between 2012 and 2022 in detail by TCIM approach and sociodemographic and health characteristics, including reports of asthma, depression, diabetes, and pain, in U.S. children aged 4-17 years.

METHODS: We examined overall TCIM use, use of practitioner-based TCIMs (TCIM directly provided by practitioners) and use of nonpractitioner TCIMs (TCIM not directly provided by practitioners). National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) in 2007, 2012, 2017, and 2022 asked questions on TCIM, but analyses were limited to 2012 and 2022 as they had the most comparable wording. Prevalence and variance estimates were calculated using Proc Survey Procedures in SAS software version 9.4 to account for NHIS's complex sample design.

RESULTS: When using the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, we found that utilization among U.S. children increased from 6.4% in 2012 to 17.8% in 2022, largely driven by use of nonpractitioner-based TCIMs, which rose from 3.2% to 14.0%. Among those using practitioner-based TCIM, use specifically for pain management increased from 28.7% to 47.6%. In both years, children who were non-Hispanic, White, Female, from families with at least one college-educated adult, and reporting current depression or asthma were more likely to utilize any TCIM.

CONCLUSIONS: Based on the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, U.S. children are increasingly utilizing TCIMs, particularly nonpractitioner approaches, mirroring similar increases in TCIM use by U.S. adults. Given the fast pace of TCIM adoption by children in the United States, future research examining the downstream impacts of these changes is warranted.

articles.title: Quantifying Data Reuse in Proteomics Using PRIDE Downloads Statistics and a Semi-Supervised LLM-Based Framework.
articles.abstract: Understanding how scientific datasets are accessed and reused is essential for resource planning and impact assessment. Here we present the PRIDE Archive download tracking infrastructure and a comprehensive analysis of 159.3 million download records from the PRIDE proteomics database (2021-2025), spanning 35,528 datasets accessed from 235 locations. The infrastructure includes nf-downloadstats, a scalable Nextflow pipeline for processing download logs, and DeepLogBot, a machine-learning framework that classifies traffic into bots, institutional download hubs, and independent user downloads. DeepLogBot combines heuristic seed selection with multi-LLM annotation (Claude and Qwen3) to produce LLM-assisted consensus labels, achieving 92.2% bot classification accuracy on a held-out test set. After separating bot traffic, analysis reveals downloads from 214 countries/regions, 249 institutional download hubs, and a concentrated reuse distribution, with the top five countries (United States, United Kingdom, Germany, China, and Canada) accounting for over 54% of independent user downloads. These findings provide actionable insights for repository infrastructure planning and highlight the importance of distinguishing automated from individual access in scientific data resources.

articles.title: Industry-Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET-Cu Current Collectors.
articles.abstract: Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film-typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high-temperature operation. Here, we report an industry-scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al2O3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll-to-roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min-1, substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al2O3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long-term cycling. The as-resulting Al2O3-coated PET-Cu CC (PET@Al2O3-Cu CC) enables 3-Ah graphite//LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C-comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET-Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low-cost and industry-scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost-efficient and high-energy LIBs.

articles.title: Willingness to Pay for Preventive and Curative Dental Procedures in Malaysia: An Urban-Rural Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for selected preventive and curative dental procedures, identify demographic, socioeconomic and behavioural factors associated with WTP, and examine urban-rural differences among Malaysian adults.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using a self-administered questionnaire based on the contingent valuation method. A total of 387 adults were recruited through multistage stratified sampling from UTC Selangor (urban) and UTC Keningau (rural). WTP was elicited for five preventive procedures (dental check-up, scaling and polishing, oral hygiene advice, fluoride varnish and fissure sealant) and two curative procedures (dental filling and extraction). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U tests and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: Median (25th-75th percentile) WTP ranged from RM50 (RM20-RM100) for oral hygiene advice to RM130 (RM60-RM240) for dental filling. Median WTP was RM100 for dental check-up (RM35-RM150), scaling and polishing (RM50-RM160), fissure sealant (RM50-RM150) and dental extraction (RM50-RM172.50), and RM80 (RM40-RM130) for fluoride varnish application. Because the payment-card upper bounds differed across procedures, these between-procedure estimates should be interpreted as conditional on the ranges presented. Higher household income, medical and dental insurance coverage and regular dental attendance were positively associated with WTP across several procedures. In unadjusted analyses, urban participants reported significantly higher WTP for all seven procedures (p < 0.05); however, study location was not independently associated with WTP after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Stated WTP varied across the selected dental procedures and was associated mainly with socioeconomic and behavioural factors. The higher observed median WTP for dental filling cannot establish that curative care is inherently valued more highly than preventive care because the procedure-specific payment-card ranges differed. The estimates should therefore be interpreted within the ranges presented.

articles.title: Impact of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors Control on Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis in Chronic Hepatitis B.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) on the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) axis in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains poorly defined.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis enrolling patients with CHB who were on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs). CMRFs were defined as per established criteria; poorly-controlled CMRFs were defined with specific cut-offs measured across 5 years. Study outcomes include fibrosis progression (liver stiffness [LS] increase by ≥ 20%), liver-related events (LREs), chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 714 NUC-treated patients (median age: 61.0 [54.5-66.7] years; 69.6% male; 90.5% undetectable HBV DNA, median NUCs duration of 14.1 [11.3-16.5] years) were followed up for 9.7 (7.2-10.2) years. LREs occurred in 112 (15.7%) patients, with annual incidence rate of 1.62 events per 100 person-years. All-cause mortality was observed in 86 (12%) patients, including 47 (6.6%) liver-related mortality. The number or types of CMRFs did not display a linear positive relationship with adverse clinical outcomes. The presence of ≥ 1 poorly controlled CMRFs is independently associated with LREs (aHR: 2.001, 95% CI: 1.350-2.965), MACE (aHR: 1.042, 95% CI: 1.030-1.081), and all-cause mortality (aHR: 2.082, 95% CI: 1.006-4.310), whereas patients having ≥ 2 and ≥ 3 poorly controlled CMRFs are independently associated with CKD progression (aOR: 1.887, 95% CI: 1.115-3.221) and fibrosis progression (aOR: 1.624, 95% CI: 1.164-2.266), respectively. The results remain robust in patients without advanced fibrosis (LS ≤ 10 kPa) at baseline.

CONCLUSION: Active optimization of CMRFs should be an integral component of CHB management in addition to NUCs therapy.

articles.title: A Photocurable Hydrogel Cardiac Patch Incorporating Formononetin-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles for Myocardial Repair After Acute Ischemia.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) induces ventricular dysfunction through ischemic necrosis and fibrotic remodeling, progressing to heart failure and constituting a major global cardiovascular burden. To address this, we developed a photocurable, hydrogel-based cardiac patch (Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel) with favorable mechanical robustness. The patch is composed of methacryloylated carboxymethyl chitosan (CACSMA) and methacryloylated gelatin (GelMA), incorporating Formononetin-loaded lipid nanoparticles (FMN@LNPs) for myocardial restoration. In vitro studies demonstrated that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel not only inhibited cardiomyocyte apoptosis by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) but also promoted migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Moreover, when a co-culture system of the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel and heart-forming organoids (HFOs) was subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) conditions, the system effectively inhibited HFO apoptosis and suppressed HFO fibrosis. In vivo experiments in MI model rats revealed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel group preserved a higher left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF: 67.2 ± 1.9%) compared to the MI group (LVEF: 41.7 ± 4.7%) at 28 days post-MI, thereby improving cardiac function. Histological analysis showed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel reduced myocardial fibrosis in the infarct border zone, promoted angiogenesis, and facilitated macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) identified pathways associated with metabolic regulation (PPAR signaling pathway), myocardial protection (PI3K-Akt signaling pathway), anti-fibrosis (inhibition of extracellular matrix remodeling), and anti-inflammatory immune regulation (TNF signaling pathway). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that the Gel-CS/FMN@LNP hydrogel promoted post-MI cardiac repair through a multi-target network involving circadian rhythm remodeling, matrix regulation, immune balance, and vascular protection. Our hydrogel system, which combines facile injectability, sustained release of active factors, and synergistic therapeutic effects, represents a promising therapeutic approach for post-MI repair.

articles.title: Methodological considerations in prognostic assessment of critically ill patients with cirrhosis.
EXPRESS: Experimental Evaluation of the Immunogenicity of Feline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) in Transfusion-Naive FEA 6-Negative Cats.
articles.journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery
articles.abstract: ObjectivesFeline Erythrocyte Antigen 6 (FEA 6) is a newly identified red blood cell (RBC) antigen in cats discovered following an unintentional sensitization event, suggesting it can be immunogenic. Its ability to consistently induce alloimmunization remains unknown. This prospective study evaluated FEA 6 immunogenicity in transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats by assessing anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production and plasma levels. A secondary objective was to bank polyclonal anti-FEA 6 antibodies.MethodsFifty-three cats underwent AB and extensive blood typing for FEAs 1-6, naturally occurring alloantibody (NOAb) screening, and compatibility testing to select donor-recipient pairs. FEA 6 prevalence was assessed in 82 type A cats. Two transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative cats received FEA 6-positive, otherwise compatible RBC transfusions and were monitored for anti-FEA 6 alloantibody production by gel column agglutination. Repeat transfusions were performed if alloantibodies became undetectable. Agreement between recipient-derived and reference anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies was evaluated in 51 type A cats using kappa statistics.ResultsFEA 6 prevalence among type A cats was 75.6% (62/82); NOAb were detected in 10.3% of screened type A cats, but none were directed against FEA 6. Both recipients developed anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies. Recipient 1 responded after two sensitizations, whereas recipient 2 responded after a single transfusion. Both reached peak titers of 1:8, with alloantibodies detectable through days 372 and 200, respectively. Recipient-derived anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies showed substantial agreement with the reference anti-FEA 6 antibody (κ = 0.64-0.78, P < .001) and almost perfect agreement with each other (κ = 0.87, P < .001).Conclusions and relevanceTransfusion of FEA 6-positive RBCs induced anti-FEA 6 alloantibodies in all transfusion-naive, FEA 6-negative recipients, supporting FEA 6 immunogenicity and its likely contribution to unexplained post-transfusion alloantibodies in cats. The resulting polyclonal antibodies may support FEA 6 typing and transfusion research, although more durable reagents remain needed.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Mineral Analysis of Feline Treats: Unrecognized Sources of Phosphorus and Calcium in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Dietary phosphorus restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management in cats. While therapeutic renal diets are formulated to limit phosphorus intake, treats also contribute to total dietary phosphorus and calcium intake. The objective of this study was to quantify the phosphorus and calcium content of some feline purée-style treats and evaluate their potential contribution to dietary mineral intake in cats with CKD.

METHODS: A convenience sample comprising four flavors of commercially available Inaba Churu purée treats and three flavors of Weurva low-phosphorus purée treats were analyzed. Phosphorus and calcium concentrations were quantified using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry and reported descriptively as milligrams per sachet and milligrams per 100 kcal.

RESULTS: Phosphorus content varied widely across products, ranging from 9 to 36 mg per sachet (64-600mg/100kcal). The evaluated Churu treats contained higher phosphorus concentrations (29-36 mg/ sachet) than the evaluated Weruva low-phosphorus formulations (9-10 mg/sachet). Calcium concentrations ranged from 0.14 to 4.06 mg per sachet (2.3-67.7 mg/100 kcal), with corresponding calcium-to-phosphorus (Ca:P) ratios ranging from 0.004 to 0.119.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Phosphorus and calcium content, including Ca:P ratios, varied substantially among the products evaluated. These differences should be considered as part of the overall dietary management of cats with CKD, particularly when treats are administered routinely.

articles.title: Bronchodilator Drug Delivery With Pressurized Meter-Dose-Inhaler Versus Jet Nebulizer With Noninvasive-Ventilation in Acute-Exacerbation of COPD: A Randomized Controlled Pharmacokinetic Endpoint Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and inhaled bronchodilator therapy are foundational in the management of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). However, optimal drug-delivery strategies during NIV remain uncertain. This study compared bronchodilator delivery via a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) interface versus standard jet nebulization during NIV.

METHODS: This randomized, open-label trial enrolled adults with hypercapnic AECOPD requiring NIV. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive ipratropium bromide via pMDI using a modified NIV mask, or via jet nebulizer integrated into the inspiratory limb. Serum ipratropium concentrations at 30 min constituted the primary bioequivalence endpoint, analysed using geometric mean ratios (GMR) and Bayesian posterior probabilities. Secondary outcomes included changes in physiologic parameters, blood gases, ventilatory asynchrony, duration of stay and cost effectiveness.

RESULTS: Forty-four patients were randomized; 41 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (pMDI n = 20, nebulizer n = 21). At 30 min, geometric mean serum ipratropium levels were higher with pMDI (110.9 pg/mL) versus nebulization (51.6 pg/mL), yielding a GMR of 2.15. Bayesian analysis showed a 95.9% probability that GMR exceeded the non-inferiority threshold (0.80). At 6 h, differences again favoured pMDI (GMR 3.18; p = 0.022; posterior probability 99.8%). Physiologic outcomes, gas exchange, and NIV duration were similar between groups, though ICU stay was shorter in the pMDI arm. No safety concerns or device-related complications were observed. Post hoc cost analysis showed markedly lower therapy cost with pMDI.

CONCLUSIONS: pMDI-based bronchodilator delivery during NIV using a customized interface is feasible, safe, cost-efficient, and achieves higher systemic drug levels than jet nebulization. Larger multicentre trials are warranted to determine clinical impact.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India CTRI/2023/07/054734.

articles.title: Quantitative UTE MRI Differences in the Meniscus Following ACL Reconstruction: A Prospective Cohort Study Using 3D Ultrashort Echo Time Adiabatic T1rho and Magnetization Transfer Imaging.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ACLR is associated with altered joint loading and increased risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity to early meniscal differences because of short-T2 signal decay and magic-angle effects.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether 3D ultrashort echo time imaging-based adiabatic T1rho (UTE-Adiab-T1rho) and ultrashort echo time imaging-based macromolecular fraction (UTE-MMF) identify regional quantitative MRI differences after ACLR.

STUDY TYPE: Prospective longitudinal cohort study.

POPULATION: 30 control scans, 19 ACLR scans at 6-12 months, and 13 ACLR scans at 12+ months were analyzed. Mean ages were 34.5, 34.5, and 37.2 years; female/male counts were 15/15, 9/10, and 8/5.

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: Participants underwent 3-T knee MRI with 3D fat-saturated UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE magnetization transfer sequences.

ASSESSMENT: UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF maps were generated with single-component exponential and two-pool magnetization transfer models. Values were extracted from four meniscal regions of interest by a blinded reader, with blinded redelineation in a subset. Patient-reported outcomes included International Knee Documentation Committee, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index scores.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied.

RESULTS: UTE-Adiab-T1rho showed significant group (q = 0.001) and region (q < 0.001) effects. Compared with controls, UTE-Adiab-T1rho was higher in LAM at 6-12 months (+5.60 ms; q = 0.035) and 12+ months (+7.09 ms; q = 0.028), and in LPM at 12+ months (+6.35 ms; q = 0.035). UTE-MMF showed significant group (q = 0.041) and region (q < 0.001) effects. LPM UTE-MMF was lower than controls at 6-12 months (-3.56 percentage points; q = 0.028) and 12+ months (-3.10 percentage points; q = 0.049). No 6-12 versus 12+ month MRI or PROM contrast survived FDR correction. MRI-PROM associations were not FDR-significant (all q ≥ 0.383).

DATA CONCLUSION: UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF mapping identified regional MRI differences after ACLR. Pairwise differences were concentrated in lateral regions, but corrected group-by-region interactions were not significant. PROMs were worse after ACLR but did not differ between postoperative windows after correction.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY STAGE: 2.

articles.title: Biodegradable Capacitive-Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration.
articles.abstract: Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive-coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo-wire interconnects, and a textile-reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio-NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery-free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB-mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro-regenerative immune modulation, calcium-related signaling, AMPK-associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB-enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic-monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

articles.title: Impact of chronic antiplatelet therapy on clinical outcomes of posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (PCS) is a leading cause of neurologic disability, yet the hospital course of patients receiving chronic antiplatelet therapy (cAPT) remains unclear. This study evaluates the effect of cAPT on PCS outcomes, including patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the National Inpatient Sample (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations in the United States for PCS with reported NIH Stroke Scale. Outcomes included inpatient mortality, routine discharge, complications, and receipt of reperfusion therapy. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for confounding factors, including stroke severity. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 148,740 PCS hospitalizations, 46,125 (31.0%) were receiving cAPT. These patients demonstrated reduced likelihood of undergoing intravascular thrombolysis (aOR: 0.902, 95% CI [0.835-0.975], p = 0.009) and EVT (0.868 [0.764-0.987], p = 0.031) compared to patients not on cAPT. Following IPTW, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.581 [0.496-0.680], p < 0.001) and increased routine discharge (1.14 [1.08-1.21], p < 0.001). These patients also demonstrated reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.767 [0.695-0.846], p < 0.001) and cerebral edema/herniation (0.761 [0.698-0.831], p < 0.001). Among hospitalizations undergoing EVT, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.556 [0.408-0.757], p < 0.001), increased routine discharge (1.60 [1.18-2.16], p = 0.003), and reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.778 [0.705-0.858], p < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: cAPT was associated with favorable inpatient outcomes in PCS, including lower mortality without an increased risk of serious neurological complications. Positive associations persisted among patients undergoing EVT. Prospective research is needed to confirm these results and guide therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Perception and satisfaction of injured workers toward rehabilitation services: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWork-related injuries pose significant physical, psychological, and economic burdens on workers, their families, and society. Rehabilitation and return-to-work (RTW) programs are essential for recovery and reintegration into the workforce. However, little is known about injured workers' perceptions of and satisfaction with rehabilitation services in Jordan.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore and compare the perceptions and satisfaction of injured employees with rehabilitation services offered by the Social Security Corporation (SSC) and evaluate their outcomes of returning to work (RTW).MethodsThis cross-sectional survey evaluated perceptions and outcomes of return-to-work and satisfaction of a random sample of injured employees in Jordan in 2022. Phone interviews were conducted by trained interviewers using a five-part questionnaire on injury and rehabilitation experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential tests, including independent t-tests, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.ResultsA total of 400 injured workers were surveyed. The mean age of the respondents was 36.1 ± 10.3 years, with the majority being males (92.5%) and married (70.3%). Less than half (46.8%) received rehabilitative services. The type and cause of injury were strongly correlated with receiving rehabilitation (p < 0.001). The mean perception rating was 3.89 ± 0.49 (out of 5), and the mean satisfaction rating among those who underwent rehabilitation was 4.52 ± 0.53. Perception was significantly higher among higher-income workers and workers who had rehabilitation services. There was a positive correlation between perception and satisfaction (r = 0.328, p < 0.001). In general, 87.5% of those who were injured returned to work.ConclusionMost injured workers successfully returned to work and expressed generally positive perceptions of SSC rehabilitation services. Enhancing awareness among employers and employees about the value and benefits of rehabilitation could further improve understanding, engagement, and utilization of these services among injured workers.

articles.title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

articles.title: Standardization of Terminology for Multiple Traumatic Dental Injuries Affecting a Permanent Tooth in a Single Episode: A Mixed-Methods Delphi Consensus Study.
articles.journal: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Inconsistent terminology in dental traumatology limits comparability between clinical, epidemiological, and prognostic studies. This is particularly relevant for traumatic dental injuries in which two or more distinct injuries affect a single permanent tooth during the same traumatic episode. Such injury patterns have been described using several overlapping terms, resulting in conceptual and reporting heterogeneity. This study aimed to establish a standardized term and corresponding definition for multiple traumatic dental injuries affecting a single permanent tooth in one traumatic episode using a mixed-methods consensus approach.

METHODS: A sequential mixed-methods design was used. First, terminology identified in a previous systematic review was analyzed to identify conceptual patterns. These findings informed the development of candidate terms and definitions. Subsequently, a modified Delphi consensus process was conducted with international experts in dental traumatology, following CREDES and ACCORD guidance. Experts rated the suitability of proposed terms and definitions on a 10-point Likert scale. Items rated > 7 by more than 70% respondents were considered to have reached consensus. A subsequent feedback exercise among practicing dentists and postgraduate students assessed broader acceptability of the proposed terminology.

RESULTS: Twenty-six terms describing multiple injuries affecting a single permanent tooth were identified in the literature and grouped into four conceptual categories: general terminology for multiple injuries, specific pairings of trauma types, tissue-level classifications, and expanded descriptive phrases. Following two Delphi rounds, the term "combination injury" reached the highest level of expert agreement (76.9%). The feedback exercise showed acceptability by 70.5% among a broader group of dentists and highlighted the need for further dissemination and clarification before widespread implementation.

CONCLUSION: The term "combination injury," supported by a refined clinically relevant definition, achieved expert consensus. Adoption of this terminology may improve consistency in clinical documentation, research reporting, and future prognostic studies. Further studies should evaluate its usability in clinical records and epidemiological datasets.

articles.title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.

articles.title: Identification and relevance of inter-tumour heterogeneity in hepatocellular adenoma according to subtypes and the context.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Different molecular subtypes of hepatocellular adenoma (HCA) can occur at the same time within the same patient, defining inter-tumour heterogeneity (ITH). We describe a series of HCA-ITH cases, most identified in Bordeaux with additional cases contributed by other international centres.

METHODS: ITH-HCA cases were subtyped by immunohistochemistry, confirmed by molecular analysis in most cases. The resulting diagnoses were HNF1A-HCA (H-HCA), inflammatory HCA (IHCA), b-catenin-mutated HCA (b-HCA) involving exon 3 or 7/8, b-catenin-mutated IHCA (b-IHCA) involving exon 3 or 7/8, sonic hedgehog HCA (sh-HCA) and unclassified HCA (UHCA).

RESULTS: We identified 26 patients with ITH-HCA including 17 women; none had underlying liver disease, whereas most men did (8/9). The largest subgroup comprised 22 patients with IHCA combined with another subtype: H-HCA (five patients); H-HCA and b-IHCA-exon 3 borderline (one patient); b-IHCA-exon 3 (six patients); b-HCA and b-IHCA exon 3 (four patients); b-IHCA-exon7/8 (two patients); sh-HCA (three patients); UHCA (one patient). The remaining four patients had sh-HCA combined with UHCA (one patient) or b-IHCA ex3 (one patient), and 2 patients with HNF1A adenomatoses, one with malignant transformation, the other associated with a b-IHCA exon3 progressed to HCC. The largest nodule was a 13 cm IHCA. One of the sh-HCA presented with bleeding.

CONCLUSION: ITH-HCA covers the whole spectrum of the HCA classification. It is rare but poses significant clinical challenges, particularly in terms of identifying those lesions at risk of malignant transformation (b-HCA or b-IHCA exon 3) or bleeding (sh-HCA). Referral to a special tertiary centre is recommended.

articles.title: Feasibility of a multidimensional interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for people with dementia and their informal primary caregivers - a randomized pilot trial with a caregiver focus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To improve the situation of informal caregivers, both supportive efforts for caregiver and rehabilitation for the person with dementia, may be needed. This randomized controlled pilot trial evaluated, among caregivers, the feasibility of a person-centred multidimensional interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for community-dwelling people with dementia that incorporated an education and support intervention for informal caregivers.

METHODS: Informal caregivers were randomized alongside the person with dementia to an intervention group (n=36) or usual care (n=31). Multiprofessional team rehabilitation for individuals with dementia and support for caregivers, were offered for one 20-week and two 4-week follow-up periods after 5 and 14 months. Caregivers were offered assessments, participation in group sessions, and individual support. After the last group session, scheduled during the last four weeks of the 20-week period, a survey was distributed. Attendance at group sessions and uptake of individual support were recorded. Blinded assessments of caregiver burden (Caregiver Burden Scale, CBS), depressive symptoms (Geriatric Depression Scale 15-item version, GDS) and health-related quality of life (Short Form 36-Health Survey, SF-36), were performed at baseline and after 5, 12, 24, and 36 months.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven participants (56%) were spouses and 26 (39%) were adult children. Participation rate in assessments of outcomes at 36 months was 100% and 87% for intervention and control group in GDS and SF-36, respectively, and 69% and 61% for CBS, respectively. Missing data were primarily due to mortality. All caregivers in the intervention group (n=36) were assessed, and all received individual interventions by team staff. Twenty-three caregivers attended group sessions, and 21 completed a survey after the last session. Twenty (95%) caregivers reported increased knowledge about supporting the person with dementia, and 19 (90%) improved coping strategies. No significant differences were observed between groups in depressive symptoms or caregiver burden, yet differences in favour of the control group were seen in subscales of health-related quality of life at 24 and 36 months.

CONCLUSIONS: The program, combining rehabilitation for the person with dementia with caregiver support, seems feasible regarding caregivers' participation in the intervention and study evaluation, and thus further evaluation in an adequately powered randomized controlled trial seems relevant. A future definitive trial should evaluate continuous support over a longer period adapted to the caregiver and refine assessment procedures, including conducting assessments during ongoing interventions to provide greater insights into rehabilitation and caregiver-support effects.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol is published online 04/11/2015 at http://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN59155421.

articles.title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations.

METHODOLOGY: This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. Classic PET/CT protocols were used: vertex to mid-thigh, skull base to mid-thigh, as well as CT-equivalent examination areas: chest/abdomen/pelvis (CAP), abdomen/pelvis (AP) and pelvis.

RESULTS: Of 200 patients with a median PSA of 1.1 ng/mL, 128 (64%) showed at least one structural correlate of BCR-PCa in the true whole-body scan. The overall detection rate did not change for limited classic PET-protocols, or CAP measurements. CAP scans would not have detected all tumor manifestations in 16 patients (8%) and not all tumor-affected organ systems in six patients (3%), AP scans in 41 patients (21%) and 18 patients (9%), pelvic scans in 61 patients (31%) and 37 patients (19%), respectively. PSA may contribute to the prospective restriction of the scan area. Patients with PSA ≤ 0.75 ng/mL showed no diagnostic gain from whole-body imaging. This means that in 45% of patients in our cohort, a limitation to CAP scan would have been possible without losing information.
