CONCLUSIONS: For a resource-saving use of routine PSMA-PET/CT, a scan from the vertex to the mid-thigh seems sufficient for detecting relevant metastases. For patients with low PSA levels, a more focused protocol that includes only the CAP region can be considered.

articles.title: Beyond Conventional Antihypertensives: RNA Interference, Endothelin Antagonism, and Aldosterone-Synthase Inhibition in the Current Therapeutic Landscape.
articles.journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
articles.abstract: Hypertension is the leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor, yet long-term adherence to antihypertensive therapy remains suboptimal. RNA-based approaches targeting hepatic angiotensinogen (AGT) have emerged as an attractive strategy for upstream renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system suppression and warrant a timely, focused review of the field. PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov and the most relevant scientific and academic databases were searched up to February 2026 to draft a narrative review of peer-reviewed clinical trials, pivotal translational studies, contemporary hypertension guidelines, and official regulatory documents relevant to innovative antihypertensive treatments, such as antisense AGT suppression (zilebesiran), endothelin antagonism (aprocitentan), and aldosterone-synthase inhibition (baxdrostat). Zilebesiran demonstrated durable blood-pressure lowering in monotherapy (KARDIA-1: placebo-adjusted ambulatory systolic blood pressure (BP) - 16.7 mmHg at month 3) and as add-on therapy (KARDIA-2: greatest effect with indapamide background). KARDIA-3 extended evaluation to a higher-risk, heavily medicated population, in which the primary endpoint was not met. The ongoing ZENITH outcomes trial will determine whether AGT silencing reduces hard cardiovascular end-points. Aprocitentan reduced office and ambulatory systolic BP in resistant hypertension (PRECISION trial) and has received regulatory approval in the USA, EU, and UK, with specific monitoring requirements for fluid retention and hematological effects. Baxdrostat demonstrated selective aldosterone-synthase inhibition with meaningful BP reductions across two phase II trials. RNA interference targeting AGT represents one of the most advanced disease-modifying platforms in hypertension, alongside the already-approved endothelin antagonism and the emerging aldosterone synthase inhibition strategy. The available evidence supports cautious optimism and continued translational investment, but not premature adoption into routine practice.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap in Physical Activity Promotion for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: A COM-B Study of Primary Care Healthcare Professionals.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify determinants of Physical activity (PA) promotion among healthcare professionals (HCPs) caring for patients with prediabetes (PD) and and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 84 HCPs involved in diabetes care. The questionnaire assessed PA-promotion practices, knowledge of PA recommendations, personal PA levels, and COM-B model constructs. Descriptive, univariate, and multivariate analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Of the 84 participants, 56% reported promoting PA most of the time, while only 29.7% correctly identified PA recommendations. Mean COM-B scores on a six-point Likert scale (1-6) were 4.00 for capability, 4.66 for motivation, and 3.24 for opportunity. HCPs who frequently promoted PA had significantly higher scores across all COM-B domains compared to non-promoters (p < 0.05). In multivariate analysis, motivation emerged as the strongest predictor of PA promotion behavior (F = 19.7), while perceived opportunity remained comparatively low.

CONCLUSIONS: PA-promotion in primary care for patients with PD and T2DM remains suboptimal despite relatively high perceived capability and motivation among HCPs. Limited opportunity- reflecting time constraints, organizational barriers, and lack of structured support may hinder implementation. Interventions targeting both motivation and system-level opportunities may enhance PA promotion and improve diabetes management in primary care settings.

articles.title: Impact of the Prognostic Nutritional Index on Outcomes in Resectable Gallbladder Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is the most common malignancy of the biliary tract, with poor survival outcomes. This study was undertaken to assess whether the prognostic nutritional index (PNI) has any impact on survival outcomes for patients with resectable GBC.

METHODS: A retrospective study analyzed patients who underwent radical resection for GBC at a tertiary care cancer center from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2024. The PNI was calculated with serum albumin and absolute lymphocyte count at the time of diagnosis (before neoadjuvant or operative treatment) and was correlated with survival.

RESULTS: The study enrolled 1312 patients, with a median follow-up period of 39.9 months. The median overall survival (OS) for the entire cohort was 28.6 months. The mean PNI for the entire cohort was 51.84. The PNI was an independent predictor of OS in both the uni- and multivariate analyses. The PNI cutoff estimated with maximally distributed rank statistics for OS was 48. The log-rank test showed that patients with PNI of 48 or higher had significantly better survival, with a differential OS in the two PNI cutoff groups of 10% at 3 years and 13.2% at 5 years.

CONCLUSION: In resectable GBC, PNI correlates with OS. This highlights systemic effects of cancer-host interaction on the inflammatory and nutritional status of patients, with an impact on long-term outcomes. Strategies aimed at improving nutritional and immunologic status in tandem with the standard-of-care cancer treatment may have an impact on survival.

articles.title: Racial and Geographic Disparities in Co-Documented Prostate Cancer and Hypertension Mortality Among U.S. Men, 1999-2024: A Multiple Cause of Death Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer is associated with incident hypertension, but this burden is largely invisible to conventional surveillance because hypertension is recorded as a contributing rather than an underlying cause of death. We characterized 25-year trends and disparities in co-documented prostate cancer and hypertension mortality among U.S. males.

METHODS: Deaths in which ICD-10 code C61 and codes I10-I15 co-appeared on the same certificate were extracted from CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (U.S. males aged ≥ 45 years, 1999-2024). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by age, race and ethnicity, Census region and urbanization, and Joinpoint regression estimated annual and average annual percent change (APC, AAPC). Four alternative cause definitions and place of death were also examined.

RESULTS: Co-documentation followed four phases: a sharp rise (APC + 31.4%, 1999-2001), a plateau, renewed acceleration (APC + 13.4%, 2018-2021), and a further plateau; the full-period AAPC was + 3.5% (95% CI 1.9 to 5.1). The AAMR rose from 6.76 to 17.78 per 100,000, and rates rose in every age, race and ethnicity, and regional stratum. Non-Hispanic (NH) Black men carried the highest burden in every year (39.79 vs. 16.91 per 100,000 in NH White men in 2024), although the Black-to-White ratio narrowed from 3.9 to 2.4. The South rose fastest (AAPC + 4.5%) and had the highest 2024 rate, having had the lowest in 1999. Mortality with prostate cancer as the underlying cause fell 42% over the same period.

CONCLUSIONS: Co-documented mortality rose across 25 years while prostate cancer mortality itself fell, so the rise cannot be attributed to a growing number of prostate cancer deaths. The burden remained concentrated in NH Black men, the South and non-metropolitan communities. The post-2021 plateau is consistent with documentation change and with reduced access to care, which these data cannot separate. The findings point to implementation of existing monitoring recommendations as the more likely constraint on reducing this disparity.

articles.title: Impact of Budesonide/Glycopyrronium/Formoterol Initiation on Healthcare Resource Utilization and Estimated Associated Costs and Greenhouse Gas Emissions Across COPD Care in Spain (ORESTES* Study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with substantial healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), high healthcare costs, and a considerable environmental burden. Triple therapy, such as budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol fumarate dihydrate (BGF), is recommended for patients with COPD not adequately controlled by dual therapy. Real-world assessments of the economic and environmental implications of COPD treatment strategies remain limited. This study estimated the impact of BGF initiation on HCRU-related costs and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Spain.

METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from the multicenter, observational, retrospective ORESTES study. Adult patients with COPD who had initiated BGF and had at least 12 months of clinical data before treatment initiation were included. HCRU and actual use of short-acting β-2 agonists (SABA) were assessed before and after BGF initiation, and associated costs and GHG emissions were estimated using unit costs and emission factors from the perspective of the Spanish National Health System.

RESULTS: A total of 718 patients were included. Following BGF initiation, annualized rates of hospitalizations, hospitalized days, emergency room admissions, primary care visits, and actual SABA use decreased by 12.9%, 9.2%, 12.0%, 4.9%, and 25.5%, respectively. Estimated annual HCRU-related costs decreased by €200.11 per patient, from €2599.46 before BGF initiation to €2399.35 after initiation, mainly driven by reduced hospitalization costs. Estimated annual HCRU-related GHG emissions decreased by 25.16 kg CO2e per patient, from 245.43 to 220.27 kg CO2e, primarily because of reductions in hospitalizations and actual SABA use.

CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis estimated reductions in HCRU-related costs and GHG emissions following BGF initiation in patients with COPD in routine clinical practice in Spain. These findings suggest that the clinical and HCRU improvements observed after BGF initiation may translate into meaningful HCRU-related economic and environmental benefits at the healthcare system level, reinforcing the broader value of clinically appropriate COPD treatment optimization.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06321731.

articles.title: Correction: Videographic Analysis of an Intervention to Improve Patient-Centered Care for People Living with Type 2 Diabetes: The QBSAFE Randomized Trial.
Discriminatory Practice in Opioid Use Disorder: In a Post-X-Waiver Era, Barriers to Buprenorphine Persist.
articles.abstract: Multiple court settlements established that it is a violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) for skilled-nursing facilities (SNF) to refuse to care for patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) who are on medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD). Yet, this discriminatory practice persists. This perspective discusses the case of a patient with cirrhosis and OUD, who was not allowed to return to his SNF due to starting buprenorphine during a hospitalization, and highlights why stigma and knowledge deficits continue to be barriers to this mortality-reducing treatment resulting in increased length of stay and negative outcomes. Sublingual buprenorphine is a commonly utilized MOUD due to its safety profile as a partial µ-opioid agonist and was what this patient with cirrhosis received. Due to the patient's resilience in the face of discrimination, the hospital's advocacy efforts including clinician-to-clinician conversations and the SNF's willingness to learn about best practice clinical guidelines and align with the ADA, this patient was able to return to the SNF on buprenorphine, despite delays in care. This perspective outlines tools that hospitalists can use in advocacy efforts with SNFs to improve MOUD treatment adoption as they leave the acute hospital setting.

articles.title: Effect of a Multilevel Intervention on Racial Disparities in Medication Adherence: An Analysis of the Rich Life Project.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in hypertension treatment and control, racial disparities in medication adherence persist. We evaluated whether a multilevel collaborative care team intervention reduced racial disparities in medication adherence among adults with uncontrolled hypertension.

METHODS: The RICH LIFE Project was a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial in 30 primary care practices in Maryland and Pennsylvania, comparing Collaborative Care/Stepped Care (CC/SC) and Standard of Care Plus (SCP) arms. Its primary outcomes were blood pressure control (systolic BP ≤ 140 mm Hg, diastolic BP ≤ 90 mm Hg) and patient activation at 12-months. Participants were non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White adults with uncontrolled hypertension. This analysis examined medication adherence, a prespecified secondary outcome, assessed at 12-months using the 4-item scale adapted from Morisky, Green, and Levine and dichotomized into adherent or nonadherent. A weighting-based approach estimated average potential outcomes within each racial group under the assigned intervention arm and the average intervention effect on the racial disparity in adherence. Sensitivity analyses categorized adherence into high, medium, and low levels and restricted follow-up to the pre-pandemic period.

RESULTS: Among 1,555 participants with treated but uncontrolled hypertension (64.2% Black, 35.8% White), Black participants were younger (mean age: 58.0 vs. 65.2 years) and more often female compared to White participants. At 12-months, adherence was similar across arms for Black participants (CC/SC: 45.4%, SCP: 46.1%) and adherence was 66.9% for White participants in the CC/SC arm versus 63.7% in the SCP arm; neither difference was statistically significant. The average intervention effect on disparity was -3.9% (95% CI: -15.8%, 9.4%), indicating no significant disparity reduction. Sensitivity analyses yielded similar findings.

CONCLUSIONS: The RICH LIFE multilevel intervention did not reduce racial disparities in medication adherence. Evidence-based strategies are needed to reduce disparities in medication adherence.

articles.title: Real-world safety and efficacy of lecanemab in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the approval of lecanemab for Alzheimer's disease (AD), evidence regarding its performance outside controlled trial settings remains scarce, leaving its real-world safety and clinical utility largely unknown.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science (through October 1, 2026) for real-world studies of lecanemab in AD. Outcomes included ARIA, discontinuation, infusion-related reactions, serious adverse events, MMSE, MoCA, CDR-SB, and amyloid PET. Random-effects models with REML and Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used. Subgroup analyses were stratified by region, APOE ε4 genotype, baseline CDR score, microhemorrhage, and white matter hyperintensity. Sensitivity analyses included leave-one-out and Egger's test. Scenario-based sensitivity analyses were also performed for overlapping cohorts. This study was registered with PROSPERO (No. CRD420261333493).

RESULTS: Thirty-seven studies were included. For overlapping cohorts, the largest dataset per outcome was retained after prioritizing peer-reviewed reports. Pooled incidence of any ARIA was 15.1% (US vs Asian studies 19.5% vs 9.7%), ARIA-E 6.5% (10.6% vs 2.5%), ARIA-H 11.5% (15.2% vs 7.0%), and symptomatic ARIA 1.3% (3.3% vs 0.1%). APOE ε4 homozygotes showed the highest rates across all three subtypes (any ARIA 34.1%, ARIA-E 10.3%, ARIA-H 18.9%), followed by heterozygotes (14.5%, 4.7%, 12.0%) and non-carriers (11.0%, 2.9%, 6.7%). Baseline microhemorrhage was associated with higher any ARIA (23.4% vs 11.5%) and ARIA-H (19.3% vs 4.2%), but not ARIA-E (5.4% vs 5.7%). ARIA incidence did not differ significantly by baseline CDR severity or deep white matter hyperintensity burden. Except for MoCA at ≤ 3 months (MD 0.515, 95% CI 0.451-0.578; 2 studies), no statistically significant changes were observed in cognitive outcomes. Amyloid PET decreased at 6 months (Centiloid MD -28.453, 95% CI -37.708 to -19.198) and 12 months (SUVR MD -0.171, 95% CI -0.291 to -0.052). Discontinuation rates were 3.5% (ARIA-related), 6.2% (adverse event-related), and 12.2% (total); infusion-related reactions were 18.5% and serious adverse events 2.8%. Sensitivity analyses supported robustness.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first large-scale systematic review and meta-analysis of real-world studies of lecanemab reporting safety and efficacy outcomes. Safety outcomes particularly ARIA may be influenced by APOE ε4 genotype and baseline microbleeds. Cognitive outcomes lacking control data cannot confirm efficacy and longer-term cross-regional controlled studies are needed.

articles.title: Association between rheumatic diseases and glaucoma risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 5.7 million individuals.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Some studies suggest that rheumatic diseases (RD) may be associated with the development of glaucoma; however, findings remain inconsistent. We therefore conducted a meta-analysis to estimate the incidence of glaucoma and assess its risk among patients with RD, to inform evidence-based diagnostic decision-making.

METHODS: Following a pre-registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024604067), we performed a systematic search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase. Pooled incidence estimates, odds ratios (ORs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using RevMan 5.4 and STATA 15.0.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies comprising 5,766,143 participants were included. RD was significantly associated with glaucoma. The pooled incidence of glaucoma among patients with RD was 4% (rate = 0.04; 95% CI, 0.03-0.06; P < 0.001). By study design, incidence/prevalence estimates were 3% in cohort studies, 9% in case-control studies, and 8% in cross-sectional studies. Compared with the general population, individuals with RD have a 66% higher risk of developing glaucoma (OR = 1.66; 95% CI, 1.15-2.40; P = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: Both the incidence and risk of glaucoma are elevated in patients with RD. These findings highlight the importance of increased ophthalmologic surveillance in this population.

articles.title: DZIP3 is a viral RNA co-sensor for RIG-I that promotes type-I interferon responses.
articles.abstract: RNA-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases have the ability to link RNA regulation to the protein ubiquitination machinery, thereby influencing diverse biological processes. Here, we identify the RNA-binding E3 ubiquitin ligase DZIP3 as an innate immune sensor that couples viral RNA recognition to downstream immune signaling. Upon viral infection, binding of viral RNA to the DZIP3 RNA-binding motif induces conformational changes that promote K63-linked auto-ubiquitination, oligomerization, and stabilization of DZIP3. Activated DZIP3 associates with RIG-I and MAVS at the mitochondrial membrane, promoting K63-linked ubiquitination of RIG-I and robust activation of the type-I interferon response. Consequently, DZIP3 depletion impairs host antiviral defense, whereas DZIP3 restricts infection by a broad range of RNA viruses. Our findings establish DZIP3 as an innate immune co-sensor that integrates viral RNA detection with ubiquitin-mediated signaling, revealing a regulatory mechanism of RIG-I-MAVS-mediated antiviral immunity.

articles.title: Critical Appraisal: "The Impact of Combined Intravenous and Topical Tranexamic Acid in Abdominoplasty with Scarpa Fascia Preservation: A Pilot Study".
articles.abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) may reduce postoperative bleeding and drainage after abdominoplasty, but the evidence for combined intravenous and topical administration remains limited. This Letter to the Editor critically appraises a recent pilot study of TXA in Scarpa fascia-preserving abdominoplasty. Important concerns include its retrospective, non-randomized design; potential temporal and indication-related confounding; absence of separate route-specific comparator groups; limited generalizability; inadequate power to detect rare thromboembolic events; and uncertain clinical relevance of the reported drainage reduction. Potential circularity in the analysis of drain duration is also discussed. Larger randomized trials with standardized protocols and patient-reported outcomes are needed before routine adoption.Level of Evidence V This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Anatomical landmark-based proportional coordinate localization in laparoscopic partial nephrectomy for completely endophytic renal tumors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate localization of completely endophytic renal tumors remains challenging in laparoscopic partial nephrectomy, and conventional intraoperative ultrasonography is experience-dependent.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate an intraoperative localization technique based on AI-assisted three-dimensional reconstruction and an anatomical landmark-based proportional coordinate system (XYZ).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 105 patients treated from May 2016 to July 2025. Patients were assigned to the XYZ coordinate-guided localization group (n = 52), using preoperative three-dimensional planning, calculation of the proportional XYZ coordinates, and intraoperative ultrasonographic verification, or the traditional localization group (n = 53), using conventional imaging and intraoperative ultrasonographic scanning. Localization efficiency, perioperative outcomes, and trifecta achievement were compared.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable. Compared with the traditional localization group, the XYZ coordinate-guided localization group had shorter localization time (225.5 s vs 317.0 s, p < 0.001), higher first-attempt localization success rate (59.62% vs 37.74%, p = 0.025), shorter warm ischemia time (21.73 min vs 27.19 min, p < 0.001), and higher trifecta achievement rate (61.54% vs 24.52%, p < 0.001). Estimated blood loss was lower (105.0 mL vs 130.0 mL, p = 0.035), blood transfusion tended to be reduced (3.85% vs 16.98%, p = 0.052), and acute kidney injury was less frequent (11.54% vs 28.30%, p = 0.032). Multivariable regression confirmed XYZ coordinate-guided localization group was associated with higher odds of achieving the trifecta and shorter warm ischemia time.

CONCLUSION: In the present study, XYZ coordinate-guided localization was associated with shorter intraoperative localization and warm ischemia times and a higher rate of achieving the trifecta than traditional localization. We will conduct prospective multicenter studies to further evaluate its effectiveness and generalizability.

articles.title: Molecular control of bacterial immunity.
articles.abstract: Phage infection places strong selective pressure on bacteria to mount a rapid immune response to ensure survival. Although recent studies have uncovered a wide diversity of bacterial immune systems, how these systems function under the tight time constraints of phage infection remains poorly understood. Here we summarize structural, biochemical and genetic insights into bacterial immunity, focusing on steps that link infection sensing to activation and effector function. We highlight how conformational change, protein assembly and spatial organization shape immune activation, and how phages employ counter-defense strategies that disrupt these processes.

articles.title: Blood, ink, and flies: A case report on the house fly (Musca domestica) feeding on active tattooing wounds.
articles.abstract: Cases of adventitious feeding on humans by non-hematophagous insects hold significant medical relevance, yet their occurrence during active body art procedures remains undocumented. This case report describes a persistent instance of opportunistic exsudatophagy by the house fly, Musca domestica Linnaeus, 1758 (Diptera: Muscidae), during a tattooing session on a healthy 32-year-old male client in Germany. Over a four-hour timeframe, four adult house flies entered the ground-floor studio through doors and windows opened for summer cross-ventilation. The insects exhibited highly persistent landing and feeding attempts directly on the freshly wounded tissue of the right lower leg, actively drinking a matrix of blood, plasma, and tattoo ink. Attraction intensified significantly once large-scale shading expanded the exuding epidermal surface area. Effective mechanical repulsion was heavily restricted by the client's enforced immobility required to ensure precise tattoo application. Following a routine aftercare protocol, the lesion healed completely without secondary bacterial infection. This report highlights a neglected hygienic hazard where the saprophagous and coprophilic ecology of synanthropic filth flies poses a mechanical vector risk for dermal pathogen inoculation, emphasizing the necessity of simple vector control strategies in tattooing facilities.

articles.title: ESR Bridges: high-risk steatotic liver disease: new developments in non-invasive tests and treatment-a multidisciplinary view.
Paradoxical inflation of prediction model performance measures in minority patient subgroups: the role of upstream bias.
articles.abstract: Predictive models in healthcare AI are expected to perform worse in underrepresented subgroups due to upstream biases such as underrepresentation, differential care access, and potential measurement error. In a previously published model predicting persistent postoperative opioid use, we surprisingly observed substantially higher model performance in Black patients (which comprised less than 5% of the sample) than in White patients. In this study, we used subgroup matching to investigate whether differences in patient characteristics contributed to the observed disparity, and replicate our findings in a second independent model. Across both models, performance differences - measured by AUC and other performance metrics - were attenuated after matching, suggesting that upstream biases may paradoxically inflate apparent model performance in minoritized patient groups. These findings challenge conventional assumptions about bias and highlight the importance of investigating performance differences using subgroup-level covariate alignment. Our results emphasize the need for careful evaluation of subgroup model metrics to ensure fair and trustworthy deployment of clinical AI.

articles.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content.
articles.abstract: We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies1. We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

articles.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent.
articles.abstract: Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored1,2. Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

articles.title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control.
articles.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

articles.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits.
articles.abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2. Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4, we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51- astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51- astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

articles.title: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial.
articles.abstract: Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

articles.title: Meier-GORLIN Syndrome Caused by Compound Heterozygous CDC6 Variants.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: Meier-Gorlin syndrome (MGORS) is a rare primordial dwarfism syndrome characterized by the triad of pre- and postnatal growth restriction, microtia, and patellar aplasia or hypoplasia. Pathogenic variants in genes involved in DNA replication licensing and initiation have been implicated in MGORS, including the uncommon disease-associated gene CDC6, for which only two affected families have been reported to date. We report a male infant born at 37 weeks' gestation to a 40-year-old primigravida via cesarean delivery due to intrauterine growth restriction and fetal intolerance of labor. He presented with severe proportionate short stature (40 cm at birth; Z score -5.22), microcephaly, bilateral microtia, cryptorchidism, hypospadias, nonpalpable patellae, and characteristic facial features including a tiny mouth and short palpebral fissures. Cardiac evaluation was normal. He developed persistent respiratory insufficiency requiring prolonged respiratory support and remains hospitalized due to tracheobronchomalacia and chronic respiratory failure. A clinical diagnosis of MGORS was suspected. Targeted gene panel testing identified a heterozygous variant in CDC6, c.920_927del (p.Ser307ThrfsTer9). Trio genome sequencing subsequently identified a second rare intronic variant, CDC6 c.461-24A>G, and confirmed that the variants were in trans. A minigene splicing assay demonstrated retention of intron 3 associated with c.461-24A>G, resulting in a predicted frameshift, p.Thr155LeufsTer8, and likely nonsense-mediated decay. We report the third family with CDC6-associated MGORS and provide functional evidence supporting the pathogenicity of a novel intronic CDC6 variant. These findings expand the mutational spectrum of CDC6-related MGORS and highlight the importance of functional studies in the interpretation of noncanonical splice variants.

articles.title: Association of Transabdominal Ultrasound Evaluation of Pelvic Free Fluid Presence, Depth, Morphology, and Location with Pathology in Reproductive-Aged Females Presenting to the Emergency Department.
articles.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between nontraumatic pelvic free fluid (PFF) characteristics (presence, depth, morphology, and location) and pathology in reproductive-aged females presenting to the emergency department (ED).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients aged 18-40 years with a uterus who were non-pregnant or in their first trimester of pregnancy and underwent pelvic ultrasound from January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2024. Exclusion criteria were bilateral oophorectomy, known ascites, recent trauma or abdominal surgery, concurrent reproductive endocrinology treatment, or inadequate ultrasound images. The primary outcome was pathology based on a composite clinical reference standard. Two blinded, ultrasound-trained emergency physicians reviewed point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) images for PFF presence, morphology (stripe, small pocket, large pocket, sliver), location, and maximal depth. Multivariable regression analyses evaluated associations between PFF characteristics and pathology. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined optimal depth thresholds for predicting pathology.

RESULTS: Of 746 pelvic ultrasound examinations, 672 patients were included. Pathology was identified in 126 of 672 (18.8%) patients and PFF was present in 174/672 (25.9%). PFF was associated with pathology (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.0; 95% CI 2.0-4.6). A 6.9-mm threshold demonstrated modest discrimination for pathology (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.69); mean PFF depth was 9.5 ± 7.8 mm. Stripe morphology, observed in 54 of 174 (31.0%) patients with PFF, was associated with increased odds of pathology compared with other morphologies (aOR 3.6; 95% CI 1.8-7.3; p < .001). Anteriorly located fluid relative to the uterus was associated with gynecologic pathology (aOR 3.4, 95% CI 1.2-9.4).

CONCLUSION: PFF characteristics on PoCUS may help refine diagnostic prioritization for pathology in reproductive-aged females presenting to the ED.

articles.title: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor regulates steroidogenic gene expression in the mouse testis and is modulated by metabolic and intracellular signaling factors.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Glucose‑dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), an incretin hormone associated with obesity and diabetes, has recently gained attention for its potential roles in reproductive physiology, although its functions in the male reproductive system remain poorly understood. This study investigated the expression and function of the GIP receptor (GIPR) in the mouse testis and examined how metabolic conditions and intracellular signaling pathways regulate Gipr expression. Immunoblotting, quantitative RT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry revealed that GIPR is expressed in Leydig cells, spermatogonia, and spermatocytes. Administration of a GIPR agonist increased the expression of steroidogenic genes, particularly Cyp11a1, in mouse testes. In MA‑10 Leydig cells, GIPR activation enhanced cAMP responsive transcription and transiently upregulated Star, Cyp11a1, Cyp17a1, and Hsd3b. Diet induced obesity resulted in increased testicular Gipr expression, whereas Gip expression remained unchanged. Pharmacological analyses demonstrated that cAMP signaling, retinoid signaling, classical and novel types of Protein Kinase C (PKC) activation, and PPARs activation modulate Gipr transcription in germ cells and Leydig cells. These findings indicate that GIP signaling directly affects Leydig cell function and suggest that metabolic conditions associated with obesity enhance GIPR responsiveness in the testis.

articles.title: Determinants and Clinical Impact of Direct Stenting in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- An ATLAS-OCT Substudy.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct stenting (DS) is a simplified strategy for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, its role in the era of advanced intravascular imaging remains incompletely defined. We aimed to identify determinants of DS use and its impact on procedural efficiency and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined stent implantation quality in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

METHODS AND RESULTS: The ATLAS-OCT trial was a prospective multicenter nationwide study mandating OCT guidance in Japan. In this subanalysis, clinical characteristics, angiographic and OCT findings, procedural metrics, and clinical outcomes were compared between patients undergoing DS and those treated with balloon predilatation. Among 436 patients, DS was performed in 32.1% (n=140), with marked interinstitutional variability (0-68.3%; P<0.01), suggesting a strong influence of operator preference. DS use was not associated with angiographic features or OCT-defined culprit plaque morphology. DS significantly reduced contrast volume and procedure time. Post-PCI OCT showed a trend towards a larger minimum stent area and greater stent expansion index with DS. These benefits were not associated with in-hospital or 1-year outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary OCT-guided primary PCI for STEMI, DS appears to be driven primarily by operator preference rather than lesion characteristics. In this study, DS was associated with improved procedural efficiency without significantly compromising OCT-assessed stent implantation quality or mid-term clinical safety.

articles.title: Bayesian Real-Time Decision Support for Strategy Optimization in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) is often prolonged, underscoring the need for timely strategy selection. Although several preprocedural scoring systems exist, they offer limited guidance regarding intraprocedural dynamics. This study aimed to develop a framework that updates success probabilities to support optimal strategy transitions during the procedure.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Two endpoints were defined: (1) successful crossing using antegrade wire escalation (AWE); and (2) time-constrained success using either AWE (<15 min) or advanced techniques (<60 min, intravascular ultrasound [IVUS] guided or retrograde). Preprocedural complexity scores (J-CTO, PROGRESS-CTO, CT-RECTOR) and procedural responses were sequentially incorporated into a Bayesian model to update real-time success probabilities. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation compared the procedural efficiency of advanced techniques. With an initial success probability of 50%, previous failure reduced the likelihood of AWE success to 26.5% and the time-based endpoint to 40.8%. Failure with intermediate-tip-load wires (~3 g) further decreased success probabilities to 6.1% for AWE and 30.5% for the time-based endpoint. When advanced strategies were required, IVUS-guided approaches showed a trend towards higher estimated procedural efficiency (76.6%) under feasibility-constrained conditions (mean difference: 3.0%; 95% credible interval: -5.6%, 11.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: A real-time Bayesian framework enables dynamic adaptation during CTO PCI and may help identify scenarios where earlier transition to advanced techniques is warranted based on evolving procedural information.

articles.title: Access, Expectations, and Experiences of Transgender and Gender Diverse Individuals With Voice and Communication Services in Brazil: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe access to speech-language pathology services, as well as perceptions and expectations regarding voice and communication among transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study was conducted online with TGD individuals aged 18 years or older residing in Brazil. Data were collected using a self-administered electronic questionnaire addressing sociodemographic characteristics, access to speech-language pathology services, voice- and communication-related experiences, vocal dysphoria, expectations regarding care, and informational needs. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used, adopting a significance level of 5%.

RESULTS: Thirty TGD individuals participated (25.7 ± 7.3 years), predominantly transgender women (46.7%) and residents of Southeastern Brazil (83.3%). Half of the participants had never sought speech-language pathology services, although 96.7% reported frequent or occasional vocal discomfort/dysphoria. The main barriers to access were high cost (63.3%), lack of qualified professionals (60.0%), and insufficient service visibility (56.7%). All participants considered greater dissemination of speech-language pathology services and specific training on gender diversity for professionals to be necessary. The most frequently reported expectations included a welcoming and safe environment (100%), technical expertise regarding trans and gender diverse voice and communication (96.7%), and individualized interventions (73.3%). Voice was perceived as important for gender identity recognition by all participants and was associated with self-esteem, social interactions, and confidence in public speaking. Vocal discomfort/dysphoria was significantly associated with seeking gender-related healthcare (P = 0.048).

CONCLUSION: TGD individuals recognize the relevance of speech-language pathology for voice, communication, and gender expression; however, important barriers continue to limit access to specialized services. The findings reveal a mismatch between the high demand for voice-related care and the utilization of speech-language pathology services, highlighting the need to expand service visibility, strengthen professional training, and promote gender-affirming and accessible models of care.

articles.title: Beyond bronchoalveolar lavage: Combined CT-guided core needle biopsy and fine-needle aspiration for the diagnosis of an atypical form of pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex infection.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)

articles.title: Comparison of two chemiluminescence assays for the detection of Helicobacter pylori antigen in stool samples.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive methods, particularly stool antigen detection, are widely employed for the diagnosis of Helicobacter pylori infection, and the evaluation of new diagnostic platforms is of practical interest. We evaluated the agreement between two chemiluminescence techniques, CLIA LIAISON® H. pylori SA and the recently developed H. pylori Ag VIRCLIA® Monotest.

METHODS: We analysed 200 stool samples from patients with suspected infection.

RESULTS: 92 samples were positive and 94 negative in both tests. Of the discordant samples, 9 were positive by LIAISON® and negative by VIRCLIA®, and 5 were positive by VIRCLIA® and negative by LIAISON®. Overall agreement was 93.0%, positive percent agreement (PPA) was 92.9%, and negative percent agreement (NPA) was 93.1%. Kappa coefficient was 0.86 (95% CI 0.79-0.93; p<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: The VIRCLIA® assay demonstrated a high level of agreement with the LIAISON® assay for the detection of H. pylori stool antigen.

articles.title: Methodological and conceptual considerations for the Steatosis Liver-Index (SLI) to stratify steatotic liver disease phenotypes.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: Comparative assessment of ultrasound and bioelectrical impedance analysis for sarcopenia screening in chronic liver disease.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia, primarily defined by low muscle mass (LMM), is associated with worse clinical outcomes in chronic liver disease (CLD). Diagnosis is challenging due to the lack of standardized tools. Ultrasound (US) offers a promising method for muscle mass assessment but requires validation against reference methods like bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA).

AIM: To evaluate the correlation and agreement between US- and BIA-based muscle measurements and the accuracy of US in identifying sarcopenia in patients with cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 88 patients with cirrhosis (HCC active or under follow-up) underwent muscle mass assessment by BIA and US of quadriceps and psoas muscles. Analyses included correlations, intraclass correlation (ICC), Bland-Altman plots, and ROC analysis to determine US cut-offs for sarcopenia.

RESULTS: Quadriceps US indices correlated with BIA-derived ASMM/h² (r = 0.35-0.45, p < 0.01), with high inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.83-0.96). The feather index demonstrated the best discriminative ability (AUROC 0.81, sensitivity 83%, specificity 72%) in this low-prevalence setting. Dual cut-off strategies improved screening value (negative predictive values above 97%).

CONCLUSION: Muscle US is a reliable, non-invasive screening tool for sarcopenia (specifically LMM) in CLD patients. Its use can reduce reliance on complex diagnostics, enabling early detection and improved clinical management.

articles.title: Periprocedural Cardiac Hemodynamic Changes and Clinical Outcomes After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To characterize serial changes in cardiac structure and function before and after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using comprehensive echocardiographic assessment and to explore their clinical relevance.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 149 patients with decompensated cirrhosis who underwent TIPS between January 2018 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, within 5 days after TIPS, and at 3-6 months of follow-up. Additional echocardiographic parameters were assessed preoperatively and early after TIPS during hospitalization to further characterize periprocedural cardiac functional changes. Echocardiographic parameters were compared across time points using repeated-measures analysis or paired tests. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to examine associations with clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: After TIPS, right atrial diameter and right ventricular end-diastolic diameter increased significantly (both P < 0.001), accompanied by a modest increase in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.029), while left ventricular structure and systolic function showed no significant changes. The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio showed a numerical decrease early after TIPS, followed by partial recovery during follow-up, although the changes were not statistically significant. Among the additional echocardiographic parameters, color M-mode flow propagation velocity (Vp) increased significantly from 62.8 to 75.1 cm/s (P = 0.04), whereas E/A, E/e', and other diastolic parameters remained largely unchanged. During a median follow-up of 1057 days, one patient developed early postoperative heart failure. Survival and overt hepatic encephalopathy did not differ significantly among groups stratified by baseline E/A ratio.

CONCLUSION: In patients with relatively preserved baseline cardiac function following appropriate pre-TIPS cardiovascular assessment, TIPS was associated predominantly with mild and transient right-sided cardiac changes, without significant deterioration in conventional left ventricular systolic function. The low incidence of clinically overt cardiac decompensation observed during follow-up suggests an acceptable cardiac risk profile in appropriately evaluated patients.

articles.title: Reporting of Fairness and Equity in Studies of Regulator-cleared Commercial AI for Acute Stroke CT: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Commercial artificial intelligence (AI) tools cleared by regulators now triage acute stroke on computed tomography (CT) scans across health systems whose patients differ in age, sex, race, socioeconomic status, and imaging hardware. It is unknown whether studies of these tools report how performance varies across such groups.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically reviewed English-language studies of commercial, regulator-cleared AI tools for adult acute stroke CT tasks. PubMed, Scopus, and PubMed Central were searched from January 1, 2018, through June 2, 2026, and Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and IEEE Xplore were searched on September 14, 2026, for records published from 2018 onward; the searches were supplemented by a backward-reference and forward-citation audit. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Eight prespecified reporting items informed by CLAIM 2024, TRIPOD+AI, and evidence on algorithmic bias were scored as reported, partial, or not reported. The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261403480).

RESULTS: Thirteen studies covering nine vendors and four CT tasks met the eligibility criteria. Only one study reported sociodemographic subgroup performance. It found lower positive predictive value for female patients than for male patients (67.3% vs. 72.7%; p = 0.02) and for Black patients than for non-Black patients (66.7% vs. 73.2%; p = 0.005). Performance by site, scanner, or protocol was reported in one other study. No included peer-reviewed study described the demographic composition of the tool's training data, and four studies acknowledged a potential bias or data gap without measuring it.

CONCLUSION: Subgroup performance was rarely reported in the included peer-reviewed evaluations. The finding of positive predictive value differences in one study is insufficient to characterize fairness across products. Missing subgroup and training-population reporting limits assessment of fairness, but does not establish that the evaluated systems are inequitable.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Chest X-Ray Radiomic Model for Identifying PRISm in Non-COPD Individuals.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Chest X-ray (CXR) is low-cost and widely accessible but lacks effective tools for identifying preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm). This study aimed to develop and validate a CXR-based radiomics-clinical combined model for PRISm screening.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Paired CXR images and clinical variables from 9 hospitals were retrospectively collected between January 2017 and December 2023. Bilateral lung fields on CXR were segmented with a fully automated segmentation algorithm. PyRadiomics was adopted to extract radiomic features. Clinical, radiomic, and combined models were established. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with DeLong's test for intermodel area under the curve (AUC) comparison. Global and local SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses were performed to interpret the model.

RESULTS: A total of 1563 participants (mean age, 63.1 ± 12.0 years; 857 males; 422 PRISm cases) were included. The combined model achieved optimal performance, with AUCs of 0.761, 0.753, and 0.759 across the training, internal, and external validation cohorts. In the external validation cohort, the combined model (AUC = 0.759, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.658-0.854) significantly outperformed individual radiomic (AUC = 0.618, 95% CI: 0.505-0.732) and clinical models (AUC = 0.655, 95% CI: 0.549-0.760; all p < 0.001). SHAP analysis revealed sex as the top predictor in the combined model, followed by radiomic features, body mass index, age, and smoking status. Local SHAP visualizations illustrated variable feature contributions for individual PRISm and normal spirometry cases.

CONCLUSIONS: The CXR-based combined model exhibits favorable stability and diagnostic performance for PRISm identification, supporting its utility as a primary-screening tool. The SHAP method enhanced the model's interpretability and clinical applicability.

articles.title: Depressive symptoms in older patients with atrial fibrillation: From clinical phenotype to targeted intervention.
Carcinomatous meningitis: Current insights into diagnosis, prognosis and management.
articles.abstract: Carcinomatous meningitis, or leptomeningeal metastasis, is a severe neurological complication of solid and haematological malignancies caused by dissemination of tumour cells within the leptomeninges and cerebrospinal fluid pathways. Clinical presentation is heterogeneous, including headache, intracranial hypertension, cranial nerve palsies or radiculopathy, which frequently leads to diagnostic delay. Diagnosis relies on converging clinical, radiological, and cerebrospinal fluid findings, with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and spine and cerebrospinal fluid cytology remaining central despite imperfect sensitivity. Emerging tools, particularly cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumour cells and circulating tumour DNA, may improve early detection and molecular characterisation. Prognosis remains poor, with survival usually measured in months. Management should be individualised according to performance status, tumour subtype, and systemic disease control, and may combine symptomatic measures, radiotherapy, targeted systemic therapies, and, in selected patients, intrathecal chemotherapy. Early integration of palliative care remains a key component of management.

articles.title: The Roles and Uses of Extracellular Vesicles in Neuroimmunologic Diseases.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Neuroimmunology is a field of neurology focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases where the immune system causes inflammation or injury to the nervous system. This includes diseases such as multiple sclerosis, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, autoimmune encephalitis, autoimmune ataxia, stiff person syndrome spectrum disorder, and neuro-rheumatologic diseases such as neuropsychiatric lupus. Over the past couple decades, there have been significant advancements in the diagnostic methods for several neuroimmunologic diseases. Despite these achievements, major needs remain for additional methods to facilitate earlier diagnosis, monitor disease activity and treatment, and elucidate disease mechanisms to aid in the development of novel or tailored treatment strategies. Currently, there is often a trade-off between the invasiveness of neurodiagnostic testing and the level of detail that can be obtained from the test without causing an iatrogenic injury. Here, we discuss the potential of extracellular vesicles (EVs), especially CNS-derived EVs obtained from peripheral blood, as a promising avenue for advancing research and clinical care in neuroimmunology. This article provides a review of the key clinical features and approaches to care for the most common neuroimmunologic diseases. We identify gaps that remain in our current understanding of these conditions. We then highlight how ongoing research in the EV field may address these existing gaps. Finally, we examine the challenges that must be overcome before EV analysis can be more widely adopted in both research and clinical care in this field.

articles.title: Neutrophil-to-Monocyte Ratio as a Predictor of Complications in Deep Neck Infections: A Multi-Centre Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Deep neck infections (DNIs) remain potentially life-threatening conditions despite advances in antimicrobial therapy and imaging techniques. This study aimed to evaluate clinical, anatomical and laboratory factors associated with complication development in patients with DNIs, with a particular focus on the prognostic value of the neutrophil-to-monocyte ratio (NMR).

METHODS: This retrospective, multi-centre study included patients diagnosed with DNIs between January 2018 and December 2023 at Harran University Faculty of Medicine Hospital (Şanlıurfa) and Diyarbakır Gazi Yaşargil Training and Research Hospital. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, infection aetiology, anatomical involvement, clinical presentation and laboratory parameters were analysed. Patients were compared according to the presence or absence of complications. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the predictive performance of inflammatory indices.

RESULTS: A total of 376 patients were included. Odontogenic infections were the most common aetiology, and the submandibular space was the most frequently involved anatomical region. Complications were significantly more common in patients with multi-space involvement, Ludwig's angina and diabetes mellitus. Patients who developed complications had significantly higher white blood cell counts, neutrophil counts, C-reactive protein levels and NMR values. ROC analysis demonstrated that NMR showed strong predictive performance for complications (AUC = 0.866). An NMR cut-off value of 20.53 provided high sensitivity and acceptable specificity for predicting complications.

CONCLUSION: Complication development in deep neck infections is closely related to the extent of anatomical spread, comorbid conditions and the severity of systemic inflammatory response. NMR appears to be a promising biomarker for early risk stratification and may provide supportive information for clinical assessment when interpreted alongside clinical and anatomical findings. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate its role in routine practice.

articles.title: Cerebrospinal fluid shunting and venous sinus stenting in sight-threatening idiopathic intracranial hypertension: a practical review of current evidence.
articles.journal: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry

articles.title: Impact of inflammation in patients with controlled standard modifiable risk factors (SMuRFs) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
Base composition reflects RNA polymerase II displacement.
articles.abstract: RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) transcribes all protein-coding and many nonprotein-coding genes in the genome. Pol II transcription termination is crucial for RNA maturation and, when disrupted, can lead to altered RNA processing and RNA export. Termination involves two intertwined processes: RNA cleavage and Pol II release from the DNA (displacement). Despite its importance, the exact mechanisms underlying Pol II displacement from the DNA remain poorly understood. Moreover, under certain cellular stress conditions, there is a partial failure of cleavage, leading to a shift of the position of displacement further downstream, a phenomenon known as readthrough transcription. We present a systematic analysis of Pol II termination across cell types and species and provide novel insights into the mechanism of displacement. Using a probabilistic mixture model to quantify Pol II dynamics across entire gene bodies from nascent RNA sequencing data, we find that genes fall into two classes defined by conserved base composition patterns near the displacement site. Both classes share a T-rich region upstream of displacement, and one class additionally carries a GC-rich region surrounding displacement. We find that GC-rich predisplacement regions have more accessible chromatin and higher levels of phospho-threonine 4 on the CTD of Pol II. Additionally, we find that displacement at genes with only the upstream T-rich pattern are more likely to be affected by perturbations that alter displacement, including heat shock, viral infection, kinase inhibition, and arsenic treatment. Thus, our work identifies two types of Pol II displacement regions, which are differentially affected by perturbations of cellular homeostasis.

articles.title: Engineering stem cell-derived islets for type 1 diabetes: genetic strategies for immune evasion and stress resilience.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune-mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, resulting in lifelong insulin dependence and disease burden. Stem cell-derived islet (SCI) replacement therapies have emerged as a promising strategy to restore endogenous insulin production; however, immune rejection, inflammatory stress, and intrinsic β-cell vulnerability remain major barriers to durable graft survival. Recent advances in gene editing and stem cell engineering have accelerated the development of next-generation SCIs designed to evade immune recognition while enhancing resistance to diabetogenic stress pathways. In this review, we examine genetic engineering strategies aimed at improving β-cell protection through modulation of antigen presentation, immune checkpoint signaling, cytokine responsiveness, and cellular stress adaptation. We discuss established immune-evasive targets including beta-2-microglobulin (B2M), class II major histocompatibility complex transactivator (CIITA), cluster of differentiation 47 (CD47), programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4-immunoglobulin (CTLA4-Ig), alongside emerging stress-resilience pathways involving renalase (RNLS), thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP), and unfolded protein response regulators. We further highlight how β-cell stress can amplify immune recognition and graft dysfunction. Collectively, these approaches support multifunctional engineered SCIs designed to overcome immune-mediated and intrinsic stress-related barriers to durable β-cell replacement. Literature was identified through PubMed and Google Scholar searches conducted from February through September 2026.

articles.title: Real-world accuracy, extended-wear performance, and user satisfaction with a novel 21-day continuous glucose monitoring system in pediatric type 1 diabetes.
Impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD): a study from the Australian National CHD Registry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 1% of live births. Advances in diagnosis and treatment have markedly improved survival, resulting in a growing adult CHD population with an increasing burden of chronic disease. Here we investigate the prevalence and impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in patients with CHD.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Cohort study from the Australian National CHD Registry, linked to national administrative health data. Control patients without T2DM were selected from the Registry and matched 3:1 by age, sex, rurality, and CHD complexity.

RESULTS: Of the 58 523 individuals with CHD in the registry, 2077 (3.55%) were identified as having T2DM. Median age was 43.1 (IQR 32.0–57.9) years, and 51% were female. T2DM was associated with a hazard ratio for all-cause mortality or heart transplantation of 1.51 (95% CI 1.31 to 1.73; p<0.001). 27.6% of CHD patients with T2DM experienced any major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) versus 10.2% of controls (p<0.001). Patients with T2DM had a higher MACE rate (rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001) and had more MACE per patient (odds ratio 4.11, p<0.001) compared with controls. Individuals with T2DM also had significantly higher rates of emergency department presentations than controls (incidence rate ratio 2.35, p<0.001) and higher rates of hospital admissions (incidence rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: T2DM in patients with CHD is associated with significantly lower transplant-free survival, substantially increased MACE, and greater healthcare utilization compared to matched CHD controls.

articles.title: Diagnosis and management of prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: a qualitative study of patient experiences.
Adebrelimab combined with apatinib and chemotherapy for neoadjuvant therapy and biomarker analysis in limited-stage small cell lung cancer: study protocol for a single-arm trial.
Development and validation of a fall risk prediction model integrating objective gait metrics for patients with cerebral small vessel disease: protocol for a two-phase study.
Glow Up: a single-centre observational study protocol to develop digital biomarkers for prediabetes screening and digital phenotyping.
Imaging-guided treatment strategy compared to standard care in at-risk individuals for rheumatoid arthritis: a cost-utility analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Some individuals present with symptoms before rheumatoid arthritis (RA) develops, and trials suggest that early treatment during this at-risk phase may be effective. This study evaluated the cost-utility of three imaging strategies—conventional MRI, modified Dixon MRI and ultrasound—combined with early treatment compared with watchful waiting in individuals at risk of RA, stratified by autoantibody status.

DESIGN: A decision tree combined with a Markov model was developed to estimate costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 2-year time horizon. Model inputs were derived from the TREAT EARLIER trial for treated patients at risk of developing RA, clinically suspect arthralgia (CSA) cohorts for untreated at-risk patients and the early arthritis clinic for patients with undifferentiated arthritis or RA. Cost-utility analyses were conducted from both the societal- and healthcare perspectives. Probabilistic and deterministic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the uncertainty of the results, and several scenarios were explored.

SETTING: Dutch hospital setting.

PARTICIPANTS: Individuals at risk of developing RA, stratified by autoantibody status.

INTERVENTIONS: Watchful waiting was compared with three imaging strategies—conventional MRI, modified Dixon MRI and ultrasound—combined with early treatment (single intramuscular glucocorticoid injection and 1-year methotrexate course) in patients with positive subclinical inflammation.

OUTCOME MEASURE: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of the interventions compared with watchful waiting. Cost-effectiveness probabilities were estimated at a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of €50,000 per QALY.

RESULTS: From a societal perspective, autoantibody-positive patients showed cost savings of €1,183 (-5348 to 2861) (ultrasound) to €1,825 (-8041 to 3861) (modified Dixon MRI). Autoantibody-negative patients had incremental costs from €21 (-3843 to 3856) (conventional MRI) to -€409 (-4499 to 3681) (modified Dixon MRI). QALYs gained ranged from 0.006 (-0.04 to 0.06) to 0.016 (-0.08 to 0.11). Probability of cost-effectiveness was 75%–80% for autoantibody-positive patients and 56%–70% for autoantibody-negative patients at a WTP of €50 000/QALY. Results were less pronounced from a healthcare perspective. Deterministic sensitivity analysis showed the results were robust to most changes in parameters; however, the results were sensitive to extreme changes in parameters related to treatment effects on quality of life (QoL) and productivity and disutilities due to treatment-related side effects.

CONCLUSIONS: Imaging-guided early treatment for arthralgia at-risk for RA may be cost-effective, particularly for autoantibody-positive patients, irrespective of imaging modality. Modified Dixon MRI seems most promising and requires further validation in CSA.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: TREAT EARLIER trial: EudraCT, 2014–004472-35 and the Netherlands Trial Register, NTR4853-trial-NL4599.

articles.title: Risk Factor Analysis of Adverse Events in Therapeutic Apheresis: A Tertiary Care Center Perspective From Eastern India.
articles.journal: Therapeutic apheresis and dialysis : official peer-reviewed journal of the International Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Therapeutic apheresis procedures are inadvertently associated with adverse events, either related to the underlying disease or to the procedure itself. This study aims to analyze the various adverse events encountered during therapeutic apheresis procedures.

METHOD: This retrospective study analyses adverse events in therapeutic apheresis procedures with reference to the type of procedure, replacement fluid used, patients' age and gender, disease type, and the adverse events encountered. The data were collected and analyzed using the software R. A p-value of less than 0.05 was taken as significant.

RESULT: A total of 348 therapeutic apheresis procedures were performed on 127 patients. Adverse events were reported in 54 procedures in 45 patients. Adverse events were significantly higher in the pediatric age group patients and those with neurological diseases, with a strong association between the number of procedures and adverse events.

CONCLUSION: This study identified the number of apheresis procedures and patients in the neurology and pediatric age groups as key risk factors for adverse events in therapeutic apheresis. Optimizing preventive strategies and close monitoring will help reduce adverse events in therapeutic apheresis.

articles.title: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies.

DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial.

SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia.

INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies.

RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24).

CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism in pregnancy associated with ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and multiple thrombophilias.
Metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas in a single patient: a 25-year evolution of three distinct lesions.
articles.abstract: A rare case of metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) over 25 years is presented. The patient initially developed a left transverse-sigmoid sinus DAVF causing pulsatile tinnitus, successfully treated with embolisation. 14 years later, he experienced pulsatile scalp lesions, numbness and muscle weakness on the right side, impairing his handwriting. Angiography revealed a superior sagittal sinus DAVF with cortical vein reflux and sinus thrombosis, treated with transvenous and transarterial embolisation, leading to significant symptom improvement. Five years later, he reported right occipital pain, retromastoid tenderness and occasional tinnitus. Imaging confirmed a new DAVF on the right transverse-sigmoid sinus (Cognard type I). He declined further treatment but remained clinically stable with unchanged MRI findings for 8 years. This case highlights the complexity of managing recurrent, metachronous DAVFs and the importance of long-term monitoring.

articles.title: Association of exercise blood pressure relative to fitness with coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise systolic blood pressure (SBP) indexed to fitness, expressed as SBP divided by peak metabolic equivalents (SBP/METpeak), is associated with cardiovascular events in patients undergoing exercise testing. We aimed to characterise the cardiac phenotype and outcomes of patients with elevated exercise SBP indexed to fitness.

METHODS: We analysed 530 participants with suspected angina from the CE-MARC trial who had complete exercise treadmill testing, invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging.
