High SBP/METpeak was defined as ≥18 mm Hg/METs. Obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) was defined by quantitative ICA as ≥70% stenosis in a major epicardial artery. Inducible ischaemia and myocardial scar were assessed by stress perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement CMR, respectively. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were defined as all-cause death and acute coronary syndrome.

RESULTS: High SBP/METpeak was present in 310 participants (58.5%) and prevalence increased progressively with the number of diseased vessels, presence of ischaemia and myocardial scar (p<0.01 for all). During a median follow-up of 15.9 years, high SBP/METpeak was associated with MACE after adjustment for age, sex, obstructive CAD, ischaemia and myocardial scar (adjusted HR per 1-unit increase, 1.02 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.03), p=0.012). Higher SBP/METpeak identified a worse prognosis in subgroups with and without obstructive CAD and in those with and without ischaemia or infarction (log-rank, p<0.005 for all).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with suspected angina, high SBP/METpeak was associated with myocardial ischaemia and scar and adverse long-term outcomes. However, this association appeared to be driven predominantly by lower exercise capacity rather than peak SBP. SBP/METpeak may therefore represent an exploratory integrated exercise marker requiring external validation.

articles.title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nomenclature change from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) better encapsulates the associated metabolic milieu. While MASLD is associated with increased heart failure (HF) risk, characteristics and outcomes of MASLD in patients with HF remain unclear. This paper aims to examine the prevalence and clinical correlates of MASLD in patients with HF from the Asian Sudden Cardiac Death in Heart Failure (ASIAN-HF) Registry.

METHODS: MASLD was defined as evidence of hepatic steatosis, with at least one of five metabolic criteria (among body mass index, glucose, blood pressure, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein thresholds). Findings were externally validated in Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS), a Hong Kong HF cohort and BIOlogy Study to TAilored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure (BIOSTAT-CHF), a HF cohort across 11 European countries.

RESULTS: Of 2698 patients with HF in ASIAN-HF, 927 (34.4%) had MASLD. They were younger, more often women and more likely to have HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) compared with those without MASLD. All-cause mortality was lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD (7.1% vs 11.7%, p=0.001), even after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR (aHR) 0.58, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.86, p=0.007). All-cause mortality was also lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD in CDARS and BIOSTAT-CHF; however, after multivariable adjustment, the association remained significant only in CDARS (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.84, p<0.001) and was attenuated in BIOSTAT-CHF (aHR 1.08, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.73, p=0.750). Using waist-to-height ratio instead of body mass index in the MASLD definition reclassified <3% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HF, MASLD is highly prevalent, especially in younger women with HFpEF and is associated with better 1-year survival than in those without MASLD.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cancer Risk in Obesity Treatment.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for numerous cancers, with body habitus, especially central adiposity, contributing to increased cancer incidence and worse prognosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), initially developed to treat Type 2 diabetes, have rapidly gained prominence as powerful anti-obesity agents due to their ability to induce significant weight loss and potential to improve metabolic health. These medications act by reducing appetite, enhancing insulin sensitivity, lowering systemic inflammation, and preferentially targeting fat mass for reduction. This review explores the growing body of evidence linking GLP-1 RA therapy to potential changes in cancer risk among individuals with obesity. To date, data suggest that GLP-1 RAs do not increase overall cancer risk and may reduce the risk of certain obesity-related cancers, likely by interrupting obesity-driven metabolic dysregulation. Still, questions remain about the beneficial effects of weight loss and the sustainability of health benefits if weight is regained after stopping treatment. We examine how GLP-1 RAs' anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects might mediate reductions in cancer risk, review emerging data regarding both protective signals and specific safety concerns (e.g., increased risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma), and emphasize the critical role of combining pharmacotherapy with lifestyle interventions to maintain muscle mass and long-term weight loss. Ultimately, given the strong link between obesity and cancer, GLP-1 RAs represent a promising new class of agents that may not only help to manage obesity but also serve as effective chemopreventive tools against obesity-associated cancers.

articles.title: Impact of nationwide parvovirus B19 DNA screening and identification of transfusion-transmitted infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Parvovirus B19 (B19V) testing is often not required to release blood components. However, the European Pharmacopoeia requires that plasma pools for fractionation contain no more than 104 IU/mL of B19V DNA. In France, pool B19 nucleic acid testing (NAT) screening was performed by Établissement Français du Sang since 2015. Since June 2024, positive pools are broken down into individual testing, allowing for the identification and management of infected blood donations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: B19V NAT is performed in pools of 96 donations (P96) with the DPX Parvo/hepatitis A virus assay (Roche). A P96 with a viral load >104 IU/mL B19V DNA is considered positive. All individual donations (IDs) testing reactive for B19V by ID-NAT are excluded from plasma-based medicinal products production, and the corresponding blood components are destroyed if not yet transfused.

RESULTS: From June 2024 to June 2025, 99 of 2,627,678 donations (3.7/100,000) were B19V DNA positive. All blood components related to 90 donations were discarded. Of the remaining nine donations, 13 blood components (9 platelet concentrates [PCs] that had undergone pathogen reduction (PR) and four red blood cell [RBC] concentrates) were transfused before NAT results were obtained. Two B19V transmissions were reported in recipients (0.078/100,000 transfusions) after transfusion of 1 PR-PC and 1 RBC unit.

CONCLUSION: B19V DNA testing for plasma intended for fractionation performed in blood services helps in avoiding transmissions by the related blood components, provided positive donations are detected prior to their transfusion. Delayed availability of results may result in transfusion-transmitted B19V infection, which cannot prevented by current PR technology.

articles.title: CAR-HEMATOTOX score to predict risk of poor outcomes with odronextamab in heavily pretreated B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
articles.abstract: The CAR-HEMATOTOX model has been shown to help identify patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) at heightened risk of severe neutropenia, serious infection and worse clinical outcomes after chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. We evaluated whether CAR-HEMATOTOX scores had prognostic value in patients with R/R follicular lymphoma (FL) or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) treated with odronextamab (cluster of differentiation [CD]20 × CD3 bispecific antibody) in the ELM-1 (NCT02290951) and ELM-2 (NCT03888105) studies. Patients were retrospectively stratified by baseline CAR-HEMATOTOX score: CAR-HEMATOTOX score low (HTlow [0-1]; FL, n = 115, DLBCL, n = 92) or CAR-HEMATOTOX score high (HThigh [≥2]; FL, n = 24, DLBCL, n = 98). The incidence of grade ≥2 cytokine release syndrome within the first 30 treatment days, and rates of grade ≥3 infection and delayed neutrophil recovery within the first 90 treatment days, were numerically higher in HThigh versus HTlow patients. In patients with HThigh versus HTlow scores, progression-free survival (PFS) was significantly poorer in DLBCL (2.6 vs. 9.6 months [p < 0.0001]), and overall survival (OS) was significantly worse in FL and DLBCL (FL, 26.5 months vs. not reached [p = 0.030]; DLBCL, 4.8 vs. 17.2 months [p < 0.0001]). These results suggest that the CAR-HEMATOTOX score may provide a readily available measure for identifying patients at risk of inferior clinical outcomes with odronextamab treatment.

articles.title: Astrocytic Cystine/Glutamate Antiporters Promote Diabetic Encephalopathy via the Induction of Glutamate Excitotoxicity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cystine/glutamate antiporter (xCT) imports extracellular cystine in exchange for intracellular glutamate. Although it plays an essential role in diabetes-associated processes such as impaired wound healing, its contribution to diabetic encephalopathy (DE) remains unclear.

METHODS: Wild-type and xCT-deficient (xCT-/-) mice were subjected to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) induction using a highfat diet combined with streptozotocin. xCT expression and activity in the brain were evaluated through quantitative polymerase chain reaction, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, chloride-dependent [14C]-L-cystine uptake, and measurements of extracellular glutamate. An adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)/Cas9 approach was employed to generate region-specific, cell type-restricted xCT knockout animals. Neuronal injury and cognitive function were evaluated via in vivo propidium iodide (PI) and neuronal nuclei antigen (NeuN) double staining, the Y-maze spontaneous alternation test, the Morris water maze test, and the object location test.

RESULTS: xCT deficiency protected mice from T2DM-induced DE. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia upregulated xCT expression via activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), thereby enhancing xCT function in hippocampal astrocytes. This maladaptive increase promoted excessive extracellular glutamate, neuronal loss, and cognitive impairment. Both astrocyte-specific deletion of xCT and pharmacological inhibition of xCT ameliorated these deficits.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify astrocytic xCT as a key driver of diabetes-induced glutamate excitotoxicity and DE progression, underscoring its potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Clinical nutrition for critically ill patients: a practical appraisal of guideline gaps and perspectives for future research.
articles.abstract: Malnutrition and accelerated muscle wasting are frequent during critical illness and make nutritional support a central component of ICU care. Nutritional support is therefore central to ICU care, but its optimal timing, route, dose, and composition remain debated. Recent randomized trials have challenged the traditional objective of early full feeding and shifted practice toward progressive, phase-adapted, and tolerance-based nutrition. This narrative review compares current international guidelines for nutritional support in critically ill adults. Guidelines broadly agree that nutrition should be initiated early after clinical stabilization, acute-phase overfeeding should be avoided, energy and protein delivery should be increased progressively, and refeeding syndrome should be anticipated. However, important differences remain regarding acute-phase energy targets, protein dosing, enteral versus parenteral nutrition, supplemental parenteral nutrition, indirect calorimetry, and enriched enteral formulas. These discrepancies reflect differences in methodology, healthcare context, and interpretation of evidence largely derived from mechanically ventilated patients during the first ICU week. Several clinically important situations remain insufficiently addressed, including prolonged critical illness, obesity, sarcopenia, post-extubation nutrition, post-ICU rehabilitation, and nutrition after major surgery. Future research should move toward individualized strategies based on illness phase, metabolic trajectory, nutritional phenotype, tolerance, and recovery-oriented outcomes.

articles.title: A hypothesis-generating study of collateral reactivation: a reanalysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes from 119 recurrent tuberculosis cases.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Recurrent tuberculosis is traditionally classified as exogenous reinfection or endogenous reactivation. We previously proposed "collateral reactivation," in which distinct Mycobacterium tuberculosis subclones derived from a hypothetical original clone are involved in separate disease episodes, in contrast to traditional endogenous ("direct-descent") reactivation. To explore whether collateral reactivation occurs beyond the single case we previously reported, we reanalyzed publicly available whole-genome sequencing data from 123 recurrent tuberculosis cases. After curation, 119 cases (pairwise single-nucleotide variant [SNV] distance, 0-18) were classified as cases of collateral or direct-descent reactivation. In 21 cases (17.6%), a hypothetical original clone could be inferred, and these cases were classified as collateral reactivation. These cases showed a higher rate of SNVs/genome/year (median 3 vs. 0.4, p < 0.0001) and a higher proportion of drug resistance-associated SNVs (23.8% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.009) than direct-descent reactivation cases. These observations support the view that collateral reactivation is not restricted to the single case we previously reported, although mixed infection or exogenous reinfection caused by closely related strains cannot be excluded as alternative explanations. To determine whether collateral reactivation should be recognized as a concept distinct from direct-descent reactivation, future studies integrating whole-genome sequencing of single colonies, lesion-specific sampling, longitudinal sampling, deep sequencing, imaging, clinical follow-up, and epidemiological exposure information will be required.

articles.title: Interpreting oxygen saturation associations in diabetic neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Brødsgaard and colleagues report associations between lower resting oxygen saturation and several neuropathy phenotypes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Three issues may sharpen their interpretation. Fingertip pulse oximetry may be influenced by neuropathy-related changes in peripheral perfusion, potentially making the exposure partly dependent on the phenotype being studied. The proposed differences between diabetes types require formal interaction testing rather than comparison of separate stratum-specific significance. Finally, discordance between continuous and dichotomous SpO₂ analyses argues for direct assessment of the exposure-response shape. Addressing these issues could clarify whether resting SpO₂ reflects systemic hypoxaemia, a peripheral perfusion-sensitive phenotype, or both.

articles.title: Personalized Prehabilitation: A Pathway to Improved Frailty Metrics and Survival in Liver Transplant Candidates.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Outpatient prehabilitation can potentially improve frailty in liver transplant (LT) candidates. Our aim was to determine the impact of prehabilitation on physical fitness and mortality, and to identify the minimum clinically important change needed to improve survival.

METHODS: In this ambispective cohort study, LT candidates underwent baseline evaluation with a dedicated physical therapist (PT) and were prescribed a personalized prehabilitation program based on their functional status. Liver frailty index (LFI), 6-min walk test (6MWT), and gait speed test (GST) were assessed. Multilevel linear mixed-effects models and multivariable survival analyses were fitted, including competing risks models against LT.

RESULTS: A total of 1275 patients (59% male, age 57±11, MELD 14±6) attended 1973 LT-PT visits. Of these, 355 attended two or more follow-up visits, participating in the prehabilitation program. At baseline, median LFI was 3.8 (3.2-4.4), 6MWT 336 m (243-403), and GST 1 (0.8-1.2); 23%, 26%, and 29% of the cohort were frail by each tool, respectively. Among subjects who improved LFI (n=226/352), the absolute change was -0.39 (-0.32 to -0.46), and for 6MWT (n=212/334) it was 54 m (43-64); fewer than half improved GST. A total of 667 (55%) patients were waitlisted, 462 (37%) transplanted, and 335 (26%) died. LFI improvement by at least 0.4 was associated with a ∼50% reduction in mortality (HR=0.56, p=0.037). Improvement in 6MWT was not associated with a survival advantage.

CONCLUSION: Individualized prehabilitation in LT candidates was associated with significant improvement in LFI and 6MWT. A minimum LFI improvement of 0.4 was associated with improved survival and could be considered a minimal clinically important difference for frailty interventions in LT candidates.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

articles.title: Human Spiroplasmosis: Clinical Characterisation of a Newly Recognised Tick-Associated Febrile Illness.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise the clinical, epidemiological, and laboratory features associated with Spiroplasma ixodetis DNA detection in adults with unexplained acute febrile illness.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 337 adults evaluated in Slovenia between 2015 and 2025. All were tested using a species-specific real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay. PCR-positive and PCR-negative patients were compared within two source cohorts using cohort-stratified analyses; 182 healthy and disease control samples were tested with the same assay.

RESULTS: S. ixodetis DNA was detected in 60 of 337 patients: 15 of 209 (7.2%) in the initial cohort and 45 of 128 (35.2%) in the targeted cohort. PCR positivity was associated with recent tick bite, leukopenia, reactive lymphocytes, thrombocytopenia, and elevated aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and lactate dehydrogenase. Headache occurred in 57 of 60 patients (95%), cerebrospinal fluid findings were normal in all 12 examined, and all 182 controls were PCR-negative. Nine patients (15%) were hospitalised; outcomes were favourable in all with available follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: S. ixodetis DNAemia was associated with a reproducible tick-associated clinical and laboratory phenotype, supporting S. ixodetis as an under-recognised cause of human febrile illness. The targeted second cohort precludes interpreting overall PCR positivity as a prevalence estimate.

articles.title: Reducing Dialysis Catheter-Associated Bloodstream Infections from Neonates to Adults: A Single Center CHG-Impregnated Cap Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.abstract: Hemodialysis catheter-related CLABSIs remain a persistent threat to patient safety, emphasizing the need for interventions that reliably reduce infection risk. We implemented a single center quality‑improvement initiative incorporating CHG-impregnated caps into standardized hemodialysis catheter care practices across adult and pediatric units, resulting in substantial reductions in hemodialysis catheter-related CLABSI rates. Findings demonstrate that CHG‑impregnated caps are a practical, scalable strategy to strengthen hemodialysis catheter safety and advance infection‑prevention outcomes.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cardio-Oncology: An Expert Consensus Statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. Endorsed by the International Cardio-Oncology Society (ICOS).
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract: This document represents a position statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) on recommendations for clinical utilization of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with cancer. The document was prepared by the SCMR Consensus Group on CMR Imaging for Cardio-Oncology and endorsed by the SCMR Publications Committee and SCMR Executive Committee. This document aims to: (1) guide the informed selection and timing of CMR; (2) inform clinical decision-making based on CMR findings; (3) educate stakeholders on the advantages and limitations of CMR in specific clinical scenarios; and (4) provide suggested protocols to tailor the CMR exam to the particular clinical question. The statements of clinical utility presented in the current document focus on the following clinical scenarios: evaluating left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction and volumes; identifying pre-clinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction with myocardial strain; and myocardial injury or edema with parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); myocarditis; vascular toxicity, with a focus on coronary artery disease (CAD); iron overload; cardiac amyloidosis; pericardial disease; valvular disease; pulmonary hypertension; and cardiac masses. Sections devoted to the special situations of radiation therapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and survivorship and pediatrics are also included. As an expert consensus statement, some recommendations are based on expert opinion and accepted best practices. This position statement emphasizes the optimal utilization of CMR in oncology patients with known or suspected cardiovascular disease; however, the authors acknowledge that CMR is not always locally available or accessible. Finally, the principal aim of this position statement is to provide specific recommendations on the use of CMR to help improve the health of cancer patients with cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: From Hypoxia to Healing: Topical Deferoxamine Enhances Wound Closure and Neovascularization in Diabetic Animal Models - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds are a major health burden, affecting approximately 0.22% of the global population. Diabetic foot ulcers are particularly common and serious, due to their high risks of infection, amputation, and recurrence. Deferoxamine (DFO), an iron chelator that stabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor signaling and promotes angiogenesis, has been studied as a topical therapy to improve diabetic wound repair in preclinical studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates topical DFO in diabetic rat and mouse wound models. Following PRISMA guidelines and prospective PROSPERO registration, MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched in November 2025. Internal validity was evaluated using the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool. The primary endpoint was wound closure rate (%), and the secondary endpoint was neovascularization assessed by immunohistochemical quantification of CD31-positive vessels. Thirty-eight studies were included in the systematic review, and 29 provided sufficient data for meta-analysis. Topical DFO significantly improved wound closure (MD 13.26%, 95% CI 10.70-15.83) and increased neovascularization (SMD 2.39, 95% CI 1.64-3.14) compared to DFO-free controls (both p < 0.0001). Benefits were observed across diverse experimental settings and delivery systems. Subgroup findings further suggest that sustained local DFO availability may enhance efficacy. Topical DFO therapy demonstrates robust preclinical evidence for improving diabetic wound healing, supporting clinical translation. Future work should prioritize developing delivery platforms that enable controlled, prolonged local DFO exposure to maximize therapeutic benefit for patients with chronic wounds, especially those with diabetes.

articles.title: Brain NaV1.5 fine-tunes neuronal excitability to facilitate female-directed social behavior in male mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5, an essential subtype for cardiac action potential generation, is also enriched in limbic regions of the brain, but its function in the central nervous system remains poorly understood.

METHODS: We performed RNAscope, immunostaining, electrophysiology, fiber photometry, Scn5a knockdown, and behavioral testing to dissect the functional role of NaV1.5 in the brain.

RESULTS: NaV1.5 channels are enriched in neurons of posterior bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNSTp) and accumulated at the axon initial segment. Activation of these tetrodotoxin-resistant channels lowers action potential threshold and accelerates spike initiation at relatively hyperpolarized levels of membrane potential (Vm). In vivo fiber photometry showed that BNSTp NaV1.5-expressing neurons in male mice were recruited by salient social stimuli and exhibited hyperpolarizing Vm dynamics during social contacts. Scn5a knockdown selectively attenuated neuronal responses to female chemosensory cues, and disrupted sex preference and female-directed behaviors.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify NaV1.5 as a Vm state-dependent regulator of BNSTp neuronal excitability, and reveal an unexpected role of this channel subtype in female-cue processing and female-directed social behavior in males.

articles.title: The Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Post-Anesthetic Pulmonary and Gastrointestinal Adverse Events: A Target Trial Emulation Using Multinational Database.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) delay gastric emptying, raising concerns about perioperative aspiration and postoperative complications. This target trial emulation aims to evaluate the association between the use of GLP-1 RAs and the risk of postoperative pulmonary and gastrointestinal adverse events in patients undergoing general anesthesia.

METHODS: Data was utilized from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. The study analyzed data from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023. Patients aged 20 years or older who underwent general anesthesia were included. These patients were divided into two groups: those using GLP-1 RA and those who were not. Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome measures were the incidence of pulmonary and gastrointestinal adverse events within one-month post-anesthesia. Hazard ratios were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models to estimate the risk of these adverse events associated with GLP-1 RA use.

RESULTS: A total of 21,948 patients were included after matching. Patients who used GLP-1 RAs demonstrated a significantly lower risk of pulmonary adverse events (HR 0.682 [0.496-0.938]). Secondary outcomes further revealed a reduction in the risk of postoperative respiratory failure, as well as postoperative hospitalization and emergency department revisits. However, there was a marginally increased risk of gastrointestinal adverse events in the GLP-1 RA group (HR, 1.034 [1.003-1.067]).

CONCLUSIONS: The use of GLP-1 RAs prior to general anesthesia was not associated with higher risk of pulmonary adverse events. A slight elevation in gastrointestinal risks was observed, although the signal remained modest.

articles.title: miR-150-5p promotes MASH progression through regulation of CTH-associated sulfur and redox metabolism.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive metabolic liver disease with few effective mechanism-based treatments. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) can coordinate disease-associated gene networks and have emerged as potential regulators and therapeutic targets in metabolic disease. Using an integrative cross-species framework that included a cynomolgus macaque model, human liver samples, and murine models of MASH, we identified dysregulated hepatocyte miR-150-5p as a conserved feature associated with disease progression. In human hepatocytes, miR-150-5p directly targeted cystathionine γ-lyase (CTH/CSE), a major hepatic hydrogen sulfide (H2S)-producing enzyme. miR-150-5p-mediated suppression of CTH contributed to reduce H2S-related signals, a lower GSH/GSSG ratio, increased oxidative stress-associated readouts, and lipid accumulation in hepatocytes. CTH re-expression attenuated these metabolic and redox-associated alterations, whereas pharmacological CTH/CSE inhibition produced corresponding changes, supporting a functional contribution of CTH to the effects of miR-150-5p. In parallel, elevated hepatocyte miR-150-5p increased TGF-β1 secretion and enhanced paracrine signals associated with hepatic stellate cell activation under lipotoxic conditions. Hepatocyte-specific inhibition of miR-150-5p using an AAV8-delivered sponge in mice with established MASH ameliorated steatosis, inflammation, and fibrotic remodeling and was associated with increased hepatic Cth expression and improvements in H2S-associated and redox-related parameters. These findings identify miR-150-5p-mediated regulation of CTH as a mechanism contributing to metabolic and redox-associated alterations in MASH and support further evaluation of hepatocyte miR-150-5p as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Association between malaria in pregnancy and children's socio-emotional development at 6 years of Age in Benin: A prospective mother-child cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2023, 12.7 million women were exposed to malaria during pregnancy (MiP), mainly in sub-Saharan Africa. MiP is linked to adverse birth outcomes and cognitive deficits in children, but its association with socio-emotional development remains unclear. This study examines associations between MiP-at any time, specific time points, and by infection frequency-and children's socio-emotional development at 6 years.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: Data derive from the MiPPAD clinical trial, the nested APEC study, and the EXPLORE follow-up at 6 years. Assessments were conducted in three health centers in the Allada district of Benin. MiPPAD enrollment occurred between 2010 and 2012. A total of 477 mother-child dyads had data on MiP and socio-emotional outcomes, and 451 on ADHD symptoms. Unadjusted and multivariate linear regressions examined associations between MiP and children's outcomes, adjusting for maternal and household characteristics. Overall, 53% of women had at least one episode of MiP or at birth. After adjustment, MiP was not significantly associated with children's total SDQ difficulties (β = -0.01, 95% CI: -0.97, 0.94), internalizing (β = 0.10, 95% CI: -0.42, 0.61), externalizing (β = -0.11, 95% CI: -0.75, 0.53), nor ADHD symptoms (β = 0.23, 95% CI: -0.26, 0.72) at 6 years. No associations were found for placental malaria, infection timing nor infection frequency after adjustment.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, in which all women received IPTp, we found no evidence of an association between MiP and children's socio-emotional difficulties or ADHD symptoms at 6 years. Small effects cannot be excluded. Future studies should assess earlier stages to identify transient effects and potential protective factors (e.g. home environment and schooling).

articles.title: Targeting the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway: Ginkgolide B mitigates oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in diabetic cognitive dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Diabetic cognitive dysfunction (DCD) is a severe complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Ginkgolide B (GB), a primary bioactive terpene lactone of Ginkgo biloba, has proven neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke, yet its role and underlying mechanisms in DCD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of GB against DCD and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms focusing on the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway. For in vivo experiments, db/db mice and high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced T2DM mice with AAV-mediated Nrf2 knockdown (sh-Nrf2) or overexpression (OE-Nrf2) were treated with GB. For in vitro studies, HT22 neurons and BV2 microglial cells exposed to high glucose were used to assess the effects of GB. The results showed that GB treatment significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia and lipid metabolic disorders in diabetic mice. Behaviorally, GB reversed deficits in cognitive abilities. At the mechanistic level, GB attenuated hippocampal neuronal loss and restored synaptic plasticity, concomitant with the suppression of oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. These neuroprotective effects were mediated by the inhibition of Keap1, leading to Nrf2 activation and the subsequent downregulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and NF-κB pathways. Notably, the cognitive benefits and neuroprotective effects of GB were completely abolished in sh-Nrf2 mice, whereas Nrf2 overexpression mimicked GB's effects without further additive benefits. Crucially, Surface-plasmon resonance and molecular docking analyses confirmed a strong direct binding affinity between GB and Keap1. These results indicated that GB alleviates DCD by targeting Keap1 to activate the Nrf2 signaling pathway, subsequently inhibiting oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Distinct seasonal lag patterns for cold- and heat-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations: a nationwide case-crossover study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature has been associated with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but evidence on seasonal lag patterns and susceptible populations remains limited. We characterized lag-specific and cumulative temperature-AECOPD associations during cold and warm seasons.

METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (2006-2019), we conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study with referent days matched by year, season, and day of the week. Cold-season exposure was defined as 2-m air temperature (November-April), and warm-season exposure as wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT; May-October). Conditional quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models estimated lag-specific and cumulative relative risks (RRs) over 0-28 days, adjusting for season-specific meteorological variables, PM10, PM2.5, and public holidays. Effect modification by age, sex, smoking, and body mass index (BMI) was examined.

RESULTS: Among 5981 AECOPD events, lower cold-season temperatures were associated with delayed, sustained risk increases over lag days 6-23, peaking at lag 14-18 (RR = 1.23; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04-1.46). Higher warm-season WBGTs were associated with an immediate increase, peaking at lag 0-1 (RR = 1.06; 95% CI 1.02-1.10), which attenuated within 1 week. Cumulative exposure-response curves were monotonic for cold-season temperature and inverted U-shaped for warm-season WBGT. Associations were stronger in men, older adults, smokers, and those with a BMI ≥25.

CONCLUSION: Cold- and warm-season ambient temperature metrics showed distinct temporal associations with AECOPD, delayed in the cold season and immediate in the warm season. Associations appeared relatively stronger among older adults, men, smokers, and individuals with higher BMI.

articles.title: From aseptic ideal to microbial community balance: The shift in gut microbiota management models for hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients.
articles.abstract: In the clinical practice of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), we find ourselves in a thought-provoking paradox. On one hand, hematologists strive to create an sterility paradigm for patients through systemic drug baths before admission, prophylactic use of broad-spectrum antibiotics during the conditioning phase, and sterile diets during transplantation. The core goal of these strategies is to minimize the risk of infection for patients. However, from a microbiological perspective, a completely different picture emerges; the gut microbiota is a virtual organ that co-evolved with the host and possesses critical metabolic and immune regulatory functions. Microbiologists point out that indiscriminate antibiotic clearing strategies, while attempting to eradicate a few pathogens, also destroy the diversity and ecological functions of the microbiota necessary for maintaining gut homeostasis, leading to the collapse of intestinal barrier, disruption of intestinal epithelial energy metabolism, and loss of immune regulatory signals. Increasing evidence suggests that this pursuit of aseptic ideal, particularly the extensive suppression of the gut microbiome by broad-spectrum antibiotics, may be opening another Pandora's box: severe gut dysbiosis, which is not only associated with unexplained fever and diarrhea but may also affect the overall reconstruction and regulation of the patient's immune system, thus correlating with the occurrence and development of challenging complications such as graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). The divergence of views between hematologists and microbiologists highlights a core cognitive conflict in contemporary HSCT management: are we treating a patient, or are we regulating a superorganism composed of human cells and symbiotic microorganisms? This comment aims to analyze this contradiction based on existing evidence and advocate for a more refined and ecologically-oriented new model of clinical management.

articles.title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in takotsubo syndrome: An interventional perspective on pathophysiology, diagnostic workflow and prognosis.
articles.abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute, usually reversible left ventricular dysfunction mimicking acute coronary syndrome without a culprit epicardial lesion. Once considered benign, it carries in-hospital mortality comparable to ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is frequently observed during the acute phase, but its relationship to TTS remains uncertain: it may be a predisposing substrate, a mediator of catecholamine-induced injury, or a consequence of edema, extravascular compression, altered loading conditions, and ventricular dysfunction, and human evidence shows association rather than mechanism. The index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) is an established invasive measure of hyperemic microvascular resistance. In TTS, IMR is frequently elevated during the acute phase, and microvascular function appears to improve as left ventricular function recovers, although often incompletely. In a pooled analysis of individual patient data from 166 patients, acute-phase IMR was the only invasive index that remained associated with mortality after adjustment. The cutoff of 54 used in that analysis is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating prognostic threshold: derived within the same dataset, it requires external validation and should be distinguished from the diagnostic threshold of ≥25 used in CMD algorithms that have not been validated in acute conditions such as TTS. Wire-based IMR remains the gold standard; angiography-derived IMR is promising, but available software platforms remain investigational. This review examines proposed mechanisms, measurement methods and their validation, prognostic evidence, and management, and outlines a workflow for future research. We conclude that the clinical utility and optimal timing of invasive coronary function testing in TTS remain uncertain.

articles.title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.

METHODS: The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000046847). Short tweet: Can multimodality imaging predict LV wall motion recovery after PCI for chronic total occlusion? Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.

articles.title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.

RESULTS: MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).

CONCLUSIONS: The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

articles.title: Clinical phenotypes, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic signatures in inflammatory myocardial disease: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory myocardial disease encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes, from subtle symptoms to fulminant heart failure. Differentiating myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis (CS), and non-confirmed cardiomyopathy (NC) remains diagnostically and prognostically challenging. We compared clinical presentation, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic profiles across these groups.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 218 adults undergoing evaluation for cardiomyopathy were classified as myocarditis (n = 81), CS (n = 84), or NC (n = 53). The primary composite outcome was all-cause mortality, mechanical circulatory support, or heart transplantation. RNA sequencing of endomyocardial biopsies was performed in 53 patients with differential expression analysis adjusted for age, RNA integrity number, and systolic blood pressure.

RESULTS: Patients with myocarditis were younger than those with CS or NC (34.7 ± 15.8 vs 57.4 ± 8.7 vs 57.6 ± 14.0 years); 70-75% were male. Myocarditis was characterized by chest pain and elevated inflammatory biomarkers, whereas CS was associated with arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction. Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested differences in event-free survival, adjusted Cox regression showed no significant between-group differences (myocarditis vs NC: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.22-4.43, p = 0.985; CS vs NC: HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.63-4.43, p = 0.307). Transcriptomic profiling revealed a more pronounced inflammatory gene expression profile in myocarditis, whereas CS showed limited differential expression and substantial overlap with NC.

CONCLUSIONS: Inflammatory myocardial disease shows distinct clinical presentations, while adjusted analyses did not demonstrate significant differences in long-term outcomes. Myocarditis showed a stronger inflammatory transcriptional signature, whereas CS exhibited limited transcriptomic differences. These findings support further investigation of RNA-based profiling as a complementary tool.

articles.title: Matching Electrode Configuration to Signal Sensing for Cardiac Electroanatomic Mapping: A Critical Appraisal.
articles.abstract: The management of cardiac arrhythmias has been transformed by electroanatomical mapping, yet it is often underappreciated how dependent mapping is to electrode configuration, sensing modality, catheter geometry, and signal-processing characteristics. This review systematically evaluates how these features influence mapping, in the context of catheters in contemporary linear, circular, grid, star-shaped and basket configurations. We compare direct sensing strategies in unipolar and bipolar configurations, monophasic action potentials, and discuss post-processing approaches including omnipolar, multipolar, and Laplacian techniques. We gather evidence from computational, experimental and clinical studies to critically discuss how these considerations may influence signal acquisition and mapping resolution in the context of clinical mapping needs and, in particular, which may be most relevant for the complex arrhythmias of atrial fibrillation (AF) and ventricular tachycardia (VT). We conclude by pointing out future directions such as ultra-high-resolution mapping, adaptive catheter geometries, computational reconstruction, and AI-guided signal interpretation.

articles.title: Update in the genetic causes of sudden cardiac death.
articles.abstract: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is a devastating complication of several different cardiovascular disorders. Over the age of 40 years the most common cause of SCD is due to coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction. In the young under the age of 40 years, inherited/genetic cardiovascular disorders are more common, including the inherited arrhythmia syndromes and the primary cardiomyopathies. Detailed evaluation of the premorbid clinical history, including a detailed family history, and comprehensive expert postmortem examination is essential. In SCD cases where no cause of death is identified at postmortem, a "molecular autopsy", i.e. genetic testing of a blood or tissue sample collected at postmortem, should be performed, with the aim of identifying a pathological genetic variant that would account for the death of the decedent, i.e. the cause of death. Establishing a cause of SCD can provide a degree of psychological relief for loved ones by providing answers and relieving uncertainty. Furthermore, clinical and genetic screening of family members is essential in the prevention of adverse clinical outcomes and SCD events in surviving relatives. Care should ideally be provided in a specialized multidisciplinary clinic setting, and this model of care should be supported and developed in countries where such services do not currently exist, reducing racial disparities and overcoming socioeconomic factors. Newer genetic and molecular developments may further improve and refine our diagnostic and management strategies with the ultimate goal to prevent SCD in our communities.

articles.title: Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI) has high mortality and limited therapies.Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the protective effects of THCQ pretreatment against LPS-induced SA-ALI and examine associated changes in gut microbiota, succinate levels, SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling and macrophage polarization.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A murine SA-ALI model was induced by intraperitoneal LPS. Lung injury, inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α), and M1/M2 polarization were assessed. Gut microbiota was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing. Succinate levels, SUCNR1, and PKA-CREB signaling were measured. Microbiota dependence was tested using antibiotic depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from THCQ-treated donors, exogenous succinate, and macrophage depletion with clodronate liposomes.

RESULTS: THCQ pretreatment attenuated lung injury, reduced IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and shifted pulmonary macrophage polarization toward an M2-like phenotype. These effects were accompanied by altered gut microbiota composition, a lower abundance ratio of bacterial families grouped in the exploratory succinate-metabolism analysis, reduced serum and pulmonary succinate levels, lower SUCNR1 expression, and increased PKA/CREB phosphorylation. Antibiotic treatment attenuated the protective responses to THCQ, while FMT from THCQ-treated donors reproduced improvements in lung injury. Exogenous succinate attenuated THCQ-mediated protection. Clo-Lipo treatment reduced the proportions of alveolar and interstitial macrophages and markedly attenuated the protective effects of THCQ.

CONCLUSION: THCQ treatment protects against SA-ALI and suppresses M1-like macrophage polarization. These effects are accompanied by changes in gut microbiota composition, reduced succinate levels, and altered SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling. Together, the findings support a role for gut microbiota-metabolism-immune interactions in the protective effects of THCQ.

articles.title: Antibody-aptamer conjugate for shear-triggered tissue plasminogen activator release and thrombolysis.
articles.abstract: Pathological blood clots cause life-threatening events, including ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction. Tissue plasminogen activator (TPA), a clinically approved fibrinolytic agent, remains a frontline therapy for clot dissolution. However, its short plasma half-life and requirement for high systemic doses pose serious risks, particularly hemorrhagic complications. To address these limitations, a shear-responsive delivery platform was engineered for controlled TPA release under pathological high-shear conditions. This system, termed Single-MOlecule-based materials with structures and functions REsponsive to Shear (SMORES), consists of a shear-amplifying microparticle conjugated to a TPA-binding aptamer and functionalized with a monoclonal antibody against integrin αIIbβ3 as a platelet-targeting element. Under elevated shear conditions, the immobilized aptamer undergoes mechanical unfolding, triggering TPA release. Optical tweezers-based single-molecule force measurements probing aptamer unfolding and refolding under constant force and varied relaxation periods revealed a narrow range of threshold forces (4-10 pN) governing the transition between folded and unfolded states. Under defined flow conditions in a microfluidic channel, single-molecule flow experiments demonstrated a flow-dependent TPA release profile, with the maximum mean release observed at 50 µL/min. COMSOL-based fluid dynamics simulations estimated a corresponding tether force of 4.76 pN and a shear rate of 3,512.9 s-1, consistent with pathological shear levels observed in stenotic vessels and aligning with optical tweezers predictions. The enzymatic activity of released TPA was confirmed by a clot dissolution assay, with the highest mean functional TPA-equivalent activity observed under the same flow condition. Together, these results demonstrate that TPA-SMORES enables mechanistically controlled, shear-triggered release of functional TPA, supporting its potential as a strategy for improving the spatial control of thrombolytic therapy.

articles.title: Mitochondrial pharmacology of cardiovascular and antidiabetic drugs: Mechanistic basis of cardioprotection and cardiotoxicity in the diseased heart.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial function is a central determinant of cardiomyocyte survival, yet mitochondrial pharmacology remains under-integrated into cardiovascular and antidiabetic drug classification, safety assessment, and therapeutic decision-making. Many cardiometabolic drugs exert direct or indirect effects on mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, calcium handling, quality control, and genome stability effects that can confer protection in some contexts while precipitating toxicity in others. In diseased myocardium, where mitochondrial reserve is constrained by ischemia, metabolic stress, ageing, or heart failure, these drug-mitochondria interactions frequently dictate clinical benefit or harm beyond the nominal drug class. This review synthesises the mitochondrial actions of widely used cardiovascular and antidiabetic therapies, including statins, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors, β-blockers, metformin, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and incretin-based agents, across acute and chronic exposure windows. We integrate key mechanistic domains encompassing electron transport chain modulation, redox and cofactor reprogramming, calcium permeability transition coupling, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and stress signalling, and relate these signatures to clinically relevant cardiometabolic disease contexts. We propose a unifying framework in which mitochondrial reserve capacity and quality control competence function as the central decision node determining whether pharmacologic mitochondrial engagement is adaptive or injurious. Finally, we outline principles for mitochondria-conscious prescribing, risk stratification, and drug development, and propose that systematic incorporation of mitochondrial endpoints into clinical trials and safety pipelines is essential for advancing precision cardiometabolic therapy.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing-based high-intensity interval training delivered via synchronous telehealth for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: protocol of the CPHIT-1 study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is becoming a leading chronic liver disease worldwide. Although exercise-centred lifestyle therapy is promising, there is still a lack of scalable, individually tailored exercise intervention strategies that can be implemented in daily practice.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the efficacy, safety and adherence of a synchronous telehealth-delivered, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET)-based high-intensity interval training (HIIT) programme, compared with a guideline-based lifestyle advice control, in adults with MASLD.

METHODS AND DESIGN: This prospective, multicentre randomised controlled trial enrolled 56 participants (aged 35-65 years) with ultrasound-confirmed hepatic steatosis, randomised (1:1) to HIIT or control. The HIIT programme comprised a 2-week run-in phase for protocol titration, followed by an 8-week home-based phase of 4 cycling sessions per week. Each session was supported by synchronous telehealth delivery, including monitoring of exercise quality via mobile hardware devices and real-time video supervision to safeguard exercise safety. Sessions consisted of 8 sets of 30s intervals at high intensity (80-90% peak VO2) separated by 60s active pauses (60-70% peak VO2). All participants received guideline-based lifestyle advice, and their usual physical activity was maintained throughout the trial. The primary endpoint was change in liver fat content after 8 weeks, assessed by magnetic resonance imaging proton-density fat-fraction; secondary endpoints included liver stiffness measurement, body mass index, cardiorespiratory fitness, overtraining metrics and protocol feasibility.

articles.title: Emergence of bimodal first passage time distributions from transcription translation coupling.
articles.abstract: Transcription and translation are fundamentally stochastic processes that drive significant variability in mRNA and protein levels within living cells. In certain cellular environments, these processes occur simultaneously, motivating the Transcription-Translation Coupled (TTC) model. We present a simple model of stochastic gene regulation incorporating TTC that yields bimodality in protein synthesis dynamics. By casting the estimation of protein synthesis times as a first-passage time (FPT) problem, we demonstrate that TTC generates robust bimodal FPT statistics with possible implications for bacterial survival strategies.

articles.title: Quantitative Analysis of Retinal Thickness and Blood Flow Changes Using SS-OCTA in Patients with Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Based on optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), we investigate the effects of Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment on retinal thickness and blood perfusion in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

METHODS: Retrospective clinical study.Forty patients (40 eyes) diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) who underwent primary 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy (25G PPV) at our hospital between January 2023 and January 2026 were enrolled. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) was performed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively to measure central macular thickness (CMT), superficial capillary plexus vessel density (SCP), deep capillary plexus vessel density (DCP), and the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and postoperative complications were also recorded, and changes in all parameters before and after treatment were compared.

RESULTS: A total of 40 patients (40 eyes) were enrolled, including 21 males (21 eyes) and 19 females (19 eyes), with a mean age of (52.65±12.91) years. The mean duration of diabetes was (10.47±6.81) years, and the baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level was (7.68%±1.34) %. At the final follow-up, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) improved significantly (P < 0.001), central macular thickness (CMT) decreased significantly, and macular edema was alleviated, showing statistically significant differences compared with preoperative values (P < 0.001). The vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus in the foveal and nasal regions was significantly improved, with a significant difference compared with the preoperative status (P < 0.05). No statistically significant differences were found in the remaining parameters ( P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The study found that in eyes with PDR following Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment, visual acuity improved and macular edema resolved. In addition to relieving vitreous traction and clearing opacified refractive media, PPV also promoted partial recovery of the superficial retinal microcirculation. However, the perfusion status of the deep capillary plexus and the architecture of the FAZ may remain relatively stable in the short term after surgery.

articles.title: Mitochondrial DNA mediated Kupffer cell activation in the pathogenesis and progression of liver diseases.
articles.abstract: The liver serves as a pivotal metabolic and immunological hub, yet its homeostatic equilibrium is highly susceptible to mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent studies have implicated mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as an important damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that links mitochondrial injury to sterile hepatic inflammation and KCs (KCs) activation. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the mtDNA mediated KCs across four major hepatic pathologies: Alcohol-associated Liver Disease (ALD), Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD), Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury (IRI), and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC). We discuss emerging evidence that Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) associated PANoptosis and nerve injury-induced protein 1 (NINJ1) mediated plasma membrane rupture may contribute to inflammatory cell death in severe liver injury, complementing rather than superseding canonical pyroptotic mechanisms. However, the extent to which mtDNA directly activates this axis remains unresolved. Furthermore, we delineate the cell-type-specific dichotomy of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) signaling, which fuels pro-inflammatory storms in KCs via the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway while promoting protective mitophagy in hepatocytes through a STING-independent cGAS-Beclin-1 interaction. In the context of immunometabolism, we also summarize preclinical evidence linking cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2) dependent mtDNA synthesis to inflammasome activation and mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) acetylation to age-associated mtDNA release during IRI. Finally, we evaluate the clinical translational potential of targeting these molecular hubs and the emergence of cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) fragmentomics-including 5' end motif analysis and diversity scoring as a transformative liquid biopsy tool for precision diagnosis. Collectively, available evidence positions mtDNA mediated KCs activation as an important, context-dependent contributor to liver disease and a potential therapeutic target, while underscoring the need for cell-specific and human validation.

articles.title: Hyperkalemia Risk in Women With Chronic Kidney Disease Receiving Spironolactone for Acne: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

articles.title: Diosmetin targets sortase A to inhibit biofilm formation and combines with vancomycin against MRSA-induced pneumonia.
articles.abstract: The global challenge of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) has driven the development of anti-virulence strategies. Sortase A (SrtA), a key enzyme responsible for anchoring surface virulence factors in MRSA, represents a promising target to overcome the limitations of conventional antibiotics. This study investigated the therapeutic potential and anti-virulence activity of diosmetin against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). In a mouse model of S. aureus-induced pneumonia, diosmetin combined with vancomycin significantly improved therapeutic efficacy, as evidenced by increased survival, reduced pulmonary bacterial burden, and attenuated histopathological injury. In vitro, diosmetin exhibited no direct antibacterial activity at concentrations up to 512 μg/mL, yet it potentiated the antibacterial effect of vancomycin, with a checkerboard assay yielding a fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) of 0.375. Diosmetin disrupted the early stages of biofilm development by impairing sliding motility, reducing exopolysaccharide (EPS) production, and inhibiting bacterial adhesion. Molecular docking identified SrtA as a potential target. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and point mutation assays further confirmed the direct interaction between diosmetin and SrtA. Meanwhile, the fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay demonstrated that diosmetin inhibited SrtA activity, with an IC50 of 9.28 μg/mL. Functional assays using the ΔsrtA mutant further supported the critical role of SrtA in mediating diosmetin's anti-virulence effects. Additionally, diosmetin protected A549 cells against S. aureus-induced pyroptosis and provided protection in a Galleria mellonella (G. mellonella) infection model. Collectively, diosmetin represents a promising anti-virulence agent targeting SrtA-associated biofilm formation and an antibiotic adjuvant for vancomycin against MRSA pneumonia.

articles.title: Advanced microscopy of oral methanogenic archaea: insights and challenges.
articles.abstract: Methanogenic archaea are an underexplored yet functionally significant component of the human oral microbiota, implicated in eubiosis and dysbiosis, periodontal disease, peri-implantitis, endodontic infections and other systemic diseases. Their low abundance, unique cell wall structures and limited taxonomic markers have historically hampered their detection and visualization. These methodological limitations have contributed to an incomplete understanding of their spatial organization and potential roles in oral health and disease. Recent advances in microscopy and molecular imaging have transformed our ability to study these microorganisms in situ, providing increasingly detailed spatial, structural and functional information. This review synthesizes established and emerging imaging approaches for oral methanogenic archaea, spanning rapid low-resolution detection, molecularly targeted imaging, ultrastructural and nanoscale characterization and emerging label-free and functional methods. We critically compare these approaches according to their taxonomic specificity, spatial resolution, quantitative capability, sample-preparation constraints and current level of validation for oral methanogens. Emphasis is placed on biological insights gained, including spatial organization within biofilms, interspecies interactions and potential functional roles in oral health and disease. Key gaps remain, including the need for standardized imaging protocols, real-time in situ visualization and quantitative methods suitable for clinical translation. To address these challenges, we propose an integrative framework combining tiered imaging modalities to guide experimental design and interpretation. By distinguishing established applications from translational and extrapolative approaches, this review provides a methodological roadmap for future imaging studies of oral methanogens and highlights priorities for their rigorous investigation in dental research.

articles.title: A validated, high-throughput and resource-efficient digital densitometric method for antiviral and cytotoxicity screening against poxviruses.
articles.abstract: Reference methods in antiviral drug discovery, the plaque reduction assay (PRA) and viral yield reduction, are labor-intensive and low-throughput, whereas tetrazolium-based metabolic assays (MTT) may be unsuitable for viruses that sustain host-cell metabolism during productive infection, including poxviruses. We validated a digital densitometric assay (DDA), which quantifies antiviral and cytotoxic effects in crystal violet-stained monolayers using the open-source software Fiji/ImageJ, against three reference methods, with vaccinia virus strain Western Reserve in Vero cells. Across 38 fungal extracts, DDA agreed substantially with PRA for antiviral activity (Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, CCC = 0.869; 95% limits of agreement -31.5 to +21.1 percentage points) and moderately with MTT for cytotoxicity (CCC = 0.677) and was more precise between replicates (median coefficient of variation 2.5% versus 5.5%). For the test compound FAC22, the half-maximal cytotoxic concentration was 238.3 μM by DDA and 46.4 μM by MTT, a five-fold difference between readouts; the half-maximal effective concentration was 8.83 μM by viral yield reduction and 11.9 μM by DDA over its non-cytotoxic range. In infected cultures MTT separated virus and cell controls by only 1.08 to 1.39-fold, precluding estimation of an effective concentration, against 1.8 to 2.3-fold for DDA. DDA met conventional robustness criteria on the screening plate (Z' = 0.818 antiviral, 0.861 cytotoxicity), comparable to PRA (Z' = 0.91), cut reagent consumption by 80 to 90%, and shortened analysis from 20 min to under 1 min per plate. DDA is accurate, resource-efficient and scalable for poxvirus screening, and applicable to other cytopathic viruses pending validation.

articles.title: Prediabetes phenotypes and the development and regression of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Prediabetes is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but few studies have assessed the impact of prediabetes phenotypes on the development and regression of MAFLD. We aimed to examine these associations.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 4768 participants with prediabetes and normal glucose tolerance (NGT) who were followed-up for approximately 3 years. Prediabetes was classified as an isolated glucometabolic defect (isolated impaired fasting glucose [IFG], impaired glucose tolerance [IGT], or impaired hemoglobin A1c [IA1c]), two glucometabolic defects (IFG + IGT, IFG + IA1c, or IGT + IA1c), and all three glucometabolic defects (IFG + IGT + IA1c). Their associations with the development and regression of MAFLD were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 4768 participants, 2687 were with MAFLD and 2081 were without. Compared with NGT, the multivariable-adjusted odds of incident MAFLD were increased by 45% (95% CI 1.09-1.93) and 92% (95% CI 1.13-3.26) among participants with two and three glucometabolic defects, respectively. In contrast, the odds of MAFLD regression were decreased by 38% (95% CI 0.46-0.82) and 62% (95% CI 0.23-0.61), correspondingly.

CONCLUSION: Greater numbers of glucometabolic defects were associated with higher odds of incident MAFLD but lower odds of MAFLD regression in prediabetes.

articles.title: From Polycystic Ovary Syndrome to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Practical Clinical Review.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), is the most common endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age. The new nomenclature reflects growing recognition that this condition extends far beyond ovarian dysfunction, encompassing complex endocrine, metabolic, cardiovascular, and psychological abnormalities. Although the diagnostic criteria remain unchanged, the name change emphasizes the multisystem nature of the disorder and may improve disease recognition and patient care. This review provides a practical, evidence-based overview of the diagnosis and management of PMOS/PCOS, highlighting recent updates from the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline. We discuss the evaluation of hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction in reproductive-aged women, as well as the assessment and treatment of obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and mental health disorders. Finally, we summarize current pharmacological therapies and emerging treatment strategies, highlighting key knowledge gaps that must be bridged to optimize long-term cardiometabolic and reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Withholding Pre-emptive Antibiotics After Pancreaticoduodenectomy in Patients with Biliary Colonization: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-emptive antibiotic therapy is frequently prescribed after pancreaticoduodenectomy when intraoperative bile cultures are positive, despite the absence of clinical infection. Evidence supporting this practice remains limited. We assessed the association between withholding pre-emptive antibiotics and postoperative outcomes in patients with biliary colonization.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 301 consecutive adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures in four French tertiary centers between January 2014 and December 2024. Overall, 89 patients received PE-ATB, and 212 did not. Propensity score matching at a 1:2 ratio yielded 138 patients, including 46 treated patients and 92 controls. The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival. Secondary postoperative outcomes were examined using prespecified exploratory non-inferiority margins.

RESULTS: Preoperative biliary stenting independently predicted PE-ATB use (odds ratio, 4.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-13.40;P =  0.019). In the matched cohort, withholding PE-ATB was compatible with the non-inferiority margin for intra-abdominal abscess, pancreatic fistula, transfusion requirements, and antibiotic duration. Overall postoperative infection did not differ significantly between groups (odds ratio, 1.42; 95% confidence interval, 0.66-3.07; P = 0.376). Five-year mortality was higher in the group without PE-ATB in the matched cohort (hazard ratio, 2.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-4.04; P = 0.048), whereas no survival difference was observed in the overall unmatched cohort.
