CONCLUSIONS: Withholding PE-ATB was not associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and was associated with reduced antibiotic exposure. The survival difference observed only after matching should be considered cautiously and may reflect residual confounding. Prospective randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Hemoadsorption to prevent acute kidney injury in elective cardiac surgery: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care.

METHODS: We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991).

RESULTS: A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p =  0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay.

CONCLUSION: Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).

articles.title: Contemporary Results of Operations for Mitral Regurgitation Caused by Posterior Mitral Valve Prolapse: The AATS Adult Quality Gateway.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In patients undergoing surgical repair of posterior mitral valve prolapse, we compared outcomes in high- and low-volume mitral surgery hospitals to those predicted by the AATS Adult Quality Gateway (AQG) and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (STS-ACSD).

METHODS: Five hospitals performed 1,517 mitral valve operations, 1,471 repairs (97%) and 46 replacements (3.0%), in the AQG training set of 55,246 adult patients. Mitral repair techniques included leaflet resection (80%), creating artificial chordae (20%), and anuloplasty (99%); surgical approach was sternotomy or partial sternotomy in 945 (64%) and anterior thoracotomy or robotic in 525 (36%). The remaining 14 hospitals performed 159 mitral valve operations, 145 repairs (91%) and 14 (8.8%) replacements.

RESULTS: In high-volume hospitals, predicted mortality by AQG was 0.87% and by STS-ACSD 0.77%; however, observed mortality was 1 patient (0.070%). For major morbidity and mortality, AQG predicted 8.1% and STS-ACSD 6.5%, but observed was 4.0%. Patients undergoing valve replacement were more likely to be older and more symptomatic and had more tricuspid regurgitation and mitral anular calcification. All repair outcomes were worse (e.g., operative mortality was 3/145 [2.1%]) in low-volume hospitals.

CONCLUSIONS: Requiring limited data entry and employing novel statistical methodology (e.g. virtual twins), AQG provided predictions similar to those of STS-ACSD, both confirming and augmenting understanding of the volume-outcome relationship in surgical management of posterior mitral valve prolapse.

articles.title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF.

STUDY DESIGN: Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019).

EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis.

OUTCOMES: Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary).

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2.

LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

articles.title: Mutidi-mensional pathogenicity characterization with emphasis on intestinal dysfunction mechanism of two circulating Chinese field strains of feline panleukopenia virus.
articles.abstract: Feline panleukopenia virus (FPV) causes severe, highly contagious infectious diseases in domestic cats, yet the comprehensive pathogenic mechanisms of circulating field isolates remain incompletely elucidated. Here, two contemporary FPV field strains (F513 and F1105) were isolated and genetically characterized from clinical samples of FPV vaccinated diarrheic cats. In vivo pathogenicity assays demonstrated that both strains induced typical FPV clinical signs, with viral replication predominantly localized to the gastrointestinal tract and shedding primarily occurring via the fecal-oral route. Both isolates triggered robust, time-dependent humoral immune responses and progressive systemic oxidative stress in infected cats. Notably, FPV infection profoundly reshaped the feline intestinal microbiota, characterized by reduced microbial diversity, depleted beneficial commensals, and expanded potential pathogens. Histopathological analyses revealed that strain F513 induced more severe systemic necrotizing inflammatory lesions than F1105, accompanied by higher viral antigen loads in all examined tissues. Mechanistically, FPV infection significantly downregulated intestinal tight junction proteins (Claudin-1, Occludin, ZO-1), while upregulating myosin light chain kinase (MLCK) and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) marker N-cadherin, thereby compromising intestinal epithelial barrier integrity. Collectively, these findings clarify the multi-dimensional pathogenic characteristics of FPV field strains and reveal a critical role for intestinal barrier dysfunction in FPV pathogenesis, providing novel insights for therapeutic target development and disease prevention.

articles.title: Distinct regulation of influenza HA head- versus stem-specific B cell responses in HA mRNA-LNP vaccinated and naïve infant African green monkeys.
articles.abstract: The generation of memory B cells following influenza virus vaccination and their rapid recruitment into the virus-specific immune response following infection is an essential component of vaccine-induced protection. We have previously reported the capacity of an influenza hemagglutinin (HA) expressing mRNA-LNP vaccine administered to newborn African green monkeys (AGM) to elicit both HA head- and stem-specific antibodies that exhibit a wide array of effector functions. Vaccine-induced responses culminated in enhanced protection compared to non-vaccinated newborn AGM. These results were noteworthy given the lack of an approved influenza vaccine for this age group. Here, we evaluated early antibody and cellular responses following respiratory infection of vaccinated versus naïve animals to gain insights into the events that may be associated with the improved protection in vaccinated newborns. Seven days following challenge, we find an increase in the number of class-switched, affinity matured antibody secreting cells in the lung draining lymph nodes of vaccinated newborns, consistent with recall of memory B cells and rapid differentiation into antibody secreting cells (ASCs). Our data are consistent with a vaccine-mediated affinity advantage in the ASC population. While this benefit extended to HA head-specific germinal center B cells, it was not the case for cells binding HA stem. This was the result of unexpectedly higher apparent affinity of these cells in naïve animals. These data extend our understanding of how vaccination and infection shape activation and differentiation of the head- and stem-specific responses in infants following influenza virus infection.

articles.title: Local antibiotic delivery using biodegradable calcium sulphate beads in paediatric masticator space infection- a technical note.
articles.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Deep masticator space infections are difficult to manage because of complex anatomy, rapid spread, necrotic tissue and limited antibiotic penetration. We describe the use of biodegradable antibiotic-loaded calcium sulphate beads in a refractory paediatric infection. A 5-year old child developed left masticator and temporal space infection with severe trismus following temporomandibular joint ankylosis surgery at an elsewhere centre. Swab culture isolated Staphylococcus pseudintermedius susceptible to vancomycin and gentamicin. After failure of systemic antibiotics, surgical debridement was performed and antibiotic-loaded calcium sulphate beads were placed for local drug delivery and dead-space management. No external drain was used. At 6 months, mouth opening improved from 9 mm to 25 mm, MRI showed resolution of infection, and no recurrence or adverse reactions were observed. This technique appears feasible as an adjunct in selected refractory paediatric masticator space infections.

articles.title: Incidence, Modifiable Risk Factors, and Management of Cardiomyopathy After Ventricular Leadless Pacemaker Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless ventricular pacemakers (LPM) provide only RV pacing, which may lead to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM). It is unclear whether LPM implant site or atrioventricular synchronous pacing using the Micra AV device influence PICM occurrence.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence of cardiomyopathy after LPM implantation and explore the association of implant site and AV-synchronous pacing with cardiomyopathy risk and LVEF evolution.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 401 patients implanted with an LPM (Micra AV n=145) between July 2015 and March 2025. PICM was defined as cardiomyopathy (≥10% LVEF decline to <50%) in the presence of >20% ventricular pacing, where pacing was considered the primary cause. Risk factors for cardiomyopathy and LVEF evolution were assessed using Cox regression and mixed-effects modelling.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 33.0 months, all-cause cardiomyopathy occurred in 13.6% (4.8%/year), while PICM was identified in 5.5% (1.9%/year). RVOT implantation was independently associated with a lower incidence of all-cause cardiomyopathy (HR 0.48, P=0.019), and a slower LVEF decline (-0.56%/year vs -1.43%/year, P=0.013) compared with mid-septal implantation. Device type (Micra AV vs VR) was not associated with clinical outcomes or LVEF evolution. Among patients developing cardiomyopathy, 92.7% were medically treated, with 57.9% achieving ≥10% LVEF improvement, and 36.8% complete recovery. CRT upgrade was uncommon (7.3%).

CONCLUSION: Cardiomyopathy occurred in a substantial proportion of LPM recipients. RVOT implantation was associated with lower cardiomyopathy incidence and slower LVEF decline, whereas Micra AV implantation did not improve clinical outcomes. However, higher AV synchrony was linked to slower LVEF deterioration.

articles.title: Impact of Surrounding Fluid Impedance on Contact Sensing Vulnerabilities and Staining Depth During Pulsed Field Ablation.
Incidence of omphalitis in foals with different umbilical disinfection protocols.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omphalitis, a common umbilical disorder in foals, can lead to complications and systemic diseases. An adequate disinfection protocol of the umbilical stump after birth is recommended to prevent infection.

OBJECTIVES: Comparison of different disinfection solutions and their efficacy in preventing omphalitis in foals.

METHODS: A total of 288 clinically healthy foals were included in this prospective, blinded cohort study during the foaling seasons of 2023 and 2024 on one stud farm. Foals were randomly allocated to one of six disinfection groups. The umbilical stump was examined clinically during the first days of life and treated twice daily with either 0.5 % chlorhexidine, 1 % iodine in 90 % ethanol, 0.05 % hypochlorous acid, or one of two different "effective microorganism" products. In an additional group, 0.5 % chlorhexidine was applied once daily. Umbilical ultrasonography was performed on the second and eighth day of life.

RESULTS: Overall, 13.9 % (40/288) of foals developed omphalitis. The lowest number of omphalitis cases was observed in the hypochlorous acid group, with 4.3 % foals affected (2/47); the highest incidence occurred in the group treated with chlorhexidine once daily, with 20.8 % of foals affected (11/53). Compared to the overall incidence of 13.9 %, hypochlorous acid was the only treatment that led to a statistically significant reduction in the incidence of omphalitis (p = 0.033). All foals recovered following antibiotic treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypochlorous acid was associated with the lowest incidence of omphalitis and appears a promising option for umbilical disinfection.

articles.title: Micronutrient Status and Host Defense Against Infectious Diseases: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Context-Dependent Interventions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Micronutrients support epithelial barrier integrity, innate immune activity, adaptive immune responses, and redox regulation. However, micronutrient deficiency and supplementation do not have uniform relationships with infectious-disease risk or clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This review examines the mechanisms linking micronutrient status with host defence and evaluates clinical evidence for micronutrient interventions across gastrointestinal, respiratory, systemic viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections.

CONTENT: Vitamins A, C, D, and E, together with zinc, selenium, and iron, influence epithelial barriers, phagocyte activity, lymphocyte function, cytokine regulation, oxidative stress, and pathogen-host nutrient competition. Clinical evidence is context-dependent. In randomised trials in children in low- and middle-income settings, therapeutic zinc was associated with shorter diarrhoeal duration, whereas findings for respiratory infections vary according to population, baseline status, intervention, and outcome. Vitamin D supplementation was associated with a modest reduction in acute respiratory infection risk in some randomised trials, but effects are not uniform across settings, and later aggregate-data meta-analyses did not confirm the earlier subgroup findings. Iron needs particular caution because deficiency can impair host defence, whereas excess available iron was associated with increased infection risk in some settings.

CONCLUSION: Evaluate micronutrient interventions by baseline nutritional status, infection type, dose, timing, concurrent treatment, outcome definition, and safety. Future studies should prioritise stratified trials, standardised outcomes, transparent reporting, and targeted supplementation over universal high-dose approaches.

articles.title: Immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory miRNA degradation via circular RNA nanosponge for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy treatment.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Managing inflammatory cytokine storms is prevalent in treatment of sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM), yet it remains a challenge to immunosuppression weaning. We herein propose an immunosuppressive termination of pro-inflammatory microRNA-33 (miR-33) degradation strategy for on-demand anti-inflammatory management. Inspired by circular RNA (cRNA) sponging capacity, we designed a miR-33-targeted sequence of cRNA (cRNA-33), including 11 of miR-33 binding sites and a single microRNA-223 (miR-223)-specific immunosuppression binding site. To improve drugability, cRNA-33 is compressed into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive polymeric assembly, and covered by tannic acid-modified hyaluronic acid to enhance cardiac inflammatory macrophage accumulation. Triggered by intracellular ROS, cRNA-33 rapidly dissociates from assembly and binds sufficient miR-33 to alleviate inflammatory actions of NLRP3 and IL-1β induction. Macrophages are subsequently shifted from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory phenotype, resulting in high expression of miR-223 that destabilizes cRNA-33 through the miR-223-responsive site to discontinue immune responses. The cRNA-33 treatment yields 80% decrease of inflammation efficacy, 90% cardiac function recovery and 87.5% survival rate in study mice. Collectively, this study has provided an advanced anti-inflammatory therapy for SICM, at a safe level.

articles.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers (IL-6, IL-10, IL-17, TNF-α) in TB patients attending a tertiary care hospital in Bhubaneswar, Odisha : a cross - sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis exhibits a complicated immune-pathogenesis that involves pro-inflammatory cytokines which modulate the host's immune responses. Cytokines like IL-6, IL-10, IL-17 and TNF-α are crucial in managing inflammation, immune protection and the progression of the disease that affect diagnostic and treatment responses.

AIM: In this study, the levels of cytokines IL-6, IL-10, IL-17 and TNF-α in the serum samples of pulmonary TB patients were estimated and their diagnostic significance was assessed and correlated with socio-demographic profile.

METHODS: Sera samples were collected from pulmonary TB patients attending a government hospital in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Levels of IL-6, IL-10, IL-17 and TNF-α were quantified using commercial ELISA kits and cytokine concentrations were determined.

RESULTS: In this study, we found the levels of IL-6, IL-10 and IL-17 to be significantly lower in the serum samples of TB positive patients as compared to the healthy controls. The majority of subjects had comparatively low TNF-α levels, while some had significantly higher quantities. IL-6, IL-10 and IL-17 concentrations were lesser in TB patients. This implies that during active TB infection, IL-6 may be downregulated. IL-10 expression may be useful as an immunological marker for diagnosis of disease and monitoring of immune status. Reduced IL-17 expression is a hallmark of active TB and could be a helpful biomarker for diagnosis.

CONCLUSION: The cytokine profiling shows that these changes could provide valuable insights into the host immune response, help in development of diagnostic biomarkers and personalized therapeutic approaches in management of TB.

articles.title: Atlastin 1 functions as a pro-viral factor during GCRV infection by interacting with viral NS80 and perturbing cellular redox homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Grass carp reovirus (GCRV) causes severe hemorrhagic disease in farmed grass carp, yet how GCRV exploits host membrane remodeling machinery to support replication remains poorly defined. Here, we identified grass carp atlastin-1 (gcATL1), an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane-fusion GTPase, as a pro-viral host factor for GCRV infection. Structural and phylogenetic analyses confirmed that gcATL1 harbors conserved domains typical of vertebrate ATL1 orthologs. Transcriptional profiling revealed broad tissue distribution of gcATL1 and significant transcriptional induction in brain upon GCRV challenge. gcATL1 localized to the ER. Functional assays showed that gcATL1 overexpression enhanced GCRV propagation, accompanied by elevated viral titers, increased viral protein abundance, and aggravated cytopathic effects. Furthermore, overexpression of gcATL1 promoted viral inclusion bodies (VIBs) biogenesis, accompanied by progressively increased ER-VIB colocalization in a GBP-domain-dependent manner. Mechanistically, gcATL1 interacted with viral NS80 via its conserved GBP domain to facilitate viral replication. Meanwhile, gcATL1 disrupted cellular redox homeostasis and exacerbated virus-elicited oxidative stress injury. Collectively, our results reveal that GCRV hijacks gcATL1 to promote infection through coordinating viral protein interaction and host stress responses, offering novel insights into the involvement of host GTPase in aquatic reovirus pathogenesis.

articles.title: Novel inflammation index and biological aging indicators in diabetes: unveiling the role of platelets in inflammaging in a population-based observational study.
articles.abstract: Inflammaging, a state of chronic low-grade inflammation, is a key contributor to biological aging and diabetes. Traditional inflammatory indices within the interplay between inflammation and epigenetic aging have remains insufficiently explored. In addition, novel platelet-based inflammatory indices based on platelets may perform better than traditional inflammatory indices. This study was a cross-sectional study with survival analysis and analyzed data from 2494 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2002. In addition to four traditional inflammatory indices (Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio [NLR], Systemic Inflammation Response Index [SIRI], Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index [SII], and Pan-Immune-Inflammation Value [PIV]). Three novel platelet-based inflammatory indices, including Neutrophil-to-Platelet Ratio (NPR), Monocyte-to-Platelet Ratio (MPR), and Monocyte-Neutrophil-to-Platelet Ratio (MNPR) were used. Biological aging indicators were quantified using seven indicators: six DNA methylation clocks (HorvathAge, HannumAge, SkinBloodAge, PhenoAge, GrimAge2Mort, and DunedinPACE) and one clinical biomarker-based measure (Klemera-Doubal BioAge). For age-based metrics, epigenetic age deviation (EAD) was defined as the residual from regression on chronological age. Multivariate linear regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to assess the associations between inflammatory indices and biological aging indicators. Cox proportional hazards models were further applied to evaluate diabetes-specific mortality risk using linked mortality follow-up data through December 31, 2019, with a median follow-up duration of 206.00 months, and mediation analysis was performed to explore the role of metabolic indicators. Traditional inflammatory indices exhibited significant associations with accelerated biological aging across multiple biological aging indicators (all P < 0.05). Compared with traditional inflammatory indices, platelet-based indices showed that the placement of platelets, particularly in the denominator versus the numerator, was associated with differences in aging-related outcomes, suggesting an important role of platelets in inflammation. Further analysis results indicate that the inflammatory indicators with platelets in the denominator perform better in risk stratification prediction. Survival analysis revealed that patients with the "High NPR + Accelerated Aging" phenotype faced the highest risk of diabetes-specific mortality, particularly within the GrimAge2Mort model. Mediation analysis identified the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index as a critical mediator in the pathway linking epigenetic aging to diabetes-related mortality. Among the evaluated indices, the novel inflammatory index, especially NPR, showed stronger associations with epigenetic aging than traditional inflammatory indices. This study not only elucidates the role of platelets in inflammaging and diabetes, but also offers a novel perspective for prognostic assessment in diabetes management.

articles.title: Outcomes after Posterior Cervical Spine Surgery: A Matched Cohort Analysis and Comparison of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Bariatric Surgery in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Obesity and diabetes can increase perioperative risk, especially in posterior cervical spine surgery. Bariatric surgery provides durable weight loss but carries surgical and nutritional risks, while glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are non-surgical alternatives that may optimize weight and metabolic status preoperatively. Evidence evaluating GLP-1 therapy in spine surgery is limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate associations between preoperative GLP-1 RA use and perioperative, short-term, and long-term complications following posterior cervical spine surgery in patients with type 2 diabetes, including comparisons to matched controls and patients with prior bariatric surgery.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective database analysis.

PATIENT SAMPLE: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin undergoing posterior cervical spine surgery between 2010 and 2023 were identified in the PearlDiver Mariner database. Patients were stratified into GLP-1 users, non-GLP-1 controls, and patients with prior bariatric surgery.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Physiologic measures included perioperative outcomes and postoperative complications assessed at 90 days and 2 years, including pneumonitis, surgical site infection, revision surgery, readmission, nutritional deficiency, and other medical and surgical complications.

METHODS: The PearlDiver Mariner database was queried for eligible patients. Propensity-score matching adjusted for baseline cohort differences. Outcomes included perioperative, 90-day, and 2-year complications, with BMI-stratified analyses conducted within the matched GLP-1 and control cohort. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: GLP-1 users demonstrated lower odds of perioperative complications, including pneumonitis (OR 0.57; 95% CI 0.43-0.75; p <0.001). At 90 days, GLP-1 users experienced reduced odds of surgical site infection (OR 0.72; 95% CI 0.65-0.80; p <0.001), revision surgery (OR 0.33; 95% CI 0.29-0.36; p <0.001), readmission (OR 0.82; 95% CI 0.76-0.90; p <0.001), and other complications. At 2 years, GLP-1 users had lower odds of revision surgery (OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.28-0.34; p <0.001), nutritional deficiency (OR 0.62; 95% CI 0.59-0.66; p <0.001), and other complications. Exploratory BMI-stratified analyses suggested similar directional trends across overweight and obese patients. Comparisons to prior bariatric surgery patients showed no significant differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative GLP-1 RA use was associated with reduced perioperative, short-term, and long-term complications following posterior cervical spine surgery in patients with type 2 diabetes. When compared with a matched bariatric surgery cohort, no significant differences in postoperative outcomes were observed. These findings should be interpreted in the context of potential residual confounding and support further prospective investigation of GLP-1 therapy as a strategy for preoperative metabolic optimization in posterior cervical spine surgery.

CLASSIFICATIONS: Cervical Spine, Outcomes Research, Risk Factors, Perioperative Complications.

articles.title: Harmonizing spatially fractionated radiation therapy: consensus and roadmap from an ESTRO workshop.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Spatially fractionated radiation therapy (SFRT) intentionally delivers nonuniform dose distributions characterized by alternating high-dose peaks and low-dose valleys, with therapeutic potential for complex, inoperable bulky tumors. Although clinical adoption is expanding, clinical implementation and practices remain heterogeneous across institutions. This consensus aims to identify system-level barriers to harmonized clinical implementation of SFRT and formulate consensus-based recommendations to enable reproducible multi-institutional integration.

METHODS: The 2025 ESTRO Physics Workshop convened multidisciplinary international experts to evaluate current implementation practices and develop harmonization priorities through structured consensus discussions. Twenty-eight delegates participated, representing centers across Europe, the United States, China, and Australia. Core domains included dose recording and reporting specifications, commissioning and quality assurance (QA), motion management, registry infrastructure, and governance.

RESULTS: Five principal domains were identified as barriers to harmonized implementation: (1) inconsistent dose recording and reporting conventions; (2) variability in commissioning and QA practices for heterogeneous small-field dose distributions; (3) uncertainty in motion management and geometric robustness evaluation in the presence of anatomical changes; (4) fragmented data infrastructure limiting multi-institutional outcome analysis; and (5) limited coordinated governance and standardization infrastructure. Consensus recommendations and a phased roadmap with measurable milestones were formulated to address these domains.

CONCLUSION: Harmonization of clinical implementation is essential to ensure reproducibility, support prospective multi-institutional trials, and safeguard consistent patient care across institutions. Coordinated international collaboration will be critical to establish standardized definitions, QA benchmarks, registry infrastructure, and governance frameworks for safe and effective clinical integration.

articles.title: DAG-informed analysis of muscle characteristics and overall survival in patients receiving radical treatment for bladder cancer.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced skeletal muscle (SM) quantity and quality may influence outcomes in bladder cancer, but most studies are associative and vulnerable to confounding and inconsistent covariate adjustment. We applied a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-informed framework to evaluate associations between computed tomography-derived SM characteristics and overall survival (OS) in patients receiving curative-intent radiotherapy-based bladder preservation or radical cystectomy.

METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included patients treated between 2014 and 2024. Computed tomography imaging closest to definitive local therapy was analysed using an automated segmentation pipeline to quantify SM quantity, expressed as skeletal muscle index (SMI), and quality, expressed as intramuscular adipose tissue ratio (IMATR). A DAG was used to prespecify the adjustment strategy, and Cox models were fitted separately within radiotherapy and surgical cohorts.

RESULTS: The final cohorts comprised 353 radiotherapy-treated and 117 surgically treated patients. In the radiotherapy cohort, higher SMI was associated with improved OS (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.94, p = 0.007), while higher IMATR was associated with worse OS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.04-1.48, p = 0.014). In the smaller surgical cohort, point estimates were directionally discordant with the radiotherapy findings and imprecise: SMI HR 1.35 (95% CI 0.99-1.85, p = 0.057) and IMATR HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.62-1.21, p = 0.39).

CONCLUSIONS: In this DAG-informed analysis, higher SMI and lower IMATR were associated with improved OS in radiotherapy-treated patients. Surgical estimates were imprecise and should be considered exploratory. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further evaluation of CT-derived muscle characteristics as prognostic markers within radiotherapy-treated populations but cannot yet establish a differential benefit for radiotherapy vs cystectomy.

articles.title: How to plan and deliver lung cancer reirradiation: A consensus approach from the ESTRO reirradiation and lung focus groups and ReCOG.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract: Lung reirradiation is seeing increased use, yet the evidence base guiding its practice remains limited despite significant technological advances. This paper provides a consensus approach addressing the technical factors underpinning clinical decision-making. It aims to answer the central question: how can clinical teams implement a safe, reproducible, and technically robust workflow for high-dose lung reirradiation? The recommendations are developed by an expert panel of radiation oncologists, medical physicists, and radiation therapists (RTT) from 14 European, American, and Canadian centres, synthesizing a broad range of clinical perspectives. The scope of this work/manuscript is to provide a structured, practical workflow applicable across diverse clinical settings. Using a clinical case, the manuscript demonstrates key conceptual principles, such as the rationale for advanced dose accumulation and the impact of anatomical changes during treatment, with clear, stepwise guidance to support consistent implementation and informed clinical judgement. Key recommended steps include retrieval of prior treatment data; consideration of prior positioning and motion management; and equieffective dose accumulation using deformable image registration or organ-at-risk (OAR)-focused rigid registration. Treatment planning should explicitly incorporate prior dose while balancing target coverage against OAR limits. Daily online volumetric image guidance is central to evaluating both bony and soft-tissue anatomy, enabling setup adjustments to protect critical structures approaching tolerance. Clear documentation and multidisciplinary communication are integral throughout. This consensus approach is intended to support both centres that aim to establish reirradiation practice and experienced teams seeking to harmonize best practices.

articles.title: Postoperative Antibiotic Duration and Treatment Failure After Aseptic Revision Arthroplasty With a Single Unexpected Positive Culture: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The clinical significance of a single unexpected positive intraoperative culture (UPC) during aseptic revision arthroplasty remains unclear. This study primarily aimed to evaluate the association between postoperative antibiotic duration and treatment failure in patients with a single UPC after aseptic revision total hip or knee arthroplasty. A secondary aim was to compare failure-free survival between patients with a single UPC and those with multiple UPCs.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 51 presumed aseptic revision hip or knee arthroplasties with UPCs performed between January 1999 and December 2023. Cases meeting the 2018 ICM criteria for periprosthetic joint infection were excluded. Postoperative antibiotic duration was the exposure of interest. Treatment failure, defined as infection-related re-revision, was the primary outcome; failure-free survival was the secondary outcome. Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Factors associated with failure were examined using univariate logistic regression, and failure-free survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test.

RESULTS: Among 39 patients with one UPC, treatment failure occurred in 18%. Antibiotic courses longer than 21 days were associated with failure (OR 28.1). In the small subgroup with available data (n = 13), synovial biomarkers did not show a statistically significant difference between success and failure groups. Patients with one UPC had better failure-free survival than those with ≥ 2 UPCs.

CONCLUSION: The observed association between prolonged antibiotic therapy and treatment failure may reflect underlying infection severity rather than a causal effect of antibiotic duration. Individualized management is recommended for UPCs in aseptic revision arthroplasty.

articles.title: Surgical Technique: An Overlooked Factor in Atrial Fibrillation After Lung Resection.
Impact of Stent Age on Antithrombotic Strategy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-eluting Stents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Although non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant (NOAC) monotherapy is generally recommended beyond 1 year after drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), the temporal evolution of ischemic and bleeding risks remains inadequately characterized. This study assessed whether the effects of NOAC monotherapy versus combination therapy differ by stent age in patients with AF who underwent DES implantation ≥ 1 year earlier.

METHODS: This prespecified analysis of the Appropriate Duration of Anti-Platelet and Thrombotic Strategy After 12 Months in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Treated with Drug-Eluting Stents (ADAPT AF-DES) trial compared NOAC monotherapy with combination therapy (NOAC plus clopidogrel) by stent age. Patients were classified into the remote percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and the intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383). The primary endpoint was 1-year net adverse clinical events (NACE).

RESULTS: No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction. Although a significant interaction was observed for composite ischemic outcomes in the prespecified analysis, it was no longer observed when stent age was modeled as a continuous variable or after adjustment in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with AF ≥ 1 year post-DES, no consistent interactions by stent age were observed for clinical outcomes, supporting the safety and effectiveness of NOAC monotherapy across the spectrum of stent age.

articles.title: Objective Assessment of Oral Feeding Development in Preterm Infants Using the Neoneur Feeding System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate feeding and respiratory skills in preterm infants using the Neoneur Feeding System (NFS) clinical biomarkers and track maturation until discharge in infants achieving full oral feeds.

DESIGN/METHODS: This prospective, observational, non-randomized, longitudinal study enrolled infants born ≤34 weeks' gestation from the level III neonatal intensive care unit at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. The NFS was used to record feeding, with each infant contributing a minimum of six feeds recorded over 3 weeks. Six NFS biomarkers were analyzed: intersuck width, swallow rate, swallow burst rate, maximum pressure/burst, suck width, and rests between bursts. Biomarker trajectories were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with an infant-specific random intercept and corrected gestational age as the longitudinal predictor.

RESULTS: The analysis included forty-two infants with mean gestational age of 29.9 weeks (SD: 2.73 w), mean birth weight of 1377g (SD: 485g), and mean birth weight Z-score of -0.27 (SD: 0.92). A total of 241 feeds from all 42 infants were assessed in the primary mixed-effects analysis. Five of six biomarkers showed a statistically significant weekly increase with corrected gestational age (Table 2); rest between bursts did not. A phase-shifted trend line was observed on two of the biomarkers, when compared with normative data, reflecting instrumentation differences.

CONCLUSION: NFS-derived biomarkers can potentially offer an objective method to track feeding skill development in preterm infants. Our findings suggest these measures may complement clinical observation and provide new insights into feeding maturation.

articles.title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net.
articles.abstract: AbstractObjective. To develop an automated method for segmentation and uptake quantification ofcarotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET while accounting forpartial-volume and tissue-fraction effects.Approach. Synthetic carotid PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth weregenerated by combining MR-derived high-resolution activity maps with GATE MonteCarlo simulation incorporating major PET physical processes and matched to theBiograph mMR acquisition and reconstruction. A two-stage network first localized thecarotid vessel wall from T1-weighted MR and then estimated voxel-wise inflammationfraction from masked PET. Both stages used a multiscale residual (MSR) convolutionalbackbone. Performance was compared with U-Net, Transformer U-Net, DUCK-Net, anditerative Yang partial-volume correction.Main results. In a two-alternative forced-choice study, five nuclear-medicine physiciansidentified real images with 54% accuracy (54/100; Wilson 95% CI 0.44-0.63; exactbinomial p = 0.48). On 184 simulated test slices from five held-out patients, the proposedmethod achieved a weighted DSC of 0.79, compared with 0.73 for U-Net, 0.69 forTransformer U-Net, and 0.75 for DUCK-Net, with corresponding HD values of 1.85, 2.29,2.32, and 2.23 voxels. Patient-cluster bootstrap comparisons favored the proposed methodfor DSC and HD against all three baselines (Holm-corrected p ≤ 0.031). Overall ENRMSEwas 0.24 versus 0.59, 0.68, and 0.59 for the three DL baselines and 0.57 for iterative Yang.In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derivedlipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage.Significance. The proposed framework improved carotid PET segmentation and uptakequantification under simulated conditions. The patient analysis is preliminary and requiresexternal validation with biological reference standards before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Optimum timing of cerebral computed tomography angiography for determination of death using neurological criteria: a retrospective sensitivity cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) is increasingly incorporated into national guidelines to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest during the determination of death using neurological criteria. However, implementation remains limited due to studies showing variable sensitivity. Clinical observations suggest the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, defined as the appearance of fixed and dilated pupils and loss of cough and gag reflexes, significantly influences CTA sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of this time interval on test sensitivity.

METHODS: We retrospectively assessed 118 intensive care unit patients undergoing determination of death using neurological criteria. Cerebral CTA was used to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest based on a four-point scoring system. Patients were categorised according to the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia to the investigation.

RESULTS: Cerebral CTA did not confirm cerebral circulatory arrest in 15/118 (13%) patients, yielding an overall sensitivity of 87.3% (95%CI 79.6-92.5%). Notably, 93.3% (95%CI 66.0-99.7%) of false-negative results occurred within 12 h of the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. Patients were secondarily stratified into early (≤ 12 h) and late (> 12 h) groups, revealing a significantly higher sensitivity in the late group (67.4%, 95%CI 51.3-80.5% vs. 98.7%, 95%CI 91.8-100%, p < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: The sensitivity of cerebral CTA increases with the time elapsed after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. We recommend delaying cerebral CTA until at least 12 h after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, and, in case of inconclusive results, test repetition at least 12 h later. Further work is required to confirm our findings and increase diagnostic confidence.

articles.title: Time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired model for late dynamic PET frame prediction from early [11C] raclopride.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To reduce the burden of dynamic PET acquisition while preserving quantitative analysis, we propose a time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired residual denoising framework for predicting late dynamic PET frames from a short early acquisition window (10 min in this study) of [¹¹C] raclopride.

APPROACH: Irregular native dynamic frames were converted to a uniform 1-min indexing grid using overlap-weighted rebinning. The first 10 min were used as the early input and to derive the spatial and intensity preprocessing parameters. For each requested late time, a shared time-aware 3D U-Net predicted an anchor-relative residual with respect to the last available early frame. A training-only DDPM-inspired Gaussian perturbation and noise-prediction branch shared the prediction backbone and regularized residual learning, while temporal-consistency loss constrained predicted frame-to-frame changes. All learning-based methods used identical subject-wise five-fold cross-validation within the development cohort, followed by evaluation on a fixed internal test set; the external cohort was held out from model selection.

MAIN RESULTS: The proposed approach achieved higher PSNR and SSIM and lower MAE than the comparison methods, while providing closer agreement with reference TACs and SRTM-derived parameter estimates across the limbic, associative, and sensorimotor striata.

SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed framework provides deterministic time-resolved late-frame estimates from early dynamic PET while using a DDPM-inspired noise-prediction objective only as an auxiliary training regularizer rather than as an iterative diffusion inference process. This design may support shortened dynamic PET protocols while retaining TAC and kinetic-parameter fidelity.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients with Left Ventricular Assist Devices: Perioperative Management and Clinical Outcome.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) are commonly utilized in severe left-sided heart disease as a bridge to transplantation or long-term treatment. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) improves mobility in these patients but entails numerous perioperative risks. Our study focused on perioperative management and clinical outcomes for LVAD patients undergoing THA, aiming to provide insights into this complex setting.

ABSTRACT: METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVADs who underwent THA at our institution from May 2019 to November 2023. The outcomes of interest were perioperative anticoagulation management, thrombotic or bleeding events, transfusion needs, mortality, surgical site complications, and reoperations. The functional outcome was evaluated using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS) and the EQ-5D quality of life score at their last follow-up.

ABSTRACT: RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 11 male patients, mean age 68.1 years. Patient survival was recorded over a 22.8-month mean follow-up (range, 1-53). Seven patients (63.6%) required postoperative transfusions and 5/11 patients (45.5%) experienced thromboembolic events. The mean hospital stay after THA was 13.5 days. The overall mortality related-to-disease rate in our series of LVAD patients undergoing primary THA was 27%. Three patients (27.3%) developed surgical site hematomas, which required one additional reoperation, and one of those was infected. Hip functionality improved markedly, with the mean mHHS rising from 27.5 to 72.3.

ABSTRACT: CONCLUSIONS: THA in LVAD patients is challenging yet feasible, offering significant functional improvements despite the increased perioperative morbidity. Mortality was associated with their underlying disease, but not the surgery.

articles.title: Untangling the causes of elongation artifacts in dual flat-panel PET: limited angular sampling versus parallax error.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Dual flat-panel PET systems provide easy patient access and high sensitivity when the panels are close together. Their images are however susceptible to elongation artifacts due to incomplete angular sampling and parallax error. These effects are reduced by respectively including depth-of-interaction (DOI) and time-of-flight (TOF) information. To guide system design, a framework is needed that predicts which effect dominates for a given object size and field-of-view (FOV) location. This study investigates the impact of TOF and DOI on elongation artifacts for a variety of phantoms in a dual flat-panel system, benchmarked against a cylindrical reference.

APPROACH: A large dual flat-panel system and cylindrical system with the same axial FOV were simulated. The TOF and DOI resolution were varied independently and iterative MLEM reconstruction was performed. Data were generated for point sources and spheres spanning 1-50 mm radius at multiple FOV positions. Point-source blur was quantified with full width at half maximum measurements, and sphere elongation using an activity-spillover metric. Findings were validated using the more clinically relevant NEMA IQ and XCAT phantoms with embedded lesions.

MAIN RESULTS: DOI uncertainty resulted in elongations independently of object size. In the cylindrical system, these only occurred at radial offsets, but in the dual flat-panel system, parallax-blur was also present at the center of the FOV. Elongations due to limited angular coverage in the flat-panel system grew with object size and dominated for features over 1-2 cm. The extent of these elongations increased towards the FOV edges and was substantially reduced by including TOF information. With adequate TOF and DOI performance, the flat-panel system matched cylindrical image quality.

SIGNIFICANCE: The framework predicts the dominant artifact mechanism as a function of object size, position, and system geometry. The insights guide detector and system design for dual flat-panel PET and corresponding artifact correction methods.

articles.title: Risk assessment and prevention of disease progression: new concepts in bronchiectasis management.
articles.abstract: Bronchiectasis management is traditionally guided by exacerbation frequency. Previous guidelines have recommended treatment escalation only in patients experiencing three or more exacerbations per year. In contrast, the 2025 European Respiratory Society (ERS) guideline introduces a paradigm shift by advocating individualised risk assessment to identify patients at high risk of future complications, instead of relying solely on prior exacerbation. High-risk features include severe daily symptoms, underlying aetiologies or comorbidities, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, rheumatoid arthritis, primary ciliary dyskinesia, and chronic infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa or enteric Gram-negative pathogens. The 2025 ERS guideline also recommends long-term macrolides as first-line treatment for a broad patient population, irrespective of P. aeruginosa status, which is relevant in settings where inhaled antibiotics are unavailable. In this study, we present a clinical case, describe the appropriate management strategy, and discuss key practical considerations, including exclusion of nontuberculous mycobacterial infection before initiation, monitoring for adverse effects, and criteria for macrolide withdrawal. The availability of more effective therapies further underscores the importance of initiating treatment and avoiding delays until the disease becomes established or severe. In summary, the central tenet of the 2025 ERS guideline, revolving around identifying high-risk patients and initiating treatment early, is a proactive approach to preventing disease progression rather than managing its consequences.

articles.title: ACF-Net: Design of an adaptive cross-modal fusion network for cross-subject wearable EEG-EMG gesture recognition.
articles.abstract: Cross-subject gesture recognition in wearable brain-computer interfaces is constrained by four structural deficiencies: symmetric cross-modal attention discarding cortical precedence over muscular execution, priors confined to post hoc analysis, invariance anchored on unimodal features, and adaptation requiring labelled target-domain data. This study closes these gaps by embedding corticomuscular coupling directly into the network architecture rather than recovering it from data.Approach: ACF-Net is a four-stage pipeline embedding neurophysiological priors directly into fusion. The corticomuscular coherence prior injection layer (CMC-Prior) encodes time-lagged coherence and phase-locking values for every electroencephalography (EEG)-electromyography (EMG) channel pair as a learnable bias tensor. Granger-causality-inspired directed cross-modal attention (GC-Attn) uses a causal mask allowing only EEG-to-EMG influence within 30-120 ms. The fused embedding is projected onto a symmetric positive definite manifold with log-Euclidean triplet loss. Physiology-consistent test-time adaptation (PC-TTA) updates only batch-normalisation affine parameters, using EEG-precedes-EMG as unlabelled self-supervision, eliminating labelled target data. Leave-one-subject-out validation on WAY-EEG-GAL (12 participants) and WEE-Ges (20 participants, three days) used fold-wise priors and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests.Main results: ACF-Net reached 87.6% on WAY-EEG-GAL and 89.2% on WEE-Ges, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.4 and 9.1 percentage points with all comparisons significant after correction. Ablation attributed gains of 6.3, 4.9, 3.4 and 1.8 percentage points to directed attention, prior injection, manifold embedding and test-time adaptation. Accuracy remained 77.5% under 20 mm simulated electrode displacement, adaptation reduced the cross-day loss from 6.8 to 2.1 percentage points, and a forward pass on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano took 32.4 ms within a 178 ms end-to-end response at 30.9 Hz. Significance: Learned coupling weights recovered central-to-forearm-extensor projection, and delays matched corticospinal conduction with motor-unit recruitment, suggesting physiological structure, not dataset-specific statistics. Yet healthy young adults, gel-based/semi-dry wired hardware, and simulated displacement make this methodological; clinical and wireless dry-electrode transfer remains unestablished.

articles.title: Characterization of an electromagnetic impact-driven needle-free injector with enhanced pulsed control in a low-jet-power regime.
articles.abstract: This study elucidates the development and performance characterization of an advanced electromagnetic impact-driven jet injector version 3 (IDM-v3), specifically engineered to achieve controllable jet formation within a low-jet-power regime. To overcome the excessive kinetic energy challenges observed in its predecessor (IDM-v2), several critical technical refinements were implemented, including the integration of a high-force solenoid, a calibrated 94 g projectile, and a reduced maximum impact stroke of 6 mm. Experimental results indicate that impact force, the calculated impact peak pressure metric, and exit jet velocity are highly sensitive to the impact configuration. The 0.2 mm nozzle produced the highest impact peak pressure, P_peak, of approximately 206 MPa, calculated from the measured peak target force using P_peak=F_peak/A_n. The corresponding jet power, calculated separately from the measured exit jet velocity, was approximately 2 W. In contrast, the 0.4 mm nozzle produced a higher calculated jet power of approximately 6 W because of its larger nozzle-orifice area. High-speed temporal analysis revealed a multi-pulse response in the area-normalized target-force signal and stable jet morphology within the initial millisecond of actuation. Validation through penetration assays on polyacrylamide gels and fresh ex vivo porcine tissue demonstrated that the 0.2 mm nozzle produced a narrower and more focused penetration channel, whereas the 0.4 mm nozzle produced greater lateral spreading and reached a greater final penetration depth under the tested conditions. These findings characterize the tunability of the IDM-v3 engineering prototype and provide a basis for further experimental development and evaluation. They do not establish biological safety or clinical or veterinary readiness.

articles.title: Pharmacological Activities of Centella asiatica: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence on Cardiovascular, Neurological, Antioxidant, and Anti-inflammatory Effects.
articles.abstract: Centella asiatica (L.) (Gotu Kola) is a medicinal herb traditionally used in Asia for cognitive enhancement, wound healing, and systemic disorders. This systematic review appraises preclinical and clinical evidence on its cardiovascular and neurological effects. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov (to June 2026) for studies of whole-plant extracts or bioactive compounds (asiatic acid, asiaticoside, madecassoside, madecassic acid, caffeoylquinic acids) in vitro, in animals, or in humans, excluding dermatological studies, reviews, and articles lacking methods. Sixty-two studies met criteria: 54 preclinical and eight clinical trials, assessed using SYRCLE, an in vitro checklist, and Cochrane RoB 2. Preclinically, C. asiatica modulated ischemia-reperfusion injury, reduced doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity, improved cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's models, and showed antidepressant-like effects, via Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant activation and NF-κB/MAPK anti-inflammatory suppression. Clinical evidence was mixed: Gotu Kola matched or exceeded folic acid for poststroke vascular cognitive impairment, and three trials of a standardized triterpenic fraction (TTFCA) improved microcirculation in venous hypertensive and diabetic microangiopathy; however, a type 2 diabetes trial found no significant effect on glycated hemoglobin, glucose, or LDL cholesterol, a mild cognitive impairment trial found no added benefit over exercise alone, and a Phase 1 safety trial is ongoing. C. asiatica shows preclinical promise as a multitarget cardiovascular and neurological agent, but clinical evidence remains limited and inconsistent, compounded by an 800-fold preclinical dosing range, variable treatment durations, and geographic concentration (47% from one country). Larger, standardized, multiregion trials targeting these outcomes are needed before therapeutic claims are warranted.

articles.title: Impact of Transition to Insulin U-500 during Pregnancy on Continuous Glucose Monitoring-Derived Glycemic Metrics among Women with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insulin U-500 is a highly concentrated regular insulin that is five times stronger than standard U-100 and is used to treat severe insulin resistance. Glycemic data from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in relation to initiation of U-500 insulin in pregnancy with type 2 diabetes are limited. We examined CGM-derived glycemic measures before and after insulin U-500 transition during pregnancy among women with type 2 diabetes.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a case-crossover study evaluating glycemic measures before and after transition to insulin U-500 during pregnancy among women with type 2 diabetes. The case period was from prenatal care to insulin U-500 transition, and the control period was after insulin U-500 transition to delivery. Outcomes included CGM metrics (time in range [TIR; 65-140 mg/dL], time above range [TAR], and time below range), mean glucose and standard deviation, estimated A1c per glucose management indicator, coefficient of variation, and number of hypoglycemic episodes and were compared pre versus post insulin U-500 transition. Adjusted linear mixed models were used.

RESULTS: Among 21 women with type 2 diabetes, the median gestational age at prenatal care initiation was 11.1 weeks, at insulin U-500 transition was 25.4 weeks, and at delivery was 37.1 weeks. The insulin U-500 dose at initiation was 300 units/day and at delivery was 422.5 units/day. The TIR was higher, and TAR and mean glucose were lower post versus pre insulin U-500 transition (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of pregnant women with type 2 diabetes, transition to insulin U-500 was associated with a modest improvement in some CGM-derived glycemic measures.

KEY POINTS: · Transition to insulin U-500 was associated with a modest improvement in CGM-derived glycemic measures.. · CGM data using U-500 insulin in pregnancy with type 2 diabetes are limited.. · This is the largest contemporary pregnancy cohort who transitioned to insulin U-500 using CGM..

articles.title: Intermediate-half-life metabolites as systemic relay nodes in metabolic disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic stress within one organ can have consequences far beyond its site of origin. In metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), reactive carbonyl species, purine metabolites, and nitric oxide-related intermediates provide a basis for examining how metabolic disturbances may extend across tissues. Selected metabolites may act as systemic relay nodes when their production, persistence, and transport permit exposure beyond the source tissue. A broadly minutes-to-hours timescale offers a useful starting point for this hypothesis, while chemical form, reactivity, tissue uptake, and clearance determine the reach of each candidate. Plasma disappearance, whole-body elimination, intracellular persistence, and covalent-adduct persistence describe distinct processes that shape the interpretation of measured exposure. Mechanistic studies, analytical measurements, and clinical interventions together inform the links between local stress and distant effects. Emerging AI and multi-omics approaches may help characterize the resulting metabolic heterogeneity. Viewed through this framework, metabolite kinetics become a bridge between molecular mechanisms and candidate approaches to patient stratification, connecting the duration and distribution of exposure with potential sites of intervention.

articles.title: COVID-19 severity among individuals with chronic diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies reported that individuals with underlying chronic diseases who are infected with COVID-19 are at greater risk for more severe outcomes. In this study, we measured these risks among a wide range of comorbidities in a large cohort.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed the risk for hospitalization and the severity and mortality risk of COVID-19 among adults with obstructive lung diseases, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, kidney diseases, malignancies and immunosuppression states before the emergence of the Omicron variant. We used univariant analyses and adjusted for age, sex, Body Mass Index (BMI), smoking habits, Socioeconomic Status (SES) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).

RESULTS: Of the 44,866 individuals who were positive for COVID-19, 2358 were hospitalized. The adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) for hospitalization was significantly greater for most chronic diseases, with the highest risk for individuals who underwent a kidney transplant (15.06; 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 7.86-28.73]). A significantly greater risk for severe COVID-19 than for mild to moderate disease (602 and 1657 patients, respectively) was found for patients with cerebrovascular diseases (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI 1.07-1.99). A greater mortality risk was demonstrated for individuals who had undergone kidney transplantation (aOR = 4.23; 95% CI 1.36-11.82) and those with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-1.99).

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with cerebrovascular disease were at increased risk for severe COVID-19, whereas individuals with CKD and past kidney transplantation were at increased mortality risk. These individuals should receive early medical intervention when they are diagnosed.

articles.title: A hybrid explainable artificial intelligence framework for equitable prediction and analysis of postnatal care uptake in Ghana: Integrating ensemble learning, counterfactuals, and causal inference.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a hybrid, equity-focused artificial intelligence (AI) framework for predicting and analysing postnatal care (PNC) uptake among women in Ghana, with emphasis on minority-class sensitivity, model interpretability, and actionable intervention insights.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional, secondary analysis of nationally representative survey data.

METHODS: Using data from the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (n = 3314), we developed a hybrid AI framework combining ensemble learning (Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine with soft voting and threshold tuning), explainable AI (SHAP analysis), counterfactual reasoning (DiCE), and causal inference (doubly robust estimators for average and conditional average treatment effects). The Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance and stratified 5-fold cross-validation was used for model evaluation. Doubly robust causal inference was conducted using the econml library, with propensity score modelling used to account for treatment assignment, and positivity and exchangeability assumptions assessed through covariate overlap diagnostics.

RESULTS: The ensemble model calibrated at a threshold of 0.45 achieved a Class 0 recall of 0.31 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AP) of 0.97, outperforming all individual baseline classifiers. SHAP analysis identified maternal age, education level, wealth status, caesarean section, and sex of household head as the most influential predictors of PNC non-utilization. Counterfactual analysis revealed that minimal, actionable changes including increased media exposure, improved educational attainment, or change of residence could shift individual predictions from non-utilization to utilization of PNC. Causal inference demonstrated significant heterogeneity in treatment responsiveness, with women aged 25-34, those with secondary education or above, urban residents, and those in female-headed households exhibiting the highest conditional average treatment effects.

CONCLUSIONS: This interpretable, fairness-aware AI framework advances the prediction and analysis of PNC uptake in Ghana. By prioritizing sensitivity to underserved women and integrating explainability, counterfactual reasoning, and causal inference, the framework provides empirical evidence for targeted, equitable maternal health interventions and is transferable to other low- and middle-income country settings.

articles.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) spheroid model exhibits a characteristic extracellular matrix-rich fibrous capsule hindering drug penetration.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), or primary liver cancer, is one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. Liver cirrhosis, characterized by deposition of excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) secreted by hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), is the major risk factor of HCC development. Although anti-fibrotic therapies hold great promise in the treatment of HCC, conventional non-animal models lack the complexity of the tumor microenvironment, especially its ECM component, driving efforts to develop more representative platforms. In this context, we bioengineered HCC spheroids by co-culturing human HCC cells (HepG2) with human HSCs (LX-2) in different ratios using a soft-embossed microwell array platform. HCC spheroids, depending on their exact composition, displayed typical HCC features, such as the presence of an ECM-rich capsule, as revealed by immunostaining of collagen type I on intact spheroids after tissue clearing. We hypothesized that the presence of this capsule, which is involved in several stages of tumor progression, could act as a 'protective barrier' that regulates the penetration and delivery of therapeutic agents. This hypothesis was confirmed using our bioengineered HCC spheroids, in which the combined presence of HSCs and ECM hinders the penetration and therapeutic efficacy of a model chemotherapeutics (doxorubicin). This could be improved by concomitant enzymatic degradation of the ECM-rich capsule. Altogether, we propose our HCC model as a relevant platform to study tumor-tumor microenvironment interactions, gain mechanistic insights into HCC, identify novel therapeutic targets and evaluate (combination) therapies targeting tumor-tumor microenvironment while integrating ECM degradation with the (targeted) delivery of therapeutic agents.

articles.title: When brain networks crash: connectivity, slow-wave activity and neural replay in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Brain connectivity disruption is a hallmark of neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet how network breakdown gives rise to cognitive deficits remains unclear. Here, we review the evidence bearing on three interconnected processes that have been proposed to link molecular pathology to cognitive decline. First, we summarize evidence that misfolded proteins propagate along brain connectivity pathways, making the connectome the biological substrate for disease progression. Second, we discuss the divergent trajectory reported across the AD continuum, an initial compensatory hyperconnectivity followed by progressive hypoconnectivity and network collapse, together with the accompanying oscillatory changes (intrusion of slow-wave activity and suppression of fast oscillatory rhythms). Third, we examine the proposal that these oscillatory alterations compromise neural replay mechanisms, critical for memory consolidation, representing the potential link between network dysfunction and cognitive decline. By integrating evidence from human neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and animal models in the AD field, this framework offers new perspectives for therapeutic interventions targeting brain connectivity and replay mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Early treatment with tecovirimat against mpox disease in cynomolgus macaques.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation.

METHODS: In this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures.

FINDINGS: Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P < 0.0001) or Day 5 (P = 0.0359) compared with untreated controls, but treatment was largely ineffective when initiated on Day 9 (P > 0.99).

INTERPRETATION: In this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates.

FUNDING: This study was supported by SIGA Technologies.

articles.title: EGFR: A promising therapeutic target in renal fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis represents the final common pathway in the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) and progressive disruption of renal architecture. To date, no approved therapy can fully reverse established or advanced fibrosis. This review comprehensively summarizes the molecular mechanisms through which epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling contributes to renal fibrosis and critically evaluates the therapeutic potential of EGFR-targeted interventions. Accumulating evidence reveals a context-dependent dual role for EGFR in kidney pathophysiology: transient EGFR activation supports epithelial repair following acute kidney injury, whereas sustained or dysregulated EGFR signaling promotes maladaptive repair and fibrogenesis. Mechanistically, persistent EGFR activation potentiates TGF-β/Smad signaling, activates mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades, promotes G2/M cell-cycle arrest and partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition (p-EMT) in tubular epithelial cells, and exacerbates inflammatory and oxidative responses involving nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), the NLRP3 inflammasome, and reactive oxygen species (ROS). Importantly, p-EMT in renal fibrosis is increasingly viewed as a profibrotic epithelial reprogramming state that impairs regenerative capacity and enhances paracrine signaling to interstitial fibroblasts rather than necessarily reflecting complete conversion of tubular epithelial cells into matrix-producing myofibroblasts. Together with metabolic dysfunction, these interconnected processes sustain fibroblast activation and pathological ECM accumulation. Current therapeutic strategies targeting EGFR include synthetic small-molecule inhibitors, natural bioactive compounds, and biological approaches. Although pharmacological EGFR inhibition demonstrates antifibrotic efficacy in preclinical models, clinical translation remains limited by systemic toxicity, insufficient renal specificity, and the absence of direct clinical validation in renal fibrosis. Overall, EGFR functions as a context-dependent molecular switch linking adaptive renal repair to maladaptive fibrotic remodeling. Future therapeutic development should therefore prioritize selective modulation of pathological EGFR activity and kidney-targeted delivery strategies that preserve beneficial repair-associated signaling while minimizing systemic toxicity.

articles.title: Exploring and strengthening day-to-day teamwork in critical care: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how teamwork is enacted, constrained, and strengthened in the day-to-day practice of critical care units, and to identify participant suggested approaches to strengthen teamwork.

METHODS: This qualitative study used interpretive description to explore clinicians' experiences of teamwork in critical care. Thirty-five healthcare professionals from six Canadian provinces participated in semi-structured interviews. Participants represented diverse roles, including nurses, physicians, respiratory therapists, pharmacists, and allied health professionals. Interviews were analyzed using an inductive and interpretive process involving open coding, constant comparison, and iterative theme development. Reflexivity was integrated throughout data collection and analysis to support credibility and interpretive coherence.

RESULTS: Teamwork in critical care was described as a multidimensional social process shaped by four interconnected themes: (1) relational practice built through familiarity, trust, and shared experience; (2) leadership, hierarchy, and unit culture, including the ways relational power shaped psychological safety and collaboration; (3) communication and coordination challenges; and (4) structural barriers to integration, learning, and stability. Across these four themes, participants frequently described nurses as central coordinators of relational and informational work, in part because of their continuous presence at the bedside.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants' experiences suggested that teamwork in critical care is a social process shaped by the dynamic interplay of relational practice, relational power, communication structures, and structural stability. Together, these conditions influenced participants' experiences of how clinicians connect, coordinate, and make decisions in the critical care context.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Participants identified relational stability, psychologically safe leadership, communication structures that support shared understanding, and staffing and orientation practices that promote continuity as potential points for strengthening teamwork. These participants suggested approaches warrant organizational consideration and prospective evaluation to determine their effects on teamwork in critical care settings.

articles.title: Effects of paternal and maternal voice on procedural pain and physiological responses during arterial blood sampling in preterm infants in a neonatal intensive care unit: a three-arm randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of paternal and maternal voice interventions on procedural pain, comfort, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and behavioral state during arterial blood sampling in preterm infants, and to compare their effects with routine care and with each other.
