METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in China between May 2024 and June 2025. Of 135 randomized preterm infants, 119 completed the study (paternal voice, n = 39; maternal voice, n = 39; routine care, n = 41). Parental voice recordings were played from 10 min before until 10 min after arterial blood sampling. Outcomes were assessed at five time points. Generalized estimating equations were used for repeated-measures analyses.

RESULTS: GEE analysis showed significant group and time effects for pain (P = 0.027 and P < 0.001), with lower pain scores in the paternal voice group than in routine care (mean difference = -0.51; 95% CI -0.96 to -0.06; P = 0.021). Paternal voice was also associated with lower heart rates during sampling, and better comfort scores at 1 and 5 min after sampling, although the overall group effect for comfort was not significant. Maternal voice intervention did not differ significantly from routine care. No between-group differences were observed for oxygen saturation or behavioral state.

CONCLUSIONS: Paternal voice was associated with favorable pain and heart rate responses in preterm infants during and after arterial blood sampling, with time-specific differences in comfort during early recovery. Its overall effect on comfort and relative effectiveness compared with maternal voice require further investigation.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Paternal voice may offer a simple, safe, and feasible adjunct to procedural pain management and family-centered care in preterm infants.

articles.title: Validation and prognostic value of the five-repetition sit-to-stand test in patients with severe exacerbation of COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A severe exacerbation of COPD (ECOPD) may negatively impact patients' functioning; however, there is a lack of validated, simple, and low-cost tools to assess physical function in this setting. Thus, the aims of this study were to explore the construct validity of the five-repetition sit-to-stand (5STS) test for assessing muscle strength and exercise tolerance, and to investigate its prognostic value in predicting exacerbation-related readmission risk in patients with severe ECOPD.

METHODS: This was a prospective observational study. Fifty-eight patients hospitalized with a severe ECOPD were included. At hospital discharge, the 5STS, quadriceps force, six-minute walk test (6MWT), COPD Assessment Test (CAT), and modified Medical Research Council scale were assessed. Exacerbation-related readmissions within six months were collected. Statistical analyses included correlation analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

RESULTS: 58 patients (mean age of 69 ± 8 years, 45% male, FEV1 41 ± 16% predicted) were included. Within six months, 31% were readmitted. The 5STS showed a significant negative correlation with quadriceps force (r = -0.487) and 6MWT (r = -0.415). The ROC curve analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.720 (95% CI: 0.588-0.853), with a cut-off of ≥13 seconds identifying patients at higher risk of exacerbation-related readmission. Patients with 5STS <13s had a higher probability of remaining hospitalization-free (86.7%) compared to those with 5STS ≥13s (50%).

CONCLUSION: The 5STS is correlated with muscle strength and exercise tolerance and has acceptable prognostic value for predicting exacerbation-related admission within six months in patients with severe ECOPD.

articles.title: Prescribing Patterns of Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis and VTE Incidence After Colorectal Cancer Resection: Insights From a Single Institution.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery are at increased risk for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Several societies recommend extended duration pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge for selected high-risk patients, but real-world use is inconsistent, and the absolute benefit in the era of minimally invasive surgery and enhanced recovery remains uncertain.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing colon or rectal resection for cancer at a single academic center between 2020 and 2023. Patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation, those with recent VTE or nonmalignant indications for surgery were excluded. Demographic, operative, and oncologic variables were collected along with inpatient and postdischarge VTE prophylaxis practices. Primary outcomes were (1) prescription of extended pharmacologic prophylaxis at discharge and (2) 90-d symptomatic VTE incidence.

RESULTS: A total of 177 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most operations were minimally invasive and performed within an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathway. Despite the presence of traditional VTE risk factors, only a minority of patients were discharged on extended pharmacologic prophylaxis. Within 90 d, two patients developed symptomatic lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (1.1%); no pulmonary emboli or VTE events were identified. Both patients had high-risk features, including advanced age and emergent surgery. Routine screening imaging was not performed, and all events were clinically detected.

CONCLUSIONS: In this enhanced recovery after surgery-based colorectal cancer cohort, extended postdischarge VTE prophylaxis was rarely prescribed; yet, the symptomatic VTE rate was low and limited to two high-risk individuals. These findings support a risk-stratified rather than universal approach to extended prophylaxis after colorectal surgery.

articles.title: Alarm fatigue levels and associated factors among intensive care unit nurses: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled mean alarm fatigue score among intensive care unit nurses and to synthesise evidence on factors associated with alarm fatigue.

METHODS: Eight Chinese and international databases were systematically searched to identify original observational studies of alarm fatigue among ICU nurses published between January 2017 and February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened the records, appraised the methodological quality of the included studies, and extracted the data. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 14 to pool mean alarm fatigue scores and their 95% confidence intervals. Sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the robustness of the findings, and potential publication bias was evaluated using Begg's and Egger's tests.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included in the systematic review, of which 15 provided data suitable for meta-analysis, comprising 4084 intensive care unit nurses. The meta-analysis revealed a pooled mean alarm fatigue score of 25.93 (95% CI, 24.38-27.48). Subgroup analysis indicated that higher levels of alarm fatigue were observed in female nurses (25.89, 95% CI: 22.72-29.06), those aged ≤25 years (26.80, 95% CI: 23.26-30.34), unmarried individuals(24.56, 95% CI: 22.70-26.43), junior-level nurses (27.42, 95% CI: 23.60-31.24), and those with a master's degree (27.15, 95% CI: 24.32-29.99). Elevated alarm fatigue was also observed among nurses without a critical care specialty (24.09, 95% CI: 22.75-25.44), those engaged in rotating night shifts (24.07, 95% CI, 21.98-26.16), nurses without alarm management training (31.52, 95% CI, 25.97-37.07), and those working in general ICUs (26.80, 95% CI, 22.27-31.34).

CONCLUSION: The pooled mean alarm fatigue score among ICU nurses fell within the moderate range. Hospitals and nursing managers should strengthen standardised alarm management procedures and provide alarm management training for all ICU nurses. These measures may help mitigate alarm fatigue, improve the quality of nursing care, and promote patient safety.

articles.title: Occult hypoxemia in the ICU: Clinical risk factors, mortality and implications for nursing practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulse oximetry (SpO₂) is the primary tool used by Intensive Care Unit (ICU) nurses to monitor oxygenation. Occult hypoxemia - a reassuring SpO₂ despite low arterial saturation (SaO₂) - is a critical patient-safety concern.

OBJECTIVES: To measure SpO₂-SaO₂ discordance in ICU patients, identify situations in which SpO₂ cannot be trusted, and assess its impact on ICU mortality.

METHODS: Retrospective single-centre cohort study (September 2019 - January 2026), reported according to STROBE. SpO₂ was charted hourly; each arterial blood gas was paired with the most recent preceding entry. Analysis was restricted to pairs within 10 min, using Bland-Altman analysis for repeated measures. Predictors of occult hypoxemia (SpO₂ ≥ 92% with SaO₂ < 88%) and its association with ICU mortality were examined using generalized estimating equations, with adjustment restricted to early-stay covariates.

RESULTS: The primary set comprised 39,554 paired measurements from 7082 ICU stays in 6348 patients. Mean bias was negligible (+0.1%) but limits of agreement were wide (-7.6% to +7.8%); 18.6% of pairs differed by ≥4%. Among 1219 pairs with SaO₂ < 88%, SpO₂ remained ≥92% in 702 (57.6%). Acidosis was most robustly associated with occult hypoxemia (adjusted OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.97-2.86 for pH < 7.35); invasive mechanical ventilation carried lower risk (OR 0.50, 0.42-0.60). Early occult hypoxemia (within 24 h) was independently associated with ICU mortality (adjusted OR 1.55, 1.17-2.05; 24-h landmark OR 1.45, 1.07-1.97). Point estimates were similar when exposure was ascertained only from pairs obtained within 10 or 5 min (1.44 and 1.49), with confidence intervals including unity because restriction reduced the number of exposed deaths by about 70%.

CONCLUSION: Among sampled measurements with true arterial hypoxemia, SpO₂ frequently remained ≥92%, particularly in acidotic and patients not receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Early occult hypoxemia was independently associated with ICU mortality. Because inclusion required a blood gas revealing the discordance, the treating team could act on it; the association reflects a severity signal rather than a causal effect of the discordance itself.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: In acidotic ICU patients and those on non-invasive oxygen support, SpO₂ frequently disagrees with concurrent SaO₂ and should not be relied on alone. Arterial blood gas confirmation may be considered when SpO₂ appears inconsistent with the clinical picture.

articles.title: Does transfusion of blood products increase the risk of multidrug-resistant infections in critically ill patients?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between transfusion of blood products during intensive care unit (ICU) stay and the incidence of ICU-acquired colonisation and infection with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria (ICU-MDR-col, ICU-MDR-inf, respectively).

METHODS: Secondary analysis of two prospective multicentre cohort studies conducted in eight ICUs in France. Adult patients admitted to participating ICUs were enrolled consecutively from May 2019 to June 2021. All patients underwent systematic screening for colonisation with MDR bacteria at admission and weekly thereafter. Exposure to transfusion of blood products during ICU stay, including packed red blood cells (PRBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet concentrates (PCs), was recorded. The primary outcome was the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and/or ICU-MDR-inf (ICU-MDR-col/inf) until ICU discharge, censored at day 28. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and ICU-MDR-inf, considered separately. Associations were assessed using mixed-effects Poisson regression models adjusted for prespecified confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed according to immunosuppression status at ICU admission.

RESULTS: Among 1103 patients, 358 (32.5%) received transfusion of any blood product. Overall, 292 (26.5%) patients experienced at least one ICU-MDR-col/inf event. Transfusion was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-MDR-col/inf (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.62; p = 0.013), mainly driven by ICU-MDR-inf (aIRR 1.62, 95% CI 1.16-2.24; p = 0.004), but not ICU-MDR-col considered individually. This association was restricted to PRBC transfusion. No significant heterogeneity was observed according to immunosuppression status.

CONCLUSIONS: Transfusion of PBRCs was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-acquired MDR infections, with no significant heterogeneity observed according to immunosuppression status.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: These findings support a restrictive approach to transfusion and warrant further investigation into its immunological and ecological consequences in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Nurse-led continuity-oriented family support across the adult ICU trajectory: a systematic review and meta-analysis of PICS-F-related outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family members of adult ICU patients are at risk of post-intensive care syndrome-family (PICS-F), but the psychological effects and optimal timing of nurse-led support remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate nurse-led, continuity-oriented family support for PICS-F-related psychological outcomes and explore differences by intervention phase and nurse type.

METHODS: PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 2026. Randomized and quasi-experimental studies were eligible if they evaluated nurse-led family support in adult ICUs and assessed at least one family-level PICS-F psychological outcome. Short-term outcomes assessed from 2 weeks to 3 months after ICU discharge formed the primary analyses. Random-effects meta-analyses used Hedges' g standardized mean differences (SMDs). Subgroup analyses were conducted by primary intervention phase and nurse type. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using validated tools and GRADE.

RESULTS: Seventeen reports representing 16 independent studies and 3,887 family participants were included. Nurse-led support was not associated with short-term anxiety (SMD = -0.05, 95% CI -0.24 to 0.14; very low certainty), depression (SMD = -0.01, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.21; very low certainty), or post-traumatic stress disorder-related symptoms (SMD = 0.02, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.15; moderate certainty). In-ICU support was associated with lower depression scores (SMD = -0.40, 95% CI -0.67 to -0.12), although phase comparisons included few studies. No ICU transition study contributed an eligible short-term primary outcome. Nurse-type analyses showed no consistent differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Nurse-led, continuity-oriented family support was not associated with improvements in short-term PICS-F-related psychological outcomes. Current evidence does not identify an optimal intervention phase or nurse type.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Intervention timing should be considered, although the optimal phase remains uncertain. Nurse-led support may strengthen family-centred care, but persistent distress may require tailored psychological support and referral.

articles.title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy.

METHODS: In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality.

RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS.

CONCLUSIONS: RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

articles.title: Did oat domestication result in loss of simple repeat sequences?
articles.abstract: Oat is one of the major cereals, especially important as a functional food. However, it is still an understudied crop. Genome repeat elements, known as simple sequence repeats (SSRs), can reveal genome dynamics and be used as markers for selection. SSRs across ancestral (Avena longiglumis and Avena insularis), wild hexaploid (Avena sterilis), and cultivated (Avena sativa) oat genomes were investigated to decouple the evolutionary impacts of polyploidization and domestication on genome architecture. The results revealed a two-step evolutionary trajectory: a "genomic shock" of allohexaploidization triggered a widespread expansion of repetitive elements in the wild A. sterilis, followed by artificial selection imposing a genetic bottleneck, resulting in a global contraction of SSRs in the cultivated A. sativa. In the AA subgenome, an asymmetric decrease of over 72,000 SSRs relative to its diploid ancestor was observed. Elimination of unstable mononucleotides in intergenic regions was observed, whereas conservation of GC-rich trinucleotides in some regions and localized expansion of SSR density within genic sequences on chromosome 3C were found. Genes exhibiting targeted SSR expansions were enriched for transcription factors and receptor-like kinases. Ultimately, these findings suggest that oat evolution is a dynamic structural reorganization driven by natural and artificial selection.

articles.title: Situational Analysis of Cancer Care Services in India: Protocol for a Nationwide Cross-Sectional Health Systems Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer is a significant public health challenge in India, contributing to 8.3% of deaths and 5.0% of disability-adjusted life years in 2016-nearly twice its contribution in 1990. Fragmented service delivery, limited specialist availability, late presentation, and significant financial hardship continue to hinder access to timely and effective cancer care, particularly in rural and underserved regions. A comprehensive, system-level assessment is essential to inform evidence-based planning and strengthen cancer services nationwide.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to assess the availability, readiness, accessibility, and quality of cancer care services across primary, secondary, and tertiary health care facilities in India. Specifically, it will evaluate infrastructure, human resources, diagnostic and treatment capacity, referral pathways, and service delivery across the 6 Institute of Medicine quality domains (equitable, effective, patient-centered, safe, efficient, and timely); compare rural-urban and public-private disparities; and use these findings to develop an evidence-informed framework for strengthening cancer care services and informing national policy and program planning.

METHODS: A 3-year cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted across 31 states and union territories using proportionate district sampling based on rural-urban population distribution. Nodal hospitals coordinated data collection from primary, secondary, and tertiary health care facilities. Facility-level data were collected using 3 standardized electronic forms-developed separately for primary, secondary, and tertiary levels of care-covering infrastructure, workforce, diagnostic and treatment services, referral systems, and service. Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize service availability and readiness, and chi-square tests to compare rural-urban, public-private, and facility-level differences.

RESULTS: The study received funding in October 2023. Facility-level data collection took place between July 2024 and March 2026. We enrolled 6896 health facilities (4353 primary, 1979 secondary, and 564 tertiary) from 352 districts across 31 states and union territories, with participation rates of 64.6% (4353/6735) for primary health centers, 75.7% (1979/2612) for secondary-level facilities, and 63.9% (564/902) for tertiary hospitals. Data cleaning and quality checks are complete, and analysis is complete but unpublished; we will report results on service availability, readiness, and regional variation separately.

CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide assessment is expected to provide one of the most comprehensive evaluations of cancer care preparedness undertaken in India. Findings are anticipated to inform national policy and program planning, including investment priorities under the NP-NCD, Ayushman Bharat, and related initiatives to support progress toward equitable, comprehensive cancer care and universal health coverage.

articles.title: A Multifaceted Intervention to Reduce Obesity Among Preschool Children in Suzhou City: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of obesity among preschool children has become a critical public health concern in Suzhou, China. Nevertheless, evidence-based, personalized, and multicomponent intervention strategies tailored to children with overweight or obesity remain inadequately established in current practice.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the prevalence and pathogenic factors of obesity among preschool children in Suzhou and to develop a comprehensive and multifaceted integrated intervention program. Through systematic assessment of its short-term effectiveness and long-term sustainability in improving obesity-related indicators and preventing overweight, it provides a scientific basis for obesity prevention and control.

METHODS: This cluster randomized controlled trial is being conducted among children aged 3 to 6 years in Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province. Children from 3 kindergartens were randomly assigned to the intervention group and children from 3 other kindergartens were assigned to the control group. The 1-year intervention includes health education, dietary guidance, and increased physical activity, adopting a multilevel approach that engages children, families, schools, communities, and society. Children participate in health education and physical activity courses in the kindergarten, while parents receive educational materials online. Parental education and regular assessment of knowledge, attitudes, and practices are key components of the family-based intervention. Body measurements will be taken at baseline, 6 months, 12 months, and thereafter, alongside questionnaires for both parents and children to evaluate their own health behaviors. The primary outcome will be the difference in BMI, BMI z scores, and body fat percentage between the 2 groups of children at the end of the intervention.

RESULTS: The study received ethical approval in March 2025. Baseline assessments were conducted from March to June 2025, followed by the initiation of the intervention, which will be completed by June 2026. Participants will then enter a noninterventional long-term follow-up until June 2032, with annual surveys conducted during this period.

CONCLUSIONS: This program will test the effectiveness of comprehensive multifaceted interventions on children. The results of this study will provide scientific evidence for formulating effective intervention strategies for childhood overweight and obesity and are also expected to offer crucial practical references for the formulation and improvement of treatment guidelines for childhood obesity in China.

articles.title: Pruritus-dominant herpes zoster with concurrent contralateral upper limb pain in a patient with complete spinal cord injury: A case report.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Sensory impairment after spinal cord injury (SCI) may complicate herpes zoster (HZ) recognition.

FINDINGS: A 76-year-old man with complete T4* paraplegia developed pruritus and vesicles in the right T4 dermatome without eruption-site pain. The asterisk denotes adjustment for stroke-related left upper-limb weakness. Empiric intravenous acyclovir preceded dermatology assessment. Contralateral shoulder and hand pain developed the day after eruption and was absent on the final treatment day.

CONCLUSION/CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Focal pruritus warrants skin examination. When HZ is strongly suspected, timely empiric antiviral therapy should not await specialist assessment. The contralateral pain course was noteworthy, but an HZ-related mechanism remained uncertain.

articles.title: Impact of Laser Vision Correction on Readiness and Operational Performance Among Active Duty Service Members.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Optimal visual performance is essential for modern military operations. Traditional forms of vision correction, including spectacles and contact lenses, may present operational limitations during deployment or field training. The Department of Defense established the Warfighter Refractive Eye Surgery Program (WRESP) to provide laser vision correction (LVC) to improve operational readiness by reducing reliance on corrective eyewear among active duty service members (ADSM). This study evaluated ADSMs' perceptions of overall satisfaction, visual outcomes, operational performance, and military readiness following LVC performed at the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA)-Lackland, Joint Warfighter Refractive Surgery Center (JWRSC).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to ADSM who underwent LVC at the JBSA-Lackland JWRSC between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2025. The survey link remained active for 2 weeks. Survey domains included perceived visual outcomes, operational performance, confidence in military duties, nighttime operations, marksmanship, and overall satisfaction after laser vision correction. Inferential statistics, including Pearson's Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression, were utilized to compare perceived outcomes across surgical cohorts and identify potential predictors of reported performance declines.

RESULTS: Of 1,971 successfully delivered survey invitations, 1,206 ADSM responded. Uncorrected distance vision improved in 99.00% of respondents, with no significant difference among procedures (P = .806). Overall satisfaction was also exceptionally high at 97.34%, which was statistically comparable across PRK (97.4%), LASIK (97.4%), and SMILE (97.2%) cohorts (P = .791). High rates of self-reported performance improvements were observed across key operational domains, including marksmanship (67.66%), physically demanding activities (78.36%), near-task performance (83.75%), deployment or field exercises performance (78.11%), tactical confidence (93.03%), and, with no significant differences by procedure type (all P > .05). A perceived decline in nighttime operations was reported by only 5.6% of respondents, occurring in 4.7% of PRK (95% CI: 3.6%-7.2%), 6.9% of LASIK (95% CI: 5.5%-11.8%), and 6.2% of SMILE (95% CI: 4.2%-12.7%) recipients (P = .184). In a multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, rank, and branch, procedure type was not significantly associated with nighttime decline (LASIK vs. PRK: P = .084; SMILE vs. PRK: P = .339). Additionally, 68.2% of respondents reported that LVC positively influenced their decision to remain in the military with no significant differences by procedure type (P = .661).

CONCLUSIONS: LVC is associated with substantial self-reported improvements in visual readiness and operational task performance, with exceptionally high, comparable satisfaction across PRK, LASIK, and SMILE cohorts. Reducing physical dependence on corrective eyewear is perceived to enhance readiness, justifying continued program investment and future objective longitudinal evaluations.

articles.title: Standardizing cardiopulmonary bypass management for left ventricular assist device implantation: A clinical framework and checklist.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPatients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation often present with end-stage heart failure, severe pulmonary hypertension, and systemic inflammation. During this procedure, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) acts as a double-edged sword: it provides essential life support but can exacerbate right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and trigger severe vasoplegia. Despite the critical nature of the transition from CPB to mechanical support, there is a lack of standardized, phase-specific CPB management protocols.MethodsBased on current guidelines, frontline perfusion experience, and an interdisciplinary approach integrating mechanical engineering principles with surgical practice, a comprehensive clinical framework for CPB management was developed. The protocol deconstructs the procedure into four distinct phases: pre-bypass assessment, on-bypass management, weaning, and post-bypass care.ResultsA four-stage standardized checklist and an intraoperative emergency quick reference card were created to facilitate clinical translation. Key interventions include identifying anatomical "minefields," maintaining a golden balance of hemodilution, executing a dynamic flow-speed handover to prevent suction events, and managing hemodynamics cautiously during protamine administration to mitigate RV dysfunction.ConclusionsStandardizing CPB management during LVAD implantation provides a practical tool to optimize hemodynamic stability and improve perioperative safety.

articles.title: Infected With the Clinical Bug.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

articles.title: Social Media Use and Digital Professionalism in Nursing Practice: Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rapid growth of social media has transformed communication, with more than 5.66 billion users worldwide in 2025 who spent an average of 141 minutes daily on platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, and TikTok. Nurses frequently use social media to exchange work-related information, communicate with others, and relieve stress. While social media can support professional development, excessive or inappropriate use at work may compromise patient care. Despite widespread use, research on nurses' demographic factors and actual workplace social media behaviors remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to determine how nurses use social media at work and how their demographic characteristics (eg, gender, age, and number of years working in health care) are related to the use of social media at work.

METHODS: This study used a quantitative, descriptive, exploratory, and nonexperimental empirical research design. Data were collected via a survey administered to a convenience sample of 132 nurses. The sample comprised of 98 women (74.2%) and 34 men (25.8%). The questionnaire consisted of 17 statements related to social media use in the workplace. A statistical significance level of P<.05 was applied. Descriptive statistics and inferential statistical tests were used.

RESULTS: Nurses used Facebook the most and spent between 45 minutes and 1 hour per day on social media. Study participants reported that they primarily used social media for communication with colleagues and acquiring new knowledge. They also used social media for its technical functions, such as file sharing. Nevertheless, a substantial number of nurses reported using social media during working hours, and many had experienced creating an uncomfortable situation after declining social media interactions with patients or colleagues.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the important topic of social media use at work by nurses. The study found that nurses frequently used social media, primarily for professional communication and knowledge acquisition. While most demonstrated positive use patterns, the findings indicate that social media use during work may pose potential challenges to professionalism. These results highlight the need for clear guidelines and training to ensure that nurses use social media responsibly, maintaining both professional boundaries and personal integrity. Encouraging mindful and regulated use can enhance the benefits of social media while minimizing risks in the health care setting.

articles.title: Making Genomic Data Actionable in Electronic Health Records: Practical Viewpoint on Standards, Governance, and Implementation.
articles.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are central to patient-centered care. However, many current EHR systems do not represent, exchange, or reuse genomic findings in structured, interoperable, and clinically actionable forms. Instead, genomic results are often retained in static reports. This limits their use in routine clinical care and clinical decision support. It also restricts their future reinterpretation as scientific knowledge evolves, as well as their reuse for research within appropriate governance frameworks. To support precision and personalized medicine, we advocate that clinically relevant genomic findings should be represented within EHRs as structured, phenotype-linked, interoperable, and versioned data. Raw and intermediate genomic files, however, should remain in appropriately governed laboratory or genomics repositories. This viewpoint is intended for health policymakers, health informatics leaders, EHR developers, research and clinical genomics laboratories, and clinicians involved in implementing genomics into routine care. It is informed by selected published literature and relevant technical standards. It is also informed by operational experience at the Cyprus Institute of Neurology and Genetics and multidisciplinary discussions from the Gen2EHR Implementation Guidelines Workshop conducted within the Extended EHR@EU Data Space and European Health Data Space for Secondary Use @CY initiatives. We examine technical, organizational, clinical, ethical, legal, and governance challenges, including inconsistent reporting formats and unclear clinical responsibility. We propose a staged, workshop-informed implementation pathway for evaluation within the European Health Data Space. The pathway combines Health Level 7 Fast Health Interoperability Resources Genomics Reporting with complementary standards and terminologies. It also includes transitional dual PDF and structured Fast Health Interoperability Resources reporting, governance for access, version control, reinterpretation, and clinical responsibility, as well as multidisciplinary pilot validation in real diagnostic workflows. The clinical effectiveness and transferability of the proposed pathway across European health systems remain to be established.

articles.title: Cross-Domain Chest Radiograph Report Generation Under Dataset Shift: Bidirectional Audit Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cross-domain chest radiograph report generation may produce formally valid reports that are nevertheless repetitive, weakly case-specific, or missing clinically relevant findings. These failures can be missed when evaluation relies on a single language-overlap or clinical-label score.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate cross-domain report generation with a bidirectional layered audit, characterize direction-specific and end point-specific failure profiles under a composite training-side control and 3 decoding policies, and explore whether selected audit dimensions remained informative for a contemporary medical vision language model.

METHODS: A fixed R2Gen-style system was evaluated bidirectionally on 575 IU X-ray and 401 MIMIC-CXR (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care Chest X-Ray) target records. The audit included surface validity, complete-report recurrence and concentration, a predefined prefix end point, lexical diversity, official Stanford CheXpert/NegBio labels, paired cluster-bootstrap inference, and blinded review by 2 medical trainees. The primary human audit included 210 reports from 70 randomly sampled cases, with blinded adjudication of unresolved primary end point disagreements. A 60-report targeted panel was used for failure-mode analysis. Separately, a fixed MedGemma 1.5 4B configuration generated reports for all 976 records.

RESULTS: In MIMIC-CXR-to-IU X-ray transfer, out of 575 reports, ON (protocol-defined training-side control enabled)+B4 (beam search with a beam size of 4) reduced the predefined recurrent prefix from 575 (100%) to 8 (1.4%; Holm-adjusted P=.002). However, 569 (99.0%) ON+B4 outputs still belonged to exact duplicate groups. In IU X-ray-to-MIMIC-CXR transfer, the 14-category CheXpert/NegBio micro-F1 was higher for ON+B4 than for OFF (protocol-defined training-side control disabled)+B4 (0.1687 vs 0.0744; Holm-adjusted P=.01). This apparent advantage was not broad-based: after cardiomegaly was excluded in a post hoc descriptive sensitivity analysis, the difference changed from +0.0944 to -0.0610. Text-level tracing showed that the original contrast was mainly driven by a labeler response to recurrent, semantically normal heart-size wording. Across the primary human-audit cells, major omissions occurred in 12 to 15 out of 35 reports, and major unsupported findings occurred in 10 to 16 of 35 reports, with no consistent configuration ordering observed. The exploratory MedGemma micro-F1 was 0.4722 on IU X-ray and 0.4340 on MIMIC-CXR, but 381 out of 575 (66.3%) IU outputs belonged to exact duplicate groups.

CONCLUSIONS: No configuration performed consistently well across end points, and no single metric captured all forms of cross-domain degradation. The MedGemma stress test suggested that recurrence and label-traceability checks remain useful across architectures, although it was not a matched performance comparison. Cross-domain report generators should undergo bidirectional evaluation, final-text verification, and image-grounded human review before external validation or clinical deployment.

articles.title: Delayed intervention of a thrombotic saphenous vein graft lesion.
An abietane diterpenoid from Tripterygium wilfordii inhibits influenza A virus replication and modulates host immunity.
articles.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection remains a pervasive global public health threat. Natural products are recognised as a valuable reservoir for the discovery and development of novel antiviral agents. This study investigated the anti-IAV activity and mechanisms of 11-Hydroxy-14-methoxy-18 (4→3)-abeo-abieta-3,8,11,13- tetraen-18-oic acid named Triptobenzene H (TPZH), a diterpenoid isolated from Tripterygium wilfordii. In IAV-infected MDCK cells, TPZH increased the viability of IAV-infected MDCK cells, limited ROS accumulation, and alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, TPZH targeted the viral replication stage, disrupting the IAV life cycle and reducing viral loads. Furthermore, in virus-stimulated macrophages, TPZH suppressed inflammatory protein expression and cytokine overproduction through inhibiting activation of MAPK and NF-κB signalling pathways. Collectively, TPZH exerts anti-influenza effects by blocking viral replication and alleviating virus-mediated inflammatory injury via modulation of macrophage-dependent immune responses. This study demonstrates that TPZH exhibits multi-target pharmacological properties and holds promising therapeutic potential for anti-influenza treatment.

articles.title: Bioassay-guided isolation of coumarins and other secondary metabolites from Otostegia fruticosa with antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens.
articles.abstract: Otostegia fruticosa (Lamiaceae) is an ethnomedicinal shrub traditionally used for cleansing and infection-related ailments in the Horn of Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. This study isolated eight secondary metabolites from the aerial parts: five coumarins-psoralen (1), bergapten (2), umbelliferone (3), prangol (5), and hydroxydecursinol (7); the megastigmane vomifoliol (4); the phenolic acid vanillic acid (6); and the polymethoxylated flavonol galetin 3,6-dimethyl ether (8), all isolated and fully characterised for the first time from the genus Otostegia. The MeOH extract, CH2Cl2 fraction, and purified compounds were evaluated by broth microdilution against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MDR A. baumannii and C. auris. The CH2Cl2 fraction showed broad-spectrum bactericidal and fungicidal activity, while the MeOH extract was selectively bacteriostatic against MDR A. baumannii. Psoralen (1) and galetin 3,6-dimethyl ether (8) were principal contributors, with compound 8, for the first time, exhibiting potent fungicidal activity against C. auris.

articles.title: Effects of Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitor Baxdrostat on Albuminuria in CKD and Uncontrolled Hypertension.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

articles.title: Toward Reinforcement Learning-Enabled Model-Informed Precision Dosing: Concepts, Applications, and Implementation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Reinforcement learning is suited to sequential decision making in clinical settings, where treatment strategies are adjusted based on patient response. This aligns with therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing, in which dosage is iteratively refined as conditions evolve. Thus, reinforcement learning is a potential dosing optimization framework. This review provides a structured and clinically interpretable overview of these applications and their implementation.

METHODS: A narrative literature review of studies that applied reinforcement learning to dosing optimization was conducted, using database searches and manual screening. Studies were qualitatively analyzed for drug type, algorithm, training environment, and their state, action, and reward definitions. A simplified implementation example using a deep Q-network illustrates the core workflow.

RESULTS: Reinforcement learning has been applied across diverse clinical settings, including anesthesia, oncology, and critical care. Most studies used simulation-based environments (pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, or mathematical models) to enable safe, scalable training. Off-policy methods (eg, Q-learning and deep Q-networks) were commonly used for discrete dosing decisions and retrospective data; on-policy methods (eg, actor-critic approaches) were applied when adaptive dose adjustment was required. Substantial variability was observed in algorithm selection and in state, action, and reward definitions. The simplified example illustrates how deep Q-network-based reinforcement learning can be integrated with pharmacokinetic models to support dose optimization.

CONCLUSIONS: Reinforcement learning provides a flexible framework that complements pharmacometric models to support dosing optimization. Further research is required to develop best-practice recommendations for study design, algorithm selection, reward design, and model evaluation to facilitate translation into clinical practice.

articles.title: Effect of randomness and delay in extracellular glucose transportation into cardiac contractility under diabetic conditions.
articles.journal: Mathematical medicine and biology : a journal of the IMA
articles.abstract: The present in-silico study incorporates a stochastic framework for GLUT4 recruitment to examine the coupled dynamics of glucose transport and myocardial contractile function. In their previous study, Das et al. (2020) developed a glucose-insulin interaction model incorporating a transportation delay associated with GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake. However, prior evidence suggests that GLUT4 recruitment exhibits stochastic behavior. Accordingly, the present study extends the model by introducing stochastic perturbations into GLUT4-mediated glucose transport. The results indicate that stochasticity constrains parameter recalibration under diabetic conditions. Moreover, in the absence of delay, although the deterministic system attains a steady state, the stochastic counterpart exhibits persistent temporal fluctuations, inducing transient dynamics at the molecular level.

articles.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: NIR-Activated ROS/NO Cascade Nanocomposite Rewires Bacterial Redox Defense for Synergistic Eradication of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Wound Infection.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm formation and bacterial redox-adaptive defenses weaken antibacterial efficacy and delay tissue repair. In this study, we reported a near-infrared (NIR)-activated reactive oxygen species (ROS)/ nitric oxide (NO) cascade nanocomposite, UCeSi-L@CA, designed to amplify oxidative/nitrosative antibacterial stress while promoting infected wound healing. UCeSi-L@CA was constructed from Ce6-loaded mesoporous silica-coated upconversion nanoparticles, with L-arginine conjugated through surface carboxyl groups and cinnamaldehyde loaded into the mesopores. Upon NIR irradiation, upconversion nanoparticles activated Ce6 to generate abundant ROS. Cinnamaldehyde exerted direct antibacterial activity and inhibited glutathione-mediated ROS scavenging, thereby sustaining ROS accumulation and weakening bacterial antioxidant defense. The accumulated ROS further triggered NO production from L-arginine, establishing a ROS/NO cascade in which ROS and NO cooperatively damaged bacterial membranes, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and induced efficient bacterial killing. Beyond antibacterial activity, NO also contributed to infected tissue repair. In vitro, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR showed excellent killing against planktonic P. aeruginosa, effectively inhibited biofilm formation, eradicated bacteria within established biofilms, and suppressed biofilm regrowth. In the P. aeruginosa-infected wound model, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR markedly reduced local bacterial burden, attenuated infection-associated inflammation, accelerated wound closure, and promoted tissue repair, with favorable biocompatibility in vitro and in vivo. This nanocomposite presents a non-antibiotic nanotherapeutic strategy integrating NIR-triggered ROS generation, cinnamaldehyde-mediated GSH-defense inhibition, and L-arginine-derived NO release for treating refractory biofilm-associated wound infections.

articles.title: Specific effects of Pulsed Field Ablation on the cardiac tissue, the nervous system and the conduction system in experimental and clinical studies.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel ablation modality for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias and has rapidly reshaped contemporary electrophysiology practice. This article provides a comprehensive analysis on the mechanisms underlying the specific effects of PFA on myocardial, neural tissue structures, and the cardiac conduction system, integrating biophysical principles with preclinical and clinical evidence relevant to contemporary electrophysiology practice.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This document provides an exhaustive mechanistic explanation for the preferential effects of PFA on myocardium and the limits of the 'tissue-selectivity' concept. The complex interplay between cellular and tissue-level biophysics, biological responses, and tissue regenerative capacity that determines differential susceptibility to electroporation across tissues is analysed. Distinct patterns of lesion formation and maturation following PFA are also reviewed, highlighting the temporal and histopathological differences compared with radiofrequency ablation. Additionally, lesion formation in heterogeneous substrates is analysed, including fibrotic and adipose-rich myocardium, where local electric field distribution critically influences lesion durability.

CONCLUSION: The article further examines the interaction between pulsed electric fields and neural tissue, with emphasis on the phrenic nerve and intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system. While nerve stimulation and transient reversible conduction disturbances produced by reversible electroporation can occur during ablation, permanent neural injury appears extremely rare in current clinical experience. Finally, this manuscript examines current understanding regarding the specific effects of PFA on the cardiac conduction system, which according to the limited available evidence appear strongly dependent on electric field dose and anatomical proximity.

articles.title: Safety considerations and clinical monitoring during pulsed field ablation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a transformative technology in cardiac electrophysiology, offering a potentially superior safety profile compared with thermal ablation due to its non-thermal mechanism of irreversible electroporation. Clinical experience confirms a substantial reduction in traditional complications such as pulmonary vein stenosis, atrio-oesophageal fistula, and permanent phrenic nerve injury, though PFA introduces a distinct spectrum of physiologic effects requiring consideration. Coronary vasospasm is the most characteristic phenomenon, ranging from transient, subclinical constriction to rare ischaemic or arrhythmic events; mitigation relies on coronary anatomical awareness, optimized lesion placement, and prophylactic vasodilators. Haemolysis, caused by red blood cell electroporation, varies with catheter design and pulse burden and is typically mild, though high exposure and inadequate hydration may rarely lead to acute kidney injury. Silent cerebral lesions could result from procedural and/or energy-related factors, including gas formation, air ingress, catheter manipulation, and anticoagulation management, with uncertain long-term clinical impact but opportunities for technique-driven reduction. Interactions between PFA and cardiac implantable electronic devices are system- and context-dependent, with monopolar configurations and catheter-lead proximity influencing the risk of transient interference and rare permanent damage.

articles.title: Pulsed field ablation: from concepts to technology.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a transformative approach for treating cardiac arrhythmias by exploiting irreversible electroporation to preferentially injure myocardium while limiting collateral damage. Translating this biophysical principle into safe and effective clinical systems requires careful integration of waveform design, catheter engineering, computational and experimental modelling, safety testing, and procedural workflow.

OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes the fundamental physical and engineering principles that govern cardiac PFA and examines how these principles influence efficacy, safety, lesion formation, and clinical usability.

BIOPHYSICAL AND TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS: Electroporation is governed primarily by the local electric field and waveform-dependent lethal thresholds rather than generator voltage alone. Key waveform variables include monophasic vs. biphasic pulses, microsecond vs. nanosecond pulse widths, duty cycle, and total application duration. Catheter design further determines electric field distribution, lesion geometry, current density, and applicability across anatomic targets, with important distinctions between bipolar and monopolar configurations.

MODELLING AND SAFETY: Experimental and computational approaches used to investigate PFA include finite element simulations, cell culture systems, vegetal substrates, and in vivo animal models, each with distinct strengths and limitations. High-voltage pulse delivery can also produce unintended effects, including Joule heating, electrochemical reactions, bubble formation, arcing, and interactions with implanted electronic devices. These phenomena highlight the importance of optimized waveform design, electrode configuration, and safety monitoring.

CLINICAL USABILITY: Clinical adoption depends not only on biological efficacy and safety but also on workflow efficiency, catheter versatility, procedure duration, mapping integration, anaesthesia requirements, and adaptability to differing clinical practices and geographic settings.

CONCLUSIONS: The performance of a PFA system reflects the interaction of biophysics, waveform characteristics, catheter design, modelling, safety controls, and procedural usability. Understanding these interconnected principles is essential for developing PFA technologies that are effective, safe, predictable, and practical for contemporary electrophysiology laboratories.

articles.title: Treatment of paroxysmal and persistent atrial fibrillation with pulsed field ablation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation has emerged as a novel energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering preferential myocardial ablation with a favourable safety profile. Contemporary paroxysmal AF clinical studies demonstrate 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence in approximately 75-85% of patients, with major complication rates generally ranging from 1 to 3%. Compared with thermal ablation, PFA offers comparable efficacy and streamlined procedural workflows. In persistent AF, PVI remains the foundation of ablation, while additional adjunctive strategies are increasingly evaluated. Current evidence suggests that PFA can achieve 12-month arrhythmia-free outcomes generally ranging from approximately 60-75% in persistent AF populations. Major procedure-related complications typically occur in <3% of cases, supporting the feasibility of broader lesion sets with an acceptable safety profile. However, the incremental benefit of adjunctive ablation beyond PVI and the optimal lesion set for persistent AF remain to be assessed further Outcome assessment after PFA requires consideration of evolving endpoints. The clinical relevance of the traditional post-ablation blanking period is being re-evaluated, while continuous rhythm monitoring and AF burden are increasingly incorporated alongside conventional recurrence endpoints. Patient-reported outcomes are an important component of PFA evaluation. Compared with thermal ablation, PFA is associated with improved procedural tolerability, reduced analgesic requirements, rapid recovery, and the potential for same-day discharge. These features, together with favourable efficacy and safety outcomes, may contribute to broader adoption of PFA across both paroxysmal and persistent AF populations.

articles.title: Controlling pulsed field ablation efficacy during ablation procedures.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as a promising ablation modality for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias because of its myocardial tissue preferential ablation and favourable safety profile. However, procedural control of lesion formation and reliable assessment of lesion durability remain important challenges. This review summarizes the main determinants of PFA efficacy and current approaches for intraprocedural lesion assessment. Experimental and clinical studies indicate that PFA lesion formation results from the interaction between delivered electrical energy, catheter design, tissue coupling, and application strategy. Lesion size and geometry are primarily determined by electric field distribution and cumulative electroporation exposure, while excessive energy delivery may induce unwanted thermal or electrochemical effects. Procedural efficacy also depends on stable catheter positioning, adequate tissue proximity, and sufficient lesion overlap. Unlike thermal ablation technologies, conventional procedural markers such as electrogram attenuation, impedance changes, and pacing threshold variation correlate poorly with durable irreversible electroporation. Multiparametric lesion estimation models integrating electrical, mechanical, and positional data have shown encouraging preclinical results, although clinical validation remains limited. Emerging strategies combining electroanatomical mapping, imaging, and automated electrogram analysis may improve real-time evaluation of lesion continuity and durability. Current PFA workflows rely mainly on standardized energy delivery protocols, optimized catheter positioning, and lesion overlap rather than real-time titration of energy. Although robust intraprocedural markers of irreversible electroporation are still lacking, ongoing advances in catheter technology, imaging, and lesion assessment tools are expected to improve procedural reproducibility and long-term lesion durability. Further studies are needed to establish validated endpoints for durable PFA lesion formation.

articles.title: Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as an important energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering tissue selectivity and procedural efficiency while introducing specific anaesthetic and sedation requirements. This narrative review examines the rationale for anaesthesia and sedation during PFA, the mechanisms underlying pain, involuntary movement, and neuromuscular stimulation, and the implications of catheter design, waveform characteristics, and patient-related factors for peri-procedural management. Available evidence indicates that both deep sedation and general anaesthesia can provide safe and effective procedural conditions when supported by appropriate monitoring, airway rescue capability, and experienced multidisciplinary teams. Deep sedation may offer advantages in workflow, recovery, and patient-centred care, particularly for standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures using contemporary biphasic systems with reduced muscle activation, whereas general anaesthesia remains appropriate for complex procedures, patients with substantial comorbidity, or settings in which complete immobility and airway control are essential. Current real-world practice is highly heterogeneous across regions and institutions, reflecting differences in regulations, staffing models, procedural complexity, and local expertise rather than a universally accepted standard. Overall, anaesthetic strategy in PFA should be individualised according to patient risk profile, expected procedural demands, and device-specific stimulation burden. Further prospective comparative studies are needed to define optimal sedation depth, standardise monitoring and outcome measures, and clarify how emerging technologies may enable lighter yet still effective sedation pathways.

articles.title: The future of PFA in cardiac ablation procedures.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as a major development in catheter ablation, with increasing clinical adoption driven by procedural efficiency and a favorable safety profile compared with thermal energies. This article summarizes the future directions of PFA in electrophysiology, focusing on technological innovation, and how these advances are expected to expand PFA clinical indications. Additionally, this article provides a perspective on current gaps and future challenges of PFA. A perspective on future developments in new waveforms, catheter architectures, and integration with electroanatomical mapping systems for PFA is summarized. The document discusses novel waveform configurations and catheter design concepts that may improve lesion quality, procedural versatility, and safety. Additionally, this article also reviews how parallel advances in electroanatomical mapping integration, artificial intelligence, and robotic navigation are expected to enhance procedural guidance and enable individualized therapy. This manuscript summarizes the potential applications of PFA beyond pulmonary vein isolation and how emerging evidence supports its feasibility for linear atrial lesions, substrate modification, treatment of complex atrial tachycardias, and ventricular arrhythmia ablation. In addition, this article provides insights on how PFA may facilitate catheter ablation in new patient populations including elderly patients and those with higher procedural risks. Finally, this manuscript provides an outlook at major remaining challenges and knowledge gaps for PFA. The lack of homogenous procedural endpoints definitions and lesion durability assessment are discussed. Furthermore, this article highlights the need for standardized terminology and reporting in an environment where the high heterogeneity between available commercial systems complicates comparison across technologies.

articles.title: The perspective of combining pulsed field ablation and left atrial appendage closure.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) are increasingly discussed as complementary strategies in atrial fibrillation (AF) care, addressing rhythm control and long-term thromboembolic risk. The rationale is attractive, but the current evidence base is uneven. Randomized evidence for LAAC around AF ablation is strongest for thermal-ablation-era workflows, particularly the OPTION trial, which showed lower non-procedure-related major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with LAAC than with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and non-inferiority for death, stroke, or systemic embolism. Dedicated PFA-specific evidence remains limited to feasibility studies and early observational experience, and no trial has demonstrated that combined ablation-LAAC procedures are clinically superior when the ablation component is performed with PFA rather than radiofrequency or cryoballoon ablation. In parallel, OAC-withdrawal trials after apparently successful ablation, including OCEAN and ALONE-AF, have reported low thromboembolic event rates in selected lower-risk populations, whereas CLOSURE-AF cautions against simple extrapolation of LAAC benefit to older, frailer patients at high stroke and bleeding risk. This review therefore positions combined PFA-LAAC as a potential option for carefully selected patients rather than an established routine strategy. We summarize procedural workflow, patient selection, trial populations, device-platform considerations, reimbursement and organizational issues, and the main uncertainties that should guide future prospective studies.

articles.title: Protective Effect of COVID-19 Vaccination on Post-Infection Visuospatial Deficits.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil : 1999)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: COVID-19 has been associated with persistent cognitive deficits months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination reduces severe disease, but its effect on post-infection cognition remains uncertain. We evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination attenuates cognitive deficits after SARS-CoV-2.

METHODS: We assessed 237 adults with COVID-19 and 105 controls. Patients were grouped by vaccination status at infection (vaccinated n=87; unvaccinated n=150). The neuropsychological assessment covered language, visuospatial ability, visual memory, verbal memory, attention, executive functions, and working memory. Group differences were tested with Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA with Holm-corrected post hoc comparisons, adjusting for education.

RESULTS: Significant group differences were observed in visuospatial ability and visual memory, assessed with the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test (Copy, Immediate and Delayed Recall) (all p < 0.001). The vaccinated group outperformed the unvaccinated group (p = 0.022) on visuospatial performance. The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test Copy did not differ significantly among participants vaccinated with CoronaVac, AstraZeneca, or Pfizer.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that COVID-19 vaccination may mitigate post-infection visuospatial deficits, reinforcing the importance of immunization in preventing cognitive sequelae associated with the disease.

articles.title: Decomposing the decline in life expectancy at birth by cause of death during the COVID-19 pandemic in Canada.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Life expectancy at birth has increased in Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development countries and across the globe over the past few decades, until 2019. However, this trend was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, which saw a significant decrease in life expectancy in Canada and many other countries. Few studies to date have decomposed the life expectancy gap by cause of death observed during the pandemic in a Canadian context.

DATA AND METHODS: Death counts were generated from the Canadian Vital Statistics - Death database. Life tables were created using Chiang's method. The Arriaga method for decomposing a life expectancy gap was implemented by comparing life tables between the periods of 2017 to 2019 and 2020 to 2022 by province and sex.

RESULTS: COVID-19 was the single largest contributor to the life expectancy decline in Canada between the periods of 2017 to 2019 and 2020 to 2022, reducing life expectancy at birth by 0.46 years for both sexes. Opioid-related deaths, another significant contributor to the life expectancy decline, reduced life expectancy by 0.22 years for both sexes. By contrast, cancers contributed to a slight increase (+0.17 years) in life expectancy between the two periods.

INTERPRETATION: Although COVID-19 was the most significant driving force in declining life expectancy during the pandemic in Canada, increased opioid-related deaths, potentially related to the indirect effects of the pandemic, also played a significant role in the notable life expectancy decline. A greater understanding of the indirect impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in terms of mortality, including the harms related to substance use and abuse, will be possible as more information on the causes and circumstances of death is made available.

articles.title: Meta-analysis of over 8,000 individuals from Hawai'i and Samoa for genetic associations to cardiometabolic phenotypes.
authors: Samoan Obesity, Lifestyle and Genetic Adaptations (OLaGA) Study Group
articles.abstract: Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) now routinely reveal genetic associations and biological insights in millions of individuals, underrepresentation of global populations, such as those from Polynesia, continue to persist. These exclusions, often driven by logistical challenges and lack of data, prevent systematic identification of population-enriched associations, such as the association of the missense variant at the CREBRF locus to BMI and type 2 diabetes discovered commonly occurring in Polynesian populations due to its rarity in global populations. Armed with the recently updated TOPMed imputation panel that could benefit studies in diverse populations that previously had poorer imputation performance, we performed the first GWAS of Native Hawaiians and Samoans, the largest to date of Polynesian-ancestry populations (combined N up to 8,461) to identify population-enriched associations for 13 adiposity and cardiometabolic traits available across both cohorts: BMI, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HDL, height, hip circumference, HOMA-IR, LDL, T2D, total cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, and waist-hip ratio. We found 25 trait-loci associations that met genome-wide significance: 20 previously reported or known associations and 5 putatively new associations via meta-analysis. In particular, with improved statistical power, we were able to confirm the previously suggestive association between the missense CREBRF variant with fasting glucose levels. The remaining 4 potentially novel loci-trait associations for BMI, LDL, and waist-hip ratio, however, were not replicated in All-of-Us. The lack of Polynesian-enriched findings outside of the CREBRF locus informs the bounds of the effect sizes or frequencies of any enriched variants and suggests that further expansion of cohort sizes from this region of the world and improved imputation references specific to these populations are needed to identify more population-enriched associations.

articles.title: The growing repertoire of putative pathogen interaction genes in the Biomphalaria glabrata vs Schistosoma mansoni system.
articles.abstract: Schistosomiasis is major neglected tropical disease of humans that is caused by trematodes in the genus Schistosoma. Humans are infected during contact with water in which schistosomes are being shed from their intermediate hosts, freshwater snails. Snail control is effective at reducing transmission, but can be expensive and ecologically problematic. Therefore, there is substantial interest in understanding the genetic mechanisms behind variation in snail resistance to infection by schistosomes, with the goal of leveraging that information to reduce transmission at the snail stage. Biomphalaria glabrata is an important host snail for transmission of S. mansoni in the New World. Here we reanalyzed an older Genome-Wide Association Study (GWAS) dataset from Biomphalaria glabrata snails challenged by the trematode, Schistosoma mansoni. We identified two new regions of association with resistance to infection, named LG5R and LG11L. LG11L contains a cluster of genes for a diverse set of secreted lectins, which could be involved in some type of recognition. LG5R contains a cluster of genes for what appear to be membrane-bound receptors. These genes are very similar to those identified in an adjacent genomic region by a recent GWAS on the African snail, B. sudanica challenged by S. mansoni. Clusters of genes for single-pass transmembrane proteins also characterize two other genomic regions of association with resistance to S. mansoni that were previously described for B. glabrata (the PTC1/GRC and PTC2 regions). We hypothesize that the proteins coded for in such clusters of genes are involved in some type of matching polymorphism that may explain the ubiquitous parasite-population by snail-population interaction in compatibility that characterizes the B. glabrata-S. mansoni system. We discuss our results in light of the state of the field of genome-wide mapping studies on Biomphalaria sp., and discuss what types of loci found to date would be the best targets for reducing transmission in natural populations.

articles.title: Schistosoma haematobium infection among school age children in two peri-urban areas of Lusaka, Zambia: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Schistosomiasis is one of the most prevalent neglected tropical diseases in sub-Saharan Africa, causing substantial morbidity and millions of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Although the WHO aims to eliminate schistosomiasis as a public health problem in several countries by 2030, current epidemiological data on schistosomiasis in Zambia are insufficient to adequately characterize transmission patterns, identify priority intervention areas, and inform the planning and evaluation of control programmes.

METHODS: We assessed the prevalence of urogenital schistosomiasis among school-age children in two peri-urban districts of Lusaka (Chongwe and Kafue). A total of 208 participants were enrolled, and infection status was determined using urine filtration microscopy, ELISA, and quantitative PCR (qPCR).

RESULTS: Urogenital schistosomiasis prevalence was significantly higher in Chongwe than in Kafue, as determined by both microscopy and qPCR. By microscopy, 34 of 48 positive cases (70.8%) were from Chongwe and 14 (29.2%) from Kafue (χ² = 4.84; P < 0.05). Similarly, qPCR revealed a prevalence of 73.9% in Chongwe and 28.9% in Kafue (χ² = 13.52; P < 0.01). No significant association was observed between sex and infection status. However, infection was significantly associated with age across the study population.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that urogenital schistosomiasis remains highly prevalent in the peri-urban districts of Chongwe and Kafue in Lusaka Province, Zambia, highlighting ongoing transmission and the need for strengthened surveillance and control efforts. These results provide updated information on the epidemiological situation of urogenital schistosomiasis in Zambia and will support planning and implementation within the WHO NTD agenda.

articles.title: Novel Protein Biomarkers to Monitor Kidney Function Decline and Treatment Response in Individuals With Normoalbuminuria and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Kidney function can decline in individuals with type 2 diabetes despite normal albuminuria, yet current risk stratification relies heavily on urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), which may inadequately capture this process. We investigated whether biomarkers reflecting inflammation, tubular injury, regenerative capacity, and fibrosis improve risk prediction and treatment monitoring beyond UACR in these individuals. Baseline UACR did not predict the composite kidney outcome, whereas TNFR-1, TNFR-2, KIM-1, and MMP-7 were independently associated. In those who developed the outcome, these biomarkers and uEGF/Cr showed divergent trajectories, unlike UACR. Biomarkers capturing pathways beyond glomerular injury may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring in these normoalbuminuric patients.

articles.title: Cross-sectional study on the association between seroprevalence among children and their parents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices in a dengue-endemic city in Bangladesh.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bangladesh is experiencing a drastic increase in dengue infections since 2019, with a record number of cases exceeding 300,000 in 2023 and 102,082 cases in 2025. Control of dengue, spread by Aedes mosquitoes, requires an in-depth understanding of knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding prevention strategies and their association with the risk of infection. This association has been rarely examined in adults and even more rarely in relation to the risk of infection in children. This study aimed to investigate the association between parents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) and children's dengue seropositivity in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional study was conducted in four neighborhoods of Dhaka in November and December 2023. A total of 297 parents and 412 children aged 2-12 years participated in the study. Parents completed a questionnaire that collected data on their previous dengue experiences, sociodemographic characteristics, social capital, and knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to dengue. Children's capillary blood samples were collected via finger prick and tested for IgM and IgG dengue antibodies. The relative risk (RR) of dengue seropositivity was estimated using a modified Poisson regression model with robust error variance.

RESULTS: The median ages of the parents and children were 32.5 and 6.7 years, respectively. The adjusted seroprevalence of dengue for both IgM and IgG in children was 14.0% (95% CI 10% -19%). Parents' KAP scores were classified as intermediate knowledge of the disease in 60.3% of participants; 64.3% reported positive attitudes towards dengue control and prevention actions; and 62.0% had a high score for dengue prevention practices. A higher parent attitude score was associated with lower child seropositivity (aRR 0.77, 95% CI 0.60-0.99).
