CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preliminary insight into the factors associated with dengue seropositivity in children in Dhaka, offering additional information about parents' attitudes towards dengue risk and prevention and the relationship with child's seropositivity. This information can guide public health interventions, such as dengue control campaigns. A more in-depth exploration of the context will help to understand the cultural and social factors that shape KAP in Dhaka.

articles.title: Targeting ZIP12-mediated Zn2+ signaling as a treatment for pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12, ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis shapes T cell biology and immune reconstitution after hematopoietic cell transplant.
articles.abstract: Successful hematopoietic cell transplant requires immunosuppression to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), a lethal, T cell-mediated complication. The phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial demonstrated superior GVHD-free/relapse-free survival for posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy)-based GVHD prophylaxis versus tacrolimus/methotrexate (Tac/MTX), but the T cell biology underpinning these outcomes remains unknown. To determine this, 324 patients were coenrolled onto BMT CTN 1801 to investigate the distinct T cell immune reconstitution pathways of these regimens, including extensive evaluation of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, via sequencing of 2359 longitudinal samples and 180,432,350 T cells. Multimodal T cell analysis revealed that PT-Cy was associated with pan-T cell deletion followed by delayed T cell expansion from a smaller founder population compared with Tac/MTX. This created a T cell diversity bottleneck, leading to reduced TCR repertoire diversity for 2 years posttransplant. Reduced TCR diversity, more common in patients receiving PT-Cy, was linked to protection against chronic GVHD when patients were analyzed without regard to study arm. Leveraging donor- and host-specific TCR clonal analysis, we determined that PT-Cy-mediated T cell depletion also depleted pathogen-specific TCRs, rendering PT-Cy patients more likely to lack detectable graft-derived pathogen-specific TCRs early after transplant, which was associated with an increased risk of severe infection. This study reveals how distinct immunosuppression strategies uniquely remodel T cell immunity and shape divergent transplant outcomes.

articles.title: A 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that selectively recognizes ergosterol's conjugated diene uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity.
articles.abstract: Amphotericin B remains the gold-standard therapy for invasive fungal infections, but its clinical utility is limited by toxicity arising from poor selectivity for fungal ergosterol over mammalian cholesterol, a challenge that decades of medicinal chemistry have failed to fully overcome. Here, we report mandimycin M16, a polyene macrolide engineered from a unique 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity. Mandimycin M16 exhibited potent, broad-spectrum activity against 11 tested World Health Organization (WHO) priority fungal pathogens. Unlike amphotericin B, which binds cholesterol, M16 exhibited no detectable cholesterol binding and showed no detectable hemolysis, cytotoxicity, or nephrotoxicity at concentrations up to 128 micrograms per milliliter in vitro and after up to seven daily intravenous doses in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that mandimycin M16 exerted rapid fungicidal activity through selective recognition of the conjugated C5-C8 diene system present in ergosterol but absent in cholesterol, a mode of sterol discrimination fundamentally different from classical polyenes. In multiple disseminated murine infection models, M16 outperformed liposomal amphotericin B at equivalent doses, achieving up to 3.4 log reduction in fungal burden and 100% survival without detectable renal injury by biomarkers or histopathology. These findings establish that the 5 + 1 polyene architecture enables complete sterol selectivity and molecularly uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity, providing a next-generation antifungal candidate for the treatment of invasive fungal infections.

articles.title: Analysis of the impact of naturally-acquired immunity on Shigella vaccine performance to inform clinical trials: A simulation-based modeling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective vaccines against Shigella, the leading bacterial cause of diarrheal disease globally, could prevent morbidity and mortality from shigellosis as well as limit antibiotic resistance. Several Shigella vaccine candidates are in late stages of development, and the design of large Phase 3 trials in target populations is underway. In high incidence settings, children are expected to rapidly accrue natural immunity such that after repeated pathogen exposure, unvaccinated infants may have similar levels of immunity as vaccinated infants. For this reason, in these settings estimates of vaccine efficacy (VE) may underestimate expected efficacy in a fully naïve population. To set expectations and support optimal planning of future Shigella vaccine trials, we aimed to quantify the potential impact of this phenomenon on VE estimates under different surveillance strategies and assumptions about Shigella immunity.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We simulated Shigella vaccine trials in low-, medium-, and high-burden settings under different assumptions about vaccine- and infection-conferred immunity. We estimated VE against severe, Shigella-attributable disease and any Shigella-attributable diarrhea under six trial designs: active surveillance for Shigella infection or symptom-based reporting paired with single-outcome, stratified recurrent outcome, or crude recurrent-outcome Cox proportional hazards models. In each scenario, we evaluated bias, 95% confidence interval (CI) coverage, and the false negative rate. Only the trial design using active surveillance for infection and single outcome models was consistently unbiased across all examined scenarios. The other five designs underestimated VE by up to an absolute 20%, with a single outcome model paired with symptom-based reporting performing least poorly. Bias generally was worse at higher-burden sites. For realistically sized trials, the 95% CI coverage and false negative rate were also worse at higher-burden sites. The results were sensitive to input parameters which depended on assumptions about Shigella natural history based on limited published data.

CONCLUSIONS: The observed VE in Shigella vaccine trials is likely to underestimate true VE, though the magnitude of underestimation described here is conditional on the simulation's inputs and assumptions. Careful trial design is needed to minimize this underestimation.

articles.title: Impact of violence on HIV outcomes among female sex workers: A global systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female sex workers (FSW) are a key population for HIV prevention and care. Increasing evidence suggests that social and structural barriers are key drivers of HIV transmission. This global systematic review assesses whether experiencing violence is associated with worse HIV outcomes among FSW.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO databases for studies published from January 1st, 2010 to June 9th, 2026 assessing the impact of violence on HIV outcomes among FSW, without restriction to language and study design. Some studies had multiple estimates due to reporting on multiple outcomes or exposures of interest. We pooled data from eligible studies using multi-level random-effects meta-analyses to quantify associations between recent (past year) or lifetime exposure to violence (physical, sexual, emotional/psychological, and/or financial) and HIV outcomes (prevalent and incident HIV infection, HIV testing, ART use, ART adherence, and viral suppression) among FSW. We preferentially used adjusted estimates over unadjusted estimates if both were available. We included 94 studies with 226 estimates, comprising 186,613 FSWs in 39 countries. Half the included studies were in low- and middle-income countries (n = 47, 50%), and one-fifth were in low-income countries (n = 18; 19%). We found higher odds of prevalent HIV infection among FSWs with recent (pooled odds ratio (pOR):1.31; 95% CI [1.16,1.48]; I2: 63%; n = 75 estimates) and lifetime (pOR:1.35; 95% CI [1.23,1.48]; I2: 39%; n = 68) experiences of violence. When stratifying violence by type, we found the strongest pooled associations between recent (pOR:1.55; 95% CI [1.24,1.94]; I2: 69%; n = 28) and lifetime (pOR:1.40; 95% CI [1.21,1.63]; I2: 47%; n = 28) experiences of sexual violence and HIV prevalence. Recently experiencing violence was associated with reduced odds of ART use (pOR:0.78; 95% CI [0.64,0.94]; I2: 8%; n = 17). Lifetime exposure to violence was associated with reduced odds of viral suppression (pOR:0.88; 95% CI [0.79,0.98]; I2: 20%; n = 6). There was no evidence of associations between violence and HIV incidence, HIV testing, and ART adherence. Our study had limitations, notably the cross-sectional design of most included studies, the heterogeneity in pooled estimates, and the difficulties of measuring experiences of violence.

CONCLUSIONS: Experiencing violence is associated with greater odds of prevalent HIV infections, and poorer HIV treatment outcomes among FSWs. HIV interventions for FSWs must address violence as a structural determinant of HIV.

articles.title: Diverse infection models demonstrate robust resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to innate immunity.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is a robust activator of innate immunity. While innate immune activation of macrophages can impact Mtb replication in vitro, there is little in vivo evidence that the innate immune system controls Mtb before the onset of adaptive immunity. Prior work has generally used specific pathogen-free (SPF) mouse models and relatively large infectious doses, which may obscure the capacity of innate immunity to control Mtb. Here, we performed ultra-low dose Mtb infections and found that the initial innate immune response was unable to curb even minimal Mtb infectious doses. Additionally, we primed the immune systems of C57BL/6 mice by co-housing with "pet shop" mice prior to Mtb exposure. Co-housed mice were as susceptible to Mtb infection as SPF mice. To pre-activate innate immunity at the site of Mtb infection more specifically, we also infected the lungs of mice with Legionella pneumophila (Lp) prior to Mtb. Innate immunity alone can clear large doses (>100,000 CFU) of Lp from the lung within a few days. However, priming the mouse lung by pre-infection with Lp only modestly reduced Mtb CFU compared to mice infected with only Mtb, indicating that Mtb can robustly replicate even in the presence of a strong anti-bacterial innate response. We performed single-cell RNA-sequencing on myeloid cells from mice either infected with Mtb alone or mice primed with Lp. We found that Lp priming before Mtb infection induced measurable changes in myeloid cells responding to Mtb, but these changes had little effect on innate control of Mtb. Together, these data demonstrate the robust resistance of Mtb to innate immune clearance under diverse experimental conditions.

articles.title: Wolbachia outcompetes mosquito-borne viruses by reprogramming host ATPSβ1-driven ATP metabolism toward symbiotic proliferation.
articles.abstract: Wolbachia endosymbionts confer broad-spectrum resistance to mosquito-borne viruses. While the antiviral metabolites in Wolbachia-Aedes have been identified during viral replication, the core metabolic gene underlying this defense across the entire viral infection cycle remains undefined. Here, we demonstrated for the first time that Wolbachia strongly suppressed the emerging alphavirus Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, extending its known antiviral spectrum. Transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed ATP synthase beta subunit 1 (ATPSβ1) as a key metabolic hub hijacked by both MBV and the symbiont. Without Wolbachia symbiosis, dengue virus and VEEV induced ATPSβ1 to promote viral binding via the viral envelope protein and increased intracellular ATP production for viral replication. Conversely, Wolbachia overrode ATPSβ1-mediated viral binding and redirected ATPSβ1-driven ATP synthesis to fuel its proliferation, strengthening antiviral activity. Pharmacologically, adenosine increased Wolbachia wAlbB density and potently suppressed viral infection in Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus cells. Oligomycin reduced intracellular ATP and inhibited viral infection in Wolbachia-free Ae. aegypti cells. Collectively, Wolbachia repurposes dual-functional ATPSβ1, which governs MBV binding and replication, into a potent antiviral effector through a metabolic tug-of-war over host ATP during symbiont-virus competition. Moreover, we highlight interventions targeting the ATPSβ1-driven metabolism as promising strategies to curb MBV transmission.

articles.title: PDIM drives the transition from repairable to catastrophic EsxA-mediated vacuole membrane damage during Mycobacterium marinum infection.
articles.abstract: During infection, pathogenic mycobacteria damage the membrane of the Mycobacterium-containing vacuole (MCV), triggering host repair responses that preserve an intracellular permissive niche before bacteria escape to the cytosol at later stages. How the MCV transitions from repairable injury to catastrophic rupture remains poorly understood. Here, we dissected the respective contributions of the ESX-1 effectors EsxA/EsxB and the cell-envelope lipid phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) during Mycobacterium marinum infection of the amoeba Dictyostelium discoideum. Combining host reporters for membrane damage and repair with single and double bacteria mutants, we show that EsxA/EsxB and PDIM are both required for full intracellular virulence but act at distinct stages of MCV damage progression. Loss of EsxA/EsxB strongly reduced recruitment of ESCRT and autophagy reporters to the MCV, demonstrating that EsxA initiates repairable membrane lesions. In contrast, PDIM-deficient bacteria retained the ability to recruit early damage reporters and ESCRT machinery but showed reduced autophagy-associated repair, failed to efficiently acquire cytosolic perilipin coating, and remained largely confined within the MCV. Genetic disruption of host autophagy restored cytosolic access and increased intracellular growth of PDIM-deficient bacteria, indicating that PDIM is specifically required to overcome host repair capacity rather than to initiate damage. Importantly, the sequential requirement for EsxA and PDIM was conserved during infection of murine microglial BV-2 cells. Remarkably, PDIM-defective mutants induced lysenin recruitment, a reporter of sphingomyelin exposure, but progression to autophagy engagement was strongly decreased. Together, our results support a two-step model in which EsxA initiates MCV membrane damage, while PDIM amplifies these lesions towards catastrophic rupture, enabling escape to the cytosol and dissemination.

articles.title: Spatio-temporal machine learning for multi-horizon prediction of bluetongue outbreaks.
articles.abstract: Reliable early warning of infectious disease outbreaks remains a major challenge for surveillance systems, particularly for vector-borne pathogens whose transmission depends on interactions among hosts, vectors, and climate-sensitive environmental conditions. Data-driven forecasting offers a promising approach for predicting outbreak risk using surveillance and environmental data. This study develops a logit-weighted ensemble (LWE), a machine-learning framework that predicts outbreak occurrence 1-6 months ahead at the administrative unit-month scale using routinely available outbreak notifications and gridded climate data. Bluetongue virus (BTV), an arbovirus of ruminants transmitted by Culicoides biting midges, provides a well-characterised system in which transmission is strongly shaped by climate, making it a useful system for applying and testing this approach. The framework is evaluated using surveillance data collected between 2005 and 2024 from France, Greece, and Italy, selected for their long-running and high-quality outbreak surveillance records. Across all three countries, the LWE achieved the strongest and most stable predictive performance under a recall-focused evaluation that prioritises correctly identifying outbreak months. It outperformed or matched 14 benchmark models, with differences becoming more pronounced at longer lead times (month +3 onward), when predictions are more uncertain and outbreaks are relatively rare. Predictability varied across countries, with the highest performance in Greece, strong performance in France, and lower, more variable performance in Italy, reflecting differences in how consistently outbreaks occur and spread across regions. Overall, the results demonstrate that horizon-aware, climate-informed forecasting can reliably identify months and locations at elevated risk of outbreak occurrence up to six months in advance, supporting surveillance planning and preparedness across heterogeneous European settings. The ensemble framework provides a robust and portable strategy for outbreak prediction using routinely collected surveillance and environmental data.

articles.title: Lyssavirus matrix protein stabilizes RGS4 to suppress ferroptosis via incomplete autophagy and iron metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Rabies virus (RABV), the prototypical lyssavirus, suppresses neuronal ferroptosis through lipid droplet (LD) biogenesis, which is a critical immune evasion strategy we previously identified. However, the mechanistic link between LD formation and ferroptosis regulation during RABV infection remains poorly defined. Here, we report that RABV upregulate Regulator of G Protein Signaling 4 (RGS4), a ferroptosis-associated regulator, and this induction is strictly dependent on triglyceride synthesis and subsequent LD formation. Functionally, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RGS4 elevates ferroptosis susceptibility, thereby restricting viral replication. Mechanistically, RGS4 depletion reduces HERC2, impairing the assembly of branched K48/K63 ubiquitin chains on NCOA4, which is essential for its proteasomal degradation, thereby enhancing NCOA4 stability. Stabilized NCOA4 promotes ferritinophagy, leading to degradation of ferritin heavy chain (FTH) and ultimately inducing ferroptosis. Critically, we identified that the lyssavirus matrix (M) protein directly counteracts this pathway: M protein inhibits RGS4 degradation via the Cys/N-degron system through incomplete autophagy, stabilizing RGS4 to maintain HERC2 expression, promote NCOA4 ubiquitination, and attenuate ferritinophagy. This mechanism reduces ferroptosis susceptibility and enables viral replication. Our findings unveil a novel lyssavirus-specific regulatory axis, RGS4-HERC2-NCOA4-FTH, that modulates ferroptosis, highlighting the critical role of ferroptosis in lyssavirus infection and pathogenesis.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Children and Adolescents.
Tricuspid Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood.

OBSERVATIONS: Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

articles.title: Tricuspid Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy-Reply.
McConnell Sign After Syncope in a Man in His 60s.
Systemic Arterial Blood Pressure Targets and Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation or Death in Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of Newborns: A Cohort Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) is a life-threatening condition requiring intensive cardiopulmonary support. The optimal systemic blood pressure target in this population remains unknown. We evaluated the association between clinician-selected mean arterial pressure (MAP) targets and in-hospital outcomes in infants with PPHN.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of infants ≥35 weeks' gestation with PPHN treated with inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) who had a clinician-documented MAP target within the first 48 hours of age. Infants were classified as having a MAP target <50 mmHg or ≥50 mmHg. The primary outcome was the composite of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and/or death.

RESULTS: Among 109 infants, 82 (75%) were in the MAP target group < 50 mmHg and 27 (25%) were in the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target group. Compared with a < 50 mmHg MAP target, a ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target was associated with higher rates of ECMO cannulation (33% vs 11%, p=0.01) and ECMO/death (48% vs 20%, p<0.01). Use of epinephrine and hydrocortisone, use of more than two vasoactive agents, and the vasoactive-inotropic score were also higher in the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target group. After adjustment for HIE, pneumothorax, and initial oxygenation index, the ≥ 50 mmHg MAP target remained associated with ECMO cannulation (aOR 4.8; 95% CI 1.6, 15.0) and ECMO/death (aOR 5.9; 95% CI 2.0, 17.3).

CONCLUSION: Among neonates treated with iNO for PPHN, clinician-selected MAP targets ≥ 50 mmHg were independently associated with ECMO cannulation and ECMO/death. Randomized trials are needed to define safe MAP targets in PPHN.

articles.title: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias is Associated with Worse Clinical and Patient-centered Outcomes in Patient Admitted for Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aims of this study are to assess clinical and patient-centered outcomes following admission for HF as stratified by ADRD status.

METHODS: We identified patients 65 years or older in the OneFlorida+ data trust with first admission for HF between October 1, 2015 and December 31, 2022. ICD-10 diagnoses codes were used to identify HF, ADRD, and relevant comorbidities. Exclusion criteria were admission with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or shock. The primary clinical outcome was all-cause 1-year mortality, and the secondary clinical outcome was 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes were length of stay and discharge home.

RESULTS: 22,342 patients with first HF hospitalization during the study period were identified. Of these, 5,261 (23.5%) patients carried a diagnosis of ADRD. Patients with ADRD were more likely to be women (57.7% vs. 53.1%, p<0.05) and Black (21.1% vs. 14.6%, p<0.05). 1-year mortality was higher in patients with ADRD (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.36, p < 0.005) as was 90-day readmissions (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.18-1.28, p <0.005). Patients with ADRD demonstrated longer lengths of stays (5.7 vs. 5.4 days, p <0.005) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR .81, 95% CI 0.77-0.84, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Patients with ADRD hospitalized for HF demonstrate higher 1-year mortality and 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes are also worse in patients with ADRD, with longer lengths of stay and are less discharge home. These findings should be used to identify research priorities and to facilitate advanced care planning in patients with ADRD and HF.

articles.title: EEG Edge-Centric Dynamics Reveal Distinct Post-Stroke Somatosensory Network Responses to Vibratory and Electrical Stimulation.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Stroke-induced somatosensory deficits disrupt sensorimotor integration (SMI) and limit motor recovery, yet the immediate network-level effects of different somatosensory interventions remain unclear, hindering patient-specific rehabilitation planning. We propose an informatics framework based on edge-centric dynamic connectivity (ECDC) to characterize transient, whole-brain EEG network responses to sensory-level focal vibratory stimulation (FVS) and neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES). We analyzed EEG recordings from 15 chronic stroke participants and 15 healthy controls during forearm stimulation and quantified temporal network dynamics, spectral network organization, and interhemispheric interactions from instantaneous overlapping functional networks. Compared with NMES, FVS in stroke participants induced a distinct neurophysiological profile, including (i) shorter global theta-network latency, suggesting faster attentional engagement; (ii) higher contralesional alpha network diversity, indicating enhanced somatosensory recruitment; and (iii) reduced theta-alpha phase-amplitude coupling, reflecting decoupled interhemispheric interactions that may support adaptive reorganization. These findings provide interpretable network signatures for differentiating stimulation-specific brain responses and suggest a data driven route toward personalized SMI rehabilitation.

articles.title: Hierarchically Gated Multiplex Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with Self-Distillation for Protein Stability Prediction.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Predicting the impact of protein residue mutations on thermal stability is critical for protein engineering and for understanding how mutations contribute to cancer development. Recent advances in deep learning demonstrate great promise in the prediction of mutation-induced protein stability changes; however, current approaches face several drawbacks to be solved: 1) neglect the inherent heterogeneity of relations among residues, 2) lack of information-filtering from noisy context, and 3) insufficient supervision of sparse and weak signals of mutation. To address these issues, we propose a protein stability prediction model named HierGate, which is featured by a hierarchically gated multiplex heterogeneous graph neural network with self-distillation mechanism. It is designed to capture the multiplex heterogeneous relations among residues; on the other hand, hierarchical gating mechanism is introduced to suppress contextual noise upon heterogeneous neighbor aggregation. In addition, self-distillation strategy is leveraged to amplify the weak mutation signal. Comprehensive evaluations on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms advanced protein stability prediction approaches, with an improvement of up to 13% over the second-best baseline on certain datasets. We also demonstrate the practical capability of HierGate in investigating the underlying mechanisms of cancer development and in guiding directed evolution in protein engineering.

articles.title: AI-Powered Structuring of Clinical Information in Parkinson's Disease: An Approach Based on Large Language Models.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Advanced Parkinson's Disease (APD) is clinically heterogeneous, and many APD-defining features are recorded predominantly in unstructured neurology narratives, limiting scalable phenotyping and longitudinal analyses. An approach based on large language models (LLMs) was designed to transform free text from electronic health records (EHRs) into an APD-oriented dataset aligned with Questionnaire for the Evaluation of Advanced Parkinson's Disease (CDEPA)-derived domains. A retrospective EHR cohort identified between January 2018 and January 2023 from a tertiary neurology service comprised 1,201 confirmed Parkinson's disease (PD) patients after diagnostic eligibility filtering. Following privacy-preserving de-identification, GPT-4o populated a schema of 22 binary APD-relevant indicators and the PD diagnosis date using four functional blocks for presence/absence/unknown classification, controlled-option selection, temporal-period extraction, and date extraction. Repeated sampling with vote-based aggregation, schema-guided recursive routing, and deterministic temporal normalization were used to reduce stochastic variability and constrain temporal inference. Performance was assessed against an expert reference standard of 120 cases annotated by four neurologists. Across 2,760 variable instances, accuracy was 83.3%, precision 61.4%, sensitivity 85.4%, specificity 82.7%, negative predictive value (NPV) 94.6%, and F1-score 71.4%. The methodology achieved higher performance than all evaluated zero-shot biomedical/clinical baselines and direct GPT-4o; paired patient-level analyses also confirmed significant improvements over GPT-4o and the no-voting ablation across all six metrics after Holm correction. Diagnosis-date extraction remained the main limitation. The proposed schema-driven workflow can convert heterogeneous EHR narratives into APD-relevant structured variables for longitudinal research and downstream modeling, with targeted clinical review for critical fields.

articles.title: Correction: Inhibitors of the small membrane (M) protein viroporin prevent Zika virus infection.
Operating Room-Complete Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Thoracoscopic Surgery Without Repositioning.
articles.abstract: Patients who cannot sustain gas exchange during one-lung ventilation may still require a brief thoracoscopic procedure. Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can support them, but conventional practice involves cannulating the supine patient and then turning them laterally while they are circuit-dependent. We describe an operating-room-complete strategy in which the semi-supine position is the single operative position: femoral access and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery proceed without repositioning, with exposure adjusted by rotating the table. The vein is cannulated with a purse-string, permitting direct repair at decannulation. No heparin is given systemically or in the prime; antithrombogenicity relies on heparin-bonded surfaces, a flow of 2.5-3.5 L/min, brief support, and predefined rescue triggers. Between October 2022 and June 2025, the strategy was applied in five of 548 thoracoscopic procedures. Operative times were 124-172 min, and venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support was 27-69 min; all were weaned in the operating room without thromboembolic or hemorrhagic complications.

articles.title: Interpreting Outcomes After Early Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy Liberation with Caution.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

articles.title: Workplace and age associated with severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies: a nationwide study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among working-age populations globally, occupational injuries and workplace cardiovascular emergencies remain major contributors to morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between workplace settings, age groups, and the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular events.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective registry-based observational study using emergency medical services data from Japan, including 454 043 working-age individuals recorded in 2021-2023. Workplace settings (office, indoor worksite, factory, outdoor worksite, construction, agriculture, and others) and age groups were analysed in relation to event severity, categorized as non-life-threatening or life-threatening. Multivariable regression models estimated the associations, and workplace-age interactions were assessed.

RESULTS: Compared with office settings, all other workplaces were associated with higher odds of life-threatening injuries, particularly agriculture and construction. Increasing age groups were progressively associated with greater injury severity. The workplace setting was associated with the severity of stroke and ischaemic heart disease, particularly in uncontrolled outdoor environments. Stroke severity was elevated in those aged 45-59 and 60-69 years, while all older age groups were associated with severe ischaemic heart disease. Workplace-age interactions were significant only for occupational injuries.

CONCLUSIONS: Workplace and age were interactively and independently associated with the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies.

articles.title: Anti-annexin A5 Autoantibodies in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Related to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection (HIV-PAH): A Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Autoantibody profiles in HIV-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (HIV-PAH) remain poorly characterized. Using a validated proteomic pipeline (two-dimensional immunoblot, mass spectrometry, ELISA), we compared 20 HIV-PAH patients with 20 HIV controls without PAH. Anti-annexin A5 (AnxA5) autoantibodies were present in 55% of HIV-PAH patients versus 0% of controls (P < .001) and anti-14-3-3ε in 35% versus 5% (P = .04), despite comparable HIV duration, CD4 counts, and virological control. Both remained associated with PAH after adjustment for coinfections. These autoantibodies mirror those described in connective-tissue-disease-PAH, suggesting a possible overlap in autoimmune features and a research biomarker warranting prospective validation.

articles.title: Before treatment alters the picture: ultrasound and metabolic biomarkers in treatment-naïve MASLD-the modifying role of BMI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: B-mode ultrasonography is widely used to assess hepatic steatosis in MASLD. The associations between ultrasound-assessed steatosis, liver size, and metabolic abnormalities have previously been studied without considering whether the patients had received treatment. Medications may modify liver enzymes, glycemic indices, lipid profiles, and body weight and may strongly affect these relationships. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate hepatic echogenicity grade and liver size in relation to body mass index (BMI) and metabolic markers in newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve MASLD patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 122 adults with MASLD, as confirmed by a gastroenterologist, were enrolled. Hepatic echogenicity and cranio-caudal liver length were assessed using B-mode ultrasonography. Metabolic parameters, including alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), total cholesterol, triglycerides (TG), total bilirubin, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), were analyzed. Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for group comparisons, while Spearman's correlation and regression models were used to assess associations, including the modifying effect of BMI.

RESULTS: In unadjusted group comparisons, ALT, AST, and HbA1c differed across steatosis grades after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, whereas total cholesterol and triglycerides showed no consistent pattern. Hepatomegaly was associated with higher BMI, ALT, AST, and HbA1c. In adjusted models, grade×BMI interactions were negative for ALT and AST (both P < 0.001), whereas the adjusted grade association between steatosis grade and HbA1c was not significant (P = 0.324). After adjustment for BMI, steatosis grade, age, and sex, liver length remained associated with ALT (β = 0.073, 95% CI 0.046 to 0.100) and AST (β = 0.062, 95% CI 0.033 to 0.092).

CONCLUSION: In treatment-naïve adults with MASLD, ultrasound-assessed steatosis grade and liver size were associated with selected metabolic and biochemical measures. Negative grade×BMI interactions were observed for ALT and AST, while the adjusted association between steatosis grade and HbA1c was not significant. These findings should be interpreted cautiously in the context of the study's design.

articles.title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

articles.title: Initial empiric carbapenem versus non-carbapenem β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor therapy in sepsis across simplified SENECA phenotypes: a retrospective study of two independent cohorts.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Whether initial empiric carbapenem therapy is associated with better outcomes than non-carbapenem β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor (BL/BLI) therapy in sepsis remains uncertain. We examined this association overall and across simplified Sepsis Endotyping in Emergency Care (SENECA) phenotypes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 4,091 patients from MIMIC-IV and 405 patients from a single-center hospital cohort. Initial therapy was defined by the first eligible carbapenem or BL/BLI regimen initiated within 24 h of admission. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included selected clinical and in-hospital microbiological detection outcomes. Each cohort was analyzed separately using inverse probability of treatment weighting and weighted logistic regression.

RESULTS: After weighting, no overall association with lower 28-day mortality was observed in MIMIC-IV (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71-1.17) or the hospital cohort (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.48-1.16). However, evidence of treatment-by-phenotype interaction was observed in both cohorts (P for interaction = 0.039 and 0.019, respectively), with lower odds of 28-day mortality among patients with the γ phenotype in MIMIC-IV and the hospital cohort (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44-0.97, and OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.04-0.46, respectively). A similar direction was observed among mechanically ventilated patients. In MIMIC-IV, carbapenem therapy was associated with longer hospitalization and more frequent detection of fungal organisms and Clostridioides difficile; these associations were not observed in the hospital cohort.

CONCLUSION: Initial empiric carbapenem therapy was not significantly associated with lower 28-day mortality overall. Consistent findings in the γ phenotype suggest possible treatment heterogeneity. These findings should be considered alongside patient characteristics and potential clinical and microbiological trade-offs.

articles.title: Does Ethnicity Influence the Long-Term Outcomes of Sleeve Gastrectomy? Results from a Prospectively Maintained Israeli Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ethnic disparities often influence patient's outcomes. This study aimed to compare the weight loss and metabolic outcomes of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) in Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients.

METHODS: A prospectively maintained cohort of 892 patients (262 Arabs and 630 Jews) who underwent LSG between 2009 and 2022 at a single tertiary academic center was retrospectively analyzed. Demographic, peri-operative, and long-term outcome data were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Arabs were younger (35 vs. 44 years) and had a higher baseline BMI (45.1 vs. 42.9). Jews had more postoperative follow-ups (6.8 vs. 6.0). Despite these differences, long-term weight loss outcomes were broadly comparable between groups. %EWL outcomes did not differ significantly at 1- and 5-year follow-up. Although Arab patients demonstrated numerically higher %TWL at 1 year, this difference did not reach statistical significance and was not sustained at longer-term follow-up. Rates of comorbidity remission, including diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, were similarly high.

CONCLUSION: Despite baseline ethnic disparities, LSG was associated with comparable long-term weight loss and comorbidity resolution among Israeli-Arab and Israeli-Jewish patients.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of mesh versus suture repairs of small umbilical hernias (≤ 2 cm).
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Updated guidelines of approaches to small umbilical hernia repairs (UHRs) ≤ 2 cm defect size are inconclusive. Operations to resolve small UHRs remain high heterogeneous depending upon local guidelines and surgical expertise, therefore there is no clear optimal approach nor guideline. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate mesh versus suture methodological approaches in small UHR.

METHODS: Systematic search of four databases (EMBASE, PubMed, OVID, MEDLINE) retrieved relevant studies after screening, de-duplication, eligibility assessment and full-text analyses were conducted. Descriptive and numerical analysis was achieved for each included study in line with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Risk of bias assessment was achieved using Cochrane risk of bias methodologies (Risk of bias in non-randomised studies, ROBINS-I; Risk of bias tool, RoB-2). Primary outcome assessed was recurrence; secondary outcomes included haematoma, bleeding, infection, systemic complications and patient-reported pain scores.

RESULTS: Mesh approaches to UHRs resulted in fewer recurrence rates postoperatively in variable follow-up periods (RR 0.46 (95% CI 0.38-0.55, I2 = 0%, p < 0.00001). Limited intra-group meta-analysis of mesh techniques demonstrated improved recurrence rates associated with onlay mesh compared with inlay/plug, intraperitoneal and sublay approaches (p = 0.00162). Suture approaches were superior for haematoma/ bleeding (RR 1.74 95% CI 1.16-2.75, I2 = 0%, p = 0.0009); infection risk (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.18-2.59, I2 = 0%, p = 0.007); however, did not reach statistical significance for pain scores postoperatively (RR = 1.20, 95% CI 0.98-1.47, I2 = 0%, p = 0.07).

CONCLUSION: Mesh-based small UHRs offers superior outcomes for short and long-term recurrence rates, although increased risk of bleeding and infection. Subgroup analyses of mesh repairs revealed merit for onlay approaches for recurrence although analysis is limited by heterogeneous study design. No significant difference in recurrence risk with choice of suture material was found. Symptomatic burden and quality-of-life detriments were not significantly higher in mesh group therefore authors contend for greater adoption of mesh-based approaches in small UHRs. Further RCTs specifically investigating small UHRs are encouraged to establish long-term adverse consequences, and longitudinal patient-reported outcome measures.

articles.title: Thermographic outcomes of auricular laser acupuncture and auricular seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain: an exploratory nonrandomized, nonconcurrent comparison.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Compare pain, quality of life, and cutaneous temperature changes within predefined anterior, lateral, and posterior shoulder regions of interest between auricular laser acupuncture and seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain.

METHODS: This exploratory, nonrandomized, open-label study enrolled 20 adults aged 60-90 years, allocated by order of entry to consecutive, nonconcurrent cohorts of auricular laser acupuncture (n = 10) or seed acupressure (n = 10), treated twice weekly for five weeks. VAS, McGill, SF-36, and thermography were assessed before the first (A1) and fifth sessions (A2) and after the tenth (A3) and analyzed using linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: From A1 to A3, VAS decreased by - 2.70 points in Laser (95% CI - 4.37 to - 1.03) and - 2.50 in Seed (95% CI - 4.17 to - 0.83); the between-group difference was - 0.20 points (Laser - Seed; 95% CI - 2.54 to 2.14). Selected McGill and SF-36 outcomes changed; McGill affective A1-to-A2 change differed between groups (Laser - Seed: -2.70; 95% CI - 4.86 to - 0.55; p = 0.017). Anterior thermal range (ΔT) showed a TIME × GROUP interaction (p = 0.007); the A1-to-A3 between-group difference was - 1.941 °C (Seed - Laser; 95% CI - 3.097 to - 0.785), although Seed ΔT was higher at baseline (+ 1.496 °C; 95% CI 0.607 to 2.385). Lateral ΔT showed a TIME effect (p = 0.033); posterior ΔT showed none.

CONCLUSION: Clinical outcomes improved over time without evidence of differential changes between interventions. Thermography identified region-specific ΔT trajectories, warranting further investigation as a complementary method.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07010627.

articles.title: Hydrogen sulfide inhibits neuroinflammation following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury via regulating glial polarization.
articles.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), an endogenous gasotransmitter, exerts potent anti-neuroinflammatory effects. Both endogenous and exogenous H2S attenuate cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury by suppressing neuroinflammatory responses. Microglia play a pivotal role in post-ischemic neuroinflammation. Upon activation, microglia polarize toward either the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype or the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. The progression of neuroinflammation is closely associated with M1 polarization, while H2S has been demonstrated to inhibit M1 polarization and promote the protective M2 phenotype. Similarly, astrocytes undergo phenotypic transformation following ischemic stroke, with A1 reactive astrocytes exacerbating neuronal injury and A2 reactive astrocytes exerting neuroprotective effects. Our previous studies have shown that both endogenous and exogenous H2S promote astrocytic polarization toward the neuroprotective A2 phenotype. This review provides a comprehensive overview of ischemic stroke and the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of H2S and its donors in cerebral I/R injury, with particular emphasis on their roles in regulating microglial and astrocytic polarization toward neuroprotective phenotypes. Additionally, we discuss the intracellular signaling pathways involved in H2S-mediated suppression of neuroinflammation. Collectively, this review highlights the therapeutic potential of H2S donors as novel agents for the treatment of cerebral I/R injury. We propose that H2S donors exert their neuroprotective effects primarily through coordinated regulation of microglial and astrocytic polarization toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes, and that this dual-cell targeting strategy represents a viable therapeutic approach for cerebral I/R injury.

articles.title: Anesthetic technique is associated with complication risk and healthcare utilization following total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Compare perioperative complications and healthcare utilization among total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) patients receiving general (GA), regional (RA), or combined anesthesia (RA + GA).

METHODS: Using the TriNetX database, patients undergoing primary TSA were identified and stratified into three groups based on anesthetic technique: GA, RA, and combined RA + GA. 1:1 Propensity score matching was performed to using the GA cohort as reference to control for baseline demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes of interest included 90-day complication rates including UTI, venous thromboembolism (VTE), acute kidney injury (AKI), prosthetic joint infection (PJI), pneumonia, constipation, and revision TSA, emergency department (ED) visits and hospital readmission, Foley catheter insertion, postoperative opioid prescriptions and mean opioid number of prescriptions. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Comparing GA with RA, each cohort consisted of 28,564 patients. RA was associated with lower rates of UTI, AKI, constipation, pneumonia, fewer patients prescribed opioids and fewer opioid prescriptions per patient while being associated with increased healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. Comparing RA + GA with GA alone, 17,926 matched patients were included in each cohort. RA + GA was associated with lower rates of UTI and opioid prescriptions, and higher rates of healthcare utilization compared to GA alone.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that while RA provides early analgesic and opioid-sparing benefits after TSA, it is associated with increased post-operative healthcare utilization. These findings help guide surgical decision making and highlight the need for standardized perioperative protocols to optimize postoperative pain control and manage rebound pain-related care utilization with RA techniques.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Authors' Reply.

Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Correspondence 2.
Diagnosis and management of polycystic ovary syndrome/polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: unmet needs and areas of clinical confidence among European endocrinologists.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a common, heterogeneous endocrine disorder whose diagnosis and management remain variable across clinical settings. Despite contemporary international guidance, several diagnostic definitions and therapeutic decisions are not consistently applied.

OBJECTIVE: To identify persistent unmet needs and areas of clinical confidence in PCOS/PMOS care, using the 2023 survey of the European Society of Endocrinology PCOS Special Interest Group as the principal data source.

METHODS: This manuscript presents a secondary, survey-informed analysis of aggregate data from an electronic cross-sectional survey distributed to members of the European Society of Endocrinology. A total of 505 respondents participated. Survey findings were interpreted in the context of current guidelines, contemporary evidence, the previous 2014 European survey, and patient-reported priorities.

RESULTS: Considerable variation was observed in the operational definition of chronic ovulatory dysfunction, the assessment of hirsutism, the biochemical evaluation of androgen excess, and the interpretation of ovarian morphology. Only one quarter of respondents reported access to liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry for steroid measurement. Uncertainty also persisted regarding the choice and duration of combined oral contraceptive therapy and the optimal pharmacological approach to chronic anovulation. Conversely, several areas of clinical confidence were evident. Respondents commonly assessed metabolic risk and lifestyle behaviours, recognized the psychological burden of PCOS/PMOS, emphasized lifestyle intervention, and supported multidisciplinary care. Physician priorities also showed increasing concordance with the concerns reported by women with PCOS/PMOS.

CONCLUSIONS: PCOS/PMOS care in Europe combines important progress in patient-centered, metabolic, and multidisciplinary management with persistent diagnostic and therapeutic variability. Greater standardization of operational diagnostic definitions, wider access to accurate steroid assays, and adequately powered comparative trials of commonly used treatments are required. These initiatives should be developed alongside, rather than at the expense of, the patient-centered practices that are already well established.

STUDY DESIGN: Secondary analysis and expert interpretation of cross-sectional survey data.

articles.title: Decoding the Safety Profile of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Facts, Myths, and Ongoing Controversies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) represent one of the most significant therapeutic advances in the management of type 2 diabetes and obesity. As their indications have expanded to include cardiovascular and kidney disease, safety concerns involving multiple organ systems have received increasing attention. This narrative review examines the spectrum of adverse effects linked to GLP-1RAs and provides a clinically relevant platform for assessing their safe prescription.

RECENT FINDINGS: Gastrointestinal intolerance, modest increases in heart rate, and a modest but reproducible increase in the risk of gallbladder and biliary disease represent the most consistently supported adverse effects of GLP-1RAs. A risk of pancreatitis is also considered to exist, although some studies have challenged this association. Conversely, correlations with neuropsychiatric and dermatological disorders, diabetic retinopathy, nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, perioperative aspiration, sexual and reproductive disturbances, sarcopenia, and malignancy remain controversial. Most available evidence derives from pharmacovigilance databases, retrospective observational studies, and secondary analyses of randomized trials, which are limited by reporting bias, residual confounding, and inability to establish causality. Heterogeneity in study design, statistical methodology, outcome definitions, and patient populations further complicates interpretation. Although several proposed adverse effects have biologically plausible mechanisms, prospective clinical validation remains limited. Notably, recent regulatory decisions, including the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)'s removal of the suicidality warning from GLP-1RA prescribing information, reflect the evolving nature of these safety assessments. The overall benefit-risk profile of GLP-1RAs is favorable. Most emerging safety concerns should currently be regarded as hypothesis-generating signals rather than established toxicities. Individualized risk assessment and appropriate clinical monitoring remain important as ongoing and future prospective studies further define the long-term safety of this rapidly expanding therapeutic class.

articles.title: Clinical performance and decision thresholds of an automated plasma p-tau217 assay for amyloid pathology in a Taiwanese memory clinic.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fully automated plasma p-tau217 assays may facilitate clinical implementation of blood-based testing for Alzheimer's disease (AD) amyloid pathology. However, data on assay-specific decision thresholds and clinical utility in East Asian memory-clinic populations remain limited.

METHODS: We evaluated plasma Roche p-tau217 in 139 participants from a Taiwanese memory clinic using amyloid PET or CSF biomarkers as reference standards. Diagnostic performance and single- and dual-cutoff decision thresholds were assessed. Head-to-head comparisons with Simoa p-tau217, Roche p-tau181, and neurofilament light chain (NfL) were performed in participants with complete biomarker profiles. Associations with body mass index and renal function were also examined.

RESULTS: Roche p-tau217 showed high diagnostic accuracy for amyloid β (Aβ) positivity (AUC 0.973). In the primary threshold-analysis cohort, a dual-cutoff approach using thresholds of 0.225 and 0.336 pg/mL classified 88.1% of participants into definitive negative or positive zones, with an overall percent agreement of 95.0% within these zones. Sensitivity analyses showed similar performance. In participants with complete biomarker profiles, no statistically significant difference in AUC was detected between Roche p-tau217 and Simoa p-tau217, whereas Roche p-tau217 showed significantly higher AUC than p-tau181 and NfL. Lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was independently associated with higher p-tau217 concentrations.

CONCLUSIONS: Fully automated Roche p-tau217 showed high diagnostic performance for identifying Aβ pathology. Cohort-derived dual decision thresholds classified most participants into definitive zones and may support plasma p-tau217-based triage for confirmatory amyloid testing in memory-clinic practice. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Demographic characteristics and comorbidities in patients with oral mucous membrane pemphigoid and pemphigus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Oral autoimmune blistering diseases (AIBDs) are a group of rare, chronic disorders causing different symptoms on the oral mucosa. The most common oral AIBDs are mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) and pemphigus vulgaris (PV). The aim of this study was to describe the demographic and clinical characteristics, as well as comorbidities, of patients with oral AIBDs in Southern and Western Finland.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-center study included patients diagnosed with AIBD with oral symptoms treated at Helsinki University Hospital and Turku University Hospital between the years 2000 and 2022. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, t-tests, Chi-square tests, Fisher's exact tests, and likelihood ratio tests.

RESULTS: Of the 115 patients (65.2% women, mean age at diagnosis 66 years) analyzed, 86.1% were diagnosed with MMP. Patients with PV were significantly younger than patients with MMP. Most of the patients who had available lifestyle information reported being non-smokers and non-alcohol users. Approximately one third of the patients had an autoimmune or neurological comorbidity.

CONCLUSIONS: There is a female predominance in oral AIBDs. Patients with MMP were older at diagnosis than patients with PV (p < 0.001). Comorbidity comparisons between diagnostic groups were limited by the small PV subgroup and should be interpreted as descriptive.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: MMP and PV are rare chronic AIBDs that can cause painful oral symptoms and thus impair quality of life. With an aging population and increasing immigration, the prevalence of these rare diseases in Western countries including Finland may rise. Therefore, early recognition and diagnosis with proper treatment and follow-up is needed.

articles.title: Long non-coding RNA LINC00657 aggravates atrial fibrosis in atrial fibrillation via the miR-144-3p/ROCK1 competing endogenous RNA axis.
articles.abstract: The clinical significance and fibrogenic mechanisms of long non-coding RNA LINC00657 in atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate whether LINC00657 served as a mechanistic driver of atrial fibrogenesis in AF via modulation of the microRNA-144-3p (miR-144-3p)/Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinase 1 (ROCK1) axis. LINC00657 expression was quantified in peripheral blood from 150 AF patients and 150 matched controls. Angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated primary rat cardiac fibroblasts and continuously infused C57BL/6 mice served as in vitro and in vivo fibrosis models, respectively. Functional assays (cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), flow cytometry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), western blot) and mechanistic experiments (subcellular fractionation, RNA pull-down, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), dual-luciferase reporter) were conducted to dissect the LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) axis. Clinically, elevated circulating LINC00657 discriminated AF patients from controls and independently predicted AF risk, correlating positively with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). In vitro, Ang II induced LINC00657 upregulation; silencing LINC00657 suppressed cardiac fibroblast proliferation, attenuated the release of inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), reduced the expression of fibrotic markers including type I/III collagen and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), and promoted apoptosis. In vivo, knockdown of LINC00657 significantly attenuated Ang II-mediated atrial fibrosis in mice. Electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring and transesophageal atrial pacing further revealed that silencing LINC00657 significantly restored the atrial effective refractory period (AERP) and markedly decreased both the inducibility and duration of AF. Mechanistically, LINC00657 was predominantly localized to the cytoplasm and functioned as a ceRNA to sponge miR-144-3p, with ROCK1 identified as a direct downstream target of miR-144-3p. Both AF patients and model mice exhibited decreased miR-144-3p and increased ROCK1 expression, which negatively and positively correlated with LINC00657 levels, respectively. Rescue experiments demonstrated that miR-144-3p inhibitors partially reversed the anti-fibrotic effects of LINC00657 silencing, whereas further ROCK1 knockdown abrogated this reversal. Mechanistically, dissection of ROCK1 downstream signaling revealed that the LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 axis specifically activated the ROCK1/myosin light chain 2 phosphorylation pathway, enhancing actomyosin contractility and stress fiber formation to drive the fibrotic cascade. The LINC00657/miR-144-3p/ROCK1 regulatory axis contributed to atrial fibrosis in AF.

articles.title: 3D printed biomimetic blade stirrer for expedient estimation of the oral bioavailability of contaminants of emerging concern.
articles.abstract: A 3D printed biomimetic blade-based microextraction device with covalently attached phosphatidylcholine (PC) is proposed as a proof-of-concept platform for the in vitro estimation of the oral bioavailability of plastic-borne organic substances with distinct physicochemical properties. The experimental conditions were designed to resemble the murine small-intestinal brush-border membrane by approximating its PC mass-to-volume ratio. The biomimetic extraction efficiency (E, %), defined as the percentage of the analyte partitioned into the PC-functionalized 3D-printed surface, was investigated as a potential in vitro descriptor. By building a multiple linear regression model incorporating E along with the solubility, hydrogen acceptor, topological polar surface area, and the aromaticity (AR) of the target compounds, an internal leave-one-out cross-validation root mean squared error (RMSE) of 7.3%, a mean absolute error of 6.2%, a bias of 1.1 and a cross validated coefficient of determination of 0.941 were obtained. As a result, the prediction error relative to the reference baseline mean prediction model is reduced by ~ 79%. The statistically significant contribution of E as an interaction term (E: AR, p < 0.01) along with the decrease of RMSE by 30% as compared to models without incorporating E suggest that the experimentally derived biomimetic descriptor captures membrane-analyte interactions that are not fully encoded by conventional physicochemical parameters. The modular design of the platform based on exchangeable blades, the low fabrication cost, and the compatibility with standard laboratory equipment supports our 3D printed biomimetic tool as a potential scalable screening tool for in vitro bioavailability assessment without need of animal models.

articles.title: Correction: Impact of age, heart rate, and body surface area on myocardial native T1, T2, and extracellular volume fraction in pediatric patients at 1.5 Tesla cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
[Sepsis-induced coagulopathy].
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) represents a frequent and prognostically highly relevant complication of sepsis, characterized by a dysregulated interaction between inflammation, endothelial activation and coagulation. Pathophysiologically, the excessive host immune response to pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMP), activation of the complement cascade, formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) and disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx collectively promote a prothrombotic and antifibrinolytic microenvironment, resulting in microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Approximately 20-25% of critically ill patients with sepsis fulfil the diagnostic criteria for SIC. Current diagnostic approaches rely on scoring systems such as the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)-SIC, ISTH overt-disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and Japanese Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (JSTH)-DIC scores; however, their clinical utility remains limited as they predominantly collate hemorrhagic parameters even though sepsis is typically characterized by a thrombotically dominated phenotype. Viscoelastic point-of-care assays enable dynamic bedside assessment of coagulation and fibrinolysis, including the frequently occurring hypofibrinolysis or fibrinolytic shutdown, which is associated with an unfavorable outcome; however, for this specific purpose, these methods have not yet been sufficiently validated or established as a diagnostic standard. Data and recommendations on specific therapeutic options are limited. A consistent pharmacological thromboprophylaxis remains the cornerstone in patients with sepsis, with low-molecular weight heparins demonstrating advantages over unfractionated heparin regarding venous thromboembolic complications. Coagulation modulating treatment, such as antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin or activated protein C, have thus far failed to demonstrate consistent survival benefits in large randomized clinical trials. Experimental approaches targeting NET formation, complement activation or fibrinolytic modulation appear mechanistically promising but require further clinical validation. Overall, SIC necessitates an individualized, pathophysiology-driven diagnostic and therapeutic approach integrating inflammatory, endothelial, thrombotic and fibrinolytic alterations.

articles.title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated transcription factor EB mRNA delivery for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent disorder characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation, frequently progressing to steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Transcription factor EB (TFEB) coordinates lysosomal biogenesis, autophagy, and lipid catabolism, and therefore represents a potential therapeutic target; however, safe and direct strategies for selectively enhancing hepatic TFEB activity remain limited. Here, liver-targeted lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) were developed to deliver mRNAs encoding wild-type TFEB or the constitutively active TFEB S211A mutant, and their efficacy was evaluated in cellular and choline-deficient, L-amino acid-defined high-fat diet (CDAHFD)-induced mouse models of MASLD. LNP-mediated delivery increased hepatic TFEB expression, enhanced autophagic flux, and reprogrammed metabolic pathways toward fatty acid oxidation (e.g., CPT1A and ACOX1) while suppressing the expression of lipogenic genes (e.g., FASN, ACC, and SREBP1). Consequently, targeted TFEB mRNA therapy significantly reduced hepatic triglyceride content, attenuated steatosis, lowered MASLD activity scores, and decreased fibrotic remodeling. Mechanistically, transcriptomic profiling, ChIP-qPCR, promoter-reporter assays, and targeted knockdown models indicated that TFEB exerts its protective effects against lipid accumulation at least partly by transcriptionally activating the fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) signaling pathway. Collectively, these findings establish LNP-mediated TFEB mRNA delivery as a useful preclinical approach for investigating hepatic biology and provide a targeted, transient, and non-integrating genetic strategy with potential for the treatment of MASLD.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Dolutegravir/Rilpivirine in Japanese People Living with HIV: Final Report of 6-Year Post-marketing Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Previous phase 3 studies demonstrated that a two-drug combination of dolutegravir (DTG) and rilpivirine (RPV) was non-inferior to three-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) with stable plasma HIV-1 RNA. In Japan, DTG/RPV was approved in 2018 for maintenance of HIV-1 suppression, but evidence on its long-term safety and effectiveness is limited.

METHODS: In this post-marketing surveillance, data on the real-world clinical use of DTG/RPV were obtained through the HIV-Related Drug Cooperative Survey, a national joint post-marketing program overseen by manufacturers of HIV medications in Japan. The data collection period was from November 26, 2018 to November 26, 2024. Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and potential risk factors associated with their incidence were examined. Effectiveness was evaluated by longitudinal changes in plasma HIV RNA levels and peripheral CD4+ T cell counts.

RESULTS: Forty-four participants were registered, of whom 43 were assessed for safety and 41 for effectiveness. Safety analyses included 39 men and 4 women, with a mean age of 53.3 years. All participants switched from other ART regimens. DTG/RPV treatment exceeded 2 years in 76.74% of participants. Four ADRs, all non-serious, occurred in three participants (6.98%): weight increased (n = 1), hypertension (n = 1), hyperuricemia (n = 1), and condition aggravated (n = 1, aggravated hyperuricemia in the participant with hyperuricemia). The incidence of ADRs differed by the following participant characteristics: treatment duration, hepatic disorder, and renal disorder. Plasma HIV RNA levels remained < 50 copies/mL for 3 years after switching to DTG/RPV in most participants. The mean (standard deviation) peripheral CD4+ T cell count was 563.3 (207.2) cells/mm3, which remained stable throughout 3 years.

CONCLUSION: This 6-year post-marketing surveillance confirms the long-term safety and effectiveness of DTG/RPV in people living with HIV in Japan who were virologically suppressed and switched to this two-drug regimen.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Toxicity Across the Cancer Immunotherapy Spectrum: Mechanisms and Management in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI) and Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell (CAR-T) Therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review evaluates the evolving landscape of cardiovascular toxicities associated with two pillars of modern cancer treatment: immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. It examines their distinct immune-mediated pathophysiologies, clinical manifestations, and management frameworks.

RECENT FINDINGS: While ICIs carry a clinical trial incidence for cardiotoxicity of approximately 1%, real-world data suggest rates of 3-5%, with myocarditis sometimes manifesting early as part of a high-mortality "Triple M" or overlap syndrome. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) occur in nearly 50% of ICI-myocarditis cases. Diagnosis relies on clinical presentation, biomarkers and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) using the modified Lake Louise criteria, with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) detection sensitivity increasing from 21.6% to 72.0% when imaged after four days of symptoms. Conversely, CAR-T cardiotoxicity is predominantly driven by cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which affects 49-93% of patients with currently licensed products. Severe CRS more than doubles the risk of cardiovascular events, including a 6-10% incidence of LVEF decline and a 4-18% incidence of arrhythmias. Recent advancements include machine learning models to predict MACE and structured screening programs to risk-stratify candidates. Cardiotoxicity remains a significant complication, highlighting the need for vigilant monitoring and early intervention. Management relies on baseline risk assessment and rapid deployment of targeted therapies, such as high-dose methylprednisolone for ICI-myocarditis and IL-6 inhibition (tocilizumab) for CAR-T-related CRS. A multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach is essential to mitigate risks. With early diagnosis and appropriate immunosuppressive strategies in a multidisciplinary setting, these complications can be better managed, optimising oncological benefits whilst reducing treatment-related morbidity and mortality in majority of patients.

articles.title: Echocardiographic predictors of left ventricular ejection fraction improvement after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has been associated with better clinical outcomes, but predictors of recovery remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify echocardiographic parameters associated with post-TAVR LVEF improvement in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) and reduced LVEF.

METHODS: Among 1,133 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR between December 2013 and June 2024, 128 with baseline LVEF < 50% and follow-up echocardiography within 3 months were analyzed. LVEF improvement was defined as an absolute increase ≥ 10%. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Post-procedural outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: LVEF improvement occurred in 64 patients (50%). Multivariable analysis identified higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.03, P = 0.01) and higher E/e' (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.18, P < 0.01) as independent predictors of improvement, whereas larger left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (OR 0.98, P = 0.01) and larger AVA (OR 0.67 per 0.1 cm², P < 0.01) were inversely associated. Patients with LVEF improvement had significantly lower 1-year all-cause mortality (98.2% vs. 87.0%, P = 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic parameters reflecting pressure overload and diastolic dysfunction predict LVEF recovery after TAVR. Postoperative LVEF improvement was associated with better 1-year survival, underscoring its prognostic value.

articles.title: Feasibility and safety of an exercise-based prehabilitation intervention before cancer surgery: a pilot randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of an exercise-based prehabilitation intervention and explore preliminary clinical outcomes in breast, colorectal, and prostate cancer patients awaiting surgery in a large regional healthcare service.
