METHODS: Patients with breast, prostate, or colorectal cancer scheduled for surgery were recruited at a single study centre and randomised (1:1) to prehabilitation or usual care. The intervention involved supervised aerobic exercise training 2-3 days per week before surgery. Usual care involved standard cancer treatment. Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, attendance, adherence, and attrition rates. Safety was evaluated via adverse event monitoring. Exploratory analyses evaluated group-by-time changes in cardiorespiratory fitness, health-related quality of life, and fatigue from baseline to the pre-surgery and post-surgery assessment timepoints, with 30-day post-operative outcomes (complications and length of stay) also collected.

RESULTS: Of 47 potentially eligible patients approached and screened, 23 were recruited and randomised, and completed baseline assessments. Twenty participants (prehabilitation n = 11, usual care n = 9) completed the pre- and T1 and T2 assessments. Participants attended an average of 5.25 ± 2.16 prehabilitation sessions. Attendance, adherence, completeness, and attrition rates were 91.3%, 82.6%, 85.7%, and 13%, respectively. Five adverse events were recorded in the prehabilitation group (fatigue, n = 3; muscular pain in the extremities, n = 2); all were grade 1. No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for cardiorespiratory fitness, health-related quality of life, or fatigue.

CONCLUSIONS: Among participants who commenced prehabilitation, attendance, adherence, and completeness were 91.3%, 82.6%, and 85.7%, respectively. No serious adverse events were observed. Exploratory clinical outcome estimates were imprecise and did not support firm conclusions regarding intervention effectiveness. Recruitment limitations and the small heterogeneous sample also preclude broader conclusions regarding feasibility.

articles.title: Parent-child discrepancies in health-related quality of life in pediatric celiac disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To evaluate differences in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) between child self-reports and parent-proxy assessments in children and adolescents with celiac disease (CeD) using the CeD Dutch Questionnaire (CDDUX), and to describe disease-specific HRQoL patterns across the included populations. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies assessing HRQoL in pediatric CeD using the CDDUX questionnaire were identified through PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library databases. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models and expressed as ratios of means (RoM). Twenty-one studies from 14 countries, including 2,453 children with CeD and 2,257 parents, were included. Children consistently reported better HRQoL than perceived by their parents, with self-reported scores 7% higher overall. Differences were observed across all domains, particularly for "Diet". Overall, CDDUX scores indicated neutral HRQoL. Across studies, domain scores followed a consistent hierarchical pattern, with "Having CD" showing the lowest scores and "Communication" the highest. Marked geographic differences emerged, with the highest HRQoL scores reported in South America and the lowest in the Middle East and North Africa.

CONCLUSION: Children with CeD reported higher HRQoL than their parents perceived, although the clinical importance of the pooled difference remains uncertain. The emotional burden of living with CeD represents the most affected dimension of HRQoL, while communication-related aspects are relatively preserved. Geographic variation emerged, however should be interpreted cautiously because comparability across language versions and cultural settings was not established.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Generic health-related quality of life questionnaires may underestimate the psychosocial burden associated with celiac disease; parent and child perceptions of disease burden frequently differ.

WHAT IS NEW: • Parents consistently report lower health-related quality of life scores than children themselves, particularly in the "Diet" domain, while the"Having celiac disease" domain represents the greatest psychosocial burden worldwide.

articles.title: Editorial Comment: Malignant Bowel Obstruction-What Is the Consensus?
The Landmark Series: Perioperative Management of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with an increasing burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-associated HCC in Western populations. In treating HCC, recurrence after curative-intent therapy remains common, creating a compelling rationale for perioperative systemic therapy.

METHODS: This Landmark Series review examines the pivotal studies that have shaped the surgical and perioperative management of HCC, tracing the evolution from principles of resectability to contemporary adjuvant and neoadjuvant immune-based strategies.

RESULTS: The development of perioperative therapy has been defined by both landmark negative trials and emerging evidence of efficacy. The STORM trial demonstrated that sorafenib's activity in advanced HCC did not translate into benefit after resection or ablation. The IMbrave050 trial subsequently demonstrated an early recurrence-free survival advantage with adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab that was not sustained with longer follow-up evaluation, whereas the KEYNOTE-937 trial failed to demonstrate benefit with adjuvant pembrolizumab. In contrast, early-phase neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor-based studies have demonstrated feasibility and meaningful pathologic responses, and the CARES-009 trial provided the first randomized phase III evidence of improved event-free survival with a perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-antiangiogenic strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative management of HCC is evolving toward an integrated, multidisciplinary treatment paradigm. Although no broadly applicable adjuvant systemic therapy has been established, emerging perioperative strategies provide proof of concept that systemic therapy may improve outcomes for selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-driven patient selection, molecular residual disease assessment, standardized pathologic response criteria, and clinical trials identifying which patients require perioperative therapy and when treatment should be delivered.

articles.title: Deep learning-based renal-trauma classification: comparison of two-dimensional convolutional neural network and vision-transformer models on arterial- and venous-phase computed-tomography images.
articles.abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of renal trauma is essential in emergency medicine. This study aimed to automatically classify renal trauma using 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) and vision transformer (ViT) models on arterial- and venous-phase computed tomography (CT) images. We analyzed CT images from 94 patients, including 47 without renal trauma and 47 with renal trauma (30,951 and 15,086 images, respectively). Arterial- and venous-phase CT images were reconstructed into axial, coronal, and sagittal images, with the renal regions cropped to construct the image datasets. Five pretrained CNN-based and five pretrained ViT-based 2D models were fine-tuned to classify renal trauma, and their performance was evaluated at the slice and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. At the slice level, the sagittal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.986 for venous-phase and 0.975 for arterial-phase images. At the patient level, the coronal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.991 for venous-phase and 0.945 for arterial-phase images. CNN-based models outperformed ViT-based models at both levels, with slice-level mean AUC values of 0.971 and 0.940 for venous-phase and 0.942 and 0.914 for arterial-phase images and patient-level values of 0.947 and 0.928 for venous-phase and 0.914 and 0.886 for arterial-phase images, respectively. The 2D models demonstrated high diagnostic performance for renal trauma, even when using arterial-phase images alone, supporting their potential for rapid decision-making in emergency settings.

articles.title: The effects of perinatal depression and anxiety on memory, attention, and cognitive flexibility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Women in the perinatal period often report experiencing cognitive difficulties, such as forgetfulness, disorientation, and a reduced attention span. However, evidence from objective neuropsychological studies is inconsistent. Depressive and anxiety symptoms have been proposed as potential contributors to these cognitive challenges, with some studies suggesting a negative association between mood disturbances and cognitive performance during pregnancy and postpartum. This review aims to characterize the relationship between perinatal depressive and anxiety symptoms and cognitive functioning (memory, attention, and cognitive flexibility).

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science and PsycINFO electronic databases. Where at least three studies with comparable designs and outcomes were available, exploratory meta-analyses were conducted and are reported in supplementary material.

RESULTS: We included 42 studies in the present review. The most consistent finding was a significant positive association between depressive symptoms and self-reported cognitive complaints across six studies. Results for objective tasks were inconsistent for working memory (k = 11), attention (k = 24), and cognitive flexibility (k = 5). Autobiographical memory was associated with depressive symptoms, but evidence was based on few studies (k = 3). Verbal memory (k = 8) and recognition memory (k = 2) were not associated with depressive or anxiety symptoms. Across domains, most studies were cross-sectional, relied on self-report symptom measures, used heterogeneous non-ecological cognitive tasks and rarely assessed anxiety, limiting the strength and generalizability of conclusions.

CONCLUSION: Depressive symptoms are consistently associated with subjective cognitive complaints, but evidence for objective cognitive impairment in the perinatal period is inconclusive. The discrepancy between perceived and measured performance highlights the possible influence of mood, sleep, mental load, and sociocultural narratives on maternal cognition. More robust longitudinal and ecologically valid studies are needed to clarify these relationships and mechanisms, and to inform the development of targeted interventions.

articles.title: [Bardet-Biedl syndrome-diagnosis, care and treatment approaches].
articles.abstract: The Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) is a genetically determined multiorgan disorder characterized by congenital postaxial polydactyly, obesity, hyperphagia and retinal dystrophy that develops in childhood. The condition is heterogeneous both in terms of molecular genetics and clinically: it is caused by mutations in at least 26 genes, and the variable extraocular manifestations include developmental delay, diabetes mellitus and fatty liver. The retinal dystrophy is also heterogeneous and presents with a broad phenotypic spectrum. While there is no specific treatment option for the retinal dystrophy, an approved treatment exists for the hyperphagia-related obesity. In addition to primary care, BBS patients should receive interdisciplinary care at specialized centers. Since 2026, patients with BBS1-associated retinal dystrophy are being enrolled in an ocular gene therapy study to evaluate the preliminary safety and tolerability of AXV-101.

articles.title: Effectiveness of cardiac resynchronization therapy in cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advances in cancer treatment have increased the number of survivors, making cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) an important concern. While cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is established for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and conduction disorders, its role in CTRCD remains unclear. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the benefit of CRT in patients with CTRCD.

METHODS: We performed a literature search of studies showing CRT outcomes in the specific group of CTRCD patients. The outcomes of interest were left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and LV volume improvement. A random effects meta-analysis was done to estimate 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: This analysis included four studies (one prospective and three retrospective) comprising 110 patients with CTRCD, the majority (91%, n = 100) being survivors of breast cancer or lymphoma/leukemia. Baseline LVEF ranged from 18.6% ± 7.6% to 28.5% ± 3.8% (mean 24% ± 7%). After a mean follow-up of 9 ± 5 months, LVEF increased by 9.95% (95% CI 7.79-12.11) and end-systolic volume decreased by 39.17 mL (95% CI 24.99-53.35). Three studies included a control group of patients with other forms of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy who underwent CRT implantation, showing no significant difference in LVEF improvement between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that CRT improves LVEF and LV volumes in selected patients with CTRCD, with a magnitude of reverse remodeling that appears similar to that observed in other etiologies of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. However, the evidence is limited to small observational studies, so conclusions about clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Thus, CRT may be considered in cancer patients who meet standard criteria for CRT implantation, but the decision should be individualized and guided by multidisciplinary assessment, cancer prognosis, and competing clinical risks.

articles.title: Interobserver agreement in prenatal ultrasound assessment of fetal urinary tract dilatation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess interobserver agreement in the evaluation of the fetal urinary tract in fetuses with urinary tract dilatation (UTD).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study evaluating interobserver agreement on renal tract features using third-trimester renal ultrasound images of fetuses with UTD. Two fetal medicine specialists and two pediatric nephrologists independently and systematically assessed ultrasound features of the fetal renal parenchyma and urinary bladder, as well as the Society for Fetal Urology (SFU) and the ONEN grading systems. Interobserver variability was analyzed using Cohen's kappa statistics and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).

RESULTS: A total of 1639 ultrasound images from 144 fetuses with antenatal UTD were analyzed. Slight to moderate agreement was observed for most renal ultrasound parameters, including cortico-medullary differentiation (κ = 0.28-0.50), renal echogenicity (κ = 0.18-0.45), and cortical cysts (κ = 0.02-0.15). A similar pattern was observed for the subjective assessment of bladder features. In contrast, both the SFU and the ONEN grading system demonstrated moderate to substantial agreement, with ICC values ranging from 0.61 to 0.73 and 0.55 to 0.66, respectively, and kappa values from 0.38 to 0.63 and 0.48 to 0.67.

CONCLUSION: Significant interobserver variability exists in the interpretation of commonly used prenatal ultrasound features for evaluating the fetal urinary tract and predicting postnatal outcomes in UTD. The SFU and the ONEN grading systems improved agreement, supporting the need for standardized ultrasound assessment tools to enhance prenatal counseling and antenatal management in fetuses with UTD.

articles.title: Fascial Dehiscence Despite Declared Adoption of European Hernia society guidelines: A retrospective study following laparotomy.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Abdominal fascial dehiscence is a serious postoperative complication following laparotomy, associated with high morbidity and mortality. Although the small-bite technique is recommended by the European Hernia Society, its implementation in clinical practice, particularly in emergency surgery, remains uncertain. This study described documented fascial closure practices among patients with fascial dehiscence following laparotomy and characterised patient-related and technical features within this cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective study included all patients who developed fascial dehiscence following laparotomy at two surgical departments in the North Denmark Region between 1 March 2021 and 1 March 2026. Data on demographics, comorbidities, operative characteristics, closure technique, and postoperative outcomes were collected from medical records and analysed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 81 patients were included. Most underwent acute laparotomy (74.1%), and 66.7% were classified as ASA score ≥ III. The declared small-bite technique was documented in 67.9% of cases, while conventional large-bite suturing was not recorded in any patient. Suture-to-wound length ratio was documented in only 2 patients (2.5%), both achieving a ratio of 4:1. Median time to dehiscence was 7 days (IQR 4-10), and reoperation was performed in 97.5% of patients. Management strategies at reoperation varied considerably, most commonly VAC therapy (46.9%) and small-bite re-suturing (43.2%), while conventional large-bite repair, absent at primary closure, was used in 6.2% of cases. The Clavien-Dindo distribution was bimodal (40.7% Grade I, 40.7% Grade IIIb), and 90-day mortality was 12.3%.

CONCLUSION: The declared small-bite technique was the predominant documented closure method among patients who developed fascial dehiscence. The high prevalence of emergency surgery and comorbidity in this cohort may suggest that patient-related and physiological factors contribute substantially to this complication. Near-universal absence of suture-to-wound length ratio documentation precludes firm conclusions regarding true guideline compliance, while marked heterogeneity in reoperative closure reflects a lack of evidence-based guidance. Improving documentation standards and directing future research toward high risk, emergency populations represent key priorities.

articles.title: Underreporting of sacroiliac joint structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in axial spondyloarthritis: a longitudinal workflow analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify documentation of predefined, conspicuous sacroiliac joint (SIJ) structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in patients with established axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) and identify associated factors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal study evaluated 516 abdominal CT examinations from 188 patients with established SpA. Two readers applied a predefined hierarchical SIJ classification, with adjudication of disagreements. The primary analysis included 226 Moderate or Major examinations; all had fusion-based patterns. Patient-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations included workflow, request-level context, structural severity, prior recognition, and scan year.

RESULTS: SIJ findings were absent from 152 of 226 reports (67.3%). Total fusion was unreported in 90 of 136 examinations (66.2%), including 83 of 129 with bilateral total fusion (64.3%). Crude non-reporting was 89.2% in acute care and 50.0% in rheumatology. The four-examination MSK-oriented subgroup was combined with rheumatology for modeling. Adjusted non-reporting was 82.7% in acute care and 50.6% in the combined MSK-pathway, a 32.1-point difference (95% CI, 6.2-52.0); the corresponding OR was 0.20 (95% CI, 0.05-0.75). Structural severity and request-level context were not independently associated with non-reporting.

CONCLUSION: Documentation of conspicuous SIJ structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT was frequently absent and varied by workflow. Including a field for SIJ findings in structured abdominal CT reports may lead more radiologists to look for joint abnormalities. Automated detection requires external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Guideline adherence in helicopter versus ground emergency medical services: an indication-based analysis of 129,783 patients from the TraumaRegister DGU®.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) are associated with higher intervention rates and improved access to specialized trauma centers compared with ground emergency medical services (GEMS). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect increased intervention intensity alone or more consistent implementation of guideline-recommended care. This study aimed to compare rates of selected guideline-recommended prehospital trauma interventions between HEMS and GEMS using a nationwide trauma registry.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study was based on data from the TraumaRegister DGU® (TR-DGU) from 2016 to 2024. Adult patients (≥ 16 years) with severe trauma, defined as maximum Abbreviated Injury Scale (MAIS) ≥ 3, receiving physician-staffed prehospital care and primary admission to German trauma centers were included. After exclusion of secondary transfers, missing key data, and treatment in local trauma centers (level 3), 129,783 patients remained, of whom 25.0% were transported by HEMS. Rates of selected interventions recommended by the German S3 guideline on the treatment of polytrauma/severe injuries were assessed using predefined indication-based subgroups derived from available registry variables as surrogates for potential clinical indications to improve comparability between transport modalities. Analyses were performed descriptively.

RESULTS: Patients transported by HEMS were younger and more severely injured than those transported by GEMS (mean ISS 23.5 vs. 20.8; ISS ≥ 16: 72.9% vs. 65.4%) and more frequently presented with impaired consciousness and shock. Across all predefined indication-based subgroups, HEMS was associated with higher rates of the evaluated interventions, including advanced airway management in patients with impaired consciousness (96.5% vs. 82.9%), overall chest tube placement in patients with thoracic injuries consistent with pneumothorax (50.5% vs. 40.9%), with substantially higher rates of prehospital chest tube placement in HEMS (14.0% vs. 5.5%), pelvic stabilization in patients with pelvic injuries of AIS severity 3-5 (56.7% vs. 44.0%), cervical spine immobilization in cervical spine injuries (84.1% vs. 77.7%), and tranexamic acid administration in suspected major bleeding (48.7% vs. 22.8%).

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide trauma registry analysis, HEMS was consistently associated with higher rates of selected guideline-related interventions across predefined indication-based subgroups. By focusing on patients with predefined guideline-related indications, the present study aimed to improve comparability between HEMS and GEMS beyond crude intervention frequencies. Nevertheless, the observed differences should be interpreted in the context of the observational study design and residual indication-related confounding. Higher intervention rates do not necessarily indicate superior guideline adherence or quality of care in individual patients.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III, retrospective comparative cohort study.

articles.title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.

RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

articles.title: Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® in treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
articles.abstract: Aim: To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® drug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database. Materials & methods: This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI. Results: A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup. Conclusion: Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

articles.title: Psychometric properties of the gum health experience questionnaire among adults in Saudi Arabia: Assessment of reliability and criterion validity.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the reliability and criterion validity of the Gum Health Experience Questionnaire (GHEQ) among Saudi adults to generate initial psychometric evidence ahead of a larger confirmatory validation.MethodsThe study adopted a cross-sectional design and was conducted among 56 adults visiting dental hygiene clinics at King Saud University. Participants completed GHEQ 64-item and underwent clinical periodontal examination including plaque and gingival index. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, reliability assessment, item-total correlations, and criterion validity evaluation through correlation with clinical parameters.ResultsThe study population comprised 51.8% females with mean age 23.8 ± 7.3 years. GHEQ internal consistency assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega found to be 0.957 and 0.962 for total score and 0.941 and 0.962 for impact score, respectively. Subscale reliability ranged from 0.800 (changes in everyday life) to 0.949 (psychological impacts). Mean total GHEQ score was 112.4 ± 41.4 (range: 55-228), while mean impact score was 13.9 ± 11.1 (range: 0-55). Item-total correlations were generally strong, with most items correlations >0.4.ConclusionsThe study provides preliminary evidence that the GHEQ may exhibits promising psychometric properties in a Saudi population, with reliability coefficients closely paralleling those of the original UK validation. The study preliminary findings suggest that GHEQ multidimensional structure may, once more fully validated, be capable of distinguishing which aspects of gum health matter most to individual patients, complementing clinical assessment. Future research studies should prioritise confirmatory factor analysis, test-retest reliability assessment, Arabic translation, and broader population sampling to confirm the validation process.Trial registrationThe study registered at https://ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06079307) https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06079307, on 16 October 2023, prior to recruitment.

articles.title: Antibiotic therapy for pelvic inflammatory disease: a network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To assess the comparative benefits and harms of systemic antibiotic regimens for the treatment of acute pelvic inflammatory disease in women of reproductive age. The secondary objectives are: to estimate the incremental effect of adding nitroimidazole to an antibiotic backbone; to compare the efficacy of azithromycin-containing regimens with relevant alternatives, where the evidence network permits (in Network B, this comparison depends on setting-disaggregated data from a single eligible trial and may not be estimable); and to describe narratively whether treatment hierarchies appear consistent between the outpatient (Network A) and inpatient (Network B) evidence, since direct statistical comparison between networks is not undertaken.

articles.title: The role of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adults with mature T-cell lymphomas.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Mature T-cell lymphomas (MTCL) are a rare, heterogeneous group of malignancies that arise from post-thymic T-lymphocytes, with a generally poor prognosis. For a long time, the standard therapy for most MTCL subtypes has been polychemotherapies. Hopes to prolong overall survival in MTCL have been associated with transplant procedures such as high-dose therapy with autologous stem cell transplantation (autoSCT) or allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT).

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of alloSCT in the treatment of MTCL in adults (≥ 18 years old) compared to any other treatment, particularly with respect to its efficacy and safety as first-line therapy, and secondarily, for its efficacy and safety as a salvage option.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, conference proceedings, and two databases of ongoing trials from January 1990 to October 2025 for prospective and retrospective studies evaluating the role of alloSCT for MTCL.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospectively planned trials assessing the role of alloSCT as first-line or salvage treatment for MTCL. As determined at the protocol stage, we excluded retrospective trials because we identified prospective ones. We excluded trials in which less than 80% of participants had MTCL, unless we could obtain a subgroup analysis for these participants.

OUTCOMES: We analyzed overall survival, progression-free survival (PFS), response rate, treatment-related mortality (TRM), quality of life (QoL), grade 3 and 4 adverse events, and incidences of acute and chronic graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD and cGVHD, respectively).

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias (RoB) in the included studies using Cochrane's RoB 2 tool for RCTs and the Cochrane Childhood Cancer Group's assessment criteria tool for observational studies. We rated the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach for all previously stated outcomes.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We followed standard Cochrane methodology, and two independent review authors performed all steps regarding study selection and risk of bias assessment in duplicate.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included one RCT of alloSCT as first-line treatment for MTCL (103 participants), and two prospectively planned trials of alloSCT as salvage treatment (119 participants): one Mendelian-randomized controlled trial for cutaneous T-cell lymphomas (CTCL) (102 participants) and one prospective observational trial for non-cutaneous MTCL (17 participants). We identified three ongoing trials. All of them are non-randomized, phase-II studies. They will mostly include relapsed or refractory lymphomas. Two other studies are awaiting classification. Overall, we rated both included RCTs to have some concerns of bias due to bias arising from the randomization process, and missing outcome data. The RoB for the prospective observational study was rated serious due to the study design, small number of participants, and reporting and detection bias.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: As we did not identify enough RCTs, we did not conduct a meta-analysis. We rated the evidence for all outcomes to be of low to very low certainty, due to the very small number of events and limitations in study design. AlloSCT compared to autoSCT for adults with MTCL (first-line) We included one RCT with 103 participants. AlloSCT compared to autoSCT may result in little to no difference in two-year overall survival (hazard ratio (HR) 1.3 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.7 to 2.4; low-certainty evidence) or PFS HR 0.9 (95% CI 0.5 to 1.5; low-certainty evidence). AlloSCT compared to autoSCT may result in a large increase in TRM (RR 18.70, 95% CI 1.11 to 315.72; low-certainty evidence), but may have no effect on overall response rate (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.73 to 1.45; low-certainty evidence). AlloSCT compared to autoSCT may result in little to no difference in the number of adverse events (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.75). 84% of all participants receiving alloSCT had aGVHD and 47% had cGVHD (very low-certainty evidence). AlloSCT for adults with non-cutaneous MTCL (relapsed or refractory setting) We included one phase-II study with 17 participants. Overall survival and PFS at two years were presented graphically in the included study, and were approximately 80% and 64%, respectively (very low-certainty evidence for both). The overall response rate was 76% after one month (70% in complete remission and 6% in partial remission; very low-certainty evidence). The two-year TRM rate was presented graphically in the included study, without making reference to absolute numbers, and was approximately 6% (very low-certainty evidence). 35% of all participants had aGVHD and 41% had cGVHD (very low-certainty evidence). Adverse events were not reported. AlloSCT compared to other treatment for adults with CTCL (relapsed or refractory setting) We included one RCT with 102 participants. AlloSCT compared to any other treatment may make little or no difference to overall survival (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.23 to 1.29; very low-certainty evidence), but may increase PFS (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.69; very low-certainty evidence). AlloSCT may make little or no difference to the number of adverse events (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.50; very low-certainty evidence). The one-year cumulative incidence of cGVHD was 31.4% (very low-certainty evidence). The overall response rate and TRM were not reported.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: In this systematic review, we identified one RCT of alloSCT as first-line treatment for MTCL, and one Mendelian RCT and one prospectively planned phase-II trial of alloSCT for relapsed or refractory MTCL. We encountered difficulties while extracting data from these studies, because there were major differences in study designs, intervention and control groups. We identified low- to very low-certainty evidence on the effectiveness and safety of alloSCT for adults with MTCL. We had some concerns about the risk of bias in the two RCTs and serious concerns about bias in the phase-II study. As there are three ongoing studies evaluating alloSCT, mostly for relapsed or refractory MTCL, it is possible that an update of this review will be published in the near future. However, none of the ongoing studies are of an RCT design.

FUNDING: Department I of Internal Medicine, Center for Integrated Oncology Aachen Bonn Cologne Duesseldorf, Faculty of Medicine and University Hospital Cologne, University of Cologne.

REGISTRATION: Protocol available via DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD014672.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Driven Precision Diagnostics and Therapeutics for Preeclampsia.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia originates in placental dysfunction yet it is detected only after maternal hypertension and proteinuria or other organ damage emerge, by which point disease-modifying interventions are not available, and delivery of the baby and placenta remains the only cure. Nanotechnology offers a route to reduce this diagnostic-therapeutic latency. Nanostructured biosensors and liquid biopsy platforms detect placental proteins, cell-free RNA/DNA, and extracellular vesicles at femtomolar concentrations and in a multiplex manner, enabling earlier risk stratification when integrated with machine-learning models. In parallel, placenta-targeted lipid-, peptide-, polymeric-, dendrimeric-, and small extracellular vesicle-based nanocarriers deliver angiogenic mRNA, antiangiogenic siRNA, antioxidants, and immunomodulators selectively to the trophoblast cells while limiting fetal exposure. Placenta-on-a-chip platforms and ex vivo placental perfusion models provide human-relevant test beds for these systems. We critically appraise these advances, examine the safety-by-design, manufacturing bottlenecks, and regulatory constraints unique to obstetric nanomedicine, and outline the convergence of theranostics and digital health that could move preeclampsia care from reactive symptom management toward proactive, placenta-targeted monitoring and therapy.

articles.title: Efficacy, Buffering Capacity and Dynamics of Saliva-Stimulating Products.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Saliva maintains the health and integrity of the oral cavity while composing a complex symphony within it. Saliva's lubricating qualities not only make talking and swallowing easier, but also promote digestion by breaking down lipids and carbohydrates through enzymatic processes.

AIM: To compare the efficacy, buffering capacity and temporal dynamics of six different saliva-stimulating products in a randomised controlled crossover trial.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: Twelve healthy adults were enrolled, each testing six products (chewing gum with mint, Salivin, Jaw Peer medium, Jaw Peer large, Jaw Peer small and control) on separate days. Stimulated saliva secretion rate, buffering capacity, and pH were measured at baseline and at 1, 3 and 6 min following product use. Comparison between products and different time points for the same product was performed using two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test. A significance level of p 0.05 was applied for statistical significance.

RESULTS: Chewing gum with mint and Jaw Peer large produced the highest stimulated saliva secretion rates. The Jaw Peer product showed the greatest decrease in buffering capacity, while Salivin showed stable buffering capacity over time. Significant temporal variations in buffering capacity were observed for all products. No significant differences were found in unstimulated salivary secretion rate between products.

CONCLUSIONS: Unstimulated salivary flow rate products exhibit different effects on salivary flow, buffering capacity, and temporal dynamics. Choice of product should be individualised based on patient preferences, specific clinical needs and duration of action, although very limited improvement was noticed with these saliva-stimulating products compared to chewing paraffin alone.

articles.title: Association Between Age, Systemic Diseases and Oral Health Habits in Stomatological Teaching Hospital Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined age-related disease patterns and health behaviours in dental outpatients to enhance risk assessment and guide clinical decision-making, providing strategies for managing medical risks in dental clinics.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 2,241 consecutive patients from a tertiary stomatological teaching hospital between November 2024 and April 2025. Based on the Pre-Treatment Risk Assessment Questionnaire for Dental Outpatients, a validated questionnaire was used to assess general demographic characteristics (10 items), systemic disease and medication use history (36 items) and oral hygiene habits (9 items). Data were analysed using SPSS 23.0 and Python 3.9.

RESULTS: It showed that 12.5% of patients were aged ≥ 60 years. Elderly dental patients had a significantly higher prevalence of both single-system and multi-system diseases compared to other age groups (p 0.001). Specifically, the population showed significantly greater proportions of sensory disorders, cardiovascular diseases, respiratory system diseases, urogenital disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, neurological disorders, and endocrine system diseases, medication use, and history of organ transplantation than younger patients, especially coronary heart disease, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, diabetes mellitus, thyroid dysfunction and osteoporosis than younger age groups (all p 0.01). Furthermore, compared to younger patients, elderly patients had lower frequencies of toothbrushing, dental floss use, water flosser use, professional cleaning, and dental check-ups but exhibited reduced gingival bleeding and oral malodor(all p 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients exhibit higher systemic comorbidities but poorer oral hygiene than younger individuals, necessitating integrated care with risk assessment and oral health education. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating geriatric medicine training to improve interdisciplinary collaboration.

articles.title: Multivariate Genome-Wide Analysis Delineates Shared Genetic Determinants Across Periodontal and Oral Microbial Phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis affects approximately 10% of the global population, posing a serious threat to tooth retention and quality of life. The disease emerges from bidirectional host-microbiome interactions that can shift from homeostasis to dysbiosis and chronic inflammation, yet conventional single-phenotype analyses cannot resolve pleiotropic loci acting across interrelated periodontal and microbial traits. We aimed to jointly model the shared genetic structure of six periodontitis-related phenotypes and to prioritise pleiotropic loci with translational relevance.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: We harmonised European-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics for six traits representing host periodontal phenotypes (gingivitis, chronic periodontitis, periapical abscess, dental calculus) and oral microbial composition (genus Porphyromonas, order Bacteroidales). A common genetic factor was estimated using genomic structural equation modelling (genomic SEM), and factor-level genome-wide association analysis was conducted on 4,899,781 SNPs. The resulting signals were annotated through locus discovery and novelty assessment (FUMA), fine-mapping (SuSiE and FINEMAP), gene-level testing (MAGMA), and transcriptome-wide association with Bayesian gene prioritisation (FUSION and FOCUS). Heritability was partitioned across functional annotations (stratified LD score regression), and cell types (CELLECT); spatial enrichment was assessed using gsMap, and a polygenic risk score was constructed with PRS-CS.

RESULTS: A single-factor model provided adequate fit (CFI = 1.0). Factor-level GWAS identified 127 genome-wide significant SNPs consolidating into 56 independent lead variants, all uniquely identified at the factor level. MAGMA prioritised RASAL2 and C5orf27. Fine-mapping yielded 56 variants with posterior inclusion probabilities exceeding 0.95. Transcriptome-wide association and FOCUS converged on the long non-coding RNA RP11-563N4.1 (PIP = 1). Cell-type enrichment highlighted a vascular-stromal axis led by hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cells, with additional signals in pericytes, cardiac and smooth muscle cells, endocardium, and lung stroma. Spatial mapping localised the strongest aggregate signal to lung tissue, consistent with an oral-lung mucosal axis. Polygenic risk was distributed unevenly across chromosomes.

CONCLUSIONS: These analyses delineate a vascular-matrix-centred genetic architecture shared across periodontal and oral microbial traits. The prioritised loci and effector genes provide genetically informed candidates for risk stratification and for targeted investigation of periodontal pathobiology. Clinically, these genetically informed candidates may aid in identifying individuals at elevated risk and in guiding mechanism-based preventive and therapeutic strategies for periodontitis.

articles.title: Endodontic Misconceptions Among Dental Patients: Prevalence and Association with Tooth Extraction Preference.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Part of proper oral health care is recognising and correcting dental myths and misconceptions that often discourage patients from seeking proper treatment decisions. Although general dental myths are well studied, little is known about the prevalence of specific endodontic misconceptions, especially those related to the effects of root canal treatment (RCT) on systemic health and their correlation with patients' preference for extraction over RCT. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of endodontic myths among adult dental patients and to explore potential associations with demographic variables and with a preference for tooth extraction over RCT.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: A self-administered paper questionnaire was distributed in person at 11 dental hospitals and private clinics in Almadinah Almunawarah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Participants in the study included adults without cognitive impairments. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic data, history of previous RCT, agreement with 10 endodontic myths, and preference for extraction over RCT. To ensure understanding and clarity of the questionnaire, a pilot test was carried out. The data were then analysed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and multivariable logistic regression tests using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25.0. The p value was set at p ≤ 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 463 participants completed the questionnaire. The most commonly endorsed myths were that root canal treatment can only be done in multiple visits (73.0%), that antibiotics are necessary during treatment (68.5%), and that root-canal-treated teeth become weak and brittle (63.1%). Almost a third of the patients (30.9%) believed that a root-canal-treated tooth remains infected; however, myths about systemic diseases were less common; these include beliefs that RCT causes cancer (6.3%), cardiovascular disease or heart attacks (10.8%), or chronic illnesses (14.3%). Older participants, lower educational levels and prior RCT experience showed significant endorsement of specific misconceptions (p 0.05). Bivariate analyses revealed that several misconceptions were significantly associated with a greater preference for tooth extraction, specifically those related to systemic health. Patients who believed that root canal treatment (RCT) causes cancer, that RCT-treated teeth remain infected and that all root-canal-treated teeth should be extracted were more likely to prefer extraction than those who did not hold these beliefs (all p 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Endodontic myths were common among patients in Almadinah Almunawara. Misconceptions concerning systemic health effects, persistence of infection, and a perceived link between RCT and cancer were associated with a preference for tooth extraction over RCT. Age, educational level, and no previous RCT experience were associated with endorsement of specific misconceptions. Targeted public education and effective dentist-patient communication may help correct these misconceptions, improve acceptance of evidence-based endodontic care, and support preservation of natural dentition.

articles.title: Immune-related Plasma Proteins Associated with Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis Identified by Mendelian Randomization and Clinical Validation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify immune-related plasma proteins causally associated with susceptibility to recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) through two-sample Mendelian randomization, and to validate their biological and clinical relevance using integrative multi-omics analyses and clinical samples.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization was performed using protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) data for immune-related plasma proteins from the deCODE genetics database and genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for RAS to identify proteins with potential causal associations. Candidate proteins were further evaluated by Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and colocalization analyses. Single-cell transcriptomic data from oral mucosa were integrated to characterize the cellular expression patterns of the corresponding genes. Finally, plasma levels of the candidate proteins were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in 35 patients with RAS (sampled during both the ulcerative and healing phases) and 35 healthy controls to validate their clinical relevance.

RESULTS: A total of 28 immune-related plasma proteins were identified as having potential causal associations with RAS through two-sample Mendelian randomization. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these proteins were mainly involved in immune and inflammatory pathways, including natural killer (NK) cell-mediated cytotoxicity, Th1/Th2 cell differentiation, and the IL-17 signaling pathway. SMR and colocalization analyses highlighted IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA as key candidate genes, with IL17A showing the strongest genetic evidence. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed distinct cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in the oral mucosa. Clinical validation confirmed statistically significant alterations in the plasma levels of IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA across different stages of RAS.

CONCLUSIONS: This integrative study combining genetic analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and clinical validation identified IL17A, MMP1, and IL2RA as key immune-related molecules associated with RAS. Among them, IL17A showed the strongest genetic evidence and may serve as a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic target for RAS.

articles.title: Multimodal Left Ventricular Rehabilitation Enabling Double-Switch Repair in Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries, pulmonary artery banding (PAB) may prepare the morphologic left ventricle (LV) for systemic work before double-switch repair; however, development of ventricular dysfunction threatens candidacy.

CASE SUMMARY: 2-year-old boy with corrected transposition of the great arteries and Ebstein-like tricuspid valve malformation developed biventricular dysfunction after PAB tightening, atrial septal stenting, and single-site epicardial pacing for heart block. Biventricular resynchronization therapy, heart failure therapy, and PAB loosening restored ventricular function. Pressure-volume analysis demonstrated comparable ventricular contractility, preserved LV diastolic function, and loading tolerance before uncomplicated double-switch repair.

DISCUSSION: Multimodal rehabilitation and serial reassessment may preserve anatomic repair candidacy when reversible dysfunction complicates LV training.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Ventricular dysfunction during LV preparation warrants evaluation for reversible contributors, including pacing-associated dyssynchrony and excessive pressure loading, before abandonment of anatomic repair. Following multimodal rehabilitation, serial imaging and pressure-volume analysis can assess LV systolic recovery, diastolic reserve, and loading tolerance for systemic work.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Patterns Relative to Vasopressin Initiation and Subsequent Septic Shock Progression in Children: A Retrospective Cohort, 2020-2023.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the hemodynamic patterns associated with starting vasopressin in children with septic shock and to compare the early patterns based on subsequent progression of shock.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort (2020-2023) study.

SETTING: Single-center, tertiary PICU in Australia.

PATIENTS: Children younger than 18 years with septic shock.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hemodynamic variables collected at 1-minute intervals during a 1-hour observation period after starting vasopressin infusion were reviewed and collated according to whether shock subsequently progressed in the following 5 hours. In a cohort of 30 children (median age, 9 yr [interquartile range, 2-14 yr]), eight had shock progression, which was defined by echocardiography, lactate, and use of extracorporeal support. Cases with subsequent shock progression, as opposedto not, had an associated higher Phoenix score (7 [7-8] vs. 6 [5-6]; p = 0.01). The vasopressin starting dose in the shock vs. nonshock progression groups was 0.03 U/kg/hr (0.02-0.06 U/kg/hr) vs. 0.02 U/kg/hr (0.02-0.04 U/kg/hr; p = 0.72). We failed to find an association between ventricular dysfunction at baseline and the shock progression group vs. no shock progression (4/6 vs. 7/18; mean difference, 28%; 95% CI, -16% to 71%; p = 0.36). In the shock progression group, earlier pulse pressure continued on a decreasing trajectory following vasopressin initiation, despite increasing systolic and diastolic blood pressures. In those without shock progression, pulse pressure increased marginally. The difference between groups in the median pulse pressures during the observation period was 7.5 mm Hg.

CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating, retrospective study of children with septic shock treated with vasopressin, subsequent shock progression was associated with early decreasing pulse pressure. Further studies are needed to test whether early changes in pulse pressure after starting vasopressin can be used as a potential marker of subsequent shock progression.

articles.title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Opportunistic Screening of Left Ventricular Dysfunction Screening Using Chest Radiographs.
articles.abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate a deep learning model (DLLV) for identifying reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on chest radiographs (CXRs) and assess its potential as a prescreening tool for selective transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in health checkup populations. Materials and Methods Same-day CXR-TTE pairs obtained between January 2016 and September 2021 were retrospectively collected for model development. Counterfactual learning was applied to enhance model performance and interpretability. External testing included one tertiary referral center cohort and two health checkup cohorts. Discrimination was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and DLLV-based prescreening was evaluated by estimated TTE reduction and missed-case burden. Results The development dataset included 24,674 patients (32,135 CXR-TTE pairs); external cohorts included 5440, 28,034, and 6085 patients (53-62% male). DLLV achieved an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.88) for LVEF ≤ 40% in the tertiary referral cohort. In health checkup cohorts, AUCs were 0.92-0.97 for LVEF ≤ 40%, with AUPRCs of 0.04 in both cohorts, corresponding to 87-fold (95% CI: 16, 404) and 37-fold (95% CI: 3, 251) enrichment over baseline prevalence. Counterfactual reinforcement learning produced heatmaps with greater heart localization precision (P < .001 for all) and higher AUC for LVEF < 50% (P = .04). DLLV-based prescreening estimated TTE volume reductions up to 85% while identifying all 12 and 7 individuals with LVEF ≤ 40%. Conclusion DLLV identified reduced LVEF on CXRs across external test cohorts and showed potential as a prescreening tool for selective TTE in health checkup populations. ©RSNA, 2026.

articles.title: The Effect of Stevioside on Hepatic Steatosis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Stevioside is a widely used natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from Stevia rebaudiana; however, its effects on MASLD and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the effects and mechanisms of stevioside on MASLD, based on the high-fat diet-induced mice model and palmitic acid-treated hepatocyte model. We found that stevioside significantly alleviated hepatic steatosis in MASLD mice and reduced plasma ALT and AST levels and hepatic triglyceride and total cholesterol. In palmitic acid-induced hepatocytes, stevioside significantly reduced intracellular lipid droplet content and upregulated the protein levels of p-AMPK, PPARα, and EHHADH. Pharmacological inhibition of AMPK and PPARα revealed that stevioside regulated PPARα expression and downstream EHHADH expression in an AMPK-dependent manner. To conclude, stevioside significantly improved hepatic steatosis in MASLD by activating the AMPK/PPARα/EHHADH pathway, potentially generating novel evidence to help control the escalating disease burden of MASLD from the perspective of natural sweetener.

articles.title: PK/PD Modeling of a Novel Pleuromutilin Derivative Pleuro2-4 against Mycoplasma gallisepticum in Chicks.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum is a major causative agent of chronic respiratory disease in poultry, and effective antimicrobial therapy remains essential for disease control. In this study, the antimycoplasmal activity, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic efficacy, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of Pleuro2-4, a novel pleuromutilin candidate, were systematically evaluated against M. gallisepticum. Pleuro2-4 exhibited potent in vitro activity (MIC = 0.0078 μg/mL) and concentration-dependent killing. Following oral administration in chicks, Pleuro2-4 was rapidly converted to its active metabolite and displayed rapid absorption and sustained exposure in lung tissue. In an M. gallisepticum infection model, Pleuro2-4 alleviated respiratory lesions, reduced mycoplasmal loads, and suppressed inflammatory responses. PK/PD integration using an inhibitory sigmoid Emax model identified AUC0-24h/MIC as the PK/PD index for dose optimization. The bactericidal target was 3372.82 h, corresponding to a recommended oral dosage of 44.99 mg/kg once daily for three consecutive days. These findings support Pleuro2-4 as a promising candidate for avian mycoplasmosis treatment.

articles.title: Natural Polysaccharides in Health and Targeting TGF-β/Smad Signaling Therapy in Chronic Diseases.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases including cardiovascular disorders, cancers, diabetes and organ fibrosis are major global causes of mortality. The transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/suppressor of mothers against decapentaplegic (Smad) cascade governs key physiological events spanning cell proliferation, differentiation, immune homeostasis and extracellular matrix remodeling. Natural polysaccharides (NPs) are bioactive macromolecules widely distributed across diverse living organisms. This review summarizes the TGF-β/Smad pathway, addresses NPs structure-activity relationships, and dissects tissue-specific regulatory mechanisms. It highlights modulation of TGF-β/Smad signaling by NPs via gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic disturbances under chronic injury. Targeting TGF-β/Smad with NPs represents a promising therapeutic strategy for related chronic diseases. This review also discusses research bottlenecks and translational strategies, integrating gut microbiota-metabolite crosstalk across multiorgan pathologies to advance mechanistic insights into NPs-driven tissue homeostasis restoration and support NPs-based targeted therapy development.

articles.title: Magnoflorine Ameliorates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease by Targeting the NDUFV1 Subunit of Complex I to Regulate the ROS/AMPK Signaling Pathway.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent metabolic disorder with limited therapeutics. Magnoflorine (MAG), a natural alkaloid from edible plants, ameliorates MASLD; however, its direct targets remain unclear. Here, by integrating thermal proteome profiling and disease target databases, we identified NADH ubiquinone oxidoreductase core subunit V1 (NDUFV1), a core subunit of mitochondrial Complex I, as a key target of MAG. MAG directly binds NDUFV1, suppresses mitochondrial electron transport chain activity, and alleviates lipid-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. In high-fat cell models and MASLD mice, MAG contributes to the restoration of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, promoting fatty acid β-oxidation and inhibiting lipid biosynthesis to maintain lipid homeostasis. Notably, the lipid-lowering effects of MAG were significantly attenuated in NDUFV1-knockdown cells. This study reveals that MAG regulates lipid metabolism by targeting NDUFV1, highlighting its potential as a natural bioactive compound for MASLD.

articles.title: Implementing Mirror Therapy and Mental Imagery for Stroke Inpatient Rehabilitation: Adoption, Acceptability, and Feasibility.
articles.journal: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
articles.abstract: ImportanceMirror therapy and mental imagery (MTMI) are evidence-based interventions for upper extremity motor recovery after stroke, yet they remain underused in clinical practice. Implementation science offers a systematic approach in improving uptake in real-world settings.ObjectiveTo evaluate the changes in clinician acceptability, feasibility, adoption, and patient reach of MTMI over 12 months.DesignProspective, single-site implementation evaluation guided by implementation science frameworks.SettingA free-standing inpatient rehabilitation hospital.ParticipantsOccupational therapists (n = 16) and adult inpatients with stroke or similar neurological conditions.InterventionA therapist-led, 60 min MTMI group was delivered two to three times weekly. Six implementation barriers were identified. Implementation strategies: clinician education, training, support, and infrastructure changes.Outcomes and MeasuresTherapist acceptability and feasibility were measured using the Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM) and Feasibility of Intervention Measure (FIM) at baseline, 4 months, and 12 months. Therapist adoption was assessed through training records and self-report. Patient reach was derived from attendance-tracking and hospital-admission data.ResultsAIM and FIM scores remained high across all time points (AIM 4.4-4.8; FIM 4.6-4.8). Adoption increased over time: therapists trained to lead MTMI rose from 11% to 61%, and self-reported MTMI use increased from 63% to 92%. The mean monthly patient reach was 39%.Conclusions and RelevanceMultimodal implementation strategies supported high acceptability, feasibility, and clinician adoption of MTMI in inpatient rehabilitation. Patient reach remained modest.What This Article AddsThis study provides practical, context-specific guidance for integrating MTMI into inpatient rehabilitation.

articles.title: Scientific Output in Septic Shock According to Country Income and Gender: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess trends in septic shock publications by country income and author gender.

DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for articles indexed with "septic shock" between January 2014 and December 2024.

STUDY SELECTION: All peer-reviewed publication types were eligible. Conference abstracts and non-peer-reviewed material were excluded.

DATA EXTRACTION: Bibliographic data, first and last author affiliations, country income level (World Bank classification: low- and middle-income countries [LMICs] and high-income countries [HICs]), and journal prestige (SCImago Journal Rank [SJR]) were extracted. Author gender was inferred using the NamSor application programming interface (API).

DATA SYNTHESIS: Of 10,352 eligible publications, LMIC-affiliated first authors increased over time (+2.13% per year; 95% CI, +1.66 to +2.61; p < 0.001) from 18% in 2014 to 37% in 2024. Women represented 35.6% of first authors and 25.0% of last authors (with around 20% of authors not classifiable by the NamSor API), with higher proportions in LMICs than HICs (p < 0.001) for both first authors (44.5% vs. 32.5%) and last authors (35.2% vs. 21.5%). Gender concordance was more frequent, with female first authors more often paired with female last authors than male first authors (31.7% vs. 21.1%). Cross-income collaborations, especially involving LMIC last authors, remained rare. Articles led by men in HICs were more often published in higher-SJR journals compared with those led by women (p < 0.001), whereas no gender differences were observed among LMIC-affiliated authors.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite encouraging growth in LMIC contributions and female representation, major inequities persist. Strengthening equitable collaborations and supporting underrepresented groups would broaden participation and enhance the global applicability in critical care research.

articles.title: Cluster Versus Individual Randomization in Prehospital, Emergency and Critical Care Trials: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings.

DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase.

DATA SELECTION: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Using absolute ln(odds ratio [OR]) for mortality and absolute Hedges' g for the secondary outcome, mean differences (MDs) in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs were analyzed using mixed regression models, presented with 95% CIs. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT). We included 65 meta-analyses in quantitative analyses, encompassing 212 randomized clinical trials (39 cRCTs and 173 iRCTs) and 315,276 patients. No statistically significant difference in absolute ln(OR) for mortality between cRCTs and iRCTs was found (MD, -0.110; 95% CI, -0.093 to 0.313). For length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, a significant difference in absolute Hedges' g was found (MD, -0.202; 95% CI, -0.392 to -0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.

articles.title: Furosemide Stress Test in Adults and Children With Acute Kidney Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic utility of the furosemide stress test (FST) for acute kidney injury (AKI) management in critically ill adults and children.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 3, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Studies evaluating the standardized FST protocol in critically ill adults or children with AKI were eligible. Outcomes included AKI stage 3 progression (Q1), kidney replacement therapy (KRT) initiation (Q2), short-term mortality (Q3), successful KRT liberation (Q4), and FST-guided vs. standard KRT initiation in randomized trials (Q5).

DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 and Risk of Bias 2. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Twenty studies (n = 1979; 11 countries; 2013-2025) were included. For AKI progression (nine studies; n = 501), pooled sensitivity was 0.69 and specificity was 0.88 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.89; GRADE: low). For KRT initiation (nine studies; n = 952), sensitivity was 0.81 and specificity was 0.75 (AUC, 0.79; GRADE: very low). For mortality (six studies; n = 487), sensitivity was 0.56 and specificity was 0.76 (AUC, 0.75; GRADE: very low). For KRT liberation (three studies; n = 177), sensitivity was 0.81 and specificity was 0.87 (AUC, 0.89; GRADE: low for sensitivity, very low for specificity). The effect of FST-guided early KRT initiation on short-term mortality was uncertain (pooled risk ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.79-1.27; two randomized controlled trials, n = 212; GRADE: very low). Pediatric analyses yielded AUC values of 0.81 and 0.63 for KRT initiation and mortality, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Based on low to very low certainty evidence, the FST may support risk stratification for AKI progression and KRT liberation in critically ill adults. Its impact on mortality when guiding early KRT initiation remains uncertain. As a low-cost bedside test, the FST can be a useful tool in resource-limited settings where novel biomarkers are inaccessible.

articles.title: A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
articles.abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

articles.title: Use of a central venous catheter as vascular access at the start of a regular hemodialysis program: impact on mortality over 2 years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The recommended access for starting chronic hemodialysis (HD) is an arteriovenous fistula (AVF), but a (CVC) continues to be frequently used. Worldwide, its use has been associated with higher mortality, but data from Brazil are lacking.

METHODS: Analytical, observational, and retrospective cohort study that aimed at analyzing the data available in the Brazilian Monthly Dialysis Registry database from Jan/2011 to Dec/2023. Using data from this registry, we evaluated the frequency of CVC use (regardless of whether tunneled or non-tunneled) at the start of HD across 13 years and assessed its impact on all-cause mortality over 2 years.

RESULTS: We studied 10,182 patients. The mean age was 59 (47-69) years; 59% were male, and 33% had diabetes. CVC use at HD entry increased substantially in the last 10 years. The 2-year mortality rates for CVC and primary AVF/graft users were 20% and 9%, respectively, P < 0.001. In the fully adjusted multivariate model, the use of CVC persisted significantly associated with mortality (HR 1.69, 95%CI 1.23-2.25, P=0.001). Other variables directly associated with mortality were age (HR 1.04, 95%CI 1.03-1.05, P=0.001), and serum ferritin (HR 1.18, 95%CI 1.06-1.30, P=0.002). Serum albumin (HR 0.86, 95%CI 0.84-0.88, P<0.001) and URR (HR 0.97, 95%CI 0.96-0.97, P<0.001) emerged as protective factors.

CONCLUSIONS: CVC use was associated with a 1.69-fold increased risk of 2-year mortality. The increasing use of CVCs in Brazil is concerning and highlights the need for public health strategies promoting timely permanent vascular access before HD initiation.

articles.title: The Effect of Nasal Corticosteroids and Antihistamines on Asthma Control in Patients with Asthma and Comorbid Allergic Rhinitis: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether treating allergic rhinitis (AR) with intranasal corticosteroids (INCS) or antihistamines improves asthma outcomes in adults with confirmed AR-asthma comorbidity.Data Sources: A systematic search of PubMed, MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted from the inception of the databases to May 2025. In addition, a supplementary hand search of the reference lists of included studies was conducted.Study Selections: Ten trials met the inclusion criteria (n = 12,924 participants; duration: 2-24 weeks). Seven studies contributed to the meta-analysis of asthma symptom scores, while other outcomes were narratively synthesized owing to incomplete or heterogeneous reporting.

RESULTS: Both interventions were associated with statistically significant improvement in asthma symptom control. The pooled effect favoured both treatment arms (standardized mean difference (SMD) = -0.55; 95% CI: - 0.67 to - 0.43), with subgroup analysis showing a consistent benefit from antihistamines (SMD = - 0.51) and a numerically larger, though nonsignificantly different, effect for INCS (SMD = - 0.87). However, no included trial compared INCS with antihistamines directly, so this comparison remains indirect. Evidence was limited for lung function, rescue medication use, bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and exacerbations, and most trials lacked data that could be extracted. Certainty level (GRADE) shows moderate for symptom outcomes and low to very low for all other domains.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive treatment of AR with antihistamines or INCS, shows a clinically relevant improvement in asthma symptom control among adults with asthma. However, the evidence base is constrained by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and suboptimal reporting. More Powered clinical trials using standardized asthma metrics are needed to clarify the long-term benefit and cost-effectiveness.
