articles.title: Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
authors: and the Cooperative Antimicrobial Therapy of Septic Shock (CATSS) Database Research Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the effect of delays in initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy from the initial onset of persistent hypotension to the outcome of Candida septic shock.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: A total of 32 academic and community hospitals in Canada, the United States, and Saudi Arabia (July 1989 to June 2018).

PATIENTS: A total of 850 adult patients with culture-positive Candida septic shock.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. A strong relationship was observed between the delay in initiation of pathogen-appropriate antifungal (PAA) therapy and hospital survival. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. In a multivariate analysis, which included the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and epidemiologic/therapeutic variables, the time to initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy emerged as the single strongest predictor of outcome. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that the adverse effects of delayed antifungal treatment were consistent across various subgroups, including different types of infections, pathogens, and antifungal drug classes. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset.

CONCLUSIONS: Administration of PAAs within the first hours of documented hypotension significantly improved hospital survival. Less than 20% of patients received appropriate antifungals within 6 hours of documented hypotension.

articles.title: Rethinking Oliguria in the ICU: From Threshold to Trajectory.
Music Therapy During Weaning From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study examined the effect of daily music therapy on weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in the ICU, with a primary focus on weaning duration. Secondary agitation, sedation, and analgesia doses, pain, delirium, and perceived stress after 90 days were assessed. Additionally, total IMV and ICU stay durations and tracheostomy rates were studied. Physiologic parameters were assessed in the music therapy group (MG). The study also aimed to promote the humanization of critical care through a biopsychosocial and creative music therapy approach.

DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally.

SETTING AND PATIENTS: Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours.

INTERVENTIONS: MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Music therapy may serve as a nonpharmacological complementary adjunct during weaning by reducing agitation, sedation, and tracheostomy rate. It may potentially decrease perceived stress and IMV and ICU stay durations. Further research is warranted.

articles.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

METHODS: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.

RESULTS: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

articles.title: A New Web-Based Word-Picture Matching Test Reveals Psycholinguistic Effects on Word-Level Reading and Auditory Comprehension in Aphasia.
articles.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Word reading comprehension deficits, often measured by word-to-picture matching (WtPM) tasks, are common in aphasia and alexia. To specify the nature of comprehension deficits, WtPM tasks should manipulate psycholinguistic features, have matched written and auditory versions, and provide normed scores measuring speed and accuracy. Here we present a novel web-based WtPM task that meets those needs. We use it to assess word comprehension deficits in left-hemisphere stroke survivors (LHSS).

METHOD: We examined scores for the novel auditory and written WtPM task in a normative sample (n = 62) and an LHSS sample (n = 63). Mixed-effects models examined accuracy and response time in both groups, and an analysis of variance compared efficiency between the groups. Correlations compared written WtPM performance and item difficulty to auditory WtPM, written lexical decision, and oral reading. A k-means clustering analysis examined deficit patterns in the LHSS group.

RESULTS: WtPM performance was modulated by modality, frequency, and regularity and was impaired in the LHSS group. Written WtPM performance and item difficulty were correlated with auditory WtPM and written lexical decision in both groups and with oral reading in the LHSS group. Over half of the LHSS sample had frank deficits on at least one WtPM task. Comprehension deficits in individual LHSS were often modulated by input modality, word frequency, and regularity.

CONCLUSIONS: We present a clinically accessible WtPM task that captures individual patterns of word comprehension impairment in both written and auditory modalities. The use of efficiency scores allows for the assessment of mild impairments that are missed by ceiling effects on currently available tasks. Input modality, frequency, and regularity affect word comprehension as measured by WtPM. Individual stroke survivors present with different combinations of these effects, which may help to identify specific deficits and spared abilities that can guide reading comprehension treatment.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33968839.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics, Lesion Distribution, and Systemic Comorbidities in Patients With Oral Lichen Planus.
articles.journal: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This cross-sectional study aimed to comprehensively evaluate clinical forms, anatomical location, symptoms, systemic comorbidities, and potentially relevant factors in patients with oral lichen planus (OLP).

METHODS: Seventy-two patients with histopathologically confirmed OLP were included. Awareness of the disease, clinical forms, lesion location, and symptoms and their relationships were investigated. Smoking and alcohol consumption, and the presence of adjacent prosthetic or restorative materials were evaluated as potentially relevant factors. The prevalence of systemic diseases was assessed.

RESULTS: The reticular form was the most frequent clinical presentation, followed by plaque-like and erosive forms. Lesions were most commonly localized on the buccal mucosa, followed by the tongue and the gingiva. The reticular form was most frequently observed on the buccal mucosa and tongue (p = 0.001). The combination of the reticular and erosive forms was most frequently observed on the buccal mucosa (p = 0.001), whereas the combination of the reticular and plaque-like forms was more commonly observed on the buccal mucosa and tongue. The erosive form was associated with more prominent symptoms (p = 0.003, p = 0.001). The most frequent systemic comorbidities were hypertension, diabetes, and hypothyroidism. No significant differences were observed in systemic diseases, symptoms, or relevant factors between sexes.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical forms of OLP may coexist within the same patient and, in some cases, within the same lesion. The most common combination was the coexistence of the reticular form with plaque-like or erosive forms. The erosive form is symptomatic. Systemic comorbidities were also commonly observed among patients with OLP, warranting attention during clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Acute Perinatal Stroke Characteristics and Outcome in Southern Finland.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Perinatal stroke can cause lifelong morbidities. Outcome prediction is important for parental guidance and follow-up. We studied characteristics of acute perinatal stroke in a Finnish cohort.

METHODS: We performed a population-based study, identifying infants with acute neonatal cerebral ischemia or sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) in Southern Finland from 2010 to 2023. We analysed the incidence of stroke types, seizures, anti-seizure medication use, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Altogether 88 infants (1 in 3101 live births) were diagnosed with acute perinatal stroke: 67% with arterial ischemic stroke (AIS), 22% with hemorrhagic stroke (HS) and 11% with CSVT. Seizures and anti-seizure medication use occurred in 78% of infants. Cranial ultrasound infrequently recognized AIS but usually noted haemorrhage. During follow-up, 34% of infants had no adverse outcome diagnosis. The most common outcome was cerebral palsy (CP, 35%). A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types.

CONCLUSION: The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

articles.title: Travel-associated Staphylococcus aureus infections: a global perspective from the GeoSentinel Surveillance Network.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, and Staphylococcus aureus is among the leading contributors to the global AMR-attributable disease burden. Data on the clinical presentation and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Staphylococcus aureus infections in returning travellers remain scarce.

METHODS: We described the clinical presentation, travel characteristics, and antimicrobial susceptibility of travellers and migrants diagnosed with Staphylococcus aureus infection through the GeoSentinel network between January 2014 and December 2022. Because no consensus definition exists for travel-associated infections, we included all cases recorded in the GeoSentinel database as travel-associated. We evaluated patients during travel or after return. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) was performed according to routine laboratory practice at participating sites.

RESULTS: We retrieved 740 travellers and migrants with Staphylococcus aureus infection diagnosed at 50 GeoSentinel sites. Four hundred thirty-eight (59.2%) were male, and the median age was 32 years (IQR 23-48). The most frequently visited regions were Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, and South-Central Asia. Most patients presented after travel (576/740; 77.8%). Skin and soft tissue infections were the predominant diagnosis (670/740; 90.5%), and most patients were managed as outpatients (579/740; 78.2%). Overall, 406/740 (54.9%) isolates showed resistance or reduced susceptibility to at least one antimicrobial class, including methicillin (224/656; 34.1%), lincosamides (144/627; 23.0%), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (129/597; 21.6%). Demographic characteristics and hospitalization frequency were similar between patients with MSSA and MRSA infections.

CONCLUSIONS: Most Staphylococcus aureus infections in international travellers presented as skin and soft tissue infections and were managed in outpatient settings. Resistance or reduced susceptibility to at least one antimicrobial class was common, with one-third of isolates identified as methicillin-resistant. These findings support the importance of AST to guide management of skin and soft tissue infections in internationally mobile populations and reinforce the need for standardized definitions of travel-associated bacterial infections and continued global surveillance.

articles.title: Integrative computational simulations uncover the conformational activation pathway of AKT1 kinase.
articles.abstract: The AKT1 kinase, a central node in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling axis, governs critical cellular processes, including survival and proliferation, and its dysregulation drives cancer, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. While structural studies have resolved static snapshots of AKT1's inactive and active states, the dynamic mechanisms orchestrating its activation, particularly the coupling of phosphorylation-induced signals to catalytic competency, remain poorly resolved. This knowledge gap hinders the development of targeted therapies addressing AKT1's pathological hyperactivation. Using integrative computational approaches, we characterize the hierarchical conformational transitions enabling AKT1 activation at atomic resolution. Microsecond-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and nudged elastic band (NEB) pathway analyses reveal that phosphorylation at T308 initiates a metastable "pre-active" state, destabilizing autoinhibitory interactions at the PH-kinase interface. This triggers potential structural rearrangements: (1) A-loop opening exposes the hydrophobic motif for regulatory phosphorylation, (2) αC-helix rotation establishes the Lys179-Glu198 catalytic salt bridge, and (3) DFG motif flipping enables Asp292-Mg2+ coordination, completing the active site assembly. By mapping the energy landscape of AKT1 activation, this work bridges static structural data with dynamic mechanistic insights, offering a framework for therapeutic intervention against AKT1-driven pathologies.

articles.title: Where to Begin? Prioritizing Procedures for Surgical Skills Training Development: SELF Series Article 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The shortage of practitioners trained to provide essential surgical care remains among the most stubborn contributors to the global burden of disease. Scaling the global surgical care workforce through independent procedural skills training is essential to address unmet surgical needs, particularly in resource constrained settings. This is a dauntingly large task; prioritization of a sub-set of surgical skills is required in order to make an impactful start. During the 2023 Surgical Education Learners Forum (SELF) Symposium, participants developed criteria to prioritize the development of self-directed and simulation-based training modules to address the most urgent needs in surgery, critical care, and perioperative care. This is the second article in the SELF series.

METHODS: The SELF community of practice members from diverse geographies convened at the SELF Symposium to gain a common understanding of the environments where SELF training modules are deployed and articulate how to prioritize the development of those materials. Participants voted to prioritize 262 procedures by impact and then effectiveness, "deployability", and outcome variability.

RESULTS: Fifty seven procedures were identified as high-priority for surgical skills development. Of these, 20 were trauma and critical care procedures, 21 were general surgical procedures, 11 were pediatric surgical procedures, and 5 were obstetrics, gynecology, and family planning procedures.

CONCLUSIONS: When faced with the dauntingly large need for surgical, critical care and perioperative procedural skills training, prioritizing the identified areas will guide training development efforts toward the greatest impacts.

articles.title: Scaling SELF Simulation Training: SELF Series Article 5.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The shortage of practitioners trained to provide essential surgical care remains among the most stubborn contributors to the global burden of disease, particularly in resource-constrained settings where expert trainers are scarce. The Surgical Education Learners Forum (SELF) is a global community of practice developing cost-effective, scalable, open-access training modules that let clinicians anywhere learn, practice, and evaluate procedural skills independently. This fifth and final article in the SELF series reports expert opinion from the 2023 SELF Symposium on a pathway to scale, addressing evidence generation, digital delivery platforms, and the barriers and actions needed to achieve widespread adoption.

METHODS: An interprofessional group of surgeons, trauma and critical care practitioners, academics, educators, technologists, and learner representatives participated in three facilitated working sessions on evidence generation and reporting, platforms, and a theory of change. Each session used structured small-group discussions guided by common prompts, thematic clustering of responses on shared working walls, and individual voting to prioritize recommendations. Responses were subsequently consolidated, re-sorted by theme, and returned to participants to verify accuracy.

RESULTS: In the evidence generation session, participants prioritized setting SELF standards and definitions-chiefly defining study types and the level of evidence required for each. For platforms, credibility and transparency, findability, and accessibility emerged as the dominant learner and developer concerns, with minimizing bandwidth and enabling offline use of the top-ranked best practice; the leading calls to action were to construct a supporting community of practice and convene a standards group. In the theory of change session, participants ranked individual factors highest, with engaging influential champions and senior gatekeepers who drive organizational decisions receiving the most votes overall, followed by language and communication, organizational, and economic and legal factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, these sessions chart a practical way forward for low-cost, open-access, self-assessed procedural skills simulation, emphasizing rigorous evaluation, credible and accessible delivery platforms, and coordinated engagement with key stakeholders. High-quality training materials must be matched by equally rigorous studies evaluating them, and by sustained, methodical efforts to overcome barriers to acceptance.

articles.title: A Bridge to Comfort: Nurses Driving Early Palliative Consults in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: Journal of hospice and palliative nursing : JHPN : the official journal of the Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association
articles.abstract: This project established a protocol that enabled all intensive care unit (ICU) patients to receive a palliative care (PC) screening. Those who met criteria received timely access to PC in the ICU setting. Delayed access to PC can result in untreated symptoms, lack of understanding of care preferences, unwanted invasive procedures, and underutilization of hospice care. A Plan-Do-Study-Act framework was utilized to establish this protocol. The multidisciplinary team sought to increase PC consults in the ICU by 30% using a nurse-driven standardized screening tool. The PC Referral Criteria established by the Center to Advance Palliative Care were used as a framework to establish the workflow/protocol. The outcome measures were the number of patients screened for PC on admission to the ICU, the number of PCs placed in the ICU, the number of code blues, and ICU staff satisfaction. PC consults increased by 163% (471) in 2024 and 143% (435) in 2025 as compared with 2023 (179). In 2023, there were 33 code blues in the ICU, and these decreased by 21% (26) in 2024 and 12% (29) in 2025. ICU staff (87%) felt that the PC screening process had a positive impact on staff and their practice.

articles.title: Myron McCall Nichols: a Connecticut Yankee in a Southern court.
articles.abstract: Myron McCall Nichols (1921-2013) was born in Bridgeport, Connecticut, was raised and educated in the Northeast, and by sheer chance of a military experience found his way to one of the premier pediatric programs developing in the country at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) under the leadership of Charles W. Daeschner (1920-2009). Dr. Nichols, affectionately known as Dr. Nick, was a scholar, musician, athlete, and showman always on stage to make a point to students, residents, and faculty colleagues or to generate a laugh from his poetry and musical antics. A self-taught neonatologist before there was such a board-certified designation, he developed what there was of an intensive care nursery at UTMB and offered observations through his scholarship on the burgeoning literature of the care of the neonate. This essay details how a Connecticut Yankee found himself deposited in the presence of a very Southern group of colleagues and his sure-footed adaptation to his surroundings.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 variant-dependent alterations in nasopharyngeal microbiota and host inflammatory response.
articles.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic saw multiple outbreaks occur over short periods. This was linked to the virus's high infectivity and rapid mutation rate, which hindered the development of effective treatments and a comprehensive understanding of COVID-19 pathophysiology. The nasopharyngeal tract, the main entry site of SARS-CoV-2, interacts with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors via the viral spike glycoprotein, triggering pro-inflammatory responses that affect both tissue integrity and the resident microbiota. Viral infection induces dysbiosis by modulating microbiome diversity. Although distinct variants produce independent symptoms and viral loads, their impact on the nasopharyngeal microbiota and host inflammatory profile remains poorly understood. To address this, we analyzed nasopharyngeal samples from Chilean individuals collected during different phases of the pandemic. The microbiota was characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region), and cytokine expression was quantified by RT-qPCR. Finally, applied rigorous data processing and machine-learning models, Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors, to identify associations between SARS-CoV-2 variants, inflammatory markers, and opportunistic bacterial genera. Our results reveal that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with distinct immunomicrobial signatures marked by increased TNF-α expression and the expansion of opportunistic taxa. These variant-dependent alterations indicate that host inflammatory responses and microbial dysbiosis are closely intertwined in the nasopharyngeal environment. This study provides a comprehensive framework integrating microbial and host factors to better understand the mechanisms underlying COVID-19 pathogenesis and highlights the potential of combining microbiome and cytokine profiling with machine-learning approaches to differentiate infection outcomes across viral variants.IMPORTANCEUnderstanding how SARS-CoV-2 infection alters the upper respiratory microbiota and host immune responses is essential to uncover the mechanisms underlying COVID-19 severity. In this study, we integrate bacterial 16S rRNA sequencing, inflammatory markers, and machine learning to identify key descriptors of infection such as TNF-α, Acinetobacter, Prevotella, and Staphylococcus. These markers define a conserved immunomicrobial signature across viral variants, linking inflammatory activation with microbial dysbiosis in the nasopharyngeal environment. Our findings highlight the value of the correct and robust application of machine learning models and nested cross-validation strategies in high-dimensional (wide) data sets to improve variant discrimination, reveal host-microbe interactions, and support the development of therapeutic strategies for respiratory viral infections.

articles.title: Impact of different clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Macrolides remained cornerstone of Mycobacterium abscessus treatment, but emerging resistance patterns compromised therapeutic efficacies. Clarithromycin resistance can manifest as either mutational or inducible, while the clinical impacts of different resistance mechanisms in M. abscessus pulmonary disease (MAB-PD) had been poorly characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study from 2011 to 2023 across four tertiary centers in Taiwan. Adults with clarithromycin-resistant MAB-PD were included and stratified by resistance type: mutational vs inducible. Outcomes included all-cause 3-year mortality, microbiological clearance, and radiographic progression. Among 108 enrolled patients, 16 (14.7%) had mutational resistance and the remaining 92 had inducible type. Isolates comprised 103 M. abscessus, three M. massiliense, and two M. bolletii. Mutational resistance was associated with significantly higher 3-year mortality (18.8% vs 4.3%, P = 0.03) and lower acid-fast smear conversion rates in treated patients (18.2% vs 67.6%, P = 0.004). Multivariable analysis identified mutational clarithromycin resistance as an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 5.21, 95% confidence interval 1.10-24.6, P = 0.04). Strains with mutational resistance demonstrated higher median minimal inhibitory concentrations to linezolid (24 vs 16 mg/L), cefoxitin (64 vs 32 mg/L), and amikacin (16 vs 8 mg/L). Mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD is associated with substantially worse clinical outcomes compared to inducible resistance, including higher mortality and poorer treatment responses. These findings suggested that more intensive treatment strategies might be needed for mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD.

IMPORTANCE: Macrolide resistance critically undermines treatment outcomes in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease, yet the prognostic impact of distinct resistance mechanisms has remained unclear. This multicenter study demonstrates that mutational clarithromycin resistance, although less common than inducible resistance, is associated with markedly higher mortality, poorer microbiological response, and broader multidrug resistance. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence that not all macrolide resistance is equivalent. Recognizing mutational resistance as a high-risk phenotype has important implications for risk stratification, prognostication, and treatment intensification, supporting a more personalized approach to managing MAB-LD in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Digital dietitians? Assessing ChatGPT's role in transforming nutrition care and dietetic practice: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly being integrated into nutrition care and dietary counseling. Evaluating their usefulness, accuracy, and limitations is essential before widespread clinical adoption.AimTo systematically review the evidence on the performance of ChatGPT and related AI tools in nutrition and dietetics, including comparisons with other AI models and human experts.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and included studies published until February 2025. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar using keywords related to ChatGPT, AI, nutrition, and diet. Of 5504 retrieved records, 31 studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were synthesized under three domains: ChatGPT's performance in nutritional guidance, comparisons with other AI tools, and comparisons with human experts.SummaryMost included studies were cross-sectional and published in 2024, with ChatGPT-3.5 and 4.0 being the most evaluated models. ChatGPT showed high-accuracy in clinical guideline adherence for conditions such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes, moderate performance in dietetics examination simulations, and variable accuracy in disease-specific diet planning. It performed well in nutrition education, dietary recall, and food recognition, but demonstrated limitations in micronutrient estimation, renal nutrition safety, and reproducibility. Compared with other AI tools, ChatGPT showed stronger clinical reasoning but lower performance in specialized food-classification tasks. Compared with human experts, it matched performance in general nutrition knowledge but lacked cultural competence and emotional intelligence. AI tools may complement nutrition care, but human dietitians remain essential for personalized care.

articles.title: SUVmax of incidental colorectal polyps on PET/cT and its association with histopathological features and dysplasia grade.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective single-center study examined whether PET/CT-derived SUVmax is associated with histopathological subtype and dysplasia grade in incidental colorectal polyps, and whether it can predict advanced colorectal neoplasia. The cohort included patients imaged for non-gastrointestinal indications, suspected colorectal malignancy, or prior colorectal cancer. "Incidental" denotes focal uptake anatomically distinct from the primary or suspected pathology.

METHODS: Patients who underwent FDG PET/CT and colonoscopy (within three months) at Akdeniz University Hospital between 2015 and 2020 were screened. In total, 126 patients with focal colorectal uptake and histopathologically confirmed polyps were included; nine (7.1%) had adenocarcinoma at the FDG-avid site. SUVmax was measured using a 3D region of interest. Pathology followed the 2019 WHO classification. Advanced neoplasia was defined as adenocarcinoma or advanced adenoma (≥10 mm, villous/tubulovillous histology, or high-grade dysplasia).

RESULTS: Median SUVmax was 11.0 (IQR 7.9-17.2) and was higher in advanced than non-advanced neoplasia (13.00 vs. 8.05; p < 0.001). SUVmax correlated with lesion size (ρ = 0.407; p < 0.001) and was higher in villous/tubulovillous adenomas (p = 0.004) and high-grade dysplasia (p = 0.002). After adjustment for age, sex, and localization, SUVmax was associated with advanced neoplasia (OR 1.217 per unit; 95% CI 1.090-1.359; p < 0.001), but not after adding lesion size (OR 0.936; p = 0.141), which remained strongly associated (OR 9.811 per cm; p = 0.003). An SUVmax cutoff ≥12.3 was associated with advanced neoplasia (OR 9.329; 95% CI 3.040-28.632; p < 0.001). Additional PET-negative lesions (36 patients, 28.6%) were smaller (p < 0.001) and less often high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma (20.0% vs. 54.3%; p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: SUVmax reflects histopathological severity in incidental colorectal polyps, but its association with advanced neoplasia was not independent of lesion size. The 12.3 cutoff is exploratory and requires prospective multicenter validation. FDG negativity does not exclude significant pathology; three adenocarcinomas occurred among PET-negative lesions.

articles.title: Characterization of a recombinant gC-deleted PRV-XJ variant reveals altered disease outcomes following different inoculation routes in mice.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pseudorabies virus (PRV) variants continue to threaten swine production and can cause severe neurological disease in non-natural hosts. Although glycoprotein C (gC) contributes to PRV attachment to host cells, its role in the pathogenic characteristics of currently circulating PRV variants remains unclear, particularly under different inoculation routes. In this study, we generated a marker-free gC-deleted recombinant virus, rPRV-XJ-ΔgC, based on the genotype II PRV-XJ variant and compared its pathogenic characteristics with those of parental PRV-XJ in C57BL/6 mice. rPRV-XJ-ΔgC retained the ability to cause lethal infection but, compared with PRV-XJ, showed delayed disease progression, reduced early central nervous system (CNS) viral accumulation, and milder neurological and neuropathological changes, particularly following intranasal inoculation. These differences were less evident after intramuscular inoculation. Intranasal infection with rPRV-XJ-ΔgC was also associated with attenuated disruption of the blood-brain barrier, consistent with reduced CNS injury. Collectively, these findings indicate that gC deletion in the PRV-XJ background is associated with altered infection kinetics and route-dependent CNS disease phenotypes.

IMPORTANCE: Pseudorabies virus (PRV) variants remain important pathogens associated with neurological disease, but the contribution of individual viral genes to the pathogenic characteristics of circulating PRV variants remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of glycoprotein C (gC) in the pathogenic phenotype of the genotype II PRV-XJ variant. gC deletion resulted in route-dependent changes in PRV-XJ-induced disease outcomes, with more evident effects following intranasal than intramuscular inoculation. These findings highlight the importance of viral genetic factors and infection routes in shaping PRV-associated disease phenotypes and provide further insight into PRV neuropathogenesis.

articles.title: Exploratory associations of gut microbiota composition with HBeAg and HBsAg status in nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B.
articles.abstract: HBeAg and HBsAg reflect viral replication and host immune status and are important determinants of treatment responsiveness in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The gut microbiota, a key component of the gut-liver axis, may influence immune regulation and antiviral outcomes. This study characterized gut microbiota profiles across different HBeAg and HBsAg statuses in CHB patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. Fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 29 healthy controls (HC) and 101 NA-treated CHB patients without cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, including 30 HBeAg-positive (EP) and 71 HBeAg-negative (EN) individuals. The EN group was further stratified by serum HBsAg levels into an advantageous subgroup (<1,500 IU/mL, n = 57) and a non-advantageous subgroup (≥1,500 IU/mL, n = 14). Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly among EP, EN, and HC groups. Species-level analyses identified nominal group-related differences in several Bacteroidales- and Firmicutes-associated anaerobic commensals, including Bacteroides uniformis, Blautia obeum, Eubacterium ventriosum, Anaerobutyricum, and Parabacteroides timonensis; however, none remained significant after global FDR correction across all detected species. Within the EN group, selected taxa showed directionally consistent associations with HBsAg strata in downsampling, leave-one-out, and CLR-based sensitivity analyses, but these subgroup findings also did not remain significant after FDR correction. NA-treated CHB was associated with exploratory taxonomic differences without detectable loss of microbial diversity. The observed associations with HBeAg status and HBsAg burden were hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger longitudinal cohorts incorporating absolute microbial quantification, targeted metabolomics, host immune profiling, and more complete dietary, anthropometric, and other relevant clinical covariates.

articles.title: Exploring antimicrobial resistance in wild and domestic animal populations: combining publicly available data with BV-BRC resources to introduce bioinformatics in an undergraduate classroom.
articles.abstract: Bioinformatics blends the fields of biology, statistics, computer science, and information technology for the processing and analysis of genomic data. Despite the growing demand for trained bioinformaticians and a positive job market outlook, most undergraduate institutions struggle to integrate bioinformatics into their life science curricula. Educators face numerous barriers to incorporating bioinformatics into their classes, including technical issues and expertise. To address this need, we are developing web-accessible, course-based materials for general microbiology, infectious disease, genomics, and other similar undergraduate and graduate classes that use bioinformatic workflows within the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC), one of three National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)-funded Bioinformatics Resource Centers. Here, we present one such activity: a three-part exercise focused on antimicrobial resistance and metagenomics that uses six publicly available metagenomic samples collected from wild and domestic animal populations to explore the distinctions between their gut microbiomes and their respective antibiotic resistance genes. To analyze community composition and identify antibiotic resistance genes, students use two end-to-end services offered by the BV-BRC: Taxonomic Classification and Metagenomic Read Mapping. This assignment was developed to introduce students to core competencies in the field of bioinformatics and to highlight the BV-BRC as an educational resource for integrating bioinformatics without requiring students and instructors to possess the technical proficiencies and computing resources traditionally needed. We successfully implemented this exercise in an upper-level undergraduate microbiology course, demonstrating the feasibility of using the BV-BRC for bioinformatics education in the classroom.

articles.title: Characterization of norovirus GI.3 and GII.12 variants detected in wastewater: proof-of-concept for integrating phenotypic insights in wastewater-based epidemiology.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, responsible for 685 million cases and 200,000 deaths annually. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) enables not only global surveillance of dominant strains but also the detection of cryptic and emerging viral variants. An important question, however, is how to link genomic diversity to clinical impact and phenotypic traits of the strains detected in wastewater. In the Global Urban Wastewater Project, phylogenetically distinct norovirus GI.3 and GII.12 lineages were detected in wastewater from Cameroon. In this study, we characterized their host- and tissue-binding specificity and antigenic makeup in comparison with other GI.3 and GII.12 lineages using a luciferase immunoprecipitation system-based assay, alongside sequence analysis of the VP1 P2 subdomain. We observed intra-genotype variation among GI.3 variants. GI.3 Cameroon/2017 shared phenotypes with its closest reference strain (GI.3 Mexico/2016), and their histo-blood group antigen (HBGA)-binding profiles suggested a narrower susceptible population compared to other GI.3 lineages. Conversely, GII.12 strains showed no significant differences in HBGA binding, antigenic profiles, and tissue attachment. Together, these results reveal distinct patterns of phenotypic diversity between the two genotypes. While GI.3 variants exhibited lineage-specific traits, the GII.12 strains appeared phenotypically conserved across lineages. These findings highlight the feasibility and importance of integrating phenotypic analysis with WBE to assess potential public health risks posed by novel viral variants.

IMPORTANCE: While detection of norovirus through case-based surveillance is limited to variants causing symptomatic infection, wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) allows for detection of cryptic and emerging variants. However, validation, such as phenotypic characterization, is needed to assess the clinical importance of a variant detected in WBE. In this study, we investigated the phenotypic traits of genetically distinct GI.3 and GII.12 lineages detected in wastewater from Cameroon. We utilized NanoLuc luciferase immunoprecipitation system (N-LIPS)-based assays to assess binding specificity and antigenicity. Compared to traditional methods involving virus isolation and virus-like particle production, N-LIPS-based assays are considerably less laborious and faster. This allows for rapid characterization of novel variants, making the timely assessment of phenotypic changes of such variants for outbreak or pandemic preparedness feasible. Finally, by integrating insights from phenotypic assays, we showed the possibility of expanding the public health value of wastewater surveillance in assessing the risk of novel viral variants.

articles.title: Infection-specific long-chain fatty acid metabolism as a broad anti-enterovirus target.
articles.abstract: Enteroviruses are arguably the most numerous group of viruses infecting humans. While most enterovirus infections are benign and self-resolving, their sheer number inevitably increases the chances of multiple complications. The diversity of enteroviruses means that the development of vaccines is only economically feasible against a select few, and no direct-acting or host-targeted anti-virals are approved to treat enteroviral infections, largely due to the rapid development of resistance against all experimental drugs. Here, we explored a universal property of enterovirus infection-a massive upregulation of phospholipid synthesis as a target for anti-viral interventions. The increased phospholipid synthesis consumes endogenously and exogenously derived long-chain fatty acids (LCFA). We demonstrate that polyunsaturated LCFAs can have a broad anti-enteroviral effect, affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs did not strictly depend on the degree of unsaturation or their capacity to induce lipid peroxidation, but significantly correlated with their conformation. This suggests that their incorporation into the phospholipid molecules makes the replication organelle membranes incapable of properly accommodating viral replication machinery. Accordingly, the inhibition of neutral lipid synthesis promoted LCFAs retargeting to the membranes in infected cells and increased their anti-viral potency. We show that this approach is effective against diverse enteroviruses in different cell types, including differentiated primary cells, and that attempts to establish viruses resistant to such treatment were unsuccessful.IMPORTANCEHumans are hosts to more than 300 distinct enteroviruses. Enterovirus infections can induce multiple short-term and long-term complications, including such serious conditions as paralysis, myocarditis, aseptic meningitis, and others. Yet, licensed vaccines are available only against poliovirus and enterovirus A71, and no specific anti-enterovirus drugs are approved for clinical practice. These viruses rapidly develop resistance to either virus- or host-acting experimental compounds. We explored a shared feature of enterovirus infection, a strong upregulation of phospholipid synthesis in infected cells, as a tool to control enterovirus replication. By altering the long-chain fatty acids composition available to infected cells, replication of diverse enteroviruses can be similarly suppressed, and the selection of resistant mutants was not successful. Thus, targeting infection-induced changes in cellular lipid metabolism, rather than individual viral or host factors, may offer a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections.

articles.title: CIRP: New Horizons for CNS Injury Biomarkers and Therapy.
articles.abstract: Cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRP) is a stress-response protein that protects cells under conditions of low temperature and other stresses. The expression of CIRP is induced by various stressors. CIRP regulates gene expression through complex, multi-layered mechanisms and plays a central role in physiological and pathological processes, including cell proliferation, apoptosis, inflammatory responses, and circadian rhythms. In central nervous system (CNS) injuries, CIRP exhibits a dual role. Intracellular CIRP has a neuroprotective function. In contrast, when released into the extracellular space as eCIRP, it acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that exacerbates neuroinflammation. Serum levels of eCIRP are significantly elevated in patients with CNS injuries, such as acute ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage, suggesting its potential as a biomarker for diagnosis and prognosis. Furthermore, targeting the eCIRP signaling pathway has shown significant therapeutic effects in various models of neurological injury. Strategies include using inhibitory peptides like C23 and M3, as well as microRNA-based approaches. Here, we systematically review the molecular characteristics, expression regulation, and biological functions of CIRP, with a focus on its neuroprotective role, biomarker potential, and therapeutic targeting in CNS injuries.

articles.title: Serotonin Neurobiology and Artificial Intelligence-Driven Biomarker Detection in Affective Disorders: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Affective disorders, including major depressive disorder (MDD) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), impose a major global health burden because of their high prevalence, early onset, disability, and substantial social and economic impacts. Diagnosis remains challenging because it relies largely on subjective clinical assessment and symptom-based criteria, which often delay recognition and contribute to heterogeneous treatment response. Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) has long been central to the understanding of these disorders, but the classical serotonin hypothesis has evolved into a broader systems-level framework in which serotonergic dysfunction is linked with neurotransmission, receptor signaling, transporter regulation, neuroplasticity, endocrine balance, immune modulation, circadian rhythm control, and gut-brain communication. Serotonin biosynthesis, metabolism, and compartmentalization are tightly regulated, and variation in the serotonin transporter and related pathways influences vulnerability to disease, symptom expression, and response to therapy. Although serotonin-targeted pharmacotherapy remains foundational, its delayed and variable clinical effects highlight the need for objective biomarkers and more-precise monitoring strategies. This Review gives a comprehensive overview of serotonin neurobiology in affective disorders and the therapeutic implications of serotonergic dysregulation. It discusses the current understanding of serotonin synthesis, receptor heterogeneity, transporter function, and broader system interactions that shape mood, stress responsivity, and treatment outcomes. The Review also examines the growing role of artificial intelligence in psychiatric biomarker discovery, including machine learning and deep learning approaches applied to neuroimaging, electrophysiology, physiological signals, and language-based data for improved diagnosis and prediction of antidepressant responses. In addition, emerging serotonin-specific biosensors are discussed as promising tools for real-time, noninvasive neurochemical monitoring. By integrating mechanistic insights into serotonin biology with AI-based analytics and biosensing technologies, this Review highlights a pathway toward more objective, personalized, and effective management of affective disorders.

articles.title: Improved disc diffusion-based detection of extended spectrum β-lactamase production in the Klebsiella oxytoca complex.
articles.abstract: Accurate discrimination between extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production and hyperproduction of the intrinsic OXY-β-lactamase (hyperOXY) in the Klebsiella oxytoca complex remains challenging, as both mechanisms can generate overlapping resistance phenotypes and lead to unnecessary confirmatory testing or misclassification. We analyzed a collection of 123 whole-genome-sequenced clinical K. oxytoca complex isolates (2009-2024), including 33 ESBL producers and multiple species-specific blaOXY variants, to develop a phenotypic strategy for distinguishing these resistance mechanisms using disc diffusion data. We performed antimicrobial susceptibility testing according to EUCAST guidelines and correlated phenotypic findings with genomic resistance determinants. HyperOXY isolates harbored classical activating mutations in blaOXY promoter regions and displayed a characteristic resistance pattern marked by high-level resistance to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and piperacillin-tazobactam, resistance to ceftriaxone and cefpodoxime, preserved or borderline susceptibility to ceftazidime, and variable reductions in cefepime susceptibility. In contrast, ESBL-producing isolates showed reproducible clavulanate synergy and distinct inhibition zone distributions for piperacillin-tazobactam, cefpodoxime, and gentamicin. A cefpodoxime inhibition zone diameter <17 mm identified all ESBL-producing isolates (sensitivity 100%) but showed limited specificity (44%). Combining cefpodoxime <17 mm with additional phenotypic criteria allowed confident ESBL attribution without additional testing (specificity 100%), albeit at reduced sensitivity (72%). EUCAST-recommended combination disc ESBL confirmatory testing using cefotaxime or cefepime with clavulanic acid demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance (sensitivity/specificity ≥ 96%). Thirty-three isolates showed ambiguous phenotypes requiring confirmatory testing. Overall, interpretative reading of routine disc diffusion patterns can reliably classify characteristic hyperOXY and ESBL phenotypes and restrict additional confirmatory testing to ambiguous isolates, thereby improving diagnostic efficiency while maintaining high accuracy.IMPORTANCEMembers of the K. oxytoca complex possess an intrinsic OXY β-lactamase that can be overexpressed and generate resistance patterns closely resembling those of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producers. This phenotypic overlap complicates routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing and frequently leads to unnecessary ESBL confirmatory testing or misclassification, with potential consequences for patient management and infection control. Using a large, genomically characterized strain collection, this study defines reproducible disc diffusion patterns that distinguish hyperOXY-mediated resistance from true ESBL production and evaluates screening and confirmatory strategies based on routinely tested antibiotics. By providing practical, phenotype-based guidance aligned with EUCAST methodology, our findings help clinical laboratories improve diagnostic accuracy, streamline workflows, and avoid ESBL-misidentification in K. oxytoca complex isolates.

articles.title: Modelling herpes simplex virus type 2 and Zika virus replication in mouse vaginal organoids and human vaginal spheroids.
articles.abstract: Sexually transmitted viral infections disproportionately affect women and have adverse outcomes on maternal and fetal health. Since they are acquired through the vaginal tract, the vaginal epithelium is an important site to study host-viral interactions. An in vitro model of mouse vaginal epithelial organoids that can be infected by herpes simplex virus was recently established. Here, we used multiple vaginal organoid systems and studied their response to infection by herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) and Zika virus (ZIKV), both of which can be sexually transmitted and result in adverse effects on maternal and fetal health. We showed that mouse vaginal organoids support the replication of HSV-2 and ZIKV and respond to interferon treatment. We also established human vaginal spheroids from VK2/E6E7 cells that contain distinct apical and basal cell layers and are also susceptible to HSV-2 and ZIKV infection. Acyclovir treatment reduced HSV-2 replication in both mouse organoids and VK2 spheroids. However, ZIKV was restricted by remdesivir in VK2 spheroids but not in mouse organoids, indicating differences in antiviral activity depending on the organoid system. Finally, we established apical-out mouse vaginal organoids that were also susceptible to HSV-2 and ZIKV infection. Altogether, our results show that vaginal organoids and spheroids are useful in vitro models to study vaginal viral infections and effects of antiviral drugs.IMPORTANCEThe vaginal epithelium is the site of acquisition of sexually transmitted viral infections in women but has been historically understudied. 3D vaginal organoids that model the vaginal epithelium can be used to study virus-host interactions and provide novel insights. We demonstrated that vaginal organoids derived from mouse tissues could be infected with herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) and Zika virus (ZIKV), and these organoids are also capable of expressing immune genes. We then generated "flipped" mouse organoids that better represent the natural orientation of the vaginal epithelial lining. We also developed spheroids from human vaginal epithelial cells and showed that they can also be infected with HSV-2 and ZIKV. Finally, we showed that antiviral drugs reduced viral infection in these vaginal organoid and spheroid models. Our findings show that vaginal organoids and spheroids possess characteristics that make them useful models to study viral infections, as well as to test antiviral drugs.

articles.title: Correlation-based analysis of gene expression in Cardinium, Wolbachia, and Tyrophagus putrescentiae reveals distinct host-symbiont interactions and parallel evolutionary expansion of infection-associated genes.
articles.abstract: Cardinium and Wolbachia are phylogenetically distinct intracellular symbionts that have convergently evolved mechanisms to infect a wide range of arthropod and nematode hosts. Here, we investigated the interaction dynamics of two basal strains, Cardinium (cTPut) and Wolbachia (wTPut), in the stored-product mite Tyrophagus putrescentiae (Acari: Astigmata). The KEGG-annotated gene expression profiles of mite samples were analyzed in single infections (Cardinium or Wolbachia) and mixed infections across three time points (2, 4, and 6 months). Temporal effects on gene expression were marginal; therefore, correlation-based network analyses were used to characterize host-symbiont interactions. The symbionts exhibited distinct host-targeting strategies: Wolbachia displayed a "broad" interaction pattern characterized by numerous weak correlations with host KEGG genes, whereas Cardinium showed a "focused" strategy involving fewer but stronger correlations. These patterns were consistent across global KEGG data sets, immune and regulatory pathways (including AMPK, autophagy, endocytosis, Hippo, lysosome, MAPK, mTOR, and Notch), receptor subsets, and metabolic pathways. Consistent with these interaction patterns, orthologous analyses across Cardinium and selected Wolbachia genomes revealed that infection-associated genes are not broadly conserved but are enriched in lineage-specific, duplicated gene families, particularly in T. putrescentiae-associated symbionts. These findings indicate that infection-related traits evolve primarily through lineage-specific gene family expansion rather than conservation and suggest that basal Cardinium and Wolbachia employ fundamentally distinct host interaction strategies.IMPORTANCEThe study provides novel insight into host-symbiont interactions: Cardinium, Wolbachia infecting mite Tyrophagus putrescentiae, an important producer of allergens (i) Cardinium gene expression responds to the presence of Wolbachia, whereas Wolbachia gene expression shows no reciprocal response; (ii) the two symbionts employ contrasting host interaction strategies with the host, with Cardinium exhibiting fewer but stronger associations and Wolbachia showing widespread but weaker correlations; (iii) distinct host pathways are differentially associated with each symbiont; and (iv) we identified 40 of the most correlated bacterial genes to the host that include candidates of viral origin, suggesting a potential role of horizontally acquired elements in the host. Furthermore, evolutionary analyses demonstrate that infection-associated genes are primarily lineage expanded rather than broadly conserved across symbiont genomes. Given the allergenic relevance of T. putrescentiae, these findings suggest that symbiont-specific interaction strategies can indirectly influence host physiology and allergen production.

articles.title: DksA regulates intestinal colonization of Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic plasticity.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Intestinal colonization by Klebsiella pneumoniae is recognized as a pivotal prerequisite for its systemic dissemination and subsequent invasive infection; however, the metabolic basis and regulatory mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq) to systematically identify metabolic genes associated with intestinal colonization in K. pneumoniae. By integrating high-throughput screening with in vivo phenotypic validation, we identified the global transcriptional regulator DksA as a key factor that markedly enhances K. pneumoniae intestinal colonization. Mechanistically, DksA may contribute to intestinal colonization through modulation of central carbon metabolism. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, together with homology modeling and molecular dynamics simulations, suggested that DksA may contribute to allosteric remodeling of key RNA polymerase structural domains, thereby influencing the expression of metabolic genes, carbon source utilization, and intestinal colonization by K. pneumoniae. Collectively, our findings highlight the important role of metabolic plasticity associated with transcriptional regulation in K. pneumoniae intestinal colonization and provide a theoretical framework and potential targets for developing anti-colonization strategies that exploit pathogen metabolic vulnerabilities.

IMPORTANCE: Intestinal colonization is a critical first step in the pathogenesis and transmission of Klebsiella pneumoniae, yet the bacterial factors that support persistence in the gut remain incompletely understood. In this study, we identified the transcriptional regulator DksA as an important contributor to intestinal colonization through genome-wide genetic screening and in vivo validation. Multi-omics analyses suggest that DksA is associated with the regulation of bacterial carbon metabolism and metabolic adaptation, processes that are likely important for survival in the nutrient-variable intestinal environment. Structural modeling further provides insight into how DksA may influence transcriptional regulation. These findings expand our understanding of the factors that facilitate K. pneumoniae gut colonization and highlight bacterial metabolic adaptation as a potential target for strategies aimed at limiting colonization and subsequent infection.

articles.title: Superior classification of visuospatial neglect in the subacute phase through free-viewing and considering overcompensation.
articles.abstract: Visuospatial neglect is a common disorder of spatial attention after stroke. Traditional paper-and-pencil tasks are widely used for diagnosis but show limited sensitivity in the subacute phase, partly due to compensatory and (over)compensatory strategies. State-of-the-art measures, including gaze bias assessed with eye-tracking during free viewing and refined line bisection scoring, may offer greater diagnostic accuracy but have rarely been tested in clinical samples. We compared traditional measures (Centre of Cancellation, directional bisection error) and state-of-the-art measures (endpoint weightings bias, mean horizontal gaze position during free viewing) in stroke patients admitted to rehabilitation (n = 34) and age-matched healthy controls (n = 32), examining which measures best discriminated neglect from non-neglect in the subacute phase. We also tested whether direction-independent (absolute) deviations better capture neglect than directional deviations, given that overcompensation can mask deficits in standard scoring. Direction-independent scores showed superior discrimination. Furthermore, a logistic regression model based on state-of-the-art measures outperformed one based on traditional measures. The strongest neglect detection was achieved by combining directional bisection error with mean horizontal gaze position. These findings support the complementary value of eye-tracking-based assessment alongside traditional neglect tasks, and highlight the importance of accounting for (over)compensatory behaviour.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
articles.abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of cortical activity and remains central to the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of iEEG data increasingly challenge conventional visual interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have accelerated quantitative analyses in electrophysiology, supporting localization, outcome prediction, and therapeutic decision-making in epilepsy. This article reviews recent advances in the application of AI to iEEG in epilepsy and in particular stereo-EEG, although the concepts discussed are broadly relevant across iEEG modalities. Although many of these approaches have shown encouraging results, the current evidence remains largely preliminary, with most studies being retrospective, single-center investigations that lack independent external validation. AI-based integration of iEEG with multimodal magnetic resonance imaging shows promise for improving surgical planning in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Concurrently, early studies suggest that AI-driven iEEG analysis may enhance epileptogenic zone identification by detecting subtle electrophysiological signatures, network interactions, and temporal dynamics. These multimodal frameworks emphasize distributed epileptic networks rather than isolated focal abnormalities. AI is also reshaping how iEEG-guided stimulation is designed and interpreted. Data-driven approaches have the potential to optimize stimulation parameters, predict network responses, and clarify mechanisms underlying diagnostic and therapeutic stimulation, laying the groundwork for adaptive, patient-specific neuromodulation. Beyond short-term epilepsy monitoring, AI applications increasingly incorporate continuous sensing, longitudinal network modeling, and integration with implantable neurotechnology platforms. Although these developments require prospective multicenter studies with external validation before widespread clinical implementation, advances in multimodal data integration, interpretable modeling, and continuous sensing position AI-enhanced iEEG as an emerging platform for precision brain network medicine for epilepsy.

articles.title: Prognosticating Factors in PET CT and MRI of Cervical Cancer Treated With Chemoradiotherapy.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aim to evaluate the functional and anatomical imaging characteristics of locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) to identify potential prognosticating imaging biomarkers in the context of chemoradiotherapy treatment (CRT).

METHOD: This retrospective review analysed patient data over a period of seven years. Patients with locally advanced cervical cancer who have undergone FDG PET CT and MRI were identified through Report Analytics. Patients with LACC who have undergone chemoradiotherapy were identified through review of the electronic records. Pre and post-treatment imaging were analysed and compared. The patients were dichotomised into complete metabolic responders (CMR) and non-complete metabolic responders (N-CMR) as per European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) criteria. Imaging parameters in PET CT and MRI including SUV max, SUV mean, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), lesion metabolic tumour volume (MTV), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) minimum were examined. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate differences in overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) between the CMR and N-CMR groups. Pearson's correlation and Fischer's exact test were used to evaluate the potential prognosticating value of the PET CT and MRI imaging parameters as predictors of metabolic response to CRT.

RESULTS: A total of 159 FDG PET CT scans were conducted in the 7-year period, of which there were 61 individual patients identified for inclusion into the present study. The average imaging follow-up for the patients included between 2019 and 2024 was 63.3 months, and chemoradiotherapy follow-up was 62.9 months. The patients were dichotomized into CMR and N-CMR groups. There is a statistically significant difference in overall survival, with 1 mortality (5%) in the CMR group vs. 19 mortality (70%) in the N-CMR group (p = 0.0001). However, no statistically significant difference in follow-up 87.1 months vs. 57.1 months (p = 0.20). In the overall cervical cancer cohort as well as the squamous cell carcinoma subgroup (n = 32), the comparison of CMR and N-CMR groups revealed a statistically significant difference in the following FDG PET imaging parameters: SUV max, SUV mean, ADC minimum and MTV. The CMR group has tumours with higher SUV max and SUV mean (difference of 7.5 and 5.1 respectively) and smaller MTV (difference of 20.1 cm3). However, there was no demonstrable difference in TLG and MRI ADC min values between the dichotomized groups. The tumoral SUV max and ADC min were weakly negatively correlated. There was no statistically significant difference in International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage of disease (individual stage and IIB or higher) and pathological grade in the dichotomized groups.

CONCLUSION: This retrospective analysis identified functional imaging predictors of positive response to CRT in LACC patients using FDG PET CT. Furthermore, this confirms the negative correlation between functional and anatomical imaging parameters, albeit non-statistically significant (namely SUV max and ADC min). The present results indicated cervical cancer with higher SUV values (max and mean) and smaller MTV were more likely to respond to CRT. There is no demonstrable difference in pathological grading and FIGO stage of disease. Prospective studies in larger cohorts are indicated to ascertain the predictive value of functional and anatomical imaging parameters and their correlation with tumour histopathological features.

articles.title: "But, but over the years you just give up!": a qualitative study of people with post stroke aphasia receiving healthcare in the community and how technology could assist.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore the perspectives of people living with chronic post-stroke aphasia and their significant others on accessing healthcare in the community and if technology could assist.

METHODS: A qualitative descriptive approach was used. People with aphasia (n = 6) and significant others (n = 5) participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Four themes on participants' experiences of accessing healthcare were developed: (1) Seeking healthcare is complex and distressing; (2) Despite differences everybody strives for independence; (3) The exceptional and underacknowledged role of a family support person; and (4) Understanding and adapting help: Doing nothing is devastating. Two themes were developed on whether technology could assist. These were: (1) Personalised support to make healthcare communication more accurate, specific, and easier; and (2) Technology could help but only if ….

CONCLUSION: People with aphasia need healthcare provider support to optimise their independence and get their healthcare needs met without distress. Co-designed technology could improve independence for some people with aphasia. However, the success of any healthcare technology hinges on investment in system level supports to enable healthcare providers to adapt communication and processes for people with aphasia.

articles.title: Heatwave-Resilient Cuticular Microbiota Protect the Leaf Beetle Plagiodera versicolora From Fungal Infection.
articles.abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves-extreme thermal events characterized by prolonged supra-optimal temperatures-exert profound impacts on global ecosystem stability and species interactions. While the disruptive effects of thermal stress on host physiology and gut microbiota are well documented, the role of cuticular microbiota in host defense under heatwaves remains poorly characterized. Here, we show that the cuticular microbiota of the willow leaf beetle Plagiodera versicolora may serve as a thermostable protective barrier against the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana. Using microbiota-manipulated larval models, we found that cuticular microbiota significantly bolstered host survival under both control (27°C) and simulated heatwave (32°C) regimes. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing revealed a dramatic microbial regime shift: Pantoea dominated at control temperatures, whereas Enterobacter proliferated and became predominant during simulated heatwaves. Both genera exhibited potent antifungal activity that markedly increased with rising temperature, suggesting a potential functional compensation property whereby thermally adaptive taxa may maintain host defensive capacity under climatic perturbations. Recolonization experiments confirmed that cuticle-isolated Enterobacter gergoviae and Pantoea anthophila are sufficient to reduce the increased fungal susceptibility of germ-free larvae. Mechanistically, these symbionts appear to inhibit fungal germination through direct antagonism and modulate host immune responses by upregulating antimicrobial peptide effectors while potentially reducing excessive immune recognition signaling. These findings highlight the resilience of cuticular defensive symbioses in the face of climate change and provide new insights into the adaptive mechanisms that sustain host-microbe-pathogen dynamics in a warming world.
