The Cytosolic Iron-Sulfur Cluster Assembly Targeting Complex Is Hijacked by Magnaporthe Effector AvrPi9 to Suppress Rice Resistance.
articles.abstract: The cytosolic iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly (CIA) targeting complex mediates the maturation of cytosolic and nuclear Fe-S proteins and governs core eukaryotic cellular processes. However, whether this complex contributes to plant disease resistance remains unclear. Here, we show that the Magnaporthe oryzae avirulence effector AvrPi9 targets the host CIA targeting complex to suppress rice blast resistance. AvrPi9 physically interacts with and stabilizes OsAE7, a core subunit of the CIA targeting complex. Using biochemical and genetic approaches, we demonstrate that OsAE7 facilitates Fe-S protein maturation, including the Fe-S protein aconitase OsACO1, and negatively regulates blast resistance in cooperation with another CIA targeting complex subunit, OsCIA1, and the carrier protein OsNAR1 in rice. Furthermore, ectopic expression of AvrPi9 enhances the activity of the CIA complex and the maturation of OsACO1. Knockout of OsACO1 elevates ferrous iron levels, triggers a reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst, and activates pathogenesis-related gene transcription, thereby strengthening rice resistance to blast. Our findings reveal a critical role of the CIA targeting complex in plant disease resistance and uncover a novel virulence strategy whereby AvrPi9 hijacks the host CIA pathway to dampen basal resistance and promote infection.

articles.title: [GOLD 2026: implications for COPD care in Sweden].
articles.abstract: The 2026 update of the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) report introduces major changes with likely implications for the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in Sweden. Disease stability and disease control are defined as treatment goals for all patients, irrespective of disease severity. The document highlights underdiagnosis of COPD and places greater emphasis on early detection through active case-finding, structured follow-up of disease activity, and systematic assessment of multimorbidity. Extended risk-assessment criteria at diagnosis mean that a single moderate exacerbation is now sufficient to place a patient in GOLD group E. The treatment strategies outlined in GOLD 2026 largely align with the Swedish Medical Products Agency recommendations from 2023, but to fully implement GOLD 2026 in Swedish clinical practice, the current recommendations need to be revised in light of the new evidence.

articles.title: Bioinspired Mechano-Chemical Titanium Interfaces With Potential for Infection-Resistant Osseointegration.
articles.abstract: Bacterial colonization and insufficient osseointegration remain major challenges for titanium-based orthopedic and dental implants. Here, we developed a bioinspired mechano-chemical titanium interface by combining an anodization-derived micro-/nano-pitted topography with a polydopamine-citric acid-quercetin (PCQ) functional layer. Inspired by dragonfly-wing micro-/nanostructures, the resulting OPT@PCQ interface exhibited hierarchical topography, enhanced hydrophilicity, and preserved overall mechanical response. OPT@PCQ showed favorable cytocompatibility and significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, with increased alkaline phosphatase activity, matrix mineralization, and RUNX2, COL1A1, and OCN expression. It also displayed pronounced antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, accompanied by bacterial morphological deformation and reduced viability. Transcriptomic analysis of S. aureus revealed broad perturbation of central carbon metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, ribosome-associated processes, and stress-response pathways. In vivo, OPT@PCQ promoted wound closure and markedly enhanced new bone formation and trabecular reconstruction in a noninfected rat femoral defect model. Qualitative hemolysis assessment and major-organ histology provided preliminary evidence of hemocompatibility and systemic biosafety under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings support OPT@PCQ as a multifunctional titanium interface with potential for infection-resistant osseointegration; however, direct validation in an infected bone-defect model remains necessary.

articles.title: Gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine with and without aura: A multimodal MRI and JuSpace analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates.

BACKGROUND: Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood.

METHODS: This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9.

RESULTS: Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction.

CONCLUSION: Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes of the Modified Oncoplastic Lift and Lymphatic Excision and Reconstruction (MOLLER) Technique in Breast Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Oncoplastic breast surgery integrates oncologic resection with reconstructive techniques to optimize both tumor control and aesthetic outcomes. The Modified Oncoplastic Lift and Lymphatic Excision and Reconstruction (MOLLER) technique is a reconstructive approach incorporating lymphatic preservation principles while aiming to preserve breast contour. However, perioperative outcomes remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study included adult women undergoing partial mastectomy or lumpectomy for malignant or benign breast conditions with the MOLLER technique (2011-2021). Primary outcomes were immediate and delayed postoperative complications; secondary outcomes were re-excision and radiation-related complications.

RESULTS: A total of 136 patients were included. Median follow-up was 3 years. Immediate complications were infrequent: hematoma and wound dehiscence each occurred in 3 patients (2.2%); seroma, infection, and paresthesia each in 2 (1.5%). Delayed complications were uncommon: arm lymphedema in 5 patients (3.7%); fat necrosis and breast lymphedema each in 4 (2.9%). The re-excision rate was 4.4%. Radiation-related complications were uncommon, most commonly skin discoloration (7.4%) and skin thickening (5.1%); no delayed wound healing occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: The MOLLER technique is a safe reconstructive approach associated with low rates of postoperative complications, re-excision, and lymphedema. Its lymphatic preservation principles may be associated with reduced lymphatic morbidity. Prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Neutralization of the PTX3/CD44 axis suppresses TGF-β1 signaling in kidney fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but effective antifibrotic therapies are lacking. Pentraxin 3 (PTX3) is markedly upregulated in CKD patients and in a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) model, correlating with renal injury, extracellular matrix accumulation, partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition markers, and TGF-β1 signaling. Genetic deletion of Ptx3 significantly attenuates UUO-induced fibrosis. Mechanistically, PTX3 promotes transcription of LTBP-1 and fibronectin, facilitating latent TGF-β1 activation and inducing a profibrotic partial EMT program in tubular epithelial cells without lineage conversion. Importantly, blockade of the PTX3/CD44 axis using a neutralizing αPTX3 antibody reduced serum creatinine levels and renal fibrosis, identifying PTX3 as a promising therapeutic target for CKD.

articles.title: Association Between Serum Magnesium Status and Bronchial Asthma Severity: A Gender-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypomagnesaemia has been implicated as a potentially modifiable correlate of poorer asthma control, but evidence from Indian outpatient populations remains limited. We evaluated the association between serum magnesium status (hypomagnesaemia versus normal or raised) and bronchial asthma severity, classified by National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) criteria, in a gender-matched retrospective cohort, adjusting for age and gender. We hypothesised a priori that hypomagnesaemia would be associated with a higher NAEPP severity grade.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Surat, Gujarat, India. Outpatient medical records were reviewed over a six-month period; 96 patients were included following 1:2 gender-based matching (32 hypomagnesaemic, 64 controls). Asthma severity was graded as mild (Grade 1), moderate (Grade 2), or severe (Grade 3) per NAEPP criteria. Association was assessed using chi-square analysis, unadjusted ordinal logistic regression, and a multivariable ordinal logistic regression adjusting for age and gender. Because the proportional-odds assumption could not be formally tested, two sensitivity analyses of severe versus non-severe asthma were performed.

RESULTS: The hypomagnesaemia group had markedly higher asthma severity: 78.1% had severe asthma versus 7.8% in controls, and no hypomagnesaemic patient had mild asthma. Chi-square analysis confirmed a highly significant association (chi-square = 49.4, df = 2, p < 0.001). In the primary adjusted ordinal model, hypomagnesaemic patients had substantially greater odds of being in a higher severity category (OR = 50.53; 95% CI 15.13 to 210.1; p < 0.001). ==Sensitivity analyses of severe versus non-severe asthma gave concordant but more conservative estimates (exact conditional OR = 39.3, 95% CI 10.75 to 178.6; Firth penalised OR = 36.8, 95% CI 11.0 to 123.0).== Neither age (p = 0.096) nor gender (p = 0.935) was independently associated with severity.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypomagnesaemia was strongly associated with greater asthma severity in this cohort, and the study hypothesis was supported in this sample. Because exposure and outcome were ascertained contemporaneously from retrospective records, these data cannot establish whether hypomagnesaemia contributes to severe asthma, arises as a consequence of severe disease or its treatment, or reflects a shared cause. The wide confidence intervals reflect sparse data in the extreme severity categories. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not support a change in current practice; prospective studies with serial magnesium measurement and adjustment for treatment, renal, and nutritional confounders are required.

articles.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of Candida albicans, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Acinetobacter baumannii among the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

articles.title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions.
articles.abstract: Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

articles.title: Complementary stable and dynamic prelimbic ensembles encode learned threat value underlying generalization and discrimination.
articles.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.

articles.title: End-of-life care of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and home mechanical ventilation: the national population-based DISCOVERY study.
articles.abstract: Background: Home mechanical ventilation (HMV), including noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and invasive ventilation (IV), is increasingly used in people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (pwALS), but its impact on end-of-life care remains unclear. Objective: To examine whether ventilation pathway (NIV or IV) influences symptom prevalence and relief during the final week of life in pwALS. Secondary objectives were to assess end-of-life discussions, place and cause of death, and anticipated death. Methods: This national, population-based retrospective cohort study included pwALS using HMV in the Swedish National Quality Registry for Respiratory Failure (Swedevox), cross-linked with the Swedish Register of Palliative Care, which contains staff-reported end-of-life data, and other national registries. Results: Among 652 pwALS, 609 received NIV (mean age 66 years, 42% female) and 43 IV (mean age 60 years, 42% female). Anxiety and breathlessness were more common in the NIV group (76% vs 48% and 72% vs 31%, both p < 0.001), while prevalence and relief of other symptoms were similar between groups. Most patients had end-of-life discussions (NIV 87%, IV 92%). NIV patients more often died in specialized palliative wards (22% vs 7%, p = 0.023). Most deaths were due to ALS (96%) and were anticipated (NIV 94%, IV 88%). Conclusions: In pwALS with HVM, NIV was associated with higher rates of anxiety and breathlessness in the final week of life, but the ventilation pathway did not influence overall symptom relief. End-of-life communications and cause of death were similar; place of death differed by ventilation pathway; however, most deaths were anticipated.

articles.title: Variability of Right Ventricular Structure and Function in Infants Across Different High-Altitude Regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO Sub-Study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Srour, MHD Osama, Darla Carvallo-Castañeda, Monica Medina, Gian Huaman, Rafael Marquez, and Katia Bravo-Jaimes.Variability of right ventricular structure and function in infants across different high-altitude regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO sub-study. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.

BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) predominance is a normal fetal state that rapidly regresses postnatally at sea level. High-altitude hypobaric hypoxic environment may alter this adaptation process. This study evaluated echocardiographic RV variations in healthy infants across different altitudes in the Peruvian Andes.

METHODS: This sub-study of the ANDES-CHD cohort included 81 healthy infants from sea level to 4,338 meters (m) in Peru. RV fractional area change (FAC) and indexed RV free wall thickness were measured. Multivariate linear regression assessed the independent effect of altitude, adjusting for relevant confounders.

RESULTS: Infants at higher altitudes exhibited a statistically significant reduction in RV FAC compared with sea level (45.5% at sea level vs. 38% at 3,259 m [p = 0.021] and 4,338 m [p = 0.006]), though all median values remained within normal physiological ranges. Sixteen percent of infants had an RV FAC < 35%, with no significant difference between high- and low-altitude groups, and no adverse outcome at 12-month follow-up. Indexed RV free wall thickness did not differ significantly across groups.

CONCLUSION: Healthy Andean infants demonstrate a physiological adaptation to high-altitude hypobaric hypoxia characterized by a statistical reduction in RV systolic function without pathological compromise, alongside normal postnatal regression of RV wall thickness.

articles.title: Prehospital point-of-care ultrasound as a decision-support tool: A structured narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) may support focused bedside decisions, but prehospital implementation remains limited by operational constraints, heterogeneous protocols, variable training, and limited outcome-focused evidence. This narrative review examines prehospital POCUS as a clinical decision-support tool across cardiac, thoracic, trauma, pediatric, and obstetric applications.

METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from April 2017 to February 2026. Search terms combined the prehospital setting, ultrasound, and clinical applications. Of 464 records identified, 38 full-text articles were included, including nine systematic reviews on cardiac evaluation (n = 2), thoracic evaluation (n = 3), and trauma assessment (n = 4). Screening and full-text assessment were performed by a single reviewer. No formal risk-of-bias assessment, certainty grading, quantitative synthesis, or meta-analysis was performed.

RESULTS: In cardiac arrest, prehospital POCUS may identify cardiac activity and selected reversible causes, guide interventions, confirm return of spontaneous circulation, and support prognostic assessment, provided that image acquisition does not interrupt resuscitation or delay defibrillation. In nontraumatic shock and cardiac dysfunction, focused cardiac, lung, and vascular ultrasound may help characterize shock mechanisms, guide fluid therapy, and identify actionable findings such as pulmonary congestion, pericardial effusion, right ventricular strain, or major aortic pathology. In acute dyspnea, lung ultrasound may improve diagnostic confidence, particularly for cardiogenic pulmonary edema. In trauma, E-FAST has high specificity and may support triage, destination choice, trauma pathway activation, and preparation for definitive care; however, limited sensitivity prevents its use as a rule-out test. Pediatric and obstetric applications are feasible but remain emerging.

CONCLUSIONS: Prehospital POCUS is an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Its value lies in answering actionable questions that may influence treatment, triage, transport destination, hospital prealert, or pathway activation. Implementation requires protocols, training, quality assurance, and governance, and must not delay time-critical care or transport.

articles.title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.

METHODS: The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.

RESULTS: Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.

CONCLUSION: In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

articles.title: Hybrid membrane vesicle-enabled sonodynamic therapy using ciprofloxacin for treating biofilm-associated infections.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated infections on indwelling medical devices pose significant clinical challenges due to antibiotic resistance and poor drug penetration. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) is a promising strategy utilizing ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers for generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, the lack of safe and effective sonosensitizers and bacterial-targeting delivery systems limits its application in treating biofilm infection. To address these limitations, we developed antibiotic ciprofloxacin-loaded hybrid membrane vesicles (CIP@HMVs), where ciprofloxacin acts as a safe sonosensitizer and HMVs serve as a detoxified bacterial-targeted delivery system. HMVs were engineered by fusing Pseudomonas aeruginosa-derived outer membrane vesicles (PAEVs) with macrophage membrane vesicles (MMVs), creating a dual-functional nanoplatform with homotypic bacteria-targeting and detoxification capabilities. CIP@HMVs exploited ciprofloxacin's sonosensitizer properties to generate singlet oxygen (1O2) under ultrasound, while HMVs enhanced bacterial uptake in P. aeruginosa. This enabled synergistic bactericidal effects against planktonic bacteria via membrane disruption and intracellular ROS burst, achieving a 5.7-log bacterial reduction in catheter biofilms in vitro. Crucially, HMVs neutralized PAEVs' LPS toxicity in vitro and demonstrated negligible systemic toxicity in vivo. In a murine catheter-infection model, CIP@HMVs under ultrasound achieved 99.8% bacterial eradication and reduced inflammation. This bacterial-targeting sonodynamic platform provides a transformative strategy for treating device-associated biofilm infections with high efficacy and biosafety.

articles.title: HIV screening in patients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections in Spanish emergency departments.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de quimioterapia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Quimioterapia
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the frequency of HIV serology requests in emergency departments (EDs) in Spain for patients with sexually transmitted infections (STIs), its longitudinal evolution (2018-2024), and associated factors.

METHODS: Multi-center study including all patients diagnosed with an STI across 14 EDs in 8 Spanish autonomous communities. Demographics, specific STI diagnoses, prior HIV testing, and HIV serology requested during ED care were recorded. Differences and temporal trends were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 35,845 STI cases (median age 34 years; 60% men; 74% Spanish; 2% previously tested for HIV), HIV serology was requested in 5,462 (15%), yielding 253 (4.6%) positive results. Main diagnoses included orchiepididymitis (24.9%), vulvovaginitis (16.4%), and non-specific urethritis (12.4%). HIV testing increased significantly from 5.3% in 2018 to 20.7% in 2024 (p < 0.001). Higher testing likelihood was associated with younger age (aOR 0.97 per year, 95% CI 0.97-0.97), male sex (aOR 3.83, 95% CI 3.35-4.37), prior HIV testing (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 1.08-1.92), and more recent years (aOR 1.34 per year, 95% CI 1.30-1.38). Testing rates varied significantly by specific STI, with higher probabilities in risk exposure, suspected STI, and urethritis but lower probabilities in orchiepididymitis, vulvovaginitis, and genital herpes.

CONCLUSIONS: HIV screening among patients presenting with STIs in Spanish EDs remains low (15%), despite a significant upward trend over time. Disparities based on age, sex, and specific STI presentation highlight the need for universal HIV screening protocols across all ED patients diagnosed with an STI.

articles.title: Community mental health workforce capacity and official early psychiatric readmission indicators in Italy: a longitudinal ecological panel study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Workforce counts and early-readmission indicators often appear side by side in health-system dashboards, encouraging the assumption that more staff should accompany fewer returns to hospital. We examined whether annual variation in previous-year medical-nursing headcount density was associated with Italy's official provider-side indicators of unplanned readmission within 30 days after eligible ordinary psychiatric discharges from public psychiatric wards and, secondarily, within 7 days.

METHODS: Using national mental-health, hospital-discharge and population data, we assembled a retrospective 2015-2024 panel of 21 Italian territorial units (210 unit-years). Exposure was medical and nursing headcount at the end of the preceding year per 100,000 adults. We modelled 30-day readmission counts using Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) with an eligible-discharge offset and territorial-unit and year fixed effects. Primary inference used a restricted wild cluster score bootstrap with 9,999 Rademacher draws and 21 clusters. Secondary and sensitivity analyses were prespecified, source blanks were not imputed, and analytical materials and scripts are openly archived.

RESULTS: Outcome counts and eligible-discharge denominators were complete for all 210 observations; exposure was available for 205. The incidence rate ratio (IRR) per 10 additional medical-nursing staff per 100,000 adults was 1.006 (95% CI 0.934-1.034; p = 0.8095), compatible with relative changes from a 6.6% reduction to a 3.4% increase. Across linear PPML sensitivity analyses, IRRs ranged from 0.995 to 1.042, with all confidence intervals including 1. Across 31 leave-one-unit or leave-one-year-out re-estimates, IRRs ranged from 0.974 to 1.044, and every confidence interval included 1. The nonlinearity test gave p = 0.8572. The 7-day IRR was 1.032 (95% CI 0.929-1.075; p = 0.6743), while the weighted linear model estimated +0.215 percentage points (95% CI -1.159 to +0.704; p = 0.7203).

CONCLUSIONS: The data did not provide evidence of a detectable longitudinal ecological association between year-to-year variation in medical-nursing headcount density and the official 30-day readmission indicator. This does not imply that workforce is unimportant: headcount does not capture full-time-equivalent availability, deployment or transition processes, and the provider-side design cannot support patient-level or causal inference. Territorial policy should combine adequate resources with a whole-system view of their deployment, post-discharge organisation, and the social, economic and health context in which care is delivered.

articles.title: Semaglutide modulates explore/exploit decision-making in major depressive disorder: A randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Explore/exploit decision-making is a crucial component of motivated behavior. Explore/exploit behaviors are related to disparate cognitive and reward-related functions and have been implicated in multiple neuropsychiatric conditions, including major depressive disorder (MDD). Several mediators of explore/exploit decision-making have been proposed; metabolic mechanisms have been theorized to potentially affect its underlying processes. Here, we examined the effects of a GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), semaglutide, on explore/exploit behavior in patients with MDD, using a four-armed restless bandit task.

METHODS: In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, 72 participants with MDD were randomized either to oral semaglutide (n = 35) or placebo (n = 37), and completed the bandit task at baseline and following 16 weeks of treatment. Explore/exploit decision-making was assessed using computational modeling of choice behavior, with a trial-by-trial reinforcement-learning model.

RESULTS: Treatment with semaglutide resulted in increased exploitation (i.e. choosing the option with the highest expected reward) (Average Treatment Effect [ATE] = 0.0242, p < 0.001), directed exploration (i.e. exploring a choice with higher uncertainty) (ATE = 0.0619, p = 0.013), and perseveration (i.e. the value-independent tendency to repeat the previous action) (ATE = 0.3017, p = 0.013). These effects were moderated by, but ultimately independent of, baseline characteristics and weight loss during the trial.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with semaglutide modulated explore/exploit behaviors in patients with MDD. These results highlight the role of metabolic mechanisms in decision-making processes in MDD and expand knowledge of the potential neuropsychiatric effects of GLP-1RAs.

articles.title: Prevalence of systemic lupus erythematosus in New Zealand primary care: A retrospective descriptive study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune condition with a high level of morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs. In New Zealand prevalence of the condition has been increasing over time, although studies to date are based on national administrative datasets or hospital records.ObjectiveWe aimed to estimate the prevalence of SLE based on primary care medical records in New Zealand and to evaluate the differences in age, gender and ethnicity.MethodsPotential SLE cases were identified through electronic primary care records from 1 January 2000 to 20 March 2024. All records were manually reviewed to identify the diagnosis based on 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria. Prevalence was based on definite and probable cases.ResultsSixty-eight SLE cases were identified (55 definite, 6 probable, 7 possible) from a total practice population of 96,348. The crude prevalence of SLE estimated using primary care records was 63.3 per 100,000 people in 2024. The World Health Organization age-standardised prevalence was 52.9 per 100,000 people in 2024. SLE prevalence generally increased with advancing age. Women were five times more likely than men to have SLE (RR 5.36, 95% CI 2.63 - 10.93. Pacific people had the highest age-standardised prevalence of SLE (94.1), followed by Asian (58.7), European/Others (48.3) and Māori (42.9 per 100,000).ConclusionThe use of primary care medical records builds on national studies based primarily on administrative databases. Prevalence of SLE is highest in the elderly (>85 years), females and Pacific people based on primary care data in New Zealand.

articles.title: Antenatally detected right ventricular outflow tract aneurysm with neonatal ventricular arrhythmia.
articles.abstract: A large right ventricular outflow tract aneurysm in a fetus was incidentally detected during a routine third-trimester ultrasound of a 30-year-old pregnant woman. The pregnancy itself was otherwise uneventful, and the infant was delivered at term. Postnatal echocardiography confirmed the presence of the right ventricular outflow tract aneurysm. Initially, the neonate was stable; however, he developed frequent ventricular premature complexes, with electrocardiographic features indicating a right ventricular outflow tract origin. Early initiation of amiodarone therapy led to a prompt resolution of the arrhythmia. The infant remained stable and was discharged with plans for close follow-up. This case adds to the limited literature on congenital right ventricular outflow tract aneurysms detected antenatally and provides valuable insight into their potential to cause arrhythmias in early life.

articles.title: High temperature-attributable chronic kidney disease burden in China, 1990-2023: temporal trends, population aging as the dominant driver, and projections to 2036.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient temperatures have risen in China over recent decades, but the long-term disease burden of chronic kidney disease (CKD) estimated to be attributable to high temperature has not been systematically quantified. We aimed to estimate this burden from 1990 to 2023 and project trends to 2036.

METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, we extracted deaths, DALYs, age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR) for high temperature-attributable CKD in China. Joinpoint regression and estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) analyses assessed temporal trends. Decomposition analysis identified drivers of DALY changes. Bayesian age-period-cohort models projected the burden to 2036.

RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, ASMR increased from 0.04 to 0.08 per 100,000, and ASDR rose from 1.42 to 1.57 per 100,000. Joinpoint regression revealed an accelerating trend (APC: 0.17% for ASDR, 1.63% for ASMR). EAPC analysis showed divergent sex-specific trends. Population aging was the primary driver of DALY increases, with other factors having offsetting effects. By 2036, total deaths are projected to reach 1,261 (95% CrI: 800-1,986), a 17.1% increase from 2023.

CONCLUSION: The burden of high temperature-attributable CKD in China has increased over three decades and is projected to continue rising. Elderly males are the most vulnerable group, and targeted interventions are urgently needed.

articles.title: Dysregulation of Growth Hormone Axis after Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Bariatric metabolic surgery has potent effects on glucose metabolism, with increases in insulin sensitivity and insulin secretion contributing to both improved glycemia and/or remission of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and development of hypoglycemia (post-bariatric hypoglycemia, PBH). Previous studies suggest GH secretion and/or action are altered after bariatric surgery and may mediate early post-surgical improvements in glycemic control. Given the importance of GH signaling in glucose metabolism, we hypothesized that reductions in GH signaling and/or action could also contribute to PBH.

OBJECTIVE: Assessment of GH responses to two distinct stimuli: (1) experimental hypoglycemia induced by hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemic clamp and (2) glucagon stimulation.

SETTING: Academic medical center.

PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) with PBH (n=20), without hypoglycemia (n=20), and weight-matched non-surgical controls (n=10).

MAIN OUTCOMES: GH responses were assessed (1) during experimental hypoglycemia and (2) after glucagon stimulation. Plasma GH receptor (GHR) and insulin-like growth factors and binding proteins were also measured.

RESULTS: Glucagon-stimulated GH levels were 5-6 times higher in both post-RYGB groups vs. controls at 120 minutes: control: 481±137 pg/ml; RYGB non-hypo 2521 ± 678 pg/ml; PBH: 3018 ±137pg/ml (control vs RYGB non-hypo p=0.02; control vs PBH; p=0.005). In contrast, PBH participants showed lower GH responses to experimental hypoglycemia. Additionally, plasma GHR and IGF-1 levels were reduced in PBH vs. controls.

CONCLUSIONS: We find that plasma GH response to 2 distinct experimental stimuli differed in participants with a history of bariatric surgery. However, these patterns did not differ in those with and without PBH. Further studies will be required to determine if tissue-level alterations in GH action contribute to improved glycemic control after bariatric surgery.

articles.title: Rapid Cycle Deliberate Practice of Pediatric Emergencies Education for Pharmacists (PEEPs).
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the development and implementation of Pediatric Emergencies Education for Pharmacists (PEEPs), a rapid-cycle deliberate practice curriculum designed to prepare inpatient pharmacists for medication-related responsibilities during pediatric emergency responses.

SUMMARY: PEEPs is a two-hour, in-person program delivered to pairs or triads of pharmacists. After a prebrief, orientation, and warm-up scenario, participants complete approximately 15 rapid practice cycles involving septic shock, severe hypoglycemia, status epilepticus, and supraventricular tachycardia. Scenarios use varied patient ages and weights so participants repeatedly identify essential patient information, select and prepare weight-based medications, use institution-specific dosing resources, and communicate medication plans. The simulation environment leverages low-fidelity pediatric models and emphasizes focus on reproduction of the local medication-use workflow, including online ordering platforms and simulated pediatric crash carts that are one for one replicas of the clinically facing tools. Six recurring "always behaviors" reinforce role identification, allergy and weight verification, recognition of the applicable emergency algorithm, anticipation of medication and vascular-access needs, familiarity with cart contents, and closed-loop communication. Scenarios are paused when a critical action is omitted or performed incorrectly; the facilitator provides concise feedback, rewinds the scenario, and allows immediate repetition. PEEPs concludes in a summative debrief which reinforces the key learning objectives and engages the learner to actively reflect on the experience, optimizing knowledge and skill retention.

CONCLUSION: PEEPs provides a reproducible, resource-conscious framework for pharmacist-specific pediatric emergency training. Its emphasis on repeated medication preparation, institution-specific workflow, and immediate corrective practice may help health systems develop pharmacist readiness for high-acuity pediatric events; clinical effects require separate evaluation.

articles.title: Chlorine Gas Exposure: Clinical Course, Outcomes, and Lessons Learned Following a Mass-Exposure Incident in Oman.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical manifestations of acute chlorine gas exposure and evaluate recovery outcomes at 48 hours and 14 days post-exposure.

METHODS: Retrospective observational case series of 31 patients exposed to chlorine gas during a mass incident in Sohar, Oman. Information regarding clinical presentation, treatment outcomes, and post-treatment complications was collected using a structured data collection tool to ensure consistency and accuracy during data extraction. Data analysis was performed using IBM SPSS v31.

RESULTS: Thirty-one patients presented to the study site and were included in the analysis. All were male with a mean age of 32.3 ± 9.4 years. At presentation, 90.3% of patients were symptomatic, with respiratory manifestations being the most reported symptoms. Eight patients (25.8%) required admission, including 3 admitted to the intensive care unit. At 48-hour follow-up, 18 (58.1%) remained symptomatic. Nine of 29 patients who attended follow-up on day 14 reported persistent symptoms, most commonly cough. No fatalities occurred.

CONCLUSION: This study reports on the clinical course of acute chlorine exposure, highlighting that recovery often exceeds 2 weeks. Findings underscore the need for standardized clinical management, public awareness, and more rigorous industrial safety oversight to mitigate future chemical surge impacts.

articles.title: Diabetes, stone composition, and renal function in a large cohort of patients with nephrolithiasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrolithiasis is linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetic patients may be at higher risk for renal decline. However, the interaction of diabetes, stone composition, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectory in patients with nephrolithiasis remains underexplored, particularly in community-based populations.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of adult stone formers with a urinary stone composition analysis on file, diabetes status and stone composition were extracted from electronic records of a large health maintenance organization. Longitudinal eGFR measurements assessed renal function decline, and the effects of stone type, diabetes, and recurrent stone events on eGFR trajectory were evaluated.

RESULTS: This study included 6,771 stone formers; 1,543 (23%) had diabetes. Diabetic patients had a significantly higher prevalence of uric-acid stones (18.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.0001). Baseline eGFR differed robustly by stone type and diabetes status. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension, the rate of eGFR decline did not differ significantly by diabetes status within either the calcium-oxalate nor uric-acid subtype. Recurrent stone formers had greater renal function loss, while socioeconomic status had limited impact on eGFR change.

CONCLUSION: Diabetic and non-diabetic stone formers show distinct baseline eGFR profiles that differ by stone composition, and diabetes was strongly associated with uric-acid stone formation; however, diabetes was not associated with an accelerated rate of eGFR decline once adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension. These findings support baseline risk stratification, rather than an accelerated-decline phenotype, as the key actionable insight for diabetic stone formers.

articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Interventional paediatric echocardiography: a call to action for training, competency, and sustainable practice standards.
Multimodal Atrial Cardiomyopathy Phenotypes for Risk Stratification in Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM) is highly prevalent in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), even in the presence of preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Structural, functional, and electrical atrial remodeling may differentially influence outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), although their integrated prognostic role remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To assess whether multimodal markers of AtCM identify distinct risk phenotypes associated with adverse outcomes after TAVI in patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 122 consecutive patients with severe AS, preserved LVEF, and sinus rhythm undergoing TAVI. Structural/functional AtCM (Echo-AtCM Risk) was assessed using indexed left atrial volume (LAVI) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr), whereas electrical AtCM (ECG-AtCM Risk) was defined according to P-wave duration and morphology. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and new-onset AF. Prognostic associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression analyses.

RESULTS: Mean age was 82.3±5.6 years. High Echo-Risk was present in 54.1% of patients and High ECG-Risk in 19.7%. During a median follow-up of 13.6 months, the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization occurred in 39 patients (32.0%), while new-onset AF developed in 17 (13.9%). High Echo-Risk independently predicted death/HF hospitalization (HR 4.17, p=0.008), whereas High ECG-Risk independently predicted incident AF (HR 3.07, p=0.034). Combined profiling identified distinct phenotypes: High Echo/Low ECG predicted HF/death (HR 4.86, p=0.008), Low Echo/High ECG predicted AF (HR 8.99, p=0.004), and combined High Echo/High ECG conferred the worst prognosis (HR 6.23, p=0.015).

CONCLUSIONS: Structural, functional, and electrical AtCM represent complementary domains with distinct prognostic implications in AS patients undergoing TAVI. Their integration may refine post-TAVI risk stratification; these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical management can be guided by AtCM phenotype.Keywords: Atrial cardiomyopathy; Aortic stenosis; TAVI; Left atrial strain; Heart failure; Atrial fibrillation.

articles.title: The emerging role of orbital atherectomy in the management of heavily calcified lesions in percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract: Severe coronary calcification is a challenge to optimal percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Adequate lesion preparation is essential to achieve appropriate stent expansion and improve long-term outcomes. Recently, orbital atherectomy (OA) has emerged as an important tool for calcium modification, offering a unique mechanism of action based on centrifugal sanding and differential cutting. This review summarizes the contemporary evidence supporting OA in heavily calcified coronary disease, compares it to other established calcium modification strategies, and highlights practical scenarios where OA offers distinctive advantages. Several calcium algorithms exist, detailing start points according to balloon crossability and stepwise escalation guided by intravascular imaging. Orbital atherectomy has recently become available across centers in Europe and the United Kingdom, providing an alternative calcium‑debulking toolkit that is of particular use in some indications, with advantages over other techniques. In this review, we look at the emerging role of OA in calcified lesions, with a critical appraisal of the data and highlighting its utility drawing examples from the published literature and our center's experience.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of latent tuberculosis infection testing and treatment for elderly individuals with pulmonary fibrosis lesions in rural communities in China.
articles.abstract: Elderly individuals with pulmonary fibrosis lesions and latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) in rural China are high-risk for active tuberculosis (TB), and tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) is effective for this group. This study used decision tree-Markov model comparing: targeted CXR_LTBI_6-week H2P2 (6-week rifapentine-isoniazid) and CXR_LTBI_6H (6-month isoniazid) for individuals with chest X-ray (CXR)-detected pulmonary fibrosis lesions and subsequent LTBI positivity, versus non-targeted LTBI_6-week H2P2 and LTBI_6H for elderly LTBI-positive individuals, validated via scenario and sensitivity analyses. Over 5 and 20 year horizons among simulated cohort of 10,000 individuals aged ≥65 years, CXR_LTBI_6-week H₂P₂ served as the only strategy on the cost-effectiveness frontier, with baseline costs of $73,122.83 and $166,058.33, total QALYs of 52,024.52 and 116,650.90, and prevented active TB cases of 40 and 63 respectively. Compared with this strategy, all other strategies were absolutely dominated, presenting fewer prevented active TB cases (1-30), reduced QALYs (0.55-38.39) and elevated total costs ($32,948.71-$1,845,680.24) with CXR_LTBI_6H brought the minimum health loss (0.55 lost QALYs) and cost increment ($32,948.71) among all dominated options. Two scenario analyses regarding the waning long-term protective efficacy of 6-week H2P2 further verified the sustained cost-effectiveness dominance of CXR_LTBI_6-week H2P2. One-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses consistently confirmed that CXR_LTBI_6-week H2P2 remained the most robust cost-saving strategy regardless of parameter variation and model uncertainty. In conclusion, CXR-guided LTBI TPT is cost-effective among rural elderly Chinese with pulmonary fibrosis lesions, with the 6-week H2P2 regimen as the optimal preventive strategy.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided cyanoacrylate embolization of refluxing tributaries during truncal cyanoacrylate closure (SLICE): Technique description and a proof-of-concept feasibility study.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTruncal cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) does not treat refluxing tributary varicosities. We describe Side-branch Local Injection of Cyanoacrylate Embolization (SLICE) - ultrasound-guided injection of the VenaSeal adhesive into refluxing tributaries during truncal CAC - and assess its technical feasibility and periprocedural safety.MethodsSingle-center retrospective review of 32 consecutive patients (49 limbs, 58 truncal veins) treated by truncal CAC between September 2024 and December 2025; SLICE was performed in 14. The primary endpoint was technical success, defined as the absence of reflux within an injected tributary on the first postoperative duplex study. Secondary endpoints included 3-month durability, truncal occlusion, and adverse events.Results22 refluxing tributaries were injected; all were epifascial, at a median depth of 4.0 mm (range 1.2-9.6). A median of four dispenser trigger pulls was used per site (range 3-8); the series was underpowered to relate pull count to diameter (Spearman rho -0.16, p = 0.50). Technical success was 21/22 (95%; 95% confidence interval 77.2-99.9) initially and 19/20 (95%; 75.1-99.9) at 3 months. On 3-month computed tomography (CT), 14 of 17 evaluable injected tributaries were occluded whereas 16 of 17 were free of reflux: anatomical occlusion lagged behind hemodynamic success. Truncal occlusion was preserved (30/30 at 1 week; 26/27 at 3 months). There was no phlebitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or adhesive removal. Hyperpigmentation occurred in 3/14 patients, all with an injection <2 mm below the skin; two mild delayed hypersensitivity reactions occurred, both over the truncal rather than an injected site. One patient (7%) required re-intervention.ConclusionsSLICE is technically feasible and reproducible within a narrow range of adhesive delivery, with no adhesive-related complication at an injected site in this small series with short follow-up. Prospective comparative evaluation with patient-centered endpoints is required before efficacy can be claimed.

articles.title: De Novo Design of a TROP-2-Targeting Peptide PET Tracer via AI-Guided Binding Interface Mimicry.
articles.abstract: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed across a range of epithelial malignancies, yet its clinical assessment still relies largely on invasive immunohistochemical analysis of biopsied tissues. In this study, we employed the PepMimic artificial intelligence platform to de novo design a TROP-2-targeting peptide, TR23, via binding interface mimicry, which was subsequently conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 68Ga to yield the peptide-based PET probe [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23. The tracer bound TROP-2 with nanomolar affinity (KD = 26.8 nM), showed selective cellular uptake in TROP-2-positive cells, and exhibited high radiochemical purity (>95%) with excellent stability in saline and serum. Micro-PET/CT imaging in pancreatic (BxPC-3), prostate (PC3), and thyroid (BCPAP) xenograft models revealed rapid, specific tumor accumulation with high contrast and low background uptake, while competitive blocking studies with excess unlabeled TR23 substantially suppressed tumor uptake, confirming receptor-mediated specificity. Quantitative analysis further demonstrated strong positive correlations between SUVmax and TROP-2 expression levels verified by immunohistochemistry across all three tumor types. Collectively, these findings establish [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23 as a promising peptide-based PET tracer for rapid, specific, and quantitative imaging of TROP-2-positive tumors, and highlight the PepMimic-enabled strategy as a versatile platform for peptide-based probe discovery, supporting the translational potential of this tracer as a pan-cancer diagnostic agent for precision molecular imaging.

articles.title: Bone-Targeting Antibodies for Skeletal Precision Therapy.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies have transformed the treatment of cancer, inflammation, infection, and disorders of bone biology by recognizing disease-associated molecular targets with high specificity. However, achieving therapeutically effective antibody concentrations at the site of disease remains a major challenge, as systemic administration does not inherently result in efficient tissue-specific delivery. Bone is a particularly demanding destination because mineralized matrix, limited vascular access, marrow complexity, and active remodeling can restrict local antibody exposure. Recent advances in bone-targeting antibody design point to a powerful reframing in which antibodies can be engineered not only for antigen specificity but also for tissue specificity. By attaching hydroxyapatite-binding motifs such as bisphosphonates or acidic peptides, antibodies can be endowed with bone-homing capabilities. The efficacy of this strategy has now been validated across multiple preclinical disease models, including breast cancer bone metastasis and osteoporosis-related bone loss. The next challenge is to define how affinity, valency, conjugation site, circulation time, and release should be tuned for each skeletal disease.

articles.title: Athletes and Medical Staff in Elite Contact Sports: a Quantitative Analysis of Use, Knowledge, and Attitudes Regarding Cannabinoids.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cannabis use among elite contact sport athletes increases with legal reform and commercial availability. Limited education in cannabinoid pharmacology, use, and risk persists among athletes and medical staff, fostering stigma and reducing evidence-based guidance and communication.

HYPOTHESIS: Athletes use cannabis but perceive stigma and discomfort discussing cannabis with medical staff.

STUDY DESIGN: Quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional surveys.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4.

METHODS: Two anonymous online surveys were administered to elite and professional contact sport athletes (Canada, United States, Australia) and medical and training staff (February 2023 to July 2024). Descriptive statistics assessed demographics, use patterns, knowledge, education needs, attitudes, stigma, communication, and league policies.

RESULTS: A total of 166 athletes (89.7% male, 35.2% aged 18-23 years) and 64 medical staff (physicians, athletic therapists, strength and conditioning coaches, etc) responded. Knowledge (pharmacology, interactions, dosing) was low. Overall, 56% of athletes currently used cannabinoids (81% having ever used), but only 21.7% knew the endocannabinoid system and 67.4% were unfamiliar with therapeutic dosing. Among medical staff, 59.5% were unfamiliar with mechanisms, only 14% were familiar with dosing protocols, and 71.4% lacked confidence in making treatment plans. Of the athletes, 86.5% believed cannabis had therapeutic value, 72.3% wanted education, and 74.1% favored qualified scientists as instructors. Of the medical staff, 79.5% reported strong educational need, with 100% of staff desiring athlete-specific cannabinoid education. Stigma and communication barriers were substantial: 81.3% of athletes perceived public stigma, 66.1% perceived staff stigma, and only 21.4% felt comfortable discussing cannabis with medical staff. Staff believed athletes would be honest if approached; however, <50% believed athletes trusted them enough to start the conversation. Both athletes and medical staff categorized cannabinoids as supplements or medications (unlike street drugs) and both supported legalization and a revision and update on league cannabis policies.

CONCLUSION: Athletes and medical staff exhibit parallel knowledge gaps and strong educational needs amid high interest, use, and significant communication barriers. Evidence-informed education and stigma-reducing strategies are urgently needed.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Athletes increasingly use cannabinoids for pain, sleep, and recovery, while medical staff report insufficient training and low confidence. System-level education, communication, and policy updates may improve safety, decision-making, and trust.

articles.title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
articles.abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

articles.title: Clinical effects of third doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines among hemodialysis patients: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
authors: Korean Society of Nephrology Disaster Preparedness and Response Committee
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the effectiveness of third-dose messenger RNA (mRNA) coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination during the Omicron-dominant period in Asian hemodialysis (HD) patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of a third mRNA vaccine dose against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, hospitalization, and mortality in Korean HD patients.

METHODS: Using the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency-National Health Insurance Service database, we conducted a nationwide cohort study of HD patients aged ≥18 years who received two or three doses of BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273 before January 16, 2022. Study outcomes were SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and death. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between third-dose vaccination and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 66,389 HD patients (mean age, 65.7 ± 12.9 years; 60.5% male), 55,125 (83.0%) received three vaccine doses and 11,264 (17.0%) received two doses. Receipt of three doses was associated with a significantly lower risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-0.60). Among 17,886 patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection, third-dose vaccine recipients had a lower risk of hospitalization (aHR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.62-0.70) and 30-day mortality (aHR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30-0.41) compared with those who received two doses. Receipt of mRNA-1273 as the third dose was associated with lower observed risks of infection and hospitalization than receipt of BNT162b2.

CONCLUSION: A third dose of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was associated with lower risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and mortality among HD patients during the Omicron-dominant period. These findings support the clinical importance of booster vaccination in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Association of alkaline phosphatase with mortality in patients on peritoneal dialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) experience high mortality rates, necessitating the establishment of reliable prognostic markers. Although serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is routinely measured while assessing chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder, its clinical relevance for mortality risk in patients undergoing PD has not been fully established.

METHODS: Using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, this retrospective cohort study examined the association between baseline ALP levels and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in 1,108 patients with ESKD who newly initiated PD between 2000 and 2020.

RESULTS: The median ALP level of the overall cohort was 76.0 IU/L (interquartile range, 60.0-95.3 IU/L). The mean age of the patients was 60.6 years (standard deviation [SD], 14.4 years), and 55.8% were male. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years, a 1-SD increase in ALP level was significantly associated with a 23% and 64% higher risk of all-cause mortality (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.38) and cardiovascular mortality (95% CI, 1.21-2.24), respectively. The patients were stratified into tertiles (T1-T3) based on ALP level. Compared with the T1 group, the adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.11 (95% CI, 0.84-1.48) in T2 and 1.39 (95% CI, 1.05-1.85) in T3. The relationship between elevated ALP and higher risk of all-cause mortality was consistent when ALP was treated as a time-dependent variable.

CONCLUSION: Elevated ALP levels were associated with increased risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing PD.

articles.title: Index for prevention and management of intradialytic hypotension with noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring based on electrical impedance tomography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is the most common complication of hemodialysis (HD) and is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events and mortality. Current management strategies are reactive, and reliable noninvasive tools for early prediction are lacking. Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) offers noninvasive, real-time monitoring of thoracic fluid content (TFC) and cardiopulmonary parameters, potentially identifying early hemodynamic instability preceding IDH.

METHODS: We enrolled 18 patients with end-stage kidney disease and frequent IDH and monitored 73 HD sessions using a 16-channel EIT system (AirTom) and a noninvasive finger-cuff hemodynamic monitoring system (ClearSight). IDH was defined as a systolic blood pressure (SBP) drop ≥20 mmHg from baseline (IDH1) or an absolute SBP <100 mmHg (IDH2). Measured parameters included TFC, stroke volume (SV), cardiac output, and other hemodynamic indices. Interventions for IDH were applied in a fixed sequence: applying cooled dialysate, passive leg raising, ultrafiltration (UF) reduction, and dialysate bolus infusion.

RESULTS: A total of 32 IDH1 and 31 IDH2 events were observed. TFC declined progressively during HD and correlated with overhydration (R2 = 0.71). In the representative time-point analysis, SV showed the greatest pre-event decrease before both IDH1 and IDH2 events, occurring 6-10 minutes before hypotension onset. Interventions for IDH elicited distinct TFC and SV responses, with dialysate bolus infusion producing the largest increase in SV.

CONCLUSION: A decline in SV precedes IDH onset and may serve as an early physiologic indicator of hemodynamic instability during HD. EIT-based monitoring provides real-time, noninvasive assessment of SV and IDH during HD and may facilitate earlier intervention and individualized management of IDH.

articles.title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
articles.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.

METHODS: Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

articles.title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

articles.title: Saxagliptin Attenuates Thioacetamide-Induced Liver Fibrosis in Rats in Association with Changes in SIRT1/Nrf2/HO-1 Signaling, Oxidative Stress, and Apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Currently, no universally effective treatment exists to stop or reverse the development of liver fibrosis. Saxagliptin (SAX), a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor, has demonstrated extra-glycemic benefits, including anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic properties, but its role in hepatic fibrogenesis has not been characterized. This study examined the protective potential and underlying mechanisms of saxagliptin against thioacetamide (TAA)-induced hepatic fibrogenesis in rats.

METHODS: Twenty-four male Wistar rats were randomly allocated to four groups: control, TAA-induced fibrosis, TAA + saxagliptin (5 mg/kg), and TAA + saxagliptin (10 mg/kg). Biochemical, molecular, and histopathological analyses were conducted to assess liver injury, lipid profile, oxidative stress, inflammatory and fibrotic markers, apoptosis, and key cytoprotective signaling pathways.

RESULTS: TAA induced significant liver injury, oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and fibrosis, together with suppression of SIRT1 and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways. Saxagliptin was associated with improvements in hepatotoxicity, dyslipidemia, oxidative-stress, inflammatory, apoptotic, and fibrosis-related parameters, together with increased SIRT1 and Nrf2/HO-1 protein levels. The higher dose generally produced greater numerical improvement across several endpoints. Histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses showed reduced fibrosis-related changes and α-SMA immunoreactivity, with the higher dose (10 mg/kg) associated with hepatic architecture and fibrosis scores approaching the control findings.

CONCLUSION: Saxagliptin was associated with attenuation of TAA-induced hepatic fibrosis and improvements in oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and fibrosis-related signaling. These findings are consistent with involvement of SIRT1- and Nrf2/HO-1-associated cytoprotective responses but do not establish pathway causality. Further mechanistic studies are required to determine whether these pathways are necessary for the observed effects.

articles.title: Modifications to cognitive behavioural therapies for depression and anxiety in adults with neurological disorders: A qualitative analysis of intervention protocols.
articles.abstract: Cognitive and Behavioural-based Therapies (CBT) can effectively manage symptoms of depression and anxiety. However, adults with neurological disorders (NDs) often face cognitive, physical, and social challenges that make it difficult to engage with traditional forms of these treatments. To address this, CBT protocols have been modified to better suit the needs of this population. This study analysed 41 randomized controlled trials with modified CBT-based protocols for treating symptoms of depression and/or anxiety in adults with a ND. It spanned 10 different NDs : stroke, epilepsy, migraine, Parkinson's disease, acquired brain injury, multiple sclerosis, and dementia. Content analysis identified seven main categories of modification. These were: (i) neurologically tailored information and skills; (ii) facilitation of learning and retention of information; (iii) cognitive compensatory strategies; (iv) tailoring intervention to individual needs; (v) multi-modal aids of delivery; (vi) caregiver involvement or training; (vii) flexibility of session delivery. These categories were broadly grouped into three main principles of modification: (1) content adaptation, (2) delivery enhancement and (3) caregiver involvement. These findings support the clinical implementation of CBT for adults with NDs and may guide best practices for managing common mental health difficulties in this population.

articles.title: Electrosurgical septotomy across the full spectrum of aortic dissection.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

METHODS: Retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure.

RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < 0.001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia or retrograde type A dissection.
