Thirty-day, in-hospital and overall mortality were 10%, 14% and 19%, with one fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

articles.title: Association of Antihypertensive Medications with Orthostatic Hypotension among OIder Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orthostatic hypotension (OH) is common among older adults actively prescribed hypertension pharmacotherapy. Associations between antihypertensives and OH are inconsistent, due to differences in drug classes and OH assessment protocols.

METHODS: Three supine and six standing blood pressures (BPs) were measured over 6 minutes, timed to initiate immediately (0 minutes) and 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 minutes after standing. OH was defined as a drop of systolic/diastolic BP ≥ 20/10 mmHg upon standing from the supine position. OH phenotypes were initial (immediately after standing), early (within 3 minutes), late (after 3 minutes), and sustained (during 6 minutes of standing). Participants were asked about orthostatic symptoms experienced during OH assessment. We investigated associations of antihypertensive classes with OH phenotypes and orthostatic symptoms via multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 863 participants (mean age 84 years), 41% had initial, 24% early, 18% late, and 17% sustained OH; 81% used antihypertensive medications. First-line antihypertensives (renin angiotensin aldosterone system blockers, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and thiazide diuretics) were not associated with OH or orthostatic symptoms. Among non-first-line, alpha blockers were significantly associated with initial OH (OR 1.80, 95%CI 1.07, 3.01) and orthostatic symptoms during postural change (OR 2.64, 95%CI 1.34, 5.23), whereas combined alpha-beta blockers were significantly associated with early, late, or sustained OH (2.24 [1.15, 4.37], 2.50 [1.21, 5.17], 2.99 [1.41, 6.30], respectively) and experienced symptoms while standing (3.08 [1.10, 8.65]).

CONCLUSIONS: First-line antihypertensives are not associated with OH among older adults, which does not support their discontinuation in the setting of non-neurogenic OH.

articles.title: Association between dietary inflammatory index and mortality in adults with chronic kidney disease: a retrospective study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence and mortality of chronic kidney disease (CKD) are high. Systemic inflammation often occurs in patients with CKD and limits overall survival. The dietary inflammatory index (DII), developed to assess the inflammatory potential of diet, may be an underrecognized risk factor for CKD mortality.

METHODS: This study included 7,113 adult participants from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 2005 and 2018. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to assess the association between DII scores and mortality in patients with CKD, with hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to evaluate non-linear associations, whereas subgroup and mediation analyses explored potential effect modifications and mediation effects.

RESULTS: The all-cause mortality rate among patients with CKD was 19.3%. After full adjustment (model 3), the highest DII quartile showed a 23% higher mortality risk (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.07-1.42; Ptrend<0.001) compared with the lowest quartile. RCS confirmed a linear dose-response relationship (Poverall<0.001, Pnon-linear=0.549). No associations were observed for cardiovascular or malignant tumor mortality. The effect of DII scores on all-cause mortality was more pronounced in patients with lower body weight.

CONCLUSION: Higher DII scores are associated with elevated all-cause mortality in patients with CKD, supporting the potential benefit of anti-inflammatory diets.

articles.title: Natural products shape microbial ecology and disease in the cystic fibrosis airway.
articles.abstract: Covering up to 2026Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-shortening autosomal recessive genetic disorder caused by mutation in the gene encoding the CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR). Dysfunction in CFTR leads to the accumulation of thick and dehydrated mucus in the respiratory tract, which serves as a substrate for a complex microbiota that includes commensal oral and respiratory bacteria and opportunistic pathogenic bacteria and fungi. During chronic infections, these microbes persist in the airways and contribute to progressive lung tissue damage, ultimately leading to respiratory failure and premature death. Within this environment, microbes synthesize a diverse repertoire of natural products, including antimicrobials, siderophores and other metallophores, signaling molecules, toxins, and other virulence factors. In this review, we thoroughly discuss natural products produced by members of the CF airway microbiota, primarily the bacterial pathogens Burkholderia spp., Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus and the fungal pathogens Aspergillus fumigatus and Scedosporium spp. When known, we describe the biosynthesis and roles of these natural products in microbial persistence, interspecies interactions, and virulence in the CF airway. When these roles are unknown, we infer potential roles based on evidence from the literature in different disease contexts. Finally, we briefly highlight natural products produced by the CF microbiota as novel sources for developing new antimicrobials and as drug targets to treat disease.

articles.title: Commercial and Novel Drug-Loaded Coatings with Anticoagulant and/or Antibacterial Functions for Clinical Applications.
articles.abstract: Drug-loaded coatings significantly improve the bioactivities of multiple medical devices. The most widespread applications are assembling anticoagulant coatings on blood-contacting medical devices to enhance blood compatibility and applying antibacterial coatings to prevent device-induced infection. Notably, a vicious cycle between bacterial infection and thrombosis may result in deterioration of condition and even lead to treatment failure. Thrombosis caused by blood incompatibility of medical devices provides niduses for bacterial colonization, whereas bacterial endotoxins accelerate thrombosis by activating platelets. In some situations, the interactional process can also trigger inflammatory responses and calcification processes. Therefore, the demands for anticoagulant and antibacterial are necessary and mutually influenced. This review presents a summary of current commercial drug-loaded anticoagulant coatings and a detailed report on novel drug-loaded coatings with anticoagulant and/or antibacterial effects. We highlight the synthesis and assembly techniques, drug-release duration, and biofunctional behavior of referenced coatings. Based on careful comparison and comprehensive summary of the state-of-the-art literature, this review reveals the difficulties in large-scale production of the emerging coatings and the functional differences compared to the existing commercial coatings, and predicts the general process for manufacturing and commercialization.

articles.title: Renal artery imaging through long-term follow-up after radiofrequency renal denervation: Results from the SPYRAL Clinical Program.
articles.abstract: Background: Renal denervation (RDN) safely reduces blood pressure (BP) in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. A potential long-term concern is the development of de novo renal artery stenosis (RAS) secondary to vascular injury. This study assesses the long-term vascular safety and incidence of RAS in patients treated with radiofrequency RDN from the SPYRAL HTN-OFF MED and -ON MED trials. Patients and methods: All patients underwent renal angiograms for assessment of the renal anatomy prior to randomization. Patients with RAS >50% were excluded from enrollment. At long-term follow-up (439+/-288 days), patients underwent duplex ultrasound imaging (DUS), computerized tomography angiography (CTA), and/or magnetic resonance angiography (MRA). Independent core labs evaluated all images. Clinically significant RAS was predefined as a stenosis ≥70%, confirmed by angiography. Results: A total of 610 patients were treated with RDN in the SPYRAL trials. At least one imaging modality was performed in 557 of the 610 patients (91%): 329 patients underwent DUS imaging, 230 underwent CTA, 148 underwent MRA, and 15 underwent renal angiography. With one possible exception, no clinically significant RAS was detected. No patients had renal artery reintervention. The proportion of images fulfilling pre-specified criteria for technical adequacy by the core lab was 100% (angiography), 87.5% (DUS), 80.6% (CTA), and 32.4% MRA. Conclusions: RF RDN appears to be safe, without confirmed vascular injury or RAS among 557 patients who had long-term imaging. Diagnostic utility of imaging modalities determined by specific criteria for technical adequacy for core lab evaluation was lowest with MRA and highest with DUS.

articles.title: Role of nurse leadership in supporting sustainable healthcare and organisational change: a case study.
articles.abstract: Nurse leaders have an important role in supporting the NHS to achieve its 'net zero' ambitions, yet sustainability initiatives are often perceived as challenging to balance with operational pressures, patient safety and infection prevention and control (IPC) requirements. This article presents a nurse-led case study from Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, England, describing the replacement of single-use pulp kidney dishes with reusable alternatives using a Sustainable Quality Improvement (SusQI) approach. Implemented in partnership with IPC, procurement and operational teams, the project delivered measurable environmental and financial benefits while maintaining compliance with IPC standards. Key lessons include the value of visible nurse leadership, interdisciplinary collaboration and embedding sustainability in existing governance and quality improvement processes. The case demonstrates how nurse-led sustainability initiatives can reduce environmental impact and support organisational change while maintaining safe, high-quality care.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Urinary Clusterin for Early Detection of Diabetic Kidney Disease in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Case-Control Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary Clusterin, a glycoprotein linked to oxidative stress and tubular injury, is being evaluated as a more sensitive biomarker for diabetic kidney disease (DKD). This study aims to assess the role of Clusterin in the early detection and prognostication of diabetic kidney disease in children with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM), addressing a critical gap in pediatric clinical data.

METHODS: This case-control study at Beni-Suef University compared 50 children with T1DM (duration ≥5 years) to 40 healthy controls. Assessments included Body Mass Index (BMI), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lipid profiles. Urinary Clusterin was measured using Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). A Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to determine the diagnostic performance of urinary Clusterin in detecting diabetic nephropathy.

RESULTS: Diabetic cases exhibited significantly higher levels of AST, cholesterol, triglycerides, and serum creatinine compared to the control group. The urinary profile revealed significantly elevated urinary creatinine, albumin, and albumin-to-creatinine ratios in cases, with urinary clusterin levels being significantly higher in children with diabetes (49.7 vs. 32.3 pg/mL, p<0.001) than in healthy controls. Within the case group, urinary clusterin significantly correlated with ALT, serum creatinine, and triglycerides, although no significant associations were found with age, BMI, or HbA1c. At a cutoff value of 37.6 pg/mL, urinary clusterin is a highly effective marker for early detection of diabetic nephropathy with an 80% sensitivity, and 90% specificity.

CONCLUSION: Urinary clusterin is a potential non-invasive biomarker for early diabetic nephropathy in children with T1DM, outperforming traditional measures and offering a promising tool for earlier screening and improved clinical management.

articles.title: Anatomic Sinus Thrombosis Post-TAVR Visualized by TEE: A Treatable Cause of Myocardial Injury.
Clinical and radiological outcomes of primary semi-constrained total elbow arthroplasty at 10-year mean follow-up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term clinical and radiological outcomes in patients undergoing semi-constrained total elbow arthroplasty (TEA). Postoperative complications and implant survival rates were also investigated.

METHODS: Of 68 patients who underwent primary semi-constrained TEA, data from 62 with a minimum follow-up of 5 years were analyzed. The mean follow-up duration was 117.1 months (range, 60-246 months). Forty-one patients had posttraumatic conditions, 11 had rheumatoid arthritis, and 10 had osteoarthritis. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS) and Oxford Elbow Score (OES), whereas radiological outcomes were analyzed using radiolucent lines and bushing wear. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to determine the implant survival rate.

RESULTS: At the final follow-up, the MEPS and OES were 88.2 (range, 55-100) and 31.6 (range, 22-42), respectively. Radiolucency of type 3 or 4 was observed on the humeral side in four patients and on the ulnar side in three patients. Grade 1 and 2 bushing wear was present in seven and three patients, respectively. The total complication rate was 25.8% (16/62), and the reoperation rate was 17.7% (11/62). Four patients underwent reoperation for periprosthetic infection after previous open reduction and internal fixation for acute fractures. In addition, three patients underwent hinge system change for hinge dissociation, four sustained periprosthetic fractures, one underwent revision TEA for gross loosening, and one underwent open repair for triceps rupture. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that the 5-, 10-, and 15-year survival rates of the implants were 100%, 92.8%, and 77.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical and radiological outcomes of primary semi-constrained TEA were reasonably good at a mean 10-year follow-up. Type 3 or 4 radiolucency was observed in seven patients and complete bushing wear in three patients, while the 10-year implant survival rate was 92.8%. Level of evidence: IV.

articles.title: Atorvastatin protects cardiomyocytes from doxorubicin toxicity by modulating YAP/TAZ signaling.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent; however, its clinical efficacy is hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, which can lead to irreversible heart failure. Despite extensive research, effective strategies for preventing or mitigating DOX-induced cardiac injury remain lacking. The Hippo signaling effectors, Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), are known to regulate cardiomyocyte survival, apoptosis, and mitochondrial quality control; however, their role in protecting the heart from DOX toxicity remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether atorvastatin, a widely prescribed HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor with pleiotropic effects, attenuated DOX-induced cardiomyopathy by modulating the YAP/TAZ signaling axis. In H9c2 cardiomyocytes, DOX suppressed the expression of YAP and TAZ, leading to the downregulation of their downstream targets, Survivin and Park2, and activation of apoptotic cascades. Atorvastatin pretreatment restored YAP/TAZ expression at both mRNA and protein levels and reversed DOX-induced apoptosis. RNA interference-mediated knockdown of YAP or TAZ abolished the protective effects of atorvastatin, confirming the importance of this pathway. In a murine model of DOX cardiotoxicity, atorvastatin preserved left ventricular systolic function, reduced myocardial apoptosis and fibrosis, and restored YAP/TAZ, Survivin, and Park2 expression in the cardiac tissue. These findings suggest that atorvastatin exerts cardioprotective effects by restoring YAP/TAZ-mediated anti-apoptotic and mitochondrial quality control signaling. Our study highlights a novel mechanism via which atorvastatin mitigates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity and supports the therapeutic potential of YAP/TAZ modulation for cardioprotection.

articles.title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

articles.title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in Oncology Patients During Active Chemotherapy: A Saudi Arabian Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a recognized complication in oncology patients undergoing contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) during chemotherapy. Limited data exist on CA-AKI incidence in patients with preserved baseline renal function, particularly in Middle Eastern populations. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a retrospective analysis of 146 adult oncology patients with baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) greater than 50 mL/min/1.73 m² who underwent CECT within 45 days of chemotherapy at a tertiary cancer center in Saudi Arabia (January 2017-December 2018). CA-AKI was defined as an absolute serum creatinine increase of 0.3 mg/dL or more, or as a relative increase of more than 50% within 48 to 72 hours of contrast administration. Given the small number of events (n=2), descriptive statistics and exploratory univariate analyses were performed. RESULTS CA-AKI occurred in 2 of 146 patients (1.4%; 95% CI: 0.2%-5.0%). Mean age was 51.5±16.2 years; 58% were women. Cancer types included solid tumors (81.5%) and hematological malignancies (17.8%). The chemotherapy-to-CECT interval was shorter in patients with CA-AKI (mean: 2 days) than in patients without CA-AKI (mean: 23.3±12.8 days; P=0.02). This association is exploratory and hypothesis-generating given the extremely limited number of events. CONCLUSIONS CA-AKI incidence was relatively low (1.4%) in oncology patients with preserved baseline renal function undergoing CECT during active chemotherapy. The observed association between shorter chemotherapy-to-imaging intervals and CA-AKI requires prospective validation and should not be interpreted as a definitive causal relationship. These findings provide preliminary regional data from Saudi Arabia and underscore the need for larger, well-designed prospective studies to better characterize CA-AKI risk in this population.

articles.title: Leveraging whole-genome sequencing to manage a Streptococcus agalactiae outbreak in a neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate late-onset Group B Streptococcus (GBS) transmission dynamics in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) using whole-genome sequencing (WGS).

SETTING: A 57-bed level III NICU in Toronto, Canada.

PATIENTS: Neonates with late-onset GBS (LOGBS) identified, July 2023-February 2024.

METHODS: An outbreak management team oversaw the investigation, hygiene audits, and stakeholder communications. Canada's National Microbiology Laboratory performed WGS (Illumina) on outbreak and prior isolates. Core single nucleotide variant (SNV) phylogeny used SNVPhyl. Clinical data included age, infection type, maternal GBS status and outcome were reviewed. Three consecutive weekly point-prevalence surveys (PPS) were conducted using rectal and throat swabs.

RESULTS: In August 2023, two LOGBS cases (bacteremia and meningitis) triggered the investigation. Two more LOGBS bacteremias occurred pending WGS results. Three of the 4 isolates matched a prior early-onset (day-1) case (0 SNVs; cluster 1, serotype Ia). The fourth was 1 SNV different from a conjunctivitis case detected a week later (cluster 2, serotype V). PPS revealed 5 asymptomatic cases genomically unrelated to either cluster. In February 2024, two further LOGBS cases (bacteremia; asymptomatic bacteruria) emerged. The first matched the mother's antepartum isolate with transmission to the second infant (0 SNVs; cluster 3, serotype IV). Hygiene audits identified gaps in hand and environmental safety; room proximity was the primary commonality. Following reinforcement of infection prevention measures, no further nosocomial GBS infections occurred through October 2025.

CONCLUSIONS: This prolonged NICU outbreak involved multiple serotypes. WGS was critical in distinguishing horizontal transmission from independent introductions, directly guiding targeted infection control interventions.

articles.title: Exercise for Older People with Heart Failure and Frailty: Should We Even Try?
articles.abstract: The benefits of exercise in older patients with heart failure (HF) and frailty are twofold: (i) improvement in cardiopulmonary capacity, thus reducing HF-related sequelae; (ii) attenuation of decline in physical function, thus improving frailty status. Despite the clear benefits, exercise training (ET) remains underutilised as a treatment modality in this patient population. Guidelines on the specific type of exercise intervention best suited for this population are still lacking. In this review, we discuss (i) pathophysiology underlying exercise intolerance in patients with HF; (ii) impact of frailty on HF and exercise capacity; (iii) benefits and safety of ET; (iv) recommended ET programme for this population; (v) mode of delivery and (vi) potential barriers in the uptake of ET and strategies to overcome them. An effective ET intervention in this population warrants individualisation to patient's physical capacity, while addressing possible barriers to uptake so as to ensure sustained participation in the programme.

articles.title: Multidomain Autonomic Dysfunction assessed with COMPASS-31 among patients with type 2 diabetes in Zanzibar: prevalence and associated factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autonomic dysfunction is an important but frequently under-recognized complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), particularly in settings where objective autonomic testing is not routinely available. The Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31) provides a practical symptom-based approach for assessing autonomic dysfunction across multiple domains. This study compared socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical characteristics among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar according to COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction and examined factors associated with its presence.

METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 665 adults with T2DM attending the diabetes clinic at Mnazi Mmoja Hospital, Zanzibar. Autonomic symptoms were assessed using COMPASS-31, including the orthostatic intolerance, gastrointestinal, and bladder domains. Participants were classified as having autonomic dysfunction when they met the prespecified threshold for dysfunction in at least one assessed domain. Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) was assessed separately using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests performed with an automated CAN Analyzer and was not included in the COMPASS-31 composite outcome. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Overall, 309 participants (46.5%) had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Orthostatic intolerance was the most common domain, affecting 271 participants (40.8%), followed by gastrointestinal dysfunction in 177 (26.6%) and urinary dysfunction in 123 (18.5%). Separately, 305 participants (45.9%) met the analyzer-based criteria for CAN. In the multivariable analysis, autonomic dysfunction was more prevalent among participants without a family history of diabetes (aPR = 1.37, 95% CI: 1.16-1.61; p < 0.001), those with diabetes duration of ≥ 10 years (aPR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.14-1.75; p < 0.001), those not using oral hypoglycemic agents (aPR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.39-1.97; p < 0.001), and those who rarely consumed vegetables or consumed one portion per day (aPR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.37-2.34; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Approximately half of the adults with T2DM in this tertiary-care population had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Higher prevalence was associated with no family history of diabetes, longer diabetes duration, non-use of oral hypoglycemic agents, and lower vegetable intake. These findings highlight the potential value of symptom-based autonomic assessment and support further prospective research to better understand the clinical and lifestyle factors associated with autonomic dysfunction among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar.

articles.title: Otorhinolaryngological manifestations of systemic autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract: In many autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases, the head and neck are the first sites of symptom manifestation. Recognizing these early signs is crucial to prevent diagnostic delays and fatal consequences. This review addresses: (1) specific otorhinolaryngological (ENT) manifestations indicating systemic diseases (2), evidence for differentiating these from isolated ENT disorders, and (3) the multidisciplinary role in patient management. A comprehensive narrative literature review was conducted utilizing established scientific databases, including PubMed/Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase, covering articles published from 1983 up to 2026. A structured search strategy applied keywords like "systemic disorders," "ENT symptoms," "granulomatosis with polyangiitis," and "Sjögren syndrome." Peer-reviewed clinical trials, mechanistic studies, and authoritative guidelines were included to synthesize current evidence regarding the clinical detection and management of systemic diseases through ENT manifestations. ENT symptoms typically manifest locally before systemic organ involvement. Sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) frequently accompanies autoinflammatory diseases. Auricular chondritis strongly indicates relapsing polychondritis (RP). Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA) and RP classically present with refractory rhinosinusitis, nasal crusting, and saddle-nose deformities. Orally, Sjögren syndrome causes severe sicca syndrome, while Behçet's disease leads to mucosal ulcerations. Furthermore, GPA (developing in 2-20% of cases) and RP are common causes of potentially fatal laryngeal involvement, including progressive subglottic stenosis. ENT manifestations frequently herald severe systemic diseases. Early detection by otolaryngologists is vital. Implementing a multidisciplinary strategy that integrates rheumatology and internal medicine ensures timely diagnosis, facilitates appropriate systemic immunosuppression, and significantly improves patient survival and overall quality of life.

articles.title: Patient characteristics and the safety of stent placement for malignant vena cava syndrome in Japan: a nationwide analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the overall safety of stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome by assessing adverse events in a nationwide multicenter population.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination nationwide inpatient database. Patients who underwent stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome between April 2019 and March 2023 were included. The primary endpoint was the overall incidence of adverse events, which were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes. Secondary evaluations included patient characteristics, underlying malignancies, therapeutic interventions, 7-day mortality after stent placement, 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission, and comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups.

RESULTS: This nationwide study included 301 patients from 137 hospitals, of whom 187 underwent SVC stenting, and 114 underwent IVC stenting. Overall, 34 adverse events occurred in 32 patients (10.6%). Red blood cell transfusion was required in 10 patients (3.3%), but no invasive treatment, including embolization, was required. Seven-day mortality after stenting was 5.0%, and 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission was 11.6%. In comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups, respiratory failure was more common after SVC stenting, whereas other adverse events and mortality were comparable between groups. Lung tumors predominated in SVC cases and liver tumors in IVC cases; multiple stents were used more frequently in IVC cases.

CONCLUSION: Stent placement for malignant vena cava obstruction demonstrated an overall complication rate of 10.6% with no serious adverse events requiring invasive intervention.

articles.title: Association between urinary heavy metal(loid)s exposure and dyslipidemia in children from e-waste dismantling areas.
articles.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
articles.abstract: To assess temporal trends of urinary heavy metal(loid)s burden and lipid levels, and explore the single and joint associations of heavy metal(loid)s exposure with lipid profiles among children in Guiyu, a typical e-waste dismantling area in China. Based on 2016 and 2024 surveys in Guiyu, 197 children (aged 3-7) were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of 13 heavy metal(loid)s were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Serum lipid parameters including total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured, and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C) was calculated. To investigate the independent and combined associations between metals and blood lipid profiles, multiple linear regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models were employed. Urinary concentrations of Chromium (Cr), Nickel (Ni), Copper (Cu), Cadmium (Cd), and Lead (Pb) in 2024 were significantly lower than those in 2016 (all P < 0.05). In adjusted models, Manganese (Mn), Cobalt (Co), Cd, and Pb were positively associated with TC and non-HDL-C, while Cd and Pb were negatively associated with HDL-C (all P < 0.05). BKMR confirmed a significant joint positive effect of a 12-metal mixture on TC and non-HDL-C, and a negative effect on HDL-C. Despite decreased individual metal levels over the eight-year interval, the biological risk from co‑exposure to these metals remains a critical concern These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding the synergistic cardiovascular toxicity of heavy metals on pediatric lipid homeostasis.

articles.title: Assessment of Candida attributes under in vitro repeated exposure to hydrogen peroxide.
articles.journal: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
articles.abstract: Fungal infections have emerged as a significant concern in healthcare, due to the development of antifungal resistance and the limited availability of diagnostic and therapeutic options. The Candida species represent a category of particular importance with regard to fungi. Therefore, the implementation of infection prevention and control measures, such as hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) disinfection, is imperative in healthcare settings. In consideration of the existing literature, which demonstrates that repeated exposure to H2O2 does not compromise microbial tolerance to the disinfectant, the expression of virulence attributes may be altered under the influence of external selective pressure.The present study aims to evaluate the effect of repeated exposure to H2O2 on antifungal susceptibility profiles, catalase production, and biofilm formation on Candida strains in a phenotypic assessment of the microbial behaviour.In previous studies, strains of C. albicans, C. parapsilosis, and C. auris were repeatedly exposed to different H2O2 concentrations and evaluated for their susceptibility to the disinfectant over 30 days. The present study demonstrated that repeated exposure to H₂O₂ resulted only in minor fluctuations of the antifungal susceptibility of C. albicans and C. parapsilosis, but not of C. auris. Repeated exposure to H₂O₂ demonstrated no variation in catalase production or alteration in biofilm formation for the evaluated species.In conclusion, repeated exposure to H₂O₂ resulted in only minor fluctuations in antifungal susceptibility in C. albicans and C. parapsilosis strains, demonstrating that utilization of H2O2 as a daily disinfectant is safe in relation to microbial adaptation. However, environmental surveillance is advised to prevent the inadvertent development of antifungal resistance.

articles.title: Genome-wide identification and characterization of the PE/PPE gene family in Mycobacterium abscessus.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Fish Scale-derived Chitooligosaccharide and Chitosan Hydrogels as Functional Biomaterials for Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Chronic and poorly healing wounds require dressings that do more than provide coverage, but actively regulate infection, oxidative stress, and tissue repair. In this study, hydrogels formulated from fish-scale-derived low-molecular-weight chitosan and chitooligosaccharide (COS) were evaluated using integrated antimicrobial, antioxidant, and in vivo wound-healing analyses to assess their comparative therapeutic performance. Antimicrobial testing against Gram-positive bacteria (Bacillus subtilis and Micrococcus luteus) and Gram-negative bacteria (Aeromonas hydrophila and Klebsiella pneumoniae) showed that COS displayed stronger activity overall, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 0.156 to 1.25 mg/mL, compared with 0.313 to 1.25 mg/mL for chitosan. COS also showed a clearer bactericidal effect, particularly against the Gram-positive strains, whereas chitosan was predominantly bacteriostatic under the conditions tested. In antioxidant assays, COS demonstrated stronger hydroxyl radical and ABTS radical scavenging activity than chitosan, indicating a more favourable redox-modulating profile. Physicochemical analyses revealed differences in the swelling and degradation profiles of the two hydrogel formulations. In vivo, both hydrogels promoted wound contraction relative to untreated wounds, with COS exhibiting the more rapid response. The COS-treated group achieved complete mean wound contraction by day 14, accompanied by greater collagen-associated staining during subsequent histological assessment. By day 21, the collagen-associated percentages reached 95.71% in COS-treated wounds and 84.81% in chitosan-treated wounds. Immunohistochemical analysis further demonstrated temporal changes in TGF-β1 expression, with increased staining during the proliferative stage of wound repair. Collectively, these findings indicate favourable wound-healing performance of fish scale-derived COS hydrogel relative to chitosan hydrogel under the experimental conditions examined. The results support further investigation of fish scale-derived biopolymers as potential materials for wound dressing development.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of surgical laser interventions and adjunctive photobiomodulation in osseous crown lengthening: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: To synthesize the available clinical evidence on laser-based interventions in osseous crown-lengthening procedures, considering surgical laser techniques and adjunctive photobiomodulation separately. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to June 2025. We included clinical studies involving adults undergoing osseous crown lengthening with laser-assisted surgery or postoperative photobiomodulation. Three reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, assessed potentially eligible full-text articles, and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed at the outcome level using RoB 2 for randomized studies and ROBINS-I for the nonrandomized comparative study. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, we evaluated findings using a structured narrative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. We included five clinical studies published between 2021 and 2024. Three evaluated lasers used during the surgical procedure, while two evaluated adjunctive photobiomodulation following conventional surgery. Some studies reported reduced intraoperative bleeding and improved surgical visibility with surgical laser techniques, although they did not consistently assess these outcomes using standardized quantitative measures. Periodontal and gingival-margin outcomes were generally comparable with conventional procedures. Findings regarding postoperative pain were inconsistent, with benefits reported in some but not all studies. Across two small studies using different irradiation protocols, adjunctive photobiomodulation was associated with reduced early postoperative pain at selected assessment times; only one study reported lower analgesic consumption. Among the four randomized studies, one assessed result was judged to have a high overall risk of bias and three raised some concerns; none was judged to have a low overall risk of bias. The nonrandomized comparative study was judged to have a serious risk of bias. Some studies descriptively reported potential intraoperative advantages with surgical laser techniques, while adjunctive photobiomodulation may reduce early postoperative pain at selected assessment times. Given the small and heterogeneous evidence base and its methodological limitations, current evidence remains insufficient to establish superiority over conventional osseous crown-lengthening surgery or to identify an optimal laser protocol.Clinical trial number: not applicable.

articles.title: Nanotherapeutic macrophage reprogramming through immunometabolic and microbial modulation for sepsis treatment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by dysregulated immune responses and metabolic dysfunction, and remains a major cause of global mortality. While nanomedicine offers new opportunities for sepsis therapy, current strategies rarely achieve comprehensive modulation of macrophage immunometabolism and microenvironmental signaling. Here, we develop a glutathione-responsive nanotherapeutic platform (EONPs) by conjugating the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) inhibitor 4-octyl itaconate to polyethylene glycol, followed by encapsulation of the dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) inhibitor EA6. Integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic analyses combined with pharmacological assessments reveal that EONPs suppress systemic hyperinflammation, reprogram macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, restore gut microbial homeostasis, and protect against multi-organ injury in septic models. Notably, EONPs enhance the production of the microbiota-derived metabolite 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), which is functionally linked to the anti-inflammatory response and may further support macrophage reprogramming. Our findings establish a previously unrecognized strategy for precise metabolic and microbiota-driven modulation of macrophages, offering a conceptual framework for further investigation of macrophage-targeted nanotherapeutics in sepsis.

articles.title: Neighborhood Walkability And Perceived Environment Are Not Associated With Physical Activity In Patients With Heart Failure.
Adverse events in paediatric spinal deformity surgery - 12-year review of specialist spinal deformity practice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Adverse events following paediatric spinal deformity surgery in the UK suffers from significant reporting gaps, as current data relies predominantly on voluntary incident submissions. This retrospective study aims to comprehensively assess the incidence of all surgical adverse events at a specialized paediatric spinal orthopaedic centre.

METHODS: A retrospective review of prospectively collected data from January 2010 to December 2022 systematically evaluated perioperative and postoperative adverse events. Patients were analyzed by scoliosis aetiology and adverse events were stratified according to the Clavien-Dindo classification system. Adverse events were further grouped by common themes including implant-related, infection-related, and neurological events.

RESULTS: A total of 871 paediatric spinal deformity patients undergoing 1,020 operations with at least two years follow-up were identified. Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis was the most common primary pathology with 545 patients (62.6%). Overall, 324 patients (37.2%) experienced an adverse event. Adverse events were categorized by severity: 14.8% grade 1, 5.3% grade 2, 1.1% grade 3A, 14.6% grade 3B, 1.1% grade 4, and 0.1% grade 5. Implant-related issues were most frequent (n = 113, 13.0%), followed by curve progression (n = 33, 3.8%) and persistent pain (n = 33, 3.8%). Neurological events included four complete cord injuries (0.5%) and four incomplete cord injuries which fully recovered (0.5%). One perioperative death occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of paediatric spinal deformity surgeries, over one-third of patients experienced adverse events, predominantly of low severity requiring minimal or no further intervention. Implant-related adverse events were most frequent, while the incidence of both complete and incomplete spinal cord injury, as well as mortality, remained reassuringly low across all procedures.

articles.title: Ultrasound-assisted proteolysis of pea protein: Structural and peptidomic modulation to enhance α-glucosidase inhibitory activity.
articles.abstract: With the increasing prevalence of diabetes mellitus, naturally derived α-glucosidase inhibitory peptides have garnered growing attention. Most studies have focused on preparation efficiency and bioactivity outcomes, while the structural mechanisms governing peptide release remain poorly understood. In this study, ultrasound-assisted proteolysis of pea protein was employed to elucidate how structural modifications regulate α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Although ultrasonication reorganized protein conformations, subsequent pepsin hydrolysis promoted a more ordered and compact structure, resulting in a superior inhibition (IC50 = 2.17 mg/mL) than acidic protease hydrolysis. Medium-molecular-weight fractions (3-10 kDa) and α-helix-rich structures favored inhibitory expression, highlighting the importance of compact conformations. Peptidomic analysis combined with machine learning and molecular docking identified phenylalanine and glycine as key residues mediating inhibition via π interactions and hydrogen bonding. These findings emphasized the structural basis for the release of α-glucosidase inhibitory peptide and provided rational guidance for the targeted and efficient production of hypoglycemic ingredients and nutraceuticals.

articles.title: Lycorine ameliorates MASH by targeting ACSL4 to regulate lipid metabolism and inhibit ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a progressive stage of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), has emerged as one of the most prevalent chronic liver diseases worldwide, yet therapeutic options remain limited. In this study, we found that lycorine effectively alleviated MASH both in vitro and in vivo. RNA-seq analysis revealed that lycorine suppressed lipid uptake and mitigated ferroptosis in MASH models. Using drug affinity responsive target stability coupled with mass spectrometry (DARTS-MS), we identified acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) as a direct binding target of lycorine. Mechanistically, lycorine targeted ACSL4 to regulate lipid metabolism and ferroptosis pathways, thereby reducing lipid uptake and accumulation, attenuating lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, and ultimately ameliorating MASH progression. Collectively, our findings elucidate the precise mechanism and direct target through which lycorine alleviates MASH, strongly suggesting that natural compounds such as lycorine hold promise as candidate therapeutics for MASH.

articles.title: Molecular survey of zoonotic protozoa in free-ranging marmosets (Callithrix penicillata) from Central Brazil: implications for One Health surveillance.
articles.abstract: Urban expansion and environmental fragmentation have intensified contact among wildlife, domestic animals, and humans, reshaping infectious disease dynamics at the human-wildlife interface. Non-human primates (NHP), particularly the black-tufted marmoset (Callithrix penicillata), readily adapt to anthropogenic landscapes and may serve as sentinel hosts for zoonotic pathogens. This study investigated the occurrence of Leishmania spp., Plasmodium spp., Toxoplasma gondii, and Trypanosoma cruzi. in 232 free-ranging C. penicillata found dead in urban and peri-urban areas of the Federal District, central Brazil, between 2018 and 2023. Liver samples were analyzed by quantitative PCR. Plasmodium spp. was not detected (0/232). In contrast, 39.7% (92/232) of marmosets were positive for T. gondii, 32.4% (69/213) for Leishmania spp., and 21.1% (47/223) for T. cruzi. Overall, 71.6% of the animals tested positive for at least one protozoan agent, and 21.2% had coinfections, most commonly Leishmania spp. plus T. gondii. Positive cases were widely distributed across administrative regions, with evidence of spatiotemporal clustering in some urbanized areas. Parasitic loads varied substantially, and most infected animals showed no lesions attributable to these infections. These findings demonstrate the widespread circulation of zoonotic protozoa in free-ranging marmosets inhabiting anthropized environments and reinforce their epidemiological relevance within a One Health framework. Surveillance of urban NHP populations can contribute to understanding transmission networks and environmental contamination, thereby supporting public health strategies for the prevention and control of zoonotic diseases in central Brazil.

articles.title: Promoting the use of osteopathic manipulative treatment with a student-led program: a retrospective review of 713 patient visits' characteristics and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Early clinical exposure (ECE), especially within osteopathic medicine, helps bridge the gap between medical theory and practical skills by giving students the chance to apply osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) early in their training. This enhances their competency and builds a stronger connection to osteopathic principles. Current literature highlights that the early use of OMT in osteopathic institutions motivates students to continue utilizing their skill set, yet few programs offer real-world, hands-on experience outside of lectures and practicals. This paper describes and evaluates one of these programs, a student-led, faculty-supervised clinic focused on enhancing early OMT skills and confidence.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to describe this student-run, faculty-supervised clinic and to document the most common somatic dysfunctions and the OMT utilized, and to compare pre-and posttreatment pain scores for participants.

METHODS: This study was a retrospective chart review of 713 volunteer patient visits over a 3-year period, from the Fall semester of 2022 to the Spring semester of 2025. Data collected included volunteer demographics such as age, date of birth, gender identifier, status (faculty, staff, or student), chief complaint, body regions with somatic dysfunction, OMT modalities, and pre-and posttreatment Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) scores. Descriptive statistics were utilized to summarize the demographic frequencies to characterize the clinic's operational impact. NPRS scores were compared before and after treatment, utilizing a Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank test for nonparametric data to assess the effect of OMT on volunteer-reported pain levels.

RESULTS: Of the 713 volunteer patient visits at the clinic, 533 (74.8 %) were students, 149 (20.9 %) were staff, and 14 (2.0 %) were faculty. Volunteers' ages ranged from 21 to 78 years, with a median age of 25.3 years. The most treated body regions were the cervical and thoracic regions, whereas the abdomen was the least treated region. On average, four body regions were treated per volunteer. The most utilized OMT modalities were the muscle energy technique and myofascial release, with lymphatic and visceral techniques being the least frequently utilized. An average of four modalities were utilized per volunteer. Posttreatment NPRS levels were consistently lower than the pretreatment scores (p<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: The data from this study provide insight into the most encountered diagnoses in a more real-world clinical setting for our students and the corresponding treatments most frequently applied. Although not explicitly investigated in this retrospective chart review, this student-run, faculty-supervised clinic allowed students to treat patients over 700 times in 3 years, presumably preparing them better to utilize OMT in their future clinical practice. Additionally, consistently improved patient-reported pain scale scores suggest the clinical effectiveness of the students' OMT interventions.

articles.title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion.

METHODS: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 h of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort.

RESULTS: Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤ 14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

articles.title: A Pathology-Responsive Hydrogel with On-Demand Ion Release for Microenvironment Remodeling and Diabetic Wound Regeneration.
articles.abstract: The healing of diabetic wounds is often impeded by severe bacterial infections, persistent inflammation, excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and abnormal matrix degradation. Although conventional free silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) possess broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, their inherent tendency to aggregate and inactivate, as well as its high cytotoxicity limits their clinical application. Moreover, a single bactericidal strategy is insufficient to completely reverse the complex pathogenic microenvironment of the wound. To address these challenges, this study developed a dual-polyphenol biomimetic extracellular matrix (ECM) composite hydrogel with matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) and pH-responsive properties, aimed at achieving spatiotemporal precision intervention and active microenvironment remodeling in diabetic wounds. This system employs caffeic acid-modified gelatin and dopamine-modified sodium alginate as a dynamically cross-linked scaffold, incorporated with AgNPs-anchored zinc-aluminum layered double hydroxide (ZnAl-LDH@Ag), that can precisely match the dynamic pathological evolution of the wound. The hydrogel exhibits pathology-adaptive behavior through two complementary mechanisms: gradual MMP-9-mediated remodeling of the gelatin network and infection-associated pH-responsive ion release. MMP-9-mediated degradation enables sustained exposure of ZnAl-LDH@Ag and prolonged matrix remodeling, whereas the acidic microenvironment promotes on-demand release of antibacterial Ag+ and regenerative Zn2+ ions. Additionally, polyphenol moieties provide antioxidant and anti-inflammatory regulation during wound healing. By integrating two-dimensional inorganic layered materials (ZnAl-LDH) with conventional metal nanocrystals (AgNPs), this strategy resolves the clinical paradox in silver-based therapies: the difficulty of balancing high bactericidal activity with low cytotoxicity. In summary, this pathology-driven therapeutic platform enables multimodal synergistic therapy for antioxidant protection, infection control, and tissue regeneration, providing a theoretical foundation and design perspectives for the development of advanced dressings for complex chronic wounds.

articles.title: The influence of loneliness & social isolation on cardiovascular risk factors: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite substantial advances in treatment and preventive medicine, heart disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While traditional risk factors have been identified, emerging research continues to underscore the importance of social interactions.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines research on how loneliness and social isolation influence the major risk factors for heart disease. Studies from 2000 up to April 2026 were searched using PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. The included research focused on loneliness and social isolation, alongside seven primary risk factors such as smoking, stress, dyslipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and lack of physical activity, and showed that people who are lonely and socially isolated have approximately a 29% higher chance of developing heart disease. Loneliness and isolation are linked with both physiological and behavioral changes, and many of these relationships are bidirectional, creating feedback loops in which social disconnection and cardiometabolic risk reinforce one another.

EXPERT OPINION: Treating loneliness as a modifiable and deeply integrated risk factor helps patient well-being and long-term health outcomes, and supports more effective clinical care, community health, and policy planning.

articles.title: Interface-Programmed Growth of High-Aspect-Ratio 1D Ni-MOF Nanofibers on MXene for Wearable Enzyme-Free Glucose Sensing.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive wearable glucose sensors capable of real-time sweat analysis offer a less discomforting alternative for long-term monitoring in patients with diabetes. However, practical implementation remains challenging. Major barriers include insufficient catalytic sensitivity to quantify the low glucose levels in sweat, limited compatibility between nanomaterial synthesis and scalable manufacturing processes, and the lack of a biofluid microenvironment suitable for enzyme-free electrochemical sensing. Here, we address these challenges by combining strong interfacial anchoring on a conductive template with surfactant-assisted growth control to engineer high-aspect-ratio (∼100) 1D Ni-TCPP MOF nanofibers as an active shell on MXene-NH2. In contrast to conventional electrospinning-assisted approaches, the resulting 1D MOF shell is polymer-template-free and thus avoids insulating scaffold components. The resulting fluffy, self-supporting Ni-MOF@MXene architecture is inherently compatible with printed electronics, enabling large-area fabrication of wearable enzyme-free glucose-sensing patches. To overcome the constraints of enzyme-free sensing in physiological biofluids, we further develop an integrated system that combines microfluidics with a NaOH/Nafion/PVA alkaline sustained-release membrane, establishing a localized alkaline microenvironment within sweat to enable continuous analysis.

articles.title: Integration of CURB-65 and CT Severity Score for Prognostic Prediction in Community-acquired Pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, age ≥65 years (CURB-65) and computed tomography severity score (CTSS) for predicting 30-day mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and length of hospital stay in patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and assessed whether CTSS added prognostic value to CURB-65.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 adults with CT-confirmed CAP. CURB-65 and CTSS were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed for 30-day mortality and ICU admission, and area under the curve (AUC) values were compared using the DeLong test.

RESULTS: For mortality prediction, the AUC values were 0.894 for CURB-65, 0.762 for mean CTSS, and 0.909 for the combined mortality model. The combined model did not significantly outperform CURB-65 (P = 0.081). For ICU admission, the AUC values were 0.851, 0.716, and 0.881, respectively; the combined ICU model significantly outperformed CURB-65 (P = 0.003). The mean CTSS was independently associated with mortality and ICU admission, but was not associated with length of hospital stay.

CONCLUSION: CURB-65 remained a strong and practical predictor of mortality and ICU admission in CAP. Mean CTSS provided additional prognostic information for mortality and ICU admission, but not for length of hospital stay. The combined mortality model did not significantly improve discrimination compared with CURB-65 alone, whereas the combined ICU model did significantly improve discrimination in predicting ICU admission.

articles.title: Retardation of human insulin amyloid fibrillation by vitamin B1.
articles.abstract: Water-soluble B-complex vitamins have been proven to undergo significant interactions with proteins both in vivo and in vitro. Understanding the impact of major vitamin B-interacting residues (VBIRs), like Gly, His, Asn, Ser, Thr, Trp and Tyr, is relevant to designing experiments related to the beneficial effects of protein-vitamin interactions. The maintenance of native folds and the monomeric form is necessary for the functioning of therapeutic proteins like insulin. Some fatal cases of amyloid generation before (during storage and in the delivery pump) and/or after insulin application (at the injection site) to patients with diabetes mellitus have been reported, which are a matter of concern. Amyloid fibrils of insulin are irreversible aggregates of insulin, rich in beta-sheet content instead of the native alpha-helical conformation. Inspired by the protein-vitamin interactions reported in the literature, the present work explored three vitamin B complexes, viz., vitamins B1, B6 and B12, and separately investigated their amyloid inhibitory activities on insulin. The thermally generated amyloid fibrils of recombinant human insulin were compared with those of vitamin pre-incubated insulin under identical heating conditions by employing different fluorimetric, spectroscopic, light-scattering, and imaging studies. The results showed the considerable amyloid inhibitory activity of thiamine on insulin aggregation in vitro. The possible mechanism includes the shielding effect of Vit. B1 through several non-covalent interactions with insulin. Vit. B6 did not exhibit sufficient insulin amyloid inhibitory activity, even though it maintained the alpha-helical form to some extent during thermal aggregation, unlike Vit. B1. Vit. B12, having a bulkier structure, could not interact with insulin in a stable manner and consequently disrupted the solvated state of insulin.

articles.title: Gas Delivery from Extruded MOF-Polymer Composites for Mitigation of Complications Associated with Catheters Used in Interventional Cardiology.
articles.abstract: The large internal surface areas and porosities of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) promise a wide variety of applications in gas capture, storage, and delivery. To realize their potential, MOFs need to be processed into suitable forms for the target function. Here, we demonstrate the preparation and functional assessment of extruded MOF-polymer composite tubing comprising 1 and 5 wt % Zn-MOF-74 incorporated into a medical-grade polyamide/polyether block copolymer for the delivery of the biological signaling molecule, nitric oxide (NO). Solutions to the challenges associated with water evolution during extrusion, which can severely affect the composite properties, are presented. We employ X-ray computed tomography to provide evidence for uniform dispersion of the MOF within the tubing, and we show that the mechanical properties of the polymer tubing are not negatively impacted by MOF incorporation. We demonstrate using in vitro experiments that the gas-loaded tubing is non-toxic and that the MOF-polymer composite delivers NO at amounts relevant for the prevention of three of the most common complications in different types of catheterizations: arterial vasospasm, catheter-related thrombosis, and microbial infection.

articles.title: Peptide-Reduced Platinum-Based Nanozymes for Wound Treatment of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Infection.
articles.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected wounds remain difficult to treat because of antibiotic resistance, biofilm formation, and persistent inflammation, highlighting the need for alternative local antibacterial strategies. Herein, we developed a platinum-based nanozyme (FmY@Pt) through a UV-assisted green reduction process using a tyrosine-containing short peptide (FmY) and evaluated its antibacterial activity and therapeutic potential for treating MRSA-infected wounds. The physicochemical properties and peroxidase(POD)-like activity of FmY@Pt were characterized, and its antibacterial effects and possible mechanisms were evaluated in vitro. The resulting nanozyme exhibited peroxidase-like activity under the tested conditions. In vitro experiments showed that FmY@Pt disrupted bacterial membranes and increased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in MRSA cells. These effects were associated with the antibacterial activity of FmY@Pt. In a mouse model of MRSA-infected skin wounds, the FmY@Pt + H2O2 treatment accelerated wound closure, with the wound closure rate reached approximately 80.8% on day 7. Moreover, bacterial survival rate was reduced to approximately 6.13%, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 93.87% relative to the control group. The treatment was also associated with attenuated inflammatory responses and improvements in tissue repair-related histological indicators. These findings suggest that the antibacterial and inflammation-modulating effects of FmY@Pt may collectively contribute to wound repair under the conditions. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the further investigation of nanozyme-based strategies for the treatment of infected wounds.

articles.title: Lysozyme-Associated Quercetin-Manganese Nanocomposites for Kidney-Targeted Antiferroptotic Therapy of Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening syndrome in which oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory amplification converge to damage renal proximal tubular epithelial cells. Although antioxidant and antiferroptotic therapies are conceptually attractive, their efficacy is restricted by rapid clearance and insufficient accumulation in injured renal tubules. Here, we report lysozyme-associated quercetin-manganese metal-phenolic nanocomposites (QMLNCs) as a kidney-targeted therapeutic platform for AKI. In this design, quercetin (QCT) functions simultaneously as an antioxidant drug and a phenolic coordination ligand, while Mn2+ participates in metal-phenolic network formation. Lysozyme is incorporated through noncovalent protein-polyphenol interactions to enhance megalin-mediated uptake by proximal tubular cells. QMLNCs exhibited favorable colloidal stability, H2O2-responsive release, and broad-spectrum radical-scavenging ability. In cisplatin-injured human kidney 2 (HK-2) cells, QMLNCs reduced Fe2+ and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential. Mechanistically, Western blot analysis indicated that QMLNCs could restore the protein levels of SLC7A11, GPX4, and FTH-1, which are key mediators of ferroptosis resistance. In macrophages, QMLNCs suppressed M1 polarization, promoted M2 polarization, and reduced tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and nitric oxide (NO) production. In vivo, QMLNCs preferentially accumulated in injured kidneys and significantly alleviated renal dysfunction in both glycerol-induced and cisplatin-induced AKI models, as indicated by decreased serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, MDA and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Overall, QMLNCs integrate renal tubular targeting, ROS scavenging, ferroptosis inhibition, and inflammation modulation into a single metal-natural product nanoplatform, offering a promising strategy for multimodal AKI therapy.

articles.title: Small Airway Dysfunction in Asthma: Associations with Control and Quality of Life.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Small airway dysfunction (SAD) is an important but frequently underrecognized component of asthma. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of SAD in asthma, as assessed by impulse oscillometry (IOS), and to evaluate its association with clinical outcomes.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study, with a 12-month prospective follow-up, included adult patients with asthma. SAD was defined by IOS as R5-R20 ≥0.07 kPa·s·L-1. The asthma control test (ACT) and the asthma quality of life questionnaire (AQLQ) were administered. Exacerbations were prospectively recorded during the 12 months after enrollment. Patients were stratified according to the presence of SAD. Clinical and functional parameters were compared between groups.

RESULTS: SAD was identified in 63 of 98 participants (64.3%). SAD prevalence differed significantly across the five Global Initiative for Asthma treatment steps (P < 0.001). Patients with SAD had significantly lower ACT scores (P = 0.021), poorer quality of life (AQLQ, P = 0.002), and more frequent exacerbations (P < 0.001) than those without SAD. In multivariable regression analyses, higher R5-R20 was independently associated with a lower AQLQ score (β = -0.18, 95% confidence interval -0.30 to -0.07; P = 0.002) and higher odds of being in a worse asthma control category (odds ratio 1.33, P = 0.010).

CONCLUSION: SAD is common among patients with asthma and is associated with poorer asthma control, lower quality of life, and an increased exacerbation burden. Higher R5-R20 remained associated with poorer quality of life after adjustment for spirometry, whereas its association with asthma control was attenuated and became non-significant after adjustment for forced expiratory volume in the first second. These findings support further evaluation of IOS-defined SAD as a potentially clinically relevant trait in asthma.

articles.title: Feedstock-Driven Design of CO2 Sorbents via Chemical Upcycling of Plastics and Elastomers.
articles.abstract: Plastic and elastomer wastes are abundant, carbon-rich feedstocks. At the same time, carbon capture requires sorbents that perform under realistic temperatures, humidity, dilute CO2, and repeated regeneration. This review surveys feedstock-driven chemical upcycling routes that transform waste polymers into CO2 sorbents, while treating carbonization-derived physisorbents as a comparative benchmark and pragmatic fallback for chemically intractable or highly heterogeneous feedstocks. We frame "waste-to-sorbent" conversion as a feedstock-driven design problem in which inherited constitutional chemistry, network and morphology, formulation, and acquired chemistry-collectively termed chemical memory-govern feasible transformations and capture performance. We organize the literature by major feedstocks-PET, PVC, polystyrene, rubbers/tires, polyolefins, and mixed plastics-and compare physisorption- and chemisorption-dominant architectures with emphasis on binding-site accessibility, transport limits, humidity effects, impurity tolerance, oxidative stability, and regeneration windows. Because cross-study comparison is often hindered by inconsistent testing conditions and incomplete characterization of both starting feedstocks and resulting sorbents, we propose a mechanism-aware benchmarking framework and minimum reporting protocol centered on feedstock descriptors, application-relevant CO2 partial pressures, working capacity, accessible-site metrics (e.g., effective nitrogen/amine efficiency), ultramicropore descriptors, and durability under humid/impure cycling. These guidelines connect feedstock chemistry to deployable sorbent design and accelerate translation beyond headline capacities.

articles.title: Defect-Engineered Core-Shell MOF Nanointerface Functionalized with Hemagglutinin for Target-Guided Anti-influenza Ligand Discovery.
articles.abstract: Preserving the biological function of conformationally dynamic proteins after immobilization remains a major challenge in biointerface engineering. Here, a defect-engineered hierarchical MOF nanointerface (D-MOF-808-HET@MOF-808@SiO2) was constructed through evaporation-induced interfacial coordination assembly for hemagglutinin (HA) immobilization and target-guided ligand screening. XPS analysis supported coordination-mediated interactions between HA and accessible Zr sites of the defect-engineered interface, as indicated by altered Zr 3d and O 1s binding energies. The immobilized HA retained a hemagglutination titer above 5.0 log2, indicating preservation of its biological activity. The HA-functionalized interface interfered with viral attachment to host cells during the early stage of H1N1 PR8 infection and was subsequently used as an affinity matrix to enrich HA-associated constituents from Mahuang-Xixin-Fuzi Decoction. Twelve candidate ligands were identified, of which hypaconitine, naringenin, ethyl caffeate, and vitexin were further evaluated by surface plasmon resonance and cellular antiviral assays. Hypaconitine exhibited the strongest HA-binding affinity (KD = 1.72 μM) but showed relatively weak antiviral activity (EC50 = 50.03 μM), whereas ethyl caffeate and vitexin displayed superior antiviral activities (EC50 = 1.54 and 2.56 μM) despite moderate HA affinities (KD = 11.06 and 12.20 μM, respectively), revealing an affinity-activity mismatch. Molecular docking predicted different ligand interaction patterns, with ethyl caffeate and vitexin showing interactions near the HA1-HA2 interdomain region, whereas hypaconitine and naringenin exhibited alternative predicted interaction regions. These differences in predicted binding modes may contribute to the observed functional disparity. These findings suggest that equilibrium affinity alone does not fully account for antiviral activity and support HA-functionalized MOF nanointerfaces as a platform for target-guided screening of bioactive constituents from complex natural-product mixtures.

articles.title: AnF-DiffPET: anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion for simulated low-dose PET/CT denoising.
articles.abstract: Objective.Positron emission tomography (PET) provides essential functional information for disease assessment. However, reducing injected activity or acquisition time produces low-dose (LD) PET with stronger count-dependent noise and less reliable uptake quantification. Diffusion models offer a promising solution for PET denoising by progressively recovering high-dose (HD) PET images from LD inputs. However, LD-to-HD PET denoising remains challenging because of limited anatomical guidance, unstable multi-scale feature propagation, and inaccurate recovery of uptake patterns in the frequency domain.Approach.We propose AnF-DiffPET, an anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion framework for computed tomography (CT)-conditioned LD PET denoising. The framework integrates anatomical-frequency guidance, Multi-Scale Cross-Transformer Reconstruction, and Frequency-Contrastive Hard Mining to enhance anatomy-aware feature modulation and frequency-domain consistency during denoising.Main results.Experimental results across four simulated LD PET/CT datasets show that the proposed method improves image fidelity, anatomical consistency, and quantitative fidelity over representative CNN-based, GAN-based, Transformer-based, Mamba-based, and diffusion-based methods.Significance.AnF-DiffPET provides a PET/CT-specific diffusion restoration framework that combines anatomical guidance, multi-scale feature reconstruction, and frequency-domain regularization for LD PET denoising. The code and trained models will be publicly released upon acceptance.

articles.title: Detonation reaction mechanisms of 3,4-dinitropyrazole: shock-induced reaction behavior and kinetic characteristics.
