TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: These 5 practical Cath-Lab clues would help you away from emergency type A aortic dissection trap. Timely recognition of Cath-Lab clues and pause; activate the aortic surgical team.

articles.title: Unmasking Latent Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Invasive and Noninvasive Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may be missed on resting echocardiography, and it requires provocation for detection.

CASE SUMMARY: A 41-year-old man with previously classified nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy presented with recurrent syncope. Serial echocardiography had demonstrated no significant dynamic LVOT obstruction. During reassessment, repeated Doppler interrogation with Valsalva maneuver revealed variable pressure gradients ranging from 25 to 46 mm Hg. Exercise stress echocardiography further unmasked severe LVOT obstruction, with a peak gradient of 108 mm Hg and worsening mitral regurgitation. Multimodality assessment, including postextrasystolic provocation and invasive hemodynamics, demonstrated comparable augmentation of LVOT gradients. Mavacamten therapy eliminated LVOT obstruction, with no recurrence of syncope.

DISCUSSION: Exercise-induced gradients paralleled those obtained with mechanistic provocation, indicating that physiologic stress can reliably reflect the magnitude of latent obstruction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Exercise stress echocardiography, supported by complementary provocation, may provide a practical approach to identify clinically significant latent LVOT obstruction.

articles.title: ICE Catheter as Transesophageal Probe in Children With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing an Electrophysiology Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is conventionally used as an endovascular imaging modality during electrophysiology procedures. Reports of transesophageal ICE are limited and have not included pediatric electrophysiology procedures.

CASE SUMMARY: We report the first case series of transesophageal ICE (NuVision NAV) in 6 infants and young children with congenital heart disease undergoing electrophysiology studies and catheter ablation. Indications included preoperative conduction mapping and clinical arrhythmias.

DISCUSSION: Transesophageal placement preserves the imaging advantages of ICE while avoiding large-bore venous access in small children without compromising image quality. The technique facilitates electroanatomic mapping by providing accurate delineation of the atrioventricular annulus in patients with complex congenital heart disease.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Transesophageal ICE with four-dimensional multiplanar imaging provides high-quality real-time anatomical guidance for electrophysiology procedures in infants and young children with complex congenital heart disease and may offer a practical alternative to intravascular ICE when large-bore venous access is undesirable.

articles.title: Dasatinib-Induced Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a serious complication of dasatinib, used for the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia. Although drug-induced PAH is a recognized entity, the timeline for onset and the degree of recovery on drug withdrawal remain poorly defined.

CASE SUMMARY: This review includes a series of 5 cases of dasatinib-induced PAH, in which PAH partially or fully reversed on discontinuation of the drug. All cases had documented normal cardiac status at baseline and developed PAH within 12-24 months of initiation. Three cases required pulmonary vasodilators in addition to discontinuation of the drug. The median time to resolution of PAH was 2 (2-4.5) months.

CONCLUSIONS: Dasatinib-induced PAH is a reversible yet serious condition, which mandates regular screening of patients for early recognition of the condition. Larger series with longer follow-up are mandated for better understanding of the factors associated with the risks and severity of the condition.

articles.title: Primary Cardiac Paraganglioma Management and Resection With Rare Recurrent Metastasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac paragangliomas are rare tumors that present with nonspecific sympathomimetic symptoms. Early recognition and multidisciplinary planning are essential.

CASE SUMMARY: A 55-year-old man presented with atrial fibrillation and pericarditis after weeks of dizziness, presyncope, and dyspnea. The patient underwent biopsy via thoracotomy, which was negative for malignancy. Workup revealed a 10 × 12 × 5 cm functional paraganglioma with left atrial involvement. He underwent cardiac autotransplantation with complete tumor resection and left atrial reconstruction. Postoperative recovery was complicated by extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement and stroke. One year later, surveillance identified a T9 vertebral metastasis, confirmed on biopsy, and later treated with Belzutifan, radiation, and kyphoplasty.

DISCUSSION: Cardiac paragangliomas often require complex surgical approaches. This case highlights diagnostic difficulty, metastatic potential, and evolving systemic therapies of interest to cardiovascular and oncology specialists.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac paragangliomas demand multidisciplinary management and long-term surveillance. Newer targeted therapies expand options for metastatic disease.

articles.title: Managing Acute STEMI in the Setting of Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura: A Therapeutic Dilemma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune condition characterized by thrombocytopenia. Despite bleeding tendencies, patients with ITP face thrombotic risks. Acute coronary syndrome in ITP is uncommon and poses a management dilemma between antithrombotic therapy and the high bleeding risk.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man with severe ITP (platelet nadir 1 × 103/μL) treated with avatrombopag presented with inferoposterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Angiography showed occlusion of the right posterolateral ventricular branch and right posterior descending artery. Plain old balloon angioplasty was performed without stenting. He remained stable without bleeding and was discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy, avatrombopag, and prednisolone.

DISCUSSION: ITP presents a clinical paradox of concurrent bleeding and clotting risks. Managing STEMI requires balancing these competing mechanisms.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Thrombocytopenia in ITP does not protect against acute coronary syndrome. Navigating the balance between bleeding and clotting following a STEMI event requires a tailored, flexible approach.

articles.title: Staged Antithrombotic Reinitiation After STEMI Complicated by LV Thrombus and Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular thrombus after anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction requires anticoagulation, and recent stenting requires dual antiplatelet therapy, but no guideline addresses antithrombotic sequencing when intracerebral hemorrhage complicates both.

CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old woman developed an apical left ventricular thrombus after left anterior descending artery percutaneous coronary intervention for late anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, then a left temporal intracerebral hemorrhage on day 2 while receiving aspirin, ticagrelor, and heparin. Declining ejection fraction and enlarging thrombi prompted staged reinitiation: cangrelor, clopidogrel, unfractionated heparin, then apixaban after serial neuroimaging confirmed stability.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: No guideline addresses the timing, sequence, or agent selection when these 3 indications converge.

DISCUSSION: Staged reinitiation with short-acting and reversible agents may allow antithrombotic escalation guided by serial neuroimaging stability.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: When competing thrombotic and hemorrhagic risks fall outside guideline pathways, antithrombotic therapy can be reintroduced in reassessable steps, starting with short-acting agents, guided by serial neuroimaging.

articles.title: AF-Triggered Bundle Branch Re-Entrant Ventricular Tachycardia Prevented by Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bundle branch re-entrant ventricular tachycardia (BBR-VT) is a macroreentrant tachycardia involving the right and left bundle branches,1 with the right bundle branch typically targeted for ablation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 68-year-old man with prior myocardial infarction presented with recurrent ventricular tachycardia (VT). Electrophysiological study suggested BBR-VT. VT was inducible only by atrial pacing and occurred clinically exclusively during atrial fibrillation (AF). Therefore, AF ablation alone was performed, resulting in complete suppression of VT.

DISCUSSION: Previous reports have described BBR-VT induced by atrial pacing2 or AF.3 When BBR-VT is triggered exclusively by AF, AF ablation may be an effective therapeutic strategy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In patients with BBR-VT that is triggered exclusively by atrial fibrillation or atrial pacing, elimination of the triggering atrial arrhythmia may suppress VT without the need for bundle branch ablation. Even when AF ablation is effective, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation and careful long-term follow-up remain essential because recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmias may precipitate VT recurrence.

articles.title: Clinical Significance of Age and Coexisting Lifestyle-related Diseases in ILD Patients with Acute Exacerbation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As the population ages, the impact of aging and comorbid lifestyle-related diseases on the prognosis of interstitial lung disease (ILD) has not been fully investigated. Therefore, we investigated the impact of age and comorbidities on the prognosis of patients with ILD who experienced acute exacerbations (AEs).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records and chest computed tomography scans of all consecutive ILD patients, with or without AE, between May 2015 and July 2025. The survival times of cases with and without AE were investigated.

RESULTS: Median survival time (MST) for 443 ILD cases was 10 years, while the MST for the 158 cases who developed AE was 2 months. The prognosis of cases who developed AE at age 80 years or older was significantly poorer than that of cases younger than 80 years. Among cases younger than 80 years, the survival curve for those who survived 3 months after the onset of AE plateaued. Favorable factors among cases who developed AE were age younger than 80 years and absence of comorbidities such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and malignancy.

CONCLUSION: For ILD patients who developed AE, "80 years of age" was the threshold age distinguishing good from poor prognosis. Some patients, particularly those with ILD who were diagnosed early, appeared likely to have an improved prognosis. Some AE patients, particularly younger patients, could be expected to have a good long-term prognosis if they survive a certain period of time.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin algorithms for emergency department rule-out and rule-in of acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Under threat: cognition in emergency medicine.
Real-time reinforcement for human-machine interface control.
articles.abstract: A major challenge involved in human-machine interfaces is developing feedback strategies that improve control and benefit patients with motor disabilities. Here, we propose, validate, and mechanistically characterize a personalized, closed-loop strategy that delivers reinforcement feedback in real time during human-machine interface control. Across five experiments involving 106 participants and two control interfaces, fewer than 20 reinforcement trials produced immediate improvements in force control and lasting retention gains. These effects were strongest when visual and/or somatosensory feedback was limited, a finding that suggests translational relevance for tasks, technologies, and pathologies with limited sensory feedback. In chronic stroke patients, real-time reinforcement likewise improved online force control under limited visual feedback, although short training did not yield retention gains. Information-theoretic analyses further revealed that reinforcement compensates for reduced feedback control when sensory feedback is sparse and promotes motor exploitation of successful actions. Overall, these findings identify real-time reinforcement as a promising strategy for enhancing human-machine interface control.

articles.title: Pulmonary Function Test Abnormalities in Subacute Cough: A Neglected Tool.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Subacute cough is often considered a benign and self-limiting condition, and pulmonary function tests (PFTs) are not routinely performed during this period. This study aimed to evaluate PFT findings in patients with subacute cough compared with those in healthy controls.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included adults with subacute cough who underwent standardized spirometry, along with age- and sex-frequency matched healthy controls. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), forced vital capacity (FVC), and forced expiratory flow at 25-75% of the pulmonary volume (FEF25-75) were recorded as absolute values and z-scores. Between-group comparisons were performed using analysis of covariance to adjust for age, sex, and height.

RESULTS: A total of 156 patients with subacute cough and 156 controls were analyzed. Patients with subacute cough demonstrated significantly lower FEV1 and FVC z-scores, and lower FEF25-75 values and z-scores (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, group differences remained significant for FVC, FEV1 z-score, and FEF25-75 (both absolute and z-score). Post-infectious cough was the most common diagnosis (37.8%), followed by asthma (25%); interstitial lung diseases (ILD) were also detected. FVC z-scores, absolute FEF25-75, and FEF25-75 z-scores were lower in the obstructive airway disease and ILD subgroups than in the post-infectious cough group. FEF25-75 z-scores showed the greatest discriminatory ability across diagnostic categories.

CONCLUSION: Subacute cough encompasses a heterogeneous group of underlying diseases and should not be considered solely post-infectious. Patients with subacute cough may exhibit impaired PFTs, especially FEF25-75 z-scores. PFTs may provide additional information for the evaluation of subacute cough.

Modifiers of the effectiveness of point-of-care troponin testing and determinants of concordance between diagnostic pathway recommendations and disposition in patients with chest pain: a post hoc analysis of a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) testing has the potential to reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS), evidence of real world effectiveness is lacking. Our objective was to examine factors that influence the real world effectiveness of POC hs-cTn-based accelerated diagnostic protocols (ADPs) in reducing ED LOS.

METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis from the “Aiming towards evidence-based interpretation of cardiac biomarkers in patients presenting with chest pain using POC testing” (WESTCOR-POC) study which included 1494 consecutive patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome presenting to the ED at a moderately sized hospital in Norway. Patients were randomised to receive hs-cTn measurements at admission and after 1 hour either by POC or central laboratory testing. This post hoc analysis examines factors affecting the effectiveness of a POC-based ADP and predictors of non-ADP-concordant disposition. Both outcomes were assessed using regression models, with significance level set at p<0.05.

RESULTS: Overall, 36.1% of patients met the ADPs’ early discharge criteria, of which 66% were discharged. In effect-modification analyses, the effect of POC testing on ED LOS differed by concordance with ADP recommendations (interaction p=0.011), with a reduction among patients with ADP-concordant disposition (−14 min 95% CI −26 to −3), but no corresponding reduction among patients with discordant disposition (13.5 min, 95% CI −4.5 to 31.4). Factors predicting hospital admission despite ADP-recommended discharge were: age >60 years (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.4 to 3.7, p=0.001), high triage category (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.2 to 3.0, p=0.003) and suspected serious differential diagnosis (OR 5.9, 95% 3.5 to 9.9, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight the need for implementation strategies that support ADP concordant disposition decisions and ensure appropriate patient selection to realise the efficiency potential of POC hs-cTn testing in the ED.

articles.title: QSAR Modeling and Fragment Contribution Analysis of N-Benzyltryptamines at Human 5-HT2 Receptor Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Serotonin 5-HT2 receptor agonists are returning to psychiatric drug development, but separating the three receptor subtypes pharmacologically remains difficult, and agonism at 5-HT2B carries a risk of valvular heart disease. A recent study reported affinities of 46 N-benzyltryptamines and N-benzyl-5-methoxytryptamines at all three human subtypes and analyzed them with an additive substituent model, which gave fragment coefficients of the same sign at every subtype and suggested that selectivity within this scaffold would be hard to achieve. We revisited that conclusion with non-additive models built under a protocol designed for small datasets: fifty stratified partitions with all filtering and hyperparameter tuning inside each training set, external statistics reported as distributions, response permutation on three partitions per endpoint, and partitions that withhold an entire scaffold or an entire substitution position. We repeated the analysis with two descriptor sets that share no variables and are built on different principles. Penalized linear models were predictive and transferable, whereas gradient boosting reproduced the training set exactly, and neither tree ensemble transferred to a held-out scaffold. Fragment contributions at 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C correlated at 0.25 compared with 0.77 for whole-molecule affinities, and both descriptor sets gave the same figure within 0.01. All models failed on para-substituted analogs, which distance-based applicability-domain criteria did not flag, whereas models trained without the ortho or the meta block stayed above a mean-predictor baseline. Aggregation over the whole molecule, rather than descriptor choice, conceals subtype divergence. One group drives the divergence: the N-benzyl substituent raises the predicted 5-HT2A affinity and lowers the predicted 5-HT2C affinity; excluding it raised the correlation to 0.93.

articles.title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

articles.title: Seasonal Initiation of Hemodialysis: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the seasonal pattern of hemodialysis initiation in a warm/subtropical climate region (Adana) and its association with the mode of initiation, early complications, and mortality. Materials and Methods: A total of 319 patients who started chronic hemodialysis at Adana City Training and Research Hospital, Department of Nephrology, between 2022 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Chi-square/Fisher's exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for seasonal comparisons. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease (coronary artery and/or valvular heart disease) were fitted for emergent initiation and for any early (30-day) complication, with a likelihood-ratio test of season as a whole; 3-month mortality (13 events) was described by season and analyzed with a season-only Firth model. Catheter dysfunction was analyzed among catheter-exposed patients, followed by sensitivity analyses. Results: A total of 58.3% of patients started dialysis emergently and 41.7% in a planned manner; only 11.3% had an arteriovenous fistula as initial vascular access. No significant seasonal differences were found in initiation type, indications, or the frequency of any early complication (161/314, 51.3%; p = 0.090). In the adjusted complication model, spring versus summer gave OR = 2.33 (95% CI: 1.23-4.41, p = 0.009; Holm-adjusted p = 0.028 across the three season contrasts), but the omnibus test of seasons was not significant (p = 0.069), and spring did not differ significantly from autumn or winter. Among catheter-exposed patients, catheter dysfunction occurred in 31.4% (22/70) in the spring and 16.5% (13/79) in the summer (p = 0.035; four-season omnibus p = 0.191); this contrast was not significant after excluding initiations from February to December 2023 (p = 0.111) or when the season was assigned at the midpoint of the risk window (p = 0.114). Season was not associated with emergent initiation (omnibus p = 0.230) or with 3-month mortality (Firth OR for spring versus summer 1.12, 95% CI: 0.28-4.48). Conclusions: Hemodialysis initiation in Adana was not associated with a winter-peak pattern in initiation counts or blood pressure. Spring initiation was associated with a higher frequency of early complications, mainly catheter dysfunction, but this exploratory single-center finding was not supported by the four-season omnibus tests and was sensitive to analytic choices, and none of the 33 seasonal omnibus tests remained significant after Holm correction. It is hypothesis-generating only and does not support a seasonal practice recommendation; confirmation in larger, multicenter, prospective studies is needed.

articles.title: Clinical Implications of the Age Threshold in the 2022 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Takayasu Arteritis: A Real-World Study of Patients Aged over 61 Years.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The age item of the 2022 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) criteria for Takayasu arteritis (TAK) (the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria) limits the reclassification of TAK among patients aged over 61 who were classified as TAK according to the 1990 ACR criteria. Therefore, we evaluated the clinical significance of the age item of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria. Methods: We included 22 previously TAK-diagnosed patients aged over 61 (TAK patient aged >61 years) and 41 TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (controls) in this study and retrospectively reviewed their medical records. We compared the satisfied items of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria between the two groups and further investigated whether these 22 TAK patients aged >61 years fulfilled the criteria for other relevant diseases. Results: In terms of absolute requirements, TAK patients aged >61 years were significantly older than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60. However, there were no further significant differences in the additional clinical and imaging criteria between the two groups. TAK patients aged >61 years exhibited a significantly higher frequency of ascending aorta involvement than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (18.2% vs. 0%, p = 0.012). Among the 22 TAK patients aged >61 years, ten were categorized as clinically isolated aortitis, and three of the ten patients with CIA could additionally be categorized as restrictively defined-isolated aortitis. Conclusions: Our findings support the need for external validation of the current age threshold in larger cohorts from different ethnic and geographical populations.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.

articles.title: Maternal RSV Vaccination and Complementary Infant-Protection Strategies in Singapore: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Consensus Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants and a major contributor to infant morbidity and mortality. A previous Singapore consensus addressed RSV disease burden and the role of the monoclonal antibody, nirsevimab, but did not extend to maternal RSV vaccination or its complementary use with long-acting monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). We sought structured expert consensus on positioning maternal RSV vaccination and a complementary prevention strategy in Singapore.

METHODS: A modified nominal group technique (mNGT) was used. A multidisciplinary panel of seven Singapore-based experts in obstetrics, including maternal-fetal medicine and paediatrics (respiratory, infectious disease, immunisation, and immunology), reviewed a pre-circulated targeted evidence review and four draft statements across four themes (burden, preventive pathways, maternal RSV vaccination, and complementary strategy), with the opportunity to submit written comments in advance. At a live virtual meeting on 16 June 2026, facilitated by a medical communications agency, the panel first discussed the evidence underpinning each draft statement and then voted openly (non-anonymously) on each statement in sequence. Consensus was predefined as ≥70% agreement. Statements that did not reach consensus were refined collectively, with each expert contributing in turn, and re-voted.

RESULTS: All seven experts attended and voted. Two statements reached consensus in Round 1 (Theme 2, 7/7; Theme 4, 6/7) and two after a single round of modification (Theme 1, 0/7 and then 7/7 after "first months of life" was specified as "first six months of life"; Theme 3, 3/7 and then 6/7 after "eligible pregnancies" was explicitly defined). The final statements cover RSV burden in the first six months of life, informed choice of preventive pathway, maternal RSV vaccination as an antenatal option for eligible pregnancies, and a complementary strategy in which a long-acting mAb (nirsevimab) is considered for infants not adequately protected by maternal vaccination.

CONCLUSIONS: This expert consensus supports maternal RSV vaccination as an antenatal prevention option for eligible pregnancies in Singapore and a complementary strategy with nirsevimab for infants not adequately covered by maternal vaccination. The statements represent expert consensus intended to inform, not replace, national guidance.

articles.title: Established and Novel Indications for Left Ventricular Unloading-When and for Whom?
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
articles.abstract: Temporary mechanical circulatory support devices are increasingly used to stabilise haemodynamics in patients with compromised cardiac output. While devices vary regarding indications and haemodynamic effects, only left ventricular (LV) unloading by microaxial flow pumps in a specific subset of patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction-associated cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) has shown a reduction in mortality. This review elucidates on this evidence-based indication for LV unloading, namely patients with AMI-CS fulfilling the Danish-German (DanGer)-Shock trial's inclusion and exclusion criteria. Furthermore, the review discusses cardiogenic shock scenarios encountered in everyday clinical practice beyond the trial population. It further extends beyond that, discussing clinical scenarios such as protected percutaneous coronary intervention including critical appraisal of recent trials, the negative results of unloading trials in AMI, as well as the settings of protected ventricular tachycardia ablation, LV unloading in veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (vaECMO) cases, escalated support with Impella 5.5 for postcardiotomy patients and as a bridge-to-decision or bridge-to-LV assist device (LVAD), and emerging indications such as protected cardiac as well as non-cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Incremental Value of Cardiovascular CT in Neonates and Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: An Integrated Multimodality Imaging Approach.
articles.abstract: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the first-line imaging modality in neonates and infants with congenital heart disease (CHD), whereas cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) is generally reserved for selected questions that remain unresolved after echocardiography. We evaluated the incremental diagnostic contribution of CCT within this multimodality imaging pathway. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients aged <1 year with CHD who underwent CCT after multidisciplinary review because TTE was inconclusive or additional anatomic definition was required for surgical planning. The primary endpoint was the incremental anatomic information provided by CCT beyond TTE. Secondary analyses included diagnostic performance against operative findings, acquisition characteristics, radiation exposure, contrast administration, and procedural safety. Results: Twenty-six patients were included; 14 (53.8%) were neonates. CCT was requested most frequently to assess coronary anatomy (9/26, 38.5%), followed by the pulmonary veins (4/26, 15.4%), aortic arch (3/26, 11.5%), and pulmonary arteries/MAPCAs (4/26, 15.4%). CCT provided additional anatomic characterization in 14/26 patients (53.8%), predominantly involving extracardiac vascular structures, and was discordant with TTE regarding the unresolved target anatomy in 12/26 (46.2%). Against the operative findings, TTE accuracy was 96.2% for intracardiac abnormalities, 41.2% for extracardiac abnormalities, and 11.1% for coronary abnormalities; corresponding CCT accuracy was 100%, 94.1%, and 100%. CCT directly informed the surgical approach in two patients with total anomalous pulmonary venous drainage. All examinations provided sufficient image quality to address the specific clinical question for which CCT was performed, and no contrast-related adverse events occurred. The median estimated effective dose was 3.62 mSv (IQR, 1.94-6.06). Conclusions: In a highly selected cohort of neonates and infants with CHD in whom expert TTE leaves a clinically relevant question unresolved, CCT may provide incremental information, particularly regarding coronary and extracardiac vascular anatomy. These findings support a targeted multimodality strategy in which CCT complements echocardiography and is tailored to the anatomic question relevant to surgical planning.

articles.title: Cancer Cachexia and the Heart: A Review with Focus on China.
articles.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic, multifactorial syndrome characterized by progressive depletion of skeletal muscle, disruption of metabolic homeostasis, and reduced survival. In experimental models, cachexia-associated mediators, including inflammatory cytokines, myostatin-related signaling, and proteolytic activation, have been implicated in driving cardiac atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired myocardial function. Conversely, data from chronic heart failure suggest that reduced tissue perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and sustained inflammation secondary to cardiac dysfunction may further aggravate skeletal muscle wasting. These observations suggest a bidirectional relationship between cancer cachexia and cardiac dysfunction, which has not been tested in patients with cancer. Approximately 4.82 million new cancer cases occur in China annually, with a disease distribution predominated by gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, and thoracic malignancies, all of which carry high risks of cachexia. Among 710,170 Chinese patients with cancer, 5.0% had cardiovascular disease and 13.0% had at least one cardiovascular risk factor. These figures indicate a large population at risk, but they do not show that cardiac involvement in Chinese patients differs in frequency, phenotype, or clinical impact from that in other populations; to our knowledge, no prospective data on cancer-associated cardiac involvement have been reported for Chinese patients, and cachexia assessment does not include cardiac biomarkers or echocardiographic measures. This review summarizes cancer cachexia epidemiology in China, shows the evidence linking cachexia to cardiac wasting, and evaluates how cardiac dysfunction may in turn influence the cachectic trajectory. Accordingly, we outline the key clinical and mechanistic questions that remain unanswered in Chinese patients and propose a research agenda in which cardiac assessment is evaluated prospectively before it is considered for routine care.

articles.title: Challenges of Conducting a Feasibility Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial During COVID-19 Restrictions: Rivaroxaban Versus Acetyl Salicylic Acid in Patients with Multiple Myeloma on Lenalidomide-Based Therapy (RithMM).
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a serious medical complication with an increased risk in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing combination treatment regimens. Acetylsalicylic acid is routinely used as a method of thromboprophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients treated with lenalidomide, and rivaroxaban has been assessed in small-scale studies in multiple myeloma patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs; yet, no study has compared the two methods. In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach. This pilot recruited patients with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide-based therapy and randomized them to either low-dose acetylsalicylic acid or rivaroxaban, then monitored bleeding and thrombotic events throughout lenalidomide-dexamethasone treatment. A total of 55 patients were recruited across three Canadian centres, with two venous thromboembolic events and two bleeding events, all in the acetylsalicylic acid arm. We conducted a post hoc analysis of active recruitment time as a definition of recruitment feasibility, as we did not achieve our pre-defined feasibility goals. Despite the challenges in enrollment, possibly due to social restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, we maintain that a full-scale trial is feasible and offers insight into thromboprophylactic management in this population.

articles.title: Survival benefit in patients with native aortic regurgitation using a dedicated transcatherter valve vs non-dedicated transcatheter valves.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Until recently, no standard of care has been established for patients with symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (AR) who are unsuitable for surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has been explored in this setting using off-label, non-dedicated valves originally designed for aortic stenosis. The recent ALIGN-AR trial evaluated the Trilogy valve, a dedicated transcatheter device specifically designed for native AR.

METHODS: We performed an indirect comparison between the overall survival (OS) reported for the Trilogy valve in ALIGN-AR and OS from seven single-arm studies using non-dedicated valves. Individual patient data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves using the IPDfromKM method. To ensure homogeneity, the follow-up period for the survival analysis was truncated at 24 months. Survival was analyzed using both hazard ratios (HR) and restricted mean survival time (RMST).

RESULTS: The analysis included 492 patients treated with the Trilogy valve and 867 treated with non-dedicated valves. OS was significantly improved with the Trilogy valve (HR 0.399; 95% CI 0.275-0.578; p = 0.0000011). RMST at 12 months was 11.4 months for the Trilogy valve versus 10.4 months for non-dedicated valves, corresponding to an OS gain of 1.0 months (95% CI 0.72-1.32) over the first year.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with native AR undergoing TAVI, use of the dedicated Trilogy valve was associated with a highly significant survival advantage compared with non-dedicated devices, corresponding to an approximate 1-month gain in OS during the first 12 months after implantation.

articles.title: Sirt3 attenuates LPS-induced mitochondrial fission in renal tubular epithelial cells through the AMPK-Drp1 pathway.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (S-AKI) is characterized by profound tubular epithelial cell injury and mitochondrial dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking mitochondrial dynamics to renal damage remain incompletely defined. This study investigated the role of sirtuin 3 (Sirt3) in regulating mitochondrial dynamics during endotoxin-induced renal injury. Reanalysis of the kidney subset of GSE40180 identified Sirt3 downregulation and AMPK-related transcriptional changes in cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-injured mouse kidneys. In LPS-induced AKI, Sirt3 deficiency aggravated renal dysfunction, tubular injury, oxidant-associated fluorescence, mitochondrial fragmentation, and Drp1 Ser616 phosphorylation; these findings were independently supported in a CLP model. In HK-2 cells, Sirt3 overexpression preserved mitochondrial morphology, oxygen consumption, and ATP content, whereas Sirt3 silencing exacerbated LPS-induced injury. Re-expression of Sirt3-WT, but not the catalytically inactive H248Y mutant, restored these protective effects. AMPK silencing attenuated the effects of Sirt3 overexpression on Drp1 Ser616 phosphorylation, mitochondrial morphology, respiration, and ATP content, supporting AMPK involvement in the Sirt3-associated mitochondrial phenotype. LPS increased LKB1 acetylation, whereas Sirt3 overexpression reduced it, and co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated an association between Sirt3 and LKB1. Under LPS exposure, Sirt3 silencing further increased LKB1 acetylation, and this increase was reversed by re-expression of Sirt3-WT but not by the catalytically inactive H248Y mutant. AMPK silencing strongly attenuated but did not abolish the Sirt3-associated improvements, indicating that the pathway is not strictly linear. Together, these findings support a Sirt3-dependent pathway involving LKB1 and AMPK in the regulation of Drp1 Ser616 signaling and mitochondrial integrity in experimental endotoxin-induced AKI.

articles.title: Co-Designing the Primary Care Individual Social Norms Musculoskeletal Data Dashboard (PRISM) for First Contact Physiotherapy: Consensus-Based Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the United Kingdom, first contact practitioners (FCPs) provide direct access to musculoskeletal (MSK) assessment and management in primary care. This means FCPs have to assess patients with no prior medical screening, which assumes reliance on developed skills and experience. The pool of appropriately experienced physiotherapists is limited, and less experienced clinicians have been recruited. A 2026 national evaluation found substantial variation in FCP service delivery, with data collection and governance among its structural causes. The Primary Care Individual Social Norms MSK Data Dashboard (PRISM) dashboard gives FCPs feedback on their clinical activity relative to their peers to support reflection toward improving MSK care.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to co-design the metrics, filters, and guidance content of the PRISM dashboard and guidebook to reflect evidence-based practice and the real-world context of FCP roles, and apply a critical realist approach to identify the mechanisms and conditions shaping its design.

METHODS: This qualitative co-design study used a modified nominal group process across 2 online workshops in June and August 2025, with 10 purposively sampled participants: clinical FCPs, national physiotherapy and data leaders, and a patient representative. Two analytic strands were applied to the same data. The consensus process produced the metric set and filters. Critical realist thematic analysis of the transcripts using NVivo (version 12 Plus; QSR International), with line-by-line coding using inductive and a priori codes, identified the conditions shaping how those metrics would need to be interpreted.

RESULTS: Participants reached consensus on a core metric set describing the breadth of the FCP role, separating variation generated by clinical decisions from variation generated by structure such as local diagnostic access, prescribing rights, and referral pathways. Contextual filters were co-designed at patient, clinician, and service level to keep structure visible. Supervision emerged as a condition surrounding the dashboard rather than a component, since the same comparison prompts reflection where role clarity and psychological safety are present and defensiveness where they are not. A tool dependent on supervision would work least well where support is weakest. This means that an option for stand-alone use is a design requirement. Three data integrity risks were identified: recording reliability, data gaming, and clinician burden. The guidebook enables these conditions to be transferred into practice, with separate guidance for FCPs and supervisors and a 4-step reflection structure.

CONCLUSIONS: Expert co-design produced a metric set describing the breadth of the role while accommodating variation between services and acknowledging the conditions under which PRISM can function as intended. This paper moves from the national position that FCP services collect data to a specification of the conditions under which collecting data produces learning. Mapping of the metrics against National Institute for Health and Care Excellence MSK guidelines and quality indicators is reported in a companion paper.

articles.title: The Vein of Marshall Promotes Re-Entry After Pulmonary Vein Reconnection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia recurrence remains a major limitation of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection and epicardial connections from the left atrium (LA) to the vein of Marshall (VoM) and coronary sinus (CS) in proximity to mitral valve are important contributors. We hypothesized that VoM facilitates arrhythmia induction through interaction with the epicardial region encircled by wide antral circumferential ablation (WACA).

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to systematically evaluate the combined effect of PV reconnection and epicardial VoM connectivity on the occurrence of sustained postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia using in silico models.

METHODS: Bilayer biatrial models were constructed from electroanatomical and computed tomographic data of 10 patients with AF. Post-AF electrical remodeling and substrate remodeling following the low voltage area distribution, and left-sided WACA were incorporated. Segments of WACA lesions were sequentially restored to simulate PV reconnection. Three connectivity scenarios were evaluated: intact CS-VoM-LA epicardial connection, CS-LA connection only, and no epicardial connections. Sustained re-entry (>10 seconds) was the primary endpoint, and connectivity conditions were compared using patient-level paired vulnerability. Induction of any arrhythmia, tachycardia cycle length, and stable rotor number were secondary outcomes.

RESULTS: Sustained re-entry occurred at 92 of 294 (31.3%) reconnection sites with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity, 37 of 294 (12.6%) with CS-LA connectivity only, and 29 of 294 (9.9%) without epicardial connectivity. Patient-level paired analysis showed 19.9-percentage-point and 22.7-percentage-point higher vulnerability with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity compared with CS-LA connectivity alone (95% CI: 7.1-37.3 percentage points) and no epicardial connectivity (95% CI: 7.4-41.3 percentage points), respectively. Mean tachycardia cycle length in the LA was 258.0 ± 25.7 milliseconds, 255.0 ± 31.4 milliseconds, and 251.0 ± 33.9 milliseconds across the 3 scenarios; the average number of stable rotors was 0.6 ± 0.3, 0.7 ± 0.2, and 0.4 ± 0.2, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The VoM is a critical epicardial driver of arrhythmia after incomplete WACA, underscoring the importance of its targeted ablation.

articles.title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and Surgical Considerations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries.

BACKGROUND: Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations.

METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to "accessory renal artery," "multiple renal arteries," "renal artery variations," "renal vascular anatomy," "kidney transplantation," "renovascular hypertension," "computed tomography angiography," "magnetic resonance angiography," and "endovascular aortic repair" were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded.

DISCUSSION: This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases.

CONCLUSION: Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

articles.title: Polysocial risk score predicts chronic kidney disease incidence and prognosis: mechanistic insights from plasma metabolome, proteome and lifestyle.
articles.abstract: The cumulative impact of multiple social determinants of health (SDHs) on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly understood. This prospective study examined the association of a polysocial risk score (PsRS) with CKD incidence and subsequent risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, and explored potential mediating pathways via multi-omics profiling and lifestyle factors. We analyzed 279,548 participants free of CKD at baseline and 19,761 patients with established CKD in the UK Biobank. The PsRS integrated 15 factors across economic, educational, healthcare, neighborhood, and social domains. Plasma metabolomic and proteomic profiles were analyzed to identify omics signatures associated with the PsRS. An unhealthy lifestyle score (uHLS) was derived based on body mass index, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, sleep, and diet. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between the PsRS and outcomes. Mediation analyses were performed in subsets with available omics and lifestyle data. Over a median follow-up of 13 years, 6,628 incident CKD cases, 3,724 CVD events, and 2,486 deaths were documented. The PsRS demonstrated a positive association with incident CKD risk among CKD-free participants (per 1-point increase: HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14), as well as with CVD (HR=1.08; 95% CI: 1.07-1.10) and all-cause mortality (HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.10-1.14) in CKD patients. The PsRS significantly improved the predictive performance of conventional clinical models across all outcomes, as indicated by increases in the C-index, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Multi-omics analyses revealed a PsRS-associated metabolomic signature (94 metabolites primarily involved in amino acids, fatty acids, and lipoproteins) and a proteomic signature (428 proteins primarily involved in immune/inflammatory responses, cellular signaling, and fibrosis). These omics signatures mediated substantial proportions of the PsRS-outcome associations (metabolomic: 16.64%-27.09%; proteomic: 53.09%-85.21%), as did the uHLS (8.26%-12.51%). In conclusion, the PsRS effectively predicts CKD development and prognosis, largely mediated through metabolomic and proteomic pathways.

articles.title: 2026 International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines.
articles.abstract: Guideline reviewers: Claudio Borghi (Italy), Fadi Charchar (Malaysia), Alfred Doku (Ghana), Maria Dorobantu (Romania), Joseph Flynn (USA), Nadia Khan (Canada), Anastasios Kollias (Greece), Reinhold Kreutz (Germany), Azra Mahmud (Pakistan), Giuseppe Mancia (Italy), Gianfranco Parati (Italy), Neil Poulter (UK), Jane Reckelhoff (USA), Nicolas Renna (Argentina), Abdulla Shehab (UAE), Markus Schlaich (Australia), Aletta Schutte (Australia), Boon Wee Teo (Singapore), Maciej Tomaszewski (UK), Rhian Touyz (Canada), Jiguang Wang (China), Thomas Weber (Austria), Paul Whelton (USA) and Yuqing Zhang (China).

articles.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence to Predict Visual Outcome in Patients With Macular Pucker.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) to predict postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) after macular pucker surgery using optical coherence tomography (OCT) data.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted of PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. Data extraction included study design, demographics, AI model characteristics, and performance metrics. Study quality was assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment + Artificial Intelligence tool, and results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Six studies involving 2728 patients (65-71 years) were analyzed. Convolutional neural networks and gradient boosting decision trees were applied to predict postoperative BCVA. The convolutional neural networks ResNet-101 and Inception-ResNet-V2 outperformed human grading, with ResNet-101 achieving the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.97). Interpretability techniques identified ectopic inner foveal layers (EIFL) and irregular inner nuclear layer-outer plexiform layer as key predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning models demonstrate potential in predicting postoperative outcomes from preoperative OCT scans after macular pucker surgery. Advanced architectures such as ResNet-101 and Inception-ResNet-v2 outperform simpler models and expert grading. However, clinical translation depends on model generalizability, interpretability, real-time application, and inclusion of functional data. Future research should emphasize multicenter validation to ensure broader applicability.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Predicts Failure of Nonoperative Treatment in Degenerative Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop an artificial intelligence-based algorithm to predict success of nonoperative treatment in degenerative posterosuperior tears and to identify the most influential features.

METHODS: Patients with degenerative rotator cuff tears initially treated nonoperatively were enrolled prospectively from January 2022 to November 2024. Exclusion criteria included age >75 years; <24 months of follow-up; massive, traumatic, and partial tears; arthritic changes (Hamada >2); and severe fatty degeneration (Goutallier >2). All patients followed a standardized physiotherapy protocol and could choose surgery if symptoms persisted; failure was defined as opting for surgery. Collected variables included demographics, comorbidities (diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and smoking), magnetic resonance imaging tear characteristics (size; International Society of Arthroscopy, Knee Surgery, and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine classification; associated cuff involvement; and biceps pathology), corticosteroid injection history, and functional scores (American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Subjective Shoulder Value, and the visual analog scale). First, a standard statistical analysis between groups was performed. Later, the dataset was split into a train (80%) and test (20%), and a random forest algorithm model was developed. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations values were computed to assess feature importance.

RESULTS: Of the 412 patients enrolled, 347 patients met the inclusion criteria. After 24 months, 66 (19%) patients opted for surgery. Mean follow-up was 30.4 months (range, 24-32). Compared with the successful nonoperative treatment group, patients who failed treatment were younger (58.5 vs 64.6 years, P = .001) and had higher body mass index (28.8 vs 27.2, P = .016), greater subscapularis involvement (13.5% vs 3%, P = .042), higher visual analog scale scores (7.7 vs 7.2, P = .018), lower Subjective Shoulder Value (30.9 vs 38.9, P = .003), and lower American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores (40.6 vs 47.1, P = .001). The model achieved an area under the curve of 84%, predicting success rate of the nonoperative treatment with 94% sensitivity, 62% specificity, 89% positive predictive value, and 77% negative predictive value. The most influential variables for the model were age, tear size, and pretreatment functional scores.

CONCLUSIONS: The artificial intelligence-based algorithm accurately predicted nonoperative treatment outcomes in degenerative posterosuperior rotator cuff tears (area under the curve 0.84, sensitivity 94%). Age, tear size, and function were the main predictors.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, prognostic retrospective case series.

articles.title: Bacterial contamination of mobile phones used by healthcare workers in intensive care units in Sudan: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To determine the prevalence and bacterial profile of contamination on mobile phones used by healthcare workers (HCWs) in intensive care units (ICUs) and to evaluate mobile phone disinfection practices in hospitals in Khartoum State, Sudan.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional laboratory-based study was conducted among 44 HCWs from ICUs in four hospitals in Khartoum State, Sudan. Mobile phone swabs were cultured on Blood and MacConkey agar, and bacterial isolates were identified using conventional methods. Factors associated with bacterial contamination were assessed.

RESULTS: Bacterial growth was detected in 31 (70.5%) mobile phones. Staphylococcus epidermidis was the predominant isolate (61.3%), followed by Staphylococcus aureus (12.9%), Micrococcus spp. (9.7%), Bacillus cereus (9.7%), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (6.5%). No significant associations were found between bacterial contamination and gender, healthcare worker category, duration of phone use, or phone use inside the ICU (p > 0.05). Regular phone disinfection was significantly associated with lower bacterial contamination (33.3% vs 80.0%, p = 0.012).

CONCLUSION: Mobile phone contamination among HCWs in ICUs was common. Regular phone disinfection significantly reduced bacterial contamination, emphasizing the importance of routine mobile phone decontamination as part of infection prevention and control practices.

articles.title: Characterization of Diabetic Retinopathy in Trimesters of Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the relationship between trimester of pregnancy and stage of diabetic retinopathy (DR) in a cohort of women with diabetes.

METHODS: In this single-center, retrospective cohort study, data were collected from adult women with diabetes who experienced a pregnancy at 5 timepoints: prepregnancy, each trimester, and postpregnancy. Progression, manifestation, and improvement of DR were tracked via logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 158 patients were analyzed. Among them, 13 (8.2%) showed progression to worse stage of DR during pregnancy, of whom 6.9%, 5.0%, and 14.3% had progression within the prepregnancy/first trimester, second trimester, and third trimester brackets, respectively, and 10.0% progressed postpregnancy; differences between the trimesters regarding incidence of DR progression were nonsignificant (P = .42). Of patients with no retinopathy at baseline, 4.62%, 7.69%, and 5.88% developed DR in each of the 3 trimesters, respectively, and 6.45% developed DR postpregnancy; differences in rates of DR manifestation were nonsignificant (P = .97).

CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy stage was not associated with risk of DR manifestation or progression in this cohort.

articles.title: Pregnancy outcome after first-trimester exposure to JAK inhibitors - an evaluation of the German Embryotox cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are increasingly being used in the management of autoimmune diseases across rheumatology, gastroenterology, and dermatology, including in women of childbearing age. Consequently, pregnancies occurring during JAKi treatment are becoming more common. However, uncertainties regarding their safety during pregnancy remain, and current human data are insufficient to allow a comprehensive assessment of fetal risk.

METHODS: Observational data of pregnancies with first trimester JAKi exposure, recorded in the German Embryotox database, was analyzed. Pregnancies were prospectively enrolled between January 1, 2017, and November 15, 2025. Study endpoints included major congenital anomalies, pregnancy loss, and neonatal parameters.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised a total of 44 pregnancies exposed to baricitinib (n = 17), filgotinib (n = 3), tofacitinib (n = 8), or upadacitinib (n = 16). A total of 32 live births were recorded. Among these, two major congenital anomalies were observed, one ventricular septal defect and one hypospadias. Five spontaneous abortions occurred, including one case of fetal anencephaly, and seven elective terminations of pregnancy were reported. Additional neonatal assessments revealed two preterm births at 36 weeks' gestation, three infants born small for gestational age, and two newborns large for gestational age.

CONCLUSIONS: The current evidence is insufficient to establish or exclude an association between JAK inhibitor exposure and adverse fetal outcomes. To date, the potential for harmful effects cannot be ruled out due to the limited available data. Therefore, routine use of JAKi during pregnancy is not recommended and treatment should be approached with caution, and requires a critical risk-benefit assessment until further data is obtained.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was retrospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on March 16, 2026 (DRKS00039622).

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Diabetes Status on Outcomes After Physiology-Guided Revascularization　- Insights From the J-PRIDE Registry.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of diabetes status on outcomes after physiology-guided revascularization remains unclear. This study evaluated clinical outcomes in patients with insulin-treated diabetes (ITD), non-ITD (NITD), and without diabetes after physiology-guided revascularization.

METHODS AND RESULTS: From the J-PRIDE registry, 3,140 patients were categorized into non-diabetes (n=1,797), NITD (n=1,133), and ITD (n=210) groups. The primary endpoint was the 1-year incidence of target vessel failure (TVF), a composite of cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target vessel revascularization. The 1-year TVF rate was significantly higher in the ITD and NITD groups than in the non-diabetes group (6.1% and 4.1% vs. 2.0%, respectively), with adjusted hazard ratios for the ITD and NTD groups of 2.14 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.19; P=0.027) and 1.63 (95 CI 1.02-2.61; P=0.041), respectively. The non-hyperemic pressure ratio cut-off predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80 was lower in the ITD than NITD and non-diabetes groups (0.87 vs. 0.89 and 0.90, respectively). The ITD group had the highest risk of TVF across all FFR values, followed by the NITD and non-diabetes groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ITD and NITD exhibit worse clinical outcomes than those without diabetes. Notably, patients with ITD remained at elevated risk across the entire FFR spectrum, suggesting that physiological severity alone may not fully capture their residual cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Current Status and Future Directions of Cardiovascular Intensive Care in Japan: Workforce, Structure, Education, and Regional Disparities　- Report of the Japan Critical Care Cardiology Committee (J4CS).
authors: Japanese Circulation Society Emergency and Critical Care Committee
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: Rapid population aging has increased the number of patients with severe acute cardiovascular diseases requiring intensive care. Contemporary cardiovascular intensive care has evolved beyond traditional management of acute coronary syndromes to encompass hemodynamic instability, multiple organ dysfunction, and advanced life-support technologies. Accordingly, cardiovascular intensive care units (CICUs) must provide comprehensive, tailored critical care for increasingly complex clinical conditions. In Japan, cardiovascular intensive care remains heterogeneous, with critically ill patients managed in various critical care settings. Structured care systems and specialist training remain underdeveloped. To clarify the current status, we reviewed nationwide survey data from the JROAD-DPC database. Substantial variability in institutional care systems, limited availability of dedicated cardiac care units/CICUs, and marked regional disparities in infrastructure and human resources were identified. Intensive care unit admission was associated with lower in-hospital mortality in cardiovascular emergencies, although these observational findings should be interpreted with caution because of potential residual confounding, differences in patient characteristics, and end-of-life care pathways. These findings support the need for appropriate triage and resource allocation according to patient acuity and institutional capability, rather than the uniform establishment of dedicated CICUs. Addressing these challenges will require optimized resource allocation, strengthened regional coordination, and structured training programs to establish sustainable cardiovascular intensive care systems in Japan.

articles.title: Whole-body MRI with DWIBS and choline PET/CT for detecting oligoprogressive castration-resistant prostate cancer recurrence.
articles.abstract: The diagnostic options for patients with advanced prostate cancer have expanded with the development of next-generation imaging modalities. These include whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI) with diffusion-weighted whole-body imaging with background body signal suppression (DWIBS) and molecular positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) using choline or prostate-specific membrane antigen radiotracers. Such modalities improve the detection of whole-body nodal and bony metastases in patients with advanced prostate cancer. A 63-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) underwent stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) targeting two pelvic nodal metastases identified by WB-MRI with DWIBS and subsequently confirmed by 11C-choline PET/CT. This case highlights the potential role of 11C-choline PET/CT and corresponding local treatment in the management of oligoprogressive CRPC.

articles.title: Treatment strategy for patients with cirrhosis complicated by esophageal varices and portal vein thrombosis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: ABSTRACTObjective : The optimal treatment strategy for patients with cirrhosis complicated by esophageal varices (EVs) and portal vein thrombosis (PVT) remains unclear. This study evaluated clinical outcomes according to treatment priority.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with cirrhosis who had PVT confirmed by contrast-enhanced computed tomography before endoscopic injection sclerotherapy for EVs. Patients were categorized into EV-first and PVT-first groups, and changes in thrombus burden and clinical outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Nineteen patients were included (EV-first, n = 10; PVT-first, n = 9). Baseline thrombus burden was greater in the PVT-first group. Thrombus reduction occurred more frequently in the PVT-first group (10% vs. 100%, p < 0.01). In the EV-first group, the maximum obstruction rate increased significantly (39.5% vs. 69%, p < 0.01), whereas it decreased in the PVT-first group (63% vs. 24%, p = 0.02). No variceal bleeding or other bleeding complications related to anticoagulant therapy or antithrombin III concentrate administration were observed during PVT treatment. After a median follow-up of 24 months, EV recurrence occurred only in the EV-first group and was associated with PVT enlargement.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, favorable thrombus outcomes were observed in patients who underwent PVT-first treatment when variceal therapy could be safely deferred.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
articles.abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

articles.title: [A systematic review and meta-analysis of effectiveness of influenza vaccine among healthcare workers].
articles.abstract: Objective: To systematically evaluate the protective effect of influenza vaccine among healthcare workers (HCW). Methods: Relevant literature from January 1, 2000 to November 4, 2025, was retrieved from China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, China National Biomedical Literature Service System, National Library of Medicine database, Dutch Medical Abstracts database, and Cochrane Collaboration Library. Two independent researchers screened the literature, extracted data and assessed the quality of the studies, based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Studies using cohort design and test-negative design were included. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A meta-analysis was performed using R software version 4.3.3, with vaccine effectiveness (VE) as the effect measure, to calculate the effectiveness of influenza vaccine among HCW. Results: A total of 24 articles involving 27 studies were included, analyzing the effectiveness of influenza vaccine among 38 855 HCW. Meta-analysis results showed that the VE (95%CI) was 33.26% (14.08%-48.15%) for cohort studies and 36.85% (9.05%-56.15%) for test-negative design studies. No statistically significant difference was observed between the two groups (χ²=0.05, P=0.814); thus data were pooled. The pooled effectiveness of influenza vaccine (95%CI) was 34.11% (18.69%-46.60%). Subgroup analysis revealed that the effectiveness against influenza-like illness (ILI) (95%CI) was 25.97% (1.88%-44.15%), while the effectiveness against laboratory-confirmed influenza cases (95%CI) was 42.68% (21.64%-58.07%). Additionally, sensitivity analysis indicated that the results were stable and not significantly affected by publication bias. Conclusion: The effectiveness of influenza vaccine among HCW is heterogeneous but generally moderate, particularly more pronounced in laboratory-confirmed cases.

articles.title: [Development and validation of a prediction model for postoperative recurrence risk of ovarian endometriotic cysts based on preoperative imaging and clinical biomarkers].
articles.abstract: Objective: To develop and validate a prediction model for the postoperative recurrence of ovarian endometriotic cysts based on preoperative imaging and clinical serum biomarkers. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted on 300 patients who underwent laparoscopic cystectomy at Shanxi Children's Hospital (Shanxi Maternal and Child Health Hospital) between June 2021 and June 2024. Patients were randomly assigned in a 7∶3 ratio to a training set (n=210) and an internal validation set (n=90) using a computer-generated random number method. Variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression; multivariable logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were constructed; the predictive ability, accuracy, and clinical applicability of the model were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The 300 patients had a mean age of (34.2±5.8) years. The median follow-up duration was 28 months (interquartile range: 24-38 months; range: 12-48 months), and recurrence occurred in 75 patients (25.0%) during the follow-up period. LASSO regression identified 10 predictive variables. Subsequent multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that age<35 years (OR=3.24, 95%CI: 1.74-6.03), revised American Fertility Society (r-AFS) stage Ⅲ-Ⅳ (OR=3.42, 95%CI: 1.81-6.47), maximum cyst diameter≥6 cm (OR=2.89, 95%CI: 1.61-5.19), bilateral involvement (OR=2.56, 95%CI: 1.41-4.65), apparent diffusion coefficient<1.2×10-3 mm²/s (OR=2.31, 95%CI: 1.31-4.08), CA-125>70 U/ml (OR=2.78, 95%CI: 1.56-4.96), and absence of postoperative pharmacological treatment (OR=4.15, 95%CI: 2.18-7.89) were risk factors for postoperative recurrence, while the duration of pharmacological treatment was a protective factor (OR=0.88, 95%CI: 0.79-0.97) (all P<0.05). The AUC for the three models in the internal validation set were 0.839 (95%CI: 0.759-0.919), 0.876 (95%CI: 0.805-0.947), and 0.894 (95%CI:0.829-0.959), respectively; the XGBoost model outperformed the multivariate logistic regression model (P=0.008), whereas the difference compared with the Random Forest model was not statistically significant (P=0.162). All three models demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test χ² values: 6.83, 5.92, and 5.14; P-values: 0.555, 0.656, and 0.743, respectively). Within the threshold probability range of 10% to 60%, the extreme gradient boosting model yielded the highest net benefit. Conclusion: The extreme gradient boosting model exhibits good predictive performance for the postoperative recurrence of ovarian endometriotic cysts and can serve as a reference for risk stratification and personalized follow-up.

articles.title: [Several recommendations on the procedure and clinical application of the oral high-fat tolerance test].
articles.abstract: The sole measurement of fasting blood lipids fails to capture the complete profile of an individual's lipid metabolism. Postprandial lipid levels are strongly correlated with multiple diseases, including diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The oral high-fat tolerance test (OFTT) is a clinical method used to evaluate postprandial lipid metabolism by analyzing changes in postprandial blood lipid levels after subjects consume a fixed high-fat meal. It facilitates early clinical screening of individuals with normal fasting lipids but who already have reduced fat tolerance and postprandial dyslipidemia, which is of great significance for early intervention and the early prevention and management of diabetes, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, and other conditions. Currently, there is no unified international or domestic standard for the OFTT procedure and result interpretation, which limits its application and promotion.This manuscript drawing on relevant domestic and international literature and practical experience from experts in the field, proposes several recommendations for the procedure and clinical application of the OFTT, aims to promote the standardization and unification of the OFTT, providing guidance and reference for the early screening and timely intervention of dyslipidemia.

articles.title: [Identification of risk factors and prevention strategies for perioperative stroke].
articles.abstract: Perioperative stroke refers to embolic, thrombotic, or hemorrhagic cerebrovascular disease occurring during surgery or within 30 days postoperatively, which can lead to disability or death in patients. This review systematically describes the pathogenesis, risk factor identification, and prevention and treatment strategies for perioperative stroke. The pathogenesis of perioperative ischemic stroke involves multiple pathological processes including thromboembolism, hemodynamic disturbances, inflammatory responses, and blood-brain barrier disruption. Risk factors include patient-related factors, surgical factors, and anesthesia management factors. Prevention strategies emphasize preoperative precise identification of high-risk patients using risk assessment tools and predictive models, optimizing control of underlying diseases; intraoperative maintenance of hemodynamic stability, implementation of cerebral oxygen saturation monitoring, and timely detection of cerebral ischemia; postoperative establishment of neurological function monitoring systems, adoption of standardized stroke screening tools to achieve early identification and timely intervention. Establishing multidisciplinary collaboration mechanisms, implementing effective perioperative management, and exploring novel neuroprotective targets and intervention strategies are key to reducing perioperative stroke incidence and improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: A Qualitative Descriptive Study of Motivation States for Physical Activity Among Middle-Aged Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midlife adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) face unique physiological and psychological challenges when balancing physical activity and rest.
