The Wants and Aversions for Neuromuscular Tasks model accounts for competing desires and aversions for movement and rest, addressing the limitations of general physical activity frameworks. Thus, we employed a qualitative descriptive study guided by the Wants and Aversions for Neuromuscular Tasks model to explore momentary motivational states governing movement and rest among midlife adults with T1DM following an exercise-support intervention.

METHODS: We conducted semistructured interviews with 23 midlife adults with T1DM (mean age 48, SD 11 y, 78% female, 91% non-Hispanic white, 35% overweight, and 26% obese). Through directed content analysis, we employed deductive Wants and Aversions for Neuromuscular Tasks framework-driven and inductive coding to map participant reflections.

RESULTS: The overarching themes mapped across the 4 quadrants revealed complex dynamics. In quadrant 1 (dread move, crave rest), participants expressed motivational conflicts driven by fatigue, device malfunctions, and glucose excursions, often opting for light movement to restore energy. Quadrant 2 (dread move, dread rest), obligation-driven resistance transformed into pride and gratification upon completion. Quadrant 3 (crave move, crave rest), participants opted for activities like yoga or outdoor walks for active recovery. In quadrant 4 (crave move, dread rest), individuals found flow in enjoyable activities and articulated an internal drive to exercise conflicting with physical fatigue or glycemic levels necessitating rest.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings underscore the dynamic nature of desires and aversions of movement and rest among midlife adults with T1DM. These insights can inform future physical activity interventions.

articles.title: Discovery of benzoxazole derivatives as novel α-synuclein aggregate ligands with potential for PET tracer development.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, and the abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) constitutes its core pathological hallmark. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of cerebral α-Syn aggregates holds great promise for the early diagnosis of PD. However, the imaging quality critically depends on the ligands with high binding affinity and selectivity for α-Syn aggregates. In this work, we developed a new type of benzoxazole-based α-Syn aggregate ligands via an SPR-based screening. Among them, candidates D15 (KD = 0.12 μM) and D16 (KD = 0.08 μM) exhibited high binding affinities for α-Syn aggregates in vitro and good potency in the SH-SY5Y cellular model and brain tissues from α-Syn PFF-injected PD mouse models, as well as excellent selectivity for tau and Aβ aggregates in rTg4510 and APP23 transgenic mouse brain sections. Thanks to their favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and suitable structures for radiolabeling for PET imaging, these new ligands represent promising candidates for the development of α-Syn PET radiotracers, offering a valuable foundation for the early diagnosis of PD and related synucleinopathies.

articles.title: Discovery of novel Lac-Phe derivatives with improved oral exposure for the treatment of metabolic syndrome.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) comprises interrelated dysfunctions linked to diabetes, obesity, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), posing a growing public health burden. Lac-Phe is an exercise-inducible metabolite that suppresses feeding and obesity reported in Nature, but Lac-Phe exhibited poor appetite-suppressing effect upon oral administration due to its insufficient metabolic stability. To improve the appetite-suppressing effect and metabolic stability of Lac-Phe, we introduced d-amino acid and performed a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR) study. Compound 18 was identified on the basis of its superior metabolic stability and pronounced appetite suppression. Moreover, compound 18 exhibited potent dual functional inhibition on GPR40/GPR120, two "fat addiction" receptors. Compound 18 ameliorated obesity and fatty liver through modulation of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling axis and induction of liver autophagy. Collectively, these findings establish compound 18 as a promising candidate and provide a strong basis for designing new therapeutics for MetS.

articles.title: Benign enlargement of subarachnoid spaces (BESS) is not associated to bridging vein rupture/thrombosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is some controversy as to whether benign enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces (BESS) in infants predisposes to bridging vein rupture/thrombosis and subdural hematomas following minor trauma.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prevalence of subdural collections and bridging vein rupture/thrombosis in infants with BESS undergoing brain MRI for macrocephaly more or less rapid increase in head circumference.

METHODS: In a single-center retrospective observational study, infants younger than one year who underwent brain MRI for macrocephaly (head circumference > 2 SD) more or less rapid head circumference increase, between January 2017 and August 2023, were included. Early preterm infants and those with incomplete MRI protocols were excluded. MRI was reviewed for subarachnoid space enlargement, subdural collections and bridging vein abnormalities. BESS was defined by a craniocortical distance above 5 mm.

RESULTS: Of 92 infants, 78 were diagnosed with BESS. Six infants with BESS (7.7%) had unilateral or bilateral non-compressive subdural collections: fluid-like signal intensity (n = 4), intermediate signal intensity (n = 1) or a hemorrhagic component with a hypointense rim (n = 1) without bridging vein abnormalities or vertex clots. In this last case, the child had no reported previous trauma and no acute clinical symptoms but had hypotonia. No history of trauma or acute clinical symptoms was reported and no direct or indirect MRI signs of bridging vein rupture or thrombosis were identified in any infant, including those with subdural collection.

CONCLUSIONS: Non-traumatic BESS may be associated with non-compressive subdural fluid collections but not with imaging evidence of direct or indirect signs of bridging vein rupture.

articles.title: Modified NUTRIC score and clinical outcomes in critically ill medical patients: A prospective cohort study in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
articles.abstract: Malnutrition and nutritional risk are prevalent among critically ill patients. However, research from medical intensive care units (ICUs) in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Western Balkans is scarce. This study sought to compare clinical characteristics, laboratory results, and hospital outcomes in critically ill medical patients, differentiating between those with low and high modified Nutrition Risk in the Critically Ill (mNUTRIC) scores. This prospective, single-center observational cohort study enrolled 102 adult patients admitted to a tertiary medical ICU from July 2025 to January 2026. The mNUTRIC score was evaluated within 48 hours of ICU admission, categorizing patients into low-score (0-4) and high-score (5-9) groups. A high mNUTRIC score was observed in 67 patients (65.7%). Compared to the low-score group, these patients exhibited greater illness severity, more comorbidities, less favorable laboratory findings, longer ICU stays (median: 11 vs. 7 days; p = 0.019), and extended durations of mechanical ventilation (median: 6 vs. 4 days; p = 0.037). No significant differences were found between the groups for overall hospital mortality (56.7% vs. 42.9%; p = 0.183) or ICU mortality (22.4% vs. 28.6%; p = 0.491). Among ICU survivors, post-ICU mortality was higher in the high-score group (44.2% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.038), though this observation was drawn from a specific subgroup. In this exploratory cohort, a high mNUTRIC score identified patients with increased clinical severity, longer ICU admissions, and prolonged mechanical ventilation. However, it did not independently predict mortality. The study could not ascertain the impact of mNUTRIC-guided nutritional interventions due to the lack of assessment of nutritional intake and interventions.

articles.title: Nighttime Symptom Burden in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Nighttime symptoms are clinically important but understudied in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). This study explored patients' perceptions of nighttime symptoms, their effects on daily life, and symptom-management strategies.

METHODS: Thirty U.S. adults with COPD and moderate-to-high symptom burden (COPD Assessment Test score ≥10), without hospitalization or emergency department visits for severe exacerbation during the previous year, participated in semi-structured interviews. All participants received single-inhaler dual or triple maintenance therapy and completed the 7-item COPD and Asthma Sleep Impact Scal. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and thematically analyzed using the Symptom Management Theory framework.

RESULTS: Participants (median age 63; 60% female; 90% White) reported a high burden of nighttime symptoms and sleep disruption (87% severely impacted based on CASIS). Participants described a pronounced nighttime symptom experience, most frequently shortness of breath, mucus/phlegm production, coughing, and difficulty staying asleep or frequent awakenings. A range of symptom management strategies was reported, including behavioral adaptations (routines, avoidance of technology, sleep hygiene), pharmacological management (antidepressants, sleep medications, rescue inhalers), and complementary and integrative approaches (meditation, acupuncture, relaxation techniques). Nighttime symptom outcomes extended beyond sleep disruption. Participants reported significant daytime consequences, including fatigue and impaired concentration. These effects contributed to activity avoidance and limitations in social participation.

CONCLUSION: Among symptomatic patients receiving single-inhaler dual or triple maintenance therapy, nighttime COPD symptoms were commonly reported and were associated with substantial physical, emotional, and functional impacts. The findings support further consideration of nighttime symptoms in clinical assessment and individualized COPD management.

articles.title: Comparison of Nebulized Long-Acting Muscarinic Antagonist Revefenacin to Ipratropium in COPD Patients With Acute Respiratory Failure Requiring Mechanical Ventilation: Results of the RARICO Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Revefenacin is a nebulized long-acting muscarinic antagonist approved for maintenance therapy in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We conducted a pilot study to evaluate the feasibility and safety of revefenacin in mechanically ventilated COPD patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF), and compare its use with the short-acting muscarinic antagonist ipratropium, the current standard inpatient therapy.

METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized controlled pilot study, intubated COPD patients were assigned to revefenacin 175mcg once daily plus three placebo doses, or ipratropium 500mcg via vibrating mesh nebulizer every 6 hours, for up to 7 days. The primary endpoints were safety and feasibility; exploratory endpoints included ventilator-derived respiratory mechanics and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-one patients (mean age 76±11 years, 60±51 pack years smoking, percent-predicted FEV1 56±26%) were randomized to revefenacin (N=12) or ipratropium (N=9). Duration of mechanical ventilation was similar between groups (2.5±2.3 vs 3.6±2.8 days; P=0.83), with similar number of administered doses (2.8±2.1 vs 14.2±11.1; P=0.74). Daily nebulization time was significantly lower with revefenacin (7.2±1.0 vs 26.8±5.3 minutes; P<0.01). Adverse events were infrequent and comparable between the groups. Revefenacin improved dynamic resistance (Rdyn) post-dose (-0.9 vs +2.6 cmH₂O/L/s; P<0.01), without differences in peak inspiratory, resistive, or plateau pressures.

CONCLUSION: Once-daily nebulized revefenacin is a feasible and safe alternative to ipratropium in mechanically ventilated COPD patients with ARF, with reduced time spent on nebulization adminitration. Improvements in airway resistance suggest a potential physiologic benefit, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Changes of serum fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) and Klotho in diabetic kidney disease and their correlation with coronary artery calcification: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association among fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), Klotho, and coronary artery calcification (CAC) in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 176 DKD patients and 160 age-and diabetes-matched controls were retrospectively analyzed. We measured serum FGF23 and Klotho levels by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and assessed CAC by CAC scoring. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of these biomarkers with CAC and their ability to discriminate CAC.

RESULTS: FGF23 levels were significantly higher and Klotho levels were lower in patients with DKD than in controls. FGF23 correlated negatively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and positively with the albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen, whereas Klotho correlated positively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively with albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen. In patients with CAC, FGF23 levels were higher and Klotho levels were lower. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that both FGF23 and Klotho discriminated CAC, and FGF23 showed a higher area under curve than Klotho. Correlation analysis further confirmed the association of FGF23 and Klotho with CAC severity.

CONCLUSION: FGF23 and Klotho were associated with renal impairment and CAC in patients with DKD and may serve as potential biomarkers of renal and cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: The impact of recreational beach tennis associated with nutritional counseling on cardiometabolic risk factors in adolescents: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether combining nutritional counseling with recreational sports confers greater improvements in cardiovascular risk factors among adolescents compared to recreational sports alone.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This 12-week randomized clinical trial included 40 adolescents (aged 11-14 years; 67% female; 45% overweight/obese) randomly assigned to a beach tennis (BT, n = 20) or BT plus nutrition counseling (BT+N, n = 20) group. Sports sessions (BT) were performed twice a week and nutritional counseling (BT+N) once a week. Outcomes assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks included biochemical parameters (high- and low-density lipoprotein, total cholesterol; triglycerides; fasting glucose; and insulin), blood pressure, and body composition. Analyses were performed following the intention-to-treat principle.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significantly higher high-density lipoprotein levels (BT: +3.8 mg/dL, p < 0.05; BT+N: +5.9 mg/dL, p < 0.001) and no differences between groups. Fasting glucose decreased only in the BT+N group. Time x group interactions significantly differed between groups for triglycerides (p < 0.01), waist circumference (p < 0.001), body fat percentage (p < 0.05), and systolic blood pressure (p < 0.001), favoring the BT+N group. No significant changes were observed in low-density lipoprotein, total cholesterol, or insulin levels.

CONCLUSION: Recreational BT alone improved some cardiometabolic parameters; however, its combination with nutritional counseling provided broader benefits, underscoring the value of integrated lifestyle interventions for reducing cardiometabolic risk factors in adolescents.

articles.title: Thymic hyperplasia in patients with acromegaly: imaging-based assessment and clinical implications.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to compare thymus visibility and volume in patients with acromegaly to those of controls, and to evaluate the correlation between growth hormone (GH), insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels, and thymus volume.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional case-control study included 66 patients with acromegaly who underwent thoracic computed tomography scans. An age- and sex-matched control group of 65 trauma patients without comorbidities was selected. All thoracic computed tomography scans were reassessed to measure thymus volume using imaging software. Comparisons of thymus volume and assessment of correlation with GH and IGF-1 levels were performed.

RESULTS: The acromegaly group (28F/38M) and the control group (27F/38M) had similar sex and age distributions. The thymus was more frequently detectable in the acromegaly group (80.3%) compared to controls (44.6%; p = 0.001). Thymus volume was significantly higher in the acromegaly group (13.1 cm3 [9.7-18.7]) than in the control (10.3 cm3 [4.6-12.3]; p = 0.013). Serum IGF-1 levels were nearly significantly higher in acromegalic patients with a visible thymus compared to those without (visible thymus: 608.5 ng/mL [377.6-921.8]; non-visible thymus: 440.5 ng/mL [201.5-596]; p = 0.054). However, no significant differences were found in GH and IGF-1 upper limit of normal levels. No correlation was found between thymus volume and other parameters.

CONCLUSION: Patients with acromegaly have larger and more frequently visible thymus glands than controls. When a mass is detected in the anterior mediastinum, acromegaly should be considered, especially before invasive procedures.

articles.title: Conduction System Pacing for Resynchronization Therapy in Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a promising modality for cardiac resynchronization therapy, but evidence of CSP in heart failure (HF) remains controversial.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CSP, including left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and His bundle pacing, to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in HF.

METHODS: The MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included clinical endpoints (HHF, all-cause mortality), cardiac resynchronization therapy responses (predefined and super-response), echocardiographic parameters (left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular end-systolic volume), electrophysiologic parameters (paced QRS duration and capture threshold), functional status (NYHA functional class and 6-minute walk test distance), procedural performance (procedural time, fluoroscopy time, lead implantation time), and device-related complications. (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261388077).

RESULTS: Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 1,054 patients (566 CSP and 488 BiVP) were included. CSP showed a significant reduction in primary composite endpoint (OR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.18-0.52; I2 = 0%), improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean difference: 3.06%; 95% CI: 0.82%-5.30%; I2 = 55%), and shorter paced QRS duration (mean difference:-11.49 ms; 95% CI: -20.70 to -2.28; I2 = 85%), compared with BiVP. In the LBBAP group, there were greater reductions in primary composite endpoint with higher rates of super-response (OR: 2.18; 95% CI: 1.44-3.30; I2 = 54%) compared with BiVP. No differences were observed in functional status or device-related complications.

CONCLUSIONS: CSP, and potentially LBBAP, was associated with a significantly lower composite endpoint of HHF and all-cause mortality compared with BiVP, supporting CSP as an alternative to BiVP in HF.

articles.title: Navigating Suicide-Related Online Content in Individuals With Lived Experience of Suicidality: Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Engagement with suicide-related content online is often assumed to be harmful, yet many individuals with lived experience describe such content as supportive or even life-preserving. Despite policy and clinical concerns, little is known about how people intentionally or unintentionally encounter this content, how they interpret it, and how these experiences shape perceived harm or benefit.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to explore how intent and context influence the ways in which individuals with lived experience of suicidality encounter, interpret, and respond to suicide-related online content, and to identify factors associated with perceived harm and benefit.

METHODS: An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted with a convenience sample of 713 UK-based participants aged 16 to 60 years and older, 95.9% (n=684) of whom reported having lived experience of suicidality. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including chi-square tests, to examine associations between engagement patterns, intent, and suicidality. Free-text responses were coded using content analysis to identify categories relating to motivations for engagement, emotional responses, and perceived impact.

RESULTS: Participants reported a broad range of experiences. While 30.0% (214/713) described suicide-related content as contributing to suicidal thoughts or attempts, others reported relief, validation, or reduced feelings of isolation, with 21.0% (150/713) attributing content to preventing an attempt. Clear differences emerged between participants who actively sought out content ("seekers") and those who encountered it unintentionally ("stumblers"). Seekers more frequently reported positive or understanding responses, often in the context of unmet offline support needs, whereas stumblers were more likely to report shock or distress. Approximately 39.9% (151/378) of participants described their engagement as neither intentional nor accidental, potentially reflecting a blurred boundary between passive exposure and active seeking, as well as the difficulty individuals face in accurately identifying and articulating their own motivations in relation to suicidality.

CONCLUSIONS: Engagement with suicide-related online content cannot be characterized as uniformly harmful. Outcomes depend on user intent, emotional state, and the context of engagement, and they may change over time. Clinical, regulatory, and policy approaches should move beyond risk-only frameworks to account for the nuanced and sometimes supportive roles such content plays in how individuals make sense of suicidal thoughts, while still protecting those at risk.

articles.title: Skull Base Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiology, Microbiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull base osteomyelitis (SBO) is a life-threatening infection arising predominantly from necrotizing external otitis, producing progressive osteitis of the temporal and central skull base. Originally described in elderly diabetic patients, its demographic profile has broadened to encompass immunocompromised hosts of diverse etiologies. Although historical mortality exceeded 50%, advances in imaging, microbiology, and antimicrobial therapy have improved prognosis substantially.

OBJECTIVES: To systematically review the epidemiology, microbiology, clinical features, diagnostic modalities, therapeutic strategies, and outcomes of SBO and to identify evidence gaps requiring further investigation.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library (inception to March 2025, updated to March 2026) was performed. Studies reporting primary data on SBO (n >=5 patients) with defined diagnostic criteria, microbiological findings, treatment protocols, and outcome measures were included. Two independent reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Findings are presented as a narrative synthesis per PRISMA 2020 guidelines. For the outcomes most consistently reported in primary cohorts, a random-effects meta-analysis of pooled proportions (DerSimonian-Laird, logit scale) was additionally performed.

RESULTS: Forty-five studies encompassing 1,628 patients met inclusion criteria. The median patient age was 68 years (IQR 57-76); diabetes mellitus was present in 74.2%. Pseudomonas aeruginosa predominated (62.4%), with ciprofloxacin-resistant strains identified in 11.3% of post-2000 series. Fungal SBO, principally Aspergillus spp., accounted for 7.8% of cases and was consistently associated with higher mortality across reported series. Gallium-67 scintigraphy demonstrated the highest sensitivity (94%) for treatment monitoring; FDG-PET/CT sensitivity exceeded 96%. Combined fluoroquinolone-based therapy yielded a cure rate of 71.4%. Evidence for adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy remains limited to uncontrolled series and a single small comparative study, with no randomized trials, so its efficacy is unproven. The overall mortality was 15.3%. In a proportion meta-analysis of primary cohorts, pooled estimates were: diabetes 82.4% (95% CI 68.2-91.1), Pseudomonas aeruginosa 55.6% (48.4-62.6), clinical cure 84.7% (74.6-91.2), cranial nerve involvement 28.0% (16.1-43.9), and mortality 8.4% (4.3-15.8).

CONCLUSIONS: SBO remains a serious condition requiring multimodal diagnostic evaluation and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Emerging fluoroquinolone resistance constitutes a pressing clinical challenge. Standardized diagnostic criteria, prospective multicenter trials, and consensus treatment protocols are urgently required.

articles.title: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of Statin-Naïve Anti-HMGCR Myopathy: Case Series and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-associated myopathy is a rare form of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy most commonly reported in patients exposed to statins. However, its occurrence in statin-naïve individuals is increasingly recognized but remains underreported. We describe two unusual cases of statin-naïve anti-HMGCR myopathy presenting with severe rhabdomyolysis, leading to acute kidney injury in one patient and dropped head syndrome in another, emphasizing that anti-HMGCR IMNM should be suspected even in statin-naïve individuals presenting with unexplained myopathy, rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI, or axial muscle weakness such as dropped head syndrome, as early immunotherapy may significantly improve outcomes.

articles.title: Hypoxemia-Associated Cerebral Microbleeds in Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
Food and water as potential vectors of Helicobacter pylori infection among Yemeni children.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infection presents a considerable public health issue in Yemen, particularly as it is predominantly contracted in early childhood. Our objective was to assess the prevalence of H. pylori in stool samples of children and adolescents under 18 years of age in the Dhamar Governorate, and to detect H. pylori in drinking water samples and food samples (red meat, chicken meat, salad, and vegetables) from different locations in Dhamar Governorate. This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence of H. pylori infection in stool samples from 500 patients aged under 18 years, focusing on various demographic and environmental factors in Dhamar City, Yemen. Additionally, we collected 50 drinking water samples and 150 food samples (red meat, chicken meat, salad, and vegetables) from different locations in Dhamar Governorate (50 samples each). Our results revealed an overall prevalence of 24.7%, with many individuals presenting with gastroduodenal disorders. The prevalence of H. pylori in people under 18 years old was 16.4%. However, no significant associations were found between infection and gender, residence, drinking water source, outdoor eating habit, socioeconomic status, or diet type (p>0.05). A significant relationship was observed between infection, households, and age (p<0.05). In terms of seasonality, spring and fall were both associated with higher prevalence. These findings highlight the urgent need for targeted public health interventions in Yemen to address the high rates of H. pylori infection among vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Atrial Cardiomyopathy in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: From Compensation to Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: A Massive Open Online Course for Primary Prevention of Stroke: Evaluation of Co-Design Process.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Public awareness and understanding of stroke are crucial to reducing its overall burden. Massive open online courses (MOOCs) are free, self-directed online learning platforms that provide accessible education.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the process, outcomes, and evaluation of co-designing the Preventing Stroke MOOC.

METHODS: The co-design process was conducted with various stakeholder groups from July 2020 to December 2024 in Australia over three phases: (1) predesign, (2) co-design, and (3) postdesign. In the predesign phase, we consulted with MOOC researchers and held a half-day in-person workshop with community members to prioritize the stroke prevention topics, structure, format, and features, followed by user testing of a single developed module. The larger study comprised 16 virtual focus groups (14 co-design and 2 user testing focus groups) with community members and health knowledge experts. Of the 14 co-design focus groups, 12 informed the MOOC design, including content, structure, and delivery. This was followed by drafting content for each module, expert review (eg, clinicians and researchers), and development of platform materials. In the postdesign phase, we conducted user testing to collect feedback and evaluated the co-design process to determine how participants' input shaped the final MOOC design.

RESULTS: In the predesign phase, 5 MOOC experts and community members contributed to a pilot module comprising 9 pages on the prioritized topics, including a focus on stories from people with lived experience of stroke. A total of 8 people tested this module, providing positive feedback about content and delivery. The co-design phase engaged 22 participants across 12 focus groups relevant to the MOOC. Their suggestions contributed to the multimedia design of the 7 core modules, with personalization via 9 optional mini-modules. Feedback on technical issues and suggested improvements identified during postdesign user testing were resolved. Evaluation of the MOOC co-design process found that the majority of participants' suggestions gathered during the co-design phase were included in the final MOOC.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured, co-design process resulted in the Preventing Stroke MOOC reflecting participants' suggestions and provided important insights on the educational information needed to inform the general population about stroke prevention.

articles.title: Individually Prescribed In-Bed Exergaming Using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure in Posttransplant Inpatients With Marked Functional Impairment After Intensive Care: Prospective Single-Arm Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early rehabilitation is important after transplantation and critical illness, but profound weakness, fatigue, and motivational, psychological, and safety barriers may limit participation. Exergaming may facilitate rehabilitation, but the feasibility of full-body in-bed exergaming in this population remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the feasibility and observed safety of individually prescribed in-bed exergaming using Nintendo Ring Fit Adventure (NFA; Nintendo Co, Ltd) in posttransplant inpatients after intensive care unit (ICU) care.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm interventional feasibility study (October 2024-October 2025) enrolled 26 posttransplant adults with prior ICU care and Functional Ambulation Category (FAC) scores ≤3. Participants were referred after ward transfer by transplant-team advanced practice nurses, and the principal investigator confirmed eligibility based on prespecified inclusion and exclusion criteria. Ten individually prescribed, supervised in-bed NFA sessions, each scheduled for 30 minutes, including setup and operation, were planned alongside usual physical therapy. Data were obtained from medical records, standardized session logs, and prespecified clinical and questionnaire assessments. Outcomes included retention; session delivery, completion, and interruptions; exercise-item completion and interruptions; session-terminating adverse events; net exercise time; satisfaction; and exploratory strength, mobility, and health-related quality-of-life changes.

RESULTS: Participants (mean age 53.0, SD 12.4 y; 14 men) included 23 liver and 3 bilateral lung transplant recipients. Mean ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration were 24.3 (SD 11.0) days and 21.3 (SD 11.6) days, respectively; median baseline FAC and Medical Research Council Sum Score were 0.5 (IQR 0.0-1.0) and 38.0 (IQR 30.5-42.0), respectively. None had an FAC score above 2. Twenty completed the final assessment (20/26, 76.9%, 95% CI 57.9%-89%). Of 227 delivered sessions, 223 (98.2%, 95% CI 95.8%-100%) were completed. Of 2161 prescribed exercise items, 2072 (95.9%, 95% CI 93.4%-97.9%) were completed. No session-terminating adverse events were observed (0/227, 0%, 95% CI 0%-1.6%). Median within-participant net exercise time increased by 159.0 (IQR 35.5-296.3) seconds from sessions 1 to 10 (95% CI 81.0-284.0; Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P<.001). Friedman tests followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (2-sided α=.05) showed baseline-to-final median within-participant changes of 8.0 Medical Research Council Sum Score points (IQR 2.3-10.3; 95% CI 4.0-10.0, P=.004), 2.0 Intensive Care Unit Mobility Scale points (IQR 1.0-4.3; 95% CI 1.0-3.5, P<.001), and 15.0 EQ-VAS points (IQR 0.0-30.0; 95% CI 5.0-25.0, P=.009). Questionnaire responses were favorable.

CONCLUSIONS: Under therapist supervision, the individually prescribed in-bed NFA program showed favorable operational feasibility, with no session-terminating adverse events. By combining the accessibility of a commercial off-the-shelf exergame with individualized exercise prescription, the program extended bedside exergaming to posttransplant inpatients with substantial functional impairment after ICU care who had not achieved independent ambulation.

articles.title: Association of Intrinsic Capacity Decline with Frailty, Polypharmacy, Nutritional Status, and Fall Risk among Older Adults: A Cross-sectional Study from a Tertiary Care Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrinsic capacity reflects an individual's physical and mental abilities and influencing healthy aging; its decline often precedes disability and is linked with frailty, malnutrition, polypharmacy, and falls.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary care center in Western Maharashtra, India, among 165 adults aged 60 years and above. Participants were enrolled by consecutive sampling. Sociodemographic details, comorbidities, medication use, fall history, and functional parameters were recorded. Intrinsic capacity was assessed across cognition, locomotion, vitality/nutrition, vision, hearing, and psychological domains. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale, nutritional status using the Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form (MNA-SF), and data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.0.

RESULTS: The mean age was 72.77 ± 9.14 years. Intrinsic capacity decline was present in 147 (89.1%) participants, with severe decline in 76 (46.1%). Locomotion was the most commonly impaired domain (106, 64.2%), followed by vitality/nutrition (74, 44.8%) and psychological domain (61, 37.0%). The mean BMI was 22.49 ± 3.83 kg/m2, the mean number of current medications was 4.32 ± 2.09, the mean Timed Up and Go duration was 12.98 ± 3.26 s, the mean MNA-SF score was 11.58 ± 2.01, the mean Clinical Frailty Scale score was 4.27 ± 1.57, and the mean number of impaired intrinsic capacity domains was 2.29 ± 1.34. Intrinsic capacity decline was significantly associated with frailty, nutritional status, polypharmacy, and fall risk.

CONCLUSION: Intrinsic capacity decline was highly prevalent among older adults. Routine multidomain geriatric assessment may help identify vulnerable individuals and guide early preventive interventions.

articles.title: Algorithmic Reflectivity in Large Language Models: Methodological Study of Linguistic Structure in Mentalization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mentalization is a core human capacity involving interpretation of one's own and others' behavior in terms of underlying mental states. Within the mentalization-based treatment (MBT) framework, it is described along multiple dimensions, integrating cognitive, affective, relational, and regulatory processes. Large language models (LLMs) can generate linguistically reflective discourse, raising the question of whether the formal linguistic structure of mentalization can bbe reproduced without experiential and affective processes.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess whether an LLM can generate mentalization profiles structurally coherent with MBT dimensions and recognized as formally mentalizing by expert clinicians. Specifically, it evaluated the structural and argumentative coherence of model-generated profiles and the level of agreement among MBT-trained psychiatrists. It also examined the distinction between psychological mentalization and algorithmic reflectivity, conceptualized as a formally coherent but nonexperiential linguistic phenomenon.

METHODS: A comparative, descriptive methodological design was adopted. A total of 50 human-model dialogues were generated under standardized conditions. At the end of each interaction, the model produced a narrative mentalization profile structured along MBT dimensions. Five MBT-trained psychiatrists independently evaluated each profile using anonymized materials. Ratings covered 4 canonical MBT axes and 2 additional higher-order dimensions-regulatory functions and synthetic profile. For each dimension, they assigned separate Likert-scale ratings for evaluative and argumentative coherence. Descriptive statistics were computed at dialogue level. Interrater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), primarily ICC(3,k), with CIs. The association between evaluative and argumentative coherence was examined using Pearson correlation coefficients with 95% CIs, with Spearman rank correlation as a robustness check.

RESULTS: Across dimensions, mean scores ranged from 3.63 (SD 0.63) to 3.98 (SD 0.31), indicating moderate-to-high structural coherence. Interrater reliability was moderate to good, with ICC(3,k) values ranging from 0.60 to 0.84 in the evaluative domain. The highest scores were observed for implicit-explicit and synthetic profile, whereas internal-external showed the lowest mean. Score distributions showed limited variability and concentration in the upper range of the scale. Evaluative and argumentative coherence were strongly associated across all MBT dimensions, with Pearson r ranging from 0.826 to 0.967 (all P<.001) and Spearman ρ ranging from 0.866 to 0.991. Informal qualitative comments frequently described the outputs as linguistically organized and clinically interpretable, while also noting limited affective variability and contextual integration.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that LLMs can reproduce the formal linguistic structure of reflective discourse, generating outputs perceived by clinicians as coherent and clinically interpretable across multiple dimensions of mentalization. However, within the present evaluative framework, this performance appears more consistent with structural language regularities than with evidence of experiential, affective, or intentional processes. These results support using LLMs as research and training tools for studying the linguistic aspects of mentalization, while highlighting the continuing importance of human clinical judgment in contexts requiring emotional, relational, and contextual integration.

articles.title: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Antifungal Susceptibility of Candidemia Patients in Various Intensive Care Unit's of a Tertiary Care Hospital in Jharkhand.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Candidemia represents grave healthcare-associated fungal infections. Being an opportunistic pathogen, Candida is becoming a cause of significant morbidity and mortality in patients at greater risk. The aim of the present study was to examine Candida isolates collected from blood cultures in intensive care unit patients at a tertiary care hospital in Jharkhand and to illustrate their various properties and its clinical correlations along with various antifungal susceptibility profiles.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study of 12 months, Candida isolates from blood were differentiated by conventional methods and compared by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight and VITEK 2 compact automated system. Findings were clinically correlated with various parameters like death, patients requiring assisted ventilation, and number of hospital stay days.

RESULTS: Out of 985 positive blood cultures, 95 were Candida species (9.64%). Seventy-nine isolates were Non-Albicans Candida (83.15%) and 16 isolates were Candida albicans (16.8%). Candida tropicalis 30 isolates (31.5%) was isolated, followed by Candida glabrata, Candida parapsilosis, and others. Mean age of the patients was 18.67 years. With a mortality rate of 45.2%, children were mostly deceased, accounting for 58% of all the deaths. Male predominance is seen, constituting 72% of all the deaths. C. tropicalis and C. glabrata were the most common organisms leading to death, both contributing 31% each, while C. tropicalis is the most common organism due to which patients required assisted ventilation. These isolates were susceptible to common antifungals.

CONCLUSION: Judicious start of antifungal drugs in patients of high risk is very important. This study will help clinicians to opt for best antifungal agents in the management of candidemia shortening hospital stay days.

articles.title: Parental Psychological Distress Associated with Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parenting a child with type 1 diabetes (T1D) represents an ongoing psychological burden necessitating continuous management of the disease. Although this issue has been recognized, few studies in Saudi Arabia have evaluated the disease-related anxiety and distress among parents of T1D children and adolescents. Therefore, this study was designed to assess levels of diabetes-related distress and anxiety among the parents of children and adolescents with T1D.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study surveyed 87 parents of children with T1D who attended the Pediatric Diabetes Clinic at King Fahd Specialist Hospital. Two validated instruments, namely the Parent Diabetes Distress Scale (PDDS) and the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, were used. To assess the reliability of both tools, Cronbach's α was calculated. Associations among parental distress, anxiety, and child or parent sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were determined using bivariate statistical techniques.

RESULTS: Parents exhibited moderate-related diabetes distress, with a mean PDDS score of 3.06 ± 0.85 on the 5-point scale. Furthermore, they demonstrated mild-to-moderate anxiety with a mean STAI score of 2.62 ± 0.39 on the 4-point scale. The highest PDDS subscale scores were observed on the parent-teen relationship and teen management subscales. Parents of children aged ≥10 years showed higher distress and anxiety compared with younger age groups (P < 0.05). The same higher distress was observed with longer disease duration.

CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight the need for appropriate psychosocial support for Saudi parents of children and adolescents with T1D, especially for those caring for adolescents and those with longer disease duration.

articles.title: Cystatin C, Neutrophil Gelatinase-associated Lipocalin, and Pro-atrial Natriuretic Peptide as Biomarkers in the Assessment of Diabetic Nephropathy Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a significant microvascular complication linked with diabetes mellitus which leads to chronic kidney disease worldwide. Conventional biomarkers, namely, serum creatinine and albuminuria often fail to detect early renal impairment.

AIM: The study aimed to compare the utility of serum cystatin C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), and pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) for assessing the severity of DN.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, observational study was conducted on 52 DN cases and 52 controls. Clinical and laboratory parameters of all were assessed at baseline. Serum creatinine, cystatin C, NGAL, and pro-ANP of cases were measured at baseline, 6 months and 12 months. Statistical analysis, including group comparison, correlation and regression analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and longitudinal analysis, was done on IBM SPSSv26.

RESULTS: At baseline, cases had significantly higher serum creatinine, cystatin C, and NGAL than controls. Pro-ANP was higher in cases but not significant. A significant Pearson's correlation appeared between cystatin C (r = -0.852), creatinine (r = -0.833), pro-ANP (r = -0.553), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (all P < 0.001). No significant correlation was observed between NGAL and eGFR. ROC analysis showed that cystatin C had the highest diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.995, P < 0.001). Time trend analysis highlighted a significant increase of cystatin C, pro-ANP, and serum creatinine (P < 0.001), but not for NGAL (P = 0.093), with increasing renal impairment over 12 months.

CONCLUSION: Cystatin C demonstrated strongest correlation with eGFR and highest diagnostic accuracy. Time trend analysis revealed significant increase in cystatin C level over 12 months, highlighting its potential role as biomarker for monitoring DN patients.

articles.title: Intellectual Functioning and Cognitive Outcomes in Poststroke Individuals: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke cognitive impairment is a frequent complication and has a significant impact on functional recovery and quality of life. Evidence from Indian populations is limited, but intellectual functioning as a measure of cognitive reserve might impact cognitive and functional outcomes following stroke.

AIM: This study aimed to assess the relationship between intellectual functioning and neuropsychological outcomes in poststroke patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study is a hospital-based cross-sectional correlational design conducted from July 2025 to March 2026 with 122 stroke survivors aged 30-60 years. Intellectual functioning was evaluated by the Binet-Kamat Test of Intelligence (BKT), global cognition by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), visuomotor integration by the Bender-Gestalt Test (BGT), functional independence by the Barthel Index (BI), and depressive symptoms by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-17 (HAMD-17).

RESULTS: The mean Binet-Kamat test intelligence quotient (BKT IQ) and MoCA scores were 100.3 ± 6.9 and 25.4 ± 2.7, respectively. BKT IQ showed a significant positive correlation with MoCA (r = 0.52), BI (r = 0.41) and BGT score (r = 0.28), and a negative correlation with HAMD score (r = -0.35) (all P < 0.05). Multiple linear regression showed that BKT IQ was the best independent predictor of cognitive performance (β = 0.38; P < 0.001), followed by education level, BI, HAMD score, and age. The MoCA, BGT and BI scores were significantly higher in ischemic stroke participants compared to hemorrhagic stroke.

CONCLUSION: Intellectual functioning was significantly related to cognitive functioning, functional independence, visuomotor functioning, and depressive symptoms after stroke. Intellectual functioning assessment can help in the prediction of prognosis and in the planning of individual neurorehabilitation in patients after stroke.

articles.title: Assessment of Heavy Metal Exposure in Adult Patients with Minimal Change Disease: A Cross-sectional Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimal change disease (MCD) is a major cause of nephrotic syndrome and is traditionally considered an immune-mediated podocytopathy. Environmental heavy metals have emerged as potential nephrotoxic factors that may contribute to glomerular injury and disease susceptibility.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to determine serum concentrations of selected heavy metals and evaluate their association with MCD in adults.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional case-control study was conducted in the Department of Nephrology at a tertiary care teaching hospital between October 2024 and December 2025. Twenty adults with biopsy-proven MCD and 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. Clinical, environmental, and occupational exposure histories were recorded. Serum concentrations of chromium, cadmium, arsenic, lead, and mercury were measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Heavy metal levels were compared between cases and controls and correlated with clinical parameters including serum albumin, urine protein-creatinine ratio, and acute kidney injury (AKI).

RESULTS: The mean age of MCD patients was 31.6 ± 12.4 years, with males constituting 70% of cases. Severe albuminuria and nephrotic-range proteinuria were present in 85% of patients, while severe hypoalbuminemia was observed in 75%. AKI occurred in 35% of cases. Mean serum chromium (3.80 ± 1.42 vs. 1.80 ± 0.52 μg/L; P < 0.001) and cadmium levels (0.58 ± 0.56 vs. 0.00 ± 0.00 μg/L; P < 0.001) were significantly higher among MCD patients compared with controls. Elevated chromium levels were detected in 95% of cases, arsenic in 75%, cadmium in 20%, and lead in 10%, whereas mercury was undetectable in all participants. No significant associations were observed between heavy metal concentrations and serum albumin levels, proteinuria severity, or AKI (P > 0.05). Steroid sensitivity and complete remission were achieved in 90% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Adult patients with MCD demonstrated significantly higher serum chromium and cadmium concentrations compared with healthy controls. However, heavy metal exposure was not associated with disease severity or renal outcomes. These findings suggest that environmental heavy metals may act as contributory factors rather than direct determinants of disease expression. Larger prospective studies are required to clarify the role of environmental nephrotoxins in the pathogenesis of MCD.

articles.title: Intraoperative New-onset Atrial Fibrillation during Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography: A Peri-anesthetic Challenge.
Association between Neuropsychological Impairments and Adaptive Functioning in Stroke Survivors: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke neuropsychological deficits are common and often impact cognition, adaptive functioning, and functional independence, which can hinder successful community re-entry.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the relationship between neuropsychological impairments and adaptive functioning in stroke survivors and to determine independent predictors of adaptive functioning.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted with 122 stroke survivors aged 30-60 years from July 2025 to March 2026. Neuropsychological functioning was evaluated with the Bender-Gestalt Test and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); the Vineland Social Maturity Scale (VSMS) was used to assess adaptive functioning; the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) was used to assess functional independence; and the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) was used to assess neurological severity.

RESULTS: The mean MoCA, VSMS composite, and FIM scores were 25.1 ± 2.8, 90.6 ± 8.4, and 94.2 ± 12.7, respectively. MoCA scores were significantly positively correlated with VSMS composite (r = 0.53) and FIM (r = 0.62), while NIHSS scores were significantly negatively correlated with all neuropsychological and functional measures (all P < 0.05). Of the factors considered, MoCA score was the best independent predictor of adaptive functioning, followed by FIM score. Cognitive, adaptive, and functional outcomes were significantly better for participants with ischemic stroke.

CONCLUSION: Adaptive functioning is strongly linked with neuropsychological functioning following stroke, and global cognitive performance and functional independence are the main predictors of adaptive functioning. A thorough evaluation of skills could help in the development of a tailored rehabilitation plan and enhance long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Remote and Resource-constrained Settings in India.
articles.abstract: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remains a major endocrine emergency in India, particularly in remote and resource-constrained settings where standard intensive care-based protocols are often difficult to implement. This narrative review examines the challenges of DKA management in rural Indian healthcare systems and evaluates the feasibility of pragmatic adaptations to existing treatment recommendations. Available evidence suggests that delayed presentation, infection, interrupted insulin access, limited laboratory support, inadequate monitoring facilities, and shortages of trained personnel significantly influence DKA outcomes in India. Selected patients with mild-to-moderate DKA may be managed safely using structured subcutaneous insulin protocols, although Indian prospective data remain limited. Future Indian DKA guidelines should incorporate resource-stratified recommendations that distinguish ideal care from minimum safe care. Context-sensitive management pathways, simplified monitoring protocols, improved diabetes education, and strengthened healthcare infrastructure are essential for improving DKA outcomes in underserved regions.

articles.title: A Cross-sectional Study for Estimation of Prevalence of Cognitive Impairment in Epileptic Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a frequent, but frequently overlooked, complication of epilepsy that has a negative impact on patients' quality of life and functioning. Recurrent seizures and neurological factors can have a deleterious effect on multiple cognitive domains such as memory, attention, and executive function. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scale was used to assess cognitive impairment in patients with epilepsy in this study.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to estimate the prevalence of cognitive impairment in patients with diagnosed epilepsy for more than 2 years using the MoCA scale, assess cognitive function using the MoCA score in epilepsy patients, and determine the prevalence of cognitive impairment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted among 97 patients with epilepsy for 18 months. A MoCA scale (0-30) was used to evaluate cognitive function. Means and standard deviations were given for numerical variables, and frequencies and percentages were reported for categorical variables. The Fisher's exact test or Chi-square test was used for the analysis of categorical variables as appropriate.

RESULTS: The prevalence of cognitive impairment was significantly higher in the group with hypertension (45, 95.7%) than in the group without hypertension (40, 80.0%) (χ2 = 5.54, P = 0.02). The association between cognitive impairment and diabetes mellitus was not statistically significant. The associations with hypothyroidism, cerebrovascular accident, and ischemic heart disease were not statistically significant, as per Fisher's exact test (P = 0.99, 0.07, and 0.99, respectively).

CONCLUSION: Based on these findings, it is concluded that there is a need to consider cognitive impairment as an important and often unrecognized comorbidity with the overall disease burden of patients with epilepsy. The authors emphasize that it is crucial to include routine cognitive assessments in daily clinical practice.

articles.title: The Ash Dieback Pathogen Resists the Chemical Defences of Its Host Tree, European Ash, by Depleting Them From the Growth Medium.
articles.abstract: Plant pathogenic fungi are major drivers of disease in forest trees, often causing substantial ecological and economic damage. Ash dieback, caused by the ascomycete Hymenoscyphus fraxineus, has resulted in the widespread decline of Fraxinus excelsior populations throughout Europe. As infection is initiated in leaves containing diverse plant defensive metabolites, the ability of H. fraxineus to cope with host chemistry may determine successful host colonisation. We therefore investigated the responses of H. fraxineus to crude ash leaf extracts and individual defensive compounds. In contrast to the non-ash associated fungi tested, H. fraxineus was not inhibited by crude methanolic leaf extracts or most plant defence compounds tested. In addition, H. fraxineus depleted ash compounds extensively from the growth medium. Consistent with these findings, untargeted metabolomics revealed extensive alterations of the ash leaf-based medium by H. fraxineus, with 48% of detected chemical features being significantly reduced following fungal growth. Moreover, the growth of H. fraxineus was promoted by nearly all tested ash metabolites in minimal medium, indicating that these compounds can support fungal growth and may serve as carbon sources. Together, these results suggest that successful colonisation of ash tissues by H. fraxineus depends on its resistance to host defences, facilitated by its ability to deplete defensive compounds from colonised tissue.

articles.title: Effects of a Generative AI Virtual Patient on Serious Illness Communication Skills: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serious illness communication (SIC) is a critical skill in medical education, especially in end-of-life care, yet clinicians often lack sufficient opportunities for deliberate practice. Standardized patients (SPs) remain the gold standard for SIC training, but they are limited by cost, availability, and consistency. To support wider access to SIC training, scalable alternatives are needed.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to evaluate whether SOPHIE (Standardized Online Patient for Healthcare Interaction Education), an AI-powered virtual patient that provides real-time dialogue and automated feedback, improves SIC skills among clinicians and trainees.

METHODS: We conducted a single-blind, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial from June to December 2024 via videoconferencing. Participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention (SOPHIE training) or control (reading module) group. Blinded SP actors and 4 independent raters evaluated outcomes preintervention and postintervention. The intervention group completed 3 interactive SOPHIE modules (Empathize, Be Explicit, and Empower) for 30 minutes, combining dialogue with an interactive virtual patient and automated feedback. Control participants reviewed reading materials covering the same framework for the same duration. The primary outcome was the change in communication skills (Empathize, Be Explicit, and Empower) assessed by SPs and blinded raters using a rubric based on an established clinical communication training framework. Secondary outcomes included self-reported confidence in communication skills.

RESULTS: Fifty-one medical, nursing, and physician assistant students and practicing clinicians (mean age 30.6, SD 13.2 years; women: 40/51, 78.4%) were recruited from academic and clinical settings. Participants were stratified by training level and randomized; all completed the study. Compared with controls, SOPHIE participants demonstrated significantly greater improvement in Empower (β=.11, 95% CI .04-.17; P=.002), Be Explicit (β=.08, 95% CI .03-.13; P=.002), Empathize (β=.07, 95% CI .01-.13; P=.03), and overall communication score (β=.09, 95% CI .04-.14; P=.001). Here, β represents the additional pre-to-post improvement in the SOPHIE arm relative to the control arm, estimated from linear mixed effects models. SOPHIE participants also reported higher confidence in their communication skills than controls (mean score of 4.31 vs 3.83 on a 5-point Likert scale; P=.009).

CONCLUSIONS: Training with an AI-powered virtual patient significantly improved SIC skills and confidence compared with reading modules. Generative AI-based simulations may provide a scalable, accessible, and effective adjunct or alternative to traditional SP training in clinical education.

articles.title: Programming Extracellular Vesicle-Biomaterial Interfaces for Diabetic Wounds: Barrier-Matched Design and Translational Criteria.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are sustained by a coupled network of unresolved inflammation, vascular insufficiency, oxidative injury, infection and biofilms, and matrix dysfunction. Although extracellular vesicles (EVs) can convey regenerative signals and engineered cargo, therapeutic performance is ultimately determined by how a wound-contact material preserves, presents, and releases them. This review reframes EV-based treatment as the programming of an EV-biomaterial interface. It relates wound barriers to cargo function; compares donor-cell engineering, post-isolation loading, surface modification, EV mimetics, and hybrid systems; and examines how composition, crosslinking, architecture, adhesion, mechanics, degradation, and stimulus responsiveness govern local exposure. Preclinical and emerging clinical evidence is evaluated alongside product-defining measurements, including EV identity and purity, cargo content and encapsulation efficiency, removal of free cargo, recovery, release, potency, safety, sterility, and batch consistency. The analysis shows that added functional complexity is not inherently advantageous unless each component is mechanistically necessary and quantitatively controlled. A barrier-matched, fully characterized interface therefore offers a rigorous basis for developing reproducible and clinically testable EV-enabled wound therapeutics.

articles.title: Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery 2: Essential Human Resources for Optimal Children's Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following its inaugural meeting at the Royal College of Surgeons of England, London, United Kingdom, in 2016, the Global Initiative for Children's Surgery (GICS) published the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery 1 (OReCS) consensus document detailing the facilities and resources required at each level of care. In addition to physical resources needed to provide care for children, the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery (LCoGS) identified the density of surgical providers as a marker of sufficient workforce in capacity. To meet the needs of patients, OReCS 2 details the varying types of providers needed at each level of care to meet the minimum expected capacity to care for children with surgical needs.

METHODS: We performed a review of the literature and reviewed LCoGS recommendations that applied solutions in low resource settings. We then used an iterative Delphi-like approach to determine the types of providers needed for each of 13 sub-specialties in children's surgical care at the different hospital levels. Participation was open to all GICS V conference attendees that were held from 24 to 26 February 2024 in Manila Philippines. This represents 441 participants from 50 countries (79% low to middle income countries). Final recommendations were made based on a greater than 75% agreement by respondents and reviewed by the 20 GICS board of directors.

RESULTS: In the current literature, there is considerable variability in the provider types described for each facility level with an emphasis on the use of non-physician health workers such as clinical officers, nurse anesthetists, and community health workers to improve access. Using the modified Delphi from GICS V, it is recommended to have a generalist medical practitioner, followed by non-physician surgical providers at the health center level. First level hospitals should have generalist medical practitioner, non-physician surgical provider, and generalist medical practitioner with pediatric-specific training. At the referring hospital level, which includes 2nd level hospital, third level hospital, and children's hospital, recommendations are generalist medical practitioner (GMP), non-physician surgical providers (NPSP), pediatric general and specialty surgeons, and some medical specialists such as cardiologist, gastroenterologist, and others, for maximum care coverage.

CONCLUSIONS: To improve access to high-quality care and perform the procedures considered essential, different types of providers are needed at different facility levels. Ranging from community health workers to surgical subspecialists to nurses with expertise in pediatric intensive care units to physiotherapists. OReCS 2 provides detailed examples of the optimal human resources and workforce needed at each facility level.

articles.title: The Impact of Immunoglobulins on Cardiovascular Diseases and Lipid Profiles in Elderly and Middle-Aged Chinese Individuals: A 15-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Humoral immunity defends via immunoglobulins. This study aimed to evaluate the association between immunoglobulins and CVDs and lipid profiles in a cohort of individuals aged 45 years and older.

METHODS: Data from 982 subjects were analyzed. The cohort had a median age of 61 years (IQR 56-72), was predominantly male (84.8%), and had a high prevalence of CVDs at baseline, including hypertension (30.3%), dyslipidemia (20.7%), arrhythmia (22.3%), coronary heart disease (12.1%), and atrial fibrillation (4.5%). Logistic regression analysis was used to examine the association between baseline and time-varying serum levels of IgG, IgA, and IgM and the presence of five CVDs: coronary heart disease, atrial fibrillation, arrhythmia, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. We additionally explored the relationship between these immunoglobulin levels and lipid profiles.

RESULTS: No significant differences in immunoglobulin levels were found between CVD and non-CVD groups at baseline, and baseline immunoglobulin levels were not associated with any CVD. However, longitudinal changes in IgG and IgA levels were positively associated with changes in free fatty acids (FFAs). Intriguingly, longitudinal increases in IgM levels were positively associated with total cholesterol, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and HDL-C.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides longitudinal evidence that increases in IgG and IgA levels are associated with elevated FFA levels, while increases in IgM are associated with an adverse lipid profile characterized by higher total cholesterol, LDL-C, and non-HDL-C, and lower HDL-C. These findings suggest a link between humoral immunity and lipid metabolism that warrants further investigation, with potential implications for cardiovascular risk assessment.

articles.title: Physicians' Perceptions of Information Quality and Access in a New Cross-Institutional Electronic Health Record (EHR) System: Mixed Methods Design.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physicians rely on electronic health record (EHR) systems to make informed decisions and deliver high-quality care. Although the introduction of EHR systems has created significant opportunities for improving patient care, it has also introduced challenges related to information overload and increased cognitive demands.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess physicians' perceptions of a newly implemented cross-institutional EHR system regarding (1) the quality, access, and presentation of patient data and (2) the EHR's effectiveness at supporting cooperation and communication with patients.

METHODS: This study used a cross-sectional mixed methods descriptive research design. Data were gathered through a closed-ended questionnaire, participant observations, and interviews with physicians at a university hospital in central Norway, which transitioned to a new EHR system in November 2022. Qualitative data were gathered from September 2023 to January 2024 and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, while quantitative data were collected from January 2024 to July 2024 and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The quantitative data showed that most surgical and nonsurgical physicians disagreed on the following: (1) that the patient's current medication list is presented in a clear format, (2) that the system provides a comprehensive summary view of patients' health status, and (3) that the system supports cooperation and communications with patients. These results were supported by the qualitative data, indicating that the physicians stressed the necessity of improving the presentation and organization of data and voiced concerns about the overwhelming volume of information. However, physicians also emphasized the benefits of enhanced access to patient data, the usefulness of the timeline function for monitoring hospitalized patients, and the efficiency of communication among health care professionals through the chat function. Additionally, some informants reported favorable experiences with the patient health portal, which facilitated more efficient communication with patients.

CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed a complex landscape regarding physicians' experiences with the newly implemented cross-institutional EHR system. Physicians stressed the need for improved organization and presentation of patient health data while also highlighting the positive impact of a cross-institutional EHR system on enhanced access to data. Although quantitative data showed that most physicians disagreed on whether the new EHR enhances cooperation and communication with patients, some informants in the qualitative part of the study highlighted positive experiences related to the patient health portal in improving communication. Based on qualitative findings, adding a feature that allows users to confirm if the patient has received or read messages could further improve the usefulness of the patient portal. Our qualitative findings also emphasized that enhancing system usability must be accompanied by comprehensive training on EHR use to achieve meaningful use. Future evaluations of the EHR system should focus on examining its long-term effects on access to patient data.

articles.title: Application of Four Frailty Assessment Tools in Elderly Patients With Coronary Heart Disease PCI and Its Relationship With Quality of Life.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is highly prevalent among elderly patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes and impaired health-related quality of life. However, different frailty assessment tools vary in their conceptual frameworks, assessment domains, and predictive performance, and their applicability in elderly PCI populations remains unclear.

AIMS: To compare four commonly used frailty assessment tools, including the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and to investigate their associations with quality of life in elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital in Shanghai from August to December 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and quality of life using the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12). Agreement was evaluated using the Kappa statistic. Associations with physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores were assessed using correlation and multivariable linear regression, while discriminatory performance was examined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and Bayesian discriminant analyses.

RESULTS: Mean PCS and MCS scores were 40.08 ± 11.23 and 52.30 ± 7.82, respectively. Frailty prevalence was 40.6% by FP, 8.6% by FRAIL, 28.3% by TFI, and 22.1% by FI. Agreement was fair to moderate (Kappa = 0.242-0.496). Higher frailty scores were independently associated with lower PCS and MCS after adjustment for age, sex, education, smoking, and comorbidity burden. FP and FI showed comparable discrimination for PCS, whereas TFI had the highest AUC for MCS. Classification accuracy was highest for FP in PCS and TFI in MCS (both 79.51%).

CONCLUSION: Frailty was consistently associated with poorer quality of life. FP and FI performed similarly for physical health, whereas TFI showed the most favorable performance for mental health.

articles.title: Serum Mycophenolic Acid Levels and Infection Risk in Myasthenia Gravis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Evidence linking serum mycophenolic acid (MPA) concentrations with safety outcomes in myasthenia gravis (MG) is limited. We evaluated whether single serum MPA concentrations were associated with clinically documented infection.

METHODS: This retrospective study included acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG patients treated with mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) for at least 1 year who had MPA and mycophenolic acid glucuronide (MPAG) measurement with same-day complete blood count testing. Exact sampling time relative to MMF dosing was not uniformly documented; therefore, values were analyzed as single serum concentrations rather than confirmed trough levels.

RESULTS: Among 112 MMF-treated patients, 60 had MPA/MPAG measurement, and 10 had recent infection. Serum MPA concentration correlated strongly and positively with MPAG concentration (r = 0.717) and moderately and inversely with lymphocyte count (r = -0.406). Infection occurred in 0/18 low, 2/24 intermediate, and 8/18 high MPA concentration groups. Patients with infection had higher MPA concentration (median 6.15 vs. 1.80 μg/mL; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.032) and higher MPA concentration per prescribed MMF dose.

DISCUSSION: Higher single serum MPA concentrations were associated with recent infection. Prospective controlled studies including patients not treated with MMF are needed.

articles.title: Coumarin Decouples ROS Homoeostasis, Membrane Integrity, and HOG Signalling to Inhibit Alternaria alternata.
articles.abstract: Alternaria alternata is a common pathogen responsible for leaf spots and postharvest decay in multiple crops, including sweet cherry. Coumarin, a plant-derived compound, exhibits broad antifungal activity against plant pathogenic fungi including A. alternata. In this study, we found that coumarin significantly inhibited mycelial growth, conidiation, conidial germination, and infection of cherry tissues. Mechanistically, coumarin disrupted reactive oxygen species (ROS) homoeostasis, impaired membrane integrity, and inhibited ergosterol biosynthesis. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that coumarin dysregulated genes involved in membrane and sterol metabolism. Notably, coumarin activated the Hog1 (High osmolarity glycerol-1) dependent stress response pathway, as evidenced by nuclear accumulation of AaHog1 and increased coumarin sensitivity of ∆AaHog1 mutants. Furthermore, coumarin enhanced the efficacy of demethylation inhibitor (DMI) and dicarboximide (DCF) fungicides. Our findings demonstrate that coumarin acts through multiple antifungal mechanisms including HOG pathway activation, oxidative stress induction, and membrane disruption, highlighting its potential as a sustainable antifungal agent for controlling A. alternata.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Hospitalized With Localized, Regional, and Metastatic Head and Neck Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a known complication in cancer patients, but data in head and neck cancer (HNC)-particularly distinguishing localized, regional, and metastatic disease-are limited.

METHODS: Using the 2016-2020 National Inpatient Sample, we examined adults ≥ 18 years with HNC, excluding patients with another primary malignancy. Metastatic status was categorized as localized, regional, and metastatic. Outcomes included odds of VTE, pulmonary embolism (PE), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), inhospital mortality, and prolonged length of stay (LOS ≥ 7 days). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with these outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 62 032 unweighted (310 160 weighted) admissions, 75.0% had localized HNC, 12.7% had regional HNC, and 12.3% had metastatic HNC; 2.6% had VTE (2.4% localized HNC, 2.3% regional HNC, and 4.1% metastatic HNC). Compared with localized HNC, regional HNC was not associated with increased odds of VTE, PE, or DVT, whereas metastatic HNC was associated with higher adjusted odds of VTE (aOR 1.52; 95% CI: 1.30-1.78), PE (aOR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.98), and DVT (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.18-1.83). VTE was associated with increased inhospital mortality (aOR 1.98; 95% CI: 1.64-2.40) and prolonged LOS (aOR 2.14; 95% CI: 1.92-2.39).

CONCLUSION: In hospitalized patients, distant, but not regional, metastatic HNC is associated with higher odds of VTE, and VTE is associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes including increased mortality and prolonged LOS.

articles.title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
articles.abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

articles.title: Catheter-related bloodstream infection with coagulase-negative staphylococci in hematological malignancy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central venous catheters (CVC) are vital in the management of hematological malignancy and complications lead to delayed care and increased costs. Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) are common, and the safety of line retention in these infections is unclear.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective review of individuals with CoNS CRBSI and hematological malignancy between January 1, 2012, and January 1, 2024 compared 90-day all-cause mortality and microbiological relapse in patients managed with CVC retention versus removal.
