Propensity-weighted analysis was performed to control for baseline differences between groups.

RESULTS: A total of 140 individual cases were included, with 68% (n = 95) having a history of haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). 80.4% (n = 111) were neutropenic at the time of CRBSI diagnosis. The predominant CoNS isolated was Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 124, 88.6%). Bacteraemia with an oxacillin-resistant organism represented 126 (90.0%) of the cases. CVC retention was more common in those with HCT (p = 0.007), while removal was more frequent with peripherally inserted central catheters (PICC)(p < 0.001) and in those hospitalised for CRBSI management (p = 0.022). Clearance of bacteraemia occurred after a median of two days for both retention and removal groups. Propensity weighted analysis demonstrated a significantly higher rate of relapse with CVC retention compared to CVC removal (hazard ratio [HR] = 6.1; p = 0.043), whereas the difference in mortality was not statistically significant (HR = 1.8; p = 0.128).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians should be vigilant for risks associated with CoNS CRBSI. Future prospective studies evaluating the implications of clinical decision-making in these infections are needed.

articles.title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear.

METHODS: NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory.

DISCUSSION: This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

articles.title: Patterns of Instrumental and Informational Workplace Health Support Use Among Hospital Service Workers of Low- to Mid-Socioeconomic Status.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeTo examine workplace health supports (WHS) use and sociodemographic and organizational correlates among healthcare workers predominantly of low- to mid-socioeconomic status (SES).DesignCross-sectional survey.SettingLarge U.S. healthcare system, 2018.Sample1283 healthcare service workers; 1196 included in final analyses (93.2%).MeasuresInstrumental and informational WHS use; SES; race; age; shift; sex; obesity; organizational health climate; coworker support; supervisor support.AnalysisPearson point biserial correlations (rpb), phi (Φ) statistics, and multivariable negative binomial regression models were used. Interaction terms between organizational health climate and sociodemographic characteristics were tested.ResultsThe median employee used two WHS (one instrumental, one informational). Older age was associated with greater informational WHS use (Φ = .13 to .21), while Black race was associated with greater instrumental WHS use (Φ = .09 to .15). Organizational health climate was modestly associated with healthy eating and physical activity WHS (rpb = .09 to .11). In adjusted models, age, race, and organizational health climate remained independently associated with WHS use. Modest interaction effects were observed between organizational health climate and race (total and informational models) and sex (total model).ConclusionDifferentiating WHS by support type reveals meaningful differences in engagement across worker groups. Findings highlight the importance of organizational context. Results should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and self-reported measures.

articles.title: Transarterial Computed Tomographic Angiography in Patients With Impaired Renal Function Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract: PurposeComputed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preoperative planning and postoperative surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Renal function impairment however limits pre- and postoperative assessment. The aim of our study was to evaluate the safety and diagnostic value of a novel technique in the setting of patients undergoing EVAR.Methods216 patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing transbrachial placement of an angiography catheter in the aorta for contrast medium administration were analyzed retrospectively. 45 patients with normal kidney function and aortic aneurysms were included as control group. 27 were female, 84 cases were for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, while 106 cases were for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Primary endpoint was the freedom from contrast-induced acute kidney injury. Secondary safety endpoints were freedom from access site complications and cerebrovascular incidents. Imaging quality endpoints were attenuation values and contrast-to-noise-ratios in predefined vessels, validated by intraclass correlation coefficients.ResultsMean creatinine change was -.11 mg/dL, mean GFR change was 2.13% in the intervention group. There were 10 (4.6%) false aneurysms and two access site hematoma (0.93%). Two cerebrovascular incidents (0.9%) were transient. Transarterial CTA attenuation values varied between 210.4 (±89) and 241.4 (±98) Hounsfield units (HU), and 306.35 (±63.27) to 321.39 (±70.12) HU in the control group. The mean amount of contrast medium used in the catheter group was significantly reduced (31.70 ± 5.82 mL) compared to the control group (P = .001). Contrast-to-noise ratios varied between 9.1 (±4.6) and 11.1 (±4.4. Intraclass correlation coefficients between the readings were very good (0.987-0.992).ConclusionCatheter-based transarterial computed tomographic angiography is a safe and efficacious way to evaluate patients with aortic aneurysms, both prior and after EVAR.

articles.title: Plasticity in Human Brain Language Areas After Stroke: What Can the Right Hemisphere Do?
articles.journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
articles.abstract: Among the most devastating effects stroke can have on the lives of survivors and those around them are language production and comprehension impairments. The most notable of them - often given the joint diagnostic label of "aphasia" despite their heterogeneity and dissociability - are associated with damage to the brain's left hemisphere, which, in large part for this reason, is considered the "language-dominant" hemisphere. However, the right hemisphere's contribution to language should not be underestimated and may in fact be key to understanding the possibilities and limitations of neuroplasticity for supporting language recovery after stroke. Thus, in this review, we focus on the role of the right hemisphere in supporting human language function, in the neurologically healthy brain and after stroke. We discuss the remarkable capability of the right hemisphere to support normal language abilities after a large left-hemisphere stroke early in life, the more limited capacity for right-hemisphere language support after left-hemisphere stroke in adulthood, and potential interactions between typically left-hemisphere dominant "core" language functions with language functions typically thought to be right-hemisphere dominant, such as emotional prosody. We conclude by highlighting gaps in current knowledge and suggesting areas for future research.

articles.title: Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. lactis CKDB001 Attenuates Hepatic Steatosis and Metabolic Dysfunction in High-Fat Diet-Induced Obese Mice.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction associated with obesity frequently coincides with hepatic lipid accumulation; however, effective preventive strategies are scarce. This study evaluated the dose-dependent effects of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. lactis CKDB001 in mice with high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to a normal diet, HFD, or HFD with CKDB001 at one of three different doses (LL1, 5.0 × 108; LL2, 1.0 × 109; LL3, 5.0 × 109 CFU/day). Following 4 weeks of HFD feeding, CKDB001 was administered daily for 8 weeks while maintaining the HFD. Among the doses, LL2 demonstrated the most consistent outcomes, including reductions in body weight gain and liver and adipose tissue weights, without affecting food or energy intake. LL2 also decreased serum total cholesterol, alanine aminotransferase levels, hepatic cholesterol content, and histological scores for steatosis, fibrosis, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Although changes in hepatic triglyceride and lipid metabolism-related gene expression were minimal, LL2 and LL3 enhanced colonic Zo-1 and occludin mRNA expression compared to the HFD group, suggesting a potential gut-associated transcriptional response to CKDB001 supplementation.

articles.title: Words That Heal: A Systematic Review of Healthcare Providers-Patient Communication to Enhance Chronic Care Management and Practice Recommendations.
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases represent a major global health burden, and suboptimal treatment adherence remains a key obstacle to long-term management. Healthcare provider (HCP)-patient communication is a modifiable determinant of adherence and psychological functioning, yet evidence remains fragmented across conditions and communication domains. This review builds on patient-centered communication scholarship and established models of communication functions and pathways linking clinician-patient communication to health outcomes. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on HCP-patient communication strategies associated with treatment adherence and psychological outcomes among adults with chronic diseases, including diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular, and respiratory conditions. Following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD42020171690), five databases (Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar) were searched. Results: Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Communication strategies clustered into four macro-domains: (1) trust and interpersonal relationship; (2) information exchange and decision processes; (3) active involvement, empowerment, and autonomy; and (4) change processes, emotional regulation, and management of difficulties. Domains were defined a priori from patient-centered communication, self-management, and behavior-change literature and refined during data extraction. Across conditions, integrated communication patterns addressing multiple domains were generally associated with favorable adherence, self-management, clinical, quality-of-life, and healthcare-utilization outcomes, although evidence strength varied by study design, disease context, and methodological quality. Findings support a provisional, evidence-informed framework in which HCP-patient communication strategies, organized within relational, informational, participatory, and change-regulatory macro-domains, may engage proximal regulatory processes that, in turn, may be associated with adherence and other chronic-care outcomes. Prospective studies are needed to test these pathways.

articles.title: A One-Stone-Two-Birds Strategy to Develop P-Por COF/PDES Composite Gels for Photothermal/Photodynamic Antibacterial Activity and Wearable Strain Sensing.
articles.abstract: Flexible wearable electronics face growing bacterial infection risks from prolonged skin contact, creating an urgent demand for flexible materials integrating efficient sensing and antibacterial functions. Herein, a novel phosphorus-containing porphyrin covalent organic framework (P-Por COF) was synthesized via a solvothermal Schiff-base reaction, and incorporated into a polymerizable deep eutectic solvent to fabricate P-Por COF/PDES composite gels through in-situ UV polymerization. The resulting gel exhibited enhanced photothermal performance, improved mechanical properties, and excellent near-infrared (NIR) triggered antibacterial activity. Under 730 nm NIR light irradiation, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel could reach 76 °C with 4 min, while showing excellent stability of photothermal cycle. Based on the synergistic effect of photodynamic production of singlet oxygen and photothermal effect, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel resulted in a high bactericidal rate of nearly 100% against both Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli (E. coli). The P-Por COF/PDES composite gel delivered a fracture strain up to 2435.82% and 2.6-fold higher toughness than pure PDES, along with stable, sensitive and self-healable strain sensing for human motion monitoring. Overall, this work provides a simple and effective strategy for developing antibacterial materials and multifunctional gels with integrated therapeutic and sensing capabilities.

articles.title: Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery 2: Tiered Recommendations for Minimum Essential Children's Surgical Procedures Across Health System Levels.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2015 the World Health Assembly (WHO), based on recommendations by the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, passed resolution (68:15) on strengthening emergency and essential surgical care and anesthesia as a component of universal health coverage. However, children's surgery was not adequately represented and in response, the Global Initiative for Children's Surgery (GICS) published the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care (OReCS) in 2019 providing insight into procedures which should be performed at different facility types. OReCS 2 addresses a gap in both policy and published literature to further define surgical conditions and procedural capabilities by hospital level.

METHODS: We performed a review of the literature to identify procedures routinely performed in a variety of settings. We then used an iterative Delphi like approach to identify specialty-specific procedures and nursing skills by hospital level. Participation was open to all members of GICS with representation from 21 working groups and more than 50 low-middle income countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). Data on essential procedures were collected for twelve specialty groups. Modifications of the recommendations provided by the working groups were made by the executive board based on firsthand knowledge of capabilities at lower-level facilities where subspecialists have less experience. Final recommendations were made based on greater than 75% agreement by respondents and review of the executive board of GICS.

RESULTS: Procedures performed at health centers were limited to those not requiring anesthesia or sedation and were largely identified to help triage and stabilize patients for transfer to higher level care. Similarly, first level hospital procedures focused on stabilization and transfer to referral level hospitals for most specialties. Alternatively, specialties such as ophthalmology and dental surgery have identified definitive procedures for lower-level facilities. Procedures performed at the National Children's Hospital level include those requiring specialty providers and equipment such as transplantation, repair of congenital heart disease, and reconstructive surgery for complex trauma, congenital anomalies, and burns.

CONCLUSIONS: This updated version of OReCS provides specific examples of procedural capabilities for twelve subspecialties at the health center, first, second, third, and referral level hospitals in LMICs. Whereas the list is not meant to be all inclusive, it provides a framework within which to define the minimum essential material resources, equipment, and personnel by hospital level.

articles.title: Bipolar Disorder and the Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic psychiatric illness characterized by recurrent manic and depressive episodes, affecting 2% of the global population. It is associated with premature mortality, including cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related mortality. Although clinically important, the absolute burden and incidence of cardiovascular outcomes in BD remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized observational evidence on CVD prevalence and incidence in adults with BD.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023484712), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and PsycInfo, screening 11,909 records. Thirty-two observational studies in adults with BD were included after Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment. Data were extracted on overall CVD, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, comorbidities, and psychotropic exposure. Pooled prevalence and incidence rate ratios were calculated using random-effects models when data were comparable.

RESULTS: The pooled CVD prevalence in BD was 7.70% (95% CI: 5.07-11.52), with coronary artery disease at 6.89% (95% CI: 4.05-11.47), cerebrovascular disease at 4.45% (95% CI: 2.13-9.05), and peripheral arterial disease at 3.30% (95% CI: 1.66-6.45). However, prevalence estimates showed extreme heterogeneity and should be interpreted as broad indicators of absolute burden rather than precise estimates for a single BD population. In controlled incidence studies, BD was associated with increased CVD incidence (IRR 1.66, 95% CI: 1.32-2.08), with elevated coronary and cerebrovascular estimates. Clinical variable analyses involving medication use, lifestyle factors, and cardiometabolic comorbidities were not feasible because reporting was insufficient and noncomparable.

CONCLUSION: Adults with BD show substantial cardiovascular burden and increased incidence. However, extreme heterogeneity, limited incidence data, observational designs, and insufficient moderator reporting limit the precision and generalizability of pooled estimates. These findings support integrated cardiovascular screening in BD populations and future prospective studies.

TRAIL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42023484712.

articles.title: Development of the Readiness to Change Diet Questionnaire (RCdQ) for Assessing Willingness to Adopt Anti-Inflammatory Diet Among Coronary Artery Disease Patients.
articles.journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a questionnaire to assess readiness to change for adopting an anti-inflammatory diet among patients with coronary artery disease. The Readiness to Change Questionnaire-Treatment Version (RCQ-TV) was adapted for dietary behavior, translated into Hindi, and evaluated using an e-Delphi approach for face validation. The study was conducted in the National Capital Region, India. Domain experts (n = 6) assessed the clarity, content, and structure of the adapted questionnaire across iterative rounds, and consensus-driven revisions were made. The validated tool was subsequently pilot tested among 25 participants. Scores for each stage of change were calculated using an established scoring template, with the highest scale score indicating stage of readiness. Open-ended expert feedback from each iteration was summarized to inform revisions, and internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Modifications included simplification of terminology, revision of instructions and specific items, addition of definitions, and simplification of the Hindi version. Pilot testing classified two participants in the pre-contemplation stage, 10 in contemplation, and 13 in the action stage. The questionnaire demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .73). Participants reported the tool to be concise, with instructions, definitions, items, and response options understandable, relevant, and appropriate, although 10 participants required assistance to complete it. Overall, the adapted questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory face validity, internal consistency, and usability in both English and Hindi, suggesting wide applicability for assessing readiness to change dietary behavior in populations.

articles.title: Periocular surgery risk after glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy for type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between GLP-1RA therapy and the hazard of involutional periocular surgical procedures among patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX electronic health record database. Adults aged 45 years and older with type 2 diabetes were included. A GLP-1RA cohort was created with evidence of continued therapy defined by a second prescription at least 1 year after initiation. The comparison cohort included patients prescribed other antidiabetic medications, excluding GLP-1RAs. Propensity score matching balanced demographics, comorbidities, and insulin use. The primary outcomes were the hazards of periocular surgery during four nonoverlapping 9-month intervals (0-9, 9-18, 18-27, and 27-36 months) and cumulatively over 0-36 months.

RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with a higher hazard of upper eyelid blepharoplasty (HR range: 1.988-2.788), blepharoptosis repair (HR range: 1.322-1.813), and brow ptosis repair (HR range: 1.683-2.393) compared with other antidiabetic medications (all p ≤ 0.028). Elevated hazard occurred within 0-9 months of treatment and generally increased through 18-27 months.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA therapy was associated with an increased hazard of involutional periocular surgical procedures compared with other antidiabetic medications, suggesting a potential association between GLP-1RA use and periocular soft tissue changes.

articles.title: Validity and agreement of bioelectrical impedance equations against dual energy X-ray absorptiometry for muscle mass assessment in patients on hemodialysis: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low muscle mass is common in patients on hemodialysis (HD), and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) predictive equations have been proposed as an alternative for estimating muscle mass. This study aimed to analyze the validity and agreement of different BIA-based prediction equations against dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) for estimating skeletal muscle mass (SMM) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM) in patients on HD.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study enrolled patients on HD. Clinical and laboratory data and body composition by BIA and DXA were collected. The accuracy of six prediction equations (Janssen, Barbosa-Silva, Kyle, Lin, Macdonald, and Sergi) for estimating SMM and ASMM was tested against DXA as the reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC), Bland-Altman analysis, Kappa statistics, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves, and Passing-Bablok regression.

RESULTS: The sample consisted of 57 participants, age 52 ± 13 years, 32 (56%) male, median dialysis vintage 14 (4-40) months, 17 (30%) with diabetes, and 48 (84%) with hypertension. The best agreement with DXA was observed for the Lin (CCC = 0.911), Sergi (CCC = 0.902) and Kyle (CCC = 0.902) equations. For low muscle mass diagnosis, Kappa values ranged from moderate to substantial, with the Lin equation showing the highest agreement (κ = 0.734). Additionally, the Lin equation demonstrated good accuracy (AUC = 0.794, 95% CI 0.68-0.91), with 68,4% sensitivity and 89.5% specificity.

CONCLUSION: The Lin equation provided the most accurate and reproducible estimates of muscle mass compared with DXA and showed good diagnostic performance for low muscle mass in patients on HD.

articles.title: Delivering a high-dose walking booster program after stroke: a multimethod study of therapists' beliefs and experiences nested within a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-dose motor training is rarely implemented later after stroke. This study explored intervention therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) within a Phase II trial.

OBJECTIVE: The objectives of this study were to (i) describe the beliefs intervention therapists held about a high-dose walking booster program prior to delivery, (ii) report facilitators and barriers to delivery, and (iii) to describe the strategies intervention therapists used to maintain training intensity during the program.

METHODS: A multimethod design examined intervention therapists' perspectives of delivering a high-dose walking booster program to stroke survivors who were more than 6-months post-stroke. Pre-program surveys assessed beliefs about high-dose motor training. Observational audits evaluated program delivery. Semi-structured interviews, informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), identified facilitators and barriers to program delivery. Survey and observational audit data were descriptively analyzed, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The HiWalk Trial was registered on January 10, 2023 (registration number ACTRN12623000316606).

RESULTS: All therapists who delivered the HiWalk program (n = 6) participated. Before delivery, intervention therapists believed high-dose training was important (98.5/100, SD 2.5) but were less confident that stroke survivors could complete 3 hours of training per day (74.8/100, SD 25.8). Audit observations indicated that, on average, observed intervention sessions met protocol expectations. Key facilitators included training (TDF Skills), team support (TDF Social Influences), and resources (TDF Environmental Context and Resources). Barriers were beliefs about stroke survivor capability (TDF Beliefs about Capabilities) and resource limitations (TDF Environmental Context and Resources).

CONCLUSIONS: Intervention therapists can deliver a high-dose walking booster program within a clinical trial when supported by training, resources, and team collaboration. Findings inform future trial design and clinical practice translation.

articles.title: Passive acquisition of hepatitis B virus antibodies after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 193 adults who underwent allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT.

RESULTS: Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. Among patients receiving neither fresh frozen plasma nor intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-HBs concentrations increased significantly after HCT (p< .0001), with a greater increase among those receiving ≥24 versus ≤23 platelet transfusions (p = .0437).

DISCUSSION: Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Dental and Craniofacial Injury Patterns in Conventional and Electric Two-Wheeler Riders in Urban Settings: A Cross-Sectional Survey-Based Study.
articles.journal: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess and compare the prevalence and pattern of dental and craniofacial injuries sustained by conventional two-wheeler riders versus electric two-wheeler (e-bike/e-scooter) riders involved in road traffic accidents (RTAs), and to evaluate the role of protective gear, riding practices, and behavioral factors on injury outcomes.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Six hundred and fifty-two riders (340 conventional two-wheelers, 312 e-bike/e-scooter) were examined and interviewed from an urban setting using a structured questionnaire. Data encompassed demographics, vehicle type, compliance with protective gears, riding behavior and practices, accident characteristics, and oro-facial injury profile. Chi-square, Fisher's exact tests, and descriptive statistics were applied (significance: p < 0.05). A supplementary binary logistic regression, adjusted for vehicle type, helmet compliance, commercial rider status, age group, usual vehicle speed, and pre-ride training, was performed to identify independent predictors of facial injury.

RESULTS: Road traffic accident involvement was significantly more prevalent among e-bike riders than conventional two-wheeler riders (70.8% vs. 47.1%; RR = 1.51; p < 0.001). Among accident cases, facial or oral injuries were significantly more frequent in e-bike riders (72.9%) than in conventional two-wheeler riders (39.4%; OR = 4.13; p < 0.001). Lacerations were the most common injury (39.3%), followed by chipped or broken teeth (21.0%), jaw or facial bone fractures (14.7%), tooth avulsion (9.8%), and tooth displacement/luxation injuries (7.1%). No significant intergroup differences were identified for any individual injury category. Accident rates were similar between commercial and personal use within vehicle groups: E-Bike: 70.6% vs. 71.0% (RR = 0.995; OR = 0.984); Road Bike: 50.0% vs. 45.5% (RR = 1.098; OR = 1.196). Consistent use of protective gear was reported by 72.6% of conventional two-wheeler riders, compared with only 5.8% of e-bike riders (p < 0.001). Pre-ride training was received by 63.8% of conventional riders, compared with 14.7% of e-bike riders.

CONCLUSIONS: Electric two-wheeler riders demonstrate a markedly higher risk of accidents and orofacial injuries compared with conventional riders. After multivariable adjustment, the association between e-bike riding and injury remained significant (aOR = 4.213, p < 0.001). However, correlated behavioral predictors (such as helmet use and pre-ride training) could not be reliably disentangled. Low helmet compliance and urgency-driven riding behavior among delivery riders in quick commerce represent critical characteristics of the e-bike cohort that warrant further investigation.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Synaptic density PET mediates the relationship between Alzheimer's disease pathology and cognitive performance.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Synaptic loss is one of the strongest post-mortem predictors of Alzheimer's disease (AD) severity and may impact how pathology affects cognition. This study compared regional [11C]UCB-J synaptic density across the AD continuum and evaluated the extent to which synaptic density mediates relationships between AD biomarkers.

METHODS: Seventy-two participants completed PET scans, MRIs, and cognitive testing. Participants were categorized into subgroups representing typical AD progression. Regional synaptic density was compared across subgroups and pathological variables. Standard mediation and moderated mediation analyses were performed using amyloid and tau as predictors/moderators and MoCA score as outcome.

RESULTS: The amyloid+/tau+/impaired subgroup showed lower synaptic density than controls, particularly for transverse temporal, inferior parietal, and hippocampal regions (Cohen's d=1.60, 1.57, 1.50). Hippocampal synaptic density had the strongest associations with tau (β=-0.473); transverse temporal synaptic density had the strongest association with amyloid (β=-0.543) and age (β=-0.614). Eight of twelve assessed brain regions demonstrated significant indirect effects across mediation frameworks. The inferior parietal lobe showed the largest mediation for amyloid (45.3%) and tau (28.9%).

DISCUSSION: These findings support the hypothesis that synaptic loss is a primary mechanism contributing to clinical AD and suggest that synaptic density imaging can provide complementary information to the existing AD framework.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Reperfusion-sensitive induction of endothelial NDRG1 identifies a dynamic vascular stress response to thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) outcome critically depends on the neurovascular unit's capacity to respond to ischemia-reperfusion stress within the salvageable penumbra. Here, we characterize the spatiotemporal regulation of N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) and identify it as an early, reperfusion-sensitive marker of endothelial stress. Under physiological conditions, NDRG1 is primarily expressed in neurons and oligodendrocytes, with minimal endothelial expression. Following middle cerebral artery occlusion, NDRG1 undergoes marked spatial and cellular redistribution, becoming strongly induced in endothelial cells across the cerebrovascular tree.Endothelial NDRG1 induction was detectable as early as 6 hours after ischemia and evolved from a vesicular pattern to diffuse vascular labeling by 24 hours. Importantly, recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator (rtPA) selectively enhanced endothelial NDRG1 expression in peri-lesional vessels in the rtPA-sensitive thrombin model, but not in the rtPA-resistant FeCl3 model, indicating that NDRG1 induction is linked to effective reperfusion. In vitro, oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) recapitulated endothelial NDRG1 induction, further enhanced by rtPA through a pathway involving the LDL receptor family.Collectively, these findings identify endothelial NDRG1 as a dynamic molecular readout of reperfusion-sensitive vascular stress. NDRG1 may serve as a biomarker of endothelial responsiveness to thrombolytic therapy, providing new insight into cerebrovascular adaptations associated with successful reperfusion.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Much ado about eating: Intermittent fasting and post-stroke neuroprotection".
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Vemuganti and colleagues highlight intermittent fasting (IF)'s neuroprotective potential post-stroke via autophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. However, clinical translation faces hurdles in metabolically vulnerable patients. This letter critiques IF's bedside applicability, emphasizing post-stroke catabolic stress, dysphagia (~50% cases), sarcopenia risk, and cardiovascular concerns. Recent evidence links short eating windows to higher mortality, countering IF benefits. The obesity paradox suggests nutritional reserves aid survival. Strategies: protein-prioritized planning, dysphagia screening, dietitian monitoring, and supplements. Until RCTs confirm safety/efficacy, prioritize nutritional adequacy. Preclinical insights warrant study.Keywords: dysphagia, intermittent fasting, neuroprotection, obesity paradox, sarcopenia.

articles.title: Perioperative management of acute type A aortic dissection using extended half-life factor IX (Alprolix) in a patient with severe hemophilia B: a case report.
articles.journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) in patients with severe hemophilia B is extremely rare, and perioperative coagulation management is a major challenge.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old man with severe hemophilia B (factor IX activity < 1%) was diagnosed with ATAAD and underwent emergency surgery. Replacement therapy with an extended half-life factor IX product (eftrenonacog alfa; Alprolix) was administered targeting a factor IX activity of 80-100%, and total arch replacement was performed. Cardiopulmonary bypass was performed under standard heparinization conditions. Since rapid measurement of factor IX activity was not possible, postoperative replacement therapy was based primarily on the clinical assessment of hemostasis, with serial activated partial thromboplastin time measurements providing supportive information, whereas intraoperative anticoagulation was managed using standard activated clotting time monitoring. Intra- and postoperative bleeding volumes were within ranges comparable to those observed in standard complex aortic surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of an extended half-life factor IX product may be a practical option for perioperative coagulation management during emergency aortic surgery in patients with severe hemophilia B.

articles.title: ABCD-Trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for the evaluation of efficacy and safety of B-Cell Depletion with rituximab (ABCD).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The exact disease-causing mechanisms in ALS remain incompletely understood. A possible cause is inflammation of neurons. Compared to other neurodegenerative diseases, neuroinflammation is pronounced in ALS, presumably leading to disease progression and neuronal death. Patients with ALS can have neuronal autoantibodies and most notably antibody-producing cells in the cerebrospinal fluid. The CD20-binding therapeutic antibody rituximab targets these antibody-producing B-cells. Rituximab is a medication commonly used in neurology. Single patients with ALS have already been treated with rituximab, which was well tolerated. We therefore want to evaluate safety and efficacy of a treatment with rituximab in ALS patients in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial. With this trial we aim for slower disease progression and unveiling disease-causing mechanisms in ALS.

METHODS: A total of 52 male and female patients older than 18 years with active sporadic ALS and disease duration of less than 24 months who are on a stable dose of riluzole (50 mg BID) should be included. Patients requiring assisted ventilation of any kind or have a known intolerance to the study medication rituximab are excluded. The study medication rituximab or placebo should be administered over a period of 52 weeks at 4 distinct time points, followed by a follow-up period of 79 weeks with 4 visits. Treatment efficacy should be evaluated using the ALS functioning scale ALSFRS-R-SE at every study visit (except safety visits). Safety will be assessed through regular laboratory analyses, adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) monitoring, and CD20+ B-cell kinetics. The primary endpoint is the change in the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R-SE) from baseline to week 79. Trial sites will be at Charité/DZNE Berlin and DZNE Bonn.

DISCUSSION: ALS is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease with limited treatment options. Recent preclinical in vivo studies suggest that B-cell-mediated autoimmunity contributes to disease progression. This trial will evaluate whether rituximab, which specifically depletes CD20+ B-cells, can slow ALS progression and provide insights into disease mechanisms.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered in the German WHO-recognized primary register Deutsches Register Klinische Studien DRKS (German Clinical Trials Register) on 3/07/2023 under registration number DRKS00030948.

articles.title: Massive enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst over 8 years with intracystic hemorrhage and complex surgical resection: a case report.
articles.journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchogenic cysts are usually asymptomatic and are often detected incidentally; however, they may become symptomatic due to infection, hemorrhage, or enlargement. We report a case of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst that showed substantial enlargement from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, ultimately requiring partial resection of the esophageal muscularis.

CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 20s presented with upper abdominal pain and nausea. Computed tomography revealed a 13-cm mass extending from below the tracheal bifurcation to the level of the gastric cardia. A CT scan obtained eight years earlier during the evaluation of abdominal pain had shown a 4.8-cm cystic lesion below the tracheal bifurcation, demonstrating substantial enlargement over the intervening period. Although conservative treatment was attempted, compressive symptoms persisted; therefore, surgical resection was performed for definitive diagnosis and symptom relief. Severe inflammatory adhesions necessitated right open thoracotomy with partial resection of the esophageal muscularis. The cyst contained a large hematoma, and histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a bronchogenic cyst with intracystic hemorrhage.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates substantial enlargement of a previously unrecognized bronchogenic cyst from 4.8 to 13 cm over an 8-year interval, with intracystic hemorrhage, symptomatic progression, and technically demanding surgical resection. The potential for substantial enlargement and increasing surgical complexity should be considered when determining the timing of resection for bronchogenic cysts.

articles.title: Mapping and analysis of the knowledge graph on the current status and key issues in global research on Norovirus infections in children over the past 28 years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies.

METHODS: This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field.

RESULTS: This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. The United States, China, and Japan are the leading contributors to research in this field, with the United States exerting significant influence through international collaboration. The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University are the research institutions with the highest number of publications. Vinje, Jan; Ushijima, Hiroshi; and Khamrin, Pattara were the most prolific core authors, while Atmar, Robert L.; Lindesmith, Lisa C.; and Patel, Manish M. demonstrated strong academic influence. Keyword analysis revealed that research in this field primarily focuses on viral molecular characteristics, epidemiological features, and clinical manifestations in children, and is gradually expanding toward disease burden assessment, global prevention and control strategies, and vaccine development.

CONCLUSION: Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Current research focuses primarily on molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity, as well as epidemiological characteristics and outbreak transmission mechanisms, while the assessment of disease burden and the optimization of global prevention and control strategies are gradually emerging as key future research directions. In the future, international collaboration, multicenter surveillance, and interdisciplinary research should be further strengthened to advance research on pediatric NoV infection from describing disease characteristics toward precision surveillance, proactive prevention, and comprehensive control and prevention measures.

articles.title: Ensuring equitable emergency, critical and operative care.
articles.journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
articles.abstract: Conditions requiring emergency, critical and operative (ECO) care account for a substantial proportion of preventable mortality and disability worldwide, yet ECO systems remain fragmented and underdeveloped in many settings. Recent global policy advances, including the adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Strategy and Action Plan for Integrated ECO Care by the World Health Assembly, provide an important opportunity to strengthen these systems. However, implementation must prioritise equity. ECO care spans a wide spectrum of complexity and cost, from basic triage, oxygen therapy and essential operations to advanced intensive care and specialised surgery. Given finite resources, health systems should first ensure universal access to foundational ECO care: early recognition of illness, basic airway and oxygen support, essential medications, monitoring, infection prevention, and timely referral. Approaches such as Essential Emergency and Critical Care (EECC) offer a feasible, highly cost-effective minimum standard of care, and prioritising such foundational ECO care is both an ethical imperative and the most effective pathway to achieving equitable population-level health gains.

articles.title: Stroke-associated pneumonia: from immunodepression to bedside management and future research directions.
articles.abstract: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is one of the most frequent complications after acute stroke, affecting approximately one in eight stroke patients. Besides prolonged hospitalisation and increased healthcare costs, it is also a major risk factor for mortality and poor functional recovery. The pathophysiology of SAP is driven by two converging processes: impaired local airway defence due to dysphagia as well as reduced airway clearance reflexes, and systemic stroke-induced immunodepression driven by dysfunction of the autonomic nervous system. While post-stroke immunodepression is a major risk factor for SAP, it might limit unwanted autoimmune responses within the brain. Conversely, SAP itself may drive neuroinflammation and contribute to post-stroke cognitive impairment. Despite its clinical importance, high-quality evidence to guide practice on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of SAP remains scarce and guideline recommendations are mostly based on expert consensus. Diagnosis of SAP is suggested to be based on standardised clinical criteria supported by chest radiography and C-reactive protein as an adjunct where uncertainty persists. After diagnosis, guidelines suggest prompt empirical antibiotic therapy according to local protocols. In contrast, preventive antibiotics, even for high-risk patients, neither improve clinical outcome nor reduce SAP frequency. Currently recommended preventive strategies for SAP therefore mostly focus on dysphagia management and early mobilisation. This review integrates the pathophysiology, long-term consequences of SAP and further research directions based on the current knowledge on post-stroke immunology with prevention, diagnosis and treatment of SAP as set out in the recent European Stroke Organisation guideline and related guidelines.

articles.title: Outcome measures and monitoring framework in juvenile systemic sclerosis: bridging routine care and clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Juvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc) is an orphan multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause significant morbidity during childhood and can lead to significant worsening of quality of life. The pathophysiological features are identical with adult-onset systemic sclerosis (SSc), jSSc exhibits a distinct clinical phenotype characterized by a significantly higher prevalence of diffuse cutaneous involvement, frequent overlap syndromes, distinct autoantibody profiles, and different long-term survival trajectories. Historically, the evaluation of jSSc has relied heavily on the extrapolation of adult outcome measures, which fail to account for developmental physiology, somatic growth, and pediatric-specific feasibility constraints.

AREAS COVERED: This review provides a comprehensive overview of indicators of disease activity and severity which might be used in daily clinical practice and adapted as outcome measures in future clinical trials. It includes global outcome measures, organ-specific outcomes (including skin, pulmonary, cardiac, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, renal, and vascular involvement), patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and clinician-reported outcomes (ClinROs). The performance of adult indices within pediatric cohorts are evaluated, if applicable. Additionally, we analyze severity scores like the Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity Score (J4S) alongside modern consensus metrics derived from the international Hamburg symposia. We emphasize the integration of pediatric-adapted clinical assessments, quantitative imaging, and patient and physician related outcomes.

EXPERT OPINION: The development of outcome measure in jSSc requires a paradigm shift from static severity scores to dynamic, multi-dimensional indicators capable of differentiating reversible inflammatory activity from potential permanent damage accrual. Validating pediatric-specific thresholds for physiological and cutaneous change remains an urgent priority. Over the next decade, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven quantitative imaging, decentralized home-based digital health tools, and molecular biomarkers probably will gain an essential role to optimize clinical trial readiness and personalize therapeutic strategies for children with systemic sclerosis.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories.

RESULTS: A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality.

CONCLUSION: Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

articles.title: Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less negative across the dysglycemic groups (p < 0.001), consistent with reduced longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI correlated positively with E/e', linking higher renal vascular resistance with higher estimated LV filling pressure (r = 0.440, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

articles.title: Evidence for Embedding Smoking and Vaping Cessation Support in Primary Care: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smoking is a leading preventable cause of disease, with vaping creating new public health concerns. This review synthesised evidence on interventions and strategies to integrate cessation care into primary healthcare.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic scoping review of PubMed and EMBASE for studies published between 19 September 2020 and 19 September 2024. Eligible studies evaluated smoking and/or vaping cessation interventions or implementation strategies in primary care settings in high-income countries (Australia, Canada, EU, UK, USA). Two reviewers independently extracted data on study characteristics, intervention types, outcomes, and abstinence verification.

RESULTS: Of 2166 records screened, 30 empirical studies were included. Most focused on smoking cessation, with only two addressing e-cigarette users. The strongest evidence supported multi-component interventions combining behavioural counselling and pharmacological treatments. Implementation strategies included electronic health record prompts, cost-free pharmacotherapy, financial incentives, and integration of cessation support into low-dose computed tomography screening or post-spirometry feedback. Evidence for the effectiveness of provider education was inconclusive.

CONCLUSIONS: The evidence supports several interventions and implementation strategies for integrating smoking cessation into primary care, though data on vaping cessation are limited. These findings will inform the development of targeted approaches to enhance cessation support in primary healthcare.

articles.title: Re-Evaluating Predictive Performance in the Clinical Risk Analysis Index of Frailty.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether the Risk Analysis Index (RAI), last calibrated in 2010-2014, requires scoring system changes to remain an effective measure of surgical frailty.

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: The RAI is among the most validated and widely used measures of surgical frailty. However, like any clinical prediction model, the RAI's scoring system might be prone to algorithmic drift that could invalidate continued use.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of patients evaluated in outpatient surgery clinics at Veterans Health Administration (VHA) or University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC). All-cause mortality was measured 180 days after frailty assessment using the RAI-clinical questionnaire (RAI-C).

RESULTS: In 410,715 patients from UPMC and 190,044 patients from VHA, the existing RAI-C scoring system demonstrated strong discrimination (c = 0.868 95% CI [0.864-0.872] for UPMC, 0.827 [0.822-0.832] for VHA) which improved modestly after recalibrating parameter weights (c = 0.872 95% CI [0.868-0.876], for UPMC, 0.839 [0.834-0.845] for VHA). Calibration improved slightly, especially at the extremes where the model tends to underpredict mortality, but little change was observed in the range around the threshold of frailty. Of note, the scoring weights associated with a cancer diagnosis demonstrated some multicollinearity-driven instability, but cancer remained the largest contributor to total score. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that reclassification of just a single additional patient as frail would require screening 1400-6000 patients with the recalibrated system, depending on the threshold score defining frailty, and after accounting for the harms of false-positive classification, weighted proportional to the odds at each threshold probability.

CONCLUSIONS: The RAI scoring system remains robust after a decade of widespread use without evidence of meaningful algorithmic drift. The minimal incremental improvement associated with recalibration does not justify the resources required to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system.

articles.title: Association of serum element levels with cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes mellitus risk in a Kurdish population of western Iran.
articles.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
articles.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a significant public health concern globally. Among the most prevalent NCDs the study aims to explore the association of some elements with the the likelihood of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) development. In this cross-sectional case control study, 300 individuals with CVDs (n = 110), T2D (n = 70), and a control group (n = 120) from the Ravansar Non-Communicable Disease (RaNCD) cohort in western Iran were examined. The RaNCD cohort is part of the PERSIAN cohort study, consisting of 10,000 adults. Participants aged 35-65 were stratified into three clusters based on their health status. Various elements, including aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), phosphorus (P), manganese (Mn), potassium (K), cobalt (Co), lithium (Li), boron (B), molybdenum (Mo), and vanadium (V) in the blood serum was performed using the ICP-MS method, and data were analyzed using multivariable techniques, including logistic regression and clustering analysis. Our analysis revealed a notable association between most elements and the risks of CVD and T2D in the logistic regression model after adjusting for age and gender. Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels. In the T2D group, four clusters were identified: Al-B, Mn-Co-Mo, K-P, and V-Li-Ca-Mg. In the CVD group, five clusters were observed: K, B-Co-Mo, Li-Mg, Ca-P, and Mn-Al-V. The study provides valuable insights into the role of some essential elements in the development of CVDs and T2D. The key elements that are most linked to the elevated risk of CVDs and T2D include calcium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, lithium, aluminum, phosphorus, and magnesium. Further exploration of the intricate relationships between elements and disease risk could enhance our understanding of preventive strategies and personalized interventions for individuals at risk of CVDs and T2D.

articles.title: VERINA: A Phase IV Prospective Multicenter Study of Vericiguat in Indian Patients with Worsening Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remain at high risk of cardiovascular (CV) death and hospitalization following a worsening heart-failure event. Data on vericiguat, a prescription oral medication used to treat symptomatic chronic HF, in adult Indian patients are limited.

METHODS: Adults with chronic HFrEF and a worsening heart-failure event were enrolled in a prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm phase IV study design. Participants received vericiguat in addition to foundational medical therapy (FMT) and were followed for approximately 48 weeks. The primary endpoint was CV death or first hospitalization for HF. Secondary endpoints included CV death, first hospitalization for HF, all-cause death or first hospitalization for HF, all-cause death and safety outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 231 patients who underwent screening, 205 received vericiguat and comprised the safety analysis set; of these, 203 patients constituted the full analysis set. The mean age of participants was 58 years. Baseline use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors was 52.7% and 75.6%, respectively. At week 48, Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates were 10.1% for the primary endpoint, 3.3% for CV death, 9.1% for first hospitalization for HF, 11.5% for all-cause death or first hospitalization for HF, and 5.9% for all-cause death. Attainment of the target dose was 91.6%, with 69.5% of participants reaching and maintaining 10 mg by week 4. Study drug-related adverse events (AEs) were reported in 3.4% of participants, and treatment-emergent AEs requiring discontinuation in 2.0% of participants.

CONCLUSION: In Indian patients with worsening HFrEF, high target-dose attainment and no new safety signals were observed during 48 weeks of vericiguat treatment.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry-India: CTRI/2022/11/047636.

articles.title: Combination of oral fluoropyrimidines and EGFR-directed antibodies in frail patients with metastatic colorectal cancer: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence of treatment strategies in frail patients (i.e. not fit for combination therapies) with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is limited to dose-reduced doublet regimens or oral fluoropyrimidines (FP) with bevacizumab. We conducted a systematic review analyzing evidence for oral FPs with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed monoclonal antibodies for patients with RAS wild-type (WT) mCRC across treatment lines.

METHODS: We searched PubMed and Cochrane Library for phase II and phase III studies evaluating oral FPs (capecitabine, S-1 or trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI)) plus EGFR-directed monoclonal antibody (panitumumab or cetuximab) in mCRC. Outcomes included efficacy and safety.

RESULTS: Seven publications met inclusion criteria (n = 262 patients). First-line data was limited to elderly cohorts receiving capecitabine plus cetuximab or panitumumab with a median progression-free survival (PFS)/median overall survival (OS) of 7.2/17.1 months (cetuximab) and 7.5/23.7 months (panitumumab), respectively. In third-line and beyond, median PFS for the combination of FTD/TPI plus cetuximab or panitumumab ranged from 2.4 (cetuximab) to 5.8 months (panitumumab), and OS from 9.8 (cetuximab) to 14.2 months (panitumumab). S-1 plus cetuximab was associated with a median PFS of 5.5 months and OS of 13.6 months.

CONCLUSION: While capecitabine should not be used together with anti-EGFR antibodies, FTD/TPI in combination with an EGFR-directed antibody appears feasible, shows promising activity and manageable toxicity profile in RAS WT mCRC potentially offering an alternative for frail patients; prospective trials are needed.

articles.title: Patient-specific management in high-risk revision total hip arthroplasty: mid-term outcomes of a next-generation constrained acetabular liner.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Managing recurrent instability in revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) requires a personalized approach, as traditional constrained liners often yield suboptimal results due to locking-mechanism failure and limited impingement-free range of motion. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term clinical outcomes of a novel constrained acetabular liner (CAL) when utilized as a patient-specific solution for a high-risk cohort undergoing complex rTHA. By tailoring the constraint to individual biomechanical deficits, this next-generation device seeks to mitigate historic failure modes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients who underwent 37 rTHA procedures with a next-generation CAL at a single urban academic center between March 2017 and October 2023. Average follow-up was 4.7 years (range, 0.3 to 9.7 years). The most common indication for rTHA was instability (70.3%), followed by infection (16.2%), aseptic loosening (10.8%), and polyethylene wear (2.7%). Just over one third of patients (37.5%) had undergone a prior revision. Preoperative constructs included fixed-bearing (37.8%), dual-mobility (32.4%), CAL (24.3%), static spacer (2.7%), and hemiarthroplasty (2.7%).

RESULTS: In most procedures (70.3%), the CAL was implanted into a pre-existing acetabular cup, whereas 29.7% involved both cup and liner revision. Following rTHA, no cases of implant wear, breakage, acetabular cup aseptic loosening, or periprosthetic fracture were observed. Six patients (18.8%) underwent a total of sixteen subsequent reoperations after CAL implantation-10 for instability and 6 for infection. Among instability-related reoperations, 4 involved revision to a new next-generation CAL. Survivorship free from all-cause reoperation was 83.8% at one year and 72.6% at latest follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates favorable mid-term clinical outcomes and reoperation-free survivorship following complex revision THA using a novel constrained acetabular liner system. For patient cohorts suffering from severe recurrent dislocation, this next-generation CAL provides an effective, tailored tool in the surgical armamentarium by adapting to unique patient anatomy and soft-tissue compromises. Further research with larger sample sizes and extended follow-up is needed to assess long-term durability.

articles.title: Association between ambient temperature and acute kidney injury: a nationwide space-time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan.
articles.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe condition characterized by a sudden decline of kidney function with a high mortality rate and healthcare costs. While extreme heat is a recognized risk factor for AKI, the effects of both heat and cold exposure across different demographics remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between ambient temperatures and AKI emergency hospitalizations, with a focus on age and sex differences.

METHODS: Using a nationwide database, we identified 119,027 AKI emergency hospitalizations from 2011 to 2019. A space-time-stratified case-crossover study with conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was applied to estimate region-specific relative risk (RR) of AKI emergency hospitalization over lag days 0-13. Pooled RRs were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Analyses were stratified by age (younger, 15-49; middle-age, 50-64; and older, 65+ years old) and sex.

RESULTS: Both extreme cold (first percentile) and heat (99th percentile) were associated with an increased risk of AKI emergency hospitalizations, with cumulative RRs of 1.24 (95% CI 1.09-1.40) and 2.21 (95% CI 2.00-2.43), respectively. Heat-related susceptibility was highest in younger (RR 4.24, 95% CI 2.93-6.15) and middle-aged men (RR 4.20, 95% CI 3.46-5.10), while in women it occurred in the older group (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.64-2.14). Cold-related susceptibility was highest among older males (RR 1.28, 95% CI 1.06-1.53) and females (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.04-1.58).

SIGNIFICANCE: Extreme temperatures elevate AKI risk, with distinct age- and sex-specific vulnerability patterns. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention strategies during temperature extremes, particularly protecting younger and middle-aged men from heat and older adults from cold exposure. Understanding the biological and social mechanisms underlying these demographic differences is essential for developing effective public health interventions in a changing climate IMPACT STATEMENT: This nationwide study reveals that both extreme heat and cold significantly increase acute kidney injury (AKI) emergency hospitalizations in Japan, with distinct age- and sex-specific vulnerability patterns. Younger and middle-aged men face a fourfold higher risk during heat exposure, while older adults of both sexes are most vulnerable to cold. These findings expand beyond heat-focused research and demonstrate the need for demographically targeted prevention strategies. As climate change intensifies temperature variability, these demographic-specific patterns highlight the need for tailored public health interventions to protect kidney health and reduce preventable AKI hospitalizations.

articles.title: Correction: VFA/TAMAI predicts aggravated organ damage after central line removal due to catheter‑related bloodstream infection in patients with enterocutaneous fistula.
Robotic emergency surgery in geriatric care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults present unique challenges in emergency general surgery (EGS) due to increased comorbidities and frailty. While minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including laparoscopic (lap) and robotic techniques, reduces perioperative morbidity, the role of minimally invasive EGS in geriatric patients remains unclear. This study compares outcomes for geriatric EGS patients following robotic, lap, and open procedures. We hypothesize that MIS approaches would improve perioperative outcomes in geriatric patients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the ACS-NSQIP database (2022-2023) including patients ≥65 years undergoing emergent or urgent intra-abdominal surgery. Operative approach was categorized as robotic, lap, or open. The primary outcome was severe complication, and secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, and readmission.

RESULTS: 58,940 patients were included: 1832 robotic, 30,137 lap, and 26,971 open. With robotic vs lap and open, operative time was shortest (82.5 vs 110 vs 96 min, p < 0.001), conversion to open was less frequent (6.2 vs 12.9%, p < 0.001), and LOS was shorter (4 vs 4 vs 8 days, p < 0.001). Readmission and reoperation were lowest following MIS (9.2 vs 7.9 vs 9.8%, and 3.7 vs 3.3% vs 7.6%, both p < 0.001). After propensity matching, robotic patients had higher ASA scores and more transfusions but lower rates of sepsis (2.6 vs 6.5%) and mortality (2.3 vs 2.7%) compared to the lap group (p < 0.001). Multivariable regression demonstrated decreased risk of severe complications for patients who underwent robotic surgery (p = 0.025) with no difference in operative time or LOS, and patients were more likely to be discharged home.

CONCLUSIONS: Robotic EGS in geriatric patients is associated with fewer severe complications, lower conversion rates, shorter LOS, and favorable discharge disposition.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Reconstruction Planning of Cheek Soft Tissue Defects: A Comparative Study Against Surgical Expert Consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reconstructive planning for cheek soft tissue defects requires expert assessment of defect size and location to preserve aesthetic harmony. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has emerged as a potential decision-support tool in plastic and reconstructive surgery. This study evaluates the accuracy and reliability of ChatGPT-4o in proposing reconstructive approaches for post-excisional cheek defects.

METHODS: A comparative observational image-based study was performed using 46 standardized oblique facial photographs of healthy volunteers, on which cheek soft tissue defects were manually delineated to simulate post-excisional tissue loss. Each annotated photograph was submitted to ChatGPT-4o alongside a standardized prompt incorporating patient-specific clinical data. Two experts independently rated AI-generated responses across five domains using a five-point Likert scale (1-5). Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).

RESULTS: ChatGPT-4o achieved high ratings across all domains: clinical accuracy 4.88/5, safety 4.59/5, aesthetic result 3.96/5, first reconstruction selection 4.05/5, and relevance of alternatives 3.65/5, with an average of 4.22/5. Strong inter-rater agreement was observed between evaluators (ICC = 0.75, 95% CI 0.57-0.86, p < 0.001), with high consistency for safety (κ = 0.82) and first reconstruction selection (κ = 0.76). However, ChatGPT-4o failed to generate illustrative depictions of the proposed reconstructive approaches.

CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated strong concordance with expert evaluators and shows promise as a decision-support adjunct in cheek reconstructive planning. However, its inability to generate visual depictions of proposed flaps remains a notable limitation. Expert supervision remains indispensable, and prospective clinical validation is warranted before routine implementation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Multiancestry conditional and joint analysis applied to GWAS summary statistics.
articles.abstract: Conditional and joint (COJO) analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) data is a standard post-GWAS analysis for identifying statistically independent associations. Although GWAS meta-analyses are increasingly conducted across multiple ancestry groups, the optimal strategy for multiancestry COJO analysis remains unclear. Here we introduce Manc-COJO, a method for multiancestry COJO analysis. Simulations and real-data analyses show that Manc-COJO improves detection of independent association signals while reducing false positives compared with single-ancestry COJO implemented in genome-wide complex trait analysis (GCTA) and its ad-hoc multiancestry adaptations. We also introduce Manc-COJO:FIX, a follow-up algorithm to identify ancestry-specific independent associations. The C++ implementation of Manc-COJO is over 120-fold faster than GCTA-COJO and supports linkage disequilibrium references derived from either individual-level genotype data or pre-computed matrices, facilitating analyses when data sharing is limited.

articles.title: Food insecurity in the development of metabolic diseases.
