METHODS: We use a panel of 241 countries (2000–2022), 13 UHC expansion episodes and harmonised microdata from four large national surveys (the Behavioural Risk Factor Surveillance System, Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde, Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares, National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey). Estimators include two-way fixed effects (TWFE), synthetic difference-in-differences, Callaway-Sant’Anna staggered difference-in-differences (DID) and wild cluster bootstrap inference for the small-group TWFE.

RESULTS: A one percentage point (pp) increase in the OOP share is associated with 0.16 additional infant deaths per 1000 (p=0.003), robust to income-growth, inequality and health-spending controls. TWFE estimates a 5.9 pp average OOP reduction across UHC episodes (p=0.024); synthetic DID yields a more conservative 3.3 pp (p=0.039), with Indonesia (−10.8 pp), Rwanda (−8.7 pp) and China (−5.3 pp) driving the pooled effect while Mexico (−0.3 pp) and Chile (−1.6 pp) show small short-run changes. In the USA and Brazil, the income gradient in poor health is steep and pro-poor in both self-reported and clinically measured biomarkers (hypertension, diabetes, obesity); in Mexico, catastrophic OOP spending displays a ‘reverse gradient’ concentrated among upper-income households who self-finance private care.

CONCLUSION: Universal coverage on paper does not mechanically deliver universal coverage in practice. The institutional design of where residual OOP falls is at least as policy-relevant as the headline magnitude of any OOP reduction.

articles.title: Patterns and determinants of antimalarial drug use and treatment adherence in Osun State, Southwestern Nigeria: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Nigeria. Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) are first-line treatments, but adherence is suboptimal and resistance is emerging. This study assessed patterns, determinants and barriers related to antimalarial drug use and adherence in Osun State, southwestern Nigeria.

METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional household survey was conducted between October 2024 and September 2025. Using multistage sampling, 1500 residents aged ≥15 years across three senatorial districts were enrolled. Data on sociodemographics, recent antimalarial use, adherence, knowledge and access barriers were collected via structured questionnaires. Descriptive and inferential statistics, including binary logistic regression, were used to identify factors associated with treatment completion.

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 26.7 (±10.7) years; 77.0% were female. Among 713 recent antimalarial users, 70.5% completed the full course. Persistent chloroquine use was reported by 46.0% of users. Cost (40.5%) was the most cited access barrier. In adjusted analysis, treatment completion was significantly associated with tertiary education (adjusted OR (aOR)=1.85, 95% CI 1.32 to 2.59), urban residence (aOR=1.55, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.18), formal drug sources (aOR=2.20, 95% CI 1.55 to 3.12) and awareness of drug resistance (aOR=1.95, 95% CI 1.42 to 2.68).

CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal adherence, persistent use of discontinued drugs and high out-of-pocket costs threaten malaria control and may accelerate drug resistance. Public health strategies should enforce prescription policies, institute basic universal health coverage to subsidise ACTs, implement behaviour change communication and address drug unavailability in rural areas to mitigate resistance risks.

articles.title: Efficacy and Feasibility of Just-in-Time Nudging in Reducing Evening Snacking Measured by Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Micro-Randomized Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to determine whether in people with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a digital nudge delivered by a smartphone app soon after dinner reduces subsequent snacking events as measured by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM).

METHODS: Participants: Adults with T2DM, managed with diet or stable oral antidiabetic medication for at least 3 months, and who habitually snacked after dinner on ≥ 3 nights/week.

DESIGN: Pictographic nudges were co-designed with consumers. After-dinner snacking behaviours were confirmed during a 2-week Lead-In phase by CGM. Thereafter, eligible participants were micro-randomized daily (1:1, MRT phase) to either a pictographic nudge delivered-in-time (Intui Research) or no nudge for a second 2-week period. The primary outcome was the difference in incremental area under the CGM curve (net-iAUC) between nudging days and non-nudging days during the period 90-min post-dinner until 4 AM.

RESULTS: Sixty-six participants completed the Lead-In phase and 56 completed the MRT phase with available CGM data. CGM data were collected over 911 nights during the Lead-In phase and 780 nights during the MRT phase, with a total of 410 digital nudges sent. Over the entire 2-week period there was no effect of nudging on the primary outcome (net-iAUC). However, secondary analyses showed that there was an initial nudge effect that faded over time. Similar results were observed for snacking behaviour and CGM time-in-range.

CONCLUSION: This study provides preliminary feasibility of delivering just-in-time nudges in adults with T2DM, with no overall glycaemic benefit. Exploratory early effects warrant confirmation and investigation of strategies to sustain efficacy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTRN12622000531718.

articles.title: Patient Use of a Comment Function in Electronic Health Records: Mixed Methods Case Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient access to their electronic health records (EHRs) could improve care and reduce errors by enabling patient contribution to documentation. However, interactive functions that support such engagement remain underresearched.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to analyze patients' use of the free-text comment function in the Swedish national patient-accessible EHR.

METHODS: Comments made by patients between 2015 and 2021 for health care professionals to view were retrieved from the patient-accessible EHR administration service in Sweden. The number and length of comments were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests, while the content was examined qualitatively using inductive content analysis. In addition, comments were coded for sentiment (positive, neutral, or negative) and note content, and users were classified according to whether they had submitted at least 1 comment referring to mental health care.

RESULTS: A total of 1670 comments were left by 659 patients, of which 15 had irrelevant content (15/1670, 0.9%; 95% CI 0.4%-1.4%), leaving 1655 comments for analysis. Most comments (948/1655, 57.3%; 95% CI 54.9%-59.7%) were related to matters other than note content, and nearly all had a neutral (920/1655, 55.6%; 95% CI 53.2%-58.0%) or negative (702/1655, 42.4%; 95% CI 40.0%-44.8%) sentiment. Patients who submitted a comment referencing mental health care tended to leave more comments overall (median 7 vs 2 comments per patient), and their comments were more frequently negative than comments written by other patients (313/495, 63.2% vs 389/1160, 33.5%; P<.001). The most prevalent categories were care engagement, perceived inaccuracies, complaints, and requests.

CONCLUSIONS: Patient engagement with clinical notes has the potential to enhance documentation accuracy and strengthen patient-clinician communication. To realize these benefits safely, such features must be deliberately designed and clearly explained to users to avoid patient safety risks and unnecessary burdens on health care professionals.

articles.title: Effect of Sleep Hygiene on Metabolic Syndrome in an Adult Rural Population in India: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) refers to a group of conditions including high blood pressure, excess weight, high blood glucose, and abnormal cholesterol and triglyceride levels that together substantially increase the risk of heart disease and diabetes. Poor sleep hygiene is associated with a higher likelihood of type 2 diabetes, while sleep duration can affect the development of various MetS components. Approximately 25% of adults worldwide currently have MetS, and this prevalence is projected to increase to 50% by 2035. However, there is a distinct lack of evidence about the specific impact of sleep hygiene on cardiometabolic health within the rural Indian population. This study will focus on addressing this literature gap by evaluating these risk factor associations by using validated tools to help develop targeted community interventions.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to estimate the prevalence of poor sleep quality and cardiometabolic risk factors in a rural Indian population and to determine the association between sleep hygiene and cardiometabolic risk factors.

METHODS: This study will be a community-based, cross-sectional, analytical study, and data collection will be carried out by trained personnel using validated tools during house-to-house visits. In this cross-sectional study of 281 rural Indian adults aged ≥40 years, sleep quality will be assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (a score >5 indicates poor sleep), alongside direct measurements of blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose, BMI (≥25 kg/m² for obesity), waist circumference, and the Madras Diabetes Research Foundation-Indian Diabetes Risk Score for diabetes risk. Data will be collected through a door-to-door approach, with informed consent entered into Google Forms, and quality checked via training and regular reviews. Using R software, analyses will include prevalence estimates with 95% CIs; chi-square or t tests for associations between poor sleep and cardiometabolic risks; and logistic regression (P<.05) adjusted for confounders such as diet, stress, and physical activity.

RESULTS: This study began in January 2025 with conceptualization and ethics approval obtained in June 2025. Data collection commenced in August 2025 following Clinical Trial Registry-India registration, with 53 participants enrolled as of May 5, 2026. Standardized tools (GAD-7, PHQ-9, and GPAQ) were incorporated to assess key confounding variables. Data collection is projected to finish by January 2027, with final analysis and study conclusion expected by March 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: The relationship between MetS and sleep hygiene warrants greater attention, particularly as poor sleep habits become increasingly prevalent alongside MetS. This study will deepen the understanding of their connection, paving the way for targeted interventions and prevention strategies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry-India CTRI/2025/08/092892; https://tinyurl.com/3sak2h9x.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/90117.

articles.title: Agentic artificial intelligence for code status extraction from clinical notes: a cross-model comparison of single agent, reflective agent, and multiagent extractor-reviewer system.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether increasing agentic architectural complexity via self-reflection or multiagent design improves clinical code status extraction (Do Not Resuscitate [DNR], Do Not Intubate [DNI], Comfort Measures Only [CMO]) across open-source large language models (LLMs) of varying capabilities.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a controlled cross-model comparison evaluating 3 architectures: (1) single extractor agent, (2) single agent with self-reflection, and (3) sequential multiagent extractor-reviewer system. Four open-source LLMs (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B) were evaluated on 1000 Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Note discharge summaries. Ground truth labels were established through a physician-AI dual review with adjudication (Cohen's κ = 0.98-0.99). Models were evaluated on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen's κ, token consumption, and processing latency. McNemar's test was used for paired comparisons.

RESULTS: For capable larger models (GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B), single-agent architectures achieved comparable or superior performance for explicit code status (DNR, DNI) relative to complex systems, whereas multiagent review doubled token consumption and latency without accuracy gains. Reflective self-review significantly impaired MedGemma-27B-IT on DNI extraction (P = .047). For the smaller DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, multiagent review provided statistically significant corrective benefits for DNR (P = .017) and CMO (P < .001), demonstrating a capability-threshold effect, though performance remained below clinically acceptable levels.

DISCUSSION: Architectural complexity does not enhance extraction performance for capable LLMs, and reflective self-review may cause conservative overcorrection. Multiagent verification value is inversely related to model capability.

CONCLUSION: Single-agent LLMs provide optimal accuracy and efficiency for explicit clinical extraction in capable models. Agentic complexity must be matched to both task characteristics and model capability rather than adopted by default.

articles.title: Exploring Perspectives and Barriers in Implementing Home Monitoring for Pediatric Pulmonary Diseases: Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home monitoring has the potential to enable early detection of disease progression in pediatric lung diseases such as asthma and cystic fibrosis (CF). There is minimal evidence regarding the opinions of caregivers and children on home monitoring.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore children's and caregivers' perspectives on home monitoring.

METHODS: This multicenter, mixed methods study included children aged 6 to 18 years with asthma or CF and their caregivers. Participants were recruited from Juliana Children's Hospital and Erasmus MC Sophia Children's Hospital between September 2023 and June 2025. Participants completed a structured questionnaire assessing experiences, attitudes, and potential barriers and facilitators to home monitoring. Fourteen children and their caregivers took part in in-depth interviews. Conventional content analysis was applied to both open-text and interview data.

RESULTS: A total of 113 caregiver-child dyads (62 [54.9%] asthma and 51 [45.1%] CF) participated in this study. Willingness to use home monitoring was high among both children (asthma: n=47, 83.9%; CF: n=30, 62.5%) and caregivers (asthma: n=54, 87.1%; CF: n=44, 86.3%). Children with asthma and their caregivers showed significantly greater willingness to use the proposed types of home monitoring than children with CF and their caregivers. Caregivers who expressed difficulty with symptom interpretation were significantly more motivated to use home monitoring. Key barriers included time demands, usability, device size, and concerns about maintaining personal contact with health care providers. Facilitators included compact, user-friendly devices, clear instructions, and improved disease understanding.

CONCLUSIONS: High willingness to adopt home monitoring was observed among children with asthma and children with CF, but preferences and perceived barriers differ. Tailoring device choice and implementation strategies to patient needs, minimizing burden, and integrating medical oversight are important for successful uptake.

articles.title: Exploring heterogeneous treatment effects for GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Understanding treatment effect heterogeneity (TEH) is essential to improve care for patients living with chronic diseases like type 2 diabetes. Individual responses to treatment can vary substantially, and identifying the factors that drive TEH may enable increased personalization of treatment and follow-up. In this study, we conduct an exploratory analysis of TEH for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists used to treat type 2 diabetes. Endpoints are defined using hemoglobin A1c measurements, body mass index, and blood pressure. We use causal forests to conduct global tests for TEH, estimate variable importances to rank candidate effect modifiers, and estimate the magnitude of heterogeneity. Data from three clinical trials are analyzed: SUSTAIN 6 (subcutaneous semaglutide versus placebo, n=3297), PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide versus placebo, n=3183), and LEADER (subcutaneous liraglutide versus placebo, n=9340), pooled to 13,670 patients after exclusions. Baseline hemoglobin A1c ranks highest among candidate effect modifiers across methods, and kidney function ranks next in the relative risk causal forest; we discuss their clinical implications. The magnitude estimates, however, show that the variation these covariates jointly explain is small. As such, large covariate-driven heterogeneity can be ruled out in these trials, and the average treatment effect provides a reasonable summary for most patients.

articles.title: Feasibility and results of the implementation of a post-discharge coordination circuit for patients with acute heart failure from the emergency department.
Spanish catheter ablation registry. 25th official report of the Heart Rhythm Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (2025).
authors: collaborators of the Spanish catheter ablation registry
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: We report the results of the 2025 Spanish catheter ablation registry.

METHODS: This retrospective registry included catheter ablation procedures performed at participating hospitals in Spain and recorded in the REDCap database using a dedicated data collection form.

RESULTS: A total of 109 centers participated, reporting 33 435 ablations. Atrial fibrillation was the most commonly treated arrhythmia (14 452 cases), with single-shot techniques being the most frequently used approach (63%) and a marked increase in pulsed field ablation (37% vs 21% in 2024). The remaining arrhythmia substrates remained at similar levels. The overall acute success rate was 95%, the complication rate was 1.6%, and the mortality rate was 0.04%. There was a marked increase in outpatient procedures (33% vs 18% in 2024), particularly atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia ablation (50%) and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation (45%). A total of 467 pediatric ablations were performed in 38 centers. Accessory pathway ablation was the most common procedure (65.3%), with a 97% success rate.

CONCLUSIONS: A similar number of centers participated, with a slight increase in the number of procedures compared with 2024. Atrial fibrillation remained the most frequently treated arrhythmia. Acute success, complication, and mortality rates remained stable. The accreditation process for centers and professionals is well-established, with a stable number of annual accreditations. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

articles.title: Late-pregnancy maternal serum alkaline phosphatase levels and risk of early postpartum cardiometabolic disease: A municipality-wide electronic health record-based cohort study in Tianjin, China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between gestational age-standardized maternal alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels and early postpartum cardiometabolic disease.

METHODS: The study included 166,986 singleton pregnancies from the Tianjin Health and Medical Data Platform in Tianjin, China (2009-2023). Maternal serum ALP levels measured within two weeks before delivery were gestational age-standardized and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcomes were early postpartum cardiometabolic diseases including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and a composite outcome comprising these conditions. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.7 years, compared with the highest gestational age-standardized ALP quartile, the lowest quartile was associated with higher risks of postpartum hypertension (HR: 1.18, 95% CI: 1.09, 1.28), diabetes mellitus (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.10, 1.37), CVD (HR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.07, 1.28), and composite outcome (HR: 1.13, 95% CI: 1.08, 1.20). Exploratory analyses showed limited incremental discrimination after adding gestational age-standardized ALP to models containing adverse pregnancy outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower gestational age-standardized maternal ALP levels before delivery were associated with a higher risk of early postpartum cardiometabolic disease. Further studies across ethnically and geographically diverse populations are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Association of Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis With Systemic Lipid Metabolism in Patients With Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Spinal epidural lipomatosis (SEL) is often regarded as a local consequence of obesity, yet its relationship with systemic lipid metabolism and symptom severity in lumbar spinal stenosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) is central to atherogenic lipid transport and ectopic fat deposition. Examining the association between systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities, including elevated ApoB levels, and epidural fat accumulation may provide insights into the metabolic pathogenesis and clinical relevance of SEL.

PURPOSE: To determine whether SEL is associated with systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities and greater preoperative symptom burden in patients undergoing surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS).

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study.

PATIENT SAMPLE: A consecutive series of 1,145 patients who underwent posterior decompression for symptomatic LSS between December 2023 and December 2025. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 patients without SEL.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Serum lipid and other biochemical markers, epidural fat/spinal canal (EF/SpC) index on lumbar magnetic resonance imaging, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores for leg and back pain.

METHODS: SEL was diagnosed and graded on preoperative lumbar MRI according to the Borré classification, using the epidural fat/spinal canal index. Propensity score matching was performed for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, drinking history, hypertension, and diabetes. Biochemical variables and preoperative clinical scores were compared between matched SEL and non-SEL patients. Conditional logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with SEL. BMI-adjusted partial Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between the EF/SpC index and biochemical markers. Regression-based trend analyses were conducted to assess changes in lipid-related markers across increasing SEL severity grades.

RESULTS: Among 1,145 patients with LSS, 105 (9.2%) met the diagnostic criteria for SEL. After matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 non-SEL controls. The SEL group had higher apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels than controls, as well as higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. ApoB remained independently associated with SEL in conditional logistic regression (odds ratio per 0.1 g/L, 1.141; 95% confidence interval, 1.019-1.277; P=0.022). Within the SEL group, the EF/SpC index correlated positively with triglycerides (ρ=0.43, q<0.001) and ApoB (ρ=0.40, q=0.002), while atherogenic lipid markers increased progressively with SEL severity. Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

articles.title: Integrative Target Fishing and Proteomics Reveal the Molecular Targets of Abrus cantoniensis in Alleviating Dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Abrus cantoniensis (AC) is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb used for hepatitis, with demonstrated lipid-regulating activity. However, as a multi-component herbal system, the specific bioactive monomers and their direct protein targets remain to be elucidated.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study integrates target fishing with proteomics to capture hepatic protein targets of AC and elucidate its lipid-regulating mechanisms.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Abrine, a pharmacopoeial marker compound employed as a probe, was used to synthesize abrine-functionalized magnetic beads (Fe3O4-SH-BP-abrine, FSBA) via photo-crosslinking for target capture from mouse liver lysates. Proteins were identified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Bioinformatic analyses, including Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), were conducted. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and Western blotting (WB) were employed for validation.

RESULTS: AC ameliorated hepatic steatosis in HFD-induced dyslipidemic mice. KEGG enrichment identified the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) as the top-ranked pathway, consistent with its central role in NADPH-dependent lipid biosynthesis. Molecular docking and MD simulations predicted stable interactions between abrine and PPP enzymes. SPR verified a direct interaction between abrine and G6PD. RT-qPCR demonstrated downregulation of G6pd, Tkt, Taldo1, H6pd, and Aldoa at the mRNA level. IHC and WB consistently showed reduced protein expression of G6PD, PGD, and TKT after AC treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Target fishing combined with proteomics uncovered AC's anti-dyslipidemic mechanism via the PPP. The identified PPP-related targets provide mechanistic insight into AC's lipid-regulating activity.

articles.title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

articles.title: Prolonged grief disorder in family caregivers after oncology palliative care: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family caregivers may experience prolonged grief disorder (PGD) and depressive symptoms after a relative's death.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate PGD prevalence and identify associated factors among family caregivers of patients who died in an oncology palliative care unit.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 80 family caregivers interviewed at least six months after the patient's death. Assessments included sociodemographic and perceived support questionnaires, the PG-13 instrument, and the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Adjusted associations with PGD were estimated using hierarchical binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: PGD prevalence was 25.0% (20/80; 95% CI 16.0-35.9), and moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms were observed in 32.5% (26/80) of caregivers. In the final adjusted model, higher odds of PGD were associated with female patient sex (OR = 16.47, 95% CI 1.30-208.80; p = 0.031) and moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (OR = 78.77, 95% CI 7.63-812.79; p < 0.001). Lower odds were associated with routine physical activity (OR = 0.07, 95% CI 0.01-0.84; p = 0.036) and perceived bereavement support (OR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.02-0.76; p = 0.024).

CONCLUSION: PGD affected one quarter of caregivers and was strongly associated with depressive symptom severity. Routine physical activity and perceived bereavement support were associated with lower adjusted odds of PGD. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Reversible wall motion abnormalities do not predict long-term mortality if coronary flow reserve is accounted for: A 15-year contrast stress-echo study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress echocardiography (SE) is widely used to detect myocardial ischaemia in the scenario of chronic coronary syndromes (CCS). Despite that, the prognostic value of SE has been rarely assessed. We aim to establish whether the presence of reversible wall motion abnormalities (RWMA), remains independently associated with long-term mortality when considering myocardial perfusion (MP) and Doppler coronary flow velocity reserve in the left anterior descending artery (CFVR-LAD).

METHOD: 1002 subjects who underwent Dipyridamole contrast SE, for suspected CCS, between 2007 and 2012 at the Parma University Hospital were enrolled. The endpoint is all-cause mortality. The probability of survival was calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method and event-rate curves were compared using the log-rank test.

RESULTS: There were 376 deaths (37.5%) during a median follow-up of 13.8 years. Mean age was 66 ± 11 years, females represented 38%, 32% had known CCS. SE results showed RWMA in 17.5%, reversible MP abnormalities in 26.2%, and reduced CFVR-LAD in 42% of the study population. Revascularization within 3 months of the SE was performed in 185 subjects (18.5%). In multivariate Cox proportional hazard analysis, among the SE variables, only CFVR-LAD<2 remained associated with mortality (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.94-3.5, p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: In the setting of CCS patients, CFVR-LAD is the only SE variable maintaining independent association with long-term mortality.

articles.title: Temporal trends and outcomes of intravascular imaging in chronic total occlusion interventions: insights from the PROGRESS-CTO registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In this study we investigated temporal trends, indications, practice variation, and outcomes associated with intravascular imaging (IVI) use in a large, multicenter chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) registry.

METHODS: We analyzed CTO PCIs performed at 76 US and international centers in 2012-2026 in the PROGRESS-CTO registry. Patients were categorized according to IVI use. P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Among 18,024 CTO PCIs, IVI was used in 10,569 procedures (58.6%). IVI use increased over time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was the predominant modality, accounting for 98.1% of IVI-guided procedures. Following 1:1 propensity score matching, technical (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group. Difference was also pronounced when IVUS was used to cross ambiguous proximal cap: technical success was 85.1% versus 75.9% (OR, 1.81; 95% CI, 1.49-2.21), and procedural success was 83.0% versus 75.1% (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.34-1.99). Centers contributing <100 cases had lower IVI use than centers contributing ≥100 cases (47.7% vs 58.7%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: IVI use during CTO PCI continues to increase. Procedures in which IVUS was used to facilitate lesion crossing were associated with higher technical and procedural success rates and similar in-hospital MACE rates. The association with success was also pronounced when IVUS was used to resolve proximal cap ambiguity. IVI use varied significantly among participating centers, highlighting differences in practice patterns and adoption of IVI during CTO PCI.

articles.title: Advanced right heart failure stage at first documentation of severe tricuspid regurgitation: beyond the late-referral paradigm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) frequently present with advanced right heart failure (RHF), commonly attributed to delayed referral for intervention. Whether this reflects delayed referral or the stage at which severe TR is first documented remains uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 625 consecutive patients with a first echocardiographic diagnosis of severe TR. RHF severity was classified using a validated hierarchical staging system (Stages 1-4). In a subgroup of 310 patients with a previous echocardiogram documenting non-severe TR, RHF stage was retrospectively assessed before severe TR was first documented. Two-year all-cause mortality was evaluated.

RESULTS: At first documentation of severe TR, 66.4% of patients were classified as Stage 3 and 17.3% as Stage 4, whereas only 16.3% were in Stages 1-2. Functional TR accounted for 85% of cases. RHF stage was associated with progressively higher TRI-SCORE and two-year mortality. Among patients with prior non-severe TR, 78% were already in Stage 3-4 before severe TR was first documented, whereas only 7% had reached Stage 4.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe TR was predominantly diagnosed in patients with stage 3-4 RHF. Higher RHF stages were already present in most patients before severe TR was first documented. These findings suggest that delayed referral alone may not fully explain the advanced clinical profile of severe TR and that eligibility for guideline-directed intervention frequently coincides with an already advanced stage of disease.

articles.title: Late gadolinium enhancement dispersion mapping predicts major arrhythmic events in patients with prior myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial scar heterogeneity is a key determinant of ventricular arrhythmias after myocardial infarction (MI). Late gadolinium enhancement dispersion mapping (LGE-DM) quantifies structural complexity, but its prognostic role in ischemic cardiomyopathy remains unevaluated.

METHODS: We retrospectively included 364 consecutive patients with prior MI (>90 days). For each LGE image, a parametric map was generated and each enhanced pixel scored (0-8) based on surrounding signal distribution; the global dispersion score (GDS) was calculated as the mean pixel score, quantifying pixel-to-pixel heterogeneity. The endpoint was a composite of sudden cardiac death (SCD), resuscitated cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or appropriate ICD therapies.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4 years, 42 arrhythmic events occurred. Patients with events showed significantly higher GDS than event-free patients (0.53 vs 0.32, P < 0.0001). Multivariable Cox regression confirmed GDS as an independent predictor (HR 1.16 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI 1.03-1.29), while LVEF and LGE extent were not, and GDS remained independently associated with events when LGE extent was forced into the model (HR 1.12 per 0.1-unit increase, P = 0.005). In patients with LVEF >35%, GDS was the only independent predictor across all multivariable models. Harrell's C-index was 0.682, with an optimism of 0.012 on bootstrap resampling. ROC analysis identified GDS >0.5 as a provisional cut-off derived within the same cohort (apparent AUC 0.74 overall; 0.81 in the LVEF >35% subgroup). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed worse prognosis in patients with GDS >0.5 (overall: p = 0.0002; LVEF >35%: p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: LGE dispersion independently predicts malignant ventricular arrhythmias post-MI, outperforming LGE extent and LVEF. GDS may improve SCD risk stratification particularly in patients with LVEF >35%, a population not adequately targeted by current LVEF-based criteria. External validation is required before the proposed threshold can be used clinically.

articles.title: Pressure-volume loop reconstruction of Impella support in severe aortic regurgitation: explaining a hemodynamic paradox.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic regurgitation (AR) causes left ventricular (LV) volume overload, while transvalvular Impella support may permit regurgitant recirculation. We constructed schematic pressure-volume (PV) loops to illustrate the interaction between ventricular unloading and systemic perfusion in severe AR.

METHODS: Conceptual LV PV loops were constructed from established principles of ventricular mechanics to depict progressive AR, cardiogenic shock (CS), and alternative hypothetical responses to Impella support. No patient-specific measurements or numerical simulation were used.

RESULTS: Increasing AR was depicted by rightward PV-loop displacement and greater LV volume excursion without quantifying effective forward stroke volume. The hypothetical transition to CS showed lower LV pressure and greater end-systolic volume. During Impella support, a leftward loop shift and smaller enclosed area were compatible with unloading; regurgitant recirculation could offset its benefit and permit recurrent LV distension. Pump flow, regurgitant flow, and effective systemic output could not be derived from the loops.

CONCLUSIONS: This qualitative framework illustrates a plausible hemodynamic paradox: LV unloading during Impella support may coexist with limited improvement in net systemic perfusion in severe AR. It does not establish the magnitude or temporal sequence of these responses.

articles.title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons (2026) Expert Consensus Document on Management of Borderline Left Heart Excluding Unbalanced Atrioventricular Septal Defect and Strategies for Biventricular Conversion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strategies to recruit the left ventricle in borderline left heart (BLH), whether utilizing primary or staged recruitment strategy, are challenged by lack of consensus regarding optimal substrate, timing, and technique.

METHODS: A panel of experienced congenital cardiac surgeons, cardiologists and imaging experts were convened to develop key questions related to BLH management, excluding unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect, from neonatal period through 1 year, using the PICO (Patients/Population, Intervention, Comparison/Control, Outcome) framework. Literature searches were performed for each question. Using a modified Delphi method, consensus statements were developed.

RESULTS: For neonates with BLH, primary biventricular repair should be adopted cautiously, and only with favorable anatomic and physiologic criteria determined by echocardiography and/or magnetic resonance imaging. Neonates in the 'grey-zone', with smaller mitral and aortic valve sizes, endocardial fibroelastosis, indexed left ventricular diastolic volume < 25 ml/m2 and ascending aortic flow < 2.0 L/min/m2, should undergo staged recruitment to potentially facilitate growth of left-sided structures and more durable surgical rehabilitation of left ventricular inflow and outflow. Timing and type of subsequent procedures should be guided by interval cardiac catheterization and magnetic resonance imaging data. Initial palliation of grey-zone neonates can be accomplished with either surgical Norwood or hybrid stage 1 with possible atrial level restriction, and subsequent endocardial fibroelastosis resection along with aortic and mitral valve repair as components of successful complete biventricular conversion.

CONCLUSIONS: Biventricular approaches in BLH should be guided by integration of anatomic and physiologic criteria, with most neonates recommended for staged recruitment rather than primary repair.

articles.title: Genomic epidemiology of Salmonella from retail chicken meat in Japan: decline in pESI-like plasmid-harboring S. Infantis ST32 and predominance of S. Schwarzengrund ST241.
articles.abstract: Salmonella is a major foodborne pathogen, and chicken meat is an important source of infection. This study investigated Salmonella prevalence, serovar distribution, antimicrobial resistance, and genomic characteristics in 150 retail chicken meat samples collected in Japan in 2023. The predominant serovar was S. Schwarzengrund (42.7%), followed by S. Infantis (7.3%), which has long been the predominant serovar in Japan. The globally expanding S. Infantis sequence type (ST) 32 harboring pESI-like plasmids has declined in Japan. In contrast, S. Schwarzengrund ST241 was isolated more frequently in winter (66%) than in summer (31%, P < 0.001) and more often from chicken meat produced in eastern Japan (47.1%) than in western Japan (29.4%, P = 0.042). Antimicrobial resistance was most common to tetracycline (50.6%) and streptomycin (45.7%), whereas kanamycin resistance (33.3%) had declined compared with 2015 to 2019, consistent with reduced use of this antimicrobial in broiler production. Moreover, the proportion of S. Schwarzengrund isolates lacking antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) increased markedly from summer (19.4%) to winter (45.5%). cgMLST analysis revealed that antimicrobial-susceptible S. Schwarzengrund isolates formed the largest clade and, notably, retained pESI-like plasmids despite apparent loss of ARG-containing regions from these plasmids. These findings demonstrate ongoing genomic shifts in Salmonella populations in Japan and underscore the need for continuous genomic surveillance to mitigate their public health impact.

articles.title: Species distribution and antimicrobial susceptibility of Nocardia isolates from patients in Iran with suspected tuberculosis: a two-year study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While nocardiosis can clinically and radiologically resemble tuberculosis (TB), its frequency and species-specific antimicrobial susceptibility in TB-suspected patients in Iran have yet to be conclusively characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the frequency, species distribution, and in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility of Nocardia isolates retrieved from unique patients investigated for suspected TB at a referral center in Iran from March 2021 to March 2023.

METHODS: We analyzed specimens from 2000 unique patients evaluated for suspected TB. Nocardia species were identified by sequencing 16S rRNA, secA1, and rpoB. was used to assess Amikacin, linezolid, imipenem, amoxicillin-clavulanate, moxifloxacin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) were assessed using broth microdilution.

RESULTS: Pulmonary TB was identified in 82 patients (4.1%) and TB-Nocardia coinfection in six (10.7%). The most frequent species were N. cyriacigeorgica (20/56, 35.7%), N. farcinica (12/56, 21.4%), and N. asteroides (10/56, 17.9%). Sputum (32/56, 57.1%) and bronchoalveolar lavage (13/56, 23.2%) were the most common specimen sources. Susceptibility to TMP- SMX (56/56, 100%), linezolid (56/56, 100%), and amikacin (52/56, 93%) was highest. Imipenem susceptibility varied by species; 13/56 isolates (23%) were susceptible to moxifloxacin, and 20/56 (36%) to amoxicillin-clavulanate. These are in vitro findings; treatment outcomes were not assessed.

CONCLUSION: In a single-center cohort of patients investigated for suspected TB but without confirmed TB or another mycobacterial infection, Nocardia was detected in 2.5%. Even though species identification and isolate-specific susceptibility testing may help to inform clinical assessment, the findings require validation and do not conclusively establish clinical treatment effectiveness or failure.

articles.title: Prospects for adiponectin-based therapeutics in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Adiponectin is an adipocyte-derived hormone with broad cardiometabolic benefits, circulating at high levels in healthy individuals but reduced in obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Low adiponectin concentrations are strongly associated with coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI), and heart failure. MIRI remains a major unmet need in contemporary ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) care. Although reperfusion is essential in limiting ischemic myocardial necrosis, it causes deleterious effects such as impaired carbohydrate oxidation, excessive fatty-acid oxidation, intracellular acidosis, calcium (Ca2+) overload, oxidative/nitrative stress, and mitochondrial fragmentation, that expand infarct size, worsen microvascular obstruction, and fuel adverse ventricular remodeling. Activation of the adiponectin-adiponectin receptor (AdipoR) axis directly counteracts these processes by stimulating adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent metabolic rebalancing, restoring mitochondrial fusion-fission homeostasis, enhancing oxidative capacity, reducing inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS-) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-mediated injury, improving endothelial nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, and enhancing microvascular perfusion. In animal models, adiponectin or its mimetics consistently reduced infarct size, improved myocardial function, and attenuated apoptosis, inflammation, and no-reflow. A growing array of therapeutic strategies has emerged, each bringing its own pharmacologic nuances and implications for translation to the clinic. This review summarizes current strategies to enhance adiponectin action, highlights the progress in peptide and small-molecule mimetics, and discusses future directions for clinical translation in cardiometabolic diseases.

articles.title: PLCB3 as a causal regulator linking ferroptosis and immune remodeling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex syndrome lacking effective targeted therapies, but its causal genes and mechanisms remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the role of PLCB3 and its association with ferroptosis in HFpEF.

METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic data and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) data and employed differential expression analysis, mendelian randomization (MR), summary data-based mendelian randomization (SMR), and colocalization analysis to identify key genes associated with HFpEF. Furthermore, functional validation was performed using a HFpEF mouse model and siRNA mediated PLCB3 knockdown in AC16 cardiomyocytes. Cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis related protein expression were subsequently assessed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying PLCB3-mediated ferroptosis.

RESULTS: Phospholipase C beta 3 (PLCB3) was identified as a candidate causal gene for HFpEF. PLCB3 expression was significantly reduced in HFpEF cardiac tissue and a mouse model induced by high-fat diet and L-NAME. Knockdown of PLCB3 decreased cell viability and induced ferroptosis, as indicated by reduced GPX4 and FTH1 expression, increased ACSL4 levels, and elevated lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen species. These effects were significantly reversed by the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1. In vivo, ferroptosis-related markers were similarly altered in HFpEF mice. In addition, immune infiltration analysis revealed significant differences in multiple immune cell populations between HFpEF and controls. Single-cell eQTL-based MR analysis further suggested that PLCB3 expression is associated with specific immune cell subsets, including B cells, CD4+ naïve T cells, and natural killer cells.

CONCLUSION: PLCB3 is a potential regulator of HFpEF and may contribute to disease progression by promoting ferroptosis and immune alterations. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of HFpEF and suggest that targeting PLCB3 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: In vitro inhibitory activity of recombinant olive flounder interferon-γ produced in Chlorella vulgaris against viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus infection.
articles.abstract: Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) is a major viral pathogen that causes substantial and persistent economic losses in olive flounder aquaculture. In this study, recombinant olive flounder interferon-γ (IFN-γ) was produced in the eukaryotic green microalga Chlorella vulgaris PKVL7422, and its in vitro antiviral activity was evaluated in epithelioma papulosum cyprini (EPC) cells. A codon-optimized olive flounder IFN-γ gene was introduced into C. vulgaris, and Western blot analysis showed that the recombinant protein was detected mainly in the culture supernatant. Cytotoxicity assays showed no detectable cytotoxicity at the concentrations tested in the antiviral assays, and cell viability remained above 85.6% even at 10,000 ng/mL. Antiviral activity was evaluated using recombinant VHSV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP). Plaque assay showed that recombinant IFN-γ reduced VHSV infectivity in a dose-dependent manner, with an IC50 of 15.42 ng/mL and reduced infectivity to approximately 0% at concentrations of 100 ng/mL or higher. Fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometric analysis showed that recombinant IFN-γ reduced the VHSV-positive EPC cell population from 60.22% in the infected control group to 28.47%, 9.57%, and 4.92% at concentrations of 20, 50, and 100 ng/mL, respectively. In addition, recombinant IFN-γ induced the expression of antiviral immune-related genes, including STAT1 and ISG15, in EPC cells. These findings suggest that recombinant olive flounder IFN-γ produced in C. vulgaris retains biological activity after purification and exerts a dose-dependent antiviral effect against VHSV in a fish cell model.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement Findings in Isolated Left Ventricular Dilatation and Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and isolated left ventricular dilatation (ILVD) are defined as left ventricular (LV) dilatation, with reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), respectively. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) findings, including LGE extent, location, and number of areas to predict all-cause death in ILVD and DCM, separately.

METHODS: Between 2008 and 2021, we conducted a bicentric retrospective study including all consecutive ILVD and DCM patients referred for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). The primary outcome was all-cause death. A propensity-score matching was performed to balance characteristics between ILVD and DCM populations. Cox regressions were performed to determine the prognostic value of each LGE feature.

RESULTS: Of 2,752 patients (age 52±8 years, 56% males), 408 (15%) patients died after a median (interquartile range) follow-up of 9 (7-12) years, including 268 (16%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 140 (13%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. Overall, 737 (27%) patients had LGE, including 472 (28%) of 1,668 DCM patients and 265 (24%) of 1,084 ILVD patients. After propensity-score matching, in ILVD patients with LGE (N=265), the LGE extent (hazard ratio [HR] 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.78, p=0.015), multiple LGE areas (HR=3.39, 95% CI: 1.66-6.92, p<0.001), and its septal location (HR=2.68, 95% CI: 1.59-4.52, p<0.001) were strong prognosticators of death after adjustment. Similarly, after propensity-score matching, in DCM patients with LGE (N=277), the LGE extent (HR=1.39, 95% CI: 1.06-1.83, p=0.018), multiple LGE areas (HR=2.70, 95% CI: 1.20-6.08, p=0.017), and its septal location (HR=2.82, 95% CI: 1.47-5.41, p=0.002) were strongly associated with death. The CMR LGE score performed well in participants with LGE (area under the curve [AUC] at 10 years, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.69-0.89]).

CONCLUSIONS: LGE findings were strongly and independently associated with death in both ILVD and DCM patients, with each successive LGE characteristic providing significant incremental prognostic value beyond traditional prognosticators, including LVEF.

articles.title: Temporal Trends in Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis Among Critically Ill Patients: Serum Galactomannan Testing Intensity and Host Risk Status.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated temporal trends in invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) incidence in relation to serum galactomannan (GM) testing intensity and compared outcomes by classical host-risk status.

METHODS: Adults with ICU stays ≥72 hours during 2017-2024 were retrospectively screened for proven/probable IPA. Consensus EORTC/MSGERC and FUNDICU definitions defined the primary cohort. Modified criteria were exploratory. Negative binomial and Cox regression assessed incidence and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 11,707 ICU stays, 135 patients met consensus definitions; 55 (40.7%) lacked classical host risk factors, rising to 48.9% under modified criteria. IPA incidence increased over time (IRR/year 1.40; 95% CI 1.06-1.85). After adjustment for serum GM testing intensity, the calendar-year IRR was 0.73 (95% CI 0.54-0.98), whereas testing intensity was strongly associated with measured incidence (IRR 6.15; 95% CI 2.81-13.43). Patients without classical host risk factors received antifungal therapy less often (12.7% vs 67.5%) and had higher crude 30-day mortality (58.2% vs 36.2%). The adjusted host-status association was attenuated (aHR 1.48; 95% CI 0.82-2.66).

CONCLUSIONS: The temporal rise in measured IPA incidence was associated with serum GM testing intensity, underscoring diagnostic ascertainment. Patients without classical host risk factors were treated less often and had higher mortality, although the adjusted association was attenuated.

articles.title: Fatigue, Anxiety and Depression 12 Months After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms.

METHODS: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work.

RESULTS: Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

articles.title: Identifying the Operational Bottleneck to Shock Delivery After Automated External Defibrillator Activation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac arrest registries record automated external defibrillator (AED) use and shock delivery but not post-activation operational timing. We aimed to identify the largest measurable bottleneck and an exploratory pad-application target for shock delivery within 60 seconds of AED power-on.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed timestamps from remotely monitored Nihon Kohden AEDs between January 2018 and February 2026. After excluding inspection records, we grouped records into activation events and quantified intervals. Shock-timing and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were restricted to initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery.

RESULTS: We analyzed 8,115 activation events. Median times were 42 seconds (interquartile range [IQR], 30-56) from power-on to completion of pad application, nine seconds (IQR, 9-11) from pad application to the first analysis, and 52 seconds (IQR, 40-66) from power-on to the first analysis endpoint. The power-on-to-pad-application interval accounted for a median of 81% (IQR, 75-85) of the total power-on-to-first-analysis interval, increasing to 87% (IQR, 85-90) when first analysis occurred more than 60 seconds after power-on. Among 900 initially shock-advised events with recorded shock delivery, the median pad-application-to-shock interval was 15 seconds (IQR 13-17). Exploratory ROC analysis yielded a power-on to pad-application threshold of ≥ 51 seconds in relation to first recorded shock delivery occurring more than 60 seconds after AED power-on.

CONCLUSIONS: The interval from AED power-on to electronically detected completion of pad application, encompassing all intervening actions, was the largest measurable post-activation bottleneck. Completion within 50 seconds may serve as an exploratory process target for first recorded shock delivery within 60 seconds among initially shock-advised events.

articles.title: Real-time feedback during bag-valve-mask ventilation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a before-and-after study (VEntilation during Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation Study, VECARS-2).
authors: Paris Fire Brigade Cardiac Arrest Task Force (collaborators)
articles.abstract: This study compared bag-valve-mask ventilation quality and adherence to the guideline-recommended ventilation volume range during 30:2 cardiopulmonary resuscitation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest before and after the implementation of real-time feedback. We conducted a before-and-after observational study of two sequential adult cohorts with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest managed by basic life support teams from the Paris Fire Brigade. A bidirectional sensor measured insufflated volume (Vi) and expiratory tidal volume (Vt). The display was masked during Period-1 and provided real-time feedback during Period-2. We assessed adherence to the guideline-recommended range using mixed-effects regression; we analyzed Vt and leak volume using gamma log-link generalized linear mixed models. We analyzed 4,300 ventilations in 163 patients, 96 without feedback and 67 with feedback. Median Vi was lower with feedback (471 mL) than without (513 mL, p=0.03 for the first ventilation of each cycle) but median Vt was unchanged (235 vs. 243 mL, p=0.84). Vi dispersion was reduced by 35% (mean within-patient IQR ratio 0.65 [95%-CI, 0.53-0.77]). Vi was 400-600 mL in 68% of ventilations with feedback vs. 42% without feedback. In contrast, Vt was 400-600 mL in only 14% of ventilations with feedback vs. 15% without feedback. In multivariable analysis, leak volume was 12% lower with feedback (mean ratio, 0.88 [95%-CI, 0.77-0.99]). Real-time feedback was associated with improved adherence to the guideline-recommended range for Vi, less dispersed Vi,and lower leak volume. Causal inference, clinical significance, and generalizability warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: Comparison of alveolar macrophages senescence between cigarette smoke-exposed and naturally aged mice and the role of P2X7R in CS-induced airway inflammation.
articles.abstract: Aging is intricately linked to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Alveolar macrophages (AMs) senescence-induced impaired phagocytosis may contribute to persistent airway inflammation in COPD. The P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) is a crucial modulator of cellular senescence. However, its roles in AMs senescence and phagocytosis remain unclear. In this study, naturally aged mice, cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed mice, and MH-S cells stimulated by cigarette smoke extract (CSE) were used to compare the degree of AMs senescence and phagocytosis between CS-exposed and naturally aged mice, and to confirm the function and mechanism of P2X7R. Results showed that pulmonary function gradually declined, AMs senescence increased, and phagocytosis decreased with increasing age. CS-exposed mice exhibited similar levels of AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis as aged mice, but more severe pulmonary dysfunction, histopathological damage, and airway inflammation. P2X7R was elevated in AMs from CS-exposed mice and CSE-treated MH-S cells. Mechanistically, the P2X7R antagonist A438079 reduced ROS levels and p-p38 MAPK, restored SIRT1 expression, and reduced Ac-NF-κB p65, thereby alleviating cellular senescence and impaired phagocytosis in CSE-treated MH-S cells. Tert-butyl hydroperoxide, a ROS inducer, can reverse the protective effects of A438079. In vivo, treatment with A438079 alleviates AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis, and improves pulmonary dysfunction, histopathological damage, and airway inflammation in CS-exposed mice. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that the degree of AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis is similar between CS-exposed and aged mice. Furthermore, CS may induce AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis via the P2X7R-mediated ROS/p38 MAPK/SIRT1/NF-κB pathway, thereby driving airway inflammation.

articles.title: A phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin/oxidized chondroitin sulfate hydrogel with reversible adhesion and self-healing properties for enhanced chronic wound treatment.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds are a major clinical challenge, commonly associated with diabetes, vascular diseases, and prolonged immobilization. Their varying depths and irregular geometries require wound dressings that can conform closely to complex wound surfaces while maintaining reliable adhesion. Although adhesive and dynamic hydrogels have been widely explored for wound management, integrating stable adhesion during application with controllable and gentle on-demand detachment, while retaining self-healing and injectability for irregular chronic wounds, remains challenging. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an adaptive hydrogel dressing capable of conforming to irregular chronic wounds while providing stable adhesion during application and controllable, gentle detachment on demand. To achieve this aim, we developed a temperature-responsive phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin/oxidized chondroitin sulfate (GP-OCS) hydrogel, integrating Schiff base and borate ester bonds formed between phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin and oxidized chondroitin sulfate. The resulting dual dynamic network endowed the hydrogel with favorable mechanical properties, self-healing ability, injectability, and temperature-responsive reversible adhesion, enabling close conformity to irregular wound surfaces and on-demand removal. These findings demonstrate a dual-dynamic-covalent hydrogel strategy that combines conformability, stable adhesion, and temperature-triggered atraumatic removal, providing a promising approach for the development of adaptive wound dressings for chronic wound management.

articles.title: Tele-Based Ischemic Conditioning for Chronic Stroke: Safety, Feasibility, and Preliminary Neurophysiological and Motor Effects.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To examine the safety and feasibility of a two-week (seven-session) tele-based ischemic conditioning (tele-IC) intervention in individuals with chronic stroke and to explore secondary neurophysiological and motor outcomes.

METHODS: Ten individuals with chronic stroke (8 males; age 61.7 ± 7.3 years; time since stroke 11.5 ± 7.5 years; Fugl-Meyer Lower Extremity score 20.5 ± 6.6) completed tele-IC. The primary outcomes were safety and feasibility. Safety was assessed through monitoring of IC-related adverse events and side effects across sessions; feasibility was evaluated through screening-to-enrollment, retention, intervention adherence, tolerability, and acceptability. Secondary exploratory outcomes included corticomotor excitability, transcallosal inhibition, lower-limb strength, paretic ankle motor control, and gait speed. Outcomes were assessed before and 24 hours after the intervention.

RESULTS: Across 70 tele-IC sessions, no serious adverse events occurred, and all 10 participants completed all seven sessions. Acceptability was high, including ratings for safety (4.9/5), remote assistance (4.8/5), and overall satisfaction (4.8/5). Exploratory analyses showed increased transcallosal inhibition (d_z = 0.929, p = 0.017), changes in bilateral lower-limb strength (d_z = 0.873-1.756), and shorter paretic ankle reaction time (d_z = 0.844, p = 0.049). Corticomotor excitability and gait speed did not significantly change.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small, uncontrolled pilot study, synchronously supervised tele-IC was delivered with complete intervention adherence, no serious adverse events, and high participant acceptability. Exploratory secondary neurophysiological and motor findings require confirmation in larger controlled trials.

articles.title: White Matter Hyperintensities of Presumed Vascular Origin: Current Understanding of Development and Progression.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) of presumed vascular origin are among the most common MRI manifestations of cerebral small vessel disease and are a major contributor to vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia. Although WMH have traditionally been attributed to chronic ischemia resulting from small vessel pathology, the biological mechanisms underlying their development and, more importantly, their progression remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in longitudinal neuroimaging, quantitative MRI, pathology, genetics, and physiological imaging have substantially expanded our understanding of WMH progression, making this an appropriate time to evaluate current concepts and synthesize emerging evidence.

OBSERVATIONS: We review contemporary evidence regarding the biological processes implicated in WMH development and progression, including hypertension and vascular risk factors, acute ischemic injury, chronic hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, endothelial activation and vascular inflammation, arterial stiffness, intracranial artery dolichoectasia (IADE), altered cerebral fluid dynamics and genetic susceptibility. Longitudinal studies demonstrate that WMH exhibit dynamic trajectories characterized by progression, stability, and partial regression, indicating that lesion evolution is not uniformly irreversible. Pathological and advanced neuroimaging studies show that WMH represent heterogeneous tissue injury involving demyelination, axonal loss, gliosis, interstitial fluid accumulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Hypertension and blood pressure variability are consistently associated with greater WMH burden and progression, whereas baseline WMH burden is the strongest predictor of future lesion expansion. Acute ischemic lesions detected by diffusion-weighted imaging contribute to, but account for only a minority of WMH progression. Longitudinal studies evaluating cerebral perfusion, BBB permeability, inflammation, arterial stiffness, IADE and cerebral fluid dynamics have yielded variable findings but, together with genetic evidence, support roles of BBB leakage, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, arterial and extracellular-matrix remodeling, and impaired interstitial fluid clearance in WMH progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Emerging evidence supports a paradigm in which WMH are viewed as a dynamic manifestation of progressive neurovascular dysfunction rather than the consequence of chronic ischemia alone. Current data suggest that early neurovascular injury evolves into a potentially self-reinforcing process characterized by persistent BBB disruption, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, altered fluid dynamics, and recurrent ischemic injury, collectively contributes to WMH progression. Future multimodal longitudinal studies integrating cerebral hemodynamics, neurovascular function and intracranial arterial remodeling will be essential to understand WMH progression.

articles.title: Peritoneal dialysis induces hepatic metabolic stress as an instigator for systemic inflammation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a lifesaving therapy in patients with kidney failure, but results in daily intraperitoneal glucose administration corresponding to 50% of the recommended energy intake, most of which enters the portal circulation. As the impact of this glucose exposure on liver and metabolic health remains unclear, we explored hepatic and systemic metabolic effects of PD.

METHODS: Healthy mice and mice with chronic kidney disease (5/6 nephrectomy C57BL/6 aged 12-14 weeks) underwent seven weeks of PD. Combining morphologic studies, untargeted tissue proteomics, targeted plasma metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics, we assessed hepatic molecular and metabolic effects of PD. Gut- and gut-vascular barriers, systemic and hepatic lipopolysaccharide abundance and zonal transcriptional changes were assessed with multiplexed spatial single-cell analysis and transcriptomics.

RESULTS: Intraperitoneally administered glucose during PD was rapidly taken up by the liver and induced hepatic metabolic inflammation. Portal-venous glucose overload bypassing the gastrointestinal tract resulted in increased glucose-to-cholesterol shunting with elevated plasma cholesterol levels, despite the absence of hepatic steatosis or glycogen storage. Increased oxidative stress and endotoxin load were associated with reduced hepatic Kupffer cell numbers without increased gut permeability.

CONCLUSIONS: Ours study found chronic hepatic metabolic stress induced by PD. Evidence of hepatic glucotoxicity and oxidative stress as instigators for systemic metabolic inflammation induced by PD suggests that similar pathologic mechanisms could also contribute to increased cardiometabolic risk on chronic PD.

articles.title: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience medication intolerance and side effects that worsen with lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). This prespecified secondary analysis assessed the safety of semaglutide by baseline eGFR.

METHODS: FLOW (NCT03819153) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing the efficacy of subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once-weekly on a primary kidney outcome (50% or more eGFR reduction, kidney failure, or death due to kidney or cardiovascular causes) in participants with T2D and CKD. Safety data were collected selectively and included serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, and prespecified AEs of special interest (AESIs). In this descriptive assessment, systematically collected safety data were reported numerically by baseline eGFR.

RESULTS: Of 3533 participants, 1767 received semaglutide and 1766 received placebo. Fewer SAEs were reported with semaglutide than placebo across baseline eGFR subgroups (45.1% versus 50.4% in the 60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup, and 56.4% versus 60.4% in the under 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup). SAEs related to infections and infestations; cardiac disorders; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders; and metabolism and nutrition disorders were generally less frequent with semaglutide than placebo, regardless of baseline eGFR. Treatment discontinuations due to AEs were higher with lower baseline eGFR across treatment groups (60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2: semaglutide 11.2%, placebo 11.3%; under30 ml/min per 66 1.73 m2: semaglutide 18.8%, placebo 18.7%). Discontinuations specifically due to gastrointestinal AEs were reported more frequently with semaglutide (4.5%) than placebo (1.1%), regardless of baseline eGFR. Frequencies of AESI were similar between treatment groups across baseline eGFR subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: In this safety assessment, SAEs were reported less frequently with semaglutide than placebo, with corresponding patterns observed for treatment discontinuations and AESIs. No unexpected safety concerns were identified across the spectrum of eGFR represented in the FLOW trial.

articles.title: A study using the REIN registry suggests a statin therapy benefits for secondary prevention in patients receiving dialysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While statins are effective for cardiovascular prevention in the general population, their benefit in patients with CKD G5D (kidney failure treated by dialysis) remains uncertain. Previous randomized controlled trials included mixed populations for primary and secondary prevention while excluding patients with recent cardiovascular events, leaving a knowledge gap regarding statin effectiveness for secondary prevention immediately following an atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event. Here, we address this gap by providing real-world evidence.

METHODS: We conducted a landmark-based observational study, informed by the target trial framework using the French Renal Epidemiology and Information Network (REIN) registry and merged with data from the French national healthcare system database from 2010 to 2023. We included adults with CKD G5D who experienced an ASCVD event. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance baseline characteristics between statin initiators and non-initiators, thereby estimating the average causal effect on all-cause mortality. Results focus on the relative and absolute risk difference and the life expectancy gain using delta restricted mean survival time (dRMST).

RESULTS: The study cohort included 5534 patients (median age: 75 years; 67% male). During the ten years of follow-up, statin use was associated with a reduced risk of mortality. The survival curves reached a maximum absolute difference at year four (risk difference -6.2% (95% CI: -10.2; -2.2); relative risk 0.88 [95% CI: 0.81; 0.96]). Life expectancy extended significantly over time with a mean survival gain of 69 days at five years (95% CI: 14-125) and reaching 135 days at ten years (95% CI: 31-239). No difference was identified between groups regarding hospitalizations for rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients receiving dialysis, statin initiation following an ASCVD event is safe and associated with a modest-to-moderate ten-year cumulative survival benefit. While interpreted within observational limitations, this real-world evidence supports their use in this secondary prevention setting.

articles.title: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study measured hepcidin, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic outcomes in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Abnormal iron homeostasis plays a critical role in extra-hematopoietic disorders. The relationship of hepcidin, the master iron regulator, to clinical outcomes, has not been characterized in a large cohort of chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: To determine if plasma hepcidin level predicts cardiovascular (CV), kidney, and metabolic outcomes in patients with CKD, we studied 3826 patients enrolled in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. Hazard ratios for hepcidin tertiles were estimated from Cox Proportional Hazards regression for primary outcomes of incident heart failure (HF), end stage kidney disease (kidney failure) or halving of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and new onset diabetes or prediabetes. Secondary outcomes included atherosclerotic events and all-cause and CV mortality.

RESULTS: The median and interquartile range of plasma hepcidin level was 43 (22, 77) ng/mL. Higher plasma hepcidin levels were associated with older age, male sex, non-Hispanic Black race, diabetes, lower eGFR, higher albuminuria, increased plasma levels of iron indices, C-terminal fibroblast growth factor 23, and markers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and interleukin-6). We found no association between plasma hepcidin level and the risk for incident HF or prediabetes/diabetes. However, compared to the middle tertile, the highest hepcidin tertile was independently associated with increased risk for kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.19; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.30) and atherosclerotic events (hazard ratio 1.34; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.64), while the lowest hepcidin tertile was associated with increased risk for all-cause and CV mortality in fully adjusted multivariable models including iron indices and inflammation.

CONCLUSION: Both low and high plasma levels of hepcidin are associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Oxidative Stress Potentiates a STAT1-APOL1 Feedforward Loop and Governs Disease Severity in APOL1-Mediated Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) risk variants (G1 and G2) confer immunity against Trypanosoma infection but markedly increase susceptibility to progressive kidney disease. However, only a subset of biallelic risk-variant carriers develops disease progression, distinct from murine models. Here, we evaluated molecular drivers of progressive kidney disease using a model that reflected the low human disease penetrance.
