METHODS: To investigate the heterogeneity of APOL1-mediated kidney disease, we generated novel APOL1 bacterial artificial chromosome transgenic mice with doxycycline-inducible systemic interferon-γ expression (G0- or G1-IFNγ mice). Podocyte-specific transcriptomics using translating ribosome affinity purification (TRAP-seq) and single-cell spatial transcriptomics via 10x Genomics Xenium In Situ platform was performed. Mechanistic validation and analysis of factors regulating APOL1 upregulation were conducted in primary podocytes and subsequently validated in mouse kidney and in human kidney biopsy specimens via immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: A subset of G1-IFNγ mice developed severe albuminuria and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, which strongly correlated with the magnitude of APOL1 upregulation. By pairing TRAP-seq with single-cell spatial transcriptomic data, we identified mitochondrial dysfunction and JAK-STAT signaling as a central mediator of podocyte injury. In primary podocytes, APOL1 risk variants triggered mitochondrial-derived oxidative stress, establishing a self-amplifying STAT1-APOL1 feedforward loop that further enhances APOL1 expression and APOL1 oligomerization. This pathogenic loop was consistently enriched in podocytes from both G1-IFNγ mice and in kidney biopsy specimens from patients with APOL1-mediated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, demonstrating translational relevance.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that biallelic risk variants initiate an oxidative stress-induced positive feedforward loop which promotes and sustains APOL1 upregulation and STAT1 phosphorylation, thereby contributing to disease susceptibility, severity and outcome.

articles.title: Hypertensive Intraventricular Hemorrhage in a Chinese Population: Clinical Characteristics, Treatment, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) is associated with high mortality and poor outcomes in survivors. This study described the clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes of patients with hypertensive IVH (HIVH) in a large single-center Chinese cohort.

METHODS: We conducted retrospective analysis of prospectively maintained stroke registry at a tertiary medical center in China from September 2018 to January 2026. Patients with hypertensive IVH were included, while those with vascular-structural lesions or trauma were excluded. Demographic data, clinical treatments, and outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: In total, 489 patients with HIVH were enrolled, including 49 (9.9%) with primary IVH (pIVH) and 440(90%) with secondary IVH (sIVH). Panventricular hemorrhage was the most common overall HIVH pattern (31%), and 170 patients (35%) received external ventricular drainage (EVD). The overall 30-day mortality rate was 26%, and the 90-day mortality rate was 29%, respectively. Multivariate analysis showed that larger hematoma volume (OR=1.02, p=0.001), lower admission GCS score (OR=1.37, p<0.001), and older age (OR=1.03, p=0.011) were independent risk factors for 90-day mortality in patients with HIVH. Subgroup analysis showed that the EVD group had significantly lower 90-day cumulative mortality risk than the non-EVD group (HR=0.57, 95%CI 0.41-0.79, p<0.001), but no significant difference in favorable functional outcome at 90 days [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2: 22% vs 27%, p=0.265]. Additionally, the EVD group had significantly prolonged hospital stay (21 days vs 13 days, p<0.001). Furthermore, there was no significant difference in 90-day mortality risk between pIVH and sIVH (HR=0.94, 95%CI 0.51-1.75, p=0.848), but pIVH had significantly higher favorable functional outcome rates (mRS 0-2: 65% vs. 21%, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Parenchymal brain injury was the predominant factor associated with prognosis in patients with HIVH. EVD was associated with lower mortality but did not improve functional outcomes.

articles.title: Convergent ferroptosis and pyroptosis in MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects ∼30% of the global population and is associated with increased risks of heart failure (particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction), atrial fibrillation, and cardiovascular mortality. Despite well-established epidemiological links between MASLD and cardiovascular disease, the molecular pathways driving MASLD-related cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. This state-of-the-art mini review examines ferroptosis and pyroptosis as potentially convergent regulated cell-death pathways relevant to both the steatotic liver and the remodeling heart. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven cell death that mediates hepatocyte injury in experimental MASLD and contributes to cardiomyocyte injury under cardiac stress. Pyroptosis is an inflammasome-mediated pro-inflammatory cell death executed by gasdermin D, which amplifies tissue inflammation in hepatic and cardiac disease. Direct preclinical evidence from a pressure-overload heart-failure model demonstrates ferroptosis-to-pyroptosis signaling through the ACSL4/ALOX12/12-HETE/NLRP3 axis; however, this cascade has not yet been directly validated in MASLD models or in patients with MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling. We therefore distinguish experimentally established within-organ mechanisms from hypothesized interorgan liver-heart links, highlight shared regulators including reactive oxygen species, the cGAS/STING pathway, and the NRF2 hub, and discuss translational strategies and evidence gaps that should guide future validation.

articles.title: Veno-arterial ECMO for the management of propofol infusion syndrome following cardiac surgery.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
articles.abstract: Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) has been described in patients requiring prolonged sedation with this drug, as may occur in some cases after cardiac surgery. Its treatment is based on discontinuation of the drug and supportive management of organ dysfunction until resolution. In the postoperative period of cardiac surgery, diagnosing PRIS poses a challenge, since it must be differentiated from other, more common complications such as postcardiotomy shock. In these patients, PRIS may fatally worsen the prognosis. Veno-arterial ECMO therapy may help maintain cardiac output. Both the diagnosis of PRIS after cardiac surgery and its treatment with ECMO have been scarcely reported. We present a case of PRIS after cardiac surgery successfully managed with ECMO.

articles.title: Shock Index-Creatinine as a Predictor of In-Hospital Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Anterior Wall ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early risk stratification in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is essential but established scores such as TIMI and GRACE require multivariable computation. The Shock Index-Creatinine (SIC) is a simpler bedside alternative, yet Indian data are sparse.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether admission SIC predicts in-hospital adverse events in anterior wall STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHODS: Two hundred consecutive patients with anterior wall STEMI undergoing primary PCI at a tertiary care centre in northern India were prospectively enrolled over 12 months. SIC was computed at admission as (Shock Index × 100) - Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. The primary outcome was in-hospital death; secondary outcomes were heart failure, cardiogenic shock, contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CI-AKI), and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: The cohort was 73.0% male with a mean age of 54.5 years; in-hospital mortality was 10.0% (n = 20). Admission SIC was markedly higher in non-survivors than survivors (82.0 ± 42.4 versus -20.1 ± 19.4; p < 0.001). AUCs were 0.992 for mortality and cardiogenic shock, 0.971 for CI-AKI, 0.909 for ventricular arrhythmia, and 0.907 for heart failure (all p < 0.001). A SIC ≥ 20 predicted death with 95.0% sensitivity and 98.9% specificity.

CONCLUSIONS: In this Indian cohort, admission SIC was a powerful bedside predictor of adverse in-hospital events after primary PCI for anterior wall STEMI. The unusually high discriminative performance requires external validation in larger multicentre populations before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Serum aflatoxin-albumin adduct profiling and exposure predictors among gastroenterology patients of tertiary hospitals in southwestern Nigeria.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: Aflatoxin, a potent hepatocarcinogenic mycotoxin, remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. Due to its severe health and socio-economic impact, aflatoxin exposure needs to be monitored and mitigated. This cross-sectional study assessed serum aflatoxin-albumin adducts (AF-ALB), an objective biomarker of systemic aflatoxin exposure, among gastroenterology patients in southwestern Nigeria using ELISA. AF-ALB levels were categorized into high and low groups based on interquartile ranges. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify socio-demographic, dietary, and temporal predictors. Of the 573 participants, 405 (70.7%) were male, and 168 (29.3%) were female. Overall median AF-ALB concentration was 3.5 pg/mL. Daily groundnut consumption showed the strongest dietary association (aOR = 9.7, 95% CI: 4.3-21.9, p < 0.001), while the sampling period was also significantly associated with AF-ALB levels (p < 0.001). The association between urban residence and high AF-ALB levels was model-dependent rather than a true independent association. AF-ALB median levels varied significantly across gastroenteric diseases (p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.478). Age, sex, education, occupation, marital status, and aflatoxin awareness status were not significantly associated with AF-ALB levels. These findings indicate that dietary practices, particularly frequent groundnut consumption, are important predictors of aflatoxin exposure in this population.

articles.title: Urinary Metabolites in Tryptophan-Kynurenine Pathway and Risk of CKD Progression in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Tryptophan-kynurenine pathway is integral for energy metabolism and immune-inflammation regulation. We sought to study the associations between urinary metabolites in tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in patients with type 2 diabetes.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 1,892 participants with type 2 diabetes from Southeast Asia were included in the primary analysis; 951 Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) participants with diabetes at baseline were included in the validation study.

EXPOSURES: Urinary tryptophan, kynurenine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, kynurenic acid, xanthurenic acid and kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio (KTR).

OUTCOMES: CKD progression defined as a composite of incident end stage kidney disease (sustained eGFR < 15 ml/min/1.73m2, maintenance dialysis, renal death) or doubling of serum creatinine concentration.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cause-specific hazard regression.

RESULTS: A total of 224 CKD progression events were identified over a median follow-up of 7.2 years. Each one SD increase in the concentration of urinary kynurenine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, kynurenic acid, and KTR was associated with 1.60 [95% CI 1.16-2.22], 1.64 [1.17-2.31], 1.47 [1.10-1.97] and 1.97 [1.43-2.71] fold higher risk of CKD progression, respectively, after adjustment for known clinical risk factors. These associations were more pronounced in participants with prevalent CKD (eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73m2) compared to those with preserved eGFR. Each one SD increase in urinary tryptophan and kynurenine concentrations was independently associated with 1.60 [1.24-2.06] and 1.35 [1.05-1.73] fold higher risk of CKD progression, respectively, in CRIC participants with diabetes.

LIMITATIONS: Observational study with unmeasured confounding.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher concentrations of urinary metabolites in the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway were associated with higher risk of CKD progression in patients with type 2 diabetes. Future studies are warranted to elucidate the biological mechanisms linking the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and progression of kidney disease.

articles.title: Reliability of Spot Urine Protein-to-Creatinine and Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratios in Acute Kidney Injury: A Cohort Study.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Spot urine protein-to-creatinine (UPCR) and albumin-to-creatinine (UACR) ratios are common surrogates for 24-hour excretion, but their validity during acute kidney injury (AKI) is uncertain because kidney function is not at steady state. This study assessed the validity of these spot ratios during active AKI compared to after its resolution.

STUDY DESIGN: A prospective paired cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: One hundred hospitalized adult patients with AKI at a single center in Thailand.

EXPOSURE: Active phase of AKI was the period between diagnosis and resolution, which was defined as the return of serum creatinine to baseline or a value ≥50% below the peak value, sustained for ≥48 hours.

OUTCOMES: The agreement and reliability between protein-to-creatine and albumin-to-creatinine ratios in spot urine samples versus in 24-hour urine collections.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Agreement was evaluated using Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis to quantify systematic bias and random error. Limits of Agreement (LoA) were defined as the range within which 95% of the differences between the two measurement methods were expected to fall.

RESULTS: Spot ratios differed from 24-hour collections during AKI (CCC: UACR 0.81; UPCR 0.68) and became more reliable after recovery, (CCC: UACR 0.89; UPCR 0.83) (p=0.001). Limits of agreement were wide during AKI (UACR 0.22 to 8.37; UPCR 0.31 to 7.99) and narrowed significantly upon resolution (UACR 0.40 to 5.48; UPCR 0.47 to 4.91). Spot ratios systematically overestimated the 24-hour collections by 36% to 56% both during and after resolution of AKI. The unreliability of the spot urine values was most pronounced in patients with preserved baseline kidney function, severe AKI, and hemodynamic etiologies.

LIMITATIONS: Defining resolution via serum creatinine may not reflect complete resolution of AKI. The exclusively hospitalized cohort may limit generalizability to milder AKI occurring in the outpatient setting.

CONCLUSIONS: Spot urine ratios exhibit significant imprecision during active AKI compared to following its resolution. Clinicians should exercise caution when using these data to establish baseline proteinuria or monitor treatment response during AKI.

articles.title: Beyond the airways: expiratory pulmonary vascular retention and reduced compressibility in asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

articles.title: IFN-γ-NOD2/IL-5-FCGR axis enhances eosinophil extracellular trap formation in allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis/mycosis.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis/mycosis (ABPA/M) is characterized by systemic eosinophilia and eosinophil-rich mucus plugs, but mechanisms programming eosinophil pathogenicity remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We aim to define eosinophil activation programs and upstream signals that promote extracellular trap formation in ABPA/M.

METHODS: We performed multi-omics analyses (RNA sequencing and proteomics) of blood eosinophils from healthy participants, patients with eosinophilic asthma, and patients with ABPA/M. Surface-marker profiles were compared between blood and airway eosinophils from patients with ABPA/M. In vitro stimulation assays using IFN-γ, IL-5, and a nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing 2 (NOD2) ligand were combined with multi-omics readouts and functional evaluation of IgG cross-linking-induced eosinophil extracellular trap formation.

RESULTS: Multi-omics profiling identified activation patterns consistent with IFN-γ and IL-5 signaling in ABPA/M blood eosinophils. ICAM-1 was upregulated on both blood and airway eosinophils, whereas PD-L1 upregulation was specific to airway eosinophils. PD-L1 induction required combined stimulation with IFN-γ and a NOD2 ligand, but not IL-5. Under IFN-γ plus NOD2 ligand stimulation, eosinophils exhibited inflammatory remodeling, including increased Fc gamma receptor expression. Functionally, pretreatment with IFN-γ and a NOD2 ligand enhanced IgG cross-linking-induced extracellular trap formation in an NADPH oxidase-dependent manner and required lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 interactions with ICAM-1. Combined stimulation with IFN-γ and IL-5 similarly augmented extracellular trap formation.

CONCLUSION: ABPA/M eosinophils are shaped by mixed inflammatory cues, in which IFN-γ cooperates with fungal-sensing signals or IL-5 to enhance Fc gamma receptor-linked, IgG-triggered extracellular trap formation, potentially contributing to mucus plugging.

articles.title: Systemic oxidative stress in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder and oxidative stress (OS) is believed to play a role in disease pathogenesis. However, reliable OS markers are lacking. In this study we aim to assess OS in AD by evaluating free thiols, which serve as key indicators of the systemic redox status.

METHODS: SCD (subjective cognitive decline), MCI (mild cognitive impairment), AD, and other dementias (Non-AD) were recruited. Comorbidity data were collected and free thiols were measured in plasma. Additionally, phosphorylated-Tau (pTau217), amyloid-beta ratio (Aβ42/40), Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light (NfL) levels were used to investigate correlation with free thiols. Further, associations between free thiols and disease severity in AD were calculated.

RESULTS: Three hundred and ten patients were included (SCD 109, MCI 51, AD 125, Non-AD 25). Free thiols were significantly lower in AD compared to SCD and MCI (p<0.01). Free thiols correlated negatively with pTau217, NfL and GFAP, also within AD (p<0.01 for all). Additionally, free thiols significantly negatively correlated with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) scores (N=210, p<0.001). Multiple linear regression showed that type 2 diabetes and age were significant predictors for free thiols (B=1.01, β=0.266, p<0.001; B=-0.040, β=-0.273, p<0.001, respectively). After adjusting for these covariates, free thiols remained significantly lower in AD compared to SCD (p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: Increased systemic OS, reflected by lower free thiols, is observed in plasma of AD patients, supporting a key role for OS in AD-pathophysiology and highlighting free thiols as potential therapeutic targets and possibly complementary biomarkers for clinical diagnostics.

articles.title: Selective NRF2 target induction despite falling NFE2L2 transcription across the MASLD spectrum: implications for marginal donor grafts and KEAP1-targeted therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects one-third of adults, and one in five progresses to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), which can cause liver failure, burdening hepatology clinics and transplant waiting lists. NRF2-KEAP1 axis is the principal regulator of hepatic antioxidant defence, yet its status across the disease spectrum is unclear. We mapped NRF2-KEAP1 transcriptional signatures across control, steatosis and MASH livers.

METHODS: Eight GEO datasets (590 biopsies: 154 control, 134 steatosis, 302 MASH) were harmonised by log2 transformation, within-dataset Z-scoring and ComBat correction. The pre-specified panel comprised NFE2L2, KEAP1 and six NRF2 targets (GCLC, GCLM, HMOX1, NQO1, SRXN1, TXNRD1). Groups were compared by ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc tests.

RESULTS: NFE2L2 was highest in control and reduced in steatotic and MASH livers (both p < 0.001), with KEAP1 reciprocally elevated. Targets were induced selectively where NQO1 and TXNRD1 peaked in MASH while HMOX1 was highest in control. NFE2L2-to-target co-expression was preserved across stages. Across fibrosis stages, NFE2L2 and KEAP1 were unchanged while NQO1 and TXNRD1 rose. Thus NQO1 and TXNRD1 rise in MASH even as NFE2L2 transcription falls.

CONCLUSIONS: NFE2L2 transcription decreases once MASLD is established, yet its targets are induced selectively and co-expression is preserved, so the pathway stays coherent while its output shifts. These are mRNA findings. We propose control of NRF2 at the protein level as a hypothesis consistent with our data and the pattern supports assessing NRF2 protein status in marginal donor livers and therapies targeting KEAP1.

articles.title: Diaphragm ultrasound-guided PEEP titration in COPD with dynamic hyperinflation.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by airflow limitation, dynamic hyperinflation, and intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure (iPEEP), which increase inspiratory threshold load and complicate ventilatory support. Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is the preferred initial ventilatory support for COPD exacerbations complicated by acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis, while invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) may be required when NIV fails. External PEEP may reduce the inspiratory threshold load in patients with expiratory flow limitation, although excessive levels can increase lung volume and compromise hemodynamics. During IMV, PEEP adjustment requires assessment of respiratory mechanics, expiratory flow, hyperinflation, and cardiovascular tolerance. During NIV, where iPEEP cannot usually be measured directly, expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) should be adjusted according to clinical response, patient-ventilator interaction, and signs of excessive lung inflation. Inappropriate ventilatory assistance may also contribute to diaphragm dysfunction. Diaphragm ultrasound allows bedside assessment of muscle thickness and inspiratory thickening fraction (DTF), although these measurements are influenced by ventilatory assistance, respiratory drive, and lung volume. This review examines the physiological basis, available evidence, and limitations of using diaphragm ultrasound to complement PEEP adjustment in patients with COPD and dynamic hyperinflation. No DTF target or clinical benefit of ultrasound-guided PEEP titration has been established in this population.

articles.title: Physical Activity Support in Diabetes Care: A Narrative Review of Practice Gaps and the Role of Qualified Exercise Professionals in Canada and the United States.
Characteristics, risk factors, and vascular outcomes of diabetic kidney disease with type 2 diabetes: Analysis of data from clinic-based patient registry (J-DOME) in Japan.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) encompasses patients with an atypical clinical course, where GFR declines precedes albuminuria. This study investigated the characteristics, risk factors, and vascular outcomes of DKD subgroups among 2,733 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: Using data from a Japan-wide patients registry (J-DOME), we classified patients by albuminuria and eGFR, analyzed annual trends in eGFR and evaluated the incidence of new vascular complications.

RESULTS: The prevalence of DKD was 45%, one-third of whom had low eGFR/normoalbuminuria. Although the low eGFR/normoalbuminuria group showed similar glycemic control to the no DKD group, the albuminuria/normal eGFR group had poorer control of lifestyle-related risk factors. Both DKD subgroups had a higher prevalence of microvascular and macrovascular disorders at baseline. During a mean follow-up of 2.5 years, compared with the no DKD group, the low eGFR/normoalbuminuria group showed a slower rate of renal function decline, while the albuminuria/normal eGFR group exhibited a faster rate of renal function decline. In contrast, the incidence of vascular diseases did not differ between either DKD subgroup and the no DKD group.

CONCLUSIONS: The albuminuria/normal eGFR group exhibited accelerated renal function decline compared with the no DKD group, highlighting albuminuria as a marker of active renal injury in type 2 diabetes. In contrast, the low eGFR/normoalbuminuria group showed short-term renal stability despite a high baseline prevalence of vascular complications, representing a distinct clinical phenotype.

articles.title: Ready, Set, Go? A Qualitative Case Study Exploring Implementation Readiness of a Type 2 Diabetes Remission Program in a Primary Care Setting Using a Scalability Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) treatment is increasingly viewed through a remission lens, reflecting a shift from chronic management to disease regression. This study examined pre-implementation conditions, including barriers and facilitators, to adopt, implement, and scale a T2D remission program in primary care using a scalability assessment.

METHODS: Using the Intervention Scalability Assessment Tool (ISAT), a descriptive qualitative case study was conducted and included semi-structured interviews with a purposeful sample of 11 multidisciplinary professionals within one Ontario (Canada) Family Health Team (FHT) (January-March 2025). Framework analysis was used to code, categorize and develop overarching themes related to scale-up elements and how to optimize program delivery and acceptance.

RESULTS: The thematic analysis generated 3 themes, outlining the primary conditions perceived to be needed for successful implementation and scale-up: (1) Effectively conceptualizing and positioning a health coach within primary care; (2) Site readiness to adopt T2D remission implementation; and (3) Perceived opportunities for fostering positive health outcomes. Participants supported integrating a T2D remission program into the existing FHT, citing broad benefits. Participants unanimously agreed that there was a strong demand for such a program, both from individuals living with T2D and healthcare providers, and was well-warranted in comparison to the lengthy treatments that can be accrued throughout a diagnosis of T2D.

DISCUSSION: Using a single site FHT to understand the potential to scale-up, a T2D remission program in primary care was acceptable and feasible if context-specific barriers and facilitators are addressed, with strategic planning around role integration, capacity, and sustained patient engagement.

articles.title: Ovariectomy abolishes cardioprotection against diastolic dysfunction and impairs cardiac glucose oxidation in female mice with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) increases the risk for diabetic cardiomyopathy (DbCM), which is often characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Pre-menopausal women have a reduced incidence of both T2D and DbCM, but this disappears following menopause. Our goal was to evaluate the potential role for ovarian hormones in mediating these differences. The effect of ovariectomy (OVX) was investigated in female mice with experimental T2D following high-fat diet feeding for 12-weeks in combination with a low-dose treatment of streptozotocin at week 4. Body weight and body composition, glucose homeostasis, cardiac structure/function via ultrasound echocardiography, and myocardial substrate metabolism via isolated working heart perfusions were assessed. Sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited increases in body weight and fat mass, as well as impaired glucose homeostasis, though these parameters were more prominent in OVX than sham females when compared to their lean counterparts. However, only OVX female mice with T2D developed diastolic dysfunction as reflected by a significant decrease in the mitral E/A and tissue Doppler e'/a' ratios, as well as an increase in the E/e' ratio. Isolated working hearts from both sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited a reduction in glucose oxidation, though this was more pronounced in the latter. Lastly, only OVX female mice with T2D demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Our data illustrate key roles for ovarian hormones in impacting how T2D impacts the progression of DbCM in females, which may have relevance to women living with T2D as they transition to menopause.

articles.title: One protein, many faces: TRAF1 from signaling hub to disease diversity.
articles.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 1 (TRAF1) is a unique member of the TRAF family, distinguished by its lack of an N-terminal RING domain. At the transcriptional level, TRAF1 expression is regulated by diverse mechanisms, including methylation, RNA-binding domain (RBD) proteins, and microRNAs. Post-translationally, TRAF1 undergoes modifications such as M1-linked ubiquitination and phosphorylation. In immune signaling pathways, TRAF1 usually displays functional duality: it activates the canonical NF-κB pathway by enhancing cIAP recruitment downstream of TNFR1, whereas at death domain-lacking TNFR superfamily members (NDDTNFRs), it drives the non-canonical NF-κB pathway through TRAF3 degradation. Conversely, TRAF1 often acts as a negative regulator in Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling. Within the MAPK pathway, TRAF1 participates in modulating multiple cascades, including ASK1/B-Raf(BRAF)/ERK1. In immune-mediated diseases, TRAF1 contributes to disease pathogenesis by regulating inflammatory cytokines, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) expression, synovial cell apoptosis and tissue destruction. In infectious diseases, the anti-apoptotic effect of TRAF1 downstream of the 4-1BB signaling pathway serves as a host strategy to combat viral infections by preserving CD8+ T cell survival. However, Helicobacter pylori exploits TRAF1 upregulation to inhibit apoptosis in gastric epithelial cells, facilitating its persistent colonization. This contrast highlights TRAF1's functional diversity across infections. This review summarizes the post-translational regulation of TRAF1, its dual roles in signaling pathways, and its contributions to immune-related and infectious diseases, aiming to clarify its mechanistic complexity within the existing biological framework.

articles.title: Homocysteine and related B-vitamins throughout our International Conferences: a historical perspective.
articles.abstract: In this invited keynote review, I reflect on biochemical, clinical, and epidemiological evidence on the role of folate and vitamin B12 in one-carbon metabolism and their relationship with homocysteine, integrating over five decades of research. One-carbon metabolism represents a central biochemical network linking folate-dependent one-carbon transfer reactions with vitamin B12-dependent remethylation of homocysteine to methionine. Disruptions in this pathway result in elevated homocysteine concentrations and impaired methylation capacity, providing a mechanistic link between micronutrient status and chronic disease. Early work demonstrated that folate is a major determinant of plasma homocysteine levels, supporting folic acid fortification policies that significantly reduced neural tube defects worldwide. Research in my laboratory in older adults shifted the paradigm of deficiency from inadequate intake to impaired bioavailability. Elevated homocysteine has been associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke, and cognitive decline, although intervention trials have yielded mixed results, suggesting that homocysteine is best interpreted as a marker of metabolic dysfunction, but when elevated, a potential target for mitigating cognitive decline. Recent advances in epigenetics and gene-nutrient interactions have expanded the relevance of one-carbon metabolism, highlighting its role in DNA methylation and gene regulation. Future research in precision nutrition may refine strategies for preventing chronic disease and promoting healthy aging.

articles.title: Divergent Effects of Trichomonas vaginalis on Cervical Cancer Cells HPV-positive and HPV-negative: Interplay with Purinergic Signaling.
articles.abstract: Trichomonas vaginalis is the protozoan that causes trichomoniasis, the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection in the world. Recently, studies have highlighted the possible association between T. vaginalis and the development of cervical cancer, as well as co-infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), suggesting a role of the protozoan in oncogenesis. In the cervical cancer context, the purinergic signaling influences immunosuppression and angiogenesis, while high concentrations of adenosine can induce cell death. T. vaginalis uptakes adenosine for survival as well it takes advantage in its immunomodulatory effects. Thus, the presence of T. vaginalis could influence cell survival, modulating the tumor microenvironment. Our study demonstrated that, in ex vivo models, T. vaginalis increased cell proliferation, immune infiltrate, and vascularization. Meanwhile, in in vitro 2D cell culture models, T. vaginalis combined with purinergic signaling differentially affects the viability of HPV-positive (SiHa) and HPV-negative (C33A) cervical cancer cell lines, with significant impact in the cell line without HPV. The ATP and adenosine signaling did not affect the cytotoxicity exerted by conditioned medium against both cell lines. T. vaginalis reduced the IL-6 production and E6 oncogene expression by SiHa cells. the Ki-67 gene expression was modulated by the parasite and ATP/adenosine metabolism, highlighting the plasticity of the purinergic signaling combined with the parasite. These findings indicate that T. vaginalis exerts cytotoxicity and modulation of pathways relevant to the tumor microenvironment, influencing cell death, inflammation, and tissue remodeling processes, and shed light to further studies on the interactions between T. vaginalis and host cells.

articles.title: Decoding autoimmune diseases through the adaptive immune receptor repertoires.
articles.abstract: The adaptive immune receptor repertoire (AIRR), composed of T-cell receptors (TCRs) and B-cell receptors (BCRs), underpins antigen-specific immunity through extensive diversity generated by V(D)J recombination and junctional modification. Advances in high-throughput AIRR sequencing have enabled comprehensive characterization of clonal diversity, gene usage patterns, and antigen-driven selection at unprecedented resolution. In autoimmune diseases, breakdown of immune tolerance permits the persistence and expansion of autoreactive lymphocyte clones, and is associated with characteristic repertoire remodeling. Reported alterations include changes in repertoire diversity, oligoclonal expansion, biased V(D)J gene usage, and convergent CDR3 motifs. Notably, repertoire changes exhibit spatial and temporal heterogeneity across peripheral blood and target tissues, highlighting the compartmentalized nature of adaptive immune responses. This review synthesizes current evidence on TCR and BCR repertoire alterations across major autoimmune diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren's disease, type 1 diabetes, and ankylosing spondylitis. We summarize emerging computational frameworks for AIRR analysis and highlight machine learning approaches for clonotype classification and antigen specificity prediction. Furthermore, we discuss the diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications of AIRR profiling, particularly the potential for identifying disease-associated clonotypes and guiding antigen-specific immunotherapies. Despite ongoing technical and biological challenges, continued advances in sequencing technologies and computational modeling are strengthening the role of AIRR analysis as a valuable framework for elucidating autoimmune pathogenesis and advancing precision immunology.

articles.title: Beyond the pelvis: redefining endometriosis as a systemic inflammatory disorder. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis has traditionally been defined as a disease localized to the pelvis. However, its clinical presentation is often accompanied by systemic comorbidities that extend far beyond the pelvic cavity, a phenomenon that challenges the traditional disease paradigm.

OBJECTIVE AND RATIONALE: This study aimed to comprehensively assess the associations between endometriosis and autoimmune diseases, allergic conditions, chronic pain syndromes, and endocrine disorders through a systematic review and meta-analysis, thereby providing evidence for redefining endometriosis as a systemic immuno-inflammatory disorder.

SEARCH METHODS: To conduct this study, a comprehensive search strategy was employed to identify relevant published studies. Electronic databases, including Web of Science and Medline, were searched from their inception up to December 31, 2025. We additionally examined the reference lists of all identified papers to capture any additional articles that were not identified through the electronic database searches. Eligible studies were observational in design (cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional) and reported quantitative data on the association between endometriosis and predefined comorbidities in women. Exclusion criteria included non-human studies, non-English publications, secondary literature types (e.g., reviews, case reports), and studies lacking sufficient data for effect size calculation. Quality assessment was conducted based on the GRADE criteria.

OUTCOMES: The final analysis included 55 studies that met the predefined inclusion criteria and were incorporated into the comprehensive analysis. Of these, 48 studies provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis). Specifically, 32 studies investigated the association between endometriosis and autoimmune diseases: 14 on systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), 8 on Sjögren's syndrome (SS), 10 on rheumatoid arthritis (RA), 5 on multiple sclerosis (MS), 5 on celiac disease (CLD), and 4 on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Additionally, 17 studies examined associations with allergic diseases, 13 focused on pain syndromes, and 6 explored associations with endocrine disorders. Meta-analysis showed that women with endometriosis had a significantly higher risk of certain autoimmune diseases in cohort studies, including SLE (RR: 1.81, 95% CI: 1.50-2.18), SS (RR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.40-1.71), and RA (RR: 1.71, 95% CI: 1.40-2.09), as well as significantly higher odds in case-control and cross-sectional studies for SLE (OR: 3.93, 95% CI: 2.59-5.98), SS (OR: 3.13, 95% CI: 1.10-8.90), RA (OR: 2.27, 95% CI: 1.75-2.95), MS (OR: 2.30, 95% CI: 1.57-3.37), CLD (OR: 4.50, 95% CI: 1.94-10.42), and IBD (OR: 2.82, 95% CI: 0.58-13.61). Significant associations were also observed for allergic conditions-such as asthma (RR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.14-1.40) and eczema (OR: 1.58, 95% CI: 1.34-1.87)-and for pain syndromes including fibromyalgia (RR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.42-1.92), chronic fatigue syndrome (RR: 1.41, 95% CI: 1.31-1.51), and irritable bowel syndrome (RR: 2.51, 95% CI: 1.55-4.07; OR: 3.49, 95% CI: 3.21-3.80). In contrast, no statistically significant increase was observed in the odds of endocrine disorders such as hypothyroidism (OR: 1.89, 95% CI: 0.61-5.90) and hyperthyroidism (OR: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.60-1.52) among women with endometriosis compared with women without endometriosis. However, the overall quality of evidence was generally low or very low according to the GRADE approach, largely due to a high risk of bias in most of the included study designs and statistical analyses.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS: The body of evidence provided by this study supports the reconceptualization of endometriosis as a systemic immuno-inflammatory disease. The associations with various comorbidities are underpinned by shared mechanisms of immune dysregulation and central sensitization. This paradigm shift necessitates a move in clinical practice from a purely gynecological intervention model toward a patient-centered, comprehensive multidisciplinary management approach. It also provides a theoretical foundation for developing novel treatment strategies targeting shared pathological pathways.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Isavuconazole.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Isavuconazole (ISCZ) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for invasive fungal infections (IFIs); however, evidence supporting its prophylactic use remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of ISCZ prophylaxis in patients with hematological malignancies at high risk for IFIs.

METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients at high risk for IFI who received ISCZ as prophylaxis at our institution from June 2023 to June 2025. The primary outcome measure was the incidence of breakthrough IFI (bIFI) within 100 days after ISCZ initiation. The secondary outcome measures were the treatment continuation rate, mortality rate, adverse events, and changes in liver and kidney function.

RESULTS: Overall, 38 patients (median age, 67 years; median body weight, 54.1 kg) were evaluated. Most patients (97.4%) were treated in the hematology-oncology department. The median duration of ISCZ administration was 119 days. Treatment continuation/completion was achieved in 44.7% of the patients. No deaths attributable to IFI were observed during the study period. No breakthrough IFIs were identified within 100 days after ISCZ initiation, and no Grade ≥3 adverse events were definitively attributed to ISCZ.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, no breakthrough IFIs occurred within 100 days after ISCZ prophylaxis initiation. Although Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred, their causal relationship with ISCZ could not be definitively established in this retrospective study. These findings provide real-world data on ISCZ prophylaxis in patients at high risk for IFIs. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is needed.

articles.title: Appropriate administration of tazobactam/piperacillin for urinary and genital tract infections based on antibiotic susceptibility testing: a single-center retrospective analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tazobactam/piperacillin (TAZ/PIPC) is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent. However, improper administration may contribute to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The objectives of this study were to evaluate the appropriateness of TAZ/PIPC administration for UGTI based on antibiotic susceptibility testing and to elucidate the patients for whom alternative antibiotics can be utilized as the initial empiric therapy.

METHODS: Patients diagnosed with UGTI at the University of Toyama Hospital between January 2022 and December 2024 who received TAZ/PIPC as initial empirical therapy were analyzed retrospectively. The appropriateness of alternative agents was determined by assessing bacterial culture and antimicrobial susceptibility results.

RESULTS: Sixty-two UGTI episodes were analyzed. TAZ/PIPC utilization appeared appropriate in 91.9% of cases. Enterococcus faecalis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa were isolated more frequently in UGTI with devices or ileal urinary diversions compared to UGTI without devices. For patients with ileal urinary diversions or devices, the differences in the appropriateness rates of TAZ/PIPC versus CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC were higher than those for patients without devices. In patients without devices, the appropriateness rates of TAZ/PIPC, CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC were 96.7% (29/30), 86.7% (26/30), 83.3% (25/30), and 80.0% (24/30), respectively. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that only the presence of an ileal urinary diversion, a urethral catheter, or a ureteral stent was a risk factor for the inappropriateness (p < 0.05) for CFPM, CTRX, and SBT/ABPC.

CONCLUSION: Based on antibiotic susceptibility testing, TAZ/PIPC may be considered for UGTI using devices or ileal urinary diversions. However, alternative antibiotics may be considered for UGTIs without indwelling devices.

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Pertussis in Hainan Province, 2023-2025.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of pertussis in Hainan Province from 2023 to 2025, describe the outbreak trajectory and patterns of population susceptibility, and provide evidence for optimizing pertussis prevention and control strategies.

METHODS: Clinically diagnosed and confirmed pertussis cases reported in Hainan Province between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the China Information System for Disease Control and Prevention; suspected cases were excluded, yielding a total of 2,927 eligible cases.Descriptive epidemiological methods were used to analyze the temporal, geographic, and population distributions of the cases; piecewise linear regression was employed to characterize monthly trends in case counts; and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify risk factors for hospitalization.

RESULTS: The incidence of pertussis in Hainan Province exhibited an outbreak-and-decline pattern from 2023 to 2025, increasing from 4.29 per 100,000 population in 2023 to 22.26 per 100,000 in 2024 before declining to 1.37 per 100,000 in 2025, with a statistically significant difference across the three years (χ2 = 2,888.2, P < 0.001).Piecewise linear regression showed that the monthly number of cases increased significantly during the ascending phase (β = 21.82, P < 0.001) and decreased significantly during the descending phase (β = -11.41, P < 0.001).The age distribution shifted significantly toward older children: the proportion of infants aged <1 year decreased from 43.1% to 27.3%, whereas that of individuals aged ≥1 year increased from 56.9% to 72.7%.Among cases with complete severity records after July 2024, infants aged 0-2 months had the highest risk of hospitalization and accounted for 90.0% of intensive care unit admissions.

CONCLUSION: This study shows that the 2024 pertussis outbreak in Hainan was followed by a rapid decline in 2025, with a shift toward older children and a persistently high hospitalization risk in infants aged 0-2 months. These findings support strengthening surveillance in schools and childcare institutions and evaluating the effectiveness of the 6-year DTaP booster policy, while maintaining maternal and infant protection strategies.

articles.title: Epidemiological comparison of cirrhosis to other long-term health conditions in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although cirrhosis is a serious long-term health condition (LTC), it tends to receive little attention from healthcare policymakers. Here, we sought to describe how cirrhosis compares to other LTCs to inform priority-setting discussions.

METHODS: We analysed data from the Our Future Health (OFH) study, a cohort of ∼1.7 million individuals from England, United Kingdom. Self-reported diagnosis status for cirrhosis and 15 benchmark LTCs (including type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, Parkinson's disease, chronic kidney disease, schizophrenia, and stage 4 cancer) were ascertained from the enrolment questionnaire. Each LTC was profiled with respect to: sociodemographic characteristics; mortality; comorbidity burden; and late diagnosis. Furthermore, information on each LTC's trajectory (i.e., increasing, stable, or decreasing over time) was determined from background mortality data over the last decade.

RESULTS: The study cohort included 1,613,777 participants, of whom 2,606 (0.2%) reported a diagnosis of cirrhosis. Mortality elevation for participants with cirrhosis versus without was substantial (HR: 7.46; P<0.001, with adjustment for age/sex) and comparable to dementia (HR:7.60), stage 4 cancer (HR:7.06), whilst higher than schizophrenia (HR:4.46) and heart failure (HR:4.01). People with cirrhosis had more co-existing health conditions/diseases than other LTCs (i.e., elevated prevalence for 58/145 distinct health conditions; second only to stage 4 cancer). Area-based deprivation score was third highest for cirrhosis, behind COPD and schizophrenia. Late diagnosis of cirrhosis was commonplace, with <15% of new-onset liver failure reporting cirrhosis at enrolment. Cirrhosis also exhibited an upward trajectory, with mortality increasing by ∼20% in the last decade.

CONCLUSION: Cirrhosis is an anomaly LTC with respect to its deprivation, comorbidity, mortality, upward trajectory, and late diagnosis profile. Our data provide comparative evidence to inform priority-setting discussions with policymakers.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Various levers are available to policy makers for reducing incidence of liver cirrhosis. However, other health conditions are often prioritised by policy makers ahead of cirrhosis; the decision-making process around this is not always transparent nor grounded in evidence. This study explores the characteristics of cirrhosis relative to other long-term conditions through a public-health lens. Our findings may guide priority-setting discussions between policy makers, advocates and other stakeholders and may shift current discourse onto a more empirical footing.

articles.title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
articles.journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions.

RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced.

CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

articles.title: Myocardial Infarction Within 6 Months before Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Strongly Associated with Postoperative Complications.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) is increasing in volume, limited data exist regarding how recent myocardial infarction (MI) influences postoperative outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of MI timing, type, treatment, and anatomical location on rates of postoperative cardiac, medical, and surgical complications following TSA.

METHODS: A national insurance database, PearlDiver, was queried to identify patients with a history of MI within two years prior to TSA. These patients were propensity-matched 1:4 to controls without prior MI based on demographics and comorbidities. The MI cohort was stratified by timing (0-6 months, 6-12 months, 12-18 months, 18-24 months), and subgroup analyses were performed by MI type (Type 1 vs. Type 2), ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) vs Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) classification, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), and infarct location.

RESULTS: A history of MI within 2 years preceding TSA had a strong association with higher odds of postoperative MI (OR 5.67; 95% CI, 3.86-8.32). The strongest association was observed when MI occurred within 6 months of TSA (OR 9.95; 95% CI, 6.50-15.24). Type 1 MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI, particularly within 6 months (OR 10.86; 95% CI, 6.96-16.95). Type 2 MI within 6 months was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 10.69; 95% CI, 2.50-45.63), DVT (OR 9.81; 95% CI, 2.30-41.79), and PJI (OR 5.24; 95% CI, 1.60-17.18). Both STEMI (OR = 6.17) and NSTEMI (OR = 5.77) were strongly associated with postoperative MI. Anterior MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 7.22; 95% CI, 3.36-15.49), whereas inferior MI was strongly associated with 90-day mortality (OR 6.46; 95% CI, 1.85-22.60).

CONCLUSION: MI within 2 years and specifically 6 months of TSA was associated with higher odds of postoperative complications. MI timing, subtype, treatment, and location should be carefully weighed when considering TSA in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Mechanistic basis for the selective recognition of the Fcγ receptor IIa by monoclonal antibody IV.3.
articles.abstract: The monoclonal antibody IV.3 selectively binds the platelet Fcγ receptor IIa (FcγRIIa), potently blocking immune complex engagement without cross-reacting with the closely-related FcγRIIb. This specificity has made IV.3 invaluable for dissecting FcγRIIa-mediated activation in diverse conditions, including infection, autoimmunity, thromboinflammation, and platelet-mediated thrombosis. We combined cryogenic electron microscopy, surface plasmon resonance, alchemical free energy calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate IV.3's binding sites on FcγRIIa and the mechanistic basis of IV.3 specificity. We find that IV.3 engages a broader FcγRIIa epitope than previously recognized, extending beyond residues H/R134 and L135 (R and S in FcγRIIb). Simulations of FcγIIa-R134 variants bearing either L135 or S135 reveal that IV.3 specificity arises from hydrophobic stabilization mediated by L135 and disruption of an R134-specific interaction network in the presence of S135. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for rational design of FcγRIIa-targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: From Diagnostic Consensus to Clinical Validation: The Next Step for REFINED-ASUC.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

articles.title: Functional expression of engineered IsPETase and LCC variants in Drosophila melanogaster reveals host tolerance and differential catalytic activity.
articles.abstract: Insects offer promising opportunities for organic waste bioconversion; however, they cannot efficiently degrade synthetic polymers such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Here, we generated transgenic Drosophila melanogaster lines to express in vitro-evolved variants of two PET-degrading enzymes with distinct biochemical properties: an engineered Ideonella sakaiensis PETase variant (TS-ΔIsPET) and a leaf-branch compost cutinase variant (TA-ΔLCC). Both enzymes, fused to a Drosophila gut-derived secretory signal, were produced and secreted by Drosophila cultured S2R+ cells and transgenic larvae. Upon secretion, TS-ΔIsPET and TA-ΔLCC enzymes were glycosylated, a post-translational modification that did not abolish their catalytic activity. Notably, TA-ΔLCC displayed ∼6-fold higher esterase activity than TS-ΔIsPET in larval samples, and TA-ΔLCC-containing extracts depolymerised PET nanoparticles in vitro under enzyme-favourable conditions. Transgenic flies showed normal development, fertility and survival. Morphological and biochemical analyses confirmed that TA-ΔLCC expression did not alter midgut structure and function. Together, these results establish Drosophila melanogaster as a model for functional expression and comparative evaluation of engineered PET-degrading enzymes and identify TA-ΔLCC as a promising candidate for further evaluation in insect species relevant to plastic-contaminated waste bioconversion.

articles.title: Major Plant Diseases and Regional Plant Health Priorities in Asia.
articles.abstract: Asia supports major food, horticultural, and plantation crops, yet uneven loss data and surveillance capacity hinder continental-scale prioritization of plant diseases. This review integrates FAOSTAT crop statistics, EPPO pathogen occurrence and host records, Scopus affiliation- based publication data, and disease-specific literature to identify regional surveillance and management priorities. Wheat, rice, maize, and potato accounted for nearly three quarters of the documented crop-pathogen intersections, highlighting shared staple-crop vulnerabilities. Rice blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, and viral diseases remain major concerns in Eastern, Southern, and South-eastern Asia, where intensive cultivation and changing pathogen populations complicate durable control. Wheat rusts, bunts, and cyst nematodes warrant attention in Central, Southern, and Western Asia, while wheat blast highlights the introduction risks in Southern Asian. Fusarium head blight and maize ear rots link crop protection with food and feed safety. Potato late blight, viral degeneration, and bacterial wilt emphasize seed-tuber health in temperate and highland systems. In South-eastern Asia, cassava mosaic disease, banana Fusarium wilt, and oil palm basal stem rot present challenges associated with infected planting material and persistent inoculum. Tomato viruses threaten Western Asian protected horticulture, while citrus huanglongbing and fire blight highlight the need for healthy nursery stock and early detection. These regional disease profiles call for management tailored to production systems and pathogen biology, prioritizing durable resistance in cereals, healthy planting material in vegetatively propagated crops, and containment of persistent soilborne diseases. Standardized diagnostics, coordinated surveillance, and resource sharing can strengthen disease management across regions with unequal research and surveillance capacity.

articles.title: More than just accuracy: A pathway-level framework for implementing blood and digital biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease care.
articles.abstract: Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for patients and health systems.

articles.title: Small-molecule modulation of VDAC enhances glucose-stimulated insulin secretion by promoting ATP flux.
articles.abstract: Reduced insulin secretion by β cells is a pivotal factor in diabetes onset and progression. The small molecule NPD976 was identified as a potent insulin secretagogue using high-throughput chemical screening employing an insulin secretion assay system. Even part of the molecular structure of NPD976, designated as DPEU (N-[2-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)ethyl]urea), retains insulin secretagogue activity. DPEU enhances insulin secretion specifically under glucose stimulation in β cells derived from mice, rats, and humans. The compound localizes to mitochondria in a manner independent of high glucose stimulation. Biochemical analyses revealed that DPEU directly interacts with voltage-dependent anion channels (VDACs) located in the mitochondrial outer membrane, enhancing ATP efflux from mitochondria into the cytosol during glucose stimulation. To our knowledge, DPEU is a positive small-molecule modulator of VDAC function that promotes ATP flux in β cells through a mechanism distinct from the classical KATP or cAMP pathways. These findings identify VDAC as a potential target for enhancing insulin secretion.

articles.title: Discovery of phage defense systems through component modularity networks.
articles.abstract: Phage defense systems in bacteria exhibit high degrees of modularity, with sensing, signal transmission, and effector enzymes frequently exchanged among phage defense gene clusters. In this study, we capitalize on this modularity to discover phage defense systems by searching for defense-associated modules in new gene contexts across Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. This approach reveals a large and interconnected network of modular components distributed across diverse gene clusters. From over 500 candidate defense systems, we select five for experimental testing and validate three: Dionysus, a TerB-encoding system that interferes with early phage infection (EPI) vesicle formation by jumbo phages; Ophion, a radical S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-containing system that blocks progression from the EPI vesicle to the nucleus stage during jumbo phage infection; and Hercules, a tightly regulated restriction-modification (RM)-like system. Collectively, we demonstrate that leveraging the modular architecture of phage defense systems is an effective approach to their discovery.

articles.title: Refractory Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Supported by Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation due to Leptospirosis at Réunion Island and a Literature Review.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis prevalent on Réunion Island. Severe forms with acute respiratory failure can lead to refractory hypoxemia, requiring the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The aim for the present study was to describe all cases of leptospirosis complicated by refractory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous ECMO on Réunion Island and to conduct a literature review. This retrospective observational study was conducted in a multidisciplinary intensive care unit of the University Hospital of Réunion Island. The aim was to describe the clinical, biological, and prognostic characteristics of patients who developed leptospirosis complicated by refractory ARDS requiring ECMO between January 2011 and December 2024. A total of 14 patients with a median age of 38 years and few comorbidities were included. The organ failure most commonly associated with respiratory involvement was acute kidney injury (93%). The median delay between mechanical ventilation and ECMO support was 0 (0-1) days. The median duration of ECMO support was short (7 [4-12] days). The mortality rate in this population was 29%. A systematic literature review revealed 50 cases of patients with leptospirosis requiring ECMO, with a median age of 34 years and a mortality rate of 20%. The favorable prognosis of patients with refractory ARDS due to leptospirosis justifies the use of ECMO. Early referral to a center equipped with ECMO is essential, given the rapid decline in respiratory function.

articles.title: Headache in Calcified Neurocysticercosis: Emerging Insights into an Inflammation-Driven Phenotype.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Calcified neurocysticercosis (NCC), traditionally considered an inert marker of past infection, is increasingly recognized as a clinically meaningful condition associated with migraine-like headaches. Evidence from population-based cohorts, clinical series, and imaging studies consistently shows that individuals with calcified NCC have a higher prevalence and severity of headache than those without lesions. Prospective neuroimaging demonstrates that intermittent perilesional inflammation, including edema and blood-brain barrier disruption, can activate migraine-generating pathways, with calcitonin gene-related peptide-mediated trigeminovascular sensitization emerging as a key mechanism. These findings challenge the assumption that calcified lesions are clinically irrelevant and instead, support the concept of a distinct inflammation-driven headache phenotype. Recognizing this entity has important implications for diagnosis, counseling, and therapeutic decision-making, particularly in endemic regions where calcifications are common and often dismissed as incidental. Calcified NCC also provides a unique human model for understanding how focal neuroinflammation shapes headache susceptibility.

articles.title: Validation of a Rapid Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification-Based Test for the Detection of Shigella from Rectal Swab.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: The rapid loop-mediated isothermal amplification-based diagnostic test (RLDT) has been validated as a simple, sensitive, and rapid tool for detecting Shigella spp. from fresh or frozen stool. When stool is unavailable or difficult to transport, rectal swabs (RSs) in Cary-Blair medium, stool collected in buffered glycerol saline (BGS), or stool-dipped swabs (SDSs) in Cary-Blair medium offer alternatives that can be easily collected and transported without maintaining a cold chain. This study evaluated the performance of RLDTs for detecting Shigella spp. from RSs, stool collected in BGS, and SDSs compared with fresh stool (FS). Paired RSs and FS were collected from 105 children younger than 5 years old at two hospitals in Bangladesh. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and accuracy were determined along with the agreement between assays using kappa statistics. The RLDTs detected Shigella in approximately 38-40% of samples across all sample types. Rectal swabs in Cary-Blair medium and SDS each showed 97.6% sensitivity and 100% specificity, with PPVs of 100% and NPVs of 98.5% (RSs) and 98.4% (SDSs) compared with FS; stool collected in BGS samples demonstrated the highest sensitivity (100%) and NPV (100%), with 98.4% specificity and 97.6% PPV. All alternative specimen types showed almost perfect agreement with FS. The RLDT performed well using RSs, indicating a practical alternative to stool for detecting Shigella. The assay was also reliable with stool collected in BGS and SDSs. Broader adoption of RLDTs could improve diagnostic capacity and strengthen surveillance and control efforts.

articles.title: Latent Melioidosis Reactivation Following Immunosuppression in Malaysia: A Report of Two Cases.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Melioidosis, caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is endemic in Southeast Asia. Over 90% of cases present acutely. The reactivation of latent melioidosis in endemic regions is difficult to diagnose, and the incidence is unknown. We report two previously healthy middle-age women from Limbang, Malaysian Borneo, who were newly diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus. They developed fulminant sepsis due to culture-confirmed melioidosis 4 to 8 weeks after starting immunosuppressive therapy. They had pneumonia and multiorgan microabscesses. One patient survived, whereas the other succumbed to illness. Diagnosing the reactivation of latent melioidosis in endemic regions is impeded by substantial gaps in clinical evaluation and laboratory diagnostic capacity, particularly within resource-limited health care systems. Maintaining high clinical vigilance for reactivation, promptly identifying disseminated disease, and initiating targeted therapy early are critical during the initiation and administration of immunosuppressive treatment. Pre-immunosuppression risk assessment and potential prophylactic strategies in high-risk individuals may help reduce the associated morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Delivery and adherence of biomarker-guided antibiotic treatment protocols in the ADAPT-Sepsis clinical trial: an in-trial descriptive process evaluation of daily procalcitonin- and C-reactive protein-guided protocols.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biomarker-guided antibiotic protocols using daily procalcitonin or C-reactive protein have been proposed to optimise antibiotic duration in sepsis. This pre-planned process evaluation of the ADAPT-Sepsis trial examined delivery and clinician adherence to procalcitonin- and C-reactive protein-guided protocols.

METHODS: An embedded descriptive process evaluation was conducted within the multicentre ADAPT-Sepsis trial including 2760 adults across 41 UK critical care units. Patients were assigned to procalcitonin-guided, C-reactive protein-guided or standard care. Algorithm-generated recommendations (strong stop, suggest stop or standard care) were relayed to research staff and clinicians who remained blinded to group allocation. Adherence was defined as stopping biomarker sampling after advice. Advice timings, frequencies, adherence rates and reasons for non-adherence were recorded and analysed.

RESULTS: Among 2760 patients, strong stop advice occurred earlier in those allocated to the procalcitonin-guided group compared with the C-reactive protein-guided group (mean difference -1.7 days, 95%CI -2.5 to -0.9, p < 0.001). C-reactive protein guidance generated a higher proportion of standard care advice (mean difference -9.1%, 95%CI -10.9% to -7.3%, p < 0.001). Overall advice adherence was greater in patients allocated to the C-reactive protein group than those allocated to the procalcitonin group (mean difference -6.8%, 95%CI -9.0 to -4.5, p < 0.001), driven by the higher proportion of standard care advice and later stronger stop advice with higher adherence (mean difference -14.3%, 95%CI -21.8 to -6.8, p < 0.001). Reasons for advice non-adherence included fixed-duration microbiology guidance, illness severity, continuing fever and elevation of routine inflammatory markers, which did not differ between groups.

DISCUSSION: A C-reactive protein-guided discontinuation protocol achieved higher clinician adherence, probably because its recommendations aligned more closely with established prescribing norms. In contrast, procalcitonin guidance produced earlier and more frequent stop signals, offering greater potential to reduce antibiotic exposure but requiring clinicians to accept earlier discontinuation than usual practice.

articles.title: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity.

METHODS: Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction.

RESULTS: The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation.

CONCLUSIONS: AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

articles.title: Time-Varying Spatial Ventricular Gradient Orientation Is Associated With Anthracycline Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracycline use is limited by cardiotoxicity resulting in heart failure (HF). The spatial ventricular gradient (SVG) is a vectorcardiographic measurement of myocardial electrical heterogeneity associated with sudden death and incident HF. It is unclear if serial measurement of SVG after anthracycline initiation can help predict subsequent HF.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine if time-varying SVG measurements are associated with anthracycline HF.

METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study of adult patients with cancer treated with anthracyclines between 1992 to 2019. Standard 12-lead electrocardiograms obtained within 6 months before and up to 5 years after anthracycline initiation were analyzed. Patients with prior HF or ≤1 electrocardiogram within 5 years were excluded. Median vectorcardiograms were constructed, and the SVG vector was obtained by integrating under the X, Y, and Z QRST complexes. Multivariable competing-risks regression was performed with SVG parameters included as time-varying covariates, incident HF as the main outcome, and death as a competing outcome.

RESULTS: Among 594 patients (median age 61 years, 48% male), 83 (14%) developed HF within 5 years. In multivariable competing-risks regression, time-varying SVG azimuth (circular angle in the transverse plane) was independently associated with HF (P = 0.0024), demonstrating a 9.4-fold gradient in risk across values. Leftward/anterior azimuth values were the lowest risk areas, whereas posterior/rightward orientations were the highest risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Time-varying SVG azimuth was independently associated with HF risk in patients treated with anthracyclines. Assessing dynamic changes in SVG azimuth during anthracycline treatment may enhance early identification of patients at risk for HF and inform the use of cardioprotective strategies during cancer therapy.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation in Valvular Heart Disease: Assessing the Impact of Genetics in the UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) in valvular heart disease (VHD) is generally attributed to pressure or volume overload with atrial remodeling, but the independent contribution of genetic predisposition remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the predictive value of a previously developed AF polygenic risk score (PRS) across VHD subtypes in the UK Biobank.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study (UK Biobank, 2000-2022), incident AF and VHD status were defined using ICD codes. VHD subtypes included mitral valve (MV) disease (MV prolapse [MVP], mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis) and aortic valve (AV) disease (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation). PRS was categorized into quintiles and grouped as low, intermediate, and high.

RESULTS: Among 452,841 participants with available PRS, 385 had MVP, 1,058 mitral regurgitation, 81 mitral stenosis, 421 aortic regurgitation, and 509 aortic stenosis. In Cox models, PRS was independently associated with incident AF in MV disease (HR: 1.7, P = 0.03 for intermediate PRS; HR: 2.3, P = 0.002 for high PRS), with the strongest effect in MVP (HR: 3.1, P = 0.03 for high PRS). In AV disease, PRS was not significantly associated with AF risk (P = 0.93 and P = 0.07 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively). Interaction analyses confirmed attenuation or absence of the PRS effect in AV disease (P = 0.04 and P = 0.004 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively), whereas no significant interaction was observed in MV disease (P = 0.80 and P = 0.11, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: In VHD, AF PRS predicts AF risk, but the genetic impact differs by subtype. AV disease shows minimal genetic contribution, suggesting predominantly hemodynamic risk, while MV disease-particularly MVP-shows substantial genetic influence.

articles.title: Patient-month modeling for longitudinal blood culture contamination surveillance during a major healthcare-system disruption: a single-center interrupted time-series study.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blood culture contamination (BCC) is an important diagnostic quality indicator, but crude temporal comparisons may be misleading when repeated sampling within patients is not considered. We evaluated longitudinal changes in BCC rates before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic using patient-month Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included blood culture sets obtained at a tertiary hospital in Japan from April 2017 to June 2025. Eligible episodes had at least two sets drawn within 24 h. Interrupted time-series analysis estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for level and slope changes at pandemic and post-reclassification transitions, with the number of sets as an offset and adjustment for seasonality and within-patient correlation.

RESULTS: Among 85,955 blood culture sets, 84,213 sets from 41,732 episodes in 23,705 patients were analyzed. Crude BCC rates were 1.05%, 1.55%, and 1.49% in the prepandemic, pandemic, and post-reclassification periods.
