No significant overall level or slope changes were observed: prepandemic-to-pandemic level-change IRR, 1.23 (95% CI, 0.93-1.62); slope-change IRR, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.99-1.01); pandemic-to-post-reclassification level-change IRR, 0.88 (95% CI, 0.68-1.14); and slope-change IRR, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-1.01). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested setting-specific post-reclassification changes in the intensive care unit. Sensitivity analyses were generally consistent, although the Omicron-era breakpoint analysis suggested sensitivity to breakpoint specification.

CONCLUSION: Patient-month Poisson GEE-based analysis showed that crude increases in BCC rates were not accompanied by statistically significant overall level or slope changes after accounting for repeated patient-level sampling and seasonality. Crude BCC trends should therefore be interpreted cautiously in longitudinal microbiology surveillance.

articles.title: Determining ICU staff's conceptions, opinions, views, experiences and reflection (DISCOVER) of organ donation - Results from a Swiss multicenter survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to examine ICU professionals' perceptions, opinions, and understanding of post-mortem organ donation, and their associations with personal and professional experiences.

METHODS: Between October 2024 and April 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional survey in three Swiss ICUs, assessing perceptions, beliefs, and understanding of organ donation (primary endpoints), and their relationship with demographic characteristics and professional experiences (secondary endpoints). Emotional and ethical perspectives were rated using Likert scales.

RESULTS: Among 338 professionals (median age 39 years; 75% women; 80% nurses; median ICU experience 15 years), most had cared for brain dead organ donors, and understanding/approval were high. While 75% would accept organs, 70% were open and 41% fully committed to donating; "helping others" motivated 30.7% of the open and 13.9% of the committed. Reluctance stemmed from dignity concerns, doubts on brain death, or fear to burden relatives. Lower willingness to donate correlated with higher age (ρ = -0.309), longer ICU experience (ρ = -0.335), and belief in life after death (ρ = -0.168), while approval of the brain death concept was positively correlated (ρ = 0.253; all p ≤ 0.002); physicians were more willing than nurses (10 vs. 9; p = 0.001), and willingness aligned with wishing to receive organs (10 vs. 2; p < 0.001). The latter was linked to lower age (36 vs. 50), fewer ICU years (13 vs. 28), stronger wish to donate (10 vs. 2), and better understanding of brain death (10 vs. 9; all p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Swiss ICU professionals support organ donation, though strong commitment to donate their own organs is limited and helping others was not reported as a predominant motivation.

REGISTRATION: NCT06640088, registered on October 10, 2024.

articles.title: Deep learning algorithms for predicting intraoperative hypotension: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with myocardial injury, acute kidney injury, perioperative stroke, and 30-day mortality. Deep learning (DL) refers to a family of machine-learning methods that learn multiple levels of data representation through nonlinear transformations. In perioperative monitoring, DL models can learn patterns from time-varying physiological signals and combine them with clinical variables to estimate impending IOH risk. DL algorithms applied to continuous physiological waveforms therefore represent a rapidly expanding paradigm for early IOH prediction, but their pooled diagnostic accuracy has not been synthesised within a unified diagnostic-accuracy framework.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the pooled diagnostic accuracy of DL-based IOH prediction models and to identify factors that modify their performance.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 2026. Methodological quality was appraised with PROBAST+AI and certainty of evidence with GRADE. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and SROC-AUC; heterogeneity was quantified by τ2(Se), τ2(Sp), and ρ. Subgroup analyses (prediction window, DL architecture, modality, IOH reference, analysis unit) and random-effects meta-regression were performed.

RESULTS: Twelve studies were included; nine contributed 22 validation datasets. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.73-0.81), specificity 0.88 (0.82-0.92), and SROC-AUC 0.87 (0.83-0.90); diagnostic odds ratio 24.7 (16.1-37.9), positive likelihood ratio 6.31, negative likelihood ratio 0.26. Heterogeneity was τ2(Se) = 0.25, τ2(Sp) = 1.04, ρ = -0.28. The 5-min window achieved the highest performance (sensitivity 0.81; specificity 0.91). Meta-regression identified DL architecture as the only significant moderator of specificity (P = 0.02), with hybrid CNN-RNN exceeding pure CNN (β = 1.77, 95% CI 0.45-3.09). Deeks' test was non-significant (P = 0.06). GRADE certainty was Low.

CONCLUSIONS: DL models for IOH prediction achieve moderate diagnostic accuracy, with hybrid CNN-RNN architectures and 5-min prediction windows showing the most favourable performance. Universal absence of formal calibration assessment, scarce external validation, and geographic concentration constrain immediate clinical translation.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261377604 Reporting guideline: PRISMA-DTA.

articles.title: Genetically informed therapy for valvular heart disease: what, where, and when to target.
Protective Effect of COVID-19 Vaccination on Post-Infection Visuospatial Deficits.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil : 1999)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: COVID-19 has been associated with persistent cognitive deficits months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination reduces severe disease, but its effect on post-infection cognition remains uncertain. We evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination attenuates cognitive deficits after SARS-CoV-2.

METHODS: We assessed 237 adults with COVID-19 and 105 controls. Patients were grouped by vaccination status at infection (vaccinated n=87; unvaccinated n=150). The neuropsychological assessment covered language, visuospatial ability, visual memory, verbal memory, attention, executive functions, and working memory. Group differences were tested with Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA with Holm-corrected post hoc comparisons, adjusting for education.

RESULTS: Significant group differences were observed in visuospatial ability and visual memory, assessed with the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test (Copy, Immediate and Delayed Recall) (all p < 0.001). The vaccinated group outperformed the unvaccinated group (p = 0.022) on visuospatial performance. The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test Copy did not differ significantly among participants vaccinated with CoronaVac, AstraZeneca, or Pfizer.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that COVID-19 vaccination may mitigate post-infection visuospatial deficits, reinforcing the importance of immunization in preventing cognitive sequelae associated with the disease.

articles.title: Correction to "Meta-Analysis: Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) Test for Identifying Significant Fibrosis, Advanced Fibrosis, and Cirrhosis in Patients with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease".
Physiologic Stress During Walking and Cycling Early After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize cardiac effort and heart rate (HR) responses during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) early after cardiac surgery, compare HR patterns between walking and cycle ergometry, and evaluate differences by sex, frailty, and atrial fibrillation status.

METHODS: We analyzed a publicly available PhysioNet dataset of adults ≥65 years with pre-frailty/frailty undergoing cardiac surgery who completed a 6MWT and symptom-limited cycle ergometry with continuous single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring (Polar H10). Cardiac effort was defined as total 6MWT heartbeats divided by distance walked (beats/m). Associations with cycle-ergometry performance were assessed using Spearman correlations with bootstrap CI; paired t tests compared HR responses between modalities; subgroup differences were evaluated using Welch t tests and multivariable linear regression.

RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled participants, 66 (83%) had analyzable 6MWT ECG recordings (mean age 73 ± 5 years; 67% male; 18 ± 8 days post-surgery). Mean 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) was 300 ± 79 m, and mean cardiac effort was 1.62 ± 0.52 beats/m. In 38 participants with paired cycle-ergometry data, HR responses were similar between walking and cycling. Greater 6MWD was associated with better cycle-ergometry performance, while higher cardiac effort was associated with lower cycle-ergometry performance. In multivariable analysis, female sex was independently associated with higher cardiac effort (β = .34 beats/m; P = .042), atrial fibrillation with lower average and end-of-test HR (P ≤ .035), and greater frailty with shorter 6MWD (P = .036).

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac effort is a feasible ECG-derived metric that complements 6MWD by integrating heart rate response with functional performance early after cardiac surgery. In this frail, predominantly beta-blocked cohort, HR responses during walking closely mirrored cycle ergometry.

articles.title: Selection and Management of Patients With Resectable Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer Receiving Perioperative FLOT: A Modified Delphi Consensus Approach.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is a guideline-recommended standard for patients with resectable gastric cancer or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma globally. Guidance is limited on patient selection, nutritional optimization, and toxicity management within existing guidelines. This study aimed to develop an international consensus to address these management gaps.

METHODS: A modified Delphi methodology, informed by the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, was conducted virtually between March and August 2025. A multidisciplinary panel of 16 experts independently rated draft clinical statements across multiple domains. Responses were anonymized, with structured, iterative rounds of feedback and re-rating. Consensus was defined a priori as a median score of 7-9 (appropriate) or 1-3 (inappropriate) with a disagreement index ≤1.0.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached on 66.3% of the statements. Experts agreed that patients aged >70 years should not be routinely excluded from perioperative FLOT but require comprehensive assessment; inclusion of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) 0-1 is appropriate, and ECOG PS 0-2 may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Adequate organ function, correction of baseline conditions, hepatitis B screening, and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase testing are appropriate before FLOT initiation. Universal baseline nutritional screening and support, proactive intervention for malnourished patients, and structured physical activity were endorsed. Surgical planning was supported through multidisciplinary input, with defined perioperative windows, individualized dosing, and flexibility in pre-/postoperative cycles. For toxicity management, the panel supported dose modification over drug omission, where possible.

CONCLUSION: This Delphi consensus provides expert-driven, practice-oriented advisories codifying fitness-based selection, nutrition-forward optimization, and pragmatic toxicity management. The resulting guidance builds on current standards and provides internationally applicable consensus statements to ultimately enhance patient care.

articles.title: Progesterone Receptor Antagonists for Labor Induction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate mifepristone, a progesterone receptor antagonist, for labor induction and cesarean delivery and related measures of maternal and neonatal safety.

DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses) 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251236886). MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Scopus were searched through October 2025.

METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included randomized trials evaluating mifepristone for labor induction in singleton pregnancies at 37 weeks or more of gestation. Studies involving pregnancy termination, intrauterine fetal death, preterm induction, or concomitant cervical ripening interventions in which the effects of mifepristone could not be isolated were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included induction-to-delivery interval, time to labor onset, Bishop score, need for prostaglandin or oxytocin, postpartum hemorrhage, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and 5-minute Apgar score less than 7. Data were pooled with a random-effects model.

TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: The primary analysis included all 15 eligible randomized controlled trials across mifepristone dosing regimens (n=1,063) and control conditions (n=811). Mifepristone was associated with 33% reduced odds of cesarean delivery (33.1% vs 41.9%, odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI, 0.54-0.82) compared with the control method of induction. Mifepristone was associated with higher Bishop scores at 24 hours, shorter induction-to-delivery intervals, and less prostaglandin and oxytocin use compared with control methods. Findings were similar in sensitivity analysis limited to placebo-controlled and high-quality trials (cesarean delivery odds ratio 0.58, 95% CI, 0.40-0.83). No differences were observed in postpartum hemorrhage, NICU admission, or low Apgar score, although most studies did not report these outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Use of mifepristone for labor induction was associated with reduced odds of cesarean delivery, as well as improved cervical ripening and labor induction efficiency. No evidence of short-term maternal or neonatal risk was found, although robust data were limited. Findings support the role of progesterone antagonists for labor induction.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO, CRD420251236886.

articles.title: A Recipe for Better Diabetes Management: The DASH4D Dietary Pattern.
articles.abstract: The 2026 American Diabetes Association "Standards of Care in Diabetes" includes extensive nutrition recommendations for people with diabetes but stops short of recommending a specific dietary pattern. Instead, the guidelines recommend that all patients be referred for individualized nutrition therapy. This approach appropriately acknowledges diverse patient needs; however, it is difficult for providers to deliver any form of individualized dietary guidance without a clear starting point to guide them. In this article we examine the tension between the needs for individualization and evidence-based nutritional standards in diabetes care. We argue that the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary pattern stands out as being supported by decades of evidence from rigorous randomized clinical trials, meta-analyses, and large observational studies that have established its benefit for cardiovascular health. We summarize the recently completed DASH for Diabetes (DASH4D) trial, which demonstrated that a modified version of the original DASH eating plan, adapted for adults with diabetes, significantly reduced blood pressure and improved glycemic control in participants with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. We conclude that while individualized dietary counseling remains the standard of care, the DASH4D diet should be a recommended diet for patients with diabetes.

articles.title: Activating Zn Sites of Au/ZnO Nanocages via Au Clusters Enables Highly Sensitive Acetone Detection for Diabetes Screening.
articles.abstract: Although acetone in exhaled breath is a reliable biomarker for diabetes mellitus, its trace-level detection under high-humidity conditions remains challenging for early noninvasive diagnosis. In this study, Au-loaded ZnO nanocages derived from ZIF-8 were synthesized. The 0.4 wt % Au/ZnO-based sensor exhibits an ultrahigh response of 260.6 toward 40 ppm acetone, a theoretical detection limit as low as 0.468 ppb, fast response/recovery (2/116 s), excellent selectivity, and long-term stability. Moreover, it successfully distinguishes simulated exhaled breath of healthy individuals from that of diabetic patients under 90% RH. Theoretical calculations reveal that Au clusters activate neighboring Zn sites through electronic transfer, enhancing the chemical adsorption capacity of Zn sites for acetone molecules-a mechanism that goes beyond the conventional view of increased adsorbed oxygen. These findings provide new insights into the activation of active sites by noble metal loading and offer a promising strategy for designing highly sensitive and humidity-resistant acetone sensors toward noninvasive diabetes screening.

articles.title: Current Advances in Antioxidant Nanozymes for Liver Diseases.
articles.abstract: The liver with unique physiological functions is susceptible to oxidative stress (OS) damage from reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, further triggering various liver diseases. Compared with conventional pharmacological and surgical therapies, natural antioxidant enzymes represent promise for liver disease therapy due to high ROS scavenging and low immunogenicity. However, their clinical translation is limited by instability and complex preparation. Antioxidant nanozymes not only mimic natural enzymes, but possess advantages including simple structure, low cost and high stability. They have emerged as ideal therapeutic options for liver diseases by mitigating OS, modulating inflammation, and remodeling the pathological microenvironment. This review innovatively elucidates hepatic OS pathogenesis from a synergistic perspective, integrating indirect (inflammatory pathways) and direct (organelle stress, oxidase activation) ROS generation routes, thereby filling gaps in existing literature. Subsequently, we systematically summarize advances in five representative classes of nanomaterials: metal-, selenium-, carbon-, organic- and metal-organic frameworks (MOF)-based, and emphasize catalytic mechanisms and activity regulation strategies to guide the design of effective, low-toxicity antioxidant nanozymes. Furthermore, this review highlights recent progress of antioxidant nanozymes in typical liver diseases, including drug-induced liver injury, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, liver fibrosis, and acute liver failure, alongside clinical translation bottlenecks. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for antioxidant nanozymes are outlined.

articles.title: Identification of Novel CD52+ Fibroblasts in Nodular Prostatic Hyperplasia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and lower urinary tract symptoms are strongly associated with chronic prostate inflammation and stromal remodeling, yet the stromal cell programs that emerge during inflammatory, nodular remodeling remain incompletely defined. A Toxoplasma gondii infection model produces persistent inflammation and nodular formations, providing an experimentally tractable system to map inflammation-linked stromal states.

METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of prostates from control and chronically infected male CBA/J mice harvested at 28 days post-infection (DPI). Stromal subset reprogramming was assessed by cluster-resolved pseudobulk differential expression and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Stromal expansion and Cd52+ fibroblast subset changes were validated by whole-section immunofluorescence at 28 and 60 DPI using a CellposeSAM-based tissue cytometry pipeline. To assess human relevance, CD52+ fibroblasts were evaluated in FFPE human prostate sections by comparing inflamed versus non-inflamed stromal regions.

RESULTS: Whole-prostate single-cell profiling resolved stromal, epithelial, immune, and seminal vesicle compartments. Infection increased immune-cell abundance and increased stromal representation among non-immune cells (53.1% in controls to 69.0% in infected prostates). Stromal reclustering identified eight subsets, including a Cd52+/Ccl5+ immune-reactive fibroblast population that showed the strongest selective expansion during infection. Whole-section imaging supported overall stromal expansion over time, and Cd52+ fibroblasts were higher during infection at 60 DPI (270% increase, p = 0.0507), whereas Cxcl13+ fibroblasts remained rare and stable across conditions. Pathway analysis indicated immune-like stromal reprogramming during infection, with antigen-presentation programs enriched in larger fibroblast subsets and interferon/JAK-STAT signaling most consistently concentrated in the Cd52+/Ccl5+ subset. In human prostate tissue, CD52+ VIM+ CD45- fibroblasts were significantly enriched in inflamed regions compared with paired non-inflamed regions within the same specimen (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0026).

CONCLUSIONS: Chronic, pathogen-driven inflammation produces selective, program-specific stromal remodeling rather than uniform fibroblast activation. An interferon-reactive Cd52+ fibroblast state expands during infection in mice and marks inflamed stromal microenvironments in human prostate, supporting discrete immune-reactive fibroblast programs as a prominent feature of inflammation-associated prostate remodeling.

articles.title: Long-Term Association Between Comprehensive Cardiac Rehabilitation and Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Rhythm-Control Interventions.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention

articles.title: The Clinical Efficacy of Cardiac Rehabilitation in Takotsubo Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite normalization of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), symptoms and impaired exercise capacity can persist ~1 year after Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). We evaluated the impact of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) on cardiac structure and function, functional exercise capacity, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with TTS.

METHODS: Patients with TTS who completed (TTS-CR, n = 33) and did not complete (TTS-CTL, n = 24) CR were retrospectively analyzed. Cardiac structure and function (via echocardiogram) were assessed at index hospitalization and follow-up (post-CR in TTS-CR; >1 month later in TTS). The 6-minute walk test distance and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts quality-of-life score were assessed pre- and post-CR (TTS-CR). Major adverse cardiovascular events within 1-year post index hospitalization were recorded (all groups).

RESULTS: The LVEF improved similarly in TTS-CR (39 ± 9% vs 60 ± 6%) and TTS (39 ± 10% vs 60 ± 7%, P = .58). The left ventricular end-diastolic volume decreased similarly in TTS-CR (125 ± 40 vs 105 ± 37 mL) and TTS-CTL (126 ± 26 vs 109 ± 27 mL, P = .81). In TTS-CR, 6-minute walk test distance (330 ± 126 vs 364 ± 97 m, P = .007) and Dartmouth Cooperative Functional Assessment Charts quality-of-life score (22 ± 6 vs 19 ± 7 m, P = .04) improved significantly from pre- to post-CR. Rates of major adverse cardiovascular events were similar between groups (P > .05).

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac rehabilitation did not enhance cardiac structural or functional recovery but did improve functional exercise capacity and HRQoL in patients with TTS.

articles.title: Low-Carbohydrate Diets, Nutritional Adequacy, Glycemia, and Perinatal Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Secondary Analysis of the DiGest Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal dietary carbohydrate intake for pregnant women is disputed internationally. Many authorities recommend a minimum of 175 g/day of carbohydrates primarily to support maternal brain glucose requirements and normal fetal brain development. We assessed whether low (<175 g/day) or very low (<120 g/day) carbohydrate intake was associated with altered nutrient intake, glycemia, or pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Women recruited to the Dietary Intervention in Gestational Diabetes Trial (DiGest) completed masked continuous glucose monitoring and a 24-h dietary recall at baseline before random assignment to receive either a standard- (2,000 kcal/day) or reduced-energy diet (1,200 kcal/day) from ∼29-36 weeks' gestation.

RESULTS: At baseline, 215 women completed a dietary assessment, of whom 66 (30.7%), 74 (34.4%), and 75 (34.9%) reported standard (≥175 g/day), low (120-175 g/day), and very low carbohydrate intake (<120 g/day), respectively. Women consuming fewer carbohydrates consumed less energy, less dietary fiber, and fewer vitamins (B and E) and minerals but proportionally more protein and fat. Consumption of <120 g/day carbohydrates as assessed at baseline before the intervention was associated with a lower time above range (TAR) >120 mg/dL (-6.8% [95% CI -13.4% to -0.2%]; P = 0.044) and lower birth weight (-9.6 [95% CI -18.7 to -0.6] centiles; P = 0.037), but no difference in large- or small-for-gestational-age birth weight was observed. Low carbohydrate intake as a proportion of total energy intake (<35%) without energy restriction was associated with reduced TAR but not with a difference in birth weight.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower carbohydrate intake at baseline was associated with modestly improved glycemia before random assignment in women with GDM, but vigilance to maintain adequate intake of micronutrients and fiber is required.

articles.title: Predictors of Type 2 Diabetes Remission and Relapse After Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery or Medical-Lifestyle Therapy in the ARMMS-T2D Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) is effective in promoting remission of type 2 diabetes, but this outcome is not universally achieved. We identified baseline patient characteristics that predict diabetes remission and subsequent relapse after various MBS procedures versus intensive medical-lifestyle intervention.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D) is a 14-year, multicenter study of health outcomes in 262 patients with type 2 diabetes (68% women, age 49.9 ± 8.3 years, BMI 36.4 ± 3.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.5 ± 1.5%) previously randomized to MBS (n = 166) or medical-lifestyle management (n = 96). Predictors of remission (defined as HbA1c <6.5% on no glucose-lowering medications) and relapse were determined using univariate time-to-event analyses of prespecified candidate predictors plus agnostic, multivariate least absolute shrinkage and selection operator.

RESULTS: Throughout a median of 11 years (maximum 14 years) of follow-up, 58% of participants randomized to MBS achieved diabetes remission versus 3% with medical-lifestyle management. Predictors of diabetes remission in univariate analyses included shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, fewer glucose-lowering medication classes used, greater body weight, higher fasting C-peptide and insulin levels, and weight loss at 1 year (all P < 0.05). Diabetes remission predictors in multivariate analyses included baseline diabetes duration, insulin use, and weight change at 1 year (all P < 0.01). Diabetes relapse after initial remission in the MBS group was predicted by longer baseline diabetes duration and greater number of glucose-lowering medication classes used.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline predictors of diabetes remission and subsequent relapse among participants randomized to one of three MBS procedures or a medical-lifestyle intervention should help inform personalized selection of diabetes treatment.

articles.title: Disrupting the PNPLA3-ABHD5 Interaction Stimulates Lipolysis and Improves PNPLA3-I148M-Associated Hepatic Steatosis.
articles.abstract: We evaluate the importance of the protein-protein interaction (PPI) between PNPLA3-I148M and its cofactor α/β-hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5) in PNPLA3-I148M-mediated hepatic steatosis. We demonstrate that disrupting the PNPLA3-ABHD5 PPI improves I148M-associated steatosis and markers of liver injury. This work supports the development of therapies targeting the PNPLA3-ABHD5 PPI for the treatment of PNPLA3-I148M-associated metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

articles.title: Performing Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation Without On-Site Cardiothoracic Surgery: Time to Step on the Pedal or Pump the Brakes?
Clinical Trial Design Considerations for the Development of Disease-Modifying Therapies for Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Several disease-modifying therapies have reduced the progressive loss of β-cell function in type 1 diabetes, with efficacy observed across a wide array of underlying therapeutic mechanisms of action. These successes highlight opportunities to accelerate the development of novel and repurposed type 1 diabetes treatments; however, only one such therapy has received regulatory approval for clinical use and few phase 3 clinical trials have been performed. For bringing emerging therapies to people living with type 1 diabetes as quickly and efficiently as possible, overall regulatory strategy and clinical trial design, especially inclusion criteria and end point selection, are essential, and planning must include their careful consideration. The considerations discussed herein represent a feasible and promising road map for developers of disease-modifying therapies and establish that type 1 diabetes remains a promising area for continued investment.

articles.title: Accelerated Epigenetic Ageing in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Comparison of 10 Epigenetic Clock Measures in Individuals With Type 1 Diabetes.
authors: FinnDiane Study Group and the GENIE Consortium
articles.abstract: We investigated whether an association existed between epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD) in type 1 diabetes, using 10 clocks and two cohorts, and whether this amplified disease progression. Older EAA phenotypic age and shorter epigenetically predicted telomere lengths were significantly associated with DKD. Progression from normolbuminuria to severely increased albuminuria was associated with increased EAA, and age, epigenetic age, and EAA were significant predictors of progression to end-stage kidney disease. Results support the development of epigenetic biomarkers predicting DKD onset and progression.

articles.title: Variability in automated sepsis case detection: a systematic analysis of implementation methods in clinical data repositories.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and characterize methodological heterogeneity in sepsis case detection using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) and eICU-CRD databases.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed and Web of Science (publication years 2016-2024). Studies were eligible if they applied the SOFA-based Sepsis-3 definition to MIMIC-III or eICU-CRD, provided at least one explicit label-calculation detail, reported a traceable detection rate, and met further criteria detailed in the PRISMA flow diagram. We classified each study by study type and unit of analysis (patients, admissions, or ICU stays) and extracted methodological details on sepsis case detection across 6 domains. For studies with available source code, we additionally examined code structure and repository dependencies to identify methodological decisions across these domains.

RESULTS: Of 396 publications screened, 64 met inclusion criteria and 12 provided source code. Sepsis detection rates ranged from 3.4% to 65.2% in MIMIC-III and from 9.8% to 47.9% in eICU-CRD. Substantial variability persisted among studies using identical cohort definitions within both databases (MIMIC-III: 16.9%-42.2%; eICU-CRD: 13.9%-31.4%). In a generalized linear mixed model, between-study heterogeneity was extreme (overall τ²≈0.79; 95% prediction interval for a new study's detection rate 5%-63%), and study-level characteristics-including database, study type, infection detection method, code availability, and unit of analysis-explained only a small proportion of this variance (≈9%), with no characteristic reaching statistical significance. The overall proportion of studies reporting methodological details varied by domain: SOFA calculation (53.1%), infection detection methods (42.2%), temporal windows (37.5%), aggregation methods (26.6%), and missing-data handling (17.2%). Source code analysis identified 321 implementation decisions, revealing heterogeneity in baseline SOFA definitions (SOFA = 0 vs dynamic baseline), temporal windows (infection-centered vs ICU-admission-centered) and infection detection methods (antibiotic-culture matching vs APACHE-based diagnosis). Dependencies among several MIMIC-III repositories suggested propagation of implementation decisions across studies.

DISCUSSION: Clinically validated sepsis definitions yield substantially different detection rates across studies using identical datasets. Statistical modeling showed that this variability is driven almost entirely by between-study implementation differences rather than sampling error or study characteristics.

CONCLUSION: To improve reproducibility in sepsis research and the robustness of sepsis prediction models, we recommend standardized reporting of sepsis case detection methodology and the publication of version-controlled source code.

articles.title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct therapeutic requirements of each phase-salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase-we designed an ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained long-term cardiac functional improvement.

articles.title: Assessment of Tidal Volume in Patients Undergoing Noninvasive Ventilation: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is widely used in acute respiratory failure (ARF), yet the association between high tidal volume (Vt) and clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the association between Vt and NIV failure overall and by ARF type, and its relationship with respiratory and clinical outcomes.

DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and Latin American and Caribbean Health Science Literature (1976 to September 2025).

STUDY SELECTION: Observational studies of adults with ARF treated with NIV reporting Vt or Vt normalized to predicted body weight (Vt/PBW) in NIV success and failure groups.

DATA EXTRACTION: Three pairs of reviewers identified studies and extracted data independently. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Eleven studies (1136 patients) were included. Vt/PBW was higher in NIV failure vs. success (mean difference [MD], 1.02 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.60-1.45 mL/kg]), whereas absolute Vt did not differ (MD, 1.30 [-33.31 to 35.91]). In hypoxemic ARF, Vt/PBW remained higher in NIV failure (MD, 0.89 mL/kg [95% CI, 0.04-1.73 mL/kg]); no data were available for hypercapnic ARF. Post hoc analyses showed that higher Vt/PBW was associated with increased mortality (odds ratio, 9.11; 95% CI, 3.88-21.37), higher respiratory rate (RR; MD, 3.14 breaths/min [95% CI, 1.36-4.92 breaths/min]), and lower Paco2 (MD, -2.38 mm Hg [95% CI, -4.16 to -0.5938 mm Hg]), but no with pressure support (PS) level (MD, 0.24 [95% CI, -0.81 to 1.29]). Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with ARF treated with NIV, higher Vt/PBW was associated with NIV failure and worse outcomes. These findings reflect prognostic associations rather than causality, and interventional studies with systematic Vt monitoring are needed. Importantly, elevated Vt/PBW, higher RR, lower Paco2, and increased mortality, without differences in PS, collectively implicate elevated respiratory drive as a driver of increased mortality (PROSPERO [CRD42024584977]).Findings: Higher Vt/PBW was associated with NIV failure, particularly in hypoxemic respiratory failure; post hoc analyses showed associations with increased mortality, higher respiratory rate, and lower Paco2.

articles.title: Antibiotic prophylaxis with vancomycin and gentamicin and the occurrence of acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: A retrospective single-centre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vancomycin combined with gentamicin (VGA) is used as an alternative antibiotic prophylaxis in cardiac surgery when cephalosporins are contraindicated. However, the nephrotoxic potential of this combination raises concerns regarding postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between VGA prophylaxis and AKI occurrence in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), while accounting for preoperative risk factors.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-centre study. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria within 7 postoperative days.

PATIENTS: Of the 8895 eligible patients between April 2013 and December 2021, 8198 were included. Subgroup analyses were performed according to preoperative AKI risk status (high-risk: insulin-dependent diabetes, cirrhosis, acute endocarditis, preoperative critical state, emergency surgery, or cardiac transplantation).

RESULTS: In our cohort, 7469 (91%) received cephalosporins and 729 (9%) received VGA. The overall AKI incidence was 16%. AKI occurred more frequently in the VGA group (29% vs. 15%, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, VGA remained independently associated with AKI [odds ratio (OR) 1.29, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.03 to 1.62, P = 0.024], confirmed by propensity score analysis (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.09 to 1.60, P = 0.005). In subgroup analyses, VGA was significantly associated with AKI in high-risk patients (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.14 to 2.04, P = 0.004), but not in low-risk patients (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.64, P = 0.285).

CONCLUSION: In this large retrospective cohort, VGA antibiotic prophylaxis was independently associated with increased AKI risk following cardiac surgery with CPB. This association was driven primarily by patients with preoperative risk factors for AKI. Alternative prophylactic regimens should be considered in high-risk patients when possible.

articles.title: When Insulin Must Wait: The Role of Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Hypokalemia During Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common life-threatening metabolic emergency characterized by hyperglycemia, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and ketosis. Severe hypokalemia before insulin therapy is uncommon but may complicate management and delay treatment. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of generalized abdominal pain and progressive shortness of breath. He was drowsy and tachypneic, with Kussmaul respirations. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe DKA, acute kidney injury, and severe hypokalemia. Insulin therapy was initially withheld according to the DKA protocol. Intravenous potassium supplementation failed to achieve sustained correction, resulting in repeated interruptions of insulin therapy. Due to refractory hypokalemia, an emergency 2-hour session of intermittent hemodialysis was performed, followed by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). During CRRT, serum potassium increased, serum creatinine decreased, metabolic acidosis improved, and the anion gap closed. Insulin therapy was resumed without further interruption. However, the clinical course was complicated by severe septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and catastrophic intracerebral hemorrhage, ultimately resulting in death. CONCLUSIONS Severe hypokalemia at presentation in DKA poses a critical therapeutic challenge because insulin therapy must be withheld until the electrolyte abnormality is corrected. In rare cases of refractory hypokalemia, CRRT may serve as an adjunctive strategy to facilitate metabolic stabilization and safe DKA management. This case adds to the limited literature and highlights the need for further studies to clarify the role and effectiveness of this approach. Biochemical resolution of DKA may not correspond to clinical recovery, and critically ill patients warrant continuous monitoring.

articles.title: Type 1 diabetes in the youngest: from distinct needs to new frontiers in care.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) in very young children poses unique clinical and psychosocial challenges due to distinct physiological, developmental, and behavioural characteristics of this age group. Advances in diabetes technology, particularly hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, are transforming T1D management in young children by integrating continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with automated insulin delivery (AID). Evidence from randomized controlled trials and real-world studies consistently demonstrates that HCL systems improve time in range, lower HbA1c, and reduce glycaemic variability without increasing the risk of severe hypoglycaemia or diabetic ketoacidosis. Benefits are especially evident overnight, when glycaemic control is more stable, although daytime management remains more complex, due to unpredictable behaviours typical of preschoolers and marked circadian variability in insulin needs. Accordingly, the use of HCL fail to decrease hypoglycaemia in this population. Additional strategies, such as insulin dilution, may facilitate safer delivery of small doses, reducing the risk of nocturnal hypoglycaemia and improving time in range (TIR). Beyond metabolic outcomes, HCL systems substantially improve quality of life for both children and caregivers, reducing fear of hypoglycaemia, easing parental burden, and improving sleep and emotional well-being. Overall, current evidence supports HCL as a safe and effective therapeutic option for very young children with T1D, offering significant metabolic and psychosocial benefits, without completely eliminating the risk of hypoglycaemia. These findings highlight the need for further refinement of age-specific algorithms capable of addressing the unique physiological variability of this population.

articles.title: LONGITUDINAL CLINICAL AND INTEGRATIVE MULTI-OMICS DATA REVEAL TRAJECTORY-DEFINED SUBGROUPS WITH DISTINCT KIDNEY FAILURE RISK IN DIABETIC KIDNEY DISEASE.
articles.abstract: Background Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of CKD globally. Despite marked heterogeneity in progression, risk stratification remains anchored to single-timepoint measures that fail to capture individual patient trajectories. We aimed to identify clinically meaningful DKD subgroups from real-world longitudinal data and characterise their molecular signatures using integrative multi-omics. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, unsupervised clustering of longitudinal creatinine and haematocrit trajectories was performed in the Salford Kidney Study (SKS; n=335 eligible for clustering, n=303 DKD) and validated in two independent cohorts: Scottish Health Research Register (SHARE; n=824) and CERCA-Diabetes (Spain; n=187). Prognostic performance was assessed by C-statistic, time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), IDI (integrated discrimination improvement), and decision curve analysis relative to the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE) and Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categorisation. Multi-omic characterisation (proteomics, metabolomics, DNA methylation) was performed in an 87-patient SKS subset using Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker Discovery using Latent Components (DIABLO). Results Two groups with markedly different progression rates were identified: high-risk (SKS-HR; n=173) and low-risk (SKS-LR; n=162). SKS-HR showed eGFR decline nearly four times faster and a higher rate of the composite kidney failure endpoint (HR 4.05 [95% CI 2.77-5.92] adjusted for age, sex, and eGFR; 2.95 [1.90-4.56] after further adjustment for haemoglobin, proteinuria, HbA1c, and cardiovascular burden; both p<0.0001). The signal was specific to renal progression (fully adjusted HR 5.98 [3.32-10.79], p<0.0001) and absent for cardiovascular or renal death (HR 1.00 [0.58-1.71], p=0.984). The subgroup-outcome association was independently replicated in SHARE (p=3.83×10⁻²⁷) and CERCA-Diabetes (p=1.72×10⁻⁴). The subgrouping added prognostic information complementary to the KFRE, raising the C-statistic from 0.689 to 0.721 when added to static KFRE and 0.711 to 0.732 when added to longitudinal KFRE. KDIGO risk categories showed limited discriminatory capacity in this predominantly G3b-G4 cohort. Hypothesis-generating multi-omic profiling showed FDR-significant enrichment for lipid transport pathways and for an independent DKD progression proteomic signature; all multi-omic findings require independent validation. Conclusions Longitudinal creatinine and haematocrit trajectories, available from routine clinical records, identify DKD patients at high risk of kidney failure with prognostic information beyond current risk tools. The high-risk subgroup warrants prospective validation and evaluation of whether subgroup assignment can improve risk stratification beyond existing clinical tools.

articles.title: Maternal Diabetes during Pregnancy and Risk of Childhood Psoriasis in Offspring: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Objective Maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with long-term metabolic and immune-related outcomes in offspring. While psoriasis is strongly linked to metabolic comorbidities later in life, the impact of in utero exposure to maternal diabetes on psoriasis risk in offspring remains unknown. We investigated whether maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with the development of childhood psoriasis in offspring. Research Design and Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest health maintenance organization. The cohort included 215,280 singleton live births between 2010 and 2023, with follow-up through 2024. Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was identified using ICD-10 codes and categorized as gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes. The primary outcome was childhood psoriasis in offspring. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, and offspring characteristics were used to estimate associations. Results Overall, 5.4% of offspring were born to mothers with diabetes during pregnancy. During follow-up, 1,557 children (0.7%) were diagnosed with psoriasis. Psoriasis prevalence did not differ between offspring exposed and unexposed to maternal diabetes (0.7% vs. 0.7%). No associations were observed by diabetes subtype, treatment modality, or degree of glycemic control. In adjusted analyses, maternal diabetes was not associated with childhood psoriasis in offspring (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.90-1.54; p = 0.246). Conclusions Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was not associated with increased childhood psoriasis risk in offspring. Our findings do not support a substantial role for prenatal metabolic dysregulation in childhood psoriasis development.

articles.title: Multifunctional nanocomposite with stage-responsive behavior for wound healing.
articles.journal: Journal of biomaterials science. Polymer edition
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds, particularly refractory diabetic ulcers, typically fail to heal due to a self-perpetuating inflammatory state driven by persistent bacterial infection, severe oxidative stress, and impaired microvascular regeneration. Conventional static dressings cannot accommodate the spatiotemporal, multiphase complexity of tissue repair. Here, a stage-responsive hierarchical nanocomposite (SNF@GQDs@Arg) was engineered by covalently anchoring graphene quantum dots (GQDs) onto radially porous silica nanoflowers (SNF), followed by surface adsorption of L-arginine (L-Arg). The resulting platform coordinates wound repair through an integrated tripartite-physical, catalytic, and metabolic-cascade. In the initial hemostatic phase, the high-aspect-ratio topography of SNF enables rapid wound closure via a non-covalent nano-bridging effect. During the inflammatory phase, the immobilized GQDs act as peroxidase-mimicking nanozymes, converting pathological hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) into bactericidal hydroxyl radicals (·OH) to eradicate biofilms while simultaneously scavenging excess free radicals to resolve the reactive oxygen species (ROS) paradox. Concurrently, the sustained release of L-Arg replenishes the substrate pool for macrophage inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), restoring physiological nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. This metabolic intervention drives pro-inflammatory M1-to-reparative M2 phenotype transition, upregulates CD31 and VEGF expression to stimulate angiogenesis, and promotes organized collagen deposition. In a murine infected full-thickness skin defect model, SNF@GQDs@Arg markedly accelerated wound closure, suppressed local inflammation, and enhanced tissue remodeling quality without inducing systemic toxicity. By synchronizing functional bioactivity with the endogenous repair rhythm, this platform provides a microenvironment-adaptive paradigm for refractory chronic wound therapy.

articles.title: What Are the Impacts of Immunoglobulin a Vasculitis on Choroidal Vascularity and Subfoveal Thickness in Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate choroidal structural and vascular changes in children with Immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV) using optical coherence tomography (OCT).

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 90 eyes of 41 children diagnosed with IgAV and 49 age-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examination and OCT imaging. Subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) were measured.

RESULTS: Subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) values were significantly lower in the patient group compared to the healthy group (p = 0.017, p = 0.018, respectively). SFCT and CVI were negatively correlated with disease activation and duration, respectively (r = -0.614 p < 0.001; r = -0.377 p < 0.05, respectively).

CONCLUSION: Children with IgAV demonstrated significantly reduced SFCT and CVI compared with healthy controls. These findings indicate the presence of choroidal structural and vascular alterations in IgAV, even in the absence of clinically apparent ocular pathology.

articles.title: A low-resource tracking workflow improves documentation and localizes the latent tuberculosis infection care gap in college student health.
articles.journal: Journal of American college health : J of ACH
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess a low-resource tracking workflow for improved documentation of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) treatment status and describe identified follow-up gaps in a Student Health clinic.

PARTICIPANTS: Students with confirmed LTBI before (2018-2023; n = 82) and after (2024-2025; n = 147) implementation.

METHODS: Retrospective before-after chart review. In 2024, the clinic added a tracking spreadsheet, nurse-initiated follow-up offering tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT), 1-month dispensing, and standardized documentation. Outcomes were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Among students prescribed TPT at Student Health, documented completion rose from 45.8 to 71.4% and known status from 58.3 to 89.3%; documented completion among students managed outside Student Health rose from 23.1 to 56.1%. Undocumented final status was essentially unchanged (35.4-34.0%), but 46/50 (92%) unresolved post-intervention cases had no response after two messages.

CONCLUSIONS: The workflow improved documentation among engaged students and identified nonresponse after TPT was offered as the main actionable gap.

articles.title: Randomized Treatment Discontinuation Trials in Nephrology.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

articles.title: Jet-injected combinational adjuvants potentiate naked mRNA vaccines for protection against respiratory viral infections in mice.
articles.abstract: The use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to enhance delivery and immunogenicity of mRNA vaccines raises safety concerns due to strong reactogenicity. Developing naked mRNA vaccines, which can be delivered through liquid jet-injection to the skin, may offer a safer alternative, but their immunogenicity has been limited. To address this challenge, we screened clinically relevant adjuvants to enhance the efficacy of N1-methyl-pseudouridine-modified naked mRNA jet-injection vaccines in mouse models. Although many adjuvants showed little or inhibitory effects on inducing humoral or cellular immunity-despite their known ability to potentiate conventional non-mRNA vaccine platforms-we identified a combination of aluminum phosphate and CpG oligonucleotide that substantially enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses with increased IgG2a/IgG1 ratio. This adjuvanted naked mRNA vaccine induced IgG2a and cellular immunity at levels comparable to those achieved with LNPs but with lower local and systemic reactogenicity. Mechanistic investigations revealed key roles for type I interferon and interleukin-6 signaling during immunization. Notably, this vaccine formulation in mice virtually eliminated infection by both SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus (A/California/7/2009 H1N1) in plaque-forming assays. Collectively, the adjuvanted naked mRNA jet-injection vaccine represents an effective, and safe platform against infectious diseases, with potential for clinic-ready translational applications.

articles.title: Endothelial neo-antigen expression initiates CD8⁺ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis amplified by peripheral immune challenge.
articles.abstract: Primary central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and devastating inflammatory cerebrovascular disease for which pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly defined, largely due to limited access to human tissue and the absence of validated experimental models. Here, we present a mouse model of CNS-restricted vasculitis based on inducible, endothelial-biased neoantigen expression, termed brain endothelial ovalbumin (BrEndO). In BrEndO mice, tamoxifen-induced ovalbumin (OVA) expression in cerebral endothelial cells (ECs) elicited a controlled endogenous CD8+ T cell response at the blood-brain barrier that remained clinically restrained. In contrast, peripheral immune activation through infection with OVA-expressing Listeria monocytogenes or systemic PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade converted this regulated response into severe, CD8+ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis with vascular injury and parenchymal infiltration. Transcriptomic profiling of inflamed cerebral microvessels and spatial transcriptomic analyses demonstrated shared inflammatory and immune activation signatures between BrEndO mice and human primary CNS vasculitis brain biopsies. These findings identify antigen-specific endothelial immune recognition as a regulated process whose breakdown precipitates CNS-restricted vasculitis and establish BrEndO as an experimentally tractable platform to investigate mechanisms and modifiers of immune-mediated cerebrovascular inflammation.

articles.title: Excess IL-18 drives fatal mousepox cytokine storm via NK cell immunodeficiency and nonspecific T-cell hyperactivation.
articles.abstract: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a hyperinflammatory syndrome with multiple contributors, often including an infectious trigger. The Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS) subtype is linked to marked IL-18 excess, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) activation, and natural killer (NK) cell abnormalities. We asked how excess IL-18 shapes NK and CTL responses to viral challenge. Mice with chronic IL-18 overproduction (Il18tg), showed baseline NK-cytopenia and CTL activation resembling MAS-susceptible patients. NK transcriptomes reflected IL-18/IFNg-axis activation and cell cycle upregulation. LCMV infection of Il18tg mice causes HLH/MAS without affecting viral control, but is not a significant NK challenge. Early after infection with NK-dependent mousepox, Il18tg NKs failed to activate appropriately, but CTLs quickly hyperactivated and mousepox control remained intact. Mousepox-infected Il18tg mice then developed signs of HLH/MAS including hepatosplenic necrosis. Their viral control was impaired, possibly because they failed to expand mousepox-specific CTLs. Il18bpKO mice, despite more normal resting lymphocytes, succumbed similarly to viremic HLH/MAS. Transfer of pre-activated NKs into Il18tg mice partially rescued virus-specific CTL responses, viral control, and survival. Thus, excess IL-18 contributes to HLH/MAS via disparate effects on CTL and NK cells, demonstrating a novel, context-specific NK immunodeficiency and highlighting how subtle host-pathogen interactions can affect the mechanisms and treatment rationale of life-threatening HLH/MAS.

articles.title: Astrocytic glutamate transporter loss drives chemoreflex hyperactivity and cardiorespiratory dysfunction in a heart failure model.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Breathing instability and exaggerated chemoreflex activation contribute to adverse HF outcomes, yet the central mechanisms linking respiratory control to cardiac dysfunction remain poorly defined. The retrotrapezoid nucleus (RTN) is a key brainstem chemosensory region regulating ventilatory and autonomic output, but whether glial dysfunction within this circuit contributes to HF pathophysiology is unknown. We hypothesized that loss of astrocytic glutamate transporter 1 (GLT-1) in the RTN disrupts glutamate homeostasis, producing chemoreflex hyperactivity and cardiorespiratory dysfunction in HF. In a rat model of nonischemic HF, reduced astrocytic GLT-1 expression in the RTN was accompanied by extracellular glutamate accumulation and heightened excitability of chemosensitive neurons. These changes were associated with exaggerated central chemoreflex responses, breathing instability, autonomic imbalance, and impaired cardiac function. Astrocyte-specific GLT-1 restoration normalized RTN glutamate levels, reduced central chemoreceptor neuron hyperexcitability, stabilized breathing, and improved cardiac performance. Systemic riluzole, an FDA-approved glutamate-modulating drug, similarly reduced RTN glutamate accumulation and attenuated chemoreflex-driven respiratory instability. These findings identify loss of astrocytic GLT-1-mediated glutamate homeostasis in the RTN as a mechanism contributing to cardiorespiratory dysfunction in HF and support pharmacological targeting of brainstem glutamate homeostasis as a therapeutic strategy requiring further investigation.

articles.title: Food insecurity in young rats induces metabolic remodeling in a sex- and diet-dependent manner.
articles.abstract: Exposure of humans to food insecurity (FI), involving sporadic access and low nutritional quality, is associated with later life development of metabolic disease phenotypes, but mechanisms are poorly understood. We exposed very young rats to a 20-day FI intervention or ad-lib (AL) feeding, using either standard chow (SC) or high fat/high sucrose (HF/HS) diets, followed by continued AL feeding on the respective diets for 10-13 weeks. We found that male, but not female rats subjected to FI on the HF/HS diet had increased body fat percentage, ratio of adipose to body weight, and fat cell size compared to AL rats, coupled with metabolomic and transcriptomic profiles consistent with reduced fatty acid oxidation in the liver and maladaptive remodeling of adipose tissue. These changes were specific to HF/HS feeding and did not occur with SC diet. Our study defines sex- and diet-specific metabolic remodeling responses to FI that may contribute to future disease phenotypes.

articles.title: FAP-targeting CAR T cells with constitutive IL-10 expression reduce kidney fibrosis in mice.
Restoration of full length filamin C is sufficient to prevent FLNC deficient cardiomyopathy in mice.
articles.abstract: Filamin C (FLNC) is an essential cytoskeletal protein required for cardiomyocyte structural integrity and mechanotransduction. Truncating FLNC variants cause haploinsufficiency associated with dilated and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, yet no therapies currently address the underlying defect of FLNC deficiency. Gene replacement is challenging because the approximately 8.2-kb FLNC coding sequence exceeds the packaging capacity of conventional adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. Here, we engineered a triple-AAV strategy optimized for full-length FLNC reconstitution in the heart. Screening in HEK293 cells identified GP41-1 and IMPDH as a compatible orthogonal pair for efficient full-length FLNC reconstitution. In tamoxifen-inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific Flnc knockout mice, systemic delivery of optimized MyoAAV2A vectors restored full-length FLNC expression and re-established sarcomeric localization following cardiomyocyte FLNC depletion. A total vector dose of 1 × 10¹³ genome copies/kg restored FLNC to approximately endogenous abundance, preserved systolic function and ventricular dimensions, limited cardiac enlargement, attenuated fibrotic remodeling and prevented premature death. FLNC replacement also attenuated pathological transcriptional remodeling and compensatory changes in cytoskeletal and junction-associated proteins. These findings demonstrate that systemic split-intein-mediated reconstitution of full-length FLNC can preserve cardiac structure and function in vivo, providing preclinical support for a mutation-independent therapeutic strategy for FLNC-associated cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Case report: Meningitis of a 66-year-old dog owner caused by Capnocytophaga canimorsus.
articles.abstract: Capnocytophaga canimorsus is a fastidious Gram-negative rod transmitted from dog saliva and typically associated with immunocompromised hosts. We report meningitis in a 66-year-old immunocompetent dog owner with prior cerebral amyloid angiopathy who presented with acute global aphasia, fever and inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) consistent with bacterial meningitis, but without meningism or history of any dog bite. Fusiform Gram-negative rods in CSF prompted extended culture in thioglycolate broth, enabling growth and subsequent species identification by MALDI-TOF MS as C. canimorsus within five days. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to EUCAST guidance for situations without species-specific breakpoints and supported continuation of ceftriaxone-based therapy for a total of 15 days, resulting in complete clinical remission and normalization of CSF parameters. This case underlines that C. canimorsus meningitis can occur in apparently immunocompetent elderly patients, illustrates the diagnostic value of targeted culture strategies, and emphasizes the feasibility of EUCAST-guided susceptibility testing for this rare pathogen.

articles.title: Distilling Direct Effects via Conditional Differential Gene Expression Analysis.
articles.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Differential gene expression (DGE) analysis is foundational for interpreting RNA sequencing data, but it conflates direct biological effects with correlations propagated through gene co-expression. Across three RNA sequencing datasets (including a genome-scale perturb-seq experiment), we find that only a small fraction of differentially expressed genes have direct effects on the trait of interest, while the majority are undirected or passengers whose associations are mediated through other genes.

RESULTS: To distinguish direct effect genes, we introduce conditional differential gene expression (CDGE) analysis, a framework that tests for conditional rather than marginal association between each gene and the trait of interest. Implemented via the GhostKnockoff procedure with lasso regression, CDGE delivers false discovery rate control, operates on summary statistics from existing DGE pipelines, and accommodates batch effects. The genes identified by CDGE mediate the effects of most other differentially expressed genes and show stronger enrichment for known protein-protein interactions and biological pathways than DGE-identified genes. These results suggest that the field has been systematically over-interpreting DGE outputs, and that distinguishing direct from mediated effects is essential for prioritizing genes for functional follow-up and therapeutic development.

AVAILABILITY: To facilitate public access to knockoff-based CDGE analysis, we have developed the R package "KnockoffCDGE" as an integrated implementation, which is freely available at https://github.com/GuJQ5/KnockoffCDGE (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23241517).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

articles.title: Longitudinal Association Between Prefrailty/Frailty and HIV-associated Neurocognitive Disorder (HAND): a Mexican Prospective Study.
articles.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
articles.abstract: Geriatric syndromes such as frailty may be more prevalent and occur earlier in people aging with HIV, negatively impacting outcomes like cognition. Cross-sectional data show strong associations between pre-frailty/frailty and HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). However, prospective studies suggest baseline HAND increases frailty risk, while pre-frailty/frailty do not predict HAND onset. We aimed to investigate longitudinal association between baseline frailty and HAND category progression. Longitudinal analysis of 194 participants aged ≥50 years from Mexico City referral center. Two standardized geriatric assessments performed at least one year apart. HAND defined using Antinori criteria, frailty by Fried phenotype. Inverse probability weighted Cox models adjusted for confounders from directed acyclic graph (age, educational level, detectable viral load, diabetes, stroke, ischemic heart disease) determined association between frailty and HAND progression. Median age 55 (53-61) years; 167 (86%) men; median follow-up 2.3 (1.6-3.1) years. Baseline: 129 (66.4%) robust, 62 (31.9%) pre-frail, 3 (1.5%) frail. No longitudinal association between pre-frailty/frailty and HAND progression was observed in this cohort (32 progression events; adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.27-1.48; p = 0.29). No evidence of a prospective association between prefrailty/frailty and HAND category progression was observed in this cohort; most participants remained cognitively stable. To our knowledge, this is the first study describing HAND trajectories and their relationship with prefrailty/frailty in older adults with HIV in Mexico and Latin America.

articles.title: Sucrose induces Cardiac Hypertrophy and Renal Perivascular Fibrosis in a Novel Mouse Model of Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excess sugar consumption increases the risk for hypertension. We previously reported pilot data demonstrating that male mice drinking 2% sucrose water develop hypertension. However, the sucrose effects on left ventricular hypertrophy, kidney fibrosis, or sex difference in hypertension remain unclear. In the present study, we characterized the cardiac and renal pathology in a larger cohort including female mice to establish a novel sucrose-induced mouse model of hypertension associated with cardiovascular remodeling.

METHODS: Eight- to nine- week-old C57BL6 mice were given drinking water containing 2% sucrose or regular water for 4 weeks. Blood pressure was monitored using a tail-cuff system. Echocardiography was performed to evaluate cardiac remodeling. Sirius red staining was performed to evaluate heart and kidney fibrosis.

RESULTS: Male mice drinking the sucrose water developed hypertension (systolic blood pressure 122.0±1.3mmHGvs 162.2±4.3 mmHG at day 28). Sucrose treatment increased left ventricular wall thickness and induced perivascular fibrosis of the heart and kidney compared to control mice. Cardiac functions were preserved. In female mice, sucrose treatment induced milder hypertension than male mice (126.9±2.4 mmHg vs 143.7±3.2 mmHg at day 28). However, sucrose treatment caused similar degree of left ventricular hypertrophy in female mice.

CONCLUSION: Sucrose water induced hypertension, cardiac hypertrophy, and fibrosis of the heart and kidney in male mice. Female mice were partially protected from hypertension but not from cardiac hypertrophy. This mouse model represents a useful tool to investigate molecular mechanisms by which hypertension and end organ damage develop with excess sugar consumption.

articles.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) on pain intensity and functional disability in individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, LILACS, Google Scholar, and ProQuest were searched. The PICOS framework included individuals with CLBP receiving ESWT, compared with placebo, usual care, exercise, or physiotherapy. Randomized controlled trials reporting pain intensity and/or functional disability were included. Data on participant characteristics, interventions, comparators, and ESWT dosimetry were extracted.

RESULTS: Of 430 records identified, nine randomized controlled trials were included. Radial ESWT (rESWT) significantly reduced pain (SMD = -0.72; 95% CI -1.30 to -0.14; I2 = 76%), whereas focused ESWT (fESWT) showed benefit in one trial. Functional disability significantly improved overall (MD = -6.12; 95% CI -10.02 to -2.22; I2 = 75%), but the effect did not reach the minimal clinically important difference. Most studies evaluated outcomes only immediately post-intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicated influence of methodological quality and heterogeneity.

CONCLUSION: ESWT, particularly rESWT, may reduce pain in CLBP, but functional improvements are not clinically meaningful. Short follow-up and substantial heterogeneity limit the strength of recommendations. rESWT and fESWT should not be considered interchangeable.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION NUMBER: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under the registration number CRD420251085206.

articles.title: Increasing contribution of dental antibiotic prescribing to community-acquired Clostridioides difficile infection: a 9-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Community-acquired Clostridioides difficile infection (CA-CDI) is increasingly recognized outside healthcare settings, yet the contribution of dental antibiotic prescribing remains poorly characterized. This study compared patients with CA-CDI following antibiotics prescribed by dental practitioners versus family physicians.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the University Hospital for Infectious Diseases "Dr. Fran Mihaljević", Zagreb, Croatia, including adults with a first episode of confirmed CA-CDI following outpatient antibiotic exposure between 2011 and 2019. Characteristics were compared by prescriber.

RESULTS: Among 666 patients with CA-CDI, 190 (28.5%) had received antibiotics from dental practitioners and 476 (71.5%) from family physicians. Dental-associated CA-CDI increased significantly over time (13.1% in 2011 to 31.1% in 2019; p = 0.003). Dental patients had a lower comorbidity burden, with less frequent diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and proton pump inhibitor use. Amoxicillin-clavulanate was the most frequently prescribed antibiotic overall; clindamycin was more common among dental patients (39.9% vs. 11.9%), 79.7% of whom had no penicillin allergy. Severity and treatment duration were similar between groups.

CONCLUSION: Dental antibiotic prescribing emerged as an increasingly important contributor to CA-CDI, associated with higher clindamycin use despite a lower burden of traditional risk factors, highlighting the need to strengthen antimicrobial stewardship in dental practice.

articles.title: Arterial Hypertension and Kidney Function Decline in Systemic Sclerosis and Sjögren's Disease: A Longitudinal Comparative Study.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal involvement is increasingly recognized in Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Sjögren's Disease (SjD). However, the association between hypertension and renal function decline in these conditions remains poorly understood.

AIM: to compare renal function changes over time in patients with SSc and SjD; identify factors associated with clinically relevant renal function decline; and to evaluate whether the association between hypertension and renal function differs between the two diseases.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with SSc and SjD, followed for up to 3 years. Renal function was assessed using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Clinically relevant renal decline was defined as a reduction in eGFR ≥10 ml/min Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with renal function decline, including the interaction between diagnosis and hypertension.

RESULTS: A total of 238 patients were included (114 with SSc and 124 with SjD), with a median age of 55 years (IQR 45-65) in SSc and 57 years (IQR 48-66) in SjD. At baseline, SSc patients showed higher eGFR compared to SjD, but experienced a greater decline over time (median -6 vs -2.1 ml/min, p < 0.05). Overall, 33.8% of patients developed clinically significant renal decline. In multivariable analysis, hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline (OR 10.01, 95% CI 3.51-28.56, p < 0.001), whereas diagnosis was not. A significant interaction between diagnosis and hypertension was observed (OR 6.56, 95% CI 1.03-41.69, p = 0.046), indicating a stronger association between hypertension and renal function decline in SSc than in SjD. In subgroup analyses, hypertension was significantly associated with renal decline in SSc but not in SjD.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension was independently associated with renal function decline, with a stronger association in SSc than in SjD. These findings warrant confirmation in prospective studies. Systemic Sclerosis, Sjögren's disease, Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate; arterial hypertension.

articles.title: Dynamic risk assessment by landmark modeling of the restricted residual mean survival time.
articles.abstract: Dynamic risk assessment is an important tool for healthcare providers to inform treatment selection and optimize patient outcomes. Frequent evaluation of clinical status provides invaluable information on adverse event risk and/or treatment urgency, based on the changes in predictive biomarkers. Landmark analysis is a useful approach for dynamic risk assessment that obviates the complexity of jointly modeling longitudinal covariates and time-to-event outcome. Traditional landmark methods often rely on the proportional hazards assumption and assume independent censoring. We propose novel methods to broaden the scope of landmark analysis by directly modeling the restricted residual mean survival time (RRMST) at each landmark date while accommodating dependent censoring. Advantages of RMST models include removing the assumption that the (hazard) model is correct at every time point; RMST models instead consider a single capped survival time. Moreover, investigators may prefer the area under the survival curve to the hazard function as a metric in terms of interpretability. We derive the asymptotic properties of our proposed estimators and validate their performance in finite samples through extensive simulations. We apply the proposed methods to analyze outcomes under natural end-stage liver disease (ESLD) history (i.e., in the absence of liver transplantation).

articles.title: Impact of Fixed-Dose Combination Therapies on Cardiovascular Mortality and Major Cardiovascular Events.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Fixed-dose combination therapy (the polypill) was developed to reduce treatment complexity and improve adherence to evidence-based cardiovascular therapies. This review evaluates contemporary evidence for its effects on major cardiovascular events and cardiovascular mortality across primary prevention, secondary prevention, and emerging heart failure applications, while addressing implementation barriers and remaining evidence gaps.

RECENT FINDINGS: Early pharmacodynamic and adherence trials established that co-formulation preserves the effects of individual components and improves medication adherence.
