Event-powered trials subsequently demonstrated clinical benefit: PolyIran and TIPS-3 reduced major cardiovascular events in predominantly primary prevention population, whereas SECURE reduced recurrent events after myocardial infarction. Individual-participant and aggregate-data meta-analyses showed relative reductions of approximately 20% to 40% in composite cardiovascular outcomes and a reduction in cardiovascular mortality, with larger benefits among patients with greater adherence and in aspirin-containing strategies. POLY-HF extended the approach to heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, improving left ventricular ejection fraction and uptake of guideline-directed therapy; reductions in heart failure events were secondary findings that require confirmation in larger outcome trials. These findings supports fixed-dose combination therapy as an effective strategy for improving adherence and reducing cardiovascular events, with a cardiovascular mortality benefit supported by pooled analyses. Its greatest potential may be in high-risk populations and resource-limited settings, where treatment complexity impedes implementation. Broader adoption will require formulation standardization, sufficient dosing flexibility, longer-term safety data, and effective integration into clinical guidelines and health systems.

articles.title: Development, implementation and evaluation of a sustainable medication-use process in the intensive care unit: a lean-based quality improvement study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), substantial quantities of medication are wasted, negatively affecting ecological and economic sustainability.

AIM: This study aimed to develop, implement, and evaluate an ecologically and economically sustainable medication-use process to reduce medication waste in the ICU of a Dutch academic hospital.

METHOD: This lean-based quality improvement study comprised three phases: (I) Three-week baseline medication waste assessment in terms of quantity (i.e., disposed medication units) and economic value per 100 ICU beds per day. (II) Development and implementation of a sustainable medication-use process using lean principles. Causes of medication waste were identified among hospital staff using qualitative methods, and targeted interventions were identified and implemented accordingly. (III) Post-implementation effect evaluation of the sustainable medication-use process on medication waste.

RESULTS: At baseline, a mean total of 113 units, worth €1037, were wasted daily per 100 ICU beds. Causes for medication waste were: insufficient knowledge among hospital staff about quantities and impacts of medication waste; suboptimal medication ordering, supplying and preparing, resulting in unnecessary medication waste; and patient's therapy changes/discontinuation. Interventions implemented were: awareness campaigns on medication waste; adjustment of protocols and work processes to prevent excess order, supply and preparation of medication; and dispensing individually labelled medication to the patient following transfer or discharge. Implementing these interventions reduced medication waste by 31.8% to 77 units per 100 ICU beds per day, and economic losses decreased by 18.4% to €846.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of a sustainable medication-use process targeting staff's knowledge and work processes, reduced the extent of wasted medications in the ICU and associated costs.

articles.title: Performance of68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for Diagnosing Tumor Thrombus and Predicting Response to Pembrolizumab and Axitinib in Patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Pilot, Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the performance of 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT for diagnosing tumor thrombus (TT) and predicting response to pembrolizumab and axitinib in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with TT.

METHODS: We reviewed RCC patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT, mpMRI, and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. Diagnostic performance for detecting TT was analyzed, with TT confirmed by experienced pathologists. We further analyzed clear cell RCC (ccRCC) patients with TT who received pembrolizumab and axitinib and evaluated imaging features for predicting therapeutic efficacy by using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Model calibration was assessed with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test.

RESULTS: A total of 166 RCC patients were initially included, of whom 56 had TT. 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT showed higher overall diagnostic performance for TT than contrast-enhanced CT and mpMRI, with incremental detection primarily observed for Mayo level 0-I TT. The sensitivity and specificity of PET/CT in diagnosing TT were 0.96 (95% CI 0.88-0.99) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.92-0.99), respectively. Then, 35 ccRCC patients with TT underwent an average of 5 cycles of pembrolizumab and axitinib, followed by surgery. Following neoadjuvant therapy, 21 patients exhibited a partial response, while 14 showed nonresponse. TT SUVmax demonstrated significant predictive value for response to neoadjuvant therapy, with an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-0.92; bootstrap-corrected, 0.79). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (P > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT may provide incremental value for detecting low-level TT and shows potential for predicting response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in RCC. However, the clinical significance of detecting early TT remains uncertain.

articles.title: Computer tomography imaging for suspected acute aortic syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute Aortic Syndrome (AAS) is a life-threatening condition that presents diagnostic challenges due to variable clinical presentations. Limited data exists regarding Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) utilisation patterns and outcomes for patients with suspected AAS in Irish emergency departments (ED). This study evaluates trends in CTA utilisation and positivity rate for patients with suspected AAS presenting to a level 4 hospital ED.

METHODS: A retrospective single-centre chart review was conducted of all adult patients (≥ 16 years) who underwent CTA aorta imaging requested by emergency medicine physicians in Tallaght University Hospital between January 2018 and December 2025. Patient demographics, imaging findings, time metrics, disposition and mortality were analysed.

RESULTS: Among 457,735 ED attendances, 797 eligible CTA aorta studies were performed. There was a 2.86 fold increase in CTA scans done across the study period from 37 studies in 2018 to 106 in 2025. Overall positivity rate for AAS was 2.76% (n = 22). Acute aortic dissection accounted for 77% of positive cases (n = 17), followed by penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (n = 3) and intramural hematomas (n = 2). Overall mortality among patients with confirmed AAS was 27.27%.

CONCLUSION: This study highlights the low positivity rate of CTA aorta scans in an Irish ED but high mortality of patients diagnosed with acute aortic syndrome. Increasing CTA utilisation, alongside the overall low incidence of AAS, suggests opportunities to improve diagnostic efficiency.

articles.title: Anaplasma spp., Coxiella, Babesia and Theileria Infections in Vermipsylla Alakurt Fleas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vermipsylla alakurt (Siphonaptera: Vermipsyllidae) is mainly distributed in alpine areas of north-western China, infesting sheep, goat and yaks, causing pruritus, anaemia and losses to animal husbandry. The carriage of vector-borne pathogens by this flea remains unclear.

METHODS: In January 2025, 89 fleas were collected from sheep in the China-Kazakhstan border area of northwest China and identified as V. alakurt by morphology and COII gene sequencing. Multiple genetic markers targeting the genera of Anaplasma, Coxiella, Babesia and Theileria were amplified and sequenced.

RESULTS: Among 83 female fleas, Anaplasma ovis (n = 6), Coxiella burnetii (n = 37), Babesia sp. (n = 7), Babesia ovis (n = 1) and Theileria annulata (n = 4) were identified. The co-infection of Coxiella burnetii with Anaplasma ovis and Theileria annulata were respectively found.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple typical vector-borne pathogens were detected at the first time in V. alakurt fleas. This finding indicates that V. alakurt fleas can carry Anaplasma, Coxiella, Babesia and Theileria in the alpine region of the China-Kazakhstan border.

articles.title: [Specific respiratory tract infections in acute cough-when is targeted diagnosis and treatment required?].
articles.abstract: In most cases, acute cough is caused by a self-limiting respiratory infection. However, symptoms, pre-existing conditions, or environmental factors may indicate a cause requiring treatment; red flags point to dangerous courses, the NEWS2 score can assess the risk of septic deterioration, and the CRB-65 score supports decision-making regarding hospital admission in pneumonia. Pneumonia cannot be reliably diagnosed clinically but is unlikely in the absence of clinical indicators. Laboratory tests can support the decision for antibiotic treatment, while the diagnosis is confirmed by chest X‑ray. An infection-related exacerbation of pre-existing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) should be specifically treated. In influenza, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), complications and severe courses may occur more frequently in risk populations. However, routine diagnostic confirmation of these pathogens is not useful in the absence of therapeutic consequences. With appropriate exposure and waning vaccine protection, pertussis can also be a cause of acute cough in adults.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation: a systematic review of surgical techniques, donor safety, and recipient outcomes.
articles.abstract: Uterus transplantation (UTx) has emerged as a promising treatment for women with absolute uterine factor infertility (AUFI), enabling pregnancy and live birth with their own genetic offspring. Living-donor uterus procurement remains the most technically demanding component of the procedure. Robotic-assisted donor hysterectomy has been introduced to improve surgical precision, reduce donor morbidity, and preserve graft quality, while recipient implantation is performed via laparotomy. This systematic review evaluated current evidence on robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for UTx, focusing on surgical techniques, donor safety, recipient outcomes, and reproductive success. Databases and trial registries were searched from inception through June 2026. Six studies reporting 29 unique robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomies across five countries met the inclusion criteria. All procedures used the da Vinci Xi robotic platform. Operative time and estimated blood loss decreased with increasing surgical experience, while major donor complications (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher) were less frequent in later series. Among cases with reported follow-up, no graft loss was observed; restoration of menstruation, embryo transfer, clinical pregnancy, and live birth were achieved, including ten live births in the largest programme. Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation appears technically feasible and has been associated with viable grafts and successful pregnancies in highly selected cases. However, major donor complications, including ureteric injury requiring reimplantation and bilateral oophorectomy, were observed, and the true incidence of donor morbidity remains uncertain. Current evidence remains limited to small observational studies, and these findings support careful evaluation within structured, multidisciplinary programmes and international registries rather than widespread expansion.

articles.title: Levetiracetam versus valproate for new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety of levetiracetam versus valproate in children with new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing levetiracetam versus valproate in children (aged 0-18 years) with new-onset or previously treated but inadequately controlled epilepsy. Outcomes included seizure freedom, exploratory analyses of survival time without seizure and time to first seizure recurrence, change in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs involving 1,000 participants were included. Seizure freedom did not differ significantly between treatments (5 studies, 655 participants; RR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.83-1.09; P = 0.45; I² = 59.5%; low-certainty evidence). Exploratory time-related outcomes favored valproate but were limited by low-certainty evidence and inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was associated with lower AST levels, although this did not establish superior hepatic safety, and with fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain.

CONCLUSIONS: No significant difference in seizure freedom was detected between levetiracetam and valproate, although the low-certainty finding was sensitive to one trial. Time-related outcomes favored valproate but were exploratory and limited by inadequate handling of censoring. Levetiracetam was associated with fewer overall adverse events and less weight gain, while behavioral and hepatic safety remained uncertain. Treatment should be individualized based on patient and medication-related factors.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Influencing Factors of Drama-Based Interventions for Social Skills in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Research on child and adolescent psychopathology
articles.abstract: Deficits in social skills are a core challenge for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This meta-analysis examined the effects of drama-based interventions on social skills in this population and explored potential moderators. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, ProQuest, EBSCO, and CNKI. Overall effects were estimated using Hedges' g, and subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were conducted to examine heterogeneity. Publication bias and sensitivity analyses were also assessed. Sixteen controlled studies involving 703 participants contributed data to the meta-analysis. Drama-based interventions showed a significant medium effect on social skills (g = 0.54, 95% CI [0.21, 0.88], p = 0.002), with substantial heterogeneity (Q(15) = 62.59, p < 0.001; I² = 76.04%). Drama approach (Q(2) = 10.78, p = 0.005), intervention setting (Q(2) = 11.30, p = 0.010), and intervention agent (Q(2) = 6.64, p = 0.036) significantly moderated effects. Participant age was not a significant moderator, and dosage indicators were not significantly associated with effect sizes. These findings suggest that drama-based interventions may support social skills in autistic children and adolescents, with effects varying by intervention organization and delivery context.

articles.title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics for identifying high risk esophageal varices of bleeding in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC.

METHODS: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics.

CONCLUSION: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

articles.title: Development and external validation of a LASSO-based nomogram to predict epidural-associated postpartum urinary retention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate a risk prediction model for postpartum urinary retention (PUR) among parturients receiving epidural analgesia (EA) during vaginal delivery, to support individualized bladder management.

METHODS: This dual-center retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic medical records from two hospitals (2022-2024). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select independent predictors from demographic, labor, and analgesia-related variables. A clinical nomogram was developed. The model underwent internal and external validation; performance was assessed using calibration, discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Among 1019 parturients receiving EA (PUR incidence 16.09%), prolonged analgesia duration and prolonged second-stage labor were independently associated with PUR, whereas higher intermittent catheterization frequency (ICF) was associated with a lower rate of recorded PUR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination, satisfactory calibration, and clinical net benefit across validation cohorts.

CONCLUSION: The validated nomogram provides real-time, individualized estimates of PUR risk during late labor. By identifying parturients at elevated risk, it offers an evidence-based basis for risk-adaptive bladder monitoring and individualized care; however, whether such model-guided management ultimately reduces PUR incidence remains to be established in prospective interventional studies.

articles.title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio as a marker of major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study examined whether the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with major postoperative complications after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and whether this association differs from that of absolute ICU admission glucose.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 731 surgical episodes from 709 adults who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. SHR was calculated as the first ICU glucose divided by HbA1c-derived estimated average glucose. The primary outcome was an unweighted composite of 30-day mortality, stroke, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury, reoperation for bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and deep sternal wound infection. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinically relevant covariates.

RESULTS: The composite outcome occurred in 90 surgical episodes (12.3%). SHR was associated with the composite outcome after adjustment (odds ratio [OR], 1.103 per 0.1 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.008-1.208; P = 0.033), whereas ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated (OR, 1.019 per 10 mg/dL increase; 95% CI 0.946-1.096; P = 0.626).

CONCLUSION: SHR at ICU admission was associated with major postoperative complications in the primary analysis, whereas absolute ICU admission glucose was not significantly associated after multivariable adjustment. Confidence intervals for SHR included 1.0 in several sensitivity analyses. SHR warrants prospective evaluation as an early postoperative risk marker after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

articles.title: Neurosurgical manifestations and management of mucopolysaccharidoses: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS) represent a group of rare inherited lysosomal storage disorders, of which neurosurgical issues arise during childhood and adolescence. The literature however remains fragmented in terms of these specific outcomes. Correspondingly, we sought to synthesize a primer for neurosurgeons in regard to MPS, summarizing the neurosurgical manifestations and management reported in the contemporary literature. A systematic interrogation of the literature was performed according to PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched from inception through June 2026. Studies reporting hydrocephalus, craniovertebral junction (CVJ) abnormalities, spinal cord compression, myelopathy, spinal deformity, neurosurgical interventions, or related outcomes in patients with any MPS subtype were included and their findings aggregated. Seventy-eight studies comprising 983 patients with 37.8% females and mean age of 12.4 years were included. MPS I (34%), MPS II (31%), and MPS IV (26%) represented the majority of reported subtypes. A total of 819 patients (83%) exhibited neurosurgical manifestations. Spinal deformity (29%) and hydrocephalus (28%) were the most frequently reported manifestations, followed by spinal cord compression/myelopathy (22%) and CVJ pathology (20%). Distinct subtype-specific patterns were observed: spinal deformity predominated in MPS I (24%), hydrocephalus in MPS II (20%), and CVJ instability/compression in MPS IV (12%). Overall, hydrocephalus was surgically treated in 74% of instances, whereas CVJ and spinal cord pathology were surgically treated in 41% and 23% of instances respectively. Patients in studies who were not treated by any prior systemic therapy reported higher rates of surgical intervention compared to those who had received treatment. Neurosurgical manifestations occur in over four-fifths of MPS patients and are clinically significant across all types of MPS. Hydrocephalus, CVJ instability, spinal cord compression, and progressive spinal deformity represent the major surgical morbidities. Early recognition, structured imaging surveillance, and timely neurosurgical intervention are essential components of MPS management.

articles.title: Biochar mitigates microplastic- and nanoplastic-induced soil degradation and plant stress: a global meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Microplastic (MP) and nanoplastic (NP) contamination threatens soil functioning and plant performance, yet the effectiveness of biochar in mitigating these impacts varies substantially among experimental conditions. We conducted a meta-analysis of 59 peer-reviewed studies comprising 1418 effect-size estimates to quantify biochar-mediated responses across the soil-plant continuum. Effect sizes were calculated as the natural logarithm of the response ratio (lnRR) and analyzed using multilevel random-effects models. Subgroup analyses examined the effects of growth medium, plant functional group, plastic type, biochar feedstock, application rate, treatment duration, pyrolysis temperature, and experimental system, while meta-regression identified continuous moderators of response magnitude. Biochar produced positive pooled responses in soil properties (lnRR = 0.130), soil biological properties (0.186), biomass yield (0.218), photosynthetic performance (0.326), and plant nutrient content (0.599). Oxidative-damage indicators declined, including malondialdehyde (lnRR = - 0.154) and H2O2 (- 0.150), while plant microplastic accumulation showed a pronounced negative response (lnRR = - 0.811). The magnitude of these responses varied significantly among environmental and management contexts. Biochar application rate was the only significant continuous moderator, whereas pyrolysis temperature and treatment duration were not significant linear predictors of overall effect magnitude. Stronger responses in controlled systems than in more environmentally complex systems further indicated a potential gap between experimental efficacy and field-scale performance. Overall, the available evidence indicates that biochar is associated with improvements across multiple soil and plant response domains under MP/NP stress, although the magnitude of these responses is strongly context dependent. These findings provide a quantitative basis for developing context-specific biochar strategies while highlighting the need for geographically broader and long-term field validation.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory versus metabolic therapy in MASLD: a randomized clinical trial of aspirin and dapagliflozin using fibroscan outcomes.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major hepatic consequence of metabolic dysfunction, yet evidence-based pharmacologic options remain limited. Repurposing widely available agents with metabolic and anti-inflammatory actions may offer a clinically meaningful benefit. To compare the effects of aspirin and dapagliflozin on hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, liver enzymes, and lipid profile in patients with MASLD. In this prospective randomized interventional study, 80 adults with confirmed MASLD were allocated (1:1) to aspirin 100 mg once daily or dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily for 6 months (n = 40 per group). Baseline and 6-month measurements included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), total cholesterol, and FibroScan-derived parameters, including controlled attenuation parameter (CAP; dB/m), which quantifies hepatic steatosis, and liver stiffness measurement (LSM; kPa), a surrogate marker of liver fibrosis. The primary endpoints included the between-group differences in changes in LSM, CAP, liver enzymes, and lipid profile from baseline to 6 months. Ethics approval was obtained (FMBSUREC/04032025). The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07338331) on 20 Dec 2025. Dapagliflozin significantly improved hepatic steatosis, reflected by lower CAP values compared to aspirin (260.35 ± 20.78 vs 271.48 ± 12.58 dB/m; p = 0.005), and reduced total cholesterol levels (138.87 ± 54.70 vs 192.48 ± 79.46 mg/dL; p = 0.003). In contrast, aspirin demonstrated a greater reduction in liver stiffness (LSM) (6.15 ± 2.55 vs 8.58 ± 4.13 kPa; p = 0.002) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) percentage change (- 44.54% vs - 17.84%; p = 0.025). Other biochemical parameters showed no statistically significant between-group differences (all p > 0.05). Aspirin and dapagliflozin exert distinct and potentially complementary effects in MASLD, with dapagliflozin preferentially improving hepatic steatosis and aspirin showing a greater impact on fibrosis-related parameters. These findings support a dual-pathway therapeutic model targeting steatosis and fibrosis and underscore the need for larger trials evaluating combined strategies and histological outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of central nervous system Klebsiella pneumoniae infection: a focus on hypervirulent and classical strains.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of 20 cases of central nervous system (CNS) Klebsiella pneumoniae infection diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), and to compare the differences between classical Klebsiella pneumoniae (cKP) and hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) in central nervous system infections.

METHODS: Retrospective single-center study of 20 mNGS-diagnosed CNS K. pneumoniae infections (January 2022 - March 2026). Univariate analysis compared hvKP and cKP groups.

RESULTS: Among 20 patients, 19 were diagnosed by CSF mNGS and 1 by abscess fluid mNGS. The cKP group had a higher proportion of tumor history (P = 0.029) and a marginally higher rate of neurosurgery history (P = 0.082). Type 2 diabetes was common in both groups (66.7% vs. 62.5%). The hvKP group had higher rates of focal neurological deficits (77.8% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.015) and bacteremia/sepsis (66.7% vs. 37.5%, P = 0.009), while the cKP group had more delirium (62.5% vs. 11.1%, P = 0.050). CSF mNGS positivity (95%) surpassed culture (23.5%, P < 0.001). Radiologically, hvKP showed more brain abscesses (P = 0.015). hvKP had worse modified Rankin Scale scores (P = 0.002) and higher mortality (44.4% vs. 0%, P = 0.002). No cKP deaths occurred.

CONCLUSION: hvKP and cKP CNS infections differ significantly. hvKP is associated with community-onset severe disease (multiple brain abscesses, pyoventricle, focal deficits) and high mortality, while cKP links to nosocomial factors and better outcomes. mNGS is key for diagnosis, offering high CSF positivity and concurrent virulence/resistance profiling. Potential prognostic factors identified include high CSF mNGS reads, resistance genes, early liver abscess drainage, timely intravitreal injection, and combination therapy.

articles.title: Map-based cloning of the susceptibility locus conditioning bs6 resistance in pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) encoding mutant alleles of pseudokinase proteins.
articles.journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
articles.abstract: The bs6 resistance gene against bacterial spot was identified by map-based cloning in pepper (C. annuum L.). The recessive bs661 locus of pepper Capsicum annuum L. var. 61R (Ca61R) conditions a non-hypersensitive resistance trait, characterized by a slightly swollen, pale green, photosynthetically active leaf tissue, following Xanthomonas euvesicatoria Race 6 (XeR6) infection. In contrast, C. annuum cv. Feherozon (CaFo) is susceptible to XeR6. Map-based cloning of the bs661 locus revealed that the bs661 locus encodes three predicted proteins, pbs661npk, pbs661n, pbs661pk in Ca61R which are the counterpart of the three wild type predicted proteins, pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK in CaFo, respectively. Sequence analysis revealed that the pBs6FoNPK protein showed 35% identity and 53% similarity to the ZRK4 pseudokinase (pAtZRK4) identified in Arabidopsis thaliana, which possesses N-terminal and C-terminal (pseudokinase) domains. The pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK proteins resemble the N-terminal and C-terminal domains of the pBs6FoNPK protein, respectively, thus, they also contain pseudokinase domains/sequences. In Ca61R, pbs661npk and pbs661n are truncated counterparts of pBs6FoNPK and pBs6FoN, respectively, as a consequence of a single-nucleotide insertion that causes frameshifts and premature stop codons, whereas pbs661pk differs from pBs6FoPK by a single amino acid, a serine to alanine substitution at position 133. These three proteins are considered functionless. The ORF of pBs6FoN, pBs6FoPK and pbs661n, pbs661pk, respectively, are encoded by a single transcript in both parental plants. For this reason the translation of pBs6FoPK was ambiguous, however, the expression of pBs6FoN-dsRed fusion protein demonstrated that pBs6FoPK in fact can be translated. The three wild type proteins (pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN and pBs6FoPK) were independently responsible for ETS (effector-triggered susceptibility), because all three genes had to be in mutant configuration to manifest the resistant phenotype, in addition, any one of the three was able to reverse the resistant phenotype to susceptibility. Functional analysis using virus-induced gene silencing and transient genetic complementation demonstrated that the three CaFo proteins contribute redundantly to XeR6 susceptibility. Silencing either Bs6FoNPK, Bs6FoN and Bs6FoPK alone did not alter susceptibility, whereas simultaneous silencing of these genes conferred resistance. Conversely, the individual expression of pBs6FoNPK, pBs6FoN, and pBs6FoPK, in the resistant Ca61R background each restored susceptibility. These results demonstrate that the three Bs6 proteins act redundantly to promote XeR6 susceptibility and that loss of function of all three corresponding proteins was required for the recessive resistance phenotype conferred by bs661.

articles.title: Nationwide outcomes of biliary atresia after Kasai portoenterostomy in Taiwan: the impact of postoperative cholangitis and corticosteroid use.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide updated nationwide outcomes of biliary atresia (BA) among patients in Taiwan, focusing on postoperative cholangitis, liver transplantation (LT), corticosteroid use, and renal outcomes.

METHODS: Infants with BA who underwent Kasai portoenterostomy were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (2008-2019). Postoperative outcomes were evaluated, and the association between cholangitis episodes and LT was analyzed using exploratory logistic regression analysis. Corticosteroid exposure was categorized by duration, and acute kidney injury was assessed as a secondary outcome.

RESULTS: This study included 334 infants. Acute cholangitis occurred in 76.3% of cases, with 24.9% experiencing ≥ 5 hospitalizations. A greater number of cholangitis episodes was associated with a higher likelihood of LT (odds ratio: 1.08, 95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.16, p = 0.044). Approximately 30.8% of patients developed biliary cirrhosis, and 33.8% received LT. Corticosteroids were prescribed to 96% of patients, and a longer treatment duration was associated with higher complication rates. About 1.8% of patients developed acute kidney injury, with no progression to end-stage renal disease.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative cholangitis remains an important clinical factor associated with LT in infants with BA. Corticosteroid treatment duration may reflect underlying disease severity rather than therapeutic benefit. Renal complications are uncommon. Optimizing postoperative care-particularly timely cholangitis management-is essential to improve outcomes.

articles.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Sequencing Identifies Altered Expression of Circadian Rhythm-Related Genes Pomc and Bmp4 in Post-Stroke Depression.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a serious complication that significantly hinders stroke patients' recovery and quality of life. Uncovering the molecular changes that drive PSD is vital for understanding how depression develops following a stroke. In this study, we established a reproducible PSD model using minimally invasive photochemical-induced focal cortical lesion. Transcriptomic sequencing demonstrated that dysregulation of circadian entrainment genes is a central pathway in the development of post-stroke depressive-like behaviors. Protein-protein interaction network analysis of these circadian rhythm-related genes identified six hub genes. Four of these, including Pomc and Bmp4, exhibited expression patterns consistent with experimental validation. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis further pinpointed cell-type-specific expression abnormalities of Pomc in endothelial cells and Bmp4 in oligodendrocytes. Subsequently, in silico perturbation analysis further indicated that their shared underlying regulatory mechanisms involve cell adhesion and extracellular matrix interaction. Collectively, using transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing in a PSD model, this study revealed altered expression patterns of circadian rhythm-related genes, providing potential targets for further investigation into the pathogenesis of PSD.

articles.title: Exploring shared genetic architecture in psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis: a multi-method approach.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are immune-mediated diseases that co-occur clinically, but their shared genetic architecture and the direction of shared effects remain debated. We integrated genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from FinnGen and UK Biobank using linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC), high-definition likelihood (HDL), ρ-HESS, MTAG, CPASSOC, colocalization, and MAGMA. The primary cross-population analysis showed a negative global genetic correlation (LDSC unconstrained: rg = - 0.3004, P = 6.70 × 10⁻³; constrained: rg = - 0.2251, P = 3.00 × 10⁻⁴; HDL: rg = - 0.3307, P = 1.14 × 10⁻³). Ancestry-matched sensitivity analyses produced positive but heterogeneous estimates (FinnGen: rg = 0.2422 to 0.6334; UK Biobank: rg = 0.1294 to 0.3777) that were not uniformly significant. Cross-trait analyses identified 95 independent SNPs and 10 additional shared loci. After allele harmonization, all 10 loci showed opposite MTAG effect directions for psoriasis and RA (two-sided exact binomial P = 1.95 × 10⁻³), indicating directional heterogeneity and possible antagonistic pleiotropy. Colocalization provided evidence for a shared causal signal at two TYK2 variants, rs11085727 and rs144309607 (PP.H4 > 0.8; r² = 0.0805 and D' = 1.0), although these results should be interpreted cautiously because they may reflect distinct correlated variants. MAGMA identified immune-related tissue enrichment for psoriasis but not RA. Collectively, these findings indicate that psoriasis and RA share genetic loci, but the global direction of genetic correlation is ancestry- and data-source-dependent and that locus-level effects include opposing directions. TYK2 remains a plausible shared target, but its therapeutic implications require direction-aware fine-mapping and functional validation.

articles.title: Insulin Resistance Markers Predict New-Onset Diabetes in Middle-Aged and Elderly Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insulin resistance (IR) is central to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, but the best IR-related marker for identifying CKM patients at high risk of diabetes remains uncertain. This study examined associations between IR-related markers and new-onset diabetes and compared their predictive performance.

METHODS: We analyzed 6,307 CKM participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and 6,388 from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess associations of triglyceride-glucose (TyG), TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), metabolic score for IR (METS-IR), and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) with diabetes. Subgroup analyses and receiver operating characteristic curves were employed to evaluate robustness and discrimination.

RESULTS: Over 7 years, diabetes developed in 736 CHARLS participants (11.67%) and 1,451 NHANES participants (22.71%). Five IR-related markers were significantly associated with the risk of diabetes and demonstrated good predictive performance. Elevated levels of TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WHtR, and METS-IR, as well as lower levels of eGDR, were associated with increased diabetes risk (all P < 0.001). Most associations remained robust across subgroup analyses. Among the five markers, eGDR demonstrated the highest predictive performance in the NHANES cohort (AUC: 0.789; 95% CI: 0.776-0.802) and showed favorable predictive ability in the CHARLS cohort.

CONCLUSION: IR-related markers are significantly associated with the risk of diabetes in individuals with CKM syndrome and serve as reliable predictors of new-onset diabetes. Among these indicators, eGDR and TyG-WHtR were relatively reliable predictors, highlighting their potential as valuable tools for early diabetes screening.

articles.title: Cellular senescence and the SASP in the oral-metabolic axis: a putative link between periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic inflammatory disorders with a bidirectional clinical association. Although microbial, immune, and metabolic mechanisms contribute to this relationship, they do not fully explain the persistence of inflammation and defective tissue repair. Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) may provide an additional framework for understanding this interaction. Within periodontal tissues, sustained microbial and metabolic stress may promote senescence-associated changes that disturb local immune regulation, tissue regeneration and bone homeostasis. These processes could interact with microbial dysbiosis and systemic inflammation as part of the oral-metabolic axis. However, the available evidence remains uneven. Diabetes-related stress can promote senescence-like changes in periodontal tissues, whereas direct evidence that periodontal senescence impairs distant metabolic organs is limited. This review examines the evidence linking cellular senescence to periodontal inflammation and T2DM, and discusses the emerging preclinical evidence for targeting senescent cells and the SASP.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of adult patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases coexisting with persistent isolated low IgM: a retrospective study in China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Selective IgM deficiency (sIgMD) is an uncommon immunological phenotype characterized by persistently reduced serum IgM, but its characteristics within autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARDs) remain poorly defined, particularly in Chinese populations. This study aimed to characterize a persistent isolated low IgM phenotype compatible with sIgMD from an ARD-centered perspective, focusing on its clinical features, and infection spectrum in a cohort of 257 patients.

METHODS: A retrospective study of adult inpatients diagnosed with both ARDs and persistent isolated low IgM was conducted. Data on demographics, ARD types, infections, treatments, and laboratory parameters were collected and analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 257 adult patients with ARDs and coexisting persistent isolated low IgM were included. The median age was 48 (35-60) years, with a female predominance (203/257, 79.0%). Systemic lupus erythematosus was the most common underlying ARD (138/257, 53.7%), followed by primary Sjögren's syndrome (51/257, 19.8%) and rheumatoid arthritis (16/257, 6.2%). Pneumonia was the most frequently observed infection type (125/257, 48.6%). Among the 257 patients, 39 (15.2%) had persistent isolated low IgM identified before exposure to immunosuppressive therapy (treatment-naïve patients), whereas 218 (84.8%) had received immunosuppressive treatment before low IgM was first documented. Overall, 40 of the 257 patients (15.6%) had documented use of intravenous immunoglobulin. Compared with treated patients, treatment-naïve patients had shorter disease duration (72 months vs. 108 months, P = 0.006) and higher IgG (15.0 vs. 12.0 g/L) and IgA (3.0 g/L vs. 2.1 g/L) levels (both P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that older age was associated with a higher likelihood of documented infection (OR = 1.049, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: This study provided a comprehensive characterization of persistent isolated low IgM in Chinese adults with ARDs. Our findings suggest that this phenotype may not be solely attributable to immunosuppressive treatment and highlight the need for further studies to clarify its underlying mechanisms and clinical significance, particularly in relation to infection. Key Points • This is the first ARD-centered study to systematically characterize persistent isolated low IgM and represents the largest clinical cohort reported to date. • Persistent isolated low IgM was observed across multiple autoimmune rheumatic diseases and was identified before immunosuppressive therapy in a subset of patients. • Older age was independently associated with documented infection in patients with ARDs and persistent isolated low IgM.

articles.title: Pancreatic stone protein versus conventional biomarkers for prognostic discrimination in sepsis: a meta-analysis of paired AUC comparisons.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic stone protein (PSP) has been proposed as a prognostic biomarker in sepsis, but its comparative performance versus C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of direct within-study paired AUC comparisons between PSP and CRP and/or PCT in critically ill adults with sepsis, septic shock, or acute infection-related conditions in whom sepsis development or clinically relevant adverse outcomes were prospectively evaluated. Differences in AUC (ΔAUC) were pooled using random-effects models. The principal conservative analysis included one comparison per independent cohort and comparator.

RESULTS: Seven studies comprising 803 unique participants contributed 21 paired comparisons. In the principal conservative analysis, PSP showed a higher prognostic AUC than CRP, with a pooled ΔAUC of 0.179 (95% CI 0.095-0.262; p < 0.001), although between-cohort heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 81.65%). Compared with PCT, the pooled ΔAUC was 0.153 (95% CI 0.114-0.193; p < 0.001), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%). The mortality-only sensitivity analysis showed a similar pooled effect for PSP versus CRP (ΔAUC 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.26), with substantial heterogeneity persisting, and for PSP versus PCT (ΔAUC 0.153, 95% CI 0.114-0.193), with no observed heterogeneity. Exclusion of the clinically distinct intra-abdominal infection cohort (Michailides et al.) likewise did not materially change the PSP-versus CRP estimate (ΔAUC 0.166, 95% CI 0.077-0.256). The direction and approximate magnitude of the pooled effects were also preserved across alternative assumptions for the within-study correlation.

CONCLUSIONS: Available comparative evidence suggests that PSP may have greater prognostic discrimination than CRP and PCT. The findings were broadly maintained across sensitivity analyses, but the limited number of independent cohorts and substantial heterogeneity in the CRP comparison warrant caution. Further prospective studies are required to confirm these findings and establish their clinical relevance.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261340301).

articles.title: Later-line Treatment Selection in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Trifluridine/Tipiracil Plus Bevacizumab, Regorafenib, and Fruquintinib.
articles.abstract: Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. This narrative review updates pivotal and recent evidence and proposes an evidence-informed framework that treats hematologic reserve as a clinical fitness construct rather than a fixed laboratory threshold. We additionally examine the clinical implications of low response rates, prior anti-angiogenic exposure, emerging molecular predictors including KRAS G12, evidence in older or vulnerable patients, and recent phase III developments. Current data do not support a validated molecular biomarker for choosing among these three options, and no randomized head-to-head comparison of regorafenib and fruquintinib exists. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

articles.title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
articles.abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

articles.title: Investigation of the most suitable 3D printing method and tissue equivalent materials for mimicking glandular-adipose tissues for production of breast phantom.
articles.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
articles.abstract: In this study, the usability of masked stereolithography (MSLA) and fused filament fabrication (FFF) type printers to produce breast phantom is investigated. ABS, PET, PLA+, PVA and TPU-95 A filaments are used on FFF type printer with infill ratios between 70 and 100%; ABS-like, PLA and PMMA-like resins are used on SLA type printer with infill ratio 100% to tissue equivalent materials. The materials' CT scans are taken at 80, 100 and 120 kVp and the Hounsfield Units (HU) dependency on the infill ratio for each filament and resin is investigated. The materials' physical densities are measured; electron densities and effective atomic numbers are calculated. The suitability of the materials for mimicking adipose, glandular and skin tissue investigated in terms of HU value, physical density, electron density and effective atomic number. It is found that MSLA type printer is not eligible for printing breast tissue equivalent materials as the common resins have higher physical density and it is not possible to lower physical density by infill ratio. However, FFF type printer technology is more eligible for mimicking breast tissue. While ABS is suitable only for mimicking adipose tissue, PET, PLA+, PVA and TPU-95 A filaments can be used to produce adipose, glandular and skin tissues by just changing infill ratio. For production of a breast phantom via FFF printing, PET and PVA among the tested filament materials are preferable over the properties of PLA + and TPU-95 A due to their proper hydrogen(H) and carbon contents (C), and other physical and radiological properties.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Therapy for Gastric Adenocarcinoma with Signet Ring Cells: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Signet ring cell-containing gastric cancer constitutes an increasingly recognized subtype. Although perioperative chemotherapy is the standard of treatment for locally advanced gastric cancer, its efficacy in signet ring cell-containing gastric adenocarcinomas remains controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to assess the impact of neoadjuvant chemotherapy compared to upfront surgery on overall survival.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane was conducted up to January 2026. Eligible studies included adult patients with signet ring cell-containing gastric cancer undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery compared to upfront gastrectomy. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool hazard ratios for overall survival.

RESULTS: Six studies, including seven cohorts and 5.388 patients, were included. The pooled analysis demonstrated no significant difference in overall survival between neoadjuvant chemotherapy and upfront surgery (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.68-1.34, I2 = 83.2%). Subgroup analyses by studies' geographic origin and design revealed consistent results with no significant differences in overall survival among Western (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.53-1.38, I² = 86.9%) or Eastern studies (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.63-1.97, I² = 83%), and among different study designs (randomized controlled trial: HR 1.16, 95% CI 0.81-1.67; observational: HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.62-1.38, I² = 85.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was not associated with a significant improvement in overall survival compared with upfront surgery in signet-ring cell-containing gastric cancer. While perioperative chemotherapy remains the recommended therapeutic approach, further studies employing contemporary chemotherapy regimens are warranted to define its role in this distinct histological subtype.

articles.title: Epidemiological Evolution of HIV in Pakistan (1987-2026): From High-risk Populations to Emerging Pediatric Cases.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This narrative review examines the evolving epidemiology of HIV in Pakistan from 1987 to 2026, focusing on temporal trends among key populations, geographic hotspots, emerging pediatric infections, and health-system gaps affecting epidemic control.

RECENT FINDINGS: Evidence indicates a persistent concentrated epidemic, with the highest burden among people who inject drugs and continuing transmission among sex workers, transgender populations, and prisoners. HIV transmission remains geographically heterogeneous, with major urban hotspots in Karachi and cities across Punjab. Recent pediatric outbreaks have introduced an important healthcare-associated dimension, with unsafe medical practices and weaknesses in infection prevention and control emerging as major concerns. Pakistan's HIV epidemic remains concentrated but is becoming increasingly complex. Persistent transmission among key populations, geographic expansion, pediatric infections, and substantial gaps in diagnosis, treatment, and viral suppression highlight the need for strengthened surveillance, prevention, infection control, and continuity of HIV care.

articles.title: Neonatal gastric perforation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical characteristics, risk factors, surgical management and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal gastric perforation (NGP) is a rare but life-threatening surgical emergency of the newborn. We systematically reviewed its clinical characteristics, risk factors, surgical management and outcomes.

METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to 31 December 2025 for observational studies reporting at least five neonates (≤ 28 days) with confirmed gastric perforation. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and appraised quality. Proportions were pooled using random-effects models; predictors of mortality were summarised as odds ratios (OR). The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO).

RESULTS: Twenty studies (410 neonates) were included. Pooled prevalences were prematurity 58.3%, low birth weight 63.5% and male sex 59.0%; abdominal distension (90.5%) and pneumoperitoneum (80.9%) were the commonest features. Primary repair was performed in 78.4% of operated neonates. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 28.6% (95% CI 22.0-36.3%). Sepsis at presentation (OR 4.10) and delay to surgery beyond 24 h (OR 3.55) were the strongest predictors of death.

CONCLUSIONS: NGP mainly affects premature, low-birth-weight neonates, and still carries approximately 28% mortality. Early recognition, prompt treatment of sepsis and timely surgery offer the clearest route to improved survival.

PROSPERO ID: CRD420261436438.

articles.title: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma: From pathogenesis to therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma (PCAS) is a rare yet highly aggressive malignancy arising from cardiac vascular endothelial cells. This tumor predominantly affects young to middle-aged males and carries a dismal prognosis, typically characterized by a median survival of less than one year. Owing to its nonspecific manifestations and rapid infiltrative growth, most patients present at an advanced or metastatic stage. Recent genomic and transcriptomic studies have revealed molecular drivers in PCAS, including recurrent mutations in POT1, KDR/VEGFR2, and PLCG1, loss of CDKN2A, and aberrant angiogenic cascade activation. In parallel, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by exhausted T cells and tumor-associated macrophages may collectively contribute to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Multimodal imaging, integrating echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, computed tomography, and PET/CT, plays a central role in detection, tissue characterization, and systemic staging. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry remains the diagnostic gold standard. Current treatment strategies rely on multimodal approaches, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, with emerging targeted therapies and immunotherapies under active investigation. Despite recent advances, clinical outcomes remain poor, highlighting the urgent need for improved mechanistic understanding and more effective personalized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Lyme Disease and Other Tick-Borne Infections.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The neurologic manifestations of selected tick-transmitted infections in North America and Eurasia were reviewed.

RECENT FINDINGS: Both Powassan virus in North America, and Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE) virus in Eurasia can cause encephalitis, often with significant neurologic morbidity. Lyme disease, Ehrlichia chaffeensis (the cause of human monocytic ehrlichiosis [HME]), and Borrelia miyamotoi infections can cause meningitis (the third primarily in immunocompromised individuals). Patients with Lyme disease may also develop cranial neuropathy, and/or radiculoneuropathy. Tick-borne infections are being increasingly recognized in North America and Eurasia. While many tick-borne infections can cause headaches, lethargy or other non-specific symptoms, these are generally not evidence of nervous system infection - i.e., neuroinvasive disease. The latter is less common but may occur in infections due to Powassan and TBE viruses, in HME and in Lyme disease. Patients with symptomatic nervous system infection due to Powassan or TBE virus are at high risk of developing significant neurologic impairment and sequelae.

articles.title: Modulating the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 Pathway: Acupuncture's Therapeutic Potential in Mitigating Muscle Hypertonia in Ischemic Stroke Rats.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of acupuncture on post-stroke muscle hypertonia (PSMH) in rats, focusing on the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway to elucidate its underlying mechanisms and support clinical translation. Behavioral, electrophysiological, TTC staining, AChE staining, and transmission electron microscope analyses were used to assess the efficacy of acupuncture. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunofluorescence were used to evaluate the expression of the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway. Pharmacological modulation using WNK463 and Gabazine suggested the involvement of WNK kinase activity. Acupuncture reduced neurological deficits and spasticity, enhanced motor recovery, suppressed spinal motor neuron hyperexcitability, and ameliorated neuromuscular dysfunction and muscular structural abnormality. Mechanistically, it downregulated WNK1, SPAK, and OSR1 and increased membrane KCC2 expression in the medulla oblongata. WNK463 partially mimicked acupuncture's effects, while Gabazine partially reversed them. Acupuncture alleviates muscle hypertonia and enhances locomotor recovery in rats with PSMH, potentially by inhibiting the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1 pathway and thereby upregulating KCC2 expression and membrane localization.

articles.title: Comparative perioperative and oncological outcomes of the da Vinci Xi versus Si robotic surgical systems in rectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The da Vinci Xi replaced the Si with a boom-mounted architecture intended to remove the re-docking and multiquadrant limits on pelvic access. Whether it changes outcomes in rectal cancer surgery is unresolved: existing syntheses pooled rectal with colonic resection. Five databases, Google Scholar and citation graphs were searched to August 2026, without language or design restriction, for comparative studies reporting outcomes separately by platform in rectal cancer resection. Screening, extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were done in duplicate. Random-effects models with a Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used; certainty was rated with GRADE. Eight non-randomised cohorts (843 patients; 380 Xi, 463 Si) were included. Pooling all five cohorts reporting operative time, the mean difference was - 27.7 min (95% confidence interval - 80.4 to + 25.0; I² 95%); restricted to the four reporting means with standard deviations, thus conditional on excluding the largest cohort, it was - 50.6 min (- 69.4 to - 31.7). Docking time was shorter with the Xi in all three reporting cohorts, which defined it differently or not at all. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of platform on anastomotic leak (risk ratio 0.53, 0.24 to 1.14), complications, conversion, reoperation, margin involvement and specimen quality; certainty was very low throughout. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of the da Vinci Xi compared with the Si on perioperative and oncological outcomes in rectal cancer, and functional outcomes have not been compared. Because the platforms were compared across periods, centres and levels of experience, no estimate isolates the platform.PROSPERO registration CRD420261480007, registered 18 August 2026, before data extraction.

articles.title: First molecular characterization of Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto genotype G1 from a common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) in the Kuwait Zoo.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cystic echinococcosis (CE) is a cosmopolitan parasitic zoonosis with public health and economic significance. In this study, we report CE in uncommon host, a chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) in the Kuwait Zoo with description of clinical and pathological findings.

METHODS: In September 2025, a 32-year-old adult female common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) died at the zoo of Kuwait after showing severe symptoms. Post-mortem examination revealed a handball-sized cyst embedded in the hepatic umbilical fissure, causing lesions. The content of the cyst was examined microscopically as well as by sequencing of the mitochondrial nad1 gene from one of the clonal protoscoleces found in the cyst.

RESULTS: The cyst proved to be Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto, genotype G1. The clinical case of the infection is described in detail. DNA sequence was nearly identical to sequences of G1 genotype of E. granulosus available in GenBank.

CONCLUSIONS: This report of CE in a chimpanzee in the zoo highlights the problem related to environmental contamination. The implication of dogs in environmental contamination and other aspects of CE epidemiology in Kuwait is discussed. This is the first report of genetically identified hydatid cyst of E. granulosus sensu stricto in Kuwait and the first genetically confirmed case of the genotype G1 in chimpanzee.

articles.title: Three dimensional reconstruction guided anatomical regional resection versus segmentectomy for congenital pulmonary airway malformation in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare CT-based three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction-guided anatomical regional resection with segmentectomy in children with congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 127 children treated between July 2023 and March 2025: 59 underwent 3D-guided anatomical regional resection and 68 underwent segmentectomy. Perioperative outcomes were compared; 119 children underwent chest CT at 1 year.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences between the two groups in the characteristics related to the disease such as the type of lesion, the number of involved lung segments, the distribution of involved lung lobes, and the preoperative infection status. Regional resection was associated with shorter chest tube duration (2.2 ± 1.4 vs. 4.1 ± 1.3 days; P < 0.001) and hospital stay (5.0 ± 1.3 vs. 5.5 ± 1.4 days; P = 0.039). Operative time, postoperative complication rates, and CT findings of atelectasis or hyperinflation did not differ significantly. No residual CPAM was detected on 1-year CT in either group among the 119 children imaged.

CONCLUSION: In selected children with CPAM, 3D-guided anatomical regional resection was feasible and was associated with shorter chest tube duration and hospital stay than segmentectomy. Anatomical resection guided by ct three-dimensional reconstruction makes anatomical lesion resection and lung preservation possible in children with CPAM.

articles.title: Coagulation and fibrinolysis markers at birth as early predictors of surgical necrotizing enterocolitis in extremely low-birth-weight infants.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early identification of surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (S-NEC) before clinical deterioration remains challenging in extremely low-birth-weight infants (ELBWIs). We evaluated whether coagulation and fibrinolysis markers at birth could predict subsequent S-NEC.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 250 ELBWIs (< 1000 g) treated from 2013 to 2022; 22 developed S-NEC. Eleven coagulation and fibrinolysis markers were measured within 24 h of birth. Multivariable logistic regression models and a simple birth-time risk score were developed.

RESULTS: Relative to controls, S-NEC infants had higher D-dimer (11.7 vs. 5.5 µg/mL, p = 0.003) and PT-INR (1.71 vs. 1.42, p = 0.023), prolonged PT (62.2 vs. 52.7 s, p = 0.022), and lower fibrinogen (107.3 vs. 160.7 mg/dL, p = 0.037). Multivariable models showed stepwise improvement in discrimination (AUC 0.668, 0.710, 0.763). A four-item risk score (D-dimer > 5 µg/mL, PT-INR > 1.5, fibrinogen < 100 mg/dL, and birth weight < 700 g) achieved an AUC of 0.702, with 85.0% sensitivity and 96.3% negative predictive value (NPV). S-NEC incidence increased across risk categories (3.7%, 14.5%, and 19.6%; p for trend = 0.013).

CONCLUSIONS: Hemostatic abnormalities at birth were associated with subsequent S-NEC in ELBWIs, suggesting perinatal or intrauterine origins. The risk score showed a high NPV and may serve as a practical rule-out tool for early neonatal intensive care unit stratification.

articles.title: The urinary microbiome after paediatric bladder augmentation: a scoping review with comparative insights from adult urinary diversion surgeries.
articles.abstract: Bladder augmentation is a lifelong reconstructive procedure for children with severe lower urinary tract dysfunction, but recurrent urinary tract infection, urolithiasis and mucus-related complications remain incompletely understood. This scoping review mapped evidence on the urinary microbiome after paediatric bladder augmentation and assessed transferable insights from adult bowel-derived urinary diversion. A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science identified peer-reviewed studies and conference abstracts published from January 2016 to April 2026 that used culture-independent sequencing. Seven studies were included: two paediatric and five adult, comprising three cross-sectional studies, two reports from one prospective cohort and two case reports. Paediatric studies reported contrasting enteric-dominant and native-bladder-like communities, with no consistent clinical associations. Adult studies more consistently suggested time-dependent restructuring, reservoir-specific microbial patterns and fungal involvement, although associations with urinary tract infection remained inconsistent. The paediatric evidence is insufficient to define microbiome composition, temporal behaviour or clinical significance after augmentation. Adult findings primarily provide a methodological template for future prospective, longitudinal, within-patient paediatric studies incorporating standardised urine and mucosal sampling, bacterial and fungal sequencing, metabolomics and predefined clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Effects of resistance training on subjective sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a secondary analysis from a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Dos Santos de Oliveira Silva NS
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to verify the effect of eight weeks of resistance training (RT) on subjective sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and quality of life in adults with OSA.

METHODS: In this randomized controlled clinical trial, 25 adults with moderate to severe OSA (age: 54.6 ± 7.2 years; BMI: 36.1 ± 7.9 kg/m²; apnea-hypopnea index: 52.2 ± 27.4 events/hour) were included. Participants were randomized into an RT group (three sessions per week) or a control group [CG (two sessions per week)]. Sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), SF-36, respectively. Generalized estimated equations verified differences between groups over time.

RESULTS: Differences were observed in domains sleep latency (RT: Δ -1.0 ± 0.3 vs. CG: 0.2 ± 0.2; p = 0.018), sleep duration (RT: Δ -0.6 ± 0.3 vs. CG: -0.2 ± 0.2; p = 0.012), sleeping medication (RT: Δ -0.2 ± 0.1 vs. CG: 0.8 ± 0.3; p = 0.007), and overall PSQI score (RT: Δ -3.2 ± 0.6 vs. CG: 0.2 ± 0.8; p = 0.004). Regarding SF-36, differences were found in emotional aspects (RT: Δ 29.6 ± 14.8 vs. CG: -17.9 ± 10.0; p = 0.008) and global score (RT: Δ 10.8 ± 3.3 vs. CG: -3.4 ± 3.1; p = 0.002) were observed. No difference was observed in ESS.

CONCLUSION: An eight-week RT program improves subjective sleep quality and quality of life in adults with moderate to severe OSA. Clinical trial registration (Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry [ReBec]): # RBR-2rg97kz. Date of registration: 01/17/2025.

articles.title: Ciliated hepatic foregut cyst in children and adolescents: a systematic review of clinical presentation, diagnosis, management, and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Ciliated hepatic foregut cyst (CHFC) is a rare congenital cystic liver lesion described predominantly in adults, in whom malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma has been reported. Pediatric experience is scattered across case reports and small series, and no systematic synthesis has been published. We conducted a systematic review per PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase (Elsevier) were searched on 3 August 2026 without language or date restrictions, supplemented by citation searching and grey-literature screening (JMIR Preprints, bioRxiv, medRxiv). We included case reports and case series of patients aged ≤ 19 years with histopathologically confirmed CHFC. Screening (Rayyan) and extraction were performed in independent duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklists. Findings were synthesised descriptively per SWiM; no meta-analysis was performed. Sixteen studies contributed 23 unique pediatric patients (female-to-male ratio 1.3:1; median age 4.0 years, range 5 months-19 years). Antenatal detection occurred in 5 (21.7%) of 23. Symptomatic presentation was reported in 14 (60.9%) of 23. Median cyst size was 6.0 cm (range 0.6-19.3), and 4 patients (17.4%) had giant cysts (≥ 10 cm). Segment IV was involved in 11 of 19 patients with location reported (57.9%). Biliary communication was documented in 5 of 14 evaluable cases (35.7%; 5/23 overall); 4 of these patients underwent Roux-en-Y biliary reconstruction. Squamous metaplasia was reported in 4 of 7 evaluable cases (57.1%; 4/23 overall). No dysplasia (0/7 evaluable) and no malignant transformation (0/22 evaluable) were reported. Postoperative complications occurred in 2 (8.7%) of 23. No recurrence (0/11 evaluable) or mortality (0/23) was reported over a median 19-month follow-up (reported for 8 patients). Pediatric CHFC appears to present more often with symptomatic, larger and biliary-communicating lesions than the classical adult phenotype. Complete excision was associated with favorable reported short-term outcomes, but the evidence is of very low certainty, and limited follow-up and substantial non-reporting preclude conclusions about long-term recurrence or malignant transformation.

articles.title: Bidirectional Regulatory Mechanisms of T cell-microglia Interactions in Cerebral Ischemic Disease: Molecular Crosstalk, Experimental Techniques and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemic diseases, such as ischemic stroke (IS) and vascular dementia (VaD), are major causes of neurological disability and mortality. Neuroinflammation acts as a pivotal driver of secondary brain injury, mediated by intricate bidirectional interactions between peripheral T cells and central nervous system (CNS)-resident microglia. This review delineates the molecular mechanisms underlying T cell-microglia crosstalk in cerebral ischemia, emphasizing their dual roles in exacerbating neurotoxicity and promoting repair. Direct interactions involve antigen presentation via MHC-TCR engagement and co-stimulatory checkpoints (e.g., CD80/CD86-CD28, PD-L1-PD-1), which regulate T cell activation and microglial polarization. Direct signaling through cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17, IL-10) further modulates microglial phenotypes: Th1/Th17 cells drive pro-inflammatory M1 polarization via STAT1/NF-κB pathways, while Tregs/Th2 cells induce anti-inflammatory M2 states through STAT6/SMAD signaling. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell omics reveal spatiotemporal dynamics of these interactions, identifying STAT1/STAT6 imbalance as a critical determinant of neuroinflammatory outcomes. Advanced methodologies, including two-photon intravital microscopy and microfluidic blood-brain barrier (BBB) models, enable real-time visualization of immune cell trafficking and synaptic communication. Therapeutically, targeting immune checkpoints (CTLA-4, PD-1) or cytokine pathways (e.g., IL-4 mimetics) shows promise in recalibrating neuroimmune responses. However, challenges such as blood-brain barrier impermeability to biologics and interspecies immune heterogeneity necessitate innovative delivery strategies. This review integrates molecular, cellular, and technological insights to propose a framework for precision immunomodulation. By elucidating context-dependent signaling nodes and leveraging emerging tools, the study underscores the potential of harnessing T cell-microglia crosstalk to mitigate neuroinflammation and enhance neural repair, offering transformative avenues for stroke and dementia therapy.

articles.title: Incidence of intra-axial brain metastases in Eastern Finland.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Brain metastases (BM) incidence and characteristics remain poorly defined due to registry data being often incomplete, recording only primary tumors or unspecified metastases. The objective of this study was to examine BM incidence rates and characteristics confirmed by MRI in North Savo, Finland.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, North Savo residents with first MRI diagnosis of BM between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 were identified through the radiology information system, irrespective of primary cancer diagnosis date. Medical and histopathological records were reviewed. Population person-years were estimated by summing annual end-year counts of all North Savo residents obtained from Statistics Finland. Crude incidence rates and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), standardized to the 2013 European Standard population, were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using age-adjusted Poisson regression.

RESULTS: Among 516 patients, 474 had histopathological verification. Cancers originating from lung and breast tissue accounted for 56.8% of BM cases. Overall crude incidence was 10.22 (95% CI 9.36-11.15) and ASIR was 9.20 (95% CI 8.42-10.04) per 100,000 person years. ASIR increased from 5.8 in 2004-2008 to 11.8 in 2019-2023. Age-adjusted Poisson regression estimated a 24% increase in incidence per five-year period (incidence rate ratio 1.24; 95% CI 1.14-1.34; P < 0.001). Age-specific incidence peaked at 33.1 per 100,000 person years among patients aged 70-74 years.

CONCLUSIONS: MRI-confirmed BM incidence increased over 20 years, despite age standardization. Incidence was highest among older adults. These findings provide contemporary population-based epidemiological data of BM incidence.

articles.title: Application of machine learning to identify risk factors for bloodstream infections caused by different antimicrobial resistance phenotypes in chemotherapy patients.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing chemotherapy.
