The rising incidence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) further challenges the adequacy of empirical antimicrobial therapy. Therefore, this study aimed to identify features associated with different microbiological profiles of BSIs in chemotherapy patients using machine learning models.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1435 confirmed BSI episodes among 1220 patients treated at a tertiary cancer center from 2017 to 2022. A multi-label classification approach was used to model BSIs associated with carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CR-GNB), methicillin-resistant staphylococci, third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCRE), fungal pathogens, and non-MDRO/non-fungal. Classifier chain models based on logistic regression, random forests, neural networks, and gradient boosting were trained and evaluated using cross-validation with an independent test set. Model outputs were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to estimate feature contributions.

RESULTS: Most BSIs occurred during the first chemotherapy cycle and were due to non-MDROs or fungal agents (1193 episodes; 83.1%), CR-GNB was identified in 109 (7.6%). Model performance varied across pathogen groups, with the highest discrimination observed for CR-GNB (AUC-ROC 83.25%; 95% CI 73.91%-91.64%). Key features included hospitalization days, hematologic malignancy, prior MDRO infection, monocytopenia, and palliative chemotherapy. Chemotherapy class contributed differently across pathogen groups, with alkylating agents contributing to candidemia, antitumor antibiotics to CR-GNB, and antimetabolites to 3GCRE. Prior CR-GNB infection was the strongest predictor for CR-GNB BSI, while palliative chemotherapy correlated with non-MDRO/non-fungal BSI.

CONCLUSION: Multi-label machine learning approaches may help disentangle the complex etiologies of BSIs in cancer patients by identifying associations between host factors, prior MDRO infection, and chemotherapy class within confirmed BSI episodes, informing future hypothesis generation.

articles.title: The effect of seizure-free period on seizure recurrence following antiseizure medication withdrawal: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The seizure-free period before withdrawal is an important factor that influences the risk of epilepsy relapse. Our study aimed to evaluate the effect of the seizure-free period on the relapse risk after antiseizure medication(ASM) withdrawal in epilepsy populations and identify the optimal timing of ASM withdrawal.

METHODS: The Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PubMed and Web of Science were searched for literature published from inception to November 2, 2025. The primary outcome was the relapse risk of epilepsy patients after ASM withdrawal. Random-effects meta-analysis models were used to estimate the pooled recurrence risk based on heterogeneity.

RESULTS: We identified 45 studies with 10,896 patients; 22 studies with 3933 patients were included in the meta-analysis. According to the analyses of all the epilepsy patients, there was a greater risk of recurrence in patients with <5 years of seizure freedom (RR (95% CI) 1.49 (1.17-1.88), p=0.001). Our results also revealed that patients with ≥10 years of seizure freedom had a higher risk of recurrence (RR (95% CI) 0.21 (0.09-0.49), p<0.001); however, it needs further validation due to the limited number of participants and the inclusion of studies. With respect to the subgroup analyses, paediatric patients who had <3 years of seizure freedom, adult patients who had <5 years of seizure freedom, European patients who had <2 years of seizure freedom and Middle Eastern patients who had <3 years of seizure freedom had a higher relapse risk(RR(95% CI) 1.70(1.20-2.39),p=0.003; RR(95% CI) 1.52(1.02-2.26),p=0.04; RR(95% CI) 2.11(1.48-2.99),p<0.001; RR(95% CI) 1.87 (1.41-2.48),p<0.001; RR(95% CI) 1.37(1.03-1.83),p=0.03).

SIGNIFICANCE: The seizure-free period may be an important factor that influences patients' risk of recurrence after ASM withdrawal. Without strong recommendations and evidence regarding the seizure-free period and risk of seizure recurrence, this meta-analysis provides evidence of the optimal timing of ASM withdrawal in epilepsy subpopulations.

articles.title: CCKBR signalling controls human definitive endoderm specification and pancreatic lineage differentiation.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Paracrine signalling by hormone-producing endocrine cells potentially influences pancreatic development, but this feedback regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the roles of gastrin (GAST), cholecystokinin (CCK) and their receptor cholecystokinin B receptor (CCKBR) during human pancreatic development.

METHODS: Human iPSCs were differentiated stepwise into definitive endoderm and then the pancreatic endocrine lineage. To assess CCKBR function, CRISPR/Cas9 was used to generate CCKBR-knockout iPSC lines. We profiled transcriptional states by bulk and single-cell RNA-seq with computational analyses, and complemented these with biochemical assays, flow cytometry (FACS) and confocal microscopy.

RESULTS: CCKBR expression peaked during definitive endoderm formation and progressively declined during differentiation, remaining detectable in pancreatic progenitors but largely absent from the endocrine lineage. By contrast, GAST and CCK were expressed only transiently during pancreatic progenitor and endocrine lineage formation. Pharmacological activation/inhibition and genetic knockout implicated CCKBR signalling during definitive endoderm formation. Consistently, bulk RNA-seq indicated that CCKBR deletion triggered ectodermal- and mesodermal-associated transcriptional programs and diminished pancreatic lineage specification. During pancreatic induction and lineage formation, sustained CCKBR activation with GAST or CCK attenuated endocrinogenesis and promoted epithelial structure formation. Further analysis revealed the emergence of a pancreatic ductal-like cell formation under prolonged CCKBR stimulation.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: This study provides mechanistic evidence that the GAST/CCK-CCKBR axis is functionally important during human endoderm and pancreas development. This pathway is repeatedly required during in vitro pluripotent stem cell differentiation, regulating germ-layer formation as well as ductal vs endocrine fate decisions. These findings support the optimisation of pancreatic differentiation protocols and inform future studies on whether this axis contributes to human pancreas development and disease.

articles.title: Nanomaterial Design for Macrophage Reprogramming: Emerging Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Inflammation and Tumor Therapy.
articles.abstract: Macrophages play a paradoxical role in inflammation and tumor. They can protect the host during acute inflammation but act as the main driver for the chronic inflammation which is a common characteristic of several diseases including rheumatoid arthritis, atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. In the tumor microenvironment, macrophages switch their phenotype to the immunosuppressive M2 state that promotes tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis. Emerging nanomaterial platforms are trying to offer transformative solutions by enabling the precise delivery of immunomodulatory drugs directly to disease-site macrophages. This review will provide comprehensive comparative analysis of these emerging nanomaterial designs strategies across two disease paradigms: inflammatory diseases and tumor. The discussion will focus on various strategies which include inhibiting chemokine axis (CCL2-CCR2 axis), selective elimination of macrophages through apoptosis, metabolic reprogramming, biomimetic and apoptotic cell-inspired nanoparticles leveraging natural macrophage clearance pathways to promote M2 polarization in inflammation, and the activation of tumor-associated macrophages via TLR and STING agonist. We highlight the role of nanoparticle surface chemistry, composition, and targeting ligands in achieving the two opposite therapeutic outcomes of these two diseases while maintaining some common design principles including EPR-mediated accumulation at the disease sites and biomimetic modifications. We also mentioned novel next-generation nanoparticle-based platforms that are currently in clinical trials for the treatment of tumor and inflammatory diseases. Finally, we discuss the barriers that limit the clinical translational potential of broad nanoparticles, with particular emphasis on nanoparticle-related immunotoxicity, macrophage heterogeneity, and manufacturing reproducibility of the nanoparticles.

articles.title: Riedel thyroiditis mimicking malignancy: a fatal surgical outcome.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Riedel thyroiditis (RT) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder that can mimic malignancy clinically and radiologically. We report an unusually extensive, ultimately fatal case and highlight its diagnostic and therapeutic lessons.

METHODS: Case report of a 40-year-old man, with review of the clinical, imaging, histopathological and follow-up data, reported in accordance with the CARE guidelines.

RESULTS: The patient presented with a right cervicothoracic mass (64 × 45 × 115 mm) circumferentially encasing the common carotid, subclavian and innominate vessels with mediastinal extension. Three tissue procedures were non-diagnostic and FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 8.15). Radical en bloc resection was undertaken because malignancy could not be excluded. The course was complicated by bilateral vocal-cord paralysis, Horner syndrome, mediastinitis, osteomyelitis and a tracheo-innominate fistula. Histology showed obliterative phlebitis, storiform fibrosis and 74 IgG4-positive plasma cells/HPF (IgG4:IgG 44%), confirming RT despite normal serum IgG4. The patient died of a recurrent tracheo-innominate fistula approximately 20 months postoperatively.

CONCLUSION: RT can mimic malignancy and, when radical surgery is undertaken for diagnostic uncertainty, may prove fatal. Adequate tissue sampling with IgG4 immunostaining is essential before contemplating radical surgery.

articles.title: Outcome of myringoplasty and type 1 tympanoplasty in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the anatomical and audiological outcomes of myringoplasty and type I tympanoplasty in the pediatric population through systemic review and meta-analysis.

METHOD: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library databases was conducted for studies published between January 2021 until September 2025. Studies involving patients ≤ 18 years undergoing myringoplasty or type 1 tympanoplasty were included. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled proportions of tympanic membrane closure and postoperative complications, as well as pooled mean air-bone gap (ABG) improvement. Heterogeneity, publication bias, sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression were performed. The risk of bias of studies was evaluated using JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist and categorizing them into low, moderated or high risk of bias according to methodological constraints.

RESULT: Thirty-eight studies comprising 4658 ears were included. The pooled tympanic membrane closure rate was 85.8% (95% CI: 83.3 to 88.3), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 81.0%). The pooled rates of postoperative infection, keratin pearl formation, and recurrent perforation rates were 11.6%, 4.0%, and 11.5%, respectively. The pooled mean postoperative air-bone gap (ABG) gain was 11.18 dB (95% CI: 9.55 to 12.81). Subgroup analysis demonstrated significantly higher success rates in studies with higher risk of bias.

CONCLUSION: Myringoplasty and type 1 tympanoplasty in children demonstrate high anatomical success rates and meaningful hearing improvement with relatively low complication rates. However, substantial heterogeneity and variability in study design warrant cautious interpretation of these findings.

articles.title: A transcriptional repressor co-regulatory network integrates iron homeostasis and mycobacterial stress tolerance to oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: A hallmark of Mycobacterium tuberculosis survival and proliferation within the host is attributable to the effective stress response of the pathogen against hostile environmental conditions. Although controlled iron (Fe) uptake and maintenance of Fe homeostasis are closely associated with intracellular survival of mycobacteria, the underlying mechanism that accounts for the interdependence of mycobacterial Fe regulation and oxidative stress response remains unknown. In this study, we discovered that Fe accumulation connects intra-bacterial redox environment via the phoP locus. Gene expression analyses coupled with genetic, biochemical, and transcriptomic studies uncover a distinct mechanism that utilizes Lsr2 and the virulence regulator PhoP to modulate transcriptional control of the major Fe storage protein-encoding gene bfrB. Remarkably, regulated expression of bfrB determines bacterial tolerance to oxidative stress and its intracellular survival. Although both regulators could independently influence bfrB expression, the most fundamental insights are derived from the inhibition of Lsr2 binding at the bfrB regulatory region of the phoP-KO mutant strain owing to Lsr2-PhoP protein-protein interactions. Building on these results, we proposed a model suggesting how Lsr2-PhoP interaction, or lack thereof, contributes to stress-specific regulation of bfrB expression. Collectively, these results uncover a key mechanism integrating Fe accumulation to oxidative stress response, an essential pathogenic determinant of M. tuberculosis.IMPORTANCEWhile the availability of Fe remains essential for Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and replication of the pathogen in human macrophages, Fe may be harmful as it catalyzes the generation of toxic reactive oxygen species from products of aerobic respiration to induce oxidative stress. Although interdependence of mycobacterial Fe regulation and oxidative stress response has been reported, the mechanism connecting Fe acquisition and oxidative stress response is yet to be fully understood. Results reported in this study identify and elaborate on a new mechanism of regulation of expression of the major mycobacterial Fe storage protein, which determines bacterial tolerance to oxidative stress and impacts intracellular survival of the pathogen. We demonstrate that the virulence-associated phoP locus controls Fe accumulation and contributes to the intra-bacterial redox environment. The results uncover a distinctly different transcriptional control mechanism of the major Fe storage protein requiring a co-repressor-dependent regulatory circuit, including nucleoid-associated protein Lsr2 and the virulence regulator PhoP. Together, these results unveil a unique mechanism of stress-specific gene expression, which integrates Fe homeostasis to oxidative stress response, an essential pathogenic determinant of M. tuberculosis.

articles.title: Finerenone: A Non-Steroidal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist and Its Emerging Role in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnected pathophysiology of metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease, leading to multiorgan dysfunction and elevated adverse outcomes. Overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), via aldosterone-dependent and ligand-independent pathways, drives inflammation, fibrosis, and oxidative stress and facilitates CKM progression. Finerenone is a selective non-steroidal MR antagonist (nsMRA) that exhibits high MR affinity, has balanced cardiac and renal distribution, and minimal off-target steroidal effects, which make it mechanistically different from steroidal MRAs. Large phase 3 trials such as FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD in type 2 diabetes with CKD, and FINEARTS-HF in heart failure (HF) with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 40%, demonstrated consistent cardiorenal benefits. The prespecified FINE-HEART pooled analysis showed finerenone reduced all-cause mortality (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), HF hospitalizations (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.92), and the kidney composite outcome (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), with benefits consistent across CKM components and background therapies including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Recent data from FIND-CKD extend utility to non-diabetic CKD. Various guidelines incorporate finerenone as an additive therapy for patients with persistent albuminuria on maximal renin-angiotensin system inhibition (RASi) + SGLT2i. This review summarizes the MR pathophysiology in CKM syndrome, compares the mechanisms of non-steroidal versus steroidal MRAs, synthesizes clinical trial evidence, safety, and guideline-directed place in therapy, addresses implementation barriers, including cost, and outlines future research directions. Finerenone may fill a critical gap in multimodal CKM management, enabling comprehensive pillar-based therapy to mitigate residual cardiorenal risk.

articles.title: Non-invasive fibrosis tests in Wilson Disease: Insights from the international Wilson Disease Registry and Barcelona Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive tests (NITs) accurately detect fibrosis and may reduce the need for liver biopsy (LB). Detection of advanced fibrosis (≥F3) is clinically important for prognosis, but few studies have explored the use of NITs in patients with Wilson Disease (WD).

METHODS: In this multicentre observational study, adult and pediatric WD patients from seven international expert centers with histologic fibrosis staging were included. NITs (Transient elastography (TE), Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), AST to platelet-ratio (APRI), Steatosis-associated fibrosis estimator (SAFE), and NAFLD fibrosis score (NFS)) and clinical data were collected. NITs were compared with liver biopsy (LB) to detect advanced fibrosis (≥F3).

RESULTS: In total, 123 patients were included: median age was 30 years (IQR 17.4, 43.1); time from WD diagnosis to LB was 6.7 months (0.7, 144.1); 30.9% had advanced fibrosis (≥F3), while concomitant metabolic risk factors (obesity and diabetes) were rare. Overall, 64 patients had NITs measured within 1 year of the LB and constituted the primary analysis group. All NITs, except FIB-4, were significantly elevated in patients with ≥F3. TE had the best overall accuracy (AUC=0.79), and performed well at an optimized cut-off of ≥8.35 kPa (sens=0.88, spec=0.85). APRI had lower accuracy, but effectively ruled out ≥F3 at the optimized cut-off of ≥1.3 (AUC=0.71, sens=0.38, spec=1.00). Combining those into a score (APRITE) achieved an AUC of 0.88.

DISCUSSION: TE demonstrated good diagnostic performance for identifying advanced fibrosis in WD. APRI showed high specificity, while the exploratory APRITE score showed encouraging performance.

articles.title: Patent Foramen Ovale and Paradoxical Embolism Complicating Postdural Puncture Headache in a Parturient.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is associated with migraine and cryptogenic ischemic stroke in young patients. Postdural puncture headache (PDPH) is the most likely cause of headache in a puerpera after epidural anesthesia.

CASE SUMMARY: A 34-year-old multipara presented with refractory postural headache, acute neurologic deficits, and elevated D-dimer following an accidental dural puncture during epidural analgesia for vaginal delivery. Investigations revealed right hemispheric infarction due to internal carotid artery occlusion, a latent PFO, and a history of migraine. Emergency thrombectomy led to full recovery.

DISCUSSION: This case suggests that PFO should be considered in postpartum women with intractable PDPH, and that strict bed rest may enhance thrombogenesis and predispose to paradoxical cerebral embolism, potentially worsening outcome.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: The association between PDPH, PFO-related headache, and stroke is rarely documented. In puerperae with intractable PDPH refractory to standard therapy, consider PFO.

articles.title: Birth and clinical outcomes of pregnant participants with advanced HIV disease.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical trials for the evaluation of novel diagnostics and treatments for HIV-associated opportunistic infections have historically excluded pregnant persons. Little information is available regarding the clinical outcomes and pregnancy outcomes of pregnant persons with advanced HIV disease while taking opportunistic infection prophylaxis for tuberculosis (TB) and cryptococcosis. In this study, we describe characteristics at enrollment, clinical outcomes, and birth outcomes of pregnant people with advanced HIV in Uganda.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled pregnant adults with advanced HIV disease within an on-going pragmatic cluster randomized clinical trial evaluating an enhanced screening and prophylaxis package for opportunistic infections (NCT05085171). The trial began enrollment in May 2022 and continues in 26 outpatient HIV clinics in the Kampala and Wakiso districts of Uganda. We present an analysis of pregnant participants enrolled through April 30, 2025, including their characteristics at study enrollment, opportunistic infections, and birth outcomes.

RESULTS: Overall, 15% (114/766) of female participants with advanced HIV disease were pregnant. Median CD4 cell count was 124 cells/µL (IQR: 82-170). Median time since HIV diagnosis was 7 days, and 45% were ART-naive at enrollment. Compared with non-pregnant female participants, pregnant participants were less likely to have a positive cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) test (2% vs 7%, p=0.023), to have a positive Alere tuberculosis (TB) lipoarabinomannan (LAM) test (11% vs 28%, p<0.001), and to be receiving active TB treatment (14% vs 39%, p<0.001). Overall, 18% (21/114) experienced at least one opportunistic infection during the study, of which 71% (n=15) were attributed to TB. Eighty-six percent (98/114) of pregnancies were carried to term. Participants on TB preventive therapy (TPT) had 94% of deliveries at term (51/54), compared with 80% (36/45) among participants who did not receive TPT (OR = 4.25, 95%CI:1.07-16.80), and 67% (8/12) among participants on active TB treatment (OR = 8.50, 95%CI: 1.60-45.25).

CONCLUSIONS: Although the incidence of opportunistic infections is less commonly reported among pregnant women with advanced HIV disease, TB is the most frequent opportunistic infection. Participants on TPT had 4-fold higher odds of having a term delivery compared with those not on TPT and 8-fold higher odds compared with those with active TB.

articles.title: Global environmental and cardiometabolic correlates of periodontitis- ischemic heart disease co-burden: a spatiotemporal network analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Geographic co-occurrence patterns and shared risk factors between periodontitis and ischemic heart disease remain inadequately characterized globally. This study aimed to characterize country-level spatiotemporal co-burden patterns of periodontitis and ischemic heart disease, thereby helping identify regions and risk profiles in which integrated periodontal and cardiovascular prevention may be most relevant.

METHODS: An ecological analysis was conducted using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data from 204 countries. Machine-learning-based feature selection was used to screen 68 risk factors. Countries were classified as concordant-burden, periodontitis-predominant, or IHD-predominant. Negative binomial regression and population attributable fractions (PAF) quantified risk contributions across 6,528 country-year observations (1990-2021).

RESULTS: Periodontitis incidence (1,740.92/100,000) remained 2.2-fold higher than IHD. Analysis revealed 73 countries (35.96%) as IHD-dominant, 74 (36.45%) as periodontitis-dominant, and 56 (27.59%) with dual burdens. Elevated systolic blood pressure was the sole shared risk factor (RR 1.006-1.008). For IHD, insufficient whole grain intake showed the highest attributable fraction (PAF 6.16%), followed by elevated BMI (4.17%) and high LDL cholesterol (3.87%); kidney dysfunction had the strongest per-unit association (RR 1.111) with a PAF of 2.98%. For periodontitis, lead exposure showed the largest model-derived PAF among the assessed factors (PAF 2.36%), followed by blood pressure (2.30%) and particulate matter (1.26%). Disease-specific factors accounted for 20.55% of IHD and 4.51% of periodontitis burden. Temporal analysis revealed strong synchronization in dual-burden regions (ρ=0.901, P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Elevated blood pressure was the only shared population-level factor associated with both conditions. Kidney dysfunction and dietary factors were more strongly associated with IHD burden, whereas lead exposure and particulate matter were associated with periodontitis burden in ecological models. Geographically tailored interventions are essential: metabolic management in IHD-dominant regions and environmental remediation in periodontitis-predominant areas, particularly Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa. Clinically, the findings support greater attention to blood pressure and cardiometabolic risk assessment in patients with periodontitis, while emphasizing that causal links and intervention benefits require confirmation in individual-level studies.

articles.title: Yin-Yang: The Dual Role of Lactate as a Context-Dependent Immunometabolic Regulator in the Inflammatory Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Lactate, once regarded merely as the terminal product of glycolysis, is now recognised as a pivotal immunometabolic regulator that actively shapes inflammatory responses. However, accumulating evidence reveals an apparent paradox that lactate can either amplify immune activation or promote inflammation resolution depending on the biological context. The mechanisms underlying this functional duality remain incompletely understood, limiting the development of effective lactate-targeted therapies. In this review, we propose that lactate functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic rheostat whose Yin-Yang properties are determined by the integration of four key factors: lactate concentration, cellular identity, disease stage and inflammatory microenvironment. We summarise how lactate regulates immune responses through coordinated control of metabolic reprogramming, intercellular lactate shuttling, receptor-mediated signalling, intracellular sensing, and protein lactylation, thereby orchestrating the activation and resolution of inflammation. We further discuss the cell-specific actions of lactate across endothelial cells, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, neutrophils, and lymphocytes, highlighting how these mechanisms collectively remodel the inflammatory microenvironment. Beyond mechanistic insights, we examine evidence from representative inflammatory disease models, including rheumatoid arthritis, sepsis, and atherosclerosis, and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lactate production, transport, sensing and metabolism. Rather than advocating indiscriminate lactate inhibition, current evidence supports context-specific modulation of lactate signalling according to disease stage and immune landscape.

articles.title: Response to Comment on Redondo et al. BMI Normalization Is Associated With Lower Risk of Progression to Type 1 Diabetes, Primarily in Youth.
Comment on Redondo et al. BMI Normalization Is Associated With Lower Risk of Progression to Type 1 Diabetes, Primarily in Youth.
Comment on Redondo et al. BMI Normalization Is Associated With Lower Risk of Progression to Type 1 Diabetes, Primarily in Youth.
Tissue-Specific Insulin Resistance Pattern Underlies Heterogeneous Disease Severity and Complications in MASLD.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance (IR) plays a pathophysiological role in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, it remains unclear whether the specific distribution of IR across muscle, adipose tissue, hepatic tissue, and the whole body is associated with the heterogeneous disease severity and its complications.

METHODS: Consecutive subjects (non-MASLD: 1239, MASLD: 1067) were retrospectively enrolled between June 2014 and June 2024, undergoing comprehensive evaluations that included anthropometric, laboratory, and imaging measurements. Tissue-specific IR indices (muscle IR, adipose IR, hepatic IR) and systemic IR were quantified using parameters derived from an oral glucose tolerance test.

RESULTS: Patients with MASLD exhibited lower muscle IR levels but higher adipose IR, hepatic IR, and systemic IR levels compared to those with non-MASLD (all p < 0.001). Multivariate analyses revealed distinct tissue-specific associations: hepatic IR was associated with the odds of moderate-severe steatosis (OR: 15.91, 95%CI 5.92-42.74, p < 0.001), systemic IR with liver injury (OR: 2.75, 95%CI: 1.89-4.00, p < 0.001), adipose IR with significant fibrosis (OR: 5.90, 95%CI: 3.31-10.53, p < 0.001), and muscle IR was inversely associated with CVD (OR: 2.87, 95%CI: 1.70-4.87, p < 0.001). Additionally, MASLD patients with co-occurring adipose-hepatic IR had a higher prevalence of liver injury compared to those with isolated muscle IR (64.0% vs. 28.8%, p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Tissue-specific IR profiles may help characterize heterogeneous MASLD manifestations and CVD-associated phenotypes. Further studies are needed to assess whether timely identification of these profiles and initiation of appropriate interventions is beneficial.

articles.title: Tumor-Microenvironment-Activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 Nanoplatform for MRI/PAI-Assisted Chemophotothermal Therapy of Osteosarcoma.
articles.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains difficult to treat because surgery and chemotherapy can provide incomplete tumor control, cause systemic toxicity, and lack reliable local monitoring. In this study, a tumor-microenvironment-activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 nanoplatform was prepared by converting Cu2O nanocubes into hollow Cu2S, coating polydopamine, growing a MnO2 shell, and loading doxorubicin. The Cu2S/PDA structure enabled strong NIR absorption and drug loading, while MnO2 responded to acidic H2O2/GSH-rich conditions to promote O2 generation, ROS-related reactions, and enhanced T1 MRI contrast. The nanoplatform showed concentration-dependent photothermal conversion at 808 and 1024 nm, microenvironment-responsive DOX release, increased intracellular ROS, and stronger killing of 143B osteosarcoma cells under NIR irradiation than carrier or free-drug controls. In tumor-bearing mice, it enhanced MRI/photoacoustic signals, enabled local photothermal heating, markedly inhibited tumor growth, and increased H&E-defined tumor damage and TUNEL-positive apoptosis, especially with 1024 nm irradiation. Hemolysis, organ histology, hematology, and blood biochemistry indicated acceptable short-term safety after repeated intratumoral administration. These results support this Cu2S/PDA/MnO2-based platform for imaging-guided localized osteosarcoma therapy.

articles.title: The use of technology to improve wound care practice.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As clinicians we may encounter patients with complicated wounds of varying etiologies.

LOCAL PROBLEM: Wound education is often lacking in nursing and medical curriculums. There is shortage of wound specialized clinicians to offer guidance. Furthermore, there is a shortage of palliative specialized clinicians to assist when the goals of wound care may need to shift to symptom management.

METHODS: The accredited Wound Care Pro app was developed as an educational resource for clinicians to meet this critical care need. It includes an overview of eight wound etiologies with descriptions, images, treatment options, case studies, and interventions to manage distressing symptoms, such as wound pain, odor, bleeding, and excessive exudate.

INTERVENTIONS: Technology was used to develop an educational tool for clinicians to have at their fingertips to help bridge the knowledge gap. The goals include empowering clinicians caring for patients with wounds to improve the healing potential when healing is the goal, to decrease the risk of complications, to improve symptom management, to decrease the wasteful use of costly wound supplies, and to decrease the risk of litigation from inappropriate wound care plans.

RESULTS: More than 11,000 clinicians have downloaded the application with positive feedback received, including how it has helped them get more appropriate, cost-effective wound care plans in place.

CONCLUSION: Although there is a shortage of wound and palliative specialized clinicians to meet complex patient wound care needs, technology can help empower clinicians whether wound healing or palliation is the goal.

articles.title: Microglial Ring1 enhances post-phagocytic myelin debris processing: Attenuation of cognitive dysfunction after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion induces myelin injury, resulting in cognitive impairment. Efficient clearance of myelin debris is important for neural repair. The E3 ubiquitin ligase Ring1 (RING finger protein 1) participates in ubiquitin signaling and gene expression regulation, However, whether Ring1 ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury-induced cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing remains unknown. In this study, we employed a hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion model, a hippocampal myelin debris injection model, and an in vitro microglia-myelin debris co-culture model to simulate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, and combined these models with proteomic and transcriptomic analyses and Ring1 gain- and loss-of-function approaches. Hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion induced hippocampal myelin injury and cognitive dysfunction, while hippocampal administration of myelin debris further impaired cognition. Transcriptomic analysis identified Ring1 as a candidate regulator associated with postphagocytic myelin debris processing. Ring1 overexpression alleviated cognitive deficits and hippocampal myelin injury and restored mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels after hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion. In contrast, Ring1 knockdown in the microglia-myelin debris co-culture model reduced mitochondrial DNAencoded gene expression and adenosine triphosphate levels and delayed post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Mechanistically, Ring1 interacted with mitochondrial transcription factor B2, with K27-linked ubiquitin signals detected in Ring1- and mitochondrial transcription factor B2-containing immunocomplexes. Ring1 depletion reduced mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling, mitochondrial DNA-encoded gene expression, adenosine triphosphate levels, and post-phagocytic myelin debris processing. Collectively, our findings suggest that Ring1 attenuates hemorrhagic shock and reperfusion-related cognitive impairment by promoting microglial post-phagocytic myelin debris processing through mitochondrial transcription factor B2-associated K27-linked ubiquitin signaling and mitochondrial regulation.

articles.title: Combined Control of Rice Sheath Blight Using a Biobased Pickering Emulsion Co-Formulated with Two Pesticides.
articles.journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
articles.abstract: Rice sheath blight, a globally significant disease caused by Rhizoctonia solani (R. solani), can be effectively managed through a codelivery technology that combines the action of two pesticides. This approach, which involves multitargeted, coordinated intervention against the pathogen, enhances the efficacy of pesticides and reduces the required dosage. Therefore, this study employed electrostatic self-assembly to prepare chitosan-alkali lignin (AC) nanocomposite particles as stabilizers. Through systematic optimization of oil-water ratio and ultrasonic power, a novel dual-drug Pickering emulsion delivery system (AZO@ACVA) was successfully constructed for combined efficacy control of rice sheath blight. This system achieves efficient coloading of the hydrophilic pesticide validamycin (VA) and the hydrophobic pesticide azoxystrobin (AZO), demonstrating multiple functional advantages: within the acidic microenvironment formed by pathogen infection, the carrier exhibits pH-responsive release properties, enabling intelligent combined efficacy release of both drugs. On leaf surfaces, the amphiphilic structure of the AC nanocarrier combined with the combined efficacy effect of Tween 80 significantly enhances the wetting and adhesion of the emulsion on both hydrophobic rice leaves and hydrophilic cucumber leaves. The deposition levels reached 2.28 times and 1.89 times that of commercial formulations, respectively, with markedly improved resistance to rain wash-off. Simultaneously, the combined efficacy barrier effect between the lipid phase and lignin effectively delays the photodegradation of pesticides. Antimicrobial experiments demonstrate significant combined efficacy effects between VA and AZO in this system, resulting in a substantially higher inhibition rate against rice sheath blight pathogens compared to either commercial pesticide alone. Furthermore, this fully biomass-based system substantially reduces acute toxicity to zebrafish, exhibiting excellent environmental compatibility. This study presents a biobased Pickering emulsion platform for the codelivery of hydrophilic and hydrophobic pesticides, providing a green and efficient strategy for controlling rice sheath blight with reduced environmental impact.

articles.title: Invasive vagus nerve stimulation paired with upper limb motor rehabilitation after intracerebral hemorrhage: A single-arm pilot cohort study.
articles.abstract: Invasive vagus nerve stimulation paired with rehabilitation improves upper-limb recovery after ischemic stroke, but clinical evidence after intracerebral hemorrhage remains limited. We evaluated the feasibility, safety, and descriptive functional signal of invasive vagus nerve stimulation-paired rehabilitation in chronic intracerebral hemorrhage. Twelve participants with chronic upper-limb motor dysfunction after intracerebral hemorrhage underwent left cervical invasive vagus nerve stimulation implantation followed by 6 weeks of supervised in-clinic rehabilitation and 90 days of home-based rehabilitation. The primary outcome was change in Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity from baseline to day 1 after inclinic rehabilitation. Secondary and exploratory outcomes included Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity change on day 90, Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity subscores, modified Ashworth scale scores, quality of life, safety, and exploratory positron emission tomography/computed tomography and arterial spin labeling findings. All participants completed follow-up. Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity increased from 23.50 ± 15.63 points at baseline to 27.58 ± 17.15 on day 1, with a mean change of 4.08 ± 3.48 points (P = 0.002). On day 90, Fugl-Meyer Assessment Upper Extremity was 27.75 ± 17.23 points, with a mean change of 4.25 ± 3.60 points from baseline. Six participants reached the minimal clinically important difference threshold on days 1 and 90. No serious perioperative complications were observed in this small cohort. Exploratory imaging in two participants showed postoperative changes in metabolic and perfusion ratios within cortical-subcortical motor-network regions. Invasive vagus nerve stimulation-paired rehabilitation was feasible and had an acceptable safety profile in this pilot intracerebral hemorrhage cohort, with a descriptive signal of upper-limb functional improvement. This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07736573).

articles.title: Mechanisms of ubiquitination in central nervous system injury and potential therapeutic targets.
articles.abstract: Ubiquitination is a highly conserved and reversible post-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, activity, and intracellular signaling through the coordinated actions of the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In recent years, increasing evidence has highlighted the critical role of ubiquitination in maintaining central nervous system proteostasis and regulating pathological responses following central nervous system injury. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in research on ubiquitination in traumatic brain injury, spinal cord injury, stroke, and central nervous system infections, with particular emphasis on its involvement in secondary injury and subsequent neural repair. The mechanisms by which ubiquitination and deubiquitination regulate neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier integrity, and programmed cell death, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, and ferroptosis, are highlighted. Disease-specific ubiquitination patterns and their contributions to vascular repair, neural stem cell activation, axonal regeneration, and functional recovery are also discussed. Furthermore, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting key ubiquitin-system enzymes, as well as nanotechnology- and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches for precise modulation of ubiquitin-dependent signaling, are summarized and their therapeutic potential is explored. Although promising findings have been obtained from cellular and animal models, the cell-type-, temporal-, and disease-context-specific nature of ubiquitin signaling, substrate selectivity, and distinct ubiquitin-chain topologies remain major barriers to clinical translation. Further studies are therefore needed to elucidate the spatiotemporal dynamics of ubiquitination and identify context-specific therapeutic windows. Overall, ubiquitination represents a central regulatory network connecting proteostasis, neuroinflammation, cell death, and neural repair, providing a promising therapeutic approach for improving neurological outcomes after central nervous system injury.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential analysis of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is a core pathological process underlying further neurological deterioration after reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Developing more effective neuroprotective agents is therefore a current priority in neuroscience research. Sertoli cells possess unique immunoprivileged and nutritional support functions within the testes and secrete exosomes that serve as important mediators of intercellular communication, with substantial potential for neuroprotection. This review addresses the protective mechanisms of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Through a comprehensive literature review, we systematically summarize their neuroprotective effects, including the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inhibition of cellular apoptosis, promotion of neurovascular repair, regulation of autophagy, and influence on epigenetic modifications and related signaling pathways. By synthesizing the latest findings in this field, we aim to provide insights into the development and translation of novel neuroprotective strategies based on Sertoli cell-derived exosomes.

articles.title: Screening and assessment of delirium in adult intensive care unit patients: a best practice implementation project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delirium affects up to 80% of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients, resulting in a significant impact on clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This evidence implementation project evaluated and improved adherence to best practice guidelines for delirium screening and assessment in a specialized ICU setting.

METHODS: This project used the JBI Evidence Implementation Framework and was conducted in a 10-bed adult neurological ICU in São Paulo, Brazil. Compliance was assessed across seven best practice audit criteria measured at baseline (n = 27) and at follow-up (n = 27). Using JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) analysis, two primary barriers were identified: nurse knowledge deficits and operational time constraints due to documentation complexity. To address these barriers, micro-learning sessions were conducted using gamification, quick-access electronic health record templates, and visual huddle reminders.

RESULTS: The follow-up audit demonstrated increased compliance across five criteria: daily observation, formal assessment (CAM-ICU), nurse training, clinical prioritization, and complete documentation. Compliance remained unchanged for two criteria: initial risk screening upon ICU admission and immediate observation following a positive screening.

CONCLUSIONS: Strategic implementation using gamified education and streamlined workflows successfully bridged knowledge and operational gaps in a high-acuity neurological ICU. Combining active-learning strategies with workflow simplification proved essential for driving sustainable improvements in clinical delirium assessment.

articles.title: Natural, clean, yet still allergenic: contact allergen burden in vulvar soothing products.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the prevalence of contact allergens in over-the-counter nonhormonal vulvar soothing products and determine whether common marketing claims identify products with lower allergen burden.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of externally applied vulvar soothing products sold through major US retailers was performed. Ingredients were compared with the North American Contact Dermatitis Group 80-allergen series. Product characteristics, marketing descriptors, and allergen burden were analyzed using descriptive and comparative statistics.

RESULTS: Among 65 products, 78% contained at least one allergen, and 49% contained botanical-derived allergens. Fragrance ingredients were the most common allergens (39%), followed by sodium benzoate (25%), phenoxyethanol (12%), and propylene glycol (9%). Marketing descriptors, including "natural," "hypoallergenic," and "fragrance-free," were not associated with lower allergen burden. Twenty-eight percent of "fragrance-free" products contained botanical scent allergens, and all "hypoallergenic" products contained at least one allergen. Ointments had lower allergen burden than other vehicles (P = 0.02), while product price was not associated with allergen burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Most nonhormonal vulvar soothing products contain common contact allergens despite marketing suggesting improved tolerability. These findings support ingredient-based counseling by Menopause Society Certified Practitioners and other menopause health care professionals when recommending over-the-counter vulvar products to minimize contact allergen exposure and contact dermatitis risk.

articles.title: Inter-α-inhibitor heavy chain 4 levels in incident and prevalent patients with primary biliary cholangitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune liver disease characterised by progressive bile duct injury. We recently showed that inter-α-inhibitor heavy chain 4 (ITIH4) levels are elevated in patients with PBC. Here, we investigated the potential of ITIH4 as a biomarker for disease severity and treatment response.

METHODS: We included 237 patients with primary biliary cholangitis, 80 incident (newly diagnosed), 157 prevalent (with established disease) and 100 healthy controls. All patients were followed for 12 months during initiation or continuation of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA). Associations with treatment response, patient type, autoimmune hepatitis (AIH-PBC) and sex were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. The prognostic value of baseline ITIH4 for following response was assessed using logistic regression.

RESULTS: ITIH4 levels were significantly higher in both PBC cohorts compared with healthy controls (incident: 274 µg/ml, prevalent: 283 µg/ml, controls: 221 µg/ml; p < .0001). In a mixed-effects model, treatment response, prevalent (vs. incident) disease and AIH-PBC (vs. PBC alone) were each independently associated with lower ITIH4 (p = .003, p = .034 and p = .013). Correlations between ITIH4 and markers of disease severity were generally weak. Baseline ITIH4 was not significantly associated with treatment response (OR 0.994, p = .14).

CONCLUSIONS: ITIH4 was consistently elevated in patients with PBC compared with healthy individuals. Baseline ITIH4 levels did not independently predict response and correlations with established severity markers remained weak. These findings do not support its use as a prognostic marker or as an addition to existing clinical biomarkers.

articles.title: Incident Comorbid Diabetes and Outcomes in Multiple Sclerosis: An English Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of diabetes mellitus and its associations with hospitalisation and mortality in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS) and matched controls.

METHODS: Using English primary care data from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, linked to hospital and mortality records, we matched adults with MS with up to 10 controls without MS by age, sex and practice. We excluded individuals with pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Outcomes included all-cause hospitalisation (number and duration) and mortality. We used Poisson, negative binomial, linear and Cox proportional hazards models, adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors, with interaction terms for ethnicity, deprivation and urbanity.

RESULTS: We included 47,247 individuals with MS and 458,951 matched controls. Over a mean follow-up of 15.2 years, people with MS had a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.16, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.21). Among people with MS, incident diabetes mellitus was associated with higher hospitalisation rates (adjusted incidence rate ratio = 1.52, 1.42-1.64), longer hospitalisation duration (median 12 vs. 2 days) and increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio = 1.41, 1.31-1.49). Similar patterns were observed among controls. The association between diabetes mellitus and increased hospitalisation was stronger in rural areas among those with MS and in White groups among controls.

INTERPRETATION: MS was associated with a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus, which was in turn associated with greater hospitalisation and mortality. These findings may support consideration of equitable screening, prevention and management of diabetes mellitus in people living with MS.

articles.title: Physical Health Crises Preceding Suicide from Late Midlife Through Older Age: Illnesses, Contexts, and Age-Group Differences.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine how physical health (PH) crises preceding suicide differ from late midlife (50-64 years) to older age (≥65 years).

METHODS: Using 2022-2023 National Violent Death Reporting System-Restricted Access Data, we analyzed suicide decedents aged ≥ 50 with a PH problem as a precipitant (N = 11,796) and reviewedct 2 coroner/medical examiner and law enforcement narratives for those with a PH crisis.

RESULTS: PH crises increased with age, occurring in 3.7% of decedents aged 50-64, 8.5% aged 65-74, 12.3% aged 75-84, and 12.8% aged ≥ 85. Terminal illness and pain were principal health correlates of PH crisis status. Pain was less frequently implicated with increasing age, whereas functional limitations, heart disease, falls, and dementia were generally more prevalent in older groups. Narratives showed that crises in late midlife more often involved occupational and economic consequences, whereas those in older age involved threatened autonomy, dependence, perceived burdensomeness, and care transitions.

CONCLUSIONS: PH crises became more prominent with advancing age, while the illnesses and contexts differed from late midlife through older age.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Healthcare professionals should assess suicide risk when older adults experience serious or worsening PH problems. Suicide prevention approaches should adopt collaborative safety planning including both health services and age-appropriate care support.

articles.title: Frontline of infection control: Parents caring for high-risk children.
articles.journal: Journal of child health care : for professionals working with children in the hospital and community
articles.abstract: Parents play an essential role in their child's care, including infection prevention and control (IPC), during hospitalisation. Despite this, their role in IPC is not clearly defined. This study explored how parents of children admitted to an Australian tertiary paediatric hospital understand and participate in IPC initiatives. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted in oncology/haematology, adolescent, and surgical wards, involving semi-structured interviews with 24 parents and 2 mature minors. Data were analysed thematically using the Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices model as a deductive framework. Three themes were derived, highlighting parents' engagement in IPC. Heightened parental vigilance involved maintaining hygiene, monitoring their child's condition, educating children, and seeking clarification when clinical communication or staff practice was inconsistent. Balancing infection risk with daily life involved recognising the ubiquity of infections, managing community exposures, and weighing risk against their child's need for a normal life. Hospital care was seen as both a risk and a necessity, emphasising reliance on treatment and concerns about potential infection exposure. Parents' IPC efforts were ongoing and adapted to the realities of home, community exposure, and hospital admission. Their role in managing infection risk highlights the importance of integrating parents into IPC in paediatric care.

articles.title: Dynamic Changes in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Levels Predicts Early Neurological Deterioration After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Minor Stroke.
authors: Biomarkers of Brain Injury Investigator Study Group
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Minor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration (END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END.

METHODS: Data originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post-thrombolysis GFAP at 24 h to baseline GFAP. Univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between ∆GFAP and END, and a nomogram was established to illustrate its predictive value.

RESULTS: END occurred in 20 (7.35%) of the 272 patients with minor stroke who underwent intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). Elevated ∆GFAP was independently associated with END (OR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.67 to 7.31; p < 0.001), even after adjusting for confounders (adjusted OR, 4.64; 95% CI, 1.86 to 11.54; p < 0.001). Furthermore, a model combining ∆GFAP, age, and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission demonstrated a good predictive value for END (AUC = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.89).

INTERPRETATION: ∆GFAP is a strong, independent predictor of END in patients with minor strokes. Integrating ∆GFAP, age, and NIHSS score into a prognostic model results in a good discriminative ability for predicting END.

articles.title: Encoding Light in Electronic Noise.
articles.abstract: Optical sensing in semiconductors is traditionally governed by photoconductive, photovoltaic, and photogating effects, in which optical inputs are encoded as continuous variations in average current. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally distinct paradigm in which light is encoded in stochastic transport dynamics rather than steady-state conductance. Using a monolayer MoS2 field-effect transistor with an aggressively scaled gate stack (∼1.3 nm equivalent oxide thickness), we access a regime where interfacial defect states dominate transport and form gate-tunable potential wells. At low temperature, carrier emission from these states is suppressed, stabilizing trapped configurations in the dark, whereas optical excitation selectively activates emission, giving rise to large-amplitude ("giant") random telegraph noise. This enables independent control of capture and emission processes through electrostatic gating and illumination, respectively, creating a direct mapping between optical input and stochastic observables such as switching rates, dwell times, and state occupancies. Interestingly, optical detection is achieved through the statistics of rare emission events, enabling sensitivity to ultralow illumination levels (∼50 fW). Spectral dependence further reveals photon energy-dependent emission kinetics, confirming the role of photon-assisted detrapping. These results show a light-induced nonequilibrium transport regime in which defect-mediated fluctuations, conventionally treated as noise, act as a functional signal and provide a stochastic sensing framework for ultralow-light detection in nanoscale electronic systems.

articles.title: Scalable Independently Tunable MoS2 Memtransistor via Contact-Engineering for Cardiac Signal Processing.
articles.abstract: Reliable and scalable neuromorphic computing demands memristive devices with deterministic analog tunability. While vertical structures enable high integration density, planar architectures are essential for complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) compatible memtransistor platforms governed by lateral charge transport. However, resistive switching in widely reported memristive devices is dominated by nucleation or filament-driven conduction between electrodes, constraining analog tunability, reproducibility, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate charge-transfer based contact engineering strategy that enables device-level, independently tunable deterministic resistive switching through controlled interfacial charge trapping/detrapping. Dynamic modulation of the metal-semiconductor Schottky barrier by interfacial trap states enables device-independent, nucleation-free, and gate-free resistive switching with a ∼102 ratio. Temperature-dependent transport exhibits linear Arrhenius behavior of ln (ID/T3/2) vs. 1/T with bias dependent slopes, confirming thermally activated, interface-limited conduction. Under gate-free operation, continuous drain current modulation supports reliable synaptic functions, including long-term potentiation/depression and spike-time-dependent-plasticity. Cardiac signal processing is further validated through ECG arrhythmia classification using the MIT-BIH database.

articles.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C predicted increased flux through glucose transport, glucose phosphorylation, and downstream glucose-associated reactions than it did at 29-30°C. Similar temperature-dependent predictions were obtained for another pathogenic Leptospira species under in vitro conditions. Consistent with these findings, analysis of leptospires cultivated intraperitoneally in dialysis membrane chambers also predicted enhanced glucose uptake and metabolism under host-temperature conditions. In vitro validation experiments showed increased bacterial uptake or accumulation of a fluorescent glucose analog, elevated expression of candidate glucose transporter genes, and glucose-dependent enhancement of bacterial growth at 37°C. Treatment with a glucose degradation pathway inhibitor, 2-deoxy-d-glucose, further supported a contribution of glucose-associated processes to proliferation at 37°C. Together, these findings indicate that pathogenic Leptospira displays condition-dependent glucose uptake and glucose-associated metabolic activity that become apparent at host-like temperature, as opposed to being glucose-incompetent at environmental-like temperature. This prediction-driven framework refines the conventional view of Leptospira carbon metabolism and provides a basis for future studies of glucose-associated metabolic capacity during mammalian infection.

IMPORTANCE: Environmental reservoirs play a central role in the transmission of many bacterial pathogens, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable adaptation to both environmental and host-associated niches remain largely unknown. Using a prediction-driven framework that combines contextualized genome-scale metabolic modeling with multi-omics analyses and experimental validation, we discovered that pathogenic Leptospira activates glucose uptake and metabolism only under host-like conditions. This finding resolves a long-standing misconception arising from studies performed under conventional laboratory conditions and fundamentally revises our understanding of Leptospira physiology. More importantly, our study establishes an integrative systems biology strategy for uncovering condition-dependent metabolic traits that would be difficult to identify experimentally alone, with broad applicability to diverse environmentally transmitted pathogens.

articles.title: Risk of venous thromboembolism in chronic inflammatory skin diseases: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

articles.title: Epidemiology of MERS-CoV in Saudi Arabia, 2012-2025: a nationwide surveillance analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS), caused by MERS coronavirus (MERS-CoV), is a severe zoonotic respiratory illness first identified in Saudi Arabia in 2012. Dromedary camels are the recognised reservoir, with human transmission occurring through animal exposure and, less commonly, person-to-person spread, particularly in healthcare settings.

OBJECTIVE: To characterise all laboratory-confirmed MERS-CoV cases reported in Saudi Arabia from September 2012 to August 2025, examine trends across four periods defined by suspected-case definitions, and identify factors independently associated with mortality.

METHODS: We analysed laboratory-confirmed cases in the national surveillance database by period and probable infection source. Case-fatality ratios (CFRs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and unadjusted odds ratios were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression assessed independent mortality associations using a prespecified model including period, age, sex, and infection source, and a fuller model additionally considering nationality, comorbidities, and pregnancy. Seasonality of primary cases was assessed using an annual harmonic term.

RESULTS: Among 2,219 cases, 1,545 (70%) were male, 1,566 (71%) Saudi nationals, and 608 (27%) aged ≥65 years. Overall, 1,211 (55%) were primary cases, including 172 (14%) reporting camel contact; 737 (33%) were healthcare-associated and 271 (12%) household- or community-associated. There were 867 deaths (CFR, 39%; 95% CI, 37%-41%). CFR declined from 65% in the earliest period to 32% in the most recent, although changing testing eligibility and ascertainment limit temporal comparisons. Older adults had the highest crude CFR. In the prespecified model, healthcare-associated infection among patients was associated with higher odds of death (aOR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.15-2.65), while odds were lower among healthcare workers (aOR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.05-0.17) and household contacts (aOR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.18-0.48). No consistent seasonality was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: MERS-CoV epidemiology in Saudi Arabia reflects persistent zoonotic spillover, episodic healthcare-associated transmission, and substantial mortality, particularly among older adults. Sustained One Health surveillance, rapid detection, and rigorous infection prevention and control remain essential.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicles released by Candida albicans yeast cells impact candidiasis lethality in insect and murine models.
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nano-sized lipid bilayer structures released by diverse cell types. For pathogenic fungi, EVs play critical roles by modulating immune responses and influencing disease progression. Previously, we demonstrated that vaccination with EVs from Candida albicans promoted protection in immunosuppressed mice subsequently infected with lethal doses of this organism. However, the impact of EVs in the presence of fungi is poorly investigated in vivo. Here, we demonstrated that co-injection of C. albicans yeasts and their EVs into Galleria mellonella larvae led to a rapid larval death compared to yeast cells alone. This effect seems to be associated with thermosensitive compounds, such as secreted aspartic proteases (Saps), virulence factors carried by C. albicans EVs. EVs from SAP knockout (KO) strains (sap1/2/3Δ and sap9Δ) impaired this harmful effect, confirming the crucial role of Saps. Deletion of SAP1-3 prevented the EV-associated decrease in hemocyte density, whereas SAP9 deletion impaired the increase in oxidative response and melanin production. In a murine model of disseminated candidiasis with intraperitoneal infection, the deleterious effect of C. albicans EVs was observed only when co-injected intraperitoneally with yeasts, but not when EVs were administered intramuscularly. Therefore, both fungal cells and EVs are required for the pathogenic effects. Our findings confirm the aggressive role of fungal EVs in the presence of C. albicans and reinforce their contribution to candidiasis, elucidating EV-pathogen interactions. Although these results do not preclude the use of C. albicans EVs in vaccine formulations, they emphasize the need to consider delivery route and presence of virulence factors.IMPORTANCEFungal infections caused by Candida albicans represent a significant threat, particularly to immunocompromised individuals. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) from fungi have been explored as promising vaccine formulations, with demonstrated protective effects. However, previous studies have also suggested that EVs may contribute to disease progression. Here, we demonstrate that EVs enhance fungal pathogenicity in vivo and identify key factors driving this effect. We show that EV-associated aspartyl proteases (secreted aspartic proteases [Saps]), along with other virulence components, directly contribute to accelerated host mortality when EVs are present alongside fungal cells, and that this outcome depends on both their composition and route of delivery. By demonstrating the involvement of EV-associated Saps in disease progression, this work advances our understanding of host-pathogen interactions and reveals critical considerations for the safe development of EV-based therapeutic and vaccine strategies.

articles.title: Cross-linking mass spectrometry guided structure prediction of disordered Encephalitozoon hellem proteins.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Microsporidia such as Encephalitozoon hellem are obligate intracellular human parasites that remain genetically intractable, limiting the functional characterization of their proteomes. Experimental structural studies are challenging, as many proteins in microsporidia comprise a large percentage of disordered regions. Computational structural studies based on homology-based modeling and the use of deep-learning algorithms for microsporidian proteins also remain limited because most have little to no sequence similarity to proteins with solved structures. To address these limitations, we developed an approach that incorporates cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) data into structure prediction. XL-MS data provide upper-bound distance constraints that can be incorporated into protein deep-learning-based modeling and subsequent docking. Using this approach, we generated a model of two interacting E. hellem spore wall proteins, spore wall protein 1B (Swp1b) and endospore protein 1 (EnP1), which have no clear homologs outside of microsporidia and contain several disordered regions. These proteins are abundant spore wall proteins of microsporidia and previously were not known to interact with one another. The resulting model not only is consistent with the experimental cross-links used to generate the model but was also subsequently confirmed by independently generated XL-MS data. The described AlphaLink-Modeller framework for structure prediction is particularly well suited to proteins with limited homology and/or substantial flexible regions, given that they adopt a defined structural state within a biological context, thereby extending integrative modeling approaches to previously inaccessible targets.

IMPORTANCE: In this article, we demonstrate an improved method for the prediction of the structure of protein complexes with no clear homologs and a considerable number of disordered regions. This is significant because these types of proteins are critical to understanding the biology of organisms, yet model generation of these classes has been inaccessible. The method incorporates experimental data obtained from cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) into the modeling process, providing a method to integrate such experimental data into computational modeling of the structure of proteins and protein interactions. For this paper, we have used this method for predicting the structure of two highly abundant Encephalitozoon hellem proteins in the spore wall that are important for host cell infection due to this pathogen of humans and other vertebrates.

articles.title: Nonlinear stability phenotypes and collapse dynamics of multi-organ radiomics in total-body PET imaging: toward digital twin-oriented robustness assessment.
articles.abstract: Radiomics analysis in PET offers a high-dimensional representation of tissue characteristics, yet its reliability is limited by sensitivity to acquisition perturbations, particularly dose reduction. This study aims to introduce a nonlinear stability phenotyping framework to characterize dose-response behavior of multi-organ radiomics and evaluate their potential relevance for future digital twin-oriented applications.Approach: A multi-center dataset of 550 total-body PET scans was analyzed. Dose reduction was simulated using list-mode subsampling (dose reduction factor - DRF = 2-100). A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted per organ. Stability was quantified using Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and summarized as stability fractions. Nonlinear models were fitted to organ- and feature-level trajectories. Stability phenotypes and critical thresholds were derived, along with organ-level instability metrics.Main results: Radiomics stability exhibited strongly nonlinear, organ-dependent behavior. Feature-level analysis identified frequent sigmoid-associated collapse patterns with high descriptive model fits (R²>0.90). The liver showed the highest instability burden (30.8% unstable features), followed by esophagus and kidneys (18-20%). Texture features were the primary source of instability, whereas shape features remained robust. Organ-level trajectories demonstrated heterogeneous responses, with some organs maintaining high stability (0.80-0.95) across DRFs, while others showed sharp declines (down to 0.64). Linear (stable) behavior dominated at the organ level, though masking underlying nonlinear feature dynamics.Significance: Radiomics stability in total-body PET follows nonlinear, phenotype-driven dynamics with identifiable tipping points and organ-specific sensitivity. The proposed framework provides a behavior-based approach for evaluating radiomics robustness and supports the selection of reliable features and organs for robust quantitative imaging and may inform future digital twin-oriented applications.

articles.title: Enrofloxacin Disrupts Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axes in Marine Medaka: Mechanistic Insights from Multiomics and Germ-Free Models.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of antibiotics has resulted in their frequent occurrence in marine environments, yet their ecological risks remain poorly understood. Enrofloxacin (ENR) is one of the most frequently detected antibiotics in aquatic ecosystems. However, its toxicological mechanisms in marine fish remain unclear. Here, multiomics, Vibrio parahemolyticus infection, short chain fatty acid supplementation and germ-free fish models were integrated to investigate ENR induced neurotoxicity and the role of gut microbiota. The results showed that ENR exposure impaired intestinal function in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma), accompanied by behavioral abnormalities, neurotoxicity, and liver injury. ENR also induced gut microbiome dysbiosis and altered SCFAs levels. Furthermore, SCFAs supplementation and germ-free fish experiments provided complementary and supportive evidence that gut microbial dysbiosis and altered SCFAs levels may be involved in ENR neurotoxic responses. Moreover, ENR pretreated fish showed increased susceptibility to V. parahemolyticus challenge, which further disrupted the gut microbiome and aggravated neurological dysfunction. Collectively, these findings suggest that ENR induced neurotoxicity is linked to disruption of the microbiome-gut-brain axis and increased susceptibility to subsequent pathogenic stress. This study provides new insights into antibiotic toxicity in marine fish and supports ecological risk assessment of ENR in marine aquaculture.

articles.title: Ebullition-Enhanced Release of Microplastics from Aquatic Sediment to Overlying Water: An Overlooked Transport Pathway.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquatic systems are typically attributed to wastewater, runoff and atmospheric inputs, whereas the remobilization of sediment-associated MPs by benthic gas ebullition remains poorly understood. Here, we show that air-purged ebullition mobilized four common MPs, polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA), from sediments into the overlying water, with release ratios of 8.9%-12.1% over 9 d. Suspended MP concentrations in the overlying water increased rapidly during the first 48 h, followed by slower release and eventual plateauing, with the decelerating release behavior empirically described by a power-law model. Theoretical calculations suggest that aggregation with suspended sediment can reduce the flotation velocities of MPs from 9.38-9.99 cm·s-1 to 8.64-9.95 cm·s-1. Combined experimental observations and theoretical analyses support a coupled flotation mechanism involving MPs attachment to rising bubbles, bubble-driven flow that counteracts gravitational settling, and transient pressure gradients. These processes could convert sediments from a long-term sink into a secondary source of MPs during ebullition. Overall, this study identifies benthic gas ebullition as an underappreciated pathway for MP remobilization and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding the fate and transport of sediment-associated MPs in aquatic environments.

articles.title: Inhalation of Environmentally Simulated PET Nanoplastics Induces Demyelinating Disorders via the CXCL12/CXCR4 Axis.
articles.abstract: The health threat from airborne nanoplastics (NPs) remains unclear, as despite inhalation being a more direct brain entry route than ingestion, current understanding relies on oral exposure and commercial particle models that obscure realistic risks. Here, by integrating environmentally simulated polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-NPs with an aerosol inhalation model that mirrors real-world human exposure (0.1, 1, and 10 mg/m3), we demonstrate that chronic NP inhalation translocated to the brain and induced demyelination, neuroinflammation, and cognitive deficits. The most pronounced effects were observed at the highest exposure dose (10 mg/m3), which is relevant to the occupational settings. Mechanistically, NP exposure triggered astrocytic CXCL12 release, leading to CXCR4-dependent microglial activation and cytokine network dysregulation. In vitro, blockade of CXCR4 with AMD3100 attenuated NP-induced microglial migration and oligodendrocytic myelin basic protein reduction. Our study thus definitively links realistic airborne NP exposure to the key neuropathological features of demyelinating disorders and pinpoints a modifiable molecular pathway that could inform exposure-based preventive strategies. These findings underscore the need for further assessment of airborne NP risks, particularly in occupational settings.

articles.title: Wearable Sensors and VOC Monitoring: Data Fusion and Machine Learning for Non-Invasive Disease Detection.
articles.abstract: Emerging technologies that detect volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emanating from the body enable rapid and non-invasive detection of diseases. Respiratory illnesses, in particular, can be identified through measurement of VOCs in exhaled breath. However, the low specificity of some methods leaves room for improvement. By combining information from multiple data streams, we can potentially improve on the results obtained from using each data stream individually. Here we evaluate a novel data fusion approach combining a wearable vitals monitor and exhaled breath VOCs for the classification of asthma patients. The wearable vitals monitor or "e-glove" measures key information such as skin temperature, trans-epidermal water loss (TEWL), heart rate, and galvanic skin response (GSR), while the breath VOC data (measured by gold standard gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, GC-MS) provide insight into the biochemical and metabolic state of the body. Data fusion is a process used in many applications for combining information from disparate sources. We leverage data fusion in this case to achieve superior classification accuracy using the integrated data streams.
