The low-level data fusion achieved a higher ROC AUC score (0.88) in asthma classification than the breath VOC-only approach (0.72, p<0.001). These results are promising for the future data analysis workflows for non-invasive diagnostic and health monitoring.

articles.title: Prevention Before Therapy in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: The Clinical, Economic, and Human Case for Weighting Resources Upstream.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is projected to become the second-leading cause of US cancer death by 2030, and survival is dominated by stage at diagnosis: roughly 44% at five years for localized disease versus about 3% with distant metastases. Only about 15% of cases are detected while localized, surgery reaches a minority of patients, and no validated screening test exists for average-risk adults. This topical review examines the biologic, clinical, economic, psychological, equity, and therapeutic evidence bearing on where scarce resources should be directed. The long interval between initiating mutation and invasive disease provides a mechanistic rationale for prevention and interception, and the modifiable exposures of obesity, tobacco, type 2 diabetes, and alcohol act largely within that window. We consider innovations that extend prevention beyond lifestyle advice-incretin-based weight management, risk stratification anchored in new-onset diabetes and biomarkers, and immunoprevention-together with early-onset disease, implementation and policy, and the barriers and evidentiary limits that temper these arguments. We propose a three-tier framework of primary prevention, early detection in high-risk groups, and therapy, and argue that research, policy, and clinical investment should be weighted upstream, because every case prevented spares the cost, capacity, and suffering that the downstream tiers must otherwise absorb.

articles.title: Aβ17-22 Derived Hexapeptide Segment Inhibits Islet Amyloid Polypeptide (IAPP) Aggregation and Attenuates Cytotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Misfolding and aggregation of islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) are associated with the decline of β-cells in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Design of short peptide-based inhibitors of β-sheet-rich amyloid plaque formation is challenging due to the dynamic nature of the amyloid species. The key sequences involved in cross-amyloid interactions shed light on the design of peptide-based inhibitors. Amyloid-β peptide (Aβ) has nearly 50% similarity and 25% identity with IAPP sequences, and their cross-interactions have been suggested to link T2D pathogenesis with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Here, we show that a short anionic amphiphilic hexapeptide (DM-P02) containing the Aβ domain (Leu17-Glu22) effectively suppresses aggregation and oligomerization of IAPP by predominantly interacting with its cationic N-terminus. DM-P02 also binds strongly to IAPP in pancreatic β-cell lines, as confirmed by confocal imaging, and protects them from IAPP aggregation-associated cytotoxicity. Our study underlines the therapeutic potential of short peptides for developing anti-amyloid agents.

articles.title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth regression was used for sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression.

CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further validation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Usability, educational engagement, and patient-reported outcomes in a mobile asthma intervention.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mobile health tools offer scalable strategies for asthma self-management, but relationships between usability, engagement, and clinical outcomes remain unclear. We evaluated whether usability of ASTHMAXcel PRO, a mobile asthma education and self-management application, promotes educational engagement and whether early engagement predicts asthma outcomes.

METHODS: Adults with asthma on daily controller therapy from three Bronx clinics participated in a 12-month study using ASTHMAXcel PRO in addition to usual care. Usability was assessed using the Questionnaire for User Interface Satisfaction (QUIS). Early engagement was measured during the first two months, with high educational engagement defined as the top quartile of chapters completed. Outcomes included asthma control (Asthma Control Test [ACT]), asthma-related quality of life (mini-Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire [mini-AQLQ]), and composite asthma-related healthcare utilization. Associations were examined using mixed-effects, interaction, logistic, and mediation analyses adjusted for age, gender, and baseline outcome status.

RESULTS: Among 44 participants (mean age 43.75 ± 14.07 years; 84.1% female; 95.5% non-White), higher usability was associated with greater early engagement (OR 2.39 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI 1.28-5.19, p = 0.01). ACT and mini-AQLQ improved over time. However, early engagement was not associated with differential improvements in either outcome. Baseline outcome status was the strongest predictor of longitudinal outcomes, and no mediation effects were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In this urban, high-burden cohort, usability predicted early engagement but not clinical benefit. Baseline outcome status remained the strongest predictor of longitudinal outcomes. These findings suggest that digital asthma interventions may require targeted, content-specific engagement strategies beyond usability alone to improve outcomes.

articles.title: METTL3 destabilizes RFX7 to ameliorate PDGF-BB-induced airway smooth muscle cell dysfunction and inflammation in an in vitro model of childhood asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood asthma represents a significant global health burden, characterized by chronic airway inflammation and remodeling. Regulatory factor X7 (RFX7) has emerged as a potential key player in asthma pathogenesis. However, its specific role in modulating airway smooth muscle cell (ASMC) dysfunction-a hallmark of asthma pathology-remains poorly understood.

METHODS: An in vitro asthma model was established by stimulating airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs) with platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB). Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting were employed to measure the mRNA and protein expression levels of RFX7 and METTL3, respectively. Functional assays, including 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine incorporation, Transwell, and wound-healing assays, were utilized to evaluate ASMC proliferation, invasion, and migration. Inflammatory responses were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) targeting interleukin-6 (IL-6).

RESULTS: RFX7 expression levels were significantly elevated in the serum of pediatric asthma patients and in PDGF-BB-induced ASMCs, whereas METTL3 expression was downregulated. PDGF-BB stimulation enhanced ASMC proliferation, invasion, and migration, all of which were markedly attenuated by RFX7 knockdown. Furthermore, RFX7 deficiency reduced PDGF-BB-induced production of IL-6, TNF-α, ROS, and MDA, as well as the proportion of CD86-positive macrophages. Notably, METTL3 exhibited a negative correlation with RFX7 in patient sera and destabilized RFX7 transcripts in a YTHDF2-dependent manner. Consequently, overexpression of METTL3 alleviated PDGF-BB-induced ASMC dysfunction by downregulating RFX7.

CONCLUSION: METTL3-mediated destabilization of RFX7 ameliorated PDGF-BB-induced ASMC proliferation, migration, and invasion, while simultaneously suppressing inflammation, oxidative stress, and macrophage polarization. Targeting this METTL3-RFX7 axis may offer a novel therapeutic strategy to mitigate airway remodeling and inflammation in childhood asthma.

articles.title: Correlation of Neuron-Specific Enolase and S100ß Protein Levels, Inflammatory Cytokines, and Neurological Injury in Children Undergoing Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The systemic inflammatory response syndrome to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) affects all organ systems including the brain. Perioperative brain injury in children with congenital heart disease is often clinically silent in the acute perioperative period and may not be detected until patients are older. The plasma biomarkers neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and S100ß protein show potential for detecting neurological injury in the perioperative period.

OBJECTIVES: The three objectives of this study were to examine the correlation of NSE and S100ß protein levels with inflammatory cytokines, parameters of CPB, and the development of neurological injury in the intensive care unit following cardiac surgery in children.

METHODS: 50 children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB had blood samples drawn at three time points: after induction of anesthesia, 30 min post-CPB, and 24 h post-CPB. Blood samples were analyzed for NSE, S100ß, and the inflammatory cytokines IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. Data were collected on CPB durations and neurological injury diagnosed in the postoperative period.

RESULTS: NSE and S100ß increased significantly following bypass and correlated with increases of IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. There was a significant positive correlation of NSE and S100ß with duration of CPB, and of S100ß with duration of aortic cross clamp. Three patients suffered neurological insult. These patients had greater levels of NSE during the post-CPB period (p = 0.02) and S100ß at 24 h post-CPB (p = 0.02) than patients without neurological deficits.

CONCLUSION: The positive correlation between NSE, S100ß, inflammatory cytokines, and neurological deficits suggests that the systemic inflammatory response to CPB may contribute to neurological injury and that NSE and S100ß may be useful tools to detect neurological injury following CPB.

articles.title: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Associated With Severe Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TCM) is a transient syndrome of cardiac dysfunction with no occlusive coronary arterial disease, which may mimic an ischemic cardiac event. The pathogenesis of TCM is thought to be primarily driven by the effects of a temporary catecholamine surge on cardiac and vascular tissue. Medetomidine (an a2 agonist commonly found in the Philadelphia fentanyl supply) withdrawal is characterized by agitation and sympathetic hyperactivity that can precipitate a catecholamine surge. Though withdrawal from other Central Nervous System (CNS)-depressing substances such as opioids and clonidine have been found to be associated with TCM, there is little documentation of this phenomenon occurring from medetomidine withdrawal.

CASE: A 51-year-old woman with no reported medical history other than opioid use disorder presented to the emergency department due to concern for withdrawal from fentanyl and medetomidine. Her opioid withdrawal was well controlled with methadone and oxycodone. Shortly after coming off her dexmedetomidine infusion (started for medetomidine withdrawal), she developed acute ST-segment changes on electrocardiogram, elevated troponin levels on bloodwork, and regional wall-motion abnormalities on transthoracic echocardiogram. Her coronary angiography showed no occlusion and repeat cardiac laboratory workup days later had normalized with improvement in ejection fraction on cardiac echocardiography and magnetic resonance imaging. This signifies a temporary stress cardiomyopathy, likely from a2 agonist withdrawal.

DISCUSSION: This case describes TCM in a patient experiencing medetomidine withdrawal. This patient's cardiac dysfunction was transient, temporally correlating with the cessation of her dexmedetomidine infusion. This suggests an a2 agonist mediated withdrawal leading to sympathetic hyperactivity which can precipitate TCM.

articles.title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) carry substantial cardiorenal risks. Conventional immunosuppressive therapies primarily target inflammation but leave a burden of residual renal and metabolic damage. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide clear cardiorenal protection in general populations, but data specific to SLE remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of SGLT2i in patients with SLE and LN.MethodsComprehensive searches across five electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus) were conducted up to April 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing SGLT2i in adult SLE/LN patients. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize cardiorenal and safety outcomes using R Software.ResultsSix studies published between 2024 and 2025 were included. Pooled data demonstrated that SGLT2i use was associated with a significant improvement in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) compared to controls (MD: 4.02; 95% CI: 1.39-6.65; I2 = 60.1%). SGLT2i significantly reduced the risks of progression to end-stage kidney disease (RR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.25-0.56; I2 = 11.0%), heart failure development (RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.56-0.75; I2 = 0.0%), incident lupus nephritis (RR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; I2 = 0.0%), and re-hospitalizations (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.57-0.79; I2 = 0.0%). Furthermore, a significant reduction in all-cause mortality was observed (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36-0.86; I2 = 76.2%). SGLT2i treatment demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across the included cohorts. The certainty of evidence for these findings was rated as low to very low, and results remain vulnerable to residual confounding from variables such as disease activity, corticosteroid burden, and immunosuppressive regimen.ConclusionPreliminary exploratory evidence suggests potential associations between SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiorenal outcomes in lupus nephritis. Given the low certainty of evidence and vulnerability to residual confounding from disease-specific variables, these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in well-designed randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Outcomes of the surviving co-twin after spontaneous single intrauterine demise in stage V twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesThis review aims to estimate perinatal outcomes of co-twins following a single intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD) occurring in pregnancies complicated by spontaneous Stage V twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), focusing on gestational age at delivery, birth weight, and neonatal death.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines and Cochrane methodology. PubMed, EMBASE, SCOPUS, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched up to March 2026. Eligible studies included spontaneous TTTS Stage V pregnancies with reported outcomes for the surviving co-twins. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models, while outcomes unsuitable for quantitative pooling were summarized narratively. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.ResultsFive studies including 32 surviving co-twins were included. The mean gestational age at birth was 29.96 weeks (95% CI 26.80 to 33.12), and the pooled neonatal mortality rate was 33.33% (95% CI 18.97 to 51.65). Birth weight was reported in three studies including 21 surviving co-twins, with mean values ranging from 616.67 to 1691.10 g across studies.ConclusionStage V TTTS may be associated with prematurity, low birth weight, and high neonatal mortality rate. Given the very low certainty of evidence, findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are needed to improve outcome counseling.

articles.title: Treatment attrition and outcomes of myeloma patients in Finland: a real-world study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Relapses, need for further treatment lines and significant treatment attrition are typical for multiple myeloma (MM). This retrospective study investigates attrition and outcomes among MM patients in Finland. Patient, material and methods: Study included all adult MM patients (n = 1733) diagnosed and treated in four hospital districts in Finland in 2013-2022. Data were collected from hospital data lakes, Statistics Finland and Social Insurance Institution. Treatment attrition was defined as death before next treatment line.

RESULTS: By the end of follow-up 31% of patients without stem cell transplantation (non-SCT) had died before initiation of second line treatment (2L), compared with 5% of stem-cell transplant (SCT) patients. The factors associating with this early attrition in the non-SCT cohort were older age (over 75 years), higher comorbidity burden, International Staging System (ISS), and (R)-ISS scores (p < 0.001). Furthermore, non-SCT patients were more likely administered less intensive therapy during 1L (p < 0.001). During the first 6 months post diagnosis in the non-SCT cohort, the most common immediate cause of death was MM. Also, during later stages MM was responsible for 54% of deaths in the non-SCT and 68% in the SCT cohorts whereas infections were linked principally with early deaths before 2L treatment.

INTERPRETATION: This study highlights significant treatment attrition across disease course and also early mortality especially in the non-SCT cohort resulting primarily from progressive MM or infections. The findings underscore the need for more tolerable and effective anti-myeloma treatments in earlier course of the disease to enhance patient survival.

articles.title: Long-term ozone exposure and adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation: the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain at high risk of cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events, but evidence on long-term ozone (O3) exposure in this population is limited.

OBJECTIVES: We examined whether long-term O3 exposure was associated with adverse cerebrovascular and cardiovascular outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort of 20757 adults with prevalent AF residing in Podlaskie Voivodeship, northeastern Poland, in 2014, with follow-up through December 31, 2019. O3, nitrogen dioxide and fine particulate matter concentrations were estimated using the GEM-AQ model and assigned by residential municipality. The primary endpoint was a composite of ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke-related death; cardiovascular mortality was the key secondary endpoint. Associations were estimated using Fine-Gray competing-risk models with annually updated previous-year O3 exposure, adjusted for clinical characteristics, meteorology, area-level socioeconomic status, co-pollutants and outdoor artificial light at night.

RESULTS: The mean (SD) age was 72.6 (11.5) years, and 52.9% were women. The median follow-up was 5.6 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-6), during which 3,139 primary composite events and 5,400 cardiovascular deaths occurred. The median annual O₃ concentration was 43.48 μg/m³ (IQR, 42.6-46.63). Each IQR increase in annually updated O₃ exposure (4.03 μg/m³) was associated with higher risks of the primary composite endpoint (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.27; 95% CI, 1.02-1.59), cardiovascular mortality (sHR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29), and ischemic stroke (sHR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.08-1.77). Associations were directionally consistent across adjustment strategies and sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term O3 exposure was associated with higher cerebrovascular and cardiovascular risks in patients with AF. O3 may contribute to residual risk in this clinically vulnerable population and warrants evaluation in other high-risk cardiovascular cohorts.

articles.title: Mapping policy instruments and challenges in health innovation development: implications for the role of early HTA - an umbrella review.
articles.journal: International journal of technology assessment in health care
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Health innovation encounters challenges across the innovation lifecycle. Although various policy instruments aim to support innovation, their alignment with stage-specific challenges remains unclear. This study synthesizes evidence to examine how innovation challenges and policy responses are distributed across the health innovation lifecycle, with particular attention to the role of early Health Technology Assessment (early HTA).

METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of review-level studies that examined health innovation challenges and related policy instruments. A comprehensive literature search was performed across five databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL. Twenty-four eligible studies were included and synthesized using a well-established analytical framework. Innovation challenges and policy instruments were mapped across stages of the development pathway and linked to the contributions of early HTA.

RESULTS: Innovation challenges were most pronounced in product design and clinical trial stages. Institutional barriers, including lengthy approval processes, became more prominent during regulatory approval and market access. Eighty policy responses were identified and clustered into economic, regulatory, and informational instruments. Economic measures were concentrated in product design and clinical trial stages, while regulatory instruments focused on regulatory approval and market access. Early HTA emerged as a complementary decision-support approach that may help address product design and clinical trial stages challenges.

CONCLUSIONS: There is a clear misalignment between where innovation challenges arise and where policy responses are applied. Integrating early HTA more systematically into innovation policy frameworks could help address challenges in product design and clinical trial stages and improve the likelihood of successful innovation adoption.

articles.title: Clinical Risk Factors for Advanced Fibrosis in Pathology-Proven Steatotic Liver Disease: Emphasis on Nonelder Subjects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) may lead to advanced liver diseases. We aimed to identify clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis in pathology-proven SLD patients in a hepatitis B virus (HBV) endemic population, with emphasis on nonelder subjects.

METHODS: Adult SLD patients diagnosed via pathology at National Taiwan University Hospital between June 2009 and December 2023 were recruited. Advanced fibrosis was defined as F2 to F4 fibrosis. Patients were stratified by age (< 50 years defined as nonelder), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and HBV infection. Clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis and at-risk steatohepatitis were investigated, and the predictive performance of noninvasive scores was examined.

RESULTS: Among 223 pathology-proven SLD patients, older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.04), alcohol consumption (OR: 5.77), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (OR: 2.13), chronic HBV infection (OR: 2.52), and obesity (OR: 2.64) were independent risk factors for advanced fibrosis. In the nonelder subgroup, older age (OR: 1.10) and obesity (OR: 3.75) were significant. In the MASLD subgroup, older age (OR: 1.04), hypertension (OR: 2.31), T2DM (OR: 3.07), and chronic HBV infection (OR: 3.59) remained significant. Obesity (OR: 4.14) was a significant risk factor for at-risk steatohepatitis in the nonelder subgroup. NAFLD fibrosis score had the highest AUROC (0.724) for advanced fibrosis in the entire cohort, while FIB-4 performed best in nonelder subjects.

CONCLUSIONS: Older age, alcohol, T2DM, chronic HBV infection, and obesity were associated with advanced fibrosis. Risk factors and noninvasive score performance varied in nonelder subjects.

articles.title: Redox-Active Nanoceria Integrated with Glucose Oxidase for Glucose-Triggered Metformin Release: Promising Nanocarrier for Managing Oxidative Stress and Hyperglycemia in Diabetes Pathophysiology.
articles.abstract: Development of a glucose-responsive drug delivery platform remains a promising strategy for self-regulated treatment of diabetes mellitus. In the present study, we developed a multifunctional nanocarrier system for the glucose-sensitive delivery of metformin (Met) based upon amine-functionalized nanoceria (NC-NH2) coupled with glucose oxidase (GOx) and capped with dextran. Nanoceria's inherent ability to scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) was made possible by its nanozyme feature, and GOx converts glucose into gluconic acid, and thereby causing drug release in a glucose-responsive manner. Drug release was controlled by the dextran shell, which served as a biocompatible gatekeeper. Under hyperglycemic conditions, the synthesized nanocarrier (NC-GOx-Met-Dex) demonstrated regulated, glucose-triggered metformin release with little release at normoglycemic levels. NC-GOx-Met-Dex showed good structural stability under physiologically simulated circumstances, selective glucose-dependent drug release kinetics in cell-free, in vitro, and ex vivo systems, and promising cellular uptake in muscle cells without causing any cytotoxicity. NC-GOx-Met-Dex enhanced glucose uptake, glucose utilization and translocation of glucose transporter protein (GLUT4) compared to the metformin-alone-treated group in palmitic acid-treated (PA, 0.75 mM) muscle cells. Further in vivo studies showed that compared to metformin alone-treated group, the nanocarrier group showed remarkable glycemic management, improvement of insulin levels, and increased metformin bioavailability in muscle tissues in animal models of diabetes mellitus. Nevertheless, NC-GOx-Met-Dex gavaging to untreated animals did not cause any abnormal behavior or adverse effects, and levels of hepato-renal biomarkers, as well as blood cell profiling, were comparable to the untreated group. In general, this research provides a viable strategy for personalized diabetes therapy through the use of a dual and multifunctional nanosystem capable of responding to hyperglycemia while preventing oxidative stress.

articles.title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste.
articles.abstract: Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800-5050 nm and width: 780-970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst's analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

articles.title: Children's Surgery: The Missing Link in the Global Child Survival Agenda.
articles.abstract: Global child health is at an inflection point. Under-five mortality has fallen substantially over recent decades, yet progress is slowing and preventable deaths and disability remain concentrated in low- and middle-income countries. As mortality from vaccine-preventable diseases and other infections declines, birth defects and other surgically treatable conditions account for an increasing share of the residual burden. For many children, access to timely, safe and affordable surgical, anesthesia and perioperative care is the difference between survival, disability and death. Yet these services remain insufficiently embedded in child health policy, service delivery and universal health coverage. Children's surgery should therefore be understood not as a peripheral specialty, but as an essential component of integrated services to improve child health outcomes. Congenital anomalies make this case clear. Outcomes for surgically treatable conditions differ starkly by setting, reflecting inequities in early recognition, safe referral, anesthesia, operative and postoperative care, infection prevention, and follow-up. The same services are also required for injuries, burns, surgical infections, complications of sickle cell disease and acute abdominal emergencies. Strengthening them would extend well beyond specialist surgery; it would build the capacity of health systems to respond to some of the most time-sensitive and disabling conditions affecting children. Recent World Health Assembly resolutions on operative care, universal health coverage and newborn screening provide a clear mandate for action. The next phase of the global child survival agenda must recognize children's surgical care as an essential service to be planned, adequately financed and routinely monitored. Integrating surgical, anesthesia, perioperative and rehabilitation care into child health programmes is critical to avert preventable deaths, reduce lifelong disability, protect families from catastrophic costs and ensure that children everywhere have the opportunity not only to survive but also to thrive.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Comprehensive assessment of the cerebral pressure-flow relationship in chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with blood pressure (BP) instability and increased cerebrovascular risk, but how CKD alters cerebral pressure-flow relationship remains unclear. Seventeen adults with moderate to severe CKD and 17 controls completed a multimetric protocol including resting supine recordings to assess spontaneous BP-middle cerebral artery mean blood velocity (MCAv) interactions using wavelet phase synchrony index and Granger based conditional joint transfer entropy, acute BP increases via 3 min isometric handgrip at 30% maximal voluntary contraction, acute BP decreases using sit to stand, and forced ABP oscillations using repeated squat-stands at 0.05 Hz and 0.10 Hz. Mean arterial pressure, MCAv, and end-tidal carbon dioxide partial pressure (PETCO2) were continuously recorded. Transfer function metrics and MCAv responses to transient mean arterial pressure increases and decreases were comparable between groups. Directional sensitivity was present in both groups at 0.05 Hz only. Wavelet phase synchrony index was elevated in ultra low frequency bands (0.030-0.035 Hz and 0.035-0.040 Hz), and Granger based conditional joint transfer entropy increased by 55% in forward MAP→MCAv information transfer in CKD persisting after PETCO2 correction. No between-group differences were detected using the linear assessments employed in this study, whereas nonlinear analyses identified differences during spontaneous resting conditions.

articles.title: Tricuspid regurgitation: choosing the right treatment for the right patient at the right time.
articles.journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery

articles.title: Widespread skeletal muscle involvement on 18FDG PET/CT in nocardiosis.
EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

articles.title: An Attending-Directed Intervention to Enhance Interprofessional Teaching on ICU Rounds.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interprofessional teaching (IPT) during rounds may enhance teamwork and collaborative patient care, but previous studies have shown low rates of IPT during intensive care unit (ICU) rounds. We designed a study to explore contributions by interprofessional providers (IPPs) during ICU rounds and an attending-targeted intervention to promote IPT.

METHODS: Using a novel observation tool, we collected details regarding contributions made by IPPs during rounds in two ICUs at an academic medical center. A study team member conducted observations for six weeks before and after implementation of an attending-directed intervention. Comparisons were made between pre- and post-intervention data.

RESULTS: Before the intervention, six attendings were observed for 59 patient-rounds with 309 contributions recorded, and after, eleven attendings were observed for 94 patient-rounds with 512 contributions recorded. The majority of contributions from IPPs were classified as "reporting" (pre/post: 42.7% vs. 43.6%) and "observing" (pre/post: 29.1% vs. 29.7%). "Teaching" contributions were rare, but increased from 3.9% (12/309) to 4.7% (24/512) of all contributions (p > 0.05). The mean number of contributions per patient did not change after the intervention (5.24 vs. 5.45), and the types of contributions were similar across different attendings. When an IPP spontaneously provided a recommendation (pre: 33, post: 55), the contribution often changed the care plan (pre/post: 97.0% (32/33), 83.6% (46/55)).

CONCLUSIONS: IPPs predominantly contribute to rounds by reporting data and providing observations. An intervention to improve attending facilitation of IPT did not affect rates of teaching. However, recommendations made by IPPs consistently impacted the patient care plan.

articles.title: Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy (PERT) in Pancreatic Cancer: First U.S. Consensus Highlights on Dosing, Management, and Provider Inertia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) is a highly prevalent, yet modifiable determinant of treatment tolerance in pancreatic cancer (PC). Despite its clinical significance, management remains inconsistent due to a lack of oncology-specific guidelines. This project aimed to establish the first U.S. multidisciplinary consensus to standardize pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) dosing, education, and longitudinal management in pancreatic oncology.

METHODS: A mixed-methods design was employed, integrating a parallel literature review, six virtual focus groups with patients and clinicians (n = 28), and a formal modified Delphi process. A multidisciplinary panel of 17 experts, including medical, surgical, and radiation oncologists, advanced practice providers, and oncology dietitians, independently rated and refined draft statements over two iterative rounds. Consensus was defined a priori as ≥ 70% agreement.

RESULTS: The process yielded 15 final Consensus Statements, all achieving ≥ 81% agreement. This manuscript highlights a critical subset of six statements focusing on clinical application (CS 10-15), which achieved 94%-100% consensus. Recommendations define standardized starting doses (48,000-72,000 lipase units per meal), evidence-based titration protocols, multi-level patient education requirements, and strategies to mitigate financial toxicity and pill burden.

CONCLUSION: These consensus statements provide a practical, evidence-based framework to reduce provider inertia and practice variability. Broad implementation of these standards offers a vital opportunity to stabilize nutritional status, improve quality of life, and optimize treatment continuity for patients with PC.

articles.title: Geo-economic variations in structure and organization of intensive care units: the ISOREA survey.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Little is known on critical care services globally. This study aimed to describe ICU resources and organization across countries and assess variability by income group, between countries, and within countries.

METHODS: Participating centers provided structured data on hospital and ICU characteristics via electronic case report form (January 2018 to July 2020). Questionnaire included 237 items covering general characteristics (2 topics) and ICU resources and organization (18 topics). We computed standardized functional domain scores (ISOREA score), classified ICUs using Marshall criteria, and readiness for essential emergency and critical care using a modified Schell score.

RESULTS: A total of 1,426 ICUs from five continents were recruited, and 1,225 were analyzed, from high-income countries (HICs, 58%), upper-middle-income (20%), and low/lower-middle-income countries (LLMICs, 22%). Most ICUs were in referral centers (90%) and large urban areas (80%). Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, with 88% showing higher levels in HICs and lower levels in LLMICs. Six domains showed major disparities: extracorporeal support, respiratory support, emergency access to interventional radiology and surgery, neurology and trauma care, patient file and general monitoring, and cardiovascular and hemodynamic monitoring. According to the Marshall classification, 79% of ICUs in HICs were classified as level III, whereas 55% of ICUs in LLMICs were classified as level I. Domains with higher ISOREA scores varied primarily between countries, whereas lower-performing domains exhibited greater variability across ICUs within the same country. Adjustment for income group reduced, but did not eliminate, country-level clustering.

CONCLUSION: Substantial disparities exist in ICU resources and organization across income groups, countries, and ICUs. ICU capacities appeared multidimensional, extending beyond resource limitations.

articles.title: Cross-Ancestry Analysis of the 1q31 Th2-Associated Interval in Steroid-Dependent Asthma.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: Hepatitis-Associated Aplastic Anemia in Children and Adolescents: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis-associated aplastic anemia (HAAA) is a rare but life-threatening subtype of acquired aplastic anemia (AA) that predominantly affects children and adolescents, characterized by bone marrow failure developing weeks to months following acute hepatitis. Although HAAA accounts for a small proportion of AA cases, it presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and remains poorly understood. Most cases are seronegative, with no identifiable viral pathogen, supporting an immune-mediated pathophysiology. Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated cytotoxic T-cell activation, reduced regulatory T-cell function, and a shared immune target within hepatic and hematopoietic tissues. HAAA follows a variable course of hepatitis and pancytopenia, which necessitates a high index of suspicion and thorough evaluation to exclude inherited and secondary causes of bone marrow failure. Management strategies are largely extrapolated from severe AA and include supportive care, immunosuppressive therapy with antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. While outcomes have improved with modern therapy, relapse, treatment failure, and clonal evolution remain challenges. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnostic approach, treatment options, and outcomes of pediatric HAAA, highlighting critical gaps in evidence and the need for prospective studies to guide risk stratification and therapy optimization.

articles.title: Providers' Perspective on Barriers and Solutions to Adult Day Services Provision in Ohio.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: BackgroundAdult day services (ADS) are essential home- and community-based supports, yet providers continue to face significant post-COVID operational and engagement challenges. Limited state-level evidence constrains efforts to strengthen ADS capacity.ObjectiveTo identify barriers experienced by ADS providers in Ohio and provider-driven solutions to sustain and strengthen services in the post-COVID environment.MethodsA sequential mixed-methods design integrated pre-survey focus groups (n = 17), a statewide provider survey (n = 28), and post-survey focus groups (n = 11). Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis were used to synthesize findings.ResultsTwo themes emerged: (1) Participants, Family, and Community Engagement, characterized by limited public awareness, caregiver hesitation, and unstable referral pathways; and (2) Operational Challenges and Limited Resources, including financial strain, staffing shortages, transportation barriers, administrative burden, and facility limitations. Providers identified solutions such as statewide education, workforce development, shared transportation models, and regulatory streamlining.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).

RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

articles.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care.

METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1. Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants' effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case-control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed.

RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case-control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants.

CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

Interrelationships Between Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Domains, Age, and Sex for Patients With Heart Failure: Findings From the CHAMP-HF and CORC Registries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) domains independently quantify patients' symptoms, physical and social functioning, and quality of life, the interrelationships between domains (eg, symptoms impacting physical limitations) have not been described, nor whether these vary by age or sex.

METHODS: Cross-sectional data from adult outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction from 2 multicenter US registries, the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (2015-2017) and Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (2001-2002), were used to fit recursive path analysis models relating age, sex, and KCCQ domain scores. The interrelationships of these factors were quantified using unstandardized and standardized effect estimates. Unstandardized effects denote the linear effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable in units specific to both variables. Standardized effects are unitless and are obtained by multiplying the unstandardized effect by the ratio of the standard deviations of the dependent and independent variables.

RESULTS: The analytic cohorts included 4839 patients from the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (mean age, 66.1±12.5 years, 29.3% women) and 547 patients from the Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (mean age, 66±12 years, 23.8% women). Standardized effect estimates revealed moderate to strong interrelationships among the KCCQ domains (effect size range, 0.34-0.70). Symptoms were strongly associated with all other domains (range, 0.61-0.70). Quality of life was most associated with symptoms and social limitations (range: 0.48-0.60), and less so with physical limitations (effect size=0.34). By comparison, the associations of age and sex with KCCQ domains were much smaller (effect sizes <0.2), and no interactions by age and sex were found.

CONCLUSIONS: KCCQ domains were strongly interrelated, and these relationships did not differ appreciably by age or sex. These data enhance the interpretation of KCCQ domain scores in research and clinical practice; in particular, symptoms and social limitations may be key drivers of impaired quality of life in heart failure. Targeted interventions prioritizing these domains may most effectively improve patients' overall health status.

articles.title: Dietary strategies to combat arterial stiffness in cardiometabolic disease: a network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and hypertension (HTN) are leading causes of global morbidity and mortality. Arterial stiffness, assessed via augmentation index (AIx) and pulse wave velocity (PWV), serves as an independent prognostic marker of vascular damage; however, the comparative efficacy of dietary interventions on these parameters remains poorly characterized. This network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to compare and rank the efficacy of dietary interventions, including supplements, nutraceuticals, and dietary patterns, on AIx and PWV in individuals with CVD or HTN. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to January 2025. Two independent reviewers screened and extracted data following PRISMA-NMA guidelines. A total of 48 RCTs comprising 2719 participants and 31 dietary interventions were included. Study quality and certainty of evidence (CoE) were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and GRADE approach, respectively. A random-effects NMA within a frequentist framework estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For PWV, grape seed extract (MD: -1.70; 95%CI: -3.36 to -0.04; CoE: Moderate) and vitamin B9 (MD: -1.46; 95%CI: -2.61 to -0.31; CoE: Moderate) reduced arterial stiffness versus placebo. No intervention reached significance for AIx, though alpha-linolenic acid, dietary nitrate, and wine extract showed the greatest numerical improvements. Sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with the primary analyses, with no publication bias detected. The grape seed extract and folic acid show potential to reduce arterial stiffness. Future population-specific, dose-optimized RCTs are warranted to establish definitive therapeutic recommendations.

articles.title: Nonlinear Associations of Body Muscle-to-Fat Ratio With Long-Term Prognosis in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As weight-loss therapies are increasingly incorporated into clinical practice for MASLD, assessing body composition has become increasingly important. Body muscle-to-fat ratio (BMFR) may provide an intuitive and integrated measure of body composition balance, but its association with long-term prognosis in MASLD remains unclear.

METHODS: We studied 83 006 UK Biobank participants with MASLD. BMFR was calculated as whole-body muscle mass divided by whole-body fat mass using bioelectrical impedance analysis. Restricted cubic spline, threshold-effect and two-piecewise Cox models assessed associations with liver-related events (LREs), cardiovascular events (CVEs), cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality, adjusting for BMI and other confounders.

RESULTS: BMFR showed significant non-linear associations with all outcomes. Sex-specific inflection points were identified for each outcome. For LREs, the thresholds were 2.82 in men and 1.45 in women; below these thresholds, each 1-SD increase in BMFR was associated with a lower risk of LREs (men: HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.75-0.98; women: HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.63-0.83), whereas above them it was associated with a higher risk (men: HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.07-1.36; women: HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.11-1.59). For CVEs, the thresholds were 2.03 in men and 1.48 in women; below these thresholds, each 1-SD increase in BMFR was associated with a lower risk in both sexes (men: HR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.70-0.85; women: HR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.81-0.89), whereas above them the association was not significant in men but was associated with a higher risk in women (HR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.09-1.30). Cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality showed sex-specific non-linear patterns similar to those observed for CVEs.

CONCLUSIONS: In MASLD, BMFR was associated with liver-related and cardiovascular outcomes. Associations were generally U-shaped in women; in men, they were U-shaped for LREs and closer to L-shaped for cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. BMFR may provide complementary information on body composition beyond BMI. Further studies are needed to validate these exploratory findings.

articles.title: Immunoglobulin kinetics and infection patterns across venetoclax-based regimens in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
articles.abstract: CLL causes immune dysfunction, which drives infections and is responsible for significant morbidity. We sought to build on prior literature suggesting venetoclax-based treatments may restore humoral immunity. In a retrospective single-center study of 93 patients (98 treatment courses) across venetoclax monotherapy, venetoclax plus anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (mAb), and venetoclax plus BTK inhibitor regimens, we tracked immunoglobulin levels and infections. We found Ig patterns over time differed by regimen, with IgA suppression most statistically significant with anti-CD20 combinations. Superior IgA reconstitution (SIR) occurred in 21% of patients and was not associated with undetectable minimal residual disease (uMRD). Despite Ig recovery, cumulative infection burden did not differ by MRD status. Our findings suggest that while there is reconstitution of humoral immunity, immunoglobulin levels alone do not determine infection susceptibility.

articles.title: An in Silico Characterisation of ATP-Binding Cassette Transporter Proteins Across Five Endodontic Pathogens: Implications for Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence.
articles.abstract:
AIM: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter proteins play pivotal roles in antimicrobial resistance and bacterial virulence. However, their characterisation across major endodontic pathogens remains limited. This study aimed to characterise ABC transporter proteins in silico across five endodontic pathogens and to investigate their implications for antimicrobial resistance and virulence.

METHODOLOGY: Reference genome-predicted proteomes of Enterococcus faecalis, Porphyromonas gingivalis, Fusobacterium nucleatum, Actinomyces naeslundii and Dialister invisus were retrieved from the National Center for Biotechnology Information RefSeq database. ABC transporter proteins were identified using InterProScan and HMMER and assigned to five functional categories based on Pfam domain signatures. Physicochemical parameters were computed and analysed by principal component analysis, the Kruskal-Wallis test and the chi-square test of independence. Domain architecture and phylogenetic analyses were performed using MAFFT, FastTree and Interactive Tree of Life.

RESULTS: A total of 574 ABC transporter proteins were identified (range: 63-168 per species), with A. naeslundii exhibiting the highest transporter density (55.3 per Mb). Putative multidrug resistance pumps were dominant (78.7%) and were highest in F. nucleatum (87.1%) and E. faecalis (82.2%). Functional category distribution differed significantly between species (χ2 = 22.043, df = 8, p = 0.005). Significant inter-species differences were identified in Grand Average of Hydropathy (GRAVY) score, aromaticity, isoelectric point and instability index (all p < 0.001). BLASTP confirmed the efrAB efflux operon in E. faecalis (EfrA: 99.65%; EfrB: 100.00%) alongside 13 homologue proteins.

CONCLUSIONS: The dominance of putative multidrug resistance pumps, including sequence-confirmed efrAB proteins and 13 homologues in E. faecalis, provides a plausible molecular framework for intrinsic resistance to intracanal medicaments in persistent endodontic infections.

articles.title: Intranasal administration of enalapril confers acute neuroprotection by mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in a rat model of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, with effective treatments hindered by its complex pathophysiology. This study is the first to explore the neuroprotective potential of intranasal enalapril, in mitigating ischemic stroke outcomes through its influence on mitochondrial function.

METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), followed by the intranasal administration of enalapril (0.03 mg/kg) post-ischemia. Neurological function was evaluated after 24 hours of reperfusion through the modified neurological severity score (mNSS), grip strength, and hot plate tests. Brain infarct volume was quantified via Triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood- brain barrier (BBB) integrity was evaluated via the Evans Blue extravasation assay. Additionally, we employed immunofluorescence techniques to assess apoptosis through TUNEL staining and evaluated mitochondrial function by examining mitochondrial swelling, succinate dehydrogenase activity, mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species production.

RESULTS: Intranasal administration of enalapril significantly reduced the infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and attenuated sensorimotor deficits in MCAO rats. These protective effects were closely associated with enhanced regional cerebral blood flow, a significant reduction in neuronal apoptosis, and improved mitochondrial function.

CONCLUSION: Intranasal enalapril may provide a novel approach to neuroprotection in ischemic stroke, potentially through mechanisms that enhance mitochondrial function and reduce neuronal apoptosis.

articles.title: High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema in Children in Mexico City: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Marín, Alejandro Ferreiro, María Paula Ferreiro Soria, Karla Sánchez Olivera, Aranza Suárez Ortega, and Luis Martín Garrido García. High-altitude pulmonary edema in children in Mexico City: A case series. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.-High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a potentially life-threatening form of noncardiogenic pulmonary edema caused by hypobaric hypoxia. Although well characterized in adults, pediatric cases remain underrecognized and are frequently mistaken for pneumonia.We describe four pediatric patients aged 7-12 years diagnosed with HAPE at a Private Tertiary Referral Medical Center in Mexico City. One patient developed classic HAPE after ascent from low altitude, and three patients developed reentry HAPE after returning to high altitude following temporary stays near sea level.All patients presented with hypoxemia (SpO2 77%-93%), respiratory symptoms, bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, absence of fever, and low inflammatory markers. Echocardiography demonstrated elevated or borderline elevated pulmonary artery pressures without structural heart disease. Supplemental oxygen resulted in rapid clinical improvement in all cases. Hospital stay ranged from 2 to 4 days, and none required mechanical ventilation. One patient experienced recurrence shortly after discharge.HAPE should be considered in children presenting with acute hypoxemic respiratory illness after recent ascent to high altitude. The combination of hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, low inflammatory markers, and rapid response to oxygen therapy may help distinguish HAPE from infectious pneumonia and facilitate timely treatment.

articles.title: TAOK1 Protects against Renal Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Aged Mice through the STK3/BNIP3 Mitophagy Pathway.
articles.abstract: The elderly suffer from a higher incidence and greater severity of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study dissects the possible role of thousand and one amino acid protein kinase 1 (TAOK1) in age-related AKI, specifically examining its regulation of mitophagy. Aged (23~24 months) C57BL/6 mice were subjected to renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and TAOK1 was overexpressed in these mice. Renal function, histopathology, inflammation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and fibrosis were assessed. The involvement of the STK3/BNIP3 pathway and mitophagy was evaluated by Western blot and immunofluorescence. In vitro, primary renal tubular cells from aged mice underwent hypoxia-reoxygenation (H/R) following Taok1 knockdown. TAOK1 expression was significantly downregulated in the kidneys of aged mice. Taok1 overexpression in aged mice ameliorated IRI-induced renal dysfunction, tubular damage, inflammation, NET formation, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, Taok1 overexpression activated the STK3/BNIP3 signaling pathway and enhanced mitophagy, as evidenced by increased expressions of key mitophagy-related proteins. Conversely, Taok1 knockdown in aged mouse renal tubular cells exacerbated H/R-induced cell injury and apoptosis, and suppressed the STK3/BNIP3 pathway and mitophagy. Our findings demonstrate that TAOK1 protects against renal IRI in aged mice by promoting mitophagy through the STK3/BNIP3 axis. The age-related decline in TAOK1 may contribute to the heightened susceptibility to AKI, positioning TAOK1 as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating AKI in the aging population.

articles.title: Successful renal retransplantation after structured optimization in a patient with diffuse systemic venous thrombosis and complex urological pathology: a case report.
articles.abstract: Renal retransplantation in the presence of extensive systemic venous thrombosis, lack of reliable vascular access and complex lower urinary tract pathology presents significant challenges. We report a 27-year-old male who presented for kidney retransplantation following chronic rejection of a previous graft. Pretransplant evaluation revealed extensive thrombosis involving central and peripheral venous systems, pericatheter thrombosis of a left femoral dialysis line, burn injury to the trunk, bilateral upper limbs and right lower limb, a previous gunshot injury to the right thigh, volume overload with dyselectrolytemia, panurethral stricture and infected allograft from first transplant. These challenges were approached stepwise by a multidisciplinary team. Peritoneal dialysis was initiated due to complexity in vascular access, and urethral reconstruction using buccal mucosal graft urethroplasty was performed to ensure a good urinary outflow tract along with transplant nephrectomy of the infected graft. The patient received desensitization therapy for donor-specific antibodies and positive crossmatch and orthotopic renal transplantation was performed after native left nephrectomy (due to extensive bilateral iliac vein thrombosis). The patient had excellent postoperative recovery with good allograft function. This case highlights the importance of careful multidisciplinary planning and staged approach for a successful renal retransplantation even in complicated clinical scenarios.

articles.title: Postoperative delirium and 1-year functional decline, institutionalization and mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is a common and serious complication in older surgical patients and has been associated with increased morbidity, healthcare costs, long-term functional decline and mortality.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether postoperative delirium is associated with functional status, quality of life, institutionalisation and mortality at 1 year after surgery in a large multicentre surgical cohort.

DESIGN: Prospective multicentre observational study.

SETTING: Forty-three hospitals in Spain. Surgical patients were recruited in November 2023 and assessed for delirium 48 h after surgery, with follow-up at 1 year.

PATIENTS, OTHER PARTICIPANTS: A total of 2442 adult surgical patients undergoing elective or urgent procedures requiring hospital admission. Postoperative delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM), CAM for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the telephone-administered 4AT according to clinical setting.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Functional status and quality of life at 1 year assessed using the 12-item World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0). Secondary outcomes included institutionalisation and mortality.

RESULTS: After excluding 81 deaths and 462 nonresponders, the 1-year telephone follow-up was completed for 1899 patients. Postoperative delirium within the first 48 h was independently associated with a 4.6-point higher WHODAS score at 1 year: adjusted mean difference = 4.60 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.57 to 7.64, P = 0.003]. Delirium was also associated with increased institutionalisation and higher mortality: odds ratio (OR) 2.5 (95% CI, 1.07 to 5.84, P = 0.03), and (16.7 vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), including 30-day, 60-day, and 365-day mortality (all P < 0.001), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative delirium is independently associated with long-term functional decline, loss of independence, institutionalisation and increased 1-year mortality. These findings highlight delirium as a key perioperative complication and support prevention strategies and structured long-term follow-up after surgery.

articles.title: Distribution of Needlestick Injuries in Hand Parts: A Retrospective Cohort Study‌.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND A large number of healthcare workers worldwide experience needlestick injuries (NSIs), placing them at risk of infection. This study aimed to analyze the incidence of NSIs involving the hand, particularly focusing on the high incidence of NSIs in operating room staff, to provide a reference for the prevention of NSIs. MATERIAL AND METHODS We investigated the incidence of NSIs and the hand regions most frequently affected among operating room staff at a hospital in China from 2015 to 2023 using self-reported NSI data. Differences in NCI incidence across hand regions were analyzed using the chi-square test. RESULTS Among the 139 NSI cases, 98 (70.5%) were attributed to the unsafe operation of medical devices, 128 (92.09%) occurred during procedures not involving surgical instruments, 87 (62.6%) were caused by swaged needles, and 46 (33.1%) occurred among staff involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgeries. Of the 139 cases, 110 (79.1%) resulted in bleeding after NSIs. Regarding source infection status, 87 cases involved confirmed infections, 24 involved suspected infections, 9 had unknown infection status, and 14 had no infectious diseases. Regarding the effect of protective equipment, no statistically significant difference was found in the bleeding outcomes between individuals wearing single-layer and dual-layer gloves (P>0.05), nor in the distribution of injury sites across different hand regions (P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS Using local protective measures, such as medical gloves with stab-resistant or thickened materials in the index fingers and dorsal hand regions, may be an effective preventative measure against NSIs.

articles.title: Nationwide Claims-Based Incidence and Associated Factors of Adverse Events after Gastric Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection.
authors: Quality Management Committee of Korean Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Most data on adverse events (AEs) following gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) originate from high-volume expert centers, limiting their generalizability to routine clinical practice. Population-level claims-based evidence on AEs after gastric ESD remains limited, although such data cannot fully account for lesion- and procedure-specific risk factors.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, retrospective cohort study using claims data from the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service. All patients who underwent ESD for gastric neoplastic lesions between 2013 and 2017 were included. Claims-defined AEs-including bleeding, perforation, pneumonia, and intensive care unit (ICU) admission within 30 days-were assessed, along with subsequent gastric surgery within 90 days. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with each outcome.

RESULTS: A total of 83,871 gastric ESD procedures were performed in 76,181 patients. The incidence of bleeding was 16.6%, whereas perforation (0.17%), pneumonia (0.65%), and ICU admission (0.94%) were uncommon. Older age was associated with a lower risk of bleeding but a higher risk of pneumonia and ICU admission, particularly among patients aged ≥80 years. Among the antithrombotic agents included in the analysis, warfarin was associated with bleeding and clopidogrel was associated with ICU admission. Procedures performed at general hospitals were associated with higher risks of multiple AEs compared with those performed at tertiary centers. Overall, 3.9% of patients underwent additional gastric surgery, almost exclusively among those with gastric cancer.

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide population-based claims study, claims-defined AEs after standard-indication gastric ESD were associated with patient-level and institution-level variables available in administrative data (cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0011604).

articles.title: Association Between Early Bedside Clinical Findings and Need for Organ Support or Mortality in Critically Ill Children: A Multicenter Study.
authors: Critically Ill Patient Working Group of the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies (SEUP)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify early bedside clinical predictors of the need for organ support and mortality among critically ill children presenting to pediatric emergency departments (EDs).

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, registry-based, multicenter observational study across 21 pediatric emergency departments endorsed by the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies. Critically ill children evaluated on the 4th, 14th, and 24th days of each month between February 2021 and July 2024 were included. Critical illness was defined as pediatric intensive care unit admission or advanced airway or circulatory intervention in the ED. The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was recorded at arrival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with severe clinical outcomes and mortality. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: We included 412 critically ill children; 63 (15.3%) had severe clinical outcomes, and 12 (2.9%) died. Abnormal circulation and appearance when evaluating the PAT and abnormal systolic blood pressure were independently associated with severe clinical outcomes (AUC: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68-0.82). Prior pediatric intensive care unit admission and abnormal appearance and abnormal circulation when evaluating the PAT were independently associated with mortality (AUC: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95).

CONCLUSIONS: Structured bedside assessment at ED presentation may provide clinically meaningful prognostic insight, supporting earlier prioritization and escalation of care for critically ill children, pending external validation.

articles.title: Social Isolation and Loneliness Across the Cardiovascular Disease Spectrum: A Narrative Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Social isolation is the objective paucity of social ties; loneliness is the subjective distress of relationships falling short of what one desires. Both are common, affecting roughly a quarter to a third of older adults, and both have cardiovascular consequences through several mechanisms, with some estimates suggesting an increase of 29% in coronary heart disease risk and 21-23% in heart failure hospitalization. We review the evidence for social isolation and loneliness' impact on cardiovascular disease separately for ischemic heart disease, heart failure, arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death, and stress- and substance-related cardiomyopathies. We also highlight plausible mechanisms by which social isolation and loneliness are linked to downstream adverse cardiovascular events, limitations with existing evidence, societal guidance, and policy frameworks currently aimed at addressing them. The evidence is densest for ischemic heart disease, though the largest cohort shows a 43% excess risk of myocardial infarction attenuating by approximately 84% to nonsignificance after full adjustment, and Mendelian randomization estimates a far smaller effect. The prognostic signal is more consistent than the etiologic one, with low functional social support carrying a pooled hazard ratio of 1.59 in established coronary disease. In heart failure, objective isolation rather than loneliness predicts post-diagnosis mortality, mainly in women, consistent with a self-care-dependent behavioral pathway.

articles.title: Brain Stimulation as a Treatment for Apathy: A Scoping Review of Effects and Safety.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Apathy is a neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by impairment of goal-directed behavior, cognition, and emotional responsiveness. In this scoping review, the authors evaluated the literature on brain stimulation for the treatment of patients with apathy across diagnostic categories and provide recommendations to guide future research and practice.

METHODS: The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, and PsycInfo for studies involving brain stimulation for apathy as a primary or secondary outcome.

RESULTS: From 1,209 records, 52 studies evaluating brain stimulation were included; of these, 10 systematic reviews or meta-analyses were synthesized separately. Modalities included repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS; N=26), deep brain stimulation (DBS; N=7), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS; N=6), electroconvulsive therapy (N=1), transcranial alternating current stimulation (N=1), and transcranial pulsating electromagnetic field therapy (N=1). Populations included patients with schizophrenia (N=477), Parkinson's disease (PD; N=289), depression (N=288), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) (N=210), Huntington's disease (N=42), PD with MCI (N=28), traumatic brain injury (N=28), stroke (N=14), COVID-19 (N=12), and dementia with Lewy bodies (N=6) (total N=1,366). rTMS improved apathy measures, most consistently in AD, with positive trends in depression, MCI, stroke, and schizophrenia. tDCS showed variable effects, with some benefits for schizophrenia. DBS showed mixed results, varying with stimulation location. Observed adverse events were mild and modality specific.

CONCLUSIONS: Investigations into brain stimulation as a treatment for apathy show some promise. Conclusions were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous study designs, and variable outcome measures. Randomized trials with common validated apathy instruments, standardized stimulation parameters, and harmonized diagnostic measures may help advance the field.

articles.title: Individualized Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndrome: Current SAPT Strategies and the Potential Role of Indobufen.
articles.abstract: Acute coronary syndrome requires effective antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while contemporary patients often present with overlapping ischemic and bleeding risks. This clinical complexity has shifted post-PCI management from fixed-duration dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) toward individualized strategies based on DAPT duration, single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) selection, and aspirin withdrawal. Aspirin is traditionally the default maintenance agent after DAPT, although long-term aspirin use is limited by gastrointestinal intolerance, mucosal injury, and bleeding risk. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy represents an important aspirin-free strategy, with clinical application influenced by drug potency, genetic variability, tolerability, cost, and adherence.
