Indobufen, a reversible cyclooxygenase-targeting antiplatelet agent, has reemerged as a potential aspirin alternative by suppressing thromboxane A2 generation through a mechanism distinct from that of aspirin. Current evidence suggests that indobufen-based DAPT may provide comparable ischemic protection with fewer bleeding or gastrointestinal adverse events in selected PCI patients, particularly those with aspirin intolerance, gastrointestinal vulnerability, or high bleeding risk. These patients often present with multiple high-risk features that simultaneously elevate both ischemic and bleeding risks, underscoring the need for careful risk stratification. Most available studies have evaluated indobufen as an aspirin substitute within DAPT rather than as SAPT after DAPT discontinuation. From a pharmacoeconomic perspective, indobufen is more expensive than aspirin, although this must be weighed against potential benefits in bleeding reduction. Future randomized trials are needed to define the optimal DAPT-to-SAPT strategy and clarify the clinical position of indobufen in acute coronary syndrome-PCI.

articles.title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

articles.title: From Physiological to Potential Cardiovascular Maladaptation in Endurance Exercise: Current Evidence, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the cardiovascular benefits of exercise may not increase indefinitely with training volume and intensity. As participation in ultraendurance sports continues to rise, concerns have been raised regarding the potential adverse cardiovascular effects of exposure to extreme or ultraendurance exercise. In this Review, we synthesize the current evidence and the pathophysiology regarding the structural, functional, and electrical cardiovascular maladaptations to endurance exercise and highlight the clinical implications of these changes. Several evidences demonstrate that extreme exertion can induce transient cardiac dysfunction; when sustained over years, it may contribute to myocardial fibrosis and associated arrhythmic events. Endurance athletes frequently exhibit a higher prevalence of coronary artery calcification, atherosclerotic plaque burden, and increased arterial stiffness. The alteration driven by long-term endurance training is also strongly implicated in the higher incidence of atrial fibrillation. Although definitive long-term outcomes remain debated, the assumption that limitless exercise yields exclusively protective cardiovascular effects might no longer seem prudent. While regular exercise is unequivocally cardioprotective, extreme endurance training may cross a threshold from physiological adaptation to potential maladaptation. Understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms of exercise-induced cardiac remodeling is critical to optimize the benefit of exercise and the potential risk associated with exercise.

articles.title: Steatotic Liver Disease with Congenital Ichthyosis in a Toddler: Chanarin-Dorfman Syndrome.
Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
articles.abstract: Neurologic manifestations of Long COVID, also called post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), include fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and headaches, which can be debilitating. Since these symptoms overlap with those of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), we sought to determine the prevalence of OSA in the population of a Neuro-COVID-19 clinic. We performed home sleep testing in 100 consecutive patients with Long COVID and no prior history of OSA who reported fatigue after an episode of COVID-19 not requiring hospitalization. The average age was 46.4 years and 70% of patients were female. OSA was present in 53% of patients, including 33% with mild OSA (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 5-14.9) and 20% with moderate to severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15). Male sex, higher age, and body mass index were significantly associated with OSA. However, there were no significant differences in other comorbidities, Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life measures (QoL), and objective cognitive function test results between groups. Additionally, multiple linear regression models demonstrated that neither AHI nor mean desaturation nadir were significant predictors of QoL or cognitive function. Although OSA is nearly twice as prevalent among our study participants compared to the general adult population of the US, it was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms, alteration of QoL, or objective cognitive dysfunction. However, 20% of patients were diagnosed with moderate to severe OSA, a clinically significant finding that warrants intervention to prevent irreversible cardiopulmonary complications.

articles.title: Carbapenem resistance and mortality in pediatric Acinetobacter bloodstream infections: determinants from a 12-year tertiary-care cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Carbapenem-resistant (CR) Acinetobacter spp. bloodstream infections (BSIs) are difficult to treat in children, yet pediatric data on factors associated with resistance and mortality remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated with carbapenem resistance and 30-day mortality in pediatric Acinetobacter BSIs. We retrospectively analyzed children with monomicrobial Acinetobacter BSIs at a tertiary-care university hospital between January 2014 and September 2025. Factors associated with carbapenem resistance were assessed using co-primary logistic regression analyses in the full cohort and within A. baumannii; 30-day mortality was assessed using Cox regression. Among 128 episodes, median age was 2.0 years (IQR 0.76-8.01), 60.2% (77/128) were male and 90.6% (116/128) had comorbidities. Carbapenem resistance was identified in 54/128 episodes (42.2%), all caused by A. baumannii (54/87, 62.1%). Increasing age, longer hospitalization before BSI onset, mechanical ventilation (MV), and prior meropenem exposure were associated with resistance in both co-primary models. Adjusted ORs for MV were 23.77 (95% CI, 7.54-74.92) in the full cohort and 23.20 (95% CI, 5.39-99.95) within A. baumannii. Overall 30-day mortality was 13.3% (17/128) and was higher in CR than carbapenem-susceptible episodes (22.2% versus 6.8%; p = 0.011). Exploratory comparisons across CR A. baumannii treatment categories were inconclusive (exact p = 0.256). Thrombocytopenia (aHR, 6.12; 95% CI, 2.13-17.61) and carbapenem resistance (aHR, 3.01; 95% CI, 1.04-8.71) were associated with mortality in the primary Cox model.

CONCLUSION: Thrombocytopenia and carbapenem resistance were associated with 30-day all-cause mortality in the primary adjusted analysis; the resistance association was not statistically significant in A. baumannii-restricted and first-episode-only sensitivity analyses.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Acinetobacter BSIs mainly affect medically complex hospitalized children. • Pediatric evidence on factors associated with carbapenem resistance and mortality remains scarce.

WHAT IS NEW: • Increasing age, longer hospitalization before BSI onset, mechanical ventilation, and prior meropenem exposure were associated with carbapenem resistance in both the full Acinetobacter cohort and within A. baumannii. • Carbapenem resistance was associated with 30-day mortality in the primary model, but this finding was not consistently supported in sensitivity analyses; thrombocytopenia remained associated with mortality.

articles.title: Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized crossover pilot study.
articles.abstract: This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were included in the analyses. The protocols comprised 250 µg histrelin IM (standard dose), 75 µg IM, 25 µg IM, no intervention, saline at Bai-hui, saline at Yan-chi, 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, and 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Ovulation was assessed by transrectal ultrasonography at scheduled examinations until detected, with ovulation within 48 h as the primary outcome. Ovulations first detected at 24 h were excluded from the primary analysis. Ovulation within 48 h occurred in 88.9% (8/9) of observations with 250 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 75 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg IM, 37.5% (3/8) with no intervention, 50.0% (3/6) with saline at Bai-hui, 100% (9/9) with 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, 12.5% (1/8) with saline at Yan-chi, and 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Exact 95% confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small sample size. Exploratory pairwise comparisons with the no-intervention protocol were performed without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously. The findings provide preliminary evidence that reduced histrelin doses, including 25 µg, may induce ovulation within 48 h in mares. However, this study did not demonstrate an advantage of pharmacopuncture over IM administration of the same reduced dose. Larger, fully randomized studies are required to confirm the efficacy of reduced-dose histrelin and determine whether administration at specific acupoints provides any additional effect.

articles.title: Visual estimation of guidewire contact forces by integrating multi-scale features and region mask.
articles.abstract: During percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), the contact force between the guidewire and the vessel wall is a key mechanical factor in vessel injury, yet it cannot be measured directly with conventional imaging. Although sensor-based methods measure the contact force directly, they increase both the complexity and the cost of the instrumentation. A sensorless guidewire contact force estimation method is therefore proposed, in which multi-scale feature extraction is combined with region mask mean pooling to learn an end-to-end mapping from conventional planar images to the contact force in each of the four predefined contact regions. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 343 samples acquired on a 3D-printed vessel phantom, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.861 g and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.036 g. Ablation experiments show that the region mask reduces the MAE by 79% relative to the identical architecture without the region mask. Requiring neither additional sensing hardware nor complex physical modeling, the method estimates the contact force from visual information alone. These results support the feasibility of vision-based sensorless contact force estimation and suggest a possible route toward force feedback in interventional procedures.

articles.title: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: from diagnosis to rehabilitation.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE) is the second most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, involving physical medicine and rehabilitation, neurology, orthopedics, and plastic surgery. It results from static or dynamic ulnar nerve instability, cubital tunnel syndrome, or space-occupying lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires thorough history, clinical examination, and selection of appropriate diagnostic tests.

SEARCH STRATEGY: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (January 2000-August 2026) using combinations of "ulnar neuropathy", "cubital tunnel syndrome", "elbow", "ultrasound", "electrodiagnosis", "conservative treatment", "rehabilitation" and "surgery". English-language original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were eligible; case reports were included only where no higher-level evidence existed. Approximately 220 records were screened; 58 were retained, following SANRA recommendations for narrative reviews.

DISCUSSION: High-resolution ultrasound provides dynamic, non-invasive, cost-effective evaluation of the ulnar nerve and real-time assessment of compression or instability, and guides minimally invasive procedures such as perineural injections, although the only randomized placebo-controlled trial did not show superiority of corticosteroid injection over placebo. Conservative treatment is usually first-line, although surgery may be required in advanced or refractory cases; comparative evidence shows no clear superiority among surgical techniques, while endoscopic decompression carries a higher complication rate than open approaches.

CONCLUSIONS: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic pathways and therapeutic options for UNE, highlighting the role of ultrasound as both a diagnostic and interventional tool, and outlines gaps in the literature regarding standardized conservative and surgical protocols.

articles.title: Construction and validation of a predictive model for sleep disorders among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to construct and validate a risk assessment model for sleep disturbance among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), to support early screening and targeted intervention.

DESIGN: a cross-sectional study using data from the 2024 baseline survey of the Active Aging Cohort in Rural Areas, Shandong Province, China.

SUBJECTS: 1,049 rural older adults aged ≥ 60 years with MCI.

METHODS: demographic, lifestyle, disease history, and psychological factors were collected through face-to-face survey questionnaires and health examinations. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Logistic regression identified independent predictors, which were used to build a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated with ROC curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation.

RESULTS: the prevalence of sleep disturbance was 54.2%. Sex, hypertension, self-rated health, and depression were identified as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.759, 95%CI: 0.731-0.778) and calibration, with internal validation confirming robustness.

articles.title: Functional characterization of TmToll-6 in mediating innate immune responses to systemic microbial infections in Tenebrio molitor.
articles.abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are evolutionarily conserved regulators of innate immunity and extensively characterized in mammals and Drosophila melanogaster; however, their functional roles in other insects remain incompletely defined. In this study, we investigated the immunological function of TmToll-6 in Tenebrio molitor larvae under systemic pathogenic bacterial and fungal challenge. Transcriptional analyses revealed that its expression was strongly induced in the fat body, gut, Malpighian tubules, and hemolymph following exposure to Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Candida albicans. The RNA interference-mediated silencing of TmToll-6 significantly increased larval mortality after E. coli and S. aureus infection, highlighting its essential role in antibacterial defense. Mechanistic evaluation further demonstrated that TmToll-6 knockdown markedly suppressed the antimicrobial peptide (AMP) gene expression, particularly in the fat body and gut, which are the main effector tissues of insect humoral immunity. Although TmToll-6 was strongly induced following C. albicans infection, its silencing produced comparatively limited effects on AMP expression, indicating that antifungal AMP regulation is less dependent on TmToll-6 and may involve partially redundant immune pathways. Therefore, TmToll-6 could function as a pivotal immune regulator in T. molitor through Toll pathway-dependent AMP regulation in a tissue- and pathogen-specific manner. This study highlighted the evolutionary diversification of Toll receptors in coleopteran immunity.

articles.title: ASIC1a as an integrating node in ischemic neurotoxicity: crosstalk with NMDAR and TRPM signaling.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers acidosis, glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, which converge to disturb ionic homeostasis through several cation channels, including acid-sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) and transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPM) channels. Emerging evidence suggests that ASIC1a functions as a context-dependent integrating node: protons directly gate ASIC1a, glutamate and bilirubin-associated signaling can modulate ASIC1a-dependent injury pathways. ASIC1a directly couples with NMDAR-dependent signaling and indirectly engages TRPM-associated pathways. Here, we discuss the mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and unresolved questions regarding ASIC1a-associated signaling in ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: Organization of the first national workshop for families in Switzerland concerned with hereditary cancer syndromes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) workshops with families affected by hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes can benefit both affected individuals and their support networks, PPI workshops are rarely being organized. This article presents the planning and implementation of a one-day PPI workshop for families affected by Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (HBOC) or Lynch Syndrome (LS) in Switzerland.

WORKSHOP DESIGN & IMPLEMENTATION: The event was funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation and planned over a 12-month period. The program included expert sessions presented by clinicians and researchers; moderated, small-group participatory exchanges exploring patients' and families' unmet health, psychosocial and educational needs; and interactions with patient advocates. Participant satisfaction surveys were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: One hundred and five adults attended the workshop in Bern in May 2025, with representation from the three major linguistic regions of Switzerland. Almost 75% of participants reported a personal genetic predisposition to cancer. Most respondents were very satisfied or satisfied with the workshop (92%), and nearly all (96%) found the presentations engaging, with the topic of immunotherapy as an emerging treatment rated highest. The participatory exchange sessions were the most valued component of the workshop overall (97% positive feedback).

CONCLUSIONS: We provide proof of concept for the feasibility and positive impact of organizing a national workshop for families affected by HBOC and LS. The participatory nature of the workshop allowed affected individuals and their support networks to communicate unmet needs related to their personal experiences and suggest future avenues for research.

articles.title: Perfusion characterization of osteosarcoma spinal metastases using advanced T1-weighted dynamic contrast enhanced MRI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Spinal osteosarcoma is rare and highly aggressive malignancy associated with poor clinical outcomes. To our knowledge, the perfusion MRI features of spinal osteosarcoma using T1-weighted DCE MRI, including plasma volume, permeability, and time-intensity analysis, have not previously been studied. In addition, changes in these features following radiation treatment have not yet been evaluated. We hypothesize that highly malignant spinal osteosarcoma demonstrates hypervascularity based on its pharmacokinetic perfusion parameters.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 27 patients (mean age 44.5, SD 21.8) of untreated metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma who underwent DCE-MRI. Perfusion parameters, including Ktrans and plasma volume (Vp) as an indicator of permeability and tumor vascularity respectively, were measured using the extended Tofts model. A subset of 12 patients underwent preradiation therapy (RT), 18F-FDG PET, and 7 patients had post-RT DCE-MRI for assessment of treatment effects. Additionally, time intensity curve analysis was conducted to evaluate post-treatment changes.

RESULTS: Thirty-five lesions in 27 patients were evaluated. Perfusion characteristics including mean Ktrans and Vp were 0.323 and 3.54, respectively, indicating that metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma is hypervascular. In the 7 patients with post-RT DCE-MRI, the mean post-RT Vp decreased to 1.77 from a pre-RT mean of 3.28, reflecting a 46.04% decrease to radiation therapy.

CONCLUSION: DCE-MRI evaluation of metastatic Spinal osteosarcoma demonstrates a rich blood supply, consistent with hypervascular metastatic disease. Changes in the time intensity curve analysis may serve as non-invasive marker of radiation treatment response.

articles.title: Factors associated with serum GDF-15, iron deficiency and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with chronic heart failure and healthy elderly people.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coexistent chronic heart failure and iron deficiency is frequently encountered in clinical practice and affects prognosis. We investigated factors associated with serum growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15, iron deficiency and lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure and healthy elderly individuals.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Blood tests were performed on 90 patients with heart failure (aged 75.0 ± 10.7 years) and 73 healthy elderly individuals (aged 76.3 ± 6.4 years). Serum GDF-15, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) α, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and hepcidin concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Left atrial volume index (LAVI) was measured by echocardiography. Hemoglobin (Hb) in healthy elderly individuals correlated with serum iron and hepcidin. In contrast, Hb in patients with heart failure correlated with serum iron and GDF-15. Serum GDF-15 concentration in healthy elderly subjects correlated with estimated glomerular filtration rate, serum iron, and hepcidin. In contrast, in patients with heart failure, it correlated with NT-proBNP and TNFα. In patients with heart failure, serum iron correlated with LAVI.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower hemoglobin levels in patients with heart failure might be associated with elevated serum GDF-15 due to higher serum NT-proBNP and inflammation, as well as iron deficiency. In contrast, lower hemoglobin levels in healthy elderly individuals might involve lower serum iron and hepcidin levels. Lower serum iron concentration was suggested to be involved in left atrial remodeling in patients with heart failure.

articles.title: Effects of inhaled nitric oxide during mechanical circulatory support: a prospective pilot study.
articles.abstract: Among patients with cardiogenic shock receiving Impella-based mechanical circulatory support, pulmonary vascular load and right ventricular dysfunction may affect left ventricular preload and device flow. Prospective data on the acute hemodynamic effects of inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) in this setting are limited. We evaluated short-term hemodynamic changes after iNO initiation in patients receiving Impella or Impella combined with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECPELLA) support. We conducted a prospective single-center pilot study of adult patients receiving Impella or ECPELLA support who were treated with iNO. iNO was initiated at 20 ppm after initial circulatory resuscitation once pulmonary artery pulse pressure could be reliably assessed. Hemodynamic variables were recorded immediately before iNO initiation (T0) and 30 min (T1) and 24 h (T2) after initiation. The primary endpoint was the change in mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) from T0 to T1. We enrolled 11 patients, and 10 were analyzed. mPAP decreased from 19.0 (14.8-20.3) mmHg at T0 to 16.5 (12.8-19.3) mmHg at T1 (P = 0.004). The T0-T2 difference was not significant. Lactate levels decreased, but this temporal change could not be attributed directly to iNO without a control group. Methemoglobin levels increased slightly at T2 without clinical methemoglobinemia. iNO was temporally associated with an early reduction in mPAP in patients receiving Impella-based support, without clear improvement in systemic hemodynamic indices. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

articles.title: Entinostat plus exemestane for hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer: long-term overall survival results from the EOC103A3101 randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: The addition of entinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, to exemestane has demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) in hormone receptor-positive (HR + ), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) following endocrine therapy failure in the EOC103A3101 randomized trial (NCT03538171). This study reports long-term overall survival (OS) results. In this study, 354 patients with HR + /HER2- ABC that had recurred or progressed after endocrine therapy were randomized (2:1) to receive entinostat plus exemestane (n = 235) or placebo plus exemestane (n = 119). After a median follow-up of 31.8 months, the median OS was 38.6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 29.6-44.0) in the entinostat-exemestane group versus 29.2 months (95% CI: 22.5-41.6) in the placebo-exemestane group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.83, 95% CI: 0.62-1.10, P = 0.184). The entinostat-exemestane group demonstrated more pronounced OS benefits when adjusting subsequent antitumor therapies such as cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors, or the combination of endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and chemotherapy. The sensitivity analysis based on the per-protocol set showed more significant OS benefits. The median time to post-discontinuation chemotherapy and chemotherapy-free survival in the entinostat-exemestane group were 11.7 and 9.3 months, respectively, compared to 6.8 and 5.6 months in the placebo-exemestane group (both P < 0.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 65.5% of patients in the entinostat-exemestane group, without new safety signals observed. In conclusion, among patients with HR + /HER2- ABC after endocrine therapy failure, entinostat plus exemestane was associated with a numerically longer OS, with an acceptable safety profile.

articles.title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

articles.title: Genetic evidence for the causal effects of malocclusion and dental attrition on temporomandibular disorders: A multivariable Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract:
STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: The causal role of occlusal factors, particularly malocclusion and dental attrition, in temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) remains unclear because of inconsistent observational evidence and confounding influences, limiting definitive conclusions regarding their independent etiological contributions.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to investigate the independent causal effects of malocclusion and dental attrition on TMDs using multivariable Mendelian randomization (MVMR).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A 2-sample MR framework used genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary data from European cohorts. Pairwise Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses and linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) estimated genetic correlations. MVMR then assessed independent causal effects, accounting for shared genetic architecture, utilizing the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method as the primary estimator. Instrument strength was verified via conditional F-statistics. Sensitivity analyses evaluated instrument heterogeneity (Cochran Q) and directional horizontal pleiotropy (MR-Egger intercepts).

RESULTS: Genetic liability to malocclusion demonstrated a strong association with TMD risk (IVW β=1.059, P<.001), remaining robust in MVMR (β=1.013, P≤.001). Conversely, dental attrition showed no causal effect (MVMR β=-.018, P=.078). LDSC revealed moderate genetic correlation (rg=.580). Sensitivity diagnostics confirmed the absence of heterogeneity and pleiotropy (P>.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Genetic liability to malocclusion was found to be an independent risk factor for TMDs, whereas attrition was found to be a secondary marker of occlusal instability, lacking an independent direct effect.

articles.title: Cumulative Exposure to High Systemic Inflammation and Incident Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to examine the association between cumulative exposure to systemic inflammation and incident metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis in mainland China.

METHODS: This study used data from an ongoing longitudinal physical examination cohort. We enrolled 9,725 participants (aged ≥18 years) who completed three consecutive biennial health examinations between 2018 and 2022, with complete follow-up in 2024. Systemic inflammation was quantified using three established biomarkers: neutrophil count (NC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). Cumulative exposure was calculated from baseline to the third examination by multiplying biomarker values by the time (years) between consecutive examinations. The primary outcome was MASLD development at the fourth examination, and advanced liver fibrosis among incident MASLD cases was further evaluated using the fibrosis-4 index (≥2.67). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to explore the associations between cumulative exposure to inflammation and MASLD incidence and fibrosis severity.

RESULTS: At the fourth examination, 939 incident MASLD cases (9.66%) were identified. In fully adjusted models, participants in the highest quartile of cumulative NC exposure had 2.20-fold higher odds of MASLD (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.81 to 2.69; P for trend <0.001) than those in the lowest quartile. Similarly, the highest quartile of cumulative SII exposure had 1.32-fold higher odds (95% CI, 1.09 to 1.59; P for trend=0.003). Conversely, cumulative NLR exposure showed no significant association with MASLD incidence. The addition of cumulative NC or SII to the basic model comprising traditional risk factors improved the ability to predict MASLD. Furthermore, among participants who developed MASLD, the highest quartile of cumulative NC (odds ratio [OR], 4.74; 95% CI, 1.76 to 12.75; P for trend <0.001) and cumulative SII (OR, 3.74; 95% CI, 1.48 to 9.45; P for trend=0.006), but not cumulative NLR, were significantly associated with an elevated risk of advanced liver fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: Greater NC exposure and excessive SII exposure were each independently associated with incident MASLD and related advanced liver fibrosis. Whether reducing inflammation can help prevent MASLD requires further investigation.

articles.title: A novel strategy for reconstruction of AORI type III proximal tibial defects : surface-type knee reconstruction following defect reconstruction with 3D-printed extension-stem augment.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: For cases of Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) type III proximal tibial defects with intact medial collateral ligaments (MCLs), knee reconstruction is conventionally performed using semi-constrained prostheses with stemmed tibial components in conjunction with cones or sleeves. This study aimed to reconstruct AORI type III tibial defects using a 3D-printed extension-stem augment, followed by surface-type knee reconstruction to achieve long-term stability and promising clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A patient-specific porous extension-stem augment was designed based on the defect morphology. The microporous structure allowed direct contact for osseointegration, the proximal portion supported tibial baseplate, while the distal stem achieved intramedullary fixation. Finite element analysis (FEA) assessed the biomechanical stability of the augment. A retrospective analysis was conducted between July 2021 and September 2023 on patients who underwent reconstruction of AORI type III proximal tibial defects with extension-stem augment and surface-type total knee prosthesis.

RESULTS: FEA demonstrated favourable stress and strain distribution and micromotion at the prosthesis-bone interface, although localized high-strain regions were observed under higher-demand loading conditions. Four patients (0 male, 4 female) were included, with a minimum follow-up of 20.7 months (20.7 to 30) and a median age at surgery of 63.0 years (IQR 60.3 to 66.3). The mean Knee Society Score (KSS) improved significantly to 85 (82 to 87), and the mean Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) score decreased by 18 (16 to 20). One patient developed periprosthetic joint infection on the femoral side at 20.7 months postoperatively and underwent revision surgery. Intraoperatively, the augment was securely integrated and could not be extracted. Radiological evaluation demonstrated satisfactory alignment and joint stability, with no evidence of prosthesis loosening or migration at the latest follow-up.

CONCLUSION: The extension-stem augment achieved anatomical reconstruction of AORI type III proximal tibial defects and provided stable support for the surface-type prosthesis, ensuring reliable knee stability after reconstruction. This represents a feasible option for revision of AORI type III tibial defects.

articles.title: Australian Gonococcal Surveillance Program, 1 January to 31 March 2026.
articles.abstract: The Australian National Neisseria Network (NNN) comprises reference laboratories in each state and territory that report data on antimicrobial susceptibility testing to an agreed group of antimicrobial agents for the Australian Gonococcal Surveillance Programme (AGSP). The AGSP data are presented quarterly in tabulated form, as well as in the AGSP annual report. This report presents national gonococcal antimicrobial resistance surveillance data from 1 January to 31 March 2026.

articles.title: Australian Gonococcal Surveillance Programme Annual Report, 2025.
articles.abstract: The Australian Gonococcal Surveillance Programme (AGSP) has continuously monitored antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) for more than 45 years through the system of jurisdictional Neisseria reference laboratories, the National Neisseria Network (NNN). In 2025, a total of 10,204 isolates across Australia, from public and private sectors, were tested for in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility by standardised methods. In 2025, the AGSP captured antimicrobial susceptibility data for 23.9% of all gonococcal infection notifications nationally. The current treatment recommendation for gonorrhoea, for the majority of Australia, continues to be dual therapy with ceftriaxone and azithromycin. In 2025, of NG isolates tested, 0.73% (74/10,204) met the World Health Organization (WHO) criterion for decreased susceptibility (DS) to ceftriaxone, defined as a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) ≥ 0.125 mg/L. This proportion of isolates meeting the ceftriaxone DS criterion was greater than that reported in 2024 (0.51%), with the majority from New South Wales and Victoria. Genomic analysis indicated that 64.9% of these isolates (48/74) possessed the mosaic penA 60.001 allele, the key target associated with ceftriaxone resistance. Resistance to azithromycin was reported in 7.1% of NG isolates nationally, increasing from being proportionally stable (3.9% to 4.7%) since 2019. Of NG isolates tested, 0.20% (20/10,204) exhibited high-level resistance to azithromycin (MIC value ≥ 256 mg/L), with cases reported across Australia, predominantly in New South Wales, Victoria and non-remote Western Australia. There were ten isolates detected in 2025 that had an extensively drug-resistant (XDR) phenotype: i.e., displaying both high-level resistance to azithromycin and decreased susceptibility to ceftriaxone (MIC ≥ 0.125 mg/L). When added to the 14 XDR isolates reported during 2022-2024, this brings the total to 24 XDR NG isolates reported in Australia since 2022. Genomic analyses of the ten XDR isolates reported in 2025 indicated all harboured the mosaic penA 60.001 allele, with several differing sequence types (ST) identified. By contrast, during 2022 and 2024, XDR NG sequence types were limited to ST-16406, consistent with reports from Europe and England. Travel information, where available, indicates infections in 2025 were associated with travel to Southeast Asia but also arose where no travel was involved. In 2025, penicillin resistance was found in 23.4% of gonococcal isolates, and ciprofloxacin resistance in 59.3% of isolates where tested, although there was variation by jurisdiction particularly in remote settings, where acquisition of cultures for antimicrobial susceptibility testing is low. Tetracycline resistance has been included in surveillance in the AGSP in recent years, coincident with increasing use of doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis for syphilis and chlamydia. Nationally 36.2% of NG isolates in 2025 were tetracycline resistant, with variation by jurisdiction. No isolates were resistant to spectinomycin; data for gentamicin, whilst no breakpoints are defined, are reported by the AGSP as these data are reportable to the WHO Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS). The emergence of antimicrobial resistant NG in Australia has largely occurred through importation, spread and local transmission. In 2025, in Australia and overseas, increased detection of drug-resistant NG isolates is of significant concern as the threat for the future of the current recommended therapeutic agents is increasingly evident, and no ideal alternate therapeutic agent has been identified. Disease prevention strategies under investigation for the future have included the MenB-4C vaccine, designed to protect against meningococcal disease. Despite early promise, recent results from a large Australian trial indicate the MenB-4C vaccine is not effective at preventing gonorrhoea in men who are at high risk of infection. The AGSP continues to monitor antimicrobial resistance and to identify emerging resistant clones by enhanced surveillance approaches, to inform strategies for disease management and treatment of gonorrhoea in Australia.

articles.title: Correction: Hypertension.
Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in U.S. Adults With Type 1 Diabetes.
Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Conditions in Medicare Advantage In-Home Health Risk Assessments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Critics argue this practice increases risk-adjusted payments without improving quality. Comprehensive data on use of in-home HRAs and downstream treatment are lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To examine trends in cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs, characteristics associated with HRA-based diagnoses, and treatment rates after diagnoses.

DESIGN: Cohort study.

SETTING: Population-based.

PARTICIPANTS: Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.

MEASUREMENTS: Using 100% Medicare claims, trends in the proportion of cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs (vs. facility-based visits) were examined. Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to estimate the association between beneficiary- and plan-level characteristics and HRA-based diagnoses and compare treatment rates across settings.

RESULTS: Among 21 496 506 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries diagnosed with a cardiovascular risk factor or disease, the proportion diagnosed during in-home HRAs increased between 2018 and 2022 for hypertension (45.9% to 47.7%), hyperlipidemia (57.8% to 66.7%), diabetes (47.8% to 51.6%), atrial fibrillation (30.0% to 36.0%), ischemic heart disease (37.2% to 41.6%), peripheral vascular disease (64.5% to 73.9%), and heart failure (34.7% to 42.6%). Racial and ethnic minority beneficiaries and those enrolled in lower-rated plans were more likely to receive HRA-based diagnoses. Treatment rates were substantially lower after HRA-based diagnoses across all conditions.

LIMITATIONS: Differences in the severity of conditions between groups could not be assessed. Prescription fills were used as a proxy for management. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding.

CONCLUSION: Among Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters.

PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

articles.title: Projected Effect of 2026 Federal Changes to the Childhood Immunization Schedule on Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infections in the United States.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination.

OBJECTIVE: To project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections.

DESIGN: Markov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection.

DATA SOURCES: Published data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection.

TARGET POPULATION: One-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million).

TIME HORIZON: 20 years.

INTERVENTION: Universal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Numbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS OF BASE-CASE ANALYSIS: Compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. These strategies would also increase the number of HBV-susceptible people at year 20 (474 000 and 1 806 000) compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (232 000).

RESULTS OF SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS: In a scenario with lower vaccine coverage (84.5%) and higher HBV prevalence (maternal prevalence of 0.72% and higher risk for horizontal infection), chronic HBV infections would increase to 1700 and 2192, respectively, with the deferred and shared decision-making strategies.

LIMITATION: Uncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk.

CONCLUSION: Proposed policy changes for vaccination through shared decision making are projected to result in an 83% increase in childhood HBV infections, and between 50% and 70% of children entering adulthood annually would be susceptible to HBV infection. Policymakers should reimplement recommendations for universal birth-dose vaccination.

PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

articles.title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
articles.abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

articles.title: The Relationship is the Intervention: Listening to Adults With Congenital Heart Disease.
Latency after preterm prelabour rupture of membranes vs. gestational age: a maturation-growth trade-off.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM), prolonging pregnancy for fetal maturity is traded against infection risk, yet latency is entangled with gestational age. We examined its determinants and, disentangled from gestational age, its impact on fetomaternal outcome.

METHODS: In a prospective tertiary-centre cohort, 96 singleton pregnancies with PPROM at 28-34 weeks, undelivered at 48 h, were followed to delivery. Admission and pre-delivery haematological and ultrasound measures were recorded. Analyses included Kaplan-Meier, restricted mean survival time, competing-risks and gestational-age-adjusted models.

RESULTS: Median latency was 5 days (IQR 3-11); 61 % delivered within a week. Gestational age at admission was the only predictor (rho -0.21, p=0.037); earlier-gestation women remained undelivered longer (restricted mean 10.5 vs. 6.4 days, p=0.006); amniotic fluid volume did not predict latency (oligohydramnios p=0.700; 6.6 vs. 9.0 days, p=0.084). Longer latency was associated with neonatal complications (OR 10.9), NICU admission (OR 3.4) and caesarean (OR 5.5). The near-zero crude latency-birth-weight correlation reflected gestational-age suppression: at equal gestational age at admission, longer latency meant greater birth weight (+129 g per 10 days, p=0.004), yet at equal age at delivery a lower weight (p=0.033). The neonatal-morbidity association persisted after adjustment (OR 1.21 per day). The serial total-leucocyte-count rise tracked chorioamnionitis (AUC 0.77), the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio did not.

CONCLUSIONS: Gestational age at admission, not amniotic fluid volume, governs latency. Prolonged latency is a genuine, double-edged trade-off, not a confounded marker of prematurity: at equal gestational age it yields maturational weight yet restrains growth-for-age and carries a gestational-age-independent morbidity and infection risk.

articles.title: Interpreting peripheral immune phenotypes in Parkinson's disease: an immune-context framework for biomarker qualification.
articles.abstract: Peripheral immune alterations are widely reported in Parkinson's disease (PD), but their biological meaning and clinical utility remain uncertain because circulating immune profiles are shaped by aging, latent infection, medication exposure, comorbidity, disease stage, and preanalytical conditions. This concept-driven narrative review examines how technically valid peripheral immune findings should be biologically interpreted and clinically qualified through an immune-context phenotyping framework. Available human evidence suggests alterations in neutrophil- and monocyte-related inflammatory indices and cellular states, α-synuclein-responsive T-cell pathways, cytotoxic and regulatory T-cell states, B-cell phenotypic alterations, and peripheral-central immune associations. Much of this evidence, however, derives from cross-sectional and cohort-dependent studies, and within the human evidence considered in this review, PD specificity remains insufficiently established for most candidate signals. An observed blood difference may reflect altered production, survival, differentiation, redistribution, denominator effects, systemic inflammatory context, or measurement-related distortion rather than a single disease mechanism. Immune-context phenotyping, therefore, integrates trait, state, disease-trajectory, measurement, and treatment contexts with biological identifiability, disease-control comparisons, cross-compartment corroboration, repeated sampling, and external validation. The framework adapts established biomarker concepts to distinguish diagnostic, prognostic, monitoring, predictive, pharmacodynamic/response, and treatment-selection claims without treating peripheral target engagement, CNS engagement, pathway modification, and clinical benefit as equivalent. Based on the human evidence considered in this review, no peripheral immune phenotype appears ready for stand-alone clinical implementation in PD. The proposed framework defines a testable path from descriptive peripheral immune associations toward biologically coherent, temporally informative, and clinically qualified phenotypes.

articles.title: Calibration compliance and risk-based maintenance: perceptions and practices of healthcare equipment users on patient safety.
articles.journal: International journal of health care quality assurance
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study examines the influence of perceived calibration compliance (PCC) and risk-based maintenance (RBM) attitudes on perceived patient safety outcomes (PSO) among biomedical technicians and equipment operators. It further explores the mediating role of equipment accuracy (EA) and the moderating role of risk category awareness (RCA).

DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: A structured questionnaire was used to collect responses from 415 biomedical staff across three NABH-accredited private hospitals in Kerala, using stratified purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0 for descriptive statistics and Smarts 4.0 for structural equation modeling, including path analysis, mediation and moderation testing.

FINDINGS: Both PCC and RBM showed a significant positive impact on PSO. EA was found to mediate these relationships, indicating that calibration and maintenance practices contribute to safety through their effect on equipment performance. RCA was found to moderate the relationships, strengthening the impact of technical practices on safety outcomes when awareness of equipment risk levels was higher.

RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: This study was limited to three private hospitals in Kerala, so the findings might not apply to government or smaller healthcare settings. Since the data were collected at one point in time, it doesn't capture changes over time. Also, the responses were self-reported, so there's a chance of bias or overstatement by the participants.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: The findings emphasize the need for regular calibration training, RBM protocols and staff awareness programs to promote a culture of safety in healthcare environments.

ORIGINALITY/VALUE: The study is novel in its investigation on how technical compliance and staff perception link to patient safety outcomes through equipment accuracy and risk awareness.

articles.title: Successful systemic fibrinolysis in pulmonary embolism with a thrombus-in-transit.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Right heart thrombus-in-transit with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a rare but potentially lethal clinical finding. Optimal management remains controversial, particularly when major contraindications or risk factors coexist. We present a 72-year-old male admitted to the emergency room with leading diagnosis acute coronary syndrome who was later diagnosed with acute PE and a massive, mobile right heart thrombus along with a concomitant ascending aortic aneurysm. Due to high surgical risk, systemic fibrinolysis was performed under close monitoring. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the intracardiac thrombus, rapid right ventricular recovery, and an intact thoracic aorta. This case highlights the importance of echocardiography in initial evaluation of patients with acute cardiovascular symptoms and also systemic thrombolysis as a viable, life-saving strategy for right heart thrombosis even in complex clinical scenarios.

articles.title: A review of the monitoring of argatroban by anti-IIa methods, ecarin assays, point-of-care testing methods and specialized drug quantification methods for patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) is caused by anti-PF4/heparin IgG antibodies stimulating platelet activation, causing thrombocytopenia and thrombosis. Classical HIT occurs due to exposure to heparin, whereas autoimmune HIT occurs via heparin-independent platelet activation (caused by anti-PF4/polyanion IgG) and relates to a platelet count fall that begins or persists without heparin. Treatment for HIT requires transitioning patients onto alternative anticoagulation. The direct thrombin inhibitor argatroban has been licensed for use in patients with HIT and was recommended to be monitored by the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT). Recent European guidelines have suggested that monitoring drug concentrations is more suitable and will reduce the risk of under or over anticoagulating patients. This review will discuss anti-IIa and ecarin-based laboratory methods for determining plasma argatroban concentrations, the use of viscoelastography methods and other point-of-care testing (POCT) methods in whole blood. The use of more specialised tests based on high-performance liquid chromatography will also be discussed, comparing these methods with aPTT.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes of pediatric thrombosis: a prospective single-center study.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: The incidence of pediatric thrombosis is increasing due to multiple causes and risk factors, including genetic and acquired factors. This study aimed to evaluate clinical characteristics, risk factors, genetic mutations, and clinical outcomes of children with thrombosis. This prospective observational study included 40 children with thrombotic events. Detailed demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging data, as well as clinical outcomes, were collected. Thrombophilia gene testing included MTHFR C677T and A1298C, Factor XIII V34L, and factor V Leiden mutations. Statistical analyses included univariate comparisons and multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of poor outcomes. Twenty percentage of the study population had genetic thrombophilia, while 80% had acquired risk factors. Acquired risk factors mainly included hematological (22.5%) and cardiac disorders (20%). Venous thrombosis was the most common site (80%), followed by arterial (10%) and cardiac (10%) thrombi. MTHFR C677T and factor XIII V34L mutations were detected with genetic thrombophilia only (P < 0.01), while factor V Leiden was present in both groups (P = 0.11). Overall, 67.5% of patients improved, 20% died, and 12.5% developed permanent disabilities. Multivariate analysis identified thrombocytopenia as an independent predictor of poor outcomes [odds ratio (OR) 18.44; 95% CI: 1.76-192.49; P = 0.02]. Positive blood cultures were associated with a fourfold increased risk of adverse outcomes (OR 4.0; 95% CI: 0.75-21.23; P = 0.1). Pediatric thrombosis was predominantly caused by acquired risk factors, though genetic mutations were significantly evident in this study. Screening and early diagnosis are essential for high-risk profiles. Identifying and managing sepsis and thrombocytopenia are critical to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Heavy menstrual bleeding with direct oral anticoagulants and vitamin K antagonists: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) is a clinically important but underrecognized complication of oral anticoagulation that can impair quality of life, cause of iron deficiency or anaemia, and lead to treatment interruption. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare menstrual bleeding outcomes among direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for HMB, anticoagulant modification, treatment for menstrual bleeding, and hospitalization, transfusion, or procedural intervention. Twenty-five studies published from 2015 to 2025 were included; most were observational. Compared with apixaban, rivaroxaban was associated with higher odds of HMB [odds ratio (OR) 2.83, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.11-3.81; I2 = 0%] and anticoagulant modification because of menstrual bleeding (OR 6.05, 95% CI 1.91-19.19; I2 = 0%). Hospitalization, transfusion, or procedural intervention did not differ significantly (OR 1.04, 95% CI 0.10-11.13). Compared with VKAs, rivaroxaban was associated with greater odds of requiring treatment for menstrual bleeding (OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.88-8.54), whereas estimates for HMB and anticoagulant modification were imprecise and nonsignificant. Pooled DOAC-VKA comparisons for HMB were inconclusive. Menstrual bleeding risk appears to vary by individual anticoagulant rather than uniformly across the DOAC class. Proactive assessment of menstrual symptoms and iron deficiency, and patient-centred anticoagulant selection, are warranted, particularly for patients with preexisting HMB or anaemia.

articles.title: Appropriateness of antiphospholipid antibody testing and its impact on diagnostic yield and clinical outcomes: a multicentre cohort study.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an uncommon but important cause of thrombosis and pregnancy morbidity. Despite guidelines, antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) testing is frequently performed outside specialist settings, potentially reducing diagnostic yield and leading to unnecessary downstream investigations. We evaluated real-world aPL testing practices, diagnostic yield, and clinical outcomes. We conducted a retrospective cohort study across three acute hospitals, two satellite sites and 63 general practices between February and June 2024. Adults undergoing aPL testing (anticardiolipin, β2-glycoprotein-I or lupus anticoagulant) were identified from electronic pathology records. Appropriateness, completeness, results and downstream clinical outcomes were assessed against BSH/EULAR guidance and the documented clinical context. Among 691 patients tested (mean age 51.3 years; 67% women), only 34% requests were considered appropriate, and complete panels were requested in 26%. APS was confirmed in 14 patients (2%). Appropriate requests were associated with higher rates of positive results [risk ratio (RR) 2.39], APS diagnosis (RR 27.0) and management changes (RR 21.4) (all P < 0.001). Haematology, Obstetrics and Rheumatology demonstrated the highest rates of appropriate testing. aPL testing is frequently performed outside recommended clinical indications, resulting in low overall diagnostic yield. Appropriate testing is associated with improved diagnostic accuracy and clinically meaningful changes in patient management, supporting the implementation of targeted diagnostic stewardship interventions.

articles.title: Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference.
authors: 2025 Surgical Palliative Care Research Conference (SPaRC) Collaborators
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings.

STUDY DESIGN: In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821.

RESULTS: The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance.

CONCLUSIONS: SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

articles.title: Sex, Age, and Survival in Traumatic Shock: An Ongoing Question, Not Yet an Answer.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons

articles.title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana, we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1's DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.

articles.title: Allometric Scaling of Left Heart Structure and Function in Elite Cyclists: Development of Sport-Specific Prediction Equations.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elite athletes frequently exceed conventional left ventricular (LV) and left atrial thresholds when guideline-recommended linear scaling for body size is applied, prompting unnecessary investigation. Few athlete-specific allometric equations yield percentage predicted values or Z scores. We aimed to develop allometric equations for LV and left atrial structure and function in elite cyclists, accounting for body size, sex, discipline, and heart rate, and to compare these with body surface area (BSA) indexing.

METHODS: We evaluated 181 elite cyclists (105 male, 76 female; age 22.7±5.5 years; 128 endurance, 53 sprint) with normal preparticipation cardiac screening. Weighted least squares allometric regression determined optimal scaling exponents for height, weight, and BSA, with models advancing in complexity only when prediction accuracy significantly improved. Equations were externally validated in 62 independent elite male endurance cyclists.

RESULTS: Men had larger BSA-scaled LV and left atrial size than women (both P<0.001). Many cyclists exceeded conventional thresholds (American Society of Echocardiography 2015: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 69.6%, LV end-systolic volume indexed to BSA 62.9%; British Society of Echocardiography 2020: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 50.8%, left atrial volume indexed to BSA 28.7%). Height provided superior allometric fit versus weight or BSA. Height, sex, discipline, and RR interval were key determinants. On external validation, only 6.5% exceeded the Z score threshold for LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA, compared with 90.3% classified abnormal by ASE guidelines.

CONCLUSIONS: Height-based allometric scaling outperformed weight or BSA for cardiac dimensions and function in elite cyclists. These sport-specific equations, validated in an independent cohort, provide clinically usable percentage predicted values and Z scores that permit quantitative assessment rather than binary thresholds and may reduce misclassification of physiological adaptation as disease in preparticipation cardiac screening programs.

articles.title: Pulmonary Embolism-Attributable Mortality in Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in the United States from 2010 to 2023.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are at increased risk of pulmonary embolism (PE) and related mortality, yet contemporary US trends remain incompletely defined. We examined PE-attributable mortality from 2010 to 2023 among patients with ASCVD, stratified by age, sex, race, ethnicity, urbanization, and region.

METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research data (2010-2023) to assess PE-attributable mortality among patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years using age-adjusted mortality rates. Concurrent trends in age-adjusted ASCVD prevalence and risk factors were evaluated using NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey). Age-adjusted mortality rates were analyzed with Joinpoint regression to estimate average annual percentage change (95% CI), and trends in NHANES were assessed using linear models.

RESULTS: From 2010 to 2023, 152 386 US patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years (80 015 male, 72 371 female) died from PE. PE-attributable AAMR rose from 3.62 to 4.96 per 100 000 (annual percentage change +3.1%; P<0.001), with a modest increase from 2010 to 2018 (annual percentage change +0.7%, P=0.003) and a sharp rise from 2018 to 2023 (annual percentage change +12.8%, P<0.001). Age-adjusted mortality rate was highest in non-Hispanic/non-Latinx Black American individuals, and American Indian/Alaska Native and Hispanic/Latinx populations had the steepest increases. Adults <65 years, rural areas, and the Western United States showed disproportionate rises, whereas the South had the highest absolute deaths. Such trends paralleled increasing ASCVD prevalence, which was driven by hypertension, obesity, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease.

CONCLUSIONS: PE-attributable mortality among US patients with ASCVD rose from 2010 to 2023 particularly among young-to-middle-aged adults, socioeconomically isolated ethnic and racial groups, and Western residents.
