articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Adherence to Antihypertensives and Associated Moderating Factors Among Adults With Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a significant public health issue affecting over a billion adults worldwide with adherence to antihypertensives being crucial for achieving sustained blood pressure control and reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. To extend previous evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis on global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives among adults.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL. Pooled prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence was estimated using generalized linear mixed-effects model in R software version 4.4.3. Cochran's Q, τ2, and I2$$ {I}^2 $$ statistics examined statistical heterogeneity with moderator analysis exploring sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis was analyzed using exact fixed-effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 123 studies with 1 052 445 adults with hypertension were included. Pooled global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives was estimated at 58% (95% CI, 52%-63%), with 39% for high adherence, 29% for moderate adherence, and 35% for low adherence. Results for sensitivity analysis were 57.91% (95% CI, 57.81%-58.01%) with δ̂ being 24.3%. Prevalence across continents was 67% for Europe, 65% for South America, 60% for Africa, 56% for Asia, and 45% for North America. Adherence to antihypertensives was similar across low-income countries (61%), high-income countries (58), upper-middle-income countries (57%), and lower-middle-income countries (56%). In multivariate model, age and assessment tool only were significantly associated with medication adherence.

CONCLUSIONS: Globally, a large proportion of adults with hypertension exhibit moderate to low adherence to antihypertensive medications. Future studies should prioritize establishing consensus-based operational definitions and cutoff values to enhance adherence.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy for Secondary Stroke Prevention in Patients With Symptomatic Large-Artery Atherosclerosis and Atrial Fibrillation: A Multicenter Experience.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke due to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis in patients with atrial fibrillation remains uncertain. We describe real-world prescribing patterns and outcomes across antithrombotic regimens.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke related to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis (intracranial or extracranial or both) at 4 US comprehensive stroke centers. Patients were grouped by discharge regimen: single anticoagulant, single antiplatelet (sAP), single anticoagulant+sAP, dual antiplatelet therapy, or triple therapy (single anticoagulant+dual antiplatelet therapy). Outcomes were recurrent ischemic stroke, symptomatic hemorrhage, and death at 90 days and 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 191 patients (median age 75 years [interquartile range [IQR], 68-83]; 40% women; 36% prior stroke/transient ischemic attack), single anticoagulant+sAP was the most common discharge regimen (33%), followed by single anticoagulant (25%), whereas triple therapy was uncommon (4%). More than half of patients switched regimens within 1 year, mostly as the planned duration ended (71%) or following an outcome event (12%). During follow-up (median 68 days [IQR, 28-120]), 21 patients (11%) had recurrent ischemic stroke, and 26 (14%) had symptomatic hemorrhage, over half of each within 90 days; 25% of deaths occurred within 90 days. Ninety-day stroke/death rate was 24%, with single anticoagulant versus 8% with single anticoagulant+sAP; symptomatic hemorrhage rate was 0% and 12%, respectively. At 1 year, stroke/death was 27.3% with sAP, 11.1% with single anticoagulant+sAP, 4.5% with single anticoagulant, and 0% with dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic hemorrhage was similar across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with atrial fibrillation and symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis, recurrent ischemic events and mortality were common, and antithrombotic management varied substantially. The combination of single anticoagulant+sAP was associated with lower observed short-term stroke/death than single anticoagulant; however, bleeding remains a concern with prolonged therapy. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal regimen and duration for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Multivariate Genomic Analysis Reveals Shared Genetic Architecture and Potential Therapeutic Targets for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and comprises multiple clinical phenotypes, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely defined.

METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and carotid plaque using genomic structural equation modeling to derive a multivariable ASCVD common factor. We applied fine-mapping, multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation, transcriptome-wide association studies, Mendelian randomization, colocalization, mediation analysis, and virtual screening.

RESULTS: We identified 289 linkage disequilibrium-independent lead single-nucleotide polymorphisms mapping to 177 genomic risk loci; 13 lacked corresponding genome-wide significant signals in the input genome-wide association studies. Eleven had prior genome-wide association study catalog association records, whereas no relevant records were identified for the loci represented by rs2294777 near SASH1 and rs4843053 near AKAP13. Fine-mapping prioritized 26 putative causal variants. Integrated functional summary-based imputation, multi-tissue transcriptome-wide association study, and multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation analyses implicated 123 genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted endothelial cells and H3K27ac-marked regulatory regions. Lipidomic analyses linked higher triacylglycerols and sterol esters to increased multivariable ASCVD common factor risk. Protein Mendelian randomization analyses in deCODE and Fenland prioritized aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), phosphodiesterase 5A (PDE5A), HtrAserinepeptidase 1 (HTRA1), and transcription elongation factor A2 (TCEA2) as candidate targets. Colocalization supported a shared causal variant between TCEA2 and multivariable ASCVD common factor. Mediation analyses suggested partial mediation by diastolic blood pressure for ALDH2, PDE5A, and TCEA2 and by triglycerides for TCEA2. Virtual screening identified candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to PDE5A and ALDH2.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating multivariate genome-wide association study with multi-omics and causal inference analyses identified shared genetic signals associated with ASCVD susceptibility and prioritized candidate protein targets, informing future functional studies and target validation.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity have elevated cardiovascular risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have established cardiometabolic benefits in the general population, but their effects in SMI are unclear. We evaluated whether GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death.

METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of 218 043 adults with SMI, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and active antipsychotic or antidepressant medications in the TriNetX database (73 health care organizations). Outcomes were incident MI, HF, and all-cause death at 1 and 3 years. The primary exposure was GLP-1RA use versus nonuse; secondary analyses examined semaglutide or tirzepatide. Exploratory analyses evaluated sex, race, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use.

RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death. Risk differences at 1 and 3 years were -0.007 and -0.010 for MI, -0.011 and -0.018 for HF, and -0.039 and -0.065 for death (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide use was also associated with lower risks of MI, HF, and death (all P<0.001). Findings were directionally consistent after accounting for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use.

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with treated SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity using GLP-1RAs, particularly semaglutide or tirzepatide, had significantly reduced 1- and 3-year risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death versus nonusers. These pooled associations should be interpreted in the context of SMI's clinical heterogeneity and the limitations of administrative case ascertainment.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.

METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

articles.title: Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

articles.title: Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer.

METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison.

RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]).

CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored.

METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men).

RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

articles.title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information.

METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed.

RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

articles.title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals.

RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals.

CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.

articles.title: Psychological Stress and the Diurnal Patterns of Sodium Excretion and Blood Pressure: Results From the SABRE Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological stress is associated with reduced blood pressure (BP) dipping, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study examined the associations among stress-induced sodium excretion, diurnal sodium excretion, and BP dipping.

METHODS: Apparently healthy adult participants underwent a laboratory session during which urinary sodium excretion was measured before and after mental stress tasks. Participants then completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring and separate awake and asleep urine collections. The change in urinary sodium excretion rate with stress was defined as the difference in urinary sodium excretion rate before and after stress. The awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate and systolic BP dipping were calculated from the 24-hour urine and BP measurements.

RESULTS: In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, mean systolic BP, mean diastolic BP, parental history of hypertension, fasting glucose, and 24-hour creatinine clearance, a smaller stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of urinary sodium excretion rate (n=180, B=0.2253 [95% CI, 0.0490-0.4016]). In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, current smoking, alcohol use, fasting glucose, 24-hour sodium excretion, 24-hour potassium excretion, 24-hour creatinine clearance, and fractional excretion of sodium, a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with lower systolic BP dipping (n=175, B=1.0127 [95% CI, 0.0599-1.9656]).

CONCLUSIONS: A lower stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a worse diurnal pattern of urinary sodium excretion, which was associated with lower systolic BP dipping.

REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT03636490.

articles.title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models.

METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively.

RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially.

CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty.

RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

articles.title: Comparison of Unfractionated Heparin and Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin in Acute Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Subanalysis of the CLOT-VENUS Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal anticoagulation in acute cerebral vein thrombosis remains uncertain. We compared unfractionated heparin (UFH) and enoxaparin, and identified predictors of functional recovery and UFH responsiveness.

METHODS: This retrospective 2-center study from the multicenter international CLOT-VENUS (Collaboration on Cerebral Venous Thrombosis) registry included adults with acute cerebral vein thrombosis treated with UFH or enoxaparin (2004-2024). Baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. UFH response was measured via a composite responsiveness index (Unfractionated Heparin Composite Response Index) based on partial thromboplastin time. The primary outcome was 6-month functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]), and secondary outcomes included discharge mRS and death.

RESULTS: Among 359 patients (median age, 40 [interquartile range, 28-54] years; 68.5% women), 220 (61.3%) received UFH and 139 (38.7%) enoxaparin. Only 64% of partial thromboplastin time values fell within the therapeutic range. UFH was associated with worse outcomes at discharge (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.89; mRS score, 2-6: adjusted odds ratio, 1.90; ordinal mRS score, adjusted odds ratio, 1.56) and at 6 months (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.63). Poor recovery was independently linked to the UFH composite responsiveness index and frequent infusion adjustments. Notably, in the sensitivity analysis limited to patients on UFH with ≥50%, ≥67%, and ≥79% therapeutic partial thromboplastin time values, the outcome differences diminished. Age was independently associated with UFH responsiveness, and female sex, body mass index, and NLR with the number of UFH infusion-rate adjustments.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with UFH was associated with worse clinical outcomes compared with enoxaparin, largely attributable to suboptimal and inconsistent anticoagulation. However, when UFH achieves consistent therapeutic levels, the outcomes are comparable. Early predictors may help guide individualized anticoagulation strategies.

articles.title: Joint Impacts of Ambient Air Pollution and Temperature on Cardiovascular Disease in West Florida.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) are well-established contributors of acute cardiovascular events, but their joint short-term effects in subtropical coastal regions have not been well characterized. We evaluated their joint associations with major cardiovascular outcomes in West Florida.

METHODS: We analyzed daily hospital admissions for myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke within the BayCare Health System from 2017 to 2024. Daily mean temperature and PM2.5 were obtained from national monitoring networks. Joint exposure-response relationships were estimated using distributed-lag generalized additive models with tensor-product interactions across lags 0 to 7 days, adjusting for temporal trends, day of week, and copollutants. Effect modification by age, sex, and race was examined.

RESULTS: Temperature showed stronger short-term associations with cardiovascular risk than local PM2.5. Among adults aged ≥65 years, myocardial infarction risk was higher at lower temperatures, compared with higher temperatures (relative risk comparing the 75th versus the 25th percentile of the exposure distribution [RR75/25], 0.92 [95% CI, 0.89-0.95]). Heart failure exhibited a U-shaped temperature-risk relationship, with greater heat-related risk observed among younger adults (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]) and Black patients (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]). In contrast, PM2.5 showed weaker overall associations, with only a modest elevation in stroke risk among Black patients (RR75/25, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.96-1.08]). Joint exposure surfaces revealed outcome-specific nonlinear patterns, particularly for heart failure at higher temperature and PM2.5.

CONCLUSIONS: Temperature and PM2.5 jointly influence short-term cardiovascular risk through nonlinear and subgroup-specific pathways, highlighting the need for integrated climate and air-quality strategies to reduce cardiovascular disparities.

articles.title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Versus Angiography-Guided Coronary Stent Implantation: An Updated Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

articles.title: Interpersonal value regulates infection-risky social contact across 61 societies.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Interpersonal contact is essential for cooperation and care, but it also provides a route for pathogen transmission between individuals. Hence, a key challenge for social organisms involves maintaining beneficial social contact while also limiting exposure to infection risks. Existing proposals suggest that this trade-off is guided by the interpersonal value of specific social targets. In addition, ecological and cultural factors, including historical pathogen prevalence, individualism-collectivism, tightness-looseness, and relational mobility, might also shape how people avoid pathogens. To test whether and how infection-risky social contact varies with individual-level interpersonal value and these societal-level factors, we collected data from 47,756 participants across 61 societies. Participants were randomly assigned to picture a social target - either a friend, acquaintance, stranger, or enemy. They then rated their comfort with infection-risky contact with that target (e.g., drinking from the same water bottle) and whether they would touch the target when greeting them. In all societies, participants were more comfortable with infection-risky contact and more likely to engage in physical contact during greetings with targets of higher interpersonal value. Such associations varied only modestly across societies. Notably, the associations between infection-risky contact and societal-level factors depended on target interpersonal value and were concentrated among high-value targets-contact was lower where historical pathogen prevalence and tightness were greater and higher where individualism and relational mobility were greater. These findings suggest that infection-risky contact is primarily guided by the value of social targets, with ecological and cultural factors playing a lesser role.

articles.title: Drivers of the likelihood of evolutionary rescue in response to novel infectious diseases.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The introduction of novel infectious diseases has caused significant declines in many species, and in some cases, local extinction. Simultaneously, hosts might adapt to these novel pathogens, allowing population recovery, an example of evolutionary rescue (ER). Novel infectious diseases differ from sudden, abiotic stressors in that disease only impacts a subset of individuals within the population and individuals might be affected for a finite period. Whether ER occurs in an infectious disease context, and how likely it is relative to abiotic stress, might depend on both host and pathogen characteristics such as the scale of transmission (e.g., local density-dependent transmission only or additional infection through an external reservoir), the degree of fatality or immunity, and the adaptive pathway in terms of whether adaptive alleles reduce mortality, reduce likelihood of infection, or enhance recovery. Here, we use a stochastic mathematical model of host-pathogen dynamics with evolution of a novel allele conferring disease robustness to quantify how population trajectories, including the probability of and time to ER, vary across adaptive pathways and disease characteristics. We find that ER is more likely to occur with dynamical disease transmission compared to a lasting stressor that affects the entire population, indicating that protecting a subset of the population from stress facilitates ER. Among cases with disease transmission, ER is generally more likely to occur with the adaptation of mortality-blocking alleles and sources of transmission that include an external reservoir.

articles.title: Structure-based targeting of Atg8 uncovers its essential role in autophagy-mediated detoxification.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Autophagy degrades and recycles intracellular material, allowing cells to maintain homeostasis and adapt to environmental stress. In the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, the core autophagy protein MoAtg8 is required for autophagosome formation and host infection. Here, we determined the crystal structure of MoAtg8 and used it for structure-guided virtual screening of a focused compound library enriched for natural products and autophagy-related molecules. This screen identified nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA), a naturally occurring lignan, as a MoAtg8-binding compound. NDGA suppressed conidial germination and appressorium formation, disrupted membrane integrity, and reduced pathogenicity in M. oryzae, with no detectable phytotoxicity to rice under the conditions tested. Mechanistically, the 5-lipoxygenase Mo5Lox, a target of NDGA, bound NDGA with lower affinity than MoAtg8. MoAtg8 associated with NDGA through Gln81 and promoted its autophagy-dependent delivery to vacuoles, thereby reducing compound availability to toxicity-associated targets. Disruption of autophagy or mutation of Gln81 in MoAtg8 increased fungal sensitivity to NDGA. These findings identify an autophagy-mediated detoxification route for an exogenous antifungal compound and reveal how MoAtg8-dependent trafficking modulates NDGA efficacy in a plant-pathogenic fungus.

articles.title: The impact of modulator therapy on the Pseudomonas aeruginosa cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts P. aeruginosa physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that P. aeruginosa lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of P. aeruginosa transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate P. aeruginosa gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with Staphylococcus aureus had limited effects. These findings show that ETI therapy has little impact on the conserved P. aeruginosa transcriptional state in human CF sputum and that refined sputum-like models remain useful for studying persistent infection in the postmodulator era.

articles.title: Heat and childhood respiratory health: exploring the evidence and raising the red flags.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Climate change impacts on the health of vulnerable groups globally. Heat, as a specific component of climate change, affects the respiratory health of children, particularly those from marginalized communities and in low- and middle-income countries. Understanding the exposure pathways for these outcomes is critical for interventions and policy development.

AREAS COVERED: A synthesis of the evidence for key heat-related childhood respiratory outcomes (asthma, infections, rhinitis and lung function) is presented. The knowledge gaps are highlighted. Interpreting the evidence requires understanding the approaches to heat exposure characterization in epidemiological studies. These exposure-response complexities are explored.

EXPERT OPINION: While the evidence for heat-related adverse events among children with asthma and respiratory infections is strong, it is less so for other respiratory outcomes. Inconsistencies exist across studies. These inconsistencies may be a result of how exposure is characterized in studies. While acute outcomes have been investigated mostly from hospital records, sub-clinical effects among children in community-based studies are absent. Limited studies have been conducted in marginalized communities or in low- and middle-income countries. Understanding exposure-response relationships and addressing gaps in the evidence is necessary for the development of appropriate interventions to protect the respiratory health of children.

articles.title: Author Correction to "Opening Up the Future of Valvular Heart Disease." Canadian Journal of Cardiology. Volume 42, Issue 5, Supplement, May 2026, Pages S59-S67. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cjca.2025.12.015.
Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Chaotic dynamics, commonly seen in weather systems and fluid turbulence, are characterized by their sensitivity to initial conditions, which makes accurate prediction challenging. Recent approaches have focused on developing data-driven models that attempt to preserve invariant statistics over long horizons since many chaotic systems exhibit dissipative behaviors and ergodicity. Despite the recent progress in such models, they are still often prone to generating unbounded trajectories, leading to invalid statistics evaluation. To address this fundamental challenge, we introduce a modular framework that provides formal guarantees of trajectory boundedness for neural network chaotic dynamics models. Our core contribution is a dissipative projection layer that leverages control-theoretic principles to ensure the learned system is dissipative. Specifically, our framework simultaneously learns a dynamics emulator and an energy-like function, where the latter is used to construct an algebraic dissipative constraint within the projection layer. Furthermore, the learned invariant level set provides an outer estimate for the system's strange attractor, which is known to be difficult to characterize due to its complex geometry. We demonstrate our model's ability to produce bounded long-horizon forecasts that preserve invariant statistics for chaotic dynamical systems, including Lorenz 96 and a reduced-order model of the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation.

articles.title: Guideline-Directed Treatment Eligibility and Burden of Untreated Stage-1 Hypertension Under the 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Hypertension Guideline: Insights From NHANES 2015 to 2020.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Adoption of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events risk model in the 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline may substantially alter the number and characteristics of adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension who are recommended for treatment. We aimed to quantify treatment-recommendation reclassification among adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension under the 2025 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based guideline compared with the 2017 pooled cohort equations-based guideline.

METHODS: This cross-sectional, nationally representative study used data from NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) 2015 to March 2020. The study population included adults aged 30 to 79 years with stage 1 hypertension, focusing on untreated participants. The exposure was the guideline-endorse cardiovascular risk assessment framework, pooled cohort equations, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events, respectively. The primary outcome was recommendation for antihypertensive pharmacotherapy.

RESULTS: Among 1926 adults with stage 1 hypertension (weighted 32.57 million), 59.59% (19.41 million) were untreated. Under the 2025 guideline, 13.84% (95% CI, 7.06%-20.63%) of untreated adults eligible under the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events threshold (0.42 million) became newly eligible for pharmacotherapy compared with the 2017 guideline. Newly eligible adults were older (mean±SE, 60.48 [0.77] years) and had higher diabetes prevalence (37.74% [95% CI, 15.45%-60.04%]) than those below the treatment threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association hypertension guideline recommendations were largely concordant with the prior guideline among adults with untreated stage 1 hypertension, while still newly identifying a subset of individuals with elevated cardiometabolic risk who may benefit from earlier intervention.

articles.title: Self-Monitoring of Blood Pressure: A Qualitative Study From Iraqi and Syrian Refugees.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) monitoring improves long-term blood pressure (BP) outcomes, but evidence on the acceptability and feasibility of SMBP in refugee populations is limited. Refugees face high cardiovascular risk due to poorly controlled BP.

METHODS: We recruited Iraqi and Syrian refugees living in San Diego, California, through the Family Health Centers of San Diego and enrolled them in a 6-week single-arm pilot acceptability and feasibility trial of SMBP with telemonitoring protocol modeled after the TASMIN (Telemonitoring and Self-Management in Hypertension) SMBP trial in the United Kingdom. Postintervention interviews assessed barriers and facilitators of the intervention. Inductive thematic analysis was performed, and results were organized using the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. Quantitative participant data were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 101 refugees participated (80% Iraqi individuals; mean age, 64±9.7; 49% men). Participants generally favored having their BP readings telemonitored and transmitted to their BP providers' office over completing the physical diary. Facilitators of SMBP included increased self-autonomy, device user friendliness, increased participant confidence, and family support. Barriers included device malfunction, old age, comorbidities, everyday life obligations, diary complexity, and forgetfulness. Participants emphasized for future interventions to promote autonomy, family engagement, and include a streamlined BP tracking method while also integrating provider-patient decision making.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study of SMBP among refugees. The intervention was found to be acceptable and feasible. Participants felt valued, self-autonomous, and confident in SMBP. Future interventions that use technology, family support, team-based care, and user-friendly devices may improve BP control in this population.

articles.title: Left Atrial Enlargement Identifies Risk of Stroke Independent of Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) enlargement has been proposed to increase stroke risk independent of atrial fibrillation (AF), but evidence accounting for AF over time is limited. We tested whether the association between LA enlargement and stroke persist independent of new-onset AF.

METHODS: In this observational study, participants from the Copenhagen General Population Study underwent cardiac computed tomography from 2010 through 2018 and were followed until December 2022. LA volume was indexed to body surface area. LA enlargement was defined using sex-specific cutoffs. The primary outcome was incident stroke. Secondary outcomes were incident AF, heart failure, dementia, and all-cause mortality. Individuals with baseline AF were excluded. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using cause-specific Cox models with AF modeled as a time-varying covariate.

RESULTS: Among 10 024 individuals (mean age 60 years, 57% women), 684 (6.8%) had LA enlargement. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years stroke occurred in 356 individuals (3.6%). LA enlargement was associated with a higher absolute risk of stroke (11.1% versus 4.6%, risk difference 6.5% [95% CI, 2.4-10.6]) and an increased hazard (adjusted HR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.09-2.05]; P=0.013), which remained similar after adjustment for incident AF, and in separate models using the CHA2DS2-VA score and P-wave terminal force in lead V1. LA enlargement was also associated with higher risk of AF (HR, 3.77 [95% CI, 3.00-4.73]) and heart failure (HR, 3.59 [95% CI, 2.54-5.06]) but not with dementia or all-cause mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: LA enlargement was associated with incident stroke independent of incident AF, supporting LA enlargement as a marker of thromboembolic risk.

articles.title: Advancing Heart Failure Classification Beyond Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction: Unsupervised Machine Learning Insights From the Japanese Nationwide Acute Decompensated Heart Failure Cohort: JROADHF.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) classification based on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) inadequately captures HF heterogeneity, limiting phenotype-specific therapies. While machine learning (ML) has been applied to HF with preserved ejection fraction, comprehensive approaches across the full LVEF spectrum remain scarce. This study aimed to identify HF phenogroups across the entire LVEF spectrum using unsupervised ML, moving beyond the LVEF-centric and fragmented understanding of HF.

METHODS: We analyzed 13 238 patients with acute HF from a nationwide, multicenter Japanese cohort (JROADHF [Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure]). Unsupervised latent class analysis identified phenogroups from 46 clinically important admission variables. The primary end point was the 5-year composite of cardiovascular death or HF readmission.

RESULTS: Three ML-based phenogroups emerged: (1) "HF with congestion and lower output" (n=2638), (2) "HF with afterload mismatch" (n=3462), and (3) "HFpEF-like HF" (n=7138). ML-derived groups stratified risk for the primary end point (P<0.001), whereas LVEF-based classification did not (P=0.267). Compared with phenogroup 3, phenogroup 1 had a higher age-adjusted risk by Cox regression model (hazard ratio [HR], 1.60 [95% CI, 1.49-1.71]) and phenogroup 2 had a lower risk (HR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.60-0.70]). Notably, variable-importance analysis by discriminative power for phenogroup assignment indicated that total bilirubin, left ventricular diastolic diameter, and hemoglobin rather than LVEF principally drove classification.

CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised ML identified novel HF phenogroups with distinct 5-year outcomes. This framework moves beyond an LVEF-centric paradigm, deepens understanding of HF pathophysiology, and may facilitate phenotype-specific therapeutic development.

articles.title: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Risk of Congenital Heart Defects in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To date, >10 million children have been conceived via assisted reproductive technology (ART) globally. However, there are some concerns about potential adverse outcomes associated with ART-conceived pregnancies, including the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs). This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between ART and the risk of major CHDs as well as their specific subtypes.

METHODS: Major electronic databases were screened for studies comparing the incidence of CHD following ART-conceived pregnancies versus spontaneous conception. The primary end point was study-defined incidence of CHDs. Secondary end points included incidence of tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries, aortic coarctation, ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, pulmonary valve atresia, tricuspid valve atresia, and hypoplastic left heart. Pairwise meta-analyses were performed using frequentist random-effect models to calculate risk ratios and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies, encompassing a total of 45 916 925 subjects (4986 conceived via ART), were included in the quantitative synthesis. ART was significantly associated with a higher risk of major CHD compared with natural pregnancy (risk ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.68-3.28]), with significant heterogeneity across the studies. An increased risk of tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect following ART-conceived pregnancies was found, while no difference was found on other CHDs. Prespecified sensitivity analyses were in line with the primary findings of the meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our meta-analysis shows a potential link between ART and increased risk of major CHDs, particularly on tetralogy of Fallot, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect.

articles.title: Polygenic Determinants of Arterial Stiffness: Implications for Hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Components of arterial stiffness (structural stiffness from aging and load-dependent stiffness from high blood pressure [BP]) are markers for cardiovascular disease risk. We evaluated relationships between polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for BP and arterial stiffness.

METHODS: Participants (n=5804) are from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) with measures of carotid ultrasound and genomic DNA. Carotid pulse wave velocity (PWV) was calculated from carotid ultrasound. Structural stiffness was calculated by adjusting carotid PWV to a 120/80 mm Hg BP with participant-specific models. Load-dependent stiffness was the difference of total and structural stiffness. BP PRSs were derived from genome-wide associations. Associations were assessed with multivariable-adjusted regression models. Mendelian randomization was performed with 2-stage least squares.

RESULTS: Participants were aged 62.8±10.3 years. Systolic BP (SBP) was 133.5±20.5 mm Hg, diastolic BP (DBP) was 74.27±10.28 mm Hg, and pulse pressure was 59.22±16.17 mm Hg. Total carotid PWV was associated with the SBP PRS (β=0.10±0.02, P=5.25E-08) and the DBP PRS (β: 0.08±0.02, P=7.26E-07) but not pulse pressure PRS (P=0.05). Load-dependent carotid PWV was associated with the SBP PRS (β=0.09±0.01, P=7.93×10-30), the DBP PRS (β=0.09±0.01, P=4.92×10-34) and the pulse pressure PRS (β=0.03±0.01, P=8.18×10-5). Structural carotid PWV was not associated with any BP PRSs. With Mendelian randomization, SBP and DBP showed significant independent positive effects on load-dependent stiffness (P<0.001); only SBP was significant for total carotid PWV after accounting for DBP.

CONCLUSIONS: There are key differences in the genetic underpinnings of the mechanistic components of arterial stiffness.

articles.title: Permissive Cardiotoxicity: An Evolving Paradigm.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Permissive cardiotoxicity is an evolving clinical practice pattern that balances the management of cancer treatment-associated cardiotoxicities with the risk of interrupting lifesaving or life-extending cancer treatments. This paradigm shift has been catalyzed by advancements in the diagnostic and therapeutic tools available to treating clinicians, as well as a recognition of the consequences of withholding or delaying cancer therapy. Permissive cardiotoxicity has become a central tenet in the practice of cardio-oncologists; however, recognition and confidence in managing cardiotoxicity is also crucial for the general cardiologist and oncologist due to the growing population of patients with cancer. This review aims to (1) highlight the philosophy of permissive cardiotoxicity, (2) provide a framework for risk stratification of cardiovascular toxicities, (3) describe systems of care considerations for successful implementation of permissive cardiotoxicity, and (4) review the existing literature and guideline recommendations for specific cardiovascular toxicity mitigation.

articles.title: Body Mass Index, Valsartan, and Myocardial Remodeling in Early-Stage Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized VANISH Trial.
authors: Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (VANISH) Investigators
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with adverse outcomes in overt hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the prevalence and impact of elevated body mass index (BMI) in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is uncertain.

METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the randomized VANISH (Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy) trial, participants were categorized according to baseline BMI (nonelevated or elevated [≥85th percentile if age <18 years; ≥25 kg/m2 if age ≥18 years]). Exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake [milliliters per kilogram per minute]) and cardiac imaging parameters were evaluated by baseline BMI and 2-year change in BMI.

RESULTS: Among 171 (96%) participants (mean age, 23±10 years; 39% female sex; 97% White), 82 (48%) had nonelevated BMI and 89 (52%) had an elevated BMI. After covariate adjustment, higher baseline BMI was associated with lower peak oxygen uptake; lower left ventricular systolic and diastolic function; higher left ventricular mass; and higher atrial, ventricular, and extracellular volumes. Similarly, greater 2-year increases in BMI were associated with greater declines in peak oxygen uptake and greater increases in left ventricular mass. Participants with elevated BMI were more likely to develop late gadolinium enhancement over 2 years (adjusted odds ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-11.9]; P=0.033). Valsartan appeared to modestly attenuate 2-year increases in body weight versus placebo (adjusted mean difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -6.2 to -0.1%]; P=0.042). Baseline BMI did not appear to modify the effect of valsartan on cardiac remodeling (Pinteraction=0.96).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated BMI was common and associated with greater hypertrophic, eccentric, and fibrotic remodeling in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Two-year increases in BMI were associated with greater phenotypic progression. These findings suggest prevention and treatment of elevated BMI may attenuate hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01912534.

articles.title: Pilot Randomized Trial of 2 Food Purchasing Interventions in Individuals With Hypertension in New Orleans: An American Heart Association Food Is Medicine Initiative.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Consuming fruits and vegetables daily is linked to improved health in individuals with hypertension. Voucher incentives have been shown to improve healthy food purchasing. The objective of this study was to compare the effects of an online versus in-store voucher intervention on food purchasing and health outcomes in hypertensive individuals.

METHODS: In this randomized pilot trial, 98 participants with uncontrolled hypertension received a $100 monthly food voucher to either an online grocery platform or an in-store local grocery. Both groups received educational materials. The primary outcome was change in self-reported fruit and vegetable consumption. Secondary outcomes were voucher use, engagement with educational materials, and changes in blood pressure, weight, and body mass index. Generalized estimating equations for repeated measures were used to assess changes in food-group consumption over 5 months.

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 57 years, and 65% were women. No difference was detected between arms for self-reported fruit and vegetable consumption. There was an overall 20% (interquartile range, -17% to 93%) increase in fruit and vegetable consumption within both arms. Voucher use was significantly higher in the in-store arm (>90%) than the online arm (<64%). Engagement with educational materials was greater in the in-store arm. No significant changes in weight, body mass index, or blood pressure were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: No difference was detected between in-store and online vouchers for fruit and vegetable consumption. Higher engagement and voucher use were observed in the in-store arm than the online arm. Future interventions should be conducted in larger populations and address technological barriers to enhance program effectiveness and assess long-term health impacts.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06214806.

articles.title: Prevalence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Established Cardiovascular Disease Among All of Us Participants: Benchmarking Against National Estimates.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The AoU (All of Us) Research Program aims to accelerate precision-medicine research. To provide context for the generalizability of findings we benchmarked cardiovascular risk factors and established cardiovascular disease prevalence in AoU against nationally representative estimates.

METHODS: We included AoU participants enrolled between May 2017 and June 2022 and the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) 2017 to March 2020 cycle. The AoU Survey cohort included participants who completed the Personal and Family Health History survey (N=185 232). AoU EHR included participants with linked electronic health record (EHR) (N=287 012). We identified cardiovascular risk factors and cardiovascular disease through survey questions in AoU Survey and NHANES, and Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine codes for AoU EHR.

RESULTS: AoU Survey and AoU EHR were older than NHANES (56.1±17 years and 57.6±17 years versus 47.5±18 years) with more female participants (64% and 60% versus 51.8%). Black participants were underrepresented in AoU Survey (9.1%) and overrepresented in AoU EHR (19.9%); 11.5% in NHANES. Prevalence of cardiovascular comorbidities in AoU Survey and NHANES were similar but lower in AoU Survey when age adjusted (eg, hypertension 31.7% in NHANES versus 19.7% in AoU Survey, diabetes 11.3% versus 8%). Black participants had higher unadjusted rates of hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease and congestive heart failure than NHANES. AoU EHR with its code-based identification had higher unadjusted prevalence of most cardiovascular comorbidities; differences attenuated with age-adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: AoU includes more historically underrepresented groups, but representation varies by whether cohorts are defined by survey versus EHR availability. Further, disease prevalence can change based on how conditions are ascertained.

articles.title: Associations of Mild or Trace Valvular Abnormalities With Cardiac Remodeling in Older Adults: The ARIC Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of mild/trace valvular abnormalities on cardiac remodeling is not well understood, despite their association with poor cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: Using data from 4684 participants in the ARIC (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) Study (2011-2013), aged 66 to 90 years, we examined cross-sectional associations of mild/trace valvular abnormalities (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and mitral regurgitation) with cardiac parameters using multivariable linear regression models. Cardiac parameters included cardiac structure (eg, left ventricular mass index), systolic function (eg, ejection fraction), diastolic function, and biomarkers (eg, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T).

RESULTS: The prevalence was 4.3% for mild aortic stenosis, 10.9% for mild/trace aortic regurgitation, and 44.7% for mild/trace mitral regurgitation. Mitral regurgitation showed the most consistent associations with cardiac measures (left ventricular mass index 5.48 g/m2 [95% CI, 4.38-6.57 g/m2]; ejection fraction -1.92% [95% CI, -2.29% to -1.54%]; high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.08 log ng/L [95% CI, 0.05-0.12 log ng/L]). Aortic stenosis was associated with impaired ventricular filling (Ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e') lateral ratio 2.00 [95% CI, 1.48-2.53]) and elevated biomarkers (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.17 ng/L [95% CI, 0.09-0.25 ng/L]), whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsened cardiac structure (left ventricular mass index 3.52 [95% CI, 1.76-5.28] g/m2) and systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction -1.54% [95% CI, -2.14% to -0.94%]). A dose-response relationship was also observed between the number of total abnormalities and all cardiac parameters examined.

CONCLUSIONS: Mild/trace mitral regurgitation was most consistently associated with all cardiac parameters examined. Aortic stenosis was associated with elevated E/e' lateral ratio and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsening in cardiac structure and ejection fraction. Our study supports the possibility of pathophysiological contributions of these mild/trace valvular abnormalities.

articles.title: Plasma Glutamine and Glutamate in Relation to Clinical Outcomes After Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Prospective Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glutamine (Gln) and glutamate (Glu) have been suggested to play a pivotal role in neuronal homeostasis and metabolic regulation, showing potential as prognostic biomarkers for stroke. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of plasma Gln, Glu, and glutamine-to-glutamate ratio (GGR) with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with ischemic stroke.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter CATIS (China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke) included 3499 participants with ischemic stroke. Plasma Gln and Glu levels were measured within 24 hours of hospital admission using ultraperformance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The primary outcome was unfavorable functional outcome (death or major disability) at 3 months after ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes included major disability, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular events. Risk discrimination and reclassification of Glu metabolites were assessed.

RESULTS: Compared with the lowest quartiles, multivariable-adjusted odds ratios of the primary outcome in the highest quartiles were 0.37 (95% CI, 0.28-0.47) for Gln, 2.05 (95% CI, 1.60-2.62) for Glu, and 0.37 (95% CI, 0.29-0.48) for GGR (all P for trend <0.001). Approximately 9% of the associations of Glu metabolites and unfavorable functional outcome were mediated by the composite marker of inflammation and insulin resistance. Incorporating Gln, Glu, and GGR into conventional risk factor models improved risk discrimination and stratification for unfavorable functional outcome, with increases in C statistics (from 0.831 to 0.842-0.848), net reclassification indices (22.9%-31.0%), and integrated discrimination improvements (1.1%-1.6%) (all P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Plasma Gln, Glu, and GGR were associated with adverse clinical outcomes, providing prognostic significance in patients with ischemic stroke.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01840072.

articles.title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.

METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

articles.title: Combined Effect of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry on Cardiovascular Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap syndrome has been linked to worse cardiovascular outcomes. Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is recognized as an early stage of chronic obstructive pulmonary diseas. However, whether the coexistence of OSA and PRISm confers increased cardiovascular risk remains unknown.

METHODS: Using data from the Sleep Heart Health Study, participants were categorized into 4 groups according to OSA and PRISm status. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. The secondary outcome was cardiovascular disease mortality. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate the association of these groups with the risk of cardiovascular outcomes.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.45 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events was 17.00% in non-OSA with normal lung function, 27.52% in non-OSA with PRISm, 25.28% in OSA with normal lung function, and 49.40% in OSA with PRISm. After multivariable adjustment, compared with non-OSA with normal lung function, the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events were 1.20 (95% CI, 0.82-1.75) in non-OSA with PRISm, 1.04 (95% CI, 0.89-1.21) in OSA with normal lung function, and 1.52 (95% CI, 1.08-2.12) in OSA with PRISm. Corresponding HRs for CVD mortality were 2.02 (95% CI, 1.26-3.24), 1.05 (95% CI, 0.81-1.35), and 2.17 (95% CI, 1.41-3.34), respectively. A significant sex interaction was observed (P for interaction=0.009), with the association present only in women.

CONCLUSIONS: The coexistence of OSA and PRISm is independently associated with increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This association is observed predominantly in women.

articles.title: Genetic Variants in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Disease: A Systematic Review and Targeted Meta-Analysis Highlighting the RNF213 rs112735431.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) is a leading cause of ischemic stroke and premature mortality, with higher prevalence in specific ethnic groups. Multiple studies have evaluated the association of ICAD and genetic variants. This study aims to systematically review and summarize the current genetic contributors of ICAD.

METHODS: Systematic review was performed following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from inception to September 2025 for human studies examining single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) associations and ICAD. Three independent reviewers extracted data on study characteristics, SNVs, alleles and P values. SNVs reported in >1 study were pooled using a fixed-effects model. Expression quantitative trait loci analysis evaluated the regulatory effects of identified SNVs across brain and arterial tissue. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted to identify relevant biological pathways.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies met inclusion criteria, comprising a total of 15 535 individuals, of whom 3638 had ICAD. Across these studies, 35 SNVs were identified, mapping to 26 unique genes. In the pooled analysis, ICAD was associated with RNF213 rs112735431 (odds ratio, 18.61 [95% CI, 11.84-29.25]). Other SNVs were found in genes including ADIPOQ, INSR, and NTNG1. Functional enrichment highlighted lipid metabolism and triglyceride homeostasis pathways as key contributors to ICAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: This review consolidates current evidence on SNVs associated with ICAD, highlighting RNF213 rs112735431 as a major genetic contributor, particularly in East Asian populations. Further research is needed to clarify the functional roles of these variants and their potential as therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Diameter Predicts Clinical Outcomes in Patients Supported With Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study sought to determine the impact of left ventricular size on clinical outcomes after a microaxial flow pump was surgically implanted.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included patients who received a surgical microaxial left ventricular assist device from May 2020 to February 2024 at 2 high-volume centers in the United States. Patients were categorized into 2 groups based on their preimplant left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD): "small LVEDD," defined as LVEDD ≤5.5 cm, and "large LVEDD," defined as LVEDD >5.5 cm, respectively. End points were all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation, in-hospital death, death 30-days after discharge, and survival at 30-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Two-hundred sixty-two patients received an Impella 5.5. Preimplant LVEDD was documented in 194 (74%) patients, where 50 patients had LVEDD ≤5.5 cm and 144 patients had LVEDD >5.5 cm. Patients with a small LVEDD had a higher rate of all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation (32% versus 11.8%, P=0.002), in-hospital death (42% versus 20.1%, P=0.004), and death 30 days after discharge (44% versus 20.8%, P=0.003). In adjusted analyses, patients with a greater LVEDD had 62% decreased risk of long-term death (hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.19-0.76]; P=0.001), compared with patients with a smaller LVEDD.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, all-comer study, we found that patients with reduced left ventricular dimension who required an Impella 5.5 had worse outcomes. Further research is warranted to recapitulate our observations across more centers.

articles.title: Thoracic Intermuscular Adiposity, Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction, and Prognosis After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body mass index is a widely-used yet imprecise measure of adiposity. Thoracic intermuscular adiposity is reported to be related with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), but their prognostic implications after cardiac surgery are not clear. This study aimed to investigate whether computed tomography-derived thoracic intermuscular adiposity and CMD provide better prognostic information than body mass index in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS: This study consecutively enrolled 666 patients undergoing elective surgery from 3 centers. Using computed tomography at the T12 vertebral level, we quantified the cross-sectional areas (cm2) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and intermuscular adipose tissue. Intermuscular fat fraction was calculated as intermuscular adipose tissue/(intermuscular adipose tissue+skeletal muscle)×100%. CMD was defined by a coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance >25. The primary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and rehospitalization for heart failure.

RESULTS: A total of 63 MACEs (9.5%) occurred during a median 17-month follow-up. Obesity defined by body mass index (10.7% of patients) was not associated with MACE (P=0.187). Each 1% increase in intermuscular fat fraction was significantly associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.14-1.31]; P<0.001), whereas body mass index showed no such correlation (P=0.964). CMD independently predicted MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.03; [95% CI: 1.15-3.61]; P = 0.015), whereas intermuscular fat fraction did not (P=0.516). The annualized MACE rate was significantly higher in patients with CMD (11.0% versus 5.2%, P=0.004).
