TRIAL REGISTRATION: chinadrugtrials.org.cn , CTR20231413.

articles.title: Characteristics and Risk Factors of Pollen-Food Allergy Syndrome in Patients With Hay Fever: A Digital Cross-Sectional Cohort Study Using AllerSearch.
articles.journal: Journal of investigational allergology & clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Pollen-food allergy syndrome (PFAS) is a frequent comorbidity in individuals with hay fever. Identifying risk factors and allergen clusters can aid targeted interventions and management strategies. Objective: This study characterizes PFAS in patients with hay fever and identifies associated risk factors using the mobile health platform, AllerSearch.

METHODS: A digital cross-sectional cohort study was conducted in Japan from August 2020 to September 2024. Participants provided demographic, medical, lifestyle, and environmental data via AllerSearch. PFAS was identified based on self-reported allergic reactions to specific fruits and vegetables. Allergen patterns were analyzed using Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection clustering, and risk factors were assessed via multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 2874 participants, 2352 had hay fever, and 1788 (23.9%) reported PFAS. The most common triggers were melon (22.9%), kiwi (18.3%), and tomato (11.7%). Significant risk factors included a history of allergic disease (OR, 1.58), asthma (1.44), atopic dermatitis (1.90), urticaria (2.73), contact lens discontinuation during hay fever season (1.50), sensitivity to yellow sand or particulate matter 2.5 (3.42), and drug allergy (3.04). Seven allergen clusters were identified, with Cluster 6 exhibiting broad allergen sensitivity and the remaining clusters each associated with a single food. Onset of hay fever was earlier in Clusters 1, 4, and 6 than in non-PFAS individuals (P=.002, P=.002, and P=.002, respectively).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights key factors and allergen clusters associated with PFAS using a mobile health approach. Our findings may facilitate tailored interventions and improve quality of life for affected individuals.

articles.title: Artificial capnothorax versus single-lung ventilation in minimally invasive esophagectomy for esophageal cancer: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial capnothorax during surgery potentially increases the risk of tumor cell dissemination and impacts survival. This trial aimed to investigate the effect of artificial capnothorax on the prognosis of patients with esophageal cancer who underwent minimally invasive esophagectomy.

METHODS: This prospective, randomized controlled trial was conducted in two high-volume hospitals in China. Between August 2019 and January 2020, 110 patients with resectable esophageal cancer were randomized to undergo single-lung ventilation ( n = 55) or capnothorax procedures ( n = 55). The analysis was based on the intention-to-treat principle. The final follow-up occurred in January 2023.

RESULTS: A total of 110 patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. After surgery, the incidence of patients exhibiting incremental changes in circulating tumor cell levels was 18.6% (8/43) in the capnothorax group and 2.7% (1/37) in the single-lung ventilation group ( P = 0.033) (mean changes, -3.9 ± 3.4 [FU/3 mL] vs. -2.4 ± 2.9 [FU/3 mL], respectively; P = 0.039). Compared with the capnothorax group, the single-lung ventilation group had better 3-year overall survival rates (81.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 72.4-92.0% vs. 65.2%, 95% CI: 59.3-78.8%; P = 0.049) and disease-free survival rates (81.6%, 95% CI: 72.4-93.0% vs. 61.6%, 95% CI: 50.1-75.7%; P = 0.019). Multivariate analysis indicated that artificial pneumothorax potentially impaired overall survival (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.35, 95% CI: 1.05-5.24; P = 0.037) and disease-free survival (HR: 2.70, 95% CI: 1.23-5.94; P = 0.014).

CONCLUSIONS: Artificial capnothorax appears to be associated with poor oncological outcomes in patients with esophageal cancer. Single-lung ventilation in minimally invasive esophagectomy is safer and more favorable than capnothorax.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ( http://chictr.org.cn ), ChiCTR1900025262.

articles.title: CPTAC Consensus Subtypes Add No Incremental Prognostic Value Beyond Stage and Grade in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Proteomic Reanalysis.
articles.abstract: Molecular subtypes from multi-omic profiling have refined the biological characterization of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but whether they add prognostic information to clinicopathological variables already in use is unclear. We evaluated the incremental prognostic value of proteomically assigned CPTAC consensus subtypes (NMF1-NMF3) against stage and grade, and asked whether subtype identity is carried by a biologically specific set of proteins. Subtypes were predicted from tumor proteomes in 211 patients under nested cross-validation and a locked hold-out design, and the analysis was repeated using methylation subtypes defined without proteomic input. A transcriptome classifier was transferred to 533 TCGA-KIRC tumors, and the transferred subtypes entered nested Cox models containing age, stage and Fuhrman grade. A curated set of 139 metabolic enzymes was compared against 500 random protein sets of the same size and against random sets additionally matched on abundance, missingness, variance and co-regulation. Classification reached a macro-average AUROC of 0.901 (95% CI 0.871-0.933) under cross-validation and 0.862 in the untouched expansion cohort; methylation subtypes were classified with comparable accuracy (0.905). Subtype proportions in TCGA-KIRC differed from CPTAC by at most 2.5 percentage points. Among 518 patients with complete clinical data, grade improved a model containing age and stage (p = 0.001), whereas subtype added nothing once grade was included (p = 0.703; change in C-index +0.0019, 95% CI -0.0023 to +0.0116); with 171 deaths, the study could detect a hazard ratio of 1.64 at 80% power, so small effects remain possible. The metabolic panel did not outperform size-matched (p = 0.649) or covariate-matched random sets (p = 0.762), whereas a housekeeping set performed significantly worse. CPTAC consensus subtype identity is highly predictable from the proteome but redundantly encoded rather than concentrated in a functional class, and adds no measurable prognostic information beyond stage and grade in this cohort. High classification accuracy for a molecular label is not evidence of clinical utility; these conclusions apply to the CPTAC NMF scheme as evaluated here and should not be extended to proteomic subtyping in general.

articles.title: Long-Term Golimumab Treatment Persistence and Clinical Outcomes in Axial Spondyloarthritis: A Real-World Cohort from Kazakhstan.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-term real-world evidence on golimumab in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) from Central Asia is limited. We evaluated clinical outcomes through week 144, treatment persistence through 36 months, factors associated with discontinuation, and reasons for discontinuation in Kazakhstan. Methods: This prospective observational cohort included 113 adults with axSpA enrolled at two rheumatology centers in Almaty in October 2019. All had received golimumab 50 mg subcutaneously every four weeks for at least 12 weeks before enrollment. Time zero for persistence analyses was the enrollment date. Clinical assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 12, 24, 52, 104, and 144. Treatment persistence was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and factors associated with confirmed discontinuation were explored using Cox regression. Clinical responses were assessed using non-responder imputation (NRI; N = 113). Results: During 36 months, 24 patients had confirmed permanent discontinuation; two patients lost to follow-up without confirmed discontinuation were censored. Kaplan-Meier estimated persistence was 89.3% (95% CI, 83.8-95.2%) at 12 months, 79.4% (72.2-87.3%) at 24 months, and 78.5% (71.2-86.5%) at 36 months. Among 88 patients with paired baseline and week 144 assessments, the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI), Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ASDAS-ESR), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI), and Maastricht Ankylosing Spondylitis Enthesitis Score (MASES) improved significantly (all p < 0.001). With NRI, 64.6% achieved BASDAI50, 59.3% ASDAS inactive disease, and 54.9% ASDAS major improvement at week 144. Higher Rheumatic Disease Comorbidity Index (RDCI) score (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.312, 95% CI, 1.042-1.653) and functional class III-IV versus I-II (adjusted HR 2.412, 95% CI, 1.037-5.611) were associated with higher discontinuation hazards in exploratory analyses. Loss of effectiveness was the most frequent reason for discontinuation (54.2%). Adverse events were recorded only when they led to discontinuation and therefore do not represent overall safety incidence. Conclusions: Golimumab was characterized by substantial 36-month treatment persistence and clinical improvement among patients who remained on treatment and were evaluable at week 144 (n = 88). Full-cohort NRI analyses also demonstrated clinically relevant responses at week 144. Comorbidity burden and poorer functional class were associated with discontinuation in exploratory analyses. These findings add long-term real-world evidence from an under-represented geographic setting.

articles.title: Apixaban for thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiology patients: Real-world data from a single institution.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombosis is a major complication in children with congenital or acquired heart disease, contributing to significant morbidity and mortality. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), including apixaban, are increasingly used for thromboprophylaxis in this population yet real-world paediatric data remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of apixaban as thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiac patients receiving commercially available adult tablet formulations outside a clinical trial setting.

PATIENTS/METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≤18 years with congenital or acquired heart disease who received apixaban at the University Children's Hospital Zurich from October 2022 to June 2025. Dosing was approximated to the SAXOPHONE trial using commercially available tablets that were split or crushed, without therapeutic laboratory monitoring. Outcomes included incident thrombosis (primary), major bleeding, clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB), and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were included with a median age of 4.6 years (IQR 3.3-9.8) and median apixaban exposure of 210 days (IQR 83-461), totalling 18,799 patient-days (51.5 patient-years). Single ventricle physiology was the most common underlying diagnosis (40/67, 60%) and Fontan circulation the most frequent indication (34/67, 51%). Two thrombotic events occurred (incidence rate 3.9 per 100 patient-years), both in the context of additional thrombotic risk factors. No major bleeding or CRNMB events were recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban appeared safe and effective as thromboprophylaxis in this paediatric cardiology cohort, with no major or CRNMB and a low rate of thrombotic events. These findings add to the growing body of real-world evidence supporting DOAC use in children with cardiac disease.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Ablation of the Left Atrial Appendage Before Mechanical Closure to Reduce Peri-Device Leak (STUN-AF).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAC) is plagued by late peri-device leak. We posited that appendage contraction prevents full LAA seal, so conversely, LAA stunning with pulsed field ablation (PFA) of the LAA (left atrial appendage ablation [LAAA]) might promote rapid appendage thrombosis/obliteration.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the impact of LAAA during concomitant procedures on eliminating leaks.

METHODS: At 3 centers, consecutive patients undergoing concomitant PFA and LAAC also underwent LAAA or did not undergo LAAA, at operator discretion. Initial (∼3-4 months) (29% transesophageal echocardiography/71% computed tomography) and 12-month imaging were compared with a primary composite outcome of LAA patency, defined as either detectable flow into the LAA or evidence of echo-free space/contrast medium behind the device.

RESULTS: Among 317 total patients undergoing PFA and LAAC, including 222 patients who underwent LAAA and 95 who did not (control patients), all underwent initial imaging and 126 reached 12-month imaging follow-up. Device compression was 28% with LAAA vs 25% without LAAA (P < 0.001). Implantation success was 100%. The periprocedural adverse event rate was 2% in both groups. The primary composite outcome of LAA patency was significantly reduced with LAAA vs no-LAAA, both at 3-4 months (29% vs 64%; P < 0.001) and at 12 months (4% vs 42%; P < 0.001). Device-related thrombus rates were low and similar (2.3% vs 3.2%; P = 0.7). A validation subset including only patients with alternating LAAA assignment (LAAA: n = 59; no-LAAA: n = 63) again revealed that LAAA was associated with reduced LAA patency (3-4 months: 34% vs 51%; P = 0.06; 12 months: 8% vs 36%; P = 0.2). Final LAA e' velocity was significantly different between groups (17 ± 7 vs 34 ± 16 cm/s; P < 0.001), with higher velocity associated with LAA patency (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: PFA of the LAA has potential to reduce LAA patency during device-based LAAC.

articles.title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.

AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.

METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.

RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

articles.title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined.

AIMS: We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch.

METHODS: Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported.

RESULTS: A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated. Feasibility was reached in 85.5% of patients and effectiveness in 77.4% of patients - except for 11.3% with suboptimal debulking, 3.2% with access-related case abortion, and 8.1% with case cancellation where no mass was found intraprocedurally. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 14.5% of patients, with a procedure-attributable mortality rate of 3.2%. VARC-3 major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, ACS, and stroke occurred in 3.2%, 8.1%, 3.2%, 3.2%, and 6.5% of patients, respectively. Intraprocedural events included hypoxia (6.5%), hypotension (9.7%), embolism (3.2%), air embolism (1.6%), and increased mitral regurgitation (6.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: TVME in left-sided and aortic arch masses is feasible and demonstrates reasonable effectiveness. However, the considerable rate of safety-related events highlights the need for better case selection and procedural refinement, such as optimal embolic protection.

articles.title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.

AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.

METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

articles.title: First Experience of a New Transfemoral Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement System.
External validation of the SNAPP score for hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after living donor liver transplantation.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Binary morphologic criteria cannot capture biologic heterogeneity among living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) recipients. SNAPP score (tumor size, number, AFP, PIVKA-II, PET/CT) yields a graded recurrence-risk estimate but lacks independent validation. We externally validated SNAPP for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence after LDLT.

METHODS: SNAPP was applied without refitting in 230 LDLT recipients with HCC at two Korean centers and benchmarked against Milan, French-AFP, Metroticket 2.0, MoRAL, RETREAT, and three LDLT-derived selection systems (Kyoto, Medanta LDLT, and National Cancer Center Korea). Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and reclassification were assessed using IPCW-weighted methods with bootstrap 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Among 230 patients (median follow-up, 91.5 mo), 49 (21.3%) recurred. SNAPP achieved discrimination comparable to the best pretransplant tool, MoRAL (Harrell C-index, 0.756; 95% CI, 0.690-0.821), and exceeded Milan (0.503; Holm-adjusted p=0.01). Discrimination was numerically higher than Metroticket 2.0 (0.605) and three LDLT-derived systems (C-index difference, 0.10-0.15), but none of these differences survived correction for multiplicity (Holm-adjusted p=0.24). RETREAT, a posttransplant benchmark, reached 0.807. Calibration-in-the-large was -0.068; slope, 0.59 (95% CI, 0.43-0.77). Within Milan-eligible patients (n=217), SNAPP resolved a monotonic, approximately 5.9-fold gradient in 5-year cumulative recurrence (11.9%, 48.8%, 70.0%). Reclassification favored SNAPP over Milan, French-AFP, and Metroticket 2.0; the center-adjusted hazard ratio per point 1.79 (95% CI, 1.51-2.14).

CONCLUSIONS: SNAPP showed discrimination comparable to MoRAL and exceeded Milan, with numerically higher but not definitively superior discrimination compared with Metroticket 2.0, French-AFP, and three LDLT-specific selection systems, while resolving biologic heterogeneity within Milan-eligible candidates using only pretransplant variables. With near-zero calibration-in-the-large but a slope below unity, SNAPP supports risk stratification at listing, though individualized probability estimates require recalibration.

articles.title: Finerenone versus Steroidal MRAs in Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease without Prior Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) markedly increase the risk of heart failure (HF) and death. While finerenone improves outcomes in clinical trials, real-world evidence and direct comparisons with steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are limited. We evaluated finerenone versus steroidal MRAs (spironolactone and eplerenone) in patients without prior HF.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX platform, we conducted a retrospective multi-center observational study. We identified patients aged ≥18 years with T2D and CKD without prior HF and ischemic heart disease, who initiated MRAs after receiving a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor as first-line therapy between 2021 and 2024 (N=3,680). Of these, 724 initiated finerenone and 1,542 initiated a steroidal MRA. After propensity score matching, each group included 551 patients. The primary outcome was all-cause death during the 18-month follow-up period; the secondary outcome was new-onset HF and renal outcome (a composite of end-stage renal disease and dialysis).

RESULTS: Over 18-month, finerenone initiation was associated with lower incidence rates of all-cause death (2.1 vs 4.5 events/100 person-years; incidence rate difference, -2.41; 95% CI, -4.38 to -0.44) and new-onset HF (6.5 vs 12.9; -6.38; 95% CI, -9.75 to -3.02), whereas no significant difference was observed for the renal outcome (8.3 vs 9.1; -0.81; 95% CI, -3.99 to 2.37).

CONCLUSIONS: Finerenone was associated with a lower 18-month risk of all-cause death compared with steroidal MRAs in patients aged ≥18 years with T2D and CKD without prior HF, who received an SGLT2 inhibitor as first-line therapy; however, residual confounding cannot be excluded, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Discrepancy Between Clinical Suspicion and Legal Outcomes in Suspected Child Abuse: A 10-Year Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract: Despite mandatory reporting, many suspected child abuse cases never proceed to formal investigation in Korea. We retrospectively reviewed 83 pediatric patients evaluated for suspected child abuse at a tertiary hospital between 2015 and 2025, screened using the Finding Instrument for Non-accidental Deeds score, and analyzed clinical characteristics, injury severity, and investigative outcomes. The mean age was 4.3 years, and mechanical injury was the most common abuse type (n = 68). Twenty-four patients (28.9%) were severe cases requiring surgery or intensive care or resulting in death. Overall, 33 patients (39.8%) were determined as 'no suspicion,' including 11 of 24 severe cases (45.8%); this proportion decreased from 45.7% to 37.8% after the 2021 policy reform. A critical gap persists between medical recognition of child abuse and the legal response, warranting closer integration of clinical assessment with child protection and investigative systems.

articles.title: Hepatic Cysts in Korea: Prevalence, Incidence, and Risk Factors Based on a 5.8-Year Follow-up Health Screening Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic cysts are fluid-filled liver lesions that are mostly asymptomatic, but fewer than 15% of patients present clinically significant symptoms. Reported prevalence ranges from 2.5% to 71%, yet prior studies have been limited by small populations and incomplete assessment of risk factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, incidence, and risk factors using data from a large health screening cohort in Korea.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 78,676 participants in the Health and Prevention Enhancement cohort who underwent abdominal ultrasound at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center from 2003 and 2014. Hepatic cysts were identified using a validated rule-based text-mining algorithm applied to ultrasound reports. Prevalence was estimated from baseline data. Incidence was assessed in 41,179 participants initially negative for hepatic cysts. Risk factors were determined through Cox proportional hazards modeling.

RESULTS: The prevalence of hepatic cysts at baseline was 8.54% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 8.34-8.73). The incidence was 23.4 per 1,000 person-years at risk (95% CI, 22.8-24.0). Cox regression identified hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBs-Ag) positivity (hazard ratio [HR], 1.20; 95% CI, 1.00-1.45) and renal cyst presence (HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.31-1.64) as independent risk factors, whereas diabetes mellitus (HR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.54-0.77) and high physical activity (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.81-0.97) appeared protective.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the prevalence of 8.54%, incidence, and risk factors of hepatic cysts. Renal cyst presence and HBs-Ag positivity are significant risk factors, whereas high physical activity and diabetic status are protective.

articles.title: Imaging-Enhanced Prediction of Upper Limb Motor Function After Stroke Using Automated Segmentation and Cluster Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, and early prediction of motor outcomes is critical for guiding individualized rehabilitation strategies. Although neuroimaging offers prognostic insights, its clinical integration remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether explainable imaging-derived features can improve the prediction of upper limb motor impairment and to identify distinct recovery profiles through cluster analysis.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 242 patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and motor function assessment. Clinical and imaging variables-including infarct volume, motor tract involvement, and subtype classification-were extracted using automated software. Predictive models for Fugl-Meyer Assessment upper extremity (FMA-UE) scores were developed using hierarchical regression, and K-means clustering was applied to standardized baseline data. Cluster characteristics were compared, and recovery profiles were visualized.

RESULTS: Incorporating imaging variables improved prediction of FMA-UE scores (adjusted R²: 0.595), with motor tract lesion volume emerging as a key predictor. Cluster analysis revealed three distinct patient subgroups: Cluster 1 (mild impairments, younger age), Cluster 2 (older patients with multiple comorbidities), and Cluster 3 (severe neurological deficits, large infarcts). Functional outcomes differed significantly across clusters, with Cluster 3 showing the greatest disability (76% with follow-up modified Rankin Scale 4-6, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Imaging-derived features from early magnetic resonance imaging improve the prediction of upper limb motor outcomes after stroke. Cluster-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups, supporting precision rehabilitation through personalized care planning and targeted secondary prevention.

articles.title: Predicting Major Amputation Rates in Diabetic Hindfoot Ulcers With Critical Infection and Ischemia: A Risk-Factor-Based Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic hindfoot ulcers pose a substantially greater risk of progressing to major amputation than forefoot or midfoot ulcers. Patients with these ulcers often experience severe psychological distress at the prospect of major limb loss. Consequently, patients, their families, and healthcare professionals prioritize understanding the actual risk of major amputation based on the patient's current clinical status. However, practical tools addressing this critical and common concern remain limited. In a previous preliminary study, we proposed a model for predicting major amputation rates in diabetic hindfoot ulcers. Nonetheless, that model, which relied solely on ischemia and infection, demonstrated limited accuracy. The present study aimed to refine the prediction of major amputation in diabetic hindfoot ulcers by 1) identifying additional risk factors and 2) evaluating amputation rates according to these factors.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted involving 1,663 hospitalized patients diagnosed with diabetic foot ulcers. From this group, 50 patients with hindfoot ulcers presenting with critical ischemia and infection were included. A total of 88 baseline clinical and laboratory parameters were evaluated to determine key risk factors.

RESULTS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) ≥ stage 3, hemoglobin < 10.35 g/dL, and albumin < 3.75 g/dL emerged as independent predictors of major amputation (P < 0.05). Univariable logistic regression demonstrated a strong positive correlation between the number of identified risk factors and the rate of major amputation. Patients without these three risk factors did not undergo major amputation, even in the presence of critical infection and ischemia. Conversely, amputation risk increased to 6% for individuals with one risk factor, 27% for those with two, and 67% for patients with all three (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: CKD, low serum hemoglobin, and low serum albumin were identified as significant risk factors for major amputation in patients with diabetic hindfoot ulcers complicated by critical infection and ischemia. The risk of major amputation increases substantially with the presence of multiple risk factors, from 6% amputation rate with one factor to 67% with three factors. Nevertheless, prospective studies with larger sample sizes are warranted to validate this risk-factor model.

articles.title: Intensivists' Perspectives and Practices on Palliative Care in the ICU: A Nationwide Survey in Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While many countries have made progress in integrating palliative care into intensive care units (ICUs), implementation remains highly context-dependent. In Korea, palliative care integration within ICUs remains limited, and intensivists' perspectives on its role and applicability have not been well studied.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, cross-sectional online survey of certified intensivists and fellows registered with the Korean Society of Critical Care Medicine between April and May 2024. The questionnaire explored knowledge and confidence in palliative care, current ICU practices, referral patterns, perceived barriers, and preferred strategies for integration.

RESULTS: A total of 241 intensivists responded (response rate, 23.9%). Most agreed that palliative care should be incorporated into ICU care (97.1%) and were willing to make referrals (98.3%). Advance care planning, symptom management, and family decision-making were the most expected domains of support. However, fewer reported involvement in psychological support, end-of-life care, or bereavement services. Referral practices were more frequent in institutions with palliative care teams, while lack of resources, unsupportive institutional culture, and unclear processes were commonly cited barriers. Clinical guidelines, professional education, and reimbursement reform were identified as priority strategies for integration.

CONCLUSION: Korean intensivists widely recognize the need for palliative care in the ICU but apply it within a limited scope. To strengthen integration, consensus on definitions, clear referral criteria, and supportive institutional and policy frameworks are required.

articles.title: Association of continuous glucose monitoring metrics with cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in type 2 diabetes: Data from the GRADE-CGM substudy.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We compared associations of CGM-derived time in range (TIR) and glucose management indicator (GMI) vs. HbA1c with CVD and eGFR decline in type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: We studied 1363 participants with ≥10-day blinded CGM in the GRADE-CGM Substudy. Exposures were TIR and GMI, with HbA1c as comparator. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HR) for the composite of any CVD or all-cause death. Linear mixed-effects models estimated eGFR slope. Models were adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, treatment group, diabetes duration, and baseline eGFR, then mutually adjusted each CGM metric with HbA1c.

RESULTS: Over median 2.3 years, 74 CVD or death occurred, eGFR slope was -2.37 mL/min/1.73m2/year. GMI, HbA1c, and TIR were each significantly associated with CVD/death (adjusted HR 1.44 [1.21-1.71] per 1% GMI; 1.37 [1.16-1.61] per 1% HbA1c; 0.73 [0.61-0.87] per 20% TIR). Higher GMI and HbA1c were associated with faster eGFR decline (-0.35 [-0.63, -0.07] and - 0.38 [-0.65, -0.11] mL/min/1.73m2/year); TIR was not significantly associated with eGFR slope. After mutual adjustment, most associations of CGM metrics and HbA1c with outcomes were attenuated.

CONCLUSIONS: In type 2 diabetes, GMI and HbA1c were comparably associated with cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, whereas TIR was associated with cardiovascular outcomes only.

articles.title: Structured communication interventions for families of patients in the intensive care unit: A scoping review.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to map structured communication interventions for families or surrogate decision-makers of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients, describe their main characteristics and reported outcomes, and organise reported intervention components into a descriptive communication-domain map.

REVIEW METHOD USED: A scoping review using descriptive evidence mapping and a combined deductive-inductive synthesis of communication domains.

DATA SOURCES: Sources of evidence included PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), LILACS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and reference list screening.

REVIEW METHODS: Eligibility criteria included primary studies reporting structured communication protocols, frameworks, checklists, bundles, tools, or reproductible interventions implemented by ICU clinical teams to support communication with families or surrogate decision-makers of adult ICU patients. Two reviewers independently extracted study and intervention characteristics, outcomes, measurement approaches, and quantitative findings, and reported limitations using a standardised form. Reported intervention components were charted and organised into descriptive communication domains through a combined deductive-inductive synthesis process; disagreements were resolved by consensus.

RESULTS: Nine studies (2010-2022) were included and grouped into structured communication frameworks, educational/training interventions, and multicomponent bundles. Reported communication components were unevenly represented across included sources. Empathy/emotional support, knowledge transmission, summarisation, and value elicitation were among the most frequently described components, whereas ethical considerations, cultural adaptation, time management, nonverbal communication, and supportive aids were less frequently reported in published intervention descriptions. Outcomes were predominantly perceptual and process related.

CONCLUSIONS: Structured ICU family communication interventions are heterogeneous in design, delivery, and outcome assessment. This review provides an evidence map of intervention types and a descriptive-domain map of reported communication components. These findings may support the development and reporting of more comprehensive, context-sensitive ICU family communication interventions.

articles.title: Contemporary outcomes after 100 consecutive HeartMate 3 LVAD implantations: a single-centre cohort study from a Swiss tertiary centre.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The HeartMate 3 left ventricular assist device (LVAD) is an established therapy for advanced heart failure, yet contemporary real-world data from low- or medium-volume centres remain limited. We aimed to describe the characteristics, management and clinical outcomes of patients undergoing HeartMate 3 LVAD implantation at a Swiss tertiary centre.

METHODS: We conducted an observational study including consecutive adult patients who underwent HeartMate 3 implantation at Lausanne University Hospital between November 2015 and January 2026. Baseline characteristics, INTERMACS profiles, perioperative data, survival and LVAD-related complications were assessed. The primary outcome was survival on LVAD support. Comparisons by LVAD indication were pre-specified exploratory analyses (destination therapy vs bridge-to-transplant). Survival analyses on LVAD support, with heart transplantation or LVAD explantation treated as censoring events, were reported.

RESULTS: A total of 100 patients (mean age 58 [standard deviation 12] years, 84% male, 29% destination therapy) underwent HeartMate 3 implantation. Ischaemic heart disease was the predominant aetiology (69%) and most patients (68%) were classified as INTERMACS profiles 3-4 at implantation. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 (IQR 0.5-3) years, 27 patients died on LVAD support, corresponding to a mortality incidence rate (IR) of 13.5 deaths per 100 patient-years, while 51 patients underwent heart transplantation, corresponding to an IR of transplantation of 25.4 per 100 patient-years. Five-year survival on LVAD support was 64%, with patients censored at LVAD explantation for recovery or transplantation. LVAD-related complications included bleeding (48%), infection (50%), ischaemic stroke (12%) and right ventricular failure (39%). Survival did not differ by LVAD indication (bridge-to-transplant as reference, adjusted HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.14-2.72).

CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary, real-world, medium-sized cohort, HeartMate 3 therapy provided durable long-term support across a broad spectrum of advanced heart failure patients, with outcomes consistent with those reported in large multicentre registries.

articles.title: Percutaneous Retrieval of a Fractured Catheter Migrated via a Patent Foramen Ovale With High-Risk Morphology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A fractured central venous port catheter can rarely migrate into the left heart via a patent foramen ovale (PFO).

CASE SUMMARY: A man in his 70s presented with a fractured central venous port catheter. Electrocardiogram-gated contrast-enhanced computed tomography confirmed that the fragment straddled from the right ventricular apex, through a PFO, into the right upper pulmonary vein. Because direct snaring of the ends was considered difficult, percutaneous retrieval was performed under transesophageal echocardiography guidance using the wire-loop technique. The catheter was dragged into the inferior vena cava and successfully retrieved into a 16-F sheath.

DISCUSSION: In a situation where direct snaring was anatomically difficult, we successfully retrieved the fractured catheter with the wire-loop technique. Detailed preprocedural multimodality imaging of the PFO crossing significantly contributed to successful retrieval.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In patients with a PFO, a fractured catheter can migrate into the left heart. Preprocedural evaluation using multimodality imaging is crucial for safe retrieval.

articles.title: An Explainable Prediction Model for Outcomes After Anterior Subcutaneous Ulnar Nerve Transposition in Idiopathic Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify preoperative clinical and electrodiagnostic predictors of outcome after anterior subcutaneous ulnar nerve transposition for idiopathic cubital tunnel syndrome and to develop an explainable model for individualized prognosis.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 119 patients who underwent anterior subcutaneous ulnar nerve transposition for idiopathic cubital tunnel syndrome between 2005 and 2022 with at least 1 year of follow-up. Candidate predictors included demographic factors, occupational category score, elbow carrying angle, modified McGowan grade, and electrodiagnostic parameters. Outcomes were graded using Messina's criteria and dichotomized as excellent/good versus fair/poor for prediction modeling. Conventional regression and six machine-learning algorithms were evaluated, with the machine-learning models internally validated using nested stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 50 times. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, F1 score, and Brier score. Interpretation relied on feature importance and local interpretable model-agnostic explanations.

RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients (57.1%) had an excellent/good outcome, whereas 51 patients (42.9%) had a fair/poor outcome. The extremely randomized trees model achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and the lowest Brier score and was selected for model interpretation. Wrist-level compound muscle action potential amplitude and modified McGowan grade were the dominant prognostic features. Exploratory model interpretation supported wrist-level compound muscle action potential amplitude ≥6.6 mV and modified McGowan grade ≤IIA as reference values for an excellent/good outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Wrist-level compound muscle action potential amplitude and preoperative clinical severity were the key predictors of recovery after anterior subcutaneous transposition for idiopathic cubital tunnel syndrome. Among the evaluated algorithms, the extremely randomized trees model achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and the lowest mean Brier score, reinforcing the prognostic importance of these variables. Explainable prediction modeling may support individualized preoperative counseling.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic III.

articles.title: Pediatricians' knowledge and practice styles regarding cow milk protein allergy among Arab countries.
articles.journal: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cow's milk protein allergy (CMPA) affects 2-6% of children, with peak prevalence in the first year of life. Despite published guidelines, significant gaps remain in awareness and practice among healthcare providers. The aim of this study was to evaluate pediatricians' knowledge and practice styles (KPS) among pediatric care providers (PCPs) working in different Arab countries regarding their diagnosis and treatment approach to CMPA.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional multinational survey in eight Arab countries including Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Lebanon, Oman, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, and Kuwait. The following PCPs: pediatric specialists (PSs), pediatric residents (PRs), pediatric consultants (PCs), pediatric gastroenterologists (PGs), pediatric immunologists (PIs), general physicians (GPs), and family doctors (FDs) were included in this study. The survey was anonymous, and participants provided input on the diagnosis and management of CMPA.

RESULTS: Of the 3000 questionnaires distributed to PCPs, 2145 (response rate 72%) were completed and analyzed. The majority of the respondents were male (n = 1255; 58.5%). The majority of participants were PSs (48%). Regarding the methods to diagnose CMPA, pediatricians and non-pediatricians used clinical diagnosis (61.4%), oral elimination challenge test (27.6%), specific IgE for cow's milk (8.6%) and skin prick test (1.2%) for diagnosis of CMPA ( P < 0.001). Furthermore, pediatricians used "clinical diagnosis" method to confirm CMPA significantly more than other non- pediatricians (87% vs 13%, respectively; P < 0.001). In terms of management of CMPA in breastfed infants, 67.8% reported that continuing breastfeeding with maternal elimination of cow's milk and dairy products was the best treatment approach, with significant differences between pediatricians and non-pediatricians ( P < 0.001). In terms of management of mild-moderate CMPA in formula-fed infants, hydrolyzed formula (eHF) was the most commonly prescribed (53%), while rice-based milk was the formula least often prescribed. eHF was prescribed as a first-line treatment of CMPA significantly more frequently by pediatricians than by non-pediatricians (88.9% vs 11.1%, respectively; P < 0.001). PCPs were more likely to comply (71.1%) with European Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) clinical guidelines for CMPA. PCPs were fully agreed (68.1%) to establish unified CMPA guidelines in Arab countries.

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variability in pediatricians' KPS regarding CMPA across the participating Arab countries was identified. The identification of these gaps highlights the need for policymakers to develop educational materials for PCPs to increase their knowledge of CMPA. Evidence-based guidelines and standardized practice are needed in the Middle East.

articles.title: Electronic Dementia Assessment Score: Screenings and Receipt of Home and Community-Based Services.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With population aging, ensuring that people living with dementia receive appropriate assessment and services is critical. The objective of this study was to determine whether electronic dementia assessment is associated with increased receipt of home-based and community-based services (HCBS) among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of community-dwelling Veterans with heart failure who received an incident dementia diagnosis between 2010 and 2023. Electronic health record (EHR) data were used to identify completion of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments from 365 days before to 90 days after dementia diagnosis. The primary outcome was receipt of HCBS. Logistic regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and health care utilization.

RESULTS: Among 46,157 Veterans with heart failure and incident dementia, 4% had documented cognitive, 82% psychiatric, and 41% functional assessments. Overall, 25% received HCBS. IPTW-adjusted odds of receiving HCBS significantly increased with electronic health record documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments.

CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia, documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments was associated with greater odds of receiving HCBS. Electronic dementia assessment may support system-level efforts to align dementia care with the goals of aging in place.

articles.title: Exploring the design space of SMART RHESINs as a modular nanocapsule platform for functional magnetic nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Magnetic core/shell nanoparticles (CSNPs) are central to emerging imaging and theranostic concepts, yet translating different magnetic payloads into a common, chemically addressable and functionally expandable architecture remains challenging. SMART RHESIN nanocapsules encapsulate different magnetic nanoparticle (NP) systems within a protective phenolic resin shell and permit structural variation and post-synthetic functionalisation. Here we map the design space of SMART RHESIN phenolic resin hollow nanocapsules across 52 reactions varying monomer choice, CSNP type, loading, co-encapsulation, and polymer additives. The platform incorporates magnetic payloads ranging from lab-synthesised magnetite to commercial iron oxides and cubic NPs, while identifying biogenic magnetosomes as a boundary case for the present synthesis conditions, with the resulting nanocapsule diameter (about 100 to 400 nm) and shell thickness (about 10 to 80 nm) varying systematically with the choice of CSNP system and reaction conditions. Magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS) indicates reduced viscosity-induced phase shifts for selected representative formulations from this expanded compositional set, phantom MPI demonstrates multi-colour imaging that resolves aqueous and immobilised SR29 signals within a single field of view, and surface carboxylates enable post-synthetic modification, illustrated by 18F-radiolabelling for PET/CT. These findings establish SMART RHESINs as a versatile nanocapsule platform for integrating magnetic NPs with additional optical, radiochemical and future targeting functionalities.

articles.title: Comparative biochemical analysis of tea (Camellia sinensis) and coffee (Coffea arabica) extracts identifies the ethyl acetate fraction of green tea as a potential dual digestive enzyme inhibitor: an in vitro and in silico study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), have prompted interest in identifying natural products capable of modulating digestive enzymes. This study comparatively evaluated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant activity, and digestive enzyme inhibitory activities of green tea (GT), black tea (BT), and green coffee (GC) extracts. Phytochemical screening, antioxidant assays (DPPH, ABTS, and SOD-like), and quantitative phenolic analysis indicated that GT contained the highest phenolic content and exhibited the greatest antioxidant activity, whereas GC showed the highest alkaloid content. Among the fractionated extracts, the ethyl acetate fraction of green tea (EtOAc fraction of GT) was selected for further investigation based on its phenolic content, pancreatic lipase inhibitory activity, and overall biological profile. HPLC analysis identified ferulic acid and chlorogenic acid as major constituents, together with syringic acid, resveratrol, myricetin, and rosmarinic acid. Both the crude BT extract and EtOAc fraction of GT exhibited α-amylase inhibitory activity comparable to that of quercetin. Kinetic analysis indicated competitive inhibition by the EtOAc fraction of GT (IC50 = 0.662 mg mL-1), whereas BT displayed mixed-type inhibition with a strong uncompetitive component. The EtOAc fraction of GT also showed the lowest IC50 against pancreatic lipase (0.264 mg mL-1) and followed a non-competitive inhibition mechanism. The EtOAc fraction maintained 98.94% of human skin fibroblast viability after 48 h at 500 µg mL-1 in a preliminary cytotoxicity screen. Molecular docking was consistent with the experimental findings, suggesting that hesperidin and rutin may contribute to competitive α-amylase inhibition and allosteric pancreatic lipase modulation. These findings indicate that the ethyl acetate fraction of green tea is a phenolic-rich fraction with dual digestive enzyme inhibitory activity that merits further evaluation in appropriate biological models.

articles.title: Pan-cancer analysis reveals DNAJC9 as an immune-related biomarker and a positive regulator of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Background: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) modulate apoptosis, proliferation, and differentiation, positioning them as potential therapeutic targets in cancer. As a member of the J-domain-containing HSP40 family, DnaJ homolog, subfamily C, member 9 (DNAJC9) has not yet been systematically investigated in a pan-cancer context. Method: Multiple public repositories were employed to perform a comprehensive pan-cancer investigation of DNAJC9. We also utilized single-cell datasets to explore how DNAJC9 expression varies across distinct cellular clusters. These efforts covered several key dimensions, including diagnostic and prognostic value, immune landscape, genomic alterations, methylation differences, and pathway enrichment. To determine its biological effects, DNAJC9 was silenced in lung cancer cell lines, and subsequent experiments assessed cellular phenotypes. The downstream PI3K/AKT signaling cascade was examined via western blotting. Results: Across multiple tumor types, DNAJC9 was markedly upregulated, especially in advanced-stage cases, and higher expression levels predicted worse prognosis. DNAJC9 expression also correlated significantly with immune infiltration, tumor mutation burden (TMB), and microsatellite instability (MSI). Tumor tissues showed substantially lower DNAJC9 methylation than normal tissues. Single-cell analysis detected DNAJC9 expression in multiple immune cell subsets. Knockdown of DNAJC9 in A549 and H1299 lung cancer cells impaired proliferation, migration, and invasion. Functional enrichment analysis then pointed to the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Western blotting further confirmed that silencing DNAJC9 reversed the activated PI3K/AKT cascade in these cells, as shown by decreased p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios. Conclusions: Pan-cancer analyses suggest that DNAJC9 may serve as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker across cancers. Importantly, its role as an upstream PI3K/AKT activator and its functional validation in lung cancer support DNAJC9 as a potential target for anti-cancer drug discovery in this malignancy.

articles.title: NIR-triggered gelatin-based hydrogel for ion-mechanical synergistic antibacterial therapy and infected wound closure.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infection and impaired wound closure remain the leading causes of refractory cutaneous wound healing disorders, inflicting substantial global morbidity and mortality while exacerbating the crisis of antibacterial resistance. Infected cutaneous wounds present a persistent clinical difficulty, given that bacterial infection and inadequate wound closure exacerbate one another. Here, we constructed a hydrogel platform that integrates antibacterial activity and active wound closure through ion-mechanical coupling. The system combines thermoresponsive, catechol-functionalized network with core-shell nanoparticles consisting of a metal-organic framework shell (MOF) encapsulating a liquid metal core (LM). Under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the liquid metal generates heat that triggers network contraction to mechanically close the wound. Simultaneously, sustained release of Zn2+ and Ga3+ from the nanoparticles provides continuous, antibiotic free antibacterial activity. In a mouse MRSA infected wound model, this hydrogel achieves complete closure within 14 days with improved tissue regeneration. By integrating ion mediated antibacterial action, photothermal bacterial inactivation, and active mechanical contraction in a single platform, this design addresses the intertwined challenges of infection and impaired closure without the compromises of conventional approaches.

articles.title: Hormone Receptor-Positive HER2-Negative Oligometastatic Breast Cancer: prognostic stratification and pattern of progression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of oligometastatic breast cancer (OMBC) remains controversial, particularly regarding selection for local ablative treatment (LAT). In HR+/HER2- OMBC, where prolonged survival is often the case, improved stratification and characterization of progression may guide treatment. We aimed to define prognostic subsets, assess the contribution of Modern-Imaging-Methods (MIMs; 18F-FDG-PET/CT or WB-MRI) to LAT selection, and describe progression after first-line therapy in these subgroups of patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: All consecutive patients with HR+/HER2- OMBC treated at our institution between 2012 and 2020 were included. OMBC was defined as ≤ 5 metastases. Prognostic factors including biological subtype, anatomical distribution, imaging modality, and LAT were evaluated for overall and progression-free survival (OS, PFS).

RESULTS: Among 145 patients (median follow-up 82.8 months), median OS and PFS were, respectively, 81.1 and 26.5 months. Luminal-A-like subtypes, absence of liver metastases, and use of MIMs independently predicted better survival. LAT improved PFS (hazard ratio [HR]=0.52; 95%CI[0.29-0.91], p=0.0233) and showed a trend toward longer OS. In patients staged with MIMs, LAT significantly improved both OS (HR = 0.29; 95%CI[0.12-0.73], p=0.008) and PFS (HR = 0.40; 95%CI[0.21-0.77], p=0.0064). After first-line systemic therapy, only 18% developed polymetastatic progression.

CONCLUSION: In HR+/HER2- OMBC, three actionable considerations emerge: staging must incorporate modern imaging to accurately define metastatic burden; LAT may be considered in selected patients with low-grade disease, absence of liver metastases, and long disease-free interval; in oligoprogression after first-line therapy, LAT should be re-evaluated within a multidisciplinary setting. These data offer pragmatic benchmarks to individualize treatment while awaiting definitive randomized evidence.

articles.title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma at 11-20 weeks of gestation and gestational diabetes risk: A prospective cohort study in China.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies have linked insulin resistance and the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus to the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP). This integrated lipid marker reflects cardiovascular risk and atherogenic dyslipidemia. However, its relationship with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is not completely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the association between AIP measured at 11-20 weeks of gestation and the subsequent risk of GDM and to identify the optimal AIP threshold for GDM prediction.

METHODS: A total of 2068 women with singleton pregnancies were included in this prospective cohort study from the Tongji Maternal and Child Health Cohort. AIP was calculated from fasting triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) measurements obtained at 11-20 weeks of gestation, before GDM diagnosis by 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analysis, restricted cubic spline models, and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess the relationship between GDM and AIP. The predictive performance of AIP alone and in combination with maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) was compared via receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.

RESULTS: Gestational diabetes mellitus was diagnosed in 252 participants (12.3%). Women in the highest AIP quartile demonstrated a substantially higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (adjusted odds ratio 2.56; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.63-4.01; P < 0.001), and higher AIP levels were associated with a progressively higher risk of GDM. AIP and GDM risk were found to be significantly positively correlated (P for overall association <0.001), with no statistically significant evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.700), as assessed by restricted cubic spline analysis. Based on the maximum Youden index, an AIP value equal to 0.091 was determined to be the ideal cut-off for GDM prediction. A multivariable model incorporating AIP, pre-pregnancy BMI, maternal age, and LDL-C showed improved discriminative ability compared with AIP alone (area under the curve 0.69; 95% CI 0.66-0.73).

CONCLUSION: Elevated AIP levels at 11-20 weeks of gestation were independently associated with an increased risk of GDM. Importantly, the inclusion of AIP alongside established maternal risk factors enhanced predictive accuracy. The findings of this study indicate that AIP might serve as a useful adjunctive biomarker in early antenatal screening to identify women at heightened risk for GDM.

articles.title: Early and Late Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery in Patients With Immune-Mediated Inflammatory Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but surgical outcomes in the modern era of immunosuppressive therapy remain unclear. We evaluated early and late outcomes after cardiac and thoracic aortic surgery in patients with IMIDs, focusing on the impact of glucocorticoids and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

METHODS: A total of 140 patients with IMIDs who underwent cardiac or thoracic aortic surgery between 2008 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality and long-term overall survival.

RESULTS: Median age was 70 [61-76] years, and 62% were women. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common IMID (36%). Prednisolone and DMARDs were used in 68% and 33% of patients, respectively. Procedures included valve (43%), ischemic (26%), and thoracic aortic surgery (23%). In-hospital mortality was 4.3%. During a median follow-up of 5.9 years (93% completeness), overall survival was 91% at 1 year, 87% at 3 years, 78% at 5 years, and 62% at 10 years, respectively. Outcomes did not differ by a surgical category or IMID subtype. Glucocorticoid use was independently associated with worse late survival (HR, 2.91; 95% CI, 1.01-8.41; p = 0.048), whereas DMARD use showed a trend toward improved survival (HR 0.46; 95% CI, 0.19-1.09; p = 0.08). Notably, a dose-dependent relationship was observed, with high-dose prednisolone (≥ 5 mg/day) showing significantly worse survival compared with low-dose (< 5 mg/day) or no glucocorticoid use (p = 0.004). Diabetes mellitus and preoperative anemia were also independent predictors of late mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac surgery in patients with IMIDs provides acceptable early outcomes but suboptimal long-term survival. Glucocorticoid use was associated with worse late survival, with a dose-dependent relationship, whereas DMARD use showed a nonsignificant trend toward better survival, underscoring the importance of optimized immunosuppressive management.

articles.title: Early Changes in Left Atrial Mechanics During Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional echocardiographic improvements after sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy have been reported in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but data on novel composite indices of atrial mechanics, particularly the left atrial (LA) stiffness index and the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI), remain poorly characterized. The authors evaluated early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and atrial mechanics following initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center observational cohort study, patients with HFpEF in sinus rhythm who were naive to SGLT2 inhibitors received empagliflozin or dapagliflozin. Clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and comprehensive echocardiography were performed at baseline and after 3 months. Echocardiographic evaluation included LA reservoir and pump strain, the LA stiffness index (E/e'/LA reservoir strain), and LACI (minimum LA volume/LV end-diastolic volume ×100).

RESULTS: Fifty patients completed follow-up (70% women; mean age, 63.9 ± 8.1 years). New York Health Association functional class improved and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels decreased significantly (347 [134.8-524.8] vs. 257 [161.3-427.5] pg/mL; P = .007). Left atrial volume index and E/e' decreased significantly (34.6 ± 5.5 to 32.6 ± 5.7 mL/m2 and 12.1 ± 3.2 to 9.8 ± 2.8, respectively; both P < .001). Left atrial reservoir and pump strain increased, whereas the LA stiffness index and LACI decreased significantly (all P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective observational cohort of patients with HFpEF, initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and LA mechanics. Composite atrial indices, particularly the LA stiffness index and LACI, changed in parallel with established clinical and echocardiographic markers, suggesting that they may provide complementary information for monitoring early atrial remodeling during SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

articles.title: Heart Failure Risk Phenotypes Based on a 2-Dimensional Tree Structure Derived from Clinical Characteristics and Associations with Disease Prevalence and Cardiovascular Mortality in the General Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Using the Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction Tree (DDRTree) algorithm, a 2-dimensional tree model was constructed based on conventional clinical indicators to identify heart failure (HF) risk phenotypes with different pathophysiological characteristics from the general adult population and evaluate their association with HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk.

METHODS: A representative sample of 24 205 general US adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018 was analyzed. Eleven routine clinical indicators from multiple physiological dimensions were fed into the DDRTree algorithm to project each of them in a 2-dimensional space. The resulting tree structure revealed distinct HF risk phenotypes whose links to outcome HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk were quantified with weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional-hazard models.

RESULTS: Discriminant Dimensionality Reduction Tree identified 3 HF risk phenotypes: normal, metabolic (characterized by upregulated glucose-metabolism markers), and inflammatory (characterized by abnormalities in inflammatory and hepatic-renal markers). After fully adjusting for confounding factors, the metabolic phenotype was significantly associated with the risk of HF compared with the normal phenotype (odds ratio [OR] = 1.96, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.47-2.62), whereas it showed no significant correlation with the risk of cardiovascular death (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.92, P = .539, 95% CI: 0.70-1.20). In contrast, the inflammatory phenotype was significantly correlated with both HF risk (OR = 3.95, P < .001, 95% CI: 2.94-5.33) and cardiovascular mortality risk (HR = 1.47, P = .002, 95% CI: 1.16-1.87).

CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates potential risk phenotypes influencing HF and cardiovascular mortality, providing new insights for precise HF risk stratification and targeted preventive interventions in the general population.

articles.title: Effects of ChatGPT Use on Self-care Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify the possible effects of ChatGPT use on self-care cardiac rehabilitation (CR) adherence in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD).

METHOD: Patients in the ChatGPT group participated in a standard cardiac rehabilitation program supplemented with personalized digital support via ChatGPT (n=48). The control group participated in conventional cardiac rehabilitation only, without AI-based support (n=48). Both groups completed a 6-month structured rehabilitation program supervised by a multidisciplinary team. Baseline demographic and clinical data, patient satisfaction assessed using a Likert scale, physical activity levels assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and metabolic equivalent of task (MET) values were recorded.

RESULTS: The postrehabilitation MET score was 1537 in the ChatGPT group and 1413 in the control group (P = 0.001). Similarly, the change in MET score after rehabilitation was greater in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (1029 vs. 875, P = 0.001). SF-36 parameters, including physical functioning, role-physical, mental health, bodily pain, and general health, were significantly higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (P < 0.05 for all). Program compliance was higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (91.7% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.028). Patient satisfaction was also higher in the ChatGPT group (4.5 vs. 3.8, P = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: ChatGPT use during CR was associated with higher patient compliance rates. Moreover, ChatGPT-supported CR was associated with higher physical activity levels, greater patient satisfaction, and better selected quality-of-life scores.

articles.title: The Evolution of Anesthesia for Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: This educational review describes the historical development of pediatric congenital cardiac anesthesia and its expanding role in the care of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Over the past eight decades, the specialty has evolved from an era in which few congenital heart defects were surgically treatable and perioperative mortality was high to one in which survival into adulthood is expected for most children with CHD. This transformation has been driven by parallel advances in surgical techniques, cardiopulmonary bypass technology, myocardial protection, monitoring, intensive care, and anesthetic management. From the first successful patent ductus arteriosus ligation in 1938 to the development of fetal cardiac interventions and the many major technological and scientific advances of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, anesthesiologists have played a pivotal role in improving the care of patients with CHD. As survival has improved, the population of adults and elderly patients living with repaired or palliated CHD has grown, and the specialty's focus has expanded beyond reducing perioperative mortality to improving lifelong outcomes. Today, congenital cardiac anesthesiologists are integral members of multidisciplinary teams responsible for perioperative risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, neuroprotection, coagulation management, mechanical circulatory support, and enhanced recovery. The history of the specialty highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continued scientific progress in improving patient safety, recovery, and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Expanding Patient Choice in Diabetes Care: Reducing Access Barriers to Inhaled Insulin.
articles.abstract: Inhaled insulin provides a unique prandial insulin option, offering an alternative, with a more rapid onset of effect, to subcutaneous rapid-acting analog insulin. Clinical studies with inhaled insulin have demonstrated its efficacy and safety, with glycemic outcomes comparable to or in some cases better than those of contemporary insulin delivery approaches. However, the use of inhaled insulin for diabetes therapy in daily life remains limited due to payer restrictions, prior authorization requirements, formulary exclusions, clinician knowledge gaps, clinician time constraints, persistent misconceptions regarding safety, and inadequate patient awareness. A panel of clinical experts in diabetes management met in June 2026 to review the safety and efficacy of Technosphere® inhaled (TI) insulin, discuss the current obstacles that limit access for people with diabetes (PwD) to TI, identify practical strategies to overcome these obstacles, and issue a call-to-action for payers, clinicians, policymakers, professional organizations, and patient advocacy groups. This article summarizes those discussions and proposes strategies to increase access and choice for PwD.

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Selective Versus Nonselective Beta-Blockers Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Receiving Sacubitril/Valsartan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers, selective (metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol) and nonselective (carvedilol), and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) are the first-line guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Concomitant use of carvedilol and ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) may result in additive vasodilatory effects, which may increase the risk of hypotension and limit dose titration of sacubitril/valsartan.

OBJECTIVE: This study examines differences in clinical endpoints between selective and nonselective beta-blocker therapy among patients with HFrEF receiving sacubitril/valsartan.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized TriNetX Research Collaborative real-world data. Patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan concomitantly with carvedilol were identified as the intervention cohort, while those receiving metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol served as controls. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause hospitalization during the 3-year follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced confounders. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to estimate event-free survival, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models for time-to-event outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings.

RESULTS: Overall, 75 230 patients received carvedilol and 21 587 received metoprolol/bisoprolol. After PSM, 20 939 patients were included in each group. Carvedilol was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint compared with those taking metoprolol or bisoprolol (52.32% vs 46.29%; HR: 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.24; P < .0001). Carvedilol was also linked to increased hospitalization risk (HR: 1.32; 95% CI, 1.28-1.36; P < .0001) but a modest reduction in mortality (HR: 0.92; 95% CI, 0.87-0.97; P = .0011). In addition, carvedilol was associated with higher risks of hypotension, end-stage renal disease, and bradycardia. Sensitivity analysis results were consistent for the primary endpoint.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Our results suggest that carvedilol may be associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint, health care utilization, and adverse events but lower all-cause mortality compared with metoprolol or bisoprolol in patients with HFrEF taking sacubitril/valsartan.

articles.title: Effect of individual and group-based dietitian-delivered education interventions on outcomes for people with chronic kidney disease stages 3a-5: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Nutrition & dietetics : the journal of the Dietitians Association of Australia
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This review aimed to determine the effectiveness of dietitian-delivered nutrition education for people with chronic kidney disease stages 3a-5.

METHODS: Four databases were searched up to July 2025. Randomised controlled trials evaluating the effect of dietitian-delivered nutrition education compared to standard care on outcomes [primary: estimated glomerular filtration rate; secondary: blood pressure, body mass index, quality of life, dietary adherence and acceptability] for people with chronic kidney disease stages 3a-5 were included. Meta-analyses were performed by pooling post-intervention data using random-effects models and inverse variance methods to determine the pooled mean difference or standardised mean difference and 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Eight trials (n = 1204 participants) were included. There was low certainty evidence from five trials (n = 462 participants) that dietitian-delivered nutrition education may result in little to no difference in estimated glomerular filtration rate and body mass index, but large improvements in quality of life compared to usual care (standardised mean differences 0.99, 95% CI -0.31 to 2.29). There was high certainty evidence from 4 trials (n = 398) that dietitian-delivered education reduced diastolic blood pressure by 4.01 mmHg (95% CI -6.13 to -1.90) and systolic blood pressure by 6.23 mmHg (95% CI -9.24 to -3.23). Exploratory sub-group analyses suggest no differences in individual versus group interventions.

CONCLUSION: Dietitian-delivered education interventions delivered individually or in groups reduced blood pressure and may improve quality of life but had no impact on estimated glomerular filtration rate or body mass index for people with chronic kidney disease stages 3a-5.

articles.title: A Bayesian framework for a sudden unexpected death in epilepsy risk-reduction indication.
Premature treatment cessation in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia due to excessive toxicity: clinical experiences and patient outcomes - a case series.
articles.abstract: Although survival in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has improved over the past decades, intensive chemotherapy may be associated with severe and life-threatening toxicities. This case series describes pediatric AML patients in whom therapy was discontinued due to excessive toxicity. Patients were identified through a national database of two consecutive AML treatment protocols in the Netherlands (2010-2023). Seven patients were included; discontinuation of treatment was because of a severe fungal infection in five out of seven cases.
