Five out of seven patients had a favorable genetic profile; four harboring RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and one with a CEBPA-bZIP mutation. All seven patients remain in continuous complete remission with a median follow-up of 6,7 years. This case series shows that selected children with AML who discontinue chemotherapy early due to treatment-related toxicity may still achieve long-term survival and possibly cure. The high incidence of invasive fungal infections highlights a critical cause of treatment-limiting toxicity. This series could inform clinical practice in future similar cases.

articles.title: Clinical and Longitudinal Heterogeneity Within the Acute Outer Retinopathy Spectrum: A Three-Case Series.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe three distinct presentations within the acute outer retinopathy (AOR) spectrum, emphasizing differences in stage, longitudinal evolution, and structure-function relationships.

METHODS: Retrospective case series.

RESULTS: The first, a 14-year-old asymptomatic male, had bilateral sectoral and spot-like outer retinal lesions in the subacute-chronic stage. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated outer nuclear layer thinning with ellipsoid and interdigitation zone disruption and focal retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) attenuation, without the angular sign of Henle fiber layer hyperreflectivity (ASHH). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) revealed lesions with a hypoautofluorescent core and hyperautofluorescent border, while fluorescein angiography (FA) showed window-defect hyperfluorescence and focal venular wall staining. The second, a 20-year-old male, developed severe visual field loss after a viral illness. FAF showed perivenular outer retinal involvement, and OCT revealed perivenular disruption with ASHH documented at 11 months. Visual field deficits were severe and partially correlated with structural abnormalities, with incomplete recovery over 3 years. Pattern electroretinography showed borderline reduction, whereas full-field electroretinography was within the lower limits of normal. The third, a 43-year-old female, presented with acute visual symptoms and mild intraocular inflammation. FAF showed sectoral peripapillary hyperautofluorescence, with corresponding outer retinal disruption on OCT. FA demonstrated venular wall staining and optic disc hyperfluorescence without diffuse vascular leakage. Perimetry showed bilateral diffuse sensitivity loss, while electrophysiology demonstrated generalized cone-predominant photoreceptor dysfunction.

CONCLUSION: These cases illustrate clinical and longitudinal heterogeneity within established AOR patterns, including asymptomatic subacute-chronic disease, perivenular disease with structure-function dissociation and late documentation of ASHH, and symptomatic sectoral disease with diffuse photoreceptor dysfunction.

articles.title: Pre-Surgical Diabetes Education Program Increased Preparedness for Diabetes Management after Total Pancreatectomy with Islet Autotransplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation (TPIAT) requires families to manage diabetes with insulin pumps and continuous glucose monitors postoperatively at our institution. Education occurs while the child is hospitalized after TPIAT, and one parent or caregiver receives all education. Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) must be effective, efficient, and completed with enough time for families to practice before discharge. We created a pre-TPIAT diabetes education program aimed at reducing subsequent inpatient education time and increasing the primary learner's preparedness for inpatient education.

METHODS: Thirty-three pediatric TPIAT recipients at Cincinnati Children's received presurgery education across three cycles of improvement. Data were extracted from clinical records and survey responses collected. Cohorts were well-balanced demographically (all P > 0.05, small effect sizes). Survey data, including paired knowledge assessments, were collected from Cohorts 2 and 3.

RESULTS: TPIAT recipients were predominantly White (87.9%), English speaking, non-Hispanic (97.0%), with balanced sex distribution (48.5% female). Mean age at surgery was 12.2 years. Parents were primary learners in 87.9% of cases. Presurgery education time showed highly statistically significant increases in Cohorts 2 and 3 compared with Cohort 1 (P = 0.0291 and P = 0.0007, respectively). Inpatient diabetes education showed a marginally significant decrease of 133 min from Cohort 1 to Cohort 2 (P = 0.0717) and directionally maintained in Cohort 3 (0.3285). Assessment results documented substantial knowledge acquisition from the intervention that was retained from pre- to postsurgery education. Learner confidence increased postintervention (P = 0.063), and overall satisfaction scores remained high except for stress/anxiety scores.

CONCLUSION: Changes in TPIAT diabetes education delivery effectively transferred some education to presurgery without compromising content, demonstrated by a statistically significant increase in presurgery education, knowledge scores that indicated retention of information, alongside numerically lower (nonsignificant) total inpatient education time after interventions.

articles.title: First seizure referral clinics or first seizure units in neurology: How long is too long?
Heart Failure Medication Discontinuation Among Hospice Patients with Concomitant Heart Failure and Dementia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) frequently co-occur, complicating medication management at the end of life.

METHODS: This secondary analysis included 1338 patients with HF and AD/ADRD across 12 hospices. HF was classified as a primary (n = 210) or secondary (n = 1128). HF-related medication use and discontinuation at hospice admission were characterized and compared by diagnosis primacy.

RESULTS: Prehospice use was highest for beta-blockers (44.0%), loop diuretics (32.4%), and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors (17.7%). Among patients with documented use, discontinuation was 91.2%-100% across medication classes, including beta-blockers (97.5%), loop diuretics (97.0%), and RAAS inhibitors (94.1%). Discontinuation did not differ by HF diagnostic primacy.

CONCLUSIONS: HF-related medication discontinuation was common at hospice admission among patients with HF and AD/ADRD, regardless of HF diagnostic primacy. Further research is needed to understand the clinical rationale and symptom outcomes associated with medication discontinuation in hospice.

articles.title: Navigating the translational chasm: a scoping review of large language models and hybrid architectures in intensive care.
articles.abstract: Foundation models, particularly large language models, can process the unstructured data central to the intensive care record, yet their clinical readiness remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map foundation-model and large language model applications in adult intensive care, characterise their architectural paradigms, and chart their validation and deployment features. Empirical studies applying a large language model or other foundation model to adult intensive care tasks were eligible for inclusion. Traditional machine-learning-only, non-intensive care, and paediatric studies were excluded. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched (January 2022-February 2026). A supplementary preprint and conference search through mid-2026 was analysed separately. Data were extracted in duplicate using an operationalised taxonomy (generative large language models, clinical language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and hybrid pipelines). Evidence-maturity mapping was performed without formal risk-of-bias appraisal. Sixty-four studies addressed decision support (51.6%), clinical NLP (23.4%), predictive analytics (20.3%), and ICU operations (4.7%). Standalone configurations predominated (79.7%); retrieval-augmented generation (6.3%) and hybrid (14.1%) architectures concentrated in higher-stakes tasks. Maturity was limited: 46.9% relied solely on retrospective MIMIC data, 6.3% reported external validation, 90.6% remained internally retrospective, and only 3.1% achieved prospective evaluation. Hybrid and retrieval-augmented architectures appear better aligned with high-risk ICU tasks, though no comparative synthesis was performed. Prospective validation and a risk-stratified 'clinical co-pilot' framework are needed.

articles.title: Association Between Oral Health Status at Admission and Length of Hospital Stay in the Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study (2024-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor oral health is linked to prolonged hospitalization, but critical care data from Latin America remain virtually absent. This study characterized baseline oral health at intensive care unit (ICU) admission in a Chilean center and evaluated its association with ICU length of stay (LOS).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including first-admission adults (n = 105). Bedside clinical examinations at admission assessed the WHO Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index, gingival inflammation, and salivary hypofunction. Adjusted associations with ICU LOS were evaluated using multivariable ordinary least squares (OLS) regression.

RESULTS: At admission, gingival inflammation and salivary hypofunction were each present in 90.5% of patients. The mean DMFT was 8.87 ± 9.40. In multivariable analysis, the DMFT index was not associated with ICU LOS (β = -0.050, 95% CI [-0.187, 0.087], p = 0.477). Mechanical ventilation status emerged as the sole independent predictor of prolonged stay (β = 3.30 days, 95% CI [0.75, 5.85], p = 0.013). Results were robust across five sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite a remarkably high baseline burden of oral disease at ICU admission, chronic caries experience was not independently associated with ICU LOS, which was driven primarily by ventilatory support.

articles.title: The Association Between Oral Lichen Planus and Diabetes Mellitus: A Scoping Review of the Evidence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated oral potentially malignant disorder. Three prior meta-analyses reported elevated diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence in patients with OLP, but the evidence base has since expanded. This scoping review synthesised all available evidence on the OLP-DM association up to November 2025.

STUDY DESIGN: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to November 30, 2025 with no lower date limit, supplemented by backward citation searching. No study design restrictions were applied. Findings were synthesised thematically per PRISMA-ScR.

RESULTS: Twenty-one sources from 11 countries were included, encompassing observational studies, Mendelian randomisation analyses, biochemical investigations, reviews, and case reports. DM prevalence in patients with OLP ranged from 9.7% to 24.5%, with the association specific to type 2 DM. Prediabetes was independently associated with OLP after multivariate adjustment. Mendelian randomisation provided causal evidence linking type 1 DM and elevated glycated haemoglobin to increased OLP risk.

CONCLUSIONS: The OLP-DM association is consistent, biologically plausible, and extends to subclinical glycaemic dysregulation. Glycaemic assessment should be considered in patients with OLP presenting with oral or systemic features suggestive of metabolic dysregulation. Future research should prioritise longitudinal studies, intervention trials on glycaemic optimisation.

articles.title: Silence and Sorrow: A Qualitative Exploration of the Hidden Role of Communication Failures in Perinatal Care.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perinatal mortality remains high in low- and middle-income countries, with Tanzania bearing one of the greatest burdens. The Three Delays framework is often used to analyze preventable perinatal deaths and includes care seeking, reaching care, and receiving definitive care. This study explores Tanzanian mothers' experiences of perinatal loss, focusing on delays and gaps in care.

METHODS: This study was conducted at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Center (KCMC) in Moshi, Tanzania. Fifty women who experienced stillbirth or neonatal death completed intake surveys about their perinatal loss experience. Of these, 40 completed semi-structured in-depth interviews 8 weeks post-loss. Interviews explored barriers in care seeking, access, delivery, and communication. Survey data were analyzed with descriptive statistics. Interview data were thematically coded using a directed content analysis combining a priori codes from the three delays framework and inductive coding.

RESULTS: Participants perceived delays in seeking care (50%), receiving care at initial facilities (27.5%), referral processes (12.5%), and care at KCMC (17.5%). Nearly half (45%) reported inadequate communication from healthcare providers. Three key themes emerged: (1) women perceived delays in care at all points along their care trajectory (2) gaps in communication impacted medical care for women and newborns, and hindered healing after perinatal loss; and (3) women emphasized the need for emotional support and compassionate communication following loss.

DISCUSSION: While structural, process, and financial barriers persist, informational and relational communication gaps represent an under-addressed challenge across the perinatal loss care pathway. Rather than being viewed in isolation, efforts to strengthen communication should be integrated into broader health system strategies aimed at reducing delays, improving access to timely and quality care, and supporting families after stillbirth or neonatal death. Strengthening communication within health systems, both as an informational and relational process, has the potential to enhance care experiences, build trust, and support emotional healing after perinatal loss.

articles.title: Beyond neuroprotection: Context-dependent effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on seizure susceptibility.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used in type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity and are increasingly considered to exert neuroprotective effects. Recent large-scale clinical and real-world studies report a predominantly neutral to protective association between GLP-1 RA use and seizure- or epilepsy-related diagnoses. However, how these agents affect neuronal excitability in patients with established epileptogenic networks remains insufficiently understood. This narrative review critically examines the experimental and clinical evidence from GLP-1 RA effects on neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility, with a focus on possible discrepancies between population-level outcomes and individual network-level vulnerability. Preclinical studies demonstrate heterogeneous, network-dependent effects of GLP-1 RAs. Although anticonvulsant and neuroprotective properties are observed in chemically induced seizure models, paradoxical pro-seizure effects occur in genetic absence epilepsy models. In contrast, population-level analyses report neutral to reduced rates of incident epilepsy or seizure-related outcomes under GLP-1 RA therapy. However, these findings are based largely on administrative diagnostic codes, lack epileptological phenotyping, and are not designed to capture transient, exposure-dependent alterations in neuronal excitability or short-term seizure dynamics. Additional factors, including delayed gastric emptying affecting anti-seizure medication absorption, rapid metabolic shifts during titration, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and agent-specific pharmacokinetics, may further modulate individual susceptibility. We propose that GLP-1 RA effects on neuronal excitability are context dependent, shaped by epilepsy subtype, network vulnerability, exposure dynamics, and treatment phase. Targeted prospective studies incorporating clinical phenotyping, therapeutic drug monitoring, and temporal seizure assessment are required to ensure neurological safety in patients with epilepsy.

articles.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
articles.abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

articles.title: Emotional experiences of workplace violence in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWorkplace violence is common in intensive care units and is often regarded as an inevitable aspect of the job. This normalisation may obscure the emotional impact of violence on healthcare professionals and the ethical tensions that arise when altruistic caregiving values conflict with personal safety. Therefore, this study was conducted to explore healthcare professionals' emotional experiences of workplace violence within the context of intensive care.Research designThis study constitutes a secondary, inductive analysis of data originally collected in 37 semi-structured interviews. The interviews were conducted between November 2024 and March 2025 in intensive care units across five hospitals in Sweden. Data were interpreted using Reflexive thematic analysis.Ethical considerationsEthical aspects were carefully considered throughout the study in line with established ethical principles. Participation was voluntary, and informed consent was obtained from all individuals before the interview. Data confidentiality was ensured, and all direct quotes were anonymised.FindingsParticipants' descriptions of their emotional experiences generated three themes. A conflict between professional obligation and human vulnerability captured how participants experienced a tension between the expectation to remain composed in their professional roles and their human vulnerability. Balancing core values of caregiving with safety illustrated the professional and moral dilemmas that emerged when violence or escalating aggression forced healthcare professionals to reconcile their commitment to compassionate care. Organisational conditions influencing emotional responses reflected the conditions that either support or undermine ICU healthcare professionals' emotional resilience when they encounter violence.ConclusionsWorkplace violence in intensive care was experienced as more than a threat to personal safety; participants described how it challenged their professional identity and caring values. Organisational conditions influenced how healthcare professionals experienced and managed these challenges.

articles.title: An Exploratory Study on the Onset Age of Child Sexual Abuse: A Comparison of Childhood and Adolescence Onset.
articles.abstract: Research on child sexual abuse has predominantly focused on cases that typically begin in early childhood. By contrast, sexual abuse and boundary violations that first occur during adolescence have received comparatively little attention. This study aims to analyze the similarities and differences in the age of abuse onset in childhood and adolescence, considering victim characteristics and abuse-related factors. The study is based on anonymously collected data from the German Sexual Abuse Telephone Helpline covering the years 2016 to 2024. The sample comprises 1,935 reported cases of sexual abuse that began in childhood or adolescence. The study examined similarities and differences between victims whose abuse began in childhood versus those whose abuse began during adolescence using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression analyses. The age of onset in childhood was significantly more likely to be associated with contact, non-penetrative abuse. By contrast, the age of onset in adolescence was significantly linked to penetrative acts. Childhood-onset abuse cases occurred more often within the family, with fathers and grandfathers being the predominant perpetrators. By contrast, abuse that began in adolescence was significantly associated with non-familial contexts, most commonly involving strangers, sports coaches, and teachers as perpetrators. Adolescents are particularly vulnerable in specific contexts, such as institutional settings. This developmental phase is characterized by growing autonomy, sexual exploration, and spending more time outside the family environment. These factors can make adolescents vulnerable to abuse. Professional fields and society need to raise awareness and learn to recognize and respond to the needs of victims who experienced abuse during adolescence.

articles.title: Long-term temporal trends in hepatitis B and C among blood donors in Brazil: Prevalence, incidence, and demographic correlates from the REDS multicenter program.
authors: NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study‐IV‐Pediatric (REDS‐IV‐P)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viral hepatitis remains a major public health challenge. We evaluated long-term trends in hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, incidence, and force of infection (FOI) among blood donors from five Brazilian blood centers and investigated associated demographic factors.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Data from the NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study program were analyzed. Prevalence was estimated among 2,062,816 first-time donors for HBV (2008-2023) and 1,673,745 for HCV (2012-2023). Incidence was estimated among 1,346,256 repeat donors for HBV and 1,151,209 for HCV. Active HBV infection was defined by reactive HBsAg and anti-HBc or reactive HBV nucleic acid testing (NAT), and active HCV infection by reactive NAT. Historical FOI was estimated using a Bayesian serocatalytic model.

RESULTS: Active infection prevalence was 136.2 per 100,000 donors (95% CI, 131.2-141.3) for HBV and 57.4 (95% CI, 53.8-61.1) for HCV. Incidence rates were 3.54 (95% CI, 3.01-4.11) and 3.99 (95% CI, 3.33-4.72) per 100,000 person-years, respectively. Prevalence decreased annually by 7.6% for HBV and 11.0% for HCV. Higher prevalence and incidence were associated with male sex, older age, lower educational attainment, and Black or mixed-race skin color. Regional differences persisted, and FOI declined markedly for both infections.

DISCUSSION: HBV and HCV prevalence, incidence, and FOI declined substantially among Brazilian blood donors, suggesting reduced transmission, although improved donor selection and screening may also have contributed. Persistent demographic and regional disparities support continued surveillance and targeted prevention.

articles.title: Real-world observational study evaluating metabolic and kidney outcomes in patients living with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus with obesity prescribed tirzepatide.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) accelerate chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. Tirzepatide, a dual glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist, has demonstrated metabolic and potential renoprotective benefits in clinical trials. There have been limited reports of the implications of prescribing tirzepatide in a real-world cohort of patients with advanced CKD.

METHODS: This observational study includes a multi-ethnic cohort of 62 adults with CKD stages 1-5 who initiated tirzepatide indicated for T2DM with concurrent obesity in a general nephrology clinic between June 2024 and October 2025. Patients were followed for a median of 21.4 weeks. Clinical outcomes including weight, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR), blood pressure, lipid profile and insulin requirements were collected.

RESULTS: Tirzepatide significantly reduced median weight (103-100 kg; p < 0.0001), HbA1c (63 [7.9%] to 54 [7.1%] mmol/mol; p = 0.002) and uACR (111-44 mg/mmol; p = 0.008), while eGFR remained stable. Significant improvements were also observed in triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and total daily insulin dose. Gastrointestinal symptoms and decreased serum bicarbonate were the most common adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-ethnic cohort, including patients with advanced CKD, tirzepatide was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in weight, glycaemic control, albuminuria, lipid profile and insulin requirements without adversely affecting kidney function. The introduction of tirzepatide to patients with CKD should be guided by a multidisciplinary team.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation in stroke patients: facts, numbers and current challenges.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading, modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke, with 20-30% of stroke patients harbouring underlying AF. Management of AF, however, differs substantially depending on clinical context. In ischaemic stroke patients with pre-known AF, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the cornerstone of secondary prevention, with initiation timing guided by infarct severity following a risk-adapted approach. In patients with no history of AF, prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring after stroke or transient ischaemic attack improves AF detection rates. However, it remains uncertain whether this translates into a reduced risk of recurrent stroke, with randomised trials such as Find-AF 2 ongoing. Subclinical AF, detected via implantable devices, is associated with an increased stroke risk correlating with arrhythmia burden; recent trials (ARTESiA, NOAH-AFNET 6) suggest that anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic stroke risk in this population, but at the cost of increased bleeding, necessitating individualised decision-making. Particularly challenging are anticoagulation decisions with concomitant cerebral amyloid angiopathy or prior intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) due to competing risks of thromboembolism and haemorrhage. Recent meta-analyses indicate that resuming DOACs after ICH reduces ischaemic events but significantly raises the risk of recurrent haemorrhage, without clear improvement in net clinical benefit. New treatment options, such as left atrial appendage closure, carotid artery filter systems, factor XIa inhibitors or rhythm control, must demonstrate in adequately powered randomised controlled trials that they can optimise treatment outcomes in this complex and growing patient group. This article summarises some common interdisciplinary neurological and cardiological questions and discusses the most recent evidence on AF-related stroke prevention across various patient groups, highlighting the importance of individualised, multidisciplinary, and imaging-informed decision-making.

articles.title: A Two-Stage Plasma Biomarker Algorithm Reduces Amyloid PET Use and the p-Tau217 Gray Zone.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Plasma p-Tau217 leaves 30%-50% of patients in an indeterminate "gray zone" often requiring Aβ-PET. We developed GRAD (Gatekeeper-Reflex for Alzheimer's Disease), a two-stage Aβ-positivity prediction model to improve classification while reserving Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty.

METHODS: GRAD was developed in 145 cognitively impaired ADNI participants and externally validated in 1644 cognitively unimpaired A4/LEARN participants. Stage 1 used p-Tau217 alone; probabilities between 0.25 and 0.75 were considered indeterminate. Stage 2 used L2-regularized logistic regression combining plasma-biomarkers, genetic and demographic features. Aβ-PET served as the reference standard (ADNI florbetapir SUVR > 1.11; A4 Centiloid ≥ 20).

RESULTS: Full model AUC was 0.915 (95% CI, 0.859-0.961) internally and 0.879 (95% CI, 0.861-0.895) externally. In the external gray zone (n = 630), Stage 2 improved discrimination over p-Tau217 alone (AUC 0.793 vs. 0.719; p < 0.001), increased correct classification without PET from 41.4% to 56.2%, and reduced PET referral from 35.9% to 24.3%. In the p-Tau181 subset (n = 256), Stage 2 outperformed p-Tau181 (AUC 0.799 vs. 0.597; p < 0.001). Overall, 89.0% of ADNI and 90.7% of A4/LEARN participants were classified without PET; modeled testing costs were 44%-52% lower than p-Tau217 screening with PET confirmation of the gray zone.

INTERPRETATION: Reflex multimarker testing improves indeterminate p-Tau217 classification while retaining Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty. GRAD may reduce PET use and testing costs in memory-clinic triage, prevention-trial enrichment, and disease-modifying therapy workup.

articles.title: Evaluation of the OPTESK VR training simulator for gastric bleeding treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract is a common and potentially life-threatening emergency that requires rapid and highly precise endoscopic intervention. As supervised hands-on training is limited and often restricted to living animal models, an immersive virtual reality (VR) simulation offers a risk-free and accessible alternative.

METHODS: A novel open-source VR training simulator, OPTESK, was developed for the treatment of upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. The system consists of a combination of conventional endoscopes used in routine clinical practice, which can be operated in conjunction with commercially available head-mounted displays and the in-house developed OPTESK hardware. The simulator covers two scenarios: the treatment of a non-bleeding angiodysplasia with argon plasma coagulation (APC) and the treatment of a bleeding angiodysplasia starting with the injection of adrenaline followed by APC therapy. The simulator was evaluated in a multicenter user study in terms of workload, usability, immersion, cybersickness, and face, content, and construct validity. User performance was assessed via scores on time, amount of treated area, and correctly applied APC intensity.

RESULTS: In total, 44 participants from more than 20 centers were included in the study. Successful hemostatic control in the second scenario was achieved by 97.4% of the participants. Regarding the content validity, participants rated the helpfulness of the simulator for training the management of bleeding with a median of 4 on a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). Mean perceived workload (NASA-TLX) and usability (SUS) were rated with 34.2/100 and 69.6/100 respectively. Face validity questions regarding the realism of endoscope movement, stomach anatomy, and application of APC were further rated with a median of 4 on the scale from 1 to 5. Regarding construct validity, gastroscopy experience showed significantly faster treatment of bleeding related tasks for both scenario one (p = .008) and two (p = .011) compared to participants with less gastroscopy experience.

CONCLUSIONS: OPTESK can serve as a valuable training tool for endoscopic treatment of bleeding in the upper GI tract. This approach may help reduce dependence on animal-based training and enable risk-free practice prior to clinical intervention.

articles.title: Emotion regulation and its association with subjective memory performance among undergraduate students at port said university.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emotion regulation (ER), particularly through cognitive reappraisal (CR) and expressive suppression (ES), plays an important role in psychological well-being and higher-order cognitive functioning. Both ER and subjective memory performance (SMP), as measured by the Prospective and Retrospective Memory Questionnaire (PRMQ), have been proposed to draw on shared executive control resources. Although memory complaints have been reported among Egyptian university students, the association between ER strategies and SMP remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to assess ER strategies and SMP among undergraduate students at Port Said University and examine the association between these constructs.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study with an analytical component was conducted among 1,287 undergraduate students from seven randomly selected faculties at Port Said University. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire comprising the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) to assess CR and ES and the PRMQ to measure SMP. Data were analyzed using Jamovi version 2.3.28 employing descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman's rank correlation, and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: Participants had a median total ERQ score of 44 and a median total PRMQ score of 50. Males reported significantly higher ES and total ER scores than females (p < 0.001 and p = 0.005, respectively), whereas females reported significantly higher PRMQ scores (p < 0.001). Faculty affiliation was significantly associated with both total ERQ and total PRMQ scores, whereas academic grade was associated only with total ERQ scores and family income only with total PRMQ scores. All ERQ subscales were significantly and negatively correlated with PRMQ scores (all p < 0.001). The largest correlation coefficient was observed between total ERQ and total PRMQ scores (ρ = -0.226), indicating a weak inverse association. In multiple linear regression adjusting for sex, faculty, and family income, both CR (B = - 0.272, 95% CI: -0.360 to - 0.184) and ES (B = - 0.270, 95% CI: -0.391 to - 0.150) were independently and inversely associated with PRMQ scores (both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that greater reported use of ER strategies is associated with fewer self-reported memory complaints among undergraduate students. Although the association was statistically significant, its magnitude was weak, indicating that ER represents only one of several factors associated with SMP. This suggests that effective emotional processing may support the cognitive resources required for daily memory tasks.

articles.title: Clinicoepidemiologic Profile of Oral Kaposi Sarcoma in People Living With HIV: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To characterize the clinicoepidemiologic profile of HIV-associated oral Kaposi sarcoma (OKS) and quantitatively synthesize its frequency, anatomical distribution, and temporal patterns across antiretroviral therapy (ART) eras.

METHODS: Six databases and gray literature were searched. Eligible observational, descriptive, and quasi-experimental studies were appraised using JBI tools. Random-effects meta-analyses of patient-based proportions and treatment-era subgroup were performed when compatible study-level denominators were available (PROSPERO: CRD420251105061).

RESULTS: Forty-eight studies comprising 1661 individuals were included, and 31 contributed to at least one meta-analysis. Pooled proportions were 0.85 (95% CI: 0.76-0.91) for palatal involvement and 0.44 (95% CI: 0.23-0.68) for OKS as a sentinel presentation of HIV. Pooled prevalence of OKS among people living with HIV was 0.06 (95% CI: 0.02-0.12). Compared with the pre-combination ART era, the combination ART era showed lower palatal (0.72 vs. 0.89; p = 0.0034) and gingival involvement (0.07 vs. 0.30; p = 0.0003), but more sentinel presentations (0.72 vs. 0.32; p = 0.0195). Methodological quality was moderate, with substantial heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Pooled evidence confirms strong palatal predilection of HIV-associated OKS. Temporal subgroup findings suggest changes in oral distribution across ART eras while reinforcing its persistent role as a sentinel manifestation of HIV infection and persistent clinical relevance despite ART.

articles.title: Needs among persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers: a multi-perspective qualitative study focusing on the potential role of palliative care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore needs among persons with advanced COPD and informal caregivers, and to explore how palliative care can address those needs.

BACKGROUND: COPD is a common, progressive disease affecting lung function and represents a leading cause of death. Advanced COPD is associated with a high symptom burden and poor quality of life. Persons with advanced COPD may benefit from palliative care, but its use among persons with COPD remains limited, also in Germany.

METHODS: A qualitative, multi-perspective interview study was conducted with persons suffering from advanced COPD, informal caregivers, and formal caregivers (general practitioners, pulmonologists, and palliative care physicians). A total of 53 interviews were analysed following structuring (Kuckartz') as well as latent content analysis methods using MAXQDA.

RESULTS: Key needs were identified in the following domains (1) management of dyspnoea and anxiety, (2) home-based healthcare, (3) emergency planning and support, (4) psychosocial care, (5) organisational support, and (6) timely information about COPD and palliative care. Persons who had previously received PC reported various needs met in the first five areas.

CONCLUSIONS: Persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers reported numerous needs. Persons receiving palliative care reported relief from various needs. Timely information about COPD's progression and palliative care could increase acceptance and thus use of palliative care among these persons and could consequently reduce or curtail the burden of living with advanced COPD.

articles.title: Malocclusion and orthodontic treatment needs among individuals with down syndrome in Egypt: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with Down syndrome commonly present with a variety of craniofacial and dental anomalies that increase the prevalence of malocclusion and the need for orthodontic treatment. Despite this, data regarding orthodontic needs in this population in the middle east, particularly in Egypt, remain limited.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to assess the patterns of malocclusion and orthodontic treatment needs among individuals with Down syndrome.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 117 individuals with Down syndrome aged 12-25 years, who met the study's eligibility criteria, were recruited from specialized institutions in Egypt in a multi-centred cross-sectional study. Clinical examination included extraoral and intraoral assessment, occlusal analysis using Angle's classification, and assessment of the need for orthodontic treatment using Dental Health Component of Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN). Additional data on oral hygiene, oral habits, and craniofacial features were recorded. Descriptive statistics were computed for all study variables. Qualitative (categorical) variables were presented as frequencies (n) and percentages (%).

RESULTS: Class I molar relationship was the most common (41.0%), followed by Class II (29.9%) and Class III (29.1%). Anterior open bite (23.1%) and posterior crossbite (21.4%) were also frequently observed. Regarding orthodontic treatment need, 71.7% of participants demonstrated borderline to very great need (IOTN Grades 3-5), with 49.6% exhibiting great or very great need (Grades 4-5). Fair or poor oral hygiene was identified in 81.2% of participants. Mouth breathing was the most common oral habit (32.5%).

CONCLUSION: Patients with Down syndrome exhibit a high prevalence of malocclusion and a significant need for orthodontic treatment. Early orthodontic assessment, preventive strategies, and multidisciplinary management are essential to improve oral health outcomes in this population.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Outdoor cycling competence and balance control in older adults - cross-sectional analysis of the BiPerAge trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although cycling offers numerous health benefits, age-related functional decline can increase the risk of accidents. Identifying balance components linked to outdoor cycling competence could inform targeted assessment and training. We aimed to exploratorily investigate the association between outdoor cycling competence and static, dynamic, and reactive balance control in older adults.

METHODS: In this exploratory cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a two-center randomized controlled trial, 116 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 65 years with ≥ 3 errors on a standardized outdoor cycling course completed a balance test battery: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), including gait speed, Modified Balance Error Scoring System (MBESS) and Four Square Step Test (FSST). Cycling-specific trunk balance was assessed with the Perturbation Stationary Bicycle Robotics (PerStBiRo) system, which delivers unannounced angular-tilt perturbations during stationary cycling. We derived mediolateral (ML) trunk sway during unperturbed cycling (UPC) and trunk time-to-peak angle (s) and trunk sway (°) during perturbed cycling (PC). Spearman correlations and multivariable models adjusted for age, sex and country were used to examine associations with the number of errors in the standardized outdoor cycling course.

RESULTS: Participants (mean age 74.0 ± 5.4 years; 53% women) made 13.1 ± 8.0 errors on the outdoor cycling course. In bivariate analyses, more outdoor cycling errors were weakly associated with more total errors on the MBESS (rs = 0.213, p = 0.022), slower gait speed (rs = -0.203, p = 0.029), greater ML trunk sway during UPC (rs = 0.246, p = 0.009), shorter trunk time-to-peak angle (rs = -0.289, p = 0.002) and lower trunk sway in PC (rs = -0.295, p = 0.002). In multivariable analyses, longer FSST time (B = 1.28 [95% CI 0.39, 2.17], p = 0.005) and greater trunk sway during UPC (B = 2.68 [0.60, 4.77], p = 0.012) were independently associated with more cycling errors.

CONCLUSIONS: This study shows weak associations between outdoor cycling competence and dynamic balance control during both UPC and FSST. Low trunk sway during UPC on the PerStBiRo is weakly associated with better outdoor cycling competence. These findings could be further evaluated in future studies aiming to improve outdoor cycling competence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This is a retrospective analysis of BiPerAge study data registered at clinicaltrials.gov: NCT06453473 (initial submission: 11/06/2024), link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06453473 .

articles.title: NR-MRC: A No-Reference Magnetic Resonance Curve Estimation Network for Tumor MR Image Quality Assessment and Enhancement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate image quality assessment (IQA) is essential for evaluating tumor magnetic resonance (MR) images in clinical practice and computer-aided diagnosis. However, most existing IQA models are designed for natural images and require reference images for training. Variability in tissue characteristics, lesion location, and lesion morphology, together with the scarcity of high-quality MR reference images, makes quality assessment of tumor MR images particularly challenging.

METHODS: To address these challenges, we propose a no-reference magnetic resonance curve estimation network named NR-MRC. First, a magnetic resonance curve estimation module uses nonlinear curve mapping to estimate spatially adjusted intensity and detail features without requiring reference tumor MR images. Second, a multi-scale feature estimation module extracts contextual features at different scales and fuses them with the initial estimates to generate enhanced MR images. Finally, a magnetic resonance scene statistics blind quality model evaluates feature consistency between the original images and their enhanced counterparts.

RESULTS: Experiments on publicly available brain tumor and bladder cancer datasets demonstrate that NR-MRC outperforms the compared IQA and image enhancement methods. In the tested U-Net and DeepLab v3 settings, training with images selected by high NR-MRC scores or enhanced by NR-MRC increased segmentation metrics by approximately 20%. These task-specific gains do not by themselves establish improved clinical diagnostic image quality.

CONCLUSION: NR-MRC provides no-reference quality assessment and enhancement for tumor MR images and shows potential utility in the evaluated downstream segmentation tasks.

articles.title: Frozen Echocardiography Foundation Model Embeddings Contain Linearly Recoverable LVOT VTI and TAPSE Report-Label Signal in MIMIC-IV-ECHO.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Quantitative transthoracic echocardiographic measurements support cardiovascular assessment, but structured report-label values may be unavailable for downstream research. We evaluated whether frozen EchoPrime study-level embeddings encoded signal associated with structured left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LVOT VTI) and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) report-label values. MIMIC-IV-ECHO studies with report labels and frozen EchoPrime embeddings were analyzed. Clip-level 512-dimensional embeddings were mean-pooled into study-level all-clips embeddings. Supervised Ridge regression used deterministic subject-level train/validation/test splits, train-fit standardization, and validation-only alpha selection. LVOT VTI was primary, TAPSE secondary. Comparators were a train-median null model and leakage-safe non-image baselines using age, sex, and acquisition metadata. For LVOT VTI, 3782 studies were split into 2654 training, 573 validation, and 555 test studies. Ridge achieved test mean absolute error (MAE) 3.64 cm versus 4.54 cm for null, root mean squared error (RMSE) 4.66 cm, R2 0.372, and MAE 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.41-3.88 cm. Observed-vs-predicted Pearson r was 0.613 (95% CI, 0.556-0.664). For TAPSE, 1131 studies were split into 787 training, 184 validation, and 160 test studies. Ridge achieved MAE 3.17 mm versus 3.79 mm for null, RMSE 3.94 mm, R2 0.284, and MAE 95% CI 2.80-3.56 mm. Pearson r was 0.539 (95% CI, 0.424-0.632). Non-image baselines were weaker than imaging embeddings. Frozen EchoPrime study-level embeddings encoded signal associated with structured LVOT VTI and TAPSE report-label values. Findings support representation-level report-label prediction experiments, not EchoPrime fine-tuning, direct measurement extraction, measurement replacement, clinical deployment, or decision support.

articles.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma with bile duct tumor thrombosis: An uncommon cause for obstructive jaundice.

articles.title: Race, Gender, and Survival: a Scoping Review of Disparities in ICU Post-Resuscitation Care and Neurological Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities in healthcare are well documented, yet limited attention has been given to the intersection of race/ethnicity and gender in high-acuity critical care. Black women experience compounded inequities affecting access to and quality of intensive care unit (ICU) treatment following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Because outcomes after OHCA are influenced by each link in the chain of survival, disparities in early intervention and subsequent clinical decision-making may contribute to differences in survival and neurological recovery. This study synthesizes evidence on disparities in ICU treatment and outcomes among Black women in the United States while examining how inequities across the chain of survival may influence post-resuscitation care, neurocritical care, and outcomes following OHCA. We conducted a scoping review, guided by the Arksey and O'Malley framework, to analyze peer-reviewed studies identified through electronic databases (e.g., PubMed, CINAHL, and ScienceDirect). Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria and were analyzed using thematic synthesis. Findings indicate persistent disparities, including lower bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) rates, delayed emergency response, reduced access to ICU interventions, and higher rates of early do-not-resuscitate (DNR) orders and withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies (WLST). These inequities may contribute to poorer outcomes and likely reflect a combination of systemic, institutional, and social factors, although relatively few studies directly examined Black women from an intersectional perspective. Addressing these disparities requires improved data disaggregation, culturally responsive care, and interdisciplinary interventions to promote equitable post-resuscitation care and outcomes.

articles.title: A spatiotemporal framework for assessing hypoxic risk to riverine aquatic life: from summary data to actionable insight in India.
articles.abstract: Riverine hypoxia, oxygen depletion in flowing waters, poses ecological risk, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics remain poorly characterized. This study presents a novel risk-based spatiotemporal framework for assessing riverine hypoxia across Indian river systems, utilizing 18,976 site-year summary data points (annual minimum, mean, maximum) across 87 sub-basins over 17 years. We conceptualized 'contextual hypoxic risk' as the probability of summary statistics falling below a critical threshold (4.0 mg L⁻1), distinguishing emerging, intermittent, and perennial hypoxic conditions. Hypoxic risks were estimated under an empirical Bayes (Poisson-Gamma hierarchical framework) to address overdispersion and stabilize standard error. Sub-basin-level aggregation mitigated site selection bias, yielding hydrologically meaningful and analytical units that facilitates policy decision. Of observations, 47% (8914) were emerging hypoxic events, 7% (1328) intermittent, and 1% (190) perennial. At least one severe hypoxic event (DO < 2.0 mg L⁻1) occurred at approximately 25% of sites-significantly exceeding the global average (12.6%). Spatial analysis revealed pronounced heterogeneity, with hypoxic risk ranging from 0 to 50%, and northwestern and Gangetic sub-basins exhibiting high hypoxic risks and faster intensification. While hypoxic occurrences revealed upward national trend, hypoxic risk showed transient patterns. Space-time interaction analysis indicated statistically significant accelerating risk trajectories-particularly for perennial and intermittent types-across six key sub-basins. By coupling probabilistic risk modelling with spatial smoothing and trajectory steepness diagnostics, this framework quantifies both spatial variability and temporal intensification of riverine hypoxia. The scalable, reproducible framework is applicable to other developing regions. Findings underscore urgent need for adaptive, sub-basin-scale management to prevent progressive establishment of chronic hypoxic regimes in India's river systems.

articles.title: Breathing at the Border: PM₂.₅ Exposure, Immigration, and COPD Across Census Tracts Close to Ports-of-Entry.
articles.journal: Journal of immigrant and minority health
articles.abstract: The North American Free Trade Agreement, now the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, has increased semi-truck and vehicular traffic at international ports-of-entry, raising air pollution concerns in the US-Mexico border region. Studying the border county of El Paso, Texas, a central hub for Mexican imports, we extend the literature by examining the prevalence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) across census tracts with varying proximities to the port-of-entry, PM2.5 exposure, and percent immigrant. We accomplish this objective by merging NASA PM2.5 measurements with health data from the US Centers for Disease Control and social vulnerability indicators from the US Census' American Community Survey. We also use ArcGIS Pro to determine each census tract's proximity to a port-of-entry. Using Generalized Linear Models, we found that PM2.5 and the percent foreign-born noncitizens are positively associated with COPD prevalence. Census tracts close to a port-of-entry, compared with those more than three miles away, have higher COPD prevalence. Moreover, COPD prevalence in immigrant communities and the effects of PM2.5 are stratified across census tracts by proximity to ports-of-entry.

articles.title: Established determinants of replicative lifespan, including mitochondrial DNA, play a limited role in early yeast stress-resistance decline.
articles.abstract: Baker's yeast is a long-standing model for studying mechanisms of aging. Due to asymmetric division, yeast mother and daughter cells are distinguishable, and mother cells usually cease division after 15-25 budding events. However, yeast suspensions consist predominantly of young cells. Here we investigated whether, under harsh environmental conditions, replicative aging-defined by the number of buds produced-manifests at early replicative ages. To test this, we adapted a flow-cytometry-based pulse-chase labeling method to track the survival of cells of increasing replicative age, from daughter cells to mother cells that had produced up to eight buds on average. We found that stress-induced mortality increased with replicative age across all nine stress conditions tested. Mitochondrial dysfunction, caused by depletion of mitochondrial DNA, altered basal stress resistance for some stresses but largely preserved the age-dependent decline in stress resistance across conditions. Similarly, deletion of FOB1, which extends replicative lifespan under optimal conditions, did not markedly alter this decline under heat shock or acetic acid. In contrast, deletion of SIR2, which shortens replicative lifespan, steepened the age-mortality slope under acetic acid stress but not under heat shock. Together, our data indicate that aging manifests early in life under various extreme environments, and that the genetic determinants of maximum replicative lifespan tested here are largely dispensable for the early decline in stress resistance.

articles.title: Are prophylactic antibiotics routinely necessary in laparoscopic adnexal surgery? A multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit of routine prophylactic antibiotics for clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery remains unclear. We evaluated whether pre-incision cefazolin reduces the incidence of 30-day surgical site infections (SSIs), and we identified perioperative risk factors for SSIs.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using clinical data from Osaka University and six affiliated hospitals. Among 1,865 patients who underwent laparoscopic adnexal surgery for benign conditions, 1,678 were included after specified exclusions. Patients received either pre-incision cefazolin (n = 1,415) or no prophylaxis (n = 263) according to institutional policy. The primary outcome was the incidence of SSI during the 30-day postoperative interval, classified according to CDC criteria. The association between prophylaxis and SSI was evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Propensity scores were estimated using age, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, endometriosis, and previous abdominal surgery. Risk factors for SSI were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by repeating the same IPTW procedure within specified subgroups, and procedure-specific supplementary analyses were performed for ovarian cystectomy.

RESULTS: SSI occurred in 1.1% of patients in both groups: 16/1,415 in the cefazolin group and 3/263 in the non-antibiotic group. In IPTW-adjusted analyses, the incidence of SSI did not differ between groups (1.1% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.915). In multivariable analysis, operative time ≥120 min was associated with SSI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-8.85). In supplementary analyses restricted to an ovarian cystectomy subgroup, uterine manipulator use was associated with SSI (aOR 4.03, 95% CI 1.26-12.90).

CONCLUSION: Routine prophylactic cefazolin was not associated with a significantly lower incidence of 30-day SSI after clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery. Given few SSI events and the potential for residual confounding, our findings support further evaluation of a selective rather than routine approach to prophylactic antibiotic use.

articles.title: Comparable efficacy of extraoral and intraoral photobiomodulation in preventing oral mucositis during high-dose methotrexate therapy in pediatric oncology: A single-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This prospective randomized controlled clinical study compared intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation (PBM) for the prevention of chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric oncology patients.

METHODS: A total of 155 patients (1-18 years), receiving high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) for leukemia, lymphoma, or osteosarcoma, were randomized to PBM-IO (n = 73) or PBM-EO (n = 82). Preventive PBM was administered daily from hospital admission through discharge. Both protocols used red light with equivalent dosimetry (660 nm, 100 mW, 1 J per point). PBM-EO required 30 s/session, whereas PBM-IO required approximately 6 min, excluding patient handling time. OM occurrence, severity (WHO scale), plaque index, and pain (numeric rating scale) were assessed on days 0, 3, 5, and 10 after HDMTX infusion.

RESULTS: The overall OM occurrence was 35.5%, with no significant difference between PBM-IO (41.1%) and PBM-EO (30.5%) groups (p = 0.168). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups for OM severity, pain, salivary pH, or plaque index at any time point (p > 0.05). Multivariable ordinal logistic regression demonstrated that PBM modality was not independently associated with OM severity. As expected, increasing age (OR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.04-1.25; p = 0.004) and higher HDMTX dose (OR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.03-1.49; p = 0.021) were significantly associated with greater OM severity. Median pain scores remained 0 at all assessment points in both groups.

CONCLUSION: Extraoral PBM demonstrated comparable effectiveness to intraoral for OM prevention in pediatric patients undergoing HDMTX chemotherapy, while reducing application time.

articles.title: Association between PM2.5 and coronary artery dilatation with Kawasaki disease in China.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Kawasaki disease is an acute febrile systemic vasculitis that predominantly affects children and can lead to coronary artery dilatation (CAD), coronary artery aneurysm, and/or thrombosis. This study aimed to investigate whether exposure to particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of CAD. A case-crossover study was conducted to investigate the relationship between PM2.5 exposure and coronary Z value in children. The study included 847 participants from 2017 to 2021. The Z value was calculated for each participant, and PM2.5 exposure levels were assigned. The risk effect of PM2.5 on the Z value was assessed using the distributed lag Poisson generalized linear model. Correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the mechanisms underlying CAD, and sensitivity analysis was conducted to verify the stability of the model. PM2.5 exposure was found to increase the risk of CAD at lag 2-4 days. On the 3rd day of lag, PM2.5 exposure led to the highest risk of CAD, with RR = 1.11, (95%CI = 1.02, 1.21). Mediation analysis showed that PM2.5 may induce CAD through C-reactive protein (CRP), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and hemoglobin (HB), and the effect size was significant, indicating that CRP, ALT and HB were the main mediating factors between PM2.5 and CAD.

CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that PM2.5 exposure is a potential risk factor for CAD in children. CRP, alanine aminotransferase, and hemoglobin were identified as the main mediators regulating the relationship between PM2.5 and CAD.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • PM2.5 may lead to an increased incidence of Kawasaki disease in children.

WHAT IS NEW: • We found that inhalation of PM2.5 may cause coronary artery dilatation in Kawasaki disease through a population-based cohort study. • This process may be mediated by increasing C-reactive protein. • The model results remained stable after sensitivity analysis.

articles.title: [Cardiac involvement in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac manifestations in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) occur more frequently than they are clinically recognized and are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. In particular, subclinical myocarditis often remains undetected due to nonspecific or absent symptoms.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to summarize the prevalence, pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, diagnostic strategies and therapeutic options of cardiac involvement in IIM and to provide practical recommendations for rheumatologists.

METHODS: A scoping review on cardiac manifestations in IIM was performed. A structured literature search was conducted using the PubMed database. The search strategy included combinations of relevant keywords and MeSH terms. Primarily, English language original studies, systematic reviews and current guideline publications related to cardiac involvement in IIM were considered. Studies were selected based on clinical relevance, methodological quality and recency.

RESULTS: The reported prevalence of cardiac involvement in IIM ranges from 4-26%, depending on the subtype and diagnostic approach. In addition to clinically overt myocarditis, subclinical abnormalities are common and can be detected in up to 50% of patients using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI). Pathophysiological mechanisms include immune-mediated myocardial injury, microvascular dysfunction and fibrotic remodelling. The initial diagnostic work-up should comprise taking a medical history, electrocardiography, measurement of cardiac biomarkers and echocardiography. The use of CMRI represents the diagnostic gold standard and enables sensitive detection of inflammatory and fibrotic myocardial changes. Therapeutically, early initiation of drug treatment, typically high-dose glucocorticoids combined with additional immunomodulating agents, constitutes the cornerstone of management.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac manifestations in IIM are common, prognostically relevant and frequently underestimated in clinical practice. A structured diagnostic approach with early use of CMRI and interdisciplinary management is essential to detect subclinical disease and guide appropriate treatment.

articles.title: The kinetic basis of photosynthetic heat tolerance.
articles.abstract: Photosynthetic heat tolerance constrains primary productivity and defines the upper temperature limit of the biosphere. However, current approaches to heat tolerance either overlook the duration of heat exposure or describe temperature-time relationships without characterizing causal mechanisms, constraining hypothesis testing and prediction under novel conditions. Heat inactivation of photosynthesis has been posited to result from protein denaturation or lipid membrane breakdown, but their relative contributions are not well resolved. Here we develop and test a quantitative theory of photosynthetic heat inactivation based on chemical kinetics and use the theory to evaluate these competing mechanisms. By analysing photosystem II temperature responses in 177 plant species from 157 families, we show that protein denaturation, not lipid membrane breakdown, governs heat tolerance. The theory also predicts an upper acclimatization limit of ~60 °C, set by the thermal stability of heat shock proteins and supported by global data for 826 species. Our findings provide a predictive, mechanistic basis for photosynthetic heat tolerance and the thermal limits of the biosphere in a changing climate.

articles.title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. We analyzed multimodal MRI data from 577 patients (MDD, asthma, fibromyalgia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, type 2 diabetes) and 275 healthy controls, constructed individual morphometric similarity networks (MSN) to identify shared cortical alterations, and applied principal component analysis with multiscale molecular annotation (transcriptomic, cell-type, neurotransmitter, and cognitive mapping) to characterize underlying mechanisms. All patient groups exhibited regional MSN abnormalities. A shared MSN pattern emerged, featuring increased similarity in visual and somatomotor regions and decreased similarity in ventral attention, limbic, and default mode networks, and was replicated in independent cohorts. This pattern was significantly associated with spatial gene expression enriched for synaptic signaling, membrane potential regulation, and neuronal architecture, with predominant expression in excitatory/inhibitory neurons and astrocytes. It further mapped onto specific neurotransmitter systems, with exploratory cognitive decoding suggesting possible relevance to emotion and social cognition. Related genes overlapped with known risk loci for Alzheimer's disease and bipolar disorder. These findings identify a robust across diseases cortical MSN phenotype linked to convergent molecular and neurochemical correlates, offering a framework for studying shared vulnerability and transdiagnostic mechanisms across depression and physical diseases.

articles.title: Applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants: implications for respiratory distress syndrome and bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a promising bedside imaging modality in neonatal intensive care units, offering real-time assessment of lung aeration without exposure to ionizing radiation. These advantages are particularly relevant for preterm infants, who are vulnerable to cumulative radiation exposure and evolving pulmonary disease. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the functional clinical applications of lung ultrasound in preterm infants. We focus on how LUS has been studied to guide early respiratory management, predict the need for surfactant and escalation of respiratory support, assess extubation readiness, identify infants at increased risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and monitor disease trajectory and response to therapy throughout the NICU course, including emerging data on longer-term respiratory outcomes. While available studies demonstrate promising diagnostic and prognostic value, interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, scoring systems, timing of assessment, and operator dependence. Further multicenter studies with standardized protocols are needed to define the role of LUS in routine neonatal respiratory care.

articles.title: INDICATE [INtroducing DIabetes Checks in A denTal sEtting]: estimating prevalence of undiagnosed pre-diabetes/type 2 diabetes in primary dental care.
articles.abstract: Aims Non-diabetic hyperglycaemia (NDH; pre-diabetes) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) represent an increasing health and economic burden. Oral healthcare professionals may support early identification of undiagnosed disease, particularly in patients with periodontitis. This study estimated the prevalence of undiagnosed NDH/T2D in NHS dental settings and evaluated the performance of two validated diabetes risk-prediction tools in primary dental care.Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in 13 NHS dental practices. Adults aged ≥40 years without a prior diagnosis of NDH/T2D were recruited. Participants (n = 803) completed two validated risk questionnaires and underwent point-of-care HbA1c testing irrespective of risk score. Individuals with HbA1c ≥42 mmol/mol (6.0%) received preventive advice and were advised to consult their general practitioner.Results Sixty one percent of participants self-identified as women, 85% as white British; and mean body mass index was 27.4 kg/m². NDH prevalence (HbA1c 42-47 mmol/mol) was 10.0%, and previously undiagnosed T2D (≥48 mmol/mol) was 3.0%. Using UK/ADA diagnostic thresholds as the reference standard, both risk tools showed good sensitivity (>80%) but low specificity (<55%).Conclusions This large UK primary care dental study demonstrates that NDH and undiagnosed T2D are common in dental attendees. Both questionnaires showed acceptable sensitivity, while point-of-care HbA1c testing improved specificity within a two-step dental risk-assessment pathway.

articles.title: Association between dietary patterns and the dental caries experience among postmenopausal women.
articles.abstract: Aims To examine the association between dietary patterns and the decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT) score cross-sectionally and prospectively among postmenopausal women.Methods Study sample included postmenopausal women enrolled in the OsteoPerio study. Dietary patterns, including the Healthy Eating Index (HEI)-2020, Alternative HEI (AHEI)-2010, dietary approaches to stop hypertension, and alternate Mediterranean Diet (aMed), were scored based on two food frequency questionnaires administered across three years preceding baseline (1997-2001). Dental examinations at baseline and year five assessed 28 teeth (excluding third molars). Numbers of DMFT were aggregated according to the World Health Organization's definition. Cross-sectional associations of dietary pattern scores with decayed teeth, missing teeth, and filled teeth, and DMFT at baseline (n = 1,214) and prospective associations with changes in MT and DMFT (n = 934) were examined.Results Cross-sectionally, higher HEI, AHEI, and aMed scores were associated with less MT (rate ratios: 0.93, 0.91, and 0.96, respectively) and less DMFT (ß: -0.32, -0.50, and -0.23, respectively). No significant prospective associations were observed.Conclusions In this group of postmenopausal women, better adherence to healthy dietary patterns was associated with fewer prevalent dental caries but not with the progression in five years.

articles.title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring.
articles.abstract: Metal-free molecular magnets differ from conventional magnetic devices that predominantly rely on metallic magnets as these metal-free materials may offer biocompatibility and bioresorbability. However, existing molecular materials lack the ferromagnetic strength required for high-fidelity sensing at clinically relevant tissue depths. Here we introduce a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet derived from graphitic carbon nitride, combining metallic-level ferromagnetism with full bioresorbability. De-nitrogenation creates spin centres coupled through a reconstructed π-σ conjugated framework, conferring robust spontaneous magnetization that remains stable under physiological conditions. Integrated with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and silk fibroin, the material forms catheter-deliverable epicardial patches for cardiac tracking and can also be dispersed in injectable hydrogels for organ-scale sensing, including the three-dimensional reconstruction of localized hepatic pathologies. Coupled with a skin-interfaced Hall array, this magnetic sensing architecture provides the continuous, untethered monitoring of multi-organ dynamics, robust against motion artifacts and tissue impedance. In porcine models, it facilitates the continuous assessment of ejection fraction over 4 weeks, followed by benign bioresorption. Benchmarked against standard-of-care echocardiography, this approach delivers clinical-grade trajectories, supporting longitudinal, infrastructure-independent physiological monitoring.

articles.title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

articles.title: G-protein-coupled receptor sensing of farnesol controls fungal dormancy and is susceptible to bacterial interference.
articles.abstract: Conidial dormancy is a critical survival strategy for fungi under stress, yet the mechanisms governing the switch between dormancy and germination remain unclear. Here we identify the G-protein-coupled receptor, Rsd1, as a farnesol-responsive sensor controlling this dormancy switch in the plant pathogen Fusarium pseudograminearum, which causes Fusarium crown rot. Under high population density and nutrient limitation, endogenous farnesol activates Rsd1 and downstream signalling pathways to suppress conidial germination. Rsd1 also responds to extracellular farnesol, linking environmental signals to an intrinsic transcriptional programme for dormancy. This adaptive response enhances survival but creates a fitness trade-off during plant infection. Specific rhizosphere-associated bacteria also contribute by promoting or inhibiting germination of dormant conidia through farnesol-Rsd1 sensing. Consortia assembled from these bacteria altered the balance between stress-resilient dormancy and infection-associated germination, thereby modulating disease severity. Our findings demonstrate how microbial interactions reshape intrinsic fungal regulatory programmes governing dormancy and infection.

articles.title: SIV reservoir depletion and clearance from neonatal macaques following transient CCR5 depletion.
articles.abstract: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses viraemia in people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), but HIV provirus persists indefinitely in CD4-expressing cells. Cells containing active provirus express viral proteins and have been successfully targeted using broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). In contrast, cells containing latent provirus cannot be specifically targeted without latency reactivation. Meaningful depletion of the latent HIV or simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) reservoirs has not been demonstrated except with cytotoxic conditioning for bone-marrow transplantation. Here we show that both the active and latent SIV reservoirs can be eliminated from infant macaques via profound but transient depletion of cells that express CCR5 using a single shot of CCR5/CD3 bispecific antibody. Neonatal rhesus macaques were infected with SIVmac251, then treated with ART beginning at 1 week after infection, followed by treatment with either a CCR5/CD3-bispecific or a CD4-specific antibody, both of which depleted target cells and accelerated the decline in plasma viraemia. Upon ART cessation, while rebound occurred quickly in all animals treated with ART alone, most animals treated with CCR5/CD3 bispecific antibody remained aviraemic for >3 months. Several remained aviraemic to the end of follow-up and efforts to detect replication-competent virus were unsuccessful. Our results show that bispecific antibody treatment achieves meaningful depletion of the replication-competent SIV reservoir and supports the possibility that clinically meaningful depletion of the HIV reservoir might be achievable for recently infected individuals.

articles.title: Chronic lung infection does not impair lentiviral vector gene transfer in a cystic fibrosis rat model.
articles.abstract: Genetic therapies offer a promising strategy for treating cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease, particularly for individuals with modulator-ineligible genotypes. However, clinical translation has been slower than anticipated. While CF gene therapy candidates typically demonstrate high efficacy in preclinical studies, all products trialled to date have failed to progress beyond Phase I/II, raising questions about the predictive capacity of current preclinical models.
