One contributing factor may be the absence of severe muco-obstructive lung disease in commonly used CF rodent models, highlighting the need to evaluate gene vectors under conditions that more closely recapitulate the CF lung environment. In this study, we evaluated a vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein G (VSV-G) pseudotyped lentiviral (LV) vector carrying the luciferase reporter gene under conditions of Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung infection in wild-type and CF rats. Bioluminescence imaging was conducted on days 7 and 14 post-LV vector administration to assess lung transgene expression under infected and non-infected conditions. At day 7, there was no significant difference in bioluminescence between P. aeruginosa-infected and non-infected animals (p = 0.537). From day 7 to day 14, bioluminescence decreased 136-fold in non-infected animals (p < 0.0001), compared with a 7-fold decrease in infected animals (p = 0.043), with a significant infection × time interaction indicating that the magnitude of decline was greater in non-infected controls (p = 0.024). These findings demonstrate that lung disease state can modulate transgene expression and persistence, highlighting the importance of evaluating gene therapy vectors under conditions that more closely mimic the CF lung environment.

articles.title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442.

articles.title: Real-World Semaglutide Initiation Behaviours in the United States: Impact on Early Treatment Discontinuation and on 1-Year Persistence.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Little is known about how glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are initiated in real-world settings and whether prescribing behaviours in routine care contribute to the high discontinuation rates seen in practice. We examined prescribing behaviours for injectable semaglutide at treatment initiation and evaluated their impact on early medication discontinuation and on 1-year persistence among US adults.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using MarketScan data (2018-2021), this retrospective cohort study identified US adults with diabetes and/or obesity on no prior incretin therapy starting injectable semaglutide. Initiating dose was categorized as low or high (≤ 0.5 and ≥ 1.0 mg/week, respectively); treatment status was followed for 12 months. Medication persistence was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Piecewise Cox proportional hazards regression assessed early discontinuation risk, logistic regression assessed the odds of high-dose initiation.

RESULTS: Among this cohort of 48 658 adults, 14.5% were started on semaglutide using high doses. The off-label high-dose regimen was associated with decreased 1-year persistence (p = 0.01), and a 25% increase in early discontinuation risk (HR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.17-1.34, p < 0.001) independently of age, obesity status, co-morbidity measures and cost. Odds of high-dose initiation were increased in the West and South (p < 0.001), for endocrinologists (p = 0.02), for patients who were male (p < 0.001), younger (p = 0.02), with obesity versus overweight (p = 0.002), and for treatment initiation in 2018 compared with 2019-2021 (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Initiation of injectable semaglutide therapy using high doses is common in real-world settings. High-dose initiation represents a modifiable risk factor for early medication discontinuation and decreased 1-year persistence.

articles.title: Impact of DBLG1 Hybrid Closed-Loop Software Optimization and Meal Declaration Pattern on Glucose Metrics in Type 1 Diabetes: A 12-Month Prospective Evaluation in 2014 Users.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The meal period is critical for the outcome of automated insulin delivery. Our aim was to explore the long-term impact on glucose metrics of algorithmic modifications of the DBLG1 hybrid closed-loop system, with special emphasis on the meal declaration pattern.

METHODS: We prospectively analysed CGM data from consenting adult patients with Type 1 diabetes across Europe who initiated the new version of DBLG1 paired with the Kaleido patch pump upon its release. Inclusion occurred over 7 months, with follow-up extended up to 12 months. Time in range 70-180 mg/dL (TIR) was the primary endpoint. Utility endpoints included the number of declared meals.

RESULTS: This study included 2014 users, age 42.5 ± 13.8 years, baseline HbA1c 7.6% ± 1.2%. Median TIR was 72.0%, 72.3%, 72.0% and 71.7% at M3, M6, M9 and M12, respectively. At M3, time < 54 mg/dL (0.2%), < 70 mg/dL (1.2%) and > 250 mg/dL (5.4%) were controlled and remained stable throughout M12, as well as GMI (7.0%-7.1%). The incidence rates of severe hypo- or hyperglycaemia remained very low. TIR in patients declaring ≥ 3 meals/day exceeded TIR in those declaring < 1 meal/day (73.3 [67.3, 78.7]% vs. 65.7 [60.7, 72.2]%, p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the sustained safety and effectiveness of the latest version of the DBLG1 software, with TIR exceeding 70% throughout the 12-month follow-up period in a large group of 2014 users. Furthermore, while glycaemic control was negatively affected when meal declaration was reduced, the software maintained its safety and acceptable effectiveness in this latter situation.

articles.title: A Clinically Occult Tubular Phenotype in Type 2 Diabetes Despite Normoalbuminuria and Preserved eGFR: Multiscale Human Kidney Evidence.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To determine the prevalence of a low-molecular-weight protein (LMWP)-defined tubular phenotype in adults with Type 2 diabetes, normoalbuminuria and preserved estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), its relation to UACR, and its human kidney context.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We studied 4046 adults with Type 2 diabetes, UACR < 30 mg/g, eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and paired morning urinary α1-microglobulin (α1MG) and β2-microglobulin (β2MG). The phenotype required α1MG > 12 mg/L and β2MG > 0.20 mg/L. We tested associations with UACR and performed medication, admission-context, high-eGFR and liver-function sensitivity analyses. Independent microdissected tubular, single-cell/single-nucleus and CosMx datasets were analysed.

RESULTS: The phenotype was present in 797 patients (19.7%). UACR alone did not discriminate the phenotype (AUC 0.466, 95% CI: 0.443-0.489), and ln(UACR+1) was not associated with it after clinical adjustment (OR: 0.873, 95% CI: 0.710-1.075; p = 0.201). Medication adjustment produced a similar estimate (OR: 0.871, 95% CI: 0.708-1.072; p = 0.191), with consistent findings in the other sensitivity analyses. In microdissected tubules, a 10-gene injury score was higher in DKD (p < 0.001); sample-level injured proximal-tubular fractions were highest in DKD in the single-cell atlas (p = 0.029), and spatial profiling resolved five injured proximal-tubular subclusters.

CONCLUSIONS: An LMWP-defined tubular phenotype was present in nearly one in five adults with Type 2 diabetes despite normoalbuminuria and preserved eGFR, and was poorly captured by UACR. Independent human kidney datasets showed related proximal-tubular injury-associated programmes with marked cellular and spatial heterogeneity. These findings support tubular phenotyping as a complementary approach to kidney assessment in Type 2 diabetes and warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Changes in Muscle Strength Following Semaglutide Treatment in Adults: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis of Handgrip Strength.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To systematically review and quantitatively synthesize within-group changes in skeletal muscle strength following semaglutide treatment in adults.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This PRISMA 2020 systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251185935). MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, LILACS and Google Scholar were searched through 20 August 2026, without language restrictions. Eligible studies included adults treated with semaglutide reporting quantitative skeletal muscle strength outcomes, including handgrip and knee extension strength. Randomized, non-randomized and uncontrolled before-after studies were included. The primary meta-analysis pooled within-group changes in handgrip strength from baseline to the longest available follow-up of semaglutide-only arms using a random-effects model. Knee extension strength was summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Sixteen reports represented eleven studies, all assessing handgrip strength; one small randomized trial also assessed knee extension strength. Ten studies (660 semaglutide-treated participants) contributed to the primary meta-analysis of uncontrolled within-group changes, showing a nonsignificant pooled handgrip strength change (-0.16 kgf; 95% confidence interval: -1.98 to 1.65), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 90.8%) and a 95% prediction interval from -5.96 to 5.63 kgf. Duration-stratified and sensitivity analyses were also nonsignificant. Individual study findings were heterogeneous. Certainty was very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence is insufficient to determine whether semaglutide is associated with changes in handgrip strength because the principal synthesis was based on uncontrolled within-group changes, with very low certainty and significant heterogeneity. These findings do not establish strength preservation or a causal treatment effect. More robust comparative studies with standardized strength assessment and longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Intraoperative Continuous Glucose Monitor Sensor-Receiver Connectivity Is Maintained With Alternative Sensor Placement: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perioperative glycaemic control is associated with reduced postoperative complications. However, regulatory restrictions on point-of-care device operation and operative positioning constraints, reducing accessibility for dermal puncture, may hinder intraoperative monitoring. Although continuous glucose monitors (CGM) support real-time glucose monitoring, intraoperative patient positioning may increase compression low susceptibility, and electrosurgery interference may affect sensor-receiver connectivity. Alternative CGM sensor placement may improve intraoperative sensor-receiver connectivity.

METHODS: In this prospective pilot study of adult surgical patients, CGM sensors were inserted in the lateral upper arm (deltoid) or lateral thigh (thigh) to limit patient position-related sensor pressure. The primary endpoint evaluated proportional duration of CGM sensor-receiver connectivity during surgery. Comparison of sensor-receiver connectivity by placement site, relation to electrosurgery and the number of alerts from the CGM receiver were also reported.

RESULTS: Forty-five subjects were randomized: 22 deltoid and 23 thigh CGM placement. Four subjects were excluded; 20 deltoid and 21 thigh CGM sensor placements were analysed. Sensor-receiver connectivity was maintained during the surgical procedure in 40 (97.6%) irrespective of electrosurgery (21 thigh, 19 deltoid; difference 0, 95% CI: 0-0; p = 0.329). Of 26 receiver alerts, 11 occurred during electrosurgery; 15 were unrelated to electrosurgery. There was no difference in receiver alerts between deltoid and thigh placement (chi square p = 0.17; difference 0.18; 95% CI: -0.07 to 0.42).

CONCLUSION: Finding consistent sensor-receiver connectivity using alternative CGM sensor placement sites supports intraoperative CGM feasibility. If future studies demonstrate alternative CGM sensor placement sites retain accuracy, then broader intraoperative CGM application may be reasonable.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06614127 | https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06614127.

articles.title: Absent Septum Pellucidum Without Polymicrogyria or Seizures in TCP1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: T-complex protein 1 (TCP1) encodes the TCP1α subunit, one of eight subunits of the chaperonin containing TCP1 ring complex (TRiC). Heterozygous TCP1 variants cause autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay or intellectual disability, seizures, pyramidal or cerebellar signs, and brain malformations, particularly polymicrogyria. However, the reported clinical spectrum remains limited. We report a 4-year-old girl with global developmental delay, speech and motor delay, behavioral dysregulation, microcephaly, hypotonia with core weakness, and a previously unreported heterozygous likely pathogenic TCP1 variant, c.1392delT (p.A465Qfs*3). This frameshift variant is located in exon 11, truncates the final 16.5% of the protein, is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, and is absent from gnomAD. Biological parental testing was unavailable, precluding determination of variant inheritance. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an absent septum pellucidum with mild bilateral frontal sulcation/gyration asymmetry without polymicrogyria; the optic nerves and pituitary were normal. No seizures were documented through age 4 years. Additional findings included bicuspid aortic valve with mild aortic insufficiency, asthma, severe eczema/atopy, and multiple food allergies. This case suggests that the molecular and neuroimaging spectrum of TCP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder may be broader than previously recognized; however, a causal association between TCP1 and absent septum pellucidum cannot be established from a single case. The relationship of the cardiac and atopic findings to TCP1 remains uncertain. Additional cases and functional studies are needed to clarify genotype-phenotype relationships.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Initiation or Simplification of Treatment With iGlarLixi in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Given the significant burden that diabetes self-management poses, it is important to assess patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for Type 2 diabetes (T2D) treatments in clinical trials and real-world studies. Complex insulin regimens are associated with increased risk of hypoglycaemia and body weight gain, which could negatively impact treatment adherence and, therefore, achievement of glycaemic targets. iGlarLixi is a once-daily fixed-ratio combination of insulin glargine 100 U/mL and the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), lixisenatide. iGlarLixi is an effective treatment alternative to complex insulin regimens, with a favourable between-group difference in body weight and reduced risk of hypoglycaemia.

METHODS: This is the first review to summarise data from multiple validated PRO measures for recent iGlarLixi studies (Soli-CGM, SoliMix, Soli-SWITCH, IDEAL, SUCCESS and SIMPLIFY JP), including: Global Treatment Effectiveness Evaluation, Audit of Diabetes Dependent Quality of Life, Diabetes Medication Satisfaction Tool, Diabetes Therapy-Related Quality of Life, Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire, Hypoglycaemic Attitudes and Behaviour Scale and Treatment-Related Impact Measure Diabetes.

RESULTS: In clinical studies, once-daily iGlarLixi was associated with numerical improvements in selected treatment satisfaction measures in those who switched from: complex insulin regimens (once- or twice-daily premixed insulin and basal-bolus insulin), basal insulin or oral glucose-lowering medications. Additionally, in real-world studies, iGlarLixi was generally associated with improvements in treatment satisfaction and quality of life outcomes in adults with T2D who previously received basal-bolus insulin or oral glucose-lowering medications ± basal insulin or GLP-1 RAs.

CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, a once-daily injection of iGlarLixi may offer a clinically beneficial, simplified treatment option for adults with T2D compared with complex insulin-based regimens.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Insulin Degludec Versus Insulin Glargine in Trial-Eligible and Ineligible Populations: A DEVOTE-Inspired Target Trial Emulation Using the Swedish National Diabetes Register.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiovascular outcomes associated with the initiation of insulin degludec versus insulin glargine using a target trial emulation approach in nationwide real-world data.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study using Swedish health registers, including the National Diabetes Register. Individuals with type 2 diabetes initiating insulin degludec or insulin glargine between 2012 and 2022 were included. Two complementary approaches were applied: a trial-eligible emulation cohort reflecting the eligibility criteria of the DEVOTE trial, and a trial-ineligible emulation cohort representing routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, i.e., myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular mortality). Secondary outcomes included the individual components of MACE, all-cause mortality and heart failure. Average treatment effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation.

RESULTS: Among 96 731 individuals identified, 44 890 met the study eligibility criteria and were included in the analyses. In the trial-eligible cohort, degludec was associated with a similar risk of MACE compared with glargine (risk ratio: 1.10; 95% CI: 0.91-1.34; p = 0.34), but a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.92; p = 0.002). In the trial-ineligible emulation cohort, degludec was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.95; p = 0.004) as well as reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal stroke and heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study, degludec was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with glargine, consistently observed in both trial-eligible and trial-ineligible populations, despite similar cardiovascular risk in the trial-eligible cohort.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal and Urological Tract Injuries During Cesarean Delivery: A Surgical Review With National Epidemiologic Data.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCesarean delivery is the most common major surgical procedure performed worldwide, accounting for approximately one-third of US deliveries. Gastrointestinal (GI) and urological (URO) tract injuries are uncommon but disproportionately morbid complications. Increasing complexity, particularly repeat cesarean and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS), and uneven on-site subspecialty coverage have expanded the role of general surgeons as intraoperative consultants for these injuries, especially outside large tertiary centers.MethodsWe analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2005-2019) to characterize the contemporary epidemiology, predictors, and outcomes of GI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery, complemented by a literature review focused on intraoperative recognition and management principles most relevant to the consulting general surgeon.ResultsAmong 3 816 895 cesarean deliveries, 8891 involved a documented GI/URO injury requiring surgical intervention (≈233 per 100 000). Bladder injuries predominated (78.2%), followed by bowel repair (13.3%), bowel resection (7.8%), and ureteral injuries (1.3%). Injuries were associated with markedly higher ICU admission (3.4% vs 0.2%), respiratory failure (1.7% vs 0.1%), in-hospital mortality (0.22% vs 0.01%), and resource utilization. Prior cesarean delivery was the strongest predictor of URO injury (OR 2.92; 95% CI 2.71-3.13).ConclusionsGI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery are uncommon but highly morbid, and the operative complexity that produces them is rising. With variable on-site subspecialty coverage, the general surgeon is frequently the first operative consultant. Familiarity with intraoperative principles, prevention strategies in high-risk cases, structured recognition, and initial repair or damage-control temporization should be considered a core competency for surgeons covering trauma, rural, or emergency general surgery call.

articles.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.

RESULTS: In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).

OBJECTIVES: To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.

METHODS: We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.

RESULTS: Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).

CONCLUSIONS: In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

articles.title: Partial Echocardiographic Remission After Sotatercept: Expanding Treatment Goals in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.
articles.abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.

articles.title: Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Data-driven risk prediction algorithms are increasingly common. However, studies suggesting that a single set of variables are most "important" within a given risk prediction model ignore the reality that other equally useful models containing entirely different features may exist. We aim to use a novel approach (Model Path Selection) to demonstrate that, for any given health outcome, there are likely many comparable counterfactual models including different sets of variables. We focus on incident stroke as a scientifically meaningful outcome to motivate this demonstration.

METHODS: Model Path Selection uses an iterative model-building procedure to illustrate a set of counterfactual prediction models ("paths"). We applied Model Path Selection to Sleep Heart Health Study data (N = 4,512 adults) to predict 5-year incident stroke, considering 30 features comprising demographics, self-reported and measured medical risk factors, polysomnography, and self-reported sleep. Area Under the Curve was estimated for each resulting path based on 10-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Model Path Selection identified 61 unique counterfactual models. 13 of these achieved Area Under the Curves between 0.81 and 0.82. Area Under the Curves of the remaining models ranged from 0.53 to 0.68 (median 0.61). All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores).

CONCLUSIONS: Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.

articles.title: Endoscopic transcanal repair of temporomandibular joint herniation into the external auditory canal: literature review.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) herniation into the external auditory canal is a rare condition associated with anterior canal wall defects, most commonly due to a patent foramen of Huschke, trauma, or infection. The clinical presentation is variable and often non-specific, which may lead to misdiagnosis. High-resolution computed tomography is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective surgical planning. While open surgical repair remains standard, minimally invasive approaches have not been widely reported. An 81-year-old male presented with right-sided otalgia exacerbated by mandibular movement and unresponsive to topical and oral antibiotics. He was initially diagnosed with malignant otitis externa. Otoscopic and radiological evaluations revealed a soft-tissue mass protruding through an anterior external auditory canal defect, consistent with TMJ herniation. After acute inflammation resolved, the patient underwent endoscopic transcanal surgical repair under general anaesthesia. The herniated TMJ capsule was dissected, and the osseous defect was reconstructed using layered autologous conchal cartilage and perichondrium. The procedure was completed entirely through the endoscopic approach without external incisions. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with complete graft integration and no recurrent herniation. Histopathological analysis excluded malignancy. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of TMJ herniation mimicking malignant otitis externa and demonstrates the feasibility of a fully endoscopic transcanal surgical approach for defect repair. The described minimally invasive technique offers a promising alternative to traditional open procedures, with reduced morbidity and favourable functional outcomes.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Tianlong Kechuanling ameliorated COPD-PH through DNMT3A-GSDMD axis-dependent regulation of endothelial cell pyroptosis" [J. Ethnopharmacol. 353, (2025), 120332].
Sustained improvement of systemic lupus erythematosus‑associated pulmonary arterial hypertension by CD19 CAR T-cell therapy: 1‑year haemodynamic follow‑up.
[Pulmonary rehabilitation: A 2026 updated expert consensus].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The effectiveness of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is supported by a high level of evidence. More recently, the indications for PR have expanded and new models of care have emerged.

STATE OF ART: This position statement summarizes recent evidence on PR regarding: 1) its objectives; 2) the key outcomes to be assessed at baseline, during, and at the end of the program, along with the recommended assessment tools; 3) its integration within the care pathway; 4) modalities of implementation, including home-based programs, telerehabilitation, and hybrid formats; 5) its core components, based on therapeutic education (including psychosocial and motivational support), exercise training, and adapted physical activity; and 6) the strategies and professionals involved in maintaining long-term benefits.

PERSPECTIVES: The extension of PR indications to other respiratory conditions (interstitial lung diseases, pulmonary hypertension, thoracic oncology) and the development of new delivery models are expected to facilitate PR access.

CONCLUSION: This position statement from French-speaking experts aims to support greater recognition of PR and to promote its integration into patient care pathways.

articles.title: Time-matched Secondary Fracture Prevention in Older Adults: A Narrative Review of Imminent Risk, Time-to-Benefit, and Treatment Sequencing.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: After a fragility fracture, subsequent fracture risk is highest during the first 6 to 12 months and remains elevated for 1 to 2 years. Anti-osteoporosis therapies differ in onset, persistence, discontinuation kinetics, and safety constraints, yet guidelines rarely operationalize treatment timing within this imminent-risk period. This narrative review examines temporal mismatch between post-fracture risk and treatment effect and proposes a time-matched secondary fracture prevention framework.

METHODS: We conducted an argument-driven narrative review using a structured, non-systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar from January 2000 through July 26, 2026. English-language guidelines, pivotal randomized trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and implementation or health-services studies relevant to secondary fracture prevention were included, with priority given to 2024 to 2026 publications. Selection was purposive; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled statistical analysis was performed.

FINDINGS: The evidence base comprised 103 publications and one trial-registry record. Subsequent fractures consistently clustered within the first 12 to 24 months after an index fracture. A pooled meta-analysis of bisphosphonate trials in postmenopausal osteoporosis estimated 12.4 months (95% CI, 6.3 to 18.4 months) to prevent one nonvertebral fracture per 100 treated women; this population-level estimate is not a drug-specific onset threshold and was not derived specifically from recent-fracture patients. Several injectable antiresorptive and bone-forming therapies show early fracture-risk reduction in pivotal trials, but treatment choice must remain safety qualified. In particular, romosozumab requires cardiovascular risk assessment because of the imbalance in serious cardiovascular events observed in ARCH and current labeling restrictions. Rare medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and denosumab-associated hypocalcemia in advanced chronic kidney disease are additional counseling and monitoring considerations. Treatment cessation is also time-sensitive, especially for denosumab because delayed dosing or discontinuation without follow-on therapy can lead to rebound bone turnover and vertebral fractures.

IMPLICATIONS: Secondary fracture prevention may be improved by initiating appropriate therapy promptly after the index fracture, matching treatment characteristics to the period of highest risk, planning sequential therapy from the outset, and minimizing delivery delays. The framework is hypothesis-generating and should not override drug-specific contraindications, local labeling, or individualized benefit-risk assessment. Prospective studies should test whether explicitly time-matched care reduces early re-fracture compared with conventional risk-stratified treatment.

articles.title: Evaluation of Inpatient Epoetin Alfa Dosing in Patients With Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Epoetin alfa labeling and clinical guidelines recommend weight-based dosing for the management of patients with anemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, fixed dosing continues to be used in inpatient practice, and comparative data in hospitalized populations are limited. This study aimed to compare fixed versus weight-based dosing in hospitalized patients with CKD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included hospitalized adult patients with anemia of CKD who were initiated on epoetin alfa at a large academic medical center between January 2014 and August 2024. The primary outcome was hemoglobin exceeding targets (>10 g/dL for non-dialysis-dependent CKD and >11 g/dL for dialysis-dependent CKD). Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, rehospitalization, major adverse cardiovascular events, packed red blood cell transfusion, new or worsening hypertension, and iron deficiency.

FINDINGS: Among 100 patients (50 in the fixed-dose group and 50 in the weight-based dose group), hemoglobin exceeded targets in 8% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.678). Ninety-day all-cause mortality occurred in 18% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.160); no statistically significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Fixed-dose regimens resulted in higher weight-normalized epoetin alfa doses than weight-based dosing (119.8 vs 67.1 units/kg; P < 0.001).

IMPLICATIONS: Among hospitalized patients with CKD, fixed-dose epoetin alfa was associated with substantially higher weight-normalized doses and numerically higher rates of hemoglobin exceeding targets and mortality, though differences in clinical outcomes were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that adherence to guideline-recommended weight-based dosing may minimize excessive epoetin alfa dosing. Larger prospective studies are needed to clarify optimal inpatient erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing.

articles.title: Comparative risk of incident Clostridioides difficile infection with vedolizumab versus anti‑TNF in ulcerative colitis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The comparative risk of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) between vedolizumab (VDZ) and anti-TNF in ulcerative colitis (UC) is unclear.

AIMS: To compare incidence densities (IDs) and risks of CDI and C. difficile nucleic acid positivity between UC receiving VDZ versus anti-TNF.

METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients receiving VDZ or anti-TNF (Nov 2020-Oct 2024) with negative baseline C. difficile tests. IDs and incidence density ratios (IDRs) were calculated. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using marginal structural Cox models.

RESULTS: Of 214 patients, 156 received VDZ (202 PY) and 58 anti-TNF (53 PY). CDI occurred in 22 on VDZ (10.89/100 PY) and 8 on anti-TNF (15.09/100 PY), IDR = 0.71 (p = 0.427). C. difficile positivity occurred in 33 on VDZ (16.34/100 PY) and 8 on anti-TNF (15.09/100 PY), IDR = 1.07 (p = 0.841). Adjusted HRs for CDI and positivity were 0.95 (95 % CI: 0.41-2.22, p = 0.907) and 1.40 (95 % CI: 0.62-3.19, p = 0.417), respectively. Sensitivity analysis in biologic-naïve patients gave consistent results.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in CDI or C. difficile positivity risk were detected between VDZ and anti‑TNF in UC. Wide confidence intervals preclude definitive conclusions, and the observed signals require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Concomitant reconstruction of the nose and upper lip using an extensive paramedian frontal flap: A technical note.
articles.journal: Annales de chirurgie plastique et esthetique
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The paramedian forehead flap (PFF), based on the supratrochlear artery, is a ``gold standard'' for nasal reconstruction due to its robust vascularity and excellent color and texture match. However, its use for simultaneous reconstruction of both nose and upper lip following trauma or oncological resection has not been previously reported.

OBJECTIVE: This technique aims to describe an extensive PFF incorporating both forehead and scalp tissues, enabling concomitant reconstruction of the nose and upper lip.

MATERIAL AND METHOD: The procedure involves at least three stages. The first stage includes harvesting an extensive skin paddle with a scalp segment to reconstruct the hair-bearing upper lip. The second stage involves in initial flap weaning to release the lip and fold the flap for nasal reconstruction. The third stage consists of complete weaning of the nasal portion of the flap.

RESULTS: Two patients underwent this technique. Both achieved adequate tissue volume, with good color and texture match for the nose and a natural hair-bearing lip. Complications included partial flap necrosis in one case, and a delay in adjuvant radiotherapy was observed for the same patient.

DISCUSSION: Key challenges include minimizing infection risk and avoiding delays in adjuvant radiotherapy. While this innovative approach shows promise, further refinements such as strategic cartilage grafting and accelerated flap weaning, are required to optimize both functional and aesthetic outcomes.

articles.title: Sex differences in lipid-lowering therapy after atherothrombotic ischemic stroke: The multicenter MaLIC study.
authors: en representación de los investigadores del estudio MaLIC
articles.journal: Clinica e investigacion en arteriosclerosis : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Arteriosclerosis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women have poorer outcomes after ischaemic stroke. The primary objective was to assess sex-based differences in the management and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy following non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA). Secondary objectives were to analyse sex-based differences in vascular risk profile, pre-event functional status, and stroke severity.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Subanalysis of the second phase of the MaLIC study (Management of Stroke in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands), a prospective, multicentre study conducted in 20 hospitals. Adults with non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or TIA were included. Vascular risk factors, stroke severity, lipid profile, and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy at hospital discharge were compared according to sex.

RESULTS: A total of 591 patients were included, of whom 223 (37.7%) were women. Women were older (76 vs. 70 years; P<.0001), had greater pre-event functional dependence (mRS>2: 16.1% vs. 7.9%; P=.003), and a lower prevalence of ischaemic heart disease (4.9% vs. 14.4%; P<0001) and peripheral arterial disease (6.3% vs. 13.0%; P=.01). Although women had higher LDL cholesterol levels at admission (103.5 vs. 92mg/dl; P=.004), they were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge (64.1% vs. 72.3%; P=.04). No differences were observed in stroke code activation or reperfusion therapies.

CONCLUSIONS: Women were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge than men, despite having higher LDL cholesterol levels. These findings highlight an opportunity to optimise lipid-lowering therapy after the cerebrovascular event.

articles.title: Parent perspectives on the potential use of smart inhalers for asthma management in children: a qualitative interview study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract: Achieving adequate adherence to preventer medication remains a challenge in the management of paediatric asthma. A minimum of 75% adherence is recommended to achieve adequate clinical control, however actual adherence rates are often lower and are influenced by the unpredictability of family life and competing demands. Smart inhalers aim to support adherence to preventer medications by monitoring use and providing medication reminders, as well as tracking reliever use. This study explored the perceptions of parents of children aged 5-9 years with recent uncontrolled asthma regarding the potential usefulness of smart inhalers to manage their children's asthma, and perceived barriers and facilitators to their use. Semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom with parents residing in New South Wales, Australia. Interviews explored parents' perspectives about barriers to asthma management, awareness and perceived need for smart inhalers, desired features and functionalities, attitudes towards data sharing, perceived support requirements and cost considerations. Data were analysed using a hybrid inductive analysis approach. Ten parents participated (children aged 5-8); none had previously used a smart inhaler to manage their child's asthma. Overall attitudes toward smart inhalers were positive. Four primary themes were identified: perceived benefits of smart inhalers, including access to reliable medication data to share with healthcare providers; barriers to adoption, including concerns about technology difficulties; cost considerations with affordability influencing the likelihood of uptake; and implementation needs including the need for support for initial set up. Parents generally viewed smart inhalers as a promising tool for managing childhood asthma. Study findings suggest that successful implementation will require consideration of cost, ease of use, and adequate support for use.

articles.title: Carotid Body Detection Rate and Size on Photon-Counting Versus Energy-Integrating Detector CT.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the carotid body (CB) detection rate and size measured on photon-counting CT (PCCT) versus energy-integrating detector CT (EIDCT), and to evaluate the effects of laterality and contrast phase.

METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at a single institution on 48 adult patients who underwent head and neck CTA on both PCCT and EIDCT on arterial and venous phase imaging. CB detection was analyzed as a binary outcome using a mixed-effects logistic regression model with modality, phase, side, and modality-by-phase interaction as fixed effects, and patient as a random effect. CB size was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with the same fixed effects and patient as a random effect. Sensitivity analysis for CB size adjusted for age, sex, and hypertension.

RESULTS: CB detection rates were higher on PCCT than on EIDCT, particularly on the right side (arterial, 96% vs 77%; venous, 96% vs 82%), and slightly higher on the left side (arterial, 85% vs 81%; venous, 83% vs 82%). In mixed-effects logistic regression, PCCT was associated with higher odds of CB detection than EIDCT (OR, 3.97; P = .009). CB size was significantly smaller when measured on PCCT than on EIDCT (estimated difference, -2.7 mm³; P = .01). The right CB was larger than the left across modalities (estimated difference, +4.7 mm³; P < .001). There was no significant difference in CB measurements between arterial and venous phases (P = .53), and no significant modality-by-phase interaction (P = .98). In sensitivity analysis, the modality and side effects remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and hypertension.

CONCLUSION: PCCT improves CB detection compared with EIDCT but yields smaller CB measurements. CB size is greater on the right than on the left, with minimal effect of contrast phase. These findings remained robust after adjustment for age, sex, and hypertension.

articles.title: Edaravone dexborneol for acute ischaemic stroke among patients undergoing endovascular treatment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) remains a major cause of disability and mortality worldwide. Endovascular treatment (EVT) is the standard of care for large vessel occlusion, yet a favourable neurological outcome is not achieved in all patients. Edaravone dexborneol (ED) has been proposed as an adjuvant therapy during EVT procedures. However, its clinical impact has not been systematically synthesized.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, Cochrane Central, and Embase were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized and non-randomized studies comparing ED versus non-ED (placebo) controls in AIS patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT) were included. The primary outcomes of this study were excellent and good neurological outcomes at 90 days, measured with the modified Rankin Scale. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed, with robust sensitivity analyses to explore heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Seven studies were included, of which three were randomized. For the primary outcomes, there was no significant difference in the proportion of patients with excellent (mRS 0-1: OR 1.14; 95% CI 0.95 to 1.36; p = 0.17) or good neurological outcome (mRS 0-2: OR 1.34; 95% CI 0.97 to 1.85; p = 0.08). The incidence of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) was similar between groups (OR 0.73; 95% CI 0.50 to 1.07; p = 0.11). Prediction intervals crossed the null for all efficacy outcomes. No significant differences were observed in mortality at 90 days (p = 0.51). However, in pooled adjusted analyses, ED was associated with a modest increase in good neurological outcome (aOR 1.46; 95% CI 1.13 to 1.90; p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Unadjusted analyses show no significant benefit of ED in reducing mortality, symptomatic bleeding events, or improving functional recovery. However, pooled adjusted estimates suggest a modest improvement in good neurological outcomes (mRS 0-2). Wide prediction intervals crossing the null indicate that the current evidence is preliminary, and confirmation in adequately powered trials is needed before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Wide dynamic range of contrast-encoding in neural responses in macaque V1.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The dynamic range of contrast-encoding in the early visual system has been investigated at both single-neuron and population levels in animals using oriented stimuli such as gratings and Gabor patches. However, contrast-encoding of unoriented stimuli such as Gaussians has been less explored, even though such stimuli can evoke a large population response. In studies that employ Gaussians, contrast response functions (CRFs) of neurons and neural populations in primary visual cortex are typically characterized across a limited range of Weber contrasts up to 100%, which may not adequately reflect the statistics of contrast in natural scenes. Indeed, our preliminary analysis shows that locations with center-surround contrasts far exceeding the level comparable to a Gaussian stimulus of 100% Weber contrast are ubiquitous in natural scenes. Thus, our current understanding of contrast encoding remains incomplete in the context of natural environments. Here, we measured spiking activities of individual neurons using electrophysiology and population responses using widefield calcium imaging in V1 of fixating male macaques (Macaca mulatta) while Gaussian stimuli were presented over a wide range of Weber contrasts, up to 900%. Both the average spiking response and the average population response continued to increase robustly above 100% Weber contrast. Only a small minority of neurons saturated below 100% Weber contrast. These results demonstrate that the dynamic range of contrast-encoding in V1 is broader than previously assumed and aligns more closely with the statistics of contrast in natural scenes.Significance Statement The dynamic range of contrast-encoding in V1 has typically been characterized using only a limited range of contrasts, often excluding the high contrasts commonly found in natural scenes. We measured contrast response functions of individual neurons and neural populations in V1 across a much wider range of contrasts. We found that the responses of the majority of neurons, as well as the overall population, increased robustly up to extremely high contrasts. These findings suggest that the dynamic range of contrast encoding in V1 extends well beyond the commonly tested range.

articles.title: Prefrontal ensembles represent freezing of conspecifics.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Social buffering is a process in which the presence of other members of the same species (conspecifics) decreases stress reactions during threat exposure. In parallel, prior reports showed that groups of individuals display synchronous actions in non-threatening situations. However, it is unknown if individuals also synchronize actions when facing threats. Prior studies showed social buffering of freezing in pairs of subjects. We now expand these findings and show social buffering of freezing during exposure to a predator and a shock grid in mice of both sexes in a larger group of four conspecifics. Furthermore, mice also displayed synchronized freezing. The presence of freezing synchrony suggests the existence of a neural representation of conspecific freezing. We reasoned that this encoding might be in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), as this region has been implicated in social behaviors and freezing. Strikingly, mPFC neural activity represented the average level of freezing across conspecifics. MPFC ensembles displayed differential encoding of self and conspecific freezing, and during predator exposure the mPFC encoded the number of conspecifics freezing and conspecific freezing bout duration. These data show, for the first time, neural representation of conspecific freezing, and suggest that the mPFC may coordinate behavioral responses to threat across conspecifics.Significance Statement Social animals display attenuated threat-elicited responses when encountering threats as a group. However, it is unknown how freezing signals from conspecifics are encoded by the brain when facing threats, as prior work has been limited to studies of pairs, or assays without social interactions. We identify a neural population in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) that represents conspecific freezing during grouped threat exposure, and these cells dynamically represent the duration of other animals' freezing bouts. Strikingly, the activity of these ensembles also represents the number of conspecifics freezing. These findings uncover a previously unknown function of the mPFC to encode conspecific freezing.

articles.title: Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion of londamocitinib after single-dose inhaled, intravenous and oral administration in healthy participants.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Londamocitinib (AZD4604) is an inhaled, selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor in development for asthma. This open-label, two-part, phase I clinical study (NCT06157255) used a radiolabelled microtracer approach to evaluate the absolute bioavailability and the absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) of inhaled londamocitinib after intravenous and oral administration in healthy male and female participants (n = 8).

METHODS: Pharmacokinetics, safety, metabolic profile and metabolite identification from plasma, urine, and faecal samples were assessed employing highly sensitive accelerator mass spectrometry. Participants received a single oral 4-mg dose of [14C]londamocitinib (NMT 37.0 kBq [14C]) in Part 1 and an intravenous 30-μg dose of [14C]londamocitinib (NMT 37.0 kBq [14C]), followed by a single inhaled dose of 3-mg londamocitinib in Part 2.

RESULTS: Mean recovery of total radioactive material after oral dosing was 76.3% in faeces and 8.7% in urine. After intravenous dosing, recovery was 67.3% in faeces and 16.0% in urine. Absolute bioavailability of oral londamocitinib was 40.4% and for inhaled administration was 62.5%. Unchanged londamocitinib constituted approximately 70% of circulating radioactivity in plasma and accounted for 47.8% and 28.4% of the administered dose in excreta after oral and intravenous administration respectively. No new safety signals were observed.

CONCLUSION: Following inhaled and oral dosing, londamocitinib demonstrated rapid absorption, and faecal excretion as the principal route of elimination. Unchanged londamocitinib and metabolite M6 were the major entities present in plasma, urine and faeces. Londamocitinib, at these doses, exhibited an acceptable safety and tolerability profile.

articles.title: Phase 1, open-label, randomized study of the elecoglipron pharmacokinetic profile in healthy participants under fed and fasted conditions.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Elecoglipron (AZD5004/ECC5004) is an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) in development for weight management in people living with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes. This study aimed to characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) profiles of two formulations of elecoglipron under fed and fasted conditions.

METHODS: We assessed the PK profiles, safety and tolerability of two formulations of elecoglipron, 50 mg, under fed and fasted conditions in healthy participants in a phase 1, open-label, randomized, single-dose, fixed-sequence, crossover study.

RESULTS: Of 23 participants screened, 14 were randomized to elecoglipron and 13 (92.9%) completed the study. The half-life for both formulations under fasted and fed conditions ranged between 20.7 and 21.2 h. Between the fed (reference) and fasted groups, geometric mean ratios (GMR) and 90% confidence intervals (CI) for the F1 formulation: area under the plasma-concentration curve (AUC) from time zero to the last measurement (AUC0-last) was 0.96 (0.82, 1.12), AUC from time zero extrapolated to infinity (AUC0-inf) was 0.95 (0.82, 1.11), and maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) was 1.15 (0.90, 1.46). Similar results were observed for F2 in the fed and fasted groups. Safety and tolerability were comparable for the two formulations. The most common AEs were gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, abdominal discomfort) and mostly mild in severity.

CONCLUSIONS: Elecoglipron demonstrated a PK profile supportive of once-daily dosing and may be administered under fed or fasted conditions. These findings support the continuing clinical development of elecoglipron. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06268145). The trial was first registered on 20 February 2024.

articles.title: The Smart MDI System in People With Type 1 Diabetes and High HBA1C: A Randomized Controlled Trial Demonstrating That Response to Alerts Drives Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The aim was to assess the efficacy and safety of the smart multiple daily injections (MDI) system versus MDI plus continuous glucose monitor (CGM) in people with Type 1 diabetes and HbA1c ≥ 8%.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: After a 3-week run-in, 143 participants were randomized to Smart MDI or MDI + CGM. The primary endpoint was between-group difference (Δ) in time-in-range (TIR) at 6 months, adjusted for baseline glycaemia and assessed for non-inferiority (margin 7.5%). Secondary endpoints included HbA1c (non-inferiority margin 0.4%) and superiority analyses for TIR and HbA1c. Smart MDI alerts prompt insulin bolus actions (in contrast to traditional CGM alerts), and post hoc analyses were performed to evaluate 'alert-responsiveness' on glycaemia. Alert-responsiveness findings were validated in a real-world cohort of 5507 users. Safety endpoints were assessed.

RESULTS: At 6 months, Δ TIR between groups was 0.19 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -4.9 to 5.3), thus meeting non-inferiority; HbA1c also met non-inferiority (Δ: -0.13 percentage points, -0.46 to 0.19) but neither showed superiority. Post hoc analyses showed higher responders to alerts (those responding more than the median response rate of 28.3%, n = 31) had greater TIR gains than lower responders (n = 28) (+8.12 percentage points; p = 0.04) and HbA1c reduction (-0.6 percentage points; p = 0.02). TIR benefits in higher responders were confirmed in the real-world cohort. One episode of diabetic ketoacidosis occurred (run-in) and one severe hypoglycaemic event occurred (control arm).

CONCLUSIONS: Smart MDI is safe and non-inferior, achieving non-inferiority to MDI + CGM regarding TIR and HbA1c. Responding to as few as 28% of alerts resulted in glycaemic improvements.

articles.title: Pharmacotherapeutic safety in patients with liver cirrhosis: a national multidisciplinary survey on resources and perceived needs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze, at a national and multidisciplinary level, the availability of resources, the level of knowledge, and the perceived needs of healthcare professionals in the management of patients with liver cirrhosis.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A national, multicenter, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted using a questionnaire aimed at medicine, pharmacy, and nursing professionals in primary care, hospital care, and community pharmacy. Professional profiles, the use of clinical decision support tools, and self-perceived training were evaluated. Qualitative variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. To assess national variability and differences by professional profiles, Pearson's ꭓ2test or Fisher's exact test was used, as appropriate.

RESULTS: A total of 275 responses were analyzed (94% national coverage). A marked polarization in healthcare delivery and a low availability of local protocols (12.7%) were detected, with significant gaps between hospital and primary care settings. Critical deficiencies were highlighted in training (only 5.1% perceived themselves as fully trained), lack of computerized safety alerts (30.5%), and absence of patient educational materials (77.8%). There is a majority demand (91.6%) for quick-reference clinical management guidelines.

CONCLUSIONS: The pharmacotherapeutic management of liver cirrhosis is limited by a critical lack of specialized training and support tools. The almost unanimous demand for resources justifies the urgent need to implement clinical decision support systems to optimize patient safety.

articles.title: Multiplexed protease activity profiling for host response-based Sepsis diagnosis.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Human proteases play major roles in various pathological conditions, including dysregulated immune responses in sepsis, making them strong candidates for developing diagnostic markers. Despite this potential, the process of developing protease-based diagnostic tools has remained slow due to significant technical barriers associated with measuring protease activity, mainly stemming from the vast diversity of human proteases and the lack of substrate specificity, which complicates the interpretation of activity profiles. In this work, we advanced the current state of assay development by engineering substrate molecules and implementing an analytical approach based on mass spectrometry. Specifically, we developed a novel approach to chemically modify protease substrates for human neutrophil elastase (HNE) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) to enhance specificity and generate unique mass-to-charge signatures, allowing the deconvolution of protease activities. We then integrated the modified substrates into a mass spectrometry-based platform for quantifying multiple protease activities within a single analytical run. We applied the assay to spared plasma samples and demonstrated that the assay detects distinct protease activity profiles. We further demonstrated that the assay achieved a diagnostic sensitivity of 88% and specificity of 87% for sepsis detection within a three-hour timeframe. ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY: We developed a novel multiplexed protease activity profiling approach to quantify immune responses and improve sepsis diagnosis.

articles.title: Prenatal Maternal Phosphatidylcholine and Children's Behavior and Cognition through 4 Years of Age: Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. Rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7, associated with Schizophrenia, Attention Deficit Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7, convey risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and increase cognitive performance.

STUDY DESIGN: A clinical trial at University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by parents on the Child Behavior Check List 1.5-5-year version (CBCL1.5-5yr). The 2 primary outcomes were Withdrawn and Attention Problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-IV Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (Full Scale-IQ). Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed phosphatidylcholine's fetal developmental effects.

RESULTS: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared to placebo produced fewer children with multiple or pervasive Withdrawn problems and increased WPPSI-IV Full-Scale IQ (mean difference 7.78, 95% CI 1.88, 13.7; p = .010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly. In exploratory analyses, 11 children had CBCL1.5-5yr Autism Spectrum T-scores in the clinical referral range and language deficits typical of Autism Spectrum Disorder, 10 of 71 from women who had placebo and 1 of 71 who had phosphatidylcholine, Risk Ratio 10.0; 95% CI 1.31, 76.1; p = .026. Twelve children had Full-Scale IQ > 120 (>90 %ile), 10 of 54 from women who had phosphatidylcholine and 2 of 49 who had placebo, Risk Ratio 4.54; 95% CI 1.05, 19.7; p = .044. Positive effects were observed regardless of presence or absence of maternal mental disorders. Phosphatidylcholine produced no significant adverse effects or safety problems for women or children. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypertension were not increased. The children had normal physical parameters at birth and through childhood. Several limitations temper the study's findings: effects on Attention problems did not reach significance, parents rated social behavior, and one-third of women were lost between prenatal enrollment and 4-year assessments.

CONCLUSION: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements provide safe, effective support of fetal brain development. Comparison of doses from this and previous trials suggests 6300 mg phosphatidylcholine or 900 mg choline, beginning as early as possible in gestation. Outcomes for the children include fewer social withdrawal problems and increased cognitive test performance.

articles.title: Human Antibody Responses to Group A Streptococcus Infection: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) is a leading global cause of infectious disease morbidity and mortality. A major barrier to GAS vaccine development is our incomplete understanding of human immunity. We undertook, to our knowledge, the first systematic review describing human antibody responses following GAS infection.

METHODS: Eligible studies were publications reporting human antibody responses to any GAS antigen in individuals with microbiologically confirmed GAS infection. Case reports and studies primarily describing post-streptococcal autoimmune complications were excluded. Databases were last searched on 15th November 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the relevant tools from the Joanna Briggs Institute. Results are presented in narrative form as meta-analysis was not appropriate.

RESULTS: A total of 143 studies spanning 1948-2025 met inclusion criteria. Most studies (83%) were conducted in the Global North and focused on tonsillopharyngitis (79·4%). Antibody responses were measured in serum (99·3%) and/or saliva (2·1%), targeting 116 distinct GAS antigens. The proportion of individuals exhibiting an antibody response to five antigens (SLO, DNase B, GAC, M protein and Streptokinase) was significantly greater in cases when compared with healthy controls. In longitudinal studies, the peak antibody titres were detected at a median of 28 days post-infection. Higher pre-infection titres of some antibodies (M protein, SpyCEP, SpyAD, SLO, DNase B, SpnA, T25, K4S2) correlated with subsequent protection from GAS infection or reduced severity of disease in three separate studies. Heterogeneity across studies prevented clear conclusions regarding how post-infection antibody responses vary by GAS serotype, participant age, infection site, or disease severity.

CONCLUSIONS: This review synthesizes 77 years of heterogenous studies describing antibody responses to GAS infection. Limitations of this review arise from the heterogeneity between studies and study risk of bias. Despite this, we identify major gaps in our understanding of the magnitude, kinetics, and protective role of antibody responses. Our synthesis uncovers information that will support GAS vaccine development including: guidance on sampling time points and the identification of antibodies that may be associated with protection from disease, as well as the need for standardisation of laboratory methodology and minimally-biased antigen discovery approaches.

articles.title: Predicting Failure to Rescue After Surgery for Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy: An ACS-NSQIP Analysis (2015-2020).
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Failure to rescue (FTR), defined as 30-day mortality among patients who experienced a major complication, has emerged as a quality metric in spine surgery. Recent FTR analyses report high discrimination using prediction models combining pre- and postoperative variables into a single model. Whether this performance reflects true preoperative risk stratification or the inclusion of peri-mortality events as predictors remains unknown.

PURPOSE: To identify predictors of FTR in patients undergoing surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and compare the discrimination of preoperative-only versus combined preoperative-postoperative models.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database from 2015-2020.

PATIENT SAMPLE: 19,108 adult patients undergoing cervical decompression and/or fusion for DCM. 938 (4.9%) experienced a major complication and formed the FTR cohort.

OUTCOME MEASURES: FTR, defined as 30-day all-cause mortality among patients who experienced a major complication within 30 days of surgery.

METHODS: Two multivariable logistic regression models predicted FTR in the complicated cohort: Model A (preoperative variables only) and Model B (preoperative variables plus composite postoperative complication categories: cardiopulmonary, septic/wound, and other). Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap iterations with optimism correction.

RESULTS: Of 19,108 DCM surgical patients, 938 had a major postoperative complication, and 48 (5.1%) experienced FTR. FTR patients demonstrated higher Risk Analysis Index (RAI) scores (median 25 in FTR vs. 22 in rescued; p=0.005), diabetes prevalence (54.2% vs. 32.4%; p=0.003), and preoperative septic shock (12.5% vs. 3.3%; p=0.004). Model A identified RAI (OR 1.07 per point; 95% CI 1.03-1.12), diabetes (OR 2.18; 95% CI 1.18-4.01), and preoperative septic shock (OR 3.22; 95% CI 1.21-8.56) as independent predictors (corrected C-statistic 0.670). Model B identified cardiopulmonary complications as the strongest predictor (OR 35.4; 95% CI 8.27-151.6), while RAI (OR 1.06; 95% CI 1.02-1.10; p=0.003) and diabetes (OR 2.01; 95% CI 1.08-3.72; p=0.027) remained independent predictors. Model B significantly outperformed Model A (corrected C-statistic 0.816; bootstrap ΔC 0.119, 95% CI 0.042-0.189; DeLong p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Among DCM patients who experienced a major complication, frailty, diabetes, and preoperative septic shock were associated with FTR with modest discrimination. Discrimination improved significantly with the addition of postoperative complications, particularly cardiopulmonary events. These findings support frailty-based preoperative risk stratification and identify cardiopulmonary surveillance as a key FTR mitigation target.

articles.title: A Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Outbreak in an Intensive Care Unit: Detection Before Recognition and Persistence After Containment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We analyzed a carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) outbreak in an intensive care unit (ICU) to improve insight into how this pathogen spreads within health care facilities and to inform the development of targeted control procedures.

METHODS: A CRAB outbreak in a tertiary referral center was investigated over a 5-month window with clinical data, molecular typing (AP-PCR, PFGE), and one month of environmental sampling. All ICU patients (n=31) were compared-epidemic-clone-positive (n=7) versus -negative (n=24)-using Mann-Whitney/Fisher tests and Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: Although the outbreak spanned 6 days clinically, index patients had been colonized up to 41 days earlier. CRAB was recovered from high-touch surfaces; 6/7 patients developed pneumonia/VAP and 6/7 died (4 CRAB-attributable). Prior A. baumannii isolation (57% vs 0%) was the only independent risk factor (Firth odds ratio 34.7; P=.004). Despite treatment, infected patients redeveloped epidemic-clone infection up to 3.5 months later.

CONCLUSIONS: In CRAB outbreaks, spread may begin weeks before clinical recognition, and-even months after the outbreak is contained-the epidemic clone can cause reinfection in previously treated patients; only high-resolution analyses spanning an extended period can document this. Multidisciplinary and administrative collaboration, extended and effective environmental disinfection, and effective isolation of positive patients are important for containing CRAB outbreaks.

articles.title: Feasibility of an Activity Control System in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Results from a Non-Randomised Controlled Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a disease that requires continuous, active management by the patient, encompassing lifestyle and activities of daily living (ADL). There is limited evidence and a scarcity of devices that monitor ADL in patients with DM using artificial intelligence-based technology. This study evaluates the feasibility of the AI2EPD home activity monitoring system, focusing on therapeutic adherence in the treatment of people with DM2.

METHODS: A pilot-controlled study was conducted. Vibration and motion sensors were placed in the home, and physical activity bracelets were worn, together with an Artificial Intelligence web system. The following scales were used for evaluation: System Usability Scale (SUS), Morisky-Green Test, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), Spanish version of the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities Measure (SDSCA-Sp), Diabetes Knowledge Questionnaire (DKQ-24), International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and EuroQol 5D.

RESULTS: Twenty-one participants were included (10 in the intervention group and 11 in the control group). The clinical results were similar for both groups. The intervention group found the system easy to use and safe, indicating high acceptance. No clinical benefit attributable to the intervention was demonstrated. The only statistically significant within-group improvement in HbA1c was observed in the control group; however, given the pilot nature of the study and the multiple exploratory comparisons, this finding should be interpreted with caution.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of the AI2EPD intelligent remote monitoring system in the home was feasible and well accepted by participants. Exploratory findings regarding therapeutic adherence and clinical outcomes warrant further evaluation in adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Association of Occupational Noise Exposure with Hypertension and the Mediating Role of Metabolic Dysregulation: A Combined Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence linking occupational noise to hypertension remains inconsistent, and potential metabolic pathways are insufficiently characterised.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 70,759 workers in Jiangsu Province and a retrospective five-year cohort analysis of 2,188 workers. We combined multivariable regression, machine-learning prediction, mediation analysis, and longitudinal modelling to examine associations and potential pathways.

RESULTS: Hypertension prevalence was 28.19%. Compared with unexposed workers, noise exposure of 70-< 85 dB(A) and 85-< 90 dB(A) was associated with higher hypertension odds (OR = 1.16 and 1.21, p < 0.001), whereas the association at ≥ 90 dB(A) was not significant after adjustment. XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance (AUC=0.84), with metabolic indicators including triglycerides, glucose, and γ-glutamyl transferase ranking among the important predictors, while noise exposure also contributed to prediction. Mediation analyses identified potential indirect pathways involving γ-glutamyl transferase, glucose, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the association between occupational noise exposure and systolic blood pressure. Longitudinal analyses showed delayed divergence in metabolic markers and larger systolic blood pressure differences during the later follow-up period.

CONCLUSIONS: Occupational noise exposure was associated with elevated blood pressure even at levels below the Chinese occupational noise exposure limit of 85 dB(A) for an 8-hour working day, which is primarily intended to prevent noise-induced hearing loss. The findings are consistent with a potential role of oxidative stress-related glucose and lipid metabolic dysregulation in this association. Future occupational health strategies should incorporate longitudinal metabolic surveillance to mitigate noise-induced risks in exposed populations.
