articles.title: Exploratory chromosome 14-focused transcriptomic profiling of PSEN1-associated familial Alzheimer's disease across brain regions.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Proteins and proteomics
articles.abstract: Familial Alzheimer's disease (FAD) is an inherited form of early-onset Alzheimer's disease associated with pathogenic variants in presenilin 1 (PSEN1). To explore chromosome 14-associated transcriptional patterns in FAD across anatomically distinct brain regions, publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) datasets from frontal cortex, temporal cortex, and whole-brain samples were analyzed. Because one FAD sample and one control sample were available for each brain region, expression differences were evaluated descriptively using observed log₂ fold-change values rather than conventional inferential differential-expression statistics. Functional annotation and protein-protein interaction analyses were subsequently used to provide biological context for the observed expression patterns. Distinct regional expression patterns were observed within the chromosome 14-focused dataset. Higher expression was observed for representative genes including FITM1, IFI27, AHSA1, and NFKBIA in the frontal cortex, and DHRS4L2, ESR2, GPR65, EFCAB11, and HOMEZ in the temporal cortex. The observed expression patterns were associated with inflammatory, cellular stress, metabolic, receptor-mediated, proteostatic, and neuronal signaling-related functions. Network analysis was used to contextualize these expression patterns rather than to infer causal regulatory relationships. Five representative proteins-NFKBIA, ESR2, GPR65, AHSA1, and IFI27-were further examined structural information to provide structural context for selected transcriptomic observations. Given the absence of biological replication and the chromosome 14-focused design, these findings should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Independent replicated cohorts and complementary transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional studies are required to determine the reproducibility and biological relevance of the observed patterns.

articles.title: Tongsai Granules Ameliorate Airway Mucus Hypersecretion in AECOPD by Remodeling LIPA-Driven Ceramide Metabolism.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed.

RESULTS: TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC.

CONCLUSION: TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

articles.title: Visualization of post-STEMI myocardial infarction and microvascular obstruction with non-contrast, free-breathing whole- heart iT2prep-IR BOOST.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT2prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR.

METHODS: A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT2prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes. Sixty-four STEMI patients underwent CMR, including iT2prep-IR BOOST, clinical T2-STIR, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and T1/T2 mapping. The diagnostic performance of iT2prep-IR BOOST was evaluated against LGE and T2-STIR to assess myocardial infarction (MI), microvascular obstruction (MVO), and edema. Subgroup analyses further investigated the association between MVO detected by iT2prep-IR BOOST and left ventricular (LV) remodeling at 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: In 60 STEMI patients, the acquisition was completed in 7.2 ± 0.6min as a single free-breathing 3D whole-heart scan. Patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity for MVO (100.0% / 87.5%) and segmental MVO detection (95.8% / 97.8%). T2prep-IR BOOST yielded robust image contrast for MI comparable to LGE, while offering comparable edema visualization to T2-STIR. Volumetric and transmurality quantifications of MVO, MI, and edema showed excellent agreement with reference standards (all r > 0.90, p < 0.001), supported by significant biophysical correlations with native T1/T2 values (p < 0.001). Furthermore, in a 1-year follow-up cohort (n=51), baseline T2prep-IR BOOST-derived MVO volume was associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, showing significant correlations with both ΔLVEDVI (r = 0.305, p = 0.029) and ΔLVESVI (r = 0.293, p = 0.037).

CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary single-center study, iT2prep-IR BOOST showed promising diagnostic performance and close quantitative agreement with conventional LGE and T2-STIR in stable STEMI patients. Further prospective validation in larger, independent, and more heterogeneous cohorts, including patients unable to undergo contrast-enhanced CMR, is required before this technique can be considered an alternative to standard LGE and T2-weighted sequences.

articles.title: Endovascular Salvage of Dysfunctional Native Haemodialysis Arteriovenous Fistulas: Clinical Outcomes and Predictors of Patency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas are an important cause of inadequate dialysis, access failure and morbidity in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and timely catheter-based intervention may help restore access function and prolong fistula usability.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy, feasibility, and safety of catheter-based interventional procedures for hypofunctioning haemodialysis fistulas in patients with CKD.

METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational follow up study, enrolled with 100 CKD patients on maintenance haemodialysis with dysfunctional native arteriovenous fistulas who underwent fistulogram and catheter-based intervention.

RESULTS: The mean age was 57.2 ± 12.4 years, 62.0% were male, and hypertension (80.0%) and diabetes mellitus (57.0%) were the major comorbidities. Radio cephalic fistula was the commonest access type (46.0%), and inadequate dialysis was the leading presentation (73.0%). Fistulography showed significant stenosis in 96.0%, with central vein involvement in 43.0% and long-segment lesions in 56.0%. Angioplasty was attempted in 96.0%, achieving technical success in 91.7% of attempted interventions and clinical success in 85.0%. Stenosis and pressure gradient reduced significantly after intervention (both p<0.001). Complications occurred in 13.0%, with no deaths. Primary patency declined from 82.0% at 1 month to 58.0% at 6 months and 38.0% at 12 months. Patency loss was independently predicted by older age, central vein lesions, long lesions, residual stenosis, and absent post-procedure thrill.

CONCLUSION: Catheter-based endovascular intervention may be an effective fistula-salvage strategy for hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas, although long-term patency was influenced by lesion complexity, residual stenosis and restoration of post-procedure thrill.

articles.title: Design of Screening Cardiometabolic Opportunities Using Transformative Echocardiography Artificial Intelligence (SCOUT-Echo-AI).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent among individuals with cardiovascular disease, but often remains undiagnosed until advanced sequelae such as fibrotic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma develop. ​​Transthoracic echocardiography routinely captures incidental subcostal views of the liver that are not used clinically. The EchoNet-Liver algorithm uses artificial intelligence (AI) to predict the presence of liver disease based on routine clinical echocardiograms. Prospective evaluation in real-world practice is needed to understand the clinical utility and impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening.

METHODS: The SCOUT-Echo-AI study is a single-arm, prospective, multicenter, open-label pragmatic interventional trial that will be conducted across six diverse U.S. healthcare systems (Kaiser Permanente Northern California, Stanford Healthcare, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, University of California Los Angeles, Northwestern Medicine, and Massachusetts General Brigham). Routine echocardiograms will be analyzed by the EchoNet-Liver AI algorithm with an estimated enrollment of ∼3,000 patients. Treating clinicians or participants themselves will be notified of potential undiagnosed liver disease with site-specific workflows in place to ensure routine clinical care for definitive case confirmation. Primary outcomes will be SLD and fibrotic liver disease detection rates and positive predictive values within 12 months of AI identification. Pre-specified secondary outcomes will assess diagnostic accuracy against other gold-standard modalities, treatment initiation, time to diagnosis, and impact on other clinical events. Outcomes will be compared against historical usual-care and contemporary below-threshold cohorts.

CONCLUSION: SCOUT-Echo-AI is a prospective multicenter study evaluating the real-world impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening using routine echocardiography.

articles.title: Open or closed? Structural characterization of plasma-derived and recombinant human plasminogen across multiple resolution scales.
articles.abstract: Plasminogen (Plg), the zymogen of the fibrinolytic protease plasmin, is a multidomain, conformationally rich protein that plays a crucial role in targeted thrombolysis for stroke and heart attack treatments. Yet, the conformational state that affects binding to Plg activators and fibrinolytic activity is rarely validated, contributing to poor reproducibility and failures in drug development. Here, we establish a structural biology workflow to characterize human Plg suspended in an aqueous solution, preserving it in a near-native state and eliminating the need for crystal growth. Two variants, cleavage-resistant Plg-RV (R561A) and catalytically inactive Plg-CAT (S741A), were expressed in mammalian cells. Both variants showed comparable global secondary structure and thermal stability (Tm ≈ 60.6 °C) and were resistant to staphylokinase-mediated activation, in contrast to commercial plasma-derived Plg. Small-angle X-ray scattering revealed substantial conformational heterogeneity, and hydrogen‑deuterium exchange mass spectrometry mapped SAK-associated local structural changes. The recombinantly-produced Plg variants adopted a closed conformation, exhibiting a good fit to the closed structure determined by X-ray diffraction. Conversely, the plasma-derived Plg populated an extended, open-like state. Cryo-EM analysis of the Plg-RV variant yielded a 4.4 Å resolution map, and a rigid-body-fitted model revealed the closed-state architecture. Our findings demonstrate that rigorous structural validation of Plg is essential for future functional studies and rational development of next-generation thrombolytic agents.

articles.title: Gal-3 N-terminal prolines within residues 69 to 117 regulate CRD glycan binding, phase separation and Gal-3-mediated cellular function.
articles.abstract: Galectin-3 (Gal-3), the only chimeric galectin, is a central driver and potential biomarker for cancer progression, fibrotic disorders, and heart failure. As a key proinflammatory factor, Gal-3 aggravates various disease states by promoting immune cell activation, cytokine storm amplification, and cell migration. Previously, we reported on the structural and functional role of prolines within Gal-3 NT residues 1-68. Here, we report on how the 14 NT prolines within the 69-117 segment affect Gal-3 structure and function. Circular dichroism (CD) and fluorescence spectroscopies showed that none of these proline-to-alanine substitutions altered overall Gal-3 conformation, whereas some of them did modulate glycoprotein-induced phase separation and ligand binding (lactose (Lac), LacNAc, (LacNAc)3), as well as Gal-3-mediated cell function, i.e., cell activation, hemagglutination, and endocytosis. Three of these prolines were found to be the most crucial to Gal-3-mediated activities, with P86A and P113A attenuating glycan-binding, glycoprotein-induced phase separation, and cellular function and P117A enhancing these processes. Correlation analysis of all prolines within the Gal-3 NT revealed that prolines within the 1-68 segment primarily modulate cellular function via glycan binding, whereas prolines within the 69-117 segment modulate glycan-induced phase separation and cellular function. Overall, our findings reveal distinct functional roles for specific Gal-3 NT prolines, provide mechanistic insight into Gal-3 structure-function relationships, and identify potential NT prolines as targets for ameliorating various Gal-3-related pathological disorders.

articles.title: Dual-functional hydrogel capable of scavenging reactive oxygen species and regulating macrophage polarization for repairing MRSA-infected wounds.
articles.abstract: The healing of infected wounds presents a remarkable clinical challenge owing to bacterial infection-induced oxidative stress and persistent inflammation. To address these issues, a multifunctional hydrogel was prepared by means of Schiff base crosslinking between oxidized konjac glucomannan (OKGM) and sericin, followed by the incorporation of polydopamine nanoparticles (PDA NPs). The OKGM/Sericin-PDA NPs (KSP) hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant capacity, facilitating macrophage polarization to the M2 phenotype. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the KSP hydrogel exerted immunomodulatory effect by activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Furthermore, the KSP hydrogel exhibited photothermal properties, thereby demonstrating potent antibacterial efficacy against both Escherichia coli (E. coli) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Significantly, in a murine model of full-thickness wounds infected with MRSA, the hydrogel combined with near-infrared irradiation demonstrated remarkable antibacterial activity and anti-inflammation, contributing to accelerating wounds healing by reducing bacterial load and regulating the wound immune microenvironment. In summary, these results indicate that the KSP hydrogel serves as a promising multifunctional dressing, offering an effective clinical approach for repairing and regenerating full-thickness infected wounds.

articles.title: Heart Transplantation in Adult Fontan Patients: New Insights from Fontan-Associated Liver Disease Beyond Traditional Predictors.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan patients are considered high risk for heart transplantation (HT) owing to their complex anatomy, multiple prior chest entries, and universal Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD). The impact of FALD and other preoperative factors remains, however, uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: We sought to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality after isolated HT in adults with Fontan circulation, with particular focus on the relationship between liver-related parameters and post-transplant outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of all adult Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT was conducted. Factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using appropriate univariate analyses and penalized multivariable logistic regression. ROC analysis was used to derive liver size cut-offs and compare the discriminative performance of selected variables. A descriptive analysis of adult Fontan patients undergoing combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT) was also performed for contextual comparison.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients (mean age 30 years) underwent isolated HT; 19% (n=8) died within 90 days. Factors associated with increased 90-day mortality were >4 previous chest entries, major perioperative bleeding, and small liver size [total liver volume (TLV) ≤1366 mL, total liver volume indexed to body surface area (TLVi) <786 mL/m2 and liver transverse dimension (LTD) <21 cm]. Multiple chest veno-venous collaterals, >4 previous chest entries, and small liver were strongly associated with bleeding and subsequent fatal complications including sepsis, graft dysfunction, and bowel ischaemia. Within the study period, five other patients had undergone CHLT. All had biopsy confirmed advanced liver disease with features of clinically significant portal hypertension or hepatocellular carcinoma. One patient died within 90 days following prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass, major bleeding, graft dysfunction and sepsis, culminating in multiorgan failure.

CONCLUSIONS: In Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT, >4 previous chest entries, major bleeding, and small liver volume were associated with increased 90-day mortality. Objective liver metrics (TLV ≤1366 mL, TLVi <786 mL/m2, TLD <21 cm) may provide adjunctive risk stratification for Fontan patients considered for isolated HT; however, these measures and proposed thresholds remain exploratory and require external validation. CHLT is a viable option, although non-liver related transplant risk factors may similarly influence outcomes. Detailed liver assessment and management at experienced, high-volume congenital transplant centres are important to optimizing outcomes in this complex population.

articles.title: The new landscape of liver transplantation: Evolving candidates, new technologies, and personalized care.
articles.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is entering a new era shaped by changes in disease epidemiology, candidate complexity, donor utilization, and post-transplant management. The decline of viral hepatitis-related cirrhosis, together with the rise of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma, has transformed the LT waitlist into an older, frailer, and more cardiometabolically complex population. At the same time, donation after circulatory death and machine perfusion are expanding the donor pool and redefining the boundaries of graft suitability. Candidate selection is also moving beyond traditional diagnosis-based criteria, with increasing acceptance of early LT for carefully selected alcohol-related liver disease, utility-based transplantation for acute-on-chronic liver failure, and biology-driven transplant oncology, in which HCC is established whereas selected iCCA and unresectable CRLM indications remain investigational. In parallel, artificial intelligence and machine learning are being developed as decision-support tools for candidate assessment, waitlist prioritization, donor-recipient matching, and prediction of post-transplant outcomes; prospective validation and evidence of clinical impact remain limited. Immunosuppression is facing a similar transformation, shifting from standardized lifelong exposure toward individualized, monitored minimization and immunologic risk profiling, while complete withdrawal and operational tolerance remain restricted to highly selected recipients within specialized protocols. In this Perspective, we argue that the future of LT will depend on integrating biological reserve, disease behavior, graft quality, and expected survival benefit into transparent, multidisciplinary decision-making. The central challenge will be to translate innovation into durable clinical benefit while preserving equity in access to transplantation.

articles.title: Individualized Prediction of Patient-Defined Treatment Success to Support Patient-Centered Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Clinical prediction models often target generic thresholds for treatment success, such as the Minimal Important Change. The Personal Meaningful Gain was introduced as a personalized threshold, capturing the improvement an individual seeks to achieve in a self-chosen domain to become satisfied with the treatment results. This study developed and internally validated a treatment-conditional prediction model estimating the probability of achieving the PMG within 3 months in patients with common hand and wrist conditions.

METHODS: This study used real-world data from 25 specialized hand and wrist care clinics in the Netherlands. We included 6263 patients (training data: n=5010; test data: n=1253) treated for common hand and wrist conditions. The prediction target was the PMG achievement at 3 months post-treatment. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (area under the curve [AUC]) and calibration. The final model was selected based on AUC, calibration, and the number of model features.

RESULTS: We selected a gradient boosting machine algorithm with thirteen predictors. The model had an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.70 to 0.76, indicating acceptable-to-good discrimination) and excellent calibration in the test set. Following a user-centered design, we built a Shiny app visualizing the probability of reaching the PMG for different treatment options (i.e., hand therapy ± injection, injection, or surgery) (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31084375).

CONCLUSIONS: A treatment-conditional prediction model using a patient-defined threshold for treatment success can provide individualized estimates of the probability of achieving outcomes that matter to patients. This generalizable approach may enhance shared decision-making and expectation management in preference-sensitive care.

articles.title: In-Hospital Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement Surgical Versus Transcatheter: A Nationwide Study with Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are two preferred methods for treating aortic stenosis. This study compared the in-hospital mortality rates associated with SAVR and TAVR.

METHODS: In accordance with the STROBE guidelines, we conducted an analytical cross-sectional study utilizing data from the National Readmission Database (NRD) spanning from 2016 to 2020. Patients who underwent TAVR or SAVR were identified using specific ICD-10 procedure codes. We employed adjusted multivariate logistic regression analysis to determine the odds ratio (OR) of death associated with SAVR compared to TAVR. Patients were followed for a year and OR with 95% CI were calculated. AI based XGBoost model were used to find the predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: Our study included a total of 361,875 patients. Among these, 182,443 underwent TAVR, while 179,432 underwent SAVR. In the TAVR group, 2,563 patients (1.4%) died during hospitalization, whereas 6,671 patients (3.7%) died in the SAVR group. The multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that SAVR is associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR = 2.66, 95% CI 2.51-2.81, p < 0.001) compared to TAVR. Follow up data at 30 days, three months, six months, did not find any difference in mortality between TAVR and SAVR. Notably, liver failure, HLD, renal failure, SAVR, female, CHF, and atrial fibrillation are amongst the top predictor of mortality in patients undergoing (TAVR or SAVR). While in cardiac rehospitalization, risk factors like female gender, CHF, Afib, HLD, DM have higher predictability than procedure.

CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that SAVR is associated with a higher likelihood of in-hospital mortality compared to TAVR, with organ dysfunction (liver failure, kidney dysfunction) as a predictor of mortality.

articles.title: High-Frequency Electrograms Abolition as a Valuable Target for Remap During Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation. The HF REMAP Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: peak frequency (PF) analysis has recently emerged as a novel tool to assess electrogram properties through their frequency spectrum. PF is an indirect marker of local myocardial activity, and its reduction after radiofrequency ablation reflects effective tissue modification.

OBJECTIVE: our study aims to evaluate PF analysis as an objective method to validate lesion efficacy during ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation.

METHODS: we retrospectively analyzed 43 (out of 247) consecutive patients who underwent VT ablation between January 2023 and December 2024, using the EnSite X mapping system with Advisor HD Grid catheter (Abbott, Minneapolis, USA). Complete pre- and post-ablation high-density sinus rhythm maps were obtained. PF analysis was applied offline to quantify the residual high-frequency (HF) electrogram burden, expressed as a percentage of the ablated area. Patients were stratified according to residual HF burden, and outcomes were assessed with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 372 days, 11 patients reached the primary endpoint (VT recurrence or arrhythmic storm). Patients with <70% residual HF post-ablation had significantly higher VT-free survival (≈90% at 12 months) compared to those with ≥70% residual HF (≈25%; log-rank p<0.001). Cox regression confirmed residual HF ≥70% as an independent predictor of recurrence (HR 13.36; 95% CI 3.52-50.7; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: PF analysis during re-mapping provides an operator-independent, reproducible tool to validate lesion efficacy. A low post-ablation residual HF burden is associated to a significantly increased VAs-free survival rate.

articles.title: Temporal Changes in LGE-CMR Enhancement After Monopolar Biphasic Focal Pulsed Field Ablation for Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel non-thermal ablation modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). While chronic lesion formation after PFA has been described, data regarding acute lesion characteristics and lesion maturation remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize acute and chronic lesion formation following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI using serial late-gadolinium-enhancement cardiovascular-magnetic-resonance-imaging (LGE-CMR).

METHODS: Six consecutive patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF underwent index PFA-guided PVI using the CENTAURI system and a focal point-by-point lesion delivery strategy. LGE-CMR was performed 1 day and 90±10 days after ablation. Quantitative assessment of regional and global left atrial (LA) enhancement was performed using a standardized segmentation protocol. Changes in enhancement burden and LA dimensions were analyzed between imaging timepoints.

RESULTS: Among six patients at mean age 65±7 years, five patients (83%) had paroxysmal AF. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients without procedural complications. Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial temporal changes between acute and chronic imaging. Enhancement within the right pulmonary vein (PV) region decreased from 3.3±2.2% to 0.8±0.8%(p=0.030), while the proportion of enhanced tissue decreased from 24.1±13.5% to 5.7±5.8%(p=0.017). Similar reductions were observed around the left PVs (4.4±3.1%vs.1.4±1.2%, p=0.064). Posterior wall enhancement decreased from 2.4±1.1% to 0.3±0.3%(p=0.007) and global LA enhancement from 12.8±6.2% to 3.3±1.6%(p=0.013), while LA volume remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial enhancement reduction of acute lesions following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI, which remained largely confined to the PV antra and adjacent posterior wall, providing novel in-human insights into lesion maturation following focal PFA delivery.

articles.title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers.

RESULTS: Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P_interaction=0.028).

CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

articles.title: Assessment of endothelial glycocalyx degradation in sepsis using direct visualization with sublingual microscopy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The endothelial glycocalyx plays a crucial role in the pathophysiology of sepsis, but assessment of glycocalyx injury in clinical settings remains challenging. Perfused boundary region (PBR) is derived from sublingual intravital video microscopy and has been studied as a surrogate of endothelial glycocalyx barrier function. The goal of this study was to determine whether PBR is associated with circulating heparan sulfate (a biochemical marker of glycocalyx degradation), sepsis status, in-hospital mortality, and intravenous (IV) fluid administration.

METHODS: This was an ancillary study to the randomized clinical trial Protocol-Based Care for Early Septic Shock (ProCESS). The patients were enrolled from six hospitals and controls from two hospitals. Subjects underwent sublingual microscopy. We assessed the association between PBR and heparan sulfate levels. We also compared the baseline PBR between sepsis and non-infected controls, and between the survivors and non-survivors. Lastly, the association between IV fluid administration and PBR was assessed using a linear mixed-effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 193 subjects were included: 144 had septic shock and the in-hospital mortality rate was 12.5%. The PBR was associated with levels of circulating heparan sulfate (r = 0.32, R2 = 0.10, p = 0.02). The baseline PBR was higher in sepsis compared to controls (2.29 ± 0.40 vs. 2.02 ± 0.41, p < 0.01) but not different between survivors and non-survivors. PBR was also not associated with IV fluid administration volume.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest a link between PBR and endothelial glycocalyx degradation observed in sepsis.

articles.title: NON-INVASIVE HemodynamicS of Non-Thrombotic Iliac Vein Lesions ARE DISTURBED IN PATIEnTS with A HiSTORY OF Deep Venous Thrombosis.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05.

RESULTS: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

articles.title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome.

METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

articles.title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR.

METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis.

RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported.

CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

articles.title: Recovery of Human Pegiviruses from Patients with Acute Febrile Illness and Sub-acute Central Nervous System Infection.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe two cases of HPgV-1 identified during high-throughput sequencing (HTS)-based investigation of previously undiagnosed acute febrile illness (AFI) and central nervous system infection.

METHODS: RNA metagenomic HTS was applied to clinical samples that had previously tested negative by PCR targeting alphaviruses, flaviviruses, enteroviruses, herpesviruses, and paramyxoviruses. Specimens were also tested for IgM antibodies against chikungunya virus, dengue virus, and Japanese encephalitis virus.

RESULTS: A complete HPgV-1 genotype 4 was recovered from a child with undifferentiated AFI. In a middle-aged man with HIV and severe neurological disorder, complete genomes of HPgV-1 (genotype 4), HPgV-2, and hepatitis C virus (genotype 3k) were identified.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of HPgV-2 detection in Indonesia, expanding its known geographic distribution. These findings underscore the complexity of viral co-infections in immunocompromised patients and the uncertain clinical significance of human pegiviruses. This further highlights the utility of metagenomic HTS for pathogen discovery and genomic surveillance in unexplained clinical syndromes.

articles.title: Paradoxical attenuation of dyslipidemia and atherosclerosis in Apoe-/-Mpst-/- mice.
articles.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a signaling molecule that affects multiple (patho)physiological pathways. Deficiency of H2S due to cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) deletion has been proven to accelerate atherosclerotic plaque formation. However, the role of 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase (MPST), a related H2S-producing enzyme that impacts metabolism, has not been studied in atherogenic dyslipidemia. We generated a double Apoe/Mpst knockout mouse (Apoe-/-Mpst-/-) in the C57BL/6 background. C57Bl/6, Mpst-/-, Apoe-/- and Apoe-/-Mpst-/-mice were fed a western diet for 14 weeks, after which blood and tissues (aorta and liver) were collected; the circulating lipid profile, atherosclerotic plaque formation and expression of enzymes involved in lipid biosynthetic pathways in the liver were evaluated in the four mouse lines. H2S production was reduced in the liver of double knockout mice, while the expression of CBS and CSE was not altered. In the serum of Apoe-/-Mpst-/-, we observed decreased levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoproteins (LDL) and triglycerides (TGs) compared to Apoe-/-; hepatic apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels were also downregulated. However, the expression of other key enzymes that participate in cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis remained unchanged. In addition, hepatic lipid deposition was not significantly altered among genotypes. In line with the reduced circulating LDL and TGs levels, atherosclerotic lesions were found to be reduced in the aorta of Apoe-/-Mpst-/-. Our results indicate that MPST deletion in the Apoe-/- dyslipidemia model leads to decreased circulating lipid levels and atherosclerosis, that correlate with a downregulation of hepatic ApoB expression.

articles.title: Infection of an NBCA-Embolized Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysm after EVAR Requiring Radical Surgical Salvage.
Effective Approaches for Improving Physical Activity in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity is a significant predictor of hospitalization and all-cause mortality in COPD patients. This study sought to identify the most successful methods for improving physical activity in COPD patients.

METHODS: Systematic reviews with or without meta-analysis from January 2012 to December 2024 according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines were included. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and other databases. Selected studies had two quality standards required by the Database of Abstracts of Reviews of Effects and focused on improving physical activity in COPD patients.

RESULTS: Ultimately, 20 systematic reviews, with 35,816 participants, were selected for this study. Four main classifications with eleven approaches to improving physical activity were identified. These approaches include: 1. Exercise (Tai Chi, traditional mind-body exercises, walking, and pedometers); 2. Technology-based interventions (Virtual reality-based therapy [VRBT], telerehabilitation [telemonitoring, applications], and smartphone devices, which increased activity by over 18.3% within 6 months and 21% over 12 months, and serious games with a 61.83% adherence rate); 3. Theoretical-behavioral approaches (consultation and coaching, and behavior change interventions); 4. Hybrid approaches.

CONCLUSION: Based on the narrative synthesis, a hybrid approach could be a useful strategy for addressing barriers to physical activity in patients with COPD. Such an approach could include tailoring interventions (e.g., combining tai chi with coaching) and delivering them through technology-based platforms (e.g., VRBT) according to individual patient and health system needs. This approach can improve patients' physical activity levels and support adherence to physical activity, thereby potentially optimizing the treatment process.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics of Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection Among Patients with High LRINEC Scores.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score is a widely used adjunctive diagnostic tool for necrotizing soft tissue infection (NSTI). However, patients with high LRINEC scores do not uniformly have NSTI and often represent a diagnostic gray zone requiring urgent differentiation from other severe soft tissue infections. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics of NSTI among patients with high LRINEC scores.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients hospitalized for severe soft tissue infections with sepsis between January 2014 and December 2023 with LRINEC scores ≥6, classified as NSTI (n = 11) or non-NSTI (n = 9). Non-NSTI cases were limited to severe cellulitis with bacteremia requiring intensive care. Clinical findings, laboratory parameters, imaging findings, and vasopressor use within 24 hours after hospital arrival were compared.

RESULTS: Patients with LRINEC had significantly higher white blood cell counts and serum creatinine levels. Fluid collection along the fascia and gas formation on CT were more frequent in the NSTI group. Mean blood pressure at presentation did not differ between groups; however, vasopressor use within 24 hours after hospital arrival was significantly more common in the NSTI group, suggesting early hemodynamic deterioration or greater disease severity CONCLUSIONS: In patients with high LRINEC scores, NSTI was associated with marked inflammatory response, renal dysfunction, specific CT findings and early hemodynamic instability. Early vasopressor requirement should be interpreted primarily as a marker of early hemodynamic deterioration or disease severity, rather than a diagnostic characteristic specific to NSTI.

articles.title: Exercise-Induced Cardiac Mechanics in Asymptomatic Primary Mitral Regurgitation: Insights from Stress Echocardiography and Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing.
articles.journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress echocardiography is recommended for evaluating asymptomatic primary mitral regurgitation (MR), but exercise-induced changes in myocardial mechanics and right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: 63 patients with moderate-to-severe or severe primary degenerative MR (NYHA I) and 20 age-matched healthy controls prospectively underwent comprehensive transthoracic and supine bicycle stress echocardiography. Left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain (reservoir, conduit and contraction), right ventricular (RV) strain, and RV-PA coupling (TAPSE/PASP) were assessed at rest and peak exercise. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) was additionally performed in a subgroup.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, MR patients demonstrated significantly lower exercise capacity, achieving shorter exercise duration (8.26 ± 2.32 vs. 10.32 ± 1.34 minutes, p<0.001) and lower maximal workload (78.0 ± 21.2 vs. 101.3 ± 9.9 W, p<0.001). At rest, LV GLS and RV strain were comparable between groups, whereas LA conduit and contraction strain were already altered in MR patients. Exercise unmasked lower peak GLS and impaired RV-PA coupling in the MR group, while peak LA contraction strain remained significantly different between groups. Seven patients developed exercise-induced MR deterioration, exhibiting loss of LA functional reserve with deterioration of all LA strain components, unlike patients without MR deterioration. Peak VO2 was lower in MR patients and correlated with exercise RV-PA coupling, but not with LA strain.

CONCLUSIONS: Exercise echocardiography combined with myocardial deformation imaging identifies chamber-specific functional abnormalities not evident at rest, providing complementary physiological insight into cardiac adaptation in asymptomatic primary MR.

articles.title: Role and mechanism of ATF6-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress in ITLN-1 against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Intelectin-1 (ITLN-1), a novel adipocytokine, exerts neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), yet its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study focused on activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), a key endoplasmic reticulum stress sensor, to explore its role in CIRI-induced neuronal injury and determine whether ITLN-1 mediates neuroprotection through ATF6 regulation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We established an N2a cell hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model and a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. Using protein molecular docking, situ proximity ligation assay, Western blotting, mitochondrial membrane potential assays, and TUNEL staining, we investigated ATF6 activation in neuronal apoptosis and its upstream regulatory mechanisms.

KEY FINDINGS: H/R injury markedly induced ATF6 activation in N2a cells, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction and promoting apoptosis. ATF6 overexpression further aggravated these effects, confirming its critical pathogenic role in CIRI. Mechanistic analyses revealed that ITLN-1 physically associates with ATF6. Both ITLN-1 overexpression and exogenous recombinant ITLN-1 administration significantly suppressed excessive ATF6 activation, modulated the JNK signaling pathway, improved cell viability, reduced intracellular calcium overload and reactive oxygen species accumulation, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis. In vivo, ITLN-1 ameliorated neurological deficits, reduced neuronal damage, and alleviated demyelination, whereas ITLN-1 knockdown produced opposite effects.

SIGNIFICANCE: Excessive ATF6 activation underlies CIRI-induced neuronal injury. ITLN-1 exerts neuroprotection by inhibiting ATF6 and modulating JNK signaling, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and reducing apoptosis. These findings highlight the ITLN-1/ATF6 axis as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Hemolin modulates IMD-related immune responses and promotes cellular immunity in Ostrinia furnacalis.
articles.abstract: Ostrinia furnacalis is one of the most destructive Lepidopteran pests in Asia and worldwide, reducing yields of corn and other grain crops. Hemolin, an immunoglobulin-like protein with both developmental and immunological functions, has been implicated in protecting insects from pathogen infections. However, the specific regulatory mechanism by which Hemolin modulates innate immunity in O. furnacalis remains unknown. In this study, the full-length Of-Hemolin cDNA sequence was obtained by rapid amplification of cDNA ends and characterized through bioinformatic analysis. Expression levels of Of-Hemolin in different tissues and developmental stages of O. furnacalis were analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR. The transcript levels of Of-Hemolin and immune-related genes in O. furnacalis larvae were detected after bacterial infection or dsHem injection. Of-Hemolin knockdown altered the expression of IMD pathway-related genes and antimicrobial peptides, suggesting that Of-Hemolin modulates IMD signaling-associated immune responses at the transcriptional level. As an opsonin, Of-Hemolin also substantially augments cellular immune reactions, including phagocytosis, encapsulation and nodulation, demonstrating its critical contribution to cellular immunity. These findings elucidate Of-Hemolin's function and suggest it may be a candidate target for green pest control.

articles.title: Pathological evidence links white feces syndrome in farmed Penaeus vannamei to severe hepatopancreatic Ecytonucleospora hepatopenaei infection in China.
articles.abstract: White feces syndrome (WFS) remains a major health problem in global Penaeus vannamei aquaculture, yet its etiology and pathogenesis remain debated. In this study, WFS outbreaks were investigated in 24 shrimp ponds across four provinces in China between 2013 and 2024, using light microscopy, histopathology, in situ hybridization, transmission electron microscopy, and molecular diagnostics. Ecytonucleospora hepatopenaei (EHP) was detected in all WFS-affected ponds examined. Microscopic and ultrastructural analyses showed that both fresh white feces from intestinal tract and pond-floating white feces were dominated by mature EHP spores, empty spore shells, and limited excretory debris, whereas bacteria were not a predominant structural component. Histopathology and in situ hybridization demonstrated that severe EHP infection was present in the hepatopancreas of WFS-shrimp, while the shrimp midgut and hind gut remain structurally intact. The observed hemocytic infiltration, encapsulation, and melanization suggest that host immune response contributes to the degradation of sloughed necrotic epithelial cells while leaving the resilient EHP spores within the hepatopancreatic tubule lumens. These massive, relatively pure spore loads were subsequently discharged into the midgut to form white feces. These findings indicate that WFS in the investigated field cases was strongly associated with severe hepatopancreatic EHP infection. The characteristic white coloration was most likely due to intense light scattering by dense spore aggregates, rather than to extensive intestinal epithelial injury or massive bacterial accumulation. WFS is recommended as a practical clinical indicator of high EHP burden in EHP-endemic shrimp farms.

articles.title: A case of feline sparganosis caused by Spirometra asiana (Cestoda: Diphyllobothriidae) discovered during left forelimb amputation.
articles.abstract: A large plerocercoid was incidentally found and removed during left forelimb amputation performed to treat a refractory wound in a cat rescued in Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Molecular analysis of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I gene identified the recovered worm as Spirometra asiana. This represents the first reported case of feline sparganosis caused by this species. Although the association between plerocercoid infection and the clinical signs remains unclear, outdoor cats may potentially harbor plerocercoids.

articles.title: Admission C-Reactive Protein-to-Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Early Major Amputation After Minor Amputation in Patients With Infected Foot Wounds.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification.

LEVEL OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Mid-Term Outcomes for Lung Transplantation in for COVID-19 Respiratory Failure: An Analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing Database.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung transplantation is a feasible therapeutic option for irreversible lung injury caused by COVID-19, but comprehensive mid-term outcome data remain limited. This study evaluated outcomes after lung transplantation for COVID-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) and post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (CPF) using a national registry.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 2020 through 2024. Recipient characteristics, perioperative complications, and graft failure-free survival were analyzed in adult lung transplant recipients with a primary diagnosis of CARDS, CPF, or non-COVID restrictive lung disease (NCRLD). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariate logistic regression were performed to adjust for potential confounders.

RESULTS: During the study period, 256 transplants were performed for CARDS, 338 for CPF, and 8071 for NCRLD. Post-COVID-19 recipients were younger (54 vs. 64 years, p<0.001) and required a higher level of care preoperatively than NCRLD recipients. Posttransplant, post-COVID-19 recipients experienced higher rates of posttransplant ECMO (22.6% vs. 10.3%, p<0.001), ventilation >48 hours (67.5% vs. 43.3%, p<0.001), new dialysis (11.0% vs. 7.9%, p=0.012), and acute rejection (7.7% vs. 5.5%, p=0.026). Graft failure-free survival was equivalent throughout the first year posttransplant between the post-COVID-19 and NCRLD recipients and, after IPTW for age and other confounders, was equivalent for up to 3 years (Hochberg-adjusted p=0.118).

CONCLUSIONS: Lung transplantation for post-COVID-19 lung damage yields comparable short-term and mid-term survival outcomes despite higher perioperative morbidity and resource utilization. Long-term studies are needed to assess chronic lung allograft dysfunction in this population.

articles.title: Independent and Joint Associations of Long-Term Ambient Meteorological Exposures and Socioeconomic Deprivation with Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Although acute meteorological events are recognized cardiovascular hazards, the combined cardiovascular impacts of long-term meteorological exposures and socioeconomic deprivation remain poorly characterized. Among 469,347 UK Biobank participants, we evaluated independent and interactive associations of 1-year average ambient temperature, relative humidity, and the Townsend deprivation index (TDI) with incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and cardiovascular death. Over median 13.7-year follow-up, 31,626 MACE, 12,565 strokes, 17,062 MIs, and 7,161 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In Cox models, the highest versus lowest temperature category was associated with lower MACE risk (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.84-0.91), whereas high humidity (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14) and high deprivation (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.34-1.44) were independently associated with elevated risk. Under a counterfactual assigning the least deprived category's risk to both more deprived categories, 11.75% (95% CI, 9.68-13.77%) of incident MACE and 17.15% (12.68-21.39%) of cardiovascular deaths over 10 years would be attributable to deprivation (total-effect specification, omitting smoking, body mass index, hypertension and diabetes; fully adjusted, 6.67% and 11.09%). Temperature and humidity showed multiplicative interactions with TDI: versus the joint low-risk reference, low temperature with high deprivation had HR 1.55 (95% CI, 1.40-1.71) for MACE and high humidity with high deprivation HR 1.51 (1.34-1.71); additive interactions were significant only at intermediate temperature or intermediate humidity (RERI, 0.20 and 0.16). The deprivation gradient was stable in every sensitivity analysis; the temperature association did not persist within assessment centres, nor the humidity association under a time-varying specification, although both persisted across exposure windows and air-pollution adjustment. These findings indicate that long-term lower temperatures and higher humidity, together with socioeconomic deprivation, are independently and jointly associated with elevated cardiovascular risk, underscoring the need for integrated climate and social welfare policies to mitigate health disparities in vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Therapeutic Effects of Stemona japonica Extract against Mycoplasma gallisepticum Infection: Association with Suppression of NF-κB-Mediated Inflammatory Response.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is the primary causative agent of chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens, causing massive economic losses to the global poultry industry. The widespread emergence of antibiotic-resistant MG strains has created an urgent need for safe and effective alternative therapies. Stemona japonica (Baibu), a traditional Chinese medicine with well-documented antitussive and anti-inflammatory properties, has not been systematically evaluated for its anti-MG activity. This study investigated the therapeutic effects of S. japonica extract against MG infection both in vitro and in vivo, and elucidated its underlying molecular mechanisms. In chicken respiratory epithelial cells, S. japonica extract significantly alleviated MG-induced cellular injury, improved cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and dose-dependently downregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ). Mechanistically, S. japonica suppressed MG-induced activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway by inhibiting the phosphorylation and degradation of IκBα and subsequent phosphorylation of p65. In a chicken MG infection model, S. japonica treatment significantly alleviated clinical symptoms, reduced body weight loss and mortality, elevated serum IgG and IgA levels, and attenuated lung pathological damage. Transcriptome sequencing further confirmed that S. japonica reversed MG-induced gene expression changes, with differentially expressed genes highly enriched in NF-κB, TNF, and cytokine-receptor interaction pathways. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that S. japonica exerts potent therapeutic effects against MG infection, which is associated with suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses and enhancement of host humoral immunity. This study provides a scientific basis for the development of S. japonica as a promising alternative agent for the treatment of CRD in poultry.

articles.title: Iatrogenic Withdrawal Syndrome in Adult Intensive Care Unit Patients: An Alternative Perspective to Design Sedation Protocols.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion

articles.title: Twice isolated, not twice ignored: Bacillus cereus catheter-related bloodstream infection in a haemodialysis patient.
articles.abstract: A 53-year-old man with chronic kidney disease on maintenance haemodialysis via a right internal jugular tunnelled catheter (permcath) presented with recurrent fever during dialysis sessions. Paired blood cultures from the catheter and peripheral vein yielded Bacillus cereus. As the organism is frequently regarded as a contaminant, repeat paired cultures were obtained, which again grew B. cereus susceptible to vancomycin and gentamicin. Catheter-drawn cultures flagged positive earlier than peripheral cultures in both sets (differential time to positivity approximately 6.2 h and 5.5 h). Echocardiography excluded infective endocarditis. The patient improved following catheter removal and antimicrobial therapy. This case highlights the importance of distinguishing contamination from true bloodstream infection.

articles.title: Y-Configuration Dual Stent Retriever Thrombectomy for Bifurcation Occlusions in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bifurcation occlusions present unique technical challenges during mechanical thrombectomy. We evaluated the angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes of Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by bifurcation occlusions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 32 consecutive patients treated with Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy between April 2018 and January 2025. The technique was used as a rescue strategy after failed single-device attempts or as a first-line approach in selected bifurcation occlusions. Angiographic outcomes, procedural metrics, complications, and 90-day clinical outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: The middle cerebral artery was the most common occlusion site (81.3%). Successful reperfusion (TICI ≥2b) was achieved in 97% of patients, with complete reperfusion (TICI 3) in 91% of cases. Following the first Y-configuration thrombectomy attempt, successful reperfusion (TICI ≥2b) was achieved in 87% of cases, irrespective of prior thrombectomy attempts. Median NIHSS improved from 16 at baseline to 7 at 24 hours. At 90 days, 53% of patients achieved functional independence (mRS ≤2). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 6.3%; any intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 9.4%, and no vasospasm, vessel dissection, device-related perforation, or subarachnoid hemorrhage was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Y-configuration dual stent retriever thrombectomy appears feasible as a rescue option for selected complex bifurcation occlusions refractory to conventional thrombectomy. Prospective comparative studies are needed to further establish its safety, efficacy, and optimal indications.

articles.title: Psoriasis: Which therapy for which patient, updated, part I. Focus on Psoriasis Comorbidities and Preferred Systemic Agents.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
articles.abstract: Patients with psoriasis (PsO) may have various comorbidities, that are either related to or unrelated to the disease itself. Selection of the appropriate treatment modality has evolved substantially with the rapid expansion of available options that can be individualized based on patients' comorbidity profiles, extent of disease, prior therapeutic response, and treatment preferences. This first article of a two-part series focuses on selecting systemic therapy for PsO patients with specific inflammatory comorbidities or a history of malignancy.

articles.title: Favorable survival for older adults treated with Axi-cel and Tisa-cel CD19 CAR-T therapy for relapsed/refractory DLBCL: a U.S. multicenter comparative analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) commonly affects older patients > 65 years old, with chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy becoming an increasingly valuable treatment modality for relapsed/refractory (R/R) disease. Real world data on safety, efficacy, and management practices of CAR-T for older patients are important to inform clinical practice and referral.

OBJECTIVE: To compare efficacy and toxicities of axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) and tisagenlecleucel (tisa-cel) in younger (age <65) and older (age ≥ 65) patients with R/R DLBCL, and to describe clinical management practices for delivery of care to older patients.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter analysis of 351 adult patients with R/R DLBCL using data from the Cell Therapy Consortium registry. Patients who underwent apheresis for commercial axi-cel or tisa-cel products from early 2018 to late 2021 were compared by age: 194 patients < 65 years old and 157 patients ≥ 65 years old. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method with 95% confidence intervals and compared using the log-rank test. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify factors associating with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

RESULTS: 328 patients (93.5%) were infused with CAR-T product. Combining all CAR-T products, younger and older groups yielded similar overall response rates (ORR, 61% vs 64%) and complete response rates (CR, 43% vs 49%). When evaluating only those who received axi-cel (n = 65), the older group had improved ORR (82% vs 65%, p = 0.02) and CR rates (63% vs 47%, p = 0.04) compared to younger patients. Median PFS (4.4 months in younger vs 6.8 months in older, p=0.44) and OS (22 months in younger vs 18 months in older, p=0.85) were similar between the two groups. In this cohort, 70% developed cytokine release syndrome (CRS, 6% grade > 3) with no significant difference by age overall or within same CAR-T product. In total, 71 patients (38%) developed immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) with 23% being grade ≥ 3. There was no difference in any grade ICANS between younger and older patients. On multivariate analysis, overall mortality was increased in patients with high IPI (HR 1.71, p < 0.01) and bulky disease (HR 1.96, p < 0.01). Age group or CAR-T product were not associated with PFS or OS at 2 years. Rates of early infection, severe (grade >3) cytopenias at 3 months, and 100-day and 1-year non-relapse mortality (NRM) were also similar between younger and older patients.

CONCLUSION: Data from our Cell Therapy Consortium retrospective analysis demonstrate that CAR-T recipients older than 65 yrs experience favorable outcomes and manageable toxicity similar to younger patients. Our results support the practice that age alone should not be a barrier to CAR-T consultation or therapy.

articles.title: [Klinische und subjektive Ergebnisse nach beidseitiger Implantation einer IOL mit partiellem Fokusbereich].
Rethinking Pathogenesis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive fibroinflammatory injury of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts that may lead to cirrhosis, hepatobiliary malignancy, and death, with liver transplantation representing the only effective intervention in end-stage disease. Rather than a single dominant pathomechanism, the data support a model in which four axes - bile acid metabolism, the intestinal microbiome and gut barrier, biliary epithelial dysfunction, and Th17-skewed immune dysregulation - are reciprocally coupled and converge on a shared periductal fibrogenic output dominated by TGF-beta signaling. This review summarizes key mechanistic advances from genetic, epigenomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and microbiome studies. These investigations implicate antigen presentation pathways, Th17-skewed immune responses, cholangiocyte senescence and profibrotic signaling, and disrupted gut-liver communication as central drivers of chronic biliary injury. Emerging spatial and multi-omics approaches further reveal complex cellular crosstalk among cholangiocytes, immune cells, macrophages, and mesenchymal populations within portal inflammatory niches. We discuss evolving biomarkers and recent clinical trial data targeting bile acid metabolism, fibrosis, the microbiome, and immune pathways. In conclusion, research data suggests viewing PSC as a network disease, which provides a unifying framework for disease pathogenesis and may enable biomarker-guided patient stratification and mechanism-based therapy development targeting distinct pathogenic pathways.

articles.title: Single-Item Anhedonia in Schizophrenia Marks Illness Severity but Does Not Independently Predict Outcomes: An Item-Level Reanalysis of the Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anhedonia has been proposed as a marker of poor functional outcomes in schizophrenia. A model that omits baseline functioning estimates a different quantity from one that includes it: the former assesses whether anhedonia identifies patients who function worse later, and the later assesses whether it adds prognostic information beyond baseline functioning. We estimated both associations using data from the Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness trial.

METHODS: We reanalysed the Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness Phase 1/1A Main Trial schizophrenia sample (759 rated and decisive model 672). We moved from the first quantity to the second quantity by removing the Heinrichs-Carpenter Quality of Life Scale anhedonia item from the outcome and then adding the baseline function. We repeated the test on the three Quality of Life Scale subscales without the item, screened all 21 items the same way, set anhedonia against 15 other baseline features, and tested independent outcomes, drug interactions and attrition.

RESULTS: Baseline anhedonia predicted the 21-item Quality of Life Scale total at 12 months (standardised β=0.309, p=4.2×10-15). Removing the item from the outcome measure did not change the association (β=0.301). Adding the baseline function collapsed it (β=0.022, p=0.58). All 21 items behaved the same way: 21 were significant in models with no baseline term, 21 with the item also removed, and 0 once baseline function was adjusted. Anhedonia ranked 13th of 21 items, 13th of 16 features, and predicted no independent outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Baseline single-item anhedonia in Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness marks concurrent clinical and functional burden. It carries no incremental prognostic value beyond the baseline function.

articles.title: Study on the capture and thrombolytic efficacy of magnetic particle clusters under a deeply focused rotating magnetic field.
articles.abstract: Magnetic particle-mediated targeted delivery of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), assisted by a rotating magnetic field (RMF), represents a highly promising approach for the treatment of venous thrombosis. However, existing magnetic strategies face bottlenecks in deep tissues and complex hemodynamics due to poor focusing and weak flow resistance. Consequently, flow washout induces particle escape, while magnetic attenuation severely limits the clusters ' operating range and fluid perturbation. Achieving deep focusing and flow-resistant retention of magnetic particle clusters (MPCs) under deep-tissue, high-flow conditions remains a critical challenge for the clinical translation of this technology. To this end, a novel deeply focused rotating magnetic field (DF-RMF) system driven by dual synchronized rotating permanent magnets is developed. It establishes an axial magnetic focusing zone with dual-peak confinement and continuous centripetal properties to effectively counteract fluid drag. Simulations and in vitro flow experiments demonstrate that the DF-RMF stably confines magnetic particle clusters as compact, continuously rotating clusters at the lumen center. This effectively expands their geometric working boundaries and significantly enhances synergistic thrombolytic efficacy. Even at distances up to 5 cm or under the normal physiological flow velocity of lower extremity veins (~14 cm/s), the system maintains a substantial particle retention rate. Rotating synchronously under the DF-RMF, the clusters generate mechanical shear while inducing intense microfluidic circulation and pressure fluctuations. This physically disrupts the thrombus and accelerates interfacial tPA transport to boost fibrinolysis, achieving complete in vitro recanalization with a removal rate ~5 times that of tPA alone. This study provides a novel physical modulation strategy with translational potential for deep, precision targeted delivery and synergistic mechanical-biochemical thrombolysis in complex blood flow environments.

articles.title: [Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia - Bridging the Care Gap in the Early Neonatal Period].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kernicterus resulting from excessive bilirubin concentrations can be effectively prevented by early diagnosis and therapy. The postnatal rise of bilirubin peaks at a time of life most newborn infants have been discharged home while the next scheduled well baby visit is several weeks ahead.

AIM: Evaluating a post-discharge bilirubin follow-up program established in 2010.
