METHODS: Retrospective analysis of newborns seen 2010-2024 at the Berlin University Medical Center bilirubin outpatient clinic, exchange transfusions performed in the same time period, and infants admitted for phototherapy in 2022.

RESULTS: The median annual number of infants consulting the outpatient clinic was 616 in 2010-2016, as compared to 1858 in 2017-2024. In 2022, 6% of newborns seen at the outpatient clinic were admitted for treatment of hyperbilirubinemia at a median age of 6 [5-7] days, with a total serum bilirubin concentration of 20.5 [19.3-21.4] mg/dl). The 2 top indications for the 81 exchange transfusions performed in 78 patients were rhesus incompatibility (n=44; 56%) and gestational alloimmune liver disease (n=24; 31%). The bilirubin level immediately prior to exchange transfusion was 15.5 [12.5-20.0] mg/dl (highest measured value 38.1 mg/dl).

CONCLUSION: A post-discharge program attached to a neonatal unit can effectively bridge the gap in care between discharge and scheduled well-baby visits several weeks ahead. A mandatory U2a could standardize follow-up care for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia in the future.

articles.title: Effects of LBBAP Pacing-Site Position under a Modelled Proximal LBBB: A 24-Model Electrophysiological Simulation Study.
articles.abstract: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) may recruit the distal left-sided conduction system, but the electrical effect of pacing-site position along the left bundle branch (LBB) remains incompletely defined. We evaluated this effect in 24 four-chamber virtual heart anatomies using a Reaction-Eikonal finite-element model with rule-based myocardial fibres and algorithmically generated His-Purkinje networks. A modelled proximal Histo-LBB disconnection preserved the distal LBB-Purkinje network while interrupting its proximal connection. Six conditions were simulated in each anatomy: a sinoatrial-node (SAN)-initiated left bundle branch block (LBBB) control, right ventricular apical pacing, right ventricular outflow-tract pacing and a modelled non-selective LBB capture configuration at proximal, nominal and distal positions. The primary outcome was BiV_TAT95, the 95th percentile of activation times across left-ventricular, rightventricular and interventricular-septal nodes. The control-versus-paced analysis used a common simulation-clock origin and was interpreted as contextual benchmarking, whereas the positional analysis used matched direct ventricular stimulation. In the matched positional analysis, median BiV_TAT95 was 104.5, 93.5 and 88.5 ms for proximal, nominal and distal LBBAP, respectively (Friedman chi-square = 48.000, P < 0.001, Kendall's W = 1.000); every anatomy followed distal < nominal < proximal. In three selected anatomies, a 20% decrease or increase in the prescribed myocardial conduction speeds altered absolute activation times but preserved this ordering in all nine anatomy-by-speed combinations. Under the tested homogeneous substrate and modelled non-selective capture configuration, the distal tested position produced the lowest simulated BiV_TAT95; this does not imply superiority for every activation metric. This conditional prediction requires validation against patient-specific electrical data.

articles.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds.
articles.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100 - 200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 days when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

articles.title: Updated treatment targets in inflammatory bowel disease (STRIDE-III): an initiative of the International Organization for the Study of IBD.
articles.abstract: Since Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease-II (STRIDE-II), new evidence has become available across inflammatory and patient-centred outcomes. We aimed to update the STRIDE recommendations for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL for studies published after the STRIDE-II search period. Findings were integrated with surveys of International Organization for the Study of IBD (IOIBD) members and paediatric gastroenterologists from the Porto group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition. Statements were subsequently voted on using a modified Delphi approach; consensus was defined as ≥75% of participants rating a statement 7-10 on a 10-point scale. Of 13 071 records identified in the systematic review, 1018 were included. Surveys were completed by 60 of 79 IOIBD gastroenterologists and 23 of 30 paediatric gastroenterologists in the Porto group. STRIDE-III defines three conceptually distinct categories of treatment targets. Actionable targets include clinical response and remission, which reflect patient priorities, and objective inflammatory targets (C-reactive protein normalisation, faecal calprotectin within target range, and endoscopic remission), supported by interventional evidence demonstrating benefits of target-guided treatment modification. Adjunctive targets (ie, urgency, histological remission in ulcerative colitis, transmural remission in Crohn's disease, and growth) are supported by studies showing association with favourable outcomes and guide treatment optimisation and tighter monitoring but do not necessarily require a change in therapeutic class. Patient-centred targets (ie, disability, fatigue, and quality of life) directly reflect patients' well-being and are impaired in a substantial proportion of patients with inflammatory bowel disease; impairment should prompt assessment of inflammation and alternative causes and management through shared decision-making. Targets are further classified as immediate, short-term, intermediate, and long-term. STRIDE-III also defines treatment-specific times to target achievement, new faecal calprotectin thresholds, and adaptations for resource-limited settings. STRIDE-III distinguishes targets that should prompt treatment change from those that primarily guide optimisation and monitoring, while establishing a separate patient-centred pathway based on shared decision-making. This framework supports consistent, evidence-based treat-to-target care.

articles.title: Oropouche virus infection in pregnant women in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a prospective cohort study.
authors: Rio de Janeiro OROV Maternal–Infant Consortium (RJOrMIC)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although adverse maternal and infant outcomes have been reported following Oropouche virus infection, the frequencies of these outcomes have not been compared with those in uninfected pregnancies. We followed up pregnant women from areas with Oropouche virus transmission in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, to evaluate potential adverse maternal and infant outcomes following Oropouche virus exposure.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study across the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, we included pregnant women receiving prenatal care in municipalities with or at high risk of Oropouche virus outbreaks. Inclusion criteria were: ongoing risk of Oropouche virus infection at the time of prenatal visit; prenatal care at one of the participating sites; and willingness and ability to consent to and participate in the study. Exclusion criteria included infection with other arboviruses and fetal chromosomal abnormalities. Maternal blood, urine, and saliva were collected and tested for Oropouche virus by RT-PCR at enrolment and pregnancy endpoints. IgG and IgM serologies from maternal blood, placental tissue PCR, and immunohistochemistry were done. Confirmed infections were defined by: positive Oropouche virus PCR in blood, urine, saliva, or placenta; positive Oropouche virus placental immunohistochemistry; or Oropouche virus-specific IgM or IgG seroconversion. Possible infection was defined as one positive IgM result without a positive PCR. Negative results ruled out infection. Adverse maternal outcomes (reported by study investigators following up participants at study sites) were maternal death or disability, fetal loss, or haemorrhage; adverse infant outcomes were neonatal death or malformations. Relative risks adjusted for maternal age, other congenital infections, and use of tobacco, alcohol, and drugs during pregnancy for adverse maternal and infant outcomes were calculated.

FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Oct 8, 2025, 544 participants were enrolled: 130 (24%) with confirmed, 143 (26%) with possible, and 271 (50%) with no Oropouche virus infection. The median cycle threshold value of RT-PCR was 29·7 (IQR 25·8-34·9). Among the 130 women with confirmed infection, 104 (80%) developed detectable IgG antibodies. Symptoms were present in 80 (62%) women with confirmed infection, not necessarily associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0∙84 [95% credible interval 0∙51-1∙21]). By the end of follow-up, the pregnancies of 119 women with confirmed infection and 193 with no infection had resulted in livebirth, stillbirth, or miscarriage; 105 (88%) women with confirmed infection had livebirths and 187 (97%) women without infection had livebirths. Adverse maternal outcomes occurred in 21 (18%) women with confirmed infection and 14 (7%) women with no infection (aRR 2∙90 [1∙52-5∙35]). Fetal loss and haemorrhage risk were three times higher in women with confirmed infection than in those with no infection (aRR 3∙08 [1∙28-7∙29] for fetal loss and 2∙79 [1∙22-6∙21] for haemorrhage). The aRR for adverse infant outcomes was 9∙18 (1∙89-47∙88). CNS abnormalities occurred in eight (8%) infants of mothers with confirmed infection and in no infants of mothers with no infection.

INTERPRETATION: Oropouche virus infection during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal and infant outcomes, including maternal haemorrhage, fetal loss, and infant CNS abnormalities.

FUNDING: The Carlos Chagas Filho Foundation for Research Support of the State of Rio de Janeiro (FAPERJ), the National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq), the Brazilian Ministry of Health, the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz), and the European Health and Digital Executive Agency.

TRANSLATION: For the Portuguese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Infectious African Swine Fever Virus in Spray-Dried Porcine Plasma Used as Feed Ingredient, South Korea, 2026.
articles.abstract: We detected African swine fever virus DNA in feed and spray-dried porcine plasma (SDPP) used as a feed ingredient in South Korea. Pigs inoculated with SDPP developed fatal infection. An isolate phylogenetically clustered with South Korea strains. Our findings highlight the need for strengthened risk management of animal-derived feed ingredients like SDPP.

articles.title: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion.
articles.abstract: Red-meat-containing diets are epidemiologically associated with diseases of chronic inflammation, while diets that restrict red meat improve health. Yet, it is uncertain how red meat incites inflammation. Here, we discover that ʟ-carnitine, an amino acid highly concentrated in skeletal muscle myocytes, drives inflammasome activation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged mice and LPS-primed murine and human macrophages. We find that extracellular ʟ-carnitine represses mevalonate synthesis, thereby triggering activation of the pyrin inflammasome, downstream of cellular import by the high-affinity ʟ-carnitine transporter OCTN2. We find that the inflammatory response to skeletal muscle injury also requires pyrin and OCTN2. Thus, in summary, we identify macrophages as sentinels of exogenous and endogenous extracellular ʟ-carnitine that serve as a proxy for skeletal myocyte damage, and we open the field to examine the mechanistic basis for how excess dietary intake of carnitine-rich food drives inflammatory disease.

articles.title: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females.
articles.abstract: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. We trace the origin of isoUDCA to a bacterial consortium, which is selectively enriched by estrogen through shaping a specialized intestinal microenvironment. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Individualized Cardiac Index-Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery: The PELICAN Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.

RESULTS: Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

articles.title: Feasibility, Safety and Efficacy of Outpatient Lipoabdominoplasty with Sedation, TAP Block, and Tumescent Anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative pain after abdominoplasty can reduce patient satisfaction, delay mobility, and increase complications like deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Multimodal analgesia, including transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks, improves pain control, reduces opioid use, improving recovery, minimizing DVT risks, and promoting early ambulation and recovery.

OBJECTIVE: This article examines the safety, effectiveness, and practical aspects of abdominoplasty under sedation and TAP block as an alternative to general anesthesia, detailing the anesthetic protocol and patient outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center case series encompassed all consecutive lipoabdominoplasty patients from December 2020 to June 2025. Epidemiology, procedures, medications, patient-reported outcomes, satisfaction, and complications were collected via standardized questionnaires, including BodyQ, Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS) and International Pain Outcome (IPO) questionnaire.

RESULTS: Forty patients (mean age 37 ± 11) underwent lipoabdominoplasty under conscious sedation and TAP-block; 45% also underwent breast surgery. During the first 24 postoperative hours, 31% of patients experienced at least one episode of severe pain, lasting a cumulative average of 2.4 hours. 90% reported minimal/no nausea. No antiemetics were required; 25% received one opioid dose. Analgesia satisfaction was 90%. Median discharge time was 2:42 h (interquartile range [IQR] 2:00-3:16). Appearance satisfaction was 100% (IQR 81-100%).

CONCLUSION: Lipoabdominoplasty with sedation, TAP block, and tumescent anesthesia can be safely performed in the outpatient setting, with minimal to no nausea, low to moderate pain, and great patient satisfaction. The evidence supports revisiting postoperative care pathways to ensure prudent utilization of hospital assets, like minimizing unnecessary inpatient observation, without compromising outcomes.Level of Evidence: IV.

articles.title: Substantial preoperative weight loss increases odds of healthcare utilization after reduction mammoplasty in obese patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with increased complications following reduction mammoplasty (RM). Preoperative weight loss is commonly recommended to reduce surgical risk, although it remains unclear whether obese patients who have recently lost weight experience outcomes comparable to their weight-stable obese counterparts. This study evaluated the impact of recent preoperative weight loss on postoperative outcomes following RM.

METHODS: Epic COSMOS was used to identify obese patients undergoing RM. Patients who lost ≥5% body weight within two years before surgery were compared with weight-stable controls. Postoperative complications were assessed. Propensity score matching and multivariable regression were used to adjust for covariates.

RESULTS: After matching, 7,874 patients were included in each cohort. Patients with substantial (>10% body weight) weight loss demonstrated highest risk of surgical site infection [SSI] (aOR 1.26; 95% CI 1.04 - 1.52) and more than double the risk of hospital readmission (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.31 - 3.25). Independent of weight loss, severe morbid obesity (BMI 40-50) was associated with increased risk of SSI (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.48 - 2.1), wound dehiscence (aOR 2.24, 95% CI 1.81 - 2.77), fat necrosis (aOR 1.51; 95% CI 1.11-2.01), and ED revisit (aOR 1.49, 95% CI 1.21 - 1.82).

CONCLUSION: In obese patients, preoperative weight loss exceeding 10% of body weight was associated with higher odds of SSI and hospital readmission following RM compared with weight-stable obese counterparts. Given the observational design and unmeasured factors including nutritional status and frailty, no broader inference regarding the effect of preoperative weight loss on surgical risk is drawn.

articles.title: Nanobody-Based Lateral Flow Assays: Applications, Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Nanobody-based lateral flow assays (LFAs) are an emerging class of point-of-care diagnostics that combine enhanced thermal stability, target affinity comparable to or in some cases exceeding that of conventional antibodies, and low-cost recombinant production of nanobodies with the versatility of conventional antibody-based detection formats. This review examines recent progress in nanobody engineering, assay architecture, and signal amplification strategies that improve analytical sensitivity, specificity, and multiplexing potential. Despite these advances, several technical and translational challenges persist, including broad analyte compatibility, difficulties in optimal nanobody pair selection, scalability of expression systems, and the need for robust and reproducible conjugation chemistries. The growing integration of computational modeling and AI-driven nanobody design has accelerated the discovery and optimization pipelines, yet standardized frameworks for validation and benchmarking remain scarce. Addressing these limitations will be important for the further clinical translation and commercial deployment of nanobody-based LFAs across diverse applications in infectious disease diagnostics, food safety testing, and environmental monitoring.

articles.title: From classroom to clinical practice: Education, training and preparedness for imaging people from prison in diagnostic radiography.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diagnostic radiographers perform examinations to support care for people from prison in acute hospitals, yet it remains unclear whether diagnostic radiography education in the UK adequately prepares students and practising radiographers to support this population. This study examined current education and provision of training, perceived preparedness and educational needs among diagnostic radiography students, HEI educators and practising diagnostic radiographers in the UK.

METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional study used an online structured questionnaire completed by diagnostic radiography students, practising diagnostic radiographers and higher education educators in the UK. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics. An inductive qualitative content analysis was completed for the open-ended responses, and categories were compared across participant groups to identify convergence and divergence.

RESULTS: Forty participants completed the questionnaire: 11 students, 8 educators and 21 practising diagnostic radiographers. Only two practising radiographers reported receiving relevant training during their radiography education. No student reported receiving specific programme education, although one received relevant information during clinical placement and no educator reported relevant curriculum content. Further education was supported by nine students, seven educators and 16 practising radiographers. Fifteen practising radiographers reported that their departments lacked relevant policies. Four overarching categories concerned safety and procedural knowledge; communication and psychosocial care; confidence and preparedness; and integrated education and specific organisational guidance.

CONCLUSION: Education and training provision was limited across all three groups, while organisational guidance varied. Participants identified safety and procedural knowledge and communication and psychosocial care as educational priorities, with confidence, preparedness and equitable care as intended outcomes.

IMPLICATION FOR PRACTICE: Proportionately integrating relevant content through academic teaching, simulation and supervised clinical learning, alongside CPD and departmental guidance, may strengthen safe, equitable and consistent imaging for people from prison.

articles.title: Psychological violence, subjective well-being, and burnout among healthcare workers: The roles of sleep disturbance and perceived occupational infection risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological violence (PCV), which includes verbal abuse, bullying, intimidation, sexual harassment and ethnic discrimination, is the most frequently reported form of workplace violence in health care and a well-documented correlate of burnout. Healthcare workers (HCWs) in infectious disease services face this psychosocial hazard alongside two further, structurally persistent conditions: impaired recovery through disturbed sleep, and the appraised risk of acquiring infection at work. How these demands combine with workers' personal psychological resources is not well understood.

OBJECTIVE: To examine (i) whether PCV exposure is associated with burnout, (ii) whether subjective well-being (SWB) functions as an intervening variable in that association, (iii) whether sleep disturbance is associated with burnout independently of SWB, and (iv) whether the strength of the SWB-burnout association depends on the level of perceived occupational infection risk.

METHODS: Cross-sectional survey of 675 HCWs (76.3% women) at a public tertiary infectious disease hospital in southern China (December 2022 - January 2023), a designated centre for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, hepatitis and, at the time of data collection, COVID-19. PCV exposure over the preceding 12 months was assessed with the ILO/ICN/WHO/PSI instrument; SWB with the WHO-5; burnout with the two-item abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory screen; sleep disturbance with three binary epidemiological items; and perceived occupational infection risk with a single validated item indexing appraised infection hazard in the respondent's own workplace. Conditional process analysis (ordinary least squares path analysis, 5000 bootstrap resamples) was adjusted for gender, age band, education, occupation, employment type, department and reported concern about workplace violence.

RESULTS: PCV was reported by 34.1% of participants and sleep disturbance by 53.3%. PCV exposure was positively associated with burnout (adjusted direct association b = 0.53, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.96, P = .015; total association b = 0.72, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.19). SWB was negatively associated with burnout (b = -0.13, P < .001) and accounted for an indirect association of 0.19 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.34), approximately 26% of the total. Sleep disturbance was independently associated with burnout after adjustment for SWB and all covariates (b = 0.46 per additional sleep symptom, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.68, P < .001). Perceived occupational infection risk moderated the SWB-burnout association (interaction b = -0.038, 95% CI -0.060 to -0.016, P < .001): the association between SWB and burnout was steeper at higher perceived risk (b = -0.085 at -1 SD; -0.133 at the mean; -0.181 at +1 SD), and the conditional indirect association rose correspondingly (0.12 to 0.26; index of moderated mediation 0.054, 95% CI 0.012 to 0.112).

CONCLUSIONS: In a workforce facing sustained occupational infection risk, PCV exposure, low SWB and disturbed sleep were each associated with greater burnout, and SWB differentiated burnout most sharply among workers appraising their workplace as most hazardous. Because the design is cross-sectional, the direction of the PCV-SWB-burnout sequence cannot be established, and reciprocal influence is likely. The findings support treating violence prevention, recovery-protective scheduling and infection-risk communication as complementary components of occupational mental health provision rather than as separate programmes.

articles.title: Slow-tempo piano music listening and short-term anxiety and burnout trajectories in a predominantly nursing sample of ICU healthcare workers: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare workers in intensive care units (ICUs) are chronically exposed to high-intensity, high-risk clinical environments, where anxiety and burnout are highly prevalent. Music listening is a low-burden, non-pharmacological supportive strategy with potential stress-reducing effects; however, randomized trials evaluating standardized slow-tempo piano music interventions among ICU healthcare workers remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare short-term trajectories in self-reported generalized anxiety symptoms and weighted MBI-GS burnout index values between ICU healthcare workers assigned to a slow-tempo piano music intervention and those assigned to a passive control condition.

METHODS: This single-center, open-label, two-group parallel randomized controlled trial was conducted in the ICUs of a tertiary hospital in China. A total of 126 ICU healthcare workers were enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the piano music group or the passive control group, with 63 participants in each group. The piano music group received a 2-week standardized slow-tempo piano music listening intervention consisting of four 30-minute sessions per week, for a total of eight sessions. The listening sessions were conducted outside ICU working hours, after the end of the participant's shift and before bedtime. The passive control group maintained their usual routines and received neither the study-specified music intervention nor a study-arranged 30-minute rest period. Anxiety and burnout were assessed after the 1st, 4th, and 8th sessions using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey. No outcome assessment was conducted before the first intervention session; therefore, the first assessment (T1) was a post-session assessment rather than a pre-intervention baseline. The study was retrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500097216).

RESULTS: All 126 randomized participants completed the three assessments. In the full sample, statistically significant group × time interactions were identified for GAD-7 scores (Wald χ2(2) = 46.29, p < .001) and the weighted MBI-GS burnout index (Wald χ2(2) = 6.78, p = .034). In the T1-adjusted analyses, the passive control group had higher GAD-7 scores than the piano music group at T2 (adjusted mean difference = 1.47, 95% CI [0.69, 2.25], p < .001), whereas the adjusted difference at T3 was not statistically significant (adjusted mean difference = 0.85, 95% CI [-0.03, 1.72], p = .057). The passive control group also had higher adjusted weighted MBI-GS burnout index values at T2 (adjusted mean difference = 0.52, 95% CI [0.24, 0.80], p < .001) and T3 (adjusted mean difference = 0.97, 95% CI [0.71, 1.24], p < .001). In the nurse-only sensitivity analysis, the group × time interaction remained statistically significant for GAD-7 scores but not for the weighted MBI-GS burnout index.

CONCLUSION: The piano music and passive control groups showed different short-term trajectories in self-reported anxiety symptoms and the weighted burnout index. However, because the study lacked a genuine pre-intervention assessment and used a passive control condition, the findings should be regarded as preliminary associations in short-term outcome trajectories, not as evidence of intervention efficacy or a specific effect of piano music. Further trials incorporating a pre-intervention baseline, active comparison conditions, and longer follow-up are warranted.

articles.title: Persistent C-reactive protein elevation and heart failure: Risk marker, mediator, or therapeutic target?
Adaptation to digital health applications and devices among caregivers and its impact on elderly care in community settings: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Digital health applications and devices are increasingly used to support community-based elderly care. However, evidence on caregivers' adaptation to these technologies and their impact on perceived health outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to examine caregivers' adaptation to digital health technologies, their usage behaviors, and factors associated with perceived health impact in community-based elderly care.

METHODS: An observational cross-sectional study was conducted among 160 caregivers working in Kantharawichai District, Maha Sarakham Province, Thailand. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing knowledge, behavioral use, adaptation, satisfaction, and perceived health impact. Descriptive statistics, chi-square analysis and Fisher's exact test were applied.

RESULTS: Caregivers frequently used health applications and digital health devices for monitoring elderly health and communicating with healthcare professionals. Overall satisfaction with digital health technologies was high, particularly regarding positive experiences with new technologies and organizational technological support (mean=3.94). Knowledge of reliable digital health information sources was high (92.5%), although awareness of medication reminder applications was limited (31.9%). Most caregivers demonstrated high adaptation to digital health technologies (63.7%). Sociodemographic characteristics were not significantly associated with perceived health impact (p>0.05), except for average family income (χ2=5.903, p=0.015; OR=1.108, 95% CI: 1.040-1.180). Technology-related factors showed strong associations with health impact, including satisfaction with digital health technologies (χ2=35.346, p<0.001) and behavioral use (χ2=4.437, p=0.035).

CONCLUSION: Caregivers demonstrated high adaptation and satisfaction with digital health technologies. Strengthening caregivers' digital competencies and supporting effective technology use may enhance community-based elderly care outcomes.

articles.title: A validated Nile Red fluorescence method following KOH/H₂O₂ digestion for microplastic detection in marine molluscs.
articles.abstract: Microplastic (MP) in marine ecosystems poses an increasing risk to the environment and human health. However standardized rapid methods for monitoring large numbers of samples are still lacking. This study validates a semi-automated Nile Red dye (NRD) fluorescence method combined with a two-step KOH/H₂O₂ digestion protocol for MP detection in marine molluscs. Twelve reference materials, including six synthetic polymer types (PE [two size fractions], PP, PA-66, PET, PMMA) and six natural materials (cotton, hemp, cellulose, wool, viscose, olive stone powder), were evaluated before and after digestion. Treatment resulted in 83.2 (± 4.8%) digestion of the natural reference, and reduced fluorescence intensity by 83.9 (± 14.9%). In comparison, the synthetic polymers lost only 13.0 ± 11.6% of their initial mass and 42.7 ± 18.4% of their fluorescence intensity, thus increasing the fluorescence discrimination ratio between synthetic and natural materials from 3-fold to 16.9-fold. The protocol retains the chemical integrity of the synthetic polymers (FTIR Hit Quality Index: 89.7-99.3%), which allows further reliable identification of the particles by FTIR. The protocol was applied to samples of Black Sea invertebrate organisms (M. galloprovincialis and R. venosa, 67 specimens) and achieved near-complete organic matter removal (>99.8%). The MP load was higher in M. galloprovincialis (median: 1.3 MPs g-1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-3.2; n = 27) than in Rapana venosa (median: 0 MPs g-1 WW; Q1-Q3: 0-0.2; n = 40). This validated workflow provides a reproducible and cost-effective approach for large-scale MP monitoring in marine bioindicator species.

articles.title: Plant-derived terpenoids in asthma: phytochemical and pharmacological perspectives from a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a chronic respiratory disorder characterized by airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), and remodeling. Structurally diverse terpenoids offer promising natural compounds with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties.

OBJECTIVE: To address this gap, this systematic review evaluated the therapeutic potential, mechanisms of action, and translational relevance of terpenoids in experimental asthma models.

SEARCH METHODS: Accordingly, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2013-2025) were searched for peer-reviewed in vivo studies evaluating pure herbal terpenoids in asthma. Two independent reviewers conducted study selection and data extraction.

DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: From the retrieved studies, data on terpenoids, animal models, and key asthmatic biomarkers (AHR, IgE, cytokines, immune cell infiltration, oxidative stress) were systematically extracted by phytochemical subclasses. Bias risk and methodological quality were evaluated using a modified Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation (SYRCLE)'s Risk of Bias tool.

MAIN RESULTS: On this basis, a total of 127 studies were included, predominantly using murine ovalbumin models. Terpenoids alleviated airway inflammation, hyperresponsiveness, and remodeling by regulating Th2 cytokines, IgE, and eosinophilic infiltration. Paeoniflorin, catalpol, farnesol, curcumol, cryptotanshinone, astragaloside IV, withaferin A, and crocin showed marked anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-remodeling effects by suppressing Th2 cytokines and modulating the NF-κB, Nrf2/HO-1, and TGF-β/Smad pathways, leading to improved airway function and restored redox homeostasis.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, terpenoids demonstrate preclinical therapeutic promise in mitigating airway hyperresponsiveness and inflammation via regulating Th2/Th1 balance, oxidative stress, and fibrotic signaling. Importantly, all of the evidence synthesized here derives exclusively from preclinical animal models; no clinical trials or human pharmacological data were available, and these terpenoids therefore remain experimental candidates whose clinical relevance is not yet established. However, translational potential is constrained by methodological limitations, particularly insufficient randomization, blinding, and sample size reporting, highlighting the need for more rigorous and standardized studies.

articles.title: Cerebral microhemorrhage and cognition in preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clarifying whether incident cerebral microhemorrhages (CMHs) contribute to early cognitive or functional decline is increasingly important in the context of anti-amyloid therapies.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether incident CMHs are associated with longitudinal changes in cognition and function in cognitively unimpaired individuals with elevated cerebral amyloid.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Post hoc analysis of individuals enrolled in the A4 study. Participants underwent serial MRI and cognitive assessments. Natural cubic spline models adjusted for baseline amyloid PET burden, age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 status.

MEASUREMENTS: Longitudinal change in the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC), Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB), Cognitive Function Index (CFI), and Activities of Daily Living.

RESULTS: Participants who developed ≥2 incident CMHs demonstrated greater longitudinal worsening in CDR-SB (estimate = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.09-0.80; P = .009) and CFI (estimate = 1.37; 95% CI, 0.11-2.60; P = .03), but not in PACC or ADCS ADL.

CONCLUSIONS: Incident CMH accumulation was associated with greater longitudinal worsening in global clinical status and participant-reported functional change, but not objective cognitive performance, among cognitively unimpaired individuals with elevated cerebral amyloid.

articles.title: Salmonella phage characterization and host-dependent responses relevant to cocktail formulation.
articles.abstract: This study was characterized infection efficiency, replication kinetics, environmental tolerance, and host-associated responses of six Salmonella phages (Yrd1, Yrd2, NB1, NB2, NB3, and FPU) as candidate parameters relevant to cocktail formulation. All phages belong to the class Caudoviricetes, comprising five myovirus-like and one siphovirus-like (NB3) morphotype, with capsid dimensions of 38-74 nm in width and 46-94 nm in length, and tail lengths of 78-109 nm. Multiplicity of infection (MOI) assays (0.001-10) showed that low MOI conditions (0.001-0.01) produced higher phage amplification, whereas a high MOI (10) markedly reduced amplification, indicating reduced infection efficiency at higher phage-to-host ratios. One-step growth analysis (MOI 0.1) showed phage-specific latent periods ranging from 10 to 30 min. Burst size ranged from 15 to 389 PFU/cell, with Yrd2 and NB1 showing the two highest values. Stability assays showed phage-specific responses. FPU displayed the broadest pH tolerance profile in the plotted comparison, retaining normalized infectivity from pH 5 to 10, and showed the highest plotted normalized infectivity at 50-60OC. All six phages showed near-zero normalized infectivity at pH 2-3, pH 11-12, and 70OC. Network-based interaction analysis showed broader OD-based inhibitory connectivity for selected cocktails than for monophages across PU13036, EN, KE, and TY. On PU519, specific FPU-containing combinations showed reduced inhibition, but these effects are not interpreted as mechanistic phage-phage antagonism or generalized beyond the tested host. Because the assays used different host backgrounds, these measurements provide candidate parameters for future cocktail-selection studies, but their predictive value requires further validation.

articles.title: Revealing the spatial heterogeneity of pine wilt disease spread in China through Geographical Pattern Causality analysis.
articles.abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) is one of the most destructive invasive forest diseases in China, yet the environmental drivers underlying its spatially heterogeneous spread remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize the spatial and temporal patterns of natural PWD dispersal, identify persistent hotspots, and determine region-specific environmental drivers of PWD habitat suitability. We developed an integrated framework combining dispersal screening, biomod2 ensemble modelling, SaTScan spatiotemporal scan statistics, and Geographical Pattern Causality (GPC) analysis to examine PWD spread and its environmental drivers at national and regional scales. Natural dispersal increased markedly after 2016 and reached a peak of 9728 newly affected subcompartments in 2020. At the national scale, Altitude, mean diurnal temperature range (Bio2), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were the dominant determinants of habitat suitability, with relative importance values of 27.52%, 25.29%, and 21.87%, respectively. However, GPC analysis confirmed pronounced spatial heterogeneity among the SaTScan-identified hotspot regions during the outbreak period. In hotspot region A, Aspect and Slope showed the strongest positive causal relationships on PWD suitability, with causal strengths of 0.361 and 0.284, respectively. In contrast, Altitude and Slope showed strong negative effects in hotspot region C, with strengths of 0.591 and 0.520, respectively. Wind speed showed negative causal relationships with PWD habitat suitability across all hotspot regions. These findings demonstrate that the environmental drivers of PWD vary substantially across spatial scales and hotspot regions, highlighting the importance of incorporating regional heterogeneity into PWD monitoring, risk assessment, and differentiated management.

articles.title: Decoding cutaneous injury-induced inflammation through single-cell RNA sequencing.
articles.abstract: Tissue repair requires rapid transitions in cellular states and robust cellular communication between tissue-resident cells and infiltrating immune cells. After injury, the amplitude and temporal regulation of inflammation must be efficiently coordinated to support subsequent tissue repair. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies and computational data analysis approaches have generated predictions about cellular states and communication that control inflammation, thereby promoting wound healing. Using skin as a clinically relevant model, we discuss how scRNA-seq has advanced our understanding of mechanisms that regulate inflammation after injury. In this review, we provide a detailed description of validated markers used to identify distinct cellular populations in murine and human skin and discuss how scRNA-seq has deepened our understanding of mechanisms regulating inflammation during acute wound healing. We further describe insights gained from scRNA-seq data generated under pathological conditions associated with dysfunctional inflammation and delayed wound healing, such as diabetes and aging. Future validation of these computational predictions and overcoming limitations associated with single-cell transcriptomics will provide greater clinical relevance for this technology that has increased the depth and rate of scientific discovery.

articles.title: Proteomics to advance meat research: Mapping and integrating biomarker-pathway interactions underlying beef marbling, color, and tenderness in longissimus muscle.
articles.abstract: Quality attributes of fresh meat represent crucial determinants shaping consumer perception and satisfaction, directly influencing purchase decisions and economic value. Over the last two decades, proteomics has enabled a deeper investigation of multiple beef quality traits, allowing to decipher the unknowns and elucidate biochemical mechanisms underlying post-mortem muscle processes and meat tenderization. Furthermore, increasing attention has been directed toward the identification of biomarkers capable of understanding biochemical changes in post-mortem muscle and their use for predicting the potential meat quality. Based on an integromics study, this work reviews on one hand the proteomic evidence on beef marbling, color, and tenderness to investigate the biological mechanisms underpinning beef quality, and on the other hand elucidates both common and trait-specific molecular pathways and compile recurrent protein biomarkers for multi-trait beef quality. A database has been built from 43 eligible proteomic-based studies with a focus on bovine longissimus muscle. From this dataset, a total of 79 putative biomarkers were identified, among which 11 were consistently identified across the three quality traits, representing a putative set of biomarkers for multi-trait beef quality. The key protein biomarkers generated in this integromics and the related biochemical pathways revealed thanks to innovative and adapted bioinformatics analyses have been thoroughly discussed. The most prominent include catalytic, metabolism & ATP metabolic processes, particularly those related to glycolysis, as well as muscle contraction, structure & associated proteins. These are followed by pathways involving chaperones and heat shock proteins, binding, transport & calcium homeostasis, oxidative stress, and proteolysis. However, differences in their relative contributions were observed across the different beef quality traits.

articles.title: Operating Room Air Filtration-Sterilization and Surgical Infections: The ORACLE Randomized Trial in 110,538 Surgeries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical infections are the most common nosocomial infections and cause substantial morbidity and mortality. Operating rooms are relatively clean, but far from sterile. An unknown fraction of infections result from wound contamination by air-borne bacteria. We therefore tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces wound infections and related complications.

METHODS: Operating rooms, our clusters, were each randomized in each 4-week blocks to either active or identical-looking sham supplemental air sterilization. All investigators, clinicians, and patients were fully blinded to treatment. No other aspect of anesthetic or surgical management was proscribed. Intent-to-treat analysis was restricted to adults who had surgery lasting at least an hour without evidence of pre-existing wound infections. We tested the primary hypothesis that supplemental active purification reduces a collapsed (one or more) composite of surgical wound infections, infection-related complications, or death within 30 days after inpatient surgery. Secondarily, we tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces the same composite after combined inpatient and outpatient surgeries.

RESULTS: A total of 110,538 combined inpatients and outpatients were enrolled across 68 operating rooms, with 107,334 qualifying for analysis. At the third interim analysis, the futility boundary on the composite outcome was crossed for inpatients and for all patients. Enrollment thus stopped with 58,938 randomized inpatients. The primary composite outcome occurred in 8.1% (n=2,389) of inpatients randomized to active purification versus 8.2% (n=2,405) with sham purification: odds ratio 0.98 (95%CI: 0.92 to 1.05), P=0.609. Across all patients, the secondary composite outcome occurred in 5.5% (n=2,959 / 53,730) of active purification cases versus 5.6% (n=2,981 / 53,604) sham cases: odds ratio 0.98 (95% CI: 0.93 to 1.05), P=0.669). Treatment effect did not vary over the weeks in the randomized periods.

CONCLUSION: Supplemental active purification did not reduce surgical wound infections or mortality in surgical patients. Infection-control efforts might better focus on limiting direct wound contamination.Trial registration:A priori registration at ClinicTrials.gov: NCT04610294.Funding: Supported by a grant from ActivePure (Bristol, VA) to the Cleveland Clinic. The funder approved the original protocol which was written by the lead author. The funder was not involved in data acquisition, analysis, or manuscript preparation. A draft of the manuscript was provided to the funder as a courtesy.

articles.title: Skull infarction and chronic subdural exudates in a pediatric patient with sickle cell anemia: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull infarction is a rare sickle cell disease (SCD) complication. While epidural hematomas from calvarial infarction have been sporadically reported, subdural collections and sterile exudates mimicking intracranial empyema remain poorly characterized.

OBSERVATIONS: A 6-year-old boy with nonverbal autism and SCD presented with progressive periorbital swelling, fever, and extremity pain. CT raised concern for orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, and subdural empyema. MRI revealed a diffuse heterogeneous calvarial marrow signal with multifocal nonenhancement and restricted diffusion consistent with bone infarction, alongside right convexity subdural fluid and bilateral epidural and subperiosteal rim-enhancing collections demonstrating susceptibility artifacts. Emergency craniotomy and orbital exploration yielded hemosiderin-stained fluid, and necrotic bone without purulence. All operative cultures were negative. Postoperative imaging demonstrated expansion of the subdural collection to 8 mm with 6-7 mm of midline shift, managed with dexamethasone. Nine months later, the patient re-presented with recurrent subperiosteal hemorrhage without infection.

LESSONS: Calvarial infarction in SCD can produce sterile collections that mimic infectious processes. Intraoperative findings and culture data are essential in distinguishing these entities. Middle meningeal artery embolization warrants caution in SCD patients, given the risk of moyamoya vasculopathy. This case underscores the importance of a broad differential when evaluating SCD patients with periorbital swelling and intracranial collections. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26291.

articles.title: Optimal timing of surgical intervention for post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture: A comprehensive evidence review.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVentricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare but devastating complication of acute myocardial infarction, historically associated with extremely high mortality rates. The optimal timing of surgical repair-balancing the risks of operating on friable, acute necrosis against the dangers of progressive cardiogenic shock during a waiting period-remains a central clinical dilemma.MethodsA systematic narrative review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from 2000 to 2024 for studies comparing early (≤7 days) versus delayed (>7 days) surgical repair of post-MI VSR. Data were extracted on patient characteristics, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, surgical techniques, and clinical outcomes, including operative mortality, reoperation rates, and long-term survival.ResultsEvidence from contemporary observational studies confirms that delayed surgical repair is associated with significantly lower operative mortality compared to early repair, primarily due to superior tissue integrity and lower rates of residual shunt. However, this mortality gap has substantially narrowed in the contemporary era with routine use of advanced MCS, particularly veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and Impella devices. These technologies enable hemodynamic stabilization, transforming early repair from a salvage procedure to a more controlled intervention. Modern management has evolved from a rigid temporal dichotomy to a patient-tailored strategy emphasizing immediate stabilization, risk stratification, and selective MCS bridging to the optimal surgical window.ConclusionWhile delayed repair remains preferred for hemodynamically stable patients, early repair supported by advanced MCS represents a viable and often necessary strategy for patients with refractory shock. The decision paradigm has shifted toward "stabilize, support, then repair," requiring multidisciplinary heart team collaboration. Future directions include standardized MCS protocols, validated risk scores, and exploration of hybrid percutaneous-surgical approaches to further improve outcomes for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Sclerotherapy for slow-flow vascular malformations: An international survey of practice patterns and periprocedural management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Slow-flow vascular malformations (SFVMs) are rare congenital anomalies that cause significant morbidity. Currently, no evidence-based therapy exists to improve SFVM symptoms and reduce its relapse in the long-term. Sclerotherapy is central to management and widely practiced, yet comprehensive international data are limited and no standardized guidelines exist. We aimed to evaluate current practice patterns, focusing on sclerotherapy and multidisciplinary care.

METHODS: An international cross-sectional survey was distributed to experts in the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) network. The questionnaire addressed treatment indications, sclerosant use and availability, anesthesia, coagulation management, risk communication, and case-based decision-making. Responses were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Fifty-two physicians from 16 countries completed the survey. Respondents included interventional radiologists (69%), vascular medicine specialists (15%), and pediatric surgeons (8%) in academic centers (90%). Multidisciplinary consultation was reported by 92% of participants. Ethanol (67%), bleomycin (58%), and polidocanol (52%) were the most accessible, although ethanol was consistently rated as the most dangerous. Sclerosant choice varied by lesion type and scenario. The risks most frequently communicated were skin necrosis (92% for lymphatic malformations and 94% for venous malformations, respectively), pigmentary changes (70% and 75%), and nerve injury (68% and 75%), whereas systemic complications such as cardiovascular collapse (16% and 22%) or death (14% and 22%) were less often discussed. In children, general anesthesia was preferred (90% and 86%), whereas adults received local (49% and 41%) or general anesthesia (47% and 43%). Preprocedural coagulation testing and anticoagulation strategies showed marked heterogeneity, especially for venous malformations.

CONCLUSIONS: This survey demonstrates substantial variability in SFVM management, particularly regarding sclerosant selection, anesthesia, coagulation, periprocedural care, and risk communication, and identifies areas where future prospective and collaborative research will be needed before evidence-based recommendations can be developed.

articles.title: Design of Smart Antifouling Surfaces Using Enzyme-Responsive Surface Topographies.
articles.abstract: Biofilm accumulation on polymeric surfaces remains a persistent challenge in biomedical, industrial, and environmental systems. Here, we report an enzyme-responsive antifouling surface that integrates particle-generated topography with biologically activated surface renewal. Microparticles of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) and the chitinase-responsive polymer PHEVD were generated by mechanical abrasion and embedded into poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) to create polymer-composite surfaces with three-dimensionally distributed microparticles. PET served as a nonenzyme-responsive control while PHEVD provided an enzyme-degradable phase designed to respond to bacterial activity. Particle-containing PDMS surfaces significantly reduced 24 h Escherichia coli RP437/pRSH109 biofilm biomass, with 2000-grit PHEVD surfaces producing the strongest inhibition and reducing biomass by 86 ± 3% relative to flat PDMS. In contrast, Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 biofilm biomass after 24 h was not significantly reduced by either PET- or PHEVD-containing surfaces, indicating species-dependent early-stage antibiofilm behavior. However, after 7 days, PHEVD-containing surfaces significantly reduced mature PAO1 biofilm biomass. Under static culture, 600- and 2000-grit PHEVD surfaces reduced PAO1 biomass by 60.0 ± 5.5% and 71.0 ± 13.4%, respectively. Under shaking culture at 200 rpm, 600-grit PHEVD reduced retained PAO1 biomass by 93.6 ± 0.03% compared with flat PDMS and by 93.1 ± 0.03% compared with 600-grit PET. These results suggest that PHEVD-containing surfaces do not primarily prevent early PAO1 attachment but instead promote mature biofilm destabilization and removal. The observed 7-day PAO1 reduction is consistent with a coupled mechanism in which mechanical disturbance exposes PHEVD-rich domains, enabling PAO1-associated enzymatic activity to degrade the exposed PHEVD phase and weaken the biofilm-surface interface. This work establishes a facile strategy for designing biologically activated antifouling surfaces that convert microbial enzymatic activity into a trigger for prolonged biofilm control.

articles.title: National Alliance of Sickle Cell Disease Consensus Recommendations for Gene Therapy Implementation.
articles.abstract: Gene therapy for sickle cell disease (SCD) is rapidly advancing, with approved products and others in development, creating an urgent need to define how treatment centers can safely and effectively deliver this care. The National Alliance of Sickle Cell Centers (NASCC) conducted a modified Delphi consensus process involving 64 SCD centers across the United States with expertise in SCD care to identify essential elements required for gene therapy delivery and longitudinal patient management. Participants evaluated proposed elements of care delivery and center infrastructure, with consensus defined a priori as ³70% agreement on categorization. Twenty-four elements were identified as essential, and four as recommended for optimal implementation. These elements span clinical infrastructure, multidisciplinary care, treatment delivery, and longitudinal follow-up. The resulting framework provides a practical foundation to guide centers in developing and standardizing gene therapy programs for SCD. These consensus recommendations support safe, consistent, and high-quality care as access to gene therapy expands and may inform future clinical practice, program development, and research in this evolving field.

articles.title: Advancing Sickle Cell Disease Care Through Collaboration: the HHS and ASH Registry Leaders' Roundtable Initiative.
articles.abstract: Access to robust data is essential to addressing complex problems for people living with SCD; however, current data sources have significant limitations (1). Manual data capture programs are highly curated but are challenging to scale, while claims or EHR-based databases scale rapidly but face challenges with reliability and validity. There have been limited coordinated efforts to address programmatic redundancies and minimize burden for clinicians, researchers, and patients. In 2022 and 2023, three Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) Registry Leaders Roundtable sessions were convened by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in collaboration with the American Society of Hematology (ASH). HHS subsequently initiated development of an SCD-specific U.S. Core Data for Interoperability Plus program (USCDI+ SCD) (2). In this viewpoint, we argue that a strong framework for interoperability, linkages between existing data efforts, and targeted curation informed by clinical expertise are necessary components of a national SCD data infrastructure.

articles.title: Virtual Reality for Enhancing Self-Compassion and Reducing Burnout Among Mental Health Care Professionals: Protocol for a Pilot Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health care professionals working in high-demand clinical environments are frequently exposed to patient suffering and trauma, placing them at increased risk for burnout and secondary traumatic stress. Compassion-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (CF-CBT) has shown promise in reducing psychological distress and enhancing self-compassion; however, traditional delivery methods may be limited by time, accessibility, and resource constraints. Virtual reality (VR) may provide an immersive and accessible approach for delivering compassion-focused interventions.

OBJECTIVE: The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a self-administered VR-enhanced CF-CBT (VR-CF-CBT) intervention for mental health care professionals. Secondary exploratory objectives are to estimate changes in self-compassion, burnout, and secondary traumatic stress (STS), as well as between-group differences that can inform the design of a future definitive trial.

METHODS: A 2-arm randomized controlled pilot trial will be conducted among mental health care professionals. Participants will be randomized to either a VR-CF-CBT intervention or an active comparison condition consisting of self-guided CF-CBT delivered via digital booklets. Participants will complete 8 brief sessions (approximately 10 minutes each) over a 4- to 6-week period. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include changes in self-compassion, burnout, and STS measured using validated self-report instruments. Primary feasibility and acceptability outcomes will include recruitment, retention, intervention adherence, session completion, participant satisfaction, and scores on the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, and Feasibility of Intervention Measure.

RESULTS: The study was funded in April 2026. As of October 2026, 38 participants had provided consent and enrolled. Recruitment for a second wave of participants is ongoing, and data collection is in progress. Enrollment and data collection are expected to continue through 2026, with data analysis and dissemination of findings anticipated by spring 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study will provide information on the feasibility and acceptability of delivering CF-CBT through immersive VR to mental health care professionals. Findings will help identify whether modifications are needed before a larger trial and provide preliminary estimates to inform the design of future efficacy testing.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07666867; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07666867.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/105754.

articles.title: Tuberculosis Among Artisanal Miners in the Mulongo Health Zone, Democratic Republic of Congo: Unmatched Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, with 10.6 million new cases and 1.3 million deaths reported in 2022. Artisanal miners in sub‑Saharan Africa are particularly vulnerable due to poverty, overcrowded living conditions, and high HIV prevalence. In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), TB prevalence among miners is high, yet determinants remain insufficiently studied.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical factors associated with TB among artisanal miners in the Mulongo health zone, Haut‑Lomami Province, DRC.

METHODS: We conducted an unmatched case-control study among miners aged ≥15 years. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire covering socioeconomic, behavioral, and biomedical variables. Interviewers were blinded to TB status to minimize bias. Determinants were assessed using bivariate and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Poverty was strongly associated with TB (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.16, 95% CI 1.95-5.11; P<.001). Primary education was associated with increased TB risk (aOR 2.78, 95% CI 1.04-7.44; P=.04), while secondary education showed a borderline association (aOR 2.53, 95% CI 0.93-6.89; P=.07). Higher education was protective (aOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40-0.95; P=.03). Poor knowledge of TB transmission (aOR 2.11, 95% CI 1.16-3.83; P=.02), cause (aOR 1.79, 95% CI 1.00-3.20; P=.049), and diagnosis (aOR 2.49, 95% CI 1.48-4.17; P=.001) were consistently linked to higher vulnerability. HIV infection was significantly associated with TB (aOR 4.65, 95% CI 1.00-21.74; P=.049). Overcrowding was more frequent among TB cases, but in adjusted models, the association was borderline (aOR 1.65, 95% CI 0.95-2.85; P=.07). Tobacco use (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 0.83-2.61; P=.18), alcohol consumption (aOR 1.18, 95% CI 0.70-1.98; P=.54), and nutritional status (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 0.78-2.37; P=.28) were not significantly associated with TB.

CONCLUSIONS: TB among artisanal miners appears to be driven primarily by poverty, limited education, poor knowledge, and HIV infection. Overcrowding showed a suggestive but nonsignificant association. Integrated interventions should prioritize poverty alleviation, improved housing, tailored health education, and strengthened TB and HIV services, while further studies are needed to clarify the role of overcrowding and other contextual factors.

articles.title: Incorporating Data From Text Messages and Email Into Psychotherapy: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As digital communication becomes central to daily life, psychotherapy increasingly has access to patients' electronic media data. Although digital phenotyping has been widely studied, less is known about whether incorporating personal communication data, such as text messages, improves clinical outcomes in psychotherapy.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether integrating personalized text message data into psychotherapy improves depression, anxiety, health-related quality of life, and therapeutic alliance and to examine whether increased access to collateral information influences clinical decision-making.

METHODS: The Electronic Media and its Impact on Psychotherapy (EMAP) study was a randomized controlled trial conducted in adult and geriatric outpatient and partial hospitalization settings at an academic psychiatric hospital. Participants receiving psychotherapy for primary depression or anxiety (n=101) were randomized to electronic media-enhanced therapy (EME; n=52) or treatment as usual (TAU; n=49). In EME, research staff reviewed participants' text messages prior to sessions using personalized mood-related key terms and presented aggregated findings on a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)-compliant clinician dashboard. TAU participants received standard care without message review. Outcomes included change scores for the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and the Working Alliance Inventory-Short Revised (WAI-SR). Linear regression and nonparametric tests compared groups. Moderation analyses assessed whether the frequency of information access influenced treatment changes.

RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in anxiety or working alliance. Among participants with SF-36 follow-up data (n=65), EME participants demonstrated greater improvement in the pain subscale. Greater frequency of information access was associated with increased treatment-related changes in the EME group. Access to additional collateral information was associated with more clinical actions but not with improved distal outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating personalized text message data into short-term psychotherapy did not significantly improve depression or anxiety, and it neither improved nor worsened therapeutic alliance. However, access to greater amounts of collateral information, including electronic media, influenced clinical decision-making, suggesting nuanced and context-dependent effects.

articles.title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking.

OBJECTIVE: We synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non-AI-based systems in primary care settings.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review following the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and reported the results according to PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. We included experimental and quasi-experimental studies evaluating AI-CDSSs used by health care professionals in primary care settings, compared with usual care or non-AI-based decision support systems, and that reported clinician-, patient-, or system-level outcomes, or safety. An information specialist designed the search strategies and systematically reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from inception to June 27, 2025. Reviewers independently performed the selection and extraction processes. Data extraction was informed by the DECIDE-AI and CONSORT-AI (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-AI) reporting guidelines and the APPRAISE-AI tool. We independently assessed the risk of bias using Risk of Bias-2 or Risk of Bias in Non-Randomized Studies of Interventions. Owing to substantial heterogeneity, we conducted a synthesis without meta-analysis and explored heterogeneity using an adapted Non-Adoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread, and Sustainability-informed implementation-context classification. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251119225).

RESULTS: We identified 4074 records through database searches and 12 additional records through citation searching and trial registration checking. We included 14 records on 11 distinct studies, including 4 experimental and 7 quasi-experimental studies. The risk of bias was high in all experimental studies and serious to critical in quasi-experimental studies. AI-CDSSs showed more consistent positive effects on workflow-related outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, particularly for screening, referral, and alert optimization tasks. Patient-level effects were limited and inconsistent, particularly in more complex contexts involving heterogeneous conditions or preference-sensitive decisions. System-level outcomes were heterogeneous, with isolated improvements in service delivery and utilization outcomes. Safety evaluation was rare and poorly specified. Only 2 studies prespecified safety outcomes, and the reported safety information mainly involved technical malfunctions or self-reported side effects. No study reported clinician interaction measures such as agreement with, override of, or reliance on AI outputs. Interpretation of the findings is limited by substantial heterogeneity, short follow-up periods, predominantly high or critical risk of bias, and evidence derived exclusively from high-income countries.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-CDSSs in primary care may provide more consistent benefits for workflow-related and process-level outcomes in structured and protocolized decision contexts, while evidence on safety remains insufficient to support confident routine implementation. This systematic review reveals an important gap between the rapid development of AI-CDSSs and the lack of robust, comparable evidence to support their reliable use in primary care.

articles.title: Decellularized Extracellular Matrix Hydrogel With Schwann Cell Conditioned Medium Accelerates Skin Wound Healing in Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic nonhealing wounds represent a major complication of diabetes mellitus and impose a substantial clinical burden worldwide. Impaired reparative function of Schwann cells (SCs), along with the subsequent loss of paracrine repair signals, has been identified as a critical pathologic driver of delayed diabetic wound healing. Decellularized dermal matrix hydrogels have emerged as promising biomimetic platforms for local factor delivery and tissue regeneration. Nevertheless, the therapeutic potential of combining SC-derived conditioned medium with decellularized extracellular matrix hydrogels (dECMMA) for diabetic wound repair remains unexplored.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, a photocrosslinkable methacrylated porcine dermal dECMMA loaded with RSC96 SC conditioned medium (dECMMA@RC) was fabricated. The microstructure of the hydrogels was characterized through scanning electron microscopy. In vitro, cytocompatibility, cell proliferation, and migration were evaluated in L929 fibroblasts, and pro-angiogenic capacity was assessed using a human umbilical vein endothelial cell tube formation assay. In vivo, full-thickness skin wounds were established in streptozotocin-induced type 1 diabetic mice. Wound healing outcomes were systematically evaluated by gross observation, histologic staining, immunofluorescence, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction.

RESULTS: The dECMMA@RC hydrogel maintained a favorable porous microstructure and exhibited no obvious cytotoxicity. Compared with the control and pure dECMMA groups, dECMMA@RC significantly promoted L929 cell proliferation and migration, as well as capillary-like tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells in vitro. In diabetic mice, dECMMA@RC treatment markedly accelerated wound closure, enhanced reepithelialization, and increased the number of regenerated hair follicles and sebaceous glands. Mechanistic analysis revealed that dECMMA@RC downregulated the mRNA levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor alpha), and upregulated the expression of angiogenic markers (CD31, VEGF-A) and neuroregenerative markers (growth associated protein 43, nerve growth factor) in wound tissues.

CONCLUSIONS: The dECMMA@RC composite hydrogel effectively accelerates diabetic wound healing through the synergistic effects of anti-inflammation, pro-angiogenesis, and neuroregeneration. This strategy provides a novel and feasible approach for the development of bioactive dressings for chronic diabetic wounds.

articles.title: Physiological Responses, Exercise Intensity, and Enjoyment During Ring Fit Adventure in Adults With Chronic Diseases: Single-Arm, Pre-Post Experimental Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and insufficient muscle-strengthening exercise remain important public health concerns among adults with chronic diseases. Active video games may offer an accessible way to support exercise participation, but many may not provide sufficient exercise intensity to produce meaningful physiological responses. Ring Fit Adventure (RFA) is an active video game that combines aerobic and resistance-based exercise. However, little is known about its physiological demands among adults with chronic diseases.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study aimed to examine the acute physiological responses, exercise intensity, perceived exertion, and enjoyment during RFA gameplay in adults with stable chronic diseases.

METHODS: A single-arm, pre-post experimental study was conducted among 20 adults aged 40 to 65 years with at least one chronic disease. Participants were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling from a hospital-based setting and public recruitment channels. After baseline assessment and familiarization, participants completed 2 stages of RFA gameplay. Heart rate (HR) was continuously monitored, while blood pressure (BP), capillary blood glucose (BG), and the rate of perceived exertion were measured at baseline and immediately after each stage. Enjoyment was assessed using the Exergame Enjoyment Questionnaire (EEQ).

RESULTS: All 20 participants completed the study, with no adverse events or missing data. The mean age was 54.3 (95% CI 51.25-57.25) years, and 10 participants were male. Hypertension was the most common condition (n=14, 70%), followed by hyperlipidemia (n=11, 55%), obesity (n=8, 40%), and diabetes (n=5, 25%). The mean continuous HR during gameplay was 111.6 (95% CI 102.6-120.6) bpm, corresponding to 67.2% of the age-predicted maximum HR, while peak HR reached 138.6 (95% CI 128.9-148.3) bpm, corresponding to 83.5% of the age-predicted maximum HR. HR increased significantly after World 1 by 16.7 (95% CI 11.42-21.88; P<.001) bpm and after World 2 by 20.7 (95% CI 13.28-28.12; P<.001) bpm. Rate of perceived exertion also increased significantly after World 1 by 2.83 (95% CI 2.32-3.33; P<.001) points and after World 2 by 3.75 (95% CI 3.18-4.32; P<.001) points. Capillary BG decreased after World 1 by 1.4 (95% CI -1.95 to 0.78; P<.001) mmol/L and after World 2 by 1.6 (95% CI -2.46 to -0.80; P=.01) mmol/L, with no hypoglycemic events. No significant changes were observed in systolic or diastolic BP. The mean enjoyment score was 77.6 out of 100 (95% CI 74.7-80.5).
