CONCLUSIONS: RFA elicited moderate average exercise intensity with periods of vigorous intensity, reductions in capillary BG, stable postexercise BP, and high enjoyment among adults with stable chronic diseases. These findings suggest that RFA may be a feasible and engaging home-based exercise option for this population. However, the small, heterogeneous sample, absence of a control condition, and single-session design limit generalizability. Larger controlled longitudinal studies are needed to determine its effects on exercise adherence, physical activity levels, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

articles.title: Not All Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis Is Equal: Site-Specific Mortality in a National Indian Cohort.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: Among 777,512 Indian adults with extrapulmonary tuberculosis, in-treatment mortality varied over tenfold by site, highest for tuberculous meningitis (adjusted odds ratio 12.48 vs. lymph node TB), miliary (5.17), and pericardial TB (3.86). Associations of HIV, diabetes, alcohol, and tobacco use with mortality varied across sites. Risk-stratified, comorbidity-aware care is warranted.

articles.title: Characterizing Behavioral Engagement in Smartphone Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) are increasingly popular for their ability to disseminate evidence-based treatments in a scalable, accessible way. Engagement with digital treatments is critical for effectiveness but remains poorly defined and measured. Most studies rely on subjective self-reports or 1 or 2 objective metrics, overlooking the multidimensional nature of how users interact with DMHIs.

OBJECTIVE: This exploratory secondary analysis applied a road map for comprehensive behavioral engagement measurement, developed for a prior smartphone cognitive behavioral therapy program for body dysmorphic disorder, to a 12-week randomized controlled trial of smartphone cognitive behavioral therapy for obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD; N=60). Aims were to (1) comprehensively characterize behavioral engagement using 21 objective app analytics-based variables, (2) identify distinct behavioral engagement profiles via cluster analysis, (3) assess whether profiles were differentially associated with OCD symptom change, and (4) evaluate associations between profiles and pretreatment credibility, expectancy, posttreatment satisfaction, and perceived app quality.

METHODS: Behavioral engagement was measured via 21 objective variables derived from app analytics, spanning use volume, frequency, feature usage, session duration, and temporal patterns. Hierarchical agglomerative cluster analysis identified engagement profiles. Associations between cluster membership and OCD severity change (Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale) were examined using hierarchical generalized linear mixed models. Objective measures were complemented with subjective self-reports: namely, cluster differences in treatment credibility, expectancy, satisfaction, and perceived app quality were examined using ANOVAs and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.

RESULTS: Cluster analysis indicated a 3-cluster solution representing high (cluster 1: 21/60, 35%), moderate (cluster 2: 31/60, 52%), and low (cluster 3: 8/60, 13%) app users. All 3 clusters experienced significant reductions in OCD severity, with no significant differences in pre- to posttreatment Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale change across clusters. Descriptively, cluster 1 had a higher rate of treatment responders than cluster 3. While clusters 1 and 2 had similar perceptions of treatment credibility and expectancy at baseline and satisfaction at posttreatment, cluster 3 perceived the intervention as significantly less credible, had lower expectations, and reported significantly lower satisfaction than cluster 2. All clusters rated app quality as similarly high.

CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive behavioral engagement measurement is feasible and informative across different DMHIs and clinical populations. The finding that all engagement profiles showed comparable symptom improvement challenges simple dose-response assumptions and may suggest that multiple paths of engagement can be therapeutically beneficial; nonsignificant differences in improvement across clusters may also reflect limited power to detect differences. Pretreatment credibility and expectancy are associated with engagement patterns, identifying a potential modifiable intervention target.

articles.title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional triage relies on clinician judgment and limited information available at first contact. AI and machine learning (ML) may improve early risk stratification, whereas tele-triage and patient-facing tools primarily support remote assessment, access, and care routing.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of AI- and ML-assisted triage systems and summarize evidence on tele-triage, workflow, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes.

METHODS: Comparative studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, evaluating AI-, ML-, natural language processing-, telehealth-, or digitally enhanced triage. At first, clinical contacts were included. PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, preprint servers, trial registries, and conference proceedings were searched. Screening and data extraction were performed independently in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Clinically comparable area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) estimates were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis; heterogeneous diagnostic, operational, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes were summarized narratively. Exploratory scenario modeling projected effects per 10,000 emergency department (ED) visits.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies were included, comprising 13 studies in the quantitative evidence stream and 14 in the narrative synthesis. Four adult ED studies evaluating critical care or deterioration outcomes demonstrated high pooled discrimination for AI-assisted triage (AUC 0.874; 95% CI 0.845-0.898; I²=94.4%; 95% prediction interval 0.803-0.922). Four studies reported directly extractable within-study comparisons favoring AI-assisted models (AUC differences of 0.097, 0.120, 0.108, and 0.065), although these could not be pooled because paired variance estimates were unavailable. Admission/disposition studies reported AI-model AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.93 and were summarized descriptively because extreme heterogeneity precluded meaningful pooling. Two pediatric studies (AUCs of 0.85-0.99) were summarized descriptively. Prediction-model studies were primarily limited by deficiencies in model analysis, calibration reporting, and external validation. Narrative evidence suggested improved front-door operational metrics with tele-triage, including reported reductions of 15%-40% in time to clinical assessment and 2-8 percentage points in left-without-being-seen rates, whereas patient-facing symptom checkers generally favored sensitivity over specificity. Exploratory scenario modeling illustrated that, under specified prevalence and threshold assumptions, AI-assisted triage could be associated with 12-38 fewer missed critical illness cases and 45-120 additional false-positive escalations per 10,000 ED visits. Economic and equity findings were assumption-dependent projections rather than observed clinical, cost-effectiveness, or equity outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: AI- and ML-assisted triage models demonstrate promising discrimination for adult ED risk stratification; however, AUC-based discrimination does not establish superiority at clinically relevant decision thresholds, improved patient outcomes, or readiness for clinical implementation. Interpretation is limited by substantial heterogeneity, incomplete threshold-level performance and calibration reporting, limited external validation, and sparse pediatric evidence. Prospective multicenter validation, workflow assessment, subgroup calibration and equity auditing, and formal economic evaluation are required before routine implementation.

articles.title: Data-Driven Comorbidity Phenotypes and In-Hospital Outcomes Among Patients With Nonvariceal Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Formative Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing risk scores for nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding (NVUGIB) may not adequately represent the heterogeneity of coexisting chronic conditions. Routinely collected hospital discharge records may enable data-driven characterization of clinically meaningful comorbidity profiles.

OBJECTIVE: This formative study aimed to identify reproducible comorbidity profiles among patients hospitalized with NVUGIB and examine their associations with in-hospital outcomes and health care use.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3193 adults hospitalized with NVUGIB at a tertiary hospital in China between 2015 and 2025. Of 55 prespecified chronic conditions, 33 with a prevalence of at least 1% were included as binary clustering variables. Patients were randomly divided into an 80% training subset and a 20% held-out validation subset. Comorbidity profiles were identified in the training subset using a self-organizing map and Ward hierarchical clustering and then assigned to the validation subset using the fixed clustering solution. Profile reproducibility was evaluated by comparing condition prevalence vectors between subsets. Multivariable regression models assessed associations with severe in-hospital outcomes, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, length of stay, and hospital costs.

RESULTS: At least 1 selected comorbidity was recorded in 89.7% (2864/3193) of patients. Six profiles were identified: low-burden heterogeneous (cluster 1), non-upper gastrointestinal neoplastic-metastatic (cluster 2), circulatory-renal (cluster 3), cardiometabolic-renal (cluster 4), atherosclerotic-vascular (cluster 5), and rheumatologic-neurological (cluster 6). Profile composition was broadly reproducible between the training and validation subsets (weighted mean Spearman correlation=0.891, SD 0.04; P=.001). The circulatory-renal profile had the strongest associations with severe in-hospital outcomes (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.57, 95% CI 5.39-14.01), intensive care unit admission (aOR 10.38, 95% CI 4.87-25.76), and in-hospital death (aOR 4.66, 95% CI 1.97-13.75). The rheumatologic-neurological and cardiometabolic-renal profiles were also associated with higher odds of these outcomes. All 6 profiles were associated with longer hospital stays and higher hospital costs.

CONCLUSIONS: Using routinely collected hospital discharge records, we identified clinically interpretable comorbidity profiles among patients with NVUGIB. The profiles were broadly reproducible within the study population and showed different associations with clinical outcomes and resource use. Profile-based information may complement established risk assessment and could be examined further as an electronic health record-based approach to clinical management and resource planning.

articles.title: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia. Although several studies have proposed that vitamin D supplementation may improve insomnia symptoms, findings remain inconsistent, and evidence from Southeast Asian populations is limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of weekly vitamin D₃ supplementation in improving insomnia symptoms, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and functional outcomes among Malaysian women with vitamin D deficiency.

METHODS: This study is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomized placebo-controlled trial conducted among women aged 19-50 years with serum 25(OH)D levels <20 ng/mL and insomnia symptoms. Participants are randomized to receive either vitamin D₃ capsules (50,000 IU/wk) or placebo (1 capsule/wk) for 9 weeks. The study is conducted in a community setting. Primary outcomes include insomnia severity assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and sleep efficiency objectively assessed using actigraphy. Secondary outcomes include daytime sleepiness measured using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and functional outcomes assessed using the Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ-10). Assessments are conducted at baseline, midintervention, and postintervention.

RESULTS: Participant recruitment commenced in December 2023 and is expected to conclude in December 2026. As of July 2026, 42 participants had been screened, 33 eligible participants had been enrolled, 22 had completed the study procedures, 4 were in the intervention phase, and 1 had withdrawn due to loss of contact.

CONCLUSIONS: If the efficacy of vitamin D3 supplementation in alleviating insomnia symptoms is demonstrated, it might be proposed as a supplementary approach to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia. Screening for vitamin D deficiency may also be considered in individuals presenting with insomnia symptoms prior to initiating pharmacological treatment.

articles.title: Comment on Qiang et al. The Effectiveness of Diabetes Prevention Programs Delivered in Primary Care for Individuals With Prediabetes or at Risk of Developing Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

Comment on Johnsen et al. Achieving at Least 15% Weight Loss Within 2 Years of Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis Is Associated With Lower Risks of Macrovascular and Microvascular Complications: A U.K. Cohort Study.
Islet-exocrine crosstalk in diabetes: Distinguishing whole-pancreas pathology from causal communication.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To critically evaluate how communication between the endocrine and exocrine pancreas contributes to diabetes and to distinguish whole-pancreas involvement from mechanistically demonstrated crosstalk.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of anatomical, imaging, histological, molecular and experimental evidence on endocrine-exocrine communication, prioritising recent primary human and mechanistic studies.

RESULTS: Islets and exocrine tissue communicate through local vascular, neural, stromal and extracellular matrix routes. Diabetes is associated with distinct whole-pancreas phenotypes: type 1 diabetes (T1D) shows reduced pancreatic volume, acinar loss, exocrine immune infiltration and periductal or perivascular fibrosis, whereas type 2 diabetes (T2D) more often shows acinar-to-ductal metaplasia, lobular or parenchymal fibrosis, angiopathy and increased pancreatic fat fraction on imaging, although histological adiposity is inconsistent. The strongest mechanistic evidence supports insulin-mediated acinar protection, acinar protease effects on β-cells and transfer of mutant carboxyl ester lipase in maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 8 (MODY8), while stromal, matrix and immune signals represent important but less fully validated amplifying pathways. In T1D and T2D, crosstalk most plausibly acts as a stage-dependent amplifier rather than a universal initiating event.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes should be studied as a multicellular pancreatic disorder without interpreting associated pathology as evidence of causation. Longitudinal human studies and multicellular models that allow selective perturbation are required to identify clinically actionable interactions.

articles.title: Examining the Association Between Shift Length, Fatigue, and Perceived Safety in NNP Practice.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal nurse practitioners (NNPs) often work extended shifts to support continuity of care in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). Prolonged shift length has been associated with fatigue and safety risks in other healthcare populations; however, evidence specific to NNP practice remains limited.

PURPOSE: The purpose was to examine associations between shift length, self-reported fatigue, and safety-related outcomes among NNPs, and to evaluate how these outcomes vary by demographic and practice characteristics.

METHODS: This cross-sectional survey examined shift characteristics, self-reported fatigue, and safety-related outcomes among board-certified NNPs. Using a national certification mailing list, 6717 NNPs were invited; 623 initiated the survey, with analytic sample size varying by item. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression.

RESULTS: More than half of respondents (n = 190, 51%) preferred 24-hour shifts despite reporting fatigue-related concerns. Most respondents (n = 435, 85%) reported that unit census and acuity influence fatigue. Nearly half (49%) reported feeling unsafe to drive home at least once after working an extended shift (>16 hours). Years of experience, rather than age, were associated with fewer reported safety concerns. Safety perceptions varied by NICU level, with less experienced NNPs reporting greater impairment.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: Fatigue-related safety concerns varied by NICU level and clinical experience, while most respondents continued to prefer 24-hour shifts despite these concerns. These findings highlight the tension between workforce sustainability, provider preference, and safety within neonatal practice.

articles.title: Key safety outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors versus DPP-4 inhibitors in general and vulnerable participants with T2DM: A target trial emulation study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), a class of oral hypoglycaemic agents (OHAs), have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits. However, safety concerns may hinder their broader adoption, particularly among frail populations. We evaluated key safety outcomes associated with SGLT2i compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4i), an OHA class with low risks of complications.

METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation (TTE) study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) and enrolled participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Eligible participants were categorized according to newly initiated SGLT2i (n = 224,510) or newly initiated DPP4i (n = 698,012) with continuous use for at least 30 days. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used to balance baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the SGLT2i group showed significantly lower incidence rate (per person-years) of several safety outcomes than the DPP4i group, including urinary tract infection (UTI) (23.84‰ vs. 27.88‰; hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.84-0.87), fractures or falls (16.55‰ vs. 17.79‰; HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.91-0.95), acute kidney injury (AKI) (1.06‰ vs. 1.91‰; HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.51-0.59), bullous pemphigoid (0.02‰ vs. 0.07‰; HR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.23-0.54), and all-cause mortality (13.05‰ vs. 19.72‰; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.65-0.67). Conversely, the risk of genital infection was higher in the SGLT2i group (2.96‰ vs. 2.05‰; HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.38-1.51). These findings remained consistent in the per-protocol analysis, across most vulnerable subgroups and individual SGLT2i and DPP4i agents.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i, compared with DPP4i, demonstrated a favourable safety profile across most evaluated outcomes, except for genital infections.

articles.title: Infection in Pediatric Auditory Brainstem Implant: A Case Study and Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Safety and efficacy of pediatric auditory brainstem implants (ABI) are well established. Commonly reported complications include cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak and pseudomeningocele. Infection is rare but potentially serious due to intracranial location of the device. Data on pediatric ABI infections remain limited. We report a case of pediatric ABI infection and perform a scoping review of the literature.

DATABASES REVIEWED: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library.

METHODS: The patient's medical record was reviewed for clinical course and outcomes. A scoping review was conducted to summarize findings of studies reporting pediatric ABI-related infections.

RESULTS: A 12-year-old female with NF2-related schwannomatosis and bilateral vestibular schwannomas underwent urgent right tumor resection with ABI placement. She represented on postoperative day 13 with meningitis and collection surrounding the device. Surgical exploration revealed purulence involving the ABI pocket and paddle. Device preservation was achieved with washout, fat graft replacement, vancomycin powder application, and prolonged antibiotic therapy. For the scoping review, 961 studies were screened and 9 included, identifying 12 pediatric ABI infections. Five were managed with antibiotics alone, 3 required additional CSF diversion, and 4 necessitated surgical intervention.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric ABI infections are uncommon but potentially life-threatening, necessitating prompt recognition and aggressive management. Our scoping review revealed that pediatric ABI infections have been managed with antibiotics with or without surgical intervention, and infection-related ABI explantation in pediatric patients has not been reported. In our case, device preservation was achieved with washout, fat graft replacement, and intravenous and intrathecal antibiotics.

articles.title: Neonatal Cardiac Tamponade Related to Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter: A Rare Case Report.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are commonly used in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) to provide prolonged intravenous access for preterm and critically ill infants. They are generally preferred over surgically placed central venous catheters because of easier insertion and, in some settings, lower infection rates. However, rare but life-threatening complications may occur. Cardiac tamponade, resulting from catheter malposition or delayed migration with perforation of the superior vena cava (SVC) or cardiac wall, is one such complication. This case highlights the need for vigilant monitoring even when initial catheter placement is confirmed as correct.

CLINICAL FINDINGS: A male infant born at 32 weeks' gestation with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) required mechanical ventilation and surfactant therapy. A PICC was inserted through the right radial vein, and radiographic assessment confirmed appropriate positioning in the SVC. The infant initially improved. On day 10 of NICU admission, he developed sudden respiratory distress, hypotonia, bradycardia, and cardiovascular collapse.

DIAGNOSIS: Echocardiography demonstrated severe pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade due to SVC perforation by the PICC tip.

INTERVENTION AND OUTCOME: The catheter was immediately removed, and emergency pericardiocentesis was performed. Despite aggressive resuscitation, the infant died on day 11 of life.

PRACTICE RECOMMENDATIONS: Delayed perforation can occur days after apparently correct placement. Preventive strategies should include risk-stratified catheter positioning, preference for lower SVC tip placement, routine echocardiographic surveillance especially after the first week and enhanced staff training for early recognition of warning signs. Continuous quality improvement and readiness for emergency intervention are essential to improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Matriarchal Influence on Black Women's Decisions to Provide Mother's Own Milk for Preterm Infants: An Integrative Review.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black preterm infants cared for in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) are less likely to receive mothers' own milk (MOM) at NICU discharge than non-Black preterm infants. This disparity increases the risk of health and neurodevelopmental problems and their associated costs throughout the lifespan. One modifiable barrier to receipt of MOM at NICU discharge may lie within the role of Black maternal matriarchs; however, this role is not well characterized.

PURPOSE: To describe and synthesize evidence related to the Black matriarch's influence on a mother's decision to provide MOM for a preterm infant hospitalized in a NICU.

DATA SOURCES: We searched the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CENTRAL, PubMed, CINAHL, and Web of Science databases and reviewed reference lists of included articles.

STUDY SELECTION: A total of 139 articles were retrieved (n = 99 after deduplication), of which 2 met a priori criteria for inclusion.

DATA EXTRACTION: We conducted an integrative review, using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) checklist.

RESULTS: One key theme emerged: the Black matriarch serves as a barrier to continued MOM provision among mothers of preterm infants in the NICU, despite mothers perceiving the Black matriarch as supportive or helpful.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: Matriarchal influence over Black women's decision to provide MOM to their preterm infant hospitalized in the NICU likely serves as a barrier to continued MOM provision. Research priorities include developing culturally sensitive instruments to measure Black matriarchal support for MOM provision and conducting intergenerational studies.

articles.title: Association of Red Blood Transfusion With Necrotizing Enterocolitis in Very Low Birth-Weight Neonates: A 7-Year Retrospective Cohort Study in Saudi Arabia.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a multifactorial disorder of the gastrointestinal tract of very low birth-weight (VLBW) infants. Blood transfusions are suspected to be associated with NEC in this population.

PURPOSE: To examine the association between packed red blood cells (PRBCs) transfusion and NEC in VLBW neonates (less than 1500 gm) or less than 32 weeks.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of all VLBW neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH) from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2020.

RESULTS: Of 3018 newborns admitted to the NICU, 441 were VLBW neonates born at less than 32 weeks of gestational age (mean: 29 weeks ± 2.3; male: 220, 49.9%). The sample was divided into 2 groups: those who developed NEC 49 (11.1%) and those who did not develop NEC 392 (88.9%). Infants who developed NEC had significantly lower birth weight, gestational age (GA), and initial hematocrit (P < 0.05). Although blood transfusions were more often noted in those who developed NEC 7.4% versus 32.1% (P < 0.01), only sepsis showed significant associations with NEC, OR 8.2 (3.893-17.259) after adjusting for other studied risk factors.

IMPLICATION FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: PRBC transfusion was not associated with an increased risk of NEC in VLBW neonates. Sepsis was the only variable found to be significantly associated with NEC. Future prospective cohort studies to assess the role of anemia, the timing of PRBC transfusion, and the number of transfusions on incidence of NEC are needed.

articles.title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
articles.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

articles.title: Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence in Pre-Implant Radiographic Imaging: A Structured Qualitative Synthesis of Performance Across Imaging Modalities and AI Architectures.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate contemporary evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) applied to radiographic imaging for pre-implant dental assessment and treatment planning, with emphasis on the distinction between technical algorithmic performance and clinically oriented planning outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Peer-reviewed original studies published from January 2021 through December 2025 were identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, and supplementary searches. Eligible studies used radiographic imaging as an integral input to AI for pre-implant assessment, planning, decision support, virtual positioning, or outcome prediction. Reporting completeness was assessed with CLAIM 2024. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-3 for eligible diagnostic/test-accuracy studies, PROBAST+AI for the prognostic prediction-model study, and RoB 2 for the randomized clinical study. Owing to heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively.

RESULTS: Thirty-six studies were included. CBCT was the predominant modality. Applications included anatomical detection and segmentation, bone assessment, decision support, implant-position prediction, automated virtual placement, workflow integration, and preoperative outcome prediction. Segmentation and anatomical-analysis studies generally reported high task-specific performance, while clinically oriented positional accuracy and planning outcomes were more variable. AI frequently reduced workflow time. QUADAS-3 was applicable to five studies; four had high overall risk of bias and one unclear risk. The prognostic prediction-model and randomized clinical studies also had high risk of bias under their respective tools.

CONCLUSIONS: AI shows greatest current support for anatomical analysis and selected workflow tasks. Evidence for autonomous implant positioning and outcome prediction remains limited and heterogeneous. Current findings support clinician-supervised integration, with further multicenter external testing, standardized clinically meaningful outcomes, reproducibility, and prospective evaluation required before broader routine implementation.

articles.title: Perspectives of Orthopaedic Trauma Association Members on Firearm Injury Prevention: Results from a 2025 Membership Survey.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Firearm injury has become an escalating public health crisis in the United States and is now the leading cause of death among children and adolescents who are 1 to 19 years of age. Orthopaedic trauma surgeons frequently manage the complex sequelae of these injuries and are increasingly engaged in prevention advocacy. This study aimed to characterize the perspectives of the Orthopaedic Trauma Association (OTA) members on firearm ownership, injury prevention, and the organization's advocacy role.

METHODS: An anonymous, cross-sectional, web-based survey was distributed to all 3,721 active OTA members between April 10 and July 7, 2025. The questionnaire, which included 27 numbered items and 7 additional open-ended comment prompts and was adapted from prior surveys by the American College of Surgeons (ACS) and the American Association of Neurological Surgeons (AANS), assessed demographic characteristics, firearm ownership and storage practices, clinical exposure, prior safety training, and views on firearm injury prevention and OTA advocacy. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses, which were contextualized within published ACS and AANS findings.

RESULTS: A total of 503 respondents (13.5% response rate) completed the survey. Among 412 clinically active respondents, 95.6% (394) reported treating firearm-related injuries. Nearly one-half (47.4%) of respondents owned a firearm, yet 85.3% supported OTA-led, nonpartisan advocacy to reduce firearm injuries, deaths, and disability, comparable with support rates in ACS studies (85.5%) and AANS studies (78.7%). Respondents emphasized firearm safety training, secure storage, and integrating mental health into prevention strategies as priorities. Qualitative responses underscored the importance of evidence-based, nonpartisan engagement sensitive to regional and legal contexts.

CONCLUSIONS: OTA members broadly endorse firearm injury prevention as a public health priority. With nearly one-half of the respondents to our survey reporting firearm ownership, similar to rates in other surgical specialties, respondents expressed strong support for training, secure storage, and advocacy initiatives, reflecting a balanced, nonpartisan approach to firearm injury prevention. These findings establish a baseline for ongoing OTA-led efforts and align the organization with broader multidisciplinary prevention initiatives.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level V. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: Safety-Net Hospitals Have Increased Costs of Care Following Acoustic Neuroma Surgery.
articles.journal: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether safety-net hospital (SNH) status is associated with differences in patient characteristics, postoperative complications, and hospitalization costs following acoustic neuroma resection.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of a nationally representative inpatient database.

SETTING: United States acute care hospitals participating in the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Inpatient Sample (NIS).

PATIENTS: Adults (18 y or older) undergoing surgical excision of an acoustic neuroma from 2001 to 2021, identified using ICD-9-CM 04.01 and ICD-10-PCS 00BN0ZZ. Patients with neurofibromatosis type 2 were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: Craniotomy for excision of acoustic neuroma.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Postoperative surgical/CNS and medical complications; total inpatient hospitalization costs.

RESULTS: The cohort included 50,991 admissions, of which 13,245 (26.0%) occurred at SNHs. SNH patients were more likely to have Medicaid insurance (8.9% vs. 4.2%) and lower household income. On univariate analysis, SNHs had higher rates of hydrocephalus (6.0% vs. 3.8%), dysphagia (4.3% vs. 2.2%), pulmonary edema (2.1% vs. 1.1%), and sepsis (0.9% vs. 0.2%). After multivariable adjustment, SNH care remained independently associated with increased odds of medical complications (OR: 1.30; 95% CI: 1.01-1.70; P=0.04) but not surgical/CNS complications (OR: 1.10; P=0.23). Mean hospitalization costs were higher in SNHs ($42,749 vs. $36,456; P=0.003), and SNH status independently increased costs by $35,679 per admission (P=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: SNHs care for socioeconomically vulnerable patients undergoing acoustic neuroma resection and experience higher medical complication rates and significantly increased hospitalization costs. These findings highlight the need for resource-informed policy efforts and targeted support to sustain equitable access to complex neurotologic surgery.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: When Human Tissue Meets the Driveline: Implications of Tissue Integration to Combat Driveline Infections.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Driveline infection remains a common complication of ventricular assist device (VAD) therapy. These infections often progress from the exit site through the subcutaneous tract to the deeper tunnel and, in severe cases, the pocket, underscoring the vulnerability of the driveline-tissue interface. In this review, we examine the biological and mechanical factors governing tissue-driveline interactions and their implications for tissue integration of the implanted driveline. Dysregulated inflammation, impaired vascular maturation, abnormal extracellular matrix remodeling, repetitive micromotion and traction, and biomaterial-tissue mismatch may all compromise optimal tissue ingrowth of the driveline. Insufficient tissue integration can lead to the formation of microgaps within the driveline tunnel, providing a potential niche for microbial colonization and biofilm formation, thereby contributing to persistent driveline infections. Recognizing the potential association between inadequate tissue integration and the occurrence of driveline infection shifts the focus from microbial eradication alone toward optimizing driveline-tissue interactions across different segments of the driveline. Such an approach may help reduce the incidence of driveline infections in patients requiring long-term VAD support. Finally, strategies to promote tissue integration and long-term driveline stability, including driveline surface engineering, modulation of physicochemical properties, and optimization of surgical techniques, are discussed.

articles.title: Identifying the Content and Pedagogical Practices Used by Educators Teaching Stuttering and Cluttering Modules.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research has demonstrated that many speech-language pathologists (SLPs) have reported having reduced knowledge and competence in the assessment and intervention of children and adults who stutter and clutter. One potential reason for this is embedded in a suboptimal educational foundation at a university level.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify the content taught and the pedagogical practices used by speech-language pathology educators teaching a module on stuttering and cluttering as part of an undergraduate or postgraduate program in speech-language pathology.

METHOD: An online survey was developed by the authors, and questions reflected the All Ireland Society for Higher Education (AISHE) model for module design. Participants were recruited in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Participants' qualitative responses were analyzed using inductive content analysis.

RESULTS: Eighty-six educators completed the survey. Descriptive data, including qualitative findings, were reported on the seven components of the AISHE model. Self-reported expertise in stuttering or cluttering was associated with greater amount of teaching content (p = .018). Participants reported teaching significantly more about stuttering than cluttering (p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified the range of content and pedagogical practices used by educators delivering stuttering and cluttering modules. Results highlighted that educators with expertise in stuttering and/or cluttering taught a higher number of content areas.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34556784.

articles.title: Demographic and clinical factors associated with Syphilis treatment initiation in a tribal health system: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) individuals are disproportionately burdened by syphilis compared with other racial and ethnic groups. Early syphilis treatment is important to reduce transmission and prevent negative health outcomes. Understanding the characteristics of individuals who test positive and the factors associated with initiating treatment will support syphilis prevention and treatment efforts.

METHODS: Cherokee Nation conducted a retrospective cohort study of individuals who tested positive for syphilis between 2016 and 2023. Data were collected from electronic health records and analyzed descriptively using counts and percentages and inferentially using Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Overall, 356 individuals tested positive for syphilis and 314 (88.2%) initiated treatment. Most individuals who tested positive were ≤ 34 years (60.7%), single (83.4%), diagnosed during the COVID-19 pandemic (75.8%), residing in a county with a Cherokee Nation clinic (84.3%), and had a non-emergency healthcare visit within one year (70.5%). Approximately half (52.0%) had documented substance use and 31.2% had an STI co-infection within one year. Individuals diagnosed outside of an emergency department or urgent care setting had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those diagnosed in an emergency department or urgent care setting (aOR=2.01, 95% CI: 1.02-3.97). Individuals with an STI co-infection had higher odds of initiating treatment compared with those without an STI co-infection (aOR=2.96, 95% CI: 1.19-7.33).

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that focusing public health and clinical syphilis treatment efforts on emergency department and urgent care providers and patients may increase syphilis treatment initiation.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Dextrocardia: Lessons From a Complex Redo Case.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Dextrocardia with situs solitus poses significant surgical challenges for left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, particularly in patients with prior sternotomy and complex valvular disease. We report on a 60 year old man with dextrocardia, advanced heart failure, prior mechanical mitral valve replacement, and bicuspid aortic valve disease who underwent successful Corheart 6 LVAD implantation during redo sternotomy with concomitant bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement. Intraoperative findings included extensive pannus/thrombus on the mechanical mitral prosthesis (causing relative stenosis) and an unsuspected 10 g left atrial thrombus, both of which were removed. Total cardiopulmonary bypass time was 330 minutes, and aortic cross‑clamp time was 233 minutes. Postoperative acute kidney injury requiring dialysis resolved, and the patient was discharged after 137 days. At 1 year follow-up, the left ventricular end-diastolic diameter decreased from 69 to 66 mm, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) remained stable (28-25%), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class improved from IIIb‑IV to II, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) recovered from 32 ml/min at 9 months to 51 ml/min at 1 year.

articles.title: Integrated Bedside Hemodynamic Assessment and Monitoring of Venous Congestion With Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS): A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: This review evaluates the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score as a bedside tool for quantifying systemic venous congestion and predicting congestive end-organ injury, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI). By assessing flow patterns in the hepatic, portal, and renal veins alongside inferior vena cava (IVC) size, VExUS enables serial monitoring of congestion trajectories. While highly prognostic in heart failure, its predictive performance varies in more heterogeneous populations. Ultimately, integrating VExUS with cardiac output indices may help clinicians identify specific hemodynamic phenotypes, guiding targeted, individualized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Weathering the storm: Predictors and resource burden of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity after severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reported incidence of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) after severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) approaches one-third, largely from cohorts that excluded early deaths. Predictors and resource consequences remain unclear. We identified predictors of PSH development and associations between diagnosis, PSH Assessment Measure (PSH-AM) subscores [clinical features scale (CFS) and diagnosis likelihood tool (DLT)], and resource utilization.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary care center intensive care unit (ICU) (October 2020-September 2025), stratified by PSH diagnosis. Two reviewers assigned PSH-AM scores. PSH cannot be diagnosed until the syndrome declares itself over days, so exposure is conditioned on survival; mortality is reported descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of PSH diagnosis. Log-transformed linear regressions estimated associations of PSH diagnosis and subscores with hospital length of stay (LOS), ICU LOS, and ventilator days. Thirty-day composite outcomes, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and landmark analysis evaluated robustness.

RESULTS: Of 509 patients with severe TBI, 86 (17%) developed PSH. Younger age [odds ratio (OR): 0.97 (95% CI: 0.96-0.98); P<0.001) and higher ISS [1.05 (1.02-1.07); P<0.001] independently predicted PSH. PSH was associated with longer hospital LOS (372.9%), ICU LOS (278.3%), and more ventilator days (266.4%; all P<0.001). Mortality was 11.6% (PSH) versus 35.9% (non-PSH). IPTW demonstrated PSH had fewer days alive and out of hospital (-46.8%; P<0.001) and landmark analysis highlighted fewer ventilator-free days (-40.2%; P=0.0097) and ICU-free days (-46.9%; P<0.001). Higher DLT subscores were associated with longer hospital (36.3%; P=0.001) and ICU (23.3%; P=0.005) stays, whereas the CFS subscore showed no associations.

CONCLUSIONS: The PSH diagnosis is contingent on survival. Younger patients with severe TBI who survive their initial injuries are more likely to develop PSH and occupy hospital beds meaningfully longer. The diagnosis likelihood tool, not the clinical features scale, tracks with that burden.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma screening in a tertiary hospital. What are we missing?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Screening for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) aims to detect early tumors, with a positive impact on survival. In clinical practice there are several challenges on the application of HCC screening: patients with unknown liver disease, poor patient adherence or problems in the health care system, leading to an underperformance. We aim to evaluate the performance of the HCC screening, the reasons of missed or delayed diagnosis, and prognostic implications in patients with HCC in a tertiary center.

METHODS: Retrospective study including patients with an HCC diagnosis, that have been discussed by a liver tumors board from 2020 to 2023 in a tertiary hospital. HCC screening was defined according to the EASL recommendations. Considering the target population for screening, subgroups were considered and compared: (a) diagnosed through screening; (b) missed screening due to suboptimal patient adherence and/or systemic healthcare inefficiencies; (c) undiagnosed advanced chronic liver disease (uACLD), that would have indication for surveillance if already diagnosed. For patients diagnosed through screening, we considered a margin of 2 months (8 months) as "complete surveillance" and between 8 to 12 months as "incomplete surveillance". To access the survival benefit, we compared the overall survival of the screened population and those do not diagnose through screening.

RESULTS: We included 174 patients, 136 had advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD): 70% Child-Pugh (CP) A; 20% CP B; 10% CP C. The most common etiologic factor was excessive alcohol consumption (37%). The proportion of patients diagnosed in screening was 26%. Regarding Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage at diagnosis, 4% BCLC-0, 37% BCLC-A, 10% BCLC-B, 33% BCLC-C and 15% BCLC-D. Patients in subgroup (a) had HCC diagnosed at earlier stages (BCLC-0 and BCLC-A). The subgroup (c) had a higher proportion CP B and C (p = 0.008), vascular invasion (p = 0.01), extrahepatic involvement (p = 0.052) and hepatic dysfunction according to ALBI score (p < 0.001) at time of diagnosis. Overall survival was significantly higher for screened group.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort, only about a quarter of HCC cases were diagnosed through screening, with impact on survival. Among patients with indication for screening, only one third achieved diagnostic yield. Our findings emphasize the need to improve HCC screening strategies and the pivotal role of primary care in the early diagnosis of underlying liver disease.

articles.title: Prolonged low-level inter-human mpox transmission in Nigeria prior to the global outbreak in 2022: a mathematical modelling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2022 global mpox outbreak was linked to clade IIb viruses that previously circulated in Nigeria. Genomic evidence suggests that, in Nigeria, sustained human-to-human transmission may have begun as early as 2016.

METHODS: Using a stochastic branching process model, we investigated the conditions under which mpox could have persisted at low levels in Nigeria between 2016 and April 2022 without triggering a clearly recognized outbreak and quantified the potential hidden burden of infection and international exportation.

RESULTS: We found that when R is close to 1 and secondary infections show low variability (low heterogeneity, i.e. no superspreading), sustained but slow transmission can persist with non-negligible probability. Under our baseline modelling assumptions (R = 1.0, Poisson offspring distribution), 9% of simulations resulted in cryptic epidemics that lasted throughout the study period. Conditional on a trajectory being classified as cryptic under this scenario, the average epidemic size was 8,500 infections (95% prediction interval: 2,900-17,000) per cryptic epidemic, compared with 241 confirmed cases reported. This implies substantial under ascertainment with a detection rate of 2.8% (95% prediction interval: 1.4-8.3%). Estimated exportations to Europe and North America were consistent with the small number of documented travel-associated cases before 2022.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the plausibility of prolonged, low-level mpox transmission in Nigeria prior to the recognized global outbreak.

articles.title: Selective Systemic Responses During Aeromonas salmonicida Subsp. Salmonicida Infection in Northern Snakehead (Channa argus).
articles.abstract: Northern snakehead (Channa argus) is a bimodal air-breathing fish in which erythrocyte-associated parameters remain relatively stable during physiological challenges such as aerial exposure. However, whether this characteristic is maintained during systemic infection remains unclear. In this study, temporal host responses were characterized following experimental Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection by integrating haematological, leukocyte morphological, biochemical, and multi-tissue transcriptional analyses. Most erythrocyte-associated indices, including RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, and RDW, showed no significant temporal changes, whereas MON, GRA, and PLT exhibited significant responses. Morphologically abnormal leukocytes increased from approximately 7% in healthy fish to 56% at 6 days post-infection and remained above 50% through 8 days, indicating persistent leukocyte-associated cellular alterations during infection. Biochemical responses were also selective, with changes primarily in protein- and metabolism-associated parameters. Transcriptional responses differed among peripheral blood, head kidney, spleen, and liver, including sustained casp7 suppression in the head kidney and distinct inflammatory and apoptosis-associated responses across tissues. Two-way ANOVA further identified significant tissue × time interactions for casp8, tnfα, and casp3. Collectively, A. salmonicida infection in northern snakehead was characterized by comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices, alongside selective leukocyte, biochemical, and tissue-dependent transcriptional responses. These findings highlight a contrasting blood response characterized by persistent leukocyte alterations despite comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices during bacterial infection in northern snakehead.

articles.title: The risk of radiotherapy toxicity in patients with laryngeal cancer: predictive factors and radiobiological modelling.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The assessment of post-radiation toxicity and quality of life is a crucial aspect of patient care. To evaluate and predict post-irradiation toxicity in a cohort of patients with laryngeal cancer, radiobiological modelling, biological and medical indicators, dose-volume variables, and radiomics were used.

METHODS: For the comprehensive evaluation, biological and medical factors, treatment plan doses, and radiomic features from pre-treatment CT images were analyzed using the PyRadiomics Python library. The Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) and Niemierko general equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) formalisms were applied for modelling and parameter estimation. The chi-square test assessed significance between categorical variables, while one-way ANOVA and the Spearman correlation were applied for continuous variables. All analyses were conducted using a custom Python 3.8 script.

RESULTS: Significant indicators impacting post-irradiation toxicity were identified. The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) comorbidity score, pre-treatment body weight loss, and weight loss during therapy were consistently associated with acute hematological, skin, and gastrointestinal toxicities. For late outcomes, pre-treatment weight loss, alcohol consumption, diabetes, and first symptoms emerged as significantly associated with overall and salivary gland toxicity. In addition, dose-volume parameters of the buccal mucosa, pharyngeal constrictor, and tongue correlated with acute mucositis, dysphagia, and xerostomia. Radiomic analysis revealed that larger and flatter target volumes were linked to increased toxicities, with PTV (Planning Target Volume) size strongly associated with hematological effects. The LKB model further identified parameters characterising the dose-response relationship for xerostomia, dysphagia, acute gastrointestinal toxicity, and overall acute toxicity.

CONCLUSION: The study identified significant factors influencing post-treatment health status and established LKB model parameters associated with radiation-induced complications.

articles.title: Prevalence of respiratory viruses among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia during the Hajj 2026: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hajj is one of the world's largest annual mass gatherings and provides favorable conditions for respiratory virus transmission because of intense crowding and extensive international travel. Contemporary post-pandemic molecular surveillance data remain limited. This study investigated the prevalence, determinants, and characteristics of respiratory virus detections among pilgrims during the 2026 Hajj season.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among adult domestic and international pilgrims over an extended peri-Hajj period (before, during and after Hajj) in the year 2026. Participants completed a structured questionnaire and provided combined nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swab specimens for multiplex real-time RT-PCR detection of common respiratory viruses. A subset of positive samples underwent genomic sequencing for viral subtype and variant characterization. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infection.

RESULTS: Among 412 enrolled pilgrims across all three phases, 58 (14.1%) tested positive for at least one respiratory virus. The prevalence of viral detection was 6.7% pre-Hajj, 16.0% during Hajj and 21.4% post-Hajj. Influenza A was the predominant virus (34.5%), followed by rhinovirus (24.1%), SARS-CoV-2 (20.7%), respiratory syncytial virus (13.8%), adenovirus (5.2%), and seasonal human coronaviruses (1.7%). Diabetes mellitus, chronic lung disease and smoking were independently associated with increased odds of respiratory virus detection. Conversely, receipt of pre-travel health advice, influenza vaccination and regular facemask use were independently associated with reduced odds of respiratory virus detection.

CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory virus transmission remains an important public health concern during Hajj. Strengthening pre-travel health advice, promoting influenza vaccination, and reinforcing personal preventive measures may reduce respiratory viral transmission during Hajj and other international mass gatherings.

articles.title: From individual markers to reformulable processing signatures in hypertension prevention.
Real-World Implementation of Telemonitoring-Supported Care Redesign in Type 1 Diabetes: Reduced Outpatient Utilization with Preserved Glycemic Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The widespread adoption of automated insulin delivery systems has created new opportunities for remote monitoring and data-driven redesign of diabetes care. However, real-world evidence on telemonitoring-supported care redesign remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a real-world before-after study in 109 individuals with type 1 diabetes treated with the MiniMed™ 780G automated insulin delivery system. Routine care was redesigned from multiple annual outpatient visits to a default annual combined physician-diabetes specialist nurse visit supported by structured remote monitoring through CareLink™ Premium. Outcomes were assessed over two consecutive 12-month periods before and after implementation.

RESULTS: Telemonitoring-supported care redesign reduced outpatient utilization from 4.92 to 2.49 visits per patient-year, representing an approximate 50% reduction. Glycemic outcomes remained stable, with no clinically meaningful change in HbA1c (56.3 ± 1.0 vs. 56.2 ± 1.0 mmol/mol) and preserved Time in Range (74.6 ± 0.7 vs. 72.4 ± 1.0%). No safety signal was identified, with one diabetic ketoacidosis event observed during each study period and no increase in severe adverse events. Treatment satisfaction improved (median DTSQc score 11.5), while satisfaction with telemonitoring-supported care and digital messaging was high.

CONCLUSIONS: Telemonitoring-supported care redesign enabled substantial reductions in outpatient utilization while maintaining glycemic control and participant satisfaction, with no safety signal identified. These findings support telemonitoring not merely as a clinical intervention but as an enabling infrastructure for organizational redesign of diabetes care.

articles.title: Impact of RapidAI® Implementation on Workflow Metrics and Access to Reperfusion Therapies in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence‑assisted perfusion imaging can support selection and coordination in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study assessed institutional changes in access to reperfusion therapies and workflow metrics before and after RapidAI® implementation.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive AIS admissions (July 2014-October 2024) at a single comprehensive stroke center, comparing pre‑implementation and post‑implementation periods (RapidAI® introduced June 2018). Primary outcomes were utilization of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT), mRS 0-1 at discharge, and decompressive craniectomy (DC). Secondary outcomes were 90‑day mRS, door‑to‑needle (DTN) time, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Analyses were adjusted for key confounders and sensitivity analyses were made.

RESULTS: Among 2,144 patients, adjusted analyses showed no significant differences in IVT (adjusted OR 0.93; 95% CI 0.52-1.69; p = 0.822) or MT (adjusted OR 2.73; 95% CI 0.70-10.61; p = 0.147) between periods. Rescue decompressive craniectomy was lower in the post period (adjusted OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.03-0.82; p = 0.029) and hospital length of stay was reduced (adjusted B -2.33 days; 95% CI -3.62 to -1.03; p < 0.001). No significant adjusted differences were observed for door to needle time (B -0.56 minutes; 95% CI -32.44 to 31.32; p = 0.972), discharge mRS 0-1 (adjusted OR 1.47; 95% CI 0.90-2.39; p = 0.126), discharge mRS ordinal (B -0.29; 95% CI -0.62 to 0.05; p = 0.091), or 90 day mRS ordinal (B -0.26; 95% CI -0.64 to 0.12; p = 0.174). Sensitivity analyses after multiple imputation produced consistent results.

CONCLUSIONS: RapidAI® implementation coincided with improved metrics in hospital length of stay and the need for decompressive craniectomy. Given low software utilization and potential secular trends, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: The Potential Role of Gut Microbiota in Combating Mycobacterium tuberculosis Infection.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.TB) infection. Although there have been significant advances in the treatment of M.TB infection, it still faces significant challenges. The gut microbiota is a highly complex ecosystem that plays an important role in regulating metabolism, immune regulation, and maintaining healthy balance in the human body. More and more studies have found that while gut microbiota regulates the immune regulation process of pulmonary TB through the "gut-lung axis," infection with M.TB can also affect the microbial stability of gut microbiota, thereby affecting host health. This article summarized and discussed the changes of gut flora in TB patients, the possible relationship and impact between gut flora and M.TB infection, and summarized and looked forward to the potential of gut flora in the treatment of TB, in order to provide a reference for the prevention and treatment of gut microorganisms in anti-M.TB infection.

articles.title: Cardiac Effects of Combined Versus Individual Interventions of Mediterranean Diet and Exercise in Adults with the Hypertriglyceridemic Waist Phenotype: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype, combining abdominal obesity and elevated serum triglycerides, is associated with adverse cardiovascular prognosis. The combination of dietary and exercise programs has the potential to improve outcomes with regard to adverse cardiac remodeling and dysfunction associated with poor metabolic health. We tested the hypothesis that the combination of a Mediterranean Diet (MedDiet) and exercise interventions improves cardiac structure and function more than the sum of each individual intervention.

METHODS: We performed a randomized 2 × 2 factorial design trial that included adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype (triglycerides ≥1.50 mmol/L, waist circumference ≥80 cm in women or ≥94 cm in men). Participants were randomly assigned to one of four 16-week interventions: (1) MedDiet alone, (2) exercise alone, (3) MedDiet + exercise, or (4) control group. The MedDiet groups received education, counseling, and key food items from the MedDiet. The exercise groups participated in a structured exercise program designed to achieve 150 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week. Data were collected during the screening, baseline, and post-intervention visits. In mixed-effects models, we compared the post-intervention echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) structure and function per intervention group after adjusting for age, sex, and baseline values. We calculated an interaction ratio between MedDiet and exercise to assess their combined effect.

RESULTS: Of the 200 recruited, 185 participants (76% women) had available echocardiographic data. LV measurements were within normal range for most participants. After the intervention, the posterior wall thickness (LV structure) was higher in the MedDiet groups (0.04 [95% CI: 0.01-0.07] cm), and the septal mitral annular tissue Doppler e' velocity (diastolic function) was higher in the exercise groups (0.4 [95% CI: 0.0-0.8] cm/s). No significant interactions between interventions were identified with respect to LV measurements.

CONCLUSION: No interaction between the MedDiet and exercise interventions on LV structure and function was observed among adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype. Further research is needed to ascertain whether the combination of these interventions can prevent the development of adverse LV remodeling over the long term or in participants with more advanced cardiac alterations.

articles.title: IL-37a, an Anti-Inflammatory Molecule and a Nuclear Cytokine: Linking Alternative Splicing, Nuclear Trafficking, and Epigenetic Regulation of Inflammation.
articles.journal: Journal of interferon & cytokine research : the official journal of the International Society for Interferon and Cytokine Research
articles.abstract: Interleukin-37 (IL-37) is an anti-inflammatory member of interleukin-1 family. Alternative splicing generates five isoforms (IL-37a-e) with distinct exon compositions. IL-37a has recently attracted increasing attention because it uniquely retains exon 3. Exon 3 encodes an N-terminal nuclear localization sequence (NLS) that enables autonomous nuclear translocation and harbors an elastase cleavage site at L21/R22. Elastase cleavage produces N-terminal IL-37a (NIL-37a) and mature IL-37a (mIL-37a). Full-length IL-37a and NIL-37a can exert IL-1R8-independent nuclear regulatory and anti-inflammatory effects in the endotoxemic shock model. Nuclear IL-37a recruits a WDR5/MLL4/C/EBPβ-associated complex to promote PPARG transcription, thereby linking cytokine signaling with chromatin regulation and PPARγ-mediated inflammatory control. These findings highlight IL-37a as a mechanistically distinct isoform and illustrate how isoform-specific sequence composition, proteolytic processing, and subcellular localization can diversify cytokine functions. This review synthesizes available evidence regarding the molecular basis of IL-37a nuclear activity, compartmentalized signaling and receptor-independent epigenetic regulation, in the context of nuclear cytokine biology and immunometabolic control. Collectively, IL-37a is a mechanistically distinct isoform whose alternative splicing, proteolytic processing, and nuclear trafficking shape compartment-specific signaling. In LPS-induced endotoxic shock, nuclear IL-37a acts independently of IL-1R8 to upregulate PPARγ through WDR5/MLL4/C/EBPβ-associated chromatin regulation; however, isoform-specific evidence requires further validation, particularly in humans.

articles.title: Alcohol screening, counseling, and medication treatment among older adults with heart failure: A missed opportunity.
articles.journal: Journal of studies on alcohol and drugs
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Both alcohol use and heart failure (HF) are prevalent among older adults. Alcohol can affect heart muscle, electrical function, blood pressure, and interact with common HF medications. Alcohol screening, brief counseling, and medications for alcohol use disorder (MAUD) are evidence-based and reimbursable by Medicare, but it is unknown whether older adults with HF receive these interventions, the details of these interventions, and if clinicians are reimbursed for them. This study identified instances of claims-documented screening, brief counseling, and MAUD receipt, as well as the sources of these services, among older adults enrolled in Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) in 2 years following HF diagnosis.

METHOD: Data are from Health and Retirement Study 2010-2018 linked with FFS claims 2008-2020. We calculated the percentage of respondents (n=1,232) that received claims-documented screening and, among those with alcohol use outside guidelines, brief counseling and MAUD following HF diagnosis. For services received, we calculated percentages by venue, clinician specialty, whether the respondent previously visited the clinician, and clinician participation in an Accountable Care Organization (ACO) contract.

RESULTS: Only 20 respondents (1.9%) received claims-documented screening. All screenings occurred in office settings. Most were administered by internal medicine specialists, clinicians that respondents previously visited, and clinicians not in ACOs. No respondents received brief counseling or MAUD.

CONCLUSIONS: Interventions for alcohol use above guidelines are uncommon among older adults with HF, indicating a missed opportunity for intervention. Further, clinicians are seemingly not capitalizing on the reimbursable nature of these services; additional support for providing, documenting, and billing for these services is warranted.

articles.title: LDiT3D: Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation Using a 3D Latent Diffusion Transformer Model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Head and neck (H&N) tumors are among the most common cancers worldwide. However, manual annotation of H&N tumors for each patient poses a significant burden on clinicians. Therefore, developing automated and accurate methods for H&N tumor segmentation is of great clinical importance.

METHODS: We introduce LDiT3D, a novel 3D transformer-based diffusion model designed to segment H&N tumors from 3D Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and X-ray computed tomography (CT) scans, primarily focusing on oropharyngeal tumors. LDiT3D utilizes stacked 3D vision transformer blocks to effectively capture spatial context in volumetric data. To address the high computational cost typically associated with 3D transformers, we incorporate a pre-trained autoencoder that projects the input into a lower-dimensional latent space where the diffusion process is performed more efficiently. In addition to the diffusion loss computed in latent space, a task-specific segmentation loss is introduced in pixel space to further enhance segmentation accuracy.

RESULTS: Methods based on U-Net and transformer architectures were selected as reference methods. Comparative results demonstrated that the proposed LDiT3D achieved highly accurate segmentation performance, with the highest Dice Score and lowest Hausdorff distance on both public and local datasets. Moreover, LDiT3D showed a more balanced performance between Precision and Recall, as indicated by the highest Fowlkes-Mallows Score. Ablation studies further confirmed the effectiveness of the key components in the LDiT3D design.

CONCLUSION: LDiT3D delivers more accurate and balanced H&N tumor segmentation compared to reference methods.

SIGNIFICANCE: These findings highlight LDiT3D's potential to improve automated H&N tumor annotation and advance medical image analysis.

articles.title: Template-Anchored Signal Decomposition and Label Refinement for Impairment Categorization on Noisy Visual Electrophysiological Data.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Visual electrophysiology offers an objective alternative to subjective vision assessments, providing enhanced reliability but remaining underutilized for visual impairment categorization due to imperfect datasets, noisy signals, and label inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we first construct a new dataset comprising ERG and VEP recordings from 1,970 participants with various ocular conditions and a mean age of 21.59 $\pm$ 4.47 years. A three-class categorization task is defined to reflect clinical disability grading. We then propose a template-anchored decomposition method for noise-aware signal feature extraction, using mode-specific ridge regression to isolate pathological components by removing both healthy patterns and noise artifacts. To collectively enhance feature representation from multi-channel signals, we design a joint attention encoder that combines channel attention with bilateral spatial attention across left- and right-eye channels to emphasize informative and coherent signal patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a template-anchored refinement mechanism that addresses label noise by updating soft labels during training based on the distances between each feature vector and the class templates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves consistent improvements over existing electrophysiology-based and general biosignal classification methods, supporting its feasibility for visual impairment categorization in a cohort composed primarily of young adults.

articles.title: New insights into β-cell vulnerability in type 1 diabetes-Lessons from nature.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes results from an autoimmune-mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, yet considerable heterogeneity exists regarding disease onset, progression and severity. Emerging evidence suggests that this variability reflects not only differences in immune responses, but also differences in the architecture and immune landscape of the endocrine pancreas. Our recent Steve Morgan Foundation Grand Challenge studies have provided important 'lessons from nature', revealing that the endocrine tissue in the human pancreas exists as a continuum of endocrine objects (EOs), ranging from isolated endocrine cells and small clusters to large islets. These structures differ in their cellular composition, vascularisation, innervation and maturity, creating distinct β-cell microenvironments that evolve throughout life and may shape susceptibility to autoimmune attack. Strikingly, β-cells in small EOs are preferentially lost in type 1 diabetes, suggesting EO size and organisation contribute to β-cell vulnerability. In parallel, we are advancing our understanding of changes in classical and non-classical human leukocyte antigen (HLA-I) expression in type 1 diabetes which can impact β-cell visibility to autoreactive T cells, and have demonstrated that soluble forms of HLA-I can be released from β-cells under inflammatory conditions associated with type 1 diabetes. Taken together, our findings support a model in which disease progression is shaped by interactions between a heterogeneous immune response and a heterogeneous endocrine landscape that can vary across the life course. Improving our understanding of how endocrine architecture, immune niches and HLA-mediated antigen presentation interact could identify new opportunities to protect and expand β-cell populations through targeted therapies in the future.

articles.title: Midlife physical activity trajectories are associated with reduced physical pre-frailty/frailty in older age: insights from the prospective ATTICA sub-study 2002-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although physical activity in older adults has been associated with lower risk of frailty, it is unclear if midlife physical activity patterns are associated with pre-frailty/frailty status in older age.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether longitudinal midlife physical activity trajectories are associated with physical pre-frailty/frailty development in older age, independent of cardiometabolic risk and other lifestyle factors.

DESIGN: Population-based prospective cohort study.

SETTINGS: In-person assessments and telephone interviews of persons living in urban communities in Attica, Greece.

PARTICIPANTS: Surviving participants of the ATTICA cohort study (2002-2024) who were older than 33 years at baseline.

MEASUREMENTS: Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, and lifestyle parameters were recorded at baseline and throughout the study. According to binary self-reported physical activity levels (<600 vs ≥600 metabolic equivalent minutes per week) at baseline, 5-year and 10-year follow-up, 4 ordered trajectories of physical activity were defined: persistently inactive, declining activity, inclining activity, and persistently active, and their association with the odds of pre-frailty/frailty development according to the phenotypic (FRAIL scale) model were investigated by applying multivariable logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Relative to persistent inactivity, persistently active and inclining physical activity lifestyles were associated with 80% and 79% decreased odds of pre-frailty/frailty at 22-year follow-up, respectively, after adjusting for age, sex, years of education, baseline body mass index, hypertension, diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia. The population fraction of pre-frailtand frailty that could be attributed to unhealthy physical activity trajectories throughout midlife is 49.5% (95% confidence interval, 36.3 to 59.9), rising to 64.8% (95% confidence interval, 49.6 to 75.4) when also considering hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and obesity.

CONCLUSION: Steadily high or rising physical activity trajectories during midlife were associated with lower odds of physical pre-frailty/frailty in older age, independently of cardiometabolic risk factors. These findings support that achieving and maintaining higher physical activity levels across midlife may be one of the keys to healthy aging.
