articles.title: Fleming Fund Implementation in Kenya: What Have We Learned About Strengthening One Health Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance for Decision-making?
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kenya has moved from fragmented, pilot-based antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance toward a coordinated One Health system, and its experience, pathways of change, and remaining gaps are relevant for other low- and middle-income settings working to operationalize One Health AMR surveillance.

METHODS: Here, we report a narrative overview of programmatic learning using 2018 as the pre-Fleming Fund baseline, drawing on national and global surveillance reports, monitoring frameworks from the Quadripartite indicators, qualitative evidence on governance, implementation and policy evolution across the One Health sectors, and Fleming Fund documentation.

RESULTS: Since 2018, AMR surveillance expanded from 2 human health sites to 30 human, animal, and environmental sites by 2025. National reports evolved to integrate AMR, antimicrobial consumption, and antimicrobial use data; routine reporting to global platforms matured; and outputs such as dashboards, reports, and policy briefs informing stewardship, Infection Prevention and Control, regulatory action, and policy decisions. External benchmarks showed improvement in AMR-related capacity, with World Health Organization Joint External Evaluation scores moving from limited to demonstrated capacity for surveillance and multisectoral coordination.

CONCLUSIONS: Kenya's experience suggests that sustainable progress depends on embedding AMR surveillance within government-led governance structures, technical systems, and coordinated partner support, but sustaining gains will require predictable financing and routine data use.

articles.title: Surveillance Data Use Through the Fleming Fund: Informing Action on Antimicrobial Resistance in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drawing on the Fleming Fund's work to strengthen antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance across Africa and Asia during 2018-2026, this article provides one of the first syntheses of AMR surveillance data use in low- and middle-income countries.

METHODS: A participatory synthesis for narrative review was conducted to summarize experience across administrative levels (facility, subnational, national, and regional).

RESULTS: Data use was most evident at the facility level, in human health systems where resistance patterns, antimicrobial use, and clinical data increasingly informed antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention and control, and other quality improvement initiatives. Data use in other sectors required different approaches. At the national level, Fleming Fund investments were associated with revisions of treatment guidelines, updates of essential medicines lists, and regulatory measures, primarily through improved governance and policy communities. Regional platforms supported member country data use at the national level. Subnational data use was undertaken in countries with decentralized health systems. Across levels, data use pathways driven by local priorities helped surveillance inform action.

CONCLUSIONS: Fleming Fund experience suggests that surveillance is more likely to inform action when data use is built into system design. Continued investment will be needed if AMR surveillance is to improve policy and practice in low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: Beyond Catastrophic Health Expenditure: Recognising Forgone Hypertension Care.
DNA-BFN: Bayesian Flow Networks for Generative Modeling of Regulatory DNA Sequences.
articles.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Designing regulatory DNA sequences is challenging due to their discrete nucleotide alphabet and complex higher-order dependencies underlying regulatory function. Many existing generative models, particularly diffusion-based approaches, learn by injecting stochastic noise into sequences and training denoising processes, which can distort discrete sequence structure and weaken biological constraints.

RESULTS: Here, we introduce DNA Bayesian Flow Networks (DNA-BFN), a generative framework that models regulatory DNA sequences through iterative Bayesian updates of per-position nucleotide distributions. By directly modeling per-position categorical beliefs, DNA-BFN realizes a diffusion-like generative process without explicitly perturbing discrete nucleotide sequences, enabling fully differentiable training while preserving discrete sequence structure. Across eight regulatory sequence datasets spanning diverse species, scales, and sequence lengths, DNA-BFN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, faithfully preserves sequence feature statistics and regulatory patterns, enables few-shot sequence design, and achieves faster sampling efficiency. These results show that framing sequence generation as progressive uncertainty reduction in probability space provides an effective and generalizable approach for nucleotide sequence design.

AVAILABILITY: The software and its source code are publicly available at https://github.com/WangLabTHU/DNA-BFN. The dataset, source code and model weights are available in the Zenodo repository: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20177972.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

articles.title: Clinical Effectiveness of AI-Based Cardiac Arrest Prediction System for General Ward Patients (VITAL-MD): Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remains a frequent and devastating event, and conventional early warning scores (EWSs) coupled with rapid response systems (RRSs) have shown inconsistent effects on patient-centered outcomes, largely owing to limited predictive accuracy and high false-alarm burden. AI-based EWSs (AI-EWSs) have demonstrated superior discrimination retrospectively, but high-quality prospective evidence in true external validation environments remains scarce. Existing AI-EWS trials have either been confined to internal-development settings or bundled the algorithm with specific implementation infrastructure, leaving the stand-alone effect of AI-based software as a medical device (AI-SaMD) on patient outcomes uncharacterized.

OBJECTIVE: This trial will evaluate whether implementation of AI-SaMD (VUNO Med-DeepCARS) as a stand-alone clinical decision-support tool in routine general-ward care reduces IHCA compared with usual care based on conventional EWSs.

METHODS: The VITAL-MD trial (validation of an AI-based clinical deterioration prediction model on patient outcomes through a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial [SW-CRT] multicenter evaluation of DeepCARS) is a pragmatic, multicenter, SW-CRT conducted at 4 tertiary academic hospitals in the Republic of Korea. Six tertiary academic hospitals were assessed for eligibility based on inpatient capacity, RRS operating hours aligned with the national RRS pilot program, and no prior AI-SaMD use. All adult patients aged 19 years or older admitted to general wards during the 12-month trial period are included; patients younger than 19 years, or with no documented vital signs throughout hospitalization, are excluded. The 4 sites are randomized to sequentially transition from preimplementation (usual care) to postimplementation (AI-SaMD-guided care) in 4 steps separated by 7-day washout periods. DeepCARS generates real-time risk scores from 4 vital signs and integrates into the existing electronic medical record interface without altering RRS workflows. The primary outcome is the incidence of general-ward IHCA, defined per the Utstein guidelines, among the target cohort (defined as patients exceeding the alert threshold at least once). Assuming a baseline IHCA incidence of 6.70%, a 40% relative risk reduction, an intracluster correlation coefficient of 0.01, and 350 patients per cluster-period, 7002 target-cohort patients (total enrollment approximately 72,695) provide 80% power. Analyses follow the intention-to-treat principle using generalized linear mixed models adjusting for prespecified covariates, with prespecified sensitivity, subgroup, and compliance analyses.

RESULTS: The trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service (KCT0010243) on February 28, 2025. Recruitment was conducted from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. All 4 sites completed transition to the postimplementation period, and data cleaning is currently underway before the final database lock, with primary results expected in 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: VITAL-MD will provide the first large-scale, multicenter randomized evidence evaluating whether an AI-EWS, deployed as a stand-alone device in external validation environments and benchmarked against real-world standard-of-care practice, improves patient-centered outcomes for general-ward patients, advancing the evaluation of AI-SaMD from retrospective diagnostic accuracy toward prospective, action-anchored clinical utility.

articles.title: Principles or Resources? Best Management of Pediatric Femoral Neck Fractures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric femoral neck fractures (PFNF) are rare but have a reported complication rate of >30%. To date, there remains a lack of consensus on the definitive risk factors for AVN following PFNF. By comparing the outcomes of PFNF treated at a major US metropolitan area tertiary-level 1 pediatric trauma center (group 1) to an equivalent trauma hospital in a major Latin American capital (group 2), we sought to weigh whether treatment principles or resources are more important for a favorable result.

METHODS: This was a retrospective review of all children (<18 years old) treated for PFNF in the past 10 years at each location. Demographics, treatment, and outcome variables were collected. Fractures were classified by Delbet criteria. Patients with incomplete fractures, pathologic fractures, and those with short follow-up (<3 months) were excluded. Univariate and bivariate statistics were applied.

RESULTS: In all, 74 fractures (73 children) were included, 39 from group 1 and 35 from group 2 (52% male, mean age 11.0±4.11). Patients from group 1 (12.5±3.95 years old) were significantly older compared with group 2 (9.35±3.72 years old, P<0.001). Group 2 had a significantly higher proportion of type 4 Delbet fractures (37% vs. 8%, P=0.01) while no other differences in fracture characteristics were observed between groups. Of the patients who underwent operative treatment for their fractures, the time to surgery was significantly shorter in group 1 (4.42 days) compared with group 2 (7.56 days, P<0.001). The preferred method of surgery was open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) at group 1 and closed reduction and percutaneous pinning at group 2 (P=0.05). There were no differences in overall complication rates, including AVN (P>0.05).

CONCLUSION: While these 2 institutions differ in resources, such as the ability to perform surgery urgently or hardware availability, and despite differences in fracture type, there were no significant differences in the outcome and incidence of complications, including AVN.

LEVELS OF EVIDENCE: Level 3, Retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: What do administrative diabetes indicators measure? Treatment-side and screening-side evidence from nationwide NDB Open Data in Japan.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Regional administrative diabetes indicators are increasingly used for population surveillance and planning, yet they are generated through the healthcare system rather than measuring disease directly. We examined what two complementary indicator families-treatment-side prescription quantities and screening-side HbA1c-measure across 47 Japanese prefectures.

METHODS: Cross-sectional ecological study using the 10th NDB Open Data release. Indicator A was oral antidiabetic agent dispensing volume per population (drug classification 396), related to ageing, income, education and population density by ordinary least squares with VIF assessment and AIC-based comparison. Indicator B comprised the HbA1c high-value rate, mean HbA1c and the D005 laboratory-testing rate, related to three claim-rate outcomes by ordinary least squares with HC3 errors (five sensitivity specifications).

RESULTS: For Indicator A, ageing was the only significant univariable predictor (β = 9961; R2 = 0.324); the lowest-AIC model retained ageing and income (R2 = 0.394; VIF = 2.18; income β = 56.6, p = 0.030). For Indicator B, the HbA1c high-value rate was associated with chronic dialysis management (β = 195.1/%pt., p = 0.006, R2 = 0.271); mean HbA1c showed a comparable association; the primary association was stable across all five specifications.

CONCLUSIONS: Neither indicator family provided a direct estimate of disease burden. Prescription quantities reflected demographic and income structure, whereas HbA1c indicators showed a selective ecological association with downstream service use. Both are better interpreted as ecological surveillance indicators than direct measures of disease burden or prevalence.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Multi-hormone Receptor Modulators for Kidney Protection in Nondiabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), together with newer multi-hormone receptor modulators that target glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon and amylin, have emerged as promising therapies for chronic kidney disease. This review examines the mechanisms through which these agents may protect the kidney and summarizes the emerging clinical evidence in populations without diabetes. Kidney protection appears to arise through complementary direct and indirect routes. Direct effects include natriuresis through inhibition of the sodium-hydrogen exchanger (NHE)-3, modulation of glomerular hemodynamics through effects on afferent arteriolar tone and vasoconstrictor pathways, and attenuation of renal inflammation; mechanisms that are largely independent of glucose lowering. Indirect mechanisms include reductions in the metabolic, hemodynamic and cardiac burden on the kidney through weight loss, blood pressure lowering, and improvement of heart failure. Beyond selective GLP-1R-agonism, the added hormonal components of multi-hormone receptor modulators engage distinct physiological pathways whose interactions may be additive, synergistic or counteracting, but remain incompletely understood. The efficacy of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators in people without diabetes is currently supported by results from secondary kidney endpoints in phase-3 obesity and cardiovascular outcome trials, including reductions in albuminuria and preservation of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Several dedicated outcome studies of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators are now underway and will determine whether these therapies become a new pillar of care in nondiabetic kidney disease.

articles.title: Changing Patterns of Diagnostic Testing in Children With Asthma: Evidence of Redistribution, Overuse, and Recovery After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world implementation of diagnostic strategies in pediatric asthma remains heterogeneous, and the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on diagnostic practice patterns is incompletely understood, particularly in middle-income countries. Guideline-recommended objective testing (e.g., spirometry) is inconsistently applied in pediatric asthma worldwide, and whether the COVID-19 pandemic produced a transient disruption or a lasting restructuring of diagnostic practice across testing domains remains unclear. We aimed to characterize longitudinal trends in diagnostic testing among children with asthma, examining pre-pandemic trajectories, COVID-associated changes, and post-pandemic recovery.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based interrupted time-series study using Colombia's mandatory healthcare registry (2015-2024). Asthma encounters were identified using ICD-10 codes (J45-J46). Diagnostic procedures were classified into nine clinically defined domains. Diagnostic intensity was calculated as tests per 100 asthma encounters. Segmented regression estimated pre-pandemic trends, immediate 2020 level changes, and post-pandemic slope modifications.

RESULTS: A total of 1,954,680 asthma encounters generated 117,324 diagnostic tests. Pre-pandemic trajectories diverged across domains. Pulmonary function testing (PFT) declined before 2020 (IRR 0.80; 95% CI 0.74-0.86) but showed a significant immediate increase in 2020 (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.28-1.57) and sustained post-pandemic acceleration (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.09-1.26). Imaging and sleep studies exhibited sharp pandemic-associated declines with partial or full recovery. Cardiopulmonary testing demonstrated marked pre-pandemic expansion (IRR 1.96).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric asthma diagnostic practice underwent domain-specific restructuring rather than uniform disruption, consistent with a process of diagnostic redistribution across testing domains. Post-pandemic intensification of PFT may reflect improved adherence to objective diagnostic confirmation, whereas persistent contraction in selected domains warrants continued monitoring.

articles.title: Complementary Value of Multimodal Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in Serial Evaluation of Rapidly Progressive Infant Cardiac Fibroma: A Fatal Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Infant cardiac fibroma is a rare fatal myocardial tumor with infiltrative growth, hard to distinguish from rhabdomyoma via routine imaging. We report a 3-month-old male infant prenatally diagnosed with left ventricular fibroma, who died of irreversible heart failure after subtotal resection. Serial contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provided complementary perfusion information: it guided surgical strategy, detected microscopic residual tumor undetectable on unenhanced ultrasound, and identified early subclinical left ventricular dysfunction. However, CEUS failed to reverse the fatal clinical trajectory. This case demonstrates the auxiliary value and key limitations of CEUS for infant cardiac tumor assessment.

articles.title: Greenspace visitation and risk of major adverse cardiovascular events: evidence from the Houston methodist cardiovascular learning health system registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether mobility-derived greenspace visitation, as a behavioural measure of environmental exposure, is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) independent of individual and neighbourhood factors.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults in the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry (2016-2023). Greenspace visitation was defined at the census-tract level using mobility-derived foot-traffic data and modelled as annual visits per resident device. The primary outcome was incident MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, and all-cause mortality). The Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and Kaplan-Meier curves assessed associations with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, smoking, and neighbourhood social vulnerability. Among 1 088 866 adults without baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, median (SD) age was 49 (17.6) years, and 59.9% were female. Greenspace visitation varied across neighbourhoods and by demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Each additional 10 annual visits was associated with lower MACE risk in unadjusted models [hazard ratio (HR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.81-0.83] and after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and smoking (HR 0.89; 95% CI: 0.88-0.91). A non-linear relationship showed risk reductions at low-to-moderate visitation, plateauing at 10-15 visits annually. After adjusting for social vulnerability, associations were attenuated and no longer significant. The Kaplan-Meier curves showed higher event-free survival in high-visitation areas, consistent across MACE components.

CONCLUSION: Mobility-derived greenspace visitation is associated with lower cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight greenspace engagement as a potentially modifiable behavioural exposure and support strategies to enhance access and utilization of greenspaces for cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Bilateral Cryptocococcal orbital cellulitis associated with sinonasal cryptococcosis: a case report and review of the literature.
articles.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic fungal pathogen that typically affects the lungs and central nervous system. Orbital involvement is exceptionally rare and may mimic bacterial orbital cellulitis, resulting in delayed diagnosis and treatment. We report an 83-year-old immunocompromised man with poorly controlled diabetes and recent corticosteroid exposure who presented with rapidly progressive bilateral orbital cellulitis secondary to invasive cryptococcal infection with extensive sinonasal involvement. Despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, surgical intervention, and systemic antifungal treatment, the patient developed progressive orbital and systemic disease and ultimately died from multiorgan failure. A focused review of the literature identified only three previously reported cases of orbital or periorbital cryptococcosis. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of orbital cryptococcal infection, the potential for contiguous spread from sinonasal disease, and the importance of early recognition and aggressive multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Improving the resolution and informativity of the majority-rule consensus tree using fine-grained dissimilarity measures.
articles.abstract: Phylogenetic analyses often require the summarization of multiple trees, e.g., in Bayesian analyses to obtain the centroid of the posterior distribution of trees, or to determine the consensus of a set of bootstrap trees. The majority-rule consensus tree is the most commonly used. It is easy to compute and minimizes the sum of Robinson-Foulds (RF) distances to the input trees. In mathematical terms, the majority-rule consensus tree is the median of the input trees with respect to the RF distance. However, due to the coarse nature of RF distance, which only considers whether two branches induce exactly the same bipartition of the taxa or not, highly unresolved trees can be produced when the phylogenetic signal is low. To overcome this limitation, we propose using median trees with respect to finer-grained dissimilarity measures between trees. These measures include a quartet distance between tree topologies, and transfer distances, which quantify the similarity between bipartitions, in contrast to the presence/absence view of RF. We describe fast heuristic consensus algorithms for transfer-based tree dissimilarities, capable of efficiently processing trees with thousands of taxa. Through evaluations on simulated datasets in both Bayesian and bootstrapping maximum-likelihood frameworks, our results show that our methods improve consensus tree resolution in scenarios with low to moderate phylogenetic signal, while providing better or comparable dissimilarities to the true phylogeny. Applying our methods to mammals, Ebola virus, and a large HIV dataset of over nine thousand taxa confirms the improvement with real data. These results demonstrate the usefulness of our new consensus tree methods for analyzing the large datasets that are available today. Our software, PhyloCRISP, is available from https://github.com/yukiregista/PhyloCRISP.

articles.title: Impact of setmelanotide on metabolic syndrome risk in patients with proopiomelanocortin or leptin receptor deficiencies.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with severe obesity due to proopiomelanocortin (POMC) or leptin receptor (LEPR) deficiencies resulting in impaired melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) signaling may be at risk for obesity-related comorbidities. Here, we report metabolic parameters and metabolic syndrome severity in patients before and after treatment with the MC4R agonist setmelanotide.

METHODS: Patients from phase 3 studies of setmelanotide for POMC (NCT02896192) or LEPR (NCT03287960) deficiencies with complete metabolic parameter data were included in this analysis. Metabolic parameters and metabolic severity Z scores based on body mass index (MetS-Z-BMI scores) were reported at baseline and following ∼1 year of setmelanotide treatment in these patients; subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, genotype, and response to treatment.

RESULTS: Metabolic parameters were evaluated in 18 of 21 patients enrolled in phase 3 trials. Group means for most parameters were within the normal range at baseline, excluding weight-related measures, fasting glucose, and triglycerides. The overall baseline mean (standard deviation [SD]) MetS-Z-BMI score was 1.49 (1.33). Most patients saw improvement in ≥1 metabolic parameter at week 52. The overall mean (SD) change in MetS-Z-BMI score after ∼1 year of treatment was -1.05 (0.88). Among subgroup analyses, MetS-Z-BMI score reductions were significantly greater in achievers of weight-based thresholds compared with nonachievers (P = .0187) and in patients with deficiencies in POMC compared with LEPR (P = .0278).

CONCLUSION: Setmelanotide was associated with a reduction in specific metabolic parameters and metabolic syndrome severity (MetS-Z-BMI scores) in patients with POMC or LEPR deficiencies.

articles.title: Therapy for Adults With Complicated Urinary Tract Infection.
Cost-Effectiveness of HCV Screening in Emergency Departments Using DETECT Hep C Trial Results.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Nontargeted hepatitis C virus (HCV) screening in emergency departments (EDs) has been demonstrated to identify more patients with HCV than targeted screening. Cost-effectiveness is key to strategy selection; however, the cost-effectiveness of these strategies in EDs remains unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness of 2 novel ED-based HCV screening strategies with no ED HCV screening.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this economic evaluation study, a cohort of individuals presenting to the ED in the US was simulated with data from the Determining Effective Testing in Emergency Departments and Care Coordination on Treatment Outcomes for Hepatitis C Screening (DETECT Hep C) trial using the Hepatitis C Cost-Effectiveness (HEP-CE) model from a health sector perspective. Using data from EDs at Denver Health Medical Center, Johns Hopkins Hospital, and the University of Mississippi Medical Center, 3 strategies were simulated over a lifetime horizon, including (1) no ED HCV screening, (2) targeted HCV screening, and (3) nontargeted HCV screening. Data were collected from November 2019 to August 2022 and analyzed from December 2021 to July 2026.

EXPOSURE: HCV screening in the ED.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were remaining life expectancy, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), and costs (2024 US dollars). An annual discount rate of 3% was applied to future costs and benefits when calculating ICERs. An ICER of less than $100 000 per QALY gained was considered cost-effective.

RESULTS: A simulated cohort with a total of 500 million individuals (mean [SD] age, 46.3 [17.2] years; 264.4 million male [52.88%]) were included in this analysis. Nontargeted HCV screening yielded the best clinical and cost-effectiveness outcomes in the base case cohort, with 65.89% of infections being cured, a discounted cost of $214 465, discounted quality-adjusted life expectancy of 15.8723 QALYs, and an ICER of $12 820 per QALY gained. Compared with nontargeted HCV screening, no ED HCV screening and targeted HCV screening, respectively, had fewer infections cured (65.60% and 65.88%), lower QALYs (15.8717 QALYs and 15.8721 QALYs), and similar discounted costs ($214 467 and $214 462). Absolute benefits appeared narrow because over 90% of those screened did not have HCV; however, benefits were clear among those living with HCV infection.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this economic evaluation study suggest that nontargeted HCV screening was cost-effective when compared with no HCV screening or targeted HCV screening in the ED. Implementing routine nontargeted HCV screening in emergency departments provides good economic value and could be an important pillar of HCV elimination.

articles.title: The complexity of congestion in heart failure: a critical review of the evidence and a proposal for a multimodality approach.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract: Congestion remains the first cause of hospitalization in acute heart failure patients, and it is the primary goal of treatment during early phases of hospitalization. Despite its clinical relevance, a universal algorithm for quantification or characterization is lacking. Indeed, congestion has been differently evaluated across several studies in terms of timing checks and diagnostic methods. Recent analyses have highlighted the importance of differentiating between intravascular and tissue congestion. Although it is associated with haemodynamic dysfunction, extravascular congestion may occur even in the absence of overt intravascular fluid overload. Importantly, tissue congestion is not merely a reflection of intravascular volume expansion. In this framework, the interstitial space surrounding the capillary barrier and its integrity may be accounted as additive drivers for tissue congestion. In clinical practice, this distinction remains anchored in simplistic clinical assessment, and poorly evaluated. A critical review of the evidences has been performed and multimodal approaches combining ultrasonography, invasive measurements, and biomarkers have been proposed.

articles.title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk.

OBJECTIVE: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026.

EXPOSURES: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use.

MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios.

RESULTS: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

articles.title: Ambulatory Electrocardiography Modalities in Pediatric Arrhythmia Detection and Management.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The diagnostic efficacy of different ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring modalities in this patient population remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the diagnostic yield and clinical utility of 3 ambulatory electrocardiographic modalities in pediatric patients.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center study took place at an outpatient clinic and an inpatient ward of National Taiwan University Children's Hospital. Patients younger than 18 years who underwent ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring between December 2022 and January 2025 were included. These data were analyzed February 2025 to March 2026.

EXPOSURE: A continuous 7-day Holter device that functioned as an event recorder was used. Recordings from the first 24 hours were defined as the 24-hour Holter results.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Arrhythmias were categorized as major (tachyarrhythmia or bradyarrhythmia) or minor (extrasystolic arrhythmia). All patients were followed up for 1 year; the final arrhythmia diagnosis was used as the reference standard. The primary and secondary outcomes were detection of arrhythmia and a change in clinical management attributable to monitoring findings, respectively.

RESULTS: In total, 435 children (235 female [54%] and 200 male [46%]; mean [SD] age, 12.3 [3.9] years) were included. The mean (SD) duration of analyzable ambulatory electrocardiographic data was 4.9 (1.7) days. Of 411 children who activated the event recorder, 10.7% had symptom-correlated arrhythmias. The 7-day Holter monitoring demonstrated a significantly higher rate of major arrhythmias (6.2%) than the 24-hour Holter or 7-day event recordings (2.3%; rate difference 95% CI, 1.9%-6.0%; P < .001). Seven-day Holter monitoring showed superior sensitivity (7-day Holter monitoring: 73%; rate difference 95% CI, 54.1%-84.6%; 24-hour Holter monitoring: 27%; rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; and 7-day event recorder: 27%, rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; P < .001) and a high negative predictive value (97.5%, 95% CI, 95.2%-98.6%). Tachyarrhythmias were associated with higher rates of management changes; management changed in 7.1% of patients with 7-day Holter monitoring, 1.6% with 24-hour Holter (rate difference 95% CI, 3.0%-7.6%; P < .001) and 2.8% with a 7-day event recorder (rate difference 95% CI, 2.0%-6.2%; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study of pediatric patients without structural heart disease who underwent electrocardiographic monitoring, 7-day continuous ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring was associated with a significantly higher diagnostic yield than 24-hour Holter and 7-day event recording. Continuous monitoring may be preferred to detect tachyarrhythmias likely to influence clinical management.

articles.title: Mifepristone Patient Agreement Form and Medication Abortion Knowledge: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: While the US Food and Drug Administration requires medication abortion patients to review and sign a patient agreement form (PAF) under its Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program, there is limited research examining whether the PAF improves patient knowledge.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients are more knowledgeable about medication abortion after reviewing and signing the PAF.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: People receiving mifepristone and misoprostol medications (15 years or older and proficient in English or Spanish) were recruited from 5 facilities in California, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, and Minnesota (January to October 2025). After receiving standard clinic counseling and the mifepristone medication guide, patients were randomized into 2 study groups and then completed a survey either before (n = 301 control) or after (n = 292 exposed) receiving and signing the PAF. Data were analyzed December 2025 to August 2026.

INTERVENTION: The control group completed the survey before receiving the PAF and any PAF-related counseling. The exposed group received and signed the PAF and any PAF-related counseling and then completed a knowledge survey.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Overall medication abortion knowledge (correct response to 12 items regarding when to seek medical care, effectiveness, administration, potential serious risks, and side effects) and responses to each individual knowledge item.

RESULTS: A total of 593 participants (mean [SD] age, 26.9 [5.8] years; 44 Asian/Pacific Islander [7%], 132 Black [22%], 181 Hispanic [31%], and 159 White [27%] individuals) completed knowledge items (301 control [51%]; 292 exposed [49%]). Across participant characteristics, study groups only differed significantly in reported abortion history. In adjusted analyses, participants answered a mean (95% CI) of 10.37 (10.26-10.48) of 12 knowledge items consistently with the PAF with no study group differences (control: difference, 10.26; exposed: difference, 10.44; adjusted difference, 0.18; 95% CI, -0.04 to 0.39). Nearly everyone knew to contact a "provider" if they "were to have an infection (590 [99%]) or heavy bleeding that soaked through 2 full-size sanitary pads per hour for 2 hours (566 [96%])." The items with answers that were least often concordant with the PAF included how often the treatment does not work (320 [54%]) and taking misoprostol 24 to 48 hours after mifepristone (458 [77%]).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The randomized clinical trial found that patient knowledge about medication abortion following standard counseling was high. Exposure to the required PAF did not result in a clinically meaningful increase in medication abortion knowledge. The findings raise questions about the PAF requirement from the US Food and Drug Administration, as it does not appear to be useful.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07604675.

articles.title: Protective effects of Rasa Manikya and Rasa Sindura against drug-resistant Salmonella Typhimurium sepsis in mice.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the in vitro antibacterial efficacy of classical herbo‑mineral formulations, Rasa Manikya (RM) and Rasa Sindura (RS), and also evaluated their ameliorative potential in combating multidrug‑resistant (MDR) Salmonella Typhimurium -induced sepsis in a murine model. Both RM and RS exhibited dose‑dependent antibacterial activity in agar well diffusion and broth microdilution assays. Oral administration of RM and RS to mice at a dose of 25 mg/kg body weight significantly (p < 0.05) improved clinical scores, restored haematological and biochemical parameters, and moderately reduced bacterial burden in liver, spleen, and kidney, compared to the healthy group. RM and RS treatment also rebalanced hepatic oxidant/antioxidant status and ameliorated histopathological damage in vital organs. Principal Component Analysis revealed a clear shift in treated groups toward normal physiological profiles. Analysis of survival trials using the Log-Rank (Mantel-Cox) test identified significant differences, with treated mice groups- RS (87.25%) and RM (81.25%) showing markedly enhanced survival, compared to untreated controls (50%). The ameliorative effects of RM and RS in a murine sepsis model underscore their potential as alternative therapeutics. However, further studies-particularly those addressing potential toxicity, and pharmacokinetics,-are warranted before any consideration of clinical application.

articles.title: A Common CD36 Variant and the Genetic Landscape of Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Individuals of African Ancestry.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure that disproportionately affects individuals of predominantly African ancestry, among whom familial clustering of disease is more pronounced relative to those of predominantly European ancestry. Truncating variants in TTN, which encodes the sarcomeric protein titin, are the most common established monogenic cause of DCM. A common CD36 nonsense variant enriched among individuals of African ancestry has also been shown to account for a substantial burden of DCM.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the contribution of a CD36 nonsense variant to DCM risk with that of truncating variants in TTN and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other established genes for DCM.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicohort genetic association study including participants of African and European ancestry with exome or genome sequence data and DCM case status from the following 4 US datasets: All of Us Research Program (recruitment: 2017-present; last follow-up: August 27, 2024), Million Veteran Program (recruitment: 2011-present; last follow-up: September 30, 2024), Penn Medicine Biobank (recruitment: 2013-present; last follow-up: November 14, 2022), and the DCM Precision Medicine Study (recruitment: 2016-2020; last follow-up: March 15, 2020).

EXPOSURE: Carrier status for TTN truncating variants, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 11 high-confidence genes for DCM, and the nonsense variant CD36 Y325* (0, 1, or 2 copies).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Risk of DCM, prevalence of variant carriers among DCM cases, and population attributable fraction of DCM.

RESULTS: Among 82 623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry across 4 cohorts, the mean age was 53.4 years (SD, 13.9 years), 47 124 were male, and 1316 had DCM. Individuals who were homozygous for the CD36 Y325* risk allele had a higher risk of DCM (odds ratio [OR], 4.8; 95% CI, 3.1-7.3) as did those who were heterozygous (OR, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.2-1.7). TTN truncating variants also conferred an elevated risk of DCM in participants of African ancestry (OR, 8.5; 95% CI, 5.5-13.0). Among 1316 individuals of African ancestry classified as DCM cases, 33 (2.5%) were homozygous for CD36, 56 (4.3%) had TTN truncating variants, and 16 (1.2%) had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other high-confidence genes for DCM. In population-level analyses incorporating both heterozygous and homozygous CD36 Y325* carriers, the population attributable fraction for CD36 (9.0% [6.2% for heterozygous carriers and 2.8% for homozygous carriers]) surpassed the population attributable fraction for TTN truncating variants (3.7%).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In 4 US cohorts, an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to DCM burden among individuals of African ancestry than established genes for DCM, including TTN truncating variants that are typically considered the most common genetic cause. These findings reshape the known genetic architecture of DCM in individuals of African ancestry and highlight the importance of representation in genomic research.

articles.title: Comparing operational definitions of screening-based cognitive impairment in the Tohoku Medical Megabank cohort: Focus on digital engagement.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDementia prevention is a global health priority, yet most large-scale population studies come from Western settings. Japan, a rapidly aging society, provides a unique non-Western epidemiological context for characterizing cognitive decline.ObjectiveTo assess whether the Tohoku Medical Megabank (TMM) cohorts replicate established dementia-related associations, and to identify correlates that are statistically significant across three prespecified operational classifications.MethodsWe analyzed data from >81,000 participants in the TMM cohorts. Participants were classified using (i) self-reported physician-diagnosed dementia and screening-defined impairment using (ii) Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) ≤ 27 and (iii) Japanese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-J) ≤ 25. Associations with 14 established dementia-related correlates and >3,800 exploratory variables were assessed using false-discovery-rate control, semantic clustering, and sequential multivariable logistic regression.ResultsParticipants with self-reported dementia had lower MMSE and MoCA-J scores. Established correlates replicated in expected directions for at least one classification, including lower education, hypertension, depressive symptoms, and hearing difficulty. We identified 106 significant correlates across all three classifications; for self-reported dementia, digital device non-use was associated with higher odds (fully adjusted OR up to 2.97, 95% CI: 1.42-6.18), while smartphone use showed inverse associations (OR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.26-0.86); directions were consistent for screening-defined impairment.ConclusionsIn this study, leveraging existing cognitive classifications available in TMM cohorts, we found that established dementia-related associations largely replicated and identified correlates across three operational classifications. Digital disengagement emerged as a correlate that may reflect early functional change; given the cross-sectional design, causal inference requires further examination. Longitudinal validation with adjudicated diagnoses is needed.

articles.title: A study on the dose-response relationship between glycemic variability and in-dialysis hypotension in patients with diabetes undergoing hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the dose-response relationship between Glycemic variability (GV) and Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) in diabetic hemodialysis (MHD) patients, identify the critical Coefficient of variation (CV) threshold, and inform precision glucose management.

METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 240 diabetic MHD patients (2023-2024). Continuous glucose monitoring provided GV parameters (CV, MAGE, SD). Patients were divided into IDH (n = 98) and non-IDH (n = 142) groups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyzed dose-response; multivariate logistic regression assessed independent effects, with Subgroup analysis and interaction tests.

RESULTS: CV was significantly higher in the IDH group (42.3% vs. 26.5%, P<0.001). RCS revealed a nonlinear positive correlation (P<0.001). When CV>36%, IDH risk increased sharply (threshold effect). Each 10% CV rise increased IDH risk by 98.4% (OR 1.984). Compared to Q1, Q3 (OR 3.512) and Q4 (OR 8.637) showed significantly higher risk. Associations were stronger in patients aged ≥60 years, dialysis duration ≥36 months, or with cardiovascular disease (interaction P<0.05). CV predicted IDH with AUC=0.856; optimal cutoff 36.5% (sensitivity 78.6%, specificity 82.4%).

CONCLUSION: A significant dose-response relationship exists between GV and IDH. CV>36% is an independent risk factor. Maintaining CV below 36% may reduce IDH risk and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Before standardizing the postmortem diagnosis of sepsis, what exactly are we diagnosing?
Serum miR-329-3p as a potential biomarker for ischemic stroke: clinical association and in vitro neuroprotection via PTPN1.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke, a prevalent disorder of the cerebral vasculature, is associated with substantial risks of long-term disability and death. Explore the expression profile, diagnostic and prognostic relevance, and underlying molecular mechanisms of miR-329-3p in ischemic stroke. 126 acute ischemic stroke patients and 92 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum miR-329-3p and PTPN1 mRNA were measured by qRT-PCR. Neurological function was evaluated via NIHSS and 3-month mRS scores. In vitro, OGD/R-induced SH-SY5Y cells were used. Cell proliferation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and PI3K/Akt pathway activity were assessed. The miR-329-3p-PTPN1 interaction was validated, and rescue experiments were performed. miR-329-3p was downregulated in stroke patients, showing good diagnostic efficacy, and negatively correlated with NIHSS and mRS scores. miR-329-3p is significantly associated with the prognosis of patients. In OGD/R cells, miR-329-3p overexpression improved proliferation, reduced apoptosis, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammation, and activated PI3K/Akt. PTPN1 was confirmed as a direct target; its overexpression abolished the neuroprotective effects of miR-329-3p. Serum miR-329-3p is a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for ischemic stroke and exerts in vitro neuroprotection by targeting PTPN1.

articles.title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure : From Implanted Hemodynamic Monitoring Toward an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Adaptive Care Cycle.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Implanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy. We review lessons from PAP-guided remote patient management and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could support more individualized eligibility assessment and multimodal longitudinal surveillance within a patient-centered adaptive care cycle to further improve clinical outcomes.

RECENT FINDINGS: HF is increasingly recognized as a systemic disease characterized, across HF phenotypes, by multiple cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities. CHAMPION, GUIDE-HF, and MONITOR-HF did not systematically incorporate comorbidity-related risk into patient selection, while PAP-guided treatment focused predominantly on diuretic adjustment, and monitoring strategies were not adapted to individual disease trajectories. AI could help integrate multidimensional phenotyping to estimate individual risk and expected benefit pre-implant, use comprehensive longitudinal monitoring data to support personalized, actionable clinical decision-making, and enable dynamic adaptation of monitoring intensity tailored to the disease trajectory. This may improve clinical outcomes, reduce healthcare professional workload, enhance patient experience and treatment adherence, and increase cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Association of Pediatric Critical Illness With Household Income Trajectories.
articles.abstract: BackgroundWe aimed to quantify longitudinal changes in household income among families of pediatric survivors of critical illness and to identify factors associated with catastrophic household income decline.MethodsThis nationwide retrospective cohort study used data from the National Health Insurance Service of South Korea. We included 10 590 pediatric patients aged 1 month to 17 years who were admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2022, and survived for at least 365 days after ICU admission. The primary outcome was the longitudinal change in household income level (ordinal scale, 0-20) between the pre-ICU baseline and the subsequent calendar-year assessment, analyzed using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models. A sensitivity analysis assessed income two calendar years after ICU admission in the 2020-2021 cohort.ResultsAmong 10 590 pediatric survivors, 2837 (26.8%) experienced a decline in household income, and 797 (7.5%) experienced catastrophic household income decline. In the primary GEE model, household income did not significantly differ between the pre-ICU and post-ICU assessments (ratio of means [RoM], 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00; P = .631). The 2-calendar-year sensitivity analysis yielded a consistent result (RoM, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.96-1.01; P = .299). In subgroup analyses, higher-income households showed decreases in income level, including Q4 (RoM, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.95-0.97; P < .001), whereas Q1 households showed a relative increase (RoM, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.94-2.16; P < .001).ConclusionsPediatric critical illness was not associated with a statistically significant change in household income at the population level. However, subgroup analyses suggested differing patterns of income change across baseline socioeconomic strata, including declines among higher-income households. These findings highlight potential socioeconomic heterogeneity in the financial consequences experienced by families following pediatric critical illness.

articles.title: Association Between Albumin-Bilirubin Index and Clinical Outcomes in Septic Acute Kidney Injury Patients.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe albumin-bilirubin index (ALBI) has been reported as a prognostic marker in various clinical conditions; however, its value in patients with septic acute kidney injury (AKI) has not been clearly evaluated. This study aimed to investigate the association between ALBI and clinical outcomes in this population.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. ALBI was analyzed as both a continuous variable in the primary analysis and a categorical variable according to tertiles in sensitivity analysis. The primary outcomes were 28-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) transfer, septic shock, and disease severity. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and mortality, and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess potential nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses were further conducted to examine the consistency across different sub-group populations.ResultsOverall, 6700 patients with septic AKI were included. In adjusted Cox models, each 1-standard deviation increase in ALBI was associated with higher risks of 28-day mortality (HR 1.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10-1.22), 60-day mortality (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.19), 90-day mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.18), and 1-year mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). The association between ALBI and mortality was generally consistent across most prespecified subgroups. Higher ALBI was also linked with septic shock (odds ratio [OR] 1.15, 95%CI 1.08-1.21, P < .001), ICU transfer (OR 1.09, 95%CI 1.02-1.16), and greater disease severity. RCS curves showed a nonlinear increase in mortality risk with ascending ALBI. Sensitivity analyses based on ALBI tertiles yielded broadly consistent findings.ConclusionHigher ALBI was independently associated with increased short- and long-term mortality and adverse clinical outcomes in septic AKI patients.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of interventions for preventing chemotherapy-induced alopecia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chemotherapy-induced alopecia (CIA) negatively affects patients' appearance and emotional well-being. This network meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy of different preventive interventions for CIA.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and EBSCO Open Dissertations from inception to March 2025. Randomized controlled trials evaluating interventions to prevent CIA in cancer patients and reporting hair preservation outcomes (as defined by individual trials, including CTCAE grade < 2, < 30 to < 50% hair loss, or WHO grade 0-2) were included. Scalp hypothermia was divided into three groups based on duration post-chemotherapy: short (0-45 min), traditional (46-90 min), and prolonged (> 90 min). Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB2. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Interventions were ranked with surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using CINeMA.

RESULTS: Of 6696 articles identified, 12 (n = 736) evaluating nine interventions (three scalp hypothermia durations, scalp compression, four pharmacological agents, and usual care) were included. Network meta-analysis indicated that prolonged-scalp hypothermia significantly improved hair preservation compared with usual care (RR = 24.66; 95%CI = 7.07-86.05; low certainty of evidence) and traditional scalp hypothermia (RR = 2.13; 95%CI = 1.15-3.93; very low certainty of evidence), and pharmacological agents (RRs ranging from 14.06 to 23.83; low certainty). However, prolonged-scalp hypothermia tended to show better hair preservation than short duration, though not statistically significant (RR = 2.06, 95%CI = 0.78-5.39). Based on SUCRA, prolonged-scalp hypothermia (97.0%) had the highest ranking, followed by short scalp hypothermia (78.6%) and traditional scalp hypothermia (76.8%). Most studies were rated as having high risk of bias, and the certainty of evidence was graded as low to very low.

CONCLUSION: Current low certainty evidence suggests that scalp hypothermia could prevent CIA. Prolonged-scalp hypothermia provides a higher degree of protection, whereas a short duration demonstrates a weaker protective effect. However, this difference was not statistically significant.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420251103932) and can be accessed via the following link: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251103932 .

articles.title: [Subsequent procedures after masculinizing surgery: neourethra and prosthetics].
articles.abstract: The goal of masculinizing genital surgery, which is usually performed over several planned operative stages, is to construct a genital that is both aesthetically and functionally satisfactory. It aims to create a phallus with the best possible sensitivity, a long-term stable neourethra for voiding in a standing position, and to enable penetrative sexual intercourse by means of erectile prostheses. Whether all of these steps are required depends on the individual needs of the trans man. Due to anatomical peculiarities (the absence of stable tissue types designed for the relevant function), both urethral surgery and penile prosthesis implantation differ significantly from those performed on cisgender male patients and result in higher complication rates. Since the neourethra is usually constructed from several tissue types not designed for contact with urine-such as the labia minora, vaginal mucosa, and formerly hair-bearing dermis-the main complications include urethral fistulas, strictures, and diverticulum formation, as well as hair growth within the neourethra with or without stone formation and consequent impaired urinary outflow. The most common complications of prosthesis implantation in trans men are infection, erosion, dislocation, and (premature) mechanical failure, which frequently necessitates further revisions and subsequent operations. The available evidence is predominantly based on retrospective data with small case numbers and is characterized by considerable heterogeneity regarding the definition of endpoints and the assessment of patient-reported outcomes. Despite these methodological limitations, the published studies overall show a high rate of functional satisfaction.

articles.title: Chicken-fat clots and pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density: a retrospective autopsy study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to explore the association between chicken-fat clots (CFCs) and neutrophil-related parameters in postmortem samples. Based on previous studies suggesting a potential role of neutrophils in CFC formation, the study aimed to assess whether CFCs are associated with increased neutrophil levels or intravascular neutrophil accumulation, rather than being explained solely by the traditional concept of "slow death".

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using autopsy data from November 2020 to November 2024. A total of 152 autopsies were screened, of which 122 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final cohort. Autopsy reports were reviewed together with available clinical documentation, including information on anticoagulants, vasoactive amines, corticosteroids, ongoing infections, and laboratory tests (leukocyte count, neutrophil percentage, and absolute neutrophil count). Because premortem laboratory data were frequently unavailable, particularly in traumatic deaths, lung tissue samples from all 122 decedents were analyzed. Digital pathology techniques, including scanning and analysis using QuPath software, were employed to quantify pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density. The association between intravascular neutrophil density and CFC presence was statistically analyzed using ROC curves, χ² tests, and odds ratios.

RESULTS: CFCs were present in 34 of 122 cases (27.9%), with septic shock representing the largest cause-of-death group among CFC-positive cases (29.4%). Increased pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density was significantly associated with CFC presence (OR 21.0, p < 0.001). A threshold of 2286 neutrophils/mm² showed good discrimination for CFC presence, with an AUC of 0.840. No significant associations were identified between CFCs and anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, or the other evaluated blood parameters.

CONCLUSION: Chicken-fat clots were associated with increased pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density in this retrospective autopsy cohort, suggesting a possible relationship with systemic inflammatory or neutrophil-mediated processes. These findings do not establish pulmonary intravascular neutrophil density as a validated marker of antemortem neutrophilia and do not exclude the contribution of agonal duration or postmortem processes to CFC formation. Further studies incorporating well-defined agonal timing and closely timed premortem laboratory data are needed to clarify the biological and temporal determinants of CFC formation.

articles.title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach.
articles.abstract: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield. In this prospective cohort study, adolescents with an abnormal ECG identified through a nationwide screening program underwent comprehensive clinical/genetic evaluation. Phenotype-negative individuals were included. Relatives underwent clinical screening, with cascade genetic testing offered when probands carried a likely/definite pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy variant. Abnormal screening outcomes included relatives with (i) de novo cardiomyopathy diagnosis, (ii) early cardiomyopathic traits, or (iii) gene-positive/phenotype-negative (G + P -) status. Sixteen adolescents (0.6%) met inclusion criteria, and 3 (18.8%) were G + (MYBPC3, MYH7, ACTC1). One in five relatives (n = 13/71, 18.3%; 95% CI 11.0-28.9%) were referred, most having an abnormal ECG (12.7%). Nine relatives (12.7%; 95% CI 4.9-20.4%) exhibited early cardiomyopathy traits at baseline. One (1.4%) relative was G + /P - . Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 3 (4.2%, 95% CI 0.9-11.8%) relatives at baseline (n = 2 HCM, n = 1 DCM). One relative with early cardiomyopathy traits underwent phenoconversion (NDLVC) during follow-up at 77 months, yielding an overall diagnostic rate of 5.6% (95% CI 2.0-13.8%) in 4 unrelated families. A joint clinical-genetic approach enabled personalized surveillance in 6 relatives (8.5%), including 2 (2.8%) diagnoses that would otherwise have been missed with conventional clinical screening.Conclusion: One in five relatives of ECG‑positive phenotype‑negative adolescents received a cardiomyopathy diagnosis or had early cardiomyopathy traits. A joint clinical-genetic approach in this subgroup may aid early cardiomyopathy detection in selected families, though findings remain exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. What is Known - What is New: •Resting ECG can identify individuals harboring conditions linked to sudden cardiac death •The penetrance of cardiomyopathy is age dependent, which explains why screened adolescents may exhibit abnormal ECG patterns in the absence of a cardiomyopathy diagnosis •Our data indicate that extending screening to relatives of ECG-positive, phenotype-negative adolescents is justified, with one in five relatives receiving a new cardiomyopathy diagnosis (5.6%) or exhibiting early cardiomyopathy traits (11.3%) •A joint clinical/genetic evaluation in this context may help personalize screening strategies.

articles.title: [Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus].
articles.abstract: Modern diabetology is undergoing a paradigm shift from glucose-centric management toward risk-adapted precision medicine. Differentiated phenotyping into clusters allows for the early identification of organ-specific risks. Pharmacotherapy now prioritizes cardiorenal protection using sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs; finerenone), which reduce vascular events beyond glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) reduction alone. Technological innovations, such as continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), complement traditional markers with dynamic metrics such as time in range. A new, realistic therapeutic goal is metabolic remission, facilitated by potent incretin mimetics and early intervention during the prediabetes stage. The ultimate objective is the sustainable restoration of normoglycemia and the prevention of end-organ damage through a multifactorial, individualized approach.

articles.title: Association Between Blood Pressure Response Index and Prognosis in Patients with Septic Shock Caused by Pneumonia.
articles.abstract: BackgroundNo noninvasive index exists to assess vasopressor responsiveness for maintaining blood pressure in severe pneumonia-induced shock. This study evaluated the association between the blood pressure response index (BPRI) and prognosis in such patients.MethodsA mixed retrospective and prospective cohort study analyzed clinical data from patients admitted to tertiary hospitals between January 2018 and January 2025. BPRI is the ratio between the mean arterial pressure and the vasoactive inotropic score. Cox regression analysis assessed the impact of BPRI on mortality risk, while Kaplan-Meier curves compared 30-day cumulative survival rates across BPRI tertiles. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated BPRI's predictive accuracy for mortality. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis explored potential nonlinear relationships between BPRI and mortality risk.ResultsThe retrospective cohort included 618 patients, with 332 (52.7%) fatalities. In the prospective cohort, 65 patients were enrolled, with 30 (46.2%) death. Cox regression analysis of the retrospective dataset indicated that higher BPRI values correlated with lower mortality risk (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]= 0.843, 95% confidence interval [CI] [0.811, 0.877]). The ROC analysis demonstrated that BPRI predicted 30-day mortality (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.7404, 95%=[0.7018,0.7790]) more accurately than the vasoactive inotropic score (AUC=0.7034, 95%CI = [0.6627,0.7440]) and mean arterial pressure (AUC=0.6638, 95%CI = [0.6201,0.7075]), consistent with prospective findings. The RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship between BPRI and mortality risk, with a cutoff value of 9.05.ConclusionA lower BPRI was significantly associated with increased mortality risk, following a nonlinear pattern. BPRI demonstrated substantial predictive value for severe pneumonia-induced shock.

articles.title: Kommerell diverticulum in right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery: Routine resection or selective management?
articles.abstract: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery (RAA-ALSA) is one of the most common complete vascular rings encountered in pediatric cardiovascular practice. The associated Kommerell diverticulum (KD), a remnant of the primitive fourth dorsal aortic arch from which the aberrant subclavian artery arises, forms part of the posterior ring and may contribute importantly to persistent airway and esophageal compression. Historically, repair consisted of division of the ligamentum arteriosum. Recognition that posterior compression can persist after ligamentum division has led many surgeons to add diverticulum resection and transfer or reimplantation of the aberrant subclavian artery. The optimal strategy remains controversial. Advocates of routine KD resection cite persistent compression after simple ring division, the low morbidity of resection in experienced centers, and abnormal diverticular histopathology that may imply future aneurysmal risk. Opponents emphasize that most children do well after less extensive repair that persistent symptoms frequently reflect associated airway disease rather than residual vascular compression, and that evidence proving superiority of universal resection is lacking. This review summarizes the embryology, anatomy, pathophysiology, and surgical management of KD in RAA-ALSA; critically examines evidence for routine and selective resection; and proposes a practical anatomy-driven approach.

articles.title: Vasopressors Combination Therapy (Norepinephrine Plus Vasopressin Receptor Agonists) Improve Septic Shock Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundStudies showed different results of vasopressors combination therapy in septic shock patients. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the outcomes of combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists in adult septic shock.MethodsCochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed databases were searched up to September 27, 2026, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists versus norepinephrine alone in septic shock patients. Two reviewers independently extracted data on mortality, ICU length of stay, renal replacement therapy (RRT) and adverse events. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess random error.ResultsTwenty-one RCTs involving 3873 septic shock patients were included. The results showed that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists was associated with lower mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.83 to 0.99, P = .02), but with an increased risk of digital ischemia (RR = 2.21, 95% CI 1.15 to 4.27, P = .02). Subgroup analysis indicated that the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may provide survival benefits for more severe septic shock patients (RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.00, P = .04). Moreover, compared with norepinephrine alone, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin showed a trend towards reducing the longest follow-up mortality (RR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.00, P = .05). TSA indicated lack of firm evidence for a beneficial effect.ConclusionsIn adults with septic shock, the combination of norepinephrine plus vasopressin receptor agonists may reduce mortality at the longest complete follow-up compared with norepinephrine alone (low quality of evidence), but may increase risk of digital ischemia (low quality of evidence). This benefit mainly appeared in more severe septic shock patients. Moreover, norepinephrine plus vasopressin may confer a survival advantage.

articles.title: Balanced Solutions Versus Normal Saline in Pediatric Septic Shock: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIn pediatric septic shock, early fluid resuscitation is a vital approach to treat this condition. The appropriate isotonic crystalloid to use (balanced salt solution [BSS] vs normal saline [NS]) remains debated. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the safety and efficacy of both isotonic crystalloid solutions in this patient population.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception until May 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing BSS with NS for fluid resuscitation in children (<18 years) with septic shock or sepsis. The primary outcome was hospital or 30-day mortality. We synthesized data using frequentist inverse-variance random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261391864), and the certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations (GRADE) for all outcomes.ResultsSix RCTs involving 9743 participants were included. For the primary outcome, BSS and NS demonstrated no significant differences in hospital or 30-day mortality rates (3.5% vs 3.7%; RR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.81-1.16, P = .72). Secondary analyses revealed that BSS significantly reduced the requirement for renal replacement therapy (RRT) (RR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97) and hyperchloremia (RR: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.57-0.75).ConclusionThe use of BSS versus NS showed no significant difference in short-term mortality among children with septic shock; however, BSS provided significant clinical and physiological advantages, including reduced incidences of hyperchloremia and the need for RRT.

articles.title: Effect of a structured healthcare professional-supported kangaroo care model on clinical outcomes in preterm neonates: A retrospective quasi-experimental cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of a structured healthcare professional-supported kangaroo mother care (KMC) model on physiological stability and clinical outcomes in preterm neonates hospitalized in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

METHODS: This retrospective quasi-experimental before-after cohort study included 64 preterm neonates (intervention: n = 33; comparison: n = 31) admitted to a tertiary-level NICU. During the comparison period, conventional KMC was provided once daily by mothers. Following implementation of a structured NICU protocol on 1 March 2025, KMC was administered eight times daily at three-hour intervals by both mothers and midwives/nurses. Primary outcomes included length of hospital stay and physiological parameters measured before and after KMC sessions.

RESULTS: Neonates in the intervention group had a significantly shorter hospital stay than those in the comparison group (p < 0.001). After adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and sex, comparison-group neonates had an adjusted hospital stay 9.88 days longer than intervention-group neonates (B = 9.884, 95% CI: 5.280-14.487, p < 0.001; R2 = 0.769). Post-KMC heart and respiratory rates were significantly lower and oxygen saturation was significantly higher in the intervention group (p < 0.001). Within-group analyses also showed significant improvements in physiological parameters following KMC, with larger effect sizes in the intervention group.

CONCLUSION: A structured healthcare professional-supported KMC model was associated with improved physiological stability and shorter hospitalization, supporting the integration of midwives and nurses to sustain KMC in NICU settings.

articles.title: Antidiabetic medications in the pipeline.
articles.abstract: There is an extensive pipeline of therapies for diabetes mellitus. It has been known for the past three decades that obesity is a key pathophysiological player, involving inflammation, insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction leading to type 2 diabetes and to significant cardiovascular, renal and hepatic complications, all central to the metabolic syndrome. On the basis of this knowledge and the disposition of drugs with multiple effects on different disease components, the diabetes therapeutic paradigm has shifted from merely glucocentric to multitargeted against these interconnected pathways.Much more recently, incretin-based multi-agonists have been developed that deliver unprecedented glycemic and weight benefits as well as weekly insulins and oral GLP-1 agonists that are able to reduce the burden of injectable therapies. An antibody-peptide conjugate that acts as a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor modulator has also shown promising results. Today, novel insulin sensitizers are modulating metabolic pathways towards higher energy expenditure with fewer side effects. Adjunctive agents for type 1 diabetes are improving glucose control while reducing hypoglycemia risk. Finally, drugs designed to restrain the inevitable muscle mass loss caused by antiobesity treatments are being tested. The diabetes pipeline is rich and there is hope that in the next few years, the therapeutic landscape will be further transformed with even more efficacious and individualized treatments.

articles.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Strains LP5 and BX62 Alleviate Liver Injury of NAFLD in Rats via Regulating Hepatic Cholesterol Metabolism and Antioxidant Signaling Pathways.
articles.abstract: Disorders of lipid metabolism and oxidative stress are pivotal factors in the advancement of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). This study aims to investigate the liver-protective effects of two Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (L. plantarum) strains, LP5 and BX62, either individually or in combined, on NAFLD in rats induced by high fat and cholesterol diet. Strain L. plantarum LP5 showed potential for modulating cholesterol metabolism, whereas L. plantarum BX62 exhibited enhanced antioxidant properties. All three intervention strategies alleviated liver injury, as evidenced by reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, intestinal permeability, inflammation, and liver injury markers. Notably, L. plantarum LP5 showed greater effects on reducing weight gain and hepatic steatosis, while L. plantarum BX62 provided additional protection against hepatic oxidative damage. Metabolic and molecular analyses suggested that the beneficial effects of L. plantarum LP5 were associated with altered bile acid homeostasis and increased expression of hepatic primary bile acid synthesis-related proteins (CYP7A1 and CYP8B1), whereas L. plantarum BX62 was associated with activation of the Nrf2-HO-1 antioxidant pathway (Nrf2, HO-1, and FTH).
