Furthermore, all intervention strategies activated AMPK signaling (p-AMPK/AMPK), accompanied by decreased expression of lipogenesis-related proteins (SREBP-1c, FASN, and SCD1) and increased expression of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins (PPARα and CPT1a), contributing to improved hepatic lipid metabolism. Collectively, our findings indicate that L. plantarum LP5 and L. plantarum BX62 alleviate HFHC diet-induced hepatic metabolic disturbances by complementary mechanisms involving cholesterol metabolism and antioxidant responses, highlighting their potential as dietary probiotics for supporting liver health and preventing NAFLD progression.

articles.title: Type 2 Inflammation in Airway Diseases: Eosinophilic Bronchiectasis as an Emerging Phenotype.
articles.abstract: Bronchiectasis is a chronic and highly heterogeneous airway disease traditionally regarded as a neutrophil-dominated condition driven by persistent infection and dysregulated innate immunity. Over the last decade, this traditional view has been increasingly challenged by the identification of distinct inflammatory phenotypes with important biological and therapeutic implications.Among these, eosinophilic bronchiectasis has emerged as a clinically meaningful and mechanistically distinct phenotype, characterized by type 2 (T2) immune activation, eosinophil-driven airway inflammation, and differential responsiveness to targeted therapies.In this narrative review, we provide an overview of eosinophilic bronchiectasis, emphasizing epidemiology, immunopathogenesis, and cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying airway damage and remodelling. We discuss key pathways involving eosinophils, epithelial-immune interactions, and T2 cytokine signalling, as well as established and emerging biomarkers for phenotype identification.We proposed a diagnostic framework and definitions for eosinophilic bronchiectasis, i.e. definite (airway eosinophilia with sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage eosinophils ≥ 3%), probable (persistent peripheral blood eosinophilia ≥ 300 cells/µL), and possible (a single elevated blood eosinophil count of ≥ 150-300 cells/µL or elevated FeNO > 25 ppb in the absence of asthma), to be provisionally used in the absence of shared consensus criteria.Particular attention is devoted to therapeutic implications, including biologic agents targeting the IL-5/IL-5r axes and novel disease-modifying strategies for eosinophilic disorders. Finally, we highlight unmet needs and future research directions toward precision medicine approaches aimed at improving outcomes in this increasingly recognized bronchiectasis phenotype.

articles.title: Short-course versus long-course antibiotics in bone infections: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The optimal duration of antibiotic therapy for bone infections remains controversial. We therefore conducted a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing short- versus long-course antibiotic therapy for bone infections.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through February 2026 for RCTs comparing short- and long-course antibiotic therapy in bone infections, including periprosthetic joint infection, diabetic foot osteomyelitis, vertebral osteomyelitis, and paediatric acute haematogenous osteomyelitis. Treatment failure and antibiotic-related adverse events were analysed using both intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) data. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using ROB 1 and GRADE.

RESULTS: In the ITT analysis, no significant difference in treatment failure was observed between short- and long-course therapy (RR = 1.12, 95% CI 0.77-1.62, P = 0.55). The PP analysis suggested a potential increase in treatment failure with short-course therapy (RR = 1.47, 95% CI 1.00-2.16, P = 0.05). Short-course therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of antibiotic-related adverse events (RR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.94, P = 0.006). Certainty of evidence was moderate for treatment failure outcomes and high for adverse events.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in treatment failure was observed between short- and long-course antibiotic therapy in the ITT analysis, whereas short-course therapy was associated with significantly fewer antibiotic-related adverse events. However, the PP analysis suggested a possible increase in treatment failure with short-course therapy. The included bone infections were clinically heterogeneous, which may limit generalisability.

articles.title: An impaired T-cell-mediated mitogen response as a potential biomarker to aid in clinical diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: A considerable proportion of suspected pulmonary tuberculosis (pTB) cases are identified and treated on the basis of clinical diagnoses, as it is often not possible to confirm Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. In the absence of pathogen detection, supplementary indicators, such as immunological biomarkers, would facilitate TB diagnostic decision-making.

METHODS: In this prospective case-control study conducted in Ghana, patients with suspected pTB (n = 83) were divided into three subgroups: confirmed cases with high (pTBhigh) or low (pTBlow) Mtb sputum load, and clinically diagnosed patients without Mtb confirmation (pTBclin). pTB patient subgroups were then compared with healthy contacts (controls; n = 49) for their immune responses to Mtb antigens (i.e. PPDMtb, ESAT6/CFP10), the mitogen phytohemagglutinin, and a superantigen.

RESULTS: About half of the pTB patients were pTBclin (n = 41; 49.4%), while pTBhigh accounted for only about one-third (n = 26; 31.3%) and pTBlow for about one-fifth (n = 16; 19.3%). Antigen-specific CD4+ T-cell responses varied among the pTB subgroups, and only the pTBhigh group had higher IFNγ+/TNFα+ T-cell proportions as compared to controls (PPDMtb, p = 0.0003; ESAT6/CFP10, p < 0.0001). In contrast, phytohemagglutinin induced significantly lower proportions of CD4+ T cells in all TB subgroups (pTBhigh, p < 0.0001; pTBlow, p = 0.0039; pTBclin, p = 0.0012 for IFNγ+/TNFα+) and this measurement distinguished patient subgroups effectively from controls (pTBhigh, p < 0.0001; pTBlow, p = 0.0132; pTBclin, p = 0.0006 for TNFα+/CD40L+). Finally, TNFα+/CD40L+ T-cell responses to phytohemagglutinine had the highest efficiency to distinguish pTBclin with severe lung manifestation from controls (AUC = 0.9; p < 0.0001; 95%CI:0.82-0.98).

CONCLUSION: This study underscores the importance of clinical pTB diagnosis and identifies a reduced T-cell cytokine response to phytohemagglutinin as a potential biomarker.

articles.title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.
articles.abstract: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

articles.title: Effect of telemedicine-delivered lifestyle interventions in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide two-arm randomized trial (PROACTIVE-19).
articles.abstract: Older adults are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes, yet randomized evidence on structured lifestyle interventions in this context remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the effects of a personalized lifestyle intervention on health-related behaviors and adverse outcomes among adults aged ≥ 60 years during the COVID-19 pandemic. PROACTIVE-19 was a nationwide, open-label, randomized trial initiated in Hungary in March 2020, during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants aged ≥ 60 years were randomly assigned (1:1) to general (group A) or personalized (group B) lifestyle counselling delivered via telephone, targeting mental health, smoking, physical activity, diet, and alcohol consumption. The primary planned endpoint was a composite of COVID-19 severity outcomes; however, due to infection rates, all-cause mortality was assessed. Longitudinal lifestyle changes were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) in a modified intention-to-treat population. A total of 441 participants were analyzed (214 group A; 227 group B). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.28-1.53). Significant overall time effects were observed for fruit and vegetable consumption (β = 0.052, CI 0.026-0.074), smoking reduction among current smokers (β = - 0.372, CI - 0.528 to - 0.222), and psychological variables. A significantly greater reduction in estimated alcohol consumption was observed in group B among baseline drinkers compared with group A (β = - 1.357, CI - 2.425 to - 0.187), particularly in women. However, BMI among participants with obesity increased in group B (β = 0.068, CI 0.013-0.119). Seasonal and pandemic-wave effects significantly influenced physical activity and psychological distress. The personalized intervention was not associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality. Several lifestyle behaviors improved over time; however, the additional benefit of personalization was limited (Supported by the Semmelweis University Research, Development and Innovation Fund, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04321928).

articles.title: Integrating volumes into myocardial work: the prognostic role of non-invasive pressure-strain-volume analysis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract: The accurate echocardiographic assessment of the left ventricular (LV) contractile state remains challenging in aortic stenosis, as ejection fraction and even global longitudinal strain are markedly load-dependent. The novel pressure-strain loop-derived myocardial work were developed to overcome this limitation; however, incorporation of instantaneous LV volume may further improve this method. We aimed to quantify myocardial work using pressure-strain-volume (PSV) loops and to evaluate its prognostic value in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We enrolled 300 patients scheduled for TAVI (age 78.7 ± 6.3 years, 41% female). The endpoint was all-cause mortality, reached by 62 patients over a median follow-up of 25 months. Echocardiography and non-invasive blood pressure measurements were performed one day before TAVI. LV pressure was estimated noninvasively, while strain curves were derived from speckle-tracking analysis. Pressure-strain relations were adjusted to instantaneous LV volumes to construct PSV loops, yielding volume-adjusted indices (GWIVi and GCWVi). GWIVi showed similar extent of LV dysfunction in classical and paradoxical low-flow low-gradient AS phenotypes compared to the normal flow-high gradient patients (46.98 ± 20.71 vs. 51.99 ± 18.43 vs. 63.74 ± 22.26 mmHg%L/m2, p < 0.001), while other LV function parameters did not. In multivariable Cox-regression, GWIVi was an independent predictor of mortality (Hazard ratio: 0.955 [confidence interval: 0.773-0.993], p < 0.05) alongside clinically relevant other markers such as hemoglobin and atrial fibrillation. PSV loop-derived myocardial work detected LV mechanical differences between AS phenotypes and provided independent prognostic value in TAVI candidates, potentially offering a more physiologically accurate assessment of LV function in this population.

articles.title: Computed tomography-derived cardiac parameters versus biochemical inflammatory indices for discriminating disease severity and identifying cardiovascular comorbidity in obstructive sleep apnoea: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: It is unclear whether haematological inflammatory indices or CT-derived cardiac parameters add discriminative information beyond standard clinical variables in obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome (OSAS). We compared both modalities, alone and combined, against age, sex and body mass index (BMI) for identifying severe OSAS and associated cardiovascular comorbidity.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cross-sectional study of 401 participants (240 OSAS, 161 controls). Four nested logistic regression models were fitted in the OSAS cohort: M0 (age, sex, BMI); M1 (M0 plus biochemical indices CAR, NLR, PLR, SII); M2 (M0 plus CT-derived cardiac parameters: pulmonary artery [PA] diameter, PA/aorta ratio, RV/LV ratio, ventricular wall thicknesses); and M3 (M0 plus CT plus biochemical). We compared discrimination (AUC, DeLong), reclassification (continuous NRI, IDI) and model fit (likelihood ratio tests), with internal validation by 500-iteration bootstrap optimism correction and repeated tenfold cross-validation. Missing predictor data were handled by multiple imputation (MICE, m = 20) as the primary approach. Cardiovascular outcomes were defined from echocardiography to avoid predictor-outcome overlap.

RESULTS: For severe OSAS, M2 improved on M0 (AUC 0.755 vs 0.716; LR p = 0.005; NRI + 0.60 [95% CI 0.35-0.83]; IDI + 0.055 [0.027-0.083]), whereas M1 did not (LR p = 0.62). M3 added nothing over M2 (ΔAUC = 0.007; LR p = 0.63). Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.705, 0.695, 0.721 and 0.716 for M0-M3, so the incremental gain was modest. Nocturnal hypoxaemia indices discriminated severe OSAS far better than CT (ODI AUC 0.888 vs PA diameter 0.699), and once ODI and T90 were available CT added little (ΔAUC < 0.01). CT parameters gave modest reclassification for hypertension, coronary artery disease and the composite cardiovascular outcome; biochemical indices did not.

CONCLUSIONS: CT-derived cardiac parameters, particularly PA diameter, added discrimination over age, sex and BMI for severe OSAS; haematological indices did not. When thoracic CT is already available for another indication, opportunistic measurement of PA dimensions may complement clinical risk stratification. These findings are exploratory and require prospective external validation.

articles.title: Differential associations of early fluid accumulation with acute kidney injury and mortality in critically ill children: a prospective cohort study with mediation and propensity-score analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cumulative fluid accumulation (FA), historically termed fluid overload, is reported to increase mortality in critically ill children, but whether its associations differ across renal and mortality outcomes-and whether any mortality association reflects a direct pathway, confounding, or mediation via acute kidney injury (AKI)-is unresolved. We applied convergent causal-inference methods.

METHODS: In a prospective cohort of 360 children (1 month-18 years) admitted ≥24 h to a tertiary paediatric intensive care unit, early fluid accumulation (first 24 h, Goldstein formula; historically termed fluid overload) was dichotomised at ≥5%.

PRIMARY OUTCOME: AKI (AKI Network criteria); secondary outcomes: PICU mortality, mechanical ventilation duration, length of stay.

ANALYSES: sequential multivariable regression, restricted cubic splines, propensity score matching, additive/multiplicative interaction, incremental discrimination, and exploratory mediation, all adjusted for the Paediatric Risk of Mortality III (PRISM III) score.

RESULTS: FA ≥ 5% occurred in 23.1%, AKI in 24.7%, mortality 19.4%. FA predicted AKI (adjusted OR 4.45; propensity-matched 2.72), with a non-linear dose-response inflecting at 2-5%. FA did not predict mortality: the crude association disappeared on AKI adjustment, the adjusted spline was flat, the matched estimate was null (OR 1.36), and FA added negligibly to PRISM III discrimination (ΔAUC 0.007). AKI dominated mortality (10.0% to 77.8% stagewise); the FA×AKI interaction was sub-additive; mediation attributed FA's small total association to AKI. FA was associated with longer PICU stay and ventilation.

CONCLUSIONS: Early FA shows differential associations: a potentially modifiable risk marker for AKI, associated with longer intensive care, but not independently associated with death once severity and AKI are considered. Limiting early FA may be a reasonable target for AKI prevention, although this requires interventional confirmation; PRISM III remains the mortality-prognostic tool.

articles.title: Clinical and metabolic factors associated with surgical intervention in pediatric urolithiasis: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify clinical, radiological, and metabolic factors associated with surgical intervention in children with urinary stone disease.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 1,018 children with urinary stone disease at 21 pediatric nephrology centers in Türkiye between January 2014 and January 2024: all 498 who underwent surgery and a purposively selected comparison group of 520 managed without surgery. Firth's penalized logistic regression identified factors independently associated with surgery (730 complete cases, 343 events, 22 terms, 15.6 events per variable).

RESULTS: The surgical group was older (median 43.0 vs. 12.0 months, p < 0.001). Stone size was the factor most strongly associated with surgery: compared with stones of 1-5 mm, adjusted odds were higher for 6-10 mm (aOR = 9.84, 95% CI: 6.31-15.36) and for stones larger than 10 mm (aOR=64.51, 95% CI: 25.95-160.34), corresponding to predicted probabilities of 22.4%, 66.2%, and 91.6%. General infectious symptoms (aOR = 4.91), ureteral stones (aOR = 2.65), isolated pyuria (aOR = 2.22), stone passage (aOR = 1.94) and hydronephrosis (aOR = 1.88) were also independently associated, whereas vitamin D supplementation was associated with lower odds (aOR=0.44, 95% CI: 0.26-0.74), an exploratory, age-sensitive association. Hematuria with pyuria was not independently associated after adjustment (aOR = 1.36, p = 0.305). Four associations remained significant after control of the false discovery rate; discrimination was high (area under the curve 0.91, optimism-corrected 0.90).

CONCLUSION: Stone size was the dominant factor associated with surgical intervention, followed by stone location, infectious presentation, and hydronephrosis. Hematuria with pyuria was not independently associated once stone burden was accounted for. External validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: When to start continuous kidney replacement therapy in critically ill children: a practical, PICU-focused, evidence-based review.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and fluid overload (FO) are common in critically ill children and have been shown to be associated with adverse outcomes. Continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) is the preferred renal support modality in paediatric intensive care to treat children with AKI and FO and may be necessary for non-renal indications like life-threatening toxin or electrolyte removal. However, the timing of CKRT initiation remains a contentious and highly variable clinical decision. Classic indications for dialysis are well established, yet modern paediatric intensive care practice increasingly emphasises earlier intervention for FO and evolving multi-organ dysfunction. Adult randomised trials have not demonstrated a survival benefit for early CKRT based on biochemical thresholds alone, mainly AKI stage. However, their applicability to paediatric populations is limited by distinct disease biology, developmental physiology, and fluid tolerance. This review synthesises current evidence and expert guidance to provide a pragmatic, physiology-driven framework for CKRT initiation in critically ill children. Emphasis is placed on dynamic assessment of kidney trajectory, fluid balance, and extra-renal organ impact rather than fixed biochemical thresholds or rigid timing paradigms. Integration of these factors balances the relative benefits and risks of early CKRT initiation and facilitates timely and individualised decisions that optimise outcomes in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: The pharmacokinetics of a single intravenous dose of difelikefalin in adolescents aged 12 to 17 years on hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to evaluate the pharmacokinetic profile, safety, and tolerability of a single intravenous bolus injection of difelikefalin in adolescents on maintenance hemodialysis.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label study, adolescents (12 to 17 years old) received a single difelikefalin dose of 0.5 μg/kg dry body weight at the end of the dialysis. Blood samples were collected over 3 days to assess difelikefalin plasma concentrations, and participants were followed up for adverse events (AEs) for 7-10 days. Key pharmacokinetic parameters were maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) from 0 to 48 h (AUC0-48 h) and AUC extrapolated to infinity (AUCinf). A prespecified numerical comparison of these parameters was conducted against data from a previous study in adults on hemodialysis (NCT02229929).

RESULTS: Eight participants completed the study and seven (3 males and 4 females; aged 12-17 [mean 15.1] years) had evaluable pharmacokinetic data. Mean (standard deviation) Cmax, AUC0-48 h, and AUCinf were 6.03 (1.81) ng/mL, 63.4 (17.4) h ng/mL, and 72.5 (23.7) h ng/mL, respectively. Systemic exposure was comparable between adolescents and adults. One participant developed two mild treatment-related AEs (headache and dizziness), but there were no serious AEs or AEs leading to study withdrawal.

CONCLUSION: After a single difelikefalin 0.5 μg/kg dose, the overall exposure in adolescents on hemodialysis was comparable to prior adult data, with no new safety signals identified, supporting further evaluation of the 0.5 μg/kg dose in adolescents with moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus.

articles.title: Response to letter to the editors: Comment on "Implementation and evaluation of a quality improvement project to standardize food insecurity screening in a pediatric nephrology clinic".
Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain.

MATERIALS & METHODS: Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality.

CONCLUSION: The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: Paediatric Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic and inflammatory diseases: a contemporary systematic review with meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is prevalent worldwide, and its potential protective role in allergic and immune diseases has been a topic of speculation. This systematic review aims to analyse recent literature to establish a consensus on this relationship. Articles published in the past 12 years regarding association of H. pylori and various allergic diseases were screened. Thirty-five articles from three databases were assessed for bias using the ROBINS-E tool. Objective data from each article were collected for this review. Among the reviewed articles, 14 focused on asthma, 10 on eliac disease(CeD), 5 on eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), 7 on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and 8 on mixed conditions. In the asthma meta-analysis, H. pylori infection was not significantly associated with asthma overall (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54-1.05; I2 = 67.3%). Subgroup analyses showed an inverse association in studies using UBT/SAT, whereas histology-based studies showed no association. Low-risk-of-bias studies likewise showed no significant association. Results for celiac and IBD were mixed. No clear trends were observed for the other conditions analysed.

CONCLUSION: Current paediatric evidence does not demonstrate a significant overall association between H. pylori infection and asthma. Apparent inverse associations were confined to specific diagnostic and risk-of-bias subgroups. Evidence for celiac disease, IBD, EoE, and other immune-mediated disorders remains inconsistent. More prospective paediatric studies are needed to understand the immune modulation of H. pylori infection.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • The relationship between Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic or immune-mediated diseases remains complex and incompletely understood. • Previous studies, including mixed studies with adult and paediatric populations, have reported inconsistent and sometimes conflicting associations.

WHAT IS NEW: • This is the first comprehensive paediatric review covering multiple conditions simultaneously, synthesising evidence on the association between Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic and immune-mediated diseases. • Analysis of paediatric data found no overall association between H. pylori infection and asthma risk. Histology-based studies confirmed this finding, whereas a slight inverse association was observed only in studies using non-invasive diagnostic methods (UBT or SAT) and in those with a higher risk of bias.

articles.title: Dorsomedial striatum calcium permeable AMPA receptors in the development of aversion-resistant alcohol drinking.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Alcohol use disorder is defined by drinking alcohol despite knowledge of negative consequences, often referred to as aversion-resistant drinking (The dorsomedial (DMS) and dorsolateral striatum (DLS) are necessary for goal-directed and habitual action selection, respectively. Leading hypotheses posit that once drug use becomes compulsive, DMS dependence degrades while DLS dependence increases. This shift may be mediated by changes in synaptic weights from glutamatergic inputs.

OBJECTIVES: Using a combination of western-blot, micro-injections, and ex-vivo electrophysiology in male and female C57BL/6J mice, we investigated the role of α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors AMPAR, which drive glutamatergic transmission, during quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in the DMS and DLS across the development of aversion-resistant drinking.

RESULTS: We found that AMPAR subunit composition and function change in the DMS across the development of aversion-resistant drinking whereby, calcium permeable (CP) - AMPARs drive behavior. Western blots revealed a negative relationship between DMS GluA1 and quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in alcohol naive mice and a positive relationship between DMS Glu A1/A2 ratios and quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in aversion-resistant mice indicating that aversion-resistance positively predicts likelihood for CP-AMPAR expression in the DMS. Female aversion-resistant mice also had significant positive relationships with DMS or DLS Glu A1/A2 ratios and female aversion-resistant mice had a significant negative relationship with GluA2 and aversion-resistant alcohol drinking. DMS CP-AMPAR antagonism caused an increase in quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in alcohol naïve mice suggesting that CP-AMPARs in the DMS prevent aversion-resistant drinking. Ex-vivo electrophysiology of DMS spiny projection neurons revealed that aversion-resistant drinking mice had greater inward rectification and CP-AMPAR antagonist sensitivity than alcohol naïve mice indicating that spiny projection neurons in the DMS express more CP-AMPARs following the development of aversion-resistant drinking. However, sensitivity to CP-AMPAR antagonism negatively predicted aversion-resistant drinking in alcohol history mice.

CONCLUSIONS: These data provide evidence that repeated alcohol binges alter DMS CP-AMPAR activity, where initial DMS activity acts to causally prevent aversion-resistant drinking but after repeated binges that result in aversion-resistant alcohol drinking, DMS spiny projection neurons recruit CP-AMPARs. CP-AMPAR antagonism was negatively association with aversion-resistant drinking within the alcohol history mice suggesting that plasticity of DMS CP-AMPARs is not related to quinine-sensitivity. These data provide evidence for a causal role of the DMS in aversion-resistant drinking and open questions as to the functional role of CP-AMPARs across the drinking history and striatal cell types.

articles.title: Thrombosed mycotic aneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery mimicking a parapharyngeal abscess in a child: a case report of multimodal imaging diagnosis.
articles.abstract: A parapharyngeal abscess, although relatively rare, is a potentially life-threatening deep neck space infection in the pediatric population that carries a risk of serious complications. Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery (ICA) is a rare vascular complication in children that can lead to catastrophic hemorrhage if misdiagnosed and attempted for surgical incision. We report a 7-year-old malnourished boy presenting with fever, dysphagia, and neck stiffness. Suboptimal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) suggested a left parapharyngeal abscess, and surgical drainage was planned. A dedicated CT, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, magnetic resonance angiography, and three-dimensional CT angiography identified a completely thrombosed mycotic pseudoaneurysm rather than an abscess. This case demonstrates that complete thrombosis transforms a mycotic pseudoaneurysm into a mass that can easily be mistaken for an abscess without the right imaging modalities and high-quality imaging.

articles.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models.

RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Cardio-hepatic injury phenotypes and short-term outcomes in acute decompensated heart failure.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal liver biochemistry is common in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), yet most studies evaluate individual markers rather than clinically meaningful patterns of hepatic involvement. We examined whether cardiohepatic injury phenotypes derived from routine liver tests identify distinct short-term prognostic profiles in patients hospitalized with ADHF.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included consecutive adults hospitalized with ADHF between December 2006 and 2017. Using peak in-hospital values of aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin, patients were classified into four phenotypes: no hepatic injury, hepatocellular injury, cholestatic injury, or combined injury. Associations with in-hospital mortality were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Post-discharge outcomes (30-day mortality, readmission, and their composite) were analyzed using Cox and Fine-Gray models.

RESULTS: Among 8332 ADHF admissions, 6792 (81.5%) had sufficient data for phenotype classification: 58.1% had no hepatic injury, 22.1% hepatocellular injury, 13.1% cholestatic injury, and 6.7% combined injury. In-hospital mortality differed markedly across phenotypes (3.5%, 16.3%, 9.0%, and 24.3%, respectively; p < 0.001). After adjustment, all injury phenotypes independently predicted in-hospital death compared with no injury. Among 6128 patients included in adjusted post-discharge analyses, hepatocellular and combined injury were independently associated with higher 30-day mortality and the composite outcome, whereas isolated cholestatic injury was not. Hepatocellular and combined injury independently predicted 30-day readmission.

CONCLUSIONS: Routine liver test patterns identify clinically meaningful cardiohepatic phenotypes in ADHF. While all hepatic injury phenotypes are associated with increased in-hospital mortality, only phenotypes with hepatocellular involvement predict adverse early post-discharge outcomes. Pattern-based interpretation of liver tests may improve early risk stratification in patients hospitalized with ADHF.

articles.title: Echocardiography-derived Left Atrial Volumetric-Mechanical Coupling Index predicts early new-onset atrial fibrillation after embolic stroke/transient ischemic attack of undetermined source.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
AIM: In patients with embolic stroke or transient ischemic attack of undetermined source (ESUS/TIA), occult atrial fibrillation (AF) is a frequent underlying mechanism with critical therapeutic implications, yet selecting patients who warrant intensified rhythm monitoring remains challenging. The Left Atrioventricular Coupling Index (LACI = LA end-diastolic volume/LV end-diastolic volume) captures atrioventricular uncoupling, whereas the Left Atrial Volumetric-Mechanical Coupling Index (LACI-VM = LAVi/a') integrates atrial size with mechanical performance; both may capture complementary domains of atrial remodelling relevant to subclinical AF. We aimed to investigate the association of LACI-VM and LACI with incident AF in ESUS/TIA.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, 285 consecutive patients with ESUS/TIA of undetermined source underwent transthoracic echocardiography at index hospitalization, including measurement of LACI-VM and LACI. The primary endpoint was new-onset AF during follow-up. Median age was 71 years and 43% were women. Over a median follow-up of 10.9 months, AF occurred in 24 patients (8.4%), with 62% of events occurring within the first year. LACI-VM was higher in patients who developed AF and remained independently associated with incident AF after multivariable adjustment (HR 6.64, CI 1.34-59.88; p = 0.041). LACI showed a non-significant association overall (HR 2.28, CI 0.74-7.01; p = 0.09), with predictive value confined to events within 12 months. A combined assessment of LACI-VM and LV filling pressures further refined risk stratification: patients with preserved LACI-VM (< 2.5) and normal filling pressures (E/e' ≤ 10) had a very low AF incidence (~ 2%), identifying a truly low-risk subgroup; conversely, when both LACI-VM (≥ 2.5) and filling pressures (E/e' > 10) were impaired, AF risk was ~ tenfold higher (~ 20%).

CONCLUSION: In ESUS/TIA, echocardiography-derived LACI-VM independently predicts incident AF and identifies patients at genuinely low risk. As a simple echocardiographic metric, its integration with LV filling pressures may support a more personalized use of rhythm monitoring.

articles.title: New insights into takotsubo syndrome: results from a multicenter cohort.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Takotsubo syndrome has long been deemed a benign condition following sudden emotional stress. While current mechanisms explaining the acute cardiac dysfunction are not fully understood, current evidence suggests certain takotsubo populations are at higher risk of adverse course. Acute neurologic emergencies commonly precede the takotsubo syndrome and new insights into the role of the brain-heart axis and central autonomic regions driving excess sympathetic activation have come about.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicenter analysis included 595 patients admitted between January 2013 and December 2024 with takotsubo syndrome across 13 German tertiary care centers. The aim of this study was to (I) assess whether acute brain pathology influences severity of cardiac dysfunction differently in comparison to other nonneurologic forms of physical or emotional stress, (II) investigate short-term recovery of cardiac function, and (III) improve identification of vulnerable patients susceptible to critical in-hospital course. Marginal odds ratios were estimated for cardiac complications of takotsubo syndrome across trigger groups using generalized estimating equations. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were fit to analyze the association between prespecified variables for short-term recovery of wall motion and systolic abnormalities as well as critical in-hospital course. Acute neurologic emergencies (47.5%) and common physical triggers (37.9%) were associated with higher risk of cardiac complications in takotsubo syndrome compared to emotional triggers (12.5%). Nonapical forms of takotsubo syndrome showed improved recovery of wall motion abnormalities (OR 2.70, 95% CI 1.34-5.45), while older patients had worse recovery of systolic function to discharge (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93). Conversely, younger male patients in which disease was triggered by neurologic emergencies or physical triggers presented with higher odds of critical in-hospital course.

CONCLUSION: Results of this study challenge the assumption of uniform reversibility of cardiac dysfunction and emphasize the need for early risk stratification and awareness of high-risk features as well as varying clinical presentations.

articles.title: Association of lipoprotein(a) with ischemia-reperfusion injury in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia adversely affects ischemia-reperfusion injury in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor beyond traditional lipid markers; however, its impact on ischemic myocardial injury remains unclear. We therefore investigated the association of Lp(a) with myocardial and microvascular damage assessed by multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), as well as clinical outcomes in STEMI patients.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective MARINA-STEMI (NCT04113356) cohort study, 518 STEMI patients (median age 59 years, 19% female) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were included. Lp(a) and lipid parameters, including low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, were measured at hospital admission. CMR was performed at a median of 4 days (interquartile range (IQR) 3-5) and 4 months (IQR 4-5) after PCI. The primary objective was to assess the association of Lp(a) with infarct size (IS) and severe microvascular injury, defined as intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) on baseline CMR. The clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause death, re-infarction, or new congestive heart failure). Median Lp(a) and LDL cholesterol levels were 27 nmol/l (IQR 20-90) and 141 mg/dl (IQR 117-166), respectively. LDL cholesterol correlated with IS at baseline (ρ = 0.114, p = 0.010) and was higher in patients with IMH (145 vs. 140 mg/dl, p = 0.031). In contrast, Lp(a) showed no correlation with IS (ρ = 0.051, p = 0.246) and no association with IMH (25 vs. 28 nmol/l, p = 0.632). Elevated Lp(a) (≥ 105 nmol/l) was not associated with MACE (8.7% vs. 8.8%, p = 0.966).

CONCLUSIONS: While LDL cholesterol was significantly associated with IS and IMH, Lp(a) was not related to ischemia-reperfusion injury patterns or clinical outcomes in patients with STEMI treated with primary PCI.

articles.title: Temporal cytokine trajectories during microaxial flow pump support identify a high-risk inflammatory phenotype in cardiogenic shock.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support, the mortality rate for patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) remains high. Current shock frameworks rely on hemodynamic parameters and fail to capture ongoing biological injury. Our study aimed to investigate cytokine trajectories during support and their association with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 113 patients with CS in SCAI stage ≥ C who were treated with microaxial flow pump (mAFP). Serial cytokine levels were measured from the time of mAFP implantation until day 7 afterwards. Time-point-specific multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 30-day mortality. The incremental prognostic value of cytokine levels was evaluated in relation to age, lactate, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), with interaction analyses conducted in relation to hemodynamic severity and blood culture positivity.

RESULTS: The overall 30-day mortality rate in the study cohort was 26.5%. IL-6 trajectories diverged progressively between survivors and non-survivors during mAFP support, with the greatest separation at 72 h. At this time point, log-transformed IL-6 was independently associated with 30-day mortality. ROC analysis at 72 h showed moderate discriminatory performance (AUC 0.745) and identified an optimal cut-off of 164.5 pg/mL (sensitivity 68.0%; specificity 82.1%). Patients with IL-6 levels ≥ 164.5 pg/mL presented with lower 30-day survival in exploratory landmark-type Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p < 0.001). This association was not modified by blood culture positivity, although infection, culture-negative inflammatory complications, and vasoplegic/distributive physiology cannot be excluded as contributors to IL-6 elevation.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by mAFP, persistent IL-6 elevation at 72 h was associated with increased 30-day mortality and provided additional prognostic information alongside established clinical severity markers. These findings suggest that ongoing inflammatory activity may provide additional prognostic information and support further evaluation of serial IL-6 measurements for risk stratification.

articles.title: Promoting equity, diversity and inclusion in intensive Care: a position paper of the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine.
Medical Conditions and Early Development in Toddlers With Down Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental and behavioral pediatrics : JDBP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations between medical conditions and early developmental skills in young children with Down syndrome (DS).

METHOD: Data were drawn from the first timepoint of a longitudinal study of children with DS (n = 114; mean age = 20.6 months). Caregivers completed a comprehensive medical history questionnaire, followed by a structured interview and review by a medical doctor to clarify endorsed conditions. Cognitive, expressive, and receptive communication, and fine and gross motor developments were assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth edition. Associations between medical condition categories and developmental skills across domains were examined using partial correlations adjusting for age. Dominance analyses assessed the unique contributions of significant medical categories.

RESULTS: Vision conditions were associated with lower developmental scores across cognitive, communication, and gross motor domains. Seizure/epilepsy was associated with lower cognitive, expressive communication, and motor domain scores. Length of neonatal intensive care unit stay was associated with lower cognitive and communication scores. Additional factors, including premature birth, structural gastrointestinal conditions, dysphagia, eczema, and thyroid disease, were associated with lower scores in specific developmental domains. Dominance analyses revealed overlapping contributions across significant predictors with each developmental domain.

CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the associations between co-occurring medical conditions and developmental heterogeneity among young children with DS. Results underscore the need for further work, including longitudinal research studies, to clarify the role of medical conditions in shaping neurodevelopment in DS.

articles.title: A Cohort Retrospective Observational Study of Hospital Accreditation Influence on Medication Safety in Saudi Hospitals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Medication errors remain a leading cause of adverse events globally and in Saudi Arabia, accounting for up to 45% of reported medical errors. Despite accreditation programs aiming to improve patient safety, evidence of their impact on medication management (MM) standards is limited. This study addresses this gap by evaluating MM compliance in Saudi hospitals from 2016 to 2023, post-implementation of the Central Board for Accreditation of Healthcare Institutions' Essential Safety Requirements (ESR).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed ESR survey data from 454 hospitals nationwide. Of these, 161 hospitals met the inclusion criteria by completing all 6 annual ESR surveys (2016-2019, 2022-2023); 293 hospitals were excluded due to incomplete longitudinal data. Scores for 3 MM standards: MM5 (high-alert medication safety), MM6 (look-alike and sound-alike medication safety), and MM41 (medication error monitoring) were extracted. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, repeated measures analysis of variance, and independent t tests comparing 2016-2019 and 2022-2023 periods. MM compliance was not reported during the COVID pandemic period (2020-2021).

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed across all MM standards over time. Mean MM5 scores increased from 69.56 in 2016 to 95.66 in 2023, MM6 from 40.79 to 96.10, and MM41 from 61.13 to 93.27 (all P < .001). Independent t tests confirmed substantial gains: MM5 rose from 70.06 to 92.28 (t = -14.50, P < .001), MM6 from 71.59 to 95.63 (t = -15.41, P < .001), and MM41 from 64.98 to 88.17 (t = -14.63, P < .001). Ownership type showed no significant effect (P > .05), and hospital bed size had no meaningful impact on MM5 and MM6, with a minor trend for MM41 (P = .001 but not statistically significant).

CONCLUSIONS: The period after implementation of the Central Board for Accreditation of Healthcare Institutions ESR standards saw significantly improved medication safety compliance in Saudi hospitals, suggesting the effectiveness of accreditation in promoting patient safety. Policymakers should sustain these efforts to maintain progress. Future research should evaluate patient outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and adopt mixed-methods approaches to explore contextual factors influencing compliance.

articles.title: Job-related stress, workplace incivility and quality of nursing care among Jordanian critical care nurses.
articles.abstract: BackgroundQuality of nursing care is one of the most important patient outcomes. The goal of Health care professionals is to provide patients and clients with safe assessment and treatment.ObjectiveThis study was conducted to explore the relationship between Job-related Stress, Workplace Incivility and Quality of Nursing Care among Jordanian Critical Care Nurses.MethodsA cross-sectional design was used. One hundred and eighty-five nurses from different hospitals participated in the study and completed the study's questionnaires including Nurses' Occupational Stress Scale (NOSS), Nursing workplace incivility (NIS) and Quality of nursing care (QONC).ResultsThe results showed that patients'/visitors' incivility (M = 41.11, SD = 7.03) was the major type of incivility in workplace among critical nurses. Critical care nurses reported high levels of job-related stress (M = 64.17, SD = 6.74). The results showed that insufficient support from coworkers was the highest among many of the participants (M = 9.45, SD = 1.51). The results from the current study show that nurses' responsibility for decision-making and delegation was highest among the participants (M = 20.11, SD = 3.27) in contrast to nursing care organization being the lowest (M = 7.14, SD = 1.13). A positive relationship between job-related stress and quality of nursing care (r = 0.551, p = 0.001, respectively) and a negative relationship between workplace incivility and quality of nursing care (r = -0.625, p = .002) were found.Conclusionsthese results might help administrators develop strategies and educational programs to improve the quality of nursing care in hospitals.

articles.title: Positioning of Depemokimab in Uncontrolled Severe Asthma.
articles.journal: Journal of investigational allergology & clinical immunology
articles.abstract: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways affecting more than 300 million people worldwide. It is estimated that between 3% and 10% have severe asthma. Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody developed for type 2 respiratory disease, enabling administration every 26 weeks. It produces rapid and sustained reductions in blood eosinophil counts. This twice-yearly regimen markedly reduces injection frequency and may lessen treatment burden. In the replicate phase 3 SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials, depemokimab reduced the pooled annualized rate of clinically significant exacerbations by 54% and exacerbations requiring hospitalization or emergency department care by 72% compared with placebo in patients aged 12 years or older with severe eosinophilic asthma. In chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), depemokimab was evaluated in the replicate phase 3 ANCHOR-1 and ANCHOR-2 trials. Both coprimary endpoints were met, and these studies provide evidence that twice-yearly depemokimab reduces the endoscopic nasal polyp score and improves nasal obstruction over 52 weeks in inadequately controlled CRSwNP. Depemokimab is approved for both severe asthma with type 2 inflammation and severe CRSwNP, making it a therapeutic option when both conditions coexist. Based on currently available evidence, depemokimab represents an additional option for patients with severe eosinophilic asthma in whom prevention of exacerbation is a major therapeutic goal. The twice-yearly dosing schedule may also be relevant when reducing treatment burden is a patient priority, although the effect of this reduction on adherence and persistence remains to be proved.

articles.title: Use of the face mask in peritoneal dialysis: Analysis of an online survey on global practices.
articles.journal: Peritoneal dialysis international : journal of the International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis
articles.abstract: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is an established home-based therapy. Face masks have historically been used as an infection-prevention measure during PD exchanges, although their effectiveness remains uncertain. Current evidence emphasizes hand hygiene and aseptic technique, while the incremental benefit of routine face mask use has not been clearly established. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of PD nurses and nephrologists to describe clinical practices regarding face mask use during PD exchanges. Participants were recruited through professional networks and international professional organizations. The survey included questions regarding patient and healthcare professional mask use, institutional guidance, patient training, and perceptions of effectiveness. A total of 733 healthcare professionals from 71 countries responded, including 617 nurses (84.2%). Face masks were reported to be always used by patients during bag exchanges or connection to the cycler by 72.3% (n = 530) of respondents. The most frequently reported reason for mask use was general infection prevention (40.9%, n = 299). Mask use was included in patient training by 80.2% (n = 588), and 77.6% (n = 567) believed that mask use helps prevent peritonitis. Significant regional differences were observed in reported mask-use practices (χ2 = 44.65, df = 8, p < 0.001). Mask use also varied according to PD program size (χ2 = 20.06, df = 6, p = 0.003). In addition, 39.6% (n = 290) reported that their facility followed specific guidance regarding mask use. Routine face mask use remains common in PD practice and is widely incorporated into patient training. Substantial regional and program-size variation was observed. Given the limited and uncertain evidence regarding the incremental benefit of routine mask use, these findings describe substantial variation in current practice and highlight the need for further evidence to clarify the role of face masks in PD infection prevention.

articles.title: Working with circular data: A tutorial for cognitive and behavioral research.
articles.abstract: Introductory statistics courses and conventional methods in behavioral and cognitive science are typically restricted to Euclidean space without explicitly stating this, leaving many researchers unaware of how to handle data with circular or periodic properties (e.g., time of day or orientation on a screen). This tutorial provides an accessible yet rigorous introduction, designed to bridge the gap between statistical theory and practical application. After discussing different ways of representing circular data mathematically and fundamental principles for working with them, we explain angular and vector representations and operations, including key considerations for implementing them in computer code. We then survey methods for visualizing circular data, including linear and polar plots and presentation of summary statistics. Next, we introduce circular measures of central tendency, dispersion, and shape: how they relate to their Euclidean counterparts and why they differ. Finally, we turn to more advanced topics of the kind needed to construct models of circular data. We introduce the most common circular distribution families, including circular analogs of the Gaussian distribution and their properties, as well as flexible distribution families that can describe skewed and heavy-tailed data. We survey common applications in the supplemental materials. The tutorial takes a method-oriented approach, not tied to specific software, but highlighting factors relevant to experimental design, data analysis, and statistical modeling. A consistent theme is the need to rigorously account for the periodicity of circular data. We also provide a consistent notation for circular statistics and parameters, addressing the lack of established conventions in the field. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Development of a machine learning-based risk warning model for potentially inappropriate medication use among older patients in a hematology service.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionOlder hematology patients often have multiple comorbidities and receive complex medication therapies; this can increase the risk of potentially inappropriate medication (PIM) use. A machine learning model could potentially serve as an automated screening and warning tool to facilitate the identification of PIM and support timely medication review in these patients. The aim of this study is to develop machine learning-based model that provide warnings regarding PIMs use in elderly patients hospitalized in the hematology service.MethodsThis retrospective pilot study was conducted on patients over 65 years of age who were admitted to the hematology service of a university hospital in Türkiye between 2018 and 2020. PIMs were determined according to the American Geriatrics Association's 2023 Beers Criteria. Python (v3.12.7) was used for data analysis in this study. The stratified 5-fold cross-validation method was used. To estimate PIM, seven different classification algorithms were used. Model performance was compared using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve, and area under the curve (AUC), brier score evaluation parameters.ResultsThis study included 190 patients. 45.8% of patients had PIM. The logistic regression model demonstrated the highest performance with 0.87 accuracy, 0.83 recall, 0.86 F1 score, and 0.91 AUC.ConclusionThe logistic regression model was determined to be the best-performing model. The developed patient-based automated screening model is promising and can be considered a reliable early warning mechanism for clinical pharmacists and physicians.

articles.title: Enhancing Patient Care and Efficiency in Gastroenterology Nursing Through Standardized Discharge Instructions.
articles.journal: Gastroenterology nursing : the official journal of the Society of Gastroenterology Nurses and Associates
articles.abstract: This quality improvement initiative at Hartford HealthCare Endoscopy Unit was designed to enhance both patient outcomes and operational efficiency by implementing standardized, procedure-specific discharge instructions. Standardized discharge instructions reduce complications, increase patient satisfaction, and decrease readmissions. The goal was to improve patient satisfaction metrics (Press Ganey overall satisfaction and instruction regarding recovery). To address inconsistencies in postprocedure care, the team employed the Plan-Do-Study-Act model to develop and implement structured discharge instruction documents. The instructions were reviewed for health literacy and translated into Spanish and Polish to ensure clear patient understanding. A key advancement was the seamless integration of these instructions into the electronic health record system via an interface between EndoWriter and the Epic electronic health record system, enabling patient access to personalized instructions through the MyChart portal. Preliminary outcomes demonstrated improvement across two measurement periods. The "Instructions Regarding Recovery" satisfaction score increased from 87.20% in calendar year 2022 to 89.17% in calendar year 2024 and similarly improved from 90.16% in calendar year 2024 to 92.64% in calendar year 2025. This initiative demonstrates the value of combining standardized, evidence-based, patient-centered education with electronic health record integration to improve postprocedure care, quality, and efficiency.

articles.title: Critical Care Diaries: A Promising Intervention to Mitigate the Consequences of Secondary Trauma From a PICU Stay?
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

articles.title: Amino Acid Profiles Distinguish Glycemic Phenotypes in Childhood and Predict 10-Year Risk of Dysglycemia in Young Adults: The BCAMS Study.
articles.abstract: Prospective evidence linking childhood amino acid (AA) dysregulation with future diabetes risk remains limited. We examined whether AA profiles distinguished childhood glycemic phenotypes and predicted dysglycemia risk in the Beijing Children and Adolescents Metabolic Syndrome (BCAMS) cohort. AA alterations were already detectable in children with normoglycemia and insulin resistance; six AAs were associated with 10-year dysglycemia risk, and their addition to clinical variables improved prediction. Ile showed the largest estimated indirect association with incident dysglycemia through follow-up insulin resistance; dietary Ile restriction in obese mice produced concordant metabolic changes, supporting AA profiling for early risk identification and Ile as a candidate modifiable target.

articles.title: [Idiopathic systemic capillary leak syndrome - a rare but serious differential diagnosis in the hypovolemic patient].
articles.abstract: Idiopathic systemic capillary leak syndrome (SCLS) is a rare, life-threatening cause of hypovolemic shock characterized by hemoconcentration, hypoalbuminemia, and acute hypovolemia due to plasma extravasation. It should be suspected in patients presenting with unexplained hypotension and markedly elevated hemoglobin levels, often following nonspecific prodromal symptoms such as malaise. Management is supportive and includes aggressive crystalloid resuscitation, vasopressor therapy, corticosteroids, and intravenous immunoglobulins. Owing to the risk of rapid hemodynamic deterioration and multi--organ failure, intensive care monitoring is essential. We report a previously healthy middle-aged man with recent upper respiratory tract infection and syncope who developed fulminant SCLS with refractory shock and died despite intensive care treatment.

articles.title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma.
articles.abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

articles.title: Effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative interventions for post-COVID-19 condition: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate supervised physical, psycho-logical, and alternative non-pharmacological interventions for improving patient-reported and objective functional outcomes in adults with post-COVID-19 condition.

DESIGN: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycInfo, and Scopus were searched from 1 January 2020 to 29 January 2026. Eligible studies were supervised, face-to-face trials evaluating physical, psychological, or alternative non-pharmacological interventions against usual care, placebo/sham, or active comparators in adults with World Health Organization defined post-COVID-19 condition. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2. Due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: 27 trials (1,998 participants) were included and evaluated physical, psychological, and alternative therapies. Supervised cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and multimodal exercise consistently improved cardiorespiratory fitness and walking capacity. Cognitive-behavioural therapy and lifestyle adjustments significantly reduced fatigue and subjective concentration complaints. Findings for neuromodulation, complementary, and oxygen therapies were heterogeneous, often showing no benefit over placebo. Only 18.5% of trials had low risk of bias, limited by small samples, unblinding, and short follow-ups.

CONCLUSION: Supervised physical rehabilitation and CBT show promising evidence for improving functional capacity and symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition. Larger trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm effectiveness and inform clinical guidelines.

articles.title: Clinical and functional outcomes of aquatic plyometrics in adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome: a dual-arm randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal management of adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome requires evidence-based interventions that maximize physical recovery without overloading the patellofemoral joint. This study investigated the efficacy of aquatic plyometric (Aquatic-Plyo) exercises on pain, muscle strength, and functional disability and health-related quality of life in this demographic.

DESIGN: A dual-arm randomized controlled trial.

SUBJECTS/PATIENTS: 56 adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome (age: 10-18 years).

METHODS: Adolescents were allocated to an experimental Aquatic-Plyo group or a control group performing conventional exercises. Both arms completed 45-min sessions twice weekly for 12 weeks. Pre- and post-treatment assessments included pain intensity, isokinetic knee (quadriceps and hamstrings) torque at 120°/s and 180°/s, functional disability, and health-related quality of life.

RESULTS: Mixed-model ANOVA confirmed the therapeutic dominance of the Aquatic-Plyo protocol. It yielded superior pain relief (p = 0.004, η2p = 0.14) and larger increases in quadriceps [120°/s (p = 0.006, η2p = 0.13); 180°/s (p = 0.008, η2p = 0.12)] and hamstring [120°/s (p = 0.007, η2p = 0.13); 180°/s (p = 0.023, η2p = 0.09)] peak torque. Moreover, the Aquatic-Plyo intervention drove greater reduction in functional disability (p = 0.03, η2p = 0.08) and notable enhancement in perceived health-related quality of life (p = 0.023, η2p = 0.09).

CONCLUSION: Aquatic-Plyo exercises effectively reduces pain and disability while improving muscle strength and health-related quality of life in adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome, making it a valuable addition to conservative rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Synergistic High-Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O-Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling.
articles.abstract: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration-induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high-entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O-doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal-support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mgPt - 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates COads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C-C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

articles.title: Antifungal ototoxicity, itraconazole, and approaches to its mitigation: a review of a sparse evidence base.
articles.journal: Xenobiotica; the fate of foreign compounds in biological systems
articles.abstract:
1. INTRODUCTION: Hearing loss is a recognised hazard of aminoglycosides and platinum chemotherapy, but the auditory risk of antifungal drugs has received far less attention. Itraconazole lists hearing loss in its prescribing information, yet dedicated peer-reviewed auditory studies appear absent.

2. AREAS COVERED: The original 139-record Web of Science (WoS) title-only corpus was retained to map the wider ototoxicity field. A targeted WoS Topic-field sensitivity search using antifungal-specific terms and broader auditory outcomes retrieved 153 records, of which 18 direct antifungal auditory safety/toxicity studies were retained. No dedicated auditory study of itraconazole was identified. The expanded evidence shows formulation- and route-dependent topical effects, a pharmacovigilance signal for oral terbinafine, no auditory brainstem response shift in a short-duration animal study of systemic voriconazole or caspofungin, and rare hearing-loss reports plus a pharmacovigilance signal for amphotericin B. Otoprotection evidence from other drug classes is considered for transferable mitigation principles.

3. EXPERT OPINION: The broader search shows a heterogeneous but sparse evidence base rather than an absence of evidence. Human systemic azole data remain particularly limited, and itraconazole lacks dedicated auditory investigation. Baseline and serial audiometry, separation of drug effects from infection and interacting medicines, and mechanistic studies are priorities.

articles.title: Bioinspired Active-Defense Coating with a Thermal Stability Relay for Mitigating Matrix Thermal Runaway Propagation.
articles.abstract: Inspired by the iron birch (Betula schmidtii), a biomimetic active-defense coating (IBMC) is engineered. Within a polymeric-aerogel matrix, rigid mica platelets mimic protective bark, while temperature-responsive sustained-release microspheres (SRMs) function as artificial cells. Upon thermal shock, SRM actively release repair agents to trigger a distinct thermal stability relay mechanism. Initially (<400 °C), the released amino-silicone oil induces rapid interfacial cross-linking to counteract polymer decomposition. Subsequently, at extreme temperatures (>800 °C), an amorphous inorganic skeleton reconfiguration occurs, where inorganic components mechanically interlock into a rigid, self-supporting scaffold, effectively propped open by hollow SRM derivatives acting as rigid spacers. This active-defense strategy effectively prevents the catastrophic structural collapse typical of conventional insulation. Consequently, the coating demonstrates exceptional dimensional stability, achieving a minimal radial shrinkage of only 5.7% at 1000 °C. By suppressing macro-cracks and thermal bridges, it retains an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.075 W/(m·K) and sustains a 197.7 °C thermal gradient. Ultimately, IBMC provides a compact and robust thermal management solution for mitigating thermal runaway across high-risk scenarios, including battery modules, steel structures, and datacenters.

articles.title: Clinical and genomic features of Chryseobacterium species isolated from clinical cultures.
articles.abstract: Chryseobacterium species are environmental bacteria occasionally implicated in human infections; however, their clinical and genomic features are not fully characterized. This study investigated the clinical, genotypic, and phenotypic characteristics of Chryseobacterium strains collected through the MultiDrug-Resistant Organisms Clinical Research Network, a multicenter prospective study of patients with carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacilli isolated at tertiary care hospitals in Japan between April 2019 and March 2024. Among 18 patients with Chryseobacterium spp. confirmed by whole-genome sequencing (WGS), 5 had infection, and 13 were colonized. Bacteremia and pneumonia were the common types of infection. The isolates comprised five species, with Chryseobacterium indologenes and Chryseobacterium culicis being the most frequently detected. Compared with WGS, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated the highest species-level identification accuracy (93.8%), followed by MALDI Biotyper (50.0%), VITEK-MS (31.3%), and VITEK 2 Blue (31.3%). All systems correctly identified C. indologenes, but other species were frequently misidentified or remained unidentified because of limited database coverage. All isolates exhibited broad β-lactam resistance, including resistance to carbapenems, which was associated with species-specific combinations of metallo-β-lactamase and extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes. Minocycline, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and cefiderocol retained activity across all species. These findings highlight that diverse Chryseobacterium species, including uncommon ones, can be associated with human infections. Incorporating genomic approaches such as WGS or 16S rRNA gene analysis can improve species-level identification, especially for rare or emerging species.IMPORTANCEChryseobacterium species are emerging opportunistic pathogens that pose a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge as they are intrinsically resistant to most β-lactams, including carbapenems, and are often misidentified by routine clinical laboratory systems. In this multicenter study, we show that clinical Chryseobacterium isolates represent greater species diversity than is typically recognized, extending beyond Chryseobacterium indologenes to include uncommon species associated with both infection and colonization. Whole-genome sequencing clarified species assignments, revealed species-specific β-lactamase profiles, and highlighted the limitations of commonly used identification platforms, particularly for species absent from commercial databases. Despite broad β-lactam resistance, cefiderocol, minocycline, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole retained in vitro activity across species. These findings emphasize the need for genomic or sequence-based identification to accurately define the clinical spectrum of Chryseobacterium species, guide interpretation of antimicrobial susceptibility, and improve recognition of these organisms as emerging healthcare-associated pathogens.

articles.title: Activity of manogepix and comparator antifungal agents against uncommon filamentous fungal isolates collected in a global surveillance program.
articles.abstract: Fosmanogepix (prodrug of manogepix) is a novel antifungal agent targeting the Gwt1 enzyme. This agent has activity against a diverse spectrum of fungal species, including species refractory to other antifungal classes or multidrug-resistant fungi. A total of 332 molds from a worldwide surveillance study were susceptibility tested for manogepix and comparator antifungal agents by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) reference broth microdilution method. Wild-type upper limit (WT-UL) values were determined for manogepix against organism groups using cumulative surveillance data. Isolates were collected from 20 countries, 41 hospitals, and 7 different infection sources. Eighteen genera were represented. Isolates included 208 non-fumigatus Aspergillus spp.; 37.3% (124 isolates) were non-Aspergillus molds.
