The manogepix minimum effective concentration (MEC50/90) was lower than the MIC50/90 for azole comparators or amphotericin B against all Aspergillus spp., Fusarium spp., Scedosporium spp., Lomentospora spp., Mucor spp., and Penicillium spp. Only Rhizopus spp. had higher MEC50/90 values for manogepix than the MIC50/90 values of the comparators. The WT-UL values reflected this, with the highest values for Rhizopus spp. at 16 mg/L and Mucor spp. at 4 mg/L, while they were ≤0.12 mg/L for all other organisms. Between 2023 and 2024, there were no organisms with MECs for manogepix above the WT-UL value. Manogepix displayed robust in vitro activity against contemporary non-Aspergillus fumigatus mold isolates. This agent was more potent than azole comparators or amphotericin B against most organism groups. Historically, less than 5% of isolates tested (n = 19) had MECs above the WT-UL cutoff values. These data support the continued development of manogepix for the treatment of mold infections.IMPORTANCEFosmanogepix (prodrug of manogepix) is a novel antifungal agent with a new mechanism of action and broad-spectrum activity, including against yeasts and molds. It is currently in two Phase 3 clinical trials for the treatment of invasive candidiasis and invasive mold infections and has previously been used for the treatment of Fusarium spp. infections during an outbreak. There are three main antifungal classes (echinocandins, azoles, and polyenes), but only azoles and amphotericin B have activity against non-Aspergillus molds; therefore, novel antifungal agents are urgently needed because invasive fungal infections have high morbidity and mortality rates. Here, we look at the in vitro activity of manogepix and comparator antifungal agents against non-Aspergillus fumigatus mold isolates collected from patient infections in 2023 and 2024. Manogepix showed potent in vitro activity against these organisms, with similar to or better activity than that of the comparators against most organism groups, and represents a promising potential future treatment option.

articles.title: Protein malnutrition facilitates intestinal colonization with highly resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae through disrupted intestinal microbial metabolism.
articles.abstract: Pediatric infections with highly resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (HR-Kp) disproportionately affect low-income countries where childhood malnutrition is prevalent. Malnutrition is an identified risk factor for infection with HR-Kp and other antimicrobial-resistant Enterobacterales, but the mechanistic underpinnings of this link and independence from other common exposures, like antibiotics, in children are unclear. Using a murine model of pediatric malnutrition, we found that mice fed a protein-deficient diet (PD) were more susceptible to colonization with HR-Kp at a 4-log lower challenge inoculum and developed a 3-log higher intestinal burden in comparison to adequately nourished mice. HR-Kp colonization in PD-fed mice persisted beyond 5 weeks, and colonization was transmitted to diet-matched cage mates. Antibiotic treatment resulted in similar HR-Kp colonization burdens regardless of diet, suggesting that nutrition-dependent colonization risk is driven by altered intestinal microbiota. Despite reduced dietary protein intake, intestinal amino acid content was maintained in PD-fed mice, supporting optimal HR-Kp growth. Furthermore, secondary bile acids, prototypic intestinal microbiota-derived molecules, were reduced in PD-fed mice, demonstrated an inverse correlation with HR-Kp burden in vivo, and partially inhibited the growth of HR-Kp in vitro. Collectively, these findings reveal a role for dietary protein intake in determining nutrition-dependent colonization resistance to HR-Kp.IMPORTANCEAntimicrobial-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae are responsible for a growing mortality burden worldwide, with disproportionate rates of infection in low-income countries where childhood malnutrition is prevalent. Several publications have demonstrated high rates of intestinal colonization with antimicrobial-resistant K. pneumoniae in children admitted with severe malnutrition in sub-Saharan Africa. However, numerous confounding risk factors in malnourished children (antibiotic use, healthcare exposure, and immune dysfunction) make it difficult to assess the direct impact of nutrition on K. pneumoniae colonization. In this study, we utilized a novel mouse model of protein malnutrition to demonstrate that dietary protein deficiency renders mice susceptible to a higher burden of intestinal colonization at a lower inoculating dose of K. pneumoniae. Furthermore, reduced microbiota-derived bile acid metabolites correlate with increased burden of colonization in protein-deficient mice. These results are the first to establish a direct mechanistic link associating dietary protein deficiency, bile acid metabolism, and intestinal colonization with antimicrobial-resistant K. pneumoniae.

articles.title: Silk Dressings Are More Cost Effective Than 2-Octyl Cyanoacrylate Mesh in Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Wound complications are costly after primary and revision total hip and knee arthroplasty (TJA). Mesh with 2-octyl cyanoacrylate can perform well but is associated with hypersensitivity and wound-healing complications. Silk dressings have shown fewer adverse events. We compared dressing costs, examining direct and complication-related expenses.

METHODS: An IRB-exempt cost-effectiveness analysis was conducted using published data on complication rates, including hypersensitivity reactions, delayed wound healing, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and application times. Direct material costs were calculated and annualized using the manufacturer's suggested retail prices (MSRPs) and bulk-purchase rates. Indirect costs were calculated for surgical costs per minute and treatment of wound complications and PJI.

RESULTS: Direct material costs were $387 (MSRP) or $79 (bulk pricing) for mesh dressings versus $120 (MSRP) or $60 (bulk pricing) for silk. When application times, differential rates of sensitivity reactions, and wound complications and their management are applied to national TJA rates, mesh costs markedly more than silk by $939/patient (MSRP) and $690/patient (bulk pricing) (MSRP: $1,090 versus $151/patient; $1.89 billion versus $2.62 million/annum; bulk pricing: $781 versus $91/patient; $1.36 billion versus $158 million/annum). Excluding PJI, which has a relationship that is several degrees away from dressing type, mesh was still more expensive than silk by $484/patient (MSRP) and $235/patient (bulk pricing) (MSRP: $634/patient versus $150; $1.1 billion versus $262 million/annum; bulk pricing: $326/patient versus $91; $566 million vs. $158 million/annum).

CONCLUSION: Silk dressings are more cost-effective than mesh dressings because of shorter application time, fewer complications, and lower pricing. For clinical and economic reasons, silk dressings should be considered for TJA.

articles.title: Real-world screening for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease among adults with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: New treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) require identification of patients at risk of progressing to cirrhosis, yet population-based screening methods are not well established.

METHODS: We conducted a pilot screening study at a large academic primary care practice among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We calculated FIB-4 scores on existing labs and contacted providers with recommendations for additional testing with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) and/or specialty referral.

RESULTS: Among 2773 patients with T2DM seen at our clinic during the study period meeting inclusion criteria, 2396 had sufficient data to calculate FIB-4. After excluding lab results from the emergency department or inpatient setting, this left a final sample of 1315 patients. Among the 1315 patients included in the study, 78 (5.9%) had FIB-4 scores >2.66, while 732 (55.7%) had FIB-4 scores between 1.3 and 2.66. The diagnostic yield (proportion of patients receiving definitive diagnosis of MASLD with F2 or higher fibrosis as a result of the intervention) among the cohort with FIB-4 > 2.66 was 12/78 (15.4%). The most common reason for fall-out was the patient not wishing to receive further evaluation, with the second being provider concerns about competing risks.

DISCUSSION: The impact of population-level MASLD screening is limited by implementation barriers. Future efforts should focus on direct-to-patient outreach and methods to identify patients without competing risks who are most likely to benefit from MASLD diagnosis and specific treatment.

articles.title: Assessing Medication Confounders Before Determination of Brain Death/Death by Neurologic Criteria: A Primer, with Opioids as a Worked Example.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide a primer on how clinicians, particularly pharmacists, can systematically assess whether a medication may confound determination of brain death/death by neurologic criteria (BD/DNC), using pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles that can be applied to any agent with the aid of tertiary references, and using opioids as a worked example.

SUMMARY: All major guidelines require exclusion of central nervous system (CNS) depressant effect before BD/DNC determination, yet none provides a general method for deciding when a given medication has cleared. Rather than cataloging every agent, this primer sets out the parameters that govern how long any drug can suppress the neurologic examination: lipophilicity and volume of distribution, elimination pathway and the effect of hepatic or renal dysfunction, active metabolites, and the context-sensitive half-life, which lengthens with the duration of an infusion and is not predicted by the elimination half-life. Special states, including obesity, hypothermia, extracorporeal support, and overdose, further prolong effect; in overdose, delayed absorption and saturable elimination can invalidate the customary five-half-life rule. Routine toxicology screens miss many relevant substances, including synthetic opioids. Opioids illustrate the framework across three common scenarios: exposure before arrival, continuous infusion, and overdose.

CONCLUSION: No validated serum concentration threshold defines clearance for most CNS depressants, and the safest determination rests on structured pharmacokinetic reasoning, toxicology consultation, and institutional protocols that specify how confounders are screened for and excluded, rather than on any single number or fixed waiting period.

articles.title: Amlodipine and Nifedipine Associations with B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Women with Hypertension and Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) are frequently prescribed to manage hypertension in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, whether individual dihydropyridine agents exert uniform class effects on myocardial wall stress remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study analyzed 465 consecutive patients with hypertension and HFpEF (354 women and 111 men) evaluated at Kumamoto Kinoh Hospital between May 2012 and July 2018. Multivariable linear regression models assessed associations between individual dihydropyridine CCBs (amlodipine vs. nifedipine) and plasma log-transformed B-type natriuretic peptide (lnBNP) levels.

RESULTS: In multiple imputation models among women, adjusted differences in lnBNP relative to no-CCB were 0.236 (95% CI, 0.031 to 0.441) for nifedipine and -0.118 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.037) for amlodipine. Direct linear contrasts in women confirmed lower lnBNP levels with amlodipine than with nifedipine (adjusted difference, -0.355; 95% CI, -0.562 to - 0.147). In men, the corresponding amlodipine-versus-nifedipine difference was -0.051 (95% CI, -0.697 to 0.595; P=0.876). The formal sex-by-drug interaction contrast in complete-case analysis yielded an adjusted difference of - 0.424 (95% CI, -1.055 to 0.208; P = 0.188), with male precision constrained by sample size (7 male nifedipine users).

CONCLUSION: In women with hypertension and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, amlodipine use was associated with lower adjusted ln(BNP) levels than nifedipine use. These observational findings challenge the assumption of an interchangeable dihydropyridine class effect on myocardial wall stress, suggesting that individual pharmacological profiles-rather than uniform class-level equivalence-warrant attention in clinical evaluations.

articles.title: Cardio-protection and monitoring for early phase clinical trials: Recommendations from the therapeutic advances in childhood leukemia and lymphoma (TACL) consortium.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many effective anti-cancer modalities potentially induce cardiotoxicity. Pediatric patients with relapsed/refractory hematologic malignancies are often excluded from anthracycline-containing regimens based on historical data showing population-level risk of heart failure after cumulative doses of anthracyclines without considering individual patient risk variability, modernized cumulative anthracycline equivalence ratios, novel anthracycline formulations, and use of supportive cardio-protectant medications. Additionally, standard guidelines are lacking for patients with a history of prior cardiotoxicity or previous anthracycline exposure.

METHODS: The Therapeutic Advances in Childhood Leukemia and Lymphoma (TACL) consortium convened a task force to review the relevant literature and create evidence-based cardiac eligibility recommendations for patients who enroll on TACL relapse clinical trials.

RESULTS: Recommendations for assessment of cardiotoxicity risk, cardiac monitoring, supportive care, management of cardiac dysfunction during therapy, and considerations for clinical trial design were created. Key guidance includes: 1) excluding potential subjects from therapies with cardiotoxic risk should be based on individual risk factors and real-time cardiac function assessments rather than past cardiotoxic exposures; 2) comprehensive subject-based cardiac monitoring before, during and after therapy is essential; 3) the liberal use of cardioprotective measures is encouraged; 4) uniform and evidence-based approaches for management of cardiac dysfunction during protocol therapy are crucial; 5) correlative cardiac aims should accompany protocols with potentially cardiotoxic therapies.

CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of these updated recommendations should allow more accurate and inclusive study eligibility criteria for TACL's clinical trials and inform future trial development while ultimately improving both quality and interpretability of study data, patient safety, treatment, and outcomes.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in rural India: a cross-sectional study in the APCAPS cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia poses a growing public health challenge in India. Despite this, epidemiological data on the condition remain largely restricted to adults >60 years of age, despite the convergence of urbanisation-driven cardiometabolic risks and socioeconomic disadvantage in rural India potentially accelerating dementia onset. We investigated the prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in a transitional rural Indian cohort of adults aged ≥45 years.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we utilised data from the Andhra Pradesh Children and Parents Study cohort from 29 villages near Hyderabad, South India (2021-2023). We collected sociodemographic, occupational, and household asset data through face-to-face, questionnaire-based interviews. Cardiometabolic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and stroke) were assessed using validated methods. Dementia screening was performed using the Brief Community Screening Instrument for Dementia. We calculated prevalence estimates for dementia and used multivariable logistic regression to identify independent associations of probable dementia with sociodemographic, socioeconomic (education, occupation, household assets), and cardiometabolic factors (diabetes, hypertension, cardiac disease, and stroke).

RESULTS: The final sample included 2,163 adults aged ≥45 years. The prevalence of probable dementia (a positive screen on the BCSI-D) was 3.4% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.6-4.6) in the 45-59 age group and 7.4% (95% CI = 6.0-9.4) in the ≥60 age group. In the multivariable model, the odds of probable dementia were 2.2 times higher among unemployed or retired participants than among those working in agriculture or animal rearing (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 2.23; 95% CI = 1.26-3.95). The odds of probable dementia among literate participants were 0.5 times those among illiterate participants (aOR = 0.54; 95% CI = 0.31-0.89). The odds of probable dementia were 3.8 times higher among participants with a history of stroke than among those without (aOR = 3.77; 95% CI = 1.67-7.94).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that the burden of probable dementia in rural India extends into middle age, and that the condition itself is independently associated with a history of stroke and socioeconomic disadvantages. This suggests a need to extend cognitive and vascular risk assessment to adults aged ≥45 years in rural India. However, as all findings reflect positive screening results rather than confirmed diagnoses, longitudinal studies with diagnostic confirmation are needed before population-level screening recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Evaluating COPD care assistance: a comparative study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE bot performance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to provide health information, yet their reliability in addressing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in the Chinese context remains unclear. To evaluate and compare the performance of three publicly available LLM chatbots - ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0 (OpenAI), and ERNIE Bot (Baidu) - in answering chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in China.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional comparative evaluation of three publicly available LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE Bot). We developed 40 COPD care questions spanning 7 prespecified domains relevant to patient education and self-management. All questions were submitted in Chinese in independent new chat sessions to minimise context carryover. Three consultant-level respiratory physicians independently rated each response for accuracy (1 = poor, 2 = borderline, 3 = good). We summarised accuracy as the sum of three ratings (range 3-9) and derived a majority-vote accuracy category. For responses rated 'good' by majority vote, physicians additionally rated comprehensiveness on a five-point scale. Information quality was further assessed using a modified DISCERN framework and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) understandability and actionability domains.

RESULTS: Most responses were rated as 'good' for accuracy across chatbots. ERNIE Bot achieved higher total accuracy scores than ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4.0, and a higher proportion of 'good' ratings in this Chinese-language evaluation. However, comprehensiveness scores for 'good' responses were low across all systems (mean ~ 1.4-2.0/5), and PEMAT actionability was limited, indicating that few responses included concrete, patient-executable steps.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that LLM chatbots may support basic COPD patient education in Chinese settings, but current responses often lack sufficient comprehensiveness and actionable guidance. These tools should not be used as standalone clinical advice and require appropriate safeguards and clinician oversight.

articles.title: Longitudinal Cardiac Damage Staging in Aortic Stenosis: The Need for Careful Validation.
Impact of prenatal pyrethroid pesticide exposure on neonatal lymphocyte subsets and apoptosis: a birth cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal pyrethroid pesticides (PYRs) exposure may elevate infection diseases susceptibility of children. However, it is unclear the relationship of PYRs exposure and neonatal immune function. We explored the association of PYRs exposure during three trimesters with neonatal immunity and the roles of lymphocyte apoptosis.

METHODS: Maternal urinary PYRs metabolites (3PBA, 4F3PBA, cis-DBCA) were measured in each trimester. Cord blood lymphocyte subsets and lymphocyte apoptosis rates were assessed by flow cytometry. Multivariate linear regression models were used to examine the associations of trimester-specific and repeated PYRs exposure during pregnancy with neonatal immune function.

RESULTS: High-level cis-DBCA exposure (>75th percentile, 0.78 μg/g) in the third trimester was negatively associated with cord blood CD3+ T cell counts (β = -0.06; 95% CI = -0.12, -0.01) and CD8+ T cell counts (β = -0.09; 95% CI = -0.16, -0.01). Repeated high-level cis-DBCA exposure across two or more trimesters was associated with reduced CD3+ T cell counts (β = -0.09; 95% CI = -0.16, -0.02), CD4+ T cell counts (β = -0.13; 95% CI = -0.22, -0.04), CD8+ T cell counts (β = -0.13; 95% CI = -0.22, -0.04), B cell counts (β = -0.10; 95% CI = -0.20, -0.01), and NK cell counts (β = -0.14; 95% CI = -0.25, -0.03). High-level 3PBA exposure in the first trimester (β = 0.11; 95% CI = 0.01, 0.22) and high-level cis-DBCA exposure in the second trimester (β = 0.16; 95% CI = 0.04, 0.28) were positively associated with cord blood lymphocyte apoptosis rates. Repeated high-level cis-DBCA exposure in two or more trimesters was associated with increased cord blood lymphocyte apoptosis rates (β = 0.19; 95% CI = 0.03, 0.35).

CONCLUSIONS: High-level maternal PYRs exposure during pregnancy may reduce neonatal lymphocyte counts and increase lymphocyte apoptosis. These effects persist throughout gestation, with the third trimester may represent a sensitive window for adverse effects on immune development.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Shear Wave Velocity Throughout the Cardiac Cycle in Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension.
Large-scale plasma proteomic profiling enhances prediction of heart failure among hypertensive individuals: prospective insights from the UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for heart failure (HF), but current clinical models have limited ability to identify high-risk individuals before overt disease. Plasma proteomics may capture early molecular changes and improve risk prediction.

METHODS: We analysed 16,128 hypertensive UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants without baseline HF. Plasma levels of 2,911 proteins were measured using the Olink Explore platform. Participants were randomly split 1:1 into training and validation sets. HF-associated proteins were identified using Cox models in the training set, followed by LASSO regression to construct a protein risk score (PRS). Model performance was assessed in the validation set using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent ROC analysis, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI), calibration, and bootstrap validation. A parsimonious panel was derived using LightGBM and sequential forward feature selection.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.1 years, 1,074 participants developed HF. In the training set, 534 proteins were associated with HF after adjustment for demographic and clinical risk factors and were enriched in cytokine signalling, extracellular matrix organisation, and immune-cell migration pathways. The 101-protein PRS was independently associated with incident HF. In the validation set, adding the PRS increased the C-index from 0.670 to 0.786 beyond age and sex, and from 0.727 to 0.787 beyond the Pooled Cohort Equations to Prevent Heart Failure (PCP-HF) model, with improved reclassification and discrimination. PRS levels were elevated years before HF diagnosis. A six-protein panel comprising NT-proBNP, GDF15, BCAN, WFDC2, CTHRC1, and CNTN5 achieved an AUC of 0.775, outperforming NT-proBNP alone.

CONCLUSIONS: Plasma proteomic profiling improves HF risk prediction among hypertensive individuals beyond conventional clinical factors and may support earlier risk stratification and precision prevention.

articles.title: Maximising the prognostic value of non-contrast cardiac CT.
Cost-effectiveness of monotherapy and combination therapy for myopia control in Chinese children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myopia poses a major public health and economic burden in China, necessitating cost-effectiveness evaluations of control strategies. We aimed to assess cost-effectiveness of single/combined myopia control in children and adolescents to optimise strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of myopia control interventions in Chinese children (aged 6-18 years). Annual changes in axial length (AL) and spherical equivalent refraction (SER) were the primary outcomes. Additionally, we used a decision-analytic Markov model with clinical and cost data from China to evaluate 16 myopia control strategies for eight-year-old children over eight years from a patient perspective, with 3% discounting. Strategies included monotherapies and combined therapies. Main outcomes were incremental cost per unit reduction in myopic shift (i.e. SER) or AL elongation, compared with single-vision lenses (SVLs). Markov cohort analysis simulated the proportion of individuals progressing to high myopia under various strategies. We assessed robustness through deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses. We performed subgroup analyses by onset age (6, 10, and 12 years) and regional economic development.

RESULTS: For SER reduction, outdoor activity was cost-effective (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio = USD -18.29/dioptre (D)). At higher willingness-to-pay thresholds, 0.01% atropine combined with defocus incorporated multiple segment (DIMS) (USD 660.74/D) and repeated low-level red-light therapy (RLRL) (USD 895.36/D) were cost-effective. For AL reduction, outdoor activity (USD -42.68/mm) and DIMS (USD 672.73/mm) were cost-effective at lower thresholds, while RLRL (USD 2011.32/mm) was preferred at higher thresholds. Compared with monotherapy, combination interventions improved preventive efficacy against high myopia. Subgroup analyses confirmed that the cost-effectiveness ranking was preserved across onset ages and regional economic settings.

CONCLUSIONS: Under limited budget conditions, outdoor activities and defocus spectacles represent advantageous cost-effective treatment options. When the budget is sufficient, RLRL may be considered a promising option pending confirmation of its long-term safety and effectiveness, and 0.01% atropine combined with DIMS is the preferred cost-effective option. Our analysis provides evidence-based guidance for clinicians and families in selecting effective myopia control strategies.

articles.title: Feeding, Fear, and Acceptance: Caregivers' Experiences of Nutritional Support During Childhood Cancer Treatment.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore caregivers' experiences and perceptions of the nutritional challenges faced by children and adolescents undergoing cancer treatment, including oral intake and the use of nutritional support.

METHODS: This was a qualitative study based on focus groups with parents and caregivers at a Brazilian pediatric oncology hospital. Eight groups were conducted with 44 caregivers, and the seven available transcripts, corresponding to 38 caregivers, were analyzed with computer-assisted lexical analysis, interpreted as themes and illustrated with representative quotes, together with an exploratory affective analysis.

RESULTS: The accounts spanned two domains, oral feeding and nutritional support, and six themes: altered oral feeding and food preferences, food hygiene and safety, gastrointestinal symptoms, oral nutritional supplements, nasoenteral tube feeding from fear to acceptance, and weight loss, fear, and coping. Caregivers described food selectivity and a shift toward ultra-processed foods, strict hygiene routines driven by fear of infection, and difficulty accepting supplements and the tube. Families who had used tube feeding described it as essential and reported learning to manage it. Negative emotions predominated in the exploratory affective profile, with sadness and fear the most frequent and trust also prominent.

CONCLUSION: The nutritional experience of caregivers during pediatric cancer treatment was shaped by fear and by a gradual acceptance of nutritional support. Supportive care should address caregivers' fears early and help families move to acceptance of oral supplements and tube feeding.

articles.title: Facet-Programmed Oxide Nanointerfaces for Metabolite Activation and AI-Assisted Disease Screening.
articles.abstract: Metal oxides are important nanocatalytic materials for small-molecule activation, owing to their variable valence states and efficient charge-transfer capabilities. This activation is governed by coupled oxide-molecule interfacial processes, for which conventional descriptors such as morphology, composition, and defects remain insufficiently precise. Here, we establish crystal facets as descriptors for oxide surface regulation and use laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) as a high-throughput readout of metabolite activation. Across CeO2, Co3O4, and Cu2O, exposed facets strongly regulate metabolite desorption/ionization, with the (110) facet consistently exhibiting superior activity. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory calculations reveal that facet exposure modulates surface valence states, oxygen-vacancy formation, charge transfer, carrier dynamics, and energy dissipation. In particular, (110) CeO2 integrates favorable defect structures, low work function, efficient charge separation, and localized energy confinement, enabling enhanced metabolite activation with up to three orders of magnitude signal improvement, high reproducibility, and salt/protein tolerance. The optimized (110) CeO2 matrix enables serum metabolic fingerprinting for AI-assisted discrimination of hepatocellular carcinoma from chronic liver disease and biomarker identification. This work demonstrates facet engineering as a strategy for designing oxide nanointerfaces that translate molecular activation into chemically informative fingerprints for disease screening.

articles.title: Regular Testing to Enhance Learning Outcomes in Macroscopic Anatomy in Dental Education.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anatomy education is fundamental to competent and reliable dental practice, yet effective strategies to enhance learning and long-term retention remain debated. Regular formative assessment may support learning through several mechanisms, including retrieval practice, repeated exposure to course content, and more distributed studying, but its impact in oral macroscopic anatomy education remains insufficiently explored.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study compared four cohorts of second-year dental students at the University of Oslo (N = 205). Two cohorts received the standard teaching without interim assessments (no-regular-testing group; n = 101), while two cohorts received the same teaching and additionally completed three mandatory formative assessments during a 6-week anatomy module (regular-testing group; n = 104). All students completed an identical 150-task test immediately after the teaching period and a cumulative practical examination four weeks later. Performance across anatomical domains was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: The regular-testing group demonstrated significantly higher performance on the 150-task post-teaching test across all domains (overall score: 71.8% vs. 53.6%, p < 0.001), with the largest gains observed in myology and neurology. At the final examination 4 weeks later, descriptive performance remained generally higher in the regular-testing group across most tasks and anatomical domains, although the substantial initial performance advantage had diminished.

CONCLUSION: Regular formative assessment was associated with substantially improved short-term performance in dental anatomy education. Although the initial advantage diminished over time, mean performance remained generally higher in the regular-testing group at the final examination. These findings support regular formative assessment as a potentially valuable component of anatomy education, while the contribution of retrieval practice cannot be separated from other mechanisms associated with repeated mandatory assessment.

articles.title: Characterisation of musculoskeletal health problems encountered following critical illness and their relationship with physical function: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Poor musculoskeletal (MSK) health is common following critical illness, negatively impacting quality of life. Holistic MSK assessment of critical care survivors has not previously been undertaken. The aim was to characterise MSK problems following critical illness and explore disability in patients with poor MSK health.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A holistic MSK assessment was undertaken in participants six months after admission to intensive care. Participants with poor MSK health underwent an exploratory, functional assessment mirroring the domains of the International Classification of Functioning Disability and Health framework (ICF).

RESULTS: Sixty-one participants underwent MSK assessment and 11 the functional assessment. Multisite problems (n = 33, 54.1%) and high levels of fear-avoidance related to physical activity (n = 15, 24.6%) were common. MSK health correlated with pain (p = 0.008), strength (p = 0.002), and fear-avoidance beliefs related to physical activity and work (p < 0.001). Participants with upper limb problems had high levels of disability with mean QuickDASH scores of 48.14 (SD24.49). Participants were sedentary for a median (IQR) of 21.7 h (20.5-22.1) per day.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants had high pain levels and experienced problems across all ICF domains. These results highlight an urgent need for research into targeted rehabilitation interventions to improve MSK health following critical illness.

articles.title: Modified non-transarticular K-wire external fixation versus traditional transarticular pinning for bony mallet finger: a prospective comparative cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of plastic surgery and hand surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional transarticular distal interphalangeal joint (DIPJ) pinning for bony mallet fingers risks stiffness and iatrogenic cartilage injury. This study compared a modified non-transarticular K-wire external fixator with traditional transarticular pinning for surgically treated bony mallet finger.

METHODS: This single-center prospective nonrandomized comparative cohort study included 120 adults with acute bony mallet finger. Sixty patients underwent traditional transarticular DIPJ pinning, and 60 underwent modified non-transarticular K-wire external fixation. The primary outcome was overall postoperative complications, including pin tract infection, joint stiffness, loss of reduction, nail deformity, or radiographic degenerative change assessed at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included operative time, hardware removal time, bone union time, DIPJ motion, Crawford grade, pain, QuickDASH score, and return-to-work time. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of overall complications.

RESULTS: Baseline demographic and injury characteristics were comparable between groups. Overall complications were significantly less frequent after modified fixation than after traditional fixation (15.0% vs 48.3%, p < 0.001). The modified technique markedly reduced joint stiffness and nail deformity. It was also associated with shorter operative time, earlier hardware removal, faster bone union, lower extension lag, greater maximum DIPJ flexion, better Crawford grade distribution, lower pain and QuickDASH scores, and earlier return to work. In multivariable analysis, traditional fixation remained independently associated with higher complication risk.

CONCLUSION: Modified non-transarticular K-wire external fixation was associated with fewer complications and better early functional recovery than traditional transarticular DIPJ pinning. This joint-sparing, low-cost technique may be a useful surgical option for selected patients with bony mallet finger.

articles.title: The effectiveness of meaning-based interventions in reducing suicide-related vulnerability: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Existential factors such as loss of meaning play a central role in suicide-related vulnerability, yet most prevention interventions target symptom reduction. We aimed to systematically review the effects of meaning-based interventions on suicide-related outcomes and characterize the mechanisms through which these effects operate.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Six databases (PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Research Information Sharing Service, and Korean Studies Information Service System) were searched from inception to April 2026. Studies were included if they evaluated meaning-based interventions and reported suicide-related outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials and RoBANS for nonrandomized studies. Given heterogeneity across populations, interventions, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively by domain.

RESULTS: Ten studies were included (7 randomized controlled trials, 2 quasi-experimental studies, and 1 secondary analysis). Meaning-based interventions most consistently improved existential outcomes, including meaning in life, spiritual well-being, and quality of life. Emotional outcomes showed partial and heterogeneous effects. Suicide-related outcomes, including hopelessness, demoralization, and suicidal ideation, generally showed reductions, although effects varied across studies. Mechanistically, most studies showed patterns of indirect pathways, whereby improvements in existential variables co-occurred with reductions in emotional and suicide-related outcomes.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: Meaning-based interventions may reduce suicide-related vulnerability primarily by enhancing existential resources rather than directly targeting symptoms. These findings support integrating meaning-centered approaches into suicide prevention strategies and highlight the need for longitudinal and mediation-based studies to examine causal mechanisms.

articles.title: Engineering nanozymes with robust chemiluminescence activity for rapid and quantitative detection of Epstein-Barr virus nucleic acids.
articles.abstract: The strong correlation between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection and diseases has been well established. However, there is still a lack of convenient methods for quantitative detection of EBV DNA. Here, we synthesize an iron-based single-atom nanozyme (MFePH) with high chemiluminescence activity and integrate it with recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) and Fe3O4-based magnetic separation for the sensitive and noninvasive detection of EBV DNA. Specifically, MFePH is synthesized by first coordinating histidine axially to the iron-porphyrin, thereby simulating the structure-activity relationship of the active site in natural peroxidase, followed by its integration into a Zn-based metal-organic framework. MFePH demonstrates comparable chemiluminescence activity to that of natural peroxidase. In the RPA reaction, EBV DNA is amplified using a primer pair labelled with biotin and digoxin. The amplified products are enriched via anti-digoxin antibody-labelled magnetic Fe3O4. Concurrently, the streptavidin-labelled MFePH is responsible for signal amplification. This detection system accurately detects as low as 100 copies per mL of EBV DNA within 25 min, which is much shorter than the 2-3 h required by traditional qPCR (quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction). Consequently, this study provides a convenient strategy for EBV DNA detection, which is expected to markedly facilitate early screening for EBV-associated diseases.

articles.title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

articles.title: Sexual Health in Heart Failure: How Age, Sex, and Dyspnea Interact to Shape Intimacy and Unmet Clinical Needs.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sexual health is a cornerstone of well-being among the least explored aspects of heart failure (HF) care. Guidelines offer minimal, male-focused recommendations, leaving female sexual health underaddressed. The ROMANT'IC study investigated how HF affects intimacy and sexuality across sex, age and symptom burden.

METHODS AND RESULTS: ROMANT'IC was a national descriptive questionnaire study including1,398 patients with HF (921 men, 477 women; age 18-93 years). Overall, 655 (46.9%) provided detailed responses:491 (53.3%) men, 164 (34.4%) women indicating a reluctance to disclose information on sexuality (p<0.001). 57.8% men, and 53.7% women reported no sexual activity in the previous three months. Sexual inactivity varied significantly across age groups (χ2=17.02, p=0.001): 52.9% at 18-40 years, 50.0% at 41-55 years, 48.3% at 56-65 years, and 65.5% at ≥66 years and increased markedly with dyspnea severity: 47.8% at Grade 1, 50.3% at Grade 2, and 79.0% at Grades 3-4 (χ2=40.96, p<0.001). Men reported erectile dysfunction (49.0%) and treatment side effects (39.5%); women reported loss of desire (65.4%), reduced sense of seductiveness (61.5%), and depression (42.3%). Severe dyspnea independently predicted sexual inactivity (OR=3.88 [2.26-6.64], p<0.001), whereas sex and age were not significant after adjustment. Overall, 72-80% had never discussed sexuality with their cardiologist, regardless of dyspnea severity or age.

CONCLUSION: HF profoundly alters sexuality. Dyspnea severity is the dominant independent driver of sexual inactivity and represents a potentially modifiable therapeutic target. These findings call for systematic, gender- and age-sensitive, dyspnea-graded sexual counselling in routine HF care.

articles.title: MR-MAS: An End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
articles.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Understanding disease-related causal mechanisms is essential for biomedical research, yet the practical use of Mendelian Randomization (MR) remains constrained by fragmented analytical workflows and a strong dependence on specialized expertise. These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses.

RESULTS: We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. Additional evaluations showed robust trait retrieval and improved code-repair performance with MRKB guidance. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS, with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

articles.title: Physical and psychological pathways associated with cognitive recovery following Baduanjin exercise combined with digital cognitive training in older adults with atrial fibrillation: A secondary mediation analysis of a randomized controlled trial.

Vinegar polyphenol extract alleviates alcohol-induced liver injury through suppressing the hepatic MAPK signaling pathway and restoring gut microbiota homeostasis and short-chain fatty acid generation in male mice.
articles.abstract: Traditional brewed vinegar is rich in polyphenolic compounds that exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective activities. However, the protective mechanisms of vinegar polyphenol extract (VE) against alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) involving gut homeostasis remain unclear. The phenolic composition of VE was characterized using UPLC-QTrap-MS/MS. Its hepatoprotective mechanisms in alcohol-treated mice were investigated through hepatic transcriptomic profiling and identification of key signaling pathways. Additionally, whether the hepatoprotective effects of VE were dependent on the gut microbiota were explored via antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion and fecal microbiota transplantation. Twenty phenolic compounds were identified in VE, and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid was the predominant component accounting for 46.67%. VE administration at 750 mg kg-1 significantly reduced serum ALT and AST levels, attenuated hepatic oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressed alcohol-induced phosphorylation of p38, JNK, and ERK1/2. Meanwhile, VE restored the integrity of the intestinal barrier and reduced the LPS burden. Moreover, VE remodeled the gut microbiota by upregulating Akkermansia and Bacteroides and reducing Escherichia, which was accompanied by restoration of SCFA generation, notably acetic acid and propionic acid. Microbiota depletion weakened the protective effects of VE, whereas fecal microbiota transplantation restored its hepatoprotective activity. These findings suggest that VE alleviates alcohol-associated liver disease by suppressing the hepatic MAPK signaling pathway and restoring intestinal homeostasis. VE is a promising food-derived functional ingredient for the prevention of ALD.

articles.title: Association between waist-to-height-haemoglobin A1c index and subclinical myocardial injury in individuals with and without hypertension.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Recently, a novel metabolic indicator, the Waist-to-Height-Haemoglobin A1c (WHH) index, has been shown to be associated with diabetes risk. This study investigated the association of WHH with the Cardiac Infarction/Injury Score (CIIS) and the risk of subclinical myocardial injury (SC-MI), stratified by hypertension status.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 5,597 adults aged ≥40 years from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey who were free of CVD. The WHH index was calculated as waist circumference/height × HbA1c. SC-MI was defined as a CIIS ≥10 on a 12-lead electrocardiogram. Using weighted generalised linear and logistic regression models, we examined the associations of WHH with CIIS and SC-MI. Nonlinear relationships were assessed using restricted cubic spline (RCS) models.

RESULTS: The WHH index was not associated with SC-MI among adults without hypertension (odds ratio [OR], 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73-1.24 per SD increase), but was positively associated among adults with hypertension (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.08-1.72; Pinteraction = 0.007). For the CIIS, each 1-SD higher WHH index was positively associated only among those with hypertension (β = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.12 to 1.63; Pinteraction = 0.020). RCS analysis confirmed a linear relationship between WHH and SC-MI risk among individuals with hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate a significant association between the WHH index and subclinical myocardial injury, particularly among adults with hypertension.

articles.title: Intravascular imaging improves outcomes in left main PCI: insights from acute and chronic presentations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an established revascularization strategy for selected patients with left main coronary artery (LMCA) disease. However, data regarding outcomes in unselected real-world populations and the impact of intravascular imaging remain limited. We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes following LMCA PCI according to clinical presentation and to assess the prognostic impact of intravascular imaging guidance.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre study including consecutive patients undergoing LMCA PCI between 2019 and 2022. Patients were classified as having chronic (CCS) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were assessed during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression and stabilised inverse probability of treatment weighting (SIPTW) analyses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 107 patients were included (19 CCS and 88 ACS; mean age 68.6 ± 11.3 years; 80.4% male). During a mean follow-up of 1121 ± 574 days, ACS patients experienced higher rates of MACCE (40.9% vs. 15.8%; p = 0.039) and all-cause mortality (29.5% vs. 5.3%; p = 0.027) compared with CCS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower risk of MACCE in multivariable analysis (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.75; p = 0.009). In a SIPTW-adjusted analysis, the association remained directionally favourable, although statistical significance was not maintained (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.26-1.29; p = 0.178).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical presentation significantly influences outcomes after LMCA PCI, with worse long-term prognosis among ACS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with lower rates of MACCE and remained directionally favourable after weighting analyses, supporting its role in optimising LMCA interventions.

articles.title: Partial Red Cell Exchange in the Secondary Prevention of Stroke in Sickle Cell Disease: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a severe complication associated with sickle cell disease (SCD). The risk of recurrence is extremely high. The present study aimed to assess the clinical and biological efficacy of Partial Red Cell Exchange (PRE) in secondary stroke prevention among a cohort of Tunisian patients with SCD.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a prospective study over a 15-year period (January 1, 2010-December 31, 2024). A total of 29 patients with sickle cell syndromes complicated by one or more strokes were enrolled. They underwent 1732 PRE.

RESULTS: The median age was 99 months (75-133). The median follow-up duration was 78 months (49-126). The mean HbS decreased from 40.1% ± 14.1% to 21.1% ± 11.1% post-exchange (p < 0.0001). Treatment failure was observed in 8 of 29 patients (27.5%), with a total of 12 neurological events over a cumulative treatment duration of 1570 months. 11 of 12 recurrences (91.7%) occurred within the first 4 years of the exchange program. The presence of moyamoya vasculopathy was predictive of therapeutic failure.

CONCLUSIONS: PRE remains an effective modality for secondary stroke prevention in patients with sickle cell disease. Stroke recurrences occur predominantly within the first 4 years of treatment and are more frequent in the context of severe cerebrovascular disease.

articles.title: Pandemic-Responsive Molecularly Imprinted Polymer-Based Electrochemical Sensor for Mpox Detection.
articles.abstract: In 2022, a global Mpox outbreak occurred, and the World Health Organization (WHO) declared it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Although the outbreak was quickly constrained, new cases of infection associated with mutated virions continue to be documented worldwide. In recent global health crises, there is an urgent need to develop rapid, cost-effective diagnostic assays. While nucleic acid assays (e.g., PCR and CRISPR-based methods) represent the current gold standard for Mpox virus (MPXV) detection, point-of-care (POC) assays for Mpox remain limited. Here, we developed a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)-based MPXV sensor targeting A29L, a surface protein involved in host cell binding. The MIP sensor exhibits a remarkable detection limit of 7.7 pg/mL (0.54 pM). Moreover, we demonstrated that the MIP sensor detected A29L in artificial interstitial fluid (AIF) with a detection limit of 12.4 pg/mL (0.86 pM), supporting sensitive detection in a lesion-relevant model matrix. The MIP sensor preferentially responded to A29L over MPXV B6R, vaccinia virus A27L, and biointerferents and retained its response after 30 days. The results indicate that the MIP-based MPXV sensor has strong potential for clinical Mpox detection and could serve as a valuable diagnostic platform in future pandemics.

articles.title: Peptide profiling of casein peptide reveals its anti-diabetic effects via DPP-IV inhibition and IRS1/PI3K/AKT signaling.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a growing global health burden, increasing demand for safe food-derived strategies for glycemic control. Casein-derived peptides have potential metabolic benefits, but their antidiabetic mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, casein peptide (CNP), enriched in low-molecular-weight peptides (<3 kDa), was investigated as the principal bioactive intervention for T2DM regulation. LC-MS/MS identified 880 peptides; among the 50 most abundant, all were predicted to inhibit DPP-IV, 26 to inhibit α-glucosidase, and one to inhibit α-amylase. CNP inhibited DPP-IV in vitro in a concentration-dependent manner (IC50 = 5.06 ± 0.41 mg mL-1) and crossed Caco-2 monolayers partly through endocytosis and PepT1-mediated transport. In HFD/STZ-induced T2DM mice, CNP improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, ameliorated dyslipidemia, attenuated tissue injury and systemic inflammation, and restored GLP-1/DPP-IV balance and IRS1/PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings identify CNP as a key food-derived bioactive peptide system that modulates T2DM through complementary effects on intestinal transport, incretin regulation, glucose-lipid homeostasis, inflammation, and insulin signaling, supporting its potential for development as a functional food ingredient for T2DM management.

articles.title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis.

RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21]; P=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

articles.title: Life-Course Blood Pressure Trajectories and Focal Myocardial Fibrosis in Older Age in MyoFit46.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of life-course blood pressure (BP) trajectories on later-life focal left ventricular (LV) fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) remains elusive.

METHODS: MyoFit46 prospectively recruited ≈500 participants from a 1946 birth cohort for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan at 77 years, assessing LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method or 5-SD method. Systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP were recorded at 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years. For each participant, annual rates of BP change (steepness) and area under the BP trajectory (cumulative burden) for each age interval were calculated using mixed-effects models. Associations between life-course BPs and LGE were tested using generalized linear models, adjusted for antihypertensives, demographics, lifestyle, and comorbidities. Time-to-event associations between LGE and incident major adverse cardiovascular event (hospitalizations for coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and atrial/ventricular arrhythmias; n=29) were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 472 participants (54% male), each 10 mm Hg greater individual SBPs at 36 to 69 years were associated with 6% to 11% greater LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method (all P≤0.033), whereas each 10 mm Hg sustained greater SBPs on any age interval from 36 to 69 associated with 16% to 24% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77(all P≤0.005), independent of SBP at 77 years. Each 1 mm Hg/y steeper SBP rise during age intervals 36 to 43, 43 to 53, and 53 to 63 was associated with 6% to 12% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77 years. LGE presence was associated with greater major adverse cardiovascular event rates (hazard ratio, 2.5 [95% CI, 1.2-5.2]).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher life-course BPs, cumulative burden, and steeper increases were associated with greater older-age LV LGE, which was linked to incident major adverse cardiovascular events. BP trajectories, beyond single-point BP measurements, warrant further investigation as tools to guide BP management strategies.

articles.title: Pyrophosphatase 2 Deficiency: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis and Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPA2 (pyrophosphatase 2) deficiency is a relatively newly recognized condition caused by biallelic variants in the PPA2 gene. The gene encodes the mitochondrial enzyme PPA2, involved in the production of orthophosphate in the mitochondrial matrix. Affected individuals typically present with sudden cardiac death or acute heart failure following common viral illnesses in infants and toddlers, or following exposure to small amounts of alcohol as teenagers. The condition has a high mortality rate in these situations. Here, we explore the clinical presentations and current management of these patients with a view to guiding future emergency clinical management of cases.

METHODS: Case records from published and unpublished affected individuals diagnosed with PPA2 deficiency were compiled in a retrospective cohort study of genotypes, phenotypes and clinical management protocols in individuals with biallelic (likely) pathogenic PPA2 variants.

RESULTS: We collated 93 affected individuals from 53 families, 14 of which have not previously been reported. Patient presentation is invariably acute, often associated with fatigue, vomiting, seizures and collapse. Generally, presenting individuals received standard emergency management with cardiopulmonary resuscitation and appropriate management of arrhythmia, and here we present compiled clinical management protocols for emergency and ongoing treatment of PPA2-deficient patients. A pronounced inheritance rate of pathogenic alleles from carrier parents is noted, and further research is warranted to confirm and investigate any selective advantage for gametes carrying pathogenic PPA2 variants.

CONCLUSIONS: PPA2 deficiency has a high mortality rate following exposure to common childhood viruses in children around and under the age of 3 and in teenagers exposed to ethanol. We have presented current therapeutic approaches gathered from a worldwide survey of clinicians treating their patients, possible pathogenic mechanisms and inheritance peculiarities of the condition and provide a comprehensive review of the current recommendations surrounding patients' clinical management.

articles.title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke.
authors: De Los Rios La Rosa F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of stroke is unequally distributed in the United States, with Black individuals experiencing more incident stroke. It remains unclear whether Black individuals also experience worse stroke recovery. We sought to study disparities in longitudinal functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke in a population-based study.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky region over an 18-month period (July 2019 to December 2020). All acute ischemic stroke events were captured. The modified Rankin Scale scores were determined at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months for patients who survived the index event. We studied the association between Black race and longitudinal modified Rankin Scale (across all time points) with mixed-effects ordinal regression, initially adjusting for age, sex, and time since stroke. Hierarchical regression was used to sequentially adjust for stroke severity and management, premorbid health, and social determinants.

RESULTS: Among 2796 patients with acute ischemic stroke (mean age, 69.0; 31% Black; 52% female), 2537 survived and were included (mean age, 68.4; 32% Black; 52% female). Black race was associated with a worse longitudinal modified Rankin Scale score (cOR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89-3.60]). Excluding patients with recurrent events did not change this association (cOR, 2.69 [95% CI, 1.92-3.78]). Adding variables reflecting initial stroke severity and management partly attenuated the association (cOR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.43-2.60]). Adding variables reflecting premorbid health further attenuated the association (cOR decreased to 1.43 [95% CI, 1.09-1.87]). The remaining association between Black race and the modified Rankin Scale score was fully attenuated by social determinants, with cOR, 1.09 (95% CI, 0.80-1.47). There was no interaction between race and time since stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Starting at discharge and persisting out to 12 months, acute ischemic stroke functional outcomes are worse among Black individuals. These disparities are significantly attenuated by clinical factors and social determinants; future studies should explore whether the social determinants can be intervened upon in the recovery period.

articles.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
articles.abstract: Rapid, portable detection of multiple nucleic acid targets is essential for infectious disease surveillance and precision oncology. CRISPR-based diagnostics have set a high bar for sensitivity and single-base specificity, yet their reliance on collateral nuclease activity complicates multiplexing, integration with amplification, and point-of-care deployment. Here, we present TIMBER (templated incision mediated by endonucleases of repair), a non-CRISPR platform that achieves comparable performance without nonspecific nuclease activity. TIMBER uses a repair endonuclease to cleave probes containing abasic sites only when they are hybridized to a matched target. The system exhibits strong specificity, enabling single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination. TIMBER provides an analytical limit of detection of 12 pM without preamplification or one copy per μL (1.6 aM) with preamplification through RT-PCR or RT-LAMP, with results observable by visual fluorescence or on lateral flow. We deploy TIMBER to detect SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and further demonstrate multiplex detection of four targets, enabling identification of EGFR mutations in lung cancer samples. This approach offers a flexible, rapid, and low-instrument-ready solution for diverse nucleic acid diagnostics, from viral detection to cancer genotyping.

articles.title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED.

METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days.

RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Genetic Counseling Is Associated With Improved Patient-Reported Outcomes Across Clinical Indications and Settings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary guidelines recommend genetic counseling for potentially inherited cardiomyopathies, channelopathies, aortopathies, and dyslipidemias, but few small studies characterize cardiovascular genetic counseling (CVGC) outcomes, impeding efforts to improve CVGC service delivery. We aimed to (1) quantify psychosocial CVGC outcomes, (2) identify clinical, demographic, and service delivery characteristics associated with the extent of benefit from CVGC, and (3) determine how outcomes are associated with patient-reported quality of the genetic counselor:patient alliance.

METHODS: The MCVGC-GO (Multicenter Cardiovascular Genetic Counseling Outcomes Study) is a longitudinal survey-based study with pregenetic and postgenetic counseling data collection. Eight hundred ninety adults attending a first outpatient CVGC appointment at 8 United States and Canadian medical centers completed questionnaires assessing empowerment (Genetic Counseling Outcome Scale), worry (modified Cancer Worry Scale), cardiac anxiety (CAQ [Cardiac Anxiety Questionnaire]), and genetic counselor:patient alliance (Working Alliance Inventory-patient) before and up to 4 weeks post-CVGC, but before results of genetic tests ordered were returned to decouple CVGC and genetic test result impact.

RESULTS: Following CVGC, empowerment increased (Genetic Counseling Outcome Scale score change, +5.94±11.6; P<0.001), worry decreased (Cancer Worry Scale score change, -0.40±3.55; P=0.002), and cardiac fear decreased (CAQ fear subscale change, -0.034±0.46; P=0.033) with no change in whole-scale CAQ (0.013±0.34; P=0.29). In linear regression, worry decreased most in patients with less formal education (P=0.0021), with an arrhythmia indication (P=0.013), and who were at-risk family members (P=0.016) although the strength of the genetic counselor:patient alliance had no impact. In contrast, the genetic counselor:patient alliance was strongly positively associated with change in empowerment (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This observational, multicenter, multiprovider study provides foundational evidence that CVGC is associated with increased empowerment and decreased worry in adults attending outpatient CVGC and suggests opportunities for optimizing CVGC services.

articles.title: A self-contained ternary probe assay integrating self-priming cascade amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a for ultrasensitive detection of infant UTI-related microRNA.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Accurate quantification of infant urinary tract infection (UTI)-associated microRNAs remains challenging due to their short length, low abundance, and high sequence homology. Herein, we present a sensitive fluorescent biosensor that integrates a self-priming extension cascade with CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated signal amplification, with the core innovation being a rationally designed ternary sensing probe that consolidates all recognition and amplification elements into a single, self-contained architecture on magnetic beads. This integrated design eliminates the need for multiple exogenously added primers, offering three inherent advantages: fixed stoichiometric ratios ensure reproducible reaction initiation, the unified format simplifies the operational workflow, and stringent coupling of amplification to target recognition suppresses non-specific background. Upon target recognition, the probe undergoes programmed conformational rearrangements that trigger sequential self-priming extension events, simultaneously generating fragments that drive autocatalytic feedback and T7 promoter-containing products for downstream crRNA transcription. The transcribed crRNA activates Cas12a collateral cleavage, producing exponentially amplified fluorescence. Under optimized conditions, the assay achieves a detection limit of 0.48 fM, excellent single-base discrimination, and reliable performance in human serum. Quantification results correlate strongly with qRT-PCR. This exogenously primer-free, self-contained cascade uniquely unifies signal amplification, target regeneration, and crRNA synthesis in a single probe format, while the seamless coupling with CRISPR/Cas12a trans-cleavage ensures both ultrahigh sensitivity and exceptional specificity. The proposed strategy provides a promising platform for early diagnosis and screening of infant UTI.

articles.title: Partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings: challenges and feasibility.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Partial heart transplantation provides living, growth-capable valve implants for paediatric recipients. The feasibility and challenges of implementing partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings are evaluated, where the burden of valvular heart disease is greatest and paediatric valve replacement options remain severely limited.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted examining partial heart transplantation clinical outcomes, organ procurement logistics, immunosuppression requirements, and the infrastructure landscape for cardiac surgery in low-and middle-income countries. A feasibility framework was developed by mapping partial heart transplantation-specific requirements against existing low-and middle-income country cardiac surgical capacity.

RESULTS: Compared to orthotopic heart transplantation, several features of partial heart transplantation are inherently favourable for low-and middle-income country adaptation: it allows for longer graft ischaemia times, requires only tacrolimus monotherapy, and can source valves from hearts unsuitable for orthotopic heart transplantation. However, significant barriers persist, including limited organ procurement infrastructure, absence of regulatory frameworks for equitable donor-recipient matching, restricted access to therapeutic drug monitoring, and high rates of loss to follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of partial heart transplantation in resource-limited settings is feasible at established middle-income country cardiac surgery centres with transplant capability. A phased strategy leveraging international partnerships, existing infrastructure, and generic immunosuppression offers a realistic pathway to bringing this innovation to the children who need it most.

articles.title: ImmunEscpMap: a gene-centered knowledgebase for immune escape in cancer and viral infection.
articles.abstract: Tumors exploit immune escape to evade elimination, whereas viruses remodel host immunity to replicate or persist. However, evidence to interpret these processes is fragmented across databases, literature, and omics analyses, hindering gene prioritization. To address this, we developed ImmunEscpMap, a gene-centered knowledgebase connecting cancer and viral-infection evidence within a unified immune-escape framework. The current release contains 55 711 gene-evidence records (53 911 PubMed records from 37 193 unique PMIDs and 1800 Gene Expression Omnibus records across 709 accessions) representing 667 distinct source genes (657 in cancer, 571 in viral infection, and 561 shared). Evidence is organized into eight immune-escape mechanisms and 14 viral contexts, with the cancer branch integrating multi-omics and clinical outcomes, and the viral branch separating mechanistic anchors from infection-associated evidence. The web interface supports identifier search, context browsing, literature views, interactive gene pages, and bulk downloads. ImmunEscpMap is freely available at https://iescpemap.cqmu.edu.cn/, providing a traceable cross-domain map to prioritize candidates and guide follow-up experiments.

articles.title: Anti-PD-1 Therapy Alleviates Klebsiella pneumoniae-Induced Liver Abscess by Effectively Activating Kupffer Cells.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae-induced liver abscess (KPLA) is the leading cause of pyogenic liver abscess (LA) worldwide. Hepatic Kupffer cells exert protective effects during KPLA progression; thus, elucidating their protective mechanisms and developing novel therapeutic strategies are imperative. A murine KPLA model was established. Hematoxylineosin (HE) staining and tissue bacterial load were analyzed to verify successful K. pneumoniae infection. RT-qPCR, Western blot (WB), and flow cytometry were employed to quantify PD-1 expression in Kupffer cells. PD-1-knockdown Kupffer-cell transfection systems and PD-1-antibody treatment groups were established. Bacterial counts (CFU) and ELISA plus flow cytometry for inflammatory cytokines were used to evaluate the relationship between PD-1 expression and Kupffer-cell bacterial clearance. Finally, the KPLA mouse model was treated with PD-1 antibody to validate the role of PD-1 in LA. In the KPLA mouse model, gross abscess formation was observed, and HE staining revealed disorganized hepatic architecture. PD-1 expression in Kupffer cells was markedly up-regulated, and the proportion of PD-1-positive Kupffer cells increased significantly. In vitro, both PD-1 knockdown and PD-1-antibody treatment enhanced Kupffer-cell bacterial clearance, accompanied by elevated TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-12 levels. In vivo, the PD-1 antibody effectively treated KPLA. KPLA up-regulates PD-1 expression in Kupffer cells, thereby impairing bacterial clearance.
