Our findings preliminarily indicate that the anti-PD-1 antibody may have application potential in the prevention or early intervention of KPLA.

articles.title: Comprehensive cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary characterization of a cardiometabolic HFpEF model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which translational progress is limited by experimental models that insufficiently reflect the cardiometabolic phenotype while affecting endogenous endothelial function. We aimed to characterize a cardiometabolic "two-hit" HFpEF model combining metabolic stress (db/db) with chronic mineralocorticoid excess (d-aldosterone), focusing on integrated cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary phenotyping.

METHODS: Female db/db mice received 4-week d-aldosterone (0.3 µg/h) or vehicle via osmotic minipumps. Metabolic profiling, high-resolution echocardiography including strain and left atrial mechanics, invasive right-heart catheterization, and thoracic aortic wire myography were performed.

RESULTS: Aldosterone-treated db/db mice developed cardiac hypertrophy and pulmonary congestion with preserved LVEF but marked diastolic dysfunction, left atrial remodeling with increased stiffness, and impaired global longitudinal LV strain. Pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular dysfunction was evidenced by elevated RVSP/estimated mPAP, reduced PAT/PET, and reduced TAPSE. Thoracic aortae from untreated db/db mice already showed impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation, which was further aggravated by aldosterone, whereas maximal endothelium-independent relaxation remained largely preserved.

CONCLUSIONS: The db/db+d-aldosterone model recapitulates key features of cardiometabolic HFpEF across the cardiac-vascular-pulmonary axis and provides a translational platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies targeting endothelial and ventricular-vascular dysfunction in HFpEF. New & Noteworthy: Current HFpEF animal models often limit the investigation of vascular dysfunction, a central component of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We provide a comprehensive functional characterization of a db/db+d-aldosterone two-hit model demonstrating obesity, diabetes, diastolic dysfunction, atrial remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, and right ventricular impairment. By preserving endogenous endothelial nitric oxide signaling, this model offers a translational platform for studying vascular and cardiopulmonary mechanisms in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

articles.title: ADVANCING RADIATION PROTECTION IN PET/CT.
Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: We aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of plasma calprotectin in detecting infections following hip fracture surgery with 3 other biomarkers: procalcitonin (PCT), C-reactive protein (CRP), and white blood cell (WBC) count.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included surgically treated hip fracture patients aged ≥ 65 years, admitted to our department from April 2023 to August 2024. Plasma calprotectin, PCT, CRP, and WBC count were measured on postoperative day 3. The outcome was any infection within 30 days (primary) and 7 days (secondary). Biomarker performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analyses in a comparative framework.

RESULTS: 166/550 individuals were analyzed (median age 85 years, 68% women). 19% (n = 31) and 12% (n = 20) had infection within 30 and respectively 7 days. For 30-day infections, calprotectin showed highest area under the curve (AUC) of 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-0.77), followed by WBC count 0.60 (CCI 0.48-0.72), CRP 0.53 (CI 0.42-0.63), and PCT 0.51 (CI 0.40-0.63). Difference in AUC was largest between calprotectin and PCT (0.14, CI 0.00-0.29), followed by CRP (0.12, CI -0.01 to 0.26), while similar to WBC count (0.06, CI -0.05 to 0.16). For 7-day infections, AUCs were as following: calprotectin 0.70 (CI 0.58-0.82), WBC count 0.69 (CI 0.56-0.81), CRP 0.56 (CI 0.42-0.69), and PCT 0.48 (CI 0.33-0.63). Difference in AUC was largest between calprotectin and PCT (0.22, CI 0.05-0.39), followed by CRP (0.15, CI -0.02 to 0.31), while WBC count was similar (0.01, CI -0.09 to 0.12).

CONCLUSION: Calprotectin demonstrated a trend towards superior discriminatory ability for infections compared with PCT and CRP, particularly for infections within 7 days. Calprotectin provided moderate diagnostic accuracy, likewise WBC count.

articles.title: Palpitations in children and adolescents in the emergency department: a state-of-the-art narrative review of arrhythmia risk, diagnostic strategy, and disposition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Palpitations are not an uncommon complaint in the paediatric emergency department, causing significant anxiety for families concerned about serious heart disease. However, most cases are benign, often stemming from normal physiological responses like fever or anxiety. Primary cardiac arrhythmias are rare in this clinical setting.

PROBLEM: The main challenge is identifying the few children with dangerous arrhythmias among the many benign cases. Fear of missing a life-threatening condition often leads to extensive, costly, and stressful investigations, even in low-risk patients, without significantly improving detection rates.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to create a structured, risk-based framework for evaluating paediatric palpitations in the emergency department. The goal is to help clinicians efficiently distinguish benign from potentially life-threatening causes, thereby optimising resource use and reducing family anxiety.

FINDINGS: A thorough clinical history, physical exam, and a standard 12-lead electrocardiogram are the most effective evaluation tools. "Red-flag" features-such as palpitations with fainting (syncope), onset during exercise, or a family history of sudden cardiac death-successfully identify nearly all children with significant arrhythmias. Barring certain risk factors and any abnormalities on a 12 lead electrocardiogram, a dangerous cardiac condition is highly unlikely.

RECOMMENDATIONS: A stratified approach is recommended. Low-risk children (no red-flag features, normal electrocardiogram) can be safely discharged with reassurance. High-risk patients require immediate, aggressive evaluation, including cardiology consultation and potential hospital admission. This strategy improves accuracy, is cost-effective, and enhances patient safety.

articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Is Not Ready for the Diagnosis of Prediabetes.
articles.abstract: With the growing availability of over-the-counter continuous glucose monitors, the question arises whether Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) can be used to diagnose prediabetes. Traditionally, prediabetes is diagnosed using the oral Glucose Tolerance Test, a test with poor reproducibility. In a study from Singapore, there was large overlap between Ambulatory Glucose Profiles of people with prediabetes and normoglycemia. The optimal threshold of 5.64% Time above 140 mg/dL, the best discriminator, yielded 88% specificity and 48% sensitivity, indicating insufficient discriminatory value in many cases. In a study from Stanford, administration of a 75-gram oral glucose load while wearing CGM showed poor agreement with venous sampling between the category outcomes normoglycemia, prediabetes and diabetes. Future large cohort studies and AI may improve this situation. But for the moment, when a question of prediabetes arises, the most practical answer is to measure HbA1c, which allows for an elegant classification of normoglycemia, prediabetes and diabetes.

articles.title: The presence of Histoplasma capsulatum in environments from the state of Nayarit, Mexico, reveals a potential risk of infection for human populations.
articles.abstract: The Histoplasma capsulatum complex clusters cryptic species with genetic diversities linked to their geographic distribution and virulence. The American continent harbours its highest diversity, making this region the main axis for H. capsulatum spread. Species of this complex cause respiratory-systemic mycosis known as histoplasmosis. Infection occurs through the inhalation of fungal propagules that grow in sites such as caves, mines, and abandoned buildings, where environments rich in organic matter containing micronutrients present in bat and bird guano favour the development of these fungal pathogens. This research was conducted in the state of Nayarit, Mexico, where the combination of environmental factors and the constant occurrence of bats in urban and rural areas contributes to the proliferation of H. capsulatum. The presence of the fungus was detected by nested-PCR using a specific marker (Hcp100) for H. capsulatum, either in guano or in bat organ samples collected in the municipalities of Tepic, Santa María del Oro (SAMAO), and La Yesca, Nayarit. Out of 27 guano samples analysed by nested-PCR, 21 were positive for H. capsulatum, while of the 12 bats studied, only five revealed infections. The fungus was isolated from a lung sample of a nectarivorous bat (Glossophaga mutica) by culture. The results suggest a potential risk to exposed populations, including different specialized workers and tourists who explored bat roosts. Avoiding guano accumulation, restricting access to bat roosts, and implementing bat-exclusion strategies in homes are general recommendations to prevent fungal infections.

articles.title: Acute behavioural disturbance in the context of substance use: case series analysis of coroner reports.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute behavioural disturbance (ABD) is a contested term describing severe agitation and behavioural dysregulation, often preceding sudden death. Concerns regarding diagnostic clarity, racial bias and law enforcement restraint have been raised, and its clinical and forensic utility have been questioned.

AIMS: To characterise fatal ABD cases following substance use to inform clinical management, forensic interpretation and policy.

METHOD: Fifty-one deaths consistent with ABD were identified from the National Programme on Substance Use Mortality (NPSUM) using textual screening and Royal College of Emergency Medicine and Faculty of Forensic & Legal Medicine criteria.

RESULTS: All cases met Royal College of Emergency Medicine criteria and most met Faculty of Forensic & Legal Medicine (84.3%) criteria. Agitation was the most frequently observed sign (86.3% of cases). Stimulants, particularly cocaine and amphetamines, were also detected in 86.3% of cases, but not necessarily in the same cases, and the rate of stimulant detection was almost three times higher than that in in the broader NPSUM cohort (32.1%). Cocaine concentrations were higher in ABD cases than in all NPSUM cocaine-related deaths (0.848 mg/L v. 0.105 mg/L). Compared with the NPSUM cohort, ABD decedents were significantly younger (30.2 ± 7.5 v. 40.5 ± 13.4) and more likely to be male (92.2 v. 73.4%), from racially minoritised backgrounds (21.7 v. 3.9%) and living in deprived areas (87.0 v. 75.9%).

CONCLUSIONS: Variability in diagnostic criteria highlights a need for clearer ABD definitions. Toxicology testing may assist in refining the ABD construct, but its results must be interpreted within broader clinical and social contexts. These findings support avoiding use of ABD as a stand-alone cause of death but retaining it as a clinical descriptor prompting urgent treatment, monitoring and reduced reliance on prolonged restraint.

articles.title: Technical Complications and Salvage of Hepatic Artery Infusion Pumps: An Institutional Experience of 2935 Consecutive Cases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe the technical complications of hepatic artery infusion pump (HAIP) placement and characterize salvage rates.

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: HAIP chemotherapy is an effective tool used in the treatment of hepatic malignancies and has become increasingly adopted at select centers. Much of the safety data is reported from small, newer programs or older, large series.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent HAIP placement at our institution between 2000 and 2022 was conducted. Pump salvage was defined as the ability to receive HAIP chemotherapy after a pump-associated complication. Pump failure was defined as an HAIP-related complication permanently stopping ongoing HAIP chemotherapy.

RESULTS: Over the study period, 2935 patients had an HAIP placed for colorectal liver metastases (n=2582, 88%), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (n=294, 10%) or another malignancy (n=59, 2%). Of all patients, 759 (26%) had an HAIP-related complication, with 404/759 (53%) having their pump salvaged. The most common complications were abnormal perfusion (n=360 [12%], 285/360 [79%] salvaged), arterial pseudoaneurysm and/or hemorrhage (n=117 [4%], 7/117 [6%] salvaged), and pump-pocket infection (n=115 [4%], 60/115 [52%] salvaged). The complications with the highest salvage rates were pump-pocket seroma (n=15/16, 94%), pump-flipping (n=41/44, 93%), and pump-pocket hematoma (n=45/49, 92%). Unsalvaged complications were catheter dislodgement from vessel (n=0/47, 0%), catheter erosion into bowel (n=0/25, 0%), and arterial thrombosis (n=0/19, 0%). The cumulative incidence of pump failure at 1 year in patients receiving adjuvant therapy was 6.6%, and 4.5% among those receiving palliative therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: HAIP-related complications occur in about one quarter of patients, predominantly perfusion and pump-pocket complications. These are salvageable in the majority of cases with multidisciplinary interventions.

articles.title: First Do No Harm: When Can and Should We Withhold Antibiotics in Neonates?
Higher tissue concentrations of cefuroxime achieved with preoperative stand-alone intraosseous regional prophylaxis in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraosseous regional administration (IORA) of antibiotics can achieve higher local tissue concentrations than intravenous administration in conventional total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study aimed to evaluate the tissue concentration and systemic concentration of preoperative stand-alone intraosseous cefuroxime in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA) and identify a candidate dose for further evaluation.

METHODS: Thirty-nine patients undergoing MAKO RA-TKA were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive intraosseous cefuroxime 750 mg (R750IO), intraosseous cefuroxime 1,500 mg (R1500IO), or intravenous cefuroxime 1,500 mg (R1500IV). No additional intravenous antibiotics were administered before incision or during surgery. During surgery, nine tissue samples were collected: bone samples from the femur or tibia, synovial and fat samples from the surgical area, and systemic blood samples twice for cefuroxime level detection. Intraoperative vital signs, inflammatory markers on days 1 and 3 postoperative, and complications within 3 months were recorded.

RESULTS: The final analysis included 38 patients: 13 in the R750IO group, 13 in the R1500IO group, and 12 in the R1500IV group. Compared with the R1500IV group, both R1500IO and R750IO groups showed significantly higher tissue concentrations (p < 0.05) but lower initial blood concentrations (p < 0.05). While the R1500IO group had higher tissue concentrations than the R750IO group, its post-tourniquet-release blood concentration was significantly higher (p = 0.005). No significant differences were found in postoperative inflammatory markers and intraoperative vital signs among the three groups (p > 0.05), and no complications occurred within 3 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite multiple intramedullary pins and longer operative time in robot-assisted TKA, a single intraosseous dose of cefuroxime still achieved high tissue concentrations. Compared to conventional intravenous infusion of 1,500 mg cefuroxime, preoperative stand-alone intraosseous administration of either 750 mg or 1,500 mg cefuroxime achieved higher local tissue concentrations. Moreover, the 750 mg intraosseous regimen was associated with a lower post-tourniquet-release systemic concentration than the 1,500 mg intraosseous regimen, supporting its further clinical evaluation as a candidate dose in RA-TKA.

articles.title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients.

METHODS: A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease.

CONCLUSION: Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

articles.title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025. Inclusion required significant right atrial remodelling, defined as a right atrial area > 25 cm2. Patients with at least moderate functional tricuspid regurgitation comprised the AFTR cohort, while patients with mild/trivial/no tricuspid regurgitation served as controls. Patients with primary valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, device-related valve disease, RV dilatation, or more than mild RV systolic dysfunction were excluded. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 152 patients were included, comprising 120 patients with AFTR and 32 controls. Compared with controls, patients with AFTR demonstrated larger atrial dimensions, higher right-sided hemodynamic-burden, impaired RV longitudinal strain, and reduced reservoir RA strain. During a median follow-up of 6.3 years, 53 deaths (45%) occurred among patients with AFTR. In univariable Cox analysis, age (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; p = 0.016), TR Vmax (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.35; p = 0.020), and lower reservoir RA strain (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p = 0.003) were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, reservoir RA strain remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: AFTR is characterized by marked biatrial remodelling and impaired right atrial function. Reduced RA reservoir strain was independently associated with mortality, supporting a potential role for RA deformation imaging in risk stratification in AFTR.

articles.title: Hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness in patients with gout: a controlled cross-sectional elastography study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Gout shares cardiometabolic risk factors with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We aimed to compare elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness between patients with gout and metabolically stringent controls, and to identify independent determinants of controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM).

METHODS: In this single-center cross-sectional study (April 2024-January 2026), 201 adults with gout and 80 controls free of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan®). Multivariable linear and logistic regression models identified independent predictors of CAP, LSM, and binary elastographic outcomes.

RESULTS: Patients with gout had significantly higher CAP (279 vs. 251.5 dB/m; p < 0.001) and LSM (6.1 vs. 5.1 kPa; p < 0.001). In unadjusted analyses, the odds of hepatic steatosis (CAP ≥ 238 dB/m; OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.40-4.20; p = 0.001) and of increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa; OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.27-4.78; p = 0.007) were higher in the gout group, and LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa was more frequent (12.9% vs. 1.3%; p = 0.001). On multivariable analysis, BMI and ALT were the principal determinants of CAP, whereas BMI and age independently predicted continuous LSM. Gout status was not independently associated with CAP, continuous LSM, hepatic steatosis, or increased liver stiffness (adjusted OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.84-4.01; p = 0.131). Serum uric acid and disease activity measures were not associated with any elastographic outcome.

CONCLUSION: Patients with gout exhibit a substantially higher burden of elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness than metabolically stringent controls. This excess was accounted for by adiposity and age rather than by gout status or urate levels, suggesting that non-invasive liver assessment in gout should be guided by cardiometabolic risk profile rather than by the diagnosis of gout itself. Key Points • In unadjusted analyses, patients with gout had more than twofold higher odds of both hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness on transient elastography compared with metabolically stringent controls. • BMI and ALT were the strongest independent determinants of CAP; BMI and age were the strongest determinants of continuous LSM. • After adjustment for age, BMI and cardiometabolic covariates, gout status was not independently associated with any elastographic outcome, including increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa). • Serum uric acid, disease activity scores, and urate-lowering or anti-inflammatory therapies were not associated with elastographic liver measures, indicating that hepatic involvement in gout reflects adiposity-driven metabolic burden rather than urate-specific mechanisms.

articles.title: Serum Soluble Programmed Death Ligand-1 (sPD-L1) as a Diagnostic Marker in Neonatal Sepsis: Authors' Reply.
Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. Her condition deteriorated to focal and dyscognitive status epilepticus, requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI showed imaging features consistent with rhombencephalitis. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed through positive qRT-PCR results from both nasopharyngeal swab and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Further analysis of the CSF using quantitative shotgun proteomics via mass spectrometry revealed a neuroinflammatory profile indicative of blood-brain barrier disruption and differential expression of several proteins relevant to brain function, including the major prion protein, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD-1), and other aggregation-prone proteins.

CONCLUSIONS: This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 can invade the central nervous system and cause severe neurological impairment, even in the absence of typical respiratory symptoms. The findings underscore the importance of considering SARS-CoV-2 in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of neuroinvasion and the potential neurotropism of emerging viral variants.

articles.title: A Review: Mast Cells as Targets for Glucocorticoid Action.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to summarize the established and potential targets of glucocorticoids (GCs) on mast cells, which are implicated in the pathophysiology of various allergic and inflammatory diseases including asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis. We sought to answer the following questions: (1) How do glucocorticoids inhibit the release of mediators from mast cells? (2) What are the effects of glucocorticoids on mast cell signaling molecules? (3) By what mechanisms do glucocorticoids induce mast cell apoptosis? and (4) What are the genomic and non-genomic mechanisms underlying these effects?

RECENT FINDINGS: Evidence published since 2020 reinforces that glucocorticoid effects on mast cells are context dependent rather than uniform. Dexamethasone can directly suppress selected functions of human and murine mast cells, including in combination with inhibitory CD300a signaling [22]. Conversely, activated human lung mast cells can reduce corticosteroid responsiveness in neighboring airway smooth muscle cells by altering glucocorticoid-regulated transcription [23]. In patients with asthma, six weeks of inhaled budesonide reduced airway mast cell infiltration and improved airway hyperresponsiveness; importantly, associations differed according to mast cell phenotype, airway location, and inflammatory phenotype [25]. Single-cell studies now reveal multiple human mast cell transcriptional states across tissues [7, 8], while integrated RNA-seq and H3K27ac profiling in primary human mast cells demonstrates selective regulation of mast-cell identity genes and super-enhancer networks [92]. These findings place glucocorticoid responsiveness within a framework of mast cell state, tissue niche, species, glucocorticoid compound, and experimental context. Glucocorticoid-associated mast cell depletion may involve reduced stromal/fibroblast-derived SCF and, in IL-3-dependent murine models, reduced IL-3 receptor expression; these are mechanistically distinct effects. Glucocorticoids can target mast cells at several levels, including mediator synthesis and release, intracellular signaling, survival, and transcriptional regulation, but the magnitude and nature of these effects vary substantially among species, tissue compartments, mast cell phenotypes/states, glucocorticoid compounds, activation pathways, and experimental conditions. Classical GR-dependent transcription involves GRE-dependent regulation and interactions with transcription factors such as NF-κB and AP-1, yet mast-cell-specific GR-regulated gene and chromatin programs remain incompletely defined. Rapid effects on degranulation are also unresolved, with evidence for membrane-associated classical GR signaling as well as other rapid mechanisms. Contemporary human and single-cell data therefore argue against treating mast cells as a single uniformly corticosteroid-responsive population. Future studies should define the molecular basis of rapid glucocorticoid signaling and map GR-responsive transcriptional and chromatin programs across primary human mast cell states and tissue niches.

articles.title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.

articles.title: Comparison of outcomes after direct extracranial-to-intracranial bypass for moyamoya disease and non-moyamoya pathology: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Extracranial-intracranial (EC-IC) bypass is an established technique to augment intracranial flow in patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and other steno-occlusive diseases. The outcomes after direct EC-IC bypass for MMD compared to non-MMD pathologies (N-MMD) have not been systematically reviewed or compared in a meta-analysis. We performed a systematic review and meta‑analysis of studies reporting on outcomes in adults undergoing EC-IC bypass stratified by indication. Patients were assigned to either MMD or N-MMD pathologies with the latter primarily consisting of intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) and extracranial carotid occlusion (CO). Outcomes include graft patency, postoperative stroke or intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), and hyperperfusion syndrome (HPS). Random effects models were used to obtain pooled estimates for each outcome. Seventeen studies met inclusion criteria comprising 1,354 patients and 1,451 hemispheres. The weighted mean age was 49.1 years and 56.7% of patients were female. The indications for bypass included MMD or MMS in 52.6% of patients. ICAD and CO comprised 46.3% and 3.1% of patients, respectively. There was no difference in graft patency rates for the MMD and N-MMD groups (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.54-1.21; I2 = 0%). There was also no difference in postoperative stroke (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.33-1.41; I2 = 23%) or ICH (OR 1.46, 95% CI 0.34-6.26; I2 = 61.4%). There was no significant difference in the rate of HPS between the N-MMD and MMD groups (OR 1.69, 95% CI 0.67-4.26; I2 = 0). This meta-analysis discovered no significant differences in technical and postoperative outcomes between direct EC-IC bypass procedures performed for moyamoya and those performed for non-moyamoya steno-occlusive diseases. Further research with large multicenter cohorts, standardized techniques, and consistent outcome reporting is required to confirm these results.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of tolebrutinib in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tolebrutinib is an oral, brain-penetrant Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor being investigated for multiple sclerosis (MS). Early data point to reduced relapse rates and radiological disease activity, along with a reassuring safety profile. This systematic review and meta-analysis bring together the available evidence on its clinical efficacy and adverse events.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through February 2026 using predefined eligibility criteria. Data were extracted on efficacy outcomes (disability progression and improvement, MRI activity, and brain volume change) and safety outcomes (any adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse events leading to discontinuation, headache, ALT elevation, and death). Continuous outcomes were pooled as means using reported means and standard deviations; proportional outcomes were pooled from event and total counts. Analyses were run in R using random-effects models, with data unsuitable for pooling described narratively.

RESULTS: Four publications met our inclusion criteria: three reporting four randomized controlled trials and one long-term extension study. Tolebrutinib reduced the risk of confirmed disability progression at both ≥3 and ≥6 months, and disability improvement at 6 months was numerically higher than with comparators, though not conclusively so. Pooled progression rates were 18.35% (95% CI 9.73-31.9) at ≥3 months and 14.08% (95% CI 6.78-26.95) at ≥6 months. Mean brain volume change was -0.69% (95% CI -0.73 to -0.65). Adverse events of any kind occurred in 75.98% of patients, serious adverse events in 11.26%, and discontinuation due to adverse events in 4.14%; deaths were rare.

CONCLUSION: The available trial evidence suggests that tolebrutinib may reduce confirmed disability progression in nonrelapsing secondary progressive MS and MRI inflammatory activity versus placebo in earlier-phase relapsing MS. These findings are preliminary and should not be interpreted as definitive comparative evidence; longer-term, adequately powered studies are needed to define durability, safety, and its place relative to established disease-modifying therapies.

articles.title: Constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a glucose-dependent phenotype in murine mesenchymal stem cells.
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) possess significant metabolic plasticity, enabling them to adapt dynamically to environmental stressors during tissue repair. Although UCP1 is associated with nonshivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue (BAT) through the uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, its impact on MSCs metabolism remains unexplored. Herein, we evaluated the ectopic expression of UCP1 in MSCs and its effects on classical surface markers, the redox state and glucose metabolism. MSCs were genetically modified to constitutively overexpress UCP1 using a lentiviral construct. Transduction efficiency was evaluated by direct UCP1 expression and the co-expressed EGFP fluorescent tag. Surface marker phenotype and proliferation were evaluated by expression of multipotency markers and metabolic activity, respectively. Metabolic phenotypes were assessed by measuring mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), quantifying cytoplasmic and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), and evaluating glucose uptake via the 2-NBDG assay, while key glycolytic markers were evaluated by qPCR and immunoblot. UCP1-overexpressing MSCs showed a marked reduction in ΔΨm; however, normalized intracellular ATP levels remained stable across varying cell densities. Crucially, persistent UCP1 expression did not affect surface markers or cell metabolic activity, retaining their classical surface marker profile; furthermore, the engineered cells showed reduced baseline ROS levels compared with the parental line. Most notably, MSC-UCP1 cells showed increased glucose uptake and increased sensitivity to glucose deprivation, displaying increased expression of glycolytic markers. Our data indicate that constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a shift in MSC metabolism towards a glucose-dependent state. This distinct metabolic profile highlights the plasticity of MSCs energetics and suggests a potential therapeutic application for genetically engineered MSCs in treating energy imbalance disorders such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Restoration of cyclin A2 by glabridin reverses pathological cell cycle arrest and drives cardiac repair in HFpEF.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a pervasive clinical syndrome characterized by complex and elusive pathogenic mechanisms. In this study, we identify aberrant cardiomyocyte cell cycle arrest as a previously unrecognized pathological driver of HFpEF that hinders tissue repair. Using in vivo and in vitro models, we further demonstrate that Glabridin (Gla), a bioactive isoflavone, can induce cardiac repair and alleviate myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis in HFpEF by targeting the cell cycle arrest pathway. Mechanistically, Gla exerts its protective effects by specifically inhibiting the degradation of Cyclin A2 (CCNA2) and mitigating cardiomyocyte oxidative damage. This stabilization of CCNA2 effectively abrogates cell cycle arrest and drives cardiomyocyte cell cycle re-entry, an effect that was successfully recapitulated by CCNA2 gain-of-function experiments. This reparative response is intrinsically coupled with the restoration of metabolic homeostasis and the attenuation of oxidative stress, as evidenced in both cardiac and hepatic cells. Collectively, our findings define cell cycle arrest as a novel target and position Gla as a potent inducer of CCNA2-mediated cardiac repair for HFpEF treatment.

articles.title: Potential uric acid-lowering effect of sacubitril/valsartan.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Longitudinal association between body weight change and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity in patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus: A post hoc analysis of the FMD-J study B.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: We investigated cross-sectional associations between body mass index (BMI) and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and longitudinal associations between body weight change and baPWV over 3 years in 874 patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus without coronary artery disease (475 men; mean age, 61.9 ± 9.5 years). baPWV was measured at baseline, 1.5 years, and 3 years. At baseline, BMI was inversely correlated with baPWV (r = -0.14, P < 0.001), and multivariate analysis confirmed this association (β = -12.5, P < 0.001). In generalized linear mixed-effects models adjusted for concurrent systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and other covariates, neither continuous percentage change in body weight (β = -1.2, P = 0.08) nor categorical body weight change (≥5% increase: β = -10.6, P = 0.45; ≥5% decrease: β = 18.0, P = 0.15) was associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV, with no interaction across baseline BMI categories. The modest body weight changes observed in this cohort were not significantly associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV.

articles.title: Projected prevalence of hypertension and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension in Japan through 2040.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Accurate projections of future hypertension prevalence are essential for planning effective public health strategies to prevent cardiovascular mortality. This study aimed to project the future prevalence of hypertension in Japan through 2040. Prevalence estimates of hypertension and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension stratified by sex and age groups were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Survey from 1986 to 2019. Hypertension was defined as systolic blood pressure (BP) ≥ 140 mmHg, diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg, or use of antihypertensive medication, and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension as systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg or diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg. Three approaches were compared: a Bayesian Lee-Carter model, a model assuming monotonic prevalence change, and a constant-prevalence model. The projected prevalence estimates were applied to the population projections from the Vital Statistics of Japan. The Bayesian Lee-Carter model demonstrated the best predictive accuracy among the three models. The model projected that hypertension prevalence remained stable among men from 47.1% (95% credible interval [CI], 45.6-48.6%) in 2020 to 48.2% (44.6-52.4%) in 2040, and among women from 36.7% (35.5-37.8%) to 35.6% (32.8-38.3%). In contrast, untreated/uncontrolled hypertension prevalence would decline among men from 31.9% (28.6-34.6%) to 26.7% (18.0-38.4%), and among women from 23.1% (21.3-24.8%) to 17.2% (13.1-22.6%). The prevalence of hypertension in Japan is projected to remain largely unchanged through 2040, while the prevalence of untreated/uncontrolled hypertension is projected to decline. The findings suggest that public health policies and clinical efforts for BP control should be maintained and further strengthened to sustain and accelerate the trend.

articles.title: Noninvasive urinary biomarkers 3-bromotyrosine and leukotriene E4 in assessing asthma control and flare-up in children: a case-control study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess urinary biomarkers 3-bromotyrosine and leukotriene E4 (LTE4) levels in children with asthma and their association with asthma control and flare-up. This was a prospective study which applied a case-control design with 2:1 ratio. Children aged 3 to 15 years diagnosed with asthma according to the GINA 2022 guidelines were included. Measurements of urinary 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4 values were done using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. The asthma group (n = 146) had significantly higher urinary 3-bromotyrosine levels (22.58 ± 8.15 ng/mg creatinine) compared to healthy controls (n = 73) (14.53 ± 1.27 ng/mg creatinine, p < 0.001). Children with asthma flare-up exhibited significantly higher urinary 3-bromotyrosine levels (32.14 ± 7.76 ng/mg creatinine) compared to those with well-controlled asthma (17.16 ± 5.48 ng/mg creatinine, p < 0.001). Levels of 3-bromotyrosine decreased significantly after symptom control in hospitalized flare-up cases. Similarly, urinary LTE4 levels were significantly higher in the asthma group (308.40 ± 90.13 pg/mg creatinine) than controls (84.54 ± 18.27 pg/mg creatinine, p < 0.001). A significant difference in LTE4 levels was observed between well-controlled and flare-up cases. Urinary LTE4 levels also decreased following symptom control in hospitalized children. Both 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4 levels showed similar patterns of increase and decrease across asthma subgroups (well-controlled and flare-up). The Pearson's correlation coefficient between 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4 was r = 0.58 (p < 0.001). The ROC curve analysis demonstrated that both biomarkers moderately predict severity of asthma. The area under the curve for predicting flare-up was higher for LTE4.

CONCLUSION: Noninvasive urinary biomarkers, 3-bromotyrosine, and LTE4 were elevated in asthma and flare-up. Both biomarkers exhibited similar trends, with levels rising or falling according to asthma control status. The area under the curve to severity of asthma was higher for LTE4.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Asthma in children is associated with airway inflammation; several inflammatory biomarkers correlate with disease activity. Non-invasive biomarkers are increasingly preferred in children because blood sampling and invasive procedures can be difficult. • Urinary biomarkers have been investigated in asthma, particularly markers related to oxidative stress, leukotriene metabolism, eosinophilic inflammation, and mast-cell activation.

WHAT IS NEW: • Demonstrates that both non-invasive urinary biomarkers, 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4, are significantly elevated in children with asthma compared with healthy controls, and their higher levels are associated with poor disease control and flare-up. Both 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4, levels showed similar patterns of increase and decrease across asthma subgroups. • The Pearson's correlation coefficient between 3-bromotyrosine and LTE4 was r=0.58. The area under the curve to severe flare-up was higher for LTE4. Biomarker levels decline after symptom control provides evidence that these markers reflect ongoing disease activity and might be useful in disease monitoring.

articles.title: TasTY: Development and evaluation of a taste test for quantifying taste sensitivity among preschool children-test-retest reliability, application, and comparison between children with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Taste dysfunction gained attention during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic; however, validated objective tests for preschool children remain limited. We aimed to develop a feasible, reliable test quantifying taste sensitivity among children aged 3-6 years and to compare performance between children with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. We included 68 symptom-free children (median age 5.1 years; interquartile range (IQR) 3.9-5.9): 36 without known SARS-CoV-2 infection (control group, CG) and 32 with confirmed prior infection (SARS-CoV-2 infection group, C19-G), tested 79 days after infection (median; IQR 56-112). Children completed a self-developed Taste Test for Young Children (TasTY), a double-blind, playful two-alternative forced-choice test with 10 samples in randomized order (sweet, sour, and salty at three concentrations each; water served as a control). Twenty controls were retested a median of 62 days later (IQR 38-64). Outcomes were total score (0-10), feasibility, task comprehension, and test-retest reliability, assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEM), and smallest real difference (SRD). Feasibility was high (3% dropout), and 89.4% correctly classified water. Total score test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.73; pooled SEM = 0.76; SRD = 2.11). Total scores were similar between CG and C19-G (8.37 ± 1.5 vs. 8.19 ± 1.5; p = 0.63). Descriptively, three-year-olds (n = 17) had lower, more variable scores.

CONCLUSION: TasTY provides an age-appropriate, reliable, objective method for quantifying taste sensitivity among preschoolers, supporting standardized group comparisons and longitudinal assessment.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • COVID-19 increased awareness of taste dysfunction; however, evidence among young children relies mainly on surveys and parental reports. • Objective taste tests for preschool children remain limited.

WHAT IS NEW: • TasTY is a feasible, standardized, and objective test for quantifying taste sensitivity among children aged 3-6 years and goes beyond parental and subjective reports. • Its standardized 0-10 score showed good test-retest reliability and may support group comparisons and longitudinal assessment of preschool children with taste-related conditions.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of ifupinostat in relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a multicenter, single-arm phase 2 study.
articles.abstract: Ifupinostat (BEBT-908) is a novel dual-targeted inhibitor of histone deacetylase (HDACs) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα). We evaluated the efficacy and safety of ifupinostat monotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) after at least 2 prior lines of systemic therapy. Eligible participants received intravenous ifupinostat at 22.5 mg/m² on days 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 12 of a 21-day cycle. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and safety. From June 2020 to July 2022, 128 patients were enrolled and included in the safety set (SS), and 115 patients were in the efficacy analysis set (EAS). At the data cutoff (July 2023), the median follow-up was 19.58 months (95% confidence interval [CI] 16.82-21.95). The ORR was 36.5% (42/115, 95% CI 27.7-46.0), with a complete response rate of 11.3% (13/115). The median DoR was 6.2 months (95% CI 3.5-14.5), median PFS was 2.7 months (95% CI 1.6-3.7), and median OS was 9.9 months (95% CI 7.8-14.8). Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 99.2% (127/128) of patients, and ≥grade 3 TRAEs in 86.7% (111/128). The most common ≥grade 3 TRAEs were thrombocytopenia (75.8%, 97/128), neutropenia (33.6%, 43/128), and leukopenia (22.7%, 29/128). No treatment-related deaths occurred. Ifupinostat demonstrated promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile as a new therapeutic alternative for patients with r/r DLBCL. Clinical Trial Registry Number: ChiCTR1900028179.

articles.title: Dysregulation of Orexin-A and Implications for Renal Function Assessment in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a long-standing kidney condition in which the kidneys are gradually damaged. It usually has multiple symptoms and is often accompanied by complications, such as hormonal imbalances, high blood pressure, anemia, and sleep disorders. Orexin, occasionally mentioned as hypocretin, is a neuropeptide that is mostly generated by orexin-containing neurons in the hypothalamus. Their receptors are found in a variety of tissues, such as the brain and kidney. This study aims to evaluate the impact of renal function on orexin-A levels in CKD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study included 44 adult patients diagnosed with CKD, and their results were compared with 44 healthy participants of the same age and sex. An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit was used to measure orexin-A, while urea, creatinine, and lipid profile were measured using spectrophotometric methods. Association with orexin-A was performed using Pearson's correlation analysis.

RESULTS: The results showed a significant decrease in serum orexin-A (P < 0.001) in patients with CKD. Correlation analysis showed that orexin-A in CKD patients was positively correlated with serum creatinine (r = 0.353, P = 0.018) and high-density lipoprotein (r = 0.354, P = 0.017), while negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate (GFR) (r = -0.424, P = 0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: Orexin-A levels decreased in patients with CKD, and this decrease reflects the disruption of the orexin system, which was inversely related to the GFR and directly related to creatinine and high-density lipoprotein levels.

articles.title: Impact of Triple Assessment on Surgical Decision-making in Thyroid Nodule Management.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate preoperative assessment of thyroid nodules is crucial for distinguishing malignant from benign lesions and making optimal decisions. Triple assessment using clinical examination, ultrasonography (USG), and fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) has been increasingly used to improve diagnostic accuracy.

AIM: The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy of triple assessment in the detection and treatment of thyroid nodules by correlating ultrasonographic findings, clinical evaluation, and FNAC results with histopathological diagnosis.

METHODS: This study was a prospective observational study of 56 patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgical management. Data were collected prospectively using structured case record forms. Baseline information, physical examination findings, USG features, FNAC records, operative details, and histopathological reports were documented. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Frequency and percentage were used to present categorical variables. The diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination, USG, FNAC, and triple assessment was evaluated by estimating specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value, and diagnostic accuracy.

RESULTS: A higher proportion of participants were female (85.7%) and were in the 41-60 years old age group. Histopathology confirmed benign lesions in 57.14% and malignant lesions in 42.86% of cases. Triple assessment achieved the most effective diagnostic accuracy, showing a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 87.50%, with a NPV of 100% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 97.86%.

CONCLUSION: Triple assessment is a dependable and useful modality for assessing thyroid nodules. Combined use of clinical examination, USG, and FNAC reduces false-negative results and supports appropriate clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Platelet Indices as Biomarkers of Disease Severity and Morbidity in Hospitalized Dengue Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue fever is a rapidly expanding mosquito-borne illness with significant morbidity in children. While thrombocytopenia is a key feature, platelet count alone poorly predicts disease severity. Platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT) may provide better insight into disease progression and complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional observational study was conducted in the Department of Pediatrics, at a tertiary care hospital over 18 months. A total of 120 children aged 1-16 years with confirmed dengue infection (NS1 antigen or immunoglobulin M positive) were enrolled. Platelet indices were recorded at admission. Patients were classified according to the World Health Organization 2009 dengue severity criteria. Associations between platelet indices and disease severity, hepatic dysfunction, and renal dysfunction were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests.

RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 35% had dengue without warning signs, 48.3% had warning signs, and 16.7% had severe dengue. MPV and PCT decreased, while PDW increased significantly with disease severity (P < 0.001). Hepatic (31.7%) and renal (9.2%) dysfunction were associated with lower MPV and PCT and higher PDW (P < 0.001). PDW showed a strong positive correlation with severity (r = 0.71), whereas MPV and PCT showed negative correlations.

CONCLUSION: Platelet indices, particularly PDW and PCT, are simple, readily available, and reliable markers for predicting disease severity and organ dysfunction in pediatric dengue. Their routine use may aid early risk stratification, timely intervention, and improved clinical decision-making, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced biomarkers may not be accessible.

articles.title: Perinatal Outcome of Sickle-cell Disease in Pregnancy: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sickle-cell disease (SCD) poses significant maternal and neonatal risks during pregnancy. Assessing the perinatal outcomes in pregnant women with homozygous SCD (HbSS) to optimize management strategies is the goal of this study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, AIIMS Raipur, Chhattisgarh, over 18 months (September 1, 2021, to February 28, 2023). All pregnant women in the third trimester with HbSS admitted to the antenatal care ward were included. Patients with chronic hypertension, diabetes, renal diseases, thalassemia syndromes, or compound sickle-cell syndromes were excluded. Data on maternal and neonatal outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: The mean hemoglobin at admission was 7.98 + 2.19 g/dL. 65.9% of women required antenatal transfusions. 38.2% of women developed sickle-cell crisis. 23.5% of women required intensive care unit admission in the antenatal and postnatal period. Notable was the mortality of 5.8% of women, which occurred in the postnatal period. 61.8% of women underwent cesarean section, with fetal distress as the most common indication. The mean birth weight was found to be 2.51 ± 0.47 kg. However, there was no neonatal mortality.

CONCLUSION: Optimizing perinatal care requires an understanding of the maternal and neonatal problems linked to SCD during pregnancy. This study emphasizes how crucial multidisciplinary management is to reducing unfavorable results.

articles.title: Optimal Reticulocyte Hemoglobin Equivalent Cutoff to Diagnose Iron Deficiency: A Study from South Indian Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia is the most common health problem affecting approximately one-third of the population worldwide, with 50% of patients suffering from iron-deficiency anemia (IDA). Hematological parameters along with peripheral smear finding may help in picking up patients with IDA but are insensitive to early stages of iron deficiency. Serum iron studies are required for confirmation but these are affected by inflammation, infection, and liver disease. Reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret He) measures the hemoglobin (HGB) content in circulating reticulocytes, reflecting iron availability for erythropoiesis over the preceding 3-4 days and it is not influenced by inflammation or diurnal variation and provides a real-time assessment of iron deficiency. However, Ret He cutoff show variation across different population.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study done at a tertiary care health center in South India, for the period of 2 years (September 2024-February 2026). The study population includes individuals more than 18 years of age and is categorized into two categories. Category I composed of 100 normal individuals with HGB values and serum iron studies within normal limits. Category II comprising of 200 individuals having serum ferritin levels <30 ng/mL or transferrin saturation (T-SAT) of <20%.

RESULTS: Comparison of the mean values of parameters such as HGB, red blood cell (RBC) count, RBC indices, reticulocyte parameters, Ret He, serum iron, T-SAT, and serum ferritin levels were reduced below normal limits in cases with iron deficiency. A strong statistically significant positive correlation is observed with mean corpuscular hemoglobin (r = 0.823), mean corpuscular volume (r = 0.8186), and HGB (r = 0.8165). Moderate positive correlations are evident with key iron profile parameters, including T-SAT%, serum iron, and ferritin. Receiver operating characteristic analysis Ret He cutoff of 29.85 pg was obtained which showed 85% sensitivity and 88% specificity with excellent area under the curve of 0.941 and statistically significant P < 0.001 in predicting iron deficiency.

CONCLUSION: Reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret-He) is a reliable and effective marker for detecting iron deficiency, demonstrating excellent diagnostic accuracy, with a cutoff of 29.85 pg. Its incorporation into routine hematological evaluation may facilitate early identification of iron deficiency, although population-specific cutoffs should be considered.

articles.title: Intrapleural TPA vs Normal Saline in Pediatric Empyema: A Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intrapleural tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) reduces hospital length of stay (LOS) vs intrapleural normal saline in children with complicated parapneumonic effusion or empyema.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study at a tertiary pediatric referral hospital in Iran, comparing children aged 1 month to 18 years treated during TPA unavailability (2012-2015; intrapleural saline, 40 mL, 1-hour dwell, daily ×3 days) with those treated after TPA became available (2015-2018; TPA 4 mg in 40 mL saline, same protocol). The primary outcome was hospital LOS, and the secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) stay, fever duration, chest-tube duration, and ICU admission. Multivariable linear regression was adjusted for baseline imbalances between cohorts.

RESULTS: Of 85 patients, 61 received TPA and 24 saline. The cohorts were comparable at baseline, except for higher pleural fluid adenosine deaminase and shorter time to first instillation in the saline group (medium and very large effects). The mean hospital LOS was 20.28 ± 5.53 days (TPA) vs 19.17 ± 3.60 days (saline). The unadjusted difference was 1.11 days (95% CI, -1.14 to 3.36; P = .366). The adjusted mean difference was 0.36 days (95% CI, -2.91 to 3.63; P = .826). Secondary outcomes showed similarly small differences, with CI ranges compatible with no clinically important effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Intrapleural TPA showed no detectable benefit over saline in this retrospective comparison. The wide CI ranges indicate insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis and not equivalence. Our findings raise, but do not confirm, the hypothesis that mechanical lavage contributes to clinical improvement. Residual confounding and selection bias cannot be excluded. Adequately powered, prospective randomized trials are needed to establish the incremental value of fibrinolysis in children.

articles.title: Association Between Neighbourhood-level Antibiotic Utilization and the Rate of Community-Associated C. difficile (CA-CDI) Infection: An Ecological Study.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite reductions in hospital-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) incidence in Canada and the United States, the incidence of community-associated CDI (CA-CDI) has remained high. We sought to investigate whether neighbourhood-level variation in antibiotic utilization is associated with CA-CDI.

METHOD: We conducted a neighbourhood-level ecological study across 1,520 neighbourhoods in Ontario, Canada. Residents aged ≥66 without hospitalization in the prior 30 days were eligible for inclusion from 2017 to 2023. Antibiotic utilization, CDI cases, and population were identified for each neighbourhood using comprehensive province-wide databases. CA-CDI rate was the outcome (incident cases of CA-CDI/10,000 person-years). Rate of antibiotic utilization (DOT per 1000 person-days) was the primary exposure. The rate-ratio (RR) of CA-CDI associated with increased antibiotic utilization was estimated using negative-binomial regression, adjusting for 8 demographic and health care covariates. We also evaluated risk based on low-, moderate-, and high-risk antibiotic strata based on published literature.

RESULT: We identified 19,757 CA-CDI cases. We observed substantial variation in antibiotic utilization across neighbourhoods (Median=21.1 DOT/1000 person-days; interquartile range [IQR], 16.7-25.6). After adjustments, we observed an association between overall antibiotic utilization (RR=1.13 per 10-point increase in DOT; 95% confidence interval [95%CI], 1.09-1.18). A gradient wherein higher risk antibiotic agents were more strongly associated with CA-CDI was apparent (Low-risk: RR=1.08; 95%CI, 1.01-1.15; Moderate-risk: RR=1.27; 95%CI, 1.15-1.39; High-risk: RR=1.73; 95%CI, 1.13-2.66).

DISCUSSION: Neighbourhoods with higher antibiotic utilization, especially for moderate and high-risk antibiotics, have higher CA-CDI incidence. Reducing variability in neighbourhood antibiotic utilization could help reduce the burden of CDI.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Postoperative Outcomes for Men and Women With Colon Cancer in the US Military Health System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Biological, behavioral, and health care access differences between men and women may contribute to differences in colon cancer diagnosis and treatment. We compared postoperative outcomes between men and women with colon cancer in the universal access Military Health System (MHS) to better understand sex-based differences in surgery.

METHODS: We identified patients with stage I to III colon adenocarcinoma receiving surgery in the Military Cancer Epidemiology (MilCanEpi) database between 2001 and 2014. Thirty-day postoperative outcomes included general cardiovascular and respiratory complications; infections (surgical site [SSI], urinary tract [UTI], and systemic); gastrointestinal (GI) complications (hemorrhage, bowel obstruction, ileus, intra-abdominal abscess, and anastomotic leakage); and hospital readmissions. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted rate ratios (ARRs) and 95% CIs in association with biological sex for the outcomes.

RESULTS: The study included 1073 male (mean age=59.5±13.5 y) and 794 female (mean age=59.6±13.5 y) patients. In the 30-day postoperative period, general complication rates were not different by sex (ARR=1.03, 95% CI: 0.76-1.40 for women vs. men). Female sex was associated with higher rates of UTI (ARR=2.44, 95% CI: 1.63-3.65) and lower rates of GI complications (ARR=0.79, 95% CI: 0.69-0.90) relative to men. There were no sex differences in 30-day hospital readmissions (ARR=0.90, 95% CI: 0.76-1.08 for women vs. men).

CONCLUSIONS: In the MHS, female sex was associated with higher rates of UTI and lower rates of GI complications relative to men undergoing colon cancer surgery. Factors other than health care access, such as biological differences in pelvic anatomy, physiology, or immune responses, may contribute to observed differences.

articles.title: Geographic Accessibility to Acute Stroke Care in Egypt: A Population-Level GIS Analysis With Hub-and-Spoke Network Optimization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Egypt faces a disproportionate acute stroke burden, but geographic accessibility to intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has not been systematically quantified using modality-specific treatment windows. The objective of the current work is to measure population-level geographic accessibility to IVT and MT across Egypt's 27 governorates, characterize access inequality determinants, and model the clinical impact and cost-effectiveness of targeted hub-and-spoke network expansion.

METHODS: We verified 29 IVT-capable hospitals and 13 MT-ready centers through a 3-phase protocol. Onset-to-treatment time was computed for 120 settlements representing 89.3% of the national population (108.3 million). MT eligibility was based on noncontrast CT for ASPECTS scoring and CT angiography for large-vessel occlusion confirmation. Treatment windows were classified as optimal (<180 min), within-window (IVT 180 to 270 min; MT 180 to 360 min), or denied (IVT >270 min; MT >360 min). A maximum-coverage location problem model identified the optimal deployment for 3 new MT hubs and 4 IVT spokes. Cost-utility analysis expressed outcomes in quality-adjusted life years over 10 years using Egypt's GDP per capita of $3800.

RESULTS: IVT optimal access was 71.8% nationally (77.0 million), while MT optimal access was only 56.2% (60.9 million), with 20.4% denied MT under the 6-hour threshold. Nine of 13 MT-ready centers (69.2%) concentrated in Cairo/Giza (19.2% of the population). Hub-and-spoke deployment improved MT optimal access from 56.2% to 75.8% nationally. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated 73.2% and 91.4% probabilities of cost-effectiveness at 3× and 4× GDP thresholds, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Egypt's MT access crisis reflects infrastructure maldistribution rather than patient ineligibility. A hub-and-spoke model using NCCT+CTA-based MT selection within the 6-hour window is clinically sound, operationally feasible, and probabilistically cost-effective.

articles.title: Geographic patterns of asthma morbidity: a systematic review of Sand and dust storm (SDS) impacts in Asia.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sand and Dust Storms (SDS) are prevalent in Asia, releasing fine particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5) that pose significant risks to respiratory health, particularly for asthmatic populations. This systematic review evaluates the impact of SDS on asthma incidence, hospital admissions, and exacerbations across Asia, providing a basis for public health interventions.

DATA SOURCES: We performed a systematic search in PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to May 2023 using terms related to sand and dust storms, SDS, asthma, and respiratory health.

STUDY SELECTION: Thirty-three studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly from Japan, Korea, and the Middle East. Cohort (n = 13; 39.4%) and panel designs (n = 12; 36.4%) were the frequent methodologies.

RESULTS: Findings consistently revealed a significant association between SDS and increased asthma exacerbations, hospital admissions, and emergency visits, peaking within 1-5 days post-exposure. Overall, the vast majority of the evaluated studies documented a positive association between SDS and asthma-related healthcare utilization, although the magnitude and statistical significance varied according to study designs and outcome definitions. The impact was disproportionately high among children and the elderly. Notably, studies from East Asia demonstrated more pronounced health impacts, including higher odds ratios and longer hospital stays, compared to the Middle East.

CONCLUSION: SDS are a significant burden on respiratory health in Asia. Our findings underscore the need for targeted, region-specific public health strategies and improved air quality monitoring. However, results are subject to limitations, including significant study heterogeneity and potential language bias due to the exclusion of non-English publications.

articles.title: Public perception of osteopathic manipulative medicine as an effective treatment for musculoskeletal disorders.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are among the most prevalent causes of disability globally, contributing significantly to diminished quality of life and rising healthcare costs. While pharmacological treatments and physical therapy remain standard, alternative modalities such as osteopathic manipulative medicine (OMM) have emerged as promising nonpharmacologic options. However, public awareness of OMM remains limited, and misconceptions persist, particularly regarding its distinction from chiropractic care. This study aimed to assess public perception of OMM and its effectiveness in treating MSDs, with the goal of informing strategies to enhance understanding and utilization of osteopathic principles.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate the public's perception, awareness, and experiences with OMM in the treatment of MSDs, and to identify knowledge gaps that can be addressed through educational outreach. This study also examined how demographic and socioeconomic factors influence awareness and utilization of OMM. Insights gained will guide the development of targeted educational materials to enhance public understanding, to promote the distinctiveness of osteopathic medicine, and to clarify the role of OMM in MSD care.

METHODS: A nationwide, web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted targeting US adults aged 18 years and older. Demographic data collected included age, location, race, ethnicity, income, marital and employment status, and number of children. The survey, administered through Random Device Engagement (RDE) methodology, was distributed within mobile apps to a randomized sample of users who opted in through nonmonetary incentives. Questions assessed knowledge of OMM, previous experiences with osteopathic care, perceived effectiveness in managing MSDs, and interest in nonpharmacological treatments. Quantitative analysis included frequency distributions and descriptive statistics to characterize awareness, perceptions, and utilization of OMM.

RESULTS: A total of 174 valid responses were analyzed after the exclusion of incomplete entries. Respondents represented a demographically diverse population across the United States. The most frequently cited uses of OMM were for back pain (n=70, 40.2 %), neck pain (n=58, 33.3 %), arthritis (n=38, 21.8 %), and chronic pain (n=33, 19.0 %). Regarding effectiveness, 68 respondents (39.1 %) rated OMM as "Very Effective," and 30 (17.2 %) rated it as "Extremely Effective." The key benefits included pain relief, improved mobility, reduced medication use, and noninvasiveness. Awareness of osteopathic distinctiveness remained low, with many respondents conflating OMM with chiropractic care.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight a favorable perception of OMM among those familiar with its use in MSD management, yet widespread knowledge gaps persist among the general public. The data support the need for targeted educational efforts that promote OMM as a safe, effective, evidence-based alternative to pharmacologic interventions. This work strengthens the case for broader integration of osteopathic principles in mainstream care and underscores the importance of outreach in reinforcing osteopathic distinctiveness. Future steps will involve the development of educational materials to address misconceptions and improve access to OMM services.

articles.title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.

METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria.

RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

articles.title: Irisin is associated with survival in sepsis and attenuates macrophage pro-inflammatory responses with involvement of AMPK signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet effective targeted therapies remain limited. We evaluated the prognostic significance of irisin, a myokine, in sepsis cohort and examined its immunomodulatory effects on macrophages using a translational approach.

METHODS: Patients were enrolled in a prospectively collected sepsis registry and biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was conducted to assess independent association between irisin and 30-day mortality. Mechanistic studies used macrophages ex vivo and a murine cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model.

RESULTS: Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.955, 95% confidence interval 0.913-0.999, p=0.044) in patients with sepsis (N=655). Irisin showed modest discrimination for 30-day mortality (AUROC 0.609), with no statistically significant difference from lactate (AUROC 0.652; p=0.145). In vitro , irisin suppressed LPS-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, preserved AMPK phosphorylation, attenuated IκBα degradation, and reduced pro-inflammatory markers in macrophages. Several of these cellular effects were attenuated following AMPKα1 depletion. In vivo , irisin improved 7-day survival after CLP (75% vs. 36%, p<0.05) and reduced systemic inflammatory cytokines at 24 hours.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher serum irisin was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality in patients with sepsis, although its standalone discriminatory performance was modest. Experimental findings further showed that irisin improved survival and attenuated macrophage inflammatory responses, with AMPK signaling contributing to several cellular effects. These findings support further evaluation of irisin as part of integrated prognostic assessment and investigation of irisin-related signaling in sepsis.

articles.title: Effect of Adhesive Dwell Time on Skin Injury in Neonates: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Advances in neonatal care : official journal of the National Association of Neonatal Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal skin is immature and highly susceptible to injury, particularly in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) where medical adhesives are frequently used. Medical adhesive-related skin injury is a common clinical concern, yet evidence regarding optimal adhesive dwell time remains limited.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adhesive dwell time on neonatal skin integrity and its association with skin injury outcomes.

METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted between August and December 2023 in a tertiary NICU. Sixty term neonates (37-40 weeks) were randomized to either a 2-hour adhesive dwell time group (n = 30) or a 4-hour routine care group (n = 30). Skin condition and risk were assessed using the Neonatal Skin Condition Score and the Neonatal Skin Risk Assessment Scale (NSRAS).

RESULTS: The experimental group demonstrated significantly lower Neonatal Skin Condition Scores on Day 1 ( P = .010) and Day 3 ( P < .001), indicating improved skin condition. No significant between-group differences were observed in NSRAS scores ( P > .05), although scores decreased over time in both groups. Birth weight and gestational age were negatively correlated with NSRAS scores in the experimental group ( P < .05).

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE AND RESEARCH: Shorter adhesive dwell time appears to improve neonatal skin condition and may represent a simple and effective strategy to reduce localized skin injury in NICU settings. However, its effect on broader skin risk profiles remains limited.
