Further research is needed to evaluate long-term outcomes and the interaction between adhesive duration and material type across different neonatal populations.

articles.title: Investigating the effect of leucine and dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine on aerosolization properties of high-dose dry powder inhaler formulations of itraconazole nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: This study aims to develop a high-dose dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulation of itraconazole (ITZ) nanoparticles with leucine and/or dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC) as excipients to increase drug solubility and aerosolization performance. To do this, we co-spray-dried leucine and DPPC with an optimized ITZ nanosuspension and measured the physical properties, dissolution and aerosolization characteristics of the formulations. Among the formulations, those containing 50% (w/wITZ) leucine (N3) or 30% (w/wITZ) leucine with 20% (w/wITZ) DPPC (N5), which had the highest FPF (68.88 ± 1.90% for N3 and 78.81 ± 1.17% for N5) and dissolved percentage of the drug (cumulative release percentage in 180 min, 69.10 ± 1.46% for N3 and 94.34 ± 1.30% for N5), were selected for in vivo pharmacokinetic studies and insufflated intratracheally to rats. An ITZ suspension was administered as a control by gavage. Among the selected formulations, N3 produced the highest AUC in lung tissue, approximately two-fold higher than N5. Furthermore, the AUCLung-to-AUCPlasma ratio for N3 was approximately 24-fold and 800-fold higher than those of N5 and the oral formulations, respectively, indicating enhanced pulmonary retention and potentially reduced systemic exposure. Overall, N3 represents a promising high-dose DPI formulation for further preclinical development of inhaled ITZ.

articles.title: Orally administered acarbose-guar gum solid dispersion mitigates diabetes-induced kidney damage via modulating inflammatory response and oxidative stress in diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus can cause progressive renal injury characterised by oxidative stress, inflammation and impaired renal function. This study investigated the kidney- and cell-protective potential of acarbose-guar gum solid dispersions (AGSDs) using in vitro and in vivo diabetic models. In BHK-21 cells, AGSD-3 showed improved biocompatibility, with higher cell viability (65.54 ± 0.41%) than acarbose (56.67 ± 0.24%) and reduced lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release (7.29 ± 0.13%) at 100 µg/mL. Under high-glucose conditions, AGSD-3 significantly reduced lipid peroxidation and enhanced superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase and glutathione S-transferase (GST) activities (p < 0.001). In diabetic rats, AGSD-3 (50 mg/kg) significantly improved renal function, reducing serum creatinine, urea and uric acid to 0.45 ± 0.02, 36.00 ± 0.96 and 2.00 ± 0.02 mg/dL, respectively, and normalised relative kidney weight. Histopathological findings further supported restoration of renal architecture. AGSD-3 enhanced renal antioxidant status, with increased SOD, catalase and GST activities, while reducing nitric oxide, xanthine oxidase and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activities (p < 0.001). Furthermore, AGSD-3 reduced TNF-α and IL-6 while increasing IL-10 levels. Overall, AGSD-3 exhibited antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and renoprotective effects, supporting its potential as an improved acarbose-based formulation for diabetes-associated renal injury.

articles.title: Daily consumption of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts beneficially affects regional brain insulin responsiveness in older adults: results of a longer-term randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Brain insulin responsiveness is implicated in age-related metabolic and cognitive conditions. We previously reported that daily consumption of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts improved memory in older adults. Here, we investigated whether changes in brain insulin responsiveness may contribute to these effects. In a randomized, single-blind, controlled crossover study, 31 older adults (67 ± 4 years) consumed either 60 g day-1 of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts or followed a no-peanut control period for 16 weeks, separated by an 8-week washout. Brain insulin responsiveness was assessed as changes in cerebral blood flow (CBF) following intranasal insulin administration using arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging (ASL-MRI). Intrahepatic lipid (IHL) content was quantified using abdominal MRI. Fasting blood samples were evaluated for markers of glucose homeostasis, lipid metabolism, and low-grade systemic inflammation. Whole-brain analysis identified one region in the right hemisphere showing reduced CBF responses to intranasal insulin after peanut intake compared with the control (mean difference: -5.4 ± 5.4 mL per 100 g tissue per min; cluster size = 552 mm3, P = 0.044). Harvard-Oxford atlas localization yielded the highest average probabilities for the lingual gyrus (20%), hippocampus (14%), parahippocampal gyrus (11%), thalamus (2%), and posterior cingulate gyrus (1%). Intrahepatic lipid content and circulating markers of glucose homeostasis, lipid metabolism, and low-grade systemic inflammation remained unchanged. These findings suggest that 16 weeks of unsalted, skin-roasted peanut consumption had a potentially beneficial effect on regional brain insulin responsiveness in memory-related brain regions in older adults. This response may contribute to the previously observed cognitive benefits of peanut intake in this population. Clinical Trial Registry: This trial was registered at clinicaltrial.gov as NCT05724654.

articles.title: Missed Opportunities for Prehospital Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Prehospital blood transfusion has been associated with improved outcomes among pediatric trauma patients, but its utilization nationally remains poorly understood. We recently conducted a similar study that builds upon the findings of the investigation by Ramgopal et al. to identify potential missed opportunities for prehospital transfusion in pediatric trauma.

METHODS: We utilized the National EMS Information System dataset from 2018-2023 to identify emergency medical services (EMS) responses for pediatric (<18 years of age) trauma patients. We identified trauma patients using the CDC Injury Mortality Diagnosis Matrix related ICD-10 codes. We identified patients at increased risk of benefiting from a transfusion using age-adjusted positive shock index thresholds. The outcome of interested was prehospital blood or blood product transfusion.

RESULTS: We found there were 1,663,601 total 9-1-1 EMS activations to a scene for pediatric trauma. There were 363,844 patients with a positive shock index who were considered to be at increased risk of benefiting from a prehospital transfusion, but only 287 (0.1%) of these patients received a prehospital transfusion. Only 10 (2%) of the 468 patients who experienced a cardiac arrest after the arrival of EMS to the scene received a hospital transfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, our results indicate prehospital transfusion rates ranging from 0.1% to 1.01% among potentially eligible pediatric trauma patients. Although positive shock index does not confirm hemorrhagic shock, these findings suggest underutilization of prehospital blood transfusion among pediatric trauma patients.

articles.title: Preparation of hypoglycemic peptides from oysters fermented with Bacillus subtilis: characterization, molecular docking, and in vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a highly prevalent chronic metabolic disorder, is primarily defined by persistent hyperglycemia due to defects in insulin secretion or action. In this study, a hypoglycemic peptide-containing fraction was prepared from oysters via liquid fermentation using Bacillus subtilis (CGMCC no. 28507). Following optimization of fermentation conditions and ultrafiltration separation, a fraction (FOP) with a molecular weight below 3 kDa was obtained, demonstrating the highest inhibitory potency against α-glucosidase. In vivo experiments using mice with T2DM confirmed that FOP markedly reduced fasting blood glucose, glycated haemoglobin levels, and insulin resistance and simultaneously improved glucose tolerance and lipid metabolism profiles, downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines and alleviating pathological damage to the liver and pancreas. Following gel chromatography purification, three bioactive peptides (KSYFPT, VGGQGFF, and LRFPGQ) were identified by LC-MS/MS. According to molecular docking experiments, these peptides exhibited stable binding interactions with the α-glucosidase active site. All synthesized peptides exhibited significant inhibitory activity. This study delineates an eco-friendly protocol for the sustainable valorization of oyster proteins, simultaneously providing a theoretical basis for the formulation of food-derived functional agents with significant hypoglycemic potential.

articles.title: Citri reticulatae pericarpium viride attenuates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by activating PGC-1α-mediated fatty acid oxidation in mice.
articles.abstract: Citri reticulatae pericarpium viride, a fruit peel from immature Citrus reticulata Blanco known as Qing Pi (QP) in Chinese, is a traditional food ingredient widely employed for culinary flavoring and aroma enhancement. Although QP exerts various metabolic benefits, the impacts and mechanisms of QP on preventing metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. Here, we found that QP extracts (extracted with 75% concentrated ethanol and ethyl acetate) not only decreased high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic triglyceride accumulation and oxidative damage, ameliorated glucose intolerance and enhanced insulin sensitivity after oral administration in mice, but also inhibited free fatty acid-induced steatosis and oxidative stress in QP extract-treated primary mouse hepatocytes. Furthermore, we profiled the absorbed components in the serum of mice by UHPLC-Orbitrap MS after oral gavage of QP extracts, and a total of fifteen flavonoid components were identified. By integrating the results of network pharmacology, molecular docking and transcriptomic sequencing, we analyzed the mechanism of action of QP extracts and found that the PGC-1α-PPARα axis and fatty acid oxidation pathway were highly enriched. QP treatment increased fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and the protein expression of p-AMPK, PGC-1α and PPARα, along with increased mRNA expression of key CYP450 enzymes involved in FAO. Pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or PPARα partially abrogated these effects. Therefore, our results highlight QP's potential as a functional food for the management of MASLD.

articles.title: Effects of repetitive pretreatment with isothiocyanates on the stress resistance capacity of RGM1 cells.
articles.abstract: In this study, we investigated the effects of repeated isothiocyanate (ITC) pretreatment on cytotoxicity, cytoprotective gene expression, and chromatin accessibility in rat gastric epithelial RGM1 cells. Cells were pretreated with ITCs at low concentrations (0-2 µM) four times at 48 h intervals, followed by exposure to higher concentrations of ITCs. Repeated benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC) pretreatment significantly attenuated BITC-induced cytotoxicity compared with untreated controls. Moreover, repeated BITC pretreatment (2 µM) markedly increased the mRNA expression levels of cytoprotective genes, including glutathione S-transferase π and heat shock protein 27. Repeated BITC pretreatment also conferred cross-tolerance to low-pH and heat stress conditions. In addition, BITC treatment significantly upregulated the expression of several carbonic anhydrase isoforms associated with intracellular pH homeostasis. A DNase I-based chromatin accessibility assay revealed that repeated BITC pretreatment promoted euchromatin formation at the HO-1 gene locus. Furthermore, euchromatin formation in cytoprotective gene regions was also induced under various stress conditions. These findings suggest that repeated exposure to BITC enhances cellular stress tolerance through the induction of cytoprotective genes and stress-dependent chromatin remodeling.

articles.title: The Effects of Training Monotony on Sway Velocity in Elite Division I Women's Basketball Players Across 2 Seasons.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.abstract: Hudy, A, Shah, J, Kraemer, WJ, Burland, JP, Glaviano, NR, Morgan, K, Wilson, J, Huggins, RA, and Casa, DJ. The effects of training monotony on sway velocity in elite Division I women's basketball players across two seasons. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026- This study examined the relationship between training monotony and sway velocity (SV), an indicator of neuromuscular control, in elite NCAA Division I women's basketball players across 2 competitive seasons. Ten high-impact athletes (21 ± 2 years) were monitored with triaxial accelerometers to quantify external load using PlayerLoad, and monotony was calculated as the weekly mean load divided by its standard deviation. SV was assessed using single-leg balance tests on a force plate at regular intervals throughout the season. Data were analyzed across seasonal phases and time periods using descriptive statistics, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and linear mixed-effects models accounting for repeated measures ( p ≤ 0.05). Monotony increased significantly during the early preseason period before stabilizing across the competitive season, while SV remained relatively stable over time. A significant reduction in SV was observed in Year 2 compared with Year 1; however, no significant association was found between monotony and SV. These findings suggest that although training monotony follows expected temporal patterns, SV may represent a relatively stable neuromuscular characteristic under typical training conditions and may be less sensitive to weekly workload fluctuations. For strength and conditioning practitioners, monitoring monotony may help identify periods of increased training stress, while SV may serve as an individual baseline metric to detect meaningful deviations in neuromuscular function.

articles.title: Walnut consumption improves mood and is associated with increased urinary excretion of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid and urolithins in a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract: Background & aims: Walnuts are nutrient-dense foods rich in bioactive compounds that may support mental health. However, evidence linking walnut consumption to mood regulation and to changes in urinary metabolites potentially associated with these effects in humans remains limited. This randomized crossover trial (RCT) aimed to evaluate the effects of an 8-week walnut (Juglans regia) intervention on mood states in young adults and to explore the potential mechanistic links through urinary serotonin metabolite (5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid, 5-HIAA), cortisol, and urolithins. Methods: In this 18-week open-label RCT, 31 healthy young adults (mean age 24.0 ± 4.2 years; 90.3% female) consumed 40 g per day of walnuts for 8 weeks (intervention) and followed a nut-free control period of equal length, separated by a 2-week washout. Mood states, perceived stress, well-being, and trait food cravings were assessed using validated questionnaires. Urinary concentrations of 5-HIAA and cortisol were quantified via ELISA and normalized to creatinine. Walnut-derived urolithins were determined in urine samples as biomarkers of intake by HPLC-QTOF-MS. Linear mixed-effects models were used to test differences in outcome variables between intervention and control conditions, and repeated-measures correlations were performed to assess within-individual associations between the outcome variables. Results: Compared to the control condition, the 8-week walnut intervention significantly reduced total mood disturbance scores (-4.85 points, p = 0.030). In addition, the walnut intervention significantly increased urinary 5-HIAA levels, with no changes in urinary cortisol. Increases in urinary 5-HIAA were significantly associated with reductions in fatigue (r = -0.392, p = 0.031) and total mood disturbance (r = -0.362, p = 0.049). Urinary levels of urolithins significantly increased during the intervention and were strongly correlated with concurrent changes in urinary 5-HIAA (r = 0.537 and r = 0.634, respectively). Conclusions: Daily walnut consumption improved total mood disturbance scores in young adults. These findings were accompanied by increased urinary 5-HIAA and urolithin levels. The concurrent changes in these urinary metabolites may reflect dietary, microbial, or peripheral metabolic responses to walnut consumption; however, mechanistic pathways warrant further investigation. These findings highlight the relevance of whole-food strategies in nutritional approaches to mental health.

articles.title: Whole egg consumption effects on vitamin D and carotenoids bioavailability in pre- and post-menopausal females: a randomized crossover controlled feeding trial.
articles.abstract: Background & aims: Whole egg (WE) is a good source of vitamin D and carotenoids but their effects on concurrent bioavailability from a co-consumed meal and differences by menopausal status, remain unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the effects of co-consuming WE with vitamin D and carotenoids-rich foods on their absorption in pre- and post-menopausal females. Methods: Nine pre-menopausal and 8 post-menopausal females completed 8 day trials (7 day controlled diet plus test day) separated by a 3-week washout. Participants consumed a cooked vegetable meal (primary source of vitamin D and carotenoids) with no egg (control) or 100 g of cooked WE (CWE). The meal provided 27 mg of carotenoids and 600 IU of vitamin D (mainly vitamin D2 from fortified mushrooms) and eggs provided ∼0.5 mg of carotenoids and 80 IU of vitamin D3. Blood was collected hourly for 10 hours and triacylglycerol-rich lipoprotein fractions (TRL) were isolated. Vitamin D metabolites and carotenoids in TRL were analyzed and the composite areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated. Results: Carotenoids AUC0-10 h in TRL was significantly higher for the CWE than control in both pre-menopausal (104.2 ± 12.4 vs. 29.2 ± 12.4 ng mL-1 × 10 h; p < 0.001) and post-menopausal females (62.7 ± 12.4 vs. 10.1 ± 12.4 ng mL-1 × 10 h; p = 0.003). 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 AUC0-10 h in TRL was also higher with CWE than for the control in the pre-menopausal (1.34 ± 0.55 vs. 0.53 ± 0.55 ng mL-1 × 10 h; p = 0.182) and significantly higher in the post-menopausal (2.70 ± 0.59 vs. 1.03 ± 0.59 ng mL-1 × 10 h; p = 0.015) females. Vitamin D2/D3 and 25-hydroxyvitamin D2 were undetectable. Menopausal status did not affect these postprandial responses. Conclusion: Co-consuming WE with a cooked vegetable meal effectively increased the absorption of carotenoids across life stages but not for vitamin D2 from a cooked vegetable meal. Trial registration: NCT02679794.

articles.title: Dissociable cortical-hippocampal dopamine dynamics support memory-guided behavior.
articles.abstract: Flexible behavior depends on neural mechanisms that integrate memory with ongoing motivational demands. Studies have revealed dopamine (DA) to have an essential role in mediating memory, behavioral flexibility, and decision-making, yet the dopaminergic contributions within prefrontal-hippocampal circuits remain poorly defined. To address this, we simultaneously monitored DA release and population calcium activity in the prelimbic cortex (PL) and ventral CA1 (vCA1) using genetically encoded sensors during threat learning, reward learning, and an approach-avoidance conflict task. Both regions exhibited distinct dopaminergic and neural responses to the cues that predicted shock or reward and to the respective behaviors that each cue elicited. DA signals in the PL, but not vCA1, tracked the latency of avoidance behavior on a trial-by-trial scale and emerged rapidly as animals acquired the threat association. By contrast, vCA1 DA showed modulation by latency to avoid at an individual level. Together, PL and vCA1 DA reorganized when animals were forced to choose between approach and avoidance. This reorganization reflects early during the trial whether animals will seek reward and later whether the animals will stay on the platform during the final epochs of conflict trials. These results demonstrate complementary dopaminergic functions in PL and vCA1 and reveal how their dynamics reshape during memory-guided actions under competing motivational pressures.

articles.title: Glucomannan and resistant starch in obesity management: a systematic review of satiety, gut fermentation, and weight-related and metabolic outcomes.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a growing global health challenge associated with dysregulated appetite, impaired gut function, and metabolic disorders. Glucomannan and resistant starch are functional dietary fibers that may influence obesity-related pathways through distinct but interconnected mechanisms. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence regarding their effects on satiety and appetite regulation, gut fermentation and microbiota-related pathways, and weight-related and metabolic outcomes. A systematic search of Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library was conducted without publication-date restrictions, with the final search performed on 25 August 2026. Eligible randomized and crossover trials, non-randomized intervention studies, and animal studies investigating glucomannan, resistant starch, or relevant formulations were included when they reported predefined obesity-related outcomes. Twenty studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising six randomized or crossover trials, three non-randomized intervention studies, and eleven animal studies. Several studies reported improvements in satiety, hunger, food or energy intake, body weight, adiposity, or metabolic outcomes, although findings were heterogeneous across interventions, populations, and study designs. Glucomannan-containing interventions were generally associated with viscosity-related satiety effects, whereas resistant starch was more frequently associated with gut fermentation, microbiota modulation, and short-chain fatty acid production. Mechanistic and metabolic evidence was predominantly derived from animal studies, and several human studies reported null findings. Overall, the findings suggest potential complementarity between glucomannan and resistant starch at the mechanistic level, but direct evidence supporting synergistic effects of their combined use remains limited.

articles.title: Ketamine attenuates habenula activity in response to aversive outcomes during Pavlovian learning.
articles.abstract: Ketamine is an NMDA receptor antagonist with rapid antidepressant properties when administered at a subanesthetic dose. Preclinical models indicate that a direct injection of ketamine into the lateral habenula (Hb), a small midbrain structure with an evolutionarily preserved role in aversive learning across mammals, can rapidly relieve depression-like behavior. However, there is limited evidence to explain how ketamine acts on the function of the human Hb. In a translational computational neuroscience study, 70 healthy adult volunteers were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive ketamine (0.5 mg/kg) or placebo (NaCl 0.9%). We used an aversive Pavlovian conditioning paradigm combined with 7-tesla functional neuroimaging to show that ketamine attenuates Hb response during aversive stimuli expectations and outcomes 24 h post-infusion. Furthermore, we present preliminary evidence suggesting that when aversive learning occurs after ketamine infusion, reduced Hb activity during the learning process may lead to downstream effects that diminish the aversive impact of negative affective memories. These findings provide translational support for ketamine's modulation of aversive learning and Hb activity and help to refine mechanistic models of its rapid antidepressant effect.

articles.title: Association of dietary choline intake with cognitive decline and related outcomes: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract: Cognitive decline is a growing global public health concern in aging populations, with genetic and dietary factors contributing to individual differences in cognitive trajectories. Dietary choline, as a precursor of acetylcholine and a key regulator of methylation and membrane integrity, may protect cognitive function. However, epidemiological evidence remains inconsistent, and the optimal intake for neuroprotection remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between dietary choline intake and cognitive decline and related outcomes, and a dose-response meta-analysis was performed. Eligible studies reporting risk estimates for cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or related outcomes according to dietary choline intake were included. Study characteristics and outcomes were extracted. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using a random-effects model and dose-response associations were assessed using a two-stage generalized least-squares framework. Eleven articles were included, of which nine independent cohorts involving 218 378 participants contributed to the primary meta-analysis. Higher dietary choline intake was significantly associated with a lower risk of adverse cognitive outcomes (pooled OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.63-0.92) and cognitive impairment/decline (pooled OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.95). A significant inverse association was also observed for Alzheimer's disease (AD) (pooled OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.55-0.99), whereas the association with dementia was not statistically significant. Dose-response analyses revealed significant nonlinear associations for adverse cognitive outcomes and cognitive impairment/decline, with the lowest risk observed at approximately 350-400 mg day-1 of dietary choline intake. Dietary choline intake was associated with lower risks of adverse cognitive outcomes, cognitive impairment/decline, and AD, with the lowest risks observed at moderate intake levels. These findings highlight the potential importance of adequate choline intake for cognitive health.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of subcutaneous efgartigimod with prednisone in moderate-to-severe pemphigus (ADDRESS): a global, phase III, randomised controlled, double-blind trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) and pemphigus foliaceus (PF) are rare, chronic, potentially life-threatening, immunoglobulin (Ig)G-mediated, autoimmune skin and/or mucosal blistering diseases. Efgartigimod, a human IgG1 antibody Fc fragment, blocks the neonatal Fc receptor, decreasing IgG recycling and reducing both healthy and pathogenic IgG autoantibody levels.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the efficacy, safety and impact of subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 (co-formulated with recombinant human hyaluronidase PH20) in conjunction with prednisone in the treatment of pemphigus.

METHODS: Adult participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing moderate-to-severe pemphigus were recruited in this phase III, prospective, multicentre, randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled study (NCT04598451). Participants were randomised (2 : 1) to weekly subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 or placebo. Subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 2000 mg was administered on days 1 and 8, followed by 1000 mg weekly until complete remission on minimal prednisone therapy (CRmin) (≤ 10 mg daily). All participants received concomitant prednisone starting at 0.5 mg kg-1 daily. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with PV who achieved CRmin by week 30, while receiving minimal prednisone, for ≥ 8 weeks. Pharmacodynamics and safety were also assessed.

RESULTS: Overall, 222 participants (PV: n = 190; PF: n = 32) were randomised (subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20: n = 147; placebo: n = 75). The proportions of participants with PV achieving CRmin within 30 weeks were comparable between the subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 and placebo groups, with no statistically significant difference observed [44/124 (35.5%) vs. 20/66 (30.3%); P = 0.60; odds ratio 1.19 (95% confidence interval 0.60-2.41)]. Total prednisone consumption over time was comparable between groups. Subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 resulted in rapid reductions from baseline in total IgG and anti--desmoglein-1 and anti-desmoglein-3 autoantibody levels, but these did not translate to improvements in Pemphigus Disease Area Index scores. The rates of adverse events (AEs) in the subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 and placebo groups were 89.1% (n = 131/147) and 76.0% (n = 57/75), respectively; most were mild to moderate [serious AEs: 12.2% (n = 18/147) and 13.3% (n = 10/75), respectively]. No deaths occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: Subcutaneous efgartigimod PH20 in combination with systemic corticosteroids did not demonstrate clinical benefit over systemic corticosteroids alone in patients with moderate-to-severe pemphigus at 30 weeks, but it was well tolerated in this patient population.

articles.title: Evidence on information, access frictions, and experience in public healthcare use in rural Bangladesh: a cluster-randomized field experiment.
articles.abstract: In rural Bangladesh, many households continue to rely on private and informal providers even when public healthcare options are available at low or zero monetary cost. This paper studies whether the barrier is mainly misinformation, access frictions, or trust and uncertainty about public care. A cluster-randomized field experiment was conducted with 2320 households across 580 neighborhoods and three sequential treatment arms. Information provision sharply increases awareness of public care options but has limited effects on actual utilization. In contrast, encouraging a one-time experience with public care produces significant increases in public uptake, substitution away from informal providers, and meaningful reductions in out-of-pocket spending, especially on medicines. Households induced to use public care reduced total health spending by ∼601 Bangladeshi taka (USD 5.46 at 2023 exchange rate; 32% of the control group mean) relative to nonusers (95% CI 373-829 taka; P < 0.001), with most of the reduction driven by lower medicine expenditure. The findings suggest that improving beliefs alone is insufficient and that lowering uncertainty through a first successful experience is a key lever for shifting healthcare demand toward public options.

articles.title: Rational Design of a Synthetic Galliphore for the Diagnostic Nuclear Imaging and Treatment of Bacterial Infections.
articles.abstract: We introduce a solid-phase synthesis platform for the rapid, modular, and scalable synthesis of the synthetic metallophore KO-NH2, which is readily recognized by bacterial siderophore transporters, but has optimized affinity for Ga3+ over Fe3+. Four synthetic protochelin (PC) analogues, KK-COOH, KO-NH2, KO-COOH, and OK-COOH were constructed. Growth recovery, radioactive uptake, and covalent photocrosslinker studies in Escherichia coli identified CirA and Fiu as the dominant outer membrane transport proteins capable of binding KO-NH2-linked, bifunctional constructs. Computational studies further supported that the structural framework of PC can be effectively mimicked by KO or OK peptides. Thermodynamic stability studies revealed an atypical inversion of thermodynamic stability trends, with logKGaL of 39.9 and a logKFeL of 36, demonstrating improved stability with Ga3+. Studies in naïve mice with 68Ga-labeled derivatives identify the lead [68Ga][Ga(KO-NH2)]3-, which remained intact in vivo and demonstrated selective, enhanced uptake in an E. coli soft tissue model of infection (1.28 % ID/g, with a 3:1 ratio of infected to inflamed/normal muscle tissue). Linkage of KO-NH2 to the antibiotic ampicillin produces an efficacious antibiotic, which supersedes the potency of the parent antibiotic ampicillin 4-fold (MIC98 = 1.9 µM) effectively treats a soft tissue infection of ampicillin-resistant E. coli.

articles.title: Self-Amplifying AIE Probe for HClO-Activatable Imaging and Antioxidative/Anti-Inflammatory Therapy of Thoracic Aortic Dissection.
articles.abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular disease, yet its accurate diagnosis and effective treatment remain challenging due to poor imaging contrast and insufficient specificity. Leveraging the overexpressed reactive oxygen species (ROS) in TAD, we reported a hypochlorous acid (HClO)-activatable molecular probe DT-PZ. It enables two-stage self-amplifying fluorescence imaging (chemical activation and then physical aggregation) and light-independent therapy on a single chemical entity. The probe initially exhibits quenched fluorescence via photoinduced electron transfer (PET). Two pathways can turn on the fluorescence via chemical activation: (1) oxidation by HClO blocks PET and turns on the emission; (2) photo-triggered radicals generation of HClO (via chloride ions or myeloperoxidase) to activate neighboring probes, creating self-amplifying fluorescence. Upon accumulation at the lesion site, the physical aggregation caused by the aggregation-induced emission effect further amplifies the fluorescence signals. This two-stage fluorescence amplification mechanism enables TAD visualization within 2 min in vivo. For therapy, the phenothiazine scavenges excess ROS during non-illuminated periods, down-regulates the NF-κB/P65 signal pathway, and up-regulates eNOS and P-Akt expressions, protecting endothelial homeostasis and then improving murine survival from 50% to 90%. Collectively, DT-PZ synergizes self-amplifying fluorescence imaging with light-independent antioxidation/anti-inflammatory therapy, holding great promise for managing deep-seated cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Leveraging Protein Dynamics for Selective Inhibition of Threonyl-tRNA Synthetase by Obafluorin Analogs.
articles.abstract: The widespread emergence of antibiotic resistance necessitates the development of novel agents with unique mechanisms of action. Obafluorin (OB), a natural β-lactone antibiotic, is a covalent inhibitor of threonyl-tRNA synthetase (ThrRS), but the high conservation of the active site between prokaryote and eukaryote ThrRSs results in minimal selectivity, hindering the therapeutic potential of OB. Here, we report a structure dynamics-based design strategy that transforms OB into a selective antibacterial agent. OB inhibits human and bacterial ThrRSs with nearly equal potency due to identical binding modes. The nitrophenyl moiety of OB is proposed as a 'kinetic sensor' that discriminates between sensitive and resistant ThrRS paralogs. Guided by this insight, we designed a series of OB analogs through rational modification of this moiety. Among them, OB-D4 bearing a para-methoxyphenyl group in place of the nitrophenyl group, exhibited a 241-fold selectivity for bacterial over human ThrRS, along with a markedly improved safety profile with minimal cytotoxicity. In a murine skin infection model, OB-D4 effectively eradicated pathogens, resolving inflammation, and promoting wound healing. Together, this work establishes a 'kinetic sensor' strategy for achieving species selectivity, turning a fundamental challenge in drug discovery-high active-site conservation-into an exploitable opportunity based on dynamic differences.

articles.title: Co-Assembled Mirror-Image DNA Nanostructure for Effective Alleviation of Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: The high demand for acute kidney injury (AKI) therapy calls for the development of new therapeutics for renal management. Oxidative stress, coupled with excessive inflammation, is the main pathological mechanism for AKI. Specifically, complement component 5a (C5a) exacerbates the vicious cycle between oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Herein, we developed a cascade-functioning mirror-image DNA nanostructure, L-DNA tetrahedron (LDT), for sequentially blocking the extracellular complement C5a to alleviate inflammation and eliminating intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) to inhibit oxidative stress. A C5a-neutralizing mirror-image aptamer (LA) was incorporated into LDT via a ROS-sensitive linker (thioketal, i.e., TK bond), which enabled the release of LA in the inflammatory microenvironment to block C5a. LA-conjugated LDT (LDT-LA) exhibited preferential renal uptake and enhanced renal retention compared with its counterpart made of D-nucleic acids and provided effective treatment in ischemia-reperfusion (I/R)-, cisplatin-, and glycerol-induced AKI mouse models. Meanwhile, LDT-LA exhibits excellent biocompatibility, making it a promising candidate for AKI therapy. The biostable, cascade-functioning LDT-LA could act as a multifunctional platform for the treatment of other diseases by conjugating with appropriate functional groups.

articles.title: CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.
articles.abstract: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based diagnostic systems have emerged as powerful platforms for sensitive nucleic acid detection, yet their clinical reliability is frequently constrained by off-target activation and insufficient discrimination of closely related sequences. This review synthesizes current advances aimed at enhancing the specificity of CRISPR diagnostics, with particular emphasis on the pivotal role of CRISPR RNA (crRNA) engineering. We detail how structural determinants of crRNA, including spacer length optimization, intentional mismatch design, secondary-structure modulation, chemical modification, strand-displacement gating, and synergistic design frameworks, govern CRISPR-mediated target recognition and define the energetic and kinetic thresholds for accurate cleavage. Key engineering strategies encompassing computational prediction and modeling, high-throughput screening, and hybrid guide architectures are systematically examined for their capacity to elevate single-nucleotide discrimination, stabilize reaction performance, and enable robust multiplexed detection for pathogen profiling and mutation identification. Despite rapid progress, outstanding challenges persist, including interference from complex clinical matrices, lack of unified evaluation standards, and scalability barriers that hinder clinical translation. Addressing these limitations through integrated crRNA design, system-level optimization, and standardized benchmarking will be essential for realizing the promise of CRISPR diagnostics. Ultimately, these advances are poised to support ultrasensitive, highly specific, and portable point-of-care testing, thereby accelerating precision medicine and strengthening infectious disease surveillance and management.

articles.title: A process evaluation of community-led distribution of HIV self-testing kits in rural communities in Zimbabwe.
articles.abstract: Community-led distribution of HIV self-test (HIVST) kits has potential to combine the benefits of community-based HIV testing with the strengths of community-led interventions. We report the process evaluation from the community-led arm of a cluster-randomized trial in rural Zimbabwe comparing community-led versus community-based HIVST distribution where distributors were paid. Twenty communities were supported to design HIVST distribution models that suited their context. We conducted community meetings where we introduced community-led HIVST, including messages on the benefits of viral load suppression (Undetectable = Untransmissible; 'U = U'). Communities determined how, and by whom, distribution would be done. Communities implemented their distribution model over 4-6 weeks. We conducted in-depth interviews with community members (n = 20), distributors (n = 20), and health workers (n = 20) as well as 12 focus group discussions (n = 91) with community members. We triangulated findings with participant observations during community meetings and implementation and descriptively analysed programme data on HIVST distribution. Qualitative data were analysed thematically. Participant observations found communities collaboratively developed and embraced HIVST distribution, demonstrating strong enthusiasm for participation. Messaging on U = U was met with interest and surprise, as many community members were unaware of this information, and became a key motivator for HIVST implementation and uptake. Across communities, 348 distributors distributed 27 812 kits door-to-door and/or from their homes or other community venues. Communities where model development was led by local leaders-rather than collective processes-expressed lower level of satisfaction and had slow implementation. Health workers supported HIVST distribution well, with opportunities for improvement noted. While distributors felt proud to deliver HIVST, many experienced logistical burdens and need for material support from the programme and community. Communities designed HIVST delivery models that were acceptable and feasible; however, efforts to make community-led models sustainable are critical. Delivering messages on U = U should continue to be prioritized and embedded within community-based HIVST distribution models.

articles.title: Trends in keratinocyte cancers in England, 2013-22: basal cell carcinoma incidence, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma incidence and nonmelanoma skin cancer mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), collectively termed keratinocyte cancers (KCs), are the most common cancers in White populations, and their incidence is increasing globally. KCs are substantially under-reported, and high-quality long-term data on patient demographics, incidence and mortality trends remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients with KCs, and to assess incidence and mortality trends in England between 2013 and 2022.

METHODS: We analysed all new KCs diagnosed in England from 2013 to 2022 using data from the National Disease Registration Service. Tumours were counted using per patient per annum (PPPA) methodology, whereby each individual could contribute one BCC and one cSCC per year. European age-standardized incidence rates (EASRs) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population, while age-specific incidence rates (ASIRs) were calculated using Office for National Statistics mid-year population estimates for the corresponding age group. Joinpoint regression was used to calculate annual percentage change (APC) and assess trends in EASRs, ASIRs and ASMRs by sex and age per 100 000 person-years (PYs).

RESULTS: Compared with the first-all-time registration method, the PPPA approach identified 67% more BCCs and 42% more cSCCs over the study period. In 2022, PPPA EASRs were 295 per 100 000 PYs for BCC and 102 per 100 000 PYs for cSCC. BCC EASRs increased initially before stabilizing from 2015 [APC -0.2%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.8 to 0.3]. In contrast, cSCC EASRs increased rapidly from 2013 to 2015 (from 79 to 89 per 100 000 PY; APC 6.1%) and continued to increase between 2015 and 2019 (from 89 to 97 per 100 000 PY; APC 2.3%). The nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) ASMR increased significantly from 2013 (APC 4.0%, 95% CI 2.5-5.7), with rates rising approximately twice as fast in male individuals (APC 4.4%, 95% CI 2.4-7.1) compared with female individuals (APC 2.2, 95% CI 0.3-4.6). For cSCC, ASIRs plateaued in middle age from 2015 onwards but continued to increase in younger (< 60 years) and older (≥ 80 years) individuals.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight the importance of accurate tumour counting methods for healthcare planning. The incidence of cSCC continues to rise alongside increasing NMSC mortality, underscoring the need for strengthened prevention strategies, early diagnosis and timely access to quality healthcare.

articles.title: Evaluating the impact of conditional micro-incentives on linkage to HIV care in rural South Africa: results from the Home-Based Intervention to Test and Start (HITS) trial.
articles.abstract: Timely linkage from HIV diagnosis to care is critical for effective treatment and epidemic control. We evaluated the effectiveness of conditional micro-incentives on linkage to HIV care in the Home-Based Intervention to Test and Start (HITS) trial, a real-world implementation trial in rural South Africa. Of 45 communities in uMkhanyakude, KwaZulu-Natal, 16 were randomized to micro-incentive arms offering food vouchers (R50 [US$3]) conditional on completing home-based HIV counseling and testing (HBHCT) and linkage to care within 6 weeks, and 29 to non-incentive arms. All individuals were eligible for HBHCT, enrolled between February and December 2018, and followed for 1 year. The primary outcome was linkage to care at 1 year among men; secondary outcomes included linkage within the 6-week voucher eligibility period among men and women, and at 1 year among women. Intention-to-treat analyses were performed using Poisson regression adjusted for study arms. Among 13 894 men and 19 884 women eligible for the study (aged ≥15 years), home-based testing uptake was 21% (n = 2867) and 29% (n = 5795), yielding 122 (4.3%) and 375 (6.5%) new diagnoses, respectively. Overall, micro-incentives nearly doubled HIV-positive diagnoses. Among men, micro-incentives did not increase linkage to care within the 6-week voucher eligibility period (risk ratio [RR] = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.51-1.21) or at 1 year (RR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.86-1.35). Among women, micro-incentives increased linkage to care within 6 weeks by 51% (RR = 1.51; 95% CI: 1.03-2.21), with no residual impact at 1 year (RR = 1.07, 95% CI: 0.91-1.26). In a hyperendemic rural African setting, once-off micro-incentives can substantially increase early linkage to HIV care among women during the incentive eligibility period but are inadequate to significantly improve care engagement among men. Trial Registration  ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03757104.

articles.title: Non-antibiotic interventions to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in women: overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
articles.journal: The British journal of general practice : the journal of the Royal College of General Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), that is, ≥2 urinary tract infections (UTIs) in the past 6 months or ≥3 in the past 12 months, are common, have a substantial impact on quality of life, and cause major antibiotic use.

AIM: To identify non-antibiotic interventions for prevention of rUTIs that have been assessed in systematic reviews, exploring their effectiveness, acceptability, and adherence.

DESIGN AND SETTING: An overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on non-pharmaceutical and pharmaceutical (non-antibiotic) interventions for preventing rUTIs in women.

METHOD: Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Google Scholar, and Cochrane from January 2014 to May 2025 were searched for systematic reviews of RCTs assessing the effectiveness of community-based non-antibiotic interventions for preventing UTI in women aged ≥16 years with rUTIs. Studies in intensive care units, relating to people with indwelling catheters, or comparing different oral antibiotic regimens were excluded. There were no limitations regarding outcome measures or language.

RESULTS: In total, 27 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria evaluating probiotics (n = 9), D-mannose (n = 7), vaginal oestrogen (n = 7), cranberry (n = 6), methenamine hippurate (n = 3), herbal medicine (n = 3), increased fluid intake (n = 2), systemic oestrogen (n = 4), acupuncture (n = 2), and vaccines (n = 2). Eight examined combination strategies. Cranberry and methenamine hippurate use are supported by systematic reviews, as is vaginal oestrogen among postmenopausal women, although questions remain around dose, duration, and treatment adherence. Reviews of probiotics, D-mannose, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and vaccines concluded that stronger evidence is needed. Increased fluid intake benefits women with low intake, but further research is needed on optimal intake. There was little information on treatment adherence or acceptability for many interventions.

CONCLUSION: For effective interventions, questions remain about promoting adherence (vaginal oestrogen), or optimal preparation (cranberry), or duration (methenamine). For other interventions a stronger evidence base is needed.

articles.title: Equity and impact of social prescribing in type 2 diabetes prevention: cross-sectional and cohort study using national primary care data.
articles.journal: The British journal of general practice : the journal of the Royal College of General Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social prescribing has expanded rapidly in English primary care since 2019 to support the prevention and management of long-term conditions. However, evidence on its equity of access and effectiveness for type 2 diabetes (T2D) prevention is limited.

AIM: To examine the reach, equity of access, and potential impact of social prescribing on T2D prevention among adults at high risk.

DESIGN AND SETTING: Observational study using routinely collected data from the Oxford-RCGP Research and Surveillance Centre, including >1800 general practices in England (January 2019 to November 2023).

METHOD: Cross-sectional analyses using multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with social prescribing referral among adults at high risk of T2D. Cohort analyses estimated the association between social prescribing referral and incident T2D, adjusting for baseline covariates. Calendar-period-stratified Cox models were used to capture programme roll-out and COVID-19 changes. Exploratory time-since-index analyses tested if effects varied over time.

RESULTS: Among 2 326 400 adults at high-risk of T2D, 271 582 (11.7%) developed T2D over a median 3.7 years (interquartile range [IQR] 1.44-4.83). Referrals to social prescribing increased 9.5-fold from 0.3% (n = 3897/1 479 172) in 2019-2020 to 2.5% (n = 47 883/1 917 187) in January-November 2023, and were more common among women (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.42, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.40 to 1.43), those living in more deprived areas (aOR 1.89, 95% CI = 1.86 to 1.93), current smokers (aOR 1.71, 95% CI = 1.68 to 1.73), people with obesity (aOR 1.19, 95% CI = 1.17 to 1.21), depression/anxiety (aOR 2.52, 95% CI = 2.49 to 2.54), and multimorbidity (aOR 1.45, 95% CI = 1.43 to 1.47). By calendar year, social prescribing was associated with an increased risk of T2D in 2019 (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.67, 95% CI = 1.20 to 2.32) but became protective by 2023 (aHR 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79 to 0.89). By follow-up, social prescribing was associated with an increased risk of T2D within 0-2 years post-referral (aHR 1.09, 95% CI = 1.04 to 1.15) but was protective after ≥3 years (aHR 0.88, 95% CI = 0.80 to 0.97).

CONCLUSION: Social prescribing reached those with greater health and social need. The protective association against T2D emerged as services matured post-COVID-19 and with longer follow-up, potentially reflecting cumulative engagement, although activity data were unavailable.

articles.title: Occult Malignancy Presenting as Pericardial Effusion: The Diagnostic Contribution of Pericardial Fluid Cytology.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pericardial effusion may occur in patients with established cancer but may also represent the first manifestation of an occult malignancy. This study evaluated the diagnostic contribution of pericardial fluid cytology and pathological assessment according to previous oncological status, with particular emphasis on previously unrecognized malignancy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients hospitalized with pericardial disease between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary cardiovascular center. The final cohort comprised 234 clinical episodes in 209 patients. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, procedural, cytological, and histopathological data were analyzed in relation to previous oncological status and malignant pericardial involvement. Results: Pathological assessment was available in 95/234 episodes (40.6%), with neoplastic involvement identified in 21/95 (22.1%). Neoplastic findings occurred in 13/33 (39.4%) evaluable episodes with known malignancy and 8/62 (12.9%) without a previous cancer diagnosis (odds ratio, 4.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.59-12.11; p = 0.004). Conversely, 20/33 (60.6%) evaluable episodes in patients with known cancer showed no neoplastic involvement. In all eight patients without previously known malignancy, pericardial fluid cytology provided the first pathological evidence of cancer; six (75%) had findings suggestive of a pulmonary origin. All presented with large effusions and hemodynamic compromise. Conclusions: Pericardial pathological assessment provides diagnostic information beyond previous oncological status. It can distinguish malignant from non-neoplastic pericardial involvement in patients with established cancer while also revealing occult malignancy when pericardial disease is its first presentation.

articles.title: Predictive performance of bleeding risk scores for extended anticoagulation in pulmonary embolism: Insights from the CURES-2 registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding risk assessment is critical at the 3-month decision point for extended anticoagulation in patients with pulmonary embolism (PE), yet it remains unclear which existing bleeding risk score best predicts bleeding during the extended phase.

METHODS: Based on the CURES cohort, this study enrolled patients with PE undergoing extended-phase anticoagulation, which was defined as regular anticoagulant therapy for ≥90 days. We compared the performance of 6 bleeding risk scores (PE-SARD, BACS, Kuijer, RIETE, HAS-BLED, and VTE-BLEED) in predicting major bleeding (MB) events within 1 year during the extended phase. The predictive performance was assessed through time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 4896 patients with acute PE receiving extended-phase anticoagulation were included in the study, among whom 18 patients (0.4%) experienced major bleeding. Compared with the other 5 bleeding scores, VTE-BLEED exhibited the highest predictive accuracy (time-dependent AUC = 0.72; 95% CI: 0.63-0.81), accompanied by superior overall calibration (Brier score = 0.0039). In subgroup analyses by anticoagulant type, VTE-BLEED maintained favorable robustness with AUCs exceeding 0.70 for patients treated with either VKAs or DOACs.

CONCLUSIONS: VTE-BLEED offers potential utility for guiding risk-stratified management of MB during extended anticoagulation in patients with PE, particularly at the 3-month reassessment point. Nonetheless, the limited number of MB events and follow-up attrition necessitate cautious interpretation and further validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Advances in physiotherapy for chronic low-back pain: a level I systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of orthopaedics and traumatology : official journal of the Italian Society of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-pharmacologic management of chronic low back pain (cLBP) should be considered the first-line treatment. However, consensus guidelines and internationally accepted recommendations on the therapeutic algorithm are missing. The present level I systematic review presents a qualitative analysis of advancements in physiotherapy over the past decades to discuss the role of physical and rehabilitation medicine in the management of cLBP.

METHODS: In August 2025, the following databases were accessed: PubMed, Web of Science and Embase. All randomised controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of physiotherapy programs in patients with cLBP were assessed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) criteria. The data extraction and risk-of-bias evaluation were performed independently by two authors.

RESULTS: Data from 150 randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (12,773 patients) were collected. The mean symptom duration was 61.2 ± 51.0 months, and the mean follow-up was 4.3 ± 5.9 months. The mean age was 44.5 ± 9.4 years, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 25.8 ± 2.9 kg/m2.

CONCLUSIONS: Managing cLBP is challenging. While individual investigations highlight the efficacy of a specific intervention, most cLBP management strategies share common elements. Combining key elements from various approaches may prove crucial. Although this result is not decisive for treatment, it paves the way for further research that considers a more holistic and multidisciplinary approach.

articles.title: Protection motivation theory and infection-prevention behavior in nursing students across 26 Thai institutions: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While nursing students often possess strong theoretical knowledge of infection control, a gap exists between their understanding and actual preventive practices. This study explored the relationship between knowledge, preventive behaviors, and Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) components among nursing students, using COVID-19 as a representative model.

METHODS: A national cross-sectional study was conducted among 463 nursing students from 26 educational institutions in Thailand. Data were collected via validated online questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation coefficients, and binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: Most participants were female (95.9%) with moderate-to-good knowledge (92.5%) and moderate protection motivation (81.6%). Despite this, 53.1% exhibited poor infection prevention behaviors. First-year students without clinical experience demonstrated significantly poorer behaviors compared to those with clinical exposure (χ 2 = 4.690, df = 1, p = .030). Knowledge did not significantly correlate with behavior (r = 0.026, p = .582). Protection motivation showed a weak correlation (r = 0.181, p = .001). Logistic regression identified perceived fear as the only significant predictor of preventive behavior (OR = 1.049, 95% CI [1.010, 1.089], p = .013).

DISCUSSION: Perceived fear, rather than knowledge, primarily drives preventive adherence. Nursing education should transition beyond knowledge-based curricula to focus on enhancing self-efficacy and positive motivation to mitigate fear and improve compliance with infection control protocols.

articles.title: The Bloomy Rind Sign: A Key MRI Marker in Leptomeningeal Carcinomatosis From Lung Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: A 48 year-old female with a history of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma to the brain presented with acute onset dizziness for 12 hours. The neurological exam was notable for subtle sustained nystagmus on right and upward gaze. A code stroke was called and CT brain revealed no acute intracranial abnormality. MRI brain demonstrated new subtle restriction diffusion and FLAIR hyperintensity along the anterior surface of the brainstem and the middle cerebellar peduncles without evidence of enhancement, concerning for leptomeningeal disease. The remainder of the supratentorial metastases were stable. Lumbar puncture was performed and CSF analysis confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning for Montreal Cognitive Assessment score estimation from gait in community-dwelling older adults: An exploratory evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine learning for gait-based cognitive assessment is rarely benchmarked against a mean-prediction null or checked for explanation stability. We evaluated an explainable multimodal model against this null to estimate Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score from gait. We assessed explanation stability and the contribution of joint-angle trajectories.

METHODS: Fifty community-dwelling older adults walked overground with markerless motion capture, yielding 713 gait cycles. Gait-MoCA associations were assessed with Pearson and partial correlations. Under participant-level five-fold cross-validation, a multimodal long short-term memory (LSTM) model was compared with summary-statistics models, reduced input sets omitting the trajectories, and a null model returning the training-fold mean. Scaling and epoch selection were limited to training data. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were computed per fold.

FINDINGS: Four gait parameters were associated with MoCA after false-discovery-rate correction in unadjusted analyses. All five variability-coefficient correlations with MoCA were positive. Stance-time and double-support-time variability had the strongest covariate-adjusted correlations (partial r=0.38 and 0.34), although no covariate-adjusted correlation survived correction. After correction, no model tested against the null improved significantly. The null-model participant-level root mean square error was 3.03, versus 2.83 for the best model, 2.96 for the multimodal LSTM and 2.92 for the selected demographics-only model. SHAP attributions concentrated at the end of the cycle, 24% in the final frame, but varied between folds.

INTERPRETATION: The variability measures capture between-cycle differences that the single-cycle models did not encode and may guide future model development. Benchmarking against a mean-prediction null and quantifying explanation stability may help identify which inputs merit further evaluation.

articles.title: Pre-stroke functional status and prognosis following mechanical thrombectomy: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionMechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an endovascular approach applicable to large- and medium-vessel occlusion in the context of ischemic stroke (IS), with recanalization rates superior to 80% and favorable clinical outcomes. However, its benefits in patients with pre-existing functional disability remain unclear because these individuals are typically excluded from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). This systematic review and meta-analysis therefore aimed to assess how pre-stroke functional status influences key prognostic outcomes after MT.MethodologyPubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases were searched for English studies published from inception to September 2025. Observational cohorts and RCTs were included if they evaluated patients with IS treated with MT, comparing outcomes (functional outcomes, recanalization, complications, and mortality) between patients with and without pre-stroke disability (PD and NPD, respectively). Disability was mainly defined as a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≥2 or ≥3, and analyses were stratified accordingly. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was explored with Baujat plots and leave-one-out analyses.ResultsThis review included 12 studies comprising 26,444 patients, of whom 2,837 had PD and 23,607 had NPD. Most studies defined PD as a pre-stroke mRS ≥3. Patients with PD had higher rates of diabetes (28.9% vs 18.5%), hypertension (78.9% vs 66.0%), and atrial fibrillation (46.7% vs 29.4%). In contrast, NIHSS, ASPECTS, occlusion site, and time to treatment were similar between groups. Intravenous thrombolysis was less frequently administered in the PD group (33.8% vs 46.9%). No significant difference was observed in favorable functional outcomes between patients with PD and NPD (OR = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.39-1.16). Otherwise, 90-day mortality was higher in PD patients (OR = 2.75; 95% CI: 2.38-3.18). Finally, the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and the rate of successful recanalization did not differ significantly between groups (OR = 1.19; 95% CI: 0.98-1.43, and OR = 0.89; 95% CI: 0.71-1.11, respectively).ConclusionPre-stroke disability was not significantly associated with functional outcomes or reduced recanalization rates after mechanical thrombectomy, although the substantial heterogeneity in functional outcomes warrants cautious interpretation. Pre-stroke disability was associated with higher 90-day mortality, which may be related to a greater baseline comorbidity burden and clinical vulnerability. These results support considering thrombectomy in selected patients with prior disability, while highlighting the need for individualized assessment. High-quality prospective studies are still required to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Asymptomatic Portomesenteric Venous Thrombosis After Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Incidence, Natural History, and Implications for Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery is most often reported in symptomatic patients, leaving its frequency and natural history across the asymptomatic spectrum poorly defined. When encountered incidentally, it frequently prompts anticoagulation, hypercoagulability evaluation, or delays in oncologic treatment, despite limited evidence that intervention alters its course. Using a cohort with routine postoperative imaging, we characterized the incidence, anatomic distribution, risk factors, and clinical course of asymptomatic PMVT.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 799 consecutive patients who underwent CRC surgery between April 2019 and June 2025. All patients underwent standardized abdominal computed tomography (CT) on postoperative day (POD) 6 as part of our institutional clinical pathway for immediate postoperative follow-up. PMVT was defined radiologically, and thrombus location was classified as peripheral intrahepatic branches or main portal/superior mesenteric vein. Management followed a risk-stratified pathway of therapeutic anticoagulation or active surveillance, with radiologic resolution assessed on follow-up CT. Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Asymptomatic PMVT was identified in 33 patients (4.1%), none symptomatic at detection. Thrombi were predominantly confined to the distal intrahepatic branches. In exploratory multivariable analysis, age ≤ 60 years (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.19-5.03, p = 0.015) and POD 5 WBC > 10 × 109/L (OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.16-4.93, p = 0.018) were independently associated with PMVT. Twenty-one patients received anticoagulation and 12 were managed with surveillance alone. Complete radiologic resolution occurred in all 33 patients within one year, including every patient managed without anticoagulation. Furthermore, there were no cases of thrombus extension, portal hypertension, or bowel ischemia.

CONCLUSION: When postoperative imaging is routinely performed, asymptomatic PMVT after CRC surgery is detected in approximately 4% of patients. It is typically confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and follows a uniformly benign self-limiting course, even in patients managed without anticoagulation. These findings argue against reflexive anticoagulation and extensive workup for short-segment, non-occlusive PMVT confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and support an individualized, predominantly conservative approach. We do not advocate routine postoperative CT; rather, surgeons who encounter incidental PMVT can be reassured regarding its favorable prognosis.

articles.title: Animal models for investigating post-stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long-term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant. This review examines PSCI from a neurovascular trafficking perspective, focusing on how laboratory animal models can be used to investigate secretory pathway stress, endolysosomal dysfunction, autophagy-lysosomal flux, extracellular vesicle signaling, blood-brain barrier disruption, glial reactivity, myelin debris clearance, white matter injury, and cognition-relevant behavioral phenotypes. Rodent models of transient or permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion, photothrombotic stroke, embolic stroke, chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, bilateral carotid artery stenosis, and subcortical white-matter injury each reproduce selected components of the human PSCI spectrum. No single model fully captures the temporal, vascular, cellular, and cognitive complexity of human PSCI; therefore, model selection should be driven by the mechanistic question, disease phase, vascular pathology, cellular compartment, cognitive domain, and welfare burden under investigation. The central argument is not that neurovascular trafficking failure is already a proven causal pathway, but that well-designed animal studies can test, refine, or falsify this hypothesis. Future studies should integrate model validity, translational rigor, and welfare refinement through longitudinal cognitive testing, multimodal imaging, cell-specific molecular profiling, extracellular vesicle phenotyping, intervention-based validation, randomization, blinding, sample-size justification, humane endpoints, perioperative care, and transparent reporting.

articles.title: Preventing Agricultural Trauma: What Rural Surgeons Should Know About Injury Patterns and Evidence-Based Mitigation.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMore than half of the global workforce is employed in agriculture-related occupations, and farm-related injuries remain prevalent to rural trauma centers. Agricultural activities have numerous inherent dangers, and this study aimed to describe the characteristics and clinical outcomes of patients with agriculture-related injuries in rural America.MethodsWe performed a retrospective review of adult and pediatric patients with agriculture-related injuries who sought care at a Level II Trauma Center in Wisconsin between 2013 and 2022. Demographic variables as well as primary diagnosis, mechanism of injury, injury severity score (ISS), and hospital length of stay (LOS) were determined. Descriptive statistics were performed, and a P level of .05 was considered statistically significant.ResultsA total of 462 patients met inclusion criteria. The most common mode of injury was blunt force trauma (95%, 441/462). Fifteen percent (67/462) of injuries were animal-related, 34% (157/462) were equipment-related, and 39% (179/462) were fall-related. Median hospital LOS was significantly longer for equipment-related than for animal-related injuries (2 days vs 1 day, respectively; P = .014). Employment status was significantly associated (P = .016) with injury type, with retired individuals experiencing a higher rate of falls (68%, 23/34) when compared with other employment categories (33%-39%).DiscussionThe most common injuries seen were falls and equipment-related, where equipment-related injuries required significantly longer hospital stays than animal-related injuries. Retired individuals experienced a higher rate of falls. These data provide insights into our largely rural population and identified areas of trauma education and prevention efforts regarding equipment safety and fall prevention.

articles.title: Additive Value of Acetylcholine Testing in ANOCA: A US-Based Multicenter FlowLab Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) is an underrecognized cause of angina with non-universal diagnostic techniques and patient management strategies. Among ANOCA testing, vasospasm provocation is not always performed mainly due to differences in institutional availability.

AIMS: Using the FlowLab Study, we quantified vasospasm prevalence among patients with ANOCA at US centers and compared physician decision-making, endotype distribution, and management between sites that did and did not include vasospasm testing in their workup.

METHODS: The FlowLab Study was a prospective, multicenter, US-based study of patients who were referred for coronary angiography and underwent ANOCA testing using the bolus thermodilution method. Presumed diagnosis before cardiac catheterization and final diagnosis after ANOCA testing were compared between participating sites with or without acetylcholine testing availability.

RESULTS: A total of 253 procedures at 14 US sites were included in this study. There were 155 procedures among sites performing spasm provocation testing and 98 procedures among sites not performing spasm provocation testing. Prior to cardiac catheterization, sites with spasm provocation testing were less likely to suspect epicardial coronary artery disease as the cause of angina compared to sites without (27% vs. 59.2%, p < 0.0001). A diagnosis of CMD was made more frequently at sites performing spasm testing compared to sites not performing spasm testing (68% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.0001). Similarly, among 125 patients who underwent spasm provocation testing, diagnostic yield increased from 34.4% with bolus thermodilution alone to 84.8% after the addition of spasm provocation testing (p < 0.001). In these patients, intensification involving calcium channel blockers was more frequent with epicardial (67%) and microvascular spasm (41%) than without spasm (24%, p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary US practice, adding spasm provocation testing to bolus thermodilution more than doubled diagnostic yield and was followed by medication changes directed toward the diagnosed endotype. Differences between sites with and without spasm testing also reflected variation in procedural practice.

articles.title: Diabetes Distress in Caregivers of Young Children With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The American Diabetes Association recommends screening for diabetes distress in individuals with diabetes and their caregivers. We evaluated the clinical utility of the Problem Areas in Diabetes-Parent Revised version (PAID-PR) distress screener in caregivers of young children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and examined associations between diabetes distress, demographic and clinical characteristics, and diabetes technology use.

METHODS: In this prospective survey study, caregivers of children with T1DM aged <8 years completed the PAID-PR during multidisciplinary diabetes clinic visits. The PAID-PR scores and clinical data were collected. Associations between diabetes distress, clinical characteristics, and diabetes technology use were assessed using the Fisher exact, Wilcoxon rank sum, and 2-sample t tests. Distress related to theoretical vs immediate burdens was compared using paired t tests.

RESULTS: Thirty caregivers (73.3% mothers) of children with T1DM (mean age [SD] = 5.4y [1.9], 70% non-Hispanic White, 60% commercially insured) completed the PAID-PR. Child median diabetes duration was 1.5 years (interquartile range [IQR] = 0.6, 2.3), median HbA1c 7.6% (IQR = 6.9, 8.1). All children used continuous glucose monitors, 73.3% Omnipod 5, 6.7% Tandem Mobi, and 20% multiple daily injections. The median distress score was 30.6/100 (IQR = 22.2, 36.1; the lowest 75th percentile of distress = 24.3 [12.5, 31.9]; the highest 25th percentile = 42.9 [38.6, 52.8]). Scores did not differ by demographics, clinical characteristics, or diabetes technology use. Caregivers indicated significantly greater distress from theoretical vs immediate burdens (P < .0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Caregivers of young children with T1DM experience greater distress related to anticipated future (theoretical) burdens than with immediate diabetes management. Understanding these distress patterns can help guide psychosocial supports.

articles.title: Nanomaterial-Based Electrochemical Immunosensors for the Detection of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis: Advancement, Challenges, and Future Perceptions.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) causes Johne's disease, a chronic infectious disease of ruminants associated with substantial economic losses in the livestock and dairy industries. Conventional diagnostic methods, including culture, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), have limitations related to analysis time, laboratory requirements, infection stage, matrix effects, and diagnostic performance. Nanomaterial-based electrochemical immunosensors have emerged as promising platforms for rapid, sensitive, miniaturized, and potentially field-compatible MAP detection was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, primarily covering studies published between 2015 and 2026. The review evaluates metal nanoparticles, carbon-based nanomaterials, magnetic nanoparticles, and hybrid nanomaterials in relation to electrode surface area, biomolecule immobilization, electron transfer, signal generation, analytical performance, and real-sample validation. Key challenges includes matrix interference, nonspecific adsorption, stability, reproducibility, and standardization. Emerging approaches, including microfluidic integration, portable potentiostats, multiplexed sensing, flexible platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis. Overall, nanomaterial-based electrochemical immunosensors show considerable promise for MAP detection, but standardized validation using diverse field samples and robust manufacturing strategies is required before routine on-farm implementation.

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Practice Guidelines on Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is an emerging multi-disease therapy, yet the quality and consistency of its available clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) remain unknown. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the quality, content coverage and recommendation consistency of FMT-related guidelines and develop an optimization framework for evidence-informed future guideline revision and standardized FMT clinical practice.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, The Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang Data, and official websites of guideline development organizations and professional societies from inception to March 11, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened and selected CPGs with actionable recommendations and conducted quality evaluation via the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation (AGREE) II instrument. Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) was computed for each AGREE II domain and interpreted according to Fleiss' criteria. Inter-guideline agreement was reported as the percentage of CPGs endorsing each recommendation.

RESULTS: Eighteen CPGs (3 general, 15 FMT-specific) with 191 recommendations were included. Applicability obtained the lowest AGREE II score (37.8%), followed by rigor of development (47.4%) and stakeholder involvement (49.7%).
