General guidelines scored higher than FMT-specific guidelines in applicability (62.5% vs. 32.9%) and stakeholder involvement (59.3% vs. 47.8%), but lower in rigor of development (38.9% vs. 49.1%). The coverage of recommendations showed marked inter‑guideline heterogeneity. Recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) was the most consistently recommended indication with the highest level of evidence (10/16). Over 75% of guidelines ignored transplant-center management, and non-CDI indications and key operational steps lacked sufficient high-certainty evidence. ICCs (0.86-0.97) showed excellent evaluator consistency.

CONCLUSIONS: Current FMT guidelines exhibit significant methodological deficiencies, heterogeneous recommendation coverage, and limited consensus beyond rCDI. FMT-specific guidelines show better developmental rigor but poorer applicability than general guidelines. Future FMT guideline development should establish core topic sets, adopt multidisciplinary collaborative mechanisms, and develop implementation toolkits with regular update protocols.

articles.title: Associations of Social Determinants of Health and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality: UK Biobank Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Social determinants of health (SDHs) play an important role in addressing inequitable and avoidable disparities in health status within countries but lack systematic assessment in broad populations. The aim of this study was to determine the association of SDHs, individually, in combination and cumulatively, with all-cause mortality risk, cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, and cancer mortality.

METHODS: Data were obtained from 190,239 adults in the UK Biobank. Exposure variables were SDHs assessed by self-reported sociodemographic characteristics using standardized questionnaires. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate the associations of combined SDHs and cumulative number of SDHs with all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality.

RESULTS: Over a median 12-year follow-up, 9,871 deaths occurred, including 1,673 from CVD and 5,199 from cancer. Compared to favorable SDHs, medium SDHs (HR 1.143; 95% CI 1.090-1.198) and unfavorable SDHs (HR 1.642; 95% CI 1.559-1.729) were associated with higher all-cause mortality risks. Medium and unfavorable SDHs were associated with increased risks of CVD mortality (by 16.3% and 81.5%) and cancer mortality (by 7.7% and 26.1%). Having ≥8 cumulative adverse SDHs significantly heightened all-cause mortality risk. In exploratory analyses, baseline hypertension and diabetes statistically accounted for a portion of the associations between combined SDHs and mortality outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Unfavorable SDHs are substantially associated with increased risks of all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality. Exploratory findings suggest that baseline hypertension and diabetes substantially explain these associations, highlighting existing disease burden as a key driver of health inequalities.

articles.title: Recognizing Fluid Overload-Associated Large B-Cell Lymphoma on Effusion Cytology: Two Illustrative Cases.
articles.abstract: Fluid overload-associated large B-cell lymphoma (FO-LBCL) is a distinct entity introduced in the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Hematolymphoid Tumors (2022). It denotes a large B-cell lymphoma confined to one or more serous cavities as effusions, without a solid or nodal mass, in the absence of KSHV/HHV8 (and largely EBV) infection, arising in patients with fluid-overload states. It was previously reported under descriptive terms such as "HHV8-negative primary effusion lymphoma-like lymphoma." We describe two cases illustrating the WHO-HAEM5 diagnostic criteria and the diagnostic and prognostic workup of this entity.

articles.title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide-Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase-Like Activity for Liver Protection.
articles.abstract: Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)-mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active-site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide-hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic-organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure-activity analysis showed that GPX-like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide-hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide-hybrid analogue, and conventional metal-based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione-dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide-hybrid material protected against acetaminophen-induced and rifampicin-induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide-hybrid frameworks as effective GPX-like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress-associated liver diseases.

articles.title: The higher adherence to the DASH diet the lower incidence and mortality from cardiovascular disease and all causes: ELSA-Brasil study.
articles.journal: International journal of food sciences and nutrition
articles.abstract: To investigate the association between adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and all-cause mortality. The study included 14,621 participants from the ELSA-Brasil cohort. DASH adherence was assessed at baseline using a continuous score. Fine-Gray competing risk models were for MACE and CVD mortality, and Cox models for all-cause mortality. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors, behaviours, comorbidities, weight change, and total energy intake. Mean age was 52 years (SD 9), and mean DASH score was 23.9 (SD 4.4). Each one-point increase in the DASH score was associated with lowerrisk of MACE (sHR 0.96; 95% CI 0.92-0.99), CVD mortality (sHR 0.95; 95% CI 0.92-1.00), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Greater DASH adherence was associated with lower incidence of MACE and reduced CVD and all-cause mortality in Brazilian adults.

articles.title: A Pilot Randomized Study of NAT2 and YEATS4 Pharmacogenetic Return of Results in Adults with Hypertension and African Ancestry: The GUARDD-US PGx Study.
articles.abstract: Almost half of individuals with hypertension fail to achieve recommended blood pressure (BP) goals. Pharmacogenetic gene-drug interactions may alter the efficacy of antihypertensive agents. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled sub-study of participants (N = 1874) with hypertension and self-reported African ancestry to determine whether pharmacogenetic return of results (RoR) would improve systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 3 months. Participants were randomized to immediate pharmacogenetic RoR (intervention) or delayed RoR at trial completion (control). Clinical decision support conveyed recommendations for YEATS4-guided thiazide diuretic selection and NAT2-guided hydralazine dosing. Prespecified subgroup analyses included those with uncontrolled BP (baseline SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90 mm Hg) and actionable genotypes. Immediate RoR did not improve SBP at 3 months in a broad population of hypertensive adults with controlled and uncontrolled SBP (covariate-adjusted change in SBP between groups: -0.3 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -1.8, 1.2). In participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype (N = 867) predicting reduced thiazide efficacy, immediate RoR led to greater SBP reduction at 3 months (-2.46 mm Hg, 95% CI: -4.57 to -0.36). In participants with uncontrolled hypertension at baseline (N = 659), immediate RoR led to a greater reduction in SBP (-2.9 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -5.6, -0.3). Although no SBP reduction was observed in the whole cohort, participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype or uncontrolled BP who received immediate RoR had a significantly greater SBP improvement than those with delayed RoR. Future studies of antihypertensive pharmacogenetics should recruit individuals with uncontrolled BP and actionable genotypes.

articles.title: Sedation strategy and the search for a better patient experience in ICU.
A systematic review on the challenges facing Latin-American tropical dairy cattle production.
articles.abstract: Driven by population growth and ascending prosperity, the demand for high-quality protein and especially dairy products is expected to surge in developing countries, particularly in tropical regions. However, satiating this appetite through intensified production poses significant challenges including rising feed costs, limited resource availability, and heat stress. Tropical livestock farming dominates the global scene when it comes to the number of animals, output, and stakeholders. Similarly, Latin America's tropical regions have been rapidly integrated into development, with large-scale dairy production as a primary economic driver, but hasty expansion has led to severe ecosystem degradation, highlighting the need for more sustainable planning. This review focuses on the unique challenges and opportunities associated with dairy production, animal health, and nutrition in tropical climates. Tropical dairy systems face interconnected environmental, nutritional, health, economic, and social constraints that can reduce productivity, profitability, animal welfare, and product quality. Heat stress, feed scarcity, variable forage quality, and disease pressure impair animal performance and increase production costs. Addressing these challenges requires integrated strategies combining heat-adapted genetics, improved nutrition, preventive health, efficient resource use, and precision technologies. In tropical Latin America, sustainable intensification also requires protecting natural resources. Collaboration among farmers, researchers, industry, and governments is essential to develop locally adapted solutions that enhance productivity, resilience, sustainability, and food security.

articles.title: Cost-effective and efficient diagnosis of bovine theileriosis in a low-income setting.
articles.abstract: Sample pooling combined with conventional polymerase chain reaction (cPCR) is a rapid and cost-effective approach for herd-level detection of Theileria spp., particularly in resource-limited settings. Bovine theileriosis is a tick-borne protozoan disease causing major economic losses to livestock production worldwide. In Sri Lanka, particularly in Jaffna, Theileria infections threaten cattle productivity, highlighting the need for affordable and sensitive surveillance tools. This study evaluated pooled cPCR for herd-level detection of Theileria spp. in cattle from three farms in Jaffna. Sixty blood samples (27, 26, and 7 animals per farm) and 27 ticks were collected. Giemsa-stained blood smears and individual cPCR analyses were performed. Then, three pools were prepared, taking 200 µL from each sample (one pool per farm) and analysed using cPCR targeting the major piroplasm surface protein (MPSP) gene. Microscopy detected a prevalence of 50%, whereas cPCR detected 81.7% (χ² = 13.374, p = 0.0003). Both Theileria orientalis (types 5 and 7) and Theileria sp. Yokoyama were identified. Pooling before cPCR and genomic DNA extraction reduced diagnostic costs by approximately 12-fold. Tick identification revealed predominance of Haemaphysalis bispinosa (88%). No significant associations were observed between infection prevalence and age, sex, or farm location. Despite widespread infection, most cattle were clinically healthy, indicating extensive subclinical circulation and possible endemic stability. Contrary to expectations, pooling samples from up to 27 cattle remained effective in herd-level detection of Theileria spp. despite low-parasitaemia levels. These findings demonstrate that pooled cPCR is a reliable and economical strategy for large-scale surveillance of bovine theileriosis in endemic, high prevalent and resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Influence of ecological and management factors on Toxoplasma gondii infection in small ruminants in Algeria.
articles.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a zoonotic protozoan of major concern for small-ruminant production and public health. This study is among the first to simultaneously compare T. gondii seroprevalence across contrasting Algerian bioclimatic zones. In summer 2024, a cross-sectional study was conducted across 82 herds comprising 4,022 small ruminants in three provinces of central Algeria (Blida, Médéa, Djelfa), representing contrasting bioclimatic zones (humid, semi-arid, and arid). Blood samples were collected from 1,052 animals older than six months to assess the apparent seroprevalence of T. gondii and associated factors. The herd-level apparent seroprevalence was 87.8%, with goat herds showing the highest apparent prevalence (94.4%), followed by mixed (87.5%) and sheep herds (85.4%). The individual animal-level apparent seroprevalence was 38.2%, with goats exhibiting significantly higher seropositivity than sheep (49.8% vs. 34.8%; p < 0.001). A climatic gradient was observed at the individual level, with apparent seroprevalence of 50.8% in the humid region (Blida), 43.4% in the sub-humid region (Médéa), and 27.1% in the arid region (Djelfa) (p < 0.001). After adjustment in a mixed-effects logistic regression model accounting for within-herd clustering, species and province remained significantly associated with seropositivity, while age, sex, and reproductive history were not. At the herd level, small herd size (< 50 animals) (adjusted OR = 14.45, p = 0.004), sedentary farming systems (adjusted OR = 9.75, p = 0.006), and cat exposure (adjusted OR = 22.78, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with seropositivity. However, convenience sampling and a final sample size below the calculated minimum should be considered when interpreting representativeness. These findings highlight the importance of regionally adapted surveillance and risk-based biosecurity measures, particularly in sub-humid peri-urban areas with intensive small-herd management.

articles.title: Changes in cardiometabolic biomarkers 1 year after direct acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C virus co-infection among people with HIV.
authors: North American AIDS Cohort Collaboration on Research and Design (NA‐ACCORD) of the International Epidemiologic Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Among people with HIV with hepatitis C virus (HCV) co-infection, we examined differences in haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk score at 12-months following direct acting antiviral (DAA) initiation, comparing people with HIV who initiated DAA with those who did not to explore the utility of DAAs beyond HCV elimination.

METHODS: Utilizing a nested exposure-matched study of people with HIV age ≥  18 years, on antiretroviral therapy from the NA-ACCORD and the Mass General Brigham HIV cohorts between 01/1/2014 and 12/31/2022, people with HIV with HCV co-infection were identified by detectable plasma HCV RNA. People with HIV who initiated DAA were matched 1:1 with people with HIV who did not initiate DAA. Multivariable linear regression models estimated HbA1c (N = 2374), TC (N = 3418) and ASCVD risk score (N = 488) at 12-months comparing people with HIV who initiated DAAs versus did not.

RESULTS: We identified no significant difference in the mean HbA1c at 12-months comparing DAA initiators to DAA non-initiators (β: 0.00%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.09% to 0.08%). The mean TC at 12-months was 13 mg/dL (95% CI 11-16 mg/dL) higher in DAA initiators and largely due to increases in LDL. There was no significant difference in the mean ASCVD risk score at 12-months when comparing DAA initiators with those who did not initiate DAAs (β: 1.10, 95% CI -0.09 to 2.20).

CONCLUSION: People with HIV with HCV who initiated DAA demonstrated no statistically significant difference in HbA1c or ASCVD risk score at 12-months compared to HIV/HCV co-infected persons who did no initiate DAA. However, TC and LDL levels increased 12 months following DAA treatment.

articles.title: Beyond Sepsis Survival: Post-Acute Vulnerability Profiles in Older Home Health Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older sepsis survivors face elevated rehospitalization risk shaped by multimorbidity and post-sepsis vulnerability, yet traditional risk models evaluate these factors in isolation. To identify clinically meaningful profiles of coexisting rehospitalization risk factors among older sepsis survivors receiving home health care (HHC), we used clustering to characterize risk subgroups and examined their association with 30-day rehospitalization.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries aged 65 years or older who transitioned to HHC after hospitalization for sepsis between January 1, 2021 and December 31, 2022 in the United States. Partitioning around medoids clustering with Gower distance was used to identify risk clusters based on risk factors available during the index hospitalization and first post-discharge HHC assessment. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations between cluster membership and all-cause 30-day rehospitalization, adjusting for contextual, HHC agency, and service delivery factors.

RESULTS: Among 21,888 index stays, two rehospitalization risk clusters were identified. Both clusters demonstrated post-acute vulnerability after sepsis hospitalization but differed in intensity and breadth of impairments. The higher vulnerability cluster had greater functional dependency, cognitive and behavioral impairment, urinary and bowel incontinence, difficulty following medical instructions, and prior healthcare utilization. Compared with the lower post-acute vulnerability cluster, the higher post-acute vulnerability cluster had a higher 30-day rehospitalization rate (27.8% vs. 21.1%; p < 0.001) and significantly higher odds of 30-day rehospitalization in unadjusted (OR 1.492; 95% CI 1.400-1.589; p < 0.001) and adjusted analyses (aOR 1.480; 95% CI 1.384-1.582; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Among older sepsis survivors receiving HHC, rehospitalization risk clustered into two post-acute vulnerability profiles that primarily reflected differences in the overall extent of multidimensional vulnerability. These profiles may help characterize co-occurring post-acute needs and support future evaluation of whether cluster-informed care coordination or stratified post-acute care can improve outcomes.

articles.title: Altered T cell immune profile and its prognostic implications in children with portal hypertension: A pilot study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Immune dysregulation in paediatric portal hypertension (PHT) is poorly understood. We aimed to characterise T cell phenotype and function and circulating immune mediators in children with PHT according to disease aetiology.

METHODS: Forty-four children with PHT (27 chronic liver disease [CLD]-related and 17 portal vein thrombosis [PVT]-related) and 15 healthy controls were prospectively enrolled. Peripheral and portal blood samples were analysed using multiparameter flow cytometry and ELISA to assess T cell subsets, chemokine receptors, cytokines and soluble immune markers. Analyses examined group differences and correlations with liver stiffness and bleeding history.

RESULTS: PHT was associated with reduced circulating T cells, altered immune phenotypes and impaired effector function. CLD-related PHT exhibited a pronounced pro-inflammatory profile, with elevated IFN-γ, TNF-α, MMP7 and soluble PD-L1 and increased CD39 and PD-1. PVT-related PHT showed relatively preserved liver function and milder systemic inflammation but altered T cell trafficking, characterised by increased CCR4 and reduced CXCR3 expression. Elevated CXCL9 correlated with CXCR3 expression. T cells in the portal circulation displayed reduced cytokine production and cytotoxicity, suggesting functional adaptation within the hepatic microenvironment. Liver stiffness correlated positively with pro-inflammatory cytokines and immune-regulatory markers.

CONCLUSIONS: Paediatric PHT is characterised by aetiology-specific T cell dysregulation. CLD-related PHT predominantly features chronic inflammation and T cell exhaustion, whereas PVT-related PHT shows a milder inflammatory phenotype with altered T cell trafficking. These findings provide mechanistic insights and identify candidate immune signatures requiring validation in larger, aetiology-specific cohorts.

articles.title: Biomarkers of native liver survival and portal hypertension in biliary atresia.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of noninvasive markers Aspartate Aminotransferase to Platelet Ratio Index (APRi) and Infantile Biliary Atresia Liver Fibrosis score (iBALF), as well as the histological Ishak fibrosis score, as predictors of native liver survival (NLS) and portal hypertension (PH) in children with biliary atresia BA undergoing Kasai portoenterostomy (KPE).

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective observational study was conducted on children diagnosed with BA who underwent KPE. APRi and iBALF were calculated using laboratory data collected at hospital discharge after KPE. The degree of hepatic fibrosis was assessed and reviewed using the Ishak fibrosis score in liver biopsy specimens collected at KPE. NLS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards regression. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Higher APRi, iBALF, and Ishak fibrosis score values were associated with lower NLS (p < 0.006, p < 0.025, and p < 0.048, respectively). APRi and iBALF emerged as good PH predictors (p < 0.005 and p < 0.032, respectively).

CONCLUSION: APRi, iBALF, and the Ishak fibrosis score showed prognostic value in predicting NLS in children with BA after KPE. These findings reinforce the potential use of biomarkers in the clinical follow-up of these patients, supporting risk stratification strategies.

articles.title: Multimodal Programming of Extracellular Vesicles via Nano-Primed SECCS-Based 3D Microenvironments for Coordinated Ferroptosis Suppression and Myogenic Regeneration in Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic glucolipotoxicity is associated with progressive skeletal muscle atrophy, bone loss, cellular senescence, and ferroptotic injury. Because ferroptosis inhibition alone may not restore compromised myogenic capacity, we developed a combined stem cell-conditioning strategy integrating fullerol priming with the stem cell screen-enrich-combine(-biomaterials) circulating system (SECCS). This integrated three-dimensional culture platform uses porous β-TCP granules and intermittent medium circulation to generate BMSCs-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs). Among 2D-EVs, F-2D-EVs, SECCS-EVs, and F-SECCS-EVs, F-SECCS-EVs exhibited the strongest anti-ferroptotic and pro-regenerative effects. In glucolipotoxicity-challenged myoblasts, F-SECCS-EVs attenuated ferroptotic injury and enhanced proliferation and myogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and functional experiments identified FOXO3 as an important mediator linking antioxidant defense with myogenic programs. In diabetic mice, F-SECCS-EVs improved motor function, muscle strength, myofiber cross-sectional area, and myogenic marker expression while modulating macrophage polarization. Free fullerol, 2D-EVs, and F-2D-EVs produced limited recovery, whereas SECCS-EVs were less effective than F-SECCS-EVs. These muscle benefits were accompanied by favorable changes in tibial bone structure. Collectively, these findings support fullerol-primed SECCS culture as a strategy for coordinating ferroptosis control with myogenic recovery in diabetes-associated musculoskeletal degeneration.

articles.title: Copper Metal-Organic Framework-Embedded Decellularized Matrix Hydrogel Remodels the Uterine Microenvironment for Endometrial Regeneration and Fertility Restoration.
articles.abstract: Severe endometrial injury is a leading cause of female infertility, driven by the convergence of inadequate vascularization, persistent inflammation, infection, and excessive fibrosis. Existing therapies address these pathologies in isolation, falling short of the coordinated remodeling essential for functional regeneration. Here, we report an injectable, thermally responsive composite hydrogel that embeds copper-based metal-organic framework (HKUST-1) nanoparticles within a porcine acellular dermal matrix (PADM) network, coupling biomimetic extracellular matrix support with sustained Cu2 + delivery. In vitro, the hydrogel promotes endothelial migration and tubular network formation, shifts macrophage polarization toward the reparative M2 phenotype, and exhibits broad-spectrum bactericidal activity. In a rat endometrial injury model, it increases gland density and CD31+ neovascularization while suppressing fibrotic collagen deposition. Crucially, it restores hormonal responsiveness by upregulating estrogen and progesterone receptor expression. These coordinated improvements translate into meaningful fertility restoration, with implanted embryos increasing from 8 ± 2 to 14 ± 1. Transcriptomic profiling indicates coordinated changes in extracellular matrix remodeling and ion transport programs. The PADM@HKUST-1 hydrogel demonstrates that integrating biomimetic scaffolding with sustained bioactive ion delivery achieves comprehensive uterine microenvironment remodeling, offering a translatable approach for clinical management of severe endometrial injury.

articles.title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
articles.abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β0-thalassaemia (HbSβ0), haemoglobin S/β+-thalassaemia (HbSβ+), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

articles.title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

articles.title: Incidentalomas in Gastroenterology and Hepatology: A Narrative Review of Guideline-Based Management, Ethical Considerations, and a Proposed Framework for Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Major advancements in medical imaging have led to higher rates of detection of incidental findings unrelated to the presenting complaint, termed incidentalomas. Despite their rising prevalence in gastroenterology and hepatology, there is a paucity of understanding regarding their clinical management and the ethical problems they entail. We aimed to synthesize the latest guidelines for managing these incidentalomas and review the ethical dilemmas they pose, with a view to formulating a management framework to assist clinicians.

METHODS: We undertook a narrative review by searching MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Embase (January 2010-May 2026) using key search terms. We prioritized recent guidelines and key consensus statements from international societies. We also identified additional ethical literature through targeted searches.

RESULTS: Management guidelines for incidentalomas in gastroenterology and hepatology share several commonalities. These include characterization using the least invasive tests, size-based triage, emphasis on growth and morphology, reserve tissue sampling, and referral of indeterminate lesions. However, they differ in intervention thresholds, second-line tests, and surveillance duration. The principal ethical issues identified include conflicts regarding disclosure and autonomy, care cascades and overdetection, distributive justice and equitable care, and medicolegal accountability. Based on this literature, the authors propose a six-step framework for managing incidentalomas: anticipate and contextualize, characterize, risk-stratify, seek multidisciplinary review when required, engage in shared decision-making, and finally, close the loop.

CONCLUSION: Incidentaloma management should follow relevant guidelines and be complemented by a patient-centered approach, particularly regarding the course of investigation and the duration of follow-up.

articles.title: Segment-based comparison of multiparametric MRI, Gallium-68-PSMA-PET/CT and combined imaging with histopathology in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level.

RESULTS: A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA.

CONCLUSION: At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

articles.title: Impact of Physical Activity on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We investigated whether accelerometer-assessed moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) is associated with cardiovascular mortality among individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in the United States.

METHODS: We performed a longitudinal analysis using the 2003-2006 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data among adults, with mortality follow-up through December 2019. We defined MASLD primarily using the Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI), followed by current cardiometabolic criteria; we used the US Fatty Liver Index (USFLI) in sensitivity analyses. We classified accelerometer-assessed PA as MVPA, total PA, and sedentary behavior.

RESULTS: Among 2785 individuals with HSI-defined MASLD, 584 deaths occurred, including 198 cardiovascular deaths, over a median follow-up of 14.7 years. A higher level of PA is associated with a more favorable predicted cardiovascular risk profile at baseline. Among individuals with MASLD, increasing MVPA was nonlinearly associated with reduced all-cause mortality in a multivariable model (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.71-0.91 per 10-min increase; P for trend < 0.001). Furthermore, higher MVPA was nonlinearly associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular mortality in MASLD (HR: 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.99 per 10-min increase; P for trend = 0.009). Although higher total PA was also associated with reduced mortality, the point estimate was substantially weaker than that observed for MVPA. Sensitivity analyses using the USFLI definition showed directionally similar but attenuated associations. Increased sedentary behavior did not impact mortality in the MASLD group.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher MVPA is nonlinearly associated with cardiovascular mortality in individuals with MASLD.

articles.title: Simultaneous Screening and Identification of Potential Bioactive Components Against MASLD in Guizhi Fuling Decoction by Integrating a Multitarget Affinity Ultrafiltration Strategy With UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As one of the most common chronic liver diseases worldwide, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) imposes an escalating burden on global health systems. However, the efficacy of Guizhi Fuling decoction (GZFLD) against MASLD and its potential pharmacodynamic material basis remain elusive.

OBJECTIVES: This work aims to explore the potential bioactive constituents of GZFLD against MASLD by integrating a multitarget affinity ultrafiltration strategy with UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS.

METHODS: The efficacy of GZFLD against MASLD was initially evaluated using an in vitro HepG2 model of MASLD. Subsequently, potential active ingredients of GZFLD against MASLD were screened out via affinity ultrafiltration coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (AUF-LC-MS/MS) targeting multiple enzymes, including pancreatic lipase (PL), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Finally, molecular docking simulations, enzyme inhibition assays, and cell experiments were performed to validate the activities of the candidate components.

RESULTS: The results demonstrated that GZFLD significantly alleviated lipid accumulation and oxidative stress in the HepG2 model of MASLD, and a total of 18 potential bioactive ingredients were identified in GZFLD. Among them, benzoylpaeoniflorin, galloylpaeoniflorin, and ellagic acid are the main active compounds of GZFLD against MASLD. Furthermore, the results of molecular docking revealed that these components could strongly bind their corresponding target by various forces. The result of COX-2 inhibition assay indicated that ellagic acid exhibited a strong COX-2 inhibitory activity. Moreover, the results of cell verifications implied that ellagic acid and benzoylpaeoniflorin exhibited significant therapeutic potential on MASLD by modulating lipid metabolism and inflammatory responses.

CONCLUSION: GZFLD demonstrated noteworthy effects against MASLD by alleviating lipid accumulation and oxidative stress, and the potential bioactive components of GZFLD and their interaction network against MASLD were first explored and constructed by combining AUF-LC-MS/MS with multiple targets, which showcased a powerful new integrating strategy for the simultaneous screening and identification of bioactive compounds in complex Chinese medicines.

articles.title: Novel acylation modifications in cerebrovascular disease: Molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Secondary injury in cerebrovascular disease involves energy failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Novel lysine acylations, including lactylation, succinylation, beta-hydroxybutyrylation and crotonylation, have emerged as interfaces through which metabolic changes in lactate, succinate, ketone bodies and short-chain acyl-CoA species are translated into transcriptional regulation and altered protein function. This review organizes the evidence according to a framework that links metabolic donors, writer and eraser enzymes, modification sites, cell types and disease stages. We distinguish relatively developed experimental evidence in acute ischemic stroke and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury from limited findings in haemorrhage and predominantly exploratory evidence in chronic hypoperfusion and vascular cognitive impairment. Proteomic studies have identified 1003 lactylation sites across 469 proteins in rats subjected to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, although most sites have not undergone causal validation. Comparatively strong evidence has accumulated for sites or regulatory axes involving MeCP2, SOD2, NEK7, ACSL4, PLBD1 and ZO-1. Collectively, current findings indicate that the effects of a given acylation cannot be inferred from its global abundance because they depend on substrate function, cellular origin and the therapeutic window. Major limitations include insufficient site-specific causal evidence, difficulty in directly quantifying crosstalk among post-translational modifications, poor correspondence between animal models and clinical heterogeneity and the absence of effective delivery systems and pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Future studies should integrate spatiotemporally resolved multi-omics, endogenous site editing, cell-specific models, measurable target engagement and independent clinical cohorts to evaluate whether selected acylation sites can progress from experimental candidates to independently validated clinical markers or intervention targets.

articles.title: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes of Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Native Vertebral Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a major cause of native vertebral osteomyelitis (NVO) and is associated with persistent infection, complications, prolonged hospitalization, and increased mortality.

PURPOSE: We conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the antimicrobial and surgical approaches used for MRSA NVO and their associated clinical outcomes.

STUDY SETTING: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: A systematic literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted on November 27, 2025. Studies were eligible if they included adults with MRSA NVO, evaluated medical or surgical treatment strategies, reported clinical outcomes, and included at least five patients. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Murad et al. tool. Random-effects models were used to pool proportions of treatment success, reinfection, and mortality.

RESULTS: Thirty studies including 677 patients were included. Treatment strategies were heterogeneous and included prolonged anti-MRSA antimicrobial therapy and surgical approaches ranging from debridement and drainage to decompression and spinal stabilization or fusion. Vancomycin-based regimens were the most frequently reported antimicrobial strategy. Among studies reporting treatment duration, intravenous therapy commonly ranged from 4 to 8 weeks, with some patients receiving oral step-down or suppressive therapy. The pooled treatment success rate was 84.9% (95% CI, 76.7%-90.7%), pooled reinfection rate was 15.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-23.6%), and pooled mortality rate was 3.1% (95% CI, 0.8%-10.8%). Subgroup analyses were not feasible because treatment-specific data were limited and inconsistently reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Management of MRSA NVO varied substantially across studies, with vancomycin-based antimicrobial therapy and diverse surgical strategies commonly reported. Pooled outcomes showed high treatment success with lower rates of reinfection and mortality. The substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity of the available evidence highlights the need for prospective studies with standardized treatment and outcome reporting.

articles.title: One Health determinants of clinically assessed cutaneous leishmaniasis in Sodo District, Ethiopia: a community-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is a neglected tropical disease shaped by interacting environmental, wildlife, household, and behavioral factors, yet few community-based studies have evaluated these determinants simultaneously within a One Health framework. We assessed multidomain determinants of clinically assessed CL among 1,356 individuals from six kebeles in Sodo District, Ethiopia. CL was defined as an active lesion or typical scar consistent with current or previous infection. Exposures were grouped into four analytic domains: household/structural, environmental, behavioral, and reservoir/animal-interface; demographic variables were used as adjustment covariates. Domain-specific multivariable logistic regression models were followed by additive domain-level risk scores and an integrated model adjusted for age, sex, education, occupation, and kebele. CL prevalence was 9.1% (123/1,356). In the integrated model (N = 1,266), each additional household/structural risk factor increased the odds of CL (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.52, 95% CI: 1.65-3.92), environmental risk showed a borderline association (AOR = 1.37, 95% CI: 1.00-1.88), behavioral risk demonstrated the strongest effect (AOR = 4.71, 95% CI: 3.44-6.71), and reservoir/animal-interface risk remained independently associated (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI: 1.35-6.41). Predicted probabilities increased sharply across behavioral risk levels, indicating a dose-response pattern. The integrated model demonstrated excellent apparent discrimination (AUC = 0.92). These findings indicate that clinically assessed CL in this setting reflects cumulative multidomain vulnerability, supporting One Health interventions that address housing, environmental exposures, risky behaviors, and human-reservoir contact.

articles.title: Unveiling the long non-coding RNA profile of Aeromonas veronii-infected mouse abdominal macrophages.
articles.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play key roles in the host's defense against pathogenic infection. Aeromonas veronii is a zoonotic pathogen capable of provoking severe inflammatory responses. However, the function of lncRNAs in A. veronii infected mouse abdominal macrophages (MAMs) remains poorly understood. MAMs serve as the primary defense against bacterial infection and play critical roles in the anti-infectious immune response. Here, we profiled lncRNAs from MAMs infected with A. veronii. RNA sequencing identified a total of 1628 differentially expressed lncRNAs (DElncRNAs), comprising 680 up-regulated and 948 down-regulated genes. An integrated analysis of lncRNA-mRNA interaction networks identified 4888 target genes of DElncRNAs (DETGs). Of these, 55 DElncRNAs were found to be involved in the regulation of seven immune pathways by regulating 41 DETGs. Furthermore, GO and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed that DETGs were significantly enriched in clusters or pathways associated with immune regulation. These findings provide the transcriptomic profile of MAMs. A comprehensive analysis of DElncRNAs in MAMs was conducted in response to A. veronii infection. Co-expression analysis indicates that lncRNAs are serving as vital regulators of immune gene activity through their critical influence on MAMs during A. veronii infection.

articles.title: LUR1 (SPRING1) promotes sortilin-induced macrophage lipid accumulation and aortic atherosclerosis via furin maturation.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study was undertaken to investigate the contributions of largely Golgi-localized proteins-lipid uptake regulator 1 (LUR1, SPRING1), the protease furin, and sortilin-in oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL)-treated macrophages and atherosclerotic mouse models.

METHODS: Bioinformatics analysis was employed to predict the interaction between LUR1 and furin and their potential involvement in AS. The binding of LUR1 to furin was detected using a co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay. Gene and protein expression was determined by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot in THP-1 macrophages transfected with recombinant lentiviruses. Cellular lipid content was measured by colorimetry, and lipid droplets were evaluated by Oil Red O staining. Plasma lipid profiles were measured using an enzymatic oxidation method. Histological staining was performed to investigate aortic atherosclerotic lesions in male LDLR-/- mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD).

RESULTS: LUR1 increased the expression and maturation of macrophage sortilin. Co-IP confirmed LUR1-furin binding. The mRNA and protein levels of furin and sortilin were increased upon LUR1 OE, while the ratios of pro-furin/mature-furin and pro-sortilin/total-sortilin decreased, thereby enhancing lipid uptake in macrophages. Infection with adeno-associated virus 9 (AAV9)-LUR1 elevated plasma levels of total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and increased lipid deposition and AS plaque area in the vessel walls of male HFD-fed LDLR-/- mice.

CONCLUSION: LUR1 was implicated in furin/sortilin maturation, accelerating macrophage lipid accumulation and the progression of aortic AS.

articles.title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

articles.title: Treatment outcomes in hepatic hydrothorax: A propensity score-matched survival analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the prognostic impact of hepatic hydrothorax (HH) in decompensated cirrhosis and compared outcomes between conservative therapy and surgical diaphragmatic repair.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 48,464 adults with decompensated cirrhosis from 2004 to 2024. After exclusions, 386 patients (0.8%) were identified with HH, of whom 120 underwent surgical repair and 266 received conservative management. Clinical characteristics and laboratory data were analyzed. The primary endpoint was 365-day mortality. Propensity score matching (1:1, caliper 0.2) incorporating eight clinically relevant variables was used to balance baseline differences. Mortality risk was assessed using generalized estimating equations and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Before matching, the conservative group had more severe liver dysfunction, with higher Child-Pugh scores (10.3 ± 3.0 vs. 8.8 ± 2.7, p < 0.001), while MELD scores were lower (16.5 ± 2.4 vs. 26.28 ± 16.17, p < 0.001). The 365-day mortality was 64.3% (171/266) in the conservative therapy group and 51.7% (62/120) in the surgical repair group, corresponding to a crude risk ratio of 1.24 (95% CI, 1.01-1.53) and an odds ratio of 1.69 (95% CI, 1.08-2.65). Survival analysis demonstrated a significant difference between groups (unadjusted log-rank test, χ² = 8.330, p = 0.004). After matching, 119 pairs showed well-balanced baseline characteristics. In the matched cohort, 1-year mortality remained lower with surgery (40.3% vs. 59.7%; Cohen's h = 0.39).

CONCLUSIONS: Surgical diaphragmatic repair was associated with lower 1-year mortality compared with conservative management after adjustment for measured baseline differences.

articles.title: Injury Patterns, In-Hospital Outcomes, and Resource Utilization of Acute Cuboid and Navicular Fractures.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute cuboid and navicular fractures can be serious injuries. However, multicenter data on their associated injuries and in-hospital course are limited.

PURPOSE: To characterize the demographics, injury patterns, in-hospital outcomes, and resource utilization of trauma center patients with acute cuboid and/or navicular fractures.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional database study.

METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2019) was queried for acute cuboid and/or navicular fractures. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with discharge to post-acute care, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and hospital length of stay in adults.

RESULTS: Overall, 3,424 patients with 4,084 fractures were identified (2,327 with cuboid and 1,637 with navicular fractures, including 540 with both). Road-traffic mechanisms accounted for 64.5%, and 25.1% had polytrauma. Metatarsal, calcaneal, and talar fractures were the most common concomitant injuries. Combined fractures were more often ipsilateral than contralateral (457 vs 18 patients). Despite infrequent complications, 50.2% were discharged home without post-acute services (home health, inpatient rehabilitation, or skilled nursing care). In-hospital mortality was 1.1%. After adjustment, polytrauma (OR 3.75, 95% CI 3.04-4.61), bilateral involvement, and ankle, tibia, fibula, or metatarsal fractures were associated with discharge to post-acute care, whereas fracture pattern was not.

CONCLUSIONS: Cuboid and navicular fractures are predominantly high-energy injuries that rarely occur in isolation. Post-acute care needs, ICU admission, and length of stay were associated with overall injury burden rather than the specific bone fractured.

articles.title: A randomized controlled trial of a novel AI-based prognostic decision support tool integrated into the electronic health record for ischemic heart disease: Rationale and design of the PM Heart trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading global cause of years of life lost. Although the clinical presentation and progression of IHD differ widely, clinical management is relatively uniform. To improve risk stratification and clinical management, we developed a decision support tool - the PMHeartIHD Algorithm (also named PMHNet) - based on extensive clinical, registry and biochemical data. This algorithm automatically calculates one-year survival following an IHD event. We hypothesize that presenting the prognoses calculated by the PMHeartIHD Algorithm to the treating physicians will improve both the clinical management and outcome of the individual patient.

OBJECTIVE: The objectives of the PM Heart trial include clinical and technical aspects. First, the primary aim is to investigate if the clinical use of the prognosis calculated by the algorithm improves patient prognosis and minimizes the risk of re-hospitalization, compared to standard of care. A secondary objective is to generate knowledge on how decision support tools in cardiology may be implemented, received, and used directly in clinical practice.

METHODS: The PMHeartIHD Aalgorithm has been integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) system (Sundhedsplatformen (SP), EPIC) for clinical use. The PM Heart trial is designed as a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, clinical trial, automatically enrolling and randomizing hospitalized patients with coronary artery disease at the cardiology departments in The Capital Region and Region Zealand in Denmark. Patients are randomized (1:1 ratio) immediately after coronary angiography, to either show or hide the calculated PMHeartIHD-prognosis or not in the electronic health record.

RESULTS: The primary outcome is a composite outcome consisting of re-admissions within 30 days and one-year survival rates after randomization. Inclusion began September 2023, and follow-up is expected to finish in 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: We present the design of and rationale for the PM Heart trial. Our aim is to assess the clinical value of implementing an artificial intelligence-based decision support tool in clinical practice.

articles.title: Aerobic exercise ameliorates cardiac function in HFpEF mice by suppressing ALCAT1, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in the paraventricular nucleus and nucleus tractus solitarius.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is commonly accompanied by sympathetic overactivation, contributing to poor patient prognosis. The paraventricular nucleus (PVN) and nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) are critical cardiovascular regulatory centers. Pathological cardiolipin (CL) remodeling catalyzed by Acyl-CoA:lysocardiolipin acyltransferase 1 (ALCAT1) exacerbates disease progression. This study aims to elucidate the roles of aerobic exercise and ALCAT1 in modulating brain-heart axis dysregulation in HFpEF.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We employed wild-type (WT) and Alcat1 knockout mice to establish an HFpEF model, followed by aerobic exercise. Neuroinflammatory model was established to investigate the role of ALCAT1 in neuroinflammation. Underlying mechanisms were explored in HT22 cells. In HFpEF mice, aerobic exercise suppressed ALCAT1 and up-regulated growth differentiation factor 5 (GDF5) in the PVN and NTS, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities, decreased oxidative stress markers, and attenuated neuronal structural damage and hyperactivation. These central improvements were accompanied by attenuated cardiac sympathetic overactivation, lowered blood pressure, and improved diastolic function. The important role of ALCAT1 was further supported, as its genetic knockout conferred significant protection in both HFpEF and neuroinflammatory models. In HT22 cells, GDF5 suppressed the LPS-induced ALCAT1 up-regulation and ameliorated cellular injury.

CONCLUSION: ALCAT1 is an important contributor to neuronal injury. Aerobic exercise suppresses ALCAT1 and up-regulates GDF5, ameliorating neuronal injury and improving diastolic function in HFpEF mice. Mechanistically, ALCAT1 and GDF5 are reciprocally regulated, which may contribute to the protective effects of aerobic exercise against HFpEF. These findings suggest ALCAT1 as a potential molecular target for exercise-based HFpEF therapy.

articles.title: Trends in cardiovascular disease and risk factors between 2004 and 2021: Findings from the U.S. Millennium Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in the United States (U.S.). Military veterans have notably high prevalences of CVD. The aim was to report the prevalence of self-reported CVD and risk factors among post-9/11 veterans from 2004 to 2021.

METHODS: The U.S. Millennium Cohort Study prospectively follows service members and veterans. Eligible participants enrolled in 2001, separated from the military by 2021, and provided CVD information post-separation. Data from cross-sectional snapshots were used to examine unadjusted and standardized prevalences of CVD and risk factors. Linear trends in prevalence tested for significant changes.

RESULTS: Among 43,769 participants (average baseline age 37.2) between 2004 and 2006 and 2019-2021, results show current smoking decreased from 23.7 to 8.2 per 100. Prevalence estimates for all other examined factors increased; obesity from 22.2 to 47.7 per 100, hypertension from 9.0 to 23.5 per 100, diabetes from 1.6 to 7.0 per 100. CVD outcomes were less common and increased from <0.8 to <3.0 per 100.

CONCLUSIONS: Among a population of post-9/11 veterans, most CVD factors increased between 2004 and 2021. Treatment and intervention programs targeted toward veterans transitioning to civilian life should consider weight management and healthy lifestyle factors related to CVD prevention.

articles.title: Evaluation of the commutability of control materials for C-peptide proficiency testing.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Commutability refers to the consistency of measurement results between reference materials (RMs) and patient samples across different measurement procedures. C-peptide is essential for diabetes classification and management, however, inter-assay variability persists despite ongoing harmonization efforts. The use of commutable materials is therefore critical for calibration and external quality assessment (EQA). This study evaluated the commutability of pooled human serum and commercial control materials using CLSI- and IFCC-based approaches.

METHODS: Commutability was evaluated using 30 clinical samples and six RMs, including three serum-based in-house prepared materials and three commercial materials. C-peptide was measured in triplicate using four major measurement procedures in Korea; Alinity i (Abbott Diagnostics), cobas e801 (Roche Diagnostics), UniCel DxI 800 (Beckman Coulter), and Atellica IM 1600 (Siemens Healthineers). Commutability was assessed using the CLSI EP14-ED4 Deming regression-based approach with 95% prediction intervals (PIs) and the IFCC difference-in-bias approach with expanded uncertainty, applying a total allowable error of 7.1% and a coverage factor of 1.9.

RESULTS: Three clinical samples were excluded from the analyses after being identified as outliers in scatter plots. Using the CLSI approach with the remaining 27 clinical samples, all RMs fell within the 95% PIs across all method pairs and were classified as commutable. In contrast, the IFCC approach, with concentration partitioning at 1.0 ng/mL distinguished differences in commutability among the RMs. Serum-based in-house prepared materials were classified as commutable or indeterminate, whereas commercial materials showed multiple indeterminate results and one non-commutable result.

CONCLUSION: Pooled human serum-based in-house prepared materials demonstrated more stable commutability than commercial materials, supporting their use in C-peptide EQA programs.

articles.title: Programmable bacterial vaccine vectors: A Design-Build-Control framework for precision immune engineering.
articles.abstract: Live bacterial vectors combine intrinsic adjuvanticity, mucosal targeting, and programmable antigen delivery within a single engineerable chassis, yet their development has historically relied on empirical attenuation rather than systematic design. We present a Design-Build-Control framework, adapted from synthetic biology paradigms, that reframes bacterial vector engineering as a unified biotechnological problem. Design principles govern trade-offs among safety, immunogenicity, tissue tropism, and route of administration. Build-stage strategies translate these principles into genetically stable vector platforms through attenuation, balanced-lethal systems, and antibiotic-free plasmid maintenance. Control-stage tools, including inducible promoters, quorum-sensing circuits, and kill switches, enable dynamic regulation of vector behavior within the host. We apply this framework across major platform classes, including live attenuated Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, probiotic chassis, and non-replicating systems such as outer membrane vesicles, bacterial ghosts, and spores, and examine how biomaterial-based formulation, including encapsulation and mucoadhesive coatings, extends engineering control into manufacturing and delivery. We evaluate translational determinants, including genetic stability, environmental containment, and regulatory compliance, alongside applications spanning infectious disease, oncology, and veterinary medicine. We further assess the emerging role of artificial intelligence in bacterial-vector design, distinguishing established computational applications, experimentally validated approaches, and prospective uses that still require experimental validation. By integrating advances in synthetic biology, biomaterials, and computational design, this review presents programmable bacterial vectors as an emerging biotechnology platform and proposes a Design-Build-Control (DBC) framework for systematically evaluating biosafety, manufacturability, and clinical translation.

articles.title: Aged Buoy-derived Microplastics Alter Photosynthetic Performance and Metabolic Regulation in Pyropia yezoensis without Short-term Growth Inhibition.
articles.abstract: Plastic aquaculture equipment can release microplastics into seaweed mariculture zones, yet the effects of these particles on cultivated macroalgae remain poorly understood. In this study, Pyropia yezoensis thalli were exposed to field-aged buoy-derived polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics at 0.1, 1, and 10 mg/L for 7 d. Relative growth rate was not significantly affected, whereas other sublethal endpoints showed polymer-specific changes. PVC exposure was associated with stronger lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate depletion at high concentration, and increasing integrated stress. PET exposure mainly induced protein accumulation and peroxidase-related antioxidant responses, with the highest integrated deviation occurring at the lowest concentration. Metabolomic profiling further supported these physiological patterns. PVC-related metabolic changes were mainly associated with antioxidant regulation, lipid metabolism, and pigment-related pathways, consistent with membrane oxidative damage and phycobiliprotein disturbance. PET-related changes were more closely linked to protein synthesis, transport regulation, and cofactor-dependent antioxidant processes. Overall, aged PVC and PET microplastics induced distinct sublethal responses in P. yezoensis, highlighting the need to consider polymer identity, aging status, and combined biomarker-metabolomic endpoints in ecological risk assessment of seaweed mariculture systems.

articles.title: Menstrual Health in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults with Cardiac Disease: An Underrecognized Component of Heart Failure, Mechanical Circulatory Support, and Transplant Care.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menstrual abnormalities, including heavy menstrual bleeding, amenorrhea, and dysmenorrhea, are frequently encountered among children, adolescents, and young adults with congenital and acquired heart disease, yet remain underrecognized in routine cardiovascular care. Anticoagulation, thrombosis risk, heart failure physiology, and limited high-quality evidence complicate management and contribute to substantial variation in practice.

METHODS: The Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network convened a multidisciplinary working group of cardiologists, hematologists, gynecologists, adolescent medicine specialists, and allied health providers. Following a literature search, the group met monthly via virtual meetings to synthesize current evidence and clinical experience and develop consensus guidance.

RESULTS: The consensus emphasizes routine, developmentally appropriate menstrual screening and recognition that traditional definitions of heavy menstrual bleeding may underestimate its clinical impact in patients with heart disease. Management requires individualized assessment of bleeding risk, thrombotic risk, cardiac physiology, and patient preferences. Menstrual abnormalities may warrant broader evaluation for changes in overall health, cardiac status, or energy availability.

CONCLUSIONS: Menstrual health is integral to comprehensive cardiovascular care. Integrating screening and individualized management into cardiology practice may reduce morbidity, improve quality of life, and support equitable, sex-informed care. Further research and culturally responsive, multidisciplinary implementation are needed to strengthen the evidence base and improve care consistency.

articles.title: Network analysis of chronic disease diagnosis co-documentation in insurance claims among older Arkansans.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity among older adults presents growing clinical and economic challenges, particularly in medically underserved states such as Arkansas. However, it remains unclear whether chronic conditions documented in routine healthcare encounters exhibit structured patterns of diagnosis co-documentation or primarily reflect incidental co-documentation. Understanding these patterns may inform future studies of multimorbidity and healthcare utilization.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize statewide, sex-stratified patterns of claim-level diagnosis co-documentation among Arkansas adults aged ≥ 65 years using administrative claims data.

METHODS: We analyzed 2024 IQVIA administrative claims for Arkansas residents aged ≥ 65 years (1408,707 claims from 35,253 unique patients). Analyses were conducted at the claim level; therefore, individuals could contribute multiple claims, and results reflect utilization-weighted diagnosis co-documentation rather than patient-level disease prevalence or multimorbidity. Twenty-five chronic condition categories were defined using ICD-10-CM codes. Pairwise diagnosis co-documentation was quantified using Lewontin's standardized disequilibrium coefficient (D'), which compares observed joint documentation with the expectation under statistical independence. Sex-stratified D' matrices, disease connectedness metrics, and hierarchical clustering were used to characterize patterns of diagnosis co-documentation.

RESULTS: Hypertension was the most frequently documented chronic condition among claims for both females (22.2%) and males (23.7%) and exhibited the highest positive connectedness in both sex-stratified analyses. Among females, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia, coronary artery disease (CAD), obesity, thyroid disorders, and heart failure (D' = 0.46-0.69). Among males, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia (D' = 0.73), obesity (D' = 0.64), CAD (D' = 0.57), and thyroid disorders (D' = 0.56). Females demonstrated relatively greater diagnosis co-documentation among musculoskeletal, endocrine, and mental health conditions, whereas males showed more concentrated diagnosis co-documentation among cardiometabolic and organ dysfunction conditions. Negative D' values identified disease pairs that were infrequently co-documented within the same claims (e.g., autoimmune disease-chronic gastrointestinal disease among males, D' = -1.00), reflecting absent or infrequent claim-level joint documentation.

CONCLUSIONS: In this claim-level analysis of Arkansas adults aged ≥ 65 years represented in the IQVIA administrative claims database, diagnosis co-documentation exhibited structured, sex-specific patterns, with hypertension demonstrating the highest positive connectedness among the 25 chronic conditions. These utilization-weighted findings provide a descriptive basis for hypothesis generation and support future longitudinal, patient-level studies to evaluate temporal disease relationships and the potential role of cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) risk management.

articles.title: Characterization of the morphological, immunophenotypical and cytogenetic features of high-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration is a rare neoplasm of mature B-cell lineage, and large-scale clinicopathological studies of this disease remain scarce. To bridge this research gap, we conducted a retrospective analysis of HGBCL with 11q aberration, aiming to elucidate its pathogenesis, clinicopathological features and molecular profiles.

METHODS AND RESULTS: By reviewing our hospital's case database from 2021 to 2025, we retrospectively screened 92 cases of high-grade or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that had 11q fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing. Among them, 27 cases were confirmed to harbour 11q aberration and were enrolled in the present study. This cohort consisted of 24 males and 3 females with a median age of 61 years (range, 6-85). Eighteen (67%) patients presented with extranodal disease and nine (33%) had nodal disease. The gastrointestinal tract was the most commonly involved extranodal site (13 patients); two of these patients had concurrent lymph node involvement in the head and neck. Fourteen (52%) patients had advanced Ann Arbor stage (III, IV) disease. Eight (30%) patients had a history of immunocompromise including HIV infection, liver or kidney transplantation and other malignant tumours. The bone marrow was negative for lymphoma at initial diagnosis in all 21 patients assessed. Histologically, 20 (74%) cases had Burkitt-like or blastoid morphology and seven (26%) cases showed diffuse large B-cell-like morphology. Most cases (96%, 26/27) had a germinal centre B-cell immunophenotype. c-MYC was positive in all 26 tested cases and BCL2 was negative in 24 of 27 (89%) of cases. Mutational analysis was performed in 14 cases and potential driver mutations were identified in all involving 44 genes. The most frequently affected genes included TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC. Following therapy, 24 patients achieved complete remission and disease-free survival. The prognosis was not related to the morphological features, Ann Arbor stage, co-occurrence of MYC aberrations or the chemotherapy regimens.

CONCLUSIONS: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration may occur across all ages and confers a favourable prognosis. These tumours manifest morphological heterogeneity, and most cases display a Burkitt lymphoma-like immunophenotype characterized by CD10 positivity and BCL2 negativity. The most frequently mutated genes in our cohort are TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC.

articles.title: Stem cells inhibit cigarette smoke extract-induced dendritic cells activation and alleviate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common lung disease; however, these is a need for new therapeutic drugs. Herein, we prepared cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced dendritic cells (DCs) activation, and investigated the effects of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) on DCs. We found that BMSCs inhibited CSE induced DCs maturation. In addition, in COPD mice, BMSCs and umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UCBSCs) decreased percentage of DCs and macrophages in lungs. Furthermore, BMSCs and UCBSCs inhibited the mRNA level of inflammatory cytokines, such as TNFα, IL-6, IL-1β and iNOS via qRT-PCR. Nr4a family members were upregulated in COPD mice, and BMSC and UCBSC treatment inhibited Nr4a1, Nr4a2 and Nr4a3 expression via qRT-PCR, immunohistochemistry and Western blot. In addition, BMSCs and UCBSCs inhibited inflammation in colon of mice with CODP and regulated the gut microbiota using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Collectively, our findings reveal that Nr4a family members are involved in the BMSCs-and UCBSCs-amelioration of COPD.

articles.title: Physical activity and sleep patterns in women 1 year after gestational diabetes: Results from the Face-it study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and adequate, high-quality sleep are important for cardiometabolic health in women with recent gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) but are likely reduced during early motherhood. These behaviours may be associated; however, device-measured sleep data and studies of these associations remain scarce in this population. This cross sectional study characterised MVPA and sleep patterns and examined their associations in women with recent GDM.

METHODS: In the Face-it trial, 185 women provided device-measured MVPA and sleep data 1 year after delivery. Sleep variables included duration and efficiency, reflecting sleep quantity and quality. Duration was categorised as <6, 6-8 (reference) and >8 h/night. Associations with MVPA were analysed using linear mixed-effects models with site as a random intercept, adjusted for potential confounders.

RESULTS: Two-thirds (61.6%) met WHO recommendations for moderate-intensity physical activity (PA), whereas few (3.2%) met recommendations for vigorous-intensity PA. Most met recommendations for sleep duration (87.6%) and sleep efficiency (83.8%). Compared to 6-8 h/night, there was no difference in MVPA among those sleeping <6 h/night (β = -2.5, 95% CI = -11.8, 6.7, p = 0.593). Durations >8 h/night were associated with less MVPA (β = -13.5, 95% CI = -23.0, -4.0, p = 0.006). Sleep efficiency was positively associated with MVPA (β = 0.6, 95% CI = 0.1, 1.1, p = 0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: The association between high-quality sleep and greater MVPA suggests that PA and sleep may not only independently be relevant to cardiometabolic health but may also be associated in women with recent GDM.

articles.title: Occupational health and safety performance in the geomatics profession: the role of digital ergonomics, safety culture and international benchmarking.
articles.journal: International journal of occupational safety and ergonomics : JOSE
articles.abstract: This study investigates occupational health and safety (OHS) among geomatics professionals who alternate between terrain-based fieldwork and office-based digital tasks.
