A cross-sectional survey of 99 professionals in Uşak, Türkiye, was analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, multiple linear regression and strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) analysis. Slips and falls were reported by 28.1% of respondents, 37.5% considered protective equipment inadequate and 69% experienced musculoskeletal or visual discomfort during computer-based work. Although 81.3% had received OHS training, regular inspections covered only 53.1% of workplaces. Statistical analyses showed that training, equipment adequacy, ergonomic conditions, digital reporting and governance practices jointly shape OHS preparedness and perceived productivity. International benchmarking also indicated gaps in inspection coverage, equipment adequacy and digital integration. The findings demonstrate the dual physical and digital safety challenges of geomatics work and support stronger inspections, improved ergonomics, technology-oriented training, inclusive practices and sector-specific risk management for emerging geospatial technologies.

articles.title: Safe Surgery Starts With Safe Anesthesia: Positioning Pediatric Anesthesia as a Core Health-System Function Within Global Children's Surgical Systems.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children's surgery is increasingly recognized as a global health priority, yet pediatric anesthesia remains comparatively under-recognized despite being essential for safe surgical and perioperative care.

THE PROBLEM: Children require specialized expertise, age-appropriate equipment, reliable monitoring, oxygen, medicines, recovery, and critical care. In many low- and middle-income countries, deficiencies across these domains limit access and contribute to preventable perioperative morbidity and mortality.

THE CENTRAL CLAIM: We posit that children's surgical systems cannot be strengthened without parallel investment in pediatric anesthesia systems. Pediatric anesthesia should therefore be recognized as a cross-cutting core health-system function rather than a supporting clinical specialty.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: This perspective integrates the WHO Health Systems Building Blocks, the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plans, the GICS Optimal Resources for Children's Surgery framework, and Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model into an Integrated Pediatric Anesthesia Systems Framework (IPASF).

RECOMMENDATIONS: Governments, professional societies, academic institutions, global surgery organizations, and development partners should integrate pediatric anesthesia into surgical-system planning, workforce development, financing, service delivery, quality improvement, and research.

CONCLUSION: Safe and equitable children's surgery requires deliberate investment in the systems that enable safe anesthesia. The IPASF provides a practical framework for policy, implementation, education, research, and evaluation across the perioperative continuum.

articles.title: Motor difficulties, motor-related health care, and associating factors in children born extremely preterm.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the prevalence of non-cerebral-palsy (CP) motor difficulties in children born extremely preterm (EPT) in Sweden, and the proportion of children receiving motor-related health care (MRHC) and related factors.

METHOD: An observational, retrospective, cross-sectional registry study was performed on 856 children (435 males) born EPT at 5 years 6 months available from the Swedish Neonatal Quality Register (SNQ). Children with CP or severe neurodevelopmental disorders were excluded (n = 137). In total, 856 children had complete data. Motor function was assessed using the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (≤ 5th centile defined as clinically significant difficulty). The SNQ provided data on health care visits, behavioural issues, and neonatal risk factors. MRHC was defined as one or more physiotherapy visits in the past year.

RESULTS: Clinically significant motor difficulties were present in 218 of 856 (25.5%, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 22.5-28.4) children born EPT; only 30 of 177 (16.9%, 95% CI = 11.4-22.5) of them received MRHC. Receiving MRHC was associated with hyperactivity/inattention difficulties (odds ratio [OR] = 4.43; 95% CI = 1.52-12.88), bronchopulmonary dysplasia (OR = 4.38; 95% CI = 1.49-12.93), and access to additional health care services (OR = 16.07; 95% CI = 2.09-123.40).

INTERPRETATION: Clinically significant motor difficulties in children born EPT are underestimated and insufficiently managed. Factors associated with receiving MRHC suggest that care is reactive and driven more by comorbidities than motor needs. These findings reveal a critical care gap and underscore the need for standardized international guidelines for extended follow-up and management of non-CP motor difficulties.

articles.title: Targeting the Gut Microbiota-Metabolism Axis: Novel Pharmacological Mechanisms and Translational Application Strategies for Oral Antidiabetic Drugs.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a highly prevalent chronic metabolic disease worldwide, and the clinical prevention and control situation is severe. Although the various antidiabetic drugs currently in clinical use can lower blood glucose levels through different mechanisms, there are significant differences in efficacy among individuals. Existing evidence suggests that differences in gut microbiota (GM) composition and metabolic function may be one of the key factors contributing to the heterogeneity in drug efficacy. Based on this, this review describes the physiological and pathological mechanisms of the GM-metabolism axis and systematically reviews the modulatory effects of different classes of antidiabetic drugs on this axis and their underlying mechanisms. Available studies suggest that metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitors, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), thiazolidinediones (TZDs), and oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may differentially affect GM composition and/or microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), and bile acids. These alterations may be associated with glucose homeostasis and insulin resistance through pathways involving GPR41/43, HDACs, AMPK, mTORC1/S6K1, FXR-FGF15/19, and TGR5-GLP-1 signaling. By integrating clinical and mechanistic evidence, this review highlights the potential contribution of the GM-metabolism axis to the glucose-lowering effects of antidiabetic drugs. However, the quantity and confidence of evidence vary substantially across drug classes, and causal and clinical relevance requires further validation. These findings provide a basis for future research on personalized interventions for T2DM characterized by SCFA-producing bacterial deficiency, BCAA overload, or dysregulated bile acid metabolism.

articles.title: From Structural Modification to Diverse Pharmacological Activities: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives of Bile Acids.
articles.abstract: Bile acids (BAs) are amphiphilic steroid acids that exert a broad range of physiological effects-including the regulation of metabolism, immune responses, and inflammatory processes-through activation of specific receptors such as the farnesoid X receptor (FXR) and the G protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1 (TGR5). The gut microbiota plays a critical role in BA metabolism, and alterations in the BA pool have been closely linked to various metabolic disorders, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and type 2 diabetes. Consequently, targeting BA signaling pathways offers a novel mechanistic perspective for the prevention and treatment of these metabolic and inflammatory diseases. With growing insight into the biological functions of BAs, the development of BA-based therapeutics and their structural derivatives is emerging as a promising strategy for the management of metabolic diseases.

articles.title: [Thoracic trauma in Hungary today: heritage, current challenges and future directions].
articles.abstract: Thoracic trauma is an important contributor to morbidity and mortality among severely injured patients. While the management of immediately life-threatening intrathoracic injuries is relatively well defined, the treatment of severe blunt chest wall injuries, particularly multiple rib fractures and flail chest, remains variable across institutions. This review aims to summarize the current situation of thoracic trauma care in Hungary, with special emphasis on chest wall injuries and the role of surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF). SSRF should no longer be regarded as an isolated technical procedure, but as part of the complex, multidisciplinary management of patients with rib fractures. Therapeutic decision-making should be based not only on the number of fractured ribs, but also on fracture pattern, chest wall instability, pain, respiratory mechanics, pulmonary parenchymal injury, the patient's physiological reserve, overall injury severity and timing of surgery. The development of thoracic trauma care in Hungary requires a shared indication language, protocol-based imaging, early reassessment, multimodal analgesia, physiotherapy, transparent regional referral pathways and auditable outcome measurement. The existing Hungarian expertise in trauma surgery, thoracic surgery, emergency medicine and intensive care provides a realistic basis for establishing a structured, nationally applicable model of thoracic trauma care. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(42): 1686-1692.

articles.title: [Integrated use of ketamine in emergency care].
articles.abstract: Ketamine has emerged as a key drug in emergency medicine in recent years due to its rapid onset of action, hemodynamic stability properties and wide applicability. However, Hungarian regulation still limits its use mainly to anesthetic indications. The aim of this study was to review the literature on the emergency use of ketamine, with particular reference to its role in prehospital and intrahospital analgesia, sedation and rapid sequence intubation (RSI) protocols. A structured literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library databases, including relevant human studies from 2010 to 2024, and supplemented by selected pre-2010 landmark studies that are pivotal in the historical and clinical context of ketamine use in emergency care. The retrieved publications were thematically categorized, and narrative synthesis was applied. Based on 82 studies reviewed, ketamine was found to be effective and safe in acute analgesia, procedural sedation, agitation management and RSI. Side effects are predominantly mild and well managed. Previous contraindications in patients with head injury are increasingly questioned in the current international literature. The place of ketamine in emergency care is evidence-based. Its use fits well into modern multidisciplinary emergency protocols. It is recommended to update national recommendations in line with international practices. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(42): 1679-1685.

articles.title: Antithrombin III use in pediatric and neonatal ECMO: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAntithrombin (AT) supplementation has been increasingly incorporated into pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) anticoagulation protocols to address heparin resistance and optimize anticoagulation. However, considerable variability exists in monitoring practices, replacement strategies, and reported clinical outcomes. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate contemporary evidence regarding AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies evaluating AT monitoring or supplementation during neonatal or pediatric ECMO through September 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on monitoring strategies, replacement protocols, anticoagulation parameters, thrombosis, bleeding, and mortality. Comparative studies reporting extractable dichotomous outcomes were included in random-effects meta-analyses.ResultsTwenty-five studies met inclusion criteria, consisting predominantly of retrospective single-center cohorts. Marked heterogeneity was observed in indications for supplementation, replacement thresholds (50-100%), therapeutic targets (60-120%), formulations, dosing strategies, and anticoagulation monitoring. AT supplementation consistently increased AT activity, improved anti-factor Xa measurements, and in several studies, reduced unfractionated heparin requirement. However, higher anti-Xa levels and increased AT activity did not consistently translate into improved clinical outcomes. Meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between AT supplementation and thrombosis (OR 1.10, 95% 0.54-2.24), bleeding (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.85-1.54), or mortality (OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.63-2.43). Pharmacokinetic investigations suggested standard dosing frequently underestimates replacement requirements in pediatric ECMO.ConclusionCurrent evidence supports the role of AT supplementation in improving laboratory markers of anticoagulation, but does not demonstrate consistent reductions in bleeding, thrombosis, or mortality. Wide variation in monitoring, dosing, and outcome definitions limits comparisons across studies. Future multicenter investigations should prioritize standardized definitions, age-specific therapeutic targets, and prospective evaluation of replacement strategies to better define the role of AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO.

articles.title: Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca2+-CaMKK2-AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one-third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb-associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (db/db, ob/ob, HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes in vitro. Hepatocyte-specific CBX2 overexpression ameliorates hepatic steatosis, improves glucose metabolism, and suppresses inflammation, whereas CBX2 deficiency exacerbates these metabolic disturbances. Mechanistically, CBX2 enhances H3K4me3 enrichment at the Orai1 promoter, promoting Orai1 transcription and increasing intracellular Ca2+ levels. Elevated Ca2+ activates the CaMKK2-AMPK signaling pathway, leading to ACC phosphorylation, inhibition of de novo lipogenesis (FAS, ACC, and SCD-1), enhancement of fatty acid oxidation (PPARα and CPT-1a), and suppression of NF-κB/JNK-mediated inflammation. Genetic and pharmacological interventions further establish the necessity of this Ca2+-CaMKK2-AMPK axis for CBX2-mediated metabolic protection. Collectively, our findings reveal a CBX2-driven metabolic regulatory circuit and highlight CBX2 and its downstream signaling pathway as potential therapeutic targets for MASLD.

articles.title: Optogenetic cardioversion: To depolarize or to hyperpolarize?
Evaluation of Agricultural Heat-Related Illness Prevention Training in Colorado.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Agricultural workers have high rates of heat-related illnesses (HRI). State-level regulations regarding HRI prevention in agriculture have been evolving and include requirements for heat-related prevention training of workers. There has been limited evaluation of the effectiveness of HRI prevention training. This study aimed to evaluate a train-the-trainer HRI prevention program.

METHODS: In 2024 and 2025, there were 13 train-the-trainer HRI prevention sessions held in English and Spanish in Colorado. The trainers then trained agricultural workers in their workplaces. Using the Kirkpatrick evaluation framework and a series of surveys and focus groups, changes in participant reaction levels, learning, behavior, and workplace outcomes were assessed. Descriptive statistics and paired t-test were used to analyze survey responses. Thematic analysis was used to analyze focus group data.

RESULTS: Across 13 sessions, 143 trainers completed the train-the-trainer program, who then trained 1,270 agricultural workers. The trainers expressed high levels of satisfaction with the training and had significant improvement in their knowledge of HRI symptoms and prevention strategies. Training led to increased confidence among trainers in their ability to train workers. Trainers and agricultural workers reported adopting practices to prevent HRI.

CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence that a bilingual, regulatory-aligned train-the-trainer program can be an effective approach to build HRI prevention capacity among agricultural employers. The Colorado-based train-the-trainer HRI prevention program increased trainer knowledge and confidence and in turn improved agricultural worker workplace heat-related prevention practices. These changes may protect worker health while also improving their well-being and productivity in the long term.

articles.title: Full-spectrum LED screen-bar lighting as an adjunct to artificial tears in visual display terminal-related dry eye: a randomized study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the short-term clinical effect of adding a full-spectrum screen-bar lamp as an environmental adjunct to artificial tear therapy in participants with newly diagnosed visual display terminal (VDT)-related dry eye.

METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, single-center study, 66 participants with newly diagnosed VDT-related dry eye and limited corneal staining were assigned to a full-spectrum screen-bar lamp plus artificial tears (intervention group, n = 34) or artificial tears alone with no study lamp (control group, n = 32). Primary endpoints were changes in Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) and non-invasive tear breakup time (NIBUT) from baseline to one month.

RESULTS: The modified intention-to-treat population included 65 participants. OSDI improved significantly in both groups at 1 month (both P < 0.001), with greater symptom reduction in the intervention group (adjusted between-group difference, - 7.33; P = 0.042). NIBUT increased in both groups (P < = 0.017), without a significant between-group difference (adjusted difference, 0.26; P = 0.726). No significant between-group differences were observed in changes in tear meniscus height, conjunctival hyperemia, lipid layer thickness of the tear film or partial blinking rate. No study-related adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding a full-spectrum lamp to artificial tears was associated with a greater short-term improvement in subjective dry eye symptoms in VDT-related dry eye, without corresponding between-group differences in objective ocular surface parameters. Further studies are required to confirm these findings. Trial registration number ChiCTR2400084309, 2024/05/14.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows.

DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

articles.title: Indirect Echocardiographic Signs of Increased Right-sided Afterload in Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis: Insights from a Multicentre Italian Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pulmonary vascular involvement is a determinant of worse outcomes in fibrotic lung diseases. Its prevalence and prognostic relevance in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of indirect echocardiographic abnormalities in progressive pulmonary fibrosis before antifibrotic therapy, characterize a baseline high-risk cardiopulmonary functional profile, and assess 12-month clinical trajectories.

METHODS: Observational, retrospective, multicentre study.

RESULTS: 158 patients (median (IQR) age of 71 (65.2-77.0) years) with PPF were enrolled. Thirty (19.0%) had ≥ 1 echocardiographic indirect sign of increased right-sided afterload, 15 (9.5%) ≥ 2, 9 (5.7%) ≥ 3 and 1 (0.6%) all four. A shortened right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (< 105 ms) was the most frequent alteration (12.7%), followed by right atrial dilation (10.8%). In univariable analysis, ≥1 sign was associated with male sex, a lower DLCO% predicted, a higher FVC%/DLCO% ratio and a shorter 6MWD; in the multivariable model only, male sex remained independently associated (aOR 3.45, 95% CI 0.99-12.07; p = 0.052). Twelve-month FVC trajectories did not differ by baseline echocardiographic status; nonetheless, ≥1 sign was associated with shorter time to acute exacerbation (log-rank p = 0.007) and all-cause hospitalisation (p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic signs suggestive of increased right-sided afterload are present in a substantial proportion of PPF patients at the time of antifibrotic initiation. They identified patients at higher risk of acute exacerbation and hospitalisation, regardless of FVC decline. This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.

articles.title: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) Pharyngeal Total Score in Post-Stroke Dysphagia.
articles.abstract: The Modified Barium Swallow Impairment Profile (MBSImP) is widely used to quantify swallowing physiology during videofluoroscopic swallowing assessment, but the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for its pharyngeal total score in post-stroke dysphagia remains unclear. This study estimated the MCID for improvement in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score during inpatient rehabilitation. This prospective multicenter observational study included stroke survivors with dysphagia admitted for inpatient rehabilitation 2 weeks to 3 months after stroke onset. Baseline and 10-day follow-up assessments included the MBSImP pharyngeal total score, Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). The FOIS was used as the primary anchor, while the PAS and PGIC were secondary anchors. Anchor-based estimates were calculated using average change, change difference, linear regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Distribution-based estimates and minimal detectable change were used as complementary context for interpreting the anchor-based estimates. Sensitivity analyses were performed using stricter or collapsed anchor definitions, including collapsed FOIS categories, ≥ 2-level FOIS improvement, collapsed PAS categories, and a stricter PGIC threshold. An exploratory interaction analysis additionally examined whether the MBSImP change associated with exactly 1-level versus exactly 2-level FOIS improvement varied according to baseline FOIS level. A total of 161 participants were included. The MBSImP pharyngeal total score decreased from a median of [9.00 (7.00, 11.00)] to [4.00 (2.00, 6.00)]. The mean improvement, used for anchor-based MCID estimation, was 4.27 points. Changes in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score were significantly correlated with the FOIS, PAS, and PGIC (r > 0.3). The pooled average-change and change-difference estimates under the prespecified anchor definitions were 2.977 and 2.004 points, respectively. Under stricter or category-based anchor definitions, average-change estimates increased to 4.633-5.141 points, whereas change-difference estimates remained comparatively stable at 1.731-2.554 points. ROC-derived cutoffs were 2-3 points under the prespecified definitions and 5 points under the stricter definitions. In the exploratory FOIS analysis, there was no evidence that the contrast between exactly 1-level and exactly 2-level improvement varied by baseline FOIS level (P for interaction = 0.776); findings were similar when restricted to baseline FOIS levels 2-5 (P = 0.503). Clinically important change in the MBSImP pharyngeal total score depended on the anchor definition and intended interpretation. Under the prespecified anchor definitions, average-change estimates were approximately 3 points, whereas stricter functional or swallowing-safety improvement definitions showed estimates close to 5 points. In contrast, change-difference estimates were comparatively stable at approximately 2 points across anchor definitions.

articles.title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

articles.title: A Micropeptide Component of the OGDH Complex Modulates ATP Production in the TCA Cycle.
articles.abstract: Since its elucidation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle has been regarded as a fully defined enzymatic pathway. Here, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized micropeptide component of this central metabolic system. Through analyzing ribosome profiling data from the mouse sORFs.org database, we discovered APPM (ATP production-promoting micropeptide), a 29-amino acid peptide encoded by a non-canonical small open reading frame within the mouse Ctsb gene. APPM localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane, where it directly binds to the E1 subunit (OGDH) of the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDHc). This interaction modulates OGDHc enzymatic activity, thereby regulating NADH and ATP production. We identified tyrosine-13 as the critical residue mediating the APPM-OGDH interaction and functional activation. Exogenous APPM administration increased ATP levels in vivo and, in a mouse model of heart failure, restored cardiac function, outperforming the reference drug trimetazidine. Collectively, our findings identify APPM as the first micropeptide regulator of the OGDH complex, expanding the known repertoire of the TCA cycle and presenting a potential therapeutic strategy for diseases characterized by bioenergetic insufficiency.

articles.title: Outcomes After Major Amputation in Octogenarians.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMajor lower extremity amputations, defined as above-ankle amputations, are morbid and significantly life-changing. Older patients may be more susceptible to poor outcomes. Our goal was to assess the short- and long-term outcomes of major amputations in octogenarians.MethodsA retrospective single-center chart review was performed on all octogenarian patients who underwent a major amputation at a safety-net hospital between 2014-2023. Demographics, operative characteristics, postoperative outcomes, and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were collected and analyzed. Multivariable binary logistic regression evaluated factors associated with 1-year mortality. Fisher's exact test evaluated univariate categorical comparisons because of small cell frequencies.Results56 octogenarian patients underwent a major amputation: 96.4% underwent an amputation for chronic limb-threatening ischemia while 3.6% of patients had acute limb ischemia. Above-knee and below-knee amputations accounted for 73.2 and 26.8% of procedures, respectively; 10.6% were guillotine amputations. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 26.3% of cases, and total mean hospital length of stay (LOS) was 13.7 days. Postoperatively, 55.4% were discharged to a skilled nursing facility, 17.9% patients to an acute rehab facility, and 12.5% to home with assistance. Thirty-day emergency department use rate was 14.3%, and hospital readmission rate was 12.5%. Most patients (83.9%) were non-ambulatory at 1-year. In-hospital mortality was 8.9%, 30-day mortality was 14.3%, and 1-year mortality was 35.7%. Univariate analyses demonstrated no statistically significant differences among evaluated variables. Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was also not statistically significant.ConclusionMajor amputations in octogenarians are highly morbid with high ICU utilization and prolonged LOS with frequent discharge to acute care facilities. About one-third of patients are not alive at 1-year. These findings suggest the need to identify opportunities for improvement in this high-risk patient population undergoing amputations, such as early revascularization, aggressive rehabilitation in concert with geriatrician collaboration, medical optimization, and improved goals-of-care discussions.

articles.title: Cardiology Support Utilization Patterns and Associated Barriers Across Northwestern Ontario.
articles.abstract: The Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre On-Call Cardiology Support Service serves a geographically vast region across Northwestern Ontario where cardiovascular disease is a major burden. The objective is to analyze service utilization patterns including locations, indications, interventions, and barriers. In this 6-month prospective study, cardiologists collected data via survey on calls from rural and remote providers. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used. The Canadian Institute for Health Information's Rural Health Systems Model was used for interpretation. Two hundred and six responses across 19 locations identified: common consultations-chest pain, dyspnea, and atrial fibrillation; frequent interventions-medical recommendations, education, and transfer decisions; key barriers-limited personnel knowledge and infrastructure. Significant associations were identified. This study characterized cardiology support service utilization across Northwestern Ontario, identifying key barriers and opportunities to strengthen rural health systems planning and cardiovascular care. These findings can inform targeted initiatives and support future evaluations.

articles.title: HIV-1 diagnosis during pre-exposure prophylaxis: A case report.
articles.abstract: We report a case of HIV diagnosis in a 36-year-old man who has sex with men receiving daily oral PrEP (emtricitabine/tenofovir) in Argentina, where viral load or HIV PCR testing is not routinely available before or during prophylaxis. In 2022, PrEP was initiated after a diagnosis of primary syphilis, with a non-reactive fourth-generation HIV test performed 13 days earlier (outside the recommended window), so very early infection already present at initiation cannot be excluded. Self-reported adherence was >95%. Serology was negative at day 23 and became reactive at day 73, with an indeterminate Western blot (gp120 only), undetectable plasma HIV-RNA and preserved lymphocyte counts; dolutegravir was added to complete antiretroviral treatment. Standard diagnostic algorithms were initially inconclusive, and confirmation required approaches beyond routine practice: HIV-1 RNA was detected only after ultracentrifugation of 14 mL of plasma (55 copies), and low-level proviral HIV-1 DNA was identified after analysis of an extensive number of cells; Nef- and p24-specific T-cell responses were also detected. No resistance-associated mutations were found on proviral DNA (integrase region). The Western blot eventually became positive at day 382, while a rapid immunochromatographic assay remained negative at 34 months. Atypical presentations of this kind have been reported under oral TDF/FTC PrEP and were subsequently characterized as long-acting early viral inhibition (LEVI) syndrome, predominantly in the context of long-acting cabotegravir. The present case illustrates the extent of non-routine investigation required to confirm HIV acquisition, and the challenges this poses in settings where oral PrEP is the only available option and HIV-1 RNA PCR cannot be routinely deployed. PrEP should be initiated promptly following a negative HIV test performed on the same day, or as close as possible to PrEP initiation, particularly when recent exposure is possible. HIV testing should be repeated sequentially after initiation, and discordant results should prompt continued serological and molecular evaluation.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental and symptomatic hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo compare the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental pulmonary embolism (IPE) and symptomatic pulmonary embolism (SPE), and to inform risk-stratified management.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed 287 patients with hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism (HA-PE). Demographic, clinical, imaging, and laboratory data were collected. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses.ResultsAmong 287 patients, 87 had IPE and 200 had SPE. IPE was more frequently classified as low-risk PE (63.22% vs. 31.50%, p < 0.001) and more often involved pulmonary artery branches (73.56% vs. 58.00%, p = 0.01), whereas SPE was more commonly intermediate- or high-risk. The 1-month survival rate was higher in the IPE group than in the SPE group (95.4% vs. 75.5%, hazard ratio [HR]: 5.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.51 - 16.5, p < 0.001), but this difference was not significant after 1 month. In IPE, cancer and bleeding were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality. In SPE, cancer and immobilization were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation, thrombectomy, and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality.ConclusionsIPE is generally associated with lower-risk, more peripheral PE, but anticoagulation should be individualized. SPE requires prompt risk stratification and timely anticoagulation, with reperfusion or thrombectomy considered for selected high-risk or deteriorating patients.

articles.title: Remote Ischemic Conditioning and Cerebral Oxygen Saturation: The Cerebral Oxygenation-Conditioning Response (Co-CoRe) Framework.
articles.abstract: Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) is a promising noninvasive intervention that may enhance endogenous cerebroprotective mechanisms following ischemic stroke. Although clinical studies suggest potential benefits, the physiological mechanisms underlying RIC remain incompletely understood, particularly whether RIC-associated hemodynamic changes are accompanied by changes in cerebral tissue oxygenation. No conceptual framework currently integrates these relationships to guide future research. The purpose of this paper is to present the Cerebral Oxygenation-Conditioning Response (CO-CoRe) Framework, a mechanistic conceptual framework describing the hypothesized relationships among RIC, compensatory cerebral blood flow, cerebroprotection, and cerebral regional oxygen saturation (CrSO₂) following ischemic stroke. The CO-CoRe Framework integrates evidence-supported relationships among RIC, compensatory cerebral blood flow, and cerebroprotection with a hypothesized relationship between RIC and CrSO2, providing a mechanistic foundation for examining cerebral tissue oxygenation following ischemic stroke. By synthesizing current evidence on ischemic conditioning, cerebrovascular physiology, and cerebral tissue oxygenation, the CO-CoRe Framework generates testable hypotheses and provides a foundation for future research evaluating CrSO₂, measured using near-infrared spectroscopy, as a physiological response to RIC. Ultimately, the framework may advance understanding of RIC-associated cerebroprotection and inform physiologic monitoring strategies in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Patterns of cardiovascular disease subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar, Pakistan: a multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Evidence on CVD subtypes in young Pakistani adults is limited. This study characterized CVD subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

METHODS: A multicentre, cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals among patients aged 18-45 years. Data were extracted from three-year hospital records. Associations were assessed using chi-square/Fisher's exact tests and logistic regression.

RESULTS: 8,650 CVD cases, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults, predominantly male (64.6%), with a median age of 40 years (IQR: 36-44). ACS was the most common subtype (61.0%), followed by cardiomyopathy (39.0%). Overweight/obesity (77.0%), hypertension (56.5%), smoking (39.7%), dyslipidaemia (21.8%), and diabetes (14.4%) were the most prevalent factors. Compared with ACS, cardiomyopathy was independently associated with high heart rate, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, and family history. Smoking was associated with lower odds of cardiomyopathy than ACS (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41-0.61, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Young adults accounted for 24.2% of CVD cases, with ACS and cardiomyopathy the most common subtypes, highlighting the need for targeted strategies. The cross-sectional design, findings indicate subtype differences rather than causal effects, while supporting smoking cessation and early hypertension detection in young adults.

articles.title: Alkalizer-based gastroretentive floating tablets of amoxicillin for localized gastric delivery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Helicobacter pylori infection is a leading cause of peptic ulcer disease, yet amoxicillin trihydrate (AMX) efficacy is limited by its acid-catalyzed degradation and rapid gastric emptying. This study aimed to develop alkalizer-based gastroretentive floating tablets to enhance localized gastric-delivery and improve AMX stability under gastric conditions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Floating tablets were prepared by direct compression using HPMC K100M, sodium-bicarbonate and microcrystalline-cellulose. A 23 factorial-design (RStudio-v4.3.3) was used to optimize microenvironmental pH, floating lag time (FLT) and drug release. Optimized tablets were characterized for micromeritic properties, XRD, SEM, in vitro buoyancy, swelling, drug release, in vitro anti-H. pylori activity and in vivo gastric retention in Sprague-Dawley rats.

RESULTS: The optimized formulation achieved a microenvironmental pH of 7.20 ± 0.26, FLT of 15.84 ± 0.50 s, and total floating time of approximately 12 h. Cumulative AMX release reached 98.49 ± 1.69% over 12 h with non-Fickian kinetics, and XRD/SEM analysis indicated reduced crystallinity and increased amorphous character of AMX within the hydrated matrix. The formulation showed significant in vitro anti-H. pylori activity and prolonged in vivo gastric retention.

CONCLUSION: Alkalizer-based gastroretentive floating AMX tablets combined microenvironmental pH modulation with sustained gastric-retention, supporting their potential as a localized strategy for improved H. pylori eradication.

articles.title: Early dietitian-led nutrition intervention and unplanned intensive care unit transfer in hospitalized adults with nutritional risk: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malnutrition and nutritional risk are common among inpatients and are associated with adverse outcomes. Although dietitian-led individualized nutrition intervention is recommended, evidence from routine practice among non-critically ill inpatients remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between early dietitian-led nutrition intervention and deterioration-related outcomes among adults at nutritional risk.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from a Chinese tertiary hospital (2016-2023). Adults aged 18-90 years with Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 scores ≥3 were included; patients directly admitted to intensive care unit were excluded. Patients receiving early dietitian-led nutrition intervention within 72 h after hospital admission were propensity score matched 1:1 to comparators. Outcomes were unplanned intensive care unit transfer, major gastrointestinal events after admission, and predefined clinically meaningful changes in laboratory indicators. Associations were estimated using logistic regression and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 96,532 eligible patients, 16,661 (17.3%) received early dietitian-led nutrition intervention. After matching, 16,419 pairs were analyzed. Early dietitian-led nutrition intervention was associated with lower odds of intensive care unit transfer (3.0% vs. 3.4%; OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.77-0.99), major gastrointestinal events (4.0% vs. 4.4%; OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.99), and higher odds of clinically meaningful reduction in C-reactive protein (12.6% vs. 10.9%; OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.11-1.27).

CONCLUSION: Early dietitian-led nutrition intervention was associated with lower odds of deterioration-related outcomes among hospitalized adults at nutritional risk. Limited early dietitian involvement despite routine nutritional risk screening suggests an implementation gap and warrants further prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Adjuvant Systemic Therapies After Nephrectomy for Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis and Multi-Criteria Benefit-Risk Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant pembrolizumab has improved disease-free survival after nephrectomy for high-risk renal cell carcinoma, and pembrolizumab plus belzutifan has further expanded the treatment landscape.

OBJECTIVE: We compared efficacy and treatment burden across adjuvant systemic therapies and examined the benefit-risk trade-off of the combination.

METHODS: Randomized trials of systemic therapy after nephrectomy were synthesized using a Bayesian network meta-analysis. Disease-free survival hazard ratios were converted to illustrative 2-year estimates using a common pembrolizumab baseline. Observed differences in 2-year disease-free survival, grade 3 or higher adverse events, and treatment discontinuation came from LITESPARK-022. Using these data, a multi-criteria decision analysis examined how outcome weighting affected the balance between the two regimens.

RESULTS: Six randomized datasets formed a tree-shaped network of eight regimens. In LITESPARK-022, adding belzutifan yielded approximately seven additional disease-free patients per 100 treated, but also approximately 22 additional patients with grade 3 or higher adverse events and 15 additional treatment discontinuations. Under the primary decision-analytic assumptions, the combination had the higher net-benefit score only when disease-free survival received roughly two thirds of the decision weight (threshold 0.68; range 0.47-0.79 across sensitivity analyses). Most comparisons relied on a single dataset, and overall survival and patient-reported outcomes remained immature.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding belzutifan to pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival but increased toxicity and treatment discontinuation. The decision analysis illustrates a model-dependent trade-off rather than identifying a preferred regimen. Because overall survival data are immature, the decision to intensify treatment remains risk and preference sensitive.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261454205.

articles.title: Echocardiographic estimates of pulmonary artery acceleration time and mortality risk in older adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery acceleration time (PAAT) is an echocardiographic measure associated with pulmonary artery pressure. Although reduced PAAT has been linked to pulmonary hypertension and adverse outcomes in selected patient populations, less is known about its prognostic significance in community-dwelling older adults, which was the focus of the present study.

METHODS: Using baseline echocardiographic PAAT measurements, we categorized 2758 participants in the Cardiovascular Health Study into PAAT >130 ms (N = 758), 100-130 ms (N = 1089), and <100 ms (N = 911). Cox regression models were used to estimate associations with mortality (reference, PAAT >130 ms), and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess nonlinearity of the associations (reference, PAAT 130 ms), during a median follow-up of 13.4 years.

RESULTS: All-cause mortality occurred in 75.2%, 82.9%, and 85.5% of participants with PAAT >130 ms, 100-130 ms, and <100 ms, respectively. Corresponding age-sex-race-adjusted HRs (95% CIs) were 1.00, 1.11 (0.99-1.23) and 1.20 (1.08-1.34). Associations were attenuated primarily by adjustment for World Health Organization Group 2 (cardiac) but not Group 3 (pulmonary) pulmonary hypertension physiology and by adjustment for subclinical biomarkers and were no longer significant in fully adjusted models. Associations and attenuations were stronger for cardiovascular mortality than non-cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated no significant nonlinearity in age-sex-race-adjusted HRs for total mortality, which increased progressively at PAAT values below 130 ms.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower PAAT is associated with higher risks of death in community-dwelling older adults. The association appears to be explained largely by cardiovascular disease and systemic health status rather than pulmonary disease alone. PAAT may serve as an integrated marker of cardiopulmonary and systemic vulnerability in older adults.

articles.title: Comparison of cardiovascular events in patients with metastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer treated with LHRH agonists to LHRH antagonists in the US: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is standard treatment for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSCaP). Patients receive LHRH-agonists (LHRH-AG: leuprolide, goserelin or triptorelin) or LHRH-antagonists (LHRH-AN: degarelix or relugolix) with intensification with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, with or without chemotherapy. Given ongoing concerns about cardiovascular risk, we used real-world data from TriNetX to compare the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) between patients receiving LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included adult patients with mHSCaP who received either an LHRH-AG or LHRH-AN. The composite primary outcome was MACE (defined as myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or all-cause mortality). Secondary outcomes were MI, stroke, and all-cause mortality. Patients were 1:1 propensity-score matched (PSM). Kaplan-Meier analysis reporting hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the outcomes was conducted. We conducted a subgroup analysis to assess the effect of intensification of therapy. Exploratory analyses were conducted to assess HR of outcomes and new-onset metabolic comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, insulin use, hypertension, and dyslipidemia) amongst patients without cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: Before PSM, there were 27,051 in LHRH-AG and 3,339 in LHRH-AN cohorts. After PSM, 3,329 patients in each cohort were compared. Compared to LHRH-AN, LHRH-AG was associated with a decreased risk of MACE (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93), MI (HR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.66-0.97), and any-cause mortality (HR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.78-0.93). Treatment intensification did not modify the association between MACE outcomes and LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.

CONCLUSIONS: Using real-world data, LHRH-AG was associated with a decreased risk of experiencing MACE. Among those undergoing intensification of therapy, there was no difference in MACE risk associated with LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.

articles.title: Cost-utility of expanded hypertension screening and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud: a Markov model using national data.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We assessed the cost-utility of expanding hypertension screening, diagnosis, and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud (SIS).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Analyses assembled in May 2026 used a 10-year cohort Markov model parameterized with the 2024 Peruvian Demographic and Family Health Survey (ENDES), SIS administrative data for 2022-2024, and published parameters. Universal and risk-targeted scenarios were compared with population-specific usual care, using S/ 25,007 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY).

RESULTS: The baseline sample included 6,098 adults aged 40-74 years; hypertension prevalence was 28.9%. Universal 80-80-80 expansion averted 60.7 cardiovascular events and 6.1 cardiovascular deaths and gained 51.3 QALYs per 100,000 eligible adults. Incremental cost was S/ 7,784,979, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of S/ 151,686/QALY. The scenario targeting 10-year cardiovascular risk ≥10% had an ICER of S/ 60,171/QALY in its eligible subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: All scenarios exceeded the threshold. Lower targeted-scenario ICERs concern different eligible populations. Estimates depend on modeled effects, the 10-year horizon, and exclusion of event-related savings.

articles.title: [Systemic sclerosis with anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody associated vasculitis: A case report].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease involving microvessels and a wide range of connective tissues. Anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a primary, systemic necrotizing small vasculitis. The coexistence of AAV and SSc is rare. We report a case of SSc combined with AAV complicated with alveolar hemorrhage, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and cerebral hemorrhage. The patient was a 56-year-old woman with a 20-year history of Raynaud phenomenon, skin sclerosis on the fingertip and face. She developed dry cough for 1 year and shortness of breath after activity for 1month. Blood routine test showed moderate anemia, blood biochemistry showed renal function damage, and urine routine test showed positive urine protein and occult blood. Immunological examination showed that anti-topoisomerase Ⅰ (anti-SCL-70) antibody was positive. Lung CT showed interstitial fibrosis in both lower lungs. Systemic sclerosis and chronic renal injury were diagnosed and she was treated with low-dose prednisone and nifedipine. During the treatment, the patient developed rapidly progressive renal insufficiency, immunological indicator showed positive anti-myeloperoxidase antibody (MPO), and renal pathology suggested crescentic glomerulonephritis. The renal damage was considered to be caused by vasculitis, and the diagnosis was modified as systemic sclerosis complicated with AAV, with crescentic nephritis and interstitial lung disease. She was treated with methylprednisolone 500 mg. One day later, the patient developed hemoptysis, alveolar hemorrhage was considered, and treatment was adjusted to methylprednisolone 1 g for 3 days, plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide. Three days later, she had vomiting coffee-colored gastric contents and melena. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage was considered, and methylprednisolone was reduced to 80 mg. Plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide treatment were continued, supplemented by acid suppression. The patient's condition was finally controlled, improved and discharged. One month later, the patient developed cough and sputum, and lung CT showed pulmonary infection. During anti-infection treatment, the patient developed gastrointestinal hemorrhage again, accompanied by cerebral hemorrhage, and finally died. This case shows that the incidence of SSc combined with AAV is dangerous, mainly with kidney involvement, manifested as crescents glomerulonephritis. When combined with alveolar hemorrhage, cerebral hemorrhage, the mortality rate is high. Clinicians should pay attention to it, early diagnosis and active treatment should be taken seriously.

articles.title: [Livedoid vasculopathy: A case report].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract: Livedoid vasculopathy (LV) is a painful and thrombotic obliterative vascular disorder characterized by spontaneous thrombus formation within skin capillaries or small veins, ultimately leading to localized hypoxia and the development of skin ulcers. LV is a rare condition predominantly affecting young women, with an incidence rate of approximately 1/100 000. Clinically, it manifests as recurrent reticular green spots and painful ulcers on the distal lower extremities, which subsequently heal, leaving behind white and atrophic scars, termed "white atrophy". The skin manifestations of the disease are prominent, often seen in dermatology. Recently, the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology of Honghui Hospital, Xi ' an Jiaotong University, admitted a patient with LV. This young female patient presented with recurrent lower limb skin purpura and ulcers, which had occurred spontaneously during the summer for the past three years. Following a skin biopsy conducted at another hospital, she was diagnosed with LV and subsequently treated with phototherapy, anticoagulation therapy, and topical corticosteroids, yet there was no improvement in her condition. In April of this year, she sought further treatment at our hospital and was admitted for comprehensive care. After completing a thorough battery of relevant examinations, we excluded other potential vascular disorders, abnormal coagulation profiles, and autoimmune diseases, such as cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cPAN), leukocyte-cracking vasculitis (LCV), and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). The patient remained definitively diagnosed with LV. Under our department's care, she received oral glucocorticoids, tacrolimus for immune modulation, and colchicine for anti-inflammatory effects. Subsequently, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged from the hospital. Four months post-discharge, a follow-up examination revealed significant improvement in her symptoms. The therapeutic approaches for LV encompassed general therapy, antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy, glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy, intravenous human immunoglobulin therapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Additionally, the use of biologics, including tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and small molecule targeted JAK inhibitors, had been reported in LV cases. Further randomized controlled trials are necessary to validate these treatment options. This report presented a case of LV where favorable outcomes were achieved through a combination of anticoagulant and immunosuppressive therapies. Nevertheless, given that the patient has been afflicted with the disease for three years and we have only conducted a four-month follow-up, which is relatively short, continued long-term follow-up of this patient remains imperative.

articles.title: [Clinical characteristics and risk factors of patients with rheumatoid arthritis complicated with urinary tract infection].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical characteristics of urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), to evaluate the effects of different treatment regimens on the risk of UTI, and to identify independent risk factors for UTI complicated with RA.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. RA patients hospitalized in the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Baotou Medical College from September 2020 to September 2023 were enrolled. General clinical data, laboratory indicators and medication information of the patients were collected. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of UTI for comparative analysis. Patients were grouped based on different treatment regimens received, and the proportions of UTI occurrence were compared among each group. The results of urine culture and drug susceptibility test in the RA patients with UTI were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analyses were further performed to screen relevant factors for UTI in the RA patients, and the diagnostic value of combined indicators was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.

RESULTS: A total of 196 RA patients were included, among whom 99 cases were complicated with UTI and 97 cases without UTI. Compared with the non-UTI group, the UTI group had higher proportions of female patients, patients aged ≥65 years, patients with RA disease duration ≥10 years, patients hospitalized for infection within the past two years, and patients with comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, hypertension, etc.). Peripheral blood leukocyte count, percentage of neutrophils, serum procalcitonin, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein level were elevated (P < 0.05), while hemoglobin, percentage of lymphocytes and plasma albumin level were decreased (P < 0.05). The RA patients were divided into four groups according to different treatment regimens: ①glucocorticoids (GCs) monotherapy group; ②conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) monotherapy group; ③csDMARDs combined with GCs group; ④ csDMARDs combined with biological DMARDs (bDMARDs)/ targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) group. The overall difference in UTI proportion among the four groups was statistically significant (P < 0.001). After Bonferroni correction, the UTI proportion in group ① and group ③ was higher than that in group ② and group ④ (adjusted P < 0.05). GSs use was associated with increased UTI risk, and the risk of UTI showed an upward trend with the increase of daily dose. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that RA disease duration ≥10 years, previous hospitalization due to infection within the past two years, comorbid diabetes mellitus, and elevated disease activity score in 28 joints based on ESR (DAS28-ESR) were independent risk factors for UTI in the RA patients. The area under the ROC curve of the diagnostic model constructed with the above combined predictors was 0.82 (95%CI: 0.76-0.88), with a sensitivity of 0.67 and a specificity of 0.94. Gram-negative bacteria were the predominant pathogens in urine culture of the RA patients with UTI, among which Escherichia coli accounted for 67.71%. Among evaluable single-isolate bacterial strains with available drug-susceptibility results, the resistance rates to levofloxacin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole were 65.4% and 52.8%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Clinical infection surveillance should be strengthened in RA patients. GCs should be rationally used on the premise of effective RA disease control, and bDMARDs/tsDMARDs therapy should be initiated timely according to disease status to reduce GCs exposure and minimize the risk of UTI. Meanwhile, antimicrobial agents should be selected in a standardized manner based on urine culture and drug susceptibility test results.

articles.title: [Risk factors of carotid atherosclerosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the characteristics of lipid profile and the risk factors of carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

METHODS: Subjects with 216 RA and 214 healthy controls, both without known cardiovascular disease (CVD), were included. CAS plaques were determined by color Doppler ultrasound. Lipid levels were compared between RA patients and healthy controls, and independent risk factors for CAS plaques in the RA patients were analyzed.

RESULTS: (1) The total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels were lower (P < 0.001, P=0.001, P < 0.001), TC/HDL-C and LDL-C/HDL-C were higher (P=0.003, P=0.009) in the RA group than in the healthy controls. (2) In RA group, TC and HDL-C were negatively correlated with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) (r=-0.237, P=0.002; r=-0.351, P < 0.001), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (r=-0.210, P=0.006; r=-0.182, P=0.018); LDL-C was negatively correlated with NLR (r=-0.200, P=0.009), triglyceride (TG) was negatively correlated with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (r=-0.184, P=0.016), TC/HDL-C was positively correlated with hs-CRP and NLR (r=0.286, P < 0.001; r=0.159, P=0.039), LDL-C/HDL-C was positively correlated with hs-CRP (r=0.161, P=0.040). In patients with RA, HDL-C levels were higher, and TG and TC/HDL-C levels were lower in the group treated regularly with conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) than without csDMARDs (P=0.035, P=0.003, P=0.006). (3) The prevalence of CAS plaques in RA patients was 37.5%. Age, disease duration, prevalence of hypertension, prevalence of diabetes, LDL-C/HDL-C, homocysteine (Hcy) and hs-CRP levels were higher in the RA with plaque group than in the RA without plaque group (all P < 0.05). (4) Logistic regression showed that age (OR=1.085, 95%CI: 1.045-1.128), disease duration (OR=1.008, 95%CI: 1.003-1.014), diabetes (OR=4.326, 95%CI: 1.606-11.655), and hs-CRP (OR=1.022, 95%CI : 1.006-1.038) were independent risk factors for the presence of CAS plaques in the RA patients.

CONCLUSION: Patients with RA are more likely to exhibit lipid metabolic abnormalities which are mainly manifested as low cholesterol levels (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C) and high lipid ratios (TC/HDL-C, LDL-C/HDL-C). Such disordered lipid profileis are associated with gender, inflammatory and drug therapy. Age, disease duration, inflammatory status, and diabetes are independent risk factors for CAS plaques in RA patients. Effective control of inflammatory status are important goals of RA management and may also be essential to delay the progression of atherosclerosis.

articles.title: [Clinical characterization and prognosis of connective tissue disease-associated hemophago-cytic syndrome in adults].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical characteristics and outcomes of macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) associated with connective tissue diseases in adults.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients aged ≥16 years with MAS who were hospitalized in the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, between 2012 and 2022. The distribution of underlying rheumatic diseases was summarized, and demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics were compared across disease groups. The patients were further classified according to in-hospital outcome as those who died during hospitalization or were discharged alive. Univariate and multivariable Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with in-hospital mortality. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the predictive performance of individual variables and the combined model for in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 109 patients with MAS were included. The mean age at MAS onset was (36.39± 13.65) years, and 82 patients (75.2%) were female. Fever and hyperferritinemia were among the most common clinical and laboratory findings. Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated MAS and adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD)-associated MAS were the two most common subtypes, accounting for 48.6% (53/109) and 25.7% (28/109) of cases, respectively. Patients with AOSD-associated MAS had a longer duration of fever than those with SLE-associated MAS. Compared with patients with AOSD-associated MAS, those with SLE-associated MAS had significantly lower white blood cell and platelet counts, ferritin levels, percentages of CD4+ T lymphocytes, and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), but higher triglyceride levels and percentages of B lymphocytes. Thirteen patients (11.9%) died during hospitalization. Multivariable Logistic regression analysis identified total protein, albumin, globulin, and D-dimer as independent factors associated with in-hospital mortality. ROC curve analysis showed that the model combining total protein and D-dimer yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.872 for predicting in-hospital mortality, compared with 0.820 for total protein alone and 0.659 for D-dimer alone.

CONCLUSION: Patients with SLE-associated MAS and AOSD-associated MAS differed in several clinical and laboratory features, suggesting clinical heterogeneity of MAS across different underlying rheumatic diseases. Assessment and management of MAS should therefore take the underlying disease into account. In-hospital mortality remained substantial in this cohort, and the combination of total protein and D-dimer showed potential value for risk stratification of in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: [Clinical characteristics of primary Sjögren syndrome with leukopenia].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical characteristics of leukopenia in a large cohort of patients with primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS), to discuss its pathogenic mechanism, and to enhance clinicians ' understanding of the disease, and reduce missed diagnosis and misdiagnosis.

METHODS: A total of 401 inpatients and outpatients who were initially diagnosed with pSS at the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Ninth People' s Hospital, Shanghai Jiaotong University School of Medicine, from November 2019 to March 2023 were selected for this study. The clinical data and laboratory examinations of these patients were analyzed retrospectively.

RESULTS: Of the 401 patients, 107 (26.68%) were complicated with blood leukopenia. The reasons for the first diagnosis were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a lower xerostomia and xerophthalmia (39.25% vs. 54.76%, P=0.006), but a higher incidence of fatigue (26.17% vs. 12.59%, P=0.001) and thrombocytopenia (11.21% vs. 2.72%, P=0.001) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in arthralgia, oral ulcer, caries, chest tightness, asthma and anemia between the two groups (P>0.05). The laboratory test indicators were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a higher prevalence of anti-SSA/Ro52+ (81.31% vs. 68.35%, P=0.040), anti-SSB+ (47.66% vs. 28.57%, P < 0.001), immunoglobulin G (IgG)+ (68.22% vs. 51.02%, P=0.002), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) elevation (67.29% vs. 41.32%, P=0.001), and thrombocytopenia (22.43% vs. 13.27%, P=0.026) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in antinuclear antibody (ANA)+, anti-SSA/Ro60+, centromere protein B(CENP-B)+, rheumatoid factor (RF)+, and anemia between the two groups (P>0.05). The positive rate of abnormal salivary gland ultrasound in pSS with leukopenia group was higher than that in normal group (P=0.029). There was no significant difference in salivary flow rate, dry eye test and lip gland biopsy between the two groups (P>0.05). The incidence of pSS combined with leukopenia and autoimmune hepatitis (10.28% vs. 3.40%, P=0.006) was higher than that of the normal group, and the incidence of interstitial pneumonia (16.82% vs. 14.97%, P=0.649), renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P=0.649) and renal tubule acidosis (2.80% vs. 3.06%, P=0.893) were no significant differences between the two groups (P>0.05). Analysis of the effect of antibody on leukopenia showed that the proportion of leukopenia was higher in anti-SSA/Ro52+ group (30.00% vs. 18.02%, P=0.015). The percentages of leukopenia (37.78% vs. 21.05%, P < 0.001), neutropenia (31.85% vs. 16.92%, P < 0.001) and lymphocytopenia (24.44% vs. 21.03%, P=0.001) in anti-SSB+ group were significantly higher than those in anti-SSB- group.

CONCLUSION: In certain patients with pSS, leukopenia manifested as the initial clinical symptom, as opposed to the typically expected dry mouth and eyes. When compared to the group with normal leukocyte levels, the group of pSS patients with leukopenia demonstrated a higher susceptibility to fatigue symptoms and exocrine gland involvement. Additionally, this leukopenia group exhibited a higher rate of antibody positivity, increased disease activity, and a greater likelihood of developing liver disease complicated by autoimmunity. These findings underscore the need for heightened clinical attention.

articles.title: [Association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history and the incidence risk of stroke: A prospective cohort study].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history and the incidence risk of stroke, and to explore the familial aggregation and intergenerational transmission of stroke risk.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study design was adopted, based on the data of the Fangshan Family-based Ischemic Stroke Study in China(FISSIC). The Cox proportional hazards model was used to analyze the association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history (paternal stroke history, maternal stroke history, parental history of stroke, and sibling stroke history) and the incidence risk of stroke. The hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were estimated. Stroke was classified as early-onset and late-onset, and the association between different types of first-degree relatives ' stroke history and the risk of early-onset and late-onset stroke was further analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 3 631 subjects were included in the study, with 1 650 males (45.4%) and a mean age of (56.7±8.4) years. The median follow-up duration was 6.98 years, during which 1 337 new cases of stroke occurred. The risk of stroke occurrence was higher in those with a first-degree relative history of stroke (HR=1.24, 95%CI: 1.08-1.43, P=0.002). For different types of first-degree relatives ' stroke history, the association between maternal and sibling history of stroke and the incidence risk of stroke was statistically significant (maternal history of stroke: HR=1.15, 95%CI: 1.00-1.32, P=0.049; sibling history of stroke: HR=1.17, 95%CI: 1.03-1.33, P=0.013). No association was observed between a paternal history of stroke or a parental history of stroke and the risk of stroke (both P>0.05). Compared with those without a family history, the HRs for early-onset and late-onset stroke in those with a maternal history of stroke were 1.40 (95%CI: 1.10-1.77, P=0.005) and 1.19 (95%CI: 1.01-1.41, P=0.043), respectively. Compared with those without a family history, the HRs for early-onset and late-onset stroke in those with a sibling history of stroke were 1.28 (95%CI: 1.02-1.61, P=0.034) and 1.17 (95%CI: 1.00-1.37, P=0.045), respectively.

CONCLUSION: Stroke exhibits familial aggregation, and the history of stroke in first-degree relatives is associated with the incidence risk of stroke. In particular, the maternal and sibling stroke history demonstrate a stronger association with the incidence risk of stroke. This finding suggests that during the intergenerational transmission of stroke risk, the genetics and family environment reflected by the maternal and sibling stroke history may play an important role.

articles.title: [Correlation between trimethylamine-N-oxide and cardiovascular metabolic markers].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between serum trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) levels and cardiovascular metabolic biomarkers, so as to provide a basis for clarifying the impact of TMAO on cardiovascular metabolic disease.

METHODS: Based on baseline data from the Beijing Fangshan Family Cohort collected from 2013 to 2017, totally 500 participants from 173 families were selected from the survey subjects. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. The correlation between TMAO and cardiovascular and metabolic disease indicators was analyzed by a linear mixed effects model.

RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was (56.52±12.52) years, with 54.20% being male. Serum TMAO levels showed significant positive correlations with systolic blood pressure (SBP) and pulse pressure (PP). Each 1 μmol/L increase in TMAO was associated with a 0.74 mmHg increase in SBP (95%CI: 0.19-1.30, P=0.009) and a 0.64 mmHg increase in PP (95%CI: 0.21-1.08, P=0.004). Subgroup analysis showed that for each 1 μmol/l increase in TMAO in men, SBP and PP increased by 0.91 mmHg (95%CI: 0.24-1.57, P < 0.05) and 0.85 mmHg (95%CI: 0.37-1.35, P < 0.05), respectively. No significant correlation was found in women. In the population aged ≥60 years, each 1 μmol/L increase in TMAO was associated with a 1.10 mmHg increase in SBP (95%CI: 0.23-1.96, P < 0.05) and a 0.98 mmHg increase in PP (95%CI: 0.23-1.73, P < 0.05). No significant correlation was found in people aged < 60 years.

CONCLUSION: The current study found that high TMAO level was correlated with the increase of SBP and PP, and TMAO might be an influencing factor of blood pressure level. No statistically significant correlation was found between TMAO and blood glucose and lipid indicators.

articles.title: [Prognostic value of angio-based microvascular resistance on left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between angio-based microvascular resistance (AMR) and impaired left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to assess its predictive value for left ventricular systolic function.

METHODS: A study was conducted, enrolling consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at the Department of Cardiology, Peking University Third Hospital from May 2023 to June 2024. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) and AMR were calculated from coronary angiography images immediately after PCI, and myocardial biomarker or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) assessed by echocardiography at half-year follow-up were collected. The correlation between AMR, QFR, myocardial biomarkers, and LVEF after half a year was analyzed. The STEMI patients were divided into normal or reduced left ventricular systolic function with LVEF 0.5 as the boundary. The accuracy of AMR in diagnosing reduced left ventricular systolic function was analyzed by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC).

RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with an average age of (63.3±13.6) years, and the average AMR value was (246.99±57.18) mmHg·s/m. Age, peak creatine kinase (CK), troponin T (TnT), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and AMR were identified as independent predictive factors for LVEF at half-year follow-up (β=-0.160, t=-2.533, P=0.012; β=-0.271, t=-3.068, P=0.002; β=-0.191, t=-2.157, P=0.032; β=-0.280, t=-4.515, P < 0.001; β=-0.162, t=-2.711, P=0.007). ROC curve analysis showed that AMR had a certain value in predicting reduced left ventricular systolic function [area under curve (95% confidence interval) was 0.631 (0.543-0.718), P=0.006], and the optimal cut-off value for predicting an LVEF < 0.5 was 250.5 mmHg·s/m.

CONCLUSION: AMR is an independent predictor of LVEF at half-year post-procedure and has significant predictive value for reduced left ventricular systolic function, potentially playing an important role in predicting the prognosis of STEMI patients.
