articles.title: [Analysis of prognostic factors in patients with acute coronary syndrome complicated with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease after percutaneous coronary intervention].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the prognostic factors of patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) complicated with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to establish a risk predictive model.

METHODS: The medical records of 148 ACS patients with moderate to severe CKD who received PCI in the Department of Cardiology, Peking University Third Hospital from September 2021 to January 2023 and completed 12-month follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. According to whether the patients had a major adverse cardiovascular disease (MACE) 12 months after PCI, they were divided into MACE group and non-MACE group. Binary Logistic regression analysis was performed on the general clinical data, clinical test results, echocardiography, coronary angiography and PCI data of the two groups of patients, the prognostic factors were analyzed by backward stepwise regression, and the risk prediction model was established. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was drawn to test the predictive efficiency of the model.

RESULTS: A total of 148 patients with ACS combined with moderate to severe CKD were included in the study, including 50 patients in the MACE group and 98 patients in the non-MACE group, and the incidence of MACE 12 months after PCI was 33.8%.Binary Logistic analysis of hospitalization data of the two groups showed that white blood cell (OR＝1.145; 95%CI: 1.017-1.290; P＝0.026), age (OR＝1.032; 95%CI: 1.001-1.065; P＝0.046) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; OR＝0.962; 95%CI: 0.934-0.990; P＝0.009) were independent influencing factors for MACE 12 months after PCI (P < 0.05), CKD stage was not associated with the occurrence of MACE 12 months after PCI. The risk prediction model for MACE was Logit(P) = 0.032× age +0.136× leukocyte－0.039×LVEF. ROC curve analysis showed that this model had good prediction efficiency, and the area under the curve (AUC) predicted by the prediction model was 0.749, 95%CI was 0.666 to 0.832. The sensitivity and specificity were 72% and 68%.

CONCLUSION: The incidence of MACE was higher in ACS patients with moderate to severe CKD 12 months after PCI, and white blood cells, age and LVEF were independent factors influencing the occurrence of MACE in these patients after PCI.

articles.title: [Risk prediction of pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the risk factors for pneumonia after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) infection in maintenance hemodialysis patients from a single center in China, and to establish a multivariate model to predict the risk of pneumonia.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected. Multivariate Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were adopted to explore risk factors of pneumonia, and a multivariate model was established to predict the risk of pneumonia occurrence.

RESULTS: A total of 209 hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection were enrolled, including 80 patients (38.3%) with pneumonia and 129 patients (61.7%) without pneumonia. Compared with the non-pneumonia group, the pneumonia group presented a significantly higher mean age [(65.8±13.7) years vs. (58.9±12.6) years, P < 0.001] and elevated C-reactive protein levels [4.58(1.62, 9.99) mg/L vs. 2.35(0.95, 6.50) mg/L, P=0.007]. In contrast, the pneumonia group had markedly lower hemoglobin [(109±15) g/L vs. (116±11) g/L, P=0.001], serum phosphorus [(1.60±0.52) mmol/L vs. (1.78±0.53) mmol/L, P=0.022], serum albumin [(35.9±4.1) g/L vs. (38.6±2.5) g/L, P < 0.001], arteriovenous fistula utilization rate (81.3% vs. 96.9%, P < 0.001), and single dialysis session duration [(232±14) min vs. (236±11) min, P=0.046]. Multivariate Logistic analysis revealed that advanced age (OR=1.030, 95%CI: 1.002-1.059, P=0.036), lower hemoglobin (OR=0.968, 95%CI: 0.942-0.995, P=0.019), lower albumin (OR=0.834, 95%CI: 0.738-0.943, P=0.004) were independent risk factors for pneumonia. Patients over 65 years old, with hemoglobin < 115 g/L or serum albumin < 36.8 g/L had elevated risk of pneumonia. A combined predictive factor Q composed of these three indicators was developed for risk prediction of pneumonia. We drew the ROC curve with the predictive factor Q [area under the curve (AUC) =0.756, 95%CI: 0.687-0.825, P < 0.001]. Taking the cut-off value of 0.575, the sensitivity and specificity of predictive factor Q for predicting pneumonia were 44.0% and 94.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, anemia and hypoalbuminemia are risk factors for pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection. A predictive marker Q value less than 0.575 indicates low risk of pneumonia, which can be applied for rapid risk stratification among hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

articles.title: [Correlation between acute kidney injury diagnosed by serum creatinine and urine output criteria and short-term prognosis in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between acute kidney injury (AKI) diagnosed by elevated serum creatinine (Scr) versus only meeting the urine output (UO) reduction criteria and short-term adverse outcomes in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery, and to evaluate the association between even mild elevations in Scr and clinical outcomes furthermore.

METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study. A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgery adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Peking University First Hospital from May 20, 2019 to March 7, 2022 were included. According to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline, AKI patients were classified into two groups: the AKI-Scr group (those meeting the Scr elevation criteria) and the AKI-UO group (those fulfilling only the UO reduction criteria). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality in patients with AKI, and the secondary outcomes were major renal adverse events, post-operative renal replacement therapy (RRT), postoperative complications, postoperative mechanical ventilation time, ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, total hospital stay, and total medical costs. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors of hospitalized death in critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery.

RESULTS: A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgical patients admitted to the ICU were enrolled, among whom 429 were diagnosed with AKI. There were 91 cases in the AKI-Scr group and 338 cases in the AKI-UO group. The primary study endpoint: no statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between the AKI-Scr and AKI-UO groups (5.5% vs. 2.1%, P>0.05). The secondary study endpoints: compared with the AKI-UO group, the patients in the AKI-Scr group had a higher incidence of major renal adverse events (9.8% vs. 4.4%), postoperative RRT (4.4% vs. 0.3%) and postoperative complications (50.5% vs. 24.0%, all P < 0.05), a significantly longer duration of postoperative mechanical ventilation (12.0 d vs. 7.5 d), ICU stay (2 d vs. 1 d), postoperative hospital stay (14 d vs. 9 d) and total hospital stay (21 d vs.17 d, all P < 0.05), and a significantly higher total medical expenditure (112000 yuan vs. 89000 yuan, P<0.001). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that postoperative RRT (OR=33.164, 95%CI: 1.305-842.794, P=0.034) and sepsis during hospitalization (OR=23.096, 95%CI: 4.242-125.175, P < 0.001) were independent risk factors for hospitalized death in the critically ill patients with postoperative AKI. Compared with the ΔScr≤24% patients (Scr increased by less than 24% from baseline within 7 d), even in the patients with only a minor elevation in Scr (ΔScr increase of 25%-49% from baseline but < 26.5μmol/L), the incidence of postoperative complications was significantly higher (48.6% vs. 19.2%, P < 0.001), along with prolonged ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d], postoperative hospital stay (13 d vs. 9 d), and total hospital stay (23 d vs. 16 d, all P < 0.05). Compared with the non-AKI group, the incidence of in-hospital mortality (2.1% vs. 0.3%, P < 0.05) and postoperative complications (24.0% vs. 18.3%, P < 0.05) was higher in the AKI-UO group, and the ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d, P < 0.001] was longer.

CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery, the short-term prognosis of patients with AKI whose diagnosis was mainly based on increased Scr was worse than patients who only met the diagnostic criteria of oliguria. Even a mild elevation in serum creatinine was associated with adverse patient outcomes.

articles.title: [Short-term clinical outcomes of complete dentures fabricated by conventional and CAD/CAM milling techniques: A self-controlled study with randomized wearing sequence].
articles.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To preliminarily compare the short-term clinical outcomes of conventional and computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) monolithic milled complete dentures and to provide clinical evidence for selecting a digital complete-denture fabrication technique.

METHODS: Seven edentulous patients were enrolled in a self-controlled study with a randomized wearing sequence. Each participant received one conventionally fabricated complete denture and one CAD/CAM monolithic milled complete denture. The fabrication technique was not actively disclosed before subjective assessment. A 2-week washout period, during which the participants wore their previous dentures, separated the two wearing periods. Subjective visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for overall satisfaction, mandibular denture retention, masticatory function, mucosal comfort, speech, and esthetics, together with pressure-point count, objective mandibular retention force, and objective masticatory efficiency, were assessed at insertion, 1 week, and 1 month. Within-patient comparisons between the two techniques were performed at each time point. Overall satisfaction, pressure-point count, objective retention force, and objective masticatory efficiency were additionally analyzed using a 2×3 fully within-subject repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons.

RESULTS: Significant between-process differences in satisfaction, aesthetics, retention VAS, mastication VAS, and pressure point counts were found over three time points (all P < 0.05), favoring CAD/CAM milling. No significant between-group difference in phonation. CAD/CAM milling yielded higher mandibular retention force at insertion, 1 week, and 1 month (P < 0.001, P=0.004, and P < 0.001, respectively). Objective masticatory efficiency was 38.53%±3.75% versus 42.73%±3.67% at insertion (P=0.057), 45.09% ±3.89% versus 52.93%±2.60% at 1 week (P=0.001), and 52.22%±3.88% versus 56.69%±3.28% at 1 month (P=0.031) for the conventional and CAD/CAM groups, respectively. Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant technique and time effects for all four variables. A significant technique×time interaction was identified only for pressure-point count [F(2, 12)=5.550, P=0.020]; the interaction for objective mandibular retention force was not significant after Greenhouse-Geisser correction [F(1.090, 6.540)=2.547, P=0.162].

CONCLUSION: In this small, short-term, within-patient study with a randomized wearing sequence, CAD/CAM monolithic milled complete dentures showed advantages in several patient-reported outcomes, objective mandibular retention force, and objective masticatory efficiency at 1 week and 1 month. These advantages did not extend to all outcomes or time points, and the between-technique difference in pressure-point count narrowed over time.

articles.title: TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 links bacteria recognition to autophagosome formation in xenophagy.
articles.abstract: Xenophagy, a selective autophagy pathway, is a critical innate immune defense mechanism that targets pathogens for lysosomal degradation. However, the molecular mechanisms enabling autophagosomes to specifically recognize and engulf bacteria remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify WIPI2, a core component that drives autophagosome biogenesis, as a novel phosphorylation substrate of TBK1 during Salmonella Typhimurium infection. We demonstrate that TBK1 phosphorylates WIPI2 at Ser96, which enhances its interaction with ATG16L1 and its binding to PtdIns3P. Crucially, the recruitment of WIPI2 to intracellular bacteria is dependent on its interaction with ATG16L1, which is localized to the Salmonella-containing vacuole. Furthermore, TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 is required for efficient bacterial clearance. Collectively, our findings reveal a molecular mechanism whereby TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of WIPI2 directs localized phagophore expansion around invading bacteria, thereby bridging bacterial recognition with autophagosome assembly.Abbreviations: ATG: autophagy related; ATG5: autophagy related 5; ATG16L1: autophagy related 16 like 1; CALCOCO2/NDP52: calcium binding and coiled-coil domain 2; CFU: colony-forming units; GFP: green fluorescent protein; GST: glutathione S-transferase; IL6: interleukin 6; KO: knockout; LPS: lipopolysaccharides; MAP1LC3/LC3: microtubule associated protein 1 light chain 3; OPTN: optineurin; PtdIns: phosphatidylinositol; PtdIns3P: phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate; RB1CC1/FIP200: RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1; RFP: red fluorescent protein;S. Typhimurium:SalmonellaTyphimurium; SCV:SalmonellaTyphimurium-containing vacuole; SQSTM1/p62: sequestosome 1; TBK1/NAK: TANK binding kinase 1; ULK1: unc-51 like autophagy activating kinase 1; V-ATPase: vacuolar-type H+-translocating ATPase; WIPI1: WD repeat domain, phosphoinositide interacting 1; WIPI2: WD repeat domain, phosphoinositide interacting 2; WT: wild-type.

articles.title: Inhibition of xanthine oxidase protects against heatstroke-related acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heatstroke-induced acute kidney injury (HS-AKI) is a critical type of visceral injury. This study aimed to explore whether xanthine oxidase (XOD) promotes the progression of HS-AKI and whether febuxostat (Feb) attenuates HS-AKI through the inhibition of oxidative stress.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Both in vitro (HK-2 cells) and in vivo (a mouse model) approaches were used to evaluate the role of XOD in HS-AKI. In vitro, genetic gain-/loss-of-function (mediated by an XDH overexpression plasmid/siRNA) and pharmacologic intervention (febuxostat) were performed in HK-2 cells exposed to hyperthermia. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice were pretreated with febuxostat (or saline) before heat exposure, and the Control, Feb, HS, and Feb + HS groups were established. Quantitative proteomics was used to screen for proteins that were differentially expressed under thermal stress. Renal function, histopathology, oxidative stress (ROS, MDA, and SOD levels), expression levels of the cytoprotective protein HO-1, inflammatory cytokine (TNF-α and IL-1β), and apoptosis were thoroughly analyzed.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis revealed upregulated expression of XOD in the HS group compared with the control group. The activity and expression of the XOD enzyme were considerably higher in a high heat environment. XOD overexpression significantly increased HS-induced oxidative stress, the inflammatory response, and apoptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells. The inhibition of XOD with febuxostat markedly reduced oxidative stress, thereby preventing inflammation and apoptosis and alleviating HS-AKI.

CONCLUSION: XOD-driven oxidative stress is a key pathogenic mechanism in HS-AKI. Febuxostat, a XOD inhibitor, showed protective efficacy in an animal model, highlighting this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Interobserver agreement among pathologists in the histological diagnosis of coeliac disease: a systematic review supports the British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines' integrated approach to diagnosis.
Maternal exposure to Helicobacter pylori impairs spatial and recognition memory in rat offspring: Ameliorative effect of monoamine oxidase inhibition.
articles.abstract: During recent years, researchers have extensively investigated various health issues associated with prenatal challenges and the subsequent outcomes emerging in the next generation. In this respect, prenatal exposure to infections is correlated with the development of cognitive deficits in offspring. There is evidence indicating that disturbance of maternal microbiota adversely affects the gut-brain axis, which in turn could compromise fetal development and cause persistent physiological defects. Previous studies have reported that Helicobacter pylori infection is correlated with cognitive decline; however, this issue has not been investigated in offspring. Therefore, we applied behavioral methods to reveal how maternal H. pylori infection could affect memory function using the Morris water maze and novel object recognition in male offspring. Then, the cellular mechanisms associated with H. pylori-induced effects were probed using specific biochemical measurements in hippocampal tissues. Results indicated that spatial and recognition memory is impaired in offspring born from mothers with a history of H. pylori infection, and this appears to be correlated with a disturbance of the balance among oxidative, inflammatory, serotonergic, and cholinergic profiles within the hippocampi. In addition, the mentioned H. pylori-related effects were found to be biochemically restored and behaviorally ameliorated by pharmacological inhibition of the monoamine oxidase enzyme, proposing a potential for amelioration of cognitive outcomes.

articles.title: p53 deficiency increases vulnerability to chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors: Role of calcium dysregulation and BDNF signaling.
articles.abstract: The tumor suppressor protein p53 is a known modulator of neurodegenerative disease (ND) processes. Although p53 expression is increased in the brains of patients with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and ischemic stroke, its role in mood disorders such as anxiety and depression remains unclear. To investigate the role of p53 in behavioral responses to chronic stress, we examined behavioral and molecular alterations in p53 knockout (p53-/-) mice and wild type mice. In p53-/- mice, increased vulnerability to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors was observed following CUMS exposure. In parallel with these behavioral changes, BDNF expression was reduced, whereas glutamate levels were elevated in the prefrontal cortex of p53-/- mice. Increased calcium-associated staining and NMDAR2B expression were observed together with increased neuronal injury- and cell death-related markers. In primary cortical neurons derived from p53-/- mice, corticosterone treatment resulted in greater increases in glutamate levels, NMDAR2B expression compared to wild-type controls. Cell death markers (cleaved caspase-3, p-p38, p-JNK) were upregulated, while neuroprotective signals (BDNF, p-Akt, p-ERK, p-CREB) were suppressed in p53-/- mice, and corticosterone-treated primary neuronal cells from p53-/- mice. These findings indicate that p53 deficiency is associated with enhanced vulnerability to CUMS-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors and is accompanied by alterations in calcium handling, glutamate homeostasis, neuronal injury-related markers, and BDNF-associated neuroprotective signaling.

articles.title: Polyphenols and Flavonoids in microRNA-Regulated Pathways of Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Potential and Translational Gaps.
articles.abstract: Although doxorubicin remains a cornerstone of anticancer therapy, its clinical utility is limited by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. Current tools for the early detection of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remain suboptimal, prompting interest in microRNAs (miRNAs) as mechanistic regulators and circulating biomarkers. Natural cardioprotective compounds, particularly polyphenols and flavonoids, have also attracted attention because of their ability to modulate oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, autophagy and regulated cell death. However, the mechanistic and translational strength of this evidence varies considerably. This critical narrative review is based on targeted PubMed literature searches up to 14 August 2026, supplemented by selective reference-list screening of relevant original articles and reviews. The literature search was not intended to be exhaustive, and the studies discussed were selected to illustrate different levels of mechanistic evidence. Studies investigating miRNA-mediated mechanisms in DIC were distinguished from circulating biomarker studies, while phytochemical evidence was classified as direct miRNA-linked, miRNA-associated without causal validation, or pathway-convergent. Among the selected examples, taxifolin provides direct miRNA-linked evidence involving the miR-200a/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, with functional miR-200a inhibition demonstrated in H9c2 cells. Blueberry extract provided miRNA-associated evidence; miR-140-5p expression was assessed together with Sirt2 and Nrf2 expression, but a causal role for miR-140-5p was not functionally validated. For the other selected compounds, the available evidence was predominantly pathway-convergent. Although miRNAs and phytochemicals offer complementary perspectives on DIC mechanisms and cardioprotection, their clinical application remains premature. Future studies require functional miRNA validation, standardized biomarker assessment, pharmacokinetic evaluation and confirmation that cardioprotection does not compromise antitumor efficacy.

articles.title: Prospective External Validation of the HFA-ICOS Baseline Cardiovascular Risk Classification in Women with Breast Cancer Receiving Anthracycline-Containing Therapy in a Central Asian Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The HFA-ICOS baseline cardiovascular risk classification was developed to standardize pretreatment risk stratification before potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapy, but its external performance across diverse populations remains incompletely characterized. We prospectively evaluated its performance in women with breast cancer receiving anthracycline-containing therapy in Central Asia. Methods: This prospective single-center external validation study used data from the PREDICATE cohort (ISRCTN12628444). Participants were classified at baseline as being at low, moderate, high, or very high cardiovascular risk according to the HFA-ICOS classification before treatment and outcome ascertainment; the high- and very-high-risk categories were pooled for analysis because of small numbers. Participants underwent serial cardiovascular surveillance, including echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain, together with serial cardiac biomarker measurements. The primary outcome was cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), defined according to the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology criteria. Results: The analysis included 108 participants. CTRCD occurred in 43 of 108 participants (39.8%). The observed proportion of participants who developed CTRCD increased from 30.0% in the low-risk group to 47.5% in the moderate-risk group and 75.0% in the high/very-high-risk group (p = 0.026). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant separation of CTRCD-free survival across HFA-ICOS risk categories (log-rank χ2 = 10.12; p = 0.006). Compared with the low-risk group, the hazard of CTRCD was higher in the moderate-risk group (hazard ratio [HR], 2.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-4.13) and high/very-high-risk group (HR, 3.59; 95% CI, 1.42-9.11). Discrimination was modest (area under the curve, 0.630; 95% CI, 0.530-0.724). Conclusions: The HFA-ICOS classification demonstrated a clear ordinal gradient in CTRCD risk and significant time-to-event separation but showed limited discrimination at the individual-patient level. It may guide initial risk stratification but should be complemented by longitudinal cardiovascular surveillance rather than used as a stand-alone predictor.

articles.title: Decision volume and temporal workload structure as dissociable correlates of fatigue and mood in intensive care physicians: a real-time observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive care physicians make hundreds of decisions per shift under sustained cognitive and emotional demands. Decision fatigue, the tendency towards less effortful choices as cumulative decision load increases, may affect clinician wellbeing and decision processes. However, the associations of decision volume and temporal workload structure with within-shift fatigue and mood in intensive care unit (ICU) physicians remain unclear. This study explored whether decision volume and temporal clustering show distinct associations with fatigue, sleepiness, mood, and post-shift decision responses.

METHODS: Five physicians (two residents, three consultants) at a surgical ICU of a German university hospital were shadowed during 38 twelve-hour shifts (456 hours) between October and December 2025. Clinical decisions were classified by severity using a study-specific, non-validated Decision Severity Score. Because recruitment was feasibility-based and involved only five physicians, all analyses were considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Psychometric assessments of decision fatigue, sleepiness, and mood (Decision Fatigue Scale, Karolinska Sleepiness Scale, Profile of Mood States - Short Form) were administered at morning, midday, and shift end. Following each shift, physicians completed a standardised scenario task requiring three binary treatment decisions. Temporal workload structure was quantified using the burstiness metric; shifts were classified into four types by median split of decision density and burstiness (quiet-smooth, quiet-clustered, busy-smooth, busy-clustered). Linear and binomial mixed-effects models with physician as random intercept were used throughout.

RESULTS: Across 17,953 recorded decisions (median 474 per shift; range 366-589), a higher mean decision rate was associated with greater end-of-shift decision fatigue: an increase of 0.5 decisions per 5-minute interval corresponded to a 2.1-point higher decision-fatigue score (95 % CI 0.6 to 3.6). Higher burstiness was associated with less mood disturbance, with a 0.10 increase in burstiness corresponding to a 6.3-point lower mood score (95% CI -10.2 to -2.3). Averaged across all shifts, changes between morning and evening were small and not statistically significant for any of the three scores. Within-shift trajectories differed by shift type, however, with mood disturbance increasing over the shift in quiet-smooth shifts only, a difference already apparent at midday. Quiet-smooth shifts, the least objectively demanding, showed the least favourable psychometric values. Response certainty in the post-shift scenario task was lower after shifts with more task interruptions, with each ten additional interruptions corresponding to a 0.29-point lower certainty score (p = 0.012), whilst a descriptive trend towards more conservative scenario responses was observed in busy-clustered shifts (odds ratio 2.25, p = 0.555).

CONCLUSIONS: Decision volume and temporal workload structure showed different associations with psychometric outcomes: higher decision rates were associated with greater end-of-shift decision fatigue, whereas greater temporal clustering was associated with lower mood disturbance, already apparent from midday onwards. That more quiet, uniformly paced shifts showed the least favourable psychometric values suggests that reducing decision volume alone may not improve physician wellbeing; this observation requires replication. Mitigation strategies may therefore need to extend beyond reducing decision volume to protecting concentrated, meaningful clinical activity and minimising hindrance stressors such as interruptions. Future multicentre studies should determine whether these associations are reproducible and whether temporal workload structure is related to objective decision quality or patient-safety outcomes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00037564. Registered 27th August 2025.

articles.title: "Take personal responsibility": Biological citizenship and individualization in Turkish diabetes news.
articles.abstract: This study examines how diabetes news in the Turkish national press articulates biological citizenship and how this discourse is shaped through sourcing practices. It is based on a qualitative content analysis of 139 diabetes-related news articles published on the websites of the Turkish newspapers Hürriyet and Sözcü throughout 2023. The analysis considers modes of news production, sourcing preferences, reported causes and complications of diabetes, and treatment and prevention recommendations. The findings show that diabetes coverage gives prominence to an individualizing register of biological citizenship, foregrounding lifestyle regulation, personal responsibility, and self-management. Social inequalities, structural determinants, and public responsibilities are not entirely absent, but remain marginal within the news discourse. Food-centered recommendations, complication narratives that mobilize fear and anxiety, and articles based on single or unspecified sources make diabetes intelligible primarily as a condition to be managed through individual regulation of the body. The study also shows that this self-management orientation persists even in articles based on mixed or relatively stronger sourcing. It argues that biological citizenship is articulated and reproduced not only at the level of content but also through sourcing practices and wider journalistic contexts. It further suggests that this discourse calls citizens/patients to self-management through a persistent sense of lack.

articles.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
articles.abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K+ channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na+ (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na+ permeability of currently available K+-conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm2. Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na+ channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K+-conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na+ accumulation attributable to residual Na+ permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K+-conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K+ selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca2+, which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

articles.title: Concomitant Endoscopic Procedure for Aortic Stenosis and Left Ventricular Thrombus.
Effect of local melatonin application on immediately placed implants in maxillary premolars (a biochemical and radiographic randomized controlled clinical trial).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Melatonin, a potent antioxidant and bone-regulating hormone, promotes osteoblastic activity and inhibits osteoclastic differentiation primarily through upregulation of osteoprotegerin (OPG) and suppression of the receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand (RANKL) pathway. Given its dual osteogenic and antiresorptive effects, melatonin may enhance bone remodelling around immediately placed implants. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of locally applied melatonin on peri-implant bone remodelling by assessing changes in OPG levels and radiographic bone parameters over time.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Twenty-four patients with non-restorable maxillary premolars were divided into two groups. The melatonin group received immediately placed implants with local melatonin application, and the control group received immediately placed implants without melatonin application. Serum OPG levels were measured one and three months postoperatively, and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) was performed immediately after implant placement and at six months postoperatively to assess relative bone density, bone volume, and marginal bone loss.

RESULTS: Biochemical findings: At one month, OPG levels were significantly higher in the melatonin group compared to the control group (p = 0.012). By 3 months, there was no statistically significant difference between the two groups (p = 0.707). Radiographic findings: After six months, relative bone density was numerically higher in the melatonin group than in the control group, although the between-group difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.372). However, the percentage increase from baseline was significantly greater in the melatonin group (p = 0.002). Bone volume decreased in both groups, with a percent reduction in bone volume that was significantly smaller in the melatonin group compared to the control group (p < 0.001). Marginal bone loss was significantly lower in the melatonin group compared to the control group (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Locally applied melatonin was associated with favourable early biochemical and radiographic outcomes, including a greater percentage increase in relative bone density from baseline, preservation of peri-implant bone volume, and reduced marginal bone loss.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was retrospectively registered at the Clinicaltrials.gov registry (Registration ID #NCT07103564), first submitted on July 29, 2025 https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07103564 .

articles.title: Eco-friendly biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles by saprophytic Fusarium solani as a sustainable therapeutic approach for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus wound infections.
articles.abstract: The rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has prompted the exploration of novel, naturally sourced therapeutic alternatives. Here, the saprophytic fungus Fusarium solani was used to biosynthesize silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), which were characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The AgNPs showed a surface plasmon resonance peak at ~ 410 nm, a zeta potential of - 42.7 mV, an average TEM diameter of 19.58 nm, and a hydrodynamic (DLS) diameter of 121.4 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.302. Against clinical methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates, the AgNPs exhibited minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) values of 0.1875-0.375 mM, with confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) showing a reduction in bacterial viability from 92.3% to 28.0% and TEM revealing marked ultrastructural membrane damage following treatment. In a murine MRSA wound infection model, AgNPs treatment increased wound healing from 12.33% to 95.33% and reduced bacterial load from 9.90 to 1.10 log CFU/g tissue relative to the untreated infected control, alongside significant downregulation of TNF-α, IL-6, and COX-2 expression and improved histopathological indices of tissue repair (all p < 0.05). These findings indicate that fungal-derived AgNPs possess potent antibacterial and wound-healing properties against MRSA, supporting their potential as a sustainable therapeutic candidate, although further mechanistic and translational studies are needed.

articles.title: Gamma-irradiated amniotic membrane graft as an adjuvant to posterior colporrhaphy: an exploratory prospective single-arm clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior compartment prolapse is a frequent pelvic floor disorder. While conventional posterior colporrhaphy is widely used, the recurrence rates and limitations in terms of tissue support remain concerns. Human amniotic membrane represents a promising biological scaffold with potent regenerative properties. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety and effectiveness of using amniotic membrane as a graft in posterior colporrhaphy.

METHODS: This pilot one-arm clinical trial was conducted on women with posterior compartment prolapse at Ain Shams University Hospital during the period (November 2023- August 2025). Twenty-five patients underwent posterior colporrhaphy using gamma-irradiated amniotic membrane as a graft on the rectovaginal septum. We assessed symptoms score via the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory 6 (POPDI-6), sexual function via the Female Sexual Function Index Questionnaire, and pelvic organ prolapse quantification (POP-Q) preoperatively, and at 3 and 6 months post-operatively, and assessed complication rates.

RESULTS: The AM graft was successfully implanted in all patients. The overall procedure was associated with reduction in POPDI-6 scores from 68.00 ± 14.52 at baseline to 20.67 ± 7.93 at 6 months (p < 0.001), with a mean percentage reduction of 68.22% ± 14.54%. The sexual function score improved from 11.75 ± 3.55 to 30.80 ± 2.75. Anatomical assessment revealed that 80% of patients achieved POP-Q stage 0, whereas 20% reached stage I by 6 months. No serious complications (wound dehiscence, visceral injury) were reported; however, vaginitis was common, affecting 76% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Posterior colporrhaphy with adjuvant gamma-irradiated amniotic membrane graft was associated with some improvement in symptoms, clinical examination, as well as sexual function of the patients. However, this is a one-arm pilot study; further studies are needed to compare this technique with conventional colporrhaphy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT06117670, on 31/10/2023.

articles.title: Postpandemic Social Contact Patterns: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Social contact patterns are one of the key determinants of infectious disease transmission, but post-coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-pandemic evidence from East and Southeast Asia remains limited. We examined age-specific contact patterns in Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam and assessed whether contact frequencies had returned to prepandemic levels.

METHODS: We conducted online, single-day contact surveys in 2025 using quota sampling by age and sex. Participants reported contacts on the preceding day, defined as physical contact or direct conversations of at least three sentences held within 2 m. Age-specific contact matrices were constructed for weekdays and weekends and combined using a 5:2 weighting. Factors associated with daily contact counts were examined using negative binomial regression.

RESULTS: The analysis used data from 10,279 individuals: 8,080 in Japan, 1,102 in South Korea, 589 in Thailand, and 508 in Vietnam. Mean daily contact counts were 8.1, 6.2, 6.4, and 8.8, respectively; medians were 4, 4, 4, and 6, respectively. All four countries showed age-assortative mixing, although assortativity was less pronounced in Thailand and Vietnam. In Japan and South Korea, younger age and larger household size were associated with more contacts, whereas greater mask-wearing tendency was associated with more contacts in Japan and fewer contacts in South Korea. Compared with available historical estimates, contact frequencies in Japan and South Korea remained below prepandemic levels. Sparse baseline data and methodological differences precluded firm conclusions being made for Thailand and Vietnam.

CONCLUSIONS: Contact frequencies in Japan and South Korea remained below prepandemic levels in 2025, suggesting persistent postpandemic changes in mixing behavior. Evidence for comparable changes in Thailand and Vietnam was inconclusive. Future surveys should collect setting-specific information, in addition to contact frequency and age, to clarify how changes in work, education, and household interaction shape postpandemic social mixing patterns.

articles.title: Glucose-Lowering Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes-Associated Sarcopenia: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence and a Muscle-Centred Framework.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognised as a clinically important comorbidity in diabetes mellitus, particularly in older adults and individuals with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Because skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, declines in muscle mass, quality, strength and physical performance may exacerbate insulin resistance and glycaemic instability and increase the risks of frailty, disability, falls, fractures, cardiovascular events and mortality. Contemporary glucose-lowering therapies have transformed diabetes care through established cardiorenal benefits and weight reduction, yet skeletal muscle outcomes are rarely prespecified or systematically assessed in pivotal trials. This evidence gap is especially relevant for weight-reducing agents such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, which are often associated with reductions in dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived or bioelectrical impedance analysis-derived lean-mass estimates. However, these changes should be interpreted cautiously, as they often occur in the context of overall weight loss and may be influenced by alterations in body water. In addition, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry- or dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived lean-mass estimates do not directly quantify contractile skeletal muscle. Accordingly, reductions in lean-mass estimates alone are insufficient to infer clinically meaningful muscle loss without concurrent assessment of muscle strength or physical performance. This narrative review summarises the bidirectional mechanisms linking diabetes and sarcopenia and appraises major glucose-lowering drug classes from a muscle-centred perspective. It integrates mechanistic insights with human evidence on muscle-relevant outcomes, including body composition, strength and physical performance, and addresses practical safety and monitoring considerations in sarcopenia-prone phenotypes, including sarcopenic obesity. We also propose a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating Cardiorenal-Muscle Quadrant Framework that considers glycaemic efficacy and cardiorenal benefit alongside muscle reserve, functional status and treatment-related risks, with emphasis on functional monitoring, resistance exercise, nutritional optimisation and individualised glycaemic targets in older or frail adults.

articles.title: Differences in Office and Ambulatory Pulse Wave Analysis in Patients with White Coat Hypertension and Other Hypertension Phenotypes.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Increased arterial stiffness is a sign of vascular damage; therefore, assessing it is crucial for evaluating cardiovascular risk. Arterial stiffness parameters such as pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (at heart rate 75 bpm, AIX@75) were shown to correlate directly with blood pressure (BP).

AIM: Since these parameters may consequently be altered in patients with white coat effect (WCE), this study examined differences in office and 24h measurements of these parameters across various BP phenotypes.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, conducted between 2018 and 2023 at three nephrology clinics, office and 24h BP measurements and pulse wave analysis (PWA) of 208 patients were examined.

RESULTS: 189 patients were included; 48 were diagnosed with controlled hypertension (HTN), 63 with uncontrolled HTN, 22 with a masked HTN phenotype, 30 with WCE, of whom 11 had white coat HTN (WCH) and 19 had white coat uncontrolled HTN (WCUH), and 26 had normal BP. By definition, patients with WCE had significantly higher office peripheral and aortic BP than the respective 24h values (p<0.0001 each). Their AIX@75 was significantly higher on office (32.7±11.4%) than on 24h measurement (27.4±7.2%, p=0.0354), and they showed a significantly greater reduction in PWV between office and 24h measurement than normotensives and all other BP phenotypes (padj <0.0001 each).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with WCE, there are significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters between office and 24h measurements, suggesting that both measurement methods provide complementary hemodynamic information. Prospective studies are needed to determine the prognostic significance of these differences.

articles.title: Renal tubule-specific Nrf2 deletion ameliorates diabetic kidney disease by attenuating glomerular hypertension and kidney injury in a mouse model of diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: We previously reported that expression of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) is upregulated in the renal tubules of humans with diabetes and in mouse models of diabetes. We hypothesised that Nrf2 deletion would ameliorate renal hyperfiltration and kidney injury in Akita mice (a model of type 1 diabetes).

METHODS: Akita Nrf2RT knockout (KO) mice were generated by cross-breeding tubule-specific (Pax8)-Cre mice with Akita Nrf2 floxed mice on a C57BL/6 background. Male non-diabetic control mice (Nrf2fl/fl), Nrf2RT KO mice, Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice and Akita Nrf2RT KO mice were studied up to the age of 20 weeks (n=8 per group).

RESULTS: The glomerular filtration rate (GFR), kidney hypertrophy, tubular injury score, glomerular basement membrane thickness, podocyte loss and foot process effacement and urinary albumin-creatinine ratio were significantly increased in Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice and were markedly reduced in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with the corresponding control mice. Attenuation of afferent arteriole vasodilation and efferent arteriole vasoconstriction was observed in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice. Furthermore, downregulation of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) and angiotensinogen expression in renal proximal tubules was observed in Akita Nrf2RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2fl/fl mice. Treatment of Akita Nrf2RT KO mice with a selective A1 adenosine receptor inhibitor increased GFR and fractional excretion of glucose, suggesting that enhanced adenosine signalling may contribute to the altered renal haemodynamics through tubuloglomerular feedback and reduced glomerular injury associated with RT-specific Nrf2 deletion.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that tubular NRF2 plays an important role in the progression of diabetic kidney disease in Akita mice through modulation of the GFR and expression of SGLT2 and angiotensinogen in renal proximal tubules and tubuloglomerular feedback.

articles.title: Prediabetes subtype-based stratification reveals distinct long-term risks for type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Prediabetes is heterogeneous, with subtypes defined by impaired fasting glucose (IFG), impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) or HbA1c, each with different risks of progression to type 2 diabetes. We compared progression across these subtypes, and evaluated the benefit of adding insulin secretion and sensitivity to risk stratification.

METHODS: We analysed 7186 Korean adults aged 40-69 years from the community-based Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study, who were followed for up to 20 years with biennial (every 2 years) oral glucose tolerance tests and HbA1c. Prediabetes was classified as IFG, IGT or HbA1c-defined, and further stratified by insulinogenic index (IGI) and insulin sensitivity index (ISI). Cox regression was used to estimate diabetes risk, and multistate Markov models were used to assess annual transition probabilities and time spent in each state.

RESULTS: Compared with normoglycaemia, the adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were 5.84 (95% CI 5.03, 6.79) for IFG, 4.60 (95% CI 4.17, 5.07) for IGT, and 4.68 (95% CI 4.22, 5.19) for HbA1c-defined prediabetes. The risk increased stepwise with the number of criteria met: the aHRs were 3.10 (95% CI 2.81, 3.41) for one criterion, 7.33 (95% CI 6.50, 8.28) for two criteria, and 15.3 (95% CI 12.2, 19.3) for all three. Markov models showed the shortest prediabetes duration (1.7 years) and lowest regression probability (5.4%) in those meeting all three criteria. Low IGI or ISI predicted higher diabetes risk, and dual impairment conferred greatest risk (aHR 4.06; 95% CI 3.37, 4.90). Even normoglycaemic individuals with low IGI or ISI had an elevated risk of diabetes compared to those with high IGI or ISI.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Diabetes progression differs based on both glycaemic subtype and physiological subtype. Integrating IGI and ISI with conventional definitions enhances risk stratification and may help to identify high-risk individuals for earlier targeted intervention.

articles.title: Metabolic health is a stronger determinant than obesity for cardiovascular disease incidence: a meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies.
articles.abstract: Overweight and obesity are established risk factors for cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), yet heterogeneity in metabolic health among individuals with varied body mass index (BMI) complicates risk assessment. This systematic-review and meta-analysis of cohort studies investigated the risk of combined BMI-metabolic health phenotypes in relation to CVDs. PubMed and Scopus were searched up to January 2025. Metabolic phenotypes were defined as individuals with metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy overweight (MHOW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), and their metabolically unhealthy counterparts, were analyzed for associations with CVD, coronary heart disease (CHD), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and heart failure (HF). Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95%confidence intervals (95% CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Fifty-one publications (44 studies) were included. Compared with MHNW individuals, individuals with metabolically unhealthy obesity exhibited significantly higher risks across all cardiovascular outcomes with HRs of 2.10 (1.85-2.40) for CVD, 1.97 (1.71-2.27) for CHD, 2.20 (1.75-2.76) for MI, 1.55 (1.38-1.78) for stroke, and 2.05 (1.65-2.54) for HF. There was a positive dose-response relationship between both higher BMI and poor metabolic health and risk of CVD, CHD, MI, and HF incidence, however, associations for metabolically unhealthy normal weight subjects often exceeded that of metabolically healthy obese subjects. For stroke, poor metabolic health appears to be a primary determinant of risk. In conclusion, worsening metabolic health and higher BMI independently associated with increased CVD, CHD, MI, and HF risk, with their combination posing the greatest risk, while stroke risk was mainly associated with metabolic health.

articles.title: TRIM36 catalyzes K63-linked ubiquitination of TAK1 to drive septic inflammation.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) pathway is critical for initiating innate immunity; however, its dysregulation drives pathological inflammation in diseases such as sepsis.

METHODS: In the present study, we utilized septic patients, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced mouse models, and LPS-treated mouse macrophages as well as human THP-1-derived macrophages to investigate the potential functions and molecular mechanisms of TRIM36 in sepsis.

RESULTS: Here, we identify tripartite motif protein 36 (TRIM36) as a key positive regulator that amplifies TLR4 signaling. TRIM36 expression was robustly upregulated in macrophages upon lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. Mechanistically, TRIM36 directly bound to TGF-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1) and catalyzed its K63-linked ubiquitination, a prerequisite for the activation of TAK1 and the downstream nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway. Functionally, genetic ablation of Trim36 in mice attenuated hypothermia, improved survival, and reduced cytokine production in an LPS-induced sepsis model. Consistently, in vitro knockdown of TRIM36 in human macrophages blunted LPS-induced signaling and the secretion of proinflammatory mediators. Furthermore, analysis of a public transcriptomic dataset revealed that elevated TRIM36 levels were associated with non-survival in patients with sepsis.

CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, our findings establish TRIM36 as a critical amplifier of TLR4-induced hyperinflammation and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for sepsis.

articles.title: Publisher Correction: Toxoplasma gondii infection reduces CD59 expression through downregulation of JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis to enhance decidual NK cell cytotoxicity via the RAS/MAPK pathway.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]

articles.title: Zyxin protects against hypertensive nephropathy by restraining FAK/Skp2-CDK8/YAP signaling in tubular epithelial cells.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tubulointerstitial fibrosis and inflammation are hallmark pathological features of hypertensive nephropathy (HN), yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Zyxin, a focal adhesion protein, has been implicated in hypertension-related pathologies, but its specific role in HN-induced tubulointerstitial injury remains undefined.

METHODS: An HN murine model was established via a multi‑hit DOCA/Ang II + uninephrectomy + high salt approach. Intrarenal zyxin was overexpressed using adeno-associated virus. In vitro, HK-2 cells were stimulated with Ang II, and zyxin levels were modulated via lentiviral transduction. Renal function, inflammation, and fibrosis were evaluated through biochemical assays and molecular signaling analysis.

RESULTS: Zyxin was significantly downregulated in the renal tubules of HN mice and Ang II-treated HK-2 cells. Zyxin overexpression significantly improved renal function and attenuated tubulointerstitial injury, with a representative reduction of approximately 40% in the expression of fibrotic markers. These protective effects occurred independently of blood pressure changes. Mechanistically, zyxin reduction is linked to Ang II-induced calpain activation. The resulting zyxin depletion potentially disinhibits the FAK/Skp2 axis and enhances CDK8/YAP signaling, which may contribute to renal inflammation and interstitial fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support a model in which zyxin acts as a protective factor in the renal tubules during HN, suggesting its potential as a novel therapeutic target.

articles.title: Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi-condition comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evaluating how appropriate current large language models (LLMs) respond to common pediatric infectious disease (PID) questions is important for understanding their potential role in education and clinical support. Therefore, we evaluated and compared the clinical quality of answers produced by different LLMs when given professionally written, clinician-style case descriptions, using a purpose-built multi-domain evaluation tool.

METHODS: Three different LLMs, including DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, ChatGPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, were investigated using 12 relevant PID scenarios. Each scenario included five open-ended questions: etiology, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment options, and complications. Two PID specialists independently reviewed all responses using a Likert scoring tool.

RESULTS: All three models received high overall scores. ChatGPT-5 achieved perfect domain scores (10.0), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp showed similarly strong results, with only minor reductions in diagnostics (9.83) and treatment (9.92). Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated higher variability, particularly in treatment (8.83) and diagnostics (9.75), while matching the other models in clinical findings and complications (10.0) and scoring 9.83 in etiology. However, there were no statistically significant differences across models in domain-level comparisons (all p > 0.05). In addition, model-level analyses similarly demonstrated high accuracy (6.0; 5.98; 5.85), completeness (3.0; 2.97; 2.87), and safety (1.0; 1.0; 0.97) for ChatGPT-5, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, respectively (accuracy: p = 0.074; completeness: p = 0.066; safety: p = 0.14).

CONCLUSION: Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early-stage clinical reasoning. However, their optimal use remains within clinician-supervised workflows, where AI-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment.

IMPACT: Current large language models (LLMs) show consistently high-quality performance across pediatric infectious disease scenarios, with no significant differences between models. Our study adds a structured, multi-domain comparison using clinician-style cases and expert evaluation, providing detailed insights into accuracy, completeness, and safety. The findings support the use of LLMs in medical education and early clinical reasoning, while highlighting their role as clinician-supervised tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment. The results demonstrate the reliability of LLMs in organizing clinical information and identifying key diagnostic and management elements in standardized scenarios.

articles.title: Brain imaging in dystrophinopathies.
articles.abstract: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD, BMD) are caused by genetic variants in the DMD gene coding dystrophin proteins. In addition to the impairment of muscular function, these patients also present frequent cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders due to impaired expression of several brain dystrophins: Dp427, Dp140 and Dp71. Cerebral imaging has shed new light on the impact of dystrophinopathies on brain structure, function, and connectivity. We review the brain imaging results obtained in patients and divers animal models, showing presence of mild cortical atrophy, slight modifications of structures volumes, decreased cerebral blood flood, white matter microstructure alterations, brain hypometabolism, altered connectivity, and an abnormal cerebral response to stress. We further discuss the putative progression of cerebral disorders, and their variable severity when Dp140 expression is affected in addition to that of Dp427. Some correlations between imaging parameters and cognitive and psychological impairments have been reported but remain to be confirmed.

articles.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: clinical and mechanistic insights.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment but can cause immune-related adverse events, including potentially severe cardiovascular toxicities. Although rare, immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIM) can present early and may be rapidly fatal, posing a significant challenge at the crossroads of oncology, immunology, and cardiology.

PURPOSE: This review synthesizes emerging clinical and experimental evidence to refine understanding of risk factors for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis and to outline a practical clinic-to-bench framework linking surveillance and diagnostic decision-making to pathogenic cellular programs.

CONCLUSIONS: We highlight the cardiac immune microenvironment as a network of multicellular interactions in which cytotoxic T cells and inflammatory myeloid subsets engage with cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts through reinforcing feedback loops. Specifically, interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-driven myeloid activation and chemokine programs (CXCR3-CXCL9/10, CXCL16-CXCR6) coordinate immune cell trafficking and promote tissue injury, while stress-related cell death pathways can trigger innate immune sensing via the cGAS-STING axis. Current management remains centered on early recognition and corticosteroid-based immunosuppression, but emerging mechanistic insights reveal opportunities to improve therapy by targeting immune cell trafficking and inflammatory amplification pathways. Together, these advances support a more integrated cardio-oncology approach to ICIM, in which mechanistic insights inform risk stratification, earlier diagnosis, and the development of more precise immunomodulatory therapies.

articles.title: Persistent hypertension and left ventricular remodeling after stenting for coarctation of the aorta: a single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: Persistent hypertension (HTN) remains common after covered stent implantation for coarctation of the aorta (CoA). However, existing evidence is derived predominantly from surgical repair cohorts and cross-sectional echocardiography, leaving the individual trajectory of left ventricular (LV) remodeling after stenting poorly defined. We retrospectively studied 84 patients with complete persistent HTN status, and 75 patients with paired follow-up echocardiography for LV remodeling analyses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression were performed to identify factors associated with persistent HTN and follow-up LV mass index (LVMI) separately. Paired changes in LV hypertrophy (LVH) and LV geometry were assessed using McNemar and Stuart-Maxwell tests. Persistent HTN occurred in 46 of 84 patients (54.8%) at a median clinical follow-up of 9 years, and was associated with older age at repair and higher preoperative systolic blood pressure. Higher follow-up LVMI was associated with higher baseline LVMI, male sex and longer follow-up duration. At a median echocardiographic follow-up of 2 years, LVH prevalence decreased from 41.3-24.0%. This net decline masked bidirectional individual trajectories: 19 of 31 patients with baseline LVH (61.3%) no longer met LVH criteria, whereas 6 of 44 patients without baseline LVH (13.6%) developed new-onset LVH. Anatomical relief after CoA stenting therefore does not preclude ongoing myocardial burden, and patients developing new-onset LVH would not be identified by preoperative risk stratification alone. Serial echocardiographic assessment should complement long-term blood pressure surveillance, though these findings require validation in larger cohorts with standardized follow-up.

articles.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies a proinflammatory S100a8/a9+ macrophage subset contributing to acute kidney injury.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Macrophages represent a heterogeneous cell population in the kidney. However, macrophage subsets and their role in endotoxemia-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) remain elucidated.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify macrophage subpopulations in mouse kidney following lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. AKI was induced by LPS treatment or renal ischemia reperfusion injury in wild-type or S100a9-/- mice. Silencing or overexpression of S100a9 was carried out to assess its function and contribution to LPS-induced inflammation and AKI. In addition, bone marrow cells from S100a9-/- mice were injected into the recipient mice to determine the effect of S100a9 deletion in macrophage differentiation and renal inflammatory injury.

RESULTS: By using single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified a unique S100a8/a9+Ly6chigh proinflammatory macrophage subpopulation in mouse kidney following LPS challenge. LPS administration induced the infiltration of Ly6c+ macrophages into kidney tissues and significantly upregulated the expression of S100a8 and S100a9. S100a9 deletion downregulated S100a8 expression, decreased CD11b+Ly6chigh macrophages, and suppressed proinflammatory cytokine production in the kidney, attenuating LPS or ischemia reperfusion-induced renal inflammation and AKI. Bone marrow transplantation from S100a9-/- mice donors, but not from wild-type mice donors, reduced infiltration of CD11b+Ly6chigh macrophages and renal inflammatory injury. S100a8/a9 overexpression activated the nuclear factor-κB signaling pathway and promoted the production of proinflammatory cytokines in macrophages.

CONCLUSIONS: S100a8/a9 plays a regulatory role in CD11b+Ly6chigh macrophage population differentiation, contributing to endotoxemia-induced AKI. S100a8/a9 blockade may be a novel therapeutic strategy for the prevention or attenuation of AKI.

articles.title: Microbes as a programmable toolbox for cancer diagnosis, monitoring, and theranostics.
articles.abstract: Microbes have evolved molecular machinery to recognize hosts, access tissues, sense local conditions, replicate, and modify their environments. These capabilities are increasingly being repurposed for cancer detection and control. Phage and yeast display generate tumour-recognition modules; engineered bacteria sense and amplify local disease signals; reporter-expressing viruses reveal tumour infection and transgene activity; and microbial signatures provide minimally invasive biomarkers. Here, we compare these mechanistically distinct platforms through an input-processing-output framework, examine their diagnostic and theranostic functions, and assess the readout, safety, manufacturing, analytical, and regulatory requirements that determine clinical actionability. We also propose tumour-reporting viruses and theranostic viruses as functional terms extending beyond the predominantly therapeutic concept of oncolytic viruses.

articles.title: Are both hemolysis and impaired myocyte integrity associated with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency?
articles.abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) is a potent antioxidant enzyme. G6PD deficiency, predominant among males, is a neonatal "neurotoxic" risk, characterized by episodic hemolysis that is sometimes infection triggered. Clinical risk among heterozygous G6PD-deficient females is often under-recognized. Recent reports of rhabdomyolysis among G6PD-deficient individuals are reviewed here. In one case, a male athlete with G6PD deficiency (<10% activity) experienced multiple, acute episodes of rhabdomyolysis, painful muscle symptomatology, injury and hemolysis after strenuous exertion. Both his mother with G6PD-deficiency (<45% activity) and maternal grandmother have chronic histories of episodic or triggered fatigue-related disruptive symptoms. Other case reports of G6PD-deficient individuals with muscle injury and exertional symptoms (with or without hemolysis) showed unique laboratory findings of elevated creatine kinase, myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and aminotransferases levels and myoglobinuria. Disrupted myocyte energetics and loss of cellular integrity can be attributed to impaired downstream pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-related oxidant stress protection, which is a key enzymatic consequence of G6PD-deficiency. These triggered stresses may explain the muscle fatigue and propensity to exertional injury. Correlation between stress-sensitive-impaired muscle injury among all G6PD-deficient individuals, including neonates, requires further clinical validation to ascertain oxidant-stress impact of impaired PPP-dependent cellular energetics of red blood, white blood, neural, and muscle cells.

articles.title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

articles.title: Polycythemia after SGLT2 inhibition: A post-treatment state, not a baseline subgroup.
Chlamydia trachomatis co-infection and cervical cancer risk in HPV-positive women: a cross-sectional and histological case-control study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise Chlamydia trachomatis (CT)-HPV co-infection and test whether CT positivity is associated with cervical cancer in HPV-positive women.

METHODS: We conducted a two-component retrospective study at two southern Chinese tertiary hospitals (January 2022-June 2025). Component 1 comprised 21,205 women tested for CT and HPV. Component 2 comprised 100 HPV-positive invasive cervical cancers and 100 HPV-positive non-neoplastic controls, with CT detected by pgp3-PCR on tissue.

RESULTS: CT positivity was 3.36%, HPV 21.27%, co-infection 1.29%. CT was associated with HPV positivity (OR 2.38, 95% CI 2.04-2.78) in five of six age strata. Eight of 28 genotypes were associated with CT after Benjamini-Hochberg correction; HPV52, HPV58 and HPV53 were not (OR 0.92-1.30). CT-positive women had more multiple-genotype infections (45.1% vs 32.1%; OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.36-2.22). CT co-infection was associated with cancer risk (36% vs 18%; age-adjusted OR 2.53, 95% CI 1.31-4.88; HPV16-adjusted OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.08-4.89) and with high-grade tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte infiltration (exploratory; age-adjusted OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.07-7.08).

CONCLUSIONS: CT co-infection was associated with HPV positivity across the screened population and, at tissue level, with cervical cancer in HPV-positive women. The CT-HPV association was genotype-selective. Whether CT is a modifiable cofactor in HPV-positive women warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Repeat antimicrobial susceptibility testing of serial bacterial isolates: clinical utility and diagnostic stewardship.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize evidence on the interpretation and temporal stability of antimicrobial susceptibility profiles in serial bacterial isolates and to identify factors that inform repeat testing within diagnostic stewardship.

METHODS: This narrative review integrates evidence from studies of serial clinical isolates with data on analytical variability, within-host resistance evolution, heteroresistance, antimicrobial exposure, and diagnostic stewardship.

RESULTS: Susceptibility profiles are generally stable over short intervals, although clinically relevant changes vary according to bacterial species, antimicrobial agent, specimen context, and elapsed time. Small MIC shifts, particularly near clinical breakpoints, may result in categorical discordance without indicating true resistance emergence. Pseudomonas aeruginosa exhibits greater short-term phenotypic variability than several other common pathogens. Repeat AST is most strongly supported when infection persists or recurs, the clinical response is inadequate, antimicrobial exposure may have selected for resistance, or the consequences of missed resistance are substantial. In selected lower-risk settings, referral to a recent susceptibility result may be appropriate, provided that laboratory and clinical override mechanisms remain available.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term susceptibility stability may support conservative referral to a recent AST result, but the degree of instability varies by organism, antimicrobial agent, and specimen context. Where a single operational interval is required, laboratories may adopt the shortest interval supported by local or otherwise applicable evidence, with predefined overrides for higher-risk clinical situations. Prospective multicentre validation is required before specific intervals can be generalized across clinical and laboratory settings.

articles.title: Bicentric comparison of 3-year clinical outcomes between endoscopic ultrasound-guided embolization with coil and hemostatic adjunct versus balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration for treatment of bleeding gastric varices: A propensity-score matched study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided coil injection (EUS-COIL) and balloon-occluded retrograde transvenous obliteration (BRTO) performed by interventional radiology (IR) are both effective obliterative procedures to treat gastric varices. Comparative studies are lacking. Our aim was to assess clinical outcomes for EUS-COIL versus BRTO for treatment of acute gastric variceal bleeding.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all patients admitted to two tertiary care centers between 2009-2024 who underwent either EUS-COIL or BRTO for bleeding gastric varices. The primary outcomes were technical/clinical success and adverse events.
