Secondary outcomes included transfusions, reintervention, length of hospital stay, further hepatic decompensation (esophageal variceal hemorrhage, new ascites, or new hepatic encephalopathy (HE)), and all-cause mortality. Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with cirrhosis, including with propensity score matching (PSM) which was conducted 1:1 for age, sex, Child-Pugh classification, MELD-Na score, and hemoglobin level on admission. Outcomes over the 36-months post-intervention were assessed using time-to-event analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 94 patients were included (48 EUS-COIL, 46 BRTO), of whom 60 patients with cirrhosis (30 per group) were analyzed after propensity score matching. In the matched cohort, technical success was 100% in both groups and clinical success was 100% versus 93.3% (p=0.49). The EUS-COIL group experienced significantly fewer adverse events (3% vs 37%; p=0.003) and had a longer time-to-reintervention (65 ± 52 days vs 10 ± 9.6 days; p=0.022) over a median follow-up 900 ± 790 days. The incidence of further hepatic decompensation was lower in the EUS-COIL group (10% vs 40%; p=0.007), as was the likelihood of further hepatic decompensation (HR 0.28 (95%CI: 0.08-0.984), p = 0.047) compared to BRTO. No significant differences were observed with regard to post-procedural transfusion requirements, rates of reintervention, length of hospital stay, and mortality in cirrhosis patients. In the unmatched cohort, technical (100% vs 80%; p=0.001) and clinical (100% vs 89%; p=0.03) success were higher with EUS-COIL than BRTO.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with gastric variceal hemorrhage, EUS-COIL demonstrated higher rates of technical/clinical success and lower rates of adverse events (both peri-procedural and on long-term follow-up) compared to BRTO. EUS-COIL had significantly lower rates of further hepatic decompensation. While larger prospective studies are required, these data suggest that EUS-COIL, when available, may be the preferred initial therapy for bleeding gastric varices as part of a step-up strategy.

articles.title: Context-dependent protective and pathogenic functions of YTHDF1 in MASLD and hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms and design of therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and can progressively develop into inflammatory metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis. During this progression, activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) leads to excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix. There is a growing trend to develop into hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The limited availability of effective therapeutics highlights the need to better understand the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a key post-transcriptional RNA modification that regulates gene expression and governs a broad range of physiological and pathological processes. YTH domain family 1 (YTHDF1) is a reader protein that recognizes m6A modifications on mRNAs and enhances their stability or translation by interacting with key components of the translation machinery. YTHDF1 exhibits context-dependent functions in MASLD and liver fibrosis, while it promotes HCC pathogenesis. Hepatocytic YTHDF1 alleviates MASLD by improving mitochondrial function, serving as a protective factor during its early stages. YTHDF1 in HSCs is important for initiating liver fibrosis, yet it also plays a crucial role in regulating HSC ferroptosis to counteract established fibrosis. Our structure-based analyses of YTHDF1 inhibitors reveal novel concepts, including inhibition of YTHDF1-induced condensates and direct degradation of YTHDF1 proteins by fullerene derivatives and metal-organic frameworks. YTHDF1 inhibitors serve as selective chemical probes for interrogating YTHDF1's cell type-specific functions in MASLD. They are also promising candidates for in vivo evaluation to treat MASLD and HCC and to prevent liver fibrosis at early stages.

articles.title: Epicardial fat inflammation: bridging adipose tissue biology and cardiovascular medicine.
Outcomes of Early Versus Delayed ERCP in Gallstone Pancreatitis, Stratified by BISAP Severity.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is commonly used for biliary decompression in gallstone pancreatitis (GSP), but its optimal timing in uncomplicated GSP remains controversial. We evaluated outcomes of early versus delayed ERCP by disease severity.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 207 adults with GSP who underwent ERCP at a tertiary center (2019-2025). Patients were categorized as early (<48 hours) or delayed (>48 hours). Outcomes included ERCP-related adverse events, pancreatitis-related complications, length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and mortality. Continuous variables were analyzed using Welch's t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Early (n=103) and delayed (n=104) groups were similar in demographics and Bedside Index of Severity in Acute Pancreatitis (BISAP) distribution, though delayed ERCP patients had higher Atlanta severity (15.4% vs 5.8%; p=0.040). Early ERCP was associated with fewer ERCP-related complications (2.9% vs 17.3%; RR 0.17; p=0.0008), less worsening pancreatitis (1.0% vs 12.5%; RR 0.08; p=0.0013), fewer acute necrotic collections (0% vs 5.8%; p=0.029), and lower ICU admission (8.7% vs 19.2%; p=0.044). Among BISAP 0-1 patients, early ERCP reduced LOS by 2.17 days (p=0.013). LOS differences in BISAP ≥2 patients were not significant. Mortality was low and did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Early ERCP in GSP is associated with fewer complications, reduced ICU utilization, and shorter hospitalization in mild disease. These findings support early intervention in mild-to-moderate GSP and underscore the need for prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Cesarean delivery and childhood respiratory outcomes.
authors: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network (MFMU)
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood asthma and respiratory illness are health concerns that result in a significant burden on children, their families, and the healthcare system. Prior research has demonstrated an association between CD and short-term neonatal adverse respiratory outcomes, but less is known about the potential impact of mode of delivery on long-term respiratory outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether there is an association between cesarean delivery (CD) and childhood respiratory outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a prospective, follow-up study of children delivered in the Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids study. Children were included if their mother was enrolled in the follow-up study and had data available for the primary outcome at age 6 or greater. The primary exposure was CD. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse childhood respiratory outcomes: abnormal spirometry, parent-reported diagnosis of asthma or of another chronic respiratory illness, or inpatient admission for respiratory illness. It was planned a priori to assess whether results differed according to whether or not CD occurred after evidence of labor. Log-binomial regression was used to calculate unadjusted and adjusted relative risks (RR), with vaginal delivery as the referent group.

RESULTS: Of 1,218 children enrolled in the follow-up study, 833 (68.4%) delivered vaginally and 385 (31.6%) by CD. The median gestational age at delivery was 36.1 (IQR 35.4-36.6) for those born by CD and 36.0 (IQR 35.3-36.7) for children delivered vaginally (p=0.90). Children born by CD had lower birth weight, were more likely to be small-for-gestational-age, have respiratory distress syndrome, and to be admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, and were less likely to be breastfed. Women of children born by cesarean delivery were older and more likely to have private insurance. The median age at follow-up was 7 years in those born vaginally as well as in those born by CD. There was no difference in the primary outcome between children born by CD and those born vaginally (48.6% vs. 41.5%; adjusted relative risk (aRR) 1.14; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.99, 1.31), although those born by CD were more likely to have had wheezing or whistling in the chest (49.4% vs. 40.2%; aRR 1.17; 95% CI: 1.02-1.34). There was no evidence that the association between CD and the primary composite outcome differed according to whether or not the CD was performed after labor.

CONCLUSION: Delivery via cesarean in children who were at risk for late preterm delivery was not associated with the primary composite of adverse respiratory outcomes.

TWEETABLE STATEMENT: Delivery via cesarean was not associated with a composite of adverse childhood respiratory outcomes.

articles.title: Octreotide Plus Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) versus PPI alone in Non-Variceal Upper gastrointestinal (GI) Bleeding in intensive care unit (ICU): A Multi-Center Randomized Trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare clinical outcomes between PPI therapy alone and PPI combined with octreotide in patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

METHODS: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, multi-center study included 56 patients allocated to either PPI alone or PPI plus octreotide. Baseline demographics and comorbidities were comparable between groups. Laboratory parameters were assessed over three days. Clinical outcomes included rebleeding, transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation, surgical intervention, ICU stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Prothrombin time was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (median 19 s vs 11.1 s; p=0.001), and urine output was significantly lower (p=0.011). Despite these differences, there were no significant differences in rebleeding rates, blood product transfusion, ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, or need for surgery. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the PPI plus octreotide group (39.3% vs 7%; p=0.011). Hospital length of stay was significantly shorter in the PPI plus octreotide group, likely reflecting higher early mortality rather than improved clinical recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: The addition of octreotide to PPI therapy did not improve bleeding-related outcomes. Prolonged prothrombin time did not correlate with increased bleeding or transfusion needs. These findings suggest no clinical benefit of adjunctive octreotide in this study and underscore the importance of appropriate patient selection.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin alleviates CYH33-induced hyperglycemia and preserves antitumor immunity against ovarian cancer in type 1 diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: PI3K is frequently hyperactivated in ovarian cancer and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target. CYH33 is a novel PI3Kα-selective inhibitor that has been approved in Japan for the treatment of ovarian clear cell carcinoma harboring PIK3CA mutations. However, its on-target adverse effect of hyperglycemia limits its clinical application, particularly in patients susceptible to diabetes, underscoring the urgent need to optimize therapeutic strategies to improve both safety and efficacy. In this study, we employed an ID8 syngeneic murine ovarian cancer model and demonstrated that CYH33 significantly inhibited tumor growth with a modest effect on glucose homeostasis. We then established mouse models of type 1 (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) to expose hyperglycemia induced by PI3K inhibition and identified that dapagliflozin effectively alleviated CYH33-induced hyperglycemia while preserving its antitumor activity in T1D mice. Mechanistically, the combination of CYH33 and dapagliflozin may improve the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in T1D mice, as evidenced by upregulation gene sets involved in interferon-α and interferon-γ response, as well as significantly enhanced infiltration of CD8+ T-cell in ID8 tumors. Furthermore, this combination synergized with anti-PD-1 antibody to further enhance antitumor efficacy. These findings provide a potential strategy for optimizing the clinical use of PI3K inhibitors and shed light on metabolic interventions to modulate tumor immune microenvironment.

articles.title: Accounting for seasonal variation of nasal gene expression improves transcriptome analysis of asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Environmental seasonal changes, including allergen exposure, pollutants, and viral prevalence, impact gene expression across human tissues. Therefore, season of sample collection is critical to consider when analyzing disease-associated transcriptional programs. In this study we aimed to investigate the effect of season on identification of asthma-associated genes.

METHODS: We analyzed RNA-seq data from nasal brushes of asthma patients (n=361) and healthy controls (n=57) included in the ATLANTIS study. Samples were compared across two time periods defined by a data-driven approach: winter-spring (Nov 15 -May 14) and summer-autumn (May 15 - Nov 14), correcting for age, sex, smoking, and asthma status. Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) scores of the obtained seasonal gene signatures were compared using Mann-Whitney U test in the independent PIAMA cohort (n=325) for replication.

RESULTS: We identified 1,731 genes differentially expressed between the two time periods (813 higher and 918 lower in winter-spring compared with summer-autumn; FDR < 0.05). This signature was replicated in the PIAMA cohort nasal gene expression data and was independent of asthma or allergy status. Samples collected in winter-spring showed a significantly lower predicted proportion of ciliated cells (p = 0.005) and a higher proportion of basal cells (p = 0.04) compared to those from summer-autumn. Crucially, including season as a covariate in models for asthma-associated gene expression nearly doubled the number of differentially expressed genes, from 126 to 271 (FDR < 0.05). We conclude that season of sampling strongly affects the nasal transcriptome, and we demonstrate that season-adjusted analyses significantly enhance sensitivity for detecting disease-associated changes.

articles.title: Intestinal epithelial- or hepatocyte-specific deletion of polymeric immunoglobulin receptor does not alter ethanol-induced liver disease in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the dominant mucosal antibody and is transported across epithelial cells by the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor (Pigr). Although chronic alcohol consumption disrupts intestinal barrier function and alters mucosal immunity, the contribution of Pigr-mediated IgA transport to alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) remains unclear.

METHODS: Intestinal epithelial cell-specific (PigrΔIEC) and hepatocyte-specific (PigrΔHep) Pigr-deficient mice and littermate controls were subjected to the oral chronic-plus-binge Lieber-DeCarli ethanol feeding model (NIAAA model). PigrΔHep mice were additionally evaluated in an oral chronic Lieber-DeCarli ethanol feeding model for 8 weeks. Fecal immunoglobulin concentrations, liver injury, steatosis, inflammatory gene expression, bacterial translocation, and ethanol metabolism-associated genes were assessed.

RESULTS: Intestinal deletion of Pigr numerically reduced fecal IgA concentrations following ethanol feeding, although this difference did not reach statistical significance, whereas fecal IgM concentrations remained unchanged. Ethanol-induced liver injury, steatosis and inflammation were comparable between PigrΔIEC and Pigrfl/fl littermate mice. In addition, markers of bacterial translocation, including systemic lipopolysaccharide levels and hepatic bacterial DNA, were similar in both genotypes following ethanol administration. Hepatocyte-specific Pigr deletion similarly did not affect ethanol-induced liver injury, steatosis, inflammatory responses, or bacterial translocation in two ethanol feeding models.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that deletion of Pigr in either intestinal epithelial cells or hepatocytes alone is insufficient to alter ethanol-induced liver disease, indicating that loss of Pigr in either compartment alone is insufficient to disrupt mucosal immune homeostasis during chronic ethanol exposure.

articles.title: Amifostine attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic remodeling via the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis in rats.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic pressure overload is accompanied by significant metabolic disturbances, including impaired myocardial lipid metabolism. This study ascertained whether the cytoprotective agent amifostine (WR-2721) exerts cardioprotective effects along pressure overload-induced remodeling and whether these effects are linked to modulation of the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis. Male Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to Sham, abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), and AAC + amifostine (200 mg/kg, i.p., weekly for 8 weeks) groups, with amifostine administered concurrently with hypertrophic stress. The cardiac structure and function were appraised using echocardiography and histological analyses, with the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and key regulators of lipid metabolism examined by Western blotting. Amifostine treatment was associated with attenuation of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy, reflected by lower heart and lung weight ratios, preservation of functional indices, and diminished myocardial fibrosis. At the molecular level, amifostine administration was accompanied by relative normalization of SIRT1 and PPAR-α expression, elevated levels of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins, and suppression of lipogenic markers. These findings suggest that amifostine mitigates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and is associated with improved myocardial metabolic homeostasis, accompanied by favorable changes in the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and lipid metabolism-related proteins. While these observations support the potential involvement of the SIRT1/PPAR-α signaling pathway, further mechanistic studies are required to establish its causal role in mediating the cardioprotective effects of amifostine.

articles.title: Tryptophan Metabolism in Heart Failure: Mechanisms, Biomarker Potential, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by progressive cardiac remodeling, metabolic dysregulation, and high morbidity and mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic reprogramming plays a central role in HF progression, among which tryptophan (TRP) metabolism has attracted increasing attention due to its involvement in inflammation, immune regulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and gut microbiota imbalance. TRP is mainly metabolized through the kynurenine pathway (KP), serotonin pathway, and gut microbiota-derived indole pathway, generating a series of bioactive metabolites with distinct cardiovascular effects. Recent studies have demonstrated that abnormal activation of the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO)-driven KP contributes to HF progression by promoting inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, and ventricular remodeling. In parallel, gut microbiota-derived TRP metabolites participate in the gut-heart axis and influence mitochondrial function, immune homeostasis, and cardiometabolic remodeling. In addition, TRP-related metabolites, particularly kynurenine (KYN) and the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio (KTR), exhibit promising potential as biomarkers for HF severity assessment and prognostic stratification. This review systematically summarizes the activation characteristics of TRP metabolic pathways in HF and discusses their mechanistic involvement in inflammation, immune regulation, gut microbiota dysbiosis, myocardial injury, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Furthermore, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TRP metabolism are highlighted, including pharmacological modulation, microbiota-targeted interventions, exogenous metabolite supplementation, and exercise-based metabolic regulation. Collectively, TRP metabolism represents a promising metabolic hub integrating immune, inflammatory, and mitochondrial signaling networks in HF and may provide novel opportunities for precision diagnosis and targeted therapy.

articles.title: Knowledge, health beliefs, and diabetic retinopathy screening practices among adults living with diabetes in Ebonyi state, Nigeria: a community-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major preventable cause of visual impairment among people living with diabetes, yet uptake of recommended retinal screening remains low in many low- and middle-income countries. This study assessed knowledge, health beliefs, behavioural practices, and DR screening uptake among adults living with diabetes in Ebonyi State, South-Eastern Nigeria.

METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among adults with physician-diagnosed diabetes in selected communities in Ebonyi State. Participants completed a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire assessing DR knowledge, Health Belief Model-based health beliefs, diabetes-related behavioural practices, and previous DR screening. Knowledge was assessed using a predefined scoring system, while health beliefs were measured using five-point Likert-scale items. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize findings.

RESULTS: Among 300 participants, 183 (61.0%) were male, 201 (67.0%) lived in rural communities, and 283 (94.3%) owned a mobile phone. Knowledge of DR was limited: 111 (37.0%) knew diabetes could cause eye problems, 114 (38.0%) knew DR could cause vision loss or blindness, and 112 (37.3%) recognized that DR could occur without symptoms. Only 122 (40.7%) knew that regular eye examinations were necessary despite normal vision. Health beliefs toward screening were generally favourable, with 189 (63.0%) considering regular screening important and 156 (52.0%) considering it worth the time and cost. Only 36 (12.0%) had undergone a diabetes-specific eye examination within the preceding 12 months, while 259 (86.3%) had never been screened. Among never-screened participants, lack of physician recommendation was the most frequent reason (49.7%), followed by cost (23.0%) and lack of knowledge (11.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Adults living with diabetes in Ebonyi State demonstrated substantial knowledge gaps and very low DR screening uptake despite generally favourable health beliefs. Strengthening patient education, routine provider recommendation, and accessible community-based screening may improve early detection and reduce avoidable vision loss.

articles.title: Incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections after PICC insertion: Impact of a newly established vascular access unit in a French university hospital.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are widely used, they remain associated with infectious risk. Even though the value of dedicated catheter teams is well-recognized, evidence regarding vascular access units is limited. This study compared catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates between a Vascular and Interventional Angiography Unit (VIAU) (insertion performed by physicians) and a newly established Vascular Access Unit (VAU) (insertion performed by nurse anesthetists under anesthesiologists' supervision).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted in a French university hospital, including patients having undergone PICC insertion from January 2017 to June 2020 (VIAU) and from January to June 2020 (VAU). CRBSI rates during catheter dwell time and within 8 days after PICC insertion were compared. Risk factors for CRBSI were assessed using logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among 3332 inserted PICCs, 266 (8.0%) CRBSIs occurred during catheter dwell time, with no significant difference between the VIAU (7.7%) and the VAU (9.3%). In multivariate analysis, the risk of CRBSI between the VIAU and the VAU did not significantly differ (adjusted OR = 0.978 [95%CI, 0.558-1.714]); non-metastatic cancer was associated with a higher risk of CRBSI, whereas older age appeared protective. The 8-day CRBSI rate (0.9%) was similar between the two departments (0.9% for the VIAU and 1.0% for the VAU). Slightly more than half of the CRBSIs were caused by Staphylococcus species, and one third by Gram-negative bacteria.

DISCUSSION - CONCLUSION: CRBSI rates between the established and the newly created units were similar. These results suggest that a dedicated vascular access unit staffed by trained professionals can achieve outcomes comparable to those obtained by an experienced unit.

articles.title: Exploring the pharmacological mechanism of Sanfu Patch for prevention and treatment of asthma from chronopharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics based on "winter disease cured in summer".
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The Sanfu Patch (SFP) is applied to back acupoints on the hottest days in summer to treat asthma, a winter-prone disease, and has been used in China for thousands of years. However, chrono- and temperature-related properties of treating asthma and the transdermal properties of active components are not fully clarified.

AIM OF STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the anti-asthmatic chronopharmacodynamics and transdermal pharmacokinetics of SFP based on the theory of "winter disease cured in summer".

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Chrono- and temperature-dependent Balb/c mouse models of OVA-induced asthma were established. The lung histopathology, pulmonary function testing, ELISA assays and Western blotting experiments were used for evaluating anti-asthma effect of transdermal SFP. The anti-inflammatory effects of six bioactive compounds were evaluated in vitro using BEAS-2B cells. The CETSA and SPR technique were employed to investigate whether the active components of SFP bind to anti-asthmatic proteins. The transdermal properties of active ingredients were analyzed by in vivo microdialysis assays.

RESULTS: Applying SFP on the back in summer can prevent the occurrence of asthma over a relatively long period of time. The preventive effect against asthma diminished progressively at one, three and five months after administration of SFP. Compared with SFP administration in low-temperature (17°C) environment, SFP transdermal administration in high-temperature (33°C) environment was demonstrated a more significant therapeutic effect in alleviating asthma symptoms, airway hyperresponsiveness, and airway inflammation. High-temperature administration of SFP further reduced the expression of CD40, CD40L, and CLN5 in asthmatic mice. Tetrahydropalmatine, allocryptopine, protopine, tetrahydrocoptisine, dehydrocorydaline, and sinapine thiocyanate were screened as key components contributing to the therapeutic effects of SFP against asthma, exhibiting in vitro anti-inflammatory effects. CETSA results showed that the thermal stability of CD40, CD40L and CLN5 was significantly enhanced after the treatment of the above six components. The direct SPR binding confirmed that protopine and sinapine thiocyanate could bind to the three target proteins. The AUC(0-t) and Cmax values of all six components were higher at 33°C than those at 17°C after transdermal administration of SFP.

CONCLUSIONS: This study has demonstrated the temperature advantages of the SFP application method for relieving asthma from chronopharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic perspectives, providing a foundation for subsequent research and therapeutic applications.

articles.title: Transition from pediatric to adult care for patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus: more than just a handover.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a chronic autoimmune disease that commonly presents during childhood or adolescence and requires lifelong multidisciplinary care. The transition from pediatric to adult diabetes services is a pivotal stage often accompanied by poorer glycemic control, reduced clinic attendance, and increased risk of disengagement from healthcare. This review summarizes current evidence on the principles, challenges, and effective strategies for transitioning adolescents and young adults with T1D from pediatric to adult care. A review of the literature was conducted, focusing on transition models, clinical and psychosocial outcomes, and recommendations from the International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) and other relevant studies. Evidence supports transition as a structured, individualized, and developmentally appropriate process rather than a single transfer of care. Successful transition programs incorporate early preparation, multidisciplinary collaboration, joint pediatric-adult care, transition coordinators, psychosocial support, and progressive patient autonomy. These approaches improve continuity of care, self-management, clinic attendance, and glycemic outcomes while reducing loss to follow-up. Although transition care is increasingly recognized as a key component of T1D management, its implementation remains inconsistent. Wider adoption of standardized, evidence-based transition pathways is needed to optimize long-term health outcomes for young adults with T1D.

articles.title: Integrative m6A epitranscriptomic and transcriptomic analysis in livers of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with hepatic metabolic remodeling, but the coordinated changes in N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification and mRNA expression in human T2DM liver remain insufficiently defined. Here, we integrated mRNA expression profiles extracted from Arraystar Human LncRNA Microarray V5.0 with newly generated m6A epitranscriptomic microarray profiles in liver specimens from first-onset T2DM patients and controls. We identified 1923 differentially expressed and 7389 differentially m6A-methylated mRNA transcripts. Integrated analysis identified 898 dual-significant transcripts, predominated by hypermethylated-upregulated transcripts (n = 864), which were mainly enriched in amino acid, lipid, carbon, and energy metabolic pathways. By integrating m6A regulator expression, module-level correlation, and regulator-gene network connectivity, METTL14 was prioritized as a candidate component of the m6A writer complex associated with metabolic pathway remodeling. Ten METTL14-associated candidate genes were further prioritized, and clinical validation confirmed increased expression of METTL14 and most candidate genes in an independent human liver cohort. METTL14 depletion in Huh7 cells using two selected independent siRNAs concordantly reduced EHHADH, ACAT2, ACADS, SDHA, C3, and DLD. Secondary analysis of GSE185109 further showed significant downregulation of eight corresponding mouse orthologs in Mettl14-deficient liver, together with descriptive alterations in m6A peak patterns. These findings identify a functionally supported METTL14-associated m6A-mRNA network linked to hepatic metabolic remodeling in human T2DM, while direct transcript-specific m6A regulation remains to be established.

articles.title: Paeoniflorin Promotes Mitophagy Against Acute Kidney Injury via PRDX5-Dependent Inhibition of RACK1.
articles.abstract: Impaired mitophagy is a core driver of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet effective pharmacological strategies to restore this mitochondrial quality control mechanism remain limited. Paeoniflorin (Pae), a natural monoterpene glycoside, has shown renoprotective potential, but whether and how it regulates mitophagy remain unclear.. This study investigated the protective effects of Pae in mice subjected to bilateral renal ischaemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and in cisplatin-treated TCMK-1 cells, with renal tubular-specific Prdx5 conditional knockout (Prdx5-CKO) mice used to determine the requirement for PRDX5. Pae treatment dose-dependently ameliorated renal tubular injury, reduced serum creatinine and BUN levels and inflammatory cytokine expression, and restored mitochondrial DNA copy number.Mechanistically, Pae upregulated PRDX5, which interacted with and negatively regulated RACK1. PRDX5 deficiency abolished the protective effects of Pae, aggravated renal injury, and further suppressed PINK1/Parkin expression. Conversely, RACK1 overexpression suppressed PINK1/Parkin and induced cellular injury, while RACK1 knockdown restored mitophagy and alleviated cisplatin-induced damage. Critically, the renoprotective effect of Pae was strictly PRDX5-dependent, as RACK1 knockdown rescued Pae efficacy in PRDX5-deficient cells. These findings demonstrate that Pae alleviates AKI by activating PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy through the PRDX5/RACK1 signalling axis, identifying PRDX5 as an indispensable therapeutic target and revealing a novel mechanism for maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis in AKI.

articles.title: The Mechanism of S-adenosylhomocysteine Hydrolase in Regulating Podocyte Apoptosis and Diabetic Nephropathy via Moap1.
articles.abstract: Elevated levels of S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) in patients with diabetes are closely associated with renal dysfunction. Inhibition of SAH hydrolase (SAHH) increases SAH levels, promotes apoptosis, and exacerbates streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic nephropathy. However, the precise mechanism by which SAHH inhibition induces podocyte apoptosis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate how SAHH inhibition specifically induces podocyte apoptosis and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. We established an STZ-induced podocyte-specific SAHH knockout mouse model and an in vitro model of high-glucose-treated podocytes. Our results showed that podocyte-specific SAHH deletion significantly exacerbated streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic kidney injury. SAHH inhibition significantly upregulated the expression of modulator of apoptosis 1 (Moap1), which in turn promoted podocyte apoptosis through activation of the pro-apoptotic protein BAX. Knockdown of Moap1 partially reversed this apoptotic phenotype. Mechanistically, SAHH inhibition downregulated DNA methyltransferase 3b (DNMT3b) expression, leading to hypomethylation of the Moap1 promoter and subsequent upregulation of Moap1 transcription. ChIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed that DNMT3b directly bound to the region of the Moap1 promoter and regulated its transcriptional activity. Restoration of DNMT3b expression reversed Moap1 upregulation and partially rescued the apoptotic phenotype induced by SAHH inhibition. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SAHH inhibition promotes podocyte apoptosis by upregulating Moap1 expression through a DNMT3b-dependent hypomethylation mechanism, which in turn activates BAX. This study provides novel potential therapeutic targets for diabetic nephropathy with elevated SAH levels.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy and incident atrial fibrillation in non-diabetic adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease: a propensity matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are potent risk factors for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet whether GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) prevent incident AF in non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD is unexamined. We assessed whether GLP-1RA therapy reduces 1-year AF incidence in this cardiorenal phenotype.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (66 healthcare organizations), we conducted a retrospective target trial emulation of non-diabetic adults aged 18 or older with obesity and CKD stages 3-5 diagnosed 2021-2024. Patients receiving semaglutide, liraglutide, or tirzepatide (n = 10,985) were compared with unexposed patients (n = 94,527). After propensity score matching, 7326 patients remained per cohort. The primary outcome was incident AF at 1 year; secondary outcomes included AF subtypes, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox models generated hazard ratios (HRs); sensitivity analyses extended follow-up to 2-3 years with landmark analyses.

RESULTS: At 1 year, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower incident AF (1.63% vs. 2.62%; HR 0.655, 95% CI 0.508-0.844; p = 0.001), a 34.5% relative risk reduction. Reductions were consistent for paroxysmal (HR 0.586), persistent (HR 0.482), and longstanding persistent AF (HR 0.527; all p < 0.05); permanent AF was non-significant at 1 year. Ventricular tachyarrhythmias (HR 0.556; p = 0.002) and hospitalization (HR 0.668; p < 0.001) were also significantly reduced. Benefits persisted across 2- and 3-year follow-up and remained consistent in landmark analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: In non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significant, durable reductions in incident AF, ventricular arrhythmias, and hospitalization. These findings are consistent with a possible cardiorenal benefit and support prioritizing this phenotype for dedicated randomized trials.

articles.title: C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and coronary microvascular dysfunction after primary percutaneous coronary intervention: The mediating role of insulin resistance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index integrates systemic inflammation, nutritional status, and immune function. We investigated its association with angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR)-defined coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and performed an exploratory statistical mediation analysis involving estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 456 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. AMR-defined CMD was prespecified as AMR ≥250 mmHg·s/m. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. Sensitivity and exploratory mediation analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: AMR-defined CMD was present in 228 patients (50.0%). In Model 3, each doubling of CALLY was associated with lower odds of AMR-defined CMD (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.80-0.94; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, Q3 and Q4 were associated with 44% (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97; P = 0.037) and 52% (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.28-0.84; P = 0.010) lower odds, respectively (P for trend = 0.018). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P = 0.001) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.310). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. Exploratory mediation analysis estimated that eGDR statistically accounted for 15.47% of the observed association.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher CALLY values were inversely associated with AMR-defined CMD after primary PCI for STEMI. eGDR may account for part of this association. CALLY may serve as an auxiliary marker for AMR-defined CMD risk stratification, pending prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Associations of PM2.5 components with dynamic and accelerated progression of different kidney function states and subsequent cardiovascular events: The GOLD-Health cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, the relationships between specific PM2.5 components and the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory remain uncertain.

METHODS: Employing multistate and accelerated failure time (AFT) modeling in a prospective cohort of 307,639 participants, we examined the associations of 2-year exposure to PM2.5 and its components (sulfate [SO42-], nitrate [NO3-], ammonium [NH4+], organic matter [OM], and black carbon [BC]) with dynamic and accelerated progression from different kidney function categories (1-4, according to estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] and self-reported CKD) to CVD, and ultimately to cardiovascular death.

RESULTS: Over 1,058,210 person-years of follow-up, we documented 23,948 CVD cases and 7763 cardiovascular death cases. We observed that PM2.5 and its components were significantly associated with the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory, with SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ exhibiting larger hazard ratios (HRs). Per-interquartile range (IQR) increments in SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ were positively correlated with the transition from kidney function category 2 to 3, and the HRs were 1.273 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.257-1.289), 1.304 (95% CI: 1.290-1.317), and 1.280 (95% CI: 1.267-1.294), respectively. The AFT model indicated that higher levels of PM2.5 and its constituents significantly accelerated the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory. The predictive transition times from kidney function category 2 to 3 for 2-year NO3- exposure were 1727.43 days at 4.2 μg/m3 and 868.56 days at 7.0 μg/m3.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings revealed that PM2.5 components (2-year exposure) may be important risk factors for adverse cardiorenal outcomes.

articles.title: Direct Effects Multiplicative Inference (DEMI): causal prediction from pairwise clinical relationships, applied to antidepressant response.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This paper introduces Direct Effects Multiplicative Inference (DEMI), a causal algorithm that reasons through a medical knowledgebase and predicts clinical outcomes from direct, unmediated effects. This study compares performance of DEMI to logistic regression, a common inference mechanism available for analysis of patient-level tabular data.

METHODS: We extracted 430 million relationships between pairs of medical concepts from the All of Us database. DEMI uses this knowledgebase to predict likelihood of outcomes, in three steps: (1) patient features are temporally ordered using pairwise precedence counts; (2) each feature's total effect on the outcome is recursively decomposed into direct and indirect (mediated) components by working backward through the temporal order; (3) direct effects are aggregated multiplicatively to estimate the odds of outcomes. DEMI uses the distribution of a pair of variables, as reported in the medical knowledgebase. Logistic regression uses patient-level tabular data, which includes the joint distribution of all variables. Performance was assessed using Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: DEMI predicted response to 15 antidepressants with a mean AUC of 0.934 (range, 0.512-0.996). Logistic regression achieved similar discrimination (mean AUC, 0.935; range, 0.512-1.000). At α = 0.05, the two methods did not differ significantly. DEMI achieved comparable discrimination using precomputed pairwise statistics without access to the joint distribution of patient features. Under the same variable-selection rule, DEMI could use on average 113 more predictors per task than logistic regression.

CONCLUSION: DEMI predicted antidepressant response from a medical knowledgebase as well as logistic regression did from patient-level data. Under its structural assumptions (no unmeasured confounding and correct temporal ordering), it does so by isolating direct, unmediated predictors and excluding effects that operate through intermediate variables.

articles.title: Nifedipine-modulated gut microbiota attenuates hypertensive vascular injury through Bifidobacterium-associated inosine-Adora2b signaling.
articles.abstract: Although antihypertensive drugs mitigate hypertensive vascular injury, their vascular benefits are not fully explained by blood pressure reduction alone. Many cardiovascular drugs reshape the gut microbiota, which in turn influences their vascular pharmacology. We therefore investigated whether gut microbiota remodeling contributes to nifedipine-mediated vascular protection in high-salt hypertensive rats and a pilot patient cohort. Combining 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, fecal microbiota transplantation, microbiota depletion, supplementation, and selective receptor antagonism, we found that nifedipine ameliorated gut dysbiosis. Transplantation of nifedipine-modulated microbiota improved intestinal barrier integrity and reduced vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, collagen deposition, and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching, while only marginally lowering blood pressure. Conversely, microbiota depletion markedly attenuated these vascular benefits despite preserving nifedipine-induced blood pressure lowering. These vascular benefits were associated with nifedipine-restored Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis 420 (B420) and increased inosine availability. Supplementation with either recapitulated major vascular protective effects of nifedipine without statistically significant changes in blood pressure. In hypertensive patients, nifedipine treatment was associated with higher intestinal B420 abundance and inosine levels. In vitro, inosine modulated macrophages in an Adora2b- and Rap1-dependent manner, with accompanying changes in cAMP and KLF4, ameliorating VSMC dysfunction via paracrine signaling. In vivo, systemic Adora2b antagonism attenuated the vascular protective effects of both inosine and B420. Together, our findings support a gut microbiota-dependent component of nifedipine-mediated vascular protection that extends beyond blood pressure lowering, involving B420, increased inosine availability, and Adora2b signaling. We also nominate B420 and inosine as candidate adjuncts to calcium channel blocker therapy.

articles.title: The cardiometabolic ageing-cardiovascular disease axis: A 32-year European study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic ageing encompasses the population-level coexistence of diabetes, obesity, and demographic ageing within the analytical framework of this study. We examined whether this profile, summarized by a Diabetes-Obesity-Ageing (DOA) index, was associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) burden and whether this association varied with national income.

METHODS: We analysed a balanced panel of 27 European Union countries from 1990 to 2021. DOA was calculated as the equally weighted mean of pooled z-scores for age-standardized diabetes prevalence, age-standardized obesity prevalence, and the proportion aged ≥65 years. The ageing component represented demographic composition. Two-way fixed-effects models examined associations with age-standardized CVD disability-adjusted life-year and mortality rates, including an interaction between DOA and ln(GDP per capita). Sensitivity analyses included alternative estimators, temporal specifications, component-specific models, and PCA-based weighting.

RESULTS: The DOA × ln(GDP) interaction was negative and statistically significant in the primary model (β = -0.111; p = 0.006), with a consistent result for cardiovascular mortality (β = -0.118; p = 0.004). Component-specific interactions were significant for diabetes and population ageing, but not obesity. The PCA-based interaction was also negative and significant. Temporal analyses showed a negative interaction in levels models and a positive interaction in short-run specifications. Lead-placebo associations were also significant, while cointegration tests provided mixed evidence of a stable long-run relationship.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher national income was associated with attenuation of the DOA-CVD relationship in levels models. The composite and component-specific analyses provide complementary perspectives on this pattern, with clearer evidence for diabetes and population ageing. These findings describe an income-dependent population-level association whose interpretation remains sensitive to temporal specification.

articles.title: MLKL Orchestrates ER-Mitochondria Stress to Drive Dendritic Cell Pyroptosis and Immunoparalysis in Sepsis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis induces systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation, leading to immunoparalysis characterized by dendritic cells (DCs) depletion and dysfunction. Mixed lineage kinase domain-like pseudokinase (MLKL) is an oranelle stress regulator; however, its role in DCs-mediated immune regulation during sepsis remains poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to elucidate the role of MLKL in sepsis-associated DCs dysfunction and to determine the underlying molecular mechanisms linking MLKL to immune dysregulation and disease severity.

METHODS: Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was used to establish sepsis in wild-type (WT) and MLKL-deficient (MLKL-/-) mice. Primary CD11c+ DCs and DC2.4 cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS), with or without MLKL knockdown. Cell death pathways, organelle stress responses, ER-phagy, and immune function were analyzed using molecular, cellular, and in vivo approaches.

RESULTS: Sepsis and LPS stimulation induced time-dependent MLKL activation and necroptosis-related signaling. MLKL deficiency attenuated NLRP3-gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis, alleviated endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial stress, restored ER-phagy, and reduced reactive oxygen species production. These effects preserved DCs maturation and costimulatory molecule expression, thereby enhancing CD4+ T-cell activation. Mechanistically, MLKL localized to mitochondria-associated membranes and interacted with mitofusin 2 (MFN2), promoting its degradation; a specific MLKL fragment was sufficient to destabilize MFN2. In vivo, MLKL ablation reshaped inflammatory cytokine profiles, reduced multi-organ injury, and improved survival following sepsis.

CONCLUSION: MLKL drives DCs dysfunction and immune dysregulation in sepsis by destabilizing MFN2 and impairing ER-phagy. Targeting the MLKL-MFN2-ER-phagy axis represents a potential therapeutic strategy for restoring immune competence in sepsis.

articles.title: Enhanced Six-Month Protection and Immune Responses in Four-Finger Threadfin Following Vaccination with Formalin-Killed Streptococcus iniae.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus iniae is a major bacterial pathogen causing severe economic losses in marine and freshwater aquaculture worldwide. This study evaluated the long-term protective efficacy and immunostimulatory effects of a formalin-killed cell (FKC) vaccine, with and without Montanide ISA 763 adjuvant, against S. iniae infection in four-finger threadfin (Eleutheronema tetradactylum). Fish were assigned to three groups: control, FKC, and FKC combined with Montanide ISA 763 (FKC+ISA). Vaccinated fish received 1.5 × 109 CFU/fish and were challenged at 1, 3, and 6 months post-vaccination (mpv) using the virulent S. iniae GSI-111 strain. An additional heterologous challenge using the S. iniae T6 strain was performed at 6 mpv. Immune-related gene expression, including complement component 2 (C2), cluster of differentiation 8, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-10, and interleukin-12 in spleen and kidney tissues, as well as serum lysozyme activity and S. iniae-specific immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody responses, were evaluated throughout the experimental period. Both vaccinated groups exhibited significantly stronger immune responses than the control group, with the FKC+ISA group demonstrating the greatest and most sustained immunological activation. Elevated serum lysozyme activity and specific IgM antibody levels were maintained for up to 6 mpv. Following homologous challenge with the GSI-111 strain, the FKC+ISA group achieved 100% relative percent survival (RPS) under the present experimental conditions at all challenge time points, whereas the FKC group provided consistently high but slightly lower protection (92.9-97.2% RPS). During the heterologous challenge with the T6 strain at 6 mpv, the FKC+ISA group again achieved 100% RPS under the present experimental conditions, while the FKC group achieved 78.6% RPS. In contrast, the control group experienced high mortality, with survival rates ranging from 50-75%. Re-isolation analysis confirmed the absence or marked reduction of S. iniae in surviving vaccinated fish. These findings demonstrate that the Montanide ISA 763-adjuvanted FKC vaccine elicits robust and durable humoral and cellular immune responses, providing long-term homologous and heterologous protection against S. iniae infection in four-finger threadfin.

articles.title: ECMO Weaning Blood Processing: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has been widely used for life support in severe refractory cardiac and respiratory failure. During ECMO weaning, the circuit usually retains 500-800 mL of residual blood. Direct discarding leads to blood loss, increased anemia, and higher allogeneic transfusion requirements, while appropriate autologous blood reinfusion can reduce transfusion risks and medical costs. However, evidence on blood processing strategies during ECMO weaning remains scattered, and no unified clinical guidelines exist.

METHODS: This scoping review strictly followed the PRISMA‑ScR 2018 checklist and JBI methodology. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang from inception to March 28, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed quality. Descriptive synthesis and qualitative analysis were performed due to high heterogeneity and lack of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

RESULTS: A total of 68 articles were retrieved, and 9 studies were finally included. The identified blood processing strategies were classified into four categories: blood cell salvage system (BCS) autologous reinfusion, pump-controlled blood reinfusion, modified CPD blood bag storage reinfusion, and direct discard.

CONCLUSION: Based on current observational evidence, autologous blood reinfusion during ECMO weaning appears feasible and is associated with favorable surrogate hematological outcomes compared with direct discard. Identified strategies differ in indications, operation, and costs, and may be selected individually according to ECMO mode, hemodynamic status, and institutional conditions. Given the limited number, low quality, and high heterogeneity of included studies, no conclusions regarding hard clinical outcomes can be drawn. This review highlights the urgency of high‑quality studies with long‑term clinical endpoints to further verify efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Bedside flexible bronchoscopy in the neonatal intensive care unit: Current evidence, clinical applications and future directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung ultrasound and targeted echocardiography let the neonatal team examine lungs and heart at the cot side, but neither shows the airway. Flexible bronchoscopy does, and it is increasingly performed inside the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

METHODS: Narrative review of published series of flexible bronchoscopy in infants cared for in neonatal units, supported by pediatric intensive care studies and society standards. Certainty of evidence was not graded.

RESULTS: Twelve neonatal series (652 infants) were identified; all but one were single-center and most were retrospective. In referred infants, airway abnormalities were reported in 60-96% and a change in management in 63-94%; when intubated neonates were examined routinely, significant airway disease was found in 19%. The main indications were repeated extubation failure, persistent atelectasis, stridor and suspected congenital anomaly. Transient desaturation occurred in 2-24% of procedures, and one bilateral pneumothorax was reported. Where identified, the operator was usually a pediatric pulmonologist, so the procedure is currently a bedside consultation, not point-of-care testing in the sense applied to ultrasound. No study has examined mortality, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, duration of ventilation or length of stay.

CONCLUSIONS: Bedside flexible bronchoscopy answers questions about the neonatal airway that ultrasound cannot, and in selected infants it often changes what is done next. Its place should be defined by prospective studies with stated denominators, consistent reporting of physiological cost, and a training pathway for neonatal operators. Reduced exposure to tuberculosis and other hospital pathogens by avoiding transport is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated benefit.

articles.title: Improving inpatient palliative care delivery in COPD: a mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is limited evidence to guide implementation of recommended collaborative palliative care (PC) models for hospitalized patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We sought to characterize palliative needs and identify barriers to PC delivery to inform inpatient collaborative care models.

METHODS: We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of hospitalized adults with COPD and physicians (hospitalists and pulmonologists) at two urban teaching hospitals in the United States. Patients rated their palliative needs in a survey, followed by a semi-structured interview. Physicians rated the perceived needs of a typical hospitalized patient with moderate-to-severe COPD, and then a purposive sample completed an interview. Survey data were summarized descriptively. Two independent coders conducted content analysis of interview transcripts to identify convergent and divergent perspectives across participant groups.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients (mean age 67 years; 47% female, 47% Black, 47% White) and 39 physicians (56% hospitalists, 44% pulmonologists, 44% female, 64% White, 23% Asian) completed surveys. All patients and 15 physicians completed interviews. Participants identified three domains of palliative needs: physical symptoms, psychosocial and emotional distress, and communication. Although physicians rated palliative needs as more burdensome than patients did, they frequently deferred addressing these needs due to competing clinical demands, prognostic uncertainty, and the perceived limited value of inpatient PC consultation. Patients reported that their palliative needs often remained unaddressed.

CONCLUSIONS: Collaborative inpatient PC models for COPD should prioritize addressing common palliative needs, strengthen generalist PC skills, establish clear criteria for specialist PC involvement, and improve coordination across care settings.

articles.title: The association between New Zealand Blackcurrant anthocyanins and airway inflammation, including PAI-1, in asthma: A placebo-controlled crossover feasibility study.
articles.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic inflammatory airway disease. Plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) contributes to airway inflammation, remodelling, disease severity, and exacerbations. As anthocyanins (ACN) possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, and oxidative stress is a key feature of asthma, investigating the efficacy of anthocyanin supplementation in this population is warranted. Although the study was originally designed to assess variability to plan a larger study in the event only five participants were recruited. The study design was a cross-over design. Participants received either a 300 mg ACN supplement or an identical placebo for eight weeks. Feasibility outcomes and asthma symptom control were assessed, alongside exploratory analyses of inflammatory markers, including fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) and salivary plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1). Associations between changes in PAI-1, Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) scores, and the PAI-1 4G/5G polymorphism were also explored. Improvements in asthma symptom control were observed following ACN supplementation, including reduced daytime and nighttime symptoms and no activity limitation, similar to the placebo phase. Moreover, an absence of short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) reliever use N/N 0/5, 0%; SABA use reappeared during the placebo phase N/N 1/5, 20%. Preliminary findings support the feasibility of conducting a larger trial of ACN supplementation in adults with asthma. While ACN supplementation may have a positive effect on asthma symptom control, the findings are exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered studies with larger sample sizes.

articles.title: A natural neuronal receptor-derived MRI probe targets β-amyloid oligomers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Early-to-mid detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because clinically used amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) probes primarily visualize fibrillar β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and require radioactive isotopes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a radiation-free alternative, but its application in molecular AD diagnosis is limited by insufficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and poor specificity toward early-to-mid Aβ species. Here, we developed a BBB-crossing liposomal MRI probe, Lipo@D1D2-Gd, by integrating a natural Aβ oligomer-binding receptor domain with a gadolinium chelator. The extracellular D1D2 domains of human leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B2 (LilrB2), a neuronal receptor that recognizes neurotoxic Aβ oligomers, were recombinantly produced and bioorthogonally conjugated with a gadolinium chelator. The resulting D1D2-Gd retained its Aβ-binding capability and MRI contrast activity. To enable brain delivery, D1D2-Gd was encapsulated within maltose-functionalized PEGylated liposomes designed to facilitate BBB transport. After intravenous administration to 4-month-old 5xFAD mice, Lipo@D1D2-Gd crossed the BBB, accumulated in Aβ-rich brain regions, and generated MRI contrast enhancement that differentiated 5xFAD mice from wild-type controls. Systemic safety evaluation showed no obvious hematological, biochemical, or histological toxicity. This study establishes a receptor-derived, BBB-crossing biomaterial platform for radiation-free molecular imaging of early-to-mid AD-associated Aβ pathology. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1) Promising Targeting Strategy: We repurposed a human-derived natural receptor domain (LilrB2 D1D2) as a targeting module for β-amyloid (Aβ) oligomers, a key pathogenic species in Alzheimer's disease (AD). 2) Non-invasive MRI Approach: We constructed a liposomal probe designed to deliver the Gd-labeled targeting agent to the brain, enabling the detection of Aβ-associated pathology in 4-month-old 5xFAD mice via non-radioactive MRI, well before overt cognitive decline. 3) Experimental Validation: We demonstrate the probe's association with Aβ oligomers/plaques, effective BBB crossing, differences in MRI signals between AD model and wild-type mice, and an initially favorable biosafety profile, with no observed toxicity under the tested conditions. 4) Clinical Translation Potential: Our work presents a promising pathway toward a safe, accessible, and early-to-mid-stage AD screening tool, with the potential to facilitate population-wide screening and earlier therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Validation studies of ICD-10 diagnostic codes for identifying common causes of hospitalization: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis codes are widely used to identify clinical conditions in administrative health data for epidemiologic research, surveillance, and health services evaluation. However, the validity of ICD-10-coded diagnoses varies across conditions and healthcare settings, and validation studies differ substantially in design, case definitions, and reporting practices.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize validation studies of ICD-10-based case definitions for eight common causes of hospitalization and identify methodological factors affecting the interpretation and comparability of reported performance estimates.

DESIGN: PubMed and Embase (2005-2025) were searched for systematic reviews and primary studies validating ICD-10-coded diagnoses for the following conditions: heart failure, osteoarthritis, pneumonia, diabetes mellitus, acute myocardial infarction, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, acute kidney injury, and stroke. Data on study characteristics, case definitions, reference standards, and performance metrics were extracted and descriptively summarized.

RESULTS: We identified 116 unique primary publications through 11 systematic reviews and our database search. Stroke and heart failure had the largest evidence base, whereas few validation studies were identified for several conditions. More than one-third of studies reported only positive predictive value, typically reflecting a study design that verified algorithm-identified cases and therefore precluded estimation of sensitivity and specificity. When reported, specificity was generally high, whereas sensitivity varied considerably; however, differences in study design limited comparability of estimates. Incorporating laboratory results, procedures, medications, or other electronic health record data often improved the performance of ICD-10-based case definitions.

CONCLUSIONS: Validation studies of ICD-10-coded diagnoses are highly heterogeneous in design and reporting, limiting direct comparison across studies. Many rely on designs that only estimate positive predictive value and therefore provide incomplete assessments of validity. Standardized, population-based validation studies measuring both sensitivity and specificity are needed to improve the reliability and reproducibility of administrative health data for epidemiologic research, surveillance, and quality improvement.

articles.title: Discovery of potent azabenzothiazoloquinoxalines as protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) antagonists.
articles.abstract: A quinoxaline benzothiazole PAR4 antagonist chemotype has been optimized by investigating aza substitutions in the benzothiazole ring. The 7'-azabenzothiazole, when combined with extended side chains discovered in previous studies, generated advanced leads with significantly improved potency, reduced cLogP, and favorable pharmacokinetic properties.

articles.title: AI-derived panoramic score and its association with major systemic diseases: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether an AI-generated, panoramic radiograph-based score was associated with five selected systemic diseases.

METHODS: 26,550 panoramic radiographs from two hospitals were analyzed using an AI model that detected teeth and implants and quantified alveolar bone loss. A radiograph-based score (0-100) was derived from missing teeth and weighted bone-loss severity. Associations with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoporosis, ischemic heart disease, and hyperlipidemia were assessed using between-group comparisons, prevalence trends across score bins, and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Incremental discrimination over covariates alone was quantified using ΔAUC and the DeLong test.

RESULTS: Patients with each condition had lower scores than controls (all P<0.001), with the largest adjusted difference for diabetes mellitus (β=-6.25). Prevalence of all five conditions showed a decreasing trend across ascending score strata (Cochran-Armitage P<0.001), with the highest Q1-to-Q5 relative risk for ischemic heart disease (4.73). After adjustment, the score remained independently associated with all diseases (AUC, 0.74-0.80), with significant incremental discrimination for diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia (ΔAUC =0.0015-0.0154; DeLong P<0.0188) but not ischemic heart disease or osteoporosis.

CONCLUSIONS: An AI-derived panoramic radiograph-based score was independently associated with five selected systemic diagnoses. Clinical significance An AI-derived score obtained from routinely acquired panoramic radiographs was independently associated with major systemic diseases. This automated, quantitative score may serve as an exploratory image-based index, supporting integrated management between dental and medical care.

articles.title: Changing global prevalence of diuretic resistance amongst patients with heart failure: a systematic review and cumulative meta-analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diuretic resistance (DR) is a major challenge in the management of heart failure, contributing to persistent congestion, prolonged hospitalization, and adverse outcomes. However, inconsistent DR definitions and study designs have resulted in uncertain prevalence estimates and limited guideline development.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the pooled prevalence of DR in heart failure using studies with valid heart-failure denominators and extractable binary DR events, and to evaluate the stability and heterogeneity of prevalence estimates over time.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Science Citation Index, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and the Database of Abstracts of Reviews of Effects were searched from 2000 through the final updated search in 2026, supplemented by reference screening.

STUDY SELECTION: Observational studies and randomized studies relevant to DR in adults with heart failure were considered for the systematic review. For the quantitative prevalence analysis, studies were required to include an unselected or consecutively assembled heart-failure denominator and an extractable binary DR event count based on a prespecified or study-defined criterion arising after cohort entry. Studies enrolling only patients with established DR, reporting only continuous diuretic-response measures, or lacking a valid binary DR numerator were excluded from prevalence pooling but could remain relevant to the qualitative systematic review. Two reviewers independently extracted data. Prevalence was pooled on the logit scale using an inverse-variance random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance and Hartung-Knapp inference. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, cumulative meta-analysis, influence and sensitivity analyses, a generalized linear mixed-model robustness analysis, and exploratory funnel-plot asymmetry testing were undertaken.

RESULTS: Twelve prevalence-eligible studies involving 24,904 patients were included in the quantitative prevalence analysis, of whom 4,861 met study-defined criteria for DR. The pooled prevalence was 23.0% (95% CI, 13.6%-36.2%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=98.5%; τ²=0.851; Q=757.17, df=11; p<0.001). The 95% prediction interval was 3.4%-71.6%. A generalized linear mixed model yielded a similar pooled prevalence of 22.5% (95% CI, 14.5%-33.2%). Cumulative analysis showed that the estimate changed as new eligible studies accrued, reaching 23.0% after inclusion of the most recent studies. Exploratory regression analysis did not demonstrate statistically significant funnel-plot asymmetry (p=0.072).

CONCLUSION: Approximately one in four patients with heart failure meets a study-defined criterion for DR in prevalence-eligible cohorts. However, the very wide prediction interval and extreme heterogeneity show that DR frequency is strongly dependent on population, setting, timing of assessment, and operational definition. Standardized diagnostic criteria and prospectively assembled prevalence cohorts are required to improve comparability and guide clinical practice.

articles.title: Weekend Admission and Early In-Hospital Mortality Among Patients with Hematologic Malignancies admitted for Febrile Neutropenia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Weekend admissions have been associated with worse health outcomes compared with weekday admissions. Our study assessed the association between weekend admission and early in-hospital mortality among patients with hematologic malignancies and febrile neutropenia. We further evaluated whether septic shock mediates this relationship, regardless of length of in-hospital stay.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the 2016-2020 NIS database identifying patients with febrile neutropenia and hematologic malignancies using ICD-10 codes. Weekend admission was the primary exposure, while 3- and 7-day in-hospital mortality were the study outcomes. Generalized linear models estimated the association between weekend admission and each outcome, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, cancer type, elective admission status and length of stay.

RESULTS: Among 45,540 patients in this study, 57% were male, 65% were white and the mean age was 51 years. Weekend admission was significantly associated with a higher risk of 3-day (RR=1.48; 95%CI: [1.21-1.83]) and 7-day mortality (RR=1.32; 95%CI: [1.12-1.56]). Mediation analysis demonstrated that septic shock significantly mediated the association between weekend admission and overall in-hospital mortality - indirect effect (RR=1.03; 95% CI [1.01-1.04]), whereas the direct effect and overall effect of weekend admission on mortality were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Weekend admission was associated with a higher risk of early in-hospital mortality. Septic shock partially mediated this relationship when assessed across the entire in-hospital stay. The absence of a direct weekend effect suggests that health system-level factors contributing to septic shock may represent key intervention targets to improve mortality outcomes in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Effect of clarithromycin on the circulating inflammatory proteome in community-acquired pneumonia: a secondary analysis of the ACCESS trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ACCESS randomized double-blind controlled trial in hospitalized adults with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) showed that adding clarithromycin to standard-of-care therapy accelerated clinical recovery within the first 72 hours after the commencement of treatment and reduced progression to organ dysfunction.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Does clarithromycin treatment modulate the circulating inflammatory protein profile in CAP, and can inflammatory endotypes identify patient subgroups with distinct clinical responses?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint. After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering.

RESULTS: IL6 was selectively downregulated on day 4 in the clarithromycin arm, whereas IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, and SCF decreased over time across both treatment arms, consistent with resolution of inflammation. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. Clustering consistently identified two inflammatory endotypes with comparable SOFA, but distinct RSS scores. The endotype with lower RSS demonstrated higher IFN-γ and globally elevated inflammatory protein expression; in that endotype 90-day mortality was decreased with clarithromycin treatment.

INTERPRETATION: Clarithromycin exerts measurable immunomodulatory effects in CAP, characterized by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL6. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04724044, EudraCT 2020-004452-15.

articles.title: Phase 2 study of fazpilodemab, a FGFR1/Klothoβ agonist, in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease with limited treatment options. Fazpilodemab, a bispecific antibody targeting fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) and Klotho β (KLB), showed promising trends in liver health markers in type 2 diabetes mellitus and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

METHODS: This Phase 2 randomized study evaluated the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of fazpilodemab in patients with MASH and hepatic steatosis. Patients were randomized to receive fazpilodemab or placebo subcutaneously every 2 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening at Week 52. Secondary endpoints included histological improvement from baseline (≥2 points reduction in MAS with ≥ 1-point reduction in either lobular inflammation or hepatocellular ballooning and no worsening of fibrosis stage), fibrosis improvement from baseline (≥1 MASH CRN fibrosis stage) and no worsening of steatohepatitis (no increase in MAS for ballooning, inflammation, or steatosis), and changes in hepatic fat fraction. Safety, PK, and immunogenicity were also assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 46 patients (fazpilodemab 50 mg [n=11], 75 mg [n=11], or 100 mg [n=11]; and placebo [n=13]) were enrolled, of whom 23 had Week 52 or early termination biopsy. The proportion of patients achieving resolution of MASH without worsening of fibrosis was 37.5% (3/8) in the 50 mg arm, 14.3% (1/7) in the 75 mg arm, and 33.3% (2/6) in the 100 mg arm, compared to 16.7% (1/6) in the placebo arm. For the secondary endpoints, improvements in liver histology and fibrosis were numerically higher in fazpilodemab-treated patients; transient improvements in hepatic fat fraction were observed. Fazpilodemab was adequately tolerated, with no new safety signals identified.

CONCLUSIONS: While the study was prematurely terminated, fazpilodemab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with previous studies. No definite conclusion could be drawn regarding the preliminary fazpilodemab efficacy profile due to the limited sample size and early dropouts.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04171765 IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Dual targeting of FGFR1 and Klotho β (KLB) with fazpilodemab demonstrated preliminary signals in liver histology and steatosis reduction alongside a favorable safety profile in patients with MASH. Although early trial termination precludes definitive efficacy conclusions, these findings support FGFR1 agonism as a viable strategy for future drug development in metabolic liver disease.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of turmeric and curcumin formulations on glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory markers in people with prediabetes: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Prediabetes is a growing global health concern associated with higher risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Curcumin has been studied for glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory effects, but comparative data across formulations remain limited. This network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluated turmeric and curcumin formulations in adults with prediabetes.
