Seven databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing turmeric/curcumin formulations with placebo. Primary outcomes included glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory markers. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. NMAs with surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) were performed. Twenty-four RCTs (25 publications, 1,952 participants; mean baseline fasting blood sugar (FBS): 110.3mg/dL) evaluating eight curcumin-based formulations were included. Turmeric extract combined with other compounds (EC) and turmeric extract (E) were associated with significant reductions in FBS with WMD -10.73 (95%CI: -14.22, -7.25;SUCRA 92.2%), and -10.57 (95%CI: -14.35, -6.79;91.5%;SUCRA 91.5%), respectively. E was associated with a significant reduction in HbA1c, while EC was associated with lower HOMA-IR with MWD -0.73 (95%CI: -1.41, -0.05; SUCRA 79.8%). Whole turmeric with other compounds (WC) was associated with a significant reduction in LDL-C (WMD: -37.19, 95%CI: -56.97, -17.42; SUCRA: 97.3%). E was associated with a lower risk of incident type 2 diabetes (RR= 0.05; 95%CI:0.00,0.78), although this estimate was based on low-certainty of evidence. No significant effects were observed for inflammatory markers. Overall certainty of evidence was low due to heterogeneity and short trial durations, and variability among combination formulations. In prediabetes, formulation-specific metabolic effects were observed. However, given the low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger, longer-term trials before clinical recommendation can be made.

articles.title: Genome-wide identification of the TIFY gene family in Sorghum bicolor and functional characterization of SbTIFY9 in salt stress tolerance.
articles.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
articles.abstract: The TIFY gene family is a plant-specific group of transcriptional regulators characterized by a conserved TIFY domain (TIF[F/Y]XG), participating in plant development, phytohormone signaling and abiotic stress responses. In this study, 21 SbTIFY genes were genome-widely identified in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L.). According to phylogeny and protein structures, SbTIFY proteins were grouped into JAZ and ZML subfamilies, and the JAZ subfamily was further divided into five clades. These proteins contain 101-429 amino acids and are unevenly distributed across six chromosomes. Genes from the same subgroup possess similar exon-intron structures and conserved motifs. Promoter analysis uncovered abundant cis-elements associated with hormone signaling, stress responses and developmental processes. Synteny analysis detected seven orthologous pairs between sorghum and Arabidopsis, and 25 pairs between sorghum and rice (Oryza sativa). Expression profiling revealed that multiple SbTIFY members exhibited differential expression across developmental organs and under stresses including anthracnose infection, cold, heat, flooding, and salt. SbTIFY9 displayed strong induction under multiple stresses: its transcript level increased approximately 10-fold at 12h and approximately 31-fold at 24h of salt treatment, implying its vital function in salt response. Subcellular localization confirmed SbTIFY9 resides mainly in the nucleus. Heterologous overexpression of SbTIFY9 in Arabidopsis improved true leaf expansion, fresh weight at germination, and root growth and biomass at seedling stage under 125 and 150mM NaCl, demonstrating its positive role in salt tolerance. This work provides insights into the evolution and stress functions of sorghum TIFY family.

articles.title: Optimized Deep Knowledge Distillation Framework for Large-Scale Virus-Host Protein Interaction Prediction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a rapidly evolving viral landscape, understanding virus-host protein interactions (VHPIs) is essential to elucidate viral infection mechanisms and support the development of effective therapeutic strategies. Accurate computational Prediction of VHPIs remains challenging because of the complexity and high dimensionality of protein sequence and functional representations.

METHODS: We propose a Knowledge Distillation framework for pairwise VHPI prediction that integrates three teacher networks with a hybrid student architecture. Protein characteristics were represented using Conjoint Triad (CT), Dipeptide Composition (DC), Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE), Pseudo-Amino Acid Composition (PseAAC), amino acid encoding, and Gene Ontology (GO) features. We used tuned Monte Carlo ISUD for feature selection and compared it with five alternative approaches: PCA, MCFS, NMF, FA, and Optuna. We used an autoencoder to compress the one-hot encoded GO features. We evaluated on 25 randomly balanced datasets and one additional balanced dataset generated using NearMiss. Five-fold cross-validation was performed at the interaction-pair level using an 80:20 training-to-test ratio in each fold. The final configuration consisted of CT features, NearMiss-based data balancing, tuned MC-ISUD feature selection, and the Knowledge Distillation teacher-student framework.

RESULTS: The proposed framework achieved 92.91% accuracy and 96.16% AUC-ROC on the evaluated virus-host protein interaction datasets. Comparative experiments demonstrated that the proposed approach outperformed the existing methods considered in this study. These results are specific to the evaluated datasets and pairwise cross-validation design and should not be interpreted as evidence of generalization to completely unseen viral or host proteins.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate that combining CT-based representation, NearMiss-based data balancing, tuned ISUD feature selection, and Knowledge Distillation provides a computational framework for pairwise VHPI prediction. The predictions should be regarded as computational hypotheses requiring independent experimental validation.

articles.title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1st, 2005, to August 6th, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency.

CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.

articles.title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2- positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with JAK2V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin.

METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IR) per 100 person-years (PY) and incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing aspirin use versus no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n=1,760 with aspirin, n=367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in JAK2V617F-positive MPN patients receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 PY (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59 - 4.65; I2=93%) with pooled IRR receiving aspirin versus no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI 0.40 - 0.86, I2=16%). The pooled IR of major and non-major bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI 1.06 - 3.65; I2=90%) per 100 PY with pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI 1.15 - 5.11; I2=43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence the better define the role of aspirin in JAK2V617F-positive MPNs.

articles.title: "Less like a Harvard student": A qualitative study exploring food insecurity among graduate students in health sciences.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While considerable research has focused on undergraduate students, food insecurity among graduate students remains a comparatively understudied yet critical issue.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to investigate the challenges food insecurity creates for graduate students, the perceived influence of food insecurity on their academic, social, physical, and psychosocial well-being, and the coping mechanisms they employ within their unique institutional and local context.

DESIGN: This is a qualitative study, where semi-structured interviews were conducted.

PARTICIPANTS/SETTING: A total of 15 graduate students in the health sciences (4 Master's, 11 PhD) at Harvard University participated in the study in Spring 2024.

ANALYSIS PERFORMED: Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and checked for accuracy. Narrative data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis and themes were generated through discussion. Food insecurity was assessed using the Six-item Short Form Food Security Survey Module. Descriptive statistics were used to describe the sociodemographic characteristics of the students.

RESULTS: Several themes were identified from graduate students' narratives demonstrating 1) the economic landscape of graduate student food insecurity; 2) perceived influence of food insecurity on food acquisition strategies; 3) the perceived influence of food insecurity on physical health; 4) the perceived influence of food insecurity on psychosocial health; and 5) student strategies and support pathways in navigating food insecurity, including individual coping strategies, community support, and government assistance through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. Most students did not discuss their food situation with faculty or advisors, partially due to embarrassment.

CONCLUSIONS: Graduate students described how food insecurity contributed to challenges in food acquisition, poorer physical and mental health and well-being, limited social interactions, and difficulties in academic and research activities. Several students adopted individual coping strategies and sought support from the community as well as government assistance; however, more well-rounded efforts are needed to ensure graduate student well-being and success.

articles.title: A Prospective Observational Real-World Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy with Glycopyrrolate/Formoterol Fumarate/Budesonide in Patients with Uncontrolled Asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Individuals with asthma remain inadequately controlled despite treatment with inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting β2-agonist (ICS/LABA) therapy. Single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) combining ICS, LABA, and long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) offers a practical treatment escalation option. This study aims to assess the real-world effectiveness, safety, and adherence of SITT with budesonide/glycopyrrolate/formoterol fumarate in adults with uncontrolled asthma.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicentric, prospective, observational study was conducted across five centers in India. Adults with uncontrolled asthma on stable ICS/LABA therapy who were prescribed SITT as part of routine care were followed for 12 weeks. Changes in lung function, asthma control (ACT), and quality of life (Mini-AQLQ) were assessed. Medication adherence, adverse events, and asthma exacerbations were recorded.

RESULTS: Of 258 enrolled patients, 231 were included in the final analysis. Spirometry measurements showed notable improvements before and after bronchodilator use (all p < 0.001). These included higher MMEF values, suggesting improved small-airway function. Mean ACT scores improved from 14.29 at baseline to 18.49 at follow-up. Mini-AQLQ scores also improved over 12 weeks, indicating better patient-reported quality of life. Medication adherence was high, and no asthma exacerbations, adverse events, or serious adverse events were reported during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: In routine practice, SITT BGF was associated with short-term improvements in lung function, asthma control, and QoL in adults with uncontrolled asthma. The mean ACT improved to partially controlled range at 12 weeks. Results suggest short-term effectiveness and tolerability, but longer-term and comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Baseline MRI markers and clinical outcomes during anti-amyloid β therapy: A real-world study in a Japanese dementia center.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Predictors of decline and of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during anti-amyloid β therapy in routine care are undefined.

OBJECTIVE: To identify baseline predictors of cognitive, functional, and safety outcomes.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive patients initiating anti-amyloid β therapy at a Tokyo dementia center, 2024 to 2026 (lecanemab, 89; donanemab, 72).

EXPOSURES: Lecanemab or donanemab.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Change in MMSE and CDR-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB); baseline medial temporal atrophy (VSRAD Z score), amyloid PET burden, and microbleeds; ARIA.

RESULTS: With lecanemab, MMSE and CDR-SB declined significantly at every assessment (CDR-SB +0.79, +1.10, +1.60 at 6, 12, 18 months); memory and orientation declined while language was preserved. Greater baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with greater 12-month CDR-SB worsening (r = 0.39; P = .01; n = 40); patients in the most severe standard category (Z ≥ 3) worsened by 2.62 versus 0.64 points (adjusted β = +2.18; P < .001). Atrophy was associated with older age (r = 0.19; P = .03) and with baseline memory-related measures - ADAS-Cog score (r = 0.32; P < .001) and the MMSE subdomains of delayed recall (β = -0.25; P = .006) and time orientation (β = -0.30; P = .04) - but not MMSE total score. Amyloid PET burden showed no significant association at most time points. All ARIA events were asymptomatic; ARIA-H occurred in 6 of 25 with microbleeds versus 3 of 136 without (odds ratio, 14.0; P < .001). Donanemab follow-up was 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with functional decline and microbleeds with ARIA-H. Pretreatment MRI may provide prognostic and safety information during anti-amyloid β therapy.

articles.title: Clinical significance of elevated body temperature without infection following removal of VA-ECMO.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported elevated body temperature following the removal of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). However, the clinical implications of elevated body temperature after the removal of VA-ECMO remain unknown.

OBJECTIVES: To characterize elevated body temperature after VA-ECMO removal in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS).

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 163 CS patients undergoing VA-ECMO removal. All patients did not exhibit any evidence of infection. Blood temperature was continuously monitored using a Swan-Ganz catheter. Elevated body temperature was defined as a maximum body temperature ≥38.0 °C within 24 h after VA-ECMO removal. All-cause mortality was compared between patients with and without elevated body temperature.

RESULTS: Elevated body temperature was observed in 58.9% (96/163) of study subjects. Patients with elevated body temperature had higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (11.1 ± 8.6 vs. 8.5 ± 6.1 mg/dL, p = 0.027), accompanied by reductions in systolic blood pressure and systemic vascular resistance, and increased lactate levels. CRP levels independently predicted elevated body temperature (OR=1.050, 95%CI=1.003-1.100, p = 0.037). All-cause mortality did not differ between the two groups (30.2%vs. 29.9%, log-rank p = 0.983). However, among patients with elevated body temperature, an increase in body temperature, especially ≥1.1 °C, was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR=1.968, 95%CI=1.096-3.535, p = 0.023).

CONCLUSIONS: In CS patients requiring VA-ECMO, body temperature elevated in 58.9% patients after the removal of VA-ECMO. In those with elevated body temperature, a greater rise in body temperature was associated with higher mortality, suggesting body temperature as a potential signature to stratify risks of mortality in CS patients without any infectious signs.

articles.title: Beyond CT-defined low muscle mass in cirrhosis: toward a more accessible diagnostic approach.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: Beyond the pleura: National trends in mesothelioma mortality by anatomical site in Spain, 1999-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mesothelioma mortality continues to reflect asbestos exposure because of its long latency. While previous Spanish studies focused primarily on pleural disease, this study assessed mesothelioma mortality across the ICD-10 C45 category in Spain from 1999 to 2024.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A population-based time-trend study was conducted using mortality data (ICD-10 C45) from the Spanish National Statistics Institute. Age-standardised mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population. Temporal trends and sex-specific parallelism were evaluated using Joinpoint regression.

RESULTS: Among 9733 recorded mesothelioma deaths (7311 men, 2422 women), ASMRs were consistently higher in men, although temporal trends were parallel by sex. Overall mortality increased until 2016 (annual percentage change [APC] 2.3%, 95% CI 1.5-3.0) and subsequently declined non-significantly, yielding an average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 1.0% (95% CI 0.2-1.7) for 1999-2024. Pleural mortality increased until 2011 before declining non-significantly, whereas recorded peritoneal mortality increased throughout the study period (AAPC 2.0%, 95% CI 0.7-3.2). Deaths coded as unspecified site (C45.9) showed the largest increase in ASMR (AAPC 2.1%, 95% CI 1.1-3.1) and accounted for 43.5% of male and 31.8% of female mesothelioma deaths in 2024.

CONCLUSIONS: Absolute mesothelioma deaths increased in Spain while age-standardised rates attenuated after 2016. The continued increase in recorded peritoneal mortality and the substantial contribution of unspecified-site deaths indicate that surveillance should not rely solely on pleural mesothelioma, highlighting the need for comprehensive monitoring of the complete ICD-10 C45 category and improved anatomical classification.

articles.title: Xanthoangelol-enriched Angelica keiskei Koidzumi targets foamy Kupffer cells to ameliorate MASLD by activating the TFEB-mediated CLEAR network.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progression is driven by lipid overload and inflammatory activation of Kupffer cells (KCs). Xanthoangelol (XAG), a major chalcone in Angelica keiskei Koidzumi, has anti-inflammatory activity, but its effects on KC immunometabolic dysfunction remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether XAG-enriched A. keiskei extract ameliorates MASLD by targeting foamy KC dysfunction.

METHODS: MASLD was induced in male C57BL/6 N mice by fast-food diet feeding for 15 weeks, followed by daily oral administration of XAG-enriched A. keiskei extract for a further 9 weeks. Liver injury, steatosis, collagen deposition, inflammatory signaling, and KC abundance were evaluated. Primary hepatocytes, primary KCs, immortalized KCs, and reporter macrophages were used to define cell-specific responses, and KC-to-hepatocyte crosstalk was assessed by conditioned-medium transfer. MASH-like KC dysfunction was modeled using palmitic acid, oleic acid, LPS, glucose, fructose, and TGF-β with or without XAG. RNA sequencing, pathway enrichment, immunoblotting, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence were used to assess inflammatory, lipid-handling, autophagy-lysosome, and TFEB-CLEAR pathways.

RESULTS: XAG-enriched A. keiskei extract reduced FFD-induced liver injury, steatosis, collagen deposition, metabolic dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, and KC accumulation. Primary hepatocytes showed limited responses in the lipid-related endpoints examined, whereas KCs exhibited pronounced inflammatory and immunometabolic responses to XAG. In MASH-stimulated KCs, XAG suppressed NF-κB/MAPK-associated inflammatory activation, reduced lipid accumulation, attenuated NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, and activated autophagy-lysosome and lipid-clearance programs. Mechanistically, XAG promoted TFEB nuclear localization and increased CLEAR network gene expression.

CONCLUSION: XAG-enriched A. keiskei extract ameliorates experimental MASLD by suppressing foamy KC inflammatory activation and enhancing TFEB-CLEAR-associated lysosomal regulation, supporting XAG as a KC-directed immunomodulatory candidate.

articles.title: Complement C3a plays a role in diabetic cardiomyopathy mainly via C3aR-ERK-PANoptosis pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is one of the leading causes of death in diabetic patients. However, the pathogenesis of DCM remains incompletely understood, and effective targeted therapies are lacking. This study aims to investigate the role of complement C3a in the development of DCM, providing a novel theoretical foundation for its precise prevention and treatment.

METHODS: Eight-week-old male C57BL/6 J mice were injected with streptozotocin (STZ) to induce a diabetes model for 26 weeks. The two intervention groups were injected with C3a receptor antagonist (SB290157, 30 mg/kg/d) and novel C3 cleavage inhibitor (CP40-KK, 2 mg/kg/d) by intraperitoneal injection for 8 weeks. Cardiac function/histopathological changes were determined by echocardiogram examination, and Millar catheter system. Human cardiomyocytes (AC16) were employed in vitro.

RESULTS: C3a was significantly upregulated in the plasma of the STZ-induced DCM model, and PANoptosis plays a critical role in cardiac tissue and cardiomyocytes. The C3a receptor antagonist (SB290157) could significantly improve the cardiac function of diabetic mice, reduce myocardial hypertrophy, and inhibit the activation level of PANoptosis pathway in cardiac tissue. Furthermore, inhibiting the C3aR/ERK pathway could regulate cardiomyocyte PANoptosis by pyroptosis (NLRP3-dependent), apoptosis (caspase-3-dependent), and necroptosis (RIP-dependent) in the DCM model and C3a-treated cardiomyocytes. The novel complement C3 inhibitor CP40-KK exerts comparable therapeutic efficacy to SB290157 in treating DCM at a lower drug dosage.

CONCLUSION: We demonstrate the crucial role of the C3a/C3aR signaling axis, and CP40-KK treatment was protective in the STZ-induced DCM model. These findings provide valuable evidence supporting potential complement-based therapies targeting the C3a/C3aR/ERK/PANoptosis pathway in DCM treatment.

articles.title: Associations between surrounding greenness, tree cover and all-cause mortality in Jordan: a 14-year nationwide panel study.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between greenness and mortality remains largely unexamined in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR). In this study, we estimated associations between long-term district-level greenness and all-cause mortality among Jordanian adults according to sex, age group, and climatic zone.

METHODS: We conducted a 14-year nationwide longitudinal panel study, using district-year as the unit of analysis. Greenness was characterized using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and tree cover percentage. Associations between each greenness metric and all-cause mortality were estimated using a correlated random-effects Poisson model, with covariate adjustment sets identified through a causal inference framework. Analyses were stratified by sex, age group, and climatic zone.

RESULTS: No overall association was observed for either NDVI (IRR 0.959, 95% CI 0.878-1.046 per 0.1-unit increase) or tree cover (IRR 0.977, 95% CI 0.893-1.069 per 1-percentage-point increase). However, in semi-arid districts, higher NDVI was inversely associated with all-cause mortality, particularly among working-age males, with associations observed from ages 20-29 (IRR 0.744, 95% CI 0.556-0.997) through 50-59 years (IRR 0.746, 95% CI 0.613-0.906). Associations were null across all strata in arid districts. Tree cover showed a comparable but more modest pattern.

CONCLUSIONS: Although overall associations were null, inverse associations were observed in semi-arid districts, particularly among working-age males. Further studies using individual-level data are needed to confirm these findings and clarify potential underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Effect modification of maternal concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances on vaccine effectiveness in children up to 6 years of age: The Japan Environment and Children's Study.
authors: Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS) Group
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests that per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure may attenuate antibody responses to vaccination. However, vaccine effectiveness as an outcome has not been investigated. This study assessed whether maternal PFAS concentrations during pregnancy modified childhood vaccine effectiveness. We analyzed mother-child pairs from the Japan Environment and Children's Study. Children's vaccination status for varicella, mumps, and influenza was collected via self-reported questionnaires at 2 years of age. Subsequent infection incidence was similarly assessed until 6 years for varicella and mumps, and 3 years for influenza. Maternal plasma samples collected during pregnancy provided PFAS measurements. Logistic regression models, incorporating interaction terms between vaccination status and PFAS concentrations, examined effect modification on both additive (relative excess odds due to interaction) and multiplicative (ratio of odds ratios) scales. Vaccinations were associated with reduced infection risk across PFAS exposure levels for all three diseases. Effect modification assessments revealed that perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) significantly reduced varicella and mumps vaccine effectiveness on the additive scale. For mumps, the odds ratio for infection among unvaccinated versus vaccinated children (higher values indicate greater vaccine effectiveness) was higher in the lowest PFNA tertile than in the highest, with a relative excess odds due to interaction of 0.94 (95% confidence interval: 0.33-1.54, P = 0.0025). Multiplicative scale effect modifications were not statistically significant. Vaccinations reduced infections in children across all maternal PFAS exposure levels. Evidence of effect modification was limited, isolated, and inconsistent. These analyses are exploratory, and confirmation is warranted.

articles.title: Evaluation of the predictive performance of CD64 and CD69 markers in the early diagnosis of bloodstream infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bloodstream infection (BSI) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive performance of CD64 and CD69, together with other cell surface markers, for early diagnosis of BSI and to compare them with conventional inflammatory markers.

METHODS: Expression levels of neutrophil and monocyte CD11b, CD14, CD64, and CD69 were measured by flow cytometry. Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, sTREM-1, calprotectin, and hematological ratios were also analyzed. Diagnostic performance was assessed using ROC analysis, and logistic regression, including Firth penalization, was performed to identify independent predictors of BSI.

RESULTS: Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, sTREM-1, calprotectin, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, monocyte-to-HDL ratio, nCD11b, mCD11b, nCD14, mCD14, nCD64, mCD64, nCD69, and mCD69 differed significantly between the culture-confirmed BSI group (n = 130) and the culture-negative control group (n = 50) (p < 0.05). Among cell surface markers, mCD69 demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.948), followed by nCD14 (AUC = 0.897) and nCD64 (AUC = 0.884). The gram-negative bacteremia group exhibited the highest median values of procalcitonin, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, sTREM-1, calprotectin, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and nCD14, and the lowest median lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio compared with the gram‑positive bacteremia and fungemia groups. Significant positive correlations were observed between cell surface markers and conventional inflammatory markers (p < 0.05). In logistic regression analysis, mCD69 and procalcitonin were statistically associated with BSI (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Cell surface markers, particularly mCD69, demonstrated good discriminatory performance between BSI and control groups. Their combined use with conventional markers may provide useful complementary information; however, future validation studies including alternative comparator groups are required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: The role of nanomedicine in infectious diseases of the central nervous system: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases in the central nervous system (CNS) are a global health problem, causing significant morbidity and mortality. One of the main challenges in treating CNS infections is the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which limits drug delivery to the brain. During infections, brain-resident immune cells, release inflammatory mediators, which further contribute to neuroinflammation and damage. Nanomedicine offers an alternative for CNS treatment that has been explored in several types of infections. Across preclinical studies, nanomedicine approaches have demonstrated substantial improvements in CNS delivery and therapeutic outcomes, including reductions in brain pathogen burden of up to 3 log10 colony-forming units, increases in brain drug concentrations of 3-4-fold, and survival improvements of up to 100% in selected infection models. However, the literature remains fragmented across pathogens, nanomaterial platforms, and experimental models, with few direct comparisons and limited clinical validation. This review provides a comprehensive, up-to-date synthesis of the current evidence, integrating emerging nanomedicine strategies across major CNS infections while highlighting common therapeutic approaches, clinical applications, limitations, and key gaps that must be addressed to advance these technologies toward clinical translation. It also highlights advances and techniques in nanomedicine for treating brain infections, discusses clinical applications, and promotes innovation and future directions.

articles.title: Poria cocos triterpenes alleviate diabetes mellitus by regulating the gut microbiota-barrier-inflammation axis and inhibiting the TLR4/nF-κB/NLRP3 pathway.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by progression associated with dysregulation of gut immunity and impairment of the intestinal barrier. Poria cocos triterpenes (PCT) exhibit hypoglycaemic effects; however, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain inadequately elucidated. We aimed to investigate the anti-diabetic properties of PCT. The findings revealed the identification of 60 PCT components, with 35 being absorbed into the serum of diabetic rats. PCT administration resulted in a significant reduction in blood glucose and lipid levels, restoration of gut microbiota homeostasis, and enhancement of intestinal barrier integrity through the upregulation of ZO-1 and occludin. PCT inhibited the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway and modulated metabolites, such as those involved in tryptophan metabolism, which were correlated with changes in the microbiota. These results suggest that PCT mitigates DM via the gut microbiota-barrier-inflammation axis, underscoring its potential for diabetes management and the integration of medicinal fungi into interventions for metabolic diseases.

articles.title: Longitudinal BCR repertoire dynamics reveal the evolution of broadly binding antibodies following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection: a single-donor case study.
articles.abstract: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B-cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodeling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

articles.title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI.

METHODS: This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%; p = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986; p = 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250; p = 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894; p = 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874).

CONCLUSION: Foot microcirculation differed significantly between patients with Cla and CLTI on CTP. Hb, TTP, and BF were independent predictors for CLTI. All models demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with model C yielding the highest AUC.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov Identifier:NCT05575778.

articles.title: Venous interventions reduce the risk of lymphedema in chronic venous insufficiency.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) significantly increases the risk of developing secondary lymphedema and related infections. This study tested the hypothesis that lower-extremity venous procedures can reduce the 5-year incidence of lymphedema in adults with CVI.

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults (⩾ 18 years) diagnosed with CVI between Jan 1, 2005, and Jan 1, 2020, were identified and followed for at least 5 years. Patients were stratified into those undergoing venous procedures, including saphenous vein ligation, phlebectomy, sclerotherapy, and endovenous ablation, and matched controls managed without intervention. Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 on demographics, comorbidities, and infection-related variables. The primary outcome was new-onset lymphedema, assessed using Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: After matching, 17,703 patients were included in each cohort. At 5 years, new-onset lymphedema occurred in 5.1% of controls versus 4.0% of patients who underwent venous procedures (hazard ratio [HR] 1.26, 95% CI 1.14-1.40). Phlebectomy showed the strongest association with risk reduction (4.0% vs 1.5%; HR 2.60, 95% CI 1.33-5.06), followed by varicose vein sclerotherapy (5.3% vs 3.6%; HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.02-2.16).

CONCLUSIONS: Venous interventions may reduce the risk of developing lymphedema in patients with chronic venous insufficiency.

articles.title: Endotoxin removal in cardiac bypass surgery in 2026: where do we stand, and where are we going?
articles.abstract: The significance of endotoxemia during cardiopulmonary bypass remains incompletely understood. This review summarizes decades of research and highlights that clinically relevant endotoxemia affects only a subset of patients, making indiscriminate endotoxin-targeted therapies unlikely to provide meaningful benefit. Future research should therefore focus on identifying high-risk phenotypes, refining endotoxin assessment, and developing personalized therapeutics. Key priorities include standardization of endotoxin measurement, source tracking, gut barrier dysfunction, bypass-related factors, immunological profiling, EndoCAb-guided risk stratification, novel pharmacological approaches, and extracorporeal endotoxin removal. Regarding patient selection for therapeutic intervention, two high-risk subgroups warrant consideration. First, patients with EAA values >0.40 may be considered biologically exposed, while those with EAA values >0.60 represent a subgroup with endotoxin activity approaching levels seen in severe systemic inflammation or sepsis. Importantly, endotoxin activity must always be interpreted in relation to the host's neutralizing capacity. Second, reduced EndoCAb levels independently predict adverse outcomes after cardiac surgery, including prolonged mechanical ventilation, postoperative complications, and extended hospitalization. These patients may be particularly vulnerable to even moderate endotoxin exposure due to impaired endogenous neutralization. Precision medicine strategies targeting these identifiable subgroups represent the most promising path forward.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension associated with lung disease - an expert review from the Cologne Conference.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic lung disease (PH_lung) is a frequent complication of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, and other parenchymal lung disorders, and is associated with impaired exercise capacity, reduced quality of life and poor survival. Despite increasing recognition of its clinical importance, major challenges remain regarding early diagnosis, hemodynamic classification, and optimal treatment. Following the 7th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension, a panel of experts reviewed from Germany and International collaborators summarized recent evidence and discussed unresolved issues relevant to everyday clinical practice. This review summarizes current concepts of the diagnosis and management of PH_lung, with particular emphasis on multimodal screening strategies integrating pulmonary function testing, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and thoracic imaging to improve patient selection for right heart catheterization. We discuss practical aspects of hemodynamic assessment, overlapping phenotypes, including connective tissue disease, sarcoidosis, and the emerging pulmonary vascular "lung phenotype", and current evidence supporting targeted therapies with emphasis on patients' pathways in real-world settings. While inhaled treprostinil has become the first approved treatment for pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease in several countries, no pulmonary hypertension-specific therapy is currently recommended routinely for COPD-associated PH, highlighting the need for careful patient phenotyping and individualized management in expert centres. The review further addresses indications for lung transplantation and outlines future research priorities. Earlier recognition, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continued translational and clinical research are essential to improve outcomes in this highly vulnerable patient population.

articles.title: Embodied Inter-Hand Sensory Experiences ("Prana" Perception): A Randomized Controlled Trial of Affective, Environmental, and Physiological Correlates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemplative traditions describe inter-hand sensations as "prana," yet these remain underexplored experimentally. This study examined whether a structured embodied attention practice elicits higher reproducible inter-hand sensory experiences and investigated their associations with affective state, environmental context, and physiological parameters in healthy individuals.

METHODS: In this participant-blinded randomized controlled trial, 107 healthy young adults (mean age 20.7 ± 1.3 years) were allocated to either an embodied attention intervention derived from pranic healing practices or a structurally matched sham condition across four standardized sessions. Intensity and spatial extent of perceived inter-hand sensations, mood introspection, nature connectedness, and physiological parameters were measured. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including linear mixed-effects models, correlation and regression analyses, and qualitative content analysis of participant-reported experiences.

RESULTS: Intervention group reported significantly higher inter-hand sensory intensity across sessions (p ≤ 0.05) and greater spatial extent in three sessions (p ≤ 0.05). Sensory measures showed large treatment effects (ηp² = .145-.155) and good internal consistency (α = .74-.81). Both groups indicating increased calmness. A small but significant decrease in forehead temperature was observed post-intervention (p ≤ 0.001). Hierarchical regression showed positive affect (β = 0.37, p = 0.005) and nature connectedness (β = 0.26, p = 0.043) predicted perceived sensory intensity, explaining 21% variance. Qualitative findings revealed recurring sensations like attraction, pressure, and vibration, more frequent in the intervention group.

CONCLUSIONS: Focused embodied attention practice in pranic healing consistently enhanced inter-hand sensory intensity and spatial extent, accompanied by mild forehead temperature reduction. Mood state and nature connectedness influenced these experiences, suggesting interactions among attentional, interoceptive, affective, and psychophysiological processes.

articles.title: Healthcare Utilization in Patients With Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps - Analysis of the Reg-ent Clinical Data Registry.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPatients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) who fail medical management are often offered endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Dupilumab is also used to treat patients with inadequately controlled CRSwNP.ObjectiveThis retrospective cohort study uses a national registry to examine the patterns in healthcare utilization in patients with CRSwNP.MethodsA review of the AAO-HNSF Reg-entSM data registry of CRSwNP patients who underwent ESS or received dupilumab from 2019 to 2025 was performed. The primary outcome of oral antibiotic and corticosteroid free-probability was summarized by Kaplan-Meier estimates and compared between dupilumab treatment and surgery by piecewise Cox proportional hazards model with follow-up time split at 6 months while adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, race, history of asthma, and allergic rhinitis. Secondary outcomes include polyp recurrence/persistence and repeat imaging.Results12,944 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated the hazard ratio changing over time indicating lower relative hazard of post-intervention antibiotics/corticosteroid use early on among patients who were treated with dupilumab, but the relative hazard of the group increased over time. Antibiotic/corticosteroid use was lower among dupilumab treated patients compared to ESS patients (HR = 0.873; aHR = 0.740; p < 0.0001) in the first 6 months, but they demonstrated higher antibiotic/corticosteroid use thereafter (HR = 1.60, aHR = 1.279; p < 0.0012). There was an increased risk of nasal polyp recurrence/persistence in the dupilumab group during both time periods (aHR = 1.189 & 2.040 before and after 6 months, p < 0.0005 & 0.0001). During the first 6 months, the hazard of repeat imaging was higher among dupilumab patients compared to ESS patients (aHR = 2.098; p < 0.0001). After 6 months, the hazard among dupilumab patients was lower than the ESS patients (aHR = 0.409, p < 0.0001).ConclusionCRSwNP patients treated with dupilumab and ESS demonstrated variable healthcare utilization over time, highlighting the importance of patient selection and shared decision making when considering initiation of dupilumab therapy for CRSwNP.

articles.title: From genotype to phenotype: reverse phenotyping of a novel INSR variant in a large family with hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.
articles.abstract: The insulin receptor gene (INSR) encodes a ligand-activated tyrosine kinase that plays a central role in glucose homeostasis. Pathogenic variants in INSR are associated with a spectrum of insulin resistance syndromes. Here we report a novel INSR variant in a large multigenerational family. A 53-year-old woman presented to the endocrinology clinic with recurrent hypoglycemic episodes. Exome sequencing was performed for the index case, and variant segregation analysis was conducted in family members by Sanger sequencing. Genetic testing revealed a likely pathogenic variant in exon 19 of the INSR gene, NM_000208.4:c.3473G > C,p.(Arg1158Pro). Segregation analysis identified eight heterozygous carriers among thirteen tested family members. Reverse phenotyping revealed recurrent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Affected individuals demonstrated normal body mass index, low adiposity, and preserved fat-free mass, distinguishing this phenotype from classical insulin-resistance syndromes. Female carriers frequently exhibited hyperandrogenic features including hirsutism, menstrual irregularities, and acanthosis nigricans. These findings expand the clinical spectrum of INSR-related disorders and highlight the importance of considering INSR variants in patients with familial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, particularly when clinical features mimic insulinoma.

articles.title: Switching from Intravenous to Subcutaneous Infliximab in Children with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Subcutaneous infliximab (IFX-SC; CT-P13 SC/infliximab-dyyb/Remsima-SC/Zymfentra) is an approved maintenance option after intravenous (IV) induction in adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but it is not approved for patients < 18 years, and the pediatric evidence remains dispersed across small, largely observational cohorts. This review synthesizes the published pediatric experience of transitioning from IV to SC infliximab, examining maintenance of remission, drug concentrations, safety, and acceptability, and situates it within the adult evidence base and the distinctly pediatric concerns of access and dosing.

RECENT FINDINGS: A systematic search (PROSPERO: CRD420261465026) identified six independent, non-overlapping pediatric switch cohorts (n = 173). Random-effects proportional meta-analysis yielded pooled treatment persistence of 92% (95%CI 84-98), maintained clinical remission of 93% (95%CI 84-99), and any-cause discontinuation of 8% (95%CI 2-16), most often for injection-site intolerance, disease relapse, or paradoxical dermatitis. New anti-drug antibody formation was rare among the 129 children in cohorts measuring immunogenicity (four children, none sustained) while previously positive antibodies frequently resolved after switching. Steady-state SC concentrations ran roughly 2-fold above prior IV troughs, an expected step-up reflecting sustained subcutaneous exposure. Patient and caregiver satisfaction was high due to decreased school absence and travel, and cost analyses signaled net savings from avoided infusion-center use. The principal barrier was administrative: age-based denial. In appropriately selected children, transition to IFX-SC sustains remission with predictable pharmacokinetics, a reassuring immunogenicity profile, and excellent tolerability, mirroring the adult experience. These observations constitute a well-supported real-world signal and warrant prospective validation and pursuit of pediatric labeling.

articles.title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

articles.title: Circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances: a conceptual perspective with implications for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a genetic disorder characterized by cyst formation, kidney enlargement, and extrarenal complications. While the role of genetic mutations in PKD1, PKD2, and other minor genes is well established, the influence of circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances on disease progression remains underexplored. The circadian timing system, coordinated by the central clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and synchronized with peripheral clocks in the kidneys, regulates key physiological processes, including glomerular filtration rate (GFR), sodium handling, blood pressure, and hormone secretion. In ADPKD, circadian disruption driven by intrinsic molecular alterations and exacerbated by sleep disorders contributes to sympathetic nervous system activation, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) dysregulation, and elevated vasopressin levels, all of which accelerate cyst growth and hypertension. Mechanistic links also involve the activation of the mTOR pathway, impaired fatty acid oxidation, and altered gut microbiota composition. These disturbances impair kidney function and increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Chronotherapy and targeted sleep hygiene interventions offer promising adjunctive strategies for mitigating circadian misalignment in ADPKD. Timed administration of antihypertensives, diuretics, and disease-modifying agents, such as tolvaptan, along with melatonin supplementation, structured light exposure, and optimized physical activity patterns, may enhance therapeutic efficacy and improve quality of life (QoL). Future research should prioritize longitudinal and interventional studies incorporating circadian biomarkers to evaluate the impact of aligning therapeutic interventions with biological rhythms on kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in ADPKD.

articles.title: Long-term changes in kidney function and urinary protein following inpatient multidisciplinary care in patients with chronic kidney disease: a 5-year follow-up study.
Safety and efficacy of prednisolone, mizoribine and lisinopril combination therapy for severe childhood IgA nephropathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi), such as lisinopril, have long been used for childhood IgA nephropathy (cIgAN). A two-year regimen including prednisolone, mizoribine, warfarin, and dipyridamole was previously shown to be superior to prednisolone and mizoribine alone in achieving proteinuria remission. Because warfarin nephropathy has been reported and the cumulative prednisolone dose used in earlier regimens was substantial, we evaluated a new two-year regimen consisting of prednisolone, mizoribine, and lisinopril.

METHODS: Among 567 biopsy‑proven cIgAN cases treated between 1976 and 2022, 93 patients met the criteria for severe cIgAN. Of these, 77 received the previous regimen and 16 received the new regimen. Severe cIgAN was defined as diffuse mesangial proliferation and/or persistent heavy proteinuria (> 1 g/gCr). To adjust for baseline differences in proteinuria, eGFR, and C‑lesions, 1:1 propensity score matching was performed, yielding 15 matched pairs.

RESULTS: Baseline clinicopathological characteristics did not differ significantly between groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the new regimen was associated with a higher proteinuria remission rate during follow-up (log-rank p = 0.01) and a shorter time to remission (median 1.0 vs. 4.0 years, p = 0.03). Hematuria remission tended to be higher with the new regimen (80.0% vs. 46.7%). Proteinuria recurrence rates were comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: The two‑year regimen of prednisolone, mizoribine, and lisinopril was more effective in achieving earlier proteinuria remission and required a shorter duration of prednisolone exposure, with no significant difference in proteinuria recurrence compared with the previous regimen in children with severe cIgAN.

articles.title: Dahuang Fuzi decoction attenuates renal fibrosis via suppression of the NF-κB pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal fibrosis is a key pathological process in chronic kidney disease with limited treatment options. Dahuang Fuzi Decoction (DFT), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula, shows therapeutic potential, but its anti-fibrotic mechanism remains unclear.

METHODS: The anti-fibrotic effect of DFT was assessed in a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rat model via histopathological examination and renal function tests. The underlying mechanism was investigated using an integrated strategy which included serum pharmacology with drug-containing serum from treated rats, network pharmacology to screen bioactive compounds and predict targets, and in vitro validation in angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated NRK-52E cells, with a focused analysis of the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway.

RESULTS: DFT treatment ameliorated renal injury, reduced collagen deposition, and improved biochemical parameters in UUO rats. DFT-containing serum attenuated Ang II-induced fibrotic responses in cells. Bioinformatics and experimental validation identified the NF-κB pathway as a key target. DFT suppressed p65 nuclear translocation and downstream target gene expression in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated NRK-52E cells, and pharmacological activation of this pathway reversed the protective effects of DFT.

CONCLUSION: DFT alleviates renal fibrosis, at least in part by inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway, as validated in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated tubular epithelial cells, providing a pharmacological basis for its clinical application.

articles.title: The coexistence of constipation and diarrhea is associated with the development of chronic kidney disease: a 10-year cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The gut-kidney axis is a potential mechanism underlying kidney dysfunction. However, the relationship between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and bowel habit subtypes, especially the coexistence of constipation and diarrhea, remains unknown.

METHODS: We investigated the association of bowel habit subtypes including the no-constipation/diarrhea, constipation-only, diarrhea-only and coexisting constipation/diarrhea groups with new onset of CKD during a 10-year follow-up period in 14,876 Japanese adults (men/women: 9,620/5,256, mean age: 47 years) who underwent annual health examinations.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 7.0 years, 2,281 participants (men/women: 1,571/710) developed CKD. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models analysis after adjustment for age, sex and several confounders showed that hazard ratio (HR) for the development of CKD was significantly higher in the coexisting constipation/diarrhea group (HR [95% confidence interval]: 1.24 [1.06-1.46], p = 0.008), but not the constipation-only group or diarrhea-only group, than in the no-constipation/diarrhea group. Sex-stratified analyses showed that the adjusted HR in women, but not in men, was significantly higher in the constipation-only and coexisting constipation/diarrhea groups than in the no-constipation/diarrhea group, though the interaction by sex was not statistically significant (p = 0.118). In the mutually adjusted analysis using frequency of constipation/diarrhea, frequent constipation was independently associated with the development of CKD. The addition of bowel habit subtypes into traditional risk factors for CKD significantly improved the discriminatory capacity.

CONCLUSIONS: The coexistence of constipation and diarrhea is independently associated with an increased risk for the development of CKD. The bowel habit subtype provides clinically relevant information regarding future risk for CKD.

articles.title: Microsurgical clipping versus Woven EndoBridge embolization for intracranial aneurysms: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: To compare microsurgical clipping and Woven EndoBridge (WEB) embolization for the treatment of intracranial aneurysms, including ruptured and unruptured cases, with respect to angiographic occlusion, morbidity, mortality, and adverse events (AEs). This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 29, 2026, for comparative studies evaluating microsurgical clipping versus WEB embolization. Cohort studies and clinical trials were eligible regardless of aneurysm rupture status or morphology. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic, and predefined subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Five observational cohort studies comprising 798 patients (402 clipping, 396 WEB) were included. The most credible estimate, from the good-quality concurrent studies, showed higher occlusion with clipping (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.14 to 1.49, I2 0%). Larger pooled estimates (RR 1.71 for complete occlusion; RR 2.04 in the two-study wide-neck analysis) were strongly influenced by fair-quality studies that used external WEB comparators and by near-ceiling clipping occlusion combined with small WEB denominators, and are presented as exploratory. Adequate or complete occlusion also favored clipping (RR: 1.61, 95% CI: 1.24-2.11; P = 0.0004). There were no significant differences in morbidity (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.33-2.25) or overall mortality (RR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.37-1.28). Reported adverse-event frequencies appeared broadly comparable, although inconsistent reporting across studies precluded formal comparative analysis, and the profile of complications differed between techniques. Across wide-neck aneurysms and within the available short-term follow-up, microsurgical clipping was consistently associated with higher angiographic occlusion than WEB embolization, which was the more internally consistent estimate, although heterogeneity increased when all wide-neck-only studies were combined. No statistically significant difference was observed in morbidity or mortality. Because WEB occlusion may progress over time and long-term retreatment and recurrence data are limited, these short-term angiographic findings should not be interpreted as evidence of superior long-term durability. Because all included studies were observational, these comparisons are susceptible to selection bias, and treatment selection should remain individualized according to aneurysm characteristics, rupture status, and clinical context.

articles.title: Publisher Correction: Investigation of a Two-Patch Within-Host Model of Hepatitis B Viral Infection.
Global cognitive and verbal episodic memory impairment in the post-acute phase of anti-nmdar encephalitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis with narrative synthesis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a recognized long-term complication of anti-NMDAR encephalitis, but its pooled magnitude, domain specificity, and time course have not been systematically quantified.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify pooled global cognitive and verbal episodic memory impairment in convalescent anti-NMDAR encephalitis relative to healthy comparators, and to assess whether impairment magnitude changes with time since disease onset.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed observational studies assessing standardized cognitive outcomes in adults with cell-based-assay-confirmed anti-NMDAR encephalitis during the post-acute/convalescent phase. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 20 June 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for cognitive domains with at least three independent cohorts, while other domains were synthesized narratively according to SWiM principles.

RESULTS: Fourteen independent cohorts comprising 439 patients were included. Six cohorts (191 patients, 182 controls) contributed to the confirmed primary global-cognition analysis, showing substantial impairment (Hedges' g - 1.26, 95% CI - 1.49 to - 1.04; I²=0%). Verbal episodic memory was also impaired (g - 0.88, 95% CI - 1.13 to - 0.63; 5 cohorts). Recognition was impaired alongside recall in the two cohorts reporting recognition trials. Narrative synthesis identified frequent executive and working-memory impairment, impaired speeded processing, and deficits in visual episodic memory and language, whereas visuospatial findings were less consistent.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-acute anti-NMDAR encephalitis is associated with substantial global cognitive and verbal episodic memory impairment, with additional deficits across several cognitive domains. Comprehensive longitudinal neuropsychological assessment, including social cognition and psychiatric symptoms, is needed to clarify recovery trajectories and mechanisms.

articles.title: Periconceptional and early-pregnancy exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors and congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are increasingly prescribed to women of reproductive age for type 2 diabetes and cardiorenal protection, and are commonly continued through the periconceptional period until pregnancy is recognized. Human safety data on inadvertent first-trimester exposure remain scarce, creating substantial clinical uncertainty.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from inception to 15 May 2026 for observational cohort studies comparing early-pregnancy or preconception exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors with active antidiabetic comparators among women with type 2 diabetes. Adjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Three cohorts, including 669 SGLT2 inhibitor-exposed pregnancies, were eligible. In the prespecified insulin-comparator analysis, SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with major congenital malformations (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68-1.29) or cardiac malformations (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.64-1.48). The inclusion of a preconception sulfonylurea comparator cohort yielded a similar estimate for major congenital malformations (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.74-1.29). In a Korean cohort, exposure during gestational weeks 4-10 was associated with congenital heart defects (RR 2.79, 95% CI 1.16-7.06).

CONCLUSIONS: Based on the limited observational evidence available, early SGLT2 inhibitor exposure was not associated with an increased risk of overall major congenital or cardiac malformations; however, the estimates were imprecise and could not rule out clinically important increases in risk. Certainty of the evidence was low to very low because of residual confounding, live-birth selection, heterogeneous exposure definitions, and few exposed events. A possible timing-specific cardiac signal requires replication.

articles.title: Duration of single-agent perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis and postoperative meningitis after endoscopic endonasal skull base surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,981 patients.
articles.abstract: Postoperative meningitis is a rare but serious complication in endoscopic-endonasal skull-base surgery. Although prophylactic antibiotics are routinely administered, the optimal regimen and duration remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the incidence of meningitis and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage associated with single-agent perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched through February 2025. Eligible studies reported postoperative meningitis or intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak after endoscopic endonasal skull-base surgery using a single primary prophylactic antibiotic. Antibiotic duration was classified as ultra-short (≤ 1 day), short (1-3 days), or long (> 3 days). Study-level proportions were synthesized using logit-transformed random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Meta-regression assessed antibiotic duration and the proportion of intraoperative CSF leaks. Fourteen studies contributed and 7,981 patients were included. The pooled postoperative meningitis incidence was 1.38% (95% CI: 0.92%-2.08%; I² = 65.8%). Among protocols that could be uniquely assigned to a duration subgroup, pooled incidences were 2.12% for long-duration prophylaxis (95% CI: 0.82%-5.36%), 1.20% for short-duration prophylaxis (95% CI: 0.38%-3.70%), and 1.24% for ultra-short prophylaxis (95% CI: 0.66%-2.32%), without a significant subgroup difference (p = 0.764). Antibiotic duration was not associated with meningitis in meta-regression (p = 0.487), whereas a higher study-level proportion of intraoperative CSF leak was associated with higher meningitis incidence (β = 0.0389 per percentage point on the logit scale; p = 0.010). Postoperative meningitis was uncommon across the included cohorts. No statistically significant association was detected between prophylaxis duration and meningitis, whereas a higher intraoperative CSF leak prevalence was associated with higher meningitis incidence. These findings suggest that operative risk characteristics may be important determinants of postoperative infection risk after endoscopic endonasal skull-base surgery.

articles.title: Haplotype structure and functional genotype-phenotype interactions of PON1 (L55M/Q192R) variants in Egyptian children with nephrotic syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is characterized by proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and dyslipidemia. Paraoxonase-1 (PON1), an HDL-associated antioxidant enzyme, contributes to lipid protection and redox homeostasis.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations of PON1 L55M (rs854560) and Q192R (rs662) polymorphisms with NS and their relationships with PON1 concentrations in an Egyptian pediatric cohort.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This case-control study included 84 children aged 4-12 years: 42 with NS and 42 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Serum PON1 concentration, lipid profile, albumin, blood urea, and urinary albumin excretion were assessed. PON1 polymorphisms were genotyped using tetra-primer amplification refractory mutation system polymerase chain reaction (T-ARMS-PCR).

RESULTS: Children with NS had higher total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, blood urea, and urinary albumin excretion, and lower HDL cholesterol, albumin, and PON1 concentrations than controls (all p < 0.001). The L55M MM genotype was more frequent in NS than controls (66.7% vs. 40.5%; OR = 3.77, p = 0.02) and was associated with an adverse biochemical profile. For Q192R, the R allele was associated with NS (61.9% vs. 42.9%; OR = 2.17, p = 0.01), while the RR genotype showed an association under the recessive model (OR = 2.67, p = 0.04). MM and RR carriers had the lowest PON1 concentrations. Haplotype analysis suggested associations between the LQ and MR haplotypes and NS.

CONCLUSIONS: PON1 genetic variation and reduced PON1 concentrations may contribute to the metabolic phenotype and susceptibility to NS, supporting a potential role for PON1-mediated antioxidant pathways in disease pathophysiology and variation in oxidative stress responses among children.

articles.title: Effectiveness of local ablative therapy combined with first-line tyrosine kinase inhibitors in epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) mutations are a significant driver of NSCLC. Although EGFR-Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (TKIs) improve outcomes, the development of resistance limits the survival advantages. Local Ablative Therapy (LAT), particularly radiotherapy, may further enhance outcomes in oligometastatic NSCLC, but its benefit remains uncertain. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy of LAT with TKI vs. TKI alone. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane from inception to May 2025 for studies comparing TKI + LAT versus TKI alone, in patients with EGFR-mutated oligometastatic NSCLC. PRISMA guidelines were followed. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and treatment related adverse effects. We pooled hazard ratios (HR) and risk ratios (RR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) using a random effects model. Statistical Analysis was performed using R software (version 4.4.2). We included 9 studies with 1077 patients, of whom 525 (48.7%) belonged to the TKI + LAT group. Mean follow-up duration was 29.3 months. Patients receiving TKI + LAT had a significantly longer OS (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.42-0.59; p < 0.001) and PFS (HR 0.44; 95% CI 0.34-0.58; p < 0.001) versus TKI alone. The toxicity risk was not statistically different between the arms, suggesting that LAT did not significantly increase adverse effects. LAT combined with TKI is associated with improved survival in selected patients with EGFR-mutated oligometastatic NSCLC, particularly when delivered as consolidation therapy, with an acceptable safety profile.

articles.title: Clinical utility and impact of myocardial viability imaging with F-18 FDG positron emission tomography to predict left ventricular function improvement following revascularization in ischemic heart disease : a single center retrospective study.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Recent studies have questioned the benefit of myocardial viability identification and its clinical impact on revascularization decisions. We aimed to evaluate whether F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (F-18 FDG)-positron emission tomography (PET) influences real-world revascularization decisions and whether PET-defined viability helps predict improvement in ejection fraction (LVEF). We conducted a retrospective chart review of Rubidium-82 (Rb-82)/F-18 FDG PET ischemia and viability studies performed from 2020 to 2024 at our institution. Baseline characteristics including comorbidities, ejection fraction (EF) at 3 months and 1 year and PET study results were evaluated. Among patients with viability, a linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF was performed to assess temporal changes and treatment strategy interaction. One hundred and eleven patients underwent rest-stress Rb-82 PET with F-18 FDG PET imaging, of whom 99 received FDG for myocardial viability assessment. Among these patients, 65 (65.6%) demonstrated ischemic viable myocardium, while 31 (31.3%) had non-viable myocardium. Viability-positive patients were more likely to undergo revascularization (57% (n = 37) vs. 36% (n = 28) received medical therapy only). At 3-month follow-up, both revascularization and medical therapy were associated with significant improvement in LVEF among viability-positive patients. In contrast, viability-negative patients did not demonstrate significant EF improvement. Among viability-positive patients with both 3-month and 1- year EF measurements (N = 28), linear mixed-effects model adjusted for baseline EF revealed that baseline EF was a strong independent predictor of follow-up EF (p < 0.0001). From 3 months to 1 year, the revascularization group demonstrated a significant increase in EF (+ 4.28%, p = 0.014), whereas the medical therapy group showed a non-significant change (+ 1.40%, p = 0.53). However, the overall EF improvement did not differ significantly between groups after adjustment (p = 0.30). EF changes in viability-negative patients remained non-significant over time. Symptomatic improvement was documented in 55.3% of viability-positive patients. Our single-center experience shows that FDG-PET viability test continues to guide management and decision making regarding revascularization and can predict functional recovery and symptomatic improvement.

articles.title: Cardiac CT demonstration of perivalvular extension in aortic valve infective endocarditis.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Delayed-phase cardiac CT depicts perivalvular abscess, demonstrating its adjunctive role to echocardiography in endocarditis evaluation.

articles.title: Oxytetracycline adsorption by clay-carbon hybrids: effects of pH, commercial formulation additives, and PET microplastics.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: The removal of antibiotics from water under environmentally complex laboratory systems remains insufficiently understood, particularly in the presence of coexisting contaminants such as formulation additives and microplastics. This study evaluates the performance of clay-carbon hybrid materials for the removal of oxytetracycline from aqueous solutions under both controlled and complex conditions.
