Natural montmorillonite and two montmorillonite-carbon hybrids were investigated through batch adsorption experiments, including kinetic and equilibrium analyses at different pH values. One of these (MDac3-210-500) exhibited a high adsorption capacity at neutral pH, reaching a maximum value of ~ 0.6 mmol/g. Mechanistic analysis suggests that chemisorption plays a key role in montmorillonite, whereas intraparticle diffusion and surface heterogeneity appear to dominate in the hybrids. To approximate realistic scenarios, adsorption experiments were conducted using a veterinary commercial oxytetracycline formulation and in the presence of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics (particles < 112 μm at 0.5 g/L). The commercial formulation led to a marked decrease in adsorption capacity for hybrids (0.05-0.08 mmol/g), highlighting matrix effects and competition for active sites, whereas, under the tested experimental conditions, PET microplastics did not substantially modify oxytetracycline adsorption by the hybrid materials. These findings highlight the sensitivity of oxytetracycline adsorption to coexisting compounds and provide a basis for understanding the performance of clay-carbon hybrids under more complex water treatment conditions. In particular, the contrasting effects of formulation additives and PET microplastics emphasize the importance of considering matrix composition when evaluating adsorbent performance.

articles.title: Epicardial Versus Circulating Adiponectin: An Unresolved Distinction in Liraglutide's Anti-Arrhythmic Mechanism.
Atypical Stafne bone defect: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs) may be challenging to identify because they deviate from the typical posterior mandibular presentation. This systematic review aims to analyze and synthesize the radiographic, anatomical, and histological characteristics of atypically located SBDs reported in the literature and to assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science databases up to January 2026. Eligibility criteria included English-language case reports and case series describing atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs). Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using an adapted assessment tool for case reports.

RESULTS: Seventy studies encompassing 91 atypical cases were included. Atypically located SBDs were most frequently reported in the anterior mandible. Despite their variable localization, these defects share key anatomical and radiographic features with classical SBDs, including well-defined unilocular radiolucencies and lingual cortical depressions. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), play an important role in confirming these features and in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Histological analysis, when available, most commonly revealed normal salivary gland tissue without evidence of neoplastic transformation.

CONCLUSIONS: Atypically located SBDs demonstrate consistent radiographic and anatomical characteristics that may assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. This review improves the understanding of this under-recognized anatomical variant and highlights the importance of appropriate imaging evaluation in ambiguous cases.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Recognition of these features may facilitate accurate diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Interaction mechanisms of MXene with bacterial division proteins: towards efficient antibacterial materials.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The rising threat of bacterial infections, coupled with the rise of antibiotic-resistant strains, has driven the search for alternative antibacterial strategies that do not rely on traditional chemical agents. Among these, antibacterial materials, particularly those based on two-dimensional nanomaterials, have emerged as promising platforms for preventing bacterial adhesion and proliferation. In this context, MXenes, a class of transition metal carbides and nitrides, have recently gained attention for their potent antibacterial properties. However, the molecular-level mechanisms by which MXenes interact with key bacterial components remain poorly understood. This study employs classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the interactions of Ti3C2O2 MXene with bacterial membrane proteins such as FtsP and EnvC, which are involved in bacterial cell division. Results indicate that both examined proteins adsorb onto the MXene surface. Specific amino acids close to the Ti3C2O2 MXene surface are identified as the main interaction sites that are the driving force for the adsorption of the proteins. Our findings demonstrate that Ti3C2O2 MXene effectively interacts with bacterial membrane proteins, with FtsP exhibiting stronger adsorption than EnvC. These protein-surface interactions could be relevant to the antibacterial activity of Ti3C2O2 MXene and may contribute to its potential effects on bacterial cell division.

METHODS: MD simulations were performed using GROMACS 2022.2 with the CHARMM27 force field for proteins (FtsP: 2UXT, EnvC: 4BH5) and literature-derived parameters for Ti3C2O2. Systems were solvated in TIP3P water, neutralized, and simulated for 200 ns at 310 K. Adsorption was analyzed through contact area and interaction energies (LJ/Coulomb), while protein stability/flexibility was assessed via RMSD, RMSF, and Rg using VMD and GROMACS tools.

articles.title: Pulpotomy of deciduous molars with deep caries using three different hydraulic calcium silicate cements: a short-term pilot randomized controlled split-mouth study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This randomized, controlled split-mouth study evaluated the short-term clinical survival of three hydraulic calcium silicate cements for pulp capping after pulpotomy in primary molars under general anesthesia.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-three children aged 2 to 6 years, each with three carious primary molars (ICDAS 4-6), were recruited for treatment under general anesthesia. Following pulpotomy, the pulp was randomly covered with one of the materials: ProRoot MTA (Dentsply Sirona), Biodentine (Septodont), or TotalFill BC RRM Putty (FKG). The teeth were restored with steel crowns. Clinical survival rate at 5 and 10 months, application time, treatment costs and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) were evaluated using the ECOHIS-G questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using non-parametric methods (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: All 84 treated teeth remained in situ for up to 10 months without clinical symptoms. TotalFill BC RRM Putty had the significantly shortest application time (median 75.5 s; p ≤ 0.001) compared to Biodentine (259 s) and ProRoot MTA (200.5 s). Biodentine resulted in the significantly lowest treatment cost (median €42.45; p ≤ 0.001), ProRoot MTA in the highest (€74.37; TotalFill BC RRM Putty: €60.01). The treatments generally led to improved OHRQoL (Median ECOHIS-G score: initial 5, after 5 months 4, after 10 months 2.5).

CONCLUSIONS: All investigated hydraulic calcium silicate cements showed no differences in short-term clinical outcomes after pulpotomy in primary molars.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Material selection may therefore be guided by practical factors such as handling time and treatment costs, while long-term outcomes, which require further investigations, should be considered. German Clinical Trials Registry: Ref. DRKS00030041.

articles.title: Digital supportive care in prostate cancer: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To map and synthesise the existing evidence on people's perspectives and requirements for patient-facing digital health technologies for use in prostate cancer care delivery. Understanding the preferences of people with prostate cancer and understanding the barriers and facilitators to maximising engagement with digital supportive care healthcare landscape.

METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched to identify suitable studies. All identified citations were imported into Covidence systematic review software for the removal of duplicate records and the study selection process by two reviewers. Methodological quality was appraised using the MMAT, and findings were synthesised narratively using the Human, Organisation, and Technology-fit (HOT-fit) evaluation framework.

RESULTS: Eighty-eight studies were included and represented a total of 29,256 participants affected by prostate cancer. Preferences for digital supportive care emerged across four interconnected domains: (1) mode of delivery, (2) type of content desired, (3) factors enabling engagement, and (4) barriers limiting use. Overall, there was willingness to engage with digital models due to their convenience, flexibility, and immediacy of access. Self-management was enhanced via decision aids, symptom management tools, informational resources, and evidence-based tools to support aspects of psychosocial functioning and emotional wellbeing, physical activity, and sexual health. Several barriers to the implementation and uptake of digital supportive care interventions were identified primarily relating to technology access, device compatibility, digital literacy, and emotional readiness.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital models in prostate cancer care were acceptable and valued for their convenience, flexibility, immediacy of access, tailored content, clinician support, and interactive features, and facilitated self-management through decision-making, symptom management, and informational and psychosocial support. Interpreted through the HOT-fit framework, their value depended on the fit between the technology, its users, and the care setting rather than on technological sophistication alone. Limited attention has been given to digital sexual wellbeing support, and further research is needed on engagement among people with low digital literacy, non-English speakers, and lower-income populations, and on the long-term sustainability of digital models.

articles.title: Development of a clinical risk score for common peroneal nerve palsy after total knee arthroplasty using a Japanese nationwide database.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop a clinical risk score to stratify the risk of post-operative common peroneal nerve palsy (CPNP) following total knee arthroplasty (TKA), based on pre-operative factors.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients undergoing primary TKA using a Japanese nationwide database (from 2014 to 2024). The outcome was post-operative CPNP identified by International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes. Candidate predictors included 24 clinical and hospital-level variables. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regularization was applied for predictor selection. Multivariable logistic regression was used as the primary model, with penalized and Firth logistic models as sensitivity analyses. Model performance and internal validation were assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: A total of 328,314 patients were eligible and CPNP occurred in 340 cases (0.10%). LASSO identified four predictors, and a 0-7 point risk score was developed: knee valgus deformity (3 points), knee contracture (2 points), low BMI < 18.5 (1 point), and spinal disorder (1 point). The observed risk rose from 0.09% (score 0) to 0.56% (score 3), and to 0.68% for scores ≥ 3, while categories of score ≥ 4 were sparsely populated. The risk score showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.55) but favourable calibration (intercept = - 0.001, slope = 1.03).

CONCLUSION: We developed a clinical risk score for CPNP after TKA based on knee valgus deformity, knee contracture, low BMI, and spinal disorder. This score may support pre-operative risk assessment and informed consent in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Neuroimaging findings in hyperammonemic encephalopathy associated with sepsis-induced liver injury: a pilot case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperammonemic encephalopathy (HE) is a severe complication of sepsis-induced liver injury (SILI), often associated with sepsis. However, its neuroimaging manifestations remain poorly understood. The aim of this pilot case series is to describe the brain MRI findings in patients with sepsis and HE.

METHODS: We analysed brain MRI data from 15 consecutive patients with sepsis and clinically confirmed HE. Assessment of cerebral changes was performed using a standard MRI protocol. The following parameters were evaluated during the analysis: localization and signal intensity characteristics of the lesions on MRI, presence or absence of diffusion restriction, presence magnetic susceptibility artifacts, and reversibility on follow‑up were evaluated descriptively. No control group was included.

RESULTS: Pathological changes were observed in all 15 patients. Symmetrical involvement of the insular cortex and cingulate gyrus was the most frequent pattern (13/15, 86.7%), followed by basal ganglia lesions (1/15) and cortico‑subcortical hemispheric lesions (1/15). All lesions were hyperintense on T2‑WI and FLAIR, with diffusion restriction on DWI suggestive of cytotoxic oedema. Follow-up MRI was performed in all patients after treatment adjustment and renal replacement therapy, demonstrating marked regression of all noted changes, concurrent with normalization of serum ammonia, transaminases, lactate and sepsis markers.

articles.title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

articles.title: Immediate Hemodynamic Effects of Pulmonary Artery Flow Restrictors in Univentricular Circulation: Hypothesis-Generating Insights from High-Fidelity Physiologic Streaming Data Using Machine-Learning.
articles.abstract: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome has been historically palliated with the surgical Norwood or hybrid procedures. Transcatheter placement of pulmonary flow restrictors (PFR) with prostaglandin to maintain an unobstructed ductus arteriosus has emerged as an option for single-ventricle patients that are poor surgical candidates. High-fidelity physiologic data has been used to predict outcomes in interstage patients. This study aimed to characterize the acute hemodynamic effects of transcatheter flow restrictors on pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio using physiologic data. A single-center retrospective review of 10 patients who underwent transcatheter flow restrictor placement was performed. High-fidelity physiologic data (1-second resolution) from before, during, and after flow restrictor placement were utilized. Data were aggregated with the Sickbay Clinical Platform. An autoregressive integrated moving average model was used to compare variables of interest before, during, and after flow restrictor placement. A total of 10 patients were included in the study for a total of 123,509 patient seconds of monitoring. A statistically significant decrease in pulmonary-to-systemic blood flow ratio, systemic saturation, and renal oxygen extraction, and an increase in blood pressure, were observed during and after PFR placement. Flow restrictor placement is associated with an acute decrease in calculated pulmonary to systemic blood flow ratio and an increase in calculated renal oxygen extraction ratio (related to an increase in systemic oxygen delivery). More importantly, this study demonstrates that high-fidelity physiologic data platforms can be used for real-time assessment of the effect of pulmonary artery flow reducers. Eventually, clinical decision algorithms may be able to guide the pulmonary artery flow reducer strategy, both intra-procedurally and afterward.

articles.title: Assessing the Potential Cumulative Effects of Longitudinal Interventions for Depression and Deviant Peer Association on Academic Achievement: a Causal Inference Approach.
articles.journal: Prevention science : the official journal of the Society for Prevention Research
articles.abstract: In various studies, depressive symptoms, deviant peer association, and academic achievement appear to be reciprocally and cumulatively related across the transition from childhood to adolescence. This study asks a hypothetical question: how much would grade 12 academic achievement improve if a preventive-intervention reduced depressive symptoms and/or deviant peer association across grades 5, 7, and 10? To answer this question, we used longitudinal datasets from 361 students in the LIFT project and employed the Longitudinal Modified Treatment Policies approach, which uses causal inference and machine learning analyses to estimate the total effect of shifting the trajectory(ies) of an exposure(s) while properly handling time-varying confounding. We estimated the effects of reducing depressive symptoms and/or deviant peer association across the grades by a hypothetical magnitude ranging from 10 to 50%. A 50% reduction in depressive symptoms, deviant peer association, or both was associated with improvements in academic achievement of approximately 7.8%, 14.0%, and 17.1%, respectively; the effects remained positive and statistically significant at every reduction magnitude examined. Implications of the findings for identifying key factors across critical developmental windows are discussed.

articles.title: A Review of the Molecular Evidence for Near-Infrared Light in Astrocyte-Mediated Neurorehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) light represents a promising, noninvasive therapeutic for neurological disorders, predicated on its capacity to modulate astrocyte function. As the primary glial population in the central nervous system, astrocytes are indispensable for maintaining neuronal homeostasis, regulating glutamate metabolism, and supporting metabolic energetics. This review synthesizes recent advancements in NIR-driven neurorehabilitation, elucidating the molecular signaling cascades and transduction pathways activated within the astrocytic network. We specifically examine translational applications across preclinical and clinical models of stroke, Alzheimer's disease, epilepsy, and psychiatric disorders. Furthermore, we evaluate how the integration of optogenetic tools and nanomaterials has refined NIR therapies, establishing a foundation for high-precision neurology. Given the rising demand for nonsurgical interventions, this review provides a timely framework for the next generation of photobiomodulation and neural modulation strategies.

articles.title: Digitalization of the diabetic eye notebook: patient and physician perspectives on a smartphone application for diabetic retinopathy management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate patient and physician perspectives on the digitalization of the Diabetic Eye Notebook into a smartphone application, focusing on expectations, concerns, and potential benefits for the management of diabetic retinopathy (DR).

STUDY DESIGN: A two-part prospective cross-sectional study comprising a multicenter patient survey and a single-center pilot usability and acceptability evaluation. (March-August 2024).

METHODS: Two independent surveys were conducted. In Study (A), 197 patients with diabetes from five institutions completed questionnaires assessing their awareness and use of the paper-based notebooks, willingness to adopt the application, and related expectations and concerns. In Study (B), a preliminary single-center pilot usability and acceptability evaluation was conducted in which eight physicians and ten patients at one institution used a beta version of the application and provided feedback on usability, functionality, and potential benefits.

RESULTS: In Study A: awareness and usage rates of the Diabetic Eye Notebook were 13.7 and 7.1%, respectively, both lower than those of the Japan Association for Diabetes Education and Care Coordination Notebook. Willingness to adopt the application was reported by 43.7% of patients. Patients willing to adopt the application were younger in the unadjusted comparison (mean age, 60.3 vs. 70.4 years; P<0.001), whereas the adjusted model showed a different direction for the age association, possibly reflecting confounding or a suppression effect related to routine smartphone-application use. Desired features included appointment reminders (47.3%), data sharing (32.2%), and visualization of clinical data (30.8%). Concerns included operational difficulty (64.4%) and data privacy (20.8%). In Study (B), physicians valued portability (75.0%) and improved communication (50.0%) but noted data entry burden (50.0%) and privacy issues (50.0%). Patients valued portability, treatment, history review, and improved communication (30.0% each), but reported privacy (40.0%) and usability (40.0%) concerns.

CONCLUSION: This study identified key expectations and concerns among patients and physicians regarding the digitalization of the Diabetic Eye Notebook. Although the application has the potential to overcome practical limitations of the paper-based format, usability for older adults and data security remain major challenges, underscoring the need for further refinement and prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Clinical course and outcomes of diabetic ketoacidosis in pregnancy: a single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We evaluated the obstetric and perinatal outcomes of pregnant women hospitalised with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and examined the association between clinical and laboratory parameters and admission to the intensive care unit (ICU).

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 32 pregnant women managed for DKA between May 2019 and December 2025 at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital, comparing those admitted to the ICU with those who were not. The association of arterial pH and serum bicarbonate with ICU admission was examined using ROC analysis and logistic regression, and biochemical severity markers were compared between pregnancies with and without DKA-related adverse outcomes. Given the sample size, all inferential analyses were regarded as exploratory.

RESULTS: Twenty women (62.5%) were admitted to the ICU. They were older and had lower arterial pH and serum bicarbonate, whereas plasma glucose did not differ between groups. Thresholds examined were ≤ 18.5 mmol/L for bicarbonate (AUC 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.95) and ≤ 7.33 for pH (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.53-0.90). In a two-variable logistic regression model, lower bicarbonate (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.37-0.91) and older age (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.07-2.08) were associated with ICU admission. Women with DKA-related adverse outcomes had lower pH (7.20 versus 7.34; p = 0.004) and lower bicarbonate (8.0 versus 17.0 mmol/L; p = 0.014).

CONCLUSION: In this small single-centre cohort, the depth of maternal acidosis rather than the degree of hyperglycaemia was associated with ICU admission and with adverse obstetric outcomes. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; the thresholds reported here require validation in larger, multicentre cohorts before any clinical application.

articles.title: Sugar Reduction in Processed Foods: Industry Initiatives, Policy Interventions, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Excessive intake of added sugars, particularly from sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs), is an important global public health concern associated with increased risks of obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and other non-communicable diseases. However, the health impacts of sugar consumption are influenced by broader dietary patterns, total energy intake, and overall diet quality. Although sugar plays important sensory and functional roles in food, including flavour enhancement, texture, colour development, and shelf-life extension, growing concerns regarding excessive added sugar intake have driven global efforts to reduce sugar content in processed foods. This review outlines current strategies undertaken by the food industry and regulatory authorities to address this challenge.

RECENT FINDINGS: Industry-driven initiatives include product reformulation, substitution with natural and artificial sweeteners, intrinsic sugar reduction through processing innovations, and portion-control strategies. In parallel, regulatory actions, such as sugar taxation, mandatory nutritional labelling, and public awareness campaigns have been implemented to promote healthier purchasing behaviours and dietary choices. While these interventions have contributed to progress in sugar reduction, challenges persist concerning consumer acceptability, labelling transparency, cross-regional policy inconsistencies, and limited long-term evidence regarding population-level health impacts. Emerging technologies, including enzymatic sugar modification, rare sugar production, and fermentation-derived sweeteners, offer promising solutions but require further validation regarding safety, scalability, sustainability, and consumer acceptance. Effective sugar reduction strategies demand an integrated framework that combines technological innovation, policy alignment, and behavioural change. Strengthened collaboration between industry, governments, and consumers is essential to developing healthier and more sustainable food systems.

articles.title: Emergency clinicians' knowledge and perceptions of training, education, and resources in eating disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency clinicians have an important role in the recognition, assessment, and emergency management of patients with eating disorders. International studies suggest emergency clinicians receive limited training in eating disorders; however, Irish data are lacking. This study aimed to evaluate emergency clinicians' perceptions of education, training, and available resources.

METHODS: A single-centre cross-sectional survey study was conducted in an Irish Emergency Department (ED). Investigator-developed surveys were distributed to emergency medicine physicians and emergency nursing staff. Surveys assessed undergraduate and postgraduate education, awareness of clinical guidelines, perceived training adequacy, and educational needs relating to eating disorders.

RESULTS: Twenty-three emergency medicine physicians and twenty-six emergency nurses participated, representing response rates of 60.5% and 27.4%, respectively. Most physicians (n = 22, 95.7%) reported undergraduate training in eating disorders compared with 57.7% of nurses (n = 15); however, only eleven (47.8%) of physicians and eight (30.8%) of nurses considered this training adequate. Postgraduate training was reported by seven (30.4%) of physicians and seven (26.9%) of nurses. Awareness of key clinical guidelines among physicians was limited, with nine (39.1%) familiar with the Royal College of Psychiatrists' Medical Emergencies in Eating Disorders (MEED) guidance. Emergency clinicians supported additional education on eating disorders.

CONCLUSION: Emergency clinicians reported substantial gaps in education and awareness relating to eating disorders and expressed a perceived need for additional training. Enhanced undergraduate and postgraduate education, guideline dissemination, and strengthened multidisciplinary resources may improve clinicians' preparedness to recognise and manage eating disorders in emergency care.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Role of Withaferin A in Huntington's Disease: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is an inherited neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded CAG repeat in the huntingtin (HTT) gene. Its pathogenesis involves mutant huntingtin aggregation, impaired proteostasis and autophagy, transcriptional dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and progressive neuronal loss. Withaferin A (WA), a steroidal lactone derived from Withania somnifera, has demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, proteostasis-modulating and stress-response effects in experimental studies. In a transgenic HD mouse model, WA-induced heat-shock-response activation was associated with reduced mutant huntingtin aggregation and attenuation of selected disease-related abnormalities. In contrast, evidence for nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/antioxidant response element (Nrf2/ARE) activation, autophagy regulation, mitochondrial protection and suppression of inflammatory signaling is derived predominantly from cellular experiments and non-HD neurological or inflammatory models rather than from validated HD models. The direct relevance of these proposed mechanisms to HD therefore remains to be established. No clinical studies have demonstrated the safety or therapeutic efficacy of WA in individuals with HD. Moreover, its bioavailability, pharmacokinetic behavior, optimal dose, long-term toxicity, central nervous system exposure and possible drug interactions remain insufficiently characterized. This review critically evaluates HD-specific and indirect evidence concerning the neuroprotective actions of WA, identifies important methodological and translational limitations and discusses priorities for future investigation. Current evidence supports WA as an experimental compound for further preclinical study rather than as an established or clinically applicable treatment for HD.

articles.title: The Impact of Ambient Ozone Exposure on Respiratory Health in the U.S. Populations: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Ozone, a photochemically generated air pollutant, continues to pose a major concern for public health in the United States, with some 125 million people living in areas that exceed national ambient air quality standards set by the United States Environmental Protection Agency. To fully understand the potential impacts of ambient ozone exposure on respiratory health, we conducted a systematic review of United States epidemiologic and experimental studies published from 1980 to 2026, encompassing both acute and chronic exposure windows. This review focused on three key domains: (1) pulmonary function, (2) asthma-related symptoms and emergency department visits/hospitalizations, and (3) other respiratory-related morbidity and mortality. Findings across diverse study designs demonstrated adverse respiratory effects, with children, older adults, and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions being disproportionately affected. This review is among the first to comprehensively synthesize ozone-related respiratory health outcomes including pulmonary functions outcomes across both experimental and population-based observational studies-highlighting consistent decrements in lung function, even at concentrations below current regulatory standards. Additionally, this work incorporated ozone-associated school absenteeism, a sensitive yet underexamined indicator for pediatric respiratory health outcome. The observed associations across multiple outcomes and exposure durations underscored the importance of strengthening ambient air quality standards and prioritizing interventions toward high-risk populations. Continued increases in ambient ozone exposure even in the presence of regulatory action and increasing contributions from sources related to climate change such as wildfires emphasize the importance of sustained research and public health planning to safeguard respiratory health in vulnerable communities.

articles.title: Comparison of PMAneo and RAPID in acute ischemic stroke: agreement in CT perfusion analysis and DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Automated computed tomography perfusion (CTP) analysis plays a key role in triaging acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to evaluate the agreement of PMAneo compared with RAPID in a multicenter setting.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 99 patients with anterior circulation AIS from three stroke centers using four different CT scanners. CTP data were processed using both PMAneo and RAPID. Volumetric agreement for ischemic core volume and Tmax > 6 s volume was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with volume discrepancies. EVT imaging eligibility was evaluated according to the DEFUSE 3 criteria (ischemic core volume < 70 mL, mismatch ratio ≥ 1.8, and absolute mismatch volume ≥ 15 mL), using RAPID as the comparator.

RESULTS: Ischemic core volumes showed excellent agreement between the two platforms (ICC = 0.881, 95% CI 0.827-0.918), and Tmax > 6 s volumes showed good agreement (ICC = 0.761, 95% CI 0.283-0.896), whereas mismatch volumes showed moderate agreement (ICC = 0.661, 95% CI 0.146-0.844). For the ischemic core threshold (< 70 mL), PMAneo demonstrated 100% (95% CI 96-100%) relative sensitivity and 67% (95% CI 38-88%) relative specificity. For the full DEFUSE 3 criteria, the relative sensitivity and specificity were 81% (95% CI 70-89%) and 84% (95% CI 66-95%), respectively. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated proportional bias, with PMAneo underestimating volumes relative to RAPID as lesion size increased. Basal ganglia involvement and imaging site were significantly associated with these volume differences (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: PMAneo showed high volumetric agreement and comparable DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility to RAPID, suggesting it is a reliable alternative for automated CTP analysis. Although proportional bias and potential diagnostic discrepancies were observed in borderline cases near clinically relevant thresholds, PMAneo may facilitate broader access to automated CTP analysis.

articles.title: Bismuth-containing quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection in penicillin‑allergic children: efficacy, safety and real‑world experience from China.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the efficacy and safety of 14-day bismuth-containing quadruple therapy (BQT) as both first-line and rescue treatment for children with Helicobacter pylori infections and penicillin allergies in China.

METHODS: This real-world, exploratory, retrospective observational cohort study enrolled children aged 6 to 18 years who underwent gastroendoscopy. The eradication status was assessed at least 4 weeks after treatment completion. A negative urea breath test or endoscopic rapid urease test result indicated successful eradication.

RESULTS: Between July 2017 and June 2025, 453 patients were analyzed in the study. Metronidazole-clarithromycin BQT as first-line treatment achieved eradication rates of 81.2% (285/351; 95% confidence interval [CI], 77.1-85.3%) and 82.5% (279/338; 95% CI, 78.5-86.6%) in modified intention-to-treat (mITT) and per-protocol (PP) analyses. Metronidazole-clarithromycin BQT as rescue therapy succeeded in 41.4% (41/99; 95% CI, 31.7-51.1%) of cases in mITT and in 42.6% (40/94; 95% CI, 32.6-52.5%) of cases in PP analyses. Three patients treated with metronidazole-minocycline BQT as rescue therapy all achieved successful eradication of H. pylori. Adverse effects were reported by 12.8% (45/351) of patients in the first-line therapy group and 9.8% (10/102) in the rescue therapy group (p = 0.40). The compliance rates for metronidazole-clarithromycin BQT as first-line therapy and rescue therapy were 96.3% (338/351) and 94.9% (94/99), respectively.

CONCLUSION: As first-line therapy, metronidazole-clarithromycin BQT achieved an eradication rate of 82.5% in Chinese children with penicillin allergies. However, this regimen was inadequate as a rescue treatment. Rescue regimens such as those containing minocycline or cefuroxime warrant further investigation.

articles.title: ST20 Staphylococcus aureus causing suppurative cervical lymphadenitis in an extremely low-birth-weight infant.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract: Neonatal suppurative cervical lymphadenitis is uncommon, particularly in extremely low-birth-weight infants. We report a 772 g infant born at 28 weeks of gestation who developed rapidly progressive unilateral cervical lymphadenitis caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) on postnatal day 31. The infant remained afebrile and blood cultures were negative despite progression requiring repeated drainage. The cervical isolate was genotyped as ST20/spa-t3929 and shared an identical genetic profile with an earlier pharyngeal isolate, suggesting that the infection arose from pre-existing S. aureus colonization. This case highlights the potential for ST20 MSSA to cause localized invasive infection in preterm infants.

articles.title: Desensitisation protocol for ethambutol in the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ethambutol is a key component of treatment for Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD), primarily through suppression of macrolide resistance. However, adverse drug reactions frequently lead to treatment interruption, and evidence-based alternatives remain limited. We evaluated the feasibility and outcomes of a structured outpatient ethambutol desensitisation protocol in patients with MAC-PD who developed ethambutol intolerance or hypersensitivity.

METHODS: We conducted a multicentre observational study across four specialist NTM centres. Patients undergoing treatment for MAC-PD who experienced an ethambutol-related adverse reaction leading to drug cessation were eligible. A patient-led outpatient desensitisation protocol commenced at 25 mg daily with gradual dose escalation to a weight-based target dose. The protocol allowed temporary dose reduction to previously tolerated levels if symptoms recurred. Success was defined as achievement of the target dose or maintenance of a tolerated dose associated with sustained culture conversion.

RESULTS: Twenty desensitisation episodes were performed in 17 patients (65% female; mean age 72 years). The most common indication was rash (70%), followed by headache (15%). Overall, 17/20 (85%) desensitisations were successful, including 13/14 (93%) among patients with delayed cutaneous reactions. Mean time to target dose was 9 weeks (median 4 weeks). No severe immediate hypersensitivity reactions occurred during desensitisation. Sixteen episodes (80%) were associated with culture conversion, and 11 (55%) patients completed therapy with ethambutol-containing regimens.

CONCLUSIONS: Outpatient ethambutol desensitisation appears feasible, safe and effective in selected patients with MAC-PD and non-severe ethambutol intolerance. This approach may help preserve an essential component of MAC therapy when treatment options are otherwise limited.

articles.title: An electrospun PCL/PVA-chitosan nanofiber scaffold loaded with selenium nanoparticles promotes antibacterial activity and accelerates wound healing: synthesis, characterization, and in-vivo evaluation.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic, epidermal full-thickness wounds present a critical clinical challenge due to high risks of infection, impaired healing, and lack of advanced dressings that synergistically combine antibacterial efficacy with tissue regeneration.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to design and evaluate a multifunctional nanofibrous scaffold that simultaneously addresses anti-infection, mechanical support, and controlled tissue remodeling.

METHODS: A tri-component nanofibrous scaffold composed of polyvinyl alcohol, chitosan, and polycaprolactone was fabricated via electrospinning. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) were incorporated to impart antibacterial and pro-healing properties. The scaffold was characterized for morphological, mechanical, and biological attributes. In vivo performance was assessed using a murine epidermal full-thickness wound model.

RESULTS: The scaffold demonstrated significantly enhanced mechanical properties and exhibited potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli. Controlled release of SeNPs reduced initial cytotoxic burst effects. In vivo tests confirmed accelerated wound closure and superior tissue regeneration compared to controls CONCLUSION: The SeNP-functionalized nanofibrous scaffold represents a promising therapeutic platform for epidermal full-thickness wound healing, effectively combining mechanical robustness, antibacterial action, and biocompatibility.

articles.title: Irisin promotes lipid clearance through the CD81-integrin-FAK axis in steatotic hepatocytes.
articles.abstract: Irisin, an exercise-induced myokine, regulates metabolic homeostasis, but its receptor mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. This study investigates the role of the co-receptor CD81 in modulating irisin signaling and intrahepatic lipid homeostasis. Clinical correlations were analyzed in 88 bariatric surgery patients and liver biopsy cohorts (n = 62). In vitro steatosis models included Clone-9 rat hepatocytes, primary mouse hepatocytes, and human HepG2 and Huh-7 cells treated with fatty acids and recombinant irisin. Receptor interactions and downstream signaling were evaluated using co-immunoprecipitation, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, subcellular fractionation, and lipid staining. Serum irisin positively correlated with BMI and steatosis grade, but inversely associated with triglycerides, fasting glucose, and HbA1c. Intrahepatic FNDC5/irisin and integrin β5 correlated with serum triglycerides, whereas membranous CD81 expression declined with advancing steatosis. Free fatty acids induced FNDC5/irisin and perilipins (Plin2/Plin5) while downregulating CD81. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed physical interaction between CD81 and integrins αV/β5 subunits. CD81 overexpression enhanced irisin-induced focal adhesion kinase (FAK) phosphorylation, restricted PPARγ nuclear translocation, suppressed Plin2/Plin5 expression, and attenuated lipid accumulation. Conversely, FAK inhibition using BI 853520 or CD81 knockdown abrogated these protective anti-steatotic effects. In conclusion, CD81 serves as a functional co-receptor that physically associates with the integrin αV/β5 complex to amplify irisin-FAK signaling, restrict PPARγ nuclear transactivation, and suppress lipid droplet accumulation in cultured hepatocytes in vitro. These findings highlight the CD81-integrin-FAK axis as a potential candidate for further translational exploration in MASLD.

articles.title: PD-1/ PD-l1 Inhibitors and Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Brain Metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is the treatment of choice for limited brain metastases (BM), and its combination with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors is hypothesized to offer synergistic therapeutic benefits. However, there are concerns regarding augmented risk of radiation-induced brain necrosis (RIBN). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the efficacy and toxicity profile of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with SRS or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (FSRT).

METHODS: Four databases were screened, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus from inception to November 2025. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), extracranial and distant intracranial progression free survival (PFS), and local control (LC). A subgroup analysis was performed based on the primary metastasis origin and radiotherapy treatment modalities. We extracted RIBN events and grade ≥ 3 neurological events. A single-arm meta-analysis was performed using the random-effects modeling. This review protocol was registered on November 2025 on PROSPERO (ID CRD420251171879).

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included, published between 2016 and 2025 comprising 2,587 patients with BM. The pooled one-year OS was 65% (95% CI 60-69). Patients with BM from Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) had one-year OS (68%) while melanoma BM had OS (61%). LC and distant intracranial PFS at one year were 87% (95% CI 79-92) and 40.23% (95% CI 17.99-62.47), respectively. The cumulative incidence (CI) of grade 3 RIBN was 5% (95% CI 3-8), and grade ≥ 3 neurological events occurred in 7% (95% CI 4-13). No statistically significant difference in RIBN rates was found between melanoma and NSCLC primaries subgroup.

CONCLUSION: The combination of SRS/FSRT with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors is associated with favorable intracranial PFS and LC and a tolerable toxicity profile, with relatively lower rates of grade 3 RIBN. These findings support the feasibility of this combined modality in the immunotherapy era. However, definitive conclusions regarding the incremental risk of RIBN require future prospective trials.

articles.title: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Correspondence.
Systematic review and meta-analysis on comparing treatment approaches of cervical fractures in ankylosing spondylitis to determine improvement in outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVE: Anterior, posterior and combine surgical approach for treatment of cervical fractures in ankylosing spondylitis is debatable in current existing literature. There are recognized advantages and disadvantages associated with anterior, posterior, and combined surgical approaches to the cervical spine when treating fractures in patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Despite growing surgical experience, the optimal approach with respect to neurological recovery, complication rates, and mortality remains unclear, and the choice is largely guided by surgeon expertise and patient-specific factors rather than high-quality comparative evidence. The study aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing treatment options for cervical fractures in patients with AS. The focus was on evaluating surgical approaches, complication rates, neurological outcomes.

METHODOLOGY: Systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using specific keywords and related MeSH on PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov to retrieve relevant literature. Only peer-reviewed English language original articles with full-text availability from 1st January, 1970 to 31st December, 2025 were considered. The pooled data analysis was conducted for binary outcomes through estimating odds ratios at 95% confidence interval with use of Mantel-Haenszel test. Forest plots were also generated for comparison of outcomes. Heterogeneity was assessed using (I²) using random effect model (I² > 50%) and fixed effect model (I² < 50%). The dichotomous model in meta-analysis was used to generate forest plots to assess heterogeneity. Funnel plots were also generated to determine the publication bias. In case of asymmetry in funnel plots, Rank correlation, Egger's regression test was performed to confirm the publication bias (p < 0.05). The statistical analysis was conducted on open meta-analyst Excel Binary Workbook.

RESULTS: Eighteen retrospective studies encompassing 1441 patients (1275 male, 166 female; mean age range 40-72.7 years) met inclusion criteria. Mean CMS was 37.89 ± 5.71 (range 30-49), indicating uniformly poor methodological quality across all included studies. Across all nine pairwise comparisons, the only statistically significant finding was a higher complication rate with the anterior approach compared to the posterior approach (OR 2.97, 95% CI 1.23-7.19, p = 0.015; I² = 65.9%). Neurological recovery did not differ significantly in any pairwise comparison: combined vs. anterior (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.41-2.29, p = 0.941; I² = 91.9%), combined vs. posterior (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.32-1.26, p = 0.195; I² = 89.7%), and anterior vs. posterior (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.45-1.07, p = 0.096; I² = 0.0%). Complication rates comparing combined vs. anterior (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.49-1.68, p = 0.752) and combined vs. posterior (OR 1.48, 95% CI 0.98-2.25, p = 0.065) were not significantly different, though the latter demonstrated a marginal trend favoring the posterior approach. Mortality did not differ significantly across any comparison: combined vs. anterior (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.84-4.72, p = 0.120; I² = 0%), combined vs. posterior (OR 1.43, 95% CI 0.77-2.63, p = 0.254; I² = 0%), and anterior vs. posterior (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.17-8.49, p = 0.853; I² = 68.2%). Funnel plots and associated statistical tests indicated no evidence of small-study or publication bias across all comparisons (all Egger's and Kendall's p > 0.05). However, these findings should be regarded as low-certainty evidence given the exclusively retrospective study designs, uniformly poor CMS scores, and very high between-study heterogeneity in neurological recovery comparisons. Funnel plot symmetry and statistical tests (Egger's regression and Kendall's rank correlation, p > 0.05) indicated no evidence of small-study or publication bias across comparisons.

CONCLUSION: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized the best currently available - though uniformly low-certainty - evidence on surgical approaches for ankylosing spondylitis-associated cervical fractures. Based on low-certainty retrospective evidence, the anterior approach is associated with a statistically significantly higher complication rate than the posterior approach, representing the only significant finding across nine pairwise comparisons. Neurological recovery and mortality were comparable across all three approach pairs. The posterior approach appears favorable from a complication-minimization perspective, particularly in patients with significant cardiopulmonary comorbidity, but this recommendation is based on low-certainty evidence and should not override individualized surgical decision-making based on fracture morphology, baseline neurological status, and surgeon expertise. Prospective, multicenter studies with standardized outcome reporting are required to generate higher-certainty evidence.

articles.title: Periodontal Disease and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Perspectives.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Periodontal disease has been increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory condition with potential systemic implications, particularly in the cardiovascular system. Heart failure (HF), a pro-inflammatory syndrome with multisystem involvement, remains a major public health burden. This state-of-the-art narrative review aims to analyze the current scientific evidence on the association between periodontal disease and heart failure, emphasizing epidemiological data, cardiac biomarkers, inflammatory mediators, and future perspectives.

RECENT FINDINGS: Current evidence indicates a high prevalence of periodontal disease among patients with HF and suggests associations between periodontal disease and elevated cardiac biomarkers, including NT-proBNP and troponin T, as well as systemic inflammatory mediators such as C-reactive protein, IL-6, and TNF-α. Interventional studies have reported reductions in some of these biomarkers following periodontal treatment, suggesting a potential biological link between periodontal inflammation and HF. However, findings remain heterogeneous, and some studies have failed to demonstrate significant associations. Current evidence supports an association between periodontal disease and heart failure, with systemic inflammation representing a potential biological link. Nevertheless, the heterogeneity of study designs, small sample sizes, and predominance of observational and cross-sectional evidence limit causal inference. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to clarify causal mechanisms and determine whether periodontal prevention and treatment can contribute to integrated strategies for patients with HF.

articles.title: From Aerosol to Epithelium: An Integrated Clinical, Pathologic, and Mechanistic Review of Nicotine and Cannabis Vaporizer Use and Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The prevalence of cannabis and nicotine vaporizer use appears to be increasing, but their effects on the respiratory system are incompletely elucidated. This review brings together clinical, pathologic, and molecular knowledge describing airway disease, acute lung injury syndromes, and structural lung injury resulting from nicotine and cannabis vaporizer use.

RECENT FINDINGS: We describe consistent epidemiologic associations of nicotine vaporizer use with obstructive lung disease, bronchitis, emphysema, and constrictive bronchiolitis; cannabis vaporizer use is more frequently associated with acute lung injury and airway disease symptoms. At a molecular level, nicotinic receptor activation drives collagen deposition, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and impaired mucociliary clearance; cannabinoid receptor activation has effects on airway inflammation, epithelial integrity, and immune cell function. Oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction likely mediate effects of nicotine and cannabis vaporizer exposure through receptor-independent mechanisms. Use of nicotine and cannabis vaporizers affects clinical pulmonary disease through a variety of converging molecular and cellular mechanisms in the respiratory epithelium. Significant knowledge gaps remain, particularly with regard to molecular investigations of cannabis vaporizer use and dual nicotine-cannabis vaporizer use. Future investigations integrating molecular mechanisms of disease with clinical and histopathologic outcomes are necessary to better characterize the effects of these increasingly impactful public health risks.

articles.title: Italian adaptation of international recommendations for the management of restless legs syndrome: A consensus statement by the scientific committee of RLS-Italia.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent international recommendations have substantially changed the management of restless legs syndrome (RLS), emphasizing systematic iron assessment, earlier use of iron therapy and α2δ ligands, and greater caution with chronic dopaminergic treatment because of augmentation. Their implementation requires adaptation to national healthcare organization, regulatory indications, reimbursement, and access to specialist services.

METHODS: The Scientific Committee of RLS-Italia conducted a structured, non-Delphi consensus process based on the 2025 American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline and systematic review, the 2026 RLS Foundation algorithm, the World Sleep Society partial endorsement, and selected supporting evidence. Successive drafts were circulated, discussed, and approved by all authors.

RESULTS: The proposed Italian framework prioritizes clinical diagnosis, exclusion of mimics, correction of exacerbating factors, systematic assessment of iron status, and iron treatment when indicated. α2δ ligands are preferred for most adults with chronic persistent RLS, whereas dopamine agonists should be restricted to selected patients and monitored for augmentation. Refractory or augmented disease should be managed by clinicians with specific RLS expertise, with consideration of intravenous iron, opioids, or device-based treatment. Dipyridamole is not included in the standard pathway, and periodic limb movement disorder should not be diagnosed or treated solely on the basis of polysomnographic findings.

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus statement provides a nationally coherent framework that can support regional implementation through locally appropriate organizational and clinical protocols.

articles.title: Anatomical and radiological analysis of ventricular catheter trajectories: neuronavigation-guided dissection and tractography-based 3D visualization.
articles.abstract: Ventricular catheter placement (VCP) is a life-saving intervention frequently performed in emergency departments and intensive care units. The free hand technique is the most commonly used approach for placing catheters. This study demonstrates the anatomical and radiological relationship between catheters inserted through the most commonly used access points and the anatomical structures in their path. Moreover, we calculate the insertion angles and catheter lengths that should be specified during VCP. Six donated human heads, fixed in 10% formalin and injected with colored silicone dye, were used in this study. Ventricular catheters were inserted through Kocher's, Paine's, Keen's, Frazier's, and Dandy's points under navigation. Dissection was performed from the skin to the inner wall of the ventricle while preserving the inserted catheters. The insertion angle and delivery length for each access point were measured both in the donated human heads and in 50 patients with hydrocephalus. In addition, magnetic resonance tractography was performed, and the relationship of each catheter with anatomical structures was presented as a three-dimensional model. Catheters inserted from Keen's and Paine's points pass through regions containing dense and crucial vascular structures. Catheters inserted from Keen's, Paine's, and Frazier's points enter the cortex through eloquent areas. The catheter inserted from Keen's point passes through the most diverse white matter pathway. Catheters inserted from Kocher's and Dandy's points pass through regions with less dense cortical vascular structures. Moreover, they pass through noneloquent cortical structures and fewer white matter tracts. This is the first anatomical dissection and tractography report describing the relationship between catheters introduced through the most common ventricular access sites and the anatomical structures along their path from the skin to the ventricle. Understanding the anatomical and radiological three-dimensionality of VCP will increase the safety of its applications.

articles.title: Symptom duration and postoperative outcomes in degenerative cervical myelopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical decompression is regarded as standard treatment for degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM). However, the timing of surgery remains a critical yet unresolved issue in clinical practice. Therefore, this meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of symptom duration on surgical outcomes and determine the optimal timing for surgery.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted on 16th November 2025 using PubMed, Ovid, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify eligible articles. Studies comprising patients with DCM undergoing surgery, assessing outcome by mJOA score at a minimum of 12 months of follow-up, were included. A risk of bias in the included studies was assessed using the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool.

RESULTS: From 1522 records, 14 studies encompassing a total of 3162 patients were included in the current meta-analysis. Symptom duration was significantly associated with postoperative mJOA score according to univariate (OR: 2.15; 95% CI: 1.64-2.81) and multivariate data (OR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.23-2.57). Meta-regression showed that neither baseline mJOA score nor age affected the association. Moreover, early surgery resulted in reduced neck pain and disability measured by the NDI score (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.24-1.95), but not quality of life according to EQ-5D (OR: 1.47; 95% CI: 0.74-2.89). At the 6-month and 12-month cut-off points, patients with longer symptom duration had significantly worse outcomes in terms of mJOA score, and after exclusion of high-risk-of-bias studies, only at the 12-month cut-off point. However, the test for subgroup differences was insignificant (p = 0.89).

CONCLUSION: Longer symptom duration is associated with poor surgical outcomes. Therefore, the duration of symptoms should be regarded as a clinically meaningful factor when counseling patients with DCM and planning surgical intervention. An optimal threshold for symptom duration, indicating when the surgery should be performed to prevent poor outcomes, cannot be recommended due to limitations of published data and needs to be established by further well-designed prospective studies. Future research should also aim to define optimal time cut-offs across different degrees of DCM severity and varied disease trajectories.

articles.title: Ectromelia Virus Reprograms the Noncanonical NF-κB Signaling Pathway in HeLa Epithelial Cells.
articles.abstract: The noncanonical nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) pathway regulates adaptive immune responses and antiviral innate immunity. Orthopoxviruses, including the human pathogen variola virus and zoonotic viruses such as vaccinia virus and monkeypox virus, have evolved multiple strategies to suppress host antiviral signaling. Our previous work using in vitro immune cell models demonstrated that the mouse-specific orthopoxvirus ectromelia virus (ECTV) inhibits the noncanonical NF-κB signaling pathway. Here, we investigated the impact of ECTV on noncanonical NF-κB signaling in human epithelial HeLa cells. Tumor necrosis factor superfamily ligands were used to activate or modulate noncanonical NF-κB signaling. Using fluorescence microscopy and immunoblot analyses, we found that ECTV reduced LIGHT (TNFSF14)- and lymphotoxin α1β2 (LTα1β2)-induced nuclear accumulation of the NF-κB subunits RelB and p52. ECTV infection alone increased whole-cell RelB and NF-κB2/p100 levels but did not significantly alter nuclear RelB levels. In TNF-α-stimulated cells, ECTV reduced levels of cellular inhibitor of apoptosis protein 2 (cIAP2), whereas in LTα1β2-stimulated cells, ECTV reduced levels of TNF receptor-associated factor 3 (TRAF3). RT-qPCR analysis revealed that ECTV upregulated RELB, NFKB2, and CHUK expression. Viral infection also increased expression of TNFAIP3 and OTUD7B, genes encoding regulators of noncanonical NF-κB signaling. Moreover, infected cells exhibited increased expression of selected RelB-responsive genes, including FBRS, CCR10, and TNFRSF6B. Together, these findings indicate that ECTV modulates components associated with noncanonical NF-κB signaling in epithelial cells in vitro, without evidence of constitutive pathway activation.

articles.title: Genetic correlates of corticobasal degeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Corticobasal degeneration (CBD) is a primary 4-repeat tauopathy marked by progressive motor, cognitive, and behavioral decline, substantial clinicopathologic heterogeneity, and few disease-modifying therapeutic options. Although MAPT variation has long been implicated in CBD susceptibility, the full genetic architecture of CBD has remained highly fragmented and poorly synthesized.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines to identify studies evaluating genetic associations with CBD through August 2026. Eligible studies reported effect estimates for MAPT haplotypes, MAPT subhaplotypes, MAPT SNPs, or non-MAPT candidate loci. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and pooled associations were calculated using inverse-variance meta-analysis. Twenty-two studies published between 2001 and 2025 were included.

RESULTS: The most consistent associations involved MAPT haplotype architecture, with H1 and H1/H1 showing increased CBD susceptibility and H2 showing a protective association. Among MAPT H1 subhaplotypes, H1c, H1d, and H1q demonstrated significant risk associations, whereas other subhaplotypes showed less significant effects. MAPT SNP-level associations were generally modest, though several variants showed small yet significant protective or risk-related effects. Among non-MAPT loci, C9orf72, MOBP, and KIF13B were associated with CBD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that genetic susceptibility to CBD is dominated by MAPT architecture; however, significant heterogeneity within and beyond MAPT exists, with significant contributions from select subhaplotypes, SNPs, and non-MAPT loci. Overall, these findings support tau-centered genetic vulnerability while highlighting candidate pathways relevant to CBD pathogenesis, glial biology, and broader neurodegenerative vulnerability, providing a foundation for future biomarker, mechanistic, and precision-medicine studies.

articles.title: Urinary Incontinence, Pelvic Floor Care, and Support Preferences Among Parous Women: A Cross-Sectional Online Survey.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Urinary incontinence (UI) is common after childbirth, but uptake of care may be limited. We aimed to describe UI burden, pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT), care-seeking, and support preferences among parous women in Japan.

METHODS: In March 2026, 1000 parous women aged 20-49 years completed a cross-sectional online survey with equal age-decade quotas. This unweighted, non-probability sample was not nationally representative. Current UI was operationalized as an International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI SF) total score ≥ 1. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs).

RESULTS: Overall, 55.8% met this inclusive criterion (558/1000; 95% confidence interval [CI] 52.7-58.9), while 28.1% had moderate-to-severe UI (281/1000; 95% CI 25.4-31.0). Only 1.7% reported a hospital visit specifically for UI; among 416 women reporting leakage on the ICIQ-UI SF frequency item, 56.2% had no intention of seeking care. Overall, 20.7% reported performing PFMT after the most recent delivery and 16.3% reported receiving PFMT instruction. Among women perceiving PFMT as important (51.6%), those who did not report performing it (35.8% overall) less often reported receiving instruction than those who did (6.4% vs 58.9%). Self-reported UI during pregnancy showed the strongest association with current UI (aPR 1.85, 95% CI 1.66-2.07). PFMT instruction was the most frequently selected support option (45.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this unweighted, non-probability Japanese online-panel sample, UI symptoms coexisted with limited healthcare contact; only a minority reported performing PFMT. The findings support prospective evaluation of accessible PFMT assessment and instruction but not population-level or causal inference.

articles.title: Expert consensus on the management of peripheral neuropathy in patients with lymphoma on brentuximab vedotin.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Brentuximab vedotin (BV) represents a therapeutic advancement in the treatment of CD30-positive lymphomas, yet its clinical utility is often limited by BV-induced peripheral neuropathy (PN). Currently, evidence-based, BV-specific guidelines for the assessment and management of PN are scarce, resulting in variability in clinical practice. This study aimed to establish international expert consensus on the optimal assessment, monitoring and management strategies for BV-induced PN in patients with lymphoma.

METHODS: A modified Delphi panel was conducted, engaging a total of 13 experts from eight different countries and representing haematology, neurology, dermatology, nursing and allied health disciplines. Panellists participated in three rounds of structured surveys, with statements developed based on a targeted literature review and guidance from an expert steering committee. Consensus was defined as ≥ 70% agreement/disagreement. Consensus was achieved on 60/87 (69%) statements across domains including risk factor assessment, symptom monitoring, pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical management.

RESULTS: Key recommendations include routine risk profiling before BV initiation, use of validated assessment tools at baseline and throughout therapy, multidisciplinary collaboration, and early intervention for worsening PN. Areas of uncertainty and variability in PN management remain, particularly regarding management of intermediate-grade PN and optimal non-pharmacological strategies.

CONCLUSION: These international consensus recommendations provide practical guidance for improving clinical management of BV-induced PN and highlight the importance of early identification, personalised care and multidisciplinary collaboration. Further research is needed to address persistent gaps and inform future clinical guidelines.

articles.title: Consensus Recommendations on the Diagnosis and Management of Noninflammatory and Inflammatory Nodules Secondary to Poly-L-Lactic Acid Injections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) is a widely used biostimulatory injectable for face and body rejuvenation. Although uncommon, nodule formation secondary to PLLA injection remains one of the most challenging complications of PLLA treatment. Inconsistent terminology and variable management approaches have resulted in uncertainty regarding diagnosis and treatment, leading to unpredictable outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to develop international expert consensus recommendations for the clinical classification, prevention, and management of PLLA-associated nodules.

METHODS: An international multidisciplinary panel of experienced aesthetic clinicians with expertise in PLLA treatment and complication management was convened to develop consensus recommendations for the classification, prevention, and management of PLLA-associated nodules based on the available literature and collective clinical experience.

RESULTS: The panel developed a practical clinical classification distinguishing noninflammatory and inflammatory nodules, together with recommendations for prevention, diagnosis, and management. A practical treatment algorithm was produced to support clinical decision making.

CONCLUSIONS: These international expert consensus recommendations provide clinicians with a pragmatic, simple-to-follow, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis, prevention, and management of PLLA-associated nodules in routine aesthetic practice.

articles.title: RAC1-YAP1-PIEZO1 signaling axis links intrauterine inflammation to uterine hypercontractility and preterm labor.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Our previous studies have demonstrated that the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 plays a critical role in regulating intracellular calcium levels and amplifying inflammation in uterine smooth muscle (USM) cells, thereby promoting USM contractility and preterm labor. However, the upstream regulatory mechanisms driving PIEZO1 expression during infection-induced preterm labor remain unclear. Here, we established an infection-induced preterm birth mouse model using intrauterine lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection and assessed USM contractility via ex vivo tension measurements. Western blotting and immunofluorescence were employed to assess the expression and cellular localization of PIEZO1, YAP1, and RAC1 in both uterine tissue and cultured USM cells. Pharmacological inhibitors (Verteporfin for YAP1 and NSC23766 for RAC1) and Rac1 siRNA were utilized to investigate the functional roles and regulatory relationships among these molecules. We found that LPS induced YAP1 dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation, which was inhibited by Verteporfin, reducing PIEZO1 expression and USM contractility, and prolonging gestation. Elevated RAC1 expression in LPS-treated tissues drove YAP1 nuclear translocation and PIEZO1 overexpression. Our findings suggest that RAC1 is involved in regulating YAP1 activation and nuclear localization, which is associated with increased PIEZO1 expression and uterine smooth muscle contractility. Thus, targeting the RAC1-YAP1-PIEZO1 axis might represent a novel strategy for preventing infection-induced preterm birth.

articles.title: Patterns of Stakeholder Participation in Advance Care Planning for Older Adults With Alzheimer's Disease in China: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine advance care planning (ACP) participation among older adults with Alzheimer's disease (AD), their family caregivers, and healthcare professionals in China, and to identify key influencing factors and challenges from a stakeholder perspective.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional survey guided by stakeholder theory. The study was reported in accordance with the The STROBE checklist.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from December 2024 to July 2025 in two tertiary hospitals and one social welfare center in Hangzhou, China. Convenience sampling was used to recruit healthcare professionals, older adults with early-stage AD, and family caregivers of AD patients. Structured questionnaires assessed ACP preparedness or participation. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: Healthcare professionals demonstrated high ACP knowledge and positive attitudes but low engagement in ACP-related behaviours. Older adults with early-stage AD showed moderate ACP preparedness, characterized by strong beliefs and motivation but relatively low attitudinal readiness. Family caregivers reported moderate-to-high ACP participation while experiencing substantial decision conflict. Stakeholder theory was used to interpret group differences in ACP preparedness, participation, and decision conflict. The findings reflect inherent disparities in decision-making power, accessible resources, and interest demands among patients, family caregivers, and healthcare professionals.

CONCLUSIONS: ACP participation in Chinese families affected by AD remains fragmented and structurally constrained. Although stakeholders recognize ACP's value, disparities in roles, resources, and power hinder patient-centered decision-making.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: This study provides references for the clinical implementation of Advance Care Planning (ACP) for dementia patients, the construction of multidisciplinary collaboration models, and the development of caregiver support strategies in the Chinese cultural context.

PATIENT AND PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Healthcare professionals, patients, and family members participated in data collection, providing comprehensive empirical evidence on ACP-related attitudes, behaviours, and decision conflicts for the study.

articles.title: Differentiating disseminated cryptococcosis from pulmonary cryptococcosis: Roles of clinical characteristics and cryptococcal antigen.
articles.abstract: AbstractDistinguishing disseminated cryptococcosis (DC) from localized pulmonary cryptococcosis (PC) is crucial due to divergent management and disparate prognoses. This study aimed to recognize associated factors for DC from PC in non-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) patients. Accordingly, 475 pathologically confirmed cryptococcosis cases (391 PC and 84 DC) were retrospectively reviewed over a 20-year period at a tertiary hospital in China. Clinical, radiographic, dynamic serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) titer profiles, treatment and prognosis were analyzed. Patients with DC were significantly associated with a history of glucocorticoid therapy (16.7% vs. 5.6%; P = 0.001) and autoimmune diseases (16.7% vs. 6.1%; P = 0.001) compared with PC, aggressive thoracic computed tomography findings, including patchy exudation (P = 0.001) and cavitation (P = 0.009), and markedly higher baseline median serum CrAg titers (1:1280 vs. 1:80, P < 0.001). By multivariable analysis, CNS symptoms (adjusted OR [aOR] 131.12, 95% CI 10.21-1683.9, P = 0.001), chronic liver disease (aOR 15.21, 95% CI 1.06-217.69, P = 0.045), and baseline serum CrAg ≥1:80 (aOR 13.51, 95% CI 1.39-131.07, P = 0.025) remained independently associated with DC. An initial CrAg titer ≥ 1:80 should prompt careful CNS evaluation and consideration of lumbar puncture. Patients with DC had significantly longer median CrAg clearance (P = 0.001) and antifungal duration (18 vs. 6 months), with higher mortality (9.5% vs. 1.0%; P < 0.001) compared to PC. Early risk-stratification is imperative to optimize interventions and improve survival.

articles.title: Timing of Insulin Glargine Administration During Intermittent Ramadan Fasting in patients With Type1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial (GLARIF).
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The effect of basal insulin timing on hypoglycemia during Ramadan fasting remains uncertain despite recommendations to administer basal insulin earlier in the evening. We evaluated whether early evening compared with bedtime administration of insulin glargine reduces hypoglycemia and improves glycemic outcomes in individuals with type1 diabetes (T1D) fasting during Ramadan.

METHODS: This multicenter open-label randomized controlled trial was conducted across 4 centers in Saudi Arabia. Participants with T1D intending to fast Ramadan were randomized to early evening or bedtime glargine administration. Glucose data were collected using self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG), intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring (FreeStyle Libre), and blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM; Medtronic iPro2).
