RESULTS: A total of 185 participants were analyzed (91 early evening, 94 bedtime). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Fasting interruption occurred in 75.9% versus 76.3% of participants (P = .94), with hypoglycemia accounting for >90% of interruptions in both groups. Hypoglycemia occurred predominantly during the morning period regardless of basal insulin timing. Severe hypoglycemia was reported in 2 versus 5 participants, and 1 diabetic ketoacidosis admission occurred in each group. Continuous glucose monitoring-derived glycemic metrics were similar between groups. Time in range (70-180 mg/dL) was 44.6% versus 46.1% (P = .70), time below range (<70 mg/dL) was 7.9% versus 6.4% (P = .35), and time above range (>180 mg/dL) was 47.5% in both groups (P = .99). Self-monitoring of blood glucose-detected hypoglycemic episodes and CGM-detected low glucose excursions were also comparable. Area under the curve below range was higher in the early evening group (P = .04).

CONCLUSION: Changing insulin glargine administration from bedtime to earlier evening hours during Ramadan fasting did not significantly reduce hypoglycemia or improve overall glucose profiles in individuals with T1D. These findings suggest that routine universal shifting of basal insulin timing during Ramadan may not be necessary and support an individualized approach based on patient preference and glucose patterns.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov identifier: NCT04383990.

articles.title: Navigating Difficult Conversations: Factors Influencing Paediatric Nurses' Bad News Delivery and Their Professional Coping Responses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breaking bad news (BBN) is a cognitively and emotionally demanding communication task for paediatric nurses, yet empirical evidence on its determinants remains scarce. This study aimed to assess the current status of BBN competence and identify demographic, professional, and training-related factors associated with this competence among paediatric nurses.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 382 paediatric nurses using a Breaking Bad News Ability Scale. The scale demonstrated good psychometric properties (Cronbach's α = 0.91; test-retest reliability = 0.85; S-CVI/Ave = 0.94). The instrument comprises five dimensions: pre-disclosure preparation, communication strategy, empathic response, child/family specificity, and communication/self-reflection. The study was designed and reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement. Univariate analysis, Pearson's correlation, and multiple linear regression were performed.

RESULTS: Total scores range from 20 to 100; each of the five dimensions ranges from 4 to 20. Higher scores indicate greater competence. The mean total score was 69.0 ± 6.3, indicating a moderate level of ability. Empathic response scored highest (14.2 ± 2.0), whereas pre-disclosure preparation (13.5 ± 2.2) and child/family specificity (13.6 ± 2.2) were the lowest-performing dimensions. Univariate analysis revealed significant differences by age, educational attainment, professional title, years of paediatric nursing experience, communication training within the preceding 6 months, and clinical department (all p < 0.01). Recent communication training demonstrated the strongest positive correlation (r = 0.419, p < 0.001), followed by years of experience (r = 0.392) and professional title (r = 0.376). Multiple linear regression (R2 = 0.394, p < 0.001) identified recent training (b = 2.09, p < 0.001), professional title (b = 1.20, p = 0.002), years of experience (b = 0.29, p = 0.007), and age (b = 0.15, p = 0.013) as independent positive predictors.

CONCLUSION: Paediatric nurses demonstrated moderate BBN competence, with notable deficiencies in pre-disclosure preparation and family-specific tailoring.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Communication training within the preceding 6 months emerged as the strongest modifiable predictor. Nurses in intensive care settings, despite frequent exposure to high-stakes disclosures, warrant targeted competency development.

articles.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligent Scribes in Oncology: Impact on Clinician Experience and Documentation Burden.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes, widely implemented to reduce clinician burden and dissatisfaction, are not optimized for oncology. We evaluated this technology at-scale at a high-volume cancer center.

METHODS: This prospective mixed-methods study used surveys, electronic health record (EHR), and utilization data to assess adoption, burden, and satisfaction with an ambient AI scribe that was implemented from June to September 2025. Descriptive statistics categorized clinicians as adopters (3+ weeks of use), attempted adopters (1-2 weeks), and never-users (0 weeks). Generalized estimating equations assessed the adoption's effect on the likelihood of closing notes on visit days and pajama time. Pre- and postimplementation surveys obtained clinicians' insights into satisfaction and documentation burden.

RESULTS: In all, 190 (19.8%) of 958 clinicians used the tool, most often with new, video, and in-person visits. Adopters (n = 124) and attempted adopters (n = 66) were more commonly physicians from medicine and surgery. Pre- to post-rollout, the likelihood of closing notes on visit days remained unchanged among never-users (70% v 70%) and decreased among attempted adopters (73% v 70%) and adopters (56% v 54%). Pajama time remained unchanged among attempted adopters (50.6 v 50.1 minutes per week) and decreased among never-users (69.5 v 62.2) and adopters (86.9 v 81.4). Clinicians completing both pre- and postrollout surveys (n = 45) showed a decrease in high/excessive note-writing time (78% v 60%; P = .043). Postrollout surveys (n = 77) showed largely positive experiences, with 73% reporting they would recommend the tool to colleagues.

CONCLUSION: This study of an ambient AI scribe at-scale showed positive satisfaction but mixed burden outcomes among oncology clinicians. Notably, despite enterprise-wide implementation and training, adoption was low and varied by clinician and visit characteristics. Future research should explore adoption barriers and tool optimization to support oncology documentation workflows.

articles.title: Effect of Glutathione S-Transferase and Metallothionein Polymorphisms on Mercury Levels and End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) in Colombian Patients.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological studies have demonstrated a link between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and environmental mercury (Hg) exposure. Colombia has a well-documented history of artisanal and small-scale gold mining, where Hg exposure affects miners and nearby riverside and urban populations. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of polymorphisms in GSTM1, GSTT1, MT1A (rs8052394), and MT2A (rs10636) on Hg levels and their relationship with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in a Colombian urban population. We conducted a cross-sectional, multicenter exploratory study on 401 CKD patients to assess the impact of polymorphisms on total Hg (tHg) levels in blood and hair, and their relationship with ESRD. Patients were divided into two groups: Group 1 (G1) with patients in Stages 1-4 CKD, and Group 2 (G2) with patients in Stage 5 CKD. Unexpectedly, tHg levels were low in our population (GM (SD) = 0.69 (2.07) and 0.73 (2.18) μg/L in blood, and GM (SD) = 0.22 (3.80) and 0.18 (2.9) μg/g in hair for G1 and G2, respectively). We found that low hair tHg levels were significantly associated with null GSTT1, double null GSTM1/GSTT1, and MT1A (rs8052394) GG genotype in G1, and high tHg with the null GSTM1 genotype in G2 patients. Furthermore, when pooling G1 and G2, the double-null genotype of GSTM1/GSTT1, as well as MT1A (rs8052394) AA and MT2A (rs10636) GC, were more prevalent among patients with hair and blood tHg levels exceeding 1 μg/g and 5 μg/L, respectively. Patients carrying the MT1A (rs8052394) AG genotype exhibited an increased risk of ESRD. In conclusion, our findings suggest that, even in a population with low Hg exposure, polymorphisms in glutathione S-transferases and metallothioneins showed stage-specific associations with hair tHg levels, and that MT1A may contribute to ESRD risk.

articles.title: Why We Must Prioritise Periodontal Disease in National Healthcare Policy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontal disease is a prevalent chronic inflammatory condition with consequences that extend beyond oral health. Despite strong evidence linking it to systemic diseases, mental health outcomes, and economic burden, it remains under-prioritised in public health policy.

AIM: This opinion piece aims to highlight the broader health and economic implications of periodontal disease and to highlight the need to prioritise it within healthcare policy and integrated care frameworks.

DISCUSSION: Emerging evidence highlights significant associations between periodontal disease and systemic conditions, including diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Beyond physical health, periodontal disease also contributes to psychosocial challenges such as reduced self-esteem, with potential links to cognitive decline. From an economic perspective, untreated periodontal disease imposes substantial direct and indirect costs on healthcare systems, particularly the NHS, due to increased demand for emergency care, need for advanced dental treatments, and complex care management needs. Preventative care and early intervention are cost-effective strategies to reduce health inequalities that also address the links between oral and systemic health.

CONCLUSION: Periodontal disease represents an important yet overlooked public health issue. Prioritising prevention, integrating oral health into general health care, and increasing public awareness are essential to improve population health outcomes. This article calls for urgent policy action to recognise periodontal health as integral to overall health and healthcare delivery.

articles.title: Structural determinants of communicable disease risk in asylum reception centres.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With over 120 million people forcibly displaced globally, asylum reception systems represent critical epidemiological interfaces. This synthesis is not confined to a single geographic region: evidence was drawn from reception systems across high-income host countries in Europe and, where available, comparable settings elsewhere, reflecting the substantial heterogeneity of reception models worldwide. Within a One Health framework, these socio-spatial environments shape communicable disease dynamics through accommodation density, sanitation capacity, and governance continuity.

AREAS COVERED: Synthesizing evidence from 2015-2026, we examine transmission patterns of respiratory infections, fecal-oral diseases, ectoparasitic and dermatological conditions, tuberculosis, and vaccine-preventable diseases in reception infrastructures. Outbreaks cluster around occupancy density, ventilation constraints, sanitation integrity, mobility, and discontinuity of care. Transmission dynamics are structurally produced by interactions between built environments, organizational processes, and health system integration.

EXPERT OPINION: Reception systems are conditionally amplifying environments: outbreak magnitude depends on spatial configuration, occupancy governance, surveillance interoperability, and clinical continuity. Reframing centers as epidemiological infrastructures enables a shift from reactive containment to structural calibration. Modular design, density thresholds, and integrated preventive-clinical pathways enhance epidemiological predictability and reduce transmission risk. Amplification is not intrinsic to populations but to the environments accommodating them, with implications for broader collective housing and public health system design.

articles.title: Association between female genital mutilation and sexually transmitted infection in sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from interpretable weighted machine learning.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) impose a heavy public health burden on low- and middle-income countries. We aimed to examine the association between female genital mutilation (FGM) and STI and develop an interpretable machine learning framework for STI identification among women in Sub-Saharan Africa.

METHODS: We analyzed Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) data from 57 548 women aged 15-49 years across 10 Sub-Saharan African countries. Eighteen prespecified sociodemographic, behavioral, health-related, symptom, and cultural features were included. Data from nine countries were used for model development and internal validation, while Sierra Leone was reserved for independent external validation. Weighted logistic regression, elastic net, random forest, and XGBoost incorporated individual-level DHS sampling weights, with hyperparameters tuned using fivefold cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used for model interpretation, and survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression quantified adjusted associations.

RESULTS: A total of 4144 women had STIs. The selected weighted random forest model showed good discrimination in both the internal validation set (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] = 0.863) and the independent external validation set (AUROC = 0.878). SHAP analysis identified history of abnormal genital discharge, history of genital sores, and FGM as the leading contributors to STI identification. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression showed that women with FGM had 82.7% higher odds of STI than those without FGM (adjusted odds ratio 1.827, 95% confidence interval 1.630, 2.049).

CONCLUSION: Female genital mutilation and genital symptom histories were associated with STI. Combining sociodemographic, behavioral, and symptom information might improve STI identification and highlight the sexual and reproductive health relevance of FGM in high-burden settings.

articles.title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

articles.title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification).

RESULTS: Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012).

SIGNIFICANCE: MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

articles.title: Impact of Insurance Type on Timing of Diagnosis and Surgical Treatment of Acute Achilles Tendon Ruptures: A 2-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Introduction/PurposeDelayed treatment of acute Achilles tendon rupture is associated with worse outcomes and higher complication rates. Prior studies suggest reduced access to care among Medicaid and uninsured patients. This study examines the effect of insurance status on the timing of diagnosis and surgical treatment among patients undergoing surgical repair of acute Achilles tendon rupture.MethodsA retrospective chart review was conducted of patients aged ≥18 years with acute traumatic Achilles tendon ruptures identified by Current Procedural Terminology codes 27650 and 27654 at 2 hospitals between January 2017 and December 2023. Dates of injury, emergency department presentation, initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation, and surgical intervention were recorded. Only patients who ultimately underwent operative repair were eligible for inclusion; because case ascertainment relied on surgical procedure codes, the cohort does not capture patients managed nonoperatively or those who never reached surgical care. Insurance status was categorized as private or Medicaid/uninsured. Postoperative complications, including re-rupture, infection, venous thromboembolism, wound dehiscence, return to the operating room, and mortality, were documented. Between-group comparisons of continuous variables were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, given non-normal distribution of the underlying data; independent 2-tailed t-tests were performed as a secondary, confirmatory analysis. Significance was set at P < .05.ResultsThirty-eight surgically treated patients met the inclusion criteria, including 23 with private insurance and 15 who were Medicaid or uninsured. Median age was 35.2 years, and 89.5% were male. All time intervals are reported as medians. Time from injury to emergency department presentation was longer in the Medicaid/uninsured group but not statistically significant (1.0 vs 0.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .079). Medicaid/uninsured patients experienced significantly longer delays from injury to initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation (17.0 vs 4.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .024) and from injury to surgery (30.0 vs 10.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .045). Time from orthopaedic evaluation to surgery did not differ significantly between groups (11.0 vs 6.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .206). Postoperative complications were infrequent in both groups; the study was not powered for comparison of complication rates and none was performed.ConclusionAmong surgically treated patients, those with Medicaid or no insurance experienced significantly longer delays to initial orthopaedic evaluation and to surgical repair compared with privately insured patients, highlighting disparities in access to timely orthopaedic care within this surgically treated population.Level of Evidence:III.

articles.title: Revitalization Treatment in Endodontics: A State-Of-The-Art Review.
articles.abstract: Ten years after the European Society of Endodontology (ESE) issued its inaugural Position Statement in 2016, revitalization (BrE: revitalisation) treatment has progressed from an experimental approach to a cornerstone of contemporary endodontic practice. This state-of-the-art review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the biological and clinical advances that have redefined the treatment options for permanent teeth with incomplete root formation after loss of pulp vitality, as well as broader applications beyond these cases. The review refines case selection by integrating biological potential with clinical aetiology and extended applications for revitalization, while evaluating the role of modern diagnostic and operative aids in enhancing procedural precision. It details technical protocols ranging from evidence-based irrigation to the precise placement of barriers and definitive restorations, ensuring a seamless transition from disinfection to long-term structural stability. Beyond methodological refinements, there is growing awareness of prognosis in relation to specific case constellations, accompanied by clearer articulation of realistic treatment aims. These aims prioritize the absence of signs and symptoms of infection and long-term tooth survival, while increasingly emphasizing patient-centred outcomes. Furthermore, the review explores the practical intersection of revitalization and orthodontic management and presents a proactive framework for early recognition and management of complications and procedural failures. By delineating these clinical boundaries, it offers a contemporary basis for clinical decision-making and supports the upcoming update of the ESE Position Statement.

articles.title: Dapagliflozin in phenotypically stratified HFpEF without myocardial fibrosis: the STADIA-HFpEF randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction(HFpEF) is characterized by increased diastolic left ventricular(LV) stiffness resulting from variable contributions of myocardial extracellular matrix(ECM) remodeling and titin-based cardiomyocyte stiffness. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors(SGLT2i) improved cardiomyocyte distensibility, inflammation, and oxidative stress in experimental and human HFpEF myocardium. We investigated whether dapagliflozin improves LV distensibility in phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis.

METHODS: STADIA-HFpEF was a 34-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. HFpEF patients underwent multi-level phenotypic stratification including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to exclude structural cardiomyopathies and significant myocardial ECM remodeling. Participants were randomized to dapagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for two 13-week treatment periods separated by an 8-week washout.The co-primary endpoints were changes in E/e'/LV end-diastolic volume index(LVEDVi) and mean LV e', reflecting LV distensibility and relaxation. Secondary endpoints included echocardiographic variables, quality of life, 6-minute walk distance, and inflammatory biomarkers.

RESULTS: Between February 2020 and October 2022, 32 patients were randomized and 29 completed the study protocol. Median age was 73(68-76) years including 28 women(88%). Dapagliflozin did not significantly modify E/e'/LVEDVi compared with placebo 0.24 (0.20-0.32) to 0.26 (0.22-0.34) vs. 0.23 (0.22-0.29) to 0.25 (0.21-0.31); p=0.370 nor did it change mean LV e' 6.2 (5.6-7.5) to 6.2 (5.7-7.1) vs. 6.6 (5.6-7.4) to 6.7 (5.4-7.5); p=0.448. Most secondary outcomes were neutral. However, an isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed during dapagliflozin treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: In phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis, dapagliflozin did not improve LV distensibility or relaxation. An isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed; however, these exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Methodological considerations in interpreting serum galectin-3 as a predictor of incident type 2 diabetes.
Epstein-Barr Virus Association and Prognosis in Taiwanese Hodgkin Lymphoma: A Nationwide Multicenter Study With Comparison to United States Whites.
articles.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in a subset of cases. We previously showed that the incidence of HL in Taiwan increased ~2.5-fold between 2001 and 2020, particularly among young women with the nodular sclerosis (NS) subtype. In this nationwide multicenter study, we evaluated EBV status in HL to determine its impact on clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. We found that the proportion of EBV-associated HL in Taiwan declined over the past two decades, from 39% to 27%. EBV-positive frequency exhibited a bimodal age distribution, peaking in children < 10 years (63%) and adults > 70 years (80%), with the lowest frequency in patients 20-29 years (11%). Compared with EBV-negative patients, EBV-positive patients were older (53.5 vs. 32.9 years; p < 0.001), predominantly male (73.1% vs. 48.7%; p < 0.001), more likely to have nodal disease (83.3% vs. 74.2%; p = 0.003) and mixed cellularity histology (37.1% vs. 11.4%; p < 0.001), and had inferior 10-year survival (56.3% vs. 85.7%; p < 0.001). Adverse prognostic factors in HL included older age (> 60 years), B symptoms, non-NS histology, EBV-positivity, advanced-stage disease (Stage III-IV), and a high International Prognostic Score (IPS, 4-7). On multivariate analysis, older age and a high IPS retained prognostic significance. Large registry datasets from Taiwan and the US further demonstrated that survival outcomes have improved over the past two decades. Female patients and those with the NS and nodular lymphocyte-predominant subtypes had significantly better survival. These findings provide insight into the biological impact of EBV in HL and help inform strategies for disease prevention and management.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease-Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (MAFLD-CKM): A Modified Framework to Predict Long-Term Mortality.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reframes cardio-renal-metabolic risk but omits hepatic dysfunction, particularly metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). This study assesses whether integrating MAFLD into the CKM framework improves mortality risk discrimination compared with the original CKM framework. MATERIAL AND METHODS We used data of 10 335 adults aged 20 to 74 years from the third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) with mortality follow-up through 2019. CKM was classified based on the American Heart Association framework, and MAFLD was identified based on hepatic steatosis and metabolic dysfunction according to established criteria. A modified CKM score was proposed, incorporating MAFLD into CKM staging. We compared the association of each staging system with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality using Cox regression. RESULTS While both staging systems are significantly associated with mortality, the proposed modified CKM staging showed superior risk stratification than the original definition, particularly in stage 3. The modified CKM system showed a notably higher hazard ratio than the original CKM system in all-cause mortality (3.84, 95% CI: 3.38-4.37 vs 3.49, 95% CI: 3.07-3.95) and CVD-related mortality (6.38, 95% CI: 4.80-8.48 vs 5.41, 95% CI: 4.12-7.12). CONCLUSIONS Integrating MAFLD into the CKM framework (modified CKM) provided an incremental improvement in prognostic discrimination for allcause and cardiovascular mortality, with stronger risk stratification observed in stage 3, highlighting the key role of the liver in the cardio-renal-metabolic axis. These findings underscore the need for a broader, multi-organ approach to provide incremental refinement for defining and managing metabolic risk.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Moderate Secondary Mitral Regurgitation After Optimized Medical Therapy in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of moderate secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) after optimized guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 2,468 ambulatory HF patients with paired transthoracic echocardiography at baseline and after 12 months of optimized GDMT. The primary composite was all-cause death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality and recurrent HFHs.

RESULTS: Mean age was 66.2 ± 12.5 years, 70.6% were male, and mean baseline LVEF was 36.1% ± 13.6%. At 12 months, 80.5% of patients had no/mild MR, 15.6% had moderate MR, and 3.9% had severe MR. During a median 6.9-year follow-up, 1,240 patients experienced the primary endpoint. Compared with no/mild MR, both moderate and severe MR at 12 months were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint (moderate: hazard ratio [HR] 1.69, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-1.95; severe: HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.44-2.29; both p<0.001). Moderate MR was also independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.32-1.79; p<0.001) and recurrent HFHs (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 2.17, 95% CI 1.81-2.60). HFH rates were 9.03, 20.0, and 26.1 per 100 person-years in patients with no/mild, moderate, and severe MR, respectively. Among patients with moderate MR at 12 months, outcomes did not differ according to baseline MR severity.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large-scale study, residual moderate secondary MR after 12 months of optimized GDMT was common and was independently associated with increased long-term mortality and HFHs.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of NT-proBNP thresholds in Dyspneic Patients in the Emergency Department according to patients' characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concentrations of N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is central to acute heart failure (AHF) diagnosis in dyspneic emergency departments (ED) patients, but optimal thresholds remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of various NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF, across the general population and these key subgroups.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including studies published up to August 28, 2025, that reported the diagnostic performance of NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF in dyspneic ED patients.

RESULTS: The analysis included 31 studies comprising 26,948 patients. To exclude AHF, a fixed threshold of ≤300 ng/L yielded an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.73 (0.69-0.77), with high sensitivity of 97.9% (96.9-98.5) and lower specificity of 46.2% (36.4-56.2); the negative predictive value of this threshold was 97.0% (96.5-97.4). Age-dependent thresholds (≥450 ng/L for patients aged <50 years, ≥900 ng/L for those aged 50-75 years, and ≥1,800 ng/L for those aged ≥75 years), evaluated in 14,410 patients, achieved an AUC of 0.84 (0.83-0.85) with a more favorable balance between sensitivity of 85.9% (85.0-86.7) and specificity of 82.0% (81.2-82.9). In patients with CKD (N=2,271), all fixed thresholds yielded AUC <0.80; age-dependent thresholds showed an AUC of 0.77 (0.75-0.78) with specificity of 62.6% (59.4-65.7). In patients with obesity (body mass index ≥30), only age-dependent thresholds were assessed, in 3,562 patients; AUC was 0.82 (0.81-0.84) and sensitivity was 81.2% (79.2-83.1), broadly comparable to the overall population.

CONCLUSION: A threshold ≤300 ng/L provides excellent rule-out performance for AHF, while age-dependent NT-proBNP thresholds offer superior diagnostic performance for ruling in AHF in the ED compared to fixed thresholds, and demonstrate consistent accuracy across subgroups. However, evidence in patients with CKD and obesity remains limited, both in terms of sample size and the range of thresholds evaluated.

articles.title: Exploring gut microbiome dysbiosis in vasculitis in adults: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Although studies have confirmed that disruptions in the gut microbiota (dysbiosis) contribute to the development of autoimmune disorders, the precise pathways through which the gut microbiota influences the onset and progression of vasculitis remain largely unknown. In recent years, research has increasingly concentrated on assessing the contribution of the gut microbiota to vasculitis. This systematic study sought to assess the dominant gut microbiota profiles in vasculitis patients and compare them to those of healthy individuals.

METHODS: The Cochrane methodology was used to design and conduct the present systematic review. Relevant articles published up to May 2025 were searched and collected from four electronic databases: PubMed, Scopus, Medline, and Web of Science. The keywords used in the search included "vasculitis," "Takayasu arteritis," "giant cell arteritis," "polyarteritis nodosa," "microscopic polyangiitis," "granulomatosis with polyangiitis," "eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis," "cryoglobulinemic vasculitis," "IgA vasculitis," "variable vessel vasculitis," "Behçet's disease," and "Cogan's syndrome" alongside phrases like "gut microbiome," "gut microbiota," and "gut flora."

RESULTS: Overall, 12 publications were included in the analysis. Three addressed individuals with Takayasu arteritis (TAK), three investigated ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), another three examined Behçet's disease (BD), while one study each pertained to IgA vasculitis (IgAV), Kawasaki disease (KD), and a nonspecific form of vasculitis. The majority of these works observed variations in both α-diversity and β-diversity, as well as in the diversity and richness of the gut microbiota. Additionally, the structure of the microbial communities differed markedly between those with vasculitis and healthy individuals. Notably, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria-the dominant bacterial phyla in the human gastrointestinal tract-were frequently diminished in affected patients.

CONCLUSION: The occurrence of intestinal microbial imbalance in individuals diagnosed with vasculitis has been validated. As observed in various other autoimmune conditions, the gut microbiota of vasculitis patients is chiefly comprised Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Disruptions in the microbial ecosystem-mainly typified by diminished diversity and population density-may play a role in triggering and advancing the disease.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: This review was not registered.

articles.title: Divergent approaches to rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: a comparative analysis of international clinical practice guidelines.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We compared international and regional clinical practice guidelines to identify agreement, differences, and gaps in RA-ILD care. We conducted a narrative comparative review of five guideline groups: ERS/EULAR, ACR/CHEST, EULAR, PANLAR, and ALAT. Recommendations were assessed across screening, diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment, together with their methodological approaches. Diagnostic recommendations showed the greatest agreement: ILD-focused guidelines emphasized high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), pulmonary function tests, and multidisciplinary evaluation. Screening recommendations differed: ERS/EULAR and ACR/CHEST favored risk-based assessment, whereas ALAT proposed a broader approach that included lung ultrasound as an adjunct, without replacing HRCT. For established RA-ILD, ACR/CHEST suggested, as implementation guidance, pulmonary function testing every 3-12 months during the first year and HRCT when clinically indicated; ERS/EULAR proposed pulmonary function testing every 3-6 months in the first years and periodic HRCT. Treatment showed the greatest divergence. ACR/CHEST conditionally recommended mycophenolate, rituximab, azathioprine, and cyclophosphamide as first-line ILD therapies, whereas ALAT emphasized integrated control of articular and pulmonary disease, particularly with abatacept or rituximab. EULAR and PANLAR primarily addressed RA treatment and did not provide dedicated RA-ILD algorithms. Antifibrotic treatment was considered mainly in progressive fibrosing disease. Guidelines converge on HRCT-based evaluation but differ in screening, monitoring intervals, and treatment priorities. These differences reflect their scope, methodology, and limited RA-ILD-specific evidence. Prospective comparative studies are needed to inform more consistent care.

articles.title: A genome-wide association study of cognitive impairment in a Chinese cohort of 1,040 individuals.
articles.abstract: While genetic heritability plays a major role in the development of cognitive impairment, most genetic risk factors are identified from studies of European populations. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) on cognitive impairment in the Chinese population by sequencing 1,040 matched case-control individuals from a longitudinal cohort of Zhejiang Province, China. We detected 19 SNPs clustered in 15 genomic loci reaching suggestive significance (P < 1 × 10- 5). Eleven of these genomic loci are newly associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) or cognitive impairment, among which five (GRP39, FAT1, EDIL3, ZNF596, and PDGFD) show nominal evidence of replication in both external GWAS of AD in East-Asian populations and summary statistics of AD in diverse populations. The detected loci are implicated in micronutrient homeostasis including zinc (GPR39), iron (STEAP1), potassium (KCNJ6), and vitamin K (VKORC1L1), cell connections (EVPLL) through cadherin regulations (PCDH18, FAT1), regulating amyloid-beta precursor protein (APP) (EDIL3), formation of amyloid-β (EDEM1) and neurofibrillary tangles (PDGFD, ZNF596), neuronal growth (NEGR1), and phosphatase regulations (SETBP1, TPTE). This study presents a robust GWAS for cognitive impairment in the Chinese population and highlights a promising set of therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative disorder.

articles.title: Impact of matched samples on domain harmonization in cross-cohort NMR metabolomics.
articles.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Machine learning models trained on metabolomics data frequently show reduced performance when applied to independent cohorts because of domain shifts introduced by differences in analytical platforms, sample handling, storage conditions, and metabolite quantification procedures. Robust approaches for harmonizing metabolomics datasets across cohorts are therefore needed to improve model transferability and reproducibility.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of matched samples on domain harmonization and cross-cohort prediction performance in NMR metabolomics data, and to compare multiple harmonization strategies for improving model generalization across independently acquired datasets.

METHODS: A machine-learning framework was developed to classify ICD-10 code I50.9 (unspecified heart failure) using plasma NMR metabolomics data from the Estonian Biobank. Models were trained on a source dataset comprising 12,000 samples measured at Nightingale Health and evaluated on an independently measured destination dataset of 295 samples acquired on a different NMR platform. Harmonization approaches included within-domain normalization, Optimal Transport, Bridge mapping, and Empirical Bayes correction. The effect of matched samples was assessed using up to 108 duplicated biospecimens measured in both datasets. Additional validation was performed using independently generated human gestational diabetes and mouse diabetes metabolomics datasets from Metabolomics Workbench.

RESULTS: Domain harmonization generally improved cross-cohort prediction compared with unaligned data, particularly when matched samples were available. Predictive performance increased as the number of matched samples used for calibration increased, although gains varied across methods. Nevertheless, simple within-domain normalization consistently provided strong performance and often matched or exceeded more complex alignment approaches. External validation using fully unmatched human and mouse metabolomics datasets demonstrated that harmonization strategies improved classification performance relative to raw data, supporting the broader applicability of the framework.

CONCLUSION: Matched samples substantially enhance domain harmonization and improve the transferability of metabolomics prediction models across analytical platforms and cohorts. However, robust normalization remains a strong baseline, and the benefits of more sophisticated alignment methods depend on the availability and representativeness of matched reference samples. These findings provide practical guidance for developing reproducible cross-cohort metabolomics machine-learning models while preserving biologically relevant signals.

articles.title: Gene-based association analysis of depression risk among European ancestry Parkinson's disease patients.
articles.abstract: Depression is one of the most common and disabling non-motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its genetic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the genetic contributions to depression in PD by estimating the burden from common as well as low-frequency single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within genes previously implicated in PD or depression risk among European ancestry PD patients from three population-based studies. Using gene-based association analyses (SKAT, Burden, and SKAT-O) in the PASIDA, PEG, and PPMI studies, we evaluated SNP sets in gene regions previously linked to PD or depression. Among PD-related genes, meta-analysis identified a significant association between KRTCAP2 and self-reported depression diagnosis in PD (SKAT-O p = 4.33 × 10⁻⁵), which remained significant after false discovery rate correction. A higher genetic burden in KRTCAP2 was associated with 20% increased odds of depression (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04-1.38). TRAF5 and LRRK2 showed marginal associations. Among depression-related genes, SPPL3 and ERBB4 were associated with depression diagnosis history, and FNIP2 was associated with current depressive symptoms. The PD polygenic risk score was not associated with depression in PD, while a higher depression polygenic risk score was significantly associated with increased odds of depression diagnosis in both cohorts and the meta-analysis (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.13-1.40). Our findings highlight immune-related genes such as KRTCAP2 and TRAF5 as potential contributors to depression in PD. Additionally, the depression PRS shows statistically significant association with depression diagnosis in PD, suggesting that a general depression-related genetic liability contributes to this non-motor feature in PD. Together, these results suggest that depression in PD may involve both shared and disease-specific genetic mechanisms, offering new insights into its pathogenesis and potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.

METHODOLOGY: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

RESULTS: Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased.

CONCLUSIONS: Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

articles.title: Changes in biventricular myocardial function after six months of ixekizumab therapy in patients with psoriatic arthritis: a prospective speckle-tracking echocardiographic study.
articles.abstract: To evaluate longitudinal changes in conventional and speckle-tracking echocardiographic indices in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) who achieved a disease activity index for psoriatic arthritis (DAPSA)-defined clinical response during ixekizumab therapy.In this prospective single-centre observational cohort, 21 adults with PsA underwent clinical, laboratory and transthoracic echocardiographic assessment before ixekizumab initiation and after 6 months of treatment. The principal echocardiographic outcome was the within-patient change in absolute left vetricle global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) between baseline and 6 months. Secondary echocardiographic outcomes included right ventricle (RV) GLS, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (RV S') and tricuspid E to E' ratio (E/E'), while clinical secondary outcomes included DAPSA, body surface area (BSA), minimal disease activity (MDA), C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Mean age was 49.6 ± 11.6 years, 57.1% were male and 11 patients (52.4%) were biologic-naïve. MDA was achieved by 17 patients (81.0%). DAPSA decreased from 28.9 ± 4.3 to 7.7 ± 4.2, accompanied by reductions in CRP and ESR (all p < 0.001). Absolute LV GLS increased from 18.5 ± 1.3% to 20.5 ± 1.9% (mean change 2.0%, 95% CI 1.49-2.51; p < 0.001), while absolute RV GLS increased from 21.5 ± 3.3% to 25.8 ± 4.2% (mean change 4.29%, 95% CI 3.37-5.20; p < 0.001). LVEF, TAPSE, RV S' and E/E' also improved significantly. Although DAPSA reduction correlated with increased LVEF, while BSA reduction with increased LV GLS and TAPSE, these associations were exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously. Among patients with PsA who achieved clinical response to ixekizumab, 6 months of treatment was accompanied by improvements in left- and right-ventricular functional indices. Because the cohort was small, responder-enriched and lacked a comparator group, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

articles.title: Tocilizumab for active rheumatoid arthritis in a patient with concomitant primary biliary cholangitis: a case based review.
articles.abstract: The coexistence of active rheumatoid arthritis and active primary biliary cholangitis represents a distinct therapeutic challenge. Evidence-based guidance for treatment selection in this clinical setting remains limited, and published experience with tocilizumab is restricted to isolated case reports. We report a 59-year-old woman with highly active, seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and marked cholestatic biochemical activity, in whom diagnostic evaluation revealed active primary biliary cholangitis in the absence of advanced liver fibrosis. Following multidisciplinary assessment, methotrexate and leflunomide were avoided because of active cholestatic liver disease, and treatment with subcutaneous tocilizumab was initiated in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid and fenofibrate. Tocilizumab was well tolerated and led to a progressive improvement in arthritis. In parallel, cholestatic liver parameters showed sustained improvement in the absence of hepatic adverse effects. To contextualize this observation, we performed a focused literature review and identified only two directly relevant case reports, both reporting favorable rheumatologic and hepatic outcomes during tocilizumab therapy. This case adds to the limited body of evidence suggesting that tocilizumab may represent a feasible therapeutic option for selected patients with active rheumatoid arthritis and concomitant primary biliary cholangitis.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of hyaluronic acid spray and low-level laser therapy on wound healing following gingivectomy: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Gingivectomy wounds heal by secondary intention, prolonging recovery and postoperative discomfort; this randomized controlled trial compared low-level laser therapy and hyaluronic acid spray for early wound healing and postoperative pain after gingivectomy. Systemically healthy patients requiring gingivectomy were randomly allocated to receive either LLLT (940 nm diode laser, 3 W, 128.4 J/cm2, applied on days 0, 3, 5, and 7) or 0.04% high-molecular-weight HA spray (applied twice daily for 7 days). Wound epithelialization was quantified through Mira-2-Ton plaque-disclosing staining combined with digital planimetric analysis (ImageJ) at baseline and on postoperative days 3, 7, and 14. Secondary outcomes included gingival index (GI), full-mouth bleeding score (FMBS), probing pocket depth (PPD), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores. A total of 64 participants were enrolled and randomized (n = 32 per group). Both groups exhibited significant wound area reduction over time (p < 0.001). However, the HA spray group demonstrated significantly higher wound epithelialization percentages (percentage reduction from baseline in the non-epithelialized, disclosing-solution-stained wound surface area) than the LLLT group on days 3 (p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.39), 7 (p < 0.001; d = 1.12), and 14 (p = 0.044; d = 0.73). The HA spray group also reported significantly lower VAS pain scores on days 1 and 3 (p < 0.05). Periodontal parameters improved significantly from baseline to week 6 in both groups (all p < 0.001), with no significant between-group differences at week 6 for GI (p = 0.999), FMBS (p = 0.843), or PPD (p = 0.718). HA spray yielded significantly accelerated re-epithelialization and superior early pain reduction compared to LLLT following gingivectomy, suggesting it may serve as a practical, patient-friendly adjunctive alternative to laser biostimulation in postoperative wound management. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Number: NCT07034625.

articles.title: Beyond the Gradient: Patient-Reported Outcomes with Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Cellular consequences of non-ablative radiotherapy, a novel approach to ventricular tachycardias.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiotherapy (RT) with a single application of ionizing radiation (STAR) has been suggested as a non-invasive alternative to radiofrequency in ablating ventricular tachycardia (VT). Emerging data reveal that STAR may suppress VT without substrate destruction, by enhancing impulse conduction instead, through increased expression of NaV1.5 channels and connexin 43. The study aims to investigate electrophysiology and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics in cardiomyocytes (CMs) from mice subjected to in-vivo RT. The emerging data led us to evaluate biochemical changes potentially linking electrophysiological response to ionizing irradiation.

METHODS: CMs isolated 2 weeks after RT with low-dose (15 Gy) or high-dose (25 Gy) were compared to those of sham-treated mice (CTRL). We evaluated: i) the properties of the transient (INaT) and sustained (INasus) components of INa; ii) AP parameters, including the prevalence of Early After-Depolarizations (EADs); iii) intracellular Ca2+ dynamics; iv) CaMKII phosphorylation and v) ROS content.

RESULTS: 25 Gy RT i) increased INaT and, to a larger extent, INasus (increased INasus/INaT ratio); ii) increased AP amplitude, +dV/dtMAX and duration (APD) and facilitated EADs; iii) depressed intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. 15 Gy RT had similar but smaller effects (dose-dependency). 25 Gy RT reduced CaMKII phosphorylation but increased cell ROS content, thus providing a mechanism for the late component of INa (INaL) enhancement.

CONCLUSIONS: The results support the view that STAR may supress VT by increasing conduction velocity, with APD prolongation providing an additional mechanism. On the other hand, INasus enhancement and Ca2+ handling depression may impair electrical stability and contractility in the irradiated region.

articles.title: Consensus-based recommendations to support sonographer training and wellbeing during work-integrated learning.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The demanding nature of sonography training, alongside ongoing workforce and service pressures, can affect the quality of clinical learning experiences and trainee support. Although challenges associated with sonography work-integrated learning (WIL) have been well documented, evidence regarding stakeholder priorities for improvement remains limited. This study addresses that gap by developing consensus-based recommendations informed by trainee sonographers and clinical supervisors.

METHODS: A sequential mixed-methods design comprising focus groups and a three-round modified Delphi study was employed. Eleven participants (8 clinical supervisors, 3 trainee sonographers) were recruited through professional networks, social media, and industry connections. Eligibility required Australian Sonographer Accreditation Registry registration and WIL participation within the previous 12 months. Focus group data were analysed thematically to identify priority areas for improvement, informing Delphi survey development. Predefined consensus, endorsement, and content-validity criteria guided item retention.

RESULTS: Focus group analysis identified four key areas influencing sonographer training and wellbeing during WIL: psychological safety and connection, clinical supervision excellence, training pathway clarity, and context-responsive WIL practices. The Delphi process identified psychological safety and connection and clinical supervision excellence as the highest-priority domains for action. Recommended strategies focused on embedding psychologically safe learning practices and strengthening the consistency, quality, and accountability of clinical supervision. Workforce shortages and escalating role expectations were identified as key barriers to implementation.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that trainee capability alone does not account for effective sonography WIL. The relational and organisational conditions in which learning occurs also matter. Psychological safety and high-quality clinical supervision emerged as foundational priorities for supporting trainee learning and wellbeing, particularly during the early stages of WIL.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Recommendations may improve trainee experiences, strengthen learning outcomes, and support workforce sustainability in sonography.

articles.title: Ziziphora clinopodioides Flavonoids exerts neuroprotective effects through PI3K/Akt pathway to improve ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam. is a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for centuries in Xinjiang, China, to treat cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. According to local ethnopharmacological records, it is traditionally employed to promote blood circulation, remove blood stasis, calm the heart, and relieve chest tightness and palpitations. Modern studies have shown that its total flavonoids (ZCF) possess anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability, involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. However, the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and its active constituents remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and to identify its potential active flavonoids.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology and transcriptomics were used to predict core pathways, followed by in vitro and in vivo experiments. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, BBB integrity, and PI3K/Akt-related inflammatory/oxidative markers were assessed. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 was used, and active flavonoids were screened by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ELISA.

RESULTS: Integrated transcriptomics and network pharmacology identified that ZCF modulates the PI3K/Akt pathway. In MCAO/R-treated rats, ZCF reduced cerebral infarction, and preserved neuronal morphology. ZCF protected BBB integrity by restoring ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-5, reducing MMP-9 and MMP-2 levels, rebalancing the Ang-1/Ang-2 ratio, decreasing NaF permeability, and increasing TEER. ZCF activated PI3K/Akt signaling in both bEnd.3 cells and MCAO/R-treated rat brain tissues, and the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 reversed ZCF-mediated regulation of tight junction proteins, matrix metalloproteinases, and Ang-1/Ang-2, suggesting that ZCF preserves BBB integrity at least partly through a PI3K/Akt-dependent mechanism. ZCF inhibited the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis, reduced IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and up-regulated Nrf2 and SOD, and these effects were reversed by LY294002. Molecular docking and MD simulations suggested that Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin may form stable binding with PI3K. Diosmin, Glycitin and Tilianin could significantly restore the activity of PI3K in PC12 cells treated with OGD/R, reduce the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and enhance the activity of SOD.

CONCLUSION: Under preconditioning conditions, ZCF maintains BBB and inhibits neuroinflammation and oxidative stress through integrity and PI3K/Akt dependence, thereby exerting anti-IS protection. Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin are potential active flavonoids that may contribute to PI3K/Akt activation.

articles.title: Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction attenuates renal fibrosis and suppresses pyroptosis-associated signaling: insights from integrated transcriptomics and serum pharmacochemistry.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction (WXD) is traditionally prescribed for chronic kidney disease based on the principle of warming yang and resolving blood stasis. However, whether its anti-fibrotic effects involve inflammation-associated pyroptosis remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the effects of WXD on renal fibrosis and associated changes in NF-κB- and pyroptosis-related signaling.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-six male C57BL/6 mice were allocated to six groups and subjected to sham surgery or unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) with or without valsartan or graded doses of WXD. The effects of WXD were further evaluated in TGF-β1/TNF-α-stimulated HK-2 cells. Kidney transcriptomics was integrated with serum pharmacochemistry-based network pharmacology restricted to blood-absorbed constituents. Pharmacological perturbations using necrosulfonamide (NSA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were performed in HK-2 cells.

RESULTS: High-dose WXD reduced serum BUN, renal fibrotic area, and GSDMD-N expression by 24.7%, 27.6%, and 29.1%, respectively, compared with UUO mice (all P < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis showed that WXD reversed UUO-induced activation of NF-κB, TNF, and NOD-like receptor signaling. Integration with serum pharmacochemistry identified 36 blood-absorbed constituents and yielded inflammation-related target and pathway profiles consistent with the transcriptomic findings. WXD reduced the abundance of phosphorylated p65, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-N in vivo and in vitro. NSA partially reproduced, whereas LPS partially counteracted, the protective effects of WXD.

CONCLUSIONS: WXD attenuates renal fibrosis in association with reduced NF-κB- and pyroptosis-associated signaling. Integrating transcriptomics with network pharmacology based on blood-absorbed constituents provides a biologically relevant strategy for investigating multi-component traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

articles.title: Harnessing BMSCs for ischemic stroke: Decoding multimodal repair and navigating the path to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is characterized by a high incidence rate, high disability rate and high recurrence rate. The existing treatment methods have limitations such as a narrow time window and limited recovery of neurological function. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) have become a research hotspot in the regenerative treatment of IS due to their multi-directional differentiation potential, paracrine regulation and immune regulation characteristics. This review explores the mechanism of action, strategies for enhancing therapeutic efficacy and the progress of clinical transformation of BMSCs in the treatment of IS. Basic research indicates that BMSCs improve neurological function through multiple mechanisms such as migrating to ischemic foci, secreting neurotrophic factors, promoting angiogenesis, and inhibiting apoptosis of nerve cells. Gene modification technology and the application of exosomes can further potentiate therapeutic efficacy. The optimization of injection routes, cell types, transplantation time Windows and cell doses is crucial to the therapeutic effect. Clinical studies have initially confirmed the safety of BMSCs treatment and some functional improvement effects, but there are still problems such as small sample size and unclear long-term efficacy. In the future, it is necessary to further clarify the treatment mechanism, optimize the treatment plan, and promote the transformation of basic research into clinical practice (Graphical Abstract).

articles.title: Long non-coding RNA LINC00885 contributes to liver steatosis through modulation of DHRS2-associated lipid metabolic programs.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent and rising liver disease. Its inflammatory subtype, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), can progress to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The role of long intergenic non-protein coding RNA 885 (LINC00885) in MASLD remains unknown. This study aims to clarify its function in steatotic liver disease.

METHODS: Public liver transcriptomic datasets, RNA sequencing of LINC00885-knockdown Hep G2 cells, and microarray profiling under lipotoxic conditions were integrated to identify candidate downstream components. Gain- and loss-of-function models, Oil Red O staining, RT-qPCR, an actinomycin D chase assay, functional rescue, and JC-1 analysis were used to evaluate the LINC00885-DHRS2 axis. Circulating exosomal RNA and exploratory ROC analyses were assessed in a pilot cohort.

RESULTS: LINC00885 was upregulated in MASH liver tissue and induced by FFA treatment in hepatocytes. LINC00885 promoted lipid accumulation and shifted lipid metabolic gene expression toward lipogenesis. Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified DHRS2 as a convergent downstream candidate. LINC00885 knockdown increased DHRS2 expression and was associated with slower DHRS2 mRNA decay. DHRS2 exerted an anti-steatotic phenotype, and DHRS2 depletion reversed the reduction in lipid accumulation caused by LINC00885 knockdown. DHRS2 perturbation was also accompanied by changes in mitochondrial membrane potential. In a pilot serum cohort, exosomal LINC00885 and DHRS2 showed opposite expression patterns and preliminary discriminative potential.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings support a functional LINC00885-DHRS2 axis associated with hepatocellular lipid accumulation, lipid metabolic gene expression, and mitochondrial membrane potential. The circulating exosomal observations are exploratory and require validation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts.

articles.title: Type 1 diabetes metabolomics and multi-omics: Current applications, limitations, and future directions - A narrative review.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disease characterized by immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, resulting in absolute insulin deficiency and lifelong dependence on exogenous insulin. This disease, if not treated, leads to acute and chronic complications affecting the cardiovascular, renal, and retinal systems and introduces significant psychosocial burdens. But even with advances in insulin therapy, optimal glycemic control remains difficult to achieve. T1DM progression spans from autoantibody seroconversion to overt diabetes, accompanied by dynamic metabolic perturbations, contributing to β-cell dysfunction. These metabolic alterations correlate with glycemic markers and provide integrated signatures of gene-environment interactions and disease heterogeneity. Therefore, metabolomics has emerged as a promising approach for identifying metabolic dysregulation associated with T1DM, with some studies reporting metabolite alterations detectable before clinical onset or autoantibody positivity; targeted and untargeted approaches enable comprehensive profiling of disease-associated metabolic pathways, although these findings largely reflect associations from observational cohorts rather than validated early-detection tools. Here, the analysis of biofluids with advanced platforms such as UPLC-MS and NMR provides high-resolution insights into systemic metabolism, supporting the discovery of candidate biomarkers that may, pending further validation, contribute to earlier diagnosis and precision medicine strategies in T1DM. Even though current metabolomic studies have substantially improved the classification of metabolic alterations associated with T1DM, the field still necessitates clarification of causal mechanisms, standardization of methodologies, validation of findings across diverse populations, and integration of metabolomics with other omics platforms in robust longitudinal designs. These gaps highlight a clear necessity of moving beyond descriptive profiling toward systematically standardized and validated metabolomic markers embedded within multi-omics and longitudinal frameworks.

articles.title: Altitude-associated circulating biomarker profiles in native Tibetans with and without chronic mountain sickness.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Native Tibetans have adapted to chronic hypoxia, yet remain susceptible to Chronic Mountain Sickness (CMS), including high-altitude polycythemia (HAPC) and high-altitude pulmonary hypertension (HAPH). CMS prevalence rises with altitude, but mechanisms remain unclear. We aim to investigate biomarker profiles in native Tibetans with and without CMS across altitudes, including extreme altitude >5,000m.

METHODS: We enrolled 91 native Tibetans across 4 altitudes (500 m/3,680 m/4,750 m/5,373 m), categorized into healthy, HAPC and HAPH groups. Seventeen biomarkers were quantified via Luminex. Biomarker associations with altitude and disease were analyzed using linear regression with Type-III-F-tests, followed by post-hoc comparison and effect-size analysis.

RESULTS: Among healthy Tibetans, multiple biomarkers exhibited non-linear altitude-dependent changes. C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (CXCL8), interferon-γ (IFN-γ), fibroblast growth factor (FGF), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 4 (CXCL4) and thrombopoietin (TPO) peaked at 4,750 m and declined at 5,373 m, whereas matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) increased at 5,373 m. Among plateau-dwelling Tibetans (including HAPC and HAPH), no independent main disease-status effects were detected across biomarkers. However, an altitude-disease interaction was observed for angiogenin, with reduction at 5,373 m in HAPH, but not in HAPC.

CONCLUSION: Rising altitude drives distinct biomarker profiles in healthy Tibetans, with CXCL8/IFN-γ/FGF/VEGF/CXCL4/TPO exhibiting an inverted U-shaped response peaking at 4,750 m, and isolated MMP-3 elevation at 5,373 m, indicating a transition from adaptive angiogenesis to pathological tissue remodeling at extreme-high altitude. The altitude-dependent angiogenin reduction observed exclusively in HAPH at extreme altitude, indicating a dysregulated vascular reparative signaling in Tibetans with HAPH. These findings provide new insights into CMS pathogenesis across hypoxic gradient.

articles.title: Revisiting chronic pancreatitis as a risk factor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: toward precision risk stratification.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is an established risk factor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). However, individual risk varies substantially, and the association between CP and PDAC is more complex than a uniform inflammation-driven pathway. Reverse causation, shared etiological factors, and biological heterogeneity may contribute to the observed association.

AREAS COVERED: We critically review epidemiological, mechanistic, and causal evidence linking CP with PDAC, focusing on heterogeneity across CP subtypes and disease trajectories. We examine five domains potentially relevant to individual PDAC risk: genetic susceptibility, cumulative pancreatic injury, metabolic trajectories including new-onset diabetes, longitudinal imaging phenotypes, and emerging molecular alterations. We propose a multidomain framework for individualized and dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

EXPERT OPINION: CP should not be regarded as a uniformly high-risk condition for PDAC. Individual risk is shaped by the interaction of genetic, inflammatory, metabolic, structural, and molecular factors. The key question should therefore shift from whether CP increases PDAC risk to which patients are most likely to develop clinically consequential PDAC. Although multidomain and longitudinal assessment may enable targeted surveillance, most biomarkers and prediction strategies remain insufficiently validated. Prospective studies are required to determine whether this approach improves early detection and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Present and future of ulta-low- and low-dose triple combination therapy in hypertension: a clinical practice perspective.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: It is increasingly recognized that initial monotherapy is insufficiently effective for sustained blood pressure (BP) control in the large majority of people with hypertension. Ultra-low- and low-dose combination therapy has emerged as a strategy to overcome limitations of conventional monotherapy-based stepped care, including delayed or inadequate BP reduction, adverse-effect-related treatment discontinuation, poor adherence, and therapeutic inertia.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes the pharmacologic rationale and clinical evidence for ultra-low- and low-dose multidrug combination therapy. To identify clinical evidence, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 31 March 2026, supplemented by manual reference screening. This review addresses practical questions in routine practice, including its relationship with compelling indications, cardiovascular protection, appropriate patient selection, and whether it reduces adverse effects. Future implementation as simplified, protocolized treatment and add-on approaches in high-risk populations is also discussed.

EXPERT OPINION: Ultra-low- and low-dose triple single-pill combination therapy should be viewed not simply as the earlier use of more antihypertensive drugs, but as a scalable treatment-delivery platform. It may support safe and earlier sustained BP control by simplifying drug selection, enabling stepwise dose escalation, reducing pill burden, improving adherence and persistence, and overcoming therapeutic inertia.

articles.title: Establishing cardiovascular safety of the small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist orforglipron in type 2 diabetes.
New and emerging pharmacological solutions for Behçet's syndrome.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Behçet's syndrome is a chronic multisystem inflammatory disease characterized by mucocutaneous lesions, ocular inflammation, and major-organ involvement. Treatment aims to prevent irreversible organ damage and maximize health-related quality of life.

AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes current therapeutic approaches based on the 2025 update of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology recommendations for Behçet's syndrome. Core recommended therapies, including colchicine, glucocorticoids, apremilast, conventional immunosuppressants, and TNF inhibitors, are selected for individual organ involvement depending on severity. The updated recommendations refine treatment strategies and emphasize individualized management rather than substantially expanding therapeutic options. This review also examines emerging non-TNF biologics targeting IL-1, IL-6, IL-17, and IL-12/23, and Janus kinase inhibitors. PubMed was searched from database inception through August 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: The rarity of Behçet's syndrome and the lack of standardized assessment tools remain major obstacles to conducting high quality clinical trials. In addition, several anti cytokine therapies may be associated with organ-specific or paradoxical manifestations in Behçet's syndrome. Further evidence is required to clarify both the efficacy and safety profiles of new therapeutic agents, and prospective controlled studies will be essential to establish their roles in clinical practice.

articles.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.

METHODS: RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.

INTERPRETATION: An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.
