FUNDING: Indian Council of Medical Research, Department of Health Research, Government of India.

articles.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.

METHODS: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.

FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.

INTERPRETATION: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

FUNDING: Eli Lilly and Company.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.

METHODS: OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.

FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.

INTERPRETATION: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

FUNDING: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of fractional one-fifth and one-half doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine compared with full dose in children aged 9-23 months in Uganda: a phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional doses of yellow fever vaccines have been shown to be safe and immunogenic in randomised controlled trials in adults and children. However, little evidence still remains in children younger than 2 years. We assessed immunogenicity of one-fifth (0·1 mL) and one-half (0·25 mL) fractional doses compared with full doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine in children aged 9-23 months in Kampala, Uganda.

METHODS: This phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial evaluating fractional dose 17DD yellow fever vaccine among children was conducted at three public-sector health facilities in Uganda. Eligible participants were aged 9-23 months at enrolment, had no history of yellow fever disease or vaccination, and did not meet the exclusion criteria. Children were enrolled in three age strata: 9-12 months, 13-18 months, and 19-23 months, and were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using block randomisation (block sizes of three and six) to one-fifth (0·1 mL), one-half (0·25 mL), or full (0·5 mL) doses of the 17DD yellow fever vaccine. Participants were followed up at 4 weeks (visit 1 [V1]), 1 year (visit 2 [V2]), and 13-48 months (visit 3 [V3]) after vaccination. The primary analysis included per-protocol participants who attended within the prespecified visit window; an intention-to-treat analysis was also conducted including all randomly assigned participants with available outcome data. Participants with missing serological data were excluded from the analysis at the corresponding visit. The primary outcome was non-inferiority in seroconversion (5 percentage-point margin) at V1 measured by 50% plaque reduction neutralisation test. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03725618, and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between March 26, 2019, and May 11, 2021, 1784 participants were randomly assigned to either one-fifth dose (n=600), one-half dose (n=594), or full dose (n=590). The median (IQR) age at enrolment was 13 (11-18) months. Both fractional doses met the non-inferiority criterion compared with the full dose with no difference in seroconversion between one-fifth and full doses and -0·17 (95% CI -0·52 to 0·17) difference between one-half and full doses in the per-protocol population at V1. There was no difference between the one-fifth and full doses.

INTERPRETATION: Both fractional doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine were non-inferior to full doses in inducing initial seroconversion. The results support the use of fractional dose yellow fever vaccines among young children for outbreak response during supply shortages.

FUNDING: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

articles.title: Transpalpebral exenteration in dogs: A retrospective study (2003‒2023).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transpalpebral exenteration is indicated in cases of neoplasia, infection or severe trauma involving the globe and orbit. Limited peer-reviewed literature exists on the indications, complications and outcomes associated with this procedure in dogs.

METHODS: This retrospective study analysed medical records of 35 dogs undergoing transpalpebral exenteration at three UK veterinary referral centres between 2003 and 2023. The data included signalment, diagnostic findings, surgical details and postoperative complications. Kruskal‒Wallis and Fisher's exact tests were used to analyse relationships between clinical variables and complications.

RESULTS: Orbital neoplasia was the most common indication (54.3%, 19/35), followed by orbital inflammatory disease (25.7%, 9/35), orbital cyst (11.4%, 4/35), orbital foreign body (5.7%, 2/35) and orbital pseudotumour (2.9%, 1/35). Immediate postoperative complications (<2 days) occurred in 60% (21/35) of cases, with surgical site swelling being the most frequent (90.5%). Short-term (2‒21 days) and long-term (>21 days) complications occurred in 20% (7/35) and 5.7% (2/35) of cases, respectively. Six patients (17.1%) required additional treatment. No significant correlations were found between the independent variables and complication rates.

LIMITATIONS: This study is limited by its retrospective nature and the small sample size.

CONCLUSION: Transpalpebral exenteration is a safe procedure with primarily minor postoperative complications that typically resolve without intervention.

articles.title: Sensory profile of cats with potential pain-related diabetic neuropathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) can cause peripheral neuropathy. This study aimed to evaluate sensory function by measuring the mechanical nociceptive thresholds (MNT) and diffuse noxious inhibitory control (DNIC) of cats with diabetes mellitus (DMcats).

METHODS: Eight cats with DM and 12 healthy controls were included in a prospective, randomised study. MNT were measured by applying pressure against the metatarsal pad (MNTbio). MNT were also measured using a mechanical actuator attached to one of the cat's pelvic limbs (MNTtop). The DNIC was assessed by comparing MNTtop before and after a conditioning stimulus.

RESULTS: MNTbio of the controls were significantly lower (2.1 ± 0.7 N) than those of DMcats (3.6 ± 1.2 N). DNIC and MNTtop were not different between groups.

LIMITATIONS: This study had a small cohort of patients and an MNT cut-off to prevent injuries.

CONCLUSION: DMcats showed hypoalgesia and loss of sensory function. This study could not differentiate DNIC between healthy and those with DM.

articles.title: Smpd2 m6A modification contributes to hypoxic pulmonary hypertension via an alveolar epithelial cell senescence-associated phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vascular remodelling induced by the abnormal proliferation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) is a core pathological feature of hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (HPH), but its exact pathogenesis remains poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the functional role and intrinsic regulatory mechanisms of an alveolar epithelial cell (AEC) senescence-associated phenotype in the pathogenesis of HPH.

METHODS: A 4-week hypoxia-induced HPH rat model and an in vitro hypoxia-induced AEC senescence-associated phenotype model were established. The effects of hypoxia on AECs were analysed by evaluating the senescence-associated phenotype and mitochondrial function. In addition, a Transwell coculture system and AEC-conditioned medium were used to evaluate the effects of hypoxia-exposed AECs with a senescence-associated phenotype on PASMC proliferation. The key signalling pathways associated with the hypoxia-induced AEC senescence-associated phenotype were identified through transcriptome sequencing and subsequent KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. The roles of the Smpd2/ceramide axis in the hypoxia-induced AEC senescence-associated phenotype, PASMC proliferation and HPH progression were explored via the administration of METTL3- and Smpd2-targeting siRNAs, AAV6-shSmpd2 for lung-directed Smpd2 silencing in vivo, the neutral sphingomyelinase (nSMase) inhibitor GW4869, the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant Mito-TEMPO (MT) and the NAD⁺ precursor β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). Finally, MeRIP-qPCR, RIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, and dual-luciferase assays were employed to elucidate the mechanisms of m6A RNA methylation in AECs with the senescence-associated phenotype.

RESULTS: Chronic hypoxia induced typical manifestations of HPH in rats, accompanied by a more pronounced AEC senescence-associated phenotype. In cultured human AECs, hypoxia upregulated METTL3, which increased Smpd2 mRNA stability through m6A modification recognized by IGF2BP2. These changes were associated with ceramide accumulation and mitochondrial dysfunction and contributed to the AEC senescence-associated phenotype in vitro. AECs with this phenotype released soluble and/or vesicular paracrine signals that were associated with abnormal PASMC proliferation, contributing to vascular remodelling and right ventricular hypertrophy. In cultured human AECs, NMN pretreatment, Smpd2 knockdown, and METTL3 knockdown attenuated the hypoxia-induced AEC senescence-associated phenotype. In hypoxia-exposed rats, NMN supplementation, lung-directed Smpd2 silencing, and pharmacological nSMase inhibition with GW4869 attenuated the AEC senescence-associated phenotype and alleviated HPH progression.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides preclinical evidence that, in hypoxia-exposed rats and cultured human AECs/PASMCs, a hypoxia-induced AEC senescence-associated phenotype may contribute to PASMC proliferation and HPH development. Mechanistically, in cultured human AECs, hypoxia exposure increased METTL3-mediated m6A modification of Smpd2 mRNA, which increased its stability in an m6A- and IGF2BP2-dependent manner and upregulated Smpd2 expression. The resulting increase in ceramide accumulation was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and the senescence-associated phenotype in AECs. In this preclinical setting, AECs with this phenotype may further contribute to PASMC proliferation and HPH development. The findings of this study provide preclinical data supporting a candidate mechanism in HPH pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future validation in human PH and cell-specific in vivo models.

articles.title: Intraprocedural Embolization of a Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair Device and Its Percutaneous Retrieval: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) is an established therapy for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in selected patients. Single-leaflet device attachment (SLDA) is the commonest device-related complication, but complete intraprocedural detachment with embolization is rare, and percutaneous retrieval of an embolized tricuspid device has been reported only exceptionally. Case Presentation: An inoperable elderly patient with previous transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and torrential functional TR underwent T-TEER. After implantation of the first clip at the anteroseptal commissure with apparently adequate leaflet capture, anterior SLDA was identified and progressed to complete detachment and right atrial embolization of the device. Despite this, the T-TEER was completed by successful implantation of the second clip, leaving only mild residual central TR. In the same session, the embolized device was retrieved percutaneously from the femoral venous system using a 15 mm gooseneck snare advanced through a 22 Fr sheath, with a safety wire and en-bloc removal, without forcing ensheathing and without venous injury. The patient was discharged on post-procedure day 2 with durable TR reduction and clinical improvement. Conclusions: Complete leaflet detachment is a possible complication of T-TEER. Confirming deep, symmetric insertion in multiple echocardiographic windows before every release is essential. When embolization occurs, knowledge of device dimensions and immediate availability of a complete snare kit is important. Although this approach may be considered in selected patients, particularly those at high surgical risk, the available evidence is limited to isolated case reports and does not allow general conclusions on its safety or efficacy.

articles.title: Effects of atropine on hemodynamic parameters following electroconvulsive therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) plays an important role in the treatment of refractory psychiatric disorders. However, it poses hemodynamic risks, such as blood pressure and heart rate elevation, arrhythmias, and transient asystole. Although atropine administration during ECT was considered a standard procedure in Western countries until the 1970s, in recent years, its use is generally limited to patients at high risk of bradycardia and asystole. We performed this meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to understand the effects of atropine on post-ECT hemodynamics and adverse events.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase was conducted to identify RCTs investigating the relationship between atropine administration and post-ECT hemodynamics through September 30, 2025. The primary outcomes included maximum heart rate and maximum blood pressure after ECT, as well as the incidence of ECT-related adverse events. The secondary outcomes included seizure duration, arrhythmia incidence, severe salivation, and cognitive function.

RESULTS: Of the 2465 studies identified, eight RCTs were included in the meta-analysis. Maximum heart rate after ECT was significantly higher in the atropine group (p < .001). There was no significant difference in the risk of serious adverse cardiovascular events requiring intervention. Bradyarrhythmia was significantly less frequent in the atropine group (risk ratio 0.35, p < .0001).

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis to evaluate the hemodynamic effects of atropine administration during ECT. The findings suggest that atropine increases maximum heart rate after ECT reduces the incidence of bradyarrhythmia. Although no increased risk of cardiovascular adverse events requiring intervention was observed, the small sample size remains an important limitation.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero) registration number: CRD 42022346729.

articles.title: Source-Specific PM2.5 Exposure and Atrial Fibrillation Risk in U.S. Older Adults: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of atrial fibrillation (AF), but the effects of individual PM2.5 sources remain unclear. We evaluated the relationship between long-term exposure to source-specific PM2.5 and incident AF among 26.3 million U.S. Medicare beneficiaries from 2000 to 2019. We resolved PM2.5 sources using the Multilinear Engine model based on PM2.5 components data from monitoring stations. Annual ZIP code-level exposures were assigned using inverse-distance weighting of monitoring stations within a 100 km buffer. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate AF risk per interquartile range (IQR) increase in source-specific PM2.5 concentrations, adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors and other environmental covariates. Over 171.6 million person-years of follow-up, 4.44 million incident AF cases were identified. Exposure to PM2.5 from vehicle emissions (HR 1.029, 95% CI 1.028-1.030), heavy oil and coal combustion (HR 1.048, 95% CI 1.046-1.050), secondary sulfate (HR 1.056, 95% CI 1.053-1.058), and secondary nitrate (HR 1.032, 95% CI 1.030-1.034) was significantly associated with higher AF risk. In contrast, biomass burning and soil and dust exhibited only modest associations, and secondary organic aerosols (SOA) showed no overall effect. Regional analyses revealed geographic heterogeneity: fossil-fuel-related sources drove AF risk in most regions, secondary sulfate and nitrate had the strongest effects in the southern U.S., and SOA was more strongly associated with AF in the West. These findings highlight the differential toxicity and regional heterogeneity of PM2.5 sources in AF risk and emphasize the need for targeted, region-specific air quality regulations focusing on traffic and industrial emissions to mitigate AF incidence in older adults.

articles.title: Mixed Presentation of Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State and Diabetic Ketoacidosis in a Pediatric Patient: a Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
articles.abstract: The coexistence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS), known as mixed hyperglycemic crisis, is a rare but potentially fatal metabolic emergency in pediatrics, and is frequently underrecognized because it is misclassified as isolated DKA. It carries a higher risk of complications than either entity alone, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We describe the case of a 16-year-old female with myelomeningocele, neurogenic bladder, obesity, and insulin resistance, who had self-discontinued treatment with metformin, atorvastatin, and allopurinol one year prior and presented with sudden neurological deterioration. Initial workup revealed extreme hyperglycemia (1,777 mg/dL), severe hyperosmolarity (431 mOsm/kg), decompensated metabolic acidosis (pH 7.13), and positive urine ketones (+++), consistent with a mixed DKA-HHS presentation. She subsequently developed septic shock of urinary origin, acute kidney injury, and acute pancreatitis (lipase 3,911 U/L). Despite intensive management guided by International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes-ISPAD recommendations, she progressed to refractory shock and multiorgan failure, dying within 48 hours of admission. To the best of our knowledge, this represents one of the most extreme metabolic derangements reported in pediatric mixed hyperglycemic crisis. The convergence of extreme hyperosmolarity, concurrent sepsis, and structural comorbidities created a lethal risk phenotype in which sepsis, rather than the degree of metabolic derangement alone, appeared to determine the fatal outcome. Early recognition and an individualized therapeutic approach are essential to improve outcomes in vulnerable pediatric patients.

articles.title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression.

METHODS: From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates.

RESULTS: Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures.

CONCLUSIONS: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).

articles.title: Electromechanical Window Negativity and Arrhythmic Risk in Arrhythmogenic Mitral Valve Prolapse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is generally a benign valvular heart disease, but a subset of patients is at particular risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (AMVP).

OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the electromechanical window (EMW) as an arrhythmia-risk marker in (A)MVP (the sum of all MVP and AMVP patients).

METHODS: Healthy controls, patients with MVP without ventricular arrhythmia (MVP/-VA), and patients with AMVP with nonsustained (AMVP/nsVA) or sustained ventricular arrhythmia (AMVP/VA) (ventricular arrhythmia >30 seconds) were retrospectively included from 3 centers (derivation cohort). An independent validation (A)MVP cohort was recruited from 2 centers. EMW was calculated blinded from apical Doppler echocardiography by subtracting the QT time from the simultaneous Q-to-aortic-valve closure time (QAoC).

RESULTS: In the derivation cohort (31 controls, 31 MVP/-VA, 29 AMVP/nsVA, 14 AMVP/VA), patients with (A)MVP displayed a borderline shorter QAoCc (P = 0.06) and significantly longer QTc than controls (P < 0.0001), resulting in a more negative EMW (-18 ms [-47 to -8 ms]; P < 0.0001). EMW was most negative in patients with AMVP/VA (-71 ms [-177 to -30 ms]). These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort (n = 76 with [A]MVP), albeit at different absolute values. In a pooled receiver-operating characteristic analysis, EMW identified patients with AMVP/VA with an area under the curve of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.91), significantly outperforming QTc and QAoCc. An EMW threshold of -30 ms was the optimal cutoff (sensitivity: 0.71; specificity: 0.83). EMW was independently associated with AMVP/VA status and improved model performance in addition to established risk parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: EMW is markedly negative in patients with AMVP/VA, reflecting electromechanical discordance. Thus, EMW emerges as a promising risk-associated marker in (A)MVP.

articles.title: Anti-angiogenic Therapy at the Vascular Crossroads: Tumor Vessel Normalization, Excessive Pruning, and Systemic Vascular Toxicity.
articles.abstract: Tumor angiogenesis contributes to tumor growth, metastasis, and treatment resistance, but the newly formed vessels are often structurally abnormal and functionally inefficient. Antiangiogenic therapy, particularly inhibition of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) signaling, is now used in the treatment of multiple cancers. Its vascular effects depend strongly on the extent of angiogenic inhibition. Moderate inhibition may temporarily improve the structure and function of abnormal tumor vessels. This vascular normalization can improve perfusion, oxygenation, immune cell infiltration, and drug delivery in selected tumor types and treatment settings. More extensive vessel pruning can have the opposite effect, reducing perfusion, worsening hypoxia, and favoring adaptive resistance. VEGF inhibition also affects normal vessels because physiological angiogenic signaling is required for endothelial homeostasis. Disruption of this signaling contributes to hypertension, thromboembolism, renal injury, cardiovascular complications, and cerebrovascular events. In this narrative review, the mechanisms that shape tumor vascular remodeling and compare the vascular effects of anti-angiogenic and other vascular-modulating anticancer therapies in tumors and normal tissues are examined. Particular attention is given to the distinction between tumor-vessel normalization and vascular injury in normal tissues, as well as treatment scheduling, combination strategies, targeted delivery, and vascular-response biomarkers.

articles.title: A Multivariate Statistics Approach to Analyze the Transition from CCR5 to Dual and CXCR4 Tropism and to Predict the Coreceptor Usage of HIV-1.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The tropism of HIV-1 is determined by the use of either or both chemokine coreceptors CCR5 (R5) and CXCR4 (X4) for entry into the target cell. The coreceptor usage of HIV-1 is mainly determined by the third variable loop (V3) of the envelope glycoprotein gp120.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We assembled a training dataset of 3071 V3 sequences with known tropism: 2428 R5-tropic, 358 dual R5X4-tropic, and 285 X4-tropic. We analyzed this dataset by using univariate statistics (t-Student, chi-square contingency table, and Cramer's V index), bivariate statistics (Pearson's correlation coefficient), and multivariate statistics (principal component analysis and Fisher's linear discriminant analysis).

RESULTS: One third of the 35 amino acid positions in the V3 loop are key drivers of transition from R5 to R5X4 and X4 tropism. Principal component analysis (PCA) indicates that the switch between the three tropism states is a gradual process involving variation for several biochemical features. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) is a good predictor of coreceptor usage. When applied to the training dataset, it showed a high sensitivity (92% of X4-tropic sequences predicted correctly) and a high specificity (90% of R5-tropic sequences predicted correctly).

DISCUSSION: The finding that the sensitivity and specificity of LDA are similar, or better than that of four widely used prediction methods (Geno2pheno, WebPSSM, 11/24/25 charge rule, and net charge rule) indicates that LDA is a valuable complement to the existing models for prediction of coreceptor usage.

CONCLUSION: Parametric multivariate statistics is a useful tool to investigate the switch of HIV-1 tropism and to predict the CCR5 or CXCR4 coreceptor usage.

articles.title: Integrated physics-data-based LPV-LMS-MPC coordinated control for simultaneous luffing-slewing of truck cranes.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous luffing-slewing control of truck cranes is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics, parameter variations, and motion coupling. To overcome these issues, this article introduces an integrated physics-data-based LPV-LMS-MPC framework for the coordinated control of an electro-hydraulic system. A physics-based affine linear parameter-varying (LPV) model is first derived from fundamental principles to capture cross-coupling dynamics. To address parameter time-variation without compromising model interpretability, a Kronecker-product reformulation is introduced. This transformation enables the least mean square (LMS) algorithm to selectively update only the uncertain coefficients online using real system output data while preserving the predefined physical structure and structural zeros. The updated coefficients are mapped back to the LPV state-space matrices to reconstruct a constrained incremental model predictive control (MPC) prediction model, enabling real-time adaptive optimization. Simulation and prototype experiments validate the framework. Results show that the LPV-LMS model reliably captures disturbed system dynamics, and the integrated LPV-LMS-MPC scheme delivers superior coordinated tracking while requiring far less computation time than nonlinear MPC.

articles.title: What is the Utility of Whole Body Imaging for Screening Patients With Craniofacial Fibrous Dysplasia?
articles.abstract: Whole body imaging is commonly performed in patients with fibrous dysplasia (FD) to screen for additional lesions. However, the frequency of newly-detected lesions in patients presenting with isolated craniofacial FD is unclear. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the frequency of newly-detected FD lesions on whole body imaging in patients with craniofacial FD and no known extracraniofacial lesions or symptoms. This was a retrospective observational cohort study at a tertiary children's hospital in an urban setting. The study population consisted of patients with craniofacial FD who underwent whole body imaging with technetium-99m (Tc-99m) bone scintigraphy or fluorine-18 sodium fluoride positron emission tomography/computed tomography (F-18 NaF PET/CT). Patients with previously identified extracraniofacial lesions, symptoms, or McCune-Albright syndrome were excluded. The primary outcome was the frequency of newly-detected extracraniofacial FD lesions. Fifteen subjects were included (80% female). Mean age at FD diagnosis was 9.6±4.3 years, and mean age at imaging was 10.4±4.2 years. Tc-99m bone scintigraphy was the most common imaging modality (86.7%). Newly-detected extracraniofacial FD lesions were observed in 1 of 15 subjects (6.7%). Two additional subjects (13.3%) had incidental skeletal findings related to recent traumatic injuries. In patients presumed to have isolated craniofacial FD, whole body imaging identified a low frequency of extracraniofacial skeletal lesions. These findings suggest that routine screening may be considered selectively based on clinical history and physical examination. Further investigation is required to develop evidence-based screening guidelines.

articles.title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds.

RESULTS: Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds.

DISCUSSION: Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

articles.title: Facial Injury Severity Scale and Frontal-Segment Involvement as Risk Stratification Markers in Panfacial Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Panfacial fractures are high-energy injuries. We evaluated whether the Facial Injury Severity Scale (FISS) and frontal-segment involvement are associated with early surgical complications, length of stay, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and craniocerebral injury. Thirty-four panfacial fracture patients treated between January 2016 and May 2026 were analyzed retrospectively at a single center. Fractures were classified with the Erdmann-Follmar four-segment model (≥3 of 4 segments); FISS used the Duke modified system. Because several tables were sparse, associations were estimated by Firth penalized logistic regression with profile penalized-likelihood confidence intervals (CIs), unadjusted and FISS-adjusted. Twenty-seven men and 7 women were included (mean age 37.2±18.6); the frontal-upper midface-lower midface pattern was commonest (38.2%), and median FISS was 13.5 (IQR 9-21). Concomitant injury occurred in 73.5% (craniocerebral 44.1%), early complications in 50.0%, and ICU admission in 52.9%. Frontal-segment involvement was associated with craniocerebral injury [odds ratio (OR) 7.14, 95% CI 1.31-74.4; P=0.021] and intracranial pathology (OR 17.59, 95% CI 1.88-2356.2; P=0.008); both were unchanged after adjustment for FISS, which showed no independent association with either. Conversely, FISS was independently associated with early surgical complications (OR 1.13 per point, 95% CI 1.01-1.27; P=0.028), whereas frontal involvement was not. The FISS ≥ 11 threshold was not validated. The 2 markers appear to index different axes of injury, but in 34 patients, CIs are wide, subgroup analyses are underpowered, and the composite craniocerebral association is partly definitional; these findings are hypothesis-generating and require multicenter validation.

articles.title: Peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis due to lung tumor in a cat.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: A four-year-old castrated male American shorthair cat presented with lethargy, anorexia, and tachypnea. Echocardiography revealed a large mass compressing both branch pulmonary arteries. An increased peak systolic flow velocity in the left pulmonary artery (3.2 m/sec; estimated peak pressure gradient, 41 mmHg) was consistent with peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis. Pulmonary hypertension was suspected based on echocardiographic findings. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated bilateral pulmonary artery stenosis by a pulmonary mass, and fine-needle biopsy cytology was consistent with lung carcinoma. Because of advanced disease with bilateral pulmonary artery involvement and suspected distant metastases, interventional treatment was not performed. This is the first report of acquired peripheral pulmonary arterial stenosis secondary to pulmonary carcinoma in a cat.

articles.title: Reduced Adverse Events Without Survival Benefit With HeartMate 3 vs. HeartMate II in Japan.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HeartMate 3 (Abbott Laboratories), a fully magnetically levitated left ventricular assist device (LVAD), has shown improved hemocompatibility vs. previous devices, but nationwide real-world data in Japan remain limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese nationwide registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed patients who underwent de novo implantation of HeartMate 3 or HeartMate II between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and device dysfunction requiring exchange or explantation within 2 years. In all, 978 patients were included in the study (HeartMate 3, n=486; HeartMate II, n=492). The 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group than in the HeartMate II group (9% vs. 23%; P<0.001). HeartMate 3 was independently associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.51; P<0.001), which remained consistent in competing-risk and several statistically matched analyses. The incidence of hemocompatibility-related adverse events, including major bleeding, stroke, and device dysfunction, was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group. In contrast, 2- and 5-year overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups (<10% for both devices).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide Japanese registry, HeartMate 3 reduced major LVAD-related complications without improving survival, supporting its clinical advantages in contemporary LVAD management.

articles.title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.

articles.title: A multimodal in situ framework for spatial characterization applied on SARS-CoV-2 live-attenuated vaccines in the nasal mucosa.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viruses frequently initiate infection in the nasal mucosa, where virus-host interactions shape disease progression and transmission. Yet this site remains undercharacterized due to anatomical and technical challenges. Spatially resolved technologies are limited by cost and complexity, leaving most studies reliant on bulk or descriptive approaches lacking spatial context. We present a framework for spatially resolved investigation of infections in the nasal cavity. Using wild-type SARS-CoV-2 and two live-attenuated vaccines (OTS-206, OTS-228) as model viruses in Syrian hamsters, we integrate standardized sampling, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, multiplex RNA in situ hybridization, and quantitative image analysis across spatial scales, including tissue, single-cell, and subcellular resolution. We identified distinct infection patterns and graduated tissue damage from wild-type to OTS-228. Despite limited infection, OTS-228 induces a robust tissue-preserving immune response. Subcellular analysis shows that both vaccines exhibit a primarily cytoplasmic distribution of host antiviral transcripts, whereas WT infection is characterized by predominantly nuclear RNA localization.

articles.title: Continuous versus intermittent, non-invasive monitoring of vital signs in hospitalised, ward based adult patients: A systematic review and narrative synthesis.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intermittent monitoring (IM) of vital signs remains the standard of care for hospitalised ward patients, yet this approach creates gaps during which patient deterioration may go unrecognised. Wearable wireless devices capable of continuously measuring physiological parameters offer the potential for earlier detection of clinical decline and prevention of intensive care unit admissions. This systematic review aimed to compare continuous, non-invasive vital signs monitoring with standard IM for the identification of deterioration and prevention of complications in adult, ward-based hospitalised patients.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE and the Cochrane database was conducted for English-language studies published from January 1980 to December 2025. Eligible studies compared continuous, non-invasive vital signs monitoring with IM in adult ward patients and reported clinical outcomes related to deterioration. Randomised controlled trials were assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias tool and non-randomised studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Outcomes of interest included mortality, hospital and ICU length of stay, ICU transfers, rapid response or escalation calls, time-critical treatment delivery and clinical complications.

RESULTS: Following removal of duplicates, 2028 records were screened, yielding 96 articles for full-text review. Thirty-one studies met the eligibility criteria. Two of these compared algorithm-generated monitoring outputs with periodically calculated early warning scores and were excluded from the primary analysis, leaving 29 studies (7 randomised controlled trials, 12 before-and-after studies, 10 observational cohort studies) in the final synthesis. Several studies reported reductions in mortality, ICU transfers or length of stay with continuous monitoring, but few of these reached statistical significance. Some reported earlier escalation and fewer postoperative complications in continuously monitored patients. Differences between studies in design, monitoring system and outcome definition prevented meta-analysis and limited direct comparison.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not demonstrate superiority of continuous over intermittent vital signs monitoring for improving clinical outcomes in ward-based patients, although trends suggest possible reductions in deterioration, mortality and hospital length of stay. To clarify these effects, larger standardised randomised trials are required. Future research should evaluate continuous monitoring in combination with decision-support tools and automated alert systems.

articles.title: A systematic review of laxative use in critically unwell patients: Are we doing more harm than good?
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diarrhoea is common in critically unwell patients and is associated with prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay and increased mortality. Its causes are multifactorial; however, emerging evidence suggests that laxative exposure may be an important, and potentially modifiable, contributor. Laxatives are frequently prescribed in ICU patients to prevent constipation, increasingly as part of bowel management protocols (BMP) and care bundles, despite limited supporting evidence. This systematic review evaluated the effects and prevailing associations of laxatives on clinical outcomes in critically unwell adults.

METHODS: A systematic literature search of MEDLINE (including PubMed), EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL and ClinicalTrials.gov databases was conducted on 21st July 2026 to review studies that included data on the impact of laxatives on clinical outcomes in critically unwell adult patients. Non-English studies, conference abstracts and studies with paediatric patients or adult patients not admitted to ICU were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the ROBINS-I V2 tool for observational studies and RoB 2 for randomised trials. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: The systematic literature search identified 28 studies suitable for review inclusion. Of these, 27 were full-text articles, comprising 21 observational studies and six randomised trials; the remaining study was a meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite their frequency, diarrhoea and constipation in critically unwell patients lack clear, consensus definitions. Evidence supporting prophylactic laxative use is limited; studies have not demonstrated consistent improvements in clinically meaningful outcomes and suggest that prophylactic use may contribute to ICU-associated diarrhoea. Although therapeutic laxative use induces defecation, the optimal agent, dose, timing and patient selection remain uncertain. Standardised definitions of bowel dysfunction and high-quality randomised trials are needed to determine the effects of specific laxative strategies on clinical outcomes and diarrhoea incidence in critically unwell patients.

articles.title: The effectiveness of sound-based interventions on promoting sleep quality in hospitalized patients: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Sleep quality strongly affects hospitalized patients' recovery, yet pain, anxiety, and environmental factors such as noise and light frequently disrupt it. Sound-based therapies offer a promising, non-pharmacological approach, but their effectiveness has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review examined fifteen studies (2012-2026, 2024 patients, mostly intensive care settings) evaluating sound-based interventions, including calming music, nature sounds, and white noise, on sleep quality. Intervention duration and timing varied widely, from brief five-minute sessions to continuous overnight administration, and sleep quality was most often measured using validated questionnaires. Despite substantial heterogeneity, sound-based interventions were associated with an overall improvement in sleep quality, although effect sizes varied considerably and several studies showed no significant benefit. These findings support the potential of low-cost, non-pharmacological sound interventions to improve sleep in hospital settings, while underscoring the need for further research to clarify which intervention characteristics drive effectiveness.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Saudi national prevention model for reduction of central-line-associated bloodstream infections: A single-center qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Central-line catheterization is a routine but high-risk procedure in intensive care, with central-line-associated bloodstream (CLABSI) infections remaining a major contributor to patient morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs. In response to nationally elevated CLABSI rates, the Saudi Ministry of Health introduced the "Go Green" Project and the CLABSI National Prevention Tool in 2022 to standardize and strengthen prevention practices.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the national prevention model in a tertiary adult intensive care unit.

METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and document reviews with 29 stakeholders, including nurses, physicians, infection-prevention specialists, and administrators. The study identified two major themes. The first one, "A practical strategy requires both professional human resources and sufficient medical supplies," comprised four codes: staffing, workload overload, competency, and medical supplies. The second theme, "An administrative strategy requires both awareness and behavioral attitudes," was represented by four codes: "Go Green," education and training, hands-off practices, and teamwork. While participants generally demonstrated strong foundational knowledge of CLABSI prevention, gaps remained among a minority.

RESULTS: Key barriers included nursing workforce shortages, inconsistent supply availability, and variable competency in ultrasound-guided catheter insertion. Stakeholders emphasized the need for continuous training, improved supply-chain reliability, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration, alongside a sustained cultural commitment to infection-prevention practices.

SIGNIFICANCE AND IMPACT: Although the institution achieved national recognition for CLABSI reduction in 2022, long-term success will depend on maintaining adherence to best practices, addressing operational constraints, and ensuring ongoing competency development to meet future performance targets.

articles.title: A survey of veterinarians suggests variability in knowledge, attitudes, and practices surrounding antifungal use and stewardship.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess veterinarians' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding antifungal use and stewardship.

METHODS: A survey was developed using an iterative approach with feedback from experts in antifungal therapy and pilot testing among target audiences. The survey was administered in June of 2025 via an online platform to primary care practitioners, dermatologists, and internists and was closed when at least 200 veterinarians had responded. Respondents' scores were calculated for fungal infections and antifungal knowledge, antifungal resistance and stewardship concerns, and comfort with diagnosing fungal infections and prescribing antifungals. Median scores were compared between primary care veterinarians and specialists.

RESULTS: 210 veterinarians (100 primary care practitioners, 49 dermatologists, 61 internists) completed the survey. Significant differences were identified in the median knowledge, concern, and comfort scores, with specialists having higher median scores for all scales. Dermatologists reported significantly higher median weekly topical and systemic antifungal prescribing than primary care veterinarians and internists (20 vs 7.5 vs 0 topical prescriptions/wk, respectively; 9 vs 0 vs 0.5 systemic prescriptions/wk, respectively). Always performing in-house cytology for suspected yeast dermatitis was reported by 49 of 49 dermatologists (100%), 53 of 100 primary care veterinarians (53%), and 19 of 61 internists (31.3%). Always performing in-house cytology for suspected yeast otitis externa was reported by 49 of 49 dermatologists (100%), 39 of 100 primary care veterinarians (39%), and 57 of 61 internists (92.8%).

CONCLUSIONS: Variability in fungal infection and antifungal knowledge, diagnostic practices, and antifungal prescribing across veterinarians highlights the need for targeted antifungal stewardship education.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study provides foundational information for developing veterinary antifungal stewardship initiatives.

articles.title: Prevalence and risk factors for impaired tissue integrity in long-term care settings: A multicenter study.
articles.abstract: This multicenter, cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence and characteristics of tissue integrity impairments including pressure injuries (PIs), incontinence-associated dermatitis, skin tears, and medical device-related PIs among older adults residing in long-term care settings in Türkiye, and to identify associated risk factors. multicenter study was conducted across eight public and seven private nursing homes and residential care centers in Ankara and Istanbul. The study population comprised 1,657 older adults residing in the participating institutions. Using a total population sampling approach, all eligible residents were invited to participate, and 1,037 older adults were included in the study. Data were collected using the Demographic Characteristics Form, the Braden Pressure Ulcer Risk Assessment Scale, the Ghent Global IAD Categorization Tool (GLOBIAD), the International Skin Tear Advisory Panel (ISTAP) classification, and the Modified Barthel Index (MBI). Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, t-tests, analysis of variance, and logistic regression analyses were performed. The overall prevalence of tissue integrity impairment was 13.3%, with specific rates of 3.0% for PIs, 9.3% for incontinence-associated dermatitis, 4.5% for skin tears, and 0.3% for medical device-related pressure injuries. PIs were most frequently observed in the sacral region, incontinence-associated dermatitis in the genital area, and skin tears on the upper limbs. Multivariable logistic regression analyses showed that higher body mass index, lower Braden scores, and the presence of neurological disorders significantly increased the likelihood of tissue integrity impairment. These findings emphasize that maintaining skin integrity is a critical component of quality geriatric care, highlighting the need for continuous risk screening, staff education, and proactive prevention strategies to reduce skin-related complications among institutionalized older adults.

articles.title: Validation of an Electronic Health Record Model for Unplanned Readmission in Patients With Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk scores aim to predict 30-day heart failure (HF) readmissions.

PROJECT RATIONALE: Current models, including Epic's Risk of Unplanned Readmission for a 30-Day Event, demonstrate modest to moderate discriminatory ability (area under the curve: 0.59-0.72).

PROJECT SUMMARY: The goals of this study were to create an electronic health record (EHR)-automatable 30-day HF readmission risk calculator; to test the accuracy of Epic's model to predict 30-day HF readmission risk; and to compare the 2 models. To derive our EHR-automatable model using machine learning, we first performed a systematic review of 30-day HF risk prediction models. We then compared the predictive capabilities of the Epic model with our model. The Epic model had a C-statistic of 0.74, and the derived EHR risk score had a C-statistic of 0.76 (P = 0.41), suggesting comparable performance.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Risk scores are fundamental for personalization of care to accelerate resources for those who need them most. Although both models had moderate discrimination in predicting 30-day HF readmission, the independently derived model provides a platform for future enhancement, such as the inclusion of electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence diagnostics.

articles.title: Preoperative Anxiety Among Hospitalized Pediatric Patients with CHD: A Qualitative Study From the Perspectives of Health Care Professionals and Parents.
articles.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Preoperative anxiety commonly occurs in children with congenital heart disease(CHD), undermining their psychological function and postoperative recovery. Targeted anxiety interventions require a systematic understanding of children's preoperative stress. As key caregivers, parents and health care professionals(HCPs) undrepin intervention development; therefore, this study aimed to explore how parents and HCPs perceive preoperative anxiety in pediatric patients with CHD within the Chinese cutural and social context.

DESIGN: This studyadopted a descripitive phenomenological qualitative approach.

METHODS: . Between January and April 2026, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 parents of pediatric patients with CHD and nine HCPs in a tertiary hospital in Kunming. Interview data were managed via NVivo 12.0 and analyzed through thematic analysis.

FINDINGS: (1) Existence versus non-existence of preoperative anxiety, (2) Preoperative anxiety due to children and parental factors, (3) Diverse manifestations of preoperative anxiety, and (4) Ways of coping with Preoperative Anxiety.

CONCLUSIONS: Anxiety in pediatric patients with CHD is sometimes suppressed or overlooked. It is crucial to improve the ability of parents and HCPs to identify pediatric anxiety and encourage children to express their emotions. Surgery-related information should be delivered to children in age-appropriate and comprehensible language. Given the communal nature of family emotions, parental negative emotions also require attention, and unnecessary parent-child separation should be minimized. Among the management strategies for preoperative anxiety, pharmacological interventions exert rapid effects, while non-pharmacological interventions are more favored due to the absence of adverse reactions. Influenced by the Confucian culture of "forbearance", some parents tend to ignore their children's anxious emotions, highlighting the importance of educating parents about the value of appropriate support.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Significance of Aberrant miR-508-3p Expression in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: The objectives were to investigate serum miR-508-3p expression in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS), determine its value for early diagnosis and prognosis of AIS, and preliminarily explore its underlying mechanism. A total of 131 AIS patients (case group) admitted between January 2023 and December 2024, and 125 healthy individuals (control group) were enrolled. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was performed to detect serum miR-508-3p expression, and an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was conducted to assess the concentrations of IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and CRP in serum samples. The clinical value of miR-508-3p was analyzed using correlation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and Kaplan-Meier methods. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 90-day outcome. In vitro, human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) were subjected to OGD/R; cell viability, injury, and apoptosis were determined by CCK-8, LDH release, and flow cytometry, and the miR-508-3p/SOCS3 targeted binding was confirmed using a dual-luciferase reporter system. Serum miR-508-3p was significantly decreased in AIS patients compared with controls (p < 0.001) and negatively correlated with National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score and levels of IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and CRP (all p < 0.001). ROC analysis yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8641 (95%CI: 0.8184-0.9098), with 87.79% sensitivity and 72.80% specificity. Multivariate analysis confirmed low miR-508-3p as an independent predictor of poor 90-day prognosis (OR 0.002, 95% CI 0.000-0.581, p = 0.032). In vitro, miR-508-3p overexpression enhanced HBMEC viability and reduced LDH release and apoptosis after oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Dual‑luciferase reporter assay confirmed that miR-508-3p targets the 3'UTR of SOCS3. Downregulated serum miR-508-3p is associated with AIS severity, inflammation, and poor prognosis, suggesting its diagnostic and prognostic potential. Its protective effect may involve targeting suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 (SOCS3) and alleviating brain microvascular endothelial cell injury.

articles.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
articles.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

articles.title: HeartFusion: A Cross-Modality Transformer for Accurate Cardiovascular Disease Diagnosis and Severity Assessment.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires diagnostic models that can integrate complementary electrophysiological and anatomical information while also representing ordered disease severity. HeartFusion was developed as a mathematically informed cross-modality Transformer framework combining electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Wavelet-derived ECG time-frequency representations were encoded with Cardioformer, MRI structure was encoded with TransUNet, and modality-specific embeddings were aligned in a shared latent space using cosine-similarity-based cross-modal attention. A transformer classifier performed diagnostic prediction, while an ordinal regression head modeled four ordered severity stages. Three controlled pseudo-paired benchmark cohorts were constructed from PTB-XL with ACDC (CVD-I), MIMIC-IV-ECG with CMRxRecon (CVD-II), and PTB-XL/MIMIC-IV-ECG with OCMR/Cardiac Atlas Project data (CVD-III). Source observations were partitioned before pseudo-pair construction to prevent cross-partition leakage, and five matched random seeds were used for evaluation. HeartFusion achieved diagnostic accuracies of 97.73%, 98.23%, and 98.02%, with AUC values of 98.12%, 98.76%, and 98.39% on CVD-I, CVD-II, and CVD-III, respectively. Severity staging achieved ordinal accuracies above 90%, with the best Cohen's kappa of 0.839 and MAE of 0.340. These findings support phenotype-level multimodal representation learning, while validation on genuinely patient-matched ECG-MRI cohorts remains necessary before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Robot-Assisted Gasless Trans-Hairline Excision of Submandibular Gland Tumors.
articles.abstract: Benign submandibular gland tumors are usually resected through a transcervical incision, which provides direct exposure but leaves visible cervical scarring. Remote-access endoscopic techniques improve scar concealment but can be limited by two-dimensional visualization, assistant-dependent camera control, and rigid instrument collision in the narrow submandibular gland space. This article presents a standardized video protocol for robot-assisted submandibular gland excision via a gasless trans-hairline approach for benign tumors. The procedure begins with postauricular trans-hairline incision design, subplatysmal flap elevation, and mechanical retractor-based creation of a gasless working cavity. After robotic docking, a 3D endoscope and articulated instruments are used for sequential dissection of the superior, posterior, inferior, deep, and anterior glandular borders. Critical steps include protection of the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve, management of the facial vein and facial artery branches, exposure of the digastric and mylohyoid muscles, identification of the lingual nerve, division of submandibular ganglion branches, clipping of Wharton's duct, en bloc gland-and-tumor retrieval, hemostasis, drainage, and layered closure. Ten female patients with clinically benign submandibular gland tumors underwent this procedure. All operations were completed robotically without conversion. The mean operative time was 134.5 min ± 36.9 min, the mean estimated blood loss was 16.2 mL ± 7.6 mL, and the mean incision length was 5.6 ± 0.5 cm. Final pathology confirmed pleomorphic adenoma in all patients. No major vascular injury, postoperative marginal mandibular, lingual, or hypoglossal nerve dysfunction, hematoma, seroma, infection, or salivary fistula was observed during the available follow-up. This protocol provides a reproducible workflow for selected patients, although larger studies with longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Taohong Siwu Decoction-Based Targeted Drug Penetration Therapy for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Hip Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a common complication after hip fracture surgery, and complementary strategies targeting coagulation, inflammation, and venous circulation may provide additional preventive benefits. This retrospective cohort study included 86 patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between June 2023 and June 2024. Patients were assigned to a control group (n = 43), receiving standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis, or an observation group (n = 43), receiving additional Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy. The primary outcome was postoperative lower limb DVT within 10 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included coagulation parameters, inflammatory markers, femoral venous blood flow velocities, postoperative pain, limb swelling, and treatment-related adverse events. DVT occurred in 1/43 patients (2.33%) in the observation group and 10/43 patients (23.26%) in the control group (Fisher's exact P = 0.007). In a parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age and baseline D-dimer, adjunctive therapy remained associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative DVT (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.68, P = 0.017). After 10 days of treatment, the observation group had lower Faces Pain Scale-Revised scores and limb swelling, longer activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, lower D-dimer levels, higher common and superficial femoral vein blood flow velocities, and lower serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 levels than the control group (all P < 0.05). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in overall adverse-event occurrence, and no severe treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy combined with standard anticoagulation was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative DVT and favorable differences in coagulation, inflammatory, and venous hemodynamic parameters.

articles.title: Machine Learning and Post-Hoc Feature Attribution for Predicting Cardiac MRI Motion Artifacts: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Anxiety-induced motion artifacts frequently compromise image quality during non-sedated cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), leading to rescans and increased healthcare burdens. This retrospective cohort study hypothesized that combining multidimensional psychological and physiological indicators could accurately predict artifact occurrence. Baseline data from 514 adult patients, encompassing 15 clinical features, were systematically analyzed. Four machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The eXtreme Gradient Boosting model demonstrated the highest discriminative ability (AUC = 0.875). To provide clinical transparency, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was applied, revealing that state anxiety (evaluated via the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory State subscale, STAI-State), maximum breath-hold duration, and heart rate variability were primarily associated with artifact risk. The novelty of this approach lies in uncovering non-linear threshold effects-such as a sharp risk escalation when STAI-State scores exceeded 45-and complex interactions between physical capacity and claustrophobia. In conclusion, this interpretable machine learning framework offers a robust tool for patient-specific risk stratification, suggesting that preemptive and targeted nursing interventions could be optimized based on individualized algorithmic predictions.

articles.title: Association of Admission Serum Homocysteine with Discharge Neurocognitive Dysfunction after Acute Cerebrovascular Disease in a High-Altitude Setting.
articles.abstract: Discharge-phase neurocognitive abnormalities may affect rehabilitation participation, self-management, and discharge safety after acute cerebrovascular disease, but early clinically accessible correlates remain incompletely defined. We examined the association between admission serum homocysteine and clinically adjudicated discharge neurocognitive dysfunction in a high-altitude clinical setting. This single-center retrospective cohort included 227 adults admitted for acute ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or transient ischemic attack. The first available serum homocysteine measurement within 24 h of hospital arrival was analyzed continuously and by cohort-derived tertiles. The primary outcome was neurocognitive dysfunction documented within 24-48 h before discharge and adjudicated independently by two reviewers blinded to homocysteine levels; standardized cognitive instruments were not systematically available. Logistic regression was sequentially adjusted for demographic, renal, neurological, neuroimaging, and cerebrovascular phenotype-related factors. Among 227 patients, 98 (43.2%) had discharge neurocognitive dysfunction. Admission homocysteine was higher in patients with dysfunction than in those without dysfunction (18.3 ± 6.2 vs. 12.4 ± 4.7 µmol/L, P < 0.001), and dysfunction prevalence increased from 22.4% in T1 to 38.5% in T2 and 69.9% in T3 (P for trend < 0.001). In the primary fully adjusted model, each 1 µmol/L increase in homocysteine was associated with higher odds of dysfunction (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.07-1.21, P < 0.001), and T3 versus T1 remained associated with the outcome (OR 4.36, 95% CI 2.00-9.51, P < 0.001). Estimates were similar in prespecified sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of delirium or positive confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU) screening and restriction to acute ischemic stroke. Higher admission homocysteine was associated with discharge-phase neurocognitive dysfunction, supporting prospective evaluation of homocysteine as a potential marker of short-term neurocognitive vulnerability rather than a validated predictor of persistent post-stroke cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Sacubitril/Valsartan Improves Cardiovascular Outcomes in Elderly Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Hypertension: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Elderly patients with concurrent coronary artery disease (CAD) and hypertension face elevated risks of cardiovascular events and require therapies that balance efficacy, safety, and tolerability. Sacubitril/valsartan has demonstrated benefits in heart failure management, but evidence regarding its long-term cardiovascular outcomes in this specific population remains limited. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 150 elderly patients with CAD and hypertension to compare the effects of sacubitril/valsartan versus amlodipine, both combined with conventional therapy. The primary endpoint was the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 12 months. Two MACE definitions were applied in this study. Primary analysis used our predefined composite endpoint, including aggravated heart failure and arrhythmia events. A sensitivity analysis adopted the conventional MACE definition (myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, revascularization), excluding isolated ventricular premature beats. Secondary endpoints included blood pressure control, cardiac function parameters, and treatment-related adverse events. Results showed that patients treated with sacubitril/valsartan had a significantly lower incidence of MACE (10.26% vs. 27.14%, P = 0.008), superior blood pressure control, and improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) compared to the amlodipine group. Cox proportional hazards regression (Cox regression) analysis identified sacubitril/valsartan treatment as an independent protective factor against cardiovascular adverse events (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.38, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.80, P = 0.011). Both regimens were well-tolerated, with no severe adverse events reported. These findings indicate that sacubitril/valsartan is an effective and safe therapeutic option for elderly patients with CAD and hypertension, reducing long-term cardiovascular risk while improving blood pressure control and cardiac function.

articles.title: Nociception Level-Guided Multimodal Analgesia with External Oblique Intercostal Plane Block in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy.
