articles.abstract: Effective perioperative analgesia remains essential in laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC), where pneumoperitoneum produces the most intense nociceptive stimulus despite the minimally invasive nature of the procedure. Objective monitoring of nociception using the nociception level (NOL) index may optimize intraoperative opioid titration; however, its integration into multimodal analgesia (MMA) strategies incorporating regional techniques has not been adequately studied. The study was conducted using a double-blind design in which patients and the postoperative outcome assessor were blinded to group allocation, whereas the investigator performing the EOIP block was necessarily unblinded. This randomized controlled trial investigated whether NOL-guided MMA, including an external oblique intercostal plane (EOIP) block, improves intraoperative nociceptive control and early postoperative pain compared with conventional intravenous analgesia. Sixty-two ASA I-II adults undergoing elective LC were randomized to receive either an EOIP block with dexketoprofen and magnesium infusion or intravenous dexketoprofen alone. In both groups, remifentanil infusion was titrated according to predefined NOL thresholds, and anesthetic depth was maintained using BIS monitoring. NOL values during pneumoperitoneum were significantly lower in the MMA group (mean difference: 13.51; 95% CI: 4.68-22.34; p < 0.004), indicating superior attenuation of peak nociceptive responses. Emergence pain scores were also reduced in the MMA group (p < 0.001), whereas total remifentanil consumption did not differ between groups. Sevoflurane requirements and extubation times were significantly lower in the MMA group, suggesting a potential anesthetic-sparing effect. No differences were observed in postoperative opioid rescue, nausea/vomiting, or other adverse events. These findings demonstrate that NOL-guided MMA incorporating EOIP block enhances intraoperative nociceptive stability and improves early postoperative analgesia without increasing opioid use. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these results and further refine NOL-integrated multimodal analgesic strategies.

articles.title: MicroRNA Regulatory Networks in Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Mechanisms from Steatosis and Inflammation to Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide and progresses through steatosis, alcohol-associated hepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are established post-transcriptional regulators whose roles in ALD-associated signaling networks have been increasingly characterized. Recent high-throughput sequencing and functional studies have revealed dual regulatory roles of miRNA families, such as miR-122, miR-155, and miR-21, at different disease stages. However, most studies have focused on individual miRNAs, and network-level cooperative regulation and clinical translation remain underexplored. This narrative review examines the molecular mechanisms of miRNAs in alcohol-induced steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, with a particular focus on network-level cooperative regulation. Key findings indicate that miRNAs function as stage-specific and cell-type-specific regulators, with miR-122, miR-155, miR-21, miR-29, and miR-34a acting as central network nodes. These insights provide a framework for the identification of early diagnostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in ALD.

articles.title: Vacuum-Assisted Breast Biopsy and Excision for Breast Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Malignant Upgrade in B3 Lesions.
articles.abstract: Vacuum-assisted breast biopsy (VAB/VABB) and vacuum-assisted excision (VAE) serve distinct diagnostic and therapeutic roles, requiring pathway-specific evaluation of their outcomes. This systematic review reconstructed a report-level and outcome-level dataset from 26 publications, of which 18 were reviewed in full text and 8 remained incompletely retrieved. Reports without complete full text were retained for narrative context but excluded from quantitative synthesis. Five full-text studies contributed 98 malignant upgrades among 844 B3 lesions after diagnostic VAB/VABB. The pooled proportion was 11.23% (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.22%-17.04%; 95% prediction interval [PI], 4.56%-25.06%; I2 = 60.8%). Three full-text studies of second-line VAE reported study-specific upgrade proportions from 5.1% to 21.4%; these estimates were not pooled because selection pathways and case mix differed substantially. Post-VAE radiologic removal, absence of residual lesion, and recurrence-free outcomes ranged from 86.0% to 99.2% across five full-text cohorts but were not combined because they represented different endpoints and follow-up intervals. Only one fully retrieved study provided reconstructable diagnostic 2 × 2 data, precluding a diagnostic meta-analysis or hierarchical model. Certainty was very low for the principal observational outcomes and low for the single randomized comparison. The evidence supports pathway-specific interpretation and multidisciplinary decision-making, not universal superiority over core needle biopsy or equivalence to surgical excision.

articles.title: Impact of Phosphatidylinositol 3-Kinase and B-Raf Mutations in Rat Sarcoma Wild-Type Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Activating mutations in phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha (PIK3CA) and B-Raf proto-oncogene (BRAF) are hypothesized to confer primary resistance to anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (anti-EGFR) monoclonal antibodies in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). However, the clinical impact of these mutations in patients with rat sarcoma (RAS) wild-type tumors remains incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association of PIK3CA and BRAF mutations with clinical outcomes in RAS wild-type mCRC patients receiving first-line EGFR inhibitor therapy. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and OVID from inception through June 2019, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. From 600 screened records, 10 studies comprising 1,478 patients with RAS wild-type mCRC were included. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), and risk differences (RDs) for objective response rate (ORR), were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). PIK3CA mutations were associated with significantly worse PFS (HR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.11-1.71; p = 0.004) and OS (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.22-2.05; p < 0.001). BRAF mutations were similarly associated with worse PFS (HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.46-1.94; p < 0.001) and OS (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.09-1.49; p = 0.003). No significant difference in ORR was observed for either PIK3CA mutations (RD, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.38 to 0.15; p = 0.38) or BRAF mutations (RD, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.28 to 0.04; p = 0.15) compared with wild-type. These findings confirm that PIK3CA and BRAF mutations are negative prognostic biomarkers in RAS wild-type mCRC, associated with inferior PFS and OS but not ORR. Incorporating BRAF and PIK3CA mutation testing into pretreatment evaluation is supported, and alternative therapeutic strategies for mutation carriers are needed. Prospective validation in larger studies is warranted.

articles.title: High-Throughput Spot Assay for Isolation of Bacteriophages Against Multiple Host Strains from Environmental Samples.
articles.abstract: Phage therapy has emerged as a promising option for treating infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria, offering an alternative to conventional antibiotics. However, conventional isolation methods are laborious and tend to favor dominant host-phage pairs, limiting the diversity of recoverable phages. Expanding the collection of phages is therefore a critical step toward advancing phage-based therapies. To achieve effective isolation outcomes, it is essential to systematically screen environmental samples against a broad range of host strains under standardized conditions. The efficiency of phage recovery depends on several factors, including enrichment strategies, host range coverage, and infection dynamics. To address these challenges, we have developed a streamlined protocol that integrates liquid culture enrichment, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-mediated concentration, high-throughput spot screening on multiple host bacterial lawns, and subsequent streak purification for clonal isolation. This approach enables simultaneous screening of environmental samples against multiple pathogens in a single experimental setup, improving isolation efficiency. Notably, it enhances the recovery of phages with diverse host ranges. Our integrated workflow can reduce manual effort and material consumption and shorten the isolation period compared with conventional methods. This robust and evidence-based method accelerates the discovery of phages with potential applications in therapy and biocontrol. We anticipate that this protocol will prove particularly useful for building phage biobanks, preparing personalized phage therapeutics, and conducting large-scale environmental phage mining. Ultimately, it will help expand the repertoire of characterized phages for combating antimicrobial-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: A Standardized Workflow for Multimodal Assessment of Right-to-Left Shunt-Related Ischemic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract: Right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been associated with cryptogenic stroke, migraine, and other neurological conditions in which ischemic brain injury may be clinically relevant. In routine practice, however, assessment is often fragmented. Shunt presence may be documented, but shunt burden, provoked versus non-provoked patterns, anatomical complexity, and MRI-defined brain injury are not always integrated into a reproducible workflow. Here, we describe a standardized protocol for multimodal assessment of RLS-related ischemic brain injury in a clinically selected cohort. The workflow includes patient screening, exclusion of major vascular and systemic factors that could independently contribute to brain parenchymal injury, contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler ultrasound (c-TCD) confirmation and shunt grading, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) classification, transthoracic and/or transesophageal echocardiographic anatomical assessment, structured data extraction, and dataset cleaning. To improve reproducibility, the protocol also standardizes key coding steps, including shunt-grade harmonization, classification of RLS as simple or complex, and interpretation of D-dimer values reported below the assay threshold. Using this workflow, a harmonized analytic cohort of 60 RLS-positive patients was established. MRI identified 23 MRI-negative and 37 MRI-positive patients. Representative analyses showed that MRI-positive findings were more frequent in patients with greater shunt burden and more complex anatomical phenotypes. This protocol provides an operational model for incorporating c-TCD, MRI, echocardiography, and structured clinical parameters into the evaluation of MRI-defined ischemic brain injury in RLS-positive patients. It should be interpreted as a workflow for standardized multimodal phenotyping rather than as a standalone physiologic assessment of all clinically significant or hypoxemia-related RLS.

articles.title: Lactobacillus derived small RNAs protect against Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a major multidrug-resistant pathogen with limited treatment options. Plant-derived natural products have broad biological activities, but their protective effects against extraintestinal multidrug-resistant bacterial infections remain poorly understood. Herein, we show that selected plant-derived natural products protect mice against CRKP pulmonary infection by remodeling the gut microbiota. Fecal microbiota transplantation and microbiota-depletion experiments demonstrated that this protection was microbiota dependent, with Lactobacillus emerging as a key genus associated with reduced pulmonary bacterial burden. Among four isolated Lactobacillus species, Lactobacillus murinus (L. murinus) conferred the strongest protection against CRKP infection. Mechanistically, L. murinus-derived membrane vesicles (MVs) delivered the small RNA mim-miR-21a-5p to pulmonary macrophages, where it targeted PDCD4 and activated the Nrf2/SOD2 antioxidant pathway. This signaling cascade preserved mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, promoted an M2-like macrophage phenotype, and ultimately restricted CRKP infection. Consistent with these findings, intestinal Lactobacillus, particularly L. murinus, was reduced in patients with CRKP infection compared with healthy controls. Collectively, our findings reveal a mechanism by which plant-derived natural products enhance host resistance to CRKP through microbiota remodeling and identify L. murinus-derived small RNAs and membrane vesicles as key mediator of this gut-lung protective axis.

articles.title: Human immunodeficiency virus infection mimicking very early onset inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract: Very early onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD), defined as diagnosis before 6 years of age, is often associated with immune dysregulation and monogenic etiologies; however, infectious mimics may be overlooked in low-prevalence regions. We report a 4-year-old male with poor weight gain, intermittent diarrhea, elevated fecal calprotectin, and persistently elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Endoscopy showed diffuse friable colonic mucosa, and biopsies demonstrated focal active colitis with mild crypt distortion. He was diagnosed with VEO-IBD and treated with mesalamine, infliximab, adalimumab, and upadacitinib, with incomplete response. At age 7, he was hospitalized with fever, cytopenias, and pulmonary infiltrates; human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) testing was positive, with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cytomegalovirus viremia. After discontinuing immunosuppression and initiating antiretroviral therapy, gastrointestinal symptoms and inflammatory markers improved. HIV-associated colitis can closely mimic VEO-IBD, and progressive lymphopenia should prompt evaluation for secondary immunodeficiency.

articles.title: Sulfonylurea receptor 1 deficiency alleviates acute lung injury by activating PARP1 in epithelial cells.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical disease with high mortality, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. In this study, we investigated sulfonylurea receptor 1 (SUR1), the regulatory subunit of ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels, in the progression of ALI. We observed elevated SUR1 protein levels in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) of patients with sepsis-associated ALI, as well as in BALF and lung tissues of ALI mouse models. Genetic deletion of SUR1, but not Kir6.2 (the pore-forming subunit of KATP channels), significantly alleviated ALI induced by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) or by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) intratracheal instillation. Mechanistically, SUR1 interacted with poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1), impairing DNA damage repair and promoting apoptosis and NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa B) activation in bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, glibenclamide, a clinically approved SUR1 inhibitor, significantly alleviated ALI, at least in part, by disrupting the SUR1-PARP1 interaction. Our findings identify SUR1 as a new therapeutic target and highlight the potential repurposing of glibenclamide as a therapeutic drug in ALI.

articles.title: Evidence for exposure to and infection with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses among polar bears inhabiting Alaska.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) have become widespread among wildlife including within the Arctic. We summarize histopathological findings for three cases of HPAIV infection among polar bears (Ursus maritimus) inhabiting Alaska, genomically characterize viruses causing disease, and assess probable non-lethal exposures. Polar bears found dead and infected with HPAIVs exhibited meningoencephalomyelitis and neuronal necrosis, consistent with neurologic disease. Genomic sequence information obtained for H5N1 and H5N5 subtype HPAIVs associated with two cases supported epidemiologically independent spillovers. Serologic testing provided evidence for antibodies reactive to H5 and N1 antigens among most polar bears inhabiting Alaska during 2023-2024, consistent with contemporary non-lethal exposures, whereas antibodies were not found among bears sampled during 2013. These data indicate that HPAIV infection may represent an emerging threat to polar bear health within the Alaska Arctic; though, population immunity seems to be building and may protect this species from widespread demographic impacts of disease.

articles.title: Diabetes Mellitus Is Associated With Increased Risk for Subsequent Hip Arthroscopy After Index Hip Arthroscopy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether diabetes mellitus is associated with higher systemic and hip-specific complications and to evaluate reoperation rates after hip arthroscopy.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX Research Network and Current Procedural Terminology and International Classification of Diseases codes, we identified diabetic and nondiabetic patients aged 12 to 65 years who underwent hip arthroscopy between 2005 and 2025. Ninety-day systemic complications and 6-month, 1-year, and 3-year hip-specific outcomes were evaluated. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed on 35 demographic and comorbidity variables. Risk analyses, Kaplan-Meier curves, and Cox proportional hazards models compared outcomes, with significance set at α = 0.05.

RESULTS: After matching, 1784 diabetic and 1784 nondiabetic patients were included. At 90 days, diabetes was associated with a higher hospital admission rate (odds ratio [OR] 1.83, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.16-2.87, P = .01). Diabetic patients had higher rates of subsequent hip arthroscopy at 1 year (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.12-1.79, P = .004) and 3 years (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.14-1.69, P = .001). Rates of arthroscopic irrigation and debridement were higher in patients with diabetes at 6 months (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.09-3.00, P = .019), 1 year (OR 1.96, 95% CI 1.32-2.92, P = .001), and 3 years (OR 1.75, 95% CI 1.29-2.37, P < .001). Infection diagnoses were also higher among diabetic patients at 6 months (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.06-2.52, P = .033) and 3 years (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.24-2.33, P = .008).

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes was not associated with higher rates of most early systemic complications after hip arthroscopy, although hospital admissions were more common among patients with diabetes. Diabetes was associated with higher rates of subsequent hip arthroscopy procedures, arthroscopic irrigation and debridement, and infection diagnoses after index hip arthroscopy; however, these findings should be interpreted in the context of database limitations, including the inability to confirm laterality or ipsilateral revision status.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Recent advances in medical hemostatic materials: Mechanisms, evaluation, and clinical perspectives.
articles.abstract: Uncontrolled hemorrhage remains a major cause of preventable death in trauma and surgery, yet the performance of hemostatic materials varies markedly with wound geometry, blood flow, coagulation status, and tissue sensitivity. This review critically examines natural polymer-based, synthetic polymer-based, inorganic, and composite hemostats by linking material structure to six principal mechanisms: fluid absorption and surface adsorption, coagulation activation, bioactive-factor delivery, photothermal assistance, adhesive sealing, and microstructural regulation. Beyond cataloging materials, we compare class-specific advantages, failure modes, and safety constraints, and analyze how hemodilution, hypothermia, acidosis, anticoagulation, infection, and high-flow bleeding reshape material performance. We further integrate clinically used products, scenario-based material selection, and a staged evaluation framework spanning mechanistic assays, hostile-condition testing, translational bleeding models, rebleeding assessment, and post-hemostasis safety. Finally, we outline stage-matched pathways for responsive and multifunctional systems. This mechanism-scenario-evaluation framework supports more rigorous design, comparison, and clinical translation of next-generation hemostatic materials.

articles.title: An Integrative Multi-Omic Biomarker Panel Distinguishes Hepatocellular Carcinoma From Chronic Liver Disease in HBV-Predominant Populations.
articles.journal: Hepatology research : the official journal of the Japan Society of Hepatology
articles.abstract:
AIM: DNA methylation is a promising diagnostic biomarker for various cancers including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aimed to identify aberrant DNA methylation and protein alterations via integrated approaches and develop a highly predictive biomarker panel for blood-based discrimination of HCC from non-HCC chronic liver disease (CLD) in an HBV-predominant population.

METHODS: Genome-wide methylation profiling was conducted to screen hypermethylated CpG sites and genes distinguishing 55 HCC and matched non-HCC tissues. Candidate marker genes were then evaluated with five protein markers in 299 blood samples, and a diagnostic model was developed and validated in an independent cohort of 149 participants.

RESULTS: Methylation pattern analysis identified 44 candidate hypermethylation biomarkers using four strategies. Through cross-validation, a panel of six methylation markers from four different groups yielded an AUC of 0.938, surpassing other methylation marker panels. A logistic regression model incorporating four DNA methylation markers and two protein markers achieved sensitivities of 91.8% and 88.4% at specificities of 95.4% and 93.8% in the training and validation sets, respectively. The 6-marker panel showed higher sensitivity of 82.9% for BCLC 0-A HCC, outperforming alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and des-gamma-carboxyprothrombin (DCP).

CONCLUSIONS: The developed 6-marker model demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for distinguishing HCC from non-HCC CLD in the studied HBV-predominant cohorts. It outperformed AFP and DCP in this case-control setting and may have potential for blood-based HCC detection. Prospective validation in surveillance cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a focus on patients with impaired ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) normalized to creatinine in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), focusing on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 144 patients emergently admitted for ACS, with urinary NGAL measured 4-48 h postadmission. Primary and secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), respectively. Optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoffs were determined using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Associations between urinary NGAL/creatinine and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: During a median 734.5-day follow-up, 8 deaths and 44 MACCE occurred. The optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoff for predicting MACCE was 20.85 ng/mg creatinine. All deaths occurred in the high NGAL/creatinine group (≥20.85), but mortality analyses were limited by statistical separation. High NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with MACCE (hazard ratio = 3.47, 95% confidence interval = 1.61-7.47) and remained associated with a higher event hazard after adjustment for age, brain natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.75; P = 0.017). In subgroup analyses, the area under the curve for MACCE was numerically higher in patients with LVEF <50% than in those with LVEF ≥50% (0.753 vs. 0.581). Formal interaction testing in the Cox model, however, did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF category (P for interaction = 0.100).

CONCLUSION: Urinary NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with long-term MACCE in patients with ACS. Although subgroup analyses showed numerically different associations according to LVEF, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF.

articles.title: Postpartum Blood Pressure After Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Subsequent Cardiovascular Disease: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between blood pressure values at 6 weeks postpartum and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) over a 20-year period among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).

DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.

SETTING: English primary and secondary care data, linked to cause-specific mortality records from 2000 to 2020.

POPULATION: A cohort of 39 934 women between 15 and 49 years of age at birth who had HDP, were registered with a general practitioner (GP) contributing to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), and eligible for linkage to hospital episode statistics (HES) data were included. We excluded 22 100 (55.3%) women with no blood pressure values recorded at 6 weeks postpartum.

METHODS: Primary analysis included multivariable Cox regression modelling (weighted by the inverse probability of having a severe HDP).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Validated composite outcome of 12 cardiovascular diseases.

RESULTS: The rate for incident cardiovascular events was 109 per 10 000 person-years; 794 (68%) of them occurred in women aged < 40 years. Women with abnormal blood pressure at 6 weeks postpartum had a higher risk of subsequent CVD than women with normal blood pressure: 10.9% vs. 5.4% - adjusted hazard ratio 1.96 (95% CI 1.51-2.54).

CONCLUSIONS: Less than half of women with HDP had a blood pressure record in their GP notes at 6 weeks postpartum. The absence of a record of normal blood pressure at this time point was associated with an increased risk for subsequent CVD The immediate postpartum period may be a crucial window in preventive care to improve women's health.

articles.title: Research trends and hotspots in colorectal cancer screening: Bibliometric and visualization analysis (2015-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC), is a highly prevalent malignant tumor worldwide, and early screening is key to improving its prognosis. Currently, CRC screening research is growing exponentially, but its core research hotspots, evolutionary trends, and interdisciplinary features are not clear. In this study, we used bibliometric analysis to analyze the distribution of literature, research hotspots, and cutting-edge developments in the field of CRC screening worldwide, and to provide a scientific basis for optimizing screening strategies.

METHODS: Publications on CRC screening from 2015 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer (v1.6.20), RStudio (v4.4.1), and CiteSpace (v6.4.2) were used for bibliometric and visual analyses. The main analyses included publication trends, countries, authors, journals, references, and keywords.

RESULT: A total of 3245 publications were included in the analysis. Global publications on CRC screening showed a steady upward trend over the past decade, with an annual growth rate of 2.17%. The United States contributed the highest number of publications, and the University of North Carolina ranked as the most productive institution. GASTROENTEROLOGY and GUT were the most frequently cited journals in this field. Lansdorp‑Vogelaar I was among the most prolific authors. The most cited article was "CRC screening for average-risk adults: 2018 guideline update from the American Cancer Society." Keyword analysis showed that the research hotspots in this field included colonoscopy, biomarker, adenoma detection rate, artificial intelligence, etc.

CONCLUSION: Current research in CRC screening focuses on traditional screening methods, population-related factors, and emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. Stronger international collaboration and interdisciplinary studies are needed to advance the field.

articles.title: Life-threatening diffuse alveolar hemorrhage associated with Rhinovirus infection and the potential role of corticosteroids in immunocompetent patients: Case reports.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is a rare but potentially fatal condition characterized by bleeding into alveolar spaces, most often associated with autoimmune disease or severe infection. Rhinovirus is a common cause of upper respiratory tract infection but is rarely associated with DAH in immunocompetent individuals. We report 2 cases of life-threatening DAH associated with rhinovirus infection, both presenting with severe hypoxemia and showing marked improvement following corticosteroid therapy.

PATIENT CONCERNS: Case 1: An 85-year-old woman presented with massive hemoptysis, dyspnea, and hypoxemia. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGOs) and patchy consolidations. Case 2: A 70-year-old woman developed worsening dyspnea and hemoptysis despite antibiotics. She was hypoxemic, and chest CT showed bilateral GGOs and consolidations.

DIAGNOSES: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrated progressively hemorrhagic aliquots consistent with DAH in both cases. Multiplex viral polymerase chain reaction identified rhinovirus as the sole pathogen in both cases, and autoimmune serologic tests were negative.

INTERVENTIONS: Both patients received high-flow oxygen therapy, empirical antibiotics, and systemic corticosteroids (Case 1: intravenous methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg/day; Case 2: intravenous methylprednisolone 500 mg/day for 3 days, followed by tapering).

OUTCOMES: After corticosteroid therapy, both patients showed rapid clinical and radiographic improvement, with resolution of hypoxemia and discharge within 10 days.

LESSONS: These cases suggest a potential association between rhinovirus infection and life-threatening DAH in immunocompetent patients. Both patients showed marked clinical improvement after corticosteroid therapy, suggesting a potential therapeutic role for systemic corticosteroids. Thus, clinicians should consider rhinovirus infection as a possible infectious trigger of DAH, and systemic corticosteroids may be considered in selected severe cases.

articles.title: Peritoneal catheter fixation versus nonfixation in open surgery: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective of this study was to compare the advantages and disadvantages of peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter fixation versus nonfixation in open surgery for PD catheter placement.

METHODS: We searched the PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang databases from their inception to March 1, 2025. Eligible studies comparing PD catheter fixation with nonfixation in open surgery were included. The data were analyzed using Review Manager Version 5.3 and Stata Version 14.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included in the meta-analysis. A total of 648 patients were included in the PD catheter fixation group, and 627 patients were included in the PD catheter nonfixation group. Compared with PD catheter nonfixation, PD catheter fixation reduced the incidence of catheter displacement during open surgery (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.04-0.16; P < .00001). However, there were no differences between the catheter fixation and catheter nonfixation groups concerning catheter malfunction without catheter displacement (OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.29-8.00, P = .62), omentum wrapping (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.18, P = .09), infection (OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.51-1.78, P = .87), bleeding (OR 2.78, 95% CI 0.11-69.74, P = .53), infusion pain (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.15-1.16, P = .10), or hernia (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.11-4.07, P = .65). In addition, the operating time in the catheter fixation group was longer than that in the catheter nonfixation group (mean difference 4.18, 95% CI 1.42-6.94; P = .003).

CONCLUSION: PD catheter fixation increased the operating time, but it reduced the incidence of catheter displacement and did not increase other complications in open surgery. PD catheter fixation is safe and effective in open surgery.

articles.title: Prevalence of mobility limitations among the elderly in Saudi Arabia: A secondary analysis of the 2025 Elderly Survey.
articles.abstract: Mobility limitations in terms of walking and stair climbing among the elderly are associated with limitations in activities of daily living (ADL), higher annual healthcare expenditure, more hospitalizations, and increased mortality. However, evidence on the prevalence of mobility limitation among the elderly in Saudi Arabia remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate this issue using data from a national public survey. Data were obtained from the 2025 Elderly Survey, which was designed and administered by the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) of Saudi Arabia. Secondary analysis was applied. The survey included both Saudi and non-Saudi residents from 13 administrative regions across the kingdom (n = 32,745 households, which yielded a weighted national population of approximately 1,758,737 individuals). In total, 42% of the individuals were aged 60 to 64 years, and 25.5% of the individuals experienced mild difficulty in terms of mobility, specifically walking and climbing stairs, whereas 10.8% experienced severe difficulty. Furthermore, 61.8% of the individuals were not physically active. Additionally, 44.7% of the individuals had multiple chronic conditions, 25.5% had 1 chronic condition, and 29.8% had no chronic conditions. The survey data indicated that more than one-third of the elderly in Saudi Arabia have mild-to-severe mobility limitations in terms of walking and climbing stairs.

articles.title: Effects of blood flow restriction training in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) has been proposed as a low-load rehabilitation strategy for symptomatic and postoperative upper-limb musculoskeletal conditions. This review evaluated the clinical effects, tolerability, and prescription characteristics of BFRT in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

METHODS: This systematic review was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261299726) and reported with reference to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. CENTRAL/Cochrane Library, Embase via Ovid, MEDLINE/PubMed, Science Citation Index/Web of Science, and Scopus were searched without a start-date restriction before February 18, 2026; backward reference-list/citation checking was also used. Randomized trials, case series, and case reports were eligible. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity, and studies were appraised using risk of bias 2 or design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute checklists.

RESULTS: Twenty reports were included: 9 parallel-group randomized trials, 1 randomized crossover trial, 2 case series, and 8 case-report publications. Across the reports, 340 participants were enrolled or randomized and 326 contributed to the analyzed/treated clinical samples; 158 were men (48.5%) and 168 were women (51.5%). In a sham-controlled lateral elbow tendinopathy trial, BFRT resulted in a significantly greater reduction in 12-week pain (between-group difference -1.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.89 to -0.18; P = .026) and patient-rated tennis elbow evaluation (PRTEE) (-15.23, 95% CI -23.57 to -6.90; P < .001). In patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis, PRTEE reduction (-24.20 ± 4.02 vs -15.60 ± 3.71; P = .001) and quick disabilities of the arm, shoulder and hand reduction (-12.83 ± 4.97 vs -7.51 ± 4.72; P = .025) were significantly greater with BFRT plus conventional therapy, whereas between-group pain and strength changes were not significant. In nonoperative distal-radius-fracture rehabilitation, mean activity-pain reduction was 4.0 versus 2.3 points (P = .03). In rotator-cuff tendinopathy, BFRT resulted in significantly greater biceps thickness (P = .002) and internal-rotation strength (P = .040). Conversely, a pragmatic elbow trial found no significant between-group difference in 12-month PRTEE (adjusted contrast + 4.32, 95% CI -9.17 to 17.81; P = .53).

CONCLUSION: BFRT may be considered a low-load adjunct in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation settings, but it is not consistently superior to active rehabilitation for pain, strength, or function. Confidence remains limited by small samples, heterogeneous prescriptions and co-interventions, uncontrolled designs, and incomplete adverse-event ascertainment.

articles.title: Integrated network toxicology, transcriptomic, and Mendelian randomization analyses explore potential molecular links between acrylamide exposure and clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Acrylamide is a potential carcinogen widely encountered in occupational settings and heat-processed foods. However, the potential molecular relationships between acrylamide-associated targets and clear cell renal cell carcinoma remain poorly characterized. The toxicological characteristics of acrylamide were predicted using ProTox-3.0 and ADMETlab 3.0. Potential acrylamide-associated targets were identified using SwissTargetPrediction, the Similarity Ensemble Approach, and TargetNet and were intersected with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC)-related genes obtained from GeneCards. Protein-protein interaction networks and functional enrichment analyses were performed using Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins, Cytoscape, and bioinformatics approaches to characterize the biological functions of the shared targets. Using The Cancer Genome Atlas Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma transcriptomic data, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox regression was applied to identify prognostic genes and construct a risk-prediction model. Two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis was subsequently conducted to evaluate associations between genetically predicted candidate-gene expression and kidney cancer risk. Representative immunohistochemical images from the Human Protein Atlas were examined as qualitative supporting evidence. Acrylamide was predicted to have potential carcinogenic properties. Among 161 putative acrylamide-associated targets and 1235 ccRCC-related genes, 50 overlapping targets were identified and were mainly enriched in chemical stress, oxidative stress, hypoxia-related processes, phosphoinositide 3-kinase-protein kinase B, hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1), FoxO, and central carbon metabolism pathways. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator identified 8 prognostic genes: TP53, EGFR, PTEN, IL6, MTOR, SLC2A1, SCARB1, and IKBKB. The internally assessed 1-, 3-, and 5-year area under the curves were 0.688, 0.647, and 0.698, indicating moderate apparent discrimination. SLC2A1 was significantly upregulated in ccRCC, and genetically predicted higher SLC2A1 expression was associated with increased kidney cancer risk (odds ratio = 1.762, 95% confidence interval: 1.247-2.491, raw P = .001, false discovery rate-adjusted P = .006). TP53 showed a less robust inverse association (odds ratio = 0.506, 95% confidence interval: 0.291-0.881, raw P = .016, false discovery rate-adjusted P = .048), with evidence of directional horizontal pleiotropy. Representative Human Protein Atlas images provided qualitative support for the transcriptomic findings. This integrative analysis identified SLC2A1 as a prioritized candidate at the intersection of predicted acrylamide-associated targets and ccRCC-related biological processes. The convergent network, transcriptomic, and genetic findings provide a hypothesis for further investigation but do not establish that SLC2A1 or TP53 mediates an effect of acrylamide on renal carcinogenesis.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitude, and acceptance of euthanasia among medical students and doctors in Pakistan: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Globally, euthanasia is a strongly debated and ethically complex issue, with views shaped by cultural, religious, and moral precepts. In conservative cultures like Pakistan, euthanasia discussions are sensitive and occasionally ignored. This study aims to evaluate medical professionals' and students' knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of euthanasia in Pakistan. From May 16 to June 16, 2025, a cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 10 Pakistani medical institutions. The study utilized convenience sampling to select MBBS first- and final-year students and practicing doctors with a minimum of 1 year of clinical experience. Outcomes were assessed using a modified Attitudes Toward Euthanasia scale and structured knowledge items to evaluate knowledge of euthanasia, attitudes toward it, and the acceptability of its legalization. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics, while one-way analysis of variance and independent-samples t tests were used to assess differences in mean attitude ratings across demographic categories. Chi-square tests analyzed relationships between categorical factors and euthanasia approval, and Spearman rank correlation examined connections between attitude ratings and continuous variables such as age and clinical experience. Statistical significance was set at P < .05. A study involving 506 participants, including first-year and final-year medical students and practicing physicians, found that only 40.1% favored euthanasia. Knowledge and attitude scores averaged 66.4 ± 10.8 and 8.7 ± 2.1, respectively, with a positive correlation between them (ρ = 0.44, P < .01). Practicing physicians showed significantly higher acceptance than students, particularly those with lower religiosity (P < .05). Acceptance of euthanasia is related significantly to religion and religiosity, with non-Muslims and less religious participants more likely to accept it. Gender, occupation, religion, province, and religiosity were independent predictors of attitude scores, while religion and religiosity were the strongest predictors of approval in logistic regression. Pakistani medical students and doctors possess limited knowledge and varied attitudes toward euthanasia, significantly influenced by professional experience, level of training, and religious beliefs. Misconceptions about the legal and ethical aspects emphasize the need for integrating structured bioethics and end-of-life care education in medical training. Targeted educational initiatives can enhance ethically informed decision-making among healthcare professionals.

articles.title: Persistent hyperparathyroidism and its predictive factors in end-stage renal disease patients after kidney transplantation: A prospective study.
articles.abstract: Hyperparathyroidism (HPT) may persist in patients after kidney transplantation (KT). A better understanding of which patients are likely to have persistent HPT after KT would help in the development of optimal management strategies. Our aim was to examine the prevalence of persistent HPT after KT in a contemporary cohort and to identify risk factors associated with persistent HPT at 6 months. We followed 104 KT subjects in a longitudinal prospective cohort at Cho Ray Hospital, Vietnam, from October 2023 to May 2025. Persistent HPT was defined as a parathyroid hormone (PTH) level of 150 pg/mL at 6 months after KT. Among the 104 patients, the prevalence of persistent HPT at 6 months was 58.65%. The average PTH levels pretransplant and at 6 months posttransplant were 375.70 (IQR = 259.00-603.25) pg/mL and 167.95 (IQR = 112.53-227.30) pg/mL, respectively. Patients with persistent HPT had significantly higher baseline PTH (median 489 vs 273, P < .001) and alkaline phosphatase levels (median 102.0 vs 89.5, P = .025), and also experienced longer durations of chronic kidney disease (median 5.0 vs 2.0, P = .007) and dialysis therapy (2.0 vs 1.0, P < .001). Higher pretransplant intact PTH was independently associated with persistent HPT across both multivariable models, whereas the association with dialysis duration was significant only when categorized as ≥1 year. Our findings suggest that high pretransplant intact PTH independently predicts persistent HPT at 6 months, whereas dialysis duration is only significant when it reaches 1 year or longer.

articles.title: Malignant transformation in diabetic foot ulcers: A cross-sectional analysis of the impact of pathology results on patient management after diabetic foot surgery.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a major cause of lower-extremity amputation, hospitalization, and mortality. Although management focuses on wound care, infection control, and limb preservation, malignancies may develop in chronic, nonhealing wounds, and tumors may mimic DFUs. Evidence on malignancy in DFUs is limited, and the diagnostic contribution of routine histopathological examination in surgically treated cases remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the frequency of histopathologically confirmed malignancy in patients undergoing surgery for chronic DFUs and assess its impact on management and care. This retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study was conducted at a Training and Research Hospital. We included 678 consecutive patients admitted with chronic DFUs between January 2019 and June 2021 who underwent surgical treatment and histopathological examination. Patients managed conservatively and those without a pathology specimen were excluded. Demographic characteristics, ulcer features, surgical procedures, histopathological findings, and changes in treatment and care were obtained from medical records. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0. The malignancy rate and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using the Clopper-Pearson method. A total of 678 patients were included. Of these, 74% were male, and the mean age was 64.69 ± 10.92 years. Wagner grade 4 ulcers accounted for 61.7% of cases, while 65.0% were classified as PEDIS grade 3. Histopathological examination identified malignancy in 4 patients (0.6%; 95% CI, 0.16-1.50); two of these patients had metastatic involvement. The treatment and care plan was modified for all patients in whom malignancy was detected. Overall, 95.6% of patients healed with wound care after surgery, without further changes to their treatment or care plan. However, 1.9% required amputation at a more proximal level, 1.3% experienced limb loss, and 1.2% died from other diabetes-related complications. Although uncommon, malignancy and metastatic involvement may occur in chronic DFUs. The possibility of malignancy should therefore be considered, particularly in nonhealing, atypical, or clinically suspicious ulcers. Ensuring appropriate histopathological evaluation of such ulcers may help healthcare professionals and wound care nurses identify primary or metastatic malignancies at an earlier stage.

articles.title: Contributions of smoking behaviour to lung cancer subtypes: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Smoking is an established cause of lung cancer (LC), but the relative causal contributions of whether a person ever smokes and how heavily they smoke across histological subtypes remain uncertain. This study investigated the causal effects of smoking status and smoking intensity on major LC subtypes. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed. Genetic instruments were drawn from the GWAS and Sequencing Consortium of Alcohol and Nicotine Use: 85 variants for smoking status, a binary trait contrasting ever with never smokers, and 23 variants for smoking intensity, a continuous trait measuring cigarettes smoked per day. Outcomes were 5 LC phenotypes from FinnGen: non-small cell LC (1627 cases), adenocarcinoma (571), squamous cell carcinoma (365), small cell LC (179), and mesothelioma (133). Inverse-variance weighted regression with multiplicative random effects was the primary estimator, with weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger as sensitivity analyses. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied across all ten tests. Analyses used R 4.2.3 with TwoSampleMR 0.7.9. Smoking intensity was causally associated with all 4 smoking-related subtypes: squamous cell carcinoma (odds ratio [OR]: 5.95 per standard deviation increase, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.12-11.37), small cell LC (OR: 4.43, 95% CI: 1.60-12.32), non-small cell LC (OR: 3.45, 95% CI: 2.30-5.18), and adenocarcinoma (OR: 2.66, 95% CI: 1.40-5.06). All 4 survived correction for multiple testing and were reproduced by the weighted median and weighted mode estimators. Smoking status showed positive point estimates for all 4 subtypes (OR: 1.40-1.61) but reached only nominal significance for non-small cell LC (OR: 1.51, 95% CI: 1.04-2.19, P = .030), which did not survive correction and was not reproduced by other estimators. Neither exposure was associated with mesothelioma. Smoking intensity shows robust causal effects on all smoking-related LC subtypes, whereas the evidence for smoking status is directionally consistent but considerably weaker. The null finding for mesothelioma, a cancer principally caused by asbestos, supports the specificity of the instruments. These results indicate that reducing consumption among established smokers warrants emphasis alongside preventing uptake.

articles.title: Effect of uric acid and estimated glomerular filtration rate on the Fibrosis-4 index: A cross-sectional and cohort analysis.
articles.abstract: Hepatic steatosis and fibrosis present a significant public health burden, especially in China. Emerging evidence suggests an association between liver fibrosis and kidney function, indicating a potential relationship among uric acid (UA) levels, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index. This retrospective cohort study investigates the correlation between UA, estimated GFR, and FIB-4 index in Chinese adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses. A total of 5051 adults with MASLD were included from 8857 individuals initially screened at the International Healthcare Center, Fourth Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The main outcome measure was the FIB-4 index. Among the 5051 participants (75.4% male; mean age, 42.3 years), the mean baseline eGFR was 98.7 mL/min/1.73 m2. Participants with lower eGFR had significantly older age and higher body mass index, systolic blood pressure, triglycerides, UA levels, and FIB-4 index than those with higher eGFR (P < .001 for all). In multivariable Cox regression analyses, each 1-standard deviation decrease in eGFR was associated with a 21% higher risk of an increased FIB-4 index (hazard ratio [HR], 1.21; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.14-1.29; P < .001). Hyperuricemia (UA ≥ 420 μmol/L) was independently associated with a 38% higher risk of elevated FIB-4 (HR, 1.38; 95% CI: 1.23-1.55; P < .001). In the unadjusted model, a significant nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed between eGFR and FIB-4 (P for nonlinear trend < .001). However, after progressive adjustment for demographic variables, family history, and metabolic covariates, the nonlinear signal was markedly attenuated. Mediation analysis demonstrated that UA partially mediated the association between eGFR and FIB-4, accounting for 6.88% of the total effect. Reduced eGFR and hyperuricemia were independently associated with an elevated FIB-4 index in adults with MASLD, with a nonlinear relationship indicating a greater liver fibrosis risk in individuals with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Partial mediation by UA suggests that metabolic dysregulation contributes to the kidney-liver interaction. Routine assessment of eGFR and UA may improve liver fibrosis risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

articles.title: Effectiveness of kinesio tape in the treatment of patients with plantar fasciitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A meta-analysis was conducted to assess the clinical efficacy of Kinesio tape (KT) for the management of plantar fasciitis.

METHODS: Two investigators conducted an electronic literature search independently to evaluate the results of the KT treatment for patellofemoral pain syndrome. As of November 2024, the electronic databases included in the search were PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, the Wanfang Database, the China Journal Full-Text Database China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the VIP database. The search was limited to languages in Chinese and English. The extraction and inclusion indexes comprised pain visual analogue scale or numerical rating scale, ankle function American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society and plantar fascia thickness. Following the extraction of the data, a meta-analysis was conducted using Review Manager 5.3 and Stata 17.0.

RESULT: A total of 16 studies were included in the review, all of which were randomized controlled trials. Subgroup analyses based on intervention types revealed significant differences. Compared with controls, KT combined with other active therapies (e.g., extracorporeal shock wave therapy, muscle energy techniques) significantly relieved pain (mean difference [MD] = -1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] [-2.1, 0], P = .05, I2 = 96%). However, KT as a monotherapy showed no statistically significant pain reduction over controls (MD = -0.54, 95% CI [-1.21, 0.13], P = .11, I2 = 90%). For ankle function American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society, only the combined therapy group showed significant improvement (MD = 7.6, P < .00001), while KT alone did not (MD = -0.9, P = .8).

CONCLUSION: KT demonstrated a statistically significant but clinically modest reduction in pain in patients with plantar fasciitis. However, the effect size did not reach the generally recognized minimal clinically important difference threshold, suggesting that the clinical benefit may be limited. KT may be considered as an adjunctive therapy, particularly when combined with other treatments, but its role as a standalone intervention remains questionable.

articles.title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for the treatment of restless legs syndrome: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in patients with Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) is uncertain. This study was performed to explore the therapeutic effect of rTMS in treating RLS.

METHODS: Databases including PubMed, EMbase, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang database were searched from their inception to May 1, 2026. Eligible studies comparing rTMS with sham stimulation were included. Data were analyzed using Review Manager Version 5.3.

RESULTS: Four studies were included in the meta-analysis. The overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could effectively reduce International RLS-Rating Scale (IRLS-RS) scores (mean difference [MD] = 6.46, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.44 -8.48, P < .00001) and Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) scores (MD = 4.80, 95% CI: 3.51-6.08, P < .00001) at different follow-up periods. Meanwhile, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could effectively reduce IRLS-RS scores (MD = 7.79, 95% CI: 3.90-11.68, P < .0001) and PSQI scores (MD = 5.58, 95% CI: 3.81-7.35, P < .00001) in the subgroup analysis by RLS subtype. However, rTMS showed no significant effect on PSQI scores in primary RLS (MD = 1.86, 95% CI: -2.65-6.37, P = .42). In addition, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that both low-frequency and high-frequency rTMS could effectively reduce IRLS-RS scores (MD = 7.79, 95% CI: 3.90-11.68, P < .0001) and PSQI scores (MD = 5.58, 95% CI: 3.81-7.35, P < .00001). Finally, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could not significantly reduce Hamilton anxiety scale and Hamilton depression scale scores in subgroup analyses of follow-up period, RLS subtype, or rTMS frequency (P > .05).

CONCLUSION: rTMS might alleviate core limb discomfort symptoms measured by IRLS-RS and improve sleep quality assessed by PSQI in patients with RLS. However, rTMS might not be effective in improving symptoms of anxiety and depression. To further confirm the conclusion, more large randomized controlled trials are necessary.

articles.title: Acute ischemic stroke despite NOAC therapy in atrial fibrillation: Clinical factors associated with AIS in a 2-center observational case-control study.
articles.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) can occur in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF) despite treatment with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs). This study evaluated clinical, treatment-related, inflammatory, and echocardiographic factors associated with AIS in NOAC-treated patients with AF. This retrospective, 2-center case-control study included 322 patients with non-valvular AF who had received NOAC therapy for at least 3 months. Of these, 112 were hospitalized with AIS and 210 were outpatient controls without AIS at the study assessment. Group differences and factors associated with AIS were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. ROC analyses were exploratory. Patients with AIS were older than controls and more often had hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, prior stroke, and prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use. In the adjusted analysis, prior stroke (OR = 32.79), coronary artery disease (OR = 3.47), prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use (OR = 2.55), female sex (OR = 2.26), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.99), and C-reactive protein (OR per mg/L = 1.10) were associated with AIS. HAS-BLED (area under the curve = 0.881, 95% CI = 0.844-0.918) and CHA2DS2-VASc (area under the curve = 0.840, 95% CI = 0.795-0.885) distinguished AIS cases from controls in exploratory ROC analyses. Among NOAC-treated patients with AF, prior stroke and cardiovascular comorbidities were strongly associated with AIS. Prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use was also associated with AIS. Inflammatory markers measured during acute stroke had limited additional value. Because this was a case-control study, the findings do not estimate stroke incidence or future stroke risk and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Divergent associations between adiposity and hernia subtypes in European populations: A Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a suspected risk factor for hernia, but observational studies are susceptible to confounding and reverse causation. We aimed to investigate the causal effects of general and central adiposity on 5 hernia subtypes using Mendelian randomization (MR). Two-sample MR analyses were conducted using genetic instruments for 7 adiposity traits from the UK Biobank and hernia outcome data (diaphragmatic, femoral, inguinal, umbilical, and ventral hernias) from the Finn Gen consortium. The inverse-variance weighted method was the primary analysis, complemented by MR Egger and weighted median methods. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, and directionality. Outliers were removed in a confirmatory MR analysis. All P values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method. Genetically predicted adiposity was associated with a decreased risk of inguinal hernia (e.g., body mass index [BMI] odds ratio [OR]: 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.76-0.92, PBH <.001) but an increased risk of umbilical hernia (BMI OR: 1.39, 95% CI: 1.18-1.63, PBH <.001) and ventral hernia (BMI OR: 1.93, 95% CI: 1.65-2.26, PBH <.001). These effects were consistent across adiposity measures. No significant causal effects were found for diaphragmatic or femoral hernias. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of findings, with no horizontal pleiotropy and valid causal direction. This MR study suggests that genetically predicted adiposity has divergent potential causal associations with hernia subtypes, protecting against inguinal hernia while increasing the risk of umbilical and ventral hernias. These findings, though limited to European populations and subject to the assumptions of MR, have implications for clinical risk stratification and weight management counseling.

articles.title: Gut microbiota, sleep and coronary artery disease: A Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Inadequate and poor-quality sleep is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Gut microbiota may play a role in sleep regulation. However, the associations between gut microbiota, sleep, and CAD risk, and the causal nature of these associations, remain unclear. We performed a 2-step Mendelian randomization analysis using summary-level data to assess the association between gut microbiota and CAD and the potential mediating roles of sleep-related traits (i.e., chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short sleep, and long sleep) herein. The inverse-variance weighted method served as the primary analysis, with several other complementary methods as sensitivity analyses. Our findings revealed that 2 gut microbial taxa were negatively associated with genetically predicted CAD risk, while 4 taxa, including species Veillonella unclassified (odds ratio: 1.054, 95% confidence interval: 1.010-1.101), showed positive associations. Regarding sleep-related traits, we found that insomnia (odds ratio: 1.553, 95% confidence interval: 1.081-2.230) and short sleep duration causally increased CAD risk, whereas longer sleep duration causally reduced CAD risk. The mediation Mendelian randomization analysis demonstrated that insomnia partially mediated the causal, predisposing effect of species Veillonella unclassified on increased CAD risk, with a proportion mediated of 5.7%. This study provides evidence for a causal relationship between specific gut microbial taxa and CAD risk, as well as the mediating role of insomnia in this relationship. These findings offer novel insights into potential strategies for CAD prevention through modulation of the gut microbiome and improvement of sleep quality.

articles.title: Additive effects of active vitamin D3 or vitamin E administration on therapeutic lower-limb home exercise for knee osteoarthritis: A pilot prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quadriceps weakness, inflammation, and reduced physical function are common in knee osteoarthritis (OA), and lower limb exercise therapy is an established non-pharmacological treatment. Vitamin D3 (vit D3) and vitamin E (vit E) have been proposed as adjunctive therapies; however, clinical findings are inconsistent. We aimed to examine whether combining lower limb home exercises with oral active vit D3 or vit E supplementation provides additive benefits compared with home exercise alone in women with symptomatic knee OA.

METHODS: Eighty-eight postmenopausal women with knee OA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2-4; 71.9 ± 5.6 years) were randomly assigned to receive therapeutic lower limb home exercise only, home exercise with active vit D3 administration, or home exercise with vit E administration. Participants performed isometric lower limb exercises twice daily for 24 weeks. Subsequently, they were assessed using the Japanese knee osteoarthritis measure (JKOM) as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes were short-form health survey, grip strength, quadriceps muscle strength, 10-m walk test, inflammatory markers, bone mineral density, and body composition. For data analyses, we used paired and independent t tests, analysis of variance, and analysis of covariance, adjusting for age, body mass index, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade.

RESULTS: Eighty participants completed follow-up. All groups showed significant improvements in JKOM score, quadriceps muscle strength, and 10-m walk test. Grip strength improved significantly only in the group that received active vit D. No significant between-group differences were observed in JKOM scores, short-form health survey-36, muscle strength, or physical performance. Inflammatory markers decreased significantly in the vit E group, although between-group differences were not observed. No other significant between-group differences were found, except in bone mineral density.

CONCLUSIONS: Administering active vit D3 or vit E for 24 weeks as an adjunct to lower limb home exercises did not yield significant additive effects on symptoms, muscle strength, or physical performance in women with knee OA. Exercise therapy alone remained effective, and vitamin supplementation showed nutrient-specific trends.

articles.title: Causal association between plasma vascular endothelial growth factor family proteins and placenta previa: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: This study investigates associations between genetically proxied plasma vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) family proteins and placenta previa using 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Exposure GWAS summary statistics were obtained from the UK Biobank and IEU resources, and placenta previa data from FinnGen. Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) analysis was the primary method, supplemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, and weighted mode analyses. The Bonferroni-corrected threshold for 5 exposures was P < .01. Cochran Q, the MR-Egger intercept, MR-PRESSO and leave-one-out analyses assessed heterogeneity and sensitivity. Genetically predicted higher plasma VEGFA was associated with increased placenta previa risk (IVW: β = 0.231, OR = 1.26, 95% confidence interval: 1.06-1.51, P = .008). The analyses did not provide statistically convincing evidence of a causal effect of VEGFB, VEGFC, VEGFD, or placental growth factor (PLGF); these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of no effect. For VEGFA specifically, Cochran Q test did not detect significant heterogeneity (IVW: Q = 21.257, P = .729), and the MR-Egger intercept (-0.026, P = .181) and MR-PRESSO global test (P = .692) did not detect evidence of horizontal pleiotropy. The VEGFA leave-one-out analysis indicated that no single SNP substantially influenced the estimate. In contrast, VEGFD showed a significant MR-Egger intercept (-0.155, P = .029), indicating possible directional horizontal pleiotropy and requiring particular caution in interpreting this exposure. The findings support an association between genetically proxied plasma VEGFA and placenta previa risk. They provide etiologic insight rather than evidence of clinical prediction; any predictive or screening role for VEGFA measurement requires prospective, pregnancy-specific validation.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of two novel bioceramic root canal sealers in the treatment of chronic apical periodontitis.
articles.abstract: Chronic apical periodontitis (CAP) is a persistent periradicular inflammatory condition driven by intraradicular infection and remains a common indication for primary nonsurgical root canal therapy. This retrospective cohort study compared 2 calcium silicate-based bioceramic root canal sealers (C-Root SP vs iRoot SP) used during obturation in adults treated for CAP between January 2022 and December 2024. CAP was confirmed by compatible clinical findings and radiographic evidence of periapical radiolucency; cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) was obtained when clinically indicated. The primary endpoint was a strict composite treatment success endpoint requiring both clinical resolution and radiographic healing at final follow-up. Secondary outcomes included pain severity measured by the visual analog scale (VAS) and treatment-related events. Among 227 eligible patients, 209 were included in the final analysis (C-Root SP, n = 101; iRoot SP, n = 108). Treatment success was higher with C-Root SP than with iRoot SP (86.1% vs 74.1%; χ2 = 4.73, P = .030), and radiographic healing was also more frequent (88.1% vs 76.9%; χ2 = 4.55, P = .033), whereas clinical resolution did not differ statistically (91.1% vs 83.3%; P = .095). After adjustment for age, sex, baseline lesion diameter, tooth location, diabetes mellitus, and baseline sinus tract, C-Root SP was associated with higher odds of treatment success (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.09-4.65; P = .028) and radiographic healing (aOR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.04-4.79; P = .040), while the adjusted association with clinical resolution was not statistically significant (aOR = 2.12, 95% CI: 0.89-5.09; P = .091). VAS trajectories were similar overall, with a modest between-group difference at 1 month. Postoperative pain, acute exacerbations, sealer extrusion, and further endodontic interventions were infrequent and comparable between groups. In exploratory analysis, sealer extrusion was associated with treatment failure (OR = 4.91, P = .002). These observational findings indicate associations rather than causal treatment effects and require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy: A comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
articles.abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized cardiac complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by impaired myocardial contractile reserve, diastolic dysfunction, and electrophysiological abnormalities. Despite its clinical significance, particularly in the setting of liver transplantation, CCM remains largely overlooked. We performed a narrative review of the literature on CCM published up to December 2025, covering pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, imaging modalities, biomarkers, and management strategies. Depending on the diagnostic criteria used, the prevalence of CCM ranges from 29% to 67.2%. Advanced imaging techniques, particularly global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance, enable early detection of subclinical systolic dysfunction. A "toxic triangle" comprising systemic inflammation, metabolic derangements, and neurohormonal activation represents an integrated pathophysiological model that drives myocardial fibrosis and dysfunction. Beta-blockers and aldosterone antagonists remain mainstays of pharmacological management, while liver transplantation is currently the only definitive therapy. CCM is an underrecognized condition with substantial clinical implications. Standardized diagnostic criteria, validated biomarkers, and large-scale prospective studies are urgently needed to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Research hotspots and evolution trends of human amniotic fluid stem cells: A cite space bibliometric analysis based on WoSCC and PubMed.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the research hotspots, knowledge structure, and evolution trends in the field of human amniotic fluid stem cells (hAFSCs).

METHODS: A bibliometric approach was employed using CiteSpace 6.2.R4 software, with the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC, 2006-2026, including 601 original research papers) and PubMed (1984-2024, including 960 publications) as data sources. Standardized, reproducible search strategies (including synonyms, abbreviations, MeSH terms, and Boolean operators) were developed for each database, and literature screening followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Using the WoSCC dataset as the core, we generated comprehensive visualizations covering author collaboration networks, countries, institutions, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, timelines, time zones, and emerging terms; the PubMed data were used for comparison of long-term publication trends.

RESULTS: The global publication volume in the field of hAFSCs has shown an overall upward trend, which can be divided into 3 phases: exploratory inception (1984-2006), rapid growth (2007-2013), and stable deepening (2014 to present). The United States (177 articles) and Italy (132 articles) form the dual engines of international collaboration, while China ranks third in publication volume (75 articles) but exhibits relatively weak international collaboration (centrality 0.02). The evolution of research themes is clear: from 2006 to 2009, the focus was on cell isolation, characterization, and in vitro culture; from 2010 to 2015, the scope expanded to multipotent differentiation, animal models, and the treatment of fetal diseases; and since 2018, exosomes/extracellular vesicles have emerged as the most active frontier with the highest emergence intensity (7.37).

CONCLUSION: Bibliometric analysis indicates that research on hAFSCs has evolved from basic biological characterization into a comprehensive field encompassing multipotent differentiation, tissue engineering, and exosome regulation. Exosomes/extracellular vesicles and targeted repair of organ damage are currently the primary areas of focus. This study is a descriptive analysis; all conclusions are based on publication trend statistics and do not involve validation of clinical translational efficacy.

articles.title: A bibliometric analysis of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity research: Trends and insights (2005-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polymyxins remain important therapeutic options for the treatment of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections; however, their clinical application is limited by a narrow therapeutic window and a high risk of nephrotoxicity. Although research on polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity has expanded rapidly in recent years, the overall evolution of research themes, knowledge structure, and emerging frontiers in this field remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the development trends and research hotspots of polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity using bibliometric analysis.

METHODS: Relevant publications on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity published between January 1, 2005, and November 13, 2024, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database. CiteSpace and VOSviewer (Baxter Healthcare Corporation) were used to analyze publication trends, authorship, institutional and country collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, and burst detection.

RESULTS: A total of 569 publications were included in this study. The annual publication output demonstrated an overall increasing trend, indicating increasing attention to polymyxin-associated nephrotoxicity research. Li Jian was the most productive author, Monash University was the most productive institution in terms of publication output, and the United States contributed the highest number of publications among all countries. Keyword analysis revealed that research themes have evolved from early characterization of nephrotoxicity and clinical safety assessment toward the identification of acute kidney injury risk factors, elucidation of oxidative stress-related mechanisms, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic optimization, and development of individualized dosing strategies and nephroprotective approaches. Burst analysis further indicated increasing attention toward biomarkers, precision dosing, and novel therapeutic strategies.

CONCLUSION: Bibliometric analysis revealed that research on polymyxin-induced nephrotoxicity has progressively evolved from toxicity characterization to mechanistic exploration and precision management. Current challenges include an incomplete understanding of interactions among nephrotoxic pathways, limited dynamic prediction models, and insufficient clinical translation of emerging protective strategies. Future research should focus on integrating multi-omics approaches, artificial intelligence-based risk prediction, therapeutic drug monitoring, and safer polymyxin formulations to optimize the balance between antibacterial efficacy and nephrotoxicity prevention.

articles.title: Systemic immune-inflammation index and in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with acute asthma exacerbation: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: The prognostic value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in critically ill patients with acute asthma exacerbations remains unclear. This study examined the association between SII and in-hospital mortality. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) database, including adult critically ill patients with asthma exacerbations. SII was calculated from laboratory values obtained during the peri-intensive care unit admission period. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations were assessed using restricted cubic spline and Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for confounders. A total of 575 patients were included, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 6.6%. Mortality rates differed significantly across SII tertiles and were highest in tertile 3 (11.5%), compared with tertile 2 (3.6%) and tertile 1 (4.7%) (P = .003). In Cox proportional hazards models, compared with tertile 2, patients in tertile 3 had a significantly increased risk of in-hospital mortality (unadjusted hazard ratio [HR] 2.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.21-6.83, P = .016; adjusted HR 2.82, 95% CI 1.12-7.10, P = .027), whereas no significant difference was observed for tertile 1. Restricted cubic spline analysis based on natural logarithm-transformed (ln-SII) demonstrated a significant nonlinear association with in-hospital mortality (P for nonlinearity < .001), with risk increasing markedly at higher ln-SII levels. Elevated SII was associated with increased in-hospital mortality and may serve as a simple prognostic marker in critically ill asthma exacerbations.

articles.title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased sympathetic activity and an elevated cardiovascular risk. Noninvasive interventions targeting autonomic regulation may offer complementary therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the acute effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters of patients with OSA. Patients with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour) were randomly assigned to an intervention group that received a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol or a control group that rested quietly in the supine position for the corresponding period without receiving manual or tactile intervention. The intervention targeted the cervical, thoracic, and abdominal regions, under controlled conditions. The primary outcomes included heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and peripheral oxygen saturation.
