Measurements were obtained at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 5 and 15 minutes post-intervention.

RESULTS: A total of 95 male patients (mean age: 48.12 ± 10.21 years) completed the study. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups, except for heart rate. After adjustment for baseline heart rate using mixed analysis of covariance, no significant group × time interaction was observed for heart rate (P = .476, partial ηp2 = .008). Similarly, no significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, or peripheral oxygen saturation (all P > .05). Although significant time effects were observed for some physiological parameters, the magnitude of these effects varied across outcomes, and none was accompanied by a significant group × time interaction. Therefore, these temporal changes were not interpreted as intervention-specific effects. No adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSION: Heart rate changed significantly over time following the interventions; however, after adjustment for baseline heart rate, the pattern of change did not differ significantly between the fascial mobilization and control groups. Similarly, no significant between-group differences in changes over time were observed for blood pressure or oxygen saturation. These findings do not demonstrate a specific acute effect of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters assessed. Further studies using advanced measures of autonomic function and longer follow-up periods are warranted.

articles.title: Lower oxidative balance score and higher systemic immune-inflammatory indices are associated with current asthma: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Whether the oxidative balance score (OBS) and complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices are associated with current asthma, relative to a correctly defined never-asthma comparison group and accounting for the survey's complex sampling design, has not been investigated. This cross-sectional study used data from a nationally representative health survey cycle (August 2021-August 2023). Current asthma (n = 517) and never-asthma (n = 3725) groups were defined using validated lifetime-diagnosis and current-status questions; a former-asthma group (n = 308) was analyzed descriptively. Six CBC-derived indices (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammatory response index, eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio) were calculated from absolute blood counts. Survey-weighted logistic regression, incorporating NHANES sampling weights, stratification, and primary sampling units, estimated odds ratios (ORs) for current asthma per 1-standard deviation increase in OBS and each index, with exposure-specific covariate adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction across the 6-index panel. Current-asthma participants had lower OBS (18.7 ± 6.9 vs 20.4 ± 6.9) than never-asthma participants and numerically higher values across all 6 inflammatory indices and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), reaching unadjusted significance for OBS, systemic immune-inflammation index, eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and hsCRP. In survey-weighted models, OBS remained associated with lower odds of current asthma (OR 0.77, 95% confidence interval 0.68-0.87), and all 6 inflammatory indices remained associated with higher odds (ORs 1.12-1.32), surviving FDR correction (all q < .05). The OBS association was consistent in a 2-day dietary sensitivity analysis, while inflammatory-index estimates were materially unchanged after additional adjustment for race/ethnicity. hsCRP was not associated with asthma status after adjustment. Within the current-asthma group, OBS was not associated with CBC-derived inflammatory indices, although hsCRP differed across OBS quartiles in a secondary analysis (FDR q = .041). Lower OBS and higher levels of several CBC-derived inflammatory indices were each associated with current asthma compared with never-asthma status; however, OBS was not associated with inflammatory index levels within the current-asthma group. These cross-sectional associations do not establish causality but support prospective investigation of dietary and lifestyle antioxidant status and systemic inflammatory indices as correlates of asthma.

articles.title: Deaths involving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cardiac arrest in older US adults, 1999-2023: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: National long-term trends and disparities in deaths in which both chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cardiac arrest are recorded on death certificates are not well characterized. We used CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (1999-2023) to identify US adults aged ≥ 65 years whose death certificates listed both COPD (ICD-10 J41-J44) and cardiac arrest (I46) as underlying or contributing causes. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization; the urbanization analysis was limited to 1999 to 2020 because those data were not available after 2020. Trends were analyzed using annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); P < .05 was considered statistically significant. Among 7,18,280 deaths involving concurrent coding of COPD and cardiac arrest, AAMRs declined from 86.4 in 1999 to 52.5 in 2023. A significant decrease occurred from 1999 to 2006 (APC: -2.87; P = .01), followed by a plateau and a further decline from 2021 to 2023 (APC: -4.77; P < .001). Older men exhibited higher AAMRs than older women (86.8 vs 55.2). Non-Hispanic (NH) White individuals had the highest mortality (69.7), followed by NH Black/African American (64.3) and Hispanic/Latino (60.7) populations. The West region reported the highest AAMR (98.9). During 1999 to 2020, nonmetropolitan residents had higher AAMRs than metropolitan residents (70.8 vs 67.9). Population-level mortality records involving both COPD and cardiac arrest declined overall but remained heterogeneous across demographic and geographic strata. These findings describe concurrent coding on death certificates and do not establish that COPD increases the risk of cardiac arrest or causes the observed deaths.

articles.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses and over 3-year follow-up. Mortality risk showed a graded pattern across Hb strata (Hb ≥10.0-<12.0 g/dL: HR, 1.66; Hb ≥8.0-<10.0 g/dL: HR, 3.33). Baseline anemia was associated with increased mortality and acute systemic complications following the first recorded SSc diagnosis; these observational findings warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Presumed oxaliplatin-related Guillain-Barré syndrome: A case report and review of chemotherapy-related Guillain-Barré syndrome.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Oxaliplatin, a platinum-based chemotherapeutic widely used in colorectal, hepatobiliary, and pancreatic malignancies, commonly causes a symmetric, cold-induced sensory neuropathy. Rarely, it has been linked to immune-mediated Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), which can be misattributed to drug-induced sensory neuropathy and delay diagnosis. Distinguishing the two is critical because GBS can progress to respiratory failure and death.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 77-year-old woman with concurrent metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal carcinoma developed acute, symmetric, ascending motor weakness with clinically preserved sensation approximately 2 weeks after her last cycle of gemcitabine, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil (GOLF), rapidly progressing to an inability to ambulate.

DIAGNOSIS: Neurological examination and cerebrospinal fluid analysis (albuminocytologic dissociation) were consistent with GBS, and nerve conduction studies demonstrated absent motor and sensory responses, indicating a severe axonal variant (AMSAN); sensory involvement was electrodiagnostic rather than clinical. An extensive infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic workup was negative, supporting a diagnosis of presumed oxaliplatin-related GBS; a Naranjo score of 4 indicated a "possible" drug association.

INTERVENTIONS: She received 5 sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange followed by 4 sessions of intravenous immunoglobulin.

OUTCOMES: No meaningful neurological recovery occurred; she developed progressive respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and died.

LESSONS: Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for GBS in patients on platinum-based chemotherapy who develop abrupt, symmetric motor weakness after common causes have been ruled out. Because causality is difficult to establish, the association remains presumed; early recognition, prompt immunotherapy, and pharmacovigilance are essential to reduce mortality.

articles.title: Effectiveness of traditional mind-body exercises on fall risk test scores and balance in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of traditional mind-body exercises on fall risk test scores and balance in older adults.

METHODS: The systematic search covered multiple databases, including PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, and Weipu (VIP), with the search period spanning from the inception of each database to December 10, 2025. We included randomized controlled trials evaluating the effects of traditional mind-body exercises on fall risk test scores and balance in older adults. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool. Meta-analysis was performed using Stata 15 software and a random-effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 31 randomized controlled trials involving 3622 participants were included. Pooled analyses showed lower fall risk test scores (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.84 to -0.28) and higher Berg Balance Scale scores (WMD = 2.60, 95% CI: 1.47-3.72) in the intervention groups than in the control groups. Heterogeneity was very high for Berg Balance Scale scores (I2 = 95.6%). Subgroup results for fall risk test scores were Baduanjin (BDJ) [SMD = -0.82, 95% CI (-1.25, -0.38)] and Tai Chi (TC) [SMD = -0.41, 95% CI (-0.70, -0.11)]. For Berg Balance Scale scores, results were BDJ [WMD = 2.91, 95% CI (1.02, 4.8)], TC [WMD = 2.37, 95% CI (0.83, 3.9)], and Wuqinxi (WQX) [weighted mean difference (WMD) = 4.80, 95% CI (1.40, 8.20)]. Examples of protocols used in the included trials included Tai Chi twice weekly for 55 minutes per session over 8 weeks, Baduanjin 3 times weekly for 40 minutes per session over 12 weeks, and Wuqinxi 4 times weekly for 60 minutes per session over 12 weeks.

CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that Tai Chi and Baduanjin may reduce fall risk test scores and improve balance in older adults, while Wuqinxi may improve balance. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and do not establish a reduction in actual fall incidence.

articles.title: Predictive role of blood urea nitrogen to serum albumin ratio (BAR) in all-cause mortality in patients with cirrhosis.
articles.abstract: We aimed to assess the potential association between the blood urea nitrogen to serum albumin ratio (BAR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in cirrhosis patients. We used X-tile software (V 3.6.1; Yale University, New Haven) to obtain the cutoff value and group the subjects. We applied 1:1 propensity score matching to reduce confounders. The primary endpoint events included ACM at 30, 90, and 365 days. The association between BAR and ACM was investigated using multivariable Cox regression analyses and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. After propensity score matching, we included 746 matched patient pairs based on a cutoff of 9.3. There were no significant differences in 30- and 90-day ACM rates between the 2 groups, while the 365-day ACM rates were 361 (48.4%) and 409 (54.8%; P = .013), respectively. Additionally, the multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that BAR was significantly associated with an increased risk of 365-day ACM, with a hazard ratio of 1.18 and a 95% confidence interval of 1.03 to 1.36; P = .022. The survival analysis showed that the low BAR group had a higher survival probability within 365 days (log-rank P = .046). BAR may be associated with 365-day mortality in hepatic cirrhosis patients in intensive care units.

articles.title: Global, regional, and national burden of chronic hepatitis C including cirrhosis from 1990 to 2021, alongside projections for the next 15 years.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C (CHC), including cirrhosis, remains a major global health challenge. While direct-acting antivirals have improved prognoses, barriers to diagnosis and equitable access hinder World Health Organization's 2030 eradication target. This study systematically assessed the global burden and trends to inform prevention strategies. Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 database, this analysis quantified the absolute numbers and age-standardized rates (ASRs) of 4 disease burden indicators, including incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), for CHC, including cirrhosis, across global, regional, and national levels from 1990 to 2021. Temporal trends were quantified using the estimated annual percent change and Joinpoint regression. Decomposition, health inequality, and frontier analyses were used to characterize drivers and socioeconomic gradients, with Bayesian age-period-cohort projections to 2036. Analyses were stratified by socio-demographic index (SDI), sex, and age. In 2021, the global numbers of incidence, prevalence, deaths, and DALYs for CHC, including cirrhosis, were substantially higher than in 1990, though the ASRs declined. Significant socioeconomic inequalities persisted, with the highest burden in low SDI regions. South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, Western Sub-Saharan Africa, and North Africa and the Middle East showed the highest absolute numbers for disease burden indicators; Sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and North Africa and the Middle East had the highest ASRs. Males exhibited higher deaths and DALYs than females. Decomposition analysis identified population growth and aging as drivers of increased disease burden, partially countered by epidemiological improvements. Frontier analysis revealed substantial unrealized potential in low SDI settings. Projections indicated a continued decline in ASRs, but the number of prevalence may reach approximately 150 million by 2036 under the continuation of current trends. Despite declining ASRs of CHC, including cirrhosis, from 1990 to 2021, the absolute burden increased due to demographic shifts. Pronounced socioeconomic inequalities persist, with the highest burden concentrated in low SDI regions.

articles.title: Completed clinical trials of p53-targeted therapeutic strategies in cancer: A cross-sectional ClinicalTrials.gov registry analysis.
articles.abstract: The tumor suppressor gene TP53 is one of the most frequently altered genes in human cancers and plays a central role in regulating cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and genomic stability. Therapeutic strategies targeting the p53 pathway have been investigated to restore or exploit p53 function in human malignancies. However, the characteristics, reporting completeness, and clinical development patterns of completed trials evaluating p53-targeted therapeutic strategies have not been comprehensively summarized. This study aims to characterize the design, therapeutic strategies, reporting completeness, and primary objectives of completed clinical trials investigating p53-targeted therapeutic strategies for cancer. A cross-sectional registry analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted using the search terms "Cancer" AND "p53 gene therapy." Completed studies available as of 1 July 2025 were screened for eligibility. Trials investigating p53-targeted therapeutic strategies, including p53 gene therapy and other therapeutic approaches directly targeting the p53 pathway, were included. Data extracted included study design, cancer type, therapeutic strategy, clinical phase, enrollment, and primary outcome measures. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize study characteristics; no inferential statistical analyses were performed. Twenty-three completed studies met the eligibility criteria, including 20 (87.0%) interventional and 3 (13.0%) observational studies. The included studies evaluated diverse p53-targeted therapeutic strategies, including adenoviral vector-mediated p53 gene therapy, chemotherapy combinations, immunotherapeutic approaches, biomarker-guided treatment strategies, and molecularly targeted therapies. Early-phase clinical development predominated, with Phase I studies accounting for the largest proportion of completed trials. Enrollment information was available for 17 (73.9%) studies, whereas six (26.1%) did not report participant numbers. Primary outcome measures were reported for 15 (65.2%) studies, while eight (34.8%) lacked clearly defined primary outcomes. Five studies (21.7%) had publicly posted study results on ClinicalTrials.gov, whereas 18 (78.3%) had no posted results available. Reported primary endpoints predominantly focused on safety, dose escalation, treatment feasibility, and biomarker evaluation. Completed clinical trials investigating p53-targeted therapeutic strategies remain predominantly in the early stages of clinical development and have primarily focused on evaluating safety, feasibility, and preliminary biological activity rather than definitive treatment efficacy. Variability in registry reporting, including incomplete enrollment, primary outcome, and study result reporting, limits comprehensive assessment of the current evidence base.

articles.title: Hyaluronic acid-based skin booster with glutathione combined with 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser and oral tranexamic acid for melasma: A prospective comparative study.
articles.abstract: Melasma is a chronic, acquired facial hyperpigmentation disorder with multifactorial pathogenesis and frequent relapse. Low-fluence 1064-nm Q-switched neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Nd:YAG) (LQSNY) laser with oral tranexamic acid (TA) is widely used, but responses are often incomplete and short-lived. glutathione (GSH), an antioxidant that inhibits melanogenesis, may improve outcomes when delivered intradermally with a hyaluronic acid (HA) carrier. We assessed whether adding an HA-based GSH skin booster (HA-GSH) to this regimen enhances efficacy and durability. Fifty Chinese women with epidermal melasma (Fitzpatrick III-IV) were randomized 1:1 to 6 monthly LQSNY sessions plus oral TA (250 mg daily), with (Group A) or without (Group B) intradermal HA-GSH. The primary outcome was change in modified melasma area and severity index (mMASI) at 6 months and at 2-month posttreatment follow-up. Secondary outcomes were patient satisfaction (short assessment of patient satisfaction) and safety. Sample size was determined a priori. mMASI was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with baseline mMASI as a covariate and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for visit-level comparisons. Thirty-six patients completed the study (18 per group); baseline mMASI was comparable (5.61 ± 1.29 vs 5.56 ± 1.20; P = .89). Fourteen participants withdrew (seven per group), none due to adverse events. Group A showed significantly greater mMASI reduction from the third session onward. Adjusted for baseline, the mean difference across all post-baseline visits was 0.72 points (95% confidence interval 0.46-0.98; P < .001) favoring Group A, evident at the first posttreatment assessment. At 6 months, mean mMASI was lower in Group A (2.50 ± 0.62 vs 3.39 ± 0.70; P < .001), an advantage maintained at follow-up (2.06 ± 0.54 vs 2.67 ± 0.59; P = .003). More Group A patients were "very satisfied" (28% vs 11%), though not significantly (P = .31). Both regimens were well tolerated; only transient erythema, mild swelling, and bruising occurred, with no serious or pigmentary adverse events. Adding intradermal HA-GSH to LQSNY laser and oral TA produced earlier, greater, and more durable melasma improvement with high satisfaction and a favorable safety profile, supporting HA-GSH as a promising adjuvant pending confirmation in larger, longer trials.

articles.title: Mendelian randomization of plasma lipidome and temporomandibular joint disorders.
articles.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to investigate the possible causal association between lipids (LP) and temporomandibular joint disorders (TMD). To investigate the causal relationship between circulating LP and TMD, we conducted a 2-sample MR analysis. Exposure data comprised summary statistics for 179 LP from the GeneRISK genome-wide association study (N = 7174 samples). Outcome data were derived from the FinnGen genome-wide association study for TMD (N = 185169 samples). Primary causal estimates were generated using inverse-variance weighted regression, with sensitivity analyses including MR-Egger, weighted median, and Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier. Robustness was assessed through pleiotropy-robust methods, heterogeneity testing, and leave-one-out analysis. Our analysis identified specific lipid species associated with temporomandibular joint disorder risk. Diacylglycerol (18:1_18:1) (odds ratio [OR] = 1.067, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.016-1.121, P = .010) and several triacylglycerols (TGs) were significantly associated with increased risk: TG (50:3) (OR = 1.053, 95% CI = 1.006-1.102, P = .028), TG (52:3) (OR = 1.073, 95% CI = 1.031-1.118, P = .001), TG (53:3) (OR = 1.062, 95% CI = 1.017-1.109, P = .006), TG (56:5) (OR = 1.057, 95% CI = 1.005-1.111, P = .032), and TG (56:6) (OR = 1.066, 95% CI = 1.020-1.114, P = .004). In contrast, Phosphatidylcholine (15:0_18:2) (OR = 0.953, 95% CI = 0.920-0.987, P = .007) and Phosphatidylcholine (16:0_18:2) (OR = 0.961, 95% CI = 0.928-0.996, P = .031) were associated with a reduced risk. Our MR analysis provides evidence supporting a putative causal relationship between specific plasma lipid species and the development of TMD. These findings highlight the potential role of lipid metabolism in TMD pathogenesis and warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Association of Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) with long-term mortality in type 2 diabetes patients with coronary heart disease: A prospective national cohort study.
articles.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is prevalent in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with coronary heart disease (CHD), increasing cardiovascular risk. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is a novel composite biomarker, yet its prognostic value in this comorbid population remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed 909 participants with T2DM and CHD from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999 to 2010, followed until 2019. EASIX was calculated using lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and platelet count. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed associations between EASIX and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively. Time-dependent C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement evaluated the incremental prognostic value of EASIX beyond established risk factors. During a median follow-up of 111 months, 617 all-cause and 251 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Higher EASIX levels were significantly associated with increased mortality risks. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile had a hazard ratio of 1.93 (95% confidence interval = 1.48-2.50) for all-cause mortality and a subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.56 (95% confidence interval = 1.05-2.33) for cardiovascular mortality compared with the lowest quartile. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear positive relationship. Adding EASIX to a base model (age, HbA1c, and estimated glomerular filtration rate) significantly improved the C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement for both outcomes (all P < .001). Elevated EASIX levels are independently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with T2DM and CHD. In this population, its inclusion in risk assessment protocols enhances the predictive value for long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Complete remission of minimal change disease after antiviral monotherapy in a patient with immune-active chronic hepatitis B: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Minimal change disease (MCD) is characterized by diffuse podocyte foot process effacement on electron microscopy, minimal structural changes on light microscopy, and the absence of immune complex deposition on immunofluorescence. In adults, MCD accounts for approximately 10% to 25% of nephrotic syndrome cases and is typically idiopathic, although secondary causes such as infections, medications, malignancies, and immune disorders have been reported. The association between hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and glomerular disease has been well established in membranous nephropathy and mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis. However, HBV-associated MCD is rare.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 42-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of generalized edema and weight gain. Physical examination revealed severe bilateral pretibial pitting edema, and laboratory evaluation revealed hypoalbuminemia and nephrotic-range proteinuria.

DIAGNOSES: The urine protein-to-creatinine ratio was elevated to 4.3, while renal function remained unchanged. Serological testing was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e-antigen, with a high viral load (HBV deoxyribonucleic acid 505,437 IU/mL), consistent with immune-active chronic hepatitis B infection. Renal biopsy showed nearly normal glomerular architecture on light microscopy, diffuse podocyte foot process effacement on electron microscopy, and no significant immune complex deposition on immunofluorescence, confirming MCD.

INTERVENTIONS: Antiviral therapy with tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg orally once daily was initiated and continued throughout the 3-year follow-up period.

OUTCOMES: Proteinuria progressively improved, and complete remission was achieved at 8 months (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, 0.2). The patient maintained sustained remission with persistent viral suppression during a 3-year follow-up.

LESSONS: Complete remission of MCD was temporally associated with antiviral monotherapy in a patient with immune-active HBV. Although potential confounding factors such as spontaneous remission or the supportive effects of concurrent angiotensin receptor blocker therapy cannot be entirely excluded, this case suggests that viral suppression may play a role in restoring podocyte function. Renal biopsy is essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning because corticosteroid therapy may exacerbate viral replication and hepatic injury. Antiviral monotherapy may represent a reasonable initial therapeutic strategy in select patients with biopsy-proven MCD and active hepatitis B infection.

articles.title: A cross-sectional study on the relationship between hepatitis C virus infection and the risk of sleep disorders among adults based on NHANES data from 2017 to 2020: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Patients with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection often report sleep‑related complaints, but the relationship between HCV and clinically significant sleep disturbances remains poorly defined. This cross‑sectional study aimed to explore whether HCV infection is associated with an increased risk of sleep disorder among adults. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017 to 2020 were analyzed. HCV infection status and sleep disorder were assessed using standardized questionnaires. Covariates including gender, age, race, marital status, alcohol use, body mass index, diabetes status, cancer history, and smoking status were adjusted in the analysis. A total of 7924 participants aged 20 to 80 years were enrolled, of whom 2310 had sleep disorder. The prevalence of HCV infection was significantly higher in participants with sleep disorder. After adjustment for potential confounders by multivariable logistic regression, HCV infection was independently associated with an increased risk of sleep disorder (odds ratio = 2.08; 95% confidence interval = 1.37-3.15; P < .05). HCV infection is significantly associated with an elevated risk of sleep disorder in adults. HCV screening among patients with sleep complaints may facilitate comprehensive clinical management.

articles.title: Biodegradable pins fixation for lateral condylar fracture of the humerus in children: A retrospective study of biodegradable pin fixation combined with versus without absorbable tension band wiring.
articles.abstract: Biodegradable pins are increasingly used in the treatment of lateral condylar fractures of the humerus (LCFH) in children, but the strength of the biodegradable pin is weaker than that of K-wire. However, to enhance the stability of LCFH fixed by biodegradable pins, absorbable tension band wiring is often combined with the application, yet high-quality comparative evidence verifying the clinical value of this auxiliary reinforcement remains lacking. This study aimed to compare and analyze whether auxiliary absorbable tension band wiring has clinical significance for Weiss type III LCFH and to clarify whether additional tension band fixation is clinically necessary in reducing postoperative complications and improving fracture stability. This study enrolled 96 children with Weiss type III LCFH admitted between January 2017 and September 2019. The patients were divided into 2 groups: A (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins alone, n = 45) and B (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins and combined with the application of absorbable figure-of-eight tension band wiring, n = 51). Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative indicators, including age, sex, operation time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, and postoperative complications, were compared between the 2 groups. Postoperative elbow function was assessed by using the Flynn grading system. All radiographic measurements and functional evaluations were performed by 2 calibrated orthopedic surgeons with excellent inter-rater reliability. Sample size calculations were performed before data collection to guarantee statistical validity. There were no significant differences in age, sex, injured side, preoperative fracture displacement, operation duration, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, or Flynn functional grading (all P > .05). Complete fracture union was observed in all patients, and no adverse complications, such as wound infection, bone nonunion, osteonecrosis, or elbow deformity, occurred in either group. Absorbable tension band wiring reinforcement is not required after biodegradable pin fixation in the treatment of LCFH in children.

articles.title: Association of 24 hour mean blood glucose levels with mortality in patients with acute pancreatitis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aims to investigate the impact of 24 hour mean blood glucose (24h MBG) levels on the mortality of patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis (AP) and to explore the clinical implications of this association. A retrospective examination of clinical datasets of AP patients was performed using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV database. The optimal 24h MBG levels threshold was determined by the X-tile tool. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to assess the prognostic significance of 24h MBG levels. A survival analysis was carried out, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves were constructed to show survival probabilities over time. To strengthen result validity and reduce covariate confounding, a 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) technique was implemented. An external validation was also performed with a cohort of 766 AP patients from the eICU database. A total of 977 subjects were enrolled in this study. The 24h MBG level's optimal cutoff for predicting in-hospital mortality was determined to be 146 mg/dL. Following PSM analysis, 336 pairs of subjects were identified, achieving equilibrium in most baseline characteristics. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that patients with 24h MBG of 146 mg/dL or higher exhibited significantly elevated rates of in-hospital, 30-day, and 90-day mortality compared to those with 24h MBG below 146 mg/dL (P < .05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis, after adjusting for potential confounding factors, indicated that patients with 24h MBG of 146 mg/dL or higher had a markedly increased odds of in-hospital mortality relative to those with a mean BG below 146 mg/dL (odds ratio = 3.9, 95% confidence interval: 1.86~8.21, P < .001). Consistent results were observed in the PSM-adjusted cohort. Our findings indicate a significant correlation between 24h MBG levels and mortality in patients who have suffered from AP. The results presented in this study are significant and emphasize the necessity for healthcare providers to take into account the impact of 24h MBG levels in effectively managing mortality.

articles.title: Three traditional Chinese patent medicines combined with transarterial chemoembolization for primary liver cancer: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate of 3 Chinese herbal medicines (Compound Banmao Capsule, Huaier Granule, and Jinlong Capsule) combined with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for primary liver cancer using Bayesian network meta-analysis.

METHODS: We systematically searched randomized controlled trials (RCTs) across the Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang databases from their inception to January 10, 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed study quality using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed using RStudio to synthesize and hierarchically rank interventions by effect size in the included RCTs. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251019361).

RESULTS: Thirty-one RCTs involving 2604 patients with primary liver cancer were included. The network meta-analysis showed that, compared with TACE alone: Compound Banmao Capsule ranked highest for ORR (OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.08, 2.08), followed by Huaier Granule (OR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.05, 2.05) and Jinlong Capsule (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.65). For disease control rate, the ranking was Compound Banmao Capsule (OR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.76, 1.93), Jinlong Capsule (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.85, 1.59), and Huaier Granule (OR = 1.12, 95% CI: 0.66, 1.91).

CONCLUSION: For ORR, the combination of the 3 Chinese herbal medicines with TACE showed superior efficacy to TACE monotherapy, with Compound Banmao Capsule demonstrating the greatest therapeutic potential among the interventions evaluated.

articles.title: Influenza A (H1N1) virus infection complicated by checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a common, potentially severe adverse event in cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy, with glucocorticoids as the standard first-line treatment. Traditionally, glucocorticoids are avoided in confirmed viral pneumonia because they may delay viral clearance and increase secondary infection risk. No standardized strategy is available for managing concurrent CIP and viral pneumonia, and inappropriate treatment can lead to irreversible clinical deterioration.

PATIENT CONCERNS: Following neoadjuvant immunotherapy, the patient developed concurrent influenza A (H1N1) infection and CIP, accompanied by persistent respiratory dysfunction and progressive pulmonary lesions.

DIAGNOSES: Combined with the patient's immunotherapy history, respiratory symptoms, imaging changes, and positive influenza A (H1N1) etiological results, a final diagnosis of concurrent CIP and H1N1 viral pneumonia was established.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient initially received antiviral and empirical antibiotic therapy. Due to ongoing clinical deterioration and poor response to anti-infective treatment, glucocorticoids were reinitiated to target CIP after comprehensive evaluation.

OUTCOMES: The patient showed early radiographic worsening and intractable respiratory failure with no response to initial anti-infective management. After glucocorticoid administration, clinical symptoms and pulmonary lesions improved significantly, achieving a favorable recovery.

LESSONS: Isolated antiviral and antibiotic treatment may fail to control disease progression in patients with concurrent CIP and influenza A pneumonia. Timely and rational glucocorticoid use can reverse clinical deterioration and improve prognosis even in the setting of active viral infection. This case provides practical evidence for the individualized management of overlapping CIP and viral pneumonia.

articles.title: The bidirectional causal relationships of insomnia with eleven cancers: A Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Insomnia is closely associated with tumors and is recognized as a risk factor for cancer development. This two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study investigated the potential causal link between genetically determined insomnia and various cancers, including brain, colorectal, esophageal, gastric, hepatic bile duct, liver, lung, malignant lymphoma, pancreatic, skin, and thyroid cancers. Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies for insomnia and eleven cancer types were examined. instrumental variables (IVs) were selected from single nucleotide polymorphisms that passed strict quality control for minimal linkage disequilibrium and genome-wide significance. All IVs demonstrated strong predictive power for insomnia, with F-statistics exceeding the conventional threshold of 10. The primary analysis was conducted using the inverse variance weighted method. Sensitivity analyses were performed using MR-Egger regression, weighted median, and weighted mode methods to test robustness, pleiotropy, and heterogeneity. MR analysis suggested potential causal associations between insomnia and increased risk of hepatic bile duct cancer (odds ratio [OR] = 4.458, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.074-18.493, P = .040), reduced risk of hepatic cancer (OR = 0.312, 95% CI: 0.100-0.973, P = .045), and reduced risk of skin cancers (OR = 0.599, 95% CI: 0.439-0.818, P = .001). However, after Bonferroni correction (adjusted threshold P < .0045), these associations did not retain statistical significance. No notable causal influence of these cancers on insomnia was observed. Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of reverse causality or significant bias. These findings, though not retaining statistical significance after stringent multiple testing correction, provide suggestive evidence that genetically predicted insomnia may influence the risk of certain cancers, potentially through mechanisms involving genetic predisposition and biological pathways that modulate inflammation, immune function, and circadian rhythms. The study highlights the translational value of understanding insomnia's role in cancer risk, suggesting that clinicians should consider this association when managing patients with insomnia. Further research with larger sample sizes is warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Causal effects of antihypertensive drugs on thyroid diseases: A trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Thyroid disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular disease, including hypertension, but whether long-term modulation of antihypertensive drug targets influences thyroid disease risk remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the associations of 7 antihypertensive drug-target classes with thyroid diseases in European and East Asian populations using a trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) framework. We performed a two-sample, trans-ancestry drug-target MR analysis of 7 antihypertensive target classes. Target-proximal single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with systolic blood pressure (SBP) were used as genetic proxies. Estimates were scaled per 1-mm Hg genetically predicted increase in SBP; the putative effect of target inhibition that lowers SBP was therefore interpreted in the opposite direction. Summary statistics were obtained for 4 primary thyroid diseases, benign thyroid tumors where available, and 3 thyroid-related proteins in European and East Asian datasets. Hypertension was used as a positive-control outcome. Random-effects inverse-variance weighting was the primary method, with Wald ratio estimation for single-nucleotide polymorphism instruments and weighted-median, Cochran's Q, MR-Egger, and Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier analyses as sensitivity assessments. Within the European populace, genetic surrogates for β-blockers exhibit (odds ratio = 0.93; 95% confidence interval = 0.87-0.99) a close association with heightened susceptibility to thyroid carcinoma, whereas KCNH2 (1.15; 1.01-1.32) demonstrates an inverse correlation with thyroid cancer risk. Moreover, calcium channel blockers exhibit a conspicuous linkage with an elevated incidence of hyperthyroidism (0.97; 0.96-0.99) alongside a diminished likelihood of thyroid cancer (1.07; 1.03-1.10). CYP17A1 exerts a protective influence against hyperthyroidism (1.04; 10.1-1.07) and Graves disease (1.10; 1.05-1.16) but manifests a pathogenic effect concerning hypothyroidism (0.99; 0.97-1.00) and thyroid cancer (0.92; 0.86-0.98). Conversely, KCNJ11 demonstrates a proximate correlation between diminished hypothyroidism risk and augmented thyroid cancer susceptibility (0.83; 0.73-0.95). Analogous estimations were noted for CYP17A1 within the East Asian cohort. Genetically proxied perturbation of several antihypertensive drug targets was associated with thyroid disease risk, with CYP17A1 showing the broadest cross-ancestry pattern. These estimates reflect lifelong target-proximal genetic effects rather than the clinical effects of prescribed drugs and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending replication, pharmacoepidemiological studies, and randomized clinical trials.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears: A systematic review from image optimization to prognosis prediction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically.

RESULTS: Sixty-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised-phenotyping study. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data. QUADAS-2 classified overall risk-of-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction-model studies as high risk-of-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference.

CONCLUSION: AI has proof-of-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and standardized task-specific reporting are required.

articles.title: Impact of a zero-visitation policy on healthcare-associated infections in a non-COVID intensive care unit: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: The impact of visitor restrictions in intensive care units (ICUs) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remains unclear. This study aimed to compare HAI rates between the pre-pandemic restricted-visitation period and the pandemic zero-visitation period in a non-COVID tertiary ICU. This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients admitted to the Anesthesiology and Reanimation ICU of the Duzce University Health Practice and Research Center between March 14, 2019, and March 13, 2021. Patients admitted during the pre-pandemic restricted-visitation period were assigned to Group 19 -20, whereas those admitted during the pandemic zero-visitation period were assigned to Group 20-21. Patients with an ICU stay of < 48 hours, infection at admission, or infection developing within the first 48 hours were excluded. The primary outcome was HAI incidence. Secondary outcomes included the standardized infection ratio, cumulative attributable difference, inflammatory markers, and microbiological findings. A total of 933 patients were screened, and 206 patients met the inclusion criteria (Group 20-21, n = 115; Group 19-20, n = 91). In the patient-based analysis, the HAI rate was significantly lower in Group 20-21 than in Group 19-20 (6.1% vs 22.0%, P < .001). Similar findings were observed in the episode-based analysis (10.4% vs 33.0%, P < .001). The time to infection onset was significantly longer in Group 20-21 (P = .003). Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, and lactate levels were significantly lower during the zero-visitation period. The standardized infection ratio for ventilator-associated pneumonia was significantly lower in Group 20-21 (P = .02). A marked reduction in the number of Acinetobacter spp. isolates was also observed during the pandemic. A zero-visitation policy in a non-COVID tertiary ICU was associated with lower HAI rates. The consistency of the surveillance indicators, inflammatory markers, and microbiological findings supports the observed association. However, these findings should not be attributed solely to visitor restrictions and should be interpreted in the context of multiple infection control measures implemented during the pandemic.

articles.title: Neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio for predicting delayed neurologic sequelae caused by carbon monoxide poisoning: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study summarized and analyzed the prognostic value of the neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for delayed neurologic sequelae (DNS) caused by carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure Database were searched to identify relevant articles from their inception to February 2026. The odds ratio and its 95% confidence interval (CI), area under the curve, meta-regression analysis, sensitivity analysis, and publication bias for NLR were estimated to predict DNS.

RESULTS: Eight studies were included, involving 1757 patients with acute CO poisoning, among whom 382 cases (21.7%) developed DNS. The pooled results show that NLR was related to DNS (odds ratio = 14.67, 95% CI: 8.26-26.04, P < .001) and had high heterogeneity (I2 = 65.1%, P = .005). The area under the curve of NLR for predicting DNS was 0.88 (95% CI: 0.85-0.91), with a sensitivity of 86% and a specificity of 72%. Subgroup analysis indicated that study design may be the source of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis suggested the robustness of the results. Deek's test did not detect significant publication bias (P = .24).

CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that an elevated NLR is associated with an increased risk of DNS after acute CO poisoning, supporting its potential utility as a prognostic marker. However, because the included studies showed substantial heterogeneity and were predominantly retrospective, these findings should be interpreted with caution and require validation in high-quality prospective studies. NLR should therefore be considered an auxiliary tool for risk stratification rather than an independent diagnostic method. Its principal clinical value may lie in resource-limited settings where advanced monitoring is not feasible.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of imeglimin hydrochloride for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with type 2 diabetes: Single-center, single-arm phase 2 (IMELD study).
articles.abstract: Imeglimin, a novel oral antidiabetic agent classified as a glimin, was developed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D). This single-center, single-arm interventional study evaluated the efficacy and safety of 24-week imeglimin treatment in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and T2D. Patients with MASLD and T2D were treated with imeglimin 1000 mg twice daily for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was reduction in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels from baseline. Secondary endpoints included changes in metabolic parameters (including hemoglobin A1c, homeostatic model assessment of β-cell function, and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance), liver-related parameters (including aspartate aminotransferase [AST], gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, hepatic fat, and fibrosis markers), and body composition. Twenty-five patients were included in the final analysis. As a primary outcome, the median ALT level was significantly reduced, from 56.00 (47.00-75.00) U/L at baseline to 34.00 (29.00-51.00) U/L at 24 weeks (P < .001). AST level and hemoglobin A1c value were also significantly reduced. The fibrosis-4 index showed a significant reduction at 12 weeks. By contrast, no significant changes were observed for gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, homeostatic model assessment of β-cell function, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance, hepatic fat content parameters, other fibrosis-related parameters (excluding fibrosis-4 index), and body composition. All adverse events were grade 1, and no patients discontinued treatment due to adverse events. Imeglimin treatment was associated with improvements in serum ALT and AST levels after 24 weeks in patients with MASLD and T2D. These findings provide preliminary evidence of the potential clinical utility of imeglimin in this population and warrant confirmation in larger randomized controlled studies.

articles.title: Acute colonic variceal bleeding treated with coil-assisted retrograde transvenous obliteration following atezolizumab-bevacizumab therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Colonic variceal bleeding is a rare but potentially life-threatening manifestation of portal hypertension. Bevacizumab therapy is associated with an increased risk of variceal bleeding, but bleeding from ectopic varices is less well recognized.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 66-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and advanced hepatocellular carcinoma developed hematochezia on the day following the initiation of atezolizumab plus bevacizumab therapy.

DIAGNOSES: Acute ascending colonic variceal bleeding in the setting of portal hypertension and portal vein thrombosis.

INTERVENTIONS: Coil-assisted retrograde transvenous obliteration (CARTO) was performed via the right common femoral vein. The portocolonic shunt was embolized using detachable coils and gelfoam slurry.

OUTCOMES: Hematochezia ceased immediately after the procedure, and the patient remained hemodynamically stable without further transfusion. Follow-up computed tomography confirmed successful embolization of the variceal complex without residual shunt.

LESSONS: CARTO may be an effective treatment option for colonic variceal bleeding, particularly in patients with portal vein thrombosis or complex portosystemic shunts. Clinicians should remain aware of the potential for bleeding from ectopic varices in patients receiving bevacizumab-based therapy.

articles.title: A quality appraisal of clinical practice guidelines for herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia using the AGREE II instrument: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study systematically assesses the methodological quality of both Western and traditional medicine clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) using the Appraisal of Guidelines Research and Evaluation (AGREE II) instrument.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted up to January 10, 2025 to identify CPGs for HZ or PHN, regardless of whether they were based on Western or traditional medicine. All CPGs addressing diagnosis, evaluation, treatment, prevention, and management were included. Two evaluators independently screened the records and extracted the data. The quality of the CPGs was independently assessed by 5 evaluators using the AGREE II instrument. The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was calculated to assess inter-rater reliability.

RESULTS: Eleven CPGs were included, consisting of ten from Western medicine and 1 from traditional medicine. The AGREE II domain scores were as follows: The "Clarity of Presentation" domain received the highest score (76.2%), whereas "Editorial Independence," "Stakeholder Involvement," and "Applicability" scored below 30%, with "Applicability" receiving the lowest score (10.9%). Inter-rater reliability was excellent, with ICCs for the AGREE II domains ranging from 0.927 to 0.990. Four CPGs were rated as Moderate quality (Recommended with modifications), and 6 CPGs were of Low quality (Not recommended). Among the Western medicine CPGs, JASP 2021 was the only 1 rated as High quality (Recommended), whereas CACMS 2013, the only traditional medicine CPG, was rated as Low quality (Not recommended).

CONCLUSION: The findings reveal considerable variability in quality, with overall low-to-moderate quality observed in the guidelines for HZ and PHN. These results highlight the need to address the domains with consistently low scores identified by the AGREE II instrument by adopting a multidisciplinary approach, strengthening applicability, and ensuring rigor in the development process to improve guideline quality.

articles.title: Moxibustion for depression: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moxibustion, a traditional Chinese medicine therapy, is widely used for various diseases and has recently been applied in treating depression. This study aims to systematically assess the efficacy and safety of moxibustion, either alone or in combination with other therapies, for depression.

METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive search across 7 databases from their inception to December 20, 2023, focusing on randomized controlled trials that compared moxibustion with sham treatments, no treatment, or conventional therapies. The primary outcomes were the overall effective rate and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores, with adverse reaction incidence as the secondary outcome. Data were analyzed with RevMan 5.4 and Stata 18, with bias risk assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Evidence quality was graded with GRADEpro.

RESULTS: This study included 15 randomized controlled trials with 1510 patients. Meta-analysis results showed that moxibustion, alone or combined with other therapies, was more effective than other treatments for managing depression (relative risk = 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI]: [1.03-1.10], P = .0003). Moxibustion, either alone or in combination with other treatments, significantly reduced Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores compared to other treatments used alone (mean difference = -2.10, 95% CI: [-3.00 to -1.20]), with its efficacy comparable to that of antidepressant medications (mean difference = -0.60, 95% CI [-1.31 to 0.12], P = .10). Additionally, in terms of safety, the incidence of adverse reactions associated with moxibustion alone or in combination with other therapies for depression is relatively low (relative risk = 0.57, 95% CI: [0.39-0.84], P = .005). However, the overall quality of the evidence was assessed as low to very low.

CONCLUSION: Moxibustion has been shown to alleviate depressive symptoms, particularly when combined with other therapies, offering both enhanced efficacy and safety. However, further high-quality studies are necessary to confirm its effectiveness.

articles.title: Association between the uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio and diabetic kidney disease in U.S. adults with type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study of NHANES 2009 to 2018.
articles.abstract: The uric-acid-to- high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol ratio (UHR) combines 2 circulating biomarkers related to metabolic and inflammatory processes. Its association with prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) was examined in U.S. adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. This study aimed to examine the cross-sectional association between UHR and prevalent DKD and assess its incremental discrimination beyond the specified covariate model. We analyzed 4010 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus from NHANES 2009 to 2018 using the complex survey design. DKD was defined as urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g and/or estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, calculated using the 2009 chronic kidney disease epidemiology collaboration equation without its race coefficient. Strict DKD required both abnormalities; severe DKD required urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g. Model 3 was the primary confounder-adjusted model, and model 4 added laboratory indicators as an extended sensitivity analysis. Supplementary analyses assessed nonlinearity, discrimination and graphical calibration. Exploratory unweighted category-based net reclassification improvement used 500 bootstrap replicates and percentile confidence intervals. Of 4010 participants, 1576 had study-defined DKD; the weighted prevalence was 35.4%. In model 3, the highest versus lowest ln-UHR quartile had an odds ratio of 2.43 (95% confidence interval 1.75-3.38) for original DKD, 4.55 (2.81-7.35) for strict DKD and 2.82 (1.57-5.06) for severe DKD. Estimates were attenuated in model 4, with the severe-DKD contrast no longer meeting the 0.05 threshold. The laboratory-adjusted spline indicated nonlinearity (P < .001). In the separate laboratory-inclusive discrimination analysis, adding ln-UHR increased apparent area under the curve from 0.75 to 0.76; the unweighted net reclassification improvement was 1.9% (95% confidence interval 0.8%-3.1%). Higher UHR was associated with prevalent DKD after adjustment for the selected potential confounders. Supplementary analyses showed a small increase in apparent discrimination. These cross-sectional findings require prospective investigation and independent external validation before use for future risk prediction or clinical screening.

articles.title: Impact of portal hypertension on clinical outcomes in critically Ill adult patients: A retrospective study: Outcomes in critically Ill patients with portal hypertension.
articles.abstract: Liver dysfunction is a common complication in critically ill patients, and portal hypertension (PHT) represents a severe hepatic pathological condition closely associated with adverse patient outcomes. This study aims to investigate the impact of PHT on clinical outcomes in critically ill adult patients. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Market for Intensive Care IV database. All critically ill patients admitted to the hospital were included in this study. Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the correlation between PHT and hospital mortality, length of stay in the intensive care unit (LOS-ICU), and length of stay in hospital in critically ill patients, and multiple collinearity checks were performed. Propensity score matching was used to minimize group differences, and subgroup analyses were conducted. A total of 46,804 adult critically ill patients were included in this study. The hospital mortality rate for critically ill patients with PHT was 19%, significantly higher than the 8.8% mortality rate for patients without PHT (P < .05). Critically ill patients with PHT also had longer LOS-ICU and length of stay in hospital and higher total bilirubin levels (P < .05). Furthermore, multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that PHT was significantly associated with hospital mortality (OR: 2.716, 95% CI: 2.330-3.158, P < .001). After propensity score matching, the baseline differences between the 2 groups were significantly reduced, and the results showed that critically ill patients with PHT had worse clinical outcomes. However, the LOS-ICU was not significantly different after matching. PHT is a significant predictor of poor prognosis in critically ill adult patients, necessitating enhanced clinical monitoring and management to improve their clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Clarifying Transfusion Endpoint and Safety Reporting in the Phase III rhTPO Trial.
Incidence and Risk Factors for C. difficile Reinfection After Faecal Microbiota Transplantation or Antibiotic Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Faecal microbiota transplant (FMT) is an effective treatment for multiply recurrent C. difficile infection (mrCDI). Less is known about rates of reinfection after successful FMT. We aimed to estimate the incidence of CDI reinfection, 6 or more months after FMT, to determine whether rates differ between mrCDI treated with and without FMT and whether proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy increases the risk of reinfection.

METHODS: Among patients with mrCDI (defined as ≥ 2 recurrences after the initial CDI episode) we compared reinfection with CDI (defined as a first recurrence > 183 days after treatment completion) in patients who underwent antibiotics followed by FMT with those treated with antibiotics alone in Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database (OPTUM CDM). We also compared reinfection between those with and without PPI use in OPTUM CDM and the American Gastroenterological Association FMT Registry.

RESULTS: In OPTUM CDM, 6384 patients treated with antibiotics alone and 1786 with antibiotics + FMT met inclusion criteria (median follow-up 704 days). One-year and 3-year CDI reinfection incidences were 5% and 10% in the FMT group and 6% and 12% in the antibiotics group: Cox regression HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.73-1.08. PPI use was associated with an increased risk of reinfection following FMT (HR 1.57, 1.03-2.41) in OPTUM CDM and in the FMT Registry (HR 1.62, 95% CI 0.84-3.12).

CONCLUSIONS: CDI reinfection rates are low after successful FMT and similar to rates in patients treated with antibiotics alone. PPI use was associated with reinfection, supporting reassessment of the ongoing indication for PPI therapy in patients with mrCDI.

articles.title: Combined Karyotyping, Copy Number Variation Sequencing, and Whole Exome Sequencing in the Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease: Detection Rates and Phenotypic Associations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the value of genetic testing in the prenatal congenital heart disease (CHD) diagnosis and evaluate the relationship between genetic variants and prenatal phenotypes.

METHODS: A total of 235 fetuses with CHD were classified into three groups: A: isolated simple CHD, B: isolated complex CHD, and C: non-isolated CHD. All patients underwent karyotyping and copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq), with whole-exome sequencing (WES) performed when indicated. Statistical analyses conducted using IBM SPSS assessed the diagnostic performance of the genetic testing and detection rates across CHD subtypes.

RESULTS: Karyotyping and CNV-seq revealed that chromosomal abnormality detection, particularly numerical abnormalities, was significantly associated with extracardiac anomalies (p < 0.05). In contrast, the detection rates of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) CNVs (CNV-seq, p = 0.384) and pathogenic gene variants (WES, p = 0.624) did not differ significantly among the three groups. The severity of intracardiac abnormalities, the presence of extracardiac anomalies, and the detection of genetic abnormalities significantly influenced parental decisions regarding pregnancy termination (p < 0.05). The combination of karyotyping and CNV-seq increased the detection rate by 5.11%. In karyotyping/CNV-seq-negative fetuses who underwent WES, WES increased the detection rate by 37.21% (16/43).

CONCLUSION: Combined genetic testing significantly improved the detection rate and the detection of chromosomal numerical abnormalities was strongly associated with the presence of extracardiac anomalies. Parental decisions regarding pregnancy continuation were significantly influenced by the severity of intracardiac abnormalities, the presence of extracardiac anomalies, and the identification of genetic abnormalities.

articles.title: Validating a Wearable Bluetooth Oximeter for Infants in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oxygen is vital for life but the wrong amount of oxygen can lead to significant risk of morbidity and mortality. Preterm infants are at particular risk from both too little (hypoxia) and excess (hyperoxia) oxygen. In the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), oxygen treatment is guided by oximetry derived from wired oximeters which are difficult to use outside of the hospital environment. We aimed to validate Bluetooth wireless oximeters in newborn infants to determine the accuracy of devices that would be more suitable for out of hospital use.

METHODS: Three 20 min sets of measurements including oxygen saturations (SpO2), heart rate (HR) and perfusion index (PI) from the post-ductal regions (left arm and lower limbs) were conducted in 21 spontaneously ventilating infants using the Masimo (1) SafetyNet and (2) Radical 7 oximeters. The wired Radical 7 oximeter was the reference. Data were downloaded onto CSV files and analysed for agreement.

RESULTS: Twenty-one (eight male) infants were recruited between July to September 2023. Median gestations and ages were 36 weeks and 3 days. Neither Bluetooth device (SafetyNet and wireless Radical 7) met International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standard (ARMSE ≤ 3%), Score 3.624 (wireless Rad-7) and 3.884 (SafetyNet). Both wearables consistently overestimated SpO2, with mean biases (wired-wearable) of -1.802 (Rad-7) and -1.803 (SafetyNet), that increased at lower SpO2 levels. Linear regression, ICC, Pearson's correlation analyses showed poor consistency.

CONCLUSION: Wireless oximeters have poor correlation with wired oximeters especially at lower SpO2 levels but ease of use, especially in the home environment in less acutely ill patients, requires further evaluation.

articles.title: A retrospective cohort study of Ukrainian beneficiaries of temporary protection living with HIV attending an Irish tertiary care service.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the demographic, clinical and healthcare utilization characteristics of Ukrainian beneficiaries of temporary protection living with HIV (UBOTPLWH) attending an Irish tertiary HIV service and to assess the impact of individual barriers to care on virological outcomes and retention in care.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational cohort study of adult UBOTPLWH enrolled in an outpatient HIV service in Cork University Hospital, Ireland, between February 2022 and April 2025. Data were extracted from clinical and laboratory records. Descriptive statistics summarized demographics, HIV parameters, antiretroviral therapy (ART), co-infections and healthcare utilization. Exploratory analyses assessed associations between individual barriers to care and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine patients were included; 59.3% were female and median age was 44 years (interquartile range [IQR] 39-51 years). Most (84.7%) had a known HIV diagnosis prior to arrival, with a median duration of diagnosis of 10 years. At enrolment, 66.7% were virologically suppressed (<50 copies/mL) and median CD4 count was 561 cells/μL. Prior opportunistic infection was reported in 25.0% of the 48 patients for whom such data were available. ART regimens were frequently modified following enrolment, particularly among those receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/lamivudine/dolutegravir prior to migration. At the most recent follow-up, viral load data were available for 49 participants, of whom 87.8% were suppressed. Barriers to care were common, including interpreter requirement (64.4%), geographic dispersion (median distance 54 km) and residential instability. In exploratory analyses, detectable viral load at enrolment was associated with missed clinic attendance (p = 0.019), while viral non-suppression at follow-up was associated with hospital admission (p = 0.007) and missed clinic attendance (p = 0.047).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite timely linkage to care and preserved immune status at enrolment, UBOTPLWH in Ireland experience substantial structural barriers that may adversely affect engagement and virological outcomes. Tailored, accessible service models are required to support displaced populations living with HIV.

articles.title: Abdominal Tics in Children and Adolescents: A Phenomenology-First Diagnostic Framework and Differential Diagnosis.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: Abdominal tics are a less commonly described axial or tonic tic phenotype in children and adolescents with Tourette syndrome and chronic tic disorders. Their abdominal location and symptom language may create diagnostic uncertainty with gastrointestinal, epileptic, myoclonic, respiratory or functional presentations.

METHODS: This clinically focused narrative synthesis identified relevant literature through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science from database inception through March 2026, supplemented by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and citation-chasing update during revision through August 2026 focused on focal abdominal motor seizures, CASPR2-associated movement phenomena, peripheral nerve hyperexcitability and related mimics.

RESULTS: Abdominal tics are supported by the same core tic features that apply across body regions: premonitory urge, partial suppressibility, stereotyped recurrence, waxing-and-waning course, sleep attenuation and prior or concurrent tics when present. Key neurological mimics include belly dancer's dyskinesia, propriospinal myoclonus, focal abdominal motor seizures, CASPR2-associated abdominal movement disorders and functional tic-like behaviours. Preserved awareness does not exclude a focal motor seizure. Gastrointestinal mimics include disorders of gut-brain interaction and inflammatory bowel disease. A pattern-directed clinical triage algorithm is proposed alongside management principles derived from established paediatric tic-disorder evidence, including behavioural intervention as first-line treatment and comorbidity-guided pharmacotherapy.

CONCLUSIONS: A phenomenology-first, red-flag-guided approach can improve diagnostic clarity and help clinicians avoid both reflexive investigation and premature attribution of organic disease to tics. This review provides a practical clinical triage framework for determining when an abdominal movement behaves like a tic, when targeted neurological or gastrointestinal investigation is indicated and when management can follow established tic-disorder principles.

articles.title: Drug-Drug Interactions vs. Therapeutic Combinations in Patients with Congestive Heart Failure and Diabetes: An Ambispective Real-World Study.
articles.abstract: Concomitant congestive heart failure (CHF) and diabetes mellitus (DM) patients frequently are treated with polypharmacy, thus potentially increasing the risk of drug-drug interactions (pDDIs). Conventional DDI screening methods often fail to distinguish clinically significant interactions from recommended therapeutic combinations. This study assessed the prevalence, severity, and clinical consequences of pDDIs in hospitalized patients with CHF and DM. This ambispective, cross-sectional study included 144 hospitalized patients with CHF and DM. We used the Micromedex and Lexicomp databases to check prescriptions. We classified clinically relevant DDIs and therapeutic combinations requiring routine monitoring by severity. 207 pDDIs were identified, of which 84.1% were moderate and 15.9% severe. Polypharmacy was a major risk factor for the DDI burden, and over seven drugs were associated with significantly more interactions than fewer drugs (P < 0.001). Polypharmacy was an independent predictor of clinically significant DDI (AOR 3.42; 95% CI 1.78-6.59) in the multivariate analysis. The most commonly seen combinations (statin-ezetimibe and sulfonylurea-metformin therapy) are guideline-recommended and do not need to be avoided. Clinical pharmacists and prescribing clinicians performing context-aware interpretation of DDI alerts by differentiating between guideline-recommended therapeutic combinations requiring monitoring and truly actionable interactions can reduce alert fatigue, preserve evidence-based therapy, and support safe prescribing in complex CHF-DM patients.

articles.title: FXI and FXII in experimental stroke and FXI in clinical stroke trials.
articles.abstract: Targeting the contact activation system through Factor XI (FXI) or Factor XII (FXII) inhibition represents a major paradigm shift in antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke. Unlike traditional anticoagulants, contact pathway factors drive pathological thrombus propagation and thromboinflammation; crucially, while FXII plays a negligible role in physiological hemostasis, FXI contributes only secondarily, thereby substantially uncoupling antithrombotic efficacy from major bleeding risk. However, a notable disconnect exists between experimental models and clinical development. Preclinical stroke literature, primarily rodent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) models, is overwhelmingly concentrated on FXII targeting, where FXII deficiency or blockade consistently reduces cerebral infarct volumes, preserves microvascular perfusion, and attenuates thromboinflammation, whereas experimental studies of direct FXI treatment remain sparse. Conversely, human clinical translation has focused largely on oral FXIa inhibitors, maintaining a favorable bleeding profile across indications but yielding mixed efficacy, ranging from neutral Phase II studies and the early termination of OCEANIC-AF to positive secondary stroke prevention data. Following positive OCEANIC-STROKE findings, asundexian (under FDA priority review as of September 2026) emerges as a prospective add-on to antiplatelet therapy for the secondary prevention of noncardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA, particularly in nonlacunar or atherosclerotic populations. Reconciling preclinical FXII data with clinical FXIa trial outcomes provides a timely rationale to systematically review evidence across MCAO models and human stroke trials to delineate the distinct therapeutic potentials of FXI and FXII inhibition.

articles.title: Venetoclax-based combinations in high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: highlights from ASH 2025 & EHA 2026.
articles.abstract: High-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS) are associated with poor survival despite standard therapy with hypomethylating agents (HMAs). Although the VERONA trial did not meet its primary endpoint, a granular interpretation of these results alongside real-life data may help identify patient subsets that could potentially benefit. At the 2025 American Society of Hematology (ASH) Meeting and at the 2026 European Hematology Association Congress (EHA), several studies reported updated data on venetoclax-based combinations in HR-MDS across clinical and biological subgroups.
