The randomized phase III VERONA study evaluated venetoclax plus azacitidine (VEN/HMA) versus azacitidine alone in the frontline setting, while additional phase I/II and real-life studies explored oral hypomethylating backbones, therapy-related disease, and molecularly defined subsets. Collectively, these data suggest that venetoclax enhances response rates in HR-MDS, although survival benefits remain heterogeneous, with a potential benefit observed when used as a bridge to transplantation. Given the lack of randomized data in transplant-eligible patients, this Correspondence provides a narrative, non-systematic review of the available evidence based mostly on abstracts and not peer reviewed publications. Additionally, we summarize the most clinically relevant findings and discuss their implications for future treatment strategies.

articles.title: Revascularize first, resect second: off-pump excision of giant SVG pseudoaneurysm.
articles.journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Saphenous vein graft pseudoaneurysm is a rare late complication of coronary artery bypass grafting. Management is particularly challenging when the pseudoaneurysm-bearing graft remains an active source of myocardial perfusion. A 67-year-old man presented 33 years after coronary artery bypass grafting with progressive exertional dyspnea. Echocardiography demonstrated a large mass abutting the right atrium. Computed tomography angiography showed a 10 × 7 × 6 cm partially thrombosed pseudoaneurysm arising from the saphenous vein graft to the right posterior descending artery, with right atrial compression. Coronary angiography demonstrated pseudoaneurysm filling from the graft, chronic native right coronary artery occlusion, patent mammary grafts, and severe proximal graft stenosis. The heart team considered transcatheter exclusion unsuitable because of the distal entry site, calcific graft disease, and ongoing distal right coronary dependence. Redo off-pump saphenous vein grafting to the right posterior descending artery was performed before old-graft ligation. After transit-time flow measurement confirmed new-graft function, the pseudoaneurysm-bearing graft was ligated proximally and distally and excised en bloc. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 5. Three-month computed tomography angiography demonstrated a patent new graft without residual pseudoaneurysm.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights that graft patency and myocardial dependence should be defined before exclusion of a saphenous vein graft pseudoaneurysm. In selected patients, revascularization before graft sacrifice can be performed off pump, avoiding cardiopulmonary bypass while preserving myocardial perfusion.

articles.title: The advances and challenges of mRNA-LNP application in fields of hematology and oncology therapeutics.
articles.abstract: The rapidly global deployment of COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines established the clinical feasibility of combining RNA medicine with LNP delivery systems, transforming a long-standing experimental concept into a scalable therapeutic modality, previously considered impossible. Currently, the value of mRNA-LNPs has been expanding from infectious disease vaccines to cancer immunotherapy, personalized neoantigen vaccination, in vivo immune-cell engineering, protein replacement therapy, mRNA-encoded biologics and genome editing, with particular relevance to hematology and oncology. However, in hematologic and oncologic settings, therapeutic success is constrained by biological barriers that less prominent in prophylactic vaccination. Systemically administered LNPs are strongly influenced by hepatic sequestration, protein corona formation and mononuclear-phagocyte clearance; solid tumors additionally present heterogeneous vasculature, variable enhanced permeability and retention, dense extracellular matrix, elevated interstitial pressure and limited intratumoral diffusion. Hematologic applications face a different set of constraints, including access to spleen and bone marrow, selective delivery to T cells, NK cells and hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and preservation of the normal marrow niche. In this Review, we therefore discuss the molecular and principles of formulation that underpin mRNA-LNP performance in hematology and oncology, including mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle architecture, intracellular trafficking and selective organ targeting(SORT) delivery strategies, oncology applications spanning neoantigen vaccines, tumor-microenvironment reprogramming, mRNA-encoded biologics, gene editing and combination therapy; and hematology applications including in vivo CAR-T, CAR-NK and HSPC engineering. We further consider how inefficient extrahepatic delivery, limited endosomal escape, context-dependent reactogenicity, repeat-dosing constraints and the manufacturing complexity of individualized products continue to limit broader clinical translation. Emerging strategies, including artificial-intelligence-guided RNA and lipid design, self-amplifying RNA, circular RNA and next-generation thermostable formulations, may help address these application limitations in the fields of hematology and oncology.

articles.title: Seizures Secondary to Aconitum Plant Poisoning: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aconitum plant poisoning typically manifests as isolated early cardiotoxicity or late neurotoxicity. However, the dynamic temporal evolution from arrhythmia-driven cardiogenic syncope to true epileptic seizures mediated by direct central nervous system injury remains rarely documented and poorly characterized.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 53-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with ventricular tachycardia rapidly degenerating into ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest following ingestion of homemade Aconitum kusnezoffii (caowu)-infused liquor. Initial convulsions were tightly coupled with malignant arrhythmias, consistent with cardiogenic syncope. After successful resuscitation, hemoperfusion, and restoration of stable sinus rhythm, the patient developed breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizures on hospital days 4-6. Electroencephalography performed during sedation withdrawal revealed bilateral occipital spike-and-slow and sharp-and-slow waves with focal epileptiform discharges, confirming direct central nervous system neurotoxicity rather than recurrent cardiac ischemia. A mechanism-based, staged treatment strategy was employed: early advanced cardiac life support and hemoperfusion targeted cardiotoxicity, while sodium valproate and acetylglutamine were administered for antiepileptic prophylaxis and neuroprotection. The patient was discharged on day 13; antiepileptic therapy was successfully tapered and discontinued at 3 months without seizure recurrence, with normalization of electroencephalography and electrocardiography.

CONCLUSIONS: This case provides the first systematic documentation, validated by electroencephalography, of the transition from cardiogenic convulsions to true epileptic seizures in Aconitum alkaloid poisoning. The findings highlight the critical role of pharmacokinetic-driven central nervous system retention in delayed seizure onset and underscore the necessity of prolonged neurological monitoring, early electroencephalography evaluation for late-onset convulsions, and sustained antiepileptic prophylaxis to reduce mortality and long-term neurological sequelae.

KEY CLINICAL MESSAGE: Aconitum plant poisoning may manifest as early cardiogenic syncope and convulsions secondary to malignant arrhythmias, progressing in the late stage to genuine seizures caused by central nervous system (CNS) injury. Effective management requires a staged treatment strategy targeting both cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity, with a focus on stabilizing cardiac rhythm and providing neuroprotection as needed.

articles.title: The impact of COVID-19 on all-cause mortality and life expectancy: findings from a population-based cohort in uMkhanyakude district, northern KwaZulu-natal.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the comprehensive death reporting system in South Africa, significant gaps persist in our understanding of the pandemic's impact in rural areas.

METHODS: We computed monthly death counts stratified by demographic factors from a population-based demographic surveillance cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal. We fit seasonally adjusted negative binomial regression models to estimate excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic period (5 March 2020 to 31 December 2021) compared to the pre-pandemic period (1 January 2015 to 4 March 2020). We then assessed the relative risk of death by health and sociodemographic factors and considering apotential interaction with the COVID-19 pandemic. Finally, we calculated changes in life expectancy at the age of 15 and conducted a decomposition analysis to identify life expectancy changes by age group.

RESULTS: We observed two major periods of excess mortality during the beta and delta waves of the COVID-19 pandemic, respectively. During the pre-pandemic period, people with HIV (PWH) had slightly higher mortality rates (RR = 1.8; 95%CI 1.3 - 2.4) than their HIV-negative counterparts. This excess risk reduced during the COVID-19 period (HIV RR = 1.5; 95%CI 1.2 - 2.0). Similar patterns were noted for individuals with diabetes (pre-pandemic RR = 1.6; 95%CI 1.2 - 2.2 vs during COVID-19 RR = 1.4; 95%CI 1.1 - 1.9). In contrast, individuals with hypertension experienced a 15% relative increase death rate during the pandemic compared to pre-COVID period (p-interaction = 0.003). Similarly, hypertensive PWH had significantly elevated mortality risks during COVID-19 (RR = 2.18; 95% CI: 1.45-3.26, p < 0.001). Throughout the study, women consistently had higher life expectancy at age 15 than men. However, women contributed more to pandemic-related life expectancy reductions, along with specific age and health groups.

CONCLUSION: We found contrasting impacts of co-morbidities on mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic in rural South Africa, and that reductions in life expectancy at age 15 were greater in women than men. These findings emphasize the critical need to consider specific needs of rural populations, and tailor public health strategies that prioritize vulnerable populations and address health inequities to mitigate the effects of pandemics in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Multimodal imaging features of nuclear protein in testis carcinoma of the submandibular gland: a case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: NUT carcinoma (NC) is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy defined by rearrangements of the NUTM1gene. Primary NC of the submandibular gland is exceptionally rare, with nonspecific imaging features that often lead to misdiagnosis as common salivary gland tumors and delayed treatment.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 32-year-old man presented with a painless mass in the left submandibular region that rapidly enlarged from 2 cm to approximately 4 cm within 1 month, accompanied by the development of ipsilateral pharyngeal and periauricular pain.

DIAGNOSES: Preoperative multimodal imaging-computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-revealed an ill-defined, invasive mass with heterogeneous enhancement and intense metabolic activity (SUVmax 18.4). The diagnosis was confirmed by histopathological examination and immunohistochemical analysis, which demonstrated diffuse nuclear positivity for NUT protein.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient underwent radical surgical resection (left neck dissection), followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

OUTCOMES: No evidence of local recurrence or metastatic disease was observed on follow-up imaging at 9 months postoperatively.

LESSONS: This case underscores that although the imaging features of submandibular gland NC are not pathognomonic, the combination of a rapidly growing invasive mass, heterogeneous enhancement, and marked hypermetabolism should raise clinical suspicion. Prompt biopsy with NUT immunohistochemical testing is essential for definitive diagnosis and early intervention, which is critical given the tumor's highly aggressive nature.

articles.title: Quality of measurement instruments assessing Planetary and One Health Literacy related constructs: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Health and quality of life outcomes
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amid accelerating anthropogenic climate and ecological crises, the expansion of health literacy as a comprehensive and multidimensional concept addressing upstream determinants of health has become relevant. A critical gap persists in measurement research to identify validated instruments for health literacy within the environment-health nexus.

OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review of the quality of existing instruments that measure Planetary and One Health Literacy or related constructs according to the COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement INstruments (COSMIN) methodology.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in Medline, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, APA PsychInfo, APA PsycArticles, PSYNDEX, and Greenline to identify development and/or validation studies of suitable instruments. We assessed the risk of bias of each study, systematically evaluated the psychometric properties of instruments, and graded the certainty of evidence to inform recommendations for instrument use and further development.

RESULTS: Out of 192 screened records, we identified four studies employing three instruments: Climate Change Health Literacy Scale (CCHLS), Climate Change and Infectious Disease Literacy Scale, and Sustainable Food Literacy Scale (SFLS). The quality of evidence for the development and content validity in all instruments was rated low or very low. Of all scales the SFLS demonstrated the best results in the assessed measurement properties supported by very good quality of evidence in its original, while its Turkish adaptation had low methodological quality in its assessed measurement properties and insufficient reliability.

CONCLUSION: The included studies emphasised quantitative validation over robust instrument development and transparency in their reporting, highlighting the need for clearly defining constructs and involving target populations in the design processes. While existing measurement instruments primarily assess knowledge, attitudes, and behaviour, the lack of attention to the health literacy's construct calls for stronger integration between health literacy, Planetary Health, and One Health research.

articles.title: Amygdala neurofeedback as an adjunct to residential dialectical behavior therapy for borderline personality disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by affective instability and amygdala hyperreactivity. Although dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) reduces symptoms and amygdala-related abnormalities, many patients show only partial remission. Real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) amygdala neurofeedback (amy-NF) directly targets hyperactive limbic responses and has shown promise in uncontrolled trials. We examined whether amy-NF adds benefit to inpatient DBT.

METHODS: Thirty-six mid-therapy people with BPD and clinically significant residual symptoms (BSL-23 > 1.5) were randomized to DBT plus amy-NF (n = 23) or DBT alone, termed treatment as usual (TAU = 13). Post-treatment assessments were completed by 15/9 (amy-NF/TAU), with 15/8 and 12/7 completing the 3- and 6-month follow-ups. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of daily-life affective instability served as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included self-reports, amygdala responses during two fMRI tasks, and resting-state fMRI. Assessments occurred at pre-, post-, 3-, and 6-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Participants successfully downregulated amygdala activity during neurofeedback. EMA showed improvements in negative affect, inner tension, and affective instability over time, without consistent superiority of amy-NF. Self-reports likewise showed no additional benefit of amy-NF, and BSL-23 scores increased after discharge in both groups. Amy-NF was associated with transient pre-post reductions in amygdala activity during both viewing and regulation in the emotion regulation task, and with more stable amygdala reactivity over time than TAU in the faces task. Resting-state analyses showed transient pre-post increases in amygdala connectivity with precuneus and dorsomedial frontal regions in amy-NF.

CONCLUSIONS: Amygdala neurofeedback is feasible and reduced amygdala activity in BPD, but did not yield additional clinical benefit when delivered alongside intensive residential DBT, although the small sample may have limited power to detect such effects.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was preregistered 2020/03/26 on ClinicalTrials.gov and received the ID NCT04333888.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality Among U.S. Women with Breast Cancer: a National NHANES Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular complications are an important and increasingly recognized concern among women with breast cancer. Racial and ethnic differences in cardiovascular disease burden suggest that certain populations may be at heightened risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study examined racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality among women with breast cancer using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 669 women with self-reported breast cancer identified in NHANES and linked to the National Death Index. Participants were categorized by race and ethnicity as Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, Mexican American, Other Hispanic, or Other Race. Heart failure prevalence was evaluated as a clinically relevant cardiovascular outcome. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause and cardiovascular-specific mortality, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and forest plots were generated to visualize differences across groups.

RESULTS: Non-Hispanic Black women demonstrated the highest prevalence of cardiovascular disease, including heart failure (8.2%), compared with Non-Hispanic White (7.4%), Other Race (6.1%), Other Hispanic (2.2%), and Mexican American women (1.7%). Non-Hispanic Black women showed a trend toward poorer survival outcomes, with an elevated risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.80; 95% CI: 0.96-3.36) compared with Mexican American women. After multivariable adjustment, this association persisted (HR 1.81; 95% CI: 0.96-3.41). Cardiovascular-specific mortality was higher among Non-Hispanic Black women, reaching statistical significance in the fully adjusted model (adjusted HR 3.46; 95% CI: 1.66-7.24).

CONCLUSION: Racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality were observed among women with breast cancer, with Non-Hispanic Black women experiencing a higher burden. These findings highlight the need for targeted, evidence-based strategies to address cardiovascular risk and improve equitable outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Improving Spanish-Speaking Caregivers' Experience with Standardized Discharge Instructions for Asthma Exacerbation in the Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric asthma is a leading cause of emergency department (ED) utilization, with higher rates among minority populations. Families with limited English proficiency, particularly Spanish-speaking caregivers, may face discharge communication barriers that contribute to outcome disparities.

OBJECTIVE: To describe Spanish-speaking caregiver-reported experiences with discharge communication and follow-up support after receipt of a standardized Spanish-language asthma discharge protocol and to explore 72-hour ED revisit rates among participating patients.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study of Spanish-speaking caregivers of children presenting with asthma exacerbations to a tertiary pediatric ED between April 2023 and March 2025. Caregivers completed a REDCap survey assessing demographics, language preferences, interpreter use, discharge communication, and follow-up support. The primary outcome was return ED visits for asthma exacerbation within 72 h, compared with a pediatric ED population using Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Fifty-four Spanish-speaking caregivers were included. Most preferred discharge instructions in Spanish (94.4%); 30% reported effective English communication. Although satisfaction with interpreter services (92.0%) and provider explanations of asthma (92.6%) was high, 61.1% needed help scheduling follow-up appointments. Contributors to discharge confusion included provider time (23.1%), terminology (15.4%), and language barriers (15.4%). The surveyed group had a significantly higher 72-hour ED revisit rate than the control population (7.7% vs. 2.1%, p = 0.039).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite high satisfaction with interpreter services and provider explanations, gaps remained in follow-up support. The participating group also had a higher 72-hour revisit rate; however, the observational design cannot determine whether discharge communication or the standardized protocol contributed to this difference.

articles.title: Planned Antihypertensive Deprescribing in Long-Term Care Residents: A Systematic Review of Randomized Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence supporting antihypertensive treatment in older adults is derived largely from populations that differ from long-term care residents, in whom frailty, dementia, multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and competing clinical priorities may alter the balance between preventive benefit and treatment burden.

OBJECTIVES: The aim was to synthesize randomized evidence on planned antihypertensive deprescribing in institutional long-term care and determine whether clinically and methodologically comparable effects support a common treatment-effect estimate.

METHODS: Randomized or cluster-randomized studies of planned antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care were systematically reviewed. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, Web of Science Core Collection, trial registries, and PROSPERO were searched from inception and updated to 20 August 2026. Meta-analysis was reserved for outcomes with at least two clinically and methodologically compatible estimates of a common, interpretable effect; otherwise, structured study-level synthesis was used. Result-specific risk of bias was assessed with the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2), and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) tool.

RESULTS: Three randomized long-term care studies involving 1548 residents were included. Their populations, deprescribing strategies, monitoring, restart criteria, and follow-up differed substantially, and no outcome was considered sufficiently clinically and methodologically comparable for meta-analysis. RETREAT-FRAIL reported an adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause mortality of 1.02 (95% confidence interval 0.86-1.21) over a median potential follow-up of 38.4 months, whereas DANTON reported an HR of 1.65 (0.95-2.85) to 32 weeks; Gulla/COSMOS had no cluster-adjusted comparative mortality estimate. At 16 weeks in DANTON, deprescribing increased systolic blood pressure by 11.0 mmHg (5.6-16.4), increased diastolic blood pressure by 4.6 mmHg (1.1-8.1), and reduced the number of antihypertensive drugs by 1.2 (1.0-1.4). Evidence for hospitalization, falls, cardiovascular events, cognition, function, and quality of life remained sparse, outcome-specific, or at risk of bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Randomized evidence for antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care remains sparse and clinically heterogeneous. Within individual trials, supervised deprescribing reduced antihypertensive exposure and raised blood pressure, but the magnitude and clinical consequences varied by strategy and follow-up. Current evidence does not establish a common effect on mortality, hospitalization, or other resident-important outcomes, making trial-specific estimates and deprescribing protocols more informative than a single pooled treatment effect.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261370802.

articles.title: Qualitative Exit Interviews to Characterize the Positive Treatment Experiences of Patients in the Phase III Trial of Orforglipron Versus Oral Semaglutide for the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: There is an unmet need for effective and well-tolerated oral formulations of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists for the management of type 2 diabetes. Orforglipron and oral semaglutide are two oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists evaluated in the ACHIEVE-3 clinical trial (NCT06045221). These novel treatments have the means to achieve clinically meaningful glycemic control and weight reduction, which may result in substantial positive changes in patients' daily lives. The objective of this study was to conduct exit interviews following the ACHIEVE-3 trial to characterize positive treatment experiences and outcomes, beyond glycated hemoglobin and weight reduction, reported by patients living with type 2 diabetes who received oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist-based treatments.

METHODS: Qualitative interviews were conducted across ten clinical sites within the USA with patients who had enrolled in ACHIEVE-3 and completed at least 3 months of treatment. Interviews were conducted in English or Spanish, audio-recorded, and transcribed. Transcripts were analyzed to identify and categorize positive treatment benefits reported during the interviews. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the sample.

RESULTS: Sixty patients completed the qualitative exit interviews. Patients had a mean age of 59.1 years (standard deviation [SD] = 10.3), and almost half were female (n = 28, 46.7%). Patients had been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for a mean of 8.5 years (SD = 5.7). By the end of the study, patients reduced their glycated hemoglobin by 1.6% (SD = 1.3) from a baseline of 8.3% and lost a mean of 4.7 kg (SD = 6.8) from a baseline of 96.0 kg. All patients reported being satisfied with the trial medication (n = 59/59), were likely to recommend the treatment to other patients, and all but one were willing to continue taking the medication. As expected, the two most important and most frequently reported positive changes were controlled glycated hemoglobin (n = 53, 88.3%) and weight reduction (n = 50, 83.3%). Other common spontaneously reported positive concepts included increased perceived energy (n = 28, 46.7%), reduced appetite and cravings (n = 23, 38.3%), improved exercise/movement (n = 18, 30.0%), and psychological improvements (n = 18, 30.0%). Additional positive changes included increased confidence/self-esteem, improved diet and eating habits, improved sleep, and improved or a lack of deterioration in vision. All reported positive changes were considered meaningful by patients.

CONCLUSIONS: The current study explored the positive experiences of patients taking an oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist in the ACHIEVE-3 trial beyond traditional clinical benefits, such as glycemic control and weight reduction. The positive changes identified may be suitable targets for future clinical trial clinical outcome assessment endpoint strategies to help differentiate treatments and in clinical practices to classify patients' experiences.

articles.title: 68Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI for identifying corticotroph adenomas in Cushing disease: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4-targeted 68Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI can localize corticotroph adenomas in patients with Cushing disease (CD), particularly when MRI is negative or inconclusive, and explore performance in newly diagnosed versus persistent/recurrent disease.

METHODS: In this single-center pilot study, 10 patients with newly diagnosed or persistent/recurrent CD, confirmed by inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS) and/or surgical pathology, underwent 68Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI. Clinical, biochemical, radiologic, surgical, and postoperative data were reviewed. 68Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI were classified as positive or negative using visual and quantitative assessment, including maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) and target-to-background (SUVmean of the blood pool in the cavernous sinus) ratio (TBR).

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 46.7 years; 9 were female. Five had newly diagnosed and 5 had persistent/recurrent CD. Two scans showed focal pituitary 68Ga-Pentixafor uptake compared to background pituitary tissue. One was confirmed by an MRI-visible lesion, positive pathology, and postoperative remission. The second occurred with an inconclusive MRI, negative pathology, and persistent postoperative disease; however, IPSS centralized. Three patients with negative scans underwent surgery and achieved remission, indicating false-negative imaging. Among 5 patients with negative scans who did not undergo subsequent surgery, 4 had persistent/recurrent CD and 1 had newly diagnosed CD treated medically.

CONCLUSION: In this pilot cohort, 68Ga-Pentixafor PET/MRI showed limited and variable performance for corticotroph adenoma localization. Although it may provide complementary information in selected patients with MRI-visible or equivocal lesions, further study is needed before it can be incorporated into diagnostic algorithms or considered an alternative to IPSS.

articles.title: Best Practices for Optimizing Recovery from Sepsis; Results of an Expert Panel.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over one million patients survive sepsis annually in the USA. After sepsis, patients often experience new morbidity, with high rates of readmission and post-acute mortality. However, there are limited data to inform best practices to support recovery from sepsis.

METHODS: We convened an expert panel to rate the validity, importance, and resource intensity of 18 care practices aimed to support recovery from sepsis using the RAND/UCLA appropriateness method (a modified Delphi approach). The multidisciplinary panel consisted of 15 experts in sepsis, critical care, hospital medicine, primary care, geriatrics, nursing, and quality improvement, as well as Veteran patient representatives. In addition to the panel members' scores of care practices, panel deliberations were used to understand members' selections.

RESULTS: Among the 18 care practices considered, all received agreement in final grading, 10 (56%) were rated as valid, and eight (44%) were rated as uncertain validity. Among 10 valid practices, five were rated as high importance and only moderately resource-intensive-suggesting they should be prioritized for implementation. The high-importance, moderate resource-intensity practices were as follows: scheduling recommended follow-up prior to discharge; screening for limitations in basic and instrumental activities of daily living (I/ADLs) and need for durable medical equipment (DME); educating patients on signs and symptoms of sepsis; educating patients on common symptoms after sepsis (e.g., fatigue, shortness of breath, brain fog); and counseling patients and/or caregivers on discharge medications and their indications. Study limitations include the panel composition (majority VHA clinicians, no social work representation), which may have impacted ratings.

CONCLUSIONS: The expert panel used a validated method to prioritize care practices for supporting recovery from sepsis. These ratings can be used to improve management, inform quality improvement efforts, and guide resource allocation.

articles.title: Apolipoprotein A1 attenuates epirubicin-induced cardiotoxicity with GPX4-linked ferroptosis-defense modulation.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity (AIC), in which ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury has been implicated, remains a major challenge in oncology. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of an apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) mimetic peptide, L-4 F, in epirubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (EIC) in a rat model. Rats received epirubicin (2.5 mg/kg/week, i.p.) for six weeks to establish the EIC model, with or without concurrent ApoA1 mimetic treatment (L-4 F, 1 mg/kg/day). Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. Myocardial tissues underwent single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), RegDiffusion-based gene regulatory network inference, Western blot, immunohistochemistry, and ELISA. Mechanistic studies used H9C2 cardiomyoblasts and CMEC-H9C2 Transwell co-culture systems under EPI exposure, with ApoA1 treatment, endothelial IL-33 knockdown, and Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) rescue. Glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression, intracellular iron, lipid peroxidation, and cell viability were assessed. ApoA1 treatment alleviated diastolic dysfunction and weight loss and partially improved global longitudinal strain. snRNA-seq revealed substantial transcriptional remodeling in cardiomyocytes. RegDiffusion analysis identified coordinated reprogramming of transcription factor regulons, including Ppara, Fos, Egr1, and Klf4. ApoA1 treatment was associated with an anti-ferroptotic pattern of ferroptosis-related gene expression, with relatively higher Gpx4 and Slc7a11 expression and lower Tfrc expression, consistent with increased GPX4 protein levels. Intercellular communication analysis suggested enhanced IL-33/ST2-mediated endothelial-cardiomyocyte signaling following ApoA1 treatment. In vitro, ApoA1 restored GPX4 expression and reduced iron accumulation under EPI stress; these effects were potentiated in co-culture conditions and attenuated by endothelial IL-33 knockdown. In the rescue model, ApoA1 and Fer-1 partially restored viability and reduced MDA. ApoA1 alone did not significantly lower C11-BODIPY oxidation, whereas the combination gave the most consistent effect. ApoA1 attenuates EIC and is associated with modulation of GPX4-linked ferroptosis-related responses. This protective effect may involve endothelial-cardiomyocyte crosstalk, with endothelial IL-33 signaling acting as a partial contributor. These findings highlight a potential cardioprotective mechanism.

articles.title: Impact of the Sociodemographic Index on Efficacy/Safety of Tofacitinib in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: Post Hoc Analysis of Phase 2/3/3b/4 Studies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We explored the impact of the Sociodemographic Index (SDI) on the efficacy/safety of tofacitinib and adalimumab in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from phase 2/3/3b/4 studies of patients with RA receiving tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg twice daily (BID), adalimumab 40 mg every 2 weeks, or placebo. Patients were stratified into country-level SDI tertiles (low/medium/high; defined as Global Burden of Disease 2010 scores of ≤ 0.708/> 0.708-≤ 0.803/> 0.803). Efficacy/patient-reported outcomes were evaluated to month (M)3. We calculated incidence rates (IRs) for safety outcomes through M24. Pooled data are reported for tofacitinib 5 and 10 mg BID.

RESULTS: Patients: low SDI, N = 1969; medium SDI, N = 1538; high SDI, N = 3071. There was a higher percentage of patients aged ≥ 50 years, ever smokers, and prior biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug users, and RA duration was longer, in the high vs low/medium SDI tertiles. Across SDI tertiles, efficacy at M3 was generally greater with tofacitinib or adalimumab vs placebo. Odds ratios vs placebo showed that American College of Rheumatology 20/70 responses at M3 for tofacitinib or adalimumab were numerically greatest (i.e., 95% confidence intervals [CIs] overlapped) in the high SDI tertile. Placebo-adjusted least squares mean change from baseline in Disease Activity Score in 28 joints with C-reactive protein/erythrocyte sedimentation rate and Clinical Disease Activity Index at M3 was greater in the high vs low/medium SDI tertile (95% CIs overlapped) with tofacitinib or adalimumab. For tofacitinib or adalimumab, IRs for adverse events/serious adverse events were numerically greatest in the high SDI tertile.

CONCLUSIONS: Efficacy at M3 was at least numerically greater with tofacitinib or adalimumab vs placebo, regardless of SDI. Placebo-adjusted efficacy responses were at least numerically greater in patients from high SDI countries. Safety IRs were also generally numerically greatest in the high SDI tertile with tofacitinib or adalimumab. Results were confounded by differences in demographics/baseline characteristics and associated lifestyle factors between SDI tertiles.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00147498, NCT00413660, NCT00960440, NCT00550446, NCT00603512, NCT00687193, NCT00847613, NCT00814307, NCT00856544, NCT00853385, NCT01164579, NCT01039688, NCT00976599, NCT01359150, and NCT02187055.

articles.title: Pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions: a population-based cohort study of presentation, management, and endocrine outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Population-based studies describing the full clinical spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions are scarce. Most available data derive from referral-based surgical or diagnosis-specific cohorts. We aimed to characterize presentation, lesion pathology, management, and long-term endocrine outcomes in a population-based cohort.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study of patients aged 18 years or younger diagnosed with sellar or parasellar lesions between 1976 and 2021 in a multicounty region. Clinical presentation, lesion characteristics, management, and endocrine outcomes were abstracted from medical records. Associations were evaluated by lesion type, lesion size (< 10 mm vs. ≥10 mm), and management approach.

RESULTS: Among 104 patients, endocrine abnormalities at diagnosis differed by lesion type (p = 0.0004) and were most frequent among patients with pituitary adenomas. Endocrine dysfunction at presentation was more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm than with lesions < 10 mm (74.2% vs. 49.2%; p = 0.0217). Post-treatment endocrine abnormalities were also more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm (64.5% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.0001). Associations with treatment modality were descriptive and subject to confounding by indication.

CONCLUSION: This population-based cohort captured a broad spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar disease, including uncommon lesions and conservatively managed cases. Endocrine morbidity was associated with lesion type and size, but clinically relevant abnormalities also occurred in smaller lesions, supporting endocrine evaluation based on clinical context and longitudinal surveillance.

articles.title: Investigation on Automatic Classification of Bone, Lymph Node, and Local Lesions in CT Images of Prostate Cancer Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning. Following a computed tomography (CT) or a positron emission tomography (PET)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning (ML) and deep learning models. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of   18  F-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96.0%. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97.9±1.2%, 95.2±1.3%, and 93.1±2.8% in the five-fold cross-validation experiments of the primary data and 96.3%, 94.0%, and 80.0% on the external test set, respectively. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Suspected Pituitary Microadenomas: The Complementary Role of Habitat-based Non-enhanced MRI Radiomics Features.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). Radiomics features were extracted from both the entire pituitary gland and its habitat subregions, generated via unsupervised K-means clustering. Eight predictive models were constructed using logistic regression: a clinical model, an intra-pituitary radiomics model, three individual habitat models (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), an early-fusion model combining all habitats, an ensemble model integrating the probability outputs of the three habitat models, and a combined model that integrated clinical, intra-pituitary, and the optimal fusion model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.Among all models, the combined model demonstrated the best predictive performance across all three cohorts, achieving areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.850-0.920) in the training set, 0.788 (95% CI: 0.690-0.885) in the internal validation set, and 0.796 (95% CI: 0.712-0.880) in the external test set. The combined model also achieved the highest accuracy and sensitivity across all datasets.The combined prediction model showed robust performance in distinguishing pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases, offering enhanced clinical decision support while reducing dependence on contrast-enhanced MRI examinations.

articles.title: The role of low muscle strength in predicting mortality in patients with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is a prevalent complication in chronic liver disease (CLD), traditionally assessed by muscle mass. Recent paradigm shifts focus to dynapenia as the primary determinant of adverse outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the role of dynapenia, as measured by handgrip strength (HGS) and ultrasound-derived diaphragmatic excursion, in predicting mortality in this population. This prospective study included consecutive outpatients with cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma history attending a tertiary hepatology unit. Muscle mass was assessed in subgroups using bioimpedance analysis (BIA) and computed tomography (CT). Associations between sarcopenia proxies and 24-month all-cause mortality were analyzed with adjusted Cox regression models, and survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves. Ninety-one patients were included (age 73.4 ± 8.1 years; 71 [78%] male); 20 (22%) had dynapenia. Twenty-two deaths occurred at two years (24.2%). Over 24 months, dynapenia (by HGS) and diaphragmatic excursion were associated with mortality in adjusted models (aHR 1.68, 95% CI 1.12-2.53, p = 0.012; aHR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97, p = 0.042). In subgroups, they remained the only muscle parameters associated with mortality, while muscle mass indices were not significant. Finally, Kaplan-Meier estimates showed lower 24-month survival in dynapenic patients across groups (in overall population 65% vs. 79%, p = 0.05). Low muscle strength is a key prognostic parameter in patients with cirrhosis and HCC. In our small cohort, it was the only muscle-related measure significantly associated with mortality. These findings support further evaluation of muscle strength assessment as a potential tool for risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Acute infection as a driver of chronic diseases and the unsung benefits of vaccination.
Risk of early stroke recurrence and procedural stroke or death in carotid near occlusion patients scheduled for carotid endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid near occlusion (NO) refers to distal internal carotid artery (ICA) narrowing caused by proximal carotid stenosis (CS). Stroke risk and optimal management of NO remain controversial. Our aim was to determine the prevalence of NO severities, rates of preoperative ischemic cerebrovascular events (iCVEs), 30-day procedural stroke and death, and hyperperfusion syndrome in patients with NO in a prospective CS cohort undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA).

METHODS: We reanalyzed posthoc CTAs from 443 symptomatic and asymptomatic CS patients. Subtle NO (s-NO) was defined as a 1.0-mm difference in distal luminal diameter between ipsilateral and contralateral ICA. NO with full collapse (fc-NO) was defined as ≤2.0 mm and/or an ipsilateral-to-contralateral ICA diameter ratio ≤0.42. Conventional stenosis was defined as CS >50% using NASCET criteria. Rates of preoperative iCVEs and 30-day procedural stroke and death were compared between s-NO, fc-NO, and conventional stenosis.

RESULTS: NO occurred in 143 (32%) patients: 124 (87%) s-NO and 19 (13%) fc-NO. NO was not significantly associated with increased preoperative iCVEs (7.6% vs 13%, OR 1.82, 95%Cl 0.96-3.47) or procedural stroke or death (5.6% vs 3.3%, OR 1.73, 95%Cl 0.67-4.50) compared with conventional stenosis. After CEA, hyperperfusion syndrome was frequent in NO patients (7.0% vs 2.7%, OR 2.8, 95% CI1.1-7.1). One patient developed fatal hyperperfusion-related intracranial hemorrhage.

CONCLUSION: CTA-detected NO is common, particularly in subtle forms, and important for stenosis assessment and management. Unlike earlier studies, NO was not associated with increased preoperative or procedural stroke or death, but hyperperfusion syndrome after CEA was more frequent.

articles.title: Higher ARNT expression is associated with the sparsely granulated phenotype in somatotroph pituitary adenomas: An immunohistochemical study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Somatotroph pituitary adenomas are a heterogeneous group comprising distinct histopathological subtypes, including the well-defined densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) phenotypes. While the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein (AIP) pathway has been implicated in pituitary tumorigenesis, the role of aryl hydrocarbon receptor nuclear translocator (ARNT) in somatotroph tumors remains poorly characterized.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 71 surgically treated somatotroph pituitary adenomas, clinically managed in a tertiary endocrinology center between 2020 and 2025. Immunohistochemical expression of AIP, AHR and ARNT was evaluated and correlated with clinicopathological characteristics, including cytokeratin pattern, hormonal expression and Ki-67 index.

RESULTS: Moderate/strong ARNT expression was more frequent in SG than in DG adenomas (60% vs. 17.6%, p = 0.002). Patients with moderate/strong ARNT expression were younger than those with absent/weak expression (median 39 vs. 46 years, p = 0.044). In multivariable analysis, ARNT expression remained associated with the SG phenotype after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR 6.84, 95% CI 2.05-22.84; p = 0.002). No significant associations were observed between ARNT expression and Ki-67 index, baseline GH or IGF1 levels, AIP/AHR immunoexpression or the evaluated clinical outcomes, including biochemical control during first-generation somatostatin receptor ligand therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Increased ARNT expression is associated with the sparsely granulated phenotype in somatotroph pituitary adenomas, suggesting that ARNT expression may reflect tumor differentiation rather than proliferative activity. However, the present findings do not demonstrate additional prognostic or therapeutic utility beyond granulation pattern. Further molecular and transcriptomic studies are warranted to clarify the biological role of ARNT.

articles.title: Dual-respiratory-phase low-dose quantitative CT for assessing COPD severity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the ability of quantitative parameters derived from low-dose dual-respiratory-phase CT to differentiate the severity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We enrolled 100 COPD patients between October 2023 and October 2024. Inspiratory CT scans were performed using a standard-dose protocol, and expiratory scans were performed using a low-dose protocol. Images were reconstructed with 60% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR). Dual-respiratory-phase image registration was performed on a dedicated "Digital Lung" platform to quantify the following parameters: end-expiratory lung volume (LVEX), end-inspiratory lung volume (LVIN), mean lung density at end-inspiration (MLDIN), mean lung density at end-expiration (MLDEX), and the mean density ratio (MLDEX/IN). The percentages of low-attenuation areas (LAA-910% and LAA-950%), emphysema (Emph%), and functional small airways disease (fSAD%) were also calculated. Correlations between CT parameters and pulmonary function were assessed. Significant variables were entered into univariate and multivariate logistic regression models, and a combined predictive model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with internal validation by bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Quantitative parameters, including LVEX, LVIN, LAA-950%, LAA-910%, Emph%, and fSAD%, were significantly correlated with pulmonary function indices (FEV1%pred and FEV1/FVC; all P < 0.01). Among these, LAA-910% and Emph% showed the strongest correlations with FEV1%pred (both r = -0.80). In univariate analysis, LAA-910% demonstrated the highest predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.887), followed by Emph% (AUC = 0.884). After adjustment for age and smoking status, multivariate logistic regression identified both Emph% (odds ratio [OR] = 1.298, 95% CI: 1.167-1.488, P < 0.001) and fSAD% (OR = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.040-1.205, P = 0.004) as independent predictors of severe COPD (GOLD 3-4 vs. GOLD 1-2). The combined model incorporating fSAD% and Emph% achieved an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.883-0.974), with a sensitivity of 80.49% and a specificity of 81.36%. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.908, confirming good model generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Low-dose expiratory CT combined with dual-respiratory-phase quantitative analysis provides reliable imaging biomarkers that correlate strongly with pulmonary function. The predictive model incorporating both fSAD% and Emph% demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance for assessing COPD severity and may serve as a noninvasive adjunct tool for disease stratification.

articles.title: From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies.
articles.journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.

articles.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

articles.title: ICU-acquired pneumonia beyond pathogen detection.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage of deep neck space abscesses: outcomes and predictors of treatment failure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical evidence supporting ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage (US-PCD) as a first-line treatment for deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs) remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of US-PCD as initial management for DNSAs and to identify factors associated with treatment efficacy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with DNSAs who underwent US-PCD as a first-line treatment at four tertiary hospitals in China between 2015 and 2022. All patients were hemodynamically stable and had a stable airway, with preprocedural contrast-enhanced CT/MRI confirming no extensive mediastinal involvement beyond the anterosuperior compartment. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify preprocedural predictors of US-PCD efficacy.

RESULTS: US-PCD was performed in 117 patients. The procedure was technically accessible in 116 (98%) patients, among whom 12 (10%) had descending mediastinitis confined to the anterosuperior mediastinum. No procedure-related major complications occurred. Drainage success was achieved in 98 patients (84%). Among the 18 patients (16%) in whom US-PCD failed, three (3%) died and the remaining 15 (13%) required open surgical drainage. Multiple septations and leukocyte count were significant in univariate but not multivariable analysis. The only independent predictor of drainage failure was the presence of serious associated events-a composite variable including descending mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and vascular thrombosis (OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 1.9-17.4, p = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage represents an effective minimally invasive first-line option for selected patients with deep neck space abscesses; however, open surgery should be prioritized when serious associated events are present.

KEY POINTS: Question For deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs), ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage (US-PCD) is a common surgical alternative, but its outcomes and predictors as a first-line treatment remain unclear. Findings US-PCD was effective as a first-line treatment for selected DNSAs. Only serious associated events-mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and thrombosis-independently predicted drainage failure. Clinical relevance US-PCD may be considered a first-line minimally invasive option for hemodynamically and airway-stable DNSA patients, even with anterosuperior mediastinal extension. Surgical drainage remains prioritized for cases with serious associated events to achieve rapid infection control.

articles.title: Morning blood pressure surge and morning hypertension in kidney transplant recipients.
articles.abstract: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) frequently exhibit abnormal ambulatory blood pressure (BP) patterns, particularly nocturnal hypertension and impaired dipping. However, morning hypertension and morning BP surge (MBPS) remain less well-characterized in this population. This analysis aims to evaluate the prevalence and phenotypes of morning hypertension and ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM)-derived morning surge indices according to nocturnal BP status and dipping pattern in KTRs. A total of 135 KTRs who underwent 24 h ABPM (ABPMpro device) were included. Morning BP was defined as mean BP during the first two hours after awakening. MBPS was assessed using pre-awakening, sleep-through and rising surge definitions. Morning hypertension was present in 53.3% of KTRs; among those with morning hypertension, 93.1% had sustained nocturnal and morning hypertension. Elevated SBP was equally frequent during morning and nighttime periods (43.7% each), but only half of them had elevated BP during daytime. Office BP underestimated morning BP burden, with masked morning hypertension identified in 18.5%. Participants with nocturnal hypertension had lower pre-awakening systolic MBPS than those without nocturnal hypertension (8.0 ± 12.1 vs. 15.2 ± 12.8 mmHg, p = 0.014), as well as lower sleep-through systolic MBPS (15.6 ± 13.0 vs. 22.2 ± 13.9 mmHg, p = 0.037), while rising MBPS did not differ significantly. Across dipping categories, MBPS indices were consistently higher in dippers and lower in reverse dippers (pre-awakening SBP surge: dippers 24.7 ± 13.1, non-dippers 10.7 ± 9.1, and reverse-dippers 1.1 ± 11.2 mmHg; p < 0.001). Morning hypertension is common in KTRs and is driven predominantly by sustained nocturnal and morning hypertension. Blunted MBPS likely reflects persistent nocturnal BP elevation and impaired dipping status.

articles.title: The β-cells in type 1 diabetes mellitus: findings from human pancreas studies.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by long-term and dynamic interactions between the immune system and pancreatic β-cells, ultimately leading to severe insulin deficiency. A paradigm shift in T1DM research has occurred in the past few years, with research now focusing on the human disease because of access to human pancreatic tissue and pancreas-draining lymph nodes. Advances in high-resolution imaging, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and histopathology based on artificial intelligence have profoundly reshaped our understanding of disease initiation and progression. These studies revealed that β-cell loss and/or dysfunction might begin earlier than previously appreciated, preferentially affecting small β-cell-rich islets and insulin-positive cell clusters, with larger islets showing transient resistance. Substantial β-cell mass often persists at diagnosis, accompanied by functional impairment rather than immediate cell death. Across disease stages, β-cells exhibit conserved molecular signatures dominated by interferon signalling, enhanced antigen presentation and adaptive immune-evasion programmes, with evidence of heterogeneity linked to age, disease duration and immune context. Parallel analyses of pancreatic lymph nodes show early immune dysregulation, including altered regulatory T cell signatures and expansion of stem-like cytotoxic T cell populations, even before overt hyperglycaemia. Together, these findings support an integrated model of T1DM progression that enables alignment of clinical staging with evolving β-cell and immune phenotypes.

articles.title: Platelet-derived microparticles induce CD8+ T cell senescence in chronic kidney disease via the transfer of microRNA-550a-5p.
articles.abstract: Infection is a leading cause of mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), in which T cell dysfunction is considered a typical feature. Although platelets are active participants in immune response, their role in regulating T cell function in patients with CKD remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that CD8+ T cell senescence may be a major contributor to the immunosuppressed state of patients with CKD, and that platelets derived from patients with CKD can induce premature CD8+ T cell senescence, potentially through mediating mitochondrial dysfunction. Further investigations reveal that platelet-derived microparticles (PMPs) from patients with CKD promote CD8+ T cell senescence via transferring miR-550a-5p, thereby decreasing PMPCB expression and inducing NDUFS8 cleavage failure. Finally, inhibition of miR-550a-5p and pretreatment with nicotinamide mononucleotide are capable of preventing platelet-induced CD8+ T cell senescence in CKD patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the ectopic transient expression of platelet-derived miR-550a-5p in CD8+ T cells promotes cellular senescence by regulating the PMPCB-NDUFS8 axis, which can be exploited to treat CKD-associated immunosenescence.

articles.title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression.
articles.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group (p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

articles.title: Developing national meta-accreditation standards for medical education accreditation bodies in Iran: a mixed-methods standards development and consensus study.
articles.abstract: Ensuring the quality and credibility of medical education systems increasingly depends on robust accreditation mechanisms, yet the performance of accreditation bodies themselves often remains insufficiently evaluated. Addressing this gap, this study developed and validated the first national meta-accreditation standards for Iran's Ministry of Health and Medical Education. Using a rigorous mixed-methods design, the study integrated insights from semi-structured interviews with 13 national experts, a comparative review of six international recognition systems, expert panel consensus, and a national survey of 90 stakeholders. From an initial pool of 184 standards, systematic refinement led to a final set of 51 standards. Stakeholder evaluation demonstrated strong consensus across practicality, necessity, and transparency (76-94%), with all standards exceeding the predefined 70% agreement threshold. The resulting framework is structured across three domains: structure and formality, accreditation processes, and accountability and quality improvement. By aligning national needs with international benchmarks, these standards enhance transparency, consistency, and trust in accreditation systems. The high level of expert agreement and methodological rigor underscore the framework's readiness for implementation and its potential as a model for strengthening meta-accreditation in similar centralized health education systems.

articles.title: Association between ambient temperature and thrombosis-related signaling lipids: Implications for early cardiovascular risk.
articles.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonoptimal temperatures significantly contribute to cardiovascular mortality, a burden expected to increase with climate change. Sensitive biomarkers for early cardiovascular risks remain scarce.

OBJECTIVE: We examined how thrombosis-related signaling lipids respond to ambient temperature, analyzing dose-response and lag patterns over a 30-day period, and assessed whether lipid changes mediate the association between temperature and thrombosis biomarkers using mediation analyses.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective panel study of 112 participants (aged 42-80) in Beijing (2016-2017), each completing an average of 3.4 visits. Targeted lipidomics quantified 12 thrombosis-related signaling lipids, including thromboxane (Tx) B2, three lyso-platelet-activating factors (LysoPAFs), seven lysophosphatidic acids (LPAs), and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P). Ambient temperature data were obtained from the China National Meteorological Information Centre. Associations between cumulative temperature exposures (up to 30 days) and lipids were analyzed using generalized additive mixed models. Mediation analyses assessed whether lipid changes mediated temperature effects on soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L), a sensitive biomarker for thrombotic disease.

RESULTS: Cold exposure was associated with significant decreases in TxB2, two LysoPAFs, and most LPAs (11-88% lower, median 45%, at a 30-day cumulative temperature of -0.8 °C vs. 18.7 °C). Heat exposure significantly increased all thrombosis-related lipids except LPA 20:3 (26% to 2,484% higher, median 65%, at a 30-day cumulative temperature of 27.7 °C vs. 18.7 °C), along with sCD40L (304% higher). Lipid effects were significant from 1-30 days of cumulative exposure, whereas heat-related sCD40L increases emerged after 6 days. LPA 18:0/18:1/20:4/22:6 and S1P mediated 12-32% of the heat-sCD40L association.

SIGNIFICANCE: Higher ambient temperatures are associated with increased thrombosis-related lipids, which may act as early indicators of cardiovascular risks from heat exposure.

IMPACT: This study quantified thrombosis-related signaling lipids across major lipid classes, i.e. eicosanoids (oxylipins), sphingolipids, and lysophospholipid, in a longitudinal panel study. Heat exposure significantly increased these signaling lipids, which responded to heat earlier than soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L), a sensitive thrombotic biomarker. Mediation analysis revealed that these lipids mediate up to 32% of the heat-related thrombotic response. These findings suggest that thrombosis-related signaling lipids may serve as early indicators of heat-related cardiovascular risk, with implications for biomarker-based screening and climate change adaptation strategies.

articles.title: Waiting times and determinants of delay for head and neck cancer in England-a population cohort study using real world data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Head and Neck Cancer (HNC), even short delays in treatment can worsen prognosis. We used real-world data to quantify waiting times and identify patient, tumour and health service factors associated with treatment delay in England.

METHODS: Using linked national datasets (Cancer Registry, Cancer Waiting Times, Hospital Episodes Statistics, Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy), we calculated waiting times from referral to first treatment (surgery or (chemo)radiation) and used multivariable logistic regression models to examine factors associated with delay.

RESULTS: Of 30,506 patients, 43% experienced treatment delay ( > 62 days from referral). Long delays ( > 90 days) affected 11% of patients treated with primary surgery and 20% of those receiving primary (chemo)radiation. Non-urgent referral (30% of patients) was the strongest predictor of long delay (aOR 4.07, CI: 3.54-4.68). Additional risk-factors included initial assessment at non-specialist (spoke) hospitals, non-oropharyngeal cancers, and higher socio-economic deprivation.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment delays in HNC are worsening, particularly for patients treated with primary (chemo)radiation. Referral route is the strongest determinant. Interventions should focus on optimising referral pathways, increasing awareness of HNC symptoms among the public and primary care, and acknowledging the different drivers of delay associated with surgery and (chemo)radiation therapy.

articles.title: LipReg4 deletion blocks hypertension induced by gut S. aureofaciens Tü117.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Streptomyces aureofaciens (S. aureofaciens) Tü117 and its metabolite α-lipomycin have been implicated in high-salt-induced hypertension. Previous studies showed that high-salt intake increases gut Tü117 abundance and circulating α-lipomycin levels. Mechanistically, α-lipomycin acts as a TRPV4 antagonist, impairing nitric oxide (NO)- and endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor (EDHF)- mediated endothelium-dependent vasodilation and thereby promoting vascular dysfunction and blood pressure (BP) elevation. However, whether hypertension is driven by Tü117 itself or specifically by α-lipomycin production remains unclear. Here, we generated a LipReg4 deletion mutant strain (ΔTü117) using Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 genome editing to selectively abolish α-lipomycin biosynthesis. Deletion of LipReg4 did not markedly affect bacterial growth but completely abolished α-lipomycin production. Compared with Tü117, ΔTü117 failed to increase circulating α-lipomycin levels or induce a sustained elevation in BP. These findings identify α-lipomycin as the key metabolite mediating Tü117-induced hypertension. They further support a direct role of gut microbial metabolites in host BP regulation.
