articles.title: Glutamate attenuates the ILC2 response and allergic airway inflammation via the kainate receptor GluK2.
articles.abstract: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) play a critical role in initiating the type 2 immune response, particularly in allergic airway diseases. Although the effects of glutamate on the immune system have been reported previously, its role in modulating the function of ILC2s and lung inflammation remains unclear.In this study, we report that the glutamate levels increased in lung tissue following exposure to allergens. Consequently, glutamate was found to restrain ILC2 responses during lung inflammation in mice. Using Rag1-/- mice, we demonstrated that the inhibitory effect of glutamate on type 2 inflammation was independent of T and B cells. Further ILC2 adoptive transfer experiments in Rag-/-Il2rg-/- mice confirmed that glutamate likely exerted its effects by directly targeting ILC2s. In vitro experiments revealed that glutamate suppressed ILC2 function through ionic kainate receptor signaling. Genetic deletion of the kainate receptor subunit GluK2 enhanced ILC2 responses and exacerbated type 2 lung inflammation. Mechanistically, transcriptome and metabolic analyses revealed that glutamate reduced oxidative metabolism in ILC2s, thereby limiting their activation. Consistently, in vivo administration of BPAM344-a positive allosteric modulator that potentiates GluK2 signaling-effectively suppressed allergen-induced type 2 inflammation. Notably, ILC2-specific GluK2 deletion markedly attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of BPAM344, indicating that its protective effects depend on ILC2-intrinsic GluK2 signaling.These findings demonstrate a novel role for glutamate in restraining ILC2 function, as it plays a protective role in alleviating airway inflammation. We propose that GluK2 activation may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for treating ILC2-driven allergic asthma.

articles.title: Body mass index is associated with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and quality of life in patients with type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is accompanied by obesity and elevated body mass index (BMI), which may be associated with poorer physical function and quality of life (QOL). However, associations of BMI with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL have not been comprehensively evaluated together in T2DM.

PURPOSE: To evaluate associations of BMI with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL in patients with T2DM.

METHODS: Patient characteristics were recorded. Body composition, muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL were assessed using validated measures. Bivariate Pearson correlations were supplemented by partial correlations controlling for age, sex, height, diabetes duration, glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and insulin use.

RESULTS: Fifty patients with T2DM were included (age: 52.90 ± 9.27 years; BMI: 33.76 ± 7.18 kg/m2). In unadjusted analyses, higher BMI was associated with greater adiposity, lower skeletal muscle mass percentage and handgrip strength, shorter 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance, lower Berg Balance Scale scores, and poorer QOL, but not with quadriceps strength, resting metabolic rate, Biodex balance parameters, or several QOL subdomains. After adjustment, BMI remained associated with body fat percentage (partial r = 0.854, p < .001), skeletal muscle mass percentage (partial r = -0.665, p < .001), 6MWT distance (partial r = -0.545, p < .001), and Nottingham Health Profile (NHP) pain (partial r = 0.426, p = .004), mobility (partial r = 0.440, p = .003), and total score (partial r = 0.351, p = .019). Associations with handgrip strength (p = .728) and Berg Balance test score were no longer significant (p = .069).

CONCLUSION: After adjustment for confounders, higher BMI remained associated with higher body fat percentage, lower skeletal muscle mass percentage, shorter 6MWT distance, and poorer QOL, whereas associations with handgrip strength and functional balance were attenuated. BMI-related functional findings should be interpreted cautiously in light of potential confounding.

articles.title: Platelet Dysfunction in Liver and Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Patients with liver or kidney disease exhibit complex hemostatic changes, including abnormalities in platelet count and function. Although patients frequently bleed, bleeding is often unrelated to and not predicted by platelet abnormalities. Likewise, routine platelet transfusion to correct platelet abnormalities does not appear to prevent bleeding. Patients also exhibit prohemostatic abnormalities such as increased von Willebrand factor levels and platelet activation, which may compensate for antihemostatic changes. Notably, thrombosis is a frequent complication in these patients. Here, we narratively review platelet abnormalities and their relation to clinical practice for bleeding and thrombosis in liver and kidney disease.

articles.title: Socioeconomic position and preoperative characteristics in Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants: a UK national observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients from more deprived backgrounds experience poorer postoperative outcomes. We analysed preoperative characteristics in UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants according to socioeconomic position to explore opportunities for targeted interventions.

METHODS: Participants were adults aged ≥18 yr undergoing major elective surgery at UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme sites. Socioeconomic position was determined using postcode data and the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) standardised aggregate scale of area-level deprivation. Associations between IMD position and patient characteristics, health behaviours, and comorbidities were analysed using descriptive statistics with appropriate parametric and nonparametric testing.

RESULTS: Of 55 938 participants included, quintile 1 (most deprived) represented the smallest subgroup (14.2%), with recruitment varying by region and site. Median age was 66 yr with IMD 1 participants 5 yr younger (62 yr) than IMD 5 (67 yr). Deprivation gradients (IMD 5 to 1) were seen for home ownership, occupation, and educational attainment. Prevalences of smoking, inactivity, and obesity increased from IMD 5 to 1. Higher prevalences of major long-term conditions including diabetes mellitus, heart failure, stroke, and ASA physical status 3-4 were observed in more deprived quintiles. Prevalence rates of dementia and renal impairment were similar across quintiles despite the age gradient. Notably, the proportions of patients living with frailty and disability increased with deprivation.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients presenting for major surgery from more deprived backgrounds do so in poorer overall health. They can encounter barriers to both research participation and available preoperative support. Addressing this unmet need to prevent widening perioperative health inequalities requires interventions tailored to the patient's socioeconomic context.

articles.title: ERα-dependent BCAA-nitrogen flux in sex-biased MASLD.
articles.journal: Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM
articles.abstract: Sex-biased metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease susceptibility is usually attributed to differences in adiposity, insulin resistance, and sex-hormone levels. I propose that hepatic estrogen receptor α shapes the partitioning of muscle-derived branched-chain amino acid carbon and amino nitrogen between oxidation, lipid synthesis, recycling, and disposal. This framework supports endocrine-state-aware biomarkers and sex-stratified trials integrating liver and muscle endpoints.

articles.title: Distinct gastrointestinal symptom phenotypes in adults with cystic fibrosis are linked to complications and medication use: the GRAMPUS-CF study.
articles.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal symptoms remain common in adults with cystic fibrosis (CF) despite cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator use, suggesting persistent and heterogeneous gut dysfunction. This prospective observational study tests the hypothesis that distinct gut symptom phenotypes in CF can be observed and linked to underlying mechanisms.

METHODS: Adults from three UK CF centres completed the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale, Patient Assessment of Constipation Symptoms and a bowel-habit questionnaire. Latent class analysis using an ordinal logistic model was applied to 36 symptom indicators. Associations between phenotypes and demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were examined using generalised linear models.

RESULTS: Three hundred participants completed questionnaires (54% male; median 31 years). We identified four symptom phenotypes: mild; moderate-constipation predominant; moderate-diarrhoea predominant and severe. The severe phenotype was associated with gastroesophageal reflux (RRR 2.86; 95%CI: 1.30-6.31; p = 0.009), distal intestinal obstruction syndrome (RRR 2.46; 95%CI: 1.04-5.81; p = 0.04), proton pump inhibitor (RRR 3.29; 95%CI 1.39-7.74; p = 0.007), and laxative use (RRR 6.13; 95%CI 2.54-14.84; p < 0.001). CF-related liver disease was associated with both moderate-constipation and diarrhoea phenotypes, respectively (RRR 2.08; 95%CI 1.13-3.81; p = 0.018; RRR 2.11; 95%CI 1.03-4.29; p = 0.04). There was a lower likelihood of long-term oral antibiotic use in the moderate-constipation phenotype (RRR 0.53; 95%CI 0.3-0.92; p = 0.025) and moderate-diarrhoea phenotype (RRR 0.46; 95%CI 0.24-0.91; p = 0.025).

CONCLUSIONS: Four distinct symptom phenotypes were identified, independent of demographics and pancreatic status, but associated with specific complications and medication profiles. These phenotypes provide a framework for mechanistic studies within the GRAMPUS-CF cohort and precision management of CF-related gut disease.

articles.title: Systemic outcomes following maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder associated with an elevated risk of systemic comorbidities. Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) surgery can reduce upper airway obstruction and improve sleep parameters, but its systemic health benefits remain less well characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis was performed to synthesize evidence on the systemic health outcomes associated with MMA in patients with OSA. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through May 20, 2026. Inclusion criteria encompassed original research studies (case series, cohort studies, trials) reporting systemic health outcomes after MMA for OSA. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using an NIH quality assessment tool. Seven studies (271 patients), with mean follow-up ranging from 5.2 months to 6.6 years, met the inclusion criteria . All studies reported significant reductions in apnea-hypopnea index postoperatively. Four studies included in a meta-analysis demonstrated statistically significant reductions in blood pressure: systolic, mean difference -8.6 mmHg (95% confidence interval -14.2 to -3.0); diastolic, mean difference -5.3 mmHg (95% confidence interval -8.5 to -2.0). MMA for OSA not only improves airway patency and sleep metrics, but is also associated with enduring systemic health benefits, including a blood pressure reduction. Limited evidence also suggests potential improvements in neurocognitive outcomes. Although the evidence suggests a positive impact, further high-quality randomized controlled trials employing rigorous outcome measures (e.g., ambulatory blood pressure monitoring) are needed to fully delineate the persistent systemic effects of maxillomandibular advancement.

articles.title: Study selection and translational NNTs in severe asthma and COPD: methodological considerations.
Project international Delphi consensus recommendations for perioperative management of inguinal lymphadenectomy in cancer patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish international expert consensus on perioperative strategies for the prevention, management, and follow-up of complications related to inguinal lymph node dissection.

METHODS: This international modified Delphi consensus study was conducted between September 2025 and March 2026 using a 2-round electronic survey. A total of 101 experts from 25 countries participated, including urologists, surgical oncologists, plastic surgeons, and other specialists with experience in ILND for penile cancer, melanoma, and vulvar cancer. Eighty-six clinical statements addressing ILND-associated complications were evaluated across 6 domains: preoperative nutritional optimization, anemia management, lymphatic complications, infectious and cutaneous complications, vascular and musculoskeletal complications, and functional rehabilitation. Agreement was assessed using a 5-point Likert scale, with consensus defined a priori as at least 70% of participants selecting "somewhat agree" or "strongly agree."

RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for 51 of 86 statements. Agreed recommendations supported standardized approaches to preoperative nutritional assessment and anemia correction, prevention and management of lymphatic complications, drain placement and management, discharge criteria, antibiotic prophylaxis, wound complication management, thromboprophylaxis, multimodal analgesia, and early functional rehabilitation. No consensus was reached regarding routine use of immunonutrition, optimal duration of antibiotic therapy, topical treatments, muscle relaxants, or hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: This international Delphi process generated consensus-based, multidisciplinary recommendations to guide perioperative ILND management. These statements may provide a structured framework to support greater standardization of perioperative care pathways across malignancies requiring ILND, reduce morbidity, and inform quality-improvement initiatives. Prospective validation is required to evaluate their clinical impact and refine areas of ongoing uncertainty.

articles.title: Angry Purkinje Syndrome: A Review of Short-Coupled Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia with Quinidine Treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) mediated by short-coupled premature ventricular complexes in patients with recent myocardial infarction is termed 'Angry Purkinje Syndrome'. These arrhythmias are typically refractory to conventional antiarrhythmic therapy but may respond to quinidine.

METHODS & RESULTS: We present a case series of patients with short-coupled polymorphic VT occurring 2-8 days after acute myocardial infarction and coronary revascularisation. All three patients had recurrent polymorphic VT episodes that were consistently initiated by ventricular ectopy with a short coupling interval of 360 milliseconds. All three patients experienced arrhythmic storms requiring multiple cardioversions and were refractory to amiodarone, procainamide, lignocaine, and isoprenaline. Quinidine led to sustained suppression of ventricular arrhythmias, with marked reduction in premature ventricular contraction burden within 24 hours. Two patients were successfully extubated 4 days after arrest, and the third was decannulated from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation 4 days after quinidine initiation.

CONCLUSIONS: 'Angry Purkinje Syndrome' is an uncommon but important cause of polymorphic VT in patients with coronary disease not related to acute myocardial ischaemia. Quinidine appears to provide effective suppression of Purkinje-mediated polymorphic VT and may represent an important therapeutic option in this setting.

Factors associated with high-flow therapy failure in COVID-19-related acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: A prospective single-centre cohort study.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The optimal selection of non-invasive respiratory support for patients with COVID-19-related acute hypoxemic respiratory failure remains uncertain. High-flow therapy (HFT) is frequently used as initial support, but early identification of patients at risk of escalation is clinically relevant. We evaluated clinical and laboratory variables associated with escalation from HFT to non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation (NPPV).

METHODS: We conducted a prospective single-centre cohort study including 139 consecutive patients initiated on HFT in a respiratory intermediate care unit. The primary outcome was HFT failure, defined as escalation from HFT to NPPV. Time to HFT failure was analysed from HFT initiation using cause-specific Cox regression; successful HFT withdrawal without escalation was treated as censoring. A parsimonious adjusted model included age, time from symptom onset to HFT initiation, baseline PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Logistic regression and a supplementary bicarbonate model were used as sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Seventy-two of 139 patients (51.8%) required escalation to NPPV. Seventeen escalations were recorded on day 0 and 44 of 72 failures (61.1%) occurred by day 1. In the adjusted Cox model, higher LDH levels were associated with an increased hazard of escalation (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] per 100U/L, 1.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.66; p=0.014), whereas higher baseline PaO2/FiO2 ratios were associated with a lower hazard (aHR per 25mmHg, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90; p=0.001). A longer interval from symptom onset to HFT initiation was also associated with a lower hazard of escalation (aHR per day, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.86-0.99; p=0.033). In a supplementary sensitivity model, higher arterial bicarbonate levels were associated with a lower hazard of escalation (aHR per 3mmol/L, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.66-0.99; p=0.039).

CONCLUSION: In this prospective single-centre cohort, LDH and baseline PaO2/FiO2 were associated with escalation from HFT to NPPV after adjustment. Arterial bicarbonate showed a supportive exploratory signal in sensitivity analysis. These findings require external validation before incorporation into treatment-selection algorithms.

articles.title: Characterization of herpes zoster cases and epidemiological trends in the Community of Madrid before and after the vaccine introduction in older adults: 2016-2025.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Community of Madrid (CM) introduced chickenpox vaccination during childhood in 2006 and herpes zoster (HZ) vaccination for those over 65 years-old (y/o) in 2022, with progressive incorporation of age groups. This study aims to describe HZ cases and epidemiological trends between 2016 and 2025.

METHODS: Observational population-based study using primary care morbidity records and hospital Minimum Basic Data Set. Sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities of the cases were described. Annual cumulative incidence (Cuml) was estimated for episodes and hospitalizations by age-group and sex. The years were grouped into three periods: 2016-19 (reference), 2020-22 (pandemic, pre-HZ vaccination) and 2023-25 (post-HZ vaccination). Risk ratios (RR) between 2020-22/2023-25 and 2016-19 were calculated by age group and sex through Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: Annual Cuml remained stable (500 cases and 13 hospital admissions per 100,000 inhabitants), being higher among women. HZ cases had a high prevalence of hypertension (26.5%), diabetes (9.0%) and cardiovascular disease (6.6%). Incidence decreased between 2016-19/2023-25, especially in men, in age-groups under 15 y/o (RR=0.40; 95% CI: 0.33-0.48), 15-29 y/o (RR=0.74; 95% CI: 0.70-0.78), and 65-80 y/o (RR=0.81; 95% CI: 0.78-0.84), but it increased between 30 and 49 y/o, especially among women (RR=1.17; 95% CI: 1.15-1.20). Concerning hospital admissions, incidence decreased, especially in men, among 50-64 y/o (RR=0.82; 95% CI: 0.63-0.99), 65-80 y/o (RR=0.69; 95% CI: 0.57-0.81) and +80 y/o (RR=0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.93). The incidence decline was more evident in age groups eligible for vaccination since 2023.

CONCLUSIONS: Recent variations in HZ incidence within age groups are observed. Strengthening epidemiological surveillance and evaluating vaccination impact remain essential.

articles.title: Disseminated histoplasmosis with gastrointestinal involvement in a patient with HIV: Case report and systematic review of the literature.
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract: Disseminated histoplasmosis is a life-threatening opportunistic infection in patients with advanced HIV. We report the case of a 43-year-old man with untreated HIV who presented with disseminated histoplasmosis and gastrointestinal involvement, including recurrent intestinal obstruction. Follow-up revealed colonic auto-amputation, a previously unreported complication. A systematic review of the literature was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Most reported cases occurred in Southeast Asia and Latin America. Colonic and duodenal involvement were the most frequent gastrointestinal manifestations. CD4 counts below 200cells/mm3 were consistently associated with worse outcomes. This case highlights an exceptional complication of intestinal histoplasmosis and underscores the need for early recognition and treatment in immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Post-registration medical imaging education as a pathway to addressing the specialist deficit in Rwanda: A needs assessment.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sub-Saharan Africa faces a critical shortage of specialist medical imaging practitioners, yet undergraduate training remains insufficient for advanced practice. Rwanda's "4 × 4 Reform" prioritises expanding the radiology workforce, but evidence-based curriculum development for postgraduate education remains lacking. This study aimed to conduct a multi-stakeholder needs assessment to inform the design, structure, and delivery of a proposed Master of Science in Medical Imaging at the University of Rwanda, College of Medicine and Health Sciences.

METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted nationally, recruiting 210 participants from multiple stakeholder groups, including clinical practitioners, educators, policymakers, and patient representatives. Data were analysed with descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact tests in R.

RESULTS: Advanced image interpretation skills were identified as hugely lacking by 72.9% of respondents. Diagnostic ultrasound (68.8%), pattern recognition (65.2%), computed tomography (61.7%), and magnetic resonance imaging (60.7%) were the top priorities. Notably, 79.0% (n = 166) of stakeholders expected graduates to develop leadership and management skills, followed by teaching and curriculum development (73.8%). Fisher's exact tests comparing clinical practitioners (n = 142) with other stakeholders (n = 68) found no significant differences across all seven skills assessed (ultrasound: p = 0.2; pattern recognition: p = 0.2; CT: p = 0.4; MRI: p = 0.5; radiography: p > 0.9; nuclear medicine: p = 0.9; radiation therapy: p = 0.6).

CONCLUSIONS: This empirical assessment in Rwanda reveals an urgent need for specialist training that integrates advanced clinical competencies with leadership and education skills.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: This study offers a guide for integrating advanced clinical skills with leadership and educational competencies into postgraduate curricula, directly addressing critical workforce shortages in low-resource settings.

articles.title: A robust biomarker combining radiomic and CA19.9 information to predict distant relapse-free survival after radiochemotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The radiomic feature Statistical Percentile 10% (p10%), extracted from [¹⁸F]FDG-PET images, has been previously identified and validated as a robust predictor of distant progression-free survival (DPFS) in unresectable pancreatic cancer (LAPC). This study aimed to maximize its prognostic potential by combining p10% with CA19.9 serum levels and assessing its generalizability across distinct clinical settings.

METHODS: We analyzed 287 LAPC patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and a validation cohort of 72 patients enrolled in the CASSANDRA trial (resectable/borderline-resectable PDAC). Cox models combined p10% with CA19.9 levels measured before RT in LAPC patients, and before surgery for CASSANDRA patients.

RESULTS: p10% was independently prognostic in both cohorts and its integration with CA19.9 significantly improved the prediction. In the LAPC cohort, the combined model achieved C-index=0.71, with median DPFS of 4.0-vs-15.0 months (p<0.0001;HR=3.22). In the pre-surgery setting (CASSANDRA trial), the model showed good rank-order discrimination (C-index=0.65), with median survival of 11.6 months vs not-reached (p=0.0018). However, the calibration slope of 0.54 suggests that absolute risk prediction requires recalibration in the surgical cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating p10% with CA19.9 provides a broader representation of tumor aggressiveness. The combined biomarkers demonstrate consistent performance across different disease stages supporting their use for treatment personalization.

articles.title: Short and Long-Term Results of Kidney Transplantation From Extended Criteria Donors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is around 9%, and with the aging of the population, it is increasing. The growing gap between the number of patients on waiting lists and the number of donors made it necessary to transplant organs from extended criteria donors (ECD).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Results of 211 kidney transplantations between 2013 and 2018 were analyzed retrospectively. Short- and long-term results were investigated, such as delayed graft function (DGF), post-transplantation e-GFR levels, rejection, graft and patient survival. The initial vasculopathy in "0" biopsy samples and the effect of the level of vasculopathy on the survival of the graft were also analyzed. The statistical analysis was made by SPSS 2.0 program. The level of significance was P < .05.

RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2018, 30 transplantations (16.57%) were carried out from ECD and 181 (83.43%) from standard donors (SD). A significant difference was found in DGF (ECD n = 10 vs SD n = 27, P = .016), and in the e-GFR levels at the control in the 1, 3, and 6. Furthermore, there was no significant difference in the incidence of rejection (ECD group n = 6, SD group n = 38, P = .572) or in the 10-year death-censored graft survival (ECD 93% vs SD 85%, P = .267). According to the vasculopathy in "0" biopsy sample results, atherosclerosis was significantly higher in the ECD group (P = .02), but it did not affect graft survival significantly.

CONCLUSION: Transplantation from ECDs can be used safely, and it increases transplantation activity in clinical practice without serious long-term harmful effects.

articles.title: Effects of structured music therapy on anxiety and mood in pediatric oncology patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children receiving cancer treatment frequently experience anxiety, mood disturbances, and symptom burden during hospitalization. This study examined structured music therapy in relation to anxiety, mood, and symptom burden among hospitalized pediatric oncology patients aged 6-12 years.

DESIGN AND METHODS: This quasi-experimental, non-randomized, single-group sequential control-phase/intervention-phase repeated-measures pretest-posttest study was conducted in a pediatric hematology-oncology unit in Türkiye between December 2024 and November 2025. Thirty children were first observed during a routine-care control phase and then participated in a structured music therapy phase. The intervention included four individual sessions delivered twice weekly over two weeks. Outcomes were assessed at matched twice-weekly measurement points across both phases using the State Anxiety Scale for Children, Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire-Child Form, Short Mood and Feelings Questionnaire-Parent Form, and Symptom Screening in Pediatrics Tool. Repeated-measures ANOVA examined condition, time, and condition × time effects. Effect sizes were reported using partial eta squared (ηp2). The study was not prospectively registered.

RESULTS: Anxiety showed significant condition, time, and condition × time effects (ηp2 = 0.607, 0.136, and 0.226, respectively), suggesting a favorable anxiety-related pattern during the structured music therapy phase. Child-reported mood showed significant condition and time effects, whereas parent-reported mood and symptom burden showed significant condition effects only. Non-significant interaction effects were interpreted cautiously. These findings indicate associations and favorable trends rather than definitive causal effects and require confirmation in larger randomized multicenter studies with follow-up.

PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Structured music therapy may be a feasible supportive intervention associated with favorable anxiety-related outcomes and may support holistic, child-centered pediatric oncology nursing care when implemented through interdisciplinary collaboration and standardized protocols.

articles.title: Extracardiovascular immune-related adverse events in patients with suspected cardiac toxicity associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but may cause immune-related adverse events (iRAEs). Cardiovascular iRAEs, especially myocarditis, carry high morbidity and mortality. Extracardiovascular iRAEs are included as diagnostic criteria for myocarditis, yet their prevalence, spectrum, and clinical impact in patients with suspected cardiovascular iRAEs are poorly defined.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-center observational study between March 2022 and December 2023. Consecutive patients referred to cardio-oncology for suspected ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity underwent systematic cardiovascular evaluation, internal medicine assessment, pharmacovigilance review, and multidisciplinary adjudication. Data included cardiovascular and extracardiovascular iRAEs, treatment decisions, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 208 patients enrolled (median age 60 years; 78% female), 206 completed follow-up. Cardiovascular iRAEs were confirmed in 108 patients, predominantly myocarditis (75%). Extracardiovascular iRAEs occurred in 32% of patients (n = 67; 97 events), most frequently endocrine (57.6%, mainly thyroid), followed by muscular and cutaneous events (each 9.3%). Most extracardiovascular iRAEs were CTCAE grade 2, while severe muscular or neurological toxicities, including myositis and myasthenia gravis, occurred in 1.4%. Myocarditis was more frequent in patients with extracardiovascular iRAEs (57% vs. 34%). In 18 cases, extracardiovascular iRAEs fulfilled IC-OS minor criteria, enabling a definite myocarditis diagnosis. ICIs were discontinued in 56% of patients, with extracardiovascular iRAEs contributing in 15%, and accounted for nearly one-third of indications for immunosuppressive therapy. Mortality was mainly cancer-related.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients referred for suspected ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity, extracardiovascular iRAEs are frequent and clinically relevant. They contribute to myocarditis diagnosis and management, supporting systematic multidisciplinary cardiology-internal medicine evaluation.

articles.title: Does performing preprocedural point-of-care ultrasound improve success rate for lumbar punctures in paediatric patients?
Time to protect adolescents against meningococcal B disease.
Giving proton-pump inhibitors after variceal ligation: is it time to change practice?
Psychometric validation of the Bengali Lupus-QoL and its correlation with disease activity, damage and low disease activity state: a two-centre cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SLE is a complex autoimmune condition requiring evaluation across disease activity, permanent damage and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). This study aimed to validate the Bengali version of the 34-item Lupus Quality of Life (Lupus-QoL) and perform a correlation analysis with global disease activity (SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K), SLE Disease Activity Score (SLE-DAS)), organ-specific involvement (British Isles Lupus Assessment Group (BILAG)), permanent damage (Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics/American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Damage Index (SDI)) and clinical targets like the Low Lupus Disease Activity State (LLDAS).

METHOD: A multicentre cohort study was conducted with 240 Bengali patients with SLE. Clinical status was concurrently assessed using physician-reported indices (SLEDAI-2K, SLE-DAS, BILAG, SDI) alongside the Bengali Lupus-QoL. Internal consistency was determined by Cronbach’s alpha while associations were evaluated using Spearman’s correlation and discriminant validity via independent t-tests.

RESULT: The tool demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha 0.86–0.97). SLEDAI-2K showed a strong negative correlation with all quality-of-life domains (p<0.01). While SLE-DAS correlated with physical and functional domains, it failed to capture fatigue, body image or intimacy. Musculoskeletal and cardiorespiratory involvements were the primary drivers of reduced HRQoL. Achieving LLDAS significantly improved physical health and planning (p=0.03) but not psychosocial domains. Permanent damage (SDI ≥1) significantly restricted physical capabilities and functional planning (p<0.01).

CONCLUSION: The Bengali Lupus-QoL is a highly reliable instrument that bridges the gap between medical data and patient experience. Standard clinical metrics like SLE-DAS and LLDAS are insufficient to capture the full psychosocial burden, highlighting the necessity of this tool for the comprehensive management of Bengali patients with SLE.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes and impact of diagnostic coding of patients with heart failure identified in primary care: insights from the OSCAR-HF cohort.
Implementation gaps in contemporary heart failure therapy: a two-country nationwide analysis.
Intermittent theta burst stimulation on the cerebellar Hemisphere to imprOve Post-stroke cognitivE impairment (HOPE): a multicentre randomised controlled double-blind trial.
Association of epicardial adipose tissue with myocardial stiffness and postoperative outcomes in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergoing transapical beating-heart septal myectomy.
Pre-Operative Ankle Brachial Index in Assessing Major Amputation Level and Outcomes in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe ankle brachial index (ABI) is a non-invasive tool used to assess vessel stenosis hindering limb perfusion. It is commonly used in diagnosis of peripheral artery disease (PAD). We propose that this diagnostic tool may have predictive applications in amputation level of patients with PAD and may contribute to the diagnostic evaluation of CLTI.Materials and MethodsThis study is a retrospective chart review of 97 patients with PAD admitted from 2014 to 2022 who underwent major lower extremity amputation (MLEA) at a major tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified into two groups by ABI severity (ABI ≤0.4: severe PAD, 0.4<ABI <0.9: less severe PAD). Statistical tests included Chi-square, T-test, multivariable logistic regression with collinearity statistics, and a receiver operator curve (ROC) to determine Youden's J.ResultsNinety-seven patients were included in this study, 53.6% (n = 52) of whom had less severe PAD and 46.4% (n = 45) of whom had severe PAD. Per multivariable logistic regression, more severe PAD based on ABI ≤0.4 was predictive of receiving an AKA (P = 0.013; OR = 2.833) as a primary MLEA surgery. Receiver operator curve (ROC) shows that at an ABI threshold of 0.42, the model achieves a sensitivity of 0.58 and a specificity of 0.65, yielding a Youden's J of 0.23. There was no difference in readmission, ipsilateral revision, or 5-year mortality between cohorts.DiscussionBased on our cohort of 97 patients, pre-operative ABI measurements contributed modestly to amputation level assessment within the broader clinical framework; however, ABI was not independently predictive of post-operative outcomes.

articles.title: Microbiome Targeted Therapies for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is a rare, progressive cholestatic liver disease of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with poor prognosis. The only life-extending treatment for PSC is liver transplantation, with up to 25% of post-transplant patients developing recurrent disease, highlighting an extrahepatic influence on disease. The gut-liver axis has been widely studied in the development and pathogenesis of PSC, with preclinical and clinical work demonstrating that targeting gut microbiota and its metabolites can elicit therapeutic effects against PSC. This review describes various microbiome-based therapeutics and their effectiveness in treating PSC, including antibiotics, probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and bacteriophages. In conclusion, the use of microbiota-derived metabolites as potential therapeutics is also addressed.

articles.title: SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy: A propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications.

RESULTS: After matching, 2,016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

articles.title: Below-knee dermatologic surgery: Prevention of surgical complications, wound healing, and reconstructive techniques-A narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Below-knee dermatologic surgery is associated with an increased risk of surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and postoperative pain. Optimizing perioperative care and reconstructive strategies is particularly important in older patients undergoing skin cancer surgery.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted in April 2025 using PubMed and Google Scholar. Clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses addressing complications, perioperative interventions, wound healing, and reconstruction following lower-leg dermatologic surgery were evaluated.

RESULTS: Preoperative cleansing with 4% chlorhexidine, perioperative compression, monofilament sutures, and zinc oxide dressings may help reduce postoperative complications. Routine perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended. Neoadjuvant intralesional methotrexate or 5-fluorouracil may reduce tumor size, simplify surgical reconstruction, or avoid surgery in selected patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Direct closure is the preferred reconstructive approach when feasible. Alternatives include secondary intention healing, pinch grafts, split-thickness and full-thickness skin grafts, and local flaps, particularly the keystone flap. Based on the available evidence and clinical experience, a practical management algorithm is proposed.

CONCLUSIONS: Below-knee dermatologic surgery requires individualized perioperative management and careful selection of reconstructive techniques. Antiseptic cleansing, compression therapy, appropriate suture selection, and selected reconstructive approaches may improve outcomes. However, much of the available evidence is derived from retrospective studies, highlighting the need for prospective investigations.

articles.title: Anticoagulation strategies during peripheral ultrafiltration in diuretic-resistant congestive heart failure.
articles.abstract: Introduction and objectives Peripheral ultrafiltration (UF) is an effective strategy for the management of diuretic-resistant congestion in patients with decompensated heart failure. However, extracorporeal circuit clotting remains one of the main technical limitations of the procedure, and the optimal anticoagulation strategy during UF has not been clearly established. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different anticoagulation strategies during UF. Methods This prospective, nonrandomized, single-center study included 87 consecutive patients who underwent UF between January 2021 and November 2025. The anticoagulation strategy was tailored according to the patients' baseline anticoagulant therapy: unfractionated heparin (UFH), n = 8; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), n = 41; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), n = 12; and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), n = 26. Procedural efficacy was defined as successful completion of the UF session without premature interruption due to extracorporeal circuit dysfunction or clinical complications. Results Baseline characteristics and UF technical parameters were comparable among groups (P > .1). Procedural efficacy was highest with intravenous heparin (UFH = 100%, LMWH = 48.7%, VKAs = 66.6%, and DOACs = 65.4%; P = .048). Extracorporeal circuit clotting was more frequent with subcutaneous heparin (UFH = 0%, LMWH = 31.7%, VKAs = 25%, and DOACs = 27%; P = .018). Conclusions UFH was associated with a lower rate of extracorporeal circuit clotting and a higher rate of successful UF completion. Complications were infrequent. Given the observational design and the small sample size, these findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

articles.title: Early Nocturnal Care Disruption and the Hazard of Incident ICU Delirium in Critically Ill Adults: A Target-Trial Emulation in MIMIC-IV.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nighttime care contacts fragment sleep and are often invoked as a contributor to intensive care delirium. Whether a higher intensity of those contacts early in the stay is associated with later incident delirium is unclear. Sicker, more sedated patients are monitored more often overnight and are also more likely to become delirious.

METHODS: We emulated a target trial in MIMIC-IV version 3.1. Adults were eligible if the first intensive care stay lasted at least 48 hours and the delirium screen was negative at that landmark. High exposure was a nocturnal contact rate above the cohort median, built from vital-sign charting, laboratory draws, and bedside medication administrations between 22:00 and 05:59 and divided by 16 nocturnal hours. Follow-up for incident delirium began at the landmark. We estimated the hazard ratio with stabilized inverse-probability weights and a pooled-logistic survival model.

RESULTS: Of 12,922 eligible stays, 2,862 developed incident delirium. High nocturnal care-contact intensity was associated with a higher hazard (adjusted hazard ratio 1.43, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 1.60). The hazard rose across tertiles of the contact rate and was higher for vital-sign charting and phlebotomy than for medication administration.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher intensity of early nocturnal care contacts was associated with a moderately higher hazard of incident delirium. Residual confounding remains possible, including reverse causation if prodromal delirium itself increases overnight contacts before the first positive screen.

articles.title: Incretin Therapy Before Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Cardiorenal Protection or Physiological Preconditioning?
Septal dysfunction and Abnormal Systolic Stretch Are Associated with Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a major determinant of outcomes after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rToF). Although right bundle branch block is present in most patients and electro-mechanical dyssynchrony (EMD) has been associated with RV dysfunction, only a subset of patients ultimately develops RV dysfunction. We hypothesized that septal dysfunction is a key feature associated with the development of EMD-induced RV dysfunction in rToF.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 126 pediatric rToF patients (median age 14.7 years) with contemporaneous ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) between 2019-2025. Septal mechanics were quantified by strain-derived systolic rebound stretch (SRS) and further combined with RV free-wall mechanics into a systolic stretch index (SSI). RV mechanical dyssynchrony was visually classified, with septal contraction abrogation and systolic stretch as key features. Multivariable models evaluated associations between systolic stretch parameters and RV dysfunction (CMR-derived RV ejection fraction (EF) ≤ 46%), adjusting for relevant covariates.

RESULTS: RV dysfunction was present in 24.6% of patients. Patients with >moderate RV outflow tract obstruction (peak gradient >40 mmHg) were excluded, median pulmonary regurgitant fraction was 35% (IQR, 26-44%). Median SSI was higher in patients with RV dysfunction than in those without (8.9% (IQR 3.2-11.3) vs 2.9% (IQR 1.5-5.5), p<0.001). Premature termination of septal deformation with subsequent stretching, quantified by SRS, was associated with RV dysfunction (p<0.001). Worse septal stretch patterns were associated with RV dysfunction, larger RV end-systolic indexed volume, and longer QRSd (p<0.001). Higher SSI was independently associated with lower RVEF (p<0.001) after adjustment for age, QRSd, RV dilation, and surgical substrate (p<0.001), whereas QRSd lost significance on RVEF after adjusting for SSI. RVEF was lower at SSI values >4%. SSI demonstrated excellent intraobserver and interobserver reproducibility (ICC 0.996 and 0.997, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric rToF, RV dysfunction was associated with abnormal septal contraction and systolic stretch. RV-SSI, integrating inefficient RV mechanics via septal and RV free-wall systolic stretch, was independently associated with RV dysfunction beyond QRSd, RV volumes and pulmonary regurgitation severity. These findings may help characterize RV electromechanical phenotypes and provide a rationale for future studies evaluating RV resynchronization therapy.

articles.title: "Left atrial dimension and new-onset atrial fibrillation in chronic Chagas disease: a competing-risk analysis of the SEARCH-Rio cohort" - Benchimol-Barbosa PR, Benchimol-Barbosa ACL, Kantharia BK. Int J Cardiol. 2026 Sep 15;464:134788. doi:10.1016/j.ijcard.2026.134788. Epub ahead of print. PMID: 42744019: Response to Letter to the Editor "Beyond Left Atrial Diameter in Chagas Disease: Interatrial Block and Competing-Risk Modelling for Atrial Fibrillation Risk" by Ullah T and Shah MT.
Water type modulates particle state and toxicity of polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastic toxicity is typically assessed using pristine particles under simplified laboratory conditions, despite growing evidence that environmental transformations can substantially alter particle behaviour and biological effects. Here, we investigated how water type influences the particle state and toxicity of polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) in the freshwater zooplankton Daphnia magna. In a chronic life-history assay, exposure to 0.5 mg L-1 PET-NPs caused no detectable effects on survival, growth or reproduction, whereas exposure to 10 mg L-1 resulted in complete mortality. We then incubated PET-NPs for four days in reverse osmosis water, ASTM artificial freshwater or natural freshwater to examine short-term particle transformations prior to exposure. Toxicity remained high following incubation in reverse osmosis water (80% mortality) and ASTM water (60% mortality), with ASTM-transformed particles additionally reducing growth and reproduction. In contrast, PET-NPs transformed in natural freshwater caused no detectable lethal or sub-lethal effects under the conditions tested. Particle-size measurements showed extensive aggregation in ASTM water, whereas PET-NPs remained largely dispersed in both reverse osmosis water and natural freshwater. Natural freshwater also altered particle zeta potential, indicating changes in surface properties. The contrasting toxicity of similarly dispersed particles in reverse osmosis and natural freshwater indicates that aggregation alone cannot explain the biological responses. Together, these findings demonstrate that water type can rapidly transform PET-NP particle state and substantially modify chronic biological effects. They highlight the importance of considering environmentally induced particle transformations when assessing nanoplastic toxicity.

articles.title: Isorhapontigenin alleviates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by targeting the RAF1-ERK1/2-CXCL10 axis to inhibit CXCR3+ neutrophil recruitment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction syndrome resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection and is characterized by persistent hyperinflammation followed by immunosuppression. Isorhapontigenin (ISO), a natural stilbene derivative found in Chinese herbs and grapes, possesses potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its potential therapeutic role in sepsis remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of ISO against sepsis-induced multi-organ injury and the underlying molecular mechanisms. Using a murine model of sepsis, we observed that ISO administration considerably suppressed the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α in the tissues. Furthermore, ISO treatment markedly improved survival rates and attenuated pathological damage in the liver and lung. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that ISO confers protection by modulating inflammatory cascades and inhibiting chemokine-mediated immune cell migration. Notably, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) was identified as a key hub gene. Mechanistically, ISO directly binds to RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase (RAF1) and inhibits the RAF1-extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway, thereby downregulating CXCL10 expression and preventing excessive infiltration of C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3-positive (CXCR3+) neutrophils into pulmonary tissue. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that ISO mitigates sepsis-induced lung injury via the RAF1/ERK1/2/CXCL10 axis, providing a potential mechanistic basis for further investigation of ISO as a therapeutic candidate for sepsis.

articles.title: Clinical and treatment-related predictors of failure of pentavalent antimonial therapy for cutaneous leishmaniasis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pentavalent antimonials remain widely used for cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), but treatment failure prolongs disease and increases patient burden. We synthesized routinely available clinical and treatment-related predictors of antimonial failure.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched through 14 August 2026 and Scopus through 30 August 2026, supplemented by citation and targeted website searches. Cohort, case-control, and prediction-model studies of antimony-treated CL were eligible. QUIPS assessed risk of bias. Heterogeneous outcomes, regimens, and overlapping cohorts precluded meta-analysis; results were synthesized following SWiM. The review was not prospectively registered.

RESULTS: Of 1,747 records identified, 1,249 were screened and 36 reports included. Prior antimonial treatment and incomplete treatment exposure or adherence most consistently signalled poorer outcomes. Greater lesion burden often predicted failure, but thresholds varied. Lesion duration was context-dependent: prolonged disease and very early non-ulcerated lesions were associated with failure in different settings. Findings for age, sex, comorbidities, geography, and species were inconsistent or context-specific. No model had convincing external validation; a recent model yielded an internally validated C-statistic of 0.608.

LIMITATIONS: All reports had moderate or high risk of bias. Inconsistent outcome definitions and regimens, suspected cohort overlap, and lack of Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL searches limit confidence and transportability.

CONCLUSIONS: The evidence supports documenting treatment history, measuring lesion burden, addressing adherence barriers, and arranging earlier review for higher-risk patients, rather than using an unvalidated score or automatically replacing antimony. Prospective external validation with harmonized failure definitions is needed.

articles.title: Development and Evaluation of an RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a Molecular Assay for Rapid Diagnosis of Theileria annulata Infection in Bovines.
articles.abstract: Tropical theileriosis, caused by Theileria annulata, continues to be the most significant tick-borne disease affecting cattle, particularly in endemic regions where it leads to significant production losses. Prompt and reliable diagnosis is critically important for timely treatment and disease control; however, conventional diagnostic methods have important limitations. Microscopic examination lacks sensitivity, particularly in carrier animals, while PCR requires specialized laboratory infrastructure. To overcome these limitations, a fluorescence-based RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay targeting the multicopy mitochondrial cytb gene was developed for rapid detection of T. annulata. Five RPA primer pairs were designed and evaluated, and primer set-5, generating a 324-bp amplicon, exhibited the best amplification performance. A CRISPR RNA (crRNA) was designed within the selected amplicon to enable specific Cas12a-mediated target recognition. The assay was completed within 50 min and demonstrated no cross-reactivity with DNA from Theileria orientalis, Babesia bigemina, Babesia bovis, Anaplasma marginale, and bovine host DNA, confirming excellent analytical specificity. Sensitivity analysis using recombinant plasmid DNA demonstrated a detection limit of approximately ten copies per reaction. The field evaluation of the assay was done by testing 206 bovine field samples. showed that the developed assay identified 163 positive samples, exceeding the detection rates obtained by PCR (151 positives) and microscopy (116 positives). On comparison with PCR, the assay achieved 100% diagnostic sensitivity, 78.18% specificity, 92.64% positive predictive value, 100% negative predictive value, with an overall agreement of 94.17%. These findings indicate that the RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a platform is a rapid, sensitive, and accurate molecular diagnostic approach with strong potential for field application and point-of-care diagnosis of bovine tropical theileriosis, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Living longer but not healthier: Global differences in longevity and cardiometabolic health.
articles.abstract: Global life expectancy has increased dramatically from 1950 to 2023, rising by 25 years for females and 24 years for males, driven mostly by advances in nutrition, sanitation, and infectious disease control, and in part by declining cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. Although age-standardized CVD mortality has declined in many settings, absolute cardiometabolic burden has increased because of population growth, aging, and rising exposure to metabolic risks. In 2023, CVD alone accounted for 437 million DALYs and 19.2 million deaths. While overall life expectancy did increase by 8.1 years globally between 1990 and 2019, healthy life expectancy increased by only 6.6 years, corresponding to a widening health span-lifespan gap. This divergence is indicative of prolonged years that are lived with disability, with cardiometabolic diseases among the modifiable drivers. Regional patterns reveal significant heterogeneity, with low- and middle-income countries facing a double burden of communicable diseases and rapidly rising cardiometabolic diseases that are primarily driven by urbanization, nutritional transitions, and inadequate primary care infrastructure. High-income countries, on the other hand, are witnessing a rising health span - life span gap due to near-stagnant growth in LE but expanding cardiometabolic morbidity. Understanding the relationship between changes in longevity and cardiometabolic health is essential for addressing the growing global burden of years lived with disability. This narrative review examines global and regional patterns of life expectancy and healthy life expectancy, with a focus on cardiometabolic disease, and highlights disparities across developmental levels, regions, and demographics to inform targeted prevention and intervention strategies.

articles.title: Ddx1 is essential for zebrafish development to adulthood but has no detectable effect on the response to tilapia lake virus (TiLV) in larvae.
articles.abstract: DExD/H-box RNA helicases are multifunctional regulators of RNA metabolism and some are associated with host defence against viruses. However, the in vivo roles of individual family members remain insufficiently characterised. Ddx1 is one such example, implicated in antiviral signalling as well as in the replication of several viruses. In this study, we investigated the function of Ddx1 during vertebrate development and viral infection in zebrafish (Danio rerio) model using both loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of ddx1 resulted in viable embryos and larvae without overt developmental abnormalities; however, knockouts failed to survive to adulthood, indicating that Ddx1 is required for later stages of development. To assess its role in antiviral defence, ddx1 knockout and wild-type larvae were experimentally infected with tilapia lake virus (TiLV), a virus known to induce a strong type I interferon response in zebrafish. Survival rates, viral loads, and expression of selected type I interferon pathway genes (rig-I, ifnφ1, mxa) were comparable between genotypes, demonstrating that Ddx1 is not essential for the larval antiviral response to TiLV. Consistently, overexpression of ddx1 did not enhance resistance to infection. Together, these findings indicate that while Ddx1 is critical for zebrafish survival to adulthood, it does not play a measurable role in early antiviral immunity against TiLV in zebrafish larvae.

articles.title: Homoacetogenic bioaugmentation with Clostridium magnum WY-4 enhances upflow anaerobic sludge blanket reactor resilience under progressive organic loading and short-term complex shock.
articles.abstract: Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactors are widely used for treating high-strength organic wastewater but are vulnerable to short-term complex shocks caused by increased organic loading, hydraulic retention time regulation, and partial sludge loss. At the same time, the role of homoacetogenic bioaugmentation in improving UASB recovery after such disturbances remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the potential of a novel homoacetogenic strain, Clostridium magnum WY-4 (WY-4), to enhance UASB resilience. Two laboratory-scale UASB reactors were operated for 184 days, and reactor performance, volatile fatty acids (VFA), extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), N-acyl-homoserine lactones (AHL), and microbial community dynamics were analyzed. Under stable conditions, WY-4 had only a limited effect on reactor performance. During and after the shock, however, bioaugmentation markedly accelerated recovery. The maximum effluent VFA concentration in the WY-4 reactor during the shock reached 190 mg/L, 53% lower than in the control. Propionate degradation was enhanced, with only trace amounts remaining in the bottom zone of the WY-4 reactor, whereas acetate and propionate continued to accumulate in the control. During the first nine days of recovery, methane yield was approximately 20% higher in the WY-4 reactor. Principal component analysis showed a faster recovery of AHL profiles, accompanied by altered AHL-EPS relationships. Although dominant microbial populations changed little, the WY-4 reactor maintained greater microbial richness and diversity. The homoacetogenic bioaugmentation with WY-4 enhanced UASB resilience by reducing VFA accumulation, accelerating methane recovery, and promoting restoration of AHL-mediated quorum sensing following short-term complex shock.

articles.title: PA4933 Mediates Dual Regulation of Oxidative Resistance and Virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Pulmonary Infection.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical opportunistic pathogen requiring rigorous prevention and control, which triggers severe infections in immunocompromised populations. Bacterial membrane proteins serve as core regulatory molecules coordinating stress tolerance and virulence homeostasis during host colonization. Nevertheless, the physiological functions of numerous structurally homologous yet unannotated membrane proteins remain largely elusive. In this study, we identified a significantly upregulated hypothetical gene, PA4933, from published transcriptomic datasets of P. aeruginosa PA14 infecting RAW264.7 macrophages. Bioinformatic prediction preliminarily confirmed that PA4933 is a highly conserved seven-transmembrane protein sharing high structural homology with ABC transporters. Mechanistically, PA4933 elevates the transcription of glnA to enrich intracellular glutamine, thereby markedly boosting glutathione (GSH) biosynthesis and enhancing bacterial antioxidant capacity. Meanwhile, PA4933 represses the transcription of virulence-related genes including phzC, rhlA, pel, motA, and motC, which consequently inhibits pyocyanin production, rhamnolipid synthesis, biofilm formation and swarming motility. Such regulatory effects alleviate bacterial damage to multiple infection models, including A549 alveolar epithelial cells, Galleria mellonella larvae and murine acute pneumonia models. Collectively, PA4933 exerts dual regulatory roles: facilitating antioxidant immune evasion while suppressing virulence and mitigating host tissue injury. This protein regulates the infection homeostasis of PAO1, it provides new insights into P. aeruginosa infection.

articles.title: Molecular identification and pathogenicity study of Pseudomonas juntendi isolated from infected Nile tilapia.
articles.abstract: Bacterial pathogens are major threats to sustainable aquaculture, leading to huge economic losses and reducing fish health and productivity. In this study, isolation, identification and characterization of the causative agent of acute mortality (approximately 55%) in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) was carried out. The isolate was identified as Pseudomonas juntendi based on multilocus sequence analysis (16S rRNA, gyrB, rpoB and rpoD), showing highest similarity to reference strains. Most of the biochemical features were in line with previously reported P. juntendi. Virulence factors of the bacterium included high swimming motility, efficient biofilm formation and β-hemolysis. Antibiogram assay indicated that the isolate was resistant to six types of antibiotics with a calculated MAR index of 0.25. Pathogenicity was confirmed experimentally after challenge of healthy Nile tilapia fingerlings, resulting in development of hemorrhagic lesions and mortality with 96 h median lethal dose (LD50) of 5.9 × 105 CFU/fish. Sublethal infection significantly altered host-response gene expression in liver and head kidney tissues, marked by upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-8), immune-related transcription factors (NF-κB and TLR-7), the chemotactic mediator CC-chemokine 1 and the antigen-presentation marker MHC-IIα. Histopathological examination revealed extensive tissue damage in the liver and head kidney with cellular degeneration, aggregation and structural disorganization, indicating systemic infection. The findings in this study clearly demonstrate for the first time that P. juntendi is a virulent pathogen in Nile tilapia, causing significant mortality, tissue damage and immune responses. This investigation contributes to our growing understanding of bacterial pathogens in tilapia farming.

articles.title: Cyclothymic temperament and obstetric severity as independent correlates of antenatal depressive symptoms in high-risk pregnancy: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antenatal depression affects 12.5%-44.2% of women with high-risk pregnancies, yet risk stratification relies predominantly on obstetric factors. We examined whether cyclothymic temperament is independently linked to antenatal depression beyond obstetric severity.

METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 161 women with high-risk pregnancies at a tertiary center (April 2020-May 2021). The primary outcome was antenatal depressive symptoms (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS] ≥10). Primary predictors were maternal-fetal intensive care unit (MFICU) admission and the cyclothymic subscale of the Korean-validated short Temperament Evaluation of Memphis, Pisa, Paris, and San Diego Autoquestionnaire (TEMPS-A). A pre-specified two-variable Firth's penalized logistic regression with bootstrap optimism correction was used; incremental value was assessed by the corrected area under the ROC curve (AUROC), calibration, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: Antenatal depression occurred in 52 of 161 participants (32.3%). Both MFICU admission (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.27; 95% CI, 1.45-7.37) and cyclothymic score (aOR, 1.63 per unit; 95% CI, 1.37-1.95) were independently associated with antenatal depression. An exploratory cyclothymic threshold ≥4 yielded a negative predictive value of 87.5%; adding the cyclothymic score to the obstetric-only model improved the corrected AUROC from 0.629 to 0.821, with good calibration and higher net benefit. Symptoms persisted into the early postpartum period in 77.5% of affected women.

CONCLUSIONS: Cyclothymic temperament and MFICU admission were independently associated with antenatal depression in high-risk pregnancies. Because both were assessed concurrently the association is cross-sectional; pending validation, brief TEMPS-A cyclothymic assessment may help identify psychologically vulnerable women.

articles.title: Prospective Cardiac MRI study comparing Recovered COVID-19 patients with Recovered Non-COVID-19 Viral Respiratory Infection Patients (R-COVID-CMR).
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with subclinical myocardial inflammation. Post-COVID-19 infection, there are concerns about subsequent heart failure and persistent myocarditis. It is unknown how COVID-19 infection compares with non-COVID-19 viral infections in terms of myocardial inflammation based on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) assessment. This prospective longitudinal study aims to determine and compare the extent and severity of myocardial involvement in patients with COVID-19 infection versus non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infections (control).

METHOD: Recruited recovered COVID-19 (RCOVID) patients and recovered non-COVID (non-COVID) patients from several hospitals and COVID-19-designated clinic underwent three CMR examinations for functional assessment, native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, with corroborating blood markers (NT-proBNP, white cell count, c-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, and high sensitivity cardiac troponin T). CMR scans took place (i) within 2-week of confirmed recovery, (ii) 3-month, and (iii) 12-month post-recovery. Linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction was used for analysis.

RESULTS: 152 participants were recruited, 112 RCOVID outpatients (mean age: 41.0; 58.9% female) and 40 non-COVID inpatients (mean age:45.0; 37.5% female). Non-COVID infections included influenza virus, rhinovirus/enterovirus, parainfluenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and human metapneumovirus. At all three time points, blood results and cardiac function parameters were not significantly different between RCOVID and non-COVID patient groups (p-value not significant). Both patient groups had no significant differences for native T1/T2 values, ECV, late gadolinium enhancement, T2 short tau inversion recovery, and overall fulfilment of the 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria at each time points.

CONCLUSION: In this prospective longitudinal study with CMR examinations, COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse myocardial inflammatory response than non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection in terms of CMR parameters, and blood markers.

PLAIN ENGLISH SUMMARY: During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreaks, some COVID-19 patients were incidentally found to have inflammation of the muscular layer of the heart. Healthcare professionals were concerned the inflammation will lead to heart not delivering enough blood to meet body demands (ie. heart failure) in the long run. Therefore, we designed this study to better understand the extent and severity of cardiac involvement in patients with COVID-19 by comparing them to patients with other types of viral respiratory infections, such as influenza, which we were more familiar with. We recruited two groups of patients, one group with patients recovered from COVID-19, the other group with patients recovered from other types of viral respiratory infections. For each patient, we arranged three assessments at 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months after their recovery respectively. During each assessment, they had blood taken and underwent a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) scan, a type of medical imaging used for assessment of heart function. 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria (LLC) is a set of criteria for diagnosis of myocardial inflammation recommended by a group of experts. We compared the two groups of patients at each time point according to LLC, as well as their blood markers and heart function. In our study, we found that COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse heart muscle inflammatory response than other types of viral respiratory infections. This is reassuring as patients with previous COVID-19 infections will likely not develop inflammation of the heart muscle nor develop heart failure.

articles.title: Structural and Functional Characterization of a Novel Broad-Spectrum Oligosaccharide Uptake Channel OmpV25 in Vibrio campbellii.
articles.abstract: Vibrio campbellii (formerly Vibrio harveyi) is a marine pathogen that causes vibriosis, a major disease affecting global aquaculture. This bacterium inhabits chitin-rich environments and uses chito-oligosaccharides as a main nutrient source. Here, we identify the novel outer membrane protein OmpV25 as a porin mediating broad-spectrum oligosaccharide uptake in V. campbellii. OmpV25 was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) Omp8, purified by nickel affinity and size exclusion chromatography, and crystallized. The resulting 2.70 Å crystal structure revealed the 25-kDa OmpV25 to be a monomeric β-barrel composed of 12 β-strands connected by six extracellular loops and five periplasmic turns. Single-channel electrophysiology demonstrated that OmpV25 forms stable monomeric pores in artificial lipid bilayers characterized by a conductance of 0.19 ± 0.003 nS in 1 M KCl. The channel facilitated binding of mono-, di-, tri- and tetragalacturonic acids, as well as chitotetraose and maltotetraose. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed moderate-affinity binding to tetragalacturonic acid (Kd = 3.04 ± 0.42 μM), chitotetraose (Kd = 6.79 ± 0.27 μM), and maltotetraose (Kd = 5.21 ± 0.78 μM). A liposome swelling assay confirmed that OmpV25 enables translocation of a broad range of oligosaccharides beyond oligogalacturonic acids. These findings define the physiological role of OmpV25 as a broad-specificity sugar channel that may support environmental resilience of Vibrio species in nutrient-variable marine habitats.

articles.title: Global prevalence of equine piroplasmosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of evidence from 2020-2025.
articles.abstract: Equine piroplasmosis remains a major constraint to equine health, productivity, and international movement. In compliance with PRISMA 2020 criteria, a systematic review and meta-analysis were carried out to estimate the pooled global prevalence of equine piroplasmosis and identify possible sources of risk variables. Databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, Europe PMC, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, CABI Digital Library, and Google Scholar were searched between 2020 to 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate pooled prevalence estimates. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and publication bias assessments were conducted using RStudio software version 4.6.0. Among the 95 studies included in the analysis, the pooled prevalence of active T. equi infection was 25.21%, while the corresponding seroprevalence was 30.96%. For active B. caballi infection, the pooled prevalence was 4.60%, compared with a seroprevalence of 10.90%. The pooled prevalence of active T. haneyi infection was 12.18%. Substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%) was identified across all pooled estimates, likely reflecting differences in sampling periods and sample sizes, geographic regions, diagnostic approaches, and host demographics. Meta-regression revealed a significant increasing temporal trend in T. equi prevalence (p < 0.05), whereas no significant trends were detected for B. caballi or T. haneyi (p > 0.05). Equine piroplasmosis remains highly prevalent worldwide, particularly T. equi, with marked heterogeneity driven by methodological factors, geographic region, and host characteristics. These findings underscore the need for standardized surveillance, harmonized diagnostics, and integrated vector control strategies to mitigate the global impact of equine piroplasmosis.

articles.title: Trends in Diversity among Medical Cancer Workforce Trainees in the United States over Fifteen years.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diverse oncology workforces improve care quality, patient satisfaction, and outcomes, particularly among underserved populations. This study aimed to evaluate long-term demographic and educational trends among U.S. cancer-related medical trainees and examine how these trends have shifted across specialties over a 15-year period.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Publicly available data were sourced from the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Data Resource Books. Gender and educational-background trends were evaluated from 2007-2023, while race/ethnicity trends were evaluated from 2011-2023 across cancer-related physician training programs, including hematology-medical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, surgical oncology, pediatric hematology-oncology, medical genetics, pathology, diagnostic and interventional radiology, and nuclear medicine. Demographic variables included gender, race/ethnicity, and age; educational background was categorized as U.S. allopathic, U.S. osteopathic, or international medical graduate (IMG). Trends were assessed using the nonparametric Mann-Kendall test, with P<.05 indicating statistical significance.

RESULTS: Between 2007 and 2023, female trainee representation rose significantly (47.0% to 51.5%; p<0.001), with notable gains in pediatric hematology-oncology and medical oncology. Hispanic/Latino representation increased significantly from 7.9% to 11.6% overall (p<0.001), while African American/Black representation remained unchanged (7.1% to 7.5%; p>0.05). Asian/Pacific Islander proportions rose in select specialties. The percentage of U.S. osteopathic graduates increased across most specialties (5.1% to 16.2%; p<0.001), whereas IMG representation declined slightly overall. U.S. allopathic representation decreased from 62.9% to 53.3% (p<0.001), with variation across specialties.

CONCLUSION: While gains in gender and Hispanic/Latino representation are evident, African American/Black trainee representation remains stagnant, and changes in IMG participation vary across specialties. These diverging trends highlight persistent representation gaps within the U.S. cancer workforce training pipeline. Continued monitoring will be important to determine how evolving educational and accreditation policies influence these trends over time.

POLICY SUMMARY: Based on these findings, program directors and professional societies should maintain inclusive recruitment practices and continue systematic monitoring of workforce diversity as accreditation policies evolve. Sustained institutional commitment may help preserve patient trust, address workforce needs, and support an oncology workforce that better reflects the populations it serves.

articles.title: Liver transplantation for adult presentations of MDR3 deficiency.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MDR3 deficiency is associated with end-stage liver disease including liver failure, portal hypertension and primary liver cancer, with increasing recognition of adult presentations. We report our single centre experience of liver transplantation (LT) for adult presentations of MDR3 deficiency.
