METHODS: A single centre retrospective study of patients who underwent LT for MDR3 deficiency from 2013-2024 and were first diagnosed above the age of 16 years. We identified demographic and clinical data from the electronic patient records.

RESULTS: There were 7 patients with genetically confirmed MDR3 deficiency who underwent LT, including 3 (43%) females, and median age at LT was 31.9 years (range, 25-37). Severity of liver disease at assessment: median bilirubin 266 µmol/L (range, 38-726 µmol/L) and MELD 22 (range, 11-38). Due to severity of liver disease and clinical trajectory, organ allocation was prioritised in 4 (57%) patients, either internally or nationally. All patients had at least 1 suspected aetiology of liver disease prior to the diagnosis of MDR3 deficiency. Only 4 (57%) were diagnosed with MDR3 deficiency at time of LT assessment, and patients with a known diagnosis of MDR3 deficiency were assessed for LT at an earlier stage of liver disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with MDR3 deficiency can be assessed for LT at advanced stages of liver disease, and the diagnosis may be reached after transplant. Genetic testing can facilitate and accurate diagnosis and allow personalised management. The timing of LT assessment needs to be considered carefully in MDR3 deficiency.

articles.title: Prior Decompensation Shapes the Clinical Phenotype and the Prognostic Performance of Biochemical Liver-Failure Criteria in Hospitalised Cirrhosis patients: A Multicentre Study.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Index and recurrent decompensation have different impacts on the course of acute decompensation (AD). Contemporary biochemical liver failure definitions for acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) do not distinguish between index and prior decompensation. We evaluated whether prior decompensation defines a clinically distinct phenotype and examined whether established biochemical liver failure criteria retain consistent prognostic performance across these phenotypes METHODS: This multicentre study evaluated 966 adults hospitalized with AD across four centres in India, stratified into first-presentation (n = 364) and prior-decompensation (n = 602) cohorts. Biochemical thresholds from APASL (bilirubin ≥5 mg/dL and INR ≥1.5), CLEARED (≥7.5 mg/dL and INR≥1.5), and EASL-CLIF (bilirubin ≥12 mg/dL) were evaluated against 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: Patients with prior decompensation were older, more often had MASLD-related cirrhosis (21.3% vs 10.7%), and showed greater extra-hepatic organ failures. Thirty-day mortality was higher in patients with prior decompensation independent of MELD and baseline infection (40.5% vs 30.5%; adjusted RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.10-1.56, p=0.003), largely attributable to hepatic encephalopathy, which was twice as common (60% vs 29%). In the overall cohort, APASL and CLEARED modestly predicted mortality (OR 1.36 and 1.41, respectively), whereas EASL-CLIF threshold did not. In decompensation phenotype-stratified analysis, prognostic performance varied; biochemical thresholds were associated with 30-day mortality only among prior decompensation (APASL: OR 1.57; CLEARED: OR 1.67; CLIF-C: OR 1.71), but not in the first-presentation phenotype. The bilirubin-only CLIF-C OF liver-failure component captured the fewest deaths and showed significant phenotype-dependent prognostic behaviour.

CONCLUSION: Prior decompensation defines a clinically distinct, high-risk phenotype mediated by encephalopathy. Liver-failure criteria perform discordantly across phenotypes with different prognostic signals in first and prior decompensations.

articles.title: Targeting the phosphoprotein enriched in diabetes/astrocytes 15 death effector domain via fragment-based and integrative structural biology approaches.
articles.abstract: Phosphoprotein Enriched in Diabetes/Astrocytes 15 (PED/PEA-15) is a 15 kDa adaptor protein whose overexpression drives tumorigenesis and type II diabetes through dysregulated protein-protein interactions (PPIs) mediated by its Death Effector Domain (DED). Despite its therapeutic relevance, no potent small-molecule inhibitors targeting the DED have yet been identified. Here, we employed a fragment-based drug discovery approach combining 19F and 1H NMR screening of a 118-compound fluorinated library to identify F2 a fragment that binds the PED/PEA-15 DED with an estimated dissociation constant of 150 μM. NMR chemical shift perturbation analysis mapped the binding site to the α2-α3 loop, α3, and α5 helices. To better characterise the protein, Small-angle X-ray scattering of the apo protein was employed, yielding a structural model in which the C-terminal tail is consistent with a conformation that is not maximally extended. Induced fit docking and molecular dynamics simulations of the PED/PEA-15-F2 complex supported a plausible binding pose and suggested a ligand-induced destabilisation of the α3 helix propagating to the α6 helix. Correlation network analysis further suggests a hypothesis in which F2 rewires the dynamic architecture of the DED and alters allosteric communication between residues of the DED and the C-terminal tail. The identification of a ligand-accessible site on the DED supports the druggability of PED/PEA-15 and provides a refined structural framework for fragment optimisation and for testing whether engagement of this site can be translated into modulation of PED/PEA-15 PPIs with therapeutic potential in cancer and type II diabetes.

articles.title: Combining minocycline with polymyxin B against Klebsiella pneumoniae in neutropenic murine infection models: one plus one is more than two.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic options for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae are limited and combination therapy is often used. In vitro studies suggested that minocycline and polymyxin B may act synergistically. We studied this antibiotic combination in neutropenic murine K. pneumoniae infection models.

MATERIALS: The PK/PD-index for minocycline against K. pneumoniae was determined in neutropenic murine thigh (N=2 strains) and lung (N=1 strain) infection models, followed by minocycline target assessment (N=4 thigh; N=2 lung). Subsequently, suboptimal polymyxin B dose levels were added to minocycline in both thigh (N=2) and lung (N=1) models. An interaction index was calculated based on Loewe additivity theory.

RESULTS: Overall, the antibacterial effect of minocycline correlated best with fAUC/MIC and was subsequently used as PK/PD-index. No killing was observed, whereas stasis was found only in the thigh infection model for 2 of 4 strains with minocycline fAUC/MIC of 18.9 and 24.5, respectively. In the combination experiments, stasis and 1-log10 kill were reached in experiments at subtherapeutic polymyxin B levels (6.5-36.6 fAUC/MICs) with minocycline fAUC/MICs of 3.1-14.5 for stasis and 8.4-26.1 for 1-log10 kill. This synergistic effect was confirmed by the interaction indices of 0.16-0.66 in the thigh- and 0.44-0.77 in the lung-infection model.

CONCLUSION: Minocycline monotherapy is not adequate to treat K. pneumoniae infections. Minocycline plus polymyxin B is synergistic reaching a 1-log10 kill effect in all 3 combination experiments and a 2-log10 kill effect in one strain. Based on limited human PK, high human minocycline doses may be needed to reach the required exposure for stasis.

articles.title: Asymptomatic vs. Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid disease, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations.

METHODS: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level one stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction, and death at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates.

RESULTS: 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (IQR 6-11). SD patients had a longer median length of stay (2 vs 1 day, p = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs 36%, p = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30- and 90-day and 0.9% at 1-year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30-day, 90-day, and one year, with no difference between AD vs SD. 1-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90-day and one year, without a difference by AD vs SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer LOS, SD patients did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

articles.title: Occurrence of Cryptosporidium sp. in fresh produce from the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica: an update.
articles.abstract: Foodborne diseases represent a major global public health problem, causing significant morbidity and mortality, and substantial economic losses. Fruits and vegetables are considered among the main vehicles for transmission of infectious agents like bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, including Cryptosporidium sp. This protozoan parasite comprises many species that infect a wide range of hosts, is environmentally and geographically ubiquitous and has become one of the leading causes of diarrheal disease; in immunocompromised hosts, the infection can result in a chronic, life-threatening disease. Considering the importance of fruit and vegetable consumption in the daily diet and the need to ensure their safety, the aim of the study was to evaluate the presence of Cryptosporidium sp. in strawberries, lettuce and cilantro marketed in the Metropolitan Area of Costa Rica and to assess the degree of faecal contamination in these foods. For this purpose, 96 samples were analysed using parasitological and molecular methods that included a nested PCR to amplify Cryptosporidium sp. gp60 gene. Moreover, the presence of total and thermotolerant coliforms and Escherichia coli was also determined by culture methods and counts, for further identification using the VITEK system. Direct examination of wet mount and Ziehl-Neelsen stains revealed five Cryptosporidium sp. positive samples by microscopy and 22 positive samples by PCR; the identified species was Cryptosporidium parvum. Cilantro samples presented the highest counts of total, and thermotolerant coliforms and E. coli was identified in14 samples among 82 samples subjected to bacteriological analyses. The detection of C. parvum in raw vegetables and fruits from different provinces in Costa Rica, particularly using molecular techniques, demonstrates the need to strengthen surveillance and control in the production and marketing of these foods, to improve risk assessment and its relevance to public health.

articles.title: Food Safety Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices among Food Handlers in the School Feeding Program in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Food safety is critical in school feeding programs to protect children's health. This cross-sectional study assessed food safety knowledge, attitudes, practices, and associated factors among 632 food handlers in the Addis Ababa School Feeding Program. Five sub-cities, four woredas per sub-city, and one public primary school per woreda were selected using multistage sampling; all eligible food handlers were included. Data collected through structured interviewer-administered questionnaires in April-May 2023 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank correlation, and logistic regression. Overall, 85.8% of food handlers were classified as having adequate knowledge, 79.6% as having positive attitudes, and 72.3% as having satisfactory practices; approximately 96% reported previous food safety training. Satisfactory practice was significantly associated with separate storage of raw and ready-to-eat foods (AOR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.01-0.90), water availability (AOR = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.16-0.93), handwashing facilities (AOR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.36-0.95), and attitude score (AOR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.11-0.28). Knowledge was weakly positively correlated with attitudes (ρ = 0.139, P < 0.001) and practices (ρ = 0.127, P = 0.001), while attitudes showed a stronger positive correlation with practices (ρ = 0.340, P < 0.001). Despite high reported training coverage, satisfactory practices were less prevalent than adequate knowledge and positive attitudes, indicating that training exposure alone may not translate into consistent food safety practices. Practical training, supportive supervision, routine monitoring, and adequate infrastructure may improve food safety. Given the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported practices, causal relationships and objectively verified compliance could not be established.

articles.title: External Validation of the CARE-BMT and Modified CARE-BMT Scores for Cardiac Event Prediction After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac events after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) are associated with increased non-relapse mortality (NRM) and inferior survival. The CARE-BMT score predicts cardiovascular events after hematopoietic cell transplantation but does not incorporate post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy). We aimed to externally validate the original CARE-BMT score and a modified version incorporating standard-dose PTCy exposure in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing allo-HCT.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study including 809 adults with AML who underwent first allo-HCT across 11 Spanish transplant centers. The original and modified CARE-BMT scores were retrospectively applied. The primary endpoint was the cumulative incidence of post-transplant cardiac events, with relapse and death considered competing risks.

RESULTS: Sixty patients developed a cardiac event, corresponding to a cumulative incidence of 6.9% (95% CI, 5.2-8.8). Cardiac events were associated with inferior 3-year overall survival (50.1% vs 62.5%; P = 0.001) and higher 3-year NRM (21.3% vs 6.2%; P = 0.001). Using the original CARE-BMT score, patients were classified as intermediate-risk (n = 246) or high-risk (n = 563), with no low-risk patients identified. Cardiac event incidence was higher in the high-risk group (8.6% vs 3.0%; HR, 2.89; P = 0.005). The modified CARE-BMT score classified patients as low-risk (n = 85), intermediate-risk (n = 558), or high-risk (n = 166), with progressively increasing cardiac event incidence (2.4%, 6.1%, and 11.8%, respectively; P = 0.011). High-risk patients had a significantly greater risk of cardiac events than low-risk patients (HR, 5.37; P = 0.024).

CONCLUSIONS: In this AML allo-HCT cohort, cardiac events occurred in approximately 7% of patients and were associated with worse survival and increased NRM. Incorporating standard-dose PTCy improved risk stratification, supporting inclusion of transplant-specific variables in cardiovascular risk prediction after allo-HCT.

articles.title: Pregnancy and Offspring Outcomes After Prenatal Stimulant or Atomoxetine Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of prenatal exposure to stimulants and atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with pregnancy, congenital, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 2026. Protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42024506319).

STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomized trials and observational studies comparing pregnancies or offspring exposed to stimulant medications, methylphenidate- or amphetamine-based agents, or atomoxetine with unexposed comparators and reported outcomes were eligible.

STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Reporting guidance for systematic reviews and observational meta-analyses was followed. Two reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled unadjusted and adjusted estimates separately. For neurodevelopmental outcomes, comparators restricted to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder populations were prioritized when available.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies were included; 23 contributed to quantitative analyses. Exposure windows included periconceptional, first-trimester, early-, late-, or continued-pregnancy exposure. Exposure was associated with major congenital malformations in unadjusted analyses (risk ratio, 1.25; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.37), but not after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.04; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-1.12). No adjusted association was observed with cardiovascular malformations (adjusted risk ratio, 1.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.88-1.63), although methylphenidate showed a modest increase (adjusted risk ratio, 1.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-1.74). In adjusted analyses, exposure was not associated with miscarriage, preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neurodevelopmental disorders, autism spectrum disorder, or offspring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Low 5-minute Apgar score remained associated with exposure after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.42). Lower adjusted autism spectrum disorder risk with stimulants was not replicated in methylphenidate-specific analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to stimulants or atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder was not associated with increased adjusted risk of major congenital malformations or most adverse pregnancy, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Attenuation of crude associations after adjustment suggests confounding by indication, residual confounding, and maternal characteristics. The observed associations between methylphenidate and cardiovascular malformations and between exposure and low 5-minute Apgar score warrant continued investigation but should not be interpreted as evidence of causal harm.

articles.title: Infectious Keratitis and Endophthalmitis Following Boston Type I Keratoprosthesis: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Long-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the incidence, clinical characteristics, and risk factors for infectious keratitis and endophthalmitis following Boston Type I keratoprosthesis (KPro) implantation.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 153 eyes (141 patients) that underwent KPro implantation at the University of Illinois Chicago between 2005 and 2023. Demographic, clinical, microbiologic, and surgical data were analyzed. Incidence rates were calculated per eye-year at risk, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess risk factors.

RESULTS: Among 153 eyes from 141 patients, 30 developed at least one infection: 12 developed endophthalmitis alone, 5 developed infectious keratitis alone, and 13 developed both. The incidence rates of endophthalmitis and infectious keratitis were 2.77 and 1.97 cases per 100 eye-years at risk, respectively. In univariable Cox analysis, immune-mediated ocular disease (HR, 3.05; 95% CI, 1.04-8.95; P = .043) was associated with endophthalmitis, and preexisting eyelid/adnexal abnormality was associated with infectious keratitis (HR, 5.67; 95% CI, 2.02-15.95; P = .001). In the model adjusted for age, immune-mediated ocular disease, and prior herpes simplex virus (HSV) keratitis, immune-mediated ocular disease was associated with endophthalmitis (adjusted HR, 3.62; 95% CI, 1.19-11.04; P = .024), whereas prior HSV keratitis showed a borderline association (adjusted HR, 3.05; 95% CI, 1.00-9.26; P = .050). The proportional hazards assumption was not met for immune-mediated ocular disease or preexisting eyelid/adnexal abnormality; the corresponding HRs represent average associations over follow-up. No multivariable model was fitted for infectious keratitis.

CONCLUSIONS: Infectious keratitis and endophthalmitis remain serious complications after Boston Type I KPro. Endophthalmitis occurred most often in the first postoperative year but continued during long-term follow-up. Immune-mediated ocular disease was associated with endophthalmitis in the adjusted model, whereas prior HSV keratitis showed a borderline adjusted association. Preexisting eyelid/adnexal abnormality was associated with infectious keratitis in univariable analysis; this finding is exploratory. Long-term surveillance and careful management of the ocular surface and eyelids remain central to postoperative care.

articles.title: Optic disc drusen as a diagnostic confounder in a child with Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
articles.journal: Archivos de la Sociedad Espanola de Oftalmologia
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 10-year-old boy referred for transient visual episodes compatible with Alice in Wonderland syndrome, described as a sensation that objects were moving away. Ophthalmic examination showed preserved visual acuity and an unremarkable anterior segment, but revealed elevation of the left optic disc, prompting evaluation for true papilledema. Macular OCT was normal, whereas optic nerve head OCT demonstrated structural asymmetry consistent with pseudopapilledema. Brain and orbital MRI showed isolated enlargement of both optic nerve sheaths and mild elevation of the left optic disc, without additional findings suggestive of intracranial hypertension. Orbital ultrasonography identified a hyperechogenic focus suggestive of optic disc drusen. The stable clinical and structural course supported the diagnosis of unilateral pseudopapilledema due to optic disc drusen, probably unrelated to the perceptual symptoms.

articles.title: Transcarotid Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With the Evolut Self-Expanding Valve: Outcomes from a Real-World Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcarotid access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the most commonly used alternate access in the United States. Real-world evidence on transcarotid access using the Evolut self-expanding valve based on larger numbers of patients may help inform treatment optimization towards better outcomes.

METHODS: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry™ was queried for patients undergoing native TAVR using transcarotid access with an Evolut (January 2015-December 2024). In-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year outcomes are reported.

RESULTS: We identified 2,105 patients (mean age 78.3±7.9 years) with mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk of mortality 6.4±5.3. Most were high/extreme surgical risk (60.0%) with New York Heart Association class III/IV heart failure symptoms (66.8%) and mean baseline Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Score 45.3±25.4. Implant success was 99.6% primarily using general anesthesia (95.8%) with median procedure time of 88.0 (Q1=68.0, Q3=115.0) minutes. Median length of stay was 2.0 (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.0) days; 89.0% were discharged to home. In-hospital, 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality was 2.1%, 3.8% and 16.5%; stroke occurred in 3.1%, 3.8% and 5.1% of patients, respectively. At 30 days, major vascular complications (1.9%), valve related (0.4%) and non-valve related (10.9%) readmissions were low. The mean change in KCCQ score from baseline to 1-year was +30.5±27.1 points.

CONCLUSIONS: Transcarotid TAVR with the Evolut TAV is an effective, safe approach for patients with unfavorable iliofemoral anatomy. Heart teams should become facile with this technique to provide optimal care across the anatomy spectrum.

articles.title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve with Giant Non-Coronary Sinus Aneurysm Compressing the Sinoatrial Node Causing Arrhythmia and Coarctation of the Aorta: A Case on Clinical Decision-Making and Surgical Challenges.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve, the most common congenital valvular disease, frequently coexists with aortic pathologies. Symptomatic arrhythmias from unruptured giant aortic sinus aneurysm compressing the sinoatrial node are exceedingly rare. The coexistence of bicuspid aortic valve, arrhythmogenic sinus aneurysm, coarctation of the aorta, and right coronary artery occlusion represents an extraordinarily complex malformation with scarce documentation and controversial management strategies.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male patient presented with chest tightness and palpitations. Echocardiography and computed tomography angiography revealed Type 0 bicuspid aortic valve (two-sinus type) with giant unruptured non-coronary sinus aneurysm (52 mm × 48 mm), descending coarctation of the aorta (14 mm), post-stenotic aneurysm (42 mm), and right coronary artery occlusion. Imaging confirmed direct sinoatrial node compression. First-stage surgery comprised biological aortic valve replacement, sinus repair, and coronary artery bypass grafting. The coarctation of the aorta was managed conservatively based on borderline transcoarctation gradient and favorable clinical status.

CONCLUSION: Direct mechanical sinoatrial node compression combined with compromised nodal arterial supply constituted the pathophysiological basis for arrhythmia. For bicuspid aortic valve with multisegmental aortic disease, individualized strategy based on anatomical characteristics, hemodynamic parameters (such as transcoarctation gradient, aortic isthmus ratio, and extremity blood pressure difference), and systemic condition is essential. Staged repair prioritizing hemodynamically threatening lesions reduces surgical trauma and spinal ischemia risk, providing clinical guidance for managing such rare complex aortic pathologies.

articles.title: Atrial Cardiomyopathy Through the Pathologist's Lens: From Tissue Remodeling to Clinical Expression.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
articles.abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy (ACM) provides a useful framework for understanding structural, architectural, contractile, and electrophysiological disease of the atria. ACM and atrial fibrillation (AF) are closely linked but are not interchangeable: ACM favors arrhythmogenesis, whereas sustained AF can accelerate atrial injury. This review considers ACM from the pathologist's perspective, encompassing primary atrial disease and secondary remodeling associated with valvular disease and classical cardiomyopathies. The histologic spectrum includes cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and myocytolysis, interstitial and replacement fibrosis, endocardial fibroelastosis, adipose and inflammatory infiltration, vascular injury, and amyloid deposition. Structural remodeling is regionally heterogeneous, and appendage specimens may underrepresent abnormalities elsewhere in the atrium. Histologic interpretation requires attention to intrinsic regional architecture, associated lesions, previous interventions, and methods of quantification. At the molecular and cellular level, genetic susceptibility and acquired stressors converge on cardiomyocyte dysfunction, inflammation, fibroblast activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Correlating these tissue changes with mapping, imaging, biomarkers, and clinical outcomes will be necessary to validate noninvasive phenotypes and identify clinically meaningful disease subsets. At present, ACM should prompt etiologic investigation and risk assessment but does not by itself constitute an indication for specific therapy.

articles.title: Preoperative Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Use is Associated With Increased Complication Risk After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Dose-Response Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) use has been associated with adverse outcomes following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). This study examined whether complication rates vary based on SSRI daily dosage.

METHODS: A claims database (2010 to 2023) identified 77,958 primary THA patients who did not have osteoporosis and who filled an SSRI prescription 60 days preoperatively. Patients were matched 1:3 to SSRI-naive individuals by age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and history of cognitive disorders, depression, anxiety, and substance use. Overall, 77,958 SSRI users were matched to 233,277 controls (mean age 65 years). After matching, baseline demographics and rates of anxiety and depression (all P > 0.13) were similar between cohorts. The SSRI doses were standardized using quantity, duration, and strength, then stratified as low (0 to 30 mg), medium (30 to 100 mg), or high (greater than 100 mg). Multivariate regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed surgical complications and revision-free survival at 2-year follow-up.

RESULTS: Preoperative SSRI use was associated with greater 2-year complications (5.2 versus 3.2%, P < 0.001). In adjusted multivariate analysis, SSRI use was associated with increased odds of component loosening (OR [odds ratio] 1.5), periprosthetic fracture (OR 1.8), periprosthetic joint infection (OR 1.7), dislocation (OR 2.0), and revision surgery (OR 1.7) (all P < 0.001). There was no dose-dependent relationship observed. Component loosening approached statistical significance at high SSRI doses (OR 3.7, P = 0.07). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated reduced revision-free survival among SSRI users (P < 0.001) at 2-year follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SSRI use, regardless of dose, was associated with higher 2-year rates of periprosthetic joint infection, dislocation, fracture, loosening, and revision. However, the absence of a dose-response relationship suggests that SSRIs are unlikely to be directly responsible for these complications.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of antihistamines, increased antihistamine dosing, and antihistamine adjuncts for chronic urticaria: a systematic review, dose-response, and network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic urticaria is a common immune-mediated condition characterized by wheals (itch and hives), angioedema, or both, lasting for greater than six weeks. It is managed with H1 antihistamines as the first-line therapy. Fundamental unresolved questions remain regarding the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts, and of H1 antihistamine dose-escalation.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts (H2 blockers or montelukast), and of H1 antihistamine dose-escalation.

METHODS: As part of updating the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology and American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters Chronic Urticaria guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and regulatory databases from inception to March 17, 2025, for randomized trials addressing antihistamines or their adjuncts for chronic urticaria. Paired reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Random effects network and dose-response meta-analyses addressed urticaria activity (composed of itch and wheal scores), angioedema activity, urticaria-related quality of life, and harms including sedation. The GRADE approach informed certainty of evidence ratings.

PROSPERO: CRD42022367280.

RESULTS: 211 trials (22,187 participants) evaluated 55 unique treatments. Bilastine, desloratadine, fexofenadine, and levocetirizine are among the most effective in improving overall urticaria activity, urticaria-related quality of life, and sleep disturbance. Cetirizine and loratadine are among the most effective in reducing overall urticaria activity and its subcomponents, with cetirizine also among the most effective in improving urticaria-related quality of life. Escalating from a single to quadruple daily dose may yield diminishing additional benefit. Second-generation agents as a class may be more effective than first-generation agents in improving urticaria activity and sleep disturbance. Sedation risk likely increases with higher doses, with first-generation agents (e.g., diphenhydramine, hydroxyzine) and doxepin among the most sedating; cetirizine, ketotifen, levocetirizine, and rupatadine among the intermediate sedating; and bepotastine, bilastine, desloratadine, ebastine, fexofenadine, and loratadine among the least sedating. Adding montelukast (moderate certainty) or an H2 blocker (very low certainty) to a second-generation agent may further reduce urticaria activity.

CONCLUSIONS: For chronic urticaria, second-generation agents differ in their efficacy and safety. First-generation agents are less beneficial and more harmful. Escalating to higher daily doses may provide additional benefits but likely increases sedation.

articles.title: Lower Nasal Sphingolipids in Pediatric Asthma and Cell-Type-Specific Effects of 17q21 Variants.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genetic variations at the 17q21 asthma-risk locus regulate GSDMB and ORMDL3, influencing inflammatory pathways and sphingolipid metabolism. Although 17q21 variants such as rs7216389 and rs12936231 are associated with ORMDL3 expression in immune and airway smooth muscle cells, their effects on airway epithelial sphingolipids remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether asthma or 17q21 asthma genotypes alter sphingolipid composition in the upper respiratory tract in children, and to define contributions of epithelial versus immune cells.

METHODS: Sphingolipids were quantified by mass spectrometry in nasal fluid and plasma from children with and without asthma. Nasal epithelial cells and PBMCs from healthy adults homozygous for rs7216389 C/C or T/T (risk) were analyzed for sphingolipid levels and ORMDL3/GSDMB associated gene expression.

RESULTS: Children with atopic asthma had significantly lower nasal dihydroceramides, ceramides, and sphingosine independent of inhaled corticosteroids and allergic rhinitis. Asthma was associated with increased plasma sphingolipids but decreased sphingolipids in blood cells, mirroring nasal findings. In PBMCs, the rs7216389 T allele was associated with increased ORMDL3 expression and suppressed de-novo sphingolipid synthesis. In nasal epithelial cells, the T allele predominantly increased GSDMB expression and did not alter sphingolipid metabolism.

CONCLUSIONS: Nasal mucosal sphingolipids are reduced in children with atopic asthma and sphingolipids generated by de-novo sphingolipid synthesis may serve as a noninvasive biomarker of disease. 17q21 risk alleles can exert cell-type-specific effects: ORMDL3-mediated suppression of sphingolipid synthesis occurs in immune cells but not in airway epithelial cells. Systemic immune or inflammatory cell-driven alterations may contribute to reduced airway sphingolipids in asthma.

articles.title: Environmental hygiene programs in public hospitals: a pilot study of pre-implementation assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental contamination contributes to the transmission of healthcare-associated pathogens, particularly multidrug-resistant microorganisms.

OBJECTIVE: To perform a baseline assessment of environmental hygiene programs in public hospitals from the perspective of housekeeping personnel.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive, and exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted in three public tertiary hospitals in São Paulo State, Brazil. Quantitative data were collected from environmental hygiene staff using the translated and adapted CDC Environmental Hygiene Program Improvement Toolkit, specifically the "B2 Baseline Assessment - Part 2 (Advanced Program)" instrument. Qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with direct supervisors of environmental hygiene teams from each participating hospital.

RESULTS: Forty-five housekeeping professionals participated. High frequencies were observed for infection prevention and control training, including hand hygiene and personal protective equipment use (100%), and supervisor availability during shifts (97.8%). Gaps were identified in structured monitoring of environmental hygiene quality (55.5%), continuous supply availability throughout shifts (51.1%), and performance feedback, with 46.7% reporting no feedback.

CONCLUSIONS: The main gaps were related to monitoring practices, feedback processes, and budget planning rather than task execution. The baseline assessment tool was successfully applied without operational difficulties, supporting its feasibility in Brazil and highlighting areas for strengthening environmental hygiene programs.

articles.title: Wound care and infection prevention among war-injured civilians and their caregivers in the Gaza Strip: knowledge, attitudes, practices, and barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When war moves wound care into homes and shelters, infection prevention depends on injured civilians and their caregivers. Their infection-prevention knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) in Gaza remain poorly documented.

METHODS: We surveyed 528 respondents (191 war-injured patients, 337 caregivers) at three referral hospitals in the Gaza Strip (July-September 2025) using a structured, self-administered questionnaire covering wound-care and infection-prevention KAP. Knowledge and Attitude scores were modeled with multivariable linear regression, cross-validated against overdispersion-corrected binomial models.

RESULTS: Knowledge was moderate (median 11/19). Recognition of individual signs of infection ranged from 43.9% to 62.1%, and only 28.8% agreed that tetanus vaccination is necessary after injury. Handwashing was endorsed by 98.1%, yet 31.8% would change dressings bare-handed when gloves were unavailable, 23.7% accepted reusing clean-looking dressings, and 47.3% considered herbal remedies an effective antibiotic substitute. Personal dressing-change experience was most strongly associated with Knowledge (β = 1.65, p < 0.001); education and age were associated with both scores. Displacement (58.4%), supply uncertainty (53.4%), and unsuitable shelter (52.4%) were the leading barriers.

CONCLUSIONS: Gaps in infection recognition, glove use, dressing reuse, and antibiotic beliefs coexisted with structural barriers, suggesting a need for infection-prevention education paired with hygiene and dressing supplies.

articles.title: Silent bronchoscopy-associated outbreak of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and pseudo-outbreak of Mycobacterium gordonae linked to contaminated rinse water and a damaged bronchoscope.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchoscopy-associated outbreaks may remain unrecognized when contamination is difficult to distinguish from infection.

METHODS: Following increased Mycobacterium gordonae isolation from bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), we performed environmental sampling, bronchoscope assessment, a reprocessing audit, and whole-genome sequencing. Recovery of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia from automated endoscope reprocessor (AER) water prompted retrospective review of S. maltophilia-positive BAL cultures.

RESULTS: Six BAL-associated M. gordonae isolates were identified during 2024-2025. Three available isolates were genomically indistinguishable (0 single-nucleotide polymorphisms), consistent with a common source or contamination process. Other nontuberculous mycobacteria and water-associated organisms were recovered from the AER water supply, although M. gordonae was not. A concurrent outbreak of S. maltophilia-positive BAL cultures was identified; positivity increased from 0.6% during 2017-2023 to 12.9% during January-June 2025. Use of damaged bronchoscope RC41 was associated with S. maltophilia cases (94% vs 46%; OR 17.73, 95% CI 2.01-156.46; p=0.002). Following RC41 removal, water-system remediation, and reprocessing changes, no further BAL-associated M. gordonae or S. maltophilia isolates were detected.

CONCLUSIONS: Investigation of an apparent M. gordonae pseudo-outbreak revealed a concurrent S. maltophilia outbreak in the setting of contaminated AER water and a damaged bronchoscope. These findings highlight point-of-use water quality, device integrity, traceability, and surveillance.

articles.title: Vitiligo-associated variants and genes beyond immune-related loci: A genome-wide association and Mendelian randomization meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Although past genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified over 50 susceptible loci associated with vitiligo risk, few have systematically explored causality among potentially associated variants and genes. To address this, we analyzed summary statistics from 3 large-scale genomic resources, including the Million Veteran Program, United Kingdom Biobank, and FinnGen. Cases were defined using ICD-9 code 709.01 or ICD-10 code L80, including all studies that contributed genome-wide summary statistics and limiting analyses to loci with ≥1 common variant (minor allele frequency ≥1%). METAL was used to conduct a fixed effects inverse variance-weighted meta-analysis with kinship adjustment. Variant-to-gene (V2G) mapping was performed using the Open Targets V2G framework. Potentially causal effects were assessed using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and genome-wide significant protein and expression quantitative trait locus instruments across 16 datasets. Genome-wide significance was defined as P < 5 x 10-8. Among 3,134 vitiligo cases and 1,383,912 controls, 5,482 genome-wide significant variants were identified, mapping to 23 distinct loci. MR found 18 potentially causative genes, 5 of which had not been previously associated with vitiligo: GDF11, ACO2, MEI1, OR2W1-AS1, GABBR1. To our knowledge, this study identifies several previously unreported potentially causal variants and genes associated with vitiligo, as well as pathogenic pathways beyond autoimmunity.

articles.title: Associations of Dietary Patterns with Dementia Burden and Environmental Footprints among Older Adults: A Country-Level Longitudinal Ecological Analysis of 185 Countries and Territories, 1990-2018.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As populations age and food-system pressures intensify, dietary patterns should ideally support both cognitive health and environmental sustainability. However, whether established dietary patterns are associated with both lower dementia burden and smaller environmental footprints remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We examined associations of four dietary patterns with dementia burden and diet-related environmental footprints among older adults worldwide.

METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal ecological analysis of 185 countries and territories at seven time points, 1990-2018. Global Dietary Database data were linked to Global Burden of Disease dementia estimates and life-cycle assessment-derived environmental footprints. Two-way fixed-effects models evaluated 10-year-lagged dementia burden and concurrent environmental footprints. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate.

RESULTS: A 10-point higher modified Planetary Health Diet Index (mPHDI) was associated with a 1.32% lower dementia disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rate 10 years later (95% CI: -2.27, -0.37; q = 0.029), but not dementia prevalence. Mediterranean diet (MED) and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) were not associated with dementia burden, and the Alternative Healthy Eating Index (AHEI) was not significant after correction (-1.14%; q = 0.086). Higher mPHDI, DASH, and AHEI were associated with lower land use (-11.39%, -8.51%, and -9.57%, respectively), and mPHDI with lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (-8.16%). All patterns were associated with greater water scarcity (mPHDI, +3.59%; DASH, +5.57%; AHEI, +7.14%; MED, +2.25%), but none with eutrophication (all q ≥ 0.225). Exploratory analyses found lower dementia prevalence with higher AHEI in South Asia (-2.7%) and greater water scarcity with higher MED in Sub-Saharan Africa (+2.6%) and DASH in high-income countries (+7.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this country-level ecological analysis, mPHDI showed the clearest health and environmental alignment, being associated with a lower dementia DALY rate, GHG emissions and land use, but greater water scarcity. These findings may inform context-specific policies considering healthy aging and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: A Real-World Beta-Cell Preservation Framework in Type 1 Diabetes: Consensus from the T1D Exchange (T1DX-QI).
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) follows a trajectory defined by four stages. Autoantibody screening and disease-modifying therapy (DMT) strategies to preserve beta-cell function are rapidly emerging. Clinical implementation guidance is limited.

METHODS: A national group of pediatric and adult endocrinology experts was formed through invitation by a nonprofit network of over 60 centers. Experts were invited based on their expertise in autoantibody (AAB) screening for T1D and treating children and adults at risk for T1D. The group comprised 22 experts from 13 academic medical centers across the U.S. Group meetings were held from November 2025 to February 2026 to agree on topics for inclusion, form writing groups, and develop evidence-based statements using a targeted literature search.

RESULTS: Topics covered include current guidelines, AAB screening framework, early stage and stage 3 T1D, clinical protocol for T1D screening, treatment and Quality Improvement framework, education, social and behavioral considerations, and the implementation gap. Early identification of T1D through screening allows additional time for families to receive comprehensive diabetes education and appropriate psychological support. This provides a smoother transition to stage 3 disease while reducing hospitalizations, length of stay, and allowing consideration of DMT in early stage or stage 3 T1D. Guidance on real-world clinical implementation of T1D AAB screening and DMT remains limited.

CONCLUSION: This article provides a national consensus from T1DX-QI on the clinical implementation of T1D AAB screening in those at risk and DMT for beta-cell preservation for individuals in stage 2 and new onset stage 3 T1D.

articles.title: Assessing the ecotoxicological impact of drugs used in anesthesia and intensive care: do we have enough data and tools?
US-based Delphi Consensus Study on Adjuvant Radiation Therapy (ART) in Node-Negative Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC).
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: There is a paucity of high-level evidence for adjuvant radiation therapy (ART) in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) creating practice variations. This study provides expert consensus recommendations on patient and tumor selection, timing, duration, dosage, and additional considerations for ART in node-negative CSCC.

METHODS: The Delphi panel included 35 experts in radiation oncology (15), dermatology/Mohs micrographic surgery (9), medical oncology (7), head and neck surgery (3), and surgical oncology (1). Consensus was defined as ≥80% concordance; near-consensus 70-79% concordance.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached to recommend ART when further surgery is not possible, but the tumor has positive gross or histologic/microscopic margins (35/35, 100%). Key consensus or near-consensus recommendations for recommending ART to the tumor bed following negative-margin surgery include: 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence (29/35, 83%) or nodal metastasis (27/35, 77%) ≥ 20%; gross cortical bone/marrow invasion (32/35, 91%); skull base invasion (32/35, 91%); 4 risk factors (RF) (35/35, 100%); 3 RF (30-33/35, 86-94%); PNI ≥ 0.1 mm and one other RF (30/35, 86%); and clinical nerve invasion (31/35, 89%). Immune status influenced ART decision-making (30/35, 86%) with 77% (27/35) more likely to recommend ART for immunosuppressed patients. Consensus was reached to omit ART for pathologic complete response following neoadjuvant immunotherapy (34/35, 97%). Among radiation oncologists, 100% (15/15) agreed the optimal window for ART to the tumor bed is 4-8 weeks and that hypofractionated regimens can be appropriate (12/15, 80%). Consensus was reached for prescription doses of 60-66 Gy in 2 Gy/fx (15/15, 100%) or 50-55 Gy in 2.5 Gy/fx (13/15, 87%), and that superficial radiation and brachytherapy are inappropriate ART modalities for node-negative high-stage CSCC (14/15, 93%). There was no consensus on elective nodal basin irradiation.

CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study provides an expert consensus-based framework to standardize ART for node-negative high-stage CSCC following surgery, informing future guidelines and utilization.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-based diagnosis of Mucormycosis: Candidate biomarkers, analytical challenges, and clinical translation.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Currently, no standard serological test is available for the detection of Mucorales. Mucormycosis is a rapidly progressing angioinvasive infection with a high mortality rate. However, since a diagnostically useful target (1 → 3)-β-D-glucan or Aspergillus galactomannan is not present in Mucorales, a negative result for such targets is a true negative and does not rule out the diagnosis of mucormycosis. PCR detection using PCR for Mucorales can be performed in the early stages, and there is a commercially available quantitative PCR kit in some places, although it is not uniform. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles present in biofluids that play a protective role against the degradation of proteins and nucleic acids and allow for their enrichment prior to measurement. Two studies provided evidence of Mucorales direct culture using extracellular RNA profiles from Rhizopus delemar and proteomic characterization of Mucor lusitanicus EVs, respectively; however, neither resulted in a patient-derived diagnostic test. This structured narrative review separates Mucorales EV direct evidence from extrapolations from other fungi and clinical EV assays. We recommend using a patient-derived discovery workflow involving EV-enriched RNA sequencing, EV-associated DNA analysis, and proteomics, followed by a locked multiplex assay of two or three independent fungal targets. Therefore, molecules from the CotH family, mucoricin, glucoamylase, iron-acquisition factors, and host-response signals should be considered as candidates and should be directly demonstrated within EVs from patients, rather than being considered as known EV markers.

articles.title: Physical Activity and Frailty in patients with Advanced Chronic Liver Disease: A prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Physical frailty is associated with adverse outcomes in advanced chronic liver disease (AdvCLD). Tailoring physical activity prescriptions to minimise frailty is challenging because the volume and intensity of habitual activity remain undefined in AdvCLD. This prospective study aimed to (a) compare device-assessed 24-hour activity profiles in AdvCLD and healthy controls, (b) identify predictors of poor activity and associated frailty, and (c) determine the physical activity profiles required to minimise frailty in AdvCLD.

METHODS: Ambulatory patients with AdvCLD (Birmingham, UK) and healthy controls wore 24-hour GENEActiv® wrist accelerometers for 14-days. Clinical characteristics, frailty and physical activity outcomes (i.e. volume and intensity of most active accumulated/continuous time-periods) were collected.

RESULTS: Forty-three AdvCLD patients (65% male, median age 56, UKELD 52; 53% ArLD) and 17 healthy age/sex-matched controls (59% male, median age 47) were recruited. AdvCLD patients spent more time inactive (56% vs 48%, p=0.005), less in moderate activity (3% vs 7%, p<0.0001), moved less intensively during their most active minute (313.4 mg vs 691.9 mg, p<0.001), and didn't sustain moderate activity (∼slow walking) beyond one minute (30-times less than health controls). Even 'robust' patients with AdvCLD (23%) didn't sustain moderate continuous activity beyond two minutes. ArLD patients were the least active (volume 13.4[4.6] vs 29.2[8.9] mg, p<0.01). Exploratory analysis revealed older age, refractory ascites and Liver Frailty Index were associated with lower levels of physical activity (all p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: Ambulatory patients with AdvCLD, especially ArLD, have drastically reduced volumes of habitual physical activity and didn't sustain moderate intensity beyond one-minute. Short bursts of higher-intensity activity are realistic physical activity goals and are associated with less frailty in AdvCLD.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Physical frailty is prevalent and associated with adverse outcomes in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (AdvCLD). Inactivity drives physical frailty, yet prescribing effective physical activity interventions remains challenging due to unclear volume and intensity parameters. Utilising high resolution, wrist-worn accelerometers and robust frailty measures we show that ambulatory patients with AdvCLD, especially those with alcohol-related liver disease (ArLD), have markedly lower volumes of habitual physical activity and did not sustain more than one minute of moderate intensity activity, (30-fold less than age/sex matched healthy controls). Additionally, in exploratory analysis, the liver frailty index (LFI) predicted activity volume and intensity, supporting its utility as a practical tool to guide physical activity prescription. Refractory ascites, higher frailty indices (e.g. LFI) and of older age were key determinants of low levels of physical activity in our study. Physical activity interventions in AdvCLD should consider short bursts of higher intensity activity rather than relying on prolonged moderate intensity activity targets, which may be unrealistic for the majority of this population. Tailored intensity-focused prescriptions, guided by frailty assessment, which prioritise older patients, those with refractory ascites, and higher LFIs may offer a pragmatic strategy to physical activity interventions in AdvCLD.

CLINICAL TRIALS NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04734496.

articles.title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS).

METHODS: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores).

RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score.

CONCLUSION: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.

articles.title: Brain Abscess Caused by Bifidobacterium spp. in a Previously Healthy Adolescent: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Brain abscesses in children are uncommon but serious conditions. Bifidobacterium species, typically considered commensal organisms of the oral cavity, gastrointestinal tract, and female genital tract, are rarely implicated in invasive infections. We present a case of multiple brain abscesses caused by Bifidobacterium spp. in a previously healthy 11-year-old male, secondary to contiguous spread from chronic left-sided paranasal sinusitis with ethmoid bone erosion. Neuroimaging demonstrated left frontal abscesses with marked perilesional edema, ring enhancement and midline shift, together with opacification of the left maxillary, ethmoid and frontal sinuses. Bifidobacterium spp. was the only organism isolated from both the brain abscess aspirate and the sinus samples. The patient was treated with burr-hole aspiration of the abscesses and same-session endoscopic sinus surgery, followed by six weeks of intravenous crystalline penicillin G. He achieved full clinical recovery without neurological sequelae, with stable residual changes on follow-up MRI. To our knowledge, this is the first detailed case report of a brain abscess caused by Bifidobacterium spp. in a previously healthy pediatric patient. This case highlights the potential of this typically commensal organism to cause serious central nervous system infection via contiguous spread from the paranasal sinuses.

articles.title: Numerous linked cases of acute genotype F hepatitis B virus infections in people living with HIV or on pre-exposure prophylaxis.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: At least 2.7 million people living with HIV are infected with HBV worldwide. Some antiretroviral treatments and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-based Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) protect against HBV infection. However, emerging antiretroviral (ARV) strategies without any activity against HBV may promote spread of this virus in the future. In this context, we studied recent cases of acute HBV infection in people at risk of sexually transmitted infections. Our objective was to better understand HBV circulation and the dynamics of its transmission.

METHODS: This retrospective study included people diagnosed with acute hepatitis B virus infections between 2022 and 2025 in France. The whole HBV genome was amplified and sequenced by NGS for network analysis.

RESULTS: Sixteen men, with a median age of 35 years, were enrolled. Six were living with HIV, including three receiving long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine treatment. Four of the HIV-negative individuals were taking PrEP. Nine had been vaccinated against HBV, and six had anti-HBs antibody titers between 10 and 100 IU/L. Analysis revealed HBV genotype F1b in 14 patients, with very high homology among the viruses. No known immune escape mutations were identified, even in the individuals with anti-HBs antibodies.

CONCLUSIONS: A transmission cluster of HBV F1b genotype was observed in a population at risk of infection. This genotype, which is endemic to Latin Ameria, is rarely detected in France. These findings may serve as a timely reminder of the ongoing circulation of HBV among exposed populations. HBV transmission among vaccinated individuals with positive anti-HBs antibodies raises questions and should be further studied.

articles.title: Probing bacteriophage-induced membrane perturbation in Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida by in-cell solid-state NMR.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida is a major bacterial pathogen of salmonids in aquaculture, and bacteriophage therapy could provide an alternative to antibiotics for its control. Bacteriophage infection of this Gram-negative bacterium begins at the cell surface and involves interactions with outer membrane components including lipopolysaccharides and surface structures such as the A-layer. Although these interactions influence phage adsorption, their impact on bacterial membrane organization remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated membrane dynamics in three strains differing in envelope architecture and phage sensitivity: AS-R3 (A-layer-positive, phage-sensitive), AS-R5 (A-layer-negative, phage-sensitive), and BIM93 (A-layer-negative, phage-insensitive). We used in vivo2H solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance combined with phospholipid and fatty acid analyses. Exogenous perdeuterated palmitic acid enabled efficient membrane labelling in intact bacteria without significantly altering the overall lipid composition. While all strains shared similar phospholipid classes, BIM93 displayed a higher proportion of saturated fatty acids and increased membrane order than AS-R3 and AS-R5. Upon exposure to phage SW69-9, membrane order decreased markedly in the sensitive strains, with a pronounced loss of viability in AS-R5. In contrast, BIM93 maintained membrane organization and high viability, whereas AS-R3 showed an intermediate response with significant membrane perturbation despite limited cell lysis. These results indicate that phage-induced membrane perturbations depend on both phage sensitivity and bacterial envelope architecture. More broadly, they suggest that changes in membrane organization during phage exposure are influenced by surface-associated bacterial structures. This study highlights the role of bacterial surface structures and membrane physical properties in shaping phage-host interactions.

articles.title: HSP70-Mediated Macrophage-Stromal Crosstalk is an Immunopathogenic Driver of Recurrent Implantation Failure.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a major challenge in assisted reproductive technology (ART), affecting a considerable proportion of patients despite multiple transfers of high-quality embryos. Although impaired endometrial receptivity is recognized as a critical contributor to RIF, the molecular mechanisms responsible for establishing a non-receptive endometrial microenvironment remain incompletely understood. The proliferative phase precedes decidualization and subsequent embryo implantation, representing a critical period for endometrial preparation. The endometrium is a highly dynamic tissue composed of diverse epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune cell populations that undergo coordinated remodeling throughout the menstrual cycle; however, the cell type-specific alterations and pathogenic immune-stromal interactions during this phase have not been comprehensively characterized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to dissect the transcriptional landscape of the proliferative-phase endometrium in RIF patients, and validate the key pathways through experimental approaches.

STUDY DESIGN: We for the first time performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of proliferative-phase endometrial tissues from RIF patients and control subjects to characterize cell-type-specific transcriptional alterations and intercellular communication patterns. Peripheral blood scRNA-seq was additionally performed to determine whether immune alterations were tissue-specific or systemic. The impact of HSP70 on the transcriptome of endometrial stromal cells was investigated using RNA sequencing. The production of HSP70 and CCL7 in RIF patients was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The HSP70/CCL7 axis-mediated functional crosstalk between macrophages and endometrial stromal cells was investigated using Transwell assay, QPCR, and SA-β-Gal staining. HSP70-induced activation of PI3K signaling was predicted using RNA sequencing data, then validated through Western blot, ELISA, and Transwell assay.

RESULTS: We identified excessive inflammatory immune infiltration as a microenvironmental hallmark of RIF endometrium, as reflected by increased percentages of T cells, monocytes, and NK cells. This alteration is associated with pathogenic macrophage - stromal crosstalk. Mechanistically, an inflammatory milieu promotes the expression of 70-kDa heat shock protein (HSP70) in macrophages, which stimulates CCL7 production in endometrial stromal cells via PI3K signaling. CCL7 drives the recruitment of multiple types of immune cells that further amplify the inflammation. Neutralization of CCL7 or inhibition of PI3K signaling prevented this pro-inflammatory infiltration. The HSP70-CCL7 axis facilitates endometrial stromal cell senescence and leads to impaired decidualization.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first single-cell transcriptomic atlas of proliferative-phase endometrium in RIF and identifies a pathogenic macrophage-stromal communication network associated with HSP70/CCL7 axis. Our findings reveal that inflammatory microenvironmental remodeling occurs before the window of implantation and contributes to subsequent endometrial dysfunction. Targeting HSP70/CCL7-mediated immune-stromal crosstalk may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for early intervention and prevention of RIF.

articles.title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications.

OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes.

METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events.

RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157).

CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

articles.title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence.

METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence.

RESULTS: Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations.

TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

articles.title: Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients.

METHODS: AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score.

RESULTS: Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSION: In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

articles.title: Association of Air Pollution Exposure and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Consistent evidence indicates that air pollution negatively impacts cardiovascular health. However, the relationship between air pollution and atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear, and exposure measurement error has been a significant concern for prior studies.

OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the association of chronic air pollution exposure and risk of AF.

METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, a community-based cohort study conducted in 6 U.S. metropolitan areas. Concentrations of 4 pollutants (PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and O3) were assessed from 2000-2018 using hierarchical spatiotemporal models that incorporated cohort-specific monitoring to estimate ambient exposure at participants' residences. In Cox regression models, pollution estimates were represented as time-varying exposures, with 2-year rolling averages updated every 30 days. In our primary model, we adjusted for demographics and health behaviors.

RESULTS: Our study included 6618 participants (mean age 62; 53% female). Over 16.5 years median follow-up, we identified 1055 AF events. In our primary model, an interquartile range increment of NO2 (13.5 ppb) was associated with 29% higher risk of AF (hazard ratio 95% CI: 1.00, 1.67). Associations with PM2.5, NOx, and O3 were weaker but also directionally consistent with higher risk.

CONCLUSION: We found evidence linking air pollution exposure to risk of incident AF. These results can be used to inform policy and other public health efforts aimed at alleviating the burden of AF, especially given that NO2 exposure estimates (median 17.3 ppb) fell well below the current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency annual standard of 53 ppb.

articles.title: Myocardial Fibrosis as an Arrhythmogenic Substrate: Integrating Genetics, Imaging and Invasive Electrophysiology for Sudden Death Risk Stratification.
Unipolar Electrograms at the Pulmonary Vein Antrum: Spatial and Directional Heterogeneity with Distinct Postablation Morphologies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disappearance of the near-field S-wave in the unipolar electrogram (U-EGM) is commonly used to assess lesion formation during pulmonary vein (PV) isolation; however, interpretation of U-EGMs in anatomically complex atrial regions remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize spatial, directional, and postablation changes in antral PV U-EGMs, and evaluate the limitations of conventional waveform interpretation.

METHODS: In 15 patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation, U-EGMs were recorded at 116 antral PV sites during sinus rhythm and distal coronary sinus (CS) pacing before and after ablation. U-EGM morphology and R- and S-wave amplitudes were analyzed.

RESULTS: Baseline U-EGMs showed spatial heterogeneity, with a small r and deep S in the right anterior PV antrum transitioning to a positive-dominant morphology (Rs) in the left-lower PV antra. Distal CS pacing altered the activation sequence, causing direction-dependent changes, most prominently in the right PV antrum. After ablation, overall S-wave amplitude decreased from -0.94 ± 0.70 to -0.08 ± 0.55 mV (P<0.001). Residual negative deflections ≥0.5 mV persisted in 18.1% (21/116) of recordings, frequently in association with direction-dependent far-field activity. Newly developed positive deflections ≥1.0 mV were observed in 17/116 sites (14.7%; mean 1.42 ± 0.42 mV), predominantly in the right-sided antra.

CONCLUSIONS: Antral PV U-EGMs frequently represent composites of near- and far-field signals with spatial heterogeneity and direction-dependent variation. Postablation responses are diverse, including S-wave disappearance, residual negativity, often reflecting contributions from overlapping far-field components, and newly developed positive deflections. PV-antral U-EGMs should be interpreted in the context of their composite nature.

articles.title: Practical Approaches to Coronary Venous Ethanol Ablation for Refractory Ventricular Arrhythmias: Technique Selection and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary venous ethanol ablation (CVEA) is a promising alternative for refractory ventricular arrhythmias (VAs); however, it has limited availability, lacks guideline support, and comprises heterogeneous procedural techniques.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes of CVEA in refractory VAs and outline practical techniques of CVEA.

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation at our center between December 2017 and December 2025 were screened; CVEA was performed after unsuccessful endocardial RFA. We performed CVEA using either tip injection, conventional double-balloon, or modified double-balloon techniques based on venous anatomy.

RESULTS: Among 204 consecutive patients undergoing VA ablation, 55 had VAs refractory to endocardial RFA. Of these, 42 with a coronary venous electrogram preceding VA onset by >20 ms underwent CVEA, including 33 with premature ventricular contraction (PVC) and 9 with ventricular tachycardia (VT). Acute success was achieved in 32/33 patients with PVC and all patients with VT. During a median follow-up of 1,024 days, long-term success was achieved in 22 patients with PVC and 5 with VT. No association was observed between intraprocedural findings and long-term recurrence. CVEA-related procedural complications occurred in 13 patients, with no fatal events reported. Exploratory analyses suggested favorable outcomes for the modified double-balloon technique in anatomically selected cases and an association between higher ethanol volume and ethanol-related complications.

CONCLUSION: In patients with VAs refractory to endocardial RFA, CVEA was associated with favorable acute and long-term outcomes, with no fatal complications. Technique selection should be tailored to the venous anatomy, with judicious ethanol volume adjustment.

articles.title: Genetic predisposition to cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicates 5-10% of acute myocardial infarctions (AMI) and remains associated with in-hospital mortality of approximately 40-50%. The clinical predictors established do not fully explain why patients with comparable infarct severity have divergent outcomes, raising the hypothesis that host genetic factors modulate susceptibility to CS.
