Therefore, we conducted this systematic review to synthesize published evidence describing genetic variants associated with the development of CS complicating AMI.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through Jun 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidance. Eligible studies included any study type enrolling adults with AMI and reporting association of any specific genetic variants with CS.

RESULTS: Of 480 records identified, 9 studies met inclusion criteria. Reported variants clustered into five biological pathways: inflammatory/cytokine signaling (TNF-α -308G>A, IFN-γ +874T>A, RANTES/CCL5 -403G>A), lipid metabolism (APOE ε2/ε3/ε4), thrombosis and fibrinolysis (PAI-1/SERPINE1 4G/4 G, MTHFR C677T/A1298C), clonal myeloproliferative disease (JAK2 V617F), and hypercoagulable/antioxidant pathways (protein C/S-related thrombophilia, PON1 Q192R). The APOE ε3/4 genotype and the TNF-2 allele showed the most direct associations with CS incidence and survival, respectively; JAK2 V617F and combined PAI-1/MTHFR variants were reported in severe, thrombus-driven case presentations of CS. RANTES and PON1 genotypes were not associated with CS occurrence, although circulating RANTES levels correlated with CS severity.

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence is limited, but the variants reported to date span inflammatory, lipid, thrombotic, and myeloproliferative pathways, suggesting that genetic susceptibility to CS complicating AMI is polygenic and mechanistically heterogeneous, requiring prospective genetic association studies.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of novel nebulized combination of glycopyrronium, formoterol and budesonide in comparison with metered dose inhaler of glycopyrronium, formoterol and budesonide in COPD - A randomized, double-blind, double-dummy clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are unable to use metered dose inhaler (MDI) or dry powder inhaler effectively and require treatment with nebulized medication. No triple combination is available in nebulized form.

METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind study, 314 patients with COPD received either Glycopyrronium 25 μg/Formoterol Fumarate 20 μg/Budesonide 500 μg (GB/FF/BUD Neb) by nebulization twice daily or Glycopyrronium 7.2 μg, Formoterol Fumarate 5 μg, Budesonide 160 μg MDI (GB/FF/BUD MDI) 2 Puffs twice daily for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) at week 12.

RESULTS: At week 12, GB/FF/BUD Neb was non-inferior (NI) to GB/FF/BUD MDI in change from baseline in trough FEV1 [LS mean (SE) difference -0.00 L (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.04); p < 0.001 for NI with NI margin -0.08 L). At week 12, the between group difference was 0.04 L (95% CI: -0.00 to 0.09; p = 0.070) in 2-h post-dose FEV1 and -0.24 (95% CI: -0.42 to -0.07; p = 0.007) in the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnoea score. There was no difference between treatments in the rescue medication use and change from baseline in trough forced vital capacity. No serious adverse event or death was reported. Overall, adverse events were comparable between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: GB/FF/BUD Neb was non-inferior to GB/FF/BUD MDI in improving lung function evaluated by trough FEV1 in patients with COPD. GB/FF/BUD Neb was found to be safe and well tolerated.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: CTRI/2024/10/075606 (Clinical Trial Registry - India).

articles.title: Association of inhaled corticosteroid use with first Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation in eosinophilic bronchiectasis: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in bronchiectasis patients with eosinophilic inflammation is controversial due to the potential risk of bronchial or pulmonary infection. This study examined the association between ICS use and first Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation across strata of blood eosinophil count (BEC).

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted in patients with bronchiectasis, who were classified according to baseline BEC at cohort entry: HighBEC (≥ 300 cells/μL), InterBEC (100-299 cells/μL), and LowBEC (< 100 cells/μL). ICS use was identified from prescription records, and first P. aeruginosa isolation was defined as the first positive culture for P. aeruginosa from a lower respiratory tract sample after cohort entry. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was used to quantify the risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation associated with ICS use.

RESULTS: Of 1,900 bronchiectasis patients assessed, 719 were analyzed: 194 (27.0%) received ICS, 525 (73.0%) did not. During follow-up, P. aeruginosa was detected in 69 (9.6%) patients. After adjustment for potential confounders and disease severity indicators, ICS use was associated with a significantly higher risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation in patients with BEC ≥ 100 cells/μL, using no ICS as reference (HighBEC: adjusted HR 4.15, 95% CI 1.29-13.38, P = 0.0172; InterBEC: adjusted HR 3.13, 95% CI 1.56-6.27, P = 0.0013), but not in LowBEC patients (adjusted HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.08-2.79, P = 0.4160). Propensity-matched analyses supported these findings.

CONCLUSION: ICS use was associated with an increased risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation in eosinophilic bronchiectasis, suggesting caution when prescribing ICS to these patients.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Toxicities Associated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Clinical Phenotypes, Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Management-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved cancer outcomes, yet cardiovascular toxicities remain difficult to recognize and manage. We review their clinical spectrum, mechanistic evidence, diagnostic work-up, surveillance, and treatment, with particular attention to where evidence is established and where it remains preliminary.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of PubMed through September 2026 and hand-searched reference lists of relevant guidelines, reviews, and primary studies. We prioritized international guidance, systematic reviews, multicenter registries, prospective cohorts, and clinically informative mechanistic studies. Case reports and experimental studies were retained when they addressed questions not covered by higher-level evidence. The review was not protocol driven and did not include duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or a PRISMA flow diagram.

RESULTS: ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity extends beyond myocarditis to temporally associated atherosclerotic events, pericardial disease, and heart failure without demonstrable myocardial inflammation, although causal attribution is less secure for these non-myocarditis phenotypes. Current guidance supports baseline cardiovascular assessment and risk-adapted surveillance, but neither a universal troponin threshold nor an outcome-proven monitoring schedule has been established. Corticosteroids remain first-line treatment for clinically significant ICI myocarditis. Abatacept, ruxolitinib, alemtuzumab, and other intensified regimens are off-label and rest largely on nonrandomized or case-level evidence.

CONCLUSION: Management should combine early recognition, careful exclusion of competing diagnoses, and coordinated oncology-cardiology decision-making. Current evidence does not justify uniform screening thresholds or a standard rescue regimen, and investigational biomarkers, imaging probes, and targeted immunomodulators require prospective validation.

articles.title: A New HOPE for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome: Technique for Primary En-Bloc Heart and Aorta Transplant with Hypothermic Oxygenated Recovery of a DCD Heart.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary heart transplantation for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) has been limited by the scarcity of neonatal donors. Although hypothermic oxygenated machine perfusion (HOPE) enables donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation, previous cannulation techniques sacrificed the donor aortic arch, precluding the reconstruction required for HLHS.

METHODS: A neonatal-sized porcine DCD heart was recovered with the entire thoracic aorta preserved en-bloc using a novel split-cannulation strategy compatible with HOPE. Following 304 minutes of ex situ preservation, the heart-aorta graft was transplanted into a recipient after reconstruction designed to replicate HLHS anatomy. Graft function, haemodynamics, myocardial oedema, and systemic outflow were assessed.

RESULTS: The split-cannulation strategy enabled stable HOPE preservation of the intact heart-thoracic aorta graft throughout ex situ perfusion. Myocardial oedema was minimal (8% weight increase during preservation, 2% above baseline after transplantation). Successful implantation was demonstrated by spontaneous recovery of electrical activity, restoration of sinus rhythm, progressive improvement in cardiac output, and satisfactory ventricular contraction on epicardial echocardiography. No significant pressure gradient was detected across the reconstructed aortic arch.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the technical feasibility of recovering, preserving, and transplanting an intact neonatal-sized DCD heart-thoracic aorta graft using a novel split-cannulation HOPE strategy. By preserving the donor thoracic aorta for arch reconstruction, this technique overcomes a key anatomical barrier to primary DCD heart transplantation for HLHS and provides the technical foundation for clinical translation.

articles.title: Successful Reuse of an Interposition Vein Graft After Free Flap Loss: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract: Free tissue transfer in a previously operated neck with limited recipient-vessel availability remains a major reconstructive challenge and may require interposition vein grafts for venous outflow. The fate of these grafts after flap failure is poorly defined. We report a 77-year-old woman with recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the right upper lip and malar region. Following oncologic resection, reconstruction was performed with a radial forearm free flap. Venous drainage was established using an interposition vein graft between the cephalic vein and the caudal stump of the external jugular vein. Arterial insufficiency developed within 24 hours. Exploration on postoperative day 6 revealed arterial anastomotic thrombosis, while an Acland patency test on the first flap's cephalic vein demonstrated backflow before the venous anastomosis was opened. The graft was retained and reused for venous drainage of a contralateral radial forearm free flap, which remained fully viable. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility and short-term functional success of reusing an interposition vein graft after confirmation of intraoperative patency.

articles.title: Inflammation-Responsive baicalin-delivering glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized bioprosthetic valve for antithrombosis and immunomodulation.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD), a prevalent age-associated condition associated with high mortality, is primarily treated by prosthetic valve replacement. Bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are increasingly preferred in clinical practice owing to their favorable hemodynamic performance and compatibility with transcatheter delivery. However, current glutaraldehyde crosslinking fails to confer antithrombotic, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties, leaving BHVs prone to thrombosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and calcification, all of which accelerate structural valve deterioration (SVD) and shorten their lifespan. Herein, an inflammation-responsive, glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel-functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) was constructed using mussel-inspired catechol chemistry, which integrated a vascular glycocalyx-like layer with baicalin-loaded, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticles. With the introduction of a biocompatible glycocalyx-mimetic layer on the xenogeneic collagenous matrix, BA@ALG-PP exhibited improved antithrombotic and endothelialization performance, which was further confirmed in vivo by the rabbit intravascular implantation experiment. Moreover, the ROS-responsive nanoparticles effectively scavenged oxidative species and enabled stimulus-responsive on-demand release of anti-inflammatory molecule baicalin, thereby modulating local inflammatory responses. Transcriptional analysis of macrophages indicated that BA@ALG-PP regulated the expression of key inflammatory-related genes (Tnfaip3, Hmox1, Stat1, and Saa3) as well as suppressed pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT. Furthermore, BA@ALG-PP demonstrated improved anti-calcification property in the subcutaneous implantation experiments in rats. Collectively, this multifunctional strategy endows BHVs with synergistic antithrombotic, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anti-calcification capabilities, thereby offering a potential strategy for improving BHV performance that warrants further investigation in large animal models and potentially mitigating factors contributing to SVD. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glutaraldehyde-crosslinked bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) suffer from structural valve deterioration driven by thrombosis, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, yet current surface engineering strategies remain functionally limited. This study reports an inflammatory-responsive glycocalyx-mimetic hydrogel functionalized BHV (BA@ALG-PP) engineered via mussel-inspired catechol chemistry. The system integrates non-glutaraldehyde crosslinking, ROS-responsive baicalin release, and endothelial glycocalyx mimicry into a multifunctional platform. BA@ALG-PP demonstrates enhanced antithrombotic performance, accelerated endothelialization, effective ROS scavenging, and macrophage polarization from M1 to M2 phenotype through NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT pathway modulation. Furthermore, it significantly reduces calcification in vivo. This work establishes a comprehensive strategy for BHV crosslinking and surface engineering, offering a clinically translatable strategy to prolong BHV durability and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: A Macrophage-Integrated 3D Spheroid Model Inoculated with Bacteria for Simultaneous Evaluation of Antibacterial Efficacy, Cytotoxicity, and Immunomodulation.
articles.abstract: Conventional antimicrobial-material testing typically relies on separate bacterial assays and two-dimensional (2D) mammalian cell cultures. Although essential as first-line screening tools, these approaches do not capture the three-dimensional (3D) tissue architecture, diffusion constraints, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and innate immune interactions encountered by host-contacting antimicrobial materials. Herein, this study introduces a macrophage-containing 3D spheroid model designed for the simultaneous evaluation of antimicrobial efficacy, host-cell cytotoxicity, and immune responses. The tripartite spheroids comprised DU 145 epithelial cells, THP-1-derived M0 macrophages, and E. coli. The influence of macrophage integration on spheroid architecture was characterized using scanning electron microscopy and scanning ion conductance microscopy, revealing significant biophysical remodeling marked by enhanced matrix compaction and surface densification. These structural alterations were further supported by changes in electrostatic properties and reduced FITC-dextran penetration, indicating enhanced barrier function. Following E. coli challenge, resident macrophages exhibited functional plasticity, polarizing toward an M1-like phenotype to suppress bacterial colonization. The platform was then used to evaluate PA-PQ-37, a cationic antimicrobial coating. In contrast to 2D monolayers, macrophage-containing spheroids retained structural integrity and live-cell esterase activity on the coating while exhibiting reduced recoverable bacterial burden. The model further differentiated the macrophage-associated responses elicited by a cationic polymer, ampicillin, and azithromycin, including inflammatory and pro-resolution-like marker profiles. This animal-free platform complements conventional antibacterial and cytotoxicity assays by supporting integrated evaluation of host-contacting antimicrobial biomaterials in a tissue-like, immune-responsive microenvironment. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Antimicrobial biomaterials are typically evaluated using simplified bacterial assays and 2D mammalian cell cultures, which do not reproduce the tissue architecture, diffusion barriers, extracellular matrix remodeling, or immune surveillance encountered in vivo. This limitation can lead to inaccurate assessment of both antimicrobial efficacy and host-cell compatibility. In this study, we developed a macrophage-integrated 3D infected spheroid model that incorporates resident immune cells into a tissue-like microenvironment for biomaterial evaluation. The model captures macrophage-driven spheroid compaction, matrix remodeling, bacterial restriction, and infection-responsive immune polarization. Using this platform, we demonstrate that cationic PA-PQ-37 coatings appear highly cytotoxic in 2D assays but are well tolerated by macrophage-competent 3D spheroids while retaining antibacterial activity. The model also distinguishes antimicrobial agents with different immunomodulatory profiles, including inflammatory, neutral, and pro-resolution responses. This work provides a physiologically relevant strategy for assessing antimicrobial biomaterials beyond conventional bacterial killing and cytotoxicity endpoints.

articles.title: Clinical and biological characteristics of Caraparu virus (Orthobunyavirus) infection in the Amazonian rainforest: a rare case report in a French military.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caraparu virus (Orthobunyavirus caraparuense) is a poorly described tropical South American arbovirus. Diagnosing acute undifferentiated febrile illness in the Amazon remains a challenge for travel medicine practitioners.

CASE REPORT: We report the case of a French soldier deployed in French Guiana who developed acute self-limited fever and headache associated with mild leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and hepatic cytolysis during a several-day mission in the Amazon rainforest.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the clinical and biological features of this understudied arboviral infection. In patients presenting with a dengue-like syndrome and living in or returning from South America, clinicians should consider arboviral infections other than the main prevalent ones, such as dengue fever.

articles.title: When Is Travel-Health AI Inference Transportable? Mobility-Conditioned Admissibility for Cross-Border Disease Risk and Decision Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for infectious disease surveillance, traveller risk assessment, outbreak forecasting and decision support. Travel creates a distinctive transportability problem because people move between epidemiological, geographic, climatic and healthcare contexts in which the conditions supporting an inference may change rapidly.

METHODS: This conceptual/theoretical methodological-development study was informed by a targeted narrative review of travel medicine, infectious disease surveillance, human mobility, border health, mass gatherings, antimicrobial resistance and health-AI validation literature.

RESULTS: We develop a mobility-conditioned admissibility framework that treats travel as movement across origin, transit, destination and return regimes. Interpretation is conditioned on mobility state, epidemiological regime, exposure history, time-dependent constraints and clinical or biological constraints. Five proposed operational states are retained: supported inference, conditionally transportable inference, active monitoring, restricted interpretation and withholding. The framework also distinguishes low probability from infeasibility and requires preservation of rare but epidemiologically feasible events.

CONCLUSIONS: Model availability and conventional predictive validity do not establish inferential transportability across changing travel contexts. Mobility-conditioned admissibility provides a complementary use-boundary layer for travel health AI by making cross-regime support explicit before outputs are interpreted or released. Its incremental value requires prospective evaluation against calibrated uncertainty, external validation and dataset-shift monitoring.

articles.title: Management of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria with artemisinin-based combination therapy: Factors associated with hospitalization and clinical, biological, and parasitological outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria is a common imported infection in non-endemic countries. We evaluated management, early follow-up, and factors associated with hospitalization at initial presentation among patients treated with artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) in France.

METHODS: We conducted a national retrospective study including adults diagnosed with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria without vomiting, treated with ACTs, and reported to the French National Reference Center for Malaria between 2021 and 2024. The primary endpoint was factors associated with hospitalization at initial presentation (versus outpatient management), assessed using multivariable and mixed-effects logistic regression. Early clinical, biological, and parasitological follow-up (days 1-7) was analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 3,248 patients treated with ACTs, 1,210/3,087 (39.2%) were hospitalized at the time of initial presentation. Fever, immunosuppression, platelet count <84 G/L, parasitemia ≥0.16%, and hemoglobin <12.4 g/dL were independently associated with hospitalization, whereas diagnosis in 2024 was associated with a lower risk. Among the 1,098 (33.8%) patients with available follow-up data, adverse events occurred in <2%. Among patients whose first documented parasitological assessment occurred during days 1-3, the parasite positivity rate was 11/460 (2.4%); no positive parasitemia was observed among those whose first documented assessment occurred during days 4-7 (0/215). In the mixed-effects model, age ≥50 years was also associated with hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: In this large national cohort, an evolving trend toward more frequent outpatient management in real-world practice was observed. The lack of documented early follow-up data in both inpatients and outpatients highlights the need to improve follow-up monitoring and reporting.

articles.title: Oxidative Stress as a Double-Edged Sword in Invertebrate Resistance to WSSV: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) inflicts severe economic losses on global aquaculture and poses a grave threat to the farming of shrimp, crabs, and other invertebrates. This review synthesizes the molecular pathways through which WSSV infection induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in the host; examines the dual role of oxidative stress, wherein moderate ROS contribute to antiviral defense while excessive ROS drive oxidative injury; and, drawing on the threshold effect concept established in mammalian studies, evaluates its applicability and limitations as a working hypothesis in invertebrate WSSV infection models. We consolidate the relatively well-characterized oxidative stress response pathways in penaeid shrimp and, based on the limited evidence available, explore potential differences in crabs, mollusks, and other taxa-highlighting the near absence of research on non-shrimp groups. We further identify key challenges and controversies in the field, including incomplete elucidation of signaling pathways, the disconnect between experimental conditions and aquaculture environments, and pronounced species imbalance in research coverage. Finally, we prospect future research directions encompassing multi-omics dissection of molecular networks, application of antioxidants and ferroptosis modulators, and selective breeding for disease-resistant stocks, thereby providing a reference framework for antiviral research and disease management in aquaculture.

articles.title: EARLY STROKE AFTER AORTIC ARCH REPAIR: COMPARATIVE AND PROPORTIONAL META-ANALYSES OF OPEN, HYBRID, AND TOTAL ENDOVASCULAR STRATEGIES.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna. Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261461659).

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.46-8.58; P=.292; I2=52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and Zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair.

CONCLUSION: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly non-comparative. Treatment should be individualised according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

articles.title: ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device as a Cost-Dominant Limb-Salvage Strategy for No-Option Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: A Decade and Half, Single-Centre Cohort Study with Health Economic and Q-TWiST Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) a median €88,820 per patient; long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist SCBD is lacking.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with non-reconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary centre (January 2008-June 2025). Primary endpoints were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness versus primary amputation, and Q-TWiST. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

FINDINGS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischaemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (HRs 1·70, 1·80, 1·71; all P ≤ ·012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = ·008). 90-day rental (€1,373/patient) reduced total expenditure six-fold versus primary amputation (€5·3M vs €30·8M), saving €76,500/patient. Q-TWiST yielded a gain of 3·37 QALYs per patient; ICER €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

INTERPRETATION: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a six-fold reduction in costs versus primary amputation, +3·37 QALYs/patient, and an ICER of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-centre cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for non-reconstructible CLTI.

articles.title: Pregnancy after renal transplant: Truth or dare? A retrospective analysis from a tertiary care centre in India.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) often face fertility challenges due to hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis disruption. While pregnancy is rare during dialysis, kidney transplantation restores fertility potential, albeit with increased maternal and foetal risks. This study evaluates maternal and foetal outcomes in post-renal transplant pregnancies at a tertiary care centre.

METHODOLOGY: A retrospective study was conducted at our hospital on female renal transplant recipients between January 2010 and January 2024. All patients who conceived post-transplant were included. Clinical data were extracted from hospital electronic medical records, including transplant details, immunosuppression, antenatal course, and pregnancy outcomes.

RESULTS: Out of 215 female transplant recipients, 11 conceived post-transplant (5.1%). Among them, 9 pregnancies resulted in live births, 1 in stillbirth, and 1 ended in abortion. Mean age at pregnancy was 28.6 ± 1.74 years. All patients underwent ABO-compatible transplantation. Induction therapy included ATG (54.5%), basiliximab (27.3%), or none (18.2%). All patients were maintained on triple immunosuppression with tacrolimus, prednisone (≤10 mg/day), and azathioprine. Complications included maternal viz. gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, preterm delivery, and fetal viz. stillbirth and fetal growth restriction (FGR). Fetal outcomes included 81.8% live births, 9.1% intrauterine death, and 9.1% abortion. Graft outcomes showed stable function in 45.5%, dysfunction in 54.5%, and graft loss in 36.3%.

CONCLUSION: Pregnancy after kidney transplantation is feasible and frequently successful, though associated with maternal and foetal complications. Meticulous multidisciplinary care and regular monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes and preserve graft function.

articles.title: Clarification of a Rare and Unexpected Breast Finding on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET scan.
Fecal Microbiota Transfer for Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection: A Retrospective Single-Center Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is the leading cause of healthcare-associated infectious diarrhea. Despite high initial response rates to antibiotic therapy, recurrence occurs in approximately 20% of patients. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has emerged as an effective treatment option for multiple recurrences, demonstrating high efficacy and a favorable safety profile. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of FMT in patients with recurrent CDI (rCDI).

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 75 patients who underwent FMT for rCDI between November 2016 and January 2026 after experiencing at least two recurrences despite standard antibiotic therapy were included. Donor screening was performed according to the requirements of the German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM). Following CDI-directed antibiotic pretreatment, FMT was administered either by colonoscopy, oral capsules, or a combination of both. Patients were followed for three months. The primary endpoint was the absence of diarrhea as a surrogate marker for rCDI, including a predefined subgroup analysis of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

RESULTS: Follow-up data were available for 65 patients, of whom 56 (86.1%) achieved sustained clinical remission. Patients with concomitant IBD (n=15) showed a comparable response rate (86.7%). The route of FMT administration had no significant impact on treatment outcome. Overall, FMT was well tolerated, with only four patients (5.3%) reporting predominantly self-limiting adverse events.

CONCLUSION: FMT is a highly effective and safe treatment for recurrent CDI, including in multimorbid patients and those with concomitant IBD.

articles.title: Impact of Anxiety Levels in Women with Late Preterm Labor on Parenting and Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the impact of anxiety levels on maternal parenting and breastfeeding self-efficacy among women with late preterm labor.

STUDY DESIGN: This cross-sectional study was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 at a state hospital in southern Türkiye, involving 217 women who met the inclusion criteria. The data were collected using a demographic form, State Anxiety Scale, Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy tool, and Modified Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form for mothers of preterm infants. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics such as number, percentage, mean, and standard deviation, as well as independent t-test, one-way analysis of variance, correlation, and regression analysis.

RESULTS: The mothers' Modified Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form (BSES-SF) score showed a weak positive correlation with the Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy Tool score, but a moderate negative association with their State Anxiety Scale score. A significant negative weak correlation was observed between the Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy Tool and State Anxiety Scale scores (p<0.05). The regression analysis revealed that exclusive breastfeeding, having an income equal to or greater than expenses, and breastfeeding the baby within the first 30 minutes after birth (β=0.128) were associated with higher breastfeeding self-efficacy. Conversely, the State Anxiety Scale total score was associated with lower breastfeeding self-efficacy. Additionally, being multiparous and having a history of late preterm birth in a previous pregnancy were significantly associated with higher maternal parenting self-efficacy. In contrast, the mean State Anxiety Scale total score was negatively correlated with the Perceived Maternal Parenting Self-Efficacy Tool score.

articles.title: Empirical Evaluation of the Repertory Rubric "Anger, Consoled, when" Using Likelihood Ratio-based Prognostic Factor Analysis in Individualized Homeopathic Practice.
articles.journal: Homeopathy : the journal of the Faculty of Homeopathy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rubric "Anger, consoled, when" is described in several homeopathic repertories and materia medica sources, but its prognostic relevance has not been quantitatively examined. This study applied likelihood ratio (LR)-based prognostic factor research (PFR) to evaluate its real-world utility in individualized homeopathic practice, aiming to bridge traditional knowledge with evidence-based validation.

METHODS: This analytical epidemiological longitudinal study prospectively documented clinical outcomes in routine outpatient care at D. N. De Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, India. Adult patients receiving individualized homeopathic treatment were followed for 3 months. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Outcome Related to Impact on Daily Living (ORIDL) scale, with scores ≥ + 2 indicating clinically meaningful improvement. Remedy-specific LR+ and LR- with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using 2 × 2 contingency tables. LR+ indicates the certainty that the given medicine will work in the given condition; LR- indicates the relationship between a symptom and a medicine if the symptom is absent. In addition, phi (Φ) coefficient statistics were applied to quantify the strength and direction of symptom-medicine associations, providing complementary effect-size information that enhanced interpretation of the prognostic relationships.

RESULTS: From 1,740 screened patients, 1,699 (97.5%) completed follow-up (mean age: 42.3 years; 62% female). A total of 73 homeopathic medicines were prescribed. Chamomilla exhibited the highest prognostic rule-in value (LR+ 2.0, 95% CI: 1.6 to 2.5), whereas Natrum muriaticum demonstrated the strongest symptom-remedy association (Φ = 0.118). Moderate associations (LR+ 1.5-1.9) occurred with Kalium iodatum, Natrum muriaticum, Arsenicum album, Natrum carbonicum, Sepia officinalis, and Staphysagria macrosperma. Phi analysis confirmed significant positive correlations (Φ = 0.12-0.18, p < 0.01) for Natrum muriaticum, Chamomilla, Sepia officinalis and Arsenicum album; Causticum showed a negative association (Φ = - 0.11, p = 0.03).

CONCLUSION: The LR-PFR empirically validated rubric "Anger, consoled, when", identifying Chamomilla as the prognostically strongest remedy, whereas Natrum muriaticum demonstrated the strongest statistical association with the rubric. Integrating phi into PFR enhanced the interpretation of association magnitude, thereby informing evidence-based repertory updates and clinical decision-making in homeopathy.

articles.title: Athyreosis and Thyroid Hormone Signaling: A System-Based Framework for Long-Term Endocrine Health.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.abstract: Thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine therapy are definitive treatments for Graves' disease, toxic nodular disease, and differentiated thyroid cancer. With improving survival rates and expanding indications for definitive therapy, a growing population is living for decades in a state of athyreosis requiring lifelong thyroid hormone replacement. Current management strategies largely emphasize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone targets and oncological surveillance, yet the long-term metabolic and physiological implications of chronic athyreosis remain incompletely explored. The potential longevity implications of long-term athyreosis are examined through a system-based framework integrating hormonal balance, mitochondrial regulation, metabolic adaptation, skeletal and cardiovascular health, and inflammatory signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from endocrinology, metabolism, oncology, and aging research to evaluate physiological differences between endogenous thyroid hormone secretion and pharmacological replacement in athyreotic patients. Particular attention is given to tissue-level triiodothyronine availability, deiodinase activity, and downstream bioenergetic effects. Athyreotic patients lack intrinsic thyroidal triiodothyronine secretion and depend entirely on the peripheral conversion of levothyroxine to generate circulating and intracellular triiodothyronine. Emerging evidence suggests that levothyroxine monotherapy may not fully replicate physiological thyroid hormone dynamics in all individuals, potentially influencing mitochondrial biogenesis, resting energy expenditure, body composition, bone turnover, and cardiovascular remodeling. In thyroid cancer survivors, chronic thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression introduces additional considerations for skeletal and cardiac outcomes. Patients treated for autoimmune thyroid disease may also exhibit persistent immune dysregulation despite gland ablation. Athyreosis represents a distinct and permanent endocrine state with implications extending beyond biochemical euthyroidism. A system-based perspective that considers mitochondrial resilience, cardiometabolic integrity, skeletal preservation, and inflammatory tone may enhance long-term management strategies for this expanding survivorship population. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the impact of various thyroid hormone replacement paradigms on functional aging and longevity outcomes.

articles.title: Rapid versus slow puncture in endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy: a multicenter randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy (EUS-LB) is increasingly used for hepatic histologic assessment; however, optimal technical approaches remain undefined. This prospective, multicenter clinical study aimed to compare tissue acquisition and safety between the rapid and slow puncture techniques for EUS-LB.

METHODS: This was a multicenter randomized crossover study. Patients undergoing EUS-LB were randomized to receive both rapid puncture and slow puncture techniques in alternating sequence during the same session. The primary outcomes were the number of complete portal tracts (CPTs) and total specimen length (TSL). The secondary outcomes were diagnostic adequacy and adverse events. Linear mixed models and generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate the technical performance.

RESULTS: A total of 62 specimens were analyzed. Compared with the conventional slow puncture technique, rapid puncture significantly increased CPTs (mean difference 2.39; 95%CI 1.50-3.27), as well as TSL (mean difference 15.19 mm; 95%CI 9.65-20.74), with corresponding improvements in diagnostic adequacy (odds ratio 16.27, 95%CI 2.41-109.97). Time period and center were not statistically significantly associated with the outcomes. No severe adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSION: The modified rapid puncture technique was associated with improved specimen quality in EUS-LB. These findings support its potential utility in clinical practice; however, further validation in larger and more diverse populations is warranted.

articles.title: Serrated polyp detection rates beyond adenoma detection rate for postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer: findings from the SCREESCO trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between serrated polyp detection rates, including proximal serrated polyp detection rate (PSPDR), and postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains unestablished. We investigated PCCRC incidence and characteristics, and explored associations of PSPDR and adenoma detection rate (ADR) with PCCRC in colonoscopy- and fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based screening within the Screening of Swedish Colons (SCREESCO) trial.

METHODS: Data from participants who underwent colonoscopy in the colonoscopy and FIT arms were analyzed. PCCRC, defined as colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed >6 months after a colonoscopy that did not detect CRC, was identified through linkage with cancer registries. Associations between PSPDR and PCCRC incidence were assessed using Cox models.

RESULTS: Of 9982 and 5875 individuals in the colonoscopy and FIT arms, PCCRC was identified in 20 and 17 individuals, with 3-year PCCRC rates of 5.9% (3/51) and 3.5% (4/115), respectively. Compared with screening-detected CRC, PCCRC more often involved right-sided location and advanced stage. The 5-year cumulative incidence of PCCRC was 0.16% (95%CI 0.10%-0.27%) and 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.15%) when colonoscopies were performed by endoscopists with low vs. high PSPDR (<10% vs. ≥10%), respectively. Among endoscopists with high ADR, 5-year PCCRC incidence was 0.13% (95%CI 0.04%-0.32%) vs. 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.16%) for those with low vs. high PSPDR, respectively. Within this group, PCCRC incidence over 8 years decreased as PSPDR increased (hazard ratio per percentage-point increase, 0.90; 95%CI 0.82-1.00; P = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the limited number of PCCRC events, this study suggests that PSPDR provides complementary information beyond ADR for identifying colonoscopies with higher PCCRC incidence.

articles.title: Branch-selective phonon localization through correlated sublattice disorder.
articles.journal: Journal of physics. Condensed matter : an Institute of Physics journal
articles.abstract: Multiband lattices possess an internal degree of freedom absent from one-band Anderson models. At each Bloch wavenumber the acoustic and optical eigenvectors distribute their motion differently over the sublattices of the unit cell, and manufactured phononic lattices acquire tolerance-induced randomness separately on each sublattice, with tolerances that can be correlated within a cell. This paper develops a branch-resolved sublattice-participation formulation of weak-disorder localization for a grounded diatomic chain, building on the Lyapunov-exponent theory of correlated multicomponent media. To leading order in the disorder strength and inside an isolated passband, the localization exponent of each branch equals the disorder covariance projected through the squared Bloch participation weights of that branch and divided by the squared group velocity. The intra-cell cross-correlation enters this law through the backscattering phase between the two sublattices. An exact finite-chain eigensolution, branch-resolved random eigenvalue statistics and the weak-disorder law are derived and compared with transfer-matrix and Monte Carlo computation, which confirms the prefactor of the law across both band interiors. Moving a fixed disorder strength from one sublattice to the other reverses which branch localizes more strongly, so disorder placement becomes a design variable. Finite-chain eigenvalue statistics and localization weight the same correlation with different phase factors. Anticorrelated disorder therefore reduces eigenvalue scatter across a whole band, and it reduces localization near the zone centre and enhances it near the zone edge. The ensemble-mean response carries the same projection as a decoherence signature that depends on disorder placement. Disorder covariance in sublattice space thereby becomes a quantitative control for multiband phononic media, with direct extensions to more sublattices and to two dimensions.

articles.title: KDM-Net: a large-kernel and bi-mamba integrated network for 12-lead atrial arrhythmia classification.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Automatic recognition of atrial arrhythmias is important for early clinical screening and computer-aided diagnosis. Distinguishing atrial fibrillation from atrial flutter remains challenging because of their similar electrocardiographic manifestations andhigh risk of misclassification. This study aimed to develop an effective model for atrial arrhythmia classification with improved multi-lead feature utilization, long-range temporal modeling, and cross-patient generalization.

APPROACH: We propose KDM-Net, which takes12-lead electrocardiogram signals as input. The network employs a large-kernel K module to enhance the perception of waveform morphology and rhythm patterns, a D module to recalibrate and fuse multi-lead features, and a bidirectional Mamba-based M module tomodel long-range temporal dependencies. KDM-Net was evaluated on the combined CUSPH and PTB-XL dataset under an inter-patient protocol.

MAIN RESULTS: In five-fold cross-validation, KDM-Net achieved an average accuracy and F1-score of 96.04% and89.21%, respectively. On the independent patient-level test set, the accuracy and F1-score were 96.41% and 88.31%, respectively. On the CinC 2020 external test set, the model achieved an accuracy and F1-score of 91.14% and 80.41%, respectively. KDM-Netoutperformed several representative models in comparative experiments.

SIGNIFICANCE: KDM-Net effectively integrates multi-lead spatial information and long-range temporal dependencies, demonstrating strong recognition performance and promising cross-patientgeneralization. It provides an effective solution for the intelligent diagnosis of atrial arrhythmias.

articles.title: Prevalence, management, and outcomes of urinary tract infections in older adults living in care homes versus older adults living outside care homes in the UK: a propensity score-matched case-control analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, rising drug-resistant urinary tract infections (UTIs) affect older populations disproportionally. We aimed to assess the incidence, management, and patient outcomes of UTIs in English care homes.

METHODS: Using linked primary, secondary, social care, and pathology data covering 2·5 million patients in London between 2018 and 2023, we matched older adults with UTIs living in care homes with older adults living outside care homes using propensity scores. We performed a time-series analysis of incidence and compared urine culture turnaround time and results (including antimicrobial resistance). We assessed UTI-related patient outcomes, including death, complications, recurrent infection, and antibiotic re-prescription within 60 days, using generalised estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and other risk factors.

FINDINGS: We identified 91 501 UTI cases, including 6648 (7·3%) in care homes. In care homes, 4678 (70·4%) of the 6448 UTIs occurred in women and 3779 (56·8%) involved individuals aged 85 years or older. The older adults living in care homes were older (median age: 86 years [IQR 80-91] vs 76 years [71-83]) and more frequently White (70·3% vs 56·7%) than older adults living outside care homes. The incidence rate of community-acquired UTIs was 1909·4 per 100 000 person-months in care homes (increasing by 3·7 [95% CI 0·8-6·6] per month), as compared with 543·5 outside care homes (decreasing by 1·3 [-1·8 to -0·7] per month). Urine cultures were used less (1366 [20·5%] of 6648 [95% CI 19·6-21·5] vs 24 699 [29·1%] of 84 853 [28·8-29·4]), were more likely to be polymicrobial (suggesting contamination; 416 [30·4%] of 1366 [28·1-32·9] vs 4325 [17·5%] of 24 699 [17·0-18·0]), and had a longer turnaround time (52·9% turnaround in 1 day [50·3-55·6] vs 66·2% [65·6-66·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Escherichia coli UTIs had higher resistance to trimethoprim (46·4% [95% CI 41·0-51·9] vs 32·0% [30·9-33·1]) and nitrofurantoin (7·5% [4·9-10·8] vs 2·4% [2·0-2·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Care home cases had significantly worse 60-day outcomes, with higher risk of death (1·99 [95% CI 1·67-2·36]; p<0·001), presenting to general practitioners (1·38 [1·01-1·89]; p=0·042) and to hospitals (1·15 [1·01-1·32]; p=0·041) with complications, recurrent infections (1·22 [1·08-1·36]; p=0·001), and antibiotic re-prescription (1·11 [1·01-1·21]; p=0·024).

INTERPRETATION: Older adults residing in care homes had higher UTI infection burden and worse clinical outcomes than matched older adults residing outside care homes. Possible explanatory factors include inadequate care, discordant prescribing decisions, and disconnect with diagnostic capabilities, in addition to the exacerbating effects on infection management during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings highlight the need for improvement in infection management in care home settings.

FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research; Wellcome Trust; Fleming Initiative.

articles.title: Thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist simedeutirom (HSK31679) for Chinese patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a 52-week, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simedeutirom is a selective thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist that has previously been shown to reduce hepatic fat content in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. We assessed the efficacy and safety of simedeutirom in patients of Asian descent with biopsy-confirmed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and F2 or F3 fibrosis.

METHODS: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial was conducted at 42 clinical sites in China. Adults (aged 18-74 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH, a non-alcoholic fatty liver disease activity score (NAS) of at least 4, F2 or F3 fibrosis, and MRI-proton density fat fraction liver fat content of at least 8% were randomly assigned (1:1:1) by block randomisation (block size of six; no stratification) via a centralised web-based system to receive once-daily simedeutirom 80 mg, simedeutirom 160 mg, or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants and study personnel were masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was MASH improvement (ie, two-point or more reduction in NAS, one-point or more improvement in hepatocellular ballooning, and no increase in steatosis score) without worsening of fibrosis (ie, no increase in fibrosis stage) at week 52. Efficacy was analysed in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose and had at least one efficacy assessment after baseline; participants without liver biopsy data after treatment or who used prohibited medications affecting efficacy were considered non-responders. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06168383) and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Jan 16, 2026, 186 participants were randomly assigned (62 per group). In the full analysis set (n=179), the median age was 42·0 years (IQR 35·0-54·0), 116 (65%) participants were men, and 63 (35%) were women. 22 (37%) of 59 participants in the 80 mg group, 18 (30%) of 60 in the 160 mg group, and six (10%) of 60 in the placebo group had MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. ORs versus placebo were 4·87 (95% CI 1·76-13·48; p=0·0023) in the 80 mg group and 5·24 (1·74-15·72; p=0·0032) in the 160 mg group, with absolute differences of 27·3 percentage points (95% CI 12·2-41·1) and 20·0 percentage points (5·7-33·6), respectively. Grade 3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in three (5%) of 61 participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, five (8%) of 62 in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) of 62 in the placebo group; no individual grade 3 event affected more than one participant, and no grade 4-5 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred. Serious adverse events occurred in three (5%) participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, four (6%) in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) in the placebo group; none were treatment related. No deaths or adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred.

INTERPRETATION: Simedeutirom led to higher rates of MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis than placebo after 52 weeks, warranting further investigation in phase 3 trials.

FUNDING: Haisco Pharmaceutical Group.

articles.title: South Africa shifts away from salbutamol-only asthma relief.
Raphe nuclei in cognition: A network-level framework for behavioral-state control.
articles.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires organisms to maintain, update, and switch between behavioral states as environmental conditions change. The raphe nuclei (RN), best known as a major source of forebrain serotonin, have long been linked to arousal, inhibition, patience, affect, and flexibility, but these functions have often been considered separately. Here, we argue that recent advances in circuit tracing, cell-type-specific manipulation, high-resolution neuroimaging and neurostimulation, and computational modeling support a more integrated view in which RN are embedded within distributed cortico-subcortical and neuromodulatory networks. Across species, RN activity tracks environmental statistics such as value, uncertainty, threat, and reward context and contributes to transitions between motivational and cognitive states. We propose a network-level framework in which RN regulate when behavioral states should persist, update, or switch.

articles.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells-derived pancreatic islet organoids (PIOs) hold promise for treating type 1 diabetes, but poor post-transplant survival due to inadequate vascularization remains a major challenge. Here, we generated vascularized PIOs (VPIOs) by co-culturing PIOs with blood vessel organoids (BVOs), resulting in integrated structures with BVOs-derived capillary networks that penetrate into the islet structures. These blood vessels structurally exhibit fenestrations characteristic of islet-specific endothelium and carry a molecular signature of organotypic vasculature. β cells within the VPIOs display partially enhanced maturation and greater resistance to hypoxia and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Following subcutaneous transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs exhibit markedly improved survival, establish vascular connections with the host circulation, and restore long-term normoglycemia. Our work presents a strategy for generating vascularized islet organoids that enhances β cell maturation and tissue-specific blood vessel specification in vitro and, critically, improves graft survival and function in vivo.

articles.title: Structural analysis of de novo-designed binders targeting the closed state of HSP90.
articles.abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) assists the folding and maturation of numerous signaling proteins and is an important therapeutic target. Most HSP90 inhibitors target the ATP-binding pocket and disrupt ATP-induced closure, whereas inhibitors targeting the closed state have not been developed. Here, we report de novo-designed protein binders that selectively recognize closed HSP90. Two binders, H2 and H4, have similar folds and affinities for HSP90 but distinct binding kinetics. Cryo-EM structures of HSP90 complexes with H2 and H4 revealed high accuracy of the BindCraft predictions. H2 and H4 compete with p23 at one, but not both, symmetrical p23-binding sites. In HEK293T cells, H2 induced a reduced heat shock response compared with the ATP-site inhibitor 17-DMAG while reducing levels of CDK4, providing functional evidence for HSP90 inhibition. These binders provide tools for probing HSP90 function and potential leads for developing closed-state HSP90 inhibitors.

articles.title: Disease progression in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis treated with disease-modifying therapies: a multicenter real-world experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is a progressive disease associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. The multimodal progression criteria proposed in 2025 integrate clinical, biomarker, and functional parameters to improve disease monitoring. However, evidence regarding their applicability in real-world practice remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter ambispective observational cohort study including 68 consecutive patients with ATTR-CM receiving disease-modifying therapies across hospitals in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain. Disease progression was assessed by comparing baseline status with the follow-up assessment available within the first 12 months after treatment initiation; no data obtained after month 12 were used to establish progression status. Progression was defined as abnormalities in at least two domains (clinical, biomarker, and functional). To assess the temporal association with subsequent cardiovascular events, a 12-month landmark analysis was performed among patients who were alive and free from the composite cardiovascular event at month 12 and had subsequent follow-up.

RESULTS: Disease progression according to the 2025 criteria was observed in 42.4% of evaluable patients. The biomarker domain was the most frequently affected (62.1%), followed by the clinical (42.4%) and functional (37.9%) domains. Patients with progression had significantly higher baseline NT-proBNP levels and worse renal function. In multivariable analysis, baseline NT-proBNP was independently associated with progression (OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.15-5.43; p=0.021). Among the 66 patients evaluable for progression, the composite cardiovascular event was more frequent in progressors than in non-progressors during overall follow-up (60.7% vs. 15.8%; p<0.001). In the 12-month landmark analysis (n=40), first-year progression was associated with a higher incidence of subsequent cardiovascular events (42.9% vs. 7.7%; HR 5.88, 95% CI 1.19-29.19; p=0.030).

CONCLUSIONS: Progression according to the 2025 multimodal criteria was common among ATTR-CM patients despite disease-modifying therapy. Progression identified during the first year was associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events occurring after month 12 in an exploratory landmark analysis. The biomarker domain, particularly NT-proBNP and renal function, was relevant for identifying progression. These criteria may be useful for longitudinal monitoring and risk stratification in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Minding the Gap: Follow-Up Cardiovascular Care After Clonal Hematopoiesis Detection.
Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS).

METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support.

RESULTS: A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.

articles.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma in Turkey: A nationwide health system database analysis of clinical patterns and survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. However, comprehensive population-level data describing etiologic patterns, treatment exposure, healthcare utilisation, and survival remain limited in many countries. This study aimed to characterise the national burden, care patterns, and outcomes of HCC in Turkey.

METHODS: We performed a nationwide, real-world analysis of adult patients diagnosed with HCC between 2016 and 2024 using administrative health data. Cases were identified by an administrative case definition requiring at least three separate records of ICD-10 codes C22, C22.0, or C22.9; at least one C22.0 code was not required, so HCC could not be confirmed at the individual level. Baseline comorbidities were restricted to conditions recorded on or before the date of diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, underlying liver disease, etiologic factors, treatment exposure, and the level and type of diagnosing institution were assessed. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. To reduce immortal-time bias, treatment exposure was analysed in a three-month landmark cohort; because treatment dates were unavailable, this reduces but does not eliminate the bias. Multivariable Cox regression was performed within the same cohort.

RESULTS: A total of 13,674 patients (64.6% male; median age 64 years, IQR 55-73) were included, of whom 61.4% had died at the data cutoff; median follow-up was 53.0 months. The median OS was 13.2 months (95% CI 12.1-14.5), with 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS of 50.9%, 41.1%, and 36.9%; because patients dying before three qualifying records accumulated could not enter the cohort, these estimates apply to patients meeting the case-identification algorithm and are likely to overstate population survival. OS was markedly longer in women than in men (median 50.9 vs 8.2 months), and longer in patients without cirrhosis recorded at diagnosis than in those with cirrhosis (18.5 vs 9.0 months; both P < 0.001). Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology (29.4%); among mutually exclusive categories, NAFLD-associated HCC had the most favourable survival (5-year OS 61.0%) and alcohol-related HCC the least (median 8.8 months), while HBV-HDV co-infection was associated with longer survival than HBV mono-infection (58.2 vs 12.0 months; P < 0.001), a difference that persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and cirrhosis; no specific etiology could be assigned in 56.1% of patients. Sensitivity analyses restricting etiologic ascertainment to codes recorded within 3 months before to 3 months after diagnosis, or incorporating viral serology, attenuated the survival of the specific viral etiologies, indicating survival-dependent ascertainment. In a multivariable Cox model fitted in the three-month landmark cohort (n = 8958), older age, male sex, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy were associated with higher mortality (all P < 0.001), with time-varying associations for age, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy. The association of local therapy with mortality was not constant over follow-up (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.72-0.85 during 0-24 months after the landmark and 1.22, 1.04-1.43 thereafter); the overall association was no longer evident after liver transplantation was excluded from the local-therapy category. Care was highly centralised within secondary and tertiary institutions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide analysis, HCC in Turkey was characterised by limited OS and pronounced sex-based disparities, with survival differing by cirrhosis status and recorded etiology; etiologic ascertainment was itself survival-dependent, so these contrasts describe recorded categories. Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology, underscoring the continued importance of HBV prevention, screening, and surveillance, while HCV, HDV, alcohol-related and metabolic liver disease accounted for smaller recorded proportions; temporal trends in etiology were not analysed. Because tumour stage and liver function were unavailable, the treatment-survival associations are descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. Efforts focused on HBV control, earlier detection, risk-based surveillance of patients with cirrhosis, and improved referral pathways may improve population-level outcomes.

articles.title: Cryopreservation protocol and antioxidant supplementation determine post-thaw functional quality of goat sperm.
articles.abstract: Goat sperm cryopreservation remains a major challenge because freeze-thaw procedures induce structural and functional damage that compromises post-thaw sperm quality. Although antioxidant supplementation has been widely investigated to reduce oxidative stress, its effectiveness remains inconsistent and may depend on the cryopreservation protocol. This study was conducted in two phases. In Phase 1, three antioxidants-ascorbic acid (2.5, 5.0 and 10.0 mg/mL), cysteamine (50, 100 and 200 μM), and glycine (5, 10 and 20 mM)-were screened using semen from six bucks (three Alpine-French and three Murciano-Granadina). Post-thaw assessments via the AndroVision® CASA system (Minitube, Germany; software version 0.26), viability (eosin-nigrosine staining), plasma membrane integrity (HOST), and thermoresistance test (TTR) revealed no statistically significant effects of antioxidant treatment on motility and kinematic parameters (P > 0.05). However, numerical differences favored glycine at 20 mM, which yielded the highest estimated marginal means for total motility (60.35 ± 3.51%), progressive motility (59.97 ± 3.55%), and fast motility (47.74 ± 3.98%), surpassing the control group. The TTR proved more discriminative: ascorbic acid at 10.0 mg/mL produced the most severe decline, whereas cysteamine at 100 μM achieved the highest values among treated groups. In Phase 2, glycine at 20 mM-selected for its numerically favorable kinematic profile-was validated in an independent experiment comparing two cryopreservation protocols: Programmable and Manual. Evaluations included CASA motility and kinematic parameters, plasma membrane integrity, acrosome integrity, mitochondrial activity, thermoresistance test, cold shock resistance test, and gene expression analysis (SOD1, HSP70, CAT). Results demonstrated that the cryopreservation protocol exerted a significantly greater effect than antioxidant supplementation. The manual protocol consistently produced superior values for total motility, progressive motility, fast motility, kinematic parameters (VCL, VAP, VSL, BCF, ALH, HAC), acrosome integrity, and cold shock resistance (P < 0.05). In contrast, glycine supplementation at 20 mM did not significantly affect any evaluated parameter (P > 0.05), nor did the Protocol × Antioxidant interaction. Relative expression of SOD1, HSP70, and CAT did not differ between protocols, treatments, or their interaction (P > 0.26). Overall, these findings indicate that, under the conditions evaluated, optimization of the cryopreservation protocol had a greater impact on post-thaw sperm functional quality than glycine supplementation, highlighting the importance of optimizing cryopreservation procedures before evaluating antioxidants as complementary strategies.

articles.title: Swanson's theory of caring applied to mechanical ventilation weaning in the ICU: Humanizing care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the scientific evidence on the application of Swanson's Theory of Caring in the process of invasive mechanical ventilation weaning in Intensive Care Units (ICU), identifying nursing interventions that correspond to Swanson's five theoretical processes (knowing, being with, doing for, enabling, and maintaining belief) and assessing their implications for clinical practice.

METHOD: Scoping review conducted according to the methodological framework of Arksey and O'Malley (2005), enhanced by Levac et al. (2010), and the updated JBI guidance for scoping reviews (Peters et al., 2020). Reporting followed the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A search of scientific literature published between January 2020 and January 2026 was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, CUIDEN, Cochrane Library and CINAHL, complemented by backward citation tracking. Forty-five articles were included after applying rigorous selection criteria, through independent screening by two reviewers with discrepancies resolved by consensus. Data were analyzed through structured extraction and narrative synthesis, organizing interventions according to Swanson's five caring processes.

RESULTS: The review identified multiple nursing interventions during ventilator weaning that showed conceptual correspondence with Swanson's theory. Only 8 of the 45 articles (18%) explicitly used Swanson's framework, and a single study directly linked it to ventilator weaning, identifying a significant knowledge gap. The "knowing" process includes individualized assessment using validated scales and continuous monitoring. "Being with" is manifested through therapeutic presence, effective communication, and facilitation of family contact. "Doing for" encompasses sedation titration, ventilation management, and respiratory physiotherapy techniques. "Enabling" comprises health education, use of augmentative communication systems, and support in decision-making. "Maintaining belief" is materialized through positive reinforcement, management of realistic expectations, and emotional accompaniment.

CONCLUSIONS: Swanson's Theory of Caring provides a relevant and potentially operational theoretical framework to structure and humanize nursing care during ventilator weaning in the ICU. The conceptual correspondence identified suggests that its systematic application could contribute to improving patient experience, reducing psychological complications, and optimizing weaning outcomes. Implementation gaps are evident due to the absence of prospective studies, scarcity of data to quantify the impact of relational care on the weaning process, and the absence of specific protocols that merge the NANDA-NIC-NOC taxonomy and the Swanson theoretical framework. Prospective studies applying Swanson's framework from the design phase are required to evaluate the specific impact of interventions based on this theory through controlled clinical trials.

articles.title: Glatiramer acetate attenuates the cytokine surge associated with acute decompensated heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is characterized by a systemic inflammatory response with elevated circulating cytokines that correlate with adverse outcomes. Glatiramer acetate (GA), an established immunomodulatory agent, exerts broad effects on innate and adaptive immunity and has demonstrated cardioprotective properties in preclinical models. We hypothesized that GA could reduce the cytokine surge associated with ADHF.

METHODS: We conducted a small, investigator-initiated, hypothesis-generating randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effects of GA on inflammatory cytokines in patients with ADHF and reduced ejection fraction. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard care or an add-on treatment with GA. Circulating cytokines were measured using multiplex ELISA assays at baseline, day 2, and day 14. Secondary outcomes included changes in NT-proBNP and troponin.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients were enrolled. GA therapy was associated with a broad attenuation of the cytokine response, with a significant reduction in IL-6 levels compared with standard care (adjusted p = 0.01). Analysis of normalized data demonstrated a marked blunting of the cytokine surge in the GA group at days 2 and 14 (pooled log2 fold-change -5.2 vs. +7.3, p < 0.0001). GA treatment was also associated with a reduction in NT-proBNP levels at both time points, whereas troponin levels were unchanged. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In this proof-of-concept study, GA was associated with attenuation of the inflammatory cytokine surge and reduction in NT-proBNP levels in ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of GA in larger trials.

articles.title: Early detection of immunoglobulin A against a vaccine backbone protein enables fast, durable, and objective identification of individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. Currently available diagnostic and research assays cannot reliably distinguish individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus from those previously infected with the virus. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. The ability to differentiate vaccine-induced immune responses from those resulting from natural infection remains an important unmet public health and research need.

METHODS: We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study.

FINDINGS: We detected increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity.

INTERPRETATION: The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies.

FUNDING: Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the Divisions of Intramural Research (DIR) and Clinical Research (DCR) of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) at the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH).

articles.title: Self-reported difficulty reading small print and in-hospital behavioral change in older adults with cardiovascular disease: Implications for post-discharge cardiovascular outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Visual dysfunction may hinder patient education and self-care in older patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD); however, its association with behavioral change during hospitalization and subsequent cardiovascular prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated whether self-reported difficulty reading small print is associated with transtheoretical model (TTM) stage progression during hospitalization and whether such change predicts post-discharge outcomes.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort study enrolled older patients who underwent cardiac rehabilitation during hospitalization. Visual dysfunction was assessed by self-reporting of difficulty reading small print. Behavioral change was evaluated using the TTM. The primary outcome was unplanned rehospitalization due to major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within one year. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with TTM improvement, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine the association between TTM improvement and MACCE rehospitalization.

RESULTS: Among 351 included patients, 31.9% had difficulty reading small print. After multivariable adjustment, difficulty reading small print was independently associated with lower odds of TTM improvement (odds ratio, 0.31; p=0.006). Patients achieving TTM improvement had a significantly lower risk of MACCE rehospitalization after adjustment for age, sex, institution, heart failure, renal disease, and TTM stage at discharge (hazard ratio, 0.37; p = 0.042).
