CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported difficulty reading small print was independently associated with reduced TTM stage improvement during hospitalization, and TTM stage improvement predicted a lower risk of MACCE rehospitalization. These findings highlight the importance of focusing on the behavioral change process during hospitalization and incorporating visual considerations into behavioral support strategies for secondary prevention in older CVD patients.

articles.title: Prevalence and predictors of early blood transfusion in renal transplant recipients: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia associated with chronic kidney disease is driven by reduced erythropoietin synthesis, chronic inflammation, and decreased red blood cell lifespan. During and after renal transplant surgery, recipients may need blood transfusions. Transfusion rates exhibit significant inter-center variability, largely driven by differing clinical criteria among transplant surgery, nephrology, and intensive care units.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted of 407 renal transplant recipients who underwent transplantation from May 15, 2023 to August 16, 2025 at the Shahid Dharmabhakta National Transplant Center, Nepal. Early transfusion was defined as any blood product administration occurring within 14 days post-surgery. Clinical and Laboratory variables were compared between transfused and non-transfused patients using either the Mann-Whitney U test or chi-square test as appropriate. Variables significant in univariate analysis were included in multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of transfusion.

RESULTS: Ninety-five patients (23.34%) required transfusions with leukoreduced red blood cells being the most common blood product. Univariate analysis revealed that preoperative hemoglobin levels, diabetic nephropathy, and the length of hospital stay were significantly associated with transfusion requirements. Multivariate analysis showed that preoperative hemoglobin and length of stay were predictors of transfusion. The hemoglobin nadir for the transfused group reached a mean of 6.3 ± 1.05 g/dL and a median of 6.1 g/dL, with an interquartile range from 4.2 to 10.0 g/dL.

DISCUSSION: The results of this study show that a conservative transfusion approach can be effective in achieving good clinical outcomes, especially in resource limited centers.

articles.title: Gut mycobiome in the spectrum of Metabolic-dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): from MASH to hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Gut Microbiome (GM) dysbiosis is associated with the development and progression of Metabolic-dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) and steatohepatitis (MASH). Human GM contains bacteria, fungi, archaea, and viruses. Gut mycobiome (GMyco) is still poorly studied in patients with MASLD. Herein we investigated GMyco composition at different MASLD stages.

METHODS: 23 patients were recruited: controls (n = 5); MASH (n = 6); cirrhosis (n = 7); and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) (n = 5). Stool samples were collected and stored in -80 °C for subsequent DNA extraction and profiled by 18S rRNA sequencing. The single sequence variants obtained were inferred with DADA2 and classified with SILVA v138. Diversity metrics (Simpson; Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA) and DESeq2 with BH FDR were used for statistical analysis.

RESULTS: Among 23 participants, 73.9% were women, and the average BMI was 30.7 kg/m2. Current alcohol use was reported in 17.4%, and chronic medication use in 56.5% of individuals. MASH patients showed greater gut mycobiota alpha diversity compared with controls (p < 0.05). Controls exhibited higher relative abundance of the phylum Ascomycota, whereas Basidiomycota predominated in MASH. At the family level, Aspergillaceae was more abundant in controls, Malasseziaceae and Sporidiobolaceae in cirrhosis, and Saccharomycetaceae in HCC. Differential abundance analysis identified three ASVs differing between groups, with one ASV (genus Naganishia) homogeneously distributed in MASH and absent in controls.

CONCLUSIONS: The gut mycobiota profile varied across the MASLD spectrum, with stage-specific enrichment of certain taxa despite overall similarity in community structure. Basidiomycetes ‒ notably Malassezia and Naganishia ‒ were more abundant in MASH, while Saccharomyces dominated in advanced stages. These findings suggest that distinct fungal signatures accompany disease progression and may serve as potential biological markers in MASLD.

articles.title: Optimal exercise modalities and doses for blood pressure management in adults with prehypertension and hypertension: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify the most effective exercise modalities and optimal estimated dose range for reducing blood pressure in adults with prehypertension and hypertension, to support more precise exercise prescription.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to December 28, 2025. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they included adults with prehypertension or stage 1 or stage 2 hypertension, evaluated structured exercise interventions, and reported resting systolic blood pressure and/or diastolic blood pressure.

RESULTS: A total of 284 randomized controlled trials, including 18,750 participants with a mean age of 56.8 years, covering ten exercise modalities were included. Aquatic exercise achieved the greatest reduction in systolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -10.28 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -13.05 to -7.49; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 93.26%. Whole-body vibration and cycling also showed favorable estimates for systolic blood pressure. Mind-body exercise showed the largest estimated reduction in diastolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -4.69 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -6.45 to -2.92; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 85.90%. Aquatic exercise and isometric exercise training also showed favorable effect estimates. Dose-response modelling indicated that 750 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled systolic blood pressure benefit for isometric exercise training, with a mean difference of -13.52 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -23.22 to -3.86. In contrast, 3600 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled diastolic blood pressure benefit for aerobic exercise, with a mean difference of -7.11 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -11.89 to -2.18.

CONCLUSION: Ten exercise modalities were associated with reductions in blood pressure, with particularly strong effects for aquatic, mind-body, and isometric exercise at specific doses. These findings may inform more tailored exercise prescription strategies for adults across hypertension phenotypes.

articles.title: The restore-adapt-abandon framework: supporting safe and meaningful living after ventricular assist device implantation.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular assist device (VAD) therapy improves survival and symptoms in patients with advanced heart failure but can impose lifestyle restrictions that challenge meaningful living. Engagement in meaningful activities is protective against all-cause mortality and positively impacts health, well-being, and quality of life, yet little is known about how VAD recipients adapt these activities post-implantation.

OBJECTIVES: To explore how VAD recipients navigate meaningful activity engagement post-implantation, and present a clinically-relevant framework characterizing how VAD recipients engage in meaningful activities across the post-implant trajectory.

METHODS: We analyzed semi‑structured interview data from VAD recipients in the Southeastern U.S. and used thematic analysis to explore patterns of activity engagement and adaptation.

RESULTS: Two major themes emerged: (1) symptom relief enables restoration of activities and social roles; and (2) identity shifts and risk management prompt modified engagement. Across themes, patients described strategies and constraints including planning over spontaneity, managing device visibility and stigma, out-of-pocket costs, caregiver-linked mobility, and climate sensitivity. These patterns informed a "restore-adapt-abandon" framework for meaningful activity engagement across the post-VAD trajectory.

CONCLUSION: Based on the findings, we recommend structured values elicitation, patient-clinician co-planning of activity adaptations, and identity-focused psychosocial support into routine VAD care. These strategies can optimize meaningful living alongside safety and redefine success in VAD therapy from survival alone to living well.

articles.title: Post-norepinephrine fluid volume and clinical outcomes in septic shock: a landmark retrospective cohort analysis of MIMIC-IV.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluid administered after norepinephrine initiation may reflect both resuscitation decisions and evolving illness severity, making observational comparisons susceptible to confounding and reverse causation.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate associations between fluid volume during the first 6 h after norepinephrine initiation and mortality and incident invasive ventilation.

METHODS: We reconstructed an adult MIMIC-IV cohort with coded sepsis and norepinephrine initiated during ICU hours 0-24. Eligibility required complete pre-norepinephrine physiology and initial norepinephrine rate, survival, and ICU observation through a 6-hour landmark. Fluid exposure was ≤1,000 versus >1000 mL. Stabilized inverse-probability weights were truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles. Doubly adjusted logistic models used patient-clustered robust standard errors.

RESULTS: The cohort included 2696 ICU stays from 2493 patients; 1572 received ≤1,000 mL. Maximum weighted standardized mean difference was 0.033. Twenty-eight-day mortality occurred in 1117 stays. Lower-volume exposure was not associated with mortality (odds ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.89-1.31; adjusted risks 42.6% versus 41.1%). Results were similar for other mortality analyses and thresholds. Among 1356 stays not ventilated at baseline, incident ventilation was not clearly associated with exposure (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.53-1.13). The spline showed no dose-response association (p = 0.983).

CONCLUSION: After source-level cohort construction and expanded adjustment, post-norepinephrine fluid volume was not associated with mortality or incident invasive ventilation.

articles.title: Patient and family engagement in patient safety in resource-limited intensive care units: A qualitative exploratory study.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient and family engagement (PFE) in the intensive care unit (ICU) enhances patient safety through detection and reporting of safety incidents that may be missed by healthcare professionals, providing an important and additional safeguard against harm. However, empirical evidence to inform policy and practice in resource-limited critical care settings remains scarce.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to explore the perspectives and experiences of patients, families, and healthcare professionals on PFE in patient safety in Ethiopian ICUs.

METHODS: A pragmatic, exploratory qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews guided by a semistructured interview protocol. Participants were purposively selected and included patients, families, and healthcare professionals. Participants were recruited from four ICUs, including both adult and paediatric/neonatal ICUs in a major university hospital in Eastern Ethiopia. Reflexive thematic analysis with inductive orientation guided by Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach was employed. Convergence and divergence of perspectives across participant groups were identified and reported. Criteria for rigour and trustworthiness including credibility, dependability, transferability, confirmability, and integrity guided the research process. The consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research were followed to ensure the transparency and consistency of reporting.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine in-depth interviews were conducted, including patients (5; 9%), families (15; 25%), and healthcare professionals (39; 66%). Three overarching themes were identified: First, contested safety roles reflected the competing views on engagement, which were endorsed rhetorically but constrained in practice due to structural and hierarchical power dynamics. Second, sociocultural logics of engagement underscored inequities between rural and urban patients/families shaped by sociocultural attributes and faith-based sense-making. Third, tensions inpatient safetyincident disclosure highlighted the discordance between the expectation of transparency and hesitancy to involve patients and families in incident disclosure due to fear of reprisals.

CONCLUSION: PFE in patient safety in Ethiopian ICUs was endorsed in principle yet remained constrained by sociocultural contexts, hierarchical power dynamics, and limited institutional support mechanisms. Clearly defining patient safety roles, implementing family-activated escalation pathways, and strengthening formal patient safety incident reporting and disclosure systems are essential to promote inclusive, equitable, and sustainable PFE in patient safety across Ethiopian ICUs and beyond.

articles.title: In situ antibacterial thermosensitive hydrogel as a versatile platform for diabetic wound therapy and molecular monitoring.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are difficult to manage because of persistent inflammation, impaired tissue regeneration, and high infection risk under hyperglycemic conditions. Microbial colonization further aggravates inflammatory responses and disrupts the normal progression of wound healing. Here, we developed a multifunctional hydrogel composed of Pluronic F-127 (PF) and tannic acid (TA), where TA acted as a natural crosslinker to improve network stability and gelation behavior. The PF/TA hydrogel exhibited in situ thermosensitive gelation within the physiological temperature range (33-37 °C), enabling rapid solidification and strong adhesion to wound surfaces. Rheological and microscopic analyses confirmed favorable viscoelasticity and a microporous structure. The hydrogel also showed antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. To provide therapeutic functionality, the hydrogel was loaded with Humulus scandens (HS) or Vitis vinifera (VV) extracts. These extracts reduced Pecam1 expression, promoted fibroblast proliferation, increased Col1a1 expression, and induced M2 macrophage polarization in vitro. For wound monitoring, gold nanoparticle-based mRNA nanosensors (NanoFlares) were incorporated to detect Pecam1 and Col1a1 mRNA associated with inflammatory and proliferative healing phases. In non-infected murine wound models, HS- and VV-loaded PF/TA hydrogels significantly accelerated wound closure under both nondiabetic and diabetic conditions, demonstrating promising potential for diabetic wound therapy and monitoring applications.

articles.title: Toxoplasma serology: Breaking the diagnostic boundary of schizoaffective disorder? Insights from a comparative peripheral immune marker analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii) infection has been implicated in the pathophysiology of psychiatric disorders, yet no study has compared its seroprevalence between schizoaffective disorder (SZA) and other psychiatric conditions. This study aimed to compare T. gondii seroprevalence between patients with SZA, schizophrenia (SZ), and bipolar disorder (BD), and to examine whether seropositivity differentially affects innate immune markers across these diagnoses.

METHODS: Overall 144 patients were included in this cross-sectional study. T. gondii seroprevalence was determined and leukocyte counts and derived immune ratios were compared across diagnostic groups according to T.gondii seroprevalence.

RESULTS: T. gondii seroprevalence was significantly higher in SZA (68.8%) as compared to BD (44.2%; p = 0.02), but did not differ significantly from SZ (52.2%; p = 0.2). Relative to SZA, higher neutrophil (p < 0.01) and monocyte (p = 0.02) levels were associated with greater odds of BD, while higher NLR was associated with both BD (p = 0.04) and SZ (p = 0.02), and higher MLR with SZ (p = 0.02). However, none of these associations remained significant after Bonferroni correction. We observed a significant interaction between basophil counts and T. gondii in SZA versus BD (padj < 0.01) and SZ (padj < 0.01), indicating a diagnosis-specific immune modulation.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that T. gondii seroprevalence in SZA is closer to SZ than BD. However, seropositivity appears to affect innate immune markers differently in SZA, without inflammatory activation. This immune profile suggests a unique pathophysiological signature in SZA and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment of tandem lesions: prognostic factors of functional outcome and the efficacy of emergent carotid stenting.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting.

METHODS: Patients with acute internal carotid artery tandem occlusion who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) were enrolled. Baseline clinical and procedural data were collected. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, and the safety endpoint was symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance covariates between patients receiving emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) and non-stenting controls. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors. Subgroup analyses were conducted on relevant risk factors.

RESULTS: A total of 112 eligible patients were included, with a mean age of 66.19 ± 9.23 years; 76 (67.86%) were male. Fifty-eight patients (51.79%) achieved a favorable functional outcome (good prognosis group). Univariate analysis revealed significant differences (P < 0.05) between the two groups in baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, puncture-to-reperfusion time, history of hypertension, and history of atrial fibrillation. After multivariable adjustment, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time were identified as independent risk factors for unfavorable 90-day functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients undergoing EVT. Emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) was not an independent predictor of 90-day favorable functional outcome (adjusted OR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.17-1.58, P = 0.246). Significant differences in stroke history and smoking history were found between the emergent stenting and non-stenting groups at baseline. Female sex and puncture-to-reperfusion time were independent risk factors for sICH in tandem lesion patients. Subgroup analysis indicated that in those aged ≥ 65 years, emergent stenting was associated with unfavorable 90-day functional prognosis (OR = 0.042, 95% CI 0.004-0.469, P = 0.01).

CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time may serve as independent predictors of 90-day favorable functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients treated with EVT. Female sex and longer puncture-to-reperfusion time appear to be potential risk factors for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Emergent carotid artery stenting was not found to be an independent predictor of 90-day functional prognosis in our cohort, and no significant increase in sICH risk was observed in association with eCAS. These preliminary findings require further validation in large-scale multicenter prospective studies.

articles.title: Ensifentrine inhibits lipopolysaccharide-induced production of cytokines by human lung macrophages: a comparison with roflumilast, and an interaction with adenosine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The dual phosphodiesterase (PDE) 3/4 inhibitor ensifentrine was recently approved for the maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in adults. Ensifentrine anti-inflammatory effects have not been studied in human lung macrophages (LMs), which are critically involved in respiratory disease. The main objectives of the present study were to compare the inhibitory effects of ensifentrine, the PDE4 inhibitor roflumilast, and the non-selective PDE inhibitor theophylline on the lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced production of cytokines by LMs and to assess interactions with the adenosine analogue 5´-N-ethyl-carboxamidoadenosine (NECA).

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: LMs isolated from resected human lungs were incubated with a range of concentrations of ensifentrine, roflumilast, theophylline, NECA, and formoterol, and stimulated with LPS for 24 h. The levels of tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), CCL2, CCL3, and CCL4 in the culture supernatants were measured using ELISAs.

KEY RESULTS: Ensifentrine reduced the LPS-stimulated production of TNF-α by LMs in a concentration-dependent manner, with a 100-fold lower potency but a 20-30% higher efficacy than roflumilast. Theophylline and formoterol were essentially inactive. The relative reductions in the LPS-induced production of TNF-α and the three CCL chemokines associated with treatment with the two selective inhibitors was further accentuated by NECA and resulted in similar levels of cytokine production inhibition (between 65% and 95%) with the two PDE inhibitors.

CONCLUSION: Clinically relevant concentrations of ensifentrine and roflumilast partially inhibited the LPS-induced production of cytokines by LMs - cytokine production that might be enhanced during inflammatory flare-ups of respiratory diseases.

articles.title: Combining responsive neurostimulation with resection or ablation for treatment of epilepsy: a multicenter experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite advances in surgical and neuromodulatory treatments, a substantial proportion of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy remain ineligible for standalone resection or ablation. Combining resection or laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) with responsive neurostimulation (RNS) has emerged as a promising approach for patients with multifocal seizure onset or eloquent cortex involvement. However, the clinical impact of combination surgery remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to characterize the clinical rationale and surgical decision-making used across multiple high-volume epilepsy centers performing combination surgeries, and to evaluate the seizure outcomes and safety profile associated with this approach.

METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who underwent RNS implantation in combination with resection or LITT at 9 epilepsy centers and had ≥ 1 year of follow-up. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and seizure outcome data were collected. The primary outcome was seizure reduction at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the Clinical Global Impression and adverse events.

RESULTS: Overall, 73 patients (40 male, mean age 34 years) with a mean epilepsy duration of 21 years were included in this analysis. The most common etiology was unknown (37%), followed by cortical malformation (16%). Most patients experienced focal impaired consciousness (FIC, 78%) and focal to bilateral tonic-clonic (FBTC, 70%) seizures. Prior resection was performed in 23%. Combination procedures were performed on the same day in 89% of patients. RNS implantation was concurrent with resection in 92% and with LITT in 8.2% of patients. Neocortical and mesial temporal regions accounted for 61% of resection/ablation targets. More than two-thirds of RNS leads were subdural strips, most commonly in the left hemisphere (73%). Indications for the combined approach included eloquent cortex involvement (67%) and multifocal seizure onset (33%) or both (9.6%). At 1 year, mean seizure reductions were 53% for focal impaired, 69% for FIC, and 67% for FBTC seizures. Overall, 48% of patients had at least a 6-month period of seizure freedom, and 4 patients had no seizures after surgery. Significant global clinical improvement (much or very much improved) was observed in 79% of patients. Three patients experienced infection, and 1 patient died due to causes unrelated to surgical treatment (sudden unexpected death in epilepsy).

CONCLUSIONS: Combined RNS with resection or ablation might provide meaningful seizure control in complex drug-resistant epilepsy with acceptable safety profiles. These findings describe current practice and support further investigation of hybrid surgical strategies in patients with challenging seizure networks as a potential treatment strategy.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a conditional failure-to-rescue prediction model after surgery for metastatic spine disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop and internally validate an optimal patient-level prediction model for conditional failure to rescue (cFTR) after surgery for spinal metastases.

METHODS: The authors performed a retrospective analysis of the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2018 to 2023. The primary endpoint was cFTR, defined as 30-day postoperative mortality among patients who experienced at least 1 major complication following surgery for metastatic spinal tumors. Uni- and multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to predict cFTR. Model performance was assessed using discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), calibration, and information criteria (Akaike and Bayesian). Penalized regression (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and elastic net) was performed to evaluate robustness. Internal validation was conducted using 5-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. Reporting of model development followed the TRIPOD statement.

RESULTS: Among 338 patients who experienced at least 1 major postoperative complication, 71 (21%) died within 30 days. Emergency surgery was found to be the strongest predictor of cFTR. In the final 6-predictor clinical model, emergency surgery, current smoking, higher preoperative white blood cell count, lower serum albumin, and functional dependence were associated with increased odds of cFTR. The model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.740) and acceptable calibration, with minimal optimism on internal validation (cross-validated AUC = 0.713, bootstrap mean AUC = 0.743). Penalized regression models demonstrated slightly higher discrimination but offered limited incremental benefit over the clinical mode. Secondary analyses showed that nonsurvivors experienced a higher burden of complications and disproportionately severe cardiopulmonary and infectious events.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with metastatic spinal tumors who experienced major postoperative complications, cFTR remained common and was largely driven by patient-level vulnerability. Conditioning on the occurrence of complications highlighted emergency presentation, impaired physiological reserve, systemic inflammation, and functional dependence as key determinants of mortality. This internally validated model provides a transparent framework for risk stratification after complications and identified potentially modifiable targets for perioperative optimization. External validation is needed to establish generalizability and clinical utility.

articles.title: Consensus, Disagreements, and Open Questions in the Psychology of Misinformation.
articles.abstract: Research on misinformation has expanded rapidly over the past decade. This review examines areas of consensus and contention within the literature on misinformation, with particular attention to conceptual definitions, measurement approaches, and theoretical explanations. We outline views on what it means to be susceptible to misinformation and advocate for assessing susceptibility by focusing on the ability to discern true from false claims. Although exposure to fake news is less common online than many think, we argue that misinformation-more broadly construed-continues to be a major problem. We review evidence on cognitive and socio-affective mechanisms underlying susceptibility to misinformation, including repetition effects, lack of analytic reasoning, political identity, and information environments. We also evaluate interventions such as fact-checking, prebunking, psychological inoculation, and accuracy prompts. Overall, the literature reveals several robust findings but also significant methodological limitations and theoretical disagreements that suggest fruitful future directions for misinformation research.

articles.title: The Risk of an H5N1 Influenza Pandemic.
articles.abstract: The last 110 years have seen four influenza A pandemics, where viruses have emerged from mammals or birds with the ability to transmit and cause disease in human populations. Since 2021, a high-pathogenicity strain of avian influenza, H5N1, has caused a panzootic (pandemic of animals), with global spread in wild birds, resulting in frequent spillovers into farmed poultry and into mammals, including mammal species not previously known to be affected by influenza A. This has created increased opportunity for reassortment, mutation, human infection, and potential adaptation to transmit. The risk to humans and the impact are difficult to quantify but of mounting concern to public health bodies. Here, we examine the risk of an H5N1 pandemic emerging and spreading in humans and the potential impact of an H5N1 pandemic.

articles.title: Survival disparities in primary malignant spine tumors: a national analysis of academic and community hospital care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Primary malignant osseous tumors of the mobile spine are rare and require complex, multidisciplinary care. Treatment outcomes may differ between academic and community hospitals due to variations in resources, expertise, and infrastructure. This study evaluates demographics, care delivery patterns, and clinical outcomes, including both short- and long-term survival, for patients treated at academic versus community cancer programs using the National Cancer Database.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database was performed. Nine hundred forty-three patients diagnosed with primary malignant osseous tumors of the mobile spine between 2004 and 2017 were identified. Patients were stratified by facility type: there were 601 patients treated at academic comprehensive cancer programs (ACADs) and 342 treated at comprehensive community cancer programs (CCCPs). Demographic, treatment, and clinical data were compared using descriptive statistics. Outcomes included inpatient length of stay, time to treatment, 30- and 90-day mortality, vital status at last contact, and overall survival. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model assessed factors associated with overall survival.

RESULTS: Patients at ACADs were significantly younger and more likely to have private insurance. The size and histopathological composition of the tumors did not differ significantly between facility types. ACAD patients experienced significantly longer inpatient stays and longer time to radiation initiation among patients receiving radiation with documented start dates. Time to chemotherapy did not significantly differ (p = 0.91). Thirty- and 90-day mortality were comparable between facility types among eligible surgical cases. At last follow-up, a significantly greater proportion of ACAD patients were alive (50.2% vs 38.3%, p < 0.001), and the median time from diagnosis to last contact or death was longer at ACADs (40.8 vs 33.2 months, p = 0.001). In the primary multivariable Cox model, treatment at an academic facility was associated with improved overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0.766, 95% CI 0.627-0.937; p = 0.009). In a sensitivity model adjusting for histopathology rather than grade, this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (CCCP vs ACAD, HR 1.19, p = 0.081).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients treated at academic centers had longer inpatient stays and longer time to radiation initiation, yet academic facility treatment was associated with improved overall survival in the primary multivariable model. After accounting for histopathological subtype in sensitivity analysis, the facility-type association was attenuated, suggesting survival differences reflect both tumor biology and system-level care pathways.

articles.title: Participant Characteristics Associated With Loneliness Reduction During a Digital Social Robot Intervention Among Older Adults Living Alone in Japan: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Among community-dwelling older adults living alone, less frequent preintervention social contact was associated with greater reductions in loneliness during a social robot intervention. Future trials should examine whether preintervention social contact modifies the effects of social robot interventions.

articles.title: Recruitment, Engagement, Experiences, and Self-Reported Changes in a Digital Patient Activation Intervention to Improve Hemodialysis Session Stability: Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When chronic kidney disease progresses to end-stage kidney disease, many patients receive in-center hemodialysis. Although lifesaving, hemodialysis is associated with intradialytic hypotension. Peer mentoring and patient activation support in hemodialysis have not been well studied.

OBJECTIVE: This Dialysafe study combined patient education and peer mentoring to promote health behaviors supporting prevention of intradialytic hypotension. We aimed to describe recruitment, engagement, completion, and attrition; assess participants' health goals and self-reported behavior changes; and evaluate satisfaction and recommendations for improvement.

METHODS: At 10 Dialysafe hemodialysis centers assigned to patient activation, all eligible English-speaking patients were invited. The intervention comprised 5 educational modules and 5 videoconference peer-mentoring sessions. Mixed methods analyses integrated electronic health record and platform data, postintervention surveys, and clinic operations committee notes. An engagement score (range 0-50) summarized intervention use. Descriptive statistics, t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and zero-inflated Poisson regression were used to assess recruitment, completion (all 5 mentoring sessions), and engagement. Qualitative data were inductively coded and integrated through joint displays.

RESULTS: Of the 639 eligible patients, 155 (24.3%) were recruited. Recruited patients were younger than nonrecruited patients (mean 57.6, SD 13.8, vs 64.3, SD 14.7 y; P<.001); each additional year was associated with 4% lower odds of recruitment (odds ratio [OR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.98; P<.001). Recruitment was more likely among college graduates (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.02-2.83; P=.04) and patients with sleep disorders (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.06-4.87; P=.03). Attrition was concentrated before mentoring sessions began. Of recruited patients, 72 of 155 (46.5%) met with a peer mentor and 58 of 155 (37.4%) completed all 5 sessions. Completers were 1.9 years younger (56.4, SD 13.8, vs 58.3, SD 13.9 y) and had Charlson Comorbidity Index scores 0.4 points higher (3.4, SD 2.0, vs 3.0, SD 2.3) than noncompleters. The average engagement score was 18.4 of 50 (SD 20.1). Engagement was higher among men (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.33, 95% CI 1.22-1.45; P<.001), Black patients (IRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.16-1.39; P<.001), and patients with dialysis vintage <1 year (IRR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.42; P=.01). Higher Charlson Comorbidity Index scores predicted engagement (IRR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P=.002) and completion (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.05-1.79; P=.02). Of 79 patients who set goals, 64 (81%) selected communication with the care team; 22 of 54 (40.7%) survey respondents identified this as their main behavior change. Both mentees and mentors identified peer-mentoring sessions as the most valuable component. Among mentee respondents, 55 of 55 (100%) respondents rated the program good or excellent, and 53 of 54 (98.1%) respondents would recommend it.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants constituted a self-selecting group. Patient-clinician communication was a priority, and participants valued peer mentoring. Digital patient activation intervention strategies to increase reach are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03171545; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03171545.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): RR2-10.2196/46187.

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Incidence Trends of Hemorrhagic Fever With Renal Syndrome in Shandong Province, China: Retrospective Observational Study With Forecasting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a severe natural focal infectious disease that remains a major public health concern in Shandong Province, China. Understanding the epidemiological characteristics of HFRS and forecasting its incidence are crucial to provide guidance for policymaking and implement timely interventions against this disease.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the long-term epidemiological characteristics of HFRS based on 15 years of surveillance data; the analysis used 4 time series models to predict its incidence trends. The aim was to provide a scientific basis for local disease control departments, thereby supporting more accurate prediction and effective prevention and control of HFRS in this region.

METHODS: HFRS case surveillance data in Shandong Province from 2010 to 2024 were collected through the China Information System for Disease Control and Prevention. Descriptive epidemiological methods were used to analyze the basic characteristics of HFRS. Four forecasting models, namely, seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average, Prophet, the Holt-Winters exponential smoothing method, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, were implemented in R to fit the time series and generate predictions. Their predictive performance was evaluated and compared using the root mean squared error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error.

RESULTS: From 2010 to 2024, a total of 15,184 HFRS cases were reported in Shandong Province, with 188 deaths. The annual incidence rate ranged from 0.45 to 1.84 per 100,000 population, showing an overall fluctuating downward trend. The peak incidence occurred during the autumn and winter months from October to December each year. Spatially, the eastern and southeastern regions of Shandong Province were the primary high-incidence areas. Demographically, the high-risk populations were mainly middle-aged and older adults, male individuals, and farmers. In the 2024 test set, the Holt-Winters model yielded the lowest prediction error metrics among the 4 models, with root mean squared error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error values of 7.56, 6.43, and 34.56%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The Holt-Winters model showed the lowest prediction error metrics among the 4 models, suggesting its potential utility for forecasting HFRS incidence. It is recommended to apply this model to enhance precise monitoring and implement targeted prevention and control measures focusing on key areas, peak periods, and high-risk populations.

articles.title: Associations between methodological quality and representation in clinical trials of systemic lupus erythematosus therapies.
articles.abstract: BackgroundRandomized clinical trials support drug development and uptake of new therapies for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, challenges to conducting high-quality clinical trials have been noted, including underrepresentation of minoritized populations. Currently, it is not known whether the methodological quality of clinical trials is associated with representativeness of US patients with SLE.MethodsFor this cross-sectional study, we identified industry-sponsored clinical trials of small molecules and biologics for SLE with at least one US enrollment site, with results published in peer-reviewed journals as of January 1, 2026. Trial characteristics were abstracted, and urbanicity of US enrollment sites were classified using the National Center for Health Statistics Urban-Rural Classification System. Trial representativeness by sex, race, and ethnicity were assessed against SLE prevalence in meta-analyzed US lupus registries using participation-to-prevalence ratios (PPRs; ≥0.8 indicating adequate representation). Trial methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Associations between trial risk of bias and representativeness were evaluated.FindingsWe identified 51 trials enrolling 18,466 participants with SLE. Trial representation was adequate for female (median PPR 1 · 03), Hispanic (median PPR 1 · 37), White (median PPR 1 · 03), and Asian participants (median PPR 2 · 40), and Black participants were underrepresented (median PPR 0 · 32). Most US enrollment sites were located in large metropolitan areas. The methodological quality of trials varied (37% at low risk of bias, 35% with some concerns, 27% at high risk of bias) but was not associated with demographic or geographic representativeness.InterpretationWe identified inconsistencies in participant representation and methodological quality across SLE clinical trials. Although trial designs were generally rigorous, limitations of participant inclusion and enrollment site distribution suggest that representation, rather than methodological quality alone, may limit the external validity of SLE clinical trials.

articles.title: Provider Practice and Patient Clinical Follow-Up Among Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Linked-Variant.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recommends spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) carrier screening be offered preconception or prenatally. SMA linked-variant incurs an increased but not absolute risk of being a carrier.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the patient population, clinical recommendations, and follow-up in a cohort with SMA linked-variant.

STUDY DESIGN: This is a retrospective cohort study performed at an urban, academic, tertiary care center of patients with the SMA linked-variant approximately 2017-2021. Descriptive statistics characterize the patient population, provider recommendations, and patient follow-up.

RESULTS: There were 856 patients, majority Black (94.2%), who tested positive for the SMA linked-variant. There was documentation of result disclosure to patients in only 62.6% of cases. Genetic counseling (88.8%) and partner testing (62.5%) were most often offered. At least one suggested follow-up was completed by 29.1% of patients, with 162 patients (30.2%) receiving genetic counseling and 61 (11.4%) undergoing partner testing.

CONCLUSION: Providers documented disclosure of SMA linked-variant results in only 2/3 of cases, and patients completed at least some of the offered clinical follow-up in only 1/3 of cases, both major gaps in care quality. Additional research is needed to understand and improve the suboptimal result review and low rates of patient follow-up.

articles.title: Polymicrogyria and Cardiac Arrhythmia in a Neonate With Biallelic Stop-Gain Variant in TMEM161B: Expanding the Phenotype.
Mapping the Canadian Oncology Physician Workforce: A Review of Training, Distribution, and Systemic Pressures Across Oncology-Related Physician Specialties.
articles.abstract: Between 1994 and 2020, new cancer cases in Canada increased by 88%, with 40% of the oncology workforce now nearing retirement age. With increasing cancer incidence and an aging workforce, organizations such as the Canadian Association of Provincial Cancer Agencies have expressed concern that Canada's cancer workforce is overstretched, with a need for workforce monitoring. This scoping review investigates the workforce trends and pressures affecting the workforce across key Canadian physician specialties involved in oncology care (surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, hematology, pediatric hematology/oncology, and palliative care). Data were synthesized from a database search and included gray literature or national workforce sources such as the Canadian Institute for Health Information. Distinct patterns, supply-demand imbalances, and emerging solutions to growing issues in each field are reported. We also report on documented strategies already being implemented to help alleviate pressures. Data showed that despite workforce growth, burnout and regional distribution pressures threaten access to Canadian cancer care, demonstrating a need for reallocation of resources.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.

METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.

RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).

CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

articles.title: Trends in mortality rates in hypotensive pediatric trauma patients undergoing emergent trauma laparotomy.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Massive hemorrhage remains the leading cause of preventable death after pediatric trauma. Emergent trauma laparotomy (ETL) is a common operation to obtain hemorrhage control. Mortality rates for adult patients in hemorrhagic shock requiring ETL remain high and unchanged. Information on mortality rates after ETL in pediatric patients is limited. We sought to evaluate trends in mortality rates for pediatric ETL patients.

METHODS: The National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) was queried from 2007 to 2023. Patients aged 0 to 18 years old were included if they underwent ETL. ETL was defined as laparotomy within 1 hour of arrival. Hypotension was defined as a systolic blood pressure <90 mm Hg on arrival. The primary outcome was annual hospital mortality rates for hypotensive patients requiring ETL. Secondary outcomes included annual 24-hour mortality rates for both hypotensive and all patients requiring ETL. Mortality rates were compared in 5-year cohorts to reduce annual variability.

RESULTS: A total of 11,374 patients underwent ETL. The majority of patients were male (79%; n=78,963/11,374). Most patients were between the ages of 12 and 17 (84%; n=9,565/11,374), followed by ages 5 to 11 (11%; n=1,227/11,374), then ages 0 to 4 (5%; n=582/11,374). Penetrating injuries predominated (69%; n=7,866/11,374). The hospital mortality rate for all patients was 18.3% (n=2,079/11,374). Of patients who died, 74% were within 24 hours of arrival (n=1,533/2,079). Overall, 19% (n=2,125/11,374) were hypotensive on arrival. For hypotensive patients, the 24-hour and hospital mortality rates were 30% (n=641/2,125) and 45.9% (n=976/2,125). There was year-to-year variability in rates of hospital mortality of hypotensive patients through the study period (p<0.001). However, the average mortality rates from 2007 to 2011 (45%; n=293/645) and 2019 to 2023 (42%; n=266/638) were unchanged (p=0.95).

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric trauma patients with exsanguinating hemorrhage requiring ETL continue to suffer high rates of mortality. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted research and performance improvement.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Mpox and sexually transmitted infections: syndemic drivers of transmission and disease outcomes-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The worldwide outbreak of mpox (formerly monkeypox) in 2022 emerged as a public health emergency posing greater threat to persons with sexually transmitted infections (STIs). This outbreak featured an increase in overlap between mpox and STIs reflecting evolving transmission dynamics in sexual networks. Epidemiological data reveal that STIs such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Chlamydia trachomatis, herpes simplex virus, syphilis have been frequently associated with mpox infection highlighting the role of sexual contact in its transmission. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar to identify relevant literature published between 2008 and 2026, focusing on mpox, STIs, co-infections, and pregnancy outcomes. Evidence suggests that biological, behavioural and structural factors may interact to influence mpox transmission and clinical outcomes. STI co-infection may be associated with mucosal invasion and immune modulation plausibly affecting disease progression, however direct mechanistic evidence remains limited. Although mpox infection has majorly affected gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM), its severity in women particularly during pregnancy raises concerns regarding vertical transmission and maternal and neonatal complications. This review highlights current evidence on mpox-STI co-infections, and applies a syndemic framework to interpret their co-occurrence within biological, behavioural and structural contexts. While this perspective provides understanding regarding transmission patterns, further research is needed to establish the extent of these interactions. Recognizing these factors is important for screening, early diagnosis and management strategies to mitigate future outbreaks and impact of mpox. Summary: This narrative review on mpox and STI co-infections explores syndemic interactions, transmission dynamics and implications for disease outcomes and public health management.

articles.title: In older adults, "mild" by GCS does not mean low risk: Multicenter study of 1,157 patients with mild TBI and acute subdural hematoma.
authors: Traumatic Subdural Hematoma Outcomes Study Group
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH.

METHODS: This was a 10-center, retrospective cohort study of adult traumas with emergency department Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13 to 15 and acute traumatic SDH on initial brain CT ('22-'23). Trauma registry, EHR, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) data were collected through automated and manual methods. The primary outcome was total mortality (TM=death+hospice discharge); the sample was stratified by 18 to 64 versus older than or equal to 65 years. Multivariable backward selection logistic regression examined 21 demographic, injury, and brain CT covariates.

RESULTS: In total, 1,157 patients were included (18-64 y: 28%; ≥65 y: 72%; 58% transferred in). Median [IQR] non-head ISS was 1 [1-5] in 18 to 64 years, and 1 [1-2] in older than or equal to 65 years. Ten percent had neurosurgical intervention (18-64 y: 8%; ≥65 y: 11%). TM was higher in older than or equal to 65 years than 18 to 64 years (10% vs. 3%). Compared with older than or equal to 65 years, 18 to 64 years were discharged home more frequently (78% vs. 51%) and to hospice less frequently (2% vs. 7%). In 18 to 64 years, factors associated with TM were race, advance directive, functional dependence, ISS, more midline shift, and thicker SDH (too few TMs for adjusted models). In older than or equal to 65 years, factors independently associated with TM were advance directive (aOR [95% CI]: 11.8 [2.9-49.0]), male sex (3.0 [1.3-7.0]), midline shift (1.8 [1.3-2.6]), shock index (1.5 [1.1-2.1]), and worsening SDH on follow-up CT (2.9 [1.3-6.6]).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite presenting as "mild", these data highlight that older adults with SDH have high TM and should continue to receive the highest-level care with timely goals-of-care discussions. The association between advance directives and TM should be interpreted within the context of baseline vulnerability and preinjury treatment preferences, not as a biological mortality predictor.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Digital Nudges Among New Gym Members: Controlled Formative Evaluation of Gym Attendance, Exercise Self-Efficacy, Habit Strength, and Exercise Adherence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital nudging strategies are increasingly implemented to promote physical activity; yet, evidence from real-world fitness settings remains limited. The early membership period in fitness centers is characterized by high dropout rates, emphasizing the need for formative evaluations that clarify behavioral mechanisms underlying exercise engagement.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the formative impact of WhatsApp (Meta Platforms, Inc)-based digital nudges on objectively measured weekly gym visits among new fitness club members and to examine behavioral determinants associated with exercise engagement.

METHODS: This controlled intervention study used a 2-parallel-group design with quasi-random individual allocation conducted separately within 2 fitness clubs. The complete-case sample comprised 61 new gym members (mean age 29.05, SD 8.06 years; 21/61, 34.4% female), including 27 participants in the intervention group and 34 in the control group. During the 3-week intervention period, participants in the intervention group received brief digital nudges through designated WhatsApp groups. The messages were developed according to the Easy, Attractive, Social, and Timely (EAST) framework. Participants in the control group received no nudge messages. Gym visits were recorded electronically over 12 weeks through the fitness clubs' computerized entry systems. Self-reported measures included exercise self-efficacy, habit strength, and exercise adherence. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, longitudinal analysis of weekly gym attendance using generalized estimating equations (GEE), correlation analyses, and exploratory regression analysis.

RESULTS: Longitudinal GEE analysis showed a significant decline in weekly gym attendance over time (b=-0.074, SE 0.016; P<.001, incidence rate ratio [IRR]=0.929), corresponding to an approximately 7.1% decrease in expected weekly visits per study week. However, the group×week interaction was not significant (b=.009, SE 0.022; P=.68, IRR=1.009). Participants attending the gym at least twice weekly reported greater exercise habit strength (mean 33.89, SD 6.49 vs mean 28.70, SD 9.05; P=.02) and greater baseline exercise self-efficacy (mean 71.37, SD 12.50 vs mean 57.24, SD 14.61; P=.001). Mean weekly gym visits were positively correlated with exercise habit strength (r=0.444), exercise self-efficacy (r=0.498), and exercise adherence (r=0.507; all P<.001). In the exploratory regression analysis, exercise adherence was the only variable retained, and the model explained 25.7% of the variance in mean weekly gym visits (R2=.257; P<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Weekly gym attendance declined significantly over the 12-week follow-up period, but the rate of decline did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. However, exercise adherence, exercise self-efficacy, and exercise habit strength were positively associated with more frequent attendance, and participants attending at least twice weekly reported greater self-efficacy and stronger exercise habits. These exploratory findings identify potentially relevant behavioral factors for future adherence interventions.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of CD4 T-Cell Count and CD4/CD8 Ratio for Identifying HIV-Related Posterior Segment Disease: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CD4 T-cell count and CD4/CD8 ratio for identifying HIV-related posterior segment disease.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 53 patients infected with HIV who first visited the ophthalmology department of Nara Medical University between January 2014 and December 2025. CD4 T-cell count and CD4/CD8 ratio were analyzed for their association with HIV-related posterior segment disease. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to compare the discriminatory ability of these markers.

RESULTS: HIV-related posterior segment disease was identified in 13 of 53 patients (25%). Diagnoses included cytomegalovirus retinitis (n = 5), acute retinal necrosis (n = 1), and HIV microvasculopathy (n = 7). In univariate analysis, lower CD4 count, lower CD4/CD8 ratio, absence of antiretroviral therapy, and active cytomegalovirus infection were associated with posterior segment disease. In multivariable analysis, the CD4 count remained associated with posterior segment disease (odds ratio 0.58 per 50 cells/μL increase; 95% CI 0.33-0.99), whereas the CD4/CD8 ratio was not. ROC analysis showed a numerically higher area under the curve for CD4 count (0.81) than for CD4/CD8 ratio (0.74), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.27). A CD4 threshold of ≤100 cells/μL yielded a sensitivity of 92.3% and specificity of 75.0%.

CONCLUSION: The CD4 T-cell count showed numerically higher discriminatory performance than the CD4/CD8 ratio, although the difference was not statistically significant. A CD4 threshold of ≤100 cells/μL showed high sensitivity and may represent an exploratory threshold.

articles.title: Expert Consensus on Robot-Assisted Vascularized Bone Grafting for the Treatment of Early-Stage Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head.
articles.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) remains a progressive clinical challenge that predominantly affects young and active adults between 20 and 50 years of age. Without timely and effective surgical intervention, natural disease progression leads to structural subchondral fracture, articular surface collapse, and secondary hip osteoarthritis, ultimately necessitating total hip arthroplasty (THA). Given the elevated lifetime revision rates of prosthetic replacements in young patients, joint-preserving strategies are prioritized during the precollapse window [primarily Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO) stages I, II, and early IIIA]. Vascularized bone grafting, specifically free vascularized fibular grafting (FVFG) and pedicled vascularized bone transfers, provides both living osteogenic scaffolding and direct arterial perfusion. Traditional manual techniques are limited by steep learning curves, prolonged fluoroscopy exposure, multiple off-target guide-wire passes, and variable spatial placement of the graft. Computer-assisted orthopedic surgical robots, real-time optoelectronic navigation, and multimodal 2D/3D registration can improve spatial accuracy, reduce the number of drilling attempts, and support more reproducible subchondral seating. This multidisciplinary expert consensus synthesizes available clinical series, meta-analyses, biomechanical evaluations, and multicenter experience to provide standardized recommendations on indications, preoperative planning, surgical technique, perioperative management, expected outcomes, and future directions for robot-assisted vascularized bone grafting in early ONFH. The document emphasizes workflows that may reduce fluoroscopy exposure, operative time, and technical variability while optimizing graft placement near the subchondral plate in the weight-bearing region. Consensus statements are graded according to the strength of supporting evidence (primarily retrospective cohorts and low- to moderate-quality meta-analyses) and expert agreement.

articles.title: Comparison of Shoulder Field Anesthesia (SFA) with Interscalene Block (ISB) for Analgesia After Arthroscopic Shoulder Surgery: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB) is commonly used for analgesia after shoulder surgery but is associated with neurologic and respiratory complications, including hemidiaphragmatic paralysis. Surgeon-performed shoulder field anesthesia (SFA) is a landmark-guided, phrenic nerve-sparing technique that may provide effective analgesia with fewer complications. The purpose of this study was to compare SFA with ISB for pain control after arthroscopic shoulder surgery. We investigated whether SFA would provide noninferior analgesia as measured by cumulative 48-hour postoperative pain scores.

METHODS: In this randomized trial, patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder surgery were assigned to SFA or ISB. Postoperative pain was assessed using the numeric rating scale (NRS) at 2, 4, 8, 24, and 48 hours. Patient satisfaction was assessed at 48 hours. Other secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, hospital stay, and block-related complications.

RESULTS: Eighty patients (mean age, 47.7 ± 15.7 years; 53 men) completed the study. All patients were classified as White; 80% were of Middle Eastern ethnicity. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the SFA and ISB groups. The primary outcome analysis demonstrated a mean difference in the cumulative 48-hour NRS pain score of -0.824 (ISB - SFA), with a 95% confidence interval of -1.853 to 0.206. The upper limit of the confidence interval remained below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.5 NRS points, demonstrating noninferiority of SFA. ISB provided lower pain scores during the early postoperative period (4 to 8 hours), and pain scores converged thereafter. Hospital stay was shorter in the SFA group. Opioid consumption, patient satisfaction, and oxygen desaturation rates were similar between groups. Two cases of Horner syndrome and 1 respiratory event requiring intensive care occurred in the ISB group; none occurred in the SFA group.

CONCLUSIONS: SFA was noninferior to ISB for the prespecified cumulative 48-hour pain end point. ISB provided superior pain relief during the first 4 to 8 hours, but SFA offered a lung-sparing alternative with similar cumulative opioid requirements and patient satisfaction, fewer clinically apparent block-related complications, and a shorter hospital stay. These findings support a risk-benefit framework to guide individualized analgesic selection.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: STAT3 operates as an inflammation-dependent transcriptional switch in antiviral NK cells.
articles.abstract: The immune system integrates signals to regulate immune responses, forming complex context-dependent networks where identical cues produce distinct outcomes. Signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) transcription factors convert cytokine receptor engagement into transcriptional responses, serving as central regulatory hubs. How concurrent STAT activation across different environments shapes immune cell function remains unclear. Here, we show that STAT3 plays a context-dependent role in antiviral natural killer (NK) cells, either promoting or impairing adaptive responses depending on the inflammatory milieu during mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) infection. STAT3 is recruited to distinct genomic loci depending on IL-15 or type I interferon availability, thus driving alternative transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, STAT3 differentially regulates downstream transcription factors MYB and B lymphocyte-induced maturation protein-1 (BLIMP-1) to shape NK cell differentiation during homeostasis and infection. STAT3 relocation is governed by epigenetic mechanisms and preferred relocation toward distinct STAT motifs. Thus, STAT3 functions as a cytokine-sensing transcriptional switch integrating IL-15 and type I interferon signals to control lymphocyte adaptation during viral infection.

articles.title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1.
articles.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

articles.title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation.
articles.abstract: Bacteriophages ("phage") are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless "escape parameter," in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

articles.title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response.
articles.abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

articles.title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy.
articles.abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.

articles.title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus.
articles.abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth's energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERFACI). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models' underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERFACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

articles.title: AI for Poststroke Epilepsy: Scoping Review of Imaging-Based Prediction Models and Implications for African Settings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke seizures (PSS) and poststroke epilepsy (PSE) are important neurological complications associated with poorer functional recovery, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life after stroke. Neuroimaging plays a central role in identifying patients at increased risk, and recent advances in AI have enabled the development of imaging-based prediction models that may improve individualized risk stratification. However, the current evidence remains fragmented, and the extent to which these approaches are applicable to African health care settings is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to chart the existing global evidence on the development of imaging-based prediction models that can help in predicting PSS and PSE, especially AI-based ones. The purpose was to look into the imaging techniques, computational algorithms, and validation methodologies used and the representation of African populations.

METHODS: This scoping review was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework, and the results were presented based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. Articles searched using databases such as PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar involved the application of computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), angiography imaging techniques, radiomic markers, or multimodal neuroimaging techniques in statistical and AI-based prediction models for seizure-related outcomes after stroke.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies published between 2005 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria. The evidence demonstrated a clear methodological evolution from conventional imaging-based prediction models to radiomics, machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, and multimodal approaches. MRI and CT were the predominant imaging modalities, with cortical involvement, lesion location, infarct volume, hemorrhagic transformation, and quantitative radiomic features emerging as the most frequently reported imaging predictors. Most AI models relied on internal validation, while relatively few underwent external validation. The evidence base was concentrated in East Asia, Europe, and North America, with no eligible imaging-based AI models having been developed or externally validated using African datasets.

CONCLUSIONS: Imaging-based AI for predicting PSS and PSE has progressed rapidly, but important methodological and geographical gaps remain. Limited external validation, heterogeneous reporting, and the absence of African development and validation cohorts restrict confidence in the generalizability of existing models. Future research should prioritize the development of explainable imaging-based AI models using representative African neuroimaging datasets and their external validation in multicenter studies.

articles.title: The RLR-MAVS-IRF3 axis activates the IFN pathway to restrict Tonate virus (TONV) infection.
articles.abstract: Tonate virus (TONV) is a neglected mosquito-borne alphavirus of the Venezuelan equine encephalitis complex associated with febrile illness, encephalitis, and fetal central nervous system abnormalities. Yet, host pathways that sense TONV infection and restrict its replication remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the interaction between TONV and the type I interferon (IFN-I) system in human T98G and A549 cells. We show that TONV infection led to the accumulation of cytosolic double-stranded RNA and a robust IFN response. RIG-I and MDA5 depletion as well as that of MAVS and IRF3 strongly reduced TONV-induced IFN response. Disruption of RIG-I, MDA5, MAVS, or IRF3 resulted in an increase of dsRNA-positive cells and a higher viral RNA accumulation. Finally, we found that treatment with exogenous IFN-I strongly inhibits TONV replication reducing both viral RNA loads and infectious particle production. Thus, together, our results identify the RIG-I/MDA5-MAVS-IRF3 axis as a major pathway sensing TONV infection and establishing an IFN-I-dependent antiviral state, providing the first molecular characterization of TONV innate immune sensing in human cells.

articles.title: Venom vesicles from the parasitoid Ganaspis hookeri facilitate venom protein entry into host immune cells.
articles.abstract: The parasitoid wasp Ganaspis hookeri infects Drosophila melanogaster larvae, laying an egg and injecting venom directly into the host body cavity. While infected hosts mount an immune response in an attempt to eliminate the parasitoid egg, parasitoid venom proteins act to inhibit these host responses and manipulate host physiology to ensure infection success. A key immune suppressive venom protein in G. hookeri is a venom-specific isoform of the SERCA (Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium-ATPase) calcium pump. However, SERCA is a large hydrophobic protein, and the mechanism by which it and other venom proteins are transported into host cells is not well understood. Electron microscopy and nanoparticle tracking analysis of G. hookeri venom revealed the presence of venom extracellular vesicles (vEVs) as a putative transport mechanism. We characterized the biophysical properties of vEVs, and found that G. hookeri venom contains multiple vesicle types that are distinguishable by size, zeta potential, protein content, and density. A subset of these vEVs contain SERCA, and we found that fluorescently labeled vEVs are able to enter into host immune cells and alter host intracellular calcium levels, and that disruption of vesicle integrity results in the loss of this SERCA activity in host cells. Together, our data support a model in which G. hookeri venom proteins, including SERCA, are packaged into an array of venom vesicles, and are transported into host cells for immune suppression.

articles.title: Gallbladder Involvement in Pediatric Hepatitis A: Findings From an Italian Outbreak Cohort.
articles.abstract:
