BACKGROUND: Gallbladder involvement during acute hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is generally considered an uncommon extrahepatic manifestation, although recent reports suggest it may be underrecognized. We evaluated the prevalence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of gallbladder abnormalities in a multicenter cohort of children hospitalized with acute HAV infection during an Italian outbreak.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter observational study, including consecutive children with laboratory-confirmed acute HAV infection admitted to 4 tertiary pediatric hospitals between January and May 2026. Clinical, laboratory and ultrasonographic findings were collected. All patients underwent abdominal ultrasonography during the acute phase of illness.

RESULTS: Thirty-three children were included. Gallbladder abnormalities compatible with acute acalculous cholecystitis were identified in 18 patients (54.5%), including marked gallbladder wall thickening (>7 mm) in 8. Children with gallbladder involvement did not exhibit more severe clinical manifestations or greater biochemical impairment than those without ultrasonographic abnormalities. Serum bile acids were markedly elevated in most tested patients but were not associated with gallbladder abnormalities. All patients were managed conservatively, and none developed gallbladder perforation, empyema, gangrene or required surgical intervention. Complete clinical recovery with progressive normalization of laboratory and ultrasonographic findings was observed in all cases.

CONCLUSIONS: Systematic ultrasonography identified gallbladder involvement in more than half of children hospitalized with acute HAV infection, suggesting that this manifestation may be substantially underrecognized rather than truly rare. Despite frequent ultrasonographic abnormalities, the clinical course was uniformly benign, supporting conservative management in the absence of complications.

articles.title: Bacterial immune priming and Wolbachia-mediated dengue blocking in Aedes albopictus mosquitoes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wolbachia is a maternally-transmitted bacterial endosymbiont that is highly prevalent amongst arthropods. Many Wolbachia strains induce pathogen blocking, thereby protecting their hosts from pathogenic microbial infections. Blocking against pathogenic bacteria occurs in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, where Wolbachia has been artificially established by microinjection. However, in Drosophila fruit flies, it occurs after oral bacterial challenge but not after systemic challenge via injection. Pathogen blocking has been linked to increased host immune activity associated with Wolbachia infection. This is similar in principle to immune priming, a memory immune response in insects, where sub-lethal exposure to a pathogen increases the ability to survive future infections. Aedes albopictus mosquitoes naturally harbor Wolbachia; however, the extent to which native Wolbachia-mediated pathogen blocking and immune priming influence host response to infection remains unclear. Accordingly, we sought to characterize the response of Wolbachia-infected Ae. albopictus to bacterial challenge, and to determine whether the combination of these microbes could hinder a subsequent infection with dengue virus.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We challenged adult female Ae. albopictus with and without their native Wolbachia infection with a sub-lethal dose of four mosquito-associated bacteria: Micrococcus, Staphylococcus (gram positive), Brevundimonas, Enterobacter (gram negative). Assessing post-challenge mortality, we observed that Wolbachia infection reduced cumulative mortality and delayed the onset of senescence amongst mosquitoes challenged with each bacterium. However, this protective effect was stronger against gram positive bacteria. Bacteria-primed Ae. albopictus were then orally challenged with DENV. We observed that mosquitoes that experienced a pre-challenge with gram negative bacteria were associated with reduced DENV prevalence and viral load, whereas Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes exhibited further reductions in viral load.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: We highlight novel characteristics of native Wolbachia infection in Ae. albopictus mosquitoes, with protection against bacterial-induced mortality, and interactions between pathogen blocking and bacterial priming that may depend on bacterial gram status. These findings provide insight into the immune interactions associated with native Wolbachia and build on our understanding of adaptive immunity in mosquitoes.

articles.title: Radiofrequency Ablation for Selective Reduction in Complicated Monochorionic Twin Pregnancies: Pregnancy-Level and Neonatal Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Monochorionic twin pregnancies may be complicated by shared placental vascular anastomoses and hemodynamic interdependence between fetuses. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a vaso-occlusive option for selective reduction when continuation of the affected fetus is expected to endanger the co-twin.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 39 monochorionic twin pregnancies treated with RFA at two tertiary centers between January 2017 and December 2025. Indications were grouped as TTTS/TAPS-related conditions, selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR)-related conditions, twin reversed arterial perfusion (TRAP) sequence, and discordant major fetal anomaly. The primary outcome was live birth of at least one fetus. Secondary outcomes included miscarriage, stillbirth/intrauterine fetal demise, termination after RFA, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), gestational age at delivery, birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, neonatal death, and survival to neonatal hospital discharge.

RESULTS: The main indications were sFGR-related conditions (14/39, 35.9%) and TTTS/TAPS-related conditions (12/39, 30.8%). Live birth of at least one fetus occurred in 38/39 pregnancies (97.4%), and pregnancy-level survival to neonatal hospital discharge occurred in 37/39 pregnancies (94.9%). PPROM after RFA occurred in 2/39 pregnancies (5.1%). Among pregnancies with live birth, median gestational age at delivery was 38.00 weeks (IQR, 34.00-39.00). Exploratory comparisons across indication groups, including direct TTTS/TAPS-related versus TRAP comparisons for gestational age at delivery and procedure-to-delivery interval, were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: RFA was associated with high rates of live birth and survival to neonatal hospital discharge in this cohort of complicated monochorionic twin pregnancies. Exploratory subgroup comparisons were not statistically significant; therefore, observed indication-specific patterns should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: LISA failure and school-age motor impairment in very preterm infants: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Background Less invasive surfactant administration (LISA) reduces the need for early invasive mechanical ventilation in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome. However, LISA failure (LISA-F), defined as the need for mechanical ventilation within 72 hours of life, occurs in a substantial proportion of cases. While the short-term complications of LISA-F are well described, the impact on long-term neurodevelopment remains unclear. Methods This retrospective cohort study included preterm infants born between 24+0 and 29+6 weeks' gestation who received surfactant therapy in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit. Infants were classified into three groups: LISA success (LISA-S), LISA-F, or primary intubation (PI). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 5.5 years of age using WPPSI-IV-NL for cognition and mABC-2 for motor function. Multivariate analyses were adjusted for gestational age, birth weight z-score, antenatal corticosteroid exposure and severe intraventricular hemorrhage. Results Among 295 infants, 225 (76.3%) received LISA; 32% experienced LISA-F. Follow-up data were available for 168 of 246 survivors (68.3%). LISA-F was independently associated with lower motor scores than LISA-S (adjusted β -2.1; p=0.004), but not with cognitive outcomes. Infants who underwent primary intubation had significantly lower cognitive scores than those in the LISA-S group (adjusted β -5.1; p=0.038). Invasive mechanical ventilation within the first 72 hours was independently associated with motor developmental delay (aOR:3.9; 95% CI 1.2-13.2; p=0.028) Conclusion LISA-F is associated with adverse motor outcomes at school age. Our findings suggest that the early respiratory trajectory after LISA is more relevant to long term motor development than the initial surfactant administration technique itself.

articles.title: Fluid Intake and Kidney Function: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fluid intake is widely recommended in clinical practice, yet evidence linking habitual fluid intake to kidney outcomes remains inconsistent. We evaluated dose-response associations between fluid intake volume and kidney function decline or prevalent advanced chronic kidney disease.

METHODS: We searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library through Feb 2025 for adult studies reporting total fluid intake, plain water intake, or urine volume in relation to eGFR decline or prevalent advanced-stage chronic kidney disease. Random-effects meta-regression and two-stage dose-response meta-analysis were used to assess linear and non-linear associations, with prespecified subgroup analyses by baseline kidney function.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies including 70,053 participants were included. Higher total fluid intake was linearly associated with slower eGFR decline (p = 0.02; β = 0.97 mL/min/1.73 m²/year; 95% CI 0.15-1.79) and with lower odds of prevalent advanced-stage chronic kidney disease (p < 0.001; log-OR -0.27; 95% CI -0.43 to -0.11). In subgroup analyses, this association was observed in studies with mean baseline eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² (p = 0.016), but not in studies with mean baseline eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m². Evidence for plain water intake and urine volume was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher daily total fluid intake, within the ranges studied, was associated with slower eGFR decline and lower odds of prevalent advanced CKD, particularly among studies with mean baseline eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m². Because the evidence was predominantly observational, these findings cannot establish that increasing fluid intake preserves kidney function. Future studies should distinguish plain water from other beverage categories and incorporate objective biomarkers of hydration and volume status.

articles.title: Guidelines for Colonic Diverticular Disease-2026, Second Edition: Management of Diverticular Bleeding and Acute Diverticulitis.
articles.abstract: Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.

articles.title: Prenatal echocardiographic predictors that increase the risk of urgent Ballon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) after birth in patients with Dextro-Transposition of the Great Arteries- Retrospective Study from Tertiary Center Lodz- Poland ICZMP (2014-2024).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) is a critical congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring prompt postnatal intervention, primarily: a line for Prostin infusion, hospitalization in an Intensive Care Unit, and in some cases, Balloon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) as a rescue procedure before planned Arterial Switch Operation (ASO). In this part, we focus on prenatal prediction of postnatal BAS.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the Department of Prenatal Cardiology, Polish Mother's Memorial Hospital in Lodz, covering the years 2014-2024. From a total of 112 prenatally diagnosed d-TGA cases, 70 fetuses (46 with isolated d-TGA and 24 with d-TGA and VSD) met the inclusion criteria; follow-up of four pregnancies ended up in other hospitals, so the final series was 66 cases. Statistical analyses were performed using Statistica software.

RESULTS: Out of 66 analyzed cases, 32 newborns (48%) required postnatal BAS, with 87.5% of these procedures performed within the first 24-48 hours of life. Prenatal echocardiography correctly predicted the postnatal management pathway in 90.9% of cases (60/66), identifying all 26 neonates requiring urgent balloon atrial septostomy (100% positive predictive value), while 6 neonates in the planned group required unexpected postnatal septostomy. We noted that the 18% (n=6) of cases not identified prenatally occurred when the last scan was performed > 14 days before birth, suggesting that the time interval significantly impacts the reliability of late-gestation FO assessment. The study identified 10 prenatal "red flags," including FO size < 3 mm, bi-directional FO flow, and pulmonary vein velocity ≥ 45 cm/s and other features, as high-reliability indicators for urgent postnatal intervention.

CONCLUSION: Prenatal functional assessment of the foramen ovale in the late third trimester was highly effective in predicting the need for postnatal urgent BAS in d-TGA cases. The accuracy of these "red flags" was significantly higher when the last fetal echocardiogram was performed within 14 days to delivery.

articles.title: Urinary biomarkers at hospital admission and community-acquired acute kidney injury: A prospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine the sensitivity and specificity of a 13-urinary biomarker (uBM) panel for identifying community-acquired acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) and to assess whether these biomarkers were independently associated with CA-AKI.

METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital. Adults admitted through the emergency department were included. CA-AKI was defined as a ≥0.3 mg/dl decrease in serum creatinine (SCr) within 48 hours or a ≥50% decrease within 7 days. Blood samples were collected daily for SCr measurement, and urine samples were obtained at admission for uBM assessment. All the uBM were classified as abnormal when they exceeded the 75th percentile of the distribution.

RESULTS: 731 patients were included (55% male, median age of 61 years; 48% had hypertension, 28% had diabetes mellitus, and 23% had heart failure). The main reasons for hospitalization were respiratory (32%), genitourinary (15%), and cardiovascular (11%) diseases. CA-AKI was diagnosed in 26% of the patients. Compared with patients without CA-AKI, those with CA-AKI showed higher rates of elevation in four uBM: KIM-1 (31% vs. 23%; p=0.032), TIMP-2*IGFBP-7 (30% vs. 23%; p=0.045), clusterin (32% vs. 22%; p=0.011), and MCP-1 (33% vs. 22%; p=0.003). The sensitivity and specificity of uBM for detecting CA-AKI ranged from 23% to 33% and from 74% to 78%, respectively, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ranged from 0.485 to 0.554. Logistic regression analyses identified conditions independently associated with CA-AKI, including: hypotension [OR (95% CI): 2.07 (1.33-3.23); p=0.001], dehydration [OR (95% CI): 2.01 (1.40-2.91); p<0.001], chronic kidney disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.19-3.35); p=0.009], genitourinary tract disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.26-3.10); p=0.003], chronic liver disease [OR (95% CI): 1.69 (1.09-2.61); p=0.018], and elevation of one or more of the following uBM: KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1 [OR (95% CI): 1.51 (1.06-2.14); p=0.022].

CONCLUSION: The expression of one or more of four uBM at emergency department admission (KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1) may help identify patients with a higher probability of having CA-AKI, even with modest AUC results.

articles.title: Telehealth and Digital Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension in Latin America and the Caribbean: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Telemedicine journal and e-health : the official journal of the American Telemedicine Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telehealth, remote monitoring, and other digital interventions may support chronic disease management, but evidence from Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) remains fragmented. We evaluated clinical effectiveness and characterized human support, clinical integration, and implementation.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, and LILACS were searched through July 2026 for studies of digital interventions in adults with type 2 diabetes or hypertension in LAC. Random-effects meta-analyses were restricted to randomized trials and used restricted maximum likelihood estimation, Hartung-Knapp adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs). Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Thirty-six studies (41 reports) from 12 countries were included: 15 randomized and 21 nonrandomized. Six trials (n = 689) showed lower HbA1c (mean difference [MD] -1.23 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.19 to -0.26; I2 = 83.8%; PI: -3.64 to 1.18). Seven trials (n = 2,280) showed lower systolic blood pressure (SBP; MD: -4.97 mmHg; 95% CI: -7.15 to -2.79; I2 = 26.1%; PI: -8.85 to -1.09), and five (n = 1,825) showed lower diastolic blood pressure (DBP; MD: -3.46 mmHg; 95% CI: -5.69 to -1.22; I2 = 76.1%; PI: -9.24 to 2.33). Certainty was moderate for SBP and low for HbA1c and DBP. Professional support and clinical integration were common, whereas sustainability, scalability, interoperability, costs, and equity were inconsistently evaluated.

CONCLUSIONS: Digitally enabled chronic care may improve glycemic and blood-pressure control in LAC, with the most consistent evidence for SBP. Heterogeneous intervention models and limited implementation evidence warrant comparative effectiveness-implementation studies.

articles.title: Sparse-EWI: Towards an automated and real time focal arrhythmia mapping technique - in silico to clinical validation.
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and identifying the origin of focal ventricular arrhythmias such as Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVC) is essential for precision radiofrequency ablation treatment. Electromechanical Wave Imaging (EWI) is a noninvasive high-frame-rate echocardiography-based technique that maps the cardiac electromechanical activation throughout the entire heart. However, estimation of activation times across the myocardium requires manual annotation of approximately 150 points per apical view, which is labor-intensive and limits clinical adoption. This study introduces an efficient, clinically applicable sparse-EWI method, in which only 15 seed points per view are manually annotated and activation times at the remaining points are estimated automatically through recursive activation-time selection based on the strain correlation between adjacent points. Sparse-EWI was compared to conventional EWI using a simulated electromechanical heart model coupled with a 3-D Field II ultrasound simulation, an open-chest canine paced at five different left-ventricular locations, and three PVC patients, with high-frame-rate acquisitions performed at 2000 fps using a 2.5 MHz phased-array transducer and a single diverging-wave transmit. Sparse-EWI reduced the number of initialization points by 10× without compromising accuracy. Relative to conventional EWI, the sparse-EWI activation-time maps achieved correlation coefficients of 0.74, 0.82±0.13, and 0.75±0.12; accuracies of 66.64%, 85.9±7.4%, and 84.2±8.2%; and source-localization errors of 7.10 mm, 2.40±2.80 mm, and 1.91±2.36 mm across the simulated, preclinical, and clinical datasets, respectively. The spatial reduction also resulted in approximately five-fold higher computational speed compared to conventional EWI, decreasing processing time from ∼900 s to ∼182 s per view. In summary, sparse-EWI achieved a 90% reduction in required initialization points and approximately five-fold faster processing across simulated, preclinical, and clinical datasets, increasing EWI's translation and providing rapid feedback during ablative treatment.

articles.title: Improving Postpolypectomy Surveillance Decisions Using an Automated Analysis of Colonoscopy and Histopathology Reports: 2-Center Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence.

OBJECTIVE: We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations.

METHODS: We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers ("pots"), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients.

RESULTS: Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance (no follow-up F1-score of 0.98 at GSTT and 0.97 at SWB; site check F1-score of 0.93 at GSTT and 0.91 at SWB; 3-year follow-up F1-score of 0.86 at GSTT and 0.80 at SWB; cancer alert F1-score of 1.00 at GSTT and 1.00 at SWB). The comparison to current clinical practice showed that the tool would improve guideline adherence primarily by reducing potential undersurveillance.

CONCLUSIONS: This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.

articles.title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts.

METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout.

RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia.

CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

articles.title: Patient Blood Management Adoption and Transfusion-Threshold Concordance Among Romanian Anesthesiologists: National Survey Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romania issued national patient blood management (PBM) guidelines in 2018. A 2023 national survey described the overall uptake of PBM among anesthesiologists but did not examine which clinicians and institutions adopted PBM, nor whether stated transfusion thresholds aligned with a study-defined restrictive reference.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify determinants of PBM adoption and to quantify transfusion-trigger concordance, using a planned, exploratory, cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 survey.

METHODS: We analyzed 511 responses to the 38-item Romanian Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care (SRATI) PBM survey. Three adoption outcomes (applying PBM, a formal hospital PBM group, and routine preoperative anemia treatment) were modeled by multivariable logistic regression against physician grade, hospital category, and local PBM educational events. Eight standardized clinical vignettes (age×cardiac disease×bleeding state) were scored against a restrictive hemoglobin reference (7 g/dL general; 8 g/dL with cardiac disease). The reported timing of the preanesthetic consultation (4 frequency items) was additionally examined as a determinant of preoperative anemia treatment. This was a planned, exploratory secondary analysis; the robustness of the main findings was examined in sensitivity analyses that accounted for survey attrition and for alternative transfusion-threshold scoring rules.

RESULTS: Overall, 73.7% (373/506) reported applying PBM, 33.1% (158/477) reported a formal PBM group, and 33.5% (117/349) reported routine preoperative anemia treatment. Local PBM educational events were the strongest adjusted correlate of reported adoption (applying PBM: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 9.78, 95% CI 4.33-22.07; P<.001; formal group: aOR 7.72, 95% CI 4.30-13.88; P<.001). Earlier preanesthetic consultation was associated with routine preoperative anemia treatment (aOR 1.79 per frequency level for consultation more than 7 days before surgery, 95% CI 1.36-2.35; P<.001). Transfusion-trigger concordance was lower for older than younger patients in otherwise identical scenarios (eg, active bleeding without cardiac disease: 195/345, 56.5% at ≥65 years vs 288/347, 83% at <65 years), and 56.5% (196/347) endorsed a liberal trigger (hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL) in at least one noncardiac scenario. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with a restrictive transfusion pattern (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 0.69-1.98; P=.56). Findings were unchanged across scoring rules, and reported PBM application was similar among respondents who did and did not complete the demographic block (246/329, 74.8% vs 127/177, 71.8%; P=.53).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cross-sectional analysis, reported PBM adoption was associated more strongly with local educational activity than with hospital category or physician seniority. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with restrictive stated thresholds in hypothetical scenarios, and respondents selected more liberal thresholds for older patients. Standardized multidisciplinary pathways, earlier anemia screening shared with the surgical team, and education focused on transfusion decisions may help address these gaps. Prospective studies using observed process measures, transfusion practice, and clinical outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries: Insights from 3473 births of a 13-year prospective cohort study in France.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although poorly researched, unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries are considered to carry a high risk of maternal and neonatal complications, with the primary suspected risk factor being the home-to-hospital travel time. The objective of this study was to describe the characteristics of unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries and to identify factors associated with maternal and neonatal complications.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Data were collected from the French unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries registry (79 of 402 mobile intensive care units). Analysis included 3473 deliveries between October 2011 and June 2024.

RESULTS: Mean women maternal age was 32.0 ± 5.4 years (range 15-49). Median parity was 2.0 (IQR 2.0-3.0). Gestational age was 39.1 ± 2.3 weeks. Most pregnancies were low-risk (84%). Mean home-to-hospital travel time was 20.7 ± 13.6 min (range 0-200), with more than 45 min for only 3% of women (110/3221) and over 1 h for 1% (23/3221). Maternal complications accounted in 8.4% of women (290/3472), placental hemorrhage in 4.5% (156/3471) and maternal death in 0.1% (2/3471). Perinatal complications occurred in 4.4% (149/3393) of all deliveries, with neonatal deaths accounting for 1.1% (38/3456). Among unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries, factors associated with maternal and/or neonatal complications included birth at 32 + 0-33 + 6 weeks of gestation (adjusted OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.69 to 4.83; p < 0.0001), birth before 32 + 0 weeks of gestation (adjusted OR 25.21, 95% CI 12.13 to 52.40; p < 0.0001), and neonatal hypothermia upon hospital admission (adjusted OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.76; p = 0.019). Hypothermia affected 63% of newborns (1256/2002). Unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries prior to mobile intensive care unit arrival were significantly associated with neonatal hypothermia on-site (adjusted OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.57 to 2.61; p < 0.0001) and at hospital admission (adjusted OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.21 to 2.00; p = 0.0005).

CONCLUSIONS: Severe outcomes of unplanned out-of-hospital deliveries were uncommon but did occur. Complications were associated with prematurity and hypothermia, but not with home-to-hospital travel time. These findings highlight the importance of universal prehospital preparedness, with particular attention to early prevention of neonatal hypothermia and initial hemorrhage management.

articles.title: Decreasing response phase lights and siren use through modification of dispatch priority response for 9-1-1 responses to personal emergency response system activations: an interventional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Emergency medical services (EMS) responses to personal emergency response systems (PERS) activations predominantly involve low-acuity patients. Recent evidence demonstrates that while most PERS calls are dispatched lights and siren (L&S), only 1% result in L&S transport. Reduction of L&S use through modified dispatch priority response for PERS calls has not been evaluated. Our objective was to evaluate the efficacy of modifying dispatch priority response mode for PERS calls to non-L&S response, the resulting reduction in response phase L&S use, and potential impact on time critical interventions.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational pre-post analysis comparing PERS responses in two 11-month periods before (January-November 2023) and after (January-November 2024) revising the dispatch priority response for PERS calls to non-L&S in December 2023. We evaluated response mode and transport mode. The primary outcome was total hours/month of response phase L&S use, with L&S duration computed as the interval between unit dispatched and arrival (patient contact) or call cancellation. Descriptive statistics were computed followed by interrupted time series analysis (ITSA) to assess the impact of the intervention on the primary outcome and maintenance of the effect across the post-intervention period (p for post-intervention linear trend).

RESULTS: Analysis included 3,262 PERS calls (pre-intervention = 1,634; post-intervention = 1,628). L&S response occurred in 98% (n = 1,601) of pre-intervention calls and 12% (n = 192) of post-intervention calls (p < 0.001). The prevalence of L&S transport was similar in both periods (0.9% vs 0.9%, p = 0.99). The ITSA revealed an immediate 13.8-hour/month decrease in response phase L&S use (95% confidence interval: -16.2 to -11.3) that was sustained across the post-intervention period (p > 0.05). Total response phase L&S hours decreased 86%, from 172 hours in the pre-intervention period to 24 hours during the post-intervention period. Importantly, only four post-intervention calls (0.2%) involved a non-L&S response followed by L&S transport, with just one of these requiring advanced life support interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: Modifying dispatch priority response for PERS calls reduced L&S responses and yielded a marked decrease in hours of L&S use which was maintained overtime. As the industry advocates for safer, more judicious L&S use, additional low-acuity call types should be identified for similar dispatch priority response revision.

articles.title: Influence of Perioperative Variables on Surgical Site Infection in Patients With Frailty and Prefrailty Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) in patients with frailty undergoing myocardial revascularization is a major clinical challenge, and there is a gap in the literature related to this topic.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify perioperative variables associated with SSI in patients with frailty and prefrailty undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting within 30 days of the procedure.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 467 patients with frailty or prefrailty aged 60 years and older who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting in 6 Brazilian centers between January 2018 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the Fried criteria. SSI was defined as a wound with exposed tissue with positive culture requiring antibiotic treatment. Univariate and multivariate analyses were carried out.

RESULTS: The rate of SSI was 5.6% (26/467). The New York Heart Association classification (P=.02), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI; P=.01), use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB; P=.003), CPB time (P=.02), total surgery time (P<.001), occurrence of bleeding (P=.04), mechanical ventilation time (P=.001), length of hospital stay (P<.001), intensive care unit stay (P<.001), and need for reoperation (P<.001) variables were associated with SSI in unadjusted comparisons. In the multivariate model, the CCI (odds ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-1.99; P<.001) and use of CPB (odds ratio 4.89, 95% CI 1.71-13.94; P=.003) were independently associated with SSI.

CONCLUSIONS: The CCI and the use of CPB were independently associated with SSI.

articles.title: In-Simulation Versus Post-Simulation Debriefing in Medical Training: A Scoping Review and Theoretical Framework for Military Application.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Simulation-based medical training is important for readiness. Feedback and debriefing are important components of simulation that support learning. Debriefs for military training are traditionally conducted at the conclusion of training, but recent evidence in the civilian medical training literature suggests that in-simulation debriefing may provide benefits for skill acquisition. The purpose of this scoping review is to map the body of literature examining post-simulation and in-simulation debriefing, highlight trends in the literature, and identify research gaps.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review of the literature was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute Scoping Review Methodology, searching PubMed, the Web of Science Core Collection, and gray literature. Studies were included if they evaluated simulation-based emergency medicine or critical care medical training with an in-simulation debriefing intervention compared to post-simulation debriefing, measured at least one learning or performance outcome, and included a randomization element. Studies were excluded if they lacked a comparison group, involved non-acute care, utilized solely device-generated feedback, or did not explicitly articulate in-simulation debriefing protocols.

RESULTS: A total of 21 articles met inclusion criteria; none involved military populations. The majority of studies (90.5%) employed rapid cycle deliberate practice as the in-simulation debriefing method, and the most studied domain was cardiac arrest and resuscitation (57.1%). No studies reported performance or retention measures favoring post-simulation debriefing, and 77.8% of studies measuring time to intervention found significant improvements when in-simulation debriefing was utilized. Effect sizes were only reported in 14.3% of included studies.

CONCLUSIONS: The majority of reviewed studies reported outcomes favoring in-simulation debriefing; no studies favored post-simulation debriefing for performance measures. Effective implementation of in-simulation debriefing in a military training context would require deliberate instructor development and standardized methods for aligning debriefing methods with the experience level of the target audience. Future research should examine the effects of in-simulation debriefing on tactical medical skill performance and the time to intervention in a military training context.

articles.title: Search for Tenebrio molitor (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae) behaviorally active compounds in Aspergillus flavus (Eurotiales: Aspergillaceae)-infected grain.
articles.abstract: Application of insecticides for pest control must be minimized due to well-known risks to human health. Application of environmentally friendly means is the best option. For stored product pests' control, new means are needed alongside a deep understanding of the ecology and behavior of the pests. The present study investigated whether the odor released from wheat grain infected by mold fungus Aspergillus flavus (Eurotiales: Aspergillaceae) influences the behavior of the yellow mealworm (Tenebrio molitor L. (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae)), a stored product pest of economic importance with worldwide distribution. Analysis of video-recorded behavior and computer data analysis revealed a significant difference in reactions depending on the beetle's sex. Females were more sensitive to fungus contamination as they discriminated between A. flavus-infected and uninfected wheat grains from the onset of infection, while males discriminated only after a 5-day period. Analysis of single volatile organic compounds (VOCs) revealed the presence of both repellents and attractants. Among those, hexanal was repellent for both males and females, 1-octen-3-ol was repellent for males and indifferent to females, 1-hexanol was attractive to females and repellent (at high concentrations only) to males, and 3-methylbutan-1-ol was attractive to females (at high concentrations only) and indifferent to males. Hexanal, as a potential repellent, was suggested for further testing under grain storage conditions.

articles.title: The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation.
articles.abstract: The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is essential for mounting robust innate immunity, yet its chronic activation can drive detrimental inflammation. Although multiple cell-autonomous mechanisms that restrain STING signaling have been reported, whether inflammatory mediators within the tissue microenvironment regulate STING activation remains elusive. Using herpes simplex virus type 1 infection as a model of STING activation, we revealed that the COX2-PGE2-PKA axis functions as a critical negative regulator of STING-mediated antiviral innate immunity. Mechanistically, PGE2 acts through the EP4-PKA cascade to induce PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-mediated mitophagy by phosphorylating STOML2 at Ser29. This pathway facilitates the clearance of damaged mitochondria that serve as a source of immunostimulatory cytosolic mitochondrial DNA, thereby attenuating downstream STING activation and type I interferons while promoting viral replication. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial quality control as the mechanistic link between PGE2 signaling and mtDNA-dependent STING activation and identify the COX2-PGE2-PKA pathway as a druggable therapeutic target to enhance STING-mediated innate immunity.

articles.title: NAD+ precursor treatment prevents cardiomyopathy but disrupts erythroid maturation in mitochondrial progeria.
Divergent interplay between STIM1 and STIM2 sets the efficacy of central synapses.
articles.abstract: Stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) are endoplasmic reticulum resident calcium (Ca2+ sensors that modulate Ca2+ homeostasis. Mammals express two isoforms, STIM1 and STIM2, but whether they serve redundant or distinct roles in neurotransmission remains poorly defined. Using Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiology in hippocampal neurons lacking STIM1, STIM2, or both, we examined presynaptic and postsynaptic functions of STIMs at excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Both isoforms redundantly activated store-operated Ca2+ entry and amplified presynaptic Ca2+ influx, sustaining neurotransmitter release by expanding the readily releasable pool of synaptic vesicles and accelerating vesicle replenishment. These presynaptic roles were synapse specific: STIM1 predominantly supported excitatory synapses, whereas STIM2 was critical for the inhibitory counterparts. Postsynaptically, STIM1 and STIM2 exerted opposing effects on glutamate and GABA receptor levels, such that simultaneous loss of both isoforms rescued postsynaptic function. Together, the findings show that STIM1 and STIM2 differentially tune synaptic efficacy according to synapse type and subcellular compartment.

articles.title: The lysis mechanism of the haloarchaeal virus HFTV1.
articles.abstract: Tailed bacteriophages can lyse their host with help of the holin-endolysin system. However, for archaeal tailed viruses (arTVs), whose archaeal hosts have a fundamentally different cell envelope, lysis mechanisms are unknown. In this study, we use the model archaeal virus-host system: Haloferax tailed virus 1 (HFTV1), which infects the methanobacteriote Haloferax gibbonsii LR2-5. We identified and characterized the lysis protein GP33, a small membrane protein that has no sequence homology with bacterial holins. Overexpression resulted in cell lysis, and the protein forms foci near the cell envelope. Molecular dynamics simulation suggests that it forms pores from which the lipids are repelled, which might result in cell lysis. Indeed, atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed that GP33 forms pores in membranes, which lead to complete membrane disruption at higher concentrations. With this work, we gain insight into a lysis mechanism from a tailed archaeal virus at the molecular level.

articles.title: Consensus machine learning for interpretable road-user fatality risk analysis: Evidence from the Canadian National Collision Database.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Fatal road traffic collisions account for a small proportion of reported crashes but impose a disproportionate societal and public health burden. This study evaluates interpretable machine-learning models and proposes a consensus machine learning (CML) framework to identify robust predictors associated with fatal collision risk using Canadian collision data.

METHODS: Person-level records from the Canadian National Collision Database (NCDB) covering 2014-2021 were used to classify fatal and nonfatal collision outcomes. Balanced random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and neural network models were developed using a common preprocessing framework. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) and precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC). Permutation-based feature-importance rankings were subsequently aggregated using the proposed CML framework to identify predictors that remained consistently important across models and reporting years.

RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the strongest predictive performance (ROC-AUC = 0.932; PR-AUC = 0.714), followed by balanced random forest (ROC-AUC = 0.898; PR-AUC = 0.585) and the neural network (ROC-AUC = 0.886; PR-AUC = 0.587). Across the three machine-learning models, collision configuration, traffic control, collision hour, and the number of vehicles involved consistently ranked among the most influential predictors associated with fatal collision risk. Roadway configuration, roadway alignment, road-surface condition, weather conditions, vehicle characteristics, and safety-device use also contributed to prediction, although their relative importance varied among models. The CML framework further identified the leading predictors of fatal collisions: collision configuration, road-surface conditions, time of collision, number of vehicles involved, roadway configuration, and weather conditions.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed CML framework consistently identified important predictors across multiple machine-learning algorithms and reporting years, providing a robust and interpretable approach to understanding fatal collision risk. Two of the defined categories, crash characteristics and traffic and environmental conditions, were identified as key feature sets for predicting collision fatalities. These findings provide evidence to support engineering, policy, enforcement, and education initiatives aimed at reducing fatal collisions while highlighting the value of consensus-based machine learning as a complementary decision-support tool for transportation safety planning.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk associated with first-line Janus kinase inhibitors versus TNF inhibitors in patients with RA: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) between tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) and Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) when initiated as first-line advanced therapy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

METHODS: Using the Korean nationwide claims database, we identified patients newly diagnosed with RA between 2010 and 2015. Patients who initiated TNFi or JAKi as first-line advanced therapy were selected for analysis. Patients were followed from initiation of TNFi or JAKi through June 2024. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or coronary revascularization. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied in the total cohort. We additionally performed propensity score (PS)-matched analyses to address confounding by indication. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to baseline cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: The study included 6,174 patients (TNFi = 5,152; JAKi = 1,022). The incidence rates of MACE were 4.1 and 3.6 per 1,000 person-years in the TNFi and JAKi groups, respectively. MACE risk did not differ significantly between JAKi and TNFi in the total study cohort (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.636, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.283 to 1.429) or in the PS-matched population (adjusted HR 0.715, 95% CI 0.187 to 2.739). Results were consistent across all prespecified subgroups, including patients with baseline cardiovascular risk factors.

CONCLUSION: First-line use of JAKi was not associated with an increased risk of MACE compared with TNFi. These findings provide real-world evidence supporting the cardiovascular safety of JAKi as first-line advanced therapy in patients with RA.

articles.title: Oral High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection Among Women Reporting Same-Sex Sexual Contact: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2009-2016.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the prevalence of oral high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection between women reporting any lifetime sexual contact with a female partner (WSW) and women reporting exclusively male partners (WSM) in a nationally representative U.S. sample, and to assess how much of the difference is explained by lifetime partner count.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of women aged 18-69 in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2009-2016 with evaluated oral HPV genotyping and sexual behavior data. Survey-weighted prevalence was estimated in the full sample. WSW were matched 1:2 to WSM by propensity score on age, smoking, race/ethnicity, and poverty income ratio. Logistic regression in the matched sample additionally adjusted for lifetime partner count (≥10, and four categories).

RESULTS: Of 7,943 women, 751 were WSW; 724 (96.4%) of them also reported male partners. Weighted oral HR-HPV prevalence was 2.84% (95% CI 1.57-4.69%) among WSW and 1.04% (0.78-1.35%) among WSM. After matching, WSW had higher odds of infection (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.15-3.64). WSW reported more lifetime partners (median 12 vs 5), including more male partners (median 10 vs 5). Adjustment for partner count attenuated the association below statistical significance (≥10 partners: OR 1.46, 0.79-2.72).

CONCLUSIONS: WSW, nearly all of whom also reported male partners, had higher odds of oral HR-HPV infection than demographically matched WSM; lifetime partner count explained part of this difference. A history of female partners should not be taken to imply lower oral HPV risk, and HPV vaccination should be offered according to current recommendations.

articles.title: Toward clinically actionable lupus biomarkers: a roadmap for research, validation, and translation.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in lupus biomarker research, clinical translation has remained limited, leading to delayed diagnosis, imprecise disease monitoring, and trial-and-error treatment approaches. This roadmap, developed by the Lupus Research Alliance's Biomarker Roadmap Committee with input from patients and experts, identifies key priorities for translating research into clinical benefit. Three major clinical unmet needs are highlighted: improving diagnostic accuracy of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and neuropsychiatric SLE, developing sensitive longitudinal markers for disease activity (including lupus nephritis), and predicting disease progression and treatment response. We review the current state of biomarker development across these domains and highlight barriers that hinder clinical validation, assay development, and clinical adoption. We propose focused strategies to overcome these challenges, emphasizing analytically validated assays, diverse longitudinal cohorts, alignment with meaningful clinical outcomes, and consortium-based efforts. The roadmap outlines a path to transform lupus diagnosis, monitoring, and precision medicine, enabling research advances to improve patient care.

articles.title: Outcomes of systemic sclerosis with overlapping myositis: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest disease-specific mortality among rheumatic diseases, with cardiac involvement and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as leading causes of death. We aimed to determine whether overlapping myositis independently contributes to cardiac involvement and mortality in SSc.

METHODS: We did a 1:1 propensity score matched retrospective cohort study of 880 SSc patients (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) at a single centre. SSc myositis required proximal weakness and elevated muscle enzymes without alternative causes. Cardiac involvement used SCTC criteria (pericardial effusion, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, conduction disease). We used standard and Firth penalised logistic regression for cardiac predictors, Cox regression for survival, and Fisher's exact test for cause specific mortality. All p values were Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted.

RESULTS: Of 880 patients, 92 (10.4%) had myositis. After matching, 92 pairs (n = 184) were analysed. Myositis independently predicted cardiac involvement (standard aOR=19.99, 95%CI 2.19-182.26, p = 0.008; Firth OR = 12.84, 95%CI 2.31-98.47, p = 0.006). Higher mRSS also predicted cardiac involvement (aOR=2.34 per 10 points, p = 0.006). Anti-Scl70 was less common in myositis (25.0% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.009). Overall mortality did not differ (13.0% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.620). In non-myositis deaths, ILD caused 33.3%; in myositis deaths, cardiac failure caused 25% and no ILD-related deaths (Fisher's p = 0.229). Cardiac involvement was significantly associated with mortality (aHR=8.09 (1.36-48.26), p = 0.022), independent of myositis.

CONCLUSION: Overlapping myositis in SSc is associated with an increased risk of cardiac involvement and a shift in the cause-of-death profile away from ILD, without a detectable difference in overall survival over the observed median 21-month follow-up. Systematic cardiac surveillance is needed in these patients.

articles.title: Nearly One-Third of Older Inpatients with Chronic Heart Failure Showed a Multidimensional High Self-Regulatory Fatigue Profile: A Cluster Analysis.
One Dose versus Three Doses of Benzathine Penicillin G in Early Syphilis in People Living with HIV: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Despite the current recommendations of the CDC and IUSTI, controversy persists regarding the adequate dose and duration of benzathine penicillin G (BPG) for early syphilis in people living with HIV (PLWH). PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched from inception to October 2025 for studies comparing a single-dose versus a 3-dose BPG regimen in PLWH with early syphilis. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome included serologic cure, defined as a ≥4-fold (2-dilution) decline from baseline in antibody titers measured by nontreponemal (lipoidal antigen) tests, including rapid plasma reagin (RPR) or venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) tests, at 6 and 12 months. A total of 8 studies, including 2randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 6observational studies, were included. Pooled analysis showed no significant difference in serologic cure between a single-dose versus 3-dose BPG at 6months (RR 1.00; 95% CI 0.93 to 1.07; P = 0.95) or 12 months (RR 0.98; 95% CI 0.92 to 1.04; P = 0.46). Overall, our pooled results did not show a significant difference between single-dose and 3-dose BPG. However, our study did not evaluate selected high-risk subgroups, particularly individuals with advanced immunosuppression or untreated HIV infection. Thus, a potential benefit of enhanced therapy in these specific populations cannot be entirely ruled out, underscoring the need for future RCTs focused on these subgroups and designed to stratify or adjust for key disease-modifying factors.

articles.title: FDA Approves a Second Weekly Basal Insulin Option for Type 2 Diabetes.
Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists' agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text.

RESULTS: Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ: 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87-84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10-89.61%).

CONCLUSION: In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists' agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows.

KEY POINTS: Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231-0.775), narrowing the junior-senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

articles.title: The Challenge of Unit Cost Harmonisation: A French National Reference Unit Cost for Healthcare Services (the MOVIE Project).
articles.journal: Applied health economics and health policy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The lack of standardised unit cost data is a major barrier to the quality and comparability of health economic evaluations in France. Although such evaluations are often required for reimbursement decisions, no national reference cost framework existed outside the hospital sector. The MOVIE project fills this gap by developing the first French reference unit cost framework for 22 healthcare services, using 2021 data from a representative sample of the National Health Data System.

METHODS: Total billed amounts, social health insurance reimbursements, and patient out-of-pocket payments were estimated, in line with the collective perspective recommended by French authorities. The methodology was structured into three steps and was repeated for each of the 22 healthcare services. Step 1 consisted of a comprehensive literature review. Step 2 consisted of developing and executing the data query plan using the 2021 ESND database and then defining the statistical unit. Step 3 aimed to verify the consistency of the database with official statistics, estimates derived from the 2% sample that were extrapolated to the national level and compared with annually published macro-level data from official institutions collected in Step 1.

RESULTS: In 2021, the mean consultation cost was estimated at €39.8 (SD €12.6) for General Practitioners (GPs) and €66.1 (SD €37.1) for specialist physicians. Results show wide variation in unit costs across services, with low variability for allied health care and GP visits, and high variability and strong right-skewness for services such as inpatient care, chemotherapy, and dental care. Mean consultation costs were higher than commonly used tariffs, reflecting additional fees and incentives.

CONCLUSION: Overall, this framework improves quality and comparability of economic evaluations and supports better-informed healthcare decision-making in France.

articles.title: SOX10 Expression in Primary Salivary Gland Tumors: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary salivary gland tumors form a heterogeneous group with diagnostic challenges. Sex-determining region Y-related homeobox 10 (SOX10) is a transcription factor studied in primary salivary gland tumors for over a decade. To date, no systematic review or meta-analysis has been conducted on its expression in salivary gland tumors.

METHODS: A PubMed literature search identified all studies in which SOX10 was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in primary salivary gland tumors. Information on SOX10 positivity, staining pattern, percentage of positive cells, and information on the antibody source and clone were tabulated in Microsoft Excel. The meta-analysis was performed with OpenMeta Analyst. The meta-analysis adheres to PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines.

RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 35 studies with 1146 histological and 35 cytological samples immunostained with SOX10. The list of SOX10-positive tumors according to our meta-analysis includes pleomorphic adenoma (pooled meta-analytic estimate of SOX10 positivity 95.8%, 95% CI 91.7-99.9%), polymorphous adenocarcinoma (pooled estimate 97.4%, 95% CI 92.3-102.6%), canalicular adenoma (pooled estimate 98.9%, 95% CI 96.4-101.4%), basal cell adenoma (pooled estimate 91.3%, 95% CI 80.2-102.5%), adenoid cystic carcinoma (pooled estimate 96.6%, 95% CI 94.1-99.2%), myoepithelioma (pooled estimate 75.2%, 95% CI 52.0-98.4%), acinic cell carcinoma (pooled estimate 97.4%, 95% CI 94.1-100.6%), intercalated duct type of intraductal carcinoma (pooled estimate 90.8%, 95% CI 75.9-105.8%), and microsecretory carcinoma (pooled estimate 96.1%, 95% CI 87.2-105.0%). Limited evidence suggests that basal cell adenocarcinoma, epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma, and myoepithelial carcinoma are also SOX10 positive. SOX10-negative entities include Warthin's tumor (pooled estimate 2.3%, 95% CI 0-7.0%), apocrine type of intraductal carcinoma (pooled estimate 10.3%, 95% CI - 10.4-31.1%), salivary duct carcinoma (pooled estimate 3.7%, 95% CI - 0.6-8.1%), and oncocytoma (pooled estimate 8.0%, 95% CI - 2.7-18.7%). Polyclonal antibodies and clones EP268, N-20, and A-2 provided similar results. Clone BC34 stained a lower percentage of SOX10-positive tumors.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis lists SOX10-positive and -negative tumors. This demonstrates the necessity of subtype-specific reporting and stating the antibody clone used in immunohistochemical studies.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Mepolizumab Versus Dupilumab in Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries with Asthma: A Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mepolizumab and dupilumab are biologic therapies used to manage uncontrolled asthma, though direct comparative real-world evidence between these two agents is limited. This study compared asthma-related hospitalizations and asthma exacerbations between mepolizumab and dupilumab among an older and clinically complex population of Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) beneficiaries with asthma.

METHODS: Data from Komodo Research Database (01/01/2018-05/31/2025) were used to identify Medicare FFS beneficiaries with asthma and a first claim for mepolizumab or dupilumab on or after January 1, 2019 (index date), as well as a subgroup of patients adherent to the index biologic for ≥ 6 months. Cohorts were balanced using overlap weighting based on a propensity score model. Rates of asthma-related hospitalizations and asthma exacerbations were evaluated while on treatment as the number of events per patient-year (PPY) and compared between weighted cohorts using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Rates of asthma-related hospitalizations were assessed for non-inferiority using a fixed-margin approach.

RESULTS: Overall, 1055 and 1218 patients were included in the mepolizumab and dupilumab cohorts, respectively (mean age 70.1 and 67.4 years). Baseline characteristics were well balanced after weighting. Mepolizumab demonstrated non-inferiority to dupilumab for asthma-related hospitalizations within the overall population (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.46, 1.08; p = 0.113; non-inferiority margin 1.10) and superiority to dupilumab within the adherent subgroup (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30, 0.99; p = 0.047). Mepolizumab was also associated with significantly lower rates of asthma exacerbations than dupilumab in the overall population (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.72, 1.00; p = 0.047) and directionally favorable rates in the adherent subgroup (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.63, 1.05; p = 0.116).

CONCLUSIONS: Among Medicare FFS beneficiaries, mepolizumab demonstrated comparable real-world effectiveness to dupilumab for asthma-related hospitalizations and was associated with significantly lower rates of asthma exacerbations, supporting mepolizumab as an effective treatment option for older, clinically complex patients with asthma.

articles.title: The Impact of Diabetes on Risk of Revision Following Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Real-World Data Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Given the increasing prevalence of diabetes mellitus (DM), understanding its impact on anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) revision risk is important for clinical decision-making and patient counselling. This study evaluated whether DM is associated with an increased risk of revision ACLR within 5 years of primary reconstruction.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using a global federated health research network (TriNetX, Cambridge, USA), including 73,951 patients who underwent primary ACLR across 53 healthcare organisations, of whom 990 had DM (type 1 and 2). Patients undergoing primary ACLR between 5 August 2005 and 4 August 2025 were included. The index event was primary ACLR, and the outcome was subsequent ACLR to the ipsilateral knee. Follow-up was extended until revision surgery or up to 5 years. Patients with DM (type 1 or type 2) were compared with patients without DM following 1:1 propensity score matching for age, sex, and BMI. Following propensity score matching, 988 patients were analysed per cohort. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and hazard ratios (HRs) were used to assess revision risk. A further sensitivity analysis excluded patients undergoing concomitant soft tissue knee procedures, including meniscectomy, meniscal repair, meniscal transplantation, and additional ligament reconstruction procedures.

RESULTS: Of the 73,951 patients included, 990 had DM, corresponding to a prevalence of 1.3% among individuals undergoing ACLR. Following propensity score matching, revision ACLR occurred in 30 of 988 patients with DM and 38 of 988 patients without DM, with no statistically significant difference in revision risk between the cohorts (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.47-1.26). In the sensitivity analysis excluding patients with concomitant soft tissue knee procedures, between 1 and 10 revision events occurred in each matched cohort (243 patients per cohort), and no statistically significant difference in revision risk was observed (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.08-2.45).

CONCLUSION: DM was not associated with an increased risk of revision ACLR within 5 years of the primary procedure. These findings were consistent in a sensitivity analysis excluding concomitant soft tissue knee procedures. The results should be interpreted in the context of the study's limitations and do not replace individualised clinical risk assessment.

articles.title: Linear versus Circular Stapled Gastrojejunostomy in Minimally Invasive Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: A Nationwide Swiss Administrative Database Study (2015-2022).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of stapling technique on early postoperative outcomes after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) remains incompletely understood. This study compared short-term postoperative outcomes following linear versus circular gastrojejunostomy.

METHODS: This nationwide administrative database study included RYGB cases in Switzerland between 2015 and 2022. The primary endpoint was major in-hospital postoperative complication (composite of diagnoses and reoperation). Secondary endpoints included individual complications, length of hospital stay (LOS), and temporal trends in stapling technique. Associations were assessed using generalised additive regression models and propensity score matching (PSM).

RESULTS: Among 21,320 RYGB cases, 18,161 (85.2%) underwent linear and 3,159 (14.8%) circular gastrojejunostomy. Circular stapling was not associated with major complication in multivariable analysis (OR = 1.221, 95% CI 0.824-1.809), whereas higher odds were observed after PSM (OR = 2.464, 95% CI 1.225-4.956). Circular stapling was associated with both surgical site infection (SSI) and LOS exceeding the 50th percentile in both multivariable (SSI: OR = 2.251, 95% CI 1.331-3.809; LOS: RR = 1.136, 95% CI 1.047-1.232) and PSM analyses (SSI: OR = 7.647, 95% CI 2.885-20.271; LOS: RR = 1.318, 95% CI 1.218-1.426). For LOS exceeding the 90th percentile, an association was observed in multivariable analysis (RR = 1.209, 95% CI 1.014-1.441), but not after PSM (RR = 1.018, 95% CI 0.604-1.715). Circular stapling decreased overall during the study period (Τ=-0.714, p = 0.013), despite year-to-year variation.

CONCLUSION: The association between circular stapling and major in-hospital postoperative complication differed across analytical approaches. Associations with SSI and prolonged LOS were more consistent. Linear stapling increasingly predominated over time. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT07483957, Registration date: 17 March 2026.

articles.title: Epidemiological and sociodemographic profile of Mpox in Brazilian Amazon: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mpox outbreak was characterized by viral transmission within sexual networks and atypical clinical presentations, requiring regional epidemiological evaluations. This study aimed to describe the sociodemographic profile, temporal notification trends, and clinical characteristics of suspected and confirmed Mpox cases in Pará, Brazilian Amazon (2022-2025).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Observational, cross-sectional, and analytical study based on the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) between March 2022 and December 2025, adhering to STROBE guidelines. The sample (N = 296) was stratified into confirmed Mpox cases (G1; n = 86) and ruled-out cases (G2; n = 210). Associations were evaluated using Pearson's Chi-square test (for expected cell counts ≥ 5) or Fisher's exact test (for expected counts < 5), with significance set at p < 0.05 in SPSS v.26.0.

RESULTS: In G1, infection was concentrated among men (97.7%), cisgender men (96.5%), adults aged 19 to 59 years (98.8%), residents of Belém (76.7%), individuals with tertiary education (53.5%), and those reporting homosexual (73.3%) or bisexual (12.8%) orientation (p < 0.001). Clinically, fever (81.4%; p < 0.001) and localized genital lesions (43.0% in G1 vs. 6.2% in G2; p < 0.001) were the primary presentations. Intimate sexual contact was the primary probable exposure pathway (65.1%; p < 0.001). A high proportion of HIV coinfection was observed in G1 (54.7%), with complete reporting overlap with immunosuppression status, alongside 23.3% presenting an active STI at notification (p < 0.001), predominantly active syphilis (16.3%). Clinical management was predominantly outpatient (7.0% hospitalization rate; p = 0.261), with a 96.5% cure rate among valid confirmed cases. No Mpox-attributed deaths occurred among confirmed cases, though all-cause mortality in G1 was 2.3% (n = 2).

CONCLUSION: Mpox cases in Pará were concentrated in the state capital, associated with intimate sexual contact networks among young adults, and characterized by high coinfection frequencies with HIV and syphilis.

articles.title: Non-surgical management of thyroid eye disease: a pilot survey of oculoplastic surgeons.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate real-world practices in the non-surgical management of thyroid eye disease (TED) among oculoplastic surgeons across participating Asia-Pacific clinical settings.

METHODS: A structured 39-item online questionnaire was distributed between August and October 2023 to 40 eligible oculoplastic surgeons identified through the Asia Pacific Society of Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery. The questionnaire assessed clinical experience, TED patient volume, and preferred non-surgical therapeutic approaches, including corticosteroids, immunosuppressive agents, orbital radiotherapy (ORT), biologic therapies, periocular injections, and micronutrient supplementation. Descriptive statistics were used because of the exploratory nature and small sample size of the survey.

RESULTS: Seventeen physicians completed the questionnaire, corresponding to a response rate of 42.5%. All respondents reported using glucocorticoids, and intravenous methylprednisolone was the predominant systemic treatment. A cumulative dose of 4.5 g, administered as 6 weekly infusions of 500 mg followed by 6 weekly infusions of 250 mg, was selected by 13 respondents (76.5%). Periocular injections were used by 11 respondents (64.7%), with triamcinolone acetonide being the most frequently used agent. Ten respondents (58.8%) reported using ORT. Immunosuppressive agents were used less frequently, with mycophenolate mofetil and methotrexate each reported by 3 respondents (17.7%). Biologic therapies included tocilizumab (4, 23.5%), rituximab (3, 17.7%), and teprotumumab (1, 5.9%). Selenium supplementation was reported only sporadically.

CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory survey demonstrates substantial variability in the non-surgical management of TED across participating Asia-Pacific settings. Given the small, non-random sample and uneven country representation, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than representative of the Asia-Pacific region as a whole.

articles.title: Latent HIV Infection of BBB Pericytes Enhances Gap Junction-mediated Crosstalk with Endothelial Cells.
articles.abstract: HIV-Associated Neurocognitive Impairments persist, with over 50% of patients experiencing cognitive decline. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) impairment is a consistent feature of this comorbidity, which is remarkable, because BBB endothelial cells are not productively infected by HIV-1. Conversely, pericytes can be productively infected with HIV-1 and are essential for cerebrovascular homeostasis. Given this, we hypothesized that HIV-1 infection of pericytes disrupts BBB endothelial cell integrity through dysfunctional gap junction and hemichannel signaling, impairing pericyte-endothelial intercellular communication. Using a co-culture model with primary human BBB pericytes and brain microvascular endothelial cells, pericytes were infected with HIV-1 for 3 or 7 days, exhibiting active and latent viral phenotypes. Findings revealed enhanced gap junction communication between HIV-infected pericytes and endothelial cells under both conditions, and blocking gap junctions modulated endothelial inflammatory responses. Overall, this study advances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying HIV-associated BBB dysfunction and may inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Clinical Performance of the IWGDF Risk Stratification System for Diabetic Foot Ulceration: A Gender-Disaggregated Study of 713 Patients.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic foot ulceration (DFU) is a major complication of diabetes and is a leading cause of lower-extremity amputation. This study evaluated the cross-sectional discriminative performance of the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF) risk classification for prevalent active DFU, described gender-disaggregated ulcer prevalence, and identified factors independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk in a specialist diabetes center.

METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 713 adults with diabetes mellitus who attended the diabetic foot service of a university diabetes center were classified according to the IWGDF risk system. The prevalence of active DFU was compared across risk categories using the Cochran-Armitage trend test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk and active DFU.

RESULTS: Active DFU was present in 21 patients (2.9%), with no significant difference between men (3.8%) and women (2.1%). Overall, 17.3% of the patients were classified as having moderate or high risk. Ulcer prevalence increased progressively across the IWGDF categories, from 0.0% in the very-low-risk group to 38.5% in the high-risk group (p < 0.001).
