The IWGDF classification showed excellent cross-sectional discrimination for prevalent active DFU (c-statistic 0.938), with 90.5% sensitivity and 99.7% negative predictive value at the moderate/high-risk threshold. Older age and higher glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels were independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk, whereas gender was not.

CONCLUSION: The IWGDF classification showed excellent cross-sectional discrimination for prevalent active DFU. Older age and poorer glycemic control, but not gender, were independently associated with moderate/high IWGDF risk. These findings support routine IWGDF-guided risk stratification in specialist diabetes care, although prospective studies are required to establish its performance in predicting future ulceration.

articles.title: Exploring uncertainties in melanoma management: a Spanish multidisciplinary Delphi consensus.
articles.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Melanoma is a highly metastatic tumor responsible for 90% of skin cancer deaths. Despite established clinical guidelines, certain areas of its management in Spain remain heterogeneous, particularly in complex scenarios such as neoadjuvant therapy, metastatic sequencing, and follow-up. This project aimed to generate expert-informed recommendations to standardize care in areas of clinical uncertainty.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A two-round Delphi process was conducted. Following a systematized review, a multidisciplinary panel of 35 specialists (oncology, dermatology, surgery, and pathology) evaluated 59 statements on uncertain areas of melanoma management. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement using a 5-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: Overall, 52 statements achieved consensus (3 unanimous, 49 by agreement). Key findings support the use of neoadjuvant immunotherapy in resectable stage III melanoma, particularly in patients with clinically detectable nodal disease, due to its benefit in reducing recurrence risk. A major pathological response was considered a key factor to individualize subsequent surgical and adjuvant decisions. In metastatic disease, therapeutic sequencing algorithms were defined according to BRAF mutational status, prior treatments, and timing of progression. The panel agreed that PD-L1 expression should not be used as the sole factor to exclude patients from anti-PD-1 therapy. Marked variability in follow-up practices was identified, highlighting the need for standardized approaches and quality indicators.

CONCLUSION: This Delphi consensus reflects the views of a multidisciplinary panel of Spanish melanoma experts on key areas of uncertainty in melanoma management. By integrating evidence and expert experience, the findings may help support clinical decision-making and serve as a complementary reference for clinical practice.

articles.title: Anticoagulation in Mechanical Circulatory Support: Contemporary Challenges and Future Directions in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy.
articles.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is increasingly used in patients with cardiogenic shock, advanced heart failure, and severe respiratory failure; however, anticoagulation management remains challenging due to the competing risks of thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and device dysfunction. In this review, we synthesize contemporary evidence on anticoagulant selection, monitoring strategies, and device-specific management across major MCS platforms, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, temporary ventricular assist devices, Impella devices, and durable left ventricular assist devices. Unfractionated heparin remains the cornerstone anticoagulant across most MCS platforms, while anti-factor Xa-guided monitoring is increasingly incorporated into clinical practice in many centers alongside activated partial thromboplastin time and other monitoring modalities. Direct thrombin inhibitors represent important alternatives, particularly for patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or heparin resistance. Recent advances include bicarbonate-based purge strategies for Impella support and evolving antithrombotic approaches in HeartMate 3 recipients, introduced by the ARIES-HM3 trial. Emerging investigational strategies, including direct oral anticoagulants, factor XI/XII inhibition, and precision anticoagulation approaches, show promise for improving hemocompatibility; however, current evidence remains limited, and further prospective studies are required before these strategies can be routinely adopted. Overall, contemporary evidence supports an individualized approach to anticoagulation based on device characteristics, patient-specific risk profiles, and current guideline recommendations, while highlighting important knowledge gaps that warrant further high-quality prospective investigation.

articles.title: Mechanical ventilation-associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework.
articles.abstract: Mechanical ventilation-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung-kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid-base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the relationship between mechanical ventilation and AKI and proposes an integrated framework for future research on the interplay between ventilatory stress, venous congestion, renal perfusion, and inflammatory injury. Emerging bedside tools such as renal Doppler indices, venous excess ultrasound score (VExUS), and kidney injury biomarkers are discussed as components of an integrated physiologic approach for early recognition and risk stratification of ventilator-associated AKI. We further propose a multimodal conceptual framework integrating respiratory mechanics, congestion assessment, perfusion monitoring, and biomarkers to support individualized kidney-protective ventilation strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized physiologic monitoring, time-varying exposure analyses, causal mediation approaches, and prospective multicenter studies to better define renal-protective ventilatory targets and advance precision critical care.

articles.title: Device-Associated Sepsis and Brain Injury: Transitioning From Early Infection Control to Late Neuroprotection.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a complex neuroinflammatory condition characterized by diffuse brain dysfunction arising from systemic infection without direct central nervous system invasion. In modern critical care, device-associated infections (DAIs) caused by invasive medical devices, such as central line-associated bloodstream infections, ventilator-associated pneumonia, and catheter-associated urinary tract infections, have become critical drivers of intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired sepsis. Biofilm formation on these devices establishes persistent inflammatory reservoirs that continuously shed microorganisms, pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) into the circulation, sustaining systemic immune activation. This review outlines an integrated mechanistic framework linking DAIs to acute brain dysfunction. Systemic inflammation and endothelial activation trigger microvascular dysfunction, impaired cerebral autoregulation, and blood-brain barrier disruption. These peripheral vascular alterations allow inflammatory mediators to access the central nervous system, where they induce microglial and astrocytic reactivity. Persistent neuroimmune activation compromises neurotransmitter homeostasis-causing glutamate excitotoxicity and cholinergic deficits-while impairing neuronal mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. The resulting oxidative stress, energy failure, and self-amplifying neuroinflammatory feedback loops culminate in synaptic damage and neuronal injury. Clinically, this manifests as altered consciousness, delirium, seizures, and long-term neurocognitive impairment. By framing SAE as a concurrent, multidimensional continuum rather than a linear sequence, this review highlights the critical role of early infection prevention, timely device removal, and targeted neuroprotective strategies aimed at stabilizing vascular integrity and mitigating neuroinflammation.

articles.title: From bystander to key player: The mechanisms and therapeutic potential of IL-24 in liver diseases.
articles.abstract: Interleukin-24 (IL-24) was initially identified during investigations on melanoma differentiation, and it is a pivotal member of the IL-10 family. As a secreted cytokine, IL-24 is recognized as a tumor suppressor cytokine that induces apoptosis and inhibits angiogenesis. The liver is a unique immunotolerant organ that maintains metabolic homeostasis while continuously responding to insults, such as viral infections, toxic substances, and metabolic stress. In recent years, accumulating evidence has elucidated the role of IL-24 in the initiation and progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), demonstrating that this cytokine may suppress tumor progression by inducing tumor cell death and modulating antitumor immunity. However, compared with its relatively well-characterized functions in HCC, the role of IL-24 in non-neoplastic hepatopathies remains less defined. Current evidence, primarily derived from in vivo and in vitro experiments, suggests that IL-24 may exert hepatoprotective effects against acute and chronic liver injury by alleviating endoplasmic reticulum stress. Additionally, IL-24 modulates hepatic stellate cell activation and influences proinflammatory cytokine release during liver fibrosis, whereas it affects hepatocyte autophagy and metabolic reprogramming in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, thereby potentially mitigating disease progression. This review comprehensively delineates the molecular characteristics of IL-24 and summarizes research progress on its roles in non-neoplastic liver diseases, particularly focusing on the underlying molecular mechanisms and possible therapeutic implications. This study additionally highlights the limitations of current evidence and outlines future research directions, aiming to provide a basis for future investigation of IL-24-targeted intervention strategies.

articles.title: Correction: Extracorporeal life support for severe heart failure in a diffuse panbronchiolitis patient awaiting lung transplant: a case report.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs

articles.title: Molecular mechanisms of cardioprotection: biomarkers, signaling pathways, and emerging molecular signatures in cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of worldwide mortality, with myocardial infarction (MI) being one of the most significant clinical indicators. Around 85% of the 17.9 million cardiovascular deaths are due to heart attack and stroke. This comprehensive review focuses on cardiac biomarkers and cardioprotection signaling pathways. This review describes key cardioprotective signaling pathways, including PKCε, RISK (Reperfusion Injury Salvage Kinase), MAPK, NO/cGMP/PKG, and SAFE (Survivor Activating Factor Enhancement), which work together to regulate cardiovascular functions, prevent cellular death, and maintain mitochondrial stability. The physiology of heart injury is examined through the complex interactions of inflammatory processes, necrotic transmissions, self-destruction, and oxidative stress, with particular attention to mitochondrial dysfunction, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. A thorough review of traditional and innovative cardiac biomarkers is provided, including long non-coding RNAs, microRNAs (e.g., miR-21, miR-486-5p, miR-126), creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), cardiac troponins (cTnI/cTnT), inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α), and natriuretic peptides (BNP/NT-pro BNP). A broad discussion of these novel biomarkers covers their applications in prognosis, screening, and medical assessment, emphasizing their roles in risk evaluation, early detection, and personalized therapy plans. This study offers an extensive perspective on cardiac protection, integrating clinical applications with physiological mechanisms to promote precise cardiovascular treatment and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: A Novel Cystodiscus Lutz, 1889 Species (Myxozoa: Myxosporea: Bivalvulida) Isolated from Three Hynobiid Salamanders in Japan: First Record of Myxosporeans from Asian Salamanders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myxosporeans infecting amphibians, particularly Asian salamanders, remain poorly investigated. I conducted a parasitological survey of Japanese salamanders to investigate the occurrence of myxosporean infections.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A parasitological survey was conducted on 132 individuals representing 27 taxa (26 species and one hybrid taxon) of Japanese salamanders belonging to three families. The parasites obtained were examined morphologically using light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and molecular analyses were performed using partial sequences of the small subunit (SSU) and large subunit (LSU) rDNA genes.

RESULTS: Myxosporean parasites belonging to the genus Cystodiscus were identified from the gallbladders of three hynobiid salamanders: Hynobius kimurae, H. tagoi, and H. utsunomiyaorum. Based on morphological and molecular evidence, the parasite is herein described as a new species, Cystodiscus uptoni n. sp. The species is characterized by its myxospore morphology and the presence of motile plasmodia. This represents the first record of a myxosporean infection in salamanders in Asia and the first record of the genus Cystodiscus from Japan. Molecular phylogenetic analyses supported the distinctiveness of the new species from previously sequenced congeners. Myxosporeans were not detected in the remaining 23 salamander taxa, although plasmodia-like structures lacking mature spores were observed in H. hirosei.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence of myxosporean infection in Asian salamanders and expands the known host and geographic ranges of Cystodiscus. The results highlight the need for further investigations of myxosporean diversity and host associations in Asian salamanders.

articles.title: Computer-aided development of novel thiazolidinone-thiazole derivatives: multidimensional structure-activity relationships revealed by quantum chemical analysis, molecular docking and biological investigation.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major global health challenge, highlighting the need for new inhibitors of the carbohydrate-hydrolyzing enzymes α-amylase and α-glucosidase. In this study, a series of thiazole-based thiazolidinone derivatives (1-10) was designed, synthesized, and structurally characterized using spectroscopic techniques. Among the synthesized compounds, 8 showed the strongest inhibitory activity against α-amylase and α-glucosidase, with IC50 values of 5.50 ± 0.40 and 5.90 ± 0.10 µM, respectively, and compared with 10.80 ± 0.50 and 11.10 ± 0.30 µM for acarbose. Molecular docking suggested that compound 8 can adopt a favorable binding orientation within the active sites of both enzymes through hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic contacts. Enzyme kinetic studies further characterized its mode of inhibition. DFT calculations were performed to examine the electronic properties, frontier molecular orbitals, and molecular electrostatic potential of selected derivatives. ADMET analysis was also conducted to provide preliminary insight into their predicted pharmacokinetic and toxicity-related properties. Overall, the experimental and computational findings identify compound 8 as a promising lead structure for further investigation as an α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitor.

articles.title: Raspberry-shaped H-COF-based dual-mode fluorescent sensing probe for tetracycline antibiotics: standalone and electrospun mat-based point-of-care applications.
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional fluorescent materials have emerged as promising candidates for applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, and disease diagnostics, particularly for point-of-care sensors. We report solvothermal development of an imine-linked 2D hydrogen-covalent hybridized organic framework (H-COF), DaTa-1, with novel raspberry-like morphology for the sensitive chemosensing of tetracyclines (TCs) in tap water and milk samples. The developed H-COF exhibited good thermal stability and strong fluorescence in aqueous suspension and in the solid state. DaTa-1 demonstrated excellent sensing performance for TCs (especially for 0.2-10 ppm and 12-60 ppm ranges), achieving low detection limits of 43.80, 46.42, 55.81, and 104.20 ppb for tetracycline, chlortetracycline, oxytetracycline, and doxycycline, respectively. Notably, the inner filter effect is primarily responsible for generating sensing signals. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggested photoinduced electron transfer (PET) as an additional pathway contributing to dynamic quenching. To make the developed system more accessible, DaTa-1 was incorporated into polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers via electrospinning and used for the on-site and smartphone-assisted visual detection of TCs.

articles.title: Confinement enhanced phosphorescent electrochemiluminescence of copper iodide cluster complex for imaging detection of organophosphorus pesticide.
articles.abstract: Owing to the spin statistics of electrogenerated excitons, conventional fluorescent ECL materials fail to utilize 75% of the triplet excitons. To improve the utilization efficiency of triplet excitons, this work proposed a strategy for the design of phosphorescent ECL material based on the synergistic effect of heavy-atom iodine enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and rigid molecular environment. A copper-iodide cluster complex Cu4I6(pr-ted)2 was successfully synthesized using 1-propyl-1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octanium (pr-ted) as the organic cation and polyvinylpyrrolidone for chain entanglement. The enhanced SOC promoted efficient intersystem crossing, and thus rapidly populated long-lived triplet excited states, which lifted the spin-forbidden transition from the triplet state to the ground state for efficient radiative utilization of triplet excitons. The rigid network could effectively suppress non-radiative transitions and mitigate dynamic oxygen quenching. The ECL process of designed Cu4I6(pr-ted)2 followed a new cluster-centered charge transfer mechanism with low non-radiative losses, exhibiting a long luminescence lifetime, high quantum yield, and an excellent ECL efficiency of 33.5%. Based on the strong ECL emission of Cu4I6(pr-ted)2, an ECL imaging sensor was constructed for the quantitative detection of organophosphorus pesticides with malathion as a model analyte, which achieved a linear detection range of 10- 3 - 103 pg/mL and a detection limit as low as 7.68 × 10- 4 pg/mL. This work provided a new approach for the development of efficient and low-cost phosphorescent ECL materials as well as their biosensing applications.

articles.title: Comment on "Association of peripheral NLRP3 inflammasome activation with prevalent and incident chronic kidney disease in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a prospective study".
articles.abstract: This correspondence comments on the study by Cai et al. examining circulating NLRP3 and prevalent and incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The inclusion of 648 participants, complementary cross-sectional and prospective analyses, and evaluation of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and albuminuria are important strengths. Nevertheless, several methodological considerations affect interpretation. Prevalent CKD appears to have been classified using baseline eGFR or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio without consistent confirmation of chronicity. A single baseline NLRP3 measurement may not reflect long-term biological activity, while adjusted associations do not establish improved prediction beyond established risk factors. The possible causal roles of OSA severity, nocturnal hypoxemia, and inflammatory markers also merit explicit consideration. Building on these findings, future multicenter studies should confirm CKD with repeat renal measurements, assess serial NLRP3 reproducibility, prespecify causally informed models, and compare clinical prediction models with and without NLRP3 using discrimination, calibration, validation, and decision-curve analysis. These steps would help determine whether circulating NLRP3 offers meaningful incremental value for renal risk stratification in OSA.

articles.title: Outcomes of abdominal wall reconstruction with and without concurrent skin excision: a single-surgeon retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
AIM: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate and compare the clinical outcomes of incisional hernia repairs performed by a single surgeon, with and without concurrent skin excisions. Given the increasing prevalence of incisional hernias and the growing need for comprehensive abdominal wall reconstruction, this study aimed to determine whether the addition of skin excision significantly affects postoperative outcomes, including length of hospital stay (LOS), complication rates, and wound infection incidence. Furthermore, the study explored the influence of patient-related factors such as body mass index (BMI) and hernia size on surgical outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 94 patients who underwent incisional hernia repairs between 2019 and 2023. These patients were divided into two groups: those who underwent hernia repair without skin excision (n = 52, 55%) and those who had skin excision as part of the procedure (n = 42, 45%). Key outcome measures included LOS, postoperative complications, and wound infection rates. Additionally, patients were stratified based on BMI (≥ 30 vs. <30) to assess its impact on surgical outcomes. Statistical analysis was performed using Pearson's chi-square and one-way ANOVA tests, with significance defined as p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The median age of patients in the study cohort was 57 years (range: 24-88 years). Patients who did not undergo skin excision had a significantly shorter LOS compared to those who underwent concurrent skin excision (mean: 2.8 days vs. 6.8 days, p = 0.023). Despite the extended hospitalisation in the skin excision group, overall complication rates were comparable between the two cohorts (34% vs. 31%, p = 0.436). There was no statistically significant difference in wound infection rates between the no-skin-excision and skin-excision groups (23% vs. 16%, p = 0.441). BMI was found to be a significant factor influencing postoperative outcomes. Patients with a BMI of ≥ 30 (n = 10) exhibited a markedly higher incidence of postoperative complications and wound infections (p < 0.001), though BMI did not appear to affect LOS (p = 0.962). Additionally, the size of the hernia was an important determinant of surgical outcomes. Larger hernias (≥ 6 cm) were associated with a longer LOS compared to smaller hernias (mean: 6.4 days vs. 2.8 days, p = 0.051). While there was a trend towards a higher complication rate in larger hernia repairs, the difference did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSION: Patients undergoing concurrent skin excision experienced a longer hospital stay, whereas postoperative complication and wound infection rates were comparable between groups on univariable analysis. However, without multivariable adjustment, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of an independent effect of skin excision. Patients with BMI ≥ 30 had higher complication rates, although the small subgroup size limits definitive conclusions. Larger prospective studies are required to clarify these associations and inform clinical practice.

articles.title: [Cutaneous larva migrans].
articles.abstract: Cutaneous larva migrans is the most frequent parasitic tropical dermatosis imported by travelers returning from tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. Epidemiologically, this skin condition is predominantly acquired during beach stays, with high-risk areas including Southeast Asia, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The underlying cause is an infection with animal hookworm larvae, most commonly Ancylostoma braziliense, which are shed in the feces of infected dogs and cats. Because humans act as accidental hosts, the larvae penetrate the epidermis but are unable to mature into adult worms or migrate into deeper tissues. The clinical presentation typically features an intensely pruritic, raised, erythematous, and serpiginous creeping track, which is most commonly located on the feet. In clinical practice, the guideline-recommended treatment consists of systemic anthelmintic therapy, primarily utilizing a single oral dose of ivermectin or a 3-day course of oral albendazole. Alternatively, topical treatments such as a thiabendazole ointment 10% can be applied locally.

articles.title: [Bed bugs, lice and fleas-an up-to-date overview of diagnosis, treatment and prevention].
articles.abstract: Despite high standards of hygiene, ectoparasites remain a significant issue in dermatology. Bedbugs (Cimex lectularius) have become significantly more prevalent worldwide over the past two decades, whilst head lice infestation (Pediculus humanus capitis) remains one of the most common parasitic infections in children. Pubic lice (Pthirus pubis) are predominantly transmitted sexually. Body lice (Pediculus humanus corporis) are rare in Central Europe, but remain of infectious disease significance as vectors of Rickettsia prowazekii, Bartonella quintana and Borrelia recurrentis. Flea bites in humans are now predominantly caused by the cat flea (Ctenocephalides felis). The clinical spectrum ranges from asymptomatic cases through papular and urticarial reactions to bullous arthropod reactions and bacterial superinfections. Diagnosis is based on medical history, clinical findings and the direct detection of parasites, nits or characteristic environmental traces. Dermoscopy facilitates the differentiation of live parasites from nits and pseudonits, particularly in cases of pediculosis. Treatment for lice infestations comprises topical pediculicides and physically acting preparations. In the case of bedbug and flea infestations, consistent environmental control measures are crucial for long-term therapeutic success; in the case of flea infestations, concurrent veterinary treatment of infested pets is also essential. This article summarises the current state of knowledge regarding the epidemiology, biology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment and prevention of these medically important ectoparasitic infestations.

articles.title: In Vitro Models to Study Fibroelastic Remodeling of the Endocardium in Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart defects (CHD) are characterized by pathological intracardiac blood flow, exposing the endocardium to disturbed shear stress. This contributes to the development of endocardial fibroelastosis (EFE), a restrictive fibrotic remodeling process associated with diastolic dysfunction. Despite the pathomechanistic role of the endocardium in CHD, EFE-derived endocardial endothelial cells (EdEECs) remain largely understudied. No standardized protocol exists for isolating and purifying them from human pediatric tissue. Tissue from N = 15 pediatric patients with (1) hypoplastic left heart syndrome, (2) pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum, and (3) pulmonary vein stenosis was included. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT). EdEECs were isolated from resected EFE tissue using CD144-based magnetic separation. Enrichment of the endocardial phenotype was evaluated by flow cytometry, immunocytochemistry and RT-qPCR. To mimic disease-like conditions, EdEECs were exposed to in vitro shear stress and transforming growth factor beta 1. EFE driven by fibrogenic activation of EECs through EndMT was observed in the left ventricle, right ventricle, and left atrium in patients with different CHDs. Magnetic CD144-based isolation provided a reliable, gentle approach to purify EdEECs from cardiac tissue, achieving > 95% purity while reproducibly preserving endocardial identity at both the protein and gene expression levels. Isolated EdEECs retained their intrinsic, disease-specific predisposition and vulnerability to EndMT under static, and high shear stress. Unlike healthy EECs (HEECs), physiological, low shear stress alone was not sufficient to restore the intrinsic fibrogenic vulnerability of EdEECs. EndMT-mediated EFE was observed across different CHD entities. A reproducible protocol for isolating and purifying EdEECs from EFE tissue preserves their endocardial phenotype and disease-specific characteristics. This provides a disease-mimicking in vitro model to study EdEEC-specific signaling pathways.

articles.title: Are we Adhering to Guidelines for Follow-up Imaging in Neonates with Simple Congenital Heart Defects? What are the Healthcare Costs of Non-adherence?
articles.abstract: Simple congenital heart defects (CHDs) are frequently identified via neonatal echocardiograms ("echos"). In 2020, the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology issued guidelines for follow-up imaging of CHDs. In this retrospective study, we evaluated adherence to these guidelines at an academic health center in Southeastern Ontario. The cohort included neonates who had one or more simple CHDs diagnosed in the first 30 days of life between April 1, 2020, and March 31, 2024. We reviewed electronic medical records up to September 30, 2025 to examine (a) rates of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging; (b) factors that may contribute to non-adherence; and (c) the costs of excessive imaging. Among 248 patients, 376 echos were performed over the study period. Adherence status could be determined for 320. Follow-up for 39.7% of echos did not adhere to the guidelines, primarily because repeat echos were performed earlier than recommended. Non-adherence was substantially higher for lesions requiring surveillance imaging, as per guidelines, compared with lesions where follow-up imaging is not recommended or findings were normal (91.9% vs. 12.0%; OR = 83.4, 95% CI: 37.5-185.5). The pediatric cardiologist's recommendation was documented for 74.5% of echos, but only 48.9% of recommendations aligned with the guidelines. Non-adherence was higher when recommendations were not documented or deviated from the guidelines. Sixty-two echos were deemed excessive, corresponding to $13,339 in extra imaging costs. The high rate of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging for simple CHDs highlights an opportunity to reduce unnecessary healthcare costs through consistent documentation of guideline-aligned follow-up recommendations by pediatric cardiologists.

articles.title: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
articles.abstract: Ductal stenting and surgical systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting (surgical shunt) are alternative strategies to establish pulmonary blood flow in infants with ductal-dependent circulation. The impact of palliation strategy on feeding, nutrition, and neurodevelopment remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 100 infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow (2017-2024) undergoing surgical shunt (n = 57) or ductal stenting (n = 43). Outcomes included feeding, nutrition, hospital course, and neurodevelopment. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with gastrostomy tube (GT) placement. Baseline demographics were similar except for cardiac anatomy. Ductal stent patients reached target enteral feeds post-procedurally sooner (3 vs. 6 days, p < 0.001), had higher discharge weight-for-age z-scores (- 1.30 vs. -1.98, p = 0.02), and smaller declines in growth during hospitalization (p = 0.007). GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting (26% vs. 51%, p = 0.011), but palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.14-1.24, p = 0.12). Oral feeding or breastfeeding within 5 days following palliation was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.81, p = 0.03). Ductal stent patients also had shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU stays and required less vasoactive-inotropic support. Total hospital length of stay, need for reintervention, suspected or diagnosed necrotizing enterocolitis, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Ductal stenting was associated with improved early post-procedural recovery, faster feeding progression, and better preservation of growth compared with surgical shunt palliation. Although GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting in unadjusted analysis, palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment. Early post-procedural oral feeding was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement but may also reflect feeding readiness and clinical recovery.

articles.title: Congenital Cardiac Surgical Workforce Inequities Across 194 Countries: A Global Cross-Sectional Analysis.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease is the most common birth defect globally, yet access to surgery remains inequitable. The availability of congenital heart surgeons (CHS) relative to paediatric population needs is poorly defined. A cross-sectional study of the Cardiothoracic Surgery Network was conducted across 194 United Nations-recognised countries and 54 territories and dependencies (T&Ds). Of 248 countries and T&Ds analysed, 123 (49.6%) had ≥ 1 CHS. A total of 4,296 CHS were identified; 71 (37% of recognised) countries with 189.5 million children had none. Low-income countries had a median of 0.15 CHS per million children compared with 9.29 in high-income countries. CHS density was strongly correlated with gross domestic product per capita. Average CHS ratios per million children were: high-income country 9.3, upper-middle-income country 2.0, lower-middle-income country 1.1, and low-income country 0.2 (p < 0.0001), representing a 46-fold disparity between high-income countries and low-income countries. Regional analysis showed North America and Europe had the highest CHS ratios (≥ 9 per million), and Sub-Saharan Africa and East Asia and Pacific had medians of zero (p < 0.0001). Only 3 T&Ds reported at least one CHS. Our findings confirm that human resource levels are even more disproportionate than previously estimated. A significant proportion of children globally remain without access to cardiac surgery, representing a major and largely unquantified burden of preventable morbidity and mortality. Accurately quantifying this unmet need should be an urgent priority for future population-level and health systems research.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Predictors of Residual Pulmonary Regurgitation and Biventricular Recovery After Pulsta Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract: Current recommendations for pulmonary valve replacement are based primarily on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived right ventricular (RV) volume thresholds established in repaired tetralogy of Fallot. However, patients undergoing self-expanding percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) often have mixed pulmonary regurgitation (PR) and pulmonary stenosis with heterogeneous right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) anatomy. We investigated CMR predictors of residual PR, residual RV enlargement (RVE), and residual biventricular imbalance (BVI) after Pulsta PPVI. We retrospectively analyzed 98 patients with paired pre- and post-procedural CMR. Residual PR was defined as post-procedural PR fraction (PRF) ≥10%, residual RVE as RV end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVi) ≥130 mL/m2, and residual BVI as an RV/LV end-diastolic volume ratio ≥1.5. Multivariable regression and restricted cubic spline analyses identified predictors of post-procedural remodeling. Residual PR occurred in 40.8% of patients, residual RVE in 38.8%, and residual BVI in 40.8%. Pyramidal/convex main pulmonary artery morphology and higher baseline PRF independently predicted residual PR, whereas reverse pyramidal/concave morphology was associated with lower residual RVE risk. Higher pre-procedural RV/LV ratio independently predicted residual BVI. RVEDVi z-score remained independently associated with RVEDVi reduction after adjustment for baseline RVEDVi. Although RV volumes decreased substantially after PPVI, LV remodeling varied considerably, and both RVEDVi and LVEDVi change independently contributed to recovery of ventricular balance. After Pulsta PPVI, anatomical factors influence residual PR and RV remodeling. RVEDVi z-score and RV/LV ratio provide complementary information that may improve patient selection.

articles.title: Transplantation for Congenital Heart Disease in Children-A Quest to Do Better.
articles.abstract: Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) represent the largest group of pediatric heart transplant recipients but experience lower graft survival than those transplanted for cardiomyopathy. We evaluated post-transplant outcomes among CHD recipients at the Hospital for Sick Children (HSC) and identified predictors of graft loss. Pediatric patients (< 17 years) undergoing heart transplantation for CHD between 1993 and 2023 were analyzed using the Pediatric Heart Transplant Society registry. Outcomes of CHD recipients at HSC (CHD HSC) were compared with cardiomyopathy HSC recipients, CHD recipients at other centers (CHD Non-HSC), and a propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort adjusting for pre- and peri-transplant risk factors. Kaplan-Meier survival and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Among 4,362 pediatric CHD transplant recipients, 152 underwent transplantation at HSC. Freedom from graft loss for CHD HSC at 5, 10, and 15 years was 71.8%, 63.0%, and 58.4%, lower than in Cardiomyopathy HSC recipients (p < 0.0001), but similar to CHD Non-HSC (p = 0.6043). Survival remained comparable in the PSM cohort (n = 140, p = 0.4599). Conditional survival beyond 1 year was similar between groups, suggesting early mortality drives differences. CHD HSC recipients demonstrated longer freedom from CAV (p = 0.0041) and infection (p = 0.0335). Predictors of graft loss included pre-transplant ECMO (HR 3.11), ICU admission (HR 2.39), PRA > 10% (HR 2.49), African American/Black race/ethnicity (HR 2.71), and longer waitlist duration (HR 1.06). Graft survival in CHD recipients at HSC remains lower than in cardiomyopathy recipients but comparable internationally. Optimizing pre-transplant care, sensitization management, and equity-focused interventions may enhance outcomes.

articles.title: Genome characterization of a begomovirus isolated from Brazilian Carica papaya plants.
articles.abstract: Papaya (Carica papaya L.) plants are susceptible to several viral pathogens. However, information regarding papaya-associated DNA viruses in Latin America is limited. In this study, we collected symptomatic papaya plants in Baraúna, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil, and screened for begomovirus infection. Three of ten samples tested positive through PCR using universal primers, and were further analyzed using rolling circle amplification and Oxford Nanopore sequencing. This approach allowed us to recover complete circular viral genomes with the typical DNA-A segment organization of begomoviruses. We named this newly identified viral agent papaya mottle virus (PaMoV). No DNA-B component was detected in the samples, suggesting that PaMoV is a monopartite begomovirus. The sequences from the three isolates shared over 95% nucleotide identity. Pairwise sequence identity along with phylogenetic analyses supported the classification of PaMoV as a member of a novel begomovirus species, for which we propose the name "Begomovirus papayavariati". This is the first report of a begomovirus associated with C. papaya in Brazil.

articles.title: Who's paying? Payor status significantly affects hospital readmission rates after ventral hernia repair.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Over 350,000 ventral hernia repairs (VHRs) are performed annually. However, there are numerous socioeconomic disparities in obtaining elective repair. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of payer status after ventral hernia repair within a national cohort on thirty-day readmission rates, hospital costs, and discharge disposition.

METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted of the Nationwide Readmission Database (NRD) for all VHRs between 2016 and 2022. Demographic characteristics along with medical comorbidities, complications after VHR, and all-cause 30-day readmissions were collected. Logistic regression was used to assess associations between payer status and overall outcomes.

RESULTS: Medicaid (12.1%) and Medicare (12.4%) were the primary payer statuses among all readmissions. Patients with private insurance (OR 0.71, p < 0.001) and self-pay (OR 0.81, p < 0.001) had lower odds of thirty-day readmission compared to Medicaid patients. Patients discharged to a short-term facility, designated center, home healthcare, or against medical advice were more likely to be re-admitted compared to patients who were discharged home (p < 0.05). The most common cause for re-admission among all patients was post-operative/device infection. Medicaid patients had the highest rate of such infections (2.20 vs. 1.68 Medicare, 1.45 Private, and 1.56 Self-Pay).

CONCLUSIONS: Payer status significantly influences readmission rates, cause for readmission, and overall discharge disposition among VHR patients. These findings might implicate underlying socioeconomic disparities in receiving adequate post-operative care. Future studies should investigate how insurance structures impact postoperative care and clinical outcomes in hernia surgery.

articles.title: Confidence without consensus? Human versus AI abstracts in urology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study asked whether urologists can tell human-written abstracts apart from artificial intelligence (AI)-written abstracts when both describe the same study, and whether the answer depends on which AI model did the writing.

METHODS: Fifteen published urology studies were selected. For each study, the original human-written abstract was paired with three AI-written abstracts covering the same material, produced by Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3 Flash using identical instructions and each model's ordinary consumer settings. Because all four versions described the same study, the underlying data were held constant, and the versions differed in how that material was written and presented. The resulting 60 abstracts were stripped of identifying information, and eight urologists read all of them without knowing which was which (480 judgments in total). For each abstract, reviewers stated whether they believed it was written by a human or by AI, rated how confident they were in that judgment, and rated the abstract's quality and credibility on 5-point scales.

RESULTS: Reviewers correctly identified AI-written abstracts 49.3% of the time, approximately 50%, compared with 62.4% for human-written abstracts (p = .011). Results depended heavily on which model wrote the text (p = .003). Abstracts written by Claude were recognized as AI only 40.0% of the time, significantly less often than human abstracts were correctly identified (p = .003) and less often than GPT abstracts (56.8%, p = .038); Gemini fell between the two at 50.9%. Quality ratings differed only for GPT, which scored lower than human abstracts (p = .046; omnibus p = .030); credibility ratings did not differ between sources at all (p = .577). Reviewers who felt confident were no more likely to be correct (p = .749), and reviewers seldom agreed with one another about which abstracts were AI-written (Fleiss' κ = -0.009).

CONCLUSION: Urologists could not reliably recognize AI-written urology abstracts, and the difficulty came mainly from one model rather than from AI writing in general. How good an abstract appeared had little to do with whether its authorship was correctly identified, and neither reviewer confidence nor agreement between reviewers gave any warning. Reading alone is therefore not a dependable way to detect undisclosed AI authorship.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Treatment-Emergent Eczematous Reactions in Patients with Psoriasis Treated with Biologics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Treatment-emergent eczematous reactions have been reported in patients with psoriasis receiving biologic therapies, but their pooled incidence and associated factors remain unclear. We aimed to estimate the incidence and associated factors for treatment-emergent eczematous reactions in biologic-treated psoriasis patients.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science (to Jan 2026) for studies reporting new-onset or exacerbated eczema in psoriasis patients treated with tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), interleukin-12/23 (IL-12/23), or IL-23 inhibitors. Two eligible studies of the oral tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitor deucravacitinib were analyzed separately as an exploratory subgroup. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, data were synthesized using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. The primary outcome was the pooled incidence of treatment-emergent eczematous reactions. Secondary analyses examined differences according to biologic class, dosage, and demographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Analysis of 26 publications (34,511 exposures) showed a 2.17% overall incidence (95% CI 1.57-2.85). Pooled incidence differed by class (p < 0.001): IL-17 inhibitors had the highest incidence (3.47%; 95% CI 2.34-4.77), followed by IL-12/23 (2.15%; 95% CI 0.04-6.59) and TNF inhibitors (1.02%; 95% CI 0.83-1.23), and IL-23 inhibitors had the lowest (0.09%; 95% CI 0.00-0.71). Within the IL-17 class, pooled incidence was higher with secukinumab (5.3%; 95% CI 2.95-8.2) than with ixekizumab (1.51%; 95% CI 0.41-3.1). High-dose regimens were associated with a higher pooled incidence than low-dose regimens (7.65% vs 3.36%; p = 0.03). Incidence was higher in studies conducted in East Asian populations (~ 6%) than in Western populations (~ 1%). A history of atopic dermatitis showed the strongest patient-level association with treatment-emergent eczematous reactions (hazard ratio, 12.40; 95% CI 6.97-22.06).

CONCLUSIONS: Eczematous reactions in biologic-treated psoriasis were associated with biologic class, dose, and study population, with the highest incidences for IL-17 inhibitors, high-dose regimens, and studies of East Asian populations.

articles.title: Effectiveness of different autologous platelet concentrates for orthodontic canine retraction following premolar extraction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous platelet concentrates (APCs) have been increasingly used to accelerate orthodontic canine retraction; however, their effectiveness and associated clinical outcomes remain unclear.

AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of platelet-rich plasma (PRP), injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF), and leukocyte-platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) in accelerating canine retraction following premolar extraction and to summarize associated clinical outcomes including canine movement patterns, anchorage loss, and treatment-related adverse outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted by searching PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library up to April 24, 2026. Randomized and controlled clinical studies involving orthodontic patients undergoing canine retraction following premolar extraction and evaluating the effects of APCs were included. Random-effects meta-analyses and GRADE assessments were performed when appropriate.

RESULTS: 28 articles representing 26 unique studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which 16 studies were included in the meta-analysis. PRP demonstrated the most consistent evidence of accelerated canine retraction during the first month of treatment. i-PRF showed statistically significant effects across multiple observation periods, whereas L-PRF exhibited an earlier response pattern, with effects observed from the first week through the third month. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed in the i-PRF and L-PRF analyses. No consistent effects were identified on canine movement pattern or anchorage loss. No consistent increase in serious adverse outcomes was observed, although transient post-procedural pain and discomfort were reported following PRP and i-PRF administration. Moderate-certainty evidence supported the first-month effect of PRP, whereas all remaining findings were supported by low- to very low-certainty evidence.

CONCLUSIONS: APCs may accelerate orthodontic canine retraction following premolar extraction without clear evidence of increased adverse outcomes. The most reliable evidence currently supports a possible short-term benefit of PRP during the first month of treatment. Although i-PRF and L-PRF demonstrated potential effects over longer or earlier observation periods, the certainty of evidence remains low and substantial heterogeneity limits confidence in these findings. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials are required to determine the clinical relevance of these effects and to establish optimal application protocols.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD 420261377123).

articles.title: The Use and Utility of Preoperative Somatostatin Receptor-Based Imaging in Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs).

METHODS: A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging.

RESULTS: The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases.

CONCLUSION: Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

articles.title: Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Neurological Outcome in Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: A Post Hoc Analysis of TRACE-III Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as a marker of increased inflammatory response, modifies the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase is uncertain in patients 4.5-24 h after stroke onset. We investigated this in the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events-III (TRACE-III) trial.

METHODS: TRACE-III was a phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-endpoint trial that enrolled 516 patients from 58 centers in China between January 2022 and November 2023. Patients had anterior large vessel occlusion and evidence of salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging, presented 4.5-24 h after symptom onset, and were randomized 1:1 to intravenous tenecteplase (intervention) or standard medical treatment (control). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were modified Rankin scale score of 0-1 at 90 days and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death, respectively. This post hoc analysis in 513 patients with complete admission NLR data compared outcomes in patients with elevated NLR (> first quartile) and non-elevated NLR (≤ first quartile).

RESULTS: In the elevated NLR group (> 3.0), tenecteplase was associated with increased functional independence (61 [30.2%] vs. 36 [19.6%]; adjusted relative rate [aRR] 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-2.17; P = 0.03) compared to standard medical treatment. This benefit was not observed in the non-elevated NLR group (26 [41.9%] vs. 25 [38.5%]; aRR 1.12; 95% CI 0.73-1.73). Safety outcomes did not differ in either the elevated or non-elevated NLR groups.

CONCLUSION: Baseline NLR may provide a potential signal for differential treatment response to intravenous tenecteplase in patients with acute ischemic stroke, although these exploratory findings require further validation in independent studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: TRACE-III is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05141305.

articles.title: The Role of Sodium Valproate in Clozapine-Associated Cardiotoxicities: The Importance of Cellular and Systemic Energetics.
articles.abstract: The antipsychotic drug clozapine is associated with one of the broadest spectra of cardiac adverse effects. Many of these are of unknown aetiology, hindering clinicians' ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat them. Risk factors for clozapine-associated cardiotoxicities include concomitant valproic acid therapy and comorbidities associated with the dysregulation of systemic metabolism, such as obesity and diabetes. Therefore, this review aims to summarise existing evidence for the adverse effects of these drugs on cellular and systemic energetics. Both drugs are strongly associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, but in different tissues. Clozapine may be bioactivated within cardiomyocytes and their mitochondria, producing reactive species that damage these organelles, thus impairing oxidative phosphorylation. Valproate may have similar effects in hepatocytes but doesn't appear to be bioactivated in all cell types, though it reportedly has modest inhibitory effects on fatty acid oxidation. Both drugs affect substrate supply, altering serum lipid, carbohydrate, and ketone levels. In concert, these medications are likely to impair cardiac metabolic flexibility and energetics. Considering the absolute dependence of cardiomyocyte function on continuous energy supply, the dysregulation of cardiomyocyte energetics is likely to have a significant role in the development of clozapine-associated cardiotoxicities. However, limited investigation has been made of the effects of these drugs in cardiomyocytes specifically. Rectifying this could inform improved prevention, detection, and management of cardiotoxicities to facilitate the development of clinical strategies to enable the safer use of these medicines.

articles.title: Outcomes of Clostridium difficile infection in liver transplant patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a significant healthcare-associated complication, especially for liver transplant (LT) recipients who are at increased risk due to their immuno-suppressed status and antibiotic use. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed at elucidating the outcomes of CDI in LT recipients.

METHODS: We adhered to PRISMA guidelines and searched databases including CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase and Scopus until December 2024. Studies included LT recipients with and without CDI. Outcomes were pooled using meta-analytic techniques with risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous data and mean differences for continuous data.

RESULTS: Among 10 included studies (1,216,500 LT recipients; 3.2% with CDI), the primary pooled analysis showed no significant difference in mortality (OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.38-4.72; I2 = 100%). Sensitivity analyses excluding influential studies showed higher mortality in LT recipients with CDI (OR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.45-2.41; I2 = 43%). Length of stay was longer among LT recipients with CDI (mean difference, 6.00 days; 95% CI, 2.83-9.17; I2 = 100%), with sensitivity analysis showing a mean difference of seven days after exclusion of one study (I2 = 0%). Elevated model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) scores were significantly higher in CDI cases (mean difference, 2.77; 95% CI, 1.34-4.20), indicating higher disease severity at baseline. Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use was not significant in the primary pooled analysis (OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 0.29-16.27; I2 = 69%) but was significant after sensitivity analysis excluding one study (OR, 5.87; 95% CI, 2.65-13.03; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: In addition to a significant association between PPI use and increased risk of CDI, CDI significantly affects mortality, duration of hospital stays and pre-operative MELD scores in LT recipients, underscoring its impact on post-operative outcomes.

articles.title: Average annual occupational radiation exposure among dental staff: a 3-years retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Diagnostic radiography is indispensable in modern dentistry for its diagnostic and therapeutic value, yet it presents potential health risks to healthcare providers from long-term occupational radiation exposure. This retrospective study aimed to quantify the average annual occupational radiation doses received by dental staff members at King Fahad Armed Forces Hospital (KFAFH) from 2022 to 2024, evaluate exposure variations across clinical specialties, and assess personnel compliance regarding Thermoluminescent Dosimeter (TLD) badge utilization. The study cohort comprised all active dental professionals (N = 277) enrolled in the institutional radiation safety program. Longitudinal dosimetry data were extracted from centralized monitoring records. Deep personal dose equivalents Hp(10) and shallow personal dose equivalents Hp(0.07) were monitored quarterly and annually using lithium fluoride detector crystals (LiF: Mg, Ti). Statistical tracking utilized a repeated-measures design via IBM SPSS Statistics. Over the three-year tracking period, the median annual cumulative Hp(10) dose rose from 0.00 mSv (Q1, Q3: 0.00, 0.00) in 2022 to 0.10 mSv (Q1, Q3: 0.00, 0.11) in 2023, reaching 0.34 mSv (Q1, Q3: 0.16, 0.45) in 2024. Concurrently, median annual Hp(0.07) doses shifted from 0.00 mSv (2022) to 0.10 mSv (2023) and 0.29 mSv (2024). Extremity radiation exposure remained at an absolute baseline of 0.00 mSv across all years. Multi-variable analysis revealed no statistically significant variations in dose metrics among clinical specialties (p > 0.05). All observed occupational metrics remained profoundly beneath the annual dose thresholds recommended by the International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP). Occupational radiation exposure at KFAFH is exceptionally low and structurally well-controlled. The statistically significant temporal increase in recorded doses from 2022 to 2024 is indicative of enhanced behavioral compliance in consistent TLD badge utilization.

articles.title: Correction: Lactic acid bacteria, potentially probiotic, in whole-grain pet biscuits: survival and technological potential of millet-based formulations (Pennisetum glaucum).
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]

articles.title: Awareness, Willingness, and Use of Doxycycline Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Among Men Who Have Sex with Men in Taiwan.
articles.abstract: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxyPEP) engagement-awareness, willingness, and use-for bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevention remains understudied in Taiwan. This secondary analysis used logistic regression to examine doxyPEP engagement and its correlates among 1,654 men who have sex with men (MSM) in Taiwan (November-December 2023). Awareness, willingness, and use were reported by 24.4%, 33.0%, and 2.9% of participants, respectively. Awareness, willingness, and use were greater among MSM not living with HIV and taking PrEP and MSM living with HIV than among MSM not living with HIV and not taking PrEP. Bacterial STI diagnosis was associated with greater willingness and use; age ≥ 40 years, condomless anal sex, and receipt of ≥ 1 mpox vaccine dose were also associated with greater willingness. These findings suggest that PrEP and HIV treatment services and bacterial STI screening and treatment encounters may offer opportunities for doxyPEP delivery, while additional strategies may be needed to reach MSM not routinely engaged in these services.

articles.title: miR-486 attenuates myocardial ischaemia/reperfusion injury by inhibiting apoptosis and autophagy activation via the FOXO1/PTEN/AKT/mTOR axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective therapeutic interventions for myocardial ischaemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI) are lacking. The expression of miR-486, a cardiac-enriched microRNA, is downregulated in ischaemic myocardium; however, its functional role and underlying molecular mechanisms in MIRI remain unclear.

METHODS: To overexpress miR-486 in vivo, MIRI rat models were administered miR-486 AAV. Cardiac function was assessed using echocardiography, infarct size using 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining, and collagen deposition using haematoxylin and eosin and Masson's trichrome staining. In vitro, H9c2 cardiomyocytes were exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) and transfected with a miR-486 mimic, miR-486 inhibitor, or respective negative controls. Dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted in HEK-293T cells to validate FOXO1 and PTEN as direct targets of miR-486. Apoptosis- and autophagy-related protein expression was analysed using western blotting. siRNA-mediated silencing of FOXO1 or PTEN and pharmacological inhibition of AKT (MK2206) or mTOR (rapamycin) were used to establish the underlying signalling axis.

RESULTS: AAV-mediated overexpression of miR-486 significantly improved cardiac function, reduced infarct size, and attenuated myocardial histopathological injury in MIRI rats. In H9c2 cells, the miR-486 mimic suppressed OGD/R-induced elevation of FOXO1 and PTEN protein levels, whereas the miR-486 inhibitor further augmented their expression. MiR-486 directly targeted FOXO1 and PTEN via their respective 3'-UTRs in dual-luciferase reporter assays. MiR-486 overexpression markedly reduced the Bax/Bcl-2 and cleaved caspase-3/caspase-3 ratios. Additionally, it decreased Beclin 1 and LC3-II/GAPDH and increased p62 expression, indicating concurrent suppression of apoptosis and excessive autophagy. Notably, these effects were reversed with miR-486 inhibition. Consistent findings occurred in vivo. siRNA-mediated silencing of either FOXO1 or PTEN partially reversed the pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic effects induced by miR-486 inhibition. Under OGD/R conditions, the phosphorylation levels of AKT and mTORC1 downstream targets, including S6K and 4EBP1, were restored with miR-486 overexpression. The contribution of AKT/mTOR signalling to the protective effects mediated by the miR-486 mimic was confirmed with AKT or mTOR inhibition.

CONCLUSIONS: MiR-486 attenuates MIRI by directly targeting FOXO1 and PTEN, thereby facilitating AKT/mTOR pathway activation to co-ordinately suppress cardiomyocyte apoptosis and excessive autophagy. These findings support the involvement of the miR-486/FOXO1/PTEN/AKT/mTOR axis as an important cardioprotective mechanism and identify miR-486 as a potential therapeutic target for MIRI.

articles.title: Curcumin alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease via gut microbiota-dependent epigenetic alterations.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly prevalent, yet effective therapies remain limited. Curcumin (Cur), a polyphenol with well-documented metabolic benefits, shows therapeutic promise in MASLD, but its efficacy and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. A meta-analysis of seven clinical studies indicated that Cur supplementation reduced serum aminotransferase levels, supporting its potential clinical benefit. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed rats, Cur reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and metabolic dysfunction, whereas these effects were markedly weakened in antibiotic-induced pseudo-germ-free rats, indicating microbiota dependence. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Cur-treated donors transferred these metabolic and histological benefits to antibiotic-conditioned recipients. Fecal 16S rRNA sequencing identified Clostridium_sensu_stricto_1 (C. sensu) as a Cur-suppressed, pro-steatotic taxon, and targeted reconstitution of this taxon abolished Cur-mediated protection. Untargeted hepatic metabolomics and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry identified kynurenine (KYN) as a C. sensu-derived metabolite and showed that Cur reduced hepatic KYN accumulation. Integrated H3K27ac ChIP-seq, bulk RNA-seq, and single-cell analyses pinpointed hepatocyte-enriched CEBPB as a key epigenetically regulated effector. Luciferase reporter assays, ChIP-qPCR, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments showed that KYN activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR), increased H3K27ac enrichment at the Cebpb locus, and induced Cebpb transcription. CEBPB knockdown blocked KYN-induced PI3K-AKT activation and lipid accumulation, whereas in vivo KYN supplementation largely reversed Cur-mediated protection. Collectively, this study reveals a novel gut-liver axis in MASLD pathogenesis, demonstrating that Cur alleviates hepatic steatosis by targeting the microbiota-KYN-AHR-H3K27ac-Cebpb epigenetic axis, positioning Cur supplementation and KYN modulation as promising therapeutic strategies for MASLD intervention.

articles.title: The toll of voting in a pandemic? Regional elections and the spread of COVID-19 in Bavaria.
articles.journal: The European journal of health economics : HEPAC : health economics in prevention and care
articles.abstract: This study investigates whether the regional elections held in the German state of Bavaria on March 15 of 2020 - shortly after the WHO declared COVID-19 a global pandemic - contributed to the spread of COVID-19 cases and COVID-related deaths. Constructing synthetic controls for each of Bavaria's 96 districts based on non-Bavarian German districts, we find that over a third of the increase in positive test results cannot be explained by district-level demographic, economic, health or child care characteristics, nor by the distance to Ischgl - a proxy for skiing tourism associated with the first COVID-19 wave in Germany. Within Bavaria, districts with higher voter participation witnessed a steeper increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths after the election, while controlling for alternative drivers, such as the distance to Ischgl and the number of strong-beer festivals. Our results are highly robust and suggest that an unfortunate timing of elections contributed to the spreading of an infectious disease.

articles.title: lncRNA HOTAIR promotes airway remodeling by regulating metabolic reprogramming through the FUS/HK2 axis in airway smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway remodeling is a critical pathological feature of chronic airway diseases and is closely associated with irreversible airflow limitation. Increasing evidence indicates that metabolic reprogramming contributes to airway smooth muscle cell (ASMC) remodeling; however, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Human ASMCs were stimulated with platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) to establish an in vitro remodeling model. HOTAIR expression was manipulated using siRNA-mediated knockdown, while FUS and HK2 were restored by plasmid overexpression. Cell viability, proliferation, migration, glycolytic metabolism, and remodeling-associated protein expression were assessed using CCK-8, EdU staining, Transwell assays, Seahorse extracellular flux analysis, qRT-PCR, and western blotting. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) and mRNA stability assays were performed to investigate the interaction among HOTAIR, FUS, and HK2.

RESULTS: HOTAIR expression was significantly upregulated in PDGF-BB-stimulated ASMCs. HOTAIR knockdown markedly inhibited ASMC proliferation, migration, and ECM remodeling, with reduced expression of Collagen I, Fibronectin, MMP9, and α-SMA. HOTAIR silencing suppressed glucose uptake, lactate production, ATP generation, and ECAR while partially restoring mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. FUS directly bound both HOTAIR and HK2 mRNA; HOTAIR depletion accelerated HK2 mRNA degradation, whereas FUS restoration rescued HK2 mRNA stability. Re-expression of either FUS or HK2 reversed the inhibitory effects of HOTAIR silencing on glycolytic metabolism and ASMC remodeling phenotypes.

CONCLUSION: HOTAIR promotes PDGF-BB-induced glycolytic reprogramming and airway smooth muscle remodeling by stabilizing HK2 mRNA through the RNA-binding protein FUS. T These findings suggest that the HOTAIR/FUS/HK2 axis contributes to PDGF-BB-induced ASMC remodeling and may represent a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Tissue Dissociation Workflows Influence Reactive Astrocyte Recovery in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has advanced our understanding of glial diversity, yet tissue dissociation remains an important technical variable. We revealed that a widely used commercial dissociation protocol can underrepresent reactive astrocytes in an acute ischemic stroke model, with preliminary observations indicating a comparable trend in a chronic tauopathy model. Benchmarking against an optimized, low-shear workflow demonstrates that different tissue dissociation workflows can substantially alter the recovery and apparent transcriptomic profile of disease-associated astrocytes, selectively losing signatures of morphological remodeling. Our findings indicate that workflow-dependent recovery biases affecting reactive astrocytes may be more prevalent than recognized, underscoring the need for pathology-tailored, gentle isolation workflows to avoid distortions in downstream neuropathological interpretations and the prioritization of therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel miniaturized robotic assisted surgery system in hysterectomy: a prospective, investigational device exemption clinical trial.
articles.abstract: To evaluate safety and effectiveness of the first-in-kind miniaturized surgical robotic platform, the MIRA Surgical System, in patients presenting with an indication for benign hysterectomy. A prospective, multi-center, multi-operator, non-randomized, consecutively enrolled Investigational Device Exemption Clinical Trial. Five surgeons participated across three types of institutions. Thirty-five patients with a mean age of 46.1 years (range 25-74) and a mean BMI of 29.2 kg/m² (range 21.5-41.5) were operated upon. Indications were menorrhagia (71.4%), fibroids (28.6%), and/or dysmenorrhea (25.7%). A total hysterectomy with uni-/bi-lateral salpingectomy was performed in 80%, a total hysterectomy with uni-/bi-lateral salpingo-oophorectomy in 14.3% and a total hysterectomy without adnexectomy in 5.7%. One subject required conversion to a laparoscopy due to a technical malfunction. Mean estimated blood loss was 52.6 ml (median 50 ml; range 10-200 ml). Specimens weighed from 31.2 g to 384 g (mean 136.1 g). No malignancies were identified. Vaginal-cuff closure was successfully completed in 34 cases, and completed vaginally in the converted case. Mean procedure duration was 141.8 min (median 127; range 73-273). Mean length of stay post-operatively was 5.0 h (median 3.5; range 1.3-29.4 h). Ten adverse events were reported: two intraoperative device-related and eight postoperative procedure-related (Seven Clavien-Dindo Grade-I, three Grade-II; no Grade-III or higher events). All resolved. The MIRA Surgical System demonstrated technical feasibility and an acceptable short-term safety profile in a selected cohort of patients undergoing benign hysterectomy. Evaluation in larger, diverse cohorts, with longer follow-up is required. (Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT06028542, Registration date: 16 August 2023.).

articles.title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%).

CONCLUSION: Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.

articles.title: Preoperative ureteral rest and outcomes of robot-assisted upper urinary tract reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether a preoperative period of ureteral rest, defined as the absence of any indwelling stent crossing the diseased or anastomotic segment (irrespective of whether upper-tract drainage is maintained by a percutaneous nephrostomy), is associated with improved surgical success and perioperative outcomes after robot-assisted upper urinary tract reconstruction, comprising ureteral reconstruction and pyeloplasty for ureteropelvic junction obstruction. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection and the Cochrane Library from inception to 31 July 2026, and included English-language studies that compared ureteral rest with immediate reconstruction. Studies without a no-rest comparator or without the key outcomes were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed in Review Manager 5.3 and R, using odds ratios (OR) or risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous outcomes. The review was registered with PROSPERO (registration number CRD420261504719). Five retrospective comparative studies including 707 patients (478 managed with preoperative ureteral rest and 229 managed without) were analysed. Preoperative ureteral rest was associated with a higher pooled surgical success rate (OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.57 to 5.07, P = 0.0005; 447/478 [93.5%] versus 198/229 [86.5%]; absolute risk difference + 7.6%, 95% CI 2.9% to 12.4%) and with a small reduction in estimated intraoperative blood loss (MD -23.91 mL, 95% CI -35.79 to -12.03, P < 0.0001; three studies). No statistically significant differences were detected for operative time (MD 7.00 min, 95% CI -2.05 to 16.05, P = 0.13), length of hospital stay (MD -0.26 days, 95% CI -1.00 to 0.48, P = 0.49; I2 = 95%) or postoperative complications (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.31, P = 0.40). Subgroup analyses by indication showed no significant interaction for any outcome (P for subgroup difference: surgical success 0.97, operative time 0.59, complications 0.98); the confidence interval for the ureteropelvic junction obstruction subgroup was wide because only two studies contributed data. Available retrospective comparative evidence suggests that preoperative ureteral rest is associated with higher surgical success after robot-assisted upper urinary tract reconstruction and with a small reduction in estimated blood loss. No clear association was observed with operative time, length of stay or postoperative complications.
