Because the available evidence is limited to a small number of retrospective studies with heterogeneous indications, definitions and reconstructive techniques, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Current data are insufficient to establish whether the effect differs between acquired ureteral strictures and ureteropelvic junction obstruction.

articles.title: Rewiring autophagy to target cutaneous wound healing: investigation of molecular mechanisms to therapeutic interventions.
articles.abstract: Rewiring of pathways regulating inflammation, metabolism, and regeneration must occur in a coordinated fashion during wound healing; however, this orchestration gets disrupted in chronic and diabetic wounds. Autophagy is a conserved lysosome-dependent pathway that controls the integration of nutrient homeostasis, adaptation to stresses, immune regulation, and cell remodelling during wound repair. Here we summarize the pivotal role of autophagy in the different crucial steps of wound healing. An open wound often attracts pathogens, leading to infection and inflammation. During this inflammation stage, autophagy mediates signalling from the pattern recognition receptors, generates cytokines, manoeuvres the defence against infection, and polarizes macrophage. During proliferation stage, autophagy promotes keratinocyte migration, fibroblast function, endothelial cell survival, angiogenesis, while minimizing oxidative injury and apoptosis. During the remodelling stage, autophagy participates in the remodelling of the extracellular matrix, collagen maturation, and scar formation. However, these processes are context-dependent; while insufficient autophagy prevents adaptation and regeneration, we see excessive autophagy may contribute to pathological conditions associated with chronic wounds. The analysis also considers new therapeutic approaches including mTOR and AMPK inhibitors, phytochemicals, exosomes from mesenchymal stem cells, and the use of biomaterials for the delivery of drugs. Although they improve re-epithelization, vascularization, and matrix organization in preclinical models, the clinical application of these approaches is hampered by the lack of specificity of the pathway, poor stability and penetrability of drugs, off-target effects, and a lack of clinical trials in humans.

articles.title: Potential role of CTHRC1 in renal fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is a major morphological feature of chronic kidney disease and is considered an important pathogenetic process that leads to a decline in renal function in the progressive course of the disease. It is characterized by excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix, tubular atrophy, interstitial inflammation, capillary thinning, and nephron structural disruption. The development of fibrosis involves transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), Wnt/β-catenin, inflammatory mediators, and intercellular communication between macrophages and activated fibroblasts. TGF-β, as one of the main driving factors of renal fibrosis, enhancing the activation of myofibroblasts and the accumulation of extracellular matrix proteins such as collagen and fibronectin through Smad-dependent and Smad-independent pathways. Collagen Triple Helix Repeat Containing 1 (CTHRC1), a secreted glycoprotein, was initially described in vascular remodeling and tissue repair processes after injury, and later studies began to consider it as a regulatory molecule in fibrotic diseases. The high expression of CTHRC1 protein in renal tissue in tubular cells and undetectable levels in glomerular cells provide a basis for investigating its association with tubulointerstitial injury in the kidney. CTHRC1 may be involved in fibroblast migration, tissue remodeling, extracellular matrix metabolism, and interaction with the TGF-β/Wnt signaling systems during kidney fibrogenesis. This review discusses the potential role of CTHRC1 in renal fibrosis, its relationship with the TGF-β and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, and its potential as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in chronic kidney diseases.

articles.title: Pediatric Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (P-VExUS): a novel approach to assess central venous pressure in the PICU.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Accurate assessment of central venous pressure (CVP) in critically ill children is important for guiding fluid management but remains challenging, as invasive monitoring is not always feasible and noninvasive tools are limited. We aimed to develop and validate pediatric adaptations of the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (P-VExUS) for bedside estimation of CVP in mechanically ventilated children. This prospective observational study was conducted in a tertiary-care PICU. Fifty-six mechanically ventilated children were included. Venous Doppler ultrasonography of the inferior vena cava, hepatic, portal, and intrarenal veins was performed at the bedside. Two P-VExUS models were evaluated: (1) a categorical grading system (0-III) and (2) a semiquantitative point-based score (0-7). Diagnostic performance was assessed for predefined, clinically relevant CVP thresholds reflecting low (< 7 mmHg) and elevated (> 12 mmHg) venous pressure states using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Both models were significantly associated with measured CVP. For predicting elevated CVP, model 1 showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.74 (95% CI 0.61-0.85), with 45% sensitivity and 98% specificity. Model 2 demonstrated superior accuracy (AUROC 0.94, 95% CI 0.84-0.98), with 82% sensitivity and 91% specificity (p < 0.001). For detecting low CVP, model 2 also outperformed model 1 (AUROC 0.80 vs. 0.69; p = 0.02). Intrarenal vein patterns had the highest discriminative ability (AUROC 0.92).

CONCLUSION: Pediatric-specific P-VExUS models were feasible and accurate for estimating CVP in critically ill children. The point-based model showed superior diagnostic performance and may represent a promising noninvasive bedside tool for assessing venous congestion.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Elevated central venous pressure (CVP) is associated with adverse outcomes in critically ill children, including mortality and renal dysfunction. • Inferior vena cava-based ultrasound indices have limited accuracy for estimating CVP in mechanically ventilated children, while pediatric adaptations of the Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) remain poorly defined.

WHAT IS NEW: • This study proposes and evaluates two pediatric adaptations of VExUS, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance of a point-based model for identifying elevated (12 mmHg) and low (7 mmHg) CVP. • Intrarenal venous Doppler showed the highest individual discriminative performance, suggesting potential simplification of venous congestion assessment in critically ill children.

articles.title: Operating under pressure: a scoping review of the effects of climate change on general surgery.
authors: SAGES and EAES Sustainability in Surgery Committee
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Climate change adversely impacts human health; however, its effect on surgical diseases remains poorly understood. We conducted a scoping review to elucidate the current understanding of climate change's role in general surgical care and care delivery.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of Medline, Embase, Cochrane, and CINAHL was supplemented by manual searches. Broad terms for climate change in general surgery and its subspecialties were used. Climate-related effects were defined as daily or seasonal temperature anomalies and extreme weather events (e.g., hurricanes, floods, wildfires). Full-text articles were reviewed for relevance to treatment of surgical diseases, postoperative outcomes, and access to surgical care attributable to climate change. Thematic analysis identified recurring themes among included studies.

RESULTS: Of 5110 studies, 28 met inclusion criteria. Three themes were identified: access to surgical care, shifts in surgical disease burden, and postoperative outcomes. Five studies described decreased access to care following extreme weather events, including one reporting increased breast cancer mortality after Hurricane Katrina. Eleven studies highlighted shifts in surgical disease patterns. Temperature anomalies correlated with higher rates of traumatic injuries, skin and soft tissue infections, and complicated appendicitis. Extreme weather events were associated with increased surgical trauma and emergency case volume. Five articles found temperature anomalies associated with higher postoperative surgical site infection rates, while two did not. Four articles examined outcomes after extreme weather events, including one associating wildfire smoke exposure with worse overall survival after lung resection and another identifying longer hospital stays in wildfire-exposed facilities.

CONCLUSION: High-level evidence regarding climate change's impact on general surgery remains limited. Emerging evidence suggests that extreme weather events and temperature fluctuations may increase demand for surgical services, disrupt timely access to treatment, and worsen postoperative outcomes. These effects may further strain healthcare systems and resources, requiring targeted mitigation and future research in this important evolving field.

articles.title: Tenecteplase, alteplase, and endovascular thrombectomy in extended-window acute ischemic stroke with intracranial large-vessel occlusion: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). An anterior-circulation LVO network and an all-available network were examined as sensitivity and exploratory analyses. Bayesian random-effects consistency models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The primary outcome was functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 at 90 days.

RESULTS: Fifteen randomized trials were included, of which 8 contributed to the primary confirmed LVO/BAO network. Compared with placebo or best medical care, EVT significantly improved functional independence (OR, 2.93 [95% CrI, 1.40-6.53]) and excellent functional outcome, defined as mRS 0 to 1 (OR, 2.22 [95% CrI, 1.30-4.11]), reduced 90-day mortality (OR, 0.71 [95% CrI, 0.50-0.98]), and increased trial-defined recanalization or reperfusion at approximately 24 hours (OR, 5.27 [95% CrI, 1.83-16.04]); sICH was also increased (OR, 2.65 [95% CrI, 1.28-5.81]). Compared with EVT, tenecteplase plus EVT showed numerically favorable but statistically inconclusive estimates for functional independence (OR, 1.10 [95% CrI, 0.34-3.52]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.16 [95% CrI, 0.52-2.64]). Direct pairwise analyses of 2 trials were similarly inconclusive. Tenecteplase alone did not show clear differences from placebo or best medical care. Findings were directionally consistent in the anterior-circulation sensitivity and all-available exploratory networks.

CONCLUSIONS: Among imaging-selected patients with confirmed intracranial LVO or BAO treated 4.5 to 24 hours after onset or last known well, EVT had the most consistent evidence of benefit versus placebo or best medical care. Tenecteplase plus EVT showed favorable but imprecise estimates, and neither network nor direct pairwise analyses established superiority over EVT alone. The incremental benefit of bridging tenecteplase remains uncertain.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use and contrast-associated acute kidney injury after contrast-enhanced CT and CT angiography in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use is associated with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CE-CT) or computed tomographic angiography (CTA) in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD).

METHODS: We conducted a TriNetX retrospective cohort study of adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD who underwent CE-CT or CTA from January 2020 to January 2025. GLP-1 RA use was defined by a prescription within six months before imaging. The primary outcome was a new acute kidney injury diagnosis within three days. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched analyses were conducted for CE-CT and CTA, with eGFR-stratified and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: After matching, the CE-CT and CTA cohorts included 6,995 and 3,285 pairs, respectively. CA-AKI occurred in 3.8% of GLP-1 RA users versus 4.5% of non-users after CE-CT (odds ratio [OR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.71-0.99) and in 4.5% versus 6.1% after CTA (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.92). The absolute risk differences were 0.7% points and 1.5% points, respectively. HbA1c remained imbalanced after matching. Negative-control outcomes were null, and eGFR-stratified associations were inconsistent between cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with a lower observed risk of CA-AKI after CE-CT and CTA in adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD. Residual HbA1c imbalance and the observational design limit causal interpretation; prospective studies using creatinine-based outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Evolving phenotype of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: a 15-year population-based comparison.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Our aim was to describe the phenotype at diagnosis and the early therapeutic profile of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes across two periods spanning approximately 15 years within the same integrated healthcare system.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services (Haifa & Western Galilee, Israel). Adults with incident type 2 diabetes in 2005-2008 (period 1: n=80,201) were compared with those diagnosed in 2020-2023 (period 2: n=101,392). Between-period differences are presented as crude estimates, with an age-stratified sensitivity analysis, and quantified using standardised mean differences (SMDs; values ≥0.20 indicate at least a small effect) alongside non-parametric and χ2 tests.

RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis increased from 63.0 to 66.7 years between the two periods; the proportion aged ≥85 years nearly doubled (from 3.5% to 6.6%). The score for the Charlson comorbidity index increased from 4 to 6 (SMD 0.48); metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) increased from 4.4% to 18.6%. HbA1c at diagnosis decreased from 56 to 53 mmol/mol (7.3% to 7.0%); pre-diagnosis LDL-cholesterol decreased from 2.90 to 2.21 mmol/l (SMD 0.65). Within 31-90 days of diagnosis, use of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors increased from 0.07% to 15.0%, use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) increased from 0% to 11.1%, and sulfonylurea use decreased more than fourfold (20.8% to 4.5%).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: The phenotype of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes has been fundamentally restructured since 2008: patients are older with a higher comorbidity burden but present with better glycaemic and lipid management, with the latter reflecting statin therapy already established before diagnosis. MASLD has emerged as a major but largely ascertainment-driven comorbidity. The shift to SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1RAs alongside declining sulfonylurea use indicates displacement of glucose-centric strategies by a cardiorenal- and weight-driven paradigm. These findings indicate a need for age-appropriate management and trials enrolling very elderly patients.

articles.title: Altered glucagon and GIP responses in South Asian versus Nordic women after gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: We aimed to compare ethnic differences in levels of glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) following a pregnancy complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to assess whether the higher insulin levels observed in South Asian compared with Nordic women could be explained by differences in the hormone secretory responses.

METHODS: We measured glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 in 178 South Asian and 107 Nordic women during an OGTT, and stratified participants by glycaemic status. Glucagon and total GLP-1 and GIP responses when fasting and post-OGTT were assessed by linear mixed models. Ethnic differences in incretin and glucagon levels were evaluated by linear regression analyses. Pre-hepatic insulin levels were estimated using deconvolution of C-peptide kinetics.

RESULTS: Ethnic differences in glucagon and incretin levels varied by glycaemic status. In the normoglycaemic South Asian group, early (0-15 min) glucagon suppression post-OGTT was significantly attenuated compared with the Nordic group (p=0.002). Fasting glucagon levels did not differ (p=0.139), but total glucagon exposure (including fasting levels) was higher in South Asian women (p=0.013). No differences in GIP and GLP responses to the OGTT were observed (p=0.490 and p=0.802). In women with prediabetes or diabetes, fasting glucagon was higher in the South Asian group (p=0.010), but there were no significant differences in early glucagon suppression post-OGTT (p=0.986). GIP responses to the OGTT were lower among South Asian women (p<0.001), despite higher insulin responses compared with the Nordic women. GLP-1 responses did not differ between the ethnic groups (p=0.661). The higher pre-hepatic insulin levels in South Asian vs Nordic normoglycaemic women were not associated with differences in incretin levels, but were associated with lower insulin sensitivity in the regression analyses (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: When examined 1-3 years post-GDM, normoglycaemic South Asian women had less early glucagon suppression and higher total glucagon exposure post-OGTT compared with Nordic women. The higher pre-hepatic insulin levels were not associated with higher incretin levels, but were associated with lower insulin sensitivity.

articles.title: Clinical and ultrasonographic effects of extracorporeal shock wave therapy in patients with lipedema: A prospective study.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo investigate the clinical and ultrasonographic changes associated with radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) in women with lipedema.MethodsThis prospective, single-arm study included 40 women with lipedema who completed six sessions of rESWT administered twice weekly to the index lower limb. Treatment consisted of 3000-6000 impulses at 15 Hz and 3-4 bar. Participants were evaluated at baseline (T0), immediately after treatment (T1), and at 4-week follow-up (T2). Outcomes included visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) scores, pressure pain threshold (PPT), limb circumference, subcutaneous fat thickness (SCFT), and tissue echogenicity. Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) was assessed at T1 and T2.ResultsVAS scores decreased from 8.45 at T0 to 5.45 at T1 and 4.17 at T2, while PROMIS scores decreased from 25.3 to 16.2 and 14.3, respectively (both p < .001). PPT increased significantly at all four evaluated sites (p < .001). Calf and thigh circumferences decreased significantly over time (both p < .001). Medial calf SCFT decreased from 16.5 to 15.2 and 15.1 mm, and medial thigh SCFT from 21.0 to 18.2 and 18.1 mm (both p < .001). Median tissue echogenicity decreased from 3 at baseline to 2 at both post-treatment assessments (p < .001). PGIC scores also improved between T1 and T2 (p < .001).ConclusionsSix sessions of rESWT were associated with improvements in pain, quality of life, mechanical pain sensitivity, limb circumference, and ultrasonographic tissue characteristics in women with lipedema, with most improvements maintained at 4-week follow-up. These findings support further evaluation of rESWT as an adjunctive conservative treatment for lipedema in controlled studies with longer follow-up.Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07683559.

articles.title: Standard Reference Material (SRM®) 1950 metabolites in frozen human plasma-use, impact, lessons learned, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: In 2011, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in collaboration with the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), issued Standard Reference Material (SRM)® 1950 Metabolites in Frozen Human Plasma to support metabolomics measurements. This critical review traces the development of SRM 1950 and assesses its use and impact over the past 15 years. To evaluate its impact, we reviewed more than 400 technical papers demonstrating its broad adoption in analytical, metabolomic, and lipidomic research. While SRM 1950 included certified values for selected amino acids, fatty acids, and clinical markers (such as cholesterol, glucose, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and steroid hormones), its greatest impact has been as a shared material for interlaboratory comparisons and the community-generated consensus or target values established for the broad scope of compounds commonly measured in metabolomic and lipidomic studies. Many studies used SRM 1950 to validate analytical methods against NIST-certified values, while over 50 papers provided extensive qualitative and quantitative characterization and compared their results with interlaboratory consensus values and other studies to assess method and platform performance. The success of SRM 1950 helped to catalyze the development of additional NIST reference materials (RMs) for the "omics" communities and highlighted the potential of existing clinical and environmental matrix SRMs for further untargeted characterization and community reporting. Based on this literature review, we offer recommendations to expand the use and impact of the next generation of SRM 1950 and other SRMs/RMs intended and/or useful for untargeted analyses.

articles.title: Endoscopic Subcutaneous Mastectomy with Cold-Knife Flap Dissection Through a Single Axillary Incision for Gynaecomastia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gynaecomastia (GNY) is the most common benign proliferation of glandular breast tissues in males and is frequently associated with psychosocial distress and aesthetic concerns. Traditional open surgical approaches are associated with visible scarring and prolonged postoperative recovery. Minimally invasive techniques, including liposuction-assisted endoscopic procedures, may still result in visible scars and residual glandular tissue. In this study, we evaluated the safety, efficacy, and aesthetic outcomes of endoscopic subcutaneous mastectomy combined with cold-knife flap dissection through a single axillary incision for the treatment of GNY.

METHODS: A total of 51 male patients with GNY involving 102 breasts who underwent surgical treatment between August 2023 and October 2024 were enrolled. Patient demographics, operative data, postoperative complications, and satisfaction outcomes were systematically recorded. Four independent observers evaluated preoperative and postoperative photographs using a 1-15 scoring system based on six major aesthetic parameters.

RESULTS: Endoscopic subcutaneous mastectomy combined with cold-knife flap dissection through a single axillary incision was successfully completed in all patients. The mean operative time was 46.84 ± 15.04 per side (range 14-87) min. The mean thickness of the resected glandular tissues was 2.80 ± 0.88 (range 1-5) cm. The mean postoperative drainage volume was 48.72 ± 34.74 (range 10-170) mL, and the mean hospital stay was 4.31 ± 1.57 (range 2-8) days. Postoperative complications included hematoma in two breasts, seromas in one breast, and effusion in two breasts, whereas skin redundancy occurred in two patients with bilateral GNY. No patient developed severe pain, infection, nipple-areolar complex necrosis, nipple retraction, or skin flap necrosis. All patients reported satisfaction with postoperative quality of life (100%), and no recurrence was observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic subcutaneous mastectomy combined with cold-knife flap dissection through a single axillary incision appears to be a safe and effective approach for GNY, offering minimal invasiveness, rapid postoperative recovery, and favourable aesthetic outcomes. This technique may improve patient satisfaction and may represent a promising treatment option owing to its favourable safety profile and cosmetic outcomes.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE IV: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine Ratings, please refer to Table of Contents or online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: ABO blood group-dependent association of serum retinol-binding protein 4 with eosinophilic inflammation and spirometric parameters in adults with asthma.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Growing evidence links retinol binding protein-4 (RBP4) to inflammation; however, its association with inflammatory cell indices and spirometric parameters in asthma remains unclear, and the potential modifying role of ABO blood group has yet to be explored. The main aim was to assess the associations of serum RBP4 with inflammatory cell indices and spirometric parameters in adults with asthma stratified by blood group O and non-O. Adults with physician-diagnosed asthma attending a respiratory clinic between January and June 2026 were consecutively enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Spearman's correlation assessed associations involving inflammatory cell indices, whereas Pearson's correlation evaluated associations between normally distributed serum RBP4 and spirometric parameters. Of the 88 adults with asthma enrolled, 64 had available ABO blood group data (38 O and 26 Non-O) and were included in the blood group-stratified analyses. In the O group, RBP4 was positively correlated with eosinophil count (ρ=0.35, p=0.03), eosinophil-to-neutrophil ratio (ρ=0.42, p<0.01), and eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (ρ=0.41, p=0.01), whereas no significant associations were observed in the non-O group. Serum RBP4 was not correlated with spirometric parameters in either group. The forced expiratory volume in one second/forced vital capacity ratio was inversely correlated with eosinophil and lymphocyte counts only in the O group, while lymphocyte count showed an inverse correlation with forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% of forced vital capacity in the non-O group. In conclusion, serum RBP4 was positively associated with eosinophilic inflammatory markers only in adults with asthma belonging to blood group O, whereas no such associations were observed in the non-O group.

articles.title: A retrospective study of flexible bronchoscopic retrieval of airway foreign bodies in adults.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Unlike in children, foreign body aspiration in adults is an uncommon occurrence. The clinical presentation is often nonspecific, with a myriad of symptoms and radiological abnormalities. These cases can mimic chronic lung conditions like asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, thereby delaying definitive diagnosis and timely interventions. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the bronchoscopy suite database (January 2022 to December 2025) to identify cases subjected to flexible bronchoscopy for suspicion of a foreign body.  Data on demographics, clinical symptoms, radiological findings, type of foreign body, retrieval methods, and procedure-related complications were retrieved and analyzed. During the study period, a total of 1679 flexible bronchoscopies were performed. Of these, 12 (0.71%) were done for suspected foreign body aspiration. A foreign body was identified in 10 cases (83.33%), and in eight cases (80%), the foreign body was successfully retrieved using a flexible bronchoscope. The mean age of the study population was 48.38±20.23 years, with a female preponderance (62.5%). The most common radiological presentation was atelectasis, and direct visualization of foreign bodies was found in five cases (627.5%). Organic foreign bodies were commonly identified (87.5% of cases); among them, betel nut was the most common foreign body. Grasping forceps and Dormia baskets were the most commonly used instruments, with no major complications. Foreign body aspiration in adults is a rare clinical entity, and a high index of suspicion is required to identify such cases. Flexible bronchoscopy is the modality of choice for diagnosis and retrieval of foreign bodies with a high success rate and minimal complications.

articles.title: Reproductive-age status and intracranial hypertension in women with cerebral venous thrombosis: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) predominantly affects reproductive-age women, but the relationship between reproductive-age status and intracranial hypertension (IH) phenotype remains unclear.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive female patients with first-ever acute or subacute CVT treated at a tertiary stroke center between September 2014 and March 2023. Patients were stratified into reproductive-age (18-45 years) and non-reproductive-age (>45 years) groups. Clinical characteristics, imaging findings, and 12-month outcomes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: A total of 182 women with CVT were included, comprising 122 of reproductive age. Reproductive-age women were more likely to present with IH at admission compared with their non-reproductive-age counterparts (59.0% vs. 41.7%, p = 0.027). In the overall female cohort, reproductive-age status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.00-3.84; p = 0.049) and superior sagittal sinus involvement (aOR, 2.73; 95% CI, 1.36-5.48; p = 0.005) were independently associated with IH. Within the reproductive-age subgroup, superior sagittal sinus involvement (aOR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.25-7.21; p = 0.014) and left lateral sinus system involvement (aOR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.37-7.56; p = 0.007) were independently associated with IH. Although overall functional outcomes at follow-up were similar, residual visual impairment was significantly more frequent in reproductive-age women with IH.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with CVT, reproductive-age status is associated with a greater likelihood of IH. In reproductive-age women, superior sagittal sinus and left lateral sinus system involvement were independently associated with IH, although the laterality-specific finding requires further validation.

articles.title: First-in-Human Permanent Totally Leadless Left Ventricular Septal Endocardial Pacing With Atrioventricular Synchrony.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless cardiac resynchronization combining WiSE system ultrasound-mediated left ventricular pacing with leadless right ventricular pacing has been reported. However, atrioventricular-sequential left ventricular pacing triggered by atrial leadless pacing impulse without right ventricular pacing has not been reported.

FIRST-IN-HUMAN/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: An 86-year-old man with complete heart block and cardiomyopathy received a dual-chamber leadless pacemaker (AVEIR DR) with WiSE left ventricular endocardial electrode on the septal wall. A novel "sync-to-pace" delay configuration enabled the atrial pacing impulse to trigger left ventricular stimulation, achieving a QRS duration of 142 ms.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates proof of concept for a fully leadless atrioventricular-synchronized system capable of delivering left ventricular septal endocardial pacing without right ventricular pacing dependency, offering a physiological pacing strategy for selected patients.

NOVELTY: First-in-human demonstration of an ultrasound-mediated left ventricular endocardial electrode triggered by an atrial leadless pacing impulse to deliver atrioventricular-sequential left ventricular septal stimulation without right ventricular pacing.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This novel totally leadless architecture is a proof of concept for a more physiological pacing option for pacing-dependent patients while avoiding transvenous lead-related complications.

articles.title: Successful Guidewire-Guided Ethanol Ablation for PVCs Originating From Epicardial Anterior Interventricular Groove Adjacent to LAD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from epicardial anterior interventricular groove and closely adjacent to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) are difficult to eliminate and carry high risks of coronary damage or occlusion. We describe a successful guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation in this high -risk patient.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man who presented with palpitations and high-burden PVCs was admitted to our hospital. Pace mapping performed at the epicardial anterior interventricular groove yielded QRS morphology nearly identical to the native PVCs. Coronary angiography revealed that the target site was directly adjacent to the proximal-middle segment of the LAD. Guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation via a small branch of the anterior interventricular vein successfully eliminated the PVCs. Postprocedural coronary angiography showed no coronary artery injury and the patient remained free of PVCs during the 2-month follow-up period.

DISCUSSION: Epicardial PVCs arising within the anterior interventricular groove where the LAD runs carry a high risk of coronary artery injury during ablation. Guidewire-assisted anhydrous ethanol ablation serves as an effective and safe therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Tachycardia Initiation by Dual-Mode PVC on Ambulatory ECG: Pattern Discovery and Invasive Electrophysiological Characteristics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanisms of premature ventricular complex (PVC)-induced long-RP tachycardia warrant investigation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with palpitations underwent 24-hour ambulatory electrocardiogram (ECG). The recording showed 4,150 monomorphic PVCs and 800 episodes of long-RP tachycardia, all triggered by the same PVC morphology. Two initiation patterns emerged. One involved direct retrograde conduction, the other showed retrograde conduction only after PR prolongation. In both patterns, induction occurred across a broad range of PVC coupling intervals. Invasive electrophysiology study (EPS) then demonstrated slow-slow atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (SS-AVNRT) involving multiple atrioventricular nodal pathways, consistent with the dual-mode patterns seen on ambulatory ECG. Ablation succeeded, with no recurrence at 6 months.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of SS-AVNRT to show distinctive PVC-induced tachycardia patterns on ambulatory ECG, corroborated by EPS.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ambulatory ECG patterns of PVC-triggered long-RP tachycardia may suggest a dual-pathway substrate for SS-AVNRT, warranting EPS confirmation.

articles.title: Transcatheter Adrenal Arterial Embolization for Life-Threatening Pheochromocytoma Crisis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pheochromocytoma crisis is a life-threatening endocrine emergency frequently complicated by Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) and cardiogenic shock. Hemodynamic stabilization is difficult to achieve with medical therapy alone, and emergency surgery carries high perioperative mortality.

CASE SUMMARY: A 50-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, de Winter sign, basal-type TTS, and refractory cardiogenic shock with extreme blood pressure lability. Imaging revealed a 6.5 × 4.7 cm adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Despite optimal medical treatment, hemodynamic stability could not be achieved. Urgent transcatheter adrenal arterial embolization (TAAE) was performed as rescue therapy with sustained hemodynamic stabilization thereafter. After 1 month of alpha-blockade preparation, elective adrenalectomy was completed uneventfully. At the 1-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with normal cardiac function and no tumor recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: In this case, TAAE served as a minimally invasive bridging measure for refractory pheochromocytoma crisis. The staged strategy combining TAAE with delayed elective adrenalectomy was associated with a favorable outcome.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Extreme blood-pressure lability in a patient with TTS should prompt evaluation for occult pheochromocytoma. Urgent TAAE may serve as an effective bridge to delayed elective adrenalectomy for refractory pheochromocytoma crisis.

articles.title: Coronary Visual Intelligence System (CorVIS) Guided Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is usually displayed in 2-dimensional planes with few fixed 3-dimensional (3D) views, which may limit appreciation of the spatial relationship between plaques and vessel. We describe initial clinical experience with CorVIS, an artificial intelligence-based coronary visualization system, in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 cases-2 chronic total occlusions and 1 heavily calcified lesion-in which CorVIS provided freely rotatable 3D reconstructions with plaque characterization. In each case, the CorVIS corresponded to specific procedural decisions, including the chosen crossing approach and calcium-modification strategy. All 3 procedures were completed successfully.

DISCUSSION: These cases suggest that artificial intelligence-based 3D CCTA reconstruction may complement conventional imaging for preprocedural planning of complex PCI. The efficacy of CorVIS in facilitating complex PCI remains to be verified in further prospective studies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In this initial case series, CorVIS delivered freely rotatable 3D CCTA reconstructions and plaque characterization, informing key procedural decisions for complex PCI.

articles.title: First-in-Human Axillary Vein Implantation of a Leadless Pacemaker: Breaking the Access Barrier.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are conventionally implanted transfemorally, with transjugular and subclavian routes reported as alternatives. Axillary access has not previously been reported.

FIH SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman with chronic sacral wounds became temporary-pacing dependent following an inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. An LP was selected given infection risk. Because of a right femoral deep venous thrombosis, an abscess at the left femoral site, and restricted neck mobility limiting internal jugular access, she underwent left axillary vein implantation of an LP.

DISCUSSION: Axillary access served as a feasible alternative route. A septal position was achieved by rotating the delivery system counterclockwise, opposite the transfemoral direction, while a perpendicular sterile table supported the extracorporeal catheter length.

NOVELTY: This is the first reported axillary vein implantation of an LP.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Axillary venous access is a feasible bailout route for LP implantation when femoral and internal jugular access are unavailable.

articles.title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Calcium Modification for a Complex Calcified Nodule With Circumferential Calcium: From Debulking to Fracturing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study objective was to describe an optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided strategy for stepwise calcium modification in a large protruding calcified nodule with circumferential calcium.

KEY STEPS: Rotational atherectomy was used to establish device crossability and modify superficial calcium. Serial OCT was performed to assess residual calcified nodule protrusion, circumferential calcium, lumen gain, and calcium fracture. When crossability was restored but substantial mechanical constraint persisted, the strategy was escalated to intravascular lithotripsy, followed by cutting-balloon dilation. Final OCT was used to confirm stent expansion and apposition.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Restoration of device crossability does not necessarily indicate adequate lesion preparation, whereas excessive burr escalation may increase procedural risk. Serial OCT should be used to assess the response to each modification step and guide timely strategy escalation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: OCT assessment may guide precise calcium modification and prevent stent underexpansion in complex calcified lesions.

articles.title: Progressive Dilated Cardiomyopathy in a 24-Year-Old Man: A Rare Manifestation of Propionic Acidemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult onset propionic acidemia (PA) is exceedingly rare, particularly when manifesting as dilated cardiomyopathy.

CASE SUMMARY: A previously healthy 24-year-old man presented with cardiac dilatation and acute progressive heart failure. His condition was refractory to guideline-directed medical therapy, deteriorating to cardiogenic shock within 6 weeks. Plasma acylcarnitine profile revealed elevated propionylcarnitine and an increased propionylcarnitine-to-acetylcarnitine ratio. Urinary organic acid analysis showed elevated methylcitric acid. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous mutation in the PCCA gene. A diagnosis of PA presenting as metabolic cardiomyopathy was established. Cardiac function and hemodynamics improved with targeted metabolic treatment combined with guideline-directed medical therapy.

DISCUSSION: Adult onset, metabolic cardiomyopathy because of PA is prone to being overlooked or misdiagnosed as refractory idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, potentially leading to premature escalation to advanced heart failure therapies. Early etiologic recognition and targeted metabolic treatment are crucial in the management of such cases.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Metabolic and genetic screening is recommended for patients with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, particularly in younger individuals. Early diagnosis and targeted intervention may preclude or delay the progression to left ventricular assist device implantation or heart transplantation in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy secondary to PA.

articles.title: Perioperative B-Cell-Targeted Therapy for High-Risk Valve Surgery in Active Primary Sjögren's Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by B-cell dysregulation. Clinically significant valvular involvement is uncommon, and evidence guiding perioperative immunomodulation remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman with SjD and severe aortic stenosis required valve replacement. Preoperative evaluation demonstrated active SjD with elevated inflammatory markers and hypergammaglobulinemia. Following multidisciplinary discussion, telitacicept, corticosteroids, and hydroxychloroquine were initiated before surgery. After improvement in inflammatory activity, the patient underwent aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement. Histopathologic examination showed degenerative valvular changes with focal inflammatory cell infiltration. The postoperative course was uneventful, with normal prosthetic valve function at 1-year follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the challenges of managing severe valvular heart disease in patients with active primary SjD and a multidisciplinary perioperative strategy incorporating B-cell-targeted therapy. Although preoperative immunomodulation may have attenuated the histopathologic evidence of immune-mediated valvular involvement, the case offers insights when guidance is limited.

articles.title: Low-Frequency Whole-Body Vibration and Isometric Exercise in Cardiac Rehabilitation: Improved Capacity and Triglyceride-Glucose Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise intolerance may persist in patients with chronic coronary syndrome despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention. Evidence regarding low-frequency whole-body vibration training (LF-WBVT) remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 62-year-old woman underwent cardiac rehabilitation for reduced exercise capacity 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention. Baseline peak oxygen uptake was 14.3 mL/kg/min. She completed an 8-week program consisting of moderate-intensity continuous aerobic training, LF-WBVT (3-9 Hz), and isometric lower-extremity resistance exercise. Peak oxygen uptake increased to 22.2 mL/kg/min, and oxygen pulse increased from 8.7 to 9.6 mL/beat. No major adverse cardiovascular events occurred.

DISCUSSION: This combined strategy improved both cardiorespiratory fitness and metabolic health. The triglyceride-glucose index reduction is a novel finding, suggesting lower future cardiovascular risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: LF-WBVT with isometric exercise is safe in selected patients with chronic coronary syndrome. Triglyceride-glucose index may serve as a metabolic biomarker for rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Ablation in Dextrocardia With Interrupted Inferior Vena Cava and Azygos Continuation to Coronary Sinus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation ablation in dextrocardia with interrupted inferior vena cava presents formidable technical challenges, particularly when anomalous systemic venous return distorts interatrial septal relationships.

CASE SUMMARY: A 58-year-old man with drug-refractory paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, situs inversus totalis with dextrocardia, and inferior vena cava interruption with azygos continuation to the coronary sinus underwent catheter ablation. Lacking an inferior route, a superior approach through the left internal jugular vein was selected. Under intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) guidance, transseptal access was obtained using a dedicated wire-based system. Pulmonary vein isolation and roofline ablation were safely completed using radiofrequency energy.

DISCUSSION: Azygos continuation to the coronary sinus drastically distorts interatrial geometry. ICE-guided, wire-based transseptal access via a superior route is a safe, practical alternative when conventional inferior access is unavailable and needle-based puncture poses high risks.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In situs inversus, the left internal jugular vein offers an optimal trajectory for transseptal puncture via a superior approach. Using a dedicated transseptal guidewire instead of a rigid needle, strictly guided by ICE, reduces the risk of mechanical complications during atypical transseptal punctures in complex congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Vascular Plug Closure of Delayed Leaflet Perforation Post-TEER in Patient With Multiple Implantable Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is the main minimally invasive therapy for severe mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high surgical risk. Roughly 10% of patients develop recurrent MR within 1 year postoperatively. Postprocedural mitral anatomical distortion complicates reintervention, rendering recurrent MR management a common clinical challenge.

CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old man with multivalvular heart disease, chronic heart failure, multiple implantable devices and dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease presented with symptomatic severe recurrent MR secondary to delayed anterior mitral leaflet perforation after TEER. Under combined fluoroscopic and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, our multidisciplinary team performed transcatheter closure of the perforation using a vascular plug. MR was markedly alleviated, heart failure symptoms resolved, and the patient recovered uneventfully before discharge.

DISCUSSION: TEER-related leaflet perforation caused severe recurrent MR. Percutaneous plug closure successfully downgraded MR to trivial, confirming the feasibility of this approach for mitral leaflet perforation.

articles.title: Pregnancy-Related Right Atrial Appendage Tachycardia Requiring ECMO and Hybrid Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right atrial appendage atrial tachycardia (AT) during pregnancy is rare and can progress to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy and shock.

CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman at 36 weeks and 5 days of gestation presented with fatigue, dyspnea, and narrow-complex tachycardia at 190-210 beats/min. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 18%. After failed medical therapy, cardioversion, and esophageal pacing, she underwent emergency cesarean delivery and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Mapping localized the AT to the base of the right atrial appendage; endocardial radiofrequency (RF) and pulsed field ablation produced only transient sinus rhythm. Thoracoscopic bipolar RF ablation with surgical clamping restored durable sinus rhythm.

CONCLUSIONS: Appendage-origin AT in pregnancy can progress rapidly to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, and timely venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support improves the prognosis. RF and pulsed field ablation may be insufficient for deep or possibly epicardial substrates; surgical ablation should be considered when catheter ablation fails.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Renal Denervation and Perirenal Adipose Tissue Debulking for Refractory Hypertension in End-Stage Renal Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both renal sympathetic nerves and perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) drive hypertension. However, evidence regarding renal denervation (RDN) in end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains limited.

FIRST-IN-HUMAN SUMMARY: A 74-year-old man with diabetic chronic kidney disease stage 5 presented with refractory hypertension despite treatment with 4 antihypertensive agents and intravenous nitroprusside. He underwent bilateral laparoscopic-assisted RDN combined with PRAT debulking without complications. At 5-month follow-up, office and ambulatory blood pressures were substantially reduced, while renal function and medications remained stable.

DISCUSSION: Our case provides preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility of a combined laparoscopic RDN and PRAT debulking strategy in a patient with ESRD and refractory hypertension.

NOVELTY: To our knowledge, this is the first report of RDN combined with PRAT debulking using the laparoscopic system in ESRD.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This combined intervention offers a promising new therapeutic option for refractory hypertension in patients with advanced kidney disease.

articles.title: Late Progressive Multivalvular Regurgitation After Heart Transplantation With Preserved Graft Function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late clinical decline after heart transplantation is commonly attributed to rejection, cardiac allograft vasculopathy, or ventricular dysfunction. Progressive structural valvular disease is less frequently emphasized when graft systolic function is preserved.

CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman underwent orthotopic heart transplantation at age 13 for familial restrictive cardiomyopathy. Nearly 10 years later, she developed progressive exertional fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and dizziness despite preserved graft systolic function and no significant cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Serial imaging demonstrated severe mitral regurgitation, moderate to severe aortic regurgitation, and moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation. She underwent redo sternotomy with bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement and tricuspid repair, with preserved ventricular function and clinical recovery at early follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights progressive multivalvular disease as an important valve-level cause of late clinical decline after heart transplantation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider structural valvular disease in symptomatic long-term heart transplant recipients with preserved graft function.

articles.title: Argatroban Anticoagulation for Transcarotid TAVR Under Conscious Sedation in a Patient With Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe argatroban anticoagulation in a patient with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve replacement under conscious sedation.

KEY STEPS: Vitamin K antagonist therapy was discontinued and intravenous argatroban initiated, with anti-factor IIa monitoring. Procedural anticoagulation consisted of an argatroban bolus followed by continuous infusion guided by activated clotting time. An ultrasound-guided intermediate cervical plexus block with remifentanil sedation maintained consciousness for neurological assessment. Argatroban was resumed postoperatively before transition to vitamin K antagonist therapy.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Surgical carotid access under argatroban requires careful balancing of thrombotic and bleeding risks. Maintaining consciousness for neurological monitoring adds an anesthetic challenge, requiring adequate anesthesia for carotid exposure while avoiding excessive sedation; an intermediate cervical plexus block may cause dysphagia.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Integrating argatroban anticoagulation with locoregional anesthesia may address the competing requirements of surgical carotid access and continuous neurological monitoring in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

articles.title: Native Leaflet Interference After Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Ring: Snare-Assisted Valve-in-Valve-in-Ring Bailout.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Native mitral leaflet interference is a rare cause of acute intraprosthetic regurgitation after transcatheter mitral valve-in-ring replacement (TMViR).

CASE SUMMARY: An 83-year-old woman with previous surgical mitral annuloplasty underwent transseptal TMViR for severe regurgitation from anterior mitral leaflet flail. After implantation of a 32-mm Myval Octapro valve, severe intraprosthetic regurgitation developed. High atrial positioning and prosthesis tilting allowed the flail anterior leaflet to overhang the ventricular valve edge and impair prosthetic leaflet coaptation. Balloon postdilation failed and increased instability. A contralateral gooseneck snare enabled controlled recrossing and deeper valve-in-valve-in-ring implantation, with complete regurgitation resolution and no left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.

DISCUSSION: Native leaflet interference should be considered after TMViR when acute intraprosthetic regurgitation occurs.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Snare-assisted recrossing may provide selective bailout when marked tilt or instability prevents safe conventional recrossing.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Advanced Heart Failure and Ventricular Dysfunction: An Evolving Heart Team Strategy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction and mitral regurgitation are underrepresented in pivotal transcatheter edge-to-edge repair trials and are often ineligible for transplantation or LV assist devices, leaving limited options when guideline-directed medical therapy fails.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe 6 patients aged 38 to 82 years with LV ejection fraction 10% to 20% and severe (4+) to torrential (5+) mitral regurgitation, 4 patients presenting in or near cardiogenic shock requiring inotropic, vasopressor, or intra-aortic balloon pump support. All underwent transcatheter edge-to-edge repair as our multidisciplinary heart team strategy evolved.

DISCUSSION: With increasing experience, the heart team incorporated individualized pharmacologic or temporary mechanical support, preprocedural hemodynamic optimization, and anatomy-driven device selection. One patient initially referred for palliative care was subsequently reassessed and treated. This series illustrates how iterative multidisciplinary learning may expand transcatheter edge-to-edge repair candidacy in carefully selected, high-risk patients with advanced heart failure and profound ventricular dysfunction and limited therapeutic alternatives.

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Distal Aortopulmonary Window by Fetal Cardiac MRI.
articles.abstract:
IMAGE: Prenatal diagnosis of a distal aortopulmonary window by fetal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

CASE SUMMARY: A fetus referred for cardiac MRI because of suboptimal visualization of the great vessels on ultrasound. MRI demonstrated a distal aortopulmonary window with a characteristic heart-shaped appearance of the great vessels.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Fetal cardiac MRI may provide complementary anatomical information when echocardiographic visualization is suboptimal and may help characterize complex fetal outflow tract abnormalities.

articles.title: Occult Penetrating Trauma: A STEMI Mimic Hiding in Plain Sight.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report a case of acute pericarditis caused by an occult penetrating foreign body manifesting as an ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction mimic.

CASE SUMMARY: The patient initially presented with chest pain, increased cardiac troponin I, and ST-segment elevation. Following emergency intravenous thrombolysis and urgent coronary angiography, an alternative etiology was suspected. Subsequent verification of the medical history and imaging examinations ultimately identified the culprit: a nail. The patient received prompt treatment, and the pericardial foreign body was successfully extracted.

DISCUSSION: Acute pericarditis and acute myocardial infarction are common causes of acute chest pain. Diagnostic confusion and treatment delays may arise due to overlapping symptoms, elevation of cardiac biomarkers, ST-segment elevation, cognitive bias, and incomplete history taking.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: This case highlights the value of bedside echocardiography combined with chest radiography. In patients with suspected ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, it is crucial to differentiate acute coronary occlusion from other causes, especially foreign body-induced pericarditis.

articles.title: Severe Bioprosthetic Mitral Valve Dysfunction: Multimodality Imaging Identifies Structural Valve Degeneration and Guides Valve-in-Valve TMVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe bioprosthetic valve dysfunction presents a diagnostic challenge because distinguishing reversible leaflet thrombosis from structural valve degeneration may not be possible using echocardiography alone.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with end-stage renal disease, previous bioprosthetic mitral and aortic valve replacement, and prior valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Multimodality imaging demonstrated severe bioprosthetic mitral valve dysfunction with restricted leaflet motion, raising suspicion for leaflet thrombosis. Empiric intravenous unfractionated heparin was commenced while cardiac computed tomography was arranged. Computed tomography excluded hypoattenuated leaflet thickening and demonstrated severe leaflet calcification, confirming structural valve degeneration. After heart team discussion, transseptal valve-in-valve mitral replacement resulted in rapid hemodynamic and clinical recovery.

DISCUSSION: Serial multimodality imaging guided escalation from anticoagulation to definitive valve intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent prosthetic valve dysfunction after anticoagulation should prompt reassessment for structural valve degeneration. Transseptal valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement is an effective treatment for selected high-surgical-risk patients.

articles.title: Valve-in-Root TAVI vs Redo Surgery in a Young Adult With Failed Bioprosthesis.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC OF CONTROVERSY: Whether valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is preferred for structural valve degeneration of a Freestyle stentless aortic root in a young adult, and whether a Ross procedure at index surgery would have better served lifetime management.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with a failed stentless aortic root (implanted at age 20 for bicuspid aortic valve regurgitation) presented with severe bioprosthetic regurgitation and ventricular dilatation. Transfemoral ViV TAVI with a 29-mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 Ultra Resilia was performed successfully.

PRO VIEWPOINT: ViV TAVI avoids redo sternotomy, preserves future options, and aligns with patient preference to avoid anticoagulation.

CON VIEWPOINT: Redo SAVR with a mechanical valve-and a Ross procedure at the index operation-may offer superior lifetime sequencing, avoiding constraints of successive transcatheter implants.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Lifetime planning must begin at the index operation; both ViV TAVI and redo SAVR require heart team deliberation with explicit consideration of all future interventions.

articles.title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
ANATOMY: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease.

PATHOLOGY: We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina.

IMAGING CORRELATION: CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting.

TREATMENT: The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

articles.title: Iliofemoral Venous Stenosis Complicating Large-Bore Access for Balloon Mitral Valvotomy, Unmasking Incidental May-Thurner Anatomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-bore transvenous access for balloon mitral valvotomy (BMV) can be complicated by unrecognized iliofemoral venous disease, occasionally unmasking a congenital variant.

CASE SUMMARY: A 51-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and NYHA functional class III-IV dyspnea, on acenocoumarol for atrial fibrillation, was scheduled for BMV. After right femoral venous access and transseptal puncture, hardware >8-F could not be advanced; venography showed a tight, recoiling right external iliac vein stenosis, not responding to intravenous nitroglycerine, treated with angioplasty and stenting, and BMV was deferred. Computed tomography venogram 14 days later confirmed stent patency and incidentally revealed left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery, consistent with asymptomatic May-Thurner anatomy rather than syndrome. Acenocoumarol was continued after stenting, held 3 days before reattempt, and BMV was then completed successfully via the same route.

DISCUSSION: Comprehensive venous evaluation during difficult large-bore access can uncover clinically silent iliocaval anatomic variants and guide individualized, staged management.

articles.title: Missed Nursing Care in the Emergency Department: A Qualitative Interview Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Emergency departments are high-risk settings for missed nursing care, which jeopardizes patient safety and nurses' physical and mental well-being. However, specific manifestations, multifaceted factors, and consequences of missed nursing care in emergency departments require further investigation. This study aims to explore the manifestations, multifaceted factors, and consequences of missed nursing care in the emergency department to guide quality improvement.

METHODS: Semistructured interviews were conducted from December 2025 to February 2026, with participants recruited via purposive sampling. The sample comprised 5 emergency nursing leaders, 14 emergency clinical nurses, and 5 emergency patients. Interview data were sorted and coded in NVivo 12 and analyzed following Colaizzi's 7-step phenomenological approach to extract core themes.

RESULTS: The analysis identified 9 themes and 34 subthemes, systematically revealing the manifestations, causes, and impacts of missed nursing care in the emergency department. Missed nursing care content included: time-sensitive interruptions to critical care and life support; challenges and omissions in fundamental and therapeutic nursing care; and rigidity of assessment, observation, and documentation. Contributing factors were categorized into system and resource factors, team and individual nursing factors, and patient and clinical characteristics. Participants reported consequences affecting patients, nurses, and hospitals.

DISCUSSION: Missed nursing care in the emergency department represents a multifaceted phenomenon driven by multifactorial causes specific to the emergency context. Given its severe clinical consequences, clinical leaders must implement targeted interventions to address the root causes of missed nursing care, thereby safeguarding patient safety and improving nursing practice.

articles.title: Aldosterone and Residual Cardiorenal Risk: Pathophysiology and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Aldosterone, the terminal effector of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, regulates sodium retention, potassium excretion, and blood pressure. Beyond these classical effects, aldosterone-associated and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR)-mediated signaling is implicated in inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, albuminuria, and progressive cardiorenal injury, while its synthesis is regulated by factors beyond angiotensin II. This is particularly relevant in chronic kidney disease (CKD), where persistent renin-angiotensin system (RAS) activation, impaired potassium handling, reduced Klotho, altered aldosterone clearance, and incomplete suppression may sustain aldosterone exposure and MR activation despite conventional RAS blockade. These mechanisms may contribute to residual cardiorenal risk despite standard-of-care therapy. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) outcome trials establish MR signaling as a therapeutic target in defined CKD populations, but therapeutic benefit from MR blockade should not be interpreted as evidence of biochemical aldosterone excess in all treated patients. This review distinguishes aldosterone excess from MR activation and proposes a nephrology-focused clinical framework separating established MRA indications, evaluation for primary aldosteronism, and the unestablished cardiorenal outcome role of aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASIs). We discuss aldosterone-associated and MR-mediated kidney injury, the cardiorenal axis, albuminuria as a downstream marker of injury and treatment response, and current and emerging therapeutic strategies, including steroidal and non-steroidal MRAs, ASIs, and combinations with SGLT2 inhibitors. Whereas MRA therapy has established outcome benefits in defined CKD populations, cardiorenal outcome benefit from ASIs remains unestablished; EASi-KIDNEY was discontinued early after independent Data Monitoring Committee review, with detailed results pending.

articles.title: High sensitivity C-reactive protein and the risk of cardio-kidney outcomes in adults with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease: a nationwide study.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: The burden and prognostic significance of inflammation in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly characterized, with prior studies yielding conflicting estimates of the association between elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and cardio-kidney outcomes.

METHODS: Observational nationwide study of 23,008 adults with CKD stages 3-5 attending nephrology care and enrolled in the Swedish Renal Registry (2008-2023). Inflammation was assessed longitudinally via 94,500 repeated hsCRP registrations. Time-varying, cause-specific Cox models accounting for competing risks estimated associations with study outcomes, which included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure (HF) hospitalization, acute kidney injury (AKI), kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (KFRT) and all-cause mortality. Pre-defined stratifiers were atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) history and CKD stage.

RESULTS: Mean age was 71 years, 65% were male, and median estimated glomerular filtration rate was 25 mL/min/1.73 m². Median hsCRP was 4.0 (IQR 1.9-7.0) mg/L, and 75% of participants had hsCRP≥2. Over median 3.9 (IQR 2.0-6.7) years, hsCRP ≥2 mg/L was associated with higher rates of all outcomes: hazard ratio 1.20 (95% confidence interval 1.12-1.28) for MACE (n=5,480 events); 1.29 (1.22-1.37) for HF hospitalization (n=8,173); 1.28 (1.18-1.38) for AKI (n=3,943); 1.09 (1.02-1.15) for KFRT (n=6,177); and 1.43 (1.37-1.50) for mortality (n=12,645). In spline analyses, associations were steeper at lower hsCRP levels and flatter thereafter for all outcomes except KFRT, where the hsCRP-response relationship was relatively flat. Associations with MACE, HF, AKI and mortality were consistent regardless of ASCVD status and CKD stage. Associations with KFRT were inconsistent across CKD stages.

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort of adults with moderate to severe CKD receiving nephrology care, inflammation was common, and higher hsCRP levels were associated with adverse cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, as well as mortality. Although associations were less consistent for KFRT, these findings collectively support the utility of hsCRP monitoring in this population.

articles.title: Long forms of cardiac troponin T are independent of kidney function and improve the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: A recently developed cardiac troponin T (cTnT) assay measuring intact or mildly fragmented cTnT (long cTnT) has shown promise in improving the accuracy of myocardial infarction (MI) detection compared to the commercial high sensitivity cTnT (hs-cTnT) assay. However, data on patients with kidney dysfunction are limited. We compared the performance of long and hs-cTnT in MI diagnostics across the full spectrum of kidney function.

METHODS: In this prospective study, consecutive patients presenting at the emergency department with an elevated (≥14 ng/L) hs-cTnT were recruited. Long and hs-cTnT were measured on admission and kidney function was determined with plasma creatinine (Crea), cystatin C (CysC) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using contemporary equations with Crea, CysC or both (Crea-CysC) together. The association of eGFR with hs-cTnT and long cTnT concentrations and the discriminative ability of hs-cTnT and long cTnT for type 1 MI and any MI were evaluated.

RESULTS: In total, 1811 patients were included, 205 (11.3%) had a MI and 204 (11.3%) had a history of chronic kidney disease. The overall median (interquartile range) Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR were 71 (51-87), 52 (36-69) and 63 (44-79) ml/min/1.73m2. In patients without MI, long cTnT showed no consistent association with kidney function (β=0.0008, P = 0.050; β=0.0005, P = 0.222; β=0.0006, P = 0.182 for Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR, respectively), whereas hs-cTnT was inversely associated with kidney function (β=-0.0032, -0.0035 and - 0.0035; all P < 0.001). Long cTnT demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with hs-cTnT for the detection of MI (P < 0.001), with the advantage becoming progressively more pronounced with lower eGFR irrespective of equation used.

CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to hs-cTnT, long cTnT is unaffected by kidney function and outperforms hs-cTnT in the detection of MI, with the greatest diagnostic advantage observed in patients with lower eGFR.

articles.title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
articles.abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) (p < 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m2, p < 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT (p = 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

articles.title: Randomized Trial Comparing Minocycline-EDTA-Ethanol Lock to Standard-of-Care Antibiotic Lock for Management of Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) cause substantial morbidity and mortality. Management often requires removing the infected central venous catheter (CVC) and inserting a new one. Effective catheter-salvage strategies are needed.

METHODS: An international, multicenter, prospective, randomized superiority trial at 34 centers in the United States, Puerto Rico, and India enrolled patients aged ≥12 years with a long-term central venous catheter (CVC) in place for ≥5 days and CLABSI. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive systemic antibiotics plus minocycline-EDTA-ethanol lock therapy (MLT) or standard-of-care antibiotic lock therapy (SOC-ALT) for 7 to 14 days. The primary endpoint was median time to catheter failure, defined as clinical failure (death, infection-related catheter removal, worsening symptoms) or microbial failure (persistent/recurrent infection or new deep-seated infection attributable to the index CLABSI).

RESULTS: From 2018-2024, 241 patients were randomized; 228 received lock therapy. Catheter retention was higher with MLT than SOC-ALT (57% vs 38%; P = 0.0025). Median time to catheter failure was longer with MLT in both intention-to-treat (not estimable vs 33 days, HR 0.53, P = 0.0006) and modified intention-to-treat populations (not estimable vs 35 days, HR 0.50, P = 0.0005). Clinical catheter failure (13% vs 28%; P = 0.006) and microbiological failure (5% vs 15%; P = 0.012) were lower with MLT. Adverse events, serious adverse events, and mortality were similar between groups, with no drug-related serious adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: MLT was superior to SOC-ALT in salvaging long-term CVCs in CLABSI and was well tolerated, addressing an unmet need in CLABSI management.

articles.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Multicenter Real-World Evidence to Advance Precision Dosing: A Critical Perspective Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Precision dosing integrates patient-specific factors to optimize pharmacotherapy. However, current evidence often relies on limited single-center studies, restricting generalizability.

METHODS: A narrative review of literature on real-world evidence, pharmacogenetics, biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI), and privacy-preserving data strategies relevant to precision dosing was conducted.

RESULTS: Single-center data are insufficient for robust precision-dosing evidence because of small subgroups and local practice biases. Multicenter privacy-preserving systems enable richer, more generalizable datasets that link doses, exposures, genotypes, biomarkers, and outcomes. However, multicenter collaborations should remain aligned with the intended population and should not imply indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous data. Secure pooled environments, federated learning, and synthetic data play distinct method-dependent roles. AI supports exposure estimation, phenotype extraction, and modeling of complex relationships but requires rigorous validation against conventional methods. Causal inference requires epidemiological rigor beyond predictive performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Advancing precision dosing requires multicenter, purpose-specific, privacy-preserving, methodologically rigorous, and clinically validated data systems guided by clinical pharmacologists, with AI serving as a complementary tool rather than a default solution.

articles.title: The association between viral infections and aplastic anemia: a comprehensive scoping review.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in clinical laboratory sciences
articles.abstract: Aplastic anemia (AA) is a rare hematological disorder characterized by bone marrow failure and pancytopenia, with viral infections implicated as a significant acquired cause. This scoping review evaluates the pathophysiological mechanisms linking viral infections to AA and assesses current therapeutic strategies for managing virus-associated cases. Following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines, a scoping review was conducted from April to May 2024 using PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. Eligible studies included those reporting viral infections associated with AA, diagnostic approaches, or therapeutic interventions. Data were extracted on study design, type of virus, diagnostic methods, and treatment strategies. A total of 48 studies were included, identifying parvovirus B19, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis viruses, human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1, and SARS-CoV-2 as key pathogens.
