Rare cases of post-vaccination complications were also reported. Identified mechanisms include direct bone marrow suppression, immune-mediated destruction, and viral reactivation during immunosuppression. Antiviral therapies and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation constitute the primary treatments, and virological monitoring is essential to prevent reactivation. Viral infections play a significant role in AA etiology and progression. Tailored antiviral regimens and proactive virological monitoring are essential for optimizing outcomes. Future research should focus on longitudinal studies to clarify causal relationships and refine therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Dual-energy computed tomography pulmonary angiography for pulmonary embolism: a three-tier evidence framework to guide individualized low-iodine scanning.
articles.abstract: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is widely studied for pulmonary embolism (PE) evaluation, but heterogeneity in protocols, platforms, and study designs complicates its clinical positioning. This narrative review, with structured search elements adapted from the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, synthesized evidence from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (January 2016-June 2026); 28 studies were eligible (26 of 1,287 screened records and 2 identified through citation tracing). Evidence was organized into a three-tier framework (image quality, diagnostic performance, and clinical outcomes). Low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging at 40-50 keV improves vascular attenuation and enables iodine load reduction to approximately 6 g in selected protocols. Pooled meta-analytic evidence shows no consistent diagnostic advantage of DECT over single-energy CT. The right ventricular/left ventricular diameter ratio remains the most stable prognostic indicator; DECT perfusion metrics have not surpassed it for mortality prediction. Iodine-map hypoperfusion in distal arteries is suspicious for, but not morphologically confirmed as, subsegmental PE; such findings carry a risk of overdiagnosis and warrant caution before anticoagulation. A body mass index- and estimated glomerular filtration rate-stratified protocol table with Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 evidence-level annotations is provided, and knowledge gaps in photon-counting CT, artificial intelligence, and cross-platform standardization are identified.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Invasive Mold Infections in Children During First-Line Chemotherapy for Primary Acute Leukemia: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold infections (IMI) are life-threatening complications during treatment for pediatric acute leukemia. Population-based data on IMI incidence, timing, and outcomes during first-line therapy remain limited. We aimed to provide a nationwide epidemiological overview of IMI during first-line treatment of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and explore potential treatment-related risk factors.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study of all children (<18 years) initiating first-line chemotherapy for AML or ALL in Denmark during 2008-2022. IMIs were classified as proven or probable according to 2020 EORTC/MSGERC criteria by review of microbiology, imaging, pathology, and chart data. Follow-up covered first-line chemotherapy. Competing risk-adjusted cumulative incidence of IMI was estimated, risk factors were evaluated using Cox regression, and survival after IMI was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Among 621 patients, 43 (6.9%) developed IMI: 14/90 (15.6%) with AML and 29/531 (5.5%) with ALL. In adjusted Cox regression, AML was associated with higher IMI hazard than ALL (HR 5.6, 95% CI 2.6 to 12.1), whereas no other prespecified risk factors were independently associated with IMI. Incidence rates were 38.6 per 100 patient-years in AML and 2.7 in ALL. Nearly half of IMIs occurred beyond 90 days after initiation of first-line chemotherapy. Four patients experienced a second distinct IMI episode; Aspergillus species accounted for 37/47 (79%) episodes and non-Aspergillus molds for 10/47 (21%). IMI-associated death occurred in 10 patients (1.6% of the cohort), yielding a case fatality rate of 23% among IMI cases; IMI was present in 43% of all deaths.

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, IMI occurred more frequently than reported in many previous pediatric studies, particularly in AML. IMIs were observed throughout first-line therapy, despite antifungal prophylaxis, and were associated with substantial mortality, emphasizing the need for sustained clinical vigilance beyond induction.

articles.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Few studies that have reported long-term trajectories of a standardized nonoperative management in patients with massive irreparable rotator cuff tears (MIRCTs).

OBJECTIVE: The aims of this study were to describe the long-term clinical outcomes of nonoperative treatment and to analyze sociodemographic and comorbidity baseline factors associated with functional outcomes trajectories in older adults with atraumatic MIRCTs.

DESIGN: A prospective cohort study was performed.

SETTING: The setting was a single tertiary health care hospital.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged ≥60 years with atraumatic MIRCTs were recruited.

INTERVENTIONS: All patients were treated with Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, a 12-week physical therapist program, home exercises, and, when required, a corticosteroid injection.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The Constant-Murley (CM) questionnaire was used to assess shoulder function, the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire for upper limb function, and the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain intensity. Four evaluations were performed, at baseline, at 3 months, 1 year, and 4 years. Because outcomes were measured repeatedly in the same participants, linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts were used to account for within-subject correlation.

RESULTS: The majority of patients (76/92) showed clinically important improvements in 3 months that persisted until 4 years. Of the patients that did not improve at 1-year, 16 underwent surgery (17%). In patients treated nonoperatively, in CM, DASH, and VAS, the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) was reached between 95% to 97% of patients at 3 months, 89% to 97% at 1 year, and all patients at 4 years (100%). In the prespecified adjusted models, longer symptoms duration (β = -1.3; 95% CI = -1.7 to -0.8) and smoking (β = -8.8; 95% CI = -13.2 to -4.4) were associated with worse shoulder function. Diabetes mellitus was associated with higher pain intensity (β = 0.3; 95% CI = 0.1 to 0.5).

CONCLUSIONS: In the long term, the majority of older patients with atraumatic MIRCTs in this cohort responded well to nonoperative treatment. Moreover, some sociodemographic and comorbidity baseline factors were associated with functional recovery trajectories in these patients. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings.

RELEVANCE: Findings showed that functional recovery trajectories are significantly influenced not only by biomechanical or related to rotator cuff tear factors but by modifiable sociodemographic and comorbidity factors which should be addressed in these patients.

articles.title: Exercise therapy for temporomandibular disorders.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To assess the effects of exercise therapy on pain intensity, jaw function/disability, and health-related quality of life in adults with temporomandibular disorders, compared with no treatment, placebo, or other non-exercise conservative interventions. Secondary objectives To assess the effects of exercise therapy on mandibular mobility and adverse events. Additionally, to explore potential heterogeneity in treatment effects by investigating whether outcomes differ according to temporomandibular disorder subtype (e.g. myogenous, arthrogenous, or mixed).

articles.title: Statins for adults with a first episode of venous thromboembolic disease.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of statins in the secondary prevention of Recurrent Venous ThromboEmbolic disease (RVTE): Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT), Pulmonary ThromboEmbolism (PTE) and Post-Thrombotic Syndrome (PTS) in patients with a first episode of deep vein thrombosis Secondary objective To evaluate the benefits and harms of statins in the secondary prevention of RVTE, DVT, PTE and PTS in patients with or without cancer, in different sexes and in the general population aged over 70 years.

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Infusion Rate on Vancomycin Dose Adjustment in Pediatric Central Diabetes Insipidus: Grand Round/A Case Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vancomycin (VCM)-associated acute kidney injury is a clinically important adverse event. Appropriate dose adjustment requires knowledge of factors influencing VCM clearance; however, these factors remain poorly characterized in pediatric patients. We report a pediatric case in which elevated blood VCM concentrations seemed to be associated with an increased arginine vasopressin (AVP) infusion rate.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 9-month-old female infant (6.9 kg, 64 cm) underwent craniotomy for hematoma removal after a traumatic fall. Postoperatively, a surgical site infection was suspected, and VCM was initiated at 90 mg every 6 hours. Initial therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) showed a trough concentration (Ctrough) of 6.3 mcg/mL, below therapeutic range for pediatric patients. The VCM dose was increased to 140 mg every 6 hours. Repeat TDM showed a Ctrough of 19.0 mcg/mL. Before VCM initiation, the patient was administered continuous AVP infusion for central diabetes insipidus (CDI) associated with trauma. During VCM therapy, the AVP infusion rate was increased from 0.6 to 1.0 mL/h because of increased urine output, but urine output remained unchanged. After the elevated Ctrough, the VCM dose was reduced to 90 mg every 6 hours, whereas the AVP infusion rate was increased further to 3.2 mL/h. TDM performed before the fourth dose after dose reduction showed a Ctrough of 10.5 mcg/mL, approximately twice the initial concentration despite the same VCM dosage.

CONCLUSIONS: Increased AVP infusion may have reduced the glomerular filtration rate and elevated the blood VCM concentration, independent of urine output. To our knowledge, this is the first pediatric case reporting elevated blood VCM concentrations associated with an increased AVP infusion rate despite persistent urine output in a patient with CDI. Clinicians should be aware that changes in AVP infusion rates may influence VCM exposure, and closer TDM may be warranted when AVP doses are adjusted.

articles.title: Correction to "A Mechanically Adaptive Titanium Scaffold with a Lattice-Modulated Piezocatalytic Coating for Infection Treatment and Bone Regeneration".
A Quality Improvement Initiative to Achieve Provincial Implementation of a Web-Based Family Satisfaction in ICU (FS-ICU) Survey to Inform Patient-Centered Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To review the web-based Family Satisfaction in ICU (FS-ICU) survey across all adult level 3 Ontario ICUs to capture patient and family experiences with critical care, and to evaluate feasibility, participation, and satisfaction scores.

DESIGN: A province-wide, multisite quality improvement study using an electronic, key-based FS-ICU survey with prospectively collected anonymous data linked to encounters through a centralized database.

SETTING: All 83 adult level 3 ICUs (52 community, 31 academic) in ON, Canada, from July 1, 2019, to May 31, 2024.

PATIENTS: The population comprised adult ICU patients, family members, or substitute decision-makers, with one survey per ICU encounter regardless of length of stay or number of family members.

INTERVENTIONS: ICUs implemented a web-based FS-ICU using a unique seven-digit key in three formats (Staff-Provided, Quick Response-Driven, Website-Code), supported by training, resources, and tablets, with no clinical care interventions beyond routine practice.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Feasibility metrics included onboarding (keys generated per ICU admission), opening, participation, and completion rates, calculated for different centers using provincial data. Over the study period, 24,679 unique keys were generated for 353,400 ICU admissions (onboarding rate, 7.0%), 13,596 keys were opened (opening rate, 55.1%), and 7,542 surveys met the greater than or equal to 70% completion threshold (completion rate, 57.6% among opened surveys; reflection rate, 2.1% of ICU encounters). Survey initiation was highest with the Staff-Provided format (88.4% of keys initiated), and overall satisfaction was high, with mean FS with Care, 87.8; FS with Decision-Making, 84.4; and FS-TOTAL 86.5 on a 0-100 scale, with nursing care rated highest and adequacy of time for questions rated lowest.

CONCLUSIONS: A provincial, web-based FS-ICU was implemented across all adult level 3 Ontario ICUs, producing a large dataset with high satisfaction scores. A small proportion completed the survey, highlighting feasibility and workflow barriers. Future efforts should improve activation and completion rates and integrate FS-ICU data into routine quality improvement to enhance patient- and family-centered care.

articles.title: Fifty Years of Non-Adrenergic Inotropes in Heart Failure.
Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/INTRODUCTION: The effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all-cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo-Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort. Lifestyle factors were assessed by questionnaire. Dietary intake was evaluated using a brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire, from which Total, Plant, and Animal low-carbohydrate diet scores were calculated. The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, or all-cause mortality. Associations were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Mean age was 51.4 ± 15.1 years, mean HbA1c was 7.9 ± 1.1%, and carbohydrate accounted for 49.3% of energy intake. During follow-up, 35 participants experienced the primary composite outcome. In multivariable Cox models, the Total LCDS (HR, 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; P = 0.012), Plant LCDS (HR, 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.94; P = 0.003), and Animal LCDS (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.87-0.996; P = 0.037) were inversely associated with the outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan, low-carbohydrate dietary patterns, particularly the Plant low-carbohydrate diet score, were inversely associated with macrovascular events or all-cause mortality.

articles.title: Targeting Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell Senescence for Cardiovascular Pharmacology: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a central role in maintaining vascular tone, structural integrity, and adaptive remodeling. With aging and chronic cardiometabolic stress, however, VSMCs undergo senescence driven by telomere attrition, oxidative stress, persistent DNA-damage signaling, and dysregulation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb pathways. This transition is accompanied by acquisition of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which promotes inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, calcification and vascular stiffening. Together, these accelerate atherosclerosis, hypertension, aneurysm formation, and related vasculopathies. Growing evidence identifies VSMC senescence as a promising therapeutic entry point for cardiovascular drug discovery. Emerging strategies include senolytics, senomorphics, metabolic modulators, and molecular reprogramming approaches designed to either eliminate senescent cells or attenuate their pathogenic secretome and downstream signaling networks. In this review, the molecular basis of VSMC senescence, its contribution to major vascular disorders, and the therapeutic landscape targeting senescence-associated pathways are discussed, with emphasis on translational opportunities and current barriers to clinical application. A clearer understanding of VSMC senescence may inform the development of mechanism-based interventions to limit vascular dysfunction and age-related cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Microsporidial keratoconjunctivitis in Central India: Epidemiological trends and outcomes over 10 years.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the epidemiological characteristics, clinical features, and treatment outcomes of microsporidial keratoconjunctivitis (MKC) over a 10-year period at a tertiary eye care center in central India.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed patients diagnosed with MKC between 2015 and 2024. Data from 2005 to 2014 were additionally used to determine hospital-based incidence and prevalence trends. Diagnosis was based on the detection of microsporidial spores in corneal scrapings or characteristic slit-lamp findings. Trends were compared between the two periods (2015-2019 and 2020-2024).

RESULTS: Of 284,211 outpatients seen between 2005 and 2024, 520 (0.2%) were diagnosed with MKC; 393 patients (402 eyes) from 2015 to 2024 were included in the study. The median age was 33 years, with male predominance (64.4%). Most patients were from urban areas (67.9%) and engaged in indoor or sedentary work (81.7%). A significant increase in rural representation and outdoor/manual occupations was observed from 2020 to 2024 ( P = 0.019 and P = 0.018, respectively). Seasonal clustering persisted throughout the rainy season. Minor ocular trauma was reported in 40.7% of cases. The incidence of concurrent diabetes mellitus increased over time. Primary epithelial debridement was performed in 88.1% of patients and was associated with faster epithelial resolution ( P < 0.001). No treatment failures were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: MKC is a seasonally patterned infection with evolving epidemiological characteristics. Increased awareness has led to more diagnoses. Increasing rural representation and associated diabetes require further studies. Although typically self-limiting, epithelial debridement may shorten the resolution time and needs to be explored further as a treatment option.

articles.title: Neurological Manifestations in People Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (PLHIV) in India: A Scoping Review and the Need for a National HIV-Neurology Special Interest Group.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Despite a low national prevalence of 0.20%, India's absolute burden of 2.544 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) presents clinicians with varied neurological complications. While combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) has extended survival, the neuro-HIV profile in India, characterized by the predominance of HIV-1 clade C, remains distinct from that reported in Western cohorts. This scoping review aimed to identify patterns of neurological manifestations in India across the pre-ART, ART, and "treat-all" eras and to support the establishment of a National HIV Neurology Special Interest Group.

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a systematic search was conducted for studies published between 1991 and 2025. Eligible studies included Indian adults living with HIV aged ≥18 years with definitive neurological syndromic diagnoses.

RESULTS: A total of 148 studies involving 3,433 patients were included. The "treat-all" era (post-2017) had the highest reporting volume from India. The central nervous system involvement predominated (94.7%), with opportunistic infections identified as the most common etiology (74.83%). Meningitis was the most-frequent neurological syndrome (1,187 cases; 54.5%), and Cryptococcus (439 cases; 12.78%) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis (374 cases; 10.89%) were the most common pathogens. Diagnoses were commonly established using a combination of clinical examination, neuroimaging, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis (2,799 cases; 81.5%). ART data were unavailable for 91.8% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: The neurology-HIV scenario in India is characterized by a high burden of acute opportunistic infections. The significant dependence on empirical polypharmacy and the identified gaps in ART-related data reveal a poorly integrated care model.

articles.title: Chronic infectious keratitis: A review of etiopathogenesis, clinical presentation and management challenges.
articles.abstract: Chronic infectious keratitis represents a distinct clinical entity characterized by indolent progression, diagnostic difficulty, and prolonged therapeutic courses. Unlike acute bacterial keratitis, chronic infections often present with subtle inflammatory signs, recurrent episodes, or poor response to empirical antimicrobial therapy. Among the most important causes are herpetic keratitis, acanthamoeba keratitis, Microsporidial stromal keratitis, and atypical (non-tuberculous) mycobacterial keratitis. Herpes simplex virus keratitis may manifest as recurrent epithelial disease or immune-mediated stromal inflammation resulting from viral latency and reactivation, frequently leading to corneal scarring and neurotrophic complications. Acanthamoeba keratitis, commonly associated with contact lens (CL) wear or water exposure, is characterized by severe pain disproportionate to clinical findings and the presence of cyst forms that confer significant treatment resistance. Microsporidial keratitis may present as either a self-limiting epithelial keratitis or a chronic stromal infection requiring surgical intervention, often masquerading as viral or fungal keratitis. Atypical mycobacterial keratitis typically follows corneal surgery or trauma and demonstrates a slow course with branching stromal infiltrates and minimal inflammation, frequently leading to delayed diagnosis. Other chronic infections such as Moraxella, Nocardia, Infectious Crystalline Keratopathy, Candida keratitis, and local adnexal factors causing chronic and recurrent bacterial infections have also been elaborated upon. These chronic pathogens share common challenges, including biofilm formation, intracellular persistence, cystic transformation, and steroid-modified presentations. Accurate diagnosis requires a multimodal approach incorporating smear, culture, polymerase chain reaction, and in vivo confocal microscopy. Management is organism-specific and often prolonged, sometimes necessitating therapeutic keratoplasty. Early recognition of chronic infectious keratitis is essential to prevent irreversible stromal damage and vision loss. This review is based on a literature search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and Cochrane databases using keywords such as 'infectious keratitis', 'herpes simplex viral keratitis', 'acanthamoeba keratitis', 'microsporidial keratitis', 'atypical mycobacterial keratitis', 'moraxella keratitis', 'infectious crystalline keratopathy', 'candida keratitis' and 'bacterial infections due to adnexal problems'.

articles.title: Evaluation of Macro- and Microstructural White Matter Changes in Hot Water Epilepsy.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Hot water epilepsy (HWE) is a form of reflex epilepsy and usually lacks definitive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features. Although white matter abnormalities have been extensively investigated in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy or generalized epilepsies, very few studies have examined quantitative changes in reflex epilepsy. This study aims to explore the white matter changes in HWE. The objective is to investigate the white matter micro- and macrostructural changes in patients with HWE using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) indices and three-dimensional structural-imaging-derived subcortical white matter volumes.

METHODS: Eighty-eight subjects with HWE and 50 age- and sex-matched controls underwent high-resolution volumetric MRI and DTI. DTI and volumetric data were processed using tract-based spatial statistics and FreeSurfer, respectively. Between-group differences in DTI metrics and regional subcortical white matter volumes were assessed. Correlations between DTI metrics, white matter volumes, and epilepsy-specific clinical variables were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Subjects with HWE showed significant alterations in DTI metrics indicative of impaired white matter integrity, including decreased fractional anisotropy and increased mean diffusivity, axial diffusivity, and radial diffusivity. These changes were evident both globally (whole-brain) and within specific supratentorial and infratentorial white matter tracts. Subcortical white matter volume loss was predominant in the thalamo-limbic, somatosensory, posterior cingulate, cuneus, and frontal regions. Positive correlations were observed between alterations in global fractional anisotropy and changes in macrostructural (subcortical) white matter volumes.

CONCLUSION: Subjects with HWE exhibited global and region-specific white matter alterations at both micro- and macrostructural levels. Somatosensory subcortical involvement may be associated with the stimulus sensitivity characteristic of this disorder. Involvement of temporal-limbic and default mode network regions is consistent with the clinical semiology, while brainstem changes concur with the reflex nature of the disease.

articles.title: Integrating Plain 2D Ultrasound and Clinical Data for Identification of At-Risk MASH: A Multicenter Proof of Concept Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying people with at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a major challenge. We aimed to use deep learning to develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to facilitate the detection of at-risk MASH.

METHODS: A multi-center cohort study was conducted across five tertiary hospitals in Japan and China. Clinical data and conventional ultrasound images were retrospectively collected. Organ segmentation using YOLO version 11 with quality control was performed, followed by creation of an EfficientNet-B6 CNN regression model, with image-level predictions averaged per patient, to estimate FAST and AGILE 3+ risk categories. Model performance was assessed using agreement across clinically relevant rule-out and rule-in thresholds, R2, root mean squared error (RMSE), and area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC).

RESULTS: The final dataset comprised 416 patients for training (7643 images), 139 for internal validation (2463 images), and 154 for external testing (3539 images). The CNN model demonstrated good agreement with FAST (R2 = 0.684; RMSE = 0.131; category agreement = 0.71) and moderate agreement with AGILE 3+ (R2 = 0.445; RMSE = 0.1964; category agreement = 0.63). For FAST, AUROC was 0.974 (95% CI 0.947-0.993) for 0.35 and 0.932 (95% CI 0.884-0.969) for the 0.67 cut-off. For AGILE 3+, AUROC was 0.908 (95% CI 0.854-0.950) for 0.451 and 0.902 (95% CI 0.839-0.953) for the 0.679 cut-off.

CONCLUSION: The CNN model applied to clinical ultrasound images can approximate the accuracy of VCTE-based composite risk scores for detecting at-risk MASH. This may support the detection of at-risk MASH in settings with limited access to transient elastography.

articles.title: The effects of novel oral preclinical PolC inhibitor antibiotic candidates on the gut microbiome in a murine thigh infection model.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Antibiotics can negatively affect gut microbiome composition and function. However, preclinical evaluations of antibiotic effects on the microbiome are rarely undertaken. The purpose of this study was to characterize pharmacokinetics and metagenomic profiles of PolC inhibitor compounds compared to linezolid in a neutropenic murine thigh infection model. Neutropenic mice thighs were inoculated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and dosed orally starting 1 h later with ACX-728, ACX-801, ACX-978, or linezolid. Untreated control mice were euthanized at 1 h for baseline data, and a second untreated group were euthanized at 24 h after the start of dosing, when all remaining mice were euthanized. At euthanasia, thigh muscles were excised for MRSA quantification, and fecal pellets, colon tissue, and plasma samples were collected for drug concentration and microbiome analyses. All PolC inhibitors were detectable in plasma and feces at 25 h. Compared with linezolid, PolC inhibitors maintained greater gut microbial richness and diversity in this acute murine infection model. PolC-treated samples preserved overall community structure and Bacteroidota dominance, whereas linezolid induced marked disruption, with secondary expansion of Pseudomonadota, primarily Escherichia coli. Microbial pathway analysis showed preservation of community-level metabolic function for PolC inhibitors but marked disruption by linezolid. Compared to controls, linezolid produced a 4.4 log reduction in MRSA colony-forming unit per gram, while the PolC inhibitors produced a mean log reduction of 0.4-2.5 per group. In these exploratory studies, PolC inhibitor compounds preserved anaerobic community structure and fermentative capacity, whereas linezolid induced depletion of healthy commensals and expansion of aerotolerant taxa. These findings highlight the importance of microbiome-informed antibiotic evaluation in preclinical studies. Larger preclinical and clinical studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

IMPORTANCE: This study evaluated the class effect of PolC inhibitors on the microbiome as part of the preclinical development plan for systemic PolC inhibitors. Similar to the non-absorbable antibiotic, ibezapolstat, a narrow effect on the microbiome was observed with these novel compounds.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of TB-LAMP assay on tongue swabs for pulmonary tuberculosis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of infectious disease mortality worldwide. However, underdiagnosis and delayed diagnosis continue to facilitate disease transmission. Tongue swab sampling has emerged as a promising non-invasive alternative for the diagnosis of pulmonary TB. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Eiken TB-LAMP assay when utilizing tongue swab specimens and refined the processing protocols following tongue swab collection. In this prospective study, consecutive outpatients with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis who were able to provide sputum specimens were enrolled. Tongue swab specimens were tested using the WHO-endorsed Eiken TB-LAMP platform (EIKEN CHEMICAL CO., LTD., Tokyo, Japan). Sputum samples were analyzed by Xpert MTB/RIF and culture tests. The microbiological reference standard (MRS) was defined as positivity by either sputum culture or Xpert MTB/RIF. Diagnostic performance was compared to both MRS and Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Among the 243 enrolled participants, 136 (56.0%) were MRS-positive, and 107 (44.0%) were MRS-negative. The tongue swab Eiken TB-LAMP assay achieved a sensitivity of 80.2% (95% CI: 72.5%-86.1%) and a specificity of 94.6% (95% CI: 88.8%-97.5%) compared to sputum Xpert MTB/RIF, and 80.1% sensitivity (95% CI: 72.7%-86.0%) and 98.1% specificity (95% CI: 93.4%-99.7%) compared to the MRS. Sensitivity varied by bacterial load, ranging from 100% (95% CI: 77.2%-100.0%) in high-load cases to 62.5% (95% CI: 45.3%-77.1%) in very-low-load cases. The Eiken TB-LAMP assay using tongue swabs offers a rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic alternative for TB diagnosis with high specificity and favorable sensitivity. It could significantly reduce the current diagnostic gap, facilitating earlier intervention and helping to curb the ongoing transmission of tuberculosis in high-burden regions.

IMPORTANCE: Effective control of the disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis is often hindered by the challenges of collecting sputum samples and the high costs associated with specialized laboratory equipment. This study examines a new diagnostic approach using tongue swabs combined with loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP). Unlike traditional methods that can be difficult for patients to perform and risky for healthcare workers to manage, tongue swabs are non-invasive, safe, and easy to collect. Because LAMP amplifies DNA under isothermal conditions without requiring thermal cycling, it is more affordable and requires minimal infrastructure, making it particularly suitable for clinics in remote or resource-limited areas. By demonstrating that this approach is effective, the research provides a foundation for faster and more accessible diagnosis. This shift could significantly improve patient care and help bridge the global gap in detecting this infectious disease.

articles.title: Translating Stroke Microenvironment Cues Into Materials Design: Intelligent Nanomaterials for Ischemic Stroke Therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS), caused by cerebral blood vessel occlusion, leads to ischemia, hypoxia, and irreversible brain tissue damage. Current treatments primarily rely on thrombolytic agents like alteplase, urokinase, and streptokinase for rapid reperfusion. However, these therapies are limited by narrow therapeutic windows, rapid clearance, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, off-target effects, and the complex ischemic microenvironment. These have led to increased interest in nanomaterial-based platforms to improve the precision and efficacy of IS treatment. The IS microenvironment, characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, ionic imbalance, acidosis, and BBB disruption, provides valuable cues for designing responsive nanomaterials. Nanomaterials engineered to respond to reactive oxygen species, pH, enzymes, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields can enable targeted drug delivery, controlled release, and multi-modal interventions, enhancing therapeutic precision. This review discusses the IS microenvironment, limitations of traditional therapies, recent advances in intelligent nanomaterials for IS treatment, and the major barriers that currently limit clinical translation.

articles.title: An Incretin-Dependent Modulation of Periprandial Neutrophilia.
articles.abstract: We determine how innate immunity adapts to transitions between fasting and feeding. Feeding rapidly induced periprandial neutrophilia. HFD accelerated this reponse. We therefore sought to examine whether periprandial states regulate neutrophil dynamics. We identified that the glucagon-like peptide 1 and insulin axis modulates the neutrophil surge, which is critical during endotoxin challenges. The periprandial state prepares the host for endotoxemia. We bridge nutrient intake and incretin-sensitive immunity to inflammatory tone, redefining postprandial inflammation, insulin resistance, and cardiometabolic risk in diabetes.

articles.title: White Matter Functional Disconnection Predicts Long-Term Disability and Early Mortality in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) has the highest short-term mortality among stroke subtypes, and progress in treatment has been hindered by the limited accuracy of current prognostic tools. We investigated whether white matter functional disconnection severity, estimated using a normative lesion network mapping framework integrating direct electrical stimulation and resting-state functional MRI data from previously published independent Data sets, improves prediction of 6-month functional outcome measured with the modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

METHODS: We analyzed 97 patients with spontaneous ICH. Ordinal logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between domain-specific disconnection severity and 6-month mRS, and to compare traditional functional outcome in patients with primary intracerebral hemorrhage and ICH scores with connectivity-enriched models incorporating disconnection measures.

RESULTS: White matter functional disconnectivity was significantly associated with 6-month functional outcome (mRS; P < .001; Nagelkerke's R2 = 0.507). Integrating disconnection severity into the functional outcome in patients with primary intracerebral hemorrhage and ICH scores improved predictive performance in both cases (Nagelkerke's R2 = 0.615 vs 0.389 and 0.651 vs 0.434, respectively), with the connectivity-enriched ICH score achieving the strongest overall fit across all models tested. Exploratory analyses showed associations between domain-specific disconnection severity, residual functional deficits, and early mortality.

CONCLUSION: Assessment of white matter functional disconnection severity seems to be a promising approach for predicting long-term disability after ICH, although prospective validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation. The findings suggest that different brain networks exhibit variable vulnerability to injury and differential potential for functional recovery.

articles.title: Acetate modulates host physiology and bacterial energetics to improve antibiotic efficacy during obesity-associated infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Antibiotic efficacy is conventionally attributed to the susceptibility of the infecting pathogen. However, obese patients experience disproportionately poor infection outcomes despite receiving antibiotics to which pathogens remain genetically susceptible. These observations suggest that host-associated factors can influence treatment outcomes independently of the bacterial genotype, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using a mechanistic comparison of diet-induced obese and healthy mice infected with Acinetobacter baumannii, we demonstrate that the effect of antibiotics is not solely a property of the pathogen but can be governed by a gut microbiota-derived metabolite acting on both host immunity and bacterial physiology. We identify obesity-associated acetate depletion as a key driver of antibiotic treatment failure, linking gut microbial metabolism to antibiotic activity during infection. We observed that this depletion impaired innate immune activation, reducing cytokine responses and neutrophil-mediated bacterial clearance. Under these conditions, A. baumannii displayed enhanced tolerance to bactericidal antibiotics, particularly tobramycin. Given these findings, we investigated whether acetate could be leveraged therapeutically to restore antibiotic efficacy. We observed that oral acetate supplementation remodeled the dysbiotic microbiome, whereas systemic acetate restored innate immune competence and neutrophil-mediated bacterial clearance. Most importantly, acetate reversed antibiotic tolerance and restored aminoglycoside killing by directly sensitizing host-induced tolerant bacterial populations. Mechanistically, acetate directly reprogrammed bacterial physiology to enhance aminoglycoside-mediated killing. Combined acetate-tobramycin treatment resulted in eradication of tolerant populations and markedly improved bacterial clearance in vivo. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between host metabolic state and antibiotic efficacy and identify acetate as a therapeutic intervention for obesity-associated gram-negative infections.

IMPORTANCE: Antibiotic treatment failure in obese patients remains poorly understood and therapeutically unaddressed. This study reveals that host metabolic state can control antibiotic response through a gut microbiota-derived metabolite that acts on both host defense and bacterial physiology. We identify obesity-driven depletion of microbiota-derived acetate as a previously unrecognized determinant of antibiotic failure, operating independently of bacterial resistance. By simultaneously restoring gut microbial balance, rescuing impaired innate immunity, and directly sensitizing pathogens to aminoglycoside killing through bacterial membrane alteration, acetate supplementation addresses the host-pathogen-microbiome axis through a single intervention. Given its established clinical safety, acetate represents a compelling combination therapy alongside aminoglycosides in obesity-associated gram-negative infections in a population for which host-directed treatment strategies are currently limited.

articles.title: The Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula combined with allicin alleviates Cryptosporidium parvum infection in immunosuppressed mice and is associated with restoration of NLRP6, IL-18, IFN-γ, and intestinal microbiota.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium parvum is a highly pathogenic zoonotic parasite with limited therapies. Current study explored the anti-C. parvum effect of Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula (QHF) and allicin in vitro in immunosuppressed mice. In vitro, QHF and allicin inhibited over 90% of C. parvum. In vivo, the 8-day treatment reduced fecal oocyst shedding to 12.88% of the model group. Infection disrupted intestinal homeostasis, reduced tight-junction protein expression, and downregulated NLRP6, while inducing systemic inflammation and elevating IL-18/IFN-γ levels, which were further increased by treatment. Treated mice also showed increased abundance of Archangium and Corallococcus and decreased abundance of Clostridioides and Butyricimonas. Predicted microbial functional pathways revealed enrichment of glycolysis-related genes (L-lactate dehydrogenase [LDH], glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase [GAPDH]) in infected mice, with treatment-associated shifts in amino acid synthesis pathways. Molecular docking suggested potential binding of benzoylpaeoniflorin, baicalin, and wogonoside to C. parvum LDH, ATP/ADP translocase, and gp40/15. Together, these findings indicate that QHF combined with allicin alleviates C. parvum infection in immunosuppressed mice and is associated with restoration of intestinal barrier markers, immune responses, and gut microbiota composition, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach for cryptosporidiosis.IMPORTANCECurrent study demonstrates that Qing Chang Hua Shi Formula (QHF) combined with allicin effectively inhibits Cryptosporidium parvum proliferation and concurrently mitigates intestinal damage and dysbiosis induced by C. parvum infection. QHF treatment was associated with upregulation of NLRP6, improved gut microbiota profiles, and elevated IFN-γ levels. These changes correlated with reduced parasite burden and alleviated intestinal injury, suggesting a potential immunomodulatory role that warrants further mechanistic investigation. Metagenomics disclosed that QHF and allicin were associated with changes in predicted microbial functional pathways, including those involved in glycolysis and amino acid metabolism, and with enrichment of certain bacterial taxa, such as Corallococcus and Archangium. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that benzoylpaeoniflorin and baicalin may bind stably to C. parvum L-lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ATP/ADP translocase, raising the hypothesis that they could interfere with parasite energy metabolism. However, enzymatic validation is required to confirm this possibility. These findings suggest a potential therapeutic approach for cryptosporidiosis and highlight alterations associated with C. parvum infection.

articles.title: Whole-genome sequencing and antibiotic resistance analysis of a clinical carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter chuandaensis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize a rare clinical isolate, Enterobacter chuandaensis, carrying the carbapenem resistance gene blaNDM-1. The antimicrobial susceptibility analysis revealed that E. chuandaensis EC001 was resistant to the majority of commonly used antimicrobial agents, except for amikacin, chloramphenicol, and minocycline. The results of the modified carbapenem inactivation method and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method confirmed that E. chuandaensis EC001 produces metallo-β-lactamase. E. chuandaensis EC001 was typed as sequence type 2493 and presented an extensive drug-resistant profile. Whole-genome sequencing analysis demonstrated that the strain harbors two plasmids (p1_EC001 and p2_EC001), among which blaNDM-1 is located on the conjugative plasmid p1_EC001 of IncFIB/IncFII-type. Plasmid p1_EC001 could be transferred into Escherichia coli, indicating its interbacterial horizontal transmission potential. The majority of plasmid-mediated resistance genes reside within or adjacent to various mobile genetic elements in p1_EC001. In addition, an IS3000 element (3,018 bp) was detected upstream of blaNDM-1, while the bleomycin resistance-related gene bleMBL was located downstream of blaNDM-1, followed by trpF, dsbD, cutA, groS, groL, and ISKpn19. Moreover, one class 1 integron harboring the genetic array intI1-dfrA12-aadA2-qacEdeltal-sul1 was identified on p1_EC001. The plasmid p2_EC001 was characterized as a mobilizable plasmid, and two key genes, mbeA and mbeC, were detected, which encode the plasmid mobilization relaxase MbeA and the accessory protein MbeC, respectively. In summary, this study demonstrated the antimicrobial susceptibility, plasmid features, and potential transmission mechanisms of E. chuandaensis EC001, which serve as evidence for controlling and prevention of clinical E. chuandaensis.IMPORTANCECurrent research on carbapenem resistance in E. chuandaensis remains relatively limited. This study performed detailed genome characterization of the two plasmids (p1_EC001 and p2_EC001) carried by E. chuandaensis EC001 and analyzed their resistance gene profiles, plasmid features, and potential transmission mechanisms. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for the formulation of hospital infection control strategies, improve the capability for early warning and prevention of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, and exhibit substantial scientific significance, as well as promise clinical application value.

articles.title: Gout May Mimic Infection, Even Years After Achilles Tendon Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gout can affect tendons in addition to joints and may clinically resemble infection. The resulting diagnostic uncertainty may lead to surgical intervention or antibiotic treatment, even in patients whose symptoms might be managed medically if gout is recognized earlier.

QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: (1) Does late-onset gouty Achilles tendinopathy after prior Achilles tendon repair clinically resemble infection? (2) What diagnostic findings, including crystal analysis of aspirate or surgically obtained material when available, helped establish or support gout rather than infection? (3) What were the outcomes after gout was confirmed or suspected?

METHODS: This is a report of 4 patients with a similar presentation. Between April 2021 and June 2024, three surgeons at three academic medical centers identified 4 adult males, aged 42 to 55 years, who developed acute atraumatic Achilles-region pain, swelling, erythema, drainage, fluctuance, or induration 2 to 18 years after open Achilles tendon repair. These presentations raised concern that gout at or near a prior Achilles tendon repair site may mimic infection and lead to unnecessary interventions when gout is not considered early. We do not have an underlying denominator of patients treated for Achilles tendon repair by these surgeons during this period, but we speculate that it is on the order of several hundred. Minimum follow-up was 6 months after the treatment selected for the index Achilles inflammatory presentation. No patients who met these criteria were excluded, and no patients were lost to follow-up before the minimum follow-up interval. To determine whether this presentation clinically resembled infection, we reviewed presenting symptoms and physical examination findings, including pain, swelling, erythema, drainage, fluctuance, induration, fever, constitutional symptoms, and the treating surgeon's initial diagnostic concern. To answer our second question regarding diagnostic findings that established or supported gout rather than infection, we reviewed laboratory studies, imaging, aspiration findings, Gram stain, bacterial cultures, surgical findings, and pathologic evaluation for monosodium urate crystals. To answer our third question regarding outcomes, we reviewed whether patients underwent aspiration, surgical irrigation and debridement, antibiotics, immobilization, antiinflammatory or urate-lowering therapy, rheumatology or infectious disease referral, symptom resolution, recurrence, and complications. Three patients underwent aspiration and/or surgical irrigation and debridement for presumed infection. One patient was treated nonsurgically for suspected gout.

RESULTS: In 3 of 4 patients, late-onset gouty Achilles tendinopathy after prior Achilles tendon repair clinically resembled infection; it raised concern for an acute inflammatory or infectious process in all 4 patients. Among the 3 patients treated surgically, chalky tophaceous material was identified adjacent to the Achilles tendon, bacterial cultures were negative, and histological analysis confirmed monosodium urate crystals. The fourth patient had suspected gout based on hyperuricemia, Achilles-region symptoms, and improvement with nonsurgical treatment, although gout was not pathologically confirmed. All patients reported symptom resolution by latest follow-up (6 to 16 months).

CONCLUSION: Acute gouty tendinopathy can present years after Achilles tendon repair and can closely mimic postoperative infection, even when serum uric acid is normal. In patients without systemic signs of sepsis, earlier consideration of gout and routine crystal analysis when aspirate or surgically obtained material is available may help avoid unnecessary surgical debridement or prolonged empiric antibiotics when infection is not otherwise supported.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Effects of testosterone on exercise capacity in postmenopausal women with stage B heart failure.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Asymptomatic individuals with stage B heart failure (HF) often have reduced exercise capacity. As exogenous testosterone may have favorable skeletal muscle and vasculature effects, this study investigated whether transdermal testosterone improves exercise capacity in women with stage B HF.

METHOD: In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial involving women aged ≥55 years with stage B HF (defined as cardiac remodeling and/or diastolic dysfunction) and reduced exercise capacity (<100% age-predicted peak oxygen uptake V˙O2peak]), participants were randomly allocated to transdermal testosterone 5 mg/day or identical placebo for 4 months with cross-over after a 4-week washout. The primary outcome was change in V˙O2peak. Secondary outcomes included changes to cardiac structure and function assessed by echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and subjective quality of life.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight participants (median age 72 years, range 60-80 years; median body mass index 33.2 kg/m2 [P25-P75 28.7-35.9 kg/m2]) completed the study. Testosterone treatment increased circulating serum testosterone concentrations and was well tolerated, with no adverse treatment-related events. Testosterone treatment had no significant effect on V˙O2peak (β = -0.05, 95% confidence interval = -0.74, 0.65, p = 0.897), cardiac structure or indices of cardiac function, or quality of life.

CONCLUSION: Transdermal testosterone treatment did not improve exercise capacity in postmenopausal women with stage B HF.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Model With Temporal Validation for Predicting Walking Ability in Nontraumatic Spinal Cord Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Walking ability is the priority for spinal cord injury (SCI) patients. Nontraumatic SCI (NTSCI) is increasing with aging populations, yet its prognosis remains understudied. Early predictionF using admission clinical indicators could facilitate decision-making and rehabilitation planning.

OBJECTIVE: To preliminarily develop and validate a machine learning model using early admission clinical indicators for predicting post-rehabilitation walking ability probability (with a classification threshold of 0.5) in patients with NTSCI.

METHODS: This retrospective study included model development and temporal external validation. We enrolled 148 NTSCI patients, randomly allocating them into training (80%) and internal test (20%) sets. Four feature sets were constructed from objective clinical measures. Nine algorithms were compared; Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) was selected based on AUC, recall, and F2-score, followed by hyperparameter tuning. The final model was validated independently on a cohort of 37 NTSCI patients (July 2025 to May 2026). Ethical approval (M202616) and consent waiver obtained; retrospectively registered (MR-11-26-021748); no patient involvement.

RESULTS: The GBDT-based model outperformed all others. On internal testing, it achieved an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.77-1.00), recall 0.92 (95% CI: 0.71-1.00), and accuracy 0.90 (95% CI: 0.77-1.00). Key predictors included total lower limb muscle strength, age, and others. On temporal external validation, it showed encouraging performance with accuracy 0.81 (95% CI: 0.68-0.92) and recall 0.70 (95% CI: 0.40-1.00).

CONCLUSION: This preliminary model may have potential for predicting walking ability in patients with NTSCI; however, these findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts before any clinical application can be considered.

articles.title: Questions for the Study of Discrimination and Social Maltreatment in Victimization Research.
articles.abstract: Research to date suggests that exposure to social discrimination and maltreatment (SDM), for example, racism, sexism, antisemitism, and anti-LGBTQ+ behaviors, is associated with a variety of psychosocial symptoms and problems in the general population. Unfortunately, studies on SDM and its effects lag behind those examining other forms of interpersonal victimization. Questions examined in this paper include why SDM research should be increased, how SDM should be operationalized, and how the association between SDM and symptomatology can best be investigated given its overlap with other related variables, including trauma exposure and poverty.

articles.title: Frequent involvement of cingulate and insulo-opercular regions in sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy: A multimodal presurgical study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE) is classically considered a frontal lobe epilepsy; however, accumulating evidence suggests that hypermotor seizures may arise from multiple frontal and extrafrontal regions. We characterized the anatomical distribution of best available localizations in patients with SHE using multimodal presurgical data.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients with clinically diagnosed SHE who underwent comprehensive evaluation, including long-term video-electroencephalographic (EEG) monitoring, 3-T high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography, and, where indicated, magnetoencephalography, stereo-EEG (SEEG), and surgical assessment. Best available anatomical localizations were assigned using a hierarchical multimodal framework incorporating surgical, SEEG, and concordant noninvasive findings. Their anatomical distribution was subsequently assessed at the cohort level.

RESULTS: Sixteen patients (94.1%) had an assigned best available localization. Cingulate or insulo-opercular regions were involved in 11 of 16 patients (68.8%), whereas the remaining cases were localized to other frontal regions. In a sensitivity analysis restricted to 10 patients with SEEG-defined and/or surgically supported localizations, six involved cingulate or insulo-opercular regions. All patients were MRI-negative. In contrast, MRI-positron emission tomography fusion provided regionally informative anatomical findings in 16 of 17 cases and contributed to multimodal localization. Interictal epileptiform discharges were identified in 15 patients, whereas regionally informative ictal scalp EEG patterns were observed in eight; ictal interpretation was frequently limited by rapid propagation, movement-related artifacts, and delayed EEG onset. Focal cortical dysplasia-related histopathological findings were identified in five of seven resected specimens, whereas interpretation in two was limited by prior thermocoagulation.

SIGNIFICANCE: These descriptive findings indicate that cingulate and insulo-opercular regions were frequently represented among the identified localizations in this presurgical cohort. Multimodal evaluation integrating electroclinical, imaging, and invasive findings may support presurgical localization in MRI-negative SHE.

articles.title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited. We performed a longitudinal analysis within the BEAT-COVID cohort, comprising hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) or ward, and age-matched healthy controls. Serum levels of the complement activation marker soluble membrane attack complex (sC5b-9) and soluble inhibitors C1-Inhibitor (C1-INH), C4b-Binding Protein (C4BP), Factor H, and Factor I were measured by ELISA. In vitro endothelial complement sensitivity was assessed by flow cytometry. Soluble inhibitors were also measured in a cohort of patients with long COVID. Patients admitted to the ICU showed elevated sC5b-9 levels compared to patients admitted to the ward and controls, correlating with disease severity, length of hospitalization, and need for mechanical ventilation, but not mortality. Unexpectedly, levels of all soluble complement inhibitors were elevated, particularly in patients admitted to the ICU. Factor H levels positively correlated with sC5b-9. Endothelial cells pre-incubated with serum from patients admitted to the ICU became more susceptible to complement attack. In patients with long COVID, Factor H and C4BP levels remained elevated compared to pre-pandemic healthy controls. Severe COVID-19 is characterized by extensive complement activation despite elevated circulating inhibitor levels, suggesting impaired local complement regulation at the cell surface, potentially amplified by overwhelming systemic activation, rather than inhibitor deficiency.

articles.title: Exercise-related anxiety, but not objective physical function, is associated with employment in adults with congenital heart disease.
Differential Cardiometabolic Risk Profiles of Lean and Obese Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Longitudinal Health Checkup Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Hepatology research : the official journal of the Japan Society of Hepatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lean metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized. Whether it represents a distinct entity or a phenotype within the MASLD spectrum remains unclear. We examined differences in risk factor contribution and metabolic trajectories.

METHODS: In a longitudinal health checkup cohort (2017-2025), we included individuals without hepatic steatosis at baseline and excluded those with alcohol intake at or above the MetALD threshold. Incident MASLD was classified at diagnosis as Obese or Lean MASLD based on obesity status (BMI/WC). Baseline risk factors were evaluated using time-to-event and competing-risk models with interaction testing. Longitudinal metabolic changes were assessed using logistic regression, and repeated trajectories were examined using linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Among 13,624 participants, 1865 developed incident MASLD (Obese MASLD, n = 1469; Lean MASLD, n = 396). Male sex, baseline obesity, glycemic abnormality/diabetes, hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and higher baseline ALT were independently associated with incident MASLD. Interaction analyses showed a stronger contribution of male sex and weaker contributions of hypertension and low HDL-C in Lean MASLD. Longitudinal analyses showed Δtriglycerides and ΔALT were consistently associated with incident MASLD in both phenotypes, whereas ΔBMI showed a stronger association with Obese MASLD.

CONCLUSIONS: Lean MASLD shared a broadly similar cardiometabolic risk structure with Obese MASLD, whereas the relative contribution of risk factors differed between phenotypes. Male sex showed a stronger association with Lean MASLD, whereas longitudinal changes in triglycerides and ALT were consistently associated with incident MASLD across both phenotypes. These findings provide exploratory evidence of phenotype-specific metabolic associations requiring validation before clinical application.

articles.title: The Hyperviscous Heart: Reversible Cardiomyopathy in Polycythemia Vera.
Dynamic Arterial Elastance: Physiologic Basis, Current Clinical Evidence, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Restoring arterial pressure in hypotensive shock is a primary resuscitation goal, yet increases in cardiac output after fluid administration do not consistently produce meaningful increases in arterial pressure. This dissociation highlights the importance of understanding pressure-flow interactions during hemodynamic interventions. Dynamic arterial elastance (EaDyn) is a functional hemodynamic index proposed to characterize these interactions. Rather than reflecting static vascular resistance, EaDyn is hypothesized to describe the dynamic relationship between cardiac output and arterial load within the framework of ventriculo-arterial coupling. Clinically, EaDyn has been investigated as a predictor of the arterial pressure response to fluid administration in preload-responsive patients and as a marker of pressure stability during vasopressor reduction. However, current clinical evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and derived largely from selected populations. This review summarizes the physiologic basis of EaDyn, critically appraises the available clinical evidence, and highlights current limitations and priorities for future research.

articles.title: Coexistance of Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity and Orthostatic Hypotension in Patients with Unexplained Syncope.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity (CSH) and orthostatic hypotension (OH) are established causes of syncope but are often considered separate entities. However, evidence suggests that CSH and OH may coexist and jointly contribute to syncope. This study investigates the relationship between CSH and OH in patients with unexplained syncope.

METHODS: A total of 1,908 patients aged ≥40 years (age, 63.7 ± 13.0 years; men, 45.3%) with unexplained syncope underwent carotid sinus massage (CSM) and head-up tilt testing (HUT). Occurrence of CSH in classical and delayed OH, including asystolic CSM responses was analysed.

RESULTS: Six-hundred-and-eighteen patients (32.4%, 68.9 ± 11.3 years) had OH, while CSH was present in 320 patients (16.8%, 72.2 ± 9.9 years), and was more common in patients with OH than without OH (24.1% vs. 13.3%, p < 0.001). Among patients with CSH, 46.6% also had OH. CSH occurred equally in both classical OH (62/275, 22.5%) and delayed OH (87/345, 25.2%). Among OH patients, CSH was associated with older age, male sex, lower supine diastolic blood pressure, hypertension, and syncope-related hospital admission. An asystolic CSM response was observed more often in OH patients (n = 42; 6.8%) compared with non-OH patients (n = 44, 3.4%, p < 0.001) and was associated with older age and lower resting heart rate.

CONCLUSIONS: CSH and OH frequently coexist in adults over 40 years evaluated for syncope. CSM may reveal a clinically relevant cardioinhibitory reflex in a subgroup of OH patients, supporting comprehensive cardiovascular autonomic testing in unexplained syncope.

articles.title: Fetal adrenal microvascular index and adrenal volume in late-onset fetal growth restriction: A prospective observational study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the fetal adrenal gland microvascular index (MVI) and adrenal volume in late-onset fetal growth restriction (FGR) using MV-Flow and three-dimensional Extended Imaging Virtual Organ Computer-Aided Analysis and assesses their associations with neonatal outcomes.

METHODS: This prospective observational study at a single tertiary center (July 2024-August 2025) included 58 fetuses with late-onset FGR and 65 healthy controls. FGR was defined as abdominal circumference or estimated fetal weight <3rd percentile or 3-10th percentile with Doppler abnormalities. Fetal adrenal MVI (microvascular perfusion relative to organ size) and adrenal volume were measured during routine ultrasound. Group comparisons, logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analyses, and correlation analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Fetal adrenal MVI was significantly higher in the FGR group (38.9% vs. 23.1%, P < 0.001). MVI was independently associated with FGR (odds ratio 1.175, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.108-1.247, P < 0.001). MVI showed good discriminative ability for FGR (area under the receive operator characteristic curve = 0.876, 95% CI 0.815-0.937), with a cutoff of 25.3% (94.8% sensitivity, 64.6% specificity). Although adrenal volume was lower in the FGR group (4.37 vs. 5.50 cm3, P = 0.016), this difference disappeared after normalization to estimated fetal weight (P = 0.149) and abdominal circumference (P = 0.558). Lower adrenal volume was associated with neonatal intensive care unit admission independently of gestational age and birth weight (partial r = -0.252, P = 0.010).

CONCLUSION: Fetal adrenal glands show reduced absolute volume but increased microvascular perfusion in FGR cases. Adrenal MVI is a size independent marker of late-onset FGR, whereas reduced adrenal volumes largely reflects smaller fetal size.

articles.title: Dormancy type, seed traits, and species identity shape seed-associated fungal community composition in tropical pioneer trees.
articles.abstract: Seed germination is regulated in many plants by seed dormancy, while postdispersal survival is often determined by soilborne fungi that infect seeds. In tropical forests, seeds in each of three dormancy types (physical, physiologically dormant, or quiescent) often share similar physical and chemical traits. We hypothesized that variation in seed traits aligned with seed dormancy should shape seed-associated fungal communities, linking dormancy to seed survival. Seeds of 18 pioneer tree species were buried in each of five common garden plots in a lowland tropical forest in Panama for up to 36 months. Seeds were screened for viability and fungal infection at intervals throughout the experiment. Plant species with different dormancy types harbored distinct fungal communities. Dormancy type explained 6.5% of variation in fungal community composition after accounting for the far stronger signature of plant species identity (34%). Within dormancy types, differences in seed traits among species explained 49-56% of the variation in fungal communities, suggesting that seed traits drive niche partitioning beyond what is imposed by dormancy type alone. This study shows that variation in seed traits within a dormancy type filters seed-associated fungal communities, which likely shapes the demography of tropical forest trees by influencing seed survival and germination.

articles.title: Temporal Dynamics of Complement Activation and Outcome in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory responses exacerbate brain injury and affect the prognosis in acute ischemic stroke.

METHODS: We characterized longitudinal complement activation after acute ischemic stroke using serial plasma samples from 10 patients and 8 controls. Initial markers of classical (C1q), lectin (mannose-binding lectin), and alternative (complement factor Bb) pathways, as well as regulatory (complement factor H) and downstream markers (C3a, C5a, and C5b-9) were measured by ELISA at 9 time points.

RESULTS: Patients with stroke showed broad complement activation, with increased C1q, mannose-binding lectin, complement factor Bb, C3a, C5a, and C5b-9, and reduced complement factor H compared with controls. Complement components showed distinct temporal patterns during follow-up. Complement factor Bb levels were lower in patients with unfavorable functional outcome and in those with moderate-to-severe stroke. C1q and C3a trajectories differed according to functional outcome, whereas C3a trajectories also differed according to stroke severity. C1q trajectories differed according to age group and infarct volume.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest dynamic, pathway-specific complement activation after acute ischemic stroke and highlight the need for larger studies to clarify its prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Combined Associations of Glycoprotein Acetylation With Lipoprotein (a) and hs-CRP (High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein) on Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in MESA.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Higher plasma glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) concentrations are associated with an increased risk for incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). We investigated the combined associations of GlycA with lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) with incident CVD.

METHODS: We followed 6676 MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) participants, aged 45 to 84 years, without baseline CVD. Lp(a), GlycA, and hs-CRP were evaluated categorically using standard cut points (Lp[a]: 50 mg/dL; GlycA: 400 μmol/L; hs-CRP: 2 mg/L). We used multivariable-adjusted Cox hazards models to evaluate individual and combined associations of these 3 biomarkers with incident CVD, coronary heart disease, and stroke.

RESULTS: Compared with those with low GlycA and low Lp(a) levels, an increase in both incident CVD and coronary heart disease risk was observed for those participants with high levels of either or both of these biomarkers. Risk was highest for those with both high GlycA and high Lp(a) levels (CVD hazard ratio [HR]=1.55 [95% CI: 1.15-2.10) and coronary heart disease (HR=1.92 [95% CI, 1.33-2.77). A similar pattern was not observed for individuals with high levels of both GlycA and hs-CRP. Compared with participants with low levels of GlycA, Lp(a), and hs-CRP, those with high levels of all 3 biomarkers had a 1.98-fold higher CVD risk (95% CI, 1.39-2.82), a 2.23-fold higher coronary heart disease risk (95% CI, 1.45-3.44), and a 2.51-fold higher stroke risk (95% CI, 1.24-5.08).

CONCLUSIONS: Routine assessment of GlycA in addition to Lp(a) and hs-CRP may help to identify individuals at particularly increased CVD risk who may benefit from more aggressive preventive therapies.

articles.title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

articles.title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty.

METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models.

RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05).

CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

articles.title: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; P = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; P = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Adaptations in Placental Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Function in babies Born with Critical Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of birth defects; most critical (c)CHD newborns will develop neurodevelopmental disorders.
