Abnormal placental development may be involved, as genetics explains only 30% of sporadic CHD cases. Growing evidence suggests that placental dysfunction may result in heart and brain defects, as it shares a common early development. We hypothesized that newborns with critical CHD exhibit sex-specific alterations in placental mitochondrial biogenesis and function which may affect the fetal growth trajectory. Term placenta and paired umbilical cord (UC) blood were collected at birth from cCHD (n=16) and matched control (n=20) neonates. Mitochondrial lipid complex (phosphatidic acid (PA), phosphatidylglycerol (PG), cardiolipin (CL)), acylcarnitine metabolites and organic acids were determined in placenta by LC-MS/MS. Gene expressions of enzymes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics and lipid pathway were measured in placenta by RT-qPCR. Placental protein expressions of β-oxidation and OXPHOS were determined by Western Blot. Mitochondrial dynamics were reduced in cCHD placentas, particularly in male infants. Long-chain acylcarnitine (LC-acar) metabolites decreased in female cCHD placentas and increased in males, while they increased in both sexes in UC plasma. Malonate levels increased in cCHD placentas, affecting the TCA cycle. CL de novo synthesis was dysregulated in the cCHD placentas, though CL concentrations were similar in both groups. The cCHD placenta may compensate for cardiac defect in a potential sex-dependent manner, leading to an accumulation of LC-acylcarnitine in the UC plasma. Placental mitochondrial adaptation to metabolic needs may have a cardioprotective and neuroprotective effects.

articles.title: Before Guillain-Barré syndrome is attributed to a Zika infection, the presence of flavivirus RNA must be confirmed by PCR.
articles.abstract: The Zika virus, an RNA arbovirus, is known to trigger Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS). However, to establish that the Zika virus is indeed the causative agent, its presence must be confirmed - preferably via direct PCR. Detection of anti-Zika IgM antibodies should not be used for this purpose, as they can persist. Confirming Zika as the trigger for GBS also requires ruling out all other potential causes of the syndrome. Furthermore, all comorbidities and concomitant medications must be documented and included in the analysis. Finally, it is essential to refer GBS patients, regardless of the underlying cause, to a specialized department as soon as typical clinical symptoms appear.

articles.title: Interpenetrating Poly(urethane-urea)/Epoxy Networks for Superior Blast Shock Wave Attenuation.
articles.abstract: Protection against blast shock waves requires materials that combine high strength, high toughness, and efficient energy dissipation under extreme dynamic loading, yet these attributes are intrinsically difficult to achieve simultaneously in conventional polyurea. Herein, we report rigid-flexible interpenetrating polymer networks (IPNs) constructed from a poly(urethane-urea) (PUU) prepolymer and an epoxy resin (EP) prepolymer through a solvent-free, one-pot casting process. The optimized formulation, PUU75EP25, delivers a tensile strength of 60.41 MPa and a toughness of 260.35 MJ m-3 and attenuates 81% of the blast shock wave peak overpressure, ranking among the highest values reported for polymeric materials. Split Hopkinson pressure bar tests at a strain rate of 3200 s-1 reveal that PUU75EP25 combines the highest energy absorption efficiency (η ≈ 0.93) with a stable flow-stress plateau up to a true strain of 0.95, demonstrating efficient energy absorption under blast-relevant dynamic loading. In the Sprague-Dawley (SD) rat model, PUU75EP25 achieved a 100% survival rate (vs. 60% for the unprotected group) and reduced the lung injury area from 85.21% (unprotected group) to 16.71% (vs. 46.22% for poly(urethane-urea) protection). This high attenuation arises from the coupling of microscopic dissipation (sacrificial hydrogen-bond breakage and stress-wave scattering at the microphase-separated interfaces) with a macroscopic large-deformation zone that absorbs the shock energy through stable, failure-free deformation. This work establishes network interpenetration as a simple, scalable design principle for blast-protective polymers.

articles.title: The critical role of PET-based assessment of cerebrovascular disease in the management of patients with cognitive impairment and dementias.
articles.abstract: A recent survey provides valuable insights into French practitioners' preparedness for implementing anti-amyloid immunotherapy (AAI) for Alzheimer's disease. It highlights the need for education but also underscores a broader challenge: clinicians must understand not only treatment protocols but also unresolved issues regarding diagnostic specificity, efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. Amyloid biomarkers should not be considered definitive indicators of disease causality or treatment response. Greater attention should also be given to functional imaging approaches and cerebrovascular pathology, which may contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of cognitive decline. A balanced, evidence-based approach is essential before widespread adoption of AAI.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of plasma amyloid-β42 and Montreal Cognitive Assessment score as composite index for Alzheimer's disease in resource-limited settings: An exploratory study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAccurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) in Indonesia remains challenging due to limited access to cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and PET imaging. Plasma amyloid-β42 (Aβ42) may offer a less-invasive and affordable alternative, particularly when combined with cognitive assessment. However, its diagnostic performance in Indonesian populations is not well established.ObjectiveTo exploratorily assess the diagnostic accuracy of plasma Aβ42, alone and as a composite index combined with Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Indonesian version (MoCA-INA) scores, as potential alternatives to CSF biomarkers for AD diagnosis in a resource-limited setting.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted involving 25 AD patients and 20 cognitively normal controls. Plasma and CSF biomarker levels were measured using ultrasensitive immunoassay. Cognitive function was evaluated using MoCA-INA. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic accuracy.ResultsPlasma Aβ42 with the level of 9.6 pg/ml showed moderate diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.78, sensitivity = 69.2%, specificity = 70.6%), while its combination with MoCA-INA Score improved accuracy (adjusted AUC = 0.93, sensitivity = 80.0%, specificity = 84.0%). No significant correlation was found between plasma and CSF biomarkers. Plasma p-tau181 was excluded from the final composite index because it showed an unexpected direction of change.ConclusionsPlasma Aβ42 combined with MoCA-INA as a composite index, demonstrated potential diagnostic performance for AD in resource-limited settings. However, these exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously and require further validation in larger and independent cohorts before clinical application.

articles.title: Empagliflozin in Lafora disease: A first-in-human 6-month pilot study with electroclinical and FDG-PET findings.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Lafora disease (LD) is a rare, fatal neurodegenerative epilepsy with no approved treatments. Empagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, has shown neuroprotective actions in preclinical models through modulation of glycogen metabolism, induction of a pseudo-ketogenic state, improved mitochondrial efficiency, and reduction of excitatory neurotransmission. Based on this rationale, we conducted a first-in-human pilot study of empagliflozin in two genetically confirmed LD patients.

METHODS: Two patients with genetically confirmed LD received empagliflozin 10 mg/day for 6 months. Serial assessments included safety and tolerability, seizure frequency, myoclonus severity, electroencephalographic findings, neuropsychological and motor evaluations, brain MRI, and quantitative FDG-PET with regional Z-score analysis.

RESULTS: Empagliflozin was safe and well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Seizure frequency, myoclonus, and overall clinical status remained largely stable over 6 months, although some neuropsychological and motor measures showed variable changes between patients. EEG background activity and spike index were largely unchanged. Brain MRI showed stable mild cortical atrophy in both patients. In contrast, FDG-PET revealed progressive and spatially expanding cerebral hypometabolism in both patients, with worsening regional Z-scores, particularly in the parietal and precuneus regions.

SIGNIFICANCE: In this first-in-human, 6-month pilot study, empagliflozin showed acceptable short-term safety and feasibility in LD, but no definitive conclusions on efficacy can be drawn. The dissociation between relative electroclinical stability and progressive metabolic impairment suggests that quantitative FDG-PET may represent a sensitive biomarker for monitoring disease trajectory in this ultra-rare epilepsy.

articles.title: Outcomes of therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty and deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty in acanthamoeba keratitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: While acanthamoeba keratitis (AK) is a sight-threatening corneal infection, a thorough comparison of the outcomes of therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty (PK) and therapeutic deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (DALK) is lacking. We aimed to compare clinical outcomes of PK and DALK in AK. The study was preregistered in the PROSPERO database (CRD420251233705). A comprehensive search of Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was conducted through 11 November 2025. Eligible studies reported outcomes after PK or DALK in patients with AK, specifically graft survival, best spectacle-corrected visual acuity (BSCVA) and postoperative complications. Of the 1257 studies screened, 28 studies comprising 478 eyes with AK were included in the meta-analysis. Individual participant data (IPD) were available from 11 studies. The pooled graft survival rate was significantly higher after DALK (0.90, 95% CI 0.48-0.99) than after PK (0.63, 95% CI 0.54-0.71) (p = 0.025). No significant difference was observed in either BSCVA improvement between PK (-1.00, 95% CI -1.36 to -0.64) and DALK (-1.29, 95% CI -2.30 to -0.28) (p = 0.314), or in postoperative BSCVA between PK (0.97, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.25) and DALK (0.86, 95% CI -0.02 to 1.74) (p = 0.739). Postoperative complications did not differ significantly between the two procedures (all p ≥ 0.91). DALK may provide superior graft survival compared with PK in AK, while visual and postoperative outcomes appear comparable between the two procedures. Within the observed follow-up periods, treatment delay alone was not clearly associated with visual outcomes after PK.

articles.title: Turkey haemorrhagic enteritis live vaccination controls disease and field virus circulation: molecular, clinical and pathological evidence in field longitudinal studies.
articles.journal: Avian pathology : journal of the W.V.P.A
articles.abstract: Live haemorrhagic enteritis virus (HEV) vaccination reduced clinical signs and lesions under field conditions.Vaccination limited field strain circulation and environmental infection pressure.Vaccinated turkey flocks remained protected from HEV until slaughter age.

articles.title: Mechanical behavior and weight reduction of titanium frameworks with topology-optimized lattice structures for implant-supported prostheses.
articles.journal: Journal of prosthodontics : official journal of the American College of Prosthodontists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the mechanical behavior of titanium frameworks with triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structures designed for additive manufacturing by topology optimization for complete arch implant-supported fixed dental prostheses.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A maxillary model supported by four implants (two posteriorly tilted and two anterior parallel) was virtually modeled using a dental computer-aided design program. Titanium frameworks for complete arch implant-supported fixed dental prostheses, which incorporated three distinct TPMS lattice structures (Schwarz, Diamond, and Lidinoid) with variable cell wall thicknesses, were designed using topology optimization software. A total of 36 optimized framework designs were analyzed by finite element analysis under vertical and oblique loading (200 N) at the canine, premolar, and molar (cantilever) regions. A solid, non-optimized titanium framework was the control group. von Mises stress (MPa), maximum displacement (µm), reaction forces (N), and weight reduction ratios (%) were analyzed. Statistical analyses were performed with ANOVA and Tukey's post hoc test (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: All topology-optimized frameworks achieved >30% weight reduction, with the Diamond lattice structure demonstrating the highest reduction of 39.92 ± 2.60 (p < 0.001). Although optimized frameworks exhibited higher displacement and stress values than solid controls because of increased flexibility, the peak stress values (190-210 MPa) remained significantly below the yield strength of titanium. Optimized frameworks generated significantly lower reaction forces than solid controls under canine and premolar loading, indicating an energy-absorbing effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Topology optimization created a semi-rigid framework that incorporates the shock-absorbing benefits of polymers while maintaining the inherent fracture resistance of metallic alloys. Topology-optimized titanium frameworks provide a clinically viable solution for reducing prosthetic weight and minimizing reaction forces at the abutment interface, particularly in complete-arch rehabilitations.

articles.title: En bloc excision of a large hydatid cyst originating from the posterior wall of the left ventricle.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Cardiac involvement in hydatid disease is rare and accounts for only a small proportion of all hydatid cyst cases. Owing to the risk of life-threatening complications, including compression of cardiac chambers, cyst rupture and anaphylactic shock, surgical resection is indicated. This case report describes the surgical management of a male patient with an incidentally detected cardiac hydatid cyst located on the posterior wall of the left ventricle. The cyst was completely excised en bloc through a left ventriculotomy. This video tutorial highlights the surgical techniques and technical considerations essential for the safe and effective en bloc resection of cardiac hydatid cysts.

articles.title: 'Double-dunk' implantation of valveless ring-reinforced PTFE conduits for neonatal truncus arteriosus repair.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: This case describes a neonatal truncus arteriosus repair using an 8 mm ring-reinforced, valved polytetrafluoroethylene conduit for right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction via the 'double-dunk' technique. The diagnosis was established prenatally in a patient with familial history of the disease. Anatomically, both pulmonary arteries arose adjacent to each other from the posterolateral common trunk; there was a mildly regurgitant quadricuspid truncal valve and an accidental finding of an intramural course of both coronary arteries.  Clinically, the neonate presented with mild cyanosis and pulmonary overcirculation. The postoperative course was complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia requiring prolonged ventilation. Discharge echocardiography showed good biventricular function, unobstructed conduit flow and mild truncal valve regurgitation. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remains clinically well.

articles.title: High-normal and mildly elevated bilirubin levels in prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis patients are associated with lower thrombotic risk.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of clinical and laboratory investigation
articles.abstract: High-normal or mildly elevated bilirubin concentrations without apparent significance are commonly observed in clinical practice. Several observations in various chronic diseases associate them with reduced risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, likely due to their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity. We aimed to investigate potential clinical and prognostic associations of high-normal to mildly elevated bilirubin in patients with prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis (pre-PMF), a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm with high inflammatory and thrombotic burden. We retrospectively analyzed clinical and prognostic associations of bilirubin levels in a total of 82 pre-PMF patients diagnosed and treated in six Croatian hematology centers. Patients with apparent liver disease or hemolytic anemias were excluded from analysis. Among 82 evaluated patients, 54 (66.7%) were JAK2 mutated; 14 (17.5%) had prior thrombosis. Median age was 66 years. Incidence rates for thrombosis and bleeding were 2.02% and 1.26% patient-years, respectively. Median bilirubin levels were 11.9 µmol/L. Patients were stratified at a data-derived ≤11/>11 µmol/L cutoff for thrombotic risk evaluation. Although higher-bilirubin patients were more likely to belong to higher revised-IPSET-thrombosis categories, to be of male sex, and to have lower platelet and lymphocyte counts, they experienced significantly lower thrombotic risk compared to lower-bilirubin patients (0.47% and 3.81% patient-years, respectively). No significant association with major bleeding, nor with mortality, was observed. In the multivariate Fine and Gray regression model, higher-bilirubin (sHR 0.029 (0.006-0.13), p < 0.001) was independently associated with lower thrombotic risk, whereas older age (sHR 1.21 (1.04-1.41), p = 0.013) and male sex (sHR 6.75 (1.45-31.4), p = 0.015) were mutually independent predictors of higher thrombotic risk.

articles.title: EXPRESS: A novel mouse model of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis based on photochemical-induction combined with in situ injection.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) is a distinct cerebrovascular disorder characterized by impaired venous drainage and blood-brain barrier dysfunction, yet its pathophysiology remains poorly understood due to a lack of refined experimental models. We developed a novel, clinically relevant mouse model of CVST by integrating localized intraluminal induction with photochemical occlusion of the superior sagittal sinus (SSS). Model fidelity was validated using laser speckle contrast imaging, MRI, and histological analysis. Our approach produced consistent, spatially restricted SSS thrombosis, resulting in pronounced acute-stage brain edema and venous infarction. Notably, MRI combined with TTC staining identified a peri-infarct region suggestive of a venous penumbra. Functional assessments revealed significant acute motor deficits followed by recovery at day 7, whereas cognitive impairments persisted longer. Compared with conventional FeCl₃ or systemic Rose Bengal photothrombosis models, this integrated method exhibited superior anatomical specificity and minimized off-target tissue injury. This study introduces a reproducible CVST model that successfully recapitulates the key hemodynamic and pathological features of human venous stroke, providing a robust platform for mechanistic investigations and the evaluation of targeted therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Collaborative Technology-Assisted Depression Program for Chronic Disease Patients in Santiago, Chile.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of a collaborative, computer-assisted psycho-educational intervention for managing depression in patients with hypertension and/or diabetes in comparison with usual care in primary care clinics in Santiago, Chile.

METHODS: Adults with moderate-to-severe depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] ≥15) enrolled in the Cardiovascular Health Care Program were recruited. The active arm (n = 180) received an eight-session computer-assisted, psycho-educational program, telephone monitoring, and usual care for chronic diseases, while the control group (n = 179) received usual care for depression and chronic diseases. Outcomes were assessed at 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups, with the primary outcome being depression improvement (50% decrease in PHQ-9 score) at 6 months. Intention-to-treat analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: The active arm showed non-statistically significant reductions in depressive symptoms and improvements in mental health-related quality of life, treatment adherence, and health care utilization compared to the control arm.

CONCLUSIONS: While results did not demonstrate statistical difference within the programs to treat the health problems included in the study, the findings support the use of computer-assisted psychoeducation intervention.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: These findings advocate for optimizing current care models by incorporating scalable, evidence-based interventions, such as technology-assisted programs, to address remaining gaps in mental health integration.

articles.title: Effects of supplemental leucine and lysine on metabolic and inflammatory responses of neutrophils and peripheral blood mononuclear cells in growing cattle.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated effects of postruminal leucine and lysine supplementation on hematological variables and ex vivo neutrophil and peripheral mononuclear cell (PBMC) responses in steers. Rumen-cannulated steers (n = 7; BW = 173 kg, 5 mo) were assigned to a 6 × 6 Latin square, with one treatment sequence replicated in the seventh steer. Treatments were a factorial arrangement of leucine (0, 15, or 30 g/d) and lysine (0 or 6 g/d) administered via continuous abomasal infusion. Blood was collected on d 7 of infusion for hematological analysis and isolation of neutrophils and PBMC. Neutrophil function was assessed by phagocytosis and oxidative burst, and metabolic responses by glucose concentrations in spent media with or without lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Peripheral mononuclear cells were cultured under concanavalin A (ConA) with or without LPS to evaluate cytokine production, glucose, and mRNA expression. Data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS with period, lysine, and leucine as fixed effects and steer as a random effect, and orthogonal contrasts were used to evaluate linear and quadratic effects of leucine and their interactions with lysine and LPS. Most hematological variables were not affected by treatment. Lysine increased platelet counts and decreased lymphocyte counts (P = 0.04), whereas hemoglobin tended to increase linearly with increasing leucine (P = 0.10). Neutrophil glucose utilization was not affected by main effects; however, a linear leucine × LPS was detected (P = 0.04), with glucose decreasing as leucine increased in the absence of LPS, but not under LPS. Neutrophil phagocytosis and oxidative burst were not affected by treatment. For PBMC, glucose concentrations were lower under ConA than ConA + LPS (P < 0.001), and a lysine × quadratic leucine was detected (P = 0.01). For PBMC, leucine linearly decreased TNFA (P = 0.05), GLUT1 (P = 0.07), and GLUT3 (P = 0.05) mRNA abundance, whereas lysine tended to increase NFKB1 (P = 0.09). Production of TNF-α was greater under ConA than ConA + LPS (P < 0.001) and was not affected by treatment. In contrast, IFN-γ increased under ConA + LPS (P < 0.001), increased linearly with leucine (P = 0.02), and tended to increase with lysine (P = 0.10). These results show that leucine modulated metabolic responses in neutrophils and both metabolic and inflammatory responses in PBMC, whereas lysine primarily influenced selected hematological variables, with limited effects on PBMC inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: A Proposed Consensus Definition of Severe COPD: a modified Delphi Study.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Advanced interventions are available for patients with more severe COPD despite guideline-recommended therapies, yet this population is heterogeneously defined and inconsistently recognized, and a standardized work-up is lacking, which could lead to mismanagement.

OBJECTIVES: To formulate a new, expert-based consensus definition of severe COPD and a minimal set of diagnostics and characteristics to be assessed in the work-up of these patients.

METHODS: A modified Delphi study with two online rounds was conducted between June 2024 and January 2025 with 55 international COPD experts representing all areas of disease management. Sixty-seven (round 1) and 20 (round 2) statements were tested in seven domains: (A) the need for a definition, (B) symptoms, (C) functional impairment, (D) quality of life, (E) physiological impairment, (F) framework definition, and (G) risk factors. Consensus was defined as ≥ 75% agreement.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached for 46 (69%) statements in round 1 and 15 (75%) in round 2. Among patients with confirmed COPD, severe COPD was defined as: (1) persistent symptoms, functional impairment, or severely reduced quality of life; (2) despite optimal treatment and not due to comorbidities; and (3) including at least one clinical characteristic: severe airflow obstruction, severely impaired diffusion capacity, severe hyperinflation, frequent exacerbations, chronic respiratory insufficiency, pulmonary hypertension related to COPD, or cachexia or unintentional weight loss related to COPD. The proposed standardized work-up comprised: (1) assessment of patient-reported outcomes for symptoms, quality of life, anxiety and depression; (2) assessment of exacerbation frequency and severity; (3) comprehensive diagnostic testing, including lung function testing, blood gas analysis, imaging, cardiac assessment, and exercise-tolerance testing; and (4) assessment of risk factors for more severe and progressive disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Using expert consensus, we devised an internationally-supported, proposed definition and work-up for 'severe COPD', accounting for disease heterogeneity. This definition may improve identification of the population and supports a structured evaluation of this often under-recognized and potentially undertreated population. Future studies are warranted to determine its clinical impact, prognostic value, and utility in research.

articles.title: Pathogenicity and virulence of NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE.
articles.abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes the sexually transmitted infection gonorrhea and is an obligate human pathogen, colonizing mucosal epithelia of the male urethra and the female endo/ectocervix, resulting in urethritis and cervicitis. These manifestations represent uncomplicated gonorrhea and highlight the gonococcus as a primarily mucosal pathogen. However, gonococci can ascend the female reproductive tract to cause pelvic inflammatory disease and may disseminate to distant anatomical sites. The gonococcus expresses a diverse array of virulence factors that mediate transmission, mucosal colonization, immune modulation, and disease progression. In this review, we outline the mechanisms of gonococcal transmission and colonization of the genital tract epithelium, and examine host-pathogen interactions that drive inflammation, immune evasion, and immune suppression. We also discuss the mechanisms underlying dissemination and the resulting spectrum of clinical outcomes. Continued investigation of gonococcal biology and host interactions will advance understanding of pathogenesis and support the development of improved treatments and preventative vaccines.

articles.title: Integrating ctDNA-Based ESR1m Monitoring Into First-Line Care for ER+, HER2- Advanced Breast Cancer: A Consensus Workflow.
articles.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is an emerging tool in precision oncology that enables noninvasive tumor profiling, detection of minimal residual disease, and treatment monitoring. Furthermore, routine ctDNA analyses offer the potential to support more personalized and dynamic cancer care. In advanced breast cancer (aBC), ctDNA-based monitoring has been investigated across multiple studies as a tool for detecting emerging resistance mechanisms, predicting treatment responses and informing biomarker-guided treatment decisions. One example, investigated in the phase III PADA-1 and SERENA-6 trials, is monitoring for emergent estrogen receptor alpha mutations (ESR1m) during first-line endocrine therapy in estrogen-receptor positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+, HER2-) aBC. While not yet widely adopted in clinical practice, broader implementation of routine ctDNA-based monitoring for ESR1m is anticipated and will require standardized diagnostic workflows, encompassing both institutional operational processes and patient-centered scheduling pathways. Insights and recommendations were gathered from multidisciplinary experts across academic and community practices in the US regarding the feasibility, barriers, and operational requirements for implementing ESR1m monitoring during first-line treatment of aBC. Here, we present practical, experience-informed considerations, supplemented by an opinion-based consensus workflow model designed to provide clinicians with a flexible framework for implementing ctDNA-based ESR1m monitoring during first-line care for ER+, HER2- aBC.

articles.title: The relationship between functional prognosis in patients with infection after upper limb trauma: a predictive model based on HbA1c stratification and the mediating role of delayed rehabilitation.
articles.journal: Journal of plastic surgery and hand surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between preoperative glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and upper limb function (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand [DASH] score) at 6 months post-surgery in patients with fracture-related infection (FRI) after upper limb trauma, and to test the mediating role of rehabilitation initiation time.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 100 patients with FRIs after upper limb trauma surgery (September 2020 to August 2025). Demographic characteristics, fracture features, HbA1c levels, time to initiate rehabilitation, and debridement frequency of patients were collected. With the DASH score at 6 months after surgery as the outcome variable, multiple linear regression was used to analyze the association between HbA1c and functional prognosis, and the Bootstrap method was used to test the mediating effect of rehabilitation initiation time.

RESULTS: HbA1c was significantly positively correlated with the DASH score (β = 6.90, 95% CI 3.91-9.89, p < 0.001). Recovery initiation time played a partial mediating role between the HbA1c and the DASH scores, with a mediating ratio of 27% (indirect effect 2.04, 95% CI 0.63-3.59, p = 0.004). There was no significant interaction between HbA1c and recovery initiation time or debridement frequency (p > 0.05). Thresholding effect analysis did not find a definite breakpoint (log-likelihood ratio test p = 0.220), and HbA1c was linearly related to the DASH score.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative HbA1c is independently associated with 6-month upper limb function in patients with post-traumatic infection, with rehabilitation initiation time playing a partial mediating role. Clinicians should prioritize glycemic control and initiate rehabilitation as early as safely possible.

articles.title: Preoperative echocardiographic parameters do not predict early outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether preoperative echocardiographic parameters can predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum.

METHODS: This prospective study examined preoperative demographic characteristics, echocardiographic findings, and left ventricular strain parameters in 35 patients undergoing arterial switch operation for late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Further, their correlation with postoperative variables, including length of ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, and inotropic score, was assessed.

RESULTS: The median age at surgery was 45 days, and the median weight was 3.4 kg. The median interventricular septal thickness was 4.1 mm, and the median left ventricular mass index was 26.4 g/m2. The median average left ventricular strain was -24.19. Thirteen patients required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. The whole cohort had a median extracorporeal membrane oxygenation duration of 0 days. The median length of ICU stay was 12 days, and the median length of postoperative hospital stay was 17 days. The median inotropic score was 28. There was no case of early mortality. None of the preoperative echocardiographic parameters showed a statistically significant association with postoperative outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative echocardiographic parameters, including left ventricular strain, did not significantly predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in patients with late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Postoperative outcomes in this patient group are likely influenced by multiple preoperative factors rather than a single preoperative echocardiographic parameter.

articles.title: Developing the Universal Child Abuse Screening Tool (U-CAST) for Epic: A Qualitative Analysis of Expert Working Groups.
articles.abstract: Child abuse and maltreatment remain major public health concerns in the United States. Early identification is challenging, particularly for clinicians without specialized pediatric training, and disparities in detection raise concerns about bias. Universal screening integrated into electronic health records (EHRs) may improve detection and equity. To develop an evidence-based, user-friendly, and broadly applicable universal child abuse screening tool (U-CAST) for integration into the EPIC Foundation System. A qualitative study engaged nine expert working groups comprising 17 specialists in child abuse pediatrics, pediatric trauma surgery, general pediatrics, and pediatric emergency medicine. Between February and April 2022, groups met virtually to discuss screening content, clinical decision support, workflow integration, and implementation considerations. Meeting transcripts were analyzed using inductive coding and thematic analysis. Five themes emerged: (1) the importance of universal screening; (2) essential tool components; (3) appropriate clinical settings; (4) actionable follow-up protocols for positive screens; and (5) local program evaluation. Preliminary implementation data demonstrated successful integration, high screening completion rates, and encouraging performance in identifying children with suspected physical abuse. U-CAST was developed through a multi-disciplinary expert process and designed for integration into Epic workflows. Preliminary findings support its feasibility and clinical utility.

articles.title: Predicting prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery: development of a nomogram for risk prediction based on preoperative and intraoperative factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite improvements in neonatal cardiac surgery, prolonged mechanical ventilation remains a prevalent postoperative complication. This study was designed to build a prolonged mechanical ventilation prediction model based on preoperative and intraoperative factors in neonates (0-28 days) after cardiac surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on perioperative data of 385 newborns undergoing cardiac surgery at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital from 2018 to 2024. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was defined as postoperative mechanical ventilation duration >7 days.

RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors, visualised via a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by area under receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified airway anomalies (odds ratio = 2.280, 95% confidence interval 1.217-4.271, P = 0.010), preoperative mechanical ventilation (odds ratio = 2.244, 95% confidence interval 1.283-3.925, P = 0.005), radical surgery (odds ratio = 0.220, 95% confidence interval 0.091-0.533, P < 0.001), intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volumes (odds ratio = 1.529, 95% confidence interval 1.065-2.195, P = 0.021), intraoperative elevated lactate levels (odds ratio = 2.352, 95% confidence interval 1.256-4.403, P = 0.008), and higher vasoactive-inotropic score at the end of surgery (odds ratio = 1.060, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.199, P = 0.001) as risk factors for prolonged mechanical ventilation. The nomogram achieved an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.784, with robust calibration and clinical utility. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with prolonged hospital stay (median 23 vs. 16 days, P < 0.001) and increased hospital mortality (12.3% vs. 1.1%, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This model accurately stratifies the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery, potentially guiding postoperative management.

articles.title: Septic arthritis attributed to a spider bite - a case report and review of the literature.
articles.abstract: Individuals who travel to tropical or subtropical areas are exposed to various infectious, environ-mental, and climatic risk factors, as well as traffic accidents, security problems, natural disasters, and direct contact with potentially dangerous plants or animals. Accidental bites by venomous spiders during long journeys are always dangerous to health and life, but it is not usually recognized that nonvenomous spiders also pose such a substantial threat to the lives of local inhabitants and travelers. Here, we present an unusual case of a 41-year-old male patient who was admitted to the University Hospital after a tourist trip to Kenya with skin lesions and abscesses located in the gluteal region and the lower limb, caused by a tropical spider bite. As a severe complication, the patient developed sepsis and septic arthritis of the hip, contralateral to the primary skin lesions. Microbiological evalua-tion of peripheral blood, synovial fluid, and pus from subcutaneous abscesses consistently identified methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) as the cause of sepsis. This case is unusual and exceptional, as it illustrates the possibility of a serious complication in the form of generalized bacterial superinfection accompanying a spider bite in an immunocompetent person. It was also the first documented report of staphylococcal septic arthritis directly related to a nonvenomous spider bite. In this publication, we present our diagnostic and treatment approach, compare it with other similar cases from the available literature, and discuss spider bites as a common and often downplayed complaint in patients returning from tropical areas in daily medical practice.

articles.title: Genetic disruptions of Hsp90-encoding genes impacted short-term evolutionary trajectories of antifungal resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
articles.abstract: Laboratory evolution has been a powerful approach to address questions about evolvability. It has been debated whether the molecular chaperone, heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90), buffers or potentiates the effects of variation, and, consequently, constrains or accelerates evolution. In this study, we experimentally evolved yeast strains carrying mutant alleles of Hsp90-encoding genes under mild clotrimazole selection. We found that knockout of HSC82, which encodes a constitutively expressed Hsp90 chaperone, led to slower evolution of clotrimazole resistance in the short term. However, all strains generally evolved resistance within seven transfers, regardless of Hsp90 status. Through whole-genome sequencing, we identified genetic changes associated with clotrimazole resistance, including prevalent mitochondrial genome loss, as well as chromosomal duplications and point mutations. HSC82 knockout populations specifically showed convergent chromosomal duplications of chrVIII and chrXV. Taken together, our results demonstrate that disruption of Hsp90 in yeast may not alter the overall outcome of evolution but may shape its evolutionary trajectories at both the phenotypic and genotypic levels.

articles.title: Prediction of 10-Year Incident Hypertension After Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a model including pregnancy-related factors for the prediction of incident hypertension after pregnancy and to assess the impact of pregnancy-related factors on model performance.

DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.

SETTING: Routine primary care data linked to the data from the Dutch Perinatal Registry and Statistics Netherlands.

POPULATION: Women with a first childbirth at ≥ 24 weeks' gestation between 2007 and 2019 were included and were followed for up to 10 years after childbirth.

METHODS: Two Cox proportional hazards models were developed to estimate the 10-year risk of hypertension. Model 1 included sociodemographic factors and CVD-related factors, while model 2 additionally included pregnancy-related factors.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ten-year risk of incident hypertension.

RESULTS: We included 28 234 women, of which 639 developed hypertension (cumulative 10-year incidence 3.3%). The C-index of model 1 was 0.659 (95% CI: 0.642-0.684) and increased to 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754-0.796) after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. The C-index difference was 0.113 (95% CI: 0.092-0.132), mostly driven by the inclusion of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Net reclassification improvement was 0.213 (95% CI: 0.159-0.273) for events and 0.001 (95% CI: -0.004 to 0.006) for non-events.

CONCLUSIONS: Our prediction model for hypertension showed good discrimination and calibration after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. This model may help to target cardiovascular risk management for women with a high risk of hypertension after pregnancy in order to improve women's cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Multiomics Profiling Supports Cathepsin B as a Protective Factor in White Matter Hyperintensities and Cognition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a common brain magnetic resonance imaging marker of cerebral small vessel disease and a major risk factor for stroke and dementia, yet the molecular mechanisms governing lesion formation remain incompletely understood. We sought to identify circulating proteins that lie upstream of WMH and influence related clinical manifestations.

METHODS: We conducted a 4-stage proteogenomic study. Stage 1 tested a WMH polygenic risk score against 2923 plasma proteins in 52 560 UK Biobank participants (mean age, 56.8 years, 53.9% female, 94.0% White), and candidate proteins against WMH volume in the neuroimaging subset (n=5443; mean age 54.2 years, 53.5% female). Stage 2 applied bidirectional Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and local genetic correlation using cis protein quantitative trait locus and cis expression quantitative trait locus instruments from plasma, vascular, and brain tissue. Stage 3 analyzed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 8 postmortem periventricular white matter samples (4 WMH lesions, 4 controls; mean age, 81 years; 50% female). Stage 4 tested circulating and genetically predicted protein levels against general cognitive ability.

RESULTS: Stages 1 and 2 converged on CTSB (cathepsin B) and ECHDC3 (enoyl-coenzyme A hydratase domain-containing 3). Higher plasma CTSB was associated with lower WMH volume (β=-0.09 [95% CI, -0.13 to -0.05]; n=5260), and Mendelian randomization estimates were directionally consistent across all 5 instrument sets (plasma protein quantitative trait locus β=-0.052 [95% CI, -0.064 to -0.040]), with concordant effects on white matter microstructure, perivascular spaces, and lacunar stroke. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing showed CTSB downregulation within lesions, predominantly in astrocytes (log2 fold change=-1.70) and oligodendrocytes (log2 fold change=-0.48; both false discovery rate P<1×10-20). Higher plasma CTSB (β=0.061 [95% CI, 0.010-0.112]; n=5193) and a cis protein quantitative trait locus polygenic score (β=0.031 [95% CI, 0.009-0.054]; n=8884) predicted better cognitive performance. ECHDC3 showed no consistent association beyond stage 1.

CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal proteogenomic evidence nominates CTSB as a lesion-suppressed protein associated with lower WMH burden and better cognition, and a candidate therapeutic target for cerebral small vessel disease.

articles.title: Implanted intracranial pressure sensors: mechanisms, fabrication, and system integration.
articles.abstract: Intracranial pressure (ICP) is a key physiological parameter for the diagnosis and management of traumatic brain injury, hydrocephalus, stroke, and other neurological disorders. ICP sensors are typically required to provide accurate pressure measurement at low pressure while maintaining long-term stability in biofluid environments. Although conventional liquid-based ICP systems remain the clinical standard, their bulky and tethered configurations increase the risk of infection and tissue injury and restrict patient mobility. Advances in miniaturized implantable sensors have created new opportunities for continuous and ambulatory ICP monitoring. This review summarizes recent developments in implantable ICP sensing technologies, covering sensing mechanisms, materials, designs, and fabrication processes. Wireless communication approaches together with emerging transient bioresorbable ICP sensors designed that eliminate the need for surgical removal are also discussed. Finally, the review highlights the remaining technical challenges and outlines future research directions toward long-term, minimally invasive ICP monitoring systems.

articles.title: Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein in cats with lower urinary tract disease.
articles.journal: The Journal of small animal practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein levels in both obstructive and non-obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease. In addition, urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein levels were investigated in cats experiencing short-term (<36 hours) and long-term (≥36 hours) urethral obstruction.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study included 32 cats, classified into two main groups: cats with feline lower urinary tract disease (n = 24) and healthy controls (n = 8). The feline lower urinary tract disease group was subdivided into obstructive (n = 16) and non-obstructive (n = 8) forms. The obstructive group was further divided based on urethral obstruction duration into short-term (n = 8) and long-term (n = 8) sub-subgroups. Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen and potassium were measured in blood samples. Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein and urinary creatinine concentrations were measured in urine supernatant samples. Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein concentrations were indexed to urinary creatinine and expressed as the urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine ratio.

RESULTS: The mean urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine values of cats with obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease were statistically higher than those in cats with non-obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease and healthy controls. The difference between the mean urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine values of cats with long-term and short-term obstruction was not statistically significant. In addition, moderately positive correlations were calculated between urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine and serum creatinine (r = .646; P < .001; 95% CI = 0.264 to 0.863) and between urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (r = .549; P < .01; 95% CI = 0.081 to 0.791) in the study population.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: This study is the first to report urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine in cats with feline lower urinary tract disease. The findings suggest that urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein/creatinine may serve as a potential biomarker for identifying post-renal acute kidney injury in cats with obstructive feline lower urinary tract disease, particularly in long-term obstructive cases.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury in pregnancy is associated with increased risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes: an integrated health system study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (PrAKI) is an uncommon but serious complication associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with limited data in high-resource settings.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 29 586 deliveries at Mayo Clinic hospitals between 2017 and 2022. PrAKI was defined using Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) creatinine criteria. Maternal characteristics, nephrotoxin exposure, clinical interventions, and neonatal outcomes were compared between patients with and without PrAKI.

RESULTS: PrAKI occurred in 341 patients (1.15%). Compared with controls, PrAKI was associated with higher rates of chronic hypertension (28.7% vs 5.2%), cesarean delivery (68.5% vs 35.1%), intensive care unit (ICU) admission (59.1% vs 6.2%), and nephrotoxin exposure (58.7% vs 31.6%) (all P < .0001). Dialysis was required in 7.1% of patients with PrAKI, with 1.17% remaining dependent at discharge and 0.88% at 30 and 90 days; no control patients required dialysis. Neonates of mothers with PrAKI had higher rates of prematurity and neonatal ICU (NICU) admission (48.7% vs 9.8%; P < .0001). Maternal mortality was rare.

CONCLUSIONS: PrAKI is a marker of severe maternal illness and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although most patients recover kidney function, a subset develop persistent dysfunction. Early identification, cautious use of nephrotoxic medications, and structured postpartum follow-up are essential.

articles.title: Risk factors for bloodstream infection caused by carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales in patients with haematological malignancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: With the aim to identify risk factors associated with bloodstream infections (BSI) caused by carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) in patients with hematological malignancies (HM), a systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251176369). MEDLINE, PubMed, and Embase were searched for studies published up to 31 October 2025. Observational studies evaluating risk factors for laboratory-confirmed CRE BSI in adult or paediatric patients with HMs were included. Adjusted and unadjusted effect estimates were analysed separately. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random- or fixed-effects models based on heterogeneity. Six studies were included. In meta-analyses based on adjusted estimates, prior exposure to carbapenems (OR 8.01, 95% CI 2.98-21.54), cephalosporins (OR 4.11, 95% CI 1.53-11.05) and fluoroquinolones (OR 3.94, 95% CI 1.83-8.44) resulted to be associated with CRE BSI. Meta-analyses of crude data showed additional associations with CRE colonization, previous infections, newly diagnosed disease or first relapse, chronic liver disease, diabetes mellitus, and prior exposure to multiple antibiotic classes. Prior exposure to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones was consistently associated with CRE BSI in adjusted analyses. However, the small number of included studies and the wide confidence intervals limit the precision and generalizability of these estimates. Previous antibiotic exposure should therefore be considered as part of an integrated risk assessment together with colonization status, previous microbiological findings, clinical severity, and local epidemiology, rather than as a stand-alone criterion for empirical therapy.

articles.title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
articles.abstract:
AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo.

METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers.

RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

articles.title: Determinants and generational patterns of age at sexual debut among men and women in South Africa: Evidence from the SADHS 2016.
articles.journal: African journal of AIDS research : AJAR
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early sexual initiation is a public health concern in South Africa and increases the risks of HIV, unintended pregnancy, and adverse reproductive outcomes. Nationally representative, gender-differentiated analyses remain limited. Analyses that examine debut patterns across the full reproductive age range to provide cohort-level generational evidence are particularly lacking.

AIM: This study examined the socio-demographic determinants and generational patterns of age at sexual debut among men and women in South Africa, using nationally representative data from the 2016 South African Demographic and Health Survey (SADHS).

METHODS: Using the 2016 SADHS data, we analysed 7 476 sexually active women (15 to 49 years) and 3 183 men (15 to 59 years). Early sexual debut was defined as the first intercourse before age 18 years. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests examined bivariate associations, and logistic regression identified independent predictors, applying survey weights for national representativeness.

RESULTS: Early debut affected 53.0% of women and 62.4% of men. For women, lower education and poverty increased odds, while higher education was protective. Provincial variation was observed. Among men, younger age strongly predicted early debut, while marriage or cohabitation reduced it. Education, residence, and province were not significant predictors for men.

CONCLUSION: Early sexual debut remains highly prevalent with gender-specific determinants. Interventions should promote education and economic support for women, and age-appropriate, masculinity-sensitive sexual health programmes for men, addressing social and structural drivers to reduce HIV and reproductive health burdens.

articles.title: Delayed normalization of tissue transglutaminase antibodies in children with celiac disease and type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diabetes mellitus type 1 (T1DM1) and celiac disease (CD) can coexist in a patient. The aim was to evaluate the characteristics of children with both CD and T1DM and children with CD alone and to compare normalization rates of tissue transglutaminase immunoglobulin A class antibodies (anti-tTG IgA) normalization.

METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal study included children with both T1DM and CD and children with CD alone found by family screening, followed up from 2013 to 2023. Anthropometric and serologic parameters were evaluated at the time of diagnosis and during follow-up.

RESULTS: Included were 18 patients in T1DM + CD group (39% girls, median age 8.9 years) and 27 patients in CD group (52% girls, median age 8.8 years). There were no statistically significant differences in gender, age, anthropometry parameters, frequency of patients with initial anti-tTG levels >10 times of upper limit of normal (78% vs. 63%, p > 0.05), frequency of follow-up visits (1.06 visits/year of follow-up vs. 0.76, p > 0.05) and follow-up period (4.3 vs. 3.89 years, p > 0.05). The only statistically significant difference was in timing of anti-tTG normalization. At 2 years after diagnosis anti-tTG normalized in 56% of patients in T1DM1 + CD versus 93% in CD alone group (p < 0.01). If only patients with high antibody titers were analyzed, the normalization was still slower in CD + T1DM group (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: It takes longer to normalize anti-tTG in children with coexisting T1DM and CD than in CD alone found by family screening. We suggest monitoring these patients more closely during the first years after the diagnosis of CD.

articles.title: Epigenetic and Metabolic Changes That Drive Trained Immunity in Response to Microbes and Vaccines.
articles.abstract: Trained immunity is a form of innate immune memory in which initial exposure to microbial components or vaccines leads to long-lasting functional reprogramming of innate immune cells through epigenetic and metabolic changes. Unlike adaptive immunity, it does not rely on B or T lymphocytes and provides broad, nonspecific protection against various pathogens. This phenomenon has been observed across a range of immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, NK cells and even γδ T-cells, as well as at the level of haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). Key inducers include microbial products (e.g., β-glucan, BCG and MMR vaccines), metabolic byproducts (e.g., mevalonate and lactate) and cytokines such as IL-1β. These agents activate signalling pathways such as the Akt/mTOR/HIF-1α pathway and lead to chromatin remodelling via histone modifications such as H3K4me3 and H3K9me3. Immunometabolism plays a pivotal role, with trained cells shifting toward glycolysis, glutaminolysis and cholesterol synthesis. Lactate and fumarate further link metabolism to epigenetic remodelling. Notably, trained immunity can be protective in infectious diseases and beneficial in noninfectious contexts, such as cancer immunotherapy and autoimmune regulation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the cellular, epigenetic and metabolic mechanisms underlying trained immunity, highlighting how innate immune cells acquire memory-like properties independent of adaptive immunity. This study also provides insights into the therapeutic potential of leveraging trained immunity for vaccine development, infection control and immunomodulation in noninfectious diseases.

articles.title: HHP-Decellularized Porcine ITA for CABG: Preserved Compliance and In Vitro Hemocompatibility.
articles.abstract: Small-diameter conduits for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) require both distensibility and hemocompatibility, but synthetic grafts have poor patency. We evaluated an acellular arterial conduit prepared from porcine internal thoracic arteries (ITAs) harvested with an ultrasonic (harmonic) scalpel and decellularized by high hydrostatic pressure (HHP). Porcine ITA was decellularized at 600 MPa and washed with DNase I and ethanol. Extracellular matrix preservation and residual DNA were assessed by histology/SEM and DNA quantification. Mechanical performance was evaluated using ISO 7198-guided methods, including suture retention, integral leakage, kink radius, and static compliance. Kink radius was measured under luminal pressurization using a cylindrical taper gauge, and static compliance was calculated as diameter-based compliance from the reconstructed inner radius under stepwise pressurization and reported as %/100 mmHg. In vitro hemocompatibility was assessed in an ISO 10993-4-guided closed-loop blood circulation assay (4 h, 37°C) by measuring TAT, β-thromboglobulin, SC5b-9, and hematology parameters. HHP decellularization removed cellular components while preserving arterial microarchitecture and reduced residual DNA to 8.1 ± 2.7 ng/mg dry tissue. The grafts maintained pressure-dependent, nonlinear diameter-based compliance comparable with native porcine ITA and showed no detectable integral leakage, including sealed branches, up to 200 mmHg under the present conditions. Mean kink radius at the onset of kinking was 6.9 mm for decellularized ITA and 6.3 mm for native ITA. Blood-contact testing showed activation of coagulation, platelet, and complement pathways comparable with the blank loop under heparinized closed-loop conditions and far below positive controls. These findings support the further development of HHP-decellularized porcine ITA as compliant conduits for CABG and warrant in vivo evaluation of patency and remodeling.Impact StatementOff-the-shelf small-diameter coronary artery bypass grafts require compliance, kink resistance, and hemocompatibility. We combine ultrasonic (harmonic) scalpel harvest (simultaneous branch sealing) with 600-MPa high hydrostatic pressure decellularization without detergents to produce a stockable porcine internal thoracic artery scaffold. ISO 7198-guided tests show no leakage from sealed branches, low kink radius, and preserved pressure-dependent, nonlinear diameter-based compliance. ISO 10993-4-guided human blood circulation indicates coagulation, platelet, and complement activation comparable with the blank (negative) loop under heparinized closed-loop conditions, and markedly lower than positive controls. This workflow provides a rationale for in vivo patency and remodeling studies.

articles.title: Updating Korean Reimbursement Criteria for Endovascular Thrombectomy in Contemporary Stroke Care.
Pancreatic steatosis is not associated with impaired insulin secretion among individuals with diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Aims We aimed to assess pancreatic and hepatic steatosis (PS/HS) association with residual insulin secretion and insulin resistance in individuals with diabetes. Methods Pancreatic/liver fat fractions (PFF/LFF) in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were used as a proxy for PS and HS in 170 participants. Insulin secretion was estimated by HOMA2-B, C-peptide response 6 minutes after an i.v. bolus of 0.5 mg glucagon (ΔC-Pe), and fasting proinsulin to C-peptide ratio (PI:C). Insulin resistance was estimated by HOMA2-IR, Adipo-IR and i.v. insulin (0.05 IU/kg) tolerance test. Results PFF did not correlate with measures of insulin secretion but it correlated with fasting indices of insulin resistance among women (HOMA2-IR, R = 0.26, p = 0.017; Adipo-IR, R = 0.29, p = 0.007). Both LFF and PFF correlated with BMI (R = 0.43 & R = 0.34, respectively, p < 0.001) but not with each other (R = 0.10, p = 0.215). Unlike PS, HS was associated with higher HOMA2-IR, Adipo-IR, HOMA2-B, PI:C and glucagon, after adjustment with confounders. Participants with PS without HS had lower fasting C-peptide, HOMA2-IR, HOMA2-B, Adipo-IR, glucagon and triglycerides (p < 0.05) compared to those having HS without PS. Cluster-based subgroups of diabetes did not differ in PF (p = 0.071). Conclusions Within this cohort, pancreatic fat was more strongly associated with adiposity than with the investigated measures of β-cell function or insulin resistance.

articles.title: Automating case extraction and screening for hospital-associated Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia surveillance in two Canadian hospitals.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Outline our process in creating an efficient surveillance system through increased automation of detecting hospital-associated Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (HA-SAB). To describe the rate and attributable source of HA-SAB over time at our institutions.

METHODS: We developed an algorithm for extracting cases that met the temporal case definition of hospital-onset Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (HO-SAB) through our electronic medical record system. The expanded temporal definition included both instances of S. aureus bacteremia (SAB) if occurring>48 hours after admission (HO-SAB Current Admission) or if admitted ≤48 hours but had a previous admission within the past 4 weeks (HO-SAB Previous Admission). Following extraction, clinical review was performed to ascertain if the algorithm extracted HO-SAB cases were hospital-associated SAB (HA-SAB) versus community-associated SAB (CA-SAB) and source(s) of infection.

RESULTS: Over a 5-year period from 2020 to 2025, the rate of HA-SAB was 15.2-26.2 per 10,000 patient admissions and 1.5-2.7 per 10,000 patient days. Our automated process screened 5,146 total cases of SAB, and determined that 222 cases (4%) fit the temporal definition of HO-SAB. Of these 222 HO-SAB, we classified 189 (85%) cases as HA-SAB and 33 (15%) as CA-SAB. The most common sources of HA-SAB were central lines (23%) and peripheral IVs (22%).

CONCLUSION: An automated process is effective at screening cases of SAB. This can improve workflows to enable a sustainable HA-SAB surveillance program as a quality metric for institutions. Our expanded definition of HO-SAB allowed detection and evaluation of an additional 38 (20%) previous admission cases.

articles.title: The Trajectory of Gastrointestinal Symptom Experience Following Fecal Microbiota Transplant for Recurrent Clostridioides Difficile Infection.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI) increases the risk of persistent gastrointestinal symptoms after treatment. Although fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) effectively prevents CDI recurrence after antibiotics, the trajectory of gastrointestinal symptom severity remains poorly characterized.

METHODS: We tracked gastrointestinal symptom severity in a prospective, multicenter cohort study of adults with rCDI after treatment with standardized FMT products. Patients who experienced a CDI recurrence during the follow-up period were excluded. The IBS Symptom Severity Scale (IBS-SSS) was used as a measure of symptom severity, not as a diagnostic tool. Patients completed the IBS-SSS at the time of FMT, 1-week, 1-month, and 3-months post-FMT. The primary outcome was the change in IBS-SSS score after treatment. Subgroup analyses were conducted among patients with baseline IBS-SSS ≥175 (moderate/severe symptom severity) and <175 (none/mild symptom severity). Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate longitudinal changes and identify clinical predictors of IBS-SSS scores.

RESULTS: Among 107 patients included, median IBS-SSS scores decreased from 170 (range: 0 to 440) at baseline to 76 (range: 0 to 390) at week 1 and 54 (0 to 445) at month 3 (P<0.001). In those with baseline IBS-SSS ≥175 (n=51), 64% had none or mild symptom severity at month 3. In those with baseline IBS-SSS <175 (n=53), symptom severity was observed to remain as none or mild at month 3 in all but one patient.

CONCLUSION: FMT administered for prevention of rCDI was followed by a rapid (1 wk) and sustained (3 mo) reduction in gastrointestinal symptom scores in patients who did not develop CDI recurrence. These data help characterize the expected early post-FMT symptom trajectory, providing foundational evidence to better inform patient expectations and future interventions for persistent symptoms.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Integrated analysis of gene networks and cellular functions identifies novel heart failure biomarkers.
Spatial and campaign-scale dynamics of trace elements in lakes and ponds of the Iowa and Nebraska - Missouri River floodplain.
articles.abstract: Trace-element contamination in small floodplain water bodies can vary sharply among neighboring catchments, and regional averages may conceal individual hotspots. Water from six lakes and ponds in western Iowa and eastern Nebraska were examined during three site-wide surveys: Summer 2024, Fall 2025, and Spring 2026, yielding 18 site-campaign observations. Eleven trace elements-aluminum (Al), arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), cobalt (Co), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), nickel (Ni), lead (Pb), selenium (Se), and zinc (Zn) were retained after data verification, and concentrations were standardized to µg L-1. Site-specific exceedance ratios (ER = C/S) and Heavy Metal Pollution Index (HPI) values were calculated using the study screening benchmarks. Lake Manawa had the highest mean HPI (327.13) and the highest overall mean ER (1.85), driven principally by Co (mean ER = 7.19), Pb (5.16), Mn (1.99), Al (1.94), and Cd (1.49). Among the remaining sites, Pinky's Glen had the highest mean ER (1.57), dominated by Mn (5.31), Al (3.24), and Co (3.15), whereas Steinhart Park showed elevated Mn (5.61), Co (3.05), and Al (2.59). An additive two-factor variance partition indicated that water-body identity accounted for more than 90% of variation in Al, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Pb, and Zn during the sampled campaigns. The campaign accounted for 95.8% of As variation and 54.2% of Cd variation. An equal-weight score based on min-max-normalized mean HPI, exceedance frequency, and mean ER ranked Lake Manawa, Pinky's Glen, and Steinhart Park as the three highest priorities for confirmatory monitoring. A recovered physicochemical survey showed the highest mean TDS and EC at Carter Lake (264.67 mg L-1 and 529.33 µS cm-1), water temperatures of 3.03-6.57 °C, and circumneutral mean pH (6.95-7.62). Because the three surveys occurred in different years, temporal comparisons and benchmark exceedances are interpreted as screening-level evidence. The findings support site- and analyte-specific confirmatory monitoring rather than pooled regional assessment.

articles.title: Lactate-albumin ratio as an early predictor of mortality in critically ill children: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early risk stratification in critically ill children relies on severity scores such as PRISM-III and PELOD-2, requiring multiple variables. The lactate-albumin ratio (LAR), a two-parameter marker, shows prognostic value in adult and paediatric critical illness. This study evaluated serial LAR for predicting PICU mortality and compared its performance at admission against PRISM-III and PELOD-2. This prospective cohort study enrolled 335 of 563 screened children aged 1 month to less than 13 years admitted to a tertiary-care PICU in South India over 12 months. Serum lactate and albumin were measured at 0, 12, 24, and 48 h. Discriminatory performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis with DeLong's test. Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors. Of 335 children, 42 (12.5%) were non-survivors. LAR at admission discriminated mortality with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.859 (95% CI 0.806-0.907), exceeding PRISM-III (AUC 0.751) and PELOD-2 (AUC 0.759) at the same timepoint (p < 0.05 for both). LAR remained independently associated with mortality after adjustment for PRISM-III, sepsis, and vasoactive support (adjusted odds ratio 3.77, 95% CI 2.22-6.40, p < 0.001), and outperformed lactate and albumin. LAR remained persistently elevated in non-survivors through 48 h.Conclusions: LAR at admission discriminated PICU mortality better than PRISM-III and PELOD-2 and remained an independent predictor after adjustment. Serial LAR changes may be a useful adjunct in predicting prognosis, though their clinical utility requires further prospective study. Derived from two routine investigations, LAR may serve as a practical addition to severity scoring, pending external validation. What is Known • Mortality risk in critically ill children is estimated with multivariable severity scores such as PRISM-III and PELOD-2. • Lactate and albumin refl ect tissue perfusion and systemic infl ammation, and their ratio has been associated with mortality in critical illness. What is New • We hypothesised that the lactate-albumin ratio, from two routine blood tests, may predict PICU mortality at least as well as multivariable severity scores. • We also hypothesised that serial measurement over the fi rst 48 hours may add prognostic information beyond the admission value.

articles.title: Impaired insulin secretion in response to mixed meal ingestion is associated with hypersomatostatinemia in individuals with cystic fibrosis.
articles.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a monogenic disease characterized by exocrine pancreas insufficiency, glucose intolerance, and a high prevalence of diabetes. Diminished insulin secretion is a key contributor to glucose intolerance and diabetes in people with CF, yet the pathophysiology of this deficiency is not fully understood. Somatostatin is a hormone secreted by several tissues in the body, including the delta cells of the pancreas, and is known to inhibit insulin secretion; however, its role in postprandial hypoinsulinemia in people with CF remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 16 people with CF (CF group) and 8 healthy control subjects (HC), each of whom underwent a mixed meal tolerance test, during which their glucoregulatory responses were assessed. We hypothesized that impaired insulin secretion in CF would be associated with hypersomatostatinemia. Plasma glucose responses to the mixed meal were higher in CF compared to HC (AUC of 27,656±2,215 and 20,564±1,028 mg/dL*180 min, respectively, p<0.05), whereas the AUC for insulin (5866±730 and 11090±1628 µU/mL*180 min, respectively; p<0.05), and C-peptide (608±42 and 998±127 pg/mL*180 min, respectively; p<0.05), were both lower. Hypersomatostatinemia in CF (AUC of 4682±278 and 3353±277 pg/mL*180 min in CF and HC, respectively, p<0.01), was inversely associated with C-peptide (r=-0.54; p<0.01), and insulin (r=-0.60; p<0.01) responses to the mixed meal. These data suggest that hypersomatostatinemia is associated with diminished insulin secretion in people with CF, and that it could be a target for improving glucose tolerance in this population.

articles.title: White Blood Cell Counting in Severely Leukopenic Samples on a Sysmex XN Hematology Analyzer: Analytical Performance Evaluation of Whole Blood Mode and Low White Blood Cell Mode.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sysmex XN-9100 (XN) measures WBC counts in whole blood (WB) mode and automatically switches to low WBC (LW) mode for leukopenic samples (WBC <0.50×109/L). However, the analytical performance of LW mode in such samples has not been evaluated according to standard guidelines. We evaluated the analytical performance of the two modes in samples with WBC <0.50×109/L.

METHODS: Precision of WBC quantification in the two modes was evaluated using four samples according to the European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (EFLM) criterion (CV% 5.6). Linearity was evaluated at five concentrations. The two modes were compared in 650 leukopenic samples. Two samples showing discrepancies between the two modes were reviewed.

RESULTS: WBC counting precision met the EFLM criterion for both modes, except in a sample with WBC <0.2×109/L. Linearity was acceptable and within the allowable deviation of ±4.8% for both modes. Very high correlation (r=0.99), minimal mean difference (0.00×109/L), and almost perfect agreement (κ=0.90) were noted. Discrepant samples were interpreted as clinically consistent in WB and LW modes in one case each.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to evaluate the analytical performance of WBC counting in WB and LW modes on XN in samples with WBC <0.50×109/L according to guidelines. The two modes demonstrated reliable analytical performance. As precision decreased at WBC <0.2×109/L and discrepancies between the two modes were rare, careful attention is recommended.

articles.title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Social Risk Screening and Referrals in the Pediatric Inpatient Setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Many professional organizations recently recommended inpatient screening for social risks. Although prior studies have explored social risk screening rates in children's hospitals, many excluded community hospitals and lacked detail on screening practices.
