We aimed to describe national social risk screening and referral practices among hospitals caring for children.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey (August 2023-November 2023) through the Pediatric Research in Inpatient Settings Network. One clinical leader per institution was surveyed on inpatient social risk screening and referral processes, populations, tools and data tracking, and barriers/facilitators to social care. Descriptive statistics summarized survey responses.

RESULTS: Of the hospitals contacted, 80.2% (77/96) completed the survey. Overall, 66.7% of hospitals reported screening for social risks in some capacity, most commonly performed by nurses. Screening tools and domains varied widely, with 21.9% using a published tool and 12.5% using internally developed questions. Food insecurity was the most frequently screened domain (91.9%), whereas screening for legal needs was least common (0%). Most hospitals had systems to refer patients to in-hospital (98.4%) and out-of-hospital (96.8%) services, primarily through social work consultations (96.5%) and printed handouts (54.4%). Fewer than 10% partnered with community-based organizations. Less than 45% of screening hospitals had a data-tracking system for referrals, and only 2.5% collected patient health care use data. Staffing was the most cited barrier to screening.

CONCLUSIONS: Social risk screening and referral practices vary widely among hospitals caring for children. Standardized policies and support mechanisms may reduce variability and promote equitable social care practices across hospitals.

articles.title: Antibiotic Stewardship, Resistance, and Mortality in Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus: A Quasi-Experimental Study of Linezolid Restrictions.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic restriction policies are intended to curb resistance, but their effects on resistance, timely treatment, and patient outcomes remain uncertain. We evaluated linezolid restrictions and whether vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) screening identifies patients most likely to benefit.

METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences study using electronic health record data from 521,493 admissions at 2 academic medical centers from 2008 through 2019. Hospital 1 introduced a formal prior-authorization pager system in 2011 and stricter linezolid-specific criteria with enhanced post-prescription review in 2014; Hospital 2 served as a control. Outcomes included linezolid use, linezolid-resistant Enterococcus isolates, in-hospital mortality overall and by VRE status, and stewardship request behavior.

RESULTS: Linezolid was used in 2.3% of admissions; 1.2% of Enterococcus isolates were linezolid resistant. Restriction policies were associated with a 27% reduction in linezolid use (-0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -1.1 to -0.7; P < .001) and a 41% reduction in resistance (-1.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -1.6 to -0.4; P = .003). Overall mortality did not increase, but mortality among VRE-screen-positive patients increased by 4.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 1.9 to 7.5; P < .001), with larger increases among those with bacteremia or sepsis. Approval rates declined first, followed by fewer linezolid requests.

CONCLUSIONS: Restriction policies can reduce antibiotic use and resistance but may benefit from screening-informed safeguards to preserve timely treatment for high-risk patients.

articles.title: Nursing Students' Experiences Caring for Children With Special Needs: An Interpretative Phenomenological Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caring for children with special needs in special education settings requires effective communication, caregiving skills, and professional adaptability. Nursing students may face challenges while interacting with these children. Understanding their experiences is important for improving educational preparation and professional development.

METHOD: This qualitative study employed an interpretative phenomenological approach (IPA). Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted with nursing students who completed placements in special education settings. Data were analyzed according to IPA principles.

RESULTS: Three themes emerged: encountering uncertainty and initial shock, being caught between closeness and distance, and being transformed: reconstructing professional identity. Students described uncertainty, fear, and inadequacy during initial encounters, followed by emotional attachment, ethical dilemmas, and challenges in maintaining professional boundaries. Over time, these experiences contributed to understanding nursing roles.

CONCLUSION: Caring for children with special needs shaped students' emotional experiences and professional identities, highlighting the need for improved educational preparation.

articles.title: Participant experience with the SpaceLabs 90227 ambulatory blood pressure monitor and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro device.
articles.abstract: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is recommended for confirming hypertension and assessing out-of-office blood pressure (BP). However, patient burden and device tolerability may limit broader implementation. We compared participant experience with a traditional oscillometric ABPM device and a compact cuff-integrated ABPM. The PRO-BP Study was a pilot randomized crossover study of 20 adults in New York City. Participants completed two 24-h ABPM periods over 7 days using the SpaceLabs 90227 and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro devices. After each period, participants rated comfort, pain, sleep interference, embarrassment, noise, skin irritation, and interference with daytime activities. Both devices achieved guideline-based recording-quality thresholds. Compared with SpaceLabs, ABPMpro was associated with greater comfort [median: 7.0 (interquartile range - IQR: 5.0-8.5) vs. 3.5 (IQR: 2.0-6.5); P = 0.026] and less pain [1.5 (0-3.5) vs. 5.0 (0.5-7.0); P = 0.022]. Other experience ratings did not differ significantly. Participant experience should be considered alongside recording quality when evaluating validated ambulatory BP monitoring technologies.

articles.title: A specialized CD107a+ macrophage subset drives hyperphagocytosis of mycobacteria.
articles.abstract: Macrophages are essential for pathogen clearance, yet phagocytic specialization among subsets is poorly defined. Bone marrow-derived macrophages cultured with L929 supernatant or macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) separate into FSCloSSCloF4/80loCD11blo (FSCloSSClo) and FSChiSSChiF4/80hiCD11bhi (FSChiSSChi) subsets. Transcriptomic and functional analyses reveal that FSCloSSClo cells possess a hyperphagocytic program driven by enhanced actin cytoskeleton regulators (e.g., Arp2/3) and pro-inflammatory signaling (NF-κB). These cells excel at internalizing Mycobacterium tuberculosis virulent H37Rv and BCG through actin-mediated, cytochalasin D-sensitive mechanisms. High surface CD107a (LAMP1) expression marks this hyperphagocytic subset and correlates strongly with mycobacterial uptake. FSCloSSClo macrophages produce more TNF and IL-6 upon mycobacterial or Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2)/TLR5 stimulation yet retain IFN-γ-mediated killing capacity. In vivo, CD107a+ alveolar macrophages in BCG-infected lungs preferentially capture bacilli and upregulate CD195, recapitulating the in vitro phenotype. These findings establish CD107a as a key surface marker of a hyperphagocytic macrophage subset, providing new mechanistic understanding relevant to tuberculosis host defense and therapeutic development.

articles.title: An atlas of sarbecovirus infectivity across diverse ACE2 orthologs.
articles.abstract: Sarbecoviruses pose a substantial zoonotic threat, yet the determinants governing their host range remain incompletely defined. To systematically investigate host entry mechanisms, we generated a panel of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudoviruses representing 46 sarbecoviruses and assessed their infectivity across 66 angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) orthologs. This analysis produced a high-resolution host-entry landscape with direct implications for cross-species transmission risk. We found that all severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) isolates, WIV1, and pangolin-derived sarbecoviruses demonstrated broad ACE2 usage, whereas no sarbecovirus utilized alternative entry factors including neuropilin-1, CD147, AXL, or TMEM106B. Notably, ACE2 orthologs from Rhinolophus affinis and Miniopterus schreibersii supported infection by nearly all clade 1 sarbecoviruses, identifying highly permissive host receptors. We also identified residues 27 and 42 of ACE2 as critical determinants of sarbecovirus host tropism. Together, these findings define host entry constraints relevant to receptor-based risk assessment and inform surveillance and pandemic preparedness.

articles.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization.
articles.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

articles.title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children. K. pneumoniae isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from K. pneumoniae neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative K. pneumoniae vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of K. pneumoniae. Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal K. pneumoniae infection.

articles.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

articles.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen's diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

articles.title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.

EXPERT OPINION: Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

articles.title: From call to home: The role of dispatcher-assisted CPR in patient survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dispatcher-assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (DA-CPR) is a key strategy to reduce no-flow time in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet its impact on long-term survival remains various across emergency medical systems.

PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the association between DA-CPR and resuscitation outcomes in a nationwide cohort of OHCA patients presenting with an initial shockable rhythm.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including all adult OHCA cases with ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (VF/VT) in which resuscitation was carried out by emergency medical services in Hungary during 2019, 2022, and 2023. Patients were stratified according to whether DA-CPR was ongoing upon ambulance arrival, or initiated by the ambulance crew. Primary outcomes were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and hospital admission with sustained circulation. Utstein-style consensus reporting guidelines were followed.

RESULTS: A total of 3,674 VF/VT OHCA cases were included, of whom 1,744 (47.5%) received DA-CPR. Patients in the DA-CPR group had significantly higher rates of ROSC (92.0% vs. 12.4%), hospital admission with sustained circulation (90.8% vs. 11.7%), 30-day survival (54.6% vs. 7.1%), and one-year survival (45.8% vs. 6.2%) compared with those without DA-CPR (all P < 0.001). DA-CPR occurrence increased over time, while declined in 2022 followed by partial recovery in 2023.

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort of OHCA patients with shockable rhythms, dispatcher-assisted CPR was strongly associated with improved early resuscitation success and long-term survival. These findings support DA-CPR as a critical system-level intervention and highlight the importance of centralised protocols and continuous performance monitoring.

articles.title: Development of CNN and LSTM fusion model for early fault warning in hydro turbine units.
articles.abstract: Early fault detection is important for the safe and stable operation of large hydro turbine units under complex and variable operating conditions. This study develops an early fault warning framework for high dimensional multisource monitoring data by integrating Kendall rank correlation-based parameter grouping, systematic data governance, sparse principal component analysis, and a CNN LSTM prediction model. Fifty two operating parameters are organized into six groups and transformed into six sparse state features. The CNN LSTM model captures local correlations and temporal evolution, achieving R2 values of 0.947, 0.955, 0.848, 0.701, 0.687, and 0.853 for SPCA1 to SPCA6. Prediction residuals combined with 2σ and 3σ thresholds identify early degradation before the recorded fault, with warning lead times of up to 33 time steps. The framework provides a practical approach for condition monitoring and hierarchical early warning of large hydro turbine units.

articles.title: Energy absorption of multicell thin walled structures filled with polyurethane infiltrated open cell aluminum foam.
articles.abstract: Compact energy absorbers are needed to protect testing electronics in high-impact systems with limited installation space. Unlike previous studies that mainly examined tubular or fully filled configurations, this work investigates selective filling within a 12-mm-high multi-cell thin-walled structure. Partial and full configurations using aluminum foam (AF) and polyurethane-infiltrated aluminum foam (AF/PU) were evaluated through quasi-static compression, dynamic impact testing, finite element simulations, and theoretical analysis. Comparisons among five configurations and three wall thicknesses showed that filler distribution affected the balance between crushing resistance and effective crushing stroke. The partially filled AF/PU structure with a 1.2 mm wall thickness exhibited the best overall performance, absorbing 895.41 J quasi-statically and 984.40 J dynamically, with a volumetric specific energy absorption of 21.32 J/cm3 and crushing force efficiency of 0.84. Compared with full filling, selective AF/PU filling uses less filler while retaining greater deformation space, providing a practical strategy for compact impact protection.

articles.title: Host-response biomarker panels for distinguishing selected acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections from mono-infections.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections complicate antimicrobial decisions because pathogen detection may not establish whether both organisms are clinically contributing to disease. We synthesized evidence from adult and pediatric acute respiratory infection cohorts, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and selected mixed-detection febrile illness studies, to evaluate host-response biomarkers for distinguishing co-infection from mono-infection. Conventional C-reactive protein and procalcitonin were most useful as supportive or rule-out markers of bacterial involvement, but lacked sufficient specificity when used alone. Dual-axis strategies that combine antiviral and bacterial-response signals, including MxA/CRP, TRAIL/IP-10/CRP, CD169/CD64, IFI44L/FAM89A, and targeted transcriptomic or proteomic signatures, provided more biologically coherent discrimination of mixed infection states. These findings support prospective validation of integrated host-response panels as rapid decision-support tools for antimicrobial stewardship and clinically meaningful co-infection diagnosis.

articles.title: Genome-wide mapping of the Galleria mellonella transcription start sites during fungal infection and treatment.
articles.abstract: Galleria mellonella is an emerging experimental model, but its current genome annotation lacks transcription start site (TSS) information. Because TSS annotation is essential for understanding transcriptional regulation, we used low quantity single strand CAGE (LQ-ssCAGE) to map cap analysis of gene expression (CAGE)-defined TSSs from 72 G. mellonella larval samples. Among these, 36 larvae were infected with the fungal pathogen Madurella mycetomatis and 36 served as healthy controls, allowing identification of TSSs under both infected and healthy conditions. Infected and healthy larvae were treated with itraconazole or ravuconazole. To assess key characteristics of the CAGE data, TSS peaks and putative enhancers were intersected with the existing genome annotation for annotation and characterization. This analysis identified two sets of TSS peaks, permissive and robust, representing the first draft TSS atlas for G. mellonella. The atlas-derived annotations showed a markedly stronger core promoter sequence signature than the NCBI reference annotation, supporting improved resolution and accuracy of TSS annotation in the atlas.

articles.title: Microenvironment shapes Staphylococcus aureus phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis over time.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), frequently preceding or coexisting with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The impact of transient P. aeruginosa infection and therapeutic intervention on S. aureus phenotypic shaping remains poorly understood. We characterized 546 isolates from a longitudinal cohort of sixteen pediatric patients in CF follow-up, either monoinfected or coinfected, over eighteen months. Isolates were grouped into three phenotypic clusters. Monoinfected patients were enriched in a cluster with high pigment and biofilm, whereas transient P. aeruginosa detection was associated with a shift toward reduced pigment and biofilm, while coinfected patients maintained stable phenotypes. Phenotypes were determined by the airway microenvironment rather than by clonal background. In two monoinfected patients, this shift coincided with transient infection and ciprofloxacin treatment with increased MRSA; in vitro, MRSA predominated over MSSA when both P. aeruginosa and ciprofloxacin were present, underscoring the need to monitor S. aureus phenotypic transitions.

articles.title: Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific.
articles.abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a complex multisystem disorder requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care. This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations for NF1 management in the Asia-Pacific region. A modified Delphi process involving two survey rounds and a virtual meeting was conducted with experts from nine countries. A total of 141 statements were evaluated using a 9-point Likert scale with a 75% consensus threshold. Consensus was achieved across key domains including diagnosis, genetic testing, surveillance, and management. Experts emphasized the importance of multidisciplinary care, risk-adapted surveillance, and integration of genetic counseling and imaging in clinical practice. These findings provide regionally relevant guidance to support consistent and practical NF1 management across diverse healthcare systems.

articles.title: Boid inclusion body disease in Boa constrictor: Unraveling the myth of immunosuppression.
articles.abstract: Boid inclusion body disease (BIBD) is an infectious disease of captive boid snakes of major relevance since the 1970s. It is caused by reptarenaviruses and characterized by intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies in most cell types. Affected snakes frequently develop secondary bacterial infections, suggesting virus-associated immunosuppression. To investigate this, we analyzed peripheral blood from 48 Boa constrictor with confirmed BIBD, three infected snakes without disease, and 84 reptarenavirus-negative snakes, assessing hematology, biochemistry, stress parameters, and immune function. A functional phagocytosis assay on peripheral blood revealed a significantly reduced proportion of phagocytic cells (Iba1+ monocytes/azurophils) in BIBD-positive and reptarenavirus-infected snakes compared to uninfected animals, indicating impaired phagocytic capacity. In addition, BIBD-positive snakes showed reduced cholesterol and total immunoglobulin concentrations, while virus-specific IgY and IgM levels were elevated. These findings indicate selective impairment of innate and humoral immune components, providing mechanistic evidence for increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial infections in BIBD.

articles.title: Choroid plexus remodeling associated with inflammatory CSF exposure in preterm acquired hydrocephalus.
articles.abstract: Acquired hydrocephalus in preterm infants follows intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) or central nervous system infection and is associated with inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles. We integrated clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), CSF cytokine profiling, primary human choroid plexus (ChP) epithelial and endothelial cell assays, and independent transcriptomic and proteomic datasets to investigate ChP remodeling. Infants requiring CSF diversion exhibited greater ChP thickness independent of gestational age, ventricular size, and IVH severity, supporting its potential as a biomarker. Growth factor-enriched inflammatory CSF increased proliferation in primary human ChP epithelial and endothelial cells; EGFR and VEGFR inhibition attenuated these responses, and recombinant epidermal growth factor (EGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) reproduced proliferative effects. Independent IVH transcriptomic data confirmed Mki67 elevation in IVH ChP tissue. Integrated proteomic trajectories support a temporally dynamic remodeling framework linking acute inflammatory signaling to proliferative ChP activation and structural remodeling.

articles.title: Association between human genomes and mycobacterial genomes contributes to severity and transmissibility of pulmonary tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remains a major infectious disease globally. This study aimed to identify determinants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) transmission clustering, treatment outcome, and pulmonary cavitation by simultaneously analyzing host and pathogen genomic data. Whole-genome sequencing of 1,960 MTB isolates identified four major lineages (L1-L4). Host population stratification by principal component analysis of genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) classified 899 patients (70%) into a genetically homogeneous main group for genome-wide association study (GWAS). Multivariate regression demonstrated that MTB lineage was the primary determinant of transmission clustering, rifampicin resistance was the dominant predictor of unfavorable treatment outcome, and host genetic group was independently associated with pulmonary cavitation. GWAS identified novel loci in collectin subfamily member 10 (COLEC10), CTNNA3, and long intergenic non-coding RNA 2775 (LINC02775) associated with clustering, treatment outcome, and cavitation, respectively, with the association of COLEC10 also found in the remaining group of patients. These findings highlight the importance of integrating bacterial and human genomic analyses to understand tuberculosis host-pathogen interaction.

articles.title: Long-term ambient benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk through accelerated biological aging.
articles.abstract: The contribution of ambient air pollutants to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) remains undefined. This study included 401,472 adults from the UK Biobank (UKB), with residential benzene estimated at 1-km resolution from the DEFRA model (2006-2020). After multivariable adjustment in the Cox models, each interquartile-range (0.151 μg/m3) increment in benzene was associated with a 26% higher risk of incident NAFLD (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21-1.30), following a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. Accelerated biological aging mediated 6.5% of this association, whereas homeostatic dysregulation and allostatic load contributed modestly. Benzene exposure and polygenic risk showed no multiplicative interaction, but their cumulative effect raised NAFLD risk among highly susceptible individuals. A machine-learning model integrating benzene and covariates predicted NAFLD with good discrimination (AUC = 0.753), and an external urinary-biomarker analysis in NHANES was directionally consistent. Thus, long-term low-level benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk, partly through accelerated biological aging.

articles.title: Bidirectional metabolic-vascular feedback loops in heart failure: From myocardial energetics to multisystem cardiometabolic crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a multisystem syndrome in which myocardial dysfunction is shaped by metabolic, vascular, and extracardiac abnormalities. Across HFrEF and HFpEF, impaired substrate utilization, mitochondrial function, endothelial signaling, coronary microvascular function, and mechano-energetic coupling disrupt the matching of ATP supply to cardiac demand, while obesity, insulin resistance, inflammation, and vascular stiffness further accentuate cardiometabolic HFpEF. In this Review, we integrate these processes into five self-reinforcing metabolic-vascular circuits: substrate-perfusion mismatch; mitochondrial reactive oxygen species-endothelial dysfunction; endothelial metabolism-nitric oxide-myocardial stiffness; immunometabolic-microvascular inflammation-fibrosis; and afterload-mechano-energetic uncoupling. We also examine how adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, liver, and kidney amplify these circuits. Together, this framework links myocardial energetic dysfunction with systemic vascular-metabolic stress and highlights circuit-directed opportunities for phenotype-informed HF therapy.

articles.title: Evaluating the potential of treatment options for chronic hepatitis B.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide, but long-term or even lifelong viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) seldom clears hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), so-called 'functional cure.' In recent years, a shift in treatment strategy from viral suppression toward cure has emerged, catalyzed by three revised international hepatitis B guidelines (2025-2026) and the first-in-class phase 3 evidence that a finite antiviral therapy, the antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen, can achieve a functional cure in about one in five NA-suppressed CHB patients with baseline HBsAg below 3000 IU/mL.

AREAS COVERED: We evaluated the spectrum of established and emerging treatment options for CHB, organized around quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) as the axis for selecting and sequencing therapy. Coverage spans backbone NAs and pegylated interferon-α, an HBsAg-guided roadmap, finite NA therapy and off-treatment outcomes, bepirovirsen, other virus-targeting and immunomodulatory agents, and genome-directed covalently closed circular DNA silencing and editing.

EXPERT OPINION: Bepirovirsen's approaching approval is an inflection point. qHBsAg should guide personalized, sequential therapy, with partial cure (HBsAg <100 IU/mL) as a potential intermediate target when functional cure is unlikely. Durability, standardized biomarkers, rational combination design, metabolic co-management and equitable access are the priorities; a sterilizing cure remains distant.

articles.title: Hepatic TMEM30A deficiency disrupts lipid metabolism and liver regeneration through PPARα-ATGL pathway.
articles.abstract: The lipid accumulation at early phase during liver regeneration is necessary process, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the role of TMEM30A, a β-subunit of P4-ATPases, in hepatic lipid homeostasis and regeneration. Tmem30a liver-specific knockout (LKO) mice and controls were fed a high-fat diet and subjected to two-thirds partial hepatectomy. TMEM30A deficiency led to hepatic steatosis, dyslipidemia, and impaired induction of key triglyceride degradation and PPARα pathway genes. Following hepatectomy, LKO mice exhibited increased mortality, severe liver injury, reduced hepatocyte proliferation, and downregulation of Cyclin B1, Cyclin D1, and Cyclin E1. The lipid accumulation was markedly exaggerated in LKO livers, primarily due to suppression of the PPARα-ATGL axis. Pharmacological activation of PPARα with Wy-14643 restored lipid metabolism, hepatocyte proliferation, and survival after surgery. These findings reveal that the PPARα-ATGL pathway functions as a crucial downstream axis of TMEM30A in coordinating lipid metabolism and regenerative capacity.

articles.title: Physical activity attenuates mortality risk associated with elevated resting heart rate in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: The independent and combined associations of resting heart rate (RHR) and physical activity (PA) with mortality in diverse chronic kidney disease (CKD) populations remain unclear. We analyzed 12,042 patients from three cohorts using Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, joint-effect, mediation, and meta-analytic approaches. Elevated RHR was associated with increased risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, whereas higher PA levels showed consistent protective associations across cohorts. Combined analyses demonstrated that high RHR with low PA was associated with the greatest mortality risk, while high PA attenuated the adverse association of elevated RHR with mortality. Mediation analyses suggested that RHR partially contributed to the association between PA and mortality. RHR and PA are independent and modifiable risk markers for mortality in patients with CKD. Promoting PA and monitoring RHR should be integrated into CKD management to improve survival.

articles.title: Pediatric-to-Adult Transition of Care in Patients with Surfactant Metabolism Disorders.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Genetic disorders of surfactant metabolism, caused by pathogenic variants in the surfactant-related genes (SRGs) SFTPB, ABCA3, SFTPC, and NKX2-1, were long considered diseases of the neonate and the infant, with an outcome measured in weeks or months. Advances in neonatal intensive care, increased awareness, earlier molecular diagnosis, structured management, and pediatric lung transplantation have generated a growing population of adolescents and young adults living with a surfactant metabolism disorder. In the largest European survey of childhood interstitial lung disease (chILD) survivors, surfactant-related disorders accounted for about one in five patients now followed in adult centers. These patients must leave pediatric services that have often known them for many years, entering adult respiratory care systems, which are primarily around fibrotic lung disease of older adults: a setting where SRG diseases are rarely recognized. No literature is specifically devoted to transition in surfactant metabolism disorders. Therefore, this review brings together three bodies of evidence: the pediatric natural history of SFTPB, ABCA3, SFTPC, and NKX2-1-related disorders; specificities of SRG ILD surviving into and/or presenting in adulthood; the general principles of transition in rare disease, including the recent European Respiratory Society (ERS) statement on transition of care in chILD and what each implies for this group. Finally, the patient and family perspective was discussed, based on very sparse qualitative research. A proposed framework and a research agenda were suggested.

articles.title: Intrinsic functional architecture predicts remote motor cortical excitability changes induced by intermittent theta-burst stimulation.
articles.abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) modulates cortical excitability both locally and remotely through connected regions. However, how intrinsic functional architecture influences these remote effects remains unclear. Leveraging multi-site stimulation (targeting the left primary motor cortex [M1], dorsal premotor cortex, and caudal inferior parietal lobule) combined with resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigate whether intrinsic functional architecture predicts rTMS-induced changes in contralateral M1 excitability. While group-level effects were absent, individual variability in excitability changes was significantly predicted by functional characteristics. When the engaged network of stimulated region is sensorimotor network, resting-state functional connectivity between the stimulated region and the right M1 significantly predicts excitability changes, moderated by within-network interactions. Otherwise, exploratory analysis found associations with network topological properties rather than direct coupling. These findings provide preliminary insights into rTMS neuromodulation and may inform future development of personalized treatments (e.g., for post-stroke motor rehabilitation), yet require further investigation in clinical populations.

articles.title: Third harmonic generation microscopy reveals structure and mucus dynamics in human airway epithelium models.
articles.abstract: Airway epithelium is the primary interface between human body and the external environment, acting as a physical and functional barrier. In vitro airway models that reproduce the epithelium architecture are valuable tools for studying infection, inflammation, and transport processes. In this work, we present a label-free, non-invasive method to visualize and measure mucociliary transport in air-liquid human models using third-harmonic generation (THG) microscopy with an optical parametric amplifier laser source at 1,300 nm. By exploiting the intrinsic nonlinear contrast at optical heterogeneities, THG provides high-resolution images of both epithelial structures and the overlying mucus layer without fluorescence staining or sample processing as recently shown for other lung-tissue environments. Time-lapse THG imaging reveals depth-dependent transport dynamics within the mucus, offering new insights into mucociliary transport. Our approach offers a physiologically relevant way to assess mucociliary function in vitro and could support studies on respiratory diseases, drug delivery and epithelial remodeling.

articles.title: Inverse directions of association of higher physical activity and higher insulin resistance with human skeletal muscle fiber-type gene expression.
articles.abstract: To investigate the interplay between physical activity and cardiometabolic traits in human skeletal muscle, we characterized gene expression and chromatin accessibility across skeletal muscle cell types in 263 Finnish individuals from the FUSION Tissue Biopsy Study. We analyzed single-nucleus RNA-seq data (168,309 nuclei), single-nucleus ATAC-seq data (242,069 nuclei), and bulk RNA-seq data. Lower insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and higher total physical activity were both associated with higher proportions of Type 1 nuclei and lower proportions of Type 2x nuclei. Traits typically associated with better health-lower trait values of cardiometabolic traits such as HOMA-IR and higher physical activity levels-were associated with higher expression of energy metabolism genes and lower expression of signaling pathway genes across muscle fiber types, total pseudobulk, and to some extent in bulk tissue. HOMA-IR and physical activity appeared to have inverse and partially independent directions of association when adjusting for both traits in the same model.

articles.title: A wavelet-guided diffusion method for brain magnetic resonance parameter mapping using MOLED-based datasets: proof-of-principle.
articles.abstract: Objective.Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) can noninvasively acquire parametric maps, providing quantitative biomarkers for clinical assessment. Parametric maps, such asT2,T2*, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), characterize distinct biophysical processes in tissue in an interpretable, numerical manner. Owing to their distinct physical origins, various parametric maps differ in physical units, numerical magnitudes, and dynamic ranges. Even for the same type of parametric map, inter-subject differences may still exist in anatomical morphology, tissue characteristics, and the local distributions of parameter values. However, deep learning methods trained in image-domain directly learn pixel-level parameter values, and variations in numerical scales and subject-specific parameter distributions may result in anatomical detail loss and localized artifacts in certain tasks. To address this challenge and to deliver dependable quantitative references for clinical assessment, we propose a wavelet-guided diffusion method.Approach.We extend the discrete convolution wavelet transform (DCWT) to two dimensions and combine it with a conditional denoising diffusion method to develop a diffusion-based DCWT (Diff-DCWT) for parameter mapping. Diff-DCWT achieves accurate parameter mapping under the guidance of wavelet coefficient maps, thereby reducing reliance on image domain learning. The performance of Diff-DCWT is evaluated through simulation andin vivoexperiments acrossT2,T2*, and ADC mapping tasks.Main Results.Both simulation and healthy volunteer experiments demonstrate thatT2,T2*, and ADC maps obtained from Diff-DCWT maintain excellent visual quality and quantitative accuracy. Clinical case studies suggest the potential utility of Diff-DCWT-derivedT2and ADC maps for stroke staging and help distinguish lesional from normal brain regions in glioma.Significance.Diff-DCWT establishes a high-fidelity framework for parameter mapping and exhibits preliminary clinical value in stroke staging and glioma characterization. Moreover, this work demonstrates the potential of wavelet-domain prior guidance for deep learning-based qMRI applications.

articles.title: Morphological plasticity facilitates lung adaptation and dynamic immune remodeling in Mycobacterium abscessus infection.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus pulmonary disease (Mab-PD) shows rising global incidence and low cure rates. Mab exhibits marked phenotypic heterogeneity, with infection outcomes likely dependent on strain-specific host interactions. Through in vivo morphotype switching, we obtained a rough strain (Mab-R) that showed higher virulence, bacterial loads, and lung pathology than the smooth morphotype. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Mab-R adapts to macrophage functional states by modulating virulence and metabolic genes, promoting intracellular survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovered dynamic macrophage reprogramming during infection. In acute infection, alveolar macrophages and C1qa+ interstitial macrophages cleared Mab-R via programmed cell death, while newly recruited monocytes showed strong phagocytic capacity but incomplete bacterial clearance. During chronic infection, enhanced T cell immunity and resident-like macrophage dominance facilitated inflammation resolution. These findings reveal host-pathogen interplay driving Mab-R persistence and identify bacterial metabolic adaptation and macrophage reprogramming as potential therapeutic targets for chronic Mab-PD.

articles.title: Long non-coding RNAs in tuberculosis: Immune regulation and clinical biomarker potential.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains the leading infectious cause of mortality worldwide, with an estimated 1.25 million deaths in 2023. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of precise early screening tools continues to impede epidemic control. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as essential modulators of host anti-Mtb immunity, and elucidating their functional mechanisms is pivotal for developing effective interventions. This review systematically synthesizes lncRNA-mediated immune regulation during Mtb infection, with emphasis on their roles in modulating immune cell death, extending beyond apoptosis to encompass necrosis and pyroptosis. Importantly, we provide a comprehensive analysis of lncRNAs and related gene polymorphisms as predictive biomarkers for anti-TB drug-induced adverse reactions. Current research gaps and future priorities are also discussed. Together, the dual potential of lncRNAs as molecular diagnostics and candidate targets for host-directed therapy represents a promising frontier in TB management.

articles.title: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor in diabetes: A promising target for cognitive restoration.
articles.abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) plays an essential role in neuronal growth and maturation, as well as in maintaining synaptic plasticity. Dysregulated BDNF levels significantly increase the risk of neurological and metabolic disorders. In type 2 diabetes mellitus, several pathological mechanisms, including prolonged hyperglycemia, oxidative damage, chronic inflammation, and impaired insulin sensitivity, are known to drive neurodegenerative processes and deterioration of cognitive function. Impaired BDNF signaling can result in compromised synaptic transmission and gradual loss of neurons, with the hippocampus being particularly vulnerable. A growing body of evidence points to a strong correlation between diminished BDNF levels and diabetes related cognitive decline. Findings from both human clinical trials and animal studies have consistently reported reduced BDNF concentrations in brain tissues and systemic circulation in diabetic conditions. Therapeutic strategies aimed at upregulating BDNF expression and modulating its downstream signaling pathways hold considerable promise for preventing or mitigating diabetes associated cognitive deficits.

articles.title: MED26 facilitates Mediator-Pol II complex assembly and promotes nuclear stress body formation during heat stress.
articles.abstract: Cells adapt to environmental stress by reprogramming gene expression. During heat stress, the transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1) translocates into the nucleus and activates heat shock-responsive loci, including the long non-coding RNA HSATIII, promoting nuclear stress body (nSB) formation. We show that the Mediator complex subunit MED26 enhances HSATIII transcription and nSB formation through a mechanism distinct from its role at heat-shock response (HSR) genes. Under heat stress, MED26-containing Mediator is recruited to HSR genes and nSBs through interactions with HSF1 and MED15. Phosphorylation of the intrinsically disordered region of HSF1 appears to facilitate Mediator recruitment to nSBs. Acute loss of MED26 leads to the dissociation of the Mediator and RNA polymerase II (Pol II) from HSR gene promoters, whereas the Mediator remains bound to HSATIII despite Pol II dissociation. These results suggest that MED26 acts as molecular switch, thereby facilitating Mediator-Pol II complex assembly at nSBs and promoting nSB formation during heat stress.

articles.title: Impact of health education on quality of life in patients with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with lower quality of life (QoL) than the general population, and health education is widely proposed to help patients manage the disease. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of studies published between 2014 and April 2024 evaluating educational interventions in adults with CKD using a validated QoL instrument. Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data, resolving disagreements with a third reviewer; risk of bias was assessed with RoB2 and ROBINS-I. Twelve studies met inclusion criteria. Educational interventions were generally associated with improvements in QoL and clinical parameters, more consistently for mental than physical health, although certainty of evidence was limited by heterogeneity in design, populations and outcomes, and by a predominance of studies with some concerns or high risk of bias. Health education appears a valuable component of CKD care, but well-designed, prospectively registered trials are needed before firm recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Neurofibrillary tangle deposition in primary idiotypic isocortices using flortaucipir PET in histopathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Tau deposition in Alzheimer's disease (AD) spreads throughout the brain in a stereotypical pattern captured by the Braak neurofibrillary tangle staging scheme. While involvement of primary isocortex defines the highest stage, it is unclear whether flortaucipir PET uptake differs among primary isocortical regions. We determined relationships between flortaucipir uptake in primary visual, auditory, motor, and somatosensory isocortices and Braak stage in 155 autopsy-confirmed participants with AD. Flortaucipir uptake was observed starting at Braak stage V, with visual and auditory isocortices showing greater and faster increases in uptake than somatosensory and motor; age and APOE ε4 influenced uptake. Flortaucipir uptake and change in primary isocortices were similar in the lateral temporal cortex but different in the entorhinal cortex. Findings suggest that tau deposition in primary isocortices in AD occurs earlier than currently emphasized, although there are differences among them. Given these findings, clinical correlations of primary isocortical involvement in AD need to be evaluated.

articles.title: Procedural circulatory support-enabled intracoronary cell delivery in advanced dilated cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Advanced heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) has limited treatment options. Although intracoronary autologous cell therapy may improve cardiac function, its use in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction is limited by procedural risk. This exploratory study investigated whether temporary mechanical circulatory support with an Impella device could enable safer therapy delivery. Twenty patients with DCM and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≤35% received granulocyte colony-stimulating factor pretreatment followed by Impella-supported intracoronary infusion of autologous bone marrow mononuclear cells. The procedure was feasible, well tolerated, and not associated with major complications. After three months, mean LVEF increased by 2.9%, with numerically greater gains in those with more severe baseline impairment. Participants also experienced symptomatic, exercise capacity, and quality of life improvements. Changes in microvascular function and circulating soluble receptor for advanced glycation end-products (sRAGE) suggested potential mechanistic pathways. As a single-arm study, these findings are hypothesis generating and support further evaluation in randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Impact of depth-of-interaction and spatially-variant point-spread-function model on the performance of ultra-high resolution brain PET.
articles.abstract: Objective.To implement a spatially-variant point spread function (VarPSF) model for the NeuroEXPLORER (NX) brain positron emission tomography (PET) scanner in the open-source Yale Reconstruction Toolkit for PET, and investigate the interplay between depth-of-interaction (DOI) resolution and resolution modeling.Approach.PSF parameters were estimated from simulated and physically measured point sources. Three primary DOI configurations were evaluated: eight-layer DOI (8DOI), two-layer DOI (2DOI), and no DOI (noDOI), with an additional 4DOI comparison in the off-center simulated Derenzo study. Reconstructions using VarPSF, a spatially-invariant PSF measured at the field-of-view center (SinglePSF), and no PSF modeling (noPSF) were assessed using simulated Derenzo and brain phantoms, a physical Derenzo phantom, and one non-human primate (NHP) scan.Main results.In simulated and physical Derenzo studies, VarPSF yielded higher peak-to-valley ratios than SinglePSF and noPSF at the final evaluated iterations, with pronounced gains at large radial offsets. In the simulated brain phantom, VarPSF reduced the estimated transverse blur by 0.3 mm relative to SinglePSF and 0.5 mm relative to noPSF in 2DOI, and by 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm, respectively, in noDOI. In the NHP study, VarPSF improved contrast and structural delineation with reduced DOI encoding at approximately matched white-matter coefficient of variation, while its incremental benefit over SinglePSF was small with 8DOI at clinically relevant iteration settings.Significance.Spatially-variant PSF modeling can partially compensate for limited DOI information. The findings motivate combining modest DOI capability with accurate resolution modeling, while further validation is required for redesigned detectors and fully corrected acquisitions. The open-source implementation enables controlled investigation of the complementary roles of DOI encoding and resolution modeling.

articles.title: A biomaterials roadmap from retinoic acid biology to kidney regenerative therapy.
articles.abstract: The mammalian kidney cannot generate new nephrons after birth, a key driver of chronic kidney disease progression toward end-stage renal disease. Retinoic acid (RA) is an evolutionarily conserved morphogen essential for kidney development, and its signaling is reactivated after injury to coordinate repair-yet this endogenous repair program is transient and insufficient to guide the kidney along the regenerative continuum toward de novo nephron formation. Despite its regenerative potential, RA's clinical translation is limited by systemic toxicity, a narrow therapeutic window, and poor pharmacokinetics. Here, we synthesize evidence from developmental biology and injury models showing that RA can activate endogenous renal progenitor programs. We then analyze its pharmacological and toxicity barriers and introduce a developmental bioinspiration framework using renal-targeted nanocarriers and multifunctional scaffolds to overcome these obstacles. By recapitulating native RA signaling dynamics, these platforms aim to steer the adult kidney away from maladaptive fibrosis and toward functional restoration.

articles.title: Metabolic reprogramming in diabetic panvascular disease: Molecular mechanism and therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus substantially increases the risk of cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, retinal and peripheral vascular complications. These are collectively referred to as diabetic panvascular disease. A traditional approach that treats each complication separately is no longer sufficient. An emerging framework places metabolic reprogramming at its center. This review examines how the diabetic environment, including hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia, rewires core metabolic pathways in vascular cells. Major changes include the diversion of glucose through the polyol, hexosamine and AGE-PKC axes, lipotoxicity resulting from excessive fatty acids, disruption of amino acid networks such as BCAA and one-carbon metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction with increased mtROS production, and epigenetic modifications that drive metabolic memory. These interconnected abnormalities promote oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, which in turn lead to endothelial dysfunction, atherosclerosis, microvascular rarefaction, and end-organ damage in the heart, brain, kidney, retina, and peripheral nerves. We also describe the current therapeutic landscape, ranging from established agents such as metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, RAAS blockers, and anti-VEGF therapies to emerging mechanism-based strategies including aldose reductase inhibitors, glucokinase activators, PKC, RAGE, NOX, and NLRP3 inhibitors, miRNA modulators, and exosome therapy. Finally, we highlight unmet needs and future directions. These may include multi-omics guided precision phenotyping, cross-organ causal inference, single-cell metabolic flux technologies, and adaptive clinical trial designs. By shifting from a glucose-centric to a metabolic reprogramming-centric paradigm, this review aims to provide a roadmap for developing more targeted therapies for diabetic panvascular disease.

articles.title: Niche-specific immune and microbial signatures across the healthy upper respiratory tract mucosa.
articles.abstract: Host-microbe interactions in the upper respiratory tract (URT) niches that form the first line of defense against respiratory infections are incompletely understood. We profiled immune and microbial features using minimally invasive samples from 44 healthy adults (20-65 years), including nasopharyngeal (NPS), oropharyngeal (OPS), and mid-turbinate nasal swabs (MTSs), mucosal lining fluid (MLF), and saliva. Multiplex cytokine and antibody assays, 16S rRNA sequencing, and pathogen detection by PCR were performed. Immune and microbial profiles differed by niche: nasal samples showed consistently higher antiviral cytokine levels and Corynebacterium dominance. Oral samples had greater microbial diversity with distinct cytokine and antibody patterns. Saliva and MLF had the highest antibody concentrations, predominantly IgA. Integrated analyses identified site-specific microbe-immune associations. These findings show the feasibility of non-invasive, integrated profiling to uncover compartment-specific host-microbe relationships, providing a scalable framework for respiratory mucosal immunology and microbiome research with applications in infection surveillance and vaccine evaluation.

articles.title: Nomogram for Poor 3-Month Functional Recovery After Total Knee Arthroplasty Using Cartilage Damage and Synovial Fluid Biomarkers: Development and Internal Evaluation.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate a multidimensional nomogram incorporating intraoperative cartilage damage and perioperative synovial fluid biomarkers to estimate the probability of poor functional recovery at 3 months after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). A retrospective cohort of 360 patients undergoing primary unilateral TKA was included in this study. Interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α, cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP), and total BDNF were measured in perioperative synovial fluid specimens collected after induction of anesthesia and before skin incision and were assessed together with intraoperative Outerbridge cartilage damage grade and routinely available demographic and clinical variables. The primary outcome was functional recovery at 3 months, defined by the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) function subscale. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for predictor selection, and a nomogram was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Six predictors were retained in the final model: age, body mass index, preoperative WOMAC function score, Outerbridge grade, log(IL-6), and log(COMP). The nomogram showed promising discrimination in the held-out internal test set (AUC = 0.861, 95% CI: 0.782-0.934) and acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p = 0.45). Bootstrap optimism correction yielded a bias-corrected AUC of 0.842. DCA suggested potential net benefit across the evaluated threshold probabilities. The nomogram integrates clinical characteristics, intraoperative cartilage damage, and perioperative synovial fluid biomarkers to estimate the probability of poor functional recovery at 3 months after TKA. It should be regarded as a development-stage perioperative prediction model that requires prospective external validation before any clinical application.

articles.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, showing that the identified host metabolic regulators reduce the intracellular survival of wild-type H37Rv. Next, we constructed a host-pathogen protein interaction network that linked them to 9 Mtb proteins. Among them, mce3E, fadA2, and ptpA were identified through knockdown (KD) experiments as host-response modulators that favor pathogen growth. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses revealed their underlying molecular mechanisms. This was evaluated experimentally by modulating the corresponding host metabolic regulators, thereby restoring intracellular growth defects in Mtb KD strains and uncovering previously unrecognized host-pathogen survival mechanisms. Exogenous PGE2 treatment further suppressed intracellular bacterial survival.

articles.title: Protective IFIH1 variant reduces islet stress and dysfunction in a type 1 diabetes genetic background.
articles.abstract: Genome-wide association studies have identified IFIH1, which encodes the double-stranded RNA sensor MDA5, as a type 1 diabetes (T1D) risk locus. The IFIH1 E627∗ variant is associated with protection from T1D, whereas A946T is associated with increased risk. To examine how these variants influence islet responses to inflammatory and viral stress, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to engineer E627∗ or A946T into human pluripotent stem cells from a T1D donor and differentiated them into stem cell-derived islets (SC-islets). SC-islets were exposed to IFNα, poly(I:C), or coxsackievirus B3 and analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays. E627∗ SC-islets compared to A946T displayed reduced inflammatory and stress responses with lower apoptosis, viral burden, mitochondrial dysfunction, and insulin secretory impairment. These findings support a protective role for IFIH1 E627∗ in human islet responses to inflammatory and viral stress and provide insight into genetic mechanisms potentially linked to T1D pathogenesis.

articles.title: Towards artificial intelligence based preoperative dosimetry for liver90Y selective internal radiation therapy.
articles.abstract: Objective.Selective internal radiation therapy delivers Y-90 microspheres through the hepatic arterial system to achieve tumoricidal absorbed dose while limiting normal-tissue irradiation. Current pre-treatment dosimetry requires angiography and 99 mTc-MAA imaging, resulting in an invasive and resource-intensive workflow. This study evaluates the feasibility of estimating post-therapy Y-90 dose distribution directly from diagnostic multiphasic CT using an automated deep-learning pipeline, without requiring angiography or surrogate-particle imaging.Approach.In 152 treatments from the multicenter PROACTIF registry, arterial- and portal-phase CT, together with clinically documented perfusion territories and injected activities, were processed through automated segmentation, rigid registration, differential CT generation, and a generative model synthesizing a PET-like Y-90 activity map. Absorbed-dose maps were computed using the Local Dose Deposition method, and predictive accuracy was assessed using tumor dose-volume metrics and voxelwise spatial agreement.Main results.For the best-performing configuration, the median tumor D70 error was 23 Gy, with substantial inter-patient variability reflecting the challenges of CT-only dose prediction. High-dose coverage (V200) showed a similar pattern. In contrast, spatial agreement was consistently strong, with perfused-volume gamma passing rates around 93% and tumor-level rates around 85%, indicating that the macro-scale distribution of microspheres can be approximated from diagnostic CT. The full pipeline was fully automated and produced predictive dosimetry in under30 S. Significance.Pre-angiography CT contains exploitable information about arterial enhancement and perfusion patterns that enables feasible CT-only prediction of Y-90 spatial distribution. While tumor-level absorbed-dose metrics remain variable, the strong spatial agreement suggests potential utility as an early planning tool to support patient selection or guide catheterization strategy prior to angiography.

articles.title: T2T-CHM13 reference genome reduces mapping bias and enhances alignment accuracy at disease-associated variants.
articles.abstract: The T2T-CHM13v2.0 reference genome added previously uncharacterized genomic sequences and improved the accuracy of repetitive stretches compared to former human genome assemblies. By comprehensive allelic variation analysis and read mapping statistics from sequencing reads aligned to hg38 and T2T-CHM13 assemblies in samples encompassing different sequencing designs, we observed that T2T-CHM13v2.0 assembly significantly reduces the reference mapping bias (RMB) and increases read mapping precision at clinically relevant sites, including BRCA1 pathogenic variants. We report the presence of sequence dissimilarities among reference genomes in the proximity of ClinVar annotated variants, suggesting the need for data re-analysis. Analyzing DNA sequencing data from cancer patients, we identified a mean 2.3% increase in variant allelic frequency (VAF) and 0.3% increase in coverage over clinically relevant variants for samples aligned to T2T-CHM13 compared to hg38. Overall, these findings support the implementation of T2T-CHM13 reference for the improvement of sequencing data analyses in the clinical genomic setting.

articles.title: Auditory associative learning drives synaptic responses in tail of the striatum spiny projection neurons.
articles.abstract: The association of cues with the absence or presence of danger is crucial to survival. The synaptic changes that enable association with the absence of danger are unknown, but a role for the tail of the striatum (TS) has been implicated. To investigate this, we conditioned mice to associate a contextual environment with the threat of foot-shock, which led to freezing, and a sound cue (CS) with the absence of shock, which suppressed contextual freezing. After learning, the CS strongly activated SPNs relative to controls, including a large direct pathway (dSPN) calcium response to sound onset that persisted during anesthesia. In the brain slices of conditioned mice, dSPNs exhibited enhanced synaptic responses to auditory thalamic inputs, with higher NMDA and AMPA receptor-mediated responses, decreased GABAergic inputs, and increased density of dendritic spines. Thus, auditory association with the absence of danger involves enhancement of TS synaptic responses to the associated sound.

articles.title: A randomized crossover study of cardiologist reporting of severe aortic stenosis with/without assistance from artificial intelligence (AI).
articles.abstract: Inaccurate echocardiographic diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis (AS) may be improved by AI. A randomised case-control fully-crossed, paired-reader, paired-case (MRMC) study evaluated the performance of AI in assisting cardiologist reporting of severe AS. 200 echos were independently adjudicated by expert cardiologists, 100 with severe AS (cases) and 100 without severe AS (controls). The AI was then applied and correctly classified all (100%) cases of severe AS, and 18 (36%) of moderate AS with signs of cardiac damage. Five independent cardiologists reported all echos according to the MRMC protocol. Without AI, cardiologists frequently misdiagnosed low-gradient severe AS. With AI, AS diagnosis rates were not improved, but AI improved reader concordance, referral for further investigation and reporting time. Cardiologists frequently misdiagnose low gradient severe AS, whereas measurement AI showed excellent accuracy. Lack of improvement in cardiologist accuracy with AI assistance highlights opportunities to improve trust in AI.

articles.title: Herbivory disrupts invasion-associated phyllosphere and arthropod community shifts in grasslands.
articles.abstract: Biological invasions and changing herbivore communities can jointly reshape grassland ecosystems by altering vegetation structure, microclimate, microbial communities, and trophic interactions. We examined these effects in temperate Australian grassy woodlands dominated by kangaroo grass (Themeda triandra) and invaded by African lovegrass (Eragrostis curvula). Across six livestock-grazed farms, we established nested herbivore-exclusion treatments (open, livestock excluded, and all mammals excluded) in paired subsites dominated by kangaroo grass or co-dominated by African lovegrass. We measured microclimate, biomass, foliar damage, and characterized microbial phyllosphere and arthropod communities. The results revealed that African lovegrass invasion and herbivore exclusion independently and interactively reduced phyllosphere diversity, while concurrently increasing litter and lowering surface temperatures. Herbivore exclusion reorganized vegetation structure and invertebrate community composition, while shifting fungal infection profiles in ways that disproportionately affected the native grass. These results suggest that native mammals and livestock can partially buffer invasion-associated changes in ecosystem structure and biotic interactions.

articles.title: Single nucleus RNA sequencing identifies PLXNA4 upregulation in end-stage arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is a rare genetic form of heart disease often caused by mutations in desmosomal proteins. We carried out single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on 11 non-failing and 8 ARVC patient right ventricular samples and transcriptionally profiled 139,347 nuclei. We identified over 4,400 differentially expressed protein-coding genes between non-failing and ARVC samples across cell types. When compared to dilated, hypertrophic, and ischemic cardiomyopathy, we found that end-stage ARVC is transcriptionally similar to other forms of end-stage heart failure. Despite broad transcriptional similarities, we identified seven cardiomyocyte genes and six fibroblast genes that were uniquely dysregulated in ARVC and validated PLXNA4 as a gene with uniquely increased expression in cardiomyocytes in ARVC compared to other cardiomyopathies. Overexpression of PLXNA4 in hiPSC-derived ventricular cardiomyocytes induced immune response gene expression, suppressed calcium signaling, and altered cardiomyocyte electrophysiology, suggesting PLXNA4 may contribute to these pathways in ARVC.

articles.title: Breath acetone changes in decompensated heart failure patients on inotropes.
articles.abstract: Early assessment of treatment response in patients with decompensated heart failure (HF) requiring inotropic support remains challenging. Exhaled breath acetone, a noninvasive marker of ketone body metabolism, may reflect dynamic metabolic changes associated with clinical status. We aimed to evaluate short-term temporal changes in exhaled breath acetone levels following inotropic therapy in patients with decompensated HF. This is a prospective, single-center observational study including patients with HF requiring inotropic therapy. Exhaled breath acetone levels were measured in decompensated HF patients requiring inotropic support using a previously described noninvasive device at hospital admission and within 48 h. The analysis was performed by spectrophotometry after reaction with salicylaldehyde. Ninety-seven patients were enrolled. Baseline median exhaled breath acetone concentration at admission was 7.75 (3.90-12.27)µg l-1and decreased to 2.15 (1.10-4.19)µg l-1after 48 h of inotrope initiation (p< 0.001 for within-patient comparison). This reduction was accompanied by clinical improvement in signs of HF decompensation and occurred in patients with or without type 2 diabetes, although the magnitude of this reduction was greater in patients without diabetes (p= 0.001). Elevated exhaled breath acetone levels were observed in patients with decompensated HF and decreased after initiation of inotropic therapy, paralleling clinical improvement. These findings are hypothesis-generating and larger prospective studies may confirm the potential role of exhaled breath acetone in clinical decision-making.

articles.title: A Geometry-Aware Bio-Inspired Sparse Reservoir With Online Learning.
articles.abstract: This article presents a cortically motivated framework for geometry-aware sparse reservoir computing with efficient online readout adaptation. The architecture is based on FitzHugh-Nagumo units coupled through sparse connectivity motifs informed by cortical statistics (reciprocity, triadic closure, and Dale's law), resulting in a structured and biologically plausible recurrent matrix. The readout weights are trained by means of an anchor-proximal ridge objective applied to streaming time windows, ensuring temporally stable online learning with a low memory footprint. It presents the results of numerical experiments on a temporal decision-making benchmark and an image-based long-range segmentation task. The proposed sparse reservoir, combined with the windowed proximal readout, is shown to achieve competitive accuracy while substantially reducing recurrent and state-storage requirements. A favorable trade-off of biological plausibility, predictive performance, and computational efficiency is thereby demonstrated.

articles.title: Assessing the effect of chemotherapy dose reductions and time delay on event-free survival in Ewing Sarcoma: A retrospective analysis of the Euro Ewing 2012 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment adjustments are commonly implemented during chemotherapy to mitigate toxicity, but their impact on event-free survival (EFS) remains poorly understood. This study aims to evaluate the causal effect of dose reductions and time delay during the VDC/IE induction regimen (vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide, alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide) on EFS in patients with Ewing Sarcoma.

METHODS: Chemotherapy administration data from the Euro Ewing 2012 (EE2012) trial were used to emulate a target trial, where the target exposures were a binary indicator for total dose reduction and a measure of continuous time delay in treatment duration. Propensity score methods were applied to the original EE2012 population to create a target pseudo-population in which treatment adjustments could be regarded as if randomized. A Cox marginal structural model was fitted to the pseudo-population, and EFS benefit compared to the reference strategy (no reduction; no delay) was estimated for different treatment-adjustment profiles, along with bootstrap confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Dose reduction was found protective for EFS (HR=0.69; 95%CI: [0.39; 1.24]), whereas time delay showed a slightly detrimental effect (HR=1.02; 95%CI: [0.90; 1.15]), both non-statistically significant. In terms of EFS benefits, dose reduction exhibited a favourable trajectory over time, while a mild trend toward a clinical disadvantage was observed as time delay increased. Results provide no evidence that reductions in dose and delays to administration, when implemented according to protocol, have a significant detrimental effect on EFS outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings provide reassurance that treatment adjustments for toxicity management do not substantially compromise patient prognosis.

articles.title: 70-gene signature MammaPrint for early-stage HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer: Outcome in the MINDACT trial for key clinical-pathological high-risk subgroups.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) can be safely omitted in patients above 50 years of age with stage I-II hormone receptor positive (HR+) HER2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer and a low-risk 70-gene signature (MammaPrint®). However, the contribution of the 70-gene signature in high-risk subgroups by nodal involvement, grade 3 or larger tumors, has not been reported, which may complicate clinical decision making for these patients.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients above 50 years enrolled in the MINDACT trial with primary stage I-II HR + HER2- breast cancer and a clinical high/genomic low-risk were selected for this exploratory analysis. In the MINDACT trial, these patients were randomized at enrollment based on their risk assessment method for the decision to receive ACT or not. Eight-year distant metastasis free survival (DMFS) was the primary endpoint.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 8.7 years. Of the 868 clinical high/genomic low-risk MINDACT patients, 490 (56.5%) patients had tumors larger than 2 cm, 232 (26.7%) had grade 3 tumors and 406 (46.8%) had 1-3 involved lymph nodes. 8-year DMFS in the no ACT group was 87.9% (95%CI: 82.9-91.6%) in patients with tumors larger than 2 cm; 91.3% (95%CI: 84.0-95.4%) with grade 3 tumors and 89.6% (95%CI: 84.2-93.3%) with nodal involvement.
