Participants underwent magnetic resonance spectroscopy scans at 3 tesla during which they were clamped at 150, 225, or 300 mg/dL before and after exposure to three 2-hour HG (target = 50 mg/dL) clamps over 2 days between December 2020 and June 2023. The primary metabolite of interest was glucose. Brain glucose transport kinetics were measured in the hypothalamus (HTL) and prefrontal cortex (PFC) during hyperglycemic clamps using reversible symmetric Michaelis-Menten model.

RESULTS: Brain glucose transport kinetics measured during hyperglycemic clamps was not different before vs after exposure to recurrent HG clamps.

CONCLUSION: Short-term exposure to recurrent HG does not upregulate glucose transport kinetics in the setting of T1D.

articles.title: Granulocyte-derived Resistin Inhibits Monocyte Maturation and Promotes an Immunosuppressive Phenotype in Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia Monocytes.
articles.abstract: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) is a hematological neoplasm characterized by expansion of malignant monocytes. However, as a stem cell neoplasm, the disease clone comprises most blood lineages, including granulocytes. To investigate their pathogenic contribution, we performed extensive phenotypic, transcriptomic and functional characterization of CMML granulocytes. These cells exhibited reduced granularity and impaired maturation, the latter of which is associated with poor prognosis. Functionally, CMML granulocytes displayed reduced phagocytic capacity and impaired NETosis, together with aberrant gene expression programs. Notably, RETN, encoding the chemokine resistin, was uniquely upregulated in CMML granulocytes. Accordingly, resistin levels were 10-fold higher in CMML plasma, correlating with inferior survival. Ex vivo exposure to resistin directly blocked monocyte maturation and macrophage differentiation, partly via TLR4 interaction, recapitulating the classical monocytosis repartitioning phenotype that characterizes CMML. Resistin-treated monocytes upregulated gene signatures related to immune suppression and myeloid-derived suppressor cell phenotype. Consistent with these findings, CMML patients displayed higher Treg proportions and Th2/Th1 ratios. Furthermore, we demonstrated that resistin directly skews the Th2/Th1 ratio via binding to monocytes. Thus, CMML granulocytes produce high levels of resistin, which contributes to defective monocyte maturation and induction of myeloid-derived suppressor cell features in monocytes, thereby fostering an immune-suppressive state in this disease.

articles.title: [A multicenter study on the risk factors for in-hospital mortality in neonates with severe asphyxia at tertiary hospitals in Henan Province].
articles.journal: Zhongguo dang dai er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of contemporary pediatrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To construct a risk prediction model for in-hospital mortality in neonates with severe asphyxia.

METHODS: A total of 836 neonates with severe asphyxia admitted to 20 tertiary hospitals in Henan Province between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively enrolled and divided into a death group (n=267) and a survival group (n=569) according to outcome. Birth characteristics, resuscitation measures, and early complications were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify risk factors, and a nomogram prediction model was developed. Receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate the model's discrimination, calibration accuracy, and clinical applicability.

RESULTS: Multivariable logistic regression showed that high lactate level, low birth weight, a 5-minute Apgar score of ≤5, use of epinephrine, volume expansion during resuscitation, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, pulmonary hemorrhage, shock, and grade III/IV intraventricular hemorrhage were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality in neonates with severe asphyxia (P<0.05). The nomogram based on these risk factors yielded an area under the curve of 0.795 (95%CI: 0.762-0.827). Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated that the model had high accuracy and good clinical applicability.

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality among severely asphyxiated neonates is closely associated with birth weight, resuscitation modalities, and early complications such as pulmonary hemorrhage and shock. The risk model constructed based on these factors shows good predictive value.

articles.title: [Guideline for intervention and rehabilitation in children with autism spectrum disorder (2026 edition)].
authors: National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China
articles.journal: Zhongguo dang dai er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of contemporary pediatrics
articles.abstract: On September 22, 2026, the National Health Commission released the "Guideline for intervention and rehabilitation in children with autism spectrum disorder (2026 edition)". The guideline applies to intervention and rehabilitation services for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) under 18 years of age. It establishes eight basic principles, namely early intervention, individualized intervention, comprehensive intervention, evidence-based practice, long-term and high-intensity intervention, primary-level care as the mainstay, family participation, and social inclusion and support, and specifies that the optimal treatment window is before 6 years of age and that intervention should be provided for at least 20 hours per week. It covers health education, intervention for developmental deficits, intervention for challenging behaviors, family intervention, digital and intelligent intervention and rehabilitation, and follow-up.

articles.title: [Application of Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction technique in chronic limb wounds following popliteal artery injury].
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effectiveness of Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction combined with debridement and dressing changes in the treatment of chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 24 patients with chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury who were admitted between January 2023 and June 2025 and met the selection criteria. There were 15 males and 9 females, aged 24-79 years (mean, 52.6 years). Causes of injury included traffic accident injury in 16 cases, mechanical injury in 6 cases, and fall from height in 2 cases. The time from injury to revascularization ranged from 4 to 16 hours (mean, 9.6 hours). There were 29 wounds in total, with wound sizes ranging from 3 cm×2 cm to 12 cm×9 cm. Among them, 18 wounds in 16 patients were persistent chronic wounds after injury, and 11 wounds in 8 patients were recurrent muscle liquefaction wounds after healing of the limb soft tissue. Wound reconstruction was performed sequentially using debridement, continuous dressing changes, Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction, and other methods. The external fixation configuration for soft-tissue distraction was individually assembled according to wound location and morphology. Wound healing, limb salvage rate, complications, and limb functional recovery were observed.

RESULTS: Of the 29 wounds in 24 patients, 28 ultimately healed, with a healing rate of 96.6%. Limb salvage was successful in 23 patients, with a limb salvage rate of 95.8%; 1 patient underwent amputation due to severe ischemic necrosis of the limb caused by thrombosis, with an amputation rate of 4.2%. All patients were followed up 12-29 months (mean, 24.1 months); 17 had more than 2 years of follow-up. The Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) score was 58-85 (mean, 72.4); Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) score was 32-68 (mean, 58.6). Twenty-two patients recovered two-point discrimination (range, 10-40 mm), and 2 patients recovered protective sensation.

CONCLUSION: Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction technique combined with debridement and dressing changes can effectively promote the healing of chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury, improve the limb salvage rate and limb function, representing a feasible treatment strategy.

articles.title: [Interpretation of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Expert Consensus on Robotic-assisted Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: From precise execution to individualized decision-making].
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract: In 2026, the Arthroplasty Society in Asia (ASIA) published the Asia-Pacific Expert Consensus on Robotic-assisted Hip and Knee Arthroplasty, comprising 18 consensus statements. The corresponding author of this article participated in the whole process of consensus formulation. This article interprets the main recommendations according to total knee arthroplasty (TKA), total hip arthroplasty (THA), and unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). For TKA, robotic assistance improves the accuracy of bone resection, implant positioning, and alignment, and provides quantitative support for individualized alignment and pre-resection soft-tissue balancing; however, optimal alignment and balancing targets and their long-term clinical benefits remain uncertain. For THA, robotic assistance improves acetabular cup positioning and reconstruction of limb length and offset. Current evidence does not indicate an increased risk of infection, but reductions in dislocation or revision have not been demonstrated, and functional planning requires further validation. For UKA, robotic assistance reduces technical variation, and some clinical studies and registry data suggest possible improvements in functional outcomes and revision risk, although interpretation is influenced by patient selection and platform differences. Safe implementation also depends on structured training, the ability to troubleshoot and convert safely when necessary, and platform-specific long-term registries. Future studies should clarify which patients are most likely to benefit, what reconstruction targets should be selected, and whether technical precision translates into durable clinical value.

articles.title: [Interpretation of the 2026 Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO) International Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Nontraumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head].
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract: Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) predominantly affects young and middle-aged adults and carries a high risk of disability. Substantial variations exist in diagnostic and treatment strategies worldwide, and unified evidence-based standards have been lacking. In April 2026, the Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO) published the first international multidisciplinary evidence-based clinical practice guideline for nontraumatic ONFH. Using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, the guideline formulated 12 standardized recommendations for diagnosis and treatment. One of the authors participated throughout the guideline-development process as a member of the Chinese working group. This article interprets all 12 recommendations and compares international and Chinese diagnostic and treatment strategies in the context of existing Chinese guidelines and clinical practice. It also examines limitations in the available evidence and proposes approaches for implementing the recommendations in China, thereby providing an evidence-based reference for standardized staging, hip-preserving treatment, and individualized decision-making between joint preservation and arthroplasty for patients with nontraumatic ONFH.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes as early indicators of long-term maternal atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) - including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preterm birth, and fetal growth deviations - are emerging female-specific cardiovascular risk factors, but their association with long-term maternal atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between APOs and subsequent AF.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Scopus. We included population-based cohort studies comparing women with and without APOs and reporting incident maternal AF during follow-up. Time-to-event associations were synthesized, pooling hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95 % confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: 12 population-based cohort studies including over 11 million women were analyzed. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were associated with higher long-term risk of AF (HR 1.50; 95 % CI 1.38-1.62), as was preeclampsia (HR 1.45; 95 % CI 1.23-1.71). Preterm birth was also associated with increased AF risk (HR 1.29; 95 % CI 1.13-1.48). Delivery of a large for gestational age infant was associated with higher AF risk (HR 1.23; 95 % CI 1.13-1.34), whereas small for gestational age delivery showed an inverse association (HR 0.88; 95 % CI 0.80-0.97). For GDM, the association was more uncertain, with wide CIs and effect estimates suggesting an increased risk (HR 1.20; 95 % CI 0.84-1.72).

CONCLUSION: Hypertensive and vascular pregnancy complications are associated with elevated long-term maternal AF risk. Associations for gestational diabetes and fetal growth phenotypes were heterogeneous and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support APOs as markers of later arrhythmic vulnerability.

articles.title: Rare-earth-free magnesium-zinc alloy with controlled biodegradation and biocompatibility for novel biodegradable metallic stent.
articles.abstract: Biodegradable magnesium (Mg) alloy stents offer a transient alternative to permanent metallic implants; however, clinically used WE43 contains rare-earth (RE) elements, raising concerns regarding the long-term biosafety of RE-containing degradation products and their potential tissue accumulation. Here, we investigated two RE-free Mg-Zinc (Zn)-based alloys, MZ01 (Mg-1Zn-0.1Ca) and ZM115 (Mg-1Zn-1.5Mn-0.5Sr), and established a mechanistic cascade linking alloy composition and microstructure to electrochemical analyses revealed alloy-dependent differences in grain structure and interfacial corrosion resistance, with MZ01 exhibiting the highest charge-transfer resistance. In a mouse subcutaneous model, MZ01 showed more uniform degradation, smaller and more rapidly resolving hydrogen gas cavities, and a significantly lower microcrack area fraction at Day 56 than WE43 and ZM115, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory and fibrotic responses. In the rabbit iliac arteries, all stents maintained luminal patency without thrombosis through 56 days, while MZ01 exhibited lower neointimal thickness, lower perivascular apoptosis and late inflammation, and enhanced early endothelialization compared with WE43. Preliminary descriptive porcine coronary implantation further demonstrated the technical feasibility and sustained patency of MZ01 over 56 days. Collectively, these findings define a composition-microstructure-corrosion-cellular response-vascular healing axis and identify MZ01 as a RE-free Mg-Zn alloy with controlled biodegradation and favorable biocompatibility, supporting its further development as a biodegradable cardiovascular scaffold.

articles.title: Twenty Years at the Crossroads: Is Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Science, Procedure, or Both?
Genomic, clinical, and radiological characterization of spontaneous cervical artery dissections: Findings from a single-center cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The pathogenesis of spontaneous cervical artery dissection (sCeAD) remains incompletely understood. In this study, we performed a comprehensive clinical and radiological characterization of sCeAD patients and investigated rare variants in genes associated with vascular fragility using next-generation sequencing (NGS).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: From January 2021 to February 2025, we enrolled consecutive adult with sCeAD evaluated at the Neurology Department of our hospital. Patients presenting at least one feature suggestive of mendelian origin (positive family history, multi-territory vascular abnormalities, dysmorphological features) underwent genetic testing using an NGS panel including 62 genes related to vascular fragility. All patients underwent neurological, dysmorphological examinations and whole-body CT Angiography.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were enrolled (mean age 47.1 ± 10.7 years; 16 women, 55.2%). The internal carotid artery was the most frequently affected vessel by the index dissection (25/29, 86.2%). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in two patients (COL1A1 and MYLK genes; 6.9%). Two patients (6.9%) were heterozygous for likely pathogenic variants associated with autosomal recessive conditions (COL4A3 and TNXB), while rare variants of uncertain significance were detected in 11 patients (37.9%). At least one dysmorphological abnormality was identified in 25/28 patients (89.3%), and multidistrict vascular involvement was observed in 20/29 individuals (69.0%) of our selected cohort of sCeAD patients. Vascular abnormalities beyond the cervicocephalic region were detected in 17 patients (58.6%).

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants considered clinically relevant to the vascular phenotype were identified in two patients of our selected cohort of sCeAD patients (6.9%). Our findings suggest that dysmorphological features and multidistrict vascular involvement may help identify sCeAD patients who are more likely to benefit from genetic testing.

articles.title: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet.

PURPOSE: The present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity.

METHODS: Cerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. VPA (300 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily) was administered within 3 h after reperfusion and continued for 7 days, followed by constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for another week (6 h/day). The ischaemic stroke phenotype was assessed based on neurological deficits, gait, forelimb use, rotarod stay time, reach success and infarct volume. Functional recovery, with associated changes in neural activities, was carried out by analysing the local field potential signals from the first reach success during the reach-to-grasp task on day 8 and day 15 post-stroke. Cortical oscillations were analysed at delta (0-4 Hz), theta (4-8 and 8-12 Hz) and beta (12-20 Hz) during the first reach success.

RESULTS: Combination therapy after ischaemic stroke significantly improved motor and neurological functions compared to monotherapy and vehicle controls. The neural oscillations revealed a significant increase in theta power in the injured motor cortex after combination therapy when compared to that with monotherapy and control groups. The significant increase in the cross-correlation between hemispheres in the combination therapy group over monotherapy indicating an increased synchronised functional connectivity between the injured (left) and uninjured motor (right) cortices. Interestingly, VPA as monotherapy did not significantly reduce infarct volume compared to the vehicle controls. Furthermore, the therapeutic efficacy of monotherapies with VPA and early-onset CIMT (initiated immediately post-stroke) showed limited efficacy in promoting motor and neurological recovery.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, the study demonstrates that VPA combined with physical rehabilitative training (CIMT) enhances functional recovery by enhancing inter-hemispheric functional connectivity and represents a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate persistent post-stroke motor deficits.

articles.title: The relationship between professional quality of life and work alienation among nurses in neonatal intensive care units: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) nurses face substantial psychological challenges. Work alienation - emotional disconnection from work - is a potential occupational concern with limited empirical attention. Left unaddressed, it may be associated with care quality and workforce stability.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate work alienation as an occupational concern and explore its associations with professional quality of life (ProQoL) components: compassion satisfaction (CS), burnout (BO) and secondary traumatic stress (STS), among NICU nurses.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study of 188 nurses from West Bank governmental NICUs used ProQoL and Work Alienation Scales. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation and multiple regression.

RESULTS: Despite the conflict-affected setting, most nurses reported average/low levels of burnout (BO) and secondary traumatic stress (STS), rather than a composite compassion fatigue score.

CONCLUSION: Work alienation is significantly associated with poorer ProQoL. Protecting NICU nurses requires interventions including peer support, restorative supervision and policy reform to sustain staff well-being and care quality.

articles.title: The active self in autism: multisensory and sensorimotor foundations of bodily self-representation.
articles.abstract: The active self, understood as the embodied sense of self arising from goal-directed action and interaction with the environment, is supported by sensorimotor processes including multisensory integration and proprioception. Atypical self-representation in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been proposed to relate to differences in these processes. To clarify this relationship, we conducted a systematic conceptual review of 37 empirical studies published between 2010 and August 2025 examining multisensory and bodily components of the active self in ASD. The literature was synthesized across three themes: (1) multisensory integration, (2) self-bias and self-other differentiation, and (3) motor underpinnings of bodily awareness. Across studies, autistic participants frequently showed differences in multisensory timing and weighting, including reduced or delayed susceptibility to some bodily ownership illusions and greater reliance on proprioceptive or immediate sensory information. Evidence also indicated differences in the flexibility of peri- and interpersonal space, self-other differentiation, agency-related processing, and motor planning and execution. However, findings were not uniform across paradigms, developmental stages, or participant groups, with relatively preserved performance reported under some unimodal or low-noise conditions. Together, these findings support an association between multisensory and sensorimotor processing and several components of bodily self-representation in autism, while substantial methodological and sample heterogeneity limits strong causal or clinical conclusions. Future research should prioritize larger and more representative samples, longitudinal and multimethod designs, standardized experimental paradigms, and objective measures of embodiment to determine whether these mechanisms can ultimately inform individualized assessment and intervention.Clinical trial number Not applicable.

articles.title: Infection or contamination - Clinical attribution of blood culture-positive episodes in neonatal intensive care: an 11-year retrospective single-center study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Positive blood cultures in neonatal intensive care do not necessarily indicate clinically relevant bloodstream infection. Interpretation is particularly challenging for coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), which may represent either contamination or clinically relevant infection depending on the clinical context. We aimed to describe how treating teams attributed culture-positive episodes as infection or contamination in routine neonatal care and to examine which clinical, laboratory, and microbiological features were associated with this original clinical attribution. As a secondary aim, we characterized the local epidemiology of culture-positive episodes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of all culture-positive episodes occurring between 2014 and 2024 in neonates hospitalized in a German tertiary NICU at the time of blood culture sampling. Original clinical attribution was extracted from documentation recorded during the index episode. Descriptive analyses and exploratory logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: Among 3246 blood cultures, 232 (7.1%) were positive. After accounting for additional follow-up and parallel cultures and other exclusions, 189 unique culture-positive episodes remained for analysis; 125 (66.1%) were attributed as infection and 64 (33.9%) as contamination. Thirty-five episodes (18.5%) occurred during the early-onset period and 154 (81.5%) during the late-onset period. Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) were detected in 114 episodes (60.3%) and showed the greatest variability in attribution. All 13 CoNS-positive early-onset episodes were attributed as contamination, whereas 64 of 101 CoNS-positive late-onset episodes (63.4%) were attributed as infection. Enterobacterales, Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Candida spp. were almost uniformly attributed as infection, whereas Bacillus spp. and environmental organisms were predominantly attributed as contamination. In late-onset episodes, maximum CRP showed the strongest association with attribution as infection in univariable and multivariable analyses (adjusted OR 4.41, 95% CI 2.59-7.51). Associations with time-to-positivity, CoNS detection, and central vascular catheter presence were weaker and imprecisely estimated after adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical attribution of culture-positive episodes was associated with the combined consideration of organism plausibility, inflammatory response, time-to-positivity, and clinical context. CoNS-positive late-onset episodes represented the greatest diagnostic uncertainty. These findings describe real-world clinical attribution rather than diagnostic accuracy and underline the need for more reproducible criteria to support antimicrobial stewardship without compromising the treatment of vulnerable neonates.

articles.title: Renal outcome at 2 years in neonates with nephrocalcinosis and bronchopulmonary dysplasia: a case-control study.
Discharge preparation experiences of intergenerational caregivers for premature infants in China's NICU: a qualitative study.
Stakeholder Consensus on Important School-Based Strategies for Increasing Girls' Physical Activity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Girls are less physically active than boys, and school-based physical activity interventions in co-educational settings are often less effective for girls. To help improve the design of these interventions, this study explored which school-based strategies stakeholders consider most important for increasing girls' physical activity.

METHODS: A Delphi study was conducted using 3 rounds of online surveys with stakeholders from 3 groups: academics, school educators, and government representatives. In the first round, participants identified strategies they believed could increase girls' physical activity in schools, and responses were analyzed using thematic analysis to generate a list of strategies. In the second and third rounds, participants rated the importance of these strategies using an 8-point Likert scale; consensus was defined as responses falling within a consecutive 3-point range.

RESULTS: Stakeholders across the 3 groups reached consensus on 19 strategies that emphasized creating inclusive, enjoyable, and empowering environments for girls including approaches, such as supportive school cultures, positive role modeling, safe and welcoming spaces, and opportunities for student voice. Additional areas of agreement differed slightly across groups, with academic and government representatives highlighting system-level and curriculum-related approaches, and school educators and government representatives emphasizing relational practices and operational supports, such as staff well-being and resourcing.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the findings highlight the importance of coordinated, multilevel strategies that combine inclusive teaching practices with broader school and policy support to enhance girls' participation in physical activity, offering guidance for researchers, educators, and policymakers seeking to design and sustain more effective school-based interventions.

articles.title: Efficacy of Lactobacillus reuteri as an adjunctive therapy for seizure control and quality of life in pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy: A prospective interventional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) remains a critical challenge in pediatric neurology, profoundly impacting cognitive development and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). Given the role of the gut-microbiota-brain axis in neuromodulation, probiotics have emerged as a potential adjunctive therapy. This study assessed changes in seizure frequency and HRQOL and evaluated the safety of Lactobacillus reuteri supplementation on seizure frequency and HRQOL in children with DRE.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, before-after interventional trial, 75 children (aged 3-18 years) with confirmed DRE were enrolled. Participants received daily oral L. reuteri (1 ×109 CFU) for 12 weeks alongside their stable anti-seizure medication (ASM) regimens. The primary outcome was HRQOL measured by the Persian-validated QOLCE-55 questionnaire. Secondary outcomes included seizure frequency, recorded prospectively using standardized caregiver seizure diaries. Statistical analyses utilized paired-sample t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with effect sizes calculated to quantify the magnitude of within-participant changes.

RESULTS: Seventy-one patients completed the study (mean age 7.26 ± 3.33 years; 53.5% male). The cohort showed heterogeneous seizure phenotypes and underlying etiologies. Total HRQOL scores increased from 33.75 ± 4.92 at baseline to 34.23 ± 4.97 after the intervention (absolute change, 0.48 points; p < 0.001), with a small-to-moderate standardized effect size (d = 0.40). However, this change was substantially below the 10-13-point MCID range used in the sample-size rationale. Median seizure frequency changed from 32 (IQR: 15-84) to 30 (IQR: 14-80) episodes per 3 months (p = 0.001; r = 0.39). Four patients (5.6%; 95% CI, 1.6-13.8%) experienced a reduction of more than 50% in seizure frequency. Adverse events were reported in 11.3% of participants and were mild and transient, with no treatment discontinuations.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-arm before-after study, statistically significant within-participant changes in HRQOL and seizure frequency were observed during the 12-week period following adjunctive L. reuteri supplementation. However, the absolute magnitude of these changes was modest and their clinical significance remains uncertain. Because there was no concurrent placebo control group, the observed changes cannot be attributed specifically to L. reuteri supplementation. Larger, adequately powered placebo-controlled randomized trials are needed to determine whether L. reuteri provides a clinically meaningful benefit in pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy.

articles.title: Postpartum urinary retention after vaginal birth: incidence and associated risk factors among nulliparous women.
articles.journal: Sexual & reproductive healthcare : official journal of the Swedish Association of Midwives
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum urinary retention (PUR) is a complication following childbirth that may result in bladder overdistension, urinary tract infections, and delayed postpartum recovery. Knowledge regarding clinically significant PUR is limited.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence of postpartum urinary retention requiring an indwelling urinary catheter and to identify associated risk factors among nulliparous women following vaginal birth.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in two Swedish birth units. The study included 1075 nulliparous women; singleton pregnancies, cephalic presentation, ≥37 gestational weeks who gave birth vaginally. PUR was defined as urinary retention requiring an indwelling urinary catheter. Data were extracted from medical records. Differences between women with and without PUR were analysed using descriptive statistics. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors.

RESULTS: The incidence of PUR requiring an indwelling urinary catheter was 5.7%. Women with PUR were more likely to receive epidural analgesia (90.2% vs. 61.2%, p < 0.001), oxytocin augmentation (88.5% vs. 56.7%, p < 0.001), episiotomy (18.0% vs. 5.5%, p < 0.001), and instrumental birth (23.0% vs. 12.3%, p = 0.019). In adjusted analyses, epidural analgesia (aOR 4.01, 95% CI 1.63-9.90), augmentation (aOR 2.87, 95% CI 1.18-6.94), and episiotomy (aOR 3.16, 95% CI 1.43-7.02) remained associated with PUR.

CONCLUSION: PUR requiring an indwelling urinary catheter occurred in approximately one in twenty women after vaginal birth. Epidural analgesia, oxytocin augmentation, and episiotomy were associated with PUR. Early identification of women at increased risk may support targeted postpartum bladder surveillance and help prevent PUR and associated complications.

articles.title: Association between serum transaminase elevations and clinical course in patients with familial Mediterranean fever.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical features, disease course, genetics, and treatment responses of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) patients with elevated serum transaminase levels.

METHODS: The charts of the FMF patients with at least one year of follow-up were retrospectively investigated for the presence of elevated serum transaminase levels. The genetic and clinical findings and disease course of identified patients were compared with a group of FMF patients with no transaminase elevations.

RESULTS: A retrospective chart review included 780 registered patients diagnosed with FMF. Forty-two patients (5.3%) were excluded because of the insufficient follow-up duration, associated viral hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis, and biopsy-proven liver amyloidosis. A total of 83 patients (11.2%) with elevated serum transaminase levels were identified, and their findings were compared with a control group of 655 patients with no transaminase elevation. FMF attacks began at a significantly older age (17.0±12.9 vs. 12.4±9.0 years, p=0.01), and the percentage of patients experiencing more frequent (≥ 3 attacks/month) attacks was higher (35.4% vs. 24.1%, p=0.01) in the elevated transaminase group. No significant differences were observed between the two groups regarding age at diagnosis, delay in diagnosis, presenting features of FMF, CRP levels at baseline and during attacks, frequency of amyloidosis, and the colchicine dose, as well as the frequency of patients requiring anti-IL-1 treatments. The frequency of MEFV gene exon 10 mutations and p.M694V homozygosity did not differ significantly between the groups. Hepatosteatosis was observed by abdominal ultrasonography in 46.7% of the patients with elevated liver enzymes. A follow-up study after 6 years revealed that transaminase levels remained elevated in 21 out of 49 patients (42.9%), and one patient developed liver cirrhosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated serum transaminase levels can be detected in approximately 11.2% of FMF patients, and this finding is not associated with colchicine use or manifestations of FMF. Ultrasonographic evidence of hepatosteatosis was observed in nearly half of the patients. Follow-up analysis showed that serum transaminase elevations may persist in 43% of the patients, which suggests further studies to determine whether this abnormality is a feature of FMF or not.

articles.title: Independent association of the LNG index with extrahepatic metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Extrahepatic metastasis (EHM) indicates a poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study evaluated the association of the logarithmically transformed neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio-gamma-glutamyl transferase index (LNG) with EHM at initial assessment and its incremental discriminative value. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 678 adults with newly diagnosed HCC. LNG was calculated as the natural logarithm of the product of its components. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic and linear regression and restricted cubic splines. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, reclassification, and decision curve analyses. EHM was present in 270 patients (39.8%). The adjusted odds ratio (OR) per unit increase in LNG was 1.25 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.48; p = 0.007). Adjusted spline analysis indicated nonlinearity (p = 0.009). Compared with the lowest tertile, adjusted ORs were 2.45 (95% CI: 1.45-4.17) and 2.59 (95% CI: 1.44-4.69) in the middle and highest tertiles, respectively. LNG yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.748 (95% CI: 0.711-0.785). In an exploratory analysis, the AUC was 0.717 (95% CI: 0.652-0.783) among patients with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels <20 ng/mL. Adding LNG to a baseline model, which included age, sex, tumor size, AFP, multifocality, and cirrhosis, increased the AUC from 0.762 to 0.797 (p < 0.001). This also improved reclassification and led to a greater estimated net benefit. Among patients with EHM, LNG was positively associated with albumin-bilirubin and Controlling Nutritional Status scores and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio. LNG may complement initial EHM assessment in HCC, though external validation is required.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Screen Time and Obesity in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults: Sex-Specific Pathways and Implications for Public Health Interventions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Screen time is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes, including obesity. However, evidence for children and adolescents is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex-specific differences have not been characterized. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on the association between screen time and obesity-related outcomes among children, adolescents, and young adults, with a focus on sex-specific pathways and implications for public health interventions.

METHODS: This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and was based on an a priori protocol. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Data were synthesized based on the direction of associations and patterns of sex differences.

RESULTS: Of the 22 studies included, 18 reported a significant positive association between screen time and obesity-related outcomes. Sex-specific patterns were also observed, with some studies reporting associations only among females (n = 6) or males (n = 4). Among females, observed associations more frequently involved adiposity, metabolically unhealthy obesity, and psychologic factors such as body image concerns and weight dissatisfaction, whereas among males, associations were more often linked to behavioral factors such as increased caloric intake, late-night screen use, and reduced sleep.

CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that screen time is associated with obesity among children, adolescents, and young adults, with evidence suggesting potential sex differences in the behavioral, physiologic, and psychologic mechanisms. These findings highlight the need for interventions that move beyond simple screen time reduction and consider the mechanisms that may underlie sex-related differences in obesity risk. Potential strategies may include promoting physical activity among girls and addressing problematic screen use, screen-related eating, and sleep disruption among boys, as well as integrating screen-related psychosocial factors into obesity prevention and management. Given the limited number of studies formally assessing sex-screen time interactions, further research is needed to better characterize these observed patterns.

articles.title: Geographic Access to Primary Care and Racial and Ethnic Disparities in the Prevalence of Maternal Chronic Conditions 2020-2024.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Unequal access to preventive health care before and between pregnancies contributes to risk for adverse perinatal outcomes. Few studies have examined access to primary care as a contributor to racial and ethnic disparities in chronic disease prevalence among women having a live birth.

METHODS: We linked 2020-2024 natality data with Health Resources and Services Administration's Area Health Resource Files and used spatial Bayesian conditional autoregressive models to estimate county-level associations between geographic access to primary care and prevalence of chronic conditions (obesity, hypertension, and diabetes) in 1,374 counties in the contiguous US. We defined geographic access to primary care using the Health Resources and Services Administration's primary care Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designation and the number of primary care providers per 100,000 persons in quartiles. We assessed racial disparities in outcomes by modeling the difference in rate differences and 95% CIs among non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White women having a live birth, controlling for county characteristics.

RESULTS: Residing in a county designated as a primary care HSPA or with lower rates of density of primary care providers was associated with modestly increased prevalence of obesity and hypertension but not diabetes. However, across the chronic conditions, the disparity between non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White women was generally consistent regardless of geographic access to primary care. For example, the rate difference between the 2 groups for obesity was 11.3 (95% CI, 10.5-12.0) per 100 births for primary care HPSAs and 9.9 (95% CI, 9.5-10.4) per 100 births for non-primary care HPSAs, while the adjusted β for the difference in rate differences was 0.005 (95% CI, -0.005 to 0.014).

CONCLUSION: Geographic access to primary care did not attenuate racial disparities in the prevalence of chronic conditions among women who had a live birth.

articles.title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA.

METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes.

RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium.

CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

articles.title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment.

METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method.

RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency.

CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

articles.title: Strategy and Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) are at high-risk, and retrograde CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is often avoided because of hemodynamic and safety concerns.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated CTO-PCI strategy selection and outcomes according to LVEF, focusing on patients selected for a primary retrograde approach.

METHODS: We analyzed 11,458 patients from the Japanese CTO-PCI Expert Registry (2014-2022), including 1,692 with LVEF <40% and 9,766 with LVEF ≥40%. Core laboratory-adjudicated angiographic findings, procedural strategies, and in-hospital outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Patients with LVEF <40% had more complex coronary anatomy. A primary retrograde approach was selected in 489 of 1,692 procedures (28.9%) in the LVEF <40% group and 2,500 of 9,766 procedures (25.6%) in the LVEF ≥40% group (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.33; P = 0.005). Overall technical and procedural success rates were comparable between groups. In the primary retrograde cohort, technical success was achieved in 450 of 489 procedures (92.0%) with LVEF <40% and 2,186 of 2,494 procedures (87.7%) with LVEF ≥40% (OR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.14-2.37; P = 0.005). In-hospital mortality, stroke, contrast-induced nephropathy, and preprocedural mechanical circulatory support were more frequent in patients with LVEF <40%, whereas other in-hospital adverse events were generally similar.

CONCLUSIONS: Reduced LVEF was associated with more frequent selection of a primary retrograde approach. Among selected patients undergoing primary retrograde CTO-PCI, technical success remained high despite greater anatomical complexity.

articles.title: LDL-Cholesterol Targets Post-ACS and CCS: Why Early Goal Achievement Counts.
Association of Life's Essential 8 With Clonal Hematopoiesis and Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), characterized by clonal expansion of hematopoietic stem cells harboring preleukemic mutations, is an emerging cardiovascular disease risk factor. The American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score is the contemporary standard for quantifying cardiovascular health. However, the interplay between this novel genetic risk factor and classical health metrics remains unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to examine the association between LE8 score and CH prevalence, and determine their joint effects on incident coronary artery disease (CAD).

METHODS: We analyzed 427,295 UK Biobank participants. Exposures included LE8 score and CH (evaluated as a composite and by common drivers: DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1). Associations with CH prevalence and incident CAD over a median 13.6-year follow-up were evaluated using multivariable regression.

RESULTS: CH prevalence was 3.4%. A higher LE8 score was associated with significantly lower odds of CH and examined driver mutations, strongest for ASXL1 (OR: 0.79; 95% CI: 0.75-0.83; P < 0.001). CH significantly modified the protective effect of LE8 on CAD incidence on multiplicative and additive scales. A 1-SD increase in LE8 yielded an adjusted CAD HR of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.70-0.78) in CH carriers vs 0.68 (95% CI: 0.67-0.69) in noncarriers (Pinteraction = 0.005). Participants with ASXL1 CH subtype and low LE8 scores experienced the highest absolute CAD risk (18.7 vs 2.0 events/1,000 person-years in noncarriers with high LE8).

CONCLUSIONS: Optimal cardiovascular health is associated with a lower prevalence of CH. Although maintaining ideal cardiovascular health is associated with lower CAD risk in CH carriers, this protective benefit is attenuated compared with noncarriers.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism During Extended Apixaban Therapy for Cancer-Associated Thrombosis.
Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy: The Importance of Ring-Like Scar Architecture.
Clinical and Metabolic Correlates of Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy in Long-Standing Type 2 Diabetes: A Tertiary-Care Cross-Sectional Study from Eastern India.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a serious and underdiagnosed complication of long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Data from Indian populations evaluating the relationship between somatic and autonomic neuropathy remain limited.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 98 patients with long-standing type 2 diabetes were evaluated at a tertiary-care center in Eastern India. Somatic neuropathy was assessed clinically and electrophysiologically, while autonomic function was evaluated using standard cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests and galvanic skin response (GSR). CAN was staged as possible, definite, or advanced. Clinical and metabolic correlates were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with CAN.

RESULTS: Distal symmetric polyneuropathy was present in 44.9% of patients, and any peripheral neuropathy was present in 59.2%. CAN was highly prevalent, with definite and advanced CAN observed in 28.6% and 46.9%, respectively. Abnormal GSR was noted in 42.9%, and overall diabetic autonomic involvement (defined as the presence of CAN and/or isolated sudomotor dysfunction) was present in 92.9%. Increasing CAN severity was associated with higher hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) ( P = 0.0055), fasting blood glucose ( P = 0.0083), and age ( P = 0.0027), while duration showed a borderline association ( P = 0.0548). HbA1c was the only variable independently associated with CAN after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio ≈ 2.10 per 1% increase). The sustained handgrip test did not demonstrate a significant association with the presence of CAN (χ², P = 0.712), indicating limited discriminatory ability in this cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Autonomic neuropathy, particularly CAN, was highly prevalent in this cohort of patients with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Poorer glycemic control, reflected by higher HbA1c, showed the strongest independent association with CAN. Comprehensive autonomic assessment should be considered even in the absence of overt somatic neuropathy.

articles.title: Immediate versus gradual noninvasive ventilatory pressure-or-duration step-down in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: a randomized trial.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Despite the proven role of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) as an effective treatment for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF) in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), no clear agreement has been reached regarding the ideal weaning strategy. This study aimed to compare three NIV weaning strategies in terms of efficiency and safety among COPD patients with AHRF. A total of 105 COPD patients stabilized on NIV were enrolled in this randomized clinical trial and equally distributed into three groups (n=35 each): duration step-down (group A), pressure step-down (group B), and immediate withdrawal (group C). The primary endpoint was successful weaning within 48 hours. Secondary outcomes included duration of NIV use, lengths of ICU and hospital stay, predictors of weaning failure, and complication rates. The results of this study indicated that successful weaning rates differed significantly among the groups, being highest in group A (82.9%), followed by group B (74.3%), and lowest in group C (54.3%) (p<0.01). Compared with other strategies, immediate withdrawal was associated with higher rates of weaning failure. Although NIV duration was significantly shorter in group C (p<0.001), complication rates and post-discharge outcomes were similar across the three groups. In this trial, gradual duration- and pressure-based step-down strategies were associated with higher rates of successful NIV weaning than immediate withdrawal, with the highest observed success rate in the duration-based step-down group.

articles.title: Evaluation of psychosocial benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with significant symptom burden, impaired quality of life, and psychosocial morbidity. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is a recommended non-pharmacological intervention, but evidence focusing on its psychosocial benefits remains limited. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of hospital-based outpatient PR on psychosocial parameters and health-related quality of life in patients with COPD receiving standard pharmacotherapy. This before-after interventional study included 50 male patients with stable COPD who underwent a structured outpatient PR program for 24 weeks in addition to standard medical therapy. Assessments were performed at baseline, 12 weeks, and 24 weeks. Psychosocial outcomes were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and quality of life was assessed using the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) and the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire-COPD-specific version (SGRQ-C). Statistical analysis was performed with significance set at p<0.05. PR led to significant improvements in psychosocial and quality-of-life outcomes. Mean HADS anxiety and depression scores showed significant reductions at 12 and 24 weeks compared to baseline (p<0.001). Quality-of-life scores improved significantly, with reductions in CAT and SGRQ-C scores at follow-up (p<0.001). A marked reduction in COPD exacerbations and hospital admissions was also observed during the study period. Hospital-based outpatient PR significantly improves psychosocial well-being and health-related quality of life while reducing morbidity in patients with COPD, supporting its routine integration into comprehensive COPD care.

articles.title: A Retrospective Benchmark of Quantitative Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction Tools.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are critical candidates for addressing the global antibiotic resistance crisis. AI-driven quantitative models capable of directly predicting peptide antimicrobial activity, specifically minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), are gaining scientific prominence by providing precise guidance for the rational design of AMPs. To assess their real-world, out-of-the-box performance, we conducted a retrospective benchmark of 10 publicly released quantitative AMP prediction tools spanning classical machine learning and contemporary deep learning approaches. Using an external dataset and reconstructed native datasets, we evaluated absolute MIC regression, retrospective reproducibility, directional prediction patterns, ranking capability, and virtual-screening enrichment. Most released tools exhibited poor absolute MIC regression and limited transferability to the external benchmark, while selected tools retained useful relative-ranking and enrichment capabilities. Retrospective evaluation further revealed marked differences in implementation-level reproducibility among the released tools. Error-stratified analyses identified systematic associations between prediction errors and peptide residue composition, together with a general compression of the predicted activity range. Collectively, these findings characterize the practical performance boundaries of currently accessible quantitative AMP prediction tools and support their use primarily as early-stage screening filters rather than precise substitutes for experimental MIC measurements.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis: preliminary findings from a single-center clinical series of angioplasty and stenting using the Coyote balloon catheter.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data on the clinical efficacy and safety of the Coyote balloon catheter for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) are lacking. This study reports preliminary findings from the first clinical series evaluating this device, with the aim of describing procedural outcomes and 6-month restenosis rates.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 32 patients (39 lesions) who underwent elective endovascular treatment for sICAS at the Interventional Radiology unit of our institution between July 2024 and December 2025. The primary endpoints were acute technical success (successful device delivery, residual stenosis < 50%, and TICI 2b/3 flow) and 30-day procedural success (technical success without 30-day stroke or death). Secondary endpoints included 6-month restenosis and 1-year target-vessel stroke.

RESULTS: The stroke rate during the first month was 5.1% per procedure (6.3% per patient). At 6-month follow-up, restenosis was observed in 7.9% of lesions. Technical success was achieved in 100% of lesions, with all cases obtaining TICI 2b/3 distal perfusion. The mean degree of stenosis significantly decreased from 88.08% preoperatively to 30.12% postoperatively (p < 0.001). The perioperative complication rate was 2.6%. The 30-day procedural success rate was 94.9%, as minor periprocedural strokes occurred in 2 cases (5.1%).

DISCUSSION: This clinical series demonstrates that the Coyote balloon catheter is technically feasible in sICAS with a favorable safety profile. The observed restenosis and stroke rates indicate a viable option for intracranial angioplasty, providing descriptive data for future prospective investigations.

articles.title: Infectious Pancreatic Necrosis in Atlantic Cod (Gadus morhua): Complete Viral Genome Characterization From the First Norwegian Field Case Suggests Cross-Species Transmission.
articles.abstract: We describe the first natural outbreak of infectious pancreatic necrosis (IPN) in farmed Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) in Norway. IPN was originally described in young salmonids, but the greatest losses have historically occurred in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) following sea transfer despite high vaccination coverage. The number of cases fell drastically in Norway after the introduction of IPN virus (IPNV)-resistant QTL-roe and the reduction of 'house strains'. However, recent reports suggest that IPN is re-emerging as an important health challenge in Norwegian aquaculture. Carrier-state infection is documented in many species of fish, molluscs, and crustaceans. Previously, the disease in farmed cod has only been reported from Denmark and the Faroe Islands (1990s). The present case occurred in juveniles in 2024. The main histopathological finding was exocrine pancreatic necrosis, consistent with IPN in salmonids. Viral antigen in lesions was visualized by immunohistochemistry. IPNV infection was confirmed by real-time RT-PCR and virus isolation. Whole-genome sequencing showed that the NVI-066 isolate clustered closely with IPNV strains typically associated with Atlantic salmon, suggesting cross-species transmission, although the source of infection could not be determined. This study demonstrates that clinically relevant IPN can occur in Atlantic cod under field conditions and extends current understanding of IPNV host range, transmission, and disease expression. The findings are particularly relevant for the expanding cod aquaculture industry, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance, biosecurity, and management strategies.

articles.title: Modeling diseased xylem networks.
articles.abstract: Vascular wilt pathogens induce xylem blockages that disrupt plant water transport, posing critical threats to agricultural productivity and food security. Key processes including xylem transport, vessel blockage, and pathogen spread within the xylem remain poorly understood, largely due to our limited ability to internally monitor infected tissues. This review explores how complementary mathematical modeling alongside laboratory studies can elucidate features governing these critical processes. I first provide a brief history of xylem imaging and quantification, highlighting technological advances, and persistent limitations. I then review modeling approaches to describe xylem water transport and pathogen dynamics, emphasizing that different pathogens require fundamentally different modeling frameworks. Existing xylem flow models may provide suitable hydraulic conductivity estimates for healthy stems under idealized conditions; however, they lack explicit representation of pit membranes and lumen-occluding structures, limiting their applicability to diseased stems where these features are actively modified during infection. Previously described biofilm models can replicate bacterial colony growth in controlled experimental settings but are often too complex for integration with flow simulations and rely on parameters that are difficult to quantify experimentally. Finally, I highlight directions and challenges for modeling occlusion and spread at the local scale and discuss how these models might be scaled to network-level architecture. While these types of models remain computationally challenging, advances in multiscale imaging technologies and scaling approaches promise significant progress in the coming decades. Insights from such models stand to advance both our understanding of disease progression and the development of resilient crops for an uncertain climate future.

articles.title: Trends in the Use of Neuraxial vs. General Anaesthesia for Transurethral Resection of the Prostate.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Historically, neuraxial anaesthesia (NA) was preferred for transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) to allow monitoring for TURP syndrome, but modern surgical techniques have largely eliminated this risk. We aimed to characterise trends in anaesthesia utilisation for TURP over a 15-year period and to identify patient factors associated with anaesthetic technique selection.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing primary TURP using the ACS-NSQIP database (2009-2023). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of the use of general anaesthesia (GA) versus NA. Subgroup analyses examined trends by patient health status and age.

RESULTS: Of 73,214 patients identified, GA utilisation increased significantly from 69.9% in 2009 to 88.8% in 2023 (P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, each successive year was associated with a 15% increase in the odds of receiving GA [odds ratio (OR) 1.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.14-1.15]. Black patients (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.47-1.87) had higher odds of GA than white patients, and hispanic patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.38-1.64) had higher odds of GA than non-hispanic patients. Conversely, older age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.84), and diabetes (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.93) were associated with decreased GA use. The shift towards GA was significantly more pronounced among medically complex patients (American Society of Anesthesiologists 3-4) than among less medically complex patients (P=0.005).

CONCLUSION: The anaesthetic management of TURP has evolved over the last 15 years, and GA has further solidified its status as the dominant modality. This evolution likely reflects the diminished risk of TURP syndrome, allowing practice to be driven by airway control and efficiency rather than by historical safety constraints.

articles.title: Trends in Australia's physiotherapy workforce: changes and future implications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Physiotherapists play a vital role in managing and rehabilitating patients across the lifespan who suffer from musculoskeletal diseases and broader health conditions. Yet, there are current and anticipated shortages of physiotherapists being reported in several areas of healthcare where specialized skills are required.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to examine Australia's physiotherapy workforce, describing the demographic profile and trend of the workforce between 2013 and 2023, workforce distribution by state and rurality, workforce comparison between 2013 and 2023, and predictors of practicing in regional, rural, and remote locations in 2023.

METHODS: The National Health Workforce Dataset (NHWDS) was analyzed over an 11-year period. Descriptive statistics were used to describe demographic characteristics. Multinomial regression analysis was used to assess associations between demographic characteristics and rural and remote practice.

RESULTS: Nationally, the number of physiotherapists increased from 21,046 in 2013 to 35,889 in 2023, a 70.5% increase, with a less‑than‑1% change in the distribution of the workforce to rural and remote areas. In 2023, 22,290 (62.1%) of physiotherapists were female, and 3,652 (10.7%) obtained their primary qualification overseas. In 2023, males were 15% less likely to practice in regional centers (vs metropolitan) compared to females [0.85 (0.78-0.92), p < .001]; also, males were less likely to practice in large, medium, and small rural towns as well as remote and very remote areas [0.73 (0.58-0.93), p = .009] compared to females. Physiotherapists aged 45-99 years were more likely to practice in large rural towns; however, they were less likely to practice in remote and very remote areas than those aged 20-34 years. Indigenous physiotherapists were 85% more likely to practice in regional centers [1.85 (1.31-2.61), p < .001] and across large, medium, and small rural towns as well as in remote and very remote areas compared to metropolitan regions, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Analysis of the NHWDS over an 11-year period suggests an ongoing maldistribution of the physiotherapy workforce, with 81.0% practicing in a metropolitan area in 2023. Males were significantly less likely to practice outside metropolitan areas across all locations, whereas Indigenous physiotherapists were significantly more likely to practice outside metropolitan areas across all locations. Strategies focusing on education practices, incentives, and support that would make rural and remote practice more attractive for the workforce are required.

articles.title: A PTPRO inhibitor Pi mitigates endotoxemia-induced encephalopathy-mediated blood-brain barrier disruption through cytoskeletal regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Septic encephalopathy (SE) is closely associated with disruption of blood-brain barrier (BBB), resulting in neurological deficits and poor clinical outcomes. Protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO) regulates disease states by dephosphorylating membrane-associated proteins and modulating intracellular signalling. Here we have examined the role of PTPRO in regulating BBB permeability and have assessed a PTPRO inhibitor (Pi) in mitigating BBB disruption during endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Genetic and pharmacological approaches, including PTPRO overexpression, knockdown or deficiency and Pi treatment, were used to evaluate endothelial dysfunction in bEND.3 cells, primary mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells and an LPS-induced murine model of endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy. Barrier dysfunction, cytoskeletal remodelling and signalling events were assessed using permeability assays, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence and in vivo BBB leakage analyses.

KEY RESULTS: LPS increased PTPRO expression in brain tissue from endotoxemic mice and cerebral endothelial cells. Elevated PTPRO promoted F-actin reorganization, stress fibre formation and intercellular gap formation, whereas Pi treatment or PTPRO silencing attenuated these changes. PTPRO overexpression worsened endothelial barrier dysfunction, while Pi reduced thrombin-induced permeability in bEND.3 cells and wild-type primary endothelial cells. Primary endothelial cells from PTPRO-deficient mice were protected. Mechanistically, PTPRO regulated cytoskeletal dynamics through the ErbB2-Rho-MLC2 pathway. In vivo, Pi treatment and PTPRO deficiency reduced BBB leakage, with limited effects on inflammatory cytokines.

CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: These findings identify PTPRO as an important regulator of BBB disruption in endotoxemia-associated encephalopathy and support pharmacological targeting of PTPRO as a potential strategy for preserving sepsis-associated BBB injury.

articles.title: Harm reduction opportunities following ICU admission for prescription opioid overdose: An 8-year comparative audit at the Royal Melbourne Hospital.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) admission following prescription opioid overdose represents an important opportunity for multidisciplinary intervention and harm reduction, yet Australian data describing inpatient management are limited. A retrospective audit was conducted of 70 adults admitted to the ICU at the Royal Melbourne Hospital with prescription opioid overdose between 2021 and 2024. The primary outcome was provision of take-home naloxone (THN) before discharge among patients meeting institutional eligibility criteria. Secondary outcomes included opioid education, multidisciplinary involvement and discharge opioid management, with comparison with the previous institutional audit where comparable data were available. Only five patients (7.5%, 95% confidence interval 3.2-16.3) were supplied with THN despite all meeting institutional eligibility criteria. Polypharmacy overdose was common (77%). Most patients received at least one specialist referral (83%), although 15% received no inpatient specialist referral. Opioid education was documented in 58 patients (87%) compared with 17% previously (P <0.001), although content and documentation were inconsistent. These findings demonstrate persistent gaps in THN provision, structured opioid education and coordinated discharge planning, highlighting ICU admission as an important opportunity for prescription opioid harm reduction. Strengthening guideline-based multidisciplinary interventions during admission may improve patient outcomes and inform harm reduction strategies nationally.

articles.title: One-Lung Ventilation for Neonatal Pneumonectomy in a Hydropic Premature Infant: Fiberoptic-guided Left Mainstem Intubation.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM) is a rare lung anomaly that can cause severe respiratory distress and hydrops fetalis. One-lung ventilation (OLV) in neonates poses extreme anatomical challenges due to the lack of appropriately sized double-lumen tubes or bronchial blockers. A male neonate (2500 g, 30 weeks' gestation) presented with hydrops fetalis and a massive right-sided thoracic CCAM. Due to progressive respiratory failure and hemodynamic instability, an emergency right pneumonectomy was scheduled on postnatal day 3. To achieve OLV, a 3.5-mm cuffed endotracheal tube (with the cuff left deflated) was advanced into the left main bronchus under fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FOB) guidance. Removal of the tube adaptor facilitated rapid, pragmatic placement while minimizing interruptions to ventilation during apneic oxygenation. Pressure-controlled lung-protective ventilation was maintained. Transient desaturation episodes during mediastinal manipulation were successfully managed. The 3-hour procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. In premature neonates in whom commercial lung-isolation devices are impractical, FOB-guided selective mainstem bronchial intubation is a rapid, feasible, and effective strategy for OLV. Individualized airway planning and FOB guidance are instrumental in ensuring accurate placement and maintaining oxygenation.

articles.title: Neuron-Derived Vesicular circMagi1 Restrains Vascular Repair After Ischemic Stroke by Promoting TRIM65-Mediated ANXA2 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) contribute to stroke pathogenesis, yet their intercellular functions within the ischemic neurovascular unit remain poorly defined. Profiling of plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) revealed a higher abundance of circMagi1 in patients with acute ischemic stroke compared with healthy controls. This upregulation was recapitulated in the ischemic mouse brain, where cell-type-resolved analyses identified injured neurons as a primary source of circMagi1-containing EVs that accumulate in endothelial cells. Mechanistically, endothelial circMagi1 binds ANXA2 and enhances its engagement with TRIM65, thereby promoting TRIM65-mediated ANXA2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and restraining angiogenesis. To therapeutically target this axis in vivo, treatment with siCircMagi1-RVG-EVs was initiated on post-stroke day 1 and maintained thereafter, while siTrim65-Ang2-EVs were introduced from either day 1 or day 9. Among the schedules tested, adding siTrim65-Ang2-EVs from day 9 was associated with greater neurovascular recovery than sustained circMagi1-targeted treatment alone or co-initiation on day 1. Together, these findings delineate a vesicle-mediated signaling axis linking neuronal injury to impaired vascular repair and support further evaluation of delayed TRIM65 inhibition during sustained circMagi1 suppression.

articles.title: Effects of three doses of tea polyphenols on lipid metabolism, intestinal barrier function, and gut microbiota in overweight mice.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overweight induced by a high-fat diet (HFD) is closely associated with dyslipidemia, oxidative stress, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and gut microbiota imbalance. Tea polyphenols have shown metabolic benefits; however, comparative information regarding their biological effects across different intervention doses remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of different doses of green tea polyphenols (GTP) on metabolic disorders in HFD-induced overweight mice.

RESULTS: Green tea polyphenols reduced body weight gain and improved lipid metabolism without affecting food intake, with the strongest overall effects observed in the 300 mg kg-1 group. Compared with the normal control (NC) group, the HFD group showed increased serum total cholesterol (TC) (+104.01%), triglyceride (TG) (+57.06%), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (+64.44%) levels and decreased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (-41.29%).
