These lipid disturbances were attenuated significantly by GTP intervention, especially in the 300 mg kg-1 group (P < 0.05). GTP also alleviated liver injury and oxidative stress, as indicated by decreased aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels, increased catalase (CAT) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities, increased glutathione (GSH) levels, and reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels. In addition, GTP intervention was associated with increased colonic goblet cell numbers and changes in the expression of the tight-junction proteins claudin-1 and occludin. Gut microbiota analysis revealed a reduced Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio and enrichment of beneficial bacteria, with the high-dose group showing a microbial profile closer to that of the normal controls.

CONCLUSION: Green tea polyphenol ameliorated HFD-induced metabolic abnormalities involving lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and intestinal barrier function, and these improvements were accompanied by marked alterations in gut microbial composition. Among the tested doses, 300 mg kg-1 showed the strongest overall effects. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Triggers and Modifiers of Acute Coronary Events and Implications for Practice: An Umbrella Review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To synthesise evidence from systematic reviews on triggers and modifiers of acute coronary events to identify clinical implications. Triggers refer to transient exposures that may precipitate acute coronary events through several potential biological and haemodynamic mechanisms.

DESIGN: An umbrella review.

DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, Epistemonikos, and Google Scholar were searched in May 2024, and an updated search was conducted in February 2025.

METHODS: This umbrella review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological guidance. Systematic reviews assessing short-term or acute triggers and acute coronary events, including acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction, coronary occlusion, or spontaneous coronary artery dissection, and published in English were included. The quality of included reviews was evaluated using the JBI critical appraisal instrument.

RESULTS: Twenty-four systematic reviews examining 11 acute coronary event triggers were included. The most frequently reported triggers were air pollution (n = 8 reviews), respiratory infection (n = 6), and physical exertion (n = 4). The hazard period was primarily 0-2 h for physical exertion, sexual activity, and emotional stress, while environmental and infection-related triggers extended to 7 days for air pollution, up to 20 days for heat exposure, and 28 days for respiratory infections. Population-attributable fractions were reported for physical exertion (10.6%), emotional stress (3.9%), and anger (3%). Potential modifiers of risk identified, such as regular physical activity, beta-blocker use, and influenza vaccination, highlight opportunities for personalised prevention strategies to reduce risk when exposed to potential triggers.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the role of triggers in acute coronary events. Future research should prioritise translating these insights into clinical nursing practice to mitigate acute event risk.

IMPACT: Awareness of trigger-specific risks can guide nurses to deliver targeted patient education, conduct precise risk assessments, and implement exposure-management strategies, particularly for individuals at elevated cardiovascular risk.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Do as I Say, Not as I Do: Exploring the Links Between Parenting Styles, Parental Aspirations, and Socioeconomic Status, and Young People's Post-School Aspirations in Scotland.
articles.abstract: There is limited population level empirical evidence examining the relationship between social class and post-school aspirations in Scotland, and previous research elsewhere finds conflicting results. Without knowledge of the relationship between social class and post-school aspirations, it is difficult to confirm whether social stratification in post-school destinations is a result of structural barriers, or the dubious prospect that disadvantaged young people simply lack education or career ambitions. To address this gap, this study explores how parenting styles, parental aspirations for their child's education, and parental socioeconomic status are correlated with young people's post-school aspirations in Scotland, using Growing Up in Scotland, a nationally representative longitudinal Scottish birth cohort study. We use three related multinomial logistic regression models to examine whether and how parenting styles, parental aspirations, and parental social class variables explain young people's post-school aspirations. We find that parenting styles are not associated with young people's post-school aspirations when controlling for confounders. Parental aspirations are, however, strongly associated with children's own post-school aspirations when controlling for confounders, and measures of social class are only associated with young people's aspirations when not controlling for these parental aspirations. While young people from all social classes and their parents hold similar aspirations-most commonly to attend university-analysis by the Scottish Government of their administrative statistics reveals that university access is very much socially stratified. This social stratification in outcomes-but not in aspirations-highlights the need to address structural barriers that impede working-class young people from achieving their goals, and the need to shift away from policy solutions that aim to solely raise the ambitions of disadvantaged youths. This study highlights the importance of productively involving parents in career guidance and calls for further research to understand the dynamics of parental and child aspirations better.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in sepsis care and research: aligning clinical questions with model selection and human oversight.
Large language models as clinical decision support in emergency medicine: promise, pitfalls, and the risk of uncritical adoption.
Contemporary Approaches to Prehospital Acute Coronary Syndrome Risk Stratification: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Chest pain is a common high-risk complaint encountered by emergency medical services (EMS). Early identification and treatment of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) improve outcomes, yet prehospital evaluation remains constrained by limited diagnostic resources. This narrative review examines contemporary approaches to prehospital ACS risk stratification, diagnostic technologies, and decision-making. A targeted PubMed search of peer-reviewed publications and selected grey literature published between 2020 and 2025 was supplemented by targeted searches and citation review. Relevant literature published after the initial search period was incorporated during manuscript preparation and revision. Studies addressing prehospital ACS risk stratification, electrocardiogram (ECG) assessment, point-ofcare biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnostics, and systems-level cardiac triage were included and synthesized thematically. Biomarker-integrated pathways, particularly HEART-derived approaches combined with point-of-care troponin testing, demonstrated the strongest evidence for safe prehospital risk assessment and reduced healthcare utilization. Biomarker-free approaches offered broader applicability but lower diagnostic certainty. ECG acquisition and transmission remained foundational for STEMI recognition and activation, while AI-assisted ECG interpretation and decision-support tools showed promising diagnostic performance but lacked prospective outcome-based validation. Gaps remain regarding atypical presentations, sex-specific strategies, and validation across diverse EMS environments. Overall, contemporary evidence supports structured prehospital risk stratification as decision support rather than definitive diagnosis. Implementation depends on provider training, protocol standardization, resources, and integration within regional systems of care. Future research should prioritize validation across diverse EMS settings, atypical and sex-specific presentations, and prospective evaluation of emerging diagnostic technologies.

articles.title: Beyond Parametric and Nonparametric Tests: A Practical Guide to Table 1 in Clinical Research.
articles.abstract: In many clinical research reports, Table 1 presents the baseline or general characteristics of study participants and helps readers understand the study population and observed between-group differences. Despite its apparent simplicity, constructing and interpreting Table 1 requires several distinct decisions, including whether formal between-group inference is scientifically justified, how variables should be summarized, and how observed differences should be interpreted. Routine significance testing of baseline characteristics is generally discouraged in randomized trials and often provides limited information in observational studies, where group differences may reflect treatment selection, exposure patterns, disease severity, or other systematic mechanisms. We propose a purpose-first framework in which investigators first clarify the intended role of Table 1, consider the study design, and determine whether a comparison addresses a prespecified and scientifically meaningful inferential question. They should then identify the variable type, evaluate distributional shape, influential observations, and clinical interpretability, and select appropriate summary statistics. For descriptive applications, transparent group-specific summaries should be emphasized, with observed absolute or standardized differences added when useful and without routine p-values. Confidence intervals should be reported when a population-level estimation objective has been defined. When formal inference is justified, investigators should define the target quantity or estimand and select a statistical method according to the variable type, data structure, distributional characteristics, and model assumptions. Effect estimates and confidence intervals should receive greater emphasis than isolated p-values. This framework distinguishes description from inference and promotes transparent, statistically coherent, and clinically meaningful construction and interpretation of Table 1.

articles.title: Large Language Models in the Emergency Department: Fairness Implications for Clinicians.
articles.abstract: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), are rapidly expanding in emergency medicine, but concerns remain regarding their fairness across diverse patient populations. Fairness extends beyond model accuracy and includes equal performance across patient groups, equitable outcomes and allocation of clinical benefits, and procedural fairness throughout the lifecycle of AI implementation. This narrative review aims to provide a practical framework for understanding and evaluating fairness in emergency medicine applications of AI and LLMs. This narrative review organizes fairness risks into three clinically relevant layers. First, datalevel fairness concerns the data used to train, fine-tune, or prompt AI systems. Biased clinical data, including non-random missingness and stigmatizing documentation, can influence model performance. Second, output-level fairness concerns whether the outputs generated by AI systems are equally accurate, safe, and useful across patient groups. In emergency care, subgroup-specific errors in recommendations, predictions, translations, or instructions may arise from aggregation, learning, or evaluation bias, even when overall model performance appears strong. Third, human-interaction fairness concerns whether the benefits of AI are realized equitably in clinical practice and by patients. Even when data and outputs are fair, inequities may arise if clinicians over-rely on or reject useful AI recommendations, or if patients are unable to access, understand, or trust AI-mediated information. Clinicians should consider potential implications for safety, transparency, and fairness alongside overall model accuracy when evaluating AI tools in emergency medicine.

articles.title: Propensity score methods in medical research: a concise practical guide with applications to emergency medicine.
articles.abstract: Propensity score (PS) methods can reduce measured confounding in observational emergency medicine research, but validity depends more on design choices and diagnostics than on the treatment-prediction model. This clinical review presents a practical workflow for defining the target estimand, selecting pretreatment covariates, choosing matching or weighting, checking covariate balance and treatment overlap, and analyzing a binary outcome in the population created by the PS design. The average treatment effect (ATE), average treatment effect in the treated (ATT), and average treatment effect in the overlap population (ATO) answer different clinical questions. A worked example of 1,200 simulated emergency patients uses a common, explicit time zero to show how confounding by indication can make immediate treatment appear harmful before adjustment and how PS matching, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting, and overlap weighting change both the comparison population and estimated effect. Standardized mean differences, PS distributions, weight summaries, and effective sample size are presented before treatment-specific risks, risk differences, and risk ratios. A standalone supplement provides package-based R code, expected output, and analysis-derived figures. Survival analysis is outside the scope. PS methods are most credible when used as design tools: define the question, construct a supported comparison, verify diagnostics, and only then analyze outcomes.

articles.title: 'We Didn't Really Learn How to Manage It': An In-Depth Mixed-Methods Exploration Into Temporomandibular Disorder Management Behaviours of First-Contact Healthcare Practitioners in Australia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) affect approximately 10% of the population. Management is often challenging, which can negatively affect patient outcomes and experiences with care.

OBJECTIVES: To explore the TMD management behaviours of first-contact healthcare practitioners in Australia and gain insight into factors influencing care.

METHODS: Sequential explanatory mixed methods design. Dentists, physiotherapists and general medical practitioners were recruited for a COM-B informed online survey (n = 150) and semi-structured interviews (n = 11). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (survey) and a codebook analysis approach (interviews).

RESULTS: Most participants reported referring to dentists and physiotherapists for initial care. Interventions perceived most important in first-line management included self-management strategies, advice and education and stress management (≥ 73%). Small but statistically significant associations were observed between practitioners' referral behaviours and their occupation, and patients' main presenting complaint (p < 0.05). Leading care challenges included 'lacking knowledge about TMD and possible management options', concerns about the financial cost of treatment to patients and difficulty accessing relevant healthcare practitioners (≥ 41%). Qualitative themes were: (1) Alignment between management beliefs, behaviours and best-practice recommendations, (2) Uncertainty sits between beliefs and behaviours, (3) Patient factors mediate the space between beliefs and management behaviours, (4) Decisions are contextualised within the realities of the broader healthcare system.

CONCLUSION: Strong alignment appears to exist between practitioners' TMD management beliefs, behaviours and best-practice recommendations; however, factors like uncertainty, concerns about patients' acceptance of management plans, and practitioners' occupation also impact care decisions. Findings may be helpful to inform strategies to improve TMD management.

articles.title: Clinical Presentation, Management and Outcome of Heart Failure Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is a major public health issue with rising hospitalizations and high mortality. This study was conducted to assess the clinical presentation, management and outcome of heart failure patients presenting to a tertiary care hospital.

METHODS: A prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary cardiac center in Nepal over a period of six months among admitted patients aged 18 years and above with heart failure. Data on demographics, etiology, treatment, and outcomes were collected via structured interviews, chart review, clinical observation, phone calls and follow-up. Etiologies were defined per standard criteria and patients were categorized according to the clinical and echocardiographic diagnosis.

RESULTS: Among 1523 patients included, the mean age of the cohort was 61.5 ± 14.9 years, and 62.0 % were male. Coronary artery disease (65.8%) was the most common etiology, followed by idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (15.0%) and rheumatic heart disease (7.2%). Acute coronary syndrome (39.9%) was the primary aggravating factor. Guideline-directed medical therapy use included Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (68.5%), Beta-blockers (66.1%), and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (61.2%); however, the use of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitors was low (15.2%). Device therapy was rare (0.26%). The overall mortality rate was 12.7%, comprising 4.7% in-hospital mortality and 7.9% 90-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Coronary artery disease is the commonest etiology, with Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker as the commonest prescription, followed by Beta-blockers and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, with device therapy being rare, with an overall mortality of 12.7%.

articles.title: Factors Related to Late Intrauterine Fetal Death in a Tertiary Level Hospital: A Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrauterine fetal death (IUFD) is an unfortunate perinatal occurrence with serious global and local impacts. Despite improved diagnostic methods, a significant fraction of stillbirths remains unexplained, especially in resource-constrained settings such as Nepal. Thus, the present study aimed to determine the frequency and associated characteristics of late intrauterine fetal death (?28 weeks) in a tertiary-level hospital in Nepal.

METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted at Dhulikhel Hospital, Nepal, from January 2024 to January 2025. Medical records from 36 women with late IUFD (?28 weeks of gestation) were reviewed. Data on sociodemographic variables, obstetric history, antenatal care (ANC) attendance, and fetal factors were gathered and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The mean maternal age was 27.3 ± 6.3 years, with most women (88.9%) in the age group between 20-34 years. The majority were multigravida (80.6%) and had attended at least four ANC visits (83.3%). The mean gestational age at delivery was 35.8 ± 4.1 weeks, with a mean fetal birth weight of 1905±834 grams. 41.7% of fetuses weighed less than 1500 grams. Male fetuses prevailed (61.1%). Surprisingly, 80.6% of instances were unexplained. Fetal malpresentation (8.3%), hypertensive disorders (5.6%), and other maternal comorbidities were all identifiable variables.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights a high proportion of unexplained stillbirths despite appropriate antenatal care in a tertiary care setting.

articles.title: Outcomes of Healthcare-Associated Infections in Respiratory Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are the major cause of morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, microbiological profile, resistance patterns, risk factors, and outcomes of HAIs in a respiratory ICU (RICU) of a tertiary care hospital in Nepal.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in RICU. HAIs were diagnosed according to the CDC criteria. Descriptive statistics were reported as mean (SD) and frequencies. Unpaired t-tests, chi-square tests were used for comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the risk factors.

RESULTS: Among 121 ICU admissions, 42 patients developed 50 episodes of HAI, yielding a prevalence of 34.7%. Ventilator-associated pneumonia was the most common HAIs. The most frequently isolated organisms were Acinetobacter baumannii in 42.0% and Klebsiella pneumonia in 18.0%. Both were resistance to Ceftriaxone. Resistance to Piperacillin-tazobactam were 85.8% and 77.8% and to carbapenems were 92% and 90% respectively. Tigecycline resistance was seen in 20% of Acinetobacter isolates and none of the Klebsiella isolates. Sensitivity to Polymyxin B was 100%. Mechanical ventilation, urinary catheters and history of prior hospitalization were the strongest predictors of HAI. Patients who developed HAI had a longer ICU stay (9.5 vs. 5.2 days, p=0.001) and higher mortality (28.6% vs. 13.9%, p=0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: HAIs, particularly VAP caused by MDR organisms, were common in our ICU and there was a high resistance to beta lactams and carbapenem antibiotics. Low resistance to tigecycline and polymyxin B warrants careful stewardship.

articles.title: Post-Rasuwa Flash Flood: The Potential Use of Artificial Intelligence in Infectious Disease Surveillance.
articles.journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
articles.abstract: Nepal frequently experiences natural disasters, including floods. On 26 August 2026, the Rasuwa flash floods struck Nepal, resulting in hundreds of deaths, and leaving thousands of people missing. Infectious diseases represent an important public health concern in the aftermath of such disasters. Evidence on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for post flash flood infectious disease risk assessment remains limited. Here, we discuss the potential integration of AI as a complementary decision-support tool to strengthen infectious disease risk assessment and early warning following Rasuwa flash flood disaster in Nepal. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Infectious diseases; Nepal; Rasuwa flash flood.

articles.title: Patient Safety Incidents Experienced by Novice Nurses During Transition to Practice: A Qualitative Phenomenological Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Novice nurses in their first year of practice are vulnerable to patient safety incidents due to limited clinical experience and transition shock. This study aimed to explore novice nurses' experiences regarding patient safety incidents, their underlying causes, and their subsequent impacts.

DESIGN: A descriptive phenomenological qualitative design.

METHODS: Conducted between February 2024 and June 2025, this study involved online and face-to-face interviews with 18 novice nurses in Türkiye with up to 1 year of experience. Data were analysed using Colaizzi's descriptive phenomenological method.

RESULTS: Analysis yielded three main themes and eight subthemes: (1) patient safety incidents (medication errors, patient identification errors, missed nursing care); (2) experiencing threats to patient safety (individual unpreparedness for independent care, team-level communication gaps and unsupportive interactions, struggling with organizational workload and staffing constraints, silence and non-reporting in clinical culture); and (3) impact of patient safety incidents (negative emotions, lessons learned).

CONCLUSION: Novice nurses face professionally and organizationally challenging patient safety incidents during transition. Strengthening structured orientation, preceptorship, non-punitive reporting systems, and supportive leadership is essential to foster safer clinical environments.

REPORTING METHOD: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative studies (COREQ).

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Findings emphasize the critical need for structured orientation, adequate staffing, and formal preceptorship during professional transition. Establishing a non-punitive reporting culture enables learning from near-misses, while supportive leadership helps novice nurses manage transition challenges and ensure safer patient care.

articles.title: SLC25A4high Hepatocytes Enhance Lifestyle Intervention Response in MASLD by Recruiting Eating Macrophages.
articles.abstract: While lifestyle interventions (LSI) are the cornerstone of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) management, the molecular mechanisms driving the histological and metabolic regression in LSI-responsive patients remain unclear. C57BL/6N mice were hydrodynamically injected with Slc25a4 and Sleeping Beauty transposon. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiled the hepatic immune landscape. Metabolomics and co-culture assays analyzed intercellular crosstalk. Responsive MASLD patients had high SLC25A4 expression, correlating with exercise-induced hepatic steatosis improvement. Slc25a4 overexpression augmented exercise effects. scRNA-seq identified a distinct population of Clec4f+Timd4+P2ry12+ macrophages, defined as lipid-eating macrophages, in livers of Slc25a4-overexpressing mice. Macrophage depletion reinstated hepatosteatosis in high-fat, high-fructose, and high-cholesterol diet-fed exercised mice with Slc25a4 overexpression. Mechanistically, SLC25A4 mediates mitochondrial ATP exchange and selective ATP efflux. Ectopically overexpressed Slc25a4 activates Pannexin 1 to release ATP, which recruits eating macrophages via P2ry12, clearing lipid-laden hepatocytes. The GDF15-PPARα axis between macrophages and hepatocytes was activated. Macrophage Gdf15 knockdown abrogated Slc25a4-mediated enhanced hepatic fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and hepatic PPARα knockdown abolished this effect as well. Slc25a4 orchestrates an LSI-responsive hepatocyte-macrophage axis: Pannexin 1-mediated ATP release recruits lipid-eating macrophages, whose GDF15 activates PPARα-driven FAO, establishing Slc25a4 as a therapeutic target to restore exercise response in MASLD.

articles.title: Association between periodontitis and exudative retinal detachment: A population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate whether periodontitis, a common bacterial-induced inflammatory condition, serves as a risk factor for exudative retinal detachment (ERD), which results from fluid entering the subretinal space due to damage to the retinal pigment epithelium or leaky intraocular vessels, typically associated with inflammatory, infectious, or retinal diseases.

METHODS: Using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (2000-2020), patients with periodontitis were identified based on at least three outpatient visits within 1 year. A comparison cohort without periodontitis was selected and matched 1:1 using propensity scores for sex, age, index year, and Charlson Comorbidity Index. Each group included 167,530 individuals. The periodontitis cohort was further divided into treated and untreated subgroups according to periodontal treatment codes (n = 68,705 and 98,825, respectively).

RESULTS: During follow-up, ERD occurred in 0.26% (n = 437) of patients with periodontitis and 0.06% (n = 100) of those comparison individuals. Compared with the comparison group, the cumulative risk of ERD was significantly higher in the periodontitis group and in both two subgroups. The incidence rates of exudative retinal detachment were 16.74 and 3.55 per 105 person-years in the periodontitis and comparison groups, respectively. Patients with periodontitis were associated with a higher hazard of ERD (3.95, 3.42, and 3.56 for crude, adjusted, and adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios, respectively). Sensitivity analyses showed the increased hazard of ERD remained significant after time-lag exclusions and in two periodontitis subgroups.

CONCLUSION: Based on the whole-population study in Taiwan, patients with periodontitis exhibit an increased incidence of ERD, suggesting a potential association between periodontitis and ERD.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Gum disease is a common infection that causes ongoing inflammation in the mouth, and growing evidence suggests it may affect more than just oral health. In this large study using national health data from Taiwan, we examined whether people with gum disease are more likely to develop exudative retinal detachment, a serious eye condition in which fluid builds up under the retina and can impair vision. By comparing 167,530 patients with gum disease with an equal number without it, matched for age, sex, and general health, we found that this eye condition occurred much more frequently among those with gum disease. Even after accounting for other medical conditions, individuals with periodontitis were more than three times as likely to experience this form of retinal detachment. This pattern was consistent regardless of whether patients had received specific gum treatments. These results suggest that chronic inflammation from gum disease may be connected to eye disorders, emphasizing that maintaining good oral health could play an important role in preserving vision and overall health.

articles.title: Unsupervised clustering to classify patients with candidemia in intensive care: algorithmic tautology or the generation of highly anticipated new data?
Hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices after cardiac arrest: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoglobin targets are absent from post-cardiac arrest guidelines. New trials suggest that patients with brain and myocardial injury, injuries common post-arrest, may benefit from higher hemoglobin targets. Trends in post-arrest hemoglobin and real-world practices remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult cardiac arrests at three academic hospitals. We screened in-hospital and out-of-hospital arrests with resuscitation efforts ongoing at hospital arrival for inclusion. Patients who survived the initial resuscitation and had a hemoglobin value measured were included. All post-arrest hemoglobin values and red blood cell transfusions were collected through 30 days; descriptive statistics and graphical visualization were used to present hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices. Exploratory analyses evaluated the association between hemoglobin and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Of 2,634 cardiac arrests, 958 met inclusion criteria, with 152 (15.9%) out-of-hospital arrests and 806 (84.1%) in-hospital. The mean initial post-arrest hemoglobin was 9.75 g/dL (SD 2.60), with hemoglobin levels declining progressively over the first 20 days post-arrest. Red cell transfusions were delivered for 369 (38.5%) patients in the 30 days post-arrest, with 1,238 total transfusions. The mean pre-transfusion hemoglobin value was 6.96 g/dL (SD 1.06). Pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels were < 7 g/dL for 762 (61.6%) of transfusions, and ≥ 7 g/dL for 476 (38.4%) of transfusions. Over 30 days, the highest proportion of patients transfused was in the first 48 h. Patients with initial post-arrest hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL had lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.46-0.84, p<0.01). In time-varying analysis, post-arrest hemoglobin through 30 days demonstrated an L-shaped association with mortality, with 95% of the total reduction in mortality hazard captured below 9.20 g/dL.

CONCLUSIONS: Anemia is common after cardiac arrest, worsening in initial survivors. There is substantial variation in pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels, reflecting clinical equipoise. Clinical trials are needed to disentangle anemia as a driver versus a marker of outcomes, and test whether the risk is modifiable.

articles.title: SALL1 as a marker for distinguishing microglia from blood-derived myeloid cells in stroke brain scRNA-seq data.
articles.abstract: Distinguishing resident microglia from infiltrating myeloid cells in stroke scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to shared myeloid markers; SALL1 shows greater specificity for microglia compared with commonly used markers (e.g. TMEM119, CX3CR1, P2RY12), and combining SALL1 with these commonly used markers improves the ability to distinguish microglia from infiltrating myeloid populations in stroke‑associated scRNA‑seq datasets.

articles.title: Body weight following a multidomain lifestyle intervention in older adults at risk of dementia - A post-hoc analysis of the AgeWell.de-trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle interventions provide a promising approach to address higher body weight as a risk factor for dementia.

OBJECTIVE: The AgeWell.de-trial was primarily designed to preserve cognitive function and reduce dementia risk. In this post-hoc analysis, we investigated body weight following the multidomain intervention among older adults with overweight or obesity, as well as the role of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss.

METHODS: Analyses used data from the cluster-randomized AgeWell.de-trial, testing a multidomain intervention (dietary counselling, enhancement of physical, social and cognitive activity, medication review, intervention for cardiovascular risk factors, depressive symptoms/grief, if applicable) over 24 months in adults aged 60 to 77 years at risk for dementia. Associations between intervention allocation and body weight at follow-up were analyzed using linear regression, controlling for covariates, based on multiply imputed data.

RESULTS: The sample included n = 678 participants with a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², mean age (SD): 68.9 (4.8), 52.1% female. Group allocation was not associated with body weight at 24-month follow-up (b (unstandardized regression coefficient) = -0.30, 95% CI: -0.51; 1.11). Older age (b = -0.14, 95% CI: -0.25; -0.03) and a high level of education (b = -1.28, 95% CI: -2.55; 0.00) were linked to lower body weight at follow-up, while higher baseline body weight predicted higher body weight at follow-up (b = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.91; 0.98). Levels of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss remained high but stable in both groups, regardless of group allocation.

CONCLUSIONS: In this post-hoc analysis, group allocation was not associated with lower body weight at follow-up. Despite high levels of motivation and confidence regarding weight loss and favorable changes in diet and physical activity in the intervention group, these changes did not translate into measurable weight loss.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: AgeWell.de was prospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on December 7th, 2017 (DRKS trial identifier DRKS00013555).

articles.title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Value of Sonographic Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter in Patients with Ischemic Stroke or Hypertensive Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) is a critical complication in nontraumatic brain injury, yet invasive monitoring carries significant risks, and noninvasive alternatives remain undervalidated. Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) ultrasonography represents a promising bedside technique, but data in nontraumatic populations are limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic and prognostic value of ONSD in neurocritical patients with ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage.

METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 100 neurocritical intensive care unit (ICU) patients with acute nontraumatic brain injury [ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage; Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) < 9] who underwent admission computed tomography (CT) and bedside ONSD ultrasonography. Sixty age- and sex-matched healthy volunteers were enrolled exclusively to provide descriptive reference values for physiological ONSD and were not included in the primary diagnostic or prognostic analyses. CT-based radiologic ICP surrogates were the reference standard. Exploratory analyses evaluated inter-eye variability, adjusted models, and in-hospital survival.

RESULTS: ONSD increased stepwise across healthy controls, patients with negative CT, and patients with positive CT (4.62 ± 0.33, 5.52 ± 0.51, and 6.50 ± 0.51 mm, respectively). Among neurocritical patients, a cohort-derived cutoff of ≥ 6.00 mm yielded 86.7% sensitivity, 85.0% specificity, 89.7% positive predictive value, 81.0% negative predictive value, 86.0% accuracy, and 0.901 area under the curve (AUC). Above-threshold ONSD remained independently associated with CT-positive elevated ICP after adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), GCS, and systolic blood pressure (SBP) in exploratory multivariable analysis. Exploratory survival analysis showed significantly higher in-hospital mortality in patients with ONSD above the cohort-derived threshold (log-rank p = 4.77 × 10-13).

CONCLUSIONS: Bedside ultrasonographic ONSD measurement appears clinically useful for early triage and longitudinal bedside surveillance in neurocritical patients with ischemic stroke or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage, particularly when invasive monitoring is unavailable or delayed.

articles.title: Comparing Intervention Outcome Measures Across Clinic and Home for Young Autistic Children: Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) and Measure of NDBI Strategy Implementation-Caregiver Change (MONSI-CC).
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Growing use of multiple Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBIs) across service settings has highlighted the need for flexible outcome measures. However, prior research has been limited by a lack of standardized tools to sensitively capture changes in autistic children's behavior and caregiver strategy use across contexts. The present study examined the feasibility and reliability of the Brief Observation of Social Communication Change (BOSCC) and the Measure of NDBI Strategy Implementation-Caregiver Change (MONSI-CC) across clinic and home settings, as well as cross-context comparability and associations between child and caregiver behaviors.

METHODS: Sixty caregiver-child dyads completed standardized 12-minute caregiver-led play tasks in both clinic and home contexts. During home administration, research staff provided real-time remote support and prompts consistent with clinic procedures. Feasibility and acceptability of home administration were evaluated using descriptive statistics. Reliability was examined in terms of internal consistency, inter-rater reliability, and test-retest reliability. Cross-context comparability and associations between the two measures were examined using paired-sample t-tests and Pearson correlations.

RESULTS: Home administration showed high caregiver acceptability and strong fidelity. The BOSCC and MONSI-CC showed generally similar reliability patterns across contexts. Most BOSCC and MONSI-CC scores did not differ significantly between contexts, and several showed significant cross-context associations. Associations between autistic children's social communication and caregiver strategy use were strongest within the same context but also evident across settings.

CONCLUSION: Brief, standardized observational assessments may provide scalable tools for assessing caregiver and child behavior across clinic- and home-based early intervention settings.

articles.title: Work productivity and psychological well-being in patients affected by type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) is a lifelong autoimmune condition that, when diagnosed during childhood or adolescence, may influence educational attainment, employment trajectories, and occupational functioning in adulthood. This observational cross-sectional study, conducted between June and September 2024 at the "Federico II" University Hospital in Naples, Italy, assessed work ability, work productivity, activity impairment, and psychological well-being in 70 adults with T1D. Sociodemographic, clinical, and occupational data were collected through structured interviews and medical record review. Work ability was evaluated using the Work Ability Index (WAI), productivity and activity impairment using the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment questionnaire (WPAI), and psychological well-being using the Psychological General Well-Being Index (PGWBI). Overall, 49% of participants were unemployed. Among employed individuals, work ability was generally preserved, with 72% reporting good or excellent WAI scores, although WAI declined significantly with age (p = 0.040). WPAI results showed low absenteeism (5.5%) but relevant presenteeism (26.7%) and activity impairment (42.7%). Activity impairment was higher among unemployed than employed participants (61.2% vs. 25.3%; p < 0.0001). Mean PGWBI scores indicated preserved psychological well-being (66.8 ± 20.3) but declined with increasing age (p = 0.001) and unemployment (p = 0.003). Higher PGWBI scores correlated with greater work ability (rs = 0.72, p < 0.0001) and lower activity impairment (rs = -0.79, p < 0.0001). Glycated hemoglobin, body mass index, occupational category, and insulin delivery technology were not significantly associated with outcomes. Overall, age and employment status emerged as relevant correlates of functional and psychological outcomes. These findings support integrated occupational strategies beyond glycemic control and appropriate targeted workplace accommodations.

articles.title: Symptom improvement with dosing above 9 g of low-sodium oxybate: effectiveness and safety in participants with narcolepsy in the DUET study.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evaluate effectiveness/safety of low-sodium oxybate (LXB; Xywav®) dosages > 9 g/night in participants with narcolepsy (type 1 [NT1] or 2 [NT2]).

METHODS: Jazz DUET (prospective, multiple-cohort, open-label study [NCT05875974]) included screening, 9-day baseline (LXB 9 g/night ["LXB 9 g BL"]), 2-8-week titration, 2-week stable-dose, 9-day end-of-treatment (LXB > 9 g- ≤ 12 g ["optimized LXB > 9 g EOT"]; twice-nightly, first/second max doses = 7.5/4.5 g), and 2-week follow-up. Endpoints included Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Narcolepsy Severity Scale-clinical trials version (NSS-CT), Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S) and Change (PGI-C), and polysomnography (PSG)-measured respiratory assessments.

RESULTS: Forty-eight participants took LXB > 9 g/night (mean ± SD age: 39.2 ± 10.9 years; 62.5% female); 44 (NT1, n = 28; NT2, n = 16) completed the study. Mean ± SD stable-LXB dosage (n = 45) was 11.1 ± 1.0 g/night (most common [43.8%], 12 g/night). From LXB 9 g BL to optimized LXB > 9 g EOT, mean ± SE ESS scores (11.4 ± 0.8 to 8.3 ± 0.9), NSS-CT (NT1) scores (17.3 ± 2.2 to 9.4 ± 2.1), and NSS-2-CT (NT2) scores (9.7 ± 1.7 to 4.3 ± 1.6) improved. Fewer participants rated their disease as severe (61.4% to 29.5%), and most (92.3%) reported their disease improved. AHI (1.8 ± 0.4 to 1.6 ± 0.3), CAI (0.01 ± 0.01 to 0.01 ± 0.00), and mean SpO2 (95.8 ± 0.2 to 95.8 ± 0.1) remained stable. Common TEAEs included nausea (12.5%), vomiting (12.5%), and headache (10.4%).

CONCLUSION: Participants taking LXB > 9 g/night experienced further improvements in narcolepsy symptoms versus 9 g/night, suggesting some patients may require higher dosages for optimal benefit. No changes in mean respiratory PSG measures were observed. TEAEs align with the known safety profile. Findings support individualized clinical decision-making with higher LXB dosages.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Trial name: A Study to Investigate the Effect of XYWAV on Sleepiness, Polysomnography, and Functional Outcomes in Participants With Idiopathic Hypersomnia or Narcolepsy; URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05875974 ; ID number: NCT05875974.

CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Narcolepsy is a heterogeneous disorder requiring individualized treatment strategies to optimize symptom management. This study fills a critical knowledge gap by evaluating effectiveness and safety of low-sodium oxybate (LXB) dosing regimens higher (> 9-12 g/night) than the recommended dosage (6-9 g/night).

STUDY IMPACT: Participants with narcolepsy taking LXB > 9 g/night experienced further overall symptom benefit compared with 9 g/night at baseline, suggesting some patients may require higher dosages to achieve optimal therapeutic benefit. The safety profile, including respiratory safety parameters, was comparable to that observed at 9 g/night. Findings demonstrate that LXB can be utilized at dosages up to 12 g/night to optimize effectiveness, supporting individualized clinical decision-making. Low-sodium oxybate (LXB; Xywav®) is a medication used to treat narcolepsy symptoms. The recommended dosage range is 6 g to 9 g/night, but it has been reported that some people take higher dosages (greater than 9 g/night). This study was the first to evaluate higher dosages of LXB (greater than 9 g/night and up to 12 g/night). Before this study, these higher dosages had not been formally studied. This study was done to evaluate whether higher dosages improve narcolepsy symptoms and/or impact side effects. LXB is a central nervous system depressant, so there was a need to see if higher dosages could impact breathing during sleep. The study enrolled people who were already taking LXB at 9 g/night (the highest recommended dose) and who clinicians thought could benefit from higher dosages. While taking LXB 9 g/night, participants completed tests to measure their symptoms. Participants then worked with a clinician for 2 to 8 weeks to find a higher LXB dosage that worked best for them. The highest dosage allowed was 12 g/night. By the end of the study, the average dosage taken was 11.1 g/night, and almost half (44%) of participants were taking 12 g/night. Once participants found their ideal dosage, they stayed on this dosage for 2 weeks. Then, they repeated the same tests that they completed before. Forty-eight participants started the study. Forty-four completed the study. With higher LXB dosages (compared to 9 g/night), participants on average had less excessive daytime sleepiness, fewer cataplexy attacks, and less severe narcolepsy symptoms. At the beginning of the study when taking LXB 9 g/night, most participants (61.4%) said their disease was severe. After taking higher dosages, this dropped to 29.5%. At the end of the study, nearly all (92.3%) said their overall disease improved with higher dosages. Nobody said their disease worsened. In general, higher dosages did not worsen breathing during sleep. The most common side effects were nausea, vomiting, and headache. These side effects are similar to what is commonly experienced with lower dosages. This study shows that LXB treatment can be adjusted for each person. Higher dosages (>9-12 g/night) may help some patients find further improvement in their narcolepsy symptoms.

articles.title: Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Non-Invasive Assessment Across the Continuum.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) is a key determinant of surgical candidacy, locoregional therapy safety, and systemic treatment outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet its non-invasive assessment remains challenging because the Baveno criteria were derived in HCC-free cirrhosis. This review synthesises current evidence on non-invasive tests (NITs) for CSPH across the HCC care continuum, organised around three clinical scenarios: pre-operative assessment, on-treatment monitoring, and pre-immunotherapy evaluation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Liver stiffness-based Baveno rule-out retains value in early HCC but can miss haemodynamically confirmed CSPH in up to 23% of patients with favourable criteria. Spleen stiffness and imaging surrogates offer higher specificity, and longitudinal NIT monitoring is emerging as a need during locoregional and systemic therapy, which themselves can modify portal pressure. Real-world data report variceal bleeding in about 7% of patients receiving atezolizumab-bevacizumab, supporting variceal screening before anti-angiogenic treatment. AI-based multimodal models show promise in cirrhosis but lack HCC-specific validation. A scenario-based NIT strategy integrating liver stiffness, spleen stiffness, imaging collaterals, and selective HVPG measurement can guide CSPH assessment from surgical candidacy through systemic treatment. HCC-specific thresholds, longitudinal validation, and randomised evaluation of NSBB prophylaxis during immunotherapy are the highest-priority research areas.

articles.title: Six-month comparative outcomes of endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty versus laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: an MBSAQIP analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: North American data regarding long-term efficacy and durability of endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) are remarkably scarce outside of clinical trial settings hampering our understanding of its optimal role in the obesity care continuum. The aims of this study are to compare safety and efficacy of elective ESG versus laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) at 6 months using accredited MBSAQIP centers.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program (MBSAQIP) database for 2023 and merged with the 6‑month follow‑up data file. The primary objectives of the study were to characterize the long-term six-month changes in weight and metabolic comorbidities of ESG patients in contrast to their LSG counterparts. Logistic regression models were to evaluate for differences in six-month serious complications and emergency department readmissions between ESG and LSG.

RESULTS: A total of 115,476 patients were included, comprising 114,967 LSG and 509 ESG procedures. Patients undergoing ESG were slightly older (44.5 ± 11.2 vs. 42.4 ± 11.9 years, p = 0.0001) and had lower baseline BMI (40.9 ± 8.6 vs. 45.0 ± 7.8 kg/m2, p < 0.0001) and mean body weight (113.2 ± 28 vs. 124.5 ± 26.3 kg). At 6 months, LSG resulted in greater weight reduction, with larger BMI loss (8.2 ± 10.8 vs. 3.9 ± 12.0 kg/m2, p < 0.0001), and total weight loss (22.6 ± 35.6 vs. 11.1 ± 37.7 kg, p < 0.0001). For patients undergoing LSG, there was a near 50% reduction in medication/insulin-dependent diabetes along with improvements in rates of dyslipidemia, hypertension, and sleep apnea. Importantly, no clinically meaningful comorbidity improvements from baseline to 6 months were seen following ESG.

CONCLUSION: When compared to ESG at 6 months, LSG provides an improvement in total body weight loss, has a reduced operative time, and is associated with dramatic metabolic comorbidity improvement including a reduction in resolution of medication and insulin-dependent diabetes. No clinically meaningful comorbidity resolution was seen in patients receiving ESG compared to LSG at 6 months although this cohort was less comorbid at baseline.

articles.title: Comparison of medium-weight vs heavy-weight mesh in minimally invasive extraperitoneal ventral hernia repairs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive (MIS) extraperitoneal ventral hernia repair (VHR) has become increasingly common, however, limited data exist comparing medium-weight (MW) versus heavyweight (HW) mesh in this setting. We hypothesized that HW mesh in this context would be associated with decreased rates of hernia recurrence at 1 year and beyond compared to MW mesh.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative database, identifying adults who underwent MIS extraperitoneal (preperitoneal and/or retromuscular) VHR with either MW (40-60 g/m2) or HW (> 75 g/m2) uncoated permanent synthetic mesh from the inception of the registry to May 2025, with ≥1 year clinical or patient-reported follow-up. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for imbalances in baseline patient characteristics. The primary outcome was 1-year pragmatic hernia recurrence, defined as recurrence based on available elements of patient-reported, clinical and/or radiographic recurrence. Secondary outcomes included 30-day surgical site infection (SSI), surgical site occurrences (SSO), surgical site occurrences requiring procedural intervention (SSOPI).

RESULTS: 821 patients were identified. After propensity score matching, 238 patients remained (119 MW, 119 HW). Most baseline covariates were well-matched. Patients with umbilical hernias were more likely to receive MW mesh (80% vs. 65%, p =0.009), while patients receiving HW mesh were more likely to have subxiphoid hernias (5.9% vs 15%, p =0.020). There were no documented SSI at 30 days. The rates of SSO (p =0.696), SSOPI (p =0.498), and 30-day reoperation (p =0.999) were similar between groups. At 1-year, pragmatic recurrence was similar between MW and HW patients (7.6% vs 12.6%, p =0.196).

CONCLUSIONS: MW and HW mesh demonstrate comparable early and mid-term outcomes following MIS extraperitoneal VHR. Further prospective study and long-term follow-up are necessary as these techniques proliferate.

articles.title: Detection, characterization, and quantification of microplastics in human biological matrices: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in the environment represents an emerging risk to human health, with growing evidence of detection in human biological matrices. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the detection, quantification, and characterization of MPs in human biological matrices. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases. Original research articles published in English up to 2025 that involved human participants were included, specifically selecting observational studies. The 40 included studies confirmed MPs in multiple human biological matrices, including blood, urine, feces, placenta, breast milk, semen, lung, and heart tissue. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess the quality and risk of bias of the individual studies. Substantial methodological heterogeneity was observed in analytical techniques, including Fourier-transform infrared microspectroscopy (μFTIR), micro-Raman spectroscopy (μ-Raman), laser direct infrared spectroscopy (LDIR), and pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), as well as in the reporting units and limits of detection. Most studies reported fragments and fibers, with a predominance of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). NOS assessment showed that 52.5% of studies were of moderate quality, indicating that while the frequent detection of these particles suggests widespread human contact, significant methodological shortcomings and potential analytical overestimations limit the accurate quantification of systemic exposure and the strength of causal inferences. The widespread detection of MPs raises public health concerns regarding chronic exposure and potential health implications. However, current evidence remains insufficient to establish causal relationships, underscoring the urgent need for rigorous epidemiological studies.

articles.title: Indocyanine Green Angiography Reduces Ischemic Complications in Immediate Implant-Based Breast Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skin- and nipple-sparing mastectomy followed by immediate implant-based breast reconstruction (IBBR) has grown substantially in clinical practice, yet mastectomy skin flap necrosis (MSFN) persists as a clinically significant source of morbidity. Intraoperative indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) enables real-time, objective quantification of skin flap perfusion, but its specific effect on IBBR outcomes has yet to be established through dedicated meta-analytic synthesis. This study aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative ICGA-guided decision-making lowers the incidence of MSFN and related surgical complications relative to conventional clinical appraisal in immediate IBBR.

METHODS: Four databases-PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library-were searched through March 2026 for comparative studies of immediate IBBR. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the Mantel-Haenszel method.

RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 1,356 reconstructed breasts (655 ICGA; 701 clinical assessment) met inclusion criteria. ICGA was associated with significantly lower risks of overall MSFN (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.73) and severe MSFN (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.22-0.55), as well as reduced return to the operating room, surgical-site infection, and flap salvage procedures. Overall complication rates, hematoma/seroma, and implant loss were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative ICGA significantly reduced the risk of overall MSFN by approximately 43% and severe MSFN by approximately 65%, with fewer unplanned reoperations and flap salvage procedures, without affecting non-ischemic outcomes. The evidence supports selective incorporation of ICGA into IBBR surgical protocols, with particular emphasis on patients carrying elevated perfusion-related risk.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine Ratings, please refer to Table of Contents or online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Development of an Injectable Boronic Ester Nanocomposite Hydrogel for pH- and Thermo-Responsive Gentamicin Delivery and Antibacterial Activity.
articles.abstract: Infected wounds require localized antimicrobial treatment strategies that provide sustained drug release, reduce systemic antibiotic exposure, and promote tissue repair. This study reports an infection-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform based on dynamic covalent boronic ester chemistry for triggered topical antibiotic delivery. Phenylboronic acid (PBA)-functionalized cationic nanoparticles (PBA-NPs) were employed as three-dimensional crosslinkers and combined with poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) to construct an injectable nanocomposite hydrogel via reversible boronic ester interactions. The nanocomposite hydrogel was characterized for morphology, injectability, rheological properties, stimuli-responsive behavior, in vitro antibiotic release, and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The resulting nanocomposite hydrogel exhibited a gel-sol transition at 39.7°C, while the pH-dependent chemistry of the boronic ester network supports enhanced network dissociation under mildly acidic conditions (pH 6.5). This dual pH- and thermo-responsive behavior enabled on-demand release of encapsulated gentamicin sulfate while preserving viscoelastic recovery consistent with dynamic network reconstruction. The cationic PBA-NPs exhibited intrinsic antibacterial activity and generated enhanced antimicrobial effects when combined with gentamicin. Zones of inhibition reached 22 mm (S. aureus) and 25 mm (P. aeruginosa) at 3% drug loading. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dynamic covalent boronic ester nanocomposite hydrogel represents a promising injectable platform for infection-responsive localized antibiotic delivery and antibacterial wound management.

articles.title: Clesrovimab in the new era of RSV prevention: one season, one dose, one chance.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in infancy worldwide. Historically, prevention relied on monthly palivizumab administration for selected high-risk infants, despite evidence that a substantial proportion of severe RSV disease occurs in previously healthy term infants. The recent introduction of maternal RSV vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies has transformed the prevention landscape. Clesrovimab (MK-1654; Enflonsia) is a long-acting monoclonal antibody designed to provide season-long protection following a single dose. In the pivotal phase 2b/3 CLEVER trial, clesrovimab reduced RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization among infants entering their first RSV season, with a safety profile comparable to placebo. The absolute risk reduction for RSV hospitalization was approximately 1.9 percentage points, corresponding to an estimated number needed to treat of 51 infants over 150 days of follow-up. In this policy-focused clinical perspective informed by a narrative review, we examine the emerging role of clesrovimab within contemporary RSV prevention strategies. We discuss efficacy, safety, implementation challenges, economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps, including the absence of head-to-head comparisons with nirsevimab, limited post-licensure data, and uncertainties regarding long-term effectiveness and affordability. Future success will depend not only on efficacy but also on equitable access, sustainable implementation, and ongoing surveillance. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The emergence of long-acting monoclonal antibodies has expanded preventive options for infants at risk of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease during their first RSV season. For clinicians, the key shift is that RSV prevention is increasingly being considered within a broader population-health framework rather than solely as a risk-based intervention for selected high-risk groups. Clesrovimab, alongside nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination, represents one component of an evolving prevention strategy aimed at reducing RSV-associated morbidity and hospitalization during early infancy. From a practical perspective, successful implementation will depend on timely administration, integration into neonatal discharge planning and well-child care pathways, and coordination with maternal immunization programs. As RSV prevention moves into routine clinical practice, equitable access, sustained coverage, affordability, and ongoing post-licensure surveillance will be as important as efficacy demonstrated in clinical trials. Ultimately, the greatest reductions in RSV-related hospitalization are likely to result from effective delivery of preventive strategies to the infants at highest risk during the RSV season. KEY POINTS: RSV continues to impose a substantial burden on infants worldwide despite decades of clinical recognition and supportive care. Most RSV hospitalizations occur in infants without traditional high-risk conditions, highlighting the limitations of selective prophylaxis strategies. Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSV vaccination have transformed prevention from a niche intervention into a population-level public health strategy. Clesrovimab demonstrated significant protection against RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in healthy infants entering their first RSV season. Future research should focus on comparative effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, long-term safety, implementation in low-resource settings, and optimization of delivery strategies to maximize population impact.

articles.title: Japan at the limits of viability: national experience and evolving outcomes of infants born at 22-23 weeks' gestation.
articles.abstract: Infants born at 22-23 weeks' gestation represent the limits of viability with substantial international variation in outcomes. Japan has consistently reported some of the highest survival rates; however, the underlying healthcare systems and clinical practices have not been comprehensively synthesized. This review summarizes Japan's national experience using data from a nationwide network database, epidemiologic studies, clinical practice surveys, and international comparisons. Survival at discharge is approximately 60% and 80% for infants born at 22 and 23 weeks' gestation, respectively, with relatively low rates of severe intraventricular hemorrhage and necrotizing enterocolitis. Key healthcare system features include regionalized perinatal care promoting antenatal maternal transfer, a nationwide clinical network for benchmarking, and universal health insurance. Clinical practice is characterized by active resuscitation and meticulous, individualized, pathophysiology-based management, including invasive respiratory support, echocardiography-guided hemodynamic management, intensive neuroprotection, and specialized nursing care. The effectiveness of these practices remains uncertain, and further research is needed. Continuous outcome monitoring and quality improvement are essential to refine context-specific strategies. IMPACT: This review provides the comprehensive synthesis of Japan's national experience in the care of infants born at 22-23 weeks' gestation, integrating outcomes with healthcare system structures and clinical practices. It identifies key system-level and clinical factors-such as regionalized perinatal care, nationwide data-driven quality improvement, and pathophysiology-based management-that may contribute to Japan's high survival rates and relatively low morbidity. It highlights the importance of integrated "package-of-care" approaches and continuous outcome monitoring, offering insights that may inform strategies to improve outcomes at the limits of viability globally.

articles.title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

articles.title: Give me the good news: four science stories to brighten your day.
Infection-associated acute kidney injury in resource-limited settings.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and life-threatening complication of infection, and a major contributor to preventable morbidity and mortality in resource-limited settings. In these contexts, AKI is commonly driven by a broad range of infections, including enteric, zoonotic and vector-borne diseases, that occur outside the hospital and in populations with limited access to diagnostics and supportive care. Infection-associated AKI results from diverse and overlapping mechanisms, including hypovolaemia, inflammation, endothelial and microcirculatory dysfunction, haemolysis and direct kidney involvement, and is increasingly shaped by environmental stressors such as heat exposure and climate-related disruptions that amplify dehydration, infection risk and kidney injury. Susceptibility to AKI is further influenced by reduced kidney reserve, which reflects nephron endowment and prior kidney injury, and can be silently depleted by severe or recurrent insults. Repeated infectious exposures and incomplete recovery from AKI might affect long-term kidney health and survival, but these trajectories remain poorly characterized. Challenges in timely recognition of both AKI and infections contribute to delayed treatment and worse outcomes, particularly among vulnerable populations. Strengthening infection prevention, improving context-appropriate diagnostics for AKI and infection, minimizing iatrogenic kidney injury, addressing environmental drivers and developing affordable scalable kidney replacement therapies are essential to reducing inequities and improving long-term kidney health globally.

articles.title: Incremental value of DXA-derived visceral versus total adiposity beyond routine anthropometric assessment for hypertension discrimination: a population-based study.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Hypertension is strongly linked to obesity, yet it remains uncertain whether DXA-derived measures of adiposity improve hypertension discrimination beyond routine anthropometric assessment and whether any incremental value reflects visceral rather than total adiposity. This study examined whether DXA-derived visceral and total adiposity provide incremental discriminatory value beyond routine anthropometric assessment for hypertension discrimination. We analyzed 7817 adults aged 20-59 years from the 2013 to 2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with valid DXA measurements. Discriminatory performance and the incremental value of DXA-derived adiposity measures beyond anthropometric assessment were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, model fit, and reclassification metrics. Among routinely available anthropometric measures, waist circumference demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for hypertension (AUC 0.791, 95% CI: 0.780-0.802). Addition of DXA-derived visceral adiposity significantly improved discrimination (AUC 0.865, ΔAUC = 0.074) and significantly improved model fit beyond waist circumference (P < 0.001), whereas total adiposity measured by fat mass index provided negligible incremental value (ΔAUC = 0.0020) and did not improve model fit. Reclassification metrics yielded consistent findings, and results generally remained robust across sensitivity analyses; however, when hypertension was defined using measured blood pressure alone, the incremental improvement was attenuated (ΔAUC = 0.012 vs. 0.074). Among DXA-derived adiposity measures, only visceral adiposity provided meaningful incremental discriminatory value beyond the best-performing routine anthropometric measure, whereas total adiposity did not. These findings suggest that when DXA-based body composition assessment is performed, the clinically relevant information may be derived from visceral rather than total adiposity.

articles.title: Exploring extracts from Wendlandia Uvariifolia Subsp. Chinensis (Merr.) Cowan as natural phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors with preclinical anti-erectile dysfunction activity.
articles.abstract: Wendlandia uvariifolia subsp. chinensis (Merr.) Cowan is a traditional medicinal plant used by the Li ethnic group in Hainan Province, China, for the treatment of herpes zoster. However, its pharmacological properties remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate its phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitory activity, identify the active components, and explore its therapeutic potential for erectile dysfunction. Through high-throughput screening of 1200 traditional Chinese herbal medicines, this plant was identified as a potential phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor. Bioactivity-guided fractionation and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis identified the petroleum ether fraction as the most active fraction, while phytol, one of its identified constituents, inhibited phosphodiesterase type 5 in vitro with an IC₅₀ value of 2.5 ± 0.1 μmol/L. In H₂O₂-injured endothelial cells, petroleum ether fraction significantly restored nitric oxide production. In a paroxetine-induced erectile dysfunction rat model, the fraction improved sexual behavior parameters, restored NO/cGMP signaling, and alleviated pathological remodeling and fibrosis in the corpus cavernosum. In a diabetes mellitus-associated erectile dysfunction rat model, the fraction also improved corpus cavernosum architecture, increased smooth muscle content, and reduced fibrosis, although the increase in the intracavernous pressure/mean arterial pressure ratio did not reach statistical significance. Overall, the results suggest the preclinical anti-erectile dysfunction potential of petroleum ether fraction and support its further mechanistic, pharmacokinetic, safety, and translational evaluation.

articles.title: Dengue virus infection.
Dengue virus infection.
articles.abstract: Dengue is an acute febrile disease caused by the Aedes mosquito-borne dengue viruses (DENV-1 to DENV-4). Annually, approximately 100 million people fall ill with dengue, which can cause debilitating pain and discomfort, reducing both physical functioning and quality of life. Some patients progress to life-threatening inflammation-driven circulatory failure. Disease burden remains primarily in urban centres; however, factors including increased travel and climate change are rapidly expanding the geographical distribution of dengue to rural and peri-urban environments. Dengue is diagnosed based on compatible clinical features, detection of viral RNA or antigens, or serological testing, depending on the phase of illness. There is no licensed antiviral or host-directed therapy for dengue; management is supportive, with close clinical monitoring and judicious fluid replacement to prevent circulatory failure while avoiding fluid overload. Thus, there is an increasing need for clinicians to be familiar with the clinical features, disease burden and management of dengue, along with the newly recognized post-acute sequelae. Although dengue vaccines have been licensed in several countries, their use has been restricted by uncertainties in dengue pathogenesis. Attention should be focused on how to use currently available vaccines to create the foundation of a larger strategy to mitigate dengue transmission and maximize public health impact.

articles.title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds.
articles.abstract: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics. MRI outcomes included total grey matter, white matter (WM), WM hyperintensities (WMHs), subcortical volumes, small vessel disease (SVD) score, cortical thicknesses, and fractional anisotropy (FA) fibre tracts. We adjusted for sex, age, principal components, and sex interactions, and corrected for multiple comparisons. We found no associations in the total sample. In males, both PGLSs were associated with smaller WMHs volume and lower SVD burden, and a thicker cortex of pars triangularis, pars opercularis, and insula. Our findings suggest a possible link between genetic propensity for longevity and lower cerebrovascular burden and certain cortical grey matter areas in males.

articles.title: Reframing Trisomy 13 and 18 Care: Moving Beyond the Myth of "Incompatibility With Life" in a South African and Low-and Middle-Income Country Context.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
articles.abstract: Trisomy 13 (T13) and trisomy 18 (T18) have historically been described as "lethal" or "incompatible with life," contributing to diagnosis-based limitations of care. Contemporary evidence demonstrates greater heterogeneity in survival and outcomes than previously recognized, including among selected children receiving intensive care or cardiac surgery. Parental perspectives further challenge assumptions that quality of life and benefit can be inferred from diagnosis alone. This Commentary draws on contemporary evidence and multidisciplinary stakeholder discussions convened in Johannesburg in August 2025 to consider the implications for South Africa and comparable resource-constrained settings. South African pathways are shaped by inequities between public and private healthcare, uneven access to prenatal screening and diagnosis, limited specialist capacity, variable referral and care coordination, and the absence of nationally standardized T13/T18-specific guidance. Published local evidence on survival, intervention and family experiences remains limited. We argue that T13/T18 should be approached as medically complex and potentially life-limiting conditions requiring transparent, individualized and proportionate decision-making rather than predetermined non-intervention. Priorities include strengthened professional training, coordinated multidisciplinary referral pathways, balanced counselling and shared decision-making, integration of palliative care alongside disease-directed care, regional centers of expertise, improved data generation, rights-aligned governance and contextually appropriate adaptation of international guidance.

articles.title: Association Between the GMI/HbA1c Ratio and Microvascular Complications in Type 1 Diabetes: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify whether the glucose management indicator (GMI)/glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) ratio (GMI/HbA1c ratio) is an independent predictor of microvascular complications in Type 1 diabetes (T1D).

DESIGN AND METHODS: Multicentre, cross-sectional, observational study including subjects with T1D with at least 5 years of evolution, users of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with a coverage ≥ 80% 56 days prior to HbA1c. Logistic regression models were used to identify the factors independently associated with grouped microvascular complications and ocular disease.

RESULTS: As per data, 1315 participants were included. Patients were classified into tertiles based on the GMI/HbA1c ratio. High glycators were older than intermediate and low glycators (55.4 vs. 53.4 vs. 50.8 years; p < 0.001), respectively. Differences were also observed among the three groups with regard to average glucose (156.3 vs. 161.8 vs. 166.1 mg/dL; p < 0.001), time in range (66.3% vs. 62.9% vs. 59.9%; p < 0.001), time in tight range (42.9% vs. 39.9% vs. 37.1%; p < 0.001), coefficient of variation (34.5% vs. 34.9% vs. 35.6%; p = 0.023), GMI (7% vs. 7.2% vs. 7.3%; p < 0.001) and HbA1c (8.1% vs. 7.3% vs. 6.6%; p < 0.001). In the high glycators group, the prevalence of microvascular complications was higher than in the intermediate and low glycators (38.9% vs. 28.2% vs. 23.7%; p < 0.001), respectively.
