Also, the prevalence of ocular disease (31% vs. 20.2% vs. 19.7%; p < 0.001), nephropathy (14.9% vs. 8.3% vs. 6.2%; p < 0.001) and polyneuropathy (10.6% vs. 6.8% vs. 3.4%; p < 0.001) was higher in high glycators, The GMI/HbA1c ratio was significantly associated with the presence of grouped microvascular complications (OR 0.71; 95% CI: 0.61-0.81; p < 0.001) and ocular disease (OR 0.71; 95% CI: 0.61-0.82; p < 0.001) after adjusting for clinical ad glucometric variables.

CONCLUSIONS: The GMI/HbA1c ratio is associated with microvascular complications in this study. These results highlight the potential of this parameter in routine clinical practice for stratifying the risk of complications and for establishing individualized control goals and screening strategies.

articles.title: Factors Associated With SGLT2 Inhibitor Initiation in Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes: A Real-World Analysis From German Primary Care.

Machine Learning Models Combining [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET Radiomics and Clinical Features to Predict Overall Survival for Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer Treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains incurable despite recent therapeutic advances. [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT (lutetium-177 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen radioligand therapy) provides meaningful clinical benefit in selected patients. However, ∼30% of the patients do not respond to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. Although several baseline prognostic factors are well known, reliable pretherapeutic predictive biomarkers are still lacking. We developed and compared several predictive machine learning (ML) models integrating clinical, biochemical, and imaging data, including [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET (gallium-68 labelled prostate-specific membrane antigen ligand positron emission tomography) radiomic features, to estimate overall survival (OS) in patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT.

METHODS: This retrospective monocentric study included 102 patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA between January 2022 and March 2024. Five lesions per patient were segmented on their pretherapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/computed tomography (CT) scans. Radiomic features were extracted following Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative guidelines. Multimodal ML models integrating clinical, genomic, biochemical, and imaging features (including radiomics) were developed to predict OS.

RESULTS: Median OS of the total cohort was 11.2 mo. Intralesional homogeneity, characterized by the second-order radiomic feature normalized inverse difference moment, was associated with shorter OS (p = 0.025). The best-performing ML model achieved a 12-mo area under the curve (AUC) of 0.778 by combining 22 clinical, biochemical, genomic, and radiomic features. The model leveraging PET data alone achieved strong performance, with an AUC comparable to the clinical model (0.715 vs 0.766).

CONCLUSIONS: ML models based on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, including radiomic features, offer a noninvasive, standardized, and widely accessible approach to predict OS in patients with mCRPC treated with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT. This study highlights the strong predictive potential of PSMA PET imaging for patient stratification in a real-world setting.

articles.title: Factors influencing the use of therapeutic play among pediatric nurses: The role of distraction skills and therapeutic relationship levels.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of therapeutic play use among pediatric nurses and to examine whether distraction skills, therapeutic relationship competence, and selected sociodemographic and professional characteristics predict its use.

METHODS: This descriptive and correlational study was conducted with 165 pediatric nurses. Data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, the Distracting Ingenuity Promotion Scale (DIPS), and the Therapeutic Relationship Assessment Scale-Nurse (TRAS-Nurse).

RESULTS: Therapeutic play was reported by 44.8% of nurses, and 6.1% had received formal training in therapeutic play or distraction techniques. DIPS and TRAS-Nurse total scores were significantly and inversely associated (p < .001), with the same pattern observed across all subscale pairings (p < .001). DIPS and TRAS-Nurse scores, at both total and subscale levels, were not significant predictors of therapeutic play use after adjustment for relevant covariates. Clinical unit was the only consistent predictor across all models, with lower therapeutic play use among nurses working in critical care settings (p < .01).

CONCLUSION: Therapeutic play remains underutilized in pediatric nursing practice. Its use appears to be influenced predominantly by clinical and organizational conditions at the unit level rather than by nurses' self-reported distraction skills or therapeutic relationship quality. The inverse association observed between these two competencies requires further examination to clarify its clinical and methodological significance.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Structured, unit-specific training programs, together with adequate material and environmental resources, are needed to strengthen the integration of therapeutic play into routine pediatric nursing practice, particularly in critical care settings.

articles.title: Paediatric bone and soft-tissue sarcomas in Ireland: Epidemiology, management and outcomes.
articles.journal: The surgeon : journal of the Royal Colleges of Surgeons of Edinburgh and Ireland
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric bone and soft tissue sarcomas are rare malignancies, that typically require multimodal oncologic therapy and technically demanding surgery delivered within a specialist multidisciplinary team setting. The epidemiology, management and outcomes of paediatric sarcoma in Ireland have not yet been described.

METHODS: This was an observational study of a consecutive cohort of patients aged <16 years with primary bone or soft-tissue sarcoma managed by Ireland's national sarcoma service over a 10-year period. The epidemiology, management, and outcomes of these patients were reported. The primary outcome was overall survival which was reported using Kaplan-Meier estimates. The factors associated with survival were also analysed.

RESULTS: Eighty-eight patients were included, of whom 53.4% (47/88) were male. Osteosarcoma was the most common diagnosis (46.6%, 41/88), followed by Ewing's sarcoma (25%, 22/88). Soft-tissue sarcoma accounted for 25% (22/88). Primary sites most frequently involved the femur (33%, 29/88), tibia (18.2%, 16/88), humerus (15.9%, 14/88) and pelvis (11.4%, 10/88). Metastatic pulmonary disease was present at diagnosis in 33% (29/88) of patients. Seventy-six patients underwent surgery. Limb-salvage endoprosthetic reconstruction was most common at 46.1% (35/76), followed by en bloc tumour resection in 36.8% (28/76) and amputation in 17.1% (13/76). All patients with a diagnosis of primary bone sarcoma received multi-modal chemotherapy guided by a multidisciplinary team. Overall mortality rate was 25% (22/88). Estimated 5-year survivorship was 81.5% for osteosarcoma, 93.3% for Ewing sarcoma, and 90.9% for soft-tissue sarcoma. Mortality was highest when metastatic disease was present at the time of diagnosis (51.7% vs 11.9%, p < .001), (HR 2.81, 95% CI 0.96-8.25; p = .061).

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of paediatric sarcoma in Ireland aligns with other European countries. Overall survivorship was relatively high, with metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis associated with lower survivorship. This study provides a benchmark for the current epidemiology and outcomes for children with sarcoma in Ireland.

articles.title: Why did residents choose neurology? Motivational profile and influence of demographic and career factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global and European burden of neurological disorders is rising, with insufficient neurologists to meet current needs. Understanding residents' motivation to choose Neurology is crucial to optimize teaching. This study aimed to characterize the motivational profile of Neurology residents and examine its associations with demographic and career factors.

METHODS: In this national cross-sectional observational survey, 131 French Neurology residents completed a validated motivation questionnaire assessing intrinsic, extrinsic, and amotivation components. Composite scores were calculated for each dimension, and a delta motivation score (intrinsic minus extrinsic) was computed. Associations between motivation and demographic/career variables, including intended academic/clinical scientist career, were analyzed. Correlation, linear regression, and repeated-measures ANCOVA were conducted.

RESULTS: Participants were 54.2% female, mean age 27.1±3.0 years. Intrinsic motivation was significantly predominant (Wilks' Lambda=0.531, P<0.001) (knowledge M=24.5±2.9; stimulation M=21.5±3.9; achievement M=19.9±4.2), exceeding extrinsic motivation (identified M=23.4±3.0; introjected M=13.4±5.6; external regulation M=14.7±4.6) and amotivation (M=6.0±3.5). Delta motivation was negatively associated with age (β=-0.339, P=0.005) and positively with year of residency (β=0.277, P=0.002) and a planned academic/clinical scientist career (β=0.210, P=0.011). Residents planning an academic/clinical scientist career had a significantly different motivational profile (Wilks' Lambda=0.901, P=0.041) because of higher intrinsic motivation for achievement (P=0.006).

CONCLUSION: Neurology residents exhibit a predominantly intrinsic motivation profile. The factors associated with were: age, residency year, and academic career intentions. These findings highlight the importance of supporting and preserving intrinsic motivation throughout training to ensure engagement and prepare the future neurological workforce.

articles.title: Exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling in COPD skeletal muscle dysfunction: From sedentary behavior to molecular rehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a multisystem disorder in which extrapulmonary manifestations substantially contribute to disease burden. Among these, skeletal muscle dysfunction (SMD) represents a major determinant of exercise intolerance, reduced physical activity, impaired quality of life, and mortality. Growing evidence suggests that physical inactivity is not merely a consequence of advanced COPD but may act as an early and potentially modifiable driver of skeletal muscle deterioration, being detectable even in patients with mild disease and potentially preceding clinically relevant airflow limitation. In parallel, epigenetic mechanisms-including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs-have emerged as key regulators of gene expression capable of integrating environmental and behavioral stimuli over time. These mechanisms may contribute to molecular pathways associated with inactivity-related muscle dysfunction. Conversely, exercise induces epigenetic adaptations in human skeletal muscle and experimental models that provide biological plausibility for a similar response in COPD. Nonetheless, direct evidence from human COPD skeletal muscle remains limited, particularly regarding exercise- or pulmonary rehabilitation-induced epigenetic remodeling and its relationship with clinical outcomes. This narrative review therefore distinguishes direct COPD skeletal-muscle findings from evidence derived from other COPD tissues, non-COPD human muscle, and experimental models, and evaluates the hypothesis that epigenetic adaptation may contribute to the biological effects of pulmonary rehabilitation.

articles.title: Haemodynamic effects of induction agents are context-dependent. Comment on Br J Anaesth Advance Access published on Apr 7, 2026, doi: 10.1016/j.bja.2026.02.023.
Changes in modifiable dementia risk factors and subjective cognitive decline in mid and later life.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Exposure to modifiable dementia risk factors (MDRFs) contributes substantially to dementia risk across the life course. Less is known about persistence and changes in these factors during mid- and later life and how they relate to early neurophysiological changes associated with dementia. This study examined rates and changes in MDRFs over two years and their associations with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among older adults.

DESIGN: Cohort study.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants were 2370 adults aged 55-92 years (M = 68.54, SD = 7.15; 56.5% female) who completed the 2018 and 2020 waves of a longitudinal survey of ageing in New Zealand.

MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported hypertension, diabetes, hearing impairment, vision impairment, current smoking, hazardous alcohol use, physical inactivity, depression, and loneliness were classified into four categories across waves: stable absence, reduction, onset, and stable presence. SCD was assessed in 2020. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between MDRF categories and SCD.

RESULTS: Survey-weighted responses indicated 8.6% of older adults experienced SCD. Diabetes, hearing impairment, current vision impairment, stable presence of physical inactivity, depression, and current loneliness were associated with increased odds of SCD.

CONCLUSIONS: Both the onset and reduction of psychosocial and sensory MDRFs in mid- and later life have measurable implications for subjective cognitive outcomes in a general population sample. Prevention and reduction of diabetes, sensory loss, physical inactivity, depression, and social isolation represent meaningful targets for supporting cognitive well-being among older adults.

articles.title: Post-Transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder After Successful Treatment of Graft-Versus Host Disease Following Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a rare complication after liver transplantation. Post-transplantation lymphoproliferative disorders (PTLD) are lymphomas that develop after transplantation due to the immunosuppression. Both disorders have high mortality risks. A 65-year-old male patient underwent LDLT from his son due to cryptogenic liver cirrhosis. In the third month, the patient diagnosed as GVHD with the initial symptom being skin changes. The patient was treated with high-dose steroids and extracorporeal photopheresis. There was gastrointestinal and bone marrow involvement. On the 11th month, the patient suffered from lymphadenopathy and was diagnosed as PTLD. The patient was treated with Rituxima, ruxolitinib. The patient is still alive with good performance. This is the first case of PTLD occurring after GVHD. Treatments such as extracorporeal photopheresis and ruxolitinib used in this case resulted in successful survival.

articles.title: Successful First-Line Haploidentical Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in an Elderly Patient With Severe Aplastic Anemia and Complex Comorbidities: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Standard management guidelines generally recommend immunosuppressive therapy (IST) as first-line treatment for older patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA), whereas the role of upfront haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) in this population remains uncertain, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on post-transplant day +12, and platelet independence was achieved on day +13. Donor chimerism reached 99.6% by day +14 and remained within the complete-chimerism range through the latest available assessment in January 2026. In late December 2025 and January 2026, the patient developed cytomegalovirus infection accompanied by transient trilineage cytopenia; after anti-CMV treatment with maribavir, the infection was controlled and peripheral blood counts subsequently recovered. At the most recent clinical follow-up on August 6, 2026, approximately 17 months after transplantation, no chronic graft-versus-host disease had developed, the previous lung adenocarcinoma remained in remission, and the thrombotic condition remained clinically stable. This case suggests that upfront haplo-HSCT combined with UC-MSCs may represent a feasible individualized treatment option for carefully selected older patients with SAA who lack matched donors, although broader conclusions require larger studies and longer follow-up.

articles.title: Author's reply: beyond predictive values - clarifying the prognostic role of RPR in alcohol-related cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver

articles.title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Prosthetic and Implant Associated Infections.
articles.abstract: Implant-associated infections are an expanding clinical challenge as joint arthroplasty, cardiac devices, vascular grafts, and spinal hardware become increasingly common. Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) alone affects a substantial proportion of revisions, carrying high cost and morbidity. 18F-FDGfluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT, leveraging glucose hypermetabolism in inflammatory cells, offers pooled sensitivity of 85% to 89% and specificity of 86% to 93% for PJI, distinguishing infection from expected physiologic postoperative uptake. The 2024 EANM/SNMMI joint guideline (v2.0) standardizes protocols and interpretation criteria across implant types. This review synthesizes pathogenesis, imaging patterns, technical optimization, and emerging modalities for implant infection imaging.

articles.title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET in Rheumatologic and Autoimmune Disorders.
articles.abstract: FDG PET detects the silent inflammation of autoimmune and rheumatologic diseases even before tissue damage, as activated leukocytes overexpress glucose transporters. It has an important role in large vessel vasculitis which includes early diagnosis, disease monitoring and response assessment to treatment. In inflammatory arthritides, it quantifies synovitis and enthesitis and detects early treatment response. In connective tissue and immunoglobulin G4 related diseases, whole body imaging maps silent disease, helps exclude malignancy, and guides biopsy. It is central to cardiac sarcoidosis and an early test in fever of unknown origin.

articles.title: Approach to Thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: Thrombocytopenia ranges from benign to life-threatening, requiring a systematic evaluation including history, physical examination, peripheral blood smear review, and targeted laboratory testing. Pseudothrombocytopenia must be excluded. Mechanisms of thrombocytopenia include decreased platelet production, decreased survival, and splenic sequestration. In the inpatient setting, clinicians should consider postoperative thrombocytopenia, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), other drug-induced thrombocytopenias, extracorporeal device-related causes, infection, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). In the outpatient setting, selected causes of thrombocytopenia include immune thrombocytopenia, chronic DIC, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), and myelodysplastic syndrome, among others. Early recognition and prompt management of life-threatening conditions such as HIT and TTP is critical.

articles.title: Socioeconomics and biodiversity in cities: moving beyond patterns to mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Socioeconomic status-biodiversity associations are widely reported in cities. However, most studies remain correlational and cannot distinguish whether socioeconomic status drives biodiversity change, biodiversity shapes socioeconomic outcomes, or whether observed patterns reflect biodiversity gains versus losses. We propose a unifying framework organizing established mechanisms from diverse urban research into four hypothesized causal pathways: (A) investment-driven biodiversity enhancement, (B) disinvestment-driven biodiversity degradation, (C) biodiversity-driven socioeconomic improvement, and (D) biodiversity loss reinforcing socioeconomic decline. This framework supports pathway-specific study designs and helps practitioners anticipate whether biodiversity interventions will reduce or exacerbate inequality. Shifting from pattern description to mechanism identification is essential for credible inference and for informing urban planning and governance interventions aimed at reducing environmental inequality.

articles.title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg CO2eq.

CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

articles.title: [Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure: Towards enlargement of implantations in centres without on-site cardiac surgery].
articles.abstract: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure is now an established strategy for thromboembolic prevention in atrial fibrillation. However, the organizational requirements governing its performance remain heterogeneous across regulations and healthcare systems, particularly in France. In this context, it is relevant to assess whether, in experienced centers, an organizational model based on specific expertise and a rapid surgical referral pathway could provide a safe alternative to the presence of on-site cardiac surgery. This article is in favor of extension in France of percutaneous left atrial appendage closure in centres without on-site cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration. Therefore, vision-language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well-established treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but it is still not known which patients will be good long-term responders. Therefore, this study proposes a physician-inspired visual question answering (VQA) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T or [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3-dimensional image encoder, the domain-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross-modal transformer to process baseline and interim (after 2 cycles) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query. The model was trained to predict 24-mo survival, and performance was compared with state-of-the-art approaches. External validation was performed with the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 cohort. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state-of-the-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query-free attention multimodal fusion model. Specifically, it achieved 81.8% accuracy (95% CI, 0.52-0.95) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate-specific antigen measurements. External validation of the VQA showed 71.9% accuracy (95% CI, 0.53-0.86) after few-shot fine-tuning, with further improvement over all state-of-the-art approaches in survival stratification. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed (log-rank test, P = 0.76). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve (0.75) among the evaluated models. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance. Conclusion: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: [18F]F-AraG PET Imaging of Immunometabolic Activity in Individuals Without Malignancy.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: [18F]F-AraG is a clinical-stage PET tracer in immuno-oncology that accumulates in activated T cells and tissues with high mitochondrial biogenesis. Characterizing its distribution in individuals without malignancy is essential for interpreting immunometabolic states relevant to cancer biology. Methods: Twenty adults without active malignancy underwent a single [18F]F-AraG PET/CT scan, with tracer uptake assessed in relation to clinical history, medications, and demographic and physiologic factors. Results: Bilateral brown adipose tissue activation was identified in 3 participants receiving potentially brown adipose tissue-activating medications, in the absence of cold exposure or fasting. One showed elevated vertebral bone marrow uptake, previously linked to poor survival in immune checkpoint inhibitor-treated lung cancer. One of 2 participants with breast implants showed asymmetric periimplant uptake. Posterior pulmonary uptake occurred in a subset of participants, often with prior respiratory conditions and thoracic lymph node uptake. Conclusion: Whole-body [18F]F-AraG PET captures diverse immunometabolic activity in individuals without malignancy, reflecting systemic processes that may influence cancer and treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Test-Retest Repeatability of [18F]FDG Uptake by Solid Tumors on PET/MRI: A Prospective, Multicenter Study Using the QIBA Protocol.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Prior oncologic PET/MRI repeatability studies have been limited by single-center designs, small cohorts, or select patient populations. Our primary aim was to estimate the test-retest repeatability of uptake metrics on [18F]FDG PET/MRI studies across a variety of cancer types. A secondary aim was to assess the impact of intersession μ-map variability on repeatability. Methods: In this prospective study involving 2 institutions with different PET/MRI scanners, subjects completing standard-of-care [18F]FDG PET/CT or MRI examinations were recruited to undergo 2 research [18F]FDG PET/MRIs (i.e., test and retest) within a 1-9 d period per Quantitative Imaging Biomarker Alliance specifications. Enrollment required at least 1 measurable lesion (long axis ≥ 2 cm, known or expected SUVmax ≥ 4.0) and no active oncologic therapy. SUVmax and SUVpeak were extracted from measurable lesions (1-5 per subject). At site 1, attenuation-coefficient maps (i.e., μ-maps) were inspected for substantial differences across sessions. Additionally, at site 1, the retest μ-map was coregistered to the test μ-map, and the PET attenuation-correction process was repeated for the test session based on the retest μ-map. Intersession repeatability was assessed via Bland-Altman plots, and within-subject coefficients of variation (wCVs) were calculated. Results: At site 1, 10 subjects with 11 measurable lesions were analyzed, and the wCVs for SUVmax and SUVpeak were 12.3% and 9.6%, respectively. At site 2, 11 subjects with 30 measurable lesions were analyzed, and the wCVs for SUVmax and SUVpeak were 9.5% and 8.8%, respectively. At site 1, repeating attenuation correction of the test PET data with the retest μ-map slightly improved repeatability, reducing the wCV to 10.1% for SUVmax and to 9.1% for SUVpeak For 8 of 11 lesions at site 1, the μ-map substitution altered the test-retest change by less than 5%, with no appreciable intersession μ-map differences or artifacts. Conclusion: The test-retest repeatability of SUVmax among hypermetabolic lesions on [18F]FDG PET/MRI, using data from 2 scanner models, was similar to the Quantitative Imaging Biomarker Alliance's wCV benchmark of 10%-12% for [18F]FDG PET/CT. Intersession μ-map variations had minimal negative impact on repeatability.

articles.title: B7H3-Targeted Molecular Imaging for Highly Specific Diagnosis and In Vivo Noninvasive Detection of B7H3 in Breast Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: B7 homolog 3 (B7H3) is widely expressed in solid tumors, but its role in the diagnosis of breast cancer is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH PET/CT in breast cancer patients. Methods: Thirty patients with diverse subtypes of breast cancer underwent both [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH and [18F]FDG PET/CT. Immunohistochemical staining for B7H3 was performed in 25 patients. Results: B7H3 positivity was detected in 84% of samples by immunohistochemistry. [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH demonstrated a higher lesion detection rate compared with [18F]FDG (96.8% vs. 92.4%) among 157 lesions. Median SUVmax was 9.5 in strongly positive lesions; bone metastases had the highest uptake (median SUVmax, 10.9). Imaging resulted in changing the stage or treatment in 8 patients. Hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative lesions showed the highest B7H3 positivity (87.5%) and uptake (median SUVmax, 10.5). Conclusion: [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH PET/CT offers high sensitivity for staging advanced breast cancer and noninvasive B7H3 screening. It may influence clinical decisions and appears to reveal subtype-specific uptake, with a tendency to favor hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative disease.

articles.title: Brain-Specific Quantification of Somatostatin Receptor Expression: SUVmax and SUVRsss as Quantitative Correlates of the Krenning Score in Meningioma.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Somatostatin receptor type 2 is highly expressed in meningiomas and can be quantified using [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET. The Krenning score, originally developed for [111In]In-octreotide scintigraphy, remains the standard visual grading system for somatostatin receptor expression and is widely used to guide eligibility for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. However, visual grading may not optimally translate to intracranial disease. This study evaluated the relationship between brain-specific quantitative PET parameters-SUVmax and SUV ratio normalized to the superior sagittal sinus (SUVRsss)-and the Krenning score in meningioma. Methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 44 patients (70 meningiomas) who underwent clinical vertex-to-thigh [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, SUVRsss, lesion size) were extracted from coregistered PET and MR images. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between imaging variables and Krenning score. Differences in quantitative PET parameters across Krenning categories were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis test and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U test. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis using the Youden J index identified optimal cutoffs for clinically relevant thresholds (Krenning score of <3 vs. ≥3 and 3 vs. 4). Results: SUVRsss and SUVmax were strongly correlated with the Krenning score (SUVRsss: Spearman ρ = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82; SUVmax: Spearman ρ = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.85; P < 0.0001). PET parameters differed significantly across Krenning categories (all P < 0.001). SUVRsss optimal thresholds were 9.00 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.96) for Krenning scores of 2 versus 3 and 29.84 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.00) for Krenning scores of 3 versus 4. SUVmax optimal thresholds were 7.20 (AUC, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) and 30.70 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.95-1.00), respectively. Conclusion: SUVRsss and SUVmax are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.

articles.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in Refractory Meningiomas: Results from the French Multicenter MELUTE Cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas derives mainly from small, single-center studies. The French national multicenter MELUTE study aimed to consolidate these data using a standardized regimen within a compassionate-use program approved by a national multidisciplinary tumor board. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in 18 French centers between July 2022 and December 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. Results: Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7-80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3-18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. Conclusion: MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Design and Development of NeuroSphere PET: A Next-Generation 7-T MR-Compatible Dedicated Brain PET Scanner.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: PET is the most powerful imaging modality for studying neurotransmitters, receptors, and neuromodulation in humans, complementing the anatomic and hemodynamic information provided by MRI. However, PET temporal resolution remains constrained by sensitivity, limiting studies of fast, dynamic neurochemical processes. To address this gap, we are developing the Human Dynamic NeuroChemical Connectome, an imaging system integrating NeuroSphere PET, a novel ultra-high-sensitivity dedicated brain PET camera, with the Siemens Healthineers Magnetom Terra.X, a clinical 7-T MRI scanner. This article describes the design, engineering, and simulation-based performance estimation of NeuroSphere PET. Sensitivity maximization drove 2 core design choices: a partial spheric detector arrangement with a 32-cm inner diameter and 70% solid-angle coverage and the use of 26-mm lutetium oxyorthosilicate crystals for high stopping power (∼90% at 511 keV), coupled to silicon photomultipliers in a light-sharing, depth-of-interaction-capable configuration. The system comprises 872 detector blocks organized across 19 rings and 218 modules. At the detector level, measured performance includes energy resolution of approximately 11% full width at half maximum (FWHM), depth-of-interaction resolution of approximately 8 mm FWHM, and coincidence timing resolution of approximately 500 ps FWHM. System-level performance was evaluated using the ultrafast Monte Carlo PET simulator, accounting for realistic detector response, positron range, photon noncollinearity, and interdetector scatter. Sensitivity was estimated from a 30-cm uniform sphere, predicting a peak sensitivity of about 38% and a whole-brain average exceeding 25%. Spatial resolution and image quality were assessed through Derenzo phantom simulations evaluated at both the center of the field of view and 8 cm off-center, indicating that 1.6-mm structures can be resolved near the center of the field of view and that resolution of less than 2 mm can be maintained at the cortex. The system incorporates a 3-dimensional-printed MRI-compatible gantry, a dedicated 16-channel parallel transmit-receive radiofrequency head coil, and a custom radiofrequency shielding enclosure for simultaneous PET/MRI at 7 T. By targeting sensitivity an order of magnitude higher than that of commercial PET systems, NeuroSphere PET is expected to enable simultaneous neurochemical and hemodynamic studies with substantially improved spatiotemporal resolution, providing new insights into brain function and connectivity.

articles.title: Single-cell multi-omics in IPF and COPD: from atlas to impact.
articles.abstract: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies are transforming our understanding of the normal lung cellular repertoire as well the molecular and cellular networks of chronic lung diseases. In this review we focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We briefly review technologies and discuss technical and analytical challenges, including strategies to optimise batch correction, dataset integration, and sample-aware differential gene expression; we describe global lung reference atlases, enabled by large-scale data-sharing, providing accessible frameworks for cross-study validation, lineage and trajectory inference, and inter-disease comparisons; and we outline the major findings in COPD and IPF. In IPF, mechanistic insights include: (i) loss of the normal alveolar niche (ii) aberrant basaloid epithelial cells linked to failed regeneration, expansion of (iii) profibrotic SPP1+ macrophages and (iv) disease-associated CTHRC1+ and HAS1hi fibroblast subtypes, that localise to fibrotic niches, and (v) extensive vascular and immune remodelling. In COPD these approaches demonstrate: (i) loss of aerocytes; (ii) expansion of MMP-expressing macrophages, (iii) activated neutrophil influx and (iv) B-cell lymphoid follicle activation and endothelial inflammation (iv) some overlapping features with IPF. We highlight gaps and future opportunities, including under-representation of early disease stages, incomplete resolution of neutrophils, tissue-resident immune compartments, and cross-organ integration. Looking forward, integration with clinical phenotypes and imaging is accelerating translation towards precision medicine, enabling biomarker discovery, cellular endotyping, and therapeutic prioritisation. Advances in multimodal profiling, computational pipelines, next generation technologies, open science initiatives and artificial intelligence will propel the field toward predictive, patient-specific insight and mechanistically informed, stratified trial design.

articles.title: A phase 2a study with SPL84: A novel RNA-targeted approach to restore CFTR function in people with CF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 3849+10 kb C→T mutation in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) gene leads to aberrant splicing and the inclusion of a cryptic exon harboring a premature stop codon, resulting in the production of non-functional CFTR protein. SPL84 is an inhaled antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designed to correct CFTR splicing and restore functional CFTR expression in people with CF (pwCF) carrying this mutation.

METHODS: This Phase 2a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multiple ascending dose study evaluated safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory efficacy of inhaled SPL84 in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. Participants received once-weekly inhalations of SPL84 (25 or 50 mg) or placebo for 9 weeks. Exploratory efficacy measures included changes in ppFEV1, ppFEF25-75, and CFQ-R respiratory symptom score.

RESULTS: Seventeen participants were included in the analysis, with fifteen completing all treatments. SPL84 was well tolerated with no drug-related serious adverse events. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and consistent with the underlying CF disease. Improvements in lung function, defined as change from baseline in ppFEV1≥5, were observed in up to 70% of the treated participants per cohort, accompanied by improvement of additional efficacy outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Inhaled SPL84 demonstrated a favorable safety profile together with encouraging signals of clinical benefit in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. These findings represent, to our knowledge, the first evidence of potential clinical benefit from a nucleic acid-based therapy targeting RNA in a pulmonary disease, supporting further evaluation of SPL84 as a mutation-specific, RNA-targeted treatment.

Experiences of Older Adults Living With HIV.
articles.journal: Research and theory for nursing practice
articles.abstract: Background and Purpose: Older people living with HIV (OPLWH) face complex challenges as they age. Although advances in antiretroviral therapy have transformed human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection into a chronic condition and increased longevity, aging with HIV is often accompanied by multimorbidity, polypharmacy, stigma, social isolation, and mental health concerns. These intersecting factors complicate clinical management and are not always fully addressed in traditional HIV care models. Methods: This study aimed to explore the clinical care experiences of OPLWH over age 50. A qualitative descriptive inquiry was undertaken to gain an in-depth understanding of participants' experiences. Semistructured individual interviews were conducted with 16 OPLWH. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis, following an iterative process of coding, categorization, and theme development to identify patterns across participants' narratives. Results: Five key themes emerged: (a) looking beyond the virus and T-cells; (b) detecting emerging health needs related to aging with HIV; (c) identifying and addressing psychological and social needs; (d) addressing barriers to accessible and coordinated care; and (e) supporting patient empowerment, advocacy, and education. Participants required more comprehensive support in advocacy, social connection, care accessibility, and care coordination. Conclusions: Findings reveal critical gaps in nursing practice and emphasize the need for patient-centered, holistic care for OPLWH. Nursing practice should incorporate comprehensive assessments that address physical, psychological, and social domains; enhance interdisciplinary collaboration; and prioritize proactive screening for age-related comorbidities, mental health concerns, and social determinants of health. Future research should develop and evaluate interventions designed to reduce loneliness and social isolation and enhance social connectedness among OPLWH.

The spectrum of cardiovascular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide case-control postmortem study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine cardiovascular pathology in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) vs. population-based controls, and its association with cause of death.

METHODS: A case-control postmortem study was performed in Australia using the National Coronial Information System (2000-2025). SLE/RA cases were identified via keyword/ICD-10 code search. Controls were selected from motor vehicle accident deaths (3:1 ratio). Cardiovascular findings/histology were extracted from autopsy reports. Associations between SLE/RA and cardiovascular findings/outcomes using logistic regression (odds ratios (OR), 95% confidence intervals (CI)).

RESULTS: 363 cases (240 RA&123 SLE) and 123 controls of similar age (cases 63y (IQR 53-72), vs. controls 59y (47-73), p=0.166) and sex (female 69% vs. controls 75%, p=0.235) were included. Adjusting for age, sex and BMI, myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR3.66, 95%CI2.00-6.72, p<0.001; RA OR3.96, 95%CI2.37-6.60, p<0.001), myocardial inflammation (SLE OR14.79, 95%CI3.35-65.37, p<0.001; RA OR6.35, 95%CI1.44-28.09, p=0.015) and cardiomegaly (SLE OR5.70, 95%CI2.99-10.86, p<0.001; RA OR3.50, 95%CI2.02-6.08, p<0.001) were more frequent in SLE and RA, as were coronary artery disease (CAD; SLE OR2.46, 95%CI1.34-4.51, p=0.004; RA OR2.56, 95%CI1.54-4.27, p<0.001) and microvascular disease (SLE OR10.28, 95%CI2.28- 46.31; RA OR6.74, 95%CI1.53-29.57, p=0.012). Associations between cardiovascular findings and SLE/RA status were strongest in under-60s, and persisted after adjusting for CAD. Cardiovascular death was associated with myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR2.35, 95%CI1.02-5.43, p=0.045; RA OR3.62, 95%CI1.81-7.27, p<0.001), cardiomegaly (SLE OR3.77, 95%CI1.71-8.27, p=0.001; RA OR2.52, 95%CI1.44-4.43, p=0.001) and CAD (SLE OR4.12, 95%CI1.76-9.66, p=0.001; RA OR12.71, 95%CI6.59-24.49, p<0.001); and microvascular disease (OR5.26, 95%CI1.40-19.77, p=0.014) and valvular pathology (OR2.68, 95%CI1.11-6.43, p=0.028) in SLE only.

CONCLUSION: This unique dataset identified increased atherosclerotic, inflammatory and fibrotic cardiovascular disease in SLE and RA, particularly in younger individuals. These pathologies were frequently associated with cardiovascular death.

articles.title: Patterns of NT-proBNP in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated patterns of N-terminal prohormone of n-terminal brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP, a biomarker of cardiac disease) in SLE, and associations with demographic and clinical characteristics.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the McGill SLE Research Cohort, including yearly serum NTproBNP. We assessed prevalence of baseline elevated NT-proBNP (≥133 ng/L) , and associations with baseline variables: age, sex, race/ethnicity, age at SLE diagnosis, SLE duration, smoking, and SLE International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index. Patients were classified into four NT-proBNP patterns: abnormal at baseline and remaining abnormal; abnormal and normalizing; normal and becoming abnormal; normal and remaining normal. We compared baseline characteristics across patterns using multivariate logistic regressions.

RESULTS: We studied 294 patients with ≥2 measurements. At baseline, 101 (34.4%) had elevated NT-proBNP. Higher levels were associated with older age at SLE diagnosis, longer SLE duration, cardiovascular damage, pulmonary hypertension, and renal damage. Of 101 individuals with abnormal baseline NT-proBNP, 79 (78.2%) remained abnormal. Of the 193 with normal baseline levels, 30 (15.5%) became abnormal. No patient with a baseline level ≥350 normalized to <133. High-risk patterns (abnormal-remaining-abnormal and normal-becoming-abnormal) were more likely to have cardiovascular damage (OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.49-12.5, renal damage (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.61-5.51), and pulmonary hypertension (OR 32.0, 95% CI 4.59-651.1).

CONCLUSION: Over one-third of SLE patients had abnormal baseline NT-proBNP; most (78%) remained abnormal. Over 15% of those with an initially normal value became abnormal. Higher levels were associated with age, SLE duration, and organ damage. Levels ≥350 ng/L did not normalize over our evaluation.

articles.title: Strengthening Spondyloarthritis Care in the Americas: A Joint Position Statement of the Pan American League of Associations for Rheumatology and the Spondyloarthritis Research and Treatment Network on Education, Collaborative Research, and Mentorship.
Persistent Opioid Exposure in Older Adults with Rheumatic Disease: National Patterns, Disparities, and Cross-Specialty Prescribing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Estimate national prevalence of opioid use, including chronic and high-risk use, among older adults with rheumatic diseases; identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with chronic opioid use; and characterize prescribing patterns by clinician specialty in a contemporary Medicare-linked national registry cohort.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of the Rheumatology Informatics System for Effectiveness (RISE) registry linked to Medicare Part D (2016-2021). Patients were ≥65 years with qualifying rheumatic diagnoses and continuous Medicare enrollment in 2021. Opioid use was identified from Part D claims. Chronic use was defined as ≥90 days' supply in 2021. High-risk use was assessed using Office of Inspector General indicators. Generalized estimating equations modeled factors associated with chronic opioid use.

RESULTS: Among 45,455 patients (mean age 75.8 years; 76.88% women), 43.13% filled ≥1 opioid prescription and 17.93% met criteria for chronic use in 2021. Very high-risk prescribing was rare (<1%). Chronic use was most prevalent in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA; 26.19%) and least in polymyalgia rheumatica (11.58%). In adjusted analyses, axSpA (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.35-1.98), fibromyalgia (OR 2.68, 95% CI 2.39-3.00), mood and anxiety disorders, higher comorbidity burden, American Indian/Alaska Native race, and greater socioeconomic deprivation were independently associated with chronic use. Non-rheumatology clinicians wrote most opioid prescriptions (62.60%) and more high-dose prescriptions (≥50 morphine milligram equivalents/day).

CONCLUSION: Opioid exposure remains common among Medicare-insured older adults with rheumatic disease, although very high-risk prescribing is rare. Coordinated, guideline-concordant pain management across specialties may help preserve appropriate opioid use for patients who may benefit while reducing avoidable long-term exposure.

articles.title: Impact of Early Versus Publicly Funded Adoption of Flash Glucose Monitoring on Metabolic Outcomes and Self-Care in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Background: Flash glucose monitoring (FGM) technology has transitioned from private acquisition to universal public subsidization. Objective: This study examined changes in metabolic outcomes and self-care behaviors associated with the timing of FGM adoption. Methods: An observational, pre-post study was conducted with 206 adults with type 1 diabetes (representing 91.2% of the local health area population). Participants were categorized into "early adopters" (prior private use) and "post-funding adopters" (initiation after public subsidy). Clinical data and Self-Care Inventory-Revised (SCI-R) scores were analyzed over a 1-year follow-up period. Results: After 1 year, both cohorts demonstrated significant improvements in glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and basal glycemia. Early adopters maintained superior glycemic profiles compared with the post-funding group (HbA1c: 6.86 ± 0.77 vs. 7.77 ± 1.24; p < .001). Post-funding adopters showed statistically significant pre-post changes in lipid profile and creatinine levels. While global SCI-R scores improved for all participants, scores for exercise and preventive behaviors remained suboptimal and showed no significant change. Conclusions: Early adoption of FGM is associated with sustained metabolic advantages. However, the persistence of low scores in exercise and prevention, regardless of technology use, underscores the critical need for targeted nurse-led interventions in primary care to address lifestyle-based self-management gaps. Implications for Nursing: The study shows that flash glucose monitoring (FGM) is associated with improved metabolic control and self-care adherence in people with type 1 diabetes. These findings may contribute to improving clinical practice, particularly nursing care and diabetes management. They may also support greater access and funding for glucose monitoring technologies. Further research is needed to address exercise promotion and self-care education in this population.

articles.title: A Retrospective Chart Review of Tirzepatide and Semaglutide Use in Prediabetes Management and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in a Rural Primary Care Setting.
articles.abstract: Background: Prediabetes and obesity are highly prevalent conditions associated with increased risk of progression to type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and cardiovascular disease. While clinical trials demonstrate the efficacy of glucagon-like peptide-1 and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, limited evidence exists in routine primary care, particularly in rural populations. Objective: This review aimed to examine associations between tirzepatide and semaglutide use and changes in glycemic status and cardiometabolic risk factors among rural-dwelling adults with prediabetes treated in a single rural primary care clinic. Methods: A retrospective chart review was conducted among 40 adults with prediabetes and overweight or obesity treated for 3-24 months with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Primary outcomes included body mass index (BMI) and hemoglobin (A1c). Secondary variables included blood pressure (BP), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and triglycerides. Results: Significant improvements were observed in A1c, BMI, systolic and diastolic BP, LDL, and triglycerides (p < .001). All participants achieved normoglycemic A1c levels. No significant changes were observed in HDL levels. Conclusions: In this rural primary care setting, treatment with tirzepatide or semaglutide was associated with improvements in glycemic control and cardiometabolic risk factors. Findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the observational design and potential confounding factors. Implications for Nursing: Nurse practitioners are positioned to advocate for and implement pharmacological therapies for early management of prediabetes. Providers can drive meaningful changes in T2DM prevention and cardiometabolic health optimization.

articles.title: An Evidence-Based Approach to Nonpharmacological Blood Pressure Management Among African Americans.
articles.abstract: Background: African Americans (AAs) are at increased risk of developing hypertension (HTN), which can lead to increased health care expenditures, related comorbidities, and mortality. Objective: This pilot study aimed to determine if receiving faith-based health education in a Southern Baptist setting would influence AAs' self-care behaviors and blood pressure (BP) management. Methods: A sample of 21 AA participants with self-reported HTN was recruited from a Southern U.S. Baptist church to participate in a one-group pretest-posttest study. The intervention consisted of 6 weekly 60-minute educational sessions utilizing American Heart Association education, biblical references, meditation, and inspirational messages. BP readings and pre- and post-survey responses on the Hypertension Self-Care Activity Level Effects were analyzed. Results: Results demonstrated that both systolic and diastolic BP measurements were reduced. Five of the six self-care behavior subscales also demonstrated improvement in lifestyle management. Conclusions: Healthy self-care habits related to HTN can be shaped by health promotion initiatives provided in a church setting. Implications for Nursing: This pilot study confirms that there is evidence that suggests a positive relationship exists between faith, health, and improved self-care behaviors among AAs.

articles.title: Mortality Risk in Steatotic Liver Disease Stratified by Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Alcohol Consumption: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) has emerged as a new nomenclature; however, the long-term outcomes of SLD associated with its subtypes have been understudied. We aimed to investigate the all-cause and cause-specific mortality risk across SLD subtypes.

METHODS: Health checkup results of 2,049,641 Korean individuals were analyzed. SLD was defined as a Fatty Liver Index ≥30. Mortality risks in metabolic dysfunction-associated SLD (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) were investigated considering cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and alcohol consumption. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: Compared with no SLD, MASLD (HR, 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24 to 1.30), MetALD (HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.44), and ALD (HR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.65 to 1.75) showed higher risks of all-cause mortality. All subtypes had an increased cause-specific mortality risk from liver-related disease, extrahepatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with liver-related mortality being the most prominent (HR, 2.57; 95% CI, 2.36 to 2.80 for MASLD; HR, 4.34; 95% CI, 3.93 to 4.78 for MetALD; HR, 6.23; 95% CI, 5.65 to 6.91 for ALD). The cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality increased as the number of CMRFs increased in all subtypes. The number of CMRFs affecting the mortality risk was the most pronounced in MASLD but the least pronounced in ALD.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that MASLD, MetALD, and ALD had an increased risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality compared with no SLD. The impact of the number of CMRFs on mortality risk was most pronounced in MASLD, calling for more customized management strategies.

articles.title: Incidence and Longitudinal Trajectory of de novo Hepatic Steatosis after Pancreatoduodenectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study Using Transient Elastography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: De novo hepatic steatosis is a recognized complication following pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD); however, its incidence and longitudinal course remain poorly defined. We prospectively evaluated the incidence, temporal trajectory, and risk factors for de novo hepatic steatosis after PD using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP).

METHODS: Consecutive patients scheduled for PD at Asan Medical Center between October 2020 and October 2023 were prospectively enrolled. Patients with baseline CAP ≥250 dB/m, preexisting diabetes mellitus, viral hepatitis, or significant alcohol consumption were excluded. De novo hepatic steatosis was defined as CAP ≥275 dB/m on follow-up VCTE. Assessments were performed at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months after surgery. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence at 12 months.

RESULTS: Of 116 enrolled patients, 100 were eligible and 92 underwent at least one postoperative CAP measurement. The cumulative incidence of de novo hepatic steatosis at 12 months was 28.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 18.6% to 37.6%). Point prevalence peaked at 3 months (20.3%) and declined to 13.1% at 24 months. Among patients with steatosis at 12 months, 55.6% showed resolution by 24 months. Preoperative body mass index was an independent predictor of steatosis development (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.41 per 1 kg/m2; 95% CI, 1.13 to 1.76; p=0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: De novo hepatic steatosis developed in approximately one-quarter of patients after PD and showed a partially reversible course. Higher preoperative body mass index and adjuvant chemotherapy independently predicted its development, supporting systematic postoperative hepatic surveillance using VCTE.

articles.title: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease presenting with mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
Exploring emotion identification and categorisation in simulated central vision loss: an event-related potential study.

Protocol for the development of a paediatric core outcome set for arthrogryposis multiplex congenita: an international multi-interest-holder consensus study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ongoing research for arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) advocates for holistic and family-centred interventions. However, clinicians working with children with AMC are often met with gaps in the literature and a lack of assessment guidelines, impacting services. Current limitations in clinical practice demonstrate the need for consensus on which outcome measures to use in paediatric rehabilitation for AMC. This multiphasic study aims to develop a core outcome set (COS) for a group of rare musculoskeletal diseases (AMC), fostering standardised and inclusive care practices.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This study follows a mixed-method multiphasic approach guided by the COMET Initiative’s standards for core outcome set (COS) development and COMET Handbook V.1.0. An international advisory panel was established, representing clinicians and individuals with lived experience across Canada, the United States, Poland, Australia and India. Preliminary COS concepts were derived from multidisciplinary research activities conducted between 2016 and 2024. A scoping review and advisory panel consultation supported outcome measure selection and refinement for the AMC population. Five candidate outcome measures were mapped item-by-item to the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to assess functional domain coverage and alignment with AMC rehabilitation needs. The resulting draft COS will now guide the consensus-building phase, including modified Delphi rounds, international focus groups and individual interviews, followed by external methodological appraisal.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval has been provided by McGill University’s Research Ethics Board (effective 21 July 2026; submission 26-05-029-01). The COS will be shared at AMC support organisation meetings, conferences and webinars, with additional knowledge mobilisation activities selected by the international advisory panel. The dissemination of findings will also be guided by the feedback provided during focus groups and interviews, to best address the needs of varied populations and ensure the accessibility of information across settings.

OSF REGISTRATION: 10.17605/OSF.IO/QG89H.

COMET REGISTRATION: https://www.comet-initiative.org/Studies/Details/3378.

Evaluation of Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Dosing for Major Bleeding Following Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Four-factor prothrombin concentrate complex (4F-PCC) may be used for significant bleeding following cardiac surgery but the optimal dosing has not been established. The purpose of this study was to compare two dosing strategies of 4F-PCC in cardiac surgery patients. This retrospective chart review evaluated 4F-PCC dosing of 25 units/kg compared to 12.5 units/kg in cardiac surgery patients following a protocol change for 4F-PCC dosing. The primary outcome was major bleeding, defined as the number of patients receiving ≥3 packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusions within 24 h of 4F-PCC administration. Secondary outcomes included other surrogate markers for bleeding (eg, Use of other blood products and hemostatic agents), thrombotic events within 14 days of surgery, hospital length of stay, and all-cause mortality. A total of 42 patients were included (31 patients in the 25 units/kg group and 11 patients in the 12.5 units/kg group). There was no difference in the number of patients that received ≥3 PRBC transfusions between the two groups with 15 patients (47.4%) in 25 units/kg group and 3 patients (27.3%) in 12.5 units/kg (P = .299). Additionally, no difference was observed in amount of additional hemostatic agents administered, hospital length of stay or mortality between the two groups. A higher rate of thromboembolic events was observed among patients receiving 25 units/kg vs 12.5 units/kg (22.6% vs 0%, P = .161). Reduced dosing of 4F-PCC from 25 units/kg to 12.5 units/kg following cardiac surgery resulted in no difference in clinical or effectiveness outcomes.

articles.title: Pathophysiology, Workup and Treatment of Cancer-Related Ischaemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Cancer and acute ischemic stroke are two leading causes of mortality worldwide. The association between these two diseases is being increasingly recognized, and with improvements in cancer mortality, the co-prevalence is increasing. Evidence suggested that cancer-related ischemic stroke is a unique subtype of stroke, including a newly proposed schematic to define this subgroup of patients. Cancer-related ischemic stroke encompasses a heterogeneous group of mechanisms that requires individualized diagnostic evaluation and multidisciplinary collaboration. In this narrative review, we describe the pathophysiology, workup, and management considerations in patients with cancer and ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Clinical Relevance of Magnesium Supplementation In Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract: Magnesium deficiency is common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), affecting up to 48% of patients, yet remains underrecognized in routine clinical practice. A bidirectional relationship between hypomagnesemia and insulin resistance has been well characterized, and observational data consistently link higher magnesium intake to reduced risks of T2DM, hypertension, stroke, and heart failure. However, supplementation trials have yielded inconsistent results, limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up, heterogeneous formulations with differing bioavailability, and variable glycemic endpoints. Serum magnesium, the most widely used clinical measure, reflects less than 1% of total body stores and may fail to detect clinically significant depletion. No randomized trial has been powered for hard clinical outcomes such as diabetes prevention or cardiovascular events. Current American Diabetes Association guidelines recommend magnesium screening and supplementation only in high-risk groups with documented deficiency, with emphasis on dietary optimization as a first-line strategy. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through December 2025, with priority given to meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, and clinical practice guidelines, particularly the ADA position statement and the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Magnesium Fact Sheet. This narrative review critically examines the evidence linking magnesium to glycemic control and cardiovascular risk in T2DM, highlights key methodological limitations, and identifies research priorities such as biomarker validation, formulation comparison trials, and adequately powered cardiovascular outcome studies needed to determine whether magnesium optimization should be incorporated into routine diabetes care.

articles.title: The Burden of Type 1 Peri-Operative Myocardial Infarction After Non-Cardiac Surgery: Insights From the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project From 2010-2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence of perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI), the quality-of-care patients receive and their outcomes, and how this varies across different operations.

METHODS: We included adults from England with AMI between Jan 2010 and March 2023 from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project registry, linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). Cox-regression models compared risk of all-cause mortality at thirty-days and five-years, subgroup analyses compared operation type (orthopaedic, vascular, upper (UGI) and lower gastrointestinal (LGI) and urological).

RESULTS: We identified 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%). Orthopaedics were the largest contributing speciality (45%). Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001). For thirty-day mortality, risk was not significant in orthopaedics and urology but was for vascular (1.75 [1.40-2.18]), UGI (1.95 [1.43-2.66) and LGI surgery (1.94 [1.50-2.51]) (all P<0.001). For those who survived to hospital discharge, PMI patients had higher mortality risk at five-years (1.26 [1.19-1.34), especially high in the UGI (1.76 [1.44-2.13]), LGI (1.34 [1.13-1.59]) and urology groups (1.61 [1.34-1.93]) (all P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: PMI mortality is significantly higher than AMI all-comers, seen across all subspecialties up to five-years, with variation in the risk of mortality from PMI according to operation type. PMI may identify a high-risk vulnerable group of patients, whose increased mortality risk persists long term, even in those who survive to discharge.

articles.title: Maternal antibody transfer confounds type 1 diabetes screening in infancy: results from the French TRAKR cohort.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The optimal age to initiate islet autoantibody (IAb) screening in first-degree relatives of individuals with type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains uncertain. The TRAKR cohort prospectively characterized IAb patterns in newborns of parents with T1D to assess the interpretability of early-life screening.

METHODS: We analyzed 148 children with available follow-up. Child blood samples were collected at birth and at 8, 18, 30, and 42 months, and parental samples during pregnancy. Insulin (IAA), GAD (GADA), IA-2 (IA-2A), and ZnT8 (ZnT8A) IAbs were measured using bridging ELISAs. Child-mother IAb specificities and longitudinal trajectories were compared.

RESULTS: At 8 months, 28/138 children (20.3%) were IAb+, of whom 25/28 (89.3%) had a single IAb and 25/28 (89.3%) had a mother with T1D. Among 21 IAb+ children with maternal IAb results, 18 (85.7%) shared IAb specificity with their mother, predominantly GADA (15/18, 83.3%). All 9 children GADA+ at 8 months with follow-up had GADA+ mothers; 6 seroreverted by 18 months and 1 by 30 months. All 5 children IAA+ at 8 months with follow-up seroreverted by 18 months. Only one child, who seroconverted to IAA and GADA at 18 months, progressed to clinical Stage 3 at 30 months, without ketoacidosis.

CONCLUSION: IAb positivity at 8 months frequently reflects passive maternal antibody transfer rather than endogenous islet autoimmunity. Screening during the first year of life may therefore overestimate child autoimmunity and prompt unnecessary follow-up. Initiating screening at 2 years of age should reduce misclassification while retaining the opportunity to detect early childhood seroconversion.

articles.title: Multi-Institutional Review of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Use in Pediatric Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children at risk for pulmonary embolism (PE) may be treated with inferior vena cava (IVC) filter insertion when anticoagulation is impossible or ineffective. The purpose of this multi-institutional retrospective review is to better understand the indications and technical and clinical outcomes related to IVC filter placement and removal in pediatric patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was open to all institutions that placed IVC filters in pediatric patients. Data collected included demographics, indications, procedural details of filter insertion and/or removal, and clinical follow-up. Univariate analysis was performed.

RESULTS: A total of 250 filters were placed in 242 pediatric patients (135 male) at 12 participating hospitals between October 1994 and June 2020. Thrombosis was present in 82.8% of patients, PE in 34.8%, and anticoagulation adverse events (AEs) or contraindications in 45.9%. Most filter insertions were technically successful (99.1%); 3.1% were associated with minor AEs, and 0.4% with moderate AEs. Breakthrough pulmonary embolism occurred in 1.4% following filter placement. Filter retrieval rate was 76%. Removal was technically successful in 88% of attempts and resulted in minor AEs in 1.1% and severe AEs in 6.5%. Minor, moderate, and severe device-associated AEs occurred in 8%, 1.6%, and 3.2% of filters, respectively. There was no correlation between age or weight and outcomes, including breakthrough PE, AEs, or mortality.

CONCLUSION: IVC filter insertion in pediatric patients is feasible and associated with a high retrieval rate.

articles.title: Pelacarsen and Lp(a)HORIZON: Interpreting the Disconnect Between Lipoprotein(a) Lowering and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Pelacarsen, a hepatocyte-directed antisense oligonucleotide targeting apolipoprotein(a), was evaluated in Lp(a)HORIZON, the first large phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial specifically designed to test whether pharmacological Lp(a) lowering reduces cardiovascular events. Topline results announced in September 2026 indicated that pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) but did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint in patients with established cardiovascular disease. Full trial data are awaited, and the mechanisms underlying this neutral result remain uncertain. We discuss potential explanations, including treatment after prolonged cumulative Lp(a) exposure, advanced vascular disease, intensive background prevention, the magnitude and duration of Lp(a) suppression, patient selection, baseline cardiovascular risk, and biological heterogeneity. We also examine implications for emerging therapies, including olpasiran, zerlasiran, lepodisiran, and muvalaplin, and for the design of ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials.

articles.title: A critical review of clinical prediction models in oncology: is this SEERious research?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The National Cancer Institute's Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) cancer registry covers almost half the United States population. Clinical prediction models developed using the SEER cancer registry have rapidly grown in number. We sought to characterise and examine the extent to which this body of work reflects formulaic research practices, reflected by a lack of clear objectives, substandard methods and practices with limited scientific value.

STUDY DESIGN AND SETTING: We conducted a systematic review of clinical prediction model development studies using the SEER data. MEDLINE via PubMed was searched for studies published between January 1 and August 10, 2023. Studies were included if they developed a clinical prediction model using two or more predictors from the SEER database. Data extraction covered study context, intended use, predictor characteristics, reporting guideline adherence, external validation practices, and the rationale provided for using SEER.

RESULTS: Of 436 eligible studies, 94% (n=412) had first authors affiliated with institutions in China, while 3% (n=14) were from the United States. Developed models mostly targeted lung (11%) and breast (10%) cancers, and most focussed on prognosis (87%). Cox regression was the predominant modelling approach (59%), and nomograms were the most common presentation format (77%). Reporting guideline adherence was low (13%), and study protocols were rarely mentioned (3%). Nearly one third of models included patients' race as a predictor (32%). Of the China-affiliated studies, only 6% reported an intended clinical setting, and 3% specified the intended country of use. Discussion of the suitability of SEER was absent in 87% of included studies. Among China-affiliated studies, 22% carried out external validation using data from China. Over a ten-year period, expanding our search strategy identified more than 4,000 SEER-based prediction model studies indexed in MEDLINE, with annual output growing from 37 in 2016 to over 700 in 2023.

CONCLUSIONS: Access to data alone does not justify model development. Most prediction models developed using SEER lack a clearly reported rationale, defined target population, an intended clinical purpose, and fail to address whether the models produced with the SEER data are appropriate for populations outside the United States. Readers should treat SEER-based prediction model studies with appropriate scepticism until evidence of rigorous methodology and clinical relevance is demonstrated. Many studies have limited scientific value and exhibit hallmarks of formulaic research created solely to boost researcher's resumé.
