Journals, peer reviewers, and data custodians all have a responsibility to ensure high research standards for studies exploiting widely available datasets, as the growing volume of such output places editorial and peer review systems under increasing strain.

articles.title: Impact of vaccination on the development of type 1 diabetes in children and vaccine safety in pediatric patients with T1DM: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune disease associated with increased susceptibility to infections, making immunization an important component of pediatric diabetes care. Despite the established benefits of vaccination, concerns persist regarding its potential role in triggering autoimmune diseases, including T1DM. This systematic review evaluated the impact of vaccination on the risk of developing T1DM in children and assessed vaccine safety in those with established disease. PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2025 in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Twenty-one original studies met the eligibility criteria. For three rotavirus cohort studies reporting directly comparable adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for subsequent T1DM, an exploratory inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Overall, the available evidence showed no increased risk of T1DM associated with vaccination. Five studies suggested possible protective effects of rotavirus or BCG vaccination against T1DM development. Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 vaccines were safe in children with established T1DM, with adverse events predominantly mild and transient. Some studies also reported reduced hospitalization rates and fewer infectious complications among vaccinated individuals. Current evidence strongly supports routine childhood vaccination and indicates that immunization is safe and may provide additional benefits for children with or at risk of T1DM.

articles.title: Diabetes, Long-term mortality, and LDL-C target attainment after an acute coronary syndrome: A population-based cohort study (2016-2024).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the excess acute coronary syndrome (ACS) burden and post-ACS mortality associated with diabetes and assess LDL-C target attainment, focusing on sex differences.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5,361 patients with the first ACS admission identified during the study period (2016-2024) in a Spanish healthcare department. Hospitalization trends were analyzed using population-based regression models. Long-term mortality was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. LDL-C target attainment was evaluated according to ESC/EAS recommendations.

RESULTS: Diabetes was present in 36.9 % of patients. ACS hospitalization rates declined by 8.3 % annually (95 % CI 6.1-10.4), with no diabetes-by-time interaction (p = 0.17). In-hospital case fatality was 6.3 % and did not differ by diabetes status. During a median 4.9-year follow-up, diabetes was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.22, 95 % CI 1.11-1.33), with a stronger association in women than men (interaction p = 0.009). Only 28.9 % achieved LDL-C < 55 mg/dL, with no temporal improvement; female sex independently predicted poor LDL-C control (adjusted OR 1.65, 95 % CI 1.38-1.97).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite declining ACS hospitalizations, DM remained associated with increased long-term mortality, particularly in women. LDL-C target attainment remained suboptimal, highlighting persistent gaps in secondary prevention.

articles.title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease Without Dedicated Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms (SAAs) represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695) RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.

articles.title: Optimal Incidence Threshold for Cost-Effective Hepatocellular Carcinoma Surveillance in Alcohol-Associated Cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend routine hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance in patients with cirrhosis when annual HCC incidence exceeds 1 per 100 person-years, a threshold derived from older studies and not specific to alcohol-associated cirrhosis. However, contemporary data suggest that HCC incidence in this population is often below 1%, leaving the value of routine surveillance uncertain.

METHODS: We developed a Markov-based state-transition microsimulation model to simulate the natural history of HCC and subsequent treatment pathways in patients with alcohol-associated cirrhosis in the United States setting. The model compared biannual surveillance with ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) versus no surveillance separately for two distinct cohorts: patients who continued to actively consume alcohol and patients who had achieved sustained abstinence. Inputs included the natural history of alcohol-associated cirrhosis, HCC incidence, test performance, surveillance adherence, and contemporary treatment. Sensitivity analyses examined the robustness of model assumptions and findings.

RESULTS: Biannual surveillance becomes cost-effective when annual HCC incidence reached approximately 0.45 per 100 person-years using willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). Among active drinkers, surveillance yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of $18,952 per QALY; among abstinent patients, the ICER was $56,000 per QALY. Per 100,000 patients, routine surveillance generated an estimated 2,083 additional life-years and 992 QALYs in active drinkers and 3,357 life-years and 1,700 QALYs in abstinent patients.

CONCLUSION: Routine biannual HCC surveillance with ultrasound and AFP is cost-effective for patients with alcohol-associated cirrhosis in the United States when HCC incidence exceeds 0.45 per 100 person-years, substantially below the historically cited 1 per 100 person-years threshold. Updating clinical guidelines to reflect these contemporary thresholds could improve early HCC detection in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Mitral annular disjunction is associated with markers of cardiomyopathy in pediatric Marfan syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

articles.title: Antiviral activity of amenamevir alone and in combination with ganciclovir against equine herpesvirus 1.
articles.abstract: Equine herpesvirus 1 (EHV-1) causes respiratory disease, abortion, and equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM), a neurological disorder characterized by ataxia and hindlimb paralysis. Although EHM remains a major concern in the equine industry, effective antiviral treatment options are limited. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of amenamevir, a helicase-primase complex inhibitor, against multiple EHV-1 strains using real-time cell analysis (RTCA) and quantitative PCR (qPCR), and compared its potency with those of ganciclovir, acyclovir, and penciclovir. Eight EHV-1 strains associated with different clinical manifestations and characterized by A, G, or C at position 2254 of open reading frame 30, which encodes the viral DNA polymerase, were examined. RTCA-based half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values were calculated from inhibition rates based on the area under the normalized cell index curve. Across the eight strains, IC50 values were 0.45-2.31 μg/mL for amenamevir, 0.45-3.95 μg/mL for ganciclovir, 17.93-50.15 μg/mL for acyclovir, and 8.38-24.52 μg/mL for penciclovir. qPCR analysis, based on concentrations required to achieve a 1-log10 reduction in viral genome copy number, showed a similar overall trend. Amenamevir exhibited in vitro antiviral activity against EHV-1, with potency comparable to that of ganciclovir and greater than those of acyclovir and penciclovir. SynergyFinder analysis showed synergistic interactions between amenamevir and ganciclovir within selected concentration ranges against EHV-1 strains in both the Bliss independence and ZIP models. These findings support further investigation of amenamevir, alone and in combination with ganciclovir, as a candidate antiviral compound for the treatment of EHV-1 infection.

articles.title: High Tumor Burden: A Key Predictor of Poor Short-Term Prognosis after First Variceal Bleeding in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The short-term outcome and prognosis of the first-onset esophagogastric variceal bleeding patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is still unclear.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively enrolled 1042 first-time hospitalized patients with cirrhosis from January 2010 to December 2020. A total of 1032 patients had esophagogastric variceal bleeding and 137 of them had HCC. Clinical, laboratory, and tumor characteristics were analyzed. Clinical characteristics and 4-week outcomes (mortality, rebleeding and the composite endpoint (death or rebleeding)) were analyzed.

RESULTS: The overall 4-week mortality, rebleeding, and composite endpoint rates were 14.6% (20/137), 21.9% (30/137), and 29.2% (40/137), respectively. Multivariate analyses identified high tumor burden (OR: 7.97; 95% Confidence Interval: 2.84-26.17; p < 0.01) as an independent risk factor for 4-week mortality. The presence of portal vein thrombosis (OR: 3.07; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.35-7.17; p < 0.01) was an independent risk factor for rebleeding. For the composite endpoint, portal vein thrombosis (OR: 3.70; 95% Confidence Interval: 1.73-8.12; p < 0.01) was identified as an independent risk factor.

CONCLUSIONS: For HCC patients experiencing their first variceal bleeding, high tumor burden is the primary driver of short-term adverse prognosis. Acute in-hospital events warrant particular vigilance in patients with high tumor burden accompanied by portal vein thrombosis.

articles.title: Treatment adherence in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and chronic myeloid leukemia: an integrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the scientific evidence on oral treatment adherence in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), and to identify effective nursing interventions.

METHOD: An integrative review of the literature was conducted. A systematic search was performed in PubMed (including MEDLINE), Scopus, CINAHL, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2015 and December 2024, including early online publications indexed in 2025. MeSH/DeCS terms related to medication adherence, chronic leukemias, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and nursing care were used. Studies conducted in adult patients with CML or CLL receiving oral tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) that evaluated nursing interventions and measured adherence using objective methods or validated scales were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists.

RESULTS: A total of 805 records was identified, of which 9 studies met the inclusion criteria. Adherence to TKIs in CML ranged from 56% to 97%. Multicomponent nursing-led interventions demonstrated significant improvements in adherence (mean difference of 25.2 percentage points; p = 0.002) and major molecular response (22.6 percentage-point difference; p = 0.010). The most effective components included personalized face-to-face education, structured telephone follow-up, proactive management of adverse events, and objective adherence monitoring. The level of evidence was classified as Grade A for multicomponent interventions and Grade B for unimodal interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: There is strong evidence (Grade A) that structured, multicomponent nursing interventions significantly improve therapeutic adherence and clinical outcomes in patients with CML treated with TKIs. The implementation of structured adherence programs is recommended as a standard of care in hematology units.

articles.title: Unplanned contacts managed by an advanced nurse practitioner after atrial fibrillation ablation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the care workload and consultation reasons related to unplanned contacts made by patients undergoing atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation to the advanced nurse practitioner in AF (ANP-AF).

METHODS: A prospective, single-centre descriptive study was conducted between March 2022 and March 2023. During the pre-procedural visit (7-15 days before ablation), the ANP-AF provided individualized education and an unplanned contact channel for non-urgent concerns, available by telephone (8:00-20:00 h) and email. All contacts were consecutively recorded, documenting type and timing of contact, telephone call duration, reason for consultation, and basic patient demographics.

RESULTS: A total of 250 AF ablations was performed, and 78 unplanned contacts were registered, corresponding to 31% of patients (1.5 contacts/week). Most contacts were made by women (55%), with a mean age of 65 ± 10 years. Telephone was the preferred communication method (95%), with a mean call duration of 9 ± 3 minutes. Twenty contacts (25%) occurred before ablation and 58 (75%) within the 12 months after the procedure. The median contact time was 11:30 h (IQR: 10:00-14:45). The most frequent reasons for consultation were AF recurrences (21%), complementary test requests (21%), post-procedural complications (19%), and questions regarding pharmacological treatment (15%).

CONCLUSIONS: One in three patients undergoing AF ablation makes an unplanned contact with the APNP-AF. Systematic identification of consultation reasons may help optimize pre- and post-ablation education and strengthen continuity of care.

articles.title: Host restriction factors in HBV-related liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of viral-host interplay and implications for therapy.
articles.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), imposing a substantial global health burden. The natural history of persistent HBV infection progresses from chronic inflammation to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and malignant transformation, driven in part by the stability of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) within hepatocyte nuclei. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) effectively suppress viral replication but rarely lead to a functional cure, necessitating long-term therapy and carrying a residual risk of resistance. PEG-interferon-α can induce a functional cure in a minority of patients but its clinical use is limited by frequent adverse effects. Host restriction factors-cellular proteins that directly inhibit viral replication-act at multiple stages of the HBV infection cycle, including entry, cccDNA transcription, RNA stability, and virion release. HBV counters these intrinsic defenses through viral proteins such as HBx, establishing a dynamic interplay between viral and host factors that shapes infection outcome and disease progression. This review consolidates recent advances in understanding the roles of host restriction factors in HBV pathogenesis and their mechanistic links to cirrhosis and HCC. We also highlight emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting these host-virus interactions to disable HBV persistence, and thereby reduce HBV-related disease burden.

articles.title: Hereditary α-tryptasemia is associated with response to omalizumab in severe allergic asthma.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Higher basal serum tryptase (BST) levels have been associated with increased asthma severity that correlated with active tryptase allele number and was linked to poor clinical responses to anti-IgE treatment (omalizumab). However, the commonest cause of elevated BST is hereditary α-tryptasemia (HαT) caused by increased α-tryptase-encoding Tryptase alpha/beta 1 (TPSAB1) copy number, and its relationship to omalizumab response in asthma remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: Our aim was to assess the relative contribution of tryptase genotype and HαT to the clinical efficacy of omalizumab treatment in patients with severe allergic asthma.

METHODS: A cohort (N=181) of severe allergic asthma patients treated with omalizumab from 2 tertiary referral centres in Slovenia and the UK underwent tryptase genotyping, and clinical features were subsequently compared between groups with and without HαT.

RESULTS: Limited benefit from omalizumab therapy was demonstrated in 22.7% of patients. Overall, HαT was identified in 8.3% of patients with severe allergic asthma treated with omalizumab. HαT was found in 20% of individuals with poor clinical responses to omalizumab, compared to 5% of those with positive responses (OR = 4.6 [95% CI 1.5-12.3]; P = .0068). In multivariable analysis, adjusted for study site and other covariates, HαT remained independently associated with poor response to omalizumab (OR = 4.56; [95% CI, 1.24-16.74]; P = .022). Among patients with HαT, 4 of 15 had BST below 8 ng/mL.

CONCLUSION: HαT is associated with poorer clinical response to anti-IgE treatment in patients with severe allergic asthma.

articles.title: Systems analysis reveals neuregulin-1 control of cardiomyocyte size and shape mediated by distinct PI3K and p38 pathways.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: Pathological and physiological stresses induce diverse forms of cardiac hypertrophy, with distinct manifestations in cardiomyocyte size and shape regulated by still poorly understood signaling networks. Here, we combined high-content morphological profiling, phospho-protein arrays, and systems modeling to characterize the diverse forms of hypertrophy induced by angiotensin II, endothelin-1, insulin growth factor-1, and neuregulin-1. Reverse-phase protein array profiling of neonatal rat cardiomyocytes and partial least squares regression modeling revealed that Akt, GSK3, and MAPK signaling are differentially regulated by hypertrophic agonists and are predictive of distinct phenotypic outcomes. Among these agonists, neuregulin-1 uniquely induced cardiomyocyte elongation in both neonatal rat and human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, in addition to increasing cell area. Pharmacological perturbations in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes demonstrated that neuregulin1-induced elongation and area expansion both require PI3K activity, whereas p38 selectively mediates cell area. A logic-based network model incorporating dual-specificity phosphatases were sufficient to capture the amplifying PI3K and transient p38 signaling dynamics driving phenotypic changes. Together, these results identify distinct signaling cascades by which neuregulin-1 coordinates cardiomyocyte size and shape, providing mechanistic insight into how hypertrophic remodeling can be differentially regulated. This systems approach provides new insight into the pathways that drive distinct forms of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, highlighting opportunities to selectively target maladaptive remodeling in heart failure.

articles.title: Tidal Breathing Exhaled Nitric Oxide Measurement Using A Novel Chemiluminescence Analyzer: Clinical Potential in Lung Disease Diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, Chinese first domestically developed chemiluminescence-based exhaled nitric oxide (eNO) analyzer, eNOglow, entered the market. This innovative device utilizes a novel methodology, termed the tidal breathing eNO method (TBNO), which enables rapid eNO measurement during natural tidal breathing without requiring patient cooperation for forced exhalation. This approach facilitates the diagnosis of airway inflammation, early detection, and precise treatment, particularly for patients unable to perform traditional fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO50, a constant flow rate of 50 mL/s sustained for 10 seconds) testing, such as children, the elderly, and severely ill patients. However, unlike FeNO50, TBNO lacks established reference values for adult asthma patients globally.

METHODS: This prospective validation study enrolled adult asthma patients and healthy volunteers from two tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were categorized into two subgroups: healthy volunteers and asthmatics. All the eNOglow (chemiluminescence-based) analyzer and conventional electrochemical-based analyzers (ECH) were utilized to measure eNO levels in all subjects at the pulmonary function clinic. Each participant underwent three FeNO50 tests using both analyzers and three TBNO tests using the eNOglow device. The clinical performance and stability of eNOglow were evaluated in both healthy volunteers and asthmatic patients, comparing its results with conventional FeNO50 parameters obtained from widely used clinical eNO analyzers. Additionally, a reference value range for TBNO was established based on the collected data. The receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curve was applied, and the best cut-off value was selected based on the maximum Youden's index.

RESULTS: The study included 189 participants (131 asthma patients and 58 healthy volunteers), with a total of 1,701 tests performed. Both devices demonstrated reproducible FeNO50 values across all subjects. The coefficient of variation (CV) for eNOglow was significantly lower than that of ECH, with overall CVs of 2.82% (1.81, 4.96) for eNOglow and 11.81% (6.31, 19.95) for ECH (P < 0.0001). FeNO50 values showed a strong correlation between the two analyzers (r = 0.9093, P < 0.0001). ROC curve analysis revealed that eNOglow had slightly higher sensitivity and specificity than ECH. The optimal FeNO50 cut-off value for eNOglow was 24.49 ppb, consistent with clinical guidelines and slightly higher than the 20.83 ppb cut-off for ECH. For TBNO values, the best cut-off values for predicting asthma were 7.67 ppb (corresponding to FeNO50 = 25 ppb) and 12.5 ppb (corresponding to FeNO50 = 50 ppb), based on the maximum Youden's index.

CONCLUSIONS: The eNOglow analyzer demonstrates reliable performance in asthmatic patients across varying degrees of airway inflammation, making it suitable for primary healthcare, large-scale clinical trials, and research applications. TBNO measurements offer clinical value, particularly for patients unable to perform FeNO50 testing. These findings validate the reliability of eNOglow and support its applicability in clinical practice and research settings, while establishing the first global reference values for TBNO in adult asthma patients.

articles.title: Digital PCR-based quantification of Leishmania infantum in Lutzomyia longipalpis: comparison between promastigote and macrophage-derived amastigote infection models.
articles.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) remains a major public health concern in Latin America, particularly in Brazil, where Leishmania infantum is primarily transmitted by the sand fly Lutzomyia longipalpis. Understanding parasite development within the vector is essential for elucidating transmission dynamics, yet classical microscopic assessments often lack sensitivity for detecting early or low intensity infections. In this study, Lu. longipalpis females were experimentally infected with either promastigote or amastigote forms of Le. infantum and the infection dynamics were evaluated by both optical microscopy and digital PCR (dPCR). Microscopic examination revealed successful midgut colonization in both groups, with higher parasite counts in amastigote-infected sand fly females during the early phase of infection. Quantification by dPCR confirmed this pattern, detecting significantly higher parasite loads at the initial time points in amastigote-fed sand flies. However, parasite loads converged between groups at later stages, indicating comparable infection dynamics regardless of the parasite infective form. Both methods showed consistent patterns of parasite dynamics, whereas dPCR provided greater sensitivity for detecting and quantifying low parasite burdens, particularly during periods of reduced infection intensity. Overall, our findings provide new insights into parasite-vector interactions and validate dPCR as a precise and sensitive tool for assessing Leishmania infections in sand fly vectors, with potential applications for entomological surveillance and transmission studies.

articles.title: Topical Vancomycin for Prevention of Grade 2 or Higher Sternal Wound Infection After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical vancomycin paste over the sternal edges in preventing sternal wound infection (SWI).

METHODS: This single-center, prospective, single-blind controlled trial 1:1 randomized 360 adult patients undergoing elective full sternotomy cardiac surgery to receive either vancomycin paste or normal saline (NCT04500275). The primary endpoint was SWI within 90 postoperative days. The secondary endpoints included postoperative acute kidney injury, emergence of resistant pathogens and systemic vancomycin exposure.

RESULTS: The incidence of grade 2 or higher SWI within 90 days was significantly lower in the vancomycin group than in the placebo group (1 of 180, 0.6% vs. 7 of 180, 3.9%, p = .031). The subdistribution hazard ratio was 0.14 (p = .065). Deep SWI rate was 0.6% vs. 2.8% (p = .099). The incidence of acute kidney injury was comparable between the groups (31.7% vs. 28.9%, p = .251), even in patients with CKD stages ≥ 3. Systemic vancomycin concentrations were negligible and declined over time in non-dialysis patients. Levels above 10-20 mg/L persisted in some patients undergoing hemodialysis. Three cases of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus from various sources were observed in the vancomycin group of patients with CKD stage ≥ 3 or undergoing hemodialysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Topical vancomycin reduced grade 2 or higher SWI without increasing the risk of acute kidney injury. Systemic exposure was negligible, except in patients undergoing hemodialysis. While the emergence of VRE cannot be excluded, its incidence was negligible and does not outweigh the benefits of SWI reduction when using topical vancomycin.

articles.title: Current Generation Self-Expanding and Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Retrospective Multicenter Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) technology warrants updated comparisons of the most commonly used current generation self-expanding (SE) versus balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THV).

METHODS: This 9-center retrospective analysis stratified patients undergoing TAVR from 2021-2024 into SE-THV and BE-THV cohorts balanced via propensity score matching. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and permanent pacemaker (PPM) need. Secondary outcomes were paravalvular leak (PVL) and acute kidney injury. All outcomes were assessed perioperatively and at 30 and 400 days. Analyses were repeated within LVEF , aortic valve area, and center-level strata.

RESULTS: The total cohort included 2,594 BE-THV and 1,058 SE-THV patients. Matching yielded 680 patients per cohort. After matching , SE-THV patients had higher risk for ischemic stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05) during index hospitalization, with no difference in mortality. At follow-up, the SE-THV cohort had higher risk of mild (p<0.05) and moderate (p<0.05) paravalvular leak, stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05). PPM after SE-THV was significantly lower in high-volume compared to low-volume centers. Kaplan-Meier survival did not differ. Among patients with LVEF ≥45%, SE-THV was associated with higher stroke risk (p<0.05); BE-THV patients with LVEF < 45% were associated with increased all-cause mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, SE-THV correlated with higher rates of ischemic stroke, PPM need, and PVL during index hospitalization and increased mild and moderate PVL upon follow-up. Mortality did not differ during index hospitalization or at follow-up. The normal LVEF SE-THV cohort was associated with higher stroke risk compared to all other groups.

articles.title: Development of a novel diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia based on microbial community characteristics.
articles.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The lung microbiota plays a key role in pneumonia. A correct diagnosis in the early stage helps treatment and limits severity progression of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

METHODS: There were 42 patients with CAP and 20 controls. Amplicon bacterial 16S sequencing from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples revealed indicator genera by linear discriminant analysis effect size, random forest and ROC analyses. The abundance of bacteria was combined with laboratory inflammatory indexes to construct logistic regression models for CAP diagnosis. The final predictive model with a lower Akaike information criterion (AIC) was internally validated by bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: After confirming lower respiratory tract (LRT) microbiome dysbiosis in CAP patients, we identified five indicator genera: Moraxella (M), Prevotella_1 (P), Lautropia (L), Neisseria (N), and Fusobacterium (F). Their combined effect was incorporated by calculation of the joint prediction probability (PRE) based on their relative abundances as PRE = 1 / (1 + EXP (-4.39 + 18.96 M + 9.30P - 5.38 L + 0.89 N + 0.70F)). A nomogram was constructed for CAP diagnosis that incorporated PRE with serum levels of CRP (cut-off ≥5.23 mg/L) and Neutrophil % (cut-off ≥66.05%). After internal validation, this nomogram showed satisfactory diagnostic performance with the bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.927 and a well-fitting calibration curve.

CONCLUSIONS: The LRT microbiome was altered in CAP patients. Indicator genera were shown to have the potential to serve as diagnosis biomarkers in the constructed predictive model. These results may provide further clues for the microbial pathogenesis, optimized diagnostics and new therapeutic targets of CAP.

articles.title: FGF21-NR1D1 Signaling Restrains the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 Axis to Counteract Integrated Renal-Vascular Injury in Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Hypertension leads to concomitant injuries in the kidney and vasculature, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying this coordinated pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify activation of the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 axis as being associated with coordinated renal and vascular injury in hypertension. In hypertension, this pathway was concurrently activated in the liver, kidney, and vasculature and was associated with renal fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, and oxidative stress. Pharmacological inhibition of CYP4A attenuated these pathological changes, supporting a functional contribution of this axis to hypertensive organ injury. Genetic and pharmacological evidence further demonstrated that FGF21 acts as an endogenous negative regulator of CYP4A/20-HETE signaling. Mechanistically, FGF21 restored expression of the nuclear receptor NR1D1, which was suppressed under hypertensive conditions, and this effect was associated with reduced CYP4A expression independently of ERK1/2 signaling. The functional relevance of the FGF21-NR1D1 axis was supported by the observation that NR1D1 antagonism largely abolished the protective effects of FGF21. Thus, these findings elucidate a mechanistic axis linking FGF21-NR1D1 signaling to the CYP4A/20-HETE/GPR75 pathway and suggest that modulation of this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for hypertensive renal and vascular injury.

articles.title: Reintervention Burden and Patency of Hemodialysis Vascular Access in a 15-Year Single-Center Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maintaining a hemodialysis access typically requires repeated intervention, yet the cumulative reintervention burden-as distinct from patency-is rarely quantified, and configuration-specific estimates from Asian centers are scarce. We evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses over 15 years at a single center.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024. Every subsequent procedure was adjudicated from operative records as patency-maintaining or access-abandoning; operations unrelated to the access under study, including kidney transplantation, catheter procedures, and peripheral arterial interventions, were excluded. Patency was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method according to accepted reporting standards and compared across configurations-radiocephalic fistula, brachiocephalic fistula, basilic vein transposition, and graft. The reintervention burden was expressed as interventions per access-year. Predictors of loss of primary patency were assessed by multivariable Cox regression, and a competing-risk analysis treated kidney transplantation as a competing event.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 14.7 months. Overall primary, assisted-primary, and secondary patency were 60.3%, 50.5%, and 44.6%; 87.1%, 81.5%, and 77.1%; and 96.8%, 95.7%, and 94.1% at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. One-year primary patency differed by configuration: 70.1% for radiocephalic fistulas, 63.3% for brachiocephalic fistulas, 71.6% for basilic vein transpositions, and 36.2% for grafts (P < .001). Across 2211 access-years, 743 patency-maintaining interventions were performed (0.336 per access-year), and 37.2% of accesses required at least one reintervention. The burden was concentrated in grafts: 1.09 interventions per access-year for grafts versus 0.25 for autogenous fistulas, an approximately 4.4-fold difference. Graft configuration (hazard ratio, 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.86-3.06), female sex (1.37; 1.10-1.71), ischemic heart disease (1.42; 1.04-1.94), and diabetes (1.26; 1.00-1.57) independently predicted loss of primary patency. Findings persisted after excluding maturation-assisting procedures and in the competing-risk analysis (graft subdistribution hazard ratio for reintervention, 2.32).

CONCLUSIONS: High secondary patency was achieved at the cost of substantial reintervention concentrated in grafts, which required roughly 4.4 times the maintenance of autogenous fistulas. Reporting an explicit reintervention burden alongside patency supports autogenous-first, configuration-aware access planning and patient counseling.

articles.title: Behavioural avoidance to imagined conditioned stimuli in differential fear conditioning.
articles.abstract: The underlying mechanisms of how a fear is born in our imagination is presently unclear. The current study used differential fear conditioning to assess how a fear is created in one's mind and how behavioural avoidance interacts with imagined fear. This study contained an Acquisition, Behavioural Avoidance, and Transfer phase. During the Acquisition phase, participants combined instructions such that whether they heard "imagine yellow" (colour instruction) or "imagine horizontal" (orientation instruction) they were to imagine yellow horizontal lines (CS+) and likewise for the "imagine blue" and "imagine vertical" instructions (CS-). Unbeknownst to participants, they only received the mild shock (US) to the orientation instructions. This manipulation allowed for a disambiguation of descriptive and depictive elements of how imagination interacts with fear. Next, participants completed the Behavioural Avoidance phase, whereby participants had the option to avoid the US after hearing the trial's instructions. Finally, in the Transfer phase, participants were visually shown the CS+ and CS- to determine how their fear transferred from imagery to perception. Self-report, skin conductance response (SCR), and behavioural avoidance attempts were used as dependent measures. Results from each phase and dependent measure suggested that fear was driven by the orientation instructions. Furthermore, fear was shown to transfer from imagery to the corresponding visual stimuli. In this way, these results suggest that both depictive and descriptive elements are involved in the creation of fears in our imagination.

articles.title: Using Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance to Improve Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Risk Stratification in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes from Primary Care and Endocrinology Settings.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Current metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) guidelines recommend fibrosis screening in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) because of their increased risk of clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2). However, fibrosis risk is variable, and clinical tools to identify individuals at lower risk are lacking. We evaluated whether assessment of insulin resistance by homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) could improve risk stratification for clinically significant fibrosis.

METHODS: We prospectively recruited 501 adults with T2D from primary care and endocrinology clinics. Participants were classified as insulin-resistant (HOMA-IR ≥2.5; n=350) or insulin-sensitive (HOMA-IR <2.5; n=151). Liver steatosis was assessed using VCTE, MRI/MRE, or liver biopsy according to the most accurate test, and the prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2) was compared between groups.

RESULTS: Insulin-resistant participants had higher prevalence of clinically significant fibrosis than insulin-sensitive participants (≥F2: 10% vs. <1%; p<0.001). They also had greater hepatic steatosis, higher ALT, AST, CK-18, HbA1c, and adipose tissue insulin resistance (Adipo-IR) levels, and lower adiponectin concentrations (all p<0.001). Fibrosis was infrequent among insulin-sensitive participants and almost exclusively limited to mild fibrosis (stage F1). Among participants with steatosis, ≥F2 fibrosis was present in 1% of insulin-sensitive participants compared with 13% of insulin-resistant participants (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinically significant fibrosis (≥F2) was uncommon among insulin-sensitive individuals with T2D and largely limited to mild fibrosis (F1). HOMA-IR <2.5 identified a subgroup at very low risk for fibrosis, supporting its potential use as a simple, clinically accessible tool for MASLD risk stratification in primary care and endocrinology settings.

articles.title: Clinical Feasibility of a Low-Dose Tirzepatide Strategy in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes: Persistence, Metabolic Benefit, and Treatment Simplification in a Real-World Cohort.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical feasibility of a low-dose tirzepatide strategy in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in routine outpatient practice.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included Japanese adults who initiated tirzepatide between April 2024 and December 2025 and received a maximum observed dose of ≤5 mg/week through week 28. The primary endpoint in adults aged ≥65 years combined treatment persistence, absence of adverse event (AE)-related discontinuation, and either ≥3% weight loss or an HbA1c reduction ≥1.0 percentage point (≥11 mmol/mol). Younger adults were contextual comparators using overlap weighting.

RESULTS: Among 122 tirzepatide initiators, 107 were included in the low-dose strategy cohort, including 37 older adults. The primary endpoint was achieved by 23/37 (62.2%); 33/37 (89.2%) remained on treatment, and 2/37 (5.4%) discontinued because of AEs. Median body weight change was -3.07%, median HbA1c change was -1.0 percentage point (-11 mmol/mol), and 19/37 (51.4%) achieved HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol). Renal, hydration, and nutritional laboratory markers remained generally stable. Overlap-weighted comparisons showed no clear age-related attenuation.

CONCLUSION: In selected older adults, low-dose tirzepatide provided modest metabolic benefit with high persistence and infrequent AE-related discontinuation.

articles.title: Differential impacts of fine particulate matter constituents on congenital heart disease across critical periconceptional windows.
articles.abstract: The effect of specific chemical constituents of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) on congenital heart disease (CHD) remains unknown and urgently needed. This study aimed to quantify the associations between PM2.5 constituents and CHD risk, identify critical exposure windows, and explore potential effect modifiers. We included 12,680 CHD cases and 10,266 controls from the Guangdong Registry of CHD (2004-2022). Multilevel logistic regression found that PM2.5 total mass and its constituents were significantly associated with CHD, particularly during the preconception period, with each interquartile range (IQR) increase corresponding to a 9-16% elevated risk. The associations were generally attenuated in later exposure windows, whereas BC and nitrate showed significant associations during pregnancy. Conotruncal defects showed the strongest association with PM2.5 constituents (ORs ranged from 1.14 to 1.36 per IQR increase). Mixture analyses indicated that sulfate and BC dominated the effects during preconception, while BC and nitrate prevailed subsequently. Subgroup and interaction analyses showed that higher socioeconomic status significantly amplified PM2.5 constituent-related CHD risk during the preconception period, whereas multiparity and lack of folic acid supplementation significantly modified risk during later windows (P for interaction <0.05). These findings underscore that periconceptional exposure to PM2.5 is associated with increased CHD risk, with effects varying by constituent and exposure window. Targeting emissions of BC, sulfate, and nitrate may help mitigate PM2.5-related CHD burden.

articles.title: MR-409 promotes neurogenesis and improves neurological function after cerebral ischemia through attenuation of microglial activation.
articles.abstract: Neurological recovery during the chronic phase of ischemic stroke (IS) remains a major clinical challenge. Our previous studies showed that the growth hormone-releasing hormone analogue (GHRH-A) MR-409 promotes neurogenesis and improves neurological outcomes. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) mouse model was used to investigate whether early modulation of microglial activation mediates these effects. MR-409 (2.5, 5, or 10 μg, s.c.) was administered immediately after tMCAO and daily for 3, 7, 14, or 28 days depending on the experimental design. The GHRH receptor antagonist MIA-602 and the microglial inhibitor minocycline (MINO) were used to assess mechanism involvement. We found that MR-409 (10 μg, s.c.) significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema and improved function and cerebral blood flow at 3 days. It suppressed hippocampal microglial activation and promoted M2 polarization at 3-7 days, decreasing TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 while increasing CD206, Arg-1, and YM1/2, which were reversed by MIA-602. MR-409 enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis, increasing Nestin+, Tbr2+, and DCX+ cells at 7-14 days and newborn neuron survival at 28 days. These effects were enhanced by MINO but abolished by MIA-602. Functionally, MR-409 or MINO improved motor performance at 7 days, whereas only MR-409 improved both motor and cognitive function at 28 days. These findings indicate that MR-409 promotes long-term neurological recovery by attenuating acute microglial activation, improving the post-ischemic microenvironment, and enhancing hippocampal neurogenesis, highlighting its therapeutic potential for IS.

articles.title: Calcium-sensing receptor-NLRP3 inflammasome signaling in cardiovascular diseases: Preclinical evidence and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: The chronic low-grade inflammation driven by NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is increasingly acknowledged as an underlying mechanism of myocardial infarction, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and atherosclerosis. Extracellular Ca2+, amino acids, and other ligands link to intracellular Ca2+ overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, reactive oxygen species generation, thioredoxin-interacting protein activation, and NF-κB-dependent inflammasome priming via the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). Experimental studies indicate that CaSR may activate the NLRP3 inflammasome through these pathways in a cell- and context-dependent manner. In preclinical cardiovascular models, CaSR-mediated NLRP3 signaling has been implicated in neutrophil- and macrophage-mediated post-MI remodeling, atrial cardiomyocyte inflammatory remodeling in atrial fibrillation, and vascular smooth muscle and endothelial dysfunction in hypertension and atherosclerosis. Importantly, CaSR signalling may exert pro-inflammatory or protective effects depending on the cell type, ligand, dose, disease stage, and local microenvironment. Here, we review preclinical evidence and emerging translational evidence separately, highlighting the CaSR-NLRP3 signalling in cardiovascular disease, describe pharmacologic approaches that may modulate CaSR, NLRP3, or downstream inflammatory pathways, and identify key mechanistic and clinical knowledge gaps. Although direct clinical evidence for a complete CaSR-NLRP3 axis in cardiovascular diseases remains limited, these findings support further investigation of context-specific CaSR-NLRP3 crosstalk as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Neuroimmune and neuroendocrine mechanisms of the brain-heart axis in cardiovascular diseases: a review.
articles.abstract: The brain-heart axis, a core bidirectional communication network linking the central nervous system and cardiovascular system, plays a pivotal role in the onset, progression, and prognosis of cardiovascular diseases when its regulatory homeostasis is disrupted. This review systematically examines the core regulatory pathways and molecular mechanisms of the brain-heart axis and highlights its pathological roles in major cardiovascular diseases, such as hypertension, coronary artery disease, heart failure, and arrhythmias. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in key pathways, including autonomic imbalance, hyperactivation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, and dysregulation of neuroimmune and inflammatory responses. In parallel, this review explored translational pathways for clinical applications, including neurostimulation therapies, psychological intervention strategies, biomarker development, and personalized diagnostic and therapeutic protocols. By integrating mechanistic insights with translational perspectives, this article aims to provide a theoretical foundation for elucidating neurogenic mechanisms in cardiovascular disease and practical guidance for developing innovative precision-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Machine-learning versus traditional scoring methods for prediction of atrial fibrillation recurrence after catheter ablation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation remains common, with recurrence rates up to 45%. Traditional risk scores demonstrate only modest predictive performance. Machine learning (ML) approaches have shown promise in improving risk stratification by leveraging high-dimensional clinical and imaging data, but direct comparisons with traditional scores remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the discriminative performance of ML models versus traditional risk scores in predicting AF recurrence following catheter ablation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched to 11 June 2026 for studies reporting head-to-head comparisons of ML and traditional risk models predicting AF recurrence after ablation. The primary outcome was model discrimination, measured by the C-statistic. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool discrimination estimates, and meta-regression was performed to compare ML and traditional approaches. Subgroup analysis was conducted to explore the effect of ML model architecture. Methodological quality was assessed using the PROBAST tool.

RESULTS: Eleven studies (n = 17,150) were included. ML models demonstrated higher pooled discrimination compared with traditional risk scores (AUC 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.86 vs. 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.62; QM 18.96, p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis suggested that multimodal fusion models achieved the highest pooled discrimination, followed by neural-network models. Tree-based models did not significantly outperform traditional risk scores in the primary analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: ML models showed higher discrimination compared to traditional risk scores in predicting AF recurrence after ablation. Methodological limitations, lack of calibration reporting, and absence of external validation limit immediate clinical adoption.

articles.title: Emergency vascular surgery in space, on the moon, and mars: fundamental principles, technical protocols, and hemostatic methods under different gravitational regimes (0 g, 0.16 g, 0.38 g).
articles.abstract: Human exploration of the Moon and Mars presents unprecedented challenges for emergency vascular surgery, as gravitational environments ranging from microgravity (0 g) to partial gravity on the lunar (0.16 g) and Martian (0.38 g) surfaces render conventional Earth-based techniques inadequate. This review synthesizes data from experimental physiology, ground-based analog models, parabolic flight testing, and theoretical hemodynamic modeling to establish a framework for vascular interventions across three gravitational regimes. In microgravity, electrosurgery is entirely inapplicable, necessitating the use of hermetically sealed fluid-filled surgical systems (AISS) for all vascular procedures. On the lunar surface, bipolar electrosurgery may be employed with strict limitations, including mandatory smoke aspiration, reduced power output, and limited activation time. Mars, with 0.38 g, most closely approximates Earth conditions, allowing standard surgical techniques with minor modifications. Differentiated technical protocols are proposed for five critical vascular emergencies: peripheral arterial thromboembolism, ascending thrombophlebitis, aortic dissection, cerebral thrombosis, and coronary thrombosis. Endovascular approaches are prioritized due to their minimally invasive nature and reduced resource requirements. Gravity-independent hemostatic modalities (laser, ultrasonic, mechanical) represent strategic priorities for future mission planning. AISS is mandatory for microgravity and lunar operations, while artificial gravity through centrifugation substantially expands endovascular therapeutic options.

articles.title: Cardiovascular phenotypes in women with Sjögren disease: hormonal, immune, and clinical perspectives.
authors: Gender Cardiovascular Disease Study Group of the Italian Society of Cardiology (SIC)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sjögren disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder with a marked female predominance and an increasingly recognised, although incompletely characterised, cardiovascular (CV) burden. This review examines the biological, clinical, and gender-related determinants of CV involvement in women with SjD.

METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE covering the period from January 2010 to July 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching to identify relevant earlier studies. Original SjD-specific studies were prioritised, while systematic reviews, meta-analyses, consensus statements, and evidence from related autoimmune or cardiovascular populations were used to provide clinical and mechanistic context. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, population specificity, and recognised methodological limitations.

RESULTS: SjD-specific observational evidence supports an association with systemic immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, subclinical vascular injury, and selected cardiopulmonary manifestations. Sex-hormone signalling, menopausal changes, and X-linked immune mechanisms may contribute to female susceptibility, although their relationship with CV outcomes remains largely hypothetical. Evidence concerning coronary microvascular dysfunction, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, arrhythmias, autonomic dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension is heterogeneous and frequently derived from small cohorts or indirect evidence. In women, fatigue, dyspnoea, pain, palpitations, and autonomic symptoms may overlap with systemic manifestations of SjD and complicate recognition of concomitant CV disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular care in women with SjD may benefit from combining established prevention and symptom-driven diagnostic pathways with attention to interstitial lung disease, systemic organ involvement, treatment exposure, and reproductive and hormonal history. The proposed assessment framework is intended to provide practical clinical orientation and to support individualised decision-making, rather than to define a standardised SjD-specific screening pathway. Prospective, sex-disaggregated studies are needed to clarify the prognostic relevance of these factors and to inform future recommendations regarding cardiovascular assessment and follow-up.

articles.title: Residual risk in coronary artery disease: Identification of cardio-reno-metabolic and psychosocial phenotypes in a Latin American cohort of the INTERASPIRE registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual cardiovascular risk remains substantial in patients with established coronary artery disease despite contemporary secondary prevention strategies. Conventional approaches focused on isolated risk factors may fail to capture the multidimensional heterogeneity of this population.

PURPOSE: To identify distinct clinical phenotypes using an unsupervised analytical approach and to explore their association with recurrent cardiovascular events.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter observational study based on the INTERASPIRE registry, including 592 Latin American patients with prior acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularization. Variables from a standardized interview were grouped into demographic, clinical, metabolic, and psychosocial domains. After variable selection, clustering was performed using Partitioning Around Medoids with Gower distance. Associations with 12-month cardiovascular events were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression models.

RESULTS: Three phenotypes were identified. Cluster 1 (42%) included younger patients with lower comorbidity burden and lower psychosocial vulnerability. Cluster 2 (27%) showed greater psychosocial burden and an adverse lipid profile, defining a higher-risk phenotype. Cluster 3 (31%) included older patients with multiple comorbidities and greater renal dysfunction. During 12-month follow-up, 7% experienced cardiovascular events. Event rates differed across clusters (3%, 10%, and 9%; log-rank p = 0.02). Compared with cluster 1, only cluster 2 showed increased risk (HR 2.66; 95% CI 1.11-6.39; p = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised phenotyping identified three clinical profiles with distinct prognostic implications. Residual cardiovascular risk appears to reflect the interaction of lipid, renal, and psychosocial domains beyond traditional risk factors.

articles.title: Multimodal characterization of equine synovitis: Correlation between arthroscopic, histopathological, and biomarker assessments in septic vs. aseptic cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopy and synovial membrane histology are complementary modalities for evaluating synovial inflammation. Cytokine involvement in non-septic arthritis is well documented but remains poorly characterized in septic synovitis.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterize the inflammatory cytokine profile associated with septic and non-septic synovitis and assess correlations among endoscopic, histological, and synovial fluid biomarker findings.

METHODS: Three groups were defined: horses undergoing elective or therapeutic endoscopy (Group 1, n=26), horses with confirmed septic synovitis (Group 2, n=25; 20 underwent endoscopic evaluation), and horses with perisynovial injuries without synovial involvement (Group 3, n=19). Synovial fluid was analysed for cell count, total protein, neutrophil percentage, and cytokine concentrations. Endoscopic and histological scores were assigned in Groups 1 and 2. Statistical analyses included non-parametric, correlation tests, and principal component analysis (PCA).

RESULTS: Endoscopic and histological scores were significantly higher in Group 2 than in Group 1 (P=.004 and P=.006, respectively). Synovial fluid cellularity was significantly higher in Group 2 (median, 19,000 cells/µL; IQR, 11,800-81,930; P<.001). IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 concentrations were significantly higher in Group 2 than in Groups 1 and 3, with IL-6 reaching a median concentration of 1,416.51 (IQR, 645.49-5,225.84) in Group 2. These four cytokines contributed most strongly to group discrimination in the PCA.

CONCLUSION: Combining endoscopic and histological evaluation with cytokine profiling provided a more comprehensive assessment of septic synovitis. IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 emerged as promising biomarkers of synovial sepsis.

articles.title: Sdhd hypermethylation promotes succinate accumulation and NLRP3-related pyroptosis in septic lung injury.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (Si-ALI) involves metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation; however, its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the role of succinate accumulation and epigenetic silencing of succinate dehydrogenase subunit D (SDHD) in Si-ALI using septic mice, macrophages, and a publicly available transcriptomic dataset from patients with sepsis. Succinate supplementation increased lung inflammation, macrophage pyroptosis, and mortality in septic mice. Analysis of the GSE54514 dataset showed reduced SDHD expression in patients with sepsis. In septic mice, Sdhd overexpression reduced succinate accumulation, pyroptosis, lung injury, and mortality. In macrophages, Sdhd overexpression reduced oxidative mitochondrial DNA (ox-mtDNA) release and NLRP3-related pyroptosis. Mechanistically, sepsis-induced upregulation of DNA methyltransferases (DNMT1, DNMT3a, and DNMT3b) was associated with Sdhd promoter hypermethylation and reduced Sdhd expression. Pharmacological DNMT inhibition with SGI-1027 reversed Sdhd promoter hypermethylation, restored Sdhd expression, reduced succinate accumulation and pyroptosis, and ameliorated lung injury. These findings support a DNMT-SDHD-succinate axis in sepsis-induced lung injury and suggest that targeting this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic target for Si-ALI.

articles.title: High prevalence of hypervirulent Staphylococcus aureus CC22-t309 in Pediatric Osteomyelitis and Septic Arthritis in China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to elucidate the molecular epidemiology, virulence factors, and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from children with osteomyelitis and septic arthritis (OM-SA) in China.

METHODS: A total of 68 S. aureus isolates were collected from pediatric patients with OM-SA in Shanghai, China, with 100 strains from children with other infections serving as controls. We performed a systematic analysis on all strains by integrating clinical metadata, whole-genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

RESULTS: Among S. aureus isolates from OM-SA cases, CC22-t309 was the dominant clone (32.3%), followed by CC59-t437 (17.6%). The prevalence of CC22-t309 in OM-SA was much higher than that in the control (32.3% vs. 8.0%, p<0.001). OM-SA patients with CC22-t309 infection presented much higher inflammatory markers than those infected with other clones (p<0.05). Notably, CC22-t309 from OM-SA exhibited higher carriage of virulence factors, including Panton-Valentine leukocidin (pvl, 100%), collagen adhesin (cna, 86.4%), and fibronectin-binding proteins (fnbA/B, 77.3%), compared with other clones (pvl, 0∼66.7%; cna, 0∼13.8%; fnbA/B, 0∼24.1%; p < 0.05). Within CC22-t309 clone, the carriage of pvl, fnbB and fnbA showed no difference between OM-SA and control group (pvl: 100% vs. 87.5%; fnbB: 77.3% vs. 85.7%; fnbA: 77.3% vs. 37.5%; p >0.05). However, the prevalence of cna in OM-SA was significantly higher than that in the control group (86.4% vs. 37.5%, p = 0.015). Furthermore, CC22-t309 isolates displayed a multidrug-resistant phenotype against β-lactams, macrolides, and lincosamides.

CONCLUSION: We identify the hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant CC22-t309 as a high-risk S. aureus lineage associated with pediatric OM-SA.

articles.title: A Single-Cell Atlas of Diabetes-Associated Remodeling in the Human Corneal Limbus.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) disrupts epithelial integrity, sensory function, basement membrane composition, wound healing, and stem cell function. Corneal epithelial homeostasis and wound healing involve the complex coordination of various sub-populations of limbal cells. However, the transcriptomic changes at the single-cell level in these cell populations associated with diabetes have never been addressed. This study aims to generate a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human DM corneal limbal tissue to advance our conceptual understanding of human diabetes-associated changes in cell types and composition, transcriptional states, cellular trajectories, and intercellular communication.

METHODS: Single-cell sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on isolated corneolimbal epithelial tissues from a total of six age-matched human donors, including three non-diabetic (N) and three DM donors using 10X Genomics. Selected transcriptomic findings were assessed at the protein level by immunofluorescence staining of corneal sections.

RESULTS: Thirteen distinct cell clusters were identified based on the top expressed gene markers in both N and DM samples. Analyses of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), biological pathways, pseudotime trajectories, and subclustering identified DM-associated transcriptional changes, cell-cycle differences, and altered inferred intercellular signaling patterns. Pathway analysis highlighted extracellular matrix organization, adhesion, inflammation, and ligand-receptor interactions that may be associated with diabetes-impaired corneal homeostasis. Immunofluorescence showed corresponding differences in protein staining patterns for selected markers, including decreased IFITM3, MMP-1, periostin, LGI4, and eNOS, and increased ADAMTS-4.

CONCLUSIONS: We provide the first high-resolution single-cell transcriptome atlas of DM-associated alterations in the human corneolimbal niche and identify molecular pathways and cellular populations that may contribute to compromised corneal homeostasis and regenerative capacity in DM.

articles.title: Is Total Urogenital Mobilization Safe and Continent-Preserving Across a Wide Age Range in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia? A Single-Center Experience of 73 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite widespread adoption of total urogenital mobilization (TUM) for feminizing genitoplasty in congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), quantitative intraoperative benchmarks remain unreported in the literature, and urinary continence outcomes in CAH remain incompletely established.

PURPOSE: To document urinary continence, complication rate and other operative parameters of TUM performed exclusively for CAH in a consecutive single-center cohort.

METHODS: 73 consecutive 46,XX CAH patients (Prader III, n=45; Prader IV, n=28), aged 2 to 168 months, underwent TUM at a single institution between January 2014 and March 2025. Operative time, estimated blood loss, complications, and urinary continence, assessed clinically and urodynamically, were analyzed. Spearman correlation assessed the relationship between common channel length and intraoperative parameters.

RESULTS: Urinary continence, supported by clinical and urodynamic findings, was preserved in all 52 toilet-trained patients (100%). No complication attributable to the surgical technique occurred over 4 years median follow-up; 11 patients (15.1%) developed catheter-related Grade I urinary tract infection, all resolving fully. Median operative time was 145 minutes (IQR 120-178) and median estimated blood loss was 16 mL (IQR 12-19); no patient required perioperative transfusion. Common channel length correlated strongly with operative time (r=0.83, p<0.001) but not with estimated blood loss (r=0.23, p=0.09). Four patients with common channel length exceeding 6.5 cm required distal urethral plate augmentation without bladder neck involvement.

CONCLUSIONS: TUM demonstrates a favorable perioperative and postoperative safety profile in CAH, with hemostatic stability independent of anatomical complexity. TUM safely preserves continence even in older children and anatomically complex cases with appropriate technical modification.

articles.title: Upfront Distal Pancreatectomy vs. Upfront Non-Operative Management in Pediatric Grade III Pancreatic Trauma: a single institution review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Management of grade III blunt pancreatic injury has shifted towards non-operative management (NOM) in pediatric trauma. In adults, the standard of care remains distal pancreatectomy (DP). We hypothesized that upfront DP in pediatric grade III pancreatic injury would be associated with faster post-injury recovery, compared to upfront NOM.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed minors presenting to a level 1 pediatric trauma center with AAST grade III blunt pancreatic injury from 2015-2025. Bivariate analyses compared baseline characteristics, management strategies and outcomes between upfront DP (<72 hours from injury) and upfront NOM (no DP within 72 hours of injury) strategies. Regression analyses evaluated independent predictors of time to full oral diet intake.

RESULTS: 31 patients met inclusion criteria (n=12 DP, n=19 NOM). The baseline characteristics of each cohort were similar. There were non-significant trends towards lower readmissions (NOM: 0 [0-1], DP: 0 [0-0]), total hospital length of stay (days, NOM: 10 [7-29], DP: 9 [6-16]), time to full oral diet intake (days, NOM: 28 [4-37], DP: 8 [4-13]) and discharge on home supplemental nutrition (NOM: 47%, DP:17%) in the DP group. There were no differences in rates of post-traumatic diabetes mellitus or exocrine pancreatic insufficiency between groups, with limited follow up (NOM: 37d [18-90], DP: 41d [20-257]). Upfront distal pancreatectomy was independently associated with earlier time to full oral diet on regression analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our hypothesis-generating findings suggest that in pediatric grade III blunt pancreatic injuries, upfront distal pancreatectomy may be associated with faster post-injury recovery, though statistical significance was not reached.

articles.title: Choroidal Microvascular Alterations on Ultra-Widefield Swept-Source OCTA in Type 2 Diabetes: Associations with Outer Retinal Structural Changes and Systemic Risk Markers.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize choroidal microvascular alterations in diabetes without diabetic retinopathy (NDR) or mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) and evaluate associations with retinal structural changes and systemic risk markers.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 209 healthy controls, 203 patients with NDR, and 199 treatment-naïve patients with mild NPDR. Ultra-widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (UWF-SS-OCTA) quantified choroidal and retinal parameters. Systemic markers, including blood pressure, HbA1c, lipid profiles, and renal markers, were assessed in diabetic participants. Correlation analyses assessed associations of choroidal microvascular parameters with retinal structural changes in the overall population and diabetic participants. Multivariable regression evaluated associations with systemic risk markers, with NDR-specific sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Choriocapillaris vascular density (CC-VD) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) were reduced in NDR versus controls, whereas retinal vascular density decreased only in NPDR (all p < 0.05). Outer retinal thickness and volume increased in NDR. In the overall cohort, both were inversely correlated with CC-VD and CVI (r = -0.25 to -0.30, all p < 0.001), with associations remaining significant in diabetic participants. Systolic blood pressure ≥140 mmHg and urinary albumin excretion rate >20 μg/min were independently associated with lower CC-VD (β = -1.03 and -1.36, respectively), whereas cystatin C >1.09 mg/L was associated with lower CVI (β = -0.92; all p < 0.05). These systemic associations persisted in NDR-specific analyses.

CONCLUSION: UWF-SS-OCTA revealed reduced CC-VD and CVI in diabetes without clinically apparent DR. Associations with outer retinal thickening and systemic risk markers suggest links among choroidal microvascular alterations, retinal structural changes, and systemic risk.

articles.title: Breathlessness catastrophizing and influencing factors study of elderly COPD patients: A latent profile analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks among the leading global causes of death, with elderly patients facing heightened risks due to age-related declines in lung function. Breathlessness catastrophizing (BC), a negative cognitive response to dyspnea including rumination, magnification. Understanding the heterogeneity of BC in elderly COPD patients is essential for developing targeted interventions.

AIMS: The objective of this study was to identify subgroups of elderly COPD patients with breathlessness catastrophizing through latent profile analysis (LPA) and to explore the related influencing factors.

METHODS: The data of 225 elderly patients with COPD were collected and analyzed. The collected data included the demographic and clinical factors, and the patients were assessed with the Breathlessness Catastrophizing Scale(BCS), the COPD Self-Efficacy Scale(CSES) and the Ruminative Response Scale(RRS).

RESULTS: The study identified three breathlessness catastrophizing subgroups: Low Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(44.4%), Moderate Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(25.8%), and High Breathlessness Catastrophizing Type(29.8%). Three factors were significantly associated with subgroups: number of COPD exacerbations in the past year, COPD self-efficacy, and rumination response (all p < 0.05). Education level and daily steps significantly influenced the low breathlessness catastrophizing type (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Elderly COPD patients exhibit heterogeneity in breathlessness catastrophizing patterns. Factors including low education levels, frequent acute exacerbations, physical inactivity, diminished self-efficacy, and excessive rumination significantly increase the risk of severe breathlessness catastrophizing. Intervention strategies should prioritize enhancing self-efficacy, managing rumination, promoting physical activity, and implementing personalized approaches for different subgroups with breathlessness catastrophizing. Multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for reducing breathlessness catastrophizing and improving health outcomes.

articles.title: Biphasic remodeling of arcuate nucleus perineuronal nets in diet-induced obese mice.
articles.abstract: The hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains neuronal populations crucial to the regulation of energy and glucose homeostasis. Many of these neurons are enmeshed by specialized extracellular matrix structures known as perineuronal nets (PNNs) that are comprised of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans, including aggrecan (ACAN), and attached chondroitin sulfate-glycosaminoglycans. In mice, the effect of high-fat diet (HFD) to increase the abundance of ARC PNNs has been implicated in obesity- and diabetes-associated metabolic impairments. However, neither the biochemical nature nor the time course of these HFD-induced PNN changes is known. In this current work, we report that the response of ARC PNNs to HFD feeding is biphasic, characterized by a steady increase in abundance during the first ∼3 months, followed by a gradual decrease at later time points, as diet-induced obesity (DIO) becomes more fully established. Our findings suggest that this novel, biphasic patten of PNN remodeling is 1) driven by weight gain rather than by HFD composition per se, 2) specific to the hypothalamic ARC region, and 3) parallels obesity-associated changes in the circulating glucose level. Furthermore, histochemical analysis reveals that the early increase of ARC PNNs is due primarily to changes in CS glycan attachments rather than the underlying proteoglycan core protein, while long-term HFD associates with reductions of both CS glycans and ACAN. This biphasic remodeling process becomes detectable with the onset of excess weight gain and is paralleled by obesity-associated changes in glycemia. Based on these findings, we conclude that in response to HFD feeding, ARC PNNs exhibit a degree of plasticity not seen in other brain areas and that dynamic PNN remodeling associates with changes in peripheral glycemia.

articles.title: Hyperactive mTORC1 underlies sex dimorphic progression of MASLD in mice with hepatocyte prohibitin-1 deficiency.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prohibitins-1,2 (PHB1,2) are highly conserved and ubiquitously expressed proteins that form a multimeric ring complex within mitochondrial and plasma membranes where they intimately control cellular growth and metabolism. Prior studies in clinical and experimental models have linked PHB1 deficiency in liver with obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), in addition to MASH and hepatocellular carcinoma, though mechanisms remain poorly understood.

METHODS & RESULTS: Mice with hepatocyte-specific PHB1 haploinsufficiency (hPHB1-KD) were maintained on a standard chow diet. Compared with wild-type (WT), male hPHB1-KD mice at 6 months exhibited moderate but significant increases in body fat, systemic insulin resistance and characteristics of MASLD, while female hPHB1-KD mice were unaffected. Comprehensive transcript-/metabolomic analysis of liver tissue in the male hPHB-KD mice revealed up-regulation of glycerolipid metabolism and Lpin1, a phosphatidic acid phosphatase regulated by mTORC1 that critically regulates hepatic lipid metabolism. Markers of mTORC1 activation were increased in liver from male and female hPHB1-KD mice in the fasted state, accompanied by lower AMPKα phosphorylation, and were not responsive to insulin. PHB1 knockdown experiments in AML12 hepatocytes showed that lipid droplet accumulation occurred in parallel with increased cytosolic, but not nuclear, lipin-1 expression.
