Notably, short-term treatment with mTORC1 inhibitor Torin1 ameliorated liver steatosis and normalized mTORC1 signaling in male hPHB1-KD mice.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings illustrate novel mechanisms by which PHB1 regulates lipid metabolism and glycemic control in the liver, and further reveal a sex dimorphic role for mTORC1 hyperactivation in pathogenesis of MASLD.

articles.title: Intimal sarcoma of the pulmonary vein with left atrial extension: a case report and diagnostic relevance of MDM2.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de patologia : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Anatomia Patologica y de la Sociedad Espanola de Citologia
articles.abstract: Intimal sarcoma is an uncommon, aggressive neoplasm originating in the tunica intima of large vessels. Although most cases arise in the pulmonary artery, primary involvement of the pulmonary veins is exceptional. We present the case of a 52-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with acute heart failure and dyspnoea. Imaging studies initially suggested an atrial myxoma. Surgical resection of the lesion revealed a proliferation characterised by a relatively monotonous spindle-cell proliferation within the pulmonary vein and a separate zone showing greater pleomorphism, necrosis, and atypical mitoses within the left atrial cavity. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated nuclear positivity for MDM2, supporting the diagnosis. Pulmonary vein intimal sarcoma is an extremely rare entity that can be challenging to diagnose. Detection of MDM2 by immunohistochemistry is a key diagnostic tool.

articles.title: Endothelial AHR-APLNR signaling preserves vascular glycocalyx integrity and limits neutrophil-driven skin injury during local MRSA infection.
articles.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a major cause of skin and soft tissue infection, yet the contribution of the cutaneous vasculature to host defense remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify endothelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling as a key regulator of vascular integrity and inflammatory responses during local MRSA skin infection. MRSA challenge reduced AHR expression in cutaneous endothelial cells in both human and murine skin. Endothelial-specific AHR deficiency exacerbated skin injury, increased bacterial burden, enhanced inflammatory cytokine production, and promoted neutrophil accumulation and activation. Mechanistically, AHR-deficient endothelial cells induced exaggerated neutrophil calcium signaling and prolonged neutrophil-endothelial interactions during transendothelial migration. Loss of endothelial AHR was further associated with glycocalyx thinning, widened endothelial junctions, and vascular leakage, indicating impaired vascular barrier function. Pharmacological AHR activation partially reversed these abnormalities. Transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that endothelial AHR maintained apelin receptor (APLNR) expression, whereas pharmacological inhibition of APLNR reproduced several inflammatory and vascular features observed in AHR-deficient mice. Collectively, these findings identify an endothelial AHR-APLNR-glycocalyx pathway that preserves vascular barrier integrity and restrains maladaptive neutrophil activation during MRSA skin infection, highlighting a potential therapeutic target for bacterial skin disease.

articles.title: A Predict → Confirm → Act Framework for AI-Augmented MDRO Control Across Hospitals and Long-Term Care Facilities.
authors: European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases Study Group for Artificial Intelligence and Digitalisation (ESGAID)
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) control depends on identifying colonized patients and emerging transmission events early enough to intervene, without overwhelming infection prevention and control (IPC) teams or unnecessarily isolating patients. Predictive models using electronic health records, microbiology data, patient movement, and genomic information may support this task. We propose a practical Predict → Confirm → Act framework for artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented infection control across hospitals and long-term care facilities. In this framework, AI generates risk signals; microbiology, genomic data, and epidemiological review provide confirmation; and IPC teams apply proportionate actions such as targeted screening, preemptive precautions, cohorting, environmental investigation, or de-escalation. The framework is model-agnostic and is intended to shift attention away from algorithmic performance alone toward bedside and unit-level decisions. Safe implementation requires local threshold calibration, named alert ownership, microbiological confirmation pathways, de-escalation rules, prospective monitoring, and evaluation using IPC-relevant outcomes, including additional carriers detected, time to isolation, MDRO acquisition, isolation days avoided, alert burden, and unintended consequences.

articles.title: REDISCOVERING PEDRO ORTIZ CABANILLAS (1933-2011): PERUVIAN CYBERNETIC AND THE SOCIOBIOLOGICAL INFORMATIONAL THEORY.
articles.abstract: Pedro Ortiz Cabanillas (1933-2011), a Peruvian neurologist and professor at Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos, spent five decades building an Sociobiological Informational Theory: a systematic account of the universe, life, and organized society built around a single, redefined concept -information- understood as a material structure exclusive to living systems. Two works anchor his legacy: El Sistema de la Personalidad (1994), which gives the theory its first systematic exposition, and the Cuadernos de Psicobiología Social (2017), its most complete formulation. Ortiz proposed a five-level architecture of life (genetic, tissue, neural, psychic, and social information) governed by upward and downward determinations and by the primacy of negentropy over entropy. Working in a Lima hospital without internet access, without sustained contact with international science, and publishing almost exclusively in Spanish, Ortiz's theory remained completely unknown outside Peru. This article situates Ortiz's trajectory and theory historically, summarizes its core architecture -a body of thought that survived, barely, at the edge of disappearance- and argues for its relevance to contemporary debates on information in biology and consciousness.

articles.title: Beyond the glycation gap: A multicompartment framework for HbA1c-glycemia discordance in Pediatric type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: HbA1c is analytically standardized but biologically indirect: the measured value integrates glucose exposure through erythrocyte survival, age distribution, intracellular glucose handling, hemoglobin chemistry, and assay behavior. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has made this indirection clinically visible by revealing recurrent disagreement between laboratory HbA1c and sensor-derived glycemia in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. This focused narrative review reframes pediatric HbA1c-glycemia discordance as a measurement-biology problem rather than a single 'glycation gap.' We separate three non-equivalent residual constructs, organize the evidence across glucose exposure, extracellular protein glycation, and erythrocyte-dependent glycation, and introduce a trait-state-measurement decomposition of discordance. We distinguish glycated albumin from fructosamine, separate CGM analytical error from interstitial-glucose physiology and temporal representativeness, and grade mechanistic claims as established, supported-but-incomplete, or hypothesis-generating. Direct pediatric evidence confirms that discordance is common and partly persistent, but mechanistic adjudication remains limited because most studies measure only two domains. We therefore propose a hypothesis-localization framework - not a validated diagnostic or therapeutic algorithm - in which analytical validity and temporal alignment precede triangulation. The central aim is explainable disagreement: understanding why valid measurements differ before allowing the difference to influence care.

articles.title: Electrolyte disturbance phenotypes and adverse outcomes in the intensive care unit: The role of magnesium and potassium abnormalities.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnesium and potassium disturbances are common in critically ill patients, but the prognostic value of their co-occurrence is poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of combined magnesium-potassium phenotypes at intensive care unit (ICU) admission with 30-day in-hospital mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and invasive mechanical ventilation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 9462 adults admitted to the ICU of a tertiary hospital in Jordan (2012-2022) with admission magnesium and potassium, classified into nine phenotypes. Mortality was analyzed by Cox regression, censoring patients discharged alive at discharge, and AKI and ventilation by logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, and modified APACHE II score.

RESULTS: Thirty-day mortality was 30.6%, ranging from 25.0% with normal magnesium and potassium to 63.6% with combined hypermagnesemia-hyperkalemia. The combined phenotype had the highest adjusted hazard of death (HR 3.01, 95% CI 2.60-3.49), with positive additive interaction (relative excess risk due to interaction 0.76, 95% CI 0.29-1.23). Isolated hyperkalemia (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.46-1.82) and isolated hypermagnesemia (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.42-1.86) were also associated with mortality. The combined phenotype was associated with AKI (aOR 2.66, 95% CI 2.09-3.38) and ventilation (aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.17-1.94). Modeled continuously, potassium showed a U-shaped and magnesium a J-shaped association with mortality.

CONCLUSION: Co-occurring hypermagnesemia and hyperkalemia at ICU admission identify a high-risk phenotype. Because both are measured routinely, this combination may serve as a simple marker for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Premature ischemic stroke mortality in China to 2030: age- and sex-specific trends and projections.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age-specific evidence is needed to describe premature ischemic stroke mortality in China and to support transparent surveillance through 2030.

METHODS: We analyzed GBD 2023 estimates for China from 1990 to 2023 in eight five-year age groups from 30-34 to 65-69 years. Age-specific mortality rates were the primary outcomes. Temporal trends were estimated with log-linear segmented regression. Candidate ARIMA models were compared using rolling-origin validation, information criteria, and residual diagnostics. A 30-69-year study-specific normalized weighted mortality rate was retained only as a secondary sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Mortality rates declined across all eight age groups for males, females, and both sexes. In 2023, both-sex rates ranged from 0.44 per 100,000 in ages 30-34 years to 100.03 per 100,000 in ages 65-69 years. Age-specific 2030 forecasts ranged from 0.10 to 35.09 per 100,000 for females and from 0.46 to 107.67 per 100,000 for males. Under the secondary project-existing weighting scheme, the 2030 composite forecasts were 17.46 (95% prediction interval 7.92-27.00) per 100,000 for males, 5.47 (2.34-8.60) for females, and 11.80 (6.64-16.96) for both sexes. These composite estimates are not official GBD age-standardized rates.

CONCLUSIONS: The primary evidence shows substantial age heterogeneity and consistently higher male rates. Conditional forecasts support continued age- and sex-specific surveillance, but they do not establish causal mechanisms, intervention effects, or policy-target attainment.

articles.title: Sexual dimorphism in high-fat diet-induced depression-like phenotypes in mice: astrocyte-centered molecular, circuit, and microbiota associations.
articles.abstract: Metabolic disorders (MetD) are linked to depression, both of which exhibit sex differences in prevalence and clinical presentation; however, the mechanisms underlying sex-specific vulnerability to MetD-related depression remain unclear. Male and female C57BL/6 N mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 weeks (8 to 20 weeks of age) to induce MetD. Depression-like behaviors were assessed using the sucrose preference and forced swim tests. Ventral hippocampus (vHPC) astrocyte-centered molecular, structural, and circuit alterations were evaluated using Fluoro-Gold retrograde labeling, immunohistochemistry, and immunoblotting. Gut microbiota composition was characterized by full-length 16S rRNA sequencing and correlated with behavioral, metabolic, and neurobiological measures. Despite equivalent HFD exposure, male mice, but not females, developed pronounced metabolic dysfunction and depression-like behaviors. HFD-associated behavioral alterations in males were accompanied by sex-dependent impairments in vHPC astrocytic glutamate regulation and morphology, along with increased vHPC- nucleus accumbens (NAc) circuit activity. Peripheral insulin resistance and selective lipid abnormalities, rather than obesity or elevated glucocorticoids, showed the strongest associations with behavioral outcomes. HFD induced broadly similar gut microbiota remodeling across sexes, superimposed on distinct baseline microbial profiles, with sex-stratified analyses identifying specific taxa associated with FST performance in males but not females. These findings provide evidence for sex-dependent alterations in vHPC astrocytic morphology and vHPC-NAc circuit activity following HFD exposure, underscoring the importance of biological sex in the neurobiological responses associated with MetD-related depression.

articles.title: Needle-knife attenuates excessive autophagy and ferroptosis in post-stroke spastic hemiplegia: association with SDC1/NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to explore the molecular mechanism of needle-knife in inhibiting ferroptosis and excessive activation of autophagy, reducing nerve injury and improving motor function in post-stroke spastic hemiplegia (PSSH) rats.

METHODS: A rat model of PSSH was established using middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Neurological function and motor performance were evaluated using modified Ashworth Scale (mASS), Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) and balance beam test. TTC staining, Nissl staining and transmission electron microscopy were used to detect the cerebral infarction area and neuronal injury. Levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), glutathione (GSH) and ferrous ion (Fe²⁺) were measured by ELISA. Protein expressions of SDC1, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), GPX4 and autophagy-related proteins (LC3, p62, Beclin1) were determined by immunohistochemistry (IHC) or Western blotting (WB).

RESULTS: Compared with the sham group, the cerebral infarction area of rats in MCAO and Erastin groups increased, the neuronal damage was obvious and the mitochondrial structure was disordered. The levels of ROS, MDA and Fe²⁺ in the infarct area were significantly increased (P < 0.05), and the levels of GSH and GPX4 were decreased (P < 0.05). At the same time, the expressions of SDC1, NRF2, SLC7A11 and GPX4 in the infarction area were decreased (P < 0.05), the autophagy-related proteins LC3II/I and Beclin1 were increased (P < 0.05), and P62 was decreased (P < 0.05). Compared with the MCAO group, the needle knife treatment could improve the nerve damage in PSSH rats, restore their motor functions, and rescue the aforementioned molecular levels (P < 0.05). Compared with the needle knife group, the ferroptosis activator (Erastin), NRF2 inhibitor (ML385), and autophagy activator (rapamycin) significantly reversed the therapeutic effect of the needle knife (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Needle-knife alleviates ferroptosis and inhibits excessive autophagy in PSSH rats, and the underlying mechanism may be potentially related to the upregulation of SDC1 and the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway.

articles.title: Hibernation-driven cardiovascular adaptation: Unraveling mammalian survival strategies.
articles.abstract: Hibernation is a unique survival strategy employed by certain mammals to endure cold, food-scarce winter conditions. During hibernation, animals reduce energy expenditure through physiological adjustments, including decreased body temperature, metabolic rate, heart rate, and respiratory frequency, thereby ensuring survival in hostile environments. Despite these profound physiological fluctuations, their cardiovascular system shows no apparent pathological damage. To explore the protective mechanisms that maintain cardiovascular homeostasis and confer resistance to injury during hibernation, this review systematically summarizes multifaceted adaptive regulatory strategies, encompassing nervous system regulation, coordinated endocrine modulation, cardiovascular autoregulatory adaptations, as well as additional adaptive processes involving telomeres and nitric oxide. Furthermore, we evaluate the translational potential of these protective mechanisms in antiarrhythmic therapy, thrombosis prevention, organ preservation, and space medicine, aiming to provide novel perspectives and a theoretical foundation for future research. Nevertheless, current investigations still face challenges related to species differences and the limited generalizability of cross-species findings. Future studies should focus on systematically comparing distinct hibernation phenotypes while integrating multidisciplinary approaches to further elucidate the underlying protective mechanisms.

articles.title: Patient selection for proton therapy in lung cancer: Updating and internal-external cross-validation of a normal tissue complication probability model for acute oesophageal toxicity.
authors: national platform for proton therapy for lung cancer
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To externally validate and update a published normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model for the prediction of Grade ≥ 2 acute oesophageal toxicity (AOT) in lung cancer patients receiving (chemo-)radiotherapy (predictors: concurrent chemotherapy, gender, tumour stage, mean oesophagus dose (MOD)).

METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patient cohorts from four centres were available. Initial external validation was performed by assessing model performance. Heterogeneity of performance across cohorts was evaluated using an internal-external cross validation (IECV) method. Based on the IECV procedure, parameters were added or removed from the model to lower heterogeneity in model performance across cohorts with the aim to create a model that performed uniformly well across centres. Ridge regression was used to create the final model and bootstrapping techniques were applied to perform further internal validation.

RESULTS: Out of 937 patients, 444 (47%) had Grade ≥ 2 AOT. External validation indicated model recalibration was necessary for 1 cohort and model revision for another. IECV showed heterogeneity of performance of the original model across cohorts. To lower heterogeneity in model performance, the predictors concurrent chemotherapy, gender, and tumour stage were removed from the model, and overall treatment time (OTT) was added. The final model containing MOD and OTT as predictors showed low levels of heterogeneity in model performance (I2 of 0% for all performance measures) with optimism-corrected AUC of 0.75, calibration intercept of -0.01 and slope of 1.26.

CONCLUSION: The validation and updating of an NTCP-model for AOT resulted in a prediction model performing well in varying patient cohorts. Therefore, this updated model was added to the national indication protocol to select lung cancer patients for proton radiotherapy.

articles.title: Accelerated 3D Late Gadolinium Enhancement Pulse Sequence with Isotropic Spatial Resolution, Self-Navigation of Respiratory Motion, and Arrhythmia Rejection for Quantification of Left Atrial Fibrosis in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The left atrium (LA) is a thin structure (1.5-2.5mm). Conventional 3D late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pulse sequences for imaging the LA typically have limited through-plane resolution (2.5-5mm) or prolonged scan times (10-15min), resulting in poor image quality and limited clinical translatability. We sought to develop and test whether a 3D LGE pulse sequence featuring 1.5mm³ isotropic spatial resolution and a predictable scan time of 600 heartbeats can produce diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T for quantification of LA structural remodeling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS: A 3D LGE pulse sequence was developed using gradient-recalled echo (GRE) readout, stack-of-stars k-space sampling with variable density along the partition direction, retrospective arrhythmia rejection, and XD-GRASP reconstruction with self-navigation of respiratory motion. Thirty patients with AF (twenty imaged prior to first-time ablation, ten prior to repeat ablation) and twenty healthy controls were scanned using this pulse sequence. The upper limit of normal image intensity ratio (IIR) was derived from the control group; specifically, 2 standard deviations (SDs) above the mean. Suspected LA fibrosis was quantified by one rater. Two cardiothoracic radiologists independently graded the image quality across three categories (conspicuity, artifacts, noise) using a 5-point Likert scale per category, with a score of 3 considered clinically acceptable.

RESULTS: The proposed pulse sequence produced diagnostically acceptable image quality scores in all three categories for AF and control cohorts. Retrospective rejection of data acquired during ectopic heartbeats significantly (p<0.05) improved contrast-to-noise ratio (+3.7%) and sharpness (blur metric -3.2%) metrics, albeit at the expense of a significantly reduced signal-to-noise ratio (-4.4%). The upper limit of normal IIR was 1.43. Using this cutoff value to identify suspected LA fibrosis, compared with the control group (2.47 ± 2.24%), the first-time ablation group (7.45 ± 7.38%) was not significantly different (p = 0.14), whereas the repeat ablation group (14.94 ± 13.83%) was significantly different (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The proposed pulse sequence produces diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T and provides evidence of LA structural remodeling in AF patients, including greater suspected LA fibrosis burden, relative to control subjects.

articles.title: Diffuse elevations of T1 and T2 are common in newly transplanted pediatric cardiac grafts without rejection and decrease over time.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric heart transplantation carries a high risk of subclinical myocardial injury and rejection. While cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) parametric map elevations detect subtle myocardial changes with rejection, the typical temporal evolution of T1 and T2 values and their correlation with diastolic function in new grafts remains poorly defined.

METHODS: This prospective study evaluated 14 pediatric heart transplant recipients without acute rejection who underwent 22 non-contrast 1.5T CMR with their routine catheterization. New grafts (≤6 months; n=7) were compared to age-, sex- and body surface area-matched controls with established, established grafts (≥12 months; n=15). Comprehensive T1 and T2 mapping was performed and systolic/diastolic function were quantified with left atrial (LA) strain, volumes, and ejection fraction. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models (LMM) and Hedge's g effect sizes.

RESULTS: Compared to established grafts, new grafts demonstrated significantly elevated Mean T1 (Δ 27 ms; p=0.005, g=1.25), Peak T1 (Δ 43 ms; p=0.02, g=1.03), and Mean T2 (Δ 2.6 ms; p=0.05, g=1.18). Longitudinal follow-up in three new grafts revealed temporal normalization of T1. Peak T2 (Δ2.5 ms; p=0.2, g=0.62) did not reach statistical significance. Functionally, new grafts exhibited trends of early diastolic impairment, including lower LA strain and higher indexed LA volumes. While these functional differences did not reach statistical significance, they demonstrated large, standardized effect sizes (g ≥ 0.8), suggesting directional trends that warrant larger investigation.

CONCLUSIONS: During the first 6 months post-transplant, pediatric grafts exhibit diffuse and focal T1 and T2 elevations accompanied by transient diastolic impairment. In this pilot study, these directional trends likely reflect expected ischemia-reperfusion injury, edema, and new graft remodelling rather than acute rejection. Utilizing graft-age-specific normative values is essential to avoid false-positive rejection diagnoses during early post-transplant CMR surveillance.

articles.title: Remnant Lipoproteins as Dynamic Metabolic States: A Residence Time-Based Framework for TRL Metabolism.
articles.abstract: Remnant lipoproteins are recognized as atherogenic derivatives of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (TRLs). However, the definition of "remnants" remains heterogeneous and incompletely resolved. Remnants have been regarded as partially lipolyzed intermediates generated during lipoprotein lipase (LPL)-mediated metabolism of chylomicrons and very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDLs). Current operational definitions vary and include ultracentrifugation-defined fractions (IDLs), remnant-like lipoprotein particles (RLPs), remnant cholesterol (RC), and apolipoprotein-defined subclasses. These approaches identify overlapping yet compositionally heterogeneous particles. Here, we propose that remnant lipoproteins should be conceptualized not as fixed particle classes, but as dynamic metabolic states arising during delayed TRL clearance. The defining characteristic of a remnant is prolonged intravascular residence time rather than density, size, or apolipoprotein composition alone. Physiological "nascent remnants" generated during normal postprandial metabolism are rapidly cleared through apoE-mediated hepatic uptake pathways, whereas metabolically "retained remnants" persist within the circulation and undergo lipolytic remodeling, oxidative modification, endothelial interaction, and acquisition of atherogenic potential. We further discuss how imbalance between TRL influx and TRL-processing reserve may contribute to remnant retention and metabolic disease. In this context, circulating intact lipoprotein lipase (intact LPL), representing structurally preserved full-length LPL, may provide a functional window into systemic TRL-processing capacity. The TG/intact LPL ratio may serve as a surrogate reflecting imbalance between TRL burden and lipolytic processing reserve. This residence time-based framework may help integrate observations across postprandial lipemia, obesity-associated dyslipidemia, multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome, and residual cardiovascular risk. More broadly, this perspective shifts the conceptual focus of remnant biology from static particle classification toward dynamic metabolic processing within the TRL cascade.

articles.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Cytokine Signatures in Real-Time PCR-Confirmed Acute Bacterial Meningitis: Diagnostic Insights from TNF-α and IL-1β.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute bacterial meningitis (ABM) is a rapidly progressive central nervous system infection where excessive neuroinflammation contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytokines are key mediators of host immune responses; however, their association with molecular pathogen detection and host inflammatory responses remains incompletely understood OBJECTIVE: To evaluate CSF cytokine responses and their association with molecularly confirmed acute bacterial meningitis METHODS: A total of 246 CSF samples from patients with suspected meningitis, submitted to the department (February 2015 to January 2021) were evaluated. CSF supernatants were used for cytokine quantification, while sediments underwent bacterial culture and Real-time PCR. Cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-6 and IL-10) were measured using cytometric bead array. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated diagnostic accuracy.

RESULTS: Bacterial DNA was detected in 53/246 (21.5%) samples, with Streptococcus pneumoniae being the predominant pathogen, particularly in children under five. Real-time PCR-confirmed cases showed significantly higher CSF TNF-α and IL-1β levels compared with non-confirmed cases (p = 0.013 and p = 0.033), indicating a predominant pro-inflammatory cytokine. Elevated IL-10 levels suggested concurrent anti-inflammatory regulation. ROC analysis demonstrated modest overall discrimination for TNF-α (AUC = 0.657, p = 0.013) and IL-1β (AUC = 0.605, p = 0.162). However, at an optimal threshold of 0.60 pg/ml, TNF-α achieved 100% specificity, establishing high reliability.

CONCLUSIONS: Real-time PCR-confirmed acute bacterial meningitis is characterized by a distinct CSF cytokine signature reflecting coordinated pro-inflammatory activation and regulatory immune responses, highlighting CSF TNF-α as a high-specificity adjunctive to molecular assays.

articles.title: Azathioprine versus mycophenolate mofetil in treatment-naive autoimmune hepatitis: 3-year follow-up of the CAMARO-trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The CAMARO trial demonstrated superior short-term tolerability and response rates of mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) versus azathioprine (AZA), both combined with prednisolone, in treatment-naïve autoimmune hepatitis (AIH). We evaluated long-term outcomes.

METHODS: Patients enrolled in the multicenter randomized CAMARO trial were retrospectively followed for up to 3 years after treatment initiation. Co-primary endpoints were trial-assigned treatment with normalized alanine aminotransferase (ALT) at 3 years and time to biochemical response (normalization of ALT and immunoglobulin G).

RESULTS: Three-year follow-up was available for 67 patients (96%; 30 AZA, 37 MMF). At 3 years, 57% versus 76% remained on trial-assigned treatment with normalized ALT (p = 0.099). Median time to biochemical response was 64 versus 16 weeks (adjusted HR 2.74, 95% CI 1.49-5.06; p = 0.001). Among patients without ALT normalization at 24 weeks, 6/12 AZA-treated and 6/11 MMF-treated patients subsequently normalized ALT. Among patients remaining on randomized treatment at 24 weeks, subsequent treatment discontinuation occurred in 5/24 (21%) with AZA and 7/37 (19%) with MMF. Steroid-free ALT normalization (64% vs. 66%) and adverse event rates during year 3 (70% vs. 74%) were comparable (both p > 0.05). Five-year liver-related event-free survival was 70% (95% CI 55-93%) with AZA and 85% (95% CI 71-100%) with MMF (p = 0.080).

CONCLUSIONS: MMF was associated with faster biochemical response and numerically better overall tolerability. Among patients tolerating their assigned treatment during the initial treatment phase, subsequent outcomes were comparable between AZA and MMF. The substantial treatment burden with both therapies highlights the need for improved treatment options.

articles.title: The Carbon Footprint of Clinical Artificial Intelligence in Anaesthesiology: An Order-of-Magnitude Comparison with Current Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping anaesthesiology and critical care, enhancing physiological monitoring, perioperative risk prediction, and clinical decision-making. As its adoption accelerates, attention has increasingly turned to the environmental consequences of digital healthcare, raising important questions regarding the energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with clinical AI. This study examines the environmental implications of AI in anaesthesiology and critical care by placing computational emissions within the broader context of healthcare sustainability. Current evidence indicates that, although AI systems generate measurable greenhouse gas emissions, their operational carbon footprint remains several orders of magnitude lower than that of established sources of emissions, including volatile anaesthetic agents, intensive care, and surgical care. Quantitative comparisons, complemented by an illustrative environmental break-even analysis, suggest that even modest improvements in healthcare efficiency may be sufficient to offset the operational emissions of current clinical AI applications. These findings indicate that the sustainability of clinical AI should not be judged solely by its computational footprint, but by its overall environmental value. The relevant question is not simply how much AI emits, but whether its implementation reduces resource utilisation, avoids unnecessary healthcare activities, and generates environmental savings that outweigh its own operational costs. Achieving this objective will require computationally efficient model design, low-carbon digital infrastructures, lifecycle assessment, and the routine integration of environmental metrics into AI evaluation. Rather than representing a major new source of healthcare emissions, clinical AI should be viewed as an opportunity to advance both digital innovation and environmental stewardship. By integrating sustainability alongside clinical effectiveness, anaesthesiologists are uniquely positioned to guide the responsible development and implementation of AI technologies that benefit both patients and the healthcare systems in which they are delivered.

articles.title: Guidance for continuous glucose monitor (CGM) use in Canadian hospitals.
articles.abstract: People living with diabetes and healthcare providers are increasingly advocating for the option to continue use of their personal continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices during hospital admission to promote continuity of care. Although no CGM devices are currently approved by Health Canada for inpatient use, CGM use in ambulatory settings has been shown to improve glycemic outcomes and patient experience compared with capillary glucose monitoring. Publications in recent years have demonstrated that CGM use in specific populations can be safe and may improve glycemic control while reducing hypoglycemia risk. Accordingly, hospitals must determine how to safely and practically integrate CGM into inpatient clinical practice. This article provides practical guidance for the use of CGM in Canadian hospitals for inpatient glucose monitoring.

articles.title: Recent advances in research on the association between lactylation and regulated cell death in sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction mediated by host immune dysregulation, and elevated serum lactate levels are an important pathophysiological feature. Lactate is not only the terminal product of glucose metabolism but also acts as a signaling molecule that regulates gene expression and protein function through lactylation. Regulated cell death (RCD), as a targetable terminal cell fate, offers a potential direction for precision intervention in sepsis.

OBJECTIVE: Although studies have indicated that lactylation can affect sepsis progression by regulating RCD, no review has systematically summarized this relationship. Therefore, this review systematically summarizes the regulatory roles of lactylation in RCD and their pathological significance in sepsis.

INNOVATION: Based on the above evidence, this review proposes that "lactylation modification imbalance-aberrant activation of RCD" may be a potential driving mechanism of sepsis progression and that the lactylation/acetylation imbalance caused by glucose metabolism reprogramming is an upstream regulatory link of this axis.

CONCLUSION: In summary, targeting lactylation modification to precisely modulate RCD may interrupt the pathological chain from lactate elevation to organ injury, providing new perspectives for sepsis treatment research.

articles.title: 24-Hour Movement Behavior Reallocations and Glycemic Variability in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Longitudinal Isotemporal Substitution Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Glycemic variability (GV) is an important cardiometabolic risk marker in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D). We estimated the effects of reallocating time among sleep, sedentary behavior, light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) on six GV outcomes in adults with T1D. Methods: This secondary analysis included 23 adults contributing 102 days with concurrent accelerometer-based activity monitoring and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Compositional rescaling was applied to ensure a 24-h in total. Isotemporal substitution models with linear mixed-effects regression were used to estimate associations of 30-min reallocations among behaviors (e.g., from sleep to LPA) with GV outcomes, including standard deviation of glucose (SD), coefficient of variation (CV), large amplitude of glycemic excursions (LAGE), mean amplitude of glycemic excursions (MAGE), continuous overlapping net glycemic action with a 60-min lag (CONGA-60), and time in range (TIR), while adjusting for covariates. Results: Participants had a mean age of 32.6 years, BMI of 28.2 kg/m2, and diabetes duration of 16.3 years. Reallocating 0.5 hours from sleep to sedentary time, LPA, or MVPA significantly reduced CV (estimate range: -14.4 to -15.2, all p < 0.05) and TIR (estimate range: -3.6 to -3.6, all p < 0.01). Replacing sedentary time with LPA significantly reduced LAGE (estimate = -3.4, p = 0.035). No significant associations were found for SD, MAGE, or CONGA-60. Conclusion: These findings highlight that optimizing glycemic stability in adults with T1D requires a nuanced consideration of how reallocations between sleep, sedentary time, LPA, and MVPA differentially affect GV, TIR, and LAGE.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of No Thromboprophylaxis after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent Saphenous VeiNs: the TRAIN Non-inferiority Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The benefit of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after endovenous radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for incompetent saphenous veins in patients without previous deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the lower limbs is unclear. This trial compared no extended thromboprophylaxis with extended anticoagulation after RFA.

METHODS: TRAIN (Thromboprophylaxis after endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent saphenous veiNs) was a multicentre, evaluator blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial. Adults with primary great saphenous vein incompetence undergoing RFA, with concomitant tributary phlebectomy and or ultrasound guided foam sclerotherapy when clinically indicated, were enrolled. Patients with previous DVT of the lower limbs were excluded. All participants received a single intra-operative intravenous dose of unfractionated heparin and were randomised to either no extended pharmacological thromboprophylaxis or rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for fourteen days post-operatively. The primary outcome was thrombosis related events within thirty days.

RESULTS: Of 406 patients screened, 354 were included in the intention to treat analysis and 304 in the per protocol analysis. The no extended thromboprophylaxis strategy was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events (risk difference -1.34%, 95% confidence interval -7.53 - 4.84%; p = .022 for non-inferiority). One participant in the anticoagulation group (one of 177; 0.6%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding on post-operative day 10. No bleeding event occurred in the no anticoagulation group (0 of 177; p = 1.0).

CONCLUSION: Omitting extended post-operative rivaroxaban thromboprophylaxis after RFA with concomitant phlebectomy and sclerotherapy in patients without previous DVT was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events. Prophylactic rivaroxaban was not associated with an increased risk of bleeding.

articles.title: Identification of predisposing factors for hematotoxicity in occupational benzene-exposed workers using machine learning and SHAP interpretation.
articles.abstract: Benzene is an important industrial material and environmental pollutant, and even low-level exposure has been associated with hematotoxicity. Therefore, the identification of predisposing factors for hematotoxicity induced by occupational benzene exposure is crucial for managing occupational benzene poisoning. Herein, we recruited 1513 petrochemical workers in southern China, including 847 control workers and 666 workers with hematotoxicity. After randomly dividing the dataset into a training set (75%) and a test set (25%), we employed six machine learning algorithms construct a prediction model. Through recursive feature elimination, 22 feature variables, including age, work years, department, benzene, toluene, xylene, noise, AST/ALT, ALP, GGT, TBIL, DBIL, TC, TG, LDL-C, HDL-C, GLU, SCr, Urea, UA, FEV1/FVC%, and DBP were initially identified. Styrene was included due to its occupational relevance, resulting in 23 input variables for model development. We found the XGBoost algorithm was the optimal model for identifying factors affecting hematotoxicity. SHAP analysis based on the XGBoost model further characterized the contributions of variables at both the overall and individual levels, identifying benzene, noise, work years, age, department, and liver function indicators as important factors while also showing the direction and magnitude of their associations with the predicted risk of hematotoxicity. In vitro experiments also shown that impaired liver function exacerbated 4-benzoquinone (1,4-BQ)-induced cytotoxicity in bone marrow cells and modulated the underlying molecular pathways. Together, liver function-related indicators emerged as important predictors of hematotoxicity risk among benzene-exposed workers. These findings may help inform occupational health surveillance and risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Studies on Women's Experiences of Initial Miscarriage Care at the First Point of Clinical Contact.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Miscarriage is a common pregnancy complication, yet women's experiences of care at the first point of clinical contact remain insufficiently understood. This systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis examined how women experience and evaluate initial miscarriage care and what needs and priorities they identify during this early stage.

DATA SOURCES: CINAHL, Scopus, and PubMed were systematically searched for qualitative and mixed methods studies published between January 2015 and December 2024 following a preregistered protocol on the Open Science Framework and PRISMA 2020 guidance.

STUDY SELECTION: Eligibility criteria were developed using the SPIDER framework and included studies reporting women's experiences of care at first clinical contact for miscarriage (e.g., emergency departments, early pregnancy assessment units, outpatient triage) and published in English. Of 1,091 records identified (1,035 after deduplication), 45 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and 10 studies, predominantly from high-income settings, met the inclusion criteria. Studies were appraised for methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data relevant to women's experiences, needs, and priorities during early miscarriage care were extracted from the 10 studies involving 232 women (nurses and nurse managers interviewed alongside parents in one review were not counted, consistent with this review's inclusion criteria) and synthesized thematically.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Four themes were developed: Emotional Shock and Vulnerability, Communication and Information Gaps, Clinical Prioritization Versus Emotional Needs, and Navigating Discharge and Ongoing Uncertainty. Across studies, initial miscarriage services were found to prioritize physical management while frequently overlooking emotional and informational support.

CONCLUSION: This review offers a focused synthesis of women's experiences at the earliest stages of miscarriage care, revealing a persistent gap between clinical and emotional responsiveness. The findings provide new evidence to inform more compassionate, woman-centered early miscarriage pathways that integrate timely clinical care with clear communication and psychosocial support.

articles.title: Maternal vitamin D status, deficiency prevention strategies, and perinatal health outcomes.
articles.abstract: Adequate maternal nutrition is vital for fetal development and maternal health. Although vitamin D is a widely utilized prenatal supplement, its clinical efficacy in improving major pregnancy outcomes remains a topic of debate. This study reviewed the physiological roles of vitamin D, evaluated the clinical impact of maternal supplementation on perinatal indices, and provided practical clinical recommendations within the context of regional public health challenges. Although observational data have consistently associated low maternal 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels with adverse outcomes, interventional evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) regarding the preventive effects of vitamin D supplementation on major obstetric complications, including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, and preterm birth, remains limited, highly variable, and condition-specific. A high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency has been reported among women of childbearing age in South Korea, highlighting the importance of maternal vitamin D status from a public health perspective. For pregnant women with confirmed or suspected deficiency, a daily regimen of 1,000-2,000 IU may help achieve adequate maternal vitamin D status, taking into account dietary intake, food fortification, and prenatal vitamin use. However, the existing evidence does not support universal vitamin D supplementation solely for the prevention of major obstetric complications. Future research should shift toward precision medicine by conducting large-scale RCTs stratified by maternal body mass index, genetic polymorphisms, and behavioral and environmental factors, including smoking and sunlight exposure.

articles.title: Prediction of pregnancy following transfer of in-vitro produced embryos using recipient health records, accelerometer sensors and meteorological data in Australian dairy cows.
articles.abstract: Embryo transfer (ET) in dairy cattle has long been used for the dissemination of elite genetics. However, achieving consistently high pregnancy rates remains a major challenge, particularly in high-producing lactating dairy cows receiving in-vitro produced (IVP) embryos. We hypothesised that recipient selection and ET program timing could be optimised using individual items of recipient and meteorological data that are routinely available on dairy farms. To investigate this hypothesis, we conducted an observational study that explored associations between recipient characteristics, health events, sensor-derived activity alerts, meteorological variables and their ability to predict successful pregnancy following ET (P/ET) in an on-farm IVP embryo program. Cow health data and ear tag health sensor alerts from a commercial dairy herd in southern Australia were used to compile a retrospective dataset of 5770 embryo transfers (ETs) in 4681 recipients. Meteorological records from two nearby weather stations were used to calculate temperature humidity index (THI). Univariable generalised linear models were used to test associations between predictors and P/ET. Outputs from models included risk differences (RD), P-values, 95% confidence intervals and area under the curve (AUC). Population RD were calculated using tabular methods. Recipient parity, days in milk (DIM), calving interval, metritis events and 'very sick' ear-tag sensor alerts were associated with P/ET, as were temperature and THI variables. Area under the curve values were close to 0.50 (range 0.50-0.55) and population RD values from many exposure variables were close to 0, indicating that optimising the ET program using individual variables as done in this study, under the conditions in this herd may have limited impact on the overall P/ET. Therefore, further research is needed to evaluate other methodologies to predict P/ET. Furthermore, future studies should incorporate non-recipient factors, such as embryo quality. It is unclear if the associations observed in this study are due to causal relationships; therefore, we recommend that observational and intervention studies be conducted to verify this.

articles.title: Postnatal Dynamics of Choroid Plexus Cysts in Newborns and Infants: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Purpose Choroid plexus cysts (CPC) are frequently detected prenatally and are generally considered benign. However, data on their postnatal course, growth dynamics, and clinical relevance are limited. This study investigates the long-term development, growth patterns, and resolution of CPC in newborns and infants. Materials and Methods We retrospectively analysed 251 CPC in 164 patients admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit between 2014 and 2024. CPC were assessed using serial cranial ultrasonography. Growth dynamics were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and chi-square testing. Results CPC were identified in both preterm and term infants, with a mean CPC size of 4.1 mm at diagnosis. Of 177 CPC with serial imaging data, 40% were not present on initial scans and appeared postnatally. The median time to resolution was 108 days. Many CPC initially increased in size before decreasing or resolving completely. A chi-square analysis showed a significant shift in growth behaviour between the 6- and 12-week follow-up groups (p = 0.006). No infant required intervention related to CPC. Conclusion Postnatal CPC often follow a benign, self-limiting course, meaning they tend to resolve naturally over time, with dynamic growth patterns. Routine monitoring of isolated CPC in asymptomatic infants may not be needed in all cases. Ziel Choroidplexuszysten (CPC) werden häufig pränatal festgestellt und gelten im Allgemeinen als gutartig. Allerdings liegen nur begrenzte Daten zu ihrem postnatalen Verlauf, ihrer Wachstumsdynamik und ihrer klinischen Relevanz vor. Diese Studie untersucht die langfristige Entwicklung, die Wachstumsmuster und die Rückbildung von CPC bei Neugeborenen und Säuglingen. Materialien und Methoden Wir analysierten retrospektiv 251 CPC bei 164 Patienten, die zwischen 2014 und 2024 auf eine neonatologische Intensivstation aufgenommen wurden. Die CPC wurden mittels serieller kranialer Sonographie beurteilt. Die Wachstumsdynamik wurde mittels Kaplan-Meier-Überlebensanalyse und Chi-Quadrat-Test ausgewertet. Ergebnisse CPC wurden sowohl bei Frühgeborenen als auch bei termingeborenen Säuglingen festgestellt, wobei die durchschnittliche CPC-Größe bei der Diagnose 4,1 mm betrug. Von 177 CPC mit seriellen Bildgebungsdaten waren 40 % bei den ersten Untersuchungen nicht nachweisbar und traten postnatal auf. Die mediane Zeit bis zur Rückbildung betrug 108 Tage. Viele CPC nahmen zunächst an Größe zu, bevor sie sich verkleinerten oder vollständig zurückbildeten. Eine Chi-Quadrat-Analyse zeigte eine signifikante Verschiebung im Wachstumsverhalten zwischen den 6- und 12-Wochen-Nachbeobachtungsgruppen (p = 0,006). Bei keinem Säugling war eine interventionelle Behandlung im Zusammenhang mit dem CPC erforderlich. Schlussfolgerung Postnatale CPC zeigen in der Regel einen gutartigen und selbstlimitierenden Verlauf mit dynamischen Wachstumsmustern und spontaner Rückbildung. Eine routinemäßige Verlaufskontrolle isolierter CPC bei asymptomatischen Säuglingen ist möglicherweise nicht in allen Fällen erforderlich.

articles.title: Time course of muscle hypertrophy with and without progressive overload.
articles.abstract: To compare the time course of muscle hypertrophy during resistance training with progressive overload (PROG) or without overload progression (N-PROG), 31 healthy untrained young adults completed a randomized within-subject trial. Each participant trained one leg with PROG and the contralateral leg with N-PROG using unilateral knee extension (3x10-12 repetitions, twice weekly for 12 weeks). Load was progressively adjusted in PROG and kept constant in N-PROG. Muscle cross-sectional area (mCSA) was assessed at Pre and after sessions 6, 12, 18, and 24. A protocol×time interaction was observed for mCSA (p=0.002). Both protocols increased mCSA from Pre to S24 (PROG: 3.36±1.94 cm²; N-PROG: 2.67±1.86 cm²), with no significant between-protocol differences in mCSA at the individual assessment time points. However, the increase in mCSA from S18 to S24 was greater in PROG than in N-PROG (between-protocol difference in change: 1.22 cm², 95% CI 0.59 to 1.84; p<0.001). Repetitions in reserve (RIR) was 0.47±0.61 at S1 and 0.20±0.37 at S24 in PROG, and 1.50±1.11 and 4.08±1.94, respectively, in N-PROG. Overall volume load and perceived exertion were greater in PROG (p<0.001). The PROG protocol maintained high relative effort, and the greater increase in mCSA compared with N-PROG was observed specifically from S18 to S24.

articles.title: Implementation of rapid pan-microbial metagenomics in paediatric intensive care: a single-centre, prospective, observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few clinical metagenomics studies have reported rapid results with associated clinical impact or described deployment of protocols beyond centres in which they were developed. We aimed to assess the feasibility and clinical impact of implementing a previously validated rapid pan-microbial respiratory metagenomic service in paediatric intensive care, reporting protocol modifications, feasibility, diagnostic performance, clinical impact, and staff perspectives.

METHODS: This single-centre, prospective, observational study was carried out at a general paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) and a cardiac paediatric ICU in Great Ormond Street Hospital (London, UK) between Nov 4, 2024, and Feb 28, 2025. Respiratory samples were obtained from patients selected by intensive care staff based on clinical suspicion of lower respiratory tract infection, with no exclusion criteria. Samples were analysed by a well-established published metagenomic workflow that simultaneously detects bacteria, fungi, and DNA and RNA viruses and provides same-day preliminary results and next-day final results; separate aliquots were sent for concurrent culture and PCR testing. Clinical impact (change in antimicrobials, diagnosis, or infection control) was evaluated through electronic health record review. Clinical staff were surveyed for their feedback via an anonymous online semistructured questionnaire.

FINDINGS: 177 samples from 122 patients (median age 3·4 months [IQR 1·2-36·0]; 54% male) were tested. 174 (98%) samples passed quality control. Sensitivity at 16-h sequencing was 89% (95% CI 80-95) for bacteria, 100% (70-100) for fungi, and 87% (76-93) for viruses, with specificities greater than or equal to 99% across all kingdoms. 42 (24%) of 174 samples analysed by metagenomics yielded 50 organisms that were not detected by routine diagnostics, all of which were confirmed by orthogonal PCR testing. Clinical impact was observed in 51 (29%) of 174 samples, comprising changes in antimicrobial therapy in 46 (26%) samples. Of these 46 samples, 15 (33%) resulted in cessation of antibiotics, ten (22%) in initiation of antibiotics, six (13%) in a change of antibiotic therapy, and 15 (33%) provided confidence to continue an empirical antibiotic choice. Of the 33 ICU staff members surveyed, 23 (72%) reported a positive view of metagenomics, none reported negative views, and 22 (67%) perceived additional benefits over routine testing.

INTERPRETATION: This clinical pilot of rapid respiratory metagenomics in paediatric intensive care showed high specificity and good sensitivity. Protocols developed for an adult population were adapted to a paediatric population, including adaptations for polymicrobial upper respiratory tract samples, which are more common in children. However, increased sensitivity and antimicrobial resistance prediction will be required for broader clinical implementation. Although changes in patient management were observed, particularly for antimicrobial stewardship, delineating the true contribution of metagenomic results offered by this study is difficult. Multicentre studies over multiple winter seasons, with control arms and predefined selection of patients and sample types, are needed to assess the impact on patient outcomes and cost-effectiveness.

FUNDING: NHS Respiratory Metagenomics Network (NHS England).

articles.title: Airborne transmission risk of monkeypox virus: the importance of infection-competent virus.
Cross-neutralisation of authentic Ebola virus and Bundibugyo virus following natural infection or Ervebo vaccination.
Correction to Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2026; 14: 894-902.
Tenosynovitis caused by Mycobacterium malmoense.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium malmoense is a slow-growing nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) increasingly recognized as a cause of extrapulmonary infections. Tenosynovitis due to M. malmoense is rare and diagnostically challenging because of its indolent course and nonspecific clinical presentation.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 65-year-old immunocompetent woman presenting with progressive wrist pain, swelling, and impaired hand function without prior trauma. Symptoms developed after exposure to fresh fish and shellfish. Surgical exploration revealed extensive tenosynovitis with median nerve compression. Histopathology showed granulomatous synovitis suggestive of mycobacterial infection. Molecular testing detected Mycobacterium genus DNA, while PCR for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was negative. After prolonged incubation, culture identified M. malmoense. Drug susceptibility testing demonstrated susceptibility to standard antimycobacterial agents except doxycycline. Initial empiric therapy targeting M. marinum was adapted following species identification. After 8 months of treatment, significant clinical and radiological improvement was observed, with no evidence of relapse at 6-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: M. malmoense tenosynovitis is extremely rare, with only few cases reported. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to low sensitivity of microscopy, slow growth in culture, and nonspecific findings. Molecular diagnostics and prolonged incubation are essential. Management requires a combination of surgery and prolonged antimycobacterial therapy.

CONCLUSION: NTM infections, including M. malmoense, should be considered in chronic tenosynovitis unresponsive to standard treatment. Early diagnostic suspicion and interdisciplinary management are crucial for favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Lactate dehydrogenase A-dependent redox control of selective mRNA translation directs monocyte fate commitment.
articles.abstract: Monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is a central process that shapes immune responses across diverse contexts, yet how inflammatory cues engage metabolism to instruct monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Here, using a CRISPR-based metabolic screen combined with monocyte-specific perturbations in bacterial lung infection, we identified lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) as a key metabolic regulator of monocyte commitment to the nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2)+ macrophage fate in vivo. LDHA-dependent cytosolic nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) regeneration enabled selective hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1α) translation through its 5' untranslated region (UTR) and is associated with structural remodeling of this region. HIF1α then functioned as a downstream effector that promoted the NOS2+ macrophage fate. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) further acted as an upstream metabolic priming signal that enhanced LDHA-dependent HIF1α regulation and supported this differentiation process. Together, these findings suggest that metabolic redox state regulates monocyte fate commitment through selective mRNA translation coupled to RNA structural remodeling.

articles.title: The binding of OTULIN restrains LUBAC activity to prevent TNF-driven immunopathology.
articles.abstract: Met1-linked ubiquitin chains (Met1-Ub), synthesized by the linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) and disassembled by the deubiquitinase OTULIN, regulate inflammatory signaling and cell death. OTULIN activity prevents tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-driven autoinflammatory pathology and embryonic lethality, but the role of the direct OTULIN-LUBAC interaction remains unclear. Here, we show that mice harboring a point mutation in the OTULIN peptide:N-glycanase/UBA- or UBX-containing proteins (PUB)-interacting motif (OTULINY56A), which disrupts LUBAC binding, are viable without spontaneous pathology but are highly sensitive to TNF-induced toxicity and TNF-mediated immunopathology during Listeria monocytogenes infection. Mechanistically, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction prevents Met1-linked autoubiquitination, thereby limiting LUBAC activity and Met1-Ub conjugation on non-LUBAC substrates. Disrupting the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction increased Met1-Ub accumulation at the TNF receptor signaling complex, which stabilized the signaling complex, increased nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, and, unlike loss of OTULIN or its activity, protected from TNF-induced apoptosis. Collectively, we identify the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction as a critical brake restricting LUBAC function and Met1-Ub-dependent signaling.

articles.title: Perinatal nicotine exposure disrupts hematopoietic stem cell development and elevates influenza severity in adulthood.
articles.abstract: Developmental exposures profoundly shape lifelong health by altering disease resilience later in life. One potential cause of increased disease susceptibility is an altered immune system, originating in epigenetically maladaptive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Here, we establish perinatal nicotine exposure (PNE) as a mouse model of developmental maladaptive immunity, wherein early-life environmental insults permanently alter HSCs. We show that PNE selectively disrupts the establishment of HSCs and tissue-resident, but not circulating, immune cells. Remarkably, the specific decrease of HSCs and lung-resident immune cells persists into adulthood. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed durable molecular reprogramming of adult PNE HSCs, with inverse regulation of positive trained immunity signatures. Functionally, adult PNE offspring challenged with respiratory virus exhibit exacerbated immune maladaptation, marked by increased weight loss, deteriorated lung pathology, hyper-permeability of pulmonary vasculature, tissue-resident macrophage depletion, and exaggerated neutrophil recruitment. Together, our findings establish that PNE imprints durable maladaptive immunity involving changes in HSCs and their progeny, suggesting a hematopoietic origin for the PNE-induced respiratory vulnerability.

articles.title: Infectious, Environmental, and Chronic Disease Burden among 1,844 Newly Arrived Humanitarian Migrants in Oklahoma, 2019-2025.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Global displacement has brought increasingly diverse migrant populations into health systems with limited experience managing large-scale humanitarian arrivals, yet contemporary data describing infectious, environmental, and noncommunicable disease burden across heterogeneous newcomer groups remain scarce. A cross-sectional analysis of 1,844 consecutively screened newly arrived individuals who completed the U.S. domestic medical examination at the University of Oklahoma Center for Travel and Immigrant Health between October 2019 and May 2025 was conducted. Screening was performed in accordance with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Refugee Health Domestic Guidance, with programmatic adaptations. The cohort represented more than 25 countries of origin, with substantial variation across key indicators. Strongyloides stercoralis seropositivity was 14.6% overall, highest among arrivals from Vietnam (27.1%) and Cuba (25.0%). Eosinophilia exhibited low sensitivity (∼12%) for S. stercoralis seropositivity. Elevated blood lead levels (≥3.5 µg/dL) occurred in 19.2% of those tested, concentrated among young Afghan children. Latent tuberculosis infection was identified in 8.9% of patients, with marked country-level gradients. Predeparture antiparasitic therapy coverage was modest (albendazole: 42.2%; ivermectin: 34.2%). Only 6.8% of eligible women had ever undergone cervical cancer screening. Noncommunicable disease burdens varied widely by country of origin. The diverse infectious, environmental, and chronic disease profiles observed across countries of origin highlight the limitations of uniform post-arrival screening. These data support risk-stratified approaches that include targeted infectious disease testing based on country of origin and epidemiological exposures, universal predeparture hepatitis B triple-panel screening, strengthened pediatric lead surveillance, and cancer screening pathways.

articles.title: Outcomes of preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump insertion in high-risk coronary artery bypass grafting: A decade of single-centre experience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe role of prophylactic preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the safety and outcomes of preoperative IABP insertion in high-risk CABG patients.MethodsA retrospective review of outcomes of patients who had preoperative IABP insertion undergoing isolated CABG at a single United Kingdom quaternary centre was conducted between January 2015 and June 2025. Indications for IABP insertion were divided into prophylactic (critical coronary anatomy) and non-prophylactic insertion (haemodynamic instability and persistent angina). Primary outcome was 30-day mortality, and secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, incidence of postoperative complications, specific complications related to IABP insertion and postoperative length of stay. Comparative analysis was performed between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed.Results610 patients underwent isolated CABG with preoperative IABP; 302 (49.5%) received prophylactic IABP and 308 (50.5%) had non-prophylactic insertion. There were 14 (2.3%) 30-day mortality and 20 (3.3%) 90-day mortality, with no significant difference in mortality between the two groups. Mean postoperative length of hospital stay was 11 ± 7 days; this was significantly longer in the non-prophylactic group (12 ± 8 vs 10 ± 7 days, p < 0.01). Postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in 42 patients (6.9%) and dialysis in 5 (0.8%), with no differences between the two groups. There were 25 (4.1%) IABP-related complications; 8 localised haematoma managed conservatively, 4 wound infections treated with intravenous antibiotics, 5 lower limb ischaemia (3 required surgical re-vascularisation), 2 fatal bowel ischaemia, 2 renal and splenic malperfusion, 2 localised femoral artery dissection and 2 retroperitoneal haematoma (1 required emergency laparotomy).ConclusionThis study supports the selective use of prophylactic IABP in patients undergoing high-risk CABG. In this selected cohort, preoperative IABP use was associated with low early mortality, favourable long-term survival and an acceptable complication profile.

articles.title: Corneal Endothelial Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Following Repeated Anterior Chamber Paracentesis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate longitudinal changes in corneal endothelial morphology following serial anterior chamber (AC) paracentesis in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: This is a prospective cohort study with both cross-sectional and longitudinal components. Participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus underwent bilateral AC paracentesis, specular microscopy analysis, and dilated fundus examination at baseline and at four-month intervals over 3 years. Endothelial parameters included cell density (CD), coefficient of variation, hexagonality, and central corneal thickness. Linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for age, sex, laterality, hemoglobin A1c, diabetes duration, diabetic retinopathy severity, and lens status.

RESULTS: One hundred twelve participants were included at baseline [median age 63 years, 50% female, median hemoglobin A1c 7.8% (interquartile range 1.93), median diabetes duration 20 years]. Most had mild-to-moderate nonproliferative DR (60%), and 30% were pseudophakic. At baseline, pseudophakic lens status (mean ± SD CD: 2566.7 ± 190.8 cells/mm2) predicts a lower CD of -161 cells/mm2 (95% confidence interval -243.1 to -83.1) compared with phakic eyes (2721.5 ± 184.1 cells/mm2). Pseudophakia also predicts a higher coefficient of variation of +3.7 (95% confidence interval, 0.2-7.0). These differences persisted longitudinally. Repeated AC paracentesis was not associated with any significant change in any parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the largest and longest prospective evaluation of repeated AC paracentesis in humans with diabetes. Despite up to 10 AC paracenteses per eye over 3 years, no adverse effects on endothelial cell morphology were observed. These findings support the broader adoption of serial aqueous sampling as a precision-medicine tool in ophthalmology and research.

articles.title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Molecular Epidemiology of Enterococcus Species Isolated at the University Hospitals of Sfax, Tunisia.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Enterococci are major causes of both community-acquired and healthcare-associated infections. The rapid global dissemination of multidrug-resistant clones poses a major challenge to clinical management and infection control. The aim for the present study was to investigate the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance patterns, virulence genes, and molecular epidemiology of Enterococcus species isolated from clinical specimens in university hospitals of Sfax, Tunisia. A descriptive, hospital-based, cross-sectional surveillance study was conducted between March 2020 and February 2021. It included all Enterococcus strains isolated in the Microbiology Department of Habib Bourguiba University Hospital. Enterococcus isolates were tested for antimicrobial susceptibility in accordance with European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing guidelines. Polymerase chain reaction assays were performed to detect resistance genes (vanA, vanB, ermA, ermB, ermC, msrA, mefE, vga, vat, vgb), virulence genes (gelatinase [gelE], aggregation substance, enterococcal surface protein [esp], cytolysin, hyaluronidase), and the IS16 marker associated with the clonal complex 17 (CC17) lineage. A total of 231 Enterococcus isolates were recovered, including Enterococcus faecalis (62.3%) and Enterococcus faecium (34.2%). All E. faecalis isolates were susceptible to ampicillin, vancomycin, and linezolid; all E. faecium isolates were resistant to ampicillin, and 7.6% exhibited vanA-mediated glycopeptide resistance. The ermB gene was the predominant macrolide resistance determinant. Among E. faecium, esp (74.7%) was the most prevalent virulence gene, whereas E. faecalis mainly harbored gelE (78.5%). The IS16 element, characteristic of CC17 clones, was detected in 86.1% of E. faecium isolates. The present study highlights the emergence of multidrug-resistant E. faecium strains with molecular features suggestive of CC17 affiliation in hospital settings in Sfax, Tunisia, underscoring the urgent need for stronger infection control and antimicrobial stewardship programs.

articles.title: Bacteria Pathogen Distribution in Late-Onset Neonatal Sepsis: Trends from a South African Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) in neonates is defined as a bloodstream infection occurring after 72 hours of life and is primarily caused by bacterial pathogens, often associated with catheter use and prolonged hospitalization. Despite its clinical and policy relevance, limited data exist on the etiology of neonatal infections in sub-Saharan Africa. This 8-year retrospective study investigated microbial patterns and antibiotic trends of LOS in a South African neonatal unit to inform infection control and antibiotic stewardship strategies. Data from neonates weighing 500 to 2,500 g admitted to the neonatal unit of a public tertiary hospital in Johannesburg (2013-2020) were analyzed for culture-confirmed LOS. Microbial prevalence was stratified by birth weight and year, and temporal shifts were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Among 7,468 neonates, 1,454 LOS episodes occurred (194 per 1,000 live births), with males accounting for 51.1%. Gram-positive bacteria predominated (55.4%), mainly coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS; 37%), followed by Gram-negative bacteria (44.4%), notably extended-spectrum beta lactamase-producing Klebsiella (13.2%) and Acinetobacter baumannii (12.8%). A marked decline in CoNS incidence was observed in 2016 (annual percentage change: -17.6%). Meropenem (35%) and vancomycin (30.5%) were most frequently used, with extreme-low-birth-weight (ELBW) neonates disproportionately affected. Late-onset sepsis remains a persistent challenge, with CoNS as the leading pathogen and increasing multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, particularly in ELBW and very-low-birth-weight infants. The observed decline in CoNS may signal improved infection control, whereas reliance on last-line antibiotics underscores an urgent need for enhanced surveillance, prevention, and antimicrobial stewardship.

articles.title: Milking the niche: Microbial control of neonatal hematopoiesis.
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cell, Howard et al. reveal how the milk glycoprotein osteopontin shapes the neonatal microbiome to regulate hematopoiesis, promoting dendritic cell development and protection from severe respiratory infection. These findings uncover a maternal milk-microbiota pathway linking early-life nutrition to immune development and long-term disease susceptibility.

articles.title: Targeting protein arginine methyltransferases to enhance cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Arginine methylation is a post-translational modification found on many proteins, including RNA-binding proteins, signaling molecules, histones, and heat shock proteins, where it can alter protein-protein and protein-nucleic acid interactions. Arginine methylation regulates many cellular pathways, including RNA metabolism, signal transduction, gene expression, cellular stress responses, DNA repair, and, more recently, innate immune sensing. Here, we discuss recent advances in innate immune sensing and the emerging role of arginine methylation in suppressing tumor immune visibility. We describe current knowledge of protein arginine methyltransferase (PRMT) inhibitors and degraders and their use from preclinical models to clinical trials, alone or in combination with other therapies, to reduce tumor progression and enhance the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes medications and their implications for cancer treatment: A comprehensive review.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a significant public health challenge with serious implications for cancer incidence and treatment. Currently affecting over 400 million individuals worldwide, T2DM is characterized by chronic hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, which contribute to a pro-tumorigenic environment. This review seeks to elucidate the complex relationship between diabetes medications and cancer treatment, emphasizing how various agents, including metformin, sulfonylureas, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, thiazolidinediones (TZDs), and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, interact with critical signaling pathways involved in cancer progression. Evidence suggests that these medications can modulate oncogenic pathways such as AMPK/mTOR, insulin/IGF signaling, and Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), leading to either inhibition or stimulation of tumor growth and survival depending on the drug class and biological context. For instance, metformin activates AMPK, inhibiting mTOR and promoting apoptosis, while TZDs exert anti-inflammatory effects that may reduce obesity-related cancer risks. Conversely, some DPP-4 inhibitors have been associated with pro-tumorigenic effects under certain conditions. Given the intricate interplay among diabetes, obesity, and cancer, understanding the effects of antidiabetic therapies on tumor biology is crucial for refining treatment strategies. This review consolidates current findings on the cellular and molecular impacts of major T2DM drug classes on cancer, highlighting their potential benefits and limitations. In conclusion, the findings presented in this analysis are intended to enhance treatment strategies and shape future research initiatives aimed at effectively addressing the complexities of managing patients who are concurrently affected by diabetes and cancer.

articles.title: Possible sarcopenia defined by the 2025 Asian Working Group for sarcopenia consensus and functional impairment among adults aged 50-64 years: a longitudinal cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 consensus simplified possible sarcopenia assessment and extended it to adults aged 50-64 years, but its association with activities of daily living (ADL)/instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) impairment in this age group remains unclear. We therefore conducted cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses to address this gap.

METHODS: Using China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study data, we included 6,904 adults aged 50-64 years for cross-sectional analyses. After excluding participants with baseline impairment, 5,730 and 5,423 were followed through 2020 for incident ADL and IADL impairment, respectively.
