Transition analyses included 3,569 and 3,200 participants, respectively. Possible sarcopenia was defined as low handgrip strength according to the AWGS 2025 criterion. Multivariable logistic regression and discrete-time complementary log-log models were used.

RESULTS: In cross-sectional analyses, possible sarcopenia was associated with higher odds of prevalent ADL (OR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.53-2.17) and IADL (OR = 1.45, 95% CI = 1.23-1.71) impairment. Over up to 9 years, it was associated with increased hazards of incident ADL (HR = 1.42, 95% CI = 1.27-1.59) and IADL (HR = 1.36, 95% CI = 1.21-1.52) impairment. In transition analyses, progression to possible sarcopenia was associated with higher hazards of subsequent ADL (HR = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.01-1.49) and IADL (HR = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.07-1.61) impairment. Reversion to no possible sarcopenia was not significantly associated with ADL (HR = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.58-1.22) or IADL (HR = 0.77, 95% CI = 0.52-1.15) impairment.

CONCLUSIONS: AWGS 2025-defined possible sarcopenia and progression to possible sarcopenia were associated with ADL/IADL impairment in adults aged 50-64 years, supporting early screening and repeated monitoring in late midlife.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Modified Masquelet technique using free vascularized fibula grafting for reconstruction of large bone defects after bone infection" [Injury 57(3) (2026) 113036].
Large-scale plasma metabolic profiling identifies signatures and biomarkers associated with air pollution and arrhythmias: A prospective cohort study from UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution is an established modifiable risk factor for cardiac arrhythmia, yet the metabolic mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate how air pollutants promote arrhythmias through metabolic pathway perturbations.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis of 449,068 UK Biobank participants without baseline arrhythmia. Exposures to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and NOx were assessed using land use regression models. Plasma metabolomic profiling including 170 metabolites via 1H-NMR was performed at baseline. Elastic net regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and mediation analysis were employed to identify pollutant-associated metabolic signatures, quantify their mediating effects, and characterize pathway enrichment across different kinds of arrhythmias.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 16.31 years, a total of 47,381 arrhythmia cases were identified. All four pollutants were prospectively associated with increased arrhythmia risk (hazard ratios ranged from 1.015 to 1.257 per 10 μg/m3). The derived metabolomic signatures significantly mediated these associations between different air pollutants and arrhythmia (mediation proportions: PM2.5-related, 11.19%; PM10-related, 5.19%; NO2-related, 7.44%; NOx-related, 9.82%). Pathway enrichment analysis consistently identified lipid metabolism, ketone body metabolism, and amino acid metabolism as core affected pathways. Notably, compared to atrial fibrillation and supraventricular tachycardia, the ketone body metabolic pathway appeared to account for a larger proportion of the association with intraventricular block.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that air pollution increases arrhythmia risk through distinct, subtype-specific metabolic perturbations, providing novel insights into the metabolic pathways linking environmental pollutants to different arrhythmia subtypes.

articles.title: Chest pain in the emergency room: value of the new HEAR score identifying patients with low risk of acute coronary syndrome without troponin testing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest pain is a frequent reason for Emergency Department (ED) visits, although only a minority of patients ultimately present an Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). Current diagnostic strategies rely heavily on troponin testing, but a new clinical tool requiring no blood sampling, the HEAR score, has recently been proposed. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the HEAR score for identifying low-risk patients presenting with chest pain, using 45-day Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) as the primary outcome.

METHODS: All patients presenting with chest pain to the ED of Dijon University Hospital in 2019 were retrospectively analyzed in this single-center study. Patients were stratified as "low risk" (HEAR < 2) or "high risk" (HEAR ≥ 2). Outcomes assessed at 45-days included MACE (defined as a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and urgent coronary revascularization) and recurrence of ED consultation for chest pain.

RESULTS: Among 2177 patients presenting with chest pain, 1807 met inclusion criteria. Of these, 653 (36%) were classified as low risk (HEAR < 2). At 45-days, 22 (3%) low-risk patients reconsulted for chest pain compared with 64 (6%) in the high-risk group (p = 0.037). No MACE was identified among low-risk patients within the available follow-up data. The negative predictive value of a HEAR score < 2 was 100% (95% CI: 99.5%-100%), with an upper 95% confidence bound for the event rate of 0.46%.

CONCLUSION: A HEAR score < 2 identifies a substantial proportion of ED chest pain patients at very low risk of short-term adverse cardiovascular events. However, given the limitations of retrospective follow-up and potential under-ascertainment of events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. The HEAR score may contribute to early clinical risk stratification rather than replace troponin-based strategies.

articles.title: Association of early CD4⁺ T-lymphocyte depletion with 28 day mortality in sepsis: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-induced immune dysregulation, characterized by T-cell loss, is associated with poor outcomes. This study investigated the association between early peripheral T-lymphocyte subset profiles and 28 day mortality in patients with sepsis.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 60 critically ill patients with sepsis and 30 healthy controls were included. Patients with sepsis were classified as 28 day survivors (n = 30) or non-survivors (n = 30). Peripheral T-lymphocyte subset percentages (CD3⁺, CD4⁺, and CD8⁺) were measured by flow cytometry within 24 h of ICU admission.

RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with sepsis had lower CD3⁺ (55.23±9.15%vs. 68.12±8.04%) and CD4⁺ T-cell percentages (30.88±10.52%vs. 40.15±7.21%) and a lower CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio (all p < 0.001). Non-survivors had lower CD3⁺ and CD4⁺ T-cell percentages than survivors (both p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression, lower CD4⁺ T-cell percentage (OR = 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.94; p = 0.002) and higher APACHE II score (OR = 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.71; p < 0.001) were independently associated with 28-day mortality. Adding CD4⁺ T-cell percentage to APACHE II increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.86 to 0.91 (p = 0.03).

CONCLUSION: Early reduction in peripheral CD4⁺ T-cell percentage was independently associated with 28 day mortality in this selected cohort. CD4⁺ T-cell assessment may provide incremental prognostic information beyond APACHE II, but external validation in larger prospective cohorts is required.

articles.title: Immune parameters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during SARS-CoV2 delta and omicron waves.
articles.abstract: Understanding immune mechanisms associated with COVID-19 severity remains important for interpreting clinical outcomes. We investigated virological and immunological profiles in 39-patients hospitalized with COVID-19 at InCor Hospital during the Delta and Omicron waves and included 28-non-hospitalized individuals with moderate COVID-19 as a comparator group for cytokine analyses. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by RT-PCR from nasopharyngeal swabs, and viral variants were identified by next-generation sequencing. RNAemia was assessed by RT-PCR and analyzed as a binary variable. Serum cytokines were quantified by cytometric bead array, while humoral responses were evaluated by anti-Spike RBD IgG levels using CLIA and a Wuhan-Hu-1-based pseudovirus neutralization assay. RNAemia was more frequent in ICU-admitted patients than in non-ICU patients, supporting an association with disease severity. Cytokine profiling showed increased IL-6, IL-8, TNF, IL-17 A and IL-10 levels in hospitalized patients compared with moderate COVID-19 individuals, but did not distinguish recovered from deceased patients. Neutralizing antibody titers measured against a Wuhan-Hu-1 spike pseudovirus were significantly higher in recovered individuals than decease patients, underscoring the relevance of antibody functionality. These data emphasize the relevance of viral dissemination and functional humoral immunity as potential biomarkers for COVID-19 progression and outcome, with RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels showing a stronger exploratory association in this cohort.

articles.title: Association of peripheral CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T-cell ratio with SYNTAX score and coronary stenosis severity in patients with coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is characterized by chronic immune-inflammatory activation. The relationship between the peripheral CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratio and coronary stenosis severity remains unclear. We investigated its association with SYNTAX score and potential as a complementary marker.

METHODS: CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts were measured by flow cytometry in 297 patients with CAD and 181 controls. Coronary stenosis was assessed by angiography and SYNTAX score. Multivariable linear regression was used for SYNTAX score, and logistic regression for moderate-to-severe stenosis (SYNTAX > 23). Models were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, HbA1c, hs-CRP, creatinine, and medications. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR was applied. ROC analysis assessed incremental value beyond risk factors.

RESULTS: CD4+ counts and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio were higher, and CD8+ counts lower, in CAD patients, especially in acute coronary syndromes. In unadjusted analyses, SYNTAX score correlated positively with CD4+ count and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio and negatively with CD8+ count (weak to moderate). After adjustment, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio remained independently associated with SYNTAX score (β = 4.88, 95% CI 1.42-8.30, p = 0.006). For SYNTAX > 23, the ratio showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.598, 95% CI 0.526-0.670; sensitivity 0.587, specificity 0.552 at cutoff 1.90). Adding the ratio to conventional risk factors showed no substantial incremental value (ΔAUC = 0.010, DeLong p = 0.43, NRI = 0.082, IDI = 0.006).

CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral T-cell imbalance is associated with greater angiographic coronary complexity in CAD. However, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio has limited discriminatory ability and should be considered a complementary candidate marker, not a standalone diagnostic or predictive tool. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required.

articles.title: Aerosolized prostaglandin E1 improves oxygenation during one-lung ventilation: A dose-finding randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying doses of aerosolized Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) on oxygenation and intrapulmonary shunt fraction (Qs/Qt) during One-Lung Ventilation (OLV) under 60% Fraction of Inspired Oxygen (FiO2). Secondary objectives included evaluating the impact on intraoperative hypoxemia, postoperative Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs).

DESIGN: A prospective, single center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial.

SETTING: The study was conducted at a single academic medical center.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 160 patients aged 65‒84 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III and Body Mass Index (BMI) < 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective esophageal cancer surgery were enrolled. Patients with certain comorbidities, respiratory diseases, or contraindications to PGE1 were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Group L ‒ Received 0.1 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group M ‒ Received 0.2 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group H ‒ Received 0.3 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group C (control) ‒ Received normal saline nebulization. Nebulization was performed for 10-minutes via a modified breathing circuit into the ventilated lung before initiating OLV.

MEASUREMENTS: Arterial blood gas parameters (arterial partial pressure of oxygen, PaO2; arterial oxygen saturation, SaO2; arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide, PaCO2), hemodynamic variables (Mean Arterial Pressure [MAP]; Heart Rate [HR]), respiratory mechanics (Peak airway pressure [Ppeak]; dynamic lung compliance [Cdyn]), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and Qs/Qt were recorded at multiple time points during OLV. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia and hypotension, PPCs within 7-days, and CPIS on postoperative day-2 were also assessed.

MAIN RESULTS: All PGE1 groups showed significantly improved PaO2, SaO2, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and reduced Qs/Qt during the first 30-minutes of OLV compared to the control group. The High-dose group (H) demonstrated the greatest improvement in oxygenation. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [Group L: 0/40 (0%), Group M: 0/40 (0%), Group H: 0/40 (0%), Group C: 3/40 (7.5%)] and hypotension did not differ significantly among groups; however, the hypoxemia finding was exploratory as the study was not powered for this endpoint. No significant differences were observed in PPCs incidence among groups, but group H was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 compared to group C. Hemodynamic changes were transient and clinically manageable.

CONCLUSIONS: Nebulized PGE1 at doses of 0.1-0.3 μg/kg improves oxygenation and reduces Qs/Qt during OLV under 60% oxygen, with the 0.3 μg/kg dose being most effective. It did not significantly reduce the incidence of PPCs within 7-days. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was lower in the PGE1 groups (0/120) compared with the control group (3/40), but this was an exploratory finding as the study was not powered for this endpoint. The higher dose (0.3 μg/kg) was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 (3.3 vs. 4.1), but CPIS is a surrogate marker, and this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. The clinical significance of this small difference is uncertain, as changes of this magnitude are below the typically recognized thresholds for meaningful clinical improvement. Hemodynamic monitoring is recommended when using higher doses of PGE1.

articles.title: Psychotropic medication in children in a tertiary paediatric intensive care unit-A single-centre retrospective study.
articles.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Psychotropic medications are used in children in intensive care for a range of indications, yet their patterns of use are not well described. We aimed to describe the timing, dose, duration, and annual trends in psychotropic medication use in children admitted to a single-centre paediatric intensive care unit (PICU).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed at the Royal Children's Hospital PICU between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2024. Children less than 18 years of age who initiated an antipsychotic or antidepressant medication during their PICU admission were included in the study. We described the clinical characteristics of children, psychotropic characteristics, and annual patterns of use.

RESULTS: There were 504 of 11 450 (4.4%) admissions in 455 children who received psychotropic medications during the study period. Antipsychotics alone were administered in 447 of 504 (88.7%) admissions, antidepressants alone in 40 of 504 (7.9%), and both classes in 17 of 504 (3.4%). Children who received psychotropic medications were older (10 years [interquartile range {IQR}: 5-14] vs 1 year [IQR: 0-6]), had slightly higher admission illness severity (Paediatric Index of Mortality: 1.6 [IQR: 0.5, 4.1] vs 1.1 [IQR: 0.3, 2.4]; p < 0.001), and experienced a greater PICU length of stay (6.7 days [IQR: 2.0, 19.0] vs 2.0 days [IQR: 1.0, 4.6]; p < 0.001). Olanzapine and amitriptyline were the most commonly prescribed medications within each class. In 69% of admissions, the duration was ≤1 week. The annual rate of psychotropic administration varied between 2.8 and 5.5% during the study period, and continuation after hospital discharge was uncommon (6.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: Psychotropic medications were used in 4.4% of admissions to a single-centre PICU, commonly in older children and predominantly antipsychotics for short duration. The annual use remained constant, suggesting established administration practices. These findings highlight the need to investigate the use of psychotropic medications further in critically ill children.

articles.title: Behavioural and environmental strategies implemented by radiographers to care for patients with neurocognitive disorders during medical imaging and therapeutic procedures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As the population ages, radiographers are increasingly likely to care for patients with dementia, Alzheimer's disease and other neurocognitive disorders in medical imaging or radiation therapy departments. Since the cognitive and behavioural presentation of these patients can vary, radiographers must be prepared to adapt their approach. To investigate behavioural and environmental strategies used by radiographers when caring for patients with neurocognitive disorders (NCDs) during medical imaging and radiation therapy procedures.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey comprising 18 questions was conducted among radiographers working across medical imaging and radiotherapy modalities. The questionnaire explored attitudes towards patients with NCDs, behavioural communication strategies, environmental adaptations, and institutional support measures. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended responses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 160 radiographers participated. Most respondents reported positive attitudes toward patients with NCDs, with 94% indicating no fear when interacting with this population. Behavioural communication strategies were frequently used, particularly maintaining eye contact (85%), using simple language (80%), and speaking slowly and clearly (76%). Caregivers were commonly involved to facilitate communication (81%). Despite this, 45% of radiographers reported frustration at not always knowing how to help effectively. Institutional environmental adaptations were limited, with most participants reporting no dementia-specific training (85%) or departmental protocols (78%).

CONCLUSION: Radiographers frequently implement behavioural strategies to support patients with NCDs, but this relies on individual initiative rather than structured organisational support, which remains limited.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Radiographers should use clear, simple communication strategies with NCD patients, involve caregivers during imaging procedures, and develop dementia-specific training and departmental protocols.

articles.title: X-ray image quality before and after radiographer commenting: A quantitative visual grading characteristics analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Radiographer Comment and Alert (RCA) model was established to provide written alerts of abnormal radiographic appearances identified at acquisition, but its quantitative impact on image quality is unknown. This study quantifies differences in radiograph image quality before and after RCA implementation.

METHODS: A total of 234 radiographs encompassing the pelvis, hand, wrist, elbow, knee, ankle, and foot were collected. This comprised all 117 investigations for these anatomical areas with radiographer comments over 12-months at one site, and 117 matched radiographs obtained one year before RCA implementation. Each image pair was displayed simultaneously, but the order and left-right orientation was randomised. Seventeen radiographers independently rated image pairs using a visual grading characteristics (VGC) analysis scale on seven quality criteria (rotation, angulation, centering, collimation, exposure, artifacts, diagnostic utility). Data were analysed using VGC Analyser Software v1.0.2. Non-parametric rank-invariant statistics generated an area under the VGC curve (AUCVGC) to measure the difference in quality between images with and without radiographer comments.

RESULTS: Across the combined dataset, images acquired after implementation of RCA received visual grading ratings for radiological quality that were significantly higher than images acquired prior to implementation (AUCVGC0.52, p = 0.016, CI[0.500862,0.532967]). Statistical significance at 95% confidence was not met for individual upper (AUCVGC0.52, p = 0.084) and lower limb (AUCVGC0.50, p = 0.746) regions, but was achieved for the axial region (AUCVGC0.54, p = 0.012). Quality improvement was driven by improved positioning, particularly rotation (AUCVGC0.57, p = 0.002). Intraclass correlation coefficient scores were good or excellent (ICC3,k ≳ 0.62-0.97) and all reached significance (p-value<0.05), indicating stable consensus and good inter-rater agreement.

CONCLUSION: Quantitative evidence demonstrates implementation of RCA significantly improves the overall quality of projection radiographs submitted for reporting.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Radiographer image interpretation models can be utilised as tools to improve radiographic image quality.

articles.title: Business model, pricing, and transparency in neurosurgery and neurology journals.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract: The business model of scientific journals - gold open access (OA), hybrid, or subscription - creates different financial incentives for publishers, since in the author-pays OA model publication fees (Article Processing Charges, APCs) are collected upon acceptance. This descriptive audit surveys 109 neurosurgery and neurology journals from six major publishing groups (Elsevier, Springer Nature/Wolters Kluwer, Wiley, SAGE, Taylor & Francis, Thieme) and verifies, journal by journal, business model, notoriety indicator (Journal Impact Factor or Scimago SJR), publication fee, and, where publicly available, acceptance rate. Every data point was individually re-verified against official publisher pages and Scimago Journal Rank, correcting a JIF/SJR confusion, several unrecorded transitions to full OA, and one misclassified business model present in the initial collection. After verification, 83 journals (76.1%) are hybrid and 26 (23.9%) are full OA, including 5 diamond (no-APC) journals; no journal is subscription-only. Mean notoriety was similar between hybrid and full-OA journals on both indicators tested separately (JIF: 3.51 vs 3.61; SJR: 0.87 vs 0.89), but full-OA journals excluding the five diamond titles showed higher and more dispersed SJR values (mean 1.24, SD 0.93) than the diamond subset (mean 0.20, SD 0.09). Publication fees were, on average, higher for the OA option of hybrid journals ($4,279, SD $755) than for full-OA journals ($3,415, SD $845). Acceptance rate was the least transparent variable: only 6 of 109 journals (5.5%) publish an identifiable rate, all hybrid; no full-OA or diamond journal discloses this figure. This sample is too small, and too skewed toward hybrid disclosure, to support any inference about whether business model influences acceptance decisions; it instead documents a broad lack of acceptance-rate transparency across neurosurgery and neurology journals and identifies pricing, not acceptance behavior, as the dimension on which a verified between-model difference could be established.

articles.title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

articles.title: Development of a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine targeting surface-exposed proteins of Chlamydia psittaci through immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology.
articles.abstract: Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular zoonotic pathogen that causes psittacosis and severe respiratory illness in humans. Despite its clinical importance, no licensed vaccine is currently available, and antibiotic treatment may not provide long-term protection or prevent recurrent infection. To address this challenge, a computational strategy integrating structural vaccinology and immunoinformatics was used to design a multi-epitope vaccine targeting the major outer membrane porin and the virulence-associated pGP3-D protein of C. psittaci. Cytotoxic T-cell and helper T-cell epitopes were identified and screened to select antigenic candidates. The selected epitopes were joined using linker sequences together with β-defensin-3 and PADRE. The vaccine construct was evaluated using physicochemical analysis, three-dimensional structural modeling, interaction analysis with TLR2, a 500 ns molecular dynamics simulation, MM-GBSA binding free-energy analysis, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. The designed vaccine was predicted to possess favorable antigenicity, a non-allergenic profile, suitable physicochemical properties, and a global population coverage of 92.15%. Computational analyses suggested stable interaction with TLR2 and indicated structural stability of the vaccine-receptor complex during the simulation. Immune simulation predicted increased IgG levels, memory B-cell formation, activation of CD8+ T lymphocytes, and a cytokine profile consistent with Th1-type immune responses. These findings suggest that the proposed construct represents a computationally designed multi-epitope vaccine candidate that requires further evaluation through experimental studies to determine its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy against C. psittaci.

articles.title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings.

METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62).

CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

articles.title: Non-Invasive Prenatal Diagnosis of Haemoglobinopathies: From Concept to Clinical Reality.
articles.abstract: Haemoglobinopathies are the most prevalent monogenic disorders worldwide, contributing significantly to childhood morbidity and mortality. Preventive strategies, including carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis, have successfully reduced disease incidence in regions with established programmes. However, definitive prenatal diagnosis currently relies on invasive procedures, such as chorionic villus sampling and amniocentesis, which carry a small but significant risk of pregnancy loss. Non-invasive prenatal diagnosis (NIPD) offers a potential alternative that enables earlier diagnosis and eliminates procedure-related miscarriage risk. This narrative review explores the genetic basis and global burden of haemoglobinopathies, current screening strategies and the established invasive diagnostic approaches before critically evaluating the emergence of NIPD for sickle cell disease and thalassaemias. We summarise the principal methodological approaches, including relative haplotype dosage and relative mutation dosage, reviewing evidence from published studies and clinical trials. While multiple NIPD strategies demonstrate promising results, challenges remain including variable fetal fraction, technical complexity, cost and accuracy. Additionally, substantial global inequities persist regarding access to screening and diagnostic services, particularly in regions suffering from higher disease burden. Although NIPD could potentially improve the acceptability and uptake of prenatal diagnosis, routine clinical adoption for haemoglobinopathies requires further validation to demonstrate consistently high diagnostic accuracy, alongside standardised methodologies and reduced costs.

articles.title: Protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during Omicron KP.3 wave.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data are limited on the protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against Omicron KP.3 infection.

METHODS: Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff in Tokyo who had received three or more doses of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and provided blood samples in June 2024, we prospectively examined the associations of XBB.1.5 vaccination and previous infection (classified by the timing of the last infection as pre-Omicron XBB, Omicron XBB, or Omicron JN.1 waves) with the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron KP.3 wave (June to September 2024). In a nested case-control analysis, we compared pre-infection live-virus KP.3.3-neutralizing antibody titers between cases and 1: 1 propensity-score matched controls.

RESULTS: XBB.1.5 vaccination was not associated with measurable protection against symptomatic infection (4%, 95% CI, -88 to 51). Previous infection conferred protection that increased with its recency: 26% (95% CI, -26 to 56) for pre-Omicron XBB, 44% (95% CI, 2 to 68) for Omicron XBB, and 89% (95% CI, 52 to 97) for Omicron JN.1 waves. Pre-infection KP.3.3-neutralizing titers tended to be lower in cases than in matched controls (GMT ratio 0.68, 95% CI, 0.35 to 1.33); KP.3.3-neutralizing activity was only modestly elevated by XBB.1.5 vaccination but markedly higher after recent JN.1 infection.

CONCLUSIONS: During the Omicron KP.3 wave, when an updated vaccine was unavailable, XBB.1.5 vaccination administered approximately 7 months earlier conferred no measurable neutralizing activity or protection against symptomatic KP.3 infection. Previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly recent JN.1-wave infection, affords substantial neutralizing titers and protection.

articles.title: Purpose in life and shingles vaccination and infection.
articles.abstract: Purpose in life is a positive psychological resource associated with preventive behavior and better health outcomes in older adulthood. This study examines whether purpose is associated with likelihood of getting vaccinated against shingles and likelihood of having had shingles. Participants in the Health and Retirement Study (N = 14,066; Mage = 68.13, SD = 10.29) reported on their purpose in life. Vaccine uptake and having had shingles was aggregated across eight waves from 2008 to 2022. Every standard deviation of purpose was associated with a 16% higher likelihood of having received the shingles vaccine (OR = 1.16, 95% CI = 1.12-1.20). This association was independent of depressive symptoms and did not vary by sex, race, ethnicity, or education. The association was slightly stronger among relatively older adults, perhaps because the recommended age of vaccination changed during the study period. Purpose was unrelated to having had shingles. Leveraging purpose in life could be a promising target to increase uptake of the shingles vaccine.

articles.title: Polymeric immunoglobulin receptor in liver diseases: a double-edged sword with therapeutic potential at the gut-liver axis.
articles.abstract: The polymeric immunoglobulin receptor (pIgR) mediates the transepithelial transport of polymeric immunoglobulin A (IgA) and plays a central role in gut immune homeostasis. Its involvement in liver diseases has become increasingly evident with advances in our understanding of the gut-liver axis. This review synthesizes current evidence on the molecular structure and regulation of pIgR expression. It examines the functional heterogeneity of pIgR across viral hepatitis, alcohol-related liver disease, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, autoimmune liver diseases, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Current evidence suggests that pIgR can exert protective effects by preserving the intestinal barrier integrity; however, under specific pathological conditions, it may contribute to autoimmune responses and tumor progression. The present review further evaluates the potential of pIgR for clinical translation as a biomarker and therapeutic target, discusses its immunopharmacological potential, and identifies unresolved questions that may guide future investigation.

articles.title: Temporin-GHa11R accelerates MRSA-infected wound healing via antibacterial efficacy and regulation of macrophage polarization.
articles.abstract: The dynamic balance of macrophage polarization is critical for the process of wound repair, whereas bacterial infection can provoke an excessive inflammatory response, consequently delaying wound healing. In this study, we demonstrated that temporin-GHa11R (GHa11R), a temporin-derived peptide, exhibited potent antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA, MIC = 3.1 μM) and strong antibiofilm capacity, as indicated by its low minimum biofilm inhibitory and eradication concentrations (MBIC50 = 1.8 μM and MBEC50 = 5.2 μM), along with a low propensity to induce drug resistance. GHa11R can adsorb onto the membrane, cause depolarization, and penetrate into the cytoplasm, indicating a non-lytic mechanism. In vitro analyses demonstrated that GHa11R significantly inhibited lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced M1 polarization in RAW264.7 macrophages by suppressing the overactivation of the NF-κB/MAPK signaling pathways, thereby exerting anti-inflammatory effects. Concurrently, GHa11R acted synergistically with interleukin-4 (IL-4) to promote macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. Furthermore, GHa11R enhanced the migration of keratinocytes (HaCaT) and endothelial cells (HUVECs), and promoted angiogenesis. In a mouse model of MRSA-infected wounds, topical application of GHa11R significantly reduced the local bacterial burden, alleviated the inflammatory response, and regulated the macrophage polarization from M1 to M2 phenotype. GHa11R treatment also facilitated wound re-epithelialization, granulation tissue formation, orderly collagen deposition, and neovascularization. Our results indicate that GHa11R exerts multiple biological functions, including antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and pro-repair activities, thereby effectively promoting the healing of infected wounds. This study lays a foundation for the application of temporin-derived peptides in the management of chronic infectious wounds.

articles.title: tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 serves as a host-directed prognostic biomarker and therapeutical target for pediatric sepsis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric sepsis and septic shock remain major causes of mortality in Children, yet robust, mechanistically anchored biomarkers for severity stratification are limited. We profiled plasma tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) in children with sepsis and septic shock, and validated candidates by qRT-PCR in an expanded cohort. tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 showed a stepwise decline from controls to sepsis and septic shock. In cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mice, tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 decreased in plasma and major organs.Prophylactic administration of tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 agomir prior to CLP improved survival, attenuated lung/liver/kidney injury, and reduced IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α responses, whereas antagomir silencing worsened outcomes in a non-severe CLP setting. Mechanistically, tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 targeted Notch1 mRNA, suppressed Notch1/NF-κB activation, and restrained an M1-like macrophage program across macrophage models. These findings define a tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001-Notch1/NF-κB axis linking tsRNA dysregulation to inflammatory amplification and organ injury, supporting an association between tiRNA-Pro-AGG-001 and disease severity and suggesting its prophylactic intervention as a promising strategy, with future therapeutic-window studies needed to establish its translational potential for pediatric sepsis.

articles.title: Clinical nursing faculty perceptions about teaching students to provide care for adults with developmental disability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with developmental disabilities (AWDD) experience health inequities that could be improved with nurses better prepared to address their unique needs. Lack of contact of nursing students with AWDD, which is pervasive in nursing education, contributes to the health inequities experienced by this population. This may be due in part to clinical nursing faculty members' perceptions about teaching students to provide care to this population.

PURPOSE: This study explored the perceptions of clinical nursing faculty about teaching students to provide care for AWDD.

DESIGN: This study used a descriptive multi-method design with a nationwide sample of 126 clinical nursing faculty.

METHODS: The survey included Likert-style scales for quantitative data analyzed through descriptive statistics, and open-ended questions for qualitative data analyzed thematically.

RESULTS: Participating clinical nursing faculty reported positive attitudes toward providing care to AWDD but biases emerged. Perceived self-efficacy to teach students about AWDD included four themes: faculty experience with DD, providing DD care, student knowledge/willingness, and time. Barriers and facilitators to assigning students to AWDD included five themes: attitudes, care complexity, clinical site considerations, extent of DD content, and faculty experience with DD.

CONCLUSION: The study findings suggest areas for professional and curricular development to increase learning opportunities for nursing students to provide equitable care to AWDD.

articles.title: Electrospun Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes for photocatalytic degradation of PET plastics with peroxymonosulfate activation: Performance and DFT insight.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics cause significant environmental harm. Traditional treatment methods, such as landfilling and incineration, can cause secondary pollution. Here, an efficient synergistic photocatalytic system is presented, based on Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes prepared by electrospinning, to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and promote the degradation of PET plastics. The results show that the as-prepared Co3O4/CeO2 composite catalyst exhibits the best performance under illumination; the weight loss rate of PET can reach ∼82.7 ± 4.5% in the presence of a 3 mM PMS solution (pH 7). The effects of parameters (e.g., PMS dose and coexisting anions) on PET degradation were systematically investigated. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and free radical quenching experiments confirm that the •OH, 1O2, and SO4•- active species contribute the most to the degradation of PET plastics. Density Functional Theory analysis shows that Co-d-pDOS and Ce-f-pDOS modulations in Co3O4/CeO2 synergistically enhance the PET photocatalytic decomposition efficiency. Finally, we discuss the mechanism by which the catalyst/light/PMS system degrades PET in water.

articles.title: Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction.
articles.abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic division of labor and substrate channeling can alleviate product inhibition and process mixed plastic waste. We also summarize metabolic engineering efforts that have enabled conversion of PET-derived terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) into more than 25 value-added products, including biopolymers, platform chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty compounds. Finally, we discuss remaining technological barriers, economic feasibility, and future frontiers (including computational enzyme design, synthetic consortia, tandem chemo-biological processes, and industrial-scale demonstration) and propose a phased roadmap for industrial translation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive resource for advancing PET bio-upcycling from laboratory innovation toward practical implementation in a circular plastics economy.

articles.title: Safer supply program enrollment motivations and medication preferences among people who use drugs in Vancouver, Canada.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Safer supply programs have been implemented in Canada as part of the response to the ongoing toxic drug crisis. Established in 2021, the Safer Alternatives for Emergency Response (SAFER) program in Vancouver, Canada, offers a range of prescribed pharmaceutical alternatives to the unregulated drug supply, including fentanyl products for witnessed use. The present study sought to characterize SAFER program enrolment motivations and safer supply medication preferences among SAFER participants.

METHODS: Between December 2021 and February 2025, cross-sectional data were collected from a prospective cohort of SAFER program participants via baseline interviewer-administered questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were used to examine self-reported reasons for enrolling in SAFER and safer supply medication preferences.

RESULTS: Among 96 participants, 26 (27.4%) identified as women or gender diverse. The most frequently cited reasons for SAFER program enrolment were: to reduce unregulated drug use or related harms (70.8%); and to improve general health, stability or social wellbeing (53.1%). The most commonly preferred safer supply medications were fentanyl powder (48.3%) and injectable diacetylmorphine (25.8%). Overall, 39 participants (43.8%) were currently prescribed their preferred medication. After fentanyl powder was introduced at SAFER in March 2022, this proportion increased from 19.4% to 56.9%, p < 0.001.

DISCUSSION: The primary reported motivations for program enrolment - reducing unregulated drug use or related harms and improving health and wellbeing - mirror the core stated objectives of SAFER, suggesting program alignment with participant goals. Observed improvements in receipt of preferred medications over time highlight the value of expanding and adapting medication options in alignment with participant needs.

articles.title: Beyond Hemodynamics: Uremic Toxins, Post-Translational Modifications, and Inflammatory-Metabolic Remodeling in Uremic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Uremic cardiomyopathy has traditionally been attributed to pressure overload, volume overload, hypertension, and neurohormonal activation in chronic kidney disease. However, growing experimental and clinical evidence indicates that nonhemodynamic mechanisms also contribute to myocardial remodeling in uremia. These mechanisms include retention of uremic toxins and protein-bound solutes, mediators of mineral metabolism, gut-derived metabolites, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and post-translational protein modifications. In this review, we discuss uremic cardiomyopathy as a systemic inflammatory-metabolic disorder in which kidney failure reshapes myocardial structure and function through interacting biochemical and interorgan pathways. We first define the major classes of uremic toxins, including small water-soluble solutes, middle molecules, protein-bound uremic toxins, and reactive chemical intermediates. We then focus on post-translational modifications, particularly urea-derived cyanate-mediated carbamylation, a well-characterized uremia-associated mechanism that can alter collagen, extracellular matrix turnover, plasma proteins, lipoproteins, and potentially long-lived cardiac proteins. Additional injury pathways, including oxidative modifications, ferroptosis, fibroblast growth factor 23/Klotho imbalance, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation by indoxyl sulfate, gut-derived adrenergic metabolites, endotoxemia, and inflammasome signaling, are discussed as complementary and partially overlapping mechanisms. Because much of the current mechanistic evidence comes from preclinical models, circulating biomarkers, or associative human studies, we distinguish established evidence from plausible mechanistic hypotheses throughout the review. Finally, we discuss therapeutic implications, including enhanced toxin removal, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and future strategies targeting uremic toxins, proteostasis, ferroptosis, inflammasome activation, and toxin-induced post-translational modifications.

articles.title: Transplacental Flecainide and/or Digoxin for Fetal Tachyarrhythmias: Therapeutic Efficacy and Clinical Experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy and safety of transplacental flecainide and/or digoxin for fetal tachyarrhythmias when sotalol is unavailable.

METHOD: We evaluated transplacental flecainide, digoxin, or combination therapy in a retrospective and prospective cohort across two Thai tertiary centers. Outcomes were classified as complete cardioversion, partial response (rate control), or treatment failure.

RESULTS: Of 24 eligible pregnancies, 14 (58.3%) had supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), 8 (33.3%) had atrial flutter (AFL), and 2 (8.3%) had ventricular tachycardia (VT). Overall, clinical responses occurred in 91.7% (22/24) of fetuses. Flecainide monotherapy achieved 100% (9/9) complete cardioversion in SVT, compared with 50% (1/2) for digoxin. SVT combination therapy (n = 3) yielded 1 complete and 1 partial response. Among 7 flecainide-treated AFL cases, 5 (71.4%) achieved rate control and 2 (28.6%) achieved cardioversion; one digoxin-treated case fully converted. Flecainide resolved 1 of 2 VT cases (50%). Response rates were unaffected by hydrops, gestational age, or cardiac defects (p = 0.087-1.000). Maternal adverse events were mild and required no treatment discontinuation.

CONCLUSION: Transplacental flecainide demonstrates high efficacy in SVT and effective rate control with preserved cardiac function in AFL. Its favorable safety profile makes it a practical alternative for first-line therapy where sotalol is unavailable and flecainide monitoring is infeasible.

articles.title: Microbial Culture Profiles Following Fetal Surgery Versus Spontaneous Preterm Prelabor Rupture of Membranes in Multifetal Gestations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess microbial culture profiles and antibiotic resistance patterns in pregnancies complicated by preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) following fetal surgery compared with spontaneous PPROM without fetal surgery.

METHOD: This retrospective cross-sectional study included women with multiple pregnancies and PPROMs < 34 weeks who underwent fetal surgery between September 2018 and January 2024. The study group comprised those who had undergone fetoscopic laser surgery (FLS) or selective fetal reduction (SFR). Endocervical swab and urine cultures were obtained upon PPROM, and placental, uterine and neonatal blood cultures were collected at delivery. A control group included women with multiple pregnancies and PPROMs < 34 weeks without fetal surgery. Cases with other fetal surgeries, terminations of the pregnancy, or delivery prior to 23 weeks were excluded.

RESULTS: Among 126 fetal surgeries, 39 (30.9%) developed PPROM; 32 met inclusion criteria. Compared to controls (n = 31), the fetal surgery group had higher rates of positive cultures (42.7% vs. 13.9% of site-level cultures, p < 0.01), and of ampicillin/macrolide resistance (18.8% vs. 4.3%, p < 0.01). There tended to be more positive placental cultures (43.8% vs. 25.8%, p = 0.47) in the fetal surgery group. No early-onset neonatal sepsis occurred in the fetal surgery group but one in the control group.

CONCLUSION: PPROM following fetal surgery was characterized by a distinct bacterial profile and greater ampicillin/macrolide resistance than spontaneous PPROM. These exploratory findings warrant prospective confirmation before informing changes to clinical practice.

articles.title: Surgical Site Infection After Trauma Laparotomy: A Concise Review.
articles.journal: Journal of trauma nursing : the official journal of the Society of Trauma Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are postoperative complications after trauma laparotomy, associated with increased length of hospital stay, readmission rates, and health care costs. Despite their clinical relevance, SSI incidence after trauma laparotomies varies widely in the literature.

OBJECTIVE: To provide a concise review of risk factors for SSI and perioperative management strategies in trauma laparotomies.

METHODS: A literature review was conducted through PubMed and Google Scholar from database inception through February 2026 using the keywords "trauma laparotomy," "damage-control laparotomy," "surgical site infections in trauma," and "surgical site infection risk factors." Studies were screened for SSI as a reported outcome, and the reference lists of selected articles were reviewed to identify additional relevant sources.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included in the analysis. Surgical site infection incidence ranged from 2.4% to 12.9% for superficial SSIs, 1.5%-4.0% for deep SSIs, and 1.3%-16.2% for organ/space SSIs. Risk factors associated with increased rates of SSI were obesity, blood transfusion volume, hollow viscus injury, colonic injury, greater number of organs injured, and damage-control laparotomy. Adherence to the Surgical Care Improvement Project guidelines for antibiotic prophylaxis was associated with a lower SSI incidence, but the evidence regarding primary skin closure and the mechanism of injury remains conflicting.

CONCLUSION: The heterogeneity of current evidence, driven by single-center retrospective designs, limits definitive conclusions. Randomized controlled trials and standardized multicenter studies are needed to advance understanding and reduce SSI burden in the trauma population. However, current evidence can guide perioperative care, including antibiotic prophylaxis, wound management, and SSI surveillance.

articles.title: Factors associated with persistent methicillin-resistant staphylococcal bacteremia after initiation of anti-MRSA therapy in the NICU: A retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMethicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative staphylococci (MRCoNS) are important causes of bacteremia in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). However, clinical factors associated with persistent bacteremia after initiation of anti-MRSA therapy in NICU patients remain poorly defined.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective observational study of infants with MRSA or MRCoNS bacteremia admitted to a tertiary NICU between 2016 and 2025. Persistent bacteremia was defined as a positive follow-up blood culture on or after day 2 of initial anti-MRSA therapy. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with persistent bacteremia.Results49 episodes of bacteremia were included, of which 16 (33%) met the criteria for persistent bacteremia. Younger postnatal age at bacteremia onset (adjusted odds ratio per 7-day decrease, 1.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-1.85; p = 0.001) and absence of central venous catheter removal or replacement within 2 days of starting initial anti-MRSA therapy (adjusted odds ratio, 11.20; 95% confidence interval, 2.16-86.60; p = 0.003) were independently associated with persistent bacteremia after initiation of anti-MRSA therapy.ConclusionsYounger postnatal age and the absence of central venous catheter removal or replacement were independently associated with persistent bacteremia after initiation of anti-MRSA therapy in NICU patients with MRSA or MRCoNS bacteremia. These findings may facilitate early identification of NICU patients at increased risk of persistent bacteremia and support closer monitoring and timely reassessment of treatment response. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and establish optimal treatment strategies.

articles.title: An Evaluation of Insulin Use in Hospitalized Patients with Corticosteroid-Related Hyperglycemia.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated insulin use in hospitalized patients who developed corticosteroid-related hyperglycemia to assess current insulin management strategies, glycemic outcomes, and opportunities for optimizing institutional practice.

METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at a community-based teaching health system and included hospitalized adults who experienced clinically significant hyperglycemia (blood glucose >250 mg/dL) on at least two occasions during admission between September 2024 and September 2025. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients administered intermediate or long-acting insulin following hyperglycemia. The secondary endpoints evaluated glycemic control, hypoglycemia, timing of insulin orders, and administration of optimized insulin regimens based on pharmacokinetics. This project was deemed exempt by the IRB.

RESULTS: Of 1,361 patient encounters screened, 708 unique patients were included, and 610 had type II diabetes (T2DM). Intermediate or long-acting insulin was administered more frequently in patients with T2DM than those without (71.1% vs 41.8%, p<0.001). A minority of patients had insulin before or with the first dose of steroid (T2DM 35.1% vs without T2DM 13.3%). Glycemic control was achieved most frequently in patients without T2DM (52% vs 35%, p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This study showed that a higher percentage of patients with T2DM received insulin before or with the first dose of steroid when compared to patients without T2DM. However, in both groups, a majority of patients received insulin after the first dose of steroid. Findings suggest that hospitalized adults with or without diabetes who develop corticosteroid-related hyperglycemia will benefit from receiving an intermediate or long-acting insulin concurrently with the ordered steroid.

articles.title: Microcirculatory Hemodynamic Changes on Full Support Microaxial Flow Pump in Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Impaired microcirculation predicts mortality in cardiogenic shock independent of systemic hemodynamics, yet current treatment strategies focus primarily on restoring macrocirculatory markers. We studied whether full-support microaxial flow pump (mAFP) therapy improves sublingual microcirculation in cardiogenic shock. A prospective, single-arm, observational study of serial sublingual microcirculation imaging via incident darkfield handheld videomicroscopy was performed in 18 cardiogenic shock patients undergoing Impella 5.5 (mAFP) placement. Microvascular flow index (MFI), microvascular heterogeneity index (MHI), proportion of perfused vessels (PPV), and perfused vessel density (PVD) were measured. Eighteen patients were enrolled. Microvascular flow index (p = 0.004), MHI (p = 0.055), PPV (p = 0.003), and PVD (p = 0.067) improved immediately on support, including when adjusted for vasoactive-inotropic score. Improvement in MFI, MHI, PPV, or PVD was most pronounced in those with impaired baseline microcirculatory hemodynamics (all p < 0.05), whereas those with preserved baseline values demonstrated no change. Improved agreement between systemic and microcirculatory hemodynamics was observed in association with mAFP support, and none experienced worsening microcirculatory function. These exploratory findings suggest full-support mAFPs may improve impaired microcirculation during cardiogenic shock, although device-specific effects cannot be isolated from overall clinical improvement; validation in larger studies is warranted. Although agreement between systemic and microcirculatory hemodynamic markers improved, no macrohemodynamic marker proved sufficient to ensure adequate microcirculatory perfusion.

articles.title: 2-Deoxy-2-[18F]Fluorosorbitol (18F-FDS) as a Potential PET Tracer for Renal Imaging and GFR Measurement: Comparative Assessment with 68Ga-EDTA and 99mTc-DTPA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is critical for monitoring renal function. This study aims to evaluate its feasibility as a PET radiopharmaceutical for renal imaging and GFR assessment. Its novelty lies in the direct, head-to-head comparison with 68Ga-EDTA and 99mTc-DTPA to comprehensively assess the potential advantages and translational relevance of 18F-FDS for clinical GFR measurement.

METHODS: 18F-FDS was synthesized via a reduction reaction, and its radiochemical purity was evaluated using radio-TLC. In vitro stability was assessed for up to 4 hours. Plasma protein and erythrocyte binding rates of 18F-FDS, 68Ga-EDTA, and 99mTc-DTPA were determined to evaluate their pharmacokinetic suitability for renal imaging. Dynamic and static renal imaging was performed in healthy male Wistar rats. Time-activity curves were generated to calculate Tmax, biological half-life (T1/2), normalized residual activity (NORA), and GFR.

RESULTS: 18F-FDS was synthesized with a radiochemical purity exceeding 98% and demonstrated high in vitro stability over 4 hours. Plasma protein binding and erythrocyte of 18F-FDS was lower than for all radiopharmaceuticals. Dynamic small-animal imaging revealed rapid renal uptake and efficient urinary excretion for all agents. No statistically significant differences were observed in GFR values or kinetic parameters derived from 18F-FDS and 68Ga-EDTA imaging (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The favorable in vitro characteristics and renal kinetic profiles of 18F-FDS support their potential use as PET radiopharmaceuticals for renal imaging and GFR quantification. In particular, the low plasma protein binding and comparable GFR measurements suggest that 18F-FDS may serve as a promising alternative to established tracers for functional renal assessment.

articles.title: AI-Driven Lifestyle Interventions for Reducing Diabetes Risk: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven lifestyle interventions are increasingly used for reducing diabetes risk. However, whether they produce clinical benefit beyond standard Diabetes Prevention Programs (DPPs) and whether effects vary by AI type, population, or delivery setting, remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of AI-driven lifestyle interventions on clinical, behavioral, and engagement outcomes among people with prediabetes or elevated diabetes risk and to assess whether effects differed by AI type, population, or delivery setting.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ClinicalTrials.gov, and citation searches were completed on August 3, 2026, for English-language reports published from 2015. Eligible studies evaluated AI-driven digital lifestyle interventions among people with prediabetes or elevated diabetes risks, or healthy participants in feasibility studies. One reviewer (OIE) screened records and extracted data; a second reviewer (TN) independently verified exclusions and extraction. Study quality was assessed with National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute tools appropriate to each design. Given substantial heterogeneity in designs, estimands, and outcome metrics, findings were synthesized narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guideline rather than pooled statistically.

RESULTS: Of 8032 records, 11 studies were included: 1 randomized, 1 nonrandomized comparative, 4 observational, and 5 uncontrolled pre-post studies. Seven evaluated AI lifestyle coaching systems, 2 predictive AI platforms, and 2 conversational AI chatbots. Ten of 11 studies used commercially developed platforms. Study quality was rated good for 5 studies, fair for 3, and poor for 3. The randomized controlled trial showed noninferiority of an AI-DPP versus human coach-led DPP for the combined 12-month outcome (23/183, 12.6% vs 23/185, 12.4%; risk difference 0.1%, 1-sided 95% CI -5.5%). Program initiation (171/183, 93.4% vs 153/185, 82.7%; risk difference 10.7%, 95% CI 4.2%-17.3%) and completion (117/183, 63.9% vs 93/185, 50.3%; risk difference 13.7%; 95% CI 3.6%-23.7%) were higher with AI, but this did not translate into superior clinical outcomes. The nonrandomized comparison found no advantage of AI-personalized messaging over static messaging in terms of BMI or physical activity. The remaining studies reported uncontrolled changes precluding causal inference. Evidence was insufficient to determine whether effects differed by population or delivery setting.

CONCLUSIONS: One randomized trial supports noninferiority, not superiority, of a specific AI-driven DPP relative to human coaching; the remaining evidence was nonrandomized, predominantly commercially developed, and hypothesis-generating. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review to stratify evidence on AI-driven diabetes prevention by AI mechanism-coaching, predictive, and conversational-and by outcome domain, extending prior scoping work that mapped apps without appraising study quality or comparative effectiveness. This structured mapping shows where evidence is the strongest (engagement and weight) and the weakest (glycemic causality and generalizability), giving health systems a concrete basis for deciding where AI-DPP tools may supplement, rather than replace, standard DPP delivery, pending independent, adequately powered randomized trials.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Functional Status and Estimating Health Care Costs in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and progressive disease associated with substantial clinical heterogeneity and high health care costs. While machine learning (ML) has been increasingly applied to predict clinical outcomes, approaches that integrate clinical prediction with downstream economic modeling remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study proposes and evaluates an ML-based framework that combines prediction of future functional status with estimation of associated health care costs in patients with PAH.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data from 181 patients with PAH were analyzed. A total of 6 supervised ML algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator [LASSO] regression, ridge regression, k-nearest neighbors, decision trees, random forest, and gradient boosting) were trained to predict the relative change in World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) from baseline to 12-month follow-up using baseline clinical variables. Predicted change rates were subsequently converted to predicted WHO-FC values at the 12-month follow-up for downstream health care cost estimation. Missing values in predictor variables were imputed using median substitution. Median imputation was performed before the dataset was split into training and test sets. Model performance was evaluated using Pearson correlation coefficient (r), and error metrics (RMSE, MAE, and MedAE), based on cross-validation and independent test set validation. Predicted WHO-FC values were subsequently linked to externally validated, stratified real-world health care cost estimates to approximate future economic burden.

RESULTS: Among the evaluated models, k-nearest neighbors showed the highest predictive performance (r=0.40; R2=0.16), followed by LASSO regression (r=0.30; R2=0.09). Prediction errors were comparable across models. Estimated mean health care costs ranged from US $12,481 to $12,614 per patient per month. Despite a significant improvement in WHO-FC over 12 months, estimated health care costs remained largely unchanged, reflecting persistent economic burden across functional class strata.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of an ML-based framework that integrates prediction of functional status with health care cost estimation in PAH. While predictive performance was moderate, the approach illustrates how ML models can be extended beyond clinical end points toward system-level applications such as cost forecasting and resource planning. Further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is required before clinical or health system implementation.

articles.title: Pharmacist-Led Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Prediabetes: Protocol for a Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediabetes represents a critical intervention window to reduce progression to type 2 diabetes. The current standard of care for treatment of prediabetes is weight loss and lifestyle modification, which are both highly effective, although limited by real-world adherence. It is well recognized that continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) improves glycemic and behavioral outcomes in people with diabetes, although outcomes among people with prediabetes are not well described.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of pharmacist-led CGM on glycemic control and health-related behaviors in adults with prediabetes.

METHODS: This study includes a prospective pharmacist-led CGM cohort and a matched retrospective usual-care cohort. Adults aged 18 to 70 years with prediabetes (hemoglobin A1c [HbA1c] 5.7%-6.4%) will be eligible for the prospective cohort if they have a compatible smartphone and no CGM use in the prior 6 months. Participants will receive CGM (Stelo glucose biosensor; Dexcom) and diabetes self-management education and support over 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change in HbA1c at 12 weeks, compared between groups. Secondary outcomes include CGM-derived metrics, changes in Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities scores and 36-Item Short Form Health Survey scores, and CGM-related adverse effects.

RESULTS: This study was funded in 2026. Recruitment is ongoing, and no participants had been enrolled at the time of writing. The planned sample size is 40 participants: 20 prospective CGM participants and 20 retrospective controls. Outcome data are not yet available. The study is expected to be completed in July 2027, and the results are anticipated to be disseminated in December 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: This study seeks to evaluate the glycemic impact, behavior change, and safety of pharmacist-led CGM for prediabetes in primary care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07529366; https://tinyurl.com/33bv7u8c.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): PRR1-10.2196/105275.

articles.title: Improving Musculoskeletal Care Quality With a Web-Based Clinical Decision Support System in UK Primary Care: Mixed Methods Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions account for one in seven general practice consultations in the United Kingdom. Despite national guidelines, suboptimal care remains common. Digital clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) offer a promising route to improve care quality but have not been robustly evaluated in MSK primary care.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, clinical effectiveness and cost-effectiveness, carbon reduction, safety, and implementation of a CDSS (CrossCover) for MSK consultations in UK general practice.

METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods, cluster-randomized controlled trial in 19 general practices between February and July 2024. Practices were randomized 1:1, stratified by list size. Intervention practices received training and access to the web-based CDSS for 3 months. We analyzed anonymized electronic health records to identify all adult MSK consultations. The primary outcome was the proportion of patient records containing one or more of 12 predefined non-evidence-based management options, assessed by blinded clinical review of 120 patient records (60 per arm). Reviewers assessed the complete 3-month record in both arms; in the intervention arm, suboptimal management was counted only where it occurred at a consultation in which the CDSS was used. Secondary outcomes included intention-to-treat treatment comparisons of self-management advice, prescriptions, referrals, and imaging. Clinician engagement, safety, environmental and economic modeling, and clinician experiences from semistructured interviews were evaluated. Outcome assessors were blinded; clinicians were not.

RESULTS: Among 10,182 eligible patients with MSK conditions (4268 intervention; 5914 control), the CDSS was used in 365 (8.6%) patient cases. Intention-to-treat analysis identified that the intervention increased self-management alone. Per-protocol analysis demonstrated that when used, suboptimal care arose in 3% (2/60) of CDSS-guided consultations vs 25% (15/60) of control consultations (adjusted odds ratio 12.30, 95% CI 2.52-59.9; P=.002). It also increased self-management advice and community referrals, and it reduced prescribing and fit-note use. Safety concerns were logged in 6.6% (24/365) of uses with no high-risk issues identified. Environmental modeling estimated an 18% reduction in carbon emissions and 10% annual cost savings if the intervention were scaled. Interviews (n=18) highlighted positive perceptions of the CDSS's content and safety netting but noted challenges in integration.

CONCLUSIONS: When used, the CrossCover CDSS significantly reduced suboptimal primary care MSK management. However, while safety and clinician feedback were favorable, overall engagement was limited, underscoring the need for improved digital integration, workflow alignment, and implementation support.

articles.title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses.

METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests.

RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata.

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03694652; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03694652.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): RR2-10.2196/30295.

articles.title: Enhancing Mental Wellness in Kenyan Adolescents and Young People: Protocol for a Platform Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are a leading cause of disability among adolescents and young people in Kenya, yet access to appropriate and timely support remains severely limited due to shortages of trained professionals, stigma, financial barriers, and geographical inequities. Digital mental health interventions, particularly those leveraging AI, present a promising opportunity to expand access to culturally relevant, low-stigma mental wellness support in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings. However, evidence on the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of AI-powered mental health tools for young people in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to co-design, develop, and evaluate "Də'skəs," a social media-based digital platform featuring an AI-powered chatbot, to support mental wellness among adolescents and young people in Kenya. The primary objectives are to assess the feasibility of implementation, usability and user experience, acceptability, and the platform's preliminary applicability across diverse urban, peri-urban, and rural contexts.
