METHODS: The study uses a human-centered design (HCD) methodology, conducted in 3 phases: formative research and co-design, platform development and iterative refinement, and implementation with monitoring and evaluation. Adolescents and young people aged 18 to 24 years will be purposively recruited from Kibra (urban), Kikuyu Town (peri-urban), and Nachu (rural). Formative data will be collected through focus group discussions to inform platform design, content, and functionality. During implementation, participants will use the platform for 2 months. Quantitative data will include baseline behavioral health screening using the Global Appraisal of Individual Needs-Short Screener (GAIN-SS) and platform use analytics. Qualitative data will be collected through interviews and feedback sessions to assess usability, user experience, acceptability, and perceived value. Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic qualitative analysis.

RESULTS: Field activities for the project started in January 2026. Formative data collection was planned to be completed across the 3 Kenyan study sites by the end of February 2026. Usability and user experience testing was planned to run from March 2026 to June 2026. Findings from the formative work, baseline data, and usability and user experience testing will be reported in subsequent original research publications. The study was funded by the Royal Academy of Engineering, UK in 03/2025 and approved by the Strathmore University Institutional Scientific Ethics Review Committee (SU-ISERC; SU-ISERC 2980/25) approved from November 4, 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol describes an adolescent-centered, ethically grounded approach to developing and evaluating an AI-enabled digital mental health intervention in an LMIC context. The findings are expected to contribute to the evidence base on the responsible design and implementation of AI-powered mental health tools for adolescents and young people and to inform future scale-up of accessible, culturally relevant digital mental wellness interventions in Kenya and similar settings.

articles.title: Acceptability and Feasibility of an Islamic Faith-Based Smoking Cessation Intervention Delivered via WhatsApp for Muslim Smokers in Saudi Arabia: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smoking is common in Saudi Arabia, particularly among men. Religion plays a protective role against smoking and serves as a motivator for quitting. Faith-based interventions have shown positive effects in supporting smoking cessation among Muslims who smoke; however, few studies have tested their acceptability when delivered via mobile phone messaging.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this pilot randomized controlled trial was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability, as well as the preliminary effectiveness of an Islamic-based smoking cessation intervention delivered via WhatsApp messaging in Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: This study was a 2-arm randomized controlled trial involving adult Muslim smokers who used cigarettes, waterpipe, or both. Participants were recruited from the Kafa organization antismoking clinic in Saudi Arabia. Participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the intervention or control group. The intervention messages were codeveloped with religious leaders and informed by formative research with Muslim current and former smokers. The intervention group received both religious and smoking-related health messages, whereas the control group received smoking-related health messages only. The messages were manually delivered daily by trained research assistants. The intervention lasted for 21 days, during which participants received 2 messages per day, one in the morning and one in the evening. The primary outcomes were the feasibility and acceptability of the intervention.

RESULTS: A total of 34 participants were recruited, resulting in a recruitment rate of 68% (34/50). The overall retention rate was 64.7% (22/34). Both groups received 44 WhatsApp messages over 21 days. Message engagement was high, with 88.2% (15/17) of participants in the intervention group and 82.4% (14/17) in the control group, reporting that they read the daily messages. The intervention was acceptable and was perceived as helpful in supporting smoking cessation. Complete abstinence from both cigarettes and waterpipe was slightly higher in the intervention group (4/17, 23.5%) than in the control group (3/17, 17.6%). Cigarette abstinence was also modestly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (5/16, 31.3% vs 3/16, 18.8%). Among 8 waterpipe users at baseline, 2 reported waterpipe abstinence at follow-up, both in the intervention group. No statistical comparisons of smoking cessation outcomes between the groups were conducted because the study focused on feasibility and included a small sample size. These findings were descriptive and should be considered exploratory rather than evidence of intervention effectiveness.

CONCLUSIONS: This Islamic faith-based intervention, delivered via WhatsApp messaging, was acceptable and may be feasible for a full-scale trial, provided that recruitment, participant retention, and follow-up data collection are improved. The pilot study provides important lessons for intervention design and implementation of a future adequately powered trial.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and severity classification in Mixed Connective Tissue Disease: a nationwide retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, real-world treatment patterns, and factors associated with severity classification in Japanese patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), aiming to clarify its heterogeneous clinical spectrum.

METHODS: This nationwide retrospective multicenter study analyzed clinical data from 249 patients who strictly fulfilled the 2019 Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare diagnostic criteria for MCTD, derived from an initial real-world registry of 311 clinically diagnosed patients. Clinical features, autoantibodies, and therapeutic regimens were summarized and compared between patients with severe versus non-severe disease.

RESULTS: The cohort was 93.1% female (median onset age 40.6 years). Common findings, specifically Raynaud's phenomenon and/or swelling of the fingers or dorsum of the hands, were present in 100%. Phenotypically, an overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-like and systemic sclerosis (SSc)-like features was most frequent (56.0%), while 32.0% had manifestations across all three phenotypic domains (SLE-, SSc-, and IIM-like). Major organ involvement occurred in 32.9% of patients, including pulmonary arterial hypertension in 12.8%. Approximately 28.7% of evaluable patients were classified as severe. Off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status was not associated with severity classification (p = 0.492) or with broad phenotypic categories. Glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive agents were used in 66.7% and 56.5% of the patients, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Mixed connective tissue disease exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity. Severity classification was not associated with off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status or broad phenotypic categories. These findings support rigorous cardiopulmonary screening and management tailored to the dominant clinical phenotype.

articles.title: Mortality From 1918-1919 Spanish Flu Among the American Expeditionary Forces Analyzed Through People-Powered Research.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Card Register of Burials of Deceased American Soldiers, 1917-1922 holds the burial cards of American servicemen and women who died at sea or overseas during or after World War I (WWI). We aimed to use this online register to study mortality statistics in the American Expeditionary Forces (AEF) during the 3 waves of Spanish flu in 1918 and 1919. However, the register, which includes 104 file units, lacks database query functionality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Over 6,000 volunteers attached to the Zooniverse platform for people-powered research submitted 4 million transcription tasks from individual burial cards in the online register. This information was used to create the American WWI Burial Cards Search Tool, which is a free online searchable database that also allows, among others, for study of mortality statistics.

RESULTS: The first wave of Spanish flu resulted in a relevant increase in mortality in the AEF. During the second wave, mortality increased significantly, peaking on October 9, 1918, with 474 deaths. Moreover, data show that the weekly mortality rate started to increase already in early August, in contrast to a previous report stating that the second wave of Spanish flu ran its course in the AEF roughly from September 15 onwards. In all, at least 14,494 servicepersons in the AEF died from influenza and/or pneumonia during the deadly second and third waves of Spanish flu. In contrast, mortality from COVID-19 in the U.S. military was low, with 96 deaths as of December 8, 2022.

CONCLUSIONS: People-powered research provided a unique possibility to study single-day mortality figures from influenza and/or pneumonia in the AEF during the different waves of Spanish flu. In all, at least 14,494 servicepersons in the AEF died from influenza and/or pneumonia during the second and third waves of Spanish flu, while we show that the weekly mortality rate during the second wave increased already in early August 1918. In contrast, mortality from COVID-19 in the U.S. military was low. Thus, pandemics of respiratory infections have different impacts on mortality in army personnel, depending on specific pathogenic characteristics of the causative agent.

articles.title: Diagnostic uncertainty in a patient with severe hidradenitis suppurativa revealing Buschke-Löwenstein tumor.
articles.abstract: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (BLT), also known as giant condyloma acuminatum, is a rare human papillomavirus-associated lesion characterized by locally aggressive growth with the potential for malignant transformation. Diagnosis may be particularly challenging when BLT arises in the setting of severe chronic inflammatory disease. We present a 44-year-old man with severe hidradenitis suppurativa, well-controlled HIV infection, recurrent gluteal abscesses, and chronic sacral osteomyelitis who presented with worsening perineal pain and chronic drainage. Although imaging demonstrated extensive infiltrative soft-tissue disease suspicious for neoplasm with superimposed infection, the patient's severe chronic inflammatory disease, recurrent abscesses, and chronic osteomyelitis created substantial diagnostic uncertainty. After the patient did not improve with broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, open biopsy of a large fungating perianal lesion established the diagnosis of BLT. This case highlights the diagnostic uncertainty that may arise when BLT coexists with severe hidradenitis suppurativa, emphasizing the importance of early tissue biopsy when clinical features are atypical or progressive.

articles.title: Partner Dyads to Promote Physical Activity among Women at Risk for CVD: Daily Perceptions of Communication and Associations with Physical Activity Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine day-to-day experiences of social support and peer partner influence during a tailored physical activity (PA) intervention.

METHODS: The parent intervention was designed for women in midlife (ages 40-65) with elevated risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), for whom lack of social support is a barrier to cardioprotective levels of PA. Women in midlife with ≥1 CVD risk factor (e.g., hypertension; N=62, MAge=53, MBMI=32.6 kg/m2, 44% from underrepresented groups) enrolled in an 8-week PA intervention combining PA coaching with formation of partner dyads for between-session support (n=31).Women who enrolled were paired in partner dyads and did not have a relationship prior to enrolling. They wore a digital PA monitor and completed daily end-of-day surveys throughout the program (94% compliance). Multilevel models tested for within-person associations between daily satisfaction with partner support (individual and dyad levels), including preliminary tests of partner influence.

RESULTS: Partners communicated on 58% of days, primarily via texting (used on 92% of communication days). Perceived support varied within-person and within-dyad (ICCs=0.37-0.48); women reported greater PA motivation and took more steps on days when they experienced greater partner support (Ps<0.040, srs=0.19-0.32). Partners' daily PA motivation and steps showed weak correlations (rs=0.008-0.24); associations between partners' perceptions and each others' PA outcomes were slightly stronger (srs=0.20-0.28) and reflected different experiences of support.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with elevated risk for CVD, support in health-focused partnerships has potential to influence daily PA motivation and behavior. Additional investigation will improve partner-based PA intervention toward reduction in CVD risk for this group.

articles.title: Nurse-led Transitional Care and Postdischarge Outcomes in Stroke Survivors: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience nursing : journal of the American Association of Neuroscience Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurse-led transitional care may improve continuity of care after stroke, but its effects on postdischarge outcomes remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its effects on readmission, functional outcomes, quality of life, and caregiver burden in stroke survivors.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched from January 2015 to November 19, 2025. English-language randomized controlled trials of nurse-led transitional care in adult stroke survivors were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was appraised using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool, and evidence certainty was rated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Sixteen trials involving 7487 participants were included. Nurse-led transitional care was associated with a lower risk of readmission than usual care (RR, 0.43; 95% CI: 0.26-0.73; I²=0%); however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because the readmission analysis included only 4 trials involving 455 participants. It was also associated with improved functional outcomes (SMD, 0.58; 95% CI: 0.20-0.96; I²=93%) and quality of life (SMD, 1.09; 95% CI: 0.40-1.78; I²=90%). Caregiver burden did not differ significantly between groups (MD, -0.68; 95% CI: -2.22 to 0.86; I²=81%). Evidence certainty was low for readmission, functional outcomes, and quality of life and very low for caregiver burden.

CONCLUSION: Nurse-led transitional care may be associated with a lower risk of readmission and improved functional outcomes and quality of life after stroke. However, risk of bias, imprecision, and substantial heterogeneity limit confidence in these findings. Rigorous trials using standardized outcomes are needed. Neuroscience nurses may promote continuity through structured discharge preparation, early follow-up, and home-based support.

articles.title: The pathogenicity factor of DNA virus interacts with Arabidopsis deubiquitinases UBP12/13 to promote viral infection.
articles.abstract: Plant DNA viruses, such as Cauliflower mosaic virus (CaMV) and Cabbage leaf curl virus (CaLCuV), are devastating pathogens that cause substantial yield losses in crops worldwide. These viruses assemble their genomes into minichromosomes with host histones. Histone post-translational modifications (PTMs) are important for viral replication and host resistance. In this study, we demonstrate that the CaMV pathogenicity factor P6 interacts with Arabidopsis deubiquitinases UBP12 and UBP13, which are typically negative regulators of plant immunity. Using affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS), we identified UBP12/13 as prominent P6 interactors and confirmed their nuclear association. CaMV infection and P6 overexpression increased UBP12 abundance, suggesting the latter promotes viral infection. By contrast, ubp12/13 mutants exhibited enhanced resistance, characterized by reduced accumulation of viral DNA and transcripts. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-qPCR showed that the monoubiquitinated H2A (H2Aub) and H3K27me3 modifications on the CaMV 35S promoter, but not the 19S promoter, were significantly elevated in ubp12/13 mutants compared with wild-type plants. Furthermore, UBP12/13 are also targeted by AC2, a transcriptional activator from CaLCuV, indicating a conserved strategy among plant DNA viruses. Our findings support a working model in which viral pathogenicity factors hijack UBP12/13, which in turn may alter H2Aub homeostasis on viral minichromosomes to relieve epigenetic silencing and promote infection. Together, these findings point to a previously unrecognized route by which plant DNA viruses may influence host chromatin-associated pathways and identify UBP12/13 as potential targets for engineering virus-resistant crops.

articles.title: Development and Validation of End-Of-Life Indicators for Dialysis Patients: A National Consensus Study in Taiwan.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: BackgroundIdentifying end-of-life (EOL) dialysis patients who may benefit from palliative care remains challenging in Asian healthcare settings where relational autonomy predominates over individual decision-making. We conducted a national consensus study in Taiwan during 2015-2016 to develop validated EOL indicators for dialysis patients, with findings subsequently validated through a decade of clinical experience including the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsWe conducted a three-phase study: (1) systematic literature review; (2) two-round expert focus groups using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method with 15 multidisciplinary experts; and (3) national survey of nephrologists from 624 dialysis facilities. Nine indicators were evaluated using 9-point Likert scales. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses identified latent constructs.ResultsOf 624 facilities, 337 responded (54.0%), yielding 254 nephrologists with complete responses (22.6% of registered specialists). Two indicators achieved high consensus (≥90%) for both hospice/dying care and advance care planning: prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV) with dialysis in unconscious state, and PMV with multi-organ failure. Factor analysis identified three EOL patient subgroups: ventilator-dependent, critically ill, and functionally dependent, with acceptable CFA model fit (χ2 = 27.6, df = 19, P = 0.091; RMSEA = 0.042; CFI = 0.99). ACP ratings yielded a two-factor structure with adequate fit (χ2 = 35.5, df = 20, P = 0.018; RMSEA = 0.055).ConclusionsDialysis patients with PMV combined with unconsciousness or multi-organ failure represent the highest-consensus EOL indicators in Taiwan. These validated findings offer actionable guidance for hospice and end-of-life care referral within healthcare systems characterized by relational autonomy and collective family-patient-clinician deliberation.

articles.title: Clinical features and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana: Insights from a retrospective study (2015-2021).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a re-emerging public health threat in French Guiana with a broad clinical spectrum. Neurological involvement (neuroleptospirosis) lacks a consensus definition and may be underrecognized. This study aimed to characterize its epidemiology, clinical features, outcomes, and associated factors.

METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted across healthcare facilities in French Guiana from 2015 to 2021. Consecutive hospital-managed patients with laboratory-confirmed or probable leptospirosis were included. Neuroleptospirosis was defined by neurological symptoms combined with objective cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and/or neuroimaging abnormalities. Patients with and without neurological involvement were compared.

RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 18 (12%) met the criteria for neuroleptospirosis, corresponding to a mean annual incidence of 0.88 cases/100,000 inhabitants (95% CI 0.52-1.39). Presentations were meningeal (78% [14/18]), encephalitic (17% [3/18]) or meningoencephalitic (6% [1/18]). Lumbar puncture was performed in 28/146 (19%) patients; pleocytosis was observed in 18/28 (64%). The median CSF leukocyte count was 42 cells/mm3 (IQR, 13-240 cells/mm3), with lymphocytic predominance in 8/13 differential counts (62%). CSF protein was mildly elevated (median, 0.51 g/L; IQR, 0.32-0.88), without hypoglycorrhachia. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed abnormalities in 2/8 patients with neuroleptospirosis: one cerebral infarction and one case of pachymeningitis. Age under 30 years (OR, 5.56; 95% CI 1.72-18), absence of leukocytosis during hospitalization (OR, 3.29; 95% CI 1.04-10.39), and absence of thrombocytopenia (OR, 4.46; 95% CI 1.39-14.32) were associated with neuroleptospirosis. Under our diagnostic criteria, neuroleptospirosis cases were associated with favorable outcomes, with lower odds of sepsis (OR, 0.28; 95% CI 0.10-0.79), no intensive care unit admissions or deaths.

CONCLUSIONS: This study clarifies the clinical spectrum and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana, highlighting the importance of clinical awareness in tropical endemic settings. Prospective studies incorporating systematic CSF analysis and microbiological testing are needed to improve understanding of its pathophysiology and standardize diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: Zika virus serologic responses during pregnancy in a dengue-endemic setting: A prospective cohort study in Thailand.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during pregnancy has been associated with adverse birth outcomes, including severe neurological abnormalities. Confirmation of infection remains challenging due to the disease's predominantly asymptomatic or mild nature. While real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) is the gold standard, its use in clinical settings and surveillance is limited. Serological point-of-care tests offer alternatives but pose interpretation challenges in Flavivirus-endemic regions.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a prospective cohort of 199 pregnant women attending the antenatal clinic at Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand, in 2021-2022 to describe the incidence of ZIKV serologic responses detected by a rapid test and associated pregnancy outcomes. Participants were monitored using the DPP ZCD IgM/IgG (Zika/Chikungunya/Dengue IgM/IgG) System rapid immunochromatography test (Chembio), with RT-qPCR and plaque reduction neutralization testing performed for further assessment. A ZIKV serologic response was defined as a reactive ZIKV immunoglobulin M (IgM) result at enrollment or seroconversion from non-reactive to reactive ZIKV IgM or IgG between study visits. The DPP ZCD rapid test revealed incident ZIKV-reactive serologic responses at 15.4 per 100 person-years, with all affected participants being asymptomatic. All RT-qPCR results were negative, and participants with ZIKV IgG seroconversion had neutralizing antibodies against ZIKV and all 4 Dengue virus (DENV) serotypes. A prior history of DENV infection was associated with increased odds of ZIKV-reactive serologic response (OR 3.53, P value 0.046).

CONCLUSION: This prospective study identified serologic responses detected by a ZIKV-reactive rapid test among pregnant women in Thailand. In a highly dengue-immune setting, these responses could reflect true ZIKV exposure, DENV reinfection, flavivirus immune boosting, or serologic cross-reactivity, and therefore cannot be attributed specifically to ZIKV. Rapid serologic testing may support screening and surveillance but cannot establish ZIKV infection or ZIKV-specific exposure without careful interpretation and additional testing.

articles.title: Association between Glycoprotein Acetylation-Indicated Inflammation and Small HDL Particle Number in Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) is a nuclear magnetic resonance-derived biomarker of systemic inflammation. GlycA shows statistical interaction with small HDL particle number (s-HDL-P) in relation to coronary artery disease (CAD). This study examines the confounding effects of GlycA-related glycoproteins, hypertriglyceridemia, and s-HDL-P on CAD risk.

METHODS: Plasma samples from 752 participants in the CATHGEN biorepository were size-fractionated by asymmetric flow field-flow fractionation and analyzed by targeted proteomics and lipidomics. Fraction concentrations were converted to HDL particle number using a volumetric approach based on apolipoprotein A-I (APOA1) concentration, HDL size, and lipoprotein lipid composition. Correlations between GlycA, glycoproteins, total triglyceride (TG), HDL composition and HDL particle number, and their associations with CAD were assessed using multivariate least-squares fit and nominal logistic regression analysis, respectively.

RESULTS: Acute-phase inflammation-related glycoproteins (GlycA-proteins) correlated strongly with GlycA. However, the size-distribution profiles of GlycA-proteins were consistent with circulation as free dimers/trimers, and their lack of overlap with APOA1 profiles suggested no detectable HDL binding. In contrast, apolipoproteins and lipid transfer proteins showed size-profile shifts relative to APOA1 consistent with HDL binding. s-HDL-P showed an inverse association with GlycA, most significantly at low TG levels. In CAD models, significant GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction emerged only when TG was included as a covariate. CAD correlated with lipoprotein lipids, apolipoproteins, and lipid transfer proteins that influence lipoprotein remodeling.

CONCLUSIONS: GlycA-proteins circulate freely without direct HDL binding. The empirical GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction is consistent with indirect coupling between systemic inflammation and altered lipoprotein remodeling associated with CAD risk.

articles.title: AI-Enabled Telerehabilitation for Chronic Nonspecific Neck Pain: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise therapy is effective in managing chronic nonspecific neck pain (CNP). Nevertheless, the high burden of CNP continues to place pressure on existing rehabilitation services, especially in remote or resource-constrained settings where continuous and standardized physical therapy may be difficult to access. By combining home-based exercise with remote supervision and movement feedback, AI-enabled telerehabilitation may broaden access to rehabilitation and support the continued management of CNP.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether an AI-enabled telerehabilitation program was noninferior to standard outpatient rehabilitation for improving neck-related disability in individuals with CNP and compared the effects of the 2 interventions on pain, health-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion.

METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, parallel-group randomized noninferiority trial was conducted at Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Beijing Jishuitan Hospital. Patients with CNP of at least 3 months' duration were randomized 1:1 to a telerehabilitation group (TG) or outpatient rehabilitation group (OG) using concealed, web-based, variable blocks stratified by center and baseline Neck Disability Index (NDI) severity. Both groups completed identical 24-week strengthening and stretching programs (3 sessions per wk; ≈30 min per session) and were assessed at weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, and 24. TG trained at home using sensor-based movement recognition and threshold rules; OG received face-to-face outpatient rehabilitation. Week-24 NDI was the primary outcome; Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), EQ-5D, and cervical range of motion were secondary. Noninferiority required the upper 95% CI bound of the TG-OG NDI difference to be <10 percentage points (5/50). Analyses were intention-to-treat; assessors and statisticians were blinded.

RESULTS: Of 312 individuals screened, 116 were randomized (58 per group). At week 24, 55 TG and 53 OG participants completed assessments; all 116 participants were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis using observed or imputed data. The between-group differences in NDI (TG - OG) were -2.8 (95% CI -6.3 to 0.7; P=.11) at week 12 and -2.5 (95% CI -6.2 to 1.2; P=.15) at week 24. At week 24, the upper 95% CI bound was below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 10 percentage points on the 0 to 100 NDI scale, equivalent to 5 points on the original 0 to 50 scale, demonstrating noninferiority of TG. Both groups showed clinically meaningful reductions in NDI, with comparable improvements in NPRS, EQ-5D, and cervical range of motion. No intervention-related harms occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: Over 24 weeks, AI-enabled telerehabilitation was noninferior to exercise-matched outpatient rehabilitation for neck-related disability, with broadly comparable improvements in pain, health-related quality of life, and cervical range of motion. AI-enabled telerehabilitation may be a practical alternative for patients with CNP who are unable to attend outpatient rehabilitation.

articles.title: "I Don't Think It Is Fair…There Should be a Solution to Every Problem": Experiences of Individuals with Sudden Arrhythmia Death Syndromes Who Attempt to Obtain Life Insurance.
articles.abstract: Sudden Arrhythmia Death Syndromes are a group of heritable genetic conditions that confer risk of sudden cardiac arrest or sudden cardiac death (SCA/SCD) in young, seemingly healthy individuals. Appropriate diagnosis of an SCA/SCD condition allows for guided management and prevents future sudden cardiac arrest and/or death from occurring. However, identification of a genetic predisposition can affect future insurance applications. While the United States' 2008 Genetic Information Non-discrimination Act (GINA) provides protection against genetic discrimination in employment and health insurance, it does not protect against the use of genetic information with regards to life insurance. This study aimed to expand the current understanding of life insurance experiences in the hereditary SCA/SCD community, gather strategies for individuals who wish to attain life insurance, and facilitate the development of life insurance specific patient and provider resources. Participants were recruited through The Sudden Arrhythmia Death Syndromes (SADS) Foundation. Semi-structured interviews were completed with 15 participants who have or are at-risk for SCA/SCD. Thematic analysis captured three themes: Emotional Outlook and Impact, Navigating the System, and Pay It Forward. Our participants with or at-risk for SCA/SCD expressed interest in attaining life insurance coverage that meets their individual needs and invested a meaningful amount of time and effort into their attempts. Most were unsuccessful. They perceived a lack of understanding regarding heritable SCA/SCD conditions by insurance professionals and felt their denials were unfairly attributed to their SCA/SCD diagnosis. Participants shared numerous suggestions for improved approaches to life insurance attainment and educational opportunities.

articles.title: INNOVATIVE SYMPTOMS ASSESSMENT APPROACH USING EHEALTH TECHNOLOGIES IN PATIENTS WITH OLEA EUROPAEA POLLEN ALLERGY USING AN ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE CHAMBER.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: what is the context and aim of the study? The prevalence of Olea europaea (Olea) pollinosis in large areas of southern Europe is very relevant. This study introduces and assesses a novel approach using eHealth technologies within an environmental exposure chamber (EEC) to evaluate Olea pollen allergy at Ramón y Cajal University Hospital (RyCUH) in Madrid. The primary goal was to clinically validate the safety and diagnostic performance of Olea pollen exposure in an EEC, representing the first reported use of olive pollen in this setting.

METHODS: what were the principal methods used? A new EEC was developed at RyCUH, ensuring reproducible pollen distribution and stable environmental conditions. The study recruited 20 volunteers: 15 Olea pollen-allergic individuals and 5 controls. REDCap, an electronic data capture tool, was used to collect patient-reported symptom scores, asthma-related data, and clinical observations before, during, and after EEC exposure. PowerBI software facilitated real-time monitoring of clinical and technical parameters to ensure patient safety.

RESULTS: What are the most important findings? The results indicated that 12 of the 15 allergic participants (80%) experienced positive reactions during the Olea pollen challenge, primarily rhinitis and conjunctivitis, with a few developing mild asthma symptoms. No symptoms were observed in the control group, confirming specificity. The use of PowerBI enabled immediate assessment of symptom severity, and all reactions were promptly managed.

CONCLUSIONS: What is the most important conclusion drawn, and what is the clinical or research relevance of the results? In conclusion, this study presents the first Olea pollen challenge in an EEC, demonstrating it to be a safe and effective method for evaluating allergic patients. The integration of REDCap and PowerBI for the in an EEC, represents a significant advancement, establishing a new precision medicine tool for symptom assessment and safety monitoring in Olea pollen allergy and contributing to the digital transformation of allergology.

articles.title: Mechanical CPR - Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention During Cardiac Arrest: Feasibility and Outcomes.
articles.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrest complicating acute coronary syndromes requires immediate coronary reperfusion; however, performing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during active manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) presents significant technical challenges. The Lund University Cardiac Arrest System (LUCAS) provides automated mechanical chest compressions and enables uninterrupted CPR during coronary angiography and PCI. Existing evidence is primarily limited to case reports and small observational studies, mechanical CPR has emerged as a practical adjunct in catheterization laboratories where manual compressions are unsafe or logistically challenging. We report two cases from our center in which LUCAS-assisted PCI was performed during ongoing cardiac arrest in the setting of cardiogenic shock and acute coronary syndromes, alongside a structured narrative synthesis of contemporary literature addressing feasibility, procedural considerations, and clinical outcomes. Mechanical chest compressions allowed uninterrupted angiography and successful revascularization in both cases, with return of spontaneous circulation achieved in one patient. Despite procedural success, survival remained poor, reflecting severe global ischemia and metabolic derangement. LUCAS-assisted PCI is a technically feasible strategy that facilitates coronary reperfusion in carefully selected patients. Evidence of survival benefit remains limited and derives predominantly from observational studies and case reports rather than randomized controlled trials. The role of extracorporeal CPR (ECPR) as a complementary or alternative strategy warrants explicit consideration at appropriately resourced centers. Improved patient selection and integration into structured resuscitation pathways may enhance clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Letter to Editor: Peripheral limitation as main factor for reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and no beta-blockers effects in patients with cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society

articles.title: Calcium Overload in Trisomy 21: An Underrecognized Cause of Persistent Hypercalcaemia - A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calcium overload in trisomy 21 is a rare and underrecognized cause of persistent parathyroid hormone (PTH)-independent hypercalcaemia in infants and young children with Down syndrome. Characteristic features include hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, renal impairment, and failure to thrive. Delayed recognition may result in avoidable long-term complications.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 21-month-old boy with trisomy 21 presented with a six-month history of recurrent vomiting, feeding difficulties, and failure to thrive. Bilateral nephrocalcinosis was detected incidentally on abdominal ultrasound. Laboratory evaluation revealed marked hypercalcaemia with suppressed PTH and 1,25(OH)₂D, hypercalciuria, and acute kidney injury. Extensive diagnostic work-up excluded alternative causes of PTH-independent hypercalcaemia. Nutritional assessment showed an almost exclusively milk-based diet with minimal solid food intake. Initial treatment with intravenous fluids and a single dose of pamidronate resulted in only transient improvement. Following the diagnosis of calcium overload, a calcium-restricted diet consisting of normal and low-calcium formula was introduced and adjusted according to biochemical response. Serum calcium normalized and remained stable throughout 11 months of follow-up. Growth and developmental progress improved, while nephrocalcinosis persisted and renal function partially recovered.

CONCLUSION: Calcium overload in trisomy 21 should be considered in young children with Down syndrome presenting with failure to thrive, recurrent vomiting, and nephrocalcinosis in combination with PTH-independent hypercalcemia. Early recognition and initiation of dietary calcium restriction may prevent long-term complications such as chronic kidney disease and prolonged growth impairment.

articles.title: Post-mortem MRI assessment of fetal corpus callosum growth patterns between 14 and 22 weeks of gestation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest commissural tract in the human brain, playing a crucial role in interhemispheric communication and neurodevelopment. Although ultrasonography and MRI have been used to assess callosal morphology, most available data are from later gestational ages, with limited normative information for fetuses below 20 weeks. This study aims to fill this gap by evaluating the biometry of the corpus callosum using high-resolution post-mortem fetal brain MRI between 14 and 22 gestational weeks.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study analyzed post-mortem MRI scans of 77 neurotypical fetal brains aged 14-22 gestational weeks. Imaging was performed on a 3T MRI scanner using a dedicated fetal protocol. T2-weighted STIR sequences provided optimal contrast for delineating the corpus callosum. The anteroposterior (AP) length and body thickness were measured on mid-sagittal images. Data were analyzed using SPSS with descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, linear regression, and ANOVA at a significance level of p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The mean AP length of the corpus callosum was 1.78 ± 0.69 cm, and the mean body thickness was 0.171 ± 0.031 cm. AP length showed a strong positive correlation with gestational age (r = 0.952, p < 0.001), while body thickness showed a moderate correlation (r = 0.613, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This study provides early normative post-mortem MRI data of corpus callosum growth between 14 and 22 weeks. The findings establish reference values that may assist in early detection of callosal dysgenesis and related neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

articles.title: Host-Shaped Microbial Metabolite Signaling in the AKI-to-CKDTransition: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Boundaries.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) increases the subsequent risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the transition is shaped by the quality of tubular repair rather than nephron loss alone. We frame the gut-kidney axis as a bidirectional host-microbial system in which AKI-related inflammation, impaired solute clearance, altered tubular transport, intestinal barrier dysfunction, medications, diet, and intestinal transit may redirect microbial metabolic output during recovery. Repair-disrupting candidates, including trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), indoxyl sulfate (IS), p-cresyl sulfate (PCS), and broader aromatic solute burden, are evaluated alongside repair-permissive candidates such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), selected indoles, and bile acids; polyamines are treated as bidirectional and stage-dependent. We connect these exposures to mitochondrial recovery, cell-cycle arrest, senescence, immune recruitment, endothelial stress, and fibroblast activation, while distinguishing microbial production from host transformation, renal clearance, and tubular uptake. Direct human AKI-to-CKD evidence remains limited, and antibiotic-depletion studies cannot isolate a single metabolite pathway. Translational studies should therefore combine longitudinal blood, urine, and fecal profiling with AKI etiology, treatment exposures, tubular injury markers, spatial kidney biology, and target-engagement endpoints.

articles.title: Montelukast combined with ICS/LABA improves clinical outcomes in moderate-to-severe persistent asthma by modulating T lymphocyte subset-related cytokine profiles.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucocorticoids and montelukast, an anti-leukotriene agent, target different inflammatory pathways. This study aims to investigate the immunological synergy of their combination.

METHODS: A prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label study was conducted. Two hundred and third-four patients were randomly assigned to two groups for a 12-week treatment period. Control group [ICS+long-acting beta₂-agonist (LABA)]; n = 118): Budesonide 400 µg/day (200 µg twice daily) + formoterol 18 µg/day (9 µg twice daily). Combination group (n = 116): Same ICS+LABA regimen + Montelukast 10 mg orally once daily.

RESULTS: At Week 12, the ICS+LABA+Mon group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in pre-bronchodilator FEV₁ compared with the ICS+LABA group (mean change: +239.0 ± 70.5 mL vs. +141.2 ± 47.9 mL; between-group difference 97.8 mL; 95% CI: 82.4 to 113.2; P < 0.001). Asthma control improved more substantially with combination therapy, as shown by greater ACQ-6 score reductions, with the mean score in the combination group approaching the well-controlled threshold. Immunologically, combination therapy produced a significantly greater increase in IFN-γ and Treg cytokines IL-10 and TGF-β, alongside more pronounced suppression of T helper 2 (Th2) cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13) and the Th17 cytokine IL-17.

CONCLUSIONS: The addition of montelukast to ICS+LABA therapy significantly enhances pulmonary function, asthma control, and suppression of eosinophilic airway inflammation in moderate-to-severe persistent asthma via a favorable immunological shift characterized by enhanced Th1 and Treg responses and more potent suppression of Th2 and Th17 pathways.

articles.title: Attributable Macroeconomic Burden and Projected Trends of Ischemic Stroke Due to Hypertension, Hyperglycemia, and Hyperlipidemia in Chinese Working-Age Adults Using a Bayesian Productivity-Adjusted Life-Year Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia are the leading modifiable risk factors for ischemic stroke in China, yet their combined long-term macroeconomic consequences for the working-age population remain poorly quantified.

METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we assessed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to these three metabolic risk factors among Chinese adults aged 20-64 years from 1990 to 2023. Temporal trends were evaluated via Joinpoint regression. Future disease burden through 2050 was projected using a Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model. The macroeconomic burden from 2024 to 2030 was estimated using a Bayesian productivity-adjusted life-year (PALY) framework, with GDP losses expressed in purchasing power parity (PPP) international dollars (Intl$).

RESULTS: In 2023, these risk factors accounted for 105,469 deaths and 5,246,634 DALYs, with age-standardized rates of 12.98 and 645.85 per 100,000, respectively. Age-standardized rates declined consistently from 1990 to 2023 (AAPC: -3.07% for mortality; -2.18% for DALYs). Despite this, the absolute number of deaths is projected to reach 249,779 by 2050. The macroeconomic burden is projected to escalate to 4.08 million PALYs lost and a GDP loss of PPP intl $162.74 billion by 2030, disproportionately affecting males and adults aged 55-64 years.

CONCLUSION: Although age-standardized burden has declined, the absolute and macroeconomic burden attributable to metabolic risk factors is projected to rise substantially, underscoring the urgent need for integrated prevention targeting high-risk working-age groups.

articles.title: Clinical Features and Genetic Diversity of Primary Hyperoxaluria: A Case Series Analysis of Chinese Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to characterize the clinical features, genetic profiles, and outcomes of primary hyperoxaluria (PH) in a Chinese cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients diagnosed with PH between 2008 and 2025 at our institution. Diagnosis was established through genetic analysis or histopathological findings combined with clinical manifestations and positive family history. Clinical, laboratory, genetic, imaging, histopathological, treatment, and outcome data were collected.

RESULTS: Thirteen patients were included (PH1, n=7; PH2, n=3; PH3, n=2; unclassified, n=1). Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 7 and 21 years, respectively. Renal involvement manifested as urolithiasis (92.3%) and nephrocalcinosis (30.8%). At diagnosis, the overall median serum creatinine was 335 µmol/L, and the median 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion was 0.8 mmol/1.73m² (n = 6). Systemic oxalate deposition was observed in 30.8% of patients, predominantly affecting bone and heart. Five previously unreported genetic variants were identified. Treatment consisted of supportive care, with vitamin B6 for PH1. Over a median follow‑up of 13.0 years, 100% of PH1 and 66.7% of PH2 patients progressed to end-stage renal disease, with two infantile-onset PH1 patients demonstrating rapid progression; conversely, PH3 patients preserved renal function (chronic kidney disease stage 1). Three PH1 patients developed recurrent oxalate nephropathy following isolated kidney transplantation. The overall mortality was 15.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: PH commonly presents with non-specific symptoms of urolithiasis, frequently resulting in diagnostic delay. PH1 is associated with a more severe clinical course than other subtypes, particularly in infantile-onset cases. This study expands the known genetic variant spectrum and underscores the importance of early genetic diagnosis.

articles.title: Premenopausal Depression and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease After Menopause: A Large Real-world Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: While depression has been linked to adverse cardiometabolic profiles in postmenopausal women, its temporal relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) when occurring before menopause remains unclear. This study examined whether depression diagnosed prior to menopause was associated with incident CVD after menopause.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Postmenopausal women were assigned to two cohorts: cohort 1 included women with depression diagnosed before menopause and without preexisting CVD, premature menopause, or conventional CVD risk factors (smoking, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, overweight/obesity, or family history of ischemic heart disease); cohort 2 included comparable women without premenopausal depression. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including age at menopause, current age, and ethnicity. Risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals(CIs) were calculated to compare incident CVD (myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: Initial queries identified 90,638 women in cohort 1 and 1,237,202 in cohort 2. After matching, 88,884 women remained in each cohort, with a mean (SD) age of 57.6(11.4) years. Follow-up varies according to database entry time, with maximum follow-up of 20 years. Women with premenopausal depression had a higher incidence of postmenopausal CVD than those without depression (4.0% vs. 3.3%; RR,1.23; 95% CI, 1.17-1.29; p<.001), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 0.7% (95% CI, 0.6%-0.9%). Because the proportional hazards assumption was not satisfied, the Cox hazard ratio was interpreted as a secondary average time-to-event summary rather than as the primary effect estimate. The estimated hazard ratio for incident CVD was 1.21 (95% CI, 1.15-1.27; log-rank p<.001), representing an average association across the follow-up period rather than a constant hazard over time.

CONCLUSION: Women with premenopausal depression had a higher cumulative incidence of postmenopausal cardiovascular disease than matched women without depression, suggesting that premenopausal depression may represent a marker of increased cardiovascular vulnerability in midlife women.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine use and short-term all-cause mortality in ICU patients with ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation: a propensity-matched analysis from MIMIC-IV.
articles.abstract: Introduction Preclinical studies have demonstrated that dexmedetomidine (DEX), a sedative widely used in intensive care units (ICUs), exerts neuroprotective effects. However, its potential protective role and underlying mechanisms in ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. The study's objective was to assess the connection between the early administration of DEX and short-term mortality from all causes in patients with ischemic stroke and AF. Methods From the MIMIC-IV database, patients with ischemic stroke and AF were identified, including those who were administered DEX and those who were not. The primary endpoint was 7-day all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was 90-day all-cause mortality. Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to ensure baseline covariates were balanced. Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and were utilized to evaluate the association between dexmedetomidine (DEX) use and mortality, with subgroup analyses conducted to ensure the findings' robustness. Results In total, 1,355 patients with ischemic stroke and AF participated, with 253 (18.7%) receiving DEX. After PSM, 208 pairs were matched. In the fully adjusted model, dexmedetomidine (DEX) administration was significantly associated with lower all-cause mortality compared with the control group at both 7 days (before PSM, HR=0.36, 95%CI: 0.19-0.68, P=0.002; after PSM, HR=0.26, 95%CI: 0.12-0.54, P<0.001) and 90 days (before PSM, HR=0.84, 95%CI: 0.66-1.07, P=0.162; after PSM, HR=0.72, 95%CI: 0.53- 0.97, P=0.031). The subgroup analyses revealed that DEX's protective effect was stronger in patients aged 70 and above, females, those with hypertension, and those without heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Kaplan-Meier survival curves consistently illustrated that DEX users had greater survival probabilities both before and after matching. Conclusion In patients with ischemic stroke complicated by AF, DEX administration is connected to decreased mortality, underlining the possible importance of DEX in ICU settings.

articles.title: Risk of kidney failure in biopsy-verified kidney disease type in type 2 diabetes: A registry-based longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The risk of kidney failure (KF) varies among people with diabetes and chronic kidney disease. We aimed to investigate whether the risk of progression to KF differs by biopsy-proven type of kidney disease in type 2 diabetes (T2D).

METHODS: In this registry-based longitudinal cohort study, we identified all Danish adults with T2D who had a clinical kidney biopsy performed between 1994 and 2022. Using Poisson regression, we calculated the cumulative risk of KF with death as a competing risk.

RESULTS: We included 1203 individuals in the study, of which 1164 could be included in the final analysis: 483 had Diabetic Nephropathy (DN), 117 had mixed disease (coexistence of DN and non-DN (NDN)), and 564 had NDN. The risk of KF [95% CI] was 35% [29-42%] in DN, 18% [14-23%] in NDN and 33% [24-43%] in mixed disease after 3 years, and 47% [40-54%] in DN and 23% [18-29%] in NDN after 5 years. The 5xyear risk was not estimated for mixed disease due to the low number of cases. In DN, there was a significantly higher risk of KF from 3 to 5 years after the biopsy compared to NDN. In mixed disease, there was a significantly higher risk of KF compared to NDN after 3 years. There was no significant difference in the risk of KF between DN and mixed disease, however, the study may have been underpowered to detect a meaningful difference.

CONCLUSION: Biopsy-proven DN and mixed disease are associated with an increased risk of KF compared to NDN in T2D. The study underscores the severity of kidney disease in T2D when histopathological changes caused by diabetes are present.

articles.title: Clinical Course and Prognosis of the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition-defined Malnutrition in Critically Ill Patients with Sepsis: A Multicenter Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a critical condition with a high nutritional risk and mortality. Although the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria have been proposed for diagnosing malnutrition, their clinical relevance in sepsis remains unclear. Therefore, we conducted a descriptive study on GLIM-defined malnutrition in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with sepsis to investigate its clinical course and prognosis.

METHODS: This was a multicenter prospective study conducted at 15 centers. Malnutrition was identified at ICU admission when both phenotypic and etiologic criteria were present. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital mortality or a decline in activities of daily living (Barthel Index <90) at discharge. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, use of parenteral nutrition, and days to achievement of each ICU Mobility Scale level.

RESULTS: Among 254 patients, 106 (41.7%) had malnutrition. The malnutrition group showed a significantly higher occurrence of the composite of in-hospital mortality and Barthel Index <90 (76.4% vs. 64.2%, p=0.04) and had significantly longer ICU stays (7 vs. 5, p=0.001). Total nutrition delivery did not significantly differ between groups, while a higher percentage of patients in the malnutrition group received parenteral nutrition (57.6% vs. 43.2%, p=0.02). Significant delays in achieving higher mobility levels were observed in the malnutrition group.

CONCLUSIONS: GLIM-defined malnutrition in patients with sepsis was significantly associated with the composite outcome of in-hospital mortality or Barthel Index <90 at discharge. These results suggest the clinical importance of an early GLIM assessment after ICU admission.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With HFpEF and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction, particularly in patients with Type 2 Diabetes, due to shared cardiometabolic and inflammatory mechanisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiovascular benefit in HFpEF, but data regarding prevention of incident AF remain limited. Objectives To evaluate the association between SGLT2 inhibitor therapy and incident atrial fibrillation/flutter in patients with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus. Methods We performed a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus receiving oral antihyperglycemic therapy were identified. Patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors were matched 1:1 with those receiving Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. The primary outcome was incident AF/flutter. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, ischemic stroke, and composite major adverse cardiovascular events (cMACE; all-cause mortality, ischemic stroke, or acute myocardial infarction). Associations were assessed using hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs). Results After propensity matching, 37,108 patients were included (18,554 per group). Compared with DPP4 inhibitor therapy, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower incidence of AF/flutter (17.8% vs 19.2%; HR 0.84, RR 0.93), all-cause mortality (12.5% vs 21.4%; HR 0.53, RR 0.59), ischemic stroke (7.4% vs 8.7%; HR 0.78, RR 0.85), and cMACE (24.4% vs 33.0%; HR 0.66, RR 0.74). Conclusions In patients with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus, SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with lower rates of incident AF/flutter and adverse cardiovascular outcomes, supporting a potential role for SGLT2 inhibitors in modifying arrhythmic risk in addition to established cardiometabolic benefits.

articles.title: High-sensitivity C-Reactive Protein as a Risk-Enhancing Biomarker in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have a >10-fold higher risk of cardiovascular mortality than the general population, influenced by both traditional and non-traditional risk factors. Residual cardiovascular risk persists despite effective lipid lowering and antihypertensive treatment, suggesting that inflammation-driven mechanisms have been neglected. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) as a sensitive marker of systemic low-grade inflammation is a recognized risk-enhancing biomarker in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but its precise role, optimal thresholds, and therapeutic relevance in concomitant CKD-ASCVD remain poorly synthesized.

SUMMARY: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and EMBASE (January 1989-March 2026) were searched to consolidate evidence on hs-CRP in CKD-ASCVD from mechanistic, epidemiological, and clinical trials. Data supports a bidirectional cardiorenal axis: progressive CKD elevates hs-CRP by uremic toxin-induced interleukin-6 (IL-6), nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) activation, atherosclerosis, while high hs-CRP aggravates renal deterioration by CD32b-Smad3-transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) related tubulointerstistial fibrosis. hs-CRP >3 mg/L nearly doubles heart failure risk in CKD. Cumulative exposure increases the risk of developing CKD by 70% (hazard ratio [HR] 1.70) and cardiovascular mortality by up to three-fold. CKD-specific recalibration needed for standard thresholds (<1, 1-3, >3 mg/L). Novel anti-inflammatory agents, colchicine and ziltivekimab, reduce hs-CRP by 77-92% and lower cardiovascular events in general ASCVD populations, but advanced CKD evidence remains limited with outcome trials ongoing.

KEY MESSAGES: hs-CRP is a marker of a pathogenic bidirectional cardiorenal loop, independently associated with cardiovascular events, CKD progression, and death, beyond LDL-cholesterol and traditional risk factors. Serial hs-CRP monitoring as a continuous measure may be superior to threshold-based categorization, pending CKD-specific validation. IL-1β/IL-6 pathway inhibitors and colchicine are promising for residual inflammatory risk but hs-CRP itself is not validated as a direct therapeutic target.

articles.title: Kidney volumetry for predicting long-term outcome in acute kidney injury: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is effective for severe acute kidney injury (AKI); however, predicting successful CRRT discontinuation and long-term outcomes remains challenging. Although urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) levels and kidney volume measured by computed tomography (CT) have been associated with renal prognosis, it remains unclear whether their combination improves predictive accuracy. This study evaluated whether combining urinary NGAL levels with kidney volume measured by CT improves prediction accuracy.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, urinary NGAL levels and height-adjusted total kidney volume (HtTKV) were assessed for their ability to predict successful CRRT discontinuation and major adverse kidney events at 90 days (MAKE90).

RESULTS: Among the 74 patients included, CRRT discontinuation was successful in 55 (74.3%), and MAKE90 occurred in 31 (41.9%). Urinary NGAL (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-0.95) was a significant predictor of CRRT discontinuation, whereas HtTKV was not. For long-term outcomes, urinary NGAL (AUC, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.61-0.85]) and HtTKV (AUC, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.54-0.80]) were significantly associated with MAKE90. Adding HtTKV to urinary NGAL significantly improved prediction of MAKE90, as demonstrated by reclassification analyses (net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement).

CONCLUSIONS: Adding HtTKV significantly improved the prediction of long-term MAKE90 based on NGAL levels, but not that of short-term CRRT discontinuation. These findings in this proof-of-concept study suggest that structural kidney assessment by CT volumetry may complement urinary NGAL for long-term risk stratification in patients with severe AKI requiring CRRT.

articles.title: Utilities of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor in the Intensive Care Units.
articles.abstract: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become foundational therapies for heart failure and chronic kidney disease and are increasingly used in critically ill patients. Their established benefits for kidney and heart health, along with emerging evidence from acute-care settings, indicate growing interest in their potential role in intensive care medicine. However, whether these benefits can be translated to critically ill populations remains uncertain, and concerns regarding safety continue to influence clinical practice. Summary Clinical evidence supporting the use of SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) during acute illness is expanding. Benefits have been most consistently observed in acute heart failure, perioperative care, and renal outcomes, where randomized and observational studies suggest improved decongestion, reduced acute kidney injury, and favorable cardiorenal outcomes. These observations are supported by several biological effects of SGLT2i that extend beyond glucose lowering, including modulation of fluid balance, renal hemodynamics, metabolic adaptation, inflammation, and endothelial function-pathways that are central to the development of organ dysfunction during critical illness. However, important uncertainties remain regarding which critically ill patients are most likely to benefit, whether chronic therapy should be continued during acute illness, and how potential benefits should be balanced against safety concerns in the ICU. This review integrates current mechanistic and clinical evidence, examines the balance between potential benefits and risks, discusses practical management considerations, and highlights key research priorities to better define the role of SGLT2i in critical care medicine.   Key Messages - SGLT2 inhibitors show promise in critical care but are not established therapies. - Cardiorenal benefits must be balanced against metabolic and hemodynamic risks. - Future research should define the right patient, the right timing, and the right treatment strategy.

articles.title: Behind the Sella: A Rare Case of Pituicytoma Mimicking a Pituitary Adenoma.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Pituicytoma is a rare central nervous system (CNS) World Health Organization (WHO) grade I glioma originating from pituicytes, the specialized glial cells of the neurohypophysis or infundibulum. It accounts for less than 0.1% of all sellar and suprasellar masses and often presents a diagnostic challenge because of its clinical and radiological resemblance to other pituitary lesions. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old man was admitted to the endocrinology clinic because of clinical symptoms of hypogonadism, headaches, and visual field defects. Hormonal evaluation revealed hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and hyperprolactinemia. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a sellar-suprasellar mass, initially suggestive of prolactinoma. Lack of response to initial hormone replacement therapy, progressive tumor enlargement, and worsening visual impairment, prompted surgical resection via a right-temporal craniotomy. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examination established the diagnosis of pituicytoma (CNS WHO Grade 1). The postoperative course was complicated by transient cognitive impairment and endocrine deficiencies requiring long-term hormonal replacement therapy. We also review the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and current therapeutic approaches for this uncommon tumor. CONCLUSIONS Pituicytoma is a rare benign tumor that may closely mimic pituitary adenoma, both clinically and radiologically. Clinical manifestations are non-specific and primarily reflect tumor size and local extension. MRI findings are not pathognomic, making histopathological confirmation essential. Surgical resection remains the treatment of choice, whereas radiotherapy may be considered after subtotal resection. The case underscores the importance of recognizing hyperprolactinemia secondary to pituitary stalk compression, careful endocrine interpretation, individualized surgical planning, and prolonged multidisciplinary follow-up, given the uncertain long-term prognosis and potential endocrine sequelae.

articles.title: Feasibility of High-Intensity Interval Exercise in Young Adult Survivors of Pediatric Brain Tumor and Young Adults With Isocitrate Dehydrogenase-Mutant Gliomas (HYPE): Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and young adult patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutant gliomas are at risk for cognitive impairment, reduced physical fitness and function, as well as poor health-related quality of life (HRQOL) and psychosocial health. Exercise improves these outcomes; however, both populations remain understudied with respect to exercise interventions. High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is a promising intervention, as it is time-efficient, safe, tolerable, enhances cognition in healthy young adults, and improves physical fitness and quality of life in adult patients and survivors with cancer. However, the feasibility of HIIT is not yet understood in survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma.

OBJECTIVE: The HYPE study is a pilot randomized controlled trial that aims to (1) determine the feasibility of a HIIT exercise intervention for young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma, (2) determine the preliminary efficacy of HIIT to improve physical fitness and function, cognition, HRQOL, and psychosocial health, and (3) explore exercise sustainability and the impact of social determinants of health on study outcomes.

METHODS: A total of 30 young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma (18-45 years of age) will be randomized to an exercise or control group. The exercise group performs virtually supervised HIIT 3 times per week for 16 weeks, followed by 16 weeks of self-directed exercise. Exercise involves indoor cycling, and sessions include 20 minutes of high- and low-intensity intervals (high intensity=60-s 60%-90% peak power output; low intensity=60-s 10% peak power output), and a 5-minute warm-up and cool-down. The control group performs a 16-week stretching program. Feasibility of the HIIT intervention is measured by the number of exercise sessions completed, including total minutes and intensity, and barriers to exercise adherence. Cognition, physical fitness and function, HRQOL, and psychosocial health are measured using standardized assessments and self-report questionnaires. Exercise sustainability is measured by change in study outcomes following the self-directed follow-up period, and social determinants of health are assessed using a self-report questionnaire.

RESULTS: Baseline data collection began in February 2024, and 13 participants have been enrolled as of June 2026. The projected study end date is December 2026. Data analysis is planned to begin in January 2027, and findings will be published in the fall of 2028.

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this study is the first to use a virtually supervised HIIT intervention in young adult patients and survivors of brain tumor. The findings will elucidate the feasibility of HIIT to design and power a randomized controlled trial to address cancer- and treatment-related sequelae. They will also provide insights into the sustainability of HIIT and the impact of social determinants of health.

articles.title: Prevalence and risk factors of hearing impairment in older Singaporeans: a population-based study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We investigated the prevalence and risk factors of hearing impairment (HI) and significant hearing impairment (SHI) in a multi-ethnic older Asian population.

METHODS: We included 2,494 adults aged ≥60 years from a population-based study. Hearing was evaluated using a SHOEBOX portable audiometer, with any HI defined as a pure-tone average hearing threshold >25 dB and SHI defined as >40 dB, based on the better-hearing ear. Sociodemographic, lifestyle and clinical characteristics were collected via a standardised clinical examination and validated questionnaires. Weighted prevalence rates were calculated using age-, gender- and ethnicity-specific sampling weights from the 2020 Singapore Census. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors for HI and SHI.

RESULTS: Of the 2494 participants (mean age ± SD, 73.4 ± 8.4 years; 55.2% female), the weighted prevalence of any HI was 67.9%, while that of SHI was 22.7%. The weighted prevalence of any HI increased with age, from 58.1% in individuals aged 60-69-years to 94.9% in those aged ≥80 years, while that for SHI increased from 9.8% in individuals aged 60-69 years to 64.5% in those aged ≥80 years. Risk factors for HI included older age (odds ratio [OR] 10.33, P < 0.001), male sex (OR 2.05, P < 0.001), Malay ethnicity (OR 1.43, P = 0.021 vs. Chinese ethnicity), lower socioeconomic status (OR 2.58, P < 0.029), living alone (OR 1.62, P = 0.032) and prior stroke (OR 2.72, P = 0.016). Similar risk factors were associated with SHI.

CONCLUSION: Two in three community-living older Singaporeans live with HI, with one in five having SHI. Targeted community hearing screening programmes for older and vulnerable groups are essential to identify individuals requiring referral and treatment.

articles.title: TM6SF2 acts at ER membrane contact sites to enable RAB7-dependent endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintain Golgi structure.
articles.abstract: Although a loss-of-function variant of TM6SF2 is a highly penetrant risk factor for steatotic liver disease, including progression to cirrhosis and cancer, its normal function is largely unknown. Here we show that endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized TM6SF2 forms membrane contact sites (MCSs) with late endosomes/lysosomes, where it activates the small GTPase RAB7 to enable an endolysosomal route for selective secretion of lipid-rich very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) particles. In accord, TM6SF2 and RAB7 deficiency similarly cause endolysosomal VLDL retention and accumulation of enlarged late endosomes/lysosomes. TM6SF2 further binds to VAMP-associated protein (VAP) ER-anchor proteins to maintain MCSs between the ER, endosomes, and the trans-Golgi network, with TM6SF2 deficiency causing Golgi fragmentation and disruption of cGAS-STING signaling known to prevent cirrhosis and cancer by clearing senescent hepatocytes. Our findings establish TM6SF2 as an ER-MCS component that enables endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintains Golgi structure, which suggests that TM6SF2 loss of function causes liver disease through steatosis-dependent and independent mechanisms.

articles.title: PERCUTANEOUS MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY: A NEW TOOL IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA.
articles.journal: Portuguese journal of cardiac thoracic and vascular surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) remains challenging due to nonspecific symptoms and signs that lead to a high mortality rate. Common causes include cardiac emboli and thrombosis of a mesenteric plaque.

OBJECTIVE: To present a clinical case of acute mesenteric ischemia that underwent successful endovascular revascularization.

CASE REPORT: 82-year-old female patient with a history of atrioventricular block, hypertension, and dementia. She was admitted to the emergency department for acute abdominal pain with onset 3 days before. Diagnosis of ischemic colitis secondary to acute superior mesenteric artery occlusion was confirmed by angioCT scan. Endovascular treatment was performed: percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy through left brachial access using the Rotarex® system (Straub Medical). She improved from her previous symptoms and was discharged at day 6, with no need of exploratory laparotomy.

DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: AMI is a vascular emergency that requires rapid identification and treatment. There are two courses of action for mesenteric revascularization: open or endovascular. Some authors have demonstrated an advantage in the endovascular approach, with reduced morbidity and mortality, especially in an often aging and frail group of patients. The Rotarex® (Straub Medical) system fragments the thrombus and aspirates it at the same time, thus avoiding embolic phenomena at distance. Despite being a new technology, it has shown to be a very promising tool for AMI treatment due to its fast restoration of blood flow with minimal invasiveness.

articles.title: Clinician Use of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Information Platform.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize clinician use of an AI-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier-verified accounts of a commonly used AI-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38.8 million queries.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined.

RESULTS: Overall, 952 008 clinicians (58.5% female), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2.5-year study period. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18.0 to 39.5. Nurse practitioners (44.5) and physician assistants (44.5) submitted more queries per active user-month than physicians (37.1). A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation (use ratio, 2.54) and residents and fellows (1.84). Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology (use ratio, 2.00), internal medicine (1.88), and family medicine (1.80), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties (ophthalmology, 0.23; radiology, 0.24; orthopedics, 0.24). Most queries addressed clinical decision-making (51.9%), particularly treatment and management (33.1%), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13.9% of queries. Queries addressing topics outside physicians' own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Over 2.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI-enabled clinical information platform. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks.

articles.title: Automated Quantification of Parkinsonian Facial Expressions via a Transformer-Based Multi-View Multimodal Fusion Framework.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Facial hypomimia, a common symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), is characterized by reduced facial expressiveness due to muscle rigidity. Its clinical assessment, typically based on the Movement Disorder Society-Unified PD Rating Scale, is challenging due to the limited clinician availability, subjectivity, and time consuming procedures. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based multi-view multimodal fusion framework for efficient and objective video-based automated assessment of PD facial expressions. The framework incorporates facial anatomical priors, jointly models global and local features, and progressively fuses complementary information across modalities. It uses a progressive fusion strategy for cross-modal interaction and compensation, together with a spatial-temporal transformer block for anatomically guided landmark modeling of global motion and local subtle dynamics. Our proposed method achieved an accuracy of 68.28% and an acceptable accuracy of 87.75% on the largest clinical dataset (637 videos from 354 PD patients) with four classes. Moreover, testing on an independent dataset from another hospital provides preliminary evidence of the model's cross-center transferability, and the framework was further evaluated on two additional medical facial assessment tasks of stroke facial palsy and facial function. In summary, the proposed framework provides an efficient and reliable solution for the objective assessment of PD facial expressions, with the potential to improve evaluation consistency and support broader clinical applications.

articles.title: Self-MAR: Self-Supervised Multi-Stage Autoregressive Model for Water-Related Optical Image Enhancement.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
