articles.abstract: We propose Self-MAR, a self-supervised paradigm for water-related optical image enhancement that enables input-only restoration via the proposed VAR-inspired Multi-stage AutoRegressive model, in which each restoration stage is conditioned on the preceding restored state. The intricate interactions between light and the water medium introduce residual degradations that are difficult to model explicitly, thereby limiting the effectiveness of existing methods that rely heavily on synthetic data or sparse annotations. Furthermore, acquiring paired ground-truth data in real underwater environments remains challenging, giving rise to the triangular dilemma in underwater image enhancement (UIE). To address these issues, Self-MAR incorporates three key components: 1) We design a multi-stage, coarse-to-fine reconstruction architecture that progressively recovers image structure and suppresses content-coupled underwater object residuals (ORs) at different resolutions, transforming OR removal into structure-aware controllable image generation. 2) We construct an asymmetric phase-amplitude interaction that combines the structural phase of the current observation with the corrected spectral-energy distribution of the preceding restoration estimate. This interaction preserves spatial organization during stage-wise upsampling and propagates corrected color-energy statistics from coarse to fine. 3) We propose the Churning constraint mechanism to preserve the original perceptual features of the input image and prevent semantic drift during the self-supervised training process. Self-MAR derives supervision targets from the inputs themselves: underwater inputs generate OR-removal targets, while in-air inputs generate structural self-reconstruction targets from their own content.Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive full-reference restoration quality, leading performance across complementary no-reference metrics (UIQM, UCIQE, NIQE, and URANKER), efficient inference, and consistent performance across UIEB C60, UCCS, U45, and Z700. Downstream evaluation on SeaThru-D1 further shows the lowest combined depth-consistency error among thecompared state-of-the-art enhancement methods.

articles.title: Latent Interpolation Learning Using Diffusion Models for Cardiac Volume Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging is a critical tool for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular disease, yet its utility is often limited by the sparse acquisition of 2D short-axis slices, resulting in incomplete volumetric information. Accurate 3D reconstruction from these sparse slices is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, but existing methods face challenges, including reliance on predefined interpolation schemes (e.g., linear or spherical), computational inefficiency, and dependence on additional semantic inputs such as segmentation labels or motion data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Cardiac Latent Interpolation Diffusion (CaLID) framework that introduces three key innovations. First, we present a data-driven interpolation scheme based on diffusion models, which can capture complex, non-linear relationships between sparse slices and improves reconstruction accuracy. Second, we design a computationally efficient method that operates in the latent space and speeds up generative 3D whole-heart upsampling time by a factor of 24, reducing computational overhead compared to previous methods. Third, with only sparse 2D CMR images as input, our method achieves SOTA performance against baseline methods, eliminating the need for auxiliary input such as morphological guidance, thus simplifying workflows. We further extend our method to 2D+T data, enabling the effective modeling of spatiotemporal dynamics and ensuring temporal coherence. Extensive volumetric evaluations and downstream segmentation tasks demonstrate that CaLID achieves superior reconstruction quality and efficiency. By addressing the fundamental limitations of existing approaches, our framework advances the state of the art for spatio and spatiotemporal whole-heart reconstruction, offering a robust and clinically practical solution for cardiovascular imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/niklasbubeck/calid.

articles.title: Prevalent Sodium-Glucose Co-Transporter 2 Inhibitor Use, Baseline Laboratory Profile, and Clinical Outcomes in a Real-World Heart Failure Cohort.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prevalence of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, baseline laboratory profiles, and associated clinical outcomes in a real-world heart failure (HF) cohort.

METHOD: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included consecutive patients with HF who were evaluated between January 2022 and January 2024. Of the 609 patients, 581 with known SGLT2i use status constituted the analytic cohort. The primary outcome was HF hospitalization. A composite outcome comprising all-cause death, HF hospitalization, stroke, or peripheral embolism was assessed as an exploratory endpoint. Propensity score matching and overlap-weighted Cox regression models were used in sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Among the 581 patients, 349 were SGLT2i users and 232 were non-users. Users had a lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher B-type natriuretic peptide concentrations, a higher prevalence of diabetes and ischemic etiology, and more intensive background therapy. In the unadjusted analyses, the rates of HF hospitalization and composite events were higher among users; however, these associations were attenuated after adjustment. In the overlap-weighted propensity score analysis, SGLT2i use was not associated with HF hospitalization (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.57-1.47; P=0.700), the study-defined composite endpoint (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.61-1.48; P=0.827), or exploratory all-cause mortality (HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.45-2.42; P=0.931).

CONCLUSION: SGLT2i users represented a treated population with more advanced clinical characteristics, and their higher unadjusted event burden did not persist after adjustment. These findings reflect treatment selection rather than therapeutic benefit or harm. Therapies proven to reduce mortality should be systematically implemented in all eligible patients with HF, regardless of their clinical status or estimated mortality risk.

articles.title: Saroglitazar improves hepatic steatosis and liver enzymes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome and MASLD: A multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the leading endocrine disorder in reproductive-age women. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in women with PCOS, but they are underrepresented in MASLD therapeutic trials. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of saroglitazar, a novel peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors α/γ agonist, for the treatment of hepatic steatosis in women with PCOS and MASLD.

METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2A trial, 60 women (18-45 y) with PCOS and MASLD were randomized 1:1 to either saroglitazar 4 mg or placebo for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was relative (percent) change in hepatic fat content, measured by MRI proton density fat fraction. Primary analysis was performed in the per-protocol population (saroglitazar: 25; placebo: 23).

RESULTS: Participants in the saroglitazar group showed a significant reduction in percent hepatic fat content at 24 weeks from baseline compared to placebo ([least squares mean±SE]: -14.81±5.52 vs. 1.96±5.75, p =0.041). When controlled for baseline HbA1c imbalance, the beneficial effect of saroglitazar was more pronounced ([least squares mean±SE]: -18.93±4.83 vs. 6.43±5.04, p <0.009). A higher proportion in the saroglitazar group achieved ≥30% reduction in magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (36.0% vs. 8.7%; p =0.025). Saroglitazar also significantly reduced aminotransferase levels, lipid parameters, and the FibroScan AST score. Adverse events were comparable between the groups, and none were serious. One pregnancy in the saroglitazar arm resulted in uneventful maternal and neonatal outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In women with PCOS and MASLD, saroglitazar significantly improved hepatic steatosis, liver enzymes, lipid profile, and FibroScan AST score. These findings support further evaluation of saroglitazar in larger studies in women with PCOS.

articles.title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes.

METHODS: Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC (n = 7) or pedestrian crash (n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments.

RESULTS: At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm2), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm3), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD (r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

articles.title: Veterinary Student Experience and Learning Using a 4D Electrocardiogram Simulator.
articles.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology and electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation present challenges for veterinary and medical education. Various resources and simulators exist to address this challenge. This study investigates the impact on learning and student experience of Epicardio Simulation™-VET in a UK undergraduate veterinary curriculum. This multi-method study invited students at the University of Liverpool School of Veterinary Science to complete a survey, comprising Likert-type and free-text questions, exploring their Epicardio experience. A case-control study used a pre- and post-learning quiz to compare learning gain in a self-directed clinical rotation ECG tutorial between a group learning with Epicardio and one learning with traditional resources. Survey responses were generally positive, with median scores of 4/5, except in response to the statement "Epicardio is easy to navigate" (Mdn 3/5), and "Epicardio workshops should replace traditional lectures" (Mdn 2/5; considerable variability in responses). Students also varied on whether "the tutorials were easy to follow." Thematic analysis identified positive themes around application, clarification, visualization, interactivity, formative assessment, and user-friendliness. Negative themes highlighted technical difficulties including navigation and structure of the software, as well as curricular integration. The case-control study showed learning gains in both groups and no difference between groups before or after the self-directed tutorial. Students valued Epicardio as an additional learning tool and learned equally well with Epicardio and traditional resources in a self-directed format.

articles.title: Preeclampsia and Hypertension Disorders of Pregnancy in Women with Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. Women with CKD are at particularly high risk, with preeclampsia affecting up to 40% of pregnancies. This chapter summarizes the current understanding of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, with an emphasis on preeclampsia in women with underlying kidney disease. We discuss the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical diagnosis, prevention, and management of preeclampsia, highlighting the unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by preexisting CKD. We review the role of angiogenic biomarkers, including the sFlt1/PlGF ratio which is a ratio of anti/pro angiogenic proteins, in the diagnosis and risk stratification of preeclampsia, current prevention and management strategies, and the importance of post-partum nephrology follow-up.

articles.title: Rituximab-Belimumab Sequential Therapy in Refractory Minimal Change Disease.
articles.abstract: Frequent relapses and steroid dependence remain challenging in minimal change disease (MCD). Rituximab depletes B cells, yet post-treatment B-cell Activating Factor (BAFF) elevation may drive disease relapse. Sequential rituximab followed by belimumab (a BAFF inhibitor) has shown benefit in lupus, but its role in MCD is unknown. A 14-year-old male with biopsy-proven MCD and acute kidney injury failed multiple immunosuppressants, including two courses of rituximab (the first induced a 6-month remission, whereas the second failed despite B-cell depletion). After another relapse, he received single-dose rituximab followed by belimumab, achieving complete remission and maintaining relapse-free for 57 months.This case suggests that sequential rituximab-belimumab therapy may offer durable remission in MCD patients who are refractory to conventional immunosuppressive regimens.

articles.title: See One.
A Cascade-Responsive Carbon Dot-Nanogel Platform for Sequential Photothermal-Chemo Cancer Therapy via GSH and NIR Dual Activation.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapeutic agents are often limited by poor tumor-specific accumulation, leading to off-target toxicity, while monochemotherapy frequently results in multidrug resistance and suboptimal treatment outcomes. To address these challenges, we have developed a carbon dot-based nanogel drug delivery system that integrates both glutathione (GSH) and photothermal dual-responsiveness, enabling controlled drug release, active tumor targeting, and synergistic photothermal-chemotherapy. Specifically, phenylboronic acid functionalized on the nanogel surface confers tumor-targeting capability. Upon internalization into tumor cells with elevated GSH levels, the nanogel disintegrates, releasing carbon dots conjugated with the chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin (DOX). Under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the carbon dots generate heat, which not only directly damages cancer cells but also triggers on-demand DOX release, achieving a synergistic photothermal-chemotherapeutic effect. Notably, both in vitro and in vivo studies reveal that this system effectively induces cancer cell necrosis through a multimodal mechanism: disruption of lysosomes, induction of DNA damage, and simultaneous suppression of heat shock protein (HSP) expression. This integrated strategy results in significantly enhanced therapeutic outcomes, overcoming key limitations of conventional chemotherapy.

articles.title: Serum apelin levels in established pulmonary arterial hypertension: A cross-sectional case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive condition involving pulmonary vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, abnormal angiogenesis, and right ventricular dysfunction. Apelin, an endogenous peptide acting via the APJ receptor, modulates vascular tone, enhances nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation, and counteracts the renin-angiotensin system, suggesting relevance to PAH.

AIMS: To compare serum apelin levels between patients with established PAH and healthy controls and to examine their relationship with cross-sectional measures of disease severity.

METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional study, 40 patients with established Group 1 PAH receiving PAH-specific therapy and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. All participants underwent echocardiographic evaluation, a six-minute walk test, and serum apelin measurement. PAH patients were additionally classified using the 2022 ESC/ERS four-strata risk model and WHO functional class.

RESULTS: Serum apelin levels were significantly higher in PAH patients than in controls (1006.20 ± 312.99 pg/mL vs. 812.46 ± 245.80 pg/mL; p = 0.003). Apelin levels did not differ significantly across PAH etiologies (p = 0.16), ESC/ERS risk strata (p = 0.84), or WHO functional classes (p = 0.06). In multivariable logistic regression, apelin remained independently associated with PAH status (OR 1.345 per 100 pg/mL; 95% CI 1.084-1.669; p = 0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Serum apelin levels were higher in patients with established PAH than in healthy controls and were independently associated with PAH status, whereas no significant association with the evaluated cross-sectional severity measures was demonstrated. Any potential diagnostic role of apelin requires validation in newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve patients and clinically relevant comparator groups.

articles.title: Rule-Out yield of the European society of cardiology 0/1-Hour troponin protocol in frail and non-frail octogenarians.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the rule-out yield of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) algorithm for 30-day major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in emergency department (ED) patients aged ≥ 80 years, and explore whether frailty modifies performance.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included patients aged ≥ 80 undergoing 0/1-h hs-cTnI sampling for suspected acute coronary syndrome. Frailty was defined using the Clinical Frailty Scale (≥ 5). The prespecified primary outcome was the 30-day MACE miss rate in the rule-out stratum against a 1% threshold.

RESULTS: Of 1,136 screened encounters, 800 were analyzed (median age 83 years; 56.9% female); 312 (39.0%) were frail. Blinded re-abstraction of 80 records yielded kappa 0.82 (0.71-0.93) for frailty and agreement ≥ 0.71 across variables. The algorithm classified 120 patients (15.0%) as rule-out (prespecified target, 236); two had 30-day MACE (miss rate 1.7%; wide 95% Wilson CI, 0.5%-5.9%), an imprecise estimate whose upper bound exceeds the 1% threshold. A post hoc bounding analysis counting all 11 rule-out patients with incomplete nonfatal ascertainment as events raised the upper bound to 10.8% (6.4%-17.7%). Sensitivity was 99.0% and negative predictive value 98.3%. In prespecified exploratory analysis, no statistically significant independent association was observed between frailty and 30-day MACE (average marginal effect + 1.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.05 to + 7.20; p = 0.744).

CONCLUSIONS: The ESC algorithm ruled out only 15% of octogenarians, potentially reflecting baseline age- and renal-related troponin elevations. Limited rule-out sample size, wide confidence intervals, and incomplete follow-up prevent a definitive safety conclusion.

articles.title: Safety, Efficacy, and Pharmacokinetics of Agalsidase Alfa in Treatment-Naive Chinese Patients with Fabry Disease: 52-Week Phase 3, Open-Label, Single-Arm Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical data on the efficacy, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of agalsidase alfa in Chinese patients with Fabry disease are limited. We evaluated the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of agalsidase alfa in Chinese patients who are treatment-naive over 52 weeks.

METHODS: This was an open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, multicenter (six centers in China) phase 3 study. Patients with Fabry disease (aged 7-65 years; either sex) received agalsidase alfa 0.2 mg/kg intravenously (every other week for up to 52 weeks). The primary endpoint was the incidence of serious treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs). Secondary endpoints included the incidence of TEAEs, changes from baseline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), left ventricular mass index (LVMI), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and agalsidase alfa pharmacokinetics.

RESULTS: Overall, 20 patients were enrolled (May 2022 to January 2024) and received ≥ 1 dose of agalsidase alfa. The median number of infusions was 27; median exposure duration was 12.0 months. Agalsidase alfa was generally well tolerated. Two patients (10.0%) reported one serious TEAE each (sepsis, ectopic pregnancy). All patients reported ≥ 1 TEAE, most of which were mild or moderate (98.2%); nine patients (45.0%) had ≥ 1 TEAE assessed as related to treatment. Baseline eGFR, LVMI, and LVEF were 118.8 (21.4) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38.0 (11.2) g/m2.7, and 66.8% (4.9), respectively. Renal function and cardiac structure and function remained relatively stable over 52 weeks; mean (SD) changes in eGFR, LVMI, and LVEF from baseline were 4.1 (12.5) mL/min/1.73 m2, 0.56 (8.71) g/m2.7, and 0.8% (3.3%), respectively. Agalsidase alfa exposure (area under the concentration-time curve and maximum serum concentration) was generally similar at week 0 and at week 28.

CONCLUSIONS: Data from this 52-week study support the use of agalsidase alfa as a long-term treatment option for Chinese patients with Fabry disease. Safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic profiles were consistent with studies in other populations. Graphical Abstract available for this article.

GOV ID: NCT04974749.

articles.title: Association of renal resistive index with coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether renal resistive index (RRI) is independently associated with the presence of coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and to explore its unadjusted associations with continuous coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 120 patients with preserved renal function who underwent renal Doppler ultrasonography before CCTA. The primary outcome was the presence of coronary artery calcification, defined as a CACS > 0. Associations of RRI with continuous CACS and CAD-RADS categories were evaluated in exploratory, unadjusted analyses. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the independent association between RRI and CACS > 0. A clinical model and the same model supplemented with RRI were compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: RRI was higher in patients with CACS > 0 than in those with CACS = 0 (0.697 ± 0.051 vs. 0.646 ± 0.054, p < 0.001) and correlated with CACS (r = 0.474, p < 0.001). RRI also differed across CAD-RADS categories (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, smoking, and dyslipidaemia, each 0.01-unit increase in RRI was independently associated with higher odds of CACS > 0 (adjusted OR 1.137, 95%CI 1.041-1.242; p=0.005). Adding RRI improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p=0.003) but did not significantly improve discrimination (AUC 0.782 vs. 0.819; DeLong p = 0.129).

CONCLUSION: RRI was independently associated with the presence of coronary artery calcification in patients with preserved renal function. Associations with continuous CACS and CAD-RADS categories were exploratory and unadjusted.

articles.title: fiLiver and spleen elastography-based prediction models for clinically significant portal hypertension and high-risk esophageal varices: a systematic review of conventional and machine-learning approaches.
articles.abstract: The presence of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk esophageal varices (HREV) are major predictors of decompensation and mortality in chronic liver disease. Liver and spleen elastography are validated noninvasive markers of portal pressure, and increasing numbers of studies have integrated elastography measurements with conventional statistical and machine-learning (ML) models to predict these outcomes. This systematic review identified, critically appraised and synthesized studies developing or validating prediction models incorporating liver and/or spleen elastography for predicting CSPH and/or HREV. A structured literature search identified studies developing or validating prediction models using transient elastography, shear-wave elastography or magnetic resonance elastography in adults with chronic liver disease. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST+AI. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in elastography modalities, prediction algorithms and outcome definitions, findings were synthesized narratively. Eleven studies published between 2015 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Three evaluated machine-learning algorithms using elastography as an input feature (LightGBM, logistic regression/XGBoost hybrid and artificial neural network), whereas eight used conventional cutoff or regression approaches. The best-performing model combined liver stiffness, spleen stiffness and fibrosis-4 within logistic regression and XGBoost, achieving AUROCs of 0.902-0.927 across three independent datasets for HREV and outperforming earlier liver-stiffness-only models. The two newest multicenter externally validated ML studies showed low risk of bias, whereas older, smaller single-center studies frequently demonstrated high or unclear risk, particularly within the analysis domain because external validation was lacking. ML-assisted models integrating liver and spleen elastography with laboratory parameters show promising performance, warranting further external validation before widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Maternity-Leave Related TikTok Videos: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Content and Viewer Engagement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Maternity leave policy in the United States is fragmented, leading to inconsistent access to job protection and paid leave. The lack of a universal policy and variation across states contributes to inequities in maternal health, economic stability, and gender equity. This study describes how maternity leave is portrayed on TikTok and examines which content features are associated with viewer engagement as a part of informal policy dialogue.

METHODS: A cross-sectional content analysis was conducted on 100 TikTok videos tagged with #maternityleave. Videos were coded for thematic content (e.g., humor, policy references, music, presence of infants) and engagement metrics (views, likes, comments, favorites). Descriptive statistics summarized content features and engagement metrics. Independent two-tailed Welch t-tests (α = 0.05) compared views, likes, favorites, and comments between videos with and without each of the four most common content features. False Discovery Rate (FDR) adjustments were applied to account for multiple comparisons, and Cohen's d was used to estimate effect size.

RESULTS: The 100 videos generated substantial engagement (41.3 million views, 3.14 million likes, 187,145 favorites, and 114,574 comments), and most featured only women (88%). Videos referencing a specific policy and videos without music received more favorites, while videos featuring an infant showed a trend toward more likes. Humor was not associated with engagement. None of the observed associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction.

CONCLUSION: Maternity leave content on TikTok attracted substantial viewer engagement, and several content features demonstrated exploratory patterns of association with engagement. Policy-referencing videos received more favorites in the unadjusted analysis, while infant-related content showed a non-significant trend toward greater likes. The results suggest that TikTok is one space where maternity leave experiences and policies are discussed. Given the modest convenience sample and the platform's dynamic nature, future research should examine whether engagement with such content relates to viewers' maternity leave knowledge, attitudes, or civic action for national maternity leave policy.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Community Health Worker Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Applied health economics and health policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes contributes substantially to healthcare costs, disability, and premature mortality worldwide. Although community health worker (CHW) interventions improve glycemic outcomes and address social determinants of health, current cost-effectiveness evidence has not been systematically synthesized. We reviewed the economic evidence for CHW interventions in type 2 diabetes management.

METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and ProQuest from inception through August 2025 for peer-reviewed primary studies evaluating economic outcomes of CHW interventions for adults with type 2 diabetes. We extracted data and assessed study quality. Owing to heterogeneity in design, cost reporting, and limited variance estimates, we conducted a narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: Of 753 records, 11 met inclusion criteria. All studies focused on low-income and/or ethnic minority populations. Ten reported program costs ($29-6235 per patient/year; 2025 USD). Nine reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. Two of three short-term studies (< 5 years) found interventions cost-effective; all six long-term studies (≥ 20 years) found the same.

CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence suggests that CHW interventions are likely cost-effective for adults with T2D, particularly when evaluated over longer time horizons.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251101900. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251101900 .

articles.title: Altered cholangiocyte subsets with neural pathway enrichment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Hepatocytes have been extensively studied in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet the role of cholangiocytes remains underexplored. We utilized a comprehensive approach that integrates high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cellular interaction evaluation, machine learning techniques, immune cell infiltration analysis, and Mendelian randomization to investigate both single-cell sequencing data and bulk sequencing datasets. Single-cell analysis identified significant alterations in cholangiocyte subpopulations in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) patients, including an increase in cholangiocytes with elevated SEMA3 pathway expression. The hdWGCNA analysis identified the green module, which is enriched with genes associated with neural pathways pertinent to MASH. Seven machine learning models assessed the diagnostic feasibility of key genes in the green module for MASLD spectrum. Immune infiltration analysis highlighted complex interactions between cholangiocytes enriched for neural-related pathways and immune cells, particularly neutrophils and monocytes. Patient stratification identified two distinct subtypes within the MASLD spectrum, with subtype 2 exhibiting enhanced activity in neural-related pathways. Mendelian randomization analysis identified PLEKHA5 as a candidate causal gene for MASLD, suggesting a potential role in neural mechanisms (SEL1L3 showed a suggestive association, P = 0.0413). Collectively, this hypothesis-generating bioinformatics study elucidates distinct characteristics of cholangiocyte subpopulations in MASH, revealing neural pathway alterations that may contribute to disease pathogenesis and providing a foundation for future investigation into cholangiocyte-related mechanisms in MASLD.

articles.title: Comparison of low volume versus high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in people receiving haemodialysis: a randomized non-inferiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colonoscopy in chronic kidney disease patients undergoing haemodialysis is crucial. Some concerns have been raised about the use of oral bowel cleansing agents for colonoscopy. We compared the efficacy, safety and tolerability of a low volume versus a high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in such patients.

METHODS: A multicentre, parallel-arm, randomized, phase IV trial with 15% non-inferiority margin was conducted. Eligible subjects were allocated to either the low volume (2 L) or high-volume (4 L) bowel preparation group in 1:1 ratio. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with adequate bowel cleansing. Secondary outcomes were polyp/adenoma detection rate (PDR/ADR), cecal intubation rate, patient tolerability/compliance and adverse events.

RESULTS: Sixty-nine patients were randomized in four centres, 35 to low and 34 to high-volume groups. No difference in caecal intubation rate, in patients with adequate preparation, was observed (96.7% vs 100%, p = 1). As per-protocol, adequate bowel preparation was achieved in the 69.7 and 63.0% of low and high-volume groups, respectively (p = 0.58). The mean Boston Bowel Preparation Scale was similar in the two groups (5.6 ± 2.4vs 5.4 ± 2.4, p = 0.51). The PDR was 39.4% in low volume and 37.0% in high volume (p = 1). No differences in adverse events were observed. No emergency dialysis sessions were required. Serum creatinine levels remained stable before and after preparation in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Optimal cleansing was difficult to obtain in haemodialysis patients. Both low and high-volume preparations were equally effective and safe. The small sample size is a limit underpowering our research. Larger studies are, therefore, required. Trial registration number The trial was approved by the Central ethic committee (protocol approval no. 0089971/23/11/2020) and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04709770.

articles.title: Development of a Simple Clinical Risk Score for Mortality Prediction in Neonatal Gram-Negative Sepsis: Authors' Reply.
Monoclonal Antibodies for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Infants and Children: An Updated Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Motivated by the emergence of a long-acting monoclonal antibody (clesrovimab), the availability of data from the complete MELODY trial cohort, and results from a large randomized trial (HARMONIE), we updated our prior network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants.

METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials that examined the efficacy and safety of RSV infection prophylaxis with clesrovimab, motavizumab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, and suptavumab versus one another or placebo or no prophylaxis in infants. We performed a frequentist framework random-effects network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Developments and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence.

RESULTS: Eighteen trials enrolling 33,283 infants were included. Clesrovimab (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.02-0.37, moderate certainty), motavizumab (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.07-0.19, moderate certainty), and nirsevimab (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.34; moderate certainty) were associated with reductions in the rate of severe respiratory syncytial virus infection. Nirsevimab, motavizumab, clesrovimab, and intramuscular palivizumab were associated with reductions in RSV infection, and several agents were also associated with reduced hospitalization. Motavizumab and nirsevimab, and clesrovimab were associated with reductions in broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes. Motavizumab reduced both mechanical ventilation use and intensive care unit admission. No significant differences were found in all-cause mortality and drug-related or serious adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: This updated network meta-analysis confirmed that the effectiveness and safety of clesrovimab were comparable to those of established monoclonal antibodies. Motavizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab showed benefits for broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes.

articles.title: Circadian disruption exacerbates alcohol-induced cardiac injury through impaired cellular quality control and increased cardiomyocyte death.
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms orchestrate 24-h oscillations in physiology and gene expression in many tissues, including the heart. Disruptions to these rhythms have been linked to increased cardiovascular risk and impaired cellular homeostasis. However, the extent to which circadian disruption influences cardiac responses to environmental stressors such as alcohol, remains poorly understood. Herein, we performed RNA-sequencing and transcriptomic analysis on hearts from C57BL/6 J mice exposed to alcohol for ten weeks and collected at two distinct circadian time points (Zeitgeber Time (ZT)8 and ZT20). Principal component analysis and differential expression profiling revealed robust time-of-day-dependent transcriptional programs induced by alcohol, with significant enrichment of pathways governing mitochondrial quality control, autophagy/mitophagy, ferroptosis, and key signaling nodes (FOXO, MAPK, AMPK, mTOR, HIF, Hippo). To investigate the impact of circadian disruption, we compared alcohol-challenged hearts from circadian disrupted and control mice. Circadian disruption markedly altered transcriptional profiles and pathways associated with cardiomyopathy and insulin resistance, while further amplifying dysregulation of quality control and stress signaling networks. At the cellular level, alcohol exposure reduced autophagosome formation in isolated adult cardiomyocytes and this decrease was exacerbated by circadian disruption. Further, circadian disruption impaired mitochondrial quality control by reducing ATP production, altering mitophagy, and mitochondrial dynamics, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction. These alterations were accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and elevated apoptotic cell death compared with either condition alone. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that circadian disruption exacerbates alcohol-induced molecular and cellular cardiac injury by compromising cellular quality control processes, mitochondrial integrity, and cell survival pathways. These findings identify mechanisms that may contribute to increased susceptibility to alcohol-induced cardiac dysfunction and may offer novel approaches to mitigate alcohol-related cardiac injury in shift-workers or individuals with disrupted circadian rhythms.

articles.title: Bioethical Deliberation in Gestational Diabetes Management: Integrating Diego Gracia's Model into Clinical Ethics Consultation and Institutional Policy.
articles.journal: HEC forum : an interdisciplinary journal on hospitals' ethical and legal issues
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) sits at the intersection of maternal bodily integrity, fetal risk mitigation, and healthcare equity, and rigid guideline enforcement can trigger bedside conflicts and institutional friction. This article examines GDM management through the deliberative model of the Spanish physician and philosopher Diego Gracia, influential in Southern Europe and Latin America but less familiar in North America, which separates moral duties into Level I (Non-Maleficence and Justice) and Level II (Autonomy and Beneficence). We explain why we start from Gracia rather than from Beauchamp and Childress: his model couples a defeasible ordering of duties with an explicit deliberative procedure that institutions can teach and document. We then argue against a misreading of the model in perinatal care that places fetal protection at Level I and maternal decision-making at Level II. Maternal bodily integrity and informed refusal also engage Level I non-maleficence duties, so bedside conflicts are better understood as clashes between two Level I obligations. We extend this reframing by translating Gracia's deliberative steps into a consultation protocol for Healthcare Ethics Committees (HECs), by using international variation in metformin's regulatory standing to show that pharmacological choice involves value judgments, and by treating access to glucose self-monitoring supplies as a matter of distributive justice. A hypothetical, composite vignette illustrates the protocol. The proposals are conceptual and untested; we suggest that structured deliberation may help institutions honor maternal self-determination without abandoning fetal interests.

articles.title: Leukotriene inhibitors in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review of animal studies.
articles.abstract: Current disease-modifying therapies for multiple sclerosis (MS) primarily target adaptive immunity but often fail to halt neurodegeneration or promote myelin repair. Leukotriene pathway inhibitors, established in the management of asthma, possess anti-inflammatory and potentially neuroprotective properties. Following the PRISMA 2020 recommendations, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus. Eligible studies included preclinical investigations of leukotriene inhibitors in MS animal models and risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE's risk of bias tool for animal studies. Five studies met the inclusion criteria, reported that inhibition of leukotriene B4 (LTB4) or cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 (CysLT1) attenuated clinical severity in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and cuprizone-induced demyelination models. Mechanistically, the included preclinical studies suggest that leukotriene inhibitors may influence several pathways potentially relevant to MS pathophysiology, including T helper 17 (Th17) cell differentiation, M1-like microglial polarization, and oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC) differentiation. In addition, targeted central nervous system (CNS) delivery using engineered exosomes appeared to enhance the observed remyelination effects. Leukotriene inhibition may exert pleiotropic effects across both peripheral immune responses and the CNS microenvironment. Although these mechanistic observations provide biological plausibility for further investigation of these agents as potential repurposed therapies for MS, particularly in the context of remyelination and neuroinflammation, they remain based on preclinical evidence and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. Well-designed clinical studies are required to determine whether these experimental effects translate into clinically meaningful therapeutic benefits in patients with MS.

articles.title: Battling the Bottleneck: Evaluating Autism Diagnostic Training in Primary Care.
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The study purpose was to implement and evaluate the STAT™ (Screening Tool for Autism in Toddlers & Young Children 24-36 months old) for primary care providers (PCPs) in a Wisconsin, USA, cohort. It examined the impacts of the training and learning community on knowledge, attitudes, and change in self-reported provider confidence in autism diagnosis.

METHODS: This study evaluated the implementation of a developmental assessment training program, for PCPs, using the STAT, followed by a year-long autism learning community involving monthly case-based discussions and knowledge exchange. English-speaking PCPs were assessed pre- and post-training on knowledge, screening and diagnostic practices, attitudes toward autism diagnosis in primary care, and comfort with autism identification and management. Descriptive statistics summarized baseline characteristics and practices. Paired-samples t-tests were used to evaluate pre- to post-training changes in provider comfort.

RESULTS: Baseline findings (n=23) PCPs indicated limited use of autism-specific screening and diagnostic tools among PCPs. Among PCPs with matched pre- and post-training data (n = 11), significant improvements were observed across multiple domains of provider comfort identifying autism risk, distinguishing autism from other developmental conditions, making formal diagnoses, and providing diagnostic feedback. Improvements in care coordination domains, such as referral practices and mental health service linkage, were more limited.

CONCLUSIONS: STAT training was associated with meaningful improvements in provider confidence, particularly in autism identification and diagnostic decision-making within primary care settings. Training PCPs to diagnose autism in young children with obvious signs, has the potential to reduce diagnostic delays and improve access to early intervention.

articles.title: C/EBPβ Drives Ischemia-Induced Microglial Inflammatory Reprogramming Through Transcriptional Activation of ATF3 and Exacerbates Brain Injury.
articles.abstract: Microglial activation contributes substantially to secondary brain injury after ischemic stroke, but the transcriptional mechanisms governing this response remain poorly defined. Here, we identified CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ) as a key regulator of ischemia-induced microglial inflammation. RNA sequencing of microglia isolated from mice subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming, characterized by activation of inflammatory pathways, including chemokine, TNF, IL-17, and efferocytosis signaling, as well as cell-cycle programs, together with suppression of homeostatic processes involved in synaptic regulation and neuronal support. Network analysis identified Cebpb as a highly connected hub across multiple inflammatory pathways. C/EBPβ expression was markedly increased in peri-infarct microglia after tMCAO and in primary microglia exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Microglia-selective Cebpb knockdown reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, CCL2, and CD16 expression, increased IL-4, IL-13, and ARG1 expression, and attenuated ischemia-induced morphological remodeling. Consistent effects were observed in primary microglia and BV2 cells, supporting a central role for C/EBPβ in microglial pro-inflammatory activation under ischemic conditions. Mechanistically, C/EBPβ directly bound the Atf3 promoter and activated its transcription, while ATF3 partially mediated C/EBPβ-dependent Il1b induction. In vivo, microglial Cebpb knockdown reduced acute ischemic lesion volume, neuronal apoptosis in the striatum and cortex, and long-term cerebral atrophy. These histopathological improvements were accompanied by sustained recovery of neurological function, somatosensory performance, motor coordination, recognition memory, and spatial learning and memory. Collectively, these findings establish the C/EBPβ-ATF3 axis as a transcriptional pathway that promotes microglial inflammation and secondary neuronal injury after cerebral ischemia. Targeting microglial C/EBPβ may therefore limit ischemic brain damage and improve long-term neurological recovery after stroke.

articles.title: miR‑18a‑5p Serves as a Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarker and Attenuates Hypoxia‑Induced Cardiac Microvascular Endothelial Injury by Targeting the HIF1A/NF‑κB Pathway in Chronic Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a severe end-stage cardiovascular syndrome with high mortality and poor prognosis. This study aimed to investigate the expression, diagnostic, and prognostic value of serum miR-18a-5p in CHF patients and to explore its molecular mechanism in regulating hypoxia-induced injury.

METHODS: A total of 125 CHF patients and 125 healthy controls were enrolled. The expression of miR-18a-5p was detected by RT-qPCR. The diagnostic efficacy was evaluated by the ROC curve. The prognostic value was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariate Cox regression. Human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMECs) were used to establish a hypoxic injury model. Cell viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokines were measured by CCK-8, flow cytometry, and ELISA. The targeting relationship between miR-18a-5p and HIF1A was verified by a dual-luciferase reporter assay. The expression of apoptosis, fibrosis, and NF-κB pathway proteins was detected by RT-qPCR and Western blot.

RESULTS: In patients with CHF, circulating miR‑18a‑5p was markedly downregulated, exhibiting a diagnostic AUC value of 0.874. Diminished miR‑18a‑5p expression was closely linked to decreased LVEF, increased levels of BNP and cTnI, higher NYHA classification, and a poorer long‑term prognosis. miR-18a-5p was a protective factor for CHF. In vitro, overexpression of miR-18a-5p enhanced cell viability, inhibited apoptosis, reduced the secretion of pro-inflammatory factors, and downregulated collagen I, collagen III, and α-SMA expression in hypoxic hCMECs. miR-18a-5p targeted HIF1A 3'UTR and negatively regulated HIF1A/NF-κB signaling. Overexpression of HIF1A reversed the protective effects of miR-18a-5p.

CONCLUSION: miR-18a-5p attenuates hypoxia-induced inflammation, apoptosis, and fibrosis by targeting the HIF1A/NF-κB pathway. Circulating miR-18a-5p therefore holds promising clinical prospects as a non-invasive serum biomarker for CHF diagnosis and risk stratification. Upregulation of miR-18a-5p provides a potential molecular strategy for preventing hypoxia-mediated cardiac microvascular remodeling in chronic heart failure.

articles.title: A Beginner's Guide to Cardiac Optical Mapping.
articles.abstract: Optical mapping is a high spatiotemporal resolution imaging technique used to study cardiac electrophysiology by recording fluorescent signals that correspond to changes in transmembrane potential, intracellular calcium, and metabolic activity. This review provides a comprehensive guide for beginners, covering the fundamentals of optical mapping system components, including dye selection, optical filters and mirrors, camera specifications, and system configurations. A range of tissue preparations, from single cells to whole hearts, is described, with attention to how preparation type affects experimental design, perfusion methods, and system setup. Pharmacological and computational strategies to reduce motion artifacts are discussed. Electrical stimulation protocols, such as pacing and restitution mapping, are described in the context of arrhythmia induction and rate dependent electrophysiological properties. Technical considerations including system maintenance and troubleshooting are also addressed. Finally, the review outlines current limitations, including dye cytotoxicity, tissue viability, and photobleaching, and explores future directions such as genetically encoded indicators and oxygen-enriched perfusates. This guide aims to equip new users with the foundational knowledge needed to design, perform, and interpret optical mapping experiments.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of headache in the patients with Neuro-Behçet's disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Behçet's disease (BD) is a chronic vascular-inflammatory condition of unknown pathogenesis presenting with mucocutaneous lesions, attacks of uveitis that may lead to blindness, and involvement of many systems including vascular, musculo-skeletal system and the gastrointestinal tract.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to examine the frequency of various forms of headache in patients diagnosed with BD, the characteristics of headache in BD, the characteristics of attacks, and the relationship between the disease and headache attacks.

METHODS: A total of 35 patients with Neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) aged ≥ 18 years, who were followed at the Department of Neurology of XX University between 2021 and 2026, were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were evaluated for demographic characteristics, headache characteristics and severity, imaging studies, cerebrospinal fluid findings, relationship to attacks, and acute and chronic treatment.

RESULTS: The most common complaint was headache. It was observed that headache could be of primary type as migraine or tension-type headache or secondary headache due to neurological involvement. Headache in NBD was frequently observed during BD attacks (aphthosis and/or uveitis) or in temporal proximity to these attacks, suggesting a possible association with disease activity.

CONCLUSION: Headache in NBD is heterogeneous and cannot be fully explained by primary headache syndromes alone; a substantial proportion is associated with disease activity and neurological involvement. The temporal association observed between headache and disease attacks may indicate an association between headache and disease activity. Therefore, in patients presenting with headache, NBD involvement should also be considered.

articles.title: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with survival outcomes via a deep survival learner.
articles.abstract: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects in survival settings is complicated by right censoring as well as the time-varying nature of the estimand. While the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) provides a natural target, most existing approaches focus on a single prespecified time point and do not account for temporal trajectory, leading to instability in estimation. We propose a deep survival learner (DSL) for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects with right-censored outcomes. The method is based on a doubly robust pseudo-outcome whose conditional expectation identifies time-specific CATEs under standard assumptions. This construction remains unbiased if either the outcome model or the treatment assignment model is correctly specified, when properly accounting for censoring. To estimate CATEs over a clinically relevant time spectrum, DSL employs a multi-output deep neural network with shared representations, enabling joint estimation of treatment effect trajectories. From a theoretical perspective, we derive error bounds for both pointwise and joint estimation over time. We show that joint estimation can leverage temporal structure to control estimation error without incurring much additional approximation cost under smoothness conditions, leading to improved stability relative to separate estimation. Cross-fitting is incorporated to reduce overfitting and mitigate bias arising from flexible nuisance estimation. Simulation studies demonstrate favorable finite-sample performance, particularly under nuisance model misspecification. Applied to the Boston Lung Cancer Study, DSL reveals heterogeneity in the effects of perioperative chemotherapy across patient characteristics and over time.

articles.title: Recurrent Acute Liver Failure and Early Chronic Liver Disease in an Infant with CALFAN Syndrome.
Improved diffusion tensor parametric maps in the brain from reduced-direction acquisitions using a deep learning approach.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study implements and evaluates a deep learning approach to enhance FA, MD, AD, and RD maps derived from 16-direction DTI to approximate corresponding maps derived from 32-direction DTI, with the aim of reducing acquisition time while maintaining quantitative accuracy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A modified 8-layer 3D convolutional neural network was trained using scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions as input and corresponding 32-direction maps as reference targets. Model performance was evaluated on an independently acquired evaluation cohort (n=33) using PSNR, %NRMSE, SSIM, Bland-Altman analysis, and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), with BM4D and AONLM as comparators.

RESULTS: The DL model reduced noise and improved PSNR, %NRMSE, and SSIM compared with raw ND16, BM4D, and AONLM (p < 0.05). DL-derived FA, MD, and AD showed the smallest deviations from the ND32 reference among the evaluated methods, although statistically significant mean differences remained. TBSS showed localized differences for FA and AD, but no significant differences for MD or RD (p > 0.05).

DISCUSSION: The proposed map-domain DL approach improved scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions while reducing diffusion acquisition time by approximately 1.8-fold. The findings demonstrate improved agreement with 32-direction reference maps, while remaining quantitative differences and generalizability require further validation.

articles.title: Esophageal resonance Raman spectroscopy tracks mixed venous oxygenation in experimental shock and hypoxemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) reflects the balance between systemic oxygen delivery and consumption and is widely used as an indicator of tissue oxygenation in critically ill patients. However, its measurement requires invasive venous access. We evaluated whether a customized probe applied to the esophageal mucosa could provide a continuous measurement of regional capillary hemoglobin oxygen saturation (SEsO2) that tracks changes in mixed venous oxygen saturation for early detection of experimental shock with minimal invasiveness.

METHODS: A miniaturized 405 nm resonance Raman spectroscopy (RRS) probe was developed to quantify esophageal regional capillary hemoglobin saturation (SEsO2) based on spectral decomposition of oxy- and deoxy-hemoglobin Raman peaks. Two rat models were investigated: progressive hemorrhage (n = 12) and graded hypoxia (n = 9). At each stage, SvO2, SEsO2, arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2), and serum lactate were measured. Tracking ability and diagnostic accuracy compared to SvO2 and transabdominal near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models (animal random intercepts), (cluster-bootstrapped) receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analyses, and Pearson correlation.

RESULTS: In both models, baseline SEsO2 was ~20% higher than SvO2, consistent with a regional capillary measurement distinct from mixed venous blood. In hemorrhage, LME showed SEsO2 was positively associated with SvO2 (β = 0.53, 95% CI 0.43-0.62; p < 0.0001) and inversely associated with lactate (β = -0.15, 95% CI -0.18 to -0.12; p < 0.0001). In ROC analysis, SEsO2 discriminated SvO2 < 40% with AUC 0.98 (95% CI 0.95-1.00). For transabdominal NIRS, the AUC was 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.95). During graded hypoxia, SEsO2 was also positively associated with SvO2 (β = 0.51, 95% CI 0.43-0.60; p < 0.0001) and inversely associated with lactate (β = -0.11, 95% CI -0.13 to -0.09; p < 0.0001). Discrimination of SEsO2 for SvO2 < 40% was AUC 0.92 (95% CI 0.82-1.00). Transabdominal NIRS demonstrated discrimination with high uncertainty (AUC 0.56, 95% CI 0.23-1.00).

CONCLUSIONS: Esophageal RRS enables molecularly specific measurement of regional capillary hemoglobin oxygen saturation and thereby tracks SvO2 across distinct experimental shock paradigms. These preclinical findings support further investigation of esophageal RRS as a potential minimally invasive monitoring approach for detection of systemic oxygen imbalance.

articles.title: A Meta-Analysis on Outcomes of Zanidatamab Plus Chemotherapy in Patients with Advanced HER2-positive Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zanidatamab is a novel HER2-targeted antibody that binds to two non-overlapping extracellular domains of the HER2 receptor. Early-phase trials have shown clinical benefit of first-line Zanidatamab in patients with advanced HER2-positive esophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA). We performed a meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of zanidatamab in this patient population.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, ASCO, and ESMO databases for studies examining zanidatamab as first-line treatment in patients with HER2-positive advanced GEA. Outcomes of interest included progression-free survival (PFS); objective response rate (ORR); disease control rate (DCR); duration of response (DOR); and incidence of adverse events (AEs). Analyses were presented as median or proportions in percentages with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Random-effect models were used for analysis, which were carried out using R software (v4.5.2).

RESULTS: Three clinical trials involving 685 patients with advanced HER2-positive GEA treated with zanidatamab in combination with chemotherapy and/or tislelizumab were included. Overall, the reconstructed pooled median OS was 26.05 months (95% CI: 23.60-30.04), while the pooled median PFS was 12.61 months (95% CI: 11.05-14.60). The pooled ORR was 70% (95% CI, 67-74), DCR was 96% (95% CI, 78-100), and median DOR was 17.11 months (95% CI, 13.07-22.40). Treatment-related diarrhea leading to dose reduction was observed in 16% (95% CI, 1%-75%) of patients. Treatment discontinuation due to any cause rate was 20% (95% CI, 3%-44%). Serious treatment-emergent AEs occurred in 66% (95% CI, 50%-81%) of patients. Common any-grade AEs included diarrhea (89%; 95% CI, 75%-98%), nausea (60%; 95% CI, 45%-74%), and infusion-related reactions (30%; 95% CI, 19%-43%). Grade ≥ 3 diarrhea, nausea, and treatment-related AEs rates were as follows: 26% (95% CI, 19%-34%), 5% (95% CI, 2%-13%), and 65% (95% CI, 58%-71%), respectively. Other important AEs include immune-mediated AEs (25% incidence rate), left ventricular dysfunction (6% incidence rate), and non-infectious pulmonary toxicity (4% incidence rate).

CONCLUSIONS: Our pooled analyses suggest that zanidatamab exhibits meaningful activity as first-line treatment of advanced HER2-positive GEA. Yet, concerning toxicity rates were also consistently reported across studies. Future randomized studies are needed to further explore its activity and safety profile in this population.

articles.title: Establishment of a Diet-Induced Systemic Metabolic SyndromeModel Reveals Early Renal Alterations and the Nephroprotective Potential of Three Jabuticaba (Myrciaria cauliflora) Formulations.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome is a progressive disorder associated with metabolic dysregulation, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and increased risk of chronic kidney disease. The kidney is an early target of metabolic imbalance, developing structural alterations before the establishment of advanced renal dysfunction. Jabuticaba (Myrciaria cauliflora), a Brazilian berry rich in phenolic compounds, has emerged as a promising functional food, and technological strategies such as microencapsulation may improve the stability and potential biological effects of its bioactive compounds. This study evaluated the effects of three jabuticaba formulations-freeze-dried whole fruit, freeze-dried peel, and microencapsulated peel extract-on renal morphology, relative elemental composition, and oxidative status in mice subjected to a high-fat, high-fructose (HFHF) diet. Fifty male C57BL/6 mice were allocated into five groups (n = 10): Control, HFHF, HFWF (HFHF + whole fruit), HFJP (HFHF + peel), and HFME (HFHF + microencapsulated peel extract). After six weeks of metabolic challenge, jabuticaba was introduced while maintaining the HFHF diet for an additional six weeks. At the end of the 12-week experimental period, kidneys were collected for morphometric, histopathological, elemental, and oxidative analyses. The HFHF diet induced early renal alterations characterized by increased vascular proportion, reduced tubular proportion, vascular congestion, tubular vacuolization, and inflammatory cell infiltration, indicating early renal structural changes associated with HFHF-induced metabolic dysfunction. Jabuticaba addition produced formulation-dependent effects on renal morphology, with the microencapsulated peel extract showing the most consistent histological preservation. The HFHF diet also altered the renal elemental profile, increasing the relative proportions of calcium and manganese and reducing sodium compared with Control animals. Among the Jabuticaba groups, HFWF shifted calcium and sodium proportions toward Control values, whereas HFJP and HFME maintained the HFHF-associated pattern for these elements. For manganese, HFJP and HFME showed intermediate values that did not differ significantly from either Control or HFHF animals. No significant differences were observed among groups for oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde, protein carbonyls, nitric oxide, and FRAP) or antioxidant enzymes (catalase, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione S-transferase), indicating that the observed morphological and elemental disturbances were not accompanied by detectable changes in renal oxidative stress biomarkers or antioxidant defenses. Thus, the effects associated with jabuticaba should not be interpreted as primarily antioxidant-mediated. These findings indicate that Myrciaria cauliflora addition in HFHF diet was associated mainly with preservation of renal histological architecture and modulation of the relative elemental profile in a formulation-dependent manner, with the microencapsulated peel extract showing the most consistent histological effects. The results highlight the potential of jabuticaba peel valorization and microencapsulation technology as strategies for developing functional ingredients aimed at preserving renal tissue during early metabolic dysfunction, although further functional and molecular studies are required to confirm nephroprotective effects.

articles.title: Association of immune checkpoint-related polymorphisms in PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 genes with susceptibility to genitourinary cancer: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This meta-analysis explored the association of immune checkpoint-related single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in programmed death-1 (PD-1), programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1), and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen-4 (CTLA-4) genes with susceptibility to various genitourinary (GU) cancers, including urothelial carcinoma (UC), renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and prostate cancer (PCa). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for case-control studies from inception to April 2026. Six SNPs, including PD-1 (rs2227981), PD-L1 (rs4143815), and CTLA-4 (rs3087243, rs231775, rs5742909, and rs11571302), were examined. The relationships between the SNPs and cancer susceptibility were evaluated using pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for dominant, recessive, and allele models. This study considered 16 case-control studies. PD-L1 rs4143815 was associated with a significantly decreased risk of UC in Asian populations under the dominant model (CC + CG vs. GG: OR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.14-0.87). CTLA-4 rs5742909 polymorphism was associated with an increased risk of GU cancer in dominant model (TT + TC vs. CC: OR = 1.41, 95% CI = 1.11-1.80) and allele model (T vs. C: OR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.05-1.72). A significantly increased risk of UC was further identified among Asian population in the dominant model (OR = 1.56, 95% CI = 1.04-2.34). No significant associations were observed for the other SNPs. In conclusion, specific polymorphisms in immune checkpoint-related genes, particularly PD-L1 rs4143815 and CTLA-4 rs5742909, are associated with susceptibility to GU cancer in Asian populations.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic implications of mitoxyperilysis: a spatially gated mitochondria-dependent lytic cell death.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Programmed cell death (PCD) has expanded to more than ten diverse lytic modalities such as pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, and disulfidptosis. In 2025, Wang et al. reported in Cell a previously unrecognized form of lytic cell death, termed mitoxyperilysis, in which plasma membrane rupture is driven not by canonical pore-forming or membrane-disrupting enzymatic effectors, but by mitochondria-mediated oxidative injury localized to the cell periphery. This process is initiated by the synergistic combination of innate immune activation and metabolic disruption, referred to as IIAMD, which induces mitochondrial oxidative damage and promotes the sustained retention of injured mitochondria at the plasma membrane, a preceding state termed mitoxyperiosis. Mechanistically, mTORC2, particularly through its defining subunit RICTOR, functions as a central regulatory switch that licenses the transition from tolerated oxidative stress to lethal membrane rupture. By suppressing RhoA-dependent actin remodeling and lamellipodia formation, mTORC2 prevents the spatial clearance of damaged mitochondria from the cell cortex, thereby allowing locally concentrated oxidative stress to overwhelm membrane repair and antioxidant defenses. This two-step framework establishes the concept of spatial licensing in oxidative cell death, emphasizing that lethality depends not only on the amount of reactive oxygen species, but also on their subcellular topology. However, mitoxyperilysis has not yet been implicated in any human disease on the basis of direct evidence. In this review, we summarize the emerging mechanisms of mitoxyperilysis, compare it with established lytic death pathways, and discuss its potential relevance to inflammatory disease, sepsis, ischemic injury, and cancer, as well as therapeutic strategies targeting mTORC2, RhoA signaling, and mitochondrial protection.

articles.title: Uniportal versus Multiportal Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy in Esophageal Cancer: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive esophagectomy has become the preferred surgical approach for esophageal cancer, with uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) emerging as a potential refinement over conventional multiportal VATS (mVATS). However, comparative evidence remains limited to small single-centre studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate perioperative and safety outcomes of uVATS versus mVATS in patients undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and CNKI from inception through April 2026. Studies directly comparing uVATS with mVATS in adults undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy were eligible. Binary outcomes were pooled as odds ratios and continuous outcomes as mean differences under REML random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework.

RESULTS: Nine studies comparing uVATS and mVATS were included. uVATS was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain on day one (MD - 2.10, 95% CI - 3.63 to - 0.57; I² = 99.3%), reduced postoperative pneumonia (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.76; I² = 43.5%), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 2.13 days, 95% CI - 3.64 to - 0.63; I² = 96.8%). No significant differences were observed between approaches for anastomotic leakage (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.61-2.09), overall complications (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.47-1.32), recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.43-1.85), perioperative mortality (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.16-1.81), intraoperative blood loss, or total operative time.

CONCLUSION: UVATS esophagectomy appears to be a feasible and safe alternative to mVATS, with potential advantages in postoperative pain, pulmonary morbidity, and hospital stay while maintaining comparable perioperative safety. The evidence base remains limited by high heterogeneity and predominance of observational studies. Multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term oncologic follow-up are needed to consolidate these findings.

articles.title: Heparin-binding protein aggravates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by inhibiting the PERK-Nrf2-HO-1 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Sepsis, a systemic inflammatory response disorder triggered by infection, often leads to multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SI-ALI) is among the most common complications. Heparin-binding protein (HBP), a major inflammatory mediator, has been demonstrated to induce vascular permeability and inflammation. Nevertheless, the mechanism by which HBP functions in sepsis-induced lung injury remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the role of HBP in sepsis-induced lung injury. A sepsis mouse model was established via cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), followed by HBP blockade using heparin. Serum inflammatory cytokine levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Neutrophil infiltration was assessed by myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity. Lung tissue pathology was evaluated using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) and Masson staining. Levels of ferrous iron (Fe2+), malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) in lung tissue lysates were quantified using commercial assay kits. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) expression was examined by immunohistochemistry. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in lung tissues were measured using dihydroethidium (DHE) fluorescence probes. Western blot was performed to analyze the protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase-nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2-heme oxygenase-1 (PERK-Nrf2-HO-1) signaling pathway. Additionally, an in vitro sepsis cell model was established by treating murine lung epithelial (MLE-12) cells with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to further validate HBP's role. HBP expression was significantly upregulated in the lung tissues of CLP mice. Pharmacological blockade of HBP reduced serum inflammatory cytokine levels, alleviated neutrophil infiltration and lung pathological injury, and attenuated ferroptosis-related alterations in septic lung tissues. HBP blockade was associated with enhanced activation of the PERK-Nrf2-HO-1 signaling pathway. Knockdown of PERK, Nrf2 or HO-1 partially abrogated the protective effects of HBP blockade against SI-ALI and ferroptosis phenotypes. Furthermore, in vitro experiments showed that HO-1 overexpression attenuated the exacerbating effect of HBP on LPS-induced ferroptosis in MLE-12 cells. The findings suggest that HBP may contribute to the progression of sepsis-induced lung injury, at least in part, by promoting ferroptosis through inhibiting the activation of the PERK-Nrf2-HO-1 signaling pathway.

articles.title: Ecological assessment of green spaces: a systematic review of parameters and a proposed seven-category classification framework.
articles.abstract: Green spaces are ecologically significant landscapes that provide critical ecosystem services across diverse environmental and spatial contexts. Despite an expanding body of research, the parameters employed for ecological assessment of green spaces remain fragmented across disciplines with no unified framework for their classification. This study addresses this gap through a systematic literature review of studies indexed in Web of Science and Scopus databases, encompassing 113 publications in the fields of ecology and environmental science. The review systematically examines assessment contexts, spatial typologies, research domains, and ecological assessment parameters. Two primary assessment contexts are identified: urban green spaces and non-urban green spaces, representing fundamentally different spatial scales, management regimes, and ecological characteristics. Seven research themes are identified: spatio-temporal dynamics, ecosystem services, health and well-being, landscape characteristics, thermal environment, mapping and indexing, and ecological assessment. Parameters employed in different assessments are identified and those parameters which are applied in ecological assessment are organized into seven distinct categories: vegetation condition, landscape integrity, hydrological regulation, anthropogenic pressure, terrain-based factors, thermal and surface stress, and LULC dynamics. This seven-category framework provides a structured and replicable basis for assessing the ecological quality of green spaces across spatial scales and environmental settings, supporting conservation prioritization and evidence-based resource allocation.

articles.title: Cell-free DNA methylation markers in the diagnosis of hepatitis B virus-related- hepatocellular carcinoma: a review.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its prognosis largely depends on detection at an early, potentially curable stage. However, current surveillance strategies based on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) have limited sensitivity, highlighting the need for more accurate and non-invasive biomarkers. This review examines the emerging role of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation analysis as a liquid biopsy approach for the early detection and surveillance of HBV-HCC. Aberrant DNA methylation is a major epigenetic event in hepatocarcinogenesis, contributing to the silencing of tumor suppressor genes, while the HBV X protein can further promote methylation dysregulation through its interactions with DNA methyltransferases. Clinically, specific cfDNA methylation markers and multi-feature panels have demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for HCC detection. More complex multi-feature cfDNA models integrating methylation with additional fragmentomic features have achieved up to 95.42% sensitivity and 97.67% specificity (AUC = 0.997) for differentiating HCC from liver cirrhosis, while maintaining a high sensitivity of 90.0% for early-stage HCC detection. In specific cohorts, methylation-based approaches have complemented AFP, detecting nearly 75% of early malignancies missed by AFP alone and increasing the AUC of combined predictive model from 0.87 to 0.90.
