Furthermore, combined mutation-methylation assays that concurrently profile genetic mutations and hypermethylation patterns have achieved validation AUC values as high as 0.93. Overall, cfDNA methylation-based approaches exhibit promising diagnostic performance compared with conventional biomarkers in specific cohorts. However, prospective validation and direct head-to-head comparisons with existing surveillance strategies are still required before their clinical utility can be established.

articles.title: Umbrella review of low-level light therapy: evidence across clinical conditions.
articles.abstract: Low-level light therapy (LLLT) and photobiomodulation (PBM) have been studied in diverse clinical fields. Although numerous systematic reviews have been published, their findings are fragmented and inconsistent. This umbrella review of systematic reviews aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness and safety of LLLT across various clinical conditions. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to February 24, 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses of LLLT in humans. Data on clinical conditions, intervention characteristics, overall direction of conclusions, and adverse events were extracted. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. A total of 100 systematic reviews were included, representing 1,164 primary-study occurrences and 790 unique eligible primary studies. Oral and dental conditions accounted for the largest evidence base (53 reviews), followed by musculoskeletal disorders (22 reviews), oncology-related complications (8 reviews), and wound and lymphatic conditions (8 reviews). Overall, 62 reviews reached conclusions favoring the evaluated intervention, 34 reported neutral or mixed conclusions, and 4 had unclear conclusions. The highest proportion of favorable conclusions was observed for oncology-related complications. Of the 100 reviews, 11 reported one or more adverse events or side effects, 32 explicitly reported no adverse events, and 57 did not provide adverse-event information. Most reviews received low (30.0%) or critically low (60.0%) overall confidence ratings using AMSTAR 2. The review literature suggests potential clinical benefit of LLLT in selected indications, particularly oncology-related complications such as oral mucositis. However, these descriptive patterns do not establish treatment efficacy or the certainty of the underlying evidence. Heterogeneity in treatment parameters, generally low methodological confidence, and incomplete adverse-event reporting limit interpretation and preclude firm conclusions about safety.

articles.title: Retatrutide treatment in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats: renal inflammatory cytokines, HIF‑1α expression, and histopathological injury profile.
articles.abstract: This study investigated whether Retatrutide, a triple incretin agonist, attenuates early diabetes-associated renal injury in a streptozotocin-induced rat model, and whether any protective effect is mediated through modulation of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α) and HIF-1α gene expression in kidney tissue. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were divided into four groups: control, STZ-induced diabetic, STZ plus Retatrutide, and Retatrutide alone. Diabetes was induced via a single intraperitoneal STZ injection; Retatrutide was administered subcutaneously for 21 days at a dose adapted from prior metabolic studies. Renal tissue underwent ELISA for interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), quantitative real-time PCR for HIF-1α expression, and semi-quantitative histopathological scoring of cortical and medullary parameters including haemorrhage, tubular dilatation, inflammatory cell infiltration, tubular vacuolisation, interstitial fibrosis, and intraluminal debris. STZ-induced rats exhibited significantly elevated cortical and medullary histopathological scores and increased renal IL-1β levels relative to controls, confirming successful early injury induction. Retatrutide did not produce statistically significant histopathological protection, although STZ plus Retatrutide animals showed consistently lower damage scores than STZ-only animals, corresponding to large standardised effects (Cliff's δ = 0.90 in the cortex and 0.85 in the medulla) that could not be confirmed under family-wise error correction. HIF-1α expression was highest in the untreated diabetic group and was significantly lower in Retatrutide-treated diabetic animals (S vs. SR, p = 0.020), whereas Retatrutide alone did not alter expression relative to controls. TNF-α did not differ significantly in any pairwise comparison; levels in Retatrutide-treated diabetic animals were nonetheless comparable to controls (g* = 0.03). Retatrutide selectively modulated HIF-1α transcriptional levels in the acute STZ model without statistically confirmed histopathological renoprotection, and without evidence of intrinsic renal toxicity. Because the acute STZ model reflects insulin-deficient rather than T2DM-like disease, the model itself is a critical limitation; chronic type 2 diabetes models, together with longer treatment durations and refined dosing regimens, are required to determine whether the observed early molecular effects translate into structural renal benefit.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted conversion of unicompartmental to total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Conversion of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) presents technical challenges due to bone loss and altered anatomy, often requiring stems or augments. Robotic-assisted systems have emerged as a potential solution by improving precision and bone preservation. This systematic review evaluates robotic assistance in UKA-to-TKA conversion and its impact on surgical performance and outcomes. This review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025643211). A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was conducted through October 2025. Eligible studies reported outcomes of robotic-assisted UKA-to-TKA conversions with a mean follow-up of 20.9 months. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on demographics, perioperative variables, functional outcomes, complications, and implant survivorship. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Five studies including 136 patients (140 knees) were analyzed. Most cases (n = 105) used the MAKO SmartRobotics™ System, while the remainder (n = 35) used the ROSA Knee System. No intraoperative conversions to manual technique occurred. Augments were required in 13.6% of cases and stems in 3.6%. Range of motion improved to 119-130° flexion with full extension. Patient-reported outcomes demonstrated improvements in r-WOMAC and OKS, with favorable postoperative FJS. Complication rates ranged from 0 to 11%, including one intraoperative tibial fracture (0.7%), two periprosthetic joint infections, three stiffness cases, and one aseptic loosening. Implant survivorship ranged from 93.2% to 100% at up to 3.6 years follow-up. Robotic-assisted UKA-to-TKA conversion demonstrates reproducible intraoperative performance, minimal need for augments, and favorable short-term outcomes. Longer-term studies are needed to confirm durability.Level of evidence: Level IV.

articles.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome: a single-center case series and systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of our study was to evaluate the clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, and prognostic features of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome (IM3OS).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of seven patients with IM3OS treated at Hospital del Mar between 2020 and 2025, together with a systematic review and descriptive patient-level synthesis of the published literature. PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase were searched for reports published between 2015 and 2025, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included case reports, case series, letters, correspondence, and conference abstracts providing sufficient individual patient-level data.

RESULTS: In our series, all seven patients were male, with a median age of 81 years. The most frequent tumor types were non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (42.8%) and urothelial carcinoma (28.5%). Diplopia (71.4%), ptosis (71.4%), and dyspnea (71.4%) were the most common presenting manifestations. Most patients received high-dose corticosteroids (71.4%), intravenous immunoglobulins (85.7%), and additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents (85.7%). The systematic review included 71 studies and 103 patients. Median age was 71 years, and 68.9% were male. Melanoma (35.9%), renal cell carcinoma (16.5%), and NSCLC (16.5%) were the most frequent malignancies. Ptosis (71.8%) and weakness (62.1%) were the most common presenting symptoms. The most frequently reported initial regimen was methylprednisolone 1 g/day (35.9%), and 52.4% of patients received additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents.

CONCLUSION: IM3OS is a rare, early-onset, clinically severe immune-related overlap syndrome with a high mortality rate requiring prompt recognition, structured multisystem assessment, close cardiorespiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary management. Current evidence remains observational and does not allow conclusions regarding therapeutic superiority.

articles.title: GNMT alleviates heart failure-induced skeletal muscle atrophy by regulating ATP5J2-mediated mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming through succinylation.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is defined as a condition characterized by abnormalities in the heart's structure or function, which lead to the heart's inability to deliver oxygen to tissues in a timely manner, and it may progress to symptoms such as muscle atrophy of skeletal muscles. Our research primarily focuses on Glycine N-methyltransferase (GNMT), an enzyme that utilizes S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to catalyze glycine, in order to explore its specific role in HF-induced skeletal muscle atrophy. In this study, an HF rat model induced by abdominal aortic constriction (AAC) and a C2C12 muscle atrophy cell model induced by angiotensin Ⅱ (Ang Ⅱ) were established. Echocardiography, ELISA, and HE staining were used to evaluate the damage of myocardial and gastrocnemius tissues. Immunofluorescence staining was used to assess skeletal muscle atrophy. Western blot, IP, and Co-IP were used to determine the molecular mechanism. In HF rats, the expressions of GNMT and Mitochondrial Fo complex subunit F2 (ATP5J2) were significantly decreased. Overexpression of GNMT/ATP5J2 contributed to alleviate HF-induced skeletal muscle atrophy. GNMT elevated the succinylation level and protein stability of ATP5J2 at lysine 22 (K22) by consuming glycine, and simultaneously reduced its ubiquitination level. Succinylated ATP5J2 improved mitochondrial homeostasis to mitigate HF-induced skeletal muscle atrophy. This study elucidated the function of the GNMT-ATP5J2 axis in HF-induced skeletal muscle atrophy and clarified the underlying molecular mechanism, providing a new theoretical basis for the treatment of HF-induced skeletal muscle atrophy.

articles.title: From incidental cerebellar atrophy to progressive motor syndrome: a case within the spectrum of ATXN2-associated neurodegeneration.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing evidence suggests that ATXN2-related disorders represent a clinical spectrum with variable presentations.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 70-year-old Chinese man carrying an ATXN2 allele with 34 CAG repeats (20/34 repeats). Cerebellar atrophy was incidentally noted on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) more than ten years before symptom onset. He later developed bradykinesia and rigidity. After rapid weight loss, he developed a rapidly progressive motor syndrome with clinical upper and lower motor neuron features, followed by type II respiratory failure requiring noninvasive ventilation.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the notion that ATXN2-associated neurodegeneration may represent a clinical continuum.

articles.title: Comorbidity patterns and their associations with performance status and treatment receipt in breast and colorectal cancers in a multiethnic Asian setting: a latent class analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Comorbidity is usually summarised as a count or index, which treats different combinations of conditions equally. Whether distinct comorbidity patterns have different implications for management decisions in cancer is unclear. We applied latent class analysis (LCA) to identify comorbidity patterns and examined their associations with performance status and cancer treatment in individuals with breast or colorectal cancer.

METHODS: Data from two Malaysian cohorts comprising adults with breast or colorectal cancer were analysed. Comorbidities, verified against medical records, were grouped into 20 categories. LCA was used to identify comorbidity patterns. Outcomes included ECOG performance status (0-1 vs ≥ 2) and receipt of treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, anti-HER2, CDK4/6 inhibitors, hormone therapy).

RESULTS: Among 1117 individuals, 695 (62.2%) had ≥ 1 comorbidity. Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes and obesity were most prevalent. LCA identified three classes: low (n = 723), cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) (n = 368) and multisystem (n = 26). All in the multisystem group and half in the CKM group had modified Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3. The CKM group was older than the low-comorbidity group (62 vs 51 years) but did not differ in performance or treatment status. The multisystem group however had poorer performance status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.04, 95%CI = 1.50-10.84), lower odds of receiving chemotherapy (aOR = 0.10, 95%CI = 0.04-0.25) and anti-HER2 therapy (aOR = 0.14, 95%CI = 0.02-0.86).

CONCLUSION: Comorbidity patterns revealed differences that counts alone would have missed. The CKM class had similar performance status and treatment receipt to the low-comorbidity class despite cardiovascular and renal comorbidity, highlighting risks not reflected by performance status. The multisystem class requires validation.

articles.title: Ambulatory blood pressure characteristics and left ventricular hypertrophy in untreated children with primary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To identify clinical and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)-derived factors associated with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in untreated children and adolescents with primary hypertension. This retrospective study included 306 untreated patients aged 9-17 years with newly diagnosed primary hypertension. LVH was defined as a left ventricular mass index ≥ 45 g/m^2.16. Propensity score-based overlap weighting was used to balance demographic and obesity-related characteristics between patients with and without LVH. Weighted logistic regression was performed to evaluate clinical, laboratory, and ABPM-derived factors associated with LVH. LVH was present in 89 patients (29.1%). Grade 2 office hypertension was the strongest factor associated with LVH (OR 4.22, 95% CI 2.29-7.77; P < 0.001). Selected metabolic and inflammatory markers showed exploratory associations with LVH. Among continuous ABPM parameters, nighttime mean diastolic blood pressure was associated with LVH (OR 1.54 per 10-mmHg increase, 95% CI 1.02-2.31), although this association was lost after adjustment for hypertension grade. In contrast, a systolic non-dipper pattern remained associated with LVH after adjustment for hypertension grade (OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.18-6.80; P = 0.020).

CONCLUSION: LVH was common among untreated children with primary hypertension, with office HTN severity being the predominant associated factor. Abnormal circadian BP patterns may provide complementary information for identifying children with LVH.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Left ventricular hypertrophy is a common form of cardiac target-organ damage in children with primary hypertension. • Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring provides information on nocturnal blood pressure and circadian patterns beyond office blood pressure.

WHAT IS NEW: • In untreated children, grade 2 office hypertension was the factor most strongly associated with left ventricular hypertrophy. • A systolic non-dipping pattern remained associated with left ventricular hypertrophy after adjustment for hypertension severity, suggesting additional value of circadian blood pressure assessment.

articles.title: Comparison of fecal continence and bowel function scoring systems following anorectal malformation repair: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multiple instruments are used to assess fecal continence and bowel function after anorectal malformation (ARM) repair, but their comparability is uncertain. This systematic review examined inter-system agreement and differences in the findings produced when two or more scoring systems were applied to the same ARM cohort.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception through 26 April 2026. Original studies applying at least two named fecal continence or bowel function scoring systems to the same ARM cohort were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Because comparable agreement estimates were sparse, results were synthesized narratively (PROSPERO: CRD420261377404).

RESULTS: Fifteen studies published from 2012 to 2025, with individual sample sizes of 20-267 participants, were included. Krickenbeck was used in 14 studies (93%) and Kelly in nine (60%). Only one study, based on 39 parent-reported assessments, reported numerical inter-system agreement estimates; weighted κ values for four score pairs ranged from 0.256 to 0.343. Other studies described category discordance or differences in group-level findings. In one cohort, Kelly did not identify a between-group difference detected by Krickenbeck and Rintala. In another small cohort, Kelly continence and the Krickenbeck constipation domain favored different surgical groups, although they assessed different outcome constructs. Blinding between instrument administrations was unreported in 12 studies.

CONCLUSION: The limited available evidence suggests that commonly used ARM bowel function instruments may yield non-equivalent information, but it is insufficient to establish their interchangeability or the superiority of any single system. Krickenbeck is currently the most frequently used instrument. Prospective comparative studies using standardized administration and appropriate agreement analyses are needed before a universal core instrument can be recommended.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence for stromal cell quality assessment: A systematic review of human mesenchymal stromal cell properties and viability.
articles.abstract: Reliable assessment of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) viability and stem cell-associated properties is essential for ensuring the consistency, safety, and therapeutic potential of MSC cultures before clinical use. However, incomplete understanding of the mechanisms underlying MSC therapeutic effects remains a major barrier to clinical translation and to establishing reliable, standardised quality attributes. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable automated assessment of these properties, but the performance and clinical relevance of AI-based approaches have not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review evaluated the accuracy and clinical utility of AI for assessing viability and stem cell-associated properties in human MSC cultures. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched five electronic databases (Cochrane, Scopus, PubMed, EMBASE, and MEDLINE) for eligible studies reporting quantitative AI-based assessments of human MSC cultures. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. The review protocol was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420256393235). Of 3,872 records identified, 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. Supervised AI models, particularly convolutional neural networks, were most used. Across included studies, reported performance metrics varied substantially because of differences in AI models, imaging modalities, datasets, and outcome definitions. Considerable heterogeneity in AI model architectures, imaging modalities, outcome definitions, and reporting metrics limited direct comparison across studies. Overall, available evidence suggests that AI can assess key MSC quality attributes and may support more objective, scalable, and standardised quality-control workflows. However, broader validation, standardised reporting, external testing, and evaluation across a wider range of MSC characteristics are required before routine clinical implementation can be recommended.

articles.title: Retinal layer thickness as a potential marker for future cardiovascular events - a UK Biobank cohort study using optical coherence tomography.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. For CVD prevention, effective screening is needed to identify high-risk individuals. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides a noninvasive, low-cost "quick look" into the brain and has recently shown thinning of certain retinal layers in patients with previous CVD. We explored if OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses could predict future major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: stroke/myocardial infarction/cardiovascular death).

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data of 51,293 participants from the UK Biobank were analyzed. We used cause-specific hazard models to evaluate the association of retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness with incident MACE, adjusting models for cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and performed subanalyses for association with incident stroke and myocardial infarction.

RESULTS: Median follow-up time was 14.7 years. Both RNFL thickness (aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, p < 0.001) and GCIPL thickness (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.92-1.00, p = 0.04) were statistically associated with incident MACE in cause-specific hazard models adjusted for CVRF. Interestingly, RNFL thickness was more strongly associated with incident myocardial infarction (aHR 0.94, 95% CI 0.88-0.99, p = 0.02) while GCIPL was more strongly associated with incident stroke (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: RNFL and GCIPL thicknesses are associated with future MACE, even after adjusting for CVRF. OCT-measured retinal layer thickness could contribute to the assessment of cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: [The acute orthoplastic patient : Definition and initial management recommendations: consensus statement of the Orthoplastic Surgery Working Group of the German Society for Trauma Surgery (DGU) and the German Society of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons (DGPRÄC)].
articles.abstract: Orthoplastic surgery combines the expertise of trauma and orthopedic surgery with plastic and reconstructive surgery for the management of complex musculoskeletal injuries associated with extensive soft tissue defects. Its primary aim is to provide early, coordinated interdisciplinary care to restore skeletal stability, achieve durable soft tissue coverage, and maximize long-term function. An acute orthoplastic patient is defined as an individual with complex musculoskeletal and soft tissue injuries requiring close interdisciplinary collaboration between trauma, plastic, and, where appropriate, additional surgical specialties. Furthermore, associated factors such as vascular injuries, infection, or relevant comorbidities may necessitate an orthoplastic treatment approach. The following recommendations were agreed upon: Patients who are hemodynamically stable and without an acutely threatened limb should be transferred to an orthoplastic competence center as early as possible, ideally within 24 h after injury. If immediate transfer is not feasible, early structured telemedical consultation with standardized transmission of clinical information, imaging, and photographic documentation of the soft tissue injury is recommended. Management should follow a standardized treatment pathway including prompt initiation of empirical antibiotic therapy, interdisciplinary radical debridement, restoration of bone stability, early vascular assessment, and timely definitive reconstruction. Whenever feasible, definitive fracture fixation and soft tissue reconstruction should be performed simultaneously or within a short time interval. These consensus recommendations provide the first structured framework for defining, triaging, and managing acute orthoplastic patients and aim to promote standardized orthoplastic care in specialized centers.

articles.title: [Clinical analysis of 369 deaths within 30 days following surgical treatment of proximal femur fracture].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 30-day mortality rate after surgical treatment of proximal femur fractures (PF) is reported in the literature to be up to 10%. Clinical studies in German-speaking countries on the suspected causes or underlying diagnoses have not yet been available, which is the reason for this study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The retrospective single-center cohort study is based on a database that records PF. Patients who died within 30 days postoperatively between 2006 and 2025 were included. The primary study endpoint was the causes of death, as documented in the final discharge summary. The secondary study endpoint was a descriptive analysis of deaths occurring within 24 h (day 0) postoperatively, as well as an assessment of variables associated with mortality between postoperative days 1-15 and days 16-30.

RESULTS: The overall cohort comprised 5431 patients with PF. Of these, 369 patients (6.8%) died within 30 days. The mean age was 85.2 years (53-101 years). Compared with the preceding 5‑year periods, the mortality rate decreased significantly in the last period (2021-2025; p = 0.007). The causes of death were respiratory (n = 105) and cardiovascular events (n = 54), multiorgan failure (n = 44), palliative condition (n = 32), renal events (n = 23), acute gastrointestinal diseases (n = 24), cerebral events (n = 15), periprosthetic infection including sepsis (n = 2), and other causes (n = 3). In 67 individuals, the cause of death was unclear. Within 24 h (day 0), 29 patients died, of whom n = 11 died from bone cement embolism or fat embolism syndrome. Five patients died in the operating room. More patients died between days 1 and 15 compared with the second half of the observation period (n = 216 vs. n = 124; p = 0.001), particularly during the first week (n =  145). In the first half, more women (p = 0.016) and patients treated with joint arthroplasty (p = 0.002) also died. All other variables were not statistically significant. With regard to the causes of death, both groups showed a similar distribution (p = 0.056).

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of patients with PF, the first postoperative week was the most vulnerable period for death. The causes of death provide an approximation to this previously largely overlooked topic, but they are consistent with registry or autopsy data. Over the 20-year analysis, mortality most recently declined significantly.

EVIDENCE: III; retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: [Invasive intracoronary imaging : Role in routine cardiology].
articles.abstract: Intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, provides detailed insights into plaque morphology and facilitates the precise planning and guidance of percutaneous coronary interventions, especially in patients with complex coronary lesions. Based on the results of multiple randomized clinical trials, current clinical guidelines recommend the use of intracoronary imaging for the treatment of complex coronary lesions. However, the appropriate application of both imaging modalities requires a thorough understanding of their technical principles, as well as their respective strengths and limitations. This article therefore reviews the technical fundamentals of optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, illustrates their clinical application through selected case examples, and summarizes the current evidence supporting their use.

articles.title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed.

RESULTS: Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

articles.title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified.

PRIMARY ENDPOINT: modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients.

RESULTS: Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months.

CONCLUSION: In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative.

KEY POINTS: Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.

articles.title: Developmental Systems Cardiology III: Measuring Adaptation Across the Lifespan.
articles.abstract: Developmental Systems Cardiology (DSC) conceptualizes congenital heart disease as a lifelong adaptive process shaped by interactions among biological, developmental, psychosocial, environmental, and healthcare systems. As survival has improved, contemporary challenges increasingly include neurodevelopment, psychosocial wellbeing, educational participation, healthcare engagement, and long-term adaptation, requiring multidimensional assessment beyond traditional physiological outcomes. This third article in the DSC series proposes a measurement framework for operationalizing adaptation across the lifespan. Rather than introducing new measurement domains or replacing established assessment recommendations, DSC provides an integrative architecture for linking existing measures across genomics and epigenomics, prenatal exposures, developmental physiology, neurocardiac interactions, family and social determinants, environmental influences, digital phenotyping, and healthcare-system context. Longitudinal measurement serves as a cross-cutting principle for characterizing adaptive trajectories and identifying periods of vulnerability and opportunity. Within this framework, adaptation is a dynamic, measurable process emerging through interactions among individuals, families, healthcare systems, and broader environments. Measurement therefore encompasses developmental functioning, resilience, participation, quality of life, healthcare transitions, and implementation outcomes alongside biological and clinical indicators. Established domain-specific standards, including neurodevelopmental assessment recommendations, can populate this broader architecture. This approach emphasizes integration rather than instrument development, while preserving the specificity and utility of established measures within individual domains. By integrating validated measures across domains, developmental stages, and time, DSC may provide a common language for research, registries, quality improvement, implementation science, and lifespan care. Its proposed contribution lies in organizing multidimensional measurement to better understand how adaptive and maladaptive trajectories emerge and evolve across development.

articles.title: Clinical Outcome of Late Survivors Following the Classic Fontan Procedure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure and multi-organ dysfunction develop insidiously in adults with a classic Fontan circulation. We evaluated late outcomes and risk factors for failing Fontan beyond 20 years after the classic Fontan procedure. Among 170 patients operated between 1978 and 1995, those surviving beyond 20 years without Fontan conversion were included. Clinical outcomes and risk factors were assessed. Sixty patients were included: tricuspid atresia in 37, double-inlet left ventricle in 14. Over 35.2 years' median follow-up, 13 (21.7%) died and 31 (51.7%) developed failing Fontan at a median of 30.8 years. Survival was lower with failing Fontan (70.2% vs. 95.2% at 35 years; P = .013) than those without. In multivariable analysis, double-inlet left ventricle (hazard ratio 2.42; P = .027) and ascites (hazard ratio 2.70; P = .007) were independent risk factors. At the last follow-up, the failing group had lower serum albumin (4.2 vs. 4.6 g/dL; P = .017) and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (774 vs. 404 pg/mL; P = .004); hepatic markers, total protein, and platelet count did not differ. After adjustment for the interval since diagnosis and exclusion of protein-losing enteropathy, only the natriuretic peptide association persisted. Peak oxygen uptake was also lower (P < .01). Late mortality and failing Fontan remained substantial beyond two decades. Double-inlet left ventricle and ascites were independent risk factors. Higher natriuretic peptide and reduced exercise capacity characterized the failing group, whereas lower albumin did not independently identify it. Regular assessment of these markers may aid surveillance.

articles.title: Thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications in NPM1-mutated AML: Association with APL-like immunophenotype and impact on early mortality.
articles.abstract: NPM1-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is generally classified as favorable risk; however, early mortality remains a concern. A subset of NPM1-mutated AML exhibits a CD34-low/negative and HLA-DR-low/negative immunophenotype resembling acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), raising the possibility that these patients may also share an increased susceptibility to coagulation abnormalities. While thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications are well recognized in APL, their frequency and prognostic significance in NPM1-mutated AML remain incompletely defined. In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with newly diagnosed NPM1-mutated AML were included. Immunophenotyping was performed using multiparametric flow cytometry, and an APL-like immunophenotype was defined by low or absent CD34 and HLA-DR expression. Clinically significant thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications were recorded within the first 100 days, and early mortality (30-, 60-, and 100-day) was assessed as the primary survival outcome. A total of 70 patients were included, of whom 24 (34.3%) had an APL-like immunophenotype. Compared with the non-APL-like group, the APL-like group had lower fibrinogen levels (309.5 [211-421] vs. 410 [214-518] mg/dL; p = 0.015) and higher D-dimer levels (5.73 [2.4-9.2] vs. 2.50 [0.9-5.0] mg/L; p = 0.012) at diagnosis. Clinically significant thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications occurred in 12 patients (17.1%) and were more frequent in the APL-like group than in the non-APL-like group (33.3% vs. 8.7%; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, the APL-like immunophenotype (OR, 8.79; 95% CI, 1.46-53.05; P=0.018) and a white blood cell count > 35 × 10⁹/L (OR, 10.96 [1.48-80.92] p = 0.019) were independently associated with these complications. Compared with patients without complications, those with thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications had lower 30-day (66.7% vs. 93.0%; P = 0.006), 60-day (57.1% vs. 91.2%; p = 0.002), and 100-day OS (45.7% vs. 87.6%; p < 0.001). Thrombotic or hemorrhagic complications remained independently associated with 100-day mortality in multivariable Cox analysis (HR, 5.79 [1.85-18.06] p = 0.003). In NPM1-mutated AML, the immunophenotypically defined APL-like subset is associated with a procoagulant profile and an increased risk of clinically significant thrombotic and hemorrhagic complications; importantly, these events were independently associated with early mortality.

articles.title: Antithrombotic strategies and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock requiring short-term mechanical circulatory support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock following acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) is associated with high mortality. Short-term mechanical circulatory support (ST-MCS) is frequently used after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to stabilize hemodynamics. However, balancing anticoagulation (AC) and antiplatelet therapy in this setting poses substantial bleeding risk.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate real-world antithrombotic strategies and associated ischemic and hemorrhagic complications in AMI-CS patients receiving ST-MCS.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included all consecutive AMI-CS patients who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS between January 2017 and October 2024. AC and antiplatelet regimens were recorded from ST-MCS initiation until shock resolution. Ischemic and hemorrhagic events during this period were analyzed. The primary composite clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of ischemic events and all-cause mortality occurring during the period of cardiogenic shock.

RESULTS: Among 71 patients with AMI-CS who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS (mean age 62 ± 13 years, 69% male), in-hospital mortality was 56%, and MACE occurred in 42%. At ST-MCS initiation, 79% received triple therapy, decreasing to 39% by Day 7. Ischemic events were infrequent (8%) and mainly cerebrovascular. No cases of recurrent myocardial infarction or stent thrombosis were observed. Major bleeding (BARC ≥ 3) occurred in 32% of patients, typically within the first 48 h, and was more frequent in those supported with VA-ECMO.

CONCLUSION: In AMI-CS patients requiring ST-MCS, ischemic events were uncommon, whereas major bleeding was frequent and occurred early. These findings underscore the need for individualized antithrombotic strategies in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Uncertainty-aware deep learning in FDG-PET: implications for generalizability in clinical practice.
Toward very early vasopressin use in septic shock: observational data accumulate but trial evidence still lacking.
Reversal of T1D and Rapid Reduction of β-Cell Stress by IL-10-Dependent MDSCs Induced by TLR4-Ab.
articles.abstract: Therapy with IgG3 Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/myeloid differentiation factor 2 (MD2) agonistic antibody (TLR4-Ab) is a novel approach to type 1 diabetes (T1D) immunotherapy that targets the innate immune system by inducing immunoregulatory myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). We sought to define the mechanisms by which TLR4-Ab induces MDSCs and how they reverse T1D. TLR4-Ab induction of MDSCs requires interleukin 10 signaling in the bone marrow, and MDSCs mediate suppression via inducible nitric oxide synthase. Induction of immunoregulatory MDSCs results in profound downregulation of β-cell endoplasmic reticulum stress and unfolded protein response associated with acute T1D. Establishing mechanisms by which TLR4-Ab reverses acute T1D defines new therapeutic pathways for human T1D that target innate immunity to restore immune tolerance.

articles.title: Direct SVC Access for Valve Replacement With Percutaneous Venotomy Suture System Hemostasis: A Way In.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult patients with congenital heart disease often have limited vascular access due to previous procedures and anatomic variations.

CASE SUMMARY: This case describes how a percutaneously placed venotomy suture system allowed for direct percutaneous superior vena cava access for delivery sheath insertion for transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement. This system allowed for a novel access approach and the achievement of hemostasis in an otherwise noncompressible site.

DISCUSSION: The availability of percutaneously placed venotomy suture placement systems allows for a more daring approach to noncompressible sites within the mediastinum and has the potential to be applied to allow large-bore closed chest access to other mediastinal structures.

articles.title: FOLFOX-Associated Ventricular Fibrillation Arrest in a Patient With Colon Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity is uncommon but may cause life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man with stage IIIB colon cancer developed chest discomfort and out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest approximately 72 hours after his first folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil (5-FU), and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) cycle. Electrocardiography showed anterior ST-segment elevations, but coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive left and right coronary arteries. Echocardiography showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 30%, which improved to approximately 50% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging without myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement. FOLFOX was discontinued, guideline-directed medical therapy was initiated, and an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for secondary prevention.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights a rare, severe presentation of fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity after the first treatment cycle despite no prior cardiac history.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ventricular fibrillation may occur early during FOLFOX therapy. Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management are essential.

articles.title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

articles.title: Child Protection Competencies in Medical Education.
articles.journal: Zeitschrift fur Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie und Psychotherapie
articles.abstract: Background: Child maltreatment is a major global public health concern with severe physical, psychological, and developmental consequences. Physicians across many medical specialties may encounter affected children, making child protection an important component of medical education. However, many medical students and early-career physicians feel insufficiently prepared to recognize and manage suspected cases. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey using self-developed questions among medical students at the University of Münster (September-November 2025). The survey assessed experiences with child protection, perceived preparedness, and preferences regarding curricular content and teaching formats. Of the 376 respondents, we analyzed 323 complete responses (11.4 % of enrolled students). Via descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and MANOVA, we examined differences across academic years. Results: Students strongly supported integrating child protection as a mandatory standalone course (92.3 %). Preferred teaching formats were communication training (88 %), simulations (83.3 %), and case-based discussions (82 %). Many students reported uncertainty in handling suspected cases, particularly regarding communication with affected children and caregivers (84.8 %) and legal aspects (80.2 %). Perceived preparedness increased significantly with academic progression (p < .001). Conclusions: Medical students demonstrate a strong interest in structured child protection education. Practice-oriented and interdisciplinary teaching approaches may strengthen competencies required to recognize and manage suspected child maltreatment.

articles.title: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies in kidney disease: mechanistic rationale and emerging clinical evidence.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Over the past decades, the therapeutic landscape of nephrology has been transformed by the expanding use of immunosuppressive therapies, reflecting major advances in our understanding of the roles of the innate and adaptive immune systems in the pathogenesis of kidney diseases. While B-cell depletion via rituximab or obinutuzumab has improved immune-mediated kidney disease management, these agents remain insufficient. They spare long-lived plasma cells, memory B cells, and innate effectors, permitting persistent antibody production and ongoing tissue injury. Consequently, increasing attention has focused on anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, including daratumumab, isatuximab, and felzartamab, which target several of these pathogenic immune cell populations. Early clinical experience and emerging trial data in diseases such as IgA nephropathy, primary membranous nephropathy, and, most notably, kidney transplantation have suggested potential benefits in selected settings, further supporting their potential role in nephrology. In this narrative review, we summarize the current understanding of the pathophysiological role of CD38-expressing immune cells in kidney diseases and critically evaluate the available clinical evidence on the use of anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody therapies across a spectrum of renal disorders. The review also compares the roles of anti-CD38 monoclonal therapies in native kidney disease and antibody-mediated rejection, since they differ in mechanism, clinical evidence, and treatment options.

articles.title: Baroreflex control of heart rate at rest and during exercise in microgravity conditions.
articles.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness
articles.abstract: One of the most important features of prolonged weightlessness is a progressive impairment of muscular function. Physiological modifications related to exposure to microgravity, e.g. altered blood volume distribution, impaired myocardial function, and a decrease in stroke volume, in addition to the alterations in muscular function, contribute to the reduced physical exercise capacity commonly reported after space flight. The interplay between muscular, hemodynamic and body fluid modifications occurring in microgravity could alter also the neural mechanisms of cardiovascular regulation both in resting conditions and during exercise in comparison to those that are normally operating on the ground. Indeed, an impairment in arterial baroreflex control of heart rate has been reported in the resting state during spaceflight. Moreover, cardiovascular and autonomic responses to exercise have been reported to be either impaired or preserved after simulated or actual microgravity conditions. Differences in results might depend on different experimental settings: the majority of studies on exercise in microgravity have been conducted using handgrips as a convenient model of muscular exercise. However, microgravity-induced muscular impairment involves mainly the antigravity muscles, i.e. leg muscles, which are those primarily involved in the reduced exercise capacity and hence are more representative of the marked changes in the musculoskeletal system induced by microgravity. This brief review aims to summarize current knowledge on baroreflex control of heart rate in resting and exercise conditions in microgravity.

articles.title: Economic burden of low cardiorespiratory fitness in France.
articles.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estimating the economic burden of low cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) may help quantify its impact on healthcare costs and productivity losses. The aim of this study was to assess the economic burden of low CRF in France. The second objective was to estimate the cost savings associated with a 10% reduction in the prevalence of low CRF.

METHODS: A prevalence-based approach was used to quantify the direct (health care) costs of low CRF, with direct costs estimated using data from the French National Health Insurance system. Indirect costs (productivity losses due to premature mortality or morbidity) were assessed using a friction cost approach. The same methodology was applied to model the economic impact of a 10% reduction in the prevalence of low CRF.

RESULTS: Some 26.9% of males and 63.1% of females were identified as having low CRF in France. In 2024, the most expensive NCDs attributable to low CRF in terms of direct costs were type 2 diabetes (€ 1.993 billion), heart failure (€ 1.598 billion) and dementia (€ 1.137 billion). The total direct costs attributable to low CRF represented 5.6% of the total annual National Health expenditure in 2024. Indirect costs attributable to low CRF were estimated at € 4.775 billion. A 10% absolute reduction in low CRF would result in an estimated avoided cost (direct and indirect) of € 3.090 billion (18.9%) per year.

CONCLUSIONS: Low CRF represents a substantial economic burden in France. Improving CRF at the population level could generate significant health and productivity savings.

articles.title: Progressing From Association to Causation: Examining Prior Antibiotic Exposure and Antimicrobial Resistance Across Three US Health Systems Using Causal Machine Learning.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic exposure is hypothesized to drive antimicrobial resistance, but confounding by indication has limited causal inference from observational data. We estimated the effect of prior exposure on subsequent same-class nonsusceptibility across 7 antibiotic classes and 3 US health systems using a causal-inference framework.

METHODS: We analyzed 1 165 151 culture episodes from Mass General Brigham (MGB), Stanford Health Care, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC; via MIMIC-IV). The causal effect of 90-day prior exposure on same-class resistance was estimated by double machine learning, adjusting for more than 35 confounders per site, including prior same-class resistant isolates, infecting-organism group, and calendar period. Robustness was assessed via inverse probability weighting, E-values, exposure-window and dose-response sensitivity, and negative-control pairs. Rates of microbiologically inactive empiric therapy were compared by prior same-class exposure.

RESULTS: Prior fluoroquinolone exposure was associated with increased nonsusceptibility by 11.9 and 12.6 percentage points at the primary sites (MGB, Stanford) and 8.6 points in validation (BIDMC) (all P < .001). Positive associations occurred for all 7 classes at all sites (sulfonamides indeterminate at Stanford), strongest at 30 days and attenuating through 365 days. Among patients with prior fluoroquinolone exposure receiving empiric fluoroquinolones for bloodstream infection, therapy was inactive in 50%-71% of episodes versus 27%-37% without prior exposure. Across classes, 3309 inactive empiric prescriptions were associated with prior same-class exposure. Median E-value was 2.5.

CONCLUSIONS: Prior antibiotic exposure was consistently associated with increased same-class nonsusceptibility across antibiotic classes and health systems, paralleling higher rates of microbiologically inactive empiric therapy. These findings support prospective evaluation of antibiotic-history-informed empiric prescribing.

articles.title: Prior Antibiotic Exposure and Subsequent Resistance in the Individual Patient: How Close Are We to the Bedside?
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

articles.title: Development, implementation, and evaluation of a mentorship program within hematology/oncology pharmacy association (HOPA) - a professional oncology pharmacy organization.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundFormal mentorship programs are important for the pharmacy profession. In 2019, the Hematology/Oncology Pharmacy Association (HOPA) launched their Mentorship Program aimed at pairing early-career pharmacists with senior HOPA members. Following an initial pilot program, the program was further expanded with supportive infrastructure as an annual offering from HOPA to eligible members.ObjectiveTo assess the impact of the HOPA Mentorship Program on involvement in the organization and to evaluate changes in self-reported professional and leadership perceptions following participation in the Mentorship Program.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed HOPA-level membership data of participants going through the Mentorship Program to assess their involvement in HOPA following program participation in domains including committee membership, committee leadership, conference attendance, and advocacy event participation. Mentees in the program also completed pre- and post-program surveys as part of their participation in the program. Median composite pre-and post-program survey responses were compared to assess changes in self-reported professional and leadership perceptions.ResultsA total of 39 mentees participated in the HOPA Mentorship Program between 2019 and 2025. Most mentees went on to serve on a HOPA committee (74%), with 28% serving in a leadership position on a committee. Most mentees (59%) also attended a HOPA-sponsored meeting following Mentorship Program participation. Mentees reported higher post-program ratings on leadership and professional development items compared with pre-program responses.ConclusionHOPA Mentorship Program participants demonstrated organizational contributions through committee service, leadership roles, and advocacy activities. Survey data demonstrated significant improvements in mentee self-reported leadership skills, career goal-setting, and professional engagement.

articles.title: Nearly doubled incidence of surgically treated primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in Southern Sweden, 2011-2025.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the incidence of surgically treated primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) in Southern Sweden between 2011 and 2025, and to examine whether demographic change or risk factor trends account for any change in incidence.

METHODS: This retrospective, population-based study included all surgically treated primary RRD cases in Southern Sweden between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2025. Crude and age- and sex-standardised incidence rates were calculated per 100 000 person-years using population data from Statistics Sweden. Cataract surgery data were obtained from the Swedish National Cataract Registry.

RESULTS: A total of 6916 surgically treated primary RRD cases were identified. Annual incidence increased from 15.8 to 29.5 cases per 100 000 person-years between 2011 and 2025, an 86.7% increase. Peak incidence of 30.4 per 100 000 person-years was seen in both 2019 and 2024. The increase persisted after age- and sex-standardisation. Mean age at surgery was 62 years and 68.3% occurred in men. Cataract surgery rate increased by 56.2% between 2011 and 2024. The proportion of pseudophakic RRD rose from 37.7% during 2011-2013 to 55.4% in 2023-2025.

CONCLUSION: The RRD incidence in Southern Sweden nearly doubled over the past 15 years, reaching levels among the highest reported worldwide. The increase persisted after standardisation, indicating that population ageing and sex distribution do not account for it. The concurrent rise in cataract surgery and in the proportion of pseudophakic RRD is notable, but these population-level observations cannot establish a causal link between the rise in RRD and the cataract surgery rate.

articles.title: Clinical Presentation, Acute Clinical Response, Drug Tolerability, and Short-Term Outcome of Cats Treated for Acute Congestive Heart Failure With Pimobendan (2017-2022): 71 Cases.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical effects, drug tolerability, and short-term outcomes of cats treated with pimobendan (PB) in conjunction with other therapies for acute congestive heart failure (CHF).

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center study (2017  to 2022).

SETTING: Academic teaching and referral hospital.

ANIMALS: Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days.

CONCLUSIONS: The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

articles.title: Deubiquitinase OTUB1 attenuates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the AMPK signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Cardiac hypertrophy, a response to pathological stimuli, eventually progresses to heart failure. Ovarian tumor-associated proteinase B1 (OTUB1), a deubiquitinase of the ovarian tumor (OUT) family, regulates inflammation, cell survival, and oxidative stress in various diseases, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unclear. Here, we investigated OTUB1 expression, function, and mechanism in pathological cardiac hypertrophy. OTUB1 expression was significantly downregulated in human hypertrophic hearts, transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced mouse hypertrophic hearts, and phenylephrine-stimulated neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). OTUB1 knockout (KO) mice exhibited exacerbated TAC-induced cardiac hypertrophy, dysfunction, and fetal gene reactivation, whereas OTUB1 overexpression attenuated PE-induced cardiomyocyte enlargement. Mechanistically, OTUB1 directly bound to, deubiquitinated, and stabilized Sirt2, thereby promoting AMPK phosphorylation. Silencing Sirt2 abolished the anti-hypertrophic effects of OTUB1 and blocked AMPK activation. In conclusion, OTUB1 protects against pathological cardiac hypertrophy by stabilizing Sirt2 and activating the AMPK signaling pathway, suggesting that OTUB1 is a promising therapeutic target for hypertrophy-associated heart failure.

articles.title: Safety and Outcomes of Percutaneous Vegetation Aspiration During Transvenous Lead Extraction: A Multicenter Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for cardiac implantable electronic device infection has high procedural success, but with a 1-year mortality approaching 25%. Potential mechanisms include septic embolization and persistent infected lead casts or "ghosts." Percutaneous mechanical aspiration of lead-related vegetations during TLE is a potential strategy to reduce vegetation burden, but safety and outcomes data are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To describe a multicenter experience utilizing percutaneous vegetation aspiration during TLE, including vegetation characteristics, procedural techniques, complications, and outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective multicenter registry included patients undergoing aspiration of lead-related masses at the time of TLE between 2016 and 2024 across six institutions. Clinical, microbiologic, and procedural data were collected. Vegetation size and outcomes were assessed using transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiography.

RESULTS: Fifty-three patients (62 ± 14 years, 28% female) underwent aspiration of 63 vegetations during extraction of 114 leads (mean dwell time 9.0 ± 8.2 years). Indications included bacteremia in 44 (83%), fungemia in 4 (8%), fever of unknown origin in 1 (2%), and aseptic thrombus debulking in 4 (8%). Mean vegetation size was 2.8 ± 1.8 cm. Aspiration devices included Penumbra Indigo (34%), Inari FlowTriever (30%), and AngioVac (36%). Complete aspiration occurred in 40 patients (75%). TLE achieved complete success in 49 (92%) and clinical success in 52 (98%). Major complications related to aspiration occurred in 2 patients (4%). After a median follow-up of 139 days, 10 patients (19%) died.

CONCLUSIONS: Percutaneous vegetation aspiration during TLE appears feasible and generally safe. However, mortality following extraction for device-related infection remains substantial, and the impact of adjunctive aspiration on outcomes requires further study.

articles.title: Statin Prescribing and Guideline Concordance Among Adults With HIV Aged 40-75 Years in a Single Urban Outpatient HIV Clinic, 2024.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with HIV (PWH) have elevated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. Following the REPRIEVE trial, 2024 HHS Adult and Adolescent Antiretroviral Guidelines recommend at least moderate-intensity statins for adults with HIV aged 40-75 years with 10-year ASCVD risk 5% to <20%. The 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline expands eligibility, supporting statins for all adults aged 40-75 years with HIV for primary prevention, regardless of LDL-C. We evaluated statin prescribing and HHS guideline concordance for primary prevention in this population.

SETTING: Single urban outpatient HIV clinic in the United States.

METHODS: Retrospective electronic health record review of adults with HIV aged 40-75 years with an outpatient HIV visit on or after February 27, 2024. Statin prescribing was an active prescription at the index visit. ASCVD risk was abstracted from clinical documentation; virologic suppression was HIV RNA <50 copies/mL. Primary-prevention eligibility followed the February 27, 2024 HHS framework: LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL plus ASCVD risk ≥5% or diabetes mellitus.

RESULTS: Of 753 patients reviewed, 414 met inclusion criteria. Statins were prescribed for 212 (51.2%). Statin-prescribed patients were older (median 62 vs. 54 years) with higher median ASCVD risk (13% vs. 7%). ASCVD risk was unavailable for 100 (24.2%). Among 242 patients eligible for primary-prevention statin therapy, 128 (52.9%) had an active statin prescription at the index visit. In multivariable modeling (n=314), higher ASCVD risk, higher CD4 count, and virologic suppression were independently associated with prescribing.

CONCLUSIONS: Only half of statin-eligible adults with HIV were prescribed statins, with the largest gap among those eligible by ASCVD risk 5% to <20% without diabetes. The 2026 ACC/AHA guideline expands eligibility to all adults aged 40-75 years with HIV. These findings highlight opportunities to improve implementation of guideline-directed cardiovascular prevention through improved cardiovascular risk assessment, clinician education, and electronic clinical decision support.

articles.title: Open Visiting Policy and Delirium in Adult Patients in ICUs: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
authors: and the Padova Intensive Care Unit (PADUA-ICU) Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To critically evaluate the comparative effects of open or flexible family presence policies vs. restricted or traditional family presence policies on the occurrence of delirium and other major outcomes among adult patients admitted to ICUs.

DATA SOURCES: We conducted a comprehensive electronic search of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to November 21, 2025.

STUDY SELECTION: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing open or flexible vs. restricted ICU visiting policies in adult patients.

DATA EXTRACTION: The primary outcome extracted was delirium occurrence. Secondary outcomes included the duration of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), ICU length of stay, hospital-acquired infections, and ICU mortality.

DATA SYNTHESIS: Thirteen RCTs comprising 3861 patients were included. Random-effects models showed that compared with restricted policies, open/flexible family presence reduced delirium occurrence (risk ratio [RR], 0.48; 95% CI, 0.29-0.81; low certainty) and IMV duration (mean difference [MD], -0.36 d; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.26 d; low certainty). The intervention did not affect the ICU length of stay (MD, 4.21 d; 95% CI, -4.65 to 13.07 d; very low certainty), the rates of hospital-acquired infections (RR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.81-1.23; low certainty), or ICU mortality (RR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.72-1.08; very low certainty).

CONCLUSIONS: Open/flexible ICU family presence may reduce delirium and shorten the duration of IMV slightly, without increasing infections or ICU mortality, although the certainty of evidence is low and heterogeneity remains substantial.

articles.title: Developing Models for Complicated Outcomes in Acutely Intoxicated ICU Patients With and Without Toxicity Information.
authors: and the INTOXICATE Study Investigators Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the prognostic value of the mean Lethality Risk Score (LRS), reflecting the toxicity of substances involved in an exposure, and to develop prediction models for complicated outcomes in ICU patients with acute intoxication.

DESIGN: Multicenter prospective cohort study.

SETTING: Seventy-eight ICUs in Europe, Australia, and the Eastern Mediterranean (2020-2023).

PATIENTS: A total of 2265 adult patients were admitted to the ICU with acute intoxication as the main reason for admission for at least 4 hours.

INTERVENTION: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was defined as ICU complications or death (22.5%). Clinical data were collected in an electronic capture system. We developed two prediction models: one incorporating laboratory variables ("Laboratory Model"), and one including the mean LRS ("Expo Model"). The mean LRS was calculated as the average of the individual LRS values assigned to the toxicants involved in the exposure. Key predictors were age, severity at presentation, systolic blood pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and hospital type. The mean LRS remained significant only when laboratory variables were not considered. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC), calibration plots, likelihood ratio tests, and decision curve analysis. Internal validation demonstrated good performance for both models (AUROCs of 0.79 and 0.77; calibration slopes of 0.94 and 0.95; intercepts of -0.06 and -0.06), with minimal overfitting. Decision curve analysis revealed clinically relevant threshold probability ranges of 0-50% for the Laboratory Model and 0-40% for the Expo Model.

CONCLUSIONS: The mean LRS had prognostic value only in the absence of laboratory test results. Both models may aid decision-making regarding the management of acutely intoxicated patients in the ICU.

articles.title: Association of Tele-Critical Care Capability With Interhospital Transfers and Potentially Low-Value Transfers Among Critically Ill Medicare Beneficiaries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Interhospital transfer is essential for accessing specialized critical care services, yet it poses clinical risk and substantial burden for patients and the healthcare system. Tele-critical care (TCC) programs extend expertise to resource-limited hospitals and may influence transfer decisions by identifying patients requiring escalation or supporting local management. We examined the association between TCC capability at index ICU hospitalizations, interhospital transfer, and post-transfer outcomes.

DESIGN: Nationwide retrospective cohort study using 2021-2023 Medicare claims linked to the American Hospital Association Annual Survey Database (AHAASD).

SETTING: U.S. acute care hospitals.

PATIENTS: Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries with ICU hospitalizations between 2022 and 2023.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: TCC capability was identified by AHAASD reporting and/or the presence of five or more TCC claims annually. The primary outcome was interhospital ICU transfer. Exploratory post-transfer outcomes included receipt of specialty procedures, death or hospice discharge within 1 day of transfer, in-hospital and 30-day mortality, and discharge disposition. Hierarchical logistic regression adjusted for patient demographics, comorbidities, acute organ failures, and transferring/accepting hospital characteristics, with transferring hospitals as random intercepts. Among 2,140,919 ICU hospitalizations, 33.4% occurred at 1,066 TCC-capable hospitals. Absolute transfer rates were similar (2.5% vs. 3.0%), but TCC capability was associated with higher adjusted odds of transfer (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.08; 95% CI, 1.01-1.14). In exploratory post-transfer analyses, transferred patients from TCC hospitals had greater illness severity yet were less likely to die or be discharged to hospice within 1 day of transfer (4.6% vs. 6.6%; aOR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.76-0.97) and more likely to be discharged home within 2 days (4.7% vs. 3.7%; aOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.03-1.33).

CONCLUSIONS: TCC capability was associated with modestly increased transfer rates, fewer potentially low-value transfers, and improved post-transfer outcomes, suggesting improved transfer selection.

articles.title: Ventilatory Management in Neurocritical Versus Non-Neurocritical Care Patients: A Pooled Analysis From the PRIME Database.
authors: PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients without ARDS (PRoVENT), PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients in Middle-income Countries (PRoVENT-iMiC), and Extubation strategies in Neuro-ICU patients and associations with Outcomes (ENIO) investigators
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe ventilatory management in neurocritical care and non-neurocritical care patients and determine whether specific ventilator settings are associated with development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and mortality in neurocritical care patients. The primary endpoint was a diagnosis of ARDS after initiation of invasive ventilation; one secondary endpoint was ICU mortality.

DATA SOURCES: Post hoc pooled analysis of harmonized individual patient data from three recent prospective observational studies combined into the PRIME database.

STUDY SELECTION: PRIME is a harmonized pooled database comprising individual patient data from three recent prospective observational studies on ventilatory management in critically ill patients: "PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients without ARDS" (PRoVENT), "PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients in Middle-income Countries" (PRoVENT-iMiC), and "Extubation strategies in Neuro-ICU patients and associations with Outcomes" (ENIO). We excluded patients with ARDS at the start of ventilation.

DATA EXTRACTION: Demographic and clinical characteristics, ventilator settings, respiratory variables, arterial blood gas values, and clinical outcomes were extracted from the harmonized PRIME database. Derived ventilation parameters included tidal volume normalized to predicted body weight, driving pressure, respiratory system compliance, mechanical power, ventilatory ratio, and Pao2/Fio2 ratio.

DATA SYNTHESIS: This analysis included 3848 patients, including 1702 neurocritical care and 1920 non-neurocritical care patients. Based on recorded ventilatory variables, neurocritical care patients received lower median tidal volumes (Vts), positive end-expiratory pressure, and Fio2. They had lower median driving pressure (ΔP), mechanical power (MP) of ventilation, and ventilatory ratio, as well as higher respiratory system compliance compared with non-neurocritical care patients. These differences were consistently observed at both assessed time points. ARDS was diagnosed more frequently in neurocritical care patients than in non-neurocritical care patients (8.7% vs. 3.9%; p < 0.001), while ICU mortality was lower (14.3% vs. 22.8%; p < 0.001).
