Among neurocritical care patients, those who developed ARDS were ventilated with lower median Vt and higher Fio2 and had higher median ΔP and MP. Vt normalized for predicted body weight in neurocritical care patients was independently associated with the development of ARDS.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, ventilatory management at the initial and 48-hour assessments differed between neurocritical care and non-neurocritical care patients, particularly with respect to key ventilator settings like Vt, positive end-expiratory pressure, and Fio2. In neurocritical care patients, ARDS was more often diagnosed than in non-neurocritical care patients.

articles.title: Comment on "Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for 90-day clinically significant medication-related harm in adults initiating oral anticancer therapy: A multicenter prospective cohort study".
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners

articles.title: Emerging non-AIDS comorbidities among adults with and without perinatally-acquired HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with perinatally acquired HIV (PHIV) who age into adulthood may be at risk for the early development of specific non-AIDS associated comorbidities (NAC). It is unclear whether the early initiation of ART among PHIV may decrease risk for the development of specific NAC.

METHODS: This retrospective study examined NAC outcomes among a cohort of PHIV and an age range-matched cohort of people with non-perinatally acquired HIV (NPHIV). Multivariate logistic regression models examined the association between clinical/demographic predictors and NAC and the association between early vs. late ART initiation and development of NAC among PHIV. Log rank test was used to compare Kaplan-Meier curves for NAC outcomes.

RESULTS: Compared to NPHIV (N=173), PHIV (N=171) significantly differed by age (30.1 vs 31.8 yrs), tobacco use, lower CD4 nadir, and with less HIV viral suppression. Both groups had high rates of HTN (PHIV 38.5%, NPHIV 29.5%), ≥stage 3 CKD (PHIV 5.9%, NPHIV 1.73%), hypercholesterolemia, and asthma. PHIV demonstrated higher likelihood of hypertension (OR 1.87, 95%CI 1.1-3.2), chronic kidney disease (OR 6.95, 95%CI 1.7-29.7), and a non-significant trend towards higher likelihood of death. PHIV had significantly earlier acquisition of HTN, and CKD. Rates of NAC among patients within the PHIV cohort did not differ based on early vs. late ART initiation.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared to NPHIV of similar age, PHIV adults had higher rates of HTN and CKD and were more likely to acquire these diseases at a younger age than NPHIV. These findings may have long term implications for cardiovascular risk among aging PHIV.

articles.title: "It's important, but at a cost…": healthcare professionals and people with aphasia describe what influences use of a novel, digital communication aid.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Safe and quality healthcare requires effective patient-provider communication. Aphasia is a communication disability that leaves people at risk of ineffective communication and inadequate care. Modifying the environment is one way to support communication. A novel mobile communication aid-The Aphasia App-was designed to support hospital interactions between healthcare professionals (HCPs) and people with aphasia (PWA). This study explored HCPs' perspectives of what influenced app use when it was introduced as a resource to support interactions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study followed an observational study, together forming an interpretivist focused ethnography on use of the app. Ten HCPs and three PWA were interviewed about their experiences using the app. Data was thematically analysed using an inductive and reflexive approach.

RESULTS: HCPs value communication support and want to provide person-centred care. However, a complex juggle of clinical, communicative, and emotional demands constrains interactions and app use, which are unsupported by the healthcare system.

CONCLUSIONS: Multi-level systems reform is needed to support HCPs to adopt communication aids and enable effective communication with people with aphasia.

articles.title: Acute hepatitis E presenting with fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock: A case report from Nepal.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis E virus infection is endemic in Nepal and commonly presents as an acute self-limiting hepatitis. Cardiac involvement is extremely rare and may be life-threatening. We report a case of a young female who presented with fever, jaundice, progressive dyspnea and hypotension. Laboratory assessment confirmed acute hepatitis E infection. Chest radiography revealed cardiomegaly with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated left ventricular dysfunction. Other infectious causes of myocarditis were excluded. The patient improved with inotropic support, heart failure treatment and other supportive management, with complete clinical recovery on follow-up. This case highlights the importance of early cardiac evaluation in patients with acute hepatitis E with features of heart failure.

articles.title: Reattaching fractured tooth fragments. The composite rod technique (CRT).
articles.journal: The international journal of esthetic dentistry
articles.abstract: Traumatic dental injury (TDI) involves coronal fractures of the maxillary anterior teeth, a relatively frequent occurrence in children and adolescents. The location in the arch of the maxillary incisors makes them precariously vulnerable to external trauma that requires immediate attention, not only to pacify the emotional anguish of the patient and parents, but also to safeguard the structural integrity of these pivotal teeth that are the cornerstone of dental esthetics. Restitution of TDI is particularly challenging if a patient presents with pulp involvement or vertical root fractures, necessitating both endodontic and restorative intervention or possibly extraction. The key elements for therapy are accurate diagnosis and expediency to alleviate pain, placate psychologic shock, and mitigate social embarrassment due to compromised esthetics. The latter is particularly significant for young patients who may encounter insensitive peer taunting that affects their mental well-being. This article focuses on the work steps for reattaching fractured tooth fragments isolated to enamel and dentin, including those involving the pulp, with a novel, minimally invasive approach called the composite rod technique (CRT) for facilitating the relocation of the fragment, optimizing fracture resistance of the fragment-abutment complex, and restoring anterior esthetics.

articles.title: Blood Transfusion Rates and Predictive Factors in Posterior-Based Minimally Invasive Scoliosis Surgery for Idiopathic Scoliosis: A LASSO-Based Prediction Model.
articles.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo investigate blood transfusion rates in posterior-based minimally invasive scoliosis surgery (MISS) for idiopathic scoliosis (IS) and to develop a prediction model for perioperative blood transfusion.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed data of 751 patients with IS who underwent posterior-based MISS between 2015 and 2026. The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression model was applied to identify predictors of transfusion among demographics, perioperative metrics, radiographic measurements, and transfusion-related profiles. The model was constructed by development cohort March 2015 and February 2024 (development cohort, n = 595) and validated using the temporal data between March 2024 and February 2026 (validation cohort, n = 156).ResultsIn the total cohort, 518 patients (69.0%) required a blood transfusion. Among them, 76 patients received only postoperative transfusions, with the majority administered within 3 days postoperatively. Post-LASSO multivariate regression analysis demonstrated that greater estimated blood loss, lower preoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, absence of tranexamic acid use, longer fusion levels, and a larger major preoperative Cobb angle were independently associated with perioperative transfusion. The perioperative model demonstrated good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.89 in the development cohort and 0.94 in the validation cohort.ConclusionsPostoperative transfusion was uncommon, and transfusion-free surgery may be feasible in selected lower-risk patients undergoing posterior-based MISS for IS. Based on our prediction model, strategies for blood transfusion-free surgery should be individualized, considering patient-specific profiles such as preoperative Hb levels, fusion level, and Cobb angle.

articles.title: Evaluation of a Structured Port Catheter Care Training Program for Nurses in Turkey: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.journal: Journal of continuing education in nursing
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Port catheters are widely used in oncology care to provide safe long-term venous access; however, improper management may lead to complications such as infection, thrombosis, and extravasation. Nurses play a key role in preventing these complications through evidence-based care. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a structured training program on port catheter care on nurses' knowledge and knowledge retention.

METHOD: This quasi-experimental study used a single-group pre-test-posttest follow-up design. The study included 60 nurses working in internal medicine and oncology units at a training and research hospital. Data were collected with a Descriptive Characteristics Form and a Port Catheter Care Knowledge Questionnaire.

RESULTS: Repeated measures analysis of variance showed that knowledge scores increased significantly after training and remained high at 1-month follow-up (p < .001).

CONCLUSION: The training program improved knowledge and supported retention. Further research is needed to assess its effect on clinical practice and patient outcomes.

articles.title: FNR/ArcA-2,3-butanediol regulatory axis enhances glucose uptake and adhE expression in high alcohol-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Previously, we found that Klebsiella pneumoniae is a high-alcohol producer, which contributes to the development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its high-alcohol production remain unclear. By comparing biological phenotypes of K. pneumoniae with those of Escherichia coli, we found that the former is better at metabolizing high concentrations of glucose, exhibits faster growth rates, and produces higher levels of alcohol, with the 2,3-butanediol (2,3-BD) pathway being the key determinant underlying these differences. More importantly, species possessing the 2,3-BD pathway, including Klebsiella aerogenes, Klebsiella oxytoca, Enterobacter cloacae, and Enterobacter hormaechei, have all demonstrated high-alcohol production capabilities similar to that of K. pneumoniae, suggesting a conserved mechanism for alcohol production among 2,3-BD-positive Enterobacteriaceae. Deletion of the 2,3-BD pathway reduced the expression of the phosphotransferase system (PTS) and the alcohol dehydrogenase gene adhE, which normally confer enhanced glucose metabolism and alcohol production. Pathway deletion also downregulated multiple virulence determinants, including capsular polysaccharides (CPS), lipopolysaccharides (LPS), and type 1 and 3 fimbriae, thereby attenuating virulence in a murine pneumonia model. In addition, the regulator FNR enhanced alcohol production by upregulating adhE and 2,3-BD pathway genes, whereas ArcA activated the 2,3-BD pathway in an ArcB-independent manner, revealing a non-canonical signaling mechanism that couples metabolic adaptation with virulence. Collectively, our findings identify the "FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD pathway axis" as a key molecular mechanism driving high alcohol production in K. pneumoniae, highlighting the 2,3-BD pathway as a key link between bacterial metabolism and virulence and a potential therapeutic target for controlling K. pneumoniae infections.IMPORTANCEKlebsiella pneumoniae has emerged as a novel cause of NAFLD due to its high alcohol-producing capacity. However, the molecular basis of this phenotype remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that the FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD pathway axis drives high levels of alcohol production by enhancing glucose-PTS system and adhE expression, and that this pathway is conserved among Enterobacteriaceae with strong alcohol-producing abilities. Moreover, loss of the 2,3-BD pathway reduces the expression of multiple virulence factors and attenuates pathogenicity in a murine pneumonia model. These findings identify the FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD axis as a potential target for mitigating excessive alcohol production and virulence in bacteria.

articles.title: Impact of diabetic foot ulcers on mortality risk: Lessons from a 35-year Brazilian cohort followed at an association of people living with diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) on mortality risk in a Brazilian cohort of individuals followed at an association of people living with diabetes mellitus.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This retrospective, population-based epidemiological study assessed the impact of DFUs on mortality risk in a cohort of Brazilian individuals with types 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus. Data were obtained from medical records covering the period from 1990 to 2024 and included sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, and therapeutic variables. Survival analyses were conducted using Cox proportional hazards models, with death as the event of interest, and were adjusted for potential confounders.

RESULTS: Among the 382 participants included in the final analysis, DFUs, amputations, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy were associated with increased mortality risk by 89%, 123%, and 37%, respectively. Peripheral artery disease showed a modest, but not statistically significant, increase in mortality risk. Patients with DFUs who were not using oral antidiabetic drugs had a 165% higher mortality risk, and those with prior amputations and poor fasting glucose levels had a 41% increased mortality risk.

CONCLUSION: Overall, DFUs were identified as critical predictors of mortality in people living with diabetes mellitus, mostly among those with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The impact of DFUs on mortality risk is multifaceted and context-dependent, highlighting the leading role of prior amputations. These findings underscore the need for targeted early interventions and the implementation of strategies aimed at reducing mortality in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Tetraethylammonium-Sensitive ventricular repolarization in diabetic rat myocardium: effects of rosiglitazone.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine ventricular action-potential responses to tetraethylammonium (TEA), a non-selective potassium-channel blocker, in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats and determine whether rosiglitazone modifies these responses.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male Wistar rats were assigned to Control (C), Control plus Rosiglitazone (C+RSG), Diabetic (D), or Diabetic plus Rosiglitazone (D+RSG) groups. Diabetes was induced with streptozotocin (45 mg/kg, intravenous). Resting membrane potential (RMP), action potential amplitude (APA), and half-repolarization time (½RT) were recorded from isolated left ventricular papillary muscles before and after TEA administration (2 mmol/L).

RESULTS: At week 8, blood glucose was 563 ± 29 mg/dL in diabetic rats and 98 ± 6 mg/dL in controls (p < 0.001). Rosiglitazone reduced the diabetic value to 336 ± 25 mg/dL (p < 0.05 vs. D). TEA increased ½RT from 18 ± 1 to 38 ± 2 ms in controls (+20 ms) and from 60 ± 3 to 65 ± 3 ms in diabetic myocardium (+5 ms). Diabetic preparations had higher post-TEA ½RT because repolarization was prolonged at baseline; however, the absolute TEA-associated increment was smaller than in controls. TEA also increased APA in untreated control and diabetic preparations.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with marked baseline prolongation of ventricular repolarization. The smaller absolute ½RT increment in diabetic myocardium does not support enhanced TEA responsiveness. Because TEA is non-selective, the findings reflect an integrated response to TEA-sensitive potassium conductances rather than dysfunction of a specific current subtype. Rosiglitazone modified selected electrophysiological responses without normalizing diabetic repolarization.

articles.title: Evaluating procollagen type III N-terminal propeptide (P3NP) as a biomarker of sarcopenia in women with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether circulating procollagen type III N-terminal propeptide (P3NP) improves the diagnosis of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-defined sarcopenia in women with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 99 women with T2DM who underwent standardized clinical assessment, handgrip strength testing, and whole-body DXA. Sarcopenia was defined using a DXA-derived fat-free mass index. Multivariable logistic regression models included age, body mass index, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and estimated glomerular filtration rate, with and without log-transformed, z-standardized P3NP. Discriminatory performance was quantified by the area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals; sensitivity analyses excluded participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60.

RESULTS: P3NP showed weak bivariate correlations with age (p = -0.210) and the Short Physical Performance Battery (p = 0.225). When incorporated into the clinical model, P3NP did not yield a clinically significant improvement (ΔAUC = 0.007). As a sole predictor, P3NP had poor discrimination (AUC 0.53) and was not independently associated with DXA-defined sarcopenia (odds ratio per 1-standard deviation, p > 0.05). Results were consistent after excluding participants with reduced kidney function and across interaction analyses; model calibration was adequate. P3NP absolute values were elevated, with 80.8% above the high threshold (>31 μg/L), and clinical/functional profiles were broadly similar P3NP strata.

CONCLUSION: In women with T2DM, circulating P3NP was not an independent discriminator of DXA-defined sarcopenia and provided no clinically meaningful advantage over standard clinical predictors. Routine screening should continue to rely on assessments of muscle strength, function, and DXA-based body composition, while P3NP may be considered an adjunct marker of extracellular matrix remodeling.

articles.title: Histo-blood group secretor status does not influence mucus plugging or asthma exacerbation outcomes.
authors: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Severe Asthma Research Program-3
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Fucosyltransferase2 (FUT2) activity in airway epithelial cells (AECs) determines if histo-blood group antigens (HBGAs) are components of mucin glycans. "Secretors" (with at least one functioning copy of FUT2) have HBGA-decorated mucins, whereas "non-secretors" (homozygous for null mutations in FUT2) do not. Prior research in animal models of asthma and in human asthma suggests that non-secretor status protects against mucus plugging and that type O secretors are prone to exacerbations.

METHODS: Secretor status was determined in 507 participants in the Severe Asthma Research Program-3 (SARP-3) using a fucose lectin binding assay in sputum and FUT2 genotyping. Blood group was determined using ABO genotyping. Mucus plugging was assessed using the computed tomography (CT)-derived mucus plug segment score, and exacerbation frequency was determined prospectively. We also explored the functional effects of secretor status on mucin outcomes in AECs in culture.

RESULTS: Secretor status determined by lectin binding in sputum was strongly concordant with FUT2 genotype. Among the SARP-3 participants, 26.2% were non-secretors, 32.3% were type O secretors, and 41.4% were non-type O secretors. Mucus plug segment scores were similar in secretor and non-secretor subgroups, and exacerbation rates were similar in type O secretors and other secretor subgroups. Mucin gene expression in AECs from secretors and non-secretor donors was similar, as were measures of mucociliary clearance and mucus gel viscosity and elasticity.

CONCLUSION: Secretor status does not influence mucus plugging or exacerbation outcomes in the SARP-3 cohort, and it does not have significant effects on mucin expression or biophysical properties of airway mucus.

articles.title: Life's Essential 8 score and arterial stiffness in patients with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Research examining the connection between Life's Essential 8 score (LE8) and arterial stiffness (AS) in patients with diabetes is currently insufficient. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between cardiovascular health and the development of AS in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in a cohort study.

SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 2,685 patients with T2D were enrolled in this study. All patients were divided into four groups based on quartiles of cumulative exposure of LE8 (cum-LE8) score. The study endpoint was increased AS (iAS), which was defined as a brachial - ankle pulse wave velocity ≥ 1800 cm/s. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to determine the cumulative incidence of iAS, while the log-rank test was utilized to evaluate the differences among groups. Cox proportional hazards regression model was applied to investigate the impact of various cum-LE8 groups on the risk of iAS.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 9.76 years, we identified 1,375 cases of iAS. The incidence rate of iAS in the quartile 1-4 were 71.02 (64.24-78.52), 67.68 (61.13-74.94), 56.05 (50.28-62.47) and 50.47 (45.05-56.53) per 1000 person-years, respectively. The cumulative incidence of iAS was highest in quartile 1 and gradually decreased from quartile 1 to quartile 4 (log-rank P < 0.01). Compared with quartile 1, the hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) of quartile 2-4 were 0.69 (0.59-0.80), 0.41 (0.35-0.49), and 0.15 (0.12-0.18), respectively.

CONCLUSION: Attaining a superior long-term cardiovascular health status is related to a reduced risk of iAS.

articles.title: Erratum: Latin American Thyroid Society expert panel consensus on anaplastic thyroid cancer.
Hepatic steatosis and postprandial hyperglucagonemia in early type 2 diabetes: Revisiting the liver-α-cell axis.
The influence of health conditions, lifestyle factors, and stress on seafarers' self-rated health - a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-rated health (SRH) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active-duty seafarers. A total of 22,432 international seafarers who were on board were included in the analysis of an electronic survey distributed via 52 shipping and manning companies in February-March 2024.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: An 82-item questionnaire assessed SRH, self-reported health conditions, lifestyle factors (physical activity, sleep/feeling rested, smoking, alcohol risk, loneliness, screen time), and perceived stress. Cross-sectional analyses used descriptive statistics and logistic regression. Models were adjusted for age, sex, rank, and time on board; stress was added as an independent predictor. Additive interactions between stress and lifestyle factors were evaluated using relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI).

RESULTS: Poor SRH was strongly associated with multimorbidity and selected conditions, particularly depression/anxiety, gastrointestinal issues, and musculoskeletal issues. In fully adjusted lifestyle models, sedentary behavior, not feeling rested, smoking, loneliness, and excess screen time remained associated with poor SRH, while alcohol risk was not. Stress was independently associated with poor SRH and amplified the effects of not feeling rested, loneliness, and excess screen time. Self-rated health captured a combined burden of physical and mental symptoms as well as recovery--related and psychosocial factors relevant to life at sea. The stress-sensitive clustering of poor sleep/rest, loneliness, and high screen time suggests that interventions may be most effective when stress management is integrated with fatigue and social-connection measures.

CONCLUSIONS: Health conditions and modifiable lifestyle/psychosocial factors were associated with seafarers' SRH, and perceived stress acted as both an independent predictor and an effect modifier. Targeting sleep, stress, social well-being, and sedentary recovery patterns may improve perceived health and potentially safety on board.

articles.title: Spatial Statistics for Screening Molecular Structures.
articles.abstract: The dominant paradigm in computational materials discovery relies on heavily parameterized deep architectures, including message-passing graph and equivariant networks, that typically require large density functional theory (DFT)-labeled training sets and produce nonconvex latent representations complicating inverse design, a limitation in the data-scarce regimes common to exploratory screening. Standard formulations also face specific difficulties with chemically disordered configurations and with distinguishing chiral geometries (e.g., E ( 3 )  -invariant models are reflection-blind by construction). These are task- and formulation-dependent tendencies, not universal deficiencies, and are reduced by pre-training, transfer, and equivariant designs. This review presents spatial-statistics feature engineering as a physically rigorous, deployable complement. Molecular structures are encoded as voxelized fields, and two-point auto- and cross-correlations are evaluated deterministically via Fast Fourier Transforms, moving spatial pattern recognition into a closed-form, physics-informed operation. Principal component analysis yields low-dimensional, convex representations supporting lean neural networks and non-parametric surrogates, achieving sub-2% normalized errors from as little as 0.1% of the dataset in reported cases. Demonstrated across periodic crystals, disordered high-entropy alloys, and non-periodic molecules, the framework enables Bayesian active learning and zero-shot extrapolation on commodity hardware, which remains challenging for large-scale architectures at equal data budgets.

articles.title: Pulmonary embolism in shoulder arthroplasty: a National Joint Registry Study.
articles.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In the UK, there is no specific guidance on prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism (VTE) following shoulder arthroplasty (SA). This study reviews the current incidence of pulmonary embolism (PE) and prophylaxis practices following SA in England.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Joint Registry (NJR) for all SAs from 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2022 and linked with Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). ICD-10 codes identified incidence of PE at 30 and 90 days from arthroplasty. Incidence for PE was calculated by cohort and implant type at 30 and 90 days postoperatively. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated independently with PE.

RESULTS: A total of 47,145 procedures were included in the NJR HES linked database; 26,403 reverse SAs (RSAs), 12,736 total SAs (TSAs) and 8,006 hemiarthroplasties (HAs). The cumulative incidence of PE was 0.25% at 30 days and 0.33% at 90 days. By implant type, the cumulative incidence was 0.32% following RSA, 0.15% following TSA and 0.18% following HA at 30 days, and 0.41%, 0.21% and 0.25%, respectively, at 90 days. Chemical VTE prophylaxis was received following 74.55% of procedures and mechanical prophylaxis following 96.27%. Most common chemical prophylaxis was low molecular weight heparin (91.34%). Congestive cardiac failure, peripheral vascular disease, metastatic disease and trauma indication were associated independently with PE.

CONCLUSIONS: Although uncommon, PE remains an important postoperative complication given its associated morbidity and mortality. Despite most patients receiving some form of prophylaxis no agreed guidance exists in SA and further studies are needed to inform such guidance.

articles.title: Voluntary levamisole intoxication: a rare case of reversible neurological toxicity without cocaine co-ingestion.
Age-associated clinical patterns in paediatric myocarditis: left ventricular function as the key early risk stratifier.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: In myocarditis, early identification of high-risk patients is essential, robust prognostic markers are lacking. We aimed to identify early clinical risk stratifier at index hospitalization for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

METHODS: We analysed 725 paediatric patients with possible/definite myocarditis enrolled in the prospective multicentre MYKKE registry (2013-2024). MACE included mechanical circulatory support (MCS), heart transplantation, or death during initial admission. Model-based recursive partitioning (MOB) and bootstrap-based logistic regression with multiple imputation were applied for risk stratifier selection out of 20 baseline variables. The model was externally validated in the Swedish SWEDCON- cohort (n = 243). Discrimination was assessed by the area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Among 725 patients (median age 14.3 years [IQR 4.0-16.4]; 33% female), 88 (12.2%) experienced MACE (MCS 10.9%, transplantation 4.3%, death 2.2%). MOB identified left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 39% as the only stable risk stratifier, delineating a "heart failure type" in younger children (1.9 years; LVEF 24%), and a "chest pain type" in adolescents with preserved LVEF (15.6 years; LVEF 59%). LVEF was confirmed as the sole robust risk stratifier (OR per 1% increase: 0.90 ; 95% CI 0.881-0.917; p < 0.01; AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.896-0.903). In SWEDCON (7.4% MACE), discrimination was maintained (AUC 0.894, 95% CI 0.80-0.991).

CONCLUSION: Reduced LVEF at presentation was the only reproducible and externally validated risk stratifier of MACE during index hospitalization. Two age-associated clinical patterns were observed: a high-risk "heart failure type" in younger children and low-risk "chest pain type" in adolescents.

articles.title: Increasing paced heart rate reduces cerebral pulsatility.
articles.abstract: Cerebral pulsatility is a key index of cerebral haemodynamics, a central determinant of intravascular shear stress within intracranial vessels, and is associated with cerebral small vessel disease. It increases with a spontaneously falling heart rate, but the effect of altering heart rates on cerebral haemodynamics is unknown. We therefore tested whether increasing paced heart rate would reduce middle cerebral artery Gosling's pulsatility index (PI)on transcranial ultrasound, during emergency or elective implantation of a pacemaker for bradycardia. In 20 participants (14 males, mean age 78), paced heart rate was increased from 50 bpm or the individual's resting heart rate up to 100 bpm in 10 bpm increments. Cerebral pulsatility was strongly and inversely associated with heart rate, with an average reduction in PI of 0.07 per 10 beats per minute in unadjusted analyses, and 0.08 in mixed effects linear models adjusted for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors (P < 0.001). Increasing heart rate reduced peak systolic velocity by 2.51 cm/s per 10 bpm and increased end-diastolic velocity by 1.26 cm/s per 10 bpm, which both mediated the effect on cerebral pulsatility. However, there was no effect on mean velocity. The decrease in peak systolic middle cerebral artery velocity was linear with increasing heart rate, but end-diastolic velocity was maximal at a heart rate of 80 bpm. Overall, cerebral pulsatility was inversely and causally associated with paced heart rate. Heart rate modification could be a potential intervention to modify cerebral pulsatility, particularly in the context of bradycardia induced by heart block.

articles.title: Modified parasacral flap for pilonidal sinus disease: an easier reproducible option.
articles.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is an acquired chronic infection that commonly involves the natal cleft, is difficult to treat and has high recurrence after surgery. The parasacral perforator flap is a useful and effective flap for coverage after excision of disease. However, it requires technical expertise and specialised equipment. We have modified the technique by leaving the base of the flap, the perforator and surrounding tissue and fat intact, making the procedure easier for general or plastic surgeons to perform.

METHODS: We included 20 consecutive patients with PSD who underwent surgical reconstruction with this technique between November 2014 and January 2022.

RESULTS: All patients were male, with a mean age of 28.35 years. Average flap size was 5 × 11.75cm. In all cases, perforators were found at the 12 o'clock and 1 o'clock positions. All the flaps survived entirely. There were minor complications in two patients, which were managed conservatively. Mean follow-up was 8.65 months. None of the patients had recurrence at final follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with PSD, our modification of the parasacral perforator flap is useful for reconstruction. The procedure is easy to perform and does not require specialised equipment or microvascular and perforator dissection expertise.

articles.title: Preoperative transthoracic echocardiogram and delay to geriatric hip fracture surgery.
articles.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delays to surgery confer increased morbidity and mortality in elderly patients who have sustained hip fractures. Preoperative investigations including transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) are often requested. The aim of this study was to determine whether there were delays to surgery when these patients underwent preoperative TTE.

METHODS: Electronic databases were searched from inception until April 2025. All relevant studies were identified with data extracted and meta-analysed.

FINDINGS: A total cohort of 2,581 patients was extracted from 5 studies; 865 (34%) patients received a preoperative TTE, and 1,716 (66%) patients did not. Baseline characteristics of age, sex, fracture pattern and treatment were similar. Patients receiving a preoperative TTE were more likely to have coronary artery disease (CAD), congestive cardiac failure (CCF) and arrythmia. The mean time to surgery was 9.4h (p = 0.09) shorter in the group not receiving a TTE. The mean length of hospital stay was 0.6 days (p = 0.03) shorter in those who did not receive a preoperative TTE.

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between time to surgery and preoperative TTE. However, the data available are limited by heterogeneity, confounding and insufficient statistical power. In general, improving access to, and efficiency in TTE could help minimise delays to surgery, particularly in centres with limited resources. Strict adherence to American College of Cardiology guidelines for preoperative TTE indications is recommended.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
articles.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI).

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework.

RESULTS: The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification.

CONCLUSIONS: Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.

articles.title: Enoxaparin dose assessment in paediatric cardiology patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enoxaparin is a commonly utilized anticoagulant, particularly in infants and children. Recent literature has highlighted the need to initiate enoxaparin at higher doses, especially at younger ages, due to differences in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. The aim of this study was to investigate the enoxaparin dose required to achieve therapeutic effect in patients ≤ 2 months, >2 to ≤ 6 months, >6 to ≤ 12 months, and >12 months old.

METHODS: This retrospective chart review includes patients aged 0-18 years admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit over a five-year period. Patients were included who achieved a therapeutic anti-Xa within goal of 0.5-1 units/mL.

RESULTS: Seventy-one patients were included in the analysis; 26 (37%) were ≤ 2 months old, 21 (30%) were >2 to ≤ 6 months old, 10 (14%) were >6 to ≤12 months old, and 14 (20%) were >12 months old. There was a significant difference in the median enoxaparin dose required among these age groups, with medians of 2.13 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.95, 2.53], 1.81 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.52, 2.40], 1.44 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.31, 1.71], and 1.16 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.00, 1.26], respectively (p < 0.001). The difference between initial and therapeutic doses was greater in infants compared to children >12 months of age, despite higher initial doses in patients ≤ 6 months old.

CONCLUSIONS: Infants admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit required an increased median enoxaparin dose and a higher number of dosing changes and experienced longer times to achieve therapeutic anti-Xa levels compared to older children.

articles.title: Competitive Sports Participation and Its Association with Glycemic Control and Disordered Eating Behaviors in Individuals with Type 1 Diabetes Running: Competitive Sports, Glycemic Control T1D.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) often face unique challenges in maintaining glycemic control, with a higher risk of disordered eating behaviors (DEB). While physical activity may be associated with improved metabolic outcomes, its relationship with DEB in adolescents with T1D remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics and prevalence of DEB among adolescents and young adults with T1D who participate in competitive sports compared to their non-athlete peers.

METHODS: An observational, cross-sectional study of 245 individuals with T1D, 13 to 21 years of age. All adolescents and young adults with T1D receiving care at our clinic, including those in competitive sports who were additionally followed by the Pediatric Diabetes Sports Clinic, were eligible for inclusion. Data were collected from medical charts, personal technological devices for assessment of glycemic variability, and self-reported questionnaires, including assessments of DEB.

RESULTS: From all participants, 12.2% were engaged in competitive sports. Participation in competitive sports was associated with lower HbA1c (OR: 0.44, 95% CI: 0.24-0.80, P = 0.007), lower DEB (OR: 0.17, 95% CI: 0.04-0.67, P = 0.012), higher BMI-Z score (OR: 1.70, 95% CI: 1.02-2.83, P = 0.04), and higher socioeconomic position (OR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.05-1.69, P = 0.015). Participants who engaged in competitive sports were more likely to use hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems compared to those who did not (36.6% vs. 17.6%, respectively, P = 0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: Competitive sports participation in adolescents and young adults with T1D is associated with improved glycemic control and a lower prevalence of DEB. These findings highlight the potential benefits of encouraging structured physical activity as part of comprehensive diabetes care.

articles.title: Global Neurointensive Care: A Field Yet to Be Born.
articles.abstract: Neurological conditions represent the leading cause of disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) and the second leading cause of death globally, with more than 11 million deaths annually, 87% of which occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). While global neurosurgery has emerged as a recognized field with dedicated frameworks for advocacy and action, the critical care continuum of neurological disease has been persistently overlooked. Global neurointensive care (GNIC) does not yet exist as a formally defined discipline, yet its need is urgent and measurable: ICU bed density in LMICs ranges from 0.1 to 2.5 per 100,000 inhabitants compared with 5 to 30 per 100,000 in high-income countries (HICs); a cross-sectional survey of 408 providers from 42 LMICs found that only 36.8% had access to a dedicated neurointensive care unit; and traumatic brain injury (TBI) mortality at 6 months exceeds 37% in Latin American LMICs. This viewpoint defines GNIC, characterizes the epidemiological and structural dimensions of the unmet need with granular supporting evidence, reviews existing initiatives and their limitations, and proposes a 6-domain strategic agenda for its development. GNIC must be established as a field parallel and complementary to global neurosurgery, ensuring the critical care continuum of neurological disease is not abandoned in the global effort towards universal health coverage.

articles.title: Hepatitis D virus infection in persons with HIV and hepatitis B virus across Europe: A cross-sectional analysis of the HDV-Europe cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infection with hepatitis D virus (HDV) is known to accelerate the progression of liver disease and is associated with mortality in individuals with HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, little is known about current HDV epidemiology, including HDV-testing practices and prevalence, in this population in Europe.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of clinical cohorts across Europe (Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Switzerland and United Kingdom). Included individuals were those living with HIV, ever hepatitis B surface antigen positive, aged ≥18 years and actively in care on December 31, 2023. We calculated the percentage of individuals tested for HDV, prevalence of individuals who ever had anti-HDV positive serology (i.e., past/current infection) and the prevalence of individuals whose last HDV RNA result was positive (i.e., active infection).

RESULTS: A total of 2970 individuals were included. Anti-HDV antibody results were available in 2189 (73.7%). Of them, 261 (12.0%) had past/current HDV infection, ranging between 3.8% in the United Kingdom and 27.3% in Poland. Among the 261 individuals with an anti-HDV-positive result, 162 (62.1%) had been tested for HDV RNA. Of them, 92 (56.8%) had active HDV infection. Of the overall population with available data, active HDV infection was observed in 4.4% (n = 92/2077), ranging between 0.9% in the Netherlands and 11.0% in Italy.

CONCLUSIONS: In Europe, about one-eighth of individuals with HIV/HBV in care have evidence of past/current HDV infection, in whom half have active HDV infection. Nevertheless, these results come from a setting where one-quarter have yet to be tested for anti-HDV antibodies.

articles.title: Mechanical ventilation before and during veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VV ECMO) has revolutionized severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) management by decoupling gas exchange from native lung function, minimizing ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). However, optimizing mechanical ventilation before and during extracorporeal support remains unstandardized.

AREAS COVERED: Pre-ECMO management heavily influences survival, requiring clinicians to balance the cumulative 'dose' of injurious ventilation against cannulation timing. On ECMO, practice remains divided between an 'open lung approach,' using higher PEEP to prevent derecruitment, and a 'closed lung approach,' prioritizing low PEEP and near-complete lung rest. Transitioning to spontaneous breathing introduces a trade-off between preventing diaphragmatic atrophy and risking patient self-inflicted lung injury (P-SILI) from excessive transpulmonary pressure swings. This review synthesizes evidence, addresses key controversies on cardiopulmonary interplay and weaning, and outlines strategies for personalizing ventilation during VV ECMO. We searched in the Medline database from inception to August 2026 to identify relevant literature on the management of veno-venous ECMO in the pre-ECMO phase, on-support, and during the weaning phases from VV ECMO.

EXPERT OPINION: VV ECMO enables lung-protective ventilation and 'buys time' for native lung recovery, but optimal management across the pre-ECMO, on-support, and weaning phases remains non-standardized and requires individualized, physiology-driven strategies rather than fixed protocols.

articles.title: Association of Referring Specialty With Limb Loss in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveChronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. While delayed referral is known to worsen outcomes, the impact of referring specialty remains unclear. This study evaluates whether different referral sources to vascular surgery impact mortality and major amputation rates.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted of patients referred to vascular surgery for CLTI at a single institution (2021-2022). The outcomes investigated were mortality, amputation and composite freedom from amputation or mortality (amputation free survival). Univariable analysis was first conducted followed by multivariable Cox regression utilizing variables which had a univariable P value of <0.1 for the outcomes.ResultsAmong 132 patients, 19.7% died and 19.7% underwent major amputation. Mean duration of follow up for included patients was 1471 days (4.03 years). Congestive heart failure (CHF) independently predicted mortality (HR 3.86, P = .0114) on multivariable analysis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD), gangrene, and non-healing wounds were associated with amputation on univariable analysis (P < .05). Referral from emergency medicine had multivariable association with higher amputation rates, while podiatry referral demonstrated a protective effect (HR 0.28, P = .0472). Referral from emergency medicine had multivariable association with reduced amputation free survival relative to all other specialties combined (HR 2.953 (1.66-5.26), P < .001) and relative to other specialties individually (P = .0023).ConclusionsOutcomes in CLTI are associated with variations in both comorbidities and referral patterns. Earlier, multidisciplinary referral pathways may improve limb salvage as patients with CLTI referred from emergency have higher amputation rates and reduced amputation free survival.

articles.title: Pocket guide Biologics in upper and lower airway diseases 2026 by EUFOREA.
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, biologic therapies targeting key inflammatory pathways have fundamentally transformed the treatment landscape for patients with chronic inflammatory airway diseases. These therapies are now widely approved worldwide and increasingly implemented in routine clinical practice (1). Real-world studies confirm their effectiveness beyond controlled clinical trial settings and highlight biologics as a major therapeutic advance for severe uncontrolled chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), asthma, and eosinophilic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (2-4). Biologics have been shown to significantly improve disease control and potentially enable the achievement of new treatment goals, including clinical and complete remission (5).

articles.title: Cost-Utility Analysis of an Integrated CBT-E Inpatient-Day Patient Treatment Pathway for Treatment-Experienced Anorexia Nervosa in the United Kingdom.
articles.journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate lifetime cost-utility of an integrated enhanced cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT-E) inpatient-day patient pathway versus prolonged inpatient treatment-as-usual (TAU) for treatment-experienced adults with anorexia nervosa requiring intensive specialist treatment in the United Kingdom.

METHOD: A five-state cohort Markov model estimated societal costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a lifetime horizon using published clinical and UK economic inputs. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses examined parameter uncertainty.

RESULTS: The integrated pathway was associated with 23.30 modelled QALYs and costs of £234,379.69, compared with 18.64 QALYs and £831,105.70 for TAU: an incremental gain of 4.65 QALYs and savings of approximately £596,726. Findings were most sensitive to treatment responsiveness, relapse, readmission, and chronic disease costs. Probabilistic analyses were broadly consistent with the base-case findings under the specified assumptions.

CONCLUSIONS: These pathway-level, model-based estimates suggest potential health and economic benefits for this intensive-care population. They depend on assumptions about relapse, recovery, and long-term service use and do not isolate the effect of CBT-E psychotherapy. Findings can inform research and service planning. Prospective comparative economic evaluation remains necessary.

articles.title: Subspecialty headache clinic visit reduced healthcare utilization in patients with migraine: Single institution retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate whether care in a subspecialty headache center, compared with a general neurology clinic, was associated with lower 90-day unplanned healthcare utilization (HCU) in patients with migraine and to identify patient-level factors associated with higher unplanned HCU.

BACKGROUND: Migraine is a common, disabling condition that frequently prompts emergency department (ED) evaluation and treatment. It ranks among the leading global causes of years lived with disability and imposes a substantial financial burden. People with migraine are most often managed in general neurology clinics rather than in specialty centers. Subspecialty headache centers can offer more advanced and guideline-based care, but their impact on post-visit HCU is not well defined.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of adults with a migraine diagnosis cared for at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center from 2018 to 2023. Unplanned HCU was defined as any ED visit, urgent care encounter, or hospital admission within 90 days after the index outpatient general neurology or subspecialty headache center visit (first qualifying migraine-coded encounter in the study period). Associations between clinic type and unplanned HCU were evaluated with adjustment for age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, Area Deprivation Index, and comorbidities, and, in a subset with available data, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System 16-item Profile (PROMIS-16) domains.

RESULTS: Of 38,472 patients included, 16,209 (42.1%) were evaluated in the subspecialty headache center. Total 90-day unplanned HCU was 12.6% in the subspecialty headache center vs. 15.4% in general neurology clinics (p < 0.001). Subspecialty headache center evaluation was associated with 15% lower odds of unplanned HCU (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79-0.90, p < 0.001). The association remained after accounting for patient characteristics (aOR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92) and PROMIS-16 domains (aOR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.59-0.76). Higher unplanned HCU was also associated with younger age at diagnosis, Medicaid and Medicare insurance/coverage, non-White races, comorbidities like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, and worse pain interference and physical function scores.

CONCLUSION: Evaluation in a subspecialty headache center was associated with approximately 15% lower odds of 90-day unplanned HCU. Subspecialized migraine care may represent a high-value care model.

articles.title: IFN-λ fine tunes protective immunity during mucosal viral infection.
Interferon-λ inhibits immunopathology and boosts T cell-mediated immunity in a mouse model of mucosal viral infection.
articles.abstract: Interferon lambda (IFN-λ) has emerged as a critical inducer of immune regulation in addition to its mucosal antiviral properties. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern its dual role during viral infections remain unclear. Here, we discovered that mucosal delivery of IFN-λ abrogates the herpes simplex virus type 2-induced (HSV-2-induced) vaginal tissue pathology observed in the absence of type I IFN signaling, through drastically inhibiting IL-6 production. At the same time, we demonstrated that IFN-λ rescued local production of CD4+ T cell-dependent IFN-γ, which is essential for protection against the development of toxic megacolon following genital HSV-2 infection. Mechanistically, we found that IFN-λ enhances the differentiation of CCR2+Ly6Chi cells into monocyte-derived antigen-presenting cells, thereby boosting T cell responses. In vivo depletion of CCR2+ cells abrogated this phenomenon. Together, these findings suggest that IFN-λ orchestrates a potent antiviral response, inhibiting hyperinflammatory responses while selectively augmenting effector T cell function. This study positions IFN-λ as a promising therapeutic candidate for enhancing local antiviral immunity and offers new insights into the regulation of immune responses in the context of mucosal viral infections.

articles.title: Sepsis-associated endothelial dysfunction: clinical phenotypes, biomarkers, bedside evidence, and translational implications.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a systemic vascular disorder in which endothelial activation, dysfunction, and structural injury contribute to shock, microcirculatory failure, immunothrombosis, and multiorgan dysfunction. Sepsis-associated endotheliopathy is not a uniform process but a dynamic trajectory that evolves from adaptive endothelial activation toward functional disruption, structural injury, and organ-specific vascular failure. In this Review, we propose a phenotype- and trajectory-oriented framework that integrates clinical manifestations, molecular mechanisms, and translational assessment of endothelial dysfunction in sepsis. We focus on four major clinically recognizable modes of endothelial dysfunction that often overlap and evolve over the course of sepsis. We further discuss biology-anchored biomarker panels, bedside physiological surrogates, and serial trajectory-based assessment as complementary approaches for identifying endothelial states, refining risk stratification, and guiding future precision strategies. Finally, we describe implications for biomarker-enriched clinical trials, microvascular-informed resuscitation, and endotype-guided endothelial cell-targeted therapies. Viewing sepsis through the lens of dynamic endotheliopathy provides a framework linking vascular biology to clinically interpretable trajectories and may facilitate the development of personalized approaches to endothelial cell-directed care.

articles.title: Multimodal assessment of exceptional responders refines subtyping-directed precision treatment in HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDWe previously defined 4 hormone receptor+/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2- (HR+/HER2-) subtypes: SNF1 canonical luminal, SNF2 immunogenic, SNF3 proliferative, and SNF4 RTK driven. The FASCINATE-N proof-of-concept trial demonstrated that subtyping-directed precision treatment improves pathologic complete response in locally advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer, yet efficacy remains suboptimal.METHODSWe integrated transcriptomic, genomic, digital pathology, and clinical data from this trial (n = 230) and focused on exceptional responders to explore opportunities for refining treatment strategies.RESULTSIn SNF1, we uncovered that perineural invasion diminished endocrine therapy efficacy, suggesting the potential benefit of incorporating perineural blockade. Digital pathology and spatial transcriptomics identified that the spatial architecture of the tumor-stromal-immune interface influenced apatinib efficacy in SNF4, highlighting the importance of interfering with the tumor microenvironment. In the SNF3 group, exceptionally well responders exhibited multiple mutations in DNA repair genes and cell cycle activation, correlating with the efficacy of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase and CDK4/6 inhibitors. Additionally, we illustrated that lymphatic vessel infiltration was linked to improved immunotherapy outcomes in HR+/HER2- SNF2 tumors.CONCLUSIONOverall, our study emphasizes the importance of multimodal assessments in optimizing precision treatments for HR+/HER2- breast cancer.FUNDINGNational Natural Science Foundation of China, grant numbers U25C2032, 82441028, and 82573645; The Shanghai Key Laboratory of Breast Cancer, grant number 12DZ2260100; The Human Phenome Data Center of Fudan University.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05582499.

articles.title: Reply to Letter to the Editor Regarding "Infection Risk Following Orthopaedic Sports Knee Surgery Is Greater in Pediatric Patients With Allergic Disease History".
Effects of dietary quality on type 2 diabetes risk and the mediating role of inflammatory markers.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the association between multiple dietary quality indices and diabetes risk and investigate the potential role of systemic inflammatory markers in such relationships. Data were obtained from 21 476 participants in the Fuqing Cohort Study who completed a FFQ. Dietary quality was assessed using the Healthy Eating Index (HEI), Diet Quality Index (DQI) and Diet Balance Index (DBI). Logistic regression models were used to examine associations among dietary quality, inflammatory markers and glycemic status. Mediation models were employed to evaluate potential mediating effects of eleven systemic inflammatory markers. All three dietary indices were inversely associated with diabetes risk. Compared with participants in the lowest dietary quality category, the adjusted OR (95 % CI) of the highest dietary quality category were 0·863 (0·768, 0·970) for HEI, 0·719 (0·640, 0·807) for DQI and 0·852 (0·754, 0·961) for DBI. Single-mediator analyses showed potential indirect effects of the HEI on diabetes risk via total white blood cell count, neutrophil, monocyte counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and systemic immune-inflammation index, with mediated proportions of 10·67 %, 11·32 %, 4·05 %, 3·22 % and 3·26 %, respectively. In the parallel multiple mediation model including all mediators, a potential indirect effect (OR = 0·980; 95 % CI: 0·759, 0·963) was observed, with a mediated proportion of 8·83 %. Higher dietary quality, as assessed by the HEI, DQI and DBI, is inversely associated with hyperglycaemia risk and linked to lower levels of systemic inflammatory markers. The adverse association of poor dietary quality with diabetes risk may be partially mediated by systemic inflammatory factors.

articles.title: Selective Serotonin Receptor (5-HT3) Antagonist Prescribing in Cancer Inpatients: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Selective serotonin receptor (5-HT3) antagonists are first-line antiemetics for chemotherapy-induced, radiotherapy-induced, and post-operative nausea and vomiting; other causes of nausea in advanced cancer warrant alternative agents. We aimed to determine patterns of inpatient 5-HT3 antagonist prescribing and its guideline concordance.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed electronic medical records of all patients admitted under Medical Oncology at a single metropolitan hospital over 6 months who were prescribed a 5-HT3 antagonist. Data on demographics, cancer, and the prescription (agent, indication, prescriber, duration, administration) were extracted and reviewed for guideline concordance. Analyses were descriptive.

RESULTS: Of 210 patients admitted between January and June 2025, 81 (38.6%) were prescribed a 5-HT3 antagonist. Mean age was 64.2 years (range 24-87); 41 (50.6%) were female, and 62 (76.5%) had metastatic cancer. Of 137 prescriptions written, 134 (97.8%) were for ondansetron. Nausea was documented in 104 (75.9%), but a specific cause in only 55/104 (52.9%). The most common prescribers were Emergency (62, 45.3%) and After-Hours (32, 23.4%) doctors. Prescriptions were brief (median 1 day); 82 (59.9%) were administered at least once, and 62/82 (75.6%) were single-dose. Overall, 93 (67.9%) were non-concordant. Concordance was 10/14 (71.4%) in Medical Oncology, 20/21 (95.2%) in anesthetics and intensive care, 4/4 (100%) in Radiation Oncology, and 4/4 (100%) in Palliative Care, but 2/62 (3.2%) in Emergency and 4/32 (12.5%) in After-Hours prescribers.

CONCLUSION: 5-HT3 antagonists were frequently prescribed outside guideline recommendations, particularly by clinicians less familiar with cancer. Targeted education, electronic order-set redesign, and structured documentation of the suspected mechanism of nausea may improve guideline-concordant antiemetic prescribing.

articles.title: Association between chronic kidney disease and the risk of myelodysplastic syndromes: A large claims database study in Japan.

Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.
articles.abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

articles.title: Distinct Etiological and Clinical Patterns of Acute Mesenteric Ischemia at High Altitude: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chen, Chen, Yang, Li, Xu, Fan, Xu, Zhijuan Liu, and Dong Wu. Distinct etiological and clinical patterns of acute mesenteric ischemia at high altitude: a retrospective comparative study. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.

BACKGROUND: Acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) is a life-threatening abdominal emergency, yet evidence regarding its etiology and clinical outcomes in high-altitude populations remains limited. This study aimed to compare the etiology, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of AMI between high- and low-altitude populations in China.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study at two tertiary referral centers in China: People's Hospital of the Xizang Autonomous Region (PHOXAR; 3,700 m) and Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH; <100 m). Mesenteric venous thrombosis (MVT) comparisons were restricted to the overlapping period of 2020-2024.

RESULTS: Among 186 patients in the high-altitude cohort and 549 in the low-altitude cohort, MVT was more frequent at high altitude (84.9% vs. 61.2%, p < 0.001). 158 high-altitude and 120 low-altitude patients with MVT were compared. Cirrhosis-related (29.1% vs. 11.7%) and erythrocytosis-related MVT (27.2% vs. 1.7%) were more common in the high-altitude cohort, whereas autoimmune disease-related MVT (0.6% vs. 11.7%) and thrombophilia (0 vs. 16.7%) were more frequent in the low-altitude cohort. High-altitude patients had higher hemoglobin/hematocrit, bilirubin, and fibrinogen levels and a higher mean onset-to-admission time (95.4 vs. 30.2 days). They underwent surgery less frequently (29.7% vs. 80.0%, p < 0.001) and had higher in-hospital mortality (26.6% vs. 11.7%, p = 0.004). Mortality was not significantly different among patients admitted within 2 days (31.6% vs. 8.3%, p = 0.111) but remained higher among those admitted after 2 days (25.9% vs. 12.5%, p = 0.012). Male sex, older age, alcohol consumption, smoking, and higher hematocrit, bilirubin, and fibrinogen were independently associated with the high-altitude MVT phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: AMI in the high-altitude population was characterized by a marked predominance of MVT, with distinct etiological and clinical profiles and poorer outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early recognition, timely referral, and improved access to appropriate treatment for AMI in high-altitude settings.

articles.title: Dietary diversity and type 2 diabetes risk: evidence from a prospective Korean cohort study.
articles.abstract: Although consuming a diverse diet is generally considered beneficial for chronic disease prevention, its relationship with type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of overall and within-group dietary diversity scores (DDS) with T2D incidence in the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study-CVD Association Study. A total of 16 666 participants aged 40 years and older without T2D at baseline were followed for 96 609 person-years, during which 953 incident T2D cases were identified. Cumulative average overall DDS and within-group DDS were derived from repeated FFQ administered at each visit. Modified Poisson regression with a robust error variance estimator was used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) and 95 % CI. A significant inverse linear trend was observed between overall DDS and T2D risk (IRR = 0·56, 95 % CI = 0·40-0·79 for men; IRR = 0·73, 95 % CI = 0·54-0·98 for women). Among the five within-group DDS, those for 'Milk and Dairy products' in both sexes, 'Fruits' in men and 'Vegetables/Seaweeds/Mushrooms' in women were inversely associated with T2D (Q4 v. Q1). No significant sex-related interactions were observed (all p for interaction > 0·05). Higher overall DDS and greater within-group diversity in 'Milk and Dairy products,' 'Fruits' and 'Vegetables/Seaweeds/Mushrooms' were associated with lower T2D risk. These findings suggest that maintaining overall dietary diversity - particularly emphasising non-energy-dense food groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy - may help prevent T2D.

articles.title: The relationship between caregiver burden, depression, suicidal thoughts, and quality of life in patients' caregivers in the adult palliative service.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to examine the relationships between caregiver burden, depression, suicidal ideation, and quality of life among caregivers of patients hospitalized in an adult palliative care unit and to identify factors associated with depressive symptoms.

METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 75 caregivers of patients hospitalized in the Adult Palliative Care Unit of Erzurum City Hospital. Data were collected using the Caregiver Strain Index, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation, (OPQOL)-Brief, and SF-36 Health Survey. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Pearson's correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression were performed.

RESULTS: High caregiver strain was reported by 52% of participants. According to HAM-D scores, 24% had mild depressive symptoms, while none had moderate or severe depression. All participants were classified as having low suicidal ideation risk. Significant correlations were observed among physical and mental health, caregiver burden, depression, suicidal ideation, and quality of life (p < 0.05). Mental health was strongly negatively correlated with depression (r = -0.607, p < 0.01) and was the only significant predictor of depressive symptoms in the regression model (β = -0.511, p < 0.001), explaining 40.5% of the variance.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: Mental health was the strongest determinant of depressive symptoms among palliative care caregivers. Although all participants were categorized as having low suicidal ideation risk, continuous suicidal ideation scores were associated with greater caregiver burden, depression, and poorer quality of life. Routine mental health screening and psychosocial support for caregivers should be integrated into palliative care services.

articles.title: Examining spiritual needs, spiritual practices, ritual, and coping in palliative care: An Australian cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to examine religious and post-Christian spiritual orientations, types of spiritual and ritual activities, coping strategies of patients with advanced illness and explore associations between spiritual needs, practices, well-being, quality of life, and coping styles.

METHODS: One hundred and two patients completed validated instruments: Post-Christian Spirituality Scale, Spiritual Needs Questionnaire, Spiritual Practices Questionnaire, Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Spiritual Well-Being Scale, Global Quality of Life Scale, and Brief-COPE Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics and scale distributions. Spearman correlations (Bonferroni-adjusted) examined associations between spiritual needs, practices, and coping modes. Multivariate regression analyses assessed whether ritual practices predicted spiritual needs.

RESULTS: Inner peace (median, 1.4; IQR, 1, 2) and humanistic/prosocial practices (median, 66.6; IQR, 44.4, 83.2) were prominent spiritual needs and frequently used rituals, respectively. Strong correlations were observed between religious needs and religious rituals (rho = 0.87). Existential, inner peace, and giving/generativity needs correlated moderately with existentialistic practices (rho = 0.56-0.69). Humanistic/prosocial spiritual practices were moderately associated with giving/generativity (rho = 0.52) and inner peace needs (rho = 0.42). Emotion-focused coping, particularly acceptance and emotional support, was most consistently associated with spiritual needs and practices, reinforcing the centrality of relational and embodied forms of spirituality at the end of life. Regression analyses confirmed existentialistic practices predicted existential and inner peace needs, while humanistic practices predicted generativity needs.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: Findings demonstrate strong alignment between spiritual needs and ritual activity, supporting development of personalized, ritual-based spiritual care frameworks. Determining individual orientations toward embodied, relational, and humanistic practices may offer an adaptable means of addressing spiritual suffering.

articles.title: Elevated Blood Lead Levels in Children With Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior reports suggest sickle cell disease (SCD) as a risk factor for lead poisoning, this association remains understudied. This paper assesses the relationship between SCD and elevated blood lead levels (BLLs) in New York City children.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective matched cohort study of children born in NYC from 2004 to 2016 and tested for BLLs from 2004 to 2022. Children with SCD were matched 1:2 to children without SCD based on maternal race and country of birth. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression estimated associations between SCD and BLLs ≥3.5, ≥5, ≥10, and ≥15 µg/dL, adjusting for Medicaid status, housing age, and maternal race. Additional analyses evaluated effect modification by age and SCD genotype.

RESULTS: The cohort included 1463 children with SCD and 2982 without SCD. SCD was associated with lower odds of BLLs ≥3.5 µg/dL (odds ratio [OR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.66-0.99), no difference at ≥5 µg/dL (OR 0.86; 95% CI: 0.66-1.10), and higher odds at ≥10 µg/dL (OR 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.13), with a similar estimate at ≥15 µg/dL (OR 2.23; 95% CI: 0.98-5.07). The SCD-by-age interaction was significant at ≥10 µg/dL (OR 4.47; 95% CI: 1.41-15.50), and children with HbSS had significantly higher odds of BLLs ≥10 µg/dL and BLLs ≥15 µg/dL than children without SCD (OR 2.25 and 2.98, respectively).

CONCLUSION: Children with SCD have increased odds of elevated BLLs at higher thresholds, especially those aged ≥3 years and those with HbSS. Targeted rescreening of these children warrants consideration.

articles.title: Human Genetics of Adipose Dysfunction: Genomic Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Cardiometabolic Disease.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases are a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality and arise from shared and distinct risk factors acting through interconnected biological pathways. Although excess adiposity is a major risk factor, body mass index incompletely captures cardiometabolic risk, reflecting heterogeneity in overall and regional fat storage capacity and ectopic lipid accumulation. Failure of subcutaneous adipose tissue to expand appropriately promotes lipid overflow into visceral and ectopic depots, contributing to insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and organ dysfunction. Human genetic studies have identified thousands of genetic loci influencing fat storage, fat distribution, and ectopic lipid accumulation, revealing that these traits reflect distinct underlying mechanisms with divergent cardiometabolic consequences. Recent scaling of genetic discovery for refined adiposity and cardiometabolic phenotypes and multitrait genetic approaches have advanced understanding of adipose-driven disease heterogeneity. We highlight variant-to-function strategies to resolve causal pathways and discuss emerging scalable approaches to accelerate biological learning from genetic discovery and translate these insights into adipose-directed therapeutics for cardiometabolic disease.

articles.title: AI and Deep Learning in Cardiovascular Imaging: From Risk Stratification to Precision Phenotyping.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of cardiovascular disease, yet the complexity and volume of imaging data increasingly exceed the capacity of conventional interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning offer new tools to extract quantitative, prognostic, and phenotypic information from routine cardiovascular images. This review summarizes the fundamentals of AI and deep learning, including model architectures, training strategies, and their relevance to cardiovascular imaging, followed by a focused discussion of current applications across chest radiography, chest computed tomography, computed tomography angiography/cardiac computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and nuclear cardiology imaging. Studies were selected with emphasis on original investigations, large cohort analyses, and external validation studies reflecting current applications of AI in cardiovascular risk stratification and precision phenotyping. Across these modalities, AI applications in automated image processing and analysis have become relatively mature. Multiple multicenter and real-world studies have validated their value in improving efficiency and supporting cardiovascular management. Approaches that move beyond conventional human-defined imaging metrics to infer cardiovascular risk and disease phenotype remain at an earlier stage, requiring further standardization, validation, and clinical evaluation. AI is expanding the role of cardiovascular imaging from visual interpretation toward integrated assessment for risk stratification and precision phenotyping, though further work is needed to confirm generalizability and real-world performance before these tools can guide individual patient management.

articles.title: Prior Venous Thromboembolism Defines Distinct Genetic and Molecular Phenotypes in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) has traditionally been considered a long-term complication of pulmonary embolism. However, a substantial proportion of patients have no history of venous thromboembolism (VTE), suggesting underlying biological heterogeneity.
