METHODS: We analyzed clinical and imaging characteristics of 712 patients with CTEPH stratified by prior VTE history. Whole-genome sequencing was performed in all patients and 2952 healthy controls to assess common variants. Bulk RNA sequencing of pulmonary endarterectomy tissues and plasma protein quantification were integrated to identify and validate subgroup-specific molecular signatures, with further validation in tissue and primary endothelial cells.

RESULTS: Patients with CTEPH and prior VTE (n=576, 80.9%) exhibited a distinct thrombotic phenotype with more proximal disease distribution (92.5% versus 66.2%) and greater likelihood of undergoing pulmonary endarterectomy (22.6% versus 3.7%). Genome-wide association study in CTEPH-VTE(+) patients versus controls identified coagulation-related loci at ABO (rs676996, P=1.1×10-9) and FGG (rs7681423, P=2.5×10-8), with high genetic correlation with pulmonary embolism (rg=0.52, P=0.028). In contrast, no consistent genomic signal was identified in patients without prior VTE. Integrative multiomics (transcriptome-wide association study, MAGMA, and bulk RNA sequencing differential expression analysis) convergently prioritized CTSS (cathepsin S) as a key molecular candidate in CTEPH-VTE(+). CTSS was consistently elevated in plasma, pulmonary endarterectomy tissue, and primary endothelial cells from CTEPH-VTE(+) patients and promoted endothelial proliferation via ERK signaling, which was attenuated by the selective CTSS inhibitor LY3000328.

CONCLUSIONS: Stratification by prior VTE history reveals biologically distinct CTEPH phenotypes with divergent genetic architectures and identifies cathepsin S as a genetically nominated therapeutic target for thrombosis-associated pulmonary vascular remodeling.

articles.title: Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years.

RESULTS: Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.

articles.title: Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Council Stroke and Neurovascular Nursing Science Committee of the Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Stroke Council
articles.abstract: Health literacy is a critical component of high-quality stroke care. Across the continuum from prevention through recovery, health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke-related morbidity. Despite its importance, it is often overlooked, leaving patients and caregivers overwhelmed by communication demands that exceed their capacity. These mismatches are especially pronounced among individuals with stroke-related cognitive or language impairments, limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, or limited digital literacy. This scientific statement synthesizes current evidence on the role of health literacy and communication within stroke systems of care and identifies nurse-led opportunities to advance equity and patient-centered outcomes while recognizing this as a shared interprofessional responsibility. Nurse-led interventions, including teach-back-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, have demonstrated improvements in stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness. However, the literature is marked by methodological heterogeneity. Many studies are underpowered and infrequently use validated health literacy or communication measures. Future directions include standardized assessment of health literacy; literacy-sensitive, nurse-led, and interprofessional care models; workforce training in plain-language and culturally responsive communication; and organizational health literacy principles. Emerging technologies, including telehealth and artificial intelligence, offer promise for improving communication and personalization but require rigorous evaluation to minimize bias and ensure equity and usability.

articles.title: Dental Student Perceived Preparedness to Work With Diverse Patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: The US patient population has become increasingly diverse with complex needs and lived experiences. To address existing gaps in dental education, this study explored dental students' self-reported preparedness to provide care to patients with diverse needs and suggestions to enhance the curriculum.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey developed by an interdisciplinary team was administered to D1-D4 dental students to assess perceived preparedness to work with patients across diverse social, cultural, and clinical contexts. Open-ended items solicited recommendations for curricular improvement. Descriptive statistics summarized preparedness ratings. Independent-samples t-tests compared pre-clinical (D1-D2) and clinical (D3-D4) students. Open-text responses were analyzed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Of 394 eligible students, 187 completed the survey (47.5% response rate), with 113 included in the final analytic sample. On 1-10 scale, students reported moderate preparedness across all diverse identities and experiences, with the lowest preparedness in caring for survivors of sexual violence (M = 4.51), intimate partner violence (M = 4.62), trauma (M = 4.83), and patients with special healthcare needs (M = 4.54), and the highest for patients differing by sexual orientation (M = 7.30), race (M = 7.18), and culture (M = 6.91). Clinical students reported significantly higher preparedness than pre-clinical students across most diverse identities and experiences. Qualitative responses (N = 40) identified recommendations to enhance the curriculum, including opportunities for: (1) Experiential learning, (2) cultural humility, (3) structured communication training, and (4) mentorship/interprofessional education.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings demonstrate that dental students reported feeling least prepared to work with patients who have trauma-related experiences and special health care needs, indicating a gap in the areas of greatest complexity and need. Integrating relational, reflective, and equity-oriented competencies into dental training may improve readiness and capacity to provide compassionate, person-centered oral health care.

articles.title: The impact of non-medical determinants of health on patient-reported outcomes in pediatric lupus: A CARRA registry study.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesSocial determinants of health (SDOH) and race are associated with disease activity, including lower achievement of the low lupus disease activity state (LLDAS), but it is unknown whether these factors are associated with patient-reported outcomes (PROs). Among a cohort with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE) in the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) Registry, we investigated associations between race, SDOH, and PROs.MethodsIn this cSLE cohort study, the primary exposure was self-reported race and ethnicity with collected SDOH including insurance status and area deprivation index (ADI). Our primary outcomes were any functional disability by CHAQ (>0) and overall health by PROMIS Global Health-7 across follow-up. Multivariable regression models assessed these associations, adjusting for demographic and disease-related factors.ResultsAmong 540 children with cSLE, most had CHAQ (86%) and PROMIS Global Health-7 (74%) scores collected at Registry enrollment. Functional disability was common (46%), and overall health was below average (median T score 38.8, IQR 34.0-42.1) at enrollment. In unadjusted and adjusted analyses, race, insurance, and ADI were not significantly associated with either outcome. However, PROMIS completion differed significantly by race (p < 0.001).ConclusionsChildren with cSLE in the CARRA Registry commonly report deficits in functional status and overall health. Although race and SDOH were not significantly associated with PROs, differential PROMIS completion by race suggests the potential for bias in these estimates. Interventions to improve completeness and representativeness of PRO data collection are needed to support accurate assessment of health disparities in cSLE across all patient groups.

articles.title: Statistical signatures of microorganism motility under environmental stress.
articles.abstract: The motility of microorganisms and small aquatic organisms provides a natural framework for studying active matter and its response to environmental perturbations. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trajectories of Paramecium caudatum and Artemia salina individuals under controlled laboratory conditions. Using video microscopy, we track the motion of organisms at low population densities and reconstruct individual trajectories over time. In addition to baseline conditions, we analyze stressed environments in which Paramecium caudatum are exposed to a toxic agent and Artemia salina are placed in distilled water. To characterize the statistical properties of the motion, we compute several trajectory-based metrics, including the mean square displacement, velocity and displacement distributions, average velocities, persistence times and lengths, tortuosity, and radius of gyration. These observables allow us to quantify changes in motility patterns across species, densities, and environmental conditions. To further interpret the observed dynamics, we develop coarse-grained stochastic models with parameters extracted directly from the experimental data. While P. caudatum is described within a run-and-tumble framework, including reversal events under stress, A. salina requires a run-and-tumble-like description with persistent orientational noise, accounting for the continuous directional fluctuations observed during its runs. The models reproduce the main trajectory-level observables used for quantitative comparison, namely tortuosity and radius of gyration. This combined experimental and modeling approach provides insight into how environmental stress modifies locomotion statistics. Our results highlight systematic differences in the statistical signatures of motion across conditions and organisms, suggesting that trajectory-based metrics may serve as indicators of physiological stress. Beyond their biological relevance, this work provides an accessible framework for active matter experiments in which individual-level statistics can be directly measured and modeled.

articles.title: A Self-Adaptive CoNi-Based Metal-Organic Framework for Autonomous Antibacterial Efficacy and Anti-Inflammatory Resolution in Accelerated Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Delayed healing of bacterially infected wounds stems from drug-resistant bacterial invasion and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS)-driven inflammation, which necessitating strategies that simultaneously eradicate pathogens and resolve inflammation. We designed a bimetallic CoNi-based metal-organic framework (CoNi-MOF) with enhanced multienzyme-like activities: oxidase-like (OXD-like), peroxidase-like (POD-like), and catalase-like (CAT-like) activities. The superior performance arises from the synergy between Co and Ni, which shifts the d-band center of Co closer to the Fermi level than those in Co-MOF and Ni-MOF. This electronic structure enhancement facilitates substrate adsorption and lowers reaction energy barriers, accounting for the strong enzyme-like activities of CoNi-MOF. At acidic infection sites, OXD-like and POD-like activities are activated to generate antibacterial ROS, effectively eliminating drug-resistant bacteria. As bacterial clearance occurs and the wound returns to neutrality, CoNi-MOF exhibits CAT-like activity and radical scavenging capabilities to eliminate excess ROS, thereby restoring oxidative balance and mitigating inflammation. Moreover, CoNi-MOF promotes macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype toward the pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. This pH-responsive enzymatic activity offers a self-adaptive therapeutic strategy, as validated by in vivo studies showing accelerated wound healing. This self-adaptive nanozyme platform integrates antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions, offering a promising antibiotic-free treatment for drug-resistant bacterial wound infections.

articles.title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.

articles.title: Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair at Centers With and Without On-Site Cardiac Surgery: A Comparative Registry With a Shared Interventional Team.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence for M-TEER performed at centers with versus without on-site cardiac surgery is lacking. We compared early outcomes at two centers that shared the same interventional operator team but differed in the availability of on-site cardiac surgery.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected registry data from 64 consecutive patients with severe (4+) MR treated at a center without on-site cardiac surgery (no-CCH, n = 21) and a center with on-site cardiac surgery (CCH, n = 43). The same interventional operator team performed every procedure. At the no-CCH center, surgical expertise was provided through a shared Heart Team and a formal emergency transfer pathway. The cohorts were treated in sequential calendar periods. Principal comparative endpoints were MVARC device and procedural success at 30 days. Exploratory non-inferiority analyses used margins of -12.5% and -10%.

RESULTS: MVARC technical success was 100% versus 97.7%. Device and procedural success were each 81.0% versus 72.1% (risk difference [RD] +8.9%, 95% CI -14.9 to +27.5; p = 0.547). Freedom from major MVARC serious adverse events was 95.2% versus 95.3%. Twelve of 16 device-success failures involved a mean transmitral gradient ≥ 5 mmHg. Surgical conversion and in-hospital death were 0% in both centers.

CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary same-team comparison, 30-day MVARC device and procedural success rates were 81.0% at the no-CCH center and 72.1% at the CCH center. Confidence intervals were wide and non-inferiority was not established. These findings support prospective evaluation of network-based M-TEER programs with shared interventional expertise and formal surgical backup.

articles.title: How do neurorehabilitation patients perceive their fundamental care needs? Findings from a qualitative study.
articles.journal: PM & R : the journal of injury, function, and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Fundamentals of Care (FoC) framework provides a structured model to support the delivery of person-centered nursing care by integrating physical, psychosocial, and relational dimensions. Although the framework has been widely applied in acute care, little is known about its relevance in long-term neurorehabilitation settings, where patients often face complex, prolonged, and multidimensional care needs.

OBJECTIVE: To explore how individuals with neurological disorders perceive their fundamental care needs during inpatient rehabilitation.

DESIGN: A qualitative secondary analysis.

SETTING: A rehabilitation hospital in Italy with a total capacity of 109 beds.

PARTICIPANTS: We recruited individuals aged 18 years and older with a diagnosis of stroke, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson disease, or who had undergone neurosurgical intervention for oncological conditions.

METHODS: A deductive content analysis was performed, using the FoC framework to guide coding and thematic development.

FINDINGS: The analysis identified care experiences across the three FoC dimensions. In the physical dimension, patients valued hygiene, toileting, mobility, and comfort not only as technical tasks but also as meaningful acts that contributed to dignity and recovery. The psychosocial dimension emphasized the importance of respectful communication, emotional support, privacy, and being informed, factors that fostered agency and trust. In the relational dimension, patients highlighted empathy, continuity, and presence as central to feeling emotionally safe and supported. Health care assistants emerged as key figures in delivering comfort-focused and relational care. Across all dimensions, fundamental care was perceived as deeply interconnected and resistant to rigid, task-based models.

CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the value of the FoC framework in capturing the multidimensional nature of care as experienced by neurorehabilitation patients. The findings reinforce the need for nurses and assistants to provide care that extends beyond physical tasks to include relational presence and person-centered responsiveness.

articles.title: Impaired Flow and Physiology in Coronaries With Anomalous Origin From the Opposite Sinus of Valsalva.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA) high-risk anatomical features (intramural segment, acute take-off angle, slit-like ostium) cause coronary stenosis leading to myocardial infarction. How these features alter coronary physiology remains unclear.

AIMS: We aimed to evaluate their impact on coronary blood supply using continuous thermodilution.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 51 AAOCA patients undergoing continuous thermodilution. Subjects were classified into an ischemic risk (IR) group (intramural segment, acute angle, oval or slit ostium) or non-ischemic risk (no-IR) group. Non-anomalous coronary arteries served as controls. We measured absolute coronary blood flow (CBF) and microvascular resistance.

RESULTS: Subjects (median age 48.4 years) presented mostly with angina, syncope, and arrhythmia. Final analysis included 48 AAOCA cases (31 IR, 17 no-IR) and 45 controls. The IR group had a median IM length of 9 mm, take-off angle of 31.9°, and a slit-like or oval ostium. The no-IR group had a median angle of 51.5° and an oval or round ostium. At rest, absolute CBF and microvascular resistance showed no significant differences among groups. However, during hyperemia, the IR group had significantly reduced CBF compared to controls (179 vs. 290 mL/min, p = 0.015). The IR group demonstrated higher microvascular resistance at rest (1473 vs. 1150, p = 0.024) and during hyperemia (433 vs. 305, p = 0.012), indicating persistently increased coronary vascular tone.

CONCLUSIONS: High-risk anatomical features of AAOCA are associated with altered coronary physiology. An intramural segment, acute take-off angle, and slit-like or oval ostium are linked to reduced hyperemic coronary blood flow due to increased microvascular resistance.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of Diurnal Salivary Cortisol Profiles in Neoplastic and Non-Neoplastic Hypercortisolism.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Salivary cortisol has the advantages of being non-invasive, readily accessible in ambulatory patients and reflecting the free bioactive fraction of cortisol. The cortisol diurnal cycle, based on six samples collected every 4 hours over a 24-hour period, allows a detailed characterization of cortisol variations throughout the day. The objective of this study was to assess the value of the salivary cortisol diurnal cycle for the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome (CS) and the differential diagnosis of non-neoplastic hypercortisolism.

DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included all the patients hospitalized in Endocrinology department of Cochin Hospital between 2012 and 2018 who had complete serum and salivary diurnal cycle assessments.

METHODS: Serum and salivary cortisol levels were measured using an automated and a radio immunoassay, respectively.

RESULTS: A total of 227 subjects without CS, 46 patients with non-neoplastic CS, 72 patients with ACTH-dependent CS and 67 with adrenal CS were included. For the diagnosis of CS, the cortisol nadir throughout the day showed better diagnostic performance than midnight cortisol, both in serum and saliva with, ROC AUCs of 0.98 and of 0.96, respectively. For the differential diagnosis between non-neoplastic hypercortisolism and ACTH-dependent CS, salivary cortisol showed better diagnostic performance than midnight serum cortisol (ROC AUC 0.97; optimal cut-off 5.3 nM; sensitivity 90%; specificity 87% for the salivary cortisol nadir).

CONCLUSION: The salivary cortisol diurnal cycle appears to be a powerful tool for the diagnosis of CS and for the challenging differential diagnosis of non-neoplastic hypercortisolism, with the major advantage of being accessible in ambulatory patients.

articles.title: Initial treatment strategies and outcomes across haemodynamic thresholds and risk stratification in incident systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a EUSTAR analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Real-world initial treatment strategies in SSc-PAH remain incompletely described. We aimed to characterise these strategies across haemodynamic thresholds and risk strata and evaluate outcome associations.

METHODS: We analysed treatment-naïve SSc-PAH patients in EUSTAR (2000-2021) fulfilling the 2022 haemodynamic definition. Initial therapy comprised treatment initiated within 4 months of RHC. As-treated (AT) analyses were primary and intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses supportive. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and 36-month PAH progression.

RESULTS: Among 301 patients, 198 (66%) initiated therapy and 170 maintained therapy for ≥3 months. Therapy was initiated in 31% with milder haemodynamic impairment (mPAP 21-24 mmHg and/or PVR 2-3 WU) versus 79% fulfilling the previous haemodynamic definition; combination therapy increased from 14% to 67% across low- to high-risk strata. Over a median 3.9 years, 125 (42%) died and 85/227 (37%) progressed. Adjusted ITT analyses showed no association with either outcome, whereas adjusted AT analyses showed lower mortality risk with sustained monotherapy and combination therapy (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.27-0.92 and HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.18-0.88, respectively) and lower PAH progression risk with sustained initial therapy (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.18-0.76). In the milder haemodynamic subgroup, the mortality estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise.

CONCLUSION: Initial treatment strategies reflected haemodynamic severity and baseline risk, while variation suggested potential implementation gaps. Sustained initial therapy was associated with lower risks of mortality and PAH progression. Contrasting ITT and AT estimates highlight challenges in observational treatment-outcome comparisons. Findings in the milder haemodynamic subgroup support dedicated prospective studies.

articles.title: Ultrashort Echo Time Magnetization Transfer MRI for Cortical Bone Collagen Assessment and Its Association With Mineralization in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) increases fracture risk beyond bone mineral density (BMD), implicating matrix quality. Whether ultrashort echo time magnetization transfer (UTE-MT) MRI can track collagen alterations in T1DM and their associations with mineralization is unknown.

PURPOSE: To evaluate UTE-MT-derived magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) for monitoring in vivo cortical collagen alterations in T1DM and to investigate its associations with mineralization and multiscale bone properties.

STUDY TYPE: Longitudinal animal model.

ANIMAL MODEL: 18 male New Zealand white rabbits (Age: 5-6 months) randomized to diabetic (n = 12) and control (n = 6) groups.

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T/3D gradient-echo UTE-MT sequence.

ASSESSMENT: UTE-MT MRI was performed at baseline (week 0) and weeks 12, 16, and 20 post-alloxan induction. Cortical MTR was calculated from paired MT-on/off images and quantified over cortical regions of interest. Reference measurements at the terminal time point (week 20) included micro-CT (cortical porosity [CtPo]), histomorphometry (mineral apposition rate [MAR], bone formation rate [BFR/BS]), fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) (collagen cross-linking), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) (hydroxyproline [Hyp]), histology (collagen maturation), and mechanical testing.

STATISTICAL TESTS: The t-tests/Mann-Whitney U for endpoint cross-sectional comparisons, linear mixed-effects model for longitudinal MTR, Pearson correlations (r) for associations; p < 0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: Cortical MTR declined in T1DM rabbits, becoming significantly lower than controls at week 12 and lowest at week 20. At termination, T1DM group demonstrated significantly higher CtPo (1.345 ± 0.270% vs. 0.591 ± 0.233%), elevated NE-xLR, reduced MAR, BFR/BS, Hyp, ECR, and collagen maturation (1.705 ± 0.548 vs. 5.474 ± 1.455). Mechanical properties (elastic modulus [E], yield strength [YS], toughness) were significantly lower in the T1DM group, with reductions of 44.1%, 35.2%, and 63.2% relative to controls, respectively. MTR at week 20 correlated positively with Hyp, ECR, collagen maturation, mineralization, and mechanical parameters (r = 0.562 to 0.900), and negatively with NE-xLR via partial correlation (r = -0.616) and CtPo (r = -0.826).

DATA CONCLUSIONS: UTE-MT-derived MTR enables in vivo tracking of cortical collagen dynamics in T1DM.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 1.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: Spinal neurocysticercosis: synthesizing evidence on clinical presentations, anatomical patterns, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Spinal neurocysticercosis (NCC) is an uncommon manifestation of NCC involving the spinal cord, meninges, nerve roots, and subarachnoid spaces. Although less common than intracranial disease, spinal involvement can cause substantial neurological morbidity because even small lesions within the confined spinal canal may produce progressive myelopathy. Disease may result from hematogenous dissemination or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) spread of Taenia solium larvae and may present as intramedullary, intradural extramedullary, subarachnoid, or, rarely, extradural lesions. Clinical manifestations are diverse and include paraparesis, quadriparesis, cauda equina syndrome, and chronic meningitis. Magnetic resonance imaging is the diagnostic modality of choice, providing detailed assessment of lesion location, evolutionary stage, inflammatory activity, and associated complications. CSF analysis and immunological or molecular tests provide supportive evidence, while histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis when tissue is available. Treatment is individualized and may include antiparasitic agents, corticosteroids, and surgery when indicated. Although outcomes are generally favorable with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, delayed treatment, extensive arachnoiditis, diffuse leptomeningeal disease, and established spinal cord damage may result in permanent neurological deficits. Further prospective studies are needed to refine diagnostic strategies and optimize management. PubMed database was searched from inception to 13 July 2026, for spinal neurocysticercosis and spinal cysticercosis.

articles.title: Unexpected Oil Cyst Formation Following Lower Blepharoplasty Despite Adinizer-Assisted Microfat Grafting: Limitations of Fat Particle Size Reduction.
articles.abstract: Oil cyst formation after periocular autologous fat grafting is infrequently reported but represents a clinically relevant complication because it may present as a palpable mass and mimic other eyelid lesions. Various fat-processing techniques, including mechanical microfragmentation, have been introduced to reduce fat particle size and improve graft survival. However, whether fat particle size reduction alone can prevent oil cyst formation in the periocular region remains unclear. We report 2 patients who developed periocular oil cysts following lower blepharoplasty with autologous fat grafting performed using a standardized protocol that included Adinizer-assisted mechanical microfragmentation and small-volume injection. A 47-year-old woman with diabetes mellitus developed a fluctuant lower eyelid nodule 3 months postoperatively, which required repeated aspiration but eventually resolved without surgical excision. A 55-year-old woman with hypertension developed a similar lesion 4 months postoperatively that resolved after a single aspiration. These cases demonstrate that periocular oil cysts may occur despite optimized fat-processing techniques, including Adinizer-assisted microfragmentation, suggesting that reduction of fat particle size alone may not be sufficient to prevent this complication. These findings suggest that recipient-site characteristics, surgical factors, and systemic vascular comorbidities may play a more important role than fat-processing methods in determining graft survival.

articles.title: A Genetic Risk Approach to Differential Diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes and Risk Stratification in the Spanish Population.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Accurate type 1 diabetes (T1D) risk assessment can improve diagnosis and preventive care, reducing misdiagnosis and enabling preclinical interventions. Genetic Risk Scores (GRS) offer a promising tool, but population-specific validation is required.Objective. To assess the performance of established vs. a novel Spanish-specific GRS for T1D differential diagnosis and risk stratification.

METHODS: From 2,338 genotyped individuals, 2,215 Spanish participants of European ancestry passed quality control: 816 T1D, 469 type 2 diabetes (T2D), 457 monogenic diabetes (MD), and 473 controls. A novel Spanish-specific GRS (T1D-SP-GRS) was developed and compared with HLA-DRB1 and two European-derived models (T1D-GRS and T1D-GRS2). The best-performing score was evaluated for T1D discrimination vs. T2D and MD, and for association with T1D-onset age.

RESULTS: T1D-GRS2 outperformed T1D-SP-GRS for T1D vs. controls (AUC-ROC: 0.888 [95% CI: 0.867-0.908] vs. 0.837 [0.797-0.877], p=0.001), retaining high discrimination vs. T2D and MD (0.886 [0.865-0.907]). In the combined pediatric-onset T1D and control cohort, the P50 cutoff yielded a sensitivity of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.76-0.84) and specificity of 0.81 (0.77-0.84); P25 prioritized sensitivity (0.97 [0.95-0.99]) while P75 specificity (0.96 [0.93-0.97]). A P90 threshold conferred 26-fold higher T1D odds vs. controls, and 18- and 17-fold vs. T2D and MD (p <0.001). Higher T1D-GRS2 in childhood- vs. adulthood-onset T1D revealed an age-dependent risk profile primarily driven by HLA.

CONCLUSIONS: T1D-GRS2 discriminates T1D from other diabetes etiologies, providing a complementary tool to support diagnostic accuracy. The higher genetic risk associated with a younger age at onset provides key insights for early-stage T1D screening and intervention strategies.

articles.title: Single Jaundice in Cirrhosis: A Neglected Acute Decompensation of Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure and Mortality.
authors: Chinese (Acute on) Chronic Liver Failure Consortium (Ch‐CLIF.C)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the risk of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) and short-term outcomes among cirrhotic patients with single jaundice, acute decompensation (AD) (including ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and/or bacterial infection), and non-AD non-jaundice.

METHODS: We analyzed cirrhotic inpatients without obstructive jaundice enrolled from two large multicenter prospective cohorts. Patients were divided at admission into classical AD, single jaundice, or non-AD non-jaundice groups. Baseline characteristics, ACLF development, and short-term outcomes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Among 2645 cirrhotic patients, classical AD, single jaundice, and non-AD non-jaundice were observed in 2163 (81.78%), 267 (10.09%), and 215 (8.13%), respectively. The 90-day liver transplant (LT)-free mortality was comparable between single jaundice patients and classical AD patients (15.09% vs. 17.81%, p = 0.266), but significantly higher than non-AD non-jaundice patients (2.45%; p < 0.01). The prevalence of ACLF (16.10% vs. 16.09%, p = 1.000) and pre-ACLF (9.36% vs. 6.43%, p = 0.094) were comparable between the single jaundice and classical AD groups. Intrahepatic precipitants, particularly hepatitis B flare with hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (odds ratio [OR] 2.69; p = 0.002), spontaneous hepatitis B flare with high HBV-DNA load (OR 23.75; p < 0.001), superimposed hepatitis A/E virus infection on HBV infection (OR 13.40; p < 0.001) and hepatotoxic drug usage (OR 3.64; p < 0.001) were associated with single jaundice.

CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhotic inpatients with single jaundice show comparably high short-term mortality and ACLF risk to those with classical AD. Single jaundice shall be considered as an AD event and is predominantly triggered by intrahepatic insults, warranting surveillance equivalent to classical AD and prioritized management of the precipitants.

articles.title: A New Application of 64CuCl2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64CuCl2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64CuCl2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

articles.title: The Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society Center for Research and Quality 2025 Annual Report.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: The Congenital Heart Surgeons' Society (CHSS) is viewed by many as one of the most prestigious professional societies dedicated to pediatric and congenital cardiac surgery. The CHSS Center for Research and Quality (CRQ) Fall 2025 Work Weekend was held in Chicago on Saturday, October 25, 2025. The purpose of this article is to summarize the proceedings of the CHSS CRQ Fall 2025 Work Weekend and to provide a 2025 Annual Report of the CHSS CRQ. At the CHSS CRQ Fall 2025 Work Weekend, multiple topics were discussed related to ongoing CHSS research and quality initiatives. The CHSS CRQ is evolving to keep pace with the rapid evolution of medical informatics and the ever-evolving regulatory issues of clinical research. This 2025 Annual Report of the CHSS CRQ summarizes some of the ongoing initiatives at CHSS CRQ designed to assure that the CHSS CRQ continues to lead innovative and collaborative clinical research to improve pediatric and congenital cardiac care.

articles.title: Precision Medicine in Sickle Cell Disease: From Molecular Pathways to Curative Strategies.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a monogenic β-globin disorder characterized by hemoglobin S polymerization, hemolysis, and vaso-occlusion, yet it exhibits remarkable clinical heterogeneity. Despite advances in supportive care and disease-modifying therapies, substantial variability in severity, treatment response, and long-term outcomes persists. Therefore, this review aims to examine the biological and clinical foundations of precision medicine in SCD, emphasizing genomic modifiers, molecular pathways, and phenotype-driven therapeutic strategies. Key pathogenic pathways including hemoglobin polymerization, vascular adhesion, and inflammatory and oxidative amplification have enabled the development of targeted agents such as hydroxyurea, voxelotor, crizanlizumab, and L-glutamine, each demonstrating domain-specific targets. Pharmacogenomic insights, particularly involving fetal hemoglobin regulatory loci (e.g. BCL11A and HBS1L-MYB), further elucidate variability in disease expression and therapeutic response. Emerging curative approaches, including allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, lentiviral gene addition, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome editing, represent transformative applications of precision hematology. Collectively, these advances support a paradigm shift from generalized symptom management toward biologically informed, individualized care. Continued integration of genomic profiling, biomarker stratification, and equitable implementation frameworks will be essential to translate precision strategies into sustainable improvements in global SCD outcomes.

articles.title: Validation of an open-source hardware for cardio-physiological studies in fish: A statistical equivalence study with a widely used research-grade electrophysiological recording system.
articles.abstract: Monitoring heart rate (fH) accurately is fundamental for fish eco-physiological studies. However, these measurements rely heavily on expensive experimental tools. Here, we aimed to validate BITalino, an inexpensive, open-hardware biosignal acquisition system for measuring fH that could help to democratize research in fish physiology. BITalino is a modular electrophysiological system with a dedicated electrocardiogram (ECG) module that records ECG signals through electrodes connected to the module via lead wires and attached directly to the subject. We compared BITalino with a widely used research-grade physiological recording system (BIOPAC) by measuring fH in fish using both devices simultaneously. Heart-rate measurements did not differ significantly between devices, and there was no significant Device×Time interaction, indicating that both systems tracked temporal variation similarly. The intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) showed that 85.9% of the variance was due to biological differences between fish, with less than 5% from device-related variance. These results confirm that BITalino can be effectively used for fH monitoring in fish physiology studies. Beyond its low cost, its portability, modular design, open-hardware architecture and compatibility with third-party analysis software make it easily adaptable for different experimental applications, and may facilitate its use in resource-limited research settings.

articles.title: Ventriculostomy-associated infection rates and routine EVD replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is associated with a significant risk of ventriculostomy-associated infection (VAI), which can lead to severe complications. The relationship between catheterization duration, routine catheter exchange, and infection risk remains debated. This meta-analysis aimed to estimate the contemporary pooled VAI rate and evaluate the effect of catheter type and management strategy on infection risk.

METHODS: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42025632997) systematic review and meta-analysis. MEDLINE, Cochrane, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL were searched through February 2024. Studies reporting EVD infection counts with catheter-days were included. Random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) meta-analysis pooled log-transformed infection rates. Subgroup analyses compared impregnated versus plain catheters and pre-/post-2010 era. Two RCTs were qualitatively synthesized. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane RoB2.

RESULTS: Nineteen cohort studies and two RCTs were included. Critically, neither RCT demonstrated benefit from routine replacement (Wong 2002: RR = 1.80, 95% CI 0.33-9.81, p = 0.50; Keong 2012: RR = 0.58, 95% CI 0.33-0.99, favouring silver-impregnated catheters over standard catheters rather than supporting exchange). All 19 observational cohort studies confirmed that routine fixed-interval EVD replacement was not practiced at any included institution, precluding direct observational comparison. Eight cohort studies contributed 167 infections across 22,839 catheter-days to quantitative synthesis. The pooled VAI rate was 7.87 per 1,000 catheter-days (95% CI 4.67-13.25; I2=91%, τ2=0.506). The 95% prediction interval was 1.78-34.85/1,000 catheter-days, reflecting wide variation across settings. Antimicrobial-impregnated catheters had a pooled rate of 4.85 versus 17.03/1,000 catheter-days for plain catheters.

CONCLUSION: Routine fixed-interval EVD replacement is not supported by current evidence, independently confirming IDSA 2017 Recommendation 78. Antimicrobial-impregnated catheters and infection prevention bundles appear more effective at reducing VAI rates than scheduled catheter exchange alone. Further adequately powered RCTs are needed and research should standardize reporting of institutional replacement practices and evaluate broader-spectrum antimicrobial catheter technologies targeting both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms.

articles.title: Ethnic inequities in mathematical models for respiratory infectious disease: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 was the most recent pandemic to highlight profound ethnic inequities. However, most mathematical epidemiological models do not adequately represent these inequities, limiting the potential for such models to inform equitable public health responses and interventions. This systematic review identifies mathematical models of infectious respiratory disease transmission that report results by ethnic group and surveys the different mathematical modelling approaches used to attempt to capture ethnicity-related outcomes. Only 28 studies met the inclusion criteria, which is rare relative to the volume of infectious disease modelling literature. The most common model frameworks were compartmental models (11 studies), individual-based models (12 studies), and metapopulation models (5 studies). Across these studies, ethnic heterogeneities were represented directly by incorporating some combination of ethnic group population demographics, ethnicity-specific interaction patterns, and ethnicity-specific disease parameters, or indirectly through spatial differences in interaction patterns or disease transmission. Consideration of ethnicity in mathematical models of disease transmission is in its infancy, with only three of the studies published before 2020, but it has the potential to provide improved evidence for public health action that reduces the epidemic burden and inequities across ethnic groups.

articles.title: Sample size in social contact surveys for epidemic modelling and risk prediction.
articles.abstract: Social contact surveys, measuring who contacts whom, are widely used for epidemic intelligence and public health decision-making. Despite their widespread use, sample size calculations are not performed. We conducted a review of social contact surveys (2008-2025) to characterize current practice. We characterized the impact of survey size on epidemic metrics using two social contact surveys, the UK Social Contact Survey and POLYMOD (Europe), and two methods. For each dataset and approach, we generated repeated subsamples and calculated the resulting reproduction numbers, characterized their distributions, and measured uncertainty. We identified 107 unique social contact surveys from 57 studies. Sample sizes ranged from 30 to more than 10 000 participants, with a median of 1 438. One quarter of surveys contained fewer than 1 000 participants. Our analysis supports recruiting at least 1 000 participants for general-population social contact surveys used for epidemic modelling. Increasing sample size to 2 000 participants provides worthwhile gains in the precision of epidemic estimates, particularly for analyses using finer age stratification or individual-level approaches. Beyond approximately 3 000 participants, additional improvements in precision were small for the epidemic metrics analysed. This provides a practical balance between precision and participant burden.

articles.title: Sex-Based Differences in Chronic Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based disparities in patient enrollment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyze sex-based enrollment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time.

METHODS: RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrollment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (HR or RR) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrollment was 27.0% (95%CI: 22.0% to 32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95%CI: 21.0% to 29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, p < 0.001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89-1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95%CI 0.68-0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: p = 0.44; RR: p = 0.95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84-0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95%CI 0.90-1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95%CI 0.50-0.93).

CONCLUSION: Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

articles.title: Essentials of Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship: Clinical Updates From the Past Decade.
articles.abstract: Ten years ago, a comprehensive series of articles was published in Pediatric Emergency Care detailing the state of pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellowship education. We intend to provide an update to the clinical elements of fellowship training, with a companion article to follow that will address the nonclinical domains. This article will summarize the core components of fellowship as mandated by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) and review significant changes and challenges to fellowship education that have occurred over the past decade. In light of upcoming modifications to fellowship education, including an increased focus on competency-based medical education and the addition of a 2-year, clinically oriented fellowship option, it is vital for stakeholders to be familiar with the core elements of PEM fellowship training as the curriculum is adapted to meet the needs of trainees and their patients.

articles.title: Restricted mean survival time ratio in oncology cost-effectiveness analysis: stability and data-driven support for treatment-effect waning modeling and survival extrapolation.
articles.journal: International journal of technology assessment in health care
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We examined long-term treatment-effect patterns relevant to treatment effect waning (TEW) modeling in oncology health technology assessment (HTA), compared the dispersion and update stability of hazard ratios (HRs) and restricted mean survival time ratios (RMSTRs), and developed prediction models to support extrapolation model selection and TEW modeling.

METHODS: Using the FDA Hematology/Oncology Approvals Database, we identified phase II/III randomized controlled trials (2006-2025) with updates. We included overall survival (OS) and other time-to-event end points (non-OS). We conducted 2/3/4/5-year landmark analyses to estimate post-landmark HRs and RMSTRs, summarized by event-weighted medians and dispersion (coefficient of quartile relative dispersion, CQR). Update-related change was quantified using updated-to-initial ratios. We predicted longer-term RMSTR using elastic-net regression with nested cross-validation and split-conformal 90 percent prediction intervals.

RESULTS: We analyzed 168 trials (270 contrasts; 150 OS, 120 non-OS). Across landmark analyses at 2, 3, 4, and 5 years, RMSTR was consistently less dispersed than HR for both OS and non-OS end points, while post-landmark HRs generally remained < 1. Update ratios were more stable for RMSTR than HR. Initial and updated RMSTR were strongly correlated (OS r = .87; non-OS r = .82). Parsimonious regularized models accurately predicted updated RMSTR, with conformal prediction intervals achieving 91 percent and 96 percent coverage for OS and non-OS.

CONCLUSIONS: Reliance on current HR-based TEW modeling practices alone may be insufficient to fully characterize long-term treatment-effect uncertainty. RMSTR was consistently less dispersed than HR and predictable from early trial data, providing an anchor for extrapolation model selection and TEW uncertainty analysis in oncology economic evaluations.

articles.title: [Clinical analysis of 4 children with tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis syndrome].
articles.journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical and pathological characteristics, treatment, and prognosis of tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis (TINU) syndrome in children. Methods: This case series study analyzed the clinical characteristics, laboratory examinations, renal biopsy findings, treatment courses, and outcomes of 4 children diagnosed with TINU syndrome, who were hospitalized in the Department of Nephrology, Capital Center for Children's Health affiliated to Capital Medical University between November 2017 and April 2024. Results: Four children with TINU syndrome included 2 males and 2 females. Their ages at diagnosis were 13 years and 11 months, 13 years and 6 months, 13 years and 7 months, and 11 years and 8 months respectively. Three patients had a history of infection or drug exposure before disease onset. Ocular symptoms preceded renal involvement by 1 month in 1 case, whereas uveitis developed 8.0, 0.5 and 14.0 months after renal involvement in the other 3 cases. All patients had acute kidney injury (AKI), including stage 2 AKI in 3 patients and stage 3 AKI in 1 patient. Glycosuria and elevated urinary β2-microglobulin levels occurred, and varying degrees of proteinuria and leukocyturia occurred in 3 patients. Serum creatinine levels at disease onset were markedly elevated at 130.0, 103.4, 188.4 and 105.7 μmol/L, and estimated glomerular filtration rates were reduced to 50.5, 56.4, 28.9 and 53.8 ml/(min·1.73 m²). Renal biopsies showed acute interstitial nephritis, and the predominant ocular manifestation was bilateral anterior uveitis. All patients received systemic glucocorticoid therapy and topical corticosteroid eye drops, and 1 patient was additionally treated with mycophenolate mofetil. During follow-up periods of 57, 82, 14 and 66 months, respectively, 1 patient progressed to stage 2 chronic kidney disease. Proteinuria resolved and ocular symptoms recurred only in 1 patient. Conclusions: Renal involvement generally has a favorable prognosis in children with TINU syndrome. However renal function may not fully recover in some patients, and uveitis may persist or recur, underscoring the need for renal and ophthalmic combined screening and long-term multidisciplinary follow-up.

articles.title: [Clinical analysis of 5 cases of pediatric respiratory viral sepsis].
articles.journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
articles.abstract: Objective: To analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric respiratory viral sepsis and to improve clinicians' awareness of this disorder. Methods: Case series study. The study retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 5 children with respiratory viral sepsis treated at Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Kunming children's hospital between March 2023 and January 2026, analyzing their clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, treatment courses, and outcomes. Results: Among the 5 cases of respiratory viral sepsis, there were 2 males and 3 females, and the ages were 3 years and 8 months, 4 years, 4 years and 7 months, 5 years and 2 months, and 8 years and 10 months respectively. All 5 cases had fever, 3 cases had cough, 2 cases had breathing difficulties and 1 each case of skin mottling, thrombocytopenia, and convulsions and consciousness disorder. Laboratory tests showed that the white blood cell count was (2.06-11.86)×109/L, platelet count (26-262)×109/L, C-reactive protein 0.62-68.15 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.09-0.35 μg/L and interleukin-6 0.50-19.64 ng/L. Pathogen examination showed 3 cases of influenza A virus infection, 1 case of adenovirus infection, and 1 case of adenovirus combined with parainfluenza virus infection. All 5 patients recovered and were discharged after comprehensive treatment including antiviral therapy, respiratory support, and immunomodulation, with a hospital stay of 8-59 d. Conclusions: Respiratory viral infections can cause multiple organ dysfunction in children and meet the diagnostic criteria for sepsis. Greater clinical attention should be paid to the diagnosis, recognition, and management of viral sepsis in children.

articles.title: [Analysis of efficacy and prognosis of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked syndrome].
articles.journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and prognosis of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) for the treatment of immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked (IPEX) syndrome in children. Methods: In this case series study, clinical characteristics, laboratory tests, transplantation protocols, post-transplant disease remission, and survival status of 9 children with IPEX syndrome who underwent allo-HSCT at the Children's Hospital of Fudan University from July 2020 to December 2025 were collected. The transplantation experiences were summarized and the efficacy and safety of allo-HSCT for IPEX children were evaluated. Results: All 9 children were males. Eight children developed symptoms within the first month of age, and 1 at 5 years of age. The initial presentations were diarrhea in 4 children, diabetes mellitus in 2 children, and rash in 3 children. FOXP3 gene variants were maternally inherited in 8 children and de novo in 1 child. A total of 11 HSCT were performed in 9 children, with an overall engraftment of 9 times. Two children who experienced primary graft failure achieved successful engraftment after second HSCT at intervals of 3 and 4 months, respectively. Donor sources included 4 haploidentical donors, 3 unrelated cord blood and 2 matched unrelated donors. All conditioning regimens were based on fludarabine and busulfan. The age at transplantation was 37.5 (12.4, 70.3) months, with a follow-up of 17.4 (9.7, 26.8) months. All 9 children survived. Eight children achieved complete donor chimerism, and 1 had mixed chimerism. The times to neutrophil and platelet engraftment were 13 (11, 18) and 9 (9, 29) d, respectively. The times for absolute CD19+and CD4+ cell counts exceed 2×108 cells/L were 165 (94, 270) and 165 (100, 183) d, respectively. Five children developed grade Ⅰ-Ⅱ acute graft versus host disease (GVHD), all presenting as skin involvement and resolved following glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy. No grade Ⅲ-Ⅳ acute GVHD or chronic GVHD occurred. Recurrent diarrhea, anemia, severe infection, eczema, and nephropathy all achieved complete remission through allo-HSCT. Among the 5 children with hypothyroidism and 2 children with diabetes mellitus, levothyroxine and insulin replacement therapy were still required, with well-controlled conditions. No new autoimmune diseases developed. Conclusions: allo-HSCT is an effective curative approach for IPEX syndrome, capable of halting disease progression, but cannot reverse pre-existing endocrine damage. No severe infections and GVHD occurred post-transplantation. Early diagnosis and early transplantation are crucial for improving outcomes.

articles.title: [Clinical analysis of modified Chinese Children Leukemia Group-Acute Myeloid Leukemia 2019 regimen in treating pediatric acute myeloid leukemia].
articles.journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical efficiency and prognosis of a modified regimen based on the Chinese Children Leukemia Group-Acute Myeloid Leukemia 2019 (CCLG-AML2019) protocol for childhood acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) (non-acute promyelocytic leukaemia, non-APL). Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, clinical data including sex, age, French-American-British (FAB) classification, genetics, molecular biology, treatment, therapeutic efficacy and prognosis of 41 newly diagnosed non-APL AML children treated at Capital Institute of Pediatrics, Capital Pediatric Medical Center, Capital Medical University from November 2019 to December 2023 were analyzed. All children received chemotherapy according to the CCLG-AML2019 protocol. For high-risk (HR) children with persistent high-level minimal residual disease (MRD) after induction therapy, a cladribine-containing intensified salvage chemotherapy regimen was introduced in the third course. According to the risk stratification criteria, children were divided into high-risk and non-high-risk groups. High-risk children received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) after 3 or 4 courses of chemotherapy. Children were divided into two groups according to age (<2 years and ≥2 years group), and the clinical characteristics and prognosis between the two groups were compared using Fisher's exact test. Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate the 5-year overall survival (OS) rate and event-free survival (EFS) rate, and Cox regression was employed for univariate analysis. Results: Among the 41 children, there were 22 males and 19 females, with an age of 5.8 (2.6, 8.0) years. Twenty-four children (59%) were classified as the high-risk group, and 17 (41%) as the non-high-risk group. The follow-up duration was 51(38, 62) months. The 5-year OS rate was (85±7)%, and the 5-year EFS rate was (79±7)%. Non-HR children achieved 100% for both, whereas in the high-risk group, the corresponding rates were (75±10)% and (65±11)%, respectively. The difference in EFS rate between the two groups had statistically difference (P=0.018). There were 10 children in the <2 years age group, among them FAB M5 or M7 subtypes were observed in 9 children, KMT2A gene rearrangements were observed in 5 children, and high-risk stratification were defined in 8 children. Core binding factor (CBF)-AML (19 children) had a KIT gene variation in 10 children, and with no relapse. During follow-up, 5 deaths occurred (2 due to relapse, 2 due to transplant-related complications, and 1 due to infection). Conclusions: The CCLG-AML2019 regimen offers favorable short-term survival for pediatric non-APL AML, especially in non-HR children. HR children still face the risks of relapse and transplant-related mortality after allo-HSCT. Children aged <2 years may benefit from chemotherapy combined with targeted therapy. CBF-AML has a favorable overall prognosis, and the high frequency of KIT gene variation did not attenuate this advantage.
