articles.title: Combined impact of dynapenic abdominal obesity on stroke risk in middle-aged and older adults: evidence from two nationwide prospective cohorts.
articles.abstract: Dynapenic abdominal obesity (DAO), characterised by the combination of low muscle strength and abdominal fat accumulation, is an emerging health risk phenotype. Its association with incident stroke remains inadequately explored. This prospective cohort study investigated the relationship between DAO and new-onset stroke in middle-aged and older adults. We analysed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, n 10 153) and used the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, n 5421) for external validation, over a seven-year follow-up. Participants were categorised into four groups: no dynapenia or abdominal obesity (ND/NAO), isolated abdominal obesity, isolated dynapenia and DAO. After adjusting for socio-demographic, lifestyle and comorbidity factors, multivariable logistic regression revealed that DAO was significantly associated with a higher risk of stroke in both CHARLS (OR = 1·96, 95 % CI: 1·37-2·76, P < 0·001) and ELSA (OR = 2·38, 95 % CI: 1·11-5·10, P = 0·025) compared with the ND/NAO group. The risk conferred by DAO exceeded that of either condition in isolation. Stratified analysis suggested a potentially stronger association in urban Chinese men; however, effect modification was not statistically significant. We conclude that DAO is a significant, independent risk factor for stroke in both populations, with combined effects exceeding isolated conditions. This phenotype represents a practical, cross-population marker for clinicians and nutritionists to identify individuals at elevated stroke risk warranting targeted intervention, with potentially important implications for urban Chinese men.

articles.title: Resting energy expenditure-guided nutritional support in acute ischaemic stroke patients: a single-centre quasi-randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Acute stroke induces a hypermetabolic/hypercatabolic state, causing malnutrition and muscle wasting that hinder recovery. Weight-based predictive equations for nutritional support may fail to meet individual energy needs. This study compared resting energy expenditure (REE)-guided nutrition with weight-based calorie calculation in acute stroke patients. This single-centre, quasi-randomised controlled trial assessed seventy-four acute ischaemic stroke patients requiring enteral nutrition. Six patients were excluded before allocation, and sixty-eight were allocated by odd/even hospital admission number to the REE-guided group (n 30; energy target 120 % of indirect calorimetry-measured REE) or the control group (n 38; 25 kcal/kg/d). The complete-case analysis included fifty-four patients (REE-guided n 24; control n 30). Primary analyses compared day 14 fat-free mass surrogate indicators after adjustment for baseline values and prespecified covariates. Secondary outcomes included nutritional and inflammatory biomarkers, feeding efficiency and complications. Baseline energy and protein intake were comparable between groups. In unadjusted comparisons at day 14, no statistically significant differences were observed for left or right temporal muscle thickness, whereas calf circumference was lower in the REE-guided group. After adjustment for age, sex, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, total energy intake and day 0 C-reactive protein (CRP), left temporal muscle thickness was significantly higher in the REE-guided group (β = 0·56, 95 % CI 0·07-1·05, P = 0·031). Right temporal muscle thickness and calf circumference showed non-significant adjusted differences. At day 14, prealbumin was numerically higher in the REE-guided group, but the difference was not statistically significant. Albumin and transferrin were similar between groups. Inflammatory biomarkers, including leucocyte count, CRP and procalcitonin, showed no statistically significant between-group differences. Clinical secondary outcomes, including complications, NIHSS score, time to reach target calories and enteral nutrition interruption, did not differ significantly between groups. REE-guided nutritional support was feasible and safe in acute ischaemic stroke patients and was associated with higher adjusted left temporal muscle thickness at day 14; biomarker findings were exploratory; only prealbumin showed a non-significant favourable numerical trend, whereas inflammatory biomarkers did not show a consistent favourable pattern. Effects on right temporal muscle thickness and calf circumference were not statistically significant. These findings support further evaluation in larger, randomised trials. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR-IPR-16010051.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices of Australian healthcare professionals related to potassium-enriched salt: a mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract: Switching from regular salt to potassium-enriched salt lowers blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, but this intervention is underutilised by healthcare professionals. We assessed Australian healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) regarding regular salt and potassium-enriched salt for hypertension management. We used mixed-methods research including surveys to quantify KAP towards regular salt and potassium-enriched salt and semi-structured interviews to gather in-depth information about knowledge, attitudes and the barriers and opportunities for recommending potassium-enriched salt use in clinical practice. Participants were general practitioners, medical specialists and allied health professionals working in Australia and caring for individuals with hypertension. Ninety-nine participants completed the survey, and thirty-six participants completed interviews. Survey participants generally had high knowledge related to regular salt; most were aware of potassium-enriched salt (94 %), but only 49 % reported familiarity with it. Of those aware, 73 % considered it safe to use and 66 % knew of the blood pressure-lowering benefits. Only 14 % had recommended it in the previous 12 months, though most interview participants were willing to recommend it in the future. Key barriers to recommendation were limited knowledge about potassium-enriched salt, insufficient time to discuss use with patients and concerns about taste, availability and affordability. The key opportunity identified was incorporating recommendations and information about potassium-enriched salt into existing resources supporting hypertension management by clinicians. Healthcare professionals are mostly aware and supportive of recommending potassium-enriched salt but lack in-depth knowledge. Advice about using potassium-enriched salt needs incorporation into clinical education programmes and hypertension management systems.

articles.title: Diabetes-mediated changes in red blood cell biomechanics reorganize capillary network hemodynamics through altered cellular trafficking.
articles.abstract: Diabetes alters shape and deformability of red blood cells (RBCs), thereby potentially modifying their transport through capillary networks. Microvascular dysfunction-including impaired capillary perfusion, endothelial dysregulation, and vascular remodeling-is a hallmark of diabetes. However, the contribution of altered RBC biomechanics to network-scale changes in capillary hemodynamics and the cellular-scale mechanisms underlying such changes remain poorly understood. Current in vivo imaging techniques cannot directly quantify critical hemodynamic parameters including endothelial mechanical load, capillary pressure, and the cell-free layer in vessels less than 10 microns in diameter. Nor can they identify the cellular-scale mechanisms responsible for network-scale hemodynamic changes. To bridge these gaps, we combined anatomically reconstructed human retinal capillary networks with a high-fidelity three-dimensional fluid-structure interaction model that fully resolves RBC deformation and transport. The simulations predict that diabetes-mediated alterations in RBC shape and deformability redistribute capillary hemodynamics with bidirectional, highly localized, and spatially heterogeneous changes. Compared to healthy RBCs, diabetic RBCs resulted in hematocrit changes by ±40%, RBC velocity by -30% to +40%, vessel pressure drop by twofold, and local wall shear stress nearly fourfold. Diabetic RBCs also shifted the Fåhræus relationship where the concentration of cells decreases with vessel diameter through diameter-dependent changes in the cell-free layer. Analysis of individual bifurcations identified three cellular-scale mechanisms underlying these network-scale changes: reduced lingering, capillary obstruction, and slower lateral migration of diabetic RBCs that altered their partitioning into downstream vessels. Together, these mechanisms reorganized downstream cellular trafficking and redistributed capillary hemodynamics throughout the network. These findings establish how diabetes-mediated alterations in RBC biomechanics give rise to localized microvascular dysfunction by linking single-cell biomechanics to altered cellular trafficking and emergent capillary network hemodynamics.

articles.title: Primary Intermammary Breast Carcinoma Presenting With Direct Sternal Invasion: A Diagnostic Pitfall of Standard Screening Mammography.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Standard screening mammogram views focus on the lateral and posterior breast tissues; the view that best visualizes the intermammary area, the 90-degree lateral or cleavage view, is not typically performed. The limited field of view of mammogram increases the importance of additional imaging with CT, ultrasound, and MRI as a tool in diagnosing neoplasm in the intermammary area. To date, intermammary primary breast carcinoma has been reported only a few times in the literature, and none of these described direct sternal invasion at presentation. CASE REPORT An 85-year-old woman with a past medical history of follicular non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with bendamustine-rituximab in 2017 (without chest radiation) and significant family history of breast cancer presented to our clinic 2 months after noticing a hard, non-tender nodule on her sternum. She had undergone a routine screening mammogram 8 months prior, which was unremarkable. Subsequent diagnostic workup including targeted ultrasound, and PET-CT identified a hypermetabolic presternal mass. Notably, diagnostic mammography 8 months after the initial screening mammogram also failed to properly visualize the lesion. Biopsy confirmed ER+/PR+, HER2- adenocarcinoma consistent with breast origin. Despite negative initial staging for distant metastasis, pathological examination after resection revealed direct invasion into the sternum, necessitating partial sternectomy. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights a rare intermammary presentation of breast carcinoma with direct sternal invasion, a feature not previously reported. It emphasizes the blind spot of standard screening mammography in the medial breast/cleavage area and the necessity of targeted imaging for palpable parasternal masses, even in the setting of recent negative screens.

articles.title: The effects of intravenous glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies evaluating intravenous (IV) glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients have shown inconsistent results. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of IV glutamine on mortality, infectious complications, length of stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation.

METHODS: A systematic search of Ovid Medline, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and KoreaMed was conducted from inception through October 2023 and updated in April 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing IV glutamine supplementation with standard care in critically ill adults were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: A total of 10 randomized trials involving 1,593 critically ill patients were included in the analysis. IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with reduced overall mortality (risk ratio [RR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.77-1.13) or overall infection rates (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.63-1.18). No mortality benefit was observed in either non-surgical or surgical/trauma subgroups. Glutamine supplementation was associated with reduced pneumonia incidence (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.49-0.87) and shorter mechanical ventilation duration (mean difference, -0.97 days; 95% CI, -1.62 to -0.32); however, these findings were based on a limited number of small studies. Intensive care unit and hospital length of stay were longer in the glutamine group.

CONCLUSIONS: IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with improved survival or overall infection rates in critically ill adults. Current evidence does not support routine IV glutamine supplementation in unselected critically ill patients.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for intensive care unit admission and mortality in rapid response team-activated ward patients: a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in South Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Factors driving intensive care unit (ICU) transfer decisions and mortality after rapid response team (RRT) activation remain unclear. We identified independent predictors of ICU admission, 28-day mortality, and in-hospital mortality in RRT-activated ward patients.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults with first RRT activation from September 2023 to August 2025 at a Korean tertiary hospital (n=549). Multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination was used.

RESULTS: Of 549 patients, 191 (34.8%) were transferred to the ICU. ICU admission was independently predicted by procalcitonin >0.5 ng/ml (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.833; P=0.021) and lower hemoglobin (aOR, 0.808 per g/dl; P=0.040), whereas solid tumor was associated with lower transfer likelihood (aOR, 0.142; P<0.001). Mortality did not differ significantly between ICU and ward groups at 28 days (27.7% vs. 27.7%, P=0.937) or during hospitalization (46.1% vs. 40.2%, P=0.162). Declining peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂)/fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO₂) ratio, rising lactate, and hyperkalemia predicted both mortality outcomes. Lower platelet count uniquely predicted 28-day mortality, whereas solid tumor, chronic kidney disease, and deep learning-based continuous cardiac arrest risk score (DeepCARS) additionally predicted in-hospital mortality. ICU admission itself was not independently associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: ICU transfer after RRT activation appears to reflect acute reversibility, clinical trajectory, and possible at/after-activation goals-of-care processes rather than severity alone. Mortality was more closely associated with oxygenation failure, hypoperfusion, and electrolyte instability than with disposition.

articles.title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction: An Adjunct to Imaging and Hemodynamic Assessment.
articles.abstract: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.

articles.title: Systematic CRS-R-based Evaluation of Disorders of Consciousness in the ICU: Development and Evolution of a Multidisciplinary Program.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract: Evaluation and prognostication following disorders of consciousness (DoC) is a complex task with significant implications. The Coma Recovery Scale, Revised (CRS-R) is a standardized neurobehavioral assessment that enables clinicians to accurately differentiate between coma, unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS), minimally conscious state (MCS), and emergence from MCS. Newly described paradigms present ambitious programs utilizing multidisciplinary clinical teams working in sync with new technologies to optimize and improve a systematic approach to prognostication following DoC. We developed a DoC program at a level 1 trauma and comprehensive stroke center to optimize diagnosis and management of DoC patients. Through an iterative approach our program developed a DoC team to standardize the use of the CRS-R for patients with DoC and formalize a training program for its use. In addition, a formal DoC consult group was created incorporating the neurocritical care faculty to provide expertise and to assist with collaborative decision making. We detail our program's development, barriers, outcomes, and future directions. The core features of this novel clinical paradigm-structured assessment, interdisciplinary collaboration, and iterative re-evaluation-can be adapted to more resource-limited settings to improve outcomes, communication, and the consistency and transparency of prognostication in disorders of consciousness.

articles.title: SETI-The Semi-Elective Transplant Initiative: A Systems-Based Approach to Expanding Kidney Transplant Access Through Operational Redesign.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether formal integration of preservation strategy with predictable operating room access was associated with measurable changes in transplant timing, preservation practice, the logistical profile of transplanted grafts, and early clinical outcomes.

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Deceased donor kidney transplantation remains a reactive process requiring urgent mobilization of hospital resources. As volumes increase and hospitals operate near capacity, this creates operational barriers that limit organ utilization. We report a retrospective evaluation of a prospectively implemented operational redesign; the design does not support causal inference.

METHODS: Adult deceased-donor kidney transplants (January 2022-June 2025) were grouped into pre-SETI, SETI-1 (expanded machine perfusion), and SETI-2 (morning operating room access). A contemporaneous SRTR cohort (N=12,302) served as the comparator.

RESULTS: Among 936 transplants, mean cold ischemia time (CIT) increased after SETI (20.2→21.9 h, P=0.0039). Donation after circulatory death (DCD) kidneys with CIT >30 hours increased from 0.5% pre-SETI to 7.7% after full implementation (P<0.0001). Overnight perfusion increased more than 3-fold, and operative starts shifted toward 8-10 AM. Kidney Donor Profile Index rose across eras (median: 29→33→43, P<0.001). No significant differences were observed in DGF (41.4→38.2%, P=0.071) or graft failure (5.4→3.2%, P=0.34); these comparisons were underpowered and do not establish equivalence. Donor hypertension predicted graft failure, whereas CIT, DCD status, and SETI era did not.

CONCLUSIONS: Systems-based operational redesign transformed reactive deceased-donor kidney transplantation into a proactive model, enabling transplantation of a greater proportion of logistics-sensitive grafts, including DCD kidneys and organs with prolonged CIT, within existing healthcare resources. Whether this increases net organ utilization was not established by these data.

articles.title: First Documented Pediatric Hantavirus Infection in Athens Metropolitan Area, Greece.
Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.abstract: The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following drug-eluting stent implantation remains uncertain. We evaluated extended DAPT versus aspirin monotherapy in patients who completed approximately 12 months of uneventful DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing these strategies. The primary outcome was myocardial infarction (MI); secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, stroke, and clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2-5). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model. Certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and trial sequential analysis was performed for MI. Six trials involving 28,601 patients were included. Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, or stroke. Clinically relevant bleeding was also not significantly different (RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 87%) and certainty was low. GRADE certainty was high for MI, cardiac death, and repeat revascularization; moderate for all-cause mortality; and low for stent thrombosis and bleeding. Trial sequential analysis for MI crossed the conventional significance boundary but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary or required information size. Extended DAPT may reduce MI, but individualized assessment of ischemic and bleeding risk remains important, and further adequately powered trials are warranted.

articles.title: The Evolving Landscape of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Treatment: Are Guidelines Keeping Pace?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common inherited cardiovascular disorder associated with morbidity. Rapid advances in therapeutics-particularly the emergence of cardiac myosin inhibitors (CMIs)-suggest that current management guidelines are lagging best practices.

AREAS OF UNCERTAINTY: Cardiac myosin inhibitors have revolutionized the management of patients with obstructive HCM. Patients with nonobstructive HCM have had limited therapeutic options historically; however, the recently published ACACIA-HCM trial demonstrated significant benefit in these patients and may represent a new treatment option in these patients, although more long-term data and research are needed in this population.

DATA SOURCES: A literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, society guidelines, and recently published clinical trials evaluating HCM, cardiac myosin inhibitors, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, septal reduction therapy, and emerging therapies for obstructive and nonobstructive HCM.

THERAPEUTIC ADVANCES: Historically, HCM management has centered on negative inotropic/chronotropic agents to alleviate left ventricular outflow tract obstruction by decreasing the force of contraction and increasing diastolic filling time. The introduction of CMIs represents a paradigm shift by directly targeting the underlying hypercontractility, representing the first therapy specifically designed to treat obstructive HCM, obviating the need for earlier agents, which had limited data and at best modest therapeutic benefit. There may finally be an available treatment for diastolic heart failure in patients with nonobstructive HCM with myosin inhibition, as results from a recent trial ACACIA-HCM were favorable. Furthermore, ongoing investigations are exploring novel approaches such as metabolic modulators.

CONCLUSIONS: The management of HCM is undergoing substantial transformation, yet guideline recommendations continue to prioritize beta blockers as first-line therapy despite mounting evidence supporting CMIs. Although treatment strategies for obstructive HCM have evolved significantly, optimal approaches for nonobstructive disease remain unclear. Addressing this gap represents a critical priority for future research.

articles.title: Intra-articular antibiotic delivery combined with one-stage revision for periprosthetic joint infection: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication after joint arthroplasty requiring surgical and antibiotic management. One-stage revision has gained attention because it reduces the number of procedures while yielding acceptable outcomes. Intra-articular (IA) antibiotic delivery has been investigated to enhance local antimicrobial exposure and address biofilm-related challenges. However, a focused systematic review of IA antibiotic delivery combined with one-stage revision for PJI is lacking. This systematic review evaluated the techniques, safety, and outcomes of this strategy.

METHODS: A literature search was conducted up to 30 November 2025 across PubMed (including MEDLINE), Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. Studies enrolling adults with PJI treated by one-stage revision combined with IA antibiotic delivery and reporting clinical outcomes with at least 12 months of follow-up were included. Study characteristics, treatment protocols, outcomes, and safety data were extracted and descriptively synthesized.

RESULTS: Ten studies were identified. IA antibiotic delivery combined with one-stage revision showed satisfactory infection-control outcomes across individual studies. Antibiotics were selected according to microbiological findings and administered via catheter infusion or direct intra-articular injection for 14-42 days. Reported complications were descriptively summarized and included catheter-related, local, surgical, and systemic adverse events. Renal-related adverse events were reported, with no documented long-term renal impairment in the included studies. Heterogeneity in treatment protocols and study designs was noted across studies.

CONCLUSION: Intra-articular antibiotic delivery combined with one-stage revision for PJI was associated with satisfactory reported infection-control outcomes and safety findings. While the current evidence is largely retrospective and heterogeneous, further prospective comparative studies with standardized protocols would help clarify its clinical role.

articles.title: Age-specific COVID-19 case dynamics during school closure periods: Evidence from 12 european countries.
articles.journal: The European journal of health economics : HEPAC : health economics in prevention and care
articles.abstract: School closures were among the most widely adopted non-pharmaceutical interventions against COVID-19, yet evidence on their association with infection dynamics remains uncertain given their substantial economic and educational costs. This observational study describes age-specific COVID-19 case dynamics during school closure periods across 12 European countries using Generalised Additive Models with zero-crossing derivative analysis and Transfer Entropy. Case dynamics were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across age groups: case counts declined early but rose again within the window among the youngest cohorts (0-4 and 5-9 years). By contrast, the 10-14 group rose steadily with no turning point, and older adolescents and young adults (15-19 and 20-24 years) rose early and then declined. Transfer Entropy analysis, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, revealed asymmetric directional relationship between age cohorts that varied across national contexts. These patterns indicate that case trajectories during closure periods were not uniform across youth age groups, with no age group showing a sustained, uninterrupted decline. Interpreted cautiously, they raise questions about the cost-benefit balance of blanket closure policies when weighed against their documented economic, educational, and distributional costs, and motivate more targeted, age-sensitive quasi-experimental evaluation for future pandemic preparedness.

articles.title: The Economic Burden of HDV in Italy: Evaluating the Potential Impact and Effects of Bulevirtide for Chronic HDV Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Chronic hepatitis D is associated with substantial clinical and economic burden due to its progressive course and risk of severe liver-related complications. The aim of this study was to quantify the economic burden of chronic hepatitis D (HDV) in Italy from societal perspectives, and to estimate the clinical and economic consequences associated with bulevirtide, peginterferon alfa (PEG-IFN-α), and best supportive care (BSC) in HDV-RNA-positive adults with compensated liver disease.

METHODS: The economic impact of HDV infection was estimated using a cost-of-illness (COI) analysis, while the costs and effects of introducing bulevirtide were estimated using a cost-and-outcomes analysis (COA). The COA compared two scenarios: a clinical practice scenario that includes PEG-IFN-α and BSC, and a scenario that introduces bulevirtide. The analyses were conducted from the societal perspective; therefore, direct and indirect estimated costs were included. The most relevant outcomes were quality adjusted life years (QALYs) and the number of deaths. Both analyses were carried out on a standardised hypothetical cohort of 1000 HDV-RNA-positive adult patients with compensated liver disease, over 10 years. A deterministic sensitivity analysis (DSA) was conducted to assess parameter uncertainty.

RESULTS: The COI estimated a 10-year economic burden of €34,939,429.41 for the management and treatment of patients with HDV infection in Italy. The COA estimated a total 10-year reduction in disease-related costs of €2,152,752.76 after the introduction of bulevirtide, an increase of 8.26% (+ 366.12) in the number of QALYs gained, and a 12.39% reduction (- 73.67) in the number of deaths.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that the introduction of bulevirtide may alleviate the clinical and economic burden associated with HDV in Italy, while improving quality of life.

articles.title: Stroke burden and associated predictors: A methodological reflection.
Ultra-high-resolution photon-counting CT argues against a suspected bilateral carotid web: a case report.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Carotid web is diagnosed almost entirely from a shelf-like filling defect at CT angiography (CTA), yet the posterolateral carotid bulb at which webs arise is also a site of flow separation in which blood of differing contrast density mixes. We describe a bilateral web-like appearance at this site and determine whether it arose from reconstruction or acquisition.

METHODS: A 75-year-old woman with a right-hemispheric transient ischemic attack had three carotid CTA examinations: a dual-energy energy-integrating-detector CT (EID-CT) angiogram five months before presentation, a stroke-protocol photon-counting-detector CT (PCD-CT) angiogram at presentation, and a dedicated ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT angiogram three days later. Each photon-counting acquisition was additionally reconstructed with other section thicknesses, kernels or energies, and attenuation across the appearance was measured.

RESULTS: A bilateral shelf-like filling defect closely simulating a carotid web was present on the EID-CT and presenting PCD-CTF angiograms but absent on the ultra-high-resolution study. The tested reconstructions neither abolished the appearance nor elicited it. The ultra-high-resolution study was acquired 16.6 s after the end of injection at less than half the table speed, versus 10.3 s on the presenting study. Attenuation at the corresponding position measured 62%, 54% and 87% of luminal attenuation, respectively. No carotid intervention was undertaken.

CONCLUSION: An acquisition-dependent bilateral carotid bulb pseudolesion can mimic a carotid web on both EID-CT and PCD-CT angiography and is most consistent with flow-related mixing of blood of differing contrast density. A slower repeat acquisition of the carotid bulb with a few seconds more delay may prevent unnecessary revascularization.

articles.title: Metformin Lowers Fasting Hyperglycemia by Increasing Glucose Clearance in People with Moderately Controlled Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Metformin is the most frequently prescribed antidiabetic drug worldwide; however, the mechanism by which it lowers blood glucose remains incompletely understood. The objective of this study was to examine the effects of metformin on whole-body and specifically on hepatic glucose and energy metabolism in type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This open repeated-measures pilot study examined this question using Positional Isotopomer NMR Tracer Analysis (PINTA) to assess rates of endogenous glucose production (VEGP), hepatic pyruvate carboxylase flux (VPC), and citrate synthase (VCS) flux in 16 men with moderately controlled type 2 diabetes (T2D; BMI 30 ± 3 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.4 ± 1.4%) undergoing two examination days with (M+; 1 g twice daily) and without metformin (M-) treatment. Hepatic ATP and glycogen concentrations were quantified by 31P/13C magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

RESULTS: M+ reduced fasting glycemia by 18%, which could mostly be attributed to a 24% increase in rates of whole-body glucose clearance. Surprisingly, these changes were accompanied by a 58% increase in VPC and a 34% increase in VCS, due to a 26% increase in plasma glucagon concentrations. The increase in VPC was offset by reductions in the contributions of glycerol conversion to glucose resulting in no change in VEGP. Metformin decreased hepatic ATP content by 16% and increased plasma GDF-15 concentrations, but did not alter rates of net hepatic glycogenolysis.

CONCLUSION: Metformin treatment in male individuals of European ancestry with moderately controlled T2D decreases blood glucose concentrations by increasing rates of whole-body glucose clearance. Metformin further inhibits glycerol-derived gluconeogenesis, which is consistent with complex IV, not complex I, being the molecular target of metformin action.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/ ): NCT04088851.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Stimulation for Essential Tremor: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Effectiveness and Safety.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Essential tremor (ET) is the most prevalent movement disorder worldwide. There are limited current pharmacological therapies, and their side effects often preclude adequate doses. Surgical therapies, such as Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) and Focused Ultrasound (FUS), are reserved for patients with tremor that debilitates activities of daily living (ADLs). Peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS), including transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS) and transcutaneous peripheral nerve stimulation (TPNS), has emerged as a promising non-invasive neuromodulatory approach for many patients with intermediate symptoms.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 guidelines was conducted, with searches across PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and Web of Science. Studies enrolling patients with ET assessing TAPS and TPNS were included. Primary outcomes were tremor severity (TETRAS performance scale, total TETRAS) and tremor amplitude. Secondary outcomes included functional disability (BF-ADL, TETRAS-mADL) and safety.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies (2,541 patients) were included. Sham-controlled analyses showed statistically significant improvement in TETRAS performance scale scores (MD = - 1.00; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%). BF-ADL scores improved significantly in sham-controlled analyses (MD = - 1.69; p < 0.0001) and single-arm pre-post analyses (MD = - 3.22; p < 0.0001). Tremor amplitude and total TETRAS outcomes were inconsistent, with high heterogeneity (I2 up to 94%) driven mainly by differences in assessment timing; the pooled total TETRAS estimate was not statistically significant (p = 0.16). Adverse events were mostly mild and transient; skin irritation was the most frequently reported (7.88%), and no serious adverse events were attributed to the intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: PNS consistently improved functional outcomes with a favorable safety profile in ET patients. These findings support PNS as a viable adjunctive or on-demand non-invasive therapeutic option, particularly for medication-refractory patients or those unsuitable for surgery.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Gamified Rehabilitation Interventions in Patients with Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effects of gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation on functional oral intake and bedside swallowing function in patients with post-stroke dysphagia, and to explore feedback modality, post-stroke duration, and the robustness of the main findings. This meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Data, and SinoMed were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials published through December 22, 2025. The Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) was designated as the primary outcome and the Standardized Swallowing Assessment (SSA) as the secondary outcome. All pooled analyses used random-effects models, with exploratory subgroup analyses and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Seven RCTs involving 340 participants were included. Gamified or multicomponent gamified swallowing rehabilitation was associated with higher FOIS scores (MD=1.53, 95% CI: 0.58-2.49, P=0.002), with very high between-study heterogeneity (I2=96%). Pooled results from four RCTs showed lower SSA scores after gamified swallowing rehabilitation (MD=- 2.44, 95% CI: - 3.84 to - 1.04, P<0.001; I2=54%). The between-subgroup difference for FOIS according to sEMG use was not statistically significant (P=0.39), whereas the SSA subgroup difference was statistically significant (P=0.01). After excluding Hou et al. (2024) in the sensitivity analysis, the direction of the FOIS effect remained unchanged (MD=1.04, 95% CI: 0.46-1.61, P=0.0004; I2=85%). Current evidence suggests that gamified swallowing rehabilitation may improve FOIS and SSA outcomes in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. However, the number of included studies and participants was limited, heterogeneity for FOIS was very high, several studies had a high risk of bias, and multiple co-intervention components made the independent effect of gamification difficult to isolate. Findings from the sEMG and post-stroke-duration subgroups should therefore be considered exploratory. Further high-quality studies are needed to optimize intervention strategies and reduce heterogeneity.

articles.title: Targeting the P2X7 receptor in Alzheimer's disease: mechanistic insights and emerging therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia worldwide and is characterized by progressive cognitive decline, amyloid-β deposition, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, and neuronal loss. Current therapies provide only limited symptomatic benefit, and although anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies have demonstrated disease-modifying potential in selected patients, additional disease-modifying targets are still needed. The purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R), an ATP-gated ion channel predominantly expressed on microglia and astrocytes, has emerged as a key regulator of neuroinflammatory signalling and AD progression. This narrative review summarizes and critically discusses recent preclinical, translational, and clinical evidence published through 2026. Evidence from cellular and animal models, post-mortem human brain analyses, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging studies, and pharmacological investigations was evaluated to assess the role of P2X7R in AD pathogenesis and therapeutic intervention. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that extracellular ATP-mediated activation of P2X7R promotes NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, caspase-1 activation, and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-1β and interleukin-18, thereby sustaining chronic neuroinflammation. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of P2X7R reduced amyloid plaque burden, attenuated tau hyperphosphorylation, improved synaptic function, and ameliorated cognitive deficits in experimental AD models. Human studies further revealed elevated P2X7R expression and increased neuroinflammatory activity associated with AD pathology. Emerging therapeutic approaches include selective P2X7R antagonists, natural-product modulators, RNA-based interventions, nanotechnology-assisted drug delivery systems, and combination therapies targeting multiple pathogenic pathways. P2X7R represents a promising candidate target for disease-modifying therapeutic strategies in AD, based on convergent in vitro, animal-model, human post-mortem, and imaging/biomarker evidence linking ATP-mediated danger signalling to neuroinflammation, amyloid and tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. However, its clinical efficacy in AD remains to be established, as no clinical trial data for P2X7R-targeted therapies in this disease are yet available. Future clinical translation will require improved CNS-penetrant antagonists, enhanced receptor selectivity, biomarker-guided patient stratification, and precision medicine approaches.

articles.title: Refining risk prediction in geriatric heart failure: the emergency heart failure mortality risk grade‑BI model under scrutiny.
articles.abstract: Risk stratification is critical for managing acute heart failure in older adults, yet existing tools often underperform in geriatric populations. Özdemir recently introduced the EHMRG‑BI model, integrating brain natriuretic peptide and endotracheal intubation with the Emergency Heart Failure Mortality Risk Grade score to improve 30‑day mortality prediction. While the model demonstrates improved discrimination in a single‑center derivation cohort, several methodological considerations warrant attention. The inclusion of intubation, a treatment decision rather than a baseline characteristic, may introduce bias and limit its utility as an arrival‑time tool. The absence of key geriatric domains such as frailty, functional status, and cognitive impairment may result in residual confounding. Additionally, modelling BNP as a linear predictor disregards its well‑documented non‑linear association with mortality. This Matters Arising offers a perspective on these challenges and proposes refinements, including external validation, integration of geriatric assessments, and flexible BNP modelling, to strengthen the model's clinical applicability.

articles.title: Sample Adequacy PD-L1 and NGS in NSCLC: Shape-Sensing Robotic Assisted Bronchoscopy Versus CT Guided Lung Biopsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine assessment of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) is recommended to guide treatment selection in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Obtaining adequate tissue for biomarker and molecular analyses is therefore essential. This study compared sample adequacy for PD-L1 and NGS testing between shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) and computed tomography-guided transthoracic lung biopsy (CTTB) in patients with NSCLC.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with NSCLC who underwent biopsy of PPL by ssRAB or CTTB between June 2020 and December 2025. Demographic, procedural, pathological, biomarker and molecular data were extracted from electronic medical records, and descriptive statistics analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 402 patients were included, comprising 198 in the ssRAB cohort and 204 in the CTTB cohort. ssRAB demonstrated significantly higher sample adequacy rates than CTTB for both PD-L1 (98.8% vs. 90.6%, p < 0.001) and NGS testing (92.3% vs. 79.1%, p = 0.005). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, ssRAB was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 sample adequacy (adjusted OR 11.48, 95% CI 2.89-78.30; p = 0.002) and NGS sample adequacy (adjusted OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.64-11.40; p = 0.004) compared with CTTB. In a separate model evaluating biopsy tools, cryobiopsy use was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 adequacy (adjusted OR 16.54, 95% CI 2.92-317.65; p = 0.010) and NGS adequacy (adjusted OR 5.83, 95% CI 1.93-25.39; p = 0.006) compared with non-cryobiopsy sampling.

CONCLUSIONS: ssRAB-acquired specimens were associated with higher rates of PD-L1 and NGS sample adequacy than CTTB-acquired specimens in patients with NSCLC. Future prospective studies are needed to better understand the procedural and specimen-related factors underlying these differences.

articles.title: Epididymal cysts in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment approaches and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To systematically synthesise current evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, natural history, and outcomes reported under different management approaches for epididymal cysts (ECs) in boys.

METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through 31 August 2026. Observational studies including males younger than 18 years with ECs and reporting clinical outcomes were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses of single-arm proportions were performed for key prevalence outcomes.

RESULTS: Nine retrospective studies published between 2002 and 2025 were included, comprising 492 paediatric patients. No controlled comparative studies were identified. ECs were most frequently detected incidentally or during evaluation for painless scrotal swelling. Lesions were predominantly unilateral (79-90%), most were located in the epididymal head, and reported cyst size ranged from 2 to 40 mm. Associated conditions included hydrocele, varicocele, and testicular microlithiasis, with no reported link to malignancy. Conservative management was the preferred initial strategy in contemporary cohorts, whereas earlier series reported higher surgical rates. Surgery was mainly indicated for persistent pain or progressive enlargement and involved open excision, with high rates of symptom resolution and low reported morbidity. Meta-analysis showed that bilateral cysts occurred in 8% (95% CI 7-9%; I2 = 12.5%) of patients, complete spontaneous regression occurred in 12.2% (95% CI 8.3-16.1%; I2 = 88.1%), and 7.4% (95% CI 3.1-11.7%; I2 = 94.7%) of children required surgery. Postoperative complications were uncommon (3.4%; 95% CI 1.1-5.6%; I2 = 0%), and reported torsion events were rare (1.6%; 95% CI 0.7-2.5%; I2 = 0%); the available data did not establish that ECs predispose to testicular torsion.

CONCLUSION: Paediatric ECs are benign lesions with a favourable natural history. Many lesions remain clinically stable, while complete spontaneous regression occurs in a minority. A conservative-first approach is appropriate in most cases, reserving surgery for selected patients with persistent symptoms, clinically meaningful enlargement, or diagnostic uncertainty.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Epididymal cysts in children are benign extratesticular lesions, usually detected incidentally and commonly managed conservatively. • Surgical indications and follow-up strategies remain inconsistent across paediatric studies.

WHAT IS NEW: • To the best of our knowledge, and on the basis of the searches performed, this is the first systematic review and meta-analysis specifically evaluating paediatric ECs. • Our findings support a conservative-first approach, with low rates of surgery and reported complications, and question the value of routine prolonged ultrasonographic surveillance.

articles.title: Impact of Dimethyl Sulfoxide on Early Cardiotoxicity After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of cryopreserved grafts in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) increased substantially. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), used as a cryoprotective agent, is well recognized for its infusion-related toxicity; however, its impact on cardiac function remains unclear.

METHODS: This prospective study included 96 consecutive patients (median age 46 years) undergoing allogeneic HSCT. Patients were divided according to graft type into cryopreserved (n = 59, 61.5%) and non-cryopreserved (n = 37, 38.5%) groups. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment was performed before and after transplantation.

RESULTS: Significant changes were observed in diastolic parameters (E/A, and E/E'), structural parameters (left ventricular mass and left ventricular mass index), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and right ventricular ejection fraction following HSCT. In the cryopreserved group, E/A ratio decreased below the normal range and E/E' ratio increased significantly, whereas no such changes were observed in the non-cryopreserved group. During the 30-day follow-up period, symptomatic cardiovascular toxicity occurred in 5 patients (5.2%), while subclinical cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction was detected in 16 patients (16.7%). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that GLS predicted cardiotoxicity with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.79-0.98; p < 0.0001). At a cut-off value of - 16.8%, sensitivity was 100% and specificity was 79%.

CONCLUSION: Cryopreserved graft administration may be associated with early alterations in left ventricular diastolic function, potentially reflecting DMSO-related cardiotoxicity. GLS appears to be a sensitive marker for the early detection and prediction of cardiotoxicity in patients undergoing allogeneic HSCT.

articles.title: Incidence, risk factors, and mortality of acute kidney injury in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: analysis by acute kidney injury subtype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. It can result from conventional causes or immune-mediated mechanisms. This study aimed to determine the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of all-cause AKI in patients treated with ICIs.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed adults treated with ICIs at Korea University Anam Hospital between 2015 and 2024. AKI occurring within 12 months after treatment initiation was defined according to the KDIGO (Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes) criteria. It was classified as transient azotemia (recovery within 72 hours) or sustained AKI (>72 hours), including acute tubular necrosis (ATN), obstruction, and ICI-associated AKI (ICI-AKI).

RESULTS: Among 943 patients, the overall incidence of AKI was 32.1%. ATN was most common, followed by transient azotemia, obstruction, and immune-mediated acute tubulointerstitial nephritis. Pre-existing chronic kidney disease and proton pump inhibitor use were independent risk factors for immune-mediated AKI, whereas low serum albumin, high C-reactive protein, and hepatobiliary cancers were associated with ATN. Transient azotemia and ATN were independently associated with higher mortality. Although ICI-AKI was also significantly associated with increased mortality, the association was modest and should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of cases (n = 25).

CONCLUSION: ATN and transient azotemia were more frequent than ICI-AKI and were associated with worse prognosis; ICI-AKI also showed a statistically significant but modest association with mortality. Identifying different risk factors for each subtype may help clinicians achieve earlier recognition and optimize management in patients receiving ICI therapy.

articles.title: Differential Effects of Direct Plasmin Inhibition and Tranexamic Acid on Atherosclerosis Progression and Vascular Remodeling in Apoe/Ldlr Double-Knockout Mice.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The fibrinolytic system may protect against or promote atherosclerosis; however, the effects of distinct antifibrinolytic interventions on plaque development and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling remain unclear.

METHODS: We compared YO-2, a direct plasmin inhibitor, and tranexamic acid (TXA), a lysine analog that interferes with plasminogen/plasmin binding to fibrin, in Apoe/Ldlr double-knockout mice fed a Western diet. The atherosclerotic burden, plaque structure, vascular marker expression, leukocyte-endothelial interactions, and nitric oxide (NO)-related indices were assessed.

RESULTS: YO-2 significantly increased the atherosclerotic lesion area compared to the control, whereas TXA had minimal effects. The thrombolytic activity in the He-Ne laser-induced thrombosis model and NO-related indices did not differ significantly among the groups. Vascular t-PA expression increased in both treatment groups. YO-2 was associated with reduced uPAR and MMP-9 expression and preservation of the internal elastic lamina and medial elastin fibers, suggesting reduced pericellular ECM degradation. TXA increased PAI-1 and TAFI expression without altering uPAR. Both treatments significantly reduced leukocyte rolling, and the E-selectin expression was significantly decreased with YO-2, with a similar trend with TXA. eNOS mRNA expression was significantly higher in both groups, although the corresponding increase in the eNOS protein expression was only a non-significant trend.

CONCLUSIONS: Direct plasmin inhibition with YO-2 aggravated atherosclerosis and it was associated with a reduced uPAR/MMP-9 expression and altered vascular ECM remodeling. TXA had limited effects on lesion burden while increasing PAI-1 and TAFI expression. These findings suggest that direct plasmin inhibition and TXA-mediated antifibrinolysis may differentially affect atherosclerosis and vascular remodeling.

articles.title: Metreleptin improves glucose metabolism and hepatic steatosis in a patient with Werner syndrome and partial lipodystrophy: a case report with review of literature.
articles.abstract: Werner syndrome (WS) is a rare autosomal recessive progeroid disorder caused by mutations in the WRN gene and is characterized by distinctive physical features and metabolic complications, including insulin resistance, diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, and hepatic steatosis. Although lipodystrophy is a recognized component of WS, clinical reports of metreleptin use in this setting remain very limited. We report the case of a 38-year-old woman with WS complicated by partial lipodystrophy, diabetes with suboptimal glycemic levels, hypertriglyceridemia and severe hepatic steatosis. She presented with distal limb lipoatrophy, a bird-like facial appearance, premature hair graying, and cataracts. Genetic testing identified two pathogenic WRN variants (c.1105C>T and c.3446del) resulting in premature protein termination, confirming the diagnosis. At baseline, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was 8.6% despite insulin and oral hypoglycemic agents, and imaging demonstrated hepatomegaly with marked steatosis. Metreleptin therapy was initiated and titrated. Over 26 weeks, HbA1c improved to 7.4% and the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio decreased, accompanied by reduction in liver transaminases, cholestatic enzymes, and imaging-based indices of hepatic steatosis, liver stiffness, and liver volume. To date, only three cases of WS treated with metreleptin, including ours, have been reported. While glycemic improvement is consistent with prior reports, our case additionally demonstrated improvements in hepatic steatosis across biochemical, and imaging parameters. These findings suggest that metreleptin may improve both glucose metabolism and hepatic steatosis in WS-associated lipodystrophy. Further accumulation of cases is essential to clarify its role in the management of WS.

articles.title: Accelerated Systemic Atherosclerosis Following Immune-Related Adverse Events in a Patient with Primary Thoracic Melanoma: A Case of Sequential Coronary and Peripheral Revascularization.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in advanced melanoma, but they may accelerate atherosclerosis, particularly in patients with immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A 64-year-old man with stage IV BRAF-wild-type primary thoracic melanoma achieved complete remission after nivolumab plus ipilimumab, but he later developed grade 3 immune-related hepatitis, requiring treatment discontinuation. Three and a half years later, symptomatic peripheral artery disease required revascularization, followed by severe coronary artery disease requiring percutaneous coronary intervention one year later. This case suggests that severe irAEs may be associated with accelerated systemic atherosclerosis, highlighting the importance of long-term cardiovascular surveillance following ICI therapy.

articles.title: The Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Atrial Fibrillation and Reflux Esophagitis Among Individuals Undergoing Health Checkups.
articles.abstract: Objective　To examine the association between atrial fibrillation (AF) and reflux esophagitis (RE).Methods　A total of 5,205 adults (3,262 men, 1,943 women; mean age, 54.9±9.8 years) who underwent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) as part of a routine health checkup were enrolled in this study. AF was defined as AF detected on electrocardiography during the checkup and/or a documented history of the condition. RE was assessed endoscopically according to the Los Angeles classification. The smoking history, habitual alcohol consumption, and use of acid-suppressive agents were also assessed.Results　AF was observed in 36 participants (0.7%). Compared with those without AF, participants with AF were more likely to be male, older, have a higher body mass index, and have a history of smoking and acid-suppressive agent use. After excluding participants receiving acid-suppressive medications, RE was significantly more prevalent in patients with AF than in those without AF (39.1% vs. 22.0%, p=0.049). The prevalence of AF was 0.9% among patients with RE and 0.4% among those without RE. However, multiple logistic regression analysis indicated that RE was not independently associated with AF after adjusting for sex, age, and other clinical factors.Conclusion　AF may be associated with RE in individuals undergoing routine health checkups. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for sex, age, and other clinical factors, suggesting that it may be largely explained by shared confounding factors.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics Associated with Mortality between Surviving and Non-surviving Adult Patients with Severe Influenza Requiring Hospitalization: An Internet-based, Prospective, Multicenter, Cohort Study in Japan.
articles.abstract: Introduction　Influenza remains a huge issue, but its prognosis and clinical characteristics are still unclear. This study aimed to clarify the clinical differences between adults hospitalized with influenza between survivors and nonsurvivors.Methods　Clinical data of patients who were severely ill with influenza and required hospitalization were gathered and analyzed between September 2019 and August 2025 (six influenza seasons) using an internet surveillance system; patients who did not survive were excluded.Results　Of the 490 patients with severe influenza, 32 (6.53%) did not survive and were older than the surviving patients. In the non-surviving patients, very few or none had been vaccinated against influenza or pneumococcal infections. The non-surviving patients had more pure viral pneumonia and more received mechanical ventilation. The male-to-female ratio, underlying diseases, virus type, and use of antibiotics were similar between survivors and non-survivors.Conclusions　Non-surviving patients were older and developed more severe respiratory failure due to pure viral pneumonia than surviving patients. Very low vaccination rates for influenza and pneumococcus might be suggested in hospitalized adults with severe influenza.

articles.title: Dynamic Bronchoscopic Evolution of a Cobblestone-like Appearance in COVID-19-associated Pulmonary Aspergillosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) is associated with high mortality and diagnostic difficulties. We report a fatal case of CAPA with a distinctive cobblestone-like tracheobronchial appearance observed during bronchoscopy. A patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis for chronic kidney disease was admitted with severe COVID-19. Bronchoscopy revealed multiple white tracheobronchial plaques, suggestive of an invasive Aspergillus infection. Despite antifungal therapy, respiratory failure progressed, and repeat bronchoscopy revealed worsening cobblestone-like lesions. The patient died despite receiving intensive treatment. Autopsy confirmed Aspergillus hyphal invasion, corresponding to the bronchoscopic findings, highlighting a rare but diagnostically important airway manifestation of CAPA.

articles.title: Bloomy Rind Sign in Leptomeningeal Carcinomatosis Associated with EGFR-Mutated Lung Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: We report two cases of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (LMC) associated with EGFR exon 19 deletion lung adenocarcinoma, in which the "bloomy rind sign" on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provided supportive radiological evidence. In Case 1, the progression of MRI findings paralleled rising cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) carcinoembryonic antigen levels, exceeding serum concentrations despite persistently negative cytology. In Case 2, the sign appeared with recurrent intracranial hypertension and positive CSF cytology results. Despite treatment, both patients deteriorated in their condition. These cases suggest that the bloomy rind sign may raise suspicion of LMC despite unrevealing cytology; in Case 1, serial CSF CEA changes paralleled the clinical course of the patient.

articles.title: Utility of Blood Neutrophil to Diagnose Bacterial Infections under Satralizumab Treatment for Aquaporin-4 Antibody-positive Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder: A Report of Two Cases.
articles.abstract: Satralizumab is an anti-interleukin-6 receptor biologic that may mask bacterial infections. We report two patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder who developed afebrile bacterial infections with normal C-reactive protein levels during satralizumab treatment. During non-infectious periods under satralizumab treatment, the neutrophil count and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio decreased, whereas the neutrophil change ratio, defined as the ratio of present to previous neutrophil counts, did not. At the time of infection, these variables were elevated compared to the intra-individual confidence intervals during non-infectious periods. These cases indicate the utility of neutrophil-related parameters in diagnosing bacterial infections during satralizumab treatment.

articles.title: Ampullary Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Presenting with Clinically Confirmed Endogenous Hyperinsulinemic Hypoglycemia.
articles.abstract: A 65-year-old man without diabetes presented with fasting hypoglycemia. During a fasting test, plasma glucose decreased to 46 mg/dL with inappropriately elevated insulin (11.1 μU/mL) and C-peptide (8.7 ng/mL) levels, confirming endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Imaging revealed a tumor of the ampulla of Vater with multiple liver metastases but no pancreatic lesions. An endoscopic biopsy revealed poorly differentiated small cell-type NEC with a Ki-67 index >90% and complete loss of RB1 expression. Despite negative insulin immunostaining, dynamic endocrine testing confirmed endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. These findings were clinically consistent with ectopic insulin secretion from the NEC, although pathological confirmation was not obtained in this case. This case highlights the importance of integrating physiological, radiological, and pathological findings when evaluating suspected ectopic insulin secretion.

articles.title: Paradoxical bradycardia from occult venous hemorrhage mimicking vasovagal syncope - A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic shock typically presents with tachycardia; however, profound hypovolemia can paradoxically induce bradycardia via the Bezold-Jarisch reflex. This can lead to misdiagnosis of vasovagal syncope, causing dangerous treatment delays.

CASE: A 50-year-old woman developed profound bradycardia and hypotension after vomiting in the post-anesthesia care unit after undergoing hysterectomy. Despite initial management of vasovagal syncope, her condition remained refractory to vasopressors. A critically low hemoglobin level of 5.5 g/dL strongly suggested massive occult hemorrhage. She underwent emergency laparotomy for a 1,500 ml pelvic hematoma and recovered without complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Paradoxical bradycardia is a rare, but life-threatening, sign of occult hemorrhage. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for hemorrhage when hemodynamic instability is refractory to standard vagal management.

articles.title: Phospholipase Fluorogenic Probes and Molecular Determinants of Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Binding to Cyclic Oligonucleotide-Based Antiphage Signaling System CapV.
articles.abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection by producing cyclic nucleotide second messengers that activate downstream effector proteins. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP)-activated phospholipase in Vibrio (CapV) is a prevalent CBASS effector whose activity is commonly monitored using the commercially available fluorogenic substrate resorufin butyrate; however, this probe is hydrolyzed by both basal and activated CapV, limiting its usefulness in CapV-related studies. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of a series of resorufin ester probes with varying acyl chain lengths to improve the fluorogenic assay used to monitor CapV (from Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio cholerae) activation. While resorufin butyrate and pentanoate exhibited substantial cGAMP-independent hydrolysis, resorufin octanoate and decanoate provided an optimal balance between catalytic turnover and activation-dependent discrimination, displaying over 5-fold and approximately 10-fold increases in hydrolysis, respectively, upon 3',3'-cGAMP activation. Using resorufin octanoate as a fluorogenic reporter, we systematically investigated the effects of cyclic dinucleotide structural modifications on CapV activation. Phosphorothioate analogues with nonbridging sulfur (exo-S linkages) retained partial agonist activity, whereas the corresponding bridging 5'-phosphorothioester (endo-S) analogues was inactive, highlighting the importance of the native phosphodiester moiety in activating CapV. Replacement of the ribose 2'-hydroxyl groups with fluorine preserved CapV activation, whereas 2'-deoxy substitutions reduced activity, with modifications on the adenosine moiety having a greater detrimental effect than those on guanosine. These findings using the fluorogenic probes were validated using phospholipid hydrolysis and activity-based protein labeling assays. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the observed activity trends arise from differential disruption of key hydrogen-bonding interactions and ligand conformations required for productive CapV activation. Together, these fluorogenic probes provide a robust, high-throughput-compatible platform for studying CapV activation and defining cyclic dinucleotide structure-activity relationships.

articles.title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Evaluator-Blind, Randomized, Comparator-Controlled Study of Belotero Intense (+), a Hyaluronic Acid Filler With Lidocaine, for Lip Augmentation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lip augmentation with hyaluronic acid (HA)-based dermal fillers is commonly performed to enhance lip volume, shape, and symmetry.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to establish the safety and effectiveness of Belotero Intense with lidocaine (BIL), a cohesive polydensified matrix HA filler, for lip augmentation, and demonstrate its noninferiority to Restylane Silk with lidocaine (RSL), a US FDA-approved HA filler.

METHODS: Patients with a Merz Lip Fullness Assessment Scale (MLFAS) rating of very thin, thin, or medium on upper and lower lips (Fitzpatrick skin type [FST] I-IV) or at least one lip (FST V or VI) were randomized 3:1 to receive BIL or RSL at baseline. Touch-up treatment was allowed at Week 4; retreatment at Week 48 was offered to BIL patients only. Primary effectiveness was assessed by a blinded evaluator using the MLFAS, and adverse events (AEs) were recorded up to 60 weeks.

RESULTS: Belotero Intense with lidocaine achieved a Week 8 MLFAS-responder rate of 91.1% (144/158; 95% CI, 85.6-95.1), with the lower limit of the CI exceeding the prespecified 50% success criterion. The least squares mean difference in change from baseline vs RSL was 0.1 (95% CI, 0.0-0.3), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (ie, lower CI limit >-0.5). Among Week 8 responders, 70/137 (51.1%) maintained improvement through Week 48 (post hoc analysis). No severe or serious related treatment-emergent AEs or unexpected AEs were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Belotero Intense with lidocaine is a safe and effective treatment for lip augmentation in patients with upper and/or lower lip volume deficits.

articles.title: Outcomes in patients with diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and heart failure treated with tirzepatide or dulaglutide: SURPASS-CVOT analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The impact of tirzepatide and dulaglutide on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and heart failure (HF) outcomes according to HF status is unknown.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were treated with tirzepatide up to 15 mg or dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly (average 4 years). The incidence of MACE-3 [cardiovascular (CV) death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke], MACE-4 (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization) and composite of all-cause or CV death and hospitalization or urgent visits for HF were analysed in patients with and without a history of HF. A history of HF (20.3%) was associated with more coronary artery disease and prior MI. Incidences of event categories were higher in the HF group. The hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF on tirzepatide vs. dulaglutide was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-0.99] in patients with HF and 0.88 (95%CI 0.78-1.00) without HF. The HR for CV death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF was 0.85 (95%CI 0.70-1.03) and 0.96 (95%CI 0.83-1.12), for MACE-3 0.90 (95%CI 0.76-1.08) and 0.93 (95%CI 0.83-1.04), and for MACE-4 0.81 (95%CI 0.69-0.95) and 0.91 (95%CI 0.83-1.00) in patients with and without HF, respectively. The patient-reported outcomes of APPADL and EQ-5D-5L visual analogue scores improved and were higher on tirzepatide in both groups.

CONCLUSION: With overall non-inferiority established, this exploratory analysis revealed lower rates of the composite of all-cause death or HF events, or MACE-4 among patients with T2D and HF treated with tirzepatide compared with dulaglutide.

articles.title: Reported outcomes for patients following postoperative periprosthetic femoral fractures : a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Postoperative periprosthetic femoral fracture (POPFF) is an increasingly common and morbid complication of arthroplasty. This review aims to determine what outcomes are reported for POPFF and how they are measured, to inform the development of a core outcome set.

METHODS: Systematic searches of major databases and clinical trial registries (June 2014 to May 2024) identified studies reporting outcomes for more than five POPFF patients in English or Chinese. Multiple reviewers performed study screening and data extraction. Outcomes were extracted verbatim, collapsed into outcome domain subcategories, and categorized. Outcomes were synthesized descriptively, with subgroup exploration by implant (hip/knee) and economic setting.

RESULTS: A total of 564 studies, comprising 119,445 POPFF patients (mean age 75.0 years (38.5 to 90.0); median percentage of female patients 61.8%), were included. Across the studies, 2,711 individual reported outcomes were collapsed into 671 unique terms within 59 outcome domain subcategories. Outcome reporting was dominated by the physiological/clinical core area (38.7%), followed by life impact (29.3%), resource use (12.8%), adverse events (11.7%), and death (7.6%). The most frequently reported subcategories were bone union/healing, surgical complications, component/prosthesis outcomes, hip function, and mortality/survival. Only 46.4% of outcomes were accompanied by a clear definition or named outcome measurement instrument; for bone union, just 7.4% provided a clear definition, 44.9% were vague, and 47.7% provided none. Health-related quality of life was measured in 6.9% of studies (39 instances) using seven instruments, most commonly the 12/36-Item Short-Form Health Survey questionnaire and EuroQol five-dimension questionnaire. Patterns varied between hip and knee POPFF and between high-income and low- to middle-income settings; one-year mortality was the most frequently reported survival timepoint.

CONCLUSION: Outcome reporting after POPFF is heterogeneous, clinician-centred, and frequently undefined, with sparse use of patient-reported outcome measures and health-related quality of life instruments. These findings support the development of a POPFF core outcome set and recommended outcome measurement instruments to standardize reporting and promote patient-centred research.

articles.title: Adult Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

articles.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges.

METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point.

RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2).

CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

articles.title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection.

METHODS: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
