Patients with compensated cardiac dysfunction and manageable neuromuscular impairment should not be excluded from transplantation solely on the basis of mitochondrial cytopathy.

articles.title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

articles.title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

articles.title: Randomized trial of counter-pressure and position maneuvers to prevent vasovagal syncope after intravenous cannulation for cardiac CT: The CoPPMan-IVC trial.
Design foresight and model humility for omics inference.
articles.abstract: Omics inference increasingly proceeds transcriptome-first: measure RNA, then ask how much biology can be extracted later. The ordering should be settled before the assay is chosen, not reconstructed from the data afterward. The first question is what the target requires to be directly observed; the second, what claims the data can honestly support. Design foresight means choosing assays, sampling, and orthogonal measurements based on the question and saying whether transcriptomics is primary, supporting, or insufficient for that claim. Model humility means refusing to promote computational output beyond what the data and assumptions can bear and writing measured, inferred, and predicted results in voices matched to their support. Using transcriptomics as the central case, we argue for question-first omics inference.

articles.title: Parallel culprit-thrombus transcriptomic and genome-wide association analyses in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: An exploratory pilot study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct molecular characterization of culprit coronary thrombi may provide insights into local mechanisms of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) that are not captured by circulating blood. We investigated thrombus-associated transcriptomic patterns and their relationship with inherited genetic susceptibility.

METHODS: High-depth RNA sequencing was performed on paired aspirated culprit thrombi and peripheral blood from 10 patients with first-time STEMI. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2, with exploratory signals defined by nominal P < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change ≥ 1.5. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied across 44,525 transcripts. Transcript-clinical associations and sensitivity analyses were also performed. In parallel, a genome-wide association study included 1787 patients with STEMI and 17,837 age- and sex-matched controls.

RESULTS: Although 708 transcripts met the nominal exploratory criteria, none remained significant after transcriptome-wide correction. The nominal signals converged on biologically relevant processes, including extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory and chemokine signaling, lipid and apolipoprotein regulation, angiogenesis, and metalloprotease activity. These patterns likely reflected both local thrombus biology and differences in cellular composition between thrombi and peripheral blood. Clinical correlations and differences according to prior coronary artery disease were not robust after multiplicity correction or sensitivity analysis. Genome-wide association analysis identified rs74755602 at the MASTL locus (odds ratio, 2.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.65-2.63; P = 7.85 × 10-10), but MASTL showed no corresponding differential expression.

CONCLUSION: Paired thrombus-blood profiling revealed coherent but exploratory transcriptomic patterns related to thrombosis, inflammation, and vascular remodeling. The independent MASTL association lacked transcriptomic concordance, supporting cautious interpretation and further functional validation.

articles.title: FDG-PET in Infection Imaging of Immuno-compromised Patients.
articles.abstract: Infectious syndromes represent a monumental challenge in the management of immunocompromised patients, directly driving high rates of morbidity and critical mortality. This clinical cohort comprised oncological populations undergoing aggressive cytoreductive chemotherapy, end-stage renal disease patients dependent on specialized long-term dialysis access networks, and individuals undergoing treatment with advanced antiretroviral regimens. Because these individuals suffer from blunted or suppressed cellular immune mechanisms, standard structural imaging methodologies (such as standard digital radiography and cross-sectional computed tomography) exhibit prolonged diagnostic latency, frequently remaining negative or ambiguous during the crucial early windows of active pathogen replication.

articles.title: The DePICtion study: Implementing a diabetes classification tool in UK primary care-A qualitative study with primary care staff and patients.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The correct classification of diabetes (type 1, type 2 or rarer genetic forms) is essential for optimal treatment, but misclassification is common. The Diabetes in Primary Care Improving Classification (DePICtion) tool uses routinely collected clinical data to flag patients at risk of misclassification and prioritise them for further diagnostic testing.

AIM: To explore the acceptability and implementation of the DePICtion tool in primary care.

DESIGN AND SETTING: A qualitative study in 11 general practices across the Southwest and East Midlands, UK.

METHOD: Twelve practices were recruited to the study; 11 practices ran the tool and reviewed flagged patients. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 staff and 11 patients to explore their experiences of the tool, reactions to the results and barriers and facilitators to use. Data were analysed thematically in NVivo.

RESULTS: Staff found the tool straightforward, compatible with existing workflows and clinically useful. Implementation required time and ownership of the process. Patients' responses were shaped by trust in staff and the personal meaning of their diabetes: Some viewed reclassification as a threat to their diagnostic identity, while others welcomed further diagnostic testing. Data privacy concerns were minimal but competing demands on staff time and resources were ubiquitously reported.

CONCLUSION: The DePICtion tool is acceptable and clinically useful for improving diabetes classification in primary care. Routine implementation is technically feasible but will require protected time, clear pathways for follow-up and support for patient communication and engagement.

articles.title: Nationwide Evolution of Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Outcomes Following Introduction of the HeartMate 3 and Destination Therapy in Japan　- The Third Official Report From J-MACS.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nationwide impact in Japan of contemporary improvement in the clinical management of durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), together with the introduction of the HeartMate 3 (Abbott, Pleasanton, CA, USA), on clinical outcomes remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed all patients undergoing durable LVAD implantation in Japan between 2011 and 2025. Patients were divided into an early era (up to 2018) and the contemporary era (since 2019), reflecting introduction of the HeartMate 3 in Japan. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during LVAD support. Among 1,859 patients, 1,587 underwent bridge-to-transplantation and 272 underwent destination therapy. Survival improved significantly in the contemporary era compared with the early era (5-year survival 84% vs. 76%, respectively; P=0.0002). Device dysfunction-free, pump thrombus-free, stroke-free, major bleeding-free, and pump exchange-free survival also improved significantly after 2019 (all P<0.0001). Right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia that required appropriate defibrillation remained frequent complications. Among patients who received a durable LVAD since 2019, destination therapy recipients had lower survival than bridge-to-transplantation recipients (3-year survival 81% vs. 91%; P=0.0057).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes after durable LVAD implantation improved substantially following the introduction of HeartMate 3 in Japan, particularly regarding pump-related and hemocompatibility-related complications. However, right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia remain major unresolved challenges.

articles.title: Physiological within-day Variation in Lipoprotein(a): Is a Once-in-a-lifetime Measurement Sufficient for Cardiovascular Risk Evaluation?
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a strong risk factor for cardiovascular events, independent of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Because the Lp(a) concentration is largely determined by genetic factors, some dyslipidemia guidelines recommend a once-in-a-lifetime measurement of Lp(a). Furthermore, a non-fasting lipid profile assessment is allowed for initial screening of dyslipidemia. Although the LDL-C concentration decreases slightly throughout the day, the within-day variation of Lp(a) remains unknown. We aimed to investigate whether the Lp(a) concentration remains stable throughout the day.

METHODS: Lp(a) concentrations were measured at seven time points throughout the day in 34 patients using a latex turbidimetric immunoassay. The Lp(a) values are expressed in molar units, which are equivalent to those determined by a mass spectrometry-based reference measurement procedure.

RESULTS: We found that the Lp(a) concentrations decreased by 2.9±5.2 nmol/L at 14:00 (p＜0.05), 3.6±4.8 nmol/L at 20:00 (p＜0.001), and 2.9±5.1 nmol/L at 24:00 (p＜0.05). The mean percent Lp(a) decreased significantly at 17:30 (-6.2±0.1%) and 24:00 (-7.0±0.1%) from the fasting level.

CONCLUSION: The Lp(a) concentration decreases slightly, but significantly, throughout the day. Considering physiological variations, it is preferable to re-evaluate the Lp(a) concentration in those with a borderline elevation.

articles.title: Associations of Albuminuria and eGFR with Stiffness Parameter β in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The stiffness parameter β is a clinical index of arterial stiffness that reflects systemic atherosclerosis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major cardiovascular risk factor in type 2 diabetes; however, it remains unclear whether a reduced kidney function or albuminuria is more strongly associated with arterial stiffness. This study examined the relative associations of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) with stiffness parameter β in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,924 patients with type 2 diabetes. The stiffness parameter β was assessed at the common carotid artery using ultrasonography.

RESULTS: The participants were 58.8% male, with a median age of 63 years and a median HbA1c level of 8.3%. According to univariate analyses, stiffness parameter β was significantly correlated with both eGFR and UACR. However, after adjusting for conventional cardiovascular risk factors, stiffness parameter β remained independently associated with UACR, whereas no independent association was observed with eGFR. Similar findings were observed when eGFR and albuminuria were analyzed according to the CKD categories. No significant interactions were observed between UACR and either age or body mass index in relation to stiffness parameter β.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes, albuminuria, but not eGFR, was independently associated with stiffness parameter β after multivariable adjustment. These findings suggest that albuminuria may serve as a marker of local carotid arterial stiffening and vascular injury.

articles.title: Capability, opportunity and motivation to support adults with type 1 diabetes experiencing fear of hypoglycaemia: A survey of Australian diabetes healthcare professionals.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the perceptions, experiences and unmet needs of diabetes healthcare professionals (DHPs) for supporting adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) with fear of hypoglycaemia (FoH).

METHOD: An online survey explored Australian DHPs' perceived capability, opportunity, motivation and behaviours related to supporting adults with T1D with FoH. DHPs were recruited via online advertisements, e-newsletters and at conferences. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were analysed thematically.

RESULTS: A total of 106 eligible DHPs were included (83% credentialled diabetes educators, 92% women, mean (SD) age 49 (11) years), from all eight states/territories. DHPs indicated that FoH is experienced by almost two thirds of adults with T1D in their clinics. Most DHPs believe addressing FoH is within their scope of clinical practice (83%), and report motivation (89%) and capability (skills and confidence, 71% and 70% respectively) to do so. While more than half (50%-71%) perceive they have the social opportunity (e.g. social norms, workplace culture), few report physical opportunity (8%-24%), for example, access to validated screening tools; financial remuneration; affordable mental healthcare referral pathways. Free-text responses highlighted the need for affordable and timely access to mental health professionals with knowledge about diabetes. Approximately eight out of ten would be (very) likely to refer those experiencing FoH to online self-guided programs, if available.

CONCLUSION: These findings show that Australian DHPs report the motivation and capability, but lack the opportunity to support adults with T1D experiencing FoH. Innovative referral pathways, including online self-guided programmes, are perceived positively and may be useful in the Australian healthcare context.

articles.title: The impact of frailty on glycaemic control in older adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus: An observational study.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

articles.title: Estimating the long-term cost-effectiveness of a free online Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support service in England: Healthy living for people with type 2 diabetes, using a matched cohort study design.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The National Health Service (NHS) offers Healthy Living, an online Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support service, to help people Self Manage Type 2 Diabetes, with modest 1-year reductions in HbA1c levels, systolic blood pressure and body mass index. We aim to assess the cost-effectiveness of Healthy Living compared with usual care.

METHODS: A patient-level economic simulation model (UKPDS-OM2.1) was used to conduct an economic analysis from the NHS perspective over a lifetime horizon, discounted at 3.5%. The model translated risk factor reductions to long-term cost and quality-adjusted life year (QALY) estimates. Additional analyses estimated intervention and medication cost consequences.

RESULTS: The UKPDS-OM2.1 predicted a modest improvement in health (0.016 QALYs) and a small reduction in lifetime healthcare costs (-£4 per person). Offsetting with intervention costs (£7 per user) and increased medication costs (£212 per user) yielded a net cost of £216 per user. The cost-per-QALY of £13,192 was below the lower NICE threshold (£25,000/QALY), indicating that the programme is cost-effective. Sensitivity analyses largely demonstrated robustness, but the finding was sensitive to structural assumptions about disease progression post-intervention with the inclusion of medication costs.

CONCLUSION: Healthy Living appears to be a low-cost, online intervention for self managing type 2 diabetes, generating modest health benefits that are likely to be considered cost-effective use of NHS resources. While there is some uncertainty in the cost-effectiveness and the modelling is based on effectiveness estimated from observational data, improvements in uptake and adherence has the potential to improve the value for money to the NHS.

articles.title: Microglial Presenilin-1 modulates neuronal function and memory-associated behaviors.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Microglial cells, the macrophages of the brain parenchyma, are increasingly recognized to play a key role in synaptic plasticity and function. Presenilin 1 (PS1) is an essential protein involved in learning and memory; the loss of neuronal Presenilin function causes cognitive deficits and impaired synapse plasticity in mice. Here we show memory enhancement in male mice lacking PS1 in microglia (PS1ΔMG). Leveraging high-throughput RNA sequencing with single-cell deconvolution-analysis, we estimate that PS1ΔMG increases Cd52-lo microglial population, a proliferative group enriched in AP-1 responsive genes; and increases chemokines Ccl7 and Ccl8 In silico prediction of binding partners showed that microglial CCL7 may act via inhibition of neuronal CCR5, a receptor known to negatively regulate learning and memory. By profiling active neuronal populations via PhosphoTRAP the data showed a non-autonomous cell effect of microglial PS1 by modulating genes involved in neuronal excitability and synaptic plasticity. Ex vivo electrophysiology and in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving mice confirm these effects with functional changes in CA1 hippocampus as seen by increased NMDA/AMPA ratios and increased amplitude of neuronal Ca2+ transients in freely behaving animals, respectively. Remarkably, PS1ΔMG mice exhibited increased memory retention in contextual fear conditioning and novel object recognition. Together, these data suggest a novel mechanism where microglial PS1 negatively regulates neuronal activity through modulation of NMDAR and memory-associated behaviors.Significance Statement Microglia are increasingly recognized as active regulators of neuronal function, yet the molecular mechanisms that constrain their influence on synaptic activity remain incompletely defined. This study identifies microglial Presenilin-1 (PS1) as a key regulator of neuron-microglia signaling that shapes synaptic transmission and learning. We show that loss of microglial PS1 shifts microglia toward a transcriptional and signaling state that enhances NMDA receptor-dependent synaptic activity and improves memory, demonstrating that microglial molecular programs can directly modulate neuronal excitability. These findings establish microglial PS1 as a physiological brake on circuit plasticity and reveal that altering microglial signaling alone is sufficient to influence cognition. Targeting microglial regulatory pathways may therefore provide new strategies to enhance synaptic resilience and cognitive function in brain disorders.

articles.title: iGABASnFR Imaging Reveals that GABA Clearance is rapidly overwhelmed in the Cerebral Cortex.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Both phasic and tonic GABAergic activity in the cortex, is shaped by the clearance of GABA from the extracellular space by GABA transporters (GATs). However, estimates of the time-course of GAT activity from GAT currents, GABAA, and GABAB electrophysiological recordings range from tens of milliseconds to multiple seconds. These estimates may reflect receptor properties rather than extracellular GABA dynamics. Understanding how long GABA is free in the extracellular space is key to understanding how inhibition controls activity, but has been technically challenging. Here, we utilize the fluorescent GABA sensor, iGABASnFr, to enable us to optically assay extracellular GABA dynamics following bursts of synaptic activity. In the mouse cerebral cortex of either sex, we show that GABA rapidly disperses from release sites via diffusion, with very little role for active transport by GATs. Following diffusion from the sites of release, GABA then accumulates in the extracellular space, where GATs require hundreds of milliseconds to remove it. For areas of high density GABA release or during bursts of activity, this clearance is further slowed. Continued GABA release and summation in the extracellular space for bursts of activity contrasts with recorded Inhibitory post-synaptic current (IPSC) signals, which rapidly depress with additional stimuli, suggesting a disconnect between IPSCs and extracellular GABA. Lastly, the resulting extracellular accumulation of GABA can act hetero-synaptically by activating and/or desensitizing GABAA receptors. Together, this raises new questions about how GABAergic inhibition works to shape network function and suggests a spatiotemporal continuum of extracellular GABA.Significance Statement We use combined iGABASnFr neurotransmitter imaging, electrophysiology, and modeling to show that with trains of synaptic activity, GABA clearance is slowed and GABA rapidly accumulates in the extracellular space. Additionally, we demonstrate that GABA largely diffuses from release sites rather than being captured by GABA transporters and that these transporters have only a small role in shaping extracellular GABA dynamics in the mouse cortex. Lastly, we show that extracellular GABA accumulation can heterosynaptically desensitize GABAA receptors, modulating local phasic inhibition.

articles.title: Degrees of certainty: beyond threshold thinking in sport and exercise science.
Deletion size and background genetic variation shape congenital heart disease phenotypes in 3016 individuals with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
UK consensus recommendations for onward testing for Lynch syndrome in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) non-colorectal/non-endometrial cancers.
Diabetic ketoacidosis in a patient with renal cell carcinoma on immune checkpoint inhibitor.
Mechanism-specific acute silent ischaemic lesions and ischaemic periprocedural stroke after PTAS for severe symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
What are we missing? Using consultation free-text to identify underdiagnosed osteoarthritis in military personnel.
Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs.
articles.abstract: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are essential for insect olfaction, enabling the detection of carboxylic acids, amines, moisture, and temperature cues that mediate critical behaviors, including mosquito host-seeking 1,2. However, the structural mechanisms underlying ligand specificity and channel activation in these receptors remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures and functional validation of the IR8a-IR75k complex from the malaria mosquito Anopheles stephensi, a carboxylic acid detector, captured in four states: the ligand-free full-length closed form (apo state), the ligand induced full-length open state, and the nonanoic acid (NA)- and octanoic acid (OA)-bound extracellular domains. These structures reveal a dynamic ligand-binding pocket in IR75k, in which specificity is determined by alkyl chain length and carboxylate geometry. Ligand binding triggers closure of IR75k's bilobed ligand binding domain (LBD), and this conformational change propagates through conserved mechanical linkers to the transmembrane domain (TMD), functioning as a molecular lever that dilates the pore via outward displacement of transmembrane helices. This gating mechanism was further corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiology. These insights provide an atomic resolution view of IR mediated host detection in mosquitoes and establish a foundation for the rational design of next generation mosquito control strategies targeting host-seeking behavior.

articles.title: Beyond BMI: The Role of Abdominal Obesity in Hypertension Risk Among Adults Aged 45 Years and Older in India.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: Hypertension is highly prevalent among adults aged 45 years and older in India, yet limited evidence exists on the combined associations of waist circumference (WC) and body mass index (BMI) with hypertension. This study examined their independent and joint associations with hypertension using Wave 1 (2017-18) of the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) among 59,658 adults aged 45 years and older. Hypertension was defined as measured blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations across combined WC-BMI categories. Overall hypertension prevalence was 31.3%. Individuals with normal BMI but large WC had higher odds of hypertension (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.37; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.19-1.58). Obese individuals with large WC had the highest odds (AOR = 1.77; 95% CI: 1.45-2.17). Both central and general obesity were independently associated with hypertension. Routine WC assessment alongside BMI may improve identification of high-risk individuals in India's middle-aged and older population.

articles.title: Serum cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) NrCAM and P-Cadherin as novel biomarkers in lupus nephritis.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify novel serum biomarkers for lupus nephritis (LN) and evaluate their potential for improving diagnosis, monitoring disease activity, and understanding LN pathogenesis.MethodsA cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) antibody microarray was utilized to identify potential biomarkers of LN using serum samples from LN, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and healthy controls (HC). Differential expression analysis and LASSO regression identified CAM biomarkers in a discovery cohort, followed by ELISA validation in an independent, discovery cohort. Biomarker correlations with clinicopathological parameters were assessed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to examine the potential diagnostic utility.ResultsOf the 17 CAMs analyzed, serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin emerged as the most promising new biomarkers, significantly discriminating LN from HC. Serum NrCAM was found to differentiate between LN and HC (p < 0.0001) as well as active LN (LNA) from inactive LN (LNI) (p < 0.01) in the discovery cohort. Serum P-Cadherin, however, differentiated LN from both HC (p < 0.0001) and CKD (p < 0.001) and distinguished LNA from LNI (p < 0.01). In a larger validation cohort, ROC analyses demonstrated strong diagnostic potential for both biomarkers, with AUC values of 0.92 and 0.82 for serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin, respectively. Significant correlations with SLEDAI, rSLEDAI, and histological indices further underscored their potential relevance to LN severity and activity. Interestingly, serum NrCAM and P-Cadherin are complementary in reflecting renal pathology changes including endocapillary hypercellularity, cellular crescents, glomerulosclerosis, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis.ConclusionSerum NrCAM and P-Cadherin show promise as non-invasive biomarkers for LN, offering potential utility in diagnosis and disease monitoring. Their ability to distinguish between disease states and correlate with clinical parameters highlights their potential to improve patient stratification and guide personalized treatment approaches in LN.

articles.title: The role of nurses in shared decision-making in primary care: Qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the primary care nursing professionals (PCN) perception of their role in Shared Decision Making (SDM) to improve the adherence in patients with chronic pathology and a new cardiovascular and/or diabetes with new pharmacological prescription.

METHODS: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted with the participation of 19 primary care nurses from two primary care centres in the Southern Metropolitan health region of Barcelona during 2022. The participating primary care nurses had to be part of the intervention group of the IMA-cRCT clinical trial. Narrative data were collected through focus groups using a semistructured guide and carried out in two phases. Phase I took place after a training on SDM but before the implementation of an SDM intervention aimed at improving primary medication adherence, during which 3 focus groups were conducted. Phase II was carried out 7 months after the intervention implementation with 2 additional focus groups. For the thematic content analysis, all focus groups were transcribed, analysed individually, and triangulated. Nvivo 15 software was used to support the analysis. All participants signed informed consent forms, and the interviews were pseudo-anonymised.

RESULTS: Seven themes were identified that illustrated the PCN perspective when implementing SDM in the approach to the chronic patient with new pharmacological prescriptions: Model of care; Patient characteristics; PCN attitude; Interdisciplinary coordination; Prior training; Resources and opportunities for improvement. No relevant differences were identified in the pre-post discourses of the participants.

CONCLUSIONS: The integration of SDM in the role of PCN is key in accompanying the health care of chronic patients. This study shows that they have not yet incorporated it into their routine. DBT requires university and continuing education, interdisciplinary coordination and a change of paradigm at all levels.

articles.title: Zfp697/ZNF697 is an RNA-binding protein that modulates TGF-β1 signaling and hepatic inflammation in liver disease.
articles.abstract: Liver diseases driven by metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and fibrosis such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and acute liver injury represent a growing global health burden. The zinc finger protein Zfp697 (ZNF697 in humans) is a newly identified regulator of inflammation and regeneration in skeletal muscle. Here, we characterize the role of liver Zfp697 and show that its expression is increased in multiple animal models of liver disease. Indeed, Zfp697/ZNF697 transcript levels show a strong positive correlation with several markers of liver inflammation and fibrosis. In line with that, in human and mouse hepatocytes TGF-β1 increases Zfp697 expression, which in turn regulates genes involved in TGF-β1 signaling, chemokine secretion, and immune cell recruitment. In mice, hepatocyte-specific Zfp697 deletion improves glucose tolerance and is associated with the absence of MASH-induced lean mass loss but does not confer uniform hepatoprotection. Biochemical purification of Zfp697 protein interactors and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) analyses reveal that Zfp697 interacts with other RNA-binding proteins and associates with over 1,000 RNAs in mouse liver. Zfp697-associated RNAs include several transcript types, with a large representation of mRNAs which group in pathways related to transcriptional regulation, PI3K/AKT signaling, and cell differentiation. These findings identify Zfp697 as a novel RNA-interacting protein and modulator of TGF-β signaling in the liver and provide a basis for further investigation of its role in liver disease.

articles.title: The Causal Role of Adiponectin in Type 2 Diabetes across Ages and Sexes - An Observational and Mendelian Randomization Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The obesity pandemic has increased the prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) across all ages and sexes. Adiponectin, an insulin-sensitizing hormone, shows protective effects against T2D in observational studies. However, it is unclear whether low adiponectin levels cause T2D, as this association might be driven by confounding factors. We aimed to investigate if the association of adiponectin with T2D is causal.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We assessed causality with Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) using Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) from multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Multivariable MR (MVMR) and Two-Step network MR evaluated whether the effect of adiponectin on T2D was influenced by adiposity-related phenotypes. Using the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), we examined mediation and longitudinal associations between adiponectin, T2D-related traits, and adiposity in youth.

RESULTS: Initial inverse variance-weighted MR estimates suggested protective effects. However, the identified causal association did not persist after removing SNPs linked to adiposity-related traits or adjusting for these traits in MVMR. Two-Step network MR showed that adiponectin could mediate the relationship between visceral fat and T2D in women. ALSPAC results suggest that adiponectin may mediate the relationship between adiposity and fasting glucose levels in youth.

CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, our MR results did not show a causal association between adiponectin levels and T2D. Instead, adiponectin potentially plays a sex-specific mediating role in the relationship between visceral fat and T2D in women.

articles.title: Association between dental pulp necroptosis-related signaling and elodont incisor growth retardation in hyperglycemic rats.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although type 1 diabetes (T1D) induces systemic allostatic load, whether sustained hyperglycemia is accompanied by necroptosis-related signaling within the dental pulp (DP) niche and its impact on the developmental kinetics of continuously growing elodont incisors remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether sustained hyperglycemia was accompanied by enhanced RIPK3-MLKL necroptosis-related signaling within the DP niche and whether these molecular alterations coincided with attenuation of elodont incisor growth.

METHODS: T1D was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats using streptozotocin (65 mg/kg). Systemic metabolic profiles, necroptotic markers in serum/dental tissues (immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and Western blotting), and mandibular incisor growth (a standardized notch-creation method for 49 days) were evaluated. Group differences were assessed primarily using two-sided Welch's t-tests, with exact Mann-Whitney U tests for sensitivity analyses, while discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC-AUC) and precision-recall (PR curve-based AP) analyses.

RESULTS: Hyperglycemic rats exhibited impaired weight gain, systemic inflammatory induction (elevated NLR/MLR), and elevated hepatic stress markers. Molecular profiling demonstrated increased oxidative damage (4-HNE) and necroptosis-related molecular alterations in dental tissues and DP-derived cells. Incisor growth rates differed significantly at the Phase-Transition (0.532 vs. 0.400 mm/day; Welch's p = 0.024), reaching definitive retardation in Phase-2 (0.594 vs. 0.408 mm/day; p < 0.001). Discriminatory performance improved from the Phase-Transition (ROC-AUC = 0.693; AP = 0.784) to Phase-2 (ROC-AUC = 1.000; AP = 1.000). Glycemic reversion was accompanied by normalization of necroptosis-related markers and incisor growth kinetics.

CONCLUSION: Hyperglycemia-induced incisor growth retardation is associated with increased oxidative stress, altered PGAM5 expression, and enhanced RIPK3-MLKL necroptosis-related signaling in dental tissues and DP-derived cells. Translationally, longitudinal evaluation of elodont incisor growth kinetics could serve as a minimally invasive phenotypic indicator of metabolic dysregulation in preclinical diabetic models and support refinement under the 3Rs principle.

articles.title: Mitophagy and ER-phagy in doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity: mechanisms, crosstalk, and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a key chemotherapeutic agent for hematologic malignancies and many solid tumors, but its clinical use is limited by doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC). DIC may present as subclinical myocardial injury, arrhythmias, left ventricular dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, or heart failure. DOX can disrupt organelle function through topoisomerase IIβ (Top2β)-mediated DNA damage and transcriptional stress, oxidative stress, disrupted iron homeostasis, and calcium imbalance. Mitochondrial and endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum (ER/SR) injury are therefore central pathological features of DIC.

AIM OF REVIEW: This review summarizes current evidence on mitophagy and ER-phagy in DIC, with emphasis on discrepancies in reported findings across different experimental settings, potential crosstalk mechanisms, and the translational limitations of targeting these pathways for cardioprotection.

KEY SCIENTIFIC CONCEPTS: Current studies suggest that mitophagy in DIC follows a checkpoint-dependent pattern. Depending on DOX dose, exposure duration, and lysosomal degradative capacity, mitophagy may remove damaged mitochondria, but it may also worsen mitochondrial injury when initiation is insufficient, activation is excessive, or flux is stalled. In contrast, direct evidence for ER-phagy in DIC remains limited. This evidence is mainly derived from CCPG1-mediated protective ER-phagy in chronic fractionated DOX models and FAM134B-associated ER-phagy-related injury signals in acute high-dose injury models. Thus, the functional divergence of ER-phagy in DIC requires confirmation in additional experimental models with rigorous autophagic flux assessment. Mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAMs) may coordinate mitophagy and ER-phagy by regulating calcium transfer, autophagosome formation, and receptor localization. Overall, current evidence does not support indiscriminate activation or inhibition of mitophagy and ER-phagy. Instead, future interventions may need to preserve flux-complete organelle clearance while avoiding excessive or stalled autophagic signaling. In addition, this framework may help generate research hypotheses that integrate cardioprotection with preservation of antitumor efficacy. However, most evidence comes from cell and animal studies, and further validation in human myocardial tissue and confirmation of cardiac target engagement are still needed.

articles.title: Identifying overlooked factors associated with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis: an ecological study across 201 countries and regions, 1990-2021.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is a critical global health challenge. Whether environmental, nutritional, and socioeconomic factors are associated with MDR-TB remains insufficiently investigated.

METHODS: We analyzed outcome and exposure data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study and four additional databases covering 201 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Sex ratio, diabetes prevalence, and HIV/AIDS burden were regressed out of each outcome before analysis. Every candidate exposure was then both regressed against the confounder-adjusted outcome and correlated with it. Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted P values, together with correlation strength, determined which factors were retained for display. Effects are expressed as the absolute change per interquartile range (IQR) increase in exposure. Drug-susceptible tuberculosis served as a control outcome.

RESULTS: Per IQR of exposure, unsafe sanitation was associated with 13.9 more prevalent cases per 100,000 (95% CI 13.0-14.7) and 2.87 more deaths per 100,000 (2.72-3.03); unsafe water source with 11.2 (10.5-12.0) and 2.64 (2.49-2.78); and polluting fuels for cooking with 10.7 (9.8-11.6) and 2.74 (2.58-2.89). After further adjustment for GDP per capita and health expenditure, six associations remained significant, including unsafe sanitation, unsafe water source, absence of handwashing facilities and underweight (e.g., unsafe sanitation 2.8 per 100,000 per IQR, P < 0.001). Most of these associations were stronger for drug-susceptible disease than for MDR-TB, with the exception of diet low in fruits.

CONCLUSIONS: Unsafe sanitation, unsafe water source, and polluting fuels for cooking are the population-level factors most strongly associated with MDR-TB burden. These associations are largely shared with drug-susceptible tuberculosis, supporting their integration into tuberculosis control efforts as a whole.

articles.title: Neuroimaging Insights into the Effects of Non-Nutritive Sweeteners on Appetite Regulation: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) are increasingly used as low- or zero-calorie alternatives to sugar while maintaining sweetness. However, uncoupling sweet taste from caloric content may alter appetite regulation and promote food-seeking behavior, although the underlying neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. To address this, we conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched up to June 2025 using terms related to NNS, neuroimaging and appetite regulation. Of 137 screened records, 21 neuroimaging reports met predefined PICO-based eligibility criteria. Eligible reports included healthy adults across weight categories and examined artificial or naturally occurring NNS (e.g., sucralose, erythritol) compared with nutritive sweeteners (NS; e.g., sucrose) or non-sweet controls (e.g., water). Outcomes included appetite-related brain responses measured using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) or positron emission tomography (PET), as well as associations with gut hormones, glucose metabolism, and eating behavior. NNS and NS both engaged gustatory and reward-related brain regions, with some reports showing reduced activity and lower pleasantness ratings for NNS. Hypothalamic activity and functional connectivity were also modulated by NNS intake, with no observed associations between brain responses and gut hormones or glucose metabolism in the available reports. Overall, the evidence remains limited and varies by NNS type, dose, delivery method, habitual intake, sex, weight status, and metabolic state. Future studies should investigate acute and long-term NNS consumption under real-world conditions with greater ethnic and demographic diversity, accounting for individual variability to better inform dietary guidelines.

articles.title: Clarifying consensus and pediatric applicability in oncology AI governance.
An m7G tRNA-derived fragment mediated thermogenic activation of brown adipose tissue through post-transcriptional repression of Uqcr10.
articles.abstract: Obesity, diabetes, and related metabolic disorders have become global epidemics driven mainly by an imbalance between energy intake and energy expenditure. Brown adipose tissue (BAT), the principal site of non-shivering thermogenesis, can be activated to mitigate obesity and its metabolic sequelae. RNA modification is as important regulators of obesity. The N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification broadly influences RNA stability, enhances translational efficiency, and helps determine cell fate. However, the specific mechanisms by which m7G regulates adipose thermogenesis remain unclear. Using untargeted metabolomics, we found that cold exposure activates thermogenic metabolism in BAT and that 7-Methylguanosine is elevated in thermogenically activated BAT. METTL1-mediated m7G modification correlates positively with adipose thermogenic activation. Loss of METTL1 reduces m7G levels and impairs adipocyte thermogenic capacity. At the same time, METTL1 deficiency alters tRNA cleavage patterns and generates regulatory tRNA-derived fragments that modulate gene expression. Overexpression of tRF-Lys-CTT, which derives from an m7G-modified tRNA, inhibits brown adipocyte differentiation and thermogenic activation; conversely, inhibiting tRF-Lys-CTT produces the opposite effects. Mechanistically, tRF-Lys-CTT associates with AGO2 to form a functional RISC complex that binds the 3'UTR of Uqcr10 mRNA and directly represses Uqcr10 post-transcriptionally. Under basal conditions, elevated tRF-Lys-CTT may constrain mitochondrial function by repressing Uqcr10 expression; upon cold stimulation, downregulation of tRF-Lys-CTT relieves this repression and promotes respiratory chain supercomplex assembly and UCP1-mediated thermogenesis. In summary, our study indicates that tRF-Lys-CTT functions as a post-transcriptional regulator of metabolism that suppresses thermogenesis, and provides new insights into the regulatory relationship among the METTL1/m7G/tRF axis and thermogenic control.

articles.title: The malonyl-CoA synthetase ACSF3 is required for metabolic editing downstream of biotin carboxylation.
articles.abstract: Acsf3, a mitochondrial malonyl-CoA synthetase, is mutated in the human inborn error Combined Malonic and Methylmalonic Aciduria. To clarify its role in mammalian metabolism, we generated Acsf3 knockout mice. We show that the loss of Acsf3 results in high concentrations of malonate and methylmalonate and exhibit expected defects in mitochondrial metabolism, but the KO mice are largely healthy similar to the human inborn error. Acsf3 KO mice exhibit redundancy in malonyl-CoA synthetase activity suggesting a genetic modifier of disease severity. Malonate and methylmalonate are metabolic poisons generated as a by-product of biotin dependent carboxylation that require metabolic editing. Indeed, the liver-specific loss of the biotin ligase, Holocarboxylase Synthetase (hlcs), inhibits all biotin dependent carboxylation and results in broad changes in liver mRNA, protein, posttranslational and metabolic regulation. Loss of Hlcs suppresses the metabolic deficits in Acsf3KO liver due to the inhibition of malonate and methylmalonate generation. Mice with a double knockout of Acsf3 and Hlcs maintained mitochondrial lipoylation demonstrating the highly redundant generation of mitochondrial malonyl-CoA. These data define the role of Acsf3 in metabolic editing of malonate and methylmalonate to maintain mitochondrial metabolism in the face of endogenously produced anti-metabolites.

articles.title: Second-line dupilumab after anti-IL5/Rα failure: remission rates and clinical outcomes in severe asthma.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Switching biologic therapies occurs in 10-25% of severe asthma patients, yet remission rates after first-line biologic failure remain poorly characterised.

OBJECTIVE: To assess clinical remission after switching from anti-IL5/Rα to anti-IL4/13 therapy following treatment failure.

METHODS: This observational cohort study included all Danish adults with severe asthma switching to second-line anti-IL4/13 after failing to achieve remission on anti-IL5/Rα. Remission at 12 months was assessed by four domains: no exacerbations, no maintenance oral corticosteroid use (mOCS), ACQ-6 ≤1.5, and FEV1 >80% predicted (FEV1%pred).

RESULTS: A total of 173 patients were included (median age 55; 45% female), with 79% switching due to lack of treatment effect. The proportion of patients meeting each remission domain increased progressively from pre-biologic baseline to switching and follow-up. At 12 months, 66%, 75%, 54%, and 39% met the exacerbation, mOCS, ACQ-6, and FEV1%pred criteria, respectively; 17% achieved full four-domain remission. Impaired lung function was the most persistent unmet criterion among non-remitters. Pre-biologic and pre-switch biomarkers did not predict remission, whereas atopic dermatitis (33% vs. 16%, p=0.05) and nasal polyps (75% vs. 49%, p=0.02) were associated with remission, and COPD with non-remission (4% vs. 34%, p=0.003).

CONCLUSION: In severe asthma patients not achieving remission on first-line anti-IL5/Rα, nearly one in five achieved remission after switching to anti-IL4/13, suggesting that interclass switching is an effective strategy for patients with inadequate response. Impaired lung function and absence of broad T2 comorbidity predict a lower likelihood of remission.

articles.title: Genetic hepatocellular cholestasis: an update.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract: Cholestasis, defined as a reduction of bile flow, may be secondary to obstruction of bile ducts or absence of production of bile by hepatocytes. Genetic hepatocellular cholestasis is a heterogenous group of diseases, including bile acid synthesis defects (BASD) and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC). It affects a gene involved in either bile acid synthesis (BASD) or bile secretion by hepatocytes (PFIC). Recent advances in molecular biology and sequencing techniques have enabled the identification of many novel cholestatic disorders beyond the three historical PFIC. These diseases, of variable severity, are responsible for chronic cholestasis, intractable pruritus and often progress toward early liver cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer. Novel therapeutics such as ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors have been developed for the treatment of pruritus. Many patients with genetic hepatocellular cholestasis will require liver transplantation during childhood because of intractable pruritus or worsening of liver function. Specific subsets of BASD manifesting as chronic cholestasis are treatable with primary bile acid therapy with excellent native liver survival in the long-term. In this publication, we will review the clinical, biochemical and molecular features of genetic hepatocellular cholestasis, as well as their management.

articles.title: High-Frequency Chest Wall Oscillation in Acute Respiratory Failure With Bronchial Hypersecretion: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway secretion retention is common in patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF), particularly in those requiring noninvasive respiratory support (NIRS). High-frequency chest wall oscillation (HFCWO) may improve airway clearance but critical care evidence remains limited.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Does adding HFCWO to standard care improve clinical outcomes in patients with bronchial hypersecretion and ARF requiring NIRS?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center randomized controlled trial in a RICU. Patients with ARF requiring NIRS, including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and/or noninvasive ventilation (NIV), bronchial hypersecretion, and ineffective cough (peak cough expiratory flow <270 L/min) were randomized 1:1 to HFCWO plus standard care or standard care alone. The primary endpoint was therapeutic bronchoscopy. Secondary endpoints included hospital length of stay (LOS), RICU-LOS, NIRS duration, endotracheal intubation and mortality. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted and adjusted models accounting for age, sex, and main cause of hospitalization.

RESULTS: Eighty-eight patients were enrolled (44 HFCWO, 44 control), with comparable baseline characteristics. Bronchoscopy was required in 6 patients (13.6%) versus 14 (31.8%) (unadjusted p=0.042); after adjustment the association did not retain statistical significance (adjusted OR 0.336, 95% CI 0.111-1.021; p=0.055). Secondary outcomes, analyzed without correction for multiple testing, are exploratory. Hospital stay (12 [10-15.5] vs 16.5 [13-21] days) and RICU stay (8 [7-10.5] vs 12 [9-17] days) were shorter, with adjusted reductions of 4.5 and 3.6 days. HFNC duration was shorter (6 [4-8] vs 9.5 [6-11.5] days) and remained significant after adjustment, whereas the reduction in NIV duration did not (adjusted p=0.166). No patient required intubation and mortality did not differ.

INTERPRETATION: In this exploratory trial, HFCWO did not significantly reduce the need for therapeutic bronchoscopy after adjustment. Associated reductions in LOS and HFNC duration are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered multicenter trials.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05751707; Tuscany Ethics Committee (Protocol: 21987-10/17/2022).

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine inhibits gene and protein expression of MUC5AC in COPD-relevant human models: evidence from a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Chronic mucus hypersecretion is highly prevalent in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and is associated with worse outcomes. MUC5AC is a key inducible gel-forming mucin driving pathological mucus overproduction. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is widely used as a mucolytic and exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Its quantitative impact on MUC5AC regulation has not been formally synthesized. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis (OSF registration ID: 2vym4) of original studies evaluating the effect of NAC on MUC5AC gene and protein expression in human respiratory cell models of mucus hypersecretion. Standardized mean differences with 95% CIs were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Heterogeneity, publication bias, sensitivity analyses, and random-effects meta-regression on NAC dose were conducted. Fifteen articles were included. NAC significantly reduced MUC5AC mRNA (standardized mean difference -1.30, 95% CI: -1.61 to -0.98; I2=37.07%), without significant dose-response. NAC produced very large reductions in extracellular (-2.70, 95% CI: -3.29 to -2.11; I2=48.89%) and intracellular (-2.38, 95% CI: -3.27 to -1.48; I2=67.35%) MUC5AC protein, with significant dose-response relationships for both. After sensitivity analyses, the pooled protein effect remained very large (-2.00, 95% CI: -2.38 to -1.62; I2=25.63%). Funnel plots and Egger's tests suggested publication bias, which diminished after exclusion of influential comparisons. NAC robustly inhibits MUC5AC gene and protein expression in human pre-clinical models of mucus hypersecretion, supporting a strong mucoregulatory action that complements mucolytic and antioxidant effects. These data reinforce the rationale for NAC use in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients with a hypersecretory phenotype.

articles.title: Association between organophosphate esters and incident type 2 diabetes risk: modification by genetic risk and lifestyle.
articles.abstract: People are widely exposed to organophosphate esters (OPEs) as flame retardants and plasticizers. OPEs may affect type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk, but prospective evidence is limited and inconsistent, and the modifying effects of genetic and lifestyle factors remain unclear. The present nested case-control study within the Dongfeng-Tongji cohort of retired adults (median age: 62 years; mean follow-up: 4.6 years) included 981 pairs of incident T2D cases and controls matched by age and sex. We measured 10 plasma OPEs in baseline blood samples and used conditional logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, quantile g-computation, and Bayesian kernel machine regression to examine their association with T2D risk. We examined effect modification by lifestyle and polygenic risk score. Each twofold increase in plasma triphenyl phosphate (TPHP) was associated with 6% higher odds of T2D (odds ratio, OR=1.06; 95% confidence interval, CI: 1.01-1.11). The odds were 49% higher in the highest tertile versus the lowest (OR = 1.49, 95% CI: 1.04-2.14). Tri-isobutyl phosphate and tri-n-butyl phosphate (TiBP+TnBP) in the highest tertile showed an inverse association versus the lowest (OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.58-0.99). Detectable tri(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) was associated with 75% higher odds of T2D versus undetectable levels (OR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.30-2.36). The overall mixture effect was not significant, with TPHP positive and TiBP+TnBP negative as main contributors. Interaction analysis using relative excess risk (RERI showed additive synergy for high TPHP combined with an unhealthy lifestyle (RERI = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.09-1.52), low TiBP+TnBP combined with an unhealthy lifestyle (RERI = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.02-1.32), and low TiBP + TnBP combined with high genetic risk (RERI = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.03-1.74). The highest odds of T2D were for high PRS, unhealthy lifestyle, and high TPHP (OR=7.16, 95%CI: 4.06-12.62) or low TiBP+TnBP (OR=6.63, 95%CI: 3.83-11.47). Healthy lifestyle may offset OPEs and genetic effects.

articles.title: Early post-sepsis innate behavioral changes in aged mice occur independently of detectable neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis disproportionately causes long-term cognitive and functional impairments in elderly survivors, including deficits in activities of daily living and functional independence. The neurobiological mechanisms driving this vulnerability in the aged brain remain poorly understood. We tested whether the aged brain possesses a unique vulnerability to sepsis-induced impairment in the early post-acute recovery period.

METHODS: Polymicrobial sepsis was induced in young (3-months) and aged (18-months) mice via cecal slurry injection, with dosing adjusted for comparable acute illness severity. Behavioral assessments (learning, memory, locomotion, innate behaviors) were performed through Day 7 post-infection. On Day 8, brains were analyzed for inflammatory cytokines, glial activation, neuronal protein expression, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability.

RESULTS: Aged septic mice exhibited alterations in nest building and sociability, whereas young mice with comparable illness severity remained behaviorally resilient. The behavioral changes in aged mice occurred in the absence of broad systemic or neuroinflammation. Conversely, young septic mice maintained normal behavior despite significantly elevated systemic and neuroinflammation. Aged mice displayed signs of glial activation, neuronal protein modulation, and BBB permeability compared to young mice, but sepsis did not significantly exacerbate these markers in either group.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate an age-dependent divergence in neurologic recovery after sepsis: while young mice exhibit behavioral resilience despite systemic and neuroinflammation, aged mice display alterations in innate behavior that are present even after the apparent resolution of acute illness. This suggests that the changes in innate behavior in the aged mice are not driven solely by sepsis-induced inflammation, but rather by a cumulative burden of age-related vulnerabilities, including microglial priming, astrocytic activation, and increased BBB permeability, that render aged brains unable to compensate for a severe acute physiological challenge.

articles.title: Hyperthermia exacerbates methamphetamine cardiotoxicity by promoting neutrophil-dominant inflammation and Map3k6-associated p38/ERK signaling.
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine (METH) abuse is frequently accompanied by life-threatening hyperthermia, yet the contribution of hyperthermia to METH-induced cardiac injury remains poorly defined. Here, we tested whether elevated ambient temperature amplifies METH cardiotoxicity by aggravating hyperthermia. C57BL/6 mice were exposed to different ambient temperatures (18 °C, 22 °C, or 28 °C) and treated with METH. METH rapidly increased core body temperature, whereas exposure at 28 °C further intensified hyperthermia and caused 20% mortality. In surviving mice, METH at 28 °C significantly reduced cardiac function-including heart rate, cardiac output, stroke volume, ejection fraction and fractional shortening, and induced myocardial eosinophilic degeneration, focal myofiber disruption, cardiomyocyte lysis and inflammatory cell infiltration. Cardiac transcriptomics revealed a distinct inflammatory program enriched for cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, chemokine signaling, leukocyte chemotaxis and neutrophil migration. RT-qPCR confirmed increased cardiac expression of CCL2, CXCL1, ITGAM, ICAM-1 and MMP9, and inflammatory cytokines were also elevated. Immune-infiltration analysis identified prominent neutrophil accumulation, and gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) indicated activation of oxidative stress-related pathways. Among stress-related kinases, mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 6 (Map3k6, also known as ASK2) was upregulated and positively correlated with neutrophil-dominant infiltration and inflammatory markers. METH at 28 °C also increased p38 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) phosphorylation. These findings identify elevated ambient temperature as a critical amplifier of METH-induced cardiac injury and implicate Map3k6-associated p38/ERK activation in hyperthermia-associated cardiac inflammation and functional impairment. Collectively, our results indicate that hyperthermia exacerbates METH cardiotoxicity, potentially involving Map3k6-associated p38/ERK signaling and neutrophil-dominant immune infiltration, providing new mechanistic insights into temperature-associated cardiac vulnerability following METH abuse.

articles.title: High Normal dietary casein attenuates bisphenol A-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats: Preservation of renal integrity, glucose homeostasis, and immune surveillance via modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) causes multiorgan toxicity via oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and the effect of nutritionally relevant elevation of casein intake is unknown. To evaluate whether a nutritionally relevant elevation of dietary casein (18% vs. 14%) attenuates BPA-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats, male Wistar rats were divided into four groups (n = 8/group) and treated for 35 days: control (14% casein), casein 18% alone, BPA (50 mg/kg/day +14% casein), and BPA + 18% casein. We measured oxidative and inflammatory markers, renal function, metabolic parameters, hematological parameters, histopathology and immunohistochemistry in kidney, spleen, and pancreas. BPA significantly increased malondialdehyde, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, creatinine, kidney injury molecule-1, insulin resistance, white blood cells, neutrophils, and monocytes, and decreased reduced glutathione, glutathione S-transferase, superoxide dismutase, catalase, interleukin-4, serum soluble CD4 and CD8 protein levels, hemoglobin, red blood cells, platelets, and lymphocytes. BPA also caused renal tubular necrosis, splenic degeneration, pancreatic fibrosis, and upregulated caspase-3 and inducible nitric oxide synthase. Co-administration of 18% casein partially attenuated these effects, reducing malondialdehyde by 35-40%, creatinine by 40%, and insulin resistance by 53%, and restoring antioxidant enzymes and glucose tolerance. However, several parameters remained significantly different from controls. Nutritionally relevant elevation of casein (18%) provides significant partial protection against BPA-induced toxicity, supporting dietary protein modulation as a supportive strategy.

articles.title: Surveillance of patients at risk of liver cancer: Expert Opinions - authors' reply.
Role of 12/15-lipoxygenase and its metabolites in cardiovascular diseases.
articles.abstract: 12/15-Lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX), a key oxidoreductase enzyme, catalyzes the peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) including omega-6 and omega-3 fatty acids. This enzyme is expressed in multiple cell types such as macrophages, endothelial cells, and epithelial cells, where it participates in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism through the hydroperoxidation pathway. The catalytic activity of 12/15-LOX generates bioactive lipid mediators, notably 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE), which serve as signaling molecules in physiological and pathological processes. Emerging evidence establishes 12/15-LOX as a critical mediator in oxidative stress and inflammatory cascades. Its pathophysiological involvement has been mechanistically linked to the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disorders, particularly through promoting atherosclerotic plaque formation, vascular endothelial dysfunction, and myocardial ischemic injury. Clinical epidemiological studies further demonstrate significant associations between 12/15-LOX activity and disease progression in atherosclerosis, essential hypertension, and acute myocardial infarction. In this review, we systematically examine the biosynthetic origin of 12/15-LOX, delineate its metabolic pathways and its pleiotropic functions in modulating inflammatory responses, redox homeostasis, and programmed cell death cascades. Furthermore, we critically evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting 12/15-LOX enzymatic activity or its downstream effectors, with particular emphasis on translational opportunities for cardiovascular disease management. This synthesis aims to advance the development of precision therapies targeting the 12/15-LOX pathway in cardiometabolic disorders.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Pharmaceutical Care in Reducing the Incidence of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-related Pneumonitis in Patients with NSCLC: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) remains a potentially life-threatening adverse event that may be mitigated through structured pharmaceutical care interventions.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the effectiveness of pharmacy services in reducing the occurrence of CIP among patients with NSCLC receiving ICIs.

METHODS: Patients who underwent immunotherapy at our hospital between November, 2023 to September, 2024 were selected and randomized into the control and intervention groups (105 patients each). Intervention group received 6 months of pharmacy services, and CIP occurrence, clinical efficacy, medication adherence, and quality of life at 3, 6, and 9 months were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a significantly lower CIP incidence and immunotherapy suspension rate due to CIP (2.9% vs. 9.5%, P = 0.043), as well as significantly improved medication adherence at all time points (P < 0.05). The intervention group also had lower CIP severity and longer onset time (8.6 months vs. 6.2 months), along with numerically higher ORR (40.6% vs. 30.3%) and DCR (81.2% vs. 71.7%), and a favorable trend in emotional function scores; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacy care can reduce the incidence and severity, and increase the onset time of CIP, thus enhancing drug safety.

articles.title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality.

METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality.

RESULTS: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

articles.title: THE CLINICAL PROFILE OF RUPTURE: A 19-YEAR CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSMS.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds.

METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. Median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < .001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = .002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio [OR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.84-2.61) and female sex (OR, 4.72; 95% CI, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds.

CONCLUSIONS: Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies.

METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in PROSPERO, was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER.

RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (OR, 2.58; 95% CI, 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%).

CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow-up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow-up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate to serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: The type of portal vein reconstruction does not affect the outcomes of pancreatic surgery or the patency of the portal vein.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety of the four types of portal vein reconstruction (PVR) as defined by the International Study Group of Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) and to analyse long-term survival outcomes in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).

METHODS: A prospectively collected pancreatic surgery registry that was supplemented retrospectively was used. Patients who underwent open pancreatic resection with PVR between 2005 and 2024 were included. Clinicopathological characteristics, outcomes, and computed tomography images were analysed and tested in multivariate and survival analyses. For survival analyses, patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy without PVR served as controls.

RESULTS: Pancreatectomies with PVR (n=386) comprised 63 tangential resections with venorrhaphy (ISGPS type I), 25 patch reconstructions (type II), 147 end-to-end anastomoses (type III), and 151 resections with graft interposition (type IV). Most type IV reconstructions (98.7%) used spiral grafts, predominantly made from the great saphenous vein (GSV). PVR thrombosis rate was 3.1% at 30 days and 5.7% at 90 days following surgery. There were no significant differences between PVR types I-IV in the incidence of PVR thromboses, complications, or mortality. Median survival for PDAC patients with PVR was 22.8 months, with no survival differences between types I-IV, compared with 31.7 months in patients without PVR, p=.003.

CONCLUSIONS: In this setting, where PVR was performed using GSV spiral grafts for interposition, the type of PVR did not associate with pancreatic surgery outcomes or portal vein patency. The rate of PVR thrombosis was low, and other complication rates and long-term survival outcomes were comparable with international standards.

articles.title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality After Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and amputation-free survival (AFS). Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%) (Table 2). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point (Figure 1). All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs 71 years; P = .047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs 47.1%; P = .064) (Table 3).

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure.
