articles.title: Response to the letter to the editor concerning "Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for 90-day clinically significant medication-related harm in adults initiating oral anticancer therapy: A multicenter prospective cohort study".
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners

articles.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals.
articles.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual's deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span-wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

articles.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2CV), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

articles.title: Quinolinic acid contributes to maladaptive kidney injury and acute kidney injury-to-chronic kidney disease transition.
articles.abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major clinical problem with unclear underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in tryptophan metabolism, particularly in the production of downstream metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QA), play a role in renal pathophysiology. QA, an intermediate in de novo nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis, is metabolized by quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We investigated whether QA contributes to kidney injury using models of folic acid-induced AKI-to-CKD transition and cisplatin-induced AKI, genetic and exogenous approaches to alter QA, and clinical observations. Untargeted kidney metabolomics identified QA as one of the most elevated metabolites after folic acid injury. After folic acid injury, Qprt haploinsufficiency exacerbated kidney injury and fibrosis-related gene expression; aged Qprt-haploinsufficient mice exhibited increased fibrosis-associated gene expression without overt renal dysfunction. Exogenous QA administration increased serum creatinine in uninjured mice and worsened renal dysfunction and fibrosis-related gene expression in the folic acid AKI-to-CKD model. Conversely, mice deficient in either 3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) or kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO), which reduce flux toward QA, showed improved renal outcomes after folic acid injury and cisplatin-induced AKI. Multimodal spatial metabolomics analysis of kidney biopsies from patients with AKI revealed QA accumulation in regions of inflammatory infiltration. Last, children with CKD exhibited higher urinary QA compared with healthy individuals. These findings underscore QA as a potential mediator of kidney injury and a therapeutic target for preventing the progression from AKI to CKD.

articles.title: Human cytomegalovirus exploits host chromatin remodeler MORC2 to promote the DNA damage response on viral genomes.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) harbors a 230-kb double-stranded DNA genome whose replication induces extensive DNA damage during lytic infection. Because HCMV lacks canonical DNA repair machinery, it relies on host DNA damage response (DDR) pathways. However, the mechanisms that govern the preferential recruitment and function of host DDR proteins on viral genomes remain poorly understood. Here, we show that HCMV co-opts the host chromatin remodeler MORC Family CW-type zinc finger 2 (MORC2) to promote DDR activation on viral genomes. HCMV infection induces MORC2 expression, which is important for efficient viral DNA replication and progeny virus production. We found that MORC2 redistributes to viral replication compartments (vRCs) in HCMV-infected cells and enhances viral chromatin accessibility in an ATPase-dependent manner, thereby facilitating γH2AX accumulation and the recruitment of DNA repair factors to vRCs. Furthermore, we found that HCMV UL112-113-mediated phase separation facilitates MORC2 recruitment to vRCs, promoting efficient DDR signaling on viral genomes. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic framework for how DNA viruses alleviate replication stress by hijacking host chromatin remodelers.

articles.title: Intranasal HSV‑1 infection drives region‑specific interferon‑dominant microglial remodeling.
articles.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is a neurotropic pathogen capable of invading the central nervous system (CNS) and is associated with chronic neuroinflammation, cognitive impairment, and neurodegenerative disease. While microglia orchestrate the initial immune response to HSV‑1, the molecular mechanisms that regulate their sustained neuroinflammatory activity in vivo remain poorly understood. To define the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms that shape microglial responses during acute HSV-1 infection in vivo, we have, for the first time, integrated single‑nucleus RNA sequencing, chromatin accessibility profiling, and spatial proteomics and transcriptomics in an intranasal HSV‑1 infection model. Single-cell multiome analysis of CD11b⁺ nuclei identified transcriptionally and epigenetically distinct microglial and macrophage populations. HSV-1 infection redistributed monocyte-lineage states, with a marked overrepresentation of interferon (IFN)‑responsive microglia and macrophage-associated populations characterized by amplification of Stat1/2, Irf1, and Cebpb rather than reflecting uniform inflammatory activation. In parallel, homeostatic microglial gene signatures (e.g., ApoE, Cst3) were reduced following HSV-1 infection. Spatial transcriptomics localized HSV‑1 antigen to discrete brainstem regions, which were enriched for predicted STAT1/2, IRF1, and CEBPB‑regulated targets identified through single‑nuclei analysis, demonstrating that these inferred transcriptional networks are activated within anatomically defined regions in vivo. Complementary spatial proteomics further confirmed increased microglial activation and astrocytic responses specifically within HSV-1 antigen-positive regions. Together, these integrated multiomic analyses demonstrate that HSV-1 induces localized transcriptional and epigenetic remodeling of microglia dominated by IFN-driven regulatory programs and a loss of homeostatic signatures. By linking single-cell regulatory architecture to spatially restricted tissue responses, our findings provide mechanistic insight into how localized viral infection sustains neuroinflammation, contributing to long-term neurological vulnerability and neurodegenerative disease risk.

articles.title: Cinderella no more: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associated liver disease steps into the ballroom.
Upholding telomeres prevents hepatic stellate cell transdifferentiation and liver fibrogenesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are principal drivers of liver cirrhosis. Whether and how telomere dysfunction affects HSC function remain unclear. This study was undertaken to investigate the role of telomere maintenance in HSCs during fibrogenesis and to evaluate its therapeutic potential by genetic and pharmacological means.

APPROACH RESULTS: Liver fibrosis was established in mice treated with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) or bile duct ligation (BDL), and characterized by tissue and molecular pathology and biochemistry, followed by HSC isolation using flow cytometry. Animals were engineered for HSC-specific overexpression of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene or Acd (encoding the shelterin component TPP1). Alternatively, mice were intraperitoneally injected with telomere dysfunction inhibitor (TELODIN), a D-amino acid octapeptide that stabilizes the telomerase activator TPP1. HSC-specific TERT expression alleviated hepatic fibrosis by suppressing HSC activation, proliferation, and transdifferentiation. Likewise, HSC-specific TPP1 overexpression mitigated hepatic fibrosis by preventing telomere dysfunction and shortening. Pharmacological stabilization of TPP1 by intraperitoneal administration of TELODIN counteracted hepatic fibrogenesis while maintaining HSC quiescence. Mechanistically, TELODIN stabilized TPP1, reduced telomere dysfunction, and decreased HSC transdifferentiation into profibrotic myofibroblasts.

CONCLUSIONS: Telomere dysfunction mediates HSC transdifferentiation during experimental hepatic fibrogenesis. Targeted interventions - that increase telomerase activity or TPP1 mediated telomerase recruitment and activation - alleviate HSC-mediated fibrosis. Pharmacological administration of TELODIN effectively attenuates experimental liver fibrosis by restoring telomere homeostasis in HSCs.

articles.title: Ascending infection of Gardnerella spp. and compartmentalized inflammatory response in fetal-maternal interface organ-on-chip model.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with ascending infection and inflammation at the fetal-maternal interface recognized as major contributors to its pathophysiology. Gardnerella spp., key species associated with bacterial vaginosis, have been implicated in adverse pregnancy outcomes; however, the mechanisms underlying their ability to ascend and trigger inflammatory responses remain poorly understood. In this study, we used a fetal-maternal interface organ-on-chip model to investigate the ascending infection of Gardnerella spp. and the resulting compartmentalized cytokine response. The device integrated decidual, chorionic trophoblast, amniotic mesenchymal and amniotic epithelial cells to mimic the in vivo architecture of the fetal membranes. Quantitative PCR revealed progressive bacterial ascension, with a significantly higher load of Gardnerella spp. in the amnion mesenchymal layer after 48 h of stimulation. Cytokine analysis demonstrated increased production of interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and IL-10 across cellular compartments, indicating a coordinated pro-inflammatory and compensatory anti-inflammatory response. These findings provide direct evidence of Gardnerella spp. invasion dynamics and immune activation at the fetal-maternal interface, supporting the use of microphysiological systems as translational tools to study infection-driven mechanisms of spontaneous preterm birth. KEY POINTS: Gardnerella spp. ascend rapidly across the fetal-maternal interface. Ascending infection induces compartmentalized inflammatory cytokine responses. Amnion mesenchymal cells exhibited the highest bacterial burden after 48 h. The fetal-maternal interface organ-on-chip provides a translational model for studying infection-driven preterm birth.

articles.title: Two New Federal Efforts Designed to Accelerate Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Both ARPA-H and the FDA recently launched programs to help accelerate clinical trials. ARPA-H announced the SURPASS program, which is intended to create faster clinical trials that are more cost-effective and have fewer participants than current studies. It is seeking ideas from cross-disciplinary teams in statistics, artificial intelligence, and clinical trial design, operations, and regulation. The FDA has created a pilot program for accelerating phase I clinical trials that pairs drug sponsors with research organizations.

articles.title: Mobile Stroke Units in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Thrombectomy Efficiency, Workflow Models, and Implementation Considerations: A Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a time-critical emergency in which the benefit of reperfusion depends not only on treatment speed but also on accurate large-vessel occlusion (LVO) recognition, destination selection, and coordination between prehospital and hospital teams. Mobile stroke units (MSUs) move imaging, laboratory testing, specialist assessment, and thrombolysis into the prehospital setting, but their effect on thrombectomy depends substantially on onboard vascular-imaging capability and local routing protocols.

SUMMARY: This narrative review evaluates MSUs through the broader construct of thrombectomy efficiency, encompassing LVO identification, destination accuracy, avoidance of secondary transfer and duplicate imaging, in-hospital parallel processing, puncture and reperfusion times, and downstream clinical outcomes. Evidence for earlier intravenous thrombolysis is retained as an important upstream benefit but is distinguished from thrombectomy-specific efficiency. The available literature indicates that non-contrast-CT-based MSUs can accelerate hospital workflows through early diagnosis and prenotification, whereas CTA-enabled models can additionally confirm LVO in the field and support direct routing to a thrombectomy-capable center or, in selected systems, direct-to-angiography pathways. The magnitude of benefit is therefore configuration- and system-dependent. Economic evaluations likewise show that value is highly sensitive to annual patient volume, catchment population, staffing model, operating hours, analytic time horizon, and baseline patient disability.

KEY MESSAGES: MSUs should not be treated as a uniform intervention. Their thrombectomy value is determined by how effectively prehospital imaging and specialist assessment are linked to destination decisions, interfacility-transfer avoidance, and receiving-center activation. CTA-enabled pathways provide the clearest mechanism for thrombectomy-specific time savings, while non-contrast-CT-based models may still improve in-hospital efficiency. Implementation is most defensible when local geography, case volume, workforce, dispatch integration, downstream thrombectomy capacity, and cost-effectiveness are considered together.

articles.title: Local RAGE Inhibition Attenuates Early Diabetic Retinal Pathology in Streptozotocin-Induced Rats.
articles.abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy, which occurs during extended periods of chronic hyperglycemia, is one of the main causes of vision loss. The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) plays a central role in inflammatory and angiogenic signaling, both of which contribute to the pathogenesis of diabetic retinopathy, but its therapeutic targeting in ocular disease has been insufficiently explored. Methods We evaluated topical RAGE229, a small-molecule RAGE inhibitor, and an intravitreally administered anti-RAGE antibody in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model. At day 84, treatment effects were assessed using masked fundoscopic scoring, RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and histological morphometry. Treated eyes were evaluated against both route-matched diabetic vehicle-control groups and paired contralateral vehicle-treated eyes. Results Both interventions reduced fundoscopic pathology and retinal Vegfa and Nfkb1 expression, whereas Ager showed only a non-significant downward trend. NF-κB p65 immunoreactivity was reduced by both treatments, while a significant reduction in VEGF-A immunoreactivity was detected only in the paired anti-RAGE antibody analysis. Morphometric analysis indicated attenuation of diabetes-associated retinal thinning with both interventions. Neither intervention altered systemic glycemic control. Although both interventions demonstrated similar overall anatomical protection, anti-RAGE antibody treatment showed more consistent effects across protein-level and structural endpoints. Conclusion These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence that local RAGE-targeted treatment may attenuate vascular, molecular, and structural manifestations of early experimental diabetic retinopathy without detectable changes in systemic glycemia. Further preclinical studies should evaluate ocular exposure, direct target engagement, functional visual outcomes, and reproducibility in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Integrated Analysis of the aKlotho-FGF23-FGFR Genetic Axis Reveals Determinants of Cardiovascular Risk in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with a markedly increased cardiovascular (CV) risk. The disruption of the αKlotho-Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF23)-FGF receptors (FGFR) axis has been implicated in chronic diseases and CV complications. We aimed to evaluate the impact of genetic variability across this pathway on renal function and CV outcomes in CKD patients.

METHODS: A total of 829 patients with CKD stages 1-5D were genotyped for 54 tag-SNPs (single nucleotide polymorphisms) and functional variants in KL, FGF23, FGFR1, and FGFR4. Associations with renal function, parameters of blood pressure (BP) and mineral and bone disorder (MBD) and CV events (CVE) were assessed using single- and multiple-marker approaches adjusting for clinical covariates.

RESULTS: FGF23 rs13312770 and KL rs211239 were associated with impaired [OR=1.77 (0.99-3.17), p=0.047] and preserved [OR=0.55 (0.31-0.98), p=0.035] renal function, respectively. Four KL SNPs were associated with BP traits, namely rs385564 and rs2283368 with diastolic BP [mean difference: -2.43 (-4.56--0.29), p=0.026 and 2.73 (0.21-5.25), p=0.034] and rs78425544 and rs9536314 with pulse pressure [5.07 (0.16-9.98), p=0.043 and 3.50 (0.06-6.93), p=0.047]. Six FGFR1 SNPs were associated with vitamin D levels, with rs2978083 showing the strongest association (p<0.0001). Seventy-three patients (8.8%) experienced CVE during follow-up. Carriers of FGFR4 rs351855 had improved CV event-free survival [HR=0.52 (0.28-0.96), p=0.037], whilst KL rs2283368, KLrs575536 and FGFR1 rs2956724 were associated with increased risk [HR=2.02 (1.09-3.78), p=0.022, HR=2.38 (1.25-4.50), p=0.007 and HR=2.18 (1.03-4.63), p=0.041, respectively]. The inclusion of these four SNPs in a clinical-only Cox model improved Harrell's C-index from 0.739 to 0.79 (ΔC=0.056, 7.6%). Haplotypes based on sliding-windows identified several 3-SNP and 2-SNP combinations with a relevant effect on CV risk. Finally, epistasis analysis showed that FGFR1 rs3758101 combined with three different KL variants in SNP pairs significantly impacted CV risk (p<0.001 in all instances).

CONCLUSION: Genetic variability within the αKlotho-FGF23-FGFR axis is significantly associated with renal function and CV outcomes in CKD. Multi-locus approaches reveal combined and interactive effects that enhance risk stratification beyond single-variant analyses.

articles.title: Structure-dynamics analysis of insulin receptor modulation by plant-derived ligands suggests a potential regulatory role for Asn711.
articles.abstract: The insulin receptor (IR) is a central regulator of glucose homeostasis and represents a promising yet underexplored target for antidiabetic drug development. In this study, an integrated computational workflow combining large-scale phytochemical screening, molecular docking, and 200 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations was employed to identify plant-derived ligands capable of stabilizing activation-relevant regions of IR. From an initial library of 140 phytochemicals, Magnoflorine and Nerolidol emerged as top candidates based on binding affinity, ADMET properties, and interaction persistence. Docking results revealed favorable engagement of both ligands within the IR ectodomain, followed by MD simulations that confirmed stable complex formation and reduced structural fluctuations relative to the apo receptor. Both ligands showed stable interactions with Asn711, indicating that this residue may play a previously underappreciated role in ligand recognition. Dynamic analyses further demonstrated ligand mobility between the two insulin-binding sites, supporting a dual-site engagement mechanism analogous to insulin. Overall, these findings provide new mechanistic insights into IR modulation and suggest Magnoflorine and Nerolidol as promising lead molecules for the development of plant-based therapeutics targeting insulin resistance.

articles.title: Inconsistent definitions and outcome measurement: A systematic review of impairments following transient ischaemic attack and minor stroke.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis systematic review aimed to synthesise and characterise studies reporting cognitive, psychological and participation outcomes in transient ischaemic attack (TIA) and minor stroke, including how impairments are measured, definitions of TIA and minor stroke and study representativeness.MethodsSystematic searches of PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, PsycInfo and the Cochrane Library were conducted (from 2013 to 4 June 2026). Articles included participants with TIA/minor stroke and quantitative measures of fatigue, cognitive or communication impairments, depression, anxiety, quality of life, return to work/education or social participation.ResultsSearches identiﬁed 39,136 records, with 190 articles included (comprising 64,638 participants). Cognitive impairment was most frequently reported (n = 134), followed by depression (n = 71) and quality of life (n = 46). Less common were fatigue (n = 33), social participation (n = 16), return to work/education (n = 14) and communication impairment (n = 8). Only 41 studies (21.6%) examined these impairments as primary outcomes. There was heterogeneity in the definition of TIA/minor stroke, the outcome measures and cut-off scores, as well as under-representation from lower-middle and low-income countries and female participants. Ethnicity was rarely reported.DiscussionWe identified a large volume of literature that measured lasting impairment following TIA/minor stroke; however, these were seldom the primary outcome. Substantial heterogeneity in outcome measures, cut-off scores and TIA/minor stroke definitions limited comparability across studies.ConclusionThis review highlights the need for a core outcome set in TIA/minor stroke assessments. Clinicians should recognise that cognitive, psychological and participation difficulties may persist after TIA/minor stroke and ensure these outcomes are considered from initial to follow-up assessments.

articles.title: Longitudinal Validity of the DUNDRUM-1 Triage Security Scale in a Canadian Not Criminally Responsible Cohort: A Retrospective Study of 85 Patients.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the longitudinal stability of DUNDRUM-1 Triage Security Scale recommendations among individuals found not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder (NCRMD) receiving care within a Canadian forensic psychiatric service.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults found NCRMD who received a DUNDRUM-1 assessment at a tertiary academic forensic psychiatric centre in Quebec between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024. Eligible participants were aged ≥18 years and had a minimum of 12 months of follow-up. Demographic, forensic, and clinical variables were extracted from electronic medical records. Primary outcomes included changes in level of therapeutic security within 12 months. Secondary outcomes included psychiatric rehospitalization and transitions across DUNDRUM security categories. Descriptive statistics, Fisher's exact tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and exploratory logistic regression analyses were performed.ResultsEighty-five individuals met inclusion criteria. The cohort was predominantly male (91.8%) with a mean age of 39.0 years (SD = 11.9). Schizophrenia spectrum disorders were the most common primary diagnosis (83.5%), while substance-related disorders (74.1%) and personality disorders (49.4%) were frequent comorbidities. Initial DUNDRUM recommendations included low security (56.5%), medium security (35.3%), open settings (4.7%), and maximum security (3.5%). Overall, 72 participants (84.7%) remained within their initially recommended level of care over 12 months, while 13 (15.3%) required a change in therapeutic security. Psychiatric rehospitalization occurred in 12 participants (14.1%). Exploratory analyses identified the mean violence-related DUNDRUM score as the only significant predictor of changes in level of care (OR = 2.88, 95% CI: 1.03-8.00, p = .043). In exploratory random forest analysis, SHapley Additive exPlanations ranked the mean violence-related DUNDRUM-1 score as the most influential model feature.ConclusionsDUNDRUM-1 recommendations demonstrated substantial longitudinal stability within this Canadian NCRMD cohort, supporting the ecological validity of the instrument and highlighting the potential importance of violence-related domains in predicting medium-term forensic outcomes.

articles.title: The Fontan Procedure in Patients with Single-Lung Physiology: Insights from a Case Report and Scoping Review.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: The Fontan operation represents the third stage of single-ventricle palliation and requires optimal cardiovascular and pulmonary conditions to achieve success. We report a 6-year-old boy with tricuspid atresia, pulmonary atresia, and functional single-lung circulation secondary to severe left pulmonary artery (LPA) hypoplasia and disconnection after previous palliation. Following comprehensive clinical, hemodynamic, and anatomic evaluation, including unsuccessful attempts at LPA recruitment, the patient underwent an extracardiac fenestrated single-lung Fontan procedure. At 2 years of follow-up, he remained in good functional status without Fontan-related complications or the need for reintervention. Additionally, we present a scoping review of published case reports and case series of children with single-lung physiology undergoing the Fontan procedure, focusing on early and follow-up survival. This case, together with the available literature, suggests that single-lung Fontan completion may be feasible in carefully selected patients following meticulous multidisciplinary evaluation, although long-term outcomes remain uncertain.

articles.title: Lipoprotein subfractions, erythrocyte membrane cholesterol in coronary artery disease: A cross-sectional clinical study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAtherosclerosis is a lipid-driven inflammatory disease in which plasma lipoproteins and cellular cholesterol pools contribute to coronary artery disease (CAD). Lipoprotein subfractions and erythrocyte membrane cholesterol (EMC) have each been linked to CAD, but their combined behavior across angiographic stages remains insufficiently characterized. EMC may also be relevant to blood flow properties and microcirculatory function.MethodsWe studied 122 patients undergoing coronary angiography and 64 controls. CAD severity was classified by the number of diseased vessels. Plasma lipid profile, LDL and HDL subfractions, atherogenic indices, EMC, and C-reactive protein were analyzed using multivariable regression, ANCOVA, ROC analysis, and an exploratory multi-marker approach.ResultsConventional lipid parameters showed limited group differences, whereas sdLDL, HDL subfractions, EMC, CRP, and selected lipid ratios differed across CAD severity groups. EMC increased across CAD categories and remained associated with CAD after adjustment for conventional lipid variables. Among lipid-related variables, EMC showed the most consistent association with angiographically defined CAD.ConclusionsEMC may provide complementary hemorheology- and microcirculation-relevant information in angiographically defined CAD. Lipoprotein subfractions and composite lipid indices may offer adjunctive characterization of CAD-related lipid remodeling.

articles.title: Identifying drugs associated with Alzheimer's disease risk using machine learning-assisted signal detection.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSeveral Alzheimer's disease (AD) clinical trials currently focus on drug repurposing. Machine learning (ML)-based pharmacoepidemiological approaches may help identify candidate drugs for trials.ObjectiveWe applied an ML-based signal detection method to identify drugs associated with AD risk.MethodsUsing Finnish nationwide register-based data, we defined drug exposure at both subgroup and drug substance levels according to the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification. Three binary embedded variables were calculated for each drug based on the frequency of dispensations over three years, starting 10 years before the index date. An algorithm combining subsampling and lasso-logistic regression was applied, with 500 replications for each drug exposure variable. Drug variables with a selection percentage (SP) ≥ 70% across replications were considered as signals. The average beta describes the direction and strength of the association.ResultsThe study population comprised 43,926 AD cases and 43,926 matched controls. The mean age was 80.3 years in both groups, and 65% of participants were women. Four drug subgroups and three individual drugs were associated with a lower risk of AD, whereas 14 subgroups and 11 individual drugs were associated with a higher risk. Drugs associated with decreased AD risk belonged to cardiovascular drugs: antihypertensives affecting the renin-angiotensin and diuretics.ConclusionsThe identified associations are consistent with established risk factors of AD and support the importance of effective hypertension management in AD prevention. Further studies are needed to evaluate whether antihypertensive drugs may exert neuroprotective effects and represent viable candidates for drug repurposing in AD.

articles.title: Single-Ventricle Physiology as a Dominant Determinant of Mortality, Resource Utilization, and Pulmonary Vein Reintervention in Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection: A Large Multicenter Study.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: BackgroundChildren with single ventricle (SV) physiology and total anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) face high surgical risk. Despite advances in single ventricle care, survival in SV/TAPVC patients has plateaued. We investigated multicenter outcomes, reintervention rates, and healthcare burden in this complex population.MethodsThe Pediatric Health Information System was queried for TAPVC repairs (2015-2024). Infants were stratified by single-ventricle versus biventricular (BiV) anatomy.ResultsAmong 1258 infants undergoing TAPVC repair, 10% (N = 120) had SV and 90% (N = 1138) had BiV anatomy. SV/TAPVC patients showed higher prematurity (11% [13/120] vs 8% [91/1138], P < .001), low birthweight (14% [17/120] vs 9% [102/1138], P < .001), and neurologic abnormalities (13% [16/120] vs 5% [60/1138], P < .001). Postoperatively, SV/TAPVC had increased delayed sternal closure (11% [13/120] vs 4% [45/1138], P < .001) and ECMO use (7% [8/120] vs 3% [34/1138], P < .001). Healthcare burden was substantially higher in SV/TAPVC children: 5-fold longer hospitalizations (102 vs 29 days, P < .001), 6-fold more hospital visits (6 vs 1, P < .001), and 5-fold higher costs ($1,019,390 vs $259,303, P < .001). Survival at 1 year after repair was severely reduced (SV: 52% vs BiV: 88%, P < .001). Pulmonary vein reinterventions were substantially higher (12-month cumulative incidence: 32% vs 5%, P < .001). Single ventricle physiology was a strong mortality predictor (HR: 3.69, P < .001), particularly pulmonary atresia with intact septum (HR: 6.62, P < .001) and hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HR: 4.42, P < .001).ConclusionsSingle ventricle physiology remains a powerful predictor of adverse outcome in children with TAPVC, with 1-year survival rates approaching 50%. Children with SV/TAPVC face substantially longer hospitalizations, higher reintervention rates, higher hospital visits, and overall 5-fold greater healthcare costs.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Echocardiography: A Critical Review of Models, Validation, and Clinical Impact.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To critically review artificial intelligence (AI) in echocardiography, linking model design and technical performance to validation and clinical use.

METHODS: We synthesized literature assembled through Web of Science and Scopus collections and targeted revision searches. Evidence was organized by echocardiographic task, model paradigm, data source, evaluation protocol, and level of clinical validation.

RESULTS: AI applications span acquisition guidance, image analysis, quantitative measurement, disease assessment, and outcome prediction, with emerging foundation, multimodal, and examination-level models. Most studies assess retrospective task performance; fewer evaluate cross-site transportability or clinical impact. Reproducible performance has been demonstrated for view recognition, segmentation, and selected measurements under aligned protocols, and prospective trials confirm workflow gains. However, evidence linking AI to improved clinical decisions or patient outcomes remains limited. Generalizability is further constrained by uneven dataset coverage and inconsistent evaluation protocols.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports AI assistance in selected echocardiographic tasks; however, clinical use requires external validation, failure reporting, and ongoing monitoring in intended settings.

SIGNIFICANCE: This review links model development with validation evidence to guide clinical evaluation and identify priorities for prospective studies in echocardiography.

articles.title: Hemispheric Asymmetry of Neuroimaging Biomarkers in Early Onset Alzheimer's Disease: Clinical and Cognitive Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease (AD) often exhibit amyloid, tau, and atrophy predominantly in the left or right hemisphere, but group-level analyses typically ignore inter-individual variability and changing asymmetry patterns when averaging data across participants in phenotypically diverse cohorts.

METHODS: We examined left/right hemispheric asymmetry in amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), tau PET, and cortical atrophy in sporadic early-onset AD from 585 deeply phenotyped individuals across 2 cohorts to investigate its clinical correlates. For each imaging biomarker, we computed a global asymmetry index reflecting left/right hemisphere signal difference, and an analogous asymmetry value for PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) voxels. We examined clinical and cognitive correlates of this asymmetry across phenotypes cross-sectionally and longitudinally in a subset of 218 participants.

RESULTS: Both left and right asymmetry were common for all clinical phenotypes and was correlated between imaging biomarkers. Asymmetry patterns varied spatially within phenotypes, and asymmetry in tau PET and MRI volumes was related to hemisphere-dependent cognitive deficits and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Longitudinal analyses revealed stable amyloid PET asymmetry, decreasing tau PET asymmetry, and increasing MRI volume asymmetry.

INTERPRETATION: Hemispheric asymmetry is common in early onset AD and correlates with clinical outcomes. Our longitudinal findings suggest a time-lagged asymmetry peak in amyloid, then tau, then atrophy. Taken together, our results position asymmetry as an important feature of AD heterogeneity, as it provides insight into disease mechanisms and trajectories. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: Mild Amyloid Burden in the Brains of Cognitively Unimpaired Individuals is Associated with Long-Term Cognitive Impairment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to identify the minimal amount of amyloid burden measured by positron emission tomography (PET) in amyloid-negative cognitively unimpaired individuals that predicts the development of cognitive impairment.

METHODS: A total of 1,896 cognitively unimpaired participants underwent longitudinal clinical/cognitive assessments for up to 20.3 years after amyloid PET imaging. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess how the risk of cognitive impairment was associated with subthresholds of amyloid PET Centiloid. Linear mixed effects models were used to associate the longitudinal cognitive decline and amyloid accumulation with baseline amyloid burden.

RESULTS: Amyloid-positive participants (Centiloid >20; n = 421) were 154% (hazard ratio 2.54, p < 0.0001) more likely to develop cognitive impairment than amyloid-negative participants. Approximately 48.7% of the amyloid-negative participants had mild amyloid burden (defined by Centiloid from 0.93 to 20) and were 43% more likely to develop cognitive impairment (hazard ratio 1.43, p = 0.008) than the lowest amyloid group (Centiloid <0.93) approximately 10 years post baseline. Longitudinal changes in amyloid PET Centiloid and cognition followed a similar pattern: amyloid-positive participants were the fastest, followed by the mild amyloid burden group and finally the lowest amyloid group, and the cognitive trajectories for the latter 2 started to separate only approximately 10 years post baseline (p = 0.003).

INTERPRETATION: Almost half of amyloid-negative cognitively unimpaired individuals were at an elevated long-term risk of cognitive impairment, when compared with those with the lowest amyloid levels. These findings suggest that the current threshold for amyloid positivity may be overly restrictive, potentially excluding a large portion of high-risk participants from prevention trials. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: Contemporary Sex-Specific Mortality Risk in Type 1 Diabetes During the Era of Advanced Therapeutic Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Amid major advances in diabetes care technologies, this study aimed to assess all-cause mortality risk among individuals diagnosed with type 1 diabetes in recent decades compared with matched control individuals.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all patients with type 1 diabetes diagnosed before age 35 between 2000 and 2022, identified through a validated registry from Maccabi Healthcare Services (MHS), a large state-mandated health care provider network. A diabetes-free comparison cohort was constructed using 1:4 propensity score matching by sex and age. Follow-up continued until 2023, death, or transfer from MHS, whichever occurred first. Cox regression and sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Mortality rates among 4,299 individuals with type 1 diabetes (mean ± SD age at diagnosis, 17.4 ± 9.1 years) and 17,196 matched control individuals (45.6% female overall) were 131.0 and 35.2 per 100,000 person-years, respectively, with 112 deaths over 204,102 person-years. Type 1 diabetes was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 3.66; 95% CI 2.53-5.31), with consistent estimates after adjustment and sensitivity analyses. Excess mortality was greater in females than males (adjusted HR 8.40 [3.71-19.04] vs. 2.90 [1.78-4.72]; P-interaction = 0.02), although absolute mortality rates were higher in males. Mortality risk was higher in those diagnosed in 2000-2010 than in 2011-2022 (adjusted HR 4.36 [1.22-15.57] vs. 2.94 [1.31-6.60]), with follow-up truncated for comparability.

CONCLUSIONS: Type 1 diabetes was associated with higher risk of mortality, particularly among females. This association was attenuated among individuals diagnosed in more recent years.

articles.title: Interpreting Hyperacute IL-1β and NET Signals in Large-Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
A Case of Severe Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in a Patient with CYP2C9*2/*2: Lessons from the Vulture Crisis.
articles.abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are a well-recognized cause of AKI, typically occurring in the setting of substantial exposure or predisposing risk factors. We report a case of severe AKI following minimal naproxen exposure in a previously healthy young adult. An 18-year-old man presented with abdominal and flank pain and was found to have KDIGO stage 3 AKI after receiving analgesic treatment for fracture-related pain. The patient had taken two oral 500-mg doses of naproxen seven days before presentation and had received two intravenous 2.5-g doses of metamizole, one on the day before and the other on the day of presentation. Clinical presentation, ultrasonography and magnetic resonance angiography argued against prerenal, postrenal and vascular causes. Suspected interstitial nephritis prompted empiric methylprednisolone therapy. Kidney biopsy revealed acute tubular injury without interstitial nephritis, and corticosteroids were discontinued. Kidney function recovered within two weeks of symptom onset. Given the severity of AKI relative to the reported drug exposure, pharmacogenetic testing was performed and revealed a CYP2C9*2/*2 genotype associated with reduced NSAID metabolism. Although the identified genotype is unlikely to fully account for the severe AKI observed, it may have contributed to the patient's susceptibility to nephrotoxicity. This case highlights pharmacogenetically impaired NSAID metabolism as a potentially underrecognized contributor to AKI and underscores the potential value of pharmacogenetic testing in selected patients without conventional risk factors.

articles.title: Reply to "Interpreting Hyperacute IL-1β and NET Signals in Large-Vessel Occlusion Stroke".
Protein and mRNA expression level of IL-38 and correlation with IL-36R in pediatric asthmatic patients.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPediatric asthma is a respiratory disease involving bronchial hyperresponsiveness to risk factors, influenced by genetic and environmental factors.Objective: This study investigated IL-38/IL-36R in pediatric asthma. Samples from 140 children aged 1-10 years, including 80 patients and 60 controls, were analyzed. IL-38 mRNA expression was assessed by qRT-PCR, while serum IL-38 and IL-36R were measured by ELISA.ResultsRevealed significant increase serum level of IL-38 74.80± 11.583pg/ml in asthmatic patients compare to control 59.33± 11.833pg/ml (P=0.01) while serum level of IL-36R in patients 226.26 ±88.07 pg/ml compare to control group167.4250 ±55.03pg/ml, results of expression of mRNA level of IL-38 shows significantly increased in asthmatic patients 2 fold with p value <0.01, significant correlation between serum level of IL-38 and IL-36R (r= -0.7459, p value =0.001), while weak correlation between concentration of IL-36R and mRNA expression of IL-38.ConclusionThe results showed that the changes in serum and expression levels of IL-38 have significant impact on asthma disease and its severity. These levels may account as diagnostic marker for pediatric asthma.

articles.title: Association between xerostomia and peri-implant health: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dental implants are a long-term and reliable solution to replace missing dentition, but subject to different patient-related and biological changes that could alter its success. Xerostomia, or the alteration of the normal salivary flow, can impair oral function and potentially affect the success of any treatment, including implant outcomes. The purpose of this study is to study the association between xerostomia and peri-implantitis.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using records of patients who received dental implants between 2010 and 2023 at the University of Michigan School of Dentistry. The patients were divided into two groups: the xerostomia group and the non-xerostomia group. Implant level assessment included the presence of peri-implantitis and marginal bone loss, restoration type, cement-retained or screw retained, and the depth of restoration margin. Patient-level assessment included sex, age, smoking history, medical conditions, and maintenance visit frequency. Univariable and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between peri-implantitis and patient-level and other implant-related variables. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were reported, and statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 173 patients were included, with 46 patients reporting xerostomia. The results showed no independent association between xerostomia and peri-implantitis in either univariable or multivariable analyzes. The history of periodontitis and cement-retained restorations were significant predictors for peri-implantitis. Age was significant in univariable analysis but lost significance in the adjusted model. The frequency of maintenance visits was associated with peri-implantitis in univariable analysis but lost significance in multivariable analysis. Sex, smoking, and diabetes mellitus were not significantly associated with peri-implantitis.

CONCLUSION: Xerostomia alone does not increase the risk of peri-implantitis. A history of periodontitis, the use of cement-retained prosthesis, and longer follow-up duration after prosthetic loading were associated with unfavorable implant outcomes.

articles.title: A randomized phase II study of fulvestrant with or without ganetespib in patients with endocrine resistant metastatic breast cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with endocrine-resistant hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (MBC) have limited effective treatment options. Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) regulates estrogen receptor stability and function; its inhibition has been proposed as a strategy to overcome endocrine resistance. Ganetespib is a second-generation HSP90 inhibitor with demonstrated anti-tumor activity in preclinical breast cancer models.

METHODS: In this randomized phase II study, 50 patients with HR+ MBC previously treated with endocrine therapy were randomized 1:2 to fulvestrant alone (n = 15) or fulvestrant with ganetespib (n = 35), respectively. Median age was 53 years. Fulvestrant was administered at standard dosing; ganetespib (200 mg/m2) was given intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival and safety/tolerability.

RESULTS: Median PFS was similar between arms (3.7 vs. 3.6 months; log-rank p = 0.79). Toxicity was higher with ganetespib, with substantially increased diarrhea (97% vs. 7%) and nausea (63% vs. 40%). Exploratory genomic analysis of on-treatment biopsies (n = 13) showed ESR1 mutations were enriched among patients without clinical benefit, while all patients with clinical benefit exhibited a Luminal A transcriptional subtype. Tumors lacking clinical benefit showed enrichment of proliferative and cell cycle-associated transcriptional programs.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding ganetespib to fulvestrant did not improve clinical outcomes and increased toxicity in endocrine-resistant HR+ MBC. Our findings support the hypothesis that ESR1 alterations and proliferative transcriptional activity contribute to established endocrine resistance, limiting the therapeutic impact of HSP90 inhibition in this setting.

CLINICALTRIALS.GOV REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT01560416.

articles.title: Differential effects of PM2.5 constituents on tuberculosis infection and disease progression in 40,379 student close contacts.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Outdoor PM2.5 has been increasingly implicated in tuberculosis, yet evidence has largely focused on total PM2.5 mass and has usually considered Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis) infection and active tuberculosis separately. Whether specific PM2.5 chemical constituents differ in their associations with infection and subsequent progression to active disease remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the associations of PM2.5 and five major constituents with M. tuberculosis infection and subsequent progression to active tuberculosis within the same high-risk population.

METHODS: We conducted two complementary analyses among student close contacts of tuberculosis patients from 458 schools in 12 cities in eastern China during 2020-2024. Daily residential outdoor exposures were assigned from daily modeled estimates of PM2.5 and five major constituents (sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, organic matter, and black carbon) on an approximately 10-km grid, which were interpolated to geocoded addresses. We first assessed associations between exposure averaged over the five years preceding contact screening and M. tuberculosis infection identified by the ESAT6-CFP10 skin test during the contact investigation. We then followed infected students identified at the contact screening to examine associations between time-varying annual exposure and progression to active tuberculosis.

RESULTS: Among 40,379 students, 1,269 had M. tuberculosis infection, and 70 infected students progressed to active tuberculosis during follow-up. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher infection risk (OR: 1.043; 95% CI: 1.018, 1.068) and progression risk (HR: 1.094; 95% CI: 1.010, 1.185). All five constituents were positively associated with infection (ORs: 1.156-5.390). Sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium were also positively associated with progression to active tuberculosis (HRs: 1.462-2.680). The findings remained generally consistent in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large multi-city close-contact study, PM2.5 was associated with both M. tuberculosis infection and subsequent progression to active tuberculosis. Three secondary inorganic aerosol (SIA) constituents, namely sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium, showed the most consistent association patterns across the two outcomes. These findings reinforce the importance of overall PM2.5 control and support further evaluation of coordinated reductions in SIA precursor emissions.

articles.title: Human vs Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Coronary Occlusions in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) on the electrocardiogram (ECG) can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), non-STEMI, ST depression, or other patterns (eg, de Winter T waves and hyperacute T waves), posing a diagnostic challenge. Even experienced physicians may overlook OMI on ECG, leading to delays in catheterization laboratory activation. Recently, smartphone apps using AI have been shown to exhibit promising accuracy in ECG interpretation in large datasets.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of our study was to retrospectively compare the diagnostic performance of an AI-based application (PMCardio) with that of interventional cardiologists in interpreting nonpathognomonic ECGs that generated debates about diagnosis.

METHODS: In total, 33 ECGs that were diagnostically challenging upon patient admission to the emergency department were included. A group of 3 interventional cardiologists, blinded to the final diagnosis, independently assessed whether the ECG suggested OMI requiring immediate invasive coronary angiography. The diagnostic performance of the cardiologists was compared to that of the AI application, using the results of coronary angiography as the gold standard and considering any lesion with ≥90% stenosis as positive.

RESULTS: Of the 33 patients, 29 (88%) had a final diagnosis of cardiac origin for their chest pain, including 23 acute coronary syndromes, of which 13 (57%) were OMI. The 3 cardiologists achieved sensitivities of 62%, 85%, and 62%; negative predictive values (NPVs) of 74%, 83%, and 69%; specificities of 70%, 50%, and 55%; and positive predictive values (PPVs) of 57%, 52%, and 47%. Their overall misclassification rates were 33%, 36%, and 42%. In contrast, AI analysis demonstrated a sensitivity and NPV of 100%, a specificity of 60%, a PPV of 62%, and an overall misclassification rate of 24%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study of challenging ECGs, an AI application demonstrated better diagnostic performance of OMI as compared to cardiologists. These findings highlight the potential of AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Beyond the label: Long-term outcomes after surgical management of Ebstein anomaly.
articles.abstract: Ebstein anomaly is a rare congenital malformation of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle characterized by marked heterogeneity in anatomy, physiology, and clinical presentation. This broad phenotypic spectrum strongly influences the natural history of the disease, the timing and type of intervention, and ultimately long-term outcomes. Patients range from critically ill neonates with severe hemodynamic compromise and circular shunts to asymptomatic children and adults with progressive tricuspid regurgitation, right ventricular dysfunction, or arrhythmias, as well as survivors of previous surgical interventions. Accordingly, long-term outcomes are best understood within the context of the presenting phenotype and its associated management pathway rather than as a single aggregate measure of survival. Contemporary management therefore requires phenotype-specific decision-making. This review summarizes long-term outcomes across the major clinical and therapeutic subgroups, including critically ill neonates managed with the Starnes procedure, stable neonates and infants undergoing biventricular repair, patients treated with historical repair techniques, contemporary cone reconstruction, and tricuspid valve replacement. Particular emphasis is placed on transplant-free survival, valve durability, ventricular remodeling, arrhythmia burden, functional status, quality of life, and the need for reintervention.

articles.title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.

CONCLUSIONS: LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.

articles.title: Infracardiac and mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection: Surgical challenges and practical solutions.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTotal anomalous pulmonary venous connection (TAPVC) remains a complex congenital cardiac malformation. Despite improved survival, infracardiac and mixed variants continue to carry disproportionate risks of early mortality, postoperative pulmonary venous obstruction (PVO), and reintervention.MethodsThis narrative review examines the anatomic and technical challenges of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC, mechanisms and consequences of postoperative PVO, and contemporary strategies to reduce residual or recurrent obstruction, with particular emphasis on primary sutureless repair and anatomy-specific surgical approaches.ResultsContemporary operative mortality for TAPVC is approximately 3-10% but remains higher in patients with preoperative obstruction. Postoperative PVO occurs in approximately 5-15% and is an important determinant of reintervention and late mortality. In infracardiac TAPVC, obstruction may occur along with the descending vertical vein, producing severe pulmonary venous hypertension and physiologic instability. Mixed TAPVC presents additional challenges from heterogeneous drainage, multiple or small confluences, isolated veins, and complex geometry. Primary sutureless repair has evolved from treatment of recurrent PVO to a preventive strategy in high-risk primary TAPVC by avoiding pulmonary venous suture lines and facilitating wide, unobstructed drainage.ConclusionsManagement of infracardiac and mixed TAPVC requires an anatomy-specific approach focused on preventing postoperative PVO. Important strategies include selective preoperative stabilization, primary sutureless reconstruction in high-risk anatomy, a no-touch approach to selected isolated veins in 3 + 1 mixed TAPVC, and complete reconstruction of the cardiac component when appropriate.

articles.title: Escalating Vasopressor Intensity and the Goals-of-Care Documentation Gap in Septic Shock: Relevance to the Proposed Refractory Shock Threshold.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe 2026 joint SCCM/ESICM Delphi consensus identified vasopressor intensity as a defining feature of refractory septic shock, yet its relationship to real-world goals-of-care documentation remains unclear.ObjectivesWe assessed the association between escalating vasopressor intensity and documented surrogate goals-of-care markers among septic shock decedents.MethodsRetrospective cohort study of adult septic shock decedents in MIMIC-IV (2008-2022) requiring vasopressors ≥6 h and surviving ≥24 h after initiation. Vasopressor intensity was quantified by peak norepinephrine equivalent (NEE) dose during ICU stay and stratified as: 0.01-0.50 (stratum 1), >0.50-0.99 (stratum 2), and ≥1.00 µg/kg/min (stratum 3). The primary outcome was death without documented surrogate goals-of-care markers, defined as having neither a documented do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order nor documented palliative care involvement.ResultsThe final cohort included 2458 patients: stratum 1 (n = 1033), stratum 2 (n = 909), and stratum 3 (n = 516). Death without documented goals-of-care markers increased across strata (23.8%, 28.3%, 31.2%; p-for-trend=0.001). After multivariable adjustment, stratum 3 patients remained more likely than stratum 1 to die without documented goals-of-care markers (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.02-1.69; p = 0.03). Palliative care documentation declined progressively with increasing vasopressor intensity (59.2%, 52.0%, 46.9%; p-for-trend<0.001), accompanied by lower rates of integrated DNR/palliative care documentation (47.0%, 40.0%, 36.4%; p-for-trend<0.001). Patients exceeding the Delphi-proposed refractory shock threshold (NEE >0.50 µg/kg/min) were more likely to die without documented goals-of-care markers than those below the threshold (29.3% vs 23.8%; p = 0.002).ConclusionHigher vasopressor intensity was paradoxically associated with a greater likelihood of death without documented goals-of-care markers and with lower palliative care documentation. These findings suggest a disconnect between escalating physiologic severity and documentation of surrogate goals-of-care markers in refractory septic shock and warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: BackgroundImpaired hand function can limit independence. Sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG) differ in stimulation characteristics and voluntary effort requirements, but comparative evidence is limited.ObjectiveTo compare SES and Alt-EMG, each combined with conventional physical therapy, on upper-limb motor function, spasticity, and muscle strength in chronic stroke.MethodsThis three-arm, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial included 60 adults aged 45-65 years, 6-18 months post-stroke, allocated equally to SES, Alt-EMG, or control groups (n = 20 each). The primary outcome was the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT); Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) and Medical Research Council (MRC) scores were secondary outcomes. ARAT was analyzed using ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and age; ordinal outcomes were analyzed nonparametrically. Benjamini-Hochberg and Holm corrections addressed multiplicity.ResultsAll participants completed the 12-week intervention. Treatment group significantly predicted adjusted post-intervention ARAT scores (F (2,55) = 23.19, P < .001, partial η2=.46). Adjusted mean gains versus control were 12.05 points for SES and 12.44 points for Alt-EMG (both P < .001), with no significant difference between active groups. Significant between-group differences were observed for shoulder, elbow, and wrist spasticity and most muscle-strength measures, except finger extensors.ConclusionsSES and Alt-EMG combined with conventional physical therapy produced greater improvement in upper-limb motor function than conventional physical therapy alone over 12 weeks. No difference was observed between SES and Alt-EMG for the primary outcome.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in partial combined 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency: functional characterization of CYP17A1 variants in ten 46,XY patients.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partial combined 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency (PC-17OHD) is a rare 17OHD subtype with residual 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase activities. In 46,XY individuals, genital virilization is highly variable, and genotype-phenotype correlations remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical and endocrine spectrum of 46,XY PC-17OHD, functionally validate uncharacterized CYP17A1 variants, and establish genotype-phenotype correlations.

METHODS: We enrolled ten 46,XY PC-17OHD patients from 9 families. Clinical phenotypes were characterized, and long-read CYP17A1 sequencing was performed. Splicing effects and enzyme activities were evaluated by minigene assays and HEK293T functional studies, respectively. Variants were classified according to ACMG guidelines.

RESULTS: All patients presented with the triad of elevated mineralocorticoid precursors, generalized androgen suppression, and preserved cortisol levels. Median age at diagnosis was 17.5 years, with hypertension in 30% (3/10) and hypokalemia in 20% (2/10). Ten distinct variants were identified, including 2 novel splice-site variants (c.666+2T>C, c.1243+2T>G). Haplotype analysis revealed a shared identical haplotype among 5 patients carrying the c.1263G>A allele, indicating a Chinese founder effect. Four uncharacterized variants showed residual 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase activities: p.Trp499Ter (11%/6.3%), p.Ala448Val (22.5%/14.2%), p.Leu433Ser (25.9%/21.7%), and c.666+2T>C (28.9%/22.6%). Notably, 2 patients with identical genotypes (c.985_987delinsAA/c.1263G>A) exhibited drastically divergent phenotypes-hypospadias (raised male) vs complete female external genitalia (raised female)-indicating that genotype alone cannot accurately predict clinical phenotypes in PC-17OHD.

CONCLUSIONS: Residual CYP17A1 activity largely determines genital masculinization, while marked phenotypic heterogeneity among patients with identical genotypes indicates that genotype alone cannot fully predict clinical manifestations. These findings improve molecular diagnosis and individualized care for this disorder.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Palliative Care Approaches in the Community: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCommunity-based palliative care is increasingly promoted as an alternative to hospital-centered end-of-life care, yet prior reviews have largely cataloged outcome measures or program components associated with favorable results, without explaining how these components interact to produce those outcomes.ObjectiveTo synthesize evidence on the effectiveness of community-based palliative care for life-limiting illness and to identify the mechanisms, rather than merely components, underlying its benefits.MethodsFollowing standard systematic review reporting guidelines, we searched multiple databases for studies evaluating community-based palliative care delivered to adults with life-limiting conditions outside hospital settings. Twenty eligible studies were analyzed using thematic synthesis.ResultsFindings coalesced into 5 interdependent mechanisms rather than a list of isolated benefits. First, anticipatory, home-based symptom monitoring enabled rapid clinical response, reducing pain, breathlessness, and psychological distress while preserving quality of life despite functional decline. Second, care was structured to conserve patient dignity and autonomy, particularly for marginalized populations, by treating patient-defined goals of care as organizing principles rather than secondary considerations. Third, family caregivers functioned as a mediating variable: structured caregiver education and burden mitigation sustained home-monitoring vigilance that made early symptom detection possible. Fourth, task-sharing between specialist clinicians and trained community health workers or volunteers allowed monitoring and social support to scale without proportional increases in specialist staffing. Fifth, early, structured advance care planning functioned as a leading indicator that plausibly mediated downstream reductions in emergency visits, hospital readmissions, and intensive care unit utilization, with corresponding per-patient cost reductions.ConclusionsCommunity-based palliative care improves outcomes not simply because care is relocated to the home, but because the home is where clinical responsiveness, caregiver capacity, task-shared workforce models, and early care planning converge and reinforce one another. Health systems that shift only the site of care, without investing in these underlying mechanisms, are unlikely to reproduce the effects reported here.

articles.title: Acute Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis: The Role of Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) remains one of the most challenging syndromes in hepatology and critical care, with high short-term mortality despite advances in supportive management. Although corticosteroids remain the only guideline-endorsed pharmacologic therapy shown to improve early survival, their benefit is modest, limited to selected patients, and frequently complicated by infection. Consequently, contemporary management extends well beyond corticosteroid therapy and requires meticulous supportive care, nutritional optimization, infection surveillance, management of portal hypertensive complications and acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), and early multidisciplinary involvement. This review summarizes the current evidence regarding the diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and medical management of severe AH. Key prognostic models, including MELD, Maddrey Discriminant Function, and the Lille score, are discussed together with evolving evidence supporting individualized corticosteroid use and emerging investigational therapies. Particular emphasis is placed on critically ill patients with ACLF, in whom extrahepatic organ failure often supersedes liver dysfunction as the principal determinant of outcome. The review also examines the evolving role of early liver transplantation (LT), one of the most important paradigm shifts in modern transplant hepatology. Contemporary approaches to patient selection, psychosocial assessment, relapse-risk evaluation, living donor transplantation, and the management of patients with catastrophic AH are discussed, along with ethical considerations surrounding organ allocation, medical urgency, and stewardship of scarce donor organs. Despite important advances in supportive care and transplantation, severe AH continues to carry substantial mortality. Optimizing outcomes requires timely diagnosis, multidisciplinary management, careful selection for medical therapy, and early recognition of patients unlikely to recover without liver transplantation.

articles.title: A Proactive Digital Valve Care Pathway for Management of Severe Aortic Stenosis: The DETECT AS II Study.

Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026.

INTERVENTION: Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications.

RESULTS: The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant and Perioperative Immunotherapy for Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Current Evidence, Endpoints, and Clinical Integration.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are being investigated across curative-intent treatment pathways for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Randomized studies show that programmed cell death-1 blockade can increase pathological complete response (pCR) when added to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, while immunochemoradiotherapy can produce high pathological response rates. This structured narrative review summarizes current evidence for neoadjuvant and perioperative immunotherapy in ESCC within the context of established chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy backbones. Particular attention is given to randomized ICI trials, the role of radiotherapy, interpretation of pathological and survival endpoints, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), postoperative therapy, perioperative safety, clinical response assessment, and regional applicability. pCR is a useful early activity endpoint and may carry prognostic information within individual regimens, but definitions and pathological assessment vary and trial-level surrogacy for overall survival has not been established. Longitudinal ctDNA is promising as a complementary measure of molecular residual disease but remains investigational for treatment adaptation. When radiotherapy is combined with ICI, established thoracic organ-at-risk constraints and careful monitoring for overlapping pulmonary and esophageal toxicity remain important because ICI-specific normal-tissue constraints have not been validated. Clinical complete response assessment also requires multimodal evaluation; post-treatment inflammatory changes can limit CT and PET-CT specificity. Overall, current data support continued phase III evaluation of ICI-containing strategies with mature event-free and overall survival endpoints and with comparators appropriate to regional treatment standards.

articles.title: Outcomes and Predictors of Sustained Response After Dose Tapering of Targeted Therapies in Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD) often requires prolonged systemic therapy. As disease control is achieved, optimizing dose tapering and identifying factors associated with sustained response are increasingly relevant.

OBJECTIVE: The aim was to identify factors associated with maintained disease control following dose tapering of biologics and small-molecule inhibitors used for AD.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from 2010 to present, along with manual reference screening. Studies evaluating dose tapering or withdrawal of dupilumab, tralokinumab, lebrikizumab, abrocitinib, baricitinib, or upadacitinib were included. Extracted data included study design, patient characteristics, tapering or withdrawal strategies, and follow-up duration. Outcomes of interest were sustained response, relapse rates, and predictors of long-term disease control.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies (4375 patients) were included. Sustained response rates post-tapering varied across abrocitinib (0-60%), baricitinib (45-61%), dupilumab (30-100%), lebrikizumab (67-82%), tralokinumab (25-50%), and upadacitinib (47-61%). Lower baseline disease activity and early clinical improvement were frequently identified as potential predictors of durability. For dupilumab, older age, lower body mass index (BMI), and prurigo nodularis phenotype were associated with sustained response in selected cohorts. For tralokinumab, longitudinal stability across multiple visits outperformed single-time-point assessments. Abrocitinib outcomes favored milder disease without allergic comorbidities, whereas upadacitinib showed higher relapse rates after withdrawal.

CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with moderate-to-severe AD achieving stable disease control, dose tapering appeared to preserve efficacy more frequently than abrupt withdrawal, although response rates and durability varied across therapeutic classes, study designs, and outcome definitions. Predictors of sustained response were drug specific, and longer prospective studies are needed to inform individualized tapering strategies.

articles.title: Beyond seropositivity: quantitative parietal cell antibody titers predict gastric intestinal metaplasia in a high helicobacter pylori prevalence setting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Anti-gastric parietal cell antibody (APA) positivity is a recognized serological biomarker for autoimmune gastritis, but whether quantitative APA titer levels correlate with the severity of gastric intestinal metaplasia (GIM) in high Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) prevalence settings remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between quantitative APA titer dilutions and histopathological GIM in a large endoscopic cohort.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of adult patients who underwent APA testing at a tertiary referral center between November 2017 and November 2019 were reviewed.
